CONTENT: Just my luck, try this on a whim and turns out I absolutely love it. Ugh! I'm a sucker for Byredo fragrances with blackcurrant anyway (Mixed Emotions, my love) but this? With rose, raspberry and what smells like chestnut??? It's so pretty! It feels like a gourmand without actually being a gourmand.

What's the most popular perfume according to the internet? Which one is the most discussed? These are the questions that "http" by Bond No. 9 manages to answer through the notes of (in my opinion) synthetic pineapple, berries and apple in the opening. The effect that you get out of this synthetic feel is fresh and newly manufactured plastic that transitions to a less aggressive variation of the patchouly-moss-vetiver accord. In the very end a light musk cleans the composition to evoke a note of clean laundry. If you didn't get the reference, it's Aventus, and if you look for a greener alternative of it, this is the place to be. Greener pineapple, greener berries.

I heard before purchasing this that it was supposed to be a lot like Creed Aventus. And me personality, have never liked Creed Aventus at all. So I don’t know why I even wanted to try this. But man, I’m so happy I did. This is what Aventus wished to be, this is just 100x better, even tho it smells kind of similar this has way more fruity notes coming through and lingers in the air perfectly, easy to wear to any occation. Even tho I’m not the biggest fan of these DNA’s, this get’s a solid 8.5/10 which is very good for this type of cologne.

…and I was having a hard time finding this one ANYWHERE. Then FragranceNet sent me an email stating they had it in stock so I pounced immediately. This one gets compared to Aventus a lot, but aside from the pineapple note, there really isn’t much of a similarity. This one is a nice, sweet, fruity scent that lasts and lasts. If you want to say it’s similar to anything, it’s probably one of its Bond brothers (A Scent of Peace). The projection is good, reaching out to an easy 4ft radius, and the sillage trail it leaves behind sits for a while, marking your territory. Longevity in this (and most Bond scents) is great; going an easy 8-10+ hours. I wish I scored the 100ml bottle, but at least I got it.

If you are about to discover Bond No9 as a line of products, this one and Chez Bond are the two you should try. Any fragrance after 2010 that has pineapple note naturally gets compared to Aventus. This one is no exception. Very fruity in the opening and ambery towards the end. A little synthetic smelling and overwhelming and cloying at times. But... Still, one of the best Bond No9 creations IMO. In small doses could be a good spring/summer/fall scent. While this is inspired by Aventus, it isn't Aventus. I'd say performance wise, this is by far stronger than most Creeds. Quality wise, however, I guarantee you a lot more people will like Aventus over this. Nevertheless, I like it and wear it rather often. Good longevity, modest projection. Try it!

http://www.bondno9.com/ is another blind buy of mine. I have wanted to own this perfume for a long time. This week, it finally happened, and a bottle moved in with me. Bond No. 9 is a brand that really divides opinions here, although http://www.bondno9.com/ is rated quite well. Personally, I like the Bond No. 9 scents. With http://www.bondno9.com/, the brand has created a perfume that will also appeal to those who usually do not pay attention to the brand. I would like to immediately contradict the statement regarding the similarity to Aventus. http://www.bondno9.com/ has absolutely no resemblance to Aventus and is an independent scent with character. I see more similarities to Nishane Hacivat, although here too, Bond No. 9 has a completely different fruit note. http://www.bondno9.com/ opens with a massive burst of pineapple, bergamot, and a spicy juniper note. However, this top note disappears after just over 10 minutes, giving the stage to the typical Bond No. 9 blackcurrant. I cannot smell any apple at all. After just over 3 hours, the woody notes emerge, and here I can smell the cedarwood indicated in the pyramid. I don’t really pick up the base notes, just a slight moss note and no strong musk that some perfume lovers fear. After just over 7 hours, http://www.bondno9.com/ fades away. The sillage lasts just over 5 hours at arm's length, after which it becomes weaker and from the 7th hour, it is very close to the skin. http://www.bondno9.com/ is truly like a fruit candy to spray on. The perfume simply puts you in a good mood.

Actually, I wanted to make fewer blind purchases, as my goal is to have a collection as small as possible with scents that I truly love instead of buying everything that isn't nailed down. That's why my collection is quite small, but it also saves money. Sometimes, however, the bottle is so beautiful that it really draws you in...

Without having offended the female gender in the headline. But it feels like we are dealing here with a softer and somewhat more synthetic version of Aventus. Typical American, everyone's darling;) I like it, yet the scent has something contrived about it. However, I can't quite bring myself to say that completely. Just because I was more familiar with Aventus.

A most appealing soapy floral is what Bond no 9 CHELSEA FLOWERS is to my nose. Actually, it seems very close to a hair conditioner floral, though I have not been able to narrow down exactly which hair conditioner. It's not Garnier Fructis, nor Pantene. Could it be L'oreal Vive (the red bottle)? Don't know, but somehow I love the opening of this composition anyway. In fact, I have what may be an irrational reaction to the initial application of this perfume. Yes, I really think that it smells like some hair conditioner in my past, and yet together with the mélange of florals--which my nose cannot tease out individually, so strong is the hair conditioner note--it actually induces in me a sense of excitement perhaps not unlike Gwyneth Paltrow's ecstatic engagement with Creed SPRING FLOWER. But I do not believe that CHELSEA FLOWERS is a facsmile or copycat of SPRING FLOWER. I think that it's closer to a cross between something like SPRING FLOWER and one of the hair conditioner frags in the D&G Anthology series. nulltheless, I like it--a lot! The only reason I won't be adding CHELSEA FLOWERS to my collection is because it has the worst staying power of any of the Bond no 9 edps I've tried to date. Given the speed with which I drained my purse spray, I just cannot justify indulging my irrational fondness for the opening of this fragrance. For it dwindles to nearly nothing in a matter of minutes, leaving me reaching for a refresher again and again... This is an oddity for a Bond no 9 perfume, which generally have a lot of oomph, projection, and excellent longevity. Am I suffering perhaps from olfactory fatigue? On ne sait jamais... Maybe I should just go wash my hair.

Smells like a Lilly of the Valley version of Elizabeth Arden Sunflowers, no idea how when Chelsea Flowers does not have lotv listed as a note…but that’s what I get. I’ve loved Sunflowers for over 25 years and blind bought Chelsea Flowers based on how similar reviews mentioned them to be. Yes, same sharp watery floral 90s vibe. I like it. However I do not love this because, for the price, I was expecting the performance to blow Sunflowers out of the water and sadly it does not. It performs exactly the same if not a little worse because the dry down goes waxy invisible instead of warm floral. I am finding Bond No9 fragrances are so hit and miss when it comes to performance. I have New York Gardenia and that sticks to everything for days on end, it is relentless. Chelsea Flowers might last a generous hour, maybe two, with a minimal scent bubble. While I do enjoy the scent, the performance just ruins the whole experience for me.

I didn't think much of buying Chelsea Flowers. Before Chinatown, it was Bond's best-selling fragrance. My newly discovered obsession with perfumes and my imagined affinity for floral scents made me eager to grab it and buy Chelsea Flowers. But I regret it a little. Phew, it's even too floral for me. The hyacinth unfortunately does not create a weak scent aura on me, and all Bonds last forever on my skin and clothing. The scent offers nothing more than a bouquet of flowers. No depth, no interesting note, no playful interplay. To be honest, it's far too blunt, not niche at all, and not worth the money. The only standout is an extremely feminine aura that you radiate with it. But I don't want that at all. I can only recommend the scent to women who feel that they appear too little feminine, sometimes come across as hard and masculine, and want to do something about it. So the scent replaces the Wonderbra, as the cup size swells from A to at least D. And exactly this feminine fertility and readiness to bear children is something I don't like to carry around with me. I love feminine scents, but they need to have an interesting facet. Chelsea Flowers is just a blunt, American floral scent that mainly smells of rose, hyacinth, and tulip. The base remains invisible - I've never smelled it. I cannot find any similarity to Sun Flowers and L'eau d'issey contrary to my predecessors below. But that's a matter of opinion, as we know. So dear flower friends: there are better, more interesting, and cheaper options. I really cannot recommend this one at this price. It smells good, but that's it - you can safely do without this scent, as you won't miss anything. Edit: In hindsight, I read here that I really wrote a load of nonsense. Chelsea Flowers is floral and slightly herbaceous-woody. The association with Sun Flowers is 100% correct - I compared it again, but the Bond scent smells finer than Sunflowers.

I really wonder what the perfumers at Bond imagine when they create these little waters? Sometimes I think that if they spent a little less time on one or another scent and more time developing a perfume, it could work wonders. At first, one thinks this is a wonderful floral perfume, but it quickly becomes clear that these are not scent-intensive flowers, but rather rapidly cultivated blooms with a fleeting scent. If they had understood how to give the perfume body and some sillage, I would have gladly bowed to this brand for the first time, because fundamentally, Chelsea Flowers is a very beautiful scent concept, but unfortunately an unfinished one, in my opinion! Fresh blooms at the top, romantic flowers on the blouse, on a classic costume with subtle wood and moss notes as a base, that’s how one could imagine this flower seller. If only the flowers had a stronger scent! The overall impression comes across as a bit colorless. Michelangela, thank you for this fleeting floral rush!

Today, Chelsea Flowers floated into my home - bringing with it romance and joyful memories. The petals practically burst from the bottle - just like the autumn wind carries my rose petals, which form a cloud in the garden. One stands in the eye of the floral whirlwind, surrounded by mimosa, peony, and rose. A sweet, full aroma envelops me - yet bright and light. I am reminded a bit of Anais, but the impression of Chelsea is softer. The hyacinth is prominent, but not piercing, softened by the green moss. Vetiver and sandalwood further emphasize the soft, cloud-like quality of the fragrance. Chelsea is feminine and casually elegant - with a touch of romance and emotion. Despite its lightness, it lasts on me forever - which I attribute to all Bonds, and for this reason, I greatly appreciate this label. Even my husband wears a friendly expression and finds Chelsea harmonious for me. A very successful blind buy!

There isn’t really much to say about Chelsea Flowers. A nice, harmless, banal floral scent. Mercilessly copied from Elizabeth Arden. But unlike Sunflowers, it doesn’t last particularly long and the sillage is not exactly generous either.

Here comes a very inconspicuous floral scent (thanks to ET for the sample!). The magnolia is the most prominent note I can detect. Unfortunately, I can't pick out the hyacinth (once again) (does anyone know a perfume that really smells like hyacinth? I would appreciate recommendations!). The other flowers are somewhat overshadowed or create a floral blend.

I think the scent is great! Fresh, floral, not too intrusive. BUT!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! You can get it cheaper! It's called Sunflowers by Elizabeth Arden and it's one of my favorite teen fragrances! The more stylish bottle is definitely Bond, but paying so many euros more for it is really unnecessary!

Violets, synthetically woody green, but with this Byredo fabric that gradually enriches itself. It always smells a little different from others. Artificial but with a lot of body, sometimes more plant-like, sometimes like fermented fruit or almost like turpentine. This one is very dry, not fruity or anything like that. Ambrette adds body, musky-plant-like, woody. The scent sits very well on the skin. Like a cosmetic product that you have on you. “Off-White” fits in that it doesn’t smell like white flowers such as jasmine and not like a clean scent. It is, of course, exactly that at the same time. After about 20 minutes, the scent becomes a bit creamy, the wood smells slightly charred, and after a brief irritation, it smells very good. Targeted smokiness, so it doesn’t become too trivial. Woody-floral, creamy-powdery-smoky, yes exactly, nothing else. Just a hint of floral. I find it not so dissimilar to Narciso, by the way. But of course more “special.” And significantly more reduced. Seriously. This one is made for careful dosing, for passive perception like elevator music, which the scent is named after. One spray too much and too precise sniffing could tip the concept. Too much elevator music can also be hard to bear consciously. I enjoy this play with perception. And a bit of irony in the name is certainly allowed. After a few hours, I have gotten so used to the presence of the scent that a suddenly intense and sweeter hint rises to my nose as a surprise. In terms of composition, it’s a scent that you might initially think, Hmm? that smells pleasant. And it remains so, including a few pleasant surprises when the scent reminds you of itself. That’s quite an achievement. Unobtrusive, hip, and elegant. That’s it. Already sold out.

Dry down smells like a “modern” Cartier’s Oud & Musc. Meaning: less natural. Although it takes time to get to that point as this opens leathery suede-y with florals. I can see the faint connection to Jasmin Exclusiff. Overall, I’m not a fan of the opening but enjoy the dry down. My opinion is only based on a spritz on the back of my hand from a decant. I have both Oud & Musc and Jasmin Exclusiff.

tested today thanks to a sample, I wanted to discover this perfume which is distinguished by the black bottle. I find a strong similarity with layton and Pegasus from pdm as well as with ani and hacivat from nishane. After 5 jours a scent of sandal reveals and reminds me santal boisé Versace or 24 rue de l Université YSL. a fresh and aniseed opening, a mid-season fragrance with an average sillage and a huge hold of around 15 hours, the price is not justified, when we see that similar scents last longer and cost less.

So many shampoo/conditioner frags, and my hair is already so clean!!! Bond no 9 ANDY WARHOL UNION SQUARE fits squarely into this relatively new (twenty-first-century?) category and for that reason makes a perfect workplace scent, particularly for those attempting to evade the perfume police. The worst that anyone wearing this fragrance--which does not build-up and has a short lifespan and low sillage anyway--could be accused of is having recently showered. For some reason, I like these fragrances. But I also love to bathe. This one has just a touch of woodiness in the drydown, but the squeaky clean musk dusted with light sterilized florals really dominates from start to finish--a rather short course, I hasten to add. Given the speed with which I drained my sample vial, I'd say that this is closer to cologne than edp.

The days are getting shorter, the thoughts longer - and I'm troubled by a little ache in my back. Could the extreme autumn couching actually not be so beneficial? Physical activity would be good - yes, it would... In the midst of my musings, the DHL man rings the doorbell with the beautiful flower star. Wow - the scent really gets me moving! Surprisingly fresh, a cheerful lily of the valley greets me, paired with radiant freesia. A slightly invigorating citrus note envelops the floral arrangement - and the sun rises. However, the impression doesn't become too floral, as birch opens up with additional green freshness. Amber is soft and slightly sweet. The zesty citrus background remains intact. Cheered up and motivated, I dust off my Puma running shoes, as I'm in the mood for some outdoor movement. The dog is leashed, and we take a stroll. Power walking - instead of extreme couching. Union Square is an exceedingly delightful, subtly floral fragrance discovery - with a freshness kick and very good longevity.

a green-floral perfume, on one hand cool, then warm again, comes in a bottle inspired by Warhol's symbolic and legendary Flower Series. Pop Art meets Perfume this scent is very ..yes I would say hard to categorize .. unisex somewhere...flowery ..but also somewhere cool and fresh Just in the foreground lily of the valley, interwoven with accents of blue freesia, golden amber, and spheroid-clear, sensual musk - fresh-green, plant-like accords and birch wood nuances surprise and transform the scent into pure, clean energy it is indeed a very lively fragrance.. and one might suspect something different behind this bottle.. sweet fruity/floral.. but it is rather green..and clear..sparkling? but interesting and captivating in its own special way.

The rose is pretty prominent in this fragrance. But it's not a powdery rose. It's jammy and fruity. Fruits.... rose....a dash of oud in the dry down. Lean feminine. It definitely projects and sticks around like most Bond No. 9 fragrances. I like it.... don't love it. If you're a male who's not into fruits, rose or fragrances that lean feminine, do not purchase. I will wear it with confidence. If you like more masculine fragrances, do not purchase.

This Nomad opens with a bright, fruity rose with somewhat of a sparkling effect. Quickly overtaken by a synthetic oud and subdued by the earthy notes of sandalwood and orris. Rather than drying down, it almost feels as if the composition was forced down without truly unfolding; as it got to the point very quickly. Ironically, Nomad means "wanderer". The notes here did that exactly. A vibrant start with a more neutral end, delivering a faint vanilla-amber accord and left with a familiar powdery finish. On my skin, the final phase was a sweet and dusty rose. A decent introduction to the world of niche perfumery and elegant packaging. If there is a con at all, the price point outweighs the quality. Bond's Nomad smells good, and while longevity is excellent it relies entirely on aroma chemicals.

I never try super pricey perfume because I don’t want to fall in love with something I can’t afford, but my wife passed her sample of this on to me after she tried it and didn’t like it. I have never received more compliments on a perfume. Some of the notes in this, like rose and blackcurrant, don’t typically get along with me, but this doesn’t smell overly floral or fruity. Instead it’s fresh, ambery, woody, slightly spicy. It has layers. The perfect blend of masculine and feminine and suitable for all seasons. Lasts ALL DAY. I love it so much and, once I use up this sample, I will probably never wear it again, because I cannot justify spending that much on a bottle.

Personal: 9/10 – Fruity, amber, and oud-lite goodness. It's awesome and super easy to love. Mass appeal: 8.5/10 – Fruity ambers are easy to enjoy and carry a glamorous vibe. Still, the richness may be too sweet for some. Performance: 8/10 – Very strong projection and longevity. This clings and radiates well. Value: 5/10 – Bond pricing is notoriously high, and while this feels luxurious, it doesn’t justify the cost compared to alternatives. But, if you find it discounted or on Reddit, it's a solid bottle. Uniqueness: 7.5/10 – Fruity amber-oud blends are common in niche and designer lines. NoMad is VERY lovable and smooth, but not revolutionary. SCORE: 76/100 Full bottle buy? YES, if I found it discounted. It's one of my favorite fruity ouds. Blind buy? NO, it’s pricey so sample first. Otherwise, it's a very safe fragrance, honestly. Recommend? YES, if you want a glamorous, ambery fruity-oud fragrance and don’t mind Bond pricing. Date night? YES, it’s bold, sweet, and seductive enough for nighttime. Office safe? YES, it's a bit heavy, but I think a couple sprays would still do just fine. Pros: Loud fruity-amber presence, luxurious polish, strong performance, and smooth oud. Cons: Overpriced, a slightly generic DNA, and performance could be better. NoMad fits squarely into Bond’s glamorous, bold style. It's a little bit loud, very rich, and the oud and fruits blend so beautifully together that it *almost* earns its exorbitant price tag. It opens with a smooth red fruit accord, and the pear and vanilla and violet leaf almost morph into an apple note, to my nose. It's surrounded by a smooth, sweet, warm oud that's not barnyard-ey at all. The oud manifests as something a bit dry and papery, which I think is absolutely beautiful contrasted with the sweetness from the top. I think it's a beautiful blend that everyone needs to smell. Truly a masterpiece in the world of easygoing oud fragrances. You're hard pressed to find something this mass appealing and pleasant. Highly recommend. Review #140 in my fragrance journey – this fragrance I own as a decant

A fragrance that lasts a long time! Longevity and sillage are very good. For me, the scent has a sensually elegant quality. You get a beautiful sweet fruity rose here, accompanied by a gentle oud note. Yes, the fruitiness paired with oud can remind one of La Capitale. However, NoMad is much creamier and more softly blended, yet it does not lose its strength. NoMad is for the rose-oud lovers among us. A uniquely sensual, long-lasting fragrance for special occasions. Not a blind buy product. The bottle is not my favorite, it can easily tip over.

I'm at Abu Dhabi International Airport between flights and the new DFS shop carries a small range of Bond no. 9 frags … including this one! I get BIG Tuberose and Gardenia here … not listed in the pyramid, but I could be smelling a combination of Freesia, Rose and Orange Blossom. It's very nice!!! The Iris is strong after a few hours … in fact I am toying with buying this fragrance. Gonna put the brakes on … if it lasts all the way to my destination (a 7 hour flight) I will buy it on the way back. Will update.

I got to smell this last week, and it's so refreshing! Definitely unique perfume, love the freesia. I like Bond's other stuff, but I think that this is a good branch off from what they usually do, taking something that hasn't been built yet and building a scent off of that.

It took me a time to make up my mind about how to express my feelings about this new release of Bond no9 collection . RoseSasso is right when writting that Hudson Yards is different from the other perfumes by Bond no9. It has a freshness and persistent green sparkle to it . Yet this is not enough for me to qualify it as original or innovative. It is just very green, neon green for most of the time, in spite of the fact that it lists white and pink flowers . Wow! I have just found out what it looks like: a completely green rose! The perfume started with a strong dose of alcohol that scared me away, maybe the pink pepper did this to me and it was not pleasant. A hint of lily-of-the valley and freesia followed swiftly and died away and a green rose and orange blossom set in, close to the skin, not moving, not whispering not letting me connect with them at all. The longevity is modest. After about 3 hours there was a faint smell of rose. The Hudson River washed my perfume away. And gone it was!
Pretty bottle, the lychee and peony scents sound perfect in the mix. Maybe someone will buy this for me, birthday in a month?? :)

Yesterday, I stumbled into my favorite perfumery, feeling weak and downcast, as I had just visited my mom in the clinic. My dear mom, my fragrance sister in spirit, would have approved of this. We often went on scent tours to comfort and invigorate our minds and souls. Yesterday, there was an interesting program on TV featuring the Bochum fragrance professor Hans Hatt. My sales associate moistened a cloth with the green, hopeful star Hudson Yard. The floral-green aromas brought a bit of life back into my leaden limbs. Lily of the valley and freesia gently pushed the dark cloud away from my forehead. The orange blossom represents sunlight, and the iris softly caresses my cold cheeks. I breathe in this positive, welcoming scent deeply - and fervently hope that everything will be alright.

Pure, clean floral freshness. Slightly creamy-soapy, minimally green, and wonderfully fresh. The prototype of a scent that one associates with sweet innocence. But with endurance, decent projection, and sillage. And thank God, never overwhelming. Lily of the valley and freesia play the leading roles in this linear perfume. Perfect for spring. Incredibly optimistic.

I struggled for a little while with whether I should even write a comment about Hudson Yards, as I have mostly not really liked the previous Bond fragrances. The scent had just arrived at the perfumery in Innsbruck, and I didn't want to disappoint the charming saleswoman when she enthusiastically packed this sample into my bag.

When the light begins to change I sometimes feel a little strange A little anxious when it's dark Fear of the dark, fear of the dark I have a constant fear that somethings always near Have you run your fingers down the wall And have you felt your neck skin crawl When you're searching for the light? (Iron Maiden) Everyone has probably experienced it - what you expect shapes the experience. After a horror movie, the nighttime walk home or to the fridge feels different, more exciting, than after a comedy. Taste is also determined by expectations, as anyone can confirm who has ever taken a bottle from the fridge (or a carton) and, expecting apple juice, accidentally had milk in their mouth. Yuck! Though milk has its own right to exist. So why the long introduction... well, that's how I felt about Midnight Candy. The dark, simple, mysterious bottle evoked in me the association with the brilliant latex man from American Horror Story. The name suggested a shamelessly sweet, perhaps forbidden treat. And then this. A powdery, floral scent, pretty, delicately carrot-like iris, underlined with powdery, rich violet. Nice. A light purple floral bottle would have suited it too. I do like these scent notes, really, but this is not new. Black isn't either. And gloomy certainly isn't. Just a pleasant, powdery scent, more suitable for daytime than evening, and due to the delicate vanilla sweetness, also more feminine than masculine. In contrast to the ambitious presentation and the name, there is too little offered here, as I can't discern more development than iris-violet-sweet. It's not poorly made; it would be a wearable everyday scent for me, but absolutely nothing special. Did someone fear the darkness? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YsmTLkTRQdk (nice eighties :-))

I may be the only person to say this, but to me Bond no 9 WEST BROADWAY really smacks of cardamom. Well, at least today it does! Yes, there is lime rind. Yes, there is cedarishness, and those notes provide the dominant character of this fragrance to my nose. Yet there is an unmistakable waft of spice, which I initially thought might be nutmeg. After putting nose to wrist many times now, I have convinced myself that it is cardamom, as I keep having vague flashbacks to Kenzo JUNGLE L'ELEPHANT, the reigning champion of cardamom-centric perfumes. Do I like WEST BROADWAY? I have to say that I do. On some days, when I am more sensitive to the Bond woody base, this fragrance seems far more masculine than feminine, and even perhaps too masculine for me. On other days, the lime really sings. Today, in part because I am comparing this side-by-side to HAMPTONS, I am struck by the spiciness of WEST BROADWAY. Interestingly enough, the first time I reviewed this creation, I thought that I smelled incense. I invariably find it spicy, but the mystery remains: what accounts for the spiciness? It's not maté, which is listed in the notes. Having spent some time in Argentina, where maté is the national beverage, I can assert ex cathedra that maté has a very bitter green smell, which I really do not detect here at all. This is not to my nose a bitter green composition. In any case, overall, this is a refreshing scent, which I do recommend for testing by guys and gals alike. Obviously, if it smells so different every time I wear it, there is some complexity here, which I generally find to be a good thing in perfume. I have not seen very much commentary on this particular selection from the Bond no 9 line-up, and I'm not sure why except that it does fall into their large category of tweaked wood base fragrances. Probably no one really needs to have more than one of these, and many people complain that they all smell the same. This one does not, it seems to me, because of the unique combination of lime, linden, and, I believe, cardamom, which liven up the woody base quite a bit. I like it, despite its occasionally masculine-leaning tendencies.

It took a long time for me to truly fall in love with this scent. 2 years on the shelf without attention, previously a spontaneous purchase as an everyday fragrance, yet later it seemed simple and expressionless to me. I wanted to sell it!! Only this winter did my nose find the mature, almost masculine sweetness and the crystalline transparency truly appealing. I could almost hear the tone of the crystal glass... No chaos, no unrest, straightforward yet gentle, lily of the valley in a unique way, very mature, very strong, yet easily wearable for women (I don’t wear men’s fragrances), I can hardly smell the lime, possibly very well embedded. There is also something woody-dark that is not listed in the notes, but is definitely present and makes the scent heavier, because this is not about light, airy spring flowers. I have been wearing the scent almost daily lately, which in itself is a great compliment. A perfect olfactory understatement. p.s. I would place West Broadway and Straight to Heaven in the same category, with the former having "glass-like" associations and the latter "metallic" ones. So much for "I don’t wear men’s fragrances," although defining Straight to Heaven as a men’s fragrance is somewhat exaggerated.

Scentrack: Nicola Conte - A Time for Spring To fall in love, the phrase we often use to easy. Concerning Riverside Drive I use this phrase in the right context. Relatively simple, but charming fragrance. The smell of the late spring or early autumn. Strong green violet lea, cuisine basil and sweet pineapple mixed with patchouli and Roucel's lavender. The base is consisted of warm and transparent sandalwood, cedar and oak moss. It sounds very serious, but it's non formal and laid back. I suppose because of the funny pineapple. Riverside Drive gives me the vision of a walk in the fields during summer. I can feel some linden blossom, taking me to the early summer vibe full of hopes. This fragrance is my compliment getter No. 1. For people who cannot imagine love, Riverside Drive is Narciso Rodriguez for Him meets Cool Water meets Hypnose Homme (only much more). Rating: 7/10

Riverside Drive is a thoughtfully composed, buoyant, green/lavender aquatic men's fragrance.  It's a descendent of Cool Water, but it's not one of the cheap imitators hurled at the market since about a minute after Cool Water hit in 1988.  In its favor, Riverside Drive is more a reflection on Cool Water than an imitation.  It tones down the 'aquatic', turns up the green, and leads to a very well-balanced drydown.  The drydown, in fact, is what I think an armful of the Creeds of the last 20 years have strived for and missed. Poised, comfortable, stable. The drydown of these Cool Water wannabes, including the Creeds, is usually described as:  (synonym for nice) + "but, well, you know" + ( antonym of nice). Riverside Drive's drydown is likeable.  Actually, it's enviable. Coherent, harmonious, firm yet without aberrant sillage. Against it, it's a thoughtful version a hackneyed genre.  How much better than the worst, is the best grilled American cheese and white bread sandwich ever made?  I appreciate Riverside Drive for its composition, but am not interested in it. Who needs another descendant of Cool Water? (... asks the man with a closet full of green chypres. Spoiler alert: glass houses.)  But I do feel it is important to acknowledge quality work however it comes across your desk.  Not my bag, but outstanding.

"Riverside Drive" connects two extremes - something like "Aventus" with "Grey Flannel". Hard to imagine and certainly not great or even acceptable for every nose - but it undeniably has a certain cheap arrogance. Hairspray, violet pastilles, green meadow, a splash of exotic fruitiness - and there you have this danceable beast. A greeny gone astray. Undoubtedly unisex for me. A powerhouse in relaxation mode. Very 80s, very piercing, very much a matter of getting used to. But somehow still attractively enough. You definitely stand out as a man if you wear this often. Not everyone will like it - but a few will jump on it like Schmitz' cat. A bit trashy, a bit rough, a bit rockish, a bit shocking. And yet at its core, it's simply a dusty-spray green thing. Bottle: 2 - without stars Sillage: a bit above average Longevity: lasts longer than it leans - 8 hours Conclusion: a floral-piercing hairspray scent without too high expectations. Violets without really good bits. Price-performance ratio is of course outrageous. Somewhere between deodorant vibes and Drakkar. Nevertheless, it exudes a trashy-sympathetic 80s aura between aerobics and village disco. Green and bold.

Somewhere I once heard that Americans sell cheap gummy bears in candy stores at the same price as the finest pralines. After all, it’s all “candy” - and if it’s colorful, it can be appealing. Riverside Drive is like such a gummy bear. The outrageous prices of Bond No. 9 are best forgotten; otherwise, it’s no fun at all. Riverside Drive connects to the everyday scent experiences we know from cheap deodorants by Axe and Co. This synthetic scent has long since crept into our noses. It is, of course, miles away from what we know and appreciate in high-priced perfumes. It would be like comparing apples to oranges if one were to bring up solid Guerlain fragrances or experimental scents from Comme des Garcons. One cannot completely dismiss this synthetic scent direction - it is indeed sexy when worn by the right men or boys. And exactly those right boys and men have ensured that we find these fragrances sexy. Who says a scent should be beautiful? It just has to work! Good fragrances of this type can be found in the mid-price range, such as those from Hugo Boss. I think of Boss Bottled Night or the somewhat lesser-known Boss in Motion Edition White. And whether the respective scent is fresher or heavier, somewhat woody or even oriental - that doesn’t matter much in this style. It is this slightly alcoholic, perhaps attributable to musk or amber variants, synthetic quality that gives off the allure of cheapness. Even with Riverside Drive, the published fragrance notes are not that important. Whether the slight fruitiness really comes from pineapple, or the cool, floral note actually derives from lily of the valley, I don’t want to know too precisely. Because to find that out, one would have to sniff the scent intensely, and that would be downright unbearable. On the skin, a lot of what I call “scratchiness” develops, as we typically find in the cheaper to mid-priced perfumes from the big chains. Riverside Drive only works in projection, and there is plenty of it. This perfume has enough sillage to inform an entire office day of the presence of colleague Müller or Schmitz. And the further away one perceives Riverside Drive from the sprayed spot, the more attractive or, depending on one’s mindset, bearable the scent becomes. Because only at a distance does Riverside Drive come together. I like the masculine synthetic quality, which in this case is also accompanied by a certain herbaceousness (basil) and freshness. Add to that a hint of soapiness - and memories of barber shop scents come flooding back. Indeed, Riverside Drive is more like the misbegotten grandson of the barber from days gone by. Unfortunately, I don’t have the mentioned Boss fragrances on hand for a comparison test, but I can already say that Riverside Drive can hold its own against the best in its field - despite the unpleasant scratchiness with too close contact. For me, the case is not yet closed - a direct comparison with one of the Boss fragrances still needs to happen soon. Of course, one wonders who is supposed to wear this absurdly expensive New York scent? Perhaps the stock market speculator who slips into sneakers and a hoodie after the Wall Street closing to look cool?

Synthetic Muguet, citrus of a lemony nature, musky sweetness, cedar-ish, aldehydes. Light airy, fairly synthetic florals, ruled by a lily of the valley, like an old fashioned cologne initially, but then this changed slightly on dry down. The florals receded and the fragrance moved down a notch to pleasant but dull. Smelled woodier on me with cedar like notes and completely different on a friend, more vanilla and musky on her. It was hard to determine many notes in this perfume. It went soapy very quickly and the overall longevity was very poor. Very uninspiring, but having then seen the name, realised it was a fragrance presumably meant to represent goodness and virtue. Well it certainly does manage that. (I'm blind testing a series of ELdO samples, so these reviews are from nose notes.)

There are a few words in Japanese that are difficult or only approximately translatable into other languages, e.g. 'Karoshi' = sudden death from overwork (usually, but not necessarily a heart attack, although the Japanese word for heart attack is completely different) or 'Chikan' = the act of 'rubbing' against complete strangers (mostly women) in the crowded subway. 'Enjokosai' describes the phenomenon where (school) girls - often exaggeratedly cute, in Japanese 'kawaii' - spend time with significantly older, wealthy men. It often amounts to nothing more than some fondling - and she does not receive money for it, but rather items like Prada shoes or a Vuitton handbag, which are often purchased together as part of the time spent together - so that neither party perceives themselves as a prostitute or a client. Of course: not every cute-looking Japanese girl with a Hello Kitty or Sailor Moon backpack engages in 'Enjokosai'! Etat Libre d'Oranges Don't Get Me Wrong Baby, I Don't Swallow (one of my favorite names from the niche perfumer from the Marais, alongside the somewhat disappointing scent Fat Electrician) plays with its floral-innocent sweetness, which does not seem to fit its vulgar-provocative name, with a very similar connotation. The floral notes are equally charming and enchanting, yet not lustful or even lascivious. On the contrary, it comes across as quite innocent and naive - despite the jasmine and lily of the valley. This innocence is supported by the sugary notes that follow - almond and chocolate - and a skin accord of musk and patchouli that is only perceptible at the end. Nothing sinful or dirty develops from this scent - which its name had essentially clarified from the very beginning. Conclusion: not a grand or very complex fragrance, sweetly charming in its essence and certainly attractive to those who enjoy floral and gourmand scents - and who are not put off by its decidedly unpoetic-subtle name. Those who expect a naughty, possibly obscene scent based on this name will undoubtedly be disappointed.

Hello everyone, welcome to a new fragrance comment from me… Hmm… yes… there are fragrance names that I should approach with caution, as these names are practically destined for me to flip out, write silly nonsense, and have my entire review (once again) removed… :DD But seriously now… THIS NAME?,… which translates to “I don’t swallow”? Aaaaaarghghghgghg… :DDD Basically, I don’t care if a woman, um… arghhghg, do you see?! DO YOU SEE??? I didn’t want to start with that, but this FRAGRANCE NAME, you just can’t help it, especially when the fragrance name actually expresses exactly WHAT it sounds like!!! Okay, okay, better think of something else quickly before I (that is, I!) completely flip out here: … fragrances… … R2-D2... … cats… :) … Delicious cake with… uh… icing on top? Aaaaaaaaaaaaaaargh noooooo!!!! … I knew it, the fuses are blowing, or it’s just warm here… :DDD The name here is worse or more intense than the name of another fragrance from this brand, namely the well-known Palace Whore (ha ha how that sounds again, I’m of course talking about the fragrance “Putain des Palaces,” which translates to Palace Whore!). But okay, I’ll smell it first. Because usually, fragrance names are much more provocative than the scent itself, as you have to stand out in the market somehow. The fragrance listing at least sounds quite nice. Among other things, there are many flowers like jasmine, orange blossom, and lily of the valley, but also other things like marshmallows. All ingredients whose components, like flowers, have a… white or milky color or whose consistency… is sticky… argh!… let’s quickly move on to the scent description :D The scent: You can immediately smell all the flowers like jasmine, neroli, and lily of the valley right from the start. It smells floral sweet and slightly herbaceous. A vanilla-like sweetness also appears in the background, but that could also result from the mix of jasmine and the listed cocoa as well as the marshmallows. However, this impression fades after the top notes. Shortly thereafter, you can smell the patchouli, which gives the scent a slightly earthy touch alongside the floral notes. But that also remains rather in the background for the rest of the scent journey, as the floral and sweet notes are always in the foreground. Therefore, you can also clearly smell the sweet musk as the scent develops. But otherwise, it remains consistently floral, which is okay, but this especially in the late base, when the sweet notes become weaker, gets a bit on my nerves. Because like many other floral fragrances, this scent here also starts to smell a little stuffy, which I really don’t like, and then it’s high time to either wash off the scent or at least reapply it. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is average to actually rather weak, as the scent becomes quite inconspicuous shortly after application. Anyone wanting to smell the fragrance would have to get quite close. I also found the longevity to be only average at about six hours. That may not sound bad, but most of the time the scent is very weak in its projection. The bottle: The bottle is rectangular and colorless. Notable for this brand is the round label that stretches from one side of the bottle to the other and looks like a target or an air force badge. The cap is chrome-plated and cylindrical. Overall, it’s quite simple, but the round label gives the bottle a distinctive appearance. Conclusion: Well… that was my scent impression. And I must say that everyone who expected an erotic, tingling, sexy, or any other scent with slightly dirty undertones (or at least distinctive notes) will be terribly disappointed. This fragrance has none of that; on the contrary, it comes across as rather pure with its lovely and sweet floral scents. I even think that the scent has a rather innocent, virginal aura (maybe this is also intended as a gag for this fragrance name). And it doesn’t really have much to offer. In my opinion, it’s nothing particularly special, as it doesn’t stand out from many other floral fragrances, so it could almost fit into the category “if you know one, you know them all.” It has no real strengths, but (aside from the weak sillage) also no real weaknesses, well, maybe just the slightly stuffy base. Because it smells quite nice and is especially suitable as an everyday companion in spring. Only the name is a bit provocative, but it could also serve as a funny gift for girls you get along well with and who also have a good sense of humor or something. Otherwise, as I said, it’s quite nice, but you won’t miss anything if you don’t try it out. And that’s it from me! I wish you all a lovely evening and see you next time :)

(Unfortunately, I couldn't help but express my associations with this name in this way. It's just too tempting. I apologize for that...) "I don't swallow" in the title has once again kept me from testing the fragrance for a long time. I am still processing the trauma I experienced from testing Secretions Magnifiques, and I am cautiously approaching the other EldO scents. But as clearly ambiguous as the name is, the fragrance is wonderfully feminine, delicious, and wearable. Surprise, surprise! Even the top note is worship-worthy. However, where others hear the bells of lily of the valley, I find myself in an orange blossom bath, with a slight jasmine undertone and a hint of aldehydic soapiness. As it develops, candied roses and just a touch of patchouli come into play; the fragrance is neither sweet nor heavy, but remains floral-fruity-fresh. I never would have expected that, despite knowing the pyramid. The base makes it slightly gourmand, as there is a brief moment of a dry cocoa note, which I unfortunately cannot detect almond from, and the cocoa does not dominate but - again surprisingly for me - the fragrance cuddles up with an orange musk soapiness. Wonderful, and just right for today. A pick-me-up.

The name is the most provocative and pornographic in the entire range of fragrances from Etat Libre d'Orange, or ELdO for short. So what lies beneath? A surprisingly charming, contemporary, light-filled, and fresh white floral composition with a clear dominant lily of the valley note. Antoine Maisondieu laid it on a fresh musk background, added a touch of the bitterness of jasmine, and the sweetness of orange blossom, creating a small floral masterpiece. For fans of Diorissimo looking for a modern incarnation, "Do not Get Me Wrong" is a delightful surprise. Even though the scent is not particularly original, with a rather banal theme, overall made with quite ordinary ingredients - it is virtuously staged by a worthy champion! A very beautiful women's fragrance, although probably not all ladies want to wear a perfume with such an obscene name, which is understandable. ;-) I think that’s the joke - the combination of this fresh, charming, purely feminine scent with this provocative name. If a man were to smell it on you and ask what you’re wearing, I would recommend saying: Lilly of the valley (since that’s not really a lie) That sounds worlds better than: Don’t get me wrong baby, I don’t swallow - at least for the first rendezvous! ;-) Composition: Jasmine, lily of the valley, orange blossom, amber, patchouli, cocoa, musk, aldehydes, marshmallow

What did I expect from a perfume with such a name? I find it amusing. "Don't get me wrong, baby, I'm not swallowing." What is this going to be? A great start, but somehow a disappointing or sobering end? What did I expect and hope for in terms of scent? Well, I expected something unusual, spectacular. I hoped it wouldn't smell like one might assume.

The name of the perfume raises the question of how or what might be happening until there is a refusal to accept whatever it is? Well, I suspect it probably has to do with a puff of air that should not be fully released.

Here it is again, another review of a brand that is mostly hated with prices that are far too high. Why? Because it happened again, I couldn't resist and had to smell it. And it started off so well. I tried some Bonds, found some wonderful scents, became curious, and searched for more on Parfumo. That's when I noticed this beautiful bottle with the fine name Nolita - named after North Little Italy, a part of New York. As it often goes with the hunt for fragrances, when there are no samples available, curiosity grows even more, despite the bad reviews, especially when the ratings are sometimes good and sometimes bad, I felt the urge to form my own opinion about the scent. Unfortunately, I couldn't find anything on Parfumo and ordered a way too expensive sample elsewhere. I was so excited when it arrived. Quickly unpacked, sprayed, and... Bäääääääh, what is this? Hairspray, piercing synthetic notes, children's perfume, yes yes I read all of this here, yet I was surprised and slightly annoyed. Is that really it? But no, of course not. After numerous tests, I should know better, Bonds are not easy fragrances, they need to be tested, explored, they are very fussy and moody. So I did it, with a slight tendency for self-torment, I kept trying the scent over and over again. And what can I say, it was a disturbed trip :) This fragrance has a lot going on - sometimes it spat out the Schauma apple shampoo from my childhood, sometimes it smelled super authentic like freesia, as if from the flower shop. When it was hot, the jasmine flowers came through as authentically as in my Ashore . Then the synthetic notes were back, sometimes hairspray. Then again flowers full of mandarin pieces, sometimes it was mandarin juice. And again and again the beautiful base full of clean musk and noble woods came through. With this fragrance, I feel clean, freshly shampooed, girly, younger, just cheeky and flirty. The synthetic notes fade quickly and the flowers come: sometimes lily, sometimes jasmine, sometimes freesia, sometimes all together, sometimes this way, sometimes that way, a young moody lady who hasn't quite found herself yet. The bottle design fits the scent very well. I was also transported back to my youth, feeling like the Nolita again, not yet formed and not quite decided. I found it nice to briefly give up the control and pressure of adulthood with this fragrance. And what can I say, it does something to you. Naturally, you want to have such a little water with you. It is definitely a love at second sniff.

A feminine and quiet composition, this fragrance unfolds gently around soft white‑floral accords that feel serene and airy. There is a subtle green nuance woven through the bouquet, adding a touch of freshness without disturbing its calm character. As it settles, the perfume rests on a skin‑like, powdery base that enhances its tender, intimate nature. Nothing here is loud or demanding—the sillage stays beautifully subdued, close to the skin, creating a personal aura that feels almost like a natural extension of the wearer. Its understated elegance lies in its simplicity: a soft, harmonious blend that remains steady and comforting, perfect for those who appreciate fragrances that whisper rather than shout.

I've been looking at this fragrance for a number of years and read many reviews compare this to Bond Central Park West. A lot of reviews claim they smell very similar, but after picking up a travel sprayer of it, and doing a side by side, I have to disagree. To my nose the only thing they have in common is that they are both big, extravagant florals. While both are big flower bonanzas, Central Park West is heavier, louder, richer, more sensuous, and much more extroverted and over the top. It's a great perfume for a night on the town. While this is loud too, the fresh, clean profile makes it more wearable for day, if used judiciously. So, right off the bat, besides having a different feel about it, it is more versatile than West as it can easily go from day to night. Also, West is more cold weather wear while this seems more geared to warm weather. I couldn't imagine wearing West in the summer as it is so heavy and dense, I think it would choke me out and everyone else within the vicinity. As to this fragrance, it is white florals at their peak of bloom right after a spring rain. Some think it has a cleanliness to it, as if you just got out of the shower, and I can see that too though it is not shampooey in the least. There's just the tinniest hint of fruitiness that adds freshness, but this is not a fruity floral either nor is it listed in the notes. But I am picking it up, though not in the way most fruity florals are done today where the fruity notes are much more pronounced and a feature of the scent. If I were to make a comparison to any Bond fragrance, it would be Earth Day, in that it has that same clean, shower fresh aspect, though it does lack Earth Day's creaminess which I prefer. But while I like this scent, (and Bond CPW), I don't love it. For this type of scent profile, I prefer something like Estee Lauder's Pleasures or Beyond Paradise, or even Bond's Earth Day. Still, if you are looking for a big fresh white floral you should give this a shot as it is not only very pretty but performs wonderfully too. I will use up this travel sprayer next spring and summer, which I think will be perfect that time of year but will not replace with a bottle when it is done.

The moment I applied Bond no 9 CENTRAL PARK SOUTH, I was reminded of CENTRAL PARK WEST. Why? Because the big floral parade of narcissus, jasmine, and ylang-ylang is once again on display. It's becoming pretty clear that Laurice Rahmé (the creative director of this house) loves narcissus, as when it figures in one of her perfumes, it tends to steal the show. Another example: HARRODS ROSE, which is more about narcissus and ambrette than it is about rose, at least according to my nose. Once again, in CENTRAL PARK SOUTH, we have a somewhat overwhelmingly floral creation which is probably not going to appeal to many guys, nor any gals who dislike CENTRAL PARK WEST. I'm wondering about this launch, actually. It's the first from Bond no. 9 in more than six months, and it seems like a permutation or Lego launch. The core of CENTRAL PARK WEST is here, plus some new notes, but because the core is so strong, it doesn't really matter much which other notes were switched out for new ones. I can recommend this composition to all and only those who love CENTRAL PARK WEST. Narcissus, jasmine, and ylang are once again here in abundance!

My first impression of 'Huge Navel' is that it is a unisex patchouli+resin combination. I get about 40% patchouli, 30% opoponax (sweet myrrh) & balsam, 10% vetiver and 20% of other things, such as a little carrot seed in the top and some pepper after that. It is nothing like most patchouli or resin bombs because this isn't a bomb. After 15 or 30 minutes, the sillage dies down and it becomes quite a soft scent. I get good longevity but there's little sillage during that time. This fragrance didn't wow me but it's still an okay scent because the notes in the drydown are quite well combined.This scent is just 'a little bit of Nirvana'

I'm mighty glad that I chose to order a sample of Nombril Immense amongst the vast array of enticing Etat Libre d'Orange scents. I knew just by glancing at the scent pyramid that I would love it. Nombril Immense sounds so beautiful when spoken in French, but the rough translation to English is huge navel, or belly button. Well, if belly buttons smelt this good, you wouldn't be able to drag my nose away from one. I can assure you, Nombril Immense is an oriental with a lovely blend of patchouli and opoponax. When I first applied this fragrance to my wrist, I was met with an intense, spicy burst of patchouli and opoponax. I was left wondering how people could describe this fragrance as subtle. However, after a few minutes, Nombril Immense did indeed become subtle. So subtle, that at times it was hard to detect. I enjoy loud scents, so I would be lying if I said that I wasn't disappointed by Nombril Immense's weak sillage. I often rectify this problem by over-spraying, and I find that the more I layer the scent, the stronger it in turn becomes. Other than the dominant accords of patchouli and opoponax, other notes that I can detect quite strongly on my skin are pepper, peru balsam and vetiver. I think this fragrance could wear well on both men and women, and is best suited to wear during Autumn and Winter. By all means, if patchouli often gives you a headache or offends you with its dominance, you may want to give Etat Libre d'Orange Nombril Immense a try. I'm certain that many will find themselves enjoying this fragrance's unique subtlety. I highly recommend. Original review written: September 2012.

Questo e l'ombelico del mondo! Anyone remember that Jovanotti song? It's what I start singing whenever I see this tiny bagged sample that I was excited to receive in 2014 and then never fished out of my patchouli sample box, distracted as I was by other shiny things to smell and think about. Seems it was enough for me to see its name to be fond of it, this huge bellybutton that is the bellybutton of the world. But its time has finally come. The beginning caused me some mild excitement, with its silky burp of gripe water - cushioned cottony musk, lavender, the plush dillwater billow of sweet, laundered air, a hint of sticky booze. Kind of like Helmut Lang EDP or Annick Goutal's Musc Nomade but less carnal. But the sweet, cozy-powdery mastic incense scent soon slides into something a little earthier and rotty-smelling, like orange peels left to decay on a wet log. The patchouli doesn't smell at all like Angel, but there is something of Mugler's famous 'moldy dishrag' accord that lingers here. Possibly, it is the slightly dirty 'orange and clove pomander' aspect of opoponax that is producing and urging along this unfortunate effect. Perhaps it is the old age of my sample that is at fault. I do sense a teeny, tiny bit of the intense, aftershavey lavender-and-clove spiciness that opoponax always brings (a wee drop of Old Spice) and a midge of sweat, but none of its golden, baby-powder-ish Shalimar-ness, which is a pity because that's the part of opoponax that I really love. Anyway, the upshot of all this is that Nombril Immense turned out to be infinitely more enticing to me while it was still trapped in its sample and swimming around aimlessly in my sample box than on my skin.

Patchouli... my nemesis. I could never fall in love with a patchouli scent, I thought. Until the first spray of Nombril Immense. A powerful, deep, and emotionally touching fragrance, striking... no: shocking! Nombril Immense did not seduce me slowly, but rather overwhelmed me with a bang. Peppered, with a slight fruity touch and from the very beginning patchouli-dark, the overwhelming begins. Then, further facets of patchouli unfold: there’s a smoky touch, a leather touch, and I also think I can smell an underlying lavender, while a very thin citrus note survives the start and becomes a close companion to the main note. Never too drastic, never so uncompromisingly overbearing as patchouli can be, yet always strong and characteristic. From the middle on, an aspect of vetiver adds a surprising smile (and once again makes one understand a typical ELdO name): Nombril Immense is the opposite of fresh laundry and freshly showered scents! Fragrant, smooth sheets, linen or soft cotton on the skin, bodies refreshed by water, young, virgin, just washed off the soap, cleaned, clear... exactly the opposite of that! Nombril Immense does not smell dirty, disgusting, sweaty, fishy, rancid, or anything else that might come to mind under the heading "unclean." But still, it is a clear rejection of fresh-body concepts. The sheets AFTER the night. The body BEFORE the water. That is Nombril Immense. Incredibly sensual and physical, but not in a directly sexy, urgent way. More like a Sunday morning in bed: still cozy, still sleepy. A lazy stretch when the bed is still warm. Wonderfully unshowered.

Myrrh, mint, and sage? I feel like I've had more than enough of that before. Did my dentist, Dr. Opoponax, once polish my face with that stuff? The nose never stops learning, even while brushing teeth. And anyone who knows the cassette of Karius and Baktus knows how to properly brush their teeth. Namely in circular motions from top to bottom. And while doing that, the white gold sometimes splashes against the mirror, onto the ceramic, and even sometimes all the way to the belly button. (Hence the name) When gargling, that is, in the finish, Listerine Nombril Patchouli tastes incredibly spicy, resinous, and incense-like, providing a long-lasting, fresh breath that must trigger a uniquely erotic, balsamic high when kissing your beloved. Louce, if THAT is your skin scent, then definitely with tongue! ;)

I haven't written a comment here in a long time - today I thought this one deserved a comment...:) Not that other fragrances don't deserve it, but this one has particularly captivated me. I'm not writing because the scent is extraordinarily wearable for men or exceptionally beautiful. Unisex here is, for me, a slip-up; the fragrance represents pure femininity. I find it funny that the scent reminds me of a now legendary fragrance here - namely Mugler's original Alien, the first version for women. HOWEVER: While the original Alien came across as very clumsy and loud, this fragrance is the noble, quiet, and graceful variant. The scent notes are very (!) similar, but they don't impose themselves like the original Alien. However, I almost only smell the typical Mugler DNA here, which indeed reminds me of an excess of Jasmine Sambac. The Heliotropia is also a sea of flowers, but combined with other white blossoms and a creamy white pear. I find it nice that the jasmine significantly decreases in the scent progression, making it still wearable for men. In the office, it's an absolute no-no-no-go - I will definitely wear the Heliotropia a few times in my free time...:) After many of the recent creations from Byredo left me somewhat disappointed, I really like this one...:)

This 'bad girl' isn't popular, I'm trying to find out why. This fragrance's character is in the raspberry and incense. I should say: the bubblegum and incense, because it doesn't smell like a real berry, more like berry flavoring. The incense is a bit hazy. A few hours in, these two notes have subsided enough so that the soft base notes peek out: a little vanilla, lily of the valley and airy musk. Reminiscent of cheap, fresh drugstore edt's, in a good and fresh way. The reason she doesn't hang out with the cool kids: She's neither this nor that. Not a bad girl, not a sweet girl, not a church girl. At some point the bubblegum blends with the incense, getting synthetic. Not unpleasant, but not appealing either. Want a bad girl perfume that combines sweetness with something else? (it's unisex enough by the way) I suggest you look at Boudoir, Divin'Enfant or Tubereuse Animale first. Nice touch: lily o/t valley used in an original way. But, try before you buy!

Out of the bottle, this smelled like bubblegum and cigarette smoke. Nothing else. Mind you, I LOVE the smell of tobacco. But this wasn't even tobacco. Just the stinky smoke part of a cigarette after it's been burned and perhaps tossed into an ashtray. I love incense but couldn't detect it on my skin either. Just the stinky smoke. I think this was a great idea on paper but, in reality, it fell apart. The incense note is a stinky type of smoke and not "true". The bubble gum is too strong and cheap. I couldn't even appreciate the sweetness of it. Besides, they didn't blend well. Like a psychotic dual personality, they seem to struggle for domination from the first spritz and all the way to the end. Not for me. Too bad... I was SO excited about this and now my hopes are kind of dashed.

Incense and chewing gum: Like checkered lily of the valley! Oh yes, apparently lily of the valley is also represented in this... Where is the intersection? What connects the two? Better, I smell the olfactory artwork that bears this name first. The top note was definitely chewing gum, sweet, synthetic, and sticky. But as a fan of 80s and US celebrity scents, I'm used to quite a bit and even find the fragrance pleasant. The heart note after an hour, or maybe more, I didn't check the clock: No chewing gum, no Hillary Duff, not even Mariah Carey. A slightly sour floral note, with incense in the background. I attribute the sourness to the raspberries; it can't be my beloved orange blossom, I would bet my life on it! A slight earthiness hovers above, the scent has made a 180° turn from plastic / kitsch to sacred. Interesting. Is this a synonym for "two souls in one breast"? Or the two faces that everyone has - Mother Teresa and Hitler? Or am I thinking about this completely unnecessarily? The longevity is, as with all the EldOs tested so far, very good. After a few hours, the musk comes through and lets the fragrance cuddle up. Strange, but not bad. Definitely wearable!

If you hurry, you smell: Bubblegum. This white variety that wants to be chewed soft and blocky, not the spearmint scent of the narrow strips. The ones with which you can really blow big bubbles. Is it my nose or the scent, but I hardly have time to dive into the pros and cons of a fragrance that I initially can hardly classify as an extended "body attractor" (that is, both pleasant and attractive). The question of whether I can experience bubblegum scent as a positive representation of myself (or at least the mood I am in) resolves itself somewhat: The bubblegum bubble bursts quite quickly, and only those who know, know that there was once something white-pink. In a scent that now remains in the green-violet. Lily of the valley? Possible, but one that has planted itself right next to a berry wood. The beauty is, there is hardly any sweetness left in this scent bastard, the bitterness is warm and spicy. I like! Vanilla may be the ingredient that intensifies everything a bit like sugar in an otherwise spicy dish, but as a standalone it is not perceivable. Orange blossom, peach, raspberry are probably responsible for the bubblegum phase, at best the peach can still be sensed later. It remains to be noted how persistent the scent is: incense and lily of the valley linger for a long time before Encense et Bubblegum completely surrenders to the incense-musk mix. And then the surprise: At the end, the bubblegum scent returns. Like a shadow of the beginning, very, very subtle, designed at the edge of perception, it conquers the surrounding 50 centimeters of airspace. However, the scent does not linger in the air for long; directly on the body, the incense note can still be detected for several hours. Encense et Bubblegum is an unusual scent cocktail that does not fit every mood. But as a change, it is quite suitable for daytime use, perhaps not necessarily in the office due to the rather dominant incense, and rather on cool days and for the neck, as the musk component is also distinctly noticeable. The sillage is not worth mentioning, but a pleasant hint remains close to the body. However, those who do not like incense should keep their hands off the bottle - the name is somewhat of a camouflage cap. So be careful: sugary and floral like bubblegum, the scent is by no means. Encense et Bubblegum may also be quite selective regarding different skin types (see below), and due to the unusual mix of high incense content with green note, I advise against an untested "blind" purchase :) Addendum: Guys (and gals?), who use this scent: Maybe it's the different hormonal cocktail that makes the scent develop such unpleasant biting tendencies? Having become aware of the comments here, I waited for the appearance of the stinky components - and didn’t quite find them. I mean, at about 30 cm distance, I sense a slight hint of acidity in the incense-lily of the valley. Whether I would have perceived this as an accompaniment to the scent without you is questionable.

FyBender and all fans of this fragrance, don’t be mad, but I’m going to tear this ELdO scent apart a bit! Actually, I like experimental fragrances and this scent should really appeal to me, as I said: ACTUALLY! Well, the top note is relatively harmless! Orange blossom with a hint of raspberry. But then it gets thick! EeB also takes a turn for me, or as they like to say in Swabia: a roll! I spread the sweet-stinging smell of beer pee! Sorry for my choice of words, but I can’t describe this smell any other way! Yuck! What is responsible for this pub-urinal note, I can only guess. With the onset of the incense, the image of a drunk person comes to mind, who can’t find the toilet in a church and ends up taking a beer pee in the sacristy! Only late in the base does the aforementioned "note" fade and a pleasant incense note spreads. Well, one swallow doesn’t make a summer, as they say. I’m still looking forward to the other fragrances from this brand!
...one of my dearest. This is always confirmed to me when I use it. Everyone feels POOCH-WELL in my presence and drawn to me.

The cloud upon spraying is initially pure bubblegum, but just as quickly as it appears, that pure note is gone again. However, it’s not an unpleasant note; rather, it’s a very pleasant scent of bubblegum that feels quite authentic.

the scent starts fruity, but then takes a sudden turn. If it's chewing gum, it must have been there briefly at the beginning. A strangely spicy smell - underlaid with musk - emerges, must be the incense in combination with? I am spontaneously reminded of a pepper-salt mixture.

Hello ! Can anyone out there hear me ? By any chance ? Finally, a human. Hello, nice to meet you, my name is Bond no.9 I love NY for Holidays. I am a bit shy but if you'll stick around, you'll know that I am a sweet chocolatey friend. Chocolatey, gourmand and citrusy at first. Yes I have a sweet taste and I usually give that yummy sensation. After a while I'll turn a bit floral/woody maintaining that sweet taste. My uniqueness is based on a combo of apricot & pomegranate. I knew it, I am quite unique. Told ya. In the end you'll still find me sweet but also a bit leathery and mature. I had to do this for a higher mass appeal, right ? My lifespawn will be easily 8 hours with a well enveloped presence. You'll know when I am around, be sure of that. I would love to meet you again on colder days & nights, that's when I can do my best for you and I'm shining the most. I am a bit pricy but forget about that fancy dress or those balenciaga shoes you had your eyes on. I am less than that and still worth more. Please let your friends know about our meeting. I want to meet more people, either men & women. Now you see how friendly I am. Thank you for stopping by ! Until we meet again, take care ! Overall : 8/10

Antihéros really is a great lavender. It starts with a pungent grassy lavender, very invigorating, like the essential oil with the addition of green woods (if there is something like that) and maybe fresh cut hay. I feel this lavender instead of being the relaxing type, clears the mind and wakes the senses. The raw lavender note morphs into something wonderful. Antihéros becomes a linear fragance then that is frankly a pleasure to wear. It is a softer lavender, keeping its aromatic, balsamic aspects, but doesnt feel as piercing as others i have smelled. Like a superfine soap. It reminds me to the opening in Dior Homme. There, the lavender overlaying the iris is very ephemeral, but in Antihéros the effect of a powdery lavender lasts all the time. I am not sure if it contains any orris, but there is a familiar polished butteriness. As for the woods, this are dusty and soft (no "radiant" aromachemicals) The key, i think, is the type of musk used for the base: clean, bordering to the laundry softener, that, believe me, is genius in here. Its neutrality is deliberate. The sillage is moderate, but the scent is light, unintrusive and classy. I see it as a great day perfume. Antihéros is a refined and solicitous fragance, unapologetic about its functional spirit (clean, fresh) and assertive elegance. This house surprise me with the outstanding quality of the fragances i have tried so far, and in this case proves they can make an interesting, different version of an overlooked, underestimated genre.

This is like a photorealist painting of lavender in a modern art gallery. Like a simile of it without being it. There is a clean minty camphorous note with a sweeter undertone of an almost caramellic nature. A massive dose of a soaring aldehyde, warm woods. null of the mud of real lavender. There is a really clean and cold draft going on. Like a huge empty space. Definitely minty. Something softer and mossier, greenish leafy sharp. Maybe galbanum but a mere jot. Then there is a musky softness like clean laundry, almost citrus in it's nature. Softening from lemon to bitter oranges. A creaminess about the underneath like clean freshly laundered soft sheets that have been sprayed with lavender and then ironed over with the edge of the metal iron crisping it to sharp. Yet the cotton is the best and softest Egyptian cotton. Really very nice and bright. Quite unexpectedly so. Crispy, clean and office suitable. Not my normal like but I love it.

Yes, ELDO is trendy and hip and different. Their shop in Paris looks more like a small gallery and the saleswomen with the obligatory lip piercings could have come straight out of an independent magazine. The lady also found the right words for Antiheroes: "Anti-Heros is kind of simple." And she didn't understate that. It's just, as Luca Turin rightly writes, simply lavender. Aha. If I wanted lavender, I would recommend Dupont Noir, but certainly not this one.

Finally, the house État Libre d'Orange has chosen a fitting name for one of its perfumes. Antihéros first conveys to me a coumarin-like, musty sourness, malty notes with minty undertones. This strikingly resembles the scent notes released by lavender flowers that have been stored in a container for a long time. The protagonist of so many perfume compositions reduced to its banal, less appealing aspects? What has been created here is not an aestheticization of a natural aroma, but a powerful highlighting of the ordinary/ugly in the scent of lavender. This approach and the means (flatness, rough strokes, graininess, and the mythologizing secularization of myths) fit, in my opinion, very well with the pop-art image that État Libre d'Orange wants to convey. Ironically, the overall impression is more pronounced and rougher, one could also call these attributes masculine, than the commonly used representations of lavender in perfumes. For me, a great pleasure.

The fragrances from Etat Libre d´Orange do not exactly enjoy the easiest reputation in the Parfumo community. And actually, after everything I’ve read about it, I would have preferred to steer clear of it. I only came across Antihéros because I solved part of the September puzzle and won it from a nice and generous Parfumo member. OK - not exactly the whole bottle, but definitely more than a regular fragrance sample. When I briefly sniffed it, I was almost knocked back. I did not expect such a piercing smell of industrial cleaner and clear varnish. I would have suspected that the contents had been spoiled or swapped with any other "fragrance brand" - but with ELdO, pure provocation seems to be the program. When I then wanted to drizzle a bit on my hand and accidentally dampened my tablecloth and various newspapers, the tide turned. Antihéros suddenly didn’t seem so intense anymore, but rather metallically cool and synthetically fresh. Thus, a welcome alternative to the usual summer scents… Today was not exactly a suitable day for my endeavor, but since I fear it will soon get colder and more wintry, I poured Antihéros on the back of my hand and neck. For me, that was quite a heroic act, as the scent still initially comes across as extremely synthetic and unsexy. I hoped that everything would quickly develop for the better, but one has to wait a long time for that. Only after many, many minutes did it become more bearable and thus wearable. There it was, that metallic cool synthetic fresh note that makes Antihéros unique. However, it really is an extremely narrow path between “terribly bad” and “not so uninteresting at all.” I perceive nothing of woods and musk - lavender is already a bit more noticeable. After two hours, the scent had settled somewhat and seemed relatively pleasant. Shortly thereafter, it had already completely evaporated. Among people, I felt a slight unease, but after several reapplications, one could get through Wednesday unscathed. However, there were neither compliments nor insults. But the wearer of this strange extract is by no means an anti-hero, rather brave, clueless, or stuffy…

"The antihero is an expression of the modern subject in all its societal ambivalences and antitheses; its existence is almost based on its ambivalences ..." (ff., wiki) Antihero, expression, ambivalences, antitheses, ambivalences. An existence of the modern subject. Man, that's me!

Interesting composition. I get lots of violet and greenery of angelica in the opening. It's a powdery and serious fragrance. I mean business meeting, presenting to the public at some convention. Leather and iris take over after 2 hours so if you love your powdery iris, this specimen is pretty good to investigate. Opening is unisex, after 4-5h starts to lean more masculine. No detectable oud in here, was a bit disappointed about that. Season fall-winter. Longevity 6-8hours, projection is very good for half that time.

I really love this perfume. It opens smoky and leathery after appleid on skin. Then I smell some cherries and sweetness, some sparkling scent from the champagne. On my skin it turns into a sweet cherry scent with a leathery underground. Lovely

Having now tried a few of the Etat Libre d'Orange perfumes, I have found that several of them contain the same leather accord, of which I am not that fond. In the case of BENDELIRIOUS, the opening has a bright and shiny almost LIPSTICK ROSE-like make-up quality, but that cedes quickly to a leather drydown which seems a bit dry and somber--even depressed. Perhaps the Bendel gal partied too late and woke up to find herself alone in a claustrophobic hotel room filled with the scent of a dirty leather jacket mingling with dingy olive green drapes never cleaned. Did she spend the night with some dreadful mec who may have transmitted to her an STD? All she knows now is that she has a hang-over, and the mec has disappeared, having left only his scent behind. The chambermaid has slipped the hotel folio--yet to be paid--under the door. To her surprise, the Bendel gal finds that lo and behold this dark musty hotel room is found in Times Square, and her wallet is now bare!

The fragrance opens with a sparkly cherry note that is dewy, sweet and irreverent. This exuberant note is quickly tamed by violet and iris which give it a more sophisticated, adult feel, pepper adding perfectly to this corset. Underneath this balanced blend is a leather vetiver base which is very sensual and creamy.
