The dry down is rich in superior patchouli, cedar smoothness and guaiac wood smokiness, and an amusing touch of creamy vanilla powder. The overall scent is captivating, not boring at all. Meseems, Leather Essence is a refined and exquisite fragrance that makes a masculine signature. I recommend this for cooler temperatures like fall and winter, both during a day and night out. Since it is not overpowering can be safely worn at work. Longevity and sillage are above the average on my skin, an exceptional fragrance. An exciting thing, the bottle is wrapped by an excellent leather cover that reminds the interior of the Ferrari GT. To me, this scent deserves a complete 8/10! You know what? I am tempted to buy Vetiver Essence as it sounds promising!!! -Elysium

Leather indeed and Ferrari, of all marques, seems to be looking out for the average person. No big price tag for such a great scent that the novice or budget minded collector of scents can afford. Not sickly sweet like Tom Ford's better known leather based perfumes. The cinnamon, clove and black leather notes make this a serious scent, special events worthy.

This parfum is representative from Ferrari mark: Elegancy and luxury in a bottle. The only difference between the parfum and the cars are the price. Ferrari Letaher Essence is a sweet and exquisite leather dessigned for the modern Uomo to wear with a leather jacket, shirt and trouser pants. Excellent sillage and Longevity up the 12 hours. Price is equivalent to buy a Fiat car not a Ferrari.

“Is this the best you could come up with? It smells like it’s from Alberto.” “I wanted to design something special, something fitting for your car brand. Better than the Fiat scents, right?” “I don’t know how we’re going to manage this... you can’t smell any leather... probably only one person can help now to save the scent and the many years of research and development. Alberto, uh... Madame Perfumer, give me the phone.” Five minutes later, a phone rings, a stocky man picks up: “Yes, please? Aha, yes, I understand. Yes.... yes, of course. Italy, you say? No problem, I can be there tomorrow. However.... you’ve dialed the wrong number, this is Trevor Ochmonek.” Another phone rings. A man on his motorcycle tries to answer the call, but his phone slips into his pants, where it continues to vibrate. After a dozen missed calls, the caller from Maranello reaches the heavily breathing man: “Wolle?” “Yes, sure.” “This is the Head of Scents from Ferrari, Cravio Briavache. We want to release a leather scent and our perfumer is suffering from the Morillas syndrome. We need you. Can you be here tomorrow to inspect the scent? See what can be saved?” “Well...” “We have beer. Lots of beer.” “Then see you tomorrow-wait a moment!” “Veltins and Karlskrone in cans, no Italian beer. Wolle? Wolle??? Just hung up....” “Excuse me, Mr. Briavache?” “Not now...” “But a Mr. Wollny is downstairs at reception, you’re expecting him.” Next day: “I can already tell what’s going on. You forgot the leather. Your apple-cinnamon compote is nice but more like a dessert. Ah, the bitter orange doesn’t cut it. Good thing it’s there, at least it covers the remaining sweetness. Where does the perfumer come from? Ferrero?” “Yes, actually, were you able to smell that out?” “No, I only know Ferrero besides Ferrari when it comes to Italy. But I’ll see what can be saved....” “Are you pouring beer into that?” “Sure, it can only get better. Leather would be good too; it should be a leather scent, right?” “I’ll get you what you need!” “Just get me leather, I’ll improvise with the rest here. It gets better after half an hour anyway.” Indeed, the patchouli took over, which smelled more like grasses. Woody notes also emerged, but they were rather weak and served mainly to maintain the initial sweetness over the following hours. Leather Essence was designed to be very pleasant, almost toothless. Leather was noticeable later, Wolle will report this, but I hope that’s not how leather seats smell in a Ferrari. Hours, if not days later: “So, I’m done. First of all, thanks for the leather you usually use to decorate your cars. I made myself a pair of pants out of it.” “With one leg and from your backside with a cutout?” “That’s how you wear it on the biggest runway in the world, in Herne.” “Yeah, well, better explain to us how you saved the olfactory disaster.” “With leather. Sure, my favorite dating portal Parfumo won’t rate the scent 9/10, that was impossible. But: solid. Solid like your sleds, although I swear by my Daihatsu. Unfortunately, it only has a hole in the dashboard. I thought it was a button and bam! Hole in it. Well. The leather, in any case, plays in the background, embracing the sweet brew at the beginning so that one thinks: Oops, this isn’t so bad after all. Not good, more like a scent of Bayer Leverkusen, but not bad either.” “Wolle, there really wasn’t anything more to be salvaged?” “It gets better later, we’re already talking about almost Europa League. The leather is almost completely gone; I needed it for my pants, and the rest was just enough to conjure up the wood-patchouli thing as arbitrarily as possible. No one thinks now, ‘Wow, that’s bad,’ but rather: ‘Oh, already forgotten the scent! Good, huh?’” “Oh no, there really wasn’t more to be done?” “I loosened it up with vanilla. Now it’s something for the whole Marley clientele.” “Good idea! But where did the vanilla come from?” “Müller chocolate pudding with vanilla sauce. I don’t like it and then poured it into the scent.” “Well, and will it stay like that?” “No, because if I had continued to accentuate the base after about an hour, it would have sooner or later become apparent that it’s rather mediocre. Therefore, it becomes mushy and poorly definable afterwards. If this isn’t a scent with a lot of leather, wink, wink.” “Wolle, even if you don’t have many skills, like not soiling the toilet when used or using deodorant, you can elevate bad scents to the gray average!” Leather Essence by Ferrari hardly smells of leather. The sweet-fruity elements are not too strong but still constructed to be acceptable. The development doesn’t fundamentally change, even when it becomes woody. Overall, a scent that doesn’t stand out negatively, which probably hardly stands out at all. Solid as a rock.

Surprise. For around €60, you get a blend of Mugler's A*MEN Havana/Malt and the typical leather notes a la Tom Ford - Tuscan Leather, just not as smoky and raspberry-like. The leather feels a bit chemically treated, but not unpleasant. We start fresh with bergamot, which lasts only a few minutes. Right after that, the heart... leather enveloped by vanilla. However, after an hour, the scent becomes rather weak. It smells more like tonka bean than leather. I hardly sense the woods... more like a caramel candy with a hint of cinnamon. What a pity. The woods in the dry down would have been important here. Hardly any sillage, under an arm's length, and only lasts 3 hours. Average, but not bad for the money. Who wears it? More for fans of 1 Million and A*Men. On men over 40, it smells almost embarrassing.

Okay obviously you should always wait for the drydown to judge but that seems particularly true here. An in-store spritz will not do it justice at all. When I sprayed it, the first word that came to my mind was "bubble gum" which I decided wasn't literally right but the broader idea of "bland candy" remained. I couldn't smell anything that appealed to me, and if it was a fragrance, it was an extremely cheap, mild, drug store fragrance. I kinda thought it was a bust. But then an hour or so later, I caught a whiff of it and for a second I didn't even know what it was! It turns out it's a really good fragrance! The white florals are so great. It doesn't have a lot of sillage I don't think, but it is long lasting and it's so fresh and clean and soapy—not just the florals of soap but just a little bit of the "bite" that soap has as well. It's a great hit to put on first thing in the morning to wake up. It's not sexy at all but I definitely intend to buy a full-size bottle. Perfect office type fragrance, or like a party where you're meeting new people and want to make a good clean first impression.

I love Bond No.9 fragrances. I definitely can't wear them all, but this one is one of 3 that I can not only smell but also wear. Just the bottle alone - magnificent. And I’m not just talking about the flower, although that caught my eye in the store right away; I mean the glass bottle itself. Very sturdy, very prominent, definitely a head-turner. All the fragrances have an unmistakably above-average longevity for me - lasting until late evening.

This is gorgeous! One of the best fresh/aquatic scents that i've ever had and smelled. And yes, smells like Sprite sometimes. Great combination of lime, yuzu and mint. It's clean, fresh and crisp. If this had more lasting power, it would me one of my top ten fragrances. Worth it. Updated January 2014

Musky aquatic floral. Salty and reminds me of sweat or tears. Not entirely unpleasant thanks to the fresh soft floral notes with hint of sweetness. Have to say my bottle is the old one with "Par" on it so I'm not sure whether the current bottle without "Par" on the name is the same scent or not....................

This one was one of my first. The one I tested, bought, and wore with joy throughout a wonderful summer. And I still remember thinking: this one, I will definitely always have! Summer passed, and although it wasn't even half empty - if at all - the bottle, which reminded me of a half-melted ice cube - 'How cool is that?' I thought back then - gradually moved to the back of the shelf. Others came, others went. I clung to some, others were just a fling, and some - none from those early fragrant years - have remained. Until today, and I find that beautiful. In kindergarten or elementary school, we make our first friendships, perhaps just because we live on the same street or both like Lego, but these first friends rarely last, even if we might think: BFF! Later, deeper friendships come along, and eventually relationships - and sooner or later, also bitter disappointment and betrayal. And yet we keep thinking: this is forever! And then we end up crying ourselves to sleep or have - intentionally or carelessly - made someone else cry. And yet we believe again: Now for sure! Forever! Now, losing a perfume is of course far less distressing than losing a person, but to like a scent so much that I want to own it, I want to believe at the moment of purchase: if not forever, then at least for quite a while! That’s pretty silly, as I have experienced many times that this doesn’t work out. But just as there have indeed been people for whom 'until tomorrow morning' was enough to simply take them home, the same is true for perfumes. We all have them, it’s not a big deal. But those we believe in are more fun. L'Eau par Kenzo pour Homme is nothing special as a fragrance. But it was for one summer. For me. Beyond its fruity-sweet triviality, it has something vulnerable that I still find in it today. I smell it, others might not. For many, it’s probably just one of many summer fresheners - aquatic, a bit like shower gel, somewhat disco - that was the 90s! It fundamentally has nothing that one could dislike, and such scents - I know today - are rarely good 'forever'. And yet it was a beautiful, blessed, and long summer with Yuzu, mint, and the others. And that’s not nothing. Conclusion: basically a terribly forgettable and irrelevant scent. And yet again, not quite.

I’m already doing my Christmas fragrance shopping because I don’t want to get caught up in the hustle and bustle that starts in November. It just occurred to me that three of my guys from our gentlemen's circle have their birthdays in November. So I need more of that stuff dreams are made of. The three candidates are not dissimilar - they were all born under the sign of Scorpio. Their fragrance preferences are also quite similar - reserved, clear, and often a bit contemplative. Of course, I could give all three of them the same fragrance, as it’s hardly likely they will visit each other and show off my gifts. But you never know.... The Scorpio itself is very particular - and it wants to possess something "unique." My husband is easy to gift, as he firmly insists on the statement shower gel. But the other two experts are a bit trickier. So I found the cool, but not too cold, Choo Ice for the police chief and now pondered over my Berlin broker. A saleswoman appeared out of nowhere and asked me: Do you know Kenzo? Of course, I know the label. Hesitantly, I followed her. Wow - I didn’t know L'éau. And it greets me fresh but gently. The lemon invigorates and is not sour - and a mild hint of pepper joins in. The mint cools the fragrance - and lotus provides a clear transparency. The cedar wafts lightly smoky above it - and I have the association of a Zen garden. My Berlin friend will like this, as he enjoys creating images with scents. We can both do this for hours. As a frequent traveler, he will surely enjoy the trip to Asia.

I bought this Kenzo last summer. When it comes to fragrances, I simply love this brand. Power, Jungle, the Homme line, and also this one. Last year I saw it in the store. It had been on my wishlist for years, but somehow other fragrances always took precedence. On a warm spring day, I finally made it happen. I was in the city in the evening to take care of some things. When you're already wandering around in a few stores, of course, testing is a must. On that wonderfully warm spring day, I chose this one. The bottle appealed to me so much that I had to test it. The bottle is simple and elegant. The light blue scent just spoke to me on that warm day. I then tested it: From the first spray, I was enveloped in a wonderful noble freshness. Lemon and Yuzu are very present from start to finish. I really like Yuzu, and here this note fits perfectly into the concept. Paired with the lemon, it slightly reminds me of fresh lemon iced tea. I also perceive a light sweet note. Mint and a hint of pepper accompany it perfectly and are mega-refreshing. Even after the test, the scent accompanied me perfectly. I enjoyed the evening sun on a bench in the park, and this fragrance perfectly emphasized the summer feeling. It is also of very high quality and stands out from many summer flankers. Unfortunately, there is a catch: The longevity is, in my opinion, abysmal. I don't know exactly, but I perceive it for about 2-3 hours. Many drugstore fragrances can easily top that. You can get this one for 40 Euros for 100ml, but I simply expect much more from brands like Kenzo. I bought it anyway, as it truly offers a great refreshment.

I got to know L'eau par Kenzo through my then-neighbor, who often vacationed in the USA and Mexico during that time (2001-2003) and brought this EdT back with him. His bottle looked different from the ones listed here: round, unremarkable with a blue cap. The liquid was also a pale blue color. I've expressed my preference for Kenzo fragrances elsewhere.

Hm, today is the day, I no longer own this fragrance in the bottle. But I carry it in my heart, in my mind, and just a tiny bit in my nose. Because today I sprayed it on for the last time. And now, as the musk-polished cedar gently shimmers away, I already regret the step I took: I traded the last 10 mL at the souk... ...for a vetiver.

I need to quickly rehabilitate him, as the scent came off far too poorly in my comment on the flanker "Eau Indigo". For Kenzo, which is often considered the epitome of blandness, LEPKPH starts surprisingly strong, namely really beautifully sour. Wonderful! Respect, dear Yuzu, I would have expected a thick, fat lemon here.

Kenzo PH was one of the first perfumes I tested about a year ago when my new expensive hobby and simultaneously (positive) addiction started. Now it was time for L'eau par Kenzo PH, even though it is still too early for summer scents. It has nothing to do with the regular PH.

What an elegant bottle! The first impression upon spraying is also promising: Yuzu, lime, mandarin, aldehydes - it somewhat reminds me of the noble opening of "Sun Men" by Jil Sander or "Silver Light" by Escada, and it has a bit of the powerhouse "Kenzo Boisée," but is definitely more delicate. A lovely floral heart note with lotus, magnolia, and iris unfolds.

To me, lavender can be cloying and a bit too sweet, of course the ratio/amount and type of lavender has a lot to do with that. I love Puig's Agua Lavanda, the citric muskiness of it. This, at first application, seems like too much, but it is different, more than lavender. This is unique! Why is my review titled "PATIENCE"? Give this three to four hours, then..........boom, beautiful drydown! Is it the cashmere woods, sage? I'm not crazy about the start but this finished rather well.

Jeez... I really like these Ferrari ones! This house is really proving that it is possible to bring high quality scents to the masses for an extremely reasonable price! What I especially appreciate with this line is that we all get a chance to try/own frags with certain notes/feels that more often are common in nieche world. Don’t get me wrong, these are most likely to be crowd pleasers. They are just a bit different than your avarege Dylan Blue, YsL Y, Blue de Chanel, Azzaro Chrom etc. These are blended more the way a nieche frag is, just in a more mass pleasing way and the offer a distinct note in every release. With that said, this one starts a beautiful Lavender note that’ll stick with you all the way (more or less). There will also be a sweet (not clawing sweet) Vanilla/Tonka mix after an hour that will carry this warm yet fresh scent forward. Some times I get a feel of ambroxan although this note is not listed. All in all, in my opinion Bright Neroli and Radiant Bergamot (I do not own noble fig... yet)are both more zesty and uplifting than this one. But this is just as gorgeous and in my world as certain! Spring, summer, fall... work, home or at the mall.. you can easily rock ‘em all!

Lavender is a great herb That often blows me away It smells quite strong and really nice In some fragrances, it also seems dull. But at Ferrari, it's hidden I search for it, wide awake It gradually becomes bland for me I can't find it, oh what a shame. It starts citrusy and spiced The top note feels very short Immediately, wood mixes in But it can't really be real. Artificially sweet, it then continues Vanilla doesn't cheer me up here Along with a light powdery note But that doesn't threaten me. The whole thing seems strange to me Maybe I'll ask in the lab Where all the notes come from They don't harmonize together. It feels quite artificial and not fine My nose calls out, "Must this be?" It clings tightly to my skin They really dared something here. I don't find the scent really fresh But it doesn't smell like fish either Yet overall, it feels very dull In my head, it goes thump-thump. The scent is unfortunately a bit confused Maybe they were a bit off while creating it It's a big jumble Perhaps coriander is still missing I'm waiting for the lavender But unfortunately, it doesn't come Did they perhaps forget it? Did the perfumer get stressed? The longevity is impeccable For some fragrances, it would be fabulous I don't find it quite so nice here Because I can't get used to it. Pure Lavender is supposed to be the name of the scent But I won't be fooled Without lavender, it's just Pure I'll just stay stubborn about it I was looking forward to testing the scent But it didn't turn out so well here Thanks to Helena1411 There's no quarrel about Pure Lavender. The bottle is really chic The rest gives cause for criticism Which I can't hold back here But one can grumble now and then. The test doesn't lead to a purchase The scent has too little to offer me Instead, I'll dare to Look for other Ferraris. The next scent will be better again There are countless waters I just wanted to tell you once Otherwise, there might be complaints later. If you don't like the comment I can't please everyone I express my opinion And certainly won't keep quiet.

Ah. A modern lavender freshie. Especially since this Pure series from Ferrari is of decent quality. It could have been so nice! But it's not. The reason is quickly told: The opening is quite promising. Citrus and lavender go well together, not too heavy and easy to wear. But then it rapidly goes downhill. After a short time, this modern sharpness disappears and what remains is: lavender. And with the temperament of a half cheese roll. Without pickles. That's not really bad or 'nasty', but incredibly boring. And in this boredom, the lavender also develops a certain annoying factor. Ah, I'll keep it short and painless: I don't want to smell like a middle-aged man in a sweater vest after mom's ironing water type of lavender dream. Not now. Never. Thank you.

The fragrances of car brands often have a bad reputation, which unfortunately is confirmed by the abundance of scents. However, there are also some really good exceptions. This one, in my opinion, is only partially successful. In the opening, the Provençal lavender note reminds me of Pour un homme de Caron, but it is already noticeably softer and sweeter here. While PuhdC initially starts with a citrus-sharp lavender note, here the citrus part seems to quickly transition into the heart note, with only a hint of cardamom briefly detectable. The lavender increasingly disappears behind the sage after a short time and is almost immediately accompanied by vanilla from the very start of the fragrance. Together with patchouli, the scent becomes very sweet after a while, and it is at this point that Ferrari Pure Lavender clearly differs from Caron. While the latter glides into a multifaceted smooth vanilla note, the Ferrari simply becomes very, very sweet and quite synthetic, which gives me a headache after some time. I can't quite perceive the cashmere wood, but I don't want to doubt that it is present in the base note's background. While the opening of the fragrance is very promising, I agree with Ajlen that the further development of the scent is disappointing. Overall, the longevity is quite good at 8 hours for me, but unfortunately, the beautiful opening fades away too quickly. For me, unfortunately, not a candidate for the collection; however, if you like sweet or even gourmand scents and don't mind a certain level of synthetics, you should definitely give this one a try.

In search of the reason why a certain component in the scent Cruel Intentions by Kilian doesn't sit well with me, I guessed it might be Oud and asked Kankuro for advice. He not only sent me a piece of pure Oud wood but also a sample of this expensive fragrance. Thank you my dear! While the piece of wood smells absolutely wonderful (so I must be able to handle Oud:-), I am more than shocked by Harrods' limited edition from Bond. Unfortunately, at the opening, it smells like goat cheese to me. I don't like goat cheese at all unless it is grilled and served on a huge bed of lamb's lettuce. Of course, goat cheese is not listed as a fragrance component here, but perhaps it is this fecal and almost urinous note that I find so disagreeable. Really yuck! The poor cumin cannot be blamed, as I love its scent in nature and am crazy about Arabic food, especially from Lebanon, which is primarily seasoned with it. And I have cumin at home and make falafel, hummus, or add it to rice...mhmmm yummy! So what is it in this fragrance that bothers me? It can only be the myrrh! Because after the goat cheese retreats back to the barn (where it belongs!), I am enveloped by ethereal clouds of smoke, as it would smell if one were to incense an entire monastery. Orientals also like to burn incense at home or as a sign when wishing someone good luck or calling for good + support. Thus, myrrh thematically fits well with cumin and pepper. As time goes on, the fragrance becomes a bit better and milder - well, after such a powerful opening, that's not a great achievement. For me, the scent is not unisex. Dear women: hands off! But even a man who smells like this, I wouldn't want as a seat neighbor. It may be that others simply find it better than I do. Now, the fragrance comes from another world, but certainly not mine......and the doubt remains, perhaps it is indeed the Oud in concentrated form that is to blame...the search for the unknown component that annoys ET continues. At the moment, it's 1:2 for Oud. Thank you Kankuro for the sample. I feel a little ashamed of my negative review, please don't take it personally.

Kenzo Jungle Homme opens with a really peculiar, distinctive and to me totally pleasant accord composed by a sort of odd spicy-green-fruity blend, much aromatic and slightly milky, with sharp lime notes juxtaposed to a creamy, fruity, slightly synthetic feel of tropical fruits (banana, a bit of coconut too), enhanced by carnation and spices – notably nutmeg and cloves. Beyond this, a perfectly-blended note of sandalwood, which is quite sweet and creamy as well. Overall the name fits this scent perfectly, as it is quite an exotic and bizarre Oriental scent which surely conjures a “jungle” mood. What I admire the most is the effort to create something less usual than predictable “green-forest” clichés, trying to evoke a whole “raw nature” ambiance – spices, woods, leaves, even a sort of aqueous-mineral feel. The opening is quite bold, then it suddenly tones down to a nutty-citrus green and creamy blend with a prominent sandalwood note, all well wrapped up in a sort of “balsamic” creaminess that tames down both the fruity-sweet side, and the spices, avoiding to become either “too gourmand” or too spiced. Totally creative and distinctive, but well balanced and restrained enough to be perfectly safe, pleasant and unisex in any circumstance. Finally, on the drydown it becomes more quiet, more gentle and more dry, with spices and woods (cedar too) emerging to the point of bringing Jungle Homme almost close to a woody fougère territory – still with a balmy-sweet Oriental vibe all over, also with distant echoes of Opium pour Homme. A bit synthetic (this meaning “cheap”) here and there, but really nice and creative, also smelling fairly “niche” (in the positive meaning). 7/10

I purchased Kenzo Jungle PH in 2009, when I was early in my fragrance hobby. I must have found a good deal on it from some now-defunct website. I'm not sure what I paid, but whatever it was, when I revisit this scent in 2023, I can't help but feel I got it for a steal. I remember the reviews at the time being divisive, and thinking, "if it's not good, it'll at least be interesting." For me, being boring is a bigger sin than being bad. And I'm sure I needed to add something to get free shipping. Almost 15 years ago, I remember trying this and being blown away - but not in a good way. It had this aggressive, almost headache-inducing vibe. Smells that I didn't think went together - the nutmeg and citrus up top, the mate and cinnamon bomb in the middle, and the woods underneath. I didn't wear it much, but I didn't dislike it. I was finding myself and finding where I felt comfortable pushing the envelope. Fast forward to 2023, and I find my bottle in tact - 14 years and 8 moves later - and I give it a spray. Immediately, I got it. I loved it. It needed it's time, but It's one of my absolute favorite fragrances in my collection. It's an experience, and it is travel in a bottle. I am taken to places that may not exist in our world, but do in my mind. 9/10 - more interesting than half of my bottles that are 5x more expensive. It's warm and inviting, while being exotic and interesting. It's not the bottle for a 90 degree day, but it's a solid 3 season smell - when you want to go somewhere different.

A spicy, but still subtle oriental featuring nutmeg, cedar, creamy guaiac wood and sandalwood with added benzoine. Rich, sweet and slightly floral. Opening with lime - a bold and somewhat surprising move for an oriental - on a note of mate, settling on nutmeg and some sweet, powdery woods. Overall, it's rather linear. Longevity and projection are average, but very fitting for this type of scent. Although I find it quite different from others I've tried from the Kenzo line (where most are either aquatic or have an asian "bamboo-feel" to it that are mostly suited for warmer weather), this is a surprisingly nice fragrance that shines in colder temperatures.

It's a great fragrance, Elegant, Classy, Sophisticated. I blind - bought this hidden gem base on positive comments. I checked reviews on YouTube, Special thanks to : Scent Land and Gents Scents. This perfume has an unusual and a very strange Opening , It smells like pencil shavings but dry down is very wonderful ! It opens up with like warm spicy then dry down is semi sweet woody. It has a unique composition. This is perfect for the spring and fall. The art of bottle design is very beautiful. I love Kenzo Jungle Homme EDT. Bravo Monsieur Cresp ! Two Thumbs Up. Rating : 8.5 / 10

My first teenage designer perfume! I’ve kept it in a 5ml bottle for years.I’m sure i’ve gone through more than five bottles of this perfume. Even today, I get goosebumps when I smell it. Such a simple and beautiful fragrance, so many beautiful memories awaken when I catch a whiff of it. But unfortunately, after owning many niche creations and developing my taste, I don’t think I’d wear it again, and it would feel very weak to me now! No matter what, I always look forward to smelling it, and for me, the scent is a solid 10/10.

Welcome to the Jungle, is the unofficial motto here at Kenzo, although it refers more to the urban jungle than to wild exotic vegetation. Somehow, it also has a clubbing vibe, a kind of elevated boldness with well-tempered woods and seductive spiciness. The ingredients sound quite sober.

Among the aquatic refreshers, Kenzo's now 24-year-old "Homme" occupies a very respectable front position - it doesn't reinvent the wheel, but it also doesn't do much wrong. The brand is not particularly broad or visually striking in the men's segment; in fact, the "Homme" horse is repeatedly ridden to death.

This Kenzo fragrance has been in my collection for about a year. Since my favorite scent "Power" comes from the same house, I ordered this one blind. Kenzo is a great brand for me, simply bringing fragrances to the market with a high recognition value. "Power," "Homme," "L'eau par Kenzo," and this one are really beautiful scents. The name "Jungle" suits this fragrance.

Most people know Kenzo primarily for Homme or perhaps Tokyo. But this rarely spotted fragrance is truly a special specimen and a tip worth sharing. It stands out with its amusing bottle cap and is hardly ever visible in its usual habitat. All the better that I encountered it in a store and was able to give it a few hours of testing time.

...is certainly not this fragrance from Kenzo! It starts with the bottle, which for me is a well-rounded piece. Grippily tapered, with a contrasting matte (etched) camouflage design... the cap adds a playful touch to the wildlife theme. It truly makes a strong impression with absolute recognizability. The same goes for the scent... unmistakable!

This perfume is a beauty. What a spectacular incense !!! an elegant, sensual, warm, cozy and voluptuous aroma, a feminine fragrance, that, even being a man, I could not resist to dress, and to my surprise, in my skin it loses that femininity and voluptuousness, and it shows me a more androgynous facet and unisex. It could well have been an independent perfume and not a limited-edition flanker, which was a seen and not seen. Very bad for Kenzo, for showing it to us and then depriving us of it, while we continue to flood the perfume market clones of each other, and authentic works of art, like this one, are born to give it a limited life ... that is not done! !! At the beginning, this perfume I tried it on my sister, and while, in it, it developed extremely feminine and charming, a vanilla incense with an outstanding note of rice, in me, the thing changed for the better. In my skin, it was a more linear aroma, a vanilla incense, something earthy, with a slight touch of patchouli, and very basic rice touch, but in my skin that female note cushioned very well, allowing me to dress without any problem . A smoky aroma, sweet, mysterious and magical, but above all sensual and placid. I've been wearing it for two full days, and it's been a while since a perfume did not make me feel so happy. A pity its descatalogación. As for its performance, it is good, in my skin it remains for more than 8 hours, with a moderate wake, but with a very marked presence. A perfume of cool and temperate climates and preferably of nocturnal use, during the day I think I would lose that mysterious and sensual touch, that the night would amplify. I have been particularly enamored with its aroma, and as quickly as I entered ecstasy upon knowing it, I fell into depression when I learned of its descatalogation and the barbarities that they ask for the few living specimens, a pity... Sorry for my bad english.

I tested this one a while ago when it was still easy to find, I liked it but was on a no buy, so I thought I would go for it in a different moment. After that all of a sudden and to my surprise, it completely disappeared from the perfume shops. I just stopped looking for it. Today I found a 30ml bottle when I came into a shop looking to test something else and couldn't help myself. It is a beautiful dark but feminine oriental. I don't like the original Amour which I find more common and dispensable. Amour Le parfum on the other hand, is original and special. It is an incensed and ambered benzoin bomb on me, darkened by the patchouli and transformed into a feminine scent by the addition of vanilla and rice notes. With a great longevity and a nice evolution, getting richer as time goes by. It makes me think of Goutal's beautiful Ambre Fetiche only without the leather so sweeter, more ladylike and easier to wear. I'm in heaven.

I confess, during my time at Müller, I didn't pay much attention to this fragrance. After Kenzo Amour and already after the flood of Kenzo Flowers, I simply couldn't take the flankers seriously anymore. With what felt like 800 women's fragrances on the shelf, you eventually have your repertoire together, and for everything else, it’s "not worth mentioning." That’s how I felt about Kenzo Amour Le Parfum. Now, with some distance from mainstream fragrances, I see it more objectively, and from a Parfumo perspective rather than a sales perspective, entirely different standards are applied, even though that’s actually nonsensical. But even if our customers can't imagine it, there simply wasn't the time or the opportunity to acquire the necessary background knowledge for every fragrance and truly store it in one's scent memory. The assortment was just too fast-moving for that. In hindsight, Kenzo Amour Le Parfum doesn't really deserve that, as it is a sensual, yet subtle and warm fragrance, whose rather heavy heart note is pleasantly kept in check by the velvety incense note. The base harmoniously follows, and I can hardly imagine any other notes in the dry down for this fragrance. Despite amber and vanilla, Le Parfum never becomes truly sweet. Daphné Bugey has found the right balance with these often inflationarily used notes. A large portion of users who have tested the perfume perceive Amour Le Parfum as oriental. I only partially agree, as I can't detect any Arabic spices. Nevertheless, the fragrance reminds me of gardens I experienced in Singapore. Tropical but not cloying, and equipped with an impenetrable airline smile, the perfume brings back carefree days from my last major trip. I think I will take off my blinders and occasionally test one of the fragrances that are available everywhere and therefore often unjustly overlooked. Who knows what I might discover.

I’m an eBay junkie. I buy my perfumes on eBay, almost exclusively so far, meaning I don’t just buy them, I hunt for them. Until I find one that I can bid on at a price acceptable to me. For my original packaged and sealed Prada Intense, I paid about a third of the MSRP. This one isn’t available on eBay. It’s almost as expensive there as in regular retail. No chance, or rather, I’ve somehow always missed the few chances to get it cheaply. I found it wonderful during the first test, exactly my style. On the test strip, it seems very patchouli-heavy, but on the skin, it is much softer. Woody, smoky, powdery, warm, spicy, not too sweet. Dark-golden, like the bottle. Frangipani only adds a bit of sweetness, making the heart note softer, which is spicy and smoky. The base doesn’t really come through step by step, but rather slowly glides in. I’m reminded of the comparison of a pixel to a vector graphic, so stepwise to smooth transition. It gradually becomes softer, powderier, sweeter. I totally love benzoin in perfumes, I realize, I’ve encountered it more often lately. Patchouli is not dominant, that would make the scent too loud, too screaming. These are overtones in perfume form. Kenzo Amour Le Parfum has been on my wish list for a long time. Today I burned my voucher and still spent more money on it than I have ever paid for another fragrance. 30 ml isn’t enough, no, more, please! And I hope there will be a few rainy days. Then I’ll have the opportunity to wear it. It’s not a summer scent, not for sunshine and heat. It doesn’t have to rain tomorrow, as I’m planning a treasure hunt for the kids in the holiday care. Rain would be a hindrance for their "hunt." But Saturday, it should rain, please.

I was faced with the choice of Kenzo Amour or Le Parfum. After reading the comments here, I was ready to buy Le Parfum blind, but someone was kind enough to send me a sample first. Now I have Amour on the left and Le Parfum on the right. The top note of Le Parfum repelled me. Very oriental-spicy and with a strong incense note. I calmed down, as I had already bought Amour and thought I had made the right choice. Amour is much softer and cozier, without the harsh notes in it. But... after 5 minutes, Le Parfum caught up and entered a race with Amour. The harsh notes faded a bit into the background, and a delicate floral note with a wonderfully soft rice note came to the forefront. Now the scent became warm and snuggly. A hint of incense and woods (which I don't particularly like) is still present, but no longer bothersome, rather fitting to the overall composition. Vanilla later mixes in, and the scent becomes even more beautiful with a creamy touch. It remains gently sweet and very warm. The spicy notes cannot be suppressed, but they stay in full harmony with the other notes. Both Kenzos are beautiful. Le Parfum is stronger in the scent aura, while Amour is cozier and softer.

After a severely negative fragrance experience with Kenzo, I felt traumatized. It was out of the question for me to test another perfume from this brand. However, after repeatedly noticing these vase-like bottles here on Parfumo, and realizing the popularity of the fragrances contained within, I dared to give it another chance...

Many years ago, I was in an Arabic restaurant. It was small, but exquisite. I remember candlelight, colorful embroidered blankets, golden trays on which countless tea lights made the light dance. Spices that enveloped the room. It was incredibly unique. If I were to go back today, I would wear my prettiest dress, high-heeled shoes, and red lipstick.

Dental clinic? No, at most in the fleeting first second of the top note, I think I briefly perceive that. But I believe my nose was misled for a moment. Marzipan? Maybe. Very distantly. Not really. Propolis? A striking similarity, yes. But somehow not really again. The scent reminds me of something, but I can't place it.

Voyage d'amour II - the love journey continues I am a passionate wearer of Kenzo Amour EDP, and it is only natural, or in the right scent, that I also keep Le Parfum in my collection. But what can we expect now with Amour Le Parfum, is there an enhancement of an intoxicating creation that contains so much beauty and so much magical love?

~ Inspiration ~ I really like "Amour" and received a large bottle of it from the lovely Eisbonbon (who unfortunately is no longer registered here). Now I was curious about the other variants and got something small to test. ~ Bottle ~ The curved vase shape has been retained - here it is in a matte brown-gold tone, which promises a warm, elegant scent.

I personally smell a very easy perfume, that typical designer shower gel vibe, like adidas or axe. Yes, it reminds of millesime imperial but on a budget and only in a small 30 min time, before that is watermelony clean shower gel, and after that is just a sport shower gel. If you like that vibe, go for it but not at its full price :-)

After several years of wanting this, I've finally pulled the trigger. Well, for the price I've paid I can say that its ok...not great. At least I can now cross it out of my list. The musk here is not the animalic, dirty musk found in darker musk based fragrances but rather a clean, fresh laundry type of musk. On first spray, only two notes are very prominent: mint and musk. At this stage, the scent is bitter, cold, and fresh. It has a cooling effect, like when you're chewing mint gum. Unfortunately, it has a tendency to irritate my throat if inhaled deeply. The mids are better and less in-your-face. This is where the other notes emerge as the dominating mint and musk subside. Watermelon, citruses and spices become more noticable. The drydown is linear continuing from the heart and continues like this until it fades. Longevity is average. Around 6 hours tops even though its an EDP. Fragrances that are similar to this are: Victorinox Swiss Army Altitude, Kenneth Cole Black, Nautica Voyage N-83 and Bvlgari Aqua. If I'm a little bit younger, I would probably loved this but I've found out my tastes are changing as I'm growing old. This is only a solid like.

Expeditions into the realm of perfume, episode 1424: The Water Cucumber. This could be how a documentary about Ferrari's Musk Essence might start. I ordered this scent in the summer, mainly because I was looking for a fresh fragrance with melon. Additionally, the performance sounded promising. And to get straight to the point: in this regard, Musk Essence truly delivers without reservation. However, I do not perceive the watermelon as such - it lacks the typical fruity sweetness for me. Instead, I smell a rather sour-water freshness that reminds me of cucumber. Therefore, I refer to it here as water cucumber instead of watermelon. Surrounding this water cucumber are other herb-fresh notes and a rather cool aquatic element, enhanced by a hint of mint. With a bit of imagination, one can also detect some lavender, vetiver, and the namesake musk later on. However, I need quite a bit of imagination for that. Generally speaking, I would say that all the aromas used are rather on the pale, watery side. And artificial to boot. Is all of this good or bad? Yes, both. The freshness is long-lasting, and from a technical and functional perspective, one could consider Essence Musk a successful summer freshie. Unfortunately, I find the scent itself rather bland and also disharmonious to the point of being dull. The synthetic notes are quite loud and at times even aggressive. It’s really not “beautiful” in the true sense. And yet, I found myself reaching for the bottle more often than expected last summer. Quite strange.

After unfortunately having only bad experiences with tests of Ferrari fragrances (Bright Neroli, Light Essence, Light Essence Aqua, Scuderia, and Red), all of which were too stuffy, one-dimensional, and sometimes too sweet for me, I was now pleasantly surprised. And this even with a blind purchase and despite the name "Musk," which usually doesn't bode well for me: As if I hadn't already crashed enough Ferraris, I dared to order another one :) after being drawn in by its fragrance pyramid and especially the grapefruit contained within. For me, this scent is an attractant ;) And I also quickly fall for mandarin and watermelon. And all of that is in this thing. So I had to have it, ordered EM, and soon opened the packaging with great anticipation. When I then took the heavy, high-quality bottle in my hand, opened the beautifully leather-wrapped cap, and treated myself to a few sprays, it was immediately over for me: WOW, it is very fruity and pleasant, albeit a bit tart. But that's precisely what gives this Ferrari its special punch and it lasts until the end. In between, a hint of lavender and especially the mint is noticeable, bringing a bit of variety, while the nutmeg plays only a homeopathic role. However, after about two hours, the base notes begin to assert themselves slowly, making the scent a bit softer and rounder. The EDT impresses with a wonderful freshness that convinces right after spraying due to its fruitiness and shapes the scent throughout its entire duration. Although it becomes increasingly sweeter towards the end, it remains very balanced based on the melon, which forms the focal point. However, it is by no means watery or bland, but optimally embedded in the base notes, flanked by the other fruity nuances, while the musk, despite the name, does not stand out particularly. The longevity is excellent at about 10 hours, for example, when sprayed on the back of the head, and the sillage is perceptible as a subtle touch of freshness with every turn of the head.

Fragrances are memories for many of us. Memories of certain times, of certain people, of certain situations... For many of us, such fragrances are among the most beautiful, as there are reasons why we have special memories associated with them... I feel the same way, of course. In addition to Hugo Boss Bottled EdT and Acqua di Giò EdT, there is a third fragrance that I have known since my youth, even though I didn’t use any perfumes back then: Kenzo Pour Homme EdT. I got to know it (the Kenzo from 1991) as a teenager, in the summer of 2000, when a cousin of my then best friend wore it day after day, and I, as a complete novice, always wondered what on earth smelled so incredibly good about him. I can remember it so well and clearly because the fragrance has not left me to this day. Moreover, that year there was the European Football Championship right around the corner (Belgium/Netherlands). Of course, as an enthusiastic player (among others, together with this slightly older acquaintance and his Kenzo), I traveled the few kilometers to the neighboring countries and experienced the event live there a few times, even though we only had a ticket for a single game. But when it’s just a stone’s throw away, you also go there without a ticket, simply to experience the big picture. And his Kenzo enveloped me amidst all those colorful people there... Many people, people from different countries, joyfully celebrating, and his Kenzo... [...] My comment now refers to the further development or reworking of the 91 Kenzo. For a long time, I owned this fragrance myself until a few months ago when, after a long "Kenzo break," I tested this new edited version in a perfume store. Right from the first spray, I had 'flashbacks'... It was all over for me; I immediately bought a bottle in the store.... I don’t even know when this new version came onto the market. It is not quite as aquatic in comparison and a bit woodier, but fundamentally, it smells - at least to my nose - quite identical or similar to the 91 bottle. The new one also opens with a dreamy, maritime, airy, and aquatic breeze that excites me. However, as it develops, it shows its first woody notes, becoming slightly sweet without losing its aromatic freshness from the beginning. Because it still remains very pleasantly fresh in an "airy" way; despite the pine note that I perceive. This aromatic freshness transports you mentally to warmer countries, to beaches with deep blue-clear seas, bright blue-clear skies, and bright yellow sun... And when the sandalwood joins in the base, the fragrance reaches its peak. This slightly creamy-balsamic sweetness paired with the velvety-warm wood is a delight, simply melting away, I find. Nevertheless, this base is still enveloped by the airy aquatic sea note. Due to its composition, it is made for the warmer season, but of course, you can wear it throughout the year. However, I know for myself that it shines best in spring or summer. The sillage that one perceives with a gust of wind feels very smooth and pleasant. That a fragrance of this composition lasts a good 6-7 hours on my skin is an indication that fundamentally fresh fragrances do not always have to have endurance problems. Conclusion: Currently, I am not using this Kenzo, as I am still waiting for spring and the first warmer days when I will wear it again with great joy. It won’t be long now... However, I keep sniffing the spray head and enjoying those moments. Because not only is the fragrance dreamy, but my memories of it are priceless... This acquaintance mentioned is unfortunately no longer with us; the dear man left us far too early... But through memories, many people live on within us; though invisible, they are still close... And even if every journey has an end, the memories of it are everlasting... [...] Thank you for reading!

Since I love fresh and aquatic scents, I absolutely had to test this classic from Kenzo (even though it has been reformulated). At first, I thought, "No, I don't like it." Maybe because one expects a typical aquatic scent like Cool Water, Acqua di Gio, or Bulgari Aqua. But that's not what the Kenzo Homme EdT is. Along with the definitely present maritime notes, there are clearly other accords added. I smell resin or something resin-like. In addition, a solid portion of woods gives the fragrance more weight and masculinity. After testing Kenzo Homme EdT on my skin throughout the day, I liked it more and more. Now I find it quite special and don't want to miss it anymore. Also, the EdT Intense, which goes in a completely different direction. Longevity and sillage are unusually good for an aquatic; I would say 5 hours is already good performance. The bottle is a classic and looks nice. The price is quite good; I bought it on sale at the perfume shop. A recommendation from me if you're looking for an extraordinary aquatic.

About half a year ago, I set out to find a new perfume. My mother had suggested this scent to me, as she would love to smell it on men. So, I tested it as well. An employee sprayed this fragrance on something cloth-like (or rather on a thinner tissue) and I sniffed it very cautiously. In my opinion, the perfume smells a bit dusty, but much better. I then sprayed the scent on my skin and stepped outside the store briefly to better perceive the unfolding of the fragrance. I was very positively surprised and ended up buying it. Regarding the scent, as I said, it has a slightly dusty quality, harmonizing with a subtle freshness of the sea. Nutmeg only becomes noticeable for me after about half an hour and ends with a delicate sandalwood note. There isn't much to say about the bottle, except that I find it very beautiful and it emphasizes the fragrance direction (fresh and woody) very well. For me, this perfume is an absolute recommendation for anyone who wants to smell a bit unusual and is looking to pursue new and extravagant goals, and has always been or wants to be a bit experimental. Have fun trying it out ;)

Finally, I managed to bring this boy to my nose, and I must say, it's a fine little scent. It starts fresh-maritime, with nutmeg grounding it into a fresh-spicy fragrance. Notably, at the very beginning, there is a distinct alcoholic note that comes through. Whether the alcohol in this fragrance simply evaporates poorly, I can't quite define. Then it becomes very piney - but full throttle! The pine makes no secret of saying "Here I am" and competes with the cedar for dominance. However, the pine is the superior part. It gives it a bit of an old-school vibe, but interesting. After the conifers have been slightly trimmed, this fragrance reveals itself to be surprisingly multifaceted. It doesn't have much on the ingredient list, which makes it all the more astonishing that it presents itself as both floral and slightly powdery, balsamic, and creamy. How is that, with so few ingredients - that's probably the secret of the creators. I like it a lot! Yes, it does remind me a bit of a foam bath, not the one with the fir needles, but of a blue substance whose name I can't quite recall right now. However, it also reminds me of another fragrance that you wouldn't expect at all, which I only discovered by chance as I tested both in parallel: the Eau de Toilette by Aramis. Yes, they are quite different. While the classic is rather herbal and citrusy, Kenzo Homme comes across softer, cozier. One could almost say it could also be a reinterpretation of that classic. Cistus gives the fragrance something warm and soft right in the middle; the sandalwood doesn't dim that down but rather creates a pleasant "bed," never feeling too dry, as can often be the case with woody scents. Fine fragrance. The sillage is very good in the first hours; it lingers on clothing for days without being annoying. On the skin, it disappears after 8-10 hours, so endurance is definitely present.

This great original definitely deserves a review. I recently treated myself to this new version, and thus the line is almost complete in my collection. I really liked the aquatic charm of the old Kenzo pour Homme Eau de Toilette version, and this "update" has turned out quite well too. It doesn't always work, for example, with Kenzo Power, the new bottle is already a downgrade. Here, the current version is absolutely successful. In terms of popularity, this original doesn't fare as well compared to the famous and slightly hyped Bisch flankers. The DNA of the original from the 90s has aged a bit, but in my eyes, it is absolutely timeless. Here too, you get a great fragrance at a fair price. Around 50€ for 110ml is absolutely fair and worth it if you're looking for a great aquatic scent with everyday usability. Kenzo is anyway a great brand with fair prices. The bottle has of course changed over the years. I still have the old bottle here, and the new bamboo version is definitely much more modern and contemporary. The new Kenzo Homme is surprisingly close to the original DNA in my opinion. I think that's good, as this was a scent that simply came across as likable and was a relief in hot and humid temperatures. Christian Mathieu is also listed as the same perfumer as the original. The pyramid has been significantly streamlined, yet it still smells surprisingly similar to the huge pyramid of the original. This distinctive aquatic freshness and the overall structure have been quite well adopted. This slight greenish touch and the woody notes are shared by both variants. This new version is ultimately a bit more modern, and that typical 90s touch has been somewhat muted. Nevertheless, it retains its charm and remains an aquatic scent that is refreshing and invigorating. The blend of fresh aquatic notes and wood is simply great. This subtle spiciness and the green nuances are also well balanced. Anyone who liked the old version will like this one too. The performance of the OG seemed a bit stronger to me, although this version still falls within the acceptable range. This scent lasts minimally 5-6 hours, and the sillage is in the medium range. It can be worn without problems in between or in everyday use. I can also recommend this new version. A low-budget recommendation is of course the "Acqua | Jeanne en Provence," which is available for a small price. High-end would be the "Shelter Island | Bond No. 9," which is even more luxurious. But this new variant also convinces. This version has retained that likable charm.

For a while, it feels like a long time ago, the predecessor of this fragrance, "Kenzo pour Homme (Eau de Toilette) | Kenzo," had almost reached signature status for me. I emptied two bottles, if I remember correctly. In high school, my love affair with Kenzo Homme began, and later during my studies, we had an intense phase as well.

"Kenzo? Is that you? No... I can't believe it! How are you doing? We haven't seen each other in ages! That's right, you were in some classes with me in high school and in the parallel class - or were you a year above or below me? Oh, I can't remember exactly. Yeah, we never really had much to do with each other, but we knew each other from back then.

A walk through a coniferous forest by the coast. It is warm. The wind blows fresh sea air over your skin and you smell the woods around you. A dreamy association that Kenzo Homme awakens in me. Homme is dynamic and feels fresh in a pleasant and mature way. An aquatic-woody freshness that feels unique to me. It lasts for at least 6-7 hours and truly makes you long for summer.

A stream of woods unleashes itself powerfully and concentrates its strength. Boisterous and raging, moss and forest air rise up to attack relentlessly and mercilessly. The air thickens, and the threat comes at an unstoppable speed to destroy everything. His gaze is motionless and clear, calm sits deep in his soul where restlessness once reigned.

Kenzo Pour Homme has accompanied me since my childhood. For most people, it is just a fragrance, but for me, it is a part of my story. I immediately associate the original from the nineties with my uncle. To me, he was like a man who walked straight out of an advertisement into the real world. Well-dressed, hair slicked back, relaxed and full of confidence.

I used to wear a couple of Maurice Roucel creations in past years, Man's Eau de Toilette and Gai Mattiolo Uomo Eau de Toilette , to be accurate, firm, and brave the former, light and bubbly the latter. I came across the fabulous TL pour Lui Eau de Toilette , and more lately, I discovered two other gems, Bogart pour Homme Eau de Toilette and Voyage Eau de Toilette , and now Forte. I seem I like Roucel's cologne quite a bit. Scuderia Forte occupied the bargain shelf of a perfume store; the 75ml size was discounted and offered 15 euro like its sibling Ferrari Black. After comparing them on a paper strip, I opted for Forte was something so captivating going on. I don't think it's entirely up to par with the Essence line, but it seems like it would be a decent workhorse frag. Scuderia Ferrari Forte is not a kind of Ferrari Black flanker, in my opinion. It is a new fragrance, which follows the current market for shareable, fruity, and sweetened perfumes that are successful at night but can also be worn during the day. Forte is a non-linear cologne that goes through fruity, woody, and oriental stages. I've smelled this a few times on paper and was impressed. A gleaming and chilly start of Italian lemon, pineapple, and crispy apple opens the game on my skin. The sweet pineapple, which is abused in modern scents with Aventus above all, melts with the crisp apple skin and the zesty lemon peel, and the outcome is everything but off-putting. The first thing I get is fruity; the apple is dominant, with like a vanilla-pineapple accord in the background. The result is a fragrance of fruity and delicious output, which does not become cloying thanks to the presence of lemon. Incredibly, both apple and pineapple are perfectly balanced and bring an air of modernity. The heart unveils an extrovert temperament expressed by cinnamon, fleshy juicy plum, and bright orange flowers. As it evolves, the plum covers the effervescent content of the orange blossom as if it were a soft layer of velvet. Without it, we would probably have a fragrance that would walk toward the same proposal of Silver Scent, for example. However, the cinnamon note was very noticeable to me, and it shows now and then. Finally, the base takes time to appear, but it has a denser and fuller side when it arises. The dry down uncovers a daring woody-oriental closing vibrant of cedarwood, powdery vanilla, and musky patchouli that exhibits a healthy and assertive personality. Finally, as the frag draws to a close, you get this caramelized patchouli along with the synthetic fruitiness of the opening. After wearing it for a night, not only has it grown on me, but it has a lot of power and gets a lot of compliments. It smells like a mix of many other fragrances currently on the market; nonetheless, it has its character. The scent has a fantastic performance. The dry down is not cheap with screechy woods or boring ambroxan. Though I do sense a lot of Iso E in the base, but not by itself, it blends well with vanilla and some fruity nuances from the opening. The fragrance does not have an absurd projection, even an Eau de Parfum. It has gained strength, and I feel that exudes well, but only for me and for those who are close, really close. It is not a scent that leaves a trace. In contrast, close to the other fragrances of the Scuderia line, the lasting has significantly improved, remaining more than nine hours on the skin. It is a spring fragrance for evening and night out. -Elysium

On spray it is quite sweet and fruity. Plum and ripe pineapple come to mind. Aas others have mentioned the cinnamon i also detect, but just slightly. It is also quite strong in the opening. Bought it for 25 bucks which is actually not much at all for this quality and 125 ml. I kinda don't reach out much to it, i guess too much sweetness.

This is not a review from a perfume expert, I'm just an enthusiast who wants to help. It is very characteristic and very strong, just like the name. If you are looking for a perfume to use in clubs, a date, bar and similar, it works excellently. Made for night use, mild temperature, cold or even a hot night as long as you don't abuse it with your finger in the sprayer. Sexy, sensual, alpha male, attractive, a masculine scent (I don't see a woman wearing this perfume). That's how it is... Wherever you go, people will ask where and who this smell comes from, it draws praise for being striking and it is to be considered that it is your signature. You will definitely rock wherever you are if that's your intention. Be careful when spraying, the name is not for nothing! Depending on where you are, it can suffocate everyone around you. The projection lasts an average of one hour to two hours. Fixation lasts an average of four to five hours. Of course, if you eat well, if you hydrate yourself, you will have a considerable improvement in performance (not forgetting your skin type as well). Ah, it's pretty cheap for what it offers. It has some similarities (not a clone) to Stronger With You.

My preference for the "fast red racers" from Maranello is well known. That's why I often browse through the men's fragrances to sniff out how many horsepower might be packed into the red and black flacons. Today, I was eyeing the shower gels on offer at Müller; but then I thought about my not-so-small stock here and dropped the idea. And yet, I was looking for a test flacon and found "Scuderia Ferrari - Forte": the excitement grew! "Forte" sounds promising: I could already hear the noise in the pit lane at the Formula 1 races. I discovered a very friendly, fruity-fresh scent that I could really enjoy as a light summer refreshment, e.g. after sports. The fruity mix that greets me is original: pineapple and apple go quite well together, and the lemon adds a certain freshness kick! Cinnamon, plum, and orange blossom form an ensemble that is delightful on its own. Together with the fresh-fruity entrée, an unusual overall note emerges: refreshing fruits complemented by warm nuances. Therefore, the expected tingling - even in the nose - is absent. The base pleasantly rounds off this fragrance: the warm, sensuous vanilla and a pleasant patchouli note blend well with the herb-spicy cedar note. All this results in a likable-fresh summer blend that is almost a bit too delicate and fine for a pure men's fragrance. As a refreshing in-between, "Scuderia Ferrari - Forte" is very welcome to me. Longevity and sillage correspond to an eau de toilette; frequent re-spraying is certainly not unwelcome. Especially on very warm summer days. The flacons are all uninspired: it's a pity, really, because the bodies of the vehicles are quite different. Probably, the concentrated creativity ends up there. Thus, the expectation of a fragrance bolide, further supported by the name addition "Forte," is not fulfilled here. This Ferrari is more like a wonderfully light carriage, pulled by content little horses trotting along, while the sunshade flutters amusingly in the breeze. So it is quite possible that this somewhat leisurely Ferrari will find a parking spot with me.

The fragrances from the house of Ferrari often fall into oblivion or are not even considered. However, many of them, such as Bright Neroli, Amber Essence, or Radiant Bergamot, boast great quality. Among them is this little speedster here, which I ordered blindly due to the appealing scent notes. And I am glad that I made that decision. About the scent: The countdown is on, and the Scuderia starts off very fruity with a hint of apple and pineapple. It doesn't take long for the plum to accelerate and take the lead throughout the entire scent journey. On the home stretch, the plum is quickly joined by light cinnamon and woods, forming a trio on the track. Thanks to the swift arrival of the woods, the scent never becomes too sweet or too fruity and doesn’t stumble around the corners. Before the final sprint, a fine vanilla makes an appearance, bringing the Scuderia and its scent notes across the finish line. The great thing about this fragrance is the perfectly balanced harmony of the notes. There’s nothing annoying or any note that overwhelms your nose. Overall, it’s a lovely mix of light strength and a relaxed scent progression. H/S: Thanks to minimal pit stops, the Scuderia lasts relatively long on the skin. For me, it was about 7 hours. I find the projection to be pleasant; it’s neither strong nor weak. Bottle: I like it thanks to its black-red coloring. The spray head delivers a good spray, but the cap is unfortunately poorly made. I see the Scuderia as a TOP all-rounder. You can use it without hesitation for work and everyday life, as well as for evenings or hobbies, at any time of the year. (Best for spring though) The only downside is the price. Just half a year ago, I got it for only 20€. Today, unfortunately, you have to shell out almost fifty bucks for it, which raises some concerns. Despite everything, my absolute favorite from Ferrari, also because I am a fan of sweeter fragrances. So, anyone looking for a perfect all-rounder and who enjoys fruity, sweet scents with a slightly fresh touch will find what they are looking for here.

Where should I start? The bottle is relatively attractive. The longevity is okay, just enough to get through the day, and the sillage is also okay; at a distance of 20cm, some people can smell it. Now to the scent, it didn't convince me much-sweet plum with cinnamon, unfortunately not as good as it sounds; it has something of candied nuts and cotton candy at the fair.

No one ever seems to talk about this beauty from Bond no 9. Perhaps it is too eccentric. It falls about half-way between their H.O.T. ALWAYS, with all of its luscious and chewy patchouli, and CENTRAL PARK, which features lots of bitter greens and linden. Here the greens are bitter, but the featured flower is lily. There is no leather in this mix, but there is some oakmoss. The patchouli is quite a bit lighter than in H.O.T. ALWAYS, but it is still detectable and yummy, and somehow I find this unorthodox blend to be quite succulent. The sillage is pretty big and the juice itself is quite potent, what I often find to be the case with Bond no 9. When they say "eau de parfum" they really mean it, and many of their edps are stronger than other houses' extraits or parfums. Despite my personal love of this intriguing composition, I must advise a skin test for anyone considering a full bottle. Why? Because I suspect that depending upon a variety of factors this might end up too acrid or even slightly sour on some people. On me it's a dream, but I wouldn't want to smell this, say, on a guy at a gym. No offense intended. ;-)

A few years ago, I visited Hamburg and thus the wonderful shopping street with the Alsterhaus. The perfumery fascinated me: there were hundreds of exotic, unusual scents and brands. Back then, spending Euro 200.00 on a fragrance was unthinkable. An extremely service-oriented employee sprayed Nouveau Bowery on me, among other things. My nose was glued to the back of my hand: extraordinarily fresh green woody. Just before closing time, I returned and invested in Bond N° 9. Proudly, I carried the trophy home. Now the fresh scent came to mind again and 'Goggel' was activated. I found it on Amazon.com. Ordered from America, within 6 days the package arrived, no customs, no fuss. I was thrilled. So the first spray: smells like a glass of water with ice, basil leaves, and a bit sharp from freshly cut pressed limes. I notice a light cucumber note that somehow reminds me of a Caipirinha. Nouveau Bowery is a fun, bright, and cheerful scent with excellent composition and by far one of the best lime notes I have ever experienced. It also reminds me of a bright lime popsicle. The heart and base notes feel green woody with a hint of vetiver. Very long-lasting. In the end, I did everything right. It also smells delicious in this 20° summer. Test it!

I bought this fragrance blind. Just on a whim, so to speak, because I was interested in the ingredients. It starts with a very spicy note, heavily thyme-based. The lime and mandarin are also quite noticeable. Very interesting. I must say, I didn't pick up on the heart note at all. No lily, and I don't know what violet wood smells like or what it even is. The base note, on the other hand, is very strongly influenced by oak moss and vetiver, but it is still very spicy. This thyme runs completely through. This is a very cool, modern fragrance. Clearly for summer. An interesting combination, for sure.

I wrote a glowing review of this on Fragrantica when I first got this fragrance. I'll post it here, and then I'll add my additional thoughts after. "I feel like it is my official duty to come here and tell you how beautiful this fragrance is. This was a blind buy for me based on the fact that I’m somewhat of a Bond No 9 fan and I trust the quality of their scents, and I like freshies regardless. But when I smelled this one- it was an instant home run. This smells like Bleu de Chanel (edt) took a tropical vacation and came back new, improved, and refreshed, ready for the summer and ready for a fun, vibrant, and fresh season. There are a lot of green notes listed, but honestly this is a blue fragrance for me. I don’t know what it is, but I get a strong powdery blue refreshing vibe from this one. My wife is hard to please, but she liked this one as well. Easily one of my favorite Bond scents out of the 5 bottles I own and 6 additional decants I’ve come across. (The other ones I like are Greenwich, Bleeker, Scent of Peace, Hamptons, and maybe Signature)." Additional thoughts: After wearing this one for some time- I absolutely get the "seaweed" green notes in this one. This one is way more of a "green aquatic" fragrance than I initially thought. I called it blue, but I'm definitely throwing in the green as well. Sea moss, kelp, seaweed, whatever it is... after wearing this out for real instead of just sampling on my arm, I got the full effect. Take what you want from that.

I haven't added it to my Bond no. 9 collection just yet, but its time will come unless they discontinued it first. It's not very common in Bulgaria or Europe, but i'll get my hands on it somehow. To give you a reference point, imagine a collaboration between Megamare and Torino 21, but without the citrus. A hold minty scent dominates, creating the unmistakable "island" vibe. I don't get much basin personally, but it doest add a certain richness to the composition. There's also a light floral freshness that gives it some airiness, while the sandalwood, amber, and oakmoss bring in playful masculine depth... it makes the fragrance straight-up sexy. A true heartbreaker scent. It lives up to its name - it really takes you to an island or the shores of Cape Cod Bay

Ferrari's Amber Essence is a sophisticated interpretation of the noble amber accord. For those who still do not know it, amber is one of the most prestigious ingredients in perfumery, ain't a single note but an accord created by the union of resinous, dusty, and sweet notes. Furthermore, it has nothing to do with fossilized amber, which is odorless, or waxy grey amber originated in the digestive system of sperm whales. That being said, I bet that Pierre-Constantin Gueros gave a new spin to the amber we are accustomed to. With a name as Amber Essence, it's rather clear what Ferrari intends to provide you with from the start. To savor this one, you must like amber to some extent. That said, I've been chasing this perfume for a long time, and it was the only missing piece of the Ferrari Essence collection. But I never lost hope, and I finally found it. Before describing the perfume, I would like to spend two words on the perfumer Pierre-Constantin Gueros. His notable creations include Oud Couture from Carolina Herrera, Poise Noire from Yardley London, 02 Owari from Odin, To Be The King from Police, September Morn from Byblos, and The Black Rose from Trussardi, the last three I own and I've already reviewed. If you wondered why I chose that title, i.e., a dry and airy amber, here we go! The opening will surprise most of you fellows since it has no amber nuance at all. Instead, it welcomes and wraps you with a dry cloud, a bit spicy and a tad woody; the cedarwood's pencil sharpener vibe is present from the very beginning. If you expected an opulent and sweet oriental blare, you would be disappointed. All of the spicinesses comes from the coriander seeds, and the bergamot is nearly ephemeral and overwhelmed by other top notes. Precious frankincense acts as a light and refreshing prelude, making the top a bit smoky and resinous without turning it into a church redolence. Amber Essence starts softly with a woody amber topped with a whisper of citrus. Still, it's bright, and I like that they didn't try to cover the amber by highlighting the coriander or bergamot notes. Those are, of course, present, but they serve the background and give Amber Essence a bit more depth. After a while, an all too short while, Amber Essence reveals its heart of blond woods, warm and dry cedar, and spicy nutmeg. At this stage, the projection is already confined to your arms. Like many of the other Ferrari Essence colognes, this one is pretty linear. What you get after a few minutes is what you're going to get from it for a lifetime. That's not a bad point in this case, as the redolence is pleasant and something that I adore getting whiffs of throughout the day. The voluptuous heart transitions to a grand finale in which the ambroxan leads the way, accompanied by the deep and seductive notes of patchouli and musk, which blend to create an unforgettable sensual signature. That's not to say that it's an absolute bomb; it isn't. It comes across as very dry, with the wood and patchouli notes being the amber's prominent supporters. Don't get me wrong, the ambroxan is not used in a Diorish manner as in Sauvage, yet it is more smoky and mossy. The scent is pure love, but performance is a significant disappointment, it is abysmal from a projection viewpoint. It is a lighter fragrance, so don't expect a sillage bomb. You'll be able to get away with spraying more than usual, and since it's quite inexpensive, it doesn't matter too much. However, even though it isn't a loud or heavy scent, it does last a long time, and I could smell it a few days after in clothes. Is it powerful? No, but it's there. This fragrance is versatile because it is so safe and inoffensive. You could wear it casually or out on a date or at the office. It's attractive and has a bit of sexiness to it. If you want something for the night club scene, you might want to go with something that stands out a bit more than this…but for everything else, Amber Essence is excellent. It is limited to wear during the colder months of the year. Overall, do I recommend Amber Essence by Ferrari? Yes, I think it is one of their best scents. Is it amazing? No, but it is reliable. I like the simplicity and the combination of notes that they used for this—a very masculine Amber with woody and musky notes. -Elysium

Ferrari Cedar is unquestionably blue as the Lebanese cedar needles, yet it is not melancholy, has no blueness, and is not blueth at all. Please don't be foolish by the name, cause there is a touch of woodiness within, though it is not a cold seasons cologne. The blue color is also used for the bottle, one of Ferrari's patented color for the Ferrari GT range: the Blu Tour de France, sough-after in models such as the Spider and California. Let's go back to the cologne. I have been looking for this perfume for a long time; in the shops like Sephora, Douglas, or Pinalli, it was on sale around 90 euros, and online, you could have it even for less than 30 euros, but it was sold out everywhere. Then, while I was browsing through various perfume online stores, I came across this and Amber Essence, the very last ones that were missing from my Ferrari Essence collection. Guess how much I found them? Just under 20 euros each, a real bargain. The aquatic nuances with the citrus and watermelon make it smell good, Ferrari did a stellar job, something in the best possible way, or shot this out of the park! Ferrari Cedar Essence starts with a slightly sharp soapy and musky smell almost like a lightly mentholated ocean scented air freshener, the marine accord maybe? The soapiness fades after a few minutes, and you are left with this bright and fresh smell of musk. The reason for the aroma is perhaps the mixture of amber, patchouli, and a hint of citrus freshness. Similar to what is well-known as "White Musk". There are some citrus and watermelon in there, too, but it takes a few minutes before that synthetic oceanic air freshener accord thankfully recedes. It gives it a cold fruity aroma that has a crisp spice to it. What is left is at first something fresh, semi-fruity, and generally pleasant overall. Peppermint is outstanding, hugged by a blend of citrus fruits and sparkling ginger root. A quarter of an hour and the heart notes begin to bright. The aromatic lavender emerges together with the spicy green cardamom, and the marine accord is still lingering in the background, not loud, not overpowering, just perfect. It isn't overly salty like many other oceanic scents, but it's there. The Atlas cedar creates a gloomy atmosphere, it is glorious, and there is no pencil-sharpener vibe as with American red cedar. The evolution is slow and very pleasant. About 2 hours after application, a salty nuance emerges as a result of the oceanic accord. The dry down comes sweet, amber, and a tad gourmand. Although the roasted coffee beans are not so evident as in Ferragamo Uomo, for instance, the smell is present and stays close to the skin. The base features even the Lebanon cedar, with its sweet, rather citrus-like odor that lingers as if the wood was just cut or machined.
