The rum adds depth. A full scent - yet without heaviness. And the sweetness also floats. It is beautiful to hold my husband's hand - and to share a meaningful silence together.

Nowadays his good taste is often called old-fashioned and his good manners are mistaken for poor performance. People rave about the top notes and them being gone too soon. For me, that is where it all starts to come together: The yellow lemon, the cool aromatic-spices and that vanillic note that seems slightly out of place at first. A quick but fascinating transition takes places and leads the whole into a steady state of both warm and fresh elements: A comfortable woody-moss base spiced up with basil and ginger. Intelligent, well-groomed and equally well-mannered, a true gentleman.

What to say about this understated masterpiece? A true, grown-up gentleman's fragrance! I suppose there is not much more to add than what has already been said, but put simply, EVERY man should smell like this! Chanel pour Monsieur was made at a time when men were expected to be self-assured, professional, kind, caring individuals who treat women with respect, seldom raised their voice, always held doors open for people, offered a woman an umbrella in the pouring rain, who remembered to stand up when she entered the room. They were not meant to be ultra-macho or overly assert themselves in the face of others, because a real gentleman was secure in himself and did what he did because he believed in being a good human being. Created in 1955 by the great Henri Robert (the man behind the famous Chanel no. 19), he was master of the understatement, and understood the value of having simple, high quality ingredients that came together to form a whole picture, making the wearer feel self-assured and good about themselves. Rather than only having a single, overpowering note, the fragrance itself is extremely well balanced, so it's hard to pick out any individual notes, however the opening is one of a citrus/oakmoss wave that is both invigorating and at the same time extremely calming. What follows is (in typical Chanel fashion), a slightly bittersweet, almost (to my nose) singiature aldehyde-like hint, to which ginger, cardamom and fresh herbs come through. All before drying down to an amazing vetiver and cedarwood finish, which settles on your skin for the rest of the journey, as well as maintaining the oakmoss vibe throughout. There is nothing about this fragrance which is loud or in your face. This is in no way a powerhouse, it's very subtle and understated, but always lets you know that it is there (without overpowering those around you). It would be perfect on any formal occasion, along with a crisp shirt, suit, tie, and well-made shoes. There is also no reason to suggest that the adult men of this day and age should not wear this fragrance either. Because the values that were expected of men in 1955 are still relevant today! I believe that any man wearing this fragrance would also display a high level of maturity and exude self confidence, because he wouldn't need to assert himself upon those around him, instead he could simply relax, be at ease with himself, and do what he has to do in life without over-proving himself to anyone and everyone. In a word, a TRUE gentleman's fragrance! Perfect for all clean, relaxed, confident men out there!

Pour Monseiur is a classic fougere. Heavy on oakmoss and cardamon, it opens with a citric burst and slowly fades to a woody oakmoss base. Definetely a classic that worth at least a try. Sillage, lasting power and projection are average. Updated January 2014

I've got the new Chanel pour Monsieur EDP 75ml. And it's not easy to convey how it smells in words. It sits right between the EDT and the Concentrée version, I mean, less citrusy and less sweety/vanilla like. But it does remind me the original, or the most recent version as I bought my EDT last June. However, Pour Monsieur EDP is very smooth and so discrete that it's hard to find someone young wearing it. Although it still doesn't smell dated, and quite modern for a chipre, Pour Monsieur EDP is running out of the present times fashion and trends. The notes are very well blended making it impossible for me to pick any one of them individually. CpM edp doesn't scream, doesn't offend, doesn't invade. It sits very close to the skin, very soft, almost powdery, but lasts for a long time. This wonderful smell follows you thoughout the day as an invisible cloud of goodness, of manhood. Too austere for work place, I've tried, unless you work in a very upper class office of any business but a serious one. I expect many could complain about silage and projection, but with Chanel pour Monsieur EDP, or the EDT for that matter, that's a good thing. Very good, indeed. Impossible not to think about other scents like Mitsouko and Profumo, Boucheron pour Homme and even A Scent by Issey Miyake, Eau Sauvage and Miss Dior, and the green scents from Chanel itself like No 19 series and Cristalle. Those who love them will find a new friend in pour Monsieur EDP.

Absolutely stunning Chanel! I thought I would never find a true classic my nose would be drawn to without labeling respectfully "old man vibe" but Pour Monsieur has done it. I do believe this will compete with my first love Platinum Egoiste as my "Upper Class" formal scent? The lemon balanced with the oakmoss makes this a real charmer that just oozes with Gentlemanly style in any decade or era. Over All ~ 9/10 on first wearing! Maybe higher on the second?

Well, I wouldn't call this fragrance 'antique', 'old-fashioned' or 'mature'. Pour Monsieur is a classic which has been around for decades, however it makes such a smooth transition into every decade, paticularly this one. Pour Monsieur is nothing utterly breath-taking.

*Note: This is a review of the current version of Chanel Pour Monsieur. Chanel Pour Monsieur goes on with a gorgeous blast of natural lemon and an herbal lime-like lemon verbena. The lemon-lime herbal citrus accord hangs around well into the heart notes, where the scent turns very powdery while also adding basil and ginger root.

Chanel Pour Monsieur EDT (the page you’re on now) and EDP offer two distinctive experiences. The EDT starts with a sharp citrus blast, that is (to my nose) similar to Dior Homme Sport 2021, making it refreshing for warmer days.

Expectation is so often the issue in not liking a perfume. We have an idea in mind and foster a notion of what a perfume will be. We might have read a list of notes or a review. Really we just shoot ourselves in the foot. But in Pour Monsieur the expectation is Chanel's fault. The top notes of PM are so singingly beautiful, so inspiring.

It is a Brilliant fragrance, Fresh, Citrusy, UPLIFTING and A Timeless Classic. Chanel Pour Monsieur EDT is one of the best men's perfumes that created , very masculine and a bit mature. If you like Eau Sauvage and Armani Eau Pour Homme EDT, you will like this one.

This is a pretty wild and unique blend, and also surprisingly unisex for a feminine designer release. World Power combines a very buttery, sweet tonka bean with a salty skin accord, a hint of the fruity, syrupy opening of the original Kenzo World and a touch of synthetic fresh woodsiness. I suppose that's meant to be cypress. At times the fragrance even smells a little like cinnamon to me, which is likely just the coumarin from the tonka. So, this is not just another Olympea-esque salty beach scent, it has more layers. Unfortunately it gives me the impression that they tried to mix in as many popular accords as possible, so the final result feels a little crowded and chaotic. I enjoy the buttery, spiced and salted tonka sweetness in this, but I'm not a big fan of the rather harsh cypress. I would like it way more if it smelled closer to a real tree and had less of that "random woodsy note in a male-marketed product" going on. All in all, I don't love it, I don't hate it, I'm still not 100% sure what to make of it. I will say that it suits the yellow eye bottle perfectly, but I'll let you decide if that's a good or a bad thing. If the marketing appeals to you, definitely do try.

Maritime-salty vanilla or coconut is already well-known. Personally, I find a maritime note in fragrances really beautiful, especially for warm days. That's why I was very intrigued by this scent. But somehow I didn't get around to getting a sample or decant of it. Two days ago, I was sitting at my PC and decided to finally buy a sample. That didn't happen, as I ended up thinking it would be better to blindly order a 30 ml bottle :D. It arrived today and of course had to be tested right away. Wow, the opening is already grand. You immediately get this beautiful maritime tonka bean. I already find maritime coconut great, but this here... My God, simply dreamy. It doesn't undergo a big transformation. On my skin, it becomes a bit sweeter than at first and develops a soft creaminess. Wonderful aromatic, salty, woody, maritime, sweet (not too sweet), and creamy tonka bean. Although maritime, it doesn't feel cool to me. I perceive it as rather warm. I'm in love. Anyone who, like me, loves tonka bean and also enjoys maritime-salty scents should definitely check this one out.

When I first laid eyes on the Kenzo Eye, I immediately flew towards the original bottle, as I am a fan of dust-catching display pieces. But alas - the EdP just couldn't land with me. The Eye and I looked at each other sadly - it would have been so beautiful... But recently I discovered the EdT - and this "eye-catching" captivated me. Very soft and endearing. Unfortunately, the Eye led a lonely existence - and disturbed my sense of symmetry. Today, however, I found - eureka! - the Power Eye! The title made me hesitate - as I hardly fit the image of a capable power woman - although I spent my youth in "Powerland," namely Sauerland. Just the first spray sweeps my doubts aside, as Power develops a very subtle "strength" - namely a very unique attraction. The sweet-salty note is refined and exciting. Capricious. Green ethereal cypress mixes in - a seductive poetry envelops me. The sexy fairy in the enchanted forest. Which brings us back to the beautiful Powerland - Sauerland. Now two eyes look at me knowingly - and to that plays The Power of Love - by Frankie goes to Hollywood.

Wow, what a surprise...Hats off...wow. I find it enchanting. Something that doesn't smell like rose...not your typical scent. Really wonderfully artificial, but aesthetic. Warm, yellow, and powerful is not an understatement; it is very pompous in a cooler way. It still smells like the bottle after 4 hours on me. The longevity is above average. Tonka is long and rich...the salt is very subtle. It's not mainstream. And one should sleep on it for a night before deciding to get it...for some noses, it can come off as extremely jumpy, here I come.

This scent reminds me of a sunset; it is so beautiful and warm at heart. The cypress remains present the whole time, but with a warm radiance that is soft and somewhat sweetly comforting, oh simply wonderful. I think you can really immerse yourself in this perfume; it lasts for soooo many hours. This salty component is uniquely beautiful, like a woman with her own opinion, and she stands by it. It makes a statement in the surroundings, stands out very well, is quickly noticed, and leaves a positive memory. I am very pleased that there is nothing floral-fruity here. It spreads a relaxed warmth that comes from great self-confidence - this woman knows how to live, smiles at her own little mistakes, has a big open heart, and loves to try out completely crazy things because she is satisfied with herself and her karma, and that smile is her most intimate companion. Beautiful bottle that attracts and feels good in the hand. Interesting, new, and very positive.

The fragrance begins with the sweet spice of tonka bean and transforms within seconds into a salty undertone - it directly reminds me of warm summer days by the sea. It is an intense scent that is still not too heavy for warm days. The salty note combined with the sweetness evokes a gentle summer breeze by the sea.

Allure Homme is by far one of my favourite scents on a man, so it made perfect sense to see what it's many versions were like. Allure Homme Edition Blanche, may not have all the rich woodsiness that made Allure Homme so appealing, but this fragrance is a nice alternative for casual wear and warm days. This fragrance opens with subtle lemon, delicate vanilla creaminess and a dash of pepper. It's quite smooth and soothing. I particularly like how clean it smells on a man. My boy tried on the aftershave version of this fragrance in the store and I really enjoyed its refreshing subtlety. He wasn't so keen on the fragrance unfortunately, mostly because he's a smoker and lighter scents are much harder for him to smell. I must admit that at times, this fragrance was even hard for me to detect. The lasting power is pretty good, in both the EDT and Aftershave concentrations, and like I mentioned before, the sillage is fairly intimate. The drydown is quite possibly my favourite aspect of this fragrance, which is a creamy sandalwood, musk and vanilla blend. In some ways I find this fragrance quite milky, a little similar to Emporio Armani White for Men. Despite its creamy approach and the rather delcious vanilla accord, this fragrance is very masculine, so don't let the notes fool you into dismissing it.

Smells exactly like a lemon pie (with a touch of pepper)! Actually this scent has almost nothing to do with others from Allure line. This is a sweet yet comforting vanilla/lemon scent. Opens with a nice pepper note, then joins lemon (here it remembers me of Habit Rouge for a little while) and finally a vanilla/amber base. Quiet but potent, lasting power is around 8 hours while sillage and projection are discret. Definetely thumbs up! Updated January 2014

Edition Blanche is such a gorgeous creamy lemon! This is my new favorite of all the citrus based fragrances, and i particularly prefer it over DHS, which i find a bit too sharp and fizzy. The slight powderiness makes it feel so refined and comforting, even empowering I would say. I tested both EDTC and EDP before buying it and they perform identical on my skin. Performance wise, projection is marvellous in the first 2 hours, but afterwards it quickly becomes a skin scent and I can barely feel it, even on clothes. After 6 hours it's completely gone. This is pretty much the biggest minus, considering that it's an EDP and Chanel charges about 10 GBP extra, compared to EDTC. 9/10

This flake of allure is certainly a gem, certainly the most interesting. The old edition was edt concentree, replaced by the edp, the latter I find it less citric in opening and less long-lived. I like the fragrances that match the top notes and base notes, although they are very different from each other, it is something that succeeds in a few fragrances (the instant de guerlain pour homme), and allure is one of those. The lemon and vanilla are quite different but thanks to this fragrance they find a beautiful harmony, given surely also thanks to the quality and the choice of the other ingredients. It opens with a lot of lemon and bergamot, which makes it absolutely fresh, very sparkling pink pepper. After a while the citric dulls and gives way to the sweetness of vanilla and tonka, when the vanilla is about to become too sweet vetiver and cedar. Many say it looks like a lemon cake but I don't feel it at all. Very refined and classy, and the way it evolves over time is beautiful. The champagne yellow color renders the goodness of the perfume very well. You can feel the DNA of Allure but it differs a lot from the brothers, not revolutionary but a nice accessory Rating: 8

My partner loves Allure Edition Blanche. Therefore I had to review it. To get to know it better. I love it myself, but I was curious to find out if there are similarities between this and some of the other scents he prefers. So here goes… Let me start by saying that I do not get any pepper - no black, no pink. With that clear, I do get loads of white musk from beginning to end. And it is good. Darn good. I do love white musk, but I admit that it works brilliantly here. The fresh citric notes blend in so well with the leather, and underneath it all - pure white musk. Amazingly enough, it lasts for many hours which surprised me. The freshness indicates that it will soon be gone and you will have to spray again. But not this one. Bottle wise I am happy. It has the original Chanel look and it suits the scent so well. 338/365

Blanche EDT opens with a sharp and dry use of lemon, vetiver, sandalwood, and pink pepper. You’re absolutely going to have to be a citrus lover with this one, to really appreciate it, as it is very sharp upon opening. The lemon is going to dominate through much of the wear.

I know I've gone off the deep end, but I smell something akin to MFK's Amyris Homme EDT in this. Except it's a "sportier," less sophisticated fragrance wherein every shared note is slightly worse. Before you spray this, pop a couple of TUMS, because the citrus opening is a very acerbic and makes me feel like I'm about to develop a horrible case of acid reflux.

You have it tough. We constantly nag at you. Don’t leave your socks lying around, put the toilet seat down, take out the trash, you never can, you never do… It’s time to praise you for everything that makes you so lovable and unique: We love it when you accompany us shopping and patiently evaluate the 500th outfit.

Chanel Allure Homme Edition Blanche was a blind purchase. And although that had often gone terribly wrong in the past, I couldn't help myself and ordered it. My curiosity had to be satisfied, and the good reviews I had read must have had their reason, I told myself. When it arrived and I tried it for the first time, I felt confirmed in my initial fears.

Chanel Allure Homme. Hm… I think the first thing you read about this fragrance line is almost always the same. These scents are said to attract women well, especially regarding the sport line. This seems to be true, as a few comments on these fragrances have shown that the sport scents actually smell good and are not just any insignificant sport fragrances.

Living in Texas, I knew i had to be one of the 400 people that would get their hands on this limited-edition fragrance. Being a proud Texan and a fragrance lover all at once, I knew that I had to snap this up and to make it all the more better, this fragrance has been created by Bond No.9 which is without a doubt one of my favourite niche fragrance companies. Texas went in a completely different direction to what I was initially expecting, I was actually something that was quite heavy, woody and masculine; kinda like an Homage to the heritage of Texas but this is quite fresh and very juicy. Its fruity notes avoid smelling immature and instead smell very grown up and very creamy in a quite sensual and adult way. The Pineapple note and blackcurrant seem to dominate the first stages of the fragrance but they never disappear, instead they sink to the bottom and form a foundation for the luscious Gardenia and Creamy vanilla to crash. The vanilla in this scent smells sexy and sort of hints at the fragrances versitility and wearability for the nighttime. The lasting power is fantastic, Its without a doubt one of my favourite Spring/Summer fragrances and its something I wear proudly. But even if i was in the situation where I disliked the fragrance, I would still buy it just for the bottle- Its fantastic!

I get a significant litchi note from the beginning to the end. Though it's very detectable, it's soft and tender, not in an aggressive way. It's fruity, sweet and sour, but incredibly clean. It doesn't smell too girly but absolutely cute and I think it works well in spring, even in hot summer as it's fresh. However, it's probably more suitable for young ladies IMO due to the image of litchi. I tested EDP too and they're very different, as EDP has somehow a masculine vibe. The longevity is about 5h and the sillage rather close. Originally written in 2013

When I finally dug out my Madly today and sprayed it out of curiosity, joy and delight enveloped me. How could I have overlooked this beautiful, unusual scent for so long? But it patiently waited for me. I am extremely fond of its smoky-sweet combination. While I don’t find it crazy, it is beautifully controversial. I like style breaks, and the sweet fruity pairing of pear and lychee, surrounded by a mysterious delicate blue-gray smoky note, is very appealing. For me, as a smoking sweet tooth, it’s just right. An afternoon on the sofa, U2's Beautiful Day in my ears, a box of chocolates at hand, a cigarette, and letting my thoughts drift. Pure relaxation. Jasmine and heliotrope add something distinctly floral. Along with the spicy cedar scent wafting over from the wardrobe. I have to think of my first cigarette, a Reval without a filter - certainly not the right choice for beginners - but it tasted wonderful. Like freshly baked bread. The quirky smoky note thankfully remains present throughout the scent's development. I am reminded of Oscar Wilde, who wrote: The cigarette is the complete archetype of enjoyment. It is delicious and leaves us unsatisfied.

I have to express my enthusiasm: This scent is delicious! As an Eau de Toilette, it lasts incredibly long! And the bottle is a true delight for the eye! Right from the first spray, the pear unfolds, sweet and fresh, similar to the "Lola" by Marc Jacobs. Just behind the pear, there is something indefinably sticky-sweet, most likely the lychee (olfactorily far from the real lychee). Nevertheless, this sweet something is not too overpowering for my nose, as it quickly makes way for the pear again. The jasmine, which unfolds after about an hour, is quite subtle. In my opinion, that's a good thing, as a hint of pear still lingers, creating a soft, creamy texture together with the blooming jasmine. At some point, I believe it was well past 2 PM (sprayed shortly after 8 AM), a pleasantly powdery feeling with a warm, "cuddly" note spread on my skin. I am blown away, the EdT is like fruit salad and cream pudding plus a fluffy cotton candy feeling. Anyone who appreciates a light, fruity sweetness in perfumes will surely enjoy Madly Kenzo! And this dew drop definitely brings good vibes with its heavenly sugar water!

~ Inspiration ~ Almost 2 years ago, I tested "Madly EDP," which I didn't like at all due to its smoky components. So the EDT ended up on my watchlist, and I received a leftover sample during a swap. ~ Bottle ~ The glass bottle in droplet shape was retained - here in pink instead of purple, which promises a lighter scent (the colorful butterflies on the outer box match this very well!). ~ Fragrance ~ It starts very fruity-sweet with juicy pears and lychee. Heliotrope and jasmine flowers give it a slightly exotic but subtle expression. Cedarwood and white musk provide a balanced base. ~ Longevity ~ On my skin, it lasts around 4-5 hours (not much longer on clothing and hair). 2 sprays are enough; otherwise, you smell like a gummy bear. ~ Occasion ~ It fits well into the warmer days and evenings in spring and summer (definitely suitable as an office scent for sweet-toothed individuals). ~ Conclusion ~ I like it better than the EDP. At first, it reminds me of Tropifrutti by Haribo!

Today at Müller, relaxing a bit after work, checking out what's new - and there it was... Madly Kenzo! Great packaging, a new Kenzo? I didn't know it yet... quickly sprayed it on: The first whiff immediately reminded me of Schauma shampoo. Those of us with not-so-young noses here still remember the scent from the 70s well. This sweet-creamy-perfumed... OK, moving on, looking at the new nail polish colors - still overwhelmingly smelling like shampoo with... hmm... I don't really know... could it be? Somehow a slight spicy hint of Kenzo Jungle... tsk tsk Heading home, first a coffee... and I'm convinced: This scent doesn't know what it wants to be... just madly... On one hand, it's sticky sweet and creamy, I can't detect the pear/lychee, I'm missing the fruity aspect - on the other hand, the cedar and musk give it a spiciness that just doesn't seem to fit for me. To me, Madly Kenzo! smells like a mishmash of a perfume - not hüh, not hott... and definitely not worth buying. What a shame... It's great that the previous comment praises the scent so much, because what if all fragrance enthusiasts found the same scent wonderful.

I received Madly as a miniature in a Kenzo set. I approached the first test quite positively because I usually liked Kenzo. But already with the first dab, I had to wrinkle my nose. Could this fruity-sweet teenage scent really be from Kenzo? Good thing I didn't buy it blind, I thought. But now I had a few milliliters. What to do? First, into the drawer... and forget.

I love "Allure Sensuelle" and that bottle almost reached its last drop, so, when I saw "Allure EdP" on sale and wanting to try a different yet *same* scent, I blind bought this - Mistake. On my skin I get a bad peach note that is arguing with the vetiver, cedar and God knows what else it's picking a street-fight with! But it's making me dizzy and slightly nauseous. I get none of the familiar Chanel vibe at all! It might as well be a completely different house! I had to wash it off....a rare occurrence but another harsh reminder that blind buys are risky even when you already own and like the *original* or *flanker*. Alas, to all of you whose chemistries embraces this: enjoy! I guess I have to find a home for this one and grace the Chanel counter once again with my lovely presence : )

I was surprised that this was a Chanel perfume. It was definitely not what I would have expected from their range. It's so deliciously soft and feminine. Other Chanel fragrances, to my nose, smelt sharp and mature, but not this one. On my skin it transforms into a lovely warm vanilla and jasmine, which surprisingly exudes sex appeal. I was always one for describing Chanel fragrances as classy and conservative, but never in my life would I have thought that one of their scents would be so sensual and sexy. Allure still does, however, stay true to the Chanel style, remaining classy, elegant and timeless. What I love most about this fragrance is its ability to suit almost every occasion. You could wear it to work, on a date, to a wedding or anywhere your heart desires. You wouldn't even have to re-apply this perfume at the end of the day because the lasting power is so good. It is fairly obvious and easy to conclude that a woman that wears this has impeccable taste in perfume.

I cannot share the positive attitude towards "Allure". To me, it is a disappointing, boring fragrance. Too cool and detached, repetitive and dull. Probably aimed at rich business women who want to feel secure by purchasing a famous brand, but where is the soul of this perfume?
I'm in love with Allure. For me, it is the best perfume ever. Elegant, sophisticated, sexy and seductive. Allure is not just a fragrance, it's a must have!

She bears the right name, she is indeed really alluring. So well blended and beautiful. A classy lady with a young vibe. I receive tons of compliments when wearing Allure, mainly from other women. It is a really a divine scent.

I class this as an oriental vanillic. Super strong and heady, in the genre of Shalimar. Tiring of it, I handed it over to my girlfriend, who loved it up and was last heard complaining there was only now a dribble left in the bottle.

I tested this for two days. I would so love to like just one 'Chanel' like many do. I loved the opening, which is why I asked for a sample. First ten minutes I find this scent alluring indeed: creamy, uplifting, unique and mesmerizing...but then, after drydown, I find it a mainstream, uninteresting scent.

This fragrance has a delicate character that reflects the idea of quiet luxury often associated with Chanel’s classic style. It carries a feminine and refined elegance without feeling heavy or overly formal. The composition is smooth and warm, with a radiant quality that makes it feel polished and balanced.

...and indeed throughout the entire day spent with the EdP from Allure. Since its release in 1999, I have happily contributed to the success of Allure, as I have often and gladly sold it. Some fragrances make it difficult to characterize them in a sales conversation, to convey them to the customer in just a few words.

Last Saturday it was time! Our youngest daughter attended her first ball. For weeks beforehand, what am I saying, almost for months, "the event of the year" was discussed. Finally, she had her "seven things" together - dress, shoes, purse, jewelry. The fragrance also had to be just right. Not the typical young girl scents were in demand.

As a woman, I love wearing rich, woodsy and masculine scents, especially if they're infused with pepper or ginger. Most of the scents I wear that are of this calibre are very strong and at times, offensive. Kenzo Tokyo has a subtlety that doesn't bother me in the slightest. Its softness provides a clean and refreshing quality that I would have never expected. The fragrance opens with light, watered-down citrus, pepper and tea. This blend is quite pleasant and refreshing. Its sensuality tends to immerge more on warmer skin or during the warmer months. With that thought in mind, Kenzo Tokyo has the versatility to be worn all year round. I'd describe this fragrance as being sometimes sharp and sometimes smooth. The citruses, pepper and ginger keep the scent lively, yet the base of soothing woods and a hint of non-smokey incense keeps the scent grounded. Sometimes I feel a little strange because Kenzo Tokyo does have some very masculine moments, but for the majority of the scent's development it keeps me entertained and I still feel like a woman wearing it. I took a huge chance with Kenzo Tokyo, having decided to buy it blind based on reviews calling it a woodsy and gingery incense delight. Well, I am disappointed that there's not a whole lot of incense, but I am impressed with its subtle, gingery woods. I recommend.

Kenzo Tokyo smells great but when you're enjoying it it's just gone. I smell a lot of spices with a great ginger and tea note in and drydown. My only complaint is about longevity, which is very weak. Updated January 2014

When I brought the bottle to my nose, I immediately felt a fresh tartness, which should reveal the top notes, as I understood, and when I applied it to my hand, I was convinced of my assumption, and I heard the spiciness of ginger and the sourness of lemon more clearly. In the middle, I heard a pleasantly spicy aroma of pepper, with a grassy-smoky aftertaste. The finish reveals woody notes from the guaiac wood with, I think, a leathery, smoky wood from the nutmeg and a hint of clove.

Tokyo starts with an appealing ginger and citrus note, which I quite like. Dior Homme Sport largely thrives on this combo, and this fragrance has really captivated me at the moment. The rest of the fragrance pyramid sounds quite interesting but does not deliver on its promise. Everything that follows is just nutmeg. The same applies to food: in small amounts, this spice can be quite enticing, but in such an overdose as in Tokyo, it quickly becomes inedible. It's a shame; I was expecting an interesting, fresh, spicy, and woody autumn fragrance. I’m very sorry to rate a Kenzo fragrance poorly, because although I wouldn’t want to wear all the scents from this brand, I find them to be very well made. I rate Tokyo poorly because it feels too unbalanced to me. If the nutmeg had been toned down and the other notes emphasized more, I would probably like it significantly better.

Tokyo caught my attention when I joined Parfumo and our hobby over 2 years ago, as it kept appearing at the end of the Men's Top 100. Therefore, it was also my first point of contact with the Kenzo brand, but unfortunately, it was never really available to test in stores. Whenever I searched for it, I was directed to the numerous Kenzo Hommes, which I also grew to love. By now, its ranking has fallen so much that it probably won't rise back up anytime soon. In my opinion, it doesn't need to, because although it's quite nice, it belongs only to the midfield even within the Kenzo cosmos. The scent is somehow Kenzo, somewhat Japanese. But it is very different from what I expected. For a brief moment, the opening feels a bit hectic, which would fit in the urban jungle of Tokyo. However, the fragrance quickly calms down, becoming almost ethereal and much more aligned with the Japanese countryside. Here, the marketing only fits in parts, unlike with Woody, where everything works perfectly together. Tokyo is a citrusy fragrance with tea-like notes and at the same time spicy-woody. But as mentioned, it only feels chaotic at first; then everything becomes discernible. The citrusy opening reminiscent of Dior Homme Sport, followed by the calming ginger tea, and concluding with the spiritual celebration in the heart of the metropolis with woods and a lot of gentle pepper in the cocktail. Cocktail fits, but I don't think there are that many trees and green spaces in Tokyo. Overall, the scent would deserve the color green the most for me, a green pencil accord. Bottle: even though it somewhat resembles Axe and Co., I really like the Japanese city-speed design. Sillage: very, very close to the skin and safe. Longevity: not catastrophic but close to 4 hours. So split like the Crazy 88 in Kill Bill, and therefore also simultaneously indecisive and strangely tame for me.

Tokyo by Kenzo smells to me just as it is named. But I don't mean the modern, neon-lit, and hectic Tokyo; rather, I refer to the traditional, contemplative, and nature-connected Tokyo. The Tokyo that is omnipresent but less obvious and more familiar. With this fragrance, the imagination begins with a traditional tea ceremony in a tatami room.

What this perfume has to do with the Moloch Tokyo is something only the creator can say. Well, I have never been to the Land of the Rising Sun, but this scent is not particularly Japanese and thus exotic; it could easily pass as an ordinary European fragrance. The association with Tokyo might come from the modern and futuristic attributes that this Kenzo brings with it.

Starts off fresh, then actually settles into the ethereal, as described by predecessors. The spicy-woody base with tea nuances truly has a Japanese flair. However, that was neither the reason for the purchase nor why I liked the fragrance so much. It was different and rarely encountered. Subtle sillage, unfortunately rather weak longevity.

Sorry for my English in advanced.. I used to be obsessed with it before truly knowing about what I liked in perfumes and the notes are very fresh and sweet to me and still like this but it’s too weak and doesn’t last on my skin at all… I would love it if this would be more powerful and long lasting.

Very feminine, very quiet, two of my favourite notes, however this doesn’t save this from being unbelievably pedestrian and dull(to my nose). Great gym scent, room scent, wardrobe scent and just before bed scent. Smells young and juvenile, but not in a cloying way. It’s just a simple, mass appealing fragrance with no nasty surprises. Not full bottle worthy, but worth a 10ml try. The sillage isn’t that great but it does slowly lift of the skin throughout the day. The longevity is so so, I got about four-five hours. After 2-3 hours I had to bring my nose close to smell it but that may be olfactory fatigue as it is very linear. There’s no evolution with can bore ones nose. What it is good for is layering with other deeper fragrances to add a floral, slightly fruity haze to other highly fruity + resinous or floral + resinous compositions. I’ve worn this with a few from Motif Olfactif, namely Nectar Boisé , Moments and De Toma à Zouma .

Chance Eau Tendre opens with a tangy freshness that immediately makes me think of apple - or rather, it’s definitely the quince. Either way, it’s fresh, light, perfect for sunny days when you want something simple and effortless. But that simplicity leans a bit toward teenage fragrance territory: an innocent, sweet juice, almost too tame, lacking depth and character. It’s the kind of olfactory candy you’d wear for a relaxed afternoon, without trying to impress. For what it offers, it feels a bit overpriced. In short, Chance Eau Tendre is a nice little treat, but it doesn’t really make me dream - just a gentle smell of apple, and nothing more.

At first there is a nice green apple scent (I suppose that is the quince) and a nice light musk holds down the base of the scent. There's really not much else to say about this scent. It's light and slightly fruity, but like there's a basket of apple somewhere around, you're not biting into a juicy apple. And those baskets are getting taken away even though you were sweating picking them and you don't get to enjoy a single one of them. Fades very fast on my skin, within an hour it turns to a skin scent.

What a tasty fragrance! It's a very good summer fragrance for ladies which are looking to have a good time. I'm usually not a big fan of super-floral scents, but this one really stood out to me because of that quince. Made me like this fragrance a lot. While not the most unique, it's still worth a try. Very youthful and uplifting.

This smells like hugging a freshly showered child who smells of shampoo but accidentally pooped a little in their pants. If I did not get the faint smell of fecal matter this would have been a great perfume. My husband also picked up on the smell so I know it is not just my nose. Maybe it is the quinche throwing it off for me.

I would probably own a full bottle of this perfume if I didn’t get into sampling more niche and unique perfumes. Eau Tendre is such a pretty, easy going and soft scent that can be used for any occasion all spring and summer long. I catch the rose, but it’s youthful, perfumey and citrusy bright.

I bought this scent a few weeks ago because I ran out of my old signature scent (YSL Mon Paris) and wanted something similar but a bit more grown up. I was so pleasantly surprised by this. For some reason, I hadn't tried any Chanel perfumes before (I was worried that they were very old-fashioned). I was waffling between getting this and Chance Eau Splendide.

sometimes the well-known ones are well-known for a reason! i love the way the notes interplay in this one — i don’t know if it’s to do with the ratio of scent to scent or what, but for my nose, it works really well. i get the fruity notes up-front, especially that quince, but the florals come up afterward in a nice blooming bouquet.

Right off the bat: as expected, Chanel hasn't completely reinvented the wheel with the launch of an EdP version of the now classic EdT. The latter represents citrus-floral lightness, so I was curious to smell the differences to the new EdP. After spraying, both smell the same to me. Citrus freshness with a hint of quince sweetness and a floral undertone.

Kenzo's Le Monde est Beau is a funny little fragrance. It's citrusy and metallic, calming and energizing. Nowadays, citrus fruits and juices are available in the US in glass jars, juiceboxes, or cans with a plastic (BPA!) liner. But they used to be sold only in unlined tin cans. I thought the metallic taste of the can was part of the good flavor of the canned grapefruit juice my mom would put in my lunch or the chilled canned mandarin orange sections she would serve for dessert. After much thought, I've realized the odd but lovely note that springs out at me from Le Monde est Beau - it's mandarin oranges in a cold tin can. And so it joins my personal pantheon of childhood smells!

"The world is beautiful" is one of the fragrances that surprised me the most when I checked the ingredient list after testing it. Blackcurrant and mandarin? It's not citrus-fresh on my skin, and definitely not sour-berry. Cherry blossom and magnolia? I can't really identify them. Cherry blossom does have a quite distinctive scent. Tonka bean and cedar? I can't recognize any individual woods. What I smell first after applying it is GARDEN! And not a perfectly maintained garden where the boring classics like lilacs, roses, tulips, etc. bloom neatly in a row in the flowerbed. But a wild garden with shrubs, weeds, tall grass, a few herbs, and lots and lots of marigolds. This green, herbaceous impression I have can at least be attributed to the basil, and I have to do that because marigolds are probably not in here at all. But anyone who has ever crushed one of those flowers in their hand will immediately recognize this scent. Floral, herbaceous, even a bit bitter. I really like it. Maybe it's due to the combination of basil and jasmine. The blooming spring garden is bathed in sunlight, it's warm. The dew from the cool night has long evaporated. And the longer you lie in this garden, the softer the grass becomes, the more aromatic and warmer the air gets, and the more you immerse yourself in this supposed chaos of nature, which possesses its own unique perfection. I get the impression of delicately sweet nectar that joins the green herbaceousness, without taking away any sophistication and naturalness, but rather rounding it off with gentle, elegant warmth. This fragrance belongs to a category that I personally call "non-perfumes," as you don't carry around a squeaky fruity or sticky heavy cloud that you identify as perfume in the first second. Instead, you are surrounded by a delicate, aromatic veil that accompanies you without pushing itself to the forefront and ideally merges with your own personal scent aura. It's almost impossible to overdo such fragrances, but they manage to make you forget them, and you don't even notice how you suddenly bounce around in a good mood and light-heartedly, because the world is simply beautiful in those moments. The world is beautiful is not cutely sweet, fruity playful, or heavy, but aromatic, natural, and friendly. It resembles no floral scent I have ever tested or owned. And it couldn't have been given a more beautiful name!

This fragrance is unique and an absolute gem, strangely quite unknown. Interestingly, it happens to be created by the same perfumer as my other "must always have" fragrance (Prada - Infusion d'iris), even though they are completely different. I smell a fresh, green, slightly wild garden in the evening sunlight, with a lovely sweetness without any sugar on it. There is nothing stuffy-floral, there is nothing sugary-papery. It smells incredibly authentic and natural like a garden, very green but without being too lemony-bitter as often found in similar fragrances. A childhood memory: My parents always had marigolds in their small garden, the lush green, the rich orange of the flowers... In the summer evenings, when my father watered everything again with the garden hose and it smelled of damp earth, late summer days, and the beloved, strong, robust marigolds... Swallow cries in the background. This fragrance also has the marigolds, but paired with this beautiful zesty sweetness: I literally see the colors orange and green in front of me when I smell Le monde est Beau. As a child, I was always very much outdoors in nature, also a lot with animals, that was my whole longing. It is still the same, and I associate this fragrance with that. It is very close to the essence of my character. Even though I don’t wear it very often because there are always other beautiful distractions/fragrances - I find it impossible that I won’t like this fragrance in 10 or 20 years, even if I should forget it in the meantime. It is far too close to my being. However, it is a bit too fresh for a signature scent. I wear this fragrance when I want to uplift myself, when I want to accomplish something, or when I have a difficult call ahead. I know it refreshes and cheers me up for upcoming tasks, I know it brings me back to myself through its closeness to nature.

Most Kenzos take my breath away, but that's on me, not the fragrances! Not so with the two pebbles Ça Sent Beau Eau de Toilette and Le Monde est Beau . The fact that I even discovered Le Monde est Beau is thanks to Parfumo. I literally stumbled upon this little stone while browsing and couldn't believe my eyes because of the identical appearance of the two bottles. How could it be that I had not heard, seen, or smelled anything about this fragrance in the 27 years since its release? "We've launched a new fragrance, but shhh!" Even now, after this discovery, I had to resort to an online shop. Asian understatement is very pleasant - but it can also be detrimental for a product. But now finally to the object of desire: The box in white and bright orange hints at a cheerful content inside. The small bottle, a rounded glass pebble, is adorned with a slightly raised leaf pattern, the name KENZO also raised into the glass. The glass is somewhat more transparent than that of Ça Sent Beau Eau de Toilette . At the top, the well-known opulent flower reigns as the cap. So good, so beautiful, and so familiar to me so far. The first spray delights me briefly with a zesty mandarin, and then the gardener comes around the corner with a big bouquet, freshly cut stems (basil), beautiful and colorful. When I hold my nose close to my arm, I even catch a whiff of a few crushed currants that the gardener probably accidentally tied into the bouquet - a little twist with a cheeky wink. From the floral arrangement, the magnolias stand out, gentle yet distinct, with cherry blossoms and jasmine supporting them. The marigolds mentioned in other descriptions are nowhere to be sniffed out. In my region, these are understandably also called "student flowers" and "stinkerle". However, this bouquet here smells very fine. With every movement, a different nuance wafts pleasantly around me, and after a while, tonka bean waves calmly from the bouquet. Only after hours do I perceive some wood. This gives the whole thing a certain grounding, as the overall progression is rather airy and light without significant depth. Le Monde est Beau is just as it (unfortunately) was marketed, pure understatement, not a loudmouth but a cheerful little cloak that I can wrap around myself at any time, whether I’m having a good day or need a bit of cheering up. A feel-good fragrance, indeed. In my review of Ça Sent Beau Eau de Toilette , I mentioned that the fragrance, in my opinion, doesn't quite match the bottle. With Le Monde est Beau , the little bottle finally has the content that harmonizes with its round, friendly shape.

... and if that doesn't quite hold true, you just spray yourself a little bit more beautiful. "Le Monde est Beau" is one of my feel-good fragrances. In this respect, the somewhat strange naming of this serendipitous find from the lower shelves of the drugstore fits. "The world is beautiful" starts with a zesty, slightly sulfurous-bitter wake-up grapefruit note. Yellow pomelo with thick skin, sliced open and lightly sugared, accompanied by a small glass of freshly squeezed mandarin juice. The scent remains herbaceous fruity with a fairly dominant, but not herbal, blackcurrant leaf note. I can't really understand where all the flowers from the pyramid are supposed to be. For me, "Le Monde Est Beau" is clearly fresh-green with a touch of dark berries and less floral. The fragrance does not seem particularly complex and has no particularly surprising scent progression. After the invigorating citrus fruit note at the beginning, it leaves a lasting "just hopped out of the shower" feeling, underpinned by a pleasantly herb-fruity and green-woody base, and lasts well throughout the entire workday. The bottle (the lying 30ml hand-charmer is a similar eyesore made of ribbed pressed glass with a plastic cap resembling rose petals in a milk glass look) should probably be hidden far back in the cupboard. But not too far, because the content is a friendly fresh "everyday fragrance" at an acceptable price for leisure and for the office, as long as the dress code allows jeans and t-shirts and is not strictly set on elegant business attire.

Flower Tag has nothing in common with the first Flower fragrance from Kenzo. For me, that's a good thing because I don't like it at all. What is powdery and sweet in FbyK is completely absent here, as Flower Tag starts with a cool fruity top note, where the mandarin and the herbaceous black currant create a refreshing opening without any notable acidity. I can't really perceive the rhubarb, but perhaps it ensures that the first impression of Flower Tag is more green than bright red for me. This invigorating yet calm top note also accompanies the heart of the fragrance, so the floral notes are clearly present but neither sultry nor sweet. Now Flower Tag comes across as elegant, subtly sophisticated, and soothing. I like this very much, especially since the character of the fragrance does not fundamentally change in the dry down. The perfume fades with a very subtle and soft base. I am still trying to transition from being a coffee drinker to at least an occasional tea drinker, and the base of Flower Tag has inspired me to round off my black, herbaceous tea with a touch of vanilla. I can't quite put into words what that certain something is about Kenzo fragrances - such a Japanese straightforwardness, more Zen and Ikebana than Honda and Sony, that's exactly what I also appreciate in Flower Tag. I do have one point of criticism. According to the sales department, there will hardly be any samples of Flower Tag in vials. In front of me are a few sachets that are currently being distributed. They also don't contain a tissue, a wax strip, or similar soaked materials for the purpose, but when you tear them open, 0.7ml of the fragrance splashes out directly. This has been enough - to not waste anything - to soak my entire arm with it. So, it's not possible to test the fragrance drop by drop with these sachets, or to carry a sample in your handbag for a few days without making a mess. There’s no way to avoid spills here. However, this is not particularly threatening, as the sillage of Flower Tag is not disruptive to the environment. Aside from that, Flower Tag is clearly a 70% fragrance for me. I don't necessarily have to buy it, but I would wear it without hesitation and have no objections to it being on our shelf recently.

Twelve months in a year, twelve pieces in a dozen, twelve jurors in a jury, twelve apostles in Christianity, and twelve flankers for Flower! There are not only the perfume (Extrait) but also annual editions, seasonal editions, etc. etc., and the Flower Day. Day - as in a tag, nameplate, plaque, or similar - describes it quite well. It is simply one of the floral flankers to Flower, with the usual suspects as components. First, there are light citrus fruit notes, then flower upon flower, until eventually a rather musty and unpleasant animalic musk note takes over, before the "scent" completely fades away. Unfortunately, this takes quite a long time, as Flower Day is also quite long-lasting. Thankfully, the sillage is rather weak, and only this way could I endure the animalic note over time. For my taste, Flower Day is one of the countless citrus-floral-fresh-and-clean scents that are offered to us with various advertising flyers from various drugstore chains like sour beer. Basically, it doesn't really matter which of these scents one ultimately chooses; they all smell almost the same. The bottle - which, by the way, is often copied by other floral fragrance manufacturers and sold on the bay - is not really beautiful. I only like two bottles from Kenzo; Le Monde est Beau and UFO, but that is purely a matter of taste. I can do quite well without the bottle and its contents.

You have to be persistent, otherwise you won't get anywhere! And that's how I ended up with a 2 ml sample of this fragrance. Like Kenzo Winter Flowers, Flower Tag doesn't really have much in common with the original. The top note is very fruity with a lot of blackcurrant. The heart note is floral, although I can't identify a specific flower. In the transition to the base, the blackcurrant reappears along with a citrus note. The base has a lot of musk and a bit of vanilla. Overall, but especially in the base, the scent strongly reminds me of I Love Love by Moschino. The longevity of Flower Tag is slightly better than Moschino, lasting about 3 to 4 hours. I wouldn't buy it like Turandot, but I would wear it without hesitation.

A stroll through the sunny flea market. Here and there, vendors were also offering their perfume bottles, and I stopped at the sight of a beautiful cherry-red bottle. Aha - Kenzo Flower Tag. Clearly, the resemblance to the Flower bottle was unmistakable. Kenzo Flower is worn by my mom, and it suits her very well. Does Tag smell similar? Not at all! With the first spray, a lush fruit basket opens up, filled with rhubarb, currants, and tangerine. Mmmm delicious! A scent like in grandma's jam kitchen. Jasmine and lily of the valley hint at summer. And musk and vanilla provide depth and longevity. One could also translate the English "Tag" with the German "Tag". Just a beautiful flower day!

I hear this quite often from my husband, as I can't get past this Japanese fragrance! I found Flower really great a few years ago and my love for this brand began! No idea if I owned a bottle. Definitely a sample and I’ve sprayed it in the store several times! Beautifully floral and lightly sweet, and also the delicate slim bottle! Flower by Kenzo Oriental is a bit too heavy for me, but again, Flower by Kenzo Le Parfum is very beautiful. I can't judge the other Flowers, as I haven't tried them yet. I not only tried Flower Tag, but I made a mess. Man, how I hate those tear-open sachets. Anyway, my freshly washed brunette hair, my arms, and even the table smell pleasant. It has a warm, soft, and floral scent. I also don't recognize any specific flowers, but rather this all-too-familiar floral herbal tea note with licorice in it. A light sweetness and also zesty! Yes, I also like the fruity top note - zesty and not too sticky, not too heavy, no danger for my respiratory organs and head! Flower Tag is again a lovely Kenzo: not intrusive, too heavy, too sweet, monotonous, boring..., but pleasant for the wearer to smell good in everyday life!

Chanel’s Chance is a fragrance that I could never go wrong with. Elegant, polite and sophisticated, it always works for me no matter what the occasion is. The fragrance reminds me of a fine crystal with a simple but elegant construction, clear and precise lines and impeccable symmetry. There are no elaborate ornaments but the clarity of this scent feels relaxing and energizing at the same time. Somehow the focal point of this fragrance is always me, not the scent. It smells fresh, clear, transparent and modern but very sophisticated. Chance opens with a fresh and aromatic citruses mixed with the pink pepper. The pineapple note is there but it is definitely not overripe or sweet one. It smells fresh and light. I also get a light patchouli note right from the start. I love how patchouli is used in this fragrance. It gives nice accent to the top, heart and bottom notes but it NEVER overpowers the other notes. The heart notes are transparent and light jasmine and hyacinth. The dry down is a mix of woody vetiver and patchouli with just a hint of vanilla. The sillage and longevity are medium but I normally reapply the scent during lunch and dinner anyway as the dry down gets a bit light with my skin chemistry. I definitely recommend this scent. (This review is for Eau de Toilette)

It's not my scent. It's not for everyday use. And yet- I love it for the feeling it gives: I feel like a real woman- sexy, confident and beautiful. I feel like every man can be mine. I feel like the whole world will be in my hands. I am addicted to this perfume.

Chanel CHANCE seems to be intended for the same market as ALLURE (which I love) and is quasilinear as well, but somehow it doesn't measure up. My problem with this edp can be summed up in four p's: pink peppercorn plastic patchouli. Somehow the pink peppercorn mingles with the patchouli and the musk to produce a plastic smell. I love patchouli, but here it really does seem to have the texture of an artificial plant, which will stay green until the end of time, adorned with finely ground pink pepper powder that crescendos all the way to the drydown, the four p's. I won't say that I cannot wear CHANCE, but there are so many better choices out there. I certainly do not consider CHANCE to be a member of the illustrious chypre category. Not sure where this one falls. Perhaps it is sui generis: pink peppercorn plastic patchouli (I didn't get much pineapple...)

I can understand the popularity surrounding this fragrance. I would classify Chance as being much more of a casual and youthful fragrance when compared to other classic Chanel perfumes. The pineapple, pink pepper and iris are really strong in this composition. It was hard for me to detect any of the other notes. As I said before, I think this would make a great casual, daytime scent, however it has enough class to be worn during the night-time. Like all Chanel perfumes, this one has great lasting power and a strong, definite and classy smell. Edit: I have since added Chanel Chance EDT to my collection. My initial observations are still in place.

For me this an ageless scent, perfect for everyday, work wear or leisure. I find this very feminine, fresh and bright. I don’t get any pepper in this at all. This is another great scent from Chanel, alongside Coco Mademoiselle, and one I’ve been wearing on and off for 20 years. It’s an easy reach when I don’t know what to wear.

Oh gosh, the pineapple notes here are so incredible and unique. The opening is intensely peppery/musky/jasmine in that Chanel-strong, aldehydic sort of way (rather than a photorealistic way) and then the cold but spicy fruitiness comes in, eventually being followed by airy and musky vanilla aspects.

I like my Chanel's. I do. As the years have progressed, each have held their place on my vanity, and at times, I've changed in my opinion of them. But this one has surprised me. Very much surprised me. I'm surprised I didn't sneeze. Pepper. And more pepper. Throughout it's entire run. I know I'm not the only one that experienced this reaction.

I received a sample of Chance by Chanel EDP recently. This is not normally a fragrance I would seek out by my own accord, but here are my thoughts. I may be the average prole with little knowledge of finer tastes, but this makes me think of wealthy and sophisticated young women in gold and silk sipping champagne.

The opening act of Chance EDP has less of the patchouli note, than the EDT version. It has a slightly fruity aroma, pink pepper, jasmine, vanilla and the musk. Initially, the jasmine is going to be the strongest of the floral notes. Then, it kind of shares duties with the iris as things move along. Though, the role of the floral notes will diminish, as well.

Kenzo 5:40pm in Madagascar is a unique perfume featuring lotus and vanilla. It smells very different from other vanilla perfumes in that it is not at all sweet. I picked up a bottle of this blind out of curiosity and initially I did not like it very much because it seemed somehow off. I have to say, however, that it has grown on me over time. Now that I am used to its strange personality, I rather like it and no longer find it sour or confused. MADAGASCAR is a true unisex fragrance, with a somewhat masculine bent, but some wearers may find the watery lotus overly synthetic, as I initially did. As my own case demonstrates, this perfume is an acquired taste!

The bottle has been in my collection for almost a year now. A blind purchase, as the comments read simply excellent. There is talk of green vanilla, fresh and woody. I had never encountered anything like it before; vanilla is definitely one of my favorites. I want to know it in all its facets. The scent is supposed to capture the hot and exotic aromas of Madagascar, more specifically the evening mood. Unfortunately, it is a limited special edition that can only be purchased at airports or ferry boats. Another reason to acquire a bottle. I would never think to describe the scent as "hot"; rather the opposite. There is definitely an exotic quality, more on that later. I associate it more with cool, unspoiled morning air, oxygen-laden to the finest degree, one wants to inhale deeply to soak up the energy of the new day. The opening is more than unusual, completely new to me until now. A mild, cool, slightly green cream greets me, aquatic and fresh, almost wet, dew-soaked. At the same time, a soft banana note appears; where does that come from? A hint of fresh lacquer, hard to describe, but by no means unpleasant, subtly spicy, faintly reminiscent of warm skin. Although only a few notes are listed, the scent has many faces. Delicately floral, watery, powdery cool, gently melting, very harmonious. The nuances skillfully intertwine, allowing one or another to take the lead at times, soon merging again into a floating, ethereal, gossamer unity. Innocent and filled with light. The vanilla presents itself in a very naked form, not refined or gilded, dusted with sparkling almond powder or similar. It has very little of the gourmand, but I like this milky, pastel yellow, gossamer vanilla. The cedar as a partner is very advantageous, gripping, cool-woody, providing a delicate, sun-bleached framework of supple wood. A breathtakingly beautiful symbiosis of cool and warm. It is not the kind of warmth you feel directly on a sunny day, the kind that tickles and burns on the skin. I have long searched for a comparison: after warming your hands on a freshly brewed cup of coffee and placing your now warm palms on your cheeks, the gentle, indirect warmth that seems to immediately reach the body's interior. That is exactly how the scent feels. It envelops you in a gossamer cocoon of gentle warmth and light; it is a very thin fabric, silky soft and cooling, unable to hold back the cold and wind of the refreshing morning, yet it offers space and freedom, feeling feather-light and floating. The minimally aquatic, watercolor-like, floral freshness fades a bit in the base. There, the scent feels a bit denser, still tempting, sweetness only shows itself very restrained, almost just a hint of fine powdered sugar, ultra-sparingly sprinkled in small amounts. It is really not easy to grasp; light-footed, gracefully, the genderless light figure slips through my fingers time and again, brushing against me painfully softly with its silky-cool garment, leaving a powdery, softly spicy, green-vanilla cloud, the air around it filled with a cool humidity. It is similar to standing next to a waterfall, with a warm wind carrying scattered, stray water droplets that settle pleasantly and gleamingly on the warmed skin. It provides comfort, peace, and harmony; one would like to sink into its friendly embrace, a touch that demands nothing but gives. It seems to be a specialty of Kenzo; I feel just as peaceful when I wear Indian Holi. Not a scent that causes a stir; it is a flattering, delicate wallflower, velvety, its voice is calm but determined. I particularly enjoy wearing it in spring; it fits wonderfully with windy days, the heavy April showers, the first rays of sunshine, the transitional mood, the new that lurks in the fresh air. A top-notch summer vanilla; in warmth, it becomes curvy and more gourmand, yet still fresh and creamy, more yogurt than cream. I have worn it on many occasions, and it elicits wonder from those I let close to me. It is described as unusual and very delicious; the sillage is very restrained, but that also fits the rather shy yet elegant overall impression. Cold seems to make it freeze; the movements are more laborious than playfully light. Online, it is declared unisex, but I find it clearly feminine, more of a shy doe than a man-eater. The longevity is surprisingly good for such a delicate-exotic lightweight. Lotus seems to play a significant role in the harmonious character, combined with vanilla, which is known to have a calming effect, a dream pair. It blends fabulously with one's own skin scent, no unnatural film that clogs the skin. As much as I am enthusiastic, I often cannot wear it. So much purity, peace, and harmony somehow overwhelms me. It appears clean and smooth, not sterile, but the salt in the soup is missing; I miss a charming flaw, a slightly morbid character trait, a moral dilemma can unfortunately be very attractive. But when I crave it, I wear it with great joy and enjoy the unusual, slightly immature, spring-fresh vanilla. A hidden gem for vanilla lovers who also enjoy it cool-woody-spicy, subtly powdery, and airy-watery-East Asian-floral. A gourmet lightweight gourmand from Madagascar, unique in its kind, nothing resembles it; you can confidently forget the comparison with Vanilla Noir.

Yes, I’m back from vacation! But since it seems no one missed me here, I shouldn’t really “bless” you with comments, but I won’t be that way… Ah, here we have another “time” fragrance from Kenzo, which, despite their simple bottles, are actually quite good and recommendable scents. And this one is particularly successful and smells really great! So let’s see what it smells like at 5:40 AM (actually 5:40 PM) in Madagascar. Besides that, I can certainly rub the scent under the nose of a dear friend, as she had no idea until recently where Madagascar is located :D Do you know? :)) Yes… “somewhere” near Africa is correct, I’ll accept that… :D And yes, Madagascar is also an animated movie (although I must say that I find Madagascar a bit boring, even though I love animated films like a child… :D). The scent: The scent starts off slightly floral, but mainly sweet and powdery, as you can already smell the vanilla. I actually don’t know what lotus smells like, but it seems to be sweet, as the type of sweetness here smells “different” than, for example, the sweetness of vanilla, and it’s not jasmine-like either. But this sweet scent is very pleasant, even slightly fruity and very delicious. It also seems to have a somewhat clean (no, nothing soapy) quality to it, which should appeal to you ladies quite a bit, and of course to us guys about you :D In the background, there’s a light cedar, and the freesias probably provide additional floral notes, but I think they can hardly be perceived or identified. A bit later, the scent becomes even more powdery and softer, and just feels wonderful on the skin. After many, many hours, the fruity notes fade almost completely, but the scent remains powdery and slightly sweet, with the vanilla becoming almost the sole main actor. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is not bad at all and radiates well over a longer period. If sprayed on generously, it could even leave a small scent cloud behind. The longevity is also quite good, lasting easily six to eight hours, which might be due to the vanilla, as vanilla scents often have good longevity. The bottle: The bottle is elegantly rectangular. It is transparent and has an image on the inside showing the island of Madagascar at dusk. The name is printed directly on the front of the bottle. The cap is cylindrical and brownish or bronze-colored. Overall, it’s simple, but the beautiful motif makes it quite nice. In my opinion, this scent is the best from this Kenzo line. It smells very pleasantly fruity-sweet. Hmm… I can hardly remember what else I could say about scents that smell so wonderful and delicious. You’re probably tired of my eternal phrases like “you smell delicious/sweet/tempting” and can’t hear it anymore. How about sexy instead? Yes, I could write that here for a change. For those expecting an exotic scent, I can reassure you. The scent is a bit exotic. You can easily imagine gazing into the distance in Madagascar or similar places, enjoying the landscape in peace and satisfaction, and having a good time. On the other hand, it also works very well as an evening scent, as it appears sexy and elegant as described, neither intrusive nor cheap, almost perfect for making a lady shine even brighter. And since the sillage is not bad at all, the scent fulfills this task quite well. The sweet notes are, by the way, not as heavy as it might have come across, so I think it could be worn in all seasons. For me, 5:40 PM in Madagascar is one of the most successful scents from Kenzo, and I would definitely recommend testing it if you happen to be lucky enough to get a sample or decant of this limited fragrance…

The somewhat different vanilla perfume. Completely unsweet, airy, dry, green. 5:40 pm in Madagascar (along with 7:15 am in Bali) spent many years just sitting in airport shops and was thus "travel exclusive". Until it suddenly enriched the shelf at our Müller. You can see what Müller has to offer. By the way, it was correctly placed in both the men's and women's fragrances, because unlike here in our database, I believe it is officially a unisex scent. From the very first testing, I was fascinated by this strange vanilla. I visited Madagascar a few times before it got to come along. Oh no, it had to come along. Although I can't wear it all the time, it is a lovely addition to my collection. This vanilla is not gourmand, not cuddly, it is very simple and subtle, and it is down-to-earth and grounding. Right after spraying, this vanilla is initially soaking wet. Lotus in the top note. I can handle lotus quite well. Here too, it is very refreshing, watery, delicately fragrant. The unsweet vanilla is right there with it. As the top note fades and the heart note makes its way, the scent changes: from soaking wet to dry. The freesia adds a bit of floralness, but already the cedar delivers the growing dryness. The scent does not become too powdery or too harsh, it remains delicately woody the whole time. And green. First wet-green, then dry-green. And vanillic. But indeed unsweet and very close to the skin. It doesn't develop very deeply, but remains very uncomplicated "there". Still, it is somehow special. I don't know of a less sweet vanilla that is still very delicious.

Hello everyone :) After receiving my first "official Parfumo samples" (thanks to Lilau), I of course wanted to start testing right away. Given the dreary weather outside, I thought I would take this one for a spin. I must admit that I expected a rather warm, enveloping scent from the bottle. It is not that at all, yet it still captivates me. Regarding the development: Right upon spraying, I get - but really only for the first few seconds - such a green, almost biting smell that I want to turn away. But before I can scrunch my nose, the initial shock passes and my wrist reveals...as expected...ta-da...vanilla. But not vanillin vanilla, not sweet, cuddly cute vanilla, but REAL fresh vanilla, just like when you scrape out a vanilla pod. Only better, because the little flowers around it create an even more exquisite scent. For me, the scent presents itself like this: Mix freshly cut flower stems with scraped vanilla seeds, combine this with a few delicate little white flowers. The cedar hardly makes its presence known; I can imagine that it simply holds all the ingredients together "only" but skillfully. Not much happens on my skin in terms of development after the first few minutes for the rest of the time. However, I do get small gentle waves, or rather breezes, coming my way repeatedly. I often feel like it could tip into a more conventional vanilla direction (which I also like!), but just before that, some green leaf combined with a fresh flower reins in the whole package and keeps it together, maintaining its warm greenness. Those are the moments when the freesia color takes on a slightly pastel touch. But really just slightly - a brief hint. A straightforward (ok - wavy ;) ) but still wonderful scent, green yet warm, very close to the body, internally very harmonious and striking due to its radiant simplicity. The longevity is great for me. It doesn’t last forever, being a rather soft scent, but I can enjoy those little mini breezes throughout a workday. I must confess that I - oh dear, please don’t hit me - owned a scent from adidas over 20 years ago that no longer exists (I think it was the first adidas woman?), which accompanied me daily. In a green bottle. This one has a similar note somewhere in between, just more elegant, softer, rounder, and...with real vanilla. Though extraordinary in its own way, it is not a scent that stands out; it creates a small fine aura around me in which I simply feel comfortable even without being wrapped up. A bit like a second skin. And whether you believe it or not - the weather adapted to the scent: the sun came out, and I wore it on a lovely, albeit not really warm, spring afternoon. It couldn’t be more fitting :)

....yes, this is how it should smell and not otherwise. I happened to be in a drugstore (orange) yesterday and was just browsing around while waiting for someone, when I saw a bottle of 5:40 PM in Madagascar standing there, it must have been waiting just for me, so it was probably fate. I first sprayed it on a test strip, well, it was okay, then on my skin.

Since I cannot award a trophy for one of the best comments here (technical issue), I have to give this recognition in the form of a comment. Dear Fran, I can wholeheartedly agree with your lines; you have provided a perfect description. Especially your phrasing "green vanilla" hits the mark! This fragrance is one of my favorites; I could bathe in it.

Chanel says Gabrielle is composed around four classic white flowers: tuberose, orange blossom, ylang ylang and jasmine. They call it, "the perfect white flower." Olivier Polge has called Gabrielle "abstract", an apparent allusion to Chanel's monumental abstract floral, no 5. Abstraction implies veering away from duplicating a given scent and instead reimagining it. Gabrielle is abstract in that it doesn't smell like any of these four flowers per se. In fact it doesn't smell appreciably botanical. Despite the press release talking points describing the perfume's flower as "imaginary" and "perfect", Gabrielle is less an ideal flower than the mean average of a set of 'floral' notes. Gabrielle is linear for the most part but it has an identifiable drydown. The perfume grows less specific as time passes, though not inadvertently. The drydown seems intentionally indistinct, recreating the risk-averse, bleary musky/woody finish found in many mainstream perfumes geared toward the young female perfume buyer. To its credit, though Gabrielle is a fruity floral it's neither gourmand nor particularly sweet. A mildly acerbic twist runs through the perfume's duration, cropping any nascent sweetness. Gabrielle hits its marks and doesn't flub its lines but it doesn't inspire. A noncommittal floral mix leading to a fairly anonymous drydown gives Gabrielle a shapelessness that undercuts Polge's efforts to create an ideal white flower. The composition seems specifically calibrated to create soft-focus haze and a dull shine. It's a ho-hum vision of femininity from the house that produced challenging and powerful feminine perfumes like 19, Cristalle and Coco. I don't doubt the expertise and technical proficiency involved in creating a perfume like Gabrielle. It performs precisely as intended and accomplishes its design goals but it reads as a collection of non-negatives. It's attractive in that it's not ugly. It's appealing in that it's not offensive. Again, this strategy seems deliberate. The most flankable perfumes tend to be those that don't commit too strongly to any olfactory characteristics and I imagine it won't be too long until Gabrielle Eau Fraiche, Gabrielle Eau Tendre and Gabrielle Edition Blanche hit the shelves. (from scenthurdle.com)

Gabrielle opens with a modern, bracing, soapy aldehyde and sweet mandarine, not the vintage-smelling aldehyde in No.5, as if it's an effort to remind people that it's a Chanel fragrance but also to send the message: "Rest assured, this is not 'old-fashioned', at all". The transition between the forcefully bright fruity aldehydic opening to the luminous, clean white floral heart is seamless. I can hardly discern any particular facets of these 4 flowers, "abstract floral" indeed. Slowly but surely, Gabrielle gets sweeter with time, and almost turns jammy and saccharine around the 3rd hour because of the cassis note. Thankfully, it then goes back to the "abstract floral" route and firmly remains in the "clean soapy fruity floral shampoo" territory till the end. Gabrielle has a moderate sillage and a longevity of 8 hours on my skin. I have to admit, the olfactory description employed in the press release is spot on. Gabrielle is indeed radiant, sparkling, luminous, feminine, and its treatment of flowers is very abstract. It's also predictable, inoffensive, pretty in the conventional way and attuned to the modern sensibility. Moreover, its jammy fruitiness is also clearly a sign that Gabrielle is engineered towards a young clientele of today, which totally makes sense for a major commercial launch from a business point of view. However, from my personal point of view, I find Gabrielle derivative and uninspiring. While wearing Gabrielle for a few times, I was initially reminded of other abstract florals such as Dior J'Adore, Chanel Beige and Jour d'Hermès. But upon examining them more closely, the touted "abstract"quality of Gabrielle actually makes it appear more muddled and less refined, and ultimately the one with the least personality. I would recommend Gabrielle to those who'd like a feminine, abstract, clean, modern aldehydic fruity floral from a widely-recognised brand, but I think there are other quality, similar-styled and more affordable choices out there, if one is not fixated on the Chanel brand.

I tried this in store with the preliminary reviews in mind. Its a hazy, white -floral melange. Its bright, but easily forgotten. No wow factor but would be a great worksafe scent. I dont think anyone could be offended smelling like this. Gabrielle as in Gabrielle Chanel? Its not.

I finally tried Gabrielle. I did not know what to expect, but I did not expect to be in a certain way. I found brightness, a lot. It is such a luminous perfume. It opens with some citrus notes, a little bit tangy and bitter. After a while, the flowers appear. Tuberose and ylan-ylang is what my skin smells like. Yes, it’s about tuberose but a light one, glorious and full of joy. I can feel the orange blossom which give some pleasant bitterness to the composition. It gives the impression that each flower of the composition has its own place and appears when necessary. This is a happy perfume. It has nothing dark in it. Maybe it is not like the others from Chanel, but I like its younger and clear approach. The base is about musk and sandalwood, so it is nice and sweet. I liked this perfume maybe because I am not a big fan of No 5. It is different from The Chanel line and it brings a younger touch to this house. My first word was: bright, so bright and full of light. Everyone should give it a try without compare it to No 5. It has good sillage and good longevity.

I got this for Christmas. Having heard so many people praising it for its classic and warm expression I wanted to try it. I told my partner and he bought me a whole bottle.
