Difficult, these things that have no scent but only an association, air, water, salt. Whatever it is, it works really well and excites me, just like the new L'Eau d'Issey pour Homme Eau de Parfum . Alongside this whatever-it-is, a floral note is present and complements it excellently. Over time, it becomes warmer and softer. Like a sunny day in summer.

I recently tested this fragrance for the first time in a perfumery in Gran Canaria. My hotel was right by the sea, and every day I enjoyed the view and the sea air. The sun was blazing. It was a really hot week. I like to browse through perfumeries on-site, get inspired, and I also enjoy shopping. One day, I ended up at "L'Eau Pure | Kenzo," and this fragrance is for me a day by the sea to spray. Nothing more, nothing less. Fresh, a bit tangy, aquatic with a hint of mandarin and lavender, a welcome refreshment on hot days. For me, the scent is absolutely unisex. The price of the fragrance was unbeatable, so I bought it right away. It reminds me of my vacation in Gran Canaria and the days by the sea. The only downside is that the longevity could be better. I have no other complaints.

Seen, beautifully presented in the store and just picked up. Something caught my attention, maybe the fact that it had hardly any reviews yet. I like the fragrance pyramid, so I applied it generously. What do you get here? A gentle blue, lovely mandarin in the opening, which even remains part of the composition until the end. When it comes to a citrus note, that's really not common. The second major player is lavender, relatively present, calming the whole composition and I like this note here. In the base, a bit of musk, woods for the foundation, nothing wild - very soft and not scratchy. A scent that doesn't rely on authentic sea freshness, but rather a lavender freshness feeling mixed with a bit of lemon/mandarin and additional elements. As unexciting as that sounds, it is beautifully constructed as a fragrance and truly brings joy. I believe it will fly under the radar with all the Kenzo bamboo tubes, but I like it. Longevity and sillage - sillage is weak but on the skin, especially from the lavender, it lasts quite a while.

I ordered a back up bottle today, the equivalent of building a bunker at the edge of the millennium, I fear world war and pestilence. I'm told there is a movie where Adolf HItler wakes up, bemused, and finds that the bullet that blitzed his brain simply sent him to sleep for 70 years. He's back, and I imagine the fields of Iris pallida and Rose de Mai as scorched earth. Coco, no angel where the Nazi's were concerned, inspired the perfume that is No 19 and I adore it. As many others vocalise this is my one and only, if I wasn't totally unfaithful to any one perfume. For a more detailed breakdown of what No 19 is driven by (no aldehydes, no labdanum, little oak moss) see Elena from Perfume Shrine's article. It's a perfume that is driven as much by what it doesn't contain as what it does contain, It is a riddle, wrapped in a mystery, inside an enigma; but perhaps there is a key. It's beautiful, just beautiful, forever and a day, until the 12th of never.

So I'm a 22 year old dude with a fairly vintage preference when it comes to perfumery. I love Bel Ami and Platinum Egoiste a lot. So...in my love search for more chypres that excites me, No 19 came across my radar. I was a bit concerned at first because I was afraid not being able to pull this off. but I blind bought it anyway. As I opened the package and sprayed it on myself, my immediate reaction is that this reminds me of No 5 big time. If you smelled No5 EDP and loved it, you will love this one for sure. However, I find this warmer and creamier than No 5 EDP. Yes, you heard me. I found No 19 warmer. While in no 5 that sharp Ylangylang punches you and leaves a trail of metallic aldehydes, No 19 becomes so comforting as it settles down. On my skin, its a haven of hyacinth and sandalwood. And it is EXTREMELY elegant. Something about No5 is a bit vulgar to me, as if the wearer is trying too hard to announce oneself. However, No 19's impression on me is confidence, in the sense that the wearer is a very pleasant person to be around. CREAMY, yep, I found this not only warm but also creamy. If you ever smelled hyacinth in nature, you will know that it has a green and fresh sharpness to it. That facet of hyacinth is gone here. Finally, to men who are watching: This is less sweet than Dior Homme OG edt and Dior Homme Intense and more floral and natural smelling, and if you appreciate chypres you would not regret buying and studying this. To ladies who are watching: You might be concerned that you find various dudes writing a review here for a perfume marketed to female, you might be wondering if this thing is too masculine. NO. As a straight guy, I would be incredibly delighted if my girl wears this. I have to admit that although it is wearable for a guy, it would accentuate femininity indefinitely better. It's just that as a perfume lover, I find it a crime for such a beautiful creation to be only enjoyed by women!!

Part 1: No. 19 Eau de Parfum Chanel No. 19 Eau de Parfum is to me a very "posh" perfume. It's powdery and elegant, and I can imagine the kind of woman who would wear it. Very controlled, very posh, but still young and beautiful. I think some kind of successful woman or rich woman. Personally I really like the Eau de Toilette and I wear it myself (I find the EdT works better on a man's skin). But first let me describe what it smells like. This perfume has a gorgeous iris/orris root note. It is well known that the type of iris used by Chanel, iris pallida, comes exclusively from a specific field in Grasse (exclusive to Chanel, it previously used to be from Florence, Italy)... and iris butter (made from roots which are dried for at least 3 years) itself is one of the most expensive perfume ingredients on earth, with the best quality (80% purity) costing around £70,000 (or $105,000) per kg. So what you get here is a wonderful iris note. This is an iris note surrounded by rose (also exclusively from Chanels field in Grasse), lilly-of-the-valley, and some green oakmoss and soft sandalwood. I would describe the Eau de Parfum as a "soft" fragrance. Soft but powerful. It smells expensive. The EdT is brighter, greener and more "alive" somehow. This one is very calm and controlled, but very beautiful. If you thought the EdT was too "green" or "sharp", this EdP is more controlled and powdery. In a word, it smells like expensive "perfume". So I would expect a woman who was rich or wealthy to smell like this. But it's a wonderful smell, and iris is definitely one of my favourite notes in perfumery. Part 2: A tale of two sisters... Chanel No.19 & Jacomo Silences Now, I want to compare between Chanel No. 19 and Jacomo Silences, as these perfumes are often compared together. Let's first start by saying that No. 19 was first, and so most other "similar" perfumes are descended or "inspired" by that one. But there is something about Silences that I like, which No. 19 doesn't have... and that is an entirely different character and personality. From the start these two are very different. Put it this way, if they were "sisters", then No. 19 (the older sister) would be the wealthy, successful rich woman of society. She has married someone rich, she lives in a nice, expensive house, she hosts dinner parties wearing her perfect black dress and pearl necklace and earrings. She hangs out with rich, wealthy people in society. She has perfect white skin, like a Greek statue, perfect hair, perfect nails. Perfect life. But, she is cold, she is quietly unhappy. She has everything but she feels like she has no control. Like her rich, successful life has been "planned" for her by others. She smiles for guests, and laughs politely, but when she takes off her makeup at night in her mirror, she sometimes wants to cry. Her younger sister is Silences. This one you could call a "free spirit". She is an artist and was once a beautiful model. She is a painter. She lives in a small, cute house by the river. She goes for a run every morning with her dog. She does not take everything in life too seriously, but she enjoys every minute of her life. She spends most of her time outdoors, in nature. She loves being in nature, running, painting, enjoying the different seasons. She loves who she wants, and she lives each day to the full. Cooking, being artistic, with the dog, out in the woods. She has no regrets in life. She does not have the money that her older sister "acquired" by marrying a rich man. She does not smell so expensive like her older sister, but she has character, and a big heart. She does not want anything more in her life, and she is happy. To me these are the differences. They are both green, both have an iris note, but this note is unbeatable in the Chanel, and is powdery, floral and smells clean, polished and expensive. The Jacomo smells "greener", like you are in the forest outside, with the smell of herbs and green leaves which the Chanel doesn't have. Basically, if you are an "active" person, or if you have memories of childhood in the countryside, then you will like and enjoy Silences. But if you want to smell the smell of "perfume", or want something "posh" or "expensive", then go for No. 19. Both are great choices. I think the Jacomo is a little more relaxed and carefree, but if you want to impress or are in a very formal situation, then go for the Chanel. Both are masterpieces!

I had tested this on a few occasions at home before buying N°19 Eau de Parfum and am now the happy owner of my first Chanel. (Yes, very late for the party :-)) I don't like most Chanels except for N°5 L'Eau Eau de Toilette (but find that too linear in the end unfortunately) and N°5 Eau Première (but I already have Liu Eau de Parfum and you don't need both). Haven't tried any from their exclusive line though. I'm a bit surprised that, for N°19 Eau de Parfum , fougère is not mentioned in the chart because that is how I would describe this scent and is probably why men like to wear it as well, without it being too masculine. I find this scent absolutely genderless. I'm always having trouble to detect the flowers in perfumes, I don't smell rose, maybe the Lily Of The Valley for it's mild soapyness and the Iris for it's slightly powdery profile (though I don't find this a very powdery scent over all)...whatever the case, they are very well blended. But I foremost get the green in that fougère way. This perfume feels like walking through the forest, looking up and see the sun peeking through the leaves when the fog has lifted. Wearing it, I feel grounded yet still able to dream. I think this is the perfect scent for high sensitive people. I also feel as though my environment expands when I wear this, asif there's more room to breath. I know that must sound weird, but I wouldn't know how to put it otherwise. The scent is not faint or weak, but quiet and mindful. The proces from first spray to final dry down goes on almost seamlessly. Last time I tested it before buying (using the last few drops out of the sample) was yesterday after a shower and before going to bed and I woke up to this clean skin scent with the memory of first spray. Edit: I like it best in fall.

I got into perfume more seriously about a year ago or so, and I distinctly remember smelling Chanel fragrances and not enjoying them, feeling they were too old fashioned and unexceptional. From time to time, when at my local perfume stores, I would go to the Chanel stand and smell a couple of perfumes, just because I knew that some day they would reveal themselves to me. It happened two weeks ago, when I smelled no. 5 and thought it was abnormally good and completely outstanding. I was lucky enough to know that 19 was also considered a gem. I did not know what to expect - I remembered hearing it was a bit weird (in an excellent way), but didn't know it was such a green one. I immediately fell in love, and made my first purchase in store. I usually go home and try to find the best deal, but I couldn't help myself this time. I am wearing it today, and just felt compelled to write about it. What a wonderful, mysterious, and unique fragrance.

I got a very good 90s vintage bottle a while ago. For me this is like the green version of Cabochard or the animalic version of Jacomo Silences. It's very beautiful classic green chypre and dried with Santos-like animalic scent. It is not a beast mode, but it has rich and delicate elegance. Bergamot, Neroli, or Ylang-Ylang in it are very difficult to detect.

Beautifully crafted perfume, a classy, grassy, sassy Chypre. The Lily, Rose, Jasmine and Hyacinth come through very quickly for me... and later the heavy-duty woody, musky tones that last and last. All kinds of wondrous adjectives may be applied, suffice it to say that this has to be a Top-Ten choice.

My passion for this fragrance is improving since the 1st day... I cannot imagine my collection without this beauty. This is my favorite Spring of all time without any doubt. The get the best out of this scent I would recommend to use it on hot weather with a t-shirt... What a masterpiece.
I like so much this perfume. I like the kind of bitterness and coldness it has. Its beyond time and gender.

I've began truly getting into fragrances Dec 2023. I think Nº19 was my 3rd or 4th fragrance going into the new year. And now, May 2024, I'm on my second 100ml. I will admit that I'm a heavy sprayer, which is partly why I'm on my second in a 5-month period. But also, longevity, projection, and sillage contributed to my over-spraying.

An amazingly beautiful perfume that opens with powerful Aldehydes, which is what makes Chanel unique, along with an amazing powdery floral for those who love the genre, such as: Heliotrope, French iris pallida, Cherry blossom, and of course musky notes. This blend simply feels like heaven on me. In terms of performance, they are quite good on me. The longevity is surprising for a perfume of this type, when from morning to evening you could smell the perfume close to the skin. As for the SILLAGE, in the first 3-4 hours it is good and then stays close to the skin. The perfume is very versatile, suitable for all seasons, day and night, work and going out. It’s a true, it is more feminine, but in my opinion the graph here is misleading and it is more balanced and suitable for men as well. Right now this perfume is on my wish list. 8.5/10.

I see much hate for cherry blossom and powdery scents all over the internet. This new Chanel has both... I bet it will receive some bad reviews... Anyway, I find it nice and easy to wear. Not a big surprise in the Chanel Les Exclusifs collection though, very Chanel spirit. Its longevity is above the average and its sillage is not very strong. You won't annoy your co-workers with Comète.

It doesn't smell like a Chanel fragrance at all and the aldehydes don't appear in the same way as in other fragrances from Les Exclusifs collection. The scent is powdery, but not as much as you might imagine from the combination of iris and Heliotrope. It is not dry powdery, like La Pausa for example. The whole thing smells rather like it has a lot of Violet and the smell in general reminds me of the color Purple (I don't immediately think of purple if smelling Iris). The aroma is sweet and "moist". Heliotrope is neither vanilla-like, nor almond-like, but the scent is thick, still not creamy and it brings the sweetness to the scent. The notes say "musky notes" and I think the scent is here very similar to Ambrette which has a sweet floral musky nuances. In the dry down the sharp scent of Violet changes into a softer texture and it's more like a mix of subtle Iris and clear Heliotrope. The scent is soft, pretty and pleasant, but I understand why we have been disappointed with it. It's hard to say if I'll buy the whole bottle. It may be that I suddenly fall in love with it, because there is absolutely nothing unpleasant in this scent or blend in overall. The smell is familiar and it reminds me of something, and I'll tell you as soon as I get it in my head. The two most recent crushes on Violet Fragrances are Amour amour and Violettes du Czar (2014) , and perhaps the most unsuccessful Violet fragrance is just lately released Palatine (I wrote about it). I will test this more and I will edit my thoughs. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

Enchanting...magic in a bottle. Divine. First, you get a hint of plush, realistic cherry that becomes enveloped in the Chanel makeupy aura, but not their usual kind: the aldehydes are quieter, especially because there's not that initial citrus punch carrying them through. Comète is soft but ever present, and while it does evolve over time, you're always enveloped in this hazy cloud of iris. It's a joy to wear. I remember trying it out at the store and feeling so conflicted: I thought I didn't like powdery stuff so much, so why is this so captivating? Why can't I stop sniffing my wrist!!!??? Two sample vials later and...full bottle. Chanel was smart to add something softer to their Exclusifs line because it's gonna be (it already is!) a hit with a loooot of people that aren't fans of the brand. And it still feels Chanel through and through. Comète is just gorgeous to experience and a true example of how perfumery can be artful and soft-spoken too.

I have a decant of Comète I swap Iris Dragee for. The Opening: Sparkling aldehydes- dry, not wet - no suds. Think a new bar of soap. *The opening reminded me of Serge Lutens Dent de Lait, which to my nose, was an overdose of aldehydes. Made me think of a cold, brightly lit white room, shining stainless steel with drains in the floor. Dexter Morgan’s kill room after it’s been clean. Way too clean. sinister * Fortunately Comete’s opening isn’t as dramatic as Dent de Lait. Orange peel! Piercing aldehydes are creating an Intense heliotrope opening - think P.T Hiver’s Heliotrope Blanc on steroids. Soft plastic (Barbie doll/cabbage patch kids) heliotrope, powdery with some almond nuances. 20 minutes later the aldehydes let up and I smell tart, pastel violet (creating the illusion of cherry blossoms which is a fantasy note) A sweet but bitter green note that reminds me of angelica enters which are enveloped in sweet, powdery - almond like heliotrope, touch of waxiness. I don’t smell Iris but I feel it in the texture it’s helping create. It’s a similar texture to L’instant Magic but they don’t smell alike. Nor do I smell Misia here or French Kiss (you’re joking) or Love in Black - what?!? Love in Black Violets and leather. Comete is too fluffy and polite. 2 hours later, the Comete scent bubble I was in stops sparkling and sits very intimately creating a quiet fluffy musk on skin. It’s a positive first impression still unsure if it Full Bottle worthy for me. The issue is Comete is Aldehydes. Heliotrope and Violets. If I want Violets and Heliotrope there are better (more affordable) fragrances- L’heure Bleue or the modern version L’heure de Nuit (which last longer and is even more of a marshmallow fluff puff than Comete) Even La Perla White Iris does Violet, heliotrope and musk better- 100 Ml $80-$100. That’s the issue. I don’t know if the addition of Chanel aldehydes to a familiar Violet/Iris heliotrope makes it full bottle worth at $375 per 75ml.

Beautiful perfume. This is the most beautiful iris ever made. The iris surrounded by cherry blossom, light aldehydes, almonds and flowers. The ingredients smell very natural and pleasant. Almond and cherry dominante the opening, and fresh sweet natural iris dominates the drydown. I would swear there’s a little bit of vanilla even though it’s not in the note pyramid.
The Les Exclusifs perfumes were announced everywhere with great fanfare, and I had the chance to try Comète at various events.

the iris plays punk here- i don't really see it. if you are an iris fan you will not be that happy if you like cool ghostly iris. however i do get a lot of sophisticated sweetness from the violet and cherry blossom notes that lasts in fucked up singapore heat. this is something i'd wear to feel good in this humid weather, to a job interview or to meet up with friends.

It's light and airy, fragile and gentle to a fault you have to chase after it to smell it, it doesn't come to you. It's inoffensive, polite, it won't get in your way even though sometimes you kind of want it to.

This fragrance presents itself as a beautiful and elegant composition, combining sweetness with a soft, powdery iris note that adds refinement and structure. There is a subtle reminder of No. 5 in the way the scent balances warmth and classic elegance, though it remains more approachable and modern in its overall impression.

I have to admit that it has been about 3 years now that I have been eyeing the Edp Kenzo Amour and Kenzo Flower without buying either of them. What is the reason for that? I always liked one of them more than the other alternately, and since I already have so many powdery scents in my collection, I somehow felt I had to choose and only buy one from Kenzo. Then there were my friends, who didn’t make the decision easy for me. One side was clearly for Kenzo Amour, as it supposedly had more of a "baby" vibe (I have a baby scent weakness :D), while the others said Kenzo Flower was "the fresh diaper" while Amour was more like the full** diaper. Outraged, I went another 3 years pondering, sniffing both in every drugstore, without any results. In the EDP Flower, I constantly felt something was missing. It was indeed very powdery and delicate... but just too green. Especially on my skin, which almost absorbs the powdery notes in fragrances and then only exudes green notes. And then two months ago... there was this bargain online. I had read too few comments on Parfumo and Fragrantica, the fragrance pyramid confused me because I wasn’t sure how I would cope with incense and jasmine, whether the rose would smell like grandma... And yet I took the plunge. What can I say? The Kenzo Essentielle has replaced my instant magic from Guerlain every other day :) I love it, my boyfriend loves it, I have rarely been approached so often about a fragrance. Flower Essentielle starts off green, and you immediately have the Flower EdP in the back of your mind. However, just two minutes later, notes mix in that are much more original and have excited me! My jasmine horror thankfully did not come true, at least not in the penetrating form one knows from the Lush store or the tea shop. It is wonderfully woven and complements the vanilla superbly, which has finally made the compromise possible for me: as gourmand and powdery as Amour, but at the same time as fresh and delicate as Flower! Flower Essentielle has a spiciness that makes this scent extremely interesting, as it doesn’t get directly shoved into the "cute" drawer. No, it almost clashes with a note that I might call cinnamon? However, the cinnamon haters among us need not worry: nothing sticks out unpleasantly here, pushes itself forward, or takes over. Musk gives the scent a powderiness despite its spiciness, as one knows from the other two Kenzos, but the incense adds much more depth and makes this scent, along with hawthorn, appear more mature. Not old, but feminine instead of girlish. The rose smells very familiar; you have smelled it in many formulations that have helped such perfumes break through. Here are the key points again: 1) Bottle: Very beautiful, the classic from Flower :) Definitely an eye-catcher in the cabinet. 2) Sillage: For a green-sweet-spicy-powder scent, really quite decent. The person next to me definitely notices it. At least ;) if I spray just one spritz too much on my wrist, it’s about as if I sprayed it directly into my nostril :D 3) Sensational 10 hours during the day plus the whole night and the morning after (though just a light trace left) Conclusion: If something was missing in the EdP Flower, you might find it in the Essentielle. If you found Flower from the floral-powdery type annoying and possibly even worse with Amour, you shouldn’t expect too much from the Essentielle: you can definitely smell the degree of similarity of the fragrances. For me, one of the best perfumes from the house of Kenzo, with Amour and Flower EDP sharing second place. I believe that all Instant Magic fans who are currently mourning this scent (production has been discontinued) should definitely smell the Flower Essentielle. It is of course a different scent, but it goes in a similar direction except for the spicy note, which one can definitely appreciate (I otherwise hate spicy scents and orientals). Shalimar fans might also like the Essentielle. So that’s it from me again, I hope this description has helped you :)

Flower by Kenzo Essentielle is very close to the original scent. However, it is a bit more robust, heavier. I perceive Flower as a flat, unremarkable floral fragrance with relatively low longevity (sorry to all fans, I'm not the floral scent type (-; ) - the Essentielle has no issues with longevity. Sprayed in the evening, some components (especially the incense) are still quite noticeable the following morning. Basically, more presence has been given to the original scent by adding incense and vanilla. This makes the Flower Essentielle significantly more robust, dry-vanilla, and a bit stubborn. I like incense scents, those robust-resinous, balsamic, sometimes citrusy fragrances - and the Flower by Kenzo Essentielle is no exception, especially because it is not completely smooth, not entirely rounded. I think I would like to test the Flower Oriental again in comparison *thinking*

I could swear that the Essentielle in the top and early heart notes smells like Flower from around 2000-2006. However, I am not aware of any reformulation. A few days ago, I ordered Kenzo Flower and was surprised at how bright and floral it smelled. I had already noticed this when testing in various perfumeries. The scent was not at all like I remembered. From 2001 to 2006, I wore Flower by Kenzo very often. And I hardly recognized it. At first, I didn't even want to buy it because I thought my taste had changed. Not that the regular Flower isn't a beautiful scent; I like it too, but it's different. In my desperation, I kept reapplying, but with no effect. The Flowers Essentielle is more powdery, creamier, and less bright. It is much more concentrated than the "current" Flower EdP. You have to apply it sparingly. I had missed exactly this strong, floral-powdery expression of Flower. Considering that it already had a strong scent and I stopped wearing it because I attracted a wasp that ultimately stung me. It had a powdery heaviness, which is now present in Flower by Kenzo Essentielle. I am glad to have purchased the Essentielle. The bright flowers are not so overwhelmingly dominant at the beginning. The whole scent is, in my opinion, more harmonious and unfolds more gently. The base becomes very beautifully soft, with incense and vanilla. The incense is prominent here. I had never known it like this. But Kenzo can wonderfully process incense softly in their perfumes. The scent becomes warmer, and the rose that plays a role in the top note makes it simply rounder and deeper. I am completely enchanted by Flower by Kenzo Essentielle and do not want to miss this scent from now on. But I definitely won't wear the scent during wasp season. The longevity is very good for me at around 10 hours.

The scent is in no way what one would expect. Comparisons with Flower are tempting due to the very similar bottle, but that is far from the truth. Here we have a distinctly powdery, warm-spicy fragrance that remains consistently pleasant on the skin. The rose dominates a bit, but is beautifully balanced by the slightly spicy incense base. Great scent!
At the beginning, rose and incense clearly dominate, after about 15 minutes vanilla joins in. A wonderfully spicy and powdery scent that fortunately has no resemblance to the regular Flower at all.
I don't like Flower by Kenzo at all. Now you've made me curious. I definitely have to go test it. The bottle is also very beautiful.

Nowadays, the floral aldehyde is a lost genre. We even forgot it is a genre. We only remember No5. All others - Sortilege, Arpege, Caleche and what else? - they are defeated and long forgotten. It is lonely at the top. Despite being engineered to perfection, No5 still works with the skin's chemistry. To me, this interaction is what makes a perfume a perfume; and I feel it is missing in many other perfumes. The downside is, it doesn't work on everyone. Spectacular on some people's skin and close to sour mold on others. It is therefore not only the most famous perfume, but arguably also one of the most regretted purchases. On my skin No5 works wonders, though. It feels like I'm emitting sparkles and feathers. Even though the whole aldehyde genre isn't a perfect fit to my taste, this is pure bliss.

Although not quite the same as the original extrait version, the No.5 EDP, which has seemingly become the standard version of No.5, captures the essence of what made this fragrance such an iconic piece of perfuming history, and truly stands the test of time. I was a bit apprehensive to wear No.5 for a long time, primarily because I'm a younger male, who despite loving and wearing a lot of the feminine classics, doesn't typically go for much of anything super floral, but after I sampled it a few times in a department store, I decided to give it a go. Imagine the absolute cleanest, most delicate and fresh floral smell you can possibly think of, and you've got No.5. I will say, it smells very different on paper and in the bottle than on does on clothes and skin, it really takes wearing it to fully understand what it is you're smelling. The opening is very clean, soapy, and ever-so-slightly citrusy, but not entirely sweet either. As it dries, the florals mesh with the aldehydes in a way that smells like actual fresh laundry that has been hung out to dry in the sun. I was shocked though, as despite hearing countless tales of the heaviness of the florals in this fragrance, I really experienced the total opposite. This is a floral fragrance, but by no means an overpowering one. It's light, but still smells like a beautiful bed of flowers on a warm summer's morning. I completely understand why this fragrance is so revered, as it's immensely gorgeous, and has become a top 5 favorite of mine (likely second only to Mitsouko) over my short time of wearing it. I only purchased a small bottle at first, but after this one is empty I will definitely buy the bigger size. No.5 is incredibly impressive even 100+ years later, and I strongly recommend everyone give this a try, regardless of usual preferences, as it's a truly magical and enlightening experience.

I am flabbergasted, really! I used to hate Chanel no 5 after smelling it years ago. But I got a free sample along with another purchase and I almost decided not to even touch it, thinking it wouldn't make sense. But I read many reviews on different platforms from people complaining about this reformulation so I thought: 'well if people who loved it in the past, don't like it now, maybe it has changed and will now match my taste better'. It made me curious anyhow and so I tested it. It's a sample from their newest bottle that I don't see in the database yet (like the one that carries the latest no 19 or like the one that carries the perfume of no 5). Well...I don't know if it is because of the reformulation or maybe my perception of scents has changed or my skin chemistry.... Whatever the case: I'm in awe! This is 'angels breath' it is how I imagine 'peace on earth' would smell like. It is now deprived of anything that - in my opinion - made this a very formal and bossy scent (think suits and pearl necklaces) it doesn't remind me of Arpège (1993) Eau de Parfum anymore, that 'stubborn' waxy smell is gone. Maybe many people mourn it for that, but I find this way, way better. Still classic, but I can't imagine anyone finding this 'old lady' (a comparison that should be forbidden anyhow :-)). I even don't get a 'vintage' feel from it any longer (I don't mind vintage by the way) it is completely timeless in my opinion. It is clean the way I love clean, the way I would have loved Pure Grace Eau de Toilette if that had been less synthetic and more versatile. Not as musky as many 'clean' scents can be. A warm, soapy freshness, but, at the same time, it is so much more than just that. It is sophisticated but not in the 'rich bitch' way and I think it could be worn in any season and for any occasion. No need to overspray: a little goes a long way. The opening may still be a little too aldehydic for some, but after ten minutes or so....pure bliss! It is one of the few perfumes of which I love the drydown, I often love the opening more (strangely, I know :-)). Here it is the other way around. That drydown is good. The sillage is strong but delicate, like a trail of stardust or sunbeams. Longevity is outstanding, I can still smell it after 12 hours. So If you never liked Chanel no 5, I think you also could at least sample/try the newest formulation. If you have always loved it: try first. It is completely different, at least in my opinion for what it's worth. Edit: After wearing it from time to time, I noticed I get a little bit weary of it at the end of the day if I spray too much. I use very, very tiny drops.

I could talk about what this 3-aldehyde combination used in such a large quantity meant to perfumery. I could talk about how Chanel has maintained No 5's smell by buying land and creating their own jasmine fields in Grasse. I could talk about how this has maintained its beauty while so much is gone. But I won't go into detail.This is the closest thing we have to visiting Paris in the 1920s and seeing the great art deco buildings go up, with their facades of glass and cement. Or visiting Weimar to see the Bauhaus when it was most active. No. 5 starts with fresh, clean lemon soap. Very austere and restrained. Then a fade to light, sweet white floral and tart peach. It doesn't have the smuttiness of Tabu or drama of Fracas. It whispers. Restrained, austere, clean, sculptural.

As for me, Chanel no 5 was, has been, and always will be a timeless classic. Warm, elegant, close to the skin, not shouting but gently whispering. With its warm, cozy, yet powerful embrace, I feel more confident, professional and elegant. A symbol of elegant femininity, a timeless fragrance expressing delicacy and strength, classicism and modernity.

You were/are my only signature scent and also the only one for which I had backup bottles. I got to know you back in the 1970s. Although I lived deep in the East, we weren't just floating around in the sausage broth, and relationships, as we know, only harm those who don't have any.

I could slap myself for not having discovered this dreamy fragrance earlier. Chanel No 5 has never crossed my path anywhere. My mother never liked it, and in my circle of acquaintances, there is no one who wears or has ever worn Chanel No 5. I began to wonder if this fragrance might be so aloof that no one dares to approach it.

You all know it well. Fragrances that are packed into a drawer labeled in big letters: OUTDATED! Often further described with words like “out of time,” “smells like my grandma,” or “matronly.” Well, I once put Chanel No. 5 into that drawer and never took it out again.

CHANEL N°5 Eau de Parfum by JAQUES POLGE It is quite remarkable how many comments have been written about N°5 Parfum (1921). It has been praised to the skies, loved, criticized, and some have wrinkled their noses at it, while others expressed their love or dislike.

Powdery creamy rose veil clouds my senses. Musk fluff on top makes it even more beautiful… wonderfully unique & elegant ** * The Flowers are quite a thing, so many different and yet similar bottles, versions, reissues, etc. I can't keep track anymore. I have a Flower by Kenzo Eau de Parfum and a Flower by Kenzo Eau de Toilette that smell almost exactly the same as the EdP at home. Here I prefer the edT, as it smells cheerier and more summery than the EdP. Then I was at the drugstore and sprayed the current Kenzo Flowers. Once the EdP and the current Flower by Kenzo (2021) Eau de Toilette . To my shame, only on paper which I then put in my bag. Unpacked it again at home and sniffed it again... I was blown away. BUT which scent smelled so good? So I consulted Parfumo, compared all the pyramids with what I smelled, and was left even more puzzled. "I can't believe this," I thought, it can only be one of the two. So I quickly ordered 2 samples of the current Flower by Kenzo's. The EdP smells just as I know it, vanillic, soft, warm, floral, and sweet. The new Flower by Kenzo (2021) Eau de Toilette , on the other hand, is a completely different scent than the ones I have smelled so far. It is incredibly elegant. This Flower starts with a powdery creamy rose veil that almost clouds my senses. Then a little musk fluff on top makes it even more beautiful. Vanilla is a minor detail and the lemon in the top notes is marginal. The rose powder nuance remains constant and envelops you with a noticeable sillage. Character-wise, this Flower distinguishes itself significantly from its predecessors, which are quite cheerful and suitable for everyday wear; this Flower is more suited for business meetings and weddings, as it is quite unique and very chic. Caution, the Flower 2021 is, in my opinion, not suitable for the height of summer, as it could be very overwhelming; one should not overdo it when spraying this one. I really like what I smell, but is it also what I smelled on the paper? NO... The search continues, and this Flower will not make it into my collection, even though I find it incredibly beautiful.

I'm not a fan of the first Kenzo Flower. It might be due to the violet (I recently realized that I don't like violet in fragrances at all). Recently, I gave Flower L'Elixir a chance, as it doesn't contain any violet. BOOM, in love. Now I discovered Flower EDT on Parfumo. It caught my attention simply because it doesn't contain any violet. However, I was concerned that it might be a soapy scent (which I also don't like). I got a sample, which arrived yesterday. Of course, I had to test it right away. As always, I applied the fragrance, stepped out of the cloud, and took my first breath. What I smelled was very pleasant. It is floral, creamy, and slightly fresh/citrusy right from the start. The rose in this fragrance is very beautiful. It doesn't overpower you but caresses instead. As for the development, the scent becomes creamier on my skin, the rose remains soft, the freshness stays, and at some point, I perceive the fragrance as veeeery subtly sweet (minimal). I imagine I catch a hint of vanilla at some point. This fragrance starts off very pleasantly and develops beautifully ---> floral, very creamy, slightly fresh, delicately vanillic (minimal), and everything dusted with a sweet powder. To me, this scent smells like a luxurious cream. There is quite a bit of musk present, but this note doesn't overwhelm. And the best part ---> I perceive NOTHING soapy on my skin. Most cream fragrances have a soapy touch for me. I don't perceive that here at all. In terms of projection, it is rather a light fragrance. I would say you scent yourself with it :). Others probably only notice it if they are standing right next to me or hugging me. With this fragrance, you don't clash anywhere. It is soft and unobtrusive. If you don't know what scent to wear, you reach for it. If you are looking for something cozy that doesn't overwhelm you, you reach for it. If you wear rather discreet and softer scents at work, you reach for it. I find the longevity acceptable for an EDT. I perceived it for about 5-6 hours. For me, this fragrance is wearable all year round. Since it is not a powerhouse but rather delicate and soft, it can also be worn well on warmer days. If you are looking for a cozy cream scent that has NO soapy touch (at least on my skin), you might want to check out Flower EDT.

It hugs me flowery-powdery orange blossom and rose, very warm. So cuddly!! I feel so comfortable with this scent. In the base there are musk and vanilla. Overall, everything reminds me very much of Gaultier Classique but a lot smoother. For me it is a wonderful alternative for which I have waited so long.

This fragrance has a very accurate name, it is as it suggests "the awter of amour". You know Kenzo Amour, that unique vanilla scent which many people adore. If you love that one but it seems suffocating and unwearable by you, you should definitely try this. It has a very strong amour vibe, it is definitely a Kenzo Amour, I dont want to say watered down as it seems ugly, "citrused/lightened down" would be a correct expression. The flacon is absolutely beautiful, it would be easily sold as a decorative itme. Also it is very easily wearable and non cloying, a safe choice!

~ Inspiration ~ I received a sample from dear Inger during a swap for “L’Eau de Kenzo Amour”. This one had been on my wishlist for a while, as I really like the regular “Amour” and “Holi Indian”. ~ Bottle ~ The slightly curved vase shape has been retained. The purple gradient is a real eye-catcher! ~ Scent ~ Contrary to expectations, it starts off very citrusy-fresh with bitter oranges and bergamot. Lush peonies and ylang-ylang give it a strong, floral character (exotic frangipani remains hidden from me). With musk and a hint of vanilla, it is gently rounded off. ~ Longevity ~ On my skin, it lasts about 7 hours (a bit longer on clothes and hair). It is quite intense at the beginning, so 2 sprays are enough for me. ~ Occasion ~ A sunny scent for the warmer days and evenings in spring, summer, and autumn. Also (when dosed discreetly!) not wrong for the office. ~ Conclusion ~ There is nothing left of the “Amour” here. My first thought was sunscreen! It leans more towards “Armani Code Luna” or “Le Parfum” by Elie Saab. So those who enjoy orange blossom and sunscreen scents will also delight in this one :)

A refined, subdued, and elegant citrusy opening immediately brought to mind "quiet luxury" and the sophisticated elegance of a lady. The sweet notes that sublimate the composition reinforce this impression. A feminine, elegant fragrance—present and noticeable, yet tastefully understated. Class, elegance, charm, and grace. It lingers on fabric for almost the entire day, gradually becoming intimately close. I have been wearing Chanel No. 5 for years—a timeless classic—but the impression that Paris-Venise left on me was unlike anything I had experienced before.

When Coco Chanel traveled from Paris to Venice, she was certainly very agitated, as it was shortly after the accidental death of Arthur Capel. It is said he was the only man she ever truly loved. Her friend Misia brought her to Venice to distract her, which evidently worked. Here she met, among others, the theater and ballet impresario Diaghilev, and her circle of friends expanded to include some illustrious names from the art and cultural scene of that time. Unlike this turbulent time in Coco Chanel's life, Paris - Venise, the fragrance dedicated to this journey, is rather reserved, though elegant and noble in typical Chanel DNA. The connection to Venice, or rather Italy, is likely provided by Neroli, which gives the perfume its foundational mood. However, this is somewhat far-fetched, as I almost want to attribute shyness to the scent, but with a bit of patience, a certain sophistication does develop on my skin. I can imagine that the clean creaminess of the perfume does suggest intimacy, but for me, it is too lacking in expressiveness, too bright, yes, I would almost say too feminine, for me to feel comfortable with it. I am sure that Coco herself would have preferred louder or rather more powerful perfumes. However, the house of Chanel is certainly addressing a customer segment that has been neglected until now. Those who love quiet, harmonious perfumes will surely feel at home with Paris - Venise. I would wear the scent as a companion for a summer now and then if I received it as a gift. But I fear I would simply forget it, as for me, Paris - Venise lacks enough recognition value.

Anyone who was expecting a blockbuster or something unprecedented from this fragrance will be disappointed. Chanel has wandered onto the path of light creaminess. One might praise the earlier classics, of course! But still, Chanel is forging new paths, in a fine and noble way, but quietly, without a bang and without being truly special! Nevertheless, I really like this scent, the only one in this line that has "persuaded" me to buy it! A fine, very creamy, not too powdery hint accompanies me for some time, but without shouting "here I am." Quite wearable on hot days, but above 30 degrees, I do miss the freshness of a summer fragrance. Usable year-round, always appropriate and never intrusive! The matching complement like body lotion and shower gel is supposed to be released in autumn, which should help the fragrance last a bit longer on the skin. I found Paris-Venise to be the most long-lasting of these three new Les Eaux de Chanel, and also the most feminine! What is written in the fragrance pyramid is indeed what you get. Those who do not like neroli can still be assured with this Eau de Toilette that nothing is sharp and everything is very finely blended with vanilla and tonka bean. These three fragrance notes harmonize wonderfully together. Not too sweet at all, wonderfully soft and cuddly, yes, like a very expensive body cream. So airy-melting, radiant, yet warm, sensual, slightly oriental, but unobtrusive! From beginning to end, simply beautiful! Great for cuddling on the couch in the evening, but also during the day when you don’t know what to wear. Simply smelling good and well-groomed, that is Chanel's idea, nothing more and nothing less. If that is too little, there is no need to test this Paris-Venise; everyone else should hold it under their nose and give it a chance. Maybe they would be as positively impressed as I am! Addendum: I must also note very positively that this fragrance bears no resemblance to any existing scent, which is not so self-evident these days!

Paris - Venice is the 2nd new Chanel fragrance that I just got to know, and it contradicts my thesis that the previously 3-part series (Biarritz, Deauville, Venice) consists of French seaside resorts. Venice in France is not even close to a sea, and if Venice is meant to be the French spelling of Venice, then that's not in France either. So far, I have only gotten to know Deauville, the fresh-herbaceous one from Normandy, but Venice caters to a different direction: the one with the soft, fruity creaminess. The Norman was a bit rougher, the Venetian is much more caressing. At times, I even smell similarities with Allure. The top note is somewhat spicy, but overall it's a cream slice with fruit. Then the cream recedes a bit, and the true intention of the fragrance comes to light: Neroli. A beautiful neroli note on a green velvet bed, with nutty tonka foam. Never really sweet, somewhat dark orange, a little smoky, this is so far my favorite fragrance of the series. Perfect as a fine summer scent,

Only the most beautiful fragrances are tested and reviewed by me. Paris - Venise is one of them. After having this fragrance in my collection for 3 months and wearing it a lot, it is now ripe for more. I had the opportunity to test it through a sharing. It was actually just a combo that was bought along. My actual wish fragrance from the ML was Paris - Deauville . Right off the bat: I am not a Chanel fan. However, I find the presentation in the stores extraordinarily appealing. Like a magnet, it draws me in, and whenever I just walk by, I HAVE to go in and spray. Even though I know that the Chanel DNA does not appeal to me at all. I sniff the fragrance on friends and like the sillage, but on me, they just don’t click. The highly praised and much-worn Chanel no.5 is absolutely terrible. When the Eau was released, I rushed to the next "Green" to try to find "my Chanel." Even that one did not appeal to me at all. Now, I had no high expectations for the two combo samples. If they jump at me in a Chanel way again, it will be nothing for us this time either. With "Paris - Deauville | Chanel," I was unsure. I sprayed it, and the Chanel DNA was only faintly detectable; unfortunately, it was a bit too green for me. But already better than everything else. With the first spray of "Paris - Venise | Chanel," I was very surprised. If I had tested it blind, I would never have guessed it was a Chanel. The fragrance was extremely light, soft, and extraordinarily pleasant. Delicate neroli meets gentle orange blossom, light, minimal citrus sprinkles adorn the fragrant pleasure. Powder and tonka add the finishing touch to the scent. The fragrance is wearable anytime and anywhere. It is never too much and is liked by everyone. For fans of heavy scents, it is probably not for them, but for all who enjoy pleasant, light, delicate fragrances, it is worth a test recommendation. The bottle: is of good quality; I personally find the square shape of, for example, 1957 much more beautiful and handy. Spray head very good! Price/performance: Clearly, the price for such a beautiful little fragrance is way too high. I hope to have inspired all "non-Chanel fans" to test and explore. The fragrance is worth it!! Have fun testing and sniffing!

If you were to ask my female colleagues, you would find out that I have a rather good, slightly overdressed sense of style. Especially the dresses that I like to wear in a more casual environment, they are great. If you were to ask me, you would learn that my sense of style wakes up about 2 to 3 hours after I do. I am an early bird, but my fashion taste is not.

A fine sun breeze of silky Neroli sparkles on my skin. Bright and radiant, entirely unsweet, lightly citrus-fresh and pure. A minimal delicate vanilla note sneaks in, followed by a very subtle hint of tonka. Both are so unremarkable and discreet that one would not suspect their presence in this fragrance if they did not know they were included.

Vacation vibes in lockdown. Somehow, you have to make good thoughts about it. There are these 3 fragrances from Chanel: - Deauville - Venise and - Biarritz I don't like Deauville. It reminds me of the scent of a freshly washed car, just out of the car wash and still warm from the "blow-drying".

If there is a suitable scent for an upper-class wallflower, then it is probably this one. Warm, creamy, unobtrusive. Definitely well-suited for inconspicuous secretaries. The scent becomes hardly noticeable after a short time. Absolutely not worth its money.

The sun is coming out today! No, it’s bright sunshine! My hand automatically reaches for Paris - Venise I want to smell floral-creamy light, feel light, and it works The weight on my shoulders lifts, the day feels easier, this fragrance lifts my spirits!

When it comes to Chanel fragrances it is either a hit or miss with me. While I quite enjoyed the spicy Coco, the powdery and soft Allure and the fresh and exciting No.5 eau Premiere, other Chanels like No.19, Cristalle and the highly renowned No.5 left me dissatisfied. However along came Allure Sensuelle which restored my respect for Chanel fragrances. The scent is unique, stylish, rich and spicy. A scent that will certainly rouse up the men and awaken your animalistic desires. Do not be turned off by the opening which tends to be rather strong and alcoholic. Once you wait it out for a few minutes, a gorgeous dusty yet sexy spice warms the skin. In reality Allure Sensuelle is a combination of a variety of smells; spices, woods, musk, fruits and flowers. Somehow all these notes blend together successfully. I'm still in awe of this fragrance. The patchouli note is dominant, so I'll admit that this won't appeal to some. The vanilla note also lingers in the background creating a slight sweetness and comforting warmth. The sillage and lasting strength is unbelievably good, so good that you would find it quite overbearing in the warmer months, so it is best worn at night or during Winter. Overall, Allure Sensuelle is indeed very sensual. Chanel never fails in producing elegant and sophisticated scents.

Gorgeous floriental! Two thumbs up! WAY UP!! I just acquired this fragrance and have only worn it once thus far, but it is absolutely swoon-worthy! Only the original Coco EdP and a couple of the Les Exclusifs EdT's can compete with Sensuelle EdP. I recently purchased Coco Noir, too, but this is so much more impressive than either Coco Noir or Coco Mademoiselle. Sensuelle is refined, elegant, and well, so very sensual!! As one would expect, the top notes are delicious---very fresh, juicy orange, peach, and bergamot as well as a strong, clean, sparkling patchouli note predominate. Gorgeous Turkish and Bulgarian roses bloom in the heart alongside an elegant jasmine and a cool, sophisticated iris. If there is fruit here, it is fresh, juicy, ripe fruit, NOT candied fruit. Any sweetness is a very natural sweetness, not a candied, sugary sweetness. The heart almost approaches a gourmand at moments, but it never quite reaches gourmand status. It firmly remains a gorgeous floral Oriental throughout. A clean, green, absolutely stunning vetiver accentuates the base along with a light, sparkling, clean patchouli and a bit of both sandalwood and vanilla. (This is how vetiver should be done, baby!) Lingering alongside these notes is the most heavenly incense note I have ever smelt in my life!! It is amazingly fresh throughout into the base notes despite that these notes are generally thought to be "heavy." I highly recommend this fragrance to lovers of both Orientals/Florientals, and fresh, green scents because it does have a wonderfully fresh, delicious vetiver and sparkling patchouli. It smells very expensive. Sensuelle is firmly one of my all time favourite Chanels now. This is without a doubt a Jacques Polge masterpiece and unmistakably a CHANEL at its finest. This is perfume as Art! It is sophisticated, clean yet sensual indeed, and it will undoubtedly get you noticed by both men and women. It is breathtaking and unforgettable. It is completely signature worthy, and it is aptly named "Sensuelle." So happy I ordered this one!! : ) Fragrance: 10/10 Projection: 9/10 Sillage: 9/10 Longevity: 9/10

Allure Sensuelle retains the elegance of Allure Eau de Parfum but amplifies the patchouli, and that’s precisely where it loses me. While the original is bold, sensual, and commanding, this version leans earthier and somewhat vintage. It’s undeniably beautiful, yet to me, not as captivating as Allure Eau de Parfum . It has impressive longevity and sillage, no question about that, but I prefer the more natural and effortlessly alluring charm of the original. That said, patchouli lovers will undoubtedly appreciate it.

Nobody could imagine that in that minimal, squared and almost austere bottle there's a so sensual scent! I usually saw the fragrances by Chanel in their corner in my favourite drugstore and I used to spray mainly n.5 and Coco. But last saturday I was attracted by the name "Allure SENSUELLE " (sensual) and I was curious to test if it really was so sensual as the name said. Well, at the first spray I smelled immediately the bright and citrusy notes made more interesting by the peppery touch. Then, I felt the feminin softness of the flowery heart with the unusual candied fruits note and the vetyver, giving a vibrant character to the scent. Finally, on my skin remained the more oriental base notes, such as the amber, a soft and not earthy patchouli and the wonderful frankincense accent. This so sexy and classy bouquet reminded me of the first lyrics of the famous song by George Harrison "Something in the way she moves...". This is , in fact, the "allure", it's a way to move, to be, to be woman. The sillage is very good although the fragrance is very balanced and not at all heavy. It lasts for many hours. It's a precious mid season scent perfect to wear in the colder season too or by night if you want to go in crowded place where you need a good but not excessive sillage. The price is high, as well as all the creations signed Chanel, but it's a little jewel.

The summer of 2018 was quite a blast and, as it had to happen, despite everyone complaining about how terrible it was, the same crowd is now yearning for that dreadful summer. I don’t need to understand this, neither one nor the other. Because the summer of 2018 was for me one like no other in a long time. A little dream. In this dream, I often wore another. My dearly beloved Allure Sensuelle. Only the citrus refreshers that hung in the air by the liter really got on my nerves. That’s not my thing. Now one might think, what the fuck, she can’t possibly wear Allure in summer, in the summer of 2018, which was as dusty and dry as the Sahara. But yes, she can. Orientals, or better, oriental-inspired fragrances are not made for winter. Just think for a moment, in the Orient it is mostly very warm. Fragrances made in the Orient are not citrus refreshers. -> Ah! So I preferred to wear Allure Sensuelle, which is similar yet different from its big sister Allure. It is less creamy, more powdery, spicier, and charmingly resinous-smoky, sweeter, and distinctly underlined with a patchouli note. Where Allure develops a somewhat harsh, almost brusque vanilla-citrus-wood sunscreen on me, which I really like but can’t always wear, Sensuelle conjures up a deep, purring sensuality that, and here it comes - in dry summers - is amplified. The warmth brings out the multifaceted aromas more clearly, and the fragrance gains a sunniness that reminds me of warmed skin on a vacation in the south. A bit of laissez-faire, a slipping strap, an absent caress of one’s own arm, a smile, a dancing dress, a few grains of sand on the feet. Allure Sensuelle is one of the few fragrances from Chanel that I consider erotic. Nevertheless, it doesn’t forget the good stable from which it comes. Thus, the sensual one can certainly be worn daily or in the office, with the eroticism coming through subtly, especially in dry warmth. When sprayed normally, it has a pleasantly noticeable sillage and presence without being overwhelming. Reapplying is also not necessary; it lasts until the evening. The citrus fruits here are not zesty but fruity, the pink pepper, this incredibly wonderful berry, actually brings a bit of spirit into the orangey fruitiness, giving the fragrance some pep; I don’t really smell the candied fruits, it’s more like a little sugar glaze makes the scent smoother or silkier, as it would come without a gritty powderiness, despite the floral sweetness. The vetiver-vanilla mixture reaches me clearly, similarly situated - minus spices and patchouli - in "The One" by Dolce, without wanting to compare the fragrances now, but in both, the vanilla-vetiver combo is noticeably present and very close. Often, I have a clear image of femininity in mind for a fragrance. With Allure Sensuelle, that is not the case. The fragrance represents for me gentle, sensual femininity without idealizing romance or overstated self-confidence. From a Catherine Zeta-Jones, Jessica Chastain, Julianne Moore to Kate Winslet, all types of women who are romantically sensual can be well associated with this fragrance for me. Essentially, it is a perfect all-rounder.

When I read the comments here, my skin must be very special;-). The perfume saleswoman confirmed this again yesterday while testing the collected Chanel Exclusif fragrances. With some of them, she looked at me with wide eyes and could hardly believe what my skin was doing with the scents.

A typical example in my case: Allure Sensuelle by Chanel. I first noticed Allure Sensuelle at a professional event. A lady I work with (tall, slim, dark hair, former top athlete, confident and extremely nice) walked past me, and a wonderful, extraordinary, memorable fragrance brushed my nose.

My cousin has a preference for Allure, which she introduced me to in her generous manner. I was thoroughly sprayed, to the point that my senses were overwhelmed. As the scent cloud settled, I perceived a somewhat exalted fragrance that, while fitting my cousin's spirited nature, was a note too loud and a size too large for me. She likes crescendo - I prefer piano.

After many years since its release, I have tried this wonderful perfume. Many thanks to the very friendly Tabla, who introduced me to it. The scent resembles a blend of Coco Mademoiselle from 2001 and Coco Chanel EdP. It contains the top notes (crystalline orange and bergamot) combined with the heart and base notes (spices, rose, and patchouli) of Coco Chanel.

"Hmmm, let me smell. Oh, you smell just like my mother, she’s been wearing it since I can remember!" - let's reflect on what was said. My mother's mother is consequently my grandmother. So I smell like grandma. Well, that settles it.

Both this fragrance and its counterpart, L'eau par Kenzo eau Indigo pour Femme, which I own and love, have some distinctive similarities. Obviously the masculine version is much crisper, with an interesting spiciness. The powdery aspect is quite prominent, however I absolutely adore this quality in a men's fragrance. You don't find many powdery colognes these days. I read somewhere that this fragrance is a much more complex version of the female scent, however I tend to disagree. L'eau par Kenzo eau Indigo pour Homme is spiced powder, whereas L'eau par Kenzo eau Indigo pour Femme is rich, plum-scented powder. Regardless of the two fragrances and their comparisons, L'eau par Kenzo eau Indigo pour Homme stands out in its own unique way. There is something so very sensual about this fragrance, mysterious almost. The lasting power is good, however the sillage is rather meek and mild. Not that this bothers me in the slightest. I do think that if this fragrance was overpowering it would lose most of its appeal.

For me it smells like Cartier Declaration but less spicy and it doesnt have the body odour smell that sometimes Declaration has. Lots of ginger, cedar and a bit of coriander very well blended. Smells refined and classic. Lasting power is very weak, about 3 hours. Projection aint that good too, very close to skin. Updated January 2014

Unfortunately, I am (still) not a Product Manager at Kenzo :) For this reason, it is completely incomprehensible to me why such a great fragrance as LEPKEIPH (with some names, even the abbreviation is a bit excessive) has to live in the shadows as a flanker (or, as they say nowadays: Line Extension). I don't like flankers, whether it's night, summer, sport, or any other special editions. In my opinion, every fragrance that is released should strive to survive independently and not be hidden away in some fleeting subcategory. Especially when it leads to unpronounceable word formations like "L'Eau Par Kenzo Eau Indigo Pour Homme." One must really be glad if they see the box sitting somewhere on a shelf and can pack it up wordlessly. Just imagine a customer throwing the name at a Douglas specialist, possibly even in correct French: "Excuse me, do you have 'Lo Parr Kennso O Äeeeedigoh puromm?" I speak from experience, as a lady once tried to sell me "Häbbit Ruhsch." Exactly, "Habit" like "Hobbit." If one dares to say "Abie," they will likely get a strange look :) Back to Eau Indigo, which would be a wonderful name on its own. This elegant creation definitely has what it takes to stand on its own, detached from its namesake "L'Eau Par Kenzo Pour Homme." Especially since it doesn't have much in common with the original anymore. I can hardly remember it; it was certainly a bit boring. And boredom is often attributed to the men's line of Kenzo. No wonder, if they rely on wastelands like "Kenzo Power," while the best horse in the stable is treated more than neglectfully. The time it takes to find this fragrance on the embarrassingly poor Kenzo website is roughly equivalent to its lifespan. Once you discover the associated 11-second video, you learn the most unnecessary details about the agency, director, lead actor, music, etc., but not essential things like, for example, the perfumer. Unpleasant! Eau Indigo pour homme and its female counterpart are supposed to be something like the evening or night version of the fresh normal version. Agreed. The sea blue turns into a dark indigo, has a velvety depth, and smells sophisticated. Here, "deep" is by no means to be equated with "heavy," as the fragrance remains free from well-known freshness suspects and, despite all the oriental and balsamic-sounding ingredients (e.g., Elemi and Labdanum), has a very pleasant lightness. My initial fear that it might become too sweet dissipated over the reasonably long duration of the fragrance. While it is not the exact opposite of sweet, the sweetness lies within a tolerable natural and fruity sweetness, as one finds, for example, in various dark berry types. Black currants or blueberries do not officially appear here, but I often had them in my mind's eye. In the end, a delicate vetiver-infused wood accord reassures that this is indeed a men's fragrance, and LEPKEIPH leaves a very good impression on me. But why am I writing so much? Well, I must admit, this fragrance has been haunting me for quite a while; I have tested it with numerous samples for weeks and have slowly become quite fond of it :)

I sprayed it and bought it the next day :-). Indigo does its own thing and that's a good thing. It's been a long time since I've experienced a top-notch Kenzo. Describing Indigo is not easy, but I'll give it a try. It has a zesty start, where lime could be mixed with ginger. Then comes a vibrant spice blend and an aroma that could involve tea. The woods are rather passive but present. A touch sweet, it could be tonka, and from now on, just relax. Sammy :-)

after just receiving a notification via email that a new comment has been made on this perfume, which is also in my collection, I wanted to say something about it. My problem is, I can write little that is helpful, as I lack the appropriate vocabulary, etc., especially when it comes to scents. I find that this fragrance has something paradoxical about it - it initially comes off very fresh and quite citrusy, I would even say lemony, and then I smell bergamot (which immediately conjures up the association of Earl Grey tea and cozy winter afternoons for me ;) and underneath, probably influenced by the name and packaging, something dark, blue in contrast to the bright, yellow lemon. The bergamot serves as the link (and somehow feels purple to me as a hobby synesthete). It doesn't smell like synthetic ingredients, at least not immediately, but I also don't directly associate it with anything tangible, so one couldn't say ah lovely like in a citrus garden or oh fascinating the aroma of a well-used cowboy saddle. The scent is abstract, foreign, exotic, and at the same time fascinating for me. The only one I like even better is "Tokyo," also by Kenzo - every time I take a whiff, it blows me away, although perhaps as an old stoner, the hint of green Maroc in the scent plays a role, ha ha. The problem is that Tokyo mutates into an undefinable and really disgusting mushy pastel-colored synthetic scent on my wrist after about 10 minutes, which I desperately want to get out of my nasal area as quickly as possible. It's heartbreaking. In any case, Indigo is, in my opinion, a very special fragrance that does not conform to any of the usual clichés ("clean" office scent, heavy sexual evening scent, masculine leather-and-boss scent, etc.) and smells damn good. I hope it's around for a while longer. Addendum: Rating has been lowered to 90 out of 100, mainly due to the longevity. The scent itself, however, hits me 100% (and that's a matter of taste).

Men are expected to do a lot these days. They should be strong, distinctive, and self-confident, protectors and real men, indeed. At the same time, however, they should be gentle, sensitive, empathetic, and good listeners. Whether a man can or should meet these expectations is another question - but there is certainly a suitable fragrance.

Season: Spring, Autumn Suitability: Casual and work; not necessarily a party scent Intensity: Reminds me of that one movie with Angelina Jolie and Nicholas Cage: Gone in 60 Seconds; After three sprays on my wrist, I could hardly smell the fragrance at home; I live 300m from the store Scent: Indigo strongly reminds me of Declaration by Cartier.

To get straight to the point: I cannot understand the enthusiasm for Indigo. The scent is quite nicely made - but nothing more. The penetrating fruit aromas of peach and apricot are already familiar to us from the women's fragrance "Escape." The same goes for the pudding-sweet vanilla base note.

because by the time I’ve fully recited it, my mouth is so dry that the saleswoman has to first give me a glass of water...... The first thought, oh look, a citrus scent. But it’s not as bad as it sounds...... It’s probably the coriander that keeps the lime a little in check. L´EPKEIPH is a Kenzo fragrance for men.

Rarely, very rarely do you come along, getting you is quite a challenge. Still wrapped, you stand there now, you won't be leaving me anytime soon. Once I had already sprayed one of your brothers, his scent made quite an effort to surround me. Very mature, spicy, woody-dry I perceived him, my nose wasn't quite ready for that yet.

Wonderful citric composition with light florals that smells much like Bel Respiro, but slightly heavier. This is a real fresh and green fragrance and it's wearable by both men and women. Definetely a must have for summer days! Sillage, lasting power and projection are medium. Updated January 2014

I was very fortunate to find this one mixed in with a giveaway of Men's Chanel samples and as I enjoy all scents (no label need apply) I have sampled/worn it enough now to give it a man's perspective. This bright citrus scent takes the chill off as I write this in the cold of January as it is clearly a warm weather scent. The lemon~aid like opening is sharp but not unpleasant almost candy like? As it dries down any sharpness fades and the citrus and bergamont blends nicely with the white florals into a soft sweet tame "blanket on the beach" for your skin. The more I wear it the more I find this is yet another example of unisex trapped behind a woman's label. I would definitely wear this fresh, fresh lineny scent to beat the heat come this Summer! Kind Regards, Pt1 Over All ~ 8/10

I agree entirely with the lemonade references made previously in other reviews all over the web. Lemon is certainly a dominant note, however the note isn't sharp or sour, rather it's a sweetened, almost candy-like, softened lemon note. Cristalle eau Verte is refreshing like a cool breeze on a beautiful Summer's day. The opening blend of lemon, bergamot and mandarin orange makes me long for home as it reminds me of my childhood, wandering through the fruit orchards which grew in my backyard and tasting and relishing the beautiful citrusy aromas that filled the air. The drydown is only vaguely floral with subtle hints of jasmine and magnolia every now and then. For a fragrance that is mostly citrus, it is surprising how much I've warmed to this scent. There are hardly any similarities between this fragrance and the original Cristalle. The original is much more green and sharp, whereas Cristalle eau Verte is much sweeter and softer. I must say that I'm rather impressed by Chanel's Summer offerings, with this fragrance and Chance eau Fraiche being my favourites so far.

Cristalle Eau Verte hits a merry-go-round of notes at first: fresh grass, orange just shy of fake-orange territory, rotten vegetable, and at last lands on a spicy-vegetable aroma with a fresh orange overtone. This is nice, but not impressive. Projection is 6" or so. Then out come the white florals (which seem to be mostly lily to me), but they dominate the other notes. It's too femme for me. I do like lilies when mixed with something else, like incense in Passage D' Enfer. I wouldn't mind if I smelled this on my wife and I imagine it would work well for women who want to radiate that kind of fresh, clean, pure, almost innocent kind of vibe. However, even that fades as the white blooms eventually turn indolic, and bring out the disquieting smell of earth and soil. This is an authentic but unpleasant scent. By hour six, it's evaporated completely. The opening was far more interesting than the heart notes. I don't mind either, but the fresh/clean/lily smell is pretty common, and the beginning was something new. Altogether, it's something I've smelled before and have never really enjoyed. Did I enjoy this scent? No, not really. It's just not for me.

If these lemons weren't as sour as they are, I would like to eat them! After about half an hour, when my gustative nerves have calmed down, I can smell a green meadow with a few flowers, more tart than sweet, on it. Once again a "lay-down-on-the-meadow"-scent for me - I like!!

Eau Verte opens bright and citrusy, airy and very clean, like an early-morning breeze. I enjoyed the freshness, but it fades too quickly and turns a touch soapy, leaving me wishing for more structure. It’s lovely and wearable, but too translucent to hold my interest for long. Feels like the ghost of Cristalle - elegant but fleeting.

Girls, I sincerely apologize, but I am wearing your scent… This summer, as well as during all my stays in the south, I have primarily reached for Chanel Cristalle Eau Verte this year. I have always had a penchant for light fragrances for the beautiful season, which were located in the unisex category; I have never owned a scent that was solely attributed to the ladies.

This fragrance ensures that you can still smell good even in the highest temperatures. It provides a cool, almost unattainable freshness, remaining dry at all times, lemony metallic. This blend is almost indescribable. White flowers join in after a while, as if the wind is blowing through a jasmine bush.

Sour makes funny! And Cristall eau verte makes happy... On my skin, citrus scents tend to easily tip towards cleaning products or toilet spray. Not so with Cristall eau verte, by the way my first Chanel, Chanel is a brand I haven't really gotten "warm" with so far, unlike my 10-year-old daughter, who has fallen in love with coco...

In my search for citrus scents, I eventually came across this one. Since I had read that it was also suitable for men, I decided to give it a try. Fragrance development: It starts off citrus-creamy, wonderfully soft.

After having to wake up at 7:15 in Bali (oh don’t ask me why I didn’t publish the 7:15 fragrance first), you can get out of bed a bit more relaxed here in Sicily. 10:10 AM is a good time to get up on weekends or during vacation (slowly but surely). And no, this doesn’t throw my rhythm off just because I get up between seven and eight during the week… But as I said, we are first and foremost in Sicily. Is it because of movies like The Godfather that I first think of mafiosi when I hear Sicily? Who knows, but the fragrance certainly exudes a relaxed scent that seems to be made for spring or warm days, even if it has become a bit stuffy for me personally due to some floral notes, which might appeal more to you girls (for me, the scent is slightly more feminine than unisex). The fragrance: The scent starts fresh with grapefruit and a slightly stronger mandarin. You can also already smell some light floral notes. The freesias, I assume, although it is getting a bit stuffy. In addition, the fragrance also emits nice green notes. In the heart note, the floral notes become a bit stronger and the initial citrus notes almost completely disappear. You can still smell freesias, but now roses are added. Unfortunately, I couldn’t smell figs very well, and you know how much I like figs. The musk makes the fragrance slightly sweeter later in the base, although it remains floral, with the fruity notes seeming to return a bit. Longevity and sillage: The longevity is average for summer fragrances, so you can expect it to last between four and six hours. The fragrance is generally rather weak from the start and becomes hardly noticeable later on. Unfortunately, you can’t expect a strong sillage, but it is still sufficient. The bottle: Like the 7:15 fragrance, this bottle is rectangular and has a wavy shape on the upper right side. Inside the bottle is an image that shows the sea among other things (oooh, sea… one should be there now…). The chrome and cylindrical cap sits slightly off-center on a navy blue ring. A nicely designed bottle. 10:10 AM is a fragrance that fits very well for vacation. Unobtrusive, light, and relaxed, you can wear it even under the blazing sun, although the scent, of course, neither lasts long nor projects strongly. Thus, it is a simple day or leisure fragrance. But of course, it can be used not only on vacation; it just looks so vacation-like (or vacationy??)! Of course, it has less to do with mafiosi, but as mentioned, it reminds one of beautiful vacation days, either by the sea or during lovely city tours in holiday areas, e.g., in Sicily at beautiful places that you can also see in mafia films :D Quite okay, but nothing exciting.

If you're looking for a citrusy-light summer fragrance, you've come to the right place. I've tested it about 3 times now, and I've always been truly impressed, especially by its long-lasting presence on me! Especially today, with temperatures over 30 degrees, the scent was a pleasant companion; on such days, for example, I don't even take out my Narciso Rodriguez, as it would be way too overwhelming... The fragrance is often described as unisex, as it is here, which I can't fully support, as the vetiver is very subdued on me, and I can mostly detect grapefruit, orange, and mandarin, with just a hint of cedar! I can agree with my predecessor regarding the similarity to Un Jardin sur le Nil; however, as mentioned above, the garden by the Nile is significantly more masculine than this one!

Sicilia is a fragrance that can truly bring a smile to your face. It starts with prominent but not overpowering citrus notes, which form a beautiful unity with the grapefruit (clearly recognizable) and slightly bitter tones. Wonderful! This is how I can actually imagine Sicily at 10 a.m., when the sun is already warming, but refreshing breezes from the lemon trees are still blowing. Sicilia reminds me a lot of Un Jardin Sur Le Nil, only much softer and more delicate - without the dominant incense note. However, when comparing the individual fragrance notes, Sicilia and the Jardin only share grapefruit, orange, and peony. After a while, the fine citrus notes fade a bit for me, allowing the grapefruit to come through "better." This is the point where I like Sicilia less, as the fruit does not smell juicy-delicious, but rather fresh-dry and somewhat synthetic. By synthetic, I don't mean that the fragrance smells cheap or bad, but that it is likely - as I find with many Kenzos - a deliberate scent effect that makes it feel a bit "more modern." However, I had expected more in terms of longevity, as the fragrance is only faintly perceivable on the skin after two hours and not at all after 4-5 hours.
