In terms of scent, it is indeed very office-friendly, but it doesn't have enough staying power for that. If you want to buy the fragrance, you don't even need to get on a plane. A non-turquoise drugstore chain has had the fragrance on its shelves since March. Update 02.04.2013: Due to several inquiries, I want to directly reveal where I bought the fragrance last year: the orange drugstore chain Müller!

Oooh yesss, this is it, the worthy successor to Armani White for her. Even more delicate, slightly citrusy, feminine and soft. A calm, unobtrusive scent. A true dream, very close to oneself. Don't be put off by the citrus notes, as they hold back pleasantly and blend into a wonderfully well-mixed odor (at least on my skin). My husband generally doesn't care about perfumes (his exact words: "You always smell good anyway"...), but with this creation, even he said that it smells absolutely wonderful :) If you're traveling by plane soon, go to the airport duty-free and test this gem.

The Bois des Iles I am reviewing is from the Les Exclusifs line in the EDT concentration. In every article I've read on this particular fragrance, Bois des Iles is hailed as being the first woody fragrance ever created for women. While I do agree that Bois des Iles has some woodsy qualities, I'm more swayed into placing it into a floral category. A floral woody musk tends to be more true to describing the scent itself. Bois des Iles opens like a classic Chanel fragrance, soft aldehydes and sparkling, clean soap. For a while it smelt like a cross between Chanel No.5 EDT and Allure EDP. However, once settled on the skin, Bois des Iles becomes quite buttery and 'golden'. This fragrance smells expensive and unusual, despite its rather predictable composition. I honestly could not detect any hint of the peach or bergamot in the opening, so on my skin the florals tend to dominate. The heart consists of oily florals that smell rather like a floral-scented lotion on the skin, rather than a perfume. This interesting quality had me sniffing my wrists for hours trying to determine why the scent felt so buttery and soft. The rich, buttery florals do not dissipate from the skin throughout the whole composition. Even with the arrival of the sandalwood, vetiver, benzoin and musk, Bois des Iles has a very distinguishable smoothness. I do believe that Bois des Iles is a bit of an acquired taste. While I enjoyed wearing this fragrance and revelled in its amazing lasting strength, ultimately this fragrance just wasn't me. I found Bois des Iles to be a fragrance better suited to a pretty, rather conservative and tame young lady which is far from my wild self.

~ After a friendly suggestion and reading many reviews I just had to have this one! So I ordered a large ml. bottle and rolled the dice on BdI. And as suspected I was not dissapointed with yet another classic Chanel masterpiece. Some say this is what Egoiste should have been and if that is the case I now understand its loyal following. This to my nose opened with a familiar Chanel aldehyde vibe much like Cuir de Russie but with a very clean sparkling soap added. A couple years ago I could not have appreciated this for what it is being the perfect blend of sandalwood, florals, vetiver and yes I get the faint gingerbread appeal. This may be labeled for a woman but also like Coromandel fits the well groomed man. It is amazing how a nose can mature when exposed to new discoveries such as this well crafted Chanel Exclusif line. ~ Kind Regards, Platinum1 Score ~ No number fits this scent just wear it with your best gown or suit and smile inside.

Bois des Iles is swanky! You can tell it is a Chanel right away, because of the slightly citrusy and very aldehydic opening, typically Chanel. The heart is floral, and I detect iris and jasmine most prominently, but they pass rather quickly, and Bois des Iles becomes all about the base. Ah, the wood. A very rich sandalwood. I understand amber and vetiver and tonka bean are also there, but the sandalwood speaks to me. Vivid and delicious.

I have to agree when people say that who uses Egoiste soon will upgrade to Bois des Iles. As said, BdI is more creamy, softer and more refined than Egoiste. Both are outstanding fragrances, but since i knew Bois des Iles, i have been using only it. To have an idea, it's like SL's Borneo 1932 and Chanel Coromandel: Coromandel is more refined while Borneo is more raw. Bois des Iles is more refined than Egoiste - it's lighter and creamy. The opening may smell a bit dated, but it does dries down to something outstanding: Bois des Iles has a sweet sandalwood base that lingers for hours. I would say this is one of the best sandal-based fragrance that i have ever smelt. The longevity is okay, around 7/8 hours, with a good projection and gentle sillage. Unisex for sure. So if you like Egoiste, Heritage and other sandalwood based fragrances, Bois des Iles is a must have! Updated January 2014

Whenever I wear this, I realize again and again it is not such a very difficult task to find a Holy Grail in perfume -as I often think it is... Being comfortable, mesmerizing, unique and of great quality, BdI not only thrills me with it's sheer perfection, it brings me home.

This review is for the contemporary Eau de Toilette. Top Notes: Aldehydes, Coriander, Peach, Bergamot, Neroli, Mandarin Orange. Heart Notes: Iris, Lilac, Orris Root, Jasmine, Ylang-Ylang, Lily of the Valley, Rose. Base Notes: Amber, Sandalwood, Tonka Bean, Opoponax, Musk, Benzoin, Vetiver, Vanilla. I have always loved Coco EdP, and I like No.

Have get awake memories of a flowery smell, mine used mother. I have the fashion style of the twenties in front of eyes; 'Changeling' with Angelina Jolie who must have borne this smell sees film parts from. And of course Coco Chanel. I understand the idea of the 'sacred Gral' meanwhile of which the talk already fairly often was.

Bois des Îles is a reworking of No5: rose-jasmine, iris, muguet & ylang-ylang, floating on a soft cloud of sandal, which overtops the vetiver. The heart has been dialled back to give more space to the woods, and the aldehydes are also less evident. On top of this, green verbena-citrus leads the head notes.

This is for review is for the vintage EDT! Bois Des Iles is a wonderful Sandalwood fragrance. It is marketed for women but it is very much unisex. I get a blast of sandalwood off top with some floral arrangements & that beautiful woody/ginger cookie note. This could ALMOST be gourmand but it falls short. It is delicious & wonderful in spring & fall weather.

not too long ago, I elevated the EdP to the status of my favorite companion - - my new signature scent - quasi subsidiary to the EdT described here, which unfortunately is no longer produced and is simply even more beautiful, even more radiant - - the more fragrant older sister - which is what this is about.

Loved it on a paper strip, it smelled sweet and watery but with just the right amount of character imparted by the lotus. Unfortunately, it was pretty overwhelming on my skin. It turned into this really overpowering sweet and waxy smell. Like someone extracted all the most synthetic components of Nivea cream and put them in a bottle. Felt a bit like being smothered in baby wipes.

The perfume smells strikingly fresh at first ... I would call it soapy, but I'm not exactly sure how mimosa smells. Never has a top note disappeared with such a "Hey, here I am" opening (really after 3-5 minutes), then the lotus comes through. No trace of the top note. It reminds me a lot of the body mist from Rituals. Although in the heart note, I find no mimosa. I know lotus scent to be fine and bright, but here I find it muted and somewhat smelling like "play dough." Perhaps the name doesn't refer to the flower at all, but rather the whole plant, with stem and everything. I didn't wait for the base note. To highlight the pink, the bloom, in the lotus, I layered it with Versace Bright Crystal.

I absolutely love this one! A warm, spicy, sensual oriental. I love how this smells. In fact I actually think this is unisex. Cloves, Spices, Amber, dark resins, creamy sandalwood, I can see this totally working on a man. I also see this much in the same way that I would something by Serge Lutens (whose perfumes are very rich and heady and are inspired by Morocco). The fragrance itself opens up to me with a blast of cloves, I also get a type of orange blossom smell, and peach or plum (dried fruit accord). I also detect Jasmine, and Jasmine is actually my favorite smell. There is also some prominent rose, but the base is where it all happens; resins, amber, vanilla and tonka, dry sandalwood... it's all there, and it's very very evocative! I've heard that Jacues Polge wanted to evoke Venice with this perfume (just as Shalimar was inspired by India and Opium by the Middle East and Southeast Asia etc.), and I can totally see Venice in this. Italian, Baroque and also Oriental, with spices and rich, warm sensuality. Jaques Polge himself would later refine the spices (along with more wood, leather and tobacco) to create his eventual masterpiece "Egoïste" released 6 years after Coco. I remember trying the female Opium EDP and I think this is a lot more wearable for those who couldn't wear that. It's Chanel, and a Chanel is never too loud, it knows just when to stop and hold you there, without being too loud or overpowering. In fact to my nose Coco is like a spicy, exotic, oriental version of No. 5; and just like No. 5, it makes a statement. It's grown up, it's mature, but also sensual and in-control. It's for someone who knows a little about life and is experienced both in mind and body. Someone who isn't afraid to be who they are, instead they celebrate it. I don't know if that description helps, but that's what Coco brings across to me. Warm, sensual, passionate, loving and even a little amount of danger at the edges. It takes guts to wear this, but it's totally worth it. Pure Emotion in a bottle.

I don't know why, but the EdP version doesn't jive with me. The EdT, on the other hand, is like my dream spicy perfume. Not too spicy like Opium (which is beautiful but a bit much for me), but soft spices, sort of like peaches poached in brandy and cloves. It's this golden amber ambrosia kind of scent. I think the EdT is softer, muskier, and more powdery than the EdP. And for a "less concentrated" perfume, it's awfully potent, lasting many enjoyable hours. I find it difficult to wear strong spices during the day. The EdT is my perfect spicy perfume because I think it's so casual that I could easily wear it day or night. Beautiful. Summary: Spiced liquid gold

When you have spent many days in a row testing all sorts of perfumes, again and again, perfumes that you had actually planned to get rid of, just to see if you might still enjoy them, even if you know deep down that you don't... Then it's a great relief to finally wash it all off, and spray on something that you know for sure that you really LOVE. Like Coco. Coco is never wrong. Coco is always right. And it will always be with me. While I save the edp for the colder seasons, the edt can be worn all year. Brighter and more sparkling than the edp, fruitier, more citrusy, less of the heavy (but-oh-so-beautiful) rose and civet. But no less marvellous. Elegant, but comfortable. Simply put: something I really love to wear - no need to think about it or having to try again, just to be sure. Coco fits. Sometimes I wonder why I even bother to worry about all those maybe- and not-sure-perfumes. I have this beauty, and when I wear it, I almost - ALMOST - feel as if I do not need any other perfumes at all... (Review of 90s vintage edt)

This deep, special purple fragrance casts a spice bomb in your face. Then its staring at you with slow pleasure, looks on your stupor with sensual smile. COCO EDT was created definitely for women. It is sweet, dangerous, tipical night-scent, and can be compared only to Poison or Opium in complexity. After obtaining you, it is calming down a bit, jasmine and cold cream are clouding, later on clean soapyness, and at the end – as coronation of the queen – spices unfold and reign. Endurance: more than 7 hours on my skin. Sillage: no complaints.

I had tryed the EDP some time ago and found it beautyful, but a bit too warm, too dense and spicy. Now I have a sample of the EDT and...what a difference (without loosing it's scent profile) ! I find the EDT much more bright and intriguing with the more yellow and orangey notes more prominent in the drydown. In the EDP the spicy notes were more prominent on my skin and I found it less versatile than this EDT. And I'm very happy that I don't smell vanilla! It isn't listed here, but on other websites I saw it being listed. I also love the way it behaves: not bold, but beautyful :-) It projects well, but in a decent way. Boyfriend likes it a lot too. There is some sexyness as well as cozyness. I find this very, very feminine, but in a good way. I smell all the flowers, not individually but as a beautyfully arranged bouquet. And then there is this brightness...a freshness that I can't explain but which is there...Lovely!

It makes good sense, that this fragrance is named with Chanel’s first name. It seems to me that this is more informal, way more sexy and closer to Coco’s personality than any other Chanel perfume I have smelled. I have an idea, that had I ever met Coco, this would be the impression of her, when she was herself - not business Coco or formal Coco. Just Coco.

The general consensus is that eau de toilette is weaker after reformulation in recent years. I also have the new eau de parfum but that’s still quite strong. This eau de toilette is a warm and complex scent. Even the note analysis reads like a shopping list.

My Coco. The Eau de Parfum has accompanied me for a long time in good times and bad, and even though I struggle with sparing application, this scent in the EdP version demands absolute caution when applying. Too often it has happened to my nose, which has long since become accustomed to this wonderful little fabric, that I used too much of it.

COCO and I were not friends, we weren't even acquaintances... no! I couldn't STAND COCO, I avoided COCO! I ignored and neglected COCO! COCO was the Parfum Non Grata!!!! I've been using and wearing perfumes since I was 14. The first scent I ever owned was Hypnose by Lancome.

Today I was out on a scent hunt again - inspired by the sunny weather and pleasant temperatures. Even as an agoraphobic, I dared to venture into the crowd! Additionally, I had the task of getting Coco for my cousin. She is the country mouse and I am the city mouse with connections to numerous fragrance dealers.

I tried it this afternoon and it is a super fresh and revitalizing aroma, I would even say that unisex, I, at least, would use it without qualms. I liked it much more than its male version. The aroma of this perfume is like an improved version of the perfume "Passionate Man" by Béjar. It has that citrus floral aroma, fresh and sweet with some shades of fresh, cool raspberry. I loved it, and I would use it without qualms, I would not even mind buying a bottle for me, if I was not with the dry law ... The performance is moderate, a little lower than the male version, staying on skin for 5 or 6 hours, more or less, and with a moderate projection pulling to low, since in the first hour it almost sticks to the skin, and from there, going down to death. It is a perfume of warm and temperate climates, and of daytime use, perfect to refresh those hot and suffocating days of summer that is approaching. I loved it, that's true, but I also have to say, that seeing what it costs, I buy several bottles of Béjar perfume, and although they do not smell exactly the same, they are similar enough not to make the investment, but if you Like, go ahead, it's a beautiful perfume and it's not too expensive either. Sorry for my bad english.

During the last sunny days, I had firmly decided to purchase Aqua Kenzo, as it harmonizes wonderfully with the sunshine. However, today on my way to the perfumery, a generous amount of Aqua poured from the sky in the form of thick raindrops. I changed my plans and bought a waterproof cap. But my husband suspected that the sun might shine again soon - and perhaps Aqua could also be worn in the rain? A reasonable objection, as Aqua developed pleasantly even under my umbrella. The mandarin reached me with a friendly aquatic note, and the raspberry leaf appeared fresh and green. The magnolia softly glowed under my umbrella. I hum "Singing in the rain" by Gene Kelly - and I am content with myself, the weather, and the fragrance. Aqua Kenzo proves to be very adaptable - and as my father used to say: There is no bad weather - only inappropriate clothing.

I tried this one a few times in Ulta before committing to a full bottle. I’ve smelled many many Chanel perfumes, none of which I really cared for. I think of all the designer houses, Chanel is one of my least favorite. Idk none of their scents seem to wow me or work with my chemistry. However, Gabrielle Essence is a spectacular fragrance. It definitely still holds the Chanel DNA but does it in a way that I love and can wear. I’m a huge lover of white florals, and especially when they’re sat next to a bunch of fruits and/or vanilla. While the scent itself is on the lighter side from what I’ve smelled from Chanel, it’s quite strong and potent. Projection and longevity are moderate, but can be made stronger if you overspray and wear in high heat. I don’t get much of the coconut note, but I do get lots of the different types of white florals and the fruity notes. It becomes more vanillic as it dries down, but holds on to the white floral + fruits vibe. Don’t let the notes fool you, this is a mature take on a fruity floral fragrance that can be worn anytime. I couldn’t really see anyone below the age of 25 wearing this. I’m really happy to have discovered this perfume and I’m even happier to have her in my collection. She’s going to be a spring and summer staple for sure!

I'm not a big fan of the original Gabrielle, but this version is much more to my taste. Which is not a big surprise, considering that I often prefer Intense/Essence/Le Parfum/... flankers over the pillar fragrances. In Gabrielle's case, I found the original too sharp, soapy and citrusy. Essence is a bit warmer, but still firmly in the clean floral territory. It starts out fresh and sparkling and dried down delightfully creamy. Ylang ylang and jasmine are easy to identify here. There is definitely a hint of the classic Chanel DNA in this, and something that reminds me slightly of Chance. I do not get a lot of the listed red fruits, instead I sense a hint of tropical notes. If scents had colors, Gabrielle Essence would have shades of yellow and white, no red. This doesn't reinvent the wheel, but it's very nicely done. I really enjoy how creamy it turns after a couple of hours. Maybe a little less citrus or more vanilla would make it even better to me, but that's a matter of personal taste. All in all I would categorize this as an elegant spring and summer scent. It smells great on warm skin and is ideal when you want to evoke something more sophisticated than fruity cocktails or sunscreen, but still feel sunny.

Gabrielle Essence opens up much better to my nose versus the original EDP. With that one, it seems harder to distinguish between notes, at first. Essence doesn’t have the same sparkling brightness as the original, but the fruity notes are better and juicier overall. Not sharp, but smoothed out by the white floral notes, that make up the Gabrielle DNA. This is a blend of peach and citrus, with a bit of coconut that becomes more noticeable deeper into the wear. While the fruity opening is better here, it also is shorter lived to my nose. This one gets down to the floral notes rather quickly, but I actually like that phase of Essence. The main difference with the floral notes for me is, Essence has a stronger emphasis on orange blossom and jasmine, at first. With the EDP, it was jasmine and tuberose. The tuberose in Gabrielle Essence doesn’t play that big of a role. Eventually, the jasmine, orange blossom, and ylang-ylang are sharing most of the duties. That’s what I get for most of the rest of the wear. It’s a bit sweet and has a nice, but not thick creaminess about it. Light musk and woodiness, at the base, but this is mostly all about those floral notes. Nothing overly complicated, just a variation of what you’d expect.

This scent just smells rich, feminine and confident. Lovely well mixed white florals and soft musk: just an amazing blend. You can feel the Chanel DNA with a youthful, classy twist. A must have for that spring, quiet luxury feel. Great projection, crazy long longevity! I wore a top just a couple of hours and hung it back in my closet and could still smell it 3 weeks later every time I opened up my closet. It lasts at least 12+ hours on my skin.

I got Gabrielle Essence as a gift. It's super classy and elegant creamy floral fragrance but not generic. If you are a business woman with a suit you really should try this out. Don't be afraid because it's Chanel. Much more youthful than most of the Chanel fragrances. I'm definitely not that boss lady so I don't think this suits me very well. However it's beautiful and performs nicely.

I've received this as a tester and I am not familiar with the original Gabrielle. This Essence version starts out thick and a little on the heavy side for me. The opening reminds me of a syrupier version of Chloé Nomade, perhaps a bit more citrusy. It's quite difficult to me to distinguish any note, it's a strong blend of all.

I've never been a huge fan of Chanel despite my countless attempts – definitely too old-lady connoted. The only perfume I can wear from this house is Coco Mademoiselle, to me their greatest success ever. After yet another disappointment with the original Gabrielle -still too 'Eau de Cologne' for old ladies, too dull - I had given up the idea of wearing another Chanel...

Gabrielle is having a bit of a hard time on the German market. It is not as "typical Chanel" as one might expect. Gabrielle dances a little out of line. Less strict, less matronly, less conservative than the well-known icons. "A fragrance full of radiance," writes Chanel on their homepage. "Warm, floral, sensual, and opulent" it is supposed to be.

The big question is: to what extent is Gabrielle 2, as I will simply call it, different from Gabrielle 1? And: is all the flankering, even at Chanel, not clichéd and unnecessary? I will answer the second question first: one could see it that way. However, if you have a brand-related weakness as a fragrance collector like I do with Chanel, it can make subjective sense.

... my grandma used to say. And I agree with her. That's why I liked the Gabrielle EdP very much. She is the nice, neat girl next door - without any pretensions. Essence, on the other hand, comes across to me like her older sister, who loves to dress up and wants to be the center of attention.

I obtained a small bottle of Kenzo 7:15am IN BALI out of curiosity from a discounter (hence, scent unsniffed), and after several wearings, I have to say that I'm not really smitten with it. I say this because it seems as though I am alone, given all of the glowing reviews I've seen. To my nose, BALI seems a bit off somehow. It may be that the orchid and fruit are imparting a slightly sour cast to the vanilla, and that may very well have been intended by the perfumer as an olfactory effect, but unfortunately it reminds me somewhat of the endless catalogue of bad synthetic sandalwood vanilla frags. I should say that, on a good day, I find this perfume rather pleasant to wear, albeit not that exciting, and I do always perceive its synthetic cast--it's just that on a good day I don't mind that so much. I suppose that since this is a limited edition travel issue to be sold at duty-free shops at airports to tourists on their way to vacations in far away exotic places, BALI is supposed to convey the calmness one feels while lying on a beach having left all one's worries behind back home. So it's not really supposed to be a high-energy, revolutionary scent. Rather oddly, every time I see the image on the bottle, before having focused, it looks like a bodybag to me. On closer examination, it proves to be some pillows on a bed. And maybe that's a good metaphor for the contents of the bottle as well.

I think to myself after testing this fragrance. At first, I didn't want to test it - it was an addition to a test package. I simply expected "humid". Well, I've never been to Bali and have never really looked into Bali either. Eyes closed, nose open, and go: Oh and oh, not at all humid and overly floral as I expected, the top note is quite subtle. So I kept sniffing and didn't throw the sample away right away. Hmmh, fine and getting finer, a blend of the heart and top notes with a slight depth, the origin of which I can't really grasp. For me, it's a wonderfully non-humid, delicate, slightly fruity, non-vanilla vanilla scent. Very close to the skin and warm, non-sillage. Anyway, for me, it's simply a warm cozy scent, a home-with-me-and-book scent. So very subjective.

Morning in Bali, at 7:15 AM. Hmm… isn’t Bali one of the most popular tourist destinations in the world? Hm… I should first complain, because I want to go on vacation again… *complain* *sigh* *complain complain* But: why is the fragrance actually called 7:15 AM? Does it smell different later in Bali? And besides, if I were on vacation there (or anywhere else), I wouldn’t get up at 7 in the morning?? But anyway, I was actually only interested in this fragrance because of its name, and I got the chance to test it. Well, let’s see…. The scent: The fragrance starts sweet, as you can smell the beautiful jasmine. Then there’s the also pleasantly fragrant passion fruit, adding a fruity and another sweet scent. The grapefruit is also present, albeit only slightly, yet you can sense its light, citrusy note. Barely two or three minutes have passed, and you can already smell the vanilla, which makes the scent more powdery; the orchid (but to be honest, it just smells a bit floral to me, I can’t say if it really smells like orchids) gives off a slightly stuffy scent, but this remains more in the background, as the sweet notes from the jasmine and the fruity scents are still very prominent and even become more intense for a while. The sweetness can occasionally come off as a bit artificial, but it still smells good, so it doesn’t bother. Over time, the vanilla becomes stronger, and the fruity and floral notes are still detectable for a while. Longevity and sillage: The longevity is about five to six hours, which is rather average, but you can always reapply. The sillage is a bit reserved, but can still be caught by someone nearby. Unfortunately, the fragrance radiates less and less over time and quickly loses its intensity. But,… as mentioned, you can always reapply. The bottle: At first glance, the bottle reminded me of the fragrances that were briefly available at Aldi last year. So, a simple, rectangular bottle with an image inside. However, this bottle has a dynamic line and also offers a nice image inside. The cap is cylindrical and bronze-colored, sitting on an orange neck. Everything is nicely done. So, 7:15 AM in Bali is a scent that could definitely be associated with something holiday-like. It simply smells casual and light and creates a pleasant atmosphere. I believe that for most people, it will just be a sweet-fruity perfume that doesn’t stand out from the crowd. While that’s true, it still smells nice. It’s a fragrance that fits well in spring and summer and could be used for everyday wear or leisure. As a holiday scent, it is also very usable. For going out, it’s quite nice, but perhaps a bit weak and inconsequential for that. Despite being labeled as unisex, I find the scent very feminine, as it contains sweet notes and passion fruit, which is more commonly found in women’s fragrances. Therefore, I would particularly recommend that women test this fragrance if they are looking for a casual, sweet scent that can be worn well in leisure. 7:15 AM. Honestly… I’m going back to sleep, good night!

My girlfriend loves Bali and constantly raves about her trips there. So I had to test 7:15. If it smells so enticing there, I would also make the long journey and set my alarm for 7 AM to not miss the special 7:15 scent. Even as a passionate late sleeper, I stretched my head out of the window to indulge in this delightful fragrance. I am greeted by a full, yet non-sticky vanilla sweetness that is brightened by jasmine. The scent is not winter warm - rather, it is sun warm. The orchid blends in finely and elegantly, with a fruity hint of passion fruit. One might think of the lush exotic vegetation or colorful, aromatic markets. 7:15 is full of life - but not loud or restless. No, it speaks of serenity and peaceful tranquility. The scent will help my girlfriend while packing her suitcase - and she will set the alarm for 7:15.

How I would love to buy this fragrance again. And see if it still fascinates me as much. Because actually, I thought 20 years ago during the first test that such a scent was far too sweet, too much vanilla, too many flowers (Frangipani?), too intense. But this fragrance was wonderful, as it was in good balance with lightness, freshness, sun on the skin. And of course, a lot of Bali vibe. Because, just like my other all-time favorite Un Jardin apres le Mousson, the name fits perfectly and immediately evokes wonderful emotions.

Paris-Deauville saved my life when I lived in Rome in a historic apartment building that didn’t allow air conditioning. Arriving back from work, I would open the fridge and spray this all over my arms and legs, which were by then coated with a sheen of moisture that never failed to astound me, as a girl from a country with very little humidity, let alone heat. Oh, it felt glorious! One of the most natural citrus notes I have ever smelled (pink grapefruit to my nose), rubbery green basil, what smells like fig leaf, some Chanel white musks, and a polite, sanitized patchouli bringing up the rear. For a brief moment, before the scent becomes ‘perfumey’ in that typical Chanel manner, it feels like sticking your face into a basket of freshly cut citrus fruits nestled between huge bunch of wet, crisp herbs. Back in Ireland, though, I sense a familial connection – however faint – with Coco Mademoiselle, which makes it feel a little less special. I realize that what I loved about Paris-Deauville in Rome was its very un-Chanel-like garden freshness, albeit one delivered to me in a Chanel-quality casing. In colder weather, sadly, the perfumeyness of the Chanel musks swells to fill the space, masking those juicy, uber-naturalistic herbs and citruses that explode out of the bottle under heat conditions. In other words, while Paris-Deauville remains one of my favorite herbaceous citrus perfumes, it earns that position mostly on the back of its enormous service to me during a ridiculously sweaty time of my life rather than its utility to me now.

Iced lemon slices in a cut glass bowl, encased in ice; fresh, crisp herbs soaking in ice water, subtle as a lacy front or two. The memory of a glass of sweet white wine, a honeyed, floral Gewürztraminer wisp; round, rich, luscious, and strangely absent for all its suggestion. Somewhere between charming and refreshing, gentle with a glint in its eye; Not overly polite yet definitely inoffensive, nothing weird you can put your finger on, but there's a phantom shimmer, a flickering presence, an impossible-to-name thing, which makes it either perfectly frustrating or frustratingly perfect.

Paris-Deauville opens up with a delicious burst of its citrus notes. The main ones are going to be lime and mandarin orange. There is also so lemon. The orange note is very familiar, since it’s the same orange from Coco Mademoiselle. Basil adds a great fresh spiciness to the blend. The citrus and green aroma is very attractive and bright for the summer months. It all sits on top of a generally green and slightly floral mix in the base. It’s all very fresh and bright. Quite unisex. Basil and lime are the main attractions for most of the wear. The other citrus notes play a supporting part. As it dries down, you do get a bit of jasmine and rose, but not much. Patchouli is the third strongest and really works well with the other two. However, Deauville doesn’t develop all that much as a fragrance. You’ll get most of what you’re going to get early on in the wear. The good news, is that it is a very nice perfume and enjoyable.

A summer fragrance that doesn’t catapult me directly to Italy or even the Caribbean already opens doors for me. Sure, oranges and basil don’t exactly grow on the Atlantic coast, but the drive from Paris to Deauville really clears the head. The playful aspects of Mediterranean Dolce Vita scents are missing here, and that does the fragrance a lot of good. The scent allows for deep breaths and remains serious. The elegance one encounters in exclusive seaside resorts is certainly recognizable. Here, there’s neither excess nor skimping; it is used in a well-measured way, and there’s even a bit of understatement at play. I perceive the scent as cool, consciously distinguishing it from "fresh." This is not a typical refreshing fragrance; rather, I would place it in Dior's "Escale" line if one wishes to make a comparison. I also assume that the creators at Chanel had similar intentions when they commissioned the three new fragrances. Paris-Deauville shows that it is possible to create an elegant summer fragrance with just a few ingredients without it appearing minimalist or even banal. I like that, but I still miss a little hook, a corner, a smile, a touch of extravagance. I would love to wear it if I received it as a gift. However, I don’t feel the need to purchase it, especially since I fear that the price is not conducive to casually picking it up. Regarding the Chanel range, I can say: This was missing - and I’m glad that Chanel is still - or once again - able to create perfumes without catering to the LVEB line. Bravo Olivier Polge! Now, of course, I’m curious about the other two fragrances in the series. Addendum in autumn 2019: As beautiful as the scent is and as comfortable as I feel with it - the short longevity does bother me now. It’s one thing to reapply a fresh perfume throughout the day in summer, but in autumn, it’s disappointing when nothing of the scent can be perceived after about 2-3 hours. Now, all I can do is send Paris-Deauville into hibernation in the depths of my closet to enjoy it again next spring, or offer the fragrance in the souk. The decision is not easy for me.

Somehow, I am increasingly fond of light, redundant fragrances. After experiencing the new, pleasant "Balade Sauvage" by Dior, the blind purchase of the new Chanel niche fragrance "Paris-Deauville" was also a "Must Keep" experience. The distance between the two places that inspired the name initially made me think of classic cars, perhaps in the 1920s, occupied by couples in love fleeing the urban summer heat, heading towards Normandy and its wild, cooling coast. Pure nostalgia! This impression fits quite well, as this beautiful unisex refresher indeed offers an extremely pleasant, slightly tangy, green, and gently wiry aromatic spectrum. Perhaps really just the two aromas mentioned above, undeniably much fresher, herb-green basil, mixed with a slightly bitter, marginally sweet orange or rather its peel. This is pleasing and shines in a rather puristic kind of beauty, which has been arranged very sensitively and skillfully by Polge. One can easily imagine how the lady and gentleman of the world, perhaps Cary Grant and Katharine Hepburn, stepping out of the classic car and having the cool, rough sea in Deauville before them, might have reached their destination, leaving behind such an unobtrusively stylish and fresh green scent trail. Lovely.

In Normandy, oranges do not grow. What were Chanel or Olivier Polge thinking? Did we somehow confuse Normandy with the Midi? Basil is also not exactly a typical Norman herb. Normans traditionally season with salt, pepper, and garlic. Garlic in a perfume would certainly not work well. Cooking is done with apples (cider, Calvados), and apples grow everywhere in rural Normandy.

When I read or hear Deauville, I immediately think of the young Leslie Caron as “Gigi,” who in the film adaptation of the musical tries to ride along the beach on a stubborn donkey, while Mamita (her grandmother?) laughs and reminisces with the now-aged bon vivant Honoré Lachaille (Maurice Chevalier) as they watch the lively scene unfold.
On the beachfront promenade of Deauville, right next to the glamorous casino, lies the famous Hôtel Normandy.

Paris - Deauville is the 1st of the 3 new Chanel fragrances (which thematically seem to be associated with seaside resorts) that I wanted to test. I knew nothing about Deauville, except that it is located in the somewhat rough Normandy.

Out of the 3, I like this one the best. Biarritz disappears in less than an hour and only smells of citrus. Venise is nice too, but it's quite a subtle scent and feels too feminine for me. Deauville is truly unisex, but it really stands out from the mainstream scents due to the basil note. I find the sillage/projection to be the best of the three.

I really like it! It smells very nice but it's way too discreet. It lasts a little. The price is not a big one. I finished its sample; unfortunately, only 1 ml and I want more! I bought it in a discovery box on N *. I would also like to test Flower by Kenzo. I see this perfume worn especially by ladies. It makes me think of my favorite teacher of all time, who I had in high school. I think this perfume would suit her. Rating: 9/10

Tried this on my skin in the perfumery and went outside to experience the scent without all scents in the perfumery lingering. At first I thought: "Wow, this is a much better take on the original Kenzo Flower (which I don't like that much)" It seemed more airy than the original and I got some 'Chanel 5 l'Eau' vibes (though in a different way, but as translucent and airy as that) and the wind wafted some good whiffs towards me. But after half an hour or so, it turned into the original Flower by Kenzo Eau de Parfum . Not my cup of tea.

...to the first urban flower farm in France. "Plein Air Paris": a project aimed at bringing people closer to natural flower cultivation and raising awareness about the urgency of returning to natural, thoughtful, and environmentally friendly agriculture. This project surely inspired the naming of this perfume. I haven't been there myself yet, but the pictures I found and the comments I read speak for themselves. If I ever travel to France, I will check out this project. Flower by Kenzo La Récolte Parisienne combines the wonderful poppy that Alberto Morillas has uniquely managed to infuse with a fragrance, with a wildflower meadow blooming in all colors. A summer day, a radiant blue sky, and I am floating through a sea of colorful flowers. A gentle breeze sweeps through this magnificent meadow with me, and a floral scent reaches my nose. I will never forget the day in 2000 when I entered the perfumery I trust, and my favorite saleswoman handed me a silky poppy bloom and sprayed it with the newly released Flower by Kenzo, holding it under my nose. I was speechless; all vocabulary had deserted me. If someone says poppy doesn't smell, oh yes it does! I believe anyone who knows and loves "Flower" will immediately think of it and have it in their nose at the sight of a poppy bloom. Since that day, Flower has been an indispensable part of my collection. Yes, and this classic "poppy scent" mixed with delicate roses and dahlias at the start, accompanied by mandarin, leading to the vanilla that perfectly rounds off the fragrance, is simply wonderfully successful in its entirety. It truly reminds me of a walk through a sea of wildflowers where many scents unite into one. The longevity is really good, lasting over 8 hours. After this time, one can still perceive the rose gently nestled in vanilla. A beautiful fragrance for anyone wanting to bring back a bit of summer and escape the uniform gray of the approaching winter. I think it should be a part of every "Flower" collection, and the beautiful bottle has captivated me; it's the little ladybug crawling up the stem of the poppy bloom.

I seem to do better with CHANEL Eau de Toilettes than Eau de Parfums, and Coco Mlle is no exception. There are so many similar creations flooding the market, even within CHANEL's own house with the Chance line, but all of those other fruity florals seem kind of baseless, like ghostly fruits that just fade into oblivion too quickly. Coco Mlle is all substance. It's surprisingly woody and complex for a fresh and fruity perfume; never boring. Longevity with the Eau de Toilette is remarkable on my skin, no worse than the Eau de Parfum. I can see this being great for casual use as well as an evening out. Maybe not for sequinned dresses or ball gowns though. SUMMARY: Easy pleaser for women of all ages

Have to admit = I hate eau de parfum version. And ++ ITS NOT CROWD PLEASER. I dont know any single woman use this around of me. + why I hate? Because grapefruit + patchouli combo. That start was terrible and my nose cant stand. Luckily this edt is better to my nose. No weird starting like edp. Yes very citrusy at start, drydown = maleish scent. But I think PATCHOULİ dose isnt very much like edp. Male style drydown comes from = patchouli and vetiver! (I dont like dominant vetiver too, lol but here its ok) Also here citruses are not so sour, bad style. While its better version heard Its discontinued, WHY Chanel!? You MUST discontinued the edp one. I only saw in 1 shop edt and tester. Males can use too.

I was originally looking for the EDP version but they didn't have a tester bottle, so I settled with the EDT. I find many similarities between this fragrance and Allure by the same house. They both have a familiar soapy, fresh vanilla scent. I can't say that the lasting power was all that, but for an EDT it isn't bad. The scent is a little common for my liking, however it is a perfect, inoffensive fragrance suitable for Spring or casual outings. Don't buy this if you're searching for something that is sensual, sexy or head-turning, Coco Mademoiselle EDT is much better suited as a bright, feminine and youthful fragrance.

Coco Mademoiselle EDT opens up quite a bit like the EDP version, though definitely smoother and not nearly as intense. What’s most noticeable, is how the orange note shares duties here with other citrus notes, and an additional litchi. Another thing that I notice here, is that, the patchouli note isn’t as dominant in this version of the Mademoiselle line. It’s there, but I feel it to be more balanced with the vetiver sitting in the base of the scent. What’s interesting is that the base of Mademoiselle EDT, is very similar to the Chanel men’s cologne, Allure Edition Blanche. The creamy vanilla, woods, and vetiver is a dead ringer. That fragrance is dominated by lemon, rather than litchi and a more general blend of citrus. What’s true about both of those fragrances, is that they both have a weaker ability to project than the flanker fragrances that they spawn from (more so in Edition Blanche’s case). Once the citrus notes have burned off and the litchi seems weaker, the floral notes really come through strong. Jasmine and rose are fairly even, but I get more jasmine, on my skin. Those two with wood, musk, vetiver, patchouli, and the vanilla note that develops further along. The final dry down is a woody vetiver scent with a less creamy aroma, that sort of starts to have a bit of a powdery feel. Not too much, but noticeable.

I have heard, that coffee, blue cheese, red wine and olives are tastes you have to get accustomed to. To me, it is true. I did not love any of these things from the beginning. But I have grown to like them simply by keeping on trying. Coco Mademoiselle, to me, is the same story. In 2001 I started noticing a new scent around me. A growing number of women would smell the same. I did not know the scent a the time, and I certainly did not like it. It was horrible for me to be exposed to it, wherever I went: the supermarket, the cinema, work, the airport. The scent was everywhere. It took some time ‘adjusting’ my nose to this sharp, citric scent. Several years, actually. To my nose it smelled of too much. I guess it was the patchouli mixed with the citrus fruits. Everyone I knew at the time loved it and spoke highly of it - and wore it. Then one day a colleague gave me an almost empty bottle. She knew of my weird hobby and asked me if I had this in my collection. I said no, and told her I did not like it. She answered ‘oh, same with me to start with - but I have grown fond if it’. Today I still have the almost empty bottle. I do not wear this scent often, but I have grown to like it, especially on hot summer days. It is perfect because it is fresh and stays that way. Now I can finally enjoy the scent. I am happy that my nose has matured. 58/365

This smells identical to the original for me, but with more citrus and fruits up top, and a lighter, more transparent heart and base. Starts with a big burst of refreshing citrus, most notably the unmistakable Coco Mademoiselle orange.

This was my first 'big girl' perfume, and I can't remember who bought it for me for a birthday or maybe a Christmas gift, but I was OBSESSED. That said, it was too mature for me (as a teen) and I don't know what happened to my bottle. But, I tried it again at Nordstrom's this week and the scent memories came flooding back!

A comparison between the different versions and the desperate attempt to find the right Mademoiselle for me. Rarely has a fragrance confused me as much as “Coco Mademoiselle.” I have certainly tested the well-known EdP dozens of times in the perfumery. I wanted to like it so much. I confess: The bottle and the brand behind it were the main reasons.

Whoever thinks: A Chanel, how elegant? I must disappoint you. Because this fragrance is similar to Coco Chanel back in the day-fresh, cheeky, but above all, unpredictable. Where did we meet again? In my fragrance hangout, my scent shelf. We spent so many days together in my youth and punk fragrance days that he became a part of me back then.

I have been using the Eau de Toilette "Coco Mademoiselle" by Chanel regularly for several years. I give this fragrance a solid 10. It is a fresh, pleasantly floral, vanilla scent. The floral components make up the main part of the fragrance but are never too dominant.

Super aquatic and not sweet at all, there's some green and apple in the opening and lots of pepper. There's very little in the way of amber, hazelnut or sesame here and I don't get much tonka either. Mostly it's just bitter and fresh water/aquatic note heavy. This does however layer freaking amazingly with Affection by Lattafa. I literally only wear this fragrance layered with Affection as it's so good this way. The all that bitter wet freshness of AKpH is complimented by the lily of the valley in AL, and the lactonic pistachio REALLY brings out the tonka, hazlenut and sesame here.

The perfume I like, but it's nothing new, I do not know if you've tried it, but it smells a lot like Tom Ford's Black Orchid, although it's super diluted, it's like an aquatic Black Orchid, fresh and very airy . I feel it more towards the fruity than the aromatic, but it is not bad aroma, especially if you like Black Orchid. The performance on my skin has been moderate, with an approximate duration of about 6 or 7 hours, with a wake very noticeable at the beginning, but which, in a matter of 15 minutes, declines to moderate, and from there, progressively falling to death skin ras. It is a cheerful and summery fragrance, and although it is cool, it is not fresh, it has a good fruit load, which makes it have some body and not very recommended for the day, I see it more focused on the nights, warm and fresh, spring and summer. I thought it was a good perfume, but Black Orchid's brazen air has made me not completely convinced, although if you like the perfume of Tom Ford, with this you will be able to continue enjoying it during the summer. Sorry for my bad english.

After this blind buy, I was a bit scared after reading all the negative reviews here on parfumo. I can - at least for myself - give complete reassurance. What is supposed to be so disgusting, grotesque, and terrible about Kento's "Aqua" is completely beyond me. Of course, this perfume is far from being a masterpiece; the similarities to One Million Lucky are just too obvious. "Aqua" simply reduces the "sweet component" compared to its Spanish counterpart. Also, the name is rather misleading. I only perceive "Aqua" as particularly aquatic on the periphery. But that doesn't mean it lacks any association with a pleasantly warm summer vacation. And here comes my headline into play. Kenzo's Aqua conveys a wonderfully unsweet beach atmosphere without any frills. Yes, it definitely has a noticeable synthetic quality, but that doesn't always have to be negative. I detect a warm, driftwood-like note that is constantly wafting around my nose. The forbidden fruit apple is hard to find with a magnifying glass. As for the hazelnut, I have to pass; yes, there is a nutty note present. However, my nose assigns this more to roasted sesame. Also nice is this ozonic, airy sea breeze. Even though the fragrance pyramid doesn't offer anything in this direction, I perceive it quite well. All in all, "Aqua" is a surprisingly unique representative of its kind. As I said, One Million Lucky has a similar DNA but is much sweeter. Kenzo's unpopular offspring can do summer! Period. The longevity is great at about 6 hours, and the sillage is also quite remarkable. Anyone looking for a pleasant summer companion without fruit, citrus notes, etc., can buy this without hesitation. Not everyone always wants fruity summer scents that often fail in longevity. With Kenzo's Aqua, you can take a long summer walk without having to worry about your scent ;) So my conclusion is: Definitely give it a try, simply ignore the reviews and rely on your own feelings. Of course, I'm not denying anyone their opinion, but let's be honest... A rating of 5... Come on! Have a great day :)

If only the name would fit.... No, nothing here is truly right, and a 5.1 as an average is a tough but fair statement. That must be said. Kenzo has carelessly poked around in its aroma vessels with this "Aqua Homme." Each of them must consist of absolutely inferior fragrance oils, just as it stings in the nose here. There is absolutely nothing aquatic about it, just a sticky-fruity base tone. The invitingly fresh photo on the packaging, which prepares you for wonderfully blue, lively "coolness," is essentially a gross deception of the consumer. Only my mood is rapidly cooling down here. A poorly executed, very artificial apple that reminds one of cheap room fragrances. In the background, there's a sticky-sweet constant nerve tone, a mix of car air freshener vanilla and sticky hazelnut. The whole thing is held together by a shower gel synthetic clamp, which has unfortunately become the ideal standard in this decade in the basic perfumery segment. Absolutely underground. I don’t need to write more about it.

CRISTALLE edp bears nearly no resemblance to the descriptions offered by reviewers of CRISTALLE edt, which is apparently an entirely different perfume. Far from being clear and crystalline, I find CRISTALLE edp very dark and heavy, similar in some ways to Estee Lauder KNOWING. In fact, upon initial application, I was sure that there was civet in this composition. I know that I'm not alone, as one reviewer reported that her s.o. told her that she smelled like "urine cakes". Clearly she was wearing the edp! I do definitely get, as advertised, a big soil note, similar to something like peat. The galbanum is very notable in CRISTALLE edp, which makes it super longlasting and viscous. My sample is dark amber, rather than limpid, and although jasmine plays an important role, I would categorize this as a classic chypre with lots of brown grassiness. The sillage is not on a par with oakmoss monsters such as EAU DU SOIR, but I wouldn't want to suffocate in an oakmoss-galbanum amalgam, so that's fine with me. I have several good chypres and so won't be adding CRISTALLE edp to my collection, but I am curious to test the edt.

In general, the 'green' fragrances leave a colder impression. Not ice-cream cold, but 'leave me alone' distant cold. My kind of cold. I can't say that Cristalle is in the ultra-green end of the spectrum, but it does hold a certain chill factor. I would score it a medium. Although my tolerance for greens is set to industrial freezer levels, so not sure if that helps anyone. Together with the citrusy, minimally powdery opening notes, the grassy greens emerge immediately. They last until the end, backed by soft moss and vetiver. A vetiver that has the typical Chanel vibrance, that I like to describe as 'glassy'. After an hour or two the vibrance is tuned down a few clicks to modest levels, while the scent really does not change much. No funny twists like fruits or animals popping up. Little development. No frills. Despite the evident vetiver-moss backbone, Cristalle remains in a mild airy state that slowly fades instead of landing onto solid ground. Cristalle does not tell a thrilling story with dramatic twists or cliffhangers. It kind of reads the news bulletin. Sober, functional and business-formal. Does not seduce, does not offend. After the sillage has settled down, I guess it would be a good office scent. Personally, I enjoy Cristalle's cold airy character the most in outdoor settings, especially in spring/summer. Mainly because of the sillage at the start.

Different, is a good word to start with when it comes to describing Cristalle by Chanel. Although Cristalle is often referred to as a 70's scent, it is surprisingly modern for its time. The fragrance opens with crisp and refreshing lemon supported by a blend of dry and unsweetened florals. The scent is quite green and fresh, somewhat similar to Chanel No.19, however it is not as sharp and chemical. It took me a while to like this fragrance seeing that the opening itself was rather overpowering and sour, however the drydown and the sudden presence of the floral notes softened the scent and gave it an undeniable feminine quality which was quite lovely. My perception on this scent is that it's rather soapy yet fresh and revitalising. I found myself detecting a note hidden somewhere in the drydown which smelt rather like a smouldering cigarette. I must add that I rather like the smell of cigarettes, particularly on the opposite sex. Honestly this isn't a fragrance that you're likely to find me wearing. Chanel's classy and sophisticated scents don't seem to do me justice, however on the right people these types of scents really have the ability to shine. While this crisp, watery, herbaceous and lemony-fresh scent doesn't suit me, I'm almost certain that it will suit lovers of these kinds of fragrances.

Some days, nothing can compare to Cristalle. The spell is capable to cast is so powerful that one's hands feel like gravitating towards its container. If I could, on those days I would bathe in it. Cristalle is utter sophistication. Enchanting, distinctive without being loud, precious in the way only great creations - of all sort - can ever be. On me, the melon/oakmoss combo dance, enraptured with each other. It's a dance of passion, the water and fire each shaping first a separate, then a common impression in the air. My mind thus keeps twirling around one, then the other, then the both, in a waltz of notes that makes me dizzy. I want to really dance, swirl around to release more of them, then drown in them. Few hours into the spell, jasmine and peach add to the ball, juicy and crisp enough to not obscure the previous duo. At last, ylang ylang and vetiver make their appearance; one dance and they leave, only to return some time later for a goodbye take. It's then that the oakmoss truly give its best and my mind goes: "How do I love thee? Let me count the ways. I love thee to the depth and breadth and height My soul can reach, when feeling out of sight For the ends of being and ideal grace. I love thee to the level of every day’s Most quiet need, by sun and candle-light." Poetry. Cristalle is my most beloved perfume poem.

cristalle is one of my best perfumes i am using it since i was 16 and the best thing that the Fragrance is continuously throughout the day, all over the body and clothing, the shower gel is wonderful,It's wonderful fragrances .

The Basenotes review by Calchic is what I echo. "It's chic, puzzling, happily paradoxical" I own Cristalle EDT, EL's Jasmine White Moss, Eau du Sud by Annick Goutal and others whose names don't immediately spring to mind. My husband owns Eau Savage and wears it often. Along with Chanel 19 EDP, Cristalle is my favourite Chanel.

Cristalle is rooted in the green chypre, and has a passing likeness to Y. It opens on citrus, and a creamy gardenia - with its taint of mushroom. And then, behind that, there's a rosy bouquet - which shows a different side to Cristalle. Instead of being a bluestocking - but coloured in green and beige - there are glimmers of sweetness that counteract the dry impression.

A lovely green fragrance that is subtle and therefore so me! Fresh and feminine with beautiful flower notes that compliment the citric top notes. When wearing it I feel sophisticated and chic - like a well-dressed Parisienne walking down Champs-élysées, looking at windows.

Edit: I actually find the 2023 version much better, it now comes with Hyacinth and honeysuckle and Iris, it still is Cristalle like I wrote below, but less linear and with more to wonder about. Still fresh, less cold in my opinion.

At the time my father bought this in the mid to late 1990s, this was a new perfume, having been released in 1993. A bit harsh, very 90s, kind of smokey, and slightly bitter. The orange fades a bit too fast, leaving the melon to sort of fester. You can smell the peach but only if you concentrate really hard.

First thoughts, this is an oud dominated scent mixed with Kenzo Homme DNA. - Kenzo Santal Marin starts with a strong dose of oud and woody/earthy scent. It has very little sea notes or lavender in the opening, if not none at all. - I sprayed a total of 5 times. Twice behind each ear, twice on the front of neck, and once in front of my chest. The longevity is okay, it lasts approximately 8 hours on my skin, projects for about an arms length for 2 hour before turning into a skin scent. It does however lasts a few days on my clothes. (Depends on skin types) Overall Rating (8,5/10) I don't hate nor like this fragrance, it's not something I would wear as oud/woody fragrances isn't a combination I enjoy smelling. But if you're a fan of Oud/Woody notes, and you're a fan of Kenzo, then this might be the perfect combination for you.

Recently, I was with colleagues at an open-air bar high up with a view over Stuttgart. Suddenly, an incredibly good expensive scent wafted into our noses, and we looked at each other simultaneously and knew we had to track it down. But how, crowded with people yet always following our noses. Just recently, two young Arab-looking men dressed tastefully and expensively in cream and white (I know, side note :-D) walked past us. We caught a whiff of iris root, powdery violet, an expensive white wood accord, and something with a milky touch, although I initially didn’t recognize the aquatic note. It smelled really elegant, expensive, and good. I immediately thought of Roja, Xerjoff, or Boadicea, and I knew it, but couldn’t place it. My colleague asked the two, and one of them mentioned it, and then it came back to me, Kenzo the blue one with the quirky cap. One of my first fragrances back then, but it has since been reformulated and there are countless flankers. At Douglas, there was only the Intense, EdP, and EdT. Yes, all nice but the final touch was missing - but finally, I found it in him, Santal - this wood-violet-milk note. Men, definitely try it or even the unisex women :-)

Once again something new from the Kenzo Homme line, where perfumer Quentin Bisch develops these fragrances. A truly great line, in which the original DNA of the classic Kenzo Homme Eau de Toilette has already been significantly altered. The Kenzo Homme Eau de Toilette Intense & the Kenzo Homme (2022) Eau de Parfum are quite popular and clearly carry this special DNA as well as the unmistakable signature of Quentin Bisch. The similarity to this Santal Marin, which was released last year, is also unmistakable. I believe this flanker is just a limited edition, but that's the case with most flankers, especially those that don't sell particularly well. This flanker hasn't really gained fame, as evidenced by the mere 27 reviews here. For me, it can definitely hold its own against the two mentioned above, especially since this DNA is quite similar. The chance of liking this one if you enjoy the other two fragrances is quite high. However, one must admit: If you already have fragrances from this line, this Santal Marin is not a must-have due to its similarity. This Santal Marin, however, takes a wonderfully softer and gentler direction. It's already a great release that you can get for just over €60 for 110ml. The bottles in this line are uniform. At least the new edition of Kenzo Homme, which is by Quentin Bisch. All have this bamboo bottle, which fits well in the hand and leaves a good impression overall. As for the scent, as mentioned, there is a very strong similarity to the EdT Intense and also to the EdP. Due to the abundant sandalwood, it gives off a very nice cozy & slightly creamy vibe that lays very gently on the skin. Even though the EdT Intense also has a sandalwood note, one can say that this one is significantly stronger and also a bit creamier. The fact that only four notes are listed here is, of course, incorrect. The fig wood note from the predecessor is, I believe, also present here. Additionally, there are those slightly synthetic wood notes that Mr. Bisch likes to use. Together with this pleasant aquatic note, it has a light driftwood vibe. Moreover, this scent is also a bit darker & more mysterious and possesses this enigmatic aura. A bit of pleasant lavender also spreads out and fits well with this aquatic-wood combo. Overall, this is really nice and soft and pleasant to wear, especially in everyday life. This spicy-woody base with subtly smoky nuances also convinces me completely. Furthermore, this scent is quite linear and, like the others in this line, has no drastic developments between the opening and the drydown. It's a really great distinctive scent that is absolutely something for sandalwood fans. Performance is, like all the others in this line, top-notch for fresh scents of this kind. The scent is still perceptible close to the skin even after 12 hours. However, it has a real sillage for about 8 hours, with the first 3-4 hours being really good. Perfect for everyday wear, also in terms of performance. Overall, a great flanker that possesses really beautiful soft sandalwood. If the EdT Intense was a bit too harsh for you, this offers a somewhat softer but also darker version. Thumbs up, and I am already looking forward to the new "Kenzo Homme Indigo | Kenzo," which I will certainly test as well.

Men's fragrances from Kenzo have generally been only so-so for me. However, it was new to me that one could fail so miserably in my surroundings and at work. Unfortunately, this happened with "Kenzo Homme Santal Marin | Kenzo." My female colleague even found it quite terrible... The longevity was decent at around 8 hours, and the sillage still elicited rather negative compliments after hours. The top note starts off very fresh, maritime, but also peppery. The heart note offers an aromatic profile that I find very difficult to interpret... and this bothers me a lot! It could be something akin to curdled milk. Even after hours, this scent annoys me. Floral hints of lavender also emerge. The base is quite woody and slightly smoky thanks to guaiac wood. In the background, I can still detect a sweet and somewhat vanillic aroma. I really am not a fan of reviewing a fragrance negatively, as I truly appreciate the diversity of perfumes. But Kenzo Homme Santal Marin has definitely failed for me. Nevertheless, I thank Sam for the sample.

I am all about the sandalwood here. I used to wear Kenzo pour Homme Eau de Toilette a lot during my teenage years and later in my 20s. As my love for fragrances was reignited here through Parfumo (not to say it has somewhat escalated), I tested Kenzo Homme (2022) Eau de Parfum through a manufacturer sample, but I wasn't impressed. Something bothered me. I only sniffed Kenzo Homme Eau de Toilette once in retail; a test is still pending. Recently, I got to know an incredibly good sandalwood that I can now call my own, and this one was mentioned in a forum post. That caught my attention. First of all: The sandalwood in this Kenzo Man is very synthetic. But at this price, you can't expect anything else. In contrast to Kenzo pour Homme Eau de Toilette and possibly also "Kenzo Homme (Eau de Toilette) | Kenzo," this flanker is rounder and softer. The sandalwood is detectable, even if, as mentioned, it is synthetic. I can't smell the lavender. The maritime notes provide a balsamic-salty component that truly creates a feeling as if you are by the sea. And anyone who has been to the sea without being on a dreamy sandy beach knows that the scent can have something challenging about it. Salty notes evoke an association with sweat. And here begins my problem with this fragrance. The sillage is incredibly strong, and I like it. However, I sometimes get sweat notes, especially when I smell directly at the spray point. I am a bit torn and don't know if I like the scent or if it will soon become annoying. In any case, I think the sillage might perform better outdoors than indoors. I need to think about it and test whether Kenzo Homme Eau de Toilette satisfies the Kenzo cravings better, so that one could forgo the synthetic sandalwood here and instead continue to satisfy the sandalwood cravings elsewhere. Two sprays are definitely enough; the sillage is enormous. In any case, it is a special scent. The Kenzo DNA is immediately present, but it is muted and deeper. The matte lower half enhances the bottle compared to its brothers. Both the cap and the spray head give a cheap impression, but this can be justified by the price set by Kenzo. An interesting scent in its own way, which really lasts forever and has quite a loud sillage. I think it's good, but whether it is worth a bottle or even love, I don't know yet. It needs to mature between us.

I must confess - I’m not really into all the new Bleus, Bleu Noirs, and Sauvages. To me, these men’s fragrances all smell very synthetic and one-dimensional. Call me old-fashioned, but if this is what modern perfumery is supposed to be, I’m out. But wait! What do we have here?

Clean and fresh with a cooling green effect. Smells very traditional without smelling old fashioned in any way, and also very natural. It’s quite an uplifting fragrance and the performance is surprisingly good. The sprayer is great, producing a nice light cloud of fragrance, to fit with the idea of natural light “eaux” fragrances. This is the most masculine of the Les Eaux line that I have tried, and definitely my favorite of the bunch.

When I was a child, it was somewhat common to lay out branches of juniper or spruce at the entrance of your house around Christmas. When you arrived as a guest and stepped on this festive season's door mat, it releases the snow from underneath your shoes while at the same time the branches would release a strong conifer scent of essential oils – a scent that reigned supreme in a botanical world that was otherwise in its deepest winter sleep. In a child's mind, that scent also initiated and released all the suspense and joy over arriving at a Christmas party, at the homes of relatives you did not see much for the rest of the year. The house itself would smell fresh of pine needles and lavender, since everyone used a special, natural soap for the kind of wooden floors that are common in my country. Little surprise for me personally, then, living through a few fairly cold and dark weeks every year, that Paris-Édimbourg quickly became my favourite winter fragrance. It has very well blended notes that I find immensely bright and refreshing – in a dark winter it is the perfect uplifting scent for outdoor activities that brightens your day every time. The sun's winter solstice has passed, and all your biological, unconscious focus is on the fact that every day brings a little more light and spring is a little bit closer in time. Although Paris-Édimbourg is not a signature scent for me, it is the perfect companion for those days.

Paris-Edimbourg opens up with a very bright and fresh greenish profile. There does seem to be a bit of citrus up top, that may just be unlisted. However, the fragrance does have that sort of quality to it. Along with that, juniper and cypress are very present early on. It has a gin-like quality, effervescence, but much woodier than the drink itself. This gives off strong forest vibes, a bit rainy, but the air is clean and crisp. The lavender note softens and lends to the fairly masculine sort of soapiness that Edimbourg has. Still, this is a unisex scent that leans masculine, unlike the others in the Les Eaux de Chanel series. As it moves along, the cypress tones down to my nose, and I get more of the vetiver and some cedar. The whole perfume feels cold and attractive with a classical style. Also, the greenish aroma diminishes as it dries down. Lavender will become more dominant, with the remaining woodsiness, and a touch of vanilla sweetness/creaminess. Not too much vanilla, but it does make an appearance. Towards the end, it is a musky lavender and woods scent.

To me, this smells like cypress needles and Murphy's Oil Soap. This is not a criticism, as I like those two smells, but it may be a little sharp for all occasions. I see myself wearing this outdoors on crisp days more than to the office. It's maybe a little pointy for the office. But I do enjoy it. If you don't like the smell of Murphy's Oil Soap, don't even consider this one.

is the title of a semi-documentary film about the life's work of the artist Anselm Kiefer, who allows the reclamation of an anthropogenically shaped or deformed landscape by natural vegetation to take place on an abandoned industrial site in southern France. He gives this - depending on one’s perspective a utopia or perhaps a dystopia - or maybe more neutrally a 'vision' space and contour, as to how the age of humans may one day end silently - and nature literally lets the memory of it sink beneath the grass. Recently, I stood in front of a house in a large city in the south - one of those multi-story apartment buildings along the avenues established in the second half of the last century, as there are many in the cities along the Mediterranean. I stopped because the house seemed to be taken over by plants across the width of just one apartment - oleanders, climbing plants, and rubber trees that were growing between the window grilles and over the balconies - still tamed, but not for long, already a meter over the railing. And for a moment, I could almost see, smell, feel how the plants would one day claim this entire house from that balcony - slowly, gently, but inexorably. After this balcony and this house, after this moment, the scent of Chanel's Paris - Édimbourg lingers. I know, of course, that Paris - Édimbourg aims to thematize and reference the vegetation of Scotland. And had that encounter with the rampant plants in the midst of this otherwise very sober house not suddenly come to mind while sniffing - I might also sense this motif in its gray-green. But instead, I find that one moment again - scents are indeed capable of unexpectedly unearthing what has been buried deep in memory - a stone house sinking beneath soft green. Here is a gentle scent, gray-green and still, of solid nature - serious like a promise, but not serious enough to seem threatening. Here is the scent of sap, as it wells from the wound of an injured plant, which, however, will not succumb to this injury. Alongside juniper and conifers, I am almost certain to discover ivy, though that may be misleading. Hesperidic notes and the roughness of vetiver are almost entirely absent for me. Instead, only the quiet relentlessness of green grass, growing silently towards a nameless eternity. Conclusion: the quiet, powerfully delicate gray-green scent of grass overtaking stones. Far beyond Scotland and Paris.

I really wanted to test this fragrance, and the lovely Turandot generously sent me a sample, thank you once again for that. The description above, defined as green-fresh, only vaguely captures it, although it will likely appeal more to those who prefer this scent direction.

A truly great scent that shines in summer. It may sound strange because forest and juniper are more associated with winter, but the fragrance is wonderfully light and is a real alternative to the eternal citrus and aquatic scents in summer. It cools, grounds, and in an unknown way makes for a fragrant home. In winter, it’s not enough for me and feels far too airy.

Knowledgeable people with good taste in music will of course immediately recognize my headline as a lyric from ABBA's new masterpiece "Don’t shut me down," which has been accompanying me since September 2, 2021. "Now and then combined" also fits the current offshoot from Chanel's "Les Eaux" line.

I confess: I mainly know Scotland from television reports, not only about the British Royals, and from the filmed novels of Rosamunde Pilcher. They allow me to get to know a landscape that wouldn’t do me any good in reality: I am somehow very Mediterranean in my rhythm and therefore not suited for this interesting yet somewhat rustic, rough beauty.

And so it is with this fragrance. Two years ago I thought, finally a Chanel scent that is different. Green, light, close to nature, refreshing, fresh herbs. And so I was in love and full of anticipation for summer and vacations, adventures, unwinding, experiences, impressions. And a travel fragrance is perfectly made for that.

A successful birth from the pairing of Opium Vapeurs de Parfum and Flower by Kenzo Eau de Lumière . The Vie is immediately comparable to Opium upon first spray. It is somewhat more subtle in the sillage, and unfortunately, the longevity is a bit shorter than that of Opium. In terms of notes, I find it has slightly less powder than Opium. While Opium has a powder/paper note, the Vie becomes marginally sweeter. Lumiere also clearly comes through here, along with a hint of the original Flower Flower by Kenzo Eau de Parfum . However, it remains very restrained. But for those who, like me, know the scent inside and out, it can be detected! Alberto Morillas is certainly responsible for this DNA, as he also created the classic. One could say that Opium, likely due to the pepper and benzoin, takes on the role of the adult, more serious father figure, whereas the Lumiere mother, with pear, jasmine, and honey, has passed on the warmer, more vibrant, playful genes. Since I have loved both Opium and Lumiere and still do, I was delighted to have found this treasure. Two favorite scents combined into one, yet somehow entirely new. But as it often goes with all the variations: this one is also becoming hard to find and will soon likely be swallowed up by the market and disappear. What remains are magical moments with every spray and every breeze that wafts the delightful scent into your nose. *swoon*

Really, I read some reviews of others that were cracking down this fragrance. Either they are Chanel haters or don’t value the quality of this scent. Chanel Superleggera shouldn’t be a limited version. It should be named Allure Homme Sport eau de Parfum, since Eau Extreme isn’t a Parfum. With 6 sprays I smell this the next day. It’s between the Allure Homme Sport and Eau Extreme in a very smooth solid way. I love it and happy that I purchased it.

Fragrance Notes Top Notes: Citrus, Mandarin, Grapefruit. Mid Notes: Woody Notes, Cedarwood. Base Notes: White Musk, Patchouli, Amber, Sandalwood. Fragrance Review First thoughts, this is an aromatic/citrus fragrance for men, similar to Allure Homme Sport. - Superleggera starts off very citrus, similar DNA to Allure Homme Sport with a subtle hint of Lavender and Aldehyde notes. Creating a lighter/airy version of Allure Homme Sport. The mid and drydown consists of Musk, and warm spicy patchouli note. - I sprayed a total of 5 times. Twice behind each ear, twice on the front of neck, and once in front of my chest. The longevity is good, it lasts approximately 7-9 hours on my skin, projects for about an arms length for 30 minutes to 45 minutes before turning into a skin scent. It does however lasts a few days on my clothes. (Depends on skin types) Overall Rating (8/10) An ideal fragrance for the summer/warm weather, it's a safe blind buy if you enjoyed the original Allure Homme Sport DNA. Quite an interesting, lighter version with a nice touch of amber warmth in the drydown. This 100ml/3.3 FL oz bottle was purchased for £130/$160.

Hello everyone, you can rely on the company..., perhaps we have a little upcoming star here. Yesterday, on Sunday, I received a sample from "a fragrance buddy" and tested it today + yesterday (at work, while sleeping, and in my free time) and would like to give you (m)e my little impression. It contains so much from the Chanel palette and yet so little... What do I mean by that exactly? You can clearly tell where it comes from, in the sense of Allure Homme Sport Eau de Toilette with its zesty, fresh, light notes and the Allure Homme Édition Blanche Eau de Parfum and a truly beautiful lemon (one of the most beautiful top notes I know), and on the side, you also notice the Bleu de Chanel Eau de Toilette , but not purely from the scent, rather from the massive PLEASANTNESS! Chanel has never positively shocked us with pure performance, but rather it has always been the pleasantness and the certain quality at that price level, and it is the same here! The scent resembles the bottle - transparent, soft, doesn’t clash, and so it is! A fresh and pleasant musk bomb! In the end, during the drydown, a light and subtle woody creaminess comes through, but it acts so subtly that you almost have to search for it. Overall, it is sooo beautiful, pleasant, clean = you feel like you just took a shower! How does it come across? Typical for Chanel = incredibly good! Where and when? Almost everywhere, whether at work, while shopping, during sports and afterwards, or just like that ;) . I see it more in the months from March to October! In winter, it works very well too, and YES it harmonizes very well with Molecule 01 , then it probably has enough power for winter. Performance: Completely okay and sufficient for a 7h or 8h workday, and it achieves that, but you can notice after 6h it gets a bit tight^^ in terms of skin scent.
