Ahh, Euphoria... Why must you confuse me so much? It's really difficult to make up my mind about this perfume. One day I love it and the next I'm grossed out by it and I want to trash it. I've figured out that it's partly because of how I choose my fragrance for the day.

First spray drew an immediate reaction of revulsion. Extremely strong, sickly sweet, and medicinal (like cough syrup, not herbs). It’s a really powerful scent, luckily it calmed down in the first 30 minutes so it was not a scrubber. It still smelled really strong, but the scent was more pleasant.

Yes, yes and more yes. Ahhhh….absolutely delicious. Heaven, pure heaven. The next morning a hint of this perfume still remains. How fabulous is that? The initial blast of honeyed milk served in a coconut shell with spices on top is extreme and brings its’ wearer to heights of delicious anticipation. Images of sitting in a tropical palm-covered hut-I can hear seagulls screeching overhead and the sun is delectably warm. The sea is crashing behind me, the sky is blue overhead with minimal clouds on the horizon. And the barkeep? Let’s just say that’s my fantasy…and Sensuous Nude takes you there. This perfume delivers a sweet musk brilliantly tempered by amber sitting in a coconut shell. If golden bronze had a color, this would be it. Lauder chose the color for the bottle correctly. Close your eyes when you spray, because that’s what you see. It can be minus 6 degrees outside with gusty winds, snow blowing around the corners of the house when I spray this perfume and my mind will still create images of that beautiful beach. It still takes me there to blue skies, warm sands under my toes and the ocean waves not far away. It’s that delicious. A nuance of top peppery notes add just the right amount of spiciness to this brew without overloading it. Bergamot adds the freshness, zing and pop in the initial blast that gives Sensuous Nude its exciting wow factor in the beginning that calms down with the honeyed milk. The sandalwood comes across more as a dried hay or dried palms, similar to the tops of little beach huts. This perfume radiates very well and lasts for hours upon hours.

This is yet another winner in terms of Sensuous flankers. Sensuous Nude is a deliciously honeyed and musky skin-scent, that surprisingly works well for most occasions and seasons. The woods are of course front row centre in this fragrance, just like the original Sensuous, however they are much less pronounced. This is a delicate fragrance, on the verge of creamy sweetness yet nicely balanced. Honey was the first note I detected in this composition, as it provided an interesting sugary accord which further complimented the musky woods and subtle citrus notes in the opening. Vanilla and coconut, while not dominant ingredients in this blend, introduce themselves during the heart of this composition in a creamy and feminine way. I find the overall feeling quite soothing and inoffensive. It's a touch powdery towards the drydown, which for me, adds to its appeal. I find its lightness refreshing and pleasing on my skin. While the scent does last considerably well, the muskiness does tend to make this fragrance settle so naturally on the skin that sometimes it is hard to detect. Sensuous Nude is nothing out of the ordinary, but for what it's worth I am highly impressed. It's actually just that little bit sexy in the way that it envelops you in a cloud of comfortable warmth and softness.

"Nude" in the sense of unobtrusive, not in the sense of "erotic". A fairly pleasant, woody-musky, very honeyed affaire, which is far too sweet for my taste. On the other hand, a discreet fragrance for women who want a warm, slightly powdery scent which does not overpower or dominate. Estee Lauder does "low-key", but not in an interesting way.

I really don't care for the top, which is a bit heavy on the LOV & jasmine for my taste. But that quickly passes and the drydown is lovely - not too floral, just a bit sweet. It's summery amber woods. Overall, Sensuous Nude is a skin scent with just a bit of presence, like warmed summer skin. It's a very comfortable fragrance and would make a nice office-friendly alternative. Also, it's highly wearable in summer. I have sampled the edp, and I own the lotion ("body veil"). The lotion has a bit more presence than the edp to me, and I clearly detect pepper in the lotion, which is barely there in the edp. Highly recommend sampling this one! I own Sensuous & Sensuous Noir. Although Sensuous Nude is a bit subdued for my style, I could be persuaded to pick the edp at the right price.

Tuesday morning, start of work, I smelled of Sensuous Nude. An annoying noise hits me as I open the group door. Caused by a huge monstrosity of a sharpener, electric, aging, running continuously. My dear colleague has taken on the worn-out colored pencils and is sharpening them in bulk. The whole room smells of freshly sharpened colored pencil shavings, woody, peppery, sweet. We can only communicate by shouting as the first children greet me: "Look, I've already put on lotion!" I know, and now I do too, everywhere those small, quick little hands could reach me. Greasy prints on jeans and a white blouse, the scent of coconut and vanilla from the sunscreen tube, and something dry and dusty, aha, the sweet little ones have already been outside and decorated every free pavement stone with their artworks in the sunshine. The door is open, the clover is blooming, and it enticingly attracts the bees with its scent. There was no time left for handwashing, little Lena is now stubbornly trying to wipe the pink-purple handprints off my thighs. In vain, what remains is a smeared, dirty layer of paint. As a consolation, she gives me a self-painted picture, it has turned out particularly beautiful, with the freshly sharpened pencils: "That's me, and that's you, and we're both laughing because kindergarten is so great!" she says, smiling at me hopefully. How right she is. Nowhere would I rather earn my living. Even my perfume smells like it: Woody, softly sweet, powdery, familiar and yet never boring.
Naaaaaaaaaackt! Argh, so much for self-control… but what can I do if a fragrance, a women's fragrance, is called “Sensually Naked”?

Today there was excitement with a police presence at the flea market, as some fragrance stalls had been "taken down". I was feeling anxious because I wanted to pay a visit to my long-time fragrance dealer there. Surely he hadn't fallen victim to the raid? I was feeling uneasy. But I found him, as secure as the watch on the Rhine - at his usual spot.

The regular Sensuous is one of my great favorites because it resembles my deeply revered fragrance "Chaos" by Donna Karan (unfortunately d/c). Not as long-lasting and a bit softer, but still: related. So I gladly try the Nude version. To be honest: the similarity to the regular Sensuous is rudimentary.

I admit it, I love to hold these ribbed bottles from Estée Lauder in my hands. The fact that this one has a beautiful old rose color was of course an additional bonus point for testing it. The day before, the editor-in-chief had typed her fingers on a hymn of praise for SN in a magazine. I was deeply impressed. It is supposed to be sexy, like a second skin, extraordinary.

First of all, I love this scent. First, this bottle in my hand. What a delight to hold, these fine grooves, these curves. If the cap were integrated, it would already be a dream for the hands without even opening it. But of course, it also has content, and it packs a punch. Cap off and just sniffing it, a wonderful woody sweetness flows out.

The slightly dull scent of freshly cooked rice, especially in Asian restaurants, not only makes my mouth water in anticipation of upcoming culinary delights, but also feels cozy, grounding, and protective to me. The shower gel Lila Reis from Laos by Yves Rocher comes very close to this scent and evokes the same associations. As a perfect complement, I imagined the rice fragrance from KenzoKi. In fact, right after spraying, alongside a sharp alcoholic aldehyde note, there is a very subtle hint of cooked rice to be sensed. It would have been so nice if it were stronger, but it cannot assert itself and quickly gives way to a somewhat indifferent fabric softener-musk-floral quality that I can only perceive very close to the skin. Already half an hour after application, I can hardly smell the fragrance at all. Whether one can even speak of perfume under these circumstances is a matter of opinion. I see it more as a care scent, and some inexpensive standard creams are similarly subtle but significantly more enduring. In any case, I managed to completely empty my sample of Rice Steam within a few hours, and I sincerely thank the kind donor for this pleasant, but far too fleeting olfactory experience.

Dear community, I unfortunately have to vent some serious (rice) steam here! Today my package arrived, yes I admit, once again I made the mistake of ordering a fragrance 'blindly'. This time I was really, really sure that with a fragrance pyramid consisting of musk, woods, tonka bean, and rice, I had absolutely nothing to lose. I have also had good experiences with aldehydes so far.. Okay, I'll keep it short: The scent starts incredibly alcoholic, piercing, and sweet. So sweet, it's unbearable for me. Alongside it comes a synthetic note, I can explain this scent mix with the addition of aldehydes and 'floral notes'. While I think of a warm, cozy scent with woods, musk, and tonka bean, this one reminds me of cheap children's perfume, sickly sweet, artificial, and also not very original. Rice or rice steam? I can't smell anything of that. Since I read numerous fragrance descriptions from other forums before my blind purchase, I feel the urge to react to certain descriptions/keywords: "Clean scent, like freshly lotioned" - not at all! For me, the keyword "glue" fits best here; while one massages it in and hopes it absorbs, I just want to wash this off. "Doesn't last long, maximum an hour" - I sprayed this body spray at 6:10 PM, it is now 9:43 PM and I can still smell it on my wrist, although not as strongly as at the beginning. And because some (like me) might be tempted to compare Kenzoki Rice Steam and Kenzo Amour: Just forget it, the scents have nothing in common whatsoever, even if one might suspect that with the notes of rice, tonka, and musk. As for the caring effect, I can't say much since the scent test on my wrist already deterred me from applying it more broadly. My conclusion: I can't even say that the scent is simply 'bad'. What I complain about is that the name "Rice Steam" and the included rice note imply something different and therefore my expectations were not met. Where rice steam is written, there should also be rice steam inside - in my opinion. You can find much more rice in Kenzo Amour and Indian Holy, even in Lann Ael by Lostmarch, which supposedly only contains a grain note, I can smell rice in it. So if you're looking for rice, you'll definitely find it, but not here. At the current price of €46.00, it is definitely too expensive for a body spray, let alone an EdT/EdC. It's really a shame that I can't say more than to sincerely advise everyone not to order this scent blindly but to look for testers... To all who love it: I'm so sorry to have to say this now, I can't emphasize enough that this is just my personal feeling! Wishing you a reflective Christmas and a Happy New Year 2016!

A dear Parfumo member once sent me a sample of this fragrance. Otherwise, I would have never noticed this scent. It was available at a time when I was less interested in perfumes. I was all the more delighted to later find a half bottle online. The scent is wonderfully delicate. It is a perfumed, caring, and moisturizing body spray. The consistency is that of a perfume. It starts off aldehydic. But very softly, classically, and gently. Musk is also immediately recognizable. Delicate, soft flowers give it a feminine touch. However, I wouldn't describe KenzoKi Rice Steam as a directly floral scent. The flowers, possibly jasmine, accompany the musk very gently. Unfortunately, I can't detect the rice. It seems almost odorless to me. Rice extract has been added as a caring ingredient. The base of musk and tonka bean, which also comes across very delicately here, is later accompanied by slightly woody aromas. The fragrance is ideal for feeling well-groomed and feminine every day. Even in very hot temperatures, the scent remains very light and pleasant. In winter, the fragrance might be too weak, but when it's cold, I don't use body sprays. For the warmer season and for in-between, it is ideal. It is a pleasure to scent myself with KenzoKi Rice Steam after showering and wanting to relax a bit. The longevity is not bad at 5 hours for a body spray. Rice is a staple for the Japanese. It is never unpleasant and accompanies all dishes daily. Thus, the name is very well chosen for this fragrance.

This perfumed beneficial water spray is very subtle yet very interesting. Gentle sandy, ambery, soft notes. Very sensually creamy, Asian-inspired. In fact, the scent lightly resembles jasmine notes from the steam.

Still, today I have a remarkable memory of CK Be when it came out in the mid-’90s. It left a clean, flowery, dusty, soapy trail. Alas, it was the perfume that a colleague of mine wore, and that is why I never wanted to wear it to go to work those days. As a replacement, I enjoyed wearing Solo Soprani Blu Eau de Toilette , so similar in result. But CK Be remained my favorite for weekends, in the days of late spring and early summer, when temperatures alternate between the crisp morning air and the warmer afternoon air. I always thought it was more geared towards what would be a traditionally masculine fragrance, despite being sold as unisex. And one of my favorite light fragrances is olfactory poetry. Unfortunately, today it is not what I was used to, but it is still good. Very sensual. Great between the sheets. The more years go by, the lighter, more delicate, and less durable it becomes, which could detract from most audiences. Clearly weakened in the latest reformulation, low intensity, and ridiculous duration. As soon as they released it, I remember the wearer leaving a nice trail behind him. However, CK Be is today a distinctive yet delicate fragrance. I’ve got a hundred million reasons to walk away, but it is an affordable and easygoing classic that I keep coming back to. Woodier, greener, and sharper than its CK One Eau de Toilette predecessor, it’s also noticeably more masculine than unisex to my nose because of the aromatic and balsamic notes. Transparent white musk covers it, enriched with a spicy note of juniper and tonic accords of mint and mandarin. It’s citrusy, tangy, and spicy, but it’s not a zingy cologne. Totally different from CK One, the chords I hear the most, regardless of who wears them, are wood, grass, and something in between powdery and soapy. The good thing about CK Be in the 90s was that everyone knew if you were wearing CK One. However, no one knew if you were wearing CK Be because it was less popular than CK One. There is a smell of clean laundry, like something that makes you smell fresh, like you just got out of the shower. It has enough of a touch of spice from fresh notes like mint and balsamic to keep it interesting, with some depth, and its floral period relatively short. I also like that this is one of the few fresh scents that doesn’t immediately evoke the scents of seawater, water, or salt, such as those that smell blue. The opening is pleasant enough and doesn’t overwhelm you like some fragrances. It is a subtle and fresh blend of musk, lavender, peach, and suave citrus. A touch of sandalwood feels very familiar and clean, and the note of orange here is a very light touch. After a few minutes, the citrus fruits fade, and a more balsamic and green accord takes shape from grassy herbs and juniper berries. The notes mentioned so far combine with lighter fruit notes. Lavender seems more substantial to me, up top, but there is a friendly cleansing in the supporting ingredients. It has its own soap-like aroma at this stage but looks greener than it will later on; a youthful energy that reminds me of the late spring and early summer days. There is a hint of spearmint hidden among the moss, which lends a nice, albeit subtle, accent to the composition. As it progresses further, it takes on more of its floral character. To this unusual start, the perfumer added a hint of lavender in the heart that supports the scent of a bouquet of magnolia in full bloom and other white flowers. The smell of peaches peeps out from time to time and is a pleasant surprise. It has such a clean, powdery, and almost soapy quality when it settles on the skin and brings out the floral and woody notes that blend into it. The moss is clean, a kind of unctuous quality, with introducing the main freesia. On my skin, it looks like an immaculate white variety of musk reminiscent of jasmine, and lily of the valley: a freshly washed white floral scent with soft citrus notes that alternate directly between masculine and feminine. And finally comes the bottom, which is all about mossy sandalwood with a fruity soapy finish. It is sweeter and less green in the last part. A musky and woody finish with a warm, skin-like fruit touch creates the scent with a unique character. White musk elevates the overall aroma, along with the herbaceous and floral accords in the heart. The peaches appear to melt into the base, and instead of creating a fruity effect, it softens and add a freshness to the opoponax. It is more complex than it may seem but appropriate for any occasion. It is harmless if you work in social settings where people could be offended by strong perfumes. I find it perfect for daytime use, whether working in the office or hanging out with friends. However, it has longevity issues. For example, it will last about a few hours, half a day. I’m sure the reformulations have taken some of its stamina away from how it once was. As for projection, it’s not a bold scent, but it’s not completely weak either, at least at first. Seasonally, Be is a warm-weather fragrance for spring and summer. I like this very soft perfume; it doesn’t smell like classic cologne. There is a very casual feel to it. It also works well in hot, oppressive weather, which is a plus. I love using it on the hottest Italian summer days when I can’t stand most of my more aggressive scents and don’t want to smother anyone nearby. There is something incredibly relaxing and calm about this fragrance. It is comfortable and lights while maintaining a confident presence that is charming and ideal. I see Be becoming a comfortable perfume for me, something simple and appropriate to wear to the gym, when I don’t want to stand out, or maybe while relaxing at home. The quality suffices to perform the task in question simply to create a clean, freshly washed impression. Incredible how much you remind me of Solo Soprani Blu Eau de Toilette . Be is like a crisp, clean, and immaculate white ironed shirt in your wardrobe. It’s not the most exciting or original thing to have, but it makes me feel fresh, clean, and tidy, even when it’s stuffy outside. I base the review on a 200ml bottle I have owned since May 2018. -Elysium

There is something incredibly relaxing and calm about this fragrance. It is comfortable and light while maintaining a certain presence that is both charming and ideal. Unisex it certainly is. While the opening is rather masculine, and in some ways similar to Bvlgari Black, the drydown is quite floral and clean, but not at all feminine. CK Be is somewhere in between, something that would smell sexy on a man and pretty on a woman. CK Be is mysterious but certainly not dark. There's an element of cheerfulness behind this fragrance and it is quite refreshing. I sense a subtle rubbery note intermixed into the notes which gives this fragrance that little something. The rubber combined with smokey woods and sweet floral notes really makes this fragrance worthwhile. The lasting power is quite good and the price is fantastic for such a quality scent. I recommend for both sexes.

CK be was the first fragrance I purchased as an adult - as an 18 year old college student. Then I was attracted to its unisex marketing and ease of wear. 13 years later, and with all my experience, in life and in fragrance, this remains my signature scent. it brings me comfort, and I can wear it anywhere at any time. No one dislikes the smell of CK be, though everyone describes it differently. To the uninitiated, the top is a familiar citrus - bergamot. But also lavender? or mint? or is it rosemary? It's powdery at the top - soap. detergent. clean. nice enough. very nice, in fact. you'll chase this scent - it is gone within 60 seconds. The middle is also mysterious. Is that peach? A "white peach?" Raspberry? Maybe it's a fantasy fruit, made up in a lab, but it is juicy and delicious. There's grass. More mint. Spices. Iris? But everything is behind a veil of powdery soap. the scent now projects to only 1 inch from the skin, and will be there for only 45 minutes. But the basenotes are what make this truly special. Tonka? Sure. Opoponax and Sandalwood? If you say so. Pepper. And musk. Yep - definitely. Not a clean musk. A body musk. If the top-notes and heart-notes were soap, the base is dirty laundry. The smell of a clean but unwashed armpit. Today's white t-shirt with this morning's fragrance and today's accumulated dirt. Yesterday's underwear. There is no projection or sillage. This is a personal scent. Others will be able to smell if you spray about 10 times - and with juice this cheap, you can afford to bathe in the stuff. But I suggest you wear it for yourself.

I shopped at Burlington this weekend as part of my job with assisting people with developmental disabilities. I noticed the fragrance rack. Because of my growing interest in affordable fragrances, I purchased two caught my attention. Calvin Klein’s Be (CK Be) is the first of the two fragrances. Admittedly, it's a fragrance that comes with a mixture of positives aspects and notable critiques. ---- The best way to describe CK Be is “Fresh out the shower clean.” It doesn't take me back to the teen years of the 1990s when Calvin Klein was notably everywhere. However, it reminds me of a soap’s fragrance lingering in the air as I get a towel to dry myself after a shower. With top notes of mint and juniper, you will feel refreshed as the mid notes of spices and peach add warmth and depth. The base notes seem like myrrh and sandalwood, and they extend the freshness until the fragrance fades away. While some scents I reviewed to this point could be unisex, CK Be is the first fragrance that I can say is unisex without an obvious lean towards masculinity or femininity. ---- In terms of the bottle, I have mixed feelings. On the positive side, I love dark bottles; the fragrance withstands light, allowing the scent to stay fresher for a longer time. However, at least for the 100 ml, only the cap or atomizer goes on the bottle. Switching between the two makes air exposure more likely and reduces the lifespan of the scent. ---- The performance for CK Be is quite underwhelming, even for an eau de toilette. Sillage and projection are minimal. People who want to announce their presence or turn heads will frown in disappointment. However, one can appreciate smelling clean and fresh for themselves or for individuals within their proximity. However, longevity is a bigger concern. Fresh fragrances usually lack stamina, and CK Be lasted for four hours. Bringing the bottle or a travel spray is required if you want to wear the scent throughout the day. ---- CK Be is decent to use in active leisure, or as a daily fragrance, as the fresh scent is invigorating and energetic. That said, CK Be is not a noteworthy evening or date night fragrance. The scent vanishes before the night ends. For similar performance reasons, it fails as a scent during the winter or in a colder environment. Likewise, one should not expect compliments for smelling clean. It is reminiscent of taking care of one’s hygiene—that is expected out of everyone and is not extraordinary. There is another side to the coin. CK Be excels in the office because of the soft sillage. No one will find the scent offensive or overwhelming. Spritz in the afternoon for a quick refresh. In addition, CK Be is a rare fragrance I offer top recommendations for workouts. It will offend no one else during a workout, and you smell fresh throughout it, even if sweaty in multiple places. ---- CK Be is not terrible; one cannot underestimate having a clean and invigorating fragrance. However, the problem is CK Be can come across as ordinary and bland. In some ways, it makes the scent underrated. With that in mind, anyone seeking a unique fragrance for a date or an evening out, or a fragrance that stands out and garners attention from others, would waste money purchasing CK Be, even at an affordable price point. However, if someone is looking for an office-safe fragrance, the rare usable gym fragrance, or just wants to smell fresh and liven up for a moment, that person will get serious mileage out of CK Be.

A fragrance released in 1996 from the good old days that brings back memories of the past with nostalgia, even if you didn't live in that era. Suitable for all times and places, it is classified as unisex but leans more towards men's fragrances. A harmonious fragrance rich in ingredients, blended with great craftsmanship so that no one aromatic ingredient overpowers the other. The scent here is rich, creamy, fresh, fruity, herbal, woody, and smoky. A magic you won't find anywhere else. A simple and uncomplicated fragrance with many ingredients, you wish from the first moment that this scent would last with you forever. Never ask about the performance; the performance is somewhat average, but it is compensated by the magic and depth of the scent. pros: - Subtle and safe fragrance - Sophisticated drydown - Pleasant and reliable scent - Easy to wear and won't offend cons: - Poor longevity - Short-lasting fragrance - The bottle design is very primitive In my personal opinion, if fragrance liquid were put in a niche bottle, it would sell for many times its simple price. I don't usually buy fragrances twice, but there's an exception to every rule. CK BE is one of the fragrance I've bought several times, and every time I use it, I get compliments as if I'm actually using it for the first time.

This smelled great on a tester and continued to smell great on the tester. This smelled terrible on me and continues to smell terrible on me. I tend to like CK so I tried it fast, but found I couldn't get it off of me fast ENOUGH!Started as a pretty good balanced Floral/ Musk, Immediatly dried down to a woody/ musk and stayed there for the remainder of 3hrs.

I had both this and CK One Eau de Toilette in the 90's and I loved them. Ross had big bottles of CK Be for sale and I caved. I remembered liking it and I looked at the notes but I couldn't really recall it the way I can CK One. I bought it and figured if it was a dud, I could keep it for nostalgia reasons. I'm surprised by how much I still like it.

This scent is the scented transposition of the concept album "The dark side of the moon", a true masterpiece by Pink Floyd I love so much. Indeed, it's could be the dark side of....CK one. If the second one is light and bright, CK be is deeper and more spicy-aromatic. But let's start describing the bottle: minimal and totally black. It suggests something mysterious.

A new job, a new perfume, a new image ... What do you not need to survive? As I lie there in the darkness, I feel like the dark is endless. But when the alarm rings, I realize that it is not a dark hole inside me, but the dawn that unexpectedly promises a new day.

Transfiguration can be something beautiful. Were the summers as a child really sunnier? Were the Christmases really whiter? Was life really so much more carefree? I have thought about this for a long time. As a child of the 1990s, I firmly believe that we still had regular white Christmases back then. Photos from that time can prove it.

Nuage Cerisier is, for once, one of the gentle ones among the usually very cloying or sweet fragrances. It evokes a relaxed and peaceful walk under a cherry blossom tree. It radiates calm, gentleness, and grace. The scent is also not intrusive; yes, when you are close to the person, it lightly smells of cherry blossoms and freshness. But not aggressively biting, rather playful and lightly tickling. However, it lasts just as briefly as the cherry blossom season. After about 2 to 3 hours, it might need to be reapplied.

Ah. Nuage Cerisier by Kenzo is enchanting. It is sweet, fruity, playful, and envelops you in a fluffy musk cloud that reminds one of laundry detergent or fabric softener. Actually, this is not my scent, yet I find myself applying a drop of it almost every morning before I go for my morning run. And I have to think of you. If you were still here and we were running together regularly, I believe I would immediately gift you a bottle of this. This fragrance is so youthful, so radiant, so clean and fresh, bringing a pleasant lightness with it. A young woman spins around laughing in the sunshine of spring, flowers blooming everywhere, wearing clothes that smell of laundry detergent and fabric softener, blowing a bubble with her fruit-flavored gum, shining in competition with the sun. The scent makes me smile. Every time I sniff my wrist. Even if it may not quite fit me. This airy musk combined with bright and delicate flowers, so full of purity, simply smells beautiful. I do not see myself; I see you in front of me. How often they mistook us for mother and daughter. We had to grin every time. And today I miss you since you moved away. Yes, I am a bit in love with this almost childlike, flower-pure Kenzo. The top and heart notes are a dream. However, the base note does not convince me 100 percent. Here comes the fruity note, which for me does not resemble a naturally occurring mandarin, but rather one like in iced tea or fruit gum, coming through a bit too strong for me, and the floral aspect recedes into the background. Nevertheless, this beautiful scent from Kenzo's Memori line simply won't let me go. I will surely treat myself to a spritz from the sample here and there again. Maybe already tomorrow morning? And who knows? Maybe I will get so used to this delicate and fine scent, which gradually fades away after about 3-5 hours, that one day I will want to buy a bottle after all. I would like to sincerely thank Diana870411 for the sharing and the testing opportunity. A surprisingly beautiful new release. I often like Kenzo fragrances. This one is also typically Kenzo.

A modern classic that is smooth, sexy, sultry and sensual. It's all about exotic spices, incense, sandalwood, musk, oakmoss and in the distance, florals that surrendered their innocence to the sensual attack of this smooth mixture of sex in a bottle. Hours of passion carelessly wrapped up in black satin sheets...Or a walk through an autumnal forrest where bonfires are lit and are scented with natures spices. Earthy and primal....this Obsession continues to lead us astray in the most delightful way. Forget 'cute', 'floral' or 'sweet' this is a wicked scent -- a wicked scent that has always been, and always will be part of my collection for all those cozy or wicked moods ; ) Silage is: "come hither....I know you can't resist." -- Longevity is: 8+ hours and the drydown is just as yummy as the first and middle stage: smooth amber and vanilla kisses. x.x.x

Obsession, well what can I say, a true masterpiece is what you are. This fragrance is everything that you could ever want in an oriental. It's spicy, warm, incensey, sensual, beautiful, rich and utterly breath-taking. Unfortunately Obsession does tend to turn away a lot of people with its opening, which is indeed very heavy and thick, almost polluting the air. However, I cannot urge others enough to let this fragrance develop, because that's where the real magic lies. When the initial intensity subsides, Obsession transforms into an alluring and comforting spicy-sweet scent. Vanilla, incense, cedar, amber, jasmine, coriander and a variety of spices all blend together creating a delicious aroma that is almost good enough to eat. When tastefully applied (that is, sprayed sparingly), Obsession is somewhat mysterious and utterly gorgeous. Unfortunately many have been exposed to this fragrance when its wearer has overloaded themselves in this rather potent juice, therefore resulting in many people disliking this scent. I think it's a shame that a lot of people dismiss fragrances from the 80's simply because they find them dated or too strong. One thing that's for sure, they don't make scents like this anymore.

Obsession is a real blast, no doubt about that. Intensive, unmistakable, loud. And beautiful, too. On my skin it develops as a mixture of musk, spices, amber and musk that is vibrantly erotic. Did I mention musk? And spices? Obsession is obviously no current fragrance but a child of its time - and even then, back in the 80s it was a loud and unmistakable fragrance. And immensely popular. Insofar it is dated, more retro than classic and it can certainly feel fusty, regardless of its vibrant eroticity: It depends entirely of its wearer's bearing which way it turns out. Because Obsession is so immensely potent and projecting I strongly recommend to use it sparingly. It's supposed to be breathtaking, yes - but not suffocating in the way that requires an emergency doctor. This might sound negative but I don't mean it that way! Applied carefully and delicately on the right person it's a truly wonderful fragrance!

Today I wore CK Obsession for the first time in a long time, and I wore with an entirely new reference in mind - skank. So, with skank in mind, what does CK Obsession smell like? 70% Dana Tabu (vintage) 30% Femme Rochas I put Obsession on, and Tabu immediately came to mind. However, as it wears, I find that Obsession has the same in-your-skin quality that Femme does. I checked the notes, and the similarities are there - the peach, cinnamon & vanilla of Femme and the spices, amber & civet of Tabu. Obsession also has a bit of a powdery quality, which I adore but might turn off many. Overall, I think Obsession is a bit "mature" in the sense that I can't imagine many 20 year olds wanting to wear this - in the 1980s & 1990s, yes, but in the 2000s & 2010s, no way. I think Tabu and Femme are much easier to wear than Obsession, primarily because many of the CK fragrances have a white floral note that irritates me sometimes. Tabu and Femme also are smoother and closer wearing than Obsession. Although I like Obsession, my DH loves it on me. Yes, it's true - men love Obsession on women. But if truth be told, I prefer Tabu & Femme. Skank tested. Skank approved.

I really love this perfume and I don't know how blind I was not to have spotted this so long. It is a superb smell which lasts all day and if preferably wearable for winter. The incense along with spices makes it a total mysterious and rare perfume. My husband likes it too.

First whiff-adoration! No matter what others say, I will always love this perfume. I truly believe all the hype and commercialization has turned people off through the years and that is a true shame. It's a beautiful fragrance that should not be taken lightly. A warm, powdery, sweet scent with amber laden spices surrounding and tickling your nose.
Do you remember when you were a kid? The memories of childhood are like the cover of Linus; each of us holds the most beautiful close trying to make them unforgettable over time.

Sometimes when you spray a scent it evokes a scene in your mind. To me the scent of Obsession takes me to the lobby of the La Scala Opera in 1921. The floor is covered with plush oriental rugs and dim light radiates from the golden fixtures on the wall.

i got my first bottle of Obsession the year it premiered in 1985 in san francisco. my rich lesbian aunt, whom i had been visiting, brought me into Neiman-Marcus and bought it for me for my 13th birthday. i used to keep it in its original box and worshiped it as if it were a deity.

If one of the main accords is listed as balsamic, it is a pretty sure bet that I like it. And with Obsession it is LOVE. I always have a back up bottle, because I dread the day that I might not be able to get her anymore. Now, I usually wear her just at home and so far didn't dare to take her with me for a night out.

I have a feeling that when people ask over and over again for recommendations for a sweet, earthy, woody, vanillic oriental, PCAYY is exactly what many of them have in mind. They've just never encountered it because there is no tester on the perfume counter in Macys, it's a little pricey, and samples are hard to come by. I lucked into it because one of my early swap partners has taste very similar to mine and she was an expert at predicting which ones I would love. She sent me a half-full mini as an extra, and bless her heart for doing that, otherwise I'd never have discovered this rich and satisfying elixir. It checks all the boxes for me: woody, earthy, vanillic, sweet, long-lasting, excellent sillage. Each and every time I wear it, a couple of my co-workers take a deep sniff of the air around me and say something like, "mmmmm . . .you smell good." It's one of a handful of perfumes I could wear everyday if I had to, and one I would truly miss if it disappeared. Epilogue, Feb. 22, 2014: How on earth has it taken me three years to notice the rose note in this one??? A subtle, smooth, but very much there ROSE!!! Woo Hoo!

I was curious about the Estee Lauder Private Collection for quite some time, what with its thinly veiled insinuation that the other members of the EL line-up are somehow destined for hoi polloi. What could "private" really mean when these new fragrances were being sold just as freely at the EL website as all of the others by, I might add, a big-time corporate monster which encompasses more than a dozen other ostensibly independent lines as well (Clinique, Prescriptives, Origins, Donna Karan, Tom Ford, Aveda, Darphin, La Mer, etc...). Having finally gained access to samples of a couple of the EL PC (not-so p.c.) perfumes, I am happily in a position to say something about the compositions, rather than waxing vainly about globalization. AMBER YLANG YLANG opens with a veritable bomb of amber, already not the most subtle of notes, and here presented in a concentration sufficient to mask even the usually strong character of ylang ylang. As the amber begins to wear away slightly (which is strange, since usually amber figures in the basenotes, not the topnotes), the vanilla and sandalwood begin to assert themselves. The lightly sweet, floral-woody drydown of this composition is just beautiful. However, the brash amber opening is a bit much for me. I would say that the question here is not about sophistication but amber tolerance. Anyone who loves hard-hitting sledgehammer ambers will welcome the opening of AMBER YLANG YLANG. Others may wish to hold their breath for several minutes. Does this "private collection creation" live up to the hype? Well, the price is definitely not right. If this perfume is succeeding, it's only because there are enough people with enough money and insufficient olfactory sophistication to know better than that paying triple digits for a bottle guarantees superior perfumosity. I, for one, am unimpressed. -------------- November 2013 update: I just finished my large sample vial and have to say that I was overly harsh above. This smells pretty good in the drydown--provided that one is in the mood for labdanum amber... I do not find it overly sweet. I still think that it is a bit dense and sledgehammerish but somehow tonight it smells nice. I have increased my evaluation, as I would wear Amber Ylang Ylang, if I owned a bottle. However, I still dislike the absurd "private collection" concept. Humph

As soon as any perfume contains amber, I have to test it. There’s hardly an amber scent that I don’t like in some way. Whether it’s gnarly, round, dark, or cozy. I love amber in every form. In Amber Ylang, the amber comes across as cuddly. And extraordinarily cuddly at that. Amber and ylang cuddle up on a bed of amber and vanilla. I can hardly distinguish individual notes; everything blends together perfectly. I feel enveloped, almost hugged, safe and secure. It wears like a wonderfully soft cashmere sweater, fluffy, snug, and gentle. Nothing disturbs, nothing scratches, and everything harmonizes. My current favorite sofa-cuddle-enveloping scent. Even if it’s almost a bit too elegant for that. I just throw on my cotton leggings and thick knitted socks with the cashmere sweater, and then it’s all good :-) The sillage is very close to the body, and the longevity is good.

Winter has returned. Outside, despite the advanced week of March, there is snow several centimeters deep. Grumbling about this fact, I left my cozy little apartment today and trudged my way into the city. The cold and the snowflakes blew me directly into the Carschhaus, where a warm-hearted saleswoman recommended this fragrance to me - even warmer. She mentioned, among other things, that it is very cuddly. That got me. Since there were no wool blankets or pillows available, I became curious and benevolent. Cuddly - that’s what I wanted, and warm... And she wasn’t lying! I had slight reservations because of the amber, but when she mentioned a certain similarity to Cinnabar, I threw all doubts overboard. "Yes! Yes! Yes! Dear lady, douse me with the golden liquid! May my heart be pleasantly warmed!" I thought. She read my thoughts and gave me a fragrance sample, this clairvoyant of a perfume saleswoman. I generously doused myself and actually caught a Cinnabar-like top note. Fruity-spicy and slightly sweet. But then a hint of White Linen spread, as the scent slipped into the soapy, yet remained warm-spicy. Warm... that’s what mattered to me. And PCAYY did not disappoint. Amber didn’t take over and stayed in the background, radiating delightful warmth and cleanliness. But predominantly, I was surrounded by a considerable sillage of creamy, smoky, slightly oriental sweetness. A skillful olfactory interpretation of the theme "Greenhouse." Warm, fertile, grounded, secure, alive. When you come in from the cold, there is nothing better than this feeling. Outside the door, it can be whatever it wants - when using PCAYY, everything is good.

Very soft and cuddly, a lot of vanilla and amber, sweet but not “squeaky.” I like that it leans towards the gourmand direction, but not so much that you want to bite into it right away. In the development of the scent, not much happens for me; at first, it’s a bit stronger floral due to the ylang-ylang, but the fragrance on my skin just becomes warmer and deeper, the ylang note blends beautifully with vanilla, amber, and sandalwood into a harmonious whole. I don’t really perceive any other notes, which I find a bit unfortunate - perhaps a pinch more incense, which is listed here, could have brought in an extraordinary moment... The scent isn’t really complex, but it does radiate a certain depth, likely from the warm base notes. In my perception, it doesn’t have that kind of “sex appeal” that makes you feel all “giddy” (at least not me ;-), it’s just too relaxed for that. Overall, a calm, warm cuddly scent, without excitement but still with a certain sophistication - for me, it certainly doesn’t come across as cheap. The scent stays rather close to my body, the longevity is okay. With regular use, it might become a bit boring for me (therefore not necessarily a candidate for purchase), but on days when it’s really dreadful outside, it definitely invites cuddling and relaxing.

Amber Ylang Ylang starts fresh and spicy, Ylang only becomes noticeable for me later. A sensual, lush fragrance in the perfect blend of floral, spicy, and a few sweet hints. The rose-patchouli mixture harmonizes beautifully with the creamy vanilla and amber. An "adult" fragrance, elegant and noble. I wear it very often, and the longevity is quite good.

Dear Aerin, how disappointed I was! Your Grandma's scent has simply been discontinued! And I searched and searched, pulled all possible strings, hoped to find a large bottle somewhere, even called your house - by the way, with absolutely courteous service - and - no! It is no longer being produced :-((. My spontaneous reaction: This can't be true!!

This is the softest and most flattering amber scent I have ever smelled. It could be that ylang-ylang and vanilla are equal players here. All three fragrance notes stand out clearly and blend very harmoniously with each other, with none overshadowing the others. I do not detect rose, patchouli, or even incense here.

for the autumn, I thought to myself right away when I sniffed this perfume! The first impression does not deceive. Actually, I wanted to get to know Amber Ylang a long time ago, but there were other favorites that blocked my way to the scent, or there simply wasn't an opportunity to get it... and so I was lucky here at Parfumo, the fragrance has now moved in with me....

I usually tend to be reserved when it comes to amber, but this scent enchanted me immediately. The amber is not too overpowering, and the ylang-ylang is not too sweet; together they create a "radiant" composition - at least that's how I feel about it. A warm, cozy, elegant fragrance that enhances a lovely evening even more.

Okay, I will be first. I am a fruity floral lover, and this is heaven. Light, blossom sweet, nutty, very powdery, gorgeous. Unusual in that it is powdery from the moment it is sprayed, rather than developing into powdery. Medium projection and lasts a good 6 hours on me. It's fast become a favourite. Dead ringer for Lancome's Tresor Midnight Rose except that Tresor Midnight Rose for an hour or so in the drydown veers into a deeper jellybean, jammy rose-nectarine, whereas this stays a little bit lighter, more blossomy and more powdery. Doesn't have much development, just fades sweetly away.

The fragrance notes of almond and plum blossom mentioned above are certainly not the entire formulation, as Fleur De Prunier has a very complex scent and undergoes an interesting development. The top note initially presents itself as quite harmless, green-floral-fresh. However, after a few minutes, it develops into a rather heavy, floral scent that is intense and distinctly floral - fruits, ginger, pink pepper, and whatever else is popular as an addition are all missing (no, they are not missing, they are just not there). The scent remains heavy and complex in a floral way. I don’t know what plum blossom smells like; I would have guessed a mix of strong floral notes - lilac, ylang-ylang, jasmine, perhaps even tuberose; all topped off with aldehydes. A tiny bit of elusive fruitiness and sweetness is also present, but extremely sparingly dosed. It stands out significantly from the floral-fruity-sweet mush that most mainstream fragrances currently offer. Fleur de Prunier smells old-fashioned, reminding me of the heavy, aldehydic floral scents of the old Guerlain floral fragrances Nahema and Chamade. Chamade was released in the 60s, Nahema in the 70s. Perhaps the floral-fruity-sweet era is coming to an end, and Fleur de Prunier is not outdated, but rather innovative. Edit: I had it on my watchlist and have tested it again. Perhaps it’s because I had little experience with so-called niche fragrances in July, while I have since become acquainted with several niche waters. In any case: today I notice an extremely artificial/synthetic note in Eau de Fleur de Prunier/Plum that didn’t bother me in July, and which I now categorize as somewhat typical for mainstream and designer fragrances. It is a rather intrusive, artificially sounding floral note, perhaps what Apicius always refers to as "scratchy." Maybe that is intended, but I don’t like it; in any case, I am no longer considering getting it, and I’m removing it from my watchlist :-)) Niche ahead, another goal!!!

This is possibly one of Estee Lauder's best fragrances. I can see why this is such a popular choice for a bride on her wedding day, and unlike most Estee Lauder fragrances, the synthetic notes in this are not as strong. Mature? Yes, it most definitely requires some maturity, sophistication and class to pull this one off. Old lady scent? Certainly not. Although this may smell like your typical 80's floral, there is something about it that never fails in gaining attention and compliments, especially from men. This is a soft and romantic fragrance with fantastic lasting strength. One spray goes a very long way in regards to wearing this.

My perspective on Estée Lauder BEAUTIFUL has always been summed up by a slogan: "BEAUTIFUL is not beautiful," which for years served as a mnemonic device that steered me clear of this fragrance at every turn. Until retesting this creation for the purpose of this review, I never used the purse spray in my collection, and now I remember why. It's not that BEAUTIFUL is another big bodacious venus flytrap floral typical of this era. It's not that BEAUTIFUL smells "old" or outdated to me. It's not that I have any objection, in principle, to wearing a bouquet comprising every flower on the planet. No, the reason why BEAUTIFUL is not beautiful to me is only because it includes a synthetic note which to me is the olfactory equivalent of the sight of canned spinach. It just makes me sick. The same note is present in both PLEASURES and INTUITION. In PLEASURES, it is so light that I can tolerate the scent to some extent. In INTUITION, the same note is so strong that it sent me screaming back to the EL counter for an exchange, as the very thought of ever wearing that fragrance again filled me with nausea and, yes, dread. I am relieved that most perfumes do not contain this mystery note. I had thought that it was only in some of the Estée Lauder creations, but I recently discovered it in a few others as well... The good news is that understanding the effect that this note has on me helps me to understand people who recoil at the whiff of their own idiosyncratic bête noire. It also serves to explain the strong, polarized reactions that people often have to perfumes with a powerful identity. So, if you can take this note, you may love BEAUTIFUL. And that's just fine with me!

On a recent day of sniffing some department store staples that I’d never tried, I happened on EL’s Beautiful. I’d never read Tania Sanchez’s review in The Guide , so I laughed out loud once I did. On smelling Beautiful I thought, this is Etat Libre’s Jasmin et Cigarette’s long-lost aunt, Rose et Cigar. I grew up in a time and place in Connecticut where shade-grown tobacco could be smelled throughout the summer. In Beautiful’s topnotes, I can recall that scent, but in this case the tobacco combines with rose. It’s a gorgeous match, but unfortunately it doesn’t last very long. The tobacco note fades fairly quickly and Beautiful winds down through a few stages of rosy-approximation/not-rose to a semi-sweet, non-descript floral. I reckon any drydown is likely to disappoint me after my topnote trip down memory lane, but I still give Beautiful a glass-half-full thumbs up.

The ultimate wedding fragrance. The unification of Man and Woman the notes unifies each others for example the Woman; Black current Fruity notes cassia Galbanum Bergamount lemon mimose magnolia Carnation Tuberose Orange blossom chomormile narcissus Fresia Lilac jasmine pink violet sage Neroli marigold Ylang Ylang Lily of the vally Geranium & Narcissus The Man; Sandalwood Musk Vanilla Vetiver & Ceder it blends wonderfully together Like the wedding vows i give it a 5

The good memories that this scent brings to me. How much I loved and I love this perfume. This is one of those fragrances that only looks good in some women, with an unique, special, beautiful character. I miss the 80s, I miss you special one.

I absolutely love it when a perfumer just create a whirlpool of scent, so many notes blended together that you can't pick it apart but because of that it has become something else, something new, something that does not quite correlate to the nature and that makes it otherworldly and that makes it beautiful

I first met this wonderful scent i 1991. A friend of mine had been to the local drugstore and she showed me her purchase which had been on sale: Beautiful edt… I loved it! This is a very unique fragrance that develops through the many hours it lasts on my skin.

Beautiful was all that one would expect from Estee Lauder in 1986. It was a large floral that can only be described as "beautiful". It was a powerhouse signature in every sense. Projection was far and wide, yet those around you totally appreciated it, unlike, Poison. The tuberose was tame, totally embellished with a very green and pink bouquet that develops for hours.
I spend my days among relatively formally dressed people. The gentlemen wear suits and the ladies either wear suits or costumes, with the 'Business' dress code allowing women a bit more leeway.

.... to me! Schmetter! Only very few fragrances from the floral category adorn my collection. I'm not really the floral scent type. But Beautiful is one of them, and it probably always will be! Thank you, Fiona, for the scent reminder, and at least I managed to get a mini of the pure perfume, which was quite a feat. Beautiful is a fragrance for dreaming.

It has been a while since I first reviewed Calvin Klein Beauty, which struck me as a good addition to that house's collection. I always liked how the house of Calvin Klein was groundbreaking in its creation of a cluster of very distinctive and completely unforgettable perfumes: Eternity, Obsession, Truth, Contradiction, and Escape. Whether one likes those perfumes or not, it cannot be denied that they have integrity, and each carved out its own spot on the grand olfactory map. Beauty fits right into this series, not only for its name--another abstract noun--but also for its clarity and univocity. This perfume falls somewhere between Eternity and Truth in concept and structure, but it is still unique. Like Truth, Beauty has a lucid quality and is a relatively simple composition. Like Eternity, Beauty is unabashedly feminine and floral, in this case, with jasmine as the dominant note and ambrette and cedar offering support. There is definitely a synthetic quality to this perfume, but that has always been a part of the modern Calvin Klein aesthetic, and it contributes in that way to Beauty as well. I hasten to add, however, that this is nothing like the Calvin Klein jug perfumes (One, Be, etc.), which I myself never took to. Those were always so flagrantly synthetic that my brief encounters with them were infelicitous. Beauty in contrast, toes the line between limpid florality and modern synthetics. Overapplied, there is real headache potential here. But lightly applied, Beauty is a very nice mainstream launch which continues the classic Calvin Klein tradition. No, this is not as appealing as a fine jasmine niche perfume, but it is good for what it is: wearable, inexpensive, widely available, and accessible. The bottle, too, conveys the simple yet compelling aesthetic which has always been the hallmark of Calvin Klein. I am happy that the acquisition of this house by Coty Prestige has not led to compromises in the original aesthetic vision of Calvin Klein. My first review was based on a sample vial, and this one on a 15ml purse spray (which came as a part of a coffret), so I can confirm batch consistency as well.
My favorite note in this perfume has got to be the musk mallow/ambrette in this. It's like the olfactory equivalent of the Photoshop blur tool. It makes the jasmine so soft and fuzzy and pretty.

There are just a select few fragrances that I love and enjoy wearing during those middle of the week work days, or days when I'm caring for young children. I don't necessarily want to wear my more expensive, or heavy gourmand scents, so I like to search my collection for a more affordable choice. So many mainstream "pretty" perfumes are either so heavy on the flowers that I've acquired a headache upon first spritz, or they are so ho-hum that it's not even worth taking the time to apply. But, when I first sampled Beauty, I immediately was drawn in by it's well rounded, voluptuous and softly sweet scent. I especially like the floral heart most of all. CK Beauty is not over the top as far as the floral aspect or the sweetness. It in fact becomes somewhat of a skin scent on me, so instead of feeling as though I'm wearing a fragrance, it has melded nicely with my own skin. I am also really drawn to this bottle, very nice.

It's not like this scent hasn't been done before, but admist the fruity floral releases over this past year, Calvin Klein's new floral scent is rather refreshing to say the least. Beauty is a cross between my very favourite Burberry Weekend and Michael Kors EDP. It's a rather bold, sparkling and Summery interpretation of a white floral scent, being mostly jasmine, lily and tuberose with a rich cedary base. The floral blend, although very clean smelling, is quite heavenly. It's somewhat elegant and innocent like the advertising suggests, however for some it is far too distant from those heavier scents like Euphoria and Secret Obsession which have been big sellers in the past. Beauty is a pretty scent, however unfortunately lacking in depth and distinction. I do like this fragrance, but I did hope for more. I quite like its floral freshness, yet every now and then I sense something that smells like a floral-scented bathroom diffuser. The longevity of Beauty is great, well worth the big bucks, however the sillage can in some ways be too strong. Seeing that I'd prefer this kind of scent in the Summer, its heaviness would probably make me ill under such hot conditions.

A friend, who knows I LOVE jasmine gave this to me. I wasn't expecting a lot, but this is lovely. I owe my friend! There is something about Calvin Klein fragrances, a DNA of sorts, which I tend not to like very much, but it works here. Beauty opens with a soft but not too powdery musk mallow, which is quite nice. The jasmine note really starts to bloom for me after about 30 minutes. The jasmine is gorgeous, clean and pure. It's not too indolic, sharp or fluffy. The jasmine/musk mallow combo works very well, and I love the cedar drydown. It is relatively linear, which I don't mind because... jasmine! I find this a fabulous fragrance for layering/blending. It's absolutely perfect for spring and summer, and it's appropriate for anyone 16+. It's also very reasonably priced. I find the longevity improves in hot, humid weather from about 4-5 hours to 7-8 hours. IMO, this fragrance is underrated and very versatile, good for work, casual occasions and evening events, especially summer fun. It's noting fancy or complex. It's simple and beautiful. A very easy reach.

This scent comes alive in the heat. There are not many scents that can stand up to extreme heat, but this can. I happen not to like this fragrance in the winter or cooler months. It doesn't smell good to me. The jasmine comes off as slightly metallic, the opening is too peppery, and the ambrette is completely MIA on my skin.

Notes: citrus cocktail, orange blossom, jasmine, neo-lily, cedarwood, ambrette seeds. Love this perfume, very versatile, unisex, its strong and delicate. Love the jasmine and cedar around the ambrette. Very musky, woody, sweet floral, its pleasant, one falls in love with this scent's personality easily.

It is safe. Safe for me means boring most of the time, but there is a place for these kind of safe juices in my life as well. Doesn't quite fit to my personality, which is more out there and flamboyant, and disappoints me a bit, because Calvin Klein came up with Obsession and Euphoria, two fragrances that I adore, and this is just so blah. Nothing to rave about for me.

This has been my signature scent for so long, its amazing for daytime, for summer, extremely versatile. its light, lovely floral very easy to fall in love with. The Jasmine is absolutely elegant, however it is not the most unique scent out there, and does lack a bit of depth

I owe my little bottle to a dear swap partner. I had tested Beauty a long time ago and found it boring. However, I made that devastating judgment extremely unprofessionally after just one test. Recently, I was in the city and decided to test it out of curiosity again. Suddenly, I perceived the scent quite differently: I liked it.

I really didn't think I would like this one based on the notes and the "Uni-Sex made for a Techno Sexual Generation" ad slogan. (whats that? A generation that knows how to use a mobile or a PC...?) I thought it would smell more like a mens cologne rather than something that I could enjoy. Wrong! I don't get any grapefruit or very much bergamot, on me it's all orchid, amber, cedar and something powdery. I dont really care for the bottle (perhaps a sign I am not a member of the: Techno Sexual Generation despite my PC & iPhone...? -- Dunno! But it looks like a soft-drink bottle rather than a perfume flacon) Bon, I shan't complain because I got 150ML at Douglass for a members only price of €19,99 : ) It's soft, flowery with a hint of bergamot and a powdery drydown plus a delicious note that I can't identify but whatever it is....it smell yummy! It's not a passionate love affair...but It's a crush, for sure! (on the juice...not the bottle ;) Silage is: a pretty floral powdery cloud that's not a fragrance bomb but noticeable nonetheless. -- Longevity is: great with on me 6+ hours. Don't judge this one by the bottle or notes! And don't buy into the claim that its for "young" people only, thats poppycock! I am a big believer that anybody of any age/gender should enjoy whatever fragrance they like! Full stop! This is one of those fragrances that rely (obviously) heavy on your chemistry. So, go and mix! ; ) Good luck!

I was truly amazed by this fragrance. When I first tried CK IN2U, it smelt rather like champagne. It had that familiar sourish and fizzy like quality. However, since testing it again, (this time on my skin), I must say that this fragrance is rather sweet. The opening of bergamot, grapefruit and currant isn't as loud on the skin as it is on paper. This scent softened into a sweet, creamy, cake-like fragrance, which somewhat reminded me of Hidden Fantasy by Britney Spears. While on some people this fragrance is primarily tarty fruits, on others, as well as myself, CK IN2U is intimate and extremely pleasant. I wouldn't say that this fragrance has great sillage, because it doesn't, however the lasting power is impressive. I have definitely grown to like this fragrance, even considering purchasing it since discovering how different and soft it smelt when applied to the skin. I urge people to not buy this fragrance based on how it smells on paper or from the bottle.

I discovered this perfume while looking for a fresher yet sexy scent for the summer time to diversify my otherwise mainly sweet and vanilla-heavy collection. To my surprise this quickly became one of my go-to scents for everyday. It's an easy reach that does mostly smell fresh and citrusy and a bit aromatic when you first apply it. However the dry-down is where this perfume really impressed me! It turns into a very woody slightly spicy scent, probably due to that cedar and amber in the base. It smells so addicting and sexy to me, which I rarely get from fresher perfumes. I've even worn this on date nights and my boyfriend absolutely loved it as well.

Sometimes when I go through my collection I dwell by a perfume and wonder why I never wear it. CK in2 You for Her is such a scent. It has been in my collection for some years, and the only time I remember sniffing it was when it came to me in a bundle of several different bottles from a generous parfumista I know. What did I sniff? To my nose it was a bit anonymous. Fresh, a bit fruity and rather unisex. CK was King of Unisex in the early 2000s, as I recall, so I was not surprised. I have a difficult relationship with CK One, being the only person not liking it and everyone else wearing it. The dry down of this one is much better, warm and a bit woody; what CK One lacks. So if you are looking for a fresh CK scent for summer days and sports - go buy this. The price is fair, even without discount. Year 2, 13/365

Often found on the cheapie shelves at Shoppers, this is a little gem that's versatile and vibrant. It does have an early 2000s CK DNA that comes across as sporty, but it evolves from bright grapefruit to a citrus cup of tea laced with woody vanilla. It's not creamy; the vanilla is a whisper to soften up any acidic edges from the citrus. An easy reach for running errands, a coffee date with friends, or anytime you need a mood lift. Will always have this in my collection!

Fifteen years ago, I was a student, had just passed my exams, and summer was approaching. I was no longer a child, but not yet an adult either. This drive, youth, and freshness—these are associations with this scent and those times that are forever gone. Overall, it's a nice, versatile scent, I wouldn't call it particularly multifaceted, but it's playful and fresh.

i love her!!!! perfect unisex. starts off very citrusy and fresh and then becomes more green as time goes on. however the performance is kind of awful... if i had this with better performance id be so satisfied but it’s a nice pick me up on its own and i dont expect much from fresh perfumes esp if its for this price

One day, a little half-empty bottle wandered into my perfume cabinet. Unloved, passed on by a colleague of a friend. "This might be something for you, it smells like lemon," I was told. For me? I'm not really into citrus scents. Well, it's worth a try. And from then on, it was love at first sniff. It starts off citrusy, but not sharp or sour, rather like a fluffy lemon cake.

“CKi2U for her” or “It’s Time for a Love Declaration” This fragrance has faithfully accompanied me for 6 years now. There hasn’t been a day when a bottle of it wasn’t in my closet. It has been with me through springs with its hint of floral scent, through summers with its sweet oranges and grapefruits, and through autumn and winter with its cozy vanilla.

Hey hey, fragrance fanatics. Welcome to a new comment from me. Today I'm talking about Calvin Klein. I know some of you might not care much about this, but we need some mainstream fragrances every now and then, otherwise it would be boring to only describe high-quality niche scents, right?

Can you pull off Envy with aplomb? Does Eden work well for you? Have you the right chemistry to tame Calyx? If you can work wet-florals or answer "yes" to any of the above then you may enjoy this unusual floral fume. In all honesty, on my skin, this scent sickens & dies, turning a testing into a stomach-twisting headache. I am not a big, bold floral gal but along with the flowers I also find stagnant water, mildew on sodden earth &, of all things, ashtrays (chemistry & scent-perception is such a strange thing!). That said, I can truly appreciate the concept. Here is a floral that aims to conjure up the still, heavy, heady moist air of a hot-house full of exotic blooms. Others (say a cool-skinned blonde) may marvel at the intoxicating pervasive perfumes but to my nose these strange flowers, wet woods & over-ripe fruits seem sad & trapped, removed from their natural environment. The start is green, sappy, peppery a little bitter. This settles to a humid, white floral heart where slighlty sickly fruits & that sour-stem note add to the still, moist, heady throng. It continues to grow & glow on my skin, a dark vine entwined round my wrist, ending in a slick of wet, woody warmth. BP has the uncanny knack of being unique & yet it reminds me of other fragrances, many of which do not sit easily on my skin. I find the hyacinth from Envy is very present along with the green note of Eden & white florals found in Premier Jour Soleil. Not for me at all - but cool-skinned floral-lovers should give it a try.

I didn't like this when I tried it at the perfume counter and so I snubbed it despite glowing reviews. There was a synthetic top note that I can't name and it just smelled watery and weak. Last Christmas there was a gift set with 4 fragrance minis and Beyond Paradise was in it. I purchased the set for travel purposes and grudgingly used this fragrance. This really started to grow on me as it changed by the hour. It was like walking through a tropical rain forest where you smell one flower, then another, and then several in combination. I could smell wet tree bark somewhere in the distance...but barely. This is definatley a fragrance that you can't knock until you try it.

Beyond Paradise is as alien as Mugler’s Angel, if not more. But EL hides its freak in a way that Mugler wouldn’t consider. The chief accord in Angel is synthetic in that it resembles food, but is poisonous. BP gives you a fetching nosegay, but one made of shards of glass, sugar-coated with laundry powder. Angel was a utterly novel concept when it was released, with an accord that leaned on the jarring side of juxtaposition and therefore read as synthetic. BP is so like so many things you’ve smelled before, most of them scented, functional commercial products. But it’s teased together into what some would call an idealized flower. I’d call it a floral least common denominator. Our noses learn over the years of sniffing cleaning products and the like to equate so-called “floral” with flowers. BP relies on this implied language of commercial scent, whispers a translation to us in press-release English and we believe that this scent is based on the Utopia Flower that grows Somewhere or other. OK, that ‘s the jaded view of corporate perfumery. As to the actual creation of this scent, it is impeccably composed, and I can’t imagine the work that went into it. But again, least common denomiator. BP is a bit like a predictable but popular Broadway show. It speaks in a theatrical language that we’re all guaranteed to understand and doesn’t advance the state of the art an inch. We talk of perfumery as art, and we should. BP is entertainment, but is it art?

I don't know what was going through my head when I decided that I actually liked this fragrance. Trying it on my wrist today made me change my mind completely. Sickeningly sweet, synthetic and reminiscent of toilet spray was how I perceived Beyond Paradise. I just couldn't get this perfume off my wrist fast enough. Definitely long-lasting, it took 3 different types of soaps to get this one off.

This perfume smells lots of hyacinth(at start) , lilly of the valley, jasmine and honeysuckle. From 1st time I try like it. Because this scent is very similar in heart notes= REBUL JASMİNE COLOGNE. And that one I like also. I remind old ladies, flower based bright color clothes. Best age =+30 but for floral lovers any age using. Elegant, chic, floral, bright, calming perfume. You can use every weather and season. Day and night, thats so simple. Not the best longevity but that wont disappoint you, girls.

One of the things that I really love about perfumes is that I can feel my nose develop over time. Perfumes that I did not like when I was 15 or 20 have proven to be worth waiting for. Beyond Paradise is one of those. When I first sniffed this, I frowned upon it because of the way too sour beginning. It smelled synthetic and I thought about who would want to wear this perfume.

I pick up a pervasive amount of Amber Frangrapani jasmine That all i can smell i could not pick up the other scents so these are more dominient. which i'm not a Amber lover. What i think About Estee Lauder Perfumes that it's a mixed bag you got good ones and you got some bad ones This one i'll give like a 6.5 a Little above Average Perfume.

This is a creamy fruity flower scent that is pretty unique and different in the current scent scene. The combination of creamy sweetness weirdly reminds me of the yellow banana marshmallows. You know those candies that look like banana, but are too sweet and flowery? My friend told me the candy are supposed to taste like the banana strain that almost disappeared, Gros Michel.

I’m another of those who fell in love with this scent as a teenager, and as I recently found an unopened vintage bottle on eBay I jumped at the opportunity to have it back in my collection. There is always a risk with such things, but in this instance it was a risk worth taking; it smells just like I remember. So - a bold, lush floral.

Liking this damn thing is not easy, as it hides behind banal stuff like fabric softener and air freshener. The joke is: it has - if you spray boldly and persist - a clever note of a hot iron on a good shirt, plus a hint of ripe pear flambéed, with a touch of thyme baked on and smelled from afar.

Although Kenzo Power Cologne was released approximately ten years ago, at that time, I already had the original Kenzo Power in my wardrobe. Therefore I did not pay too much attention to it being Cologne a flanker of it. However, a couple of weeks ago, I ran into a bottle of Cologne tester, and immediately my mind returned to that time, the original floral smell of that perfume made of a secret powdery, androgyne, and oriental aura created by Power. Without hesitation, I bought it for a ridiculous price. I happened this morning I noticed the bottle on the shelf of my bathroom, and I wore it to go to the office. The opening of Power Cologne is rich of bergamot along with verbena and cardamom. The verbena is an excellent substitute for the original Power's neroli as it also carries the citrus aspect along with a slightly floral character. The cardamom imparts a crisp, soft spiciness, which also lends itself towards a citrus feel. The combination of bergamot and cardamom is the same as in the original Power and carries surprising "power" for a fragrance trying to emulate an eau de cologne. The heart starts with a geranium note, which is green and floral at the same time, sharing that similarity to the lavender in Aqua Admirabilis. That starts as pepper and coriander take the geranium and add a fresh feel to the middle of this. These notes add a touch to the floral character, which makes it less clean and sweet and more spicy and floral. Yet in Power Cologne, I catch that powdery and buttery aspects of the iris flower, or better the orris root, which in my opinion is the secret flower never mentioned in the pyramid notes. The base is a woody mix of cedar and tolu balsam with a touch of vetiver thrown in. It gives Power Cologne the feel of the original Power in the woodiness. Where the original went for amber to warm things up, in this fragrance vetiver keeps the woods on the clean and fresh side of the fragrance line, which is appropriate for a modern cologne. Power Cologne has outstanding longevity and sillage. It is remarkable because of most Eau de Colognes last only a short while. I am not the biggest fan of flankers when they are too similar to the original, but in this case, the perfumer has done an excellent job of marrying the qualities of a traditional eau de cologne and the unique Power. In doing so, he has created a fragrance that is recognizably made up of that fragrant genetics but can stand on its own, deservedly so. Cologne is a more gentle fragrance to the original Power and can easily be worn daily. I find this highly distinct and rather dull with its citrus opening cute green heart and lovely oriental dry down. You should give this a try if you ever come across a bottle. I was hoping you wouldn't make the same mistake I did long ago. I like the scent because of its lightness but the lingering and passionate smell. It is ideal of ordinary days when you want to go to the office, or for men who want to smell fresh while hitting the gym, or just during the average days of spring and summer. To my flavor, Cologne is suitable for spring and summer days and early evenings, for both young and older men. -Elysium

A beautiful, gentle and flowery cologne. Citruses, mixed meadow flowers on a soft green and woody background. Well blended, transparent and easy to wear. Pale green color of liquid perfectly fits to this already discontinued composition. Olivier Polge is incredibly creative perfumer, as seen in this mini masterpiece. Hope he will do the same in Chanel. Rating: 8/10

Since Kenzopower was such a thin little water, I immediately bathed my wrist with 5 sprays. After all - there was indeed something to smell. Kenzopower smells like floral soap, with a certain sharpness that enhances the soapiness. I feel somewhat transported back to the 70s, when a soap, like "Lux," was marketed as a luxury item. Who still remembers the unbearable advertisement with - I believe it was Senta Berger - showcasing the softness of her skin thanks to Lux to the astonished television audience? Personally, I don't really want to smell like I've run out of water while showering. However, there may still be contemporaries who see perfumed soap as a luxury item. The poor things! Kenzopower Cologne seems - with a generous application - to be a bit stronger than Kenzopower. Yet Kenzopower, despite all its weakness, is a fragrance to be taken seriously. The Cologne, on the other hand, only becomes acceptable in the drydown, when the sharpness fades, the soapiness diminishes, and a distinct dry-powdery note emerges. Acceptable, but still not good. And it's not even a Cologne; it has Eau de Toilette strength. The entire marketing gives me the impression that this fragrance is aimed at completely inexperienced buyers. If it's Kenzopower, then please the original. I find the Cologne unpleasant to insignificant.

First of all: Is Kenzo Power a masculine fragrance? I'm surprised. I would have expected it to be unisex. *thinking* In that regard, I also thought that Kenzo Power Cologne was unisex. However, it is also labeled as masculine in the database. Well. Today at Karstadt: A prominently placed table with selected fragrances. Oh, what's this? A new scent? As a Cologne fan, I immediately spotted the beautiful bottle of Kenzo Power Cologne. Clear glass, light green liquid. I had never seen it before. Maybe it's due to the temperatures that they placed it there, it fits thematically.. I must confess: I really wanted to like Kenzo Power back then. This bottle, this name, these fragrance notes - I tried several times. Unfortunately, the scent always turned out to be... *clears throat*... too boring. Now there's a Cologne. I want a Cologne to provide a light yet intense refreshment. This fragrance does achieve that at the beginning. The opening is classic with bergamot, lemon, and verbena. However, it quickly becomes too warm for me. Already in the heart note, it gets sweeter with vetiver, and the tolu balsam in the base reinforces that. The cedarwood is too light for me; the scent could use a touch more woodiness. Now, after a few hours, a bright warm slightly powdery sweetness remains. The fragrance is not intrusive, not extraordinary, actually quite nice. You can wear it, but you don't have to. Oh, and I think a woman could wear it too.

Kenzo Power Cologne... it's already been 3 years since I had it in my collection. I bought it back then with my ex-girlfriend at the Centro in Oberhausen, as she thought it looked great on me.
