It has a depth and a resonance that makes it almost surreal next to the fragrances of the following decades - a Chypre pulsating like an open heart from the depths of memory, equally blazing with fire and heavy with tears. Just like City's melancholic seven-minute classic, which still makes me whisper when it crosses my path: 'Psst, be quiet for a moment!' Conclusion, in Toni Krahls' haunting voice: 'Once know, this stays forever - is not intoxication that already accuses the night, is not color melt, not candle shimmer - long chased away by the gray of the morning.'

.....an olfactory journey to Brittany. "Alliage" by Estee Lauder is a masterpiece by perfumer Bernard Chant, one of a kind. GREEN-- Galbanum lets a cool wind refresh, rough Atlantic greetings. The warmth of summer is bearable, indeed PLEASANT. Summer in Brittany. Shady forests, rocky landscapes.

I can still remember well, at that time the popular patchouli and musk scents were in vogue. I had clothes like ABBA on stage and we drove a Citroën 2CV!! And then came this green, spicy fragrance that had nothing sweet about it. After the "make-love-not-war" and pill revolution years, cleanliness and order were back in style.

Alliage (here likely in the sense of mixture, blend) is derived from the Latin 'ligare', to bind, connect. And my nose quickly finds the cool-silvery-green thread that holds and connects fruits, flowers, wood, and moss: the Galbanum that I highly appreciate. To support my work, I like to use aromatic scents and often incorporate Galbanum as part of a fragrance blend.

I have read such beautiful reports about Alliage here on Parfumo. That makes me happy because I also like this scent so much. I first tested Alliage in 1988. After a long day at work in the office, pregnant with my eldest daughter, I went to an Estée Lauder cosmetics consultation.

June 1992. A large bank. First day in the office. New country, new city, new system, new colleagues. PURE FEAR!!! Everything is foreign and so indescribably far from the familiar. It’s no use, I have to get through it, because I have to support a family. An own office, an own desk, and an own PC.

This fragrance is already foreign to me, with its sparkling green essence and its light-footed liveliness: Perhaps for me today, as an old lady, it feels a bit too fresh, a bit too green and restless, for I only encountered “Parfum d’Été” now. But it is beautiful and has its own charm, this composition by Kenzo, where summery fragrance notes create a pleasing melody that develops into an entertaining companion throughout the day, perhaps even a kind of "earworm". Like many creations from the eighties and nineties, this one has passed me by, and therefore I am glad that we are meeting today. A romantic summer love with all its buoyancy has been captured in this scent: Clear, sometimes strong colors and fragrance tones harmonize in fresh, down-to-earth lily of the valley leaf green, spicy hyacinth violet and pink, the feathery variety of peony blossoms, together with a sensual abundance of white jasmine flowers. They all rest on a spicy sandalwood-patterned musk blanket. “Parfum d’Été” evolves into a watercolor in fragrance over its course; for a pastel idyll, it is too spicy and too vibrant, but it is extremely lively and sparkling like the first glass of Prosecco of the still young summer and the playfulness of the first flirt of this promising season: They all sparkle wonderfully excitingly and create a desire for more! Kenzo's “Parfum d’Été” was created at a time when, even with this summery “love song in scent”, great value was placed on craftsmanship, and thus also on sillage and longevity. It was not just thrown together to survive a summer season, but was carefully crafted with consideration for the future wearer, so that each fragrance note in this composition is in the place from which it can best accompany and support the entire fragrance song: “Parfum d’Été” is full of radiant summer and resembles a beautiful, timeless melody that could be sung by the lark in the morning. That is why it is still loved and worn even after more than twenty years. I wanted to test its summer feeling just once, out of curiosity, but then received a whole bottle of this summery creation in its extraordinary bottle from a dear perfumer. As mentioned at the beginning, this beauty is too green, too lively for me - simply too foreign; we do not match at all in type! But as is well known, every pot finds its matching lid: A lover encountered “Parfum d’Été” while browsing through my collection, left a corresponding note, and today the package with this scent-turned “summer melody” and another one of my “less loved children” (there are indeed these fragrances: beautiful, but fundamentally foreign) is on its way and will be appreciated in the future as every fragrance deserves. These treasures from another, not forgotten time should be loved and valued and ideally come into the right hands, onto the right skin: They want to be worn, to be lived! And that is why I am very happy that “Parfum d’Été” can embark on a hopefully happy future today: Love, in whatever form, and summer scent are timeless! Once again it shows: With this multitude of creations from the eighties and nineties, not all could survive, yet the fragrances we encounter today are witnesses of a generous, colorful, and lively era that we fondly remember. We should cherish them!

Another package arrived from dear Ola. (No surprise, I ordered again from the abundance of her offerings)! If anyone is really looking for good vintage fragrances, take a look at the collection of Olkaolka in the category: "Flakon to go," it’s worth it. (I hope I’m allowed to write that?) Well then, I thought to myself, I somehow know Kenzo d'Ete from the past, so I’ll buy it, just on a whim. And what can I say: I am very taken with it! It has a wonderful floral arrangement. You feel transported to a garden bustling with white blossoms. Butterflies flutter by, bumblebees buzz, little bees hum, in the sky small, fluffy clouds, it sings and swings, it smells of life and I am happy. The fragrance starts with the lily of the valley, which I love so much, but they appear not sweet but rather restrained, as is fitting for these small, lovely white flowers. But wait, it’s not the bells that are fragrant; it’s a lily of the valley leaf, hence this green twist, hence this restraint, which is, however, very attractive. Then follows, at least for me, immediately the hyacinth, it is present in almost all my preferred fragrance waters, oh yes, jasmine is also included, but not so strong that it takes your breath away, rather very friendly, soft, like an unexpectedly warm sunbeam hitting slightly chilly skin. At least that’s how I perceive it at the moment, because today is sunny, but occasionally clouds come by that unfortunately cover the warm rays, so you feel doubly happy when the sunlight bursts forth again and warms us. Oh yes, sandalwood and musk are also supposed to be present, but I can’t really identify them individually, but it doesn’t matter, the overall impression convinces me and I will wear it often and thoughtfully, as it is no longer produced in this form. (Mine is still the version that came out in 1992. - At least I think so). I don’t know the newer version. It is said to be produced unchanged, but should I believe that? All in all, we have here a fine, fresh, floral fragrance that carries you lightly through the day, smells floral green and does not excite. On the contrary, it makes you really curious about this scent because you can’t immediately define whether it’s floral or green or both? A big thank you to sweet Ola for this fragrance treasure (and the wonderful extras)! Wishing you all a lovely day.

Out of all the Estee Lauder fragrances, contemporary & vintage, YDAN is my second favorite (after Sensous Noir). Initially, I didn't much care for it. However, the more I wore it, the more I liked it ... and the more compliments I received. YD may be named after Youth Dew, but YDAN is only distantly related, perhaps the niece or grand niece of the original YD. In my opinion, YDAN is more closely related to Cinnabar, perhaps her daughter - a lighter, brighter version without spice. Regardless, YDAN is better than either YD or Cinnabar, imo. And I've owned (and liked) both. I swear there is vanilla on top (what others call coca-cola? maybe rootbeer like Tabu). I also get a bit of the plastic dollhead. However, YDAN is all the drydown, and the drydown is all about the amber, which is a beautifully warm, old-timey amber. Several reviewers have mentioned incense, which I don't sense but is resplendent in the YD bath oil. YDAN is great in evenings in summer, but daytime wear is best reserved for cooler weather. YDAN is not a fragrance to sniff up-close but from a distance. which may be the reason that I didn't like it at first but others did. It's modern enough to seem fresh but traditional enough to have a lineage to 2 EL fragrances, Youth Dew and Cinnabar. I have grown to love this one. Don't let it pass you by & don't jump to conclusions. Take your time. It's a grower!

This one is a really lovely amber-oriental perfume, that keeps the charm of the old-fashioned style that it follows, but never at any point, manages to feel outdated or old. Amber Nude is a modernized classic, strongly inspired by the original and unforgettable Youth Dew, but with a more contemporary feel to it. The notes are very well blended, and the whole composition feels incredibly rich, sensual and opulent with a texture like warm liquid gold. Sweet amber, spicy cinnamon, bitter carnation and creamy sandalwood and patchouli mix together to give birth to a very balmy elixir that feels lavishly elegant and expensive. It's perfect for a night out at a luxurious event. Amber Nude is a very sensual fragrance, exceptionally sexy and alluring in a silver screen femme-fatale fashion. In my opinion this is one of the best ambers around (the feminine, seductive, vintage-style type), with very good lasting power and amazing projection. And another thing that's amazing about it is the very affordable price at which it can be purchased online. Nice job, Estee Lauder, Laudamiel and especially, Tom Ford, on this one. On my wishlist, of course.

Estee Lauder YOUTH DEW AMBER NUDE, like its namesake, has an intangible catacombic quality to it, somehow conveying the aura of not exactly death but something sickly or moribund--or perhaps simply petrified. The juice reminds me a bit of what I imagine would be the smell of a Coke and bourbon that someone didn't finish drinking at a party and which then sat out overnight. The next day the host has the task of cleaning up and is accosted by the strong, dark, alcoholic smell now flat and entirely unappealing. YOUTH DEW AMBER NUDE does not smell like amber to me, and if I were to compare it to another perfume, I'd say that it comes closest to TABU without the skank. Is this really the smell of Catholic churches? Thank "God" (or reasonable facsimile) I'm agnostic. Could be a skin chemistry issue, but this one's definitely not for me. Désolée. ** Update: having now read the reviews in The Guide of YOUTH DEW and YDAN (both of which receive 4 stars), I am forced to modify my earlier hypothesis. I no longer believe that LT is an EL shill. I now believe that he is a middle-aged suburban middle class housewife who spends his afternoons collecting gwps from the EL counters of major department stores.

Youth dew Amber nude if you parallel this from the older sister Youth Dew, it gives you an impression of a younger less oily and more velvety feel amber nude is correct. Amber nude starts off with dry unsweetened cinnamon with ginger nuances there is a short period of sweetness due to the lovely magnolias the sweetness is distempered by the domineering scent of ginger. The three elements that makes this scent powdery is rose carnation and ylang ylang the tea note mmmmmmmmm? it's in there but like a lot of other notes it fades quickly but it adds a nice addition. The drydown really in my opinion gets the prize of course of it's namesake Amber Nude there is a predominate alot of it but it's the Sandalwood that stands out the sandalwood gives out an velvety feel to the skin then the original Like deep sandalwood incense burning I love the Color of the flacon like an sheer bronze sheet caressing you in a spartan bedroom with Burnt orange lights around you on a circular Bed. Gives the thought when 1 wear this
Nice-smelling amber saved from simplicity by a dull rubber note that balances the amber’s syrup. (Also, less youth Dew than Cinnabar.)

Among the thirteen EL fragrances I own this is the warmest. Medicinal, yes. Potent, yes. My partner finds it too loud and sickening. But I also perceive it as warm. It feels like a sweater on a winter’s day. The original Youth Dew can be a bit overwhelming but YDAN is so perfectly balanced - for me, that is. I am a huge fan. It is, however, not a scent I wear in public.

I can’t stand the original Youth Dew its very overwhelming/stifling and has a bad scent association with an elderly bully from my childhood. It’s surprising I would be willing to try anything connected to Youth Dew but I know that flankers/revisions often smell nothing like the original.

is - perhaps just slightly behind the even more epic "Hallelujah" - the most famous, the greatest, the immortal song of the famous, the great, the immortal Leonard Cohen, who was a singer and a poet and so much more.
On the hunt for the perfect amber scent part 4 I was once again provided with plenty of testing material by dear Parfumas. Thanks again, you lovely people! I received this sample from DieselWiesel.

Dear Mom and Dad, Today I unfortunately have to beg you for money again, because I absolutely need to attend an advanced English course. Since my basic course, strange things keep happening with my fragrances: I still have Grey Flannel from Grandpa. Okay, I thought it would match my gray wool cloak and went to the medieval festival with it.

This perfume immediately caught my attention the first time I sniffed it. It's sharp, fresh, and powdery, supporting a tropical fruit tone. The herbs remain in the background. As it settles, the aquatic and eucalyptus notes become more prominent yet still ancillary to the melon-mango-citrus melange. Escape is slightly sweet and delightfully sharp. I love this perfume for the summer. It exudes a masculine freshness that is disparate from the typical summer citrus-aquatics. Escape always projects enough to turn a few smiling heads and has fair longevity. I've been told that I smell "yummy" when I've been hugged while wearing this fragrance. Who doesn't like to smell yummy?

While I'm usually one for darker and sexy scents on a man, I really do appreciate Escape for Men. This fragrance is very Summery and fresh. However instead of being Summery in a citrusy sense, this is more accustomed to being green, spicy and slightly aquatic. The melon and mango notes make the scent a little sweet but the strong herbs and spices keep the scent masculine. The eucalyptus note in Escape is rather strong, and for all those fellow Australians out there, or people who have visited our country, the scent is very much like the Aussie outback in the middle of Summer, with large stretches of land covered with Eucalyptus gums, dry brown grass and rich, fertile soil. To me this is the scent of a rugged bushman. Since I grew up in the bush, Escape is comforting and natural for me. Also, like the female version of Escape, there is a subtle oceanic quality, rather like sea salt lingering softly in the background. Certain parts of this fragrance certainly remind me of the beach. All in all, Escape really doesn't get the credit it deserves. Although popular, very rarely will people see the composition itself, which is exquisite. I do really love this on a man. One of my favourite Summery male scents by far.

This is a sweet fruity green aquatic scent that's still manly...somehow. If you haven't smelled this before, go for it. It's a nice scent... Don't you love it when a blind buy goes well?! I can't wait to use this during the spring and summertime, drinking some lemonade, while wearing shorts & a tee shirt. Maybe walking on the pier. Anyway, that's where I see myself using this frag. I used six sprays...both wrist, back & front of my neck, my chest and on my shirt. Would I buy this again?...Yeah! Does this fragrance enter BEAST MODE, good, just okay or weak sauce at best? Good. What's the strength of this? EDT. Am I willing to trade this fragrance? Yes. Should You Skipped It, Sample It First or Blind Buy It? Blind Buy Worthy. Can you use it as a unisex scent? No. Is it the old, new formulation? New. What's its availability; in production, limited edition or discontinued? In production. SKU Number: 088300190515 (Tester) Batch Number: 6298 (Production Date: October 24, 2016) Age: 18+ From: FragranceNet Size: 100ML Scent: 5/5 (Awesome). Value: 5/5 (Cost $16.50). Sillage: 3.5/5 (Four to three feet). Longevity: 3.25/5 (Six hours plus). Creativity: 5/5 (Sweet & fresh reminds me of springtime). Projection: 3/5 (90 minutes tops). Versatility: 3.25/5 (Can't wait to wear this during the spring & summer, during the day or night & anywhere). Compliments: 3.75/5 (Well received, everyone liked it.). Until next time, I'll catch you on the flipside.

Escape was one of my first scents. I bought it in 1996 and at that time i was in love it. It's a real nice release from CK that remains great untill now. It's an all-year-around fragrance, but works better in hot months. Fruity and fresh, definetely worth it. I smell mostly fruits such as melon and also lots of herbs/spices. Updated January 2014

If u value the Calvin Klein of old the vintage is what u want. I find myself constantly saying this in all of my reviews. Why? Because anything made after the year 2000 has been butchered and neutered due to the that hapless draconian communistic organization the IFRA. They are no friends of mine and they never will be because they have, along with the EU (European Union,) single handedly ruined modern perfumerie and then hide behind the reason of safety. To that i say crap!! Instead of intelligently labelling the bottles with allergy warnings they flat out banish centuries old raw materials necessary for a fragrances makeup. Escape by Calvin Klein is another such casualty. On the one hand I have a frosty bottle from the early 1990s and on the other hand I have a bottle from last year and the difference is astounding, simply astounding. The early bottle gives me at least three more hours of longevity. Why? Because they haven't tinkered with the oak Moss like they have in the current version. If u value what u wear that should matter in a big way. The fruity beginning is pleasant enough but after that there's not much else. It says oakmoss as one of the notes but u and i know it's barely in there since perfumeries can not use any more than 0.1% of oakmoss absolute. You can't do much with that. Yes oakmoss, PURE UNADULTERATED OAKMOSS is that important to the lifeline of any fragrance. Supposedly some makers have come up with new versions of the stuff that's supposed to mirror the real thing. Whatever. IMO Escape by Calvin Klein should be more, so much more but sadly it just is not.

It is a nice scent, Fruity, Fresh and Sweet. It was in my radar and I found it with inexpensive price ! My mother wore Calvin Klein Escape for women about 25 years ago and I was curious about Escape for men. It opens up with like sweet fresh fruity and green notes in the background then dry down is semi sweet green woody.

Do you remember those belt hole punches? Those pliers with a wheel of tips of different diameters to punch a new hole in your belt or whatever you call it. One of those utensils that my parents own. - Just like those egg guillotines to massacre your breakfast egg.

Today I discovered Escape for Men edt at my flea market dealer. I have fond memories of the women's Escape, so I took a chance and bought it blind. And what can I say - now I'm wearing the escape - which turns out to be a very pleasant refuge. This fragrance starts softly fresh - not like a splash of cold water in the face.
Escape for Men .... That was back then the scent of my boyfriend (now my husband), and when I just moved in with him and we started sharing things, I ended up using this fragrance among others.
After all, it's been 23 years, and yet "Escape for men" strongly reminds me of many artificially fresh scents that have been cluttering the shelves for just over half a decade. Reformulated or not?

Yesterday, in inhospitable temperatures, off to the flea market. Shivering, I hurriedly followed my nose to my fragrance stands. I had already found treasures at two stands and could have headed home - with my loot in tow. But I couldn't skip the last stand in the farthest corner out of courtesy - because my dealers know me. Oh, there was Flower in the Air waiting for me. No thanks - I already have it. But this flower in the air was more floral and transparent than the bottle waiting for me at home. The pear - grapefruit combination is clear and flowing - and transitions fully into rose and freesia. The musk note adds a subtle elegance. Very nice - and somehow different from my home bottle. Considered good and purchased. At home, I realized that I own the EDP - and it has a fruitier, sweeter orientation than the EDT. The scents are indeed similar - but they present themselves differently. So my nose did not deceive me - and I find that both fragrances appeal to me in their own way.

CK Free is a fragrance that promises so much, yet delivers so little. The notes in the pyramid look absolutely amazing; however the scent in the bottle bears little to no resemblance to those notes. That said it's not actually a bad fragrance. It's clean, light and fresh. Unfortunately it's also very generic and very run-of-the-mill.

I'm a little shocked by looking at the notes listed here. CK Free doesn't smell as unique as its composition. I'm in agreeance with the other reviewers, CK Free is very bland and boring. It's missing something that makes it stand out from the rest of the male scents on the market. CK Free is not unpleasant, I find it very wearable, however it has a very citrusy and fresh edge that is starting to become a little overdone in the fragrance industry. I don't see citrus listed here in the notes, but I swear I can smell some bergamot and lemon with an almost aquatic type note. The woods are not very prominent. In fact, the oak and cedar are so subtle that they could be easily dismissed. More in the way of the juniper berries, coffee and patchouli would have given this fragrance an interesting touch and would have made this fragrance far more complex than it is. All in all, CK Free is a pleasant Summer scent that just hasn't managed to reach the mark with me.

It is a nice fragrance, easy to wear, Fresh, Clean and Woody. It smells so good and very pleasant with reasonable price. In my opinion, It is better than the most of perfumes has been launched in 2020 and 2021 that has been crap. It opens up with like fresh , slightly spicy green and leather notes in the background then dry down is green woody. This is perfect for the spring and summer. I really enjoy it and I like CK Free for Men by Calvin Klein. Longevity is average. Rating : 7.5 / 10

A light, cool, cozy, casual, masculine, and refreshing summer daytime fragrance. If you read about the perfume's ingredients before smelling it, you might imagine it's a dark, wintery fragrance. A fragrance that is accepted by everyone and is not annoying. If you cannot love it, you certainly will not hate it. The scent is dominated by juniper berries, followed by a balanced blend of star anise, jackfruit, suede, cedar, and woody notes. One of the biggest drawbacks of this fragrance is its poor sillage projection and not being a long-lasting fragrance. Performance is at best two hours. This limitation can be overcome by increasing the spray dose. To be honest, I didn't find any synthetic scent in any of its stages, from the opening to the drydown stage. The bottle design is very unique and attractive. The price is very reasonable and affordable for everyone. Final word: If you are a fan of CK fragrances and love CK Truth fragrance line, you will definitely like CK Free.

bought in 2014 thanks to an advantageous price offered by my works council. I had already discovered it in the summer of 2009 at the sephora at the Gare de Lyon in Paris. it is a light summer fragrance, fresh aquatic and synthetic, ultimately quite banal. even if it is really pleasant in the evening. I liked it at the time because I had not yet discovered so many nuggets in perfumery. With hindsight, I tell myself that it is much more suitable for a young teenager, for his first perfumes. It seems to me that it is no longer marketed in France.

and the durability is just as bad as people say it is. The fragrance doesn’t change, the projection bubble is very small, and the sillage is nonexistent. The longevity problems aren’t exaggerated; this one dies out in barely 2 hours. Then it becomes an absolutely SOFT skin scent. A very nice scent; very bright and fresh.

Ck Free, yet another fragrance where the name doesn't quite match the program. As I mentioned in my other reviews, my mother brought me a travel size set from Mr. Klein. Not necessarily bad, but far from my hopes for all 5 scents in the set. Ck Free also gives the feeling of not being quite finished.

..therefore just briefly: Insignificant, shallow little water, hardly noticeable on the skin. It actually just smells very clumsily aquatic, the ingredient list above is a joke, I can hardly smell any of it. This is pure smoke and mirrors, what is listed above. A hint of artificial exoticism at the start (jackfruit?), otherwise just pure, shallow, synthetic aquatics.

...doesn't have to be a bad thing! Personally, I prefer the scent of CK Free by far over standard aquatics like Cool Water. It feels rounder and more harmonious to me, and perhaps that's why it has a reputation for being boring. Because no one will be taken aback by this fragrance, which is something that can't usually be said about the top-rated scents.

Not only is the bottle successful, but the scent is as well. I was looking for an everyday fragrance and ended up with the new Calvin Klein scent. As the name suggests, "Free," and that's exactly what I was looking for. I'm at university during the day and don't want to use heavy fragrances that might disturb those around me ;) The scent is very light and uncomplicated.

Very nice perfume as usual from Calvin Klein. Its strong though appropriate for summer or spring. Very aquatic and flowery too. Excellent sillage and longevity. The chamomile note is very strong in the beginning but later it settles down and the other notes arise. I would categorize this perfumes as very aromatic. Thanks CK.

what a WONDERFUL fragrant! I tried it today for the first time. Most peoples comments are about it's nostalgia, given I am only 20 and have no nostalgia from it I still LOVED it!!! It is a bit strong at first but the drydown is esquisite! I think I will purchase a small bottle for my collection. hrs after I sprayed it it is still very strong.

I read these reviews before I tried this perfume, and I must say I was preparing myself for an overpoweringly strong, mature perfume. I should make note of the fact that I'm 18 and that I really liked this fragrance when I finally got around to testing it. Strong, yes, but not so strong that it would knock someone out upon first sniff. Sophisticated, warm and sensual is how I would describe Escape. I can see this perfume being worn any time, whether it be during the day, at night or even during a special occasion. It may be a perfume that smells very similar to a lot of fragrances these days, but there's something about Escape that is intriguing and rather charming. Update: When I first tested this fragrance I had never noticed that Escape had a salty note. I was quite surprised to discover this as it did indeed remind me of the ocean. Seeing that all my memories associated with the beach are good ones, this will most definitely be top priority on my wishlist. Second update: Escape did not work well with my skin chemistry. Unfortunately I had to push this one aside.
Escape is Indian summer in a bottle. Strangely it holds no beach associations for me but instead conjures those golden blue sky days that segue sunny and warm into the Australian autumn.

Calvin Klein is an interesting brand. I have 18 of his fragrances, some are great, some are not my thing. Escape is in between - I like the start but not the rest. The jasmine is there from the beginning, and it suits the scent. To my nose the fruits are barely there, only as a silent whiff underneath from time to time, and it is mostly the apple that shows itself. Escape quickly becomes quite strong and flowery with a significant rose/jasmine expression. And then all of a sudden it turns into EA’s Sunflowers - the jasmine note hitting my nose so violently, somewhat cloying. I am not a fan of Sunflowers, so this is where the journey ends for me. I do not think it is enough to like the first 10-15 minutes of a fragrance and it is impossible to wash this off due to the sillage. Strong and everlasting. There is no Escape after spraying this… 48/365

Everybody know the Lancome tresor. Its bottle, liquid, smell. If you have mother, aunt, grandma grand grandma Im sure one of them or every of them loves tresor. İts similar because when I spray this to my room(I dont like much) my mom came and I asked her and she said= that was the lancome Tresor similar.

I really enjoy the scent of this fragrance. One day, a colleague of mine wore it, and at that moment, I didn’t know what it was called. I only caught a penetrating yet simultaneously delicate, floral freshness. The impression was so uplifting and different from usual that I immediately asked what fragrance it was. "Escape" was the answer.

Today while dusting, I discovered the second, still wrapped perfume box. I scolded myself for being a "scatterbrain" and opened the little box with a guilty conscience. Escape. The bottle is simple and modern - but the scent is surprisingly different.

When a consciously abstract name is chosen for a sensuous object like a perfume - Calvin Klein particularly enjoyed doing this in the 90s and was indeed quite successful - it is helpful if the scent associations connected to that name are perceived as accurate.

Anyone who consciously experienced the 90s knows it. The Calvin Klein posters in black and white. Something completely new, even provocative. Kate Moss had her breakthrough with it, and who didn’t enjoy looking at the sculpted body of Mark Wahlberg. The 90s were characterized by Calvin Klein underwear but also by Calvin Klein perfume.

This was gifted to me and I'm so very happy with it! The opening is so glorious, bright and green in an enchanting way! Then the oakmoss comes through, I then fear the bitterness, but with Azuree, it is balanced out by the herbal and green, fresh notes. That bitterness is still there, but I've learned to perceive it as 'the grounding of the scent'. In the following stage, I do get why some people find her reminiscent of Jean-Louis Scherrer Eau de Toilette , but this lady Azurée is far more complex, deeper and less linear. Also less yellow, I think. In the sillage I get something 'clean' (not soapy!) which makes me think the vetiver may be the Haitian kind of vetiver, but I don't know. Longevity and sillage are great, but olfactory fatigue is lurking when oversprayed, I really smell this chypre best when used light handed. It's a lovely fresh and beautyful, intriguing scent for spring and summer! The more I wear this, the more I love it.

It was the same ritual every morning. The alarm clock rang early, and she stepped to the window, opening it wide. She loved this early hour. There was still a light mist over the meadows, and a slightly fresh breeze was blowing. She quickly got ready and went down the stairs. Her first stop was always the kitchen. Peeling lemon zest and adding it along with some herbs to fresh mineral water. Lightly chilled, it made a wonderfully aromatic summer drink. Everyone could help themselves to it throughout the day. Then out into the garden. The earth under her feet was already a bit sun-warmed, but still a tad moist. Passing by the small colorful flower bed, where there was almost more greenery than roses visible. Her destination was the old hammock, whose green fabric had become a bit rough over time, and the wide leather lacing had almost grown into the tree trunks. She always found this place pleasantly rustic. A finely delicate bitter, spicy scent emanated from the herbs she would soon pick. But first, she settled into the hammock, let her feet dangle, and enjoyed the feeling of the soft, subtly spicy moss brushing against her as she gently swayed. Here, she took her time, relished the sweet idleness, and recharged her energy. Warm, soft, and golden, the sun's rays diffused through the spicy foliage, melting in the cool shade, causing a few small, bright resin droplets on the branches to shimmer gently. Slowly, she stood up, cut the slightly bitter herbs, and walked back to the house with a smile along the sunny path.

At the bottom of the pool, sun spirits dance as I glide weightlessly through the water. They shimmer around my limbs, just like the afternoon heat will later, when it melts the water droplets on my warm skin. Above me, dried leaves and dirt have gathered. Surely, a few of them will get caught in my hair when I surface. She says the pool is dirty. A filthy puddle. But what does she know about dirt? All night, the crickets have chirped on the sand-colored stones, in the nooks of the house with the azure shutters, and even in the vines on the unplastered walls. The mugwort stands half-dried in full bloom, and the lemons hang so ripe on the branches of the frail trees that I wonder when they will touch the ground, where lush moss thrives. It is this spot where the earth still remembers the past rain, where I have dug my fingers into the moist warmth, where the shoe with the leather straps and high cork sole still lies. She probably doesn’t even know where the other one has disappeared to. Yet she never tires of admonishing me that I mustn’t stumble carelessly in high heels. When I surface from the pool, I will go to her, withstand her stern gaze while she pretends not to look at me, and her eyes will wander from the golden fuzz on the scar on my belly to the chipped nail polish on my toes. Even when the wind rustles in the lemon trees, it won’t puff out the flowers on her fully buttoned blouse, and yet she has taken my diary, follows my traces in the house even at night, and mostly with her clattering fingers on the keyboard. She follows the unmistakable sounds to this brittle leather couch and later, much later, to the headlights on the stone path. Once, she was me and I was her. Because we condition each other. ** Somehow it’s a pity that François Ozon’s “Swimming Pool” always comes to mind when I wear Azuree, even though Jacques Deray’s “La Piscine” from 1969 happens to be from the same year as the fragrance. But unfortunately, the older film hasn’t left a lasting impression on me, whereas I find Azuree’s contradictory facets without much imagination in the peculiar relationship between the strict, somewhat buttoned-up Brit Sarah (Charlotte Rampling) and the carelessly lascivious Frenchwoman Julie (Ludivine Sagnier). Azuree is just like Chabochard and Aramis a herbal-spicy leather chypre by Bernard Chant, and the close relationship cannot be denied among all three fragrances. Azuree is the youngest family member and brings, alongside the chypre-typical balance of green strictness on the surface and sensual warmth behind the scenes, plenty of Mediterranean sunshine. The fragrance starts with a cool blend of bergamot and aldehydes, which soon moves towards candied lemon zest, underlaid with herbal green notes, especially mugwort. Azuree is more summery than its siblings, yet no less capricious, a bit like a radiant summer day when thunderclouds could roll in at any moment. Moreover, the fragrance thrives on its contrasts: lemon sunshine and bitter herbs, floral shimmering Hedione musk and harsh leather (perhaps Isobutyl Quinoline like in Bandit and Jolie Madame), balsamic darkness of earthy-mossy patchouli and slightly smoky-scratchy vetiver. The inner contradictions of the notes rub against each other like the controversial characters of the two women in François Ozon’s film. Yet just like Sarah and Julie, they also condition each other through their interaction, and one side could not exist without its contrasting counterpart, until they finally intertwine into an inseparable unit. The vintage version of Azuree, which I admit I only know fleetingly, is oilier, more floral, and has a more pronounced oakmoss note. Additionally, there is an iris in the heart, which I no longer perceive in the modern fragrance. Generally, in the reformulated version, citrus and herbal green notes embedded in musk prevail, heading towards a leathery Isobutyl Quinoline base with patchouli. Despite the differences, the character of the fragrance has remained intact, and I perceive none of that annoying scent ingredient (no idea what it could be, but I would be happy if someone with knowledge chimes in!), which has smoothed the edges and corners of so many classics in their modern form. Azuree proves the summer-appropriate side of leather chypre and offers exactly that little bit more that I often miss in citrus-dominated fragrances. A summer favorite. For now and forever.

I was a bit startled when I read that Azuree was being released in new packaging, but when I tested it in my perfumery, I was relieved. It still smells just as it should, only a little more floral. I can reassure all Azuree fans. Everything is still there, in the right place. Read my report on the "regular" Azuree.

Azurèe and Knowing are the two chypre perfumes that I love from the Estèe Lauder brand. I had the opportunity to test both versions: the old and the current one. The vintage scent is of course uniquely complex, rich in clear, natural oak moss and a magnificent floral bouquet. But how much of this masterpiece has been preserved in the current (newly formulated) fragrance? I find that the scent still retains its DNA. The characteristic "warm coldness" (aldehydes and oak moss) is still present. The oak moss has obviously been replaced by synthetic notes and a beautiful 'fractionated' patchouli. The perfume initially contains fewer aldehydes than the vintage version; the citrus and basil notes are still central and well balanced. After half an hour, the perfume becomes darker and warmer, it becomes denser, the green and earthy note of mugwort (which is now almost no longer used) blends with the moist and woody aspect of vetiver. The rose makes everything even more enveloping and warmer. The perfume settles on the skin with a light note of leather, patchouli, and amber (actually, it is an olfactory balance reconstructed with labdanum and woody notes). The bitter aspect, fresh and warm at the same time, the metallic facets (given by the aldehydes), the woody and green notes have remained similar. Because of all these contrasting and beautiful qualities, I like to refer to the scent as “wild elegance”. The wild DNA (which has distant echoes of the great "Bandit (1944) (Perfume) | Robert Piguet" and Cabochard (1959) Eau de Toilette ) has been dressed in elegant and refined notes. Azurèe represents an elegance that one must undress to rediscover the languorous and secret sensuality. Nowadays, no one wants to discover and explore the mysterious and hidden aspects of personalities anymore, but rather settle for a sad and inauthentic surface. Who can still use Azurèe today? Only those who loved the old scent and find in the new version the core that has remained unchanged, albeit with less magic. A heartfelt thank you goes to the two wonderful people who brought this masterpiece to my attention. Thank you Tabla and Cappuccetto from a lover of true chypre fragrances.

Grace Kelly and Sophia Loren refresh themselves after a hot sailing day in the Aegean at a small bar with a sea view. A large holm oak provides dry shade, and the evening twilight settles over the sky with a gentle breeze. The heat of the day rises from the stone wall, the maquis exhales, infusing the evening atmosphere with its spicy herbal scent.

in theory, it should be love at first sight (smell) - delicate and sweet freesia with incense. in practice, there is a lot of smoke, the floral notes don't go into any particular direction, definitely don't remind me of freesias, and the staying power is minimal. out of all the incense-based perfumes out there i will confidently say that la religieuse by serge lutens is more like something what i was expecting from this one and it's just superior.

In my humble opinion, this is niche quality in a designer bottle. Kenzo and Gucci are one of my favorite designer houses because they ever more than often tend to think outside the box and actually come up with something of their own instead of just copy pasting what other designer houses are doing. It's gorgeous and has so much more going on. The notes pyramid does not do it justice. It is a bit light but totally persistent, unique but also very likable. Sensual and warm, has an earthy undertone with the florals backing it up just beautifully. Smoky and leathery with slight animalistic nuances just to make it interesting enough to keep sniffing it, it's an addictive type of scent. Semi-sweet with a little freshness. The smoke is just done very right here, just the right amount. It's balanced and of good quality. Performance is decent. To make it even more interesting, I had women test it and they all said it is on the masculine side but when I had the guys test it almost all of them told me that it leans more feminine. Which makes this fragrance completely UNISEX just based on the reaction I've seen so far. Brilliant release by the house of Kenzo, bravo.

Great masculine fragrance that's clean and fresh. Would work as a quick grab fragrance that leans a little more formal, especially for a little warmer weather. Utility and versatility are very good, similar to Explorer and Platinum Explorer - nice scent that most everyone will like, useful any day, any time. The reason I don't like it is the dismal performance for me. After about 1 to 2 hours, it was only a very weak skin scent. Tested from a sample and won't be buying a FB.

It starts fairly interesting; masculine, fresh, green apple. There is also a modernized lavender fougere accord. Afterwards it develops into a basic masculine scent, something you'd find in a shower gel or a deodorant. It's pleasant, but uninspiring. Longevity is fine, but it has zero projection. On me it was a skin scent for the whole 7 hours. Yes, it's cheap and it could be an easy reach perfume, but I still think there are better options out there.

A pleasing green and fresh scent. A good combination of classic (it reminds me of some older perfumes, but I can't remember which ones) and modern, wearable in practically any situation. The apple, although a bit synthetic, is a pleasant surprise. It's fair to call it EDP for CK standards, but yes, it doesn't last very long. Thankfully, it's cheap :)

...I thought to myself when the last attempts with the well-known label went thoroughly wrong. The fragrances themselves were never the problem. Sure, they were mostly not scent milestones, but still wearable (albeit quite synthetic) perfumes. Much worse was actually always the issue of longevity. Hardly inhaled, they were already gone. Therefore, I took a break from CK fragrances for a long time. However, I must admit (yes, I confess - Shame on me) that a bargain caught my attention again. The quite well-rated CK Eternity EdP for 25 euros/100ml? I just had to grab it. Said and done, I unpacked the perfume without too many expectations, applied it, and Boom! What is this??? A fresh-green (and not very synthetic) lavender/apple bomb hits me. What a beautiful opening Eternity EdP has. Great, I thought. Did I really spray a "Klein"? Indeed. My goodness, this perfume has an incredibly lovely sweet-green character! Now I must confess that despite my biblical age (47), I know the original Eternity only from a distant memory. So I won't make any comparisons in this regard. The sillage is impressive. Finally, something green to show off, and you don't smell directly like a forest. I couldn't detect a significant scent development during the 8 hours of longevity, and I find that EXACTLY right. Because just as the scent starts, that's how I want it to be. I don't perceive any leather (thankfully), at best a minimal earthy note that comes from the vetiver. A well-groomed soapiness with a fine watery fresh note cannot be denied in Eternity either. I am thus completely thrilled, and Calvin has not disappointed me this time. Even though I have only been using the fragrance for 5 days, I attest it full summer suitability. That's how you want to smell on a walk. Eternity will surely find its use on many mild days in spring/autumn as well. Now I am actually also interested in one or two flankers of Eternity. If there is a similar scent DNA present, I am not averse. Total successful blind buy, I am happy and not so grumpy about Mr. Klein anymore ;) Have a fragrant day :)

Calvin Klein Eternity for men EdP is significantly better and more intense than the previously available Edt. That’s the bottom line. Why? Fresher, greener, and above all, better longevity and projection. In my opinion, the scent doesn’t really develop; it doesn’t need to. The dominant ingredients are cypress, sage, lavender, and suede. One immediately associates it with forests, nature, herbs, trees, etc. Vetiver is the only note that joins later, in my opinion, adding another burst of freshness to the perfume. Eternity for men EdP can actually be worn in any season and for any occasion. However, it is particularly suitable for autumn and outdoor occasions in the fresh air. Calvin Klein has not chosen Jake Gyllenhaal as the model for the fragrance without reason and appropriately. Longevity and sillage are great for a green, fresh scent, around 6-8 hours of good projection. Thus, the price is also right, as is usual with Calvin Klein fragrances.

A blast of sage from the very first second - fresh, aromatic, spicy, slightly edgy, wild. When briefly sniffing, there’s also a scent connection to (unripe) apple, but for me, the sage clearly stands out. And I love it. One of my top 3 kitchen herbs. But I digress.

After some research and a good offer, I decided to go for it and got myself a bottle. In hindsight, I can say: Good decision! An authentic, green spring fragrance that always brings a smile to my face when I catch a whiff of it. The apple is well embedded in the ozonic notes and, together with various herbs, makes up the top note.

Here I must break a lance - Eternity for Men Eau de Parfum is truly a good fougere and that at a really excellent price point. Lavender and sage are well represented, and vetiver is nicely woven in. The additional addition of ozonic notes and green apple gives this fougere a modern, fresh twist.

... my little herb garden. The scent of sage and other spices rises to my nose. From the garden come the fragrances of the blooming plants. When spraying this fragrance, the first thing that hits the nose is herbal notes. This is followed by a green apple. Soon a floral note and spices join in. In the end, leather and wood come together.

Eternity starts citrusy and zesty with a shower-freshness. Synthetic water and ozone notes provide a refreshing lightness. The equally artificial apple forms the top of the fragrance with indeterminate herbs. This feels somewhat overloaded and unclear. The warm spice wood base also remains vague and offers no balance.

I've never really been a fan of Estee Lauder fragrances, I always found them to smell slightly odd to my nose, however Intuition surprised me to say the least. I really enjoyed the citrusy opening which was refreshing and instantly reminded me of Summer. I just loved the way the lemon, grapefruit and bergamot blended so well together creating a scent that was sweet and lively. Unfortunately it is scents with these citrusy openings that never blend well with my skin chemistry, and sure enough this beautiful scent turned to rotten grapefruit when I wore it. Despite the fact that this fragrance and I are not meant to be, I still admire this scent when worn by other people. The heart of Intuition becomes a soft and somewhat powdery floral blend, which is absolutely gorgeous. The rose note is an absolute standout and it gives this fragrance that classy, feminine touch. I'll also agree with the other reviewers that sensed a vanilla note in Intuition, it is certainly present for my nose as well, particularly in the drydown. I actually adore the bottle design of Intuition, which is surprising because I very rarely pay attention to a fragrance's packaging. The oval shaped bottle with the slightly off-centre, abstract cap is clearly something you would take pride in displaying on your dresser. The lasting strength was great on other people, however on myself, not only did it smell off but it also didn't last. I do urge you not to do a blind purchase on this fragrance because you may end up with the same results as me. Apart from that this fragrance is a crisp, pleasant and casual scent which I highly recommend.

Today the sun was shining. I reached for a summer scent, even though we are in the beginning of January. Intuition was just nearby so I sprayed it. I know it well. It is not the best summer scent I have, and sadly there is nothing remarkable about it. But having so many perfumes I would like to wear, test and review, I do not always go for the remarkable. And Intuition deserves a review, too. It starts out with the citric notes and the orange blossom. There is a bitter note among the sour, that makes it perfect for very hot days. Then come the flowers. I must admit, that I have not yet been able to detect Chinese Rhododendron. I have several rhododendron bushes in my garden, but they all have a quiet smell, so that must be the reason. Gardenia, Rose and Freesia I do get. The heart lasts for one to two good hours. The base is very subtle my skin - almost nonexistent. Summing up Intuition is short lived, fairly shy but has a delicious beginning. Not one of EL’s best fragrances. 180/365

When I was little, my mother wore "Je Reviens" by Worth. It is one of my earliest childhood memories to perceive that wonderful green-soapy-floral hint when she and my father went out and she gave me a kiss goodbye. Je Reviens (in the blue bottle), red, vibrant hair, and the ornate thin gold chain on her light, freckled décolletage - that was as inseparable for me as cookies at Christmas and sparrows in the cherry tree behind our house. At some point, I was sure I was already a teenager, the original Je Reviens was no longer available. My mother was inconsolable and occasionally tried other fragrances - (though with years in between, she was nowhere near as obsessed with scents as I am). Sometimes Lauder's White Linen, sometimes Chanel No5 adorned the shelf in the bathroom. Dune seemed to be a hit in 2008/09...what a wonderful scent. Unfortunately, at the end of 2009, my mother was diagnosed with an incurable illness, and during her treatments, her sense of smell changed - she could no longer tolerate Dune. She still wanted to indulge in a beautiful scent, and of course, I actively supported her in that. Shortly after the diagnosis, I gifted her a set of miniatures from Estee Lauder that had caught my eye at the airport. The choice fell on the elegant floral-woody "Intuition." A few years earlier, I had enthusiastically worn the gentle floral-woody Intuition for two bottles and somehow lost track of this scent. What does Intuition smell like? Intuition starts floral-fresh with a rather herbaceous-woody, rather than sweet tendency. I perceive a note that faintly reminds me of citrus peels. After this fresh overture, we enter a flower bed and delight in the scent of roses and gardenias. The sensual base of amber and woods clearly shines through and gives the fragrance a kind of rounded softness. true to its name, Intuition is never loud or upfront. It is (aside from its individual significance) not a cheerful "party" scent for me, but a fine, feminine, womanly-flattering fragrance that suits an elegant dinner better than a rock pub in Sachsenhausen. I recently read somewhere that the also red-haired actress Julianne Moore wears Intuition, and I think that is a "perfect match." I would classify this scent as "floriental," the sillage is pleasantly noticeable, but not overpowering. The longevity of Intuition on my skin is about eight hours. When my mother was dying in 2011, we were advised in the hospice to place a cloth with a tiny hint of my father's Eau de Toilette (he has been using the same scent for 30 years) or her own favorite scent in bed with our dying mother. Since it was quite humid at that time and we didn't want to overwhelm her with scent, we decided that it might be better for each of us to scent one wrist so she could smell a bit of it. Thus, I ended up wearing a hint of her Intuition daily for more than a week, and I still have her bottle today. Just recently, I wore Intuition for the first time again, and I believe my mother would be very pleased about it.

I really like Estee Lauder fragrances, except for the fresh laundry-scented clean lady perfumes "White Linen" and "Pleasures." Intuition is not one of those, nor is it a Chypre or an Oriental. Rather, it is a distinctive representative of a floral-woody fragrance concept, enriched with bitter green leaf notes, which is difficult to categorize within the common fragrance genealogies. We once received dwarf rhododendron bushes at the nursery where I work, whose small, rough leaves had an aromatic scent. With every touch. The fragrance somehow fascinated me. I found it irresistibly bitter, spicy, and autumnal. No other fragrant leaf plant had this "novel" aroma until now. After the green-fruity opening of "Intuition," a perfume accord very similar to the leaf scent soon appears and lingers for quite a while, enveloped by flowers like in a transparent veil. Additionally, from time to time, I can perceive sunscreen-like scents, like a hint of the past summer that still hangs in the air. Woods, as if from trees by a body of water, gently introduce the base of the fragrance. Moist, but not wet. Cool, but not chilling. At the same time, golden warm and sunny. Like autumn days, whose nights are often already very fresh, but have plenty of sunshine hours. This "Intuition" is a very interesting Lauder fragrance. Usable for many occasions, good in longevity without overwhelming sillage. However, this fragrance cannot be classified as a niche perfume; it is too "classic" and possesses a restrained elegance that is characteristic of simple yet warm and independent people. Knowing that mere masquerade is not everything, but rather a total appearance that makes this unnecessary, is much more important. This is how "Intuition" by Estee Lauder smells to me.

Today, I came across the beautiful Intuition - a lovely gift from my friend Sharon, who unfortunately is separated from me by thousands of kilometers, as she lives in New York. But geographical distance cannot affect a soul connection - as we both happily confirm time and again. The blessed emailing brings us together again, so close that we can regularly exchange thoughts - and also regularly forget about the time difference. But that doesn’t matter when emailing - at least we don’t wake each other up with phone calls at odd hours. We both excel at that, and are each surprised to hear a sleepy voice on the other end of the line. We are indeed very similar. Unfortunately, I don’t like to travel - especially not for hours - and so the dear one squeezes herself into economy class so we can spend time together. I pick her up from the airport in my sporty Corsa, and even though I drive a civilized 120 km/h, she pales at the "mad" speed and praises my "Opel Sportscar". "Welcome to good fast Germany" is always her first comment when we are on the road. Then she rummages in her bag for my "poison," which we always find amusing, as she now knows that "Gift" in German is not exactly positively connoted. She explained her choice of fragrance by saying that she considers me an intuitive person. I must return the compliment, as her fragrance gifts for me are always excellent. Intuition starts lively and fresh - one of my character traits. But it also has a dreamy, even romantic quality due to its floral notes - even tender. The woods and the warm skin accord convey closeness - without being overwhelming. Without a doubt - a sensitive fragrance. It would suit Sharon well, too. In any case, Intuition makes me want to write to her right away - no matter how late it is on the other side of the world. She will be pleased.

The scent starts with a bitter/fruity bergamot, mandarin provides fruity/juicy sweetness, grapefruit freshness. The orange blossom remains rather background for me, which I find pleasant as I often perceive it as overpowering and overshadowing other notes; a hint of green is also recognizable, I would say dark green firm leaves, perhaps from a citrus tree.

"Intuition" is floral without being too sweet, light and feminine. It reminds me of a little sister of "J'adore" - just as feminine and elegant, but much more subtle. If "J'adore" is an elegant lady admired by all, then "Intuition" is the quiet, yet very deep water.

This is a lovely "It's-raining-Saturday-afternoon-I-still-need-to-clean" scent. In the opening, it's slightly citrusy, smoothly transitioning into the delicate flowers. The freesia, which is quite a strongly scented flower, holds back gracefully here. Above all, however, lies the gentle amber-vanilla accord, which also lasts well.

....unfortunately!! That's why I liked this scent so much!! My boyfriend gave it to me for Christmas!! I was overjoyed!! A wonderful sweet floral fragrance where the vanilla also comes through beautifully. Feminine, sensual, cheeky, sexy. However, I could never smell it for more than 2 hours, then I unfortunately got a headache.

I didn't get much lemon in Kenzo Homme Sport Extreme. The opening is more like peppery mint to me. The mint is present throughout the whole development, providing freshness and a subtle sweetness. Afterwards KHSE swings between a generic lavander man aftershave, and a pleasant elemi scent embellished by a handful of saltiness on a woody base. Fortunately it approaches more and more to the later. However, it certainly would be much better if it could have sticked to the later. The sillage is moderate and the longevity is pretty good on me. It's easily detectable after 10 hours. I don't find it particularly sporty as its name suggests. It's more of an aromatic woody everyday scent.

I wasn't very impressed with Kenzo Homme, which is so highly praised here. It just seemed too medicinal to me with a balm-like scent. The fragrance here smells less like a balm, but still not good enough for a regular EDT. Only the marine notes with the well-perceived salt save the scent a bit and make it more summery. Therefore, I find the fragrance quite okay as a sport scent. And since this Kenzo is also a sport scent, it fulfills its purpose quite well, albeit with some minor flaws. The scent: The scent starts with a cool mint and pepper and has a hint of lemon in the background. All of this feels refreshing, but also somewhat too synthetic; right upon spraying, the shower gel-like character hits the nose, which is probably normal for sport scents of this type. The pepper becomes a bit stronger over time. A few minutes later, marine notes come into play, along with a pinch of salt, which, like the pepper, will become even stronger. The marine notes smell pleasantly reminiscent of a vacation by the sea, and that is the strength of this fragrance. In the base, it becomes woodier, while the vetiver is less pronounced. Additionally, it becomes sweeter. Yet until the end, the fragrance does not lose its shower gel character, which is a somewhat bothersome factor for me personally, even if this impression fades into the background towards the end. The longevity is good; the scent lasts several hours on the skin before it fades. I think it was around three to five hours. The sillage is also good, as it is quickly noticeable. Of course, the sillage diminishes soon, but that is the case with most summer fragrances. The bottle looks exactly like the regular Kenzo Homme in shape. Since I didn't have it in my hand, I don't know if it's made of glass or plastic, but it has a rather unimpressive design, at least in terms of bottles. It is gray, tall, and slightly curved with a gray, milky-transparent cap. The bamboo leaves as details look nice, though. The scent not only smells like shower gel, as mentioned, but also looks design-wise like it. Kenzo Homme Sport Extrême is not a special fragrance. I find it a bit too cheap and synthetic for a regular scent; however, as a pure sport scent, it is quite okay, as the fragrance is not unpleasant. The salty aquatic notes are good and save the scent, as it smells nicely of the sea, so it could also be used well by the lake or something similar. As a sunny vacation scent, I find this Kenzo okay. Fans of Kenzo in general can take a sniff, but everyone else has nothing to lose by ignoring it; however, I would recommend testing it because of the marine notes. A bit cheaper and a little less shower gel-like, and it would have been even better. Rating: 60%

After the high-quality, albeit rather conventional sports scent, now comes the extreme variant. Everything is included - many good fragrances have been worsened this way. Kenzo, on the other hand, has taken the opportunity to give the original more sophistication. The difference when smelling both side by side is enormous - leaning towards more depth and refinement. The top note already presents a subtly sweet, almost gourmand character, without ever being intrusive. Citrus, peach, and aldehydes come together in a delightful harmony. The algae set the tone, yet they are almost playfully surrounded. After some time, the absolute treat arrives, namely a peppery spiciness. This makes the fragrance noticeably more robust than the Bois?. Towards the end, it becomes beautifully powdery, with a very modestly dosed hint of patchouli and benzoin. The overall effect of the fragrance is that of a true gentleman, unmistakably masculine. It is rather understated-fresh in nature, not overpowering, yet it radiates warmth. For men who enjoy "Pour Monsieur" or "Eau Sauvage" but desire a modern variant, this is highly recommended.

A mercurial scent. It is easy to fall in & out of love with this fragrance...indeed it is one scent that has you flik-flakking around with ambiguous feelings. What I do know is that I find myself reaching for this scent more often than other more entrancing beauties. The most pronounced notes are cedar, a pseudo-vanilla-lily & musk, all touched by vetiver but the entrance is a light & sour citrus. The overall feel of the scent is at once veiled & volumous & yet watery, translucent & like a sighing breeze in a silent green forest. The peony & bamboo combined with the honeyed clover make the magic here - green & watery without being crisp. The woodsy notes save this scent from becoming too sweet or high - here is an elegant, classic perfume that will grace your skin with a smooth, long lasting dry-down. Yes, it is soft...but this scent has power! It is light in nature, but thick & heavy in powder-weight. The powder here is never dry & dusty, but creamy, rich & heady laced with silky florals & warm musk. Why they are discontinuing this perfume is puzzling to me...Truth has much more of a voice, greater lasting power & suitable sillage than many of CKs more recent offerings. Snap it up before it goes!

Truth was a blind buy for me, found it really cheap online. Actually, you can rarely go wrong with 90-ies/beginning of 2000 perfumes (maybe, for those older among us). Especially, when 3 great perfumers worked on it! And - my search for the perfect green and fresh cut grass in perfume is over! Too bad, the longevity is pretty poor, but who cares if you can carry the bottle around and re-apply, given its ridiculous price? Go get it, definitely.

Let’s start with scent and truth. Bamboo? Wet Woods? Silk tree flower? Seems a bit insincere from the start, I’d say. If you’re going to list ridiculous note without a trace of botanical truth, why not branch out from botany and list notes like fractiousness, regret, serenity or stasis. But I love the way Truth smells. It shows a wonderful and converging use of synthetic tones. There’s a green woody sappiness and a tart fruit/musk combination that both extends and redefines the ‘freshness’ that defines the middle of the road of designer fragrance. The result is a beautiful ambiguity without a hint of tension.

I agree that this is a green fragrance, but it is a bit more complex than that. It is all of the things that create the "green" impression - stalk, stem, young woods, wildflowers. And there is a pulpy moistness to it, like the shoots and stems are being crushed between your fingers. It is also the origin of the vegetation - wet earth, warm breezes, and early morning sun. Visualize being on a forest path dappled with light. Like a tapestry that is more than simply a collection of threads, Truth creates an experience for the wearer rather than just being a conglomeration of notes. It is not the trendsetting, airy, ozonic fragrance that many asscociate with CK. It is calm and introspective.

I have emptied a few bottles of Calvin Klein TRUTH edp, and now all that remains in my collection is a perfume mini. I am constantly toying with the idea of buying TRUTH again, although I also feel that its time in my perfume history has passed, along with the other CK frags that I frequented around the turn of the century. Yet something keeps drawing me back to TRUTH, despite the inherent paradox and pretense of a limpid liquid that seems to be the essence of purity without being water. On the one hand, TRUTH is like a beautiful Buddhist garden filled with bubbling fountains and streams. Simple, zen-like rocks have been carefully placed among minimalist green-leaved plants on grassy lawns to make it seem as though all of this were pristine, untouched nature. I smell clover and bamboo. I feel the texture of watercress, as though I were a cow grazing peacefully in a meadow all alone, while the blades and leaves dance ever so lightly about my feet in the gentle springtime breeze. On the other hand, TRUTH simultaneously evokes images of tall chrome and glass buildings with mirrored windows, such as the Hancock building in Boston. It's a colossal, imposing artifice but as beautiful as a tiny, perfect crystal.

I don't have anything in my collection that smells similar to Truth. Bitter Truth... I think the name is very apt. If you enjoy green, casual, herbal scents with zero to very little sweetness, this is definitely a quality, affordable option to try. I am intrigued and will keep testing it on myself on those days when am tired of my usual potent spicy orientals.

There is something about the white florals in many of the CKs that just doesn't agree with me. Sadly, Truth is another in a long line of CK fragrances that I like but can't wear. This time, it's the lily which is amplified on my skin, becoming cloying, sweet, & headache-y. Otherwise, Truth is a superb scent & very under-rated, imo.

Reminds me more of a unisex EdP. A sweet/sour blast hits upon initial application. It's like walking into the forest after the winter thaw and upturning logs, discovering soggy leaves that are underneath and moldy with dirt. It's musty. I know this works for many, and at times, it works for me. Is it green as others have said? Most definitely.

I must say this was an interesting and unique choice by Calvin Klein when they created this fragrance. I love that this scent is complex and forever changing from citrus, to spiciness, to freshness. From the beginning, the lemon note is very prominent and strong, with notes of patchouli and bamboo lingering in the background.

At top note Lemon then in a few minutes Cloves Mimiose a distant wisp of Vetiver Bamboo and the lovely florals of Peony and Lily comes to the picture. there is a presence of Sandalwood not overpowering but strong enogh to be noticed. but i don't smell any Blackberries.

Very few fragrances have such a qualitative difference between a light dose and a drenching. If applied heavily, Estee has the definitive “bug spray accord” that gets discussed in ‘old lady’ perfumes. I don’t deny that, and in fact I enjoy it. For the benefit of those I love, though , I wouldn’t wear Estée at this dosage unless I were home alone, with no plans to see anybody before my next shower. But with a very light hand, and probably at least ½ hour after administration for a cooling down, this is a beautiful dry, aldehydic, woody floral. At this volume, Estée has moderate sillage, excellent endurance and becomes pleasantly soapy. I know some see this as a floral chypre, and they likely have more discriminating noses than I, but I don’t get the moss. I do wonder, though, if it’s there behind the long-lasting aldehyde in Estée and I just can’t see it. With this quality and concentration (Pure Fragrance Spray, huh? Never understood the EL terminology.) Estée, along with Alliage , Private Collection and Azurée, represent the best-spent money in perfumery. Remarkable that this stuff is so inexpensive.

If the sound of softly blowing wind chimes could be bottled, this would be it. Aldehydes and floral notes dance together perfectly in its initial feminine, soapy opening. Once that wanes, woods and spices start shining through, as well as a syrupy sweet stickiness. After about an hour, I could faintly detect the fruity notes, which was a nice surprise. All around very natural & comforting scent. A lot of older aldehydic/chypre perfumes like this get shrugged off as 'old lady' fragrances, but I completely disagree. This one has a definite vintage vibe. It's very '70s chic in my opinion, but not in some old, reserved or stale way. Instead, I picture sunkissed and freckled skin, feathered tresses with flowered hair garlands & floppy hats. Perfect for a carefree boho/hippie vibe.

There is a smoothness and freshness to this marvellous gem from EL’s broad range of perfumes. I find this one of her best. Made in 1968 this could have been outdated as are some of the 70s’ scents. But this one has a modern, contemporary expression to it, that makes it an all times’ fragrance. It will always be ‘in’. The start gives me lots of aldehydes. This gives the scent an extraordinary freshness. Very soon the honey softness up the scent and the flowers take over, still with the freshness, but softer. In the end the base of sandalwood and musk stays on my skin for a couple of hours. The sent is great waking up to, sniffing your wrist the next morning. I have considered introducing this to my daughter. She is more into floral/fruities but I am sure she will appreciate it. It could be the bridge, that loads her into more complex and varied perfume-land. 83/365

It's easy to get confused when trying to understand Estee Lauder's fragrance concentration terminology, so for the sake of writing this review I will make note of the fact that I am reviewing Estee Super in the EDP. I believe this is the current formulation, in a bottle as pictured above. I am really enjoying Estee, probably more than I thought I would. I may not be in this fragrance's intended age range, but that won't stop me from wearing it every now and then. I don't think I've ever met anyone that wears Estee. It's quite a distinctive, classic powdery scent with dominant notes of carnation, honey, rose and sandalwood. On the skin it smells both clean and sweet, which are two qualities I really admire. Estee does have a rather mature feel, however I wouldn't rule out its younger consumers. I am after all only twenty-two myself. The sugary honey note makes it quite versatile. Supposedly Estee was created for warm weather. For Spring, yes I certainly agree, but I unfortunately find it a little overwhelming on a hot Summer's day. The sillage packs quite a punch. It's not a fragrance for the light of heart. Estee is one of the less talked about fragrances from Estee Lauder. I wonder why that is? I believe that many disregard it as dated, however I see the fact that it has lasted more than forty years as one of its strong points. Not to mention the longevity is truly one of a kind. Expect to find Estee lingering on your skin well into the next day. Original review written: January 2013.

Given some of the negative reviews of Estee Lauder ESTEE (not only here, but elsewhere as well...), I had put off testing the bottle I acquired for fear that it would prove to be another reformulated JE REVIENS-type experience. In fact, all my fears were for naught. ESTEE is another floral aldehyde in the EL line-up, a sibling to WHITE LINEN, not a purely floral perfume. ESTEE also inhabits the same general olfactory neighborhood as CALANDRE, which I tested earlier today and was not really very excited about (though I should say that I may have been sniffing an inferior reformulation... on ne sait jamais ces jours-la!). On comparing these three fragrances, I find that I actually prefer ESTEE's brightness, clarity, crispness, and general cleanness. However, I should also warn prospective sniffers that the first ten seconds or so are rather sour and off-putting. Fortunately, things improve significantly after that. I can see, though, how some people would be immediately turned off by the opening. I also do not understand how anyone can claim to have tested this perfume if they've never let it mingle with and develop on their skin. ESTEE is an excellent example of how a perfume "on paper" and "on skin" will be two very different things about which very different evaluations are bound to be made, even by the same perfumista, it seems to me. I definitely recommend ESTEE for those who are mourning the discontinuation of CALANDRE. In fact, I think that ESTEE is better than CALANDRE, except for the first ten seconds. Needless to say, only aldehyde lovers need apply!

Opens with definite citrus and ALDEHYDES, my love and hate, mostly hate, though I am able to appreciate them sometimes. Yay, metal and pee. I get sandalwood and rose when I hit the drydown after about 10 mins, but very little sticky sweet honey. I thought at first there was cinnamon in it because I smelled warm spice and sweetness.

She had received the certificate of inheritance weeks ago. It had taken a very long time for her to be located. Now the lawyer had handed her the keys. During the drive to the house, she was lost in thought. Dorothea. She had never heard that name from her mother, and until the inheritance notification, she hadn’t known she had an aunt.

I encountered Estee Super around 1970 and have remained loyal to it, of course with a few flings, until today. Yes, it is floral, but completely without heaviness and sultriness. It also lacks the playful-romantic quality that often characterizes this fragrance group.
Estée Lauder (1908-2004) was one of the great American pioneers who showed women that caring for themselves, applying makeup, or wearing perfume is nothing to be ashamed of; on the contrary.

Who doesn’t remember the opening of the popular sixties "Space" series, where it said: "Space.....the final frontier. We are in the year......(1968) and the spaceship zoomed through black holes and vast fields of stars. So infinite, only in fragrance form, comes the perfume "Estee," which used to have the addition "Super." I mean the old one, in the ribbed bottle.

The scent of blueberry: Incredibly fruity and slightly sweet. Clearly invigorating in effect. Black currant or the flower of the black currant has an intensely fruity, tart note that provides freshness and clarity. Black currant refreshes and creates a clear mind, thereby strengthening the body. All parts of the black currant plant are aromatic (the stem, the leaves, the buds, the berries). The outstanding scent of black currants and flower buds comes from the trichomes, a substance that conveys an aroma reminiscent of a cat's urine alongside the fruity facets. Some can smell it, others cannot. Luckily, I am spared from this. Now the violet. In the language of flowers, the violet is considered modest and humble. The substance that gives the flower its distinctive scent is called Jonone. Violet scent has a light, clear sweetness that evokes an impression of floral purity, innocence, and freshness. In aromatherapy, violet is used to reduce aggression. Restless sleep is said to be improved by the bright, cheerful scent. Inner balance is strengthened, and the effects of shock are softened. The gentle, harmonious violet scent also helps with fears and emotional disturbances. It calms and opens the mind to new things. All these components make Couleur Kenzo Violet a fruity - not overly sweet - cocktail that comes across as slightly creamy, refreshing, and radiating good vibes. A lovely scent and - regardless of whether it's winter or summer - wearable in every season. Longevity is rather low - about 4-5 hours. But you can always reapply :-)

I’ve really enjoyed chypre fragrances for a while and I have Cristalle to thank. When I first smelled Cristalle (many years ago before I really became a perfume hobbyist) I didn’t really know anything about categories of fragrances or what made them what they were. It was 1982 and I was in college. I wore Antaeus, Kouros, No 5, and Je Reviens. Powerhouse men’s 80s and lady-like floral aldehydes. When I tried Cristalle at some department store or other, I had no idea what to make of it. It’s as if this had dropped in from space. I can’t say I loved it, but it marked me. When I smelled it again many years later I found it simply gorgeous. It smelled just as it had the first time, but I had changed. I was ready for it. It is pristine. I know some find it off-putting (even many who like it) but I find it has just the right timbre, the perfect inflection. It is an odd, spare chord and might not be particularly harmonious in a feel-good, symphonic sense but it has a perfect tonality. My only difficulty with it (as with both No 19 edt and Pour Monsieur) is that it just doesn’t last for me. It has just a fraction more lasting power than an eau de cologne. Despite this, I love its evolution over time. It starts green, strong, astringent and then has a fairly quick transition to a mossy, melon-like floral like nothing else I’ve smelled. From this point it just sort of blows away, becoming a ghost of itself, but, for an hour or so, a recognizable one.

This fragrance, whilst being a classic, is certainly (not) for everyone! What hits me upon initial impression is the bitterness of it all.
