"This damn poverty. We are scraping together the last remnants from the iron reserves, nothing can go wrong and we are also running out of time. Damn. Endless pressure, my eyes are watering, my hands are shaking, and my hearing sometimes fails me.

Misia wafted friendship and the wind into my home... and of course, she was welcomed with beaming eyes and an open nose. Misia! Without fixating on the name, without prejudice, just with the greatest curiosity rubbed under my nose.... and? For me, an absolute dream! I won't linger long on the top note; the heart note immediately transitions into the deep, seductive base!

But I don't care. I often find the lost treasures particularly interesting.. Eau de Fleur de Yuzu is also a random find on eBay and I like to wear it in the warmer months. There is no progression, and apparently the scent is meant to be monothematic. Allegedly, Yuzu and grapefruit are supposed to smell quite similar. However, I don't find any grapefruit here, like my predecessor. The citrus scent is very soft and gentle, not a trace of sourness or sharpness. Rather layered with something floral, it could be violets, but very transparent, not as powdery as is often the case in violet fragrances. Very pleasant. And it stays like this for about 3 hours. If I spray heavily, there is a bit of sillage, but it doesn't last longer because of that either. That's about it. The concentration is apparently EDT, but most of my colognes last longer. Eau de Fleur de Yuzu is a feel-good scent for errands that are really annoying. Dentist visits, trips to the authorities, everything that is really tedious, because this gentle veil of scent has an incredibly positive effect. Therefore, I forgive it for its short longevity. I'm not surprised that Eau de Fleur de Yuzu couldn't hold its own in the market. There is simply too little happening here. I also don't think I would have bought the scent regularly in a store. The Kenzo fragrances are priced in the average designer range. Even though Eau de Fleur de Yuzu is really nice, I wouldn't value it at (estimated) €40, because it is too simple and too short-lived. But as a cheap random find, it brings me joy. Finding unknown fragrances from (partially) well-known brands is always particularly fun for me. Maybe because you always associate something specific with the brands and are often surprised.

Offended by the duty-free shop, I set off to the local perfumery. null of what I wanted was available at the airport. So I had to grab something, anything. I know, frustration purchases are not a good idea. With my nose completely scent-blind, I stumbled upon this Kenzo fragrance and just took it with me. After a strong inhalation of coffee, I revisited this little water, yes, little water. And since I had a bad night's sleep, I had time for experiments. Eau de Fleur de Yuzu starts citrusy, fresh with a slight sweetness. Grapefruit smells different to me, but there is definitely a citrus fruit in play. I think it's more likely the yuzu fruit. As the scent develops, the yuzu blossom gradually takes the lead. It is warm, sweet, and soft. This is a satisfying fragrance that fits well in autumn, as it doesn't have that sour freshness of grapefruit. Apparently, the fragrance has no base. Maybe that's why it disappears so quickly, because it's missing a third?! In the middle of the night, I had a brainwave. Since only vetiver shows up in Ninfeo Mio in cold weather (at least for me), I dared to layer the two together. Here, the yuzu water earns a point from me. Ninfeo Mio has become significantly more feminine, and yuzu has gained in longevity.

I am quite surprised... In the Estee Lauder test fever :) no familiar Goddess DNA in the opening, even a bit piercing (Ambrox), extremely rare for Lauder, and now comes the point where I really get curious and think... somehow this feels familiar. I actually have fragments of Neroli Portofino and Mugler's Feminity here. Citrusy bitter fig, neroli, and bergamot. Once this brief Ambrox opening is over, it actually has something interesting. People who have always steered clear of the brand and like fragrances such as Neroli Portofino, Womanity, or even Desigual might enjoy this scent. In the dry down, however, we have the soft coconut milk with fig nectar again. So it definitely has a twist!

I imagine this in my mind's eye, informed by the nose through sniffing this fragrance, as follows: Blooming lemon and orange trees bearing fruit at the same time, some fig trees scattered in between, at the edge of the grove pines and cedars, and above all, a bright blue sky adorned with small, white clouds! Dreams of the South? Definitely! But the "South" also exists in bottles with fragrant contents! Sniffing it, in turn, creates the "dream of the South".... The circle closes again! The fragrance itself is not "blue" at all! Rather, it begins quite bright "lemon yellow," to gain first impressions. Slowly, like in slow motion, this "perfume color" transitions into increasingly orange tones, as mandarins and orange blossoms join in. The sweetness of the blossoms and the fine fruity acidity complement each other fabulously and have a warm-inviting radiance. When subtle fig scent and woody notes (certainly pines and cedars) are added, it results in a light brown wood tone with fine green specks. This also leads to a slightly bluish background (more turquoise, as green and yellow tones come together) But the main contribution to the blue impression is owed to the sky above! It bathes everything in this "southern light" :-))

I don't need to tell you what everyone knows about the summer of 2020. No flights to the azure coasts of this world! Curfews, contact bans, hotel and restaurant bankruptcies, shutdowns. News after news, questions after questions - an annoying, unavoidable pastime. So I’ll just bring the coasts of southern France home! It works out semi-well. My apartment already looks a bit like the Côte d'Azur. Unfortunately, I'm in Hamburg and the pollen are already a bit annoying at the end of April. At least there's sunshine. I spray this new summer number from Lauder on my skin on Sunday morning and head to the balcony with fresh orange juice. He is wonderful. The scent has less to do with the 2019 “Fraiche” version. Rather more with Tom Ford's Neroli Portofino. Well, we already have so many of those out there, right? Wait. The appearance is deceiving. Yes, Neroli is present, but the bitter orange paired with a load of chemical lemon makes a statement first, then pauses for the introduction to the Neroli/fig cream outcry! Exciting! What a combination. It can be done like this, but it's not good enough for a straight grade “1.” More like a “2.” I immediately think of Via Camerelle EdT from Carthusia. The Italians somehow do it better. More natural, citrusy, and also creamier. But I don't want to complain or advertise. Lauder is, after all, less niche-oriented. It should appeal to the broad masses. The price is neither Tom Ford (also Lauder Group), niche, nor drugstore. Bronze Goddess 2020 in azure turquoise tones then. What could that mean? Neroli / Bitter Orange / Flowers / Fig Milk / Sunscreen / Maritime Wind. For me, the azure is definitely girlish. There’s a bit of pink and rose in there too. Great bottle and nice longevity. Orangey and really quite turquoise creamy. Someone in the lab must have said I want the 2020 scent flanker to really smell turquoise! A slight sea note comes through. So left fresh and right creamy. I got it. Musk, cedar, and coconut are just side characters. It radiates about an arm's length away and quickly becomes body-close. Something in me also thinks of Mugler Cologne and suddenly it becomes clear to me that it does have the DNA of Eau Fraiche 2018 and 2019. Unfortunately, not as good in my eyes. But I don't want to be too strict; it’s good, but suffers somewhere from an overload of note congestion and transitional problems from fresh to creamy woody. Plus, there’s always that slightly cheap-sounding chemical club. I’m being a bit too critical now, but I can still recommend it for summer 2020. Maybe I’m just a bit dizzy in the head from all the fresh disinfectant. I smell like toilet cleaner every day. The Lauder scent is really good enough for this sad pandemic as well as beyond that, and it still surpasses most 4711 colognes from drugstores around the world. The best affordable alternative to it is even the 4711 - Remix Cologne - 225 years. There’s a lot of similarity, except for those turquoise fig milk notes. Fine. As soon as the first flight goes, I hope to be back in Nice. Whether I’ll take this scent with me, I don’t know yet; there are simply better alternatives to a still well-made Bronze Goddess flanker. I can still forgive that one heavy turquoise sunscreen note in the evening when I notice how beautifully it stands on the shelf next to the big “Fraiche” sister from 2019. I doubt that this limited scent will still be available in 2021. I can recommend it with a clear conscience at around €30-40 for 50ml. Stay healthy, my dears. I send you warm hugs.

Hello dear ones, my last fragrance from Lauder Bronze Goddess is from 2017. Unfortunately, it is coming to an end, just like summer. Now I am trying the new scent, and I am thrilled. Light, fresh, enchanting. Like a summer breeze. Absolutely recommend for purchase.

In my book, there are two types of enjoyable perfumes: the ones that please and the ones that excite. 31 Rue Cambon is a pleaser. It exudes both friendliness and elegance. It has a warm welcoming heart that is hard to not like. And it has quality ingredients that are engineered to perfection - resulting in a controlled performance and maximum wearability. Personally I would wear this on evenings out or on cozy casual occasions. I don't detect much development in 31RC. The pepper note is prominent in the opening, but it fits surprisingly well in the smooth slightly powdery composition. The chypre base feels very familiar and highly refined. It gives off a lovely glow-in-the-dark warmth. Mildly radiant, never too much. This whole lovable care-bear glow is also why I consider 31RC a perfume that does not excite. There is no drama here, and nothing that shocks, awes or surprises. But that is fine. Sometimes a warm heart is all you need.

First of all, I'll say that until recently I didn't really know this perfume. Until I came across someone who was selling it at a good price, I went straight in to check the notes of the perfume and saw a scent profile that I was sure I liked and I bought it blindly. And I will say that it was an excellent purchase. Floral, Chypre, green scent profile. Every time I wear it I get compliments from people even long hours after I wore it and that just shows how great this perfume performs. Iris, ylang ylang, green notes that lighten the combination, bergamot and more that take this perfume and make it versatile for all seasons. 9/10.

A stunning perfume from Chanel. I remember the first time I tried it in Vienna, it blew me away, a really beautiful perfume. After trying almost 800 perfumes it’s really hard to impress me but 31Rue Cambon did it. This is a perfume of iris, ylang-ylang, aldehyde and amber. The iris is very prominent in the opening. I can fell the amber, but it is very very subtle and present. In the drydown it is powdery, honeyed, you can feel patchouli and a little bit of woody notes. 31 Rue Cambon is a fresh oriental chypre perfume. Very French, luxurious and elegant. Longevity over 15 hours, the projection is really great, it definitely fills the room.

This one took me by surprise, its amazing but i tried to wear it and its too feminine and grand for me, i felt too uncomfortable and out of my element when i wear this. Now to the scent, its very complex and has 3 phases: 1st one is the peppery green citrus blast in the opening, its refreshing and provides a contrast to what is later to come. After that comes 2nd phase, a powdery grand floral mid, it has a funky indolic smell to it, but never goes full animalic. But the funk is there for sure. 3rd phase is the resinous labdanum patchouli combo, also slightly funky and dirty. This fragrance doesnt have oakmoss, but it has that chypre contrast feeling to it for sure. Along with Antaeus and Cristalle, these are the best Chanels chypre offerings you can get.

To me this screams urban summer - great for the office, great for wearing on a weekend strolling around the city, when a different perfume would be simply too much in high temperatures; great for mornings and evenings alike. It's fresh, it's just a bit green and just a bit flowery, it's perfect. I fell in love with it!

Yes, I know, Adenauer is said to have said that. But don't we all feel that way from time to time? I have caught myself today - 5 years later - no longer standing by my statement about 31 Rue Cambon EdP. However, since there are agreeing responses underneath, I won't delete it. After all, it was my impression at the time.

Hesperidic at the start, floral in the heart, spicy, vetiver woody and earthy in the base. Perfumes with these scent notes are recommended for business meetings where a woman must be confidently persuasive. It does not smell too feminine, but can assert itself in the still male-dominated leadership levels. It radiates self-assured and strong sovereignty.

Today, one would say Coco Chanel was a "Guest in Residence" at the Ritz Hotel in Paris. She lived here for many years, experiencing her numerous affairs, including with the musician Igor Stravinsky. His wife and four children lived in their house outside the city, which she had bought for herself and her tragically deceased great love Boy Capel.

What remains of the spirit of Chanel today? Perhaps the aesthetic and stylistic canon has changed somewhat, but there are fragrances like 31 rue cambon that have remained deeply faithful to a French, unchanging, and luxurious style. I dare say that in the grand and pompous era of Chanel By Lagerfeld, 31 Rue Cambon represents the DNA of Chanel even more than Chanel N 5.

This wonderful perfume is described by Chanel as "the refuge of Gabrielle Chanel in the heart of Paris." The address must have been extraordinarily beautiful to inspire such a fragrance and to be named after it. Unfortunately, I have never been there. As is well known, 31 Rue Cambon is a chypre of the finest kind.

I wore the perfume almost daily for quite some time and was a fan of the fresh scent, which makes it very suitable for spring and summer. Highly recommended as an everyday perfume, even though it is difficult to find at an acceptable price. Main accords are fruity, white flowers, citrusy, fresh, tropical, aquatic, floral, sweet, musky, and woody.

Pure White Linen Light Breeze is the perfect scent for hot Summer days. It's the scent equivalent to a chilled glass of sparkling, fizzy soda water. Estee Lauder seems to have a knack for summery scents. They are all incredibly pleasant and easy to wear. Pure White Linen Light Breeze is no exception. Thankfully there is quite a difference between this flanker and the original White Linen. It's quite a crisp and fresh scent, with a huge emphasis on green citrus. Fortunately, this is a citrus scent I can wear, as the grapefruit note is less sharp and sour than it is in other fragrance compositions. If a bottle ever happened to fall into my hands, I would wear it every now and then, but I doubt that I would ever buy myself a bottle. It's a nice fragrance, but sometimes 'nice' is just not enough. I tend to grow tired of smelling it over a short period of time. Pure White Linen Light Breeze is most appealing when applied after a morning shower or when used as a 'pick me up' after a long, strenuous day. I also wouldn't shy from wearing this fragrance to the gym or to the beach. Inoffensive, delicate and refreshing are three words that sum up Pure White Linen Light Breeze. I believe that it is fairly well-received, if not a big seller during the Summer months. The longevity is fairly impressive and the sillage is moderate. Original review written: October 2012.

I like this fresh, citrusy scent even though it's not terribly unique. It's sort of like a cross between Dior Addict 2 and Versace Versense. Surprisingly long lasting - no easy feat for a citrus based scent

*English translation* It may be that these linen clothes were white at some point, but at the moment they certainly are not. This garment smells like it has been worn for 3 days at the medieval market in Tuntenhausen near Bad Aibling. However, and this is a big plus, it smells completely authentic. Water and soap have never seen this fabric. The animalistic, dirty, no, filthy sweetness suggests the consumption of several barrels of mead by its wearer the night before; forwards and backwards. Thank you, friend Hasi, you have made me a HUGE joy with this!

I love this one, not really a bestseller but if you like creamy perfume than go for it. This starts very planty, and very soft all i smell is a plant and gras, full of gras field, but later it gets more creamy super creamy like a mix of vanilla with lavender Not bat al all. At the start you could say that this is a super unisex, but later i dont know gets more feminine, What do you think?? Let me know in the comments.

Jersey, a bone of contention between Great Britain and French Britain. Due to its location on the mild Gulf Stream of the English Channel, it is unusually English sunny here, lush vegetation thrives splendidly, and light-shy tax rates are kept low. The fragrance at hand is also a bone of contention. One person's high spirits are another's mediocre indifference. The former dislikes criticism. Justifiably, certainly. But the anonymous makes use of the discreet suppression of disturbing scent sensations, so that only hymns of green synthetic dominate the picture. Well, true Bretons are considered rebellious and sometimes defend their views rather harshly. I will rather strengthen myself with a delicious Far Breton to shed light on the mild breeze of the Channel Island. Les Exclusifs by Chanel were real eye-catchers in their original EdT versions starting in 2007, with Jersey added in 2011. For whatever reason, starting in 2016, the overpowering EdP version had to take over the island. Enough of the backstory, tea is served! Sizzle! Boy, it gets deep green here. Even on Jersey, there are not just sea burials; landlubbers can also find their final rest amidst "ivy". Well, the living can play hide and seek in the boxwood labyrinth, or perhaps rather scare each other in the thuja maze. Like father, like son. Polge Junior colors Scotland's capital similarly morbid green. Paris - Édimbourg is thematically consistent, while Papa Polge builds a Victorian theme park on the Channel Island. Barely does the green note whisper softly in my ear to pre-order my coffin in time, when a lively lavender comes along and slaps me awake from my morbid slumber. Whack, whack! Together with the jasmine, the two flowers exude such a rigid attitude that even concrete walls appear soft as butter. Goodness gracious, the island is not under the crown for nothing! Now, let's tease the tea drinkers: in the Dépendance de la Couronne, one should descend deep into the cellar to laugh. Best without a lamp and with enough gall to not disturb the moralistic maggots. What kind of accord is this? Between the sour death green, the stiff lavender in the tradition of a Yardley house, and the Rottweiler jasmine, even my own breathing sounds almost like a bomb in the catacombs! Best to stay completely still, as even the slightest clink of the porcelain cup could bring down the Wedgwood dynasty! So, insularly, something sweet is naturally served in the oh so joyful tea round. Just no barbaric hand movements; the strange rose in the vase could look even stranger! Sleeping dogs should not be awakened… A brief reminder of the Far Breton, which served as a template for the English plum pudding. And something Anglican is now being served, albeit with a tonka bean filling instead of plum. One should stoically gulp down the oh so refreshingly delicious something, but with class. Meanwhile, the first lavender sweat bead rolls down my temple. Plop, bomb in the middle of the teacup! (I know, one probably shouldn't say "ass," so here's a gentler expression with local color.) The milk curdles instantly, but one should not let it show. The rose in the vase has, of course, not missed the faux pas, and she looks really strange, her twisted gaze suggests nothing good. So quickly, an After Eight into the mouth of the noblewoman; the chocolate mint should save the mood for a few moments. (Chocolate patchouli with a bit of menthol is likely also involved here.) It is not proper to bring up inappropriate topics. Complimentary remarks about the neatly trimmed lawn, praising the indentation of an Oscar Wilde in his time, and delightfully dissecting the failed dress code from last Sunday in church are allowed. And now the true Victorian proves himself! For amidst all the thumb screws, maintaining composure and wit borders on a miracle! From the base, a synthetic, dark note gently pulses, lightly woody ambrosial for connoisseurs of the matter. But just a hint of it. Enough pretext to say goodbye in time. But, oh what a wonder, a drizzle of vanilla will accompany the tormented guest over hill and dale. And while one ironically smiles on Jersey, the Bretons on the other side of the channel enjoy very sumptuous moments. So long Jersey! Before I forget, to musically illustrate the scent on the coast of the island, I recommend the life-affirming song by Morrissey "Everyday is like Sunday". Enjoy!

Years ago, I almost loved Jaques Polge because he said that women over 50 are the most interesting. Aha, you French rascal, because you probably don’t have to put in any effort with them anymore? I don’t love you anymore! Jersey is such a snooze scent that you probably designed in bed, with a tablet on your lap. In Jersey bed linen. Flannel pajamas and felt slippers in front of the bed. Next to you lies no exciting woman 50+. Cultivated boredom, so to speak. With the emphasis on “cultivated.” I had to really struggle to put my thoughts into words, as I kept dozing off. That must be the lavender, which is anyway a sleep inducer. Jaques, who sent you the briefing? Where’s the grass? You might have smoked some. Maybe then you would have remembered the amazing scents you used to create. I’m dozing off again and counting flannel sheep. They are kind of cute too. They nibble on a few flowers here and there in the meadow. I can’t dream of anything more here. Polite, well-behaved, unremarkable. Jersey has fallen without making an impression. Nothing more! The end!

In 1913, Coco Chanel opened a hat and accessory boutique. She had long noticed that women even walked on the beach wearing hats and tightly laced corsets, as if they were in the city. Therefore, Chanel designed sporty fashion for herself and her friends, which caused some surprised looks on the streets. Chanel had tapped into the spirit of the times. Her fashion, with its own simple, natural elegance, was in high demand among the elite. People admired, inquired, and bought. What matters to Chanel are straightforwardness, comfort, natural freedom of movement - and at the same time the desire to seduce, as some texts about Chanel say. This made her a trendsetter: at a time when only the foot was seen through clothing, her skirts left the ankle exposed. She cut her hair, deliberately exposed her face to the sun, and wore trousers - revolutionary to scandalous for that time. Neither corset nor whalebone constricted the body in her fashion. And when fabrics became scarce just before World War I, she allegedly bought up a stock of jersey. A stretchy knit fabric (first produced on the namesake island in the English Channel), which until then had been reserved exclusively for making men's underwear. Chanel was the first to apply it to outerwear. She turned necessity into virtue, and applause followed. And why am I writing all this? Because jersey seems to me a fitting name for this perfume. It embodies everything Chanel represented with her fashion. For me, it is the epitome of natural, simple elegance. In terms of fragrance notes: an aromatic, subtly spicy, and powdery scent. The Chanel website mentions that “it loses its boyishness with a hint of vanilla.” I found jersey to be somewhat boyish as an Eau de Toilette with an herbal top note. Once you get past that, a bright, subtly spicy, elegant scent unfolds - long-lasting. And I know what I'm talking about. A nearly full 75 ml bottle broke on me. Not a drop was left to save. The bottle lay cleanly broken in two halves on the wooden floor. However, the towel I used to wipe up the contents scented our apartment for months. Until my husband accidentally (or perhaps not accidentally) put the towel in the washing machine with all the other towels. At least, the entire contents of the laundry drum smelled of jersey, if only for that one time. Shortly thereafter, the Eau de Parfum variant appeared. It seems to me that the initial herbaceous note of the Eau de Toilette has been toned down, and the scent quickly imparts that ethereal, elegant aura that I already loved in the Eau de Toilette. I wear jersey often. In all seasons. Even now, at a good 30C and after so many consecutive days that I think in the evening: “but tomorrow I should wear a different scent”... that thought is discarded as soon as a fine hint of jersey wafts into my nose the next morning. Just passing by yesterday's clothes is enough, and I am already enchanted again. I am honestly amazed by the longevity and sillage. For Parfumo standards, I am probably what one would call a light sprayer. At most 3-4 sprays. And yet I can still perceive the scent well the next day when passing by yesterday's clothes. Jersey is not a diva. Where some perfumes make a loud statement, jersey is more understated - reserved and elegant. But by no means inconspicuous.

Flower by Kenzo edT is for me the epitome of well-groomed. No fragrance radiates as much freshness and purity as Flower. My aunt always wore this scent, she always smelled incredibly good. At some point, when I started to become interested in fragrances, I set out to find it, it just wouldn't leave my mind. I was very curious whether it would smell just as wonderful on me as it did on her. I was not disappointed. The first spray and I felt it! This clean, pure, fresh scent. It shines cloud-white like a wonderful spring awakening, I feel uplifted, inspired, and truly get spring feelings. Flower is delicately floral, fruity fresh, light and softly green, and the base is not at all sticky sweet or particularly dense but subtle and harmonious. I cannot break the scent down into its components. It is simply an absolutely harmonizing, homogeneous unit that works perfectly. It lasts for hours on me and gives me the feeling of smelling absolutely wonderful. I am often approached about it and looked at in amazement when I say it is Flower by Kenzo. My skin seems to enter into a true symbiosis with it. For me, it is simply wonderfully balanced. Even if it doesn't appeal to the majority here, for me it is the ideal spring/summer feel-good scent that exudes good vibes. Love it to the max. PS: I don't know exactly which fragrance I have, the bottle looks like the edP - the box says edT - but the scent notes don't match the edT. A sample of the edP smells like my edT bottle. WHO can make sense of that?

Most fig scents are very green and leafy or rely strongly on coconut and/or sandalwood. This is something different. It's the ripest, juiciest fig I have ever smelled in a perfume. Really fruity and unmistakable fig and not just some random fruitiness. The opening has a hint of greenery and citrus, but not too much. In the heart phase a dark woodiness surfaces for a moment, then the scent turns sweeter. I can't say that I would have singled out vanilla, rose and pear in this without the notes list, but after reading it, it totally makes sense that they're listed. The base the fig lies on is warm and slightly feminine, maybe floriental would be the best description. But the overall impression is very heavy on the lush, ripe fig. This is the perfect fig for those who are bored by the usual green fig scents. Very original, summery in feel, but wearable year round. Love it! The only downside is that silly name and maybe the boring bottle.

I *love* fig fragrances, and specifically, I love the smell of fig fruit, rather than the leaf, so when I heard this was a fruity fig fragrance I had to try it. It opens up bombastic sweet fruity fig with incredible sillage. I had sprayed it on the back of my right hand and after that it was far and away the most dominant and persistent fragrance in my scent bubble for a good few hours. After that, the fragrances becomes a little more sweet fruity with a floral aspect that kinda reminds me of green muscat grapes and white floral and goes through a (thankfully) short messy latex plastic bit before that recedes and it slowly descends into a woody amber base that gets closer and closer to the skin. The longevity is ok in that it's still detectable on skin at roughly 10hrs in, but I would say the "main attraction" of the perfume is in the first 6hrs. Surprisingly all-season for a fig fragrance and much more fig dominant than BDK Gris Charnel, which I suppose is the only other all-season fragrance I can think of that features fig. Much sweeter and juicier than most of the famous figs out there, like L'Artisan Premier Figuer and Diptyque Philosykos. Sweeter and not as woody/creamy as Essential Parfums Fig Infusion or Satellite a la Figue! Less bright and watery floral than Parfumerie Generale Jardin de Kerylos. Sprayed on from the tester bottle at Ministry of Scent in SF on a 75F day. Worn about 10hrs at time of writing.

Sampling Borntostandout Fig Porn, a fresh, sweet, green, fig-lend blend that also includes woods, florals, and vanilla. It’s fittingly brighter in the opening but dries down to be a bit of a darker, sweeter gourmand, and I rather prefer the opening since it’s the brighter, greener side of fig that I intend to enjoy in fragrances (Dior Balade Sauvage, for example) but this is still enjoyable throughout, quite pleasant, a playful intersection of notes that’s easy to wear and not nearly as provocative as its name may suggest. As with the rest of the line, it’s EDP concentration and priced at $210/85 for 50/15ml, available through US boutiques like Ministry of Scent, which carries the full line. I think this performs quite well, also. 7 out of 10

starts with a promising crisp and leafy green fig with touches of pear but quickly gets overthrown by disgustingly powdery, overly sweet, matronly rose that almost pulls soapy too. I don’t get much else in the composition but the overbearing rose even in the dry down which does nothing but amp up that sweetness and add a touch of musk. Just a messy combination

The fig was considered in Ancient Greece to be a highly erotic fruit. You take the way it was eaten, you take its texture, you take its shape, it was related to beliefs of fecundity and vigor. Fig Porn is a name that makes me see it from this point of view, despite being a fragrance that sees a very pulpy fig in the opening, accompanied by juicy and fruity notes, which fades and becomes creamier and greener. A nice discreet and elegant interpretation.

If every fig fragrance comes close to this, then I can see why fig fragrances are trending. This fig was so good. At first spray I am hit with a creamy juicy fig with a green background, like someone had to crush some bright green leaves to pick the fig which they then dipped into marshmallow fluff.

I’m going to have high expectations on the way a note is executed if the note is part of the fragrance name. This is not a fig perfume to me by any means. If I really want to stretch it, I’d say it could smell like really sweet figs macerating in a thick amber bath. This fragrance is extremely sweet and sticky.

I picked this up not expecting to like it, the name just made me laugh but it ended up being one of the fragrances that immediately put an image in my head. You’re on a tropical island, sunbathed all day, it’s got a hint of that creamy sunscreen vibe, but also like a fruity floral shampoo vibe in there, ever so slightly salty/ skin like, and then a woody/ cozy base.

As a lover of fig notes, I have read about Fig Porn time and time again and have finally been able to try it. I immediately detect the long-awaited fig at the beginning. It is beautifully green and crisp. Wonderfully present and also dominant as a top note. Then, however, after almost 3 minutes, the rose comes through.

After a long rave in the ticker about this scent, I finally decided to share this fragrance with our wonderful community, a little spoiler in advance: BUY THIS SCENT! When I first smelled this fragrance on paper, I was immediately captivated by its seductive and sweet nature; even then, I knew it was not a bad purchase ;).

The most amazingly wonderful summer fragrance EVER!! I's not beachy in the sense that this is not aquatic, not tropical-the coconut is barely noticable, not the smell of suntan lotion. It just smells the way your skin smells in the summer. Warm and yummy. Can't get enough of this one!

As Summer transitions to Fall, I'm trying to relish the last warm days. Thankfully, Azuree Soliel helps. This is the scent of summer and might even be best characterized as an experience scent. Azuree Soliel is the scent of summer. It's not the scent of beaches or of suntan lotion or of water. As PA Princess says, it's the scent of your skin in summer. Perhaps that's why it's called a Skinscent???? It's a skin scent, that's for sure, but it's not coy & shy. It's got a bit of sillage. Of course it helps to layer, which I do - lotion, oil & juice. But an Azuree flanker? No. Unlike some other TF creations for EL, Azuree Soliel is nothing like its namesake and bears no resemblance to it. Azuree Soliel is a flanker in name only. I usually can't wear EL florals, especially white ones, and thankfully I don't sense any jasmine, orange blossom or gardenia. For that matter, I don't sense the listed citrus. On me, this is all base, quite linear and very long-lasting. Highly recommended to floral phobs and those who just want to relive Summer.

From one day to the next, summer had disappeared, driven away by thick gray clouds that approached from the west, damp and heavy, slowly and steadily and inexorably, pushing warmth ahead of them and the light, the lightness, and the bright little flags in which I shivered and froze, now that the sun had hidden itself and the thermometer sank lower and lower. And while my mood prepared to follow the temperature on its way down, my gaze fell upon a small bottle with a golden cap that sparkled and glimmered in the light of the lamp, shining and striving to draw my attention. "Azurée Soleil" I read - and in the next moment, it seemed to have become five degrees warmer around me. Sun, blue sky, fluffy clouds, and a silky soft wind painted themselves on my inner canvas, followed by classic kitschy images of turquoise seas, powdered sugar white sandy beaches, and coconut palms leaning deeply over the water. Just as one imagines places they have never been, whose drawers, however, spring open unasked as soon as keywords like "sunscreen" and "coconut" appear in the mind. And while it was gray and wet outside, while the wind tore the leaves from the trees and chestnuts and hazelnuts pattered to the ground, I redeemed my ticket to the South Seas, which, I was promised, cost nothing more than a spray and closed eyes. Perhaps it is because I started without a GPS. Because I was never really good at geography and my sense of direction provides some amusement. For whatever reason, I find myself on the Île de Bréhat, that Breton island northeast of Paimpol, which bears the dreamlike and so fitting nickname "Island of Flowers and Pink Rocks." So warm and mild it is there, thanks to the Gulf Stream, that an endless wealth of flowers and plants floods the island throughout the year and always surrounds it with a delicate light green touch. Here and there, faint citrus nuances, fine creamy accents, and the scent of sun-kissed skin weave through the light wind that carries the salt of the English Channel and brushes against mulberry, eucalyptus, and fig trees. My path leads north, which is green and rocky, wild and almost uninhabited and wonderful.

Thanks to the lovely Alienrose, this fragrance is part of my collection. Once again, I blind bought it due to the wonderful scent notes. Overall, the brand seems very likable to me. After testing Sensuous Nude and finding it very beautiful as well, I am interested in several fragrances from the house of Lauder. Azuree Soleil encompasses a whole range of decorative cosmetics and skincare products. A complete collection, so to speak, inspired by the perfume classic Azuree and the beaches of the Mediterranean. I am not familiar with Azuree itself. From what I can see, it goes in a completely different scent direction. Azuree represents a legendary place that Estee Lauder created to capture the glamorous era of the 70s. This is also reflected in the bottle design, which is meant to maintain the balance between past and present. Since I was born only at the end of the 80s, I can't really comment on that. The fragrance starts fresh and optimistic. The mandarin appears rather green and even a bit herbal. Together with bergamot, it creates a rounded and thoughtful introduction to the tropical scent. The creamy and light coconut note reveals itself to me quite quickly. I used to be not particularly picky about coconut. However, after I had the chance to test Virgin Island Water by Creed last spring, my standards regarding coconut have been completely redefined. More specifically, VIW contains the essence of copra, which is the dried coconut flesh used to produce oil. Coconut can only smell like this for me now. So light yet creamy. Not synthetic at all and simply wonderfully exotic. A similarly beautiful coconut can also be found here. Wrapped in a thin, crispy layer of caramel, spiced with a bit of myrrh. A lovely contrast, as the coconut note does not smell edible due to the addition of myrrh. Alongside this, there is a transparent yet rich fullness of flowers. Not too sweet, just a bit powdery, pleasantly milky and caressing. null of the mentioned flowers pushes itself to the forefront. Here, it is gently melting, warming, and idyllic. Nevertheless, the fragrance consistently retains a bit of freshness and "windiness," never transforming into a heavy, oriental gourmand despite the amber. In soft waves, the scent seems to hover above the skin. Like a warm, gentle breeze brushing through a palm frond. Complemented by a snow-white powdered sugar beach, pleasant temperatures, and crystal-clear, sparkling, azure blue sea. Only the faint sounds of the local fauna and the rustling of palm leaves break the silence. Truly, a legendary place, this Azuree. In the base, the scent reveals itself a bit quieter and more grounded. Vetiver and sandalwood soften the fragrance somewhat and ensure that coconut and caramel do not become too sticky. From start to finish, a beautiful vacation scent. Sweet, airy, light, a bit woody and spicy, the flowers do not turn into sillage monsters, coconut and caramel refine the fragrance and never feel overloaded, synthetic, or squeaky. I especially like this dynamic-fresh and breezy accent. This is the first time I have noticed this in a fragrance. This lightness and carefree quality likely make the scent so unique and likable. It makes the gray everyday life seem more colorful and easier to manage. The longevity is fantastic for a so-called skin scent. It easily lasts eight hours with moderate sillage. To be honest, I did not expect that. The fragrance fits wonderfully for various occasions, knows no age or season. In winter, it is an uplifting escape from the cold temperatures. Now in spring, it is a nice preview of the hopefully soon-coming summer. Having a vacation every day would be quite monotonous. Similar to living in the Caribbean day in and day out. That would take away the charm of the whole thing. Although I really like the scent, I can't wear it for several days in a row. It feels like having to endure or produce good mood with all one's might. I gladly let this fragrance transport me to a sun-drenched, warm, tropical, and happy place. Shedding worries and doubts like worn-out, old clothes. I turn my face with closed eyes towards the sun, breathe deeply, enjoy the pleasant warmth, let myself fall, and arrive. At my better place.

The similarity to Bronze Goddess is strong. Nevertheless, I believe there are subtle differences. The top note of both Eau Fraiche Skinscents starts fresh and zesty. While the freshness clearly remains with Bronze Goddess until the end and the scent becomes relatively thin and fleeting, Azurée Soleil develops a spicy note after just a few minutes that is distinctly paired with caramel. The base of Azurée Soleil is creamier, and its longevity is better. All in all, both fragrances are absolutely pleasant companions through hot summer days. My favorite is Azurée Soleil because it develops more substance and depth on my skin. But in the end, one could argue about the fine different nuances or just leave it. Conclusion: Both are great coconut scents in a very harmonious blend of fragrance notes, not too sweet and not too bitter.

I can remember 2007. Healed from a serious illness, I wanted just one thing - to go on vacation to the Canary Islands again. Beach. Sun. Nature. Good friends. Four of us set off on the adventure, and I will never forget how Tom Ford created Azuree Soleil for Estee Lauder in 2007. Finally arrived in the sun, I bought a bottle. It was so incredibly beautiful.

I briefly considered taking my summer samples on vacation and testing them under various, hot conditions... Azuree Soleil would definitely have been in my suitcase with its tropical blend of floral coconut milk and sunscreen on women's skin. Few perfumes embody sun, beach, tropical islands, and coconut milk as sensually and classy as this Estee Lauder fragrance from 2007.

A pleasant surprise from Chanel (a house which can be hit or miss for me). It's by far my favorite from the Chance range. The lemon here is sunny, thanks to the aldehydes. Eau Fraiche is a lemonade with white flowers, served in glasses of teak, with one or two teaspoons of amber. On hot days, I almost feel like drinking it in big gulps. It projects and lasts much better than the other Chance EDTs. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Uite si o surpriza placuta de la Chanel: Chance Eau Fraiche parfum! Este pe departe favoritul meu din gama Eau cu sticlute rotunjite de la aceasta casa. Lamaia aici este insorita multumita notelor de aldehyde care o insenineaza. O limonada cu flori de iasomie servita in pahare de lemn de teak cu o lingurita sau doua de ambra. Zau ca l-as bea cu guri mari pe o zi de canicula. Imi aminteste oleaca de Cristalle Eau Verte, dar cumva este un pic mai domol, mai matur. Eau Verte e mai jucaus si vesel, pe cand Eau Fraiche, desi tanara, e imbracata in haine apretate si calcate si poarta parasol in drum spre biserica. Proiecteaza surprinzator de bine comparativ cu celelalte eaus de la Chanel.

Hello everyone, I got my hands on the fragrance through a decant, and since my wife and I are big fans of "Chance Eau Fraîche (Eau de Toilette) | Chanel," it was more or less a must to test the scent, and WE deliberately did not look at the notes and reviews beforehand - I find it "BETTER" to test a certain fragrance without any bias! Both of us were surprised - why? The EDT offers quite a few notes, and some of you may find it a bit herbaceous/bitter (very zesty citrus). The lemon here is softer and, in my opinion, less bitter than in the EDT. However, the EDP is very linear for about "1 hour," but this doesn't bother me at all! Gradually, the citrus direction shifts towards a jasmine note with a hint of the remaining lemon, and for 3 to 4 hours, the scent is very zesty, fresh, and clean, and less floral than it was in the EDT. After the mentioned 4 hours, a bit more woodiness comes in, becoming increasingly present. As for the type of wood - whether cedar or teak, I curiously can't pinpoint it, but we really like it, and if I’m HONEST... I would almost categorize the scent as unisex! Regarding performance: Yes, it is better, BUT really only in a subtle range of 1 to 2 hours more; generally, I always recommend using Molecule 01 as a "BOOSTER" for performance! How is it received: So far, at work and in private - excellent! When can I recommend it? From spring to autumn, it can be worn daily, regardless of age! Can I recommend you buy it? More yes than no - why? Is it better than the EDT - yes! Is it soooo much better - no! If you already have the EDT, do you need the EDP - probably not! And yet we will get it soon - why? On one hand, my wife's EDT is running low, and on the other hand, I am a fan of quality and noticeable high value + execution, and with an XXL bottle, you have a lot of fun for a long time! Get a decant like I did and test it. If I really weren't convinced, I wouldn't recommend it to you! And now have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______

Nowadays, many fragrance houses in the mid to high price range tend to follow a well-received perfume with flankers, as is the case with Chanel. Either they differ in concentration or they create changes to the original version while maintaining the core theme, sometimes with hints of another fragrance genre. We fragrance lovers here are certainly interested in finding out whether the new one is really that different from the old one, in what ways, and: is it worth acquiring? We make that last decision when testing. Personally, I always find the impressions of my fellow perfume enthusiasts here at Parfumo interesting before I get the scent under my nose. The EdT version seems to be more complexly structured according to the listed fragrance notes in the pyramid. It is a herb-fresh-citrusy-floral-woody scent for the warmer season. The same goes for the new EdP sister. The EdT starts with a very herbaceous citrus kick that is certainly intensified by the cedar listed in the top notes. (I could never name that without knowing the fragrance pyramid). The EdP starts citrusy, almost exclusively citrusy, without being herbaceous at first. Very quickly, the flowers and woods of the base come into play in both versions. The theme of the heart notes is equally jasmine in both. In my impression, it is the focal point of both sisters; however, it is a bit fresher and brighter in the EdT, which is surely achieved through water hyacinth and pepper. In the EdP, the jasmine is soft-indolic - not as bright, but also not heavy. The wood notes of the base are similar, with the EdP having a stronger amber impression, while the EdT seems a tad more powdery due to iris and musk. The EdP feels overall softer and woodier, which might appeal more to those who find the herbaceousness of the EdT too much. In the EdT, the herbaceous impression remains until the end. When I smell both versions not in parallel, but with a certain time gap in between, I immediately recognize the strong similarity. Nevertheless, there are typically very fine differences characteristic of Chanel. Some voices in the forums claim that the EdP is actually a completely different scent. For me, the longevity is equally good for both, and the EdP also suits hot days.

I had hoped for a more refined and longer-lasting version of the EdT with this fragrance. With high expectations, I tested the perfume on my skin and definitely detected a clear lemon in the first few minutes, but unfortunately also got strong vibes of bathroom cleaner! Normally, I am not sensitive in this regard at all, and since I am such a big fan of the EdT, the EdP would have almost been a blind buy for me. Lucky me! Don't get me wrong, it is certainly not a bad fragrance, and probably because it comes as a "rounded version" of the EdT, it meets the expectations of most! For me, however, the absence of the bitter freshness of its predecessor unfortunately also means the loss of that certain something and the sophistication that I expect and am used to from Chanel fragrances. The updated version shows very little character to me and is also hardly perceptible on the skin after a maximum of 4 hours. In summary, I miss the freshness and the wow factor, especially for the price. However, you can't go wrong with this fragrance, for example in the office, and it definitely doesn't offend. Unfortunately, I cannot share the purchase recommendation and enthusiasm of my fellow commentators!

Since it has been so hot, I finally took out my Chance Eau Fraiche EdT again. A lucky find, as it is wonderfully refreshing in this heat. Even my scent-sensitive husband has no objections. But now the bottle was running low. I mentioned this to my husband, and today the postman rang the bell and brought me a 100ml Chance Eau Fraiche EdP. My husband acted promptly. What a beautiful replenishment! The EdP is very similar to the EdT. It is also refreshing with a delicate elegant note. The Chanel vibes are clearly recognizable. However, the EdP is a bit sweeter than the EdT, which I personally like. Additionally, it lasts longer. That's good too. I think it would still pass as unisex with a slight tendency towards the feminine. A good summer companion.

... day at the Viktualienmarkt. First, I come across a stand that only has apples, and there I take in the scent of a fresh green apple. The aromas of the lemons and floral scents from the market join in, along with the wood of the stalls.

The sparkling citrus in the opening is beautifully full-bodied and continues to accompany the fragrance. The jasmine slightly dampens the citrus and creates a feminine elegance. Cool citrus and warm white flowers dance intertwined with each other, creating lightness despite the fragrance's density. The teak wood and amber combination also creates an inviting scent character.

Chanel Eau Fraiche (EdP) is, in my opinion, THE summer fragrance for any woman (let's say over 30) who is looking for something "fresh and zesty." It's pretty much the only one from Chanel that I can imagine for warm days. Here you get a fresh lemon tree growing close to the Italian coast.

Pleasures Delight = 1 part Escada Moon Sparkle + 1 part Mariah Carey M + 2 parts Angel. Very BTDT sugary vanilla-patch flanker in the Pleasures line-up. $74 for 100ml? Way over-priced for a nothing special, nothing unique, very ordinary scent. Pleasures Delight hurts my teeth and makes my DH gag. It's that sweet. Run the other way.

Estee Lauder and myself tend to have our ups and downs. I rather enjoy her older and more classic fragrances, however the more recent fragrances often get bad reviews from me. Pleasures Delight is one of her scents that I do like. This fragrance is very gourmand. It's mostly rich caramel, strawberry icecream, marshmallows, pulpy pomegranate and sugared rose petals. The scent in my opinion is a little strong and often headache inducing, especially if over-applied. Because of its thick and syrupy, candy-like structure, Pleasures Delight won't appeal to everyone. In some instances it reminds me of Fantasy by Britney Spears and Fancy by Jessica Simpson. When this fragrance was released there was a massive trend for sweet scents, however recently there has been more of a need for soapy and refreshing scents. So evidently this fragrance wouldn't be as popular as it may have been, however for those of you that do love gourmands, especially those with a strong caramel note, Pleasures Delight may indeed delight you.

It has a strong fruity opening of pomegranate and strawberries. It soon develops its heart of peony and marshmallow sweetness! It's deep sweet gourmand ,candied caramel and patchouli.It differs from all the pleasures editions.It's different in the way that most of pleasures are florals wearable in spring or summer ,this fruity gourmand is nice warm and easy wearing in winter time.Longevity is very good also.

Vanilla birthday cake with strawberry filling and white bakery frosting, plus a little bazooka bubble gum mixed in. I also get a plasticy smell. I feel like all the notes in here are artificial. It also doesn't last very long. Not impressed.

Some time ago, I received a sample of Pleasures Delight from the lovely Tarata (thank you for your generous "donation campaign"!). Well, the title promises both pleasure and delight! So, let’s get to work (testing) in a light and fresh manner! In the top notes, I am greeted by a truly delicate and fine strawberry and freesia. The promised green notes remain very subtle in the background; I can't really identify them! Soon, I start to miss these green notes, as the fragrance develops into something sweeter, sweeter, and even sweeter. Mind you, this development is not toothache-sweet, but in my opinion, it is very much a matter of taste (not quite mine, anyway). The nice strawberry from the top notes seems to be drowning in a molasses in the heart notes and was not seen again in the further development! At this point, I must take a moment of silence for the little strawberry! The other flowers announced in the pyramid have not shown themselves at all, probably out of fear that they might end up like the strawberry. On we go! In the base, the molasses finally pairs with egg, resulting in marshmallow. Grandma Caramel is the midwife at the birth. It’s a shame that the father listed on the birth certificate, the patchouli herb, has disappeared and shamelessly left mother and child in the lurch! Even though patchouli has a sweet tone, it could have at least added some complexity to the base! ------------------- Perhaps this all sounds much worse than I actually experienced. However, the longer I had PD on my arm, the less I wanted to continue on this journey with it. While I felt reminded of "Pleasures," I increasingly missed its delicate floral character and light green notes! So: Those who enjoy sweetness and do not place value on a complex gourmand note will be well served here. Those looking for a fresh strawberry (in a subtly woody base) will be much better off with "Esencia de Higo"!

Candy !!! If you are looking for an super sweet fragrance that makes you crave a mountain of sweets, here it is: Pleasures Delight !!! After a promising fruity start, a toothache-inducing sticky sweetness follows ... tons of caramel candies, marshmallows, vanilla sugar ... Does anyone want more? No thanks, I've sniffed enough. Goodbye, this was not a pleasure this time!

The first fragrance I own where I can really smell strawberry hmmm delicious, I love strawberries! :) That's why I also like Pleasures Delight, unfortunately the longevity leaves something to be desired, but it is definitely a nice everyday scent. Thanks to RingofKerry now mine :) Addendum: The longevity is actually quite impressive, I notice after further testing.

This had been on my radar for years and I finally took the plunge and bb this during the holiday sale at Harrods. I really love this now though at first, I was a little unsure because I didn't think the leather note worked very well. I found it a little jarring, which I think was because I didn't expect it to play such a prominent role. But the more I wear this the more I fall in love with the way it works here. For a while now I had been searching for a tamer and drier Guerlain Insolence. I love Insolence, but she can be a beast in the performance department, and sometimes I don't want to make quite such a statement. This is everything I hoped for as it is more sedate and low key, though no less fabulous. A big plus is that it is different enough from Insolence where it is worth having both in my wardrobe. A violet and iris perfume that is softly powdery from the musk, lightly fruity, with leather, benzoin and vanilla. I love how the tonka adds just a touch of sweetness and a hint of cherry, which I think is what is giving me that lipstick vibe. It really is a beautiful perfume. I am so glad I took the risk and bought this after all. I am just sorry I waited so long.

This is such a beautiful floral, creamy, powdery creation. It is such a beautiful blend of notes, smells like lipstick. It is very elegant, very sophisticated and reminds me of few Guerlain creations. Simply put, it is quintessentially French!

Misia, married for the third time to "José" Sert, one of the leading Spanish painters of her time, was, like many of her Russian compatriots living in Paris, born in St. Petersburg (1872). Not exactly poor, she soon emerged as a muse, friend, and patron of numerous renowned artists in Paris. This spectrum included painters, writers, singers, and musicians. In this respect, she resembled "the muse of Vienna," Alma Schindler, widow of Mahler, divorced from Gropius, and finally married to Werfel! These women loved and supported across borders! However, she is particularly remembered as the best friend of Gabrielle "Coco" Chanel. The two were friends for many years; sometimes more, sometimes less: female friendships are notoriously not entirely problem-free. Coco and the Sert couple spent many vacations together; how often did they lie on the beach at Lido near Venice, pondering how to spend their evenings in the most entertaining way. It was Misia who helped Coco through the difficult time after the car accident of her lover, Arthur Edward "Boy" Capel. Not that she considered the purchase of a house "in memoria" to be a happy decision: Coco later allowed her lover Igor Stravinsky's wife and children to live there for free and paid for their living expenses while the artist himself stayed with her and later tried to manipulate her with threats of suicide. That, of course, didn't work: Coco and the Serts went traveling - thus, a bit of air was let out of this affair! Only Stravinsky felt he had to "suffer" for a long time. But Misia encouraged Coco in her grief for "Boy" in the endeavor to bring a fragrance to the market. That had been one of their last shared thoughts and plans. And so she established contact with Francois Coty. He was then "the market leader in fragrances" and subsequently presented Coco with several compositions that were simply numbered. Since "Five" was her lucky number, she chose the vial with that number - thus "Chanel No. 5" was born and named. It is actually a logical consequence that Chanel launched a fragrance named "Misia." "Misia" has the fortune of many who come after her: she is not burdened with becoming a kind of "cult fragrance"; she can simply be herself! By the way, what does "cult fragrance" mean? A perfume, as impressive or expressive as it may be, is a companion of everyday life and not "cult"! "I’m a star - get me out of here!" fits, in my opinion, very poorly with that. But that’s just a side note. "Misia" is primarily charming; this fragrance is feminine, lady-like, and a little bit old-fashioned. "Misia" simply has style! Iris and its root elegantly recruit a wonderfully dark, fragrant violet; it gladly accepts their reference! Her Majesty, the noble Turkish, also "Oriental" rose, joins them majestically: together they form a harmonious whole! Thus, a fragrance emerges that is intensely floral and thoroughly feminine. In memory of Francois Coty, the pioneer of Chanel fragrances, their European sister from the fragrant Grasse is also included. Coty also moved part of his workshops there. Two varieties of fragrant roses, which write history with their abundance, form a magical community with violets and iris! The aroma of tonka bean slightly irritates me; however, its sweetness enhances the powdery impression: everything seems as if it has been dusted with fine powdered sugar. Here, the iris root stretches its head again: I’m here, do you see me!? This floral quality, this exquisite bouquet of flowers, ultimately needs a solid base. This is called benzoin here: its wonderfully resinous spiciness gives "Misia" stability and elegantly rounds off this fragrance composition. Thus, a not exactly slim, but very sensual fragrance being is created, which does justice to its name! "Misia" fits perfectly into the house of Chanel! Here it shows that friendship can truly bridge time and space: Coco and Misia - two women who are unforgettable and connected! This full-bodied longevity of the fragrance accompanies me for several hours; the progression changes from initially floral-powdery to floral-resinous spicy: absolutely round and completely without edges and corners! Now, I am known as "fish blood," not exactly a standard for fragrance developments and longevity; but I like it. "Misia" is much more sympathetic to me than "Chanel No. 5": this fragrance seems more alive to me, not so "figurine-like" as the well-known and so famous "sister." (Oops, now I’m sure I’ll get hit again - so be it!) Not as classic as firmly sprayed hair and the Chanel suit; rather a bit more casual, though not careless. It really seems as if "Misia" is free from the burden of the "big name" and can be the "best friend" while also leading her own life. So I can imagine giving "Misia" a place in my life as a friend. I can’t do that with "Chanel No. 5" or "Coco." Getting to know this fragrance is thus a gain for me. We will see how far our shared path takes us until the bottle is empty. Anything is possible!

Blessed is he who knows someone in a foreign, large city. For our family vacation in London, my cousin was able to give us many helpful tips and show us around. There was an "involuntary specialization" included: Surely we would have visited the Tate Gallery of Modern Art on our own, but just "for the sake of it." As an art lecturer, she already knew everything there, and so instead of entering the permanent collection, we ended up in the special exhibition on Georgia O’Keeffe. The name meant nothing to us, but upon seeing the poster, it dawned on us: "That's the one with the giant flowers!" The catalog, in sidewalk tile format, also featured the floral giant (https://goo.gl/images/obVhgP). By the way, my wife absolutely had to carry off the book - along with one or two additional catalogs - right away. At the airport, she innocently wondered about the inexplicable weight gain of the suitcases; our luggage was on the edge. Just a side note. We quickly realized that the infamous mega-flowers make up only a small fraction of the artist's work. There are other plants, landscapes, cities, bones(!), and more. I mention this because Misia can be slightly misleading in its form. Anyone expecting a scent analogous to the weighty floral descriptions is mistaken. Sure, flowers play a role, but just "a" role, not "the" role. The iris pushes its root forward in the double mention, while the violet joyfully explores its outermost limits. A bitter iris-violet combination opens, brushing against the leathery, while on the other hand, touched by a hint of sweetness and warmth. Soon, surprisingly strong-fresh green and an unexpectedly sour fruit candy note join in. The scent seems to float, to iridesce. A fragile work of art, carefully constructed. And quite daring. After an hour, the violet drifts into the un-floral, almost charcoal-blackened it seems now. Yet the risk pays off; nothing falls apart and nothing collapses. A mild-resinous layer from late morning supports and gently binds the colleagues, while the possibly indispensable lipstick note remains elegantly restrained around noon. Now the retreat has already begun, of course - perhaps for that reason - without any loss of quality. The sweetness transforms from a hint into a veil, and as it progresses, a kind of ventilated wood appears, which surprisingly ends the scent rather quickly after about six hours. Certainly wiser than a tedious farewell. Fragments are still noticeable into the evening, initially more musky than tonka-like, and finally, something vanilla indeed caresses. I cannot make a comparison with the EdT due to my lack of knowledge of it. I can only state that I quite like Misia as an EdP, although it comes across to me as a bit too lyrically reduced and speckled. It might also appeal to those gentlemen who enjoy the style of Kurkdjian's Lumière Noire pour homme (not a scent twin!). I thank Ergoproxy for the sample.

.. not half past, but at ten. 24.03.2012. When the postman rings twice. Mine didn’t ring, but threw the envelope in the mailbox. Our postman is tall, as thin as a matchstick figure, and when he rings the bell, he risks getting his finger stuck in it. So he doesn’t ring. 10:05 AM. Envelope ripped open. Oh, a few channels I don’t know yet. Nice! 10:07 AM. Sprayed on. Violets that bloom not in hiding. Nice! 10:12 AM. It’s powdery! Joy, I love powdery scents. My Akemi is wagging her tail. She always gets happy when I’m happy. Is she wafting the dry iris clouds to me? Or did she fart? No, when doggy farts, it doesn’t smell like iris. Nice! 10:30 AM. My powder dog wanders off. Brushed satin glides through the room. Nice! 11:45 AM. I love dry, dusty iris scents. Yawn... a bit linear and unimaginative. Polge might have had to save... uh, nice! 12:00 PM. Unsweet, unlovely flowers. Roses? Dreamy... an angel is sitting on my balcony... no, it’s my cat digging up my potted plants. “Will you stop or I’ll pull your legs long!” To the cat, not the scent. Not nice. 12:30 - 5:30 PM. Testing break. Nap. After that, a trip with mom (84), she needs some fresh air too. 5:30 PM. Remnants of the violet iris powder scent. Faint woody note at the end. Nice! 5:35 PM. Wish list..... 185 euros for 75 ml? Not nice!

Christmas Giveaway Comment No. 8 Misia is one of those fragrances that always fits but never gets boring. I believe you must definitely like violets and be open to androgynous women's scents, but even if someone nearby doesn't, it doesn't necessarily clash. The iris root here is rather herbaceous and leathery, which gives the violets a certain dryness.

Expectation A wonderfully woody violet, slightly powdery, a bit playful with fruit, but by no means sweet. Noble and a complex scent for going out. What really happened A violet pastille with fruit syrup spreads across my arm (just one spray!) and takes on nuclear proportions. It is sweet and pulsating.

Today I would like to write my first review and I want to dedicate it to “Misia.” Unfortunately, I couldn’t get a sample or anything similar beforehand, so I placed an order online with Chanel. According to the description, I should like Misia. But I have been mistaken before.

Misia… when I first heard her, I knew she was the one. Isi and Jacky, when I first saw them, I knew we belonged together. Many months passed, we met regularly, each time far too short. Fluffy, cuddly, snuggly, tender. Not smooth, noble, and sophisticated like Ory, my silky white cat prince. No, luxurious, charmingly opulent and elegant.

Now this is gorgeous and opens up with a creamy buttery ylang ylang followed by a very refined supple almost suede like leather. As time passes you can smell jasmine,dry woods, iris all woven tightly together that the scent shimmers on your skin. Smell it one moment you get the leather, smell it again and you can smell the jasmine. It is a beautiful classy multifaceted fragrance. Deep into the drydown after many hours I can even smell a soft and sensual animalic scent on my skin. This scent lasted seven hours on my skin and the projection and sillage was decent. I have to say this is one of the most luxurious and classy fragrances I have ever smelled. Bravo to Chanel this is just a beautiful refined gem of a scent. Big thumbs up!

I know the Exclusif series and I am a big fan of Coromandel, I think it is in art form of perfume creation and just love to smell it both on a lady or on myself. Today I went to the Chanel boutique to sample this exclusifs series and I liked Boy, Sycomore and of course Coromandel. I tried the Cuir Russie for which I had big expectations, right from the flacon to the nose and I got a strong smell of dry pissoir, identical to the one from Musc Ravageur. Funny thing, I even see that Parfumo mentions Musc Ravageur as "loved by the ones who love Cuir Russie". Maybe it is a nice smell, for the people who do not perceive this dry pissoir from the Autobahn scent.

The opening of this perfume is an open-handed slap of aldehydes and flowers in true Chanel style, reminding me very much of No. 5. The expected leather never arrives, however, because Cuir de Russie is a leathery scent, but not overly so. Once opened, the scent settles on a leathery yet not dry note, supported by floral/aldehyde notes that lighten it while leaving the animalic tone inherent in the olfactory profile intact. In the background of the composition, there remains a hint of smoke and resins that support the leather and make it more decisive, contrasting the lighter floral notes. The opening tends to be more feminine, while from the heart onwards, it becomes unisex, tending towards masculine; overall, truly beautiful and worthy of a bottle in a collection. Excellent longevity, with a contained sillage, especially after opening. Excellent perfume for spring and autumn; I don't find it too warm or too cold; I associate it with the transitional seasons. Beautiful!

Lady of old nobility in the here and now. A bit out of time, arrogant, irritable, impatient with her staff. Just returned from the racetrack. Chanel suit, large hat, and sunglasses. Her butter-soft leather gloves, which she just held a bit too tightly, she carelessly drops onto a table. It’s probably best not to approach her today. A softly creamy hint of leather, hand cream, and a bit of sweat gently wafts from the gloves. __________________________________________________________ Cuir de Russie (EdT) opens briefly with a spritz of bergamot and then transitions into a dreamily beautiful, creamy, and mandarin-like leather note. Since I haven't had much experience with this fragrance direction so far - falling prey to the misconception that leather scents would always reveal themselves to me as variations of Maggi - I now notice for the first time that in those scents that appeal to me, there is often an interplay of mandarin, birch or birch wood, and leather note, which then creates a wonderfully rich, not too clean, spicy creaminess overall. This is also the case with Cuir de Russie. However, the fragrance also has a very prominent, indolic jasmine note at its heart, which comes across as a bit too intense for me when I smell it at the spray point, while at arm's length it simultaneously radiates this beautiful leathery creaminess. I have, however, become cautious with jasmine by now. The note is quite present for a long time on me. I can imagine that on a day when I might be stressed, annoyed, or angry, the fragrance could really get to me and I might condition myself to develop an aversion to it. I recently experienced how quickly that can happen with an impulse purchase that went straight back. Beautiful, this Chanel... but this jasmine phase does instill a certain respect in me. The fine leather "whiff" at arm's length is truly a dream. After an hour, the jasmine is still present, giving off a subtly aggressive vibe. The fragrance also comes across as a bit Chanel-aldehydic-soapy to me as it develops. Conclusion: a very elegant, "clean" leather scent, which, due to the jasmine, definitely has a self-assured floral-animalic aspect. Based on my previous experiences that this particular note can also act as an unfavorable amplifier of negative moods for me, the purchase of the fragrance would ultimately be too risky. Here, I only speak for myself. Those who appreciate jasmine in fragrances will definitely find a very elegant perfume here that imparts a beautiful aura. However, since the EdT is apparently supposed to be significantly less floral, I definitely want to test that as well, as I really liked the opening of the fragrance very much. (with many thanks to Susan)

To my shame, I must confess... uh, no, it’s not a shame, it just happens. Christmas is Chanel, Chanel is Christmas. And I don’t worry about why I’m head over heels in love with a leather scent, because it’s a Polge product. Polge is a kind of Thierry Wasser, just more Chanel-like. And Thierry, as brilliant as he is, has not been able to create a leather scent that I truly, truly love, just like his predecessors from the same company. Polge has. I wasn’t really inclined to test, like, or even approach Cuir de Russie uncritically. I had almost dismissed all too leather-heavy fragrances for myself. Some have found their way into my home over the decades! ...but none became a great love: Farina's Russian Leather was surprisingly good, Habit Rouge I only really liked as a dress code, and some fragrances with suede enchanted me for a certain time. Recently, however, a perfumer, whose opinion I generally consider quite well-founded, mentioned that Chanel's Extrait of Cuir de Russie is divine. Unfortunately, I didn’t manage to get the Extrait, only the EdP, which may not be quite as perfect, but for me, it’s already damn great. It combines everything I expect from a wearable leather scent: soft to almost creamy, with light, fresh fruity notes at the beginning, then the delicate leather united with sweet spicy notes. Roses form the bed on which the Chanel leather pouch lies, a little wood underlines and supports the noble effect. Absolutely classic, not subjected to any fashion or trend, like No.5, here only as a leather object of desire. That’s Chanel.

Still an elegant leather Royal. The fragrance starts with a very brief greeting of bergamot, quickly becoming creamy and smelling of mandarins, ylang, and jasmine. Suddenly, birch wood emerges from the ride with a Haflinger (leisure horse) through the Bois de Boulogne forest. Traces of smoke are very, very minimal.

Cuir de Russie... for me, this is leather from the first minute. It drove me crazy when I stood in front of the beautiful Chanel display at Türkisen in Cologne, and the friendly sales associate carefully sprayed this jewel on me. The price is steep, and I had to step away for a moment; the scent needed to settle! Was it too masculine for me?

When I spray CdR, a "fresh-floral-soapy" breeze first wafts towards me... really delicate, fine, aldehydic soap bubbles, somewhat like when you sniff freshly hung laundry in the summer, dried by the warm sun.... In addition, I get a creamy note of soft leather....

This is a fragrance starts so delectable that it tempts you to lick the skin of the person wearing it. It starts with a berry sweetness, a natural sweetness that you typically don't get with other BTSO fragrances. The berries mix with the boozy, spicy, and woody notes. This is drinking cognac off of a lover's lips. Its a great start to the fragrance and I wish it would last a little longer. The berries, booze, and spice mellow out into a creamy wood vanilla dry down, its good but fairly basic. This fragrance lasted all day, over 8 hours. The projection was good but not super strong, so its office appropriate. A 50ml will cost you $205.

Rich red berries burst forth in the opening but are crushed in seconds under the weight of citrus, juniper and pepper, an accord which is fun for a moment, but quickly begins to resemble an artificial 'car vent clip-on freshener' smell. Moments later, it fades to something a touch sweeter and warmer, but still feels commercial, designer. It's just a touch too synthetically 'fresh', and whatever note is giving that effect is holding the composition back instead of serving to make it more complex, lingering like the unpleasant frigid chill of a blasting air conditioner in a luxury car dealership. It's like I can smell the cinnamon and cardamom and sandalwood trapped beneath it, knocked unconscious by its weight. I'm slightly taken aback by how 'un-sexy' this feels to me. I can tell it's *trying* to be sexy, but in the way someone hitting on you is, at an event you've attended with your spouse, who has excused themselves to the washroom. It's missing context and obviously misses the mark. Update a few hours later: the fresh note dissipates after about two hours, and the sweet resinous base is pleasant, but just too basic for what this fragrance promises (and costs)! The drydown is nearly indistinguishable from Prada Ocean Luna Rossa. This fragrance's middle was bold in all the wrong ways, and its base too boring. Just a dissonant strike-out.

i don't really know what i'm smelling but it's not bad. slightly sweet and sexy, the smell of my handbag after a night out, like if a fresh shower + going-out perfume + makeup + bar ambience + sweat was a really nice perfume. the drydown smells like the synthetic base of a man's cheap cologne plus a little sweetness. it's like my own niche $300 gourmand perfume has mostly worn off but the man i was kissing left his oversprayed chemical weapon all over my jacket. i don't hate it.

On an ordinary day, the paths of two lives can cross as if fate has suddenly decided to intervene. The heart begins to beat differently, as if it has recognized a long-forgotten feeling. An unexpected love will emerge, bringing unimaginable joy. We will laugh together, we will spend time together, and the world will suddenly shine in a new beauty. In that moment, you will understand that love can be born when you least expect it, transforming normality into an extraordinary journey, to a place where only our feelings live and that only we are allowed to enter. The scent of tipsy love, the sweet feeling of being in the heart of another, the spirit intoxicated by wonderful thoughts. For me, Drunk Lovers by Borntostandout is leathery, fruity, tipsy, and one of my friend's favorites.

I really wanted to test Sugar Addict from BTSO, as I had read and heard so many good things about it. Said and done. Well, when the package with the fragrance samples arrived, Sugar Addict was not included, but rather a 5ml sample of Drunk Lovers. What? I questionedly checked all the samples again, found nothing. So I checked the order again - and lo and behold - I had "clicked" the wrong one. Well, never mind, I’ll just test Drunk Lovers now. And what can I say - I was thrilled from the first spray, the scent is simply a dream. It starts fruity, fresh, juicy. I perceive citrus notes only very subtly, but deep red, dark berries with a slight sweetness. My nose also picks up woody elements of the berry bush, or I imagine that the stems of the berries are woven into the scent as well. Then, a pleasant alcoholic note quickly comes to the fore. It smells like cognac, but it could also be an expensive rum. This alcoholic note harmonizes very well with the fruits; it is never too dominant, although it has a certain depth. In the drydown, it becomes sweeter and spicier, but it never gets too much. You feel slightly "tipsy," cozy, warm. Hours after spraying, I could still smell the scent on my wrist - soft, vanillic with a hint of cognac in the background. After wearing it several times, I finally have a full bottle of Drunk Lovers on my shelf. (Sugar Addict who?)

I was initially unsure because opinions on Drunk Lovers really vary. But on my skin, it works really well.
