Overall this is a very good low budget perfume for warm weather, but I doubt I'd rebuy this once it runs out. Very pleased, 8/10

I got this as a gift that someone likely got from an airport. I don't love it, but I do like it. It is pleasant, and as others have said it is enjoyable, agreeable, and it is nice to spray on after the shower. Its performance is lackluster. It goes away after 2-3 hours. Perhaps I am noseblind to it, but I doubt it, since other perfumes I have I can smell through the day.

CK has been on a downward slope for years... You hear that again and again. But when were they not? When did this start? And what has been the previous, cruel peak of the brand? The most hated long-running fragrance, In2Him, might shed light on all these questions & many more.

...what do you give to someone who wears Calvin Klein underwear as a gift for a perfume...naturally something from Calvin Klein. And since it shouldn't always be CK1, I set out to find another one. CKIN2U, cool name, the look in the form of a bottle...simply genius. This has to be well received.

I got In 2U to have an affordable alternative for everyday office use. The fragrance fulfills this task, no more and no less. In 2U is not a heartbreaker, but if you don't want to spend a fortune to sit in your own scent at your office, In 2U is a good choice. Fresh, slightly bitter, not too intrusive, I would buy it again for this purpose.

The perfume has little character. The scent itself is very unremarkable and, in my opinion, too synthetic. It is not an unpleasant scent, but one that is quite weak and "shy". The perfume fades away after just a few hours, even after intense application. I only bought it because I got 150 ml for €25, but even that hasn’t really been worth it for me.

Curious due to a great offer from a well-known drugstore chain, I took a look at "CK In 2U Him" - hoping to find a suitable gift for my beloved. Calvin Klein certainly hasn't reinvented the wheel in terms of men's fragrances with "CK In 2U Him." But surprisingly, I really like the scent. I thought it would smell a bit too sweet and cheap, but that's not the case at all.

Upon application, this fragrance is like an electric shock, refreshing, and the strong grapefruit is immediately recognizable! The energetic burst fades after about 1 to 2 hours, and then the citrus scent remains. It doesn’t remind me of a lemon cake, but rather of a fresh lemonade on a hot summer day. Anyone looking for a refreshing kick that stays powerfully present will be completely satisfied with this fragrance. Personally, I’m unfortunately not a fan, as this scent is almost too citrusy and biting for me; I had hoped that it might have a slightly aquatic quality.

When I encountered this perfume for the first time in my life, I was a teenager and hated it on the spot. Never before had I come across anything so artificial and chemical. Over the years, I have often revisited this scent, I tried to appreciate it, but never quite succeeded. To me, it will always remain harsh and soapy, - and I will never understand why perfume critics like Turin talk about "rose" in the context of "White Linen". To me, this perfume smells of hospitals and chrome. It does not inspire me with any positive feelings at all - one of the perfumes which are as remote from nature (i.e. flowers!) as you can possibly get.

Take a deep breath. This blend of white flowers, especially honeysuckle and tulip, is simply summery fresh and airy light. Like Raffaelo to spray on! In 1978, I was 20, newly at university, in love - life lay before me like a white cloth, only a few traces marked, a few lines planned. The summer seemed endless, everything was light. We skipped lectures to have picnics in the Duisburg city forest - the professors sometimes joined us because they knew where generations of lazy students hung out.... I liked to wear 3-tiered skirts made of light, airy fabrics, back then super slim size 36. Ah... those days! Death, illness, and sorrow were far away - that only affected others. There was something in those days that can only be described in retrospect as the "unbearable lightness of being," the positive naivety of youth. But back then, money was extremely tight - the little pocket money and a bit more from jobs at the library. In any case, so little that acquiring such a fragrance meant months of scrimping and saving. I had received a sample and was smitten - this scent, this freshness, cleanliness, airiness. Musthaveitsoon! Mom still dried the sheets on the Leifheit clothesline back then, which regularly collapsed, causing all the splendor to billow down on the meadow below. This scent reminds me of that sight - even today. In 1978, I was so eager for the stuff that I worked extra shifts, washed cars, mowed lawns, curled the neighbor's hair.... you understand.. everything. Everything! When the money finally added up, I went to Karstadt - bought the smallest size. Proud. Joy. Outside, a spritz in the neckline and with my head held high through the city. This scent still has the aura of early youth for me, which is why it fits - for me - today only as a memento (mori) - rather not as a daily fragrance. For short outings, at home after a shower, I gladly take this brilliant combination to bed or into the garden. Just don’t have a clothesline. You should try it, for me it has a strong flair of the 70s - the music, fashion, time.

Yes, I can hardly avoid this comparison here. I have now tested several dozen women's fragrances from my large mini-collection that I acquired last month. Most of them were, well, okay; many were too floral and "aunt-like" for my taste, but this one has truly captivated me. The analogy to freshly washed bed linen is almost overwhelming, specifically freshly washed and still slightly warm from the dryer. Wonderful. Free from any aggression and exaggeration, simply light, soft, and - yes - sensual. Truly a very successful composition that (and here I return to my title) is certainly capable of spreading that "cozy feeling" that I experience with "Lalique White." A "de-stresser" that calms. Certainly not one for going out or for the club, but one of those fragrances that you wear at home alone in the evening to unwind. I would indeed love to smell this "in real life" on the right wearer.

...it was recommended to me about 20 years ago - and I was thrilled by this special scent - it had something - yes, it was different from other fragrances and I felt special with it - fresh but also reminiscent of white flowers, not too sweet - a bit woody and aromatic... somehow I always thought of my grandma's linen cupboard. I used it for several years, only to test it again later - however, I don't like it as much today as I did back then - it's not cheeky and zesty enough - and the time with it is over for me - an old - but special love!

Now I’m taking a look at an older miniature again. This time it’s "White Linen (Eau de Toilette) | Estēe Lauder." This soapy chypre scent is fine by me. However, the longevity is really poor and the sillage is hardly better. After 2 hours, it smells very close to the skin, and after about 3 to 4 hours, I can’t smell anything anymore. The top note starts fresh, green, and citrusy with bergamot and a hint of aldehydes. Then it becomes beautifully floral thanks to lily of the valley and rose water. The heart note remains floral with iris, violet, and garden carnations. Afterwards, vibes of fabric softener and soap emerge. The base smells earthy and rooty with moss and vetiver. This is not a standout fragrance but also not a bad one, in contrast to the weak performance. My miniature will move on.

… I kinda fell in love with this fragrance. It has quite a special scent of tobacco, some vanilla and floral notes. It’s all very smooth. A very original scent that I haven’t smelled anywhere else. The only gripe I may have is that the longevity is quite long. Maybe because I’m a non-smoker I enjoy the first couple of hours but at a certain moment I’m like… that’s enough. Still, it’s not overly strong or pungent or anything so it’s not that big of a problem. But it’s such a special scent, I wish it was a bit cheaper and had a bit less longevity. Oh yeah one more thing. That bottle, omg yuck… for such a price one may expect something more special.

This is the smell of a forest fire after its been put out. Its not complete devastation, there are trees still standing, their bark smoldering and sap bubbling out. But there are trees left unharmed, their pine needles growth bright and green. This is a smokey pine fragrance, the pine is green, balsamic, and woody. For the first hour or so, there is a plastic band-aide smell. After the band-aide and smoke notes fade, you are left with a sweet creamy woody smell. This scent lasted all day, about 8 hours and the projection was decent. This is actually a fairly restrained fragrance for this brand, they usually make them super sweet and super strong. This is a nice change in pace for them. A 50ml will cost you $205.

Sampling Borntostandout Smokin’ Gun, my final sample of the Dark & Drunk discovery set, a spicy, smoky, boozy pine scent with key notes of rum, whiskey, juniper, incense, and leather, with a bit of an interesting black licorice vibe at the very opening, giving way to a smoother dry down with less of the sharpness and acidity over time. It’s a fun, dark, multifaceted concoction that I instantly loved from first spray, and it’s probably tied with Drunk Maple as my favorite of the line that I’ve tried so far, a really great option for cooler weather and to stand out interestingly, and it performs quite well, also. As with the rest of the line, this is EDP concentration and priced at $210 for 50ml, reasonable enough for niche perfumery in the current market. 8 out of 10

I honestly expected something stronger. This is actually a pretty mild scent, considering the notes. It is only slightly smoky, there are much, MUCH smokier fragrances out there. It kinda smells like a generic fancy aftershave or like a barbershop. Pity, I expected something truly groundbreaking, considering the name and the notes.

The pyramid reads wonderfully. The impressions practically scream for a blind buy, and more than once I've been on the verge of it. But in the end, I chose other fragrances from brands I already know and love. But now, let's talk about this work from BTSO. At this point, thanks to DarkWinterCS for the great exchange offer and many exciting fragrances that I will gradually test. This one is at the top of the list! The scent hits me with a full blast of sweet dough, pastries, sugar cane, molasses, and other gourmand notes. The spiciness of the juniper is kept in check, and Campari doesn't show itself at all. Gradually, woody notes join in. They are soft, dry, charred, sweet, sour, in a very subtle way cold and smoky, but overall rather alcohol-laden and ethereal. I have the feeling that the weapons were drawn but haven't been used for a long time. And then there's the spicy part of the fragrance. Cinnamon, vanilla, and tobacco further soak the scent, dressing it in evening attire and putting on the finest shoes. It's off to a gala or art exhibition, with jazz and rum. The progression loses its already subtle and intimate sultry impression and becomes more and more sweet and edible wood in my nose. Not wrong, but far below my expectations. And this very expectation keeps me from warming up to this composition. Unfortunately, I lack experience regarding which whiskies or rums are popular in South Korea, so I may have had the wrong expectations. But what can I say... Put the revolver away, today there will be no shooting. I think I’m standing in a paradise of avenger stick coffee pieces.

tricky - once again one of those products that aren't really found everywhere on the shelf - and thus very high on my collecting passion... The bottle is almost a bit reserved...simple - but a sturdy little guy... Now to the scent: At first...and quite briefly...bitter, sourly fresh orange, Campari Bitter followed by gentle juniper...

“Smokin’ Gun” opens with a strong, smoky-bitter punch: Campari, rum, bitter orange, and juniper create a sharp, sweet-spicy citrus note that feels almost shocking. Parfumo In the heart, a mix of leather, whisky barrel oak, incense, pine, and cinnamon unfolds - the scent becomes harder, darker, herbaceous-smoky, and slightly earthy-woody.

Well, my little darling, do you remember how we met? I was strolling through the airport, my flight was delayed, I had already finished my book, and then I thought to myself - oh dear, my partner's mother just had a birthday recently! So off to the Duty-Free to find something suitable. Preferably something summery-playful, sweet, and heavy she can manage on her own. I didn't know you yet, so I approached you very cautiously. Sweet - yes, but subtle. Floral - yes, and how! Cherry blossom and peony, a hint of white lilac and rose. Yes, it’s the rose that made you not girlish but rather ladylike. On the skin, you became very creamy, I enjoyed the caresses. Some citrus notes came through as well, but they were quite subdued. It wasn't the zest and acidity of a grapefruit, but the slightly oily-bitter scent of a grapefruit peel. You were also a bargain. So you just came along. But gifting you didn’t work out - my now ex didn’t want me anymore. So unfortunately, his mom never got to know you. Here you are also quite unknown. You were a seasonal appearance, a holiday flirt, so that’s how I feel about you. You don’t last long (about 4 hours), the bottle is almost empty, but so what. There will be many others. You bring a slightly dreamy smile to my face, give me good vibes, cause no headaches - mission accomplished. Kisses!

Estee Lauder may offend me sometimes with her female scents, however in the case of her masculine fragrances, like Beyond Paradise for Men, she has me overwhelmed with shock and joy. This fragrance is refreshing, sexy and unique. It's a touch synthetic like Beyond Paradise for Women, however it's not reminiscent of rotting flowers and a chemistry lab like its female counterpart was. Beyond Paradise for Men relies on its distinctive fruity notes and exotic floral combination. It brings to mind everything that's summery; beach, hot sun, cool drinks etc. Strangely enough, despite its rather feminine composition, this fragrance is very manly. However I wouldn't rule out this fragrance for women altogether as I find the scent rather unisex. Luca Turin raves over this fragrance, describing it as being very colourful and complex. I somewhat agree, even though I do still prefer dark, woodsy and spicy scents on a man. I thought of my boy the moment I sprayed this fragrance onto a piece of card, which unnerved me a little. For this reason alone, I feel that this fragrance would probably suit his relaxed, somewhat clueless sense of style and humour. Beyond Paradise for Men speaks character, liveliness and youthfulness. In some ways it strikes me as being a little aquatic, but not in a dominating and suffocating sense of the word. It sits on the skin smoothly and lasts quite well, with the sillage being rather impressive. I highly recommend.

Beyond Paradise for Men opens with a very sharp grapefruit and bitter melon melange that comes off as a bit aldehyde-like. The sharp citrus remains to a degree in the early heart, joined by floral elements of honeysuckle and jasmine with an underlying oceanic accord almost certainly comprised of calone hanging around throughout. The oceanic floral aspects remain through the dry-down with the melon accord finally extinguished, now accompanied by a plum-like woody accord that must be the plum wood listed in the official scent pyramid (I confess I have never smelled plum wood before, so I can't be entirely sure). Projection is average and longevity is very good. Ah, the much maligned Beyond Paradise for Men... It would be all too easy to join the crowd and trash this one, but I really don't find it unpleasant at all. Sure, it is laced with the dreaded calone that many scent aficionados disdain (myself included). That said, it distinguishes itself from a crowded group of similar scents by its relatively skillful use of florals in the heart notes and its different woody base that presumably is the plum wood (a note you may not often if ever come across in a scent outside this one). I am not going to say that it is a great scent or even one I would buy (it isn't on both counts), but folks looking for something different in the aquatic genre could do much worse for a lot more money. In the end, Beyond Paradise for Men is an above average to good smelling floral aquatic, earning 3 stars out of 5.

Imagine a soda flavour 'Tropical fruit & exotic hardwood shavings' and you pretty much have it. Artistically brilliant composition doesn't always equal wearability. On the other hand, if fruity-woody aquatics are your thing, I doubt there's anything better (or even half as good) out there.
Equally well-composed and unappealing. Same issue I have with the original Beyond Paradise, but I'm equally less conflicted and less interested.

In the mid-2000s, I was what one would call a 'Young Professional' today - happy to finally be out of university and 'arrived in (professional) life': a regular daily routine and income, suit, job ticket, and occasionally a taxi included. And as much as I appreciated all that I had long desired, I missed 'my wild 90s' just as much. I still sometimes listened to Blank & Jones on Sunday afternoons and watched a few old episodes of Friends on DVD - and in weak moments considered whether I should perhaps paint the hallway terracotta again in sponge technique, at least one wall. And in very weak moments, I thought of Beyond Paradíse for Men by Estée Lauder. Estée Lauder's Pleasures for Men (with the matte gray cap) had been 'my' fragrance in the 90s - metallic fresh and youthful, with a sweet glue-like scent - it had experienced Blank & Jones and Friends and terracotta-painted walls in the hallway with me. Our shared time ended with the conclusion of my studies and the move to another city, but I was certainly not averse to choosing a potential successor 'from the same stable.' And as fondly as I remember my time with Pleasures for Men - and still do - and as much as I still occasionally listen to Blank & Jones and watch an episode or two of Friends on Sunday afternoons - I am glad I never acquired Beyond Paradíse for Men. Its essence is still fully that of the 90s - probably the longing aspect worked so well back then for that reason. Beyond Paradíse for Men is sweet-metallic - even sweeter and more metallic than Pleasures for Men was. It conveys androgynous good cheer in almost psychedelic cheerfulness: floral colorful and fruity loud and almost clownishly tropical-Caribbean, like in a comic strip, with the subtlety and effect of an alcopop, as they were so popular in the 90s: Bacardi Breezer, Sierra Slammer, Smirnoff Ice. By 2004, its time was over, but some indecisive people still try to jump on every trend at the very last moment. Estée Lauder's Beyond Paradíse for Men was already 'beyond everything' back then. Conclusion: stupid for a while. The wrong fragrance at the wrong time - even more so today than in the mid-00s. Good that I resisted it back then. Just like the terracotta sponge-painted wall.
...once asked every Saturday evening Heiner Müller his then-girlfriend Kim Kardashian, who responded with a blank, dull stare without actually saying anything. K.K.

I smell a whole aquarium full of green-brown water and all types of algae; brush algae, long-threaded green algae, short-threaded green algae, gray-brown diatoms, brown diatoms, blue-green cyanobacteria, black-blue cyanobacteria, black spot algae, green spot algae, and suspended algae. Please correct the fragrance pyramid.
As if a veil of mild fatigue were laid over the eyes, causing the world to blur into a pastel painting of soft shapes and colors, "Beyond Paradíse Men" envelops the heart of its wearer.

Let's forget Luca Turin's 5-star rating of Beyond Paradise. Sometimes, positive reviews and exaggerated expectations can really be a burden. Personally, I have owned this fragrance long before I heard of Luca Turin or the creative perfume platform Parfumo. So let's try to approach a fragrance without bias and perhaps discover its value that way.

Even the kitschy design and the even kitschier name would actually be reason enough to leave this fragrance to the generation of braces. But since Luca Turin praises it at every opportunity, I thought there must be something to it. Now I have endured the fifth attempt, and my clear verdict is: undefinable, but disgusting! On the strip, it smells somewhat pleasant.

I gave it two wears to make sure--this one is challenging. My thoughts from a couple dabs on my wrist. Initial 5 min: Sickly, sticky, sweet mango. Something "off" starts to show itself. Pervasive sweetness. Even from a small dabber, the strength was there. 30 min mark: The mango lightens a lot, but the leather gets stronger. Spicy/sharp--but I'm not sure where that's coming from. The synthetic underbelly is more apparent. It's smokey. I think it's so intense that I went nose blind based on my SO's reaction. It seems it's much stronger in the air. Onward: It sticks and overpowers. I couldn't smell anything outside of my wrist. I put on a Stéphane Humbert Lucas perfume (Pink Boa) on my chest (3 sprays) and all I could smell was Black Mango --it completely drowned the other out. The longer I wear it, the more I "accept" it, but it's too much. My SO hated it and wouldn't stop complaining about the scent, saying, "Too much leather. And smoke. Smells like a smoker died and you're sniffing them." Update from same day: It's in the deep dry down now (6 hours in). I can still smell it wafting. However, I get hints of halitosis? Or sweet armpit? Something like that.... must be the oud they use. Update 2 (weeks later to start with a fresh nose): I tried it again and had others smell. Based on their unanimous negative reactions, I have to rate this one lower due to the lack of wearability for most people. I'm more accepting--but that's because fragrance is a hobby of mine. Most simply want to smell good to others. I don't believe most will like this scent. This is NOT a safe blind buy.

i really, really wanted to love this. on the first spray and for like 20-30 minutes after that, its the most gorgeous, delicious mango scent that I’ve smelled in a perfume. not quite photorealistic for me, but like a really good mango candy, or maybe a smoothie. but after that the woody notes are too strong for my taste, it smells overwhelmingly of a bonfire once it settles on my skin, even fabrics too. and it’s not even like i hate that scent, i don’t hate it but it’s just so powerful and i don’t know if I want my person to smell like that, you know? ill keep the rest of the sample that i have just in case i have a change of heart (and that initial scent really is that good, maybe it’s more suited to colder weather?), but unfortunately i was a little disappointed by this :( still planning on trying the others in this collection tho

Black Mango begins as tropical fantasy electric mango rush with vibrant citrus. Then the scent wades into indulgent gourmand territory: mango lassi and vanilla weave warmth and sweetness. Finally, it plunges into bold depths of oud, leather, sandalwood, and cypriol — transforming into a smoky, animalic statement. Very strong and potent, hence the ‘Extrait Extreme’ collection. Somehow this is good to wear all year round. Little bit expensive for 50ml bottles, but for me it is absolutely worth it!

Smells exactly like a mango lassi: milky, slightly spicy, lots of mango. This stuff is very potent, half a spray lasted until next day, with heavy projection in the first hour in a pretty cold day. Some people sense mostly the oud & leather, but to my nose the mango lassi smell dominated the whole wear. In a few words: very potent & very delicious. Fortunately I managed to get it for 2/3 of retail price & is absolutely worth it for that price!

Anyone who thinks of a sweet-fruity, friendly scent when it comes to Mango and BTSO has miscalculated with BORNTOSTANDOUT. The Black Mango is not a fragrance for a summery morning stroll; it is a portrayal of an overripe mango that has lost its innocence; rather, it is an aggressive fruity exoticism with a dangerous depth. Before I reveal too much, let's get into it: - In the opening, an extremely plump, overripe mango greets you; a slight zest from the orange, but the mango dominates massively here. An intense mélange of this overripe mango, which is not the mango you usually know; not just sweet, but really ripe, almost in the fermentation process. - The mango actually remains a present companion throughout the entire fragrance, although it must be said that this overdose of ripe mango acquires a slightly velvety structure and the whole thing balances out better; whether it is the balsamic aspect or the vanilla cannot be distinguished in this overdose of mango, but the mango becomes noticeably more balanced in the drydown. As it progresses, a good accent of dark woods is added, the fruitiness of the mango is balanced by this dry, slightly leathery woodiness, without the mango really disappearing entirely, but rather blending with these dark woods. - Longevity and sillage are both in the upper third, a real powerhouse. The Black Mango is a statement fragrance; it is a scent with edges and corners and takes a rather oriental path with this dark, overripe mango paired with dark woods. Not as friendly as other mango fragrances, but definitely with character. Mainstream? No, definitely test it first.

Yesterday, my husband waved me over to the Calvin Klein stand. Wow - does he actually have an interest in fragrances? He pointed out ck Gold to me - with a pair of headphones as a goodie! Aha, now I see where the wind is blowing from. But since I have a few CK fragrances, I was also eager to test Gold. And it is indeed a lovely uncomplicated unisex scent - very suitable for summer to autumn. The subtly sweet fig particularly appeals to me - lightly spiced with sage. Neroli is pleasantly cool, and the violet adds a subtle bitterness. Vetiver with woody notes skillfully rounds off the fragrance without robbing it of its transparency. I would have said "Yes!" to Gold even without the headphone goodie, but with the gimmick, the purchase is all the more worthwhile. Now I am wearing Gold - and from the headphones, "Clocks" by Coldplay surrounds me. A beautiful combination.

When I first saw it on the shelf, I thought: Oh my God, "1 Million" says hello! The aesthetic minimalist Calvin Klein would probably never have commissioned this gold if he were still running his own shop - Bling-Bling is just not what you usually associate with the Calvin Klein brand. But one shouldn't be guided solely by appearances, so I was curious and actually tried it. Even though it differs significantly from the original "cK one" and comes across as much sweeter, I still see it as a true flanker, as it varies the fruity-floral chypre theme. In part, "cK one Gold" fits into the pudding mainstream of recent years; on the other hand, it has a refined and light elegance reminiscent of the original "L'Homme" by Yves Saint Laurent. Cardamom, aldehydes, mandarin, melon, jasmine, rose, sandalwood, cedar, amber, and tonka set the tone. It comes across as lively as champagne and a Strauss waltz, yet thanks to its not-to-be-underestimated sillage, it is more suited for autumn and winter. Conclusion: Even though it doesn't reinvent the wheel, it is damn well made - no scratching anywhere, the scent is not overwhelming, and in terms of aesthetics, it's more Joop! Jump or Go than Calvin Klein. So, if you're simply looking for a good scent, leaning towards the androgynous side, and nothing super-innovative, you are well served here.

I accidentally sprayed this fragrance at Müller and then searched for it for days until I finally found it by chance... I ordered it right away and was extremely disappointed.. Amazing scent, exactly my style, and a great bottle, but the fragrance lasts less than an hour on my skin... it's a shame that it just sits there now :/

Here I sit on the leisurely train, behind me the dinner from the red-gold fast-food chain is being unpacked.... A fresh breeze wouldn't be wrong right now, I thought, and generously applied the sample that had been thoughtfully packed into the bag for me at the Turkish place. A fresh breeze is also what rises from my wrists; I smell fig, or rather fig leaf; it could also be the combination of fig and sage, which I usually don't pick up at all. There’s something fresh upon spraying; that must be the bergamot. In the top notes, there's quite a bit going on; I briefly perceive something floral, a lot of spice, zesty sweetness. Then it becomes linear on my skin: fig and wood. This through the heart and base, and very quickly close to the skin. Delicious! When the sample was tossed into the bag, I thought, "Nice, but such a flanker won't be anything new." That's true, but in a different way: At first, the scent is still undecided between Womanity and Womanity Aqua Chic, then it increasingly leans towards the latter.... For me, no problem; Aqua Chic has been discontinued, and as a big fan, I have today found a possible successor, should my beloved bottle of WAC ever run out!!

I acquired this fragrance a few years ago, when I hadn't yet developed my passion for scents. Back then, I was mainly attracted by what I consider to be a very stylish bottle. Considering my ignorance, it was truly a lucky find! It starts off very fresh and somewhat citrusy. I smell spring, the first rays of sunshine on slowly warming days. Over time, it becomes sweeter, in a very pleasant way. I find the fruity sweetness beautifully balanced with fresh and woody notes. The longevity could be better, but it lasts about 4-5 hours on me. So for a very fresh scent, that's quite okay. I now always have it in my gym bag, but I have also worn it at work for a while. In summer, I enjoy wearing it every day as well.

CK Gold - the next offshoot in the CK-One line and a blind buy for me. The whole range is so affordable that you can take a risk. Based on the descriptions here, I had no idea what to expect: fresh, fruity, sweet, good for warmth, not for hot temperatures, feminine, unisex - it's all there. I find that always offers exciting possibilities to discover something.

I have tested quite a few fragrances in my life, but I have never come across anything like CK One Gold . Sprayed on, I thought: quite fresh, lightly citrusy, somewhat floral, (for CK One standards) relatively bitter. Not bad, but also somehow unremarkable. And then the "unremarkable" actually turned into nothing.

I picked this up yesterday because it was on sale. But I'm not sure if it was worth it. Essentially, it's a typical summer scent. It spreads a cheerful mood and I totally love ginger in the summer. It reminds me of a clumsy version of Dior Homme Sport but more rounded or down-to-earth. With DHS, you soar high - but not with Kenzo - At the regular price, I probably wouldn't have bought it, but I think it's good enough for the office. It doesn't last forever, or at least it doesn't annoy anyone :-) The sillage is also rather in the lower third. You really have to be in close contact with the skin to still smell it after 4 hours. So probably not everyone will get to enjoy this Kenzo scent :-) And I don't really understand the addition of Wild Edition...

I really enjoy the scent. It’s a gorgeous, sweet guava scent that reminds me of a green mango with sugar syrup on top. It lasts a long time, I could smell it on my clothes for a couple of days. Don’t expect it to change too much after spraying it - it’s very linear to my nose (which is NOT a bad thing). What I don’t think is appropriate is the price - ca. 280,-€ for 50 ml is insane in my opinion, although it would last you a long time as 1 spray goes a far way. I went for the 15 ml version (110,-$) instead. Although I don’t regret my purchase I want to have said that it smells very similar to an extremely affordable scent by Lattafa - Ajayeb Dubai Portrait.

I love love love this. Tried this in Seoul and it was absolutely divine. Smells like a concentrated guava juice. The guava is strong for the first 2 hours then fades into a lighter watered down version, still beautiful. On my clothes it lasted over a day. Its sad about the packaging. I found the bottle to be meh. Price wise its a little overpriced imo for 50ml. Its set at an even higher price point than xerjoff. Come to think of it, this actually does remind me of cruz del sur II from xerjoff except its using guava instead of mango.

gorgeous combination of earthy, woody and fresh fruity notes. at first u get the guava and its loud. picture a red smoothie. tangy fruits. then the oud creeps in, along with the amber, making it warm and muddy. my favorite I tried from this brand. probably wouldn't wear it in summer but every other season would be appropriate

The fragrance starts with a very rosy opening. The three types of roses dominate everything at the beginning. After about half an hour, however, they recede more and more, and the fruity notes take over. Especially the guava is very noticeable to me. What remains is a rosy, slightly sugared guava scent with extraordinary longevity and sillage. Personally, I perceive little to nothing of the oud. A few words about the bottle. The packaging and the bottle are in a dark blood red, as if Dracula himself had designed it. I personally like it, but at that price, it's also to be expected.

Hello, this fragrance simply puts you in a good mood. Of course, it's usable in summer, as long as it's not too strong for you and doesn't give you a headache; otherwise, it's an incredibly nice fruity scent with mandarin and a light sweet floral touch. The floral aspect is actually more in the background, as the main star is definitely the fruity guava. However, in my opinion, it is optimally usable in autumn or spring. Do you know those days? You know, when it's gray and gloomy outside. You have to get up and go to work, university, or school, or just take the child to kindergarten or walk the dog, etc. And you look outside and just think **....hahaha.... Well... this fragrance here somewhat destroys your negative vibes and simply creates a good mood. Then maybe a tea, coffee, cocoa, or a freshly squeezed orange juice, and the day just starts off great. Many people are sad, grumpy, and you walk past them with your fruity, sweet good mood fragrance, brightening up the day a bit. Sillage and longevity are, of course, above average with so much oil content, which is why some people also get headaches from it. Additionally, I have to mention that it is quite linear. In other words, if you don't like it in the first 10 minutes, you might as well wash it off, as well as you can with that much oil content. For me, however, it's a very good fragrance, as long as you like fruity guava like I do. So, have a nice day/evening. All the best

Encounter has different meanings in the English language: to find someone, to meet unexpectedly, to fit in conflict, or to face problems, to name a few. To me, the encounter with this scent was awkward. I blindly bought this, and I expected something dark, mysterious, sensual, and deep, alas it is a sweet and masculine floral woody scent but nothing of the adjectives as mentioned earlier. Encounter starts with a smooth mandarin orange note, which is soon spiced up by warm whiffs of mentholated cardamom. The first quarter-hour is reminiscent of a glass of rum with free minty and zesty notes of crushed cardamom seeds and mandarin's slices, the latter very similar to Italian Mandarinetto Isolabella, a classic among sweet liqueurs, with all the fresh and sweet fragrance of Mediterranean tangerines. This stage is boozy, citrus, fruity, and delicious, and altogether these notes give off a "minty" vibe. Then, a strong, slightly synthetic jasmine note takes over. But don't worry, men. It doesn't smell feminine at all. A more floral yet masculine aroma then develops. It's sweet, but not too sweet and not cloying at all, while the modern patchouli gives it a touch of dirtiness setting against the sweetness. The dry-down is a sweet and green blend of sheer woodiness and muskiness. Now you might be wondering, "where is the oud?". The answer is, "Uh... I don't know, either." If oud is in there, it must be so soft and white that I could barely smell it. Perhaps, I am accustomed to pungent, medicinal, and opulent oriental oud, frequently blended with notes of rose, orris, violet, or saffron. I am not able anymore to get this subtle one, at least not as a clear and dominant note. I have been wearing it to go to the office today, and I feel quite comfortable. However, I would say that Encounter is more of a night cologne, for instance, for clubbing or going out than it is a day one. The most disappointing thing about this fragrance is the missing notes. Cognac and oud are all mentioned in the press release but, if they are included in the scent, they are so light they can't be smelt. And it's a shame because they may have added a touch of originality to the composition. That being said, the fragrance longevity and sillage are moderate. The resulting blend is appropriate for cold weather, fall and winter evenings and nights, and ideal for young men. I look forward to reviewing its flanker Encounter Fresh! Stay tuned. -Gian

A nice Woody Spicy fragrance with Rum and Cognac Theme. Boozy, Warm and Classy. This is perfect for the cool weather, Nowadays it is rare and hard to find. It opens up with semi sweet fresh spicy, boozy and spices notes in the background then dry down is musky woody. I'm so happy that I have it in my collection and I really enjoy it. Longevity is Average. Rating : 7.5 / 10

I have owned this since the beginning of this year. It was added to the cart untested. Alongside some more expensive fragrances, I usually order a few very affordable alternatives. For under 30 euros for 100ml, you can definitely call this a bargain. Even though CK doesn't have the best reputation here, I find the fragrances to be solid and suitable for everyday wear. Even though this scent has only "earned" a rating of 5.9, I found the fragrance pyramid appealing and ordered it for that reason. First of all, it should be mentioned that this is not a typical CK for me. Compared to the rest of the range, this one stands out significantly. In a positive way. While other CK fragrances are solid everyday scents without much recognizability, this one is quite distinct. During my first brief test, I put it aside again. Probably because I unpacked too many scents at once. A few months later, I gave it a second try with more patience. It starts fruity, and I can clearly perceive the alcoholic notes. The combination of mandarin with cognac and rum is really very delicious. After a while, it becomes a bit spicier, but the pleasant base concept remains intact. Musk and oud really round off the composition wonderfully. It's a matter of taste, but I find this scent to be a great companion. For me, it's a wonderful mix of playfulness and seriousness. In my opinion, this fragrance shines best in the autumn. The sillage is really good at first but unfortunately weakens a bit. However, it remains noticeably within range. The longevity is fair for this price. There are fragrances that cost three times as much and disappear faster. The bottle is really elegant and I like it very much. Conclusion: For me, a great fragrance, especially in autumn. Definitely worth a test for the price.

The scent is very interesting and modern. Initially very strong, it settles down and becomes an intriguing companion. Unfortunately, it lasts only 6 hours on me, but it is something different and very exciting. When I met a friend in the city for a greeting and hugged her, the next day she said she could still smell the fragrance on her for at least 2 hours. A scent that stays in memory and leaves a positive impression. So, in short... Encounter has left a lasting impression and is very well received by my circle. Unfortunately not very long-lasting, but still fully meets expectations;-) By the way, on fabric (shirt, hat, etc.) the scent lasts easily 24 hours very intensely! A perfume that the modern man should at least try.

There is good news to report: CK has left the world of bland unisex fragrances and is trying something new. With the men’s fragrance Encounter, the perfumers aim even lower, targeting the suspected musk variants of many shower gels and drugstore perfumes - just to get the best out of what is presumably a modest budget. Regarding the top note, I must agree with my predecessor; it is very well done. For me, it has a hint of mandarin, forest fruits, and gummy bears - since it is very subtle, it works quite well. Surely, it is the only element in Encounter that could relate to the "typical" CK fragrances. After that, it becomes peppery-spicy, especially directly on the skin. There, Encounter is not really pleasant; ultimately, these fragrance components, which I suspect are in the musk category, are only good from a distance from the sprayed spot - but then they are really attractive, more rounded than rough, with a slight sweetness! As much as this type of scent is in everyone's noses, it is ultimately difficult to describe. The vague term musk represents for me a certain animality that emphasizes the physical presence of the wearer. Since the notes of this kind predominantly occur in very inexpensive, pocket-money-friendly fragrances, many of us have probably learned to associate it with youthfulness - this is how boys smell when they just come from practice. Some eager perfume testers from Parfumo may not think much of Encounter. Those who cannot keep their nose away from the sprayed spot will primarily perceive bitter-woody synthetics after the top note fades and will rate Encounter accordingly weak. So, out with the noses from the crook of the arm and away from the back of the hand! No sensible person walks around like that! Here, it is better to spray a bit more and wait until Encounter comes to you on its own. And it will come! Nomen est Omen, Encounter belongs to those fragrances that are directed at others, rather than focusing on the well-being of the sniffing wearer. Encounter needs the cloud, because that’s the only way it works. I like the idea of starting in the budget range and then making something good out of it. Although the price gap to the world of Axe deodorants in the case of Encounter is not that large. For perfumes that seem to follow this concept, you can also spend significantly more money (Bond No.9 Riverside Drive). Encounter is a contemporary and youthful everyday scent. It is fun if you are willing to overlook the quality standards of niche perfumery and the usual testing behavior. Oh yes, and I did not notice the now obligatory oud in new releases, let alone as a base note.

This beautiful flagship from CK has been anticipated for a long time, and the bottle has turned out to be almost as beautiful as it appeared in pictures, a real eye-catcher in any collection, go big or go home is the motto here, hats off to Calvin Klein!

In the absence of other alternatives, I purchased "Encounter" from the bargain bin for little money. Seen this way, it was a trade, as I had to get rid of the extremely unpleasant "Aqua Quorum" by Puig, which was personally the worst fresh scent I ever put on my skin. Sounds strange compared to the local reviews, but that's how it is. Maybe it was "off" or something...

Beautiful, hearty blue, enriched with a lovely effect - the bottle is top-notch! But the scent is gradually sinking into the black void of the ocean. Unfortunately not very expressive, yet for a brief moment, it is very pleasant to smell. What I miss, however, is the passionate and the animalistic in this fragrance.

Encounter actually has everything that a promising fragrance can showcase these days. Great bottle, appealing scent pyramid, big name, elaborate advertising ... Yes, even when I spray Encounter on myself, I think: “Not bad at all!” However, this only applies to the first moments. The opening is quite sweet, powdery, with a successful blend of spiciness and fruitiness.

The bottle is insane! That had to be said first! It stands there almost like a work of art, with sharp edges, dark glass, chrome in the right places, in the right amounts - modern, exotic, unusual - like from another world and not at all round and soft like One or Be, for example. Just for the appearance alone, one would almost want to get the perfume and display it.

My grandfather was an impressive man. Worldly, well-traveled, incredibly generous, and completely devoted to his granddaughters. He lived to be 93 years old, taught me that education is a gift (he would have loved to study physics but was drafted right after high school), and that traveling broadens the horizon. His scent was Aramis Eau de Toilette and whenever I catch a whiff of that fragrance today, I can't help but smile. However, I immediately thought of him when I encountered "Paradise Moon | Estēe Lauder." My grandfather also had a sweet tooth, not just for marzipan (he was originally from Lübeck), but also for dried apricots. And those come flying at you with the first spray. Wow, quite intense. I love the scent of fresh apricots, but I don't like the dried version, just as I don't enjoy eating dried fruits. The smell is quite overpowering and has a somewhat synthetic quality; I don't perceive any fine osmanthus flowers here. The leather quickly mixes in and creates a blend with the sweet, artificial apricot note that doesn't quite sit right in my nose. nulltheless, I can vividly picture my grandfather in his leather apron, standing in his woodworking shop, creating wonderful things from wood, occasionally reaching into the bag of his beloved dried apricots. I almost think I can detect a very subtle woody note in the background, but I'm quite sure my nose is playing tricks on me. The scent doesn't change much and remains this synthetic fruit-leather mix from start to finish, which doesn't really excite me. I enjoy fruity notes in perfumes, but they need to have a certain zest, which is completely absent in Paradise Moon. I find it simply sweet-leathery, intrusive, and penetrating, especially since it lasts quite well and the projection isn't too bad. So, my conclusion is that while I appreciate being reminded of my beloved grandfather through this scent, the aforementioned Aramis Eau de Toilette does that just as well, so I will be steering clear of this fragrance. I really don't want to be annoyed by artificial apricot aroma mixed with leather the whole time.

Oops, am I the first? Maybe the only one, but what must be, must be. I got this scent at Duty-Free two years ago. I found it likable. It starts fresh and then gradually the lilac comes through. But not the heavy, lush headache-inducing lilac in its full bloom and splendor, but the first early "curious" lilac that is just thinking about blooming. Whenever I wear this scent, a certain memory comes to mind. I was 16, it was the first nights of May, and during one of them, it rained. Gentle cool rain that I absolutely had to dive into!!! I was just coming home from a party, and instead of hiding at the bus stop, I danced almost into the little park, feeling the wet cool lilac kisses on my face! Delightfully sweet, refreshing, light! But as quickly as the scent comes, it is also gone again. Even for an EdT, it has relatively poor longevity. Well, spring is just short.

I think the branding of this fragrance has led to many rather negative reviews. When you hear "Oud Candy | Borntostandout," you expect a cotton candy scent complemented by oud; however, what you actually get is something completely different. The branding is not optimal in this respect, but the fragrance itself is by no means as bad as it is sometimes portrayed, just different from what one might expect. Before I reveal too much, let's get into it: - The fragrance starts, contrary to the expected sweetness, not really "candy-sweet" in the top note, but primarily with a lightly sweet, burnt sugar note that has a good nutty touch, which doesn't make it really sweet (except for the first 10 seconds, it feels), but rather nutty-spicy, almost smoky with a slight sweet undertone. - Very quickly, a woody accord comes in, which is very present; I have the feeling that the dry cedarwood here, along with the oud and leather accord, are the main players, with saffron also being distinctly noticeable. Unfortunately, caramel gets completely lost in this combination and is swallowed up; yes, a certain sweetness does emerge after countless hours, but only towards the end phase. I think the fragrance would have received much more appreciation if caramel and vanilla had been more pronounced. It could also be that the oakmoss brings in this inky, gray, and dry texture, but yes, I can't assess that because too much intertwines. - Longevity and sillage are brutal, typical BTSO Extrait... Overall, for me, it's a typical BTSO powerhouse that promises one thing; presence and dominance. Does the name fit? Absolutely not, or only to some extent; for me, the sweetness is missing in the drydown to make the fragrance more appealing to the masses, but that's exactly what makes it so exciting from my perspective, this dry-oriental aspect in the drydown, with slight sweet touches. ... definitely test it beforehand... it's too special for a blind buy :)

For me, a shock - super synthetic for the first 3 hours and I don't smell any of the notes mentioned above (especially the top and heart notes) - almost like "burnt" yet still special. The sillage definitely has a recognizable quality - you sit in your cloud. After 3 hours, I perceive more leather, oud, and caramel, and I like the scent a bit more. For me (or on my skin), it's not a fragrance as expected and liked (also in comparison to the other 3 fragrances of this edition), but definitely a special and strong scent with recognition value.

Reveal is an Autumn / Winter scent from the house of Calvin Klein. This is one of the better releases from CK in my opinion. It is a sweet and boozy scent perhaps touching the gourmand area. There is pear brandy, Tonka bean and amber notes which seem to be blended well. There is a little spiciness also but cant detect from which note. Reveal has good Longevity and also the silage to me is above average on my skin. This scent tends to be overlooked and it is usually inexpensive. If you are a fan of sweeter boozy fragrances with some body this i think would be a decent buy and worthy of collection . I dont think this would be an everyday office scent as it could be perhaps be too much for some noses but more of an evening scent or something to cut through cold Winters day. A decent winter scent which is underrated in my opinion Overall 7.5

THIS is a SCORE people; $25 at any TJ Max, and it is a KILLER performer. Longevity and sillage are RIDICULOUSLY good. The sweet dark scent reminds me of my all time favorite (And unfortunately discontinued) DKNY leaded fragrance... especially upon opening. While it’s not completely the same vibe, the fact that it even REMOTELY catches that train makes me EXTREMELY happy... and again... it’s $25 at any TJ Maxx. It loses that magic touch as it slowly dries down, but it is indeed an extremely enjoyable scent. It dries into a leathery feel that projects very nicely. The longevity I get is an easy 10+ hours, and at least half of that is projecting a trail that people can’t help to notice. It is indeed a unique scent; very sweet and very dark, but if you like those darker, boozy, leathery notes you can’t go wrong.... and like I said people...

This is One of the best Calvin Klein Men's Perfumes, Boozy, Sweet, Ambery, Sexy and Fruity. Reveal has special notes and Unique note : Agave. I bought it blind-buy after watching it on YouTube and I read positive comments. SPECIAL Thanks to Scent Land on YouTube. It opens up with sweet boozy fruity and warm spices notes in the background then dry down is sweet Ambery. It reminds me of Azzaro Amber Fever in the dry down but the opening is not the same. Reveal was launched in 2015 before Azzaro Amber Fever. It is suitable for the spring ,fall and winter. Four Master perfumers created Reveal by Calvin Klein. Longevity is good, Highly Recommended. Thumbs Up. Rating : 8 /10

Reveal Man had been on my wish list for several months or even years. Even though the newer CK fragrances are often torn apart or rated rather mediocre, I must praise this brand. Starting, of course, with the price. Many scents I like can already be found for about 30 euros for 100ml. The performances are average to good. I own many from the brand, especially loving Encounter. This Reveal was also allowed to join my collection. I purchased the small 30ml version for about 20 euros. However, in many shops, you can get 100ml for about 25 euros. Very fair and affordable. Bought and tested at the beginning of the year. Although I had never tested it before, I found the pyramid, the price, and the concept intriguing, and I wanted to have it. After testing it once, I wasn't very impressed. A scent that could definitely polarize. Especially the top note, which lasts a long time, is very special and takes some getting used to. Even though this combination is very creative and unique, it will definitely not appeal to everyone. With this scent, it is rather difficult to pick out individual notes. Pear brandy is definitely in the foreground alongside ginger. Here, candied ginger is prominent. The scent definitely has a decent amount of sweetness... A sweet ginger note, enhanced by tonka. The lovely note reminds me of a fair, especially due to the boozy brandy note. Pear brandy! The pear is not entirely distinguishable, but recognizable through a wonderful fruity note. It also has a kind of lavender touch. Initially very polarizing, later rather softly cuddly, while it retains its DNA throughout. Great! Especially after 1-2 hours, it goes in a wonderful direction. The performance for me is fantastic. I don't understand how some rate the performance so low just because they don't like the scent. This is the case with many fragrances here. Some with high ratings are also overvalued in performance. If you're unsure: You can also leave the performance open. Here, I give a clear 10 out of 10 for longevity, as it lasts about 12 hours on me. The sillage is also very good over long distances, and even after many hours, there's still something noticeable without being too close to the skin. Top. Especially for fans of sweet scents, it's worth a test. Particularly suitable for colder temperatures. Thanks to good performance, it's also suitable for outdoor and club use. However, it should definitely be tested. Not everybody's darling. For me, it is very likable due to its individuality.

Beyond the boundaries. Conveying expansiveness. Providing familiarity. Liberating and redeeming from conventions. A plea for niche in the mainstream. A special leather. Diffuse. Airy. Hard to grasp. A violet leaf leather. Reminiscent of - of course - Fahrenheit. But different. Softer. Only hinted gasoline. Along with licorice. Sea salt. Love apple. Freshness. And a moderate, balsamic-amber base, whose warmth feels delicately cookie-like with a touch of tonka. Everything muted. Flowing into each other like watercolors. A washed-out scent in the truest sense. Without clear contours. But with wonderful contrasts. Its effectiveness lies in the pleasant restraint of all components, which nevertheless form a unity. A distinctive scent image. A warm-spicy, spherical leather with a mysteriously fruity-aquatic touch. One for all those for whom black leather is too intense, iris leather too fine, and violet leaf leather too harsh. Those who can handle synthetics. A lot of synthetics. But not with intrusive projecting chemical bombs. And those who desire to smell different. Without sacrificing likability. For me, the ideal leather scent. With a wonderfully aromatic, unusual aura. Slightly bitter. Slightly sweet. Slightly warm. Slightly spicy. Slightly fresh. A very independent DNA. For me, one of the most unconventional in the designer sector. Bold for Calvin Klein standards. Out of the box. As a mainstream release (product design: Ann Gottlieb) brave. Probably too brave, as it was - launched in early 2015 - already discontinued. Last productions to my knowledge in 2019. A scent that captivates me consistently. A rediscovery. Tested in 2017. Fascinated by salt and fruit back then. But fundamentally not understood. Yet always kept in mind. And then during the retest four years later. Again: salt and fruit and - wait - licorice. Wow. That can't go together. But it does. Even wonderfully. Unique, without being cumbersome. This is ensured by the subtle base that binds and rounds everything off. And Rodrigo Flores-Roux (now Vice President of Givaudan), a specialist in the use of unusual ingredients as well as the creation of aromatic leather fragrances (John Varvatos). It only dawned on me after some time that this is also leather. Because it is so skillfully and calmly woven in (shower gel and aftershave balm convey the impression more clearly, by the way). For me, a small miracle. So different, so (always) wearable. And the pleasure lasts. Even in the radiance. In a considerate way. Performance is not important to me, but here I am glad that others notice it. And about the fact that such conceptual gems are still being produced in the mainstream from time to time. I want to call out to the companies: Be bolder again!

Did we really need another CK fragrance? --> Since everyone deserves multiple chances & I believe there has been some change in the CK leadership lately: yes, why not? Does the men's version have more justification for existence than the women's version? --> I could only briefly test last year's women's version... but both seem to be on equal footing.

New Calvin Klein fragrances certainly don't inspire me to dance with joy out of anticipation. However, when you come across one while strolling, you don't leave it completely untouched; hope dies last. The bottle looks more appealing in photos than it actually is. The contents visually remind one of a synthetic all-purpose aqua fragrance.
The start of the new fragrance year once again presents the perfumery standard bearers with - did anyone really have hope? - a concoction that does not deserve the name "perfume.

At first, one can perceive a very intense sweet fruity note that smells like a typical, still somewhat delicate unripe pear and brings with it a wonderful crisp juiciness, leading me to guess pear liqueur instead of pear brandy.

Reveal by Calvin Klein is a rather unpleasant representative of the cinnamon scent faction. This fragrance family, where vanilla or cinnamon practically envelops you permanently, has, apart from a few exceptions, only a right to exist during Christmas for me. With Reveal, it starts off sweet and fruity in the top notes. I mainly smell pear and a leaden heavy sweetness.

I have loved this fragrance for decades. It enchants me into a world full of secrets and mystical realms. Woody, spicy, and yet playful. I wander through the forest and the freshly mown cornfields. Dark, mysterious, almost threatening clouds gather and cast everything in a mysterious, gloomy light. Only a few sunrays manage to break through the dark clouds, transforming everything into a golden light. A storm is brewing. You can already smell the rain and the freshly mown fields in the warm, stormy air. The world seems to stand still for a moment. But what do I see there? A beautiful mythical creature hides behind the trees and has been watching me the whole time...and I start dreaming again. This scent takes me to unimaginable worlds...again and again, as soon as I spray it on...I feel unique and special through Spellbound. No other perfume has ever achieved that. Eva M. January 6, 2024 A Was this review helpful? a 0 I No 0

I am a child of the eighties, yet this is only reflected in my passion for fragrances. Loud, sweet, opulent, always in search of THE scent!!! The blame lies with none other than Mom. I could describe my childhood through various scent memories. The first thing I perceived even before I opened my eyes in the morning was the lovely fragrance of my mother. The sillage gently woke me, flowing from the bathroom into the bedroom. Later, when I became interested in perfumes, I gradually remembered all the scents. From Paris to sun moon stars. In contrast to me, she used bottle after bottle. Since I became a mother myself last year and am now on parental leave, I like to combine our walks with short detours to my fragrance dealer, who, oh how wonderful, now fills ten ml of scent for ten euros. Packaging and bottles often attract me like magic, so I neatly sweep one or two notes that I don't like under the proverbial rug, beautifully adorned. Were the 80s perhaps also superficial?! Thus, I ended up testing this Estee Lauder. The name sounded promising as well. I took a quick sniff from the test strip because little Parfumo started to fuss and detected nothing disturbing, so I decided to take it and go. While walking, I sprayed the fragrance on my wrist and waited. A sweet, juicy scent enveloped me on that sunny January morning; it must have been the apricot. It felt incredibly familiar. Rose and lily of the valley flirt a bit with the carnation, but rather unsuccessfully. Medusa, dressed in fine satin, eats honey bread while the snakes spew apricot jam. It doesn't undergo much development. The fragrance has, as expected, a high radiance and lasts on my skin for eight hours until it is only very faint. You will definitely be noticed with this sillage, and some might even get Alien headaches. Fragrances of the 80s unite :)) Memories of beautiful moments interpreted in a modern way, as there's a bit of Lush shop in there too. Similarities to sun moon stars and Narcisse are evident. Both fragrances were favorites of my mother. May my little Parfumo also grow up with a scent DNA that he associates with love, trust, and beautiful memories.

An absolutely fresh and also zesty surprise. In search of something invigorating and fresh, I stumbled upon this body fragrance and fell in love immediately. I made comparisons with Biotherm scents, but this one stood out. The light, zesty ginger note is refreshing and invigorating, lasts a long time, and you feel wonderfully fresh.

I was very curious what a fragrance called Mud would smell like. Especially with those pretty, not very muddy sounding notes. Now that I tested it, I think the name kind of fits, but kind of doesn't. It doesn't smell dirty in any way, not even particularly earthy, but it does have a muddy texture, at least in the beginning. Imagine a clay mask that slowly dries. The scent starts out like a mix of autumn leaves, dark plum liqueur and powdery rose. The plum vanishes first and the whole scent turns very dry and powdery for a while. After a while the chocolate and almond move forward, so it turns a tad sweeter and creamier again. I get hints of a barely sweetened chocolate pudding made with almond milk. Unfortunately, the cold, dry undertone never really leaves and it bothers me. I enjoy the chocolate note in here a lot, it's milky without being waxy or extremely sugary, but the rose and elemi make me think someone poured a bowl of potpourri into my pudding. I'm sure eating that would be much worse than just smelling it though. The scent is not bad and also quite unique, but ultimately it's not for me.

This is a gourmand for people who do and don't love gourmands. Its strong without being overpowering, sweet without being candy, and it has complexity. The scent does start strong creamy and nutty. That settles into a dark sweet chocolate where I can pick up a little bit of the plum and rose that adds depth to the chocolate. When it drys down its a beautiful warm, musky, sweet wood that is close to your skin. This scent projects just enough that you can smell it on yourself but you won't upset everyone at the office. The scent also lasted the full day on my skin, over 6 hours.

Very well done gourmand. Unisex, comfy, I get the comparison with Eau Duelle but here it’s simple, what is not a bad thing. The chocolate is sweet but not clingy, it’s not a teenager perfume - this is adult perfumery. It’s comfy, easy, but yet sexy in a subtle way. I like this a lot, for my collection would be a bit redundant but it’s a solid choice for any gourmand lover.

Mud is primarily a creamy scent for me. Creamy, clean, and slightly sweet. Almond milk with a touch of plum and barely noticeable chocolate. Overall, it is relatively light and becomes quite close to the skin fairly quickly. At least, that’s my impression. My girlfriend can actually detect a bit of chocolate. I personally have some trouble really recognizing chocolate. But that’s just how it is in our world of scents. Fragrance impressions are always subjective. The scent starts for me with a creamy almond milk, sweetened with a bit of plum. In addition, there is a really soft and pleasant rose. Furthermore, the Mud here even comes across as slightly fresh. Then it becomes noticeably closer to the skin. The plum recedes, and a bit of sandalwood, vanilla, and amber emerge. Everything is kept very subtle and calm. I can’t say much more about the Mud. It’s a bit difficult to define everything precisely here. The performance is okay. But I actually expected more.

Another test candidate from BTSO, which unfortunately did not surprise positively again, but at least performs significantly better than the Naked Laundry . Provocative branding - as always - but this time the execution is not exactly groundbreaking. Let's get into it: - The opening is restrained; a milky mélange with a bit of almond; that's it. Really nothing more, nothing less, the opening disappointed me a bit, to be honest, but then the beautiful plum slowly seeps through, synthetic, but quite alright. - Then a little bit of chocolate comes in, but very subtle and restrained, blending into this creamy plum base. Again, neither fish nor fowl, somehow everything, but then again nothing. At least better than the opening, but still not groundbreaking. In the drydown, the fragrance then transitions into a creamy-woody vanilla base, not abrasive, not special, just "something". - H/S better than Naked Laundry , feeling like it's in the middle, nothing groundbreaking. Overall, you can tell, the fragrance has also disappointed me a bit, not speechless, but not particularly inspired to type this up either :) Just as uninspired as the creators of the fragrance probably were.

I guess CK were aiming at a Chance Eau Fraiche type fragrance that would please everyone - any age, any fashion, any weather...anyone else find this one a little Zzzzzzzz? Instead of being universally appealing (like ChanceEF) I find SB a bit middle-of-the-road, banal, bland....dare I say it, down-right-dull. This does not mean that Sheer Beauty is unpleasant in any way - it really isn't. SB is nice & safe & as pleasant as a clean & fruity shampoo, a £1 body spray, a spring-flowers room deoderiser....but who is going to part with good money for that? Not me. To break it down: I can easily detect that generic CK lemon-butter-biscuit base (found in CKin2U et all) with a thin, watery-red-berry note & an all too familiar sharp-floral with a touch of jasmine. A high-pitched, cleaned-to-a-bleach-white synthy musk whines like tinnitus from first spritz to dry-down. There is a strong alcohol finish to this scent - not far off a cologne - with a sour, wilted stems edge. Add a shot of some aspartame-filled bitter citrus drink & you just about have it. Lasts a few hours with a tame projection & not much development - lasts gasps are of a sour, washing-powder musk. So who will buy it? Those who need a clean, unobtrusive scent for work....perhaps. Chanel-worshipers .......possibly. People who are a little confused by scent & enjoy the safety of the body-spray.......Zzzzzzzz. Sorry, I just lost interest.

"Sheer Beauty" is a bit generic and normally not my type of fragrance. But since many of the heavy chypres I love and the vintages I adore are not always well-suited for my job, I was looking for a light, clean, fresh, mainstream scent to carry with me in my bag. "Sheer Beauty" was heavily reduced in my local perfumery, probably because it's going to be discontinued. But when you compare it to Marc Jacob's "Daisy Eau So Fresh" or the latest "Chloé Love Story", you'll find that it is prettier than those, and less sweet and fruity. The peachy opening is the best part of the fragrance (I love peach-scents). No masterpiece, but not worse than all the other synthetic light fruity-floral somethings on the market. I also like the bottle-design and prefer it to the plastic, juvenile and trashy stuff done by Marc Jacob's.

Sheer Beauty by Calvin Klein may be severely lacking in originality but that doesn't make it any less pretty. This simplistic and fresh floral blend is perfect for Summer and compliments almost every skin type. Although I prefer the original Beauty, this sheer flanker has many likable qualities. For starters, it's inoffensive, so women that aren't fans of anything too 'perfumey' are sure to love this. Another positive aspect is its fresh and clean approach. To my nose it smells like an expensive floral shampoo. Sheer Beauty is not a fragrance that will blow you over backwards, but it is very pleasant and wearable. Both my friend and I enjoyed this fragrance when we smelt it together a few days ago, so it has both of our ticks of approval. The bottle for Sheer Beauty is really quite girly and fun. I would proudly display this bottle on my dresser. The main notes according to my nose are as follows; fresh jasmine, green, zesty bergamot, musk, sandalwood and a subtle hint of red berries. I unfortunately couldn't detect the peach bellini accord on my skin. If I had a bottle of Sheer Beauty, I honestly don't think I'd wear it very often. I'd save the bottle for Summer, but would probably forget about it when the weather is most appropriate. I would recommend that you buy it only if you truly love it and know that you'll wear it often. Original review written: September 2012.

Sometimes I don't understand why some fragrances are received so poorly here. This is the case for me with Sheer Beauty from the good old Calvin Klein. The scent immediately captivated me - one of the few fragrances that made me head straight to the checkout. The special feature here is the Bellini note. Bellini is a cocktail made from Prosecco, sparkling wine or champagne, white peach, and a bit of sugar syrup. Furthermore, I can especially detect the lily (very subtle here) and the vanilla blossom. The overall impression of the fragrance is fresh, clean, and well-groomed. It is also worth mentioning that Sheer Beauty lasts a whole workday and has a decent sillage (you don't leave a trail behind you, but that doesn't always have to be the case, in my opinion). So, I simply love this fragrance and always feel attractive with it!

This fragrance is said to possess a transparent sensuality, embedded in fresh, floral, and fruity notes. It sounds quite good in principle, but it can be implemented differently. Sheer primarily means pure; I would rather translate it as gossamer. In this case, the fragrance starts off quite alcohol-heavy. Bergamot is initially fresh and sparkling here, but soon gets overwhelmed by synthetic fruit notes. The peach Bellini accord sounds exclusive, but unfortunately, it is rather banal. There’s no sweet, round peach that feels velvety and makes you want to rub your nose against it. No, it's spiked with toothbrush bristles and comes off quite scratchy and artificial. The red berries are quite sweet, but fortunately also a bit sour. This just allows the top note to curve around and become softer and more pleasant towards the heart. The scratchy peach takes a backseat, but doesn’t completely disappear at first. Here, the fragrance feels slightly aquatic, subtly fresh, soapy, sweet-sour fruity, and gently floral. Unfortunately, it has a synthetic touch throughout and is quite insignificant for me. The flowers blend into a nonspecific mixture. So, no luck with the pink lily accord either. Towards the base, the fragrance fades gently and unremarkably. This happens to me after about four hours, which I find quite poor for an EDT. Accordingly, the sillage is also rather weak. For my standards, I had applied quite a bit, but received neither positive nor negative feedback. Consequently, the fragrance is not wrong for work or leisure, can generally be used in various situations, and fits well with all seasons. I can't say that the fragrance is fundamentally bad. Unfortunately, there are just too many perfumes that smell similar. It lacks that certain something that reminds me of a situation, a pleasant feeling, a beautiful memory, or an extraordinary place. Moreover, I miss the sensuality. The sensuality or eroticism in this fragrance is comparable to a three-second lap dance you can enjoy in the cinema when someone squeezes through the rows of seats. (Sorry, I couldn't resist ;-)). Unfortunately, it is not a pure but a flimsy beauty that cannot score points for originality. For fans of unobtrusive, fresh, and fruity florals, it might be a must. For everyone else, it's a fragrance that you can test and then comfortably forget. Thanks to Ti for sending it.

This fragrance is a jack-of-all-trades, it always works!.. I prefer to use it on very warm days, as other scents become too cloying for me.. I get very easily nauseous, especially when vanilla or incense is in the air.. My worst experience was once on a bus, when a woman had sprayed Opium. Sprayed is really an understatement; you could think she had bathed in it.

For me, the best of all Calvin Klein fragrances, easily holding its own against very expensive creations. A brilliant blend of softness (musk, vanilla) and freshness (bergamot, peach) that suits all occasions. I have never been approached about a fragrance so often. A very beautiful scent progression is noticeable: First, a crisp freshness.

I wore "Sheer Beauty" in my early 20s. The scent is very feminine, soft, gentle, and smells like a lovely peach. I still find the fragrance very beautiful, but unfortunately, the longevity and sillage are not good, which means you only get to enjoy it for a short time. If both were better, I would definitely recommend it to girls and young women.

It was my birthday gift. Something biting throws everything into chaos, creating disharmony. A contrasting element that my nose keeps bumping into and which simply does not round off the entire composition, but rather stands out like an unnecessary leftover. Perhaps it’s just the whole fruit aspect in this composition that reminds me of sour candies?!

I have thought long and hard about whether to write something about this fragrance. But I find it so boring and unremarkable that it drives me crazy. To me, Sheer Beauty smells of peach from start to finish and also of that unpleasant scent that self-tanners often leave behind. And then SB is already gone. I have tested the sample 3 times now and am throwing it away.

This is a lighter summer version of the floral-clean "Pleasure fragrance," which was launched in 1995. If you don't like the original Pleasures scent, you should not consider Eau Fraiche, as the new variant is not far from the first creation. Why would Lauder change much about this bestseller? true to the motto "Never change a winning team," the differences are hardly noticeable. Peony, jasmine, lilies, pink pepper... all these components remain intact, the light lilac top note is not present in the heart (disappointment for me - I would have liked more lilac). The fragrance comes across as a bit fresher and greener than the regular "Pleasures," but since I could never really warm up to the neat original version, "Eau fraiche" is also not on my wish list. "Pleasures Eau fraiche" smells somewhat artificial-synthetic and has that special charm of "clean person"... so a clinically clean, sterile aura. "For the sheer pleasure of it" is the tagline for the fragrance. No pleasure for me. By the way: the pink plastic cap on the bottle does not look particularly elegant.

Since my mom owns all the Pleasures fragrances, I was glad to find another flanker that she doesn't yet have in her collection. Pleasures Eau Fraiche. I like all the Pleasures scents, but they suit my mother better than they do me. I think they all have a charming girlish quality, just like my mom, even though she is 29 years older than me. Still, they also convey elegance - in a very natural way. And Eau Fraiche has achieved that once again. The character of the original Pleasures shines through clearly, but the Fraiche lives up to its name, as it is even a touch fresher without losing longevity and expression. The green notes are invigorating, and the lily is subtly elegant. Then I am delighted by full lilac and bright jasmine, spiced with mild pepper. The sandalwood, mixed with patchouli, provides a smooth finish. The fragrance suits a girlish lady, like my mother, perfectly. I look forward to surprising her with Eau Fraiche.

Oops; no one has commented on this yet? Well, then I'll just take care of it! This fragrance sample called out to me this morning: "Spray me on, come on, finally spray me on! How long am I supposed to just lie here in the drawer?" So, quite biased, I generously sprayed the sample on my décolletage and freshly washed hair. Mmh; fresh; mmh, probably just another one of those scents with no distinctive character; just spray and evaporate, I think to myself... At first, it smells super fresh and bright; after about half an hour, the jasmine comes in. Jasmine, jasmine, I can identify it precisely; explosively, just like nature is currently throwing out all the greenery that wants to emerge from the earth in any way. After three hours, Eau fraiche is still present, and not just in a simple way; it now conveys a certain elegance; mmh, my outfit today, blue jeans and a checkered blouse, does not match at all, mmh, I wouldn't have expected that. I'm amazed! After more than six hours, the jasmine is still there; weaker, but the elegance has faded by now, and a hint of peony comes in, but very faintly. Conclusion: A jasmine office scent for spring/summer! If I were to receive it as a gift, I would use it, but it's not a must-have for me. (The sample will still be used up tomorrow, pffft!) :-)

I already mentioned that black exerts an enormous attraction on me. So here as well. ...and then also at Kenzo where I love the fragrances so much. I just couldn't help myself again and had to somehow get my hands on the bottle. I really had to search for a long time until I could catch this cat. There it was, black and slender, standing before me. Very, very pretty, I think. The scent opens with freshly picked wild strawberries, which have a very unique, special taste. A hint of clementines mixes in, making it all very delicious. And then slowly the velvet paw awakens and floral nuances blend in, caressing the preceding fruits.
