Imagine a cat rubbing against your legs; that's how peony, tuberose, and jasmine gently play around the nose. But if you want to pet the little kitty now, it pulls back and gives you a swipe with its velvet paw. Because now amber and patchouli come into play. I hardly perceive any musk. It takes a little moment for everything to merge into a unity, but this is by no means disturbing. This unity from the flowers to the patchouli is truly a beautiful blend. Different from what one usually knows from the fragrances of the Kenzo house. I absolutely did not expect this, but I am more than positively surprised. The scent is different. What I find a bit disappointing is the longevity. After about 8 hours, the fun is almost over. Very, very faintly and with a little imagination, you can still sense a hint of amber/patchouli. I really would have expected a bit more. But well, it is what it is. The little kitty just doesn't feel like playing with me anymore after eight hours. I want to give her some peace.

When reading the title Jeu d'amour felin, I thought of a cuddly kitten with a blue silk ribbon around its neck, purring as it snuggles up to me. But far from it. This cat is a wild beast, a dangerous predator that should not be trifled with. The game of love with her is a game with fire. Of course, very alluring. Who hasn’t burned their fingers on love? And it is precisely the dark, unpredictable side of life that is the exciting one. The unknown makes us ponder and captivates us at the same time. Bitter experiences do not help in love. The flame flickers too enticingly, and one must always draw closer and closer, even though one knows the devastating power of fire. The sparkling sparks are thrilling - and the glow illuminates the dark night. The heart warms - until the heat becomes unbearable - and it hurts. The scent is wild, unruly, and carries danger - but it fascinates at the same time. Falling in love is often like a shocking natural disaster. U2 have put it into words and melody: Oh love You say in love there are no rules Oh love Sweetheart You're so cruel

DGAF is my first try of the house of Borntostandout, via their Dark & Drunk Discovery Set, purchased at Twisted Lily, a spicy blend of incense, pepper, sandalwood, rose, musk, sage, and bergamot, a bit fresh, green, warm, and resinous, but mostly spicy and woody, really a classy, versatile blend that, while more apt for cooler weather in terms of its spiciness is still pleasant enough and not too heavy for year-round wearing. It’s sophisticated, feels a bit reminiscent of some classics, while still being a bit modern and provocative, very nicely put together. I immediately regard it as an apt cold weather signature scent, perhaps a little masculine stereotypically but overall pretty unisex. I recall seeing one source describe it as an aromatic fougere but I wouldn’t quite call it a fougere, myself. As with the rest of the line, DGAF is EDP concentration and priced at $210 for 50ml, sold via a few boutiques / shops in the US like Ministry of Scent and Max Aroma. Overall it’s a great first impression of the house, even though it was seeing Drunk Maple that first drew me to the line. DGAF performs well and is very useful and classy, and the pricing is fair enough for current nice perfumery, but it’s not cheap, considering that something Robert Graham Valour accomplishes a similar result, in my opinion, whilst being much more modestly priced. I wish a travel size were available for further testing / less volume, but I’ll have to consider this one some more, though it is quite great, overall. 8 out of 10

This is a smokey limeade which sounds weird but works really well. Smokey like incense, not like smoldering wood. I typically don't like bergamot, it tends to overpower every other note and make the fragrance linear. This fragrance balances the sweet and bitter citrus with incense and herbal notes, making it aromatic and fresh. Its a fresh take on a commonly used fragrance note and while leaning more masculine, it can be fairly unisex. It has a sweet and creamy dry down that is typical of BTSO fragrances but stands out from the others in being more creative and tamer than the rest of their line. This fragrance lasted all day, about 7 hours, on my skin. This is more of a skin scent, so not much in the way of projection but that is okay. Its $205 for 50ml. This would be a great everyday and office appropriate or business event fragrance.

With its fresh, citrusy, slightly green notes and creaminess, it feels to me like a shower gel, but in a luxurious and, above all, more expensive way. In my opinion, it's perfect for after sports or warmer days when there's a lot to do, as the scent simply keeps you feeling fresh :)

I always order samples first, without expectation and without a plan of what I'm actually looking for. I read the descriptions and try to feel the scenes and moments. DGAF is not hard to feel for me. So I spray it on and my first thought is: I would f*ck that guy! A packed nightclub with great, loud music and purple spotlights from the ceiling. Everything else is black, the beats thump under the hot skin of the dancers, who follow the tingling rhythm, swimming in the wave of euphoria, inhaling the pheromones of others. Sweat beads drip onto the vinyl floor. Ice cubes clink in expensive drinks somewhere on a high floor above a pulsating city. Nightlife. A hand slips under a shirt. The pulse quickens. Someone flinches. Heavy, luminous, sweet haze wafts through the room. The mind slowly slips away, thoughts turn into mere feelings. And prayers. Oh God, please...!

I honestly could not smell a thing when I tried this fragrance. I'm definitely anosmic to certain notes in Eternity Moment. I thought it was a bad tester bottle at first, but I tried it again in another store and there was still no luck. There was the slightest hint of jasmine after about 5 minutes, but I had to really press my nose to my wrist to smell this one.

I got Eternity Moment quite cheaply on eBay after a brief test sniff in a drugstore. I definitely wouldn't have bought it at full price. First of all, I wonder why it is associated with Eternity. In my opinion, they don't have much in common. Calvin Klein has a bit of a reputation for being very mainstream and unremarkable when it comes to fragrances. In the case of Eternity Moment, this is quite justified. This floral-fruity scent can also be found at half the price, and the longevity isn't the best either. However, what makes Eternity Moment enjoyable is that the individual components of the fragrance blend wonderfully together. This sets it apart from the average drugstore scent. It is not sharp or overpowering, but light and pleasant, as long as you don't overdo it - better to carry it with you and reapply. I can most clearly detect the lychee scent. Lychee does have a somewhat sharp note; you have to like that, but here it is still quite subtle, and the little flowers in the heart note round it off beautifully. I would describe Eternity Moment as an all-rounder. Any woman could wear it in any season, but rather during the day. For the evening, it simply lacks that certain something. But you can't go wrong here. That's the advantage of this interchangeability. It has no recognizability. I would most closely compare it to Laura by Laura Biagiotti. Maybe it's the jasmine, but Laura is a bit more aquatic, while Eternity Moment is considerably more floral and sweet. So... if you want to smell pleasant but remain beautifully inconspicuous, this Calvin Klein scent is a good choice. But don't expect anything extraordinary.

Outside, it is pouring rain and the wind is blowing cold around the corners. Although I am a child of winter, I can't make much of this season. It is dark, you are bundled up to the point of being unrecognizable and look like a Michelin man. Skiing doesn't please me either, as I often have to chase after the runaway skis after sorting out my limbs. Oh yes, and then there's the morning, sleepy snow shoveling. Even the little dog doesn't want to go outside, and so we gaze longingly into the garden, which is also wearing its winter coat. I look into my fragrance shelf, and there I spot a charmingly graceful pink package - Eternity Moment. I spray it, and the scent brings about a pleasant weather change - at least in my mood. Pomegranate blossom and lychee speak of spring with its delicate pastel colors. The jasmine also envelops me in a white and floral embrace. The water lily reminds me of smooth ponds, where the sun gently reflects and goldfish curiously peek out of the water. The rosewood is spicy and noble, bathing the scene in a moody evening red. I snuggle my face against my dog's ears and whisper to him: Spring will come again. And he understands me perfectly.

The role of the stepchild flanker in the Eternity family, the black sheep that no one really knows why it was placed THERE, does not do justice to this super-pleasing bouquet. At the Eternity family celebration, it impresses with euphoric presence and cheerful attitude, keeping a clear distance from the brash and dominant big showcase sister. Yes, this moment may be mainstream, yes it is an endearing crowd-pleaser, and fans of Filippo Sorcinelli and the like will only smile mildly, but it makes up for its lack of complexity. With its radiant, all-encompassing nature, a core that is untouched by evil, a naive freshness that promises a mostly friendly weather situation, and allows one to soar into bright realms emotionally. This truly allows for a fabulous celebration of the moment, and the little sister has no other demands anyway.

The commonality with the beautiful big sister lies in the jasmine, musk, and sandalwood. The relationship is not immediately recognizable. The scent opens with a very large green. I always thought it was white lily, but now that I have the fragrance notes here, I finally know what it is - guava!!! I have eaten this fruit many times, and in nature as well as in this scent, it lacks sweetness and fruitiness. The fruit tastes unusually floral like its floral-green scent. No trace of raspberry. Now I also finally understand why the perfume simply does not want to lose its greenness over time. The flowers in the top note are repeated in the heart note. Passionflower, jasmine, and lily are again flowers that lack sweetness and charm. The base notes are very pleasant - they remind me of the unbeatable original. It is clearly a spring fragrance, as in this season characterized by buds, nature is just waiting to unfold its full green. Spring flowers smell only lightly, with a few exceptions, but very fine. It has an extremely long-lasting power and strong scent intensity. It is suitable for all age groups, but fits better with adult women, as the jasmine is very dominant and it lacks a bit of sweetness. Overall, it is a fresh-green scent with floral traces. This makes it invigorating and energizing. I use it to wake up, as my favorite fragrances are too delicate and romantic for this purpose.

Eternity Moment is a present yet unobtrusive floral-fresh scent with white musk. The main impression for me is "freshly washed." A very clean, laundry detergent-like floral fragrance, slightly aquatic, a bit green, with a few pink roses, a few snow-white jasmine flowers, a hint of raspberry (did you use Princess Lillifee shampoo to wash your hair?

Few perfumes turn out to be as ambivalent for me as "Eternity Moment". After a quick test on paper, I snagged a 100 ml bottle as a bargain. Unfortunately, it was a bad purchase, because what had hinted at being a light, warm fragrance on the paper strip turned out to be unbearable for me in everyday life.

When I tested it, I smelled white lilies. I once received a bouquet like that as a gift, and when the buds opened, they released an incredible fragrance. While testing, I immediately felt transported back to that moment, but now I see no trace of it in the pyramid. Maybe it's the water lilies or the passion flowers - although they have their own distinct scent.

I first got to know Eternity Moment in 2004 when it was released. At that time I was 20 and received it as a Christmas gift from my ex-boyfriend. I found it beautiful, but somehow I wasn't ready for Eternity Moment yet, as I was floating on a Poison cloud! ;) Thus, the scent was too light for me...

So, my resolution to not buy any more perfume has apparently gone out the window. I just had to get it at Müller during the bargain sale. This is certainly not a scent that will turn heads. But it won't stand out negatively either. And that's exactly what I wanted for my collection. One that I can wear well during my 12-hour shifts in the summer heat.

Flower Summer 2011 meets the skin with a soft litchi scent blended with mandarin. The litchi here doesn't smell like the fresh juicy one in Madly EDT, but a rippen litchi because of the tartness brought in by mandarin. Soon the unmistakable incense-like Flower sharpness comes out along with violet and musk. However, it stays very soft and close to skin. I don't find it particularly powdery either. Those who were a little scared of the sharpness and powdery texture of the original might still be able to like it. The longevity reaches around 5 hours. A tender fragrance for spring and summer, there is no doubt, though there are also other interesting choices in the same floral-fruity category.

BTSO Nuts is an impressive creation that closely mirrors the character of DS & Durga Pistachio, thanks to its shared core of pistachio, almond, vanilla and patchouli. The resemblance is striking, yet Nuts introduces its own personality with a sweeter opening, where caramel, rum and honey gently linger in the air before fading almost imperceptibly on the skin. Unlike Les Nobles Essences Mirage Gourmand, a full-bodied gourmand from the same perfumer, Nuts avoids veering into overly sweet or “foodie” territory. Instead, it strikes a sophisticated balance, making it a 100% unisex fragrance that anyone can wear confidently. This versatility aligns perfectly with my personal preference for gender-neutral scents. The subtle presence of tobacco and sesame in the background adds depth without overwhelming the composition - a welcome restraint, as tobacco and coffee notes in some fragrances can dominate and disrupt harmony. The projection and longevity are impressive. I only used a single spray on my wrist when I first unboxed it and even after three hours, I could still detect the syrupy notes lingering in the air and the nutty nuances on my skin. Hours later, the delicate skin scent continued to tease my nose, making me want to keep sniffing my wrist. IMHO, Nuts is effortlessly adaptable, suitable for any time of day and any season, making it a valuable addition to any collection. My only wish? A 100ml bottle at this price point would feel more justified.

Sampling Borntostandout Nuts (formerly Happy Nuts, as best I can tell), a fittingly nut-led blend that has a syrupy sweet quality mixed with a heady sharpness via the combination of the pistachio and almond, two of the sharper nutty notes in fragrance, though both the sweetness and sharpness become toned with time as the fragrance dries down, becoming a bit more of a sturdy gourmand than something too edgy. Other notes include woods, spices, and other gourmand elements like caramel and vanilla. It’s tender and has an aromatic component that gives it an air of sophistication while still being a mostly-gourmand. It’s likely among my few favorites of the house while not being an amazing standout, not quite having the effect of Drunk Maple, for instance, but I quite like it and it performs well. Like the rest of the line, this is EDP concentration and pried at $210 for 50ml, available in the US via boutiques like Ministry of Scent. 7 out of 10

The name of the fragrance really says it all: From the very first spray, I was overwhelmed by a strong almond-pistachio note that reminded me of all sorts of delicacies. A mix of marzipan and amaretto describes it best. The top note lasts quite a while, and then the scent slowly develops into a wonderfully creamy, non-intrusive base dominated by tonka bean. A truly delicious gourmand, perfect for cold days.

Summer 1997, a tent sleepover party at my friend Manu's. Manu had very liberal parents who were not bothered by the various bottles of Berentzen's milk liqueur range and some examples of a well-known Irish toffee liqueur making their way into the orchard. After all, we were all confirmed already. Dear Josy was absolutely thrilled and dove in wholeheartedly. She wanted to throw all inhibitions overboard that evening and finally land with Christoph. She poured the sweet, sticky stuff into herself as if there were no tomorrow. Christoph seemed quite taken with it and followed her lead. At some point, he had the idea to mix Josy a delicious long drink: Baileys with apple juice. I watched with interest, but from a safe distance, as the mixture formed funny flakes and didn't look particularly appetizing in color. However, Josy was undeterred and drank with reckless abandon what Cupid had offered her. At some point, she got up from her cross-legged position. Her complexion had changed. Not necessarily for the better. She now resembled the pale beige-green of the previously consumed mixed drink. Instead of heading to the bathroom, Josy took a big lunge toward my brand-new igloo tent. She quickly went down on her knees, and at that moment, a sweet-sour torrent of her stomach contents poured onto the previously immaculate bright blue tent wall. I will never forget that smell. Thanks again, dear Josy! With the arrival of Happy Nuts, I could now relive this wonderful moment of my youth in all its olfactory glory. Happy Nuts is a conglomerate of all sorts of gourmand notes that seem so arbitrary and disharmonious that I am at a loss for words. I smell nothing nutty, or at least nothing I could associate with pleasant nut scent. A piercingly artificial ethyl maltol sweetness accompanies this impenetrable dessert puree. So far, so bad. If it weren't for the patchouli and tobacco that also fell into the mix, which give it a certain dull acidity that catapults me straight back to 1997. Fermented chocolate sweetness. The scent is absolutely unbearable for me, and it would be highly uncomfortable if someone smelled like this. No nuts for Cinderella.

I'm on my second bottle of CK MAN, I recently bought back after using it over a decade ago, when it was just launched on the market. I just wanted to write a statement here, and so I retrieved the bottle, regrettably empty, only to remember the smell through the sprayer. A bit of perfume remained in the straw, enough to spray. And that spray immediately reminded me why I fell in love because of the nuance that recalls the masterpiece Nino Cerruti pour Homme dated 1979, in a more modern key. Happily, this new bottle has the same smell as the original one, maybe did not suffer too many reformulations. There is always a level of snobbery in the fragrance community, so something as big a market as CK won't get much recognition. For me, this is one of my favourite releases of them. For a perfume collector, this will not be anything revolutionary, but for me, it's a great general smell. It is fresh, sharp and versatile. The bottle is quite minimalist, square, clear-glass, without too many frills, front and back covered with an asphalt-black film which results in stylish dark-coloured glass and a light grey juice inside. And the box is nothing more than the bottle itself, the design and colour are identical. The overall fragrance smells like the air after a light morning rain in the woods, the atmosphere comes alive with a fresh smell, hard and pungent. The forest floor is scattered with coarse bay trees, their cinnamon-like odour tingling in your lungs. The wild nature of melted mushrooms comes with fresh raindrops, eucalyptus and abundant moss soon they also make their way. The air smells good. It may have the trail of damp moss, rain, wet tree trunks, flowers and a path covered with needles. Walking through a damp forest after the rain has a unique smell. The hush of the forest takes hold of your wandering mind, and it forces you to face questions of your being. CK MAN is like open arms; ready to embrace you without judging, to give power and support. It caresses you with its beauty, sounds and smells, and it feels good on your skin, too. Stepping into this cologne is like walking through a gate. You leave all the fuss, busy life and smooth asphalted roads behind, to be greeted with peace and fragrant nature. It has fresh spicy, aromatic, and woody main accords. Upon opening, I get the blend of zesty sweet mandarine and green, vivid violet resulting in gorgeous harmony. Soon it melts with a touch of creamy bergamot velvetiness and mentholated rosemary aromaticity. It is a crisp, incredible opening, with bay already lingering in the air. The herbs keep the overall overture a bit enticing. Middle notes of bay leaf, incense, nutmeg, and mint follow. The minty accord mixes nicely with a subdued, unburned incense aroma; the heart of the fragrance with its minty incense is my favourite part of Calvin Klein MAN. As the mint calm down, I can detect the spicy nutmeg. And when the nutmeg shines, it signals the start of the fragrance warm finishing of guaiac wood, with a tinge of rosy aroma, sandalwood, amber wood, cypress, and musk notes closing this masterpiece. The dry down adds a warm incense-cypress woodiness in the concoction with a little smokiness and a dark, scratchy tone while the sweetness and softness of sandalwood keep it in balance. Amberwood joins the dry down with gorgeous Iso E Super and pristine white musk, the threesome becomes dominant and mesh with the green notes giving CK MAN a charming, pleasant, green, clean scent. With moderate sillage and longevity, this scent works well throughout the middle seasons, Spring and Fall, at any time of the day and evening out. A strong, bold and hard-muscled perfume with an arduous and assertive character. It is subtle and close to skin type and supposed to be layered on the skin and although not to be judged at initial spray, let it settle and project with a man's natural scent upon dry down, it complements your natural fragrance. Earthy, green and woodsy like a rugged man. This is a classy, unique, elegant, crispy and spicy aroma without going into so played out watery-woody territory. CK MAN is unique, sophisticated and intriguing in an understandable and widely acceptable manner. It is one of those scents that you need to test on your skin, and not just that...you need to wait for the dry down. As most of the CK perfumes for men, in my humble opinion, this one is underrated too, yet it has a grip of steel. It smells fresh and young, but still distinguished. Stay well; stay healthy. -Elysium

Picture a sleek modern office building, a painting of a forest behind the receptionist's desk. A suited man enters, 'hi Violet' he says and walks between two rows of tall, impossibly clean-looking potted plants towards her giant wooden desk, a gust of air following him in from the street. He reaches the desk and Violet looks up with her cool green eyes and gives him a knowing glance but doesn't smile. CK Man is a versatile masculine fragrance, indeed the bottle itself recalls the sleek modern office building from my abstract intro, the scent is most certainly suited to the contemporary urban workplace. Not a warming scent, the coolness of green plants and the evergreen cypress trees lends CK Man a slightly cold and serious vibe, however this is balanced out with the strong & alluring note of violet leaf which is really the star of the show until the gaiac wood reveals itself fully later on. Some spicy & herbal accords particularly from the nutmeg but also rosemary add a little underlying playful mischief to ensure that it isn't all work and no play. So a modern urban fragrance, with a little nod to some 'manly' woody & evergreen fragrances of the past. A city dweller who goes hiking in nature at the weekend, when he gets the chance and isn't distracted by Violet's eyes.

I tried (on my arm): CK One, CK All, CK Be, CK Everyone, CK Man (I still need to try CK Shock, which should be the best one) All the Fragrances above are more versatile and can be used for every weather/occasion but have very poor performance besides CK Man, which performs good/very good but more of a night fragrance for me. CK One: citrusy/versatile CL All: it starts citrusy, becomes sweet CK Be: Also versatile, but it smells more soapy. CK Everyone: citrusy/versatile CK Man: Starts dark, becomes fruity-sweet, ends with sweet/woody. The only Fragrance that I could still smell strong on my arm after 3 hours (and still going strong). For me it's more of a night/autumn fragrance than a day/summer one. I'm very picky about fragrances, still love this one. disclaimer: fragrance noob here, so I might not get all the smells correct.

I once genuinely liked this scent. Its sweetness borders on being overly indulgent, yet it doesn't really crosses that line, I don't think. It's also very fresh, and have some uplifting qualities. So all this makes it versatile for a wide range of occasions. However, over time, I just realized it's to synthetic to me. Since then, I find myself reaching for it far less often than I used to.

This is a hidden gem, Elegant, Classy and Romantic. It is between freshness and warmth. If you like the Violet Leaf note , you will like this one. It opens up with like fresh citrusy, violet leaf and green notes in the background then dry down is slightly smoky , woody. It is suitable for the all seasons. I really enjoy it and I like Man Calvin Klein EDT for Men. I'm so happy that I have it in my collection. Highly Recommended. Thumbs Up. Rating : 8 / 10

I have had this scent from CK for several years now. How long exactly, I can't remember anymore. It was pretty much at the beginning of my passion for perfume. Calvin Klein was my starter brand back then. I really enjoyed buying them. CK One, CK Be, Euphoria, and whatever they were all called. Very mainstream. I still like this CK Man very much today. I bought it in a set.

The name Calvin Klein stands in the fashion world for a minimalist, timeless - but also lascivious and sexy style. Through androgynous designed and reduced to the essentials print and TV campaigns in black and white, the brand became a cult label, and with models like Mark Wahlberg, Kate Moss, and Linda Evangelista, it had its international breakthrough in the early 90s!

In a coming-of-age film like "Breakfast Club" or "Sing Street," it’s about teenagers in puberty, their paths & problems of growing up & just things that occupy us humans in the wild years between childhood & adulthood, between the schoolyard & the disco.

The notes are wonderful and the mixing ratio is a botched job. The cut bitter trees are simply a dream. The mandarin overwhelms everything. The gradations are so drastic, yes uneven, here a fabulous idea of a damp bitter autumn forest in light gray mist for real lumberjacks or nature boys has been downgraded to a proletarian water due to pure imbalance.

First, a very soft and smooth sweet mandarin is perceived, which, however, is not sticky but radiates a bit of the side of its still somewhat green peel and is enveloped by a beautiful, almost dense floral, lightly sweet-tinged violet leaf note.

Nanatopia was the first perfume i ever tried from BTSO/borntostandout. Nanatopia made me love the brand and made me want to discover more from there brand! Nanatopia is very similar to a syrupy banana bread which smells and tastes delicious! The banana is there through the whole wear which is really rare for banana peerfumes nowadays. Nanatopia lasts around 10 hours on my skin which is great in my opinion. I would recommend this to someone looking for a unique sweet, fruity gourmand scent!

opens with a spiced boozy rum that quickly turns into a caramelized banana bread note; the heart of this sits a bit as a rum soaked banana bread loaf…but the dry down is where this falters heavily. this gives off the scent of a hamster cage…and I don’t know if the tonka bean helps at all to balance out that animalic accord in the base. It just smells like earthy, animalic, hay? there’s no remnants of the smooth rum or the bready caramel or sweet bananas whatsoever, it’s just a synthetic herbal overtly earthy mess. had high hopes for this and wanted to believe ppl dissing this were wrong…but alas this scent is terrible.

This is a delicious banana scent. It goes from candy to warm with spice to sweet woody dry down. To be more specific, the scent starts with a light, creamy, sweet candy banana, like runts candy. Even though the spices are listed as the top note, I got the candy banana first with the spices in the background and as the candy-ness mellowed out, I got a dense spiced loaf of banana bread. The notes are distinct too, you can individually pick out the caramel, cinnamon, nutmeg and banana bread. The spice mellows and then you get a lightly sweet woody skin scent. I love this, I was worried that it would be too candy for me but the spices and dry down are delightful. The projection is fairly strong, I was able to pick up this scent for at least 4 hours. The longevity is good too, I was able to get the dry down on my skin even 6 hours later.

The first time I smelled this, it made my brain type in Wingdings. The explosion of rainbow candy in the opening is so weird and creative. It's what a sexy clowngirl would smell like. It settles to a syrupy center and a warm toasty base that lasts all day (I get the wood chips comparison, even the woody part smells clean and cooking-grade to me, although I don't know what kind of oven for baked goods would be stoked with wood chips). While it has some spice, it has a much more bright, saturated feel than dry or autumnal.

Sampling Borntostandout Nanatopia, a fittingly banana-focused, with notes of liqueurs and spices fostering a sweet, boozy gourmand blend that also curiously has some restraint and non-gourmand aspect in the cypriol note, and I think it’s overall a very interesting option for those like banana notes but want them wrapped in something sophisticated rather than smelling like a banana laffy taffy, as much as others might want that, all the same. This does a good job with banana, in my opinion, as I generally find it to be a difficult note to enjoy in fragrance, given that I find it quite distractive and playful rather than classy or classic. As with the rest of the house’s catalogue, it’s EDP concentration and priced at $290/210/85 for 100/50/15ml, fairly reasonable in the current market. It performs quite well, also. I’m not sure I’d wear it myself, in conclusion, but I quite like it and find it to be a very interesting treatment of banana. 6 out of 10

This is about a parfum for vetiver lovers. A raw, wild, sharpy and spicy vetiver. I've tried 2 other Estee Lauder references of that collection and I admit they are weak to my nose. This one is quite the opposite. Amazing, powerful, charming vetiver, more suitable for cold seasons. Unisex. Very well done!

The CK One line, now a huge collection with many flankers. I just like them because they usually have a very uncomplicated freshness. In my opinion, they are often undervalued when compared to other fresh scents that sometimes have miserable performance. Even though many CK fragrances are unjustly criticized and often forgotten, I can only highly recommend them. CK All can probably also be counted among the CK One line even without the One addition. The typical bottle shape of the classic is the same, and the scent goes in a similar direction. I tested this fragrance at the end of this summer and it made its way onto my wish list. I had my eye on it for a while due to the pyramid. The test confirmed it: a great scent in the fresh category. I finally bought it in September. Even though summer was pretty much over and now is, I buy fresh fragrances throughout the entire year, especially since it's priced great. After a few months, you can already find it on sale and very cheap. CK All is not that far from CK One. In terms of scent type, they are very similar, but the DNA has been wonderfully tuned and modernized here. Specifically, fruity and floral notes have been added to the tried-and-true recipe for success. At first, a lovely mandarin note dominates. Along with a typical bergamot freshness and also a nice floral note. A really beautiful fruity-fresh-floral note that is not weak in the sillage at all. It comes through well in the nose. After a while, it becomes softer. Especially when the mandarin has faded, fresh and floral notes dominate. In the pyramid, sea water is mentioned. A very refreshing, slightly aquatic freshness is definitely noticeable. Along with gentle flowers. In the base and in the drydown, it comes quite close to CK One with amber and musk. Overall, a really great fragrance that is not trivial at all. The DNA is successful, and the concept of the line has been proven for a long time. Especially with the great price. The performance is, like many fragrances from the brand, rated too low. On me, it lasts several hours, similar to CK One. Moreover, the sillage is really good over a long period. Also extremely noticeable on clothing for a long time and provides a pleasant freshness. Unisex is justified. Especially for women, it suits very well due to the floral and fruity notes. Synthetics are present, but not exaggerated. Therefore, it's more suitable for a casual look rather than for snobby types. It has a carefree lightness. Overall, not a milestone, but I'm glad I bought this.

I never liked CK One unconditionally. Of course, I had to have this unisex fragrance phenomenon in the 90s, that's clear. Nowadays, I even like it a little better. I prefer its crisp citrus-tea freshness in the heat, but only for a maximum of 2 days in a row. After that, it annoys me. With CK All, that won't happen. It's much milder in scent. Right from the start, I have CK One in my nose, the same citrusy opening. But only for a very short time, although the citrus notes remain subtly until the end. A slightly floral note sneaks in, and I perceive a gentle synthetic woodiness with musk. This fragrance is pleasing, suitable for everyone on all occasions. With this, you can be sure not to offend anyone. That was certainly the manufacturer's intention, and the price is moderate. I don't mind this concept in the slightest; I like the scent. The longevity is mediocre.

When "cK one" and "cK be" came out in the mid-90s, they revolutionized the fragrance market while simultaneously polarizing it. The intended reconciliation of the genders and Calvin Klein's provocative androgynous slim aesthetic attracted America-loving fans and sharp industry criticism. Those times are long gone; with Bulgari and "Eau de Cartier," Unisex has finally become a viable mainstream option. Thus, "cK all" also connects to the old coolness but has simultaneously evolved into a wearable, rather austere office scent that doesn't irritate the environment with excessive floral notes. A metallic-spicy note, Yuzu, pomegranate, rhubarb, moss, ferns, and musk dominate, and it beats with the heart of the cool alpine violet. This minimalist aesthetic is still vividly remembered from Marc Jacobs' Splash line, with "Pomegranate" being the most similar. Now, these wonderful fragrances were discontinued back then; and so I am pleased that the admittedly not very innovative "cK all" is now filling this gap again. It is harmoniously composed, and for those who find Azzaro's "Chrome" annoying and "Eau de Cartier" too elaborate, this offers a wearable alternative.

Normally, I stock up on the CK summer editions because they are great companions in warm weather. But I also find CK All very appealing. The sugary citrus reminds me of my mom's homemade lemonade, with a crunchy sugar rim on the long drink glass. The aquatic sea note brings a certain beach feeling and creates a sense of coolness. Light and white, the lily shines through and pleasantly brightens the fragrance. Amber adds a soft and sweet touch. A fresh - cool scent with a subtle powderiness and attractive mildness. Well done and even a bit special. I am expecting guests today - and the fragrance will not disturb anyone indoors either. A good all-rounder that blends in, yet gives the wearer a cozy feeling. One doesn’t want to stand out with their scent every day and everywhere.

A sample of this new CK offshoot was included with an order from Flaconi. Yuck, I thought at first. Despite my great concerns, I dared to test this latest offshoot of the CK family. Good thing I had no expectations. Therefore, I was not disappointed. At first, I thought it was okay. But after a short time, the artificial citrus freshness and the slight floral notes disappeared. After that, the suddenly appearing artificial aqua freshness quickly fades away to make room for the sour chemistry. The base is pure synthetic and burns my nasal mucosa. My eyes are also watering slightly. Amber, musk, vetiver? At most in homeopathic doses, so scientifically and nasally undetectable. Paradisone is an artificial substitute for "Hedione." According to internet research, the scent is supposed to be citrus-floral. Also only present in traces. The fruity components correspond to scent notes like tonic or apple, etc. in similar cheap productions. Longevity is poor. After an initial sillage cloud, the scent quickly becomes skin-close. This is also a blessing for the environment. It seamlessly fits into the 08/15 shower gel-fresh variations of recent years.

New day, new CK flanker You immediately notice the family resemblance upon spraying - just like with Everyone and CK One Essence, here you again have the typical fresh/citrusy opening. After a while, you can faintly detect rhubarb and light green notes, but not much tea. Overall, it remains very fresh.

What makes this wonderful fragrance special is Cassia. The cinnamon, sweet scent is complemented by light, delicate flowers like violets and the classic rose. The Flower by Kenzo Limited Edition from 2004 is a delicate, light variation of Flower by Kenzo Le Parfum. A strong similarity cannot be denied here. Those who like the red Le Parfum will also like this one. The bottle is radiant white, matte, and not red. Only the spray head and the red lettering remind of the satin red of Le Parfum. The scent also appears white to me. Baby powder, Nivea powder could easily be its name. You will be surrounded for a long time by a white, quite dense, warm, cinnamon-floral-sweet powder cloud. However, the Flower by Kenzo Limited Edition is not too sweet, but pleasantly sweet. I really like this cuddly scent. I also enjoy the other Flower by Kenzo fragrances. This one fits quite seamlessly into the Flower lineup. The base is also powdery white and has a slightly cinnamon-vanilla touch. The longevity is about eight hours, which is normal. I perceive the sillage of this fragrance as rather close to the skin. However, I can continuously sense it on me when I move. Therefore, I assume that I am trailing a certain powder cloud behind me. Unfortunately, my husband is rather insensitive to powder scents. He simply does not perceive them properly on me. He often judges them as "weak" or "unfragranced." In any case, they do not stand out to him on me. And I love powder scents on myself very much. This one is a great example of that, which is why I give it a full 100%.

Firstly, let me say that Estee Lauder has produced some of my most beloved fragrances such as Private Collection, Cinnabar, Youth Dew, Beautiful, and Tuscany per Donna, but Modern Muse Le Rouge is disappointing. It is really nothing more than a mishmash of fruit and some weak florals that could easily be a B&BW body spray which I would not like. Smelling it now, I realise I have smelt this on many women before and never liked it, but I had no idea what they were wearing. I never would have guessed it was an Estee Lauder fragrance. I heartily recommend all of the other EL fragrances mentioned above, but I cannot recommend Le Rouge, and do not think it is a safe blind buy. The quality is poor. Fragrance: 3/10 Sillage: 4/10 Projection: 4/10 Longevity: 4.5/10 Presentation: 5/10 ETA: Anyone who wants to try a well made perfume in this vein, i.e. a fruity red rose with a bit of woodiness, would do well to try Serge Lutens's. La Fille de Berlin, or if budget is an issue, you would do better with B&BW You're The One, which is an excellent fruity rose for the price point and one of my favourite B&BW scents.

This is so much more interesting than I was expecting! I love those vinyl/leathery notes, and this is what really gives it its appeal. The rose, cherry and patchouli come together and give it a dirty and delightful sort of smokiness. I kept on seeing commercials and ads all over the place so I figured I'd try it just to see what all the fuss what about. Now that I've tried it - I must say - I have no idea what they were thinking with their ad campaign. Kendall Jenner? A red business suit? To me, Modern Muse Le Rouge feels a bit more wild, flirty, and maybe a little more rock 'n' roll. I feel like Demi Lovato would've been a more suitable frontwoman for a scent like this.

With Modern Muse and Chic, I initially struggled a bit because I found the two graces too elegant for me. I appreciated these muses in my mom - and she encouraged me to wear both for a longer time. And - lo and behold - they also go well with my rather casual outfit. A muse kiss with delayed effects. That's why I confidently bought Le Rouge today without trying it first - and I have no regrets. The "Red" greets me more warmly than her companions, almost with a readiness to cuddle - without falling directly around my neck. The velvety rose, intertwined with delicious raspberry, surrounded by vanilla makes the welcome easy and lovely. But then Le Rouge collects itself and shows with slightly bitter patchouli poise and character strength. Mild pepper and noble saffron emphasize this shift into elegance. The centifolia adds a touch of exclusivity, as Le Rouge wants to remain individual. It succeeds with ease. Le Rouge is an interesting, independent muse, with a friendly start and a pleasantly unique development. I can well imagine the scent with original second-hand clothing - but it will also enhance everyday outfits. Nevertheless, this muse is not everyday - so to speak, an affordable niche fragrance.

The bottle makes quite an impression with its oversized plastic Plexiglas cap - at least it is unusual. I will leave the environmental aspects aside when it comes to aesthetic evaluation. That this type of bottle is very difficult to dispose of is unfortunately obvious (and not everyone collects bottles!). And who really believes in "climate change?" Due to the striking presentation, I tested the fragrance a few days ago (also at Karstadt, just like my predecessor - but came to a completely different conclusion - well...) At first, I noticed the almost grotesquely exaggerated synthetic top note, a freshness-evoking accord that you usually find in the cleaning product industry (ironically fittingly upside down is the name "Women" - universally responsible for the cleaning business" - the eternal cleaning lady, after all). Not particularly enthusiastic, I then labeled a scent card with "Women" to describe the base note later; besides, I didn't want to judge too hastily. On my wrist, at least, a barely bearable mix of cardboard-like vanilla, artificial orange, and a dull, tormenting wood note developed. A real "scrubber," indeed. But in its primitiveness and crude form, it is quite new. Please don't get me wrong: Synthetics are absolutely okay! Of course, hardly any perfume works without "aroma chemicals." The art lies in incorporating them in such a way that they create the illusion of naturalness or at least a certain harmony. Under no circumstances should the used aroma substances trigger headaches, the uncontrollable urge to scrub off the scent, or other aversions or nasty associations (I think, for example, of Trump, his female voters, and the apocalypse). After exactly three days (wrapped in plastic to avoid inhaling the scent), the scent card that is now "naked" lying in front of me on the desk (and I don't want to grab it ever again!!!) emits such a penetrating chemical, devastatingly bad smell that I will now sink it in the trash bin before I become even more depressed. So it seems that the innovation of 2018 from Calvin Klein is as follows: The fragrances have deteriorated even further. "Women" is, for me, the low point of their previous launches. And they call this perfume "Women" - so, so sad! Impeachment? I would welcome it. This is nothing to make Calvin Klein great again.

Wow, you really get torn apart quite often. Sweat, synthetic... It's very funny that I keep noticing that totally hyped fragrances that get rated 9 or 10 smell really creepy on me. And scents that are often rated really poorly here smell really good on my skin. Okay... Now seriously... Should I be worried about this? What’s wrong with my skin, my nose? ? Because Woman smells fresh, clean, bright, and clear on me right away.... I find orange blossom extremely disturbing in many perfumes, but here I think the blend of the other notes is really good. So it's not an omG, I've never smelled anything this great, but I find Woman good for warm days. It actually reminds me a bit of Pure Poison. So for me, it's an absolute fresh scent and unfairly rated so poorly. If it were a more expensive niche fragrance, it would surely enchant half of the people here....

At Kstadt, I was looked at. Not curiously, or controlling like the eye of the law - but completely calm and yet interested. Several eyes of the decorated CK bottles are looking at me. Eyes are the window to the soul - and I find myself caught in their pull. An eyecatcher in the boldest sense of the word. And the scent draws me in as well. It is transparent, yet sweet with a minty freshness. This combination is unusual - and unique. Lovely and cool at the same time. The fresh eucalyptus skillfully blends with the warm orange blossom. Cypress wafts ethereally and woody above it. Finally, a special cK scent again! As I watch in the commercial how a model lovingly frees a Nina Simone record from its cover, and then carefully places it on the turntable, I am enchanted. Her cool warm music with a touch of sentiment fits well with the new CK creation. Women puts a spell on me.

Through the purchase of another fragrance, this sample came to me. In the late morning, I sprayed 2 spritzes on my wrist. Sniffing and checking Parfumo to see if my impression is correct. Oh dear... overall fragrance rating 5.9! Uh oh, it’s definitely going to develop musty... reading reviews... fragrance rating 1... oh God, what else might be coming?? So... let’s get to the point: the terrible development did not occur. Bad ratings are okay; we know that fragrances are perceived very individually. To give a fragrance a 1... well... I found CK Women to be very fresh upon spraying, somehow reminding me of Davidoff Cool Water. This first impression fades away before the spritzes on my wrist are even dry. Synthetic notes follow, similar to Zarkoperfume The Muse. Finally, the orange blossom develops. Very subtle and close to the skin. The fragrance lasts a good 4 hours before it fades away. I can no longer perceive a base. In summary, a very understated everyday companion. However, it will not accompany my everyday life as orange blossom is not one of my favorites.

I received CK Women as a birthday gift and found it not as bad as it's rated here from the very beginning. It's not a scent that knocks me off my feet, but it's still pleasant and enjoyable. While reading through the notes, I was somewhat surprised; eucalyptus cones are supposed to be the top note? I could swear I smell pepper! This makes the opening not too sweet-floral, not too pronounced, yet somehow special. My favorite part, however, is when the orange blossom reveals itself. While the scent initially seemed absolutely unisex, it now becomes warmer and creamier, feeling like a friendly hug. This delicate orange blossom lingers on my skin for several hours, so there's no talk of poor longevity for me. I also like the packaging. The glass bottle is heavy and feels high-quality. The cap is indeed a bit awkward, but the design with the eye is extraordinary and looks great in my collection. Overall, CK Women is a good everyday fragrance. I'm glad I received it as a gift, but for me, it probably won't be a candidate for repurchase.

I really can't understand the many negative reviews (but that's a matter of taste). CK Woman is one of my favorite fragrances in my collection and has been repurchased multiple times. The scent always gives me a fresh feeling, like just having taken a shower. It smells floral, a bit woody, and for me, it also has a slightly soapy quality.

I love tonka bean, not just in my pancakes. It is special, it is very sincere and for me an inspirational scent. Creative, it could definitely be called that now... lasts extremely long. The successful blend between bitterness and a hint of sweetness in the aftertaste. Definitely not mainstream.

A misty morning in a mountain forest, where dew glistens on the undergrowth. The cool air is filled with the scent of earth, moss, pine needles, and soaked bark. There is silence, peace, healing. Inner harmony—the balance of a warrior, a wise and mature man who makes decisions with both mind and heart. A deep understanding of the essence of one's own nature. These are the perfumes of silence and strength. A composition to be worn for oneself, not for the rest of the world.

This is a great scent if you want to smell like a forest with a little campfire smoke. This scent opens up very peppery and smokey but not overpowering like smoke can be sometimes. Its like a campfire that is trying to light a wet piece of wood. The pepper and smoke within a few minutes and settles into this really nice pine and cedar smell with a little bit of tree sap. Its a mix of rubbing your face up against some pine needles and opening an old warm cedar chest. Breezy but comforting. The dry down is a light sweet tobacco and earthy smell. I was still able to detect it on my skin after 6 hours. The projection is decent, I was catching whiffs of throughout the day.

Hinoki... what is that anyway? This question occupied my mind first when I first laid eyes on this fragrance during a swap offer. I found the name and the bottle immediately appealing, and a glance at the fragrance pyramid did not diminish my interest in this previously completely unknown scent. The only thing I viewed with a somewhat skeptical eye was the Georgywood, yet I decided to go for a swap and welcomed the bottle to my home a few days later. But what is Hinoki now? It is a Japanese precious wood derived from the false cypress. This cypress is one of the five sacred trees of Japan. This listing likely arises from the fact that the wood from these 5 trees has mostly been used for the temples and shrines of Japanese culture. However, there are differing opinions on which 5 trees exactly belong to this list. Anyway, as I said, I like the name, the bottle, and also the following sentence that belongs to the fragrance description. Quoted below: "Inhaling cigarette smoke while we make love, somewhere in the Hinoki forest." My nose does not quite capture this type of description, yet it is an exceptionally beautiful scent that I will definitely keep. I do not perceive cigarette smoke, or anything smoky at all. What I get here is a green, fresh, and slightly woody fragrance. The green foliage presents itself in a very fine way. It is not uncommon for the needle-bearing wooden towers to have this distinctly woody note, often paired with noticeably sweet components. For this reason, some fragrances of this category have already moved out. Hinoki-Shower perfectly caters to my taste. This woody, green pine combines here with a potent and distinctly noticeable fresh note. Yes, somewhat synthetic at times, but never bothersome or overwhelming. Camphor likely plays a significant role here as well. Even though you do not get its classic sharpness here, it certainly contributes to this freshness kick. Vetiver and moss form a perfectly tuned base for this. Tobacco plays almost no role for me here. In summary, a wonderfully refreshing, woody, slightly synthetic green fragrance with moderate longevity and gentle sillage. The sprayer is very pleasant; it mists exceptionally fine from my perspective and perhaps symbolizes a bit of the calm, refined, and rather reserved culture of Japan. Hinoki? You are mine!

A misty morning in the forest, the sun is just rising, the air is cool, fresh, and clear. Camphor trees and cypress stand majestically beside pines, exuding their spicy scent. The smell of fresh resin and clear, pure water fills the air. We venture deeper into the forest, stepping on soft mossy ground, feeling the warmth of the sun as an intense aroma of thyme greets us. We discover a hidden corner where tobacco leaves are drying, and the scent of ripe tobacco mingles with the earthy freshness of tree moss. The surroundings radiate warmth and tranquility. A vibrant fragrance that unites nature, freshness, and depth. The various facets range from refreshment to deep calm. Masculine tendency, but definitely unisex.

Upon first spray, this is a delectable combination of milk, cookies, and caramel. I enjoy how it’s not too sickly sweet, and the iris seems to round it out well. It’s thick, creamy and gourmand, and the dry down starts to smell almost coconutty to my nose. It’s a bit too heavy for my taste, but it’s perfect for the gourmand lovers, and not dirty at all.

I thought about how I wanted to write this review and decided to share my impressions, associations, and reactions completely unfiltered and chronologically. The scent arrived fresh from Korea. Due to previous statements, I paused briefly after spraying it on my skin and mentally prepared myself... skepticism... I just closed the cap again... and bam, I caught a part of the sillage from afar. Caramel, but distinctly... a short loud laugh from me and extreme relief... "I knew this was nonsense..." I thought with a big grin on my face. Okay, arm to the nose... yes, caramel... vanilla... musk... quite strong... oh oh... marshmallow blush? Bianco Latte?? Oh please not... I already have something like that... 10 minutes pass... Ah... okay... now it’s changing... Akigalawood and iris create a different scent impression, more mature?... is that supposed to be the "dirty" part? There’s definitely that condensed milk impression. Cashmeran ensures that the scent remains very creamy. And this musk... I love what BTSO uses there. I found it fabulous in Fig Porn as well. After half an hour to an hour, the scent development diverges significantly from the aforementioned and becomes something completely its own. Not as sweet as others in the category. Then 2-3 hours in, the deeper drydown begins, and the musk with an absolutely fabulously embedded tonka bean. It’s almost addictive. Conclusion and summary: Good sillage, caramel-milky vanilla start. On the skin, as described, first a caramel milk that then transforms, while the scent needs a few minutes to "organize," into a beautifully light iris milk (I’m not usually an iris fan, but this one is great!) with woody support. The deep drydown features one of the most pleasing tonka beans I know, right behind Blanche bête. No, the scent has nothing to do with blanche bête, except for the tonka note in the drydown. On clothing, this milk and later condensed milk impression lasts significantly longer. People were very nice to me today and came quite close, so it seems I wasn’t the only one who liked it. If Bianco Latte was too vanilla for you, blanche bête too incense-heavy, and other vanilla scents too boring, you might want to give this one a chance. A very pleasing, milky, not over-the-top sweet scent.

I love milky, creamy scents so much. For a long time, I have been searching for the holy grail, personally for me. Dirty Milk is it. I have finally found it in Dirty Milk. This fragrance is very sweet, milky, creamy, yes even creamy and buttery I would describe it. The iris brings a touch of elegance into it. It is warm, soft, simply enchanting. I don't want to be without it anymore. My holy grail of milky scents.

Freshly sprayed, I catch a whiff of milkmaid in my nose, I briefly consider whether I should stop breathing because so far it's nice and the name Dirty Milk might lead one to expect something unpleasant. So, I move my arm away from my face and take a round of fresh air. Here, NOTHING is Dirty; on the contrary, I get a wonderful hint of iris that perfectly balances the sweetness. Pepper and musk skillfully enhance this beautifully pleasant scent, refreshing it in a lovely way. I like it.

With the first breath, Dirty Milk unfolds its dark, almost mysterious aura. In the bottle, it appears heavy, vanillic, almost smoky - like a velvety shadow that lays itself on the skin. This fine smoke, never dominant but clearly perceptible, subtly resonates throughout the later stages. It reminds one of the cool aunt with the raspy voice, cigarette holder in hand, who always smells so good of vanilla. By the way, there’s no need to fear smelling like a chain smoker - this smoke association thankfully doesn’t arise, rather the feeling of the “cigarette after.” The opening is intense: dark, sticky caramel, warm and lush, almost mouthwatering. Black pepper adds a lively, fine, barely tangible spiciness - a gentle tingling that keeps the sweetness in check. Hardly has one internalized this first impression when Dirty Milk glides into a soft, creamy phase. It’s as if one is diving into warm, sweet condensed milk - a hint of vanilla sauce, rich, round, and comforting. Despite all the sweetness, the fragrance never feels childish or sticky. It remains elegant, grown-up, and carries a gentle warmth that does not overwhelm but envelops. Over time, the tonka bean emerges and melds with the caramel into a full-bodied, almost gourmand heart. The result is a dessert - but not an innocent one. It is a wicked, luxurious dessert, served at a masquerade ball, by candlelight. One sees the mysterious woman in black satin gloves, red lips, her gaze demanding - she savors every spoonful deliberately, knowing that all eyes are on her. (Maybe I’ve also watched too many dessert commercials) Dirty Milk is sweet, creamy, and sensual, yet always with a hint of darkness in the background - like a temptation that one cannot fully grasp but also cannot forget. The scent is incredibly memorable and invites one to sniff again - an absolute compliment magnet that stirs desire.

The name “Dirty Milk” definitely does justice to the fragrance. Right from the first spray, this “dirty” aspect comes through very clearly: a spicy, slightly animalistic, almost dirty note that is immediately present.

I grabbed up this scent because of Calvin Klein One Summer (2021 version). Just couldn't help myself, I loved the bottle design so much. . At first, I wasn't a big fan of the 2021 version because of the longevity. But the more I wore it, I loved it for what it was worth. . These scents are cheap, but very well blended. Doesn't smell cheap, but with as many versions as they have, im sure they can get a little boring.. That's not here in the "Summer Daze" though. . This scent is very well blended! It's sweet, tart, fresh, slightly aquatic & has a mild musky feel to it. The kumquat is the first thing you notice. The "ice tea" note comes out shortly after, probably about 5 mins into the scent. The problem is, it feels like the sent only last 5 mins lol. Jk......Not really, maybe last about 3-4 hours, after the first hour & a half it becomes a skin scent. . The dry down is musky yet still tart & cloudy, it's very unique in its own way. I think it's an easy reach on a summer day when you don't know what to wear that day. . I'd save it for summer but a warm spring, fall day/evening. It could be worn. Just reapply after about 3 hours. But it's pleasant, it's distinct, it's worth the cheap price you can get it for because of how unique the note breakdown is. . JUST GOTTA KEEP LIVING MAN! ...........L-I-V-I-N!

Personally, I love the CK One Summer fragrance series. Every year, they renew this series of fragrances. It comes with innovative, refreshing scents that are suitable for summer and suitable for both sexes, and its price is very reasonable. CK One Summer is a very refreshing fragrance that contains kumquat as the main scent. The idea of ​​the fragrance is completely based on it, hence the light orange color of the bottle. Then come the scents of iced tea and then light mint on a base of Sorbettolide (musk): comfortable, soft, fruity, clean, powdery, and sensual notes… similar to the smell of skin. Overall it gives the feeling that you are drinking a can of Fanta orange. This fragrance is suitable for after showering in the summer, and it is also suitable as a first-class refreshing home fragrance. The fragrance performance is below average and lasts for about an hour or two with a very close scent on the skin. If you are a fragrance collector, a lover of fresh scents, or a fan of unconventional scents, then know that this fragrance will satisfy your taste.

As a fan of the CK Summer fragrances, the latest one is a must-have. Blind buy? Of course. So far, every one of my CK Summer fragrances. Disappointed? No, definitely not. The longevity should be clear to everyone. 4-5 hours. That's all there is. The new 2022 fragrance smells incredibly strong of mandarins. This makes it beautifully fresh. I can't actually smell anything more - and that's okay. Visually, of course, in the familiar style.

I am always on the lookout for summer scents and was curious about what CK would bring to the market this year. And I am pleasantly surprised: the fragrance is fresh, yet summery-warm, and it is hard to overdo it. It is somewhat "watery," meaning the scent lasts about four to five hours, after which it "fades" away. The fragrance is designed as a unisex Eau de Toilette, but this year it is more herbal and less soft than it was last year. A fruity sweetness (kumquat) is noticeable, but it does not dominate. The fresh mint quickly comes into play as a companion. I like this scent; for me, it is mainly perfect for warm summer evenings, but it also works during the day.

... sitting on the porch in a rocking chair in the southern states, enjoying a ginger/mint iced tea, with a bowl of kumquats beside me. I take one and bite into it. Simply delicious. We talk about everything under the sun and look out at the park surrounding the mansion. Upon applying this perfume, a fruity freshness hits the nose. The aromas of the iced tea join in, adding a tea vibe to it. This is then softened and cleaned up a bit, enhancing the fruity note. Vetiver makes it dry and adds a light citrus accord. The longevity and sillage are moderate. This unisex fragrance is a wonderful perfume for warm to hot days that can be worn for any occasion on such days. To enjoy it longer, the bottle should be tucked away or a small decant taken along. Anyone who enjoys a fruity, fresh iced tea can have fun with this affordable scent.

This review is simultaneously a tribute to the entire Summer line. For what it is, what it aims to achieve, and the price segment it occupies, it is simply optimal. Here too, you get a fresh opening - this time very mandarin - and then the base of the fragrance. This time it is a sweet mandarin iced tea with a hint of mint and a touch of ginger.

I've always liked the entire CK One Summer line, just like this one, which is my second from the series. This fruity freshness is really nice. For me, it's like a tropical fruit basket without being able to pinpoint a specific fruit. The iced tea note makes it interesting in a way, and a hint of mint and ginger rounds the perfume off quite well.

I did not consider touching Estee Lauder perfumes last 10 years - too bold, too fresh, too flowery, too meh. I have never really been a white flower/must kind of girl. Especially after having negative experience in my younger years with Pleasures, Beyond Paradise, Spellbound (will always be remembered for the worst migraine I have ever had) Also when I saw my favourite bloggers positing new Estee Lauder boutique collection and was really sceptical, but decided to give it a try, luckily there are adorable 4 ml samples/mini versions of the perfume. "Radiant Mirage" was interesting mainly because it was made by Quentin Bisch, author of oh-so-popular these days Ganymede. It smelled divine from the blotter, it produces beautiful sillage. But I don't quite like it, at first it smells very Estee Lauder DNA - cold flowers. It opens more interesting with time though, but all the way preserves this coldness that is not my cup of tea.

My friend Ilona, who naturally knows my curiosity for fragrances, included a double card with eight scent samples from the new generation of the well-known brand Estée Lauder in her last package. This series is titled: “Fragrance exists in the Mind, not just in the Senses.” Of course, I wondered: “What awaits me here?” and so I discovered aromatic, sometimes balsamic, summery-light novelties that should not be compared to the classics of this brand that we know so well. “Radiant Mirage” leaves a constant sensual glow and belongs to the spicy-warm fragrance family with distinctly woody accents. If you don’t like jasmine, patchouli, or sandalwood, you should better not test this creation at all: there’s nothing else! For me, all three fragrance notes appear as a troika; none takes the lead, and thus the typical division into top, heart, and base notes is absent: All three dance in the same rhythm, which becomes calmer and more delicate over time, without losing its step. This results in a light, pleasantly fragrant eau de toilette with corresponding (and expected) sillage and longevity, where reapplying is no problem. This fragrance entity retains its graceful personality, even though the blend of the mentioned components fades slightly and elegantly over time. As Pluto writes in her statement about “Radiant Mirage,” I also find what unfolds and develops on my skin surprisingly sexy! Now, this shouldn’t really come as a surprise, as all three fragrance components represent sensuality and fine animalistic eroticism. One should not underestimate this water-clear, harmoniously composed, and slightly provocative liquid. Even light fragrance veils can be stimulating, especially with this composition: Do you see it lightly floating in a dance with the sunlight?

Drunk maple caught my eye the second i saw the name of it because i love the taste of maple syrup! I expected it to be very sweet but nothing could prepare me for the scent. It was the most realistic and strongest maple scent my nose had ever felt and i fell in love at the first whiff. I cant really find anything else than maple in this scent but if thats what you like you have found your new scent! Drunk maple is very strong so it lasts around 12 hours on my skin so i would only wear it during the colder seasons or when i want someone to feel my scent. Overall a great scent but it might be a little to sweet for some peoples noses.

Sampling Borntostandout Drunk Maple, probably the fragrance I’ve seen online most from this house, and the one I was most drawn to try, and it’s really quite aptly named, mixing maple and booze in a rich gourmand that smells refined and classy, a nod to gourmand lovers that’s not overly sweet, and one of the best conceptions of maple that I’ve smelled in fragrance. The main notes are maple, rum, coffee, pink pepper, and benzoin. It has a vaguely metallic vibe that for me coincides with the extreme caramelization of toffee, and it works as a great counterpoint Like the rest of the line, this is EDP concentration and priced $215 for 50ml, sold via various US retailers like Ministry of Scent and Twisted Lily. It performs well and is personally a fragrance that I enjoy very much, and it makes the pricing palatable. 8 out of 10

It’s so dirty delicious! As most of BTSO it’s sticky, dark and lasts so well. Feels like an organic maple syrup toffee and vanilla liquoriche - it’s one of these eatable scents you wanna bite your skin to have a full experience. So sweet but dangerously deep and masculine in a sweaty way. It’s boozy rich and smoky in a Johnny Depp way, a bit arrogant but cool buddy. It’s mysterious but honest - you can feel all the mentioned ingredients but on the same time very well blended. I have already rather similar Kerosene but I wouldn’t mind Santa giving me bottle of Drunk Maple as well ;)

If each state had its own designated scent, this would be the scent of Vermont. This is a toasted wood that is slightly smoldering. You just put out the fire because the pot where you were reducing down the maple sugar water is done, its maple syrup now. This is the real maple syrup you pay good money for, its a natural sweetness with hint of wood and spice. This is rustic cozy and decadent. Don't worry about the "smoke." Its a bit of spice that adds depth without distracting from the main scent. As if you were smelling a burning leaf pile on the wind. You won't smell like you just left a BBQ. This is fairly typical BTSO fragrance in that it toes the line of being a "beast mode" fragrance. The projection is pretty strong, you will leave a scent trail behind but it not so strong that you are causing headaches. It also lasted a pretty long time, about 6 hours on my skin. There is only one size available, 50ml for $205. Pricey, but with a fragrance that lasts this long and projects this much, a little goes a long way.

Drunk Maple is one of the very few fragrances that really challenged me. The opening and generally the first phase of the scent do not suit my taste at all and, as harsh as it sounds, totally put me off and disgusted me. I was really close to washing it off and scrubbing it down. In my opinion, the fragrance contains three main accords. These would be rum, suede, and coffee. All three notes are already recognizable at the beginning. After the first spray, I thought to myself as the scent lingered in the air: "Wow, an iced coffee vibe. An instant iced coffee powder mixed with milk. Nice." But when I held my nose to the surface of my hand, I thought: "Phew, this is exhausting and quite hard to get used to." A few moments later, I thought: "Okay, now it’s getting really disgusting." To better categorize and describe the whole experience, here’s a suggestion for visualization. Imagine you are in an ancient pub where heavy smoking is allowed. The pub contains many leather sofas, leather armchairs, and chairs. The leather furniture has absorbed all the cigarette smoke from many years and is deeply ingrained with it. The furniture doesn’t look nice anymore and has ancient coffee stains that were never properly cleaned. In the pub, there are also people who are always a bit tipsy, first downing some coffee and then the old rum. These are roughly the associations I get, and personally, it’s just too much for me. It disgusts me a bit. I was close to washing the scent off completely, but then I thought: "No Dennis, you can do this, let it dry down further and see how it develops." Now comes the crazy part. Over time, it actually gets good. These "disgusting" vibes completely fade away for me after about 1-2 hours, and a wonderful lightly sweetened coffee scent develops. I now envision a sweetened coffee. Coffee, maple syrup, and a bit of vanilla. Towards the end, the pleasantly creamy sandalwood joins in. However, since I struggled quite a bit during the first two hours and was really disgusted, I can't really rate it well. What a shame! But tastes and impressions of fragrances can be so different. So definitely don’t let my review and somewhat harsh words deter you. Test the fragrance for yourself and form your own opinion.

A beautiful, soothing, balanced, discreet perfume that has that something. I have a miniature of it and I want to enjoy it to the fullest. I like to collect and also consume perfumes even if they are in miniature. It may sound strange, but it is the kind of perfume that makes you feel that everything is okay, that life is beautiful and that it will be fine. It also makes me think of a stable love relationship between a man and a woman; a wonderful relationship that does not need many words and where love is in the air. In short: I really like this perfume and I highly recommend it! Rating: 9/10

Beautiful Belle is an impressive floral perfume with hints of orange blossom, lychee, and mimosa—three of my favorites! The scent is soft, perfect for spring and summer wear or year-round in warmer climates. I love the sweetness of this perfume. It’s just right for breakfast, church, or going to the market. It’s almost refreshing to wear. It’s not a groundbreaking fragrance. It’s nevertheless mainstream and pleasant. It’s safe. I would wear this to a wedding. Sillage is close, maybe 12 inches, but I don’t overspray. Longevity is several hours in the air conditioning, but fewer in the heat.

For a long time, I debated whether to buy Beautiful Belle (BB), as the reviews didn’t bode well. But as a fan of Estee Lauder (EL) and especially of Beautiful, I overcame my doubts and ordered a 50ml bottle at a rather good price. And I was not disappointed! This fragrance is wonderful, but one thing at a time... First, the bottle resembles the classic from EL, but the cap is a bit different, the diffuser is amazing, very fine spray mist, so no soaking wet skin, which I really like! The scent itself stays more like a fine veil around you, so it’s not a fragrance bomb; however, the sillage becomes quite close to the skin after a short time, a small downside that also prevents over-application. At the beginning, I perceive a bitter, slightly fruity freshness that quickly becomes floral and slightly powdery. The marzipan flits by for a moment and then (thankfully) stays where it always disappears to or doesn’t reappear. As it develops, the flowers come in, and after about 2 hours, a kind of soft woodiness (the suede?) starts to spread more and more. In the first test, alongside this woodiness, the floral creaminess remained more prominent; today, in the second test, there’s more of a slightly fruity-bitter note over suede; here, BB also reminds me of a well-known fragrance that I just can’t recall. Why BB smells one way to me one time and another way at another time seems to be hormonally influenced; I have several fragrances that behave similarly. I’m curious to see how it develops in warmer and especially more humid temperatures. Yesterday and today, it was around 15 degrees and dry; I could imagine that it might become a bit scratchier in cooler temperatures. So I am thrilled with this fragrance and can’t quite understand some of the reviews, but everyone perceives scents differently, and they unfold differently for each person. Surely, the Ambroxan might not excite many, and I usually have my issues with it, but not here. BB is a classically simple fragrance that will surely accompany the modern bride but also fits well with a suit, leather pants, or torn jeans; it actually goes with everything. In my opinion, the campaign doesn’t really match; when I saw the clip for the first time, I had a completely different idea of this fragrance. It’s a shame that BB is not available in stores here; I could only find it online, and even then, not everywhere. Anyone looking for a fine, classic, unsweetened fragrance should give BB a chance.

In 1985, Estee Lauder launched their floral-radiant perfume "Beautiful," marketed at the time as a "wedding scent." A masterpiece that fulfilled the fundamental condition set by the renowned perfumer Guy Robert: "Un parfum doit sentir bon." In 2018, the new fragrance "Beautiful Belle" from Lauder apparently tried to connect to the great model from '85. "Beautiful Belle" (I will refer to the scent as BB from here on) is, however, neither "belle" nor "beautiful." This was not the work of a genius like Sophia Grosjman, but rather some fragrance technicians who must have toiled under the directives of the marketing department. I imagine their considerations/ brainstorming session as follows: "La vie est belle" is a mega-seller - stop - good people, we can also speak French, so why not use "Belle" for the name? It might ring a bell with our customers... ... Bride and flowers, always a popular choice - let's activate the positive associations that the classic "Beautiful" evokes in women aged 50 and above! - we are focusing on "Modern reinterpretation"! What does the chemistry toolbox offer us in this context? - We will not construct a Chypre, as this genre does not appeal to younger consumers... (And oakmoss has been "out" for a long time anyway.) - Artificial fruit aromas in the top note sell well... always!!! - Lychee! Splash! - Then tuberose, orange blossom, now standard. - Can we add a bit of sweetness? (- Not too gourmet - it shouldn't be annoying or burdensome, as that doesn't fit a "bridal scent.") Technician-Chemist 2 suggests "Marzipan - Musk." (Although it smells more like fabric softener than real marzipan, the suppliers of aroma chemicals are currently selling this molecule very well.) Ambroxan!!!!! Ambroxan big time! Of course, you need it for the fixative... ---- yes, almost perfect, we're getting there... ---- However, Aerin Lauder, who is presenting the new creation, still feels something is missing. "The bride of 1885 was not as cool as the model who is supposed to represent it in 2018." Does the scent need a little "edgy touch"? - Suede. Suede, the little contrast to the floral program, okay, let's indulge... quite bold, isn't it? "But please not too much." ---- What has emerged is a mainstream, completely unremarkable daytime scent with a shocking overdose of Ambroxan and a huge disappointment potential. Estee Lauder! For me, it used to be a brand whose fragrances were milestones in perfume history. Youth Dew! Alliage! White Linen! You name it... But in 2018? BB. Beh, Beh. Meh, Meh. (On Fragrantica, a perceptive user from the USA wrote: "It's going to flop, will definitely end up at Tkmaxx." She was right. It's already there. Went quickly. Currently €32 in Cologne).

If you want character in a fragrance, if you love an original touch, if it's unusual notes you're after or if you crave experimental, audacious scents - do avoid this one. "Downtown" is a banal, simplistic soft floral for people who hate their fragrances to be potent or bold. It's a meak dilution of some flowers and cheap aromachemicals which suggest that the last thing you want on earth is sexuality in a perfume bottle. "Downtown" is airy, hasn't got much staying-power. You won't be noticed, neither downtown nor uptown. And I thought the rise of clean, slightly fruity soft florals was over. Can't believe that this fragrance was launched by the company which gave us "Obsession".

I can understand why Downtown was slept on. When it was introduced, people were hoping for something edgy, attention grabbing... the next Euphoria. And Downtown is not in your face at all.
