What it is though, is haunting. I did find this one special. Peppery at the start, then moving into juicy fruit notes, then creamy floral and a soft vanilla-musk drydown. It stays pretty close to the skin, almost giving the impression of a beautiful fancy lotion. It reminded me slightly of 212 Sexy, but it's not as sweet as that one. Downtown is a rather nice cozy scent and I believe it suffers from the fate of the smell not matching up with the name, packaging or advertising. I would absolutely buy another bottle, it is a great fragrance for when you're just being relaxed and casual.

My immediate sense was one of pleasure. This is a scent that hugs you and just makes you feel comfortable. Unfortunately, it's similar to many others on the market today. Is it the pear or the plum again that makes it another common scent that's flooding today's market? Come the dry down, the pepper mixes in delicately to make this a soft fragrance perfect for any age, wearable to the office and perfect for day wear. It's a good relaxing perfume, one to go to sleep with, to spritz your pillows and dream. There's a fruity composition to Downtown and it makes the name a misnomer for some who might have been expecting something else to live up to this name. But, people should learn the name and the face that pushes the fragrance shouldn't matter about what's truly in the bottle. What is important is how a perfume reacts with your chemistry. If it makes you feel good, then it works. Downtown works as another fruity blend of 2013, adding the pepper with a dose of musk. If you don't already own this type of fragrance, certainly give it a trial run. If you do, sample it and see if it's one you'd like to add to your stock. Nothing special, nothing to write home about, nothing to remembered by. Just something comfortable, like an old favorite sweatshirt. Regardless, another one chalked up to the perfume annals of Calvin Klein.

I am certainly not suspected of bursting into enthusiasm over pink mainstream fragrances. Nevertheless, I believe it is too easy to judge the scent with a shrug and a dismissive "nice." I understand that anyone currently engaged with Roja Dove or oud fragrances will - if they even deem it worthy of being tested - see their prejudice against such bread-and-butter perfumes confirmed. Downtown is supposed to earn money for Coty and not herald a golden age of perfumery. But to dismiss it as weighed and found wanting feels to me like criticizing light vacation reading for not being a profound drama. Yet the scent is not as banal as it seems. The plum in the top note already saves it from being interchangeable, its floral notes are bright and by no means sweet, and in the drydown, Downtown becomes somewhat serious on my skin, especially since the often unavoidable vanilla is not employed here to add a cuddly factor. I would have no problem wearing Downtown as a daytime fragrance. Mind you, during the day and perhaps for a city stroll. To experience something special with Downtown in the sense of Petula Clark's evergreen, we certainly have other fragrances in the collection.

Sometimes you have spontaneous associations. Sometimes they are accurate, sometimes they lead you quite astray. And sometimes you just can't understand the associations of other people. As a child of the early 1970s, I grew up with a hit from 1964, which was still a chart-topper back then and has now become an evergreen. In hardly any other song is there such fervor in singing about a beautiful experience that lifts you up when you simply go into the city, seek the company of others, and let yourself drift like in "Downtown" by Petula Clark. "We can forget all our troubles, forget all our cares So go downtown Things will be great when you're downtown Don't wait a minute more, downtown Everything is waiting for you, downtown" With these lines on my lips, I now stand in front of the shelf of a perfume store. The fragrance can only lose from here, as the bar of expectations is set damn high. It should definitely be a feel-good scent. The packaging is definitely not wrong. A beautiful pink box with a slight ribbing and a Calvin Klein-typical clear labeling. Inside is a very simple and heavy bottle. A pure cylinder made of clear glass with a very solid and rounded base. The unembellished cap is silver and has a depression on top with pink inlay work. The slightly pink liquid radiates subtly and gives the bottle an elegant appearance. I like it, also because of the heavy feel. But then my gaze falls on the rather dull expression of Rooney Mara, who is supposed to promote this fragrance in the media - I have no idea what message this look is supposed to convey to me. Luckily, I still have Petula Clark in my head. The fragrance opens with a concentrated fruity and floral sweetness, which I have already encountered in so many other pink women's fragrances. I can only guess at citrus components; instead, I perceive artificial pear and plum. Alongside this are floral notes, unfortunately also synthetic and unidentifiable for me. In the background, at some point, musky notes appear combined with something woody, unfortunately quite arbitrary and imprecise. I cannot detect any smoky, herbal, or even peppery tones of the pyramid, no matter how hard I try. "Downtown" feels very rounded and harmonious, almost streamlined. No corners or edges disturb. This makes the fragrance interchangeable, confusing, arbitrary, without a distinctive character. For me, it's a typical American office scent. Not to stand out, not to take center stage, and not to clash. Leaving no traces in the office downtown. Leaving no scent trail when someone else takes your place in the cubicle tomorrow. For that, "Downtown" also lacks sufficient sillage and longevity. You can only survive the workday with this scent if you refresh it during your lunch break. The projection is also tailored to the scant two square meters of a cubicle - you hardly smell it any further. For the elevator, it’s almost too penetrating, were it not for the fact that the scent is so feminine, soft, subtly fruity, and floral. "Downtown" is a nice fragrance. Nice - but nothing more. Nice for the office. Thus, Ann Gottlieb definitely did not have Petula Clark's song in mind when composing this fragrance.

Completely untypical for me, I have fallen in love with this round fragrance composition, as I usually prefer exciting, angular, fresh, and striking scents. If vanilla had been added, which I personally often find intrusive and clingy, it would probably be a popular fragrance for many who favor gourmand scents.

~ Inspiration ~ The small bottle caught my attention because of its color. I sprayed it on a test strip at the department store, but it didn't convince me. Now, I received a sample from the lovely Tiane during a swap. ~ Bottle ~ Modern and simple.

Is that really so? "Downtown" was included in my sample pack and intrigued me from the start, as I was a passionate Calvin Klein wearer 25 years ago, back then it was "Obsession." The previous comments had internally prepared me for the fact that this is a rather delicate fragrance and not a powerhouse like the aforementioned Obsession.

hits the mark for me as well! I just noticed that I've rated everything as mediocre. Yes, it’s not bad, smells quite nice. It spontaneously reminded me of "See by Chloe". Just like this Chloe scent, I perceive it more as a fabric softener fragrance or it reminds me of laundry detergent, pleasant but not really special, interchangeable, inconspicuous, and clean!

If someone had shown me the scent and told me it was a brand like Calvin Klein, I probably wouldn't have believed it. It smells sweet and synthetic with a hint of fruit. At first, it makes a good impression, but that quickly fades. The whole scent disappears quickly, not just the impression. So it remains just an impression, and the rest you have to search for.

With Time for Peace for Her, I would like to dedicate myself today to a little gem of a fragrance that has been in my collection since the year of its launch, namely 1999. This scent is now hard to come by, as it was limited (unfortunately, the information from Parfumo is incorrect here), supposedly to 200,000 pieces, but I can't say for sure. I acquired it during a personal time frame when fragrances didn't play as big a role in my life as they do today (or did in earlier times), but were simply tested, bought, and worn according to the motto: Like. The 100ml bottle -- and Time for Peace was only available in this size -- has survived the years unscathed, accompanying me through moves, life phases, ups & downs, mild, quiet, and friendly. Just as if we had Japan in the bottle before us. Here I am certainly speaking quite boldly, as I have never been to Japan - unfortunately - the Japanese culture encounters me only in superficial contact with Japanese people, visits to Japanese tea houses, learned knowledge, reports from friends who have spent longer periods in Japan, the music of Ryuichi Sakamoto, and above all: in the form of the brilliant drawings and stories of the manga artist Jiro Taniguchi. His works like "The Observation of Things," "A Zoo in Winter," or "Familiar Strangers" captivate me with their strong expressiveness, the love for detail combined with artistic simplicity, and the intensity of emotions. Human fate and feelings that can be understood and felt regardless of country or culture are grandly portrayed here. And yet they are deeply rooted in Japanese culture. The first internationally recognized work by Jiro Taniguchi is "The Walking Man." A small book about a man who, on his quiet, solitary, lonely walks in very different places at various times of the day and year, takes in impressions, delights in small moments, finds beauty and inspiration in the everyday, completely unpretentiously and simply. He takes the time for it and allows us readers/viewers to quietly partake in these unspectacular things. This is immensely relaxing, quiet, and yet not boring. But since we want to talk about fragrances here, I would like to conclude my little book review and, developing from that, come to Time for Peace. When I breathe in this fragrance, I perceive olfactorily what the walking man conveys to us with all his other senses: Clarity. Refreshment of the spirit. Inspiration. Beauty. Gentleness. Kindness. Warmth. Unobtrusiveness. Peacefulness. The scent is quiet, although the sillage is quite noticeable and present, which I find surprising. It begins with a gentle citrus note, and even here the character is already present: calm, unobtrusive, restrained. Not a refreshing citrus shower, but soft with a hint of warmth, without being sweet. I can clearly smell mandarin, but here it is as delicate and smooth as the porcelain skin of a young Japanese woman, nothing jarring or dominant or overly refreshing. I can hardly perceive blackcurrant; I suspect it is responsible for the very slight bitterness, dryness that flashes for a moment, but even this is without dominance. Everything weaves harmoniously and kindly with the subtle floral progression; I cannot clearly sniff out a single note described in the fragrance pyramid, although I have really tried. Everything is: round. Harmonious. Intertwined. Friendly. A delicate powder joins in, but even this *naturally* only as an unobtrusive impression. Interestingly, however, I discover a small leathery hint, too weak for me to attribute the character of "leather" to the fragrance, but still clear enough that I would like to smell it on a man at this stage. A skin-like effect, interestingly reminiscent of a bit of dirt on the skin, somewhat "greasy," almost a little leather-gasoline note, certainly not clean-skin-like, and such fascinating, surprising elements, I have truly never smelled like this before. Now one might want to reflect on the depths of the clean Japanese culture, as there is no doubt about its existence, and literature & film have certainly already pondered many thoughts about it. But I do not want to elaborate too much on this, even if this dirty leather-skin effect seems quite intentional to me, as it is clearly a conscious break from the peaceful, feminine gentleness. Or perhaps it is just a clever transition to the warm, sensual base that settles in for me after about 4-5 hours: amber finely sweet, not overwhelming, and musk completely caressingly soft: now Time for Peace has fully returned to gentle, warm, sensual femininity. Just like the walking man, who returns home to his wife's arms after his long, solitary excursions, recharged with strength and inner peace, to face the everyday madness once again.

it smells like a broken up chocolate chip cookie on the floor of an indoor swimming pool (i get chlorine lol, maybe from the raspberry + animalistic notes?). in the base, it’s rather airy and vanillay, and has a burnt-like quality like this cookie has been in the oven for too long. paired it with nanatopia in store and it’s quite scrumptious! other person at the same boutique as me sprayed it on a strip and said it smells like something from bath & body works. i saw videos of people calling it “be my arsonist” and be my “dookie”, but ion get any of that. it’s definitely not a bianco latte kind of gourmand, but it has that edge one would expect thinking about BTSO. i also know that they removed the “skatole” note after initially marketing this frag with it. i don’t smell anything resembling shit, so i wouldn’t worry lmao. don’t blind buy though, especially if you can’t handle a darker, animalistic note, because you will find it here, albeit not that poo-y of one. got a sample to play around with along w others before i decide if i want a full bottle or no

ive sampled this several times now and i feel like ppl very much over exaggerated the fecal note. on the opening i thought it was a very nice and sensual musky scent that i initially thought was very sexy but i wouldnt wear it. but as it dried down it sweetened and it became rich, chocolatey, the fecal note just added depth and sex appeal to it. i once saw a review comparing it sharing a post coital snack of cookies was very accurate. this is such an interesting gourmand and i hope “animalic gourmands” continue on would love to see how this compares to pas de chat by odette in this category. cant believe i want a whole bottle but until i have the funds ill annoy my local perfumery by going in to smell this once a week truly nothing else like it on the market

BTSO first marketed this with a "scatone note", which sounds disgusting, especially in combination with their promo pic of a chocolate-smeared perfume bottle. I really don't think fecal notes have any business being in perfumes, but I was still curious enough to get a 1 ml decant. Especially after they received some backlash and changed the note to a less controversial castoreum. Cookies, raspberry and a slight animalic edge doesn't sound too bad, and I know that BTSO's marketing is often edgier than the actual fragrances. That's also the case here. Despite the bad rating (only a measly 5.6 as I'm posting this and even lower when I first looked at this page!), I think this scent is fine. It mainly smells like dark chocolate and raspberry to me, so, nothing repulsive here. The raspberry note is not juicy, it's more on the dry side, a bit like the freeze-dried raspberries you'd find on a chocolate praliné maybe. So, on point with the theme. There is a slightly sharp, musky undertone to this, but I find it more synthetic smelling than animalic, let alone dirty. It calms down as the scent settles on the skin, so the fragrance as a whole is better in the drydown than in the opening. Otherwise it doesn't change a lot. In this price class, I expect a little more complexity, and I could do without the sharpness of the opening, but otherwise, I like this. I'd recommend any fan of chocolate gourmands to try it and see for yourself.

I had the chance to smell this last weekend and at first you think you smell cookies and sweetness which you do smell and that part is nice but at the same time in the opening it is a blast of anamalic stink. Which is a sexual and urine smell. I dont see it being sensual and attractive maybe for some tastes in private situations but no this is one i will not be buying a bottle of.

A dark room. He just stands there quietly, present, with a cookie in his hand. His gaze? Fixed. Hungry. Not for the cookie. For me. Something about him is sweet.. but not cute. It's heavy, warm, almost animalistic this blend of vanilla, dough, and a hint of raw desire. He doesn't smell like a baker. He smells like the forbidden, which you still want. Absolutely. I approach him not because I have to. But because I want to. Because my body knows first, what my mind still suppresses. And suddenly.. there are no more thoughts. Only instinct. Be my Cookie is not an invitation. It's a command, wrapped in butter and sin. And yes, for something like this, I kneel down, even with a smile.

Be My Cookie is a very special fragrance. This scent will definitely not appeal to everyone. It is definitely "niche" here. I actually had a lot of trouble with the initial phase, but over time it becomes much more pleasant and beautiful! The fragrance starts off quite peculiar. This is definitely not for everyone.

This scent is like a Tinder date with a picture of chocolate cookies that then turns out to be an old tobacco dealer. Instead of sweet baking aromas, you get a full dose of "I'm sitting at the regulars' table and philosophizing about cigar formats.

Thanks to Annecy for the great sharing and the extra included fragrances. If I hadn't had the bonus scents, I wouldn't have been so happy with Be My Cookie on its own... I thought this would be a nice, delicious gourmand, but I was shocked that it... well... isn't that at all :') It starts with an extremely piercing synthetic cookie note.

Tested it today and I must say, yes, this one is not for the faint of heart. It starts off quite alcoholic and has a very sharp, piercing note. It really bites. But after a little while, the cookie note comes out more and more and it stays. Dominant and the scent doesn’t really change. Subtle raspberry, yes, but hardly noticeable. Vanilla is subtle.

The beginning of the fragrance is really hard to get used to, or to be honest, I really don't like it. A very piercing, chemical, and almost burnt cookie smell. The raspberry completely gets lost, and to be honest, I had to Google the other two notes because I didn't know them.

Today I had to take care of something in one of my many neighboring cities. Fortunately, there were four perfumeries right on site, at least one of which is owner-operated, and I was hoping to find some lost treasures or bargains or even both. In addition to the usual suspects, I actually discovered something that had never consciously crossed my path before - namely, Intuition for Men by Estée Lauder. The tester still seemed relatively fresh, and together with the charming and friendly saleswoman, I tried to figure out what might be in it. As a start, bright spicy, woody notes waft towards you, and a sweet powderiness also makes its presence felt. Initially, sandalwood and iris were suspected, but the summoned owner was able to quickly clarify the contents, which he apparently copied from a sales brochure from Estée Lauder. That was really very customer-oriented, but only after the base note faded can I say with certainty what to think of Intuition. Since the entire experience is over in just four hours, I also know that I haven't missed anything all these years. Unfortunately, Intuition for Men reminds me too much of Minotaure by Paloma Picasso, albeit in a slightly woodier version and less with a floral undertone. In this case, I would still prefer Intuition - all in all, this fragrance is just not for me, and I wonder why on earth four perfumers had to tinker with it.

A friend of mine tested Intuition on me and then gifted it to her boyfriend for his birthday. Good decision, I think. Intuition is overall quite "empathetic", warm and at the same time a bit cool. It is not very woody, nor particularly spicy, rather it is aromatic and with a gentle depth, which is likely subtly taken on by the incense. The longevity is quite decent, the effect rather restrained, which is necessary for Intuition. You can also happily receive it as a gift. Sammy :-)

Here I was raving on about Polo Blue for having such a lovely cucumber note for about a week, when low and behold there was an even nicer interpretation of cucumber just around the corner. Eternity Aqua has some similarities to its original, however this fragrance is much fresher, more oceanic and a touch more modern. I've really been enjoying Eternity Aqua for the few hours I've known it. It opens with lovely crisp and slightly sweet melon and citrus, with a hint of salty sea water. As it begins to develop, Eternity Aqua has a slight spiciness, mainly brought about by the lavender and pepper. Summer is not far away for me, and seeing that I'm craving the beach these days, Eternity Aqua only excites me more for the coming months. There's nothing sexier than a man that smells fresh and enticing on a hot Summer's day. In the base there is a likable woodsy earthiness, classing this fragrance as a bit of a woody aquatic. I was very much excited about this relatively new release, yet unfortunately like many reviewers have already mentioned, the lasting power is fairly poor. Because this is such a sexy, refreshing and masculine fragrance I will continue to rave about it, however I'll be interested to see for how long it can hold my attention.

I Love the drydown... Very fresh and warm at the same time, like a summer night by the beach,laundry softener smell, but i can't stand the initial blast, reminds me of Donna Karan Delicious Red.. I sense a coffe note in it. Also it's sharp at the first hour. Strange opening! I like the fragrance, but only if i can skip the top notes :)

... it’s just that it was made by the new CK house, and has zero longevity. I know freshies aren’t expected to go very long, but this guy disappears in 3-4hours. I actually enjoy the sweet, fresh scent it gives, but sillage, projection, and longevity all suddenly “drop” out when it’s done working, and there’s not even a “skin scent” left. Thankfully CK fragrances aren’t very expensive (I’m not a fan anyway), as they don’t “perform” well at all.

When I look for new fragrances, I often seek help from the comments here on parfumo. This way, it quickly becomes clear whether the scent falls into the "hit" or "miss" category. If I had done that with Eternity Aqua for Men, it definitely wouldn't be in my collection - which, spoiler alert - would be a real shame. Because: it’s not as bad as it’s made out to be here - on the contrary - I actually find it very good. You just have to know for which occasion to use it. Certainly not for a romantic dinner - definitely never in the evening. But the name already implies that - Acqua. It sounds fresh, sporty, light. And these attributes, in my opinion, are exactly what Eternity Aqua for Men embodies. It’s a light, unobtrusive scent, almost perfect for the workplace or after sports. There is no scent dissonance - which some might associate with being boring - but I like sporty fragrances that don’t aspire to be more than that. By now, it costs next to nothing and I really think you can’t go wrong with this scent. You just have to spray a few more spritzes - then it lasts a bit longer.

I initially perceived Eternity Aqua for men rather casually, but I found it to be a pleasant fragrance. I almost forgot about it until I came across a discounted special size of 200 ml. The poor reviews did surprise me a bit - and spurred me on to verify for myself whether this really is, without me noticing, the last dreadful concoction. Some of you perceive it as a knockoff of "Polo Blue." Certain similarities are indeed recognizable, namely the fresh cucumber note. However, what characterizes Eternity Aqua is a sweet-floral top and heart note with mandarin, which brings us to the DNA that also defines the classic "Eternity for men." With its softly sensual aura, oscillating between cheerfulness and melancholy, it shares at least as much in common with "Bleu" by Chanel or "Eau de Cartier," although like the classic Eternity, it is distinguished by a particularly strong body. It is not a delicate fragrance; those who do not expect this but simply want a practical and masculine scent will find Eternity Aqua to be just right. Conclusion: Not a masterpiece, but a successful child of its time, and at a very fair price!
It has become quite common for me to receive samples from dear perfume enthusiasts to write a comment and share my opinion, often from fragrances that don’t have any comments yet.

The original Eternity for men is, for me, one of the most timeless classic perfumes for men. Accordingly, I was very curious about the Aqua offshoot of Eternity for men. And I was bitterly disappointed. Because what has been composed here is almost unparalleled in its mediocrity. The Eau de Toilette has nothing at all to do with the classic Eternity.

Well, I'm not a big connoisseur of aquatic fragrances, and my nose can't perceive the possible subtleties of these scents or find them particularly pleasant. To me, it's a Calvin Klein fragrance of the current generations. Completely bland with soap. We take 2 parts leftover CK In 2 U (Men), 1 part leftover Eternity, and one part leftover Eternity any summer variant.

I mostly like the fragrances from Calvin Klein: I own Eternity EdP, of course CK One, as well as CK Be. But especially the CK One Summer flankers appeal to me. Eternity Aqua EdT goes in this direction, although it must be clearly stated that it is a different kind of scent than the CK One Summer EdTs. These are mostly fresh and fruity.

Tested today. The scent from Calvin Klein starts off very fresh and aquatic. I would say that this fragrance is well-suited for everyday use, especially for school; it is optimal for teenagers and young adults. I think if you are a young person reading this, this scent is good.

If the colour pink had a smell, it would be this. It smells so girly and fun! I personally don't think the nail polish note in the opening is too harsh or off-putting at all. You're hit with a blast of it at the beginning, but it mellows down pretty quickly. I don't get any of the pink pepper. I'm mostly getting the cotton candy and raspberry notes in this scent with some of the nail polish note lingering in the background, but they all blend together really well in my opinion! It dries down into a more musky, powdery, vanilla-ish scent. It's a really sweet and synthetic scent overall and I think anyone who enjoys fun and girly scents would like it. Don't let the nail polish note scare you!!

This fragrance will give you and your neighbors cavities. That is how sweet and powerful this is. Its the cotton candy that you can smell, but not see, as you are walking into the county fair. Its the smell of fresh hot spun sugar made right in front of you. The dry down eases up on the sweetness and becomes more musky in the dry down but overall this isn't a complex fragrance. Its pure sugar. It lasted well over 6 hours on my skin and the projection was powerful the whole time. Its $205 for 50ml, which is a lot. But if you want a fragrance that you only want to apply once and will have people notice you, then this might be the fragrance for you.

Sampling Borntostandout Angels’ Powder, my first try of the Dirty & Sticky discovery set, a sweet and powdery blend defined by a peculiar mix of cotton candy, vanilla sugar, and nail polish, with the sweet and sharp elements playing against the rather chemical acerbic concept of nail polish, with additional supporting notes of pink pepper and heliotrope to add character. Predictably a bit sharper/headier/more powdery in the opening and smoother, sweeter, a bit creamier in the dry down, I quite prefer the more tempered feeling of the dry down to the more provocative opening, but it’s the opening that feels a bit more unique to me. I quite enjoy its creativity, even if I’m doubt it’s something I would wear with any frequency over a more mainstream vanilla/sugar. As with the rest of the line, this is EDP concentration and is priced at $210/85 for 50/15ml, sold via a few boutiques in the US like Ministry of Scent. It performs very well, adding to its value, and overall the pricing is not bad for niche perfumery. 7 out of 10

Maybe it's just my skin, but the top notes on this are an assault of peppercorn. That's all I can smell, like I just stuffed my face in a bowl of fresh crushed pepper. There is a hint of alcoholic nail polish, but I think that only makes the pepper more aggressive. I will say once I let it sit for around an hour, the pepper died down a lot and it became more powdery. I wouldn't say sweet, but like it had the thought of becoming a gourmand. Out of my discovery set, this one was in #7 out of #8th place.

What a treat! This opens like nail polish once you’ve finished you're set and you’re trying not to smudge it. The nail polish comes through strong on me and I love it. Even in the dry down it never went away. It was like an icy, chemical, cotton candy memory. Very sweet and synthetic in the best way. After hour 4 it got a bit cloying, though. Impressive sillage and longevity here. Happy to test, would not purchase a full bottle.

I actually didn't expect much, a fragrance for women, pink in an elegant bottle, only the description here had piqued my curiosity. But how wonderfully I have been surprised. It starts with fig, it stays with fig, and it lasts long with fig. But from which world does this wonderful fig scent come? Because I have never experienced a scent like this before. A delicacy, a sweetness that never feels exaggerated or even intrusive. A quiet aura surrounds this fragrance and it remains present for a long time. The orange brushes against me lightly, I perceive vetiver. A powdery scent and a phenomenal fragrance. One wants to sink into this scent, like in a magnificent velvet divan between night and day. A twilight in which one wants to linger...perhaps even forever...

CK One Shock, did actually come as a shock to me. I really didn't expect something so sweet and sugary, especially not from a CK One flanker. I am pleasantly surprised however. I get a lot of sweet berries and vanilla. It somewhat resembles the scent of berry flavoured yoghurt. It's a little tart, but mostly soft, feminine and delicately sweet. There are no spices here, as far as I can smell. It's more floral than spicy. The sweetness never diminishes, however the fragrance develops into something quite floral and powdery, with hints of sugary jasmine and passion flower towards the heart. It's a bit of a different approach from the house of Calvin Klein. CK One Shock tends to be less unisex and perhaps more appealing to the younger crowd. CK One is unfortunately becoming one of those classics that appear to the younger market as outdated, so this new release should interest some new fans. I do miss the refreshing citrus in this fragrance though, that CK One and its flankers have been renowned for in the past. This fragrance lasts relatively well, but the sillage is fairly intimate. I'm glad it's not a loud fragrance, otherwise it could probably compete with Britney Spears Fantasy in being the loudest and sweetest scent on the market. I will recommend this fragrance with slight hesitation that it may not be for everyone.

My first impression for this perfume is that it smells like candy, very sweet, warm, powdery. CK One Shock for her is suitable for winter, fall, not really for hot and humid weather. Its sweetness makes me feel young, could be a bit overwhelming with the sweetness after smelling for a while. It should be suitable age range from 16 to 24 or even younger. Despite the very sweet and fruity smell, you should not expect too much from this perfume since it will not last long. Let's say around 2 3 hours. At the end, I would get this perfume if i am really fascinated with the fruity smell, and like to wear it for short while. As for me, I personally would not purchase it again since its longevity just does not worth it.

Takes quite a few sprays to enjoy the creamy vanilla in this Calvin Klein edition. The name and bottle are evidently geared again to a pocketbook that knows no bounds and that is truly a shame. The scent is pretty straight forward. A berry vanilla with a sprinkling of cocoa mixed in for good measure with no sillage and no longevity. It does smell good but really, what is it's point? There are far too many excellent vanilla potions on the market at lower, exactly the same and higher price points. There is no shock value here, except the price and the fact that "Mr. Klein" slapped his moniker on yet another bottle. More of an expensive body splash that has a name and a trendy bottle. Tsk, tsk, tsk. This is a young ones' delight to show off to their friends.

The chocolate/patchouli/amber/vanilla notes in CK One Shock are reminiscent of Mugler's Angel, especially after it sits on the skin for 1+ hrs. With that in mind, its not a patchouli bomb at all. It's refreshing and bright with a cozy dry down. It's well blended and youthful but not overly sweet. It doesn't last very long or project very far so I have to reapply throughout the day, which I don't mind since I got my bottle at Burlington for $20. I find myself wearing this to the office since it has weak sillage and is decently inoffensive. I can smell it on myself for a few hours and love feeling like a sweet and girly Mexican hot cocoa.

I own the male counterpart to Ck One Shock for her, which I like extraordinarily well and will never remove from my collection. Thanks to our dear perfume "hunter," I was finally able to test Ck One Shock for her. I was out in the countryside over the weekend and I still had samples, as I couldn't quite decide. I was torn between Silver Scent Deep by Jacques Bogart and Blue Jeans by Versace. Click! Samples from the hunter made it clear in my mind. We were just sitting down for our third coffee, the table had already been cleared, and only the coffee cups and the sample remained on the table. Ronja, the 11-year-old daughter of my best friend Lea, is now slowly entering the phase where she is becoming interested in fragrances. A true fan of Lady Gaga, and Ronja bears a resemblance to Stefani Joanne Angelina Germanotta (the real name I only know through Ronja). Of course, she also owns Fame and Eau de Gaga; she received Fame from her mom a year ago and Eau de Gaga from me about 6 months ago. Curious as children are, Ronja wanted to finally know what was in the little tube :-) "What’s the name of the fragrance?" "No idea, it was a blind draw, but I have the slips that say who it’s from, what it’s called, and what notes are included." "Then spray it already!" "One for me too?" "Yesss!" Ronja said, beaming with joy. Done, Ronja got one on her right wrist and one on her neck (she always perfumes herself this way; I should take a cue from her sometimes - Michel and Dior Homme Intense? I have to be careful not to completely zone out and empty the whole bottle on my skin; I once managed a quarter of 50 ml and was totally shocked when I came back to "reality". :-)) Alcohol is the first thing Ronja and I perceive, as well as Tine, Jonas, and Lea. "Is it spoiled?" Tine asked. This question was not unwarranted, as perfumes that are about to go bad smell extremely of alcohol and then of Maggie/celery. However, there are also fragrances where this is just how it is at the beginning; Sweet Gourmande Vanilla by Unic is also an example of this. Five minutes later, the alcohol has dissipated, and I immediately smell the poppy; Ronja couldn't relate to this scent component at all but found it pleasantly milky and reminiscent of almond. The little one is not bad at all, as that’s exactly how poppy smells. By coincidence, poppies grow in front of Tine's house, so I took Ronja outside, showed her the flower, and explained that the oil is obtained through steam distillation and that it smells like she described. To this poppy note, the peony joins clearly and distinctly, in its best bloom. You can also sniff out the passion flower very well. The top note lasts about 15-20 minutes for me. For Ronja, however, it lasts a few minutes longer, about 10 minutes. After the top note, Ronja and I have the same image in mind: blackberry jam on toast and a cup of cocoa with a nice fine crema on top. Blackberry and jasmine are the most clearly perceptible; in the background, cocoa and daffodil are at play, these two components are used in such a way that the jasmine and blackberry appear even stronger and creamier. After 5 hours, the base unfolds for me; sweet patchouli is enveloped by lovely vanilla, amber, and musk give the base a nice deep insight. Overall, the fragrance lasts a good 7 hours on my skin; for Ronja, it lasts another 2 hours longer. The sillage is in a good middle ground, it doesn’t disturb anyone, it’s not overwhelming, but if you come into contact at half an arm's length, the fragrance will definitely be noticed. Ronja has had more luck with this fragrance regarding longevity and sillage, as for Ronja, the sillage is stronger, lasts longer, and the famous blackberry jam toast with crema cocoa comes through every now and then. Here too, Calvin Klein has proven that even a women's fragrance in the lower price segment can be convincing.

~ Inspiration ~ "CK One Shock" made it onto my wishlist primarily because of its vanilla-cocoa notes. ~ Bottle ~ The well-known, flat shape of the "CK" flanker appears here in white lacquer. Under the black logo, the word "Shock" is written in pink, slanted lettering, designed to look as if it were written with lipstick.

In search of new fragrance impressions, I was introduced to CK One Shock for her, and we seemed to get along very well at first. On my skin, it initially presented itself in a light-sweet, fresh-berry way with a hint of patchouli in the underlying tones, and within the next half hour, it transformed into a caramel-chocolate scent that blew me away.

This is a case of "I'll give them a sample, a sample, a sample, and another sample..." - you get filled up with it. What am I doing in my fear? Testing - you can't just pour everything down the drain. Hello Kitty sends her regards! A scent can't be pinker. A taste experience of a special kind - it smells like Five Gum Flood tastes.

It wasn't particularly large but inviting and cozy. Even before entering, one could smell the sweets paired with the beautifully decorated flowers. In the display window, peonies, whose blossoms were as big as baby heads, lined up next to deep red poppies and tender jasmine branches. Inside the store, a huge chocolate fountain greeted you.

One winter, I decided to tighten my financial belt. Soon, however, I needed something new in fragrance... You surely know the feeling: It's not that you have nothing left, but you've worn everything for a while, you want something else........ ;) So, as a middle-aged lady, I ended up with Pink, Sweet, Hello Kitty.... Can this work? Yes it can!

I can´t imagine this fragrance for a night out. It feels more likea deodorant in the scent. You spray some when you want to feel fresh and clean. It might be a great work fragrance if sprayed gently. I haven´t decide yet if it´s a keeper. It´s not unpleasant in any way. The coconut appeals to me.

EL Brasil Dream is a summer tropical white floral. Because of the white florals - which don't wear well on me in heat - this will be a cold weather fragrance. It will be perfect to be whisk me away to the tropics when the snow is knee-deep in a few months. EL Brasil Dream very similar to Liz Claiborne Bora Bora to me. BD has more fruit & BB has more ginger, but yes, they're similar. Ironically, I think Brasil Dream smells more like Bora Bora than LC Bora Bora. Nothing terrible or spectacular about BD. I obtained a bottle in a swap, and I will probably let it go in a swap.

Right now, Brazil is on everyone's lips. However, I'm not really interested in football. I have never been to Brazil, I have no idea what it looks like there or how it smells. As an Estee Lauder customer, I am naturally shown all the new fragrance releases, and a few years ago, I was sprayed with Brazil Dream. I still remember very well that I received several compliments that day for my pleasant scent. Brazil Dream is a fruity fresh fragrance that spreads a holiday mood. The exotic fruits have a woody and bitter undertone. It smells very special and refreshingly spicy. I can clearly recognize the pineapple and the orange, as well as the citrus notes. The floral part with jasmine and gardenia, which sweetens the fragrance, also has this slightly woody-bitter undertone. I don't know any fragrance that is as bitter as Brazil Dream. The longevity is good, the scent is very distinctive yet not at all intrusive. Does it smell like this in Brazil? I don't know. As a child, I spent several weeks of summer vacation in Peter Rosegger's forest homeland. An old miner's house was converted into holiday apartments. The caretaker was a very energetic woman and lived on the ground floor. Her daughter-in-law spent that summer with her. Ruth was from Rio de Janeiro and had met and married the caretaker's son there. She could not communicate with her mother-in-law, as she spoke no English. Ruth was only a few years older than me, and with my school English, I was able to converse with her. Her husband was back at work as a mechanic somewhere in the world, and Ruth was very lonely. We became friends. She occupied the former children's room of her husband. All her belongings were packed in a travel bag. On her bed sat a bright orange plush tiger - a gift from her siblings. She told me a lot about Brazil and her family. Ruth was very homesick. We both enjoyed all the attractions that the forest homeland had to offer at that time. We walked in the woods, picked blackberries and ate them afterwards, and now and then we marched down the dusty path to St. Kathrein am Hauenstein to the swimming pool. We could not have been more different. Ruth, the dark, petite Brazilian, and I, the pale, then scrawny creature. And yet, that was the foundation for a long (pen) friendship. As a farewell gift, she gave me the plush tiger. Her marriage ended in divorce, she moved back to Brazil, remarried, and at some point, we lost touch. I still have the little plush tiger. He sleeps in the farthest corner of my wardrobe. During major cleaning, he gets shaken and petted. In the almost forty years, I have not been able to bring myself to part with him. When I wear Brazil Dream, I have to think of Ruth. I have never been to Brazil, I don't know what it looks like there or how it smells. But I knew Ruth!

A typically exotic-fruity scent, as the name suggests, without any edges or corners. It’s interesting that the fragrance market in Brazil operates completely differently than in Europe or the States. What is considered classic or mainstream here would not be worn by anyone in Brazil. I saw this recently in a documentary. They tested new LYNX fragrances (known as AXE here) on pubescent Brazilian boys. In tropical countries, much more fragrance is used than in the northern hemisphere, as people sweat more and shower more often. But that’s beside the point. Back to Brazil Dream, which would probably not evoke much enthusiasm in Brazil, as it also has notes of orange. And according to the aforementioned documentary, oranges are very cheap in Brazil. Therefore, people don’t want to smell like them. Overall, this is a typical summer fragrance for me, as it is very light and lacks significant depth, spice, or sweetness. Ideal for women who want to surround themselves with a hint of exoticism without standing out. I don’t count myself among them.

Calvin Klein OBSESSION NIGHT WOMAN is a great flanker, but it is completely misnamed. It should really be called: CERRUTI 1881 SANS SAVON. I jest not, the similarities between ONW and CERRUTI 1881 are patent, despite the apparent dissimilarities of their floral notes. The bases are nearly identical, and the proportions of flowers must be about the same, although OBSESSION NIGHT WOMAN boasts neither iris nor violet. It's rather remarkable, in fact, how wrong OBSESSION NIGHT WOMAN is as a name for this very likeable, totally unobsessional, daytime, unisex fragrance. This is a light woody-floral, slightly sweet and barely spicy perfume, which I like a lot. I prefer CERRUTI 1881, because it has a bit more depth and I do like its soupcon of soapiness, but if I run into a bottle of ONW, I might well add it to my collection. Very nice and subtle. Essentially the antithesis of OBSESSION.

This fragrance struck me as being very unique, also being very different to what I expected it to smell like. Obsession Night in my mind, was a darker and sexier version of the original Obsession, perhaps a little smokier and sweet. In reality, Obsession Night is mostly a gentle floral with some masculine qualities, a tad too musky and in some ways synthetic, but not in an unpleasant way. Everytime I smell this fragrance, I'm stuck for words to describe it. It's non-descript yet rather appealing. The scent itself is quite subdued, mostly a nice blend of clean white florals, a hint of sweet citrus and dusty vanilla. Towards the drydown is where Obession Night begins to smell slightly masculine. It has a somewhat woodsy, pencil-shavings kind of smell to it. After awhile the scent does bore me, however if I bring my wrist to my nose and inhale deeply, I am once again intrigued and fascinated. Obsession Night may be one of those fragrances that grow on you. As I'm reviewing this fragrance now, I almost feel bad for saying what I've said in the previous paragraphs, because the more I smell it, the more I begin to like it. Smelling it again, it almost smells like baby wipes. I must add that I like the scent of baby wipes. My opinions on this fragrance are continually changing. I don't believe that it's possible for me to come to any kind of conclusion. In terms of sillage and lasting strength, I'll give this fragrance the thumbs up. All I have left to say is that this is an interesting scent, rather smooth, sometimes creamy, and generally likable.

From the series ‘Little hidden gems to be dusted off now and then'. Got it in July and it was nice, sprayed it today: even better! Now, as for the ‘Night’ part – I don’t get any Night vibe, to be honest. I would’ve called it Obsession Shine, or Sun, or Gold, whatever. It’s crystal-clear, clean, shining. There’s a nice woody presence, but not that deep nor intense enough to turn it dark. Honestly, the original Obsession feels more ‘Night’ than this one. Oh, and aside from the name, this flanker has nothing in common with the OG. Like, zero. It’s an easy everyday scent, but don’t expect a usual white floral. It’s got something extra. Really lovely

In a neighborhood perfumery, I bought this little treasure not too long ago as a discounted item. But "Obsession Night" really does not smell like a "discounted item." It is a beautiful, slightly dark, but also finely aquatic chypre fragrance that comes to my nose. The EdP has little in common with Calvin Klein's oriental-chypre "original" Obsession. Instead, it has other qualities. With its spicy fresh top notes, it takes me straight to a late spring evening. And this almost imperceptibly transitions into a velvety violet night, where the soft floral notes take center stage. A dark rose stands out, flanked by jasmine, green lily of the valley, and fresh gardenia. I find myself in a garden, in the middle of which a large water lily pond "reigns." A hint of nearby water... Especially velvety and "violet" seem to me the wonderful vanilla and wood notes that almost sneak in during the nighttime silence. And, I believe I can catch at least a fine veil of delicious moss that clings to the trunk of an old tree.

I’ve done a bit of detective work... Recently, I encountered an incredibly interesting perfume on an intriguing woman I spent a few days with. Something that women of the strong, confident, intelligent, and slightly extravagant type wear. I’m not really any of that and, of course, I didn’t dare to ask what fascinating fragrance she was wearing. But this scent captivated me, and I immediately associated it with dark blue... radiant, deep, and mysterious. So I did some online research and vaguely moved in that direction, testing a few potential candidates... nothing. This blue bottle had actually been part of my test group from the beginning, but I first couldn’t find the liquid and then ultimately buried the whole project in defeat. No chance of finding the needle in the haystack. Today, I was just passing by and intended to quickly sniff something completely different when, by chance, this blue bottle stood before me, and I thought: "Oh yes, right, I actually wanted to..." A spritz on the paper strip... cautiously sniffed... BOOM! Obsession Night. That’s it. A spritz on the wrist and let it all unfold. My heart races. This scent starts invitingly, fresh, and promising. But then, unexpectedly, an incredible depth opens up. A mixture of flowers, both bright and dark and radiant. Intense. Beneath it, a slightly bitter base, where a hint of warming vanilla emerges. A fragrance full of contradictions that confuses me and makes me happy at the same time. I actually have a completely different type of taste and wouldn’t have thought I could wear something like this. But it works; on me, the scent develops much more intensely and darker than on paper. It’s as if it had been waiting for me. Yes, it is intense and can be overdone, but even the effect of a spritz lasts long and leaves a fascinating scent trail. Definitely not an everyday scent for me, but Obsession Night will definitely be my new going-out fragrance. Or the perfume for special occasions when I need that touch of extravagance. If my beloved Chloé EdP is my "me," then Obsession Night will be my alter ego.

No, I don't mean a beer mix brew, but Alster water. The water of the Alster. At least sometimes the Alster smells like this. On certain summer evenings, at sunset. In the spots where it is green and cozy, and where only a few joggers rush by. There I park my bike, sprawl out on the grass, and stare blankly into the distance.

Dear Peanut, it's your fault! You should have known that as a Hamburg boy, I can't resist the scent of the Alster! And that I absolutely have to bring it into my Rhineland exile when it's bottled! For that, I'm just a bit cheeky and stealing your headline.;-) Indeed, Obsession smells like water - unlike most aquatic fragrances with their marine accord of algae, etc.

Now that this fragrance had such a hard time reaching me, I want to dedicate a comment to it. The lovely Pauline sent it to me last week (along with 2 other samples), and we both wondered why nothing arrived. Vandals had set fire to the mailbox of the post office, and Obsession Night along with the other two fell victim to it. Rest in peace.

I sprayed Night and Obsession side by side, and to my surprise, Night is milder and brighter than Obsession. Night is probably more suited for the White Nights in St. Petersburg, or the bright nights at the Arctic Circle, where the sun does not set in summer. This impression is further enhanced by the white flowers and the lily of the valley.

Recently, I was thinking about scents that help me relax in my everyday life and bring me peace. Because somehow I realized that I don't have a fragrance in my collection that truly conveys that feeling of calm and serenity. I love my fragrances. However, I currently long for tranquility and composure, just like many others probably do in our fast-paced times.

Perfume Kenzo L'Eau par Kenzo Mirror Edition for Women - Flanker of the famous perfume L’Eau par Kenzo for Women (1996). However, it is the freshest and has richer juicy fruit notes. The floral accord resonates with light floral accents. Good for the summer season. Limited. The author of the fragrance is perfumer Antoine Lie, who also created Valentino Gold, Armani Code Giorgio Armani, Crystal Noir Versace, etc. In the L'Eau par Kenzo Mirror Edition for Women, the bouquet of the composition is based on expressive refreshing mint and fruit accords, which are complemented by lighter sweet accents, floral notes of lily of the valley, violet, and sandalwood aromas. Raspberry and melon are rather subtle, not too intrusive. This allows the freshness to dominate the sweetness and reveals an aquatic note - something spring-like that melts in the wind, a bit like willow. The aroma is floral, aquatic, even a bit toy-like. It creates an image that may be somewhat flirtatious and frivolous, but that does not detract from it. It is more of a daytime fragrance. Overall, it is girlish and youthful, but on an adult woman, it will look completely adequate.

Intimacy and comfort are promised, purity is expected... well, what I smell is fresh laundry, but not the nice fresh laundry scent; instead, very cheap bleach has definitely been used here, and then the laundry was left for what feels like 3-4 days without a spin cycle. Long story short: - The opening is really pleasant for about 10 seconds, until those aldehydic components with this synthetic note go in a direction that really smells like bleach. It absolutely does not smell "fresh, clean" afterwards, but rather chemically synthetic, yes, like bleach cleaner. - This bleach note is so pronounced that you hardly notice any of the sweetness that is supposed to be there; yes, if you concentrate really hard, you might catch a whiff of sweetness, but it is very subtle; at most, a light honey note in the background. - As it develops, thankfully this bleach note significantly fades, and you are left with a synthetically minimal creamy "clean base." - Performance is, well, below average. Provocative concept, yes, but the craftsmanship in this case is really subpar from my perspective. It's not that I don't like this type of fragrance; it's just that it is effectively not well thought out. Too synthetic, too piercing, too trivial. One must also be critical from time to time, and in this case, I believe it is truly justified.

I’ve been looking for light, airy, fresh scents for the hottest days of summer, and for that criteria this is an absolute win. On first sniff I find it very evocative; it definitely has those Aegean vibes! The opening is green, a tad citrusy, lots of violet leaf. A touch ozonic. After about 30 minutes it becomes sweeter and creamier, with the coconut milk becoming the dominant note against a background of watery florals. I’ve got to say, I love it. This is a surprise to me as normally I prefer scents that the neighbourhood can smell, and this one is quiet, clean, effortlessly sexy and put-together. It creates an intimate bubble of sweet yet refreshing scent, and never comes anything close to cloying. It’s everything I hoped, and absolutely perfect for summer. It’s not the longest lasting, but tbh I wouldn’t expect it to be; crazy longevity is not the assignment here and I’m happy to respray.

After the first sniff from the bottle, I was very surprised by the freshness of the bergamot. It came across as very dominant and reminded me strongly of Lady Million Eau my gold at first spray. My first thought was, "quite nice, but can move on." But then the fragrance underwent an unexpected transformation. It suddenly became very warm and soft, revealing a very noble coconut note paired with sweet fig. All of this, however, is very light and airy, like a warm summer breeze. It smells extremely high-quality, yet absolutely unobtrusive. H&S are very subtle. Therefore, a clear recommendation for both the office and the evening. It caresses in a very special way.

Here you get a fresh coconut summer scent. The fragrance is not as sweet as I had expected. In fact, it feels very fresh and light. Longevity and sillage are not very strong with this scent. Those who enjoy fig and coconut with fresh notes from Italian bergamot will find this appealing. However, I don't get any sunscreen vibes from it. It comes across as too fresh for that.

When I saw the announcement, I was thrilled. Greece is the vacation destination this year. No wonder Estee Lauder is also thinking about how to take their Bronze Goddess there. And how they can do that. While the summery sunscreen creaminess, which is very reminiscent of Soleil Blanc by Tom Ford, spreads and envelops you, a sweet and later especially a green fig gradually comes through. The scent that spreads especially on the islands when you take a little break in a quiet spot during your lunch break. I'm a fan! In my current vision, I definitely see myself wearing this this summer. A more detailed review will come when the temperatures really head in that direction.

Typical Goddess DNA, moderate sillage. Nothing disturbs, nothing is overwhelmingly present. No sticky sunscreen associations. Somehow elegantly crafted. For me, fig (not green, not earthy) and a subtle coconut note are the most prominent. Above all, a hint of citrus lingers. Perfect for the upcoming summer days. Whether those around me notice it is questionable. Personally, I perceive it as a rather intimate scent, for that personal vacation cloud feeling.

This fragrance presents a citrusy, aromatic character that immediately feels more assertive than its classic counterpart. While the original version offers a soft, smooth, and pleasantly summery citrus profile, this interpretation pushes the composition in a bolder direction. The notes come across sharper, more masculine, and distinctly spicier, giving the scent a tougher edge and a more dynamic personality. The sillage is slightly more pronounced, creating a clearer presence in the air, though the overall longevity remains similar to the classic. It’s a vibrant twist on a familiar formula—recognizable, yet noticeably more daring.

The "Original" CK One has been a staple in my perfume collection since the 90s. Some of the numerous summer and other variants have also found their way into my collection for a time and were quite pleasing, so I was very curious about the announcement of "CK One Essence | Calvin Klein." The pyramid makes my heart flutter, except for the incense! So here comes the bottle, designed in the typical CK One style, very chic in silver metallic. Thanks to the design, you can still see the fill level! Just for you today, the comparison test with the original CK One Eau de Toilette on the other arm AND also on my test subject aka husband (short: GG ....too bad I can't post pictures here, his facial expression was priceless - he doesn't like wearing perfume, and the prospect of two scents at once didn't exactly make him jump for joy). ON HIM: great peppery start with soft lemon, could also be lime; no blood orange and no trace of tea anywhere ON ME: hardly any pepper, no tea either, but significantly more almost biting citrus (just barely avoiding a cleaner association) and it turns green much faster. after 30+ min: ON HIM: the scent can't quite decide between green and aquatic, but it's nice and fresh - the CK One tested in parallel shows slightly more residual fruit and is significantly less present at the same dosage. ON ME: Essence has opted for aquatic, I don't smell any geranium. Sporty fresh but almost too masculine for my unisex-loving taste. GG agrees with me and said that the little bit more "edge" it has on me would be wearable for him, but on me, it comes across as sport shower gel-like. CLEAR difference on the skin compared to CK One - the original is softer on me (more musk), white-green instead of blue. Towards the end: For both of us, CK One Essence dries down to a woody-spicy finish, interestingly more bitter on me than on my husband. I suspect the moss-incense combo; I haven't really warmed up to it yet. So I like the scent - but I prefer it on men rather than on me! For both of us, the longevity and sillage of Essence were significantly stronger than that of the original. Fairness requires considering that CK One is "only" an EdT. The price has always been great anyway. So to make it short: NO - CK One Essence is not CK One Eau de Toilette "just stronger"! I like it a lot, but I think it will suit men better, and I predict a 80/20 percent split among owners here later. My bottle will probably have to find a new owner, my GG looked too panicked when I said he could use up the bottle ;) It is a great, fresh, sporty, and depending on the skin, green or aquatic summer scent that does without sweetness and floral notes. A solid office and everyday fragrance!

“CK One Essence” is a tasty bore. Zesty blood orange paired with the most classic, neutral “CK One” DNA. Everything is super subtle and quiet. That’s okay. It’s wearable. But somehow, there’s a lack of that certain something at every corner… Zesty, fresh, clean, unisex. Over time, it becomes slightly creamy-skin-like, almost leaning towards a very, very subtle sunscreen. That’s it. One shouldn’t expect miracles. It does its job. It doesn’t reinvent the wheel. Not even a spoke. It works. After a shower, during sports, for changing rooms and leisure. The 90s have been making a comeback for a while now, culturally replacing the 80s. “CK One Essence” hits this note and plays it extremely safe. I don’t see an essence of anything here, no matter how hard I try. Bestsellers smell different. Because too much “lowest common denominator” doesn’t create a major breakthrough anywhere. The blood orange as a minimal-modern “kick” can hardly be called a “kick.” And it’s seriously lacking in character and uniqueness. Especially with the shiny appearance and the title “Essence,” one expects more of everything than what is delivered here… Bottle: silver, shiny, not bad Sillage: subtle when it’s burning Longevity: 5 hours, at best Conclusion: not outstanding - even compared to the many other CK Ones… Never stinky, but a pretty nondescript freshy. It falls in line.

CK One Essence earns some initial points because the marketing here is on point. By now, Elixir, Intense, or Absolute versions from a brand can be something completely different from the original product - but not here. At its core, Essence is a more intense, deeper version of the original, while largely retaining the lightness and DNA of the famous predecessor. After the zesty opening, it goes in the direction of a lemon tea with quite strong lemon and green nuances, if you will. In the base, you can sense the pepper and woods a bit, and it develops slightly towards sunscreen, but maintains the lemon note throughout. I find the longevity and sillage to be just as "poor" or typical as with any flanker. First of all - yes, there is enough difference that this product has its place. It is indeed different - without being better or worse. For me, it feels a bit "more mature" and modern, but slightly loses its OG charm. In case of doubt, I would prefer the OG, but I also find joy in this flanker.

CK One Essence is a more intense reinterpretation of the iconic CK One. The fragrance opens with a fresh blend of bergamot and blood orange, providing a zesty start. At its heart, the characteristic green tea remains, while the base adds a warmer and deeper note with sandalwood and musk. Compared to the original, the longevity is noticeably better, without losing the light, unobtrusive DNA. The fragrance remains uncomplicated, modern, and versatile. The bottle stays true to the minimalist design but appears even more elegant with its metallic finish.

This is a lovely fragrance. Musky, sweet, light and unique. It's a typical musk in that it sets close to the skin and doesn't project. What makes it most challenging is that you can't get closer than 8-12" from where you sprayed it to smell it. If you do, the civet and animalics take over and it's not enjoyable. So while I really enjoy the fragrance, I don't think I can invest in a bottle that can only be enjoyed with so many constraints. What a shame because it's beautiful under perfect circumstances.

I became aware of the brand borntostandout through the grand Dirty Milk and tested a few of the different fragrances. This one is, in my opinion, one of the most interesting, but at the same time, it is the most ambivalent for me. The scent starts strong and intense with a mix of pineapple and a sweet honey note. This is not a quiet "Hello," but a loud "Here I am, Deal With it." The slightly animalistic note right from the start suits it very well and prevents it from slipping into the edible territory and overwhelming you with honey. The pineapple fades relatively quickly, replaced by a more floral, deeper sweetness. Here it gets really "filthy" and lives up to its name. The whole thing somehow makes me think of warm, slightly sweaty skin after a sunbath. I think to myself, "Okay, let's see where this leads us. Pushing the boundaries, but let's go with it." They don't always have to be these "pretty" scents. In the era of all those super-clean fragrances, this is a nice change." If it ended here, I would probably give the scent a solid 8/10. What really bothers me, however, is the further development. For me, a "sticky" and almost piercing sweetness increasingly comes to the forefront until the drydown, which completely ruins the scent for me and makes it personally unbearable. I suspect the rum. But I am also very sensitive to boozy notes and often don't like them. It could well be that others don't perceive it that way. Overall, it's an intriguing scent, but in the end, for me personally, a "sticky" musk remains in the nose rather than a "filthy" musk.

There are fragrances that enter through the front door - freshly shaved, neatly dressed, ready for small talk. And then there is this one. It comes in through the back door, throws its jacket in the corner, and makes itself comfortable on my sofa without asking. Filthy Musk imposes its direct physicality on me. It smells like... human. But not like shower gel human. More like "I've been out all day and now I'm sitting next to you, deal with it!" But before I want to make my escape, something wonderful happens: beneath the roughness of the first impression of the wild beast lies something surprisingly tender. Creamy layers of musk, a soft cotton shirt. A hint of leather, a suggestion of unmade beds, and perhaps a shadow of powder that charmingly envelops the whole thing. As it develops, it becomes less "filthy" and more "musk". The dirt remains, yes, but it transforms - from street grime to patina, from chaos to character. You can smell a certain degree of life here, not just fragrance. And while I perceive all of this, I quietly smile to myself. Others hope that I smell like fresh cotton in the sun. However, Filthy Musk, worn by me, serves them an honest, raw, and direct opinion. Rarely have I been glad not to have to ask for others' opinions, but instead to revel in glances. The moral??! This is not a fragrance for the mother-in-law, and that is its greatest charm. Whoever wears it needs no absolution, but only the calm to endure the untidy in the scent - and perhaps even discover the truly human within it.

The brand was initially unknown to me, but a test in the store changed everything. At home, I smelled the sample again and was thrilled: A fascinating winter fragrance! The longevity is impressive - even after a week, my sweater still smells. About the scent: No pineapple, but it doesn’t need it. It radiates warmth, reminiscent of roasted almonds with caramel, honey, and a nutty note. Despite my reservations about gourmand fragrances, this one has won me over. Sweet tonka bean, creamy musk, jasmine, and a gentle vanilla blend into a harmonious, well-thought-out composition. A unique, rounded scent - absolutely recommended for winter!

Originally reviewed on February 28, 2012: I bought this one completely, utterly, totally blind. I did not have a smart phone on which to confer with Fragrantica when I bought this. My criteria for bringing this home were (a.) it had a tropical name, thus, it must be a tropical scent and (b.) it was an Estee Lauder fragrance. I’ll buy a fragrance blindly so long as it alludes to being tropical. It isn’t really a very good litmus test but alas, I still employ it. Bali Dream is a satisfying tropical fragrance but its tropical nature isn’t immediately apparent upon first spray. It starts out syrupy sweet and gingery. Nice but not exactly the kind of tropical I had in mind. That was my second mistake (the first being blind-buying scents based on the word ‘tropical’)—there are more tropical environments besides the obvious coconuts-and-fruit-salad ones I had envisioned. [Redacted online user] once mentioned a trip to Bali and the scents of the land itself, not the beaches. Once I read that I realized this was a uniquely exotic trip to Bali, not a seaside seat on a generic tropical beach. Thanks to [redacted online user] I had a new appreciation for this scent. The syrupy sweet ginger quickly gives way to a fizzy-with-a-kick ginger ale that is refreshing and cool. About a half hour later the scent of orchid unfolds and stays consistently lovely for the entire ride. Anyone smitten with BBW’s Enchanted Orchid will fall in love with this fragrance. The sillage tastefully trails with medium strength and the fragrance last for quite a long time, staying even post-shower. I love most Estee Lauder creations, this one being no exception, but this one is different from the average EL creation. This one seems to be more carefree and untraditional, like Beyond Paradise’s eccentric little sister. It is completely enjoyable! It's October 10, 2023 and I have a better grasp of the meaning of the word 'tropical': Yes, I've since learned that 'tropical' doesn't always mean something coconutty and gourmand and 'holiday' is another word for 'vacation' (forgive me, I'm an American). Bali Dream was an education for me. There were elements of other familiar Estee Lauder perfumes—namely Sensuous Nude and Beyond Paradíse , something sweet, woody, and floral—thrown in the mix. In the end, it was too sweet. I think I also had "Mambo (Eau de Parfum) | Curve / Liz Claiborne", which was a tamer, drier ginger; I preferred the less saccharine ginger root of "Mambo (Eau de Parfum) | Curve / Liz Claiborne" to the ginger chews of Bali Dream . This had unmistakable Estee Lauder DNA but it wasn't enough for me to keep it.

It's all about the dry down with this fragrance! In the first 3 hours is just some pastry smell But then comes the magic - must be the patchouli and the musk in the base. They last for a very long time on my skin, even on the next morning I can feel their strong and divine presence... Tranquil Mystery . All in all is very charming and sensual fragrance. Like an invisible smile in the night.

It is a Nice Scent, Woody, Spicy and Unique. It is 70% similar to Tom Ford Black Orchid in dry down but Tom Ford has High Quality Composition If I compare it with Black Orchid, I must tell that Obsession Night launched in 2005 one year before Tom Ford Black Orchid. I bought it blind-buy after reading positive comments with reasonable price. It opens up with fresh spicy , fruity , herbal and spices notes in the background then dry down is powdery vanilla, Patchouli and Woody. Longevity is Average. I really enjoy it when the weather is cold. Thumbs Up. Rating : 7.5 / 10

This one was "Ultra Male" (by JPG) before "Ultra Male". Obsession Night starts off with a good amount of pear. This is accompanied by a bit of cardamom, a pleasantly powdery addition to its character! The background consists of vanilla and vetiver, powdery-sweet and cooling. Sometimes patchouli comes through, giving this fragrance a bitter, almost dirty note. There's hardly a trace of leather, which isn't so bad: the scent is already decent. The projection is acceptable, just like the longevity: the powdery cold base can still be detected after 8 hours. The bottle I tested has been around for a few years. Still, it doesn't seem as old and dusty as its downgraded clone Ultra Male. The few extra notes hardly make a difference; one can confidently prefer this one over the newer version.

CK Obsession Night was my first more expensive perfume back then and thus contributed to my collection and passion for fragrances. I just rediscovered it by chance and bought it immediately. Unfortunately, it's not available everywhere anymore. But it's also not too expensive anymore. Price 25 euros for 125ml is an absolutely good price for an EDT of this class. Of course, every scent is a matter of taste, but I just find the fragrance great! The scent is fruity, vanillic, and leathery, perfectly balanced like a poem. The sillage is quite strong. The longevity for me is a good 8 hours. I wear many EDTs in rotation, but CK Obsession Night is one that I almost always get complimented on as a wonderful scent. Warm, good fragrance at a good price for the modern gentleman. Unfortunately, it's no longer in production, thus a glowing star. Such a shame!

And once again, an example of how a well-known name has been used to attract customers. Whether the result is successful is something everyone must decide for themselves. Please forgive me, but this fragrance does not do justice to its namesake at all. It evokes all sorts of associations, but obsession is definitely not one of them. Therefore, I will not compare the two fragrances. To me, this scent feels like a country boy going dancing for the first time with his older siblings, who dedicates himself to his appearance intensely but also awkwardly. He showers extensively with something fruity, spreads half a tube of spicy hair gel in his damp hair to achieve a "cool" look. Now the teen faces the question of what to wear. The solution is quickly found. Today, he will wear the new jeans and the T-shirt from Kik, and to look older, he grabs his oldest brother's old leather jacket. While it does emit that overwhelmingly cheap leather scent, who cares, as long as he looks cool. Satisfied, he looks in the mirror and wonders if something is missing? Yes, the deodorant, because anyone who dances also sweats accordingly. So he quickly applies a generous amount of sweet Axe, liberally spread over his still not-so-masculine body, and off he goes to the village disco. But only until 11:00 PM, because he can't stay out later even on a Saturday... Even after multiple tests, this fragrance always conjures the same image in my mind. Teen in village disco. ONpH starts off unmotivatedly fruity, with a hint of stale spice, the leather note is overwhelmingly bitter, and in my opinion, the dry-down lacks any refinement. Sorry, but this one is a no-go for me!

Obsession, at least the original version, I find fantastic. A highly erotic scent that, however, takes its time to unleash the full power it holds. The name was program: OBSESSION!! Unfortunately, the obsession has now been exorcised by the terrible exorcist Dr. Reformulus. Instead of black silk, there’s scratchy cotton. Naturally colored, of course. Insanely erotic!

At first, a lemony alcohol note hits me, but once that evaporates, it becomes lovely - soft, fruity (pear fits in) and spicy-warm. The cardamom is truly dominant, and after a minute, some bananas at different stages of ripeness join the pear. Vetiver also leaves the first scent trail, and vanilla wraps everything in a soft veil.

In my impression, you cannot compare "Obsession Night" with the classic "Obsession for men" - they are simply two completely different fragrances! They only share their name, which (rightly) indicates an intense sensuality, but in both cases, it is interpreted in completely opposite ways.

I got this scent together with the "regular" Obsession for Men. This one is also very pleasant, not at all overpowering, and is particularly good for evening occasions. Unfortunately, it is a bit weak, almost a bit TOO weak compared to "Obsession"... For anyone who likes Obsession, OBSESSION NIGHT is definitely worth a try!

Phew! If this were a blind test, I would say someone is trying to poorly counterfeit the real, classic "Obsession Men" with the cheapest ingredients and simplest methods. The underlying sage note that I perceive after about 5-10 minutes gives me cause for this. It stems from the true DNA of the original. But otherwise? The opening is to be avoided.

If I hadn't recently smelled crushed bamboo leaves, I would have wanted to give "KenzoKi Bamboo Leaf" only 10% because you can't give 0, then it is considered unrated. I smelled the crushed leaves of the evergreen bamboo because I wanted to know if bamboo green smells like bamboo wood. A very expensive perfume brand smelled like bamboo wood in all the samples I had available for testing, a scent I can't stand. The bamboo leaves, on the other hand, smelled of almost nothing, just slightly green, much less than grass. But that doesn't mean much; bamboo belongs to the grasses, and there are countless varieties. Our native reed is also a type of bamboo (not the bulrush). The perfume "Bamboo Leaf" therefore smells of almost nothing, a little green, a little citrusy, somewhat resinous, not a trace of sweetness, yet it breathes out a hint of flowers. Tulips have such a scent when they smell at all. And also a little of the bamboo shoots that you buy in a can; bamboo shoots harvested as the roots of a bamboo species. These smell and taste slightly bitter and a bit like almonds, but only hinted at. This bamboo shoot note develops increasingly and makes "Bamboo Leaf" surprisingly long-lasting. The sillage, however, remains extremely subtle. I was about to give it only 20%. But wait, that's not fair, I decided. "Bamboo Leaf" has been on the market for 7 years, so there are people who particularly love such a delicate and unobtrusive scent. They want exactly that. And for that, it is a very fine and skillfully composed fragrance with a very delicate almond note. It's just a pity that Ambroxan keeps pushing its way in, which makes "Bamboo Leaf" synthetic at intervals. A scent for spring, for hot summer days. But only for those who want to be lightly scented. I would classify it as unisex.

Sampling Borntostandout Sin & Plesaure, a sweet, spicy, floral caramel/leather blend that is comparably provocative to its name. It’s smooth, inviting, sensual, quite interesting even though I feel like it falls short of excellence. The full note list mostly rings true: white flowers, ylang ylang, caramel, almond, vanilla, oud, leather, patchouli, rum, white musks, oakmoss, sandalwood. The caramel/almond/vanilla grouping in contrast to oud/leather is the biggest component of its narrative. It’s mostly-gourmand that overall works quite well and I could easily see this being a go-to for many for nighttime or cold weather. As with the rest of the line, this is EDP concentration and priced at $210 for 50ml, sold in the US at boutiques like Ministry of Scent. It performs quite well, also. 7 out of 10

One of the more palatable perfumes I’ve smelled from BORNTOSTANDOUT. Initial spray impressions reminded me of TF Black Orchid for some reason. It starts off with a synthetic cherry/almond extract scent and some noticeable Oud and a hint of ylang ylang. The rum and vanilla is through the whole wear.
