Here too, with "Free Coco | Borntostandout," the combination of coconut and macadamia was a bold choice, and I must say, based on the notes, I probably wouldn't have picked up the fragrance, but somehow the allure was there :) - In the opening, you quickly get the coconut vibes and the nutty character of the macadamia. The first seconds were not challenging for me, but simply surprising. I didn't expect this combination to be so impactful, but for the first few minutes, it effectively delivers a good dose of both, sweet-spicy-tropical, very special. The pear is subtly in the background, less noticeable. - As time goes on, this initial almost spicy "nutty" quality diminishes, the fragrance balances out a bit, both coconut and macadamia find equilibrium, and from here on, the scent becomes really pleasant for the surroundings and less challenging. A creamy vanilla then joins in during the drydown. This nutty character lingers the longest on the skin along with the vanilla, while the coconut fades over time, but is still subtly perceptible. - H/S: I don't understand the reviews, especially regarding performance. After a week of continuous testing, I can confirm that the scent easily lasts for 6 hours. I just tested it again yesterday, sprayed at 7 PM, and after midnight, the fragrance was still well noticeable on my skin. The sillage and projection are stronger in the first approximately 30 minutes, after which the scent becomes pleasantly present in the air, neither "loud" nor too "quiet," more skin-close, yes, but actually well noticeable when standing next to the person. It's not a scent that shouts, but its special character makes it stand out. PS: I usually do between 6-8 sprays for such fragrances, based on this, my rating. In summary: Always read the comments and reviews with nuance, both good and bad, because from my perspective, a few milliliters and a single test wear are not enough to form a solid opinion, especially since individual perception can vary greatly from day to day. Yep, the fragrance is creative, and yep, BTSO has its character, but I absolutely do not perceive the scent as "bad" as it is portrayed here. You can't expect a "finely tuned Roja" from BTSO, although you can't really expect that from Roja anymore either. BTSO fragrances are often not "masterpieces" in the sense that we sometimes imagine/wish, but they are true to the brand. With that said; I hope this helps you and enjoy the weekend.

Brasil Dream by Estée Lauder is a really wonderful, spicy dream of a fragrance! It's smooth and spicy with cinnamon, paprika, pepper and nutmeg, patchouli and smooth leather... and it smells gorgeous! Cardamom, coriander, spices, sweet cinnamon & leather are the perfect combo between sweet, smooth & spicy. I really like this one a lot! I imagine a really well dressed, sexy seductive man wearing this one. It smells a LOT more expensive than it is (and unfortunately discontinued as well). As other people have said before, this is like a tropical version of Gucci pour Homme. I can totally see that. Ultimately, this fragrance is what is says, a dream... and just like a dream, it's now gone. If you can find this I highly suggest it for men. You will really find something special. Fantastic exotic, tropical, spicy, manly fragrance! I love and respect the house of Estée Lauder, and this is one of the reasons why.

A fragrance that has been discontinued & is now very hard to find - with this statement, I always feel an undeniable urge to strike, be it on eBay, somewhere abroad, or here on Parfumo. This risk & the higher price than during its official run have been worth it for several fragrances, and few have been disappointments. From Relax to Envy or Yohji Homme - there have been a few rare gems among them. Surely, almost everyone here knows this feeling. "Brasil Dream for Men" is one such case, it sat on my wish list for a whole 5 years without really standing out or enticing me with an acceptable price. However, I was in the mood for a blind buy of such an OOP fragrance (Out of Print), so I managed to snag 50ml on eBay for an acceptable €45. A spicy, unusual summer scent just sounded too tempting. "Brasil Dream" is, especially given its name & its former distribution exclusively at airports, not really a vacation & summer scent at first glance. It neither feels sunny nor Brazilian, making it hardly surprising that it found few loyal fans. However, upon closer inspection, it offers a rather unique, interesting spice combination that is hard to categorize - which is both an advantage & a disadvantage. So first, forget about Copa Cabana & the beach, think more of rainy leisure/summer days - like this July. Nutmeg plays a significant role in this Brazilian dream; I imagine an older LeRoy Sane type as the perfect wearer. It can best be described as a mix of Kenzo's Jungle Homme, Hermessence Paprika & Gucci PHI, only in an extremely muted, subtle & light way, making it even harder to describe. Like a spicy cocktail, but completely without sugar & sweetness. In my opinion, a bit more of that cocktail feeling would have made it not only younger but also better. Nowadays, it would surely be unthinkable to release such a fragrance, especially with summery intentions. While initially spices from coriander to cumin color the scent brown, a hint of cinnamon lightens it up, making it at least a bit brighter & sweeter. However, it's so fleeting that one could almost overlook this underlying tone. Especially when the leathery base shines through early on & points fully back towards evening, masculinity & darkness - not a scent for young surfer boys, but rather for their older, mature father at the beach, who cheers them on with rapt attention & still knows how to score with ladies of all kinds! Tanned leathery skin, gray chest hair, a charming macho smile - tough exterior, soft core. Bottle: handy, fine, chic. Sillage: very calm spices that almost seem summery because of it. Longevity: the scent can be well enjoyed for 5 hours. Conclusion: Summer & Brazil in a different way - a spicy-brown, hard-to-categorize fragrance that you wouldn't expect. All the more delightful is the surprise & this little rarity!

First of all, super herbal, I'm not used to that and was really startled, then the scent develops, becoming sweet, warm, creamy - vanilla and tonka come to the forefront. Around me, a warm sweet cloud, almost like a second skin - so actually the definition of a clean scent for me. Borntostandout mentions something about champagne, I don't read that here in parfumo, I also didn't quite pick that up. Longevity: after 5 hours I get a vanilla-floral scent, almost a bit like ylang ylang - or is it the wood? - the scent is still super present and I can perceive it. And even 8 hours later, I'm sitting in my little clean vanilla-floral-woody cloud - not intrusive - completely clean - and still there.

I was not around for the 80s, but from what I've seen in films and TV, there was this one archetype known simply as The Businesswoman. I don't think it's ever clear what her job was, other than the nebulous Business, but she had giant hair and giant shoulderpads and the aggression to back it up. Invariably, this would all change when the Right Man came along, but let's try to ignore that for now and focus on the Businesswoman as she is. This is a scent for her. It's soft and floral, made-up with dusky pink eyeshadow and rosy lipgloss, but with an iron core beneath. For once, I find this oakmoss perfectly balanced. Often I think chypres, particularly floral ones, end up either too floral (merely nodding in the direction of moss without daring to commit to it) or too mossy (smelling more like a bottle of gin than a perfume), but this walks the line between both of them. Like many floral perfumes of the era, it's carefully noncomittal about its florality— I do perceive the damascones that I associate with roses, but I would be hard-pressed to call it a rose perfume. Anyway, I find it genuinely impressive the way it can conjure up memories of an era that I didn't even exist for. This is honestly fun to wear.

This is something which should be preserved forever as an example of pure joy and beauty. An iconic fragrance. I am male, but I have huge respect for this beautiful piece of art. I my self have worn Shalimar in Eau de Cologne concentration, and I actually can't stop myself wearing something so beautiful and timeless as this. It wasn't such a big step for me as I used to love the floral aldehyde feel of "Tabac" by Maurer & Wirtz. Except the later had a prominent tobacco vibe. The Eau de Cologne is vintage and generally much stronger than the modern formulation. That being said, the floral aspects of it are to die for, and the projection & sillage are astounding. In short, I just want to say... I think every woman should smell like this at least once in her life. Please, enough with the countless generic teen florals etc. When you get tired of them, and want men to treat you like the lady that you are, you can't make a better statement than this. Timeless.

In front of me is a 100ml splash bottle of Chanel N°5. In the old EdC version. Still three-quarters full, hardly darkened. Nevertheless, at least 25 years old, maybe even 30 or 40 years old. The label has already yellowed, and the formerly rectangular edges are partly rounded off. An aging-related varnish smell that affects the top note dissipates after about 20 minutes and allows - as if through a transparent curtain - a glimpse of the heart and base notes. I know and appreciate the N°5 perfume and the current EdT. In comparison, I would describe the three versions with these images: The perfume shows the fully ripe fresh bouquet of flowers, which reaches its maximum, still sun-warm fragrance intensity with jasmine, lily of the valley, rose, and violet root. The EdT mixes in noticeably more robust tones of woody sandalwood and earthy vetiver to the now several days old bouquet of flowers - the bouquet is still fresh, but shows a slightly more autumnal character. It has not necessarily lost its freshness, but the brightness of the colors is somewhat muted. The opulence of the flowers recedes to the extent that the green-brown components of amber, sandalwood, and vetiver gain more presence. With the EdC, a light gray veil has settled over the whole picture. The colors are not only muted in their brightness but also broken. The bright red has turned into a dark velvet red, white has become beige, and green has turned into olive green. The scent still clearly reminds of jasmine, lily of the valley, rose, and violet root, but in a version that is already dried and wilted. Earthy components like patchouli and musk dominate the scent progression much earlier and more equally in the picture. A wonderful, slightly morbid scent that is probably rarely preserved in its original splendor today. Nevertheless, still desirable - even if a vintage EdT likely holds greater chances of offering an unrestricted view of the original.

Chanel N°5 has always been for me the Eau de Toilette version of my grandmother. I found it flowery and old-fashioned as a child in the 70s. During my perfume workshop at 4160Tuesdays, I had the opportunity to explore the Vintage Vault. And there we were able to discover the Eau de Cologne version. That was a real enlightenment. Not flowery and old-fashioned at all! That’s how the legendary number 5 should be: The bottle was from the late 40s, the scent perfectly preserved, Mademoiselle Chanel's spirit was among us. She probably spoke to me too, but I was so intoxicated that I can't remember exactly :) Barely back from London, I organized 2 bottles, you never know... The EdC is significantly less flowery than the EdT, less sweet but drier, more aldehydic. More Roaring 20s than demure 50s. More jersey dress than Dior corset. And thus resolutely modern, timeless, and elegant. Subsequently, for comparison purposes, I also had to get the Vintage Extrait version, purely for scientific comparison, of course... The Extrait is, of course, also a dream, but closer to the body. The EdC has more sillage, shoulder pads in a way. Otherwise, they are very similar, as they are not as flowery as the EdT. Overall, the wearer - or the wearer - should be close to aldehydes and not allergic to white flowers, as a floral base cannot be denied, although it is processed in a modern way. One of my Holy Grails, to return to the diction of the present and end the trance state!

Dear Angelliese has allowed me to try the long-discontinued EdC of my signature scent. I sincerely thank you. To put it simply: The EdC also convinces me completely and confirms Chanel's No 5 as my signature scent, even though I wear it less frequently due to impending nose blindness. Like the vintage EdT and the perfume, the EdC is overall more robust than the modern versions of No 5. The former seem somehow denser "woven," the fragrance notes blend together more quickly. Of course, there is a progression: aldehydic-soapy-floral-warm-slightly spicy. However, it unfolds more quickly, providing more of an overall impression. (See my comparison comment on the EdP). New for me with the EdC is an impression of licorice after about 1 hour. Really just an impression that comes and goes, but recognizable to me. It could be the addition of violet root... And I was surprised by the mention of patchouli in the above fragrance pyramid. I initially wanted to dismiss it with a shake of my head, as it clearly lacks that chocolaty, dark, earthy note. But then I recalled Lehmann's "Singapore Patchouly," which is also a rather light, slightly floral patchouli, and thought, it could be. Perhaps the patchouli used in those times (20s, 30s) was lighter, more floral? And last but not least, a rather green finish is new to me with the EdC. I perceive vetiver most clearly at the end; it may be that oakmoss supports this. I cannot recognize musk and civet, both of which are also not listed in the other versions, although I must admit I have no idea what civet smells like. I was impressed by the longevity of the EdC. With up to 7 hours, it is comparable to a modern EdT. Conclusion: Apart from the completely new No 5 versions (Première and L'Eau), I always feel comfortable with No 5.

Hello everyone, Today's review is perhaps one of the most sentimental for me and is truly filled with emotions, as I want to talk about a fragrance that one person always (and only this one!) wore... and has been gone for almost 20 years..., I want to discuss the signature scent of my great-grandmother, N°5 Eau de Cologne . According to my grandfather, my great-grandmother wore it since roughly 1970, and since she was professionally in Paris several times a year, she bought nearly 5 bottles of the fragrance every year (no joke!). Surely, one might wonder why one needs so much? And yes, I understand this..., my probable "fragrance obsession" I inherited from her, but she did things I have never done until now... She would spray clothing (not white) with it, hang them in the closet (tops + pants), and items she rarely wore, like special blazers or evening dresses, would get a refresh of N°5 Eau de Cologne after xx weeks... The entire apartment, the furniture, the cushions, the sofa, everything smelled of it, and that’s why this fragrance will always be deeply embedded in me... Recently, thanks to a lovely lady here from the souk, I had the chance to get a small sample, because it actually hasn’t been available (in that concentration since 1990)...! And when the day came and it arrived, I immediately went to the AZ, grabbed a fragrance strip and go.... sprayed it on... and what happened... I cried like a baby.... The scent instantly catapulted me back to her living room, to my childhood -_- ...., yet I am grateful for this experience, because today I perceive it differently than back then and perhaps I will understand more why she cherished the fragrance so much... (And if anyone has a remaining old EDC bottle - please get in touch!) The fragrance: How should I aptly describe the masterpiece... : Synthetic (due to aldehydes, of course), floral, classic, creamy, clean, and typically Chanel. In my personal opinion, almost every DD from Chanel builds upon this truly classic DD. Guerlain and Xerjoff (in the Stonelabel series) work with it almost 1:1 (small examples of fragrance notes include rose, iris, sandalwood, musk, amber, vanilla, and patchouli). I also believe that soon there would be no fragrances from the house like, for example, Coromandel Eau de Toilette , because it is indeed the foundation for that. Chanel's masterpiece: Chanel has generally created something with the No.5 line (thanks to COCO) that has shaped the fragrance industry, and if the "legend" is to be believed, with the 5 fragrance strips, where the perfumer back then said 1 - 4 were great, but COCO took number 5 on principle, hence the name..., then I am not sure if the hobby we have would exist in this form... The fragrance was and is the greatest stroke of genius that CHANEL has ever released, and in my opinion, no fragrance will ever sell like it (it is almost 102 years old!)... Personal opinion: Due to my history, I cannot make a perfect statement, but I can make this one without bias. If a fragrance (now in a different concentration than back then from EDC to EDP) has existed for over 100 years (!), then it is worth testing. In my eyes, alongside Shalimar Extrait , it is one of the (2) fragrances that one must have tested! Because then, in my opinion, one will truly understand + possibly appreciate more what people created back then... Thank you for your time and thank you, my beloved great-grandmother (Dora)... If I truly weren't convinced, I wouldn't recommend it to you! And now, have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______

Thoughts on August 8, 2023: I have a "backup bottle" of Tuscany per Donna (2015) from 2020. I had to open it up to see how different it was from the older reproductions of Tuscany per Donna (2015) from Estee Lauder, and further back, to the original Tuscany per Donna Eau de Parfum . It's watered down, which I fully expected. What was en vogue and au courant in 1993 is now dated; loud spices and ostentatious sandalwood need to be muted for today's tastes. It's still a throwback scent, muted as it is. I didn't know Samsara Eau de Parfum existed in 1993. Tuscany per Donna Eau de Parfum was readily available in every American suburban mall and was Samsara Eau de Parfum 's loud gum chewing sister. Both were strikingly gorgeous but there was a slightly trashier edge and accessibility to Tuscany per Donna Eau de Parfum that made her fun and possibly more suitable for a seventeen-year-old bookish girl. I waxed poetic about my prom night and this scent in my original review of Aramis's version. I still get nostalgic when I smell it. I still have a late 1990s bottle in my possession for reference. Given my history and nostalgia with Tuscany per Donna Eau de Parfum I think I'd be within my rights to hate this reformulation. I don't hate it, though. It's not what I had back in 1993 but I'm not that bookish seventeen year old. And I'm okay with all of it. It has it's basic structure—it's more or less the same scent—but with a gossamer haze. I've tried reformulations of other nostalgic fragrances that have been neutered and hacked beyond recognition. If a gossamer haze is all Tuscany per Donna (2015) got in the end, I'm okay with that, too. So, proceed and remember, my thoughts and feelings haven't really changed. Just sprinkle the word 'gossamer' to my original review. Original review from July 29, 2012: I cannot help but tie this fragrance to nostalgia; I wore this fragrance to my senior prom. Nostalgia aside, this is actually a really enjoyable hearty fragrance. Tresor may have popularized the spicy pitted-fruit floriental trend of the 1990s but Tuscany Per Donna perfected that trend. TPD smells like the 1990s but it encapsulates the best of what the decade had to offer in a bottle. TPD is distinctive, redolent with spice-laden stone fruit preserves. There are no spices listed but it smells spiced—I think the spiciness can be attributed to the carnation (I’m not a fan of carnation but it is so irresistible here). (An aside from 2023: I LOVE CARNATIONS! I was still learning what I liked and did not like in 2012, and I thought I didn't like carnations. I have since learned I have a love-hate relationship with aldehydes, which were often used with carnation perfumes. The more you know, right?) It does not take long for the vanilla, amber, and warm woods to imitate the scent of bakery goods—those fruit-filled butter cookies come to mind. It’s blissful! This decadent scent will stick around from first spray to next shower. The sillage and projection are typical of most 1990s scents: strong and sturdy. I have an aged bottle—my second one—from the late-1990s that has only gotten richer with proper storage and time. I liked it when I was seventeen but I love it now that I am old enough (read: evolved) to appreciate all its phases. I love TPD for its unabashed personality and its ability to be gourmand at heart without being sickly saccharine.

The fragrance arrived yesterday and I could hardly wait, as Black Karak embodies the idea of Karak tea combined with the "provocatively bold" philosophy of the house BTSO. Was the scent a misfire? Absolutely not, I'm increasingly warming up to the Extrait series of the house, as they are simply loud, bold, and provocative, exactly what one wants and needs from time to time. - In the opening, the fragrance starts with an explosive presence; yes, the Karak tea/chai beautifully seeps through in the first minutes with a good dose of cardamom. Yes, spicy, special, and above all radically strong. An almost medicinally invigorating sharpness, dense and somehow unrefined, rough, but beautiful - beautiful for me at least. An opening that refuses to be pleasing. - After that, the fragrance becomes a bit tamer, saffron comes through, a certain woody vein shimmers through, while the scent doesn’t really become lighter but remains dark and mysterious. At the same time, a leatheriness emerges, increasingly building up, with a small portion of unsweetened coffee in the background, merging together with the oud into a spicy-woody base. Rustic, but successful. This black tea note is more noticeable in the drydown, meaning you transition from a "creamier" Karak chai towards a spicy, dark tea. - Sillage is bombastic, you can tell right from the spray that this fragrance needs a wearer who can carry it. An absolute statement scent. Projection is, of course, beast mode; when the bottles from BTSO are red, you know it’s going to be a showstopper. Would I say it’s a masterpiece? No, absolutely not folks, but that’s not the philosophy of BTSO, especially with the Extrait line; it’s about courage, creativity, and individuality. From my perspective, that’s exactly what this fragrance delivers.

I think Dazzling Silver is successful for the same reason that No 5 is. They both play with the notion of a flower or a bouquet of flowers using floral references, then add something else entirely. For No 5, these references are famously from actual botanicals, ie. Chanel’s own rose & jasmine harvests. For DS, I image the floral references are more chemically derived. To this floral understructure, they both then add heavy doses of aromachemicals that are recognizable more for their specific nose-tones or qualities rather than for their floral reference. No 5’s famous aldehydes, DS’s helional. In both cases, floral is the start, not the goal.

I had been warned. But I generally don’t listen to others. My older Coromandel model (EdT), which I had loved for years but used sparingly, as I have encountered little patch tolerance in my surroundings (and I’m not a fan of an "excess" of earthiness myself), was to be complemented. By the king class, the Extrait. So I expected: The best of patch for cowards and finest chocolatier craftsmanship. The chocolate, the chocooolate! And then from Chanel! (If you can’t afford anything else from this company, at least the chocolate has to be Chanel-like..) But it turned out differently. Even beforehand, I was told that the Extrait shouldn’t be so gourmand, but still heavenly. That didn’t exactly deter me. Then - the first encounter! Yes, clear signs of unsweetened, greenish orange, which don’t stay with me for long. Too bad, really, because it’s beautiful. Slowly, my fear opponent approaches. It starts to become earthy and slightly spicy. Where is the big Lindor ball when you need it? I perceive smokiness, very mild sweetness, little wood. I can’t identify any flowers. After a time of constant sniffing, the sweet, spicy smoky notes become more noticeable, forming a very gentle, oriental connection with the patch. The fear opponent has been tamed, thank goodness. Now a chocolate note also comes in - equally welcome. And yes, it’s not "mass-produced chocolate," but high-end, high cocoa content, noble bitter. Powdery instead of creamy. In combination with the tamed, soft patch, it’s a formidable thing. So I can only agree that Coromandel Extrait, besides the general attributes of a pure perfume (expensive, chic outfit, long-lasting), has one special feature: Unlike an earlier chocolate advertisement, it’s not "A lot of milk, little cocoa!" but "A lot of cocoa, soft patch!" I’m really glad about that! And what about you?

To all readers of this community who appreciate short and concise texts, I would like to recommend at the outset to scroll directly to the second half of this comment - this will be a bit longer. Coromandel has never been a fragrance that could be dealt with in just a few sentences, and the Extrait of this milestone also deserves a more detailed exploration (not least due to its horrendous price). Coromandel has fascinated me from the very beginning, regardless of the fragrance concentration. For me, it is by far the most fatalistic perfume I have ever encountered. Enthusiasm or disgust, war or peace, victory or defeat - Coromandel is the exact opposite of a pleasing scent. No compromises, just clear edges. Praised or cursed by those around me, but never regarded with indifference. Wonderful! Definitely not a fragrance for all occasions, but for me, it is absolutely mood-dependent. On some days, I cannot stand Coromandel; on others, it is (as they say nowadays) indispensable. When I saw a few days ago, while casually reading, that Chanel had released a brand new Coromandel Extrait, my attention was immediately piqued. I read the statement from Aika1547 - and I could almost hear the bang as the trap snapped shut… less patchouli! Not so earthy! A lot of vanilla? Thank you, bring it on. Immediately. Within 24 hours, I placed my order in Chanel's online boutique, a capitulation of the purest kind and unparalleled decadence. Never before have I bought so little perfume for so much money, never before have I dared a blind purchase in this price range. No matter - addiction is addiction, and Coromandel is, after all, Coromandel, right? Since most readers of this detail page are probably interested in how the Extrait resembles or differs from its predecessors, I would like to compare the EdT and the EdP with the freshly launched Extrait and attempt a sort of summary overview. Eau de Toilette (2007): The first Coromandel I got to know. The citrus opening is extraordinary - not musty or stale, but truly high perfumery of the old school and absolutely classic. Dominating in the heart note, alongside orris root, is the massive patchouli accord, whose sour-earthy intensity excites some and repels others. I found it increasingly bothersome with each test - that smell of damp, musty earth piles that seemed to be piling up next to me overshadowed most other components and completely ruined the scent for me. The unique, beautiful base note could no longer help, that perfect golden veil of dry vanilla, musk, and incense… I parted with the decant and ventured after some time to the Eau de Parfum (2016): The same classic citrus opening, the almost identical scent progression. But here, patchouli is significantly reduced; the earth piles have been swept away and removed. What remains is a patchouli note that one can certainly live with, even if one usually does not like patchouli. The EdP feels softer, more mature compared to the EdT, no longer so edgy. Like a spirit that only unfolds its perfect aroma after longer aging. Unfortunately, the aging process seemed to come at the expense of longevity, which has diminished somewhat compared to the EdT. The base is again typically Coromandel - namely perfection. Accordingly, my expectations for the Extrait were high, where patchouli was supposed to recede even further into the background. While that is true, there are far more significant differences. Extrait (2019): The classic Coromandel opening, the citrus note, is gone. Simply and plainly reduced. According to the fragrance pyramid, citrus fruits are supposed to be present here, but I must agree with Aika1547 that the Extrait indeed starts immediately with the heart note. This unmistakably reveals the original Coromandel, here with dominant iris. Patchouli is only faintly perceptible; the earth piles have disappeared, leaving only a few dry crumbs. Dry vanilla and incense are noticeable much earlier compared to the EdT and EdP, and this also reveals the next clear difference from the predecessors: the Extrait has almost no scent progression. The way the scent starts is largely how it remains. The (less patchouli) heart note and the base merge early, with at least the base note remaining practically unchanged. The scent quickly becomes skin-close, but is still slightly perceptible in the room after an hour. After 4-5 hours, I have to practically search for it on my skin; this poor longevity was also confirmed by test subjects I asked for their opinion or nose: one only perceives the scent faintly after I had dabbed it on my skin several times 3 hours earlier. I find this longevity and sillage shockingly poor for an Extrait in this price range. There is no comparison to the EdT or EdP, which are still clearly perceptible in the afternoon after 2-3 sprays in the morning… The overnight test of the Extrait also showed: what was dabbed on in the evening was practically completely gone by the next morning. Conclusion: I expected a kind of Coromandel under the magnifying glass, a sparkling, radiant version with less patchouli that would allow other fragrance notes to shine. This hope has only been partially fulfilled. The Extrait does forgo most of the patchouli, but also the entire top note of its predecessors - and especially their longevity. Devoted Coromandel fans from the beginning may be horrified to ask where the other half of this great fragrance has gone… Coromandel has lost its edges in the Extrait, especially its complexity, which most fans love about the scent. Would I have bought the bottle if I had tested the Extrait beforehand? Probably not, solely due to the poor longevity. My favorite will thus remain the EdP. I must mention in this context, however, that I have a pronounced preference for so-called heavy hitters, and my assessment here naturally reflects only my personal opinion… I am very curious to see how other users will evaluate the Extrait here. Who will be disappointed: everyone who mourns the clear statement of the Eau de Toilette will likely find no comfort in the Extrait. The edginess that was so softened in the EdP has now completely disappeared here. Nevertheless, Coromandel Extrait will also find its lovers, and they will be numerous when reading the comments and statements about the EdT and EdP. Who will love it: all those who have hoped and prayed in recent years for a softer, more pleasing, gentler (quieter?) version of Coromandel, where patchouli is put in its place - there is good news and bad news. The good: Chanel has heard your prayers. This should be the Coromandel version you have been waiting for. The bad: 15ml for 225 euros - the fulfillment of some wishes comes at a high price; this fragrance is no exception :)

CHANEL COCO NOIR EXTRAIT Jacques Polge and Christopher Sheldrake 2014 (edp 2012) I took a risk based on some reviews and it was worth it. I was anticipating the darkness of Coco Noir and found it in “Extrait de Parfum”. Fell in love earlier with luminous edp because of other reasons though. When the name “Coco Noir” was given I think it was based on the Parfum concentration. It’s in overall darker than edp, it has a seductive femme fatale character while edp is more a ladylike, happy and pretty. Extrait is intense, all the notes are very deep, dense and it’s more complex. It’s somewhat glamorous with a richness of 80s and 90s perfumes. It’s extravagant compared to edp which is very charming for sure yet very bright and easy to wear. Coco Noir Extrait is for those intimate passionate moments and mysterious evenings when someone is coming close to your skin. It’s potent but I’m sure you don’t want to bath in that precious juice in tiny 15ml bottle to get more projection. What comes to the notes this is a strange perfume - it’s very difficult to separate them and that is the reason why I don’t even try to analyze them. You have to experience the scent yourself. “A voluptuous and enveloping ambery scent with a noble accord of Egyptian jasmine and May rose that adds depth and sensuality. The trail unfurls with magnetic notes of Indonesian patchouli and Venezuelan tonka bean, along with the more pronounced notes of bourbon vanilla and New Caledonian sandalwood.” Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

I'm disappointed with Coco Noir Extrait for more pleasant and harmonious its fragrance might be. In my opinion, considering that Coco Noir received a treatement of a main launch, not a flanker variation of another creaqtion, this is one of the needless Chanel launches of the last years.I had hopes that the extrait formulation would give the identity that the EDP wasn't able to, but i see that the brand hasn't put efforts on this sense. I'm passionate about the Chanel extraits for two reasons: a bigger richness in the floral aromas and more intensity and sofistication at the base, This is, from what i remember, one of the exceptions between the extraits and the only thing that i really see here as an advantage is cutting the excess of patchouli sweetness from the EDP. The extrait gives more emphasis to the flowers, but yet there is not a saturation or distinction on none of them. I don't see an intense jasmine, an outstanding rose (like the wonderful on of coco extrait) and if there is any narcissus here it's used in very minimal doses for the record only. The basenote accord of sandalwood has a tasty smell, but nothing out of this world, and it keeps itself inside of the musky vanilla sandalwood structure of Coco Noir. In performance aspect, this extrait almost work as an edp, it was a good projection on skin. This would be an adorable formula to the EDP, which is more 'get-at-able', but for an expensive and luxuous extrait, this is mediocre and disappointing altough it's wearable. I'll finish my decant of it without wanting at all to revisit it.

Hello everyone, today I would like to talk about a fragrance that truly deserves and must carry the term "masterpiece," it's "Coco Noir (Extrait de Parfum) | Chanel." I know the prices for the 15ml version of this extrait are really outrageous, and I find it very, very difficult to say that it is worth the price, BUT you have to experience it at least once. My wife and a few others (and my mother-in-law) are big FANS of the regular "Coco Noir (Eau de Parfum) | Chanel," but I always wished for a bit more from it, more in terms of performance, edges, and I saw sooooo much potential in it, almost that it could go further, and about 3 months ago I received a sample (here in the Souk) and it showed me what I hoped for + also suspected. The scent is, in short, exactly what I wrote BELOW in the statements. It is dark, mystical, captivating, incredibly high-quality, noble, made for THE appearance, very economical as it is very potent, so incredibly rounded and perfectly balanced. If you know and love the EDP but wish for more, then give this a try! I can hardly stop with the superlatives, even though it is hard for me - it is a FACT - PERIOD! One day this masterpiece will find its way into our home, this test has convinced us more than anything! And now have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______

After wearing Allure Sensuelle Eau de Parfum , Allure Sensuelle Parfum , Allure Parfum , and Allure Eau de Parfum , I allow myself to make a slightly more detailed comment. All four have a class that deserves a tip of the hat. Fresh, fruity, balanced sweet, cuddly, green, balsamic, and so well-balanced, deep, and full; so elegant; that's Chanel for you. Allure presents itself - according to my nose - as a good deal less earthy/herbaceous than Allure Sensuelle, which I find more pleasant. And the EdP is even more intense than the parfum. So the parfum would be my choice. It is softer and more endearing, rounder, more cuddly, and more pleasing. But perhaps others prefer the EdP precisely for that reason. I also see it not only on women who are advanced in years but also of middle age. Simply a masterpiece - one can't help but rave about it, even if one usually prefers something else.

Allure was described as such when it was launched in 1996. It made an immediate impact. However, it was not promoted by stars or highly paid models, but by modern, pretty, yet unknown women. As early as 1974, Chanel had introduced a fresh, clear, and vibrant scent with Cristalle. In 1996, Jaques Polge (and at that time, in my opinion, he was much more creative than today) aimed to create an elegant, floral, feminine fragrance that is both simple and sophisticated. Allure has also managed to be named one of the 100 legendary fragrances. A light mandarin note serves as the opening, which quickly transitions to a bouquet of jasmine, honeysuckle, water lilies, and other flowers that only grow in Grasse. A hidden iris adds a slightly distinct powderiness. A hint of green vetiver oil and sparingly used vanilla complete the composition. Allure was meant to be provocative, yet conservative, flirtatious but also morally correct. According to Coco Chanel's earlier statement, it was for a woman who felt like a woman but lived like a man. Even today, Allure is presented in the elegant glass bottle. I describe the pure perfume as vintage and do not know how many dilutions the current Allure has undergone.

I had a "madeleine-effect" when I tested this perfume on the mouillette and on my skin too: my head went to the smell of the old lipsticks of my mother and my grandma when I was a child. I can't understand which ingredient could smell like this: maybe the iris concrete? Anyway, I found this fragrance a little synthetic although not bad. I wasn't a fan of the classical Eternity, maybe I prefer this one in comparison, but we aren't very far from a perfumery masterpiece! Quite high price .

It’s always well-intentioned when acquaintances who know you like perfumes gift you a fragrance. What these kind people usually don’t realize is: There’s nothing more finicky than perfume enthusiasts who have already experienced everything. They would rather be pleased with a bar of pure soap than with a meaningless mainstream scent from the local drugstore. That’s how I felt recently when a nice colleague thanked me with a bottle of Eternity Intense for a favor. My first thought was: Thank goodness, only 30 ml. Especially since I still had the original Eternity in my nose, those white, artificial flowers that used to detach themselves from their wearers like free radicals 30 years ago and led a dreadful life of their own in the shopping streets of city centers. Back then, the fragrances by Sophia Grojsman, especially Trésor, Paris, and the aforementioned Eternity, had the unpleasant trait of immediately seizing air superiority with the first spray and leading a fine dust-like existence for hours. And now I had received this in an intensified form, horrendous. But before I passed on the spray bottle, curiosity won, and I tried it out. Whoa? What was that? No trashy plastic flowers from Mars, but rather a solid base of sweet and woody teen notes, over which the anonymous perfumer had laid a powdery iris. I was stunned. This actually hit my taste. A mainstream scent that I initially deemed dreadful turned out to be a wearable, even fine and elegant fragrance that pairs wonderfully with any polka-dotted afternoon dress with ruffles and lace or a simple, sea-blue suit. Whoever designed this fragrance ironically achieved exactly the opposite of the intrusive original. Eternity Intense smells almost like an apology, a sort of Eternity excuse: look here, we can also be refined. So, I kept the fragrance and wear it more often; I even received a compliment for it (which is very rare for me), from a German eco-saleswoman with orange dreadlocks in a natural food store: "Oh, dat is aber n jutes Paföng, wat Sie da ham." Fits perfectly. A slightly woody, slightly sweet, powdery iris scent that doesn’t offend any nose from the green eco-store to the elegant afternoon tea at the Reids Palace in Madeira. You can hardly ask for more from a daytime fragrance.

Yesterday, my friend and I both had a dentist appointment, and afterwards we both felt we deserved to treat ourselves. At first, we rummaged through the niche fragrances, but then we turned to the mainstream ones. A synchronous grab for Intense - and synchronous enthusiasm. The powdery, herb-sweet cloud delighted us immensely. Not mainstream at all - but also not pretentious. With Intense, you wear something noble, unique - without having to put on a grand gown. No, jeans and a T-shirt are nicely elevated. The powderiness of the iris receives some transparency and creaminess from the aquatic flowers. Very appealing. Osmanthus and rose are valuable and proud, but not arrogant. The vanilla is soft and sweet. There were exactly two bottles waiting - obviously for us. Just like we had snagged the last two "Baronesse" roses from the gardener. So Eternity Intense was just right for us "Baronesses".

Why this fragrance is called “Intense” is a mystery to me. I already get frustrated with all the EDTs, EDPs, L’Eaus, Intenses, Absolues, Sensuelles, Sports, Couchs, Summers, Winters….. and when we can’t think of anything else, we throw another “Rose” or some other floral version on the market… The cow just wants to be milked. But one would initially think that Intense is a stronger variant of the original. However, that is absolutely not the case here, and a completely new, different name would have been appropriate. The fact is, this Intense has absolutely NOTHING to do with the original (which I find far too herbaceous and floral). And it has NOTHING to do with the seemingly 100 Eternity flankers. This Intense should not even be called that because it is not intense at all! It is actually a delicate, soft, sweet, and floral powder scent, which I like because I enjoy powder fragrances. However, Eternity Intense remains rather close to the skin and lasts on me for about four hours, so far from Intense… Conclusion: If I didn’t already have so many - and also a bit prettier - powder scents, it would be a candidate for my collection despite the deceptive packaging. I wouldn’t buy it for myself, but I wouldn’t refuse it as a gift.

Bottega Veneta Eau de Parfum probably comes across as somewhat of an oddity in the world invaded by a plague of cloying pinkish compote waters. My guess is the younger crowd will wrinkle their noses after smelling a perfume like Bottega Veneta, which, to be honest, does not bother me at all. Despite not being groundbreaking or trend-setting, to me, Bottega Veneta EdP is a unique fragrant composition. I'm not going to attempt to describe its effect on me since I would be forced to resort to such cliched adjectives as "modern (with a classic twist)", "gentle", "sophisticated", "classy", "elegant", to name just a few. Bottega Veneta EdP IS all this and so much more. Even though it's been composed of run-of-the-mill notes, they're blended exquisitely. The scent starts off fresh and slightly spicy-citrusy. Then it moves to its floral-fruity heart (courtesy of jasmine, violet and plum), and signs off with oak moss and patchouli. The heart and base notes create a very pleasant rendition of leather, thanks to which on my skin, BV turns into a delicate and alluring skin scent. A considerable number of fellow perfumistas have commented on the unisex nature of this fragrance. In my opinion, a man can pull it off with the proviso that he's not put off by BV's head and heart which do lean more towards the feminine side. However, the reward in the form of the heavenly drydown is well worth the risk. Bottega Veneta EdP is pure delight and one of the best mainstream feminine perfumes out there at the moment.

The opening of this fragrance is, hands down, among the very best I have smelled so far during my short time as a perfume enthusiast. I do not get a jasmine overload (still an Alien girl), nor is this plainly a woody violet for me. Goes to show how different our noses are! What I DO get is a classy, subdued yet complex and soooooo alluring spicy-woody and just little bit of floral opening & heart with undertones of the developing leather; on my skin BV dries down (a bit too quickly, for which I docked half a star) to a somewhat pungent mossy leather. Those dry notes stuck to my skin for 12 hours after spraying. I am not a fan of the pungency; however this is a superb fragrance in my book, and quickly becoming my shape-up-and-get-stuff-done perfume. I may have to write to Santa or forego a few restaurant lunches, but either way I need this in my cabinet, and my sample won't last forever. In short, I love it, and definitely think it's worth a try especially if you're into leather fragrances. Give BV a little bit of time to open up, though: it won't yield all of its glory at first spray.

I'm a Leather fiend... when it comes to scents and this one is a stand out. This is my fave latest find. A refined and elegant fragrance...! Its been refer to as a GENTLE LEATHER! Due impart to its mysterious powdery ..smoky feel A classy leather,is always a Unisex scent in my book. I got compliments on my fragrance today while walking my dog... now who can say that's not a delight.

My beautiful Neiman Marcus Scent Event bag arrived today. What a coup. Unlike the Sephora promos, this one contained a large proportion of fragrances never tested by me and which I have been wanting to try. Top of the list? You guessed it: BOTTEGA VENETA. The hype over this launch has been so overwhelming that I came dangerously close to buying a bottle of this perfume blind--perhaps even as a qualifying purchase for the scent event! Fortunately, rationality prevailed, and I restrained myself, despite the fact that I had fallen in love at first sight with the bottle... To my great surprise, BOTTEGA VENETA turns out to be a close olfactory neighbor to a number of recent--and equally hyped--perfumes, including Balenciaga PARIS and Tom Ford VIOLET BLONDE. Yes, to my nose, BOTTEGA VENETA falls squarely into the woody violet camp! Before you accuse me of being anosmic or ignorant or crazy--or some combination of the three--please be aware that listed among the ingredients of this perfume is none other than that word so dear to me, 'ionone', which as a matter of fact is used in perfumery to impart the violet scent so beloved to violet aficionados! Indeed, it is the fourth listed ingredient, which means that it is present in substantial concentration!!!! So, no, I am not imagining the woody violet demeanor of BOTTEGA VENETA. Marketing hype be damned, to my nose this is a woody violet perfume, not a leather, not a jasmine, and certainly nothing new. As a certified violet 'ho', I'll definitely consider adding this perfume to my collection later on down the line, but there is no way that I would pay the current MSRP.

Bottega Veneta EDP opens with a fantastic, sharp, simple yet powerful and distinctive powdery-earthy blend, with a zesty bergamot note (which will be gone in seconds), juicy red pepper, patchouli, oakmoss and a vibrant yet tamed-down jasmine note, all surrounded by a light shade of leather and “reinforced” by aldehydes which also provide a sort of classic allure to the composition. The texture is really peculiar, as it smells at the same time cristalline, clean and vibrant yet thick, somehow “grayish” and dense: an elegant, powdery, talc white-floral accord beautiful sustained by dark, earthy and rooty notes of moss and patchouli, which smell at the same time dirty and perfectly restrained – so don’t expect anything realistic, raw or exotic: the inspiration is quite “glossy” and French in my opinion. Finally I smell a sort of mineral-salty feel which seems arising from the base earthy-mossiness, blending with aldehydes and the floral-indolic feel of jasmine. On the drydown it becomes increasingly less sweet and talc, and more herbal-mossy, but always extremely gentle and sophisticated. There is a genius and really well executed harmony going on between the powdery plushiness and the almost-indolic earthiness of the base notes, which makes Bottega Veneta smell incredibly good, refined and unique. Plus, don’t be “fooled” by the pyramid, as all notes smell quite unusual to me if compared to how they usually smell – not sure whether it’s because of the good quality of materials, or Almairac’s talent, but I had quite a hard time in “detecting” them – I expected something quite different, while here they all smell different than usual, in a totally good way. Bottega Veneta EDP is elegant and versatile, but peculiar and quite memorable: it’s a sort of half white/pink, half greyish/earthy fragrance, with nice shades and a gentle feel of pastel grace beautiful dirtened by darker notes. All, as I said, created with great and bright creativity. Worthy a try (or even a blind buy, as it is not that expensive). 7,5-8/10

Today sluggishly I wear a simple puristic outfit. Today does not feel me on flattering or ferment Cuddle. Today every too much said word is a torture for my ears and my mind. Today the air is so clear outdoors that I can look from the spire about the whole country. Today there sounds Chopin from the Cd-player. Today it may be a Martini Sec.

Less complex, non heady, suede, kinda wet yet smooth. Erotic, sensual and magnetic. Projection is average while longevity (close to skin stage is amazing) is fantastic, even on clothes. From cold evenings, fall, winter and rainy days (as good as NR for Men) this will rock. As per compliments, men and women gave high remarks.

When I wear this fragrance I get so many compliments, from both men and women. This fragrance is so chic and class, but also sexy. It is an elegant chypre. The suede / leather note makes this scent so special. I have many scents but this is my signature scent forever.
Didn't have big expectations about this one. But... what a pleasant surprise. One of my best non-niche acquisitions. Not a fan of leather but was so carefully created that I felt in love :D

After just recently selling my full bottle online, I feel this one deserves a few words. It is a discontinued signature scent of Italian fashion house, Bottega Veneta, known for their woven leather bags and minimalist clothing. The smell itself is similar to both hot sand and pure, wet clay. Plain cotton warmed in the sun.

I'll admit I was somewhat disappointed when I smelt this. I absolutely love Euphoria and I was looking for an equivalent that I could wear during the warmer months. Unfortunately this wasn't it. Although it isn't classed as a fruity floral, there is a considerable amount of fruity notes in this fragrance. The drydown does consist of some rich, woodsy notes that were a major component in the original fragrance, yet Euphoria Blossom doesn't have that distinctive darkness and sensuality that made the original so sexy. I heard somewhere that this fragrance was created to appeal to the Asian market, because a majority of them dislike heavy fragrances. I'd be interested to hear how well Euphoria Blossom is doing over there.

the opening starts off with citrus and pomegrante in a few cliche minutes comes the scent of intoxicating orchid the drydown has a woody base. calvin klien never seems to dissapoint me he and the noses behind the fragrances have an unique talent of notes & t.v advetisments. the reson it's not my favorite fragrance because of the heavy woody basis just dominates this but it's still a good fragrance it is sensuous and young.

Euphoria, Euphoria, you smell so sexy, I know that. But this Blossom is not a flower, but a spring-wrapped lie. Euphoria's little, deceitful, pink sister smells like armpit sweat in polyester. I was in a hurry and sprayed the Blossom on, but I wouldn't dare go out among people like that. It would have been embarrassing, as if I hadn't showered in hours, days, and years. The lotus flower is probably to blame for everything, but I lack more than just the necessary patience to analyze it. I feel utterly miserable, almost sick, as I write on, I surely need a bucket. Anyone who doesn't believe me and wants to hold their nose to it gets Blossom for free and can keep it forever and ever!!!

As a passionate "Euphoria" fan, I have long struggled to write about and evaluate "Euphoria Blossom." Today was finally the time for a thorough test. I can understand the rather unenthusiastic reactions when one first experiences the top note. Its piercing camphor freshness, combined with bitter bergamot and peony à la "Pleasures," lingers for a long time. Anyone who loves the enchanting warmth of "Euphoria" will inevitably be disappointed. But it is worth the wait - this fragrance requires a longer warm-up phase. The classic heart of "Euphoria" is perceived only as a hint for a long time; in any case, it is varied here towards a brighter shade. Alongside freesia, lily of the valley, cinnamon, and heliotrope, I detect the sweet scent of fresh paprika - very delicious! On one hand, "Euphoria" approaches sunshine scents like "Pleasures"; on the other hand (and I dare say, otherwise it wouldn't be a typical Calvin Klein), it radiates that special, soft elegance and thus maintains its individuality. So, anyone expecting the sex appeal of "Euphoria" will inevitably be disappointed. However, those looking for a pleasant, stylish everyday fragrance should definitely give "Euphoria Blossom" a try.

Today I completed the Euphoria family with the missing Blossom. Afterwards, I quickly went to the vet to get little Kira vaccinated. There, I was greeted by a colorful audience consisting of a pug, Jack Russell, Ridgeback, Great Dane, French Bulldog, and a white shepherd. For me, as a dog lover, it was pleasant company. I squeezed myself between the Ridge and the Jacky with my poodle baby. But hardly had I sat down when the Ridge started licking me from the left, and I gently patted his head. That was the starting signal for a heart-wrenching howling that ranged from the pitch A to the written C. My sympathetic words only encouraged the "singer" to perform more arias, and even the comforting words from her owner did not curb her urge to communicate. After an hour of listening, I needed an "art break" and sprayed Blossom outside in the hallway. And that, in turn, had a calming effect on me. The juicy pomegranate, mixed with green notes and the bitter kumquat, cooled my hot ears. Lotus and orchid have a unifying quality and provide clarity. The peony is noble - floral, and the woods are indeed light - spicy. The scent is very well balanced and green-bitter clarifying - but I do not find it overly floral. I wouldn’t have called it Blossom. Nevertheless, I like it well, as it creates a clear mind. Sorted like this, I confidently return to the waiting room and dedicate myself to the accompaniment music of the musical dog. She must have endured the treatment unscathed, as she only received a vaccination. But she has my understanding - I am also a softie when it comes to doctors.

I can't quite explain why this fragrance leads such a shadowy existence here on Parfumo; I find it beautiful, always wearable and suitable for everyday use, but also lovely for special occasions. Euphoria Blossom was a spontaneous purchase for me, but a completely successful one.

No, not a spring fragrance, it's too musty for that - this Blossom in the name doesn't fool me. No, it doesn't belong to winter, nor to autumn, and certainly not to summer. So, where does it belong? I don't know. It combines the floral notes of spring with the fruity aspects of summer and the mustiness of winter.

Euphoria Blossom was a real cream surprise cake for me. I have tested it extensively several times, at home, outside, overnight, at my (physically active) workplace... And my opinion on it: I was lucky with it, the cream cake ;) At the beginning, I also perceive what has already been described as synthetic or piercing.

... I am used to something stronger! EBlossom comes across as a bit too soft, somewhat bland, or already something I've smelled a thousand times elsewhere. Floral - yes, spring-like - yes, fruity - yes, but overall rather thin. When it gets warmer, it will surely be nice to wear, but it lacks power for me. After wearing it for a whole day, I like it better.

Oh, I love you so much my Euphoria Blossom. I hate your mother Euphoria, but you are nothing like her...you are so delicate and yet sexy...Simply something warm, floral, and wonderful. You always flatter me. You and I...we somehow belong together. I will never forget you! --Bottle Perfect:) --Scent The Blossom smells floral!..as the name suggests.

Despite having won a couple of “prizes” among which the Basenotes Award, apparently this scent seems quite controversial, with many connoisseurs being disappointed by it. It looks like one of those perfect candidates to be discontinued soon – many “people who love fragrances” seem to consider it too trendy and shallow, many “people who love mainstream” probabily consider it too light and understated. Well, I am among the fans instead. Love at first sniff, and it even grew on me. I find Bottega Veneta pour Homme filled with an insane amount of class and intelligence: it’s discreet, utterly enjoyable to wear, rather complex, fascinating and incredibly well blended. The opening is memorable, at least to my tastes: a sort of green, fizzy pine-citrus accord on a super thin yet dark base of patchouli, finished leather, and a warm resinous-floral-earthy note of labdanum which provides a subtle feel of warmth underneath the overall freshness. Now imagine this just whispered, toned down to an almost “meditative” quiet. A refined, hyper-modern concept of elegance, perfectly solid and substantial. It’s like being in a minimalist contemporary building in the middle of the forest: you feel the aromatic cold green breeze from outside, but there is also an aseptic, clean, silent feel of modernity – almost alienated (the astringent citric notes play a role here, as they smell almost like “ammonia” in a way). A sort of futuristic reading of “classic” clean masculine elegance – this is actually the interesting thing here, besides the fact it smells great (not that this is secondary...): the notes I’ve listed are possibly the most common in classic “fresh” colognes, but Bottega Veneta pour Homme smells just completely different from all of them. Miles away from any other cologne. To me, Maisondieu and Andrier perfectly managed to “translate” the classic structures into a future language - made of, well, I don't know what, probably a creative use of synthetics and naturals, or whatever magic they made to make Bottega smell like this. About projection & persistence, which seems quite “debated” as well as many people seem to consider them a flaw here; it is undoubtedly much close to skin, but surprisingly, you smell it “around” you for hours – you get this green-black smell coming and going, which is subtle yet much more distinctive than you think. To cut it short, I’ll be honest: I find this both one of the best “contemporary formal” fragrances at the moment, and call me idiotic, a smart, compelling, clever and apparently completely underrated avantgarde rewriting of classic canons. Which makes Bottega Veneta pour Homme almost challenging to wear, as it’s so deceptively subtle it’s so easy to underrate it and dismiss it as a shallow trendy scent. While it’s not, it’s a veil of great contemporary perfumery. I appreciate Bottega Veneta had the guts to come out with something like this. Although I admit the volume knob may need a fix (but I think they made the “extreme” version for that?), I personally love this a lot. 8,5/10

This release stands out from a lot of modern day designer releases for its quality. It is just about a hidden gem and if you are after a safe, but very nice masculine, it would be well worth checking out. Please see my video review.

If you like the "Bottega" fragrances for women, you'll be halfway hooked because "Bottega Veneta pour Homme" is similar in structure. It's a related formula of intense citrus head-notes except the "pour homme" -version goes into a more herbacious, woody direction by adding fir resin and pine. In the drydown I can smell the same leathery note as in the scent aimed at women (which I prefer). The female "Bottega" includes some kind of "oakmoss" which makes it more interesting for me, particularly in view of the fact that it is a recent perfume coming from Coty. Well, there is no oakmoss in this decent, beautiful masculine version, which seems to lack projection and longevity. Coming from "Bottega Veneta" you would expect something elegant and sophisticated, and that's what you get. In spite of the accent on wood and leather, this one is a "smoothie". The person who uses this fragrances probably plays it cool, my impression was that I never felt obvious wearing it. Might work well as a kind of fragrant security blanket.

Bottega Veneta pour Homme opens with an all too brief blast of relatively sharp bergamot citrus and alcoholic gin-like juniper berry before the fragrance turns slightly green as it transitions to its early heart derived from coniferous pine that slowly turns into green fir tree. Joining the coniferous woods lies a vague near aqueous mildly herbal woody undertone that adds a soft, smooth texture. The dry-down turns to a labdanum derived slightly powdery amber and subtle leather tandem joining patchouli from the base as the coniferous greens disappear. Projection is below average (though more than a skin scent) and longevity is above average at 9-10 hours on skin. While I never purchased the original Bottega Veneta release I have fond memories of sniffing it at their Las Vegas Palazzo boutique while on vacation and coming away relatively impressed. Based on those positive sister scent memories my expectations for Bottega Veneta pour Homme were much higher than normal. Unfortunately, different perfumers were responsible for the sister compositions, and alas, Bottega Veneta pour Homme comes up more than a bit short in comparison. The composition's heart really revolves around what I can only describe as "vague aqueous soft woods". Unlike the vast majority of occurrences where that term means "artificial smelling" in this case they really do not largely come off that way. That said, while the execution is rather good, the whole thing comes off as a tad too familiar until soft leathery labdanum in the late dry-down adds much needed distinguishing character. The bottom line is Bottega Veneta pour Homme is a cut above the average release and is pleasant enough to wear, but it does not distinguish itself enough from the ever growing crowd of competitors to warrant an unreserved recommendation earning a "good" rating of 3 stars out of 5.

Leather type of Bottega Veneta pour Homme makes me think of its possible descendants like Antaeus by Chanel en a little bit of Bel Ami by Hermes - a similar masculine leather and herbs mix. On me its a calming and introvert scent that makes me think of a forest with its sweetish scent of fir balsem and the nuance of the decaying leaves. It definitely has the character due to the leather and herbs notes on a dark base. But it's calm and not overpowering due to low silage - makes it a good office scent for someone who likes powerful, but not overpowering fragrances. And it has its elegancy as well.

The appointment of Tomas Maier as Bottega Veneta’s Creative Director can, no doubt, be seen as a major turning point for the company. He’s successfully applied his artistic and aesthetic vision on its overall image as well as its products, including (luckily!) fragrances.

Problem is you may have to reapply often. Performance is low. This is an easy going piney leather, not overly complex but has depth. Low polarization very versatile. I think I get a little juniper berry and clary sage to kind of round things out. Subtle, grown up, classy and a little refined. You can get it for a great price.

Bottega Veneta pour Homme starts really mature due to a heavy juniper note. Heavy because it's boosted by other ingredients, probably the pine or pimento. And Mature with a big M, like Pasha or Santos by Cartier, or how Égoïste can be mature.

Leather fragrances are among my favourites. When I started taking the world of perfumes seriously, Brit Rhythm for Him Eau de Toilette was my first perfume in this category, smooth leather for newbies. It was 2015. Sure, I've used leathery fragrances before, but I needed to be fully aware.

I join the group of people who didn't like this scent. I have wanted to test this perfume for a very long time and when I finally managed to do so, I was left with a feeling of considerable disappointment. I agree with the statement of the reviewer below that the scent is a bit in the opening, for my nose it is the least pleasant part of this composition.

Calvin Klein CK One Summer 2014 is probably still the most popular / hyped CK One Summer version in recent memory, no doubt due to it being one of the best, a margarita-meets-pina colada mix that features a mix of citruses, coconut, tequila, sugar, florals, and woods. It’s fresh, a good balance of salty and sweet, slightly boozy and fruity, with some savory undertones. Certainly it feels most appropriate in the daytime during warmer weather, but it’s refreshing and awakening any time. It compares to Tommy Bahama Set Sail St. Barts well, though St. Barts is a bit sweeter, leaning into the coconut more, whereas CK One Summer 2014 is a bit saltier, referencing the margarita somewhat more. It performs moderately, but that’s fair, given that the price point was reasonable, especially on the secondary market, though I’m not sure how easy it is to find a bottle nowadays. Overall, it’s quite nice, and I’d recommend nabbing a bottle if you would like a slightly saltier alternative to St. Barts. 7 out of 10

First off..... I just tried this on yesterday and wore it again before going to sleep. My review might change soon. Also, I have not made an official count or done any serious survey but there seems to be MANY, A LOT, NUMEROUS aquatic/beach/summer flankers and limited edition releases out there. You're bound to come across a few that seem to smell alike or "cross paths". Anyone who has read my reviews knows I'm not a great nose. Some reviewers on fragrantica, "fraghead" websites and youtube reviewers can break down notes and nuances. I just tend to give my general idea on the overall aroma and projection/longevity. This one seems synthetic and the notes are muddled. It's nice but c'mon, does it really stand out? How many times can you do the whole "melon", "aquatic" and "lime" notes? I'm happy with Tommy Bahama's Set Sail which covers that and smells similar to an expensive Creed VIW.

The World Cup summer is just around the corner, and I’m excited. It fits perfectly with my current endeavor to expand the summery side of my collection. If possible, not with too many new orange fragrances - I already have many, including some of the best. Right now, I’m looking more for other summer refreshers - mint, lime, fruits, ice, cocktails. I find it very difficult to deal with marine aquatics, but it’s also quite interesting to find suitable candidates. Overall, it’s a challenging task to distinguish between the often very similar summer perfumes and to separate the wheat from the chaff. But let’s get to the latest CK One Summer - which deserves an extra detailed comment from me. Get ready for it, here’s one of my recommendations for your summer, and it’s limited and very affordable. And unique, different, sexy, young. Perfect for a samba summer. Sure, it’s not perfect, but I’m happy to start a bit of hype here so that at least more people will test it. Because it has convinced me so much that I will even take a closer look at the other summer editions, having already ordered the predecessor blindly. It hit a nerve and deserves to be bought. The original could also be considered, a perfect entry-level perfume, which never really fit into my large collection. This spot could now be taken by one or two of the summer editions, which might even gain value over the years and become rarer. Plus, it has a hot beach look and no boring ideas - collector’s heart, what more could you want! I did test one of the Summers during my early days and commented on it - back then, however, it was just very quickly, strictly, and I didn’t catch a particularly spectacular vintage. Unlike this Rio-Caipirinha with bite, zest, and party mode. With this scent, the hips shake, the sun burns, and the holiday and leisure heart laughs. It starts with tequila, lime, and a lot of sugar - of course, the fragrance pyramid is also marketing. But besides courage, ideas, and coolness, I’m simply convinced by this laid-back Caribbean scent. Sure, it’s not niche, quite the opposite. It’s definitely synthetic and sometimes scratchy and odd. At first, I thought, oh no, too much melon. But overall, this thing rocks and just dances away the criticism. One could really imagine raw sugar. I even smell a very slightly salty note, as if you’ve been dried out for 3 hours after a trip to the sea. Coconut is only very lightly present at the end, plus a powdery musk drydown. Conclusion: Award for being particularly bold and slightly tipsy! Bottle: stylish, colorful, young, cool. But there have been much prettier ones. Sillage: free and summery - don’t expect too much. Longevity: here, too, low expectations help - then you’ll be rewarded with 7 hours. Despite the synthetics and flaws here and there - the 2014 CK One Summer is an extraordinary vintage that will be talked about for a long time. So secure your copy, even if that sounds sensational. At least test it and let me know your opinion. I think especially the younger ones around 20 will love this cocktail with tequila! P.S.: Alcoholics and children, please keep your distance ;)

Spring is just around the corner, spring and summer fragrances are slowly being brought out again, and some summer smashers are moving from the wish list to the have-it list. Who doesn't know the anticipation? The transition from heavy to light and vice versa? I always look forward to a change in scent. I got this one last year along with the CK One Summer version 2016. I like CK One and all its flankers and limited editions. Similar to the classic, you can get them for a small price, and they are really very good flankers. Especially the summer versions. The 2016 version is a fruity mojito cocktail, while this one is a truly fresh fruit tequila cocktail. This scent is really very light and summery, as the series suggests. This lovely cocktail note also makes it a good evening scent. It starts off fruity-fresh. Grapefruit, lemon, lime, and also a nice melon note. Added to that is tequila with a decent sugar note. It really smells delicious. If my cocktail smelled like this, I would love to drink it. Unisex is also completely justified here, as it is with all summer flankers. Good vibes are guaranteed. The sillage is also quite good, especially in the first two hours. The downside is unfortunately the longevity. I would estimate 4-5 hours. However, this is a problem that many fresh fragrances have, even at significantly higher prices. It is definitely suitable for a refreshing summer scent. For longer activities, I would choose a different fragrance. Summer 2014 is a lovely casual scent for spring and summer. Although it is a limited edition, it is consistently available at many shops. For under 30 euros for 100ml, it's a nice bargain for the upcoming warm season.

CK One Summer 2014 I would describe as a lovable fragrance. Since last Friday, the weather has been doing somersaults. Starting with summer heat at 35°C; then thunderstorms and finally rainy weather at well below 17°C. In the last 5 days, there has been something for everyone. In such weather, the olfactory chaff separates from the wheat. I would definitely assign this EdT to the wheat: Tropical heat: The wearer sweats but the fragrance works. No unpleasant combinations that could leave others breathless. Summer thunderstorms, storms, and downpours: As long as you don't get soaked to the bone, the fragrance holds up, which is no small feat. But even in a drenched state, a pleasant scent remains. Heavy rain and dreary weather: The fragrance spreads summer lightness and instills confidence that the sun will soon show itself again. What more could a man or woman want? CK One Summer 2014 is definitely not a fair-weather fragrance. The EdT performs just as well beyond the 30-degree mark as it does on rainy, gloomy bad weather days.

... hot day in Florida, picking oranges and lemons on a fruit plantation. Booked a few days in advance. The foreman shows us how to properly harvest these fruits without damaging the plants. Just like on a strawberry field, we can eat as many fruits as we want. And the ripe oranges taste simply fantastic. When applying this fragrance, you get a little rush of citrus fruits.

The newest addition to my BV family is Bottega Veneta Illusione. She must be a cousin, since at first sight both bottle and scent are different and you do not see the family bond between her and “the siblings” right away. Not before wearing a few times. Then suddenly you get it. The siblings are, by the way, Bottega Veneta EdP, Eau Sensuelle and Eau Légère. I adore the original BV bottle design, the chubby and heavy bottle with the tag around the neck. It is quite delicate and looks great on the shelf. BVI comes in a cubic design with no metal details. Colour wise it is more to the feminine side whereas the siblings are significantly unisex. It fits the scent which I regard as feminine. The scent is also far more feminine than the other three. The fragrance starts with berries, sweet and citric. Then the flowers appear and soften the edges, making the scent deeper and more faceted. During the next hours it slowly turns into an even deeper scent due to the tonka bean. When looking at notes, this is up a totally different alley than the siblings. But then something happens. A slightly dry note evolves and exposes the line between the cousin and her relatives. I wore it a few times before noticing, mainly because I focused on how different it smelled. Perhaps I was surprised that it was so different, a bit embarrassing since I do not expect all my Diors or Chanels to smell the same, do I? It is a reminder to myself to keep my mind open. So what do I think about the cousin? I really like her. She is a keeper like the others. She offers something totally different. More fruity and sweeter. And feminine. The bottle is nice, though it does not look as classy and expensive as the original design. I do admire when a House invents a great design and use it for all their bottles - but I do like to look at my bottles as well as sniffing the juice and wearing it. So I enjoy whenever I find a new interesting design. Year 2, 8/365

Finally, I have my new love in my collection. If I could, I would marry this fragrance. The only negative is that there is no larger bottle than 75 ml. Citrusy start, but not clean, rather juicy (bergamot fans, take note!!). This is immediately followed by the interplay of orange blossom, tonka, and I can even detect a hint of blackcurrant. All underpinned by OLIVE WOOD, which I can actually perceive just like that. I have not consciously noticed olive wood in any other fragrance before, but here I can clearly identify the note. This combination smells so wonderful, I just want to dive into it. It smells expensive, special, of quality, of an Italian summer evening, the sun warms my skin, my feet dangle in the cool water, where a wooden boat rocks in the waves, and I enjoy a refreshing St. Pellegrino lemon soda. Please do not overlook this amazing little fragrance. I randomly sprayed a few scents in the perfumery (that's how I've found several heartthrobs) and fell head over heels in love. It lasts forever on clothing, projection is good for the first few hours, then becomes a bit closer to the skin, but still well noticeable. A big WOW from me, and it will surely never leave my collection voluntarily.

I am now 30 - that's 60 Marks! Accordingly, my choice of fragrance should also become more mature at some point. Still, I am drawn to my usual pink sugary waters. I just can't get away from sweet-fruity-floral perfumes. Today I tested the sample of Illusione for the second time. At first, I smell blackberries (probably the currant?), but in a way that's quite natural, similar to Amethyst by Lalique. Then it quickly transforms into a direction similar to Ange ou démon le secret. But it's lightly underlaid with bright woods that soften everything. So young and yet so feminine. In the base, it becomes a bit greener, even though the fig leaf is actually listed in the heart note. On one hand refreshing, on the other hand also calming. And indeed natural. The sillage is rather close to the body, but the longevity is quite good. This fragrance just fits always. And especially well with my age. This could actually become my new daily companion.

Finally, a completely new scent from Bottega Veneta. The bottle is square, with a deep, solid drop-shaped base, a round cap, and a cutout in the middle for the sprayer - great! The initial scent experience: refreshing, citrusy, red fruity, delicious! Then it becomes woody, very lightly, softly, and comfortably tonka bean-like. I perceive this fragrance more as a Cologne. In the height of summer, it's super wearable and as a refreshing splash, the first 10 minutes are invigorating, delightful, uplifting, and refreshing, and for the next 2 hours, it is a soothing, aromatic, maritime, Italian companion. Not a constant companion or even a friend or partner. No, a fleeting pleasure. Everything else would be an illusion!

Dear Parfumos, I usually don’t write reviews, but this bottle has captivated me.
