So please be forgiving if I’m missing some information, as this is my first perfume review ️ For a long time, it stood as a tester, quite inconspicuous in my display case. I thought: Bottega Veneta, what could be so great about it? The bottle is unremarkable, rather old-fashioned looking.

I've read quite a bit about the fragrances from Bottega Veneta. And always only good things. So, from time to time, I click through, check the notes, and see if there’s maybe one that I should really test. Then I stumbled upon Illusione and immediately found two of my trigger notes, namely olive wood and fig leaf. Off it went onto my wish list.

If we are honest - your appearance probably wouldn’t have attracted me in my favorite perfume store. You stand there so inconspicuously, yes, almost unremarkably, and as biased as that may sound - the eye smells? famously with it.

Today, after a long time, I was back in the perfume store and had almost ordered this scent blind a few times before. Just the bottle speaks to me 100%. When I saw Illusione on the shelf, it was clear which one I would try first. For me, the scent is quite spicy in the opening, even though there are no "spice notes" included.

I can only agree with the other comments; the scent truly evokes a Mediterranean vibe. When you close your eyes, you can really imagine strolling through the alleys of a small Italian town. It reminds me of pizza and wine under olive trees. Vacation, relaxation, and enjoying other cultures. Dolce Vita!

I must do a preface: I've recently tested and re-tested this scent and nowadays I like it....but the problem is the wrong name. If for the warm and rich " Obsession" the name was perfect, here, in this pure, clean scent, I don't see and I don't smell the sense of "trouble in mind". Anyway, the result on my skin is pleasant: the opening is fresh with a very light resinous touch, the heart is a little warmer and aromatic, almost unisex, but the notes I mainly smell are the synthetic ones , giving a weird character to this minimalist scent. The sillage and the longevity aren't so good in comparison to the price and the bottle is very minimal , in the style of Calvin Klein 's creations. So, this scent could be re-named "Zen" or "Pure", but I think there's no obsession in it!

If you took the fresh green from cK One, gave it a fine gourmand note and put it on fluffy woods, you'd have something like this. As an evolution of the perfume brand, developing the theme of cK One into new territory makes perfect sense - to a marketing strategist. However, back in the real world... flathorn called something 'hard-to-object-to' ... but I would say more than that, once the top notes have gone, and you're left with a fluffy sweet drone, this is easy-to-be-bored-by.

If one dares to create a successor to Obsession, one should work very carefully on the formula to make it as memorable as the great predecessor. Unfortunately, Obsessed does not provide me with an Aha moment. Why would one be obsessed with a lab-created musk molecule and a lot of laundry-scented lavender? At most, if one hasn't showered in weeks and longs for cleanliness. The old Obsession scent was a confident, strong seducer. Obsessed smells of slightly bitter lavender and clean musk. The color of the bottle and the liquid fits... very transparent, not intrusive. Kate Moss is once again the face of the campaign, hardly aged, freshly washed? What does such a colorless scent say about our society? Why this need for cozy, old-fashioned lavender (again! Mon Guerlain is bringing it back too...) on one hand and well-groomed bathroom tile aesthetics in white on the other? Do we want to make such a bland statement or do we long for a relaxation room, an oasis free from dirt from the hostile environment? Donald can't grope us here, and if he has indeed violated our pussy or our brains, we wash everything back clean and white. The perfect perfume from the USA: the name alone is fake news. I wouldn't dream of being obsessed with lavender.

...underestimated on my part when I first smelled it in the perfumery shortly after its release. Why it was named "Obsession" is completely illogical. It really has nothing in common with the CK classic. As I said: according to my statement from 3 years ago, I smelled very little, certainly not the expected lavender. The scent came back to my mind after I frequently walked around in the last few months with Chanel's lavenders "Boy", "Jersey EdP", + Chloe's "Eau de Fleurs - Lavande" and enjoyed these different lavender scents anew every day. Unfortunately, Chloe no longer produces their lavender. In the mainstream area, lavender as a fragrance note is not very present, which is why I tested the CK repeatedly. At first, I am greeted by nonspecific synthetic fresh notes with a slight sharpness. Unremarkable, the term "drugstore scent" comes to mind. Gradually, everything sorts itself out, and lavender floral notes emerge, fixed by synthetic musky, slightly woody base notes. My scent impression can best be described as a cool, synthetic lavender-dominated clean musk. Not a blooming lavender field. And: I like the whole thing. Wearable with, at, and alongside everything as a clean accessory when it should be unremarkable, or for feeling good. Longevity is average on the skin, all day long in my hair.

While strolling through Kstadt, my husband brought me a beautifully shaped crystal-clear bottle, filled with equally clear liquid. This sight is pleasant and somewhat unspectacular - almost harmless in its purity. But the first spray sweeps me away to the North Sea, where the stiff breeze nearly knocks me off my path. A hunched figure approaches me - the local postman - and he dryly announces: The dike is a bit soft. Better carry the furniture to the first floor. I am somewhat unsettled by his words - but the Northman remains perfectly calm. Goodbye! And he pushes his bicycle vigorously against the storm. Yes - the North German temperament is admirable. And just as harsh as up on the dike, Obsessed blows towards me. The clear bottle doesn’t exactly suggest the raging elements like Nis Randers: Crashed and howled and bursting night .... I turn the bottle in my hands in amazement. Definitely for Women. Although I initially wanted to assign the scent to a weather-beaten sea dog, I find myself liking it more and more. It has everything I enjoy: Cool neroli and deep lavender - citrusy and soft ambrette seeds. But I didn’t expect the scent to hit me like sea spray. How did the storm and the North Sea get into the bottle? Magic and somehow fascinating. Definitely the right choice for sea dogs - but also for anyone who loves the wild, primal sea.

When I wear this perfume, I am a girl on a 90s poster in my baggy jeans and with loose, smooth hair, without makeup, and the poster is black and white. I have more buddies than girlfriends but am still feminine. And my few girlfriends are not bitches, but laid-back and prefer to surf or skateboard rather than talk endlessly.

So, today I tried Obsessed, well, I'm a bit disappointed. I find the bottle just so great, puristic, clear, and very special, and I had hoped that the liquid would match the material. Well, the bottle does a lot more for me than the liquid inside. The scent is indeed light, thus fitting the clear packaging, but unfortunately really nothing special.

Well, it smells very intense of lavender to me. I will test it again. It reminds me of Mon Guerlain. It is quite intense and sweet. Will lavender be the next trend? I can add something now. I even bought the fragrance after all because I liked it very much in the dry down. But now I find it not sweet at all, rather clean. Refreshing but still pronounced.

I had high hopes for this one (strong ties to the first Bottega Veneta fragrance!), but can't form any attachment to "Knot". It is a white floral with notes of orange blossom, neroli, white rose and peony. The added lavender enhances the "bathroom effect": the smell of fresh soap and herbaceous cleanliness, white bathtowels, white tiles. "Knot" does not belong to the plethora of common fruity florals, but it's somewhat generic in its use of orange blossom plus neroli, plus lavender &musk. The result is a fragrance with no warmth at all and rather synthetic overtones. No knot in my handkerchief to remind me of buying this one (in spite of the fantastic perfume vessel).

For some reason I didn't notice this perfume's soapiness when I bought it. Usually my nose doesn't malfunction at perfume counters, but the beautiful citrus, the florals and musk are soon so drenched in that sudsy note that it's hard to appreciate them. Not much else to say. Longevity and sillage are average.

Fresh Spicy Neroli, Orange and Lime in the opening which is fleeting. It has a sharp citric edge from the White Rose in the heart along with a creamy, dry and earthy Lavender that reminds me of a moisturing hand cream. Along with Jojoba which gives it a waxy, buttery texture. It does go very round, Floral, Musky and Hazy quickly after the brightness of the citric elements doesn't hang around long. You're left with a dusty lavender musk. I prefer the Lavender in bvlgari Au the Bleu as it's more Minty fresh rather than creamy and buttery here.

When I purchased Bottega Veneta Eau Légère, I received a miniature of Knot. Today, on this last day of the year, I applied Knot. Well, I could be mistaken, maybe my nose is playing tricks on me, but this scent feels very familiar. Knot is, for me, a scent twin of Alien Eau de Toilette. Perhaps others with more trained noses could make another comparison, but I have both here and they are very, very similar. Knot is definitely a very warm, elegant scent, starting off distinctly with mandarin. It is not overly sweet, the sillage does not overwhelm. Rather, this fragrance caresses its wearer. One really thinks of sun-drenched orange and mandarin groves in sunny Italy. Knot is truly a very beautiful and worth-testing fragrance, the development on the skin is very pleasant, not too intrusive, very noble, one can wear the scent in just about any situation. It is present but not overpowering. I can easily imagine it in any season, although I would be more cautious with the dosage in summer. And I don't really think it's suitable for very young girls. But that's a matter of taste. Overall successful. With this, I can slide well into the new year. I wish the same for all of you :)

Knot surprised me in two ways. It is in no way tangled like a knot, and it is also not leathery like the Bottega. No, the scent is clear and well-ordered. Knot greets me fresh with lime and clementine, cooled by clear neroli. The orange blossom adds gentle sunshine. The lavender is pleasantly calming and the white rose delicately elegant. The tonka bean is round and soft, providing a comforting finish. My mom is in the hospital, and I spritz myself with the scent to avoid completely wearing out the carpet. May everything turn out well.

Knot was lying in a package with a big bow under the Christmas tree.... I unwrapped it impatiently, admired the beautiful heavy and simple bottle for a moment, and then sprayed it on... The scent cloud slowly lands on my hand. I breathe in the fragrance... Oranges, mandarins, and clementines.....so fresh and juicy! just the way I love it.

Even with the first spray, I thought, this is very noble! The scent is initially fruity, fresh, and yet immediately warm. It starts on my skin not obviously citrusy but rather reveals a slightly bitter scent, gently supported by the citrus notes. Very interesting.

Knot starts off surprisingly green for me. After spraying, I think of freshly mowed grass rather than one of the aforementioned fragrance notes for the first 5 minutes. Then it begins to turn citrusy. Clearly, it heads in the direction of orange. The longer it’s on, the more the orange comes through. With every movement, a fresh hint of orange wafts towards me.

The opening is fresh, cheerful, and instantly uplifting. Knot is not really citrusy, but that’s definitely thanks to the orange blossom. It’s been about 2 1/2 hours since I sprayed it, and I can still perceive the top notes well. Now warmth and powder have joined in without sweetness: white rose.

The interesting thing is that I couldn't categorize this scent at first; it smelled quite floral, so that was my first impression. I felt that it wasn't for me. Through research, I perceive the perfume quite differently; it smells of clementine, but spicy, and over time it becomes a bit bitter, which I find very special.

Illusione is an odd duck. It's not really gourmand-y at all, but somehow the adjective that first leaps to my mind when I smell it is "delicious". But of course, that makes no sense at all, as it is, in essence, a slightly tart riff on Dior Eau Sauvage Parfum. It's missing that almost effervescent heaviness that E.S.P. has, but if you remove that, and add a bunch of bitter orange, Illusione is more-or-less where you end up. It's incredibly nice, weirdly kind of mouth-watering, and, in short, "delicious." Unfortunately, though, it does have a near-fatal flaw: the longevity here is shameful. On my skin, I get maybe two hours, and up to 4 total on my clothes - for the price, that's pretty much clown shoes. And yes, it does also have a pretty limited sillage, but it *is* a warm weather frag, so that's kind of to be expected. But the longevity? I am tempted to call it "pathetic". So, it leaves me with a bit of a quandary. If they made this concentration a little stronger - or just tweaked it so it lasted a bit longer - this would be a top 5 warm weather/office fragrance for me. But as it stands, the amount one has to overspray to get any sort of longevity out of it will have my 100mL bottle gone by the end of next summer, if I try to put it in the rotation, and I can't really justify it - nor can I encourage that. In the end, then, I guess we have this: (1) the fragrance itself is fantastic (2) it's also got some of the worst longevity in my entire 100+ bottle collection, and (3) she costs a fair bit. Granted, I got it for a better-than-retail price, but still - it was too much to pay for this level of performance. And yet... I really, really like it, for the time that it lasts. Sooo... 5/10 for longevity 10/10 for the fragrance itself = 7.5/10 overall. Basically, if you see it for a good price (sub $65/100mL), the profile sounds intriguing, and you're willing to put up with the shite longevity, maybe grab it. If you get annoyed when a frag only lasts half the day? Don't.

A small twig broke off from the branch of the old cedar at the corner of Chester Gate and Albany Street, was caught by the wind, and soon fluttered down Robert Street, where it came to rest before the threshold of No. 21. Then it was still again. Just then, Anselm unlocked the door. He picked up the twig, took it inside, and placed it on the mantelpiece. Then he fell back into deep thought. In less than an hour, he would meet Miss von Hallmackenreuther. What should he wear? And which perfume would be the right one? He decided on the faded army chinos and the dark blue Comme Des Garcons blazer he had bought at the little second-hand shop at Portobello Market. And the old brown Edward Green monks. He felt safest in no other shoes. And now for the scent. That would be much more difficult. But then he had an inspiration. Why not this new one from Bottega Veneta? It wasn’t too fashionable, but also not too old-fashioned. Somehow timeless. That’s how he wanted to come across, right? Maybe she would finally see him as he saw himself. Sometimes he had the strange feeling that they had known each other for a hundred years. That some curious trick of fate kept bringing them together, yet never allowed them to truly connect. He sniffed once more at the pretty little bottle. Yes, a wise decision. He liked this fragrance. First a bit lemony and fruity, but deeper than usual. Perhaps a third lower. And then so devilishly fairy-tale-like resinous, almost forest-magical, soft dark green in any case. Later also sweet, but still spicy. Undecided like himself. Somehow outdated and yet hip. He didn’t even like the word. And yet he secretly used it often. He felt so out of time again. Anselm took a few sprays and set off. Several blocks away at Fitzroy Square, a young woman with short curly hair stood in front of the wardrobe, meticulously surveying its contents. Lina von Hallmackenreuther chose the polka-dotted light blue dress with the Peter Pan collar. If she had to meet him in a place like the Groucho, she wanted to make the most of it. There weren’t many places where she felt comfortable in this dress. As a counterpoint to the dress, she would wear a men’s fragrance. She knew immediately which one. Illusione. It suited her because it didn’t commit to anything. Herbal, fruity, woody, and yet also sweet. And soft in the end. Would she be soft in the end too? In any case, she wanted Anselm to… She wasn’t quite sure herself. He should find her unconventional. Not like the others. For that, this was the right perfume. As the wind picked up again in the big city and the clouds drifted over the sea of chimneys like lost sheep, the two sat across from each other at a small table in the back of Café Groucho. Anselm appeared particularly calm. He cautiously sniffed in her direction, for he was very eager to know what kind of scent she had chosen for him. After all, at least this was one thing that connected them - the love of perfume. One of the few things they both knew about each other. He sniffed and sniffed - but… there was nothing. Only his own scent was detectable, the fine, soft-sweet aura of Illusione. How strange. What could that mean? Had she changed so much that she went out without a scent? Suddenly it dawned on him. She wanted to show herself to him without any embellishment, without games, without a backdrop. She wanted no distance, perhaps more closeness instead. Anselm's heart began to race. Lina was not really excited, but somehow… nervous. As if something unusual were in the air. She sniffed in his direction. Surely he was wearing Grey Vetiver again. But no, there was nothing of vetiver or anything similar, there was… she couldn’t define it. Then she almost jumped. She leaned a bit closer to him to take a lint off his collar. He was obviously not wearing any scent today. Only her own fragrance was present, only Illusione, nothing else. What could that mean? Was he trying to tell her something? That he wanted to become a different person? Nonsense. Suddenly a thought came to her. Yes, that could be it. She was almost sure. He didn’t want to overshadow her, to show her that she was enough on her own with her aura, to make her feel, you alone should be the center… The waiter came and brought the coffee. He looked a bit strange. He was wearing some kind of bathrobe. Quite hip territory, the area around Russell Square. He set down the cups and smiled at the two. “You smell good,” he said. “Illusione… I like it too!”

I discovered this fragrance at a tasting workshop in a small perfumery in Cologne. I still remember that we were exploring fresh scents and the hosting lady mentioned basil. Only that there is no basil in it at all! ;-) In the end, this was by far the best scent for me among perhaps 15 total (including brands like Comme de Garcons, Dolce & Gabbana, and Diptyque). That's why I quickly bought it, even without basil! When looking at the creations by Antoine Maisondieu - doesn't that mean House of God? ;-) - I notice that this perfumer has a tendency towards using as few ingredients as possible, much like many star chefs advocate for their dishes. Illusione leans more towards the citrusy than the woody direction, with the lemon coming across only gently sour. The cedar wood integrates subtly. Vetiver and tonka bean skillfully cushion everything and ultimately convey an earthy-sweet undertone. With a bit of imagination, I can even detect pine needles on the forest floor, surrounded by a balsamic aura. An illusion perhaps? ;-) Long story short: Illusione manages to create a nature-inspired aura with just a few ingredients, which is quite linear, fresh-woody, and yet balsamic. Nothing in the top note is jarring to the nose, leaving behind a pleasant feeling that definitely reminds one of lemon balm, as found in some bath additives. If fresh harmony is what you're looking for and synthetic bombs are off the table, this is an absolute recommendation! Unfortunately, the longevity and sillage are rather poor.

Bottega Veneta's Illusione was one of my biggest surprises this year. It caught me off guard, without me wanting it to. Few YouTubers even had it on their radar, and although there was a subdued campaign, it left me completely cold. Ultimately, it was a free fragrance sample that enchanted me. My first impression back then during the sample was quite negative. I smelled a bitter, almost aggressive orange and I immediately told myself: "No! This is not for you!" However, this fragrance then developed into a direction I did not expect. Warmth, balm, coziness, sauna stay, fir forest ... Thoughts and memories rushed through my mind - I had to have it, and I needed it yesterday! I work a lot in a smaller office with several people. Daily Aventus and I would have been quartered. The fact that Illusione starts off prominent, but then becomes calm and reserved, suited me well. And the fact that the fragrance is only really noticeable for 2-4 hours does not bother me at all. I actually find that to be its strength. I don’t want to be the scent tree in the car every day and be the center of attention for the noses present. Sometimes, yes sometimes, I just want to be there without being overly smelled. Like an illusion indeed. When is the best time to wear it? In fact, I bought it in the depths of winter and I associate the fragrance more with warming coziness and fir balm in tow. It’s not a scent I would wear in the height of summer at 30 degrees. However, in my opinion, it can be flexibly worn in all seasons in many situations. Just not in the club, where it feels out of place, just like I do. ;) I even think it’s a fragrance I would recommend to the 30+ generation. It is neither cool, sexy, youthful, nor sporty. It radiates calmness, serenity, and elegance. Fitting for the brand image of Bottega Veneta. (That doesn’t mean there aren’t elegant, serene, and calm people under 30 ;) The bottle is unique to me, mainly because of the cap, which isn’t really a cap at all. The marbled-looking top is open at the top and therefore doesn’t protect the spray head 100% from oxygen, giving it more of an artistic touch. The bottom is strongly curved inward, creating an illusion of water rising up. Lacoste must have found the idea intriguing as well, as the current fragrance "Match Point" looks similar at the bottom. Overall, a beautiful, citrusy fragrance that drifts into a warming, balsamic, and serene coziness. Very light, almost non-existent, and therefore strong for some days.

To label “Illusione” by Bottega Veneta as an unknown fragrance is somewhat puzzling, given its 127 reviews and 54 owners about a year after its release. Nevertheless, somehow it seems to me that despite its potential, it hasn’t really “hit” here, almost dissipating as if it glides quietly along the edge of visibility. “Illusione” resembles its somewhat more well-known predecessors in the men’s segment from BV (the pour Homme line and the - male - Essence Aromatique), AND yet it fundamentally differs from them. This too requires explanation. Similarities exist in the resinous components - somewhat the hallmark of BV men’s fragrances, even more so than a partial leatheriness (which is absent in “Illusione”). Such resinousness is central to my nose in “Illusione,” without being unpleasantly dominant. An abstracted (needle) woodiness. Furthermore, a beautifully integrated citrus note connects all the mentioned fragrances, although I believe this is significantly more pronounced in the Essence Aromatique. In “Illusione,” it hides behind fir needles and soft-warm woodiness. One should not expect a clearly recognizable, standout lemon like in some classic colognes. And there is another connecting element: BV men’s fragrances “match” incredibly well with the brand’s design presentation. A visit to a store is recommended for this - where the wonderful Parco Palladiano line can also be tested. However, there are also differences. “Illusione” has a “non-vanilla,” unobtrusive sweetness that I personally really like and that I prefer over the pseudo-leathery base of the pour Homme line. The vetiver indicated here is something I can truly smell, as a very subtle, soft component that “grounds” the resinousness. And then the mentioned soft woodiness wraps around all of this... Not spectacular, not avant-garde, but very beautiful and very easy to wear, especially from spring to autumn, at work, but also just for casual wear. Somehow the average rating here is justified: “Illusione” does not stand out, is not an aha experience, but simply a well-made “mainstream” fragrance. And perhaps that is why it has become the fragrance I wear most often. It is also... … more Arvo Pärt than Andrea Bocelli. … more tango in Finnish forests than Italian tarantella. However, in summer under a blue sky. … more suited for suit wearers than “casual.” … more less than more. A walk, lost in thought, dew freshness in the early morning, clarity, groundedness. Unpretentiousness, understatement, simplicity. Allerseelenruhe. A “business fragrance” like Prada L'Homme yet entirely different. I commend BV for not cutting into its own flesh with a release overkill like some other houses (even though I am aware that it is now merely a brand within a performance-oriented large corporation). Five men’s fragrances in the “mainstream area” in seven years - that is pleasantly manageable. I admit that each spray pierces my olfactory heart, as I already know in advance that this beautiful scent will not last long unless I get close to myself. But hope dies last: Perhaps one day “Illusione” will be available in a more intense, longer-lasting version like the original pour Homme. The bottle is definitely already a real eye-catcher.

I haven't had too many of the 2019 releases under my nose yet; I don't even know if there's enough for a top/flop blog this year. Only a few things have truly intrigued and tempted me, in addition to the already decreasing testing rhythm. However, I was definitely excited and curious about the new Bottega Veneta; something drew me to it. Its color, its weight, its gravitas.

In my second home, Lake Garda, where the south begins. Where cypress trees and mountains unite and the sun makes the water shine in a thousand colors. Where a hint of lemon is in the air and you hear a friendly Buongiorno when you go jogging along the promenade in the morning, with the scent of the lake wafting around you.

If the fragrance had been released 15 years ago, I would have "blind smelled" it as a flanker of Gucci's Envy for Men. It really goes in that direction... It could also be called "Envy Cologne" or "Envy Spring Break." The notes are completely different, yet I cannot deny a strong similarity.

With the title Illusione, I became intrigued - as I love living in illusions. My husband, on the other hand, is a realist - which complements each other quite well. The fragrance starts citrusy fresh and free - which is not illusory. What else might come? Balsam fir can conjure romantic forest desires - but here it goes straight into the underbrush.

Do you know that feeling? When you have no other choice but to buy a fragrance just because it reminds you of something? That was the case for me. This scent reminds me of the 60s, of Sundays, of young gentlemen in white shirts, with a bit of pomade (it was called Brisk back then) in their hair. There’s something “clean, fresh” about it.

The card defines this a “juicy oriental fougère” balanced with “exotic woods”. Pretending I didn’t read the “fougère” part in order to keep my lunch in my stomach, what I get out of Eternity Now is basically only the “juicy” and the “exotic” parts, both in the tritest and cheapest way you can imagine - as juicy and exotic as a tin can of sweetish synthetic drugstore tropical soda. Juvenile, shabby and – ok, you get it. 4/10

Name: Eternity Now for Men Brand: Calvin Klein Line: Men/Designer Perfumer: Ann Gottlieb Year: 2015 Sizes: 30 / 50 / 100 Gender: Men Price: 30 - 70€ Test basis: Worn for over half a day (12-11 PM) Concentration: EdT Purchase options: Douglas, Pieper, Müller, everywhere First thoughts upon hearing the name: not another Eternity ... not NOW! Bottle: simple, heavier glass than expected Sillage: very quick, very weak Longevity: very quick, very weak (4 hours max.) Comparable perfumes: Encounter (Fresh), Virgin Island Water, Marc Jacobs Men, CK One Summer '14 Seasons: Spring + Summer, almost year-round Wearing occasions: always & nowhere Dominant notes: Coconut, citrus, sugar Character: naive & youthful at first, then muted Worth the price?: not very expensive, but also not really good Fits celebrity: Justin Bieber - on the path to improvement Music style: Pop, still Optimist or pessimist: a pasted-on smile Does the name fit?: not a scent for eternity, but okay for the here & now generation Associations: kids' cocktail Fragrance color: turquoise/green/yellow Matching film: Plein Soleil meets Bugsy Malone Suitable adjectives: sweet, watery, young, spontaneous, fruity, fruity, short-lived Mainstream or special?: Mainstream, even though it has seen less original scents Sexy?: yes, for under 21s Typical CK?: oh yes, as CK as hardly anyone else... whether that is positive is up to each person to decide ;-) Conclusion: it could have been worse, it could have been worse... the beginning is really cool & fruity, the beginning is really cool & tasty... the more I tell myself this, the more it works, the truer it becomes?

Project: Eternity NOW (2015) Inspiration: “The good old Eternity. Shouldn’t we do something with that again?” - “Yeah, we need to get that stuff out of the back zone. The 90s were so awesome. I was still little back then, almost not even born, but it must have been really wild. Techno, House, Hip-hop. MTV and Viva. Not like today, where everything is so wishy-washy. Although there’s a lot of cool stuff today too...” - “Yeah.” (Excerpt from the brainstorming of the C.K. creative heads) Instruction to the perfumer: Take the old Eternity (1989). There’s really not much you need to change. Just add a bit more sugar. Hey, ginger! Starfruit is also trendy right now. Those guys at Creed did something crazy like that, a cocktail with coconut water. But you really have free rein. The rest will be taken care of by marketing. Oh, and it shouldn’t cost too much. We’re aiming for a younger target audience. However, we’d like to have a few real crowd-pleasers in there. Patchouli is a pretty cheap raw material and smells earthy. It doesn’t have to be too earthy because of the youthfulness (You understand: “Sex” without sex). Can you manage “Moroccan cedar”? I mean without REAL cedar? And Madagascar vanilla? Because that sounds really high-quality with the provenance details. The good perfume houses all do that, it’s basically standard today. And a bit of aquatic-salty-sex feeling wouldn’t be bad either. Maybe a bit more of that, you can then tone down the vanilla a bit, also smart in terms of pricing. Otherwise, as I said, you have free rein. Have fun! Desired associations (can be contradictory --> aim for a broad target audience): sweet, sweeter, youthful (sweet youthful seducer! young! vulnerable teenage macho, possibly with a guitar, blonde, maybe a few tattoos... no, actually without a guitar), cocktails (Ibiza!), sex! (see advertising campaign), cool, fresh (business people and office types like that) Fougère (we’ll write that on the sample cardboard flap, the older and very old folks will like/know that too), exotic woods (I mean: whoever doesn’t bring that is to blame themselves. There are a thousand such molecules out there. A combination of those will surely be something new). We can’t think of anything else at the moment. That’s something already. Design: Old design + something peppy added. Looks great! (--> additional tagline??) Marketing campaign: We’ll spend some money on that. Either we show a base jumper jumping off a cliff. The sexy adventure type, but you can’t see his tattoos in the suit (too little sex appeal?). Or we show a scene at the beach, a few sleepy boys and girls, naked but covering each other up (the morning after a hot outdoor summer night??), sand on the skin, dreamy melancholic girl eyes. Sounds brilliant. Or something completely different, something urban. The modern seducer in the concrete jungle...? But others have done that already... It’s really difficult to stand out from the crowd these days. We might stick to something tried and true that fits the brand and stay in our lane (Underwear). Hey, let’s just show sexy models in underwear, an erotic couple (the grown-up and adapted crazy heads of the 90s?). That will create beautiful images. Yes, immediately one should think: C.K.! You don’t really have to reinvent yourself every time. Opinion of an end consumer (fan mail, age category: 35+): Dear cool people at C.K. I’m really a huge fan of your latest men’s fragrance Eternity Now (and also your underwear *smile*). I already knew the old Eternity and liked it back in the 90s. The new one is quite similar, but seems a bit cooler to me. Also fresher and sweeter. I can’t say exactly, I’m not that familiar with perfumes. All I have are the images that arise in me. I really feel irresistible, sexy with it. I wear it all the time at the office. Unfortunately, I’ve never been approached about my new scent (which may still happen). It could be that people think, because the new cool scent is so similar to the old one, that I’m still wearing the old one and they don’t dare to mention the minimal difference (in my opinion, the new details really make the scent much better, you guys at C.K. really haven’t done anything wrong) to me. I’ve gained a lot of confidence from your perfume and I believe that I’m now much better received by women. At lunch in the cafeteria, I thought I caught a few longing glances from girls in my direction. Anyway, I have no doubt that one day I will win the hearts of women, at least I already smell good and also wear your sexy underwear. So, nothing can really go wrong *smile*. In solidarity - Now: your eternally young underbrush

I have owned "Eternity Now" since 2016, and I haven't worn it very often. But not because I think it's bad! On the contrary... This fragrance is, I believe, the only one so far with coconut as a noticeable note that doesn't annoy me! However, I think that the coconut combined with the star anise in the top notes is the reason why many associate it with a sweet "cheap scent". I find it amusing that the fragrance smells very unique precisely because of the prominent star anise; I have never smelled anything that reminds me of it. It does come across as a bit "obvious", as it smells exactly the same from the first second until the end of its perceivability, which is already there after a few hours, - but it is also not unnecessarily intrusive. (Unless you bathe in it..) Somehow, the mixture of notes, I guess through "star anise-star fruit-ginger-vanilla", creates a pseudo-orange impression for me; and I think that also triggers the "fruit candy fear reflex" in many. ;P (By the way, it's funny that there are two "star" fragrance notes in it, right? ^_^) EN didn't scare me off right away, which is why I have come to appreciate it very much, and I rise above its slightly cliché appearance. Due to its sweet-spicy-fruity nature, it fits for me almost only in the cold season, meaning when it is snowing outside like it is right now. I also find it more of a feel-good fragrance for cozy hours, not really a "party banger". If I had to look for parallels, I would first think of "Uomo Casual Life" by Salvatore Ferragamo, somehow also sweet, slightly spicy with an orange touch. (In this case, I believe it is the tiramisu-lemon-geranium mixture that creates the olfactory image of orange for me) I wouldn't say they smell super similar, but they strongly remind me of each other and somehow do a similar job for me. However, I find the underground rating for EN here a bit unfair, especially in comparison to Casual Life, which I find less exciting to smell. I also find the product advertising images very fitting for the fragrance; they convey the easy-living feeling very well that the fragrance radiates. It is more designed for young, lighthearted people rather than for super-serious tie-wearers. And when I say "young," I mean people who feel young; there is no age for me where one cannot wear something like this with dignity if they feel like it. (: I have also reflected again whether I am exaggerating.. and no. There are fragrances like Armani Code, which achieve a rating of 7.5 here, and I still put it back on the shelf after testing it for the 100th time in the store because it just smells so generic and bland. So in my opinion, an underrated fragrance that you can definitely give a chance, especially at this price, particularly if you are looking for something light-footed for winter and want a change from the really good heavy hitters like DHI, Herod, LNDL, Pure Havanne, etc. :)

During my last shopping trip, the Douglas employee handed my 7-year-old son a sample of CK Eternity Now. The little rascal of today is surely the cool guy of tomorrow :-) However, Junior's excitement didn't last long, as he had to give the sample to Dad right away - because of the alcohol content! Somehow, the sample did persuade me to invest in the 30ml bottle. In the first few days, I was quite taken with it, as CKEN noticeably starts with ginger, but then quickly transitions into a pleasant spiciness. I don't perceive the scent as sweet and fruity at all. After about 2 hours, I only smell a slightly woody vanilla. The sillage also noticeably diminishes after about 2 hours. Up close, I can still catch the remaining vanilla aroma for about 6 hours, but unfortunately, no female colleague sticks that closely to my neck. I think the scent can be worn all year round; maybe take a break in the height of summer. Leisure, work, or the mother-in-law's funeral... it works for almost any occasion. Unfortunately, the scent doesn't have the same effect on me as it does in the ads, even though I also sport a three-day beard like Tobias Sorensen. Well, my wife will probably be just fine with that. In conclusion, it's not a scent that one absolutely must own. Maybe I'll end up giving the bottle to my son after all. By the time we walk to elementary school, most of it will have evaporated anyway; but then, of course, it won't do much for the girls.

Once again - and without hope for recovery - a Klein fragrance product for men that does not deserve the name "perfume" at all. Simply annoying and unpleasant - that is really all that needs to be said about "Eternity Now". Shallow, artificially foggy wafts of plastic-like coconut milk swirl around the nose, contrasting with cheap vanilla aromas from the lab.

I almost dismissed the ladies' version of Eternity Now when the good sides of the fragrance revealed themselves. So I don't want to judge the men's version too quickly either. The first impression is somehow blurred - I can't distinguish the ingredients. After a while, I recognize coconut and ginger, which blend with star anise.

Calvin Klein has recently taken a step in a better direction in the men's fragrance sector, at least moving away from the same old blandness reloaded. Innovation might be too strong a word for it, as it lacks that final step, but the scent pyramids are not only interesting to read. The components are indeed noteworthy as well.

Does the damned gold bar even exist as a women's version? No idea.... At least this thought immediately crossed my mind when I sprayed Eternity Now on a test strip recently. Terribly sweet, terribly much chewing gum, in my opinion it comes damn close to OM, just more feminine and significantly toned down in terms of sillage and longevity.

I smelled Eternity Now for Men at my best friend's place and wow. It smells damn good. It has this sweet note, but it's not too overpowering. Even after hours, it still comes across well in the nose. So, anyone looking for something sweet and not too intrusive will find this very suitable.

The original Bottega Veneta is one of my favourite mainstream fragrances of the last years. This new, extremely light interpretation is a beautiful and aromatic mélange of fresh bergamot and coriander, subtle rose and patchouli (yes, there is such a thing as a low-key-patchouli note in this scent) resting on a base of languid tonka bean and vanilla plus a dash of sandalwood. It does disappear quickly on my skin (after 1 h), but I know it is an Eau de Cologne, so I shouldn't complain. Difficult, given the high price... No leather in this one, by the way, at least I can't smell any. I still prefer the original EdP, but if you're looking for a much lighter and more summery version of "Bottega Veneta", you might want to give "Essence Aromatique" a try. As I said before, the so-called "Essence" is so light you can drench yourself in it without annoying your colleagues. This new EdC is ideal for people of elegant calm and natural poise. Discreet and stylish.

As a child, I was allowed to look at the old photos at my grandmother's house. It was always so much fun when she took the old decorated box out of the cupboard and sat down next to me on the sofa! The photos showed my grandmother's parents and siblings, as well as my mother and her siblings as little children. The stiff figures with their serious facial expressions, dressed in clothes that I already liked so much back then, adorned with hair ribbons, hats, and fine shoes, fascinated me. There was also a wedding photo of my grandmother from the 1930s. In a dark suit with a bouquet of white flowers at the side of a handsome young man I never met - who I am told I resemble. For each picture, she told me stories. The distant figures became alive and real to me. In my imagination, they accompanied me and became my confidants. There were also a few "new photos" - in color - me as a little girl sitting on my father's shoulders, a bright blue sky, colorful flower meadows, happily laughing faces. And all of this comes to mind - I can't get it out of my head since I tested Bottega Veneta Essence Aromatique. I disregarded the saleswoman's objections that this was a scent for the warm season. Determined, I fetched the tester, as if guided by magic. This is my fragrance! How could I have grown old without it? Essence Aromatique is like a part of me - my second skin, a part of my heart, my soul. The bergamot gives a hint of freshness at the beginning. But soon the coriander appears, which I love so much, sweet-spicy - almost comfortingly beautiful. I can recognize the delicate rose and also patchouli - but this beautiful coriander note remains in the foreground for me. All the fragrance notes embrace the sweet, soft coriander. The flattering delicate woody note has captivated me. A creamy, tender fragrance clings to my wrist, climbs along my arm, wraps around my neck, my shoulders, envelops me and protects me - for a long time. The longevity is very good; even the next morning, I could still indulge in memories. I wanted the largest bottle of it immediately! The satin-finished, simple bottle in a delicate green outer box now stands here beside me. A fragrance that belongs to me, that evokes memories, which also make me nostalgic. The people in the old photos are no longer alive. But they are part of me. The habits and traits of these serious-looking people in the camera may continue to live on in me, are part of me, influencing my actions and decisions. Bottega Veneta Essence Aromatique has made me into the little girl who climbs onto a sofa, listens to her grandmother's stories, and then breathes life into the "black-and-white people" in play and dreams, embarking on journeys to the land of dreams with them.

Beautiful, stylish scent for every day and every occasion, it has real potential for THE ONE. At first sniff, it has a slight leathery-peppery note like the other fragrances in the line. I like it, but this time it fades quickly. Otherwise, it initially smells fresh and lightly citrusy like a good, rounded, by no means sharp cologne with green-spicy coriander and cardamom (?). Even though this phase is nice, I wasn't overly excited in the drugstore: This type of accord is nothing particularly special, and fragrances in this category usually fade quickly with a weak and thin, artificial white musk note or similar... However, on the way home, I smelled it again and was surprised: After a while, Essence Aromatique transforms over the bright rose into an absolutely skin/powder/light wood cuddle scent with perfectly dosed sweetness. Yet, it is zero animalistic, but soft and transparent - still not bright white, dusty-clean, or innocent, but rather casually sexy due to a spicy, slightly peppery (?) touch. Sexy in the sense of how stylish French women dress: "I don't care about fashion, I just threw something on this morning." (Of course, that's not true, but it looks fantastic precisely because of that impression.) The scent corresponds to this image following an outfit like a combination of medium blue, perfectly but casually fitting favorite jeans with a deeply unbuttoned white men's shirt and fine suede ballerinas. (I also find the barefoot on wooden floor image from my predecessor's comment very fitting.) To transfer the French concept of nonchalance to the scent: "I don't wear perfume, just a spritz of this simple cologne..." -> Subtext: "This seductive scent aura emanates from my freshly bathed body." - That's basically what a signature scent should ideally achieve. Essence Aromatique is definitely not an EDC due to its heart and base, as well as its longevity; it only plays with the concept of cologne. The surprising transformation from the unisex cologne top note to the warm skin scent, the extremely natural impression of the notes, and the resulting feminine, casual elegance drive me completely crazy. I want it! (It's spring now, after all, it's made for this... ;)

The Aromatique is aptly named, as it indeed comes across as aromatic. High quality, it clings to my skin from the very first contact and spreads a pleasant spiciness. Lightly underscored by gentle citrus notes that slowly dissipate. I really like the opening, as it brings a kick of freshness to the day. The theme here is naturally the spiciness, with a cold freshness, gentle lemon that slowly sinks into the green meadows. A wonderful scent for spring, but also for the fading summer. It fits very well on rainy days, as I have experienced and enjoyed several times. It's truly fabulous when you get a little wet, or when you open the window from a warm room and let the cool freshness in. It really invigorates the body, mind, and soul. You can really smell the scent of wet asphalt and wet wood. Yes, that excites me! The scent here prolongs the enjoyment, as it adapts very well to these circumstances. Over time, patchouli comes in subtly, but it doesn't overpower; instead, it joins the other components in a reserved manner. In the end, it becomes slightly sweet, with a pleasant powdery quality. As mentioned, the main theme, the pleasant spiciness, with the present freshness and the nice green, are always there. In short, it's described for me. A spicy, fine enjoyment. I think this scent can be seen and smelled well. The sillage is in the middle range, and the longevity for me is around 7 hours, during which it beautifully melds with the skin's surface. I am positively impressed and already looking forward to the next rain :)

Essence Aromatique - I have been circling around this scent for a long time. I keep testing it again and again - until I finally bought it yesterday. Aromatique starts fresh, like a glass of still water with the juice of a freshly squeezed lemon and a generous portion of coriander. Quite quickly, patchouli joins in and gives the fragrance a slightly balsamic incense stick touch. I find this absolutely commendable, as it makes the scent special and also has a cooling effect. It reminds me of Japanese incense sticks, which often emit a clear, spicy fragrance. Sandalwood adds depth and groundedness to the scent. The rose is not in the foreground but gives the fragrance a fine, subtle sweetness and makes it appear feminine despite the fresh-spiciness. Tonka and vanilla wrap around the entire composition like a fine web and create a powdery impression. I can relate very well to the associations below as "rainy day scent" and "black-and-white photos." Essence Aromatique gives a cozy, "arrived" feeling. I find it very special despite its simplicity and can easily imagine wearing it year-round. The sillage is in the close to medium range and fits well with the statement, the understatement of the fragrance. The longevity is good; I perceived the scent on my arm for about 7 hours. I find the bottle beautiful; the glass is velvety-fine like the scent and feels good and heavy in the hand.

Hello!? What exactly is fresh here, please? The glass bottle in hand, yes, but nothing more. Maybe it would help if I stand outside in the wind with the perfume, but I’m not in the mood for that right now. Baby, there’s powder! And I mean the full blast. The precursor to Teint de Neige. Heliotrope, buttery iris, and a hint of leather.

"I received 'Bottega Veneta Essence Aromatique | Bottega Veneta' in a collection of miniatures. Until now, I was not familiar with the scent. I briefly "sniffed" all of them and initially thought about the Bottega, "Wow, spicy," and put it back on the shelf. This spicy, warm note wouldn't leave my mind, and that day I had to keep sniffing it.

Where a school essay would have received at least a 5, Essence Aromatique gets a straight 100% from me. And this, even though the scent is absolutely not what I expected based on the name and fragrance description. I previously associated Aromatique with more herbal, woody scents like Clinique's Aromatics Elixir.

The Bible already knew this, specifically Mark 3:25. And the Venetian knickknack shop adheres to this good Italian tradition: "Essence Aromatique" cannot deny its dear relatives despite the rebellion with the French name and the frills of the satin bottle!

My first comment here. It simply has to be. (To say something about my fragrance history, I have been addicted to Chanel for about 17 years. Allure, Chance, and Coco, also No. 19 Poudre) in between a detour to Prada L'infusion d'iris (but Chanel 19 Poudre was closer to me).
Exotic sweet spicy perfume, very long lasting, modern with a cute bottle, in one word fantastic. Reminds me a bit of "let it rock" with more heavy patchouli notes. Best for cold winter time.

I agree with Grottola on Fragrantica, this is indeed an ambitious fragrance. It was also something I didn't expect. I really like the focus on dry patchouli in Jimmy Choo. It's a note that is not always popular, but has always been a hit with me. The patchouli has been complimented by sweet toffee, chocolatey orchid and an array of tropical fruits. I get the sense that perhaps Jimmy Choo is attempting to follow in Angel's footsteps, but the overall result is quite different. It's dry, spicy and foody most of the time, with the occasional hint of syrupy orange and pear. I actually like this fragrance despite it being quite strong and earthy. It's an enticing scent to say the least. I'll have to disagree that this smells like Flowerbomb. Perhaps in the drydown there's a slight resemblance, in terms of Jimmy Choo being quite musky, soft and sweet, but to my nose this fragrance smells unique. I really enjoy the dark richness that Jimmy Choo conveys. It lasts an incredibly long time and it projects extremely well. All in all, Jimmy Choo smells good to me, but for some it may be too masculine, earthy or too heavy.

Another rather expensive scent whose name conjures up images of lots of pretty shoes and a "Sex and the City" walk-in wardrobe. It was a gift, and I am glad I didn't pay for it: here is why. To my nose it's 'nice'. Not earth-shattering, unusual or sexy. No, just 'nice'. Now don't get me wrong! I like and use 'nice'! The problem is I have lots of 'nice' scents that are cheaper...and perhaps even 'nicer'...? The opening is pure toffee with patchouli and a hint of pear. The longer it's on my skin the more toffee-ish it gets. One could say it's too sweet or too gourmand. Or one could love it. I think it's just 'nice'. I will wear it but I wont buy it myself. Too many other scents are on my 'want' list that are begging for me to own them! ; ) Silage is: "I smell like patchouli smoked toffee!" -- Longevity is: "I am a blast of toffee and after about an hour I become a close to the skin powdery pear scent....fading into the distance". Sniff before purchase! And on the skin if you can. This one costs enough and should be really liked! Good luck.

This is called a "fruity chypre" or a "fruitchouli", but to me the patchouli note contained in "Jimmy Choo" smells boring, artificial and chemical. Other releases of the last years ("Oriens" by Van Cleef & Arpels or "Sensuous" by Estee Lauder for that matter) were constructed in the same way, a strong, artificial woody base with overtones of toffee and sandalwood plus patchouli, resulting in very strong, tenacious scents which I find head-ache inducing. "Jimmy Choo" comes in a beautiful perfume vessel, though. Obviously, the big companies think today's clients have better eyes than noses.

I love this smell). It reminds me of designer shoes somehow. It is when something is special but you can't say what exactly is special there. The shoes are shoes but they do have some edge or something which makes them different.) Smell wise Jimmy Choo is like bubblegum to me. The smell is divine on my skin. I remember walking into the lift in the office one day and a total stranger telling me: "Wow! You smell gorgeous." I do know that the smell is different on different people but it does suit me and at the same time I know it will not be the same for everyone. I think it's not only the chemistry between your skin and the perfume, it is also about the perfume's and your personality. You just need to connect on some deeper level. When I want to lift my mood I just take a bottle and smell it.) I don't consider this perfume classic or luxurious but I do love it a lot. It's just special for me.)

It was started in Eva (Ukrainian cosmetic store) last autumn, where I smelled some samples. I liked this one and I bought it later from my first salary. For the first time it was so heavy for me. It starts with patchouli and then there goes sweet, but light pear. It has a bit toffee, but not too much like caramel, which I hate

After a fruity opening of a few minutes, with the entrance of toffee and patchouli, Jimmy Choo did make think of Van Cleef & Arpels Oriens. While I was not very fond of the floured raspberry in Oriens, Jimmy Choo's pear and mandarin manage to show a more juicy aspect. Then the fragrance evolves into its own path.
Sophisticated sweetness of the finest grade, super feminine in a very delicate way. So perfect with silky lingerie and silky bed sheets. It carries a strong romantic vibe. Just lovely.

Alas, I was certain I would love this perfume. I spend a lot of time reading reviews, researching the notes and comparing it to perfumes that I've tried before. I convinced myself that I was going to love this perfume for its sweet juicy pear, the exotic orchid and the sweet toffee. On top of that, there are many raving reviews for Jimmy Choo to be found.

After the entire Euphoria family has taken up residence with me, I couldn't just pass by the latest offspring indifferently. My girlfriend was already restlessly shifting from one foot to the other, as we had already gone through a perfume sample. I had also extensively browsed through books, and one should not overstrain the patience of innocent companions. "Endless," she sighed with a meaningful glance. But the first summery spray of bergamot, mandarin, and cherry blossom was a blessing against the inhospitable winter cold. I would have liked to warm my hands with it. Sweet rose and lovely violet floated comfortingly into my cold nose. Musk and bamboo transported me to far eastern realms, where the sun surely shines gently in the sky. The whole scene is bathed in a pale pink. Quickly whipped out the Visa card and Endless was mine. I hurried through the sleet, drawing strength from my wrist again and again. But the sunbeams I had captured on my hand faded increasingly. Moment, please stay a while - I thought like Faust once did, but Endless did not live up to its name. Already in the cold car, the pink sun had set on my skin. A beautiful scent, without question, but it calls for re-spraying.

I was in our small branch of the perfumery with personality, as I wanted to buy a complementary product of my girlfriend's favorite scent for her birthday. After the "Piepearl" informed me about shower gel and body lotion (but currently not available in the store), I had her spray Endless Euphoria on me. The scent is fresh, slightly juicy, floral, and sweet. For me, the first impression was a bit too sweet. Maybe the sweetness will lessen or completely dissipate, I thought to myself, but as I left the store with a "Yes, this is a light scent and goodbye!" I was surprised. Endless Euphoria had evaporated from my wrist. I smelled my wrist again more intently, but the scent was simply gone! Of all the "Euphorias" I have known so far, this new release is a big disappointment for me, and 48 euros (40 ml) is a lot of money for a scent that disappears so quickly after spraying!

I do not like Ur-Euphoria... I don't like it at all! It smells so out of place on me, way too old and burdensome. Endless Euphoria has nothing to do with its oppressive mother! I could never put it in a box. The scent starts softly citrusy, giving everything a refreshing opening and a longing for warm sun rays. The cherry blossom (thankfully it stays with me until the end) immediately catches my attention; somehow I associate the scent of cherry blossom with the scent of body lotion :D and so I get the feeling that I am lying fresh and creamed on a lounger in the garden after a refreshing shower. Dreamy! The rose and violet of the heart note soon join in, and I can almost hear a few little birds chirping, although I do not find the heart note particularly dominant. The musk and sandalwood round everything off beautifully warm, like warming sun rays on the skin. Bamboo saves it from becoming a cuddly scent and reminds me of the fresh green joy of summer. Conclusion: On me, the scent lasts an average of about 5 hours, which is just okay for the price. It does not have a killer sillage, more of a pleasant "mediocre," but who wants to wear a heavy scent in spring and summer? Even those who do not like Ur-Euphoria should definitely give this one a try! :) It has to move in with me!

my favorite scent in my youth was Euphoria, but over the years I unfortunately got tired of it. Now, after all these years, I saw the new variant, Endless Euphoria. A beautiful bottle, in lovely pastel colors, it practically screams spring. The scent starts off super fruity, I can clearly smell mandarin, followed by cherry blossom. Then it gets warmer right away, the fruitiness blends with musk and fine woods, and the scent of violet comes in. A dreamy fragrance. Very feminine, very fruity, but not overpowering, not to be compared with, for example, La vie est Belle. The longevity is very good, a few spritzes are enough for the day. I will definitely repurchase this scent, it will become my new daytime fragrance along with Lady Million.

The bottle is as usual, handy, beautifully shaped, and present. It starts with sweet pink roses and a hint of mandarin, while the bergamot doesn’t make an appearance for me. The cherry blossom and violets are briefly detectable. It remains pink and rosy. I was really looking forward to the base note, but the scent hardly changes on me.

With this fragrance, I initially only perceive cherry blossom. Then lilac and rose gradually join in, without the scent coming across as old and dusty. The rose remains more in the background. The fragrance lasts about 2 to 3 hours. After that, the fresh bamboo comes through. It is mainly this that I can perceive, albeit very subtly and close to the skin, until the evening.

~ Inspiration ~ Last year I already tested "Euphoria" and was now curious about the new "Endless Euphoria" (I still miss the "Blossom" version!) ~ Bottle ~ You can tell by the half-round, curved shape that it belongs to the "Euphoria" family.

As a former lover of the original Euphoria (now it feels a bit too old and musty for me), I stumbled upon "Endless Euphoria" during a sale at the red centaur. Quickly Googled the fragrance pyramid, found it pleasant, pulled out a gift voucher, and along with diapers and burp cloths, the well-scented piece hopped into my shopping basket.

One of the things I like about the Jimmy Choo fragrances is the fruit notes are very realistic on me. The peach note is gorgeous. It's very fresh, not jammy or overripe. The mandarin brings a bit of sourness, preventing the opening from being cloying, but this is a very sweet fragrance. I like the jasmine, but what I really like is how noticeable the lily is in this fragrance. On me, lily often gets drowned out by other floral or fruity notes. The peach note remains throughout the life of the fragrance, which is substantial- over 12 hours in cool, dry weather. This isn't a completely linear fragrance on me, in spite of how long the peach note lasts. The drydown is very pretty. I love the balsamic note. The peach/vanilla combo is very gourmand, although I wouldn't class this fragrance as a gourmand. I do think it would appeal to folks who like gourmands. I think this has the advantage of being a vanilla (gourmand-ish) scent that is lovely in the heat, albeit with minimal sprays because projection and sillage are *strong*, and it will also work as a floral scent in cold weather. IWC is appropriate for a lot of different occasions and for anyone who likes feminine-leaning (IMO) fragrances, aged 12-102.

So I just recently got into fragrances. I have been a body mist and matching lotion type of girl for a long time. You know going into Victoria's Secret's Pink and getting the body spray and matching lotion that lasts 10 minutes lol But I decided about a month ago that I wanted to start investing some money into things that would last me longer. Unfortunately I have learned that the scents that I prefer are scents that usually don't last quite as long and need to be reapplied throughout the day, which was kinda sad because I was trying to get away from that. So I went into Macy's and told the lady that was there what I like and that I wanted to get away from my normal go to vanillas and I also told her that I'm not a big floral person and she had me test a few and this is the one that I left with. I was really surprised to see the floral notes in it because I was convinced that floral in anything would be a no for me but I'm very happy that I went to somebody who kind of knew what she was talking about because this is my number one right now My husband will not stay off of me when I have this on! He definitely gives this a 10 out of 10 I give it an eight or nine out of 10! And it is lasting on me all day! Not to mention he can actually smell me when I walk by him which is something that none of my other perfumes have done I can't really tell you what I smell from it because again I'm still new and I'm still learning how to pick up what is what in a perfume but I can tell you it is sweet and it is fruity and I love my body sprays to be fruity so it makes sense that this is something that I would go for

Reminiscent of 1990’s perfumes, I Want Choo is extremely potent with a very far reach. It’s a floral perfume, but honestly it’s so strong that I can’t decipher specific notes. I only sprayed it once and I was dying to remove it immediately, however, I gave it another two hours to give it time to meld with me. Nothing changed. It didn’t change on my arm and my feelings about it were the same, so I washed it off. It had second thoughts about me and lingered on my skin a good six hours after I washed it off. The longevity is both historic and horrific—great for those who love it, but bad for those who don’t. I just wish I liked it. I won’t be buying this bottle, and am happy I tested it first, because it sure has a lot of hype.

This is strong and long lasting. I had tried it a couple of times in Sephora and liked it and finally decided to go for it when I found a huge 4 ounce bottle for an absolute steal. When first sprayed, this is a soft floral, creamy clean peachy vanilla without being juvenile or too sweet. It’s somewhat generic in that it shares the same jasmine vanilla combo so many fragrances have had over the last ten years. Very much a product of its time. And I do not fault it for that! This is a period piece and that’s totally okay. However, because the longevity is so good, after a while it starts to morph into this vague heavy smell that starts to make me nauseous. I think this is where most perfumes would simply disappear but this one just marches on. Once all of the top and middle notes fade, the remaining lingering vanilla is persistent and smells like an old used candle on my skin. I couldn’t figure out why this was happening and realized I had been sampling it in the winter when I liked it, and now it is hot and humid and I am not liking it as much. This does not agree with thick humid air. I am saving my bottle to bring back out after it gets cold again. Hopefully I fall back in love with it.

The clerk at the perfume shop really raved about this one and sprayed some on my wrist. At first, on the blotter, I thought I liked this; fresh and very shampoo-y, with a hint of peaches. But it developed REALLY strong and it didn’t come off despite how many times I washed my hands. The overwhelmingly clean accords sharply pierced my nose and I couldn’t get over how much it disturbed my other senses when eating or drinking. Very perfume-y. Objectively it is a good scent, but very strong and long-lasting, not to mention synthetic and overwhelming. Not something I would like to put on my skin.

I Want Choo is such an easy, feminine scent. The juicy peach, soft jasmine, and smooth vanilla create something simple but stunning. It may not be groundbreaking, but it’s effortlessly beautiful and works for any time or occasion! Definitely signature-worthy. Someone said its mature, but I disagree )

I Want Choo opens up with its fruity notes out, the peach is the stronger of the two, but you will get a dash of the mandarin juice. But, the fruits up top aren’t really allowed to truly express their full juiciness, as the middle floral notes and the resinous vanilla qualities from the base are there early too. It’s got a sparkling fruitiness to it instead.

It smells nice but I don't love it, it lacks that something. The bottle is nice. It's a sweet perfume but not annoyingly sweet; it's moderate. It's feminine. Being sweet, I recommend it in the cold season, at any time of the day. It seems a bit expensive to me. I had higher expectations from this perfume.

Curiously, I accepted the I want Choo sample, as I am on familiar terms with Choo. The appealing fragrances from this label have always scored points with me. Pleasant mainstream scents - but always with that "certain something." Imaginative fragrances - without imaginative prices. And the wait for I want Choo was worth it.

Since this fragrance hasn't received much attention so far, I’ll just write a few lines. Maybe I can spark a little curiosity. The scent convinced me right away: "You need me in spring!" Normally, I always struggle to find a new beautiful spring fragrance after my beloved winter scents (not that I really need one : )).

Velvet that falls on the skin like snowflakes and warms your soul ... that is Bottega Veneta Eau de Velours! Actually, this is not my usual type. Rose is tricky, especially in combination with patchouli. I didn't like unsweet scents at all until recently, but this fragrance has stuck with me after the test. So I told myself, Sweetsmell ... out of the usual type and into the fragrance cabinet with the bottle! I haven't regretted it ;) About the scent: Eau de Velours starts off peppery with citrus notes. But before you can even say bergamot, the rose comes in. This rose is even beautiful to me. It is interspersed with plum sprinkles and underscored with jasmine. It becomes slightly spicy as it develops. However, my nose struggles to identify which spices are present. The base features soft leather and a lot of patchouli. Musk also joins in. Although it's not listed, I can smell it. It gives the fragrance a cozy-warm atmosphere. Eau de Velours wears like velvet on the skin and is absolutely unsweet! A fragrance for autumn/winter and the cooler spring days. The longevity is a good 8 hours plus, and the sillage is not overwhelming but well noticeable for the first few hours; after that, I am subtly enveloped in a rosy patchouli-musk cloud. I find Eau de Velours to be very effective - stylish - feminine! The bottle is very pretty and high-quality with its leather ribbon. The bottle color matches the fragrance. Conclusion: Noble leather, patch & a red rose - velvety soft with plum sprinkles. Subtle - unsweet - effective! Velvet Water fits ... nicely so :) Girls ... you really have to test this one ... it's so beautiful! :)

Welcome to Casa Bottega Veneta! It's a pleasure to have you here as a guest today. Allow me to introduce: the lady of the house "Bottega Veneta EDP", very feminine, gentle, yet assertive. At the core of her heart, she still holds on to the old values. The stern gentleman beside her is, by the way, her husband, "Bottega Veneta Pour Homme". A truly striking character, elegant and strong-willed. The slender lady to her left is her sister, the "EDT". Yes, the family resemblance is immediately apparent, even though the sister is a bit lighter and cooler. Across from them sits the French cousin "Essence Aromatique". Admittedly, there is no obvious similarity, but the same stunningly charming style. I personally prefer to avoid the English cousin "Knot" over there. She only talks about her flower and fruit garden. Exhausting, I tell you. And the daughter, the "Eau Floral" next to her, is similarly inclined, just much more boring. Here in front is my little sister, the "Eau Sensuelle". She is still a bit reserved, but very nice in closer company. And you can immediately see the resemblance to the lady of the house. Yes, after all, she is the mother. By the way, I am "Eau de Velours", Mama's eldest - even though I arrived last at the celebration today. Don't you think I look just like her? I'm proud of that. But as much as I love my family: I am very independent and definitely have my own mind. ... I must admit, I find it difficult to view "Eau de Velours" independently from the other fragrances in the line. I believe no other perfume series has managed to captivate me as much as this one. "Eau de Velours" is no exception. The fine leather note that runs through the series (with the exception of the outside cousins) also intrigues me here. The subtle sweetness is just my thing. This fragrance is very similar in warmth and radiance to the "EDP", but has a slightly different character. While the "EDP" offers an elegant, very mature note with oak moss in the base in fine dosage, "Eau de Velours" is more feminine and sensual due to the rose scent. However, the rose remains part of the ensemble and does not become an overpowering soloist. For me, each family member has its reason for existence, but if I had to choose, I would remain loyal to the Grand Dame. So I am pleased to have already received the second sample bottle this year.

Recently, I was once again at one of my doctors on the upper Kurfürstendamm. There, in the area of Olivaer Platz, boutiques - or are they called "flagstores" now? - have settled over the years, where the mere mention of their names should ideally elicit a delighted "Oh!" or "Ah!". With a bit of luck, you might still find showcases right in the middle of the wide sidewalks. As always, I was early, so I took a look at the shop windows and these showcases. "Hermès", known for its beautiful scarves, still had those foulards displayed, whose colors are so loud that just looking at them makes my ears ring! In three showcases, there are only six large silk scarves stretched out: their theme apparently lies in the realm of "Back to the Roots" or "Back to Nature". The patterns on the heavy silk are partly in an orange that currently makes the suits of the Dutch Olympic team shine. The blue is shockingly shrill; the green as well. Sapphire and emerald, on the other hand, appear almost colorless. Who would want to buy that? In any case, this sight reminds me of a colleague who wore new clothes for the first time so skillfully that the label with the price tag was visible. She had a talent for that! When she was pointed out to this fact, she acted surprised and slightly embarrassed ("Oh, how embarrassing!"); but never forgot to say: "Not from 'C&A', my dear - only the finest!". Well, these foulards don't offer the possibility of a forgotten price tag; but maybe there's a special way of tying that reveals the logo or lettering of these luxury brands. Each of the three adjacent showcases is more minimalist: each glass display holds only one handbag: one more beautiful than the other! These showcases belong to "Bottega Veneta". Handbags in a leather that seems so finely polished, as if it were pure silk velvet, with that very specific shimmer! The question remains: is it matte smooth leather or very fine suede? In one of these "non-colors" for handbags: a very light milk coffee brown with a hint of gray - "Greige" is what it's called, to my knowledge. A "non-color" that harmonizes so ideally with the eagerly awaited spring and the matching clothing. The first yellow crocuses on the wide median strip nod approvingly. Here I stand now - a single woman between three handbags and ask myself the question of all questions: Which bag would/should/could it be? If I hadn't had the doctor's appointment, I would probably still be standing there: I couldn't decide! However, the decision for "Bottega Veneta - Eau de Velours" comes easily! There is no doubt: we both like each other at first sight! For this fine scent mist is spun from such noble leather nuances that even I immediately sink into a state of slight ecstasy: it is well known that leather scents are not exactly among my favorites. This "Eau de Velours" is, however, the famous exception to the rule. The sometimes slightly musty bergamot is here dusted with a bit of pink pepper; so fine that even my nose couldn't be bothered by it. Spiced ripe plum, a deep dark violet accord, next enters this scent stage. Spicy clove is likely in its company, possibly even a little pinch of cinnamon. Whatever it is - it creates a certain enticing tickle of the olfactory nerves on the fine leather with the fruity, slightly peppery note! The fully bloomed large-flowered jasmine and an extremely skillfully placed dose of rose absolute (perhaps from Rosa Alba?) refine the previous scent composition to perfection. Even now, it is such a temptation for me that I would prefer not to take my nose away from my wrist and elbow. For a mysterious being has settled there. The moment this fragrant something marries with patchouli, "Bottega Veneta - Eau de Velours" is perfectly rounded off. And I gladly forget the shock that Tom Ford's "White Patchouli" recently gave me. Rounded off? Rather, the delicate scent progression takes the shape of an eight - a certain infinity. The longevity is, of course, not infinite; it is, after all, an eau de toilette, despite the noble name. It departs lightly and quietly after a few hours, leaving a fine hint that responds absolutely friendly to re-spraying: it rises again without complaining or being fussy - a well-behaved being! "Bottega Veneta - Eau de Velours" is an ideal scent for occasions when one prefers not to stand out, but still leaves their "scent mark" in the most impressive way: "... what here!" Thus, it presents itself as a practical yet elegant business scent. It has a certain elegance; yet it is so considerate that even I feel comfortable with this fragrant companion at the moment; disheveled and run over as I currently look and actually feel. For that reason alone, I like this "Eau de Velours": it tenderly caresses with fairy fingers without being intrusive; flatters its wearer and reminds one of a soft piece of music that is present but not disturbing. You can tell: I want to slip into this scent like into a soft, delicately perfumed glove! Maybe not forever - but for a certain time!

Last night, my girlfriend threw me out of bed because she has worries. Yes, at night, dark thoughts plague you the most. So I prepare myself for Rembrandt's Night Watch - because friendship is not just about laughing together - but also about watching over each other. But I have no gun ready - instead, I have muffins, cigarettes, and Eau de Velours. Although I am crouching on a hard kitchen bench, the scent transports me to a soft suede armchair - comfortable and therapeutic. Well - where does it pinch? The pink and white rose bouquet smells even more intense at night and lets thoughts flow. I recall many pieces of advice. The soft patchouli provides depth - and the plum is comforting, plum-soft. I can listen attentively and empathize. Velours creates closeness - and the ability to engage. We both found some sleep after all.

I am totally into leather fragrances and have several in my collection. One of my favorites is the original Bottega Bottega Veneta Eau de Parfum . I had heard about Bottega Veneta Eau de Velours , which is said to be even softer and more supple. So I tried to get a sample of it, which I ultimately succeeded in doing. What can I say, it is a Bordeaux Red Velvet Dream. An incredibly beautiful suede leather scent. Such a wonderfully creamy, finely suede-like skin and soul caresser. It starts immediately with a dreamy leather note and a light pepper note that is absolutely unobtrusive but quite noticeable, with a delicate hint of something citrusy that hardly makes an impact. Right with the top note, the heart note comes in with a dry, unsweetened plum-spice drink and a lush bouquet of dreamy dark red roses and small, delicate jasmine flowers. The flowers are not overpowering, the rose is not overwhelming but accompanies this wonderful composition. Almost immediately after, I am in the seventh "leather" heaven. I have never smelled such a soft, delicate suede in a fragrance before. It is a dream, silky, soft, creamy, powdery, slightly roughened but not harsh, rather like a well-worn, cared-for suede skirt. It clings so velvety, eventually becoming skin-close and caressing my soul.
