The combination of unsweetened fruit, jasmine, and rose with leather and patchouli is absolutely brilliantly executed and completely harmonious. Surely this fragrance won't appeal to every woman; it is not sweet, it is not pleasing, it has edges and corners and is precise. For me, this is a great office scent. It radiates strength, self-confidence, and assertiveness without ever being intrusive or commanding. I like it almost even better than the original Bottega. The big problem - it has been discontinued... It's not like I didn't know that beforehand, but I didn't realize I would like it so much. Good thing I was able to snag a bottle. ❤️ I generally like the Bottega bottles quite a bit, and this one is a little dream. Not just the bottle, but also the velvet liquid.
I have tested this fragrance repeatedly for some time now, and as so often before, I found it to be biting, annoying, and intrusive upon first spray, yet still possessing a certain something.

Oh, the bottle is so pretty, trendy, merlot-plum colored - shifting Bordeaux, a little ribbon around the slender neck... you’re flirting with me too enticingly... bought in a weak moment of that I-must-reward-myself feeling, because the scent, well, it really does, it comforts so beautifully...

I personally find leather-like scents often a bit challenging, but this one almost hugs the skin. The rose note is very delicate, truly pleasantly floral and clean. However, it does not come across as too artificial. Jasmine rounds it off a bit and is only subtly integrated.

…and I do. I discovered you around the time I started to become more interested in floral-fresh scents, rather than just sweet gourmands. With you, it was clear right away, you are “one of those”. One from that category that has appealed to me much more over the past 3-4 years. But You don’t always make it easy for me. Especially the wonderful qualities that define you, this zesty freshness from the quince and the spring-like floral notes of the peach blossom - and in an outstanding intensity, which I find unusual for comparable fragrances - sometimes give me headaches :( You smell like a floral deodorant, just a bit more complex, which I find incredibly appealing. If you were just a little less assertive, you would simply be a dream.

For just over a year, eternity now has been gracing the shelf with my perfume collection. There's hardly anything missing, I've only used it very sparingly from time to time. I liked it enough to buy it, but not so much that I wanted to use it more often. Until yesterday. Why save it, there are countless perfumes, so I sprayed it on generously, neck, hair, sweater left and right, yes... you can really notice it now. I drive off, pick up my son from school, we have lunch, I take the laundry off the line, hang up new ones, load the dishwasher, and suddenly I feel a sense of unease. I drink a glass of water and continue. But I feel strange, I get slight headaches, and I have to sit down for a moment. I feel extremely uncomfortable, no nausea. A tightness when breathing. And suddenly a thought shoots through my mind like lightning... it’s this scent that I’m inhaling constantly, I ponder back and forth whether this could be possible, I google a bit, and indeed find reports from people who react to certain scents with headaches, even migraines, discomfort, or even nausea. I immediately change my clothes and treat my neck with a washcloth and soap. Not even 10 minutes later, I feel better, the feeling of unease is gone. Thank goodness. Later, I smell the sprayed sweater again. Pungent, stinging, almost repulsive. It goes into the laundry, and I read more experiences online about perfume intolerance. I had used it a few times before, but more subtly. At my later appointment, I catch whiffs of eternity now here and there. I am disgusted and glad that my appointment is over and I can FINALLY take a long shower. I don’t think I will ever wear eternity now again.

Today I couldn't get out of bed - and only when my little dog was tapping his paw on my face in the late morning did I get up, tired and grumpy. While rummaging in the kitchen, I came across the Eternity Now sample that was given to me at the fair. I didn't find it that impressive there, and had carelessly placed it on the table. Today I sprayed it again - without high expectations - and was surprised by its invigorating freshness. The zesty opening of lychee and quince sorbet is a real wake-up call. Only now did I become aware of the delicious quinces. Peony and neroli create a floral - cool blend that relaxes the nerves. Cashmere softly rounds off Now. A fragrance that gently guides me into the here and now. I admit, I initially underestimated Now and almost set it aside. But it truly brings light to the gloomy rainy day and gives me a boost. Exactly what I needed today.

With my last order, I received a sample of Eternity Now. Samples are always nice, but my enthusiasm for Calvin Klein is still limited... I don't know any truly innovative or special fragrance from Calvin Klein; everything is so unremarkable, and Eternity Now is no different. At first, the lychee note is the most prominent. So far, so nice. But just nice... After the lychee, you really have to make an effort to catch anything else in the development. This is not due to the complexity of the fragrance but rather to the sillage and longevity. These are practically nonexistent. The only thing I can still smell is a hint of peony. I must honestly say that it is really disappointing when after about 20 minutes you can hardly smell anything anymore (and 20 minutes is a generous estimate)... Above all, it reminds me of a perfume I had as a child. I'm pretty sure it was by Malizia. And I'm also quite sure that my childhood perfume lasted significantly longer! If you're looking for something inconspicuous and nothing really special, then Eternity Now is just right for you. It's nice, but nothing more... I apologize in advance to the lovers of this fragrance! But I couldn't write anything nicer.

While transferring at Dubai Airport, I saw the advertisement for the new Estee Lauder fragrance for the first time, a huge poster featuring a brunette beauty with a tropical flower in her hair. The name caught my attention: “Adventurous=adventurous,” as I was on my way to an adventure (traveling through India and Sri Lanka) along with the note “travel exclusive.” The marketing team at Estee Lauder did a great job; I absolutely needed this fragrance. Unfortunately, time was quite tight, and I couldn't test it, so I quickly bought the perfume. At the first opportunity, dinner at the hotel, I used it immediately. Now it smells a little fresh at first, then very floral, later warm and woody. The “red berries,” which are currently so popular and almost never left out of mainstream women’s fragrances, are not found here. I do perceive a sweet note, but it is not fruity; rather, it is initially floral. Lotus and frangipani with a hint of jasmine, gentle, not piercing, and well-balanced. Then the scent becomes warmer, softer, and I smell the sweet notes of caramel and honey, with jasmine still clearly recognizable among the floral notes, and then the woody base note comes into play. Vetiver also plays a subtle role in the base note. Now the scent is no longer so floral-fresh; instead, it has transformed into a sweet fragrance. The longevity is unfortunately not very impressive; after a few hours, everything has faded, and you need to reapply. A light, unobtrusive gourmand scent with floral notes, sweet but not fruity-sweet, and soft, warm woody notes in the background. Not necessarily a “must-have,” but quite nice and suitable for everyday wear. The scent is certainly not an adventure, as it simply lacks the “special” quality in my eyes. Estee Lauder didn't take many risks here but rather oriented itself towards a large customer base.

Dior Homme Cologne is quite possibly my favorite fragrance, period. My one and only problem with it? it's expensive and has terrible performance. I, like many others, figured that the solution to this was to buy a clone that I could spray as much as I wanted, because its inexpensive. I have had my bottle of Man Ice for about 10 days now, and while Man Ice smelt good, DHC (at least the 2022 version onwards, which I smell every time I go to a store) just smelt stronger and more powerful. the citrus felt sharper and more present, it smelt cooler and crisper, and overall was just more potent. I have noticed my Man Ice starting to smell closer over the 10 days since I first sprayed it, and in the air I'm sure they smell basically the same, I cant help but notice the difference, and if people describe DHC as a glass of freshly poured cold lemonade, this is the same lemonade after 20-30 minutes when the ice has melted. its still cold, but its watered down and dilluted. On top of that, the biggest problem DHC has, its performance, is even worse with Man Ice. I swear this thing is gone in 20 minutes and basically just a skin scent. While the value for a 200ml bottle is great and costs like 60USD after tax and shipping on jomashop, I still dont want to need to reapply after every hour just for someone to actually smell it on me without needing to press themselves against my skin or shirt. for what its worth, in nearly every other metric this fragrance is awesome. The packaging was nice, the bottle was great, it feels premium, the atomizer is one of the best I've ever seen, but unfortunately it doesn't solve the main issue I would buy this clone over the original for, which is the same smell for cheaper, or close to it but way better performance. There are some clones that are so good you no longer feel any need to own the original (CDN Sillage or CDN Milestone for example), and while I don't regret this purchase at all, I still think I am just going to get myself the real thing for Christmas, wear that when I leave the house, and use this one for supplemental sprays throughout the day. Its not bad in any way, I never felt like it did anything wrong, but if you want to buy this as a cheaper alternative to DHC like I did, I'd still just buy the real thing.

Amazing Fragrance ! Uplifting, Airy, Elegant, Clean and Fresh. Its Opening is similar to Dior Homme Cologne but dry down is not the same. It smells so good and very pleasant with reasonable price. It opens up with like fresh citrusy and green notes in the background then dry down is creamy musky woody. This is perfect for the spring and summer. I really enjoy it and I like Jimmy Choo Man Ice EDT. The art of bottle design is very cool, It has frosted glass with white cap. Longevity is good. Highly Recommended. Thumbs Up. Rating : 8 / 10

I love dior homme cologne bcs its very refreshing and quite uniqe there is nothing like it, i didnt know if it really smeled like a fresh lemonade or if its just another citrus fragrance but it indeed was a lemonade scent. The problem was the price... i loved it but didnt want to spend 120+ on a bottle and thats where i found jimmy choo man ice. At first i didnt think it would be similar since the notes arent and some say its not but i was positivly suprised! it really is similar, the dior homme is maybe a tiny bit better but this is super close and hard to smell the difference so if u are looking for somethig like dior homme cologne which many say lemonade in a bottle this is it on a budget!

One of the coolest bottles in my collection and smells like advertised- a icey version of jimmy Choo man. I will say tho, as much as i enjoy the scent it VANISHES from my skin in about an hour. love the smell but will never buy another bottle due to that unacceptable performance, even for such a good price.

Today I was looking for a fragrance for my friend, who works with many clients. So nothing intrusive - and also not too rugged. That's just not his type. He is the kind of sensitive biker. I think I've found it with Man Ice. The scent is citrusy - but not sour. A refreshing coolness envelops me, which I find very pleasant. Mint hovers above it, which cools - but does not feel frosty. In the hustle and bustle of the day, one can certainly handle a bit of coolness. Slightly woody notes are cushioned by soft moss - and vetiver blends in gently sweet. An unremarkable beautiful scent that subtly but skillfully showcases its ingredients. Moreover, it is transparent and stays close to the skin. Despite its clarity and lightness, it proves to be long-lasting on me. I perceive it as unisex, as it is adaptable. I also have it on my radar for myself.

I was so excited when I first tested it at Müller... Jimmy Choo Man Ice how shocking the result is, follows now in my first comment on this fragrance. Right after the first spray, it immediately reminded me of my beloved Dior Homme Cologne 2013. Quite simple, fresh, citrusy - the perfect summer fragrance indeed.
When I think of Ice, I primarily think of fresh, minty, and citrusy aquatics.

I must confess that there isn't much to say about this scent! But it does what it was created for. It smells fresh, lemony, minty, and slightly sweet. Not a complex fragrance, nothing that blows you away, but this is exactly what makes it rather likable for me; it smells neither cheap nor overwhelming, it's just there and smells high-quality fresh.

I would say it’s a great body spray for summer. Perfect for beach days or at the pool! For the price, you can easily use a 5ml spray bottle in one day without feeling guilty :D The scent lasts on my skin better than on clothing! Unfortunately, I can’t perceive the scent on my clothes after 15 minutes at all.

(From a woman's perspective, I can say: On a man, this scent would be absolutely fantastic, so the review is for men) I was recently out and about in the city and, as often, strolled into a fragrance store. Without any great expectations, I sniffed through a few perfumes until I suddenly came across a scent that really surprised me.

Truth for Men is one of the nicest green aromatic scents around. Because it is so likable, I will not hesitate to place this fragrance into a unisex category. This fragrance opens with clean and crisp 'metallic greens', with a subtle hint of pepper. The scent is rather fresh, although not overly Summery or too watery, it has substance. Surprisingly this fragrance strikes me as being very natural, like the scent of grass on the floor of a forest and a man that has showered with spicy soap. Truth for Men is almost luscious and smooth. It's not what I'd call particularly sexy, however on a man, it's very approachable. Through discovering this fragrance, I've realised that green scents work way better on men. Those grassy and earthy notes could suit practically any man, despite his personality, style or age. The lasting strength of Truth for Men is great, as is the sillage, although not powerful, has a great projection. In my opinion this is the perfect choice for a man seeking a naturalistic, clean fragrance at a reasonable price.

Tropical rainforests worldwide are pretty diverse but share several defining characteristics, including climate, precipitation, canopy structure, complex symbiotic relationships, and species diversity. An essential aspect of rainforests is apparent in their name. Rainforests lie in the intertropical convergence zone, where intense solar energy produces a convection zone of rising air that loses its moisture through frequent rainstorms. Rainforests are subject to heavy rainfall. Even in seasonal forests, the period between rains is usually not long enough for the leaf litter to dry out completely. During the parts of the year, when less rain falls, the constant cloud cover is enough to keep the air moist and prevent plants from drying out. I can't help but relate this smell to the air after a rainfall. There's a powerful ozonic effect that smells like rain, waterfalls, and rainforest. This is my second bottle. I bought the former when the cologne was released and the current one a few years ago. It is fresh and uplifting, teal and modern, not including ambroxan. It's a simple, linear perfume, which is highly pleasant if you look for a lighter scent. Also, something unique. Nothing else in the world can be like this. At least I haven't run into a similar fragrance yet. Compared to the other CK fragrances, Truth is closer to CK One Eau de Toilette and far from Obsession for Men Eau de Toilette and stands out as a less sweet, more refined smell than CK's other offerings. There is also a smell to Truth Eau de Parfum for Women, but it's more of a lush meadow with some flowers. Truth unfurls greenish, refreshing, and aqueous, like wet fern after a storm, bamboo core, or cut grass with a minty accent. The initial blast is terrific, and I think the juice's colour is just right, a pale green. We are facing a contemporary fougère, very green, luxuriant. Those first breezes of late summer mornings, those first rains of spring evoke a sense of melancholy. The opening comprises aromatic notes of stunning tea leaves, the slightly minty cardamom, and tons of crispy green foliage. It's so fresh and rainy with hints of sourness, yet no citrus or zesty nuance. Green, very green and moist, a very intense and pleasant aroma that grows and softens a bit, leaving room in the heart for a charming smooth combo of herbs and grass. The soft warmth of the cardamom softens the aromatic basil, and these two notes blend with the indolic light and sweet jasmine. I get wet fern leaves wrapped in some resins. Imagine walking into the greenest forest you can think of after a few days of thunderstorms, and then the scorching sun comes out, and it's high at noon, eagerly searching for every drop of moisture on every piece of green foliage. The dry-down ends with a mild muskiness and reminds me of the lush vegetation of tropical forests in the morning after a nightly rain, damp earth, sandalwood vapour mixed with cedar and resinous super clean patchouli. There is freshly cut grass and a mound of lush wet driftwood. The cedar is there but in a more background way and never overpowers our green stuff. Reasonably linear, this dry-down is soothing and lasts long, despite remaining relatively close to the skin. Truth is a surprising and attractive fragrance. It calms my busy day and relaxes my mind and nerves, putting me in a state of peace and harmony. A real magic potion for me! If you smell it on someone else, it could be much stronger than you can feel it on yourself if you missed it. It has a very moist, musky, sweet smell. Great fragrance, best for early spring and summer days. This scent is also lovely for a rainy day in those seasons. Truth is a pretty flexible scent, but the rainy season matches the effect and mood. It is wearable for daily informal activities such as doing sports, shopping, and leisure. And I use it for wearing in the office or at informal parties but could be used in the evenings at a bar or on a date. This is the most underrated fragrance in my collection. Truth is my go-to bottle whenever I'm looking for something uncomplicated. Like I said before, it's a grassy and woody fragrance but still has a subtle heart note of spice that lasts the longest. I base the review on a 100ml bottle I have owned since October 2015. -Elysium

Fresh and fresh again. It is my feeling when I put on this fragrance. The opening starts with fresh herbal scent that is a little spicy. It reminds me spring in mountainous area after after a rain in the morning. That is why I like to wear it in the morning. Both longevity and projection is acceptable according to the price. It lasts 4 to 5 hours and all the time you can feel the projection. I think the silage is around your arm length which is enough for daily usage. Although after 5 hours It is needed to refresh, The scent is on the skin with an slight projection. I think It is wearable for daily casual activities such as doing sport, shopping, visit a friend. I've found it a little informal for wearing in the office or formal parties. Absolutely summer and spring scent. All in all I like this fragrance. It is not something very special to me, but I like to wear it occasionally.

Okay, not *all,* because I'm going to keep talking. Criminally underrated. Is it an undergarment-remover? No, but it's also not a 6.4 out of 10. Stop hatin', haters. This is a great summer fragrance I won't over-describe; others have done that job for me. It stays fairly close to the skin and is inoffensive enough to wear at work, bringing the scents of spring and summer green into the sterile environment of the office. You won't bog people down in a cloud of perfume, but perk up anyone who gets close enough, with the bright, clean allure of the great outdoors. You have vim and zest and verve! And you smell like it! If you want to knock it, it's not exactly a complicated fragrance. It's fresh and green-on-green, and it pretty much stays that way. If you want something simple and fun, Truth is no lie.

It is a simple scent. It's just okay. Reminds me of shower gels and fabric softener (in the drydown). It appears to be discontinued, but it is available through discounters. Fresh, clean, mildly aquatic (but not salty) and mildly green. Sweet too, but in a shower gel kind of way. In the drydown it's a bit more woody and sort of balsamic (I guess it's the cardamom) but still stays fresh. I guess I'm getting some whifs of rain smell, or maybe that's just placebo from reading other reviews haha. It doesn't project much, but it stays on for a good amount of time. I only sprayed 2 times though, you could overspray it for better results. It's an easy reach but too boring for me. I'd recommend this to someone who's not into perfumes but still wants to wear something and smell good. It's versatile, since it is so simple and unoffending. It's sort of a boring, but good blue fragrance, suited better for warmer weather. Bottle looks funky but is actually really comfortable to hold, it sits quite well in my hand.

This is a great fragrance, Fresh, Clean and Green. It smells so good and very pleasant with reasonable price. It is my favorite choice from Calvin Klein and also Truth for Women that I bought for my wife 19 years ago. Both of them are the best for Men and Women. It opens up with like fresh spicy and green notes in the background then dry down is green woody.

... which is inextricably linked to my personal memories of moving to the Ruhr area, as it perfectly matched the rugged charm of this industrial environment. Essentially the same fragrance direction as Minotaure by Paloma Picasse, Allure Homme by Chanel ... a powdery, somewhat richer fougère scent with noble woods and a hint of sweetness.

In my eternal search for a cool patchouli scent, I stumbled upon Truth and found it, like everything from CK that I've had under my nose, quite synthetic, but not that terrible either. Compared to other fruity testers from this brand, Truth was actually quite nice. I can't identify any pepper to save my life.

About 3 years ago, I bought a fake for 5 €. I spontaneously liked it somehow because it smelled so different from the other stuff. Back then, I didn't know what it was made to imitate. Later, when I saw the Truth bottle, I had a slight suspicion, but I never dared to compare them. The other day, I finally did, and I truly feel they are 100% the same.

Wow, this is something special indeed. I'm a big fan of the original pour homme, and this is related but not identical. Thankfully, my favorite part of the original is still present: the pine/fir-capsacin-and (of course) leather combo, but still different enough to justify both. Doesn't project as well as the original either, but is a thicker presence with a definite richness. I would like to say the pour homme feels like a serious man on a set path in life of his own choosing, and the parfum is representative of his arrival in success.

Here i review 2017's flanker to the original Pour Homme eau de toilette. Although a stronger concentration, this is an altogether different scent that retains just some of the original's dna. I hope you enjoy.

Who stands there in the forest, completely still and silent? A Bottega Veneta, rubbing itself against a conifer with its leathery-woody nature and smelling of light resin notes. BV fragrances are as unmistakable in the fragrance landscape as nothing else. No matter which scent you choose from the men's or women's collection, it has a typical character that I can recognize very clearly. However, that doesn’t mean that you take one and know them all. No, each fragrance from BV has its own advantages, its properties, and peculiarities that can be very flattering. For me, this fragrance is a must-have in my collection. A status that it will probably never lose. The exceptionally long-lasting composition of leather, wood, light spice, and resinous-balsamic coniferous forest makes my otherwise not so green fragrance heart beat very fast. This is also because I am really into the scent of coniferous wood. A great fragrance with a grand characteristic across the entire spectrum and a wonderful scent that is typically Bottega Veneta.

I really like all four Bottega Veneta men’s fragrances. They are very good new releases in the classic mainstream men’s fragrance segment. The regular “Pour homme” is a very fine, spicy-leathery but unfortunately also very light scent. The “Extrême” version seems more durable, but unfortunately not as fresh anymore. And the “Essence Aromatique” leans more towards summery notes. Very fine and fresh. All Bottegas suffer from one issue: durability. So the announcement of a “Parfum” version was all the more pleasing. At least it raised hopes for better performance. For Father’s Day, I received the fragrance as a gift from my loved ones. And one thing upfront: It is still unmistakably “Bottega Veneta Pour Homme.” However, the freshness of the original Pour Homme is increasingly fading. The spicy-leathery notes can at best accompany the scent. Here, the balsam fir clearly and unmistakably dominates. Very fresh, resinous, and woody. For me, it reminds me a bit of the pine needles in “Blenheim Bouquet”; however, it is a bit sharper. I like the forest in a bottle. But it may not be everyone’s cup of tea. Unfortunately, the performance here also leaves much to be desired. Sillage is almost non-existent and the longevity is below average. More than five to six hours close to the skin is not achievable. The bottle, the packaging (yes, I know, not really important), and the sprayer, on the other hand, are top-notch. However, the price seems a bit exaggerated to me. It has now reached the same outrageous level as Armani. Who should buy this fragrance? Well, good question. Anyone who likes the base scent of the three variants and has nothing against a woody fragrance in a bottle can go for it. It is, as my predecessor rightly mentioned, pure understatement. This applies to all three variants. Otherwise, I actually recommend the “Extrême” version. It offers the best compromise and is, in my opinion, the longest lasting. Overall, I consider the fragrance and its two offshoots to be perfect signature scents. They are fresh, spicy, subtly leathery, worthy of being a signature, and not intrusive. As for the headline? I couldn’t think of anything. So I borrowed a response from HaraldK from my statement: “I hardly believe that it can convince me more than the Essence Aromatique (if only because the terrible tonka bean is in it), but it will get a chance to be tested :)” Don’t worry, HaraldK, it’s not that terrible… Best regards Your Profumorist

Just before Christmas, I bought the Chanel Allure Homme Sport Eau Extreme at Galeria Kaufhof. The good thing about most purchases is that you get a few samples. Unfortunately, they are usually ones I already know inside and out. CK One or Boss Bottled - I strangely almost always get those two. This time I got lucky. Bottega Veneta, a brand popular in the fragrance world, has never really achieved a major commercial breakthrough. Nevertheless, there are quite a few whose popularity and sales figures are not bad. Here, the brand is also well regarded. I tested this fragrance without high expectations, as I find the scent notes extremely unremarkable and woody-spicy fragrances are generally not my thing. nulltheless, I want to evaluate this fragrance objectively. The bottle is very chic, elegant, and truly classy, just like the entire line or brand. This elegant bottle suits the fragrance, as it feels more suitable for older or more mature gentlemen in my opinion. The prices are not exactly cheap for a designer fragrance. Most hover around the 100 Euro mark for 100ml. It starts off very unpleasant for me. An extremely penetrating spiciness that I find off-putting. There’s something spicy in the opening that bothers me immensely, I have no idea what. After half an hour, a solid pleasantly spicy day fragrance develops. I don't find any major highlights here, but that’s not always necessary for a day fragrance. The main player in this scent is the fir balsam. It doesn’t smell like a Christmas tree at all, but a nice fir note is very noticeable throughout the entire duration. Pine and cedar also come through clearly. I don’t perceive cardamom or especially the tonka bean at all here. Nevertheless, this fragrance has a strong spiciness that becomes quite pleasant after half an hour. Additionally, there’s leather, which is present in most EDPs and intense versions, as this note lasts a long time. Here, it is not in the foreground. Overall, a solid creation, which I see most as an everyday fragrance. It is pleasant, but I don’t perceive any major highlights here. In terms of type, it’s rather not casual, and if so, more suited for a dressier outfit. Moreover, I find the fragrance more suitable for mature gentlemen. In my opinion, it fits best for men over 40. While it’s not old-fashioned, it does resemble some vintage fragrances. The performance is quite good for an EDP. Sillage is also decent. The perfumer is the talented Daniela, who is responsible for the wonderful Prada fragrances. Great woman. Even though the fragrance doesn’t really suit my taste, it’s a great scent that will suit some very well.

I was really very excited when it was announced in December that Bottega Veneta pour Homme would also be available as a perfume. I am a fan of the regular EdT version as well as the Extreme, as I really like the clear, fresh, and leathery scent. I find it very pleasant that there is no floral or sweet accompaniment here.

A truly very "woodsy" scent. It smells to me of fir and pine, leather and cardamom I only perceive in the background. Very balsamic and ethereal. Fresh and somehow even sexy. I also notice the tonka bean later on. I really like it a lot. It has - as Profumorist has aptly described - something boss-like about it.

I was recently comparing The Body Shop MIDNIGHT BAKULA to Calvin Klein EUPHORIA, but now that I've had a chance to try FORBIDDEN EUPHORIA, I recognize that it is much closer in notes and structure. I do detect a strong peachiness in this composition, along with a mingling of different flowers and patchouli, and the oriental spirit of the two creations, conjoined with their similar notes, makes them close neighbors on the grand olfactory map, according to my nose. I think that I may actually prefer this perfume to MIDNIGHT BAKULA, which is very strong on the patchouli and slightly dirty. FORBIDDEN EUPHORIA, in contrast, is crunchy and clean, while still being more oriental than fruity-floral, it seems to me. Neither of the two is overly sweet: the fruits seem thick and somehow stewed but without any sugar added. I'm going to acquire a second sample of this worthy Calvin Klein flanker before issuing a final verdict, but for now I can report that I like it.

Sweet Euphoria with the same excellent length as the original, I could say the Summer Euphoria. Reminds a lot of flowerbomb, Jimmy Choo and Lady Million. An airy sweet spicy perfume, not heady at all. I could wear it during my summer holidays without turning bitter. Happy indeed with my choise.

Fruit pies baking, sizzling french sauces, heady aromas in the kitchen making my head spin. Now this Euphoria is really, really good. Surprisedly good. I just wasn't expecting a fragrance from today's stock to make me sit back and really appreciate the delightful aromas. Or to put me in another place. But it does. Euphoria evokes images of country kitchens, spaciousness, warm cider and friends gathering around the Thanksgiving holidays preparing a vast array of dishes while the air is brisk outside, the leaves have turned and a great many have fallen off the limbs of the trees. This is a fruity composition with a sweet patchouli base that doesn't seem sexy to me at all. Rather, it's more of a friendly fragrance that embodies good times with friends. In fact, it brought me back to a time from college, when a group of us had a Thanksgiving together. Those were real patchouli days when essences and herbal fragrances were real. We wore our patchouli straight from the bottle. We were the original Patchouli addicts. I won't forget that memory of a group of young adults preparing a meal together for the first time away from home. Laughter, camaraderie and fun with people. I have this fragrance to thank for bringing back that memory. That may not be the image that Calvin Klein's advertising wanted for his fragrance, but it's what it evoked in me. Euphoria draws out a warmth and pleasantness ideal for jeans, boots and over-sized sweaters. This is a wonderful cool weather scent of fruits, patchouli with a bit of hidden musk. It doesn't seem to last very long tho, on an average two hours at best. After sampling it, I chose to purchase a rollerball also, so I could refresh the fragrance when I'm out. Otherwise, it's gone and I'm without anything. Sillage is decent, just wafting closely around a person. An excellent dupe is Fragrance Rebel/ParfumsdeCoeur Romance & Dreams. The EdT is identical. I tried it on one arm vs. FE on the other, and could not tell them apart.

Very thick heavy musk, artificial or tinned mandarin oranges that have been left in the open tin and raspberry cake flavouring. Rich, overwhelming, with an animalic twang that reminds me of ambergris (but not quite) and halitosis. Before the perfume dries I get a sweet peppery wood but a couple of minutes in it becomes just a strange combination of food and musk (lots and lots of heavy musk). Powerful and way too much for me. On my 'use it or lose it' kick this is a lose it. Manufacturer's carded sample picked up sometime in 2015.

I love raspberries. The sweetness of it when it enters your mouth, with a whiff of something citric. The amazing colour. I have a coat exactly that colour, and it has become my favourite coat over the years. There are so many scents in which raspberry plays an important role: Flower by Kenzo, Dolce&Gabbana pour Femme, Christian Lacroix’s C’est la Vie and YSL’s Elle. All four are so delicious and they are scents that I return to. Therefore I had great expectations when I got my hands on the Forbidden Euphoria. Sadly, my expectations were too huge. It starts out sweet and fruity. Nice feeling to it but not something outstanding. And I do notice that the raspberry note is a bit synthetic. Then comes the heart notes, jasmine and orchid, very smooth and flowery. The base is pretty much patchouli. It last for three hours and sillage is ok. Looking at the ads I was expecting so much more. The experience for me was a bit synthetic, a bit short and something I will soon forget again 49/365

Not surprisingly, with notes such as raspberry, orchid, mandarin orange, white musk, patchouli, peony & jasmine... this is the definition of a fruity floral. Is that a bad thing? No. Not if you are looking for one. I have not tried the original Euphoria but this one doesn't seem to have what it takes to be a big hit, or even memorable.

Recently, after a visit to the cemetery, I drove home feeling gloomy. It was pouring rain and on the radio, Christina Aguilera sang "Hurt". "The music doesn’t help," my friend Sharon said sympathetically. I remained silent until I decided to head to a perfume shop. Said and done. I immediately came across the pretty bottle of Forbidden Euphoria.

Euphoria and all of its flankers are not entirely unsympathetic to me. Forbidden Euphoria is also a creamy treat with a velvety fruity note. However, it bears a striking resemblance to Betsey Johnson, which, in my opinion, is not officially available in Germany but is quite affordable in the USA.

First of all: I love the classic Euphoria! The scent is very sensual, intense, and rather heavy for me, with killer longevity! Therefore, it is an absolute going-out fragrance, meaning when the people around me keep a certain socially acceptable distance.

I'm on my second bottle of the original, eponymous Bottega Veneta fragrance and at some point during these purchases I scored a gorgeous little boxed mini of Eau Legere, the inevitable flanker. I should mention here that the bottles from this house are truly praiseworthy: simple, clean and expensive-looking with hefty glass bottoms and restrained details, such as the basket weave pattern on the base paying homage to the brand's heritage as a high-end leather goods designer. But the bottle alone won't do it - with a generous mini at my disposal, I've had the chance to sample this over a couple of seasons and I'm not entirely convinced. According to the company's website, the intention of this flanker was to "illuminate the brightest, freshest facets of the Bottega Veneta fragrance" and to that end they have succeeded with Eau Legere. Given that flankers generally go in one of two directions: "extreme" or "fresh", what we have here is the latter: Bottega Veneta Lite. This opens with the signature leather accord that characterised the original; not a smoky, birch tar leather - to my nose, the "leather" in both these fragrances reads more like a cedar note, but perhaps the citrus-like nuances of pink pepper and bergamot are influencing that impression. Either way, the opening of Eau Legere is familiar, albeit more subdued, and distinguished by a stronger lime-like citrus note. After a promising opening, the heart and base notes are where this fragrance really begins to part ways with the original. The milky, plummy violet-like jasmine of the original has been replaced with a clean, crisp gardenia and jasmine heart with a trace of the opening leather/citrus hummimg quietly in the background and keeping sweetness at bay. At this point, Eau Legere begins to smell somewhat generic, like a pleasantly clean but faceless floral you've smelled many times before. The extended oakmoss base note, a highlight of the original, seems entirely absent in this version, being replaced by a soft musk. Discussion of base notes is somewhat irrelevant, however, as after a couple of hours Eau Legere has retreated to a very close skin scent and has all but disappeared by the three to four hour mark in my wearings, even with lavish application. It seems a shame that the trade-off for "freshening up" the more distinctive elements of the first Bottega Veneta fragrance has resulted in something less distinguished and noteworthy than the original. This assessment probably sounds a little harsh but I don't mean it to be dismissive. It's just that (in Australia) the 75ml EDT retails for $165, which is approaching niche territory. For that price I want a little more bang for my buck. I can see this one having appeal for those who found the original a little too declarative and want a light, close-wearing floral leather that feels crisp and fresh for the summer months. I would emphasise testing on skin before purchase, as Eau Legere had significantly more presence on paper than it did on my skin.

I love a good, simple scent. It is nice to be able to detect the notes and enjoy them, together with the feeling of being able to do it. BV Eau Légère is a simple scent, consisting of only 6 different notes. It is also in my top20 of favourite fragrances because it bringes me into a certain mood whenever I spray it on. I immediately feel much better, no matter how my mood has been. Top is pink pepper and bergamot. These two work really well together, creating a dry, almost woody expression and, imho, giving this scent a unisex feeling. After 10-15 minutes the flowers, gardenia and jasmine, arrive. They add some depth to the scent and the dryness disappears, making the scent more feminine. I still think, though, that men can wear this as well as women. Finally, oakmoss and musk land this fragrance beautifully. All in all this takes you on an 8 hour journey, eventhough it is rather subtle. Not much ado or loud singing - just a really nice travel companion all the way. The bottle is pretty. No wonder that BV has used it for several of their fragrances. This bottle has the smoky metal top, a nuance I like a lot on metals. To me this fragrance has a distinct and rare expression that leaves me with a feeling of sitting in a garden, smelling both the herbs and the flowers. I am almost through the bottle and I am going to buy it again. 33/365

The first two women's fragrances from Bottega Veneta have corrected my rather skewed perception of today's mainstream perfumery. As different as the two are in their essence - just like night and day - they are remarkably similar in their innermost core. Bottega Veneta EDP is a powdery-floral chypre with a warm, gentle leather note and a dreamy oakmoss-patchouli base that evokes thoughts of earthy, mossy forest floors, while Bottega Veneta Eau Legere is a cool, white floral bouquet resting on oakmoss, reminiscent of the freshness of a lively bubbling forest spring. This may sound like there are few similarities - yet, when you have both in front of you at the same time, the shared DNA becomes clear: This green-woody base note interspersed with white flowers, which in Bottega Veneta EDP takes on its characteristic quality with soft leather and aromatic oakmoss and slightly earthy patchouli. In Bottega Veneta Eau Legere, this special green-woody-floral note is underpinned by pepper and musk, contributing to that unique lightness that defines the essence of the lighter - and I would also claim - younger variant. Bottega Veneta EDP is inherently warm, softly enveloping, intense, and distinctly darker than the much lighter Bottega Veneta Eau Legere, which exudes a distant, cool, yet very feminine freshness paired with youthful lightness. The sillage is quite strong in both versions, but Bottega Veneta Eau Legere performs better on warmer days, while Bottega Veneta EDP, due to its intensely powdery-leathery character, is more suited for cooler days. For me, Bottega Veneta EDP and Bottega Veneta Eau Legere are not only perfectly rounded chypre fragrances but also the most elegant mainstream scents launched in recent years.

I was searching in all the stores for a butter-soft leather jacket, preferably in black and in a denim style. I had no idea that this would be an almost impossible task. Eventually, I looked on eBay and found it. There it was, just as I had imagined and in the right size. Even the photo conveyed to me the tactile softness and the smooth leather scent. The fact that the piece was second hand made it even more attractive to me, as leather improves with wear. The price was moderate, and soon the object of my desire found its way to me. And in person, the jacket matched my expectations exactly. I want to wear it in bed too. Today I wore it while visiting the perfume stand. The dealer wisely handed me Legere - which was completely compatible with my jacket. The scent clings to the skin, smooth, without weighing it down. The bergamot appears fresh - softened by sweet pepper. The gardenia glows dark red - illuminated by bright jasmine. Oakmoss dims the scent into a bitterness - enhanced by musk. And above all, the fine lamb nappa leather scent hovers. I feel gently and simultaneously daringly enveloped - with a kick of secretive eroticism. The allure of the fragrance is that it doesn't reveal everything at once. It is like a flirt that promises everything - without the obligation to fulfill any of it.

There in moss-covered clefts, Where the cooling west winds blow, And the crown around temples and hips Elves engage in a dance. Joseph von Eichendorff The scent of Bottega Veneta, Eau légère is so successful that only poetry can adequately describe it - in this case, of course, not my own, but that of a great Romantic. "Moss-covered clefts" can indeed be found in Bottega Veneta E.L.; the crisp freshness of oakmoss (which substitute has been found here for the 'real thing', I cannot say, oakmoss is on the list of fragrance materials that are supposed to disappear from perfumes) is palpable, the user of this fragrance experiences cooling through lemon, which does not bite, but together with very subtle floral notes leads down a green path into muted light. Here, everything is really just wafted, even the soft leather note. Nevertheless, it is precisely the delicacy and restrained elegance of this "light water" that can breathe joy into weary souls - grandiosely, what the perfumer Michel Almairac has accomplished here... and then it also comes from a mainstream giant, namely Coty... - Wonders do happen. Yes, there is also a small drop of bitterness - like many beautiful impressions, this "light water" leaves me after two hours, it fades a bit too early, but I forgive it, as it is so delightful and perfect as long as it is present. And for all those who prefer it less poetically: The Bottega Veneta Eau de Parfum lasts better (understandably), has more leathery components and a more pronounced chypre character. This "light water" that I celebrate here is characterized by its citrusy, green top notes, which are particularly pleasant in summer. This "light water" is exactly the summer fragrance I have always been looking for.

I couldn't stand the original at all...I wouldn't have tested Eau Legere on my own either, but my sales assistant at the Parfümerie Liebe in Hannover sprayed it on a paper strip for me. Since I had already tested about 8 fragrances, I didn't smell it at all. I was looking for a new scent and decided to follow my sales assistant's suggestions.

As a change from my predominantly fruity-sweet fragrances, I was looking for something fresh and more robust. Here in the forum, I received the tip to try Eau Légère by Bottega Veneta. That was truly an absolute blind buy, which I do not regret. Eau Légère starts very distinctly with bergamot.

Even as a child, I didn't like the comparisons with my family members: "Just like Mom!" or "Just like Dad!" Depending on whose circle of acquaintances I was in at the time. I must have sensed back then that the truth lay somewhere in between - and yet I overlooked it. Later, it was the comparisons with my cousins that drove me to fury.

Now I finally had the luck to receive a sample of this beautiful scent. The description immediately appealed to me, but I was skeptical about its similarity to Cuero Mujer. I had once bought a miniature of that and found it absolutely terrible. Now I am sure it must have gone off. I also learned it was very old and more suited for a display case.

I simply love this scent! It is light yet has character. The pink pepper and bergamot are clearly noticeable but still very soft. I find this fragrance very well-rounded and quite special. I've now gotten the EDP for a change? -)))

It's enough to make you scream. I had already filed Jimmy Choo, the old stiletto maker, in the not-so-important drawer shortly after "Flash." Why should I waste a thought on checking out a rather expensive fragrance from him now? Exactly. No reason at all. Then came the day when I, driven by my old bottle addiction, turned my attention to "Iris Crush." My gaze wandered down to the fragrance pyramid. Two words in it began to glow and pulse. Lipstick and Heliotrope. My pulse slowly started to rise. Arbitrarily, I read the last comment, a teaser as it appears on the phone. Then I wildly researched where and how and what. "Iris Crush" echoed in my ears. "Jimmy Choo," the voice of reason held back, a distant, thin little voice that I could successfully ignore with little effort. Pah. I already have so many wonderful, sexy, old-school, girly, powdery lipstick scents. Enough said. Without realizing it, I ordered a sample. Only when it arrived in my mailbox a few days later did I realize what I had done. I had put myself in great danger! My heart, my poor, corona-ridden heart, just barely recovering, and now this Iris comes to crush it? I sensed trouble. And as usual, this feeling did not deceive me... I did not perceive the top note as drastically as my pre-commentators. A bit of pepper, maybe a bit of pencil. But then I glide over into my home port "Boudoir with velvet curtains and feather boas - the roar of the greasepaint, the smell of the crowd." This is the scent that brings back the hyper-feminine eroticism of long-gone decades, the 50s, 60s, but transplanted into the here and now. Lipstick on - nice, but not so multifaceted. French Kiss - girlier, fruitier. Love, Chloé - more modern, straighter. ...there are a few others I could compare, but that's not the point. Iris Crush has all the character traits that convince me. The powdery, feminine sweetness of an old lipstick. The glamour of old makeup remover cream. The morbidity of Heliotrope. The brittle smokiness of Tonka.. Ah, not to forget: the Iris. Not unlike Iris Ganache. As you may have easily recognized: Nellycatcher, but absolutely. (And that from a shoemaker.)

As a confessed lover of lipstick scents (what a word ;-) I naturally want to share a few words about this new treasure. I often ponder what exactly makes up this mysterious lipstick accord that smells so wonderfully waxy-powdery and mineral-dry. Unfortunately, I have yet to find an answer; perhaps it is the interplay of several fragrance notes!? It is definitely that exact smell that wafts up when wearing certain lipsticks, regardless of whether there is something fruity or gourmand around it. Interestingly, the situation is reversed with "Seduction Collection - Iris Crush." The new lipstick collection from Jimmy Choo has been perfumed with this scent, so here it's "Perfume before Lipstick." Right off the bat: the bottle is an absolute dream. It is made of heavy, faceted glass, a solid "gold" plate, and a really heavy, high-quality "gold" stopper. The sprayer works well, allowing for quite accurate dosing. Now to the scent: The "nose-perceived" similarity to "Replica - Lipstick On" has already been mentioned in the statements. I applied the fragrances in parallel and can definitely confirm this impression. They start with the exact same lipstick note, although "Replica - Lipstick On" is a bit sweeter at the beginning. In both, I can clearly perceive heliotrope in the top note, while the Replica also has a small fruity nuance; this only emerges later in the Jimmy Choo. In terms of scent consistency, I perceive "Seduction Collection - Iris Crush" as slightly finer and deeper, perhaps more serious, while the Replica tends to be more powdery and playful. But the differences are indeed quite minimal at this point. A major drawback of all the lipstick fragrances tested so far is, unfortunately, the relatively short longevity of this special note. When I apply a fragrance and this lipstick accord wafts into my nose, I automatically start to anxiously wait to see how long this note will be perceivable. So far, it has always dissipated quite quickly. "Replica - Lipstick On" also falls into this category. After about half an hour, it increasingly develops into a cozy, powdery iris scent. This is quite nice, but it only gently recalls the top note. It has already been mentioned in the statements that the lipstick accord in "Seduction Collection - Iris Crush" fortunately lasts a long time. So, I approached the test with great hope and a cheerful spirit. After about 1 hour, I initially had the impression that here too, the lipstick aspect was fading more into the background. Both fragrances then gently glide into two very beautiful scents that still resemble each other quite a bit. The Jimmy Choo also develops a slightly fruity nuance over time, which becomes even more pronounced than in the Replica. While this fruity note has a somewhat cherry-like quality in the Replica, it comes off as slightly berry-like in the Jimmy Choo. However, I hardly perceive this fruity note in projection; it is more present when sniffing directly on the skin. "Replica - Lipstick On" is perhaps a touch warmer, airier, powderier, cozier, and sweeter in comparison. Heliotrope remains more present in the Jimmy Choo. In the base, I can smell the patchouli more distinctly in the Replica, which gives it a slightly spicy-earthy nuance. However, the striking similarity between the two fragrances remains intact. When I sniff directly at the applied spot of "Seduction Collection - Iris Crush," I can still distinctly perceive the original lipstick scent after several hours (!) - hooray, a true novelty! In projection, however, it only reaches me very softly. Here, surprisingly, it reminds me a bit of "Panthea Iris." They share a certain synthetic note, which I do not find unpleasant. I will test this further to see if I can verify it; often, memory can be deceiving. While testing "Seduction Collection - Iris Crush" and "Replica - Lipstick On" in parallel, the image of two fragrance waves came to mind. They start at the same point, oscillate for a long time with very similar frequency and amplitude, sometimes overlapping, then gently glide apart again without straying too far from each other. Overall, the Jimmy Choo clearly has the upper hand regarding the intensity and duration of the lipstick note. The Replica tends to develop into a generally powdery, cozy, sweet makeup scent. The sillage and long-lasting performance of both fragrances are very satisfactory. Conclusion: "Seduction Collection - Iris Crush" is a sweet, wonderful, elegant, and simultaneously cozy iris scent with a long-lasting lipstick note. I am strongly torn between: I am not sure whether, given the described similarities, one actually "needs" both fragrances, and at the same time, "Seduction Collection - Iris Crush" clearly has the upper hand for me. Overall, it feels slightly more valuable and holds the record for longevity of the lipstick accord among all the lipstick fragrances I have tested so far. And since "Replica - Lipstick On" apparently is no longer being produced, its fans now find a wonderful, albeit slightly more expensive alternative in "Seduction Collection - Iris Crush." If I had to choose one, it would clearly be the Jimmy Choo!

Unaware of anything exciting, the fragrant messenger pigeon fluttered to me with Sharingpost - as it often does. Slightly annoyed, it dropped a few envelopes. Among them was the "Wonder Box." That's what I like to call the little packages that are tied up by particularly lovely perfumers... One such perfumer recently asked me which scent from her collection I would like to test in addition to the sharing fragrance, and that’s how I came to Iris Crush. The statements had piqued my curiosity, but I am initially cautious with "sweet-powdery." Sweet doesn’t always work for me. It’s the treats in my collection that have captivated me at first sweet sniff, and with which there were no initial difficulties. Skepticism regarding heliotrope and tonka, but primarily skepticism towards the lipstick note! Looking forward to pepper and iris! Well, and finally it came - this fantastic lipstick! There it is - the carrot in a velvety dress, butter-soft shimmering, with subtle blush and stylishly applied lipstick... I didn’t expect that. Powder: Yes! If I could touch this powder, it would feel like velvet. Sweet: also! But without overflowing and initially slightly peppery (a dream). That’s sweetness as I like it! Just as velvety as it begins, it eventually fades away (I won’t give time indications - the longevity was satisfactory for me, let’s say for a workday ;-)). A well-rounded thing, I tell you! I’m in love, and my wish list has grown. At this point, my heartfelt thanks to you, L.! ;-)

In the past, lipsticks simply smelled different than they do today. I don't want to say better, but different, somehow more intense. As a child of the 60s, it was the greatest thing for me to get a mini or sample lipstick. For me, as a little girl, that was synonymous with luxury and the big wide world. Back then, it sounds like I'm almost as old as a dinosaur, durability was valued and care was rather neglected. Fortunately, that's a bit different today, as care and durability no longer exclude each other in the 21st century. So far, so good. Iris Crush opens with a gentle pepper note, but the impression of lipstick is immediately present. Neroli flashes briefly and very subtly in the background, only to quickly withdraw again. I can't perceive freesia, at least not consciously. The heliotrope takes its time to appear, but then immediately connects with the lipstick note. As it progresses, the lipstick becomes darker and somehow creamier, which I attribute to the blend of patchouli, musk, and tonka. If that's even possible, an additional layer of "sensuality" is also added. Throughout the entire development, the lipstick is present. It almost hovers above everything, although other components join in. However, they never overshadow it but allow it to become darker over time. From a bright, vibrant red to a dark berry tone, I can't describe the evolution any other way. I smell lipstick and see in my mind's eye a Marilyn Monroe, who breathes into the microphone with perfectly painted lips and absolutely sexy "Happy Birthday Mr. President …". Can it get any more erotic? Iris Crush is sexy, seductive, sensual, erotic, and modern. The scent has nothing, absolutely nothing dusty about it, even if this lipstick note reminds me of long-gone times. Marilyn is an icon who will forever stand for femininity and sexiness. She, and her wonderful films, will remain unforgettable forever, and that is exactly what Iris Crush captures perfectly for me. Iris Crush is the first fragrance from the house of Jimmy Choo that has come under my nose, but this perfume captivated me from the very beginning. It made an immediate "bang." The longevity of more than 10 hours is absolutely commendable and effortlessly survives a party night. Personally, I see Iris Crush more on a woman, as I don't know any man in my/our circle of acquaintances who would wear the scent or for whom it would even be remotely suitable. However, that doesn't mean anything, as there are certainly men who would wear the scent and for whom it would fit. In my experience, many perfumes develop differently on men's skin, and perhaps some gentlemen will sniff Iris Crush and share their experience with us. I would be pleased. I was able to snag the scent as a decant in a sharing, so I can't evaluate the bottle. I've never seen it, but in photos, it looks simply beautiful and very elegant. My skin reflects scents very poorly, and therefore I also don't evaluate the sillage, as I never drag a scent trail behind me. Unfortunately.

I am looking for a scent similar to "Replica - Lipstick On | Maison Margiela" and in my search, I immediately stumbled upon this little gem! I also agree that I have found a great substitute and lipstick scent here. Upon spraying, the fragrance is very waxy, reminiscent of crayons in my opinion, and has a somewhat bitter note. However, apart from the rather high price, this is the only thing I dislike about the scent, and fortunately, it fades away quite quickly. I find it vintage without being outdated. Sweet without being sticky. Dry without being dusty. Powdery but not baby powder. Present but not overpowering. It is feminine, hugs its wearer, and is suitable for any age! In short, I find it very successful! Longevity and sillage are ideal for me, present yet not overwhelming or room-filling. When it comes to dosage, one should still be careful not to overdo it; otherwise, I think it could become a bit too much. Depending on the season, a little more can be applied, or in summer, it should be used sparingly. I think it is wearable year-round, but I will test that further! The bottle is a real eye-catcher and will look very nice in any collection, I am still waiting for a discount promotion, and then I will add this beautiful fragrance to my collection!

There are fragrances that you spray on, and there are fragrances that you apply and wear like make-up. Iris Crush belongs to the second category. It is not a perfume in the classic sense, but the olfactory counterpart to a classic red lipstick: perfect, sensual, flawless.

When Frédéric Malle sold his brand to the Estée Lauder Group in 2015, he immediately knew that he wanted to reinterpret some of the great classics that had been personally released by the Grande Dame EL. Why it then took nine more years for the Legacy Collection to appear remains Mr. Malle's secret… Now, Malle is not a nose, but sees himself as a "publisher." The Legacy Collection was created in collaboration with Anne Flipo ("La Nuit de L'Homme (Eau de Toilette) | Yves Saint Laurent," "Invictus (Eau de Toilette) | Paco Rabanne," L'Interdit (2018) Eau de Parfum ), Carlos Benaïm ("Polo (Eau de Toilette) | Ralph Lauren," "Hugo Just Different (Eau de Toilette) | Hugo Boss," Euphoria Eau de Parfum ) and Bruno Jovanovic ("Monsieur. | Editions de Parfums Frédéric Malle," Dries Van Noten par Frédéric Malle ). The goal was to "revive 'Azurēe | Estēe Lauder,' Estée, 'Knowing (Eau de Parfum) | Estēe Lauder,' Private Collection, and 'White Linen (Eau de Parfum) | Estēe Lauder' as 'museum pieces' with the help of talented perfumers." However, simply swapping out individual notes does not work. Like in a game of Jenga, removing one note can cause the entire composition to collapse. Malle discovered that Estée lost warmth and richness without its honey note. So he kept it and enhanced the effect with an amber note. I actually wanted to buy the whole collection as minis and Knowing Legacy in full size. Unfortunately, Estée Lauder USA does not ship abroad, and Harrods does not carry the five-piece mini set in their assortment. The decision to limit myself to Knowing Legacy was easy: first, Knowing holds a special place in my heart - it was my very first perfume, which I bought as a teenager with the earnings from a summer job. And second, connoisseur Christi Long explained on Facebook that Knowing Legacy is the interpretation that is furthest from the original. And while I consider Knowing to be a great, timelessly elegant classic, I wanted something special for the substantial price, well, you know. Knowing Legacy is a decidedly bold, dark, somewhat wicked interpretation. Iris, styrax, and labdanum give the fragrance a rock-inspired, modern feel, yet not at the expense of class and elegance. Some who love Knowing Eau de Parfum will surely be disappointed by this rebirth. Personally, I am enchanted. Frédéric Malle has reinterpreted the Knowing DNA in such a way that a wonderful tribute to Estée Lauder's life's work has emerged.

Have you ever found yourself obsessed with something, so consumed with something that you can hardly even think of anything else? A relationship, a new phone, a perfect body, your reputation, good grades, a great cologne, a unique style—anything can leave you obsessed. Calvin Klein Obsession for Men was what I considered to be my first "grown-up" perfume. I've always felt it was a generational fragrance for the men of a specific time. It was why I was very interested in the new releases from Calvin Klein: Obsessed for Men. I was wondering if this might become the same kind of defining fragrance for this generation. Is the new Obsessed perfume merely a remake of Obsession? Well, I don't deem so. CK Obsessed for Men seems like a very familiar scent even though I cannot pinpoint what specific cologne it reminds me of. I'm leaning towards it being a mix of several fragrances and just triggering my memory all at once. The opening gives me a fresh start with the sweetie, or oroblanco grapefruit, pepper, and cardamom stepping out in front. The bitterness of black cardamom note compensate the sweetness of the oroblanco; the resulting blend is impressive. I do get a powdery note similar to orris, yet there is neither orris nor iris listed among the notes. However, this is the first aspect I love the most. The heart of this crystalline juice is mainly leathery with cedar leaves and sensual labdanum, which stands up, a bit dirty, animal, and almost reminiscent of sex at times, and reinforces the leather-like smell. A modern smooth leather, ain't no rude cowhide as in many vintage scents. The dry down is ambery, a contemporary sweet amber that gets its aroma from the synthetic ambroxan. Again, that sweetness is mixed with the creaminess of the black vanilla, and the earthiness of the patchouli. On my skin and a paper strip, the scent develops differently, more ambery on the former, and more vanillic on the latter. Though, the vanilla note is always present and ties the whole stuff together. Not gourmand, it is sweet, reasonably warm, and darkened by the other base notes. It's quite intriguing. Obsessed is a very clean fragrance; it is on the lighter side, and almost unisex, but man, I like the super fresh energy that I get from it. As it wears on, it becomes more powdery and ambery than it's initial citrusy and spicy accord. Still quite fresh and clean and upbeat. Projection wise, Obsessed is moderate. The longevity of my test run was about 4-5 solid hours, and then maybe another hour wear it was still noticeable but weak. Again, not great, but not the worst either. Perhaps it'd be better in different weather or with more wear from me, but that's what I got with the one time deal. Right off the bat, I would recommend it for the coldest days, and there is that warm sweetness in all the stages that might not work with warm and hot seasons—a day fragrance, perfect for weekdays as well as the weekend. Overall, I do like the way it smells, but I'd want some more time wearing it before making a call. -Elysium

Currently, Parfumo's average score for this is only 5.5, but it's not something to be rated as low as that. It's moderately spicy, moderately sweet. It's suitable for summer days even if it's not aquatic. And it's relatively long lasting even if the last thing left is only synthetic vanillin and ambroxane. Its advantages are comfort, familiarity, and very good price. I didn't get this because I have a lot of colognes better than this, but if I can go back to university freshman, there's no reason not to pick up Obsessed to attract the attention of girls of the same class. It shares DNA similar to other CK scents, and also fits the latest trend. If you are in your early twenties, this is a pretty good choice. Especially if you are a fan of Ambroxan, you should definitely try it.

Well, Calvin Klein feels like the lowest quality (more expensive) mainstream brand of the last decade - that's my impression - and thus leads the Flop 10. This pathetic copying of flacons and names from its own house once again confirms that nothing perfume-related from Klein is worth more than 10 euros per 100 ml. "Obsessed" starts off typically small in its originality - a very synthetic, piercing citrus/fruit impression, shower gel cheap, annoying, pure lab creation. The aromas above are 80% perceived deception, little of it can be recognized in this brew. After about an hour, the highly synthetic, sharp shower gel-like quality fades, and the scent stylistically shifts into a (also) lab-like vanilla quality, surrounded by a very milky Ambroxan note. That's almost original for Klein's standards, as it at least contains "2 in 1" scents in the new release. Two synthetic perfumes for the price of one - who wouldn't dream of that? (Irony off)

That the name of a perfume does not necessarily reflect its true nature may occasionally cause confusion and head-shaking, but on the other hand, it is not that rare. The eternal and best example remains Estee Lauder's Youth Dew - in German: 'Tau der Jugend' - which sounds wonderfully shy and timid, but is a veritable war galley of a scent. On the other hand, Youth Dew is now over sixty years old - perfumes were made differently back then, perhaps that is permissible. Guerlain's famous La Petite Robe Noire is, at least in terms of Coco Chanel's definition of the Little Black Dress she created - thus 'a kind of uniform for all women with taste' - latently misnamed, but at least it has a significant recognition value with its characteristic cherry note. Calvin Klein's Obsessed, on the other hand, is a scent of the present, and its name - in German: 'besessen' - boldly promises a polarizing, at least somewhat memorable fragrance. In reality, however - one might as well forget all the supposedly used ingredients mentioned above - it possesses a triviality and interchangeability that is almost remarkable in its audacity. Obsessed has the character and distinctiveness of a completely generic deodorant: fresh-synthetic-spicy-slightly metallic, if one wishes to flatter. The old Obsession - whether one liked it or not - which it seeks to emulate in name, through the shape of its bottle, and the use of the also aged Kate Moss, does not deserve such a successor. Conclusion: any further words are one too many.

Overloaded synthetic total failure. Smells roughly like a perfume store on Black Friday, where inflationary amounts of various perfumes are sprayed all over the body, hair, and skin at every corner. The dull sweetness ensures that the "fragrance" is definitely perceived by everyone. Longevity is unfortunately not that bad. Unfortunately.

The scent doesn't smell incredibly good or particularly extraordinary, but definitely not as bad as many have described here. Sweet and synthetic, yes, but not unpleasant. Wearable in every season and really quite pleasant for the evening after a shower. It lasts on the skin for about 6-7 hours, projecting for the first 2-3 hours.

This is a great scent. And very under the radar, like the whole line, actually. Its seems a very simple composition, and, in a way, it is. A classic combo of Patchouli and cedarwood but with a twist. A fresh and green note of pine needles. The same used in the whole masculine line. It reminds me of Cartier Roadster. They both share that elegant, woody patchouli drydown, with a fresh herbal/green opening. This one, instead of mint, uses pine needles to fresh things up. The fragrance acts like a cologne but without a strong citric element. It lists bergamot as a top note but i can't smell much of it. But the pine makes it a really cooling scent and very sophisticated. The projection is not great but it lasts 6-8h. Really good option if you want something different for summer and spring time. 3/5

Bergamot, so-so. Instead, I think of a bit of nimm2 lemon, including the creamy-sharp content. Along with something ethereal-fresh, brushing against mint. All garnished on a rough, astringent-hesperidic base. The fruity part soon turns completely green, leaving only a hint of nimm2 as time goes on. A sheep-cheesy, pupated intermezzo after half an hour briefly raises concern. Unjustly - for soon the boss appears: balsamic-herbaceous coniferous wood. It doesn’t smell like the pines I know in nature, so I like to believe there’s a contribution from Siberia. I really like this, a spicy-elegant scent, where “the creaminess of the special pine” takes off a bit of the edge. As it progresses, the matter moves charmingly back and forth between the resinous and the creamy, edging towards midday in a style that even resembles throat lozenge leather. Only resembles, this is undoubtedly not a leather scent. But perhaps the folks at Bottega Veneta can’t quite help themselves considering their core competency. Or I’m just unconsciously assuming that. Otherwise, the scent is stable and shows at least three-quarters of its herbaceous-spicy-balsamic coniferous brew: relatively quiet, but quite enduring, although a generous application is recommended for this (as already mentioned). Patchouli plays a significant role for me only directly on the skin for long stretches. It only becomes more prominent in the overall fading scent from late afternoon onwards. With all that, the non-niche ambition and area of application are undoubtedly revealed. And in light of this, the Essence Aromatique can be considered a hit. That it can feel a bit boring over time is then obvious. My rating should definitely be understood solely against this background; those looking for a stylish, timeless all-rounder will be well served at a reasonable price. I actually like Bottega Veneta pour Homme Essence Aromatique better than the earlier Bottega Veneta pour Homme. Although - I must not hide this - I had tested the latter back then with very little experience. I thank Ergoproxy for the successful surprise.

The two previous Bottega Venetas always catch my eye in every store due to their classically beautiful design & are stored in my mind under "pleasant light leather scents." However, none of them has really stuck with me, or at least not without a desire to purchase. A similar fate could befall the summery Essence Aromatique, as this successful blend of Versace's L'Homme & M7 Fresh appears even more subtle & lighter than its brothers. Additionally, any leather notes have been removed. Ess. Arom. is a dry-masculine wood-citrus scent. Not outdated, but timeless. Not a wimp, but intentionally understated & full of decency. A breath of fresh air among many olfactory sugary loud monkeys in the men's segment, I absolutely agree with my predecessors. Bergamot, light woods & a fine hint of patchouli that at least adds some depth. Ethereal, dry, & despite performance issues, quite characterful. You just have to reapply quickly & not be stingy. Here it shows once again: simple, still suits the classic man best. From spring to autumn a hit, in summer sometimes even a bullseye. Bottle: classically masculine Longevity: 4-5 hours scratch the average. Sillage: pleasantly inconspicuous. Conclusion: a very pleasant signature & office scent for warmer days, which meaningfully complements the BV PH series & represents a male exception in the designer segment. However, it simply does not stand out in the "normal world"!

The Bottega Veneta men's fragrance is, for me, one of the best new releases of recent years in the mid-range segment. Committed to a puristic style, it is more aromatic than herbal, yet discreet and understated. Like few others, its concept combines attractiveness and allure with simplicity and wearability. Those looking for a perfume for everyday use will find it perfectly suited here. While the subsequent flankers may hardly surpass the first fragrance in the series, the question remains whether they can match it. The bright bottle of the new Essence Aromatique signals that this time it could go in a fresher direction. The first impression is citrusy-herbaceous, striking, and very, very familiar - a reunion with an old acquaintance? A few shelves over it stands, confirming in direct comparison: the opening is Armani's Eau pour Homme! The quintessential Armani had its heyday in the 80s and 90s, and of course, the 2013 remake could not quite live up to nostalgic memories. That Eau was a real stinker, with basil and lemon, still very typical of the time of Aromatic Fougères. However, the version available today is still quite potent, as is fitting for a contemporary fragrance. In Essence Aromatique, Amandine Clerc-Marie employs this accord quite differently than Roger Pellégrino did back then. For her, the tone is three levels softer. It presents itself in the top note, only to send restrained impulses down to the base. This is powdery-woody and quickly makes its presence known. Its understated nature is thematically connected to the other two fragrances in the series. The fact that the fragrance development is already over after two hours could have been considered in the naming, perhaps with the addition of "Cologne". Amandine Clerc-Marie has earned her stripes by placing a classic accord in a completely modern framework, perhaps introducing it anew to a younger audience. Personally, however, I have never felt the need to rub myself with basil and lemon. Armani's Eau - in whatever form - is therefore not part of my collection.

I accidentally tested this for the first time in spring. Since I liked it, I wanted to test it a second time and sprayed on the women's version. Of course, that is not comparable, and soon I realized my mistake. When I encountered it again today during a sale, I had to spray it on once more, and what can I say. This herbaceous citrus freshness is just exactly what I need on hot days. It simply can't be sweet for me. The saleswoman kindly pointed out that it is for men, but I just said that no one will notice when I wear it. Now it's mine, and summer can come.

With "Bottega Veneta pour Homme Essence Aromatique | Bottega Veneta," we are undoubtedly dealing with a masterpiece - always within the limits of what a cologne aims for and is capable of achieving. Most readers will know: The Essence was discontinued some time ago. It shares the fate of all current fragrances distributed under the Bottega Veneta brand by Coty.

Hhmm, I wonder what this will be: the first men's fragrance that I comment on! The comment is triggered by two things. I own the "female" counterpart, the Essence aromatique pour femme, and I gifted the fragrance to my husband - kind of a Yin and Yang thing.

The fragrance composition of Bottega Veneta's Essence Aromatique, available for men since 2016, I consider to be very well done. Essence Aromatique starts with a strong citrus-fruity top note, which soon gives way to a sour green, slightly woody underlying herbaceousness.

Essence Aromatique is the walk through the evening pine forest, after a brief bite into a somewhat green lemon at the edge of the woods. The freshness is especially present at the beginning, but the deeper the path leads into the forest, the woodier and stuffier it becomes.

Today was a long day, and my husband and I are settling into our sofa universe in anticipation of Mr. Jauch. I’m looking forward to showing off my knowledge - because when I look around, nothing shines in this room. Well - no one can see it. Not fully thought through yet, the phone rings and Mani announces his visit in 30 minutes. "Mani is coming, and when he says he’s coming, he arrives promptly," I sing to my bewildered husband. We both feel the flush rising to our faces. A fever spike? I quickly consider whether I should spruce myself up or the living room? Only one can be done. What will please him more? Division of labor. My husband will clear the table of bottles and little bottles - and bits and bobs - while I work on my style. My husband tidies up like a roadie and I fluff up my flattened hair. Perfume in the hair unfolds particularly well, and I feverishly reach for it - fever. Ooh la la - what a fruity effect. Soft plum flatters me, and tart grapefruit focuses me. I carefully apply a line of eyeliner, accompanied by alluring jasmine. Powdery vanilla orchid goes hand in hand with my nude powder.
