The aromatic almond harmonizes with my now shiny eyes, and the plum-colored lipstick creamy emphasizes my mouth. The timid little bunny has turned into a sexy bunny. The scent of transformation. Mani rings the bell: All set? - Of course!

The little rascal! Thanks to the lovely Mrs. Nickhun, I get to meet him. :-) Jimmy comes along on his little, chubby legs, with a giant basket of sweets that he immediately tips over my arm - without regard for losses. A cloud of the finest candy envelops me, sweet, red, creamy. The berries (where are they even??? They are not listed, but I smell them anyway) dominate, but the little guy turns around and pours sweet, heavy plum syrup over me - delightful! So REALLY sweet, but dark, while I find the Escada Limited Editions suitable for summer and somehow fresh-sweet, little Jimmy is a bit stocky. ^^ This doesn’t detract from the fragrance at all; on the contrary. The flowers and sandalwood prevent it from becoming TOO sweet, or rather, the base keeps the squeakiness in check, even the benzoin doesn’t bother me here. A full, sweet gourmand. Reminds me of "Bonbon" by V+R. It makes you crave the red Campino candies. ^^ But... after three-quarters of an hour, only a not-so-sweet hint remains, little Jimmy has sulkily left the stage and slammed the door behind him. Sorry Jimmy, but you already exist in other outfits and above all, the boys are significantly more loyal ... uh, more durable than you. But what I have from you, I will enjoy very, very much. :-D

On Saturday, I had nothing to do and was just bored... I called my grandfather and asked him if he would like to go to the perfume store with me again, and he didn't need to be asked twice :)). On the way there, he asked me what scents I wanted to test, and I simply said that I wasn't quite sure yet but that we should just let ourselves be surprised :) And it was worth it! :D Once we arrived, I looked around a bit... Everything I should know, I already knew... The new releases unfortunately didn't blow me away.... Sooooo, on to further searching..... Until I stood in front of the Jimmy Choo perfume shelf and the bottle of Fever caught my eye:))) I found the bottle alone to be beautiful*-* I know the original Jimmy Choo, and I didn't like it at all because it has some annoying synthetic note that bothered me a lot... But Fever is completely different! Much, much prettier and above all more interesting :) My grandfather also said that the bottle is very beautiful :D I first considered spraying Fever on a test strip because I didn't know the scent yet, but my curiosity was greater, as I was very interested in how it would smell on my skin:))) I sprayed a bit on my wrist.... And I was immediately head over heels in love!*-* (Which rarely happens to me with fragrances!) The scent..... starts with a beautiful and sexy lychee + grapefruit note (The plum note was only briefly perceptible on my skin).... simply wonderful!*-*-*-* I must emphasize that I have NEVER smelled such a harmonious scent progression like this one! No note stands out or is overpowering! Neither synthetic nor unbearable, everything in the scent progression is just lovely!:))) But let's continue with the scent description!:D I can almost say that I could detect a very light but soooo damn beautiful raspberry note*-* Vanilla orchid.... How should I describe it.... I can't find the right words for this note, it is such a beautiful, sexy, sultry, and mysterious vanilla that gives the scent and its progression an indescribably beautiful depth*-* Jasmine is very lightly but still in the most beautiful form to smell! Jasmine adds a slight but minimal pleasant freshness to the scent progression... The tonka bean and almond note is really noticeable in the base note*-* Almonds and tonka merge and give the scent a beautiful and seductive creamy note; you just don't want to take your nose off your wrist because it smells sooo good :D Especially, I spent half the day just smelling my wrist like a crazy person :D This is something I have only experienced with the La Nuit Trésor fragrances....Sandalwood gave the scent a subtle powdery note...(For those like me who don't handle pure scents well, Fever will be very satisfying as the powdery aspect is very delicately and pleasantly done :)))) I also read here that the scent shouldn't last long, and now I speak for myself... It held extremely well on my skin; I could smell it for about 6-7 hours, and my mother could also smell it strongly, especially when she sat next to me. So my conclusion... Those who, like me, love dark, feminine, and sexy scents will definitely be very happy with this one!:)) In my opinion, it's also perfect for going out! My grandfather also said that he hasn't smelled such a good women's fragrance in a long time :D So it must mean something good ;) I hope I didn't sound crazy in my scent description, but I describe fragrances as I smell and perceive them! :)

This fragrance is unfortunately a blind buy fail for me. I don't want to say that the scent itself is bad, but it has zero longevity on me and disappears after just a few minutes. It lasts a bit better on clothing, but not by much, and I have to spray a lot and then really sniff it. It was a blind purchase based on a few YouTube recommendations, and I was looking for a warm, sweet autumn scent. It is indeed quite warm and soft, but it has too many points that really bother me. The bottle and the packaging are really pretty, and the price I got Fever for was truly a bargain. However, I have to say that I can't really pick out any of the individual notes, neither plum, nor grapefruit, neither jasmine nor coffee, which I have seen listed elsewhere. My first impression was actually quite good; on paper and in the bottle, the scent smelled really pleasant, although I spontaneously thought that it somehow seemed too trivial to me. On my skin and clothing, it is a disaster, also has a somewhat old-fashioned, unpleasant quality. I can understand the comparisons to Black Opium (even though I find BO significantly better in comparison) and I can imagine that anyone who likes BO will also like this one (if Fever works with their body chemistry). I also read a statement here that this fragrance has a Maggi note, and although I couldn't imagine that for the life of me, I absolutely have to agree, as that Maggi note actually passed by my nose as well. I can't seem to get over that now, and it certainly doesn't endear the scent to me. It makes me really sad, as the reviews were mostly really good, and the bottle and scent notes were promising. Overall, it is just too insignificant for me, lacking depth and dimension, and especially with zero sillage and longevity, which I really hate. Did I perhaps get a defective bottle? I really don't understand the many good reviews. Fever, I was really looking forward to you and wanted to like you, but unfortunately, you don't evoke any fever in me, just a disappointed shake of the head. I am still very interested in Jimmy Choo EDP; can someone tell me if the longevity there is really that good and if the scent is as unique as I've read many times?

Beautiful dark purple bottle with velvety contents. The first spray lets dark berry notes crawl into the nose, very gourmand and delicious. Like a very dark forest berry in a fine Belgian bitter chocolate. Wow, I'm really high on this, you have to like it, it suits the autumn with its cold and wet windy days very well. The color of the bottle penetrates directly into my heart and warms it up, the perfume becomes vanilla-like and a little woody, almost with a hint of Oud??? And then this extremely delicious fruity slightly bitter fruit note. A very nice scent, perhaps more suitable for the hours in the afternoon and evening, it is quite seductive. Even 4-5 hours later, the dark little fruit still has its presence, softer but no less in focus. Somehow this is an exotic scent due to the fruits, it almost reminds me of very fine and particularly elegantly crafted candied fruits lying in a fine wooden box dusted with a bit of vanilla. Succumbing to this delicacy... Oh, I've been caught... mischievous smile!

When it's freezing cold outside and a woman has to make her way to work early in the morning, she needs a comforting companion and soul soother that allows her to escape from the down comforter, tear herself away from the scent of warming morning coffee, and venture out into the frosty snowstorm...brrrr !!
I really don’t understand why this fragrance is being criticized so harshly, because it truly isn’t!

So as I was once again crawling through various fragrance pyramids, I stumbled upon you. You present me with a seemingly beautiful composition that I immediately like. The next time I’m out and about, I’ll test you & see if we match, I thought to myself. Yesterday was the day & I saw you standing on the shelf. Relatively inconspicuous, yet also elegant.

After my first Jimmy Choo I Want Choo Forever could only prove itself as a test spray, too sweet, too syrupy like cherry liqueur, a party girl in a leather mini skirt with a sequined top and high heels, which I'm not, I turned my back on the brand for years. Until my favorite perfume friend whispered something about Fever to me.

When I was passing the time at London airport in 2018, I discovered this fragrance rather casually. The bottle somehow caught my eye, so I sprayed a little on my wrist and strolled on, as I actually had no intention of buying anything. But this scent immediately captivated me.

Do you believe in the signs of fate? Do you pick up on when the universe seems to send you a message through an event? I knew about the release of this novelty at CK, but strangely, I didn't pay it the proper attention. It will be one of the many flankers of CK One, I said to myself, or something trivial, boring, and crowd-pleasing, with a lot of ambroxan as has been fashionable in recent years. And so, I avoided it until a few weeks ago. Then, I got some perfumes bought online, and among them is a pack of Defy, not required, replacing another one. I wrote to the support; they did the necessary checks, apologized for what happened, and asked me to do the replacement. I accepted. I sent the package back and waited for the sought-after perfume to arrive. A week went by. It's December 8th. The courier rang, and I ran to collect the package. I was excited, couldn't wait to smell the perfume and write my first impressions right away as it's a holiday in Italy, so I had some free time to do it. I opened the package and noticed that they had sent me Defy again to my enormous amazement mixed with regret. Why Defy again? But hell, what's going on? I immediately got in touch with the support, explaining yet another mistake. "There must be some problem with the warehouse. Let's check and let them know," they told me. The next day they informed me that, given the recurrence of the inconvenience, I could keep Defy as a token of their apology and that they had issued a new order for the perfume I had ordered, with no extra cost. Maybe it's a sign of fate or simply a coincidence. Defy had to be in my collection, at any cost. And wearing it, my opinion of it changed. So, let's dive right in. Defy starts with an energizing coolness but quickly switches to seductive woody warmth with a hint of dry, salty smoke. We should note that, in addition to the three keynotes mentioned almost everywhere, namely bergamot, lavender, and amber, there is more to the blend. I would classify it as an aromatic, fougére, and semi-aquatic colony. I immediately get the hint of bergamot and mandarin, which gives it a sweet and fresh start, but the fragrant lavender provides a herbaceous tone already at the opening. The citrus is subdued, not as strong as typical citrus fragrances intended for summer or sport. Plus, the tangerine peel and citrus leaf make the opening a little greener and fruity but not too tart or acidic. Because of the blend of bergamot, lavender, and a warm, musky undertone that is clear from the first spritz, I get an atmosphere that belongs to the fougére family. There is something immediately familiar to me, and that reminds me of several popular fragrances for men out there. The initial blast is pleasant, no doubt. However, I don't find it innovative or disruptive. There are few edges in common with Sauvage Eau de Toilette , but Defy is more citrusy and less woody and spicy, with an open-air and perhaps oceanic taste. The heart, formed mainly of purple lavender and herbaceous vetiver, gives a touch to the fragrance that comes out dry and woody. Briefly, bitter puffs rise from the sage leaf. My nose is sensitive enough to detect this bitterness inherent in clary sage. Moreover, if you know the aqueous chord, you will catch the aqueous atmosphere of the violet leaf as I do. These are the undertones I get, and it's a proper purplish, herbaceous kind of smell in the heart. The base moves into a more decadent and seductive territory, with the scent of amber that warms it. A powerful woody and musky background contrast with the crisp freshness of the beginning. The musky and musty tones are heavy. I can hear them clearly if I bring my wrist close to my nose. Deep, earthy, animalic. Although Defy has many other notes, it is the purplish ones that shine and dominate. Not a bad thing, especially if you like amber types of fragrances rich in lavender and violet. My last word, Defy, didn't take my breath away, as I assumed, but I think it's a pleasant scent, so it's fun and non-polarizing. It is a rather versatile fragrance, but I would prefer to wear it during the day rather than at night, in the warm seasons, a good perfume suitable for the office because it is harmless. When I need to reach for a scent to smell good but subtly, this would be a contender. The projection is average to good. I feel it, and those around me should do it too. It has a fresh shower smell. It is very refreshing, with a hint of woodiness and mossiness. The only doubt is, does it take three perfumers to build a fragrance with such ordinary and lackluster notes? It will remain an unknown secret ... I base the review on a bottle I have owned since November 2021. -Elysium

With Defy the house has followed the current trend that has worked so well in the market, for this they have released what I would call the blue Calvin Klein fragrance. Smelling it reminds me of other fragrances of those styles but if you compare it hand by hand it is not exactly the same, after a fresh, clean opening and with that point between metallic aquatic that usually contain that type of fragrance, that exit will give way to a more earthy, dry heart, mainly slightly sweet, preserving a bit of the initial shine, in this phase everything is very balanced and its smell is subtle. Its background goes towards the amber. It is a fragrance made to be easy to wear, for hotter climates. A bet without much risk that can be liked by those who like simple fragrances that smell good and leave those who are looking for different and risky smells cold.

I bought Defy back then because I was looking for an everyday alternative to Davidoff Cool Water. For reasons that are unclear to me today, I chose this fragrance as it conveyed a somewhat fresh-herbaceous-aquatic vibe on the test strip, similar to Cool Water. I expected an everyday scent that works all the time; indeed, it does work for every occasion, for sports, at work, when going out. It always fits because it has no edges or corners, or anything particularly special. Yet, historically, jeans represent a counterpoint to the establishment, and the name carries a somewhat rebellious defiance - however, I truly miss all these attributes. I don't want to be unfair; it's not bad, but it's just nothing special. The bottle and the advertising convey a denim color, yet the complementary clothing piece and accessory that would complete the outfit in an interesting and unique way are missing. What remains is an inconspicuous scent that doesn't disturb but also doesn't enchant. The bottle is now empty and will remain so.

A basic fresh scent with citrus, a bit of sweetness, some floral notes, and a hint of earthy and woody notes in the base. However, these are definitely on the more synthetic side and not particularly decipherable. Pleasant, but nothing more interesting than a basic fresh, body wash. Longevity is relatively poor, projecting relatively minimally and lasting only a few hours even as an intimate scent. It's hard to believe anyone would call it a bad smell, and I've honestly had more people compliment this than some of my other fragrances. As someone who likes storytelling in fragrances, who enjoys more challenging notes, and who ultimately wants to smell something unique, this is absolutely none of these things.

In the past, not everything was better. But sometimes it certainly feels that way. I am often glad, or at least relieved, that I am not a child today when I read (or observe) how mean children can be to each other. When I was little, being 'mean to other kids' meant holding someone back at the bus stop by grabbing their backpack - or taking someone's gym bag and throwing it onto the roof of a garage. That was annoying, for sure. But unlike today, where even thirteen-year-olds post real or fabricated compromising content about their peers on Instagram, Facebook, or elsewhere (which remains on the internet until the end of time), the gym bag incident was annoying but fundamentally harmless. The idea of grafting an (over-)pointed fruity note onto a fragrance that is otherwise (over-)conservatively masculine arranged (here: pepper, wood, and patchouli) is not new. On the contrary, Aventus and its famous pineapple note are perhaps the most prominent example of a 'cheeky fruity scent for men', and even Bleu de Chanel (where it is grapefruit instead of pineapple) relies on such a concept. Jimmy Choo Man uses a nearly identical formula - not even attempting to disguise this - and yet it does not come close to the - certainly not uncontroversial - qualities of the two aforementioned 'classics'. It should be noted that many other 'fruit meets sport' candidates appear far cheaper and more synthetic - in contrast, Jimmy Choo Man is almost reassuringly peaceful. Conclusion: it is not truly terrible - but in its almost provocative lack of ideas and predictability, it is simply unnecessary. Not quite as bad as nude pictures on Instagram - but as silly as a gym bag on the garage roof. Annoying, yes. But ultimately harmless.

Since I found Man Ice for one friend yesterday, I tried Man for the other friend today. He is a humorous drummer who likes to hit the drums hard - but a fragrance shouldn't knock him off his feet, as he is sensitive. Man should suit him, as the ingredients are balanced and keep him in rhythm. Honeydew and mandarin are clear and aquatic, and the lavender radiates calmness. A gentle, soothing opening. The pink pepper appears soft and sweet - but adds spice to the mix. The suede feels comforting in the background, and the woods are light and translucent. Patchouli wafts gently above. A casually elegant fragrance - with a sense of finesse - that my dear friend also displays in his interactions with me. I will repay him with this harmonious scent.

I just had to test this fragrance, especially since "Jon Snow" is endorsing it. And I was positively surprised. However, the scent of Jimmy Choo cannot deny who it is imitating. It is the flagship of Chanel. I would describe Jimmy Choo as a more watery version of Bleu de Chanel. And that is also the reason why I am considering adding this fragrance to my collection. As much as I love Bleu, it is not particularly suitable for summer, as it tends to become a bit too sweet for my taste. Unfortunately, this newfound lightness comes at the expense of longevity: I can’t perceive the scent for more than four hours... In short: this fragrance certainly has "good genes" to be able to stand the test of time in the market.

When I had the new, first men's fragrance from Jimmy Choo under my nose, I immediately thought of the title of Unruh's comment... How bland & characterless can a scent be? And this as the first men's perfume from a major brand. Quite pathetic and cowardly. And yet, Jimmy Choo is no small name; the presentation is pretty & all creative and successful possibilities were open... and then such a generic fragrance that tries not to hurt anyone. But it hurts me even more, because with a decent, distinctive perfume, there would have been potential at Jimmy Choo... Would have, could have, if only, you see, I’m getting lost in wishful thinking and I’m "just" a critic and neither a perfumer nor a senior employee or consultant at Jimmy Choo. But I can get worked up about something like this! I’ve often heard that Jimmy Choo Man is the better Invictus... what nonsense! It’s just prettier on the outside; the rest could really learn something from Rabanne's trophy, it’s not even a light version. JC Man is a fresh-fruity forget-me-quick. Mandarin and melon at the start, but they are very synthetically smeared and don’t really refresh. I hardly perceive pineapple, so at least they didn’t try to jump on the Aventus bandwagon, which I initially suspected. There’s no talk of a base; in the heart, even the often generously noticeable and used pepper is diluted and lacks courage. Grade: almost 6! Bottle: really valuable and beautiful. Sillage: not worth a word Longevity: 4-5 hours - at least longer than the scent stays in your mind. Conclusion: almost worse than a stinking experiment... because that at least requires some courage. This doesn’t stink, but it simply puts you to sleep incredibly.

The scent generally has a pleasant honey melon aroma. This makes it great for everyday wear, especially if you’re looking for something subtle for the season, autumn and winter. Although the fragrance has a moderate finish in terms of sillage and longevity (max.

I wouldn't have thought that I would stumble upon a fragrance in the local orange drugstore that I don't know yet. I don't even know the brand. Rightly so... "Jimmy Choo Man" starts off with a lot of fruitiness. I can clearly smell melon and mandarin, both very artificial and too sweet. Here and there, a hint of pepper comes through.

Eternity Aqua by Calvin Klein is a wonderful flowery girlie perfume.First comes the opening with white flowers and then the dry down is a sweet apple mystery.Has some "pink" notes in it however there is no rose in the perfume notes.I suggest this perfume for Spring and for young girls!It is very refreshing and uplifting.Fresh, clean aquatic a must for summer also!!

This scent feels like splashing the water of a cool mountain spring on your face, watching the sunrise on a cool summer morning. It is distinctly aquatic but in the way of freshwater rivers rather than the marine quality of the sea. The combination of gardenia, apple and magnolia impart the perfume with a clean, feminine sweetness softly entwined with the fresh punch of cucumber. I first bought this perfume in a drugstore because it was very affordable. In the following years, I have completely fallen in love with the scent. It is very disappointing that it has been discontinued, so I have been using my bottle sparingly. It is certainly more of a summer perfume rather than spring, and the cool aquatic scent brings a much-needed burst of freshness to humid summer days.

Eternity Aqua found its way into my collection after some twists and turns. I don't know the original Eternity, whether that's an advantage or a disadvantage I can't judge. I'm just being optimistic, so I can approach this scent completely unprejudiced. I tested Eternity Moments back then and found it very beautiful, but at that time it was too "grown-up" for me. The beautiful campaign with Scarlett Johansson has stuck in my memory until today, as has the Eternity line. So I tested this fragrance under the delusion that it was the new summer flanker, which, to my delight, is supposed to contain wisteria. Smells great, but no wisteria, what a fool I am. Did I confuse the two? Nevertheless, I had to have EA because of its beautiful and fruity freshness. Many thanks to Waldfee for the nice swap. Eternity Aqua opens with a hearty bite into a delicious red apple that just drips with fruit juice. It's possible that this impression is enhanced by the watery, fresh coolness of the cucumber. I don't find it particularly synthetic. A cool, fresh, and very fruity breeze welcomes me here, underlined by the most interesting cucumber note, which I already liked in Eau Mega. Sweet apricot puree joins in, which is almost creamy. Fortunately, there's no sugary sweetness, as the apricot mixes with the slightly tart apple, and thus it is born: the Aprikapfel. The peony only lightly swings in with a delicate pink touch, standing as a godmother in a white dress. It doesn't rush into the heart note. A large bouquet of white flowers is handed to me here. No vigorous left-right combination. Feminine, fresh, modern, elegant, and yet casual. I really like that the scent, although so fresh, zesty, fruity, and aquatic, still comes across as very elegant and feminine and doesn't drift into sporty territory. I also find it nice that there are no citrus fruits here. Unfortunately, the latter sometimes develop a shrill and cleaning product-like scent in great heat and high humidity for me, so to speak, they enter into a heavy affair with Mr. Clean. The slightly synthetic, aquatic undertone now comes into play more strongly. This smell could possibly lead to headaches, but it doesn't bother me. I prefer to compare it to a lightly swaying satin blanket, similar to a trampoline for the indicated fruits and flowers, which reflects the gradient of the bottle. This image lasts for several hours, losing some of its fruit acidity and becoming softer, almost creamy. The fresh and clean character remains throughout, giving a fresh feeling, as if just stepped out of the shower, even at muggy 38 degrees. The woods are perceived more as a delicate, sun-bleached framework, musk lightens the scent, and cedar adds depth. The sweet hybrid still rolls around here, albeit somewhat faded. The longevity is surprisingly good for the fruity-fresh air kiss. It lasts a good seven hours on me. The sillage is rather average. The scent is perceivable to those around me as a light pleasant aroma, but they can't pinpoint the exact source. Especially during the last heatwave, the scent was a pleasant companion for days and managed to convince me. A nice all-rounder in a color-coordinated bottle, only the cap feels a bit cheap. Anyone who is a fan of aquatic scents like Cool Water or Eau Mega might want to take a sniff here. Moreover, I find it very nice that the scent is very feminine due to the floral notes despite the freshness and is thus also suitable for going out and celebrating. Hopefully, summer still has many hot days and exciting nights in store.

I find that aquatic scents smell great on so many others. Fresh, clean, cheerful, airy, and so on. On me, somehow... not. I've tried for years. Tested many different perfumes. It's always the same. At first, the scent smells wonderful. Fresh, clean, cheerful, airy, and so on. And then it drifts away. Suddenly, I start to feel uncomfortable. Somehow cold. Impersonal. Not like me. I don't know why. A while ago, a friend who works in a perfume shop convinced me to try this scent. I was there spontaneously, and we chatted a bit, and I told her about my problem with aqua scents. She showed me this one, saying it was quite different. She sprayed it on. Yes, it smelled good. Delicious, like summer. The cucumber is very noticeable, which I like. We talked a bit more, and the summery top note lingered for a long time. I thought, okay, I'll take this one, this scent is different. I went home, showed the scent to my husband. He thought it was nice too, light indeed. And then it happened, as it had to. Shortly after I got home, I no longer felt comfortable. I smelled increasingly sharp jasmine. I wanted to wait it out, ignore it. But it got worse. And the base never settles on me. It remains foreign, cold, too much jasmine. I tried. Different occasions. Different weather. But it stays the same. I passed it on. To a woman who, strangely enough, smells delicious with it and feels fresh, clean, cheerful, airy, and so on. I believe that with Calvin Klein Eternity Aqua, my era of trying aquatic perfumes comes to an end. It's a shame about the cucumbers; maybe I'll find one that smells cozy and warm, homey and not foreign, despite the cucumber.

I haven't been able to test the popular women's classic Eternity yet, and I couldn't find much to appreciate in the men's counterpart either, unlike its numerous admirers. For me, it's not the best CK fragrance, but by no means bad. Now my dear friend pulled out some dusty samples from her closet while cleaning, including Eternity Aqua. I can only agree with the comment below: very trivial. But also fleeting. An interesting, wet, aquatic cucumber in the opening, adorned with some fruity notes. I just about like that. However, the floral medley that follows is utterly disappointing. Undermined by the aquatic base note, it takes an absolutely disappointing turn after the good start. Soapy, slightly woody, slightly headache-inducing. The bottle is attractive, but it could also be the 100th CK One Summer flanker. Does every somewhat successful fragrance really need a sport/aqua or light version? I say NO. Longevity is a pitiful 5 hours... pitiful. Sillage is like a summer breeze... in winter. Which means: very thin and almost frozen. Overall, another Aqua flop... it's a shame that the much-discussed Aqua doesn't wash these versions off the market even faster!

~ Inspiration ~ I received a sample of this, otherwise I probably wouldn't have tested it, as I didn't like "Eternity" that much either. ~ Bottle ~ The simple, elongated, flat shape has been retained. In keeping with the name "AQUA," the liquid is presented in shades of blue. ~ Scent ~ Pure, aquatic, and fresh.

Beautiful Belle Love could be a love story translated into fragrance. At the beginning, struck by lightning, an eccentric rose, slightly leaning towards the gourmand-fruity direction through almond, vanilla, and orange blossom honey, collides with down-to-earth elements like patchouli and amber. I find this start quite stormy and loud; the parties still need to find each other, passionately fighting for their positions. I observe this from a respectful distance and am not quite there yet, missing the harmony between the protagonists. It may be the almond (I think of Amaretto) or patchouli that slightly stings my nose and disturbs the overall impression, but one cannot overlook it; this is not a subtle fragrance. As characters smooth out over time, the contrasts here also find a common ground after a while; the impression becomes creamier, softer, more pleasant, and by the end of the fragrance's development, I am enveloped by the ever-pleasant scent of vanilla-amber-musk. Beautiful Belle Love is not really my thing. I would see the fragrance more on a younger, somewhat extravagant person. Longevity and sillage are good to very good. I am curious how long this creation will hold up in the market.

Normally, I prefer short statements, but here more needs to be said. Lauro was the start of my fragrance journey. Back then, I didn't know that I was dealing with a little masterpiece. This scent is very hard to describe. Lauro is delicate yet energetic. Green, but not a "freshie." Aromatic, but not herbal. I don't overly detect any of the fragrance notes. Everything is wonderfully balanced. Bay leaf, rosemary, and sage are accompanied by floral notes. Wood, resin, and pepper remain in the background. Lauro is pure elegance. If I had to describe the scent with an image, it would be a walk through a Mediterranean garden in spring. A great love.

And bind me to it forever ... For me, the perfect scent. As much as I feel, so little can I express in words. A balance and elegance that I only know from other perfumes in the line and from the old Egoist from Paris. Laurel, soft pepper, and woody accords come together effortlessly to create a perfect melange. The sillage is powerful but not intrusive, and the longevity is unmatched. Even after washing, I can still enjoy it. It’s a shame that this masterpiece is no longer produced. If I could take one scent across the Styx, it would be this one. I bow humbly

My first fragrance was the good old Boss in the mid-80s. A simply designed bottle, straightforward yet a scent I will never forget. Since then, I have tested, bought, and sprayed - I don't know how many - fragrances, but the longer I do this, the harder it becomes to find something truly new. It feels like everything has already been done or smelled. Of course, the industry itself can't reinvent the wheel. There are countless ingredients that can be mixed in different ways, but eventually, all possibilities are exhausted, and new creations inevitably resemble a fragrance that already exists or existed in at least a similar form. There are certainly trends, like the Oud in recent years, which nearly every manufacturer incorporated into their 14th flanker, but otherwise...? As I get older, I no longer seek out fragrances that run around like a loudspeaker, shouting everything left and right. I appreciate sillage and longevity, but there is still a fine line between being intrusive and subtle. And so I ultimately stumbled upon the Parco Palladiano line from Bottega Veneta. Two years ago, I was fascinated by the bottle because it looks like a glass into which numerous prisms have been cut. An optical highlight, without a doubt. The price scared me off so much back then that I didn't even test it. This time - and as I said, in search of something special - I allowed myself to be tempted into a blind purchase, which created a mix of bad feelings and anticipation until delivery. The unboxing itself is unspectacular; for the price, I expected more than a plain cardboard box. Even though I don't care for velvet boxes, I throw both types straight into the trash. Still, a little appreciation for the consumer would have been nice. The bottle, yes, as mentioned, very attractive, yet here too is a point of criticism: the cap. While visually adapted to the bottle, removing and replacing it just doesn't match the price. Too tight, too heavy, you have to apply some force. A magnetic closure would certainly better reflect Bottega Veneta's own standards. However, the sprayer does a good job and releases the contents with vigor into the air. Wait a moment, let it settle, and then take a deep breath. Classified as spicy-green, I would perhaps add woody, initially maybe even slightly fresh, definitely pleasant, and super pleasant. A true nose-pleaser. I can't detect the announced rosemary. Sage can quickly become annoying if too prominent (like in throat lozenges), but here it is finely dosed and combined with bay leaf, creating a fantastic composition. Green fragrances are often risky because they can drift into mustiness, but here, let me say in advance, that doesn't happen even after hours. To me, the fragrance feels soothingly calming. It's not a forest walk in the usual sense, as it's too light, but with the aforementioned "freshness," perhaps better expressed as "lightness." PP V Lauro doesn't overwhelm you in the thicket or in the moss; despite its green character, it carries energy. I find myself repeatedly enjoying the scent. When I sit down, a little whiff wafts from my open shirt into my nose. Lauro is classic without being boring. It feels very natural compared to many synthetics. Omnipresent, but never intrusive or loud. A statement without making a grand entrance. The fragrance doesn't need to do that; it works just fine as it is. Passing by others, it leaves a fine impression without overwhelming anyone. It simply makes its mark. Very, very elegant, very successful. Throughout the day, the lightness gives way to a slightly intensified green, and the woody undertones present from the beginning become more pronounced, emphasizing the masculine character. Lauro carries me through the day and is still my companion at dinner. At the beginning, I mentioned that more or less every fragrance has been done before in some way or another. And yes, of course, there are plenty of green fragrances from other brands, yet this one is something special. Because the complete arrangement is nearly perfect for me. A real blockbuster. The fragrance scores full marks with me; I simply can't find a point of criticism. Sillage and longevity can be individually increased depending on the desired dosage. However, overdoing it in terms of fogging does not match Lauro's character. Normally, it lasts 10 hours, which is quite decent. I have already expressed my thoughts on the bottle. Now we need to talk about the price. Okay, the bottle isn't off the shelf, but the people at Bottega Veneta are charging according to the motto "take it from the living; the dead don't pay anymore." 170 bucks for 50ml is absolute pain threshold. Yes, other niche products also come with a similar price tag, and yes, luxury always sells. However, one shouldn't push the patience and willingness to buy of consumers to the limit, because once it's crossed, you've lost the customer. A fragrance with a unique selling point that I will surely enjoy wearing in the fall and winter!

I am pleasantly surprised by this Choo creation, and upon looking at the notes I am even more surprised. Perhaps it's my chemistry but upon first spray this smells to me as a delicious aquatic with a musk undertone and a hint of vanilla. After a while the notes becomes more apparent and I can smell citrus (the tangerine?) *Hmmm* a sugary sweetness (strawberry?) and a featherlight tuberose note that is sprinkled with a dash of pepper, but nothing in this scent is too harsh. It's a very well balanced creation and I love it because its fresh/floral/spicy and sweet without that it smells like a mess! It's a fresh breath from the *usual * gourmand and IMHO is far more original than Choo's "Jimmy Choo". Autumn is at our doorstep...if you want a new scent to go with the new season give this one a try...this unusual seductive combination of fresh yet velvety, and floral yet spicy-sweet will keep you smiling! Well, it does me : ) Silage is: Fresh & floral yet spicy as far as your arm can reach - Longevity is: You aint Choo-ing me away anytime soon! Enjoy!

I love the warm ambery/smoky/patchouli/incense of the original Jimmy Choo, so I grabbed this to try it in the store this week. There's something about the smell of strawberry in perfumes I find unattractive, although I love the smell of real strawberries. Put that with pepper, tuberose and woods and for me, not a pleasant scentsation. I class this as melon and aquatic, a synthetic, cool smell.

Flash aptly named...my initial impression was bubblegum, fancy diamond-studded synthetic strawberry. This was followed by anise-like candy (must be the pink pepper) and a bright delicate sweetness of candy- very flirtacious. Next I went straight into a heliotrope spiral. I miss some of the jasmine and woody notes, but still it was tempting. I am not sure I could wear this...the S.A. said she liked it at first and then it gave her a migraine, so I had to make a split decision not to test on the skin since it was only 7 am and I was in the duty free shopping looking forward to a 4 hour flight in a recirculated air capsule- couldn't risk it turning cloying or uncomfortable in the pod. To me, this is an improvement to the original Jimmy Choo Fragrance which smells like a sickly alien outer-space candy to my nose....this is more wearable by comparison, but not for the faint of heart either. Try before you by these are an acquired style and taste.

This is yet another 'fume that I have °salvaged° by the technique of sequestering it away for a while until I forget about it, & then one day, coming across it again °at the back of the drawer° (either literally or figuratively) I say "let's give that another go!" & do precisely that. I kind of °pitched° into buying this, with only a little less than half my reflexes holding me back; & I think when uw do that, uw hardly if atall judge the 'fume aright. I kept picking at it & picking at it & ... until I was weary of it. Now I've simply putten the thing on, getting to know it afresh: &, for instance, that accord of various floral & fruity notes whereat I at first chafed myself "is it just a dull generick cheapo fruito-floralo job, or is there actually somewhat of art in it?" has now ¯renascated¯ itself as clearly an instance of art. Not, indeed, one of the ¯great works¯ is it; but it's definitely ^something^, and something ^well-decent^ at that. I don't know whence its familiar to me - nowhere I think: & that's the point, of course. It's a rather curious floral-fruity-woody accord in which no note stands-out conspicuously - ~well integrated~, without doubt. It's a little °sneezy° as well - seems to °tickle° one's respiratory tract a little (let none IFRA snoop be reading this - if thou art, be thou accursèd!!), and I do like a bit of that - lends a 'fume substance. The level of muskiness is quite acceptible also - the musk being of a reasonably rich kind with some swooniness - but one cannot expect a full-body olfactory-faculty musk-massage fræ a 'fume of this price-brackett. Nice bit of salvage-work there, I do deem! I'm prompted here to raise this matter of sequestering 'fumes that one has doubts about, to give them a ¯latency¯ period. I realise this properly belongs in the forum; but I'll do little more than initiate the question here. I have read in other reviews of other 'fumes in other places (yes I am being cryptic, & I shall carry on being, as ^very^ strong feelings are often involved!) in which advice is given that the flacon be left to ¯stand¯ for a month or so; & other reviews that strongly gainsay this advice, adducing that the manufacturer has already done all the ¯leaving-to-stand¯ that might ever boot it. I wonder now, having °salvaged° three or four 'fumes recently by this latency-period method, whether the worth of it ever consists in other than a metamorphosis of one's ^perception^ of the 'fume - a dissipation of the tensions and guiltitudes stemming from the buying °battle°. And it is a battle often, trying to keep one's balance & poise & right-discernment amidst the continual buffets of retail staff under a grinding brief of maximal-selling. { ... @bout vi hr later ... } Uw know, I'm liking this more & more. It's just caught me a glancing blow - which is nearly always the best way to perceive a 'fume - & momentarily I wondered what it was, assuming it was one of my more belovèd 'fumes lingering on some garment y-leften-out. And another little (or maybe notso little) thing: it synergises well with the smell of coffee. And that is important with me, and with many other, I should think. Has a pleasant evolution also, with that °sneeziness° morphing into a certain °powderiness°.

Jimmy Choo Flash opens with a strange strawberry scent, not the real juicy one, nor the strawberry flavour one, very difficult to define. I was initially curious if the strawberry will play along with the white flowers. However, this fruity opening soon dissipates and leaves no trace on the then-coming strong white flower scent, which is quite similar to Jesus Del Pozo In White to my nose. This white flower blossom stage lasts about 2 or 3 hours. It then dries down into a gentle floral-musky scent, very soothing and feminine, which is also my favourite part in Flash. The sillage is moderate and the longevity is at least 8 hours. However, I don't think I'll buy it any time soon as the white flower stage is just too similar to In White, though the drydown is lovely.

In the past, when I was a little kid and had a few coins to spare, I would go to the "kiosk" and buy things there with a serious expression. Choosing from the colorful jars was always the best part. Into the small pointed paper bags went this and that - but always the red foam strawberries - which I still like today.

About 321 days ago, I wrote a negative comment and labeled the scent as cheap water. That was after a fleeting test in the perfumery and unfortunately fatal. Since I really like Jimmy Choo, I thought I should give it another chance and have now tested it extensively.

"Flash" is much better than Choos first fragrance, which I didn't like (a fruitchouli gourmand mix). "Flash" presents itself as a floral-fresh representative, but it also has an aromatic component, offering more than just white flowers.

Flash = Trash? Somehow yes. But with a certain something! The synthetic aspect cannot be denied. To put it cautiously. But it has a recognition value, wow! At least on my girlfriend. On her, it lasts a good while. I wouldn't expect such attributes from this fragrance if I only referred to the Parfumo database as an information source.
I find Jimmy Choo Flash successful... it is a spicy perfume that reminds me of Just by Roberto Cavalli.. The sillage is wonderful, I often get compliments on the scent.. Affordable and classy :)

Sprayed on - Bam - Time jump: Vienna, 8th district, Josefstadt, year 2005, inn "Zum narrischen Kastanienbaum", courtyard, on the plate "Wiener Wäschermädel" (for non-Viennese: a delicious pastry temptation with apricots - uh, I mean apricots), above us the mad chestnut tree spreads its old branches. It is in full bloom and the honey-sweet scent with a slight bitterness lays like a fragrant blanket over the garden. This is how "Azalea" begins for me. Not with the namesake azalea, which joins later and then defines the scent experience, but with sweet chestnut blossom, honey, and vanilla included. Those who know chestnut honey or the wonderful lush scent of the chestnut blossom will also detect the characteristic slightly bitter-herb undertone here. I love it, though my children rejected it for a long time - they simply demanded "real" honey. At this stage of the fragrance, "Monte Bianco," which Floramalia describes in her comment as beautifully appetizing, cannot be overlooked. For me, it is actually THE nightmare par excellence. Much of what I fear and avoid in fragrances is combined here: honey, vanilla, sweetness, and creamy, rich creaminess. Therefore, I can also understand Caligari's statement that the fragrance did not really convince him. That would have been it for me and "Azalea," if it weren't for, yes, if it weren't for another component that would come into play. The bloom of the azalea. We lived in the USA for some time, and there was the "National Arboretum," a landscape garden divided into thematic areas, including a "Holly Park" - made up of various types of holly, and also the "Azalea Valley." When we first visited the arboretum, we made fun of the names on our way there, following the motto: The Americans really know how to blow their own horn: Park, Valley - how big can it really be? Well, several hours later we knew: gigantically big! In this azalea garden, I experienced for the first time in my life an azalea bloom that developed a scent in the humid-warm climate that hung like a bell over the valley. I could not get enough of the fine, delicately sweet natural scent, and during that and all subsequent years there, the arboretum during azalea bloom was an absolute must. Currently, I live in a small town that also has a wonderful old landscape park. When the linden trees bloom, I ride long rounds alone on my bike, but when azaleas and rhododendrons are in full bloom, my three men must join me - the desire to share and enjoy this natural spectacle with them is too great. In Bottega Veneta's "Azalea," the vanilla sweetness of the beginning gradually retreats and makes way for the scent of the azaleas. It becomes more transparent and translucent, developing into a delicately romantic floral scent of astonishing longevity. It envelops me like a web, woven from the dust threads of the azaleas. It lingers with me for a long time until it dissolves with a final melancholic sigh and fades away. Only a hint of bloom remains, a whisper of vanilla. Among the perfumes I use, there are not many scents of this kind. Normally, I prefer perfumes with structure and profile, with a more exciting development and edges and corners. The exceptions "La Chasse aux Papillons," my linden blossom wonder, and "Azalea" are both scents that touch me because they evoke memories that are deeply emotional and personal. Memories of past times, places, and people in my life, but at the same time they carry the promise that everything in life has its time - and that the linden trees, the chestnuts, and the azaleas will bloom for us again next year.

My skepticism towards gourmand fragrances is significant and usually keeps me from testing them. However, since I received a sample of Azalea from a very nice perfumer, I really like the Parco Palladiano line, and the scent is described as not sweet, I decided to conduct a full-day office test. To me, the fragrance smells almost exclusively of the wonderful Italian dessert "Monte Bianco," made from cooked and pureed chestnuts, meringue, and fresh whipped cream, flavored with a bit of vanilla. I can't detect anything floral and also notice no scent progression. For fans of such dessert scents, this is surely a great fragrance. I usually refrain from associating fragrances with seasons, but here I can clearly understand the autumn associations. The similarity to Eau Duelle, which is mentioned, I only perceive in the base. Due to the sweetness, Azalea is not for me; the sillage is pleasant and the longevity is also acceptable.

For a few weeks now, I have been the proud owner of Parco Palladiano IV, as I was able to purchase a partially used bottle here at the Souk. I haven't been able to test all the fragrances in this wonderful line yet, but among the three I know, this one is the absolute winner and at the same time a big surprise for me! Surprise in the sense that vanilla scents have never ranked high on my popularity scale, as they simply seem too sweet to me. Vanilla is predominantly associated with sweet things - desserts, cakes, cookies, and all sorts of other treats. However, if you smell a vanilla pod, you will perceive the typical scent, but it is not sweet. This became clear to me once again when I spoke with a spice seller shortly before Christmas, who offered a sea salt with vanilla, and I first asked him how this works together and what it could be used for. He offered it to me to try and pointed out that vanilla in its natural form is not sweet at all, and he is absolutely right; the combination of salt and vanilla convinced me and now has a place in my kitchen. But what does this have to do with this fragrance? A lot, because the fact that I could spontaneously get excited about it also has to do with the fact that the vanilla here comes across very fine, almost a bit bitter, and absolutely not sweet. In combination with the azalea, it creates a wonderfully creamy scent that is not sweet, yet soft and enveloping. The chestnut in the fragrance pyramid puzzles me a bit, as I have never perceived a scent from a chestnut that has stayed in my memory. I can only speculate that the slightly bitter note with which the fragrance always greets me is attributable to the chestnut. Regarding longevity, it can be said that it is quite good, but the fragrance is never intrusive; rather, it is a soft, delicate cloud. I thought at first that it wouldn't last too long, but since I am often approached hours after spraying it, it is indeed quite perceptible for a long time. In any case, this Palladiano is an absolute feel-good fragrance that brings me compliments time and again, and for the first time in my life, I wear a fragrance with joy and enthusiasm where vanilla is in the foreground.

This perfume has an amazing sillage and longevity. I spray it on in one room and my husband can smell it from the other side of the house. I pet the cat - boom, now she too smells like fresh fruity flowers. The perfume has a warm tone, it reminds me of a hot bath with flower petals and my favorite fruity wine. I wouldn't say it's suitable for closed environments such as the office - it's too strong. But when you go out for a walk during a summer night, wearing a light coat or just a sweater to wean off the slight cold that appears as everything around you cools down, this scent is exactly what you need.

It smells floral, fruity, and sweet at the same time and is one of the perfumes for which I have only received positive comments. Maybe it's the perfumer, because Flash has the same effect on me. By the way, if you layer Blossom with a scent from La vie est belle, you get the following scent progression, for example, for me it was like this: Top note: Simply sweet (but pleasant) Heart note: Wonderful flower meadow Base note: Red fruit compote with vanilla sauce, but not artificial, rather authentic, like at grandma's back then The combination of the two fragrances happened by chance while testing perfumes at Müller. The La vie est belle scent was either "L'eclat", the original, or "Rose". Since I have the original, I will give it a try. If this scent doesn't exist yet - it should be invented. Blossom is already brilliant on its own, but with that it's a blast :-)

Actually, I'm still haunted by the bill from the heating installation, but a discount voucher from Kstadt is also burning a hole in my pocket. What can I say? Humans are weak. And so I couldn't resist the raspberry-colored little box. As soon as I opened the box, a berrylicious scent wafted towards me. Polar bears roll towards me, as the fragrance is pleasantly cool. Red, sweet berries frozen - very appetizing. Nevertheless, Blossom does not turn into a heavy gourmand, as the sweet pea mixes in lightly, entwined with soft red rose. Sandalwood lays this delicious scent creamy on my skin. I am reminded of Baby Doll by YSL. For hours, it envelops me cheerfully and closely, as the longevity is very good. Even my husband feels attracted and realizes that this discount voucher was wisely redeemed, At night, polar bears looked kindly into my window.

This is a vibrant, spicy, peppery, citrus scent that I used to enjoy in my youth. I don't know if it's the tonka overload in the dry-down, but I just can't wear this nowadays - my tastes have changed drastically. I'm not going to discuss that starfish note marketing ploy nonsense. It was heavily marketed as a sports freshie, and it came in a plastic bottle to be chucked carelessly into a gym bag. Scent-wise, I never got the sportiness at all, but it's certainly geared towards the younger crowd, and more appropriate for warm weather. Projection and longevity are both moderate at best. Masculinity Level: The black & white CK ads weren't far off with that androgynous waxed young dude in his tighty whities.

Crave is a very light, sweet and synthetic smelling fragrance. No doubt aimed at the younger end of the perfume buying market with it's modern looking plastic bottle that will doubtless intrigue today's gadget obsessed generation. Not my favourite CK scent by a long way, but an ok fragrance all the same that can still be picked up fairly cheaply despite being discontinued.

Hello Fragrance Fam! On todays Web blog of "finding the Vintage batch" We're covering Crave by Calvin Klein. This is a soapy scent, similar in scent profile to Perry Ellis America for men (the clear bottle), JOOP Nightflight, or to a lesser extent Acqua Di Gio for men EDT. Overall it has a clean aromatic scent profile, with a sharp and salty calone sort of smell that was popular in the early 2000's. The good news is this fragrance never underwent any reformulation! Coty/Prestige produced this fragrance for Calvin Klein from 2002-2005 approximately and because of it being discontinued so quickly is why it fetches such a high price tag in todays market! Hope this helps, enjoy the journey!

I have known CK Crave for quite a long time. Long before my passion for fragrances, I had a sample of this scent in the early 2000s. Back then, I enjoyed testing samples but never bought anything. At that time, I preferred to have a small, manageable collection since I occasionally received fragrances as gifts. More than 10 years later: Stored in my memory and never really forgotten: You used to love this one, order it. Good decision. Unfortunately, it is now hard to find, as it was unjustly discontinued. Some other CKs deserve it more. The bottle is really the biggest piece of junk :-) It looks 100% cheap, even though it is unusual. It also cannot stand up. Bottom drawer. Luckily, bottles are rather secondary for me. The scent twin is Tom Ford "Costa Azzura." I can't confirm that, as I don't know it, but it's quite possible when comparing the scent pyramids. Crave is definitely something special for me, as it is really not a run-of-the-mill fragrance. It starts extremely fresh-herbaceous-spicy with a lot of bergamot, basil, and coriander. This nice herbal spiciness fits wonderfully with the fresh bergamot note. It stays like this for a long time and later fades gently. A very soft, subtle sweetness comes through from tonka, along with musk and gentle woody notes. However, this wonderful Crave spiciness remains. Overall, a beautiful scent with recognizability and not as interchangeable as many CKs. Discontinued unjustly. The performance is in the medium range and completely okay for a fresh scent. It lasts a few hours easily with a reasonably strong sillage. If you find it somewhere online: I can recommend it. A fresh fragrance with a lot of individuality.

I don't know what to think about my nose on some days. I really test carefully, no more than two perfumes per day (one on the right, one on the left), usually just one, always on the skin, and not always do the respective scent experiences provide enough for a comment afterwards. By now, I should really be getting some routine and seeing progress. How on earth can it be that with Calvin Klein's Crave, I seriously smell UHU glue as the opening??? oO It really can't be that the good CK has to stretch his perfume with so much solvent that this is the first impression... - or? The middle part doesn't get much better. Although the extremely unpleasant top note fades away very quickly, afterwards I feel like I am locked in Johann Lafer's spice cabinet. Basil, coriander, allspice... I would be lying if I claimed I could pick them out individually. To me, it just smells like a spice mix. In the base, this continues; this time I can indeed distinctly smell the nutmeg. It does get a little woody warm, but the nutmeg dominates. Let's call it spicy at best. I am disappointed. I am used to much better from CK, so I can really only say: I am disappointed. To me, the scent is neither masculine nor feminine; it is simply unpleasant, and I don't want to smell it on myself or my husband. Maybe Johann Lafer's spice cabinet fell over and he had to glue it with UHU, which would explain a lot. But how it all ended up with Calvin Klein, I'm unfortunately at a loss.

the familiar strong and spicy opening from CK, just how I love it! The fragrance notes are extensive, you can't pick out individual components. The perfume does not change until the end. I would classify it as unisex The perfume is strong but not heavy or cloying The bottle, or rather, the disposable plastic bottle does not fit at all into my CK collection.

Fabien Baron has done a much better job compared to Yves Cassar, Pascal Gaurin, and Jean-Marc Chaillan. The bottle promises an experience that the scent cannot deliver. I can hardly comment on "Crave" as a fragrance, because even though I reapplied it just 5 minutes ago, there is nothing in my nose that I could comment on.

The bottle is very creatively designed, but the scent is rather less so. I really wonder if this is supposed to be a men's fragrance. However, since it was on the men's shelf, it must be correct. Absolutely not for me. I have also heard that it has been discontinued. However, you can still buy it at Douglas.

For me this is Cartier Declaration but more “green”. Imagine Your in a wood with the sea not far away. Excellent spring fragrance & do not overspray! The opening is a wonderfull cypress leaf wich lifts your energy up!

Mild-spicy green, miles away from the nose-stinging local false cypress. A hint of nuttiness that pairs well with pink pepper. A fresh, watery impression of... cucumber? Indeed, after a few minutes, it smells like an extravagantly spiced oriental cucumber salad with coriander and a tiny, non-sweaty hint of cumin. I can only manage with pink pepper and juniper in terms of spices. Oh, and: A little salt is, after all, also essential in such a salad. It’s also conceivable, in relation to cucumber and salt, that: When preparing tzatziki, the grated cucumber must be drained; otherwise, it turns into slush. The water can be removed either by vigorously squeezing it in a dish towel or by sprinkling it generously with salt. Naturally, I prefer the former. It’s more thorough, as only with sheer force can nearly dried cucumber pieces draw out enough liquid from the creamy yogurt, resulting in a beautifully creamy-thick tzatziki. But today, one can sense the option of dehydrating with salt, if desired. As the morning progresses, I end up with a bulgur salad. Its aroma, as is well known, practically depends solely on what has been added to the durum wheat mash. In this case, I stick with coriander, rounded off with a bit of lemongrass and perhaps a pinch of sweet paprika. Just to be clear: Bottega Veneta is certainly not delivering a gourmand here, especially not in the conventional sense. And a dish arrangement of such provenance smells exquisite! However, by lunchtime, all associations with a Mediterranean buffet fade away. Of course, that’s slowly being eaten up now. So we leave the food thoughts behind. The scent becomes creamier, the spice milder and more perfumed. The green gradually reveals its balsamic sides, supported by a mossy-foamy base. Very refined, without becoming classically soapy. In the end, a gently herbaceous, yet primarily creamy green remains directly on the skin, with which the number two gently bids farewell after eight or nine hours, without any compromises to its noble appearance. I thank Gerdi for the sample.

Maybe a little upfront: the title is the program for my review. Until now, I only knew Jimmy Choo as an elegant high heels brand. My first association was "glitter, glamour, Jimmy Choo." When I heard from some entertaining YouTubers about THE vanilla perfume par excellence, I became intrigued. I mean, we are talking about vanilla here. This was already the reason to read a bit about this rather unknown scent. Unfortunately, I couldn't obtain a sample in any way. What was left? Blind buy - under the motto - no risk no fun ?. The bottle convinced me at first glance. Now to the scent! I must confess, and I am being honest here, the first spray didn't really blow me away. It wasn't bad, but buying a scent for that price that doesn't wow you left a somewhat "bitter" aftertaste for me. Well, I guess I got an everyday scent for a rather hefty price, that's fine too. What happened? A few days later, while out in the city, I sprayed myself with Vanilla Love. The scent wafted around me constantly. I was pleasantly surprised. Despite the cold, I was enveloped by an indescribably beautiful vanilla scent that I had never smelled before. On one hand silky, soft - on the other hand expressive and present. I couldn't believe it was the scent that I hadn't really liked at first. I still don't know what it was? Did it need to recover? Does the scent shine particularly in the cold? Anyway. I try to describe what I perceive: vanilla that starts with a fruity aromatic kick and gradually transforms into a spicy sweet, very, very stylish soft scent. I think the tonka bean and toffee sweeten this scent, but the other notes ensure it doesn't drift into the edible. That's art. It is not piercing or biting, not synthetic and not edible. In my eyes, this scent is an elegant, attractive fragrance with a vanilla that has simply convinced me with its diversity. I claim it enhances the beauty of every woman. I wouldn't label this scent as unisex. But again - to each their own :). In the end, I am glad to have stumbled upon this scent and to own it. P.S. every time I walk past the hallway (where the jacket I wore hangs), a waft of Vanilla Love always comes to my nose. AND that means something!!! What remains? The scent has convinced me ?.

When I close my eyes and spray 1-2 spritzes into the air around me, I feel like I’m standing in one of those small wonderful chocolate shops in Bruges. It smells so fine and delicious, a gourmand is kissing me right now. The room is cool, decorated in warm wooden tones, and the scent of such fine, expensive, rare, and highly aromatic aromas hits me so unexpectedly that I become dizzy with anticipation. I also perceive something like a hint of good old rum. Since my eyes are still closed, my feeling is that I have a very noble praline in front of me that seems to lure me in with its beautiful scent. Such good and noble cocoa beans, the finest vanilla pod, the slightly spicy note of an exceedingly expensive saffron, warm toffee, a few splashes of the best apple stomata, and a pinch of good black pepper. Can the reader follow me... divine! A delicate, finely fruity vanilla scent lingers on my skin. It lasts very well for many hours - but becomes close to the body. With this scent, one will probably be nibbled at; it is said that men are very fond of vanilla scents on a woman, I would say - let’s give it a try. The bottle is from the beautiful new series with many cut facets and the golden ball as a cap, very tasteful.

When you like floral/fruity fragrances like me, this is just not my thing. Maybe it's because it's a unisex fragrance, and I'm having a very hard time loving unisex perfumes. The salty notes in this one are not for me. The longevity is fine, the fragrance stays on me for about 7/8 hours, even when it's hot and humid in the summer. The sillage is good as well; when I wear it, I do recieve compliments from both women and men. I'm trying to let this one grow on me, but this scent doesn't work for me.. So far.

I really couldn't pass up on this one at the airport for a mere 30 euros. I've never had a bad experience with the summer editions of CK One, especially while traveling. But even in the evenings after showering or for sports, I often reach for one of the colorful bottles. What can the new one in the series offer? It certainly looks colorful and poppy, and I think the included stickers to place wherever you want on the bottle is a great idea. Now I have a perfume that no one else has exactly like it ;) The scent is a bit less striking. But still very solid. Salty, zesty, a little fruity, and very invigorating. Very lively and youthful, pulsating and tingling. Perfect for summer activities like street soccer, beach parties, or receptions all in white. It comes closest to the 2013 version. Watery and bright, a bit more masculine and a bit edgier than some of its predecessors, which I have known for almost 15 years now! The salty sea breeze is supported by minimal tea splashes that spread a sense of calm and inner peace. A combination that instills confidence. A nice, easy-to-wear casual scent that rarely goes wrong. It could have been a bit more potent, longer-lasting, and stronger for me. Although it might behave differently at home in a more temperate climate. Here in the south, perfumes seem to have a much harder time, and I feel like you encounter fragrant people here significantly less often - at least that's my experience. No wonder if the scents only last half as long or behave completely differently than at 10-20 degrees. Bottle: hip, fun, colorful. Not pretty but fitting. And eye-catching. Something different. And the individual stickers are simply genius! Sillage & Longevity: I've only been able to test it in warm Cyprus so far - but it is quite subtle and fades quickly. 4 hours at most. But of course, as always, very affordable, so reapplying isn't a hassle. Conclusion: from the look to the sea-salty summer refreshing scent - the 2019 edition of CK One Summers is a little hit. It lifts your spirits, stays fresh, and feels sexy, clean, spontaneous, and ready for any vacation. Just as it should be! I can imagine that it will someday become a popular collector's item. Especially because of its bottle. For me, it's already my second favorite in the series after the "Brazilian" 2014 version!

Hello there. It's time to test a totally mainstream fragrance again. And it's CK One Summer 2019 from … well, from CK! :D I tend to randomly test CK's summer fragrances, if I happen to remember (for example, I missed it in 2017). However, this time I was quickly drawn to this scent when I saw it on the shelf. Yes, just look at the bottle. The way "Summer" is written on it totally reminds me of comics, right? It looks like you're reading a Batman comic and the masked hero is beating up some villains, with "Pow! Bam! Wham!" written as visual sound effects, which by the way were also present in the funny Batman series from the 60s (you know, that series with Batmaaaaan. Batmaaaaan. Batmaaaaaan. Batmaaaaan. Batman. … Na na na na na na na na na na na na na, Batmannnnnnn!.. uh, you surely know the song from the series!! :D). As I said, I found the bottle interesting, which piqued my curiosity. But I might have tried the scent anyway, as I think that CK's summer fragrances are never really special, but they don't smell bad either; on the contrary, I even think that one could definitely use such a fragrance during a summer if it’s at a good price! The scent: The scent starts fresh with fruity-sweet notes. Yes, that's right, the top note mentions marine notes, but I find that these only really kick in after a little while, so at the beginning, the fragrance smells more fruity-fresh. I perceive a berry-like note, which is quite nice. However, soon this berry blends into a more generally fruity note, meaning it’s more of an indeterminate fruitiness where you just know it’s fruity without being able to name a specific fruit. The matcha tea, which smells a bit like tea, a bit like green notes, and somewhat like diluted scents, is also quite nice and comes across refreshingly, but unfortunately a bit weak. By the way, this time the sweetness of the fragrance is rather low. Aside from the top note, the scent later mainly smells marine, that is, aquatic with salty notes and a slightly woody background, and sometimes it resembles a nice, fresh shower gel. I also have to mention the synthetic notes, without which these fragrances would certainly come across much nicer, but which have never really bothered me in this fragrance line. Additionally, I felt that the synthetics in this scent are somewhat less pronounced than in some other CK summer fragrances. And so the scent remains, mainly fresh-salty-aquatic and at the very end a little woody. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is moderate, but due to the marine notes, it is slightly better than in the fragrances of the last years in this line. Up close, it should be somewhat noticeable for a while. For a summer fragrance, the longevity is quite good at over six to seven hours. The bottle: The bottle has the shape of all CK One fragrances. It is rounded rectangular, flat, and looks like a small bottle. It is transparent and clear and has this comic-like label printed on the front, where the fragrance name is written. While it looks nice and interesting, I found the older bottles with the beautiful color gradients much better, as they fit the theme (holiday/summer fragrance) better. So, the new CK One Summer 2019 turned out quite well for a CK One Summer fragrance; for me, it even belongs to the most beautiful CK Ones that I have tested recently. It’s noticeable that a certain type of sweetness is missing this time, namely that sweet note that often came across to me like an ice cream cone, which is delicious but also smelled quite synthetic. Although this fragrance is synthetic, it smells different this time and brings a bit of variety to the CK One Summer line, which often featured lime and cucumber. Because this one smells of the sea, as it has a salty aura and could appeal to anyone who likes that salty scent. Even though the salty note isn't free from synthetics, it smells nice and especially reminds me of the moist and salty air near a holiday destination, where you can't wait to run to the beach and… go into the water of course (yes, yes, I know exactly that you all expected me to write something like "Watching hot bathing beauties in sexy bikinis," tsss… I really should think about my reputation here… it’s shocking what you think of me… *sigh* … he he :D And I can't help it if bathing beauties look so great, aaaargh! :D Hmm… I guess I don't need to mention that CK One Summer 2019 is a… summer fragrance? :DD Anyway, it’s especially good during the day, especially on hot days, but still be cautious of potential blind buys, as salty notes aren’t everyone’s cup of tea, as they can sometimes come across as quite stuffy. Just give it a try, especially on a hot day, to see how you like this scent. I wouldn’t spend 40 euros on it, but I also think that especially with a good deal, you couldn’t go wrong with such a fragrance for a summer! Well, that’s it again, and I wish you all a lovely evening :)

The CK One Summer series is really great. For little money, you get a new, summery EdT every year. The 2019 version is heavily influenced by sweet and fruity accords. Notable are the tangerine and the water lily. In the drydown, aquatic notes and woods come into play. A fragrance that doesn’t clash. Any similarities to the original are only subtly present, perhaps the gentle sweetness. An affordable, summery refreshment, a perfect cool-down when the EdT comes out of the fridge and is applied right after showering! However, typical for CK One, it has a short longevity and weak sillage (about 3 hours). A successful release with a good price/performance ratio. It’s worth trying, but not a must.

The scent is very fresh and has a slight peach aroma, making it perfect for summer. In my opinion, it is more of a fragrance for young people as it is not woody or herbal, but rather fruity and fresh. It can be used for leisure, sports, etc.

I can confirm the freshness, woody....yeah...but more like damp and somewhat musty wood, yet still not unpleasant. Overall, it reminds me a bit of Febreze laundry scent. A man can wear it...but personally, I would prefer to smell it on a woman.

The oldest of my CK Summer Editions has an appealing profile on paper - and since I have liked the other editions, I had high hopes that I would like this one. And I do. A strong, cool, aquatic-citrus opening - it would definitely come off well from the fridge. Calvin Klein fragrances often have this classic freshness at the start for me.

BV, in my eyes, is a Power House. They have some really great fragrances and one of them is even ranked as no. 69 in the Top 100 Most Popular Scents for Women. That is quite an achievement for a rather small Italian company compared to mega brands as Givenchy, Dior, Guerlain and Parfum de Marlys. I have been curious about this brand since my first encounter with Eau Légère back in the early 10s. Being fond of leather smelling fragrances - I love Chanel’s Cuir de Russie, particularly the parfum - I became so happy when I first smelled the dry and unique BVEL. What a love affair! This scent will always be a true favourite and eye opener to me. After this, there was no turning back. I started looking for BV fragrances but found none. BV is not well represented in my country, so I have bought all four I have from other people. Which is why Eau Sensuelle joined my collection just a few months ago. My BV journey started out with Eau Légère, then BV signature, then Illusione and finally Eau Sensuelle. The latter is less interesting compared to the other three. She is also the lowest rated of the four - lowest rated still means highly rated (7.7). If I stay in the siblings’ term she is cute, a bit young and playful. She has not yet met the worries of the adult world and she is at the age right between wearing lipstick and playing with dolls. On the brim of adulthood. Luckily, there is the leather note at the end. Consider it the growing awareness of what is about to come over the next few years. Growing responsibilities, a blooming sexuality and a more complex look at the world. She could be Jenny in “An education” or Cassandra in “I capture the Castle”. A soon-to-become woman. BV changed my view on unisex fragrances. Before BV unisex was CK One, which I absolutely… do not like. To my nose it is just awful. BV made me think of unisex in a different and positive way. Year 2, 9/365

Before Bottega Veneta could conquer me, time passed. I turned a cold shoulder to the beautiful scent - and let myself be persuaded. Quite the tough nut. My husband can sing a song about it. But now I always buy large bottles. I didn't have such starting difficulties with eau Sensuelle. It was love at first sight, as the scent conquered me with its softness. Gently, it envelops me in butter-soft pastel-colored suede, drizzled with peach nectar and gentle bergamot. Gardenia emphasizes the flattering scent fully, but not piercingly - and jasmine crowns it with elegant jasmine. Yes, this is how I want to be embraced. Sensuelle doesn’t come on too strong - but shows undeniable presence. A charming, sensual scent, intimate, and with a yearning for togetherness. Soft conquest that makes women's - and men's hearts beat faster.

With "Sensuelle," my old mind first signals "bland, boring"; a prejudice I have not been able to shake off. How often have I been mistaken. And here with "Bottega Veneta Eau Sensuelle," that is not the case at all. I put myself in the corner and feel ashamed! The leather accord mentioned here in the base runs through the entire fragrance for me; a pleasant and harmonious greeting takes place; I feel welcomed. White peach, an ever-inviting refreshment in summer, appears ripe and juicy; yes, here too, the peach scent is juicy and wonderfully creamy! It comes hand in hand with bergamot: their aromas correspond excellently with the already present leather. Where is my often recurring aversion to leather? It is not there, and I do not miss it! On the contrary: even now, my soul is pleasantly touched; it rejoices in this encounter. Gardenia - also a somewhat tricky scent note for me - is overshadowed by the powerful jasmine rush: jasmine and leather - a successful blend that simply convinces. To crown the fragrance, pink pepper is added; the white peach is especially looking forward to it! The brand Bottega Veneta has once again succeeded in conjuring the impression of refined leather goods into a fragrance. I feel as if I am entering one of the impressive stores: fine leather nuances embrace me, but are immediately infused with powerful jasmine clouds. This climbing jasmine winds around the noble gardenia blossoms; it casts them a bit into the shade. In this fragrance composition, it is the champion!
