For refreshment, pretty glass plates with peach and bergamot slices are served, crowned with pink pepper. Unfortunately, the matching glasses filled with cool champagne do not appear in the scent. All of this has been filled into one of the typical bottles and adorned with the smooth name "Bottega Veneta Eau Sensuelle." The result is extremely pleasing: a fragrance that caresses me and provides comfort and tenderness to my (currently so often tormented) soul. These caresses are very welcome and accompany me like soft music for several hours. Elegant and charming, expressive yet unobtrusive. This "Eau Sensuelle" does not have me on a leash: we are equal partners facing life together! So we set off. Where to?

There are people who find the fine leather accord in the first Bottega scent too much, which I cannot understand. In the new flanker called "sensual" (as if the other Bottegas weren't), I don't sense any real leather. Maybe I'm just too insensitive to "delicate, soft, light suede"; I don't even know what such leather smells like in real life. In any case, it wasn't just me, but also my friend. Both of us, as confessed Bandit fans, could not recognize leather ("the way we know it"). Yet supposedly leather, as the DNA of the brand, is also present in Sensuelle, at least in the base note. And somehow you can still recognize the Bottega DNA in "Sensuelle," whether leathery or not. In any case: The scent is beautiful. It comes across as more floral and delicate than the Bottega "original," and thus the delicate pink tint of the liquid is fitting. Instead of leather, I smell musk in the drydown, which gives the fragrance the substance it urgently needs if it doesn't want to be "demeaned" to mere floral water. This new version is cleverly made - and not, as so often, just an unnecessary and boring flanker. This new EdP is very refined and fits well into the line of the already very successful predecessor Bottegas. Hard to believe that Coty is behind it.

Welcome to our temple of fragrance consumption. Here with us, mediocrity is the measure of all things. Find yourself a spot right at the front of the shelf so you stand out and our customers can discover you right away. So kids, make some room for the new girl. Come on Sensi, stand next to Deli (I've forgotten her real name, but the Be Delicious clan sends us a newcomer every few weeks). Chic your outfit all in Rose Quartz, the Pantone trend color of 2016. The first impression: a fresh, mild peach breeze - fits. Followed by a gentle, indefinable floral mix with jasmine, but nothing distinctive. Is that supposed to be leather? No, that's the currently very popular musk drydown - very good. Just don’t stand out. Fortunately, you are different from your character- and individuality-focused relatives Bottega Veneta and Bottega Veneta Eau Legere, and will therefore find plenty of appeal with our customers. Finally, Bottega Veneta has arrived at the dozen goods. It was about time. It would also be nice to have a sugared berry variant for the candy girls among our customers in the fall. And then in November the collaboration with H&M... What, this year it's Kenzo's turn, with designer fashion for H&M. Well, maybe next year then. But how about a vanilla bomb for Christmas, for the vanilla freaks? It can't be rocket science, just throw a mega vanilla cap over Sensi. And in spring then launch an aquatics in a blue box - for the freshness fanatics, of course........Mah, I'm getting scared of my clairvoyant abilities. Enough of that! I’ll stick with Bottega Veneta Eau Legere and that's that.

Minigolf may forgive me for referencing their Oktoberfest comparison now. But from today, the fun in the city is over again, and when it comes to taste, for the next two weeks, "eyes closed and through" is all that helps.

Almost right on time for the start of the "Oktoberfeste," I received a sample of a fragrance, "Bottega Veneta eau Sensuelle," which I am currently testing. And involuntarily, this scent fits right in. Perhaps it's just my occasionally blooming imagination that leads me to associate fragrances with the most impossible situations.

Expensive, soft suede. It is floral, yet for me it has a harsh, masculine touch. I can understand the white peach, but "fruity" is about the last thing I associate with this scent. I apologize in advance for any clichés: I spontaneously associate it with a Hamburg real estate agent or banker in a well-fitted suit, pretty but somewhat strict, with a tight blonde ponytail.

This smells like part Estee cologne, part Pleasures, and not as nice as either. Neither the florals or honey accord bring a richness; which the orignal had. There is a green quality- but higher pitched than the original; more like a LOV type of green. The woodsy aspect in the dry down, with the florals is unpleasantly sharp. I respect Malle. I love Flipo’s work; she is one of my favorite noses. However, Estee (Pure Fragrance spray, Super Cologne, and even edp- in “pineapple” bottles) is one of my favorite perfumes of all time, and this is a huge disappointment. For all this, they could have kept the (bad, but much less expensive) current offering.

This is the first cherry scent that doesn't turn into cough syrup on me. Hurray! IWCF opens with an almond that is a bit synthetic, but the synthetic quality disappears quickly for me. The bright, boozy cherry starts to appear as that synthetic quality disappears, and the almond becomes more soft and creamy. I only get a hint of rose, but the pepper adds a lively zing to the almond and cherry liqueur. Jimmy Choo's fruit notes always seem to work well on me. I really enjoy the cherry liqueur note. It isn't synthetic, nor does it resemble cough syrup. I get the sense of a real cherry liqueur, sweet, boozy with just the right touch of sourness, almost throughout the life of the fragrance. For a short time, I get the cherry liqueur only, but jasmine soon makes an appearance, bringing a white-floral richness of which I'm very fond. The vetiver adds a dry, earthy quality the scent needs and of which it could use a bit more, IMO. The cherry liqueur stays through a good part of the drydown, which is nice. When the cherry does fade, the vanilla, tonka, mossy drydown is nothing original, but I'm particularly fond of those notes and really like the perfectly unisex drydown. IWCF doesn't have much in common with the original IWC except in that they are both very sweet fragrances with a dominant fruit note (peach for IWC) and great longevity. IWCF is darker, slightly less sweet (althogh still very sweet) more suitable for colder weather and IMO, only, more unisex. I think this is a bit pricey for what it is, but I may buy a small bottle for the not-at-all-like-cough-syrup-which-I-hate cherry note. IWCF easily lasts all day, with strong projection and a really good sillage trail.

This smells 99% like Cacharel Yes I am Fabulous. Fruity, vanilla, lactonic. Pleasant enough, but in no way remarkable. I got this in a sample set and it was among the two samples that I enjoyed most of them. I think it is a trendy perfume profile that will sit well with the younger generation. I also think it has similarities with Yves Saint Laurent Black Opium Le Parfum.

opens with a sweet nutty almond and cherry liqueur with a mild floral note coming from the rose. The vetiver and jasmine are a smooth and woody segway to the dry down which is a creamy and sweet tonka bean with earthy oakmoss. The vanilla here is sweet and light with an earthy roundness to it from the other notes. I know a lot of ppl were probably expecting more cherry from this but the top and middle notes are short lived and the dry down happens fairly early on and stays like that for hours later, which is why I enjoy this! This scent is simple, sweet, creamy, and date night worthy. One of my favorite designer scents

I love the bottle which looks like a dress. If you end it or you don't like the smell, the bottle will be good accesorie for your shelf. For me it smells literally sweet rose jam with almonds. I feel cherry a bit, but it makes the scent richer. I wear it only on nights out because the perfume is heavy for everyday

It smells fresh to me. As if it is going to be perfect for Spring, perhaps even summer. So for now I am simply going to allow it to do its thing and to macerate. What I wil say is that the bottle is truly beautiful. I do hope that this develops to where I smell the almond & the cherry more.... But we shall see

Recently, while I was at our trusted perfumery, I walked past the designer perfumes for the first time in a long while. Not because I planned to buy something, but simply because I hadn't tested designer perfumes in so long that I wanted to see what new offerings there were.

The bottle is already beautiful. Here on Profumo, many notes are missing; it would be good to supplement the information. Top notes: Pear, Sage, Apple, and Lavender => fruity/herbaceous Heart notes: Rose, Magnolia, Freesia, and green notes => white flowers and green freshness Base notes: Iso E Super, Musk, and Violet. Ideal for traveling, the office, and formal occasions. For all generations and seemingly unisex. For me, it is clearly a feminine fragrance. Ideal for spring and summer. For the cold season, even I reach for something cottony, warm, fluffy, and cuddly. Salvia Blu is fresh, woody, and green. Launched in 2018, the nose behind it is Quentin Bisch. I smell morning sun, fresh breeze, pure and calming. Blue symphony at dawn. Awakening of nature. Blue hour in all its beauty. The sillage is good, and the longevity is decent for a fresh fragrance. Parco Palladino is a fragrance collection, it is meant to be a reimagining of what grows in a famous Italian garden of the Villa Rotonda in Vicenza. At least, this was an idea from Tomas Maier, the creative director. 15 creations later, they are all different interpretations of sage notes. It is meant to be a soliflore that you either like or dislike; there is nothing in between. Bottles are handcrafted in the Intrecciato pattern. What looks like a simple woven pattern of different stripes is actually a patented way of working with leather. More about various Intrecciato techniques: https://www.thecuttingclass.com/bottega-veneta-intrecciato-weave/ Salvia Blu is for me a classic that should not be missing in the collection of anyone who loves a timeless freshness.

80% clear, natural rose water. I mean the kind you can dab on your face. So it smells very authentic. 15% sage leaves. 5% lavender bush. In my nose, a sweet rose, rather feminine and ideal for spring and summer. Not really complex and universal. Holy Peony (Dior) goes in the same direction. The longevity & sillage could be better. Although this problem exists with many Palladianos... The bottle gets a 10/10. The scent not so much, even though it’s not bad, but just not enough for the money :D I would have guessed musk as well.

I wrote a statement about five months ago after I purchased CK One Summer 2020 on a whim. It's not a terrible fragrance, but I found it underwhelming. After smelling it again at the time of this review, my opinion worsened. ---- CK One Summer 2020 opens with a blend of orange and ginger. However, the combination comes across as an artificial citrus smell, reminiscent of a freshly cleaned home or apartment. (Lemon Pine-Sol comes to mind). The clean scent is not unpleasant or unwelcome, but it is quite unremarkable. Once the citrus softens after 30 minutes, the dry down softly combines sweet amber and light herbs with saltiness. This aspect makes the fragrance worth trying. Like most of the CK One line, the scent receives promotion as a unisex scent. However, unlike most of the CK One line that has a feminine feel, Summer 2020 genuinely doesn’t have a masculine or feminine lean. ---- Performance-wise, there is not much to say about CK One Summer 2020, except to not to have high expectations. In terms of longevity, it lasts about only four hours at most. Three hours is more likely, which may work for a quick errand or date, but is nowhere near enough for a day at the office without a respray or two. In terms of sillage and projection, the scent stays close to the skin. However, a person sensitive to citrus scents may pick it up as you pass by them. This means that while it won’t gather attention from other people, it won’t offend people either. To be fair, this is typical of most summer scents in the affordable price range. ---- In terms of seasonal usage, CK One 2020 gets promotion as a summer fragrance, and it mostly fits that bill. The sweetness gives it some flexibility in milder spring and autumn temperatures. Socially, the versatility of the fragrance is it's largest strength. It could work in an office or school setting—if you are okay with respraying. It can also work on a quick date or a meetup with friends. (With an emphasis on the word quick.) That said, the sweetness from the citrus and amber makes it a decent casual scent for both relaxing at home or going out on a walk in the evening. However, the sweetness is not overbearing and makes it a reasonable option for a post-workout scent. ---- Overall, CK One Summer 2020 is a decent budget-friendly option found in rack stores like TJ Maxx, Marshall’s, Burlington, etc., or at an online retailer. That said, I wouldn't recommend blindly buying it if you're paying the retail price. (Then again, I wouldn’t recommend buying any Calvin Klein fragrance at full retail.) Also, if you’re looking for an artistic flair or something that draws attention, disappointment awaits. I believe there are better summer options available in the market (especially at the affordable price range). CK One Summer 2020 is a disappointment that I recommend passing on, unless you really enjoy a cleaner-style citrus smell.

I am a fan of the CK One line. The 2019 Summer flanker was beautifully fruity, fresh, and slightly sweet. CK One Summer 2020 is a bit less fruity, but a touch more rugged and green. In my opinion, it’s even a bit fresher, more citrusy. Mandarin, sea salt, woods, and grasses. Amber provides slightly better longevity. On really warm days, I would prefer to wear the EdT in the evening; during the day in the heat, it could be a bit too much. The longevity is slightly better for a CK One scent due to the amber, but it still only lasts about 3 hours. The sillage is also very subtle. I find the 2020 version to be a lovely refreshment on warm days and can be worn during sports. The price-performance ratio is, as always, great.

I annihilated a full 1.7 ounce bottle of Beautiful Magnolia in under eight weeks last summer/fall and decided to buy this one instead of replacing it as there was a great 50% off deal online and I started to feel like Beautiful Magnolia smelled a little too much like Pleasures. I love L’eau even more! It’s lighter in texture but not in performance. Moderate to mid high scent bubble with longevity around 4 hours. You need to respray this one but that goes for all of my aquatic florals, just the kind of fragrance it is. In comparison to Beautiful Magnolia, L’eau is crisper and airier, fresher. I was afraid there would be a heavy melon type note and there is not, it is more minty but not like peppermint, and it isn’t dense, but just kind of dances around lifting the scent up. I can’t smell any lavender at all. Very crisp fresh without going citrus, and it is going to be perfect for hot humid days in the Midwest.

I was surprised to discover that the EDT differs considerably in terms of composition to the EDP which I tried only months before. Jimmy Choo EDP seems to be a lot heavier on the patchouli, and in turn a lot less fresh than the EDT. I'll start by saying that I personally prefer the EDP due to my love for patchouli, but for patchouli haters, the EDT may be a better choice overall. This fragrance is quite fruity and dry. From the very word go, Jimmy Choo EDT opens with mashed pear, spicy ginger and tarty rose. It tends to sway ever so slightly towards being a chypre, but it's ultimately too fruity and juicy to call it so. In my opinion, the dominant pear accord when blended with the cedar in the heart, isn't exactly a pleasant blend, at least to my nose. I find the overall composition a little bitter and acrid, but then again, that's just my opinion. In warmer weather, the composition tends to smell a lot sweeter, with a hint of subtle soapiness. However if worn in the cooler weather, or by someone with the wrong skin chemistry, the cedar note is far too dominant, giving Jimmy Choo EDT that bitter and masculine edge. In this case, you'll either choose the EDT or the EDP as your poison of choice. Very rarely will it be the two of them together. I must add however, that the longevity is fantastic, very lasting and bold on the skin.

I really don't care for the eau de parfum of this fragrance as I find it too sweet and earthy for my tastes, but I love this version. It is such a pretty, sparkling, fruity floral that's a little spicy, slightly sweet; and thankfully doesn't have that nauseating patchouli note that is in the edp. It also lacks the sticky toffee sweetness, so it wears much cleaner and fresher too. Maybe I'm just lucky, but I have no issue with silage or longevity. It lasts on me for many hours before having to do a touch up. When it finally becomes a skin scent, it smells like the prettiest peppery rose I've ever smelled. I can think of a dozen fragrances that smell similar, so it's certainly not unique to the fruity floral genre, but there is something about this that sets it apart from the crowd. Speaking of crowds, this is a crowd pleaser that never fails to bring in the compliments. Whether at work or out and about, someone always asks me what I am wearing and how much they like it. Though I wear perfumes for myself, it's still nice to know that others enjoy it too.

I sold the bottle. The bottle is so cute. The scent has a tingly smell at first, which quickly changes to a strong shampoo-like smell. It's a rather strong scent. This may not be a review at all, but I feel very uncomfortable when "popular with everyone" and "popular." I laughed at the expression,This is what someone said, "new pages of a magazine." but I think they were talking about the top note "smells like glue." That really gets it. It's like Aron Alpha (Krazy Glue). Also, it has the scent of a perfume that conservative gals would smell like. I don't really recommend it.It has a metallic synthetic smell.

Surprisingly, I really like this blind buy! It’s my second one from Jimmy Choo and another success. Such a perfect everyday perfume: soft, delicate, beautifully soapy/shampooy and definitely office friendly! It’s such an easy perfume and its clean like freshly washed hair! Plus, the bottle is super cute :)

I have passed by this brand for a very long time. Until I once won it for "pocket change" on eBay. For the amount I spent, it was a real surprise. It flatters my nose, albeit somewhat artificially, which isn't too bothersome since it neither stings nor scratches... However, it is really extremely close to my skin. So, the sillage is practically non-existent. I also can't notice any significant development; after just 5 minutes it becomes skinny and warmer, then remains nice and unobtrusive, without surprises, but solidly suitable for daytime wear. A scent that will hardly steal anyone's senses. However, I can hardly imagine anyone turning away in disgust. It puts me in a good mood, without wanting to smell it daily. Nevertheless, I am glad that I took it "blind," and it will surely be my companion more often in the upcoming spring months, or a good starter for the morning hours.

Jimmy Choo Eau de Toilette is personally the better choice for me, after I also acquired the Eau de Parfum a few months ago. I didn’t pay attention to the fragrance pyramid when buying the EdP. It didn’t even occur to me that both could actually smell different, especially since the first tester in the drugstore convinced me.

Jimmy Choo's fragrances intrigued me also because of the beautiful design of the bottle. However, I was indecisive to unsure about which one to choose. I ultimately decided on the classic EdT. The pear clearly dominates the top notes. Anyone who doesn't like the scent of pears should steer clear. The pear is quite pleasant, as it is not sharp, but rather strong yet soft.

The saleswoman had thrown a sample of Jimmy Choo into my bag, and I am surprised by how much I like it. It must be the pear that has made its way into the fragrance still with its stem and leaves. I always enjoy pear aroma, as it is also one of the few fruits I like to eat.

Actually my all-time favorite, my companion in everyday life for years, I keep coming back to it. Sweet, elegant raspberry, not too heavy, and a delicate Far Eastern tea note is present, but it’s not a green tea scent. You could also wear it in the evening if you "layer" a bit.

The following scenario: It's morning, the first rays of sunshine are making themselves known as I enjoy the dew-fresh meadow - I am on my way to a new hairdresser. Supposedly an "exclusive," somewhat pricey one, but I want to check it out.

Recently, the first fragrance from the brand Bottega Veneta has joined my collection. I definitely wanted to have one of these great brands. A designer brand that has caught my attention with serious and everyday-appropriate scents. All have a certain elegance without major childish moments. Nevertheless, they have charm. Specifically, the Pour Homme line has many classic elements. The Illusione line combines clean elegance with pleasing and modern accents. Ultimately, I chose this Bois Nu, which is already flying under the radar. You can get 50ml for around 40 euros, which is fair for this high-quality scent. The bottle comes in a great box, and the bottle itself is already elegant like the fashion of this brand. Simple, great thick base, beautiful cap. It looks fantastic in any collection. Perfumer Antoine Maisondieu is already well-known, especially in the designer fragrance world. I like his creations, and he really hits the taste of the masses. In the statements, some similarities to Reflection Man are mentioned. I don't find that to be the case, but if you like this style, you can definitely give it a try. Stylistically, the two are not that far apart: fresh, pleasant wood, floral-polished appearance, and already elegance and sex appeal. Of course, this does not come close to that luxurious Amouage DNA, but for those who don't want to spend that much money, this is a great alternative. The opening completely reminds me of Prada L'Homme. In the top note, one could perceive it as a flanker or scent twin. This clean freshness with this polished elegance comes across very well. After the top note, it develops in its own direction. A unique floral heart note with gentle wood emerges. A pleasing sweetness is also present, which is not too extreme. A slight synthetic note (probably due to the Akigalawood) is noticeable, but it does not come off as cheap. The dry down is already quite seductive with great woody sweetness. Overall, a fantastic scent that you can't go wrong with, without being too ordinary. It is pleasing, yet has a lot of individuality. Perfect for in-between, everyday wear, and also suitable for dates. With a never too strong sillage, you can wear this scent for many occasions throughout the year. Sillage is in the medium range, and longevity is also rather average. It should last around 6 hours, perhaps even longer when experienced up close. Overall, a great release that most will enjoy. Very gentleman-like and absolutely not for bad boys. A wonderful mix of fresh everyday DNA and seductive date scent. Definitely worth a test!

The scent of Bottega Veneta "Illusione" was a blind buy for me some time ago. I liked the fragrance notes and the price was fair. Now I have been able to test the scent for a while and here I summarize what I think of it. The fragrance creation of Bottega Veneta "Illusione" is generally characterized by a very strong sweetness, where I miss a bit of freshness as a balance. With lemon, bergamot, and bitter orange, one would think that the scent has a refreshing opening, but unfortunately, this is not the case, as the vanilla paired with tonka bean in the base note quickly comes to the forefront, resulting in the extreme sweetness. The scent is perfect for beginners in the world of perfumes due to its typical "designer" fragrance notes. It is also recommended for dates, dinners, or clubs, as its sweetness makes it versatile.

Since I started wearing perfume, there have been days when many women's fragrances olfactorily get on my nerves. Bois Nu has become a scent for such days. I actually got to know it through one of the many letter exchanges, which is a great thing. Because I had already written off the Bottega Veneta fragrances with "not my thing". In the top note, I get a lot of citrus peel with its slight bitterness, which is immediately accompanied by a tonka bean glaze. The heart note is accompanied by a mild soapy scent, which probably makes it attractive to me. The Prada similarity was mentioned, but unfortunately, I'm scent-blind to that. In the base, I have a patchouli woodiness, and the sweetness is very subdued for me. Overall, I find it a great everyday companion that doesn't require much thought; it somehow always works. And for me, that's the art of creating a scent that functions as an all-rounder without giving you a headache.

Citrusy at the start, but with a clear woody edge behind it. The sage comes through very well, and a spicy, strong base rounds off the fragrance. As mentioned, it has a pleasantly citrusy freshness, not coming off as too light, and is generally very seductive. It has a somewhat synthetic-alcoholic feel and is clearly masculine. There is also a certain soapiness to it. It reminds a little of BdC but has a completely different DNA. Longevity is quite good, but not outstanding. For an EdT, it's acceptable. In short, a really well-made perfume that is absolutely fine for the price.

Illusione bois nu by Bottega Veneta is one of my favorite fragrances! As a beginner in the world of scents, this perfume simply blew me away. It is fresh, spicy, and woody at the same time - just perfect! I wear it almost every day and can't get enough of it. I can only recommend it. However, the longevity leaves a bit to be desired for me. But that might also be due to the way I apply it!

I love this scent, I stumbled upon it in a perfume shop and despite the bottle looking so simple/boring, it caught my eye. I fell in love with it immediately upon the first test spray. I don't like strong floral perfumes and this one convinced me because it smells so subtle and also so different.

Every year, CK One releases a summer flanker. While browsing the internet, this bottle immediately caught my eye. CK One is one of the classics for me. Unisex and almost everyone knows it. A classic that theoretically always works. Unfortunately, CK One is quite worn out due to its frequent presence. That's where flankers come in handy, as I really like the concept of the CK One line. The decisive factor for my purchase was the note of Mojito. For a fragrance, it's truly an extremely interesting note. This note is also strongly noticeable from the very first moment. The Mojito stands out alongside a fruity note. The fruity notes are really very pleasantly delicious and fit perfectly with the Mojito note. A truly uncomplicated summer scent that radiates good vibes. Unisex is completely justified here. The sillage is quite good when freshly sprayed but unfortunately fades quickly. Unfortunately, the longevity is below average. It doesn't last longer than 4-5 hours. Similar to CK One, you can get this fragrance for a good price. Conclusion: If you want to smell like Mojito, you can get this fragrance. A pleasant scent for little money.

CK One. Well… A scent that many use, even though it is, in a way, absolutely average, somewhat synthetic, and with weak sillage. A fragrance that you don't necessarily need to have. Especially if you deal with fragrances more often, you eventually realize how you hardly even notice such scents anymore. If it weren't for the countless flankers that appear on the market every year, like the Summer Editions here. And you know what? Despite the clearly noticeable synthetics and the banality of the overall composition, one must admit that the scent itself doesn't smell too bad. The scent: The fragrance starts fresh with fruity notes, and you can indeed smell the mentioned Mojito. However, I didn't find the scent very apple-like; instead, it was sweet-fruity. Overall, I was reminded of a waffle ice cream with fruit flavor. I almost felt like biting into the waffle. So, somehow very tasty, albeit synthetically sweet. Perhaps this scent was created from a combination of Tiare and especially guava, but I'm not so sure about that. Gradually (after a very long time), this impression faded a bit, and the scent developed slight woody notes. The fruity notes are always detectable, but they clearly diminish towards the base. And if you concentrate, you can even catch a tiny hint of coconut or coconut milk. In the end, I had that nice ice cream scent in my nose again. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is quite okay at the beginning. For about 30 minutes, it is strong; the next half hour, it loses power significantly, and after that, it becomes almost a bit too weak. The longevity is also not lasting. Four hours in, and you can tell how weak the scent has become. It doesn't last another four hours. The bottle: The bottle is the same as CK One. The same in green, quite literally. Because you can see green palm leaves all over the bottle, which looks nice and definitely better than the regular white CK One bottle, even though the bottle shape is simply average. Still quite nicely done. Summer 2016 means a new summer scent from CK, just like some other manufacturers like Miyake do every year. The question is whether it is worth getting a new scent from this line every year. Well, that can be seen either way. The scent smells similar but at the same time offers something slightly new. Still, I think that the owners of the older scents should finish those first, unless they buy the fragrances because they want to collect the pretty colorful bottles. I could write here that there is an endless number of better summer scents, but as already mentioned, this scent doesn't smell too bad at all. You can definitely give it a try, especially if you like fruity sweet notes. However, it is not suitable for going out, as it is weak. And since it doesn't smell citrusy, it doesn't really refresh either. But as a summery daytime or casual scent, it is well-suited. So, the scent is okay (for me personally better than the original CK One) and smells especially at the beginning like delicious Mojito (and a bit like ice, at least that's how it seemed to me...). It's just unfortunate that now I have a craving for ice cream. Just when I've started exercising again… but it smells so delicious like fruit ice cream. … oh, you know what? Screw it,… I'm going to get something to lick… and yes, I know how that sounds, and I don't even want to know what you all thought again, tssss….!

Actually, before this year's vacation, it was clear: the new CK One Summer would definitely be packed in my suitcase or picked up at the airport for the fair €30. Yes, if it weren't a blatant copy of one of its predecessors. It is not, and yet other fragrances took precedence, and even €30 was not easily spent. The 2016 vintage is not bad, skillfully combining the Mojito vibe of its '14 brother with a juicy green apple. Apple-Mojito on the familiar clean CK One musk base, surrounded by a few flowers that make it appear brighter & more feminine than many would like. Overall, it probably offered too little new to trigger a buying reflex. Understandable, I feel like I've already had 18 Summers in front of my nose - all good, okay, a few outliers upwards, nice collector's items. However, you don't need the 2016 version. Still super easy to wear, playful, young & easy-going. Bahamas, DomRep & Aruba. However, I missed the kick & I hope that in the coming years, the creators of the line come up with something more. There are still so many summery variations & playful ideas that could be explored. How about really bright flowers, a sand accord, algae-salty accents, or a truly strong coconut feeling? What about pear, fig, or the scent of a new air mattress? Chlorine, sunscreen, an unusual cocktail, or air conditioning?... Okay, forget the last point ;) Bottle: summery & colorful - as always stylish. Long live the palm tree! Sillage: whether at the beach or in a restaurant - it scores from 20 degrees. Longevity: 4 hours - a short fun. But not too short. Conclusion: the sun is calling! It makes you want to fly away again. Still: if you've smelled or even own many other CK One Summers, the 2016 version offers little to nothing new, combining "only" good old scents. Newcomers, please grab it in any duty-free shop - your vacation in the south will benefit & be perfectly complemented ;)

As the name says, this one is truly floral but also fruity and airy. It's light, beautiful and so fresh and lasts on the skin surprisingly well. After awhile I can smell the other notes as well it's sooo pretty and feminine. I think it's more young than mature (I don't see why mature women couldn't wear it but just to give you the vibe). Definitely safe for work, doesn't make me (who is very sensitive) nauseous or give me a headache at all. I'd say it's more of a spring scent!

Opens with some juicy fruits. Then you get fruity-florals. And I'm not sure where this is coming from, but now I'm getting fruitchouli? Fruity, fruity, fruity. But not necessarily an edible fruitiness, for anyone who doesn't care to smell like food. The bottle is shaped like an avocado, so I snicker at it a little.

A few days ago, I spritzed Floral in a brisk passing moment, in the slipstream of my rushing husband, who is shopping with typical male purpose. I could only catch a glimpse of Floral - just to keep pace with the "Pacemaker". Yesterday, the same procedure, a reach for the Choo bottle - and off I went. But the beautiful scent - despite its lightness - dropped anchor. I shifted into reverse - and returned to the pretty bottle. In the meantime, my husband had disappeared among the knitwear. But I found Jimmy Floral "captivating". Fresh and aquatic, bergamot and mandarin waft around me - plus a deliciously juicy note of nectarine. From the floral frame, the sweet pea emerges, which also delights me in the garden. Delicate woods subtly form the background for this transparent, appealing fragrance. I pause, because Floral is more special than I thought - and in a quietly eloquent way. It gently brings summer back - even if it's raining cats and dogs outside. I almost left this pleasant, friendly Jimmy behind - hence the saying: Haste makes waste.

I was recently at the lake and had sprayed the Eau Floral in the city beforehand. It was important to me that I could jump into the water right away. So I tossed my things aside and jumped into the water - a wonderfully pleasant scent wafted through the air. I asked the guy, as he is better than I am at locating scents, and he said, "I think that's your deodorant." And yes, the fragrance somehow fits the location - the lake surrounded by plenty of flora. The top note is - often like many other fragrances - quite citrusy. Bergamot, nectarine, and mandarin create a citrusy, fruity start. Up to this point, it’s nothing wild, but then the aromas of the heart note come in. The magnolia, together with the apricot blossom, enhances the fruitiness and the citrus. Meanwhile, the sweet pea adds a refreshing touch, making the scent something special. It elevates this mixture of fruits, citrus, and lovely flowers, giving the fragrance a bit of sparkle. Ambroxan, musk, and woods form a great base that gives the scent both lightness and longevity. For an l'Eau, the fragrance is great and long-lasting, and I am also very impressed by the sillage. The addition of Floral leads some customers to associate it with a beautiful bouquet - ideally of white flowers. The rather citrusy aspect can be somewhat irritating to consumers, as they expect a different type of floral scent. Overall, the fragrance is wonderful. It is light, summery, and yet it has something. You can wear it wonderfully in your free time but also at business meetings. All in all, it’s worth it if you need something special for the office that is more clean than sexy and a bit unique. It’s important to engage with the scent, and it would be great if you like the smell of sweet peas, as that is dominant here, but not unpleasant.

...barefoot into the garden, the grass still wet with dew. The cold creeps up my legs, but it’s already clear that it will be a great day, not a cloud in the sky. A pair of blackbirds are singing acrobatics over the hedge, and somewhere a robin is squawking - how can such loud sounds come from such a small bird? I let my gaze wander contentedly over the bushes and flowers, stopping at the colorful sweet peas. I can’t help but smile, as a wave of satisfaction washes over me. About the day, the weather, life itself, in this moment it is perfect and I enjoy it with all my senses, fully absorbing this little happiness of the moment. I bite into my breakfast nectarine and the flesh crunches away from the pit (I prefer my nectarines unripe and still hard like apples; once they are ripe and start leaving a mess every time you eat them, my enthusiasm for this fruit noticeably cools). After I finish eating, I sigh contentedly once more and then head back into the house to face the challenges of everyday life... This is the image that forms in my mind when I smell Jimmy Choo Floral. The nectarine is simply enchanting (why is it that you rarely smell it?), not quite my beloved apricot, but very close. And the blossoms dance a round with it, but without any attitude, trying to outshine it. Throughout, the fragrance maintains a very cool impression for me. But not unpleasantly cool, more like a cool morning, from which you already know for sure that the temperatures will climb to 25 degrees in the next few hours. I had to dig a bit into my memory as to why it seems so familiar to me, especially with this coolness that resonates: it reminds me of Jour d'Hermès Eau de Parfum . When comparing the notes, the sweet pea and the apricot blossom catch my eye, could it be because of that? Of course, the fragrances are not identical, but their vibe is very similar and fits perfectly into spring, when the warm days are becoming more frequent and summer is just a hop away. Did Miss Turner take inspiration from Monsieur Ellena? In any case, I am very taken with it and say thank you, Mister Choo!

He will come, the next July, for sure. Maybe we will be able to move freely again. Maybe we will get on our bikes and cycle through enveloping warmth along sun-drenched country paths, into the woods, crossing state borders, country borders, and back home. Who knows ... Melagrana was born this month. The time of black currants. A berry scent of enchanting simplicity like the entire Parco-Palladiano line from which it originates. It shifts between picked berry, green shrubbery, infusion, and jam, while remaining summery light, floating, unobtrusive. Berry softness, delicacy. A scent impression midway between naturalness and artificiality, which I also experienced with many other fragrances in the line, such as the ones I appreciate like Quadrifoglio, Lauro, Olivo, and others. But wait! Really black currant? That would only be half the truth. Because "melagrana" means pomegranate. Can one be so mistaken? Already with Quadrifoglio ("Clover"), I was surprised that basil was the dominant note and clover was not detectable to my nose. It is similar here. Where is the pomegranate, that sweet-bitter fruit? Where are the tannins? Where is the zesty fruitiness, when I rather smell something like transparent berry notes with a gentle green-creamy accompaniment? I spray the scent on again and think. Admittedly, there is a certain bitterness. But my scent impression simply does not lead me to freshly cut pomegranate. Maybe to grenadine syrup, but not so cloyingly sweet. Perhaps this scent is simply meant to be an abstraction of nature, a simplification, a reduction, where boundaries blur. So be it. This scent deserves a comment, even if it is rather a rarity here. I like it in its simplicity and unreserved cheerfulness, which is not loud. By the way, I do not perceive it as unisex, rather as a women's fragrance. Nothing more needs to be said about the bottles in the line - they are personally unmatched for me. But that's a matter of taste.

I have a thing with musk. The note can be subtle and nice - and it can be like a roaring airplane. I prefer the former. This scent from Calvin Klein belongs to the group of subtle and nice musk notes. Actually, I find it fresh even though the musk note is there from the beginning to the end. In this composition the musk entwines with the peach and pear blossom so wonderfully, that the overall impression is freshness. Amazing! The heart of especially rose and lilac also offers a wonderful combination with the musk. And when you finally get to the base the cedar compliments the musk so well. Unfortunately, the scent does not have much sillage and longevity is poor. I have to spray every two hours to keep it going. But it is a really lovely scent. The bottle is a beautiful classic design, a lot like several of CK’s scents. Minimalistic and with the recognizable font. 47/365

and in a positive sense! This will be my first Parfumo comment on one of the perfumes where I asked the saleswoman for a fresh showered/clean/pure scent. Because I think I can definitely count myself among the Parfumo members who enjoy clean fragrances. And this one is definitely one of those for me; the lady in the perfume shop really hit the nail on the head. The scent initially reminded me of the old Pantene Pro-V hairspray (that was my thought!), which I liked very much. Very fresh, delicate, a bit sweet with a hint of synthetics and - somehow bright. Like the color and the bottle of the little water. And here we are at the keyword: little water. It’s so light that after a quarter of an hour, it’s hardly recognizable; even on fabrics and scarves, you can barely smell it later. Only in the hair does it still have a slight scent in the evening when combing, and that’s only because I didn’t hold back while spraying. I would say this is a fragrance that one could use all the time, but probably not if you want to be "smellable" for yourself and others. And the bottle is really beautiful and simple, which perfectly matches the scent itself.

it's amazing that there was only one comment about this. my new favorite Omg! with a Douglas order, I received the Calvin Klein Sheer Beauty body lotion in full size for free. until now, I wasn't a fan of Calvin Klein fragrances.. as CK Eternity reminded me very unpleasantly :( when I applied this lotion, I liked it immediately.. and the more often I used it, the more I liked it. after a few times, I became so addicted to it that I had to keep smelling myself :D I find it wonderfully feminine, delicate, slightly sweet, and floral. it is very feminine and not heavy. now I finally bought it as a bottle and am overjoyed. it smells exactly like the body lotion. the bottle is absolutely beautiful. simply classic without any frills just the way I love it. Sheer Beauty, you enchant me :3

Admittedly, this fragrance didn't reinvent the wheel. "I thought, 'Another one...'" before I sprayed it on paper... but then everything changed. The other beauties from Calvin Klein don't appeal to me; I approached this one with zero expectations. It turned out differently. On the skin! It got better: I can smell a delicate peach scent for a short while, and then: lilac! I would have liked to hold onto that longer, but as so often happens, it quickly fades away to make room for the roses. Here, there's a blend of the two rose components, light rosy - subtle, yet not to be underestimated, as this is the crux of the fragrance. The magnolia only joins in afterwards, as I discovered after several tests. I can't detect the base in its individual components; it gently fixes the still slightly fruity floral notes and gives them good longevity. The reason for me to acquire this perfume that the world wasn't waiting for is that it instantly puts me in a great mood. Besides this crucial reason for purchase, it should also be noted that it is well-suited for hot weather, but not only.

This fragrance is officially the first one from the Jimmy Choo I have ever owned. Although I don’t particularly care about their perfumes, I tried it after getting it in a swap with another fellow fragrance enthusiast. Unlike a couple of years ago, when I sold or swapped perfumes for which I didn’t care about before writing a review, this time, I decided to give this one a chance and wear it for a month. TOP NOTES On initial application, the interplay of lavender and bergamot delivers a refreshing herbal-citrus burst. Black pepper adds a subtle piquancy, while clary sage contributes an aromatic, almost velvety texture. It’s nice, all right, just not for me. I guess teenagers are going to enjoy it much more than us, a little bit older perfume aficionados. HEART NOTES After the initial brightness, ambroxan emerges, lending a marine sensuality. Cypress adds a green‐woody nuance. The overall atmosphere is pleasant and energetic. This mid-phase feels well-balanced: neither too citrusy nor overly green, making it suitable for casual settings. BASE NOTES As the scent evolves into its dry-down phase, a cosy and smooth base of vanilla and sandalwood emerges, establishing the essence of its enduring nature. Vanilla unfolds with its signature sweet, cosy, and comforting aroma—primarily driven by vanillin—which also imparts subtle animalic and woody facets that help fix the fragrance on the skin. OVERALL Jimmy Choo Man Blue is a reliable, well-rounded Eau de Toilette that blends freshness, spice, and warmth in a polished package. The thing is, it’s neither unique nor for me. These types of scents would have suited me in the mid-to-late 2000s when I was much younger. Even with this statement, I don’t think it pushes the perfume industry forward or does anything else besides being a versatile warm-weather fragrance for younger guys. Read the full review at scentgrail.com

Beautiful. I love it. Best of the line along with parco palladiano V and one of the few lilac based perfumes which a man could wear. Projection and silage are above average and the scent is just fantastic. 9 out of 10

CK One Summer Edition surprises - in the best way. Those expecting a simple summer scent will find much more here: a fresh, aquatic-sparkling experience that simultaneously bridges back to the 90s. The fragrance opens with a sparkling freshness - lemony, slightly green, almost like a leap into cool water. Beautifully fizzy, pleasantly unobtrusive, and with that typical "clean" aura that made many 90s fragrances so special. What stands out particularly: CK One Summer smells significantly more high-quality than one would expect in this price range. The aquatic notes are harmoniously integrated, nothing feels artificial or cheap. It remains light, but not trivial - a scent with style and a hint of nostalgia, and unfortunately discontinued. Longevity and Sillage: For a summery-fresh fragrance, both longevity and sillage are absolutely in the green zone. It lasts several hours well on the skin and unfolds very evenly. The sillage is moderate - not intrusive, but noticeable, especially in the first two hours. Conclusion: CK One Summer Edition is a special summer fragrance: refreshing, pleasantly different, and with a hint of 90s vibe. Those looking for a light yet high-quality everyday scent for warm days will find it here.

A youthful summer, carefree times and now a leap into refreshing nostalgia. A summer day by the pool, a refreshingly watery and minty pleasant coolness. Accompanied by a rather synthetic fruity trail, yet it plays a beautiful role in the background. I perceive zesty mandarin and a bitter citrus hand in hand with this fragrance, swimming to the forefront. The watery mint, water lily, and cumin give it a certain touch that makes it still wearable for me today at my age. Even for a summer designer fragrance, it accompanied me for hours, which is incredible. The sillage is natural and can only be sensed close to me. Nevertheless, it is a scent that accompanied me in my youth and is marked by memories. That’s why I bought it again 11 years later, memories in a bottle.

After I found the latest 2014 CK One Summer so successful, I immediately went for the highly praised 2013 version without hesitation. And I must say, this one also met my expectations and refreshes me to the core. A successful addition to any summer fragrance lineup. Despite its high similarity and the original CK One at its heart, I might even buy the 2012 version, of which only remnants are available at the usual unbeatable price (25-35€ for 100 ml). In my opinion, all versions before that are no longer officially available or can only be found at inflated prices in stores. And I won't spend more than that, despite the successful overall package. Fragrance description: mint, melon, synthetic, chewing gum, freshness, waterfall, flowers on a lake, woods next to Niagara Falls, refreshing, invigorating, cooling, musk in the drydown like all CK One Summers, youthful, perfect after a shower, exclusive for hot days, not quite as good as the 2014 cocktail, diver's scent, vacation scent, affordable, versatile. Bottle: looks nicer in the pictures than in reality. Sillage: safe, even for someone who hates perfume right next to them. Longevity: goes through - 6-7 hours is summer good. It doesn't always have to be niche and expensive - even after 2.5 years of constant fragrance exposure and nose training :) It's nice that I still enjoy such scents, even though I can't overlook the criticisms - especially the synthetic undertone beneath it all.

Admittedly: CK One itself is not necessarily known as something that lovers of exclusive fragrances would order for their collection. And I don't hold the classic in particularly high regard either, as it smells rather unremarkable to me. However, what I am curious about every year - at least - is the Summer Edition of the CK flagship. In 2008, I picked it up for the first time - simply because the color scheme of the bottle appealed to me. Well done, dear friends of CK marketing! But even more than the bottle, it was the scent itself that ultimately captivated me, as it brought a lovely watermelon note that I adored throughout the entire summer when it was blazing hot outside. Unfortunately, I didn't particularly like the following CK Summer editions. This year, however, I struck again - although with a rather low purchase price, perhaps "struck" is the wrong word. CK One has brought back "my" watermelon in its pure form after five years. I simply love the 2013 version because it requires little thought. After spending the entire cold season navigating and philosophizing over complex Amouage scents from honey to incense to tobacco notes, accompanied by almost unreasonable expenses in the three-digit range, it feels really good to invest 40 euros for 100ml in CK One Summer, which simply smells good. I have never sniffed water lilies or lotus flowers - and the existence of sunwood would not have been known to my nose either, but anyone who sprays this watermelon refreshment on their chest on hot days is in for a wonderful day. Of course, this scent is probably not suitable for business meetings or suits in general, but anyone who jumps in the shower after a workday, takes a few spritzes of it, and then sits on the terrace in a polo shirt will find that this is how summer leisure should smell. In any case, I will order and stock up on two or three more packs of the scent. Who knows if it will take another five years before "the little ones" grant me watermelon again.

A nose-pleaser, just the way I like it: warm, soft, cuddly. Once sprayed, I was hooked. I smell warm wood with amber and a hint of something citrusy in the top notes. In balance, I perceive sandalwood, amber, and slightly floral-orange nuances. The pepper and the easy-going leather give the fragrance its uniquely light spicy character. I wear the scent in summer and winter because I simply love it, because it wonderfully envelops me with fascinating accords, because it truly works for me all the time... simply because it is an experience for my senses. The longevity is quite good for a splash, and the surroundings have reacted consistently positively to the little fragrance. :-) Simply beautiful!

Happy day, big smiles, good mood. Magnolia, to me, smells like a white floral and citric hybid. That's why I didn't hesitate to purchase a decant of this. This Parco Palladiano I does not disappoint, I've read people mention other notes, all I get is magnolia, no wood, magnolia may smell a bit like lilly-of-the-valley to some though. Longevity is not great. Edit: Longevity of this scent is better than I first thought, just awesome!

The old stately house has long been abandoned and overgrown with woody underbrush. The once bright, friendly facade is peeling, and the windowless frames stare blindly into the void. A warm, sultry night has settled over the swamp land. The Milky Way stretches its silver sparkling band across the velvet black firmament. The loud concert of frogs and cicadas fills the darkness, occasionally interrupted by the call of an owl on the hunt. From time to time, a soft gurgling can be heard as one of the alligators glides into the moonlit dark water. The archaic lizards have returned, as soon as the estate lay still and lifeless once again. Muffled voices drift over from the wide river, barges making their way south, and sometimes a historic and illusion-restored paddle steamer, laden with tourists on a sentimental quest for relics of a long-gone glorious era. From the river, the once-proud mansion is no longer visible. Shrubs and vines have woven a cocoon around the terrain over countless years of abandonment, in which it now lies hidden in deep slumber, resigned to its fate covered in cobwebs. The passage of time has brought relentless changes, as it always does. Everything has long since become different. Everything except for one thing. The magnolias are still there, and they have always exuded their sweet, heavy scent. They remain untouched by rotting wood and moldy facades. They alone are witnesses to rise and fall, pride and damnation, submission and liberation. They still belong to the house; nothing and no one has been able to drive them away so far. They would have stories to tell of masters and slaves, of wealth and misery, of raucous parties and bitter tragedies, of love and suffering, of happiness as well as pain, blood and tears. Here, there was dancing and beating, loving and fighting, laughing and betraying, murdering and marrying, being born and being buried. Time, the great equalizer, has spared no one. Sooner or later, the swamp will reclaim the land wrested from it generations ago, along with the once fertile plantations. Already, the old secluded cemetery and with it the graves of the former inhabitants have sunk into its mire. Only the magnolias still bloom and defy the all-consuming underbrush. They unflinchingly spread their scent, heavy, sweet, intoxicating, and enchanting the senses. But perhaps their time will also pass in the swamp someday. The great river cares little for this. From the distant shore of the Mississippi, a soft song drifts over: “Ol' Man River, that Ol' Man River He must know somethin', but he don't say nothin' He just keeps rollin', he keeps on rollin' along. He don't plant taters, and he don't plant cotton And them what plants 'em is soon forgotten But Ol' Man River, he just keeps rollin' along.” On its way to the sea, it carries a hint of magnolia scent with it.

Bad news. This fragrance is not an infinitely better work than the traditional one. But when the traditional is a big nothing, anything that exists is "better than nothing". The performance of this version, even being superior to the EDT, disappoints precisely because it is an EDP. This version does carry a memory of the predecessor but it is by far another fragrance. It opens more fruity and sweeter than the traditional one. A toasted pineapple with tonka bean. Pink pepper is also more expressive, making the combination fruit + pink pepper + tonka bean + patchouli = many other fragrances. Due to the sweet and smoky pineapple perfumes like Animale For Men and PR 1 Million are easily associated with memory. The body is lightly peppered and a masculine geranium floral. But make no mistake! Nobody will turn to you if you are using JC Man Intense and ask you if you are using, for example, PR 1 Million. The base is still generic with the old and well-known notes of 90% of male fragrances (I have two Zara fragrances that remind me of that - Mexico Soul and Night Pour Homme III) Still, it's a good perfume to buy for everyday use. Don't be fooled by the intense name as it will easily disappear on a party night. It's worth it if you find yourself with an unmissable promotion price. It's also a great gift option for men who are used to "anything" in terms of perfume.

Where I always find Cristalle Eau de Parfum a bit dull and boring, Cristalle Eau Verte Eau de Parfum does have that extra 'pizazz' that the original is missing, but without loosing that beautyful ethereal quality. Got a sample of it and it is beautyful. Sillage is rated rather low here, but I can tell you: This radiates. I smell wafts of it when moving around with only one spray on the back of my hand and it is stunningly beautyful. It is so bright with a bit of soapyness; in here the 'green' is not an earthy kind of green (as in Chanel 19), but the green of fresh juicy leaves. Angelic; Bright and tingeling like chandeliers...Really very beautyful!

A long time ago, I read somewhere about a woman who described the scent of her colleague. "She always smells like she just stepped out of the shower." What does she mean by that?! Then my bathroom was renovated. 7 days without a shower. In July. A hot July. It became clear to me what she meant. I wandered around frustrated, as I constantly had to apply for shower asylum somewhere through a drugstore. Since I "grew up" with Chanel, I reached for "Christall." My father had brought it to me when I was a teenager. He thought it was a fresh scent for a young girl (that was in the 90s). I didn't like it. I found it toxic and simply piercing. Here was "Christall" again. Is it still available? Let's see how I find it today, I thought naively. Already with the first spray into the air, I smelled something completely different. "Freshly showered" shot through my mind. So I took the Eau de Parfum with me and learned that green scents could indeed be something for me. It is described as citrusy, but I find that at the beginning it smells like I am grating a lemon and a lime. Fresh, zesty, but also a bit like apple cider vinegar. Just stepped out of the shower, the window cracked to let the steam escape, the towel just hung up, and I sprayed the green liquid onto my damp skin it immediately condenses into a lovely, floral iris and a sweet jasmine bloom. Floral, lovely, fresh. But not piercing, as I always read about other "citrusy" perfumes. It is more spring-like. A fresh June. Not a fresh March. Freshly stepped out of the shower. In my case, the only bit of luxury I could afford after my morning cat wash over the kitchen sink. Showering only in the evening at some friend's place. The longer it stays on the skin, the more floral it becomes. The longevity is okay. I'm glad when a perfume is gone by the evening and doesn't linger on my clothes for days.

As a teenager, I only knew No 5 by Chanel because my Aunt Gretchen wore it. My childish nose couldn't make sense of the scent, which is why I crossed Chanel off my list. I wore Y by YSL and found it much more beautiful. But one day, I found a Cristalle sample in my shopping bag next to my Y purchase. A Chanel? Let's see... This clear, light scent made me forget my reservations about Chanel. I happily let my boyfriend gift me the 100ml bottle. I remembered this episode when my fragrance dealer handed me Eau Verte. It was my beloved Cristalle with a delicate green touch. Floral, citrusy, and softly powdered, it reaches my nose. Fresh and elegant at the same time, with a subtle green tendency. Spring feelings brighten the gray autumn. Music: Here comes the sun.

It's open with peppery notes, mint pepper. After a while, there are some herbal tea hints. However, they are very fragile on my skin. When you smell on a blotter, it is almost like good tea houses. Unfortunately, I don't feel pear and rose with was something I was looking for. The scent is not linear and start with vibrant peppery and transform to woody dry-down

Pepper? Something is pricking my nose - is that supposed to be mint? I only smell pepper and am waiting in vain for the pear. Probably the pear fell into the grass and there it lies now, spreading a musty smell. The longevity is enormous. At night I sleep with a peppered wrist and wake up with it in the morning. Unfortunately, no heavenly cloud.

Darkness. You open your eyes, look around. About 24°C, dry air, the dusty radio clock from the 70s shows 6:52 in red digits. The wooden shutters are closed, but the orange light of the sunrise seeps through the slits. You get up, close your eyes, focus on the chirping of the crickets outside. You throw on a T-shirt and step out onto the balcony, the bright light dazzles you. You take a deep breath of this clean air, letting your gaze wander. Over the pines, the mountains, the narrow, faded road without markings leading to the sun, which slowly crawls over the horizon. You grab a tea, sit down on the old plastic chair on the balcony, and let the scene wash over you. The air is already warm but still pleasantly fresh. The scent of fresh mint tea wafts over and mingles with the green aroma of the pines and cedars. From the neighbor's garden, you can also sense something fruity. The rest of the family is still asleep. Absolute silence, time seems to stand still. There are these moments that last forever. One spray and I am back in my mind's eye, on a balcony in the Middle East. Bottega Veneta has created a fantastic fragrance for warmer days with PP III. It is fresh but not unnecessarily aquatic, not a fruit bomb, and it smells very natural. In my eyes, it is neither masculine nor feminine; I perceive it as unisex. However, it is very green and later becomes a bit bitter, which one should appreciate. This makes PP III a very individual scent, with a strong recognition factor. Performance? Easily 8-10 hours, long-lasting and noticeable for people who come closer. Reactions from relatives and friends have been consistently positive so far. It performs best at temperatures above 20 degrees, but it also works well as a mood lifter even at lower temperatures. Final checklist? Scent: Emotional connection present, mood brilliantly captured. Performance: Very good, without ifs and buts. Bottle: Thick glass, beautiful pattern, heavy metal cap. Perfectly crafted, stunning. Price: €265 is steep, but considering the quality offered, it’s perfectly fine for me. Conclusion: Hopefully, Bottega Veneta won't discontinue this dream of a perfume anytime soon.

It is a very hot day, the caravan is moving through the desert, there is not a shadow-casting tree in sight and the strength is slowly fading.....! But then suddenly an oasis comes into view, or is it just an illusion? No, it is reality, green palms frame a deep blue body of water, the scene is of an almost surreal beauty. The exhausted travelers encounter more people here, who greet them warmly and immediately offer them a wonderfully fragrant mint tea, which they gratefully accept. I can't help but get such associations when I wear Parco Palladiano III. The whole thing could take place in a garden by the Nile or in a beautiful courtyard in Morocco; in my mind's eye, I definitely see palms and water and feel a peaceful atmosphere full of calm and relaxation. Fountains gurgle softly, colorful flowers outdo each other in their beauty, and a canopy of green leaves hovers above everything. No unwanted sound disturbs this peaceful mood. The mint, which opens with its green freshness, gradually gives way to a softer, still very fresh scent that also embodies the color green. It is a freshness that is far removed from any aquatic, piercing scents; rather, it feels very natural and reminds me of the Moroccan mint tea that I love to drink because it tastes a bit fresher than regular mint and smells even better. However, throughout the entire scent journey, I do not find the pear; it could at best be an unripe pear, as I cannot recognize the sweet juiciness of a ripe yellow pear at any point. Parco Palladiano III is definitely a wonderful refresher for hot days and absolutely unisex. On cooler days, I can't imagine it as well, but it surely depends on a try; as a mood lifter, it definitely does a good job......!

Can’t afford Jimmy Choo shoes? No problem! I can still wear the perfume. The bottle is simply exquisite, made to be reminiscent of Venetian glass. It reflects light like a little pink jewel on my vanity. The scent inside is not exactly groundbreaking, but it’s so lighthearted and pretty! I can compare it to Chance Au Tendre by Channel. Of course, Channel is more citrusy and not so sweet. This one has a little of bergamot in the opening and is much sweeter in the end. The sweetness must come from that delicious nectarine in the heart of it. It performs more like an eau de toilette, softer and it’s a delicate powdery scent. However, on me it lasts for a long time. Up to 5 hours or more. You can always spray a little more. I never understood why so many people get so upset with more delicate perfumes. I am not always in the mood for a powerhouse performance, and so in my view this is a fine every day scent. It’s like if you walked into a garden, and a light breeze wrapped you in a sweet cloud of hibiscus and peachy musk. You sat on a swing in a pink tutu skirt and tapped you fancy Jimmy shoe in a coquettish reverie. Why not?

I bought Jimmy Choo's "L'Eau" last week as a Christmas gift for my mother. My mother is a very well-groomed, dynamic, sporty young-at-heart woman (in my opinion, 50 is not necessarily old). Mom is fashion-conscious and with her blonde mane, she is an attractive woman. That's exactly what L'Eau radiates for me. Elegance combined with sporty freshness, dynamism, and cleanliness. A fresh citrus start that gradually transitions into a fresh spring bouquet. Feminine floral notes underpinned by woods form the base. Clean drydown, adult straightforwardness. No note dominates too much or overshadows others; each fragrance note has its own performance and appears for an adequate duration due to the good longevity. I like L'Eau. It is wonderfully uncomplicated yet high-quality. It is versatile and adaptable. I can imagine the scent as both an office fragrance and a going-out fragrance - and if Mom were to wear it every day - it would never be bothersome or clash anywhere due to its approachable, pleasant notes. I hope Mom feels the same way. Edit 2024: Mom hasn't worn it a single time; I've been watching it sit for 7 years.

On the sales table of the department store, the spring fragrances were stacked in pastel colors. The L`eau time has come! I just had to reach for the pink Jimmy Choo L`eau. The bottle is pretty - and the scent is perfectly spring-like. The fresh bergamot pairs harmoniously with the sweet nectarine, bringing an appealing delicious factor. The pink peony shines full of blooms, accompanied by delicate hibiscus. A walk in the awakening garden. A subtle hint of wood gives the L`eau substance - because the longevity is quite good on me. L`eau reveals itself as a pleasant, likable spring companion that will surely retain its allure in summer as well.

This stuff is gorgeous. Period. I own two 100ml bottles, a 19ml splash bottle, a 50ml vintage Egoiste edt and a 50ml vintage Egoiste Platinum. I love this entire line. During the 90s, being here in America, Calvin Klein was all the rage. I totally missed out on this beauty. I don’t know what got me interested in Egoiste edt, but I decided to buy a vintage bottle. This might have been one of my better decisions when it comes to blind buying. The beautiful notes of rose and cinnamon blew me away. It was divine! Then I heard about Egoiste Cologne Concentree. Everyone stated it was a stronger version of the edt and it was imperative to get my nose on it. Egoiste CC is dense, slightly syrupy, and very sexy. This version is much more generous with the sandalwood, which gives it a very luxurious vibe. It smells of money and definitely has that Chanel quality and dna. I wish I could bathe in this and the fact this was created in 1992 but still smells relevant in 2024 is beyond me. Truly transcendent. Egoiste CC is a signature scent and I will cherish my bottles for as long as I live.

Much has been harped on about this magic and rarefied elixir called Egoïste Cologne Concentrée. You can almost hear a choir and see a beam of light cleave the sky in twain at the mere mention of this seemingly contradictory fragrance category: the concentrated cologne. And therein lies my chagrin. For the life of me I cannot figure out what the difference is between this and the regular edition! I swear to God all those people who rave about the CC are either lying or else under some psychological illusion - "Ooooh, it came out and got discontinued....it must be amazing then!....yes I can smell it!!! Yes!!! Yes!!! It's so different!!!" Uhh..NOPE! Thankfully, there are many people who realise the folly of this condition and can categorically say that there is precious little if no discernible difference between the two versions in terms of smell. Some will concede that the CC lasts a couple of hours longer, but that hasn't been the case in my experience. In fact, there are some who say the regular edition (as long as it's not the reformulated version) actually lasts a bit longer. And this makes sense to me; was Chanel trying to reinvigorate the flagging sales of the fragrance by creating a new name for the established 'eau de toilette' category - the "cologne concentrée"? It honestly wouldn't surprise me if it was revealed that this was just such a marketing tactic - perhaps a play on the double C's of Chanel. No doubt some other company will soon come out with an EdT but call it an "Eau De Parfum Dilué"? Please!

Where should I start? Drowning in the niche world, about 1.5 years ago, a nice Parfumo user suggested I try Egoiste. Egoiste, which you can find everywhere at Douglas? Why not - give it a chance. I sprayed it on and was immediately enchanted. It became interesting when the scent also passed the "elk test" with my wife, who normally doesn't like vintage fragrances or overly masculine scents. The real problem began when I noticed how weak at least the formulation on my chest was, which I tested in 2020. After much research and good tips from some vintage experts here at Parfumo - I took the next step. I acquired a vintage Egoiste. A science in itself to get the right bottles. Eau de Toilette over Chanel / under Chanel / Greendot / Barcode / Splash Bottle, etc. Through extensive research and good access to vintage scents, I quickly got hold of a still sealed Egoiste 1992 version. What can I say - Opening, heart & drydown - significantly stronger / sometimes more demanding (because sharper) & indeed noticeably stronger on the chest. The yellow (not white like today) juice had it all. Actually, the drop was already sucked and the topic was practically closed - if it weren't for the same Parfumo user who recommended Egoiste coming around the corner and telling me about THE one and only Egoiste, namely the Cologne Concentree. Initial research quickly led me to the known establishments (Etsy, Ebay, etc). 50ml for €500 / 100ml around €1,000. Not with me, I thought. I have to have it - BUT not at that price. After tapping into my vintage sources multiple times, I found relatively quickly access to a market that offers the Cologne Concentree at very humane prices. In the meantime, after an initial sampling from a nice Parfumo user here, a whole army of Cologne Concentree has found its way to me. Now to the scent: You can really only understand it well if you know the current Egoiste and have another vintage version as a reference. The current one is quite smooth and noticeably more cinnamon than the vintage Egoiste. The vintage version has a rather sharp and very demanding opening, which doesn't settle down quickly. Upon the first spray of the Cologne Concentree, you get exactly that sharp note of the vintage EDT in your nose - BUT only for exactly 5 seconds. Then the madness begins. The complete scent note breakdown is significantly stronger and more intense. It is also much more harmonious, which is rare for such sillage monsters. The noticeably higher sandalwood content is noticeable. Furthermore, I have a constant cola association, which I previously only knew from Roja's Enigma. I will report again in January whether the different bottles (depending on storage - the scent is from 1992) behave differently.

Hard to find. The formula is somewhat identical to that of the EDT, yet the presence of ambrette seed/sandalwood is heightened here, finally exuding a richer, more intoxicating, dirtier, and warmer aroma, a kind of truly sexy and indisputable scent (while the Eau de Toilette formula emphasizes the presence of rosewood and aromatics, which - running through spices and dark roses - eventually leads to a finally oriental/woody base). The texture and longevity are finally stronger. This fragrance is both super stylish and dirty in a rather erotic musk-amber way.

I recently chose Illusione Tonka Solaire as my spring fragrance. Twice, when I wore it, my friend asked, "What fragrance are you wearing? You smell so fresh and clean. Like freshly showered, only better." The association "freshly showered" wouldn't have come to me on my own, but I know what she means. The scent is light, mildly sweet, and as white floral as the bottle suggests. I can also detect the slight hairspray note that appears in several reviews/statements. For me, it's not unpleasant at all, as the fragrance still has an elegant and subtle quality overall. It's a bit like a feel-good cocktail of fragrant creams and products that one uses after a long shower. Personally, I would assess the longevity and sillage better than the rating suggests. I don't often get comments on my fragrances, but I have on this one, as mentioned. And I can still perceive the scent on my clothes in the evening after wearing it, sometimes even days later.

On a warm Sunday evening in the Corona year 2020, I sat with my mask on in the Berlin U5. You can be sure that normally no pleasant scents come to mind when you think of the Berlin public transport system. But that evening, an apparent tourist got on the subway and walked past me. However, the scent I perceived was not the typical smell of Strausberger Platz. No, it awakened memories of all the beautiful vacations of my childhood in Italy and southern France. Mixed with an endless creaminess that left a gentle film on my nasal mucosa, despite the mask. I hesitated for a moment, but in the next moment, I stood up and cautiously approached her to ask which fragrance she was wearing. She revealed to me in broken English that it was Illusione by Bottega, but the white one, and that it was soon to be discontinued. Thus began not only the search and subsequently the hoarding of this fragrance that evening, but also my general enthusiasm for scents. And by the way, it lasts with me all day, albeit rather shyly, especially on my clothes, and my colleagues have also commented on it.

Clean, fruity, fresh, white, light scent. A bit artificial, reminiscent of hairspray. But a very good everyday fragrance with moderate longevity. You can only smell it very subtly throughout the day. Very well suited for summer, as it brings a certain lightness. Nothing special, but a good allrounder.

My title says it all. It's in the genre of geranium/sage freshies that seem to be all over the place. After struggling to find a spring/summer scent for everyday wear and trying tons of stuff, I'd rate it as follows: 1) Nowhere near as good Afternoon Swim and not as good as Sedly; 2) but similar in smell and quality to Allure Sport Eau Extreme; and 3) definitely better than Dylan Blue, Cool Water, Polo Blue, Eternity Aqua, and Aqua di Gio. It's also relatively inexpensive and so I think a legit decent value. I'm not getting it, because I'd rather just spring for something expensive that I'm thrilled about, but if you are looking for a pretty-good, inexpensive freshie to wear often, I think this is one of the best choices. The bottle is also relatively large, so you get a lot of liquid for your money. Also, my number rankings and comments here are pretty much how I feel about Allure Sport Eau Extreme as well, so this whole review could apply to it too.

This was a free sample. I honestly did not think I would like this, as I'm not big on beachy scents. Initially, it has that ocean breeze, grapefruit, floral scent, which while not typically my thing is pleasant and not synthetic. On my skin it dries down rather quickly into warm wood and amber with some sweetness from the cardemom to it. It's lovely, but the marineness to it dissapears completely on me. I find it very easy and appealing, masculine but with some soft feminity to it. It's just a shame that it has so little projection and wears off so fast. Within half an hour it was only perceptible skin-close. While I like it, I will not be looking to get more once i've used up this sample.

The Aqua is, as the name suggests, an aquatic scent. Very fresh, slightly fizzy citrus fragrance. It can easily be equated with shower gel. It starts surprisingly pleasantly sporty and is very suitable for summer. The grapefruit makes you feel awake and eager for sun/sport. Relatively quickly, the maritime note comes through, and you really feel fresh, as if just showered. Unfortunately, it doesn't last very long. If you don't mind spraying yourself a second or third time during the day, this scent is definitely worth a try. Longevity and sillage are still okay.

... I stroll leisurely. Here, one almost feels like being by the sea. Only the saltiness in the air is missing. I watch the surfers and sailors while enjoying the ice cream I got. The sun shines pleasantly on my face. When applying this fragrance, the first thing that hits the nose is aquatic notes (even though these are not listed in the fragrance pyramid), which linger for a long time. This is followed by citrus and cardamom accords. The aquatic notes are now emphasized by the salt of the seawater. Something spicy follows.
