More marine notes come through the greenness of the coastal moss. The patchouli adds a slightly dark and masculine touch. The perfume is lightly sweet. The longevity and sillage are average. Here we have a light men's fragrance that can be worn at any age. On warm days, this scent is a nice light refreshment. I would only wear this during the day, e.g., at school, university, in the office, while exercising, shopping, or simply in my free time. I find this scent too boring for the evening. Ladies can certainly give this fragrance a try. For those who enjoy a fresh, citrusy, aquatic, slightly salty sweet scent, this one might be just right.

The obvious aquatic opens with a successful portion of grapefruit, fruity and spicy with a kick of cardamom and rounded off with a slightly floral note. Just moments later, however, the field of heart and base notes opens up. The moss is briefly very dominant here and will certainly irritate some, but it quickly finds its rhythm and forms a counterpoint to the maritime freshness with the patchouli. The ensemble remains, even though the grapefruit quickly fades, distinctly fresh and aromatic despite the green-earthy and spicy-aquatic notes. It is more of a "cheerful day at the gravel pit" than a "sunbathing on the Italian Riviera" type of aquatic. The scent does not reinvent the wheel; apart from the little moss situation, it is unobtrusive, polite, and pleasant. It is a well-made functional fragrance, not an olfactory journey into a fairy tale realm. Some cynics might call it "conformist and characterless," but some cynics also smell like damp barns and civet urine and feel good about it. How one evaluates the longevity largely depends on one's own expectations. On my skin, the scent lasts a good 4 hours, but it remains significantly perceptible as a skin scent for much longer. The performance is absolutely fine, especially for closed spaces and a professional environment, even at high temperatures.

Hello everyone, I would like to share a few words about Beige Parfum . As I mentioned in the title, I personally believe that no company (!!!) can achieve this balancing act of timelessness, elegance, and high quality = you can smell the oils used and the charm that this company simply has and radiates = that is Chanel. I feel that Beige Parfum is one of the greatest "modern classics" that Chanel has released (for the upscale line). I know the EDT and also the EDP, and both are good (no question), but especially the EDP is very good, but the PARFUM... WOW! (To kneel for!) It is a lovely, friendly, and nice + uncomplicated light floral scent with its certain sweet moments of honey. I wouldn't want to wear it myself, but I am truly thrilled when my wife wears it. In my opinion, it is one of the top 5 fragrances for women at Chanel! Performance: H = very good S = good (the very high concentration is to blame) My recommendation: I see the fragrance as less suitable for women under 23, but from then on for every season, every occasion. It is that one fragrance that always works and always fits; with discreet DOSAGE (!) it will never offend negatively, that is Chanel. Price-wise..., yes it has its price and I know that, but it is also very economical ;). Its true potential is still known to far too few...! If I were not truly convinced, I wouldn't recommend it to you! And now have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______

First of all, I must mention that owning this little bottle (about 225 euros) is a bit of awe-inspiring luxury, the beautiful packaging - the safe and the typical bottle, lovely! I always get wide-eyed when I unpack it, a nice ritual. Now let’s talk about the scent, an herb comes into my nose - the hawthorn is unmistakable and remains throughout the entire scent journey, but it is not overpowering. And I perceive honey well, it gives the whole thing a powdery softness and warm intimacy. You notice it well, but only when you come very close - I really like that, it’s not that miles-wide scent trail. The floral notes obediently arrange themselves underneath, excellently highlighting this finest herbal-honey perfume. I find it suitable for any occasion, with a cashmere scarf, a rock-style leather jacket, or a business outfit. A feminine companion for a woman who has many soft-hearted sides but knows exactly what she can do and who she is!!! I find it lasts above average, creating a wonderful arrangement in combination with your own skin scent, a bit cuddly, your loved one won’t leave your side - I promise... And how beautifully Coco already said - scent yourselves in the places where you want to be kissed!

I own the Eau de Toilette and I really enjoy using it. Therefore, the decision to go for the Extrait of Beige was relatively easy. The price, oh yes, appropriate for an Extrait, but is it worth it? The small bottle is packed bomb-proof, so not a single drop of this sinful expensive elixir can escape. The glass stopper fits very well, and I can dab the pure gold essence on me in a retro manner, where the delicious Extrait can fully unfold. I love the Eau de Toilette because it develops in a way that is extravagant, powdery, honey-scented, very elegant, and feminine on me, without overwhelming the surroundings, even though the scent lasts a long time. The Extrait is really strong when I dab it on; it lacks the fresh kick of an Eau de Toilette. This scent is immediately very intense, darker, and spicier, but initially different from the Eau de Toilette. Over time, this powdery elegance comes through, the honey fights its way through, and all the other ingredients, and it’s almost as if this drop of fragrance slowly recovers and becomes softer. I use it by dabbing it behind my ear, on my neck, on my wrist, and then additionally using the Eau de Toilette with a few sprays, so to speak, to fix the Extrait, and it is incredibly delicious. The lady from Chanel recommended it to me this way. I have also worn the Extrait alone, but despite its strength, I miss the longevity, because the tiny drop eventually stops radiating. And it is just a hint that I can dab with the glass stopper. I believe this bottle with its 15 ml will last forever, but I still need the Eau de Toilette additionally to get my scent aura. Conclusion: It is a great Extrait and for those who are looking for the perfect Beige, it is a perfect complement to this beautiful fragrance.

What strikes me first is a raspberry that is still a bit green behind the ears, and suddenly it becomes very retro rose-soap-like, an old-fashioned rose that is quite woody and prickly. In the dry down, it remains soapy, rose-soapy, all the other notes fade away for me. Was it really necessary to create yet another countless muse?

This is pure, beguiling, bold and yet demure class. With capital C! The neroli here is played so well that no age boundaries are created. Young, mature, old: any woman confident in her own skin can fit in the imaginary feminine picture this wonderful fragrance evokes. Peony and mandarin orange just a tad, a dash of cedar, a bit of lavender and magic permeates the air. Wear with confidence as a reminder of what a pleasure being a woman can be. Absolute delight.

Yesterday, I finally wanted to treat myself to Knot, and in the hustle and bustle of Friday, I hastily grabbed. But at home, I discovered that it was the Eau Florale. With glasses, that wouldn't have happened! Sighing and resigned to fate, I sprayed it on - and my clouded forehead smoothed out! Softly floral and delicately powdery, the scent settles on my skin. The mandarin greets me warmly, cooled by neroli and calmed by lavender. My favorite ingredients - carefully harmonized. The rose dusts over it with a velvety touch, and the peony promises fullness. The romantic fragrance experience is rounded off by smooth tonka. A charmingly feminine scent with a calm, elegant statement. It is smooth and cuddly - and there’s no Gordian knot to untangle. Thanks to the forgotten glasses, I am even more satisfied than with my original purchase plan - although the original Knot remains on my list. Unexpected things often happen.

I wore the Antaeus After Shave consistently from 1986 to 1995. It accompanied me daily during my youth and student years. Applied in the morning, you could enjoy this amazing scent all day long - and that as an After Shave! It perfectly matched my heavy leather jacket - from the lecture hall to the disco. There was nothing and nowhere else for me. Crazy times with a super scent. It was always heavy, masculine, and extraordinarily noble. At some point during that time, Egoist also hit the market. For me, it was the softened opposite of that. But it instantly skyrocketed everywhere. I remained loyal to Antaeus - like a statement. Through the highest highs and the lowest lows. In fact, I recently wanted to get the Antaeus as a current version again. Unfortunately, the scent evoked almost no associations for me anymore. And then I realized that it wasn't the After Shave either, or that it no longer existed. You can't bring back youth anyway. Better to keep moving on to new horizons. But it was a beautiful time, with a scent that was iconic for me.

i know a lot of people are calling this a tropical, summer fragrance, but on me this doesn't smell like that at all. this is a sweet blend of jasmine, orchid and rose on a backdrop of vanilla sandalwood goodness. no coconut to be detected. still, it's way too strong to wear out when its over 35 degrees celsius. the longevity is unexpected, since most floral perfumes fade pretty quickly, but on me this lasts about 6-7 hours. overall, gorgeous. got this as a gift when i wasn't the biggest floral girl, but this really stood out to me as a great perfume.

I believe this fragrance would be far more appreciated if not for the unfortunate naming. As everyone else mentioned, there's no rose in it at all. It's a pleasant sparkly floral fruity-tropical scent that is the definition of "nice" in a bottle. She's that girl that's friends with everyone and no one has a bad thing to say about her. It stays consistently sweet, but not cloying. Fruity, but not too juicy. A tiny bit fresh too, but it's perfectly blended into everything else. The perfume has barely any sillage, so it won't offend anyone who dislikes perfumes, but stays on the skin for half a day at least. It doesn't change much during the wear too, so there's zero risk to be hit with unexpected notes all of the sudden. It's definitely a very safe, very beginner-friendly sweet floral scent, perfect for all occasions. It won't stand out and isn't exactly of a "signature" kind, but it smells very nice.

I discovered this fragrance on YouTube (I think it was on Jus de Rose) and took a chance on a blind buy because the price was just right. First, a reassurance for fragrance lovers who, like me, are cautious with the note of rose: this scent has nothing to do with roses at all. Except maybe for the color of the pretty, girlishly playful bottle. The fragrance unfolds quite linearly for me. In the opening, the tropical flowers come through a bit stronger, then it quickly becomes creamy on my skin with coconut, jasmine, and sandalwood. The vanilla adds sweetness and warmth, but for me, it’s not too much. Overall, a beautiful, warm summer fragrance that doesn’t break the bank, isn’t too complicated, and layers well with other coconut or sandalwood scents. There is a similarity to Alien Goddess Intense, which I perceive as even more intense, dense, and warm.

I received a sample and I am thrilled with the price-performance ratio. Like the previous reviewer, I believe that the scent has nothing to do with rose ;) . So don’t reject it just because of the name. With frangipani, jasmine, and orchid, it smells very floral. But really not old-fashioned floral, rather cozy and summery, almost tropical. Sandalwood and vanilla give the fragrance a deep, creamy note that lingers. Not listed here, but I also find it very fruity. What exactly, I can't say. Delicious sweet, floral fruit salad with indefinable contents. I could also imagine wearing it every day in spring or summer, but not at utopian temperatures of 30 degrees and above. I can imagine it actually becoming too sticky then. Not for the little black dress - I see Rose Passion more as a floral summer dress while sipping cocktails. EDIT: Now after almost five months of sitting around, it actually smells a bit like freshly washed flowers.

So first of all: There is no rose in this. Just ignore the name. This is a beautiful scent for summer. Very linear progression, I can hardly notice any differences between the first spray and after 3 hours. As a perfume newbie, I often find it difficult to pick out individual notes in a fragrance. I can usually identify 1-2 notes or just perceive the overall scent. Not here!

Oh how beautiful, oh so fresh, oh so healing.....but not a squeaky lemon at the beginning, but the full, wonderful bergamot. Then soon come beautiful, fine herbal notes that stay with you for a while. Then a light and sensual incense note settles underneath and gives the entire fragrance something very harmonious. Oh how delightful - the spring-like wake-up call, a fresh, green, pure, healing aura fragrance for everyone. Unfortunately, the longevity is a bit fleeting and the sillage is really only for oneself, so the only solution is to reapply every now and then, and immediately you feel refreshed, enveloped, and carried. Truly a daily go-to. I think I will have to put this one in my cabinet. PS. Attention - this was my first. Please don't be too harsh. 'I'm still in training' :-))) PSS. Thanks again to Aglianico for the fragrance sample :-)

It all started quite differently for us than the usual love stories. For both of us, it was more like a spontaneous one-spray stand. I met you online, on one of those free dating sites. In a scent-filled, perfumed narrow corridor, somewhere in the vastness of the digital sphere, someone wanted to share you. So I knew from the very beginning that I wasn’t your only one and wouldn’t remain so. It didn’t bother me. Perhaps it was your proud glass Intrecciato body and your pale green, slightly glowing blood in the light that caught my attention. Yes, I just found you beautiful. And then there was your beautiful name with that beautiful last name. Quadrifoglio, (four-leaf) clover. We chatted a bit, and I asked you what defined you and what you were into. As soon as I asked my questions, a fear arose in me that I might have been too forward and scared you off. You were a bit mysterious, silent, but I learned a little about you. That you were half-Italian, from a park near Vicenza, but also that you had a tattoo under your foot. You twisted and showed it to me: “Made in Spain” was the text. In an unnoticed moment, I perfumed myself and learned that your French dad (single parent?) is named Aurélien Guichard and has quite a few children, some of whom I had heard of before (Sole di Positano, Chinatown, and Eros). Maybe not the best family, but hey, I was only interested in you! Even “Vogue” has published an article about your family, more specifically your brothers and sisters and your dad. And you are mentioned too: “(A) green-powdery stimulant (…). Rating: addictive!” Now that’s a statement! I was fascinated. My expectation: to spend a few hours in green-creamy dolce far niente and maybe, if it fits, a friends-with-benefits situation. They usually fade away after a few days, weeks, or months anyway. So I finally agreed to take you home with me on the very first evening. Well, what can I say? It turned out to be a fantastic evening. I welcomed you at the apartment door, and you greeted me with a firm yet gentle hug. You smelled subtly fresh, clean, as if you had washed your hair and head with a bergamot shampoo. But there was something else. Mmh, green spiciness, slightly bitter, but not unpleasant, as if you had chewed on some basil leaves before our date because you read somewhere that it prevents bad breath. I liked that and invited you into the heart of my apartment. In the living room on the comfortable couch, you quickly fell into my neck, and I wanted to carry you in my arms immediately. I no longer remember whether it was a Saturday or Sunday, but somehow I associate those long, cozy hours with a Catholic mass: what we had immediately felt like something significant, without me wanting to glorify our first meeting in hindsight. It was simply what it was. I fell in love with your elegance and restraint right away, but also with your endurance, which is best noticed by giving you attention, as is the case with many other things in life. “Give me more basil,” I said, and you gave. Happily, we lay in each other's arms. You smiled gently. We chatted about trivial things, and I learned that money is unfortunately not entirely unimportant to you (which I forgave you in my budding infatuation). And then finally this question arose: “Do we actually have a basis?” Uff, such fundamental questions so early, I thought, attributing it to your youth, and answered in my pleasant daze perhaps a bit cryptically: “It was beautiful with you from the very beginning; be as you are; you don’t need to play another role.” You understood that, my green spring love. Unfortunately, you quickly ran out of steam. Although you do have such endurance. 5 ml seemed a bit scant to me. “I’m fading,” you cried, and I got scared. “You look fantastic!” I shouted desperately, not knowing why I hadn’t asked better, “What do you say to having breakfast together tomorrow?” Never mind. You told me that there were others interested in you, men, but also women, gender relatively irrelevant, and that you weren’t monogamous, asking if I had a problem with that. And I said: “Bi? Pan? How wonderful! I’m not, but I’m not jealous either. I also live and spray by the motto: ‘Other flacons have great daughters too!’ You are not the only one in my life, and not my only love.” You looked at me delighted and asked: “So are we officially together now?” I held you in my arms and said, without thinking long, still enchanted by the last six, seven, eight hours: “Yes! Yes! - Just in case of a wedding, you might want to change your last name.” PS: Please be gentle, my firstborn :)

I forgot how creamy, fluffy, powdery and smooth this sensual elixir gel version of No.5 is. I had an unfortunate accident with my bottle soon after receiving it about 3 years ago, to my horror, half of it spilled out on the bathroom floor. Luckily the gel form pours slower than the liquid or it would have been all gone. So I have been hoarding the remaining portion for special occasions. Well tonight I dusted it off to write this review and wow, so pretty! I must confess I love aldehydes! I can't think of anything better after a long hot bath. This is still so fine. It has just the skeleton of the original fragrance but is much more sheer in the powder and floral department and on my skin the cozy woody base really comes out giving a very calming feeling. This is indeed very sensual, familiar with out being exactly that same old No.5 tune. Perhaps I am a little jaded having worn No.5 original EDP all through high school...and having been very unpopular with the fellas. I wasn't until I switched into Terra Nova's China Rain and Paco Rabanne's Calandre that heads started to turn, so I think of Chanel as more of- meh, although I can now respect it's stunning purity and legendary status. But the Sensual Elixir is really a unique creature in many ways. I highly suggest that if you liked the original but found it a little too stuffy, proper or repressed that you try the elixir. If you don't like the original at all, you may also want to check this one out...it's more modern in its construction. Yet,if I were assigned with the task of giving this a proper unique conceptually based name I think I would call this fragrance "Sheer silk".

N°5 Elixir Sensuel is one of the substances dreams are made of. In a beautiful splash bottle, the delicate oily texture resides. Those who love the N°5 body cream might also fall in love with the Elixir Sensuel. When I first opened the splash bottle, I was surprised, as it only had a very faint scent of individual N°5 notes coming from the bottle. I quickly realized that it follows the same principle as every product in the N°5 line. It must be applied to the skin, specifically where the pulse beats! There it is... Of extraordinary delicacy, the Elixir impresses with sensual heights. I immediately had the scent of the body cream in my mind, but a bit more centered. It lays a gentle caring film on the skin. In combination with Eau de Parfum or Extrait, it is an absolute must for me. Especially on warm days when the skin does not require the rich care of the body cream, I really enjoy using the Elixir. The particularly rich and smooth texture of the Elixir makes the application a delightful ritual of perfuming.

Jimmy Choo Urban Hero, to me this is a cross between Invictus and Starwalker Extreme, it starts out similar to Invictus but a little more spicy as it goes through the mids it is a little sweeter. As it dries down you get more wood/leather. I’m sure the ambergris is probably ambroxin but that gives it some stay power. It’s not a beast, but for an edp it is respectable. I like it and it would work in most weather conditions and is inoffensive and could work in small or large groups. It also would work on a date. Blind buy? Yes if you would like a woodier version of Invictus. Or you like starwalker extreme. I really don’t see any hate here it is a decent release. The bottle and packaging is awesome and as usual the Jimmy Choo atomizer is one of the best in the industry.

Urban Hero is a pleasantly wearable, modern everyday fragrance - lightly spicy, fresh, and with a distinctly synthetic note, as is common with many mainstream scents. It comes across as well-groomed and unobtrusive, fitting well in the office and for daily wear, but unfortunately offers little uniqueness. Everything is agreeable, smooth, and easy to wear. Only the "Hero" factor is missing for me. A nice, clean scent without edges or corners, but also without any particular signature.

As in many films unfortunately, our protagonist/hero here lacks personality and character. He could be a fabric softener. Or a soap. Or the room scent of a fashion store. The name "Urban Hero" takes on an ironic twist. As if it were the foreign term for a slick pretender. Urban Hero doesn't smell bad; I've even received compliments for it. But if there were an opposite to a signature scent, it would be Urban Hero. If you want your perfume to not draw attention to yourself, but just smell pleasant, and you don't shy away from shameless synthetic notes, you can certainly spray it on. However, I am glad that I only purchased 30ml back then. The main reason for my purchase was probably that my sensitive nose didn't have much trouble with Urban Hero due to its flat profile. At that time, I rarely wore perfume and only in a subtle way; any perfume with character would have been an unwanted statement. And Urban Hero simply lacks character.

I made a purchase at the Duty Free at the airport after my better half gave the green light. Initially slightly lemony-fresh with a hint of pepper, after a short time, subtly dosed woods, vetiver, and a touch of leather come to the forefront. It smells very pleasant and you can wear the fragrance both at work and in your leisure time without drawing unpleasant attention. However, for an EdP, the longevity is quite poor; after about 3 hours, it is only perceptible up close. Overall, not a bad scent, but also not a standout.

Gabrielle Chanel L'Eau is an elegant, light, floral classic. These perfumes are smooth, polite, warm, and luminous from start to finish. Subtle in perception, they sit close to the skin. The classic, effortless elegance of a young Chanel woman. I believe it may serve as a safe blind buy for a young lady.

Overwhelming artificial sweetness, pear schnapps in milk chocolate pralines... somehow also hair styling products that are scented. If you were an employee, I would mildly say... a rebellious squeaky nuisance. This is a scent that when I smell it as a daily public transport user, I have to breathe into my jacket. And of course, it lasts and lasts. Patchouli and moss, where are you to cool things down and provide some relief?

I love this perfume a lot...and layer it sometimes with Jour d'hermes gardenia....it works excellent on me....gets also many compliments when i wear it, on its own or layered, one i will keep in my collection for along time..

On my journey through the realms of the great Chanel Extrait classics, "Gardénia" had thus far escaped my attention. A pity, but also no wonder: advertised nowhere, rarely found at perfume fairs, and when it is, it is prohibitively expensive, and this site has so far provided little insight. Were it not for YouTube's Chanel expert "Dacob," I would never have come closer to this treasure. At his suggestion, I discovered the rare Gardenia here a while ago in the souk and immediately, despite the high acquisition cost, pounced on the remaining bottle. A first impression revealed high Chanel artistry, quality, and nobility. The bottle quickly found its way into the cool, dark storage... and was forgotten. On a whim, I recently decided to take it to the theater in more elegant attire. I like to apply Extraits a bit stronger on the spots recommended by Mlle. Chanel in newer formulations to get a better impression of the scent. The top note reveals considerable power and presents a distinct, highly elegant, floral-noble bouquet of tuberose, jasmine, and delicate orange blossom. To my shame, I must confess I have never seen a real gardenia, nor have I experienced its scent. My research indicated that its fragrance resembles that of tuberose. As is often the case with Chanel, the flowers have a naturalistic touch, yet remain ultimately abstract - like an impression of nature, but interpreted through the nose of Ernest Beaux. It is pleasant that despite the slightly indolic tuberose and jasmine, freshness prevails here. "Green" is certainly not a scent, but an association that I immediately receive. Overall, I find the scent in its further development predominantly linear. (The old) Chanel would not be Chanel if there were not further layers composed into it that accompany the progression. Soft woody facets complement the slowly fading, but absolutely not wilting, bouquet of flowers. Patchouli, incredibly subtle, resonates along with the slightly fresh note of vetiver, which gives the gardenia a foundation, a stem, and accompanying foliage. At the end of the scent journey, one has similarly "descended" into the gardenia, and delicate woody notes blend in. Musk and vanilla, often figures from the ghost train of many contemporary fragrances, I can only sense and they likely provide a certain roundness. Sandalwood, which I love dearly (oh "Bois des Îles"!), ennobles the scent. Overall, the fragrance conveys high elegance and thus simultaneously a certain distance with an underlying, cheerful calm. On what occasion can one wear it? Good question! A suitable occasion does not readily come to mind, nor do potential wearers of our time. Perhaps it has also fallen somewhat out of this, our time, in which nobility and elegance seem to be mere quotes from bygone eras. For me, it will remain a highly private pleasure in the future. Even after hours still detectable on clothing, less on skin, I can linger on the described feeling and take joy in having made its acquaintance. The 15ml bottles are now history, and Chanel has interpreted "Noblesse oblige" in its own way and will likely only produce "Gardénia" and other Extrait classics for the appropriate clientele, the (money) nobility of this world. How nice that I seem to have caught the right moment! Whoever encounters it, enjoy and indulge! ;)

A greenish-soapy note opens. From the floral corner, alongside a rather delicate rose, the typical peony sting quickly reveals itself. Peonies - we will need them later in a different context for longer! But for now, let's continue: It is initially fragrant and airy, but the innocence soon dissipates; a rough base forms and absorbs the clean impression of the opening. The rose now finds itself in a bit of a scent crisis (as opposed to a visual crisis) and requires some goodwill. The candy-like nuance, which might have been intended as a reinforcement for the grande dame, does not help here; it is too much of a sweet treat. I pondered long over the floral-tinged clean note, and it took the help of my colleague, who pointed out that it doesn't smell directly soapy - more like laundry detergent. Yes! The aforementioned laundry detergent accompanies me through the morning, before gradually a pea-like throat lozenge sweetness emerges, which I can only partially reconcile with the descriptions. I am confused: Besides the expected sweetness and creaminess, there seems to be a (camouflage?)-leather note at play, and something sour even resonates in the background. Nevertheless, it will essentially be sandalwood that concludes the scent over the course of the afternoon. A somewhat diffuse vanilla note nearly conceals that the remaining wood is likely not entirely cedar, but also sourced from the lab. Regardless, all this provides us with a conventional finish and inevitably leads to the following conclusion… Uh, wait a minute! What is that? At the very back, creaminess, roughness, and rose merge in a completely new second approach. The fruit candy discovers its floral side and finally delivers rose with characterful punch. Who would have thought that after the anemic appearance from the front? And - perhaps I am going a bit overboard now - I even think I detect a labdanum-like indecent twist, not just friendly sandalwood. Thus, the most beautiful part of the fragrance hides itself in the evening. It saves a few points. So, what do I make of the conclusion? I had wanted to write: The fragrance is quite nice. It is solid and conventional, perhaps a notch more feminine. Ultimately, the feeling arises that it appeals to people who don’t flinch at pharmacy prices for stylistically average offerings - as long as the brand aura is right. I find VI to be significantly overpriced for what is offered. The Touaregh, referenced by Yatagan (thank you very much for the sample!) as a benchmark for masculine roses, is stronger and costs half. I must at least add a compliment regarding the ending. Unfortunately, it’s just too long a journey to get there. I therefore still suggest to the gentlemen to approach the Touaregh instead (caution - by no means a scent twin or even a relative!) and to use the saved money to buy an advanced tree peony for the garden instead. With those things, a lot of patience is also necessary. I planted my specimen four or five years ago as a little stick, and it is (albeit admittedly in a less than optimal location) now about thirty to forty centimeters tall. I am curious if I will see three flowers this year; that would be a 50 percent increase. But iiiiiirgendwann it will be a pompous bush like from the catalog, I am confident. I thank Yatagan for the sample.

Hello everyone, Later in the evening, I would like to focus on the Gabrielle Chanel Parfum . I’ll keep it short, honest, and painless... when we talk about the regular Gabrielle Chanel Eau de Parfum , it was one of those fragrances that you somehow didn’t need... What do I mean by that exactly? It felt somewhat unfinished or unnecessary. There are sooooo many wonderful fragrances from the house for women, and then there was the Gabrielle Chanel Eau de Parfum ... well! Now we come to the Gabrielle Chanel Parfum and its masterclass has proven CHANEL once again! Bright floral, creamy with subtle sweetness = the house really excels at this, and has been for xx years. Longevity is very good, and when we talk about hours, we are in the 9h to 10h range and sometimes even a bit more, and for those who find that "too little", I can recommend Molecule 01 ! And the sillage is somewhat weaker due to concentration, but I see that more as an advantage! Who/ when/ where! Who: From 25 to 30 (and up) When: Except for summer + high summer, it works pretty much all the time. Where: It works pretty much, not necessarily for sports, but otherwise it is very versatile ;). My wife wants to get it at some point, as we really liked it! It is definitely worth a test! And now have a nice day/ evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______

Green, fresh and slightly floral. A very interesting olive note (no olive oil!) with an unexpected floral undertone, smells very elegant and refined. Along with Salvia Blu, my favourite of this amazing line.

The olive tree (true olive tree) is a symbol of peace and fidelity - often with biblical references. And anyone who has seen olive trees in person, for example in Crete, where the oldest tree in the world is said to be located, knows how graceful and calming they can be to the observer. The imposing curved and massive wood, the stable and elevated stature, the liveliness and persistence in an often barren and heat-drenched environment. Even the olives preserved in oil, as a staple of Mediterranean cuisine in all its facets, reflect these impressions in a certain way. Fresh bread and olives(-oil) - is there a more beautiful culinary minimalism? The question of how to translate such aspects into a perfume did not occur to me for a long time. Such an endeavor seemed too unsuitable. The olive tree is a wonderful symbol and purely contemplative. The product is meant for eating, rather for enjoyment. Until I tested Olivo by Bottega Veneta from the Parco-Palladiano line: The scent is truly not easy to grasp. For me, it is a sensation. And that can be quite well described as coming to rest. Olivo is unsweetened, yet by no means bitter. Dry, but not withered. Airy, but not fleeting. The longevity is quite decent, and the projection knows how to assert itself despite the overall restraint of the fragrance concept. Perfumes that are suddenly and effortlessly present again and wonderfully permeate through the nose with a body movement are rare. Olivo is exactly such a perfume. To speak plainly, Olivo has something of a clean scent. Clear and transparent. To call it fresh would be an insult. It is pure of heart. And ethereal. Like, for example, Vetiver Insolént by Miller Harris. However, Olivo lacks any oriental spice. At most, a fine aromatic quality can be discerned, in my opinion. Olivo is self-contained, completely grounded and centered. Self-referential. On parfumo, only green notes, woody notes, and green olive are listed. I think the good endurance is thanks to a portion of Iso and/or musk. And immediately after spraying, resinous notes come into play. But, and I particularly like this, there is nothing "vegetable" involved here. The scent also lacks any sharpness and herbaceousness that green fragrances often exhibit. On the contrary: I perceive a slight creaminess, especially as it develops further. However, Olivo is a largely constant perfume. A bit like a small, balsamic melody. And universal. A holistic approach. Therefore, I can imagine the scent for almost any occasion and season. Whether for a PP presentation or during a sabbatical in a monastery - Olivo helps one get through the day, making the beautiful more beautiful and the bad bearable. The entire Parco-Palladiano line is remarkable. Cipresso and Lauro, for example, are also extraordinarily well done and stylistically comparable to Olivo, Castagno with a subtle sweetness and thoroughly unisex. All the fragrances feel natural and high-quality, very wearable and lively. Definitely worth testing and don’t focus on the price.

The scent is a "more concentrated" version of one of the best perfumes of the last decade. The best combination of leather with Jasmine Sambac Absolute and pink pepper. All notes are enhanced by an additional concentration of Ambroxan, yet never come across as synthetic. The perfume is suitable for winter and its longevity and sillage are exorbitant. With the "Absolue" version, Michel Almairac once again demonstrates how high-quality raw materials can blend with synthetic notes to create a great fragrance. Mastery is a rare thing in perfumery today, and unfortunately, this jewel has also disappeared from production.

Today I finally stepped out the door again - and ended up in my regular perfumery. And my regular saleswoman immediately offered me L'absolu. Another flanker from Bottega? Do I need it? The answer is - yes. Here, the leather theme is skillfully realized in a floral, softly sweet combination. I envision the inviting deer brown leather sofa in my parents' house, into which one sinks with a contented sigh. One is tempted to put their feet up and take a nap there. On the wooden table, there is a bouquet of jasmine in a vase - blending beautifully with the muted leather tone. Valuable elegance with a touch of coziness. You can also make yourself comfortable with this fragrance. Calm and tranquility spread with a hint of luxury.

After wearing Allure Sensuelle Eau de Parfum , Allure Sensuelle Parfum , Allure Eau de Parfum , and Allure Parfum , I allow myself to make a somewhat more detailed comment. All four have a class that deserves a tip of the hat. Fresh, fruity, balanced sweet, cuddly, green, balsamic, and so well-balanced, deep, and full; so elegant; that's Chanel. Allure Sensuelle presents itself - according to my nose - as a good deal earthier/herbaceous than Allure, which I attribute to vetiver and patchouli. And the EdP is even more angular and intense than the parfum. So the parfum would be more my choice. It is softer and more endearing. But perhaps others prefer the EdP for that very reason. I also see it more suited for women of advanced age. But still, a masterpiece like this - it makes one rave.

Ah, I don't want to complain. Today I turn 39. There have been enough loud and flashy birthdays. We've celebrated in, out, and through. One becomes more settled. Quieter. More adult. Uh, does one? Maybe some, but not me. I'm still a crazy noodle. And especially on my birthday. I want to hug the whole world, persuade three monks to cuddle, and dance on the table. Instead, this year suddenly calls for bed rest. After an unavoidable foot surgery. So no partying, no monks, and no dancing. What does one do then? One quietly calls for the husband and asks for the black box. The box with my soul comforts. These are scents that give me security and permanence. A certain protection. And you are one of them. You are something very special. You are a Chanel, that much is clear. All Chanels have something similar in their essence; you can recognize them immediately. You are a perfume, so you are quite close to the skin, but you have a lot of endurance. You last nearly forever. And you smell like a nice chat over a cup of tea in the garden. Yes, something like that. I perceive flowers, and bergamot, and the citrusy scent of a mandarin, but also the bitterness of the peel. Peel, like scarf. You can snuggle into you, like into a scarf. So, now you are applied. And now I will simply sleep through my birthday. Why not? I'm wearing my prettiest pajamas, I just finished a piccolo with my beloved. And in your company, the night and day will be beautiful. I receive calls and messages from halfway around the world, there will surely be a coffee with family, and you give me support. You force me to keep my back straight and pay attention to my manners. After all, you are a Chanel!

it took another wearing for me to get a better idea of what this offered, after wearing it for about two hours I was finally struck by the scent when a breeze came up behind me. Beautiful, so when I looked it up again on here and another scent website I was surprised to see it rated it so low. Then I thought about the manufacturer, the brand, I get the feeling it's rated lower because of the high price.

Most of the time, when I was in Italy - in July, because of the sales and because I finally wasn’t freezing - the parks were more gray-brown than green: the moisture was lacking and the large green areas were burned; even the "Palladian Villas" on the Terra Ferma sometimes suffered from their missing green embrace, which their creator had so harmoniously planned into the overall picture. Perhaps that is why the scents of the "Parco Palladiana" series by "Bottega Veneta" are so appealing to me. They show me what could be; what I, unfortunately, have never been able to experience personally due to my travel planning. So too with "Parco Palladiana XI - Castagno". Afternoon calm at the hour of Pan under the green, cool canopy of the chestnut trees. It whispers and rustles in the leaves, even the cicadas had been sleeping until now and are just beginning to timidly tune their instruments again. The gaze sweeps over the green expanse of the park until it settles on one of the typical Venetian villas by Andrea Palladio: what a sensual delight! My eyes cannot get enough of all the architectural beauty and the overall picture that presents itself to them. Sensual experiences replace every photo in the most beautiful way; the senses expand through this beauty, breathing it in deeply. The scents in whose soft arms I rest complete this picture: Green, herbaceous, and woody: shade-giving foliage creates light paintings in various shades of green and brown, interspersed with shimmering lights. Not only the spicy foliage, but also the woody, slightly austere aroma that the sun-warmed trunks exude permeates the afternoon, accompanied by a slightly sweet chestnut balm. These chestnut fruits are still lacking their final ripeness, but in winter their time will come again: roasted chestnuts, a delicacy, not just for warming hands: just think of chestnut puree! But now with "Parco Palladiana XI - Castagno," these thoughts are still far away: enveloped by afternoon silence in a fragrant capsule of aromatic, breathing nature, I feel comfortable and secure. With its light, woody-spicy, and balsamic sillage with summer durability, this fragrance composition is a joy for the senses: carefully thought out and also a bit extraordinary - thanks to the chestnuts. A perfectly wearable counterpart to all the citrus freshness that accompanies warm summer days. An afternoon in the shade of chestnut trees in the company of the god Pan and full of fragrant beauty. A summer afternoon shaped by scent, over which already lies a faint memory of the autumn ripeness of the fruits - still far away, but already to be sensed!

Disclaimer: This is my first review here on Parfumo. Please forgive me if I make a few mistakes / if I can't express myself very well yet :) About three weeks ago, I first smelled Castagno from the Parco Palladiano line in a perfume store, and it immediately captivated me. The chestnut scent doesn't come across as "quiet"; the green top note fades away for me in a matter of seconds, and I am enveloped by warm (almost somewhat oriental?) woods that come together in my nose to form a full and rounded chestnut orchestra. With each breath, I feel like I'm delving further into a fragrance world that seems vaguely familiar yet somehow completely new to me. I love woody scents, but the fact that balsamic notes, which keep pushing forward in Castagno, can captivate me so much is entirely new to me. When properly dosed, they give the fragrance a wonderful core. If over-sprayed, it becomes more smoky-resinous - this can also appeal to many! The scent gives me a feeling of calm and balance. Certainly one that you might wear a bit more for yourself than for others :)

If perfumes were actors, this would be the Vin Diesel of Nerolis. For lovers of strong, clear interpretations of Neroli: Top! For those who prefer it softer and with more nuances: Caution... For those who don't like the 4711 aspect of Neroli: Stay away. I let myself be seduced into buying this scent against my better judgment. Inspired by the second of several trips to Morocco, I was fully on the Neroli trip. I searched for the note everywhere and seized every opportunity to add the corresponding fragrances to my collection. What I didn't know back then: I like the floral, fresh-fruity aspect of Neroli. Preferably in combination with other notes. And I like scents with multiple layers. The clarity that characterizes this fragrance, among other things, does not appeal to me. Additionally, I have a critical view of 4711. An aspect to consider when purchasing - I had to learn this too: Strong scents always have an advantage at the perfume counter in department stores or duty-free shops, as they stand out. What is an advantage in the olfactorily loud department store can quickly become overwhelming at home without the surrounding 10,000 other fragrance notes. I experienced this in this case as well. The noble, fantastic bottle definitely helped with the purchase. Just the weight of it in hand. A dream. Well done, Bottega Veneta... Scent: A distinction between top, heart, and base notes is not relevant here, as the scent smells intensely, strongly, spicy, and soapy of Neroli from top to bottom. Rather bitter and with clear (albeit noble!) hints of 4711. A bit of blossom, yes, but more in the background. At the beginning (= the first few hours, as the longevity is eternal) Petitgrain also dominates. Over time, it becomes a bit softer and woodier. Season / Occasion: If you like the direction, then definitely wearable all year round. I wouldn't wear the scent if I were going to the cinema or for a meal. In other words, for occasions where my neighbors have to come close to me and you can't simply change seats. It's too intense for me, and the risk of putting my fellow humans in "Neroli-Overkill" is too great. The reactions I received to the scent have been strikingly mixed: Compliments on one hand. Questions and confused looks, wondering if it had just been freshly cleaned on the other. For the latter reaction, just nod, smile, praise the diligent cleaning crew, and discreetly remove yourself :-)

This is almost identical to Creed Spice and Wood. A little lighter and slightly less spicy. This is very pleasant and inoffensive. But it's a subtle and careful fragrance. It's not gonna demand attention unless people are very close. Ideal for spring and summer, and maybe bedtime if you are one of those people.

Since I seem to be the only one in the community (and will remain so?) who owns this fragrance, I wanted to leave a little memento. I find this scent great for everyday wear, for outdoors, for indoors, for all time, and especially for spring. I combine it with everything I feel like, and everything becomes a bit more beautiful and spring-like because of it. What could possibly be wrong with more flowers?

Association with the white sands, the breezy palms. Ivory beaches, lush tropical vegetation and azure waters. Suncream on my body. Marine life - corals, turtles, manta rays and more. There’s a shimmer in the air, awakening senses and spirit. As the ocean breeze strokes your skin and soft sands caress your toes, you feel more alive than ever. This magical realm is your canvas for painting cherished memories with the people you love most.

At first sniff Hinoki was the stand out to me and my favorite from the new mezzanote collection … BUT After wearing all three fragrances from the collection on skin for a few days my opinion has changed drastically .. this is BY FAR the smoothest and easiest to wear , Hinoki comes off too harsh after the beautiful opening almost burning my nostrils everytime I would smell it off my arm . Almost Dawn on the other hand is smooth like butter and last all day because these are actually all parfum concentration. I don’t have anything in my collection with delectable truffle vanilla and chestnut wood . This is not a gourmond vanilla by the way and its perfectly unisex if anything leans more masculine because of the heavy chestnut wood . All three of these are woody but in different ways. Almost dawn is chestnut wood, Hinoki is obviously Hinoki wood and GoodMorning midnight is oud wood . I just went and purchased my bottle of almost dawn can’t wait to use it this fall/winter . I HIGHLY recommend to try these all on skin as these are very high quality ingredients and change according to your chemistry.

The way I have been dying to try this scent out since I caught wind of it. I finally got to try it the other day at Bergdorf Goodman (my New Yorkers, if you know you know), and I had the most gorgeous sales rep bless me with a 2 ml sample to take home. Now I’ll be honest, this is probably the first Bottega fragrance I’ve tried because quite frankly, my mind doesn’t go to ‘perfume’ when I think of the brand. But it seems like this Mezzanote line is the most elusive and exclusive line as of recent. I can’t remember how they landed on my radar (probably through the main page of Parfumo tbh), but I’m so so happy that I came across this specific one. Almost Dawn smells like if you took the entirety of Planet Earth, wrapped her the finest of suede, and dipped her into a divine, creamy, and natural vanilla. I can’t lie and say I wasn’t scared of the truffle oil, but it’s really not as ‘foody’ as some are making it out to be. At least, not on my skin. It’s more soil-like/savory than it is ‘mushroomy’. Paired with a soft patchouli and some woods, makes for a beautiful, earthy and woody scent that gets sweeter as it dries down. It’s so rich and delicious, and smells as expensive as it is. Speaking of, for the price you’re paying, you do get a long lasting, high quality scent that is sure to stick to your clothes and hair. It’s truly perfect for the cooler seasons, and would make an excellent date night / gala fragrance. Now I don’t know where I’m getting $500 to spend on this, but I might treat myself to a bottle after I finally get promoted. Bottega, honey, you ate snapped with this one! So unique, yet so wearable and stunning!

Three new fragrances from Bottega Veneta's Venetian collection have been released as perfumes (the first five were EDPs). In my opinion, all three reveal different facets of oud. Goodmorning Midnight is an almost classic combination of rose with almost animalistic oud. Hinoki is a woody, pure oud for meditation. And in "Almost Dawn | Bottega Veneta," the oud adds a very soft, leathery undertone. The leather, or rather suede, gives the rich vanilla a subtle bitterness and thus a special nobility that makes it a true perfume, not a gourmand. If I had to compare it to other fragrances, I would liken it to some Shalimars that have the same leathery, slightly rubbery undertone. And with "Mica d'Oro I | Valmont," where I would draw a parallel between the vanilla notes. While I smell Valmont for a few days, Almost Dawn lasts about 8-10 hours on my skin and then fades delicately. It envelops the wearer like a cocoon, a roughly one-meter-high aura of bitter vanilla. And of course the bottles - it's a story of hate to love. When I first saw them in a photo, I thought it was a mistake, but time passed, and when I held the bottles in my hands, I was already enchanted: their shape, the marble stand, and the tiny bubbles in the glass that remind the bottle of frozen tree resin and bring it to life; it truly seems to be a creation of nature. To summarize: The perfume suits me; it will be my scent this autumn. The first bottle has almost run out in sharing, and I am now considering a second one.

I like the aromatic, spicy opening, but after 15 minutes or so the scent's smoky leathery heart takes over, and from then on it just smells like any of a million other scents like it. One-dimensional, heavy, dark, and generic. I wish it had some more nuance to add some depth or character, or just something to counterbalance the intensity of the labdanum or leather.

A voluptuous, leathery myrrh with a heavy hand of pepper. The mandarin opening fooled me into thinking this was going to be a fruity-pepper, but the leather thunders in around thirty minutes to lay down the law. The myrrh provides a slight sweetness once the citrus scurries out, as well as a faint smokiness. It’s a “speakeasy” scent in my mind: dark, deep, indulgent. Sillage and longevity is knockout. Not even a full day of compulsive hand-sanitising could kill it at my wrists. Spritz safely. I’ll admit, I was primarily lured in by the vessel. The Venice collection bottles all look like a molten pineapple Haribo bear in a top hat, and I wouldn’t have it any other way. null tempted me enough to rationalise the cost, but Alchemie might have been a contender if the pepper and leather weren’t so imposing. Mental Snapshot: They say if you tip your hat – at just the right angle – to the tanner, he will usher you into the alchemist’s. They say the laboratory is upholstered entirely in tufted leather and deals impossible elixirs. They say it is here you can drink liquid smoke and breathe gold vapour. They say a lot of things, but what else can explain the umbral aroma that curls about the shop? tl;dr: tenebrous leather

So far, this little treasure had escaped me, but a dear friend brought it into my life, and I am eternally grateful for that! As a former Allure wearer from the 90s, I hadn't given a thought to my former great love in recent (Parfumo) years, and I might not have even considered its summer variant if I had known of its existence. But... bam! Now it has me. Allure Été is a wonderful summer fragrance! Actually quite strong for a summer scent, similar to Jil Sander SUN, but not comparable in the slightest. Rather, the juicy fruity note reminds me of Spanish orange fragrances, like Gala by Loewe or Andalucia Sensuelle by Derroisne. Delightfully bittersweet-orange, long-lasting, and not artificial. You can sense the Allure DNA, but only in the top note and otherwise rather latent, accompanying. Escada with its squeaky cocktails can take a slice of orange from this summer scent. I want a glass of sangria right now. Oh, what am I saying... a bucket and a straw! Olé!

The scent is a lighter version of Allure - complemented by a juicy blood orange note. I also have Cristalle Eau de Toilette and Eau de Parfum in my collection, quite lovely summer fragrances, but personally not feminine enough for me. The Allure refresher, on the other hand, has that certain something without coming off as too "madamish" like her aristocratic aunt or too frivolous like the much-discussed Miss. Although I also appreciate and enjoy using both of those, in the current tropical temperatures they either become too thin immediately or leave behind only a few inappropriate elements of their usual splendor. The remarkable thing about my liaison with Allure is that it fit so well into my olfactory universe that I almost emptied the bottles (yes, even an EdP...) without much fuss and would have almost forgotten them if I hadn't kept them. Yes, there was no relationship crisis between Allure and me, but I still returned to Mademoiselle. Three more obsessive years... Then I met No. 19 (EdT), which hasn't strayed as much. It's strange that Allure Eau Fraîchissante hasn't been commented on yet. It surely isn't being produced anymore; I haven't seen it on the shelves or on the Chanel homepage for years. What a pity, even the price was moderate (once you accept that fine fragrances always come with a price...): 100 ml cost in 2005 as much as 35 ml EdP. And even after 8 years, my remaining stock (at least 10 ml) still smells as fresh as the day I bought it.

This is the fragrance i wear and i love it. It's a little fruity and more spicy. It's definitely for colder weather, cause it's kind of a warm juice. It's not much masculine, but more unisex fragrance. The only downside is that there is not much projection, it stays close to the skin, anyway i like it a lot.

One might accuse me of lying, but CK One Red Edition for Him (CKOR) strongly reminds me of Chanel Allure Homme Sport Eau Extrême, yet it is of course much more affordable. It is the balanced blend of freshness and sweetness that characterizes both fragrances, and which is not overly common in the vast world of scents. The opening of CKOR is fresh and reminds me of an unripe pear. Here, the two fragrances still differ from each other. Soon, a sweet undertone joins in, likely from the tonka bean. This, in turn, reminds me of cocoa powder. As it develops, suede and pepper add a slightly rugged touch, emphasizing the "For Him" in the name. Combined with the synthetic elements, this all in all creates a somewhat rough-looking blend that somehow finds its balance and keeps prompting me to take another sniff. Sillage and longevity are average for the price. Definitely a year-round scent for everyday wear, I like it! I have actually been approached about it several times.

Should I start with the bottle? Absolutely beautiful. The glass, the real marble base, and even the wooden cap. There are so many beautiful perfume bottles, but this presentation might take the cake. The fragrance itself is also just as gorgeous. While not listing leather as a note, it’s throughout the entire wear. It’s adorned with lovely florals. I get mainly rose and saffron. The top has a very photorealistic strawberry scent, but it quickly dissipates. The base notes I get are great quality oud, laudanum, and sandalwood. Compared to other oud/rose combos I’ve tried, this is incredibly smooth. There’s nothing I don’t like about this fragrance. It is incredibly strong— both in silage, and longevity. It’s not office-friendly, but I’d try to get away with it once in a while if I owned the bottle. My only gripe isn’t with the fragrance itself but the cost is unfortunately extremely prohibitive. $490 USD is hard to swallow. Until I can justify it, I’ll savor the sample that I got with my wallet.

Euphoria Amber Gold is a beautiful fragrance that, unfortunately, has been discontinued. It stands out as one of the finest offerings from Calvin Klein. This scent opens with a subtle whisper of fruit and florals. Plum, mandarin orange, and rose... but they quickly fade into the background. The heart reveals soft notes of honey, orange blossom, and orris (iris root), adding a delicate sweetness and a slightly powdery character. What truly defines this fragrance is its deep, resinous base: amber, sandalwood, vanilla, and labdanum. The honey note is dark and rich, never overly syrupy or sweet. The amber is dominant — warm, golden, and thick — wrapped in a slightly smoky, not-too-sweet vanilla, and the leathery, balsamic richness of labdanum. The amber has an almost cola-like undertone. It’s slightly spicy, adding depth and contrast to the sweetness. This is a gorgeous, "dark" scent. Perfect for cool evenings, it wears like molten gold on the skin.

After the beautiful and enthusiastic comment from user Profuma, I expected a mix of Obsession and Venice. Two fragrances that I love very much. Profuma's description was indeed very euphoric and promptly led me to make a blind purchase. Her description is also somewhat accurate, as Euphoria Amber Gold is a balanced, rounded, soft, and delicate oriental fragrance. It doesn't smell exactly like Obsession or Venice, but it is definitely a close relative of both, though not a thoughtless copy. I have loved Obsession and Venice for ages. Opium and also Obelisk. Christmas spices enchant my senses and completely twist my head. Euphoria Amber Gold is, to my nose, a very delicate oriental and certainly very suitable for women who (still) do not dare to try extremely strong spicy-oriental fragrances or only like very subtle and quiet orientals. Those who know and love the vintage versions of Opium and Obsession (like I do) might wish for Amber Gold to be a bit stronger and the sillage more pronounced. The top note makes a bit of noise, but then the fragrance quickly dims down to a subtle level and lasts very well on my skin for several hours. The base note is particularly beautifully vanilla-cinnamon-sensual with a hint of caramel. According to the pyramid, the composition contains Gelée Royale, but fortunately, the sweetness of Euphoria Amber Gold is not sticky or honey-like, but very discreet. My nose has been accustomed to spicy-oriental fragrance notes for a lifetime, so I might not perceive them as strongly anymore. Perhaps other users find Euphoria Amber Gold to be a strong fragrance. I wouldn't want to be too definitive as the measure of all things. In any case, it is a harmonious, beautiful oriental whose pleasing composition I really like. I also do not detect the plum. More sensitive noses that do not like plums as much as I do might notice it. I consider this fragrance from Calvin Klein to be very successful and appealing. For my taste, the most beautiful Calvin Klein fragrance in years. No nuance wants to dominate or disturb the fragrance progression. Everything is extremely skillfully and harmoniously coordinated. This fragrance is successful, pleasant, and cozy. Perfect for late summer and the upcoming winter months. But also good to wear in high temperatures. The bottle is also very attractive: the warm, bronze color fits excellently with the fragrance, and the bottle design is very artistic. A beautiful piece in any perfume collection.

One spray and my thoughts run wild. Head and nose cinema are running at full speed. In my brain, brownish fragments with one matte and one bronze-glossy side whirl around wildly, creating blinking-blinding flashes. Almost as dense as the "snow" that used to appear on television screens at the end of broadcasts. Accompanied by that exact monotonous noise. Today, bronze snow and shshsh... It takes a moment before I can put into thoughts and words what is currently blowing my mind and simultaneously tuning my brain to the end of the broadcast. So after the rather elaborate opening for the nose and brain, I can finally categorize my perceptions. The plum and a bit of ripe mandarin already open here with a strong amber punch, even though it should appear more in the course. Nevertheless, it is already part of the program here and sets the tone. Everything is loud but pleasantly gourmand, sweet but not too sweet. I do not perceive the rose as such, nor do I miss it. There are fragrances where roses fit better and do not get lost in other loud notes. Here, one could have confidently left it out. With the opening, the initially chaotic and searching thoughts come with a déjà-vu aspect. As the first fog slightly clears, I realize what EAG reminds me of so much. It is Calvin Klein Obsession and Yves Rocher Venice. As if these two fragrance giants in the perfume cosmos found each other and merged in love. That is exactly how it smells to me here, and the longer the subsequent molecules work, carrying orange blossoms and a hefty dose of vanilla with wood shavings, the clearer this impression becomes. That labdanum contributes a syrupy resinous coating only reinforces this. Moreover, both house some common and similar fragrance ingredients in their DNA. EAG is for me the better and richer Obsession and also revives a bit of Venice DNA. The result is a really dense, presumably thick-flowing and syrupy floral amber juice, whose sensual aromas tend to move more towards caramel than vanilla. One rather feels like having to spoon the fragrance laboriously to apply it, rather than pumping it through the tube. Somehow, my perception of time also shifts with this impression, and the minutes become longer. The scent is so indulgently gourmand and so massive that it simply cannot be faster than syrup or resin, or very thick but clear honey. One almost loses oneself in thoughts, the swirling scent curtain, and the image of a drop leisurely running down the bottle. Very slowly. Dark amber-colored. At its top, the small star-shaped reflection of an equally tiny golden light. Time almost stands still. The scent, however, remains. It even outlasts time here. In cooler seasons or simply on a fresher day, I think its entire spectrum truly shines. Sweet-toothed individuals will get their money's worth, fragrance nostalgics will find themselves transported to long-gone scent times, and newcomers can spend hours discovering and enjoying it. For everyone who indulges in this fragrance experience, their own thoughts and feelings will be unleashed.

A refreshing summer fragrance, aquatic, light, cool, and universally acceptable, from the Eternity fragrance series, but in a light blue form. It is most likely classified as a blue marine fragrance. When you wear this fragrance, you feel the following notes at first glance: Sea Water, Ozonic Notes, and Juniper Berry, and the fragrance relies entirely on these notes. The performance is somewhat weak; it may last for two hours at most and then remains close to the skin. The bottle design comes in the traditional shape of the Eternity fragrance series but in an attractive, slightly light blue color. The price is also reasonable and not exaggerated. Conclusion: Regardless of the fragrance's performance, the scent is acceptable to everyone, even though it does not offer anything new.

This is my third Eternity flankers. The other two are the Summer Edition 2015 and 2017, respectively. To start with, CK Eternity Air is not a standard aquatic scent despite it contains ozonic and sea notes. It is comparable to the contemporary ambroxan men's colognes such as CD Sauvage, Versace Dylan Blue, Bvlgari Atlantique, just to mention a few, anyway it is not a knock off of any of those. I don't know why ambroxan is so wildly popular right now, but for some reason, Calvin Klein seems to have gotten it right, at least for me. Weird to say, CK Eternity Air for Men is classified as an aromatic fougère men's fragrance, perhaps due to its lavender and moss blend. Yet when I think of fougère, my mind takes me to Azzaro pour Homme, the fougère for excellence, and Air has nothing to do with it. Let's now dig into the fragrance, which greets you with a loud blast of energizing dry mandarin aroma with breezy and water-like sensations. CK official page states that they used the unique 'Sky Of The Sky' accord, which imparts a powerful, fresh lime-like, citrusy-floral, and sweet odor with little or no terpenic undertones. It is a new, bright, clean scent with notes of bergamot, lemon, and lime with soft floral notes like fruity orange impression. All of this sweetness and is adjusted with tones of slight aromatic juniper berries appearing on the edges. The slightly metallic ozonic note appears in the middle of the headnote flurry, lending a definite light and airy quality that fits the name. This elegant aroma, awakening the aromatic core of vibrant lavender and violet. The heart has that gentle touch of lovely violet leaf, not dominant, flanked with lavender and green apple skin, actually being used better here than in other apple-based scents. Green apple skin is now dancing gracefully about the heart node horizon, giving the initially tangy fruity experience a more subdued apple one, accented by the lasting sweet and spicy partnership of the lavender-patchouli. I then sense patchouli naturally creep in together, which anticipates the drydown trail. Warm and inviting, earthy facets of patchouli blend with glowing nuances of ambergris, sparking a lingering dry down that exudes masculinity. The base is the aforementioned light ambergris note supplied by the ambroxan, dry patchouli, and a peck of sea moss to fill it out. A slight salty sea touch emerges with the sea moss, and the ambergris adds a tiny bit of animal charm. This is a light, lovely, fresh, and well-thought-out ambroxan/aquatic hybrid that will scratch a specific itch for somebody into the modern style but not ready to leave behind the previous decade's freshies, nor swamp themselves in tons of amber woods toxicity. The very lightness of Eternity Air for Men is both its greatest strength and biggest weakness, though, since longevity is nearly on par with an eau de cologne, making this become a skin scent in under 3 hours. It's light, of modest reach and moderate longevity - par for the course for modern designer fragrances. You may need to reapply during the day, but a scent like this makes it feel very worthwhile. No one will hate this, many will love it. Keep it to spring casual use if you come into ownership of it. After about 15 minutes or so, the intensity of Eternity Air fades and remains quietly and subtly clean and aromatic. A pleasant warm weather flanker of the original classic Eternity, being far less tangy but retaining much of the aromatic flair. If Eternity Aqua cools you off on a summer day, this will warm you up on a chilly spring or summer night, and I feel like they complement each other perfectly. Worth a try, though it's nothing subversive, in my opinion. Yet I happen to like it. Overall, I think the name fits. It's airy, but not in a 'cool breeze' sort of way. It's warm, slightly salty, a little bit floral. -Elysium

Once again, I’m testing a fragrance that I purchased in a bundle. I was a bit skeptical when spraying it on and... as expected, a synthetic shower gel scent hit me first. My wife, who came into the room shortly after, asked if I had just come out of the shower. So it does have projection, at least at the beginning. It’s a fresh and synthetic scent that will surely work well in the summer. My wife even liked it quite a bit. Indeed: you smell like you’ve just showered, which is never a bad thing. But it’s not exactly exciting. After spraying it on, I actually got a bit of Invictus vibes from the sweet-fresh synthetic notes. That subsides after a while, and the scent becomes a bit softer and slightly woody. I must admit that I don’t recognize any of the notes listed in the fragrance pyramid. To me, it’s all synthetic mush. Contrary to some comments, the scent thankfully never turned musty on me. The longevity is about 4 hours, after which it can really only be detected by putting your nose to the skin (but even then, after 8 hours). The projection is quite decent in the first 30-60 minutes. I find the Eternity bottles rather bulky and unappealing. However, the sky-blue glass looks quite nice here and fits the theme of "Air." Conclusion: if you like Invictus and are looking for something that projects less and evaporates quicker, you might be quite satisfied with this fragrance. I believe the 100ml bottles can now be found for under 30 bucks, which is quite reasonable for a fresh gym scent.

The summer editions are back. Yay, I've never had any CK version of this in a review. There were some that were not bad at all, but they often lacked longevity and radiance. CK One 2016 summer was very nice. How does one make Eternity suitable for summer in 2018? Result: far removed from the mentioned top notes, I get coconut, sea breeze, green cocktail, and a hint of woodruff. Lavender joins in the middle along with something woody/creamy. The lavender bothers me quite a bit here. Herbal patchouli on amber rounds it off. Delicious. Not bad at all, but also a bit strange this Pina Colada Eternity. It lasts for 6 hours and can certainly convince fans, especially those who like it tropical. So be it! All coconut-woodruff-tropical cuddle lovers should grab it. I'll skip it this year; it's been on the market in Spain for a week now. I’ll also check out the "for her" version. For now, I’ll treat myself to a Pina Colada. It fits so well.

Do you love honey? And do you like "Euphoria"? Then the new limited edition scent could be your cup of tea (with honey, of course). The familiar structure of "Euphoria", the fruity candyfloss, can still be experienced under huge layers of sweet, golden honey. Very strong fragrance. I found it nauseating. But then again, I really dislike honey.

My nose is stuck! On my wrist! Help! I got the Euphoria Gold "sourced" from EvilCal (Oh, thank you!!!) and now: Now I can't get my nose away from this fragrance! Happy little bees are buzzing in my brain. And the bear is dancing pirouettes around the apricot tree. Or how else should I describe it? I'll try to be completely rational: When the kids were little, they had fruit puree in the afternoons. Occasionally, the ones from the jar. I particularly liked peach-apricot! Me? Of course, because they always left some behind. And Mama would nibble on the leftovers with a plastic spoon. Yum! I admit: There is a bit of plastic in Euphoria Gold too. A hint of artificial. But there’s also so much more fruit puree. Especially right when you spray it! Oh, if only it could always smell like that in the first 5 minutes. Then I would give it 100%! There’s also a citrus-fresh note. As if fully ripe peaches have just fallen from the tree after a rain. At first, I was disappointed when I realized how quickly the scent changes again. That was before I cooked the peaches or apricots. With a BIG spoonful of honey added! The scent fills the entire house. Standing right by the stove, you think: Uh, sweet! But from a distance: Delicious! Want it! Nose to the wrist. And sniff, sniff, sniff! I’m not interested in the gardenia or the daffodil. Especially not what’s supposedly in the base note. The top note and the honey are enough for me. As already mentioned: This is not a fragrance for people who don’t like gourmand scents. But if you have a penchant for big, thick, dark brown bears, and want to let them dance happily together with little, euphoric bees.... PS: Mine has just stopped dancing. Instead, he’s vying for space on my wrist.

~ Inspiration ~ I am always on the lookout for fragrances with honey - that's how I came across "Euphoria Gold." I received a sample for testing from the lovely Duftige. ~ Bottle ~ The name already hints at the prominent golden honey note. The round, curvy bottle immediately indicates that it is a flanker of "Euphoria" - it looks more luxurious in the golden tones, though. ~ Scent ~ Upon dabbing, a sweet, creamy honey note greets me right away. Ripe apricots add a slight fruitiness, rounded off with daffodils and gardenias. It finishes warm and sensual with sandalwood and patchouli. ~ Longevity ~ On my skin, it lasts about 6 hours (a bit longer on clothing and hair). A few sprays are enough, as it is quite intense. ~ Occasion ~ A nice scent for the colder days and evenings in autumn and winter. However, for the office, it might be a bit too gourmand for me. ~ Conclusion ~ I like it very much, as I expected a lovely honey scent and was not disappointed :)

...or actually, the bear is being lured. Honey, honey, honey from head to base. And this honey doesn't change. I am left in awe that something like this exists... The classic Euphoria really appealed to me when it was released. I would only reach for this if I want to bait a big bear :) then however, this scent would be my first choice ;)

and then the terrible word in the heart note makes itself known: honey! It's not for nothing that they have it in bold, because only this scent note spreads after a lovely fruity, apricot-like opening... of course, I knew it beforehand, but as a convinced gourmand lover, I was also convinced that honey scents fit my taste... once again fallen for the blind buy... For me, it's not sweet enough, rather strange, but definitely DIFFERENT... let's see if I give it another chance... I actually thought it would go in the direction of Roberto Cavalli Gold, which I like very much... but there’s no honey in that one either... so if someone is looking for a pure honey scent, this one is the right choice... the other listed notes can be considered a footnote... it does have one plus point, namely the longevity... anyone who wants to be enveloped in honey will be for a long time... I, for one, believe I'm not a bear after all...

The recipe: 2-3 golden yellow ripe bananas, 2 fresh figs, 1 ripe mango, 1/2 small ripe pineapple ("extra sweet"), 3-4 ripe apricots, a handful of raisins or sultanas. One should chop all the fruits and puree them with an immersion blender. The mixture is rounded off with 3-4 tablespoons of Provençal acacia honey, which is stirred in at the end.

I blind-bought Jimmy Choo Exotic a few years ago, based on my love for Jimmy Choo Stars. These two are opposing sides of the same coin: Both are closely related to the original Jimmy Choo EDP, with Stars being the warming wintery Christmas orange version and Exotic being the lively, summery, fruity variant. It reminds me of cocktails and warm nights, it's lush, syrupy and thick. Smells just like the listed notes: A fruitchouli with the same dank patch as in the original JC and the same powdery orchid, but with juicy notes of raspberry and blackcurrant and a tropical, tart edge of grapefruit and fruity passion flower. Sometimes notes like these can turn a little too sour on me, but they absolutely don't in this scent. I think there might be a hint of the original's caramel in this, too, that keeps the base warm and sweet. This is quite intense and sexy for a summer fragrance. Not quite as heavy and sweet as the EDP or JC Stars, but not too light to wear it in winter, too. If you hated the fruitchouli trend of the 2010s, this won't be to your taste, but if you still like it, this is an underrated gem.

I had my doubts about Jimmy Choo Exotic, as it looks like a heavy duty fruity floral. I was drawn in , though by the "black currant sherbet" note, as I am always seeking the ultimate black currant. It turns out to be a strong but pleasant "fruitchouli" that reminded me a bit of Nicole Miller Frenzy, but with darker fruit. (Frenzy has a lot of orange in it, to my nose.) It seems like the strongest fruit note in Exotic is raspberry, with barely any black currant. It's not terrible, but not that different from a lot of other "fruitchouli" scents. And, unlike the others, it gave me a bit of a headache.

~ Inspiration ~ "Jimmy Choo Exotic" ended up on my wishlist because I really enjoy exotic scents in the summer! ~ Bottle ~ You can tell from the round, faceted glass bottle with a flower-shaped cap that it is a Jimmy Choo - here in dark pink or fuchsia. The name addition "Exotic" promises a summery variant. ~ Scent ~ The typical "Jimmy Choo" character hits me right away, which I don't particularly like (it reminds me of the spicy tea note from "Flowerbomb"... the bottles also seem quite similar to me). Grapefruit and blackcurrant sorbet give it a slightly tart opening, while passionflowers and tiger orchids provide a sultry floral quality. Earthy patchouli and raspberries resonate throughout the entire scent journey. ~ Longevity ~ On my skin, it lasts about 4-5 hours (a bit longer on clothing and hair). 1-2 sprays are enough; otherwise, it becomes too much for me. ~ Occasion ~ It fits quite well into the mild and cooler days of spring and autumn (I wouldn't necessarily wear it to the office). ~ Conclusion ~ I expected an exotic perfume, but unfortunately, there is nothing exotic in it at all. It just smells like the regular "Jimmy Choo" with earthy raspberries... What a pity!

actually my first perfume. I absolutely love the smell, fresh and strong. Although bein very calm. I feel like it only works inside because it will disrepair if you wear it outside. Really cheap so definitely not a bad buy........................................................................................................................................................ . . . .. . . . . . . . .. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .. . . . .. . .. . . .. .. ... .
