At first, I found it very difficult to choose a CK One. After a long testing period, this one stood out to me. And what can I say? I consider it the best of all. It is fresh and just right for the peak summer. The longevity leaves something to be desired, but at this price, you can't really complain. For me, it's a fragrance that you can happily wear in the summer when you just need to step out, for example, for shopping or washing the car.

I am currently mainly sniffing men's fragrances, as my men expect fragrance gifts from me. To this, a stick with a music mix I created is very welcome. Out of my own arrogance, I also add a cute plush toy, so that the entire package bears my fingerprint. For the fragrances, uncomplicated and practical options are in demand, which fit into the recipient's living space. So I cannot come up with something stunning for Vet Wolfi, as his animal patients are very sensitive - just like the doc himself. Then the shiny Platinum caught my eye. Aromatic apple spiced with pepper, rounded off with cinnamon, is very pleasing to my nose. The clear lavender brings tranquility and the light woody note adds a sense of calm. Vetiver grounds the rather transparent scent loosely and permeably. Platinum stays close to the skin - and will not disturb the practice operation. Not an exciting fragrance - but solidly crafted and mainly perceptible to the wearer. In my feeling, unisex and a good everyday scent.
Strongly reminiscent of Tommy Hilfiger Girl... unfortunately does not do justice to the classic CK One. The bottle is nice to look at. The scent is artificial-aquatic.

Amber can mean so many things. Originally it's a warm blend of vanilla and balsamic notes, which can range from sweet to resinous in a rugged way. In the last decade it also became a synonym for synthetic molecules like ambroxan, ranging from fuzzy-woodsy to really scratchy and harsh. You never know what you get! Jimmy Choo's take on this versatile note is sweet, warm and kind of fuzzy. The resins here feel transparent without any heaviness. Benzoin is maybe my favorite balsamic note, it's so soft and creamy and never harsh, so I love that they used it here. I also really enjoy the top notes, they're all noticeable for a long while. The mix of peony, bergamot and pink pepper adds a fresh, sparkling, rosy layer on top of the amber that makes the scent stand out from other ambers. I really can't think of anything that smells just like this! There is a hint of cinnamon, too, but I don't perceive this as a Christmas scent or a gourmand. It just adds touch of additional warmth. I find Amber Kiss very feminine and suitable for autumn, winter and early spring. Most ambers feel more clearly autumnal/wintery to me, but the lovely clean peony makes this scent more versatile. This is wishlist material for me.

Some fragrances are incredibly context-dependent. Fresh mandarins come to mind. When I smell them on a plantation by the Mediterranean, I smell summer, lightness, sunshine. However, in winter, by candlelight and choral singing, it is one of the most Christmassy scents I know. Now, it is probably this very thing about context that shapes my impression of Amber Kiss. The opening is spicy - personally, a bit too sharp for me, almost peppery. I think I can sniff out cardamom and a little ginger. Gradually, it becomes warmer, almost cozy, yet with a heavy blanket of spices hanging over everything. The longevity is incredible - even after hours, I can distinctly perceive the scent on my wrist. And the more the spices fade, the more beautiful and sweeter the fragrance becomes. Warm, cinnamon, a hint of vanilla, I would say. But above all, there is an all-encompassing impression: Christmas. And here lies the crux: Is it the spiciness, the warmth, the woodiness that makes me think of Advent and the festive season? Or is it much more the perfumery, which is already decorated for Christmas, promoting the most beautiful gifts for her and him? I can't help but mentally start making the first plans for the holiday and adding gingerbread to the shopping list. I wonder if Amber Kiss would have had the same effect on me had I tested it in February. As it is, it is simply an intense Christmas scent that makes me dream of spiced almonds, sleigh rides, and contemplation under the Christmas tree.

So I've had Mon Guerlain for years and use it all the time. Love it, one of my staples year round. I got a decant of Goddess along with Her and Her Elixir, which I was much more interested in trying. I was expecting to like the other two, and had no idea what to expect from Goddess. As it turns out, Her and Her Elixir smell terrible on me, so after those disappointments, the Goddess sample stayed on my shelf for a month or two before I finally tried it, expecting to dislike it too. As soon as I put it on, I knew I loved it. The opening is strong lavender and vanilla for me, almost exactly like Mon Guerlain, but with slightly more creamy sweetness. Both the lavender and vanilla stay around, and ocassionally I get a hint of ginger and cacao as well, which I don't get from Mon Guerlain. Beautifully blended, not too overbearing, an absolute gem of a perfume. Once I have finished my current Mon Guerlain, I will be replacing it with this.

Opens very Mon Guerlain-sh but with heaps and heaps of vanilla. The lavender isn’t as pronounced but it is enough for a little aromatic vibe! The ginger is a nice element as it makes the vanilla slightly fresh, such that the perfume isn’t gourmand and never gets too sweet. Goddess is a very well constructed perfume, and one that I fell in love with instantly! It performs well with good projection etc but it never gets noisy! I can also see the perfume fitting many occasions/activities and working in all seasons. The bottle is elevated and looks expensive. I think the advertising campaign captures the essence of the fragrance well. That said, I hate the price. It is ridiculous and greedy. Would I repurchase? I think so. I am moving into this type of vanilla profile and Goddess fits the bill.

She`s no Goddess, more like a rosey, chubby angel munching on delicious puffs of gingery-vanilla fluffy clouds. What a cute gourmand! She reminds me of Ani Extrait de Parfum with the sweetness dialed down and some of the fruits removed, but definitely a cousin of that awesome lemon cheesecake of a fragrance. The lavender barely makes an appearance on my skin, the ginger-vanilla yoghurt dominating for the most part. After a few hours it settles into a comforting skin scent with shades of milk cocoa.

I bought a 3.4 oz bottle of this a year ago when I was just dipping my toe into the fragrance-obsession waters, way before I realized I want to own 4839927 decants and smell like something different everyday. I thought this was so beautiful when I tested it in Sephora, and kept sniffing my arm the rest of the afternoon. I bought my bottle off eBay. I quickly went headfirst down the super sweet gourmand slide shortly after and decided that this had entirely too much lavender for me so my big ass bottle sat mostly unused for the last 11 months. Now it’s coolllldd outside, and I started randomly opening the cap to smell the nozzle like a weirdo, deciding if I wanted to try it out again… and somehow it’s started making its way back into my rotation. The lavender note seems less intense in the opening now, with a little hint of gingery spice that feels appropriate for the weather. I’ve been asking my husband and random friends which fragrance I should wear between Goddess and various other options, and 90% of them say Goddess - I’m amazed at how many people on my life love this one. It doesn’t smell like vanilla to me (I have plenty of vanilla scents, it’s definitely my favorite profile). It’s not sweet either - not sure how to describe it other than that it’s extremely “perfume-y” but not in an obnoxious way. It feels like a grown up fragrance that suits a woman in her late 30s like me. It’s been pleasing to me wearing it to work, and I just wore it to a fancy evening party and kept getting whiffs all night that made me happy. Longevity is great, definitely noticeable even after 5 hours at this party tonight - and I go nose-blind easily. Am I falling back in love with it? Jury’s out. But it’s for sure vibing with me lately!

I stumbled upon this one by pure luck. Entered a SDM and it was right there at the front. Boyfriend stopped me to smell it and then sprayed it on himself at my demand. I returned the next day to spray it on myself. As a vanilla and gourmand lover, I was sure I'd find something great in this one. I just want to take a moment to chime in about the recent ridiculous prices I've seen on designer frags. 153$ CAN for a 50ml is just way too expensive and I can't justify it. Goddess was a travel retail store exclusive for a month before coming into general retail stores and drugstores. It's not even a private line or an exclusive line. So that's my rant concerning the price. Moving on to the scent-part of the review, I'm quite pleased I got to try it. It's a lovely warm (think luxurious body lotion) type of vanilla. There is a tinge of bitterness coming in from the cocoa and a hint of spiciness coming from the ginger at the beginning. Both of those notes remain faint in the grand scheme of this scent as the vanilla is truly the star here. Lavender surprised me about an hour later, giving the perfume a lighter, more airy accord to it. Vanilla is still the star, but the lavender imparted a more dreamy aspect to it that I found unique. There is a contrast between the more heavy vanilla aspect at the beginning and the lighter vanilla aspect at the end. Many retail stores mention there is a fragrance pyramid and I tend to believe this, now that I've tested it for myself. This perfume is a clear fit for colder weather, which is why I question its release in the heart of summer. I find it way too heavy and cloying in the heat, but perfect for that cozy feeling when it's cold outside. Leisure yes and night out for certain, but be sure not to overspray as I found it had a bigger sillage than the other Burberry perfumes I've tested up until now.

So immensely overhyped. It's way to strong and very heavy on the lavender which I don't appreciate due to the lingering smell which does not go away. Some may perceive this as a good thing, I personally don't like it. The longevity is pretty good must admit, but the vanilla in the scent is just not present enough, really unfortunate. For me it honestly just stank.

Goddess is a gorgeous, feminine, sexy lavender vanilla. It’s a simple blend but I find it so comforting, relaxing, addictive and intoxicating. This is a perfect scent for day or night, and any occasion. It’s an easy reach. The Lavender note the strongest (which I love) followed by the vanilla. The ginger, cacao and vetiver linger in the background.

I was so curious about this one since I see it so often in IG. The opening of this perfume is amazing. It's something quite unique what comes to designers but even niche Vanilla perfumes. Vanilla, Lavender, cacao and Ginger works together perfectly creating absolutely interesting and surprising combination.

What an interesting beginning and what a sad ending. The pyramid definitely has an udeclared lemon at the top (it's great, it gives a vivacity) and ambersomething with burnt sugar at the base, which, on the one hand, makes it mainstream, but on the other hand - how many times can them spoil everything with this "smell"?

Goddess may very well be my favorite perfume. It’s what kickstarted my obsession this year, I got it as a gift in june and was blown away by it. It has that designer DNA for sure, where notes are harder to discern, but the vanilla is so well done and elegant, it’s a no brainer and a year-round staple.

I actually like Eternity Flame. It's not the greatest fragrance I've ever smelled, still trying to figure that one out, but it smells good. My wife always says I smell good when I wear it. Trust me, if she doesn't like a fragrance she lets me know. I actually had a random woman at the grocery store tell me I smelled good when I was wearing it. It's fruity, leathery, with a slight herbal tone. Projects pretty good for first couple of hours and lasts six or seven hours on my skin. If I spray my clothes I can get about eight hours. Perfect for the Fall and it's inexpensive. So what more can you ask for in a fragrance? Smells good, lasts long, can pull compliments, and cheap. It does it's job!

It´s nice. Blindbought It and It did not disappoint. Several faces during freshly sprayed to the last dry down. Pineapple, a bit Oriental, amber, Sage and least to say alot of potent Rosemary. Clean n´ Fresh. Longevity is a good 8h+ and sillage over moderate. The shirt smells really good the day after I would say. It has the original Eternity edt dna but spicier and more things going on. Keep reaching for it quite often because it suits many situations well. A little hidden Gem and a cheapy that deserves more love. Actually well done (in the Eternity flankers jungle

On my skin, this has the distinct Eternity DNA that runs through the line. It's a leather note scent, enhanced by sweet, sharp pineapple in the top notes, herbal rosemary in the middle and dark, deep labdanum in the base. I was honestly underwhelmed with this, which is a shame since Eternity is one of my favorite designer fragrances.

Stop, stop, stop! Before you roll your eyes at the absolutely cheesy and clichéd phrase in my title (ugh, what a thought!!), I only chose this because of the fragrance name, which carries the subtitle "Flame." I could have just as easily written something about "Fire and Flame," which wouldn't have turned out any better either :D Anyway, Eternity Flame for Men is my first test of a men's Eternity fragrance, and it was purely by chance that I sprayed this scent on myself. I was once again standing in front of the fragrances and somehow didn't really know what to try. So I closed my eyes, reached out my hand, and grabbed a random fragrance. When I think about it, it was kind of lucky that there wasn't a lady in the department (since women like to wander into the men's section), who knows what I would have "grabbed" with my eyes closed... :D Well, I almost wanted to shout "yuck, not Eternity" after grabbing the fragrance, but I must admit I was quite positively surprised by the scent, despite its clear synthetic notes! The Scent: Right from the start, the fragrance smells intensely sweet and spicy. But before it really kicks in with rosemary, general spices, and an amber-like sweetness, you first notice the pineapple. No, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no, no (by the way, I'm typing all these "no's" individually, this is NOT copy & paste :D) no, no, no!!!! Just because you can smell pineapple doesn't mean it smells like Aventus. And I won't make a comparison with Aventus just because you can smell pineapple... you Aventus disciples are really incredible freaks!!!! Anyway, back to the scent! So it smells of pineapple, which has a pleasantly fruity-sweet aroma, but it doesn't last very long. Very soon, this fruity note mostly fades away, and then herbal-spicy and warm-sweet scents emerge, namely the described amber-like notes (probably the labdanum), which come across as warm alongside the crisp-spicy aura, as well as the rosemary, which smells nice as a culinary herb but soon recedes a bit into the background. After that, not much really changes, as labdanum (or this lovely amber-like sweetness) together with generally undefined spices forms the base. Alongside, there’s the usual mainstream synthetic scent, which is quite okay and doesn’t bother me at all. All in all, a nice fragrance worth checking out. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage was quite okay or good, so the scent should be noticeable for a while without having to get too close. I also found the longevity to be really good at over eight hours. The Bottle: The bottle is rectangular and has a rounded top. On it sits the chrome-plated, cylindrical neck, on which the square, capless spray head is placed, which by the way disperses a rather fine mist. The fragrance liquid is red-brown, fitting the name and the sweet amber scent. All in all, quite nice. So, I liked "Flame for Men." It may not be a fragrance that you absolutely need (otherwise, you'd really have to have more than 1000 fragrances on your shelf if you had to have everything, right??? :DDD), but in my opinion, you wouldn't make a mistake if you treated yourself to this scent (and this is how the shelf actually fills up with 1000 fragrances over time :DDD). Yes, seriously, I'm not really a big Eternity fan; for example, I don't like the original women's version, but this one comes across very well with its spicy-warm and sweet scent, especially now in autumn or winter. It has a pleasant aura, lasts long enough, and is suitable for both day and evening wear. Viewed this way, it’s a jack-of-all-trades or all-rounder and is therefore worth a test, especially if you don't mind the noticeable but not overly bothersome synthetic notes, or like me, don't get bothered by them. And that’s it, so I’ll wrap it up and wish you all a nice evening, until then :)

Recently, I was looking for a fragrance that would emit a fresh, citrusy aura on cooler autumn days, while still being minimal in the sweet/aromatic direction. Just to be able to radiate a bit of cozy body warmth during weekend activities on cooler days in autumn. The fragrance should be suitable for casual occasions. In the office, I usually only use subtle and super-safe "go-tos". I was already familiar with Boss' The Scent and Armani's Stronger with You - both of which are not so bad for me, but still a bit too synthetic/tacky. It should be a little greener and more natural. Joop's Wow! would have also worked for this purpose, but it's too strong for me. I wanted something more discreet. In the process, I stumbled upon this rather unknown Eternity flanker and must say that it pretty much meets my expectations in this regard. However, I am also a "CK" fan (which I believe is not so common here). I think the theme of "Flame" has been quite well transferred to the Eternity DNA. I am particularly fond of the heart note with the rosemary and amber progression. If you enjoy this kind of spiciness and like (or used to like) Eternity, you might want to take a closer look at Eternity Flame. The bottle is quite stylish, the perfume color is nice, and the scent is pleasing. However, it doesn't work for me above 10°C, as it is still too sweet for that.

Somehow, I didn't have my sights set on this fragrance at all. It was more of a chance encounter during one of my forays to see if anything useful had emerged in the mainstream. It certainly wasn't a sense of anticipation for a possible flanker of the original.

...but a warm-spicy-fruity-woody autumn and winter chill dispeller. And above all, a clone of----? ...nothing, none of the fragrances I know so far. Perhaps a little bit like its own original - without Flame. Simply "for men" -- yet also completely different. It may be a bit confusing. Yet I can't keep my nose off my wrist. A perfume of metamorphoses.

I blind bought stars from Ebay a few years ago because I really like Jimmy Choo EDP, but can't stand the artificial smelling pear top note in it. I thought a version with orange instead of pear would be more to my taste. It did not disappoint, I wear this a lot around Christmas. This is exactly what I imagined, Jimmy Choo with a beautiful warm fruity orange instead of the screechy pear that reminds me of nail-polish remover. I really love the combination of sweet, sticky, caramelly toffee, dirty patchouli, dusty vanillic orchid and juicy fruit. Like the original Jimmy Choo, it might be a typical fruitchouli on paper, but they all have a unique, distinctive note about them and smell kind of addictive to me. Very delicious and a bit sultry, intense and very long lasting. The warm orange also makes Stars a bit Christmas-like, so I wouldn't wear this in summer. In the colder seasons I find it quite versatile though, as it balances on the line between cozy and sexy.

This is such a yummy, gourmand scent that is actually quite appropriate for daytime wear. Definitely a cold-weather fragrance, I wore it to work today and was surrounded by a wonderful cloud of toffee, orange, and patchouli goodness! I couldn't wait to get home and spray more on myself (without worrying about asphyxiating anyone around me!) It is incredibly long-lasting, 8 hours at least on my skin. A very successful blind buy!

I am so glad that I was able to snag this scent in the souk. I only learned about it after it was discontinued, so I didn't know it, yet its fragrance notes really appealed to me. I do not regret it. This scent is caramel-like and sweet, but not edible. It is a beautiful, sensual fragrance with a very special note that has captivated me. Some time ago, I had a moment of recognition when I discovered this note in another perfume - it is the Tiger Orchid. Despite my green thumb, it might even be worth getting one :-)

~ Inspiration ~ I wasn't really impressed by the regular "Jimmy Choo." So I had higher hopes for this limited "Stars" variant and received a sample from Chrissy1409. ~ Bottle ~ The round shape with indentations has been retained - but here in a golden tone. ~ Fragrance ~ Upon spraying, it is a bit earthy due to the patchouli. After a few minutes, a somewhat artificial, tangy-sweet mandarin note unfolds with caramel-like toffee. Warm sandalwood and tiger orchid also provide a woody-floral spiciness. ~ Longevity ~ On my skin, it lasts about 6 hours (a bit longer on clothing and hair). You should spray it from a distance; otherwise, it becomes too musty-synthetic for me. ~ Occasion ~ It fits well into the cooler days of spring and autumn. Instead of candied apples, there are candied oranges here! ~ Conclusion ~ Unfortunately, this variant didn't really convince me either... you can recognize this typical "Jimmy Choo" character, just more orange in this case.

Despite I highly respect their fashion side, I’ve never really been a fan of Burberry fragrances. London and Touch are basically the only ones I consider worth trying and/or having, and especially London. I am much of a fan of Antoine Maisondieu, and if you like him too, London is surely one not to miss. The notes may seem “conventional”, but the result is well distinctive and peculiar. It opens with a really nice and sophisticated sort of crisp, greenish, herbal tobacco accord rounded by a fantastic and really recognizable note of mimosa (that sort of warm “pollen” feel), and an equally unusual frame of notes ranging from slightly honeyed-fruity, to ambery (“ambroxan-ish”, actually), resinous-sweet and slightly floral, all topped with a sprinkle of spices; quite complex if you ask me, but it works just perfectly. Leather is listed, but you’ll have to dig for it, and it’s the usual sort of contemporary leather – subtle, clean, “polished” leather. Shortly it’s a sort of thin, quite discreet and really clean “contemporary herbal-Oriental” scent revolving around tobacco with a sprinkle of color around it - from greenish, to spicy, to that fruiy-resinous-floral stuff. It has a sort of “niche” vibe, it smells creative and quite different from the usual mainstream paths, and the quality seems really good to my nose. The evolution is funny; the opening is quite bold and intriguing, then it looks like disappearing from your skin for a while, then it “arises” back again with a persistent and cozy drydown mostly comprising tobacco, leather and dusty-incense amber, still with a “manly” floral-honeyed nuance. Worth having for me; it isn’t a masterpiece but it smells good, classy, distinctive, rather “young” (in a positive meaning), much discreet but with a solid sillage, “contemporary” and with that sort of transparent, crisp cleanness that characterizes Maisondieu’s style. Well worth the cheap price. 7,5/10

Burberry London unfolds like a seafarer's story: a bold opening of tobacco leaves steeped in rum and molasses, cut with black pepper and cinnamon. The scent evokes the intimacy of a well-aged navy cut tobacco, dry yet intoxicating, drawing you into its spicy warmth and port wine undertones. Then, like waves calming after a storm, it transitions—soft mimosa glows beneath supple leather, reminiscent of old taverns and worn jackets. Resinous opoponax and guaiac wood add depth, mellowing the spice into whispers. Finally, it lingers with an ambered glow, not shouting but quietly enveloping, like fading sunlight over the ocean. Elegantly composed yet accessibly priced, this fragrance offers a timeless dance of sweetness, spice, and nostalgia—a modern ode to age-old adventures. 9/10

There are parks near where I live. Every now and then I go there for running or jogging. If it has rained recently, the smells of drizzle, grass, wet earth, leaves, resin, wood and pine needles mix in my nostrils, and what comes out is like this scent. It tastes like wet woods and spices. Well, I don't find it particularly spicy, not like an Indian dish; it focuses on moderately sweet but not cloying raw tobacco. The mimosa note feels good and looks great, especially in the opening, and is entirely faithful, as it is synthetic. Mimosa is one of those hints that are difficult to recognize for those who have never heard it just picked or in the next two hours. I love mimosa, and I like to put my nose in a fresh and fragrant bouquet. Almost immediately after application, the misty mimosa rises above me. It is the first note to break through and leaves an aggressive impression. There's a hint of subdued lavender and bergamot, quickly set aside by hot cinnamon, hot pepper, and sweet orange. London knows how to add spice to woody and floral scents to help create a different take on the spices. The initial blend, on my nose, blends perfectly and soon turns into something that reveals evergreens and leather. I must say that this unknown perfume took me entirely by surprise. It reminds me of the smell of some studies full of books, the scent in the waiting room when I went to the family doctor as a child, and we had to wait our turn. Then comes the leather, a tarred birch, I guess, along with the fortified wine. The roaster claims to be port wine, an aromatic liqueur from Portugal, which shares some similarities with Italian Marsala. They are both red wines infused with aromatic herbs. I don't find it dark but pungent. Tobacco, mixed with cinnamon leaves, also reveals its more acrid and less woody nature. The Burberry London aroma improves over time, and this is where it shines. Tobacco is a major player here. It's a pretty sweet tobacco note, an excellent match of leather and cinnamon to give it something unique. Something a little smoky and aged just right, like a whiskey barrel, with port instead of whiskey. As the middle notes develop, the leather continues to hold its own, and a sweet and ever so soft aroma takes over. That beautiful leather accord marks the beginning of the transition to the dry down. The port-wine present in the heart has almost disappeared, and woody notes emerge from the base. The last phase includes opoponax and honey-like tobacco. This aroma is sweet and narcotic, a cherry and vanilla pipe tobacco. I don't know why the Burberry colony takes this route on me, but it is undoubtedly a pleasant journey into foggy, humid and decadent London. The dark notes, composed of smoked guaiac wood and oak bark, show a dominant presence throughout the fragrance's life and give it a dark, sweet and vigorous depth. The dry, woody and amber accord with a bit of bitterness remains exquisitely on the skin. A few hours after spraying it, there is only a very close smell to the skin, which no one feels. I hope it marries your skin better because it's worth it. Like other Burberry perfumes, this one is moderate in the way it projects and moderates its longevity. I love it when the masculine fragrance successfully balances warmth, masculinity and sweetness, and Burberry London does. It is one of my favourite scents on the scarf and sweaters, as it seems to bloom under the wool lining as my body heat amplifies it. If you are looking for a great perfume that ripens in the crisp autumn air, Burberry London should be on your list. I've always liked wearing it in the evening, but it's also good during the day. It is an opulent and magnetic perfume that evokes autumn in all its splendour. Just wait for the temperature to drop enough to call for a thick jacket or sweater. I would recommend this product to anyone who loves the outdoors or loves to smell like the outdoors. Ultimately, in the same baseball field as Bogart, but not quite similar apart from the opening. Bogart becomes powdery vanilla, where London remains piney resinous. And you, did you already know this fragrance? What do you think? I base the review on a 100ml bottle I have owned since February 2016. -Elysium

I was eager to test Burberry London for Men as a potential purchase for my then-boyfriend, who was a rather heavy smoker. Unfortunately this fragrance didn't suit him, however I am quite captivated by the scent. Burberry London smells like the ideal man to me. Masculine, strong, fierce and sophisticated. This fragrance is certainly spicy, but not in a nose-burning, Indian cuisine type sense. It's more peppery and herbaceous. In the opening, the violet leaf, lavendar and bergamot create a somewhat soothing and aromatic quality, however the pepper note insists on making this fragrance masculine and strong. The introduction of mimose in the heart is actually really unique in the way that it adds a little sweetness along with the smooth yet sexual scent of leather. Despite the sweetness, Burberry London has rugged appeal. Although I am not a smoker myself, the scent of tobacco puts me at ease. I love the way my ex-boyfriend smelt; like smokey tobacco, mint-flavoured chewing gum, musty clothes and fruit-scented hair gel. The drydown in a way reminds me of him. It has a very smokey, musty and woodsy quality that I wouldn't mind wearing myself. With that being said, although Burberry London is essentially a very masculine fragrance, a woman could perhaps succeed in wearing it. It would take the right kind of woman however.

Let me start with saying that this is an excellent autumn/winter fragrance. It has a very masculine and sophisticated scent. It opens fresh, spicy with notes of lavender, pine and a strong cinnamon presence. As it dries down, it transforms into a sweet, tobacco-like scent with a subtle leathery touch and a hint of smokiness. Many people describe it as "Christmas in a bottle," and I would agree. Longevity is average, around 4 hours, but those 4 hours are absolutely wonderful. I wouldn't recommend over-spraying it; instead, reapply it to avoid overwhelming others. It is inoffensive and doesn't have a big scent cloud so this makes it a safe office scent. I got a 100ml bottle for under 30€, which is a great deal. I blind bought London for Men Eau de Toilette , and it’s definitely one of my best blind buys. I highly recommend it—it's a fantastic choice for cold days, especially for the chilly December holidays.

Probably my favorite fall scent, the only Burberry that matters, and a proof that you can do much with little, meaning that a brand with not a large amount of money to spend on fragrances could do a great job, if the perfumer envolved is good.

A great and very classy gentleman's mix of cinnamon, tobacco and liquor. Smooth, rich, a little sweet and fruity and wears perfectly in the winter like a soft wooly sweater. In my opinion it's a woody and spicy oriental with a touch of lavender and vanilla.

"Burberry London Men" is my personal favourite among all the Burberry fragrances, because it's refined and elegant, but not too formal. I feel very comfortable wearing it myself, especially in autumn/winter.

Only in some very rare cases a perfume has been presented so much in sackloth and ashes as Burberry London Men. The greyish-brown tartan fabric that covers the bottle seems to date back to those times when the Scots had only some weak plant juices to use on their sheep's wool, no colourful chemicals.

Burberry London comes across as a light, spicy, oriental scent that if perfect for a gentleman. It has all the characteristics of a "serious" or refined masculine fragrance. I like it. I also like that it's inspired by a city which I live in (London). Although I think this better represents someone's "idea" of London rather than the city itself.

The philosopher Slavoj Zizek once referred to Coke Zero without caffeine as the pure nothing. This formulation also fits this fragrance wonderfully. Even while the sprayed liquid dries on the skin, the scent vanishes into the imperceptible without ever having been present. A hint of orange and lavender lingers, but to say that one could 'smell' this would be too much. It's astonishing that this exercise in olfactory reduction comes from the same perfumer with the unpronounceable name who is also responsible for Yves Saint Laurent's Tuxedo, which is quite popular here. So unfortunately, this fragrance is not worth mentioning, and I only wrote this review because after trying out some rather prominent scents today, this petit rien caught me off guard ;-)

Eternity for Women Aromatic Essence offers a subtly coconut, gently aromatic composition that immediately creates a soft holiday atmosphere. There is an easygoing, sun‑kissed quality to the scent that makes it very pleasant and effortless to wear, especially for relaxed, casual moments. It diverges noticeably from the original Eternity, presenting a different style and mood—lighter, more carefree, and with a warm tropical undertone rather than the classic floral structure. Overall, it’s an enjoyable, laid‑back fragrance that brings a touch of vacation ease into everyday life.

Coconut. Sandalwood. Clean, sweet, sleek. Synthetic. Smells like the base fragrance used in about 65% of shower gels targeted at female audience. Lavender is also technically there, standing awkwardly in the corner like a child who knows that no one really wanted him at this party, but whose mother still made him go. This has nothing to do with the original Eternity Eau de Parfum . The whole thing honestly feels like an afterthought to Eternity for Men Aromatic Essence . As if the women's team remembered that they had this project due 2 days before the deadline and asked the men's team for whatever scraps they had left and to copy their homework. It's fresh, but by "feeling clean after a shower" association rather than on its own merit. Becomes a skin scent in less than ~30 minutes. About an hour into the experience coconut mellows out and assumes a support role to sandalwood. That's it. The next ~10 hours are just creamy shower gel-like sandalwood that slowly gets softer as time goes by. In the last hour it sours and starts smelling like body odor. What can I say... A fitting finale for this kind of experience?

Well I'm disappointed. I was really hoping my skin would pick up this amazing strawberry, fruity gourmand scent I've seen people raving about, but it was not the case. At first spray I smelled this weird sour strawberry alcoholic beverage on me. I think the strawberry got drowned out by the tart cherries and raspberries. After this initial scent dissipates I'm left with this generic and synthetic perfume smell. I think I could pick out a bit of jasmine and violet, but there was this weird plastic accord that came through. After a good hour, things finally began to settle. I could smell tart fruits: not the sweet-smelling yummy ones, but the almost over-ripe sour ones. I did sense the musk trying to turn everything in this soft feminine perfume. Jasmine and violet were nowhere to be smelled although I did detect a small aspect of creaminess (nothing that was really a wow factor though). After about two hours, it ended up smelling like expensive strawberry shampoo: synthetic but fruity. It became a bit nicer, but it wasn't enough to save everything. I will certainly not be getting a bigger sized bottle. I'm still very disappointed as I was hoping I could add a nice strawberry and fruity perfume to my collection. This won't be it.

The 2nd most disgusting perfume I have ever smelled. It smells like a nuclear synthetic strawbery air freshner and people around me thought the same, so trying this perfume has made me wonder about perfumery and people tastes.. like one of the most beatiful things in the world is diversity and people have difference tastes and we have to respect them but with this one I cant understand it and I dont get what was MFK thinking T-T Sorry for the people who loves it, I hate giving this kind of statements, but it is one of those that gave to me such a strong physical reaction that I have to exorcice it. I hate cheap synthetic fruits in my perfumes and this one has too much

There is a note here that I can’t get past. It reminds me of a friend that loves gourmand fragrances and who smokes pot and those two scents blended together is stuck to her car seat. It’s that. However it is a lovely fragrance if synthetic notes don’t bother you. I prefer this in the colder months.

This is better than expected. This is like a whiff of bubble gum or fruity soda. I say whiff because it isn't overpowering like I expect from most fruity "feminine" fragrances, it has an airiness to it. Its a light, sweet, and fruity fragrance with a hint of tartness. This is very feminine leaning and I would say its good for young girls as well as older women. Its well made, its not synthetic or super sugary, a pleasant surprise. It has a scent bubble, so it lifts off of the skin just enough to be noticeable to those close to you. Unfortunately, it didn't have great longevity. I would say this maybe lasted 3 hours on my skin. There are several sizes available, a 100ml is $168, a 50ml is $135, and a 30ml is $105.

I had finished up what was left of my decanter a few months ago and have been absolutely devastated and missing her since. More recently, I got myself the full sized bottle and she's just as lovely as I remember. Fruity, sweet, almost overwhelmingly so, but it does mellow out the longer it sits on my skin. Less candy and more true berries and florals. If I wasn't so in love with the way they've formulated this strawberry note, I might look the other way. But there's something about it that other perfumes I've tried in between just haven't been able to hit for me. I always find myself reaching for her, gravitating towards her. It also lasts a long while on my skin and clothes, so it just feels so worth it to me. It's so nice and sweet and fruity in all the right ways, it just makes me happier when I wear it!

Lately, I'm used to hate popular perfumes and love the hated ones so, don't get me wrong. I guess that's my nose not working properly. So, when I saw the notes of this perfume I was so excited and thought it would be a nice candidate for my next signature. It let me down.. As a gourmand lover let me explain how I rank my perfumes into this category.

Although this fragrance didn't come out until 2018, this reminds me of a girl who used to wear this when I was in college. It feels very bittersweet and nostalgic to me - like fleeting memories of simpler times, being with friends and watching the sunset; sweet, innocent, but something you know won't last forever so you try to cherish it.

The Burberry Her Eau de Parfum is a clean, sweet berry blend of strawberry, raspberry, and blackcurrant that is candy-like. As it dries down, there are notes of florals, jasmine and violet that peep through, overall making a powdery scent. The dry down is warm leaving a creamy texture.

When i first got this one it reminded me of a creamy strawberry scented lip balm or body mist but with much better lasting power and projection. I do get the smallest similarity between Burberry Her and Ariana Grande Cloud, this one being a strong strawberry scent and cloud more coconut. I absolutely love Cloud and Her. Her is better suited for spring/summer.

Sometimes House Burberry nail it as with Burberry Brit EdT, which I have had and loved for many years now. Or as with Burberry for Women, which I had, used up and loved because of its wonderful warmth and depth. Sometimes they do not as with Burberry Weekend, which I dismissed due to the heavy and, on my skin, sweaty Musk note. Or as with Burberry Her.

Really starting to like this one. A clean fuzzy smell that works great in summer. I really don’t feel this is a generic fragrance at all. Fresh and not too fruity sweet. Floral without being heavy. The freesia smells amazing in this. Moderate sillage and longevity with 5-8 sprays, nothing spectacular, but it’s one of those fragrances I can smell on myself close up all day and I don’t mind reapplying an extra spray here and there.

This latest iteration of CK Eternity feels like it's wandered far from its roots. Forget the green, fresh, woody, and semi-spicy fougere you associate with the original. Instead, prepare for a syrupy sweet experience with vanilla and rum notes – a far cry from the classic. While it's understandable that brands want to stay contemporary, this feels less like an evolution and more like a completely different fragrance that could have stood on its own. If you're chasing the original Eternity DNA, stick with the EDP, which offers a much truer, modern fougere interpretation. This new version, while pleasant enough, leans heavily into "Stronger With You" territory and misses the mark for those seeking the essence of Eternity.

We shake hands. We smile at each other. Pleasant. You leave. I have forgotten you. At the beginning: lavender imitation. Not bad, but not a complete lavender. For a long time, nothing happens, then suddenly there’s rum and vanilla. Very nice and very cozy, just unfortunately also very weak. Oh that one? Yes, that was quite nice. What, he’s not coming this time? Well, that’s okay too. But send him my best regards!

This fragrance brings together what belongs together. It allows one to sink into the unwritten love letters of such beautiful innocence. A renaissance of long-past youthful romances. The euphoria when signs of young love gradually become apparent. It envelops with fragile, sweet woods and finds in its dramaturgy a conclusion in its wicked place. However, the real highlight lies precisely between the beginning and the end. For there it seduces us, with vanilla, lemon, and honey it captures us and makes us vulnerable. I speak with the best intentions in recommending it to all those who are searching for Cupid's arrows.

This is a safe, although boring woods centric scent. You get a few minutes of bergamot and pepper, a bit of pine, but after that is all cedar. That’s it. Everyone go home. It’s boring but I like it, it’s well crafted, not a lot of nonsense notes to mislead the customer. It’s just a nice fresh woody scent. Projection and longevity suck, but at discounters, the price isn’t bad at all. Recommended if you want a nice not in your face scent at a good price.

A perfect flanker. You get the edt for day in the office or outdoors and this for the cozy evening. Benzoin sweetness with Frankincense cooling it and cedar in the background, probably my favorite out of the whole line. Sweet and cozy not particularly unique or interesting but its very nice resinous sweet frag for sure.

This version of Burberry Hero begins with the fleeting season of apricots and musing on how easily they bruise, how you’ll never again know the childhood euphoria of that pretty smocked easter dress the color of rice powder and coconut with ruffles and lace and three pearly buttons but you will never forget the unabashed joyful flavor of a mouth crammed full of jelly beans. What Hero where and who is it that smells like the sour cream powdered sugar sweetness of picnic ambrosia salad, all pools of Cool Whip, and marshmallows soaked in the juice of tiny mandarin oranges and pineapple syrup, but not that really–rather the phantom of that atomic summer fruit confection, the faint lingering fragrance of it, at the bottom of a polished cedar bowl.

I will start this by saying it is not a bad smell, not particularly interesting or unique however. All I smell is the benzoin and woods, don’t get any of the fruitiness some people claim. Lasts for a while 10-12 hours and projects pretty decent. Good for when I don’t know what to wear. Price 5/10 (not worth the hefty price would be worth it if like say 80-50 bucks) Smell 8/10 (boring) Longevity 7/10 Projection 8/10 Bottle 9/10 Total: 37/50

One of my first bottles I ever purchased after taking one whiff of a spray from a decant and I had to have this in my life. Pretty much sweet pine and some balsamic spiciness. Vibing with the outdoors here. Through the mids comes up a sort of smoky vanilla note, but not very sweet. Just enough to compliment the top along with some incense type note to play in the background. The base is exploding with cedar, but fear not, it's not all pencil shavings. It's more complex. I would assume the different cedars brings out the best in each other and you are left with a slightly dry resinous, cedar powerhouse that lacks the sweetness of many modern scents of today, which, in my opinion, is welcome to my palate. While it can be hard to pull off in the dog days of summer, even in cooler summer days, I can give this a spray or two and be pleased. I have to admit, I am not much for designer fragrances these days, but this one makes my cut. Well worthy of anyone seeking a masculine outdoors scent. Also, the magnetic bottle cap is a chef's kiss.

... sang Bonnie Tyler in the eighties - and I sang along fervently - even though I didn't actually wish for a "hero," but rather a sympathetic, empathetic man who knows how to deal with my weaknesses. That's already "heroic" enough.

I tested the fragrance at my trusted perfumery and was immediately smitten. There’s a lot of complaining about this scent not smelling woody, yes, that’s true. That it is very sweet, yes, that’s also true. Actually, everything that is said is true. Not green, synthetic, sweet, and creamy, but is that bad?

For those who enjoy woody, forest scents, the skin pores stand at attention when reading about the fragrance ingredients in Hero Perfume. I soon had to visit my favorite drugstore to sniff the candidate. I'll say it straight: a big disappointment for me. A heavy sweet cloud hovers over everything that could even remotely smell like wood, forest, or resin.

In my opinion, Burberry Hero is a perfect everyday fragrance. A fresh, sweet, and slightly woody scent. Also good for a quick refresh. The perfume hardly develops at all (constant same smell). It is a perfect everyday fragrance for me for several reasons. The perfume is not intrusive due to its weak sillage.

Burberry Hero is a good sporty daytime fragrance without any rough edges. Very pleasing for those who enjoy something sporty, slightly sweet, and a bit creamy. The scent hardly changes over the course of wearing it. One perceives the pine needles paired with cedar and then the sweetness. After about 4-5 hours, the hero has done his job and takes a rest.

What a beautiful rose scent, I would almost say elegant - so fine and ladylike. The rose is so delicate and finely powdered by the sandalwood and musk. After about half an hour, it has taken on a somehow clean aura, which I really like. There is nothing piercing or loud, just everything in an incredibly fine and cultivated manner - the aristocratic woman. But she also winks with her eye and cheekily jumps into a puddle in her very elegant rubber boots, laughing her soft, melodious laugh. Her scent lingers in every room she has been in and spreads like a fine bottle of old and wonderfully fragrant port wine. Everything here is fine, reserved, and noble. Her scent is unmistakable, and that’s how you know she was there. An excellent fragrance - I would say from mid-thirties onwards. Just let the lady out, my dears. The scent lasts longer than a day - thus her memory remains. The bottle is a gem, full of cut facets, like the many sides of a woman. And on top, as a finishing touch, the golden ball, for us girls, the crown.

I reached Burberry Hero with no expectations, when it was released. And it didn't gave me good impressions. I wrote in a statement that it is very boring and generic cedar-iso e super smell and that Encre Noire is a better woody experience. Well, i still think that Encre Noire is better but, this is actually good. Not great, not fantastic, but decent and well blended. Aurélien Guichard is a great perfumer and has done some classics by now, so it's not a surprise that this would be good. The combination of juicy and fresh bergamot with the aromatic and dry woody base is very appealing and masterfully well blended. It didn't convinced me in my first impressions because it seemed very vulgar but, for a fragrance in the mainstream world, where everything has weird sweetness all over, this is really chic and sophisticated. As it dries down, the cedarwood (the combo of 3 different types, in fact) is what makes this fragrance a good one and not a cheap and generic one. Because of the high quality of these materials, the drydown is actually good and long lasting, and don't became cheap like many other offerings. This is not revolutionary, neither a great and must have fragrance, but it's a really nice, well blended scent, that makes a good office scent, or a causal everyday type of fragrance. If you want something versatile, masculine and polite, this is a contender, along with Encre Noire, Terre d'Hermes of even Bleu de Chanel. The bottle is nice and the magnetic cap it's a nice touch. I don't like the new fond in the name of the brand and the name Hero it's not that accurate, but what matters it's the fragrance itself, so, if you want something new and not sweet, young and fun, but want something masculine and with nice quality for a good price, this could be your next purchase. 3/5

Scentrack: Tina Turner – We Don’t Need Another Hero I was excited when Burberry announced the release of the new masculine line. Although a little bit concerned because of the name – Hero. Unfortunately, my concerns were justified. Burberry Hero is just another 2020’s fragrance. Inoffensive, easy to wear and politically correct male fragrance. Still, it possesses some pale interesting woody nuances that Aurelien Guichard replayed from his earlier creations like This is Him by Zadig & Voltaire or Bois Noir by Robert Piguet. Hero starts with, nowadays very popular, bergamot, some metallic undertones and a nice creamy touch that morphs into a full-blooded cedar heart. The cedar accord is really made of a fresh Virginian variety and a sweeter Atlas one. The composition is extremely contemporary woody, yet not overly synthetic. It has some nice woody and masculine undertones which I can associate with the classic Burberry brand. However, too weak, and bland. Hero is not a bad composition. It smells good, it is versatile, and easy to wear. Not so heroic, but a perfect ticket for newcomers to enter the serious niche woody game. Still, do we need another Hero? No Burberry, we don’t.

I knew about this fragrance for some time but never took the time to really try it and test it out, then i saw a great price on it and looked on parfumo , seemed lke my type of fragrance then i went and tried it out and this is how it smells: When u first spray it , it smells synthetic and alcoholic. Then it becomes very woody, ambery, spicy and fresh which is my favorite type of smells. later u get a bit more fruitiness but it smells like another flanker to the chanell alure line exept the first 2 minutes are very synthetic. Performance is average , nothing to complain about but nothing to compliment either, its ok. I love magnetic caps so thats also the plus and the bottle is simple and juice colour describes the fragrance very good as well. Price is ok on discounters i think its a good daily fragrance with amber, woods and some spicy freshness, versatility is top tier as well , easy all year around , school , office , work, walk out... For who is it for? For someone looking for a versatile daily that is good but not everyone has it , perfect age group i would say 20 plus , but as a 17 yr old i easily pull it off. Scent: 9/10 , perfect dose of every note and accord, lots of wood and amber and other stuff u alredy know what i mentioned , maybe if they could make it not smell weird at first and blend it even better it would be 10. Performance: 5/10 average perfomance which is okay i dont mind it. 6 hours on skin with ok projection Versatilty: 10/10 one of the most versatile fragrance i have ever tried, and i tried many blue and versatile fragrances bcs i love them so much... Value for money: 7/10 great value but its hard to find anything these days that is really amyzing value. Overall: 8/10

Regarding the aroma, it is a very mass appealing smell, it is fresh, woody and spicy. It's a safe choice, it doesn't have anything too artistic or creative, it's a normal smell but not regular to the point of being boring or lacking personality. It has a golden and rejuvenating aura, I would say it is a fragrance for an active, sophisticated, professional, elegant, confident and modern man. It has a slightly charming vibe. Regarding performance, it has a moderate longevity, around 6 hours - quite good for such a fresh Eau de Toilette. It also has a decent projection - nothing out there, but anyone standing 1/2 arms away can smell it (at least for 1h30). I imagine it is mostly used in summer, spring and autumn, precisely in that order, and especially during the day. It is a good option for the daily routine: work, leisure and, in some cases, sporting events.

Burberry Hero is marketed as a men’s fragrance in a marvelously ridiculous advertisement with Adam Driver but I try not to think of perfume in terms of gender, so you won’t hear me discussing whether something smells masculine as opposed to feminine. Which I am sure that some people find frustrating and my response to that is “so what?” There’s better and more interesting and exciting ways to think about and talk about the art and application and aesthetics of fragrance than filtered through the construct of gender. Despite all that high-minded talk, I’m not sure that there is actually any sort of exciting way to talk about Hero. I’m tempted to share my thoughts on the characteristics I find appealing in my platonic ideal of what a hero is supposed to be, but that’s just the thing, isn’t it? Heroes come in all shapes and sizes, and I believe (or at least after school specials and Saturday morning cartoons have taught me) that anyone is capable of rising to the occasion and performing a heroic feat. And maybe that’s the problem here; I feel like this composition while pleasant enough in a crisp-cedary-breeze way and a sunny-sweet-mild-citrus-slice-in-a-glass-of-sparkling-water way, is one of those scents that, in trying to appeal to everyone, becomes awfully bland and nondescript, lacking in any amount of charm or charisma. I wore it for a few hours and what I am left with is a sour tannic powderiness, with a weirdly aquatic translucence. Like an Arnold Palmer powdered drink mix stirred in with too much water and poured over an excess of ice, and piped in through the vents of a day spa, I guess? This is a fragrance I would prefer as a scented dry shampoo or some form of quick refresh, so I can see it working in certain circumstances. Circumstances being you're on autopilot and you want to put in the minimum amount of hygiene-related work but you also don't want to be smelly, so admittedly the bar is really low for this situation. My main stumbling block here is that they went with Adam Driver to market this perfume to us ...and I am inclined to imagine Adam Driver as more deliciously, overwhelmingly, bombastically stanky than the milquetoast reality of Hero

This fragrance gets hated on for being “boring” and then there’s the token complaints about it not lasting past the 6 hour mark. I would understand this if Hero EDT was from a niche brand and you had to pay over $100 to get a bottle. But we are talking about a designer Eau De Toilette that can be found on discounter websites for under $50.

As a good Adam Driver fan, I've been to the local perfume shop to smell Hero by Burberry, finally! I’ll be honest, I expected much much more. Probably it’s because it’s 1 year that I’m exploring niche perfumery so I’m used to other kind of stuff even if I don’t disdain commercial perfumery... but this was so...”anonymous”/generic?

The notes say it all. Very woodsy, with a splash of bright bergamot in the opening and spicy, aromatic nuances throughout. A safe perfume if you're looking for something masculine and woodsy that isn't likely to offend people. A bit too safe for my tastes, but I wouldn't mind sitting next to someone who was wearing this.

Well, i like to see some natural ingredients in fragrances. Hero supposedly has a trio of cedarwood oils which made me test it. Well... This is another average fragrance, i have smelled hundreds of similars. I could never detect a natural facet at any stage of the scent. A woody base, a citrus aromatic top and mid...

This is an aromatic herbal fragrance balanced with citrus. Its clean and fresh but not very exciting. This is a typical cologne formula but without the harshness or scratchiness that you come to expect from most mainstream colognes. That tells me its not pumped full of cheap "filler" formulas. It also doesn't dominate the room, its polite and perfect for everyday office use.

Touch for Men is basically the only other Burberry scent I kind of enjoy together with London for Men, and the good old Burberrys from 1992. From the very first sniff, Touch screams “2000s” all over: that synthetic musky-watery texture, the spicy woodiness, the softer hint of violet leaves providing a powdery feel conforming to that “androgynous” type of “new millenium’s urban-informal elegance” so many masculine scents of that decade seemed conforming to. And a really enjoyable smoky vibe (I guess coming from vetiver), just to keep it “manly” enough. Slightly reminding me of Nemo by Cacharel, albeit much less heavy on the spices, but somehow they share a sort of common “mood”; both are mellow, kind of plastic in a fascinating way, spicy and exotic but with a peculiar sort of smooth and slightly aqueous texture. Touch smells just fresher and more focused on vetiver/cedar and spices, with a musky base and a powdery frame, but there’s indeed a tonka-nutty breeze that makes Nemo come to mind. However that’s it, the evolution is almost absent, the projection is elegantly close to skin. Miles far from being a groundbreaking scent, not the greatest quality around for sure... but still a decent crisp fragrance less generic than it may look. 6,5/10

I started to appreciate Burberry colognes only in the last few years, and Brit Rhythm was the first blind buy I won on eBay auction. Then came Sport with its red elastic band, London, Brit, Brit Rhythm Intense, Brit Splash, and recently Touch. I don't have Burberry Man and Mr. Burberry series yet, and I am unsure whether to buy Weekend and The Beat, the latter has very poor longevity and sillage when tested on my skin. So far, I overlooked Touch, perhaps due to its light blue color, which is delicate yet reminds me of Davidoff Echo, Lanvin pour Homme, or Azzaro Chrome. Don'tDon't get me wrong, and I love all of them, I didn't want to have another ozonic, metallic, aquatic clone in my wardrobe. Miserably, I was wrong, because it is reminiscent of none of them. Touch is as a woody-musky-aromatic scent. It combines floral and citrus scents with a hint of cedar, musk, vetiver, and spice. What comes out of this blend is a pure but sweet scent that lingers on you for a long time. It does not stand out initially, but it grows in on you. Initially, it graces the skins with a soft, fresh, and watery violet leaves along with citrus mandarine petitgrain and aromatic slight medicinal artemisia. Here, the perfume begins to move from the lightest of comfort to a more rounded warmth that buzzes with a creamy evergreen. It'sIt's so soft and incredibly comforting, like a bright white most beautiful cotton shirt you put on right after the morning shower... A somewhat soapy, powdery, and gentle aura prevails. While floating to its enchanting heart, the opening blends nicely with Virginia cedar, refined white pepper, and nutmeg, imparting more sweetness and some faint spiciness to the blooming violet with dry woods serving as a backdrop to its powderiness. The dry down becomes a bit more subtle, and the other notes come forward of the white musk and tonka bean. Touch ends with a light vanilla-like accord. There is a heavy tonka bean base note that is particularly strong, and if you don't like that sort of scent, then you're not going to enjoy Touch for Men. My overall impression of Touch is of cleanness, not only the clean lathers and talcum powders of a barbershop but the fresh smell of freshly laundered clothes dried outdoors in the summer sunshine. The ubiquitous violet leaf is further transported to its comforting base, where it is reinforced with sweet tonka bean, clean skin musk, and a dash of vetiver roots for smokiness. This powdery, floral composition is a quality fragrance and has mediocre projection and longevity on my skin and clothes, regrettably. Brilliantly made and named as it is a continuous touch of soft and fresh sensuality. The sensation of lying in a newly bad just made after using your favorite shower gel can be intoxicating. If you are like so many other men who prefer fragrances that speak of dangerous adventure, treasures, and elegant wisdom, Touch is not for you. It is soft like a spring morning dawn, the Touch of your mom's caress, the first kiss you ever received. It is springtime now when I first tried this. It has that smell of spring too it. Various fragrances like springtime, new, refreshing, and alive fill it. It's very catching and seductive. You will either like it or not. If you want it, you will notice the scent grabs you right from the first spray. It's a spring-summer fragrance that could bet worn at any time of the day, in your leisure time, as well as during your working time. Have a lovely Easter Monday, folks. -Elysium

My friend imported bottles of perfume from Australia. I had originally ordered Invictus Legend from her because my bottle was running low. Invictus Legend is one of the few good blue scents but I digress. She insisted I test this instead. It was the first time I recognized violet in a fragrance. We all must take a journey along in fragrance to find the notes we love the most and what combinations of notes we love for any occasion. Burberry Touch is a tapered bottle resembling an exaggerated v taper of a man in a suit with broad shoulders. The cap is wooden and nice. There really isn't alot to Touch. The name suggests it's purpose. You have a light citrus-floral opening. Some call it soapy, but on my skin and not on a card, it smells nothing like soap or bodywash. On my skin the citrus dissipates quickly. Next there sits the beautiful 'cool sensation' of violet balanced with white pepper that's further accentuated with cedar. Creamy tonka bean rounds out the vetiver and musk in the base. Base notes are important because they affect sillage and longevity the most. The perfumer carefully crafted this perfume in a way that let's the cool violet linger ever so sweetly with a 'touch' of powder (the synergy of violet and tonka bean is key) waft from my skin for three hours in 90 degree heat and 30% humidity. After three hours, the violet sits closer and creamy tonka can be smelled. I have no issues with projection or longevity with Touch. Projection and sillage is a proper arms length, even in the harsh heat and sweat of Cambodia. Now my bottle is empty but I keep the bottle because the violet note clings to the cap and is so soothing for me to smell. I already loved tonka bean but I had no idea how much I love the note of violet. Now my perfume journey has me seeking other violet fragrances. Thank you my friend for suggesting this fresh beautiful floral fragrance. It's almost unisex. It was 20 years ahead of it's time and to me it is timeless.

I see this as a nice casual Spring fragrance. Woody, fresh and a bit powdery. I get the vibe of "baby powder" that many are talking about. The smell is quite pleasant, easy to enjoy, not that strong but not that weak either. The Violet is pretty present here. It smells quality, that's what I enjoy about it. It doesn't smell cheap even if it is a cheapie. Somewhere around 20-30$ for a 100ML bottle. Nice looking bottle and nice sprayer as well. Performance is pretty decent. 7 hours, maybe even pushing a bit if you spray more. Sillage and projection are moderate, not weak, not beastly. Some people really love this one. I do encourage you to give it a shot ! Overall : 7/10

I like this one. Burberry Touch for Men has some very likable qualities, which is enough to keep me intrigued. This fragrance opens as a somewhat herbaceous aromatic, however this is not just green herbs, it's a touch powdery and sweet as well, adding to this fragrance's complexity. The pepper note alongside the violet leaves creates an interesting tartness that can either agree or disagree on your skin, depending solely on the individual. Some find this fragrance sweet and powdery, however to my nose it's more spicy-sweet in a masculine sense, and powdery in a way that isn't like baby powder. It smells like a powdery blend of wood shavings and ground nutmeg. The sillage of Burberry Touch for Men is strong but not overwhelming. It's a nice balance between being casual and formal, a fragrance that can suit almost any occasion. Supposedly Burberry Touch for Men is a hit with the ladies, and I can certainly see why. This fragrance is soothing and masculine without trying too hard. In a sense it's perfectly balanced. The longevity was really impressive, lasting a lot longer than I expected it to. I honestly don't think this fragrance could suit just any man, so it is worth testing before buying. I nearly bought this fragrance blind myself because I couldn't manage to track it down. I am pleased to have discovered it, but I don't think it's a fragrance that I could ever pull off.

Scentrack: The Feeling - Sewn At the dawn of the new millennium in 2000, Burberry decided to show the public their vision of 21st century man. Apparently, Touch for Men was a restart of classical masculinity – androgynous, airy and clean. Devoid of emotions, and structured like a vision of sterile and antiseptic future.

Clean, fresh and powdery, with a subtle musk. I enjoy Touch a lot more than I thought I would. Where the fragrance is lacking in complexity, it makes up for it in versatility and is generally inoffensive and easy to wear. Perfect for a day out or office use. I personally enjoy it most after a shower/bath as it makes me feel nice and fresh.

I've tested this a few times in boots. I like it but don't love it. It has a smooth soapy texture and blend. The Notes that are most prominent to me are White Pepper, Vetiver, and White Musk with a subtle hint of Violet and Cedar. Don't get much Mandarin. It is pleasant but something a little synthetic grates on me to stop me wanting to buy a bottle.

I have always been intrigued by a gorgeous fragrance's enchantment - a scent that characterizes a moment and narrates a story about the individual who wears it. I’m thrilled to present my review of Touch For Men, a timeless fragrance from Burberry that I have come to appreciate over the last few weeks. TOP NOTES Touch opens up clean and fresh and gives a 90s vibe.

A soft, powdery, spicy, musky and floral fragrance. This scent reminds me a lot of baby powder and gives the same clean feeling. Suitable for use in spring and moderate weather. The fragrance is dominated by the scent of violet leaves and white musk. The rest of the notes work weakly in the background. Suitable for men over 30 years old and above.

Hannover, at a wedding, 33 degrees. The perfume is spot on. North Sea during the day, breezy 20 degrees. The perfume is spot on. At the university in miserable 12 degrees. The perfume is spot on. ...but seriously: The London Flash is a truly wonderful all-rounder. I can hardly think of an event or occasion where you wouldn't smell great wearing it. Not too quiet and not too loud. It's quite possible that the perfume has been labeled “boring” for this reason. I find it absolutely wonderful. All day long, gentle lychee clouds drift around me, and without the fruitiness getting on my nerves. This is often the case with fruity perfumes. Here, however, the lychee is very gentle, wrapped in cozy, cotton-soft musk. Btw: Yes, I know my headline is quite silly. How about “Flash for Jimmy Choo”? :-P

During my last purchase at the perfume store, I received a fragrance sample and was very excited, as I had wanted to test the perfume in its original version for a long time. The presentation of the perfume and even the sample makes a girl's heart skip a beat. Lots of shimmer and sparkle on the box, and the bottle is a little jewel. An eye-catcher made of cut glass in the shape of a cube, with a crystal cap in delicate purple. I almost bought the fragrance just for that. Fortunately, I got the sample, and my girl’s heart took a sad and disappointed stumble. It is a generic scent - for me, it has no recognizability - no bling bling, no glamour, instead of princess, it’s more like the everyday scent of a housewife doing the weekly shopping. Throughout the entire scent progression, musk dominates with very noticeable citrus accents, and the rest is a continuous mix from which I cannot separate individual components.

This is a strange one for me - it smells so much like a clean, fresh, dewy pine tree after a good rain. I think the woody notes mixed with the peach and wormwood are what's causing this, but man.. it's delightful. And perhaps because of pine association, I feel it's most appropriate in winter (or perhaps even spring, with the aforementioned dewiness). That said, I don't get much warmth from this one, either - To me, it's cool, crisp and refreshing. If I had an office job, this is exactly what I'd wear to work. It's pleasant, doesn't overpower, and isn't at all 'provocative' in my opinion. Which is why I was so perplexed when I saw the adverts here for it. A mostly nude woman lounging lasciviously in an overcoat? And here, I totally pegged this one for an office-appropriate scent!

I really admire Burberry as a house, and it's not because they create anything particularly spectacular, but because their fragrances exude a beautiful sense of warmth and elegance while remaining casual. Burberry Body is a lovely fragrance, very much along the same lines as the Sensuous series by Estee Lauder. Both fragrances sit rather lightly on the skin with a cuddly, yet creamy woodsiness. Some may be initially turned off by Burberry Body's opening, which to my nose was a little chemical, like the scent of insect repellent or hairspray. I was admittedly annoyed by these top notes, and had grave fears for what would follow. Thankfully Burberry Body improves throughout its development. It's not an extremely loud fragrance, yet it does have good projection. Cashmere wood and sandalwood are the most dominant accords to my nose, followed by musk and creamy vanilla. The rose is very subtle, tending to be more sweet and fresh rather than tart-like. Although it isn't technically a skin-scent, Burberry Body smells rather natural and smooth on the skin, like a lightly scented lotion rather than a perfume. I love that I can go about my daily business and occasionally get wafts of a beautiful, inoffensive woods and vanilla blend emanating from my wrists. The longevity is wonderful, really surprising actually. I was thrilled to detect this light fragrance on my skin a good twelve hours after application. I haven't tried the Body Intense flanker, but somehow I don't want to. This fragrance is perfect just the way it is.

Fruity,rosy and musky.The whole composition is good ,nice blended but.....there is something sharp green (may be the absynthe) that keeps me from not loving it.This is good floral with rose and peach dominating ,the base is soft woody with sandalwood and cashmerian wood .All in all is nice for daily wearing with good staying power.

Prefacing my cruelty on September 12, 2023: I've had eleven years to smell this out there in the general public. I tried to give it a second chance last year when I stole a quick spritz of my friend's bottle. Uh, no. It's still a big, stinking NO. I asked my friend if she smelled the floral Nair depilatory cream I smelled. She said she could but it was faint. Also, she said it was one of her guilty pleasure scents, like gasoline or bus exhaust—like things we should not mimic in scent. I was hoping time would soften my opinion. It has only solidified it. Originally written on May 18, 2012 I remember smelling Burberry Body on a co-worker when this first came out. I though it smelled nice but it didn’t exactly leave me coveting a bottle. I wanted to try it out for myself but I just never cared enough to do so. Several months later I came across a sample that was thrown into a bag of loot from Ulta. First impression? Does anyone remember the scent of Nair from the 1980s and 1990s? It was a frightfully heady mix of artificial generic flowers and caustic chemicals that could fumigate a house. I had a flashback to the summer of 1989, when I tried desperately to find shaving alternatives and ended up stinking to high heaven for days, upon application of Body. I must confess this was not a happy kind of flashback. I shudder when I think back to that incident and I don’t appreciate it when a perfume dares to stir up bad memories. About a half hour later Body attempted to cover up the toxic depilatory scent with a hearty amount sweaty musk and chemical roses. Vanilla was lurking somewhere underneath but it’s not very discernible amid the nameless chemicals, sweaty musk, and room deodorizer roses. This tenacious little bugger stayed on me throughout the day, constantly mocking me for a bad decision made twenty three years ago. Luckily, others were not subjected to smelling this chemical trainwreck as it stayed close to the skin, as others had mentioned. Maybe if I had left the Nair alone I wouldn’t be so harsh on this fragrance but I didn’t and now I am.

Recently, I experienced a unique and touching situation with this perfume. "Body" was my latest acquisition in my still somewhat manageable, but not too small fragrance collection. Full of anticipation, I sprayed it on my wrist, let the scent settle for a moment, and took a sniff. Euphoria was initially absent. But it was pleasant, warm, comforting, without being truly sweet. With each breath, I merged more with the scent. Skin, bare skin, lambskin in front of a crackling, glowing fireplace, a wooden cabin... warmth, a fine organza scarf. This image fits. A glass of cognac, a book... not necessarily erotically romantic. Rather disarming, "naked" femininity that has the power to entice... Is someone watching? This is the direction the scent takes. A feel-good fragrance. For myself. Not an erotic bombshell. It doesn't shout. A quiet seducer - just for the beloved. A scent for closeness and security. What happened next touched my heart. My little daughter stood in the doorway and wanted to know what I was doing. I held out my arm for her to sniff briefly. My arm was embraced, her little nose pressed against it, sniffing and sniffing and sniffing... She didn't want to let go. "Mama, you smell soooo good!" Until her nap, she was practically glued to my arm, running back to sniff again, beaming. In her little bed, she wrapped her arms around my arm again, pulling it close to her... "You smell sooooo nice like Mama!" ...And she fell asleep with a gentle smile. Does it smell like love and security?

This is my first comment, please be patient with me - I’m still practicing and I’m a delicate perfume soul. In my shopping cart is everything I wanted to buy in terms of beauty and perfume. Then comes the note: “Just €31 more and shipping is free.

So, this will be my very first comment here, even though I've been reading along with you for ages and have often been tempted. Please be lenient with me. Fortunately (or unfortunately), there is a branch of a well-known Swiss perfume chain not far from my workplace.

Today I was happily whistling my way around, and nearly knocked over an old lady because I was a bit distracted by the advertisement for Body by Burberry. Rosie Huntington is lounging almost naked and looking lazily and voluptuously in my direction.

She was beautiful. She was well-groomed. She had dark hair and green eyes. She was tall and slim. She was confident and tough. She was successful. She loved Aperol Spritz and sunsets in Spain. She was socially engaged and had an open ear for people. She was a doer. She was intelligent and quick-witted. She was a gut person. She loved the beautiful things in life.
The company Burberry represents British understatement like no other with its unmistakable check pattern and the legendary trench coat: understated, cool, functional, and tradition-conscious.

Yesterday I left the house under a beautiful mild November sun - and wandered through the shopping center. But when the sun disappeared, autumn showed me its cold shoulder. So I sought refuge in the perfume department of Karstadt. Flame? A flame promises warmth, doesn’t it? And indeed, Flame glows on my cold wrist like a gentle, soothing little fire. Labdanum appears soft and woody - and remains transparent through the aquatic mandarin. The sweet pea adds a floral garden feeling. An unusual scent blend that fits well into the autumn-winter season. An unconventional Eternity flanker - that pleasantly dances out of line. Its warm, subtly spicy statement definitely speaks for it.

Playful, raspberry and rose, when the light synthetic notes (lemon soda/gum balls) fade, it moves towards the Fa Divine shower cream and Delina DNA! A youthful scent, fans of Club de Nuit Impériale and Choose Happiness who don't want to spend too much money will surely enjoy this. H/S okay.

If you want to flirt without having to say a single word, then by all means add Burberry Brit Parfum to your wardrobe. It's the complete opposite of the one created for us. Brit for men is dry, bitter and very uninteresting. Brit for women is sexy, flirtatious, alluring and addictive. Lime, almond and pear make it just a tad bit tropical. Peony brings a touch of class. Mahogany wood, amber, tonka bean and vanilla gives Brit a warm-sensual feel.

Why be Skipper when you can be Barbie? I feel like BRIT is the younger, less worldly by far, sister of DIOR ADDICT. She's jealous of her accomplished sibling, and never seems able to hold her own. She hasn't lived enough. Some might say the innocence is endearing, but I'd argue that it's limiting. BRIT is too small and narrowminded. Overall, BRIT plays tennis well, but she pouts when she loses.

Normally, fruity florals don't appeal to me, as a lover of spices and woods.
