On top of that, I usually associate fruity florals with young women and girls, and I am, both sadly and thankfully, no longer young. But that lime top note drew me to Burberry Brit, despite my prejudices. That refreshing lime note lingers a bit, extending into the heart where it meets up with peony and pear. The drydown is a lightly almond-flavored vanilla. There's a creamy woodiness here, too. This fragrance has very wide appeal, and I understand why. I unhesitatingly recommend it for summer, even if you don't care for the rest of the Burberry line. I ended up buying bottles of both the edt and the edp, which are slightly different.

I love that every Burberry fragrance I have tried manages to be unique yet classy at the same time. Burberry Brit certainly does not fail me in that opinion. Brit is slightly sweet, yet nothing like the sweet celebrity scents on today's market. The sweetness of the pear and the lime is rather refreshing. Brit also exudes elegance and sophistication, making it a perfect scent for special occasions or evening wear. I love that this fragrance, if sprayed on your clothes, leaves a divine warm vanilla scent which you can smell everytime you open your wardrobe. While wearing this scent you are guaranteed to feel feminine, desirable and incredibly sexy. This is one very unique and lovable fragrance.

Burberry BRIT is a pleasant if unexceptional linear floriental perfume which I'd rank as a distant cousin to Chanel ALLURE. The same sort of finely woven texture of notes appears here, although the precise notes themselves are not the same. This type of fragrance appeals to me—and Dior DUNE is another example—as a sort of comfort scent without the dessert aspect present in perfumes such as Chopard CASMIR. Sandalwoodiness, vanilla, “abstract” florality and a sort of nondescript creaminess combine to create a soothing sort of scent in BRIT. I was honestly expecting sour sandalwood and synthetic aftertaste but have been pleasantly surprised. My previous experiences with Burberry have not been all that positive, although I do own a bottle of RED, which has this same linear tightly woven texture but, again, with different notes. I don't find BRIT or RED to be very subtle or complex, but they are nice enough to wear.

Ok i heard good reviews on this fragrance so i Decided to buy it The Scent i didn't know what to make of it at first and i thought maybe it will grow on me so i used it for a while. but i got tried of it and i'm swaping it.

This scent is unique; you won’t confuse it with anything. It’s such a beautiful and unexpected balance of sweet and fresh! Like a lime macaron. I had a small bottle of this when I was a student and I remember enjoying it in summer very much. Years after, when I saw the pyramid, I couldn’t believe my eyes: so much sweetness!

This fragrance was on my list for Santa, and he decided to bring it to me, even though it was a fragrance I hadn't tried. I've been testing it since Christmas day when it was gifted but I liked it from the beginning.

Burberry Brit is a rather mild vanilla and almond scent to my nose. I prefer it for fall or cold and rainy summer days. I find it pleasant and comforting, but not very captivating. It starts off with a blast of lime, which on me disappears rather quickly. After that I just smell the vanilla and almond.

I like this on my skin a lot better than on the testing strip. On my skin I smell more lime and pear, almost a musk. On the tester I smell way too much vanilla and peony! Similar to Joop! All About Eve.

Disclaimer: This is not my favorite fragrance genre...in fact "Aquatic" is usually the last thing I hear before I start running in the opposite direction. Fortunately, I did an impulse spritz today without reading up on this flanker first and I was pleasantly refreshed. It bore an initial hint of the original Eternity, but stopped short of the Vavoom over the top sillage and wantonness of the original- instead, veering to the clean minty airy with aquatic note hanging delicately underneath as a wispy after thought...not bad at all. There is not too much occurring behind the scenes with this one. I don't really detect any base white musk, perhaps just a touch of amber but it is gentle and fleeting at best. I may try it again in the future, I have learned the hard way with Calvin Klein fragrances to try at least 3 times before considering a FB purchase- or it will sit there on my shelf getting lonely for the next 5 years until I use it as air freshener. But if you are looking for a bright blue-ish green clean crisp French Riviera-ish calone experience- this may make you day in the same bold beautiful bottle design of the Eternities of the past. No one will say you didn't smell clean and fresh wearing this breezy scent.

The scent has absolutely nothing to do with the original, but I suppose that's not the point. Still, I find it super beautiful! It smells to me like freshly washed, but with a special soap. I don't perceive the scent as a perfume, more like a special body lotion. Yes, soapy and like freshly moisturized. If it were cheaper, I would have bought it. It would be a great care scent, but not one to stand out or go out in the evening.

So here’s another comment. As soon as I spray the perfume, I feel like I'm on vacation. I stand by the sea where a small flower meadow can be found behind the dunes. The pleasant freshness is complemented by the light floral notes that keep emerging. I instantly feel more relaxed and in a vacation mood;-) It's fresh but not citrus-fresh, which I really love because you usually find that in most fresh perfumes. I'm truly impressed by the wonderful scent; it lasts really well on me, sprayed in the morning and still detectable in the afternoon, even on my scarf the next day. It’s really a beautiful, light, and fresh summer perfume;-) I think I'll order another bottle to stock up. The bottle is also very beautiful; in the light, the rainbow colors are lovely to see, just a shame that you’re supposed to store perfume in a dark and cool place;-) Now we just need the summer temperatures to arrive;-)

In the first few seconds, this Eternity Summer smells (surprisingly pleasant) aquatic. However, this note quickly takes a back seat and unobtrusively supports the flowers that then emerge with a fresh touch. I can't pick out a specific bloom, but they are well coordinated and smell beautifully fresh, not at all cloying or heavy. The floral scent remains constant, but over time it transforms towards fresh laundry with a slight creamy nuance. For me, it's a delicious summery clean scent!

Softly it smells sweet, reminiscent of a somewhat contemplative summer. At first, the scent was fresher and had an aquatic aroma of a Baltic Sea vacation, but it quickly becomes thickly sweet, smelling a bit like melon and unknown round floral-fruity notes. After a short time, a creamy character emerges, somehow reminding me of calendula hand cream.

Today the bottle of Eternity Summer 2013 arrived. Shortly after spraying, there was initially a slightly aquatic impression, then a floral mix. A little later: "Why do I keep smelling 'Innocence' (Chloe)?" No, not really, Innocence is stronger, sharper, and more distinctive, IT is more pleasing, but there is definitely a certain similarity!

I only wore this for 2 days, so take my review with a grain of salt. This is a boring sweet-ish amberwoods fragrance. As with most amberwoods fragrances, up close this doesn't smell great, if you can smell it, but as you get wafts of it in the air throughout the day it smells better. In the air, this is a balance between sweet, woody, and spicy, in that order. I can detect the clary sage accord, but I don't know if I can pick out the black pepper distinctly from the "red thyme." I don't detect a distinct geranium accord, but there's a bit of freshness, so that might be the geranium. The tonka note isn't distinctly tonka. I think it's just general purpose sweetness. Strictly speaking this isn't a linear fragrance because the top and middle notes fade as the wear goes on, but you can smell the base notes from the beginning, so you don't get anything new as the wear goes one. Overall, this sort of smells like if a sweet fall candle (without cinnamon) was made into a men's fragrance. At least the cap is heavy and the sprayer is pressurized.

It's brave to give a perfume the name of the city. Scuttlebut tells me Yves Saint Laurent was sent to Coventry (not London) by his contemporaries when he used 'Paris'. I don't know if there is any basis to that gossip. Should there be great gravitas attached to the consideration of 'London' for the name of a fragrance? It's forever now, so I suppose there should be. Does it fit? Does every woman who wears 'Beautiful' have to be beautiful, technically? Is every woman who wears 'London' expected to know that the fearsome Queen of the Iceni, Boudicea, retook Plowonida, or modern day London to you, from the Roman conquerors? That London sits on a bed of red ash from the fires that destroyed it? It was a tale that Queen Victoria capitalised on when she became Queen at the age of eighteen, part of her marketing campaign, one might say. Elizabeth the 2nd became Queen as a young woman of twenty five just as her namesake, Elizabeth Tudor, did in the 1500s. I'm really warming to the idea of a heady white floral becoming a symbol for London; the association is working for me now. Strong women, loyal and true, warlike at times, but always women. I will wear 'London' with pride. As a Jasmine lover it's dead easy. My Dad, dead now, might sing 'Any, any, any old iron' with the best of them but his favourite, surely, was "I get a funny feeling inside of me, when I'm walking up and down. Maybe it's because I'm a Londoner, that I love London town'

Minus things= Bottle a bit tacky. Not ergonomic. Sillage isnt wow. + longevity is middle or under middle. You cant see how much liquid I got because cloth of Burberry style doesnt let u see. Sometimes too much tangerine coming to my nose. Plus things= my best loved perfumor 's Job he is Dominique Ropion. Wait till strong tangerine flows, the heart is beautiful, elegant, soft, romantic honeysuckle, light rose(little bit), jasmine combination. Not bad quality I think thats good quality + very realistic honeysuckles. Thats one of the best honeysuckle perfumes in market(affordable one). For me right now BEST BURBERRY WOMEN perfume.(the others are bad longevity or weird bad smells). If u like WHİTE FLORALS u can blind buy this, cause very safe.

Very rarely do I test a fragrance and feel the sudden urge to buy it right then and there without letting it develop fully on my skin. However, London was almost an exception. London is such a delicate and pretty floral scent. Not only is the fragrance beautiful when you first apply, but it continues its heavenly scent right until the very end. There is nothing to dislike about this fragrance. It has a classic-like smell, possibly because of the rose and jasmine notes, however this is in no way an 'old lady' perfume. The scent is soft, feminine, youthful and elegant. I wouldn't describe London as being outrageously sexual or provocative, because it definitely is none of those. Burberry scents are what I refer to as 'comfort scents', fragrances that you can feel comfortable wearing during the daytime, around the house, on a picnic or simply relaxing. I love that laid-back approach they have when creating their scents. Although I have never been to London, I believe this fragrance has captured the beauty and history that makes London so special. This fragrance would also be suited to England's cold climate, with its ability to create warmth and to uplift your spirits on a cold Winter's day. Although I resisted the urge to purchase this fragrance the other day, it will definitely stayed fixed on my wishlist until I buy it, which will probably be very soon.

Warning: Be light on the trigger with this! I was a bit careless and sprayed as much as I usually do. This is a GRAND bouquet of white flowers where no one stands out compared to the others. For me it is enough to spray on the finger and dab a little behind the ears. In moderation it is absolutely lovely and a compliment getter.

A real beautiful smell here. A delicate and balanced floral done in a very good way which really brings out the jasmine, honeysuckle and orange citrus aspects. This is a very clean, polished floral scent which is like old fashioned hand made floral soap, but totally wearable for the current generation. I have the men's version and I wear that one but I could see this as a very worthy, equally classy, totally elegant companion to that one. Burberry London for Women opens with honeysuckle and tangerine, it is so fresh and clean and soft smelling, very warm and comforting. The mid is a host of white florals: jasmine, tiare and peony, whilst the base is a typical sandalwood, white musk & patchouli combination. I think this would make a fantastic choice for women. Although I have worn it there is something so beautiful and fresh and feminine about it that I realise it would smell fantastic on an attractive young woman. It gives out a young, carefree, polished vibe that is very alluring on the right person. At times I think it might be too much in hot weather, so I think the best time for this one is Autumn and Spring (especially Spring and early Summer). There is something about it (perhaps the gorgeous white florals?) that lends itself to that time of year. Overall, a perfect choice for young, trendy women, and women of all ages in general. Jasmine is one of my absolute favourite notes to smell on anyone, and here the combination with the soft, musky, soapy florals which surround it give it a plush, polished and warm inviting vibe. Highly recommended, especially for spring and summer, and for the price you can't beat it.

Burberry's London is such a nice, relaxing scent. I love the jasmine notes it initially gives off, and the bottle fits the smell perfectly - a classic. The longevity of the scent is great - usually a little on your pressure points is enough. It's a very traditional scent, I suppose, but I absolutely love the design and scent of London.

I can see the vision here: an elegant, refined, mature floral. That's exactly what you get. It's not necessarily a bad fragrance but it's definitely not for me. The jasmine and tiaré are done in a way that brings out the aspects of white florals that I'm not a fan of and while I am a fan of honeysuckle in very specific cases here it just makes everything kinda screechy.

Burberry is a classic brand producing classic scents. At the moment I have four of them. London is not the best of them, but I do find it delicate and quite discreet. It has a sweetness to it that makes it comfortable to wear and a sillage that makes it appropriate to wear. Unfortunately, I do not need a scent like this so it spends most of the time on the shelf in my closet.

Light-footed, she walked up the few steps to the front door, unlocked it, and quickly pulled the heavy wooden door shut behind her. She stood in the dark, cool hallway and felt as if she had shut out the noise, dust, and traffic of the city. She took a deep breath, took a shower, and slipped into a breezy, white linen dress.

Burberry, tjajajaja... A colleague always smelled so beautiful and elegant. When I asked her what her perfume was, she first said, wait I'll check at home, and then, it's Burberry. What I didn't know back then was that there are so many Burberrys and finding the right one, phew... So I set out on a search and decided on this one, thinking it was the right one. Well, um no!!!

Unusual - that was also my feeling after the first spray and sniff of this little Shock offshoot. Although I must admit that I have had little experience with cocoa and chocolatey gourmands in general so far. However, I cannot really understand the often made classification as a summer fragrance. The overpowering cocoa odor, which at this point already bursts through the top note with brute force and shows no signs of making room for shy middle notes of lemon, is something I wouldn't want to deal with at 30 degrees and midday sun. Maybe it's just a matter of a specific scent perception or my skin chemistry. Because the original Shock for him, rated in the community as chocolate-dominant and better suited for cooler days, I prefer to wear as significantly fresher on warm days. Overall, I find the elements listed in the fragrance pyramid alongside the cocoa to be rather weak (citrus) to almost nonexistent (geranium). Good for the cocoa, because it stubbornly holds on - in varying degrees - from start to finish. And the Mojito, well. If anything, Calvin probably had it mixed very business-oriented. Lots of soda, little lime juice. Whatever. It cannot be denied that the whole composition still smells delicious and unusually intriguing for a perfume. I would estimate the longevity and sillage of the SE as above average. The major drawback, however, that this fragrance has in my opinion, has already been mentioned further down by Showdown: Whether street, leisure, club, sport, work, or festivity, I cannot think of any occasion where I would prefer Sfh SE over any of my other fragrances and want it as a companion around me. Maybe for a cool, rainy Sunday afternoon spent lounging on the couch in front of the TV. But then thirty euros for a chocolate-Mojito cloud above the sofa would still be too much of a good thing for me.

One thing is for sure: "CK One Shock for him" is an extraordinary fragrance. Chocolate as an ingredient for a perfume for the warmer days... I couldn't really imagine that. The cocoa note, which is supposed to form the base of the fragrance, unfolds immediately after spraying, strong yet unobtrusive. It is not too bitter and evokes associations with milk chocolate. In the top note, you can already detect hints of citrus fruits. At first, the combination takes some getting used to, but I couldn't take my nose off my wrist. You have to immerse yourself in the opening to truly enjoy it. The cocoa note gradually recedes, allowing the citrus fruits to unfold. In the background, I discover mint and aquatic notes. After about an hour, lime stands out from the citrus potpourri. The fragrance, which in the top note was a wild mix of subtly bitter, citrusy, and slightly sweet, is now primarily sour and fresh. "CK One Shock for him Street Edition" is a pleasant feel-good fragrance for warm days with an extraordinary opening that I have somewhat fallen in love with. Sure, the base doesn't reinvent the wheel, but the tried-and-true combination of fresh citrus scents, a hint of mint, and aquatic notes makes this perfume a great summer scent with good longevity. And it comes in a stylish bottle that would surely look good in any collection.

Ck One Shock has been a real staple for me this winter, and I think it is one of the best chocolate scents on the market. It is also very well received by the public and finds its way into many noses thanks to good projection. Now I read a lot about the new Street Edition, the flanker of the flanker. I was very much looking forward to a more summery version of the pleasant chocolate shocker, but I was unsure if there would be too few differences from the original. However, after some research and conversations here at Parfumo + the Douglas price, I went for the 50 ml version. Luckily just the 50 ml version, because unfortunately I don’t like the SE as much as the regular Shock. It’s good, and you try to arrange yourself with perfumes in your collection as best as possible; some you learn to love over time. But at the moment I am still skeptical, which doesn’t mean the scent is bad. It is actually quite special. To use the name Shock not just for marketing purposes, the CK people kept the chocolate base, which runs through the entire scent. But to create a street version for all skaters and the like on warm days, they injected a good amount of citrus into the dark chocolate. Whether that’s a mojito, I believe and find less so. I drink it rarely, but that’s not how I remember it. But through and through chocolate and light spices have of course also been significantly altered. This rather sweet-sticky mixture of chocolate and lime I have not smelled combined like this before; it smells unusual, but most of the time unfortunately quite simple and almost cheap. The uniqueness lies in the intertwined structure of the SE. First citrus, then chocolate, that’s common. But throwing both into a pot and stirring is new and, for me, takes some getting used to. Also, the eagerly awaited spring/summer will probably have a hard time with the acclimatization. But I’ll let myself be surprised. CK One Shock SE comes in a very stylish graffiti bottle that can be admired! The sillage is slightly below the original thanks to summery citrus shots, but for a supposed scent for warmer days, it is still quite heavy. Longevity is just okay at 6 hours. Overall, it is absolutely not a must-have, even for fans of the original. For those who find the original too heavy and want to try the unusual mixture, please test it before buying blind!

So, I'm actually not good at writing comments because I can't really pinpoint the individual ingredients I sniff out, but I can describe it a bit :) I received a small bottle (50ml) from England today and of course tested it right away. The base note of the original "CK One Shock for him" is still detectable. But unlike the original, the Street Edition doesn't have that penetrating sweetness. It's incredibly fruity and reminds me of "Connected Kenneth Cole Reaction" or "Berlin" by Playboy, which have many similarities for me. On top of that, there's a slight spiciness that most resembles "Polo Black". All in all, it's a totally crazy combination that is noticeably fresher and zestier than the original Shock and is incredibly intense. I haven't conducted a proper long-term test regarding sillage and longevity yet, but I spritzed some on my neck and sprayed a little cloud into the air to walk through, then went for a walk at our beach where it smelled extremely of stagnant algae... the Street Edition still managed to shine through. I personally find the bottle extremely cool, but it certainly won't be to everyone's taste ;) I think it's really great, although it's a bit too fruity for me for winter. It will probably be more of a spring/summer scent for me. The price was also great; I paid 20 pounds + shipping for the 50ml bottle. I'll write to Coty in the coming days to see if this will be a limited edition for a short time or if it will be kept in the program longer. Otherwise, I'll need to buy a bit more :)

Since I completely overhauled my collection, many candidates have fortunately found a new home, and I am now constantly on the lookout for new treasures that are meant to stay. Ones that you won't get tired of. Boldly, I decided to shop for something fruity. You know the moment when you switch to a different fragrance direction - let's start with the development of Jimmy Choo Blossom Special Edition 2018. The first spray is already a bit peppery/floral and, in my opinion, a little synthetic. But that fades quickly. I immediately smell peach and sweet pineapple, and very soon frangipani joins in. I can't really assess the longevity yet, as it just arrived yesterday. The bottle is very beautiful, and the peachy color evokes a warm summer day with sunshine, sitting in a chic floral dress at a beach bar, sipping a fruit cocktail. I also currently don't know what to compare the perfume to. It is definitely a lovely scent for hot days.

Since I like the Jimmy Choo fragrances, I ordered Blossom blindly. When it arrived, I was already taken by the beautiful bottle with the pink liquid. But the first spray turned out to be very light and somewhat nondescript. Disappointed, I set it aside. However, after just a few minutes, a pleasantly sweet fruity scent spread, reminiscent of berries. Soft and accented by creamy sandalwood. It becomes exotic through frangipani. Blossom remains transparent despite its sweetness and can be worn well even in this heat, as it stays in the air. A fragrance that evolves from "well, okay" to "oh la la." It adds a touch of exotic to everyday life and makes you think of Caribbean beaches.

------Blind Buy-------- I remember requesting a strawberry perfume, and was recommended this. Since it was a really popular one, I decided to buy it. Heeh.. turns out I really hated this. It literally has a certain DNA that we find in so many other fragrances, like; Violet Vibe , Strawberry Letter , Cheirosa '68 Cloud Eau de Parfum ....are we not tired... But, I still decided to give it another chance by wearing it again (for one day) (before selling it for good). I still don't smell the strawberry milkshake, like, actually, there's none and I'm dying to know how you can smell it. In the initial sprays, it's so sweet, creamy, and I smell a mix of strawberry AND blackberry, the sweetness is very good at first. But when it fades, it loses that sweet and fruity aspect and turns into a plastic/sharp jasmine. I must say, the longevity is really good tho, stays for the entire day. I took the "intense" version, and I'd like to say, if the "elixir" version still doesn't work for you, the intense version may be what you're looking for in Elixir ;)

Ive changed my mind on this fragrance a couple of times. I ended up buying it and thought it was pleasant enough to use as a grab and go perfume for work, however I find the scent really bland. I can barely smell it and, having worn it a few times now, it has a weird musky note in the background that I just don’t like. This isn’t powdery, which I wouldn’t have minded, it’s a dusty musky skin scent. I really have to dig my face into my wrist to smell anything, and that’s with spraying it a whole tonne! If I had gotten an 80’s strawberry shortcake smell I would have kept it for the nostalgic value, but I don’t get that either sadly, I also don’t get much berry. Maybe it’s my sense of smell. If anything I find this scent actually just irritates me now, to the point I will sell it cheap, give it way just to get rid of it. If my opinion changes or something changes with what I smell from this I’ll change my review, but for now I’ll stick to Meraki by Botanicae!

Tested: skin and fabric over 8 hrs. TLDR: Smooth, simple, and well-blended Strawberry Shortcake doll scent. Extremely short life span. - First impression after a spray on each wrist: warmth! Not in a spiced way, but in depth. The berries in the opening are darker compared to the original Her, in a way that reminds me of the YSL Mon Paris line. Like a smooth and *sweet* wine, no dry bitterness here. After about 10 minutes (so quick…), it turns into a strawberry musk. I often hear this scent being compared to a “strawberry milk/shake”, but I don’t pick up anything lactonic or particularly milky. Actually, I directly compared Elixir to a strawberries & cream flavoured milk, and some strawberries and cream candy. While this scent is smoother than the tangy fruitiness of candy, it’s not nearly creamy enough to be reminiscent of anything dairy-based. It’s creamy in terms of *texture*. Instead, Elixir reminds me very much of how they used to scent Strawberry Shortcake dolls. The soft plastic, hinted with artificial strawberry that gets dense in the hair, slightly faded over time. This must be why it mixes so well into skin; the original Her, in her bright and fruity glory, sits right on top. Elixir makes herself at home. It makes me think of an artificial, idyllic childhood. I want to wrap myself in soft blankets, watch the 80’s Care Bears Movie, and eat vanilla pudding. It’s sweet and innocent without the baby powder note often used to achieve the feeling. As I said, this fades way too quickly. By 8 hours, Elixir is a (barely) sandalwood ghost of its former self. I’m not sure it stuck to my clothing at all tbh. Additionally, I didn’t find it to project very well, as I had to bring my wrists to my nose to smell anything almost immediately after application. I love this flanker. It’s quietly sweet, comforting, and very nostalgic. A more demure version of the original. If only it lasted long enough to enjoy. Would be excellent to layer any strawberry or milk-focused scents with!

The girl that wears Burberry Her Exilixr may not be the main character…But she is definitely the girl that the main character has been obsessed with since the first grade. Burberry Her Elixir is strawberry shampoo, matching silky pink pajama sets, and silky smooth hair down to the waist, a 12 step skincare routine, a sweet smile and wave to a stranger. Burberry Her Elixir is bubblegum pop music, singing into a hairbrush, and sleepovers with feather-down pillow fights. She may not be unique, but she knows that there is nothing wrong with being like “other girls.” And for that reason among many, she is beautiful.

I'm starting to think my skin chemistry doesn't vibe well with the whole Burberry Her line. I had previously tried Burberry Her EdP which I had disliked because of the synthetic, almost plastic scent that emanated from my skin and this one isn't much better. There's a tart, almost sour tinge to the strawberry and blackberries which I associated with plastic doll-like figurines that smelled of strawberries and fruits back in the day. It's synthetic, screechy and I'm just overall so turned off by it. As time goes by, the plastic accord fades a little bit and I finally gain acces to this semi-sweet strawberry milkshake people have been raving about. I'm not sure about the lactonic / creamy aspect of it since the plastic accord is still present and distracts me from the rest, but I can imagine it smells like strawberry milkshake on other peopl'e skin. Just wished it did the same on mine. As you can see, I'm one of the minorities who dislikes this perfume, so the fault goes probably to my skin chemistry and the old memories I have of strawberry scented dolls I played with when I was young. Might be a nice feminine-leaning, gourmand perfume for most people, but to me, it's a perfume I'll be forgetting.

A sweet, girly, and bright berry scent with a warm vanilla underpinning that fades into a lovely and light amber jasmine. The juicy, sour blackberry sticks around for a long time and keeps the scent from feeling heavy or overly sweet! Definitely synthetic, but not in a bad way. I was looking for a nice, pretty every day perfume and Burberry Her Elixir was love-at-first-smell.

:( so disappointed by this. smells like midnight fantasy to me which is also a big let down. Smells like Pantene shampoo. Mildly fruity, settles into a vaguely fruity musky vanilla. Thoroughly unexciting, boring and weak. Cant even believe this has any hype around it wow.

Waited to review until I smelled Her, Intense, and Elixir... and I can say without a doubt Elixir is my fave so far. -OG: too much 'baccarat bandaid' for me, and the synthetic berries gave me a migraine. -Intense: richer with benzoin, the berries smell more real (blackberry especially), but still has a medicinal/cough syrup smell that I can't get on with.

For some reason, the original Burberry Her perfume does not smell good to me. Thankfully I bought the travel size but when I went back to Sephora with my boyfriend I smelled the Elixir and omg this is so much better. I bought the big size and it smells so good on me and is so much better than the og. Highly recommend this perfume if you love overly sweet perfumes.

Creamy. Jammy. Decadent. Like McDonalds' strawberry topping that they put on ice cream. Teeth-rottingly sweet, juicy, thick, and if you're lucky – even has some full strawberries in it. I'm not even into strawberries, but this is genuinely kind of impressive. The sillage is moderate past the initial cloud.

The idea behind this fragrance is quite ambitious: summery and wintry accords, cleverly combined in one scent. A perfect companion for the transitional period. Well, on paper, everything seems to support this. But how does it perform in practice? Right after spraying, the fresh and citrusy accords rise to the nose. In the background, however, the incense is noticeable from the very beginning, which essentially forms the signature of this fragrance. Unfortunately, the summer vibes dissipate relatively quickly, and the scent remains a sweet-spicy winter fragrance with a whole lot of incense until the end. Longevity and sillage are unfortunately quite poor, especially considering that there is a lot of amber, incense, and vanilla included, which should normally last much longer. But no: after a maximum of 5 hours, it was over for me. Conclusion: It could have been so nice. A fragrance that combines the best of two worlds and is wearable in any situation. However, what has come out is a somewhat boring, smoky-ambered uniformity that wants to please everyone but ultimately doesn't quite succeed. I only had a small sample of this perfume, and that’s how it will stay. Unfortunately, no recommendation!

This is my very first review. In the first section, I will try to introduce the perfume to you without much fuss. The second section is for the detail-loving hardcore perfume fans. Calvin Klein attempts to refine the eternal classic Eternity with a layer of amber - unfortunately, what has come out is more like: Eternity based on synthetic resin. The opening whispers warm and spicy, but before it gets really interesting, the scent collapses in on itself. The amber does not feel like it was pulled from the depths of the earth, but rather like it was ordered from a chemistry lab. The sweetness? Sticky and artificial - as if one had sucked on a plastic candy. Anyone who knows real amber will inevitably think: what a shame. Sillage? More of a whisper. Longevity? Not worth mentioning. For the price? To be honest: a complete disappointment. Amber Essence sounds noble - but is rather a smoothed-out shadow of itself. For me: a fragrance that promises much and delivers little. ____________________________________________ The Scent Under the Microscope Opening - The Quiet Beginning The opening feels like a cautious approach: warm, slightly spicy, a fleeting hint of promised depth. But instead of a sensual fire, a lukewarm steam bubble emerges. There is a lack of substance - the opening fizzles out before an image can form. A cheap sweetness pushes forward and devours the last bit of tension. Heart - The Synthetic Middle Here, a balsamic-woody heart could have emerged, carried by velvety amber and noble spices. Instead: a flat sound carpet of sugar and synthetic resin. Cardamom? Cinnamon? Maybe in homeopathic dosage. The heart remains soulless, like a painting without color - the structure is there, but it lacks life. Drydown - The Sad Exit Where other fragrances gather in the base and leave a lasting trace, Amber Essence simply lets go. A dull, creamy sweetness remains, which creates neither depth nor intimacy. Almost a skin caresser - but one that leaves no impression. Just a faint, synthetic veil that slowly fades away. Sillage & Longevity - Silent Presence The sillage is reserved to the point of being non-existent - a subtle aura that almost seems shy. The longevity ranges somewhere between "short visit" and "vanished without a trace." After at most four hours, only a pale memory remains. Disappointing for an Eau de Parfum with such aspirations. Wearability - Yes, but why? Sure, you can wear it. To the office, on the train, while shopping. It doesn’t hurt anyone - but that is exactly the problem. It remains obedient, interchangeable, smooth. For a signature scent, it lacks character. For special occasions, it lacks soul. For amber fans, it lacks personality. Conclusion - Amber Without Weight Eternity Amber Essence feels like a glass sculpture: nice to look at, but cold, empty, and fragile. The basic idea could have offered a lot - but the execution falls far short of the possibilities. Those who want real amber should reach for niche fragrances or at least spicier designers. Here, there is only a synthetic echo of what is essentially a deep accord.

Brit for Men is the third Burberry fragrance I’ve brought into my life—following Sport for Men Eau de Toilette and Brit Rhythm for Him Eau de Toilette , which I’ll revisit soon. My affection for those two, paired with the quiet insistence of countless glowing reviews, led me to blind-buy both Brit and London. Sometimes you don’t need a sample—you just need a feeling. This morning, faced with a grey, rainy weekday—humid and still, like the air didn’t quite know where to go—I reached for Brit. There’s something deeply British about it, not just by name, but in spirit. It smells introverted, homey, and comforting in slightly odd, endearing ways. A scent for someone who carries a private world inside them. I sprayed it on my chest and immediately felt a blend of floral-woody-oriental softness—fresh, powdery, unmistakably masculine. It felt right. Cold weather, late autumn, a day when everything outside is damp and pale and waiting. Brit doesn’t cheer you up. It sits beside you, understands the quiet. The opening is sharp—bergamot like Earl Grey, green cardamom crushed just enough to release its warm nuttiness. On my wrists, the first impression is a bright, balsamic freshness. Ginger and mandarin cut through the blend like thin light through heavy drapes—crisp, slightly stinging, never sweet in an obvious way. This isn’t sugar or syrup—it’s spice and skin and a memory of warmth. As I stepped outside, the cold air met the fragrance, and something changed. The scent turned softer, deeper. A warmer tone emerged—velvety, smooth, confident. Like something well-worn but beautifully kept. I sensed rose, not the showy kind, but something wilder, more grounded. Surrounded by fragrant cedar and a restrained touch of nutmeg, it moved gracefully. The longer I wore it, the more I noticed how well it held together. Balanced. Designed with care. This isn’t the powder of iris in Dior Homme—the lipstick-powder elegance I love for entirely different reasons. Here, it’s something more understated. The rose and iris feel like silk, pressed but not stiff. The powder is gentle, warm, brushed with a masculine hand. Eventually, it settles into something smoky, spiced, and woody. Tonka bean and musk give it softness; cedar and vanilla offer structure. It’s not gourmand, not edible—just quietly sweet, like the memory of a baked good, not the thing itself. The scent becomes a cocoon. A soft mantle, a kind of olfactory introspection. To me, Brit is a scent of cold mornings, fogged windows, and thoughtful pauses. The rose here doesn’t wear a desert robe—it wears a wool coat and walks under wet branches. Still, there’s a freshness that makes me curious to try it in spring. I wouldn’t wear it in summer; it would bloom too much, feel too heavy. But for autumn and winter, it’s a companion. Quiet, steady, and present. Versatility is one of its strengths. I’d wear it to the office, on a solitary walk, or during a quiet dinner with someone who sees through noise. It’s a scent that adapts without losing its shape. Whether for day or evening, work or wandering thoughts, it knows how to stay close. On my skin, the fresh edge lasts a couple of hours before the woods and powder take over. Longevity is solid—around eight hours. It lingers in the way a conversation might, long after the words are gone. The bottle, of course, is classic Burberry—checkered, understated, confident. I’d give it an 8 out of 10. Not because it lacks anything, but because it knows what it is, and stays true. This morning, it made the rain feel less cold—and the stillness, a little more bearable. — Elysium

Upon applying this to my wrists, I heard a tinny commanding voice in my ears: "Greetings earthling. I am the baby oil vibe. I am your new master. Meet my minions, class and fresh. They are accompanying me to your skin where we will sample your body for nine hours and then return to our planet. You must tell your fellow creatures of your experiences, because we like your bodies, and want to return." (*) Being familiar with words, I agreed. The baby oil certainly dominates, but the scent feels richer, the way Skarb does, and there's a fresh zing to it as well. It's a clean, thick, meaty, and slightly oriental scent. However, it comes off as a "Yo, I am a sexy perfume trying to be sexy," as if it were trying too hard. The initial silage is about two feet. By five hours, it's down to about a foot, and it smells more like oil and vanilla. By six hours it's down to half a foot, and by nine hours, only a musky sweet base remains. This scent is not as simple as Curve Crush, and it's more consistent than Zino, but that doesn't mean that the experience was one I'd like to repeat (sorry aliens!). Burberry Brit seems excessive somehow. It's not a horrible scent, but the bad boy scents are my least favorite of all the categories of fragrance. I'd rather it had it gone the direction of a heavy citrus scent, like Silver, but the baby oil rules all. I do appreciate the advanced technology of the sample (thanks DigInDirt!); instead of a vial, or a pipette, it's merely an absorbent pad in a pouch. So whether it's your thing or not, you get one or two uses and there's little waste. Do they still put these things in magazines? I'm not a big magazine reader, which means I can never run for vice president I suppose, but I'm not the target audience for fashion magazines. * No, I didn't actually hear this voice. This review is a dramatization of the actual experience, and Burberry Brit will not induce schizophrenia. You are perfectly safe wearing it, earthling.

Burberry hits it out of the park with this delicious amber woody classic. Launched in 2004 this smooth offering stays with you for a long while giving you gentle whiffs here and there. Kind of a spicy opening followed by some more spice with woods and finally the base which is the best part. A truly awesome drydown. The tonka bean and patchouli really shine here and it's so wonderful you don't want it to end. A versatile scent that can be worn wherever, whenever.

It was slightly difficult for me to collect my thoughts and form an opinion regarding Brit for Men, because the scent kind of left me slightly disappointed. Burberry Brit for Men, seems to me, to be lacking in substance and character. I can barely smell it, apart from spontaneous wafts of powdery ginger and damp woods. Perhaps it is supposed to be subtle, and while I don't like anything too strong on a man, this is going way beyond subtlety. Sporty, casual maybe, but nothing too outstanding. Pleasant enough but underwhelming in the sense that it doesn't evoke any kind of feelings in me. Honestly, this fragrance could suit a man that loathes fragrance. The powderiness is not bothersome for me, as I don't find it feminine like some reviewers perceive Brit for Men to be. It's masculine but too faint. There's not enough power to make me love it. I didn't pick up on a rose note at all, but I advise men to not be turned off by rose in a masculine composition. Rose, when done well, can smell amazing on a man, take Le Labo's Rose 31, for example. Edit: I have since re-tested this fragrance, and it's growing on me. I was able to smell the rose note the second time around. I do believe I'll be purchasing it for one of my male friends.

A 21st century hommage to a Victorian rose. Charmingly sloppy dandy scent. Not easy to love due to the strong powdery character. First notes of mandarin and ginger not so impressive, but powdery rose and musky-woody-sweet base are gorgeous. Soft and flowery gentleman. It possess some twisted British humor for cold and foggy days. Really appreciate Maisondieu's creative skills. Flankers of this Brit are forgettable. Rating: 6.5/10

Brit for Men is well put together with good transitions and no false moves, but it has a screechiness due to a large amount of synthetic fruit and woody amber molecules, which is a shame; it's an otherwise comfy and likeable night time scent, darkly sweet - offset by a cool bitter floral.

This is a great fragrance for the cooler months. It is very warm and powdery with a spicy quality that hangs around until the scent wears off. The longevity and projection on this one are also quite good. Overall, it is a pleasant and versatile fragrance that most people should enjoy whether that be in the office, on a date, or somewhere in between.

This one is nothing i wear when i go outside ... This is something that i grab when i had a bad day or feel sad. Its something about this Scent that makes me happy and life me up For the Price ... its a steal Its a realy lovely smell of Rose with Sweet Orange i realy would enjoy it on a woman.

After the initial few seconds of citrus opening, Burberry Brit for Men turns out to be peppery and extremely woody on me. Spices mixes very well with the woody notes. The ginger here is quite dry. This first hour projects well and is the most masculine phase to my nose.

I consider Brit for Him, Touch and London to be the triumvirate of masculine fragrance offerings from Burberry in what otherwise seems to be a rather bland and unoriginal range, especially after 2010. It starts with a distinct accord of citric and cardamom cold and stingy freshness.

Not bad. I'll wear it. I'm not sure how much I love the mojito note, though. The sweet citrus notes are a bit 'aggressive'. It feels less like I've spritzed myself with a light citrus essence and more like I'm sticky after making a sweet mojito. Basically, I like how it smells generally but it feels a lot heavier or stuffier than it does light and airy. The heaviness has its pros though, as a result it has decent staying power. The silage may not be incredible but if I put on lotion and spray 5 or so sprays around me, I will smell it coming off my body for a few hours.

Yes, yes, one would have been surprised if certain brands had not released their summer editions this year, just like every year. This is the case with Issey Miyake, with DKNY, and it is no different with Calvin Klein. This may sound negative, but many of these fragrances are usually quite nicely done. They may not be showstoppers, no special scents that immediately blow you away, and also not fragrances that have something absolutely new to offer (so that one could sometimes say "If you know one, you know them all!" and suddenly everything sounds a bit negative :D), BUT: They usually smell nice, are often available for relatively little money, and you can get through the summer quite well with them! And that is the main thing! The only criticism of most fragrances: You have to live with the fact that a noticeable synthetic scent is often detectable in these perfumes. But if that doesn't bother you, you can confidently go for such fragrances. All others will probably run away, just like I do at the sight of hot girls in the women's department when I want to spray on women's fragrances and then get extremely nervous… *sigh* :DD The scent: The beginning… yes, the beginning. The first few seconds are quite strange to me; it smells slightly stuffy with limes and somehow muggy notes. But it could also be that it smells this way on my skin, yet that’s not a big deal since it only takes about a minute for the actual scent to finally come through. The top note now consists for me of fresh limes and a bit of peppermint, with the peppermint possibly coming from the mojito. There are also light aquatic and synthetic scents. A little later, light, sweet scents emerge, along with fruity notes that remind me of pineapple. Coconut is also detectable, giving the fragrance a rather summery impression, especially since the scent is also soft and creamy, thus smelling like sunscreen. Basically, the scent remains as described in the base and mainly smells of limes and sweet-fruity sunscreen notes, only now cedarwood is added. The synthetic impression, as with all CK scents, remains, but I don’t find it bothersome here at all. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is moderate to weak. You will certainly be noticed nearby, but probably not for a very long time… anyway, the scent is light and casual, so you can generously spray several times! The longevity is also moderate. Well, still better than some other summer fragrances that barely last two hours. This one can at least be perceived for four to five hours. The bottle: The flat and slightly bottle-like flacon hasn’t changed in ages, except that it keeps getting a new coat of paint. This one is blue like the sea and actually reminds of the wonderful water at beaches. It feels good in the hand and is therefore quite okay! However, the tester I had had a somewhat wobbly spray head and didn’t produce a good mist, but this could also be because 10,000 people are spraying the scent like crazy and some of them handle the flacon carelessly… argh! So, I liked the scent here. I don’t necessarily need to have it, but I could definitely go for it at a good price. It fits perfectly with its nice and fresh scent… hmm… although this expression sounds quite brutal, hmm… let’s just say… like the cap to the flacon! But wait… this flacon doesn’t even have a proper cap (at least you can’t put it back on once the spray head is attached), mu ha ha ha, so the eye must serve!! :DD Well, it fits not only because of its fresh scent into summer, but also because it actually reminds of vacation and the sea with its mojito scent, as well as its somewhat creamy aura that evokes sunscreen. It may have a somewhat low sillage and a certain synthetic quality, but since it smells quite nice as described and averages only about 30 euros for 100 mL, I think there’s really nothing to complain about! A "sniffer" could definitely be worth it! Aaaaaaaaaaahhh!!!! Now I want to lie on the beach with a mojito in one hand and a coconut water drink with a straw and umbrella in the other hand! And before anyone thinks that I might drop both… luckily, I’m not one of those people who are so clumsy that they spill everything… I must have some strength after all,… if not a good "woman-picking-up-skill," then at least the ability to hold two drinks at the same time!!… *sigh* :DD

According to the marketing, the top notes should include lemon and mojito lime. However, this summer does not smell like a mojito on vacation at all. I rather thought it smelled like melon and cucumber. The scent is fresh and cool, making it suitable for summer. Chemically enhanced with artificial fragrance additives, aquatic and slightly green, it makes the hair on the back of my neck stand up. I also resist the other advertised fragrance notes. In the heart phase, pineapple, guava, and white flowers are supposed to enchant the summer. While some fruity and sweet notes can be detected, neither the sweet-sour of a pineapple nor the sweet-dense nectar characteristic of white flowers come through. The finish is supposed to be cedarwood and coconut milk. I can indeed detect something milky and creamy, but there is no trace of cedarwood, not even a hint. A synthetic green-sweet veil runs through the fragrance phases, which keeps the scent fresh but does not improve it. Let’s wait and see until Calvin Klein brings something more natural to the market again..

That's how I would summarize my experience with Calvin Klein's latest summer flanker. First, I must say that I got it at a really good price. I reserved it online yesterday at the store for 23.99 for 100ml, which is a fair price. The bottle is very nice. Deep blue. My thoughts immediately drifted to the deep blue sea. At home, I sprayed it on at 23 degrees. It starts off very synthetic with a light mojito aroma and hints of pineapple. After 3 minutes, the coconut joins in, giving the skin a slight sunscreen touch. After 30 minutes, I could hardly smell anything anymore. So... 8 sprays on the entire arm. Now we're talking! Not really. Exactly the same progression. It's been 40 minutes now, and the scent is only faintly perceptible. I need to test CK Summer at 30 degrees (hopefully that will help), but I feel a bit cheated. Maybe it's my skin, but this "longevity" is just not acceptable. This is almost a fraud against the consumer. I will report back on how it performs in the height of summer, but for now, I am really disappointed. :-(

Unfortunately, I have to start with the durability and sillage, but more on that later. Like all CK One Summer fragrances I know, this one from 2018 is really good as well. It's not my favorite from the line, but it's very refreshing and invigorating. The opening is synthetically fresh and comes across like lime juice. The slight sweetness probably comes from the guava, which I don't really perceive. The perfume has no development, but I don't find that bothersome. A woody undertone mixes in, and that's about it. Unfortunately, the durability and sillage are at the lowest level and not really good. After 2 hours, the perfume is completely gone and can only be faintly smelled on the clothing. You need to reapply immediately. Still, I find the price/performance ratio quite okay. A fresh, light designer scent for little money and good for casual wear.

It's a fresh and energetic fragrance, Elegant, Classy and Woody, It smells so good and very pleasant, It reminds me of Mochino Uomo but Burberry launched in 1995 before Mochino. It opens up with like fresh citrusy , herbal and floral notes in the background then dry down is musky woody. This is perfect for the spring and fall. I have new reformulation and Longevity is very good. I really enjoy it and I love Burberry for Men EDT. Highly Recommended. Two Thumbs Up. Rating : 8.5 / 10

This is a very classic barbershop scent that never fails to do it’s job. Opening starts with mint, citrus and lavender which I do really like an appreciate, yes it may smell cheap or synthetic for educated noses but this is not necessarily a bad thing since synthetic smell is not overpowering (looking at you, Sauvage”). We should also acknowledge that this fragrance can be buy for dirt cheap, 30-40 dollars for 100ml, so synthetic smell is inevitable. When it comes to the drydown, it becomes woodier, greener and slightly floral. Middle notes are when this fragrance really shine. When it comes to the base notes, you will basicly just smell woods alike to the Terre d’ Hermes along with some other notes from middle. Performance wise it is fine. Not quite powerful but it is decant. I get about 6-7 hours of longevity with about 1 feet projection for a 3 hour duration. Considering that this is an edt and somewhat noticable even though the intimate projection, I will say that this performance is enough. This fragrance is for fall and spring, but definitely can be worn during the winter and summer. This fragrance might be too woody/spicy for extreme heat and it will not be warm/strong enough for really cold weather. It can be an amazing office/school scent and I got compliments with this one, but this won’t be the most suitable scent for romantic occasions. But before you buy, you should acknowledge that this is a little bit mature scent. Yes, it is not as mature as Terre d’ Hermes, but I do not thing it will fit teenagers or young adults. Also, this is a kind of an outdated fragrance, so do not have any expectations from the other’s opinion. Smell it and buy it if you like, it’s a good scent but definitely not one of the “attention grabbers”

Cool, crisp, elegant masculinity in a bottle. This scent from my birth year (1995, 30 years ago) has hardly aged a day. My vintage 1997 bottle (which reads Burberry's of London on the label) is bright, breezy, sharp, juicy, and fresh, with an underlying sweetness and creaminess which makes this simply one of my absolute favorite wears in my collection. Is it the most original scent? No. If you're familiar with 90s fragrances, you will detect that classic DNA in the oversoul of Burberry Men. This is essentially an aromatic fougere with an oriental twist. I think it'd be best described as a mix of Platinum Egoiste and Allure Homme (the OG, not Eau Extreme) - it's got that sharp, metallic, aromatic freshness of Platinum Egoiste and the smooth, creamy, succulence of Allure Homme. This is the definition of effortlessness. You can weaar this any time, anywhere if you want to smell clean, classy, and fresh. It might not garner you the most compliments in the world, but everyone will agree that you smell good. The only strike against it in my mind is the performance. Even a vintage bottle like the one I have isn't the longest lasting scent, netting me about 4 or 5 hours of longevity and light projection. But that's alright with me - there's so much pleasure in reapplication. Overall, this is one of my favorite 90s fragrances. It is just so damn good. Scoop up a vintage bottle on Ebay while the going's still cheap. 9/10

I believe the scent was the first Burberry men's fragrance, released right in the middle of the trashiest and most colorful decade of all time. But the perfumes from that time were exactly contrary to the flashy fashion, music, and pop culture. Burberry for Men belongs to the category of perfect all-rounders for me, classic yet pleasing. Hardly anyone wears it anymore, and that could make it interesting again. Not to mention that besides London and partly Brit, no Burberry fragrance has ever reached this level again. A real insider tip that creates a bridge between the modern Burberry sweetener and the classic men's EdC in a charming and, above all, stylish way. For me, it's an absolute signature scent for men over 30 and also very office-appropriate. And these men experienced their heyday in the 90s and will feel reminded of many beautiful things, somewhat romanticized and more beautifully thought out, of course. Bravo, techno, Love Parade, FIFA 98, youth, school, love, ultra-hot and never-ending summer vacations, carefree kicking on the playground, public pool, Ed von Schleck ice cream, DM, mixed bag... I find all of this in Burberry for Men. Just now grown up, experienced, and fully in a job, maybe even a boss already. An absolutely masculine apple, a fresh, classic bergamot, a bit of mint and spice. And underneath it all, a sweet vanilla undertone - you can hardly be more of an all-rounder or more at peace with oneself than this perfume. A perfectly balanced mix, more worldly than British. Still, the scent would surely suit James Bond perfectly. Bottle: simple and easy to overlook. Sillage: mediocre Longevity: 7-8 hours, maybe a few overtime hours in the year-end sprint. For me, an absolute job discovery and almost on par with Platinum Egoiste or Laliques White... unjustly overshadowed by many inferior Burberry soups like Sport or Touch.

At first spray, Burberry gives me a nice, uncomplicated scent impression with their men's flanker. I see a certain closeness to other office-appropriate fragrances like "YSL L'Homme" or "Gabrielli Homme" as a fundamental characteristic. A smooth fruity start, a bit of apple, subtle peach, already lightly underlined with lavender. A hint of rather unusual, slightly anise-like floral notes comes through from marigold (Tagetes). An interesting freshness kick, much higher quality than in all the current horror creations, arises from a harmonious interplay of lime and mint in the heart phase, which avoids the gruesome cocktail touch that is so often incorporated into men's(!) fragrances these days. Jasmine contributes very moderately bright floral nuances. The base then becomes sweeter, where vanilla, tonka bean, and the previously emerging cedarwood create a pleasant, balanced impression. The garden fruitiness remains quite long as a background shimmer, allowing "Burberry Men" to carry its fundamental character through all phases.

There are fragrances that are not groundbreaking, but good. Fragrances that you like to spray on in the morning. Fragrances that make you think not of 'perfume', but of 'just smelling good'. Fragrances that don't hurt your wallet, to which you don't set high artistic or other expectations. Except for those: to smell good and to feel comfortable.

Just a few seconds after the citrusy opening, it becomes obvious: "Burberry for Men" feels somehow familiar. I may be wrong, but it initially reminded me of Dolce & Gabbana's pour Homme, with a little splash of Cool Water added. Secondly, Minotaure by Paloma Picasso came to mind with its sweet spiciness.

There are fragrances that are considered classics, and for me, Burberry for Men is one of them. This scent is not overpowering, but it lets the surroundings know that you are there. It will never be a classic compliment getter, but if someone gets closer, the fragrance knows how to impress. For me, it is a permanent part of my collection that will never disappear.

My dearest sister sent us - as she does every Christmas - a beautiful and well-filled package, with gifts and little things that are meant to bring us joy ..: well, what can I say … she gifted my husband this fragrance for Christmas without having the faintest idea of what she had actually accomplished.

You can't go wrong with this one. It fits always and everywhere with a sympathetic spice and freshness that simply accompanies you well throughout the day without being too generic or pleasing. I find it very pleasant here, what I often see as boring in others. It hardly changes and lasts a long time.

A bit mysterious perfume this Obssesed Intense. I tried to figure out the notes without success, it's kind of ambery/woody with a touch of orange. By the last I mean that it reminds me of something similar to orange... but without it being orange. It must be the combination of rhubarb with other notes, or that is the explanation I have made myself. I expected more projection from him but no, I see him as more of a personal bubble. What it does have is good permanence on the skin, surpassing many current watered-down perfumes. The aroma can be intense if you are used to fresh or sweet things... for me it is simply different and with a mysterious air. This is one of those fragrances that until you try it, it is very difficult to get an idea of where it is going... so if you have the opportunity to try it, I recommend that you do... but never pay crazy prices for it, you don't have to feed the speculators!

At first, one can perceive an intense and powerful sweet note that brings with it a decidedly strong, refreshingly greenish sour note, thanks to the rhubarb. At the same time, the rhubarb is accompanied by another sweet nuance that hides a slight citrus-tinged orange tone, and I suspect the use of bergamot and orange, instead of sweetie. These two notes are enveloped by a fine aromatic, subtly spicy nuance that, in my opinion, ensures that the top note retains some liveliness despite its sweetness and originates from the pepper. A little later, the rhubarb is considerably dimmed and only slightly perceptible, taking on an incredibly intense sweet, mystically appearing reddish-brown woody note that exudes a very nice lacquer-like, delicate medicinal touch, giving the fragrance a wonderful dark heaviness, and I suspected oud, instead of cypriol. The cypriol is underscored by another woody note that carries a slight incense-like tone and appears very dense, and I imagined the use of cedarwood and incense, instead of cedar leaf. The cypriol and cedar leaf are enveloped by a slightly synthetic-seeming nuance that simultaneously imparts a light, almost transparent radiance to the fragrance, and I considered the use of Iso-E-Super, instead of cashmeran, to be possible. In the last 4 hours, a very nice balsamic spicy note gradually joins in, giving the fragrance a pleasant snugness and originating from the black amber. At the same time, the amber is underscored by a bright, peppery, bitter nuance, which I suspect to be vetiver and musk, providing a fine smooth masculinity, and my research has shown that the aforementioned scent perception could indeed stem from gurjun balsam, although this scent note has unfortunately been unknown to me until today. These two notes are enveloped by a light sweet-tinged rosy note that brings a delicate woody smoky tone and provides a deep finish, thanks to the guaiac wood. Overall, the fragrance lasts 9 hours on my skin. The sillage is designed to be very noticeably 1.5 meters in the first hour and maintains a very clear whole arm's length for 3 hours, before gradually minimizing until the fragrance's conclusion. I would like to express my sincere thanks to our Parfumo "Honk1510" for the sample.

Scentrack: The Verve - Bittersweet Symphony The great master of jasmine and rose F.K. has presented another beautiful rose. His recognizable fresh and fragile rose supported by wet flowers. Very feminine and gentle perfume with some classical aura. It contains some specific Burberry note encountered before in great Burberry Body. The bottle is fantastic, especially the button-like cap. Burberry British rose which perfectly evokes the humid climate of English gardens. Rating: 7.5/10

Well, it was a decent idea at least. Burberry have attempted to evoke a garden after the rain with this fragrance composed by it-perfumer Francis Kurkdjian, but the perfume seems to run out of steam (or should that be cash) after a very brief time both on my skin and on a tester strip. Granted, the fragrance is suitably sharp and elegant when it does manage to make an appearance, but the brevity of that opening loveliness is all too brief for me. All that's left is a beige patchouli nothingness, and by the time that point is reached, I've forgotten what the start smelled like. A nice try from Burberry, but there's hundreds of other perfumes that do this better. In particular, take a look at Guerlain's Après L'ondée for the most beautiful post-rain experience in perfumery.

It was years that I have not seen a decent release from the house till I randomly checked for My Burberry and I found it quite astonishing. This perfume blooms out so modern, yet, apparently has root in classics on 80's. What it presents is a fresh and crispy floral, twisty, and casual smell of fruity fresh floral theme that pushes the citruses of the opening down and bring quince up plus lactonic shades of fruits. Surprisingly, the fragrance gains even more shades of beauty once settled in the core and base. Still young and delicate as the opening, still fresh and elegant with strange fruity dimensions. Longevity: 7/10 Projection: 5/10, try it in rainy weather. Scent: much higher than expectations.

A london garden after the rain. You hit the nail on the head Mr. Kurkdjian. My Burberry is an elegant classic floral. Refined rose, plesantly feminine sweet pea, British geranium and warm patchouli. The bottle itself exemplifies the house of Burberry. The hand tied bow is made from gabardine, the very same material used for the Burberry trench and the cap is made after the buttons of the trench. There are many comparisons to Chloe Eau de Parfum, but in my opinion there really is no comparison, except for the rose note. Coty Prestige hasn't put out luxury in a while and Bottega Veneta is above and beyond for this distributor. BPI however, still houses luxury brands with quality fragrances. My Burberry is a must have for those fond of rose or classic florals.

My Burberry is a masterfully created good quality fragrance that has a very strong silage and is long lasting. It is a flowery powerhouse in my view with a very specific note that has been left out of the description here. I think it might be linen or leather? Not exactly sure. But it’s the note that gives it a very clean, sharp feeling that manages to convey the crispness of a camel colored trench. And it does smell like a beautiful Rose and I suppose geraniums are there and grass and it isn’t too sunny or playful at all. No sir! This one has a rather serious almost business like personality evoking big city, reserved character and office like settings to me. It is very feminine with a very edgy masculine note. I picture a confident independent lady in a power suit very stylish and polished, very together and not a hair out of place. It is very beautiful but not very touching. You know, like it’s almost too perfect. And that made it very hard for me to love it.

Freesia blast with a (very) faint hint of sweetpea and quince. No violet, no rose, no citrus, not detectable as this fragrance is utterly ruled by freesia in top note, and musk which takes centre stage as heart note and remains linear to drydown. It's a sober without being dated scent. But it's nothing new, or extraordinary.

I enjoy wearing this perfume, as it’s classic. There’s a fruity top note and then a wonderful floral take over. It’s so classy and timeless, perfect to wear literally anytime. Sillage and longevity are fantastic. This makes it worth every penny.

Yesterday, I was once again wandering around a well-known drugstore to check out some fragrances. I was actually looking for a different one, but unfortunately, it wasn't the same as I remembered it from back then, and that was quickly settled. Two shelves up, I discovered "my burberry," and I must admit, I would have never tested it if it hadn't been so ruthlessly on sale.

While I was still a bit hesitant with the EdT, especially because it takes its time with the scent development, the EdP immediately appeals to me. It stands by me with selected politeness right away - and remains reliably there. Just like the fine English way, it does not impose itself. As loyal and gallant as my friend Bruce - who is always there when you call him.

..I will be able to act with this fragrance, anyone who visits my profile will immediately see "My Burberry." Because this scent is truly MY BURBERRY, it has wrapped me around its finger, so I will tell you, whether objectively or not, how the fragrance works for me.

Putting excessive amounts of Iso-E Super in a fragrance is a lottery - some people perceive it normally, while others are completely anosmic to it. I only came to understand this after buying DH 2020, which is also based on generous amounts of the molecule. Actually, these two share quite a few notes - bergamot and pepper in the top, vetiver and cashmere note in the base, and, of course the cedar note courtesy of the aforementioned Iso-E. Contrary to what most reviewers say about the performance, this can last a good 10 hours on my skin, but analogous to DH 2020, it does not project crazily and seemingly disappears only to reappear later on, which is the distinctive feature of this elusive woody molecule contained therein. Sadly, that might be the reason this was ditched not long after its launch, despite being (in my humble opinion) the one Eternity flanker with the most natural ingredients. Nobody was able to tolerate this elusive performance in 2016 and still many are not able to tolerate it in the era of the new DH 2020 - even more now maybe, in the era obsessed with loud beastmode fragrances. If you are still able to find it for a decent price, give it a go, spray further away from your nose, don't sniff your arms every 2 minutes and you might appreciate the subtle elegance this offers.

The top note of this fragrance is truly well done. Blind tested and without knowing what was landing on my forearm, I initially suspected a scent from the Prada l'homme line. I was really excited. But the joy didn’t last long, as the top note unfortunately fades away far too quickly. Thus, this top note is a tribute to perhaps the most untalented, yet iconic goalkeeper in Bundesliga history from the 90s to the 00s, Tomislav Piplica. For both the top note and Tomislav Piplica would have been world-class if they had held on better. After the top note, there is a brief phase where something Sauvage-like is presented, before the fragrance drifts into a sweet, pleasing medley that unfortunately has little recognizability. And so, for both, the fragrance and the gentleman goalkeeper, only the top note remains in memory. (For those who don’t know what this means, check out the 15-second YouTube video "Piplica.")

I am looking for a farewell gift for my dear neighbors, as they are unfortunately leaving the city. They are a well-groomed couple - always tastefully dressed. I am now searching for a fragrance that is not too quirky, but also not too bland and generic. With Eternity Intense, I believe I have found the right one. It has a slightly sweet powderiness that gives it character without being overwhelming. It is also not harshly masculine, but remains smooth. I do not find it excessively "intense," although it does show some distinctiveness. The white pepper is mild, rounded off by an aromatic tea note. Calm and cool, lavender joins in, wrapped in soft Chashmeran. Delicately powdered, everything is complemented by the iris. Intense exudes casual elegance, yet remains completely relaxed. I think it is a good farewell gift - after a harmonious neighborhood,

l love when something surprises me and makes me question what I think I know about myself. On paper, I would have never given this scent a chance. Until I smelled Burberry for Women my favorite perfume was Prada by Prada. I thought I only liked resinous, spicy, earthy scents. I was positive that I hated anything sweet or fruity. But one day on a whim I sprayed Burberry for Women on me while shopping in a department store. 30 minutes later, I was rapidly retracing my steps to the fragrance counter to purchase what was the most delicious thing I'd ever smelled. I wanted to eat my own arm. This perfume and my body chemistry are like totally LYLAS BFFs. Just a few months later, and I'm already on my second bottle. I REGRET NOTHING! I've never craved a scent as much as I do this. I feel sort of melancholy on the days I choose another scent from my wardrobe. I find that I'm always eager to come home, shower, and spray the Burberry. Burberry for Women is just comfortable. It's comforting. It's home.

This is a rather hard to find fragrance due to it being listed under so many different names eg. Burberry for Women, Burberry Classic, Burberry London etc. When I eventually found it I had my fingers crossed that I hadn't been searching for something that was going to be a disappointment. Disappointed, I was not. Crazy about the scent? No, not really. This fragrance is light, creamy and warm. Unlike other Burberry scents, I felt that this fragrance stayed very close to the skin, making it an intimate perfume. When I smell Burberry Woman I immediately think of a hot sunny day, so I'd most likely wear this during the warmer seasons. The peach, apricot, pear and black currant add a fruity freshness to this scent without making it too sour or overpowering. This is actually a fruity opening that I rather enjoyed. I don't get a lot of jasmine in this fragrance, however the musk is fairly strong. Overall the scent is comforting and suitable for any age group, but with that being said this fragrance didn't grow on me because I found it rather linear and common. It's not the best perfume choice if you're looking to stand out from the crowd. Burberry Woman is friendly and casual, not sexy, romantic or outstanding.

Burberry Woman (Classic) is the mother of Burberry Brit, that's for sure! And thankfully for me, neither Brit nor Classic are similar to the dreadful, drugstore floral called Burberry Weekend. Burberry Woman is a very easy-to-wear, low-sugar peaches & cream, vanilla-based scent. It stays close to the skin but lasts a very long time. The jasmine is well-behaved on me (which is rarely the case!) and doesn't have much of a presence (good!). The fruits are present but neither sickly nor sugary... just fresh & sweet. I'm not sure why this is classified as a fruity floral. It's an oriental vanilla to me & the freshest one I've ever tried. However, it's not for the kids - this one is for the women, imo. Burberry Woman would make a great choice for an office fragrance, an everyday scent, or even a bedtime perfume. It's wearable nearly any time of the year, except perhaps on the hottest days of summer. I often use it as a comfort scent. It's not gonna get your rocks off, but not every fragrance should. It's an easy-to-wear, pleasant fragrance. I'm a sucker for fleshy fruits (peach, pear, apricot, apples), and sandalwood & vanilla are awesome on my skin. For me, it's not only full-bottle worthy, but I have a back-up too! The notes of Burberry Classic (for Women): Top - peach, apricot, cool pear and black currant Heart - jasmine, sandalwood and cedar Base - musk and vanilla

I love the smell of peaches but I find that in many fragrances they turn out to be overly sweet or too watery. The peach note in Burberry is done just right. It is delicious but not sickly sweet. It is delicate but not too light. Burberry is pretty, cozy but also classy. It is great for those days when I would like to smell nice but I do not want to make a strong statement. I love the opening of this scent and I actually think that I smell very nice green apple note along with the peach. The woody notes come through right away and to my nose the scent stays linear with a lovely woody-peach-vanilla combo. I can see that many reviewers compare this scent to Fancy Love by Jessica Simpson and I agree that two of them have similarities. I find that Burberry a bit more on a woody side and Fancy Love is more on a gourmand side. Overall score is 7.5/10. I do like this scent. Somehow it makes me feel happy and pretty and…oh so peachy. The sillage is medium and longevity is 5 hours on my skin. I definitely recommend it if you are looking for vanilla and peach fragrances.

A fragrance bought a long time ago which ended up in the back of the closet - what a shame! When I finally started using it I must say that it surprised me in a positive way. Especially the heart notes are lovely. The cedar, sandalwood and moss make my nose cheer. I do not get any apple or blackcurrant, though. This stays close to the skin and it does not last for long - but it is worth the swift journey. I love the bottle! Pierre Dinand is on my top 20 of bottle designers. He is the genius behind iconic bottles such as Rive Gauche (my favourite), Opium, Obsession and Calandre. In this case I love the smoothy feeling when holding the bottle and the simplicity of the expression. Classy and tactile. All in all a beautiful perfume. 2/365
This fragrance was a "belly flop" for me. I should have known better! When I read that some people said it smelled like Jessica Simpson's Fancy Love, I should have ran for the hills!

Burberry for Women is warm and sweet, giving peach, pear, vanilla, and burnt rubber. Attractive and wearable, especially in the fall or winter, it feels a little young and uncomplicated for me, lacking boldness and complexity.

I wear perfume twice daily during the day. And at night, I chose this one as my nighttime fragrance for this evening. And I am pleasantly surprised. I love the smell. It's definitely a fall fragrance to me. But right now is summer and I like a deeper fragrance when i'm going to sleep. I'm not fancy.

Almost 20 years ago, I once owned a bottle of you. I must have bought you somewhere in Hesse. At that time, I went through various professional stages and just as many moves, until I returned to my homeland in 2006. I wore you in the office, out in the evenings, and even at my wedding.

I am repeatedly surprised that some fragrances pass by my nose for years - oh, what am I saying, decades. This was the case with Euphoria, with Emporio Armani She, and now it is the same with Burberry for Woman.
