I am sure I must have tested it at some point, but I have also tested many other Burberrys, and until today, it has never really been my brand.

The OG was a start of a new dna potential, woody, green generic but pleasing. The edp was a miss of the dna, but its a nice resinous frag that's wonderful for cold evenings. THIS? this is fruity?? I get some weird sweetness and I cant pinpoint to what it is, it was such a nice line but Burberry had to jump on the hype train of weirdly sweet "AmBeRwOoDy" fragrances. not my cup of tea at all.

The opening starts off with an extremely sweet balsamic (amyris) for about five to ten minutes. Try to ignore this part and don't judge the fragrance on the opening. After this time it turns into a sort of cedar-pine amalgam (hints at pine but is not pine, it is drydown of amyris/elemi) for the remainder of the fragrance (which is a very very long time). In summary a linear balsamic cedar with the cypriol providing a earthy-smoky characteristic (hinting at incense but not incense). Hints at pine, is not pine. Hints at incense, is not incense. Should be totally cedar, but the other stuff mutes the cedar so it's not fully cedar and makes it much sweeter than cedar would normally be. It stays middle-of-the-road so as to not offend the young male testing panel with too sharp a smell of any one thing. Trying to formulate something that pleases most people leads to mediocrity but I do have to say, it smells really good. I don't love it, but I do like it a lot (wearing it right now as I write this review). The overall vibe is sweet-woody with just a hint of earthiness—admittedly a bit cloying at times Bottle: Though it looks basic it has a build and finishing touches where in comparison other maisons simply fail: the base is bottom-heavy and trapezoidal-shaped which prevents tipping (yes!), the bottle can be picked up by the cap because the magnet is very strong, the glass is tinted and not just a colour painted over clear glass which chips over time. Sprayer is outstanding. Minimalistic but very functional and gets high marks from me. I don't apply fragrances as "dumb reach" ever - there's always some thinking that goes into spraying something that resonates with the mood I'm in...but I can totally understand this as such a class of fragrance. You can wear this anywhere and you're practically guaranteed that you'll smell great, though I would stay that it's perhaps a bit loud for the office unless you spray your chest and it's under a closed dress shirt (a male strip dancer could wear this bare chested and that would work—I suppose if you have a job where you stroll around with an unbuttoned shirt bare-chested then essentially any fragrance will do lol). Very long lasting, absolutely linear after the first ten minutes, I would agree that the smell leans towards basic...but a basic with indisputable quality a notch above. Long lasting parfum that is *actually* a parfum (lasts all day). There's only one gripe: the price. MSRP $183 USD for a 100ml? $220 for a refill? You're competing with other western houses that I would argue produce more memorable fragrances, and let's not forget the middle eastern houses that make fragrances for under $50 that are very nearly always nuclear in strength (which make both memorable and/or dumb-reach fragrances). You're competing with designer (dumb-reach) and competing with grey-market niche (price). I don't see the market for this at this price...but I've witnessed the younger generation (the ones that say they're always broke, mind you) drop $30 for a coffee and a bagel when the coffee shop also functions as a cool hangout spot...and this is marketed towards them. This is an under-40 fragrance which corresponds to the new street-urban demographic Burberry now tries to reach (look up the music video "FKA twigs papi bones" to get a feel for what I'm talking about)—serving a proper rejoinder to something like Creed Aventus. Someone who wants to smell great but pays extra to say they wear "Burberry," because the brand has cachet within their social circle as it signals you have disposable income to buy something that expensive. I'm not in that circle and I find it is sweet in a very youthful kind of way and thus out of place for me...but begrudgingly I cannot deny that price aside if a younger person wore this I'd think they'd smell great.

I don't know any other fragrances from this series, I was never interested in any Hero from Burberry, but I received a sample of Hero Parfum for purchase. What can you say about this fragrance? It is definitely very masculine, the beginning is a strong kick of cedar, the opening is quite sharp. Then the cedar is mixed with slightly sweet cypriol. The composition smoothes out, becomes woody, resinous, a bit smoky, and sometimes a slightly dill note appears. It's not a bad scent, but it seemed generic and didn't impress me much. Typically mainstream, heavier men's perfumes. Quite boring.

I am a bit more impressed than most with Hero Parfum. Seems like the consensus in the community is that the EDP is the best in the line, but I completely disagree. In fact, the EDP is the only one that I just don’t enjoy much because I find it to be too sweet. But I digress. Hero Parfum starts with a short lived citrus but then goes into what this fragrance is really about. WOODS. This is an absolute cedar explosion. And when I say woody, I mean it. The cedar is front and center and dry. It’s not like those non-descript/barely there “woods” you get in most modern masculine designer fragrances. It’s also accompanied by a sweetness that doesn’t come from your typical vanilla or tonka notes. The sweetness in this comes off resinous, which gives it a really nice subtly sweet warmth. Hero Parfum also has a green tinge to it. There is something coniferous in it that gives it that green bite. This isn’t niche level perfumery, or anything I’d call challenging to wear, but it’s a lot more interesting and different to most cooler weather designers that are being cranked out right now that are usually sickeningly sweet vanilla bombs. For the price you can get this from discounters, this is a no brainer if you are into woody scent profiles and want something that will make you stand out in the fall and winter seasons. Like Parfums usually go, this one has moderate projection for a few hours then sits closer to the skin. It lasts a very long time though, especially if you spray on clothing. The presentation is nice and fitting of the scent. The dark brown bottle reminds me of dark stained or charred wood. I like the bottle shape of the Hero line and the tester bottle I have has a magnetic cap. The atomizer is a bit of a hose and I wish it would have a little bit wider of a dispersal. Nothing deal breaking though.

This fragrance offers exactly what you expect from it for a change! A woody, sweet scent more suited for cold days. I received it as a gift from my girlfriend and was convinced. At first, it was almost too "masculine" for me, but over the course of the day, it matures into a very pleasantly sweet, creamy/woody note.

Basically, I have already described the scent through the title as I perceive it. I find it quite sweet, with a slightly woody note. In my opinion, it fits perfectly into spring. It is not heavy enough for winter, but in summer, on the other hand, it would be TOO heavy. It is very pleasant to have this scent around you. You just smell good with it.

My wife loves this scent on me. When we tried it last year at the orange "M," the first word that came to her mind was "lumberjack." She simply enjoys the wicked, woody, smoky, and yet sweet aspects of it. A bearded man, chopping wood at a cabin in the woods, with a fire burning behind him, its heavy smoke mingling with the scent of the wood.

First of all, I want to say that the scent couldn't be a better fit for Burberry. Everyone knows the brand for its luxurious scarves and coats. Accordingly, it is a fragrance for cold seasons. How did I come across the scent? My girlfriend tested it at the airport and said it was her favorite. To me, it actually smells quite balsamic but unisex due to the sweetness.

For me, this fragrance has become a classic; the woody-spicy notes make this masterpiece an all-rounder. The sweetness that comes after the drydown makes it better than the Hero predecessors. Whether on a date or at a bar with the guys, this everyday scent delivers. The newer versions with leather aren't really my thing, so I stick with this fragrance.

there was a young woman who, on a sunny summer day, took a day trip to Lake Constance with one of her friends. To Friedrichshafen, to be precise. She already knew Chanel No. 5 and didn't particularly like it. That didn't stop her from spraying the hair variant of it in a department store. And she had long hair. Back then. Shortly thereafter, she strolled along the lake. Suddenly, a wasp flew by and instantly fell in love with the young woman. However, she did not return his affection; in fact, she found him bothersome. She felt harassed by the striped insect. The wasp, on the other hand, was relentless and devotedly buzzed around her. The friend found a certain comedy, perhaps even schadenfreude, in this situation. Meanwhile, the harassment did not cease. So the two maidens decided to rent a pedal boat. It turned out that the lake was deeper and larger than the wasp's love, and so he finally gave up. What does this story tell us? I have no idea. I certainly didn't see the creature again.

It is remarkable in that it contains 'Petalia', (a patented perfume molecule by Givaudan) and this piqued my interest. If you like Love, Chloe and No 19 Poudre this may join the ranks. I bought it after wearing it from shop testers where your perception is often clouded by the many competing perfumes of that micro climate and, hesitant, unconvinced, I happened to see Victoria Frolova's charming review. It was 'almost free' ( I am beyond shame) and it made its way from a grey market retailer to my door. What do you get? A touch of Ivoire, a bit of white pepper, the orange and the iris. The lavender doesn't come through much, doesn't speak to me, your experience may differ. I don't like the unimaginative bottle designer or the pinky tinge but I guess it's meant to play up the British lavender theme. Up against Love Chloe and Ivoire (new) it's an 'also ran' but the dry down is pleasant and a bit tart, making it office friendly. Lasts about three hours on me. A nice scent for a soft cotton summer dress, quite girl-next-door and the absolute opposite of its marketing hype.

Burberry's new fragrance for women was created by Givaudan's perfumers Nathalie Cetto and Antoine Maisondieu who tried to incorporate the smell of English lavender from Kent into a contemporary fashion fragrance. The press material talks about English lavender being "stronger" than the French variant and the important role of using an "English" ingredient in order to emphasize the "Britishness" of the brand. I don't smell any natural lavender in this fragrance at all, be it British or French. "Brit Rhythm" also features iris (in the form of orris absolute, they say) and it's this particular mixture of (synthetic, I'd reckon) iris and lavender which defines "Brit Rhythm". Orange flowers and vetiver contribute to the slightly greenish aspect of the fragrance which in spite of its musical name and the campain aimed at a younger audience smells like a bad version of "Infusion d'Iris". If you want English lavender, try one of the traditional colognes which have been around for ages. If you want iris, buy a true iris-fragrance. I see no need to purchase this weird, synthetic mixture.

Top Notes: Lavender, Pink Pepper, Neroli, Aldehydes Heart Note: Orris, Petalia, Blackberry Leaf, Orange Blossom Base Notes: Musk, Woodsy Notes, Vetiver, Cedar, Courmarin I am on a mission to use up some of the many, many samples I have accumulated over the last few years. Tonight it was a toss up between Brit Rhythm and Elizabeth Arden Green Tea. I chose Brit Rhythm because I mistakenly looked at the notes for Brit Rhythm for Him and thought that was what I had on hand. Well, it worked out quite well. I really like this a lot! Lavender, like coconut, is a really tricky note for me, but it is done absolutely BEAUTIFULLY here! I am impressed because lavender is not an easy note to incorporate into a fragrance as far as I am concerned. It is blended so beautifully here with the musk and all the other notes. I detect some lovely aldehydes in the top notes that persist well into the dry down on my skin--just lovely, fresh, clean, classic even. This fragrance is not only both clean and fresh, it is somehow also warm and comforting. At times, it almost borders on gourmand it smells so good. Yes, it is just a tad synthetic but not so much as to be off putting. Everything just works in this fragrance. If the notes sound good to you, then give this one a try. I think you will be very pleasantly surprised. This is the sort of fragrance that could be your default "it smells so lovely; it works in any setting imaginable; it is a crowd pleaser that will make everyone around you inhale deeply and smile; and, it does it all without breaking the bank type fragrance." Brit Rhythm for Her is a very comforting, cuddly fragrance, yet somehow it sparkles with a certain effervescence that draws you in. Although marketed as a feminine fragrance, I think young men especially could wear this fragrance. I am sitting here now inhaling deeply and thinking........mmmmm......this is very nice indeed! :) I am rating this fragrance amongst its peers as an affordable designer fragrance that is a real winner for any age group and both sexes. Performance could be better, but as an affordable designer eau de toilette, it performs as expected. If you have an opening in your wardrobe for this "type" of fragrance, Brit Rhythm for Her would fill the slot quite nicely indeed. Fragrance: 7/10 Projection: 5/10 Sillage: 5/10 Longevity: 5/10

This is a clean, fresh (without lemon lime but still somewhat citrusy) warm and slightly spicy fragrance that was quite frankly born in the wrong era. It is harmless and perfect for an office day during spring/summer. Given the clean fragrance trend nowadays I think it would have profited if it had been released later. It is also quite strong for a EDt. It lasts 7-8 hours. It is also quite lavender forward and if you don't like that steer clear.

The three or four Burberrys that I have been able to sniff so far all seemed a bit bland to me. So I set my expectations for Brit Rhythm rather low. I was all the more surprised that I liked this scent right away. And after I criticized a Burberry, it's only fair that I dedicate a few positive words to Brit Rhythm. Brit Rhythm starts with a sparkling, slightly peppery orange blossom. I'm reminded of fizzy drinks, it tickles pleasantly in my nose. Lavender underlines everything in the background, while iris and musk give the scent a “pure” touch, a fresh *clean and neat feeling*. And my nose picks up a hint of fine leather, yes, yes, I know it's not in there, but I perceive this soft leather note. (Just like I do in Après L’Ondée :o) Towards the base, Brit Rhythm becomes a bit powdery and ends with a warm wood note. This scent has something noble about it, and it serves as both a business and casual fragrance. The longevity is surprisingly good, lasting about 6 hours on my wrist, and the sillage is subtle but noticeable. Brit Rhythm is not restricted to a particular season, though it might be a bit too weak in sub-zero temperatures. And after the second test, I raise my rating from 70% to 80%, this scent deserves it.

... by The Clash immediately comes to mind with Brit Rhythm, as the scent reminds me of swinging good old London. Traditional yet modern - and relaxed. I am an incorrigible London fan, and Burberry skillfully conveys the British style. The opening with English lavender and neroli is wonderfully nostalgic and reminds me of walks in the venerable Hyde Park.

I had Brit Rhythm on my wish list for a long time, as it seems I am slowly turning into a lavender lover. Now I found it on sale and had to grab it (also as a consolation for my ancient Thé Vert going bad).
So either my scent nerves are out of whack or I'm right. I'm really curious to see how other comments about this fragrance will turn out. But I smell Persil and bubblegum.

So, this morning I specifically strolled over to Rossi. They have Rhythm by Burberry this week for just under 20 euros for 30 ml. I bought it blind because I expected a certain level from this scent after my studies. I was just curious, regarding the following comment with "Persil and Bubblegum," about what it might smell like. Now I know what was meant.

~ Inspiration ~ After I wasn't so fond of "Burberry Body," but liked "Burberry Brit" much more, I was curious about what to expect from "Burberry Rhythm." ~ Bottle ~ The square shape with the hinted check pattern has been retained, only the ribbed glass is new. It looks cool and simple. The perfume has a beautiful rosy tone.

It is already Fall. I am at home reading a book and drinking warm peach tea. I look at the window and notice that it is raining. As I open the window, the room is filled with that great smell. It is a mix of my peachtea, rain, soil and a little bit of roses. A nische-like fragrancy. Longlasting, luxurious, uncomplicated

I first tried this in my sisters collection a few years ago. It was an instant love. The combination of peaches and rose, with Amber in the base is fabulous. Longevity is really good, I can smell it throughout the day. It's one of my favourite designer fragrances, and I don't regret buying it in the 90ml bottle.

....of my handbag, I unearthed a small black box today. My Burberry black. Oh Mr. Kurkdjian created the scent. That raises high expectations. The fragrance reaches me buttery soft and gourmand - quite untypical for a Burberry. The fullness of the scent is also unusual - but appealing. A single timid spray develops into a veritable cloud, where the candied rose, topped with peach nectar, dominates. Amber serves as the "scent bed" for these two prominent ingredients, softened by patchouli. Nevertheless, Black remains surprisingly powerful, and does not leave my side by even a millimeter. However, I do not perceive it as black - rather velvety red, like the sweet rose petals. Black does have a tendency towards heaviness - good thing I applied it cautiously, otherwise it could be too much of a good thing. The longevity is enormous - respect. A beautiful gourmand in itself - but it probably comes into its own best in winter.

The EdP would have actually pleased me, but...would have...if only Bergamot and Freesia hadn't teamed up and launched an attack on me. Would have over would have. But with the Black version, that's a thing of the past. Now, Is reigns over Is! Is it strong? Yes...it is strong! Is it floral? Oh yes, and how floral it is. As if horsepower were rushing through the gas pedal to the engine to give it the (hoof) kick to take off, billions of micro-particles loaded with lush Jasmine burst from the bottle, barely giving you a moment to consider pressing the sprayer. Those little critters were already sniffing around my new and absolutely pristine glass bottle before I even got to the eagerly anticipated spraying. I thought to myself, this is going to be quite the ride! That would turn out to be an understatement. So, as mentioned, the Jasmine stampede opens the scent blast and leaves me completely flattened for a few moments. But somehow wonderful, even if really intense. You get plowed into the still unscented air behind and beside you as if you had jumped onto a TGV at the front. Yes, yes...that works in the movies! In the mind's eye too. To ensure you don't fall off the speeding vehicle, it's quite difficult to hold on, but a very sugary Rose and a lot of Peach Nectar come to the rescue as glue, and the rapid ride continues. Curves? Not a chance. It goes straight ahead at top speed, and sometimes you almost feel like you're heading straight for doom. The scent is so strong at times that, despite the pace, you want to spell the word "give up." But a real perfume holds on and clings tightly to the high-tech express train. Somewhere, we finally pass through places where the speed is slightly reduced, and at all the stations, the Amber flag is waved. Luckily, this takes some of the wind out of the Jasmine's sails before I run out of breath. I am immensely relieved when we reach our destination. Slowly, the train rolls in with squeaking brake blocks and a rushing sound into the terminal covered with glass domes on steel supports and finally comes to a complete stop. The people on the platform suddenly rush to the compartments to catch their loved ones. I, meanwhile, peel myself off the glue and let myself slide down to the tracks at the front of the train. Even as I reach the wall up to the platform, the dense cloud of Patchouli from the bouquets that many gentlemen have brought to greet their ladies reaches me. Dazed from the ride and this final plea of the fragrance, I drag myself to a bench and let myself sink onto it. What a ride! My Burberry Black is a fragrance whose concentration nearly paralyzes the senses even in small amounts, whose Jasmine has the power of a herd of Mustangs and sweeps over you as if there were no tomorrow. Luckily, this intensity is somewhat tamed by Rose and Peach, and Amber envelops softly and darkly. In the end, you also have to endure Patchouli. If you like all these notes, if you love strong and present fragrances with a statement, and if EdP and EdT were too weak for you, then you will find what you need here. Black came just at the right time for me, but I don't always feel like such a train ride. Now and then, however, I like to hop on...this TGV by Burberry.

This is my first Burberry fragrance. The other Burberrys never interested me, mainly because of the terrible check patterns (sorry to all the fans) and the regular My Burberry was too soapy and bland for me. Then I discovered My Burberry Black during my weekly addiction trips to the perfume store. I grabbed the bottle (my God, what a chunk, at least here in D.) and sprayed it on a test strip. Wow.. What a wave of sweetness hit me. I couldn't pick out any of the ingredients. It was just sweet! Well, it was okay. I stuck the strip in my handbag and moved on. When I emptied my handbag that evening, the strip came back into my hands. Ohhh.. that smells good. What was that again? My Burberry Black came to mind. Since it now had something I liked, I placed it on my dresser. All evening and night, my room smelled of My Burberry. Incredible, even Alien and Angel couldn't achieve that with me. I was really fascinated. A week later, I strolled back into the big D. and sprayed the fragrance on my wrist. Yes, it is intense and sweet.. but it has something. Something that captivates me.. honestly, I don't smell any peach nectar or anything like that. I only smell a sugary sweet rose and the jasmine. Later, the amber and patchouli come through and make it more luscious. But I don't care, it just smells good. I love this fragrance. In summer, it would be too much for me. Now that it’s getting colder, I could bathe in it. But be careful, as mentioned before, one or two spritzes are more than enough with this fragrance. More and you’ll get a headache and annoy others with it.. I think that despite this lush rosy sweetness, the fragrance has something elegant about it. It is very sweet, but also sexy and feminine. This is not a teen fragrance, but something for women who know what they want! It’s more of an evening scent. Wearable during the day, but then preferably in the colder months. Even though My Burberry Black doesn’t exactly stand out, it has potential. But I don’t care, it doesn’t always have to be special :) I’m into it and will carry the scent with me for a long time ;)

A sunny day, a funfair with loud stalls, noisy children, colorful lights, slightly stressed parents, and various treats wafting their scents all around. Spotted: A cotton candy stand! How wonderful! A sweet treat full of childhood memories, sweet promises, and fluffy soft enjoyment on a child's tongue!

Burberry fragrances are not really my usual preference. However, this one has a lot of what I am looking for. Great longevity, elegance, and still a certain sweetness. Yasmin is not overwhelming for me, yet noticeable. Smoky due to patchouli. The rose is also immediately present, but subtle. Soapy? A bit, but in an elegant way. The name Black fits like a glove.

With the My Burberry series, English fragrance tradition has been skillfully implemented. All three variants of the series contain a moist floral note that evokes the atmosphere of a rainy spring or autumn day in London.

one spray on a test strip placed on the coffee table was enough to scent the living room for three days :-) I layer (only in winter) one spray with Yves Rocher's amber, that is the limit for me. A decant of this fragrance would have sufficed, definitely very economical.

I love how this smells and all but at the end of the day I don’t think I’d ever buy it again. Don’t see how it adds to anything. I have most of the BDC line and accessories. This one seems like an odd man out. I’m happy to have tried it but I just see the point. Spray some more of your fragrance rather than wasting money on this.

I like this fragrance very much. I thought this might end up being boring and generic. It was such a pleasant surprise. A perfect daytime scent. This perfume is guaranteed not to offend anyone around you. It's light, soft and fresh. The notes are blended together nicely. On my skin it's citrusy, woody, green and aromatic. Not being a musk lover, I'm relieved that I don't get much of that on my skin. The only downfall is that the scent doesn't last long at all. It disappears before the end of the day, unlike many of my other fragrances that seem to last and last. I found my bottle on clearance for a good price and I don't regret my purchase as this perfume is not as easy to find as it once was. This fragrance also has a unisex vibe going on, making it suitable not only for women, but for men as well. I'll be reaching for this a lot during the summer months. A well rounded scent that I'm happy to have in my collection.

THE BEAT by Burberry Dry, spicy, white musky, lightly-earthy, lightly-citric, black tea of low sweetness. Opens with a blast of very dry bergamot, cardamom, and heavy handed dose of biting pink pepper. I get very little sweet mandarin from this one on my skin. Develops further with a rush of unsweetened black tea infused with a hint of earthy iris. Everything is engulfed by a flourish of grainy-lightweight vetiver, white musk, and a sharply lingering cedar finish. I wouldn’t call it fresh so much as simply dry, bitter, and devoid of any vegetal sweetness throughout development. I find it prickly and abrasive, attempting to wave the flag of elegance due to the absence of sweetness, and failing rather obviously due to a consistent rasping crudity of grainy bitterness, and an overly dry, harshly-abrasive lack of smoothness that is unrelieved throughout any stage of development. All in all, it’s rather like a mixture of insect repellent and furniture polish on my skin.

The aroma of tea in perfumes is not a favorite of mine, at least not if it changes over time and becomes almost tobacco-like. In The Beat it is so soft and modest, so it's really great. The more I smell this perfume the more I like it. Once it has settled down on the skin it is like a beautiful bouquet of flowers that one cannot stop smelling. I think that this is a perfect fragrance to use at work or if you are visiting someone who is not so fond of perfume scents. Very nice, very subtle and fresh and just a tiny bit powdery.

I love Dominique Ropion, but I tend to find his group collaborations less compelling than his solo work, much of which is masterful. Same for Béatrice Piquet, may she rest in peace. I definitely do not want to suggest that in Burberry THE BEAT there were too many cooks in the kitchen—this is certainly not an unwearable mess! But I do think that this composition falls squarely into a currently crowded category of the grand olfactory map. Among other close neighbors are Calvin Klein BEAUTY and DKNY PURE. THE BEAT edp is a clean musk composition with some florality and spice (cardamom) but not enough to really mark itself off as very distinct from the many other perfumes with similar compositions (albeit variations in the small details...). Another problem that I have with THE BEAT is my bête noire of dilution. I have used about half my roller ball cylinder (which I however have sprayed on, since I think that I get a better sense of a perfume through that means of application) in only two wearings. I generally dislike roller balls—with their childproof safety features making it impossible to overapply—but in this case all of the effort is for naught. Detach the roller and pour this liquid all over yourself: you will still not be over-perfumed. So, yes, the sillage is low and the longevity poor. All of that said, I'm sure that THE BEAT would work for those looking for inoffensive clean musk compositions with a slightly oriental quality. Although this fragrance is a tad bit sweet, some guys may like it as well.

I find it very difficult to find a Burberry fragrance that I don't like. If I had all the money in the world I would buy every single one of their fragrances, male and female. I was slightly off-put by the top notes which were a little too citrusy for me, yet the drydown caught me off guard and sent me spiralling into a state of love. The Beat is modern, eccentric and powerful. The scent can be sweet at times, but it never loses its sex appeal or transforms into something sickeningly sugary. I sense a coconut note for some strange reason, which makes me think that this fragrance is the perfect scent for a celebration. Perhaps it is also the bottle which is shaped like a flask that makes me think of a party-like atmosphere. This scent's only downfall was the lasting power, which shocked me because Burberry fragrances usually last for ages on my skin. The Beat unfortunately didn't last any more than an hour on me.

The Beat is a fresh fruity fragrance with a warm cardamom note. It does not change a lot during the hours, which are 6-7. Sillage is an arms length. I must admit that I like the bottle better than the scent, which is good but a bit ordinary. The bottle, however, is smooth and really nice. I do not remember when or from who I got it.

Am I really that easily impressed? Am I a sensitive soul? After multiple tests, I sit like a rabbit in front of the snake, anxiously awaiting the last drop of “The Beat” and practically wetting my pants out of fear. Holly’s version contains not just any fragrance. The Blob is in there. How so?

The spoiled stepsisters and the wicked stepmother rushed away. Cinderella sighed, then shrugged her shoulders and got to work - she could forget about the ball. Whistling, she sorted the grains thrown by the stepmother, swept the floor, and mopped it. Then a good fairy appeared at the window. She handed her a simple pink bottle. She conjured a beautiful dress for her.

Recently, I gifted my mother-in-law The Beat EdT because I liked it so much. I would have liked to keep it for myself - but one must also be generous. That's why I was pleased when The Beat appeared at a fair price at Rossi. Immediately grabbed a bottle - and at home - Oops! realized that it was the EDP. Would I like it just as much as the EdT?

Burberry Beat was a blind purchase for me. I already have several fragrances from Burberry and somehow found that they really know how to match my taste. That's why I had to get Beat on sale at the discount store for drugstore items. And I got lucky with this blind buy; I was not disappointed.

Bois Noir has been lost since the last century. When the scent does appear, it fetches exorbitant prices. Even empty bottles are almost unaffordable. The chance of encountering Bois Noir is vanishingly small, as it was only available for a short time exclusively at Chanel. Therefore, any comment can only be theoretically interesting and cannot be considered a guide for a purchase. Here is my personal story about this scent Yeti: I encountered Bois Noir in 1989 in the bathroom of my then Parisian weekend relationship. Since I already had a penchant for Chanel at that time, the bottle was secretly placed in my "beauty case" during our farewell. It was the last weekend with this charming gentleman, and thus a souvenir of a beautiful but brief time. Unfortunately, only the memory of this souvenir remains, as the empty bottle was lost during one of my moves. Now it would make no sense to write a comment about a scent impression that dates back so long. Especially since Bois Noir is stored in my memory as a scent of tightly woven components, which due to its complexity & opulence makes the identification of individual fragrance notes very difficult. The aforementioned narrow fragrance pyramid certainly does not list all the ingredients from which Bois Noir, the legendary predecessor of Égoiste, was created. Thanks to a dear friend from London - who generously left me a few drops of this rare essence - I am able to dare to make a comment. And now, boldly and without respect for the irretrievability of this essence, I quickly uncork the vial and dab it on my wrist - before I change my mind! To my dismay, the opening is clouded; evidently, time has taken a toll on the top note. The once green freshness, which came with the wood note of rosewood, rounded off with bergamot & mandarin, has been lost over the decades. Without citrus fruits, a herbal mustiness remains, which seems strange and foreign. I am already on the verge of despair when the moldy mustiness dissipates and familiar notes emerge. Now the scent reminds me of Scottish fruitcake that I love to bake during the Christmas season, albeit with a distinct dried plum note. There are spices to be smelled, primarily cinnamon and coriander. The accompanying gourmand sweetness is beautifully intertwined with flowers; the geranium, which many find disturbing, cannot assert itself, it merely softens the prominent rose without killing it. This gourmand cocktail claims the nose so much that only over the next hour can I slowly perceive a fragrance development. The fruitcake is now accompanied by vanilla tobacco, a diffuse smoky note reminiscent of Lapsang Souchong, and the remnants of rosewood and ample sandalwood come into play. This is the moment when Mr. Dorian Gray enters my fragrant thought world: before my mind's eye, the image of an opulent Victorian interior develops. A dim, high room with dark red wallpaper, through which only a little light of early noon penetrates, to vaguely illuminate precious rosewood and rosewood furniture with gilded fittings and exotic plants in blue and white Ming vases from the darkness. On the mantelpiece stand potpourri vases exuding rose fragrance made of antique Sèvres porcelain. A golden case with Turkish cigarettes lies on a delicate table, next to it a wafer-thin, exotically painted teacup with smoky tea, on whose saucer lie the remnants of carelessly crumbled fruitcake. On the chaise longue in front of the extinguished fireplace sits a handsome man, who scantily covers his nakedness with a silk bathrobe. He gazes mercilessly and unwaveringly at the bed with its florid carvings, waiting for the regular breath of a sleeping naked beauty, whose innocent features - as dreamed by a Pre-Raphaelite master - are still unaware of the doom that awaits her. In the base, the scent - entirely without kitsch - then becomes cozy: vanilla and tonka unite with the sandalwood to unfold in a floral-resinous depth, spiced with a small piece of leather. So much for the scent experience, now to the scent history and the little stories. Many rumors and tales surround Bois Noir and Égoiste. What are the differences in composition & scent progression, if they even exist? Compared to its successor Égoiste, I find that Bois Noir is denser and more intense in composition. It behaves in comparison somewhat like comparing an EdT and an EdP of a fragrance. The wood notes and the slightly sticky sweetness that we are familiar with from Égoiste are much more pronounced in Bois Noir. Even though the 80s have gone down in history as the decade of unrestrained hedonism and powerhouse scents, I can well understand that Bois Noir "flopped" at the time: I myself had difficulty finding occasions where I wanted to smell like Mr. Dorian Gray. Moreover, I think that the majority of gentlemen who found their way into a Chanel boutique back then preferred the conservative and universally wearable "Pour Monsieur." How did Chanel come up with the idea of launching a men's fragrance like Bois Noir? Jacques Polge explained in an interview that at that time, Chanel intended to realize a men's collection, while simultaneously wanting to launch a new men's fragrance. This would have had a synergy effect that would have benefited both endeavors: with a "young" Chanel scent for men, they could have excited fashion-interested gentlemen for Chanel menswear - and men's fashion would have boosted sales of men's fragrances as PR. So Monsieur Polge developed the men's fragrance Bois Noir, inspired by Bois des Îles, whose opulent sandalwood fascinated him. The idea of a men's collection was discarded, but Polge was allowed to put his fragrance into production. Allegedly, Bois Noir was such a hit that they came up with the idea of delighting the broad public with it - which I personally consider a fairy tale. For marketing reasons, Bois Noir was renamed Égoiste. However, Égoiste never became a big bestseller. J. Polge says nothing about the changes made. But it is more than likely that they took the opportunity to tone down the composition to make it mass-compatible - just as my nose has confirmed. Why not? After all, the broad mass of consumers never had a clue how Bois Noir smelled - they didn't even know of its existence. I myself owe it solely to happy circumstances that I encountered Bois Noir. Now I have reached the end of my comment, which should attempt to shed some light on the mystery of Bois Noir. When it comes to comments on rare, discontinued fragrances, there is often a hint of sadness and disbelief. Here, however, there is the option for a happy ending, simply buy J. Polge's favorite Chanel: ÉGOISTE.

Scentrack Suzanne Vega - Caramel Did Jaipur, the magnificent Indian Pink City get equally magnificent perfume version? YES... Jaipur Homme is a beautiful hidden, and perfectly cut perfume diamond made by Annick Menardo. Annick Menardo is one of my favorite perfumers. Her every perfume tells a story, and Jaipur is a fairy tale. Almost too good to be true. Jaipur opens up with soft Indian citrus fruits and then cardamom. The sunny Oriental refreshment is soon followed by cinnamon storm with benzoin lightings. Carnation in the middle gives some serious old school vibe, while rose and jasmine a fragile romantic heart. Tonka and vanilla are both responsible for the almost gourmand sweetness, but never becoming a true gourmand. I also feel the heliotrope which always livens up vanilla heavyweight perfumes. Behind this benzoin wall I sense some apricot and tobacco Southern sweetness. Jaipur shares some similarities with Givenchy Pi, but while Pi is a good scent Jaipur is a great perfume. Additionally, I sense the same benzoin theme shared with Menardo's Body Kouros. At the beginning Jaipur does possess some good old school qualities, associated with wealth and power. Oriental, but very clean (Nivea cream accord!!). Soon, it becomes more personal, gentle and balmy. Beautifully structured from top to base. Like it was covered with virtual star dust. Great idea materialized in Oriental golden drops. Often we look for something great on far more expensive places. No need, while Jaipur is here. In the example of Jaipur, useless is a classic designer / niche dichotomy. Rating: 10/10 More on Scentimentalwords

A spicy, floral powder bomb. Well-composed, but take the glowing reviews with a grain of salt. I find this extremely powdery, formal, and opulent to the point that I'm not comfortable wearing it. It also smells very feminine to my nose, particularly concerning the use of florals and their relation to the powder. If you love a good floriental, this will be right up your alley. However, while people rave about the beautiful vanilla dry down (especially in the EDP), keep in mind these other things I just mentioned before buying it blindly. Good fragrance but totally not my style and I think the casual, younger man may not like this at all. The EDP is dense, rich and more focused on vanilla. The EDT is spicier, lighter, develops more, and delivers a brighter heliotrope. In my opinion, it's much more interesting, and maybe even a bit more masculine.

For a long time I was not interested in oriental fragrances, until I met Boucheron Jaipur. It is warm and sweet. The "citrus" opening is discreet, then the spices (cinnamon !) and resin are durably in the foreground without being agressive. There is a background of floral and woody notes. It is oriental but without "pepper", it remains highly civilized (Jaipur, not the jungle). Longevity and sillage are really good in the EDT and excellent in the EDP. If you want something original for next Fall and Winter, try this one. It will warm you up !

I had never heard of Boucheron before i really got into fragrances. More or less i forced myself to be introduced to it, because i knew that Annick Menardo had created this one. I was under the assumption that this would be special, and boy was i entirely correct. Jaipur is sweet, but not candy-like in any way shape or form. It's woody without being dusty or irritating, and spicy without muting the other notes. A true work of art, and because of this scent i will be looking further into Boucheron. I have said it before, and i'll say it again. Annick Menardo is the master of refined sweet fragrances (body kouros, Xeryus rouge, LLAM,Fuel for life). Not regal enough to be a "dress up" only fragrance, and too well made to be a strictly casual creation. Jaipur, in my opinion, is great for a dinner, work or while hanging out with friends and family. The top: Is interesting, there is lime there no doubt, i find it hard to ignore once my nose latches onto it. Margarita esque, the lime in this composition almost has a "soaked in booze" smell to it. Cardamom in the top notes are very interesting, one doesn't often see them there, rather in the middle and base. By doing it this way i feel like there is much more character from the beginning (don't get this confused with being "front loaded"). Lemon and bergamot are clearly included in the top to cut it a bit, and to clean things up. Don't want things getting too bold too quickly! The heart: After sifting through a FOG of rich carnation, one may be able to start differentiating the middle of this fragrance. To sidetrack a second, i believe that the carnation in this fragrance is what gives it it's "fancy" qualities. Powdery jasmine co-operates together with cinnamon to sort of create a "pollen dusted earthy spice" accord. Very interesting and unique. One will also find rose, wich is paired perfectly with the strong carnation. Moist, innocent and sweet, rose makes up for many other notes rudeness. The base: Sunny, inviting patchouli is there to greet you warmly at the dry down. Strong, but not obnoxious the patchouli performs as a "binder" of sorts for the base, allowing all of the other accords a floor to stand on. Once ones nose smells past the patchouli the earthy, sweet tonka beans are thrown onto the soft wet sand to bake in the sun. Benzoin crystals are what add a soft of "at the beach" tone to this piece. I imagine a flower shop on the boardwalk. It may be the combination of the benzoin and cedar, i'm not too sure.

Hawa Mahal is situated at Badi Choupad, Pink City of Jaipur, and is also known as "Palace of Breeze." It was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, the grandson of Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh, who was the founder of Jaipur. It has 953 windows on the outside walls and is made with the red and pink sandstone. The honeycomb-shaped and beautifully carved windows allow the zephyr to blow through the palace and make it a perfect summer palace. Can you fancy a gentle breeze smelling like Jaïpur Homme that caresses you like a lullaby? Yeah, I guess I can. I was lucky enough to find both Jaïpur Homme and Boucheron pour Homme on an online site at a ridiculous price. I had been keeping an eye on them for some time, but I always wavered, having never had the opportunity to try them. Years ago I thought it smelled very oldfashioned and I didn't care for them. But in the end, I took them blindly. To begin with, Jaïpur Homme is a spicy oriental cologne that exists in both EDT and EDP concentrations, and today I'm going to review the EDT one. It is a precious little gem, and the cap represents a famous Boucheron ring named Boucheron Paris Jaipur Lapis Lazuli Cabachon 18k Gold Ring. It smells dusty, powdery, sweetish spicy, woody, and resinous. However, there is no one dominant spice you get but a beautiful mix of them all. The scent is perfect, especially for those who like colognes that are rich in spices. A hidden gem indeed. Not many people know about this masterpiece. The opening is hot and sweet, but not cloying in any means, aspect, or style. There is an exciting addition for the leading note cinnamon, and you can smell cinnamon powder in this one, which completely spices this jewel fantasy. It greats you with a royal cardamon, plenty of heliotropes, light citrus that last as a blink of an eye. The overall accord is somehow reminiscent of Givenchy PI, neither a clone nor a rip-off, merely sharing the same vibe and opening. Hence, a costly citrus-bergamot starting with cinnamon, nutmeg, and heliotrope, playing a remarkable role. The woody accord is gorgeous, majestic in every aspect of the word. After the start, the fragrance is a benzoin-centric strong poison. It grows on your skin and gets better and better hour after hour. The dustiness and powderiness are nostalgic of mama's Felce Azzurra talcum powder, for those who were accustomed to it. One will also find carnation, and I believe that in this fragrance is what gives it it's superior qualities. Moist, innocent, and sweet, the rose makes up for many other notes rudeness without turning this scent into an opulent Emirate rosy perfume. It goes down to the skin scent territory in about three hours, ain't vanilla cake. Yet, a vanilla powder maybe thanks to benzoin pairing. The dry-down is warm, sensual, and somewhat bitter. It turns to be delightfully powdery and woody with a consistent dose of vanilla, or tonka, according to the roaster, that's perfectly balanced and orchestrated never to become overwhelming or even dominant. Very rich, tremendously long-lasting, and even a bit loud but masterfully executed. Reminiscent of Ghivency PI, subtle powdery, and soft vanilla. Jaïpur Homme brought to my nose that familiar nice powdery, smooth, and the sweet vanilla note of PI, but the similarities ended there. The sophisticated and elegant structure, rich spices with comforting sweet notes, and bold projection make Jaïpur Homme perhaps one of the best examples of the male Orientals. But the similarities do not end here, cause Jaïpur Homme has that barbershop fill akin to Brut by Fabergé. Under some aspects, you might be reminded of Habit Rouge and Shalimar by Guerlain, and even Lolita Lempicka Au Masculin. Jaïpur Homme is sharing more than one similarity with the latter. Still, while the first turns to a dominant vanilla dry-down and the second surely exceeds in the gourmand aspect, it is perfectly balanced by the clever use of heliotrope. It has a little of each but is not equal to anyone. Jaïpur Homme is a Fall for the EDT, but I feel that early Spring is also an option. In contrast, Winter is for the EDP since it is more luxurious and slightly spicer. I wouldn't wear it in the heat since I tent to choose sweet fragrances this time of year (e.g., it's middle Winter now in Italy) and fresh ones in the warmer days. This fragrance can be worn day or evening, and I think it is more suitable for casual wear. This scent is relaxing and suits weekend downtime. Overall, I think if you are someone who considers themselves a nobleman, you should check Jaïpur Homme out. An excellent oriental composition in almost every sense of the word, it's woody without being vexatious, and spicy without muting the other notes. Annick Menardo mastered it, smooth as silk, not regal enough to be a dress-up only fragrance, and too well made to be a strictly casual creation. -Elysium

Classic french oriental. Sweet and elegant, that's a must have for oriental lovers. Suitable for colder days or nights. It remembers YSL Opium but less spicy. The fragrance is basically composed by some spices and some herbs very well blended with vanilla and benzoin at the base. Great lasting power and projection. Updated January 2014

This oldschool classic is still very relevant. Even suitable for someone in their 20s if they are brave enough to rock it. It smells sweet and spicy, almost like a gingerbread cookie. I would definitely say it is masculine. The price-value is fantastic, the bottle is classic but not outdated looking, the juice is outstanding. Very underrated gem for the fall/winter season.

Some fragrance ingredients electrify you, for me these are - among many other ingredients - pineapple, plums, heliotrope, pepper, clove, and cinnamon. Of course, it often doesn’t work out well. Either you don’t perceive the ingredients, feel them completely differently, or the scent doesn’t come together as hoped despite the appreciated ingredients.

... because this fragrance is neither too "heavy," meaning overly oriental, nor too "Western," meaning mass-compatible. Boucheron has achieved a clean and fine mélange here. Spicy-heavy, with rather many ingredients that never overdo it, but always stay within limits, pushing them to the utmost nonetheless.

My experience with Iris de Syracuse seems to reflect that of Littlegrassstraw. The opening is ever so lovely: a tenderly sweet woody iris, with a bit of starchy yet creamy, velvety texture. I don't perceive any earthy, metallic, carroty aspects of the iris. Iris de Syracuse at this stage, embodies the olfactory equivalent of an elegant pastel purple velvet gown. Unfortunately, once it starts to dry down after roughly 2 hours, its magic begins to wear off. A sweet ambery accord pervades the creamy iris, turning it into a candy iris with a tiny suggestion of lipstick, which reminds me of a less ambery dry down of Jacques Fath Bel Ambre. It's still lovely, but in comparison to the graceful opening, it feels rather generic and déjà-vu. The sillage is mostly close to the skin, and the longevity is around 8 hours. I thoroughly enjoyed Iris de Syracuse, especially that its velvety sweet woody iris opening imparts a sophisticated yet approachable elegance. The transition to the candy ambery iris is also quite subtle, making it mostly linear, easy to appreciate and versatile as well. However, because of the intense competition of many great iris fragrances, Iris de Syracuse, as lovely as it is, ultimately feels lack in personality and identity, a problem that impacts the whole range of Boucheron La Collection. Personally, I think there are other iris fragrances able to fulfilling a similar function as Iris de Syracuse, and with more personality and creativity as well. The high price and limited availability of Iris de Syracuse also don't help. All in all, if you love iris and would like to get hands on each and every one possible, or if you happen to be on a quest for slightly starchy and creamy sweet iris, Iris de Syracuse would be quite enjoyable to sample, even though I suspect that there are better and more affordable alternatives somewhere else.

Boucheron has an elegant line of perfumes that is seldom seen or discussed anywhere. This group of perfumes that refer to ancient cities and kingdoms, includes Iris de Syracuse, Oud de Carthage, Néroli d’Ispahan and many others. Part of the problem may be the complicated marketing and ownership arrangement between Inter Parfums and Boucheron. It is a shame really because Iris de Syracuse is a beautiful and powerful iris fragrance. This was created by Nathalie Lorson in 2017. The notes listed for Iris de Syracuse on the Inter Parfums website are black pepper, pear, iris concrete, heliotrope, patchouli and white musk. What you get with this perfume is a strong beautiful iris, with a few additional notes that feel like an afterthought. The opening note is obviously iris, displaying the well-known dual personality of this accord. You get a nice suede leather note as well the floral note. No wonder iris is a common note in men’s perfume. As expected, Iris de Syacuse has a shaving cream vibe in the opening. There are nuances of pepper and pear also in the opening, but these are totally overwhelmed by the suede and iris. I do not smell orange and vanilla anywhere in Iris de Syracuse. In the heart notes, the suede note subsides to elevate the floral iris, perhaps with some heliotrope. Heliotrope has overlapping characteristics with many other notes in this perfume, making it difficult to identify its unique presence. The base notes are musk and a bit of patchouli, with remnants of iris. Despite all the notes mentioned here, Iris de Syracuse is essentially iris all the way through. This perfume performs well on my skin. I get longevity lasting over eight hours, with a musky iris hanging on for longer. The sillage is nice in the opening hours, but not with any obnoxious projection. It is safe to wear this at office, though it may not turn heads at a party with other ambient smells. Boucheron Iris de Syracuse is a beautiful iris, worthy of a spot in any collection. The suede note tempers the floral attribute of iris, adding to the strong personality of this perfume. But keep in mind that this is a single-minded iris fragrance. I have no hesitation recommending this perfume, especially when it costs less than $80 at the discounters.

Why is no one talking about this fragrance line? After that stunning patchouli, now there's this noble iris. I’ve tested it multiple times and honestly, it’s made it into my top 3 iris scents ever. I’m seriously in love with it — it’s warm, radiant, and full of character. It’s smooth, soft, and has this effortless elegance that never gets boring. It opens fresh and powdery, then slowly melts into something softer, more velvety… with a gorgeous base that’s slightly powdery and earthy, but still super refined and delicate. This iris is something truly special. B e a u t i f u l.

In my garden, a white iris grows. On its petals are pearls from the last rain, and when the first rays of sun fall on it, I have the image for this scent. The iris, first dry, then juicy, with minimal fruits, later refreshing like rain, with a delicate musk. We have one of those long, hot summers, not like this year so far, but really hot and dry, for a long time. Nature is thirsting for rain. Even the nights bring no coolness. But today it should happen, the clouds are gathering, but it’s dragging on... I sit on the balcony, no thought of sleep, and then this scent comes... A first movement of the air, a leaf, that moves, and then a breeze... A gentle wind, carrying the scents of summer. It no longer holds me on the balcony, I go down into the garden, and the first drops fall... quietly... plop.... One moistens my eyelashes, I catch the second with my tongue... there are more... Faster and faster... The musk rises like steam, as the rain moistens the hot tar road. Light... Gentle... I take off my shoes, and start to dance in the rain. It is warm and yet so refreshing. The drops run down my face, the blouse soaked, clinging to my body. And I sing and dance... barefoot 'Raindrops keep falling on my head.... https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hziG9Nr6KHU And the air smells fresh and damp. I smell the iris, delicate fruits, underlaid with soft musk. Everything is much more intense and refreshing and feels good.

Here it is again, the paper iris - I can hardly smell anything, so I spray the strip again properly. I wonder if iris feels lonely without its violet; or at least without something delicious and sweet to nibble on to combat the boredom. Keyword: compensation.

The scent appears to me unsweetened, powdery-creamy, musky, mature, and unique in its character. Fresh-spicy pepper with a sour-citrusy mandarin and a hint of pear conceal one of the most beautiful powdery iris notes on this earth. So much powder like a fine, white endless sandy beach. One wants to fall into it and let the sand trickle through their fingers.

In Syracuse, the indigo blue sea meets the azure blue sky. Dionysus, the cheerful, very hairy, and well-fed party god of Greek Olympus, has just arrived on this side of the Sicilian island. (The Romans have not yet discovered Sicily as an important and strategic point for themselves.) He wants to find a fertile spot for his followers and groupies.

From the data sheet, exactly my type: powdery, warm vanilla, delicate flowers, earthy and woody. Sounds good for a winter scent. Marketed as unisex and available since 2017. If you like iris, this fragrance is just right for you. Warm, feminine with a hint of musk. This fragrance developed too much warmth and too much musk on my skin.

Tuberose opens the heart of the fragrance with a buttery sweetness delicate note of jasmine gives an herbal feel and smell Narcissus dominates the middle notes almost drowning the others into obillvion with it's deep and intoxicating scent Lily of the Vally is the elusive note of all i can't dectect, the drydown to the ending sweetish with amber patches of musk and traces of Civet for animalitic properties Benzoin note makes the perfume a bit milky and resianious; the finishing notes of sandalwood adds the dryness and vanilla with it's powdery sweetness.

Boucheron EdP is a classical beauty from the 80s that always makes me think of the most expensive lush velveteen cream with a citric vibe. Amber, orange, jasmine and vanilla are the first notes that charm my nose and make me feel elegant, irresistible and cozy. It's a comforting scent yet makes you feel very feminine and beautiful without that it feels like the perfume is wearing you. Boucheron has this rare quality that blends with your chemistry to enhance your natural beauty, rather than overwhelm you with a force-field of scent. It's a true modern-classic that is very well blended and will enchant most women and seduce many men. A must sniff/own for every Perfumista for those moments that you want to wear something that embraces you in a feeling of classy, soft beauty. A Crimson velvet cape of sexy and warm "Hmmm". Silage is: "An aura of warm, elegant & inviting beauty." -- Longevity is: Amazing with on me 6+ hours in which it warms up and gets more amber-like. Simply YUM!

The previous reviewers all over the web that highly praise this scent are definitely written by people with excellent taste in fragrances. Boucheron is a scent which defines sophistication, elegance and class. A rich, unmissable fragrance that doesn't have the popularity that it deserves. I spent many months searching for this particular fragrance, and only managed to find the EDT concentration in an exclusive fragrance boutique. I was highly impressed by the EDT, and when I read that the EDP is even more impressive, I can't help being dumbfounded by this scent. Boucheron is everything that a fragrance should be; complex, unique, intense and memorable. This fragrance has been created with the upmost care, blended beautifully, resulting in a rich, warm and feminine scent. The top notes are not your typical nose-burning citruses and fruits, they have all been blended perfectly creating a scent that is inviting and interesting. Vanilla makes it's presence known right from the very beginning. It's the combination of the vanilla mixed with the lemon, orange and basil and then with the floral accords in the heart of this scent, that fascinates me in so many ways. In no way is this fragrance dusty and 'old-smelling'. To describe this fragrance as being suited only to mature aged women is very misinformative. Any woman that loves this fragrance should be able to pull this off, it's not restricted to any age group. Everything from the scent to the bottle is clearly elegant and sophisticated, making this scent perfect for those strict formal events and occasions. It's such a shame that this fragrance isn't more readily available in my country, although I have heard that where it is available, it sells extremely well. Classic, Boucheron most certainly is. Expensive, but well worth the money spent. The lasting strength is guaranteed to be a highlight as it lasts well into the next day and clings to your clothes for days, managing to scent your wardrobe with its rich aroma. I highly recommend this fragrance and advise people that have not tried this scent to "get thee to a tester immediately", this perfume is not to be missed.

I reached for Boucheron and oh....it smells so good, I have been out today so I used a not to heavy hand, but now I am back home and Now I used my heavy hand, I enjoy so much the beautiful cloud of this fragrance around me...

10 years after discovering Boucheron EDT, I decided to try the original EDP. Yes, these are 2 separate productions. Both are large, dramatic epics composed of the same ingredients. If you know one, you will immediately recognize the other. However, they are like looking through a telescope with different lenses. EDP is stronger and you experience a lot more details. When this hit the market in 1988, we remember this as the apex of major releases of the 1980s. Samsara and Boucheron were at the top of the line. We are talking about the biggest releases of the decade of giants. Here in the USA , everyone knew Samsara. Boucheron was never really marketed among Elizabeth Taylor Passion or Giorgio. Hence, I never experienced Boucheron on an individual. By the time the decade closed, this grand style of fragrance was quickly becoming yesterday's news. Boucheron would not be forgotten. I fact, it became quite popular as the white floral began its second act in the 1990s. White Diamonds to Versace Blonde all fell under the shadow of Boucheron. This is a royal class composition from a well established jeweler the was willing to spare no expenses in this lavish production. The EDP seems to hail from another time. You can imagine the "powdered wig crowd" using this in pre revolutionary France. Its a bit like Bal A Versaille with more flowers. That understates this majestic and enigmatic masterpiece. She is fussy, sophisticated and difficult to wear on most occasions. Yet, there the same warm underlayer that seduces and whispers other to come closer. As a man, Boucheron wears me. I love the drydown, yet the florals are difficult except on the coldest nights. The EDP is much more floral with the tuberose leading the pack. Its done beautifully, can last in your skin until your next shower. Amber and sandalwood dance with the powdery iris with a perfume experience you will never forget. One bottle is not enough.

Orange blossom & tuberose bubblegum; lifted by tart, green, woody and spicy notes. A typical 80’s confection, the juice - a Cyndi Lauper shade of auburn - tells you what it’s about, even before it's left the bottle. This is for those girls (and guys – why not) who just wanna have (a) fun (perfume).

I discovered Boucheron in autumn 2021. It convinced me with its familiarity; it reminds me of my childhood. An intimate form of security, I feel transported back, floating in nostalgia: spices, powder, soap, fabric softener, church on Sunday, grandmother's mahogany vanity, the scent of her cosmetics, freshly baked cake, Elizabeth Taylor on the cover of a housewife magazine.

GABRIELLE CHANEL reminds me of a house in a white flower field. In this flower field, there is a clothesline with freshly washed and still damp bed sheets. It is a fragrance that builds around four flowers. Exotic and intense jasmine, ylang-ylang with fruity notes, fresh orange blossom, and velvety, feminine tuberose. The scent smells fresh, it is clean floral, powdery, subtly resonating with a citrus note. Somehow, it also reminds me of shampooed hair. What else can I say? I love this fragrance.

Sampling Boucheron Ambre d’Alexandrie, a saccharine but slightly animalic amber fragrance, a vanillic amber with hints of spices, ambergris, and musk. It’s a bit sharp and heady while also being sweet, with some of the depth of the amber being supplanted by spices. Still, there’s a slight animalic side underlying the dominant sweetness. Overall, it’s just a bit too much treble, not enough bass as a resinous fragrances go. In the US, Ambre d’Alexandrie is available for $114 for 125ml on FragranceNet, though retail pricing via Harrods in the UK is $210. It seems to perform pretty well and is very nice to try. I bought a sample off of FragranceNet. 7 out of 10

A sublime perfume for which I fell in love immediately! It's a warm amber coupled with a fruity shisha tobacco and a nice dose of cinnamon. There is also a liquorous side and I am pretty sure there is rum here. This fruity tobacco and cinnamon combination gives an impression of apple pie but we are here very far from the ultra sweet result that Angels'Share offers; it’s delicate and perfectly measured. In reality I find it better than Ambre Narguilé which I find low in dosage and better than the Kilian, which I find too "pastry". Truly superb.

Here we have it! The flagship, the C-weapon, or also the Death Star of Boucheron. One from the sixth series of the new collection. An amber scent that packs a punch. Extremely delicious, extremely rich, and extremely long-lasting. That can certainly be said. A small spritz on my wrist from the tiny sample lasted for several hours, including three hand washes. Ambre d'Alexandrie is so durable and resistant that it has truly impressed me. It is the strongest of the entire collection. So much for that! So how does it smell? Well,... it has a little twin that is familiar to almost all of us. This little, weak, and not inexpensive scent twin resides in our bathroom. It is preferred during the pre-Christmas season. In my opinion, this label produces completely overpriced handbags and luxury leather goods. Admittedly, I have a few of them, but they were gifts from Mrs. Can. She is an absolute fan of the label. This particular scent twin was even gifted to her by me. Because it smells so deliciously of apple pie with cinnamon and vanilla sauce. And it is from H-e-r-m-e-s. Which scent twin could that be? Naaaaa?,....Bingo,....Ambre Narguilé. But with Ambre d'Alexandrie, everything is immensely amplified. It's like Godzilla versus Maya the Bee. This scent just oozes power and endurance. It smells delicious, even extremely delicious in my opinion, but it smells like Ambre Narguilé. That's it! OK!,....I'll give it another exciting description. It smells like a huge, gigantic, and warm gourmand apple pie, from which cinnamon-sweet-spicy steam rises. Bubbling and delicious vanilla pours over it and combines with buttery soft amber into a spicy-smoky and enticing delicacy. So?,... how was that? Delicious, right? Conclusion Longevity: From one solar eclipse to the next. So long! Sillage: It can go through walls. So strong! Gender: Unisex. We all love sweet things. But one must really want it. A deliciously fragrant opulence monster to love and cuddle. Highly concentrated in longevity and aura. Delicious and indescribably tasty.

. And here we go with strong fruit. And sweetness. Fruit basket with raisins. You could believe it. . Then a push into the cream, with heavy bergamot that could be a bit fresher, capturing the whole macchia with cistus. Labdanum brings in the amber and benzoin gives the crown. . A very rich fragrance, almost like under a rose arch. Medium brown amber with a soft melt. In its powerful wearability, a composition that becomes darker over time. . It rises strongly into the round and builds up into the round. Powerful vanilla, entwined with the balsamic amber. It lasts. Almost a bit coarse, almost a bit heavy. It has to be like that sometimes. I like it. 9.0 . And if you use it sparingly, you might like it, just like I do. .

At first, one can perceive an intense sweet - creamy Bourbon vanilla, stirred for so long that only the cream - foam remained and was skimmed off. At the same time, the vanilla merges with a large, sweetly - fruity appearing, "dense" Golden Delicious apple, harvested at just the right time, evoking the image of an apple pie filled with vanilla, which I attribute to the shisha smoke. In the background, there is a very fine and warming balsamic hint of milk chocolate, leading one to feel that next to the cake stands a cocoa, whose scent wafts into the nose, thanks to the benzoin. This constellation is perceptible on my skin for 30 minutes before the heart note unfolds. The Bourbon vanilla in the heart note is slightly dimmed but still very clearly perceivable and unites with a fine - bright, yet deeply sweet, slightly viscous nuance that smells of "flower honey," giving the fragrance a captivating charm and comes from labdanum. The labdanum is enveloped by an incredibly beautiful, snug, and cozy sweet - spicy note that is hard to resist, even evoking a longing for love, stemming from the amber accord. The heart note is perceptible on my skin for 5 hours before the base asserts itself. In the last 3 hours, Ambre d' Alexandrie becomes very clear and pure - sweet thanks to the musk, without reminding one of freshly washed laundry, receiving a smooth resinous touch from the amber, behind which a very subtle smokiness hides, beautifully rounding off the fragrance. Ambre d' Alexandrie is a wonderful companion in the spring, autumn, and winter months for both women and men of all ages who are looking for a gourmand sweet, creamy, spicy, and resinous fragrance that possesses a longing-inducing charm. Overall, the fragrance lasts 8 hours on my skin. The sillage is designed in the first 2.5 hours so that one is perceived very clearly up to 3 meters away and then settles for 2 hours at a very noticeable full arm's length before it reduces in minimal steps until the fragrance fades away. I would like to express my sincere thanks to our Parfumo "Verbaplex" for the sample.

I will say that although I truly did enjoy this fragrance, I have to admit I pondered on if this scent would be better as a room mist or in a diffuser. I'm not sure I'd want to wear it on me daily due to its VERY fragile nature and evanescent performance. The price is also pretty steep, even for a cologne. I do get why it's beloved by many and I agree it's a staple in the blue fragrance family. A fragrance that conjures beautiful images of relaxation and vacation; like taking a walk by the sea. I sense a citrusy top note even though it's not listed anywhere, soon followed by a sweet, but salty skin type of scent. Drydown becomes a bit more herbal and aromatic due to the sage, but it overall stays true to its name. It has a certain warmth to it I wasn't expecting, but also remains fresh and uplifting at the same time. A steep price and abyssmal performance (both for the sillage and longevity on skin) is why it won't be making it into my collection. I do agree thoguh that it's a very pretty fragrance and in aromatherapy, smelling this one would make me want to relax and enjoy myself by taking a walk along the beach shore.

This fragrance is an amazing unisex scent. It combines minerals, spice & aquatics & some how makes it classy. . I also, for the life of me, will not understand why everyone says it has weak performance. This fragrance isn't NUCLEAR but it doesn't make it weak. I put it on today at 12:30pm. & we're going towards 4:30, & it's still very present on my skin. It may last longer on the skin than the cloths but I'd have to test that theory. For instance, I put it on today & layered it/combined it somewhat with Kilian Vodka on the Rocks. & I gave both their own top of my hand spray. Kilian on the left hand & Jo Malone on the right hand. & here we are 4 hours later, the Wood Sage & sea salt very much present on My hands, was catching whiffs of it until about 30mins ago. Which means it projected for about 2-3 hours, to some degree. The Vodka on the rocks, I can still smell on my hand but it is much more faint & a tad harder to pick up thoroughly. I also stopped catching whiffs of it about an hour or two ago. It projected for about an hour or so. I bring this up because on this site, Vodka on the Rocks is said to have better longevity than this fragrance & I disagree, at least for the day time. & this isn't the first time I've thought that. . The musky dry down on this fragrance is wonderful & a lot of people think it leans slightly more feminine but I think it's pretty 50-50. It works for a man with confidence too & it's a great situational fragrance. Summer vacation, a weekend get away to Nantucket or a "all white" outfit party in the Hamptons. Could even work for a day time wedding. Enjoy this in summer/spring even maybe a nice, easy fall day. . It's Saturday afternoon in a bottle for those memorable days

Wood Sage & Sea Salt is a breezy, elegant escape to windswept shores and salty cliffs. The marine accord blends effortlessly with mineral rich sea salt and earthy sage, evoking the feeling of ocean air and untamed nature. It's fresh yet grounding, clean yet warm, perfect for those who crave a scent that feels both effortless and sophisticated. A coastal retreat in a bottle.

Truly reminds me of my summers in brittany as a kid. It has the same smell as the peach tea we drank on the beach, that was a bit too warm because of the sun and also salty because of the remains of the sea on our lips after bathing. People on fragrantica pointed out a grapefruit note that I could definitely smell and I loved it. It smells clean, coastal and nice but definitely didn't last for long. I'd rather go to a beach during the summer and come back with that same smell.

Wood Sage & Sea Salt opens with a brightly illuminated explosion of grapefruit. This grapefruit is happy, energetically awakening the senses and saturating them in sunshine. An exceptional way to start a beach inspired fragrance. So far, so good. A lively citrus can also bring to mind sensual tropical islands, dotted with palm trees, but certainly not the pebbly, chilly beaches of England that they are trying to evoke. As the fragrance progresses, the sharp citrus note mellows and a layer of herbal sage is conjured up. This adds a pleasant sweet and savory accord, not unlike the beginning to a fantastic marinade. Wait a minute, I think my trip to the beach just got hijacked to Italy. How about some English flora like sea kale, thrift, dune helleborine, alexanders or perhaps yellow whitlow grass. I’m thinking that “Wood Thrift and Sea Salt” might have been more interesting as well as a more regionally accurate concept for this English beach inspiration. While the smell of thrift might not be as intoxicating as the smell of sage, the pretense has conceptual context. Back to the fragrance at hand. Wood Sage & Sea Salt’s heart launches with the introduction of a blonde, sun-baked driftwood vibe. This wood is desiccated, aromatic and perfect for what one might experience beachside. An enticing fruity, savory blend layered with an intensely dry wood note does create intrigue. Once a bit of surf is added with sharp sea salt, it wraps up this interesting harmony. Last but not lease, ambrette seed gives the fragrance a slightly musky note, adding a bit of nature to this otherwise unoccupied beach. Wood Sage & Sea Salt’s light aromatic nature, diffusing and clarifying, offers a nicely rounded finish. While I really enjoyed Wood Sage & Sea Salt, I think the ad campaign’s conceptual strategy is confusing. Many people are well-read enough or, if lucky, well-traveled enough to understand the concept of the English seaside. As we all know, grapefruit nor more grows in England that mangoes grow in northern Minnesota. Jo Malone’s English beach-themed fragrance seems to be a bit of a stretch at best. Speaking of stretches, sage on the English beachside. Is this idea not just another oxymoron in Wood Sage & Sea Salt’s personality? Enough of all of this nonsense, let’s just remove the word “English” from the concept. This would make Wood Sage & Sea Salt a more generalized beach experience instead. It might give this fragrance a more universally acceptable idea for anyone who’s ever been to any beach in their life.

I love this scent but it’s way overpriced for an eau de cologne, and not even an EDP! Wood Sage and Sea Salt sits so close to the skin, it’s difficult to smell unless you constantly have your wrist to your face. The longevity is also extremely poor! It disappears so quickly. This just isn’t worth your hard earned cash!

This fragrance I wore yesterday for the first time so share some thoughts I had on it so far. I had a replica of this fragrance from a different company awhile back and quite liked it, especially as a lighter fragrance for the day, so I wanted to try the real deal as I have started my fragrance journey.

Let's go down the line. Parfumo says the top note is ambrette seeds. If I Google that, it's all over the map: "sweet, musky, animalic, often fruity or nutty, soft, warm, sensual, powdery, floral or woody." Well, after wearing it a while (not too long, because it really doesn't last, hubby answered my request to describe what he smelled with, "I smell sexy.

A blind purchase. I imagined something like a skin smell, with a fresh, slightly citrusy, animalic and aromatic touch. But I didn't feel any of that. What I felt was a creamy, half-solar scent, with a fruity output that actually reminded me of the fig note that I have already felt in several perfumes.

I was gifted a few miniatures from Jo Malone and I often find something to be very synthetic or unimpressive about them. There are many fragrances that can and have executed this fresh, aquatic seaside scent better. Especially considering the price point, this fragrance isn't really special, but it does become better as it dies down.

Now that the warmer days have finally arrived, I am testing Chance Eau Fraîche Eau de Toilette and Chance Eau Fraîche Parfum Cheveux in parallel. In comparison, I actually find it almost more beautiful, as it has more sweetness and a certain powderiness that I miss a bit in the edT. Also, wearing it in the hair enhances the sillage on warm (sweaty) days and significantly improves the personal perception. It stays fresher and more citrusy in my hair for longer than the edT does on the skin and drifts into the woody notes much later. Citrus and a light cedar open up. It remains refreshing/sparkling due to the pepper, but already gets the first cuddle factor. After a good 4 to 5 hours, a light sweetness remains, which grounds Vetiver and Patchouli. And then I spray again :-D A lovely refreshment, for sure!
