The way this performs in an intimate setting and carries in the air, even I find myself enjoying it. Cocoa complimenting touches of orris powder and a really lovely smoky woody aroma. It’s semisweet, a little dry (but not dusty) and creamy, with touches of the spiciness throughout. This scent makes me feel… Good. I spray this, inhale, and the cloud of calm that comes over me is wonderful, and for a solid 8 hours I enjoy this calm confidence. Well worth giving this a sampling at your local beauty/dept stores if you haven’t. I’m almost through a 100ml bottle in under a year and will definitely be buying this again.

I had already seen this EDP boisee actually cheaper than the straight EDP and EDT on a site i used as a price reference. I think it is a pretty pleasant surprise having smelled it yesterday and thinking it reminded me of a fragrance in particular, for some time i couldn't tell which one it was, though. And then it just popped into my mind: OG CH MEN!!! I guess the sugar / leather combo on that one which to me gives kind of the ilussion of smelling a fine chocolate put inside a leather bag, is quite similar to an accord here in Gentleman EDP boisee. I assume, the cacao, woods, orris and smoke make the ilussion of that. A slightly sweet pretty sexy aroma. bottom line: I have heard some reviews on other sites saying that the Gentleman line lacks a DNA representative of itself. I think it is not the case, all modern (And even the vintage has some of that) Gentlemans have a common leather and sweetness, warm spicy, iris kinda DNA. boisee is no exception.

Tested inside a shop and i confirm: cocoa gave tha amazing part, so different from the normal givenchy. I liked so much, i never had doubt on this. It is for elegant and also mature men, recommended, not for young because of the smoky part but it is very a good change from each others from the givenchy line. if you like misterious men this is nice for a gift or for your husband. I do not prefer designer parfume as personal taste but this one you should try. Longevity is okey, but not a 10 i suppose, it may be an 8.

This is a great fragrance, Spicy, Woody, Floral, Warm and Seductive. My wife bought this perfume for me as a Gift, before she asked me what fragrance do you like? I said Givenchy Reserve Privee, She tried both of them and bought Boisee for me , Now I love it. It opens up with warm spicy, floral and Cacao notes in the background then dry down is earthy, floral woody. The Orris, The Black Pepper and burning wood notes are dominant in this scent. I really enjoy it and I'm so happy that I have it in my collection. Longevity is good. Thumbs Up. Rating : 7.5 / 10

This one definitely gains some depth on skin. Beautiful, clean iris with a woody base, but different from other iris scents I've tried. Very unique. Wouldn't recommend for warmer days though, it can get cloying. I tried it on a hot day for the first time and regretted the purchase for a while, until I used it again on a colder, rainy day.

One of my favourites for the colder weather. Light but complex scent because of the cacao, little bit powdery iris, the various wood and the spicy opening. I find it sweet & vanillic personally, maybe because of the cacao in it. It's intoxicating to me. Not the strongest but it last long and projects just enough.

This fragrance from the Gentleman Givenchy line was a pleasant surprise for me. I've never been particularly interested in the line, but the blend of iris and cocoa in this scent is unique and intriguing. Both notes are equally present, and the fragrance avoids feeling too floral or lipstick-y due to the grounding effect of sandalwood and a touch of cedar.

One of my favourites so far it smells amazing. I would use this fragrance every time I'm a bit better dressed (work, date, meeting, drink) etc. This fragrance It s a bit dry mixed with this perfect woody/spicy touches with a sweet finish making me feel confident. The first impressions about longevity are good but as skin scent.

Gentlemen Boisee is the flowery, woody addition to the Gentleman line of fragrances by Givenchy, but it would be rude to just stop there. It has a lot going for it and not a single aspect that can be called bad, although it is not perfect either. The bottle and atomizer are great, with the price also being decently affordable.

I like beige, pink, and white flacons. I also enjoy scents like J'adore Eau de Parfum and the like - on the test strip and, for example, on a good friend. But unfortunately, often not on me because a) they either contain vanilla as a note (yuck yuck yuck) or b) they turn terribly cloying on my pesky skin. These subtly elegant, minimally floral creations, which are almost reminiscent of rather expensive body lotions, are just so beautiful. They don’t have to be overpowering; I don’t want to cause headaches for my office colleague in our small two-person office, and sexy doesn’t have to be a priority in that context either. I’m looking for Grace Kelly in a beige blazer and white blouse for the office. I’ve been using Eternity Eau de Parfum since the 90s and I particularly like it in the summer; it’s a bit greener and fresher. Eau Fresh has this pink creaminess that makes it feel a bit more feminine and elegant. Yet it still remains fresh and sporty in some way. As I said, it’s more suited for the office than a candlelit dinner. Pear is nonexistent on my skin; in general, I hardly perceive the top note, as the flowers almost immediately take over, but they remain moderate. The sillage is also moderate, but that’s okay; who wants to walk through the halls like a scent comet? I find the longevity for an EdT to be about 3-4 hours (better on clothing!) and then it lingers closer to the body for even longer. In small rooms or during the first hour, it is still perceptible to those around me, but remains discreet. My mentioned office mate immediately remarked, "Mmm, your body lotion smells great." I find the prices of Calvin Klein fragrances to be excellent. I don’t have to pay over €80 for 50ml out of principle, under the crazy assumption that only then would something olfactorily acceptable be found on the shelf. I won’t elaborate much on the flacon; it won’t win any beauty awards, but it’s not ugly either, simple and uniform, and somehow fits the understated main theme (and hey, it’s space-saving!) Eau Fresh has become my all-purpose weapon for daytime use; only in very warm temperatures do I prefer something more citrusy, as it becomes too floral/creamy for me. But for spring/fall/winter (in NRW, it’s pretty much a constant temperature), it works perfectly.

If you have Her Elixir, which 'replaced' this as an "intense" flanker, you don't need this one. I agree with the medicinal notes others mention, I think due to the benzoin-berry blend... and it is more amber-y than I prefer. But, if you know you like Her *and* you prefer amber-rich scents, this would be worth it. I'm glad I tried it but I'm going to stick with the more lactonic and less-medicinal Elixir.

Well, hello there! This one really packs a punch! Finally, I have no reason to complain about the H&S when it comes to a fragrance. I’ve already made a statement, but I still feel the need to elaborate! I sprayed it on Saturday morning at 7 and it got to accompany me on my furniture shopping spree. And I must say, it showed more endurance during shopping than my husband. But that's really not saying much. Upon spraying, I smell, just like with the Her edp, strawberries. No blackberries, raspberries, or any other berries, just strawberries. I'm already happy that I can specifically pick this out. While the Her edp now develops a somewhat soapy-artificial (hairspray) note that I quite like, the Intense goes all in and supports the berry opening with a warm floral bouquet (according to the pyramid, jasmine) but nothing cloying or overwhelming, it simply serves to refine and enhance the berry sweetness. And it lasts and lasts and lasts. Well into the afternoon, then the fragrance takes a turn, transforms into butter-caramel, and smells simply delicious enough to bite into. I probably always associate the caramel scent with benzoin. At least from my perspective. So dreamy and elegant. I could still perceive it on me at 1 AM, and not exactly quietly. Other fragrances could take a few notes from this one! Okay, I smell like a sweet treat now, but I never feel uncomfortable with it. The scent is designed in such a way that it just fits. It also doesn’t cause any nausea, which can happen with some others. It has sillage, but although it clings to me like glue, it's anything but unpleasant! My husband certainly hasn’t claimed otherwise or dared to! No one complained at the office today either. It seems to have a connection with my skin chemistry! At least I hope so! :-D I can’t answer the question of whether it comes close to BR540. Unfortunately, I haven’t tested it yet, but I will soon. Although I’m still hesitant due to the ambivalence regarding the scent perception. I’ve had Cloud by Ariana Grande before and must say that it also smells similar. But by no means as rich, and certainly not as long-lasting as this magnificent specimen here. Absolutely no comparison. The design of the bottle is okay. But that’s not important to me in light of the content! I hope I could bring it a bit closer to you. A test for all sweet tooth lovers must be in order!

While strolling through the flea market, my fragrance dealer approached me and pressed Her Intense into my hand. "This is something for you," were her conspiratorial words. She knows me, as I belong to the regular clientele. However, I am not allowed to test there. But I was familiar with Her EdT and I like it a lot. So I wrapped up the Intense. At home, the reveal. Her Intense is truly intense - and also has an intense sweetness. But before it becomes too much of a good thing, it takes a turn towards the smoky - very pleasant and interesting. Moreover, the jasmine softens the blackberry sweetness, giving it a touch of elegance. The longevity is also good, and I am glad that my dealer recommended this fragrance to me.

Today I got to know Burberry. And this is a classic jam made from red berries in the most delicious sense of the word. So when you cook the jam and it starts to boil and thicken, a frothy film forms on the surface. It is airy and sweet. That's exactly what you try with a spoon... very carefully you blow on it and dive in :-) The jam foam will stretch a bit and stick to your teeth. At the bottom of the pan, the jam got a little burnt and a faint bitter smell lingered in the air. * I don't hear any jasmine (to my regret). And as for the benzoin, I have no idea :-) But when you press your nose directly to the skin, there is a note that is strange. As if a beetle is sitting on a huge beautiful raspberry. But for the aromatic flavor, one can endure not just the little pest, but much much more :-).... maybe that's the benzoin? But overall, it is a red, sweet, and transparent jam syrup with berries on top.

We know that Francis Kurkdjian creates wonderful scents, especially after Baccarat Rouge 540. It’s not a dupe, but it has that certain something that almost all Kurkdjian fragrances have. It is sweet and fruity, reminding me of some kind of candy. You can perceive the blackberry, but I would say it’s more of a forest fruit mix, with raspberry and others. Even a hint of jasmine occasionally shines through. For layering, I can very well imagine Jardin Bohème Episode Romantique. Absolutely delicious, and the sillage and longevity are great. Perhaps a bit too dominant for everyday wear, but perfect for going out.

Burberry Her Intense... so often I showed you no interest, so many times I would have strolled past you... And then there was the nice saleswoman who held a test strip under my nose. And just like that, you had my full attention. The scent starts sweet and fruity. It actually reminds me of the raspberry candies that wonderfully ruin your palate.

Very, very elegant formulation - It has the vibe of the purple Skittle in a very noble form! ? You can't even compare it to Baccarat, only the sparkling quality is shared. Baccarat smells only slightly sweet to me, not in the direction of cotton candy to my nose.

The scent description and bottle intrigued me. So I sprayed it hopefully on my wrist. Fruity, sweet, alluring. I was enchanted. Only to sniff it again after a very short time and be deeply disappointed. Some component gives me a headache. Just the thought of being exposed to this fragrance for a longer period makes me uneasy. What a shame.

Admittedly, the vibe is there - but I can't smell a dupe here. Much more, you immediately perceive the blackberry, or rather a berry mix, sweet raspberry candies. At first sniff, it’s somewhat synthetic, but that changes with the jasmine. It is rounded off by benzoin, hence the delicious vanilla scent. A warm, sweet, and slightly plush fragrance that feels cozy.

I bought the scent like many before me, because it comes from the perfume god Kurkdijan and - as we know - is supposed to resemble BR540. I understand that the vibe is similar, but not really. I clearly miss the fullness and complexity of BR540; I wouldn't call Burberry Her Intense a dupe - BUT the scent is still an absolute dream, surprisingly good, warm with a special twist.

Utterly lovely, a wonderfully balanced, refreshing composition. This is meant to evoke the pleasure experienced when drinking a nice cup of Earl Grey tea. Christine Nagel managed to capture the smell of bergamot and jasmine without "overdoing" it. The fragrance offers a delicate impression rather than a loud and strong version of "Earl Grey". Bergamot can be felt in the topnotes, of course, whereas jasmine gradually emerges quite shyly on a bed of slightly aquatic notes mixed with apple. The drydown is lovely, too, with cedar and musk. Well, there's just one little drawback: In the true Jo Malone-style, "Early Grey&Cucumber" is an Eau de Cologne, so it stays close to the skin and has little sillage. This said, it is still a wonderful scent that will have people around you sniffing the air with pleasure for the first 10 minutes after application (think of your bathroom). I used this as a pick-me-up fragrance for early mornings and had a 30 ml bottle, but I wouldn't mind owning a 100ml flacon of this gem!

perfectly catching the moment of opening a fresh tin of loose earl grey tea. it's strong and punchy at first, almost suffocating, but within 5 seconds it settles into the most soothing, realistic experience of getting yourself a strong cup of the tea. i can't imagine not having this in my collection - as a tea lover, i use it as my layering multitool. really, the amount of combinations it fits into is just unreal. whether it is to bring in more tea asset into other tea scents that just don't have enough of power in that note (russian tea and o, unknown, i'm looking at you two specifically...), or just creating different scent profiles such as fruity tea, milky tea, floral tea - it's just a magic item. i could go on for days, listing all of my favourite combinations, so i encourage y'all to just try it out and experiment. one thing that i feel like i need to mention is the longevity. i really don't get the hate that jo malone gets for having no staying power. all the ones i tried give me at least solid 6 hours (12h with the cologne intense) of pleasant, linear wafts whenever i move.

I love Earl Grey tea. The aromatic component of the bergamot oil added to the calming fragrant black tea makes for an amazing taste. It's tough to translate that feeling into a fragrance, but Earl Grey and Cucumber has done quite a good job with it. The majority of the composition is this honey-sweetened tea accord, with the cucumber note added for freshness. The result is an aromatic, light, slightly floral scent that works really well on warm spring days. It is perfectly unisex and very mass-appealing. Underrated by the fragrance community.

My girlfriend and I wandered through the spring city - quite leisurely and in good spirits. We had time and no rush pushed us forward. Then a beautiful, curvy, colorful saleswoman with a charming bright smile offered us Earl Grey. And this clear, transparent scent fits the bright day and our strolling mode. The Earl Grey tea note reaches me calmly, refreshed by bergamot. The jasmine also reminds me of jasmine tea. A relaxing tea time in the perfumery. The cucumber note adds a refreshing touch. Beeswax makes the scent creamy and the vanilla attractively soft. Time passes more slowly - and we hardly wanted to part from the beautiful one and from the Earl. But she took the trouble to fill us a bit of the enchanting elixir. What service! There was also an invitation for a hand and arm massage with the Malones. Perfect. I can easily imagine this scent on both men and women, as it is generally relaxing. The likable Earl is well-suited in his approachable manner for gifting - but also for keeping for oneself.

Jo Malone's "Earl Grey & Cucumber" conjures up three summery scenes in which I would love to enjoy my tea. First of all, of course, the classic velvety green English lawn, where the elegantly arranged tea table reigns: set with fine linen, a silver teapot, delicate porcelain, and of course cucumber sandwiches, scones, and "clotted cream". One approaches cultured, accompanied by a sun hat and the "Times" to the "Five o'clock"! The second option is an "Alfresco Breakfast" à la Edouard Manet and Claude Monet. A clearing under birches and other bright deciduous trees; playful, chasing sunspots on the blanket: cheerful gentlemen and ladies chat on and around it. Almost everything that contributes to the general enjoyment is on the blanket or in the nearby picnic basket. And finally, a completely homely impression: a picnic in the garden of the painter Max Liebermann's villa. Located right by the Wannsee, the large lawn is adorned with the slender, light birches known from many paintings. The villa, the family home, with the café terrace and the large, colorfully planted flower bed in front, completes this view from the water. The vegetable and perennial garden is on the other side towards the street. The Liebermann family is absent, but guests have the freedom to use the garden as they please. Chairs and benches are generously available, as well as a white tea pavilion right by the water. Thus, a tea break is staged on the lawn under the birches that rivals the two previously mentioned. The blanket and the filled picnic basket were brought along; the tea in a thermos. Unfortunately, the times are also over here when "families could brew coffee." That would of course be optimal! The elegance of the English-celebrated tea is certainly not achieved here. However, the view of the sunlit Wannsee, over which the sailboats glide picturesque, is much more impressive. This variant is definitely more relaxed and entertaining. The group of painting guests with their easels and sketchbooks is also a welcome addition to the afternoon: much beauty and sights are created there. Some will later adorn one or another small bank branch in an "exhibition of local artists". All these images can be evoked by a pure summer fragrance like "Earl Grey & Cucumber". Just the top note - green and fresh and aromatic through the jasmine, which also blooms here in hedges, refreshes immediately: cool and cheerful. The bergamot clearly perfumes our tea here. Now, however, the cucumber cannot be denied any longer: freshly sliced, it adds its typically green scent to the existing composition. It is embraced by its carefully selected companions of the top note. This fragrance does not remain so light and fleeting either: warm vanilla blends with sun-warmed beeswax, musk and cedar harmoniously round off the whole. Jo Malone's "Earl Grey & Cucumber" is a summer fragrance that refreshes and cools; despite all its lightness, it still possesses a certain groundedness. This fragrance is a slightly different freshness kick that fits in any bag thanks to the well-known, square bottle. Whether for business or leisure - it always fits! Even in direct customer contact, this summery Jo Malone scent is never perceived as unpleasant or intrusive. The longevity is, as always, not all-day: but "Earl Grey & Cucumber" easily tolerates more frequent reapplication; it is also highly recommended as a hair perfume, providing a special treat for the nose. This "Perfumed Tea-Cucumber" blend surrounds you lively, without ever becoming annoying or even musty for a moment. A fine fragrance web with light depth - interesting and accompanying a true summer day fresh and lively. I do not want to miss "Earl Grey & Cucumber" anymore. This fragrance has earned its permanent place in my collection: it has now deserved its spot there.

That the British cult brand Jo Malone has dragged me to the checkout more than once with its refined creations is unfortunately not a lie. Blackberry & Bay is still one of my all-time faves, and in Wood Sage & Sea Salt, I found a wonderful companion for the gray days last autumn.

"Earl Grey & Cucumber" by Jo Malone is another beautiful example of how difficult and complex it can sometimes be to evoke a sensation and memory that feels so "simple" to our noses and minds, like "Ah, of course, this is Earl Grey tea!
…is airy fruity, but not sweet at all, slightly spicy, yet in a very delicate pleasant way, and overall this cucumber tea may not be something to drink, but it is wonderfully refreshing on the skin.

So… Here once again sits a cup of tea on my table. Black tea, as often. And on the side, I’m biting into a delicious and crunchy… no, not a cookie! But a cucumber!! Ööööhh,… does that even fit? Cucumbers and tea? But of course it fits. Have you never had a proper breakfast with all the trimmings?

...asks the waiter. "In this heat, warm drinks are actually healthier... how about a pot of Earl Grey tea with intense bergamot aroma? Or a cup of jasmine tea? Or would you prefer a large, ice-cold apple soda?" "Earl Grey & Cucumber" by Malone offers - at least for the nose - all three, in exactly that order.

This fragrance opens with an exceptionally creamy and gently sweet accord—though not in a typical gourmand manner. Instead of leaning into a dessert‑like richness, the sweetness feels airy, refined, and beautifully inviting. The opening wraps you in a smooth, velvety warmth that immediately sets a comforting mood. As the scent settles, it gradually drifts into a soft vanilla base that feels both cozy and elegant, maintaining a delicate balance between warmth and subtlety. The overall experience is truly lovely: serene, creamy, and quietly enchanting from start to finish.

It's okay. At the beginning angelica root is the most pronounced note, and the overall scent is herbal with a bit of gentle spice to it. I like the heady sweetness of the flowers below – on my body it's tuberose and ylang-ylang more than jasmine. It's woody, gooey and sweet, but in a relatively subdued way by modern femme perfume standards. Not great, but it has some charming qualities. Herbal sweetness, gooey resins, heavy white florals, tangy blackcurrant peeking through – it's like a multicultural witch hut! I wish that first impression would last longer. It doesn't. After the first ~15 minutes I notice that the things I liked about it are starting to fade away. The scent quickly becomes... simpler. Flatter. Predominantly ambery, and somewhat synthetic. An esoteric shop with cheap incense sticks currently burning inside of it. It's airy. Projects about an arm's length away, but just barely. Settles on skin after the first ~2 hours and at that point becomes completely one-dimensional. No angelica, barely any flowers – just the cheap ambery-esotheric flavor with a faint hint of smoke. In another ~4 hours it fades away. It's... okay. I don't hate it, but if I didn't write things down – come next morning I would barely remember any of it. That's not a kind thing to say, but I feel like nothing of value would be lost if it never existed. Meh.

I searched for a long time and have now found it... an almost identical twin of the hot and dearly loved Joop Nuit d'été. I can hardly believe it myself, especially the Ylang Ylang and the Jasmine, or rather the Herodes perfume, is very similar, and the longevity is very long. Perfect for long nights.

At last, the big egg did crack. "Peep," said the young one, and out he tumbled, but he was so big and ugly. The duck took a look at him. "That's a frightfully big duckling," she said... He was a swan! ... Other swans said "The new one is the most handsome of all. He's so young and so good-looking." The old swans bowed in his honor! Mr. Burberry is like the ugly duckling. With its dark and shaded grey bottle and black hat. It can't be all things to all people. If you try to please everyone, you'll end up pleasing no one. And Mr. Burberry is a pleasure for many but not for everyone. After many Brit flankers, Mr. Burberry is a nearly recent new release that heavily deviates from those flankers, both in the look and in the smell. Mr. Burberry smells clean, meaning this in the literal sense. It opens up with some subtle citrus grapefruit, which has an undertone of synthetics, blended with some warm creamy-minty-spicy tones that I speculate are cool cardamom combined with spicy tarragon. This stage awakens the senses, and an aura of masculinity permeates the fragrance. Gently, the citrus and herbal evanesce and Mr. Burberry becomes woody and smoky. To me, the fragrance seems to have a manifest presence of wetness. It smells like a city after rain, which is not by chance that drizzly London was such an inspiration. You can still feel the mist in the air mixed with the smell of smoke and soil from the street. The scent comprises a full and sturdy heart, whose classic fougère structure is masterfully reinterpreted in an extremely contemporary key. An accord of birch leaves gives a warm aroma to the essence, while cedarwood adds strength and balance to the sparkling top notes. A while later, Mr. Burberry turns very soapy. It reminds me of shaving cream, the one that my dad prepared every morning with a shaving brush. The soap smell makes Mr. Burberry an excellent choice for occasions when you want to smell good without being noticed. Birch leaves contribute to the greenish facet of the heart, and a little freshly grated nutmeg adds the right touch of spiciness. The light and the glowing base is a true celebration of the lively nature of vetiver. Improved with guaiac wood, it flows into intense smoky notes that do not endanger the bright aroma that evokes the smell of the earth. It lasts on me many hours, even though it is barely detectable after four hours. The dry-down is a combination of pitches, roots, moss, and woods. It stays transparent and slightly sweet, yet fresh and green. There is a slight synthetic tinge to it, which I don't mind. It transitions smoothly from one stage to the next, herbal then green-spicy then woody-resinous, notably are the sandalwood, the cedarwood, and the guaiac wood. To my flavor, it could be worn anywhere, anytime, it works for any occasion, any age, and any weather, yet my preferences drive me toward spring and summer days. The woods and resins in it might work in cold weather like early fall, but I have not tested it yet. Hence, what is an ugly duckling to the hype, it turns to be the most handsome swan to me. -Elysium

By far one of the most irrelevant, pedestrian, nonsense new launches I smelled in a long time. If something like, say, Dior’s Sauvage seemed like that for you, then Mr. Burberry will make your nose explode. Someone on Basenotes’ forum mentioned an Axe deodorant, and I now regret having used that same term of comparison for scents which compared to Mr. Burberry don’t really deserve that. Because in fact, in my experience Mr. Burberry is the scent which absolutely went the closest to that. Actually it even went further and below– no kidding, the 2,50 EUR deodorant I carry in my tennis bag smells more appealing, nuanced and rich than this garbage. Basically this is a truly nondescript, extremely artificial, puzzingly uninspired sort of a counterfeit Bleu de Chanel meeting a sport deodorant with a drop of Interparfums’ irritating signature musky-tonka base accord (Armani Code all over again- please fix that time machine, Interparfums!). There’s some synthetic citrus, some extremely generic woody stuff with a pointless sort of subtle minty-creamy nuance (a bit as in Paul Smith London), something sweet-spicy, and that’s it. I’m using the term “something” not out of laziness but because it’s truly the best approximation I can use – I read the composition, but none of the notes mentioned is remotely detectable here for me. It would be a joke to mention cardamom or vetiver here. It’s just woody stuff, spicy stuff, citrus stuff, cheap lab replicas of some “idea” of woods and spices. The same exact materials you find in supermarket deodorants in fact. Just a big generic “something”. And it’s so vastly nonsense that I can’t even think of a possible audience for this, neither can I understand how could Burberry approve to invest money for something so desperately unappealing and cheap. So shortly, if it wasn’t clear enough, my opinion is that this is a complete depressing trainwreck on every level – quality, inspiration, identity. And if you want to understand better how it smells, I can’t really describe it better than I did above – I know my description sounded generic but this is truly how this scent smells. I’ve never been a fan of Burberry but I’ve always (kind of) respected Kurkdjian’s work on commission, even recently – for example, Carven Homme from 2014 was quite good, and if you compare it to Mr. Burberry you can definitely sense the immense gap of budget and efforts that separates the two scents. This is on the contrary easily the worst scent Kurkdjian ever put his name on, and one of the worst scents by Burberry ever. 3/10

WOW, AMAZING FRAGRANCE ! Elegant, Classy and Nostalgic, l don't care for the negative comments , I decide that one perfume is good or bad, not others ! In my opinion this one is better than Dior Sauvage and Blue de Chanel and they are not the same. It opens up with like fresh spicy, green and spicy notes in the background then dry down is green woody. This is perfect for the spring, summer and fall. I really enjoy it and I love Mr.Burberry EDT, I'm so happy that I have it in my collection. Longevity is good. Two Thumbs Up. Rating : 8.5 / 10

People have said that this is an underrated fragrance and I agree. I regard Burberry fragrances along the same level as Azzaro's; they are reliable cheap fragrances that are rarely revolutionary. But the Mr. Burberry line would have fared better if it was released by the likes of Azzaro and Ralph Lauren. Some just like to hate on Burberry despite some solid offerings like Touch and London. I imagine when Burberry commissioned Kurkdjian to start a new line for them, shortly after he did Baccarat Rouge 540, that the conversation went something like this... Burberry: "We want a blue line of fragrance that is distinctly Burberry; it captures the shower gel experience and evokes a well-groomed English gentleman." Kurkdjian: "So a fragrance that makes the wearer smell like he's just got out of the shower and straight into a classic London barbershop." Kurkdjian has effectively created a blue barbershop fougere with Mr. Burberry EdT, which is why it has also been criticised for being generic since it is the combination of the two most popular men's fragrance categories. But how many blue barbershop fragrances are really out there? Mr. Burberry EdT smells way more expensive and luxurious than the measly price I paid for at the discounter, and performs like an EdP. If they create a Parfum version, I would certainly like to see the addition of vanilla, leather and/or tobacco for a sexy evening Mr. Burberry, which Mr. Burberry EdP sadly was not.

Reading some other reviews on this scent, I have detected that I don't get the notes delayed in stages -- the notes hit me all at once. That's strange, but especially strange for this fragrance, because they show up in force and then flee. In four to six hours, I have been ghosted. Where did Mr. Burberry go? I'm left pondering the question like someone after a crush moved without saying a word. However, this all began better than it ended. Let me explain. Mr. Burberry shows up suave. This is a scent with presence -- not a powerhouse scent, so nearby windows are safe -- but a wrap-around you kind of silage. To my nose, it is subtly orange, with baby oil and a hint of pepper -- masculine and refined without exuding machismo. The orange is mostly aromatic and warm, not strongly individualistic. As time goes on, the scent alternates between soapy/clean and heavy, creamy, cozy/spicy. The baby oil is there, but I'm holding my fire, because the overall effect works. By hour four it has amped down to vanilla. Not much later, Mr. Burberry has split apart -- one wrist has a creamy/vanilla scent, while the other wrist radiates orange. This is an unsettling ending, much like the confusing end to a relationship. There's no closure here, and even those into weird scents like I am, will probably find this unsatisfying. Mr. Burberry started off strong but lost his way, like he had wandered off into the woods to repeat phrases at greater and greater distances away. What went into the woods is not what eventually emerged. If you're into the spicy/clean/soapy style scents, try Endymion (Penhaligon's) instead.

Elegant, casual and office friendly, for every occasion and time. This fragrance can be the only one you need, the best buy because it's not expensive and you get quality and a brand name. It's a slightly similar to Bleu de Chanel, but of course you can't expect quality of Chanel for this price. I would take Mr.Burberry over Sauvage anytime.

Burberry is England, is style, is class. With a bit of luck & Christmas money, I might someday afford a piece of clothing. If I am willing to spend a fortune for high quality + the name. Probably not. A few perfumes are decent (London, Brit, Sport with some caveats), although never at the level & prestige of the clothing. But which brand still manages that?

Mr Burberry comes off relatively poorly in my humble opinion. What is the reason for that? Even though I generally feel more at home with niche fragrances, I still have a few mainstream scents that I enjoy wearing, and Mr Burberry is definitely one of them. Of course, it always depends on what one expects from a mid-range fragrance.

Burberry - actually known for expensive fabrics, also tries its hand at various fragrances. However, with Mr. Burberry, they have really missed the mark. A piercing chemical smell spreads upon spraying, it all smells very cheap.

With Mr. Burberry, you absolutely dare nothing. But do you always have to? Well, I must admit, I like Mr. Burberry because it reminds me of my first wet shave. I was maybe 16 when Dad showed me how wet shaving works. "It works, it's super easy," thought the young me, freshly shaved under the guidance and supervision of my father, shaking it off and then trudging on my way.

Like peeling a fresh clementine/mandarine orange - a refreshing, lovely, but warm citrus in the opening. Soon the citrus becomes woody, soft, warm, cozy, but still clearly an orange if you pay attention or are sensitive enough to fragrance. Surprisingly I do find the orange persists through the dry down to woods, making this a very special fragrance, unlike others that open with fleeting citrus or try to create a citrus accord that doesn't quite hit citrus. This one does it. Some Hermès orange compositions are a similar warm orange - but of course this doesn't have that Hermès scent that is in all of their perfumes.

I noticed this great bottle last Christmas. Together with the name, it immediately caught my attention. Unfortunately, I wasn't able to get a bottle back then, as it was limited. Now I finally got to test it, thanks to a dear friend from Parfumo! Thank you for that, Henry:-)! Bitter Orange smells incredibly delicious right from the start. A slightly sweet orange meets a lightly fresh-bitter Petitgrain/Bergamot. Radiantly bright, as if kissed by the sun, with an extra dose of Vitamin C. Although the notes of the top note suggest a consistent scent experience, it still smells completely unique. After about 10-15 minutes, a certain sweetness creeps in that I can't quite place. I can't say it smells like prunes, perhaps they contribute to this subtle sweetness. I don't find it wintry or even Christmassy, nor does it smell like potpourri. But this is the phase where I wish it were below 10 degrees; then I could enjoy this slightly warming phase more than in the current humid 28 degrees. What I can identify quite precisely, however, is the enchanting mix of spicy-aromatic sandalwood and dry papyrus. Because this very successful mix is also offered to me by Bentley Absolute in the base; you just have to fade out the frankincense and partly the cedarwood, and then the same "accord" remains. Balsamic-creamy with a hint of orange on top, this is how Orange Bitter ends for me after 5-6 hours. The development takes about 45 minutes, and the sillage is quite strong, which might be a bit much in summer. When I was at Ludwig Beck in Munich at the beginning of June, I received the pleasant news from a Jo Malone salesperson: This limited fragrance is supposed to remain limited, but will be re-released in November for the Christmas season. Let's see in what sizes it will be available then, because with this strong scent, 30ml would probably last me forever. No matter... I won't let it slip away again;-)!

Here I am testing a Jo Malone fragrance again after weeks. Actually, I went into the fragrance shop without a specific goal, but a friendly (and by the way, really nice :) saleswoman "pulled" me over to the Jo Malone stand, as she believed I absolutely had to try this new scent. However, I had also hoped to discover something new... I just didn't expect it to be a Jo Malone. Of course, I trust her taste very much, and I was looking forward to a scent I didn't know yet, but I approached it with a certain skepticism, as I had found some good fragrances among the many Jo Malones, but hardly any of them truly convinced me. Well, this was supposed to change with this fragrance here... The Fragrance: Wow,... as a citrus fragrance lover, I can't say anything else at the beginning. The scent starts with a wonderful and natural orange. Initially slightly sweet, it then becomes a bit spritzily bitter, as if you were smelling the peel of this fruit. I must admit that I first thought of mandarins when it came to the peel, but it turned out to be orange peel after all. The fantastic top note is almost like a mix of the two Hermès fragrances Mandarine Ambrée and Concentré d’Orange Verte. The plum in the heart note blends more with the other slightly sweet notes and is therefore not very noticeable. Over time, the fragrance becomes a bit spicier or more autumnal. It is soft and especially woody in the base, with a light, earthy note. This earthy note is the patchouli and remains more in the background. The amber is also a bit light, but gives the fragrance a nice, sweet note. The oranges are still somewhat present in the base, but as mentioned, the scent becomes increasingly woody. All in all, a really successful fragrance. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is above average, unfortunately, as I would have preferred it to be stronger for a fragrance that can also be used well in winter. But well, it is still just barely noticeable, but it won't leave a fragrance cloud behind. I believe one should really spray it on clothing as well. The longevity is somewhat better; the fragrance lasts about eight or nine hours on the skin, although it is noticeably weaker in the later hours. The Bottle: The bottle is rectangular and has a golden cap, which somewhat resembles a (door) knob. In terms of shape, the bottle looks just like most Malone bottles. The label on the front also displays the name and logo of the fragrance as usual. However, the bottle is "covered" with black diamond patterns, giving it a great and varied look. Everything is nicely done and looks a bit better than the standard bottles. Have I already said "Wow"? But seriously. I have tested really many Jo Malone fragrances lately (especially in summer). And I mean really, really many (I just haven't commented on most of them...), so many that I have been to the Jo Malone stand so often that the girls at that stand have probably already given me the nickname "The Sniffer"... Anyway, some of the fragrances were okay, some were so-so, but there were also quite a few really good ones among them. However, I hardly discovered such a wonderful fragrance as this one among them (aside from the beautiful Rare Tea fragrances, which are also great and some other exceptions), which may be why I am so excited about this one. The fragrance has turned out really beautifully and with its orange notes, mixed with woods and sweet scents, it feels nicely autumnal or wintery and even a bit oriental. However, I think the sillage could have been stronger, because as beautiful as the fragrance (and especially the top note) is, it is more suitable as a daytime and casual fragrance, as it is a bit too weak for going out. Furthermore, I think that Orange Bitters also stands quite well on its own. After all, most Jo Malones can be layered well together. But precisely for that reason, I find some of the fragrances somewhat "unfinished," as if they are just waiting to reveal their true effect when combined with other fragrances, but this one smells quite good on its own. Well,... in any case, it is a fragrance that should be tested, best as soon as possible, as it is limited. Of course... now that I really like a Jo Malone fragrance again, it is not only limited but almost sold out again...

Opens up beautifully…spicy from the cardamom, some vanilla, some woods. Stays like that for about an hour. You may buy a bottle based on that first hour, then get home and be pretty damn disappointed with whats left on your skin. It begins to dry down to something that smells very feminine, synthetic, chemically, cloying and almost like scented body lotion. Very, very disappointing considering how beautiful the opening is. I would skip this, and save your money, go with a different flanker in the line.

I agree with the light Iris in the opening, but I get a “chocolatey” feeling in it as well, and then it dries down into something very similar to Ferragamo Uomo in my opinion. It’s nothing groundbreaking, but it’s also getting a lot of hate atm, and I don’t think it’s as bad as the haters are saying it is. It is definitely different than its predecessors, and I think that THAT is why the disdain is being given. I’d say the projection is a moderate 2ft bubble, with a lingering sillage trail that goes for an easy 6-8 hours. Give it a peek before you buy it, but it’s not as terrible as many are saying it is.

How many different opinions of this Gentleman. My experience: neutral, versatile, sweet and rich, but absolutely dispensable. Cardamom stands out in the first phase, with a floral air, I don't know if it's sage or tuberose, but it reminds me of violet, which brings a lot of elegance, the background is woody, with a marked palo santo so fashion currently. All accompanied by a very controlled sweetness of vanilla. I've been trying it for a couple of days and I can't perceive vetiver around here. Unfortunately, I can't find any connection with the Gentleman line. It didn't drive me crazy, in Argentina it's a bit expensive, about $120 approximately. I highly recommend not buying blindly like I did.

It's fine. Smells like a good designer perfume. Fuzzy creamy cardamom, sharp fragrant sage. For the first ~10 minutes or so I am pleasantly surprised. It's cozy and aromatic, with plenty of vetiver below and budding yellow florality the type of which I don't see very often. But then narcissus blossoms and so does vanilla. And I immediately get bored. Sharp florality and overwhelming vanilla sweetness drown out the upper notes and turn the composition into another faceless crowd pleaser. About 2 meters worth of sillage. Smells good. Strong, but not too overwhelming. Pleasant, but entirely forgettable. A man at the bar who leaves an overall nice impression, but whose face I struggle to remember as soon as I turn away. Takes about an hour to settle in the wearer's immediate vicinity, and another hour to settle on skin. During these ~2 hours vanilla and narcissus remain the only things in the spotlight, drowning out everything else. I can feel cardamom and sage close to my skin, but it's a struggle to get that close without going nose blind. A shame. They're lovely. By the time it settles on skin and mellows out, upper notes disappear. Narcissus also starts fading. The next ~2 hours are ruled by vanilla and vetiver. I can feel a bit of sleek sandalwood in the background, but it doesn't catch any attention if I don't deliberately sniff it out. Then the drydown begins. Sweet, soft, creamy and vaguely woody. It lasts into the night (was light, but still visibly sweet when I took a shower and went to sleep ~4 hours into it). When I woke up the next day, the arm I tested it on didn't necessarily smell like it, but its base scent was slightly sweeter than usual. I'm not a fan of that, but I'm sure there are people who would be happy with that kind of longevity. It's... fine? Have you ever received a good grade at school compared to the rest of your class, but had the teacher still look at you with disappointment, as if silently saying that they expected something better from you? That kind of thing used to annoy me immensely when I was a kid, but this perfume makes me understand my teachers' feelings a little bit. Compared to most other designer perfumes I smell on the streets – it's pretty good! But it had so much potential it didn't live up to that I can't help but feel a bit disappointed in it.

I must say it doesn't really fit into the gentleman line, but its very pleasant and not deserving of the hate. It's creamy sweet florals with sandalwood and an actually nice narcissus. Im not a fan of the narcissus in H24 Eau de Toilette but here it does wonders, not necessarily "gentlemanly" but its fitting for a nice sunny day out, my gf really likes it on me. Its younger brother Gentleman Society Eau de Parfum Extrême is much nicer with the added coffee.

Gentleman Society is probably one of my favourite scents ever (I love Vetiver!). The refined masculine edge is deliberately complemented by the vanilla, cardamon, and sandalwood, bringing forth a perfect fragrance for date nights or classier evenings. However, I must mention that it's not for everyone, not in terms of scent, but in terms of well... scent.

After testing Gentleman Givenchy Society, one can clearly see the brand's intention: to create a fragrance that sells well and appeals to both a younger and somewhat more mature target audience. Two points were taken into consideration. An opening that is sweet-fresh, embodying the currently trendy shower gel vibe. Could they possibly have thought of Eros?

I received the fragrance for testing and must say I am positively surprised. I'll try to explain it in a way that everyone can understand. The opening of the fragrance is very pleasantly powdery. Not as piercing as a DHI or the others from the Gentleman line, but all the more pleasant.

The Gentleman Society was something very special for me, right from the first spray. For me, it is unique, special, and a perfect everyday fragrance for the modern man of today. The opening is something extraordinary; immediately, the pleasant and refreshing sage note rises to the nose. Simply wonderful! I get a fresh yet sweet, balsamic, woody top note.

... and off I go to my date. Dressed well and with a refined scent on my chest and a certain charisma make the evening perfect. When applying this fragrance, the first thing that hits the nose is chestnuts (even though this is not listed in the fragrance pyramid). Along with it, there is a slight alcoholic note. A little later, a wood aroma joins in.

Calvin opens with a sharp bergamot laced herbal green mix of sage-like artemisia and oakmoss rising from the base, with underlying anise-like tarragon support before transitioning to its heart. As the composition enters its early heart the bergamot vacates, leaving remnants of the artemisia to couple with the now focal tarragon and rugged mossy green oakmoss with sharp, woody vetiver and earthy patchouli adding significant support. During the late dry-down the development stays highly linear staying herbal green throughout, as the tarragon, oakmoss and woody vetiver remain the focus with relatively dry sandalwood adding support through the finish. Projection is outstanding, and longevity excellent at over 12 hours on skin. Calvin has proven quite elusive to find on the aftermarket nowadays except at what some may consider "crazy" prices, making sampling the perfume difficult over the years. Luckily, I was able to get my hands on a mini from the 80s to see what all the fuss is about as I don't recall smelling much of it back then. The first thing I noticed when applying the perfume on skin was its powerhouse strength. The oakmoss and herbs project seemingly for miles and miles... Anyone growing up in the 80s would recognize this strength as "the real deal." If I were to gauge influences for Calvin, it would have to be perfumes of its age like the original Polo, and it in turn influenced perfumes that immediately followed like Quorum by Puig. In truth, I think it is closer to the latter. There really isn't much in the way of development throughout, and while Calvin smells excellent, it never challenges the *true* greatness and originality found in its much more accessible Polo predecessor, making the argument for seeking it out somewhat tenuous. The bottom line is the $433 per 100ml bottle on the aftermarket Calvin is another "very good" to "excellent" 3.5 to 4 stars out of 5 rated example of the sublime powerhouse 80s, but it doesn't quite distinguish itself from its contemporaries to merit the hunt and relatively stratospheric cost of seeking it out today, earning it a recommendation solely to 80s vintage perfume completionists.

I remember wearing Calvin in 1985. It was the best thing CK ever created for a man. It complimented my CK jeans and t-shirt. I felt like I was at the hight of American fashion. The original formula was last seen in 1995 still in tact. I would now refer to it as a woody chypre. Then it was just perfect. Herbal, spicy, woody and very clean. The blue bottle matched the contents. It was the perfect male counterpart for the ladies red bottle. No endless, mindless flankers were required. They stood just fine in any season. Then along came Obsession, Eternity and all of that other mass produced "bug sprays". The name CK has become something less. Do they even make jeans anymore?

Like a phantom, this mysterious scent and its modernist-dark bottle haunt the scene; it suddenly appears and then disappears again, largely unsung by fragrance critics. Those who want to know what Calvin smells like should take a dark musk fragrance, Fougère type, about halfway between Kouros, Polo, and Marbert Man, and largely replace the animalistic notes with an intensely turned-up citrus tone and a gentle, white clove note. Calvin is hyper-masculine, retro-barbershop, and extremely musky in a clean-soapy, skin-like direction, clearly more conservative than its appearance suggests, and feels like the men's fragrance that everyone knows from somewhere and many love. Many do not, however. The radiance at the beginning is "powerhouse," which calms down after 30 minutes. Throughout the day, crisp citrus waves, noble soap, and the typical connection tone of skin and musk - especially for the wearer themselves - remind you that you are wearing a high-quality Eau de Toilette. The search is worth it. Pure coincidence that Balafre, Patou pour Homme, Macassar, or Nobile are currently the stars - Calvin holds his own easily. Simple (and) exciting.

Calvin Klein is a rather strange brand: for years they have been successful with pale, pastel-colored designs. Just as indecisive as the presentation are most of the fragrances - often unisex and made for people who don't like to commit, because they don't really have their own opinion - and if they do, it's a very tame one. Fans may forgive me - but that's how it all comes across to me. The original Calvin appeared at a time when this brand had not yet found its current indecisiveness. Calvin is very much a child of its time, as the look at the pyramid suggests. There we have the variety of aromas that is so typical for that time, making it impossible to quickly dissect the scent. In general, it is soapy with a tendency towards sharpness. The remaining notes all point in different directions and sort of cancel each other out. It leaves a musky-patchouli background. In this respect, Calvin already hints at that indifference which today characterizes the perfume style of Calvin Klein. No, this cannot excite me - this is CK with flared pants, but unfortunately without the cult factor. No one will miss that. Many thanks again to AromiErotici, who has supplied me with plenty of samples of vintage perfumes from his collection.

Calvin Klein, the lifestyle brand from the 1990s that achieved cult status with models like Mark Wahlberg, Kate Moss, and Milla Jovovich, has covered pretty much every segment with its fragrance range and reached every target group. All age groups have been catered to in 30 years of the fragrance business. There are the Orientals "Obsession," the Spicy "Escape" and "Eternity," the Floral "Beauty," the Fresh "Truth For Men," including the seemingly 20 Eternity summer flankers, the Sensual "Euphoria Woman" and "Secret Obsession," the Youthful "Crave" and "CK In 2U," and of course the Androgynous "CK One." The latter is probably the most successful Klein fragrance and likely the best-selling young classic in the world! Speaking of unisex - for many young people, including myself, the journey into the world of perfume began with this neutral-scented water. However, few know that the actual Big Bang in the "Calvin" fragrance universe took place back in 1978, 16 years earlier, with "Calvin" (Woman). CK entered the men's segment three years later with the male counterpart, which also bore the simple name. The (fragrance) bottle, completely unknown to me until now, presented itself simply. A slim, androgynous bottle in classic black. The rounded plastic cap features the "Calvin" name in large letters. At the time, it was an optical revolution; today it may seem a bit uninspired, even cheap. The packaging, also entirely black, stays true to the motto "Black is beautiful!" The print campaign featured a young gentleman with slicked-back hair in a suit, confidently and characteristically gazing into a baroque mirror. The fragrance was contemporary and classic for its time. It is a typical fougère with a herbal, ozonic flair. "Calvin" disappeared in the early 1990s and was re-released in 1999 in a limited edition. I am commenting on the reissued version (many thanks to trueBlood, who gifted me his bottle), which should not deviate significantly from the original. The opening features a gray lemon note that, combined with chamomile, has a herbal, floral flair with a bitter undertone. There are similarities to YSL's Kouros Cologne Sport, which has a similarly cool presence. The ingredient list is rich and creative, yet I can only discern a few ingredients. As the scent develops, a spicy cinnamon note becomes noticeable. The fragrance departs earthy/green and leaves a masculine/bitter touch. The longevity is average - 5 hours are quite possible. In summary, an interesting men's fragrance that would certainly stand out from the Klein mainstream range today!

I put this on earlier in the day. I sniffed my wrist a few hours later, and I had to wrack my brain to remember what I put on. Then I remembered after looking at the bottle sitting on my bathroom counter. This is not a distinct perfume at all. I DO like it; it's a nice spicy, creamy perfume that's great for cool weather. However, you could slap on a celebrity name or a brand like Hugo Boss on the label and I wouldn't know the difference. Longevity is between 4 to 6 hours on me.

When spraying, I get hungry. This is so fruity in a sweet way, it makes me feel like eating a fruit salad or diving into a huge fruit buffet. This is in my Burberry top three together with Burberry for women, a warm spicy fragrance and Brit Sheer, a citric lychee/mandarine combo. This starts out sweet with sweet on top. Luckily, it has the citric note from Italian lime to bring the scent into balance. It moves through the sweetness and into the floral phase, elegantly presenting the peony. Finally, after some hours the vanilla and amber end the dance. No mahogany for my nose. Sillage is good. The bottle has the classic Burberry look. I like it; square, simple and with a recognizable pattern. 257/365

Reminds me of rain, plaid blazers, thick rimmed glasses. Studying late at night for a philosophy test. Hot cup of earl gray tea in a hand thrown ceramic mug with a lipstick stain on the side This is one of the first fragrances I bought as a young adult and has stayed a fall/winter staple in my life ever since. It’s not one of the most expensive perfumes I own. It’s actually the most affordable. It will never not remind me of my days in Uni studying for finals.

Hello everyone, Brit (EDT) by Burberry is, in my opinion, a very beautiful fragrance for spring with excellent longevity. At the beginning, I perceive the pear and the fresh lime, then the scent on my skin becomes very powdery and then glides into sweeter nuances. The pear remains subtly noticeable, with the powdery scent lying above it. Just right for those days when you still prefer to wear a silk scarf around your neck because the spring breeze is still a bit too fresh. The fragrance is very suitable for everyday work - without being perceived as a "typical" business scent.

Great, appetite-stimulating fruity-gourmand scent with a heartwarming finish. Excellent longevity (8 -10 hrs). Perfect for all not-too-hot days when you want a protective, loyal, and non-provocative companion ;-)

I’m quite cautious with the Brits these days, as I find them great, but especially the regular Brit tends to linger in my nose throughout the day, which annoys me in the evening, except for the Gold LE.

This is a really beautiful fragrance. Right from the get go I can smell the lilac being very prominent on my skin. Reminds me of when I was a child and I'd pick lilacs and bring them home for my mother and the smell would waft through the entire house. The orange blossom is also very nicely blended in and smooth. These two notes are what I predominantly smell on my skin. I love when I wear it and catch whiffs of it all through the day. It's a scent that just makes you feel happy and uplifted. I have such a tiny bottle of it so it's used sparingly to make it last. I would love to get a big bottle one day. I have no problem with its lasting power either. At the end of the day I can still smell it. This one is a must have!

I grew up surrounded by orange groves and still take a drive along the grove roads each season they are in bloom.There is nothing as wonderful as the smell of an Orange Grove in bloom. It is magical and if you've never experienced it you really need to. The opening of this brought tears to my eyes. It was perfect. I could almost believe I was running through a grove in bloom. The balance of floral and green notes was spot on. Perfectly delightful. After a bit it warms up and the lilac base steps forward and blends nicely with the grove. It's not the longest lived perfume but it's heaven while it's there. I love it. Edit: The last few times I've worn this perfume the "orange grove" has faded away after about an hour and it becomes a rather linear Lilac perfume. It's still lovely but Lilac is definitely the soloist after the Orange grove completes it's bright introduction and exits the stage. A good one to try if looking for a basic Lilac. Oct 10 2013

I first sampled this a year ago. I was pleasantly surprised but not "wowed". It seemed a bit simplistic to me so I kept looking in vain for a better orange blossom scent. Today I finally bought a bottle. It is VERY pretty. I find it refreshingly uncomplicated and easy to wear. I'd like to think that this smell suits me. It's not angry, aggressive or offensive. It's gentle, elegant and honest. These are attributes that I value. I want to be approachable. I want to be kind. I want to smell like orange blossoms. When I don't know what to wear- I will reach for this. I'm not one who feels comfortable leaving a trial of scent in my wake. Orange Blossom lasts a long time on my skin but doesn't project far. I don't know why I waited so long for a full bottle.

When I was 18, I was dating the boy who used to live next door to me, but who had since graduated high school and moved to Indiana to attend Notre Dame. We spent a week together on summer break, during which time he had flown down South to stay with me and my family. It was early in this visit that he proposed to me on the beach one night, and I accepted…though something told me that this was a doomed venture. I knew it was not going to last, and yet I agreed anyway; I suppose I just liked the idea that something interesting loomed in the distant future for me. One late afternoon a few days later, we took a drive; the sun hung low on the horizon, the windows were down, and on the wind that ruffled our hair was the musky, sweet scent of orange blossoms, as we had just driven past a massive orange grove. Jo Malone’s Orange Blossom smells like that summer afternoon, sweet blooms and dying suns and the melancholy of tears yet to be shed for reasons you’re not quite sure of.

This fragrance conveys to me the happiness and lightness of being in an orchard, on a blue and sunny day, on a spring morning. The orange and tangerine are realistic, exaggeratedly juicy and discreetly spicy (they are delicious)! They reproduce the natural smell, looking like we kneaded and rubbed it with our own hands. There is a silky note, which is very evident and brings a certain femininity, possibly it is the water lily. I have the impression of feeling a light tuberose (not listed). The evolution of the fragrance was slow and smooth, so that the drydown still has similarities with the starting notes. It keeps exhaling, rising to the nostrils, close to me, gracefully. I'm very familiar with Jo Malone's natural fragrances and this is a one-way street. Its addicting. Once you like this kind of olfactory signature, pure and realistic, you start to find most other fragrances too synthetic, forced and desperate to get attention.

I had looked at Orange Blossom, and read many good reviews, but never purchased because I had 20+ orange blossom and neroli fragrances, and thought that I didn't need another. I was wrong. JM's Orange Blossom is a wonderful addition to my collection. It was Briarthorn who suggested trying it, and when she mentioned the gorgeous lilac drydown I knew I had to try it.

My first impression of this cologne, the scent smelt like piss because of how strong the smell came off. After a couple months of owning it, it now reminds me of a fresh glass of orange juice from Vietnam. I'm actually growing on this cologne; it is strong at first, a burst of citrus in your face but as it dries becomes more subtle.

This may be my next full bottle buy for summer! Like others have said, this perfume opens with a sweet, juicy burst of fresh mandarin and then dries down to a delicious bouquet of orange blossoms and other white flowers. This reminds me of walking near the orange groves in Southern California.

Orange Blossom is my new go-to scent for a fresh floral for the spring and summer! This is a very photorealistic orange blossom scent that is citrusy on the opening while maintaining a very strong distinction as a floral fragrance rather than a fruity one.

Orange blossom and I have a complicated relationship. It’s one of those notes I never know what to expect from. At its worst, it smells like kitchen cleaner. Most of the time, it’s just an inoffensive fresh white floral. At its best, it smells like this: a creamy, sweet, slightly citrusy, indulgent white floral. I wouldn’t have my florals any other way.

L'Interdit - Audrey Hepburns fragrance, of which I own the perfume, the EdP and the EdT - is my signature fragrance. So after reading various comments at parfumo.de, I absolutely had to test the new versions - I chose the EdP and the EdP-Intense (luckily only the 30ml versions of both). So after they arrived I tested them immediately. On the left the Intense and on the right the EdP on the respective wrist. I have commented on the EdP separately, so here is the intense one. Those who know me know that I don't have much of a thing for animalistic orientals. I like really well-made amber scents that combine many facets. The Intense is something I had to wash off my wrist immediately. It makes me sick and I'm afraid Audrey Hepburn would feel the same if she smelled this brew. Because here too, the bottle is reminiscent of L'Interdit. The content is puffy, sweet, animalistic and irritates my nose in a very unpleasant way. However, he is intense. The silage is so big that in no time our entire living room smelled of it (ventilating it only helped to a limited extent). The durability is good, but this "scented water" can be washed off quite easily with a lot of soap (luckily). NO NO NO please no more such “reissues” of legendary fragrances. This can only go wrong, as this “scented water” proves!

The L’Interdit line has a large number of flankers, making it difficult to pick the best among them. We learn in business school that successful brands produce the most line extensions. L’Interdit is a very successful brand indeed. This review of L’Interdit EDP Intense is based on a 15 ml tester vial from Givenchy. This perfume comes in an interesting all-black bottle. I am always eager to test any perfume created by Dominique Ropion. I have reviewed the original L’Interdit EDP earlier. Though a flanker, the EDP Intense is different enough to be considered separately. The bergamot, ginger and jasmine in the original L’Interdit EDP has been replaced by vanilla and black sesame. This substitution changes the flavor of the white floral accords and darkens them. The opening is an intense blast of vanilla, tuberose, orange blossom and sesame. The development is not significant in L’Interdit EDP Intense. All the notes continue uninterrupted until you get to the base notes stage, where the sesame and the vanilla shines brighter. It smells as if I had applied sesame oil on my skin. But it still retains hints of vanilla and white florals. Contrary to what is listed on many websites, L’Interdit EDP Intense does not open with black pepper, and it is not listed as not by Givenchy. The patchouli and vetiver are very mild, gently enhancing the black sesame accord in the end. I consider L’Interdit EDP Intense to be superior to the L’Interdit EDP, as the sweetness in the latter is very loud and cuts into its sophistication. L’Interdit EDP Intense is a high-performing fragrance, as its name implies. The floral notes stay on the skin for 6-8 hours and the vanilla and sesame for another four hours or so. Unless you are extremely judicious, this is not a work perfume. The sillage and projection are very good. Be aware that tuberose can satiate our noses and hearts very quickly. So, I would stick with just one perfume from the L’Interdit family, preferably the smaller 50 ml size. I recommend L’Interdit EDP Intense as the one to buy from this group. I confess that I have not tested some of the rare ones such as the L'Interdit Nocturnal Jasmine or the L'Interdit Tubéreuse Noire, both of which are rated highly. For what it offers, L’Interdit EDP Intense is very affordable, with 80 ml costing about $60 on US grey market sellers. But if you want to buy it, you must hurry because this perfume has already been discontinued.

This is not a grown up scent. It's strong and sweet and really, really girly, but it's edgier than Barbiecore because it smells purple and is in a black bottle. And while the dry down does have this slightly dark vetiver and patchouli thing going on, and there is an interesting creaminess from the sesame, these are very subtle in comparison to the endless wall of purple grape you're getting. As an androgynous adult who isn't twink, this is probably the most challenging perfume in my collection. I do like it, it isn't a poorly composed or badly made, it's just very girly and very loud about it. I did some experimenting though and this is actually kinda wearable on me in that 'beautiful, androgynous goth in the smoking area of a nightclub' kinda way, if I layer it with something masculine and oakmossy, or heavy on the vetiver. I usually go with a very light touch of Quorum, or a few healthy spritzes of Encre Noir.

On my skin, this does not work AT ALL. I LOVE this line, and adore Rouge, Ultime, & Absolu... But this one- I had to scrub it off. It smells like Bug Spray with a Grape note to it. A very strong one at that. I really hate it... I am just surprised at how much I hate it. If it works for you, great. But do not go into this thinking that it smells anything like Rouge. It is definitely long lasting and strong. But for me, this one totally missed the mark

I became aware of this wonderfully feminine scent L'Interdit (Intense) through three very esteemed ladies, as it should be. First, a month ago, Runa (I always enjoy your great photos and refreshing texts - it's nice to have you here!) wrote a passionate comment scoring 10 (or 12) points. Next, two weeks ago, Edda (you know I'm a fan of you and your Haiku statements!) posted an almost equally enthusiastic short review here. And last Friday, my dear favorite colleague handed me a sample of the fragrance, which she received for free at the perfumery, with the remark: "For your swap box. It only gives headaches." That piques curiosity. I will come to the actual scent later and first sneak in through the accidental details. The fragrance is not called "Interdit" (forbidden), but "L'Interdit," which is the more exciting and ambiguous name. "L'Interdit" can also mean the interdict, a mild form of ecclesiastical ban (as a punishment for crimes or heresy). Even if this is probably not the intended meaning, this connotation surely resonates unconsciously for the French listener. The main meaning is "prohibition," but also "taboo." I find the name quite fitting for this tension-filled, dreamily elegant scent that dances on the edge of a knife. The perfumers also catch attention. Dominique Ropion is one of the greats, and he has often collaborated with Anne Flipo. Together, they have created such famous (and heterogeneous) fragrances as Acqua di Gioia, Invictus, and Lady Million. Without Anne Flipo, he is responsible for countless other mainstream and niche fragrances, from Krazy Krizia, La Vie Est Belle, and Alien EdP to Portrait of a Lady, Oud Malaki, and Vetiver Extraordinaire. Flipo, in turn, created the highly interesting La Chasse aux Papillons. Interestingly, Acqua di Gioia is one of my favorite colleague's favorite scents... The marketing color of this fragrance is black, which leads to a false trail. Because the scent impression is not dark. Emotionally, it is not a gloomy fragrance, but rather awake and perhaps erotically charged, yet at the same time also flattering, soothing, and even comforting. Synesthetically, I perceive the scent as multi-toned gray and brown, a symphony in anthracite, ash, ochre, sienna, chamois, and sepia. Tactilely, L'Interdit feels very firm and densely woven to me, like a fabric that warms and provides security, never tearing, yet at the same time soft and light. Overall, L'Interdit Intense is noble but unpretentious; sensual but cool; material to the point of edibility, yet simultaneously distant and representational. On fabric, this "prohibition" unfolds in a slightly tart, almost green, almost fruity direction; I am reminded of Creed's Vetiver Original, although softer and more saffron-like. On my skin, I perceive a completely different scent development (and I am left with the open question of what the overall impression would be if I accompanied a lady who had applied the fragrance to her skin and clothing). Here, I perceive the scent in layers, like a puff pastry or a geological formation, where the individual layers, in the ochre and gray tones described above, play with the viewer like a moiré pattern: There are, after a distinctive, highly marked opening that evokes a memory in me that I cannot quite grasp, slightly sweet lines, powdery-floury, cocoa, or rather soy flour, which then lose their sweetness and perhaps turn into crushed clay. There is a sparkling, clear, fine sharpness, a gray dry crackle that then glides back to a velvety finish on soft skin. There are far, far distant hints of soft chamois leather that, as soon as one tries to grasp them, transform into bittersweet chocolate. Without a doubt, the fragrance has a strongly floral side. At times, this seems dense and heavy, evoking thoughts of lilac and hyacinths. However, the perfumers manage to break through and lighten this heaviness so that L'Interdit Intense never feels oppressive or old-fashioned, but rather innovative and light despite all its coziness. The scent of roasted sesame oil, which I know well, I cannot perceive, but rather a wonderful gentle benzoin-like tickle in the nose. The longevity and projection are quite pronounced, but surprisingly restrained for an "Intense" fragrance. This fits well with the essence of the scent, which is intense and lively, yet does not drunkenly shout in the streets; it is emotional, but also clear and precise; mysterious, yet not convoluted. I love such ambiguous, undefined fragrances. Currently, I am in a generous phase regarding scoring, which is reflected in my occasionally raising old reviews a bit against my usual habit. So perhaps 9.5 is also a tiny bit due to the excitement of the moment. But it is undoubtedly an unusually beautiful fragrance, without question. Whether L'Interdit belongs to the women's fragrances that I could also imagine on myself, I do not yet know. The thought does not seem completely absurd to me, but for now, I would like to leave it entirely to the beautiful ladies in my virtual and real environment. Except for my favorite colleague, to whom I certainly wish anything but headaches.

For a long time, I contemplated which version of L'Interdit I wanted to buy. The story behind the fragrance intrigued me. A perfume created especially for the great actress Audrey Hepburn. Of course, I know that the original scent doesn't have much in common with today's versions. But I simply love orange blossom. And I just can't resist that.

“No - not another one!” -- “But you like me so much, ...!” -- “I know, but where would I put you, what for at all?” -- “I am different from all the others that you like!” -- “I know, and I’m really sorry, and I know that I would love to have you around, but too much is simply too much!” -- “You don’t like me as much as you say ...

Blind buy. According to reviews "sexy, sultry, and particularly niche": I couldn't resist, even though a quiet voice in my head was already expressing concerns that I actually don't like orange blossom, as it often manifests as a migraine with headaches and nausea (Hello Armani Code, you trauma!). And pepper has never been my favorite spice either...

A very expressive and almost dominant scent that is softened somewhat by the vanilla over the course of the first approximately 3 hours. Nevertheless, it is a perfume that has something to say and rushes past many others. The roasted sesame is strangely present in my nose the whole time; I am actually waiting for my oh-so-beloved patchouli.

A little (true) anecdote about longevity and sillage: It's half past 6 in the morning in Germany. I've just showered and stand perplexed in front of the perfume shelf. The deep black bottle of L'Interdit Eau de Parfum Intense catches my eye. Why not? It doesn't always have to be understated. I'm a big fan of the L'Interdit line and love all the scents.

That the new CK Women fragrances are not particularly popular is no secret. I tested both in advance at the perfume store, couldn’t find much negative on the first sniff, and ordered samples of both for more extensive testing during my vacation. This review will focus on the Eau de Toilette: It starts off floral-citrusy, which doesn’t bother me, fitting the cheerful to cloudy weather at 20°C. A delicate and sweet character emerges, and I like it so much that I apply a bit more. It vaguely reminds me of the Eau de Parfum, but it is much more agreeable than that one, without the polarizing eucalyptus note, and maybe that’s the problem: It is absolutely interchangeable. After leaving the vacation apartment for a little shopping tour, I forget about it again right away, despite reapplying. Only in the perfume store do I realize that I’m already wearing perfume. Here, I apply it generously and have to notice again that I actually like the scent. Holding the original bottle in my hand, I feel ambivalent about it. The glass is heavy, high-quality, and feels good in the hand, but what’s up with that weird cap with the giant eye? The plastic feels cheap, unwieldy, and I feel like I’m being suspiciously watched, or did that creepy thing just wink at me? I don’t know and test a few other perfumes before daring to venture back into the wild. And once again, I immediately forget CK Women; it has vanished, almost faster than I could spray it on. Really damn unfortunate… We could have been friends, but not with this miserable longevity. Still, I want to give it a second chance and spray it with all my attention, in the safe environment of my four walls, once more: There they are again, the floral and citrus notes, which almost bring a creamy and honey-like quality. All the listed top and heart notes come into play simultaneously, merging into a delicately caressing whisper, from which none of the fragrance notes stands out. I immediately feel spring vibes, despite the autumn late summer. Soon, I notice the first gentle traces of incense, which I also like. And then it fades away softly with a musky touch. But once again, I am almost shocked by its short longevity. In conclusion, I can recommend it to those who enjoy uncomplicated floral spring fragrances and suggest that they definitely spray it in higher doses on clothing, as it is much more long-lasting there than (at least on my) skin. CK Women is not a major hit, but it doesn’t hurt anyone either.

Scent is nice and clean, floral. I remember getting a sample of this at Jo Malone in the morning and while at dinner I could still smell the scent on my hand several hours later. Projection is average to slightly above average. I love the fragrance but for the price there may be others with better value.
