Amongst Jo Malone, this was one of my favorite scents so I bought a bottle. I wear it for myself when I'm at home and it smell great but I don't think it would be a crazy compliment getter with several complex notes. This is just my opinion and I'm relatively new at this hobby so take this review with a grain of (wood sage and sea) salt. =P

This is nice, an easy pleaser. What ? You want me to develop more ? This is something my dad could pull it off, or my boss, or my teacher or my banker, at least someone that wears dress shirt or polo Smells clean and fresh, like a fancy aftershave, like a man that like to take care of himself, or at least once in a while. In my opinion this is a classic male cologne, for someone (in 2024) that is 30+ years old or want to smell like someone that has his life on track. Not bad, not challenging, could be a blind buy gift for someone that fit the above description

Golden afternoon light lies over the hilly landscape, gentle sunbeams caress the leaves of the vines that are slowly turning autumnal and warm the clusters hanging with their plump, almost ripe grapes. A fine fruity hint is already in the air: Which grape could it be that will later accompany us and our meals as a welcome wine? I would love to taste some berries fresh from the vine right away. Proudly, the cypress trees of the nearby avenue stretch their sharp green spears into the air, releasing their spicy resinous aroma; their shadows are slowly growing longer. How I love these sun-warmed southern trees - also the sprawling pines and the cedars with their silk-like shimmering trunks - with their needle garments, which do not skimp on their aromas at this time of day: They embrace generously and allow us to partake in their green life. From somewhere, a cloud of lavender drifts through this golden impression, already touched by afternoon ripeness: Richly spun from flowers, leaves, woods, and earth! I still enjoy the shade, surrounded by the fine moisture of moss and a touch of vetiver, but soon I will step into this wonderful scenery that “Cypress & Grapevine” conjures on my skin and feel comfortable in it for a while - perhaps until sunset? As is well known, I love these clear fragrance creations, as they are so typical of the brands Jo Malone and Patricia de Nicolaï; they are always so cool and fleeting, but perhaps that is precisely why they provide a welcome break or accompaniment for me. “Cypress & Grapevine” is also expressive, but like many of these creations, it is not made for prolonged contact; I do not expect more. That is why I affectionately call this genre “fragrance waters”! My bottle contains only a sediment of this wonderful composition and came to me purely by chance. I have never experienced that there were the usual samples at Jo Malone counters: It was tested on-site, on the skin or on a strip; always accompanied by friendly, knowledgeable conversations. Now, at the end of July, our branch of “Galeries Lafayette” here in Berlin was closed, and for me, after many years (was it 30?) of togetherness, it was only natural to say “Au Revoir” in person; albeit out of cowardice, almost at the last moment! It was very sad to see the beloved gourmet department in twilight, with only a few almost empty shelves left, while attempts were still being made to maintain the illusion of a “normal” sales operation. The feeling of farewell spread. The perfume department did not seem quite as lifeless, even though many of the test bottles and cosmetic and makeup displays (all that lovable little stuff) had already disappeared. I must have looked quite sad when the lady from Jo Malone spoke to me; thus, we started a conversation while she searched for a fragrance here and there and let me test it. We had time! “Cypress & Grapevine” was unfamiliar to me, but I immediately liked the fragrance profile that emerged shortly after spraying; although I would not have purchased it. It was probably due to the exceptional situation that I was gifted this tester - likely before it disappeared into one of the waste/remainder containers. (Can you imagine how many fragrance treasures shared that fate!) So it is not only the mood of a golden moment in the south but also a trace of melancholy, yes, almost sadness, that accompanies me with this summery-spicy freshness and reminds me: Golden autumn, radiant late summer: It was beautiful - merci!

Even a gifted horse should smell good! So I visited my trusted Jo Malone store again, and they gave me this fragrance in a 50ml bottle with my purchase. I'm really into the shower gel and body cream and have spent quite a bit of money there. Anyway… I tried it at home right away, and well, I felt like I was at my sink, a mix of citrus dish soap and red wine. The longevity of the fragrance is, as is typical for Jo Malone, not the best; after about 4 hours, I could hardly perceive the scent anymore. I'm sure it will find its fans, but I won't be one of them.

Lavender, bergamot, and geranium were once, and probably still are, the definition of a fougere fragrance. Many scents call themselves fougere, whether they truly are - difficult to say. This cologne intense could very well be a classic fougere. The lavender at the first spray feels strained and too strong, quickly balanced out by the cedar and amber. Strong memories of Platinum Egoiste come to mind, whether that fits with the fougere is an intriguing question. The lack of longevity cannot be confirmed, the resemblance to Sauvage can only be sensed with great imagination. The next morning, amber is pleasantly noticeable on the palm, something that never happens with other fragrances. For a scent that does not want to be considered mainstream, it does its job well. It’s not enough to be a room filler, yet it is definitely different and very interesting and surprisingly long-lasting. Grape is written on the packaging, but it is not recognizable throughout the entire fragrance journey. The question arises anyway, what a grape is doing in a scent. Instead, the moss comes to the forefront, which may explain the many negative comments.

Cypress & Grapevine Cologne Intense is one of those fragrances that doesn't need to be loud to make an impression. Right from the start, the cypress takes center stage: cool, aromatic, slightly resinous. Not a piercing green, but a controlled cleanliness in the British style. The grape note does not bring fruity sweetness, but rather a dark, dry nuance.

Soft, sweet, and incredibly clean. Smells like warm laundry fresh out of the dryer. It dries down quickly and does not project much. On me, this is almost a skin scent. However, the scent does last all day if you check for it (sniff sniff!) and it leaves a subtle sweetness on clothes that I can get a whiff of when picking up laundry. I’m prone to migraines and nausea from fragrances and this does not trigger any negative response for me. Seems to work well in many seasons as I wore it throughout spring and summer. In super high summer heats it felt a little heavy - but not quite cloying. Now into the fall with freezing temperatures upon us, performance doesn’t seem to be affected and is just as pleasant as when I first tried it. My number one easy reach for work or when I just want to feel pretty and cozy.

This is definitely a beautiful perfume that gets compliments, but the sweet fruity note in it always makes me feel a bit unsure. I couldn’t really detect the woody notes, and they didn’t bother me either. I guess I just couldn’t warm up to that subtle sweetness. If you're transitioning from fresh fragrances, make sure to test it on your skin first. It's certainly not a sugary perfume, but I wouldn’t call it light either. It’s more suitable for seasons other than summer

I'm so happy I picked up a sample of this! I did not enjoy this fragrance. It smelled horribly synthetic and cheap to me. (I'm usually okay with cheapies!) This was way worse than any B&BW I have ever smelled. Besides that, it was also just very generic- a definite perfume smelling perfume, iykyk. It is very floral with some musk and a touch of fruit, but they don't seem to mesh together very well. I can't say anything about performance though- it lasted until a day later in the room even with me airing it out.

after the first spray, i thought i was going to hate it, but it's alright. the opening did not give me the impression of fruit i was expecting, but more of a synthetic shampoo impression, with strong projection. after fully drying down, it became a little bit more powdery/floral, which i enjoyed more than the sparkly opening. then, after a few hours of powdery floral, i was finally able to pick out some of the ambrette/musky aspects. while i liked these base notes the most, i feel like the medicinal shampoo and powder scents got in the way for most of the time that the fragrance was detectable. additionally, while it is fairly pleasant on a strip of cardstock, the fragrance performs unpleasantly on my skin. it feels a bit one-dimensional, and it never blends with my own body scent, instead sitting on top of my skin like a contaminant to be washed away. (i am reminded of working in a wet eeg lab and rinsing baby shampoo and salt from my pruny fingers.) although i don't particularly enjoy it on its own, i like layering it, in a comparatively small dose, with musk-heavy rose fragrances. it adds a little synthetic shimmer.

I'm surprised I love this one! Shouldn't be, it has notes I love - pear, ambrette seed, rose, orris/iris, woods - but the only catch that knocks it down from a 9 or 10 is the synthetic hint in the base. It's a hint too sickly sweet, and kind of plasticky, to be something I'd want to wear every day, but in the right moments, this is something I would enjoy. I finished off a sample bottle because I enjoyed this scent so much, but it's not so amazing that I'm coveting every little drop until I budget a full size. I'm sure a lot of folks would enjoy this scent, and it's inoffensive for an office setting or public transport. I personally prefer green, aquatic, or fresh scents for the office, but if you prefer sweet through and through, this is a nice one.

I loved this fragrance immediately! It's soft, airy and feminine. Sweet but never cloying. The woody notes give it a gentle, clean vibe. The scent bubble is unobtrusive and fairly intimate. In fact, it could be mistaken for an expensive body wash. As skin-scents go, it is very long lasting.

A pretty, pink, girly-girl fragrance. It's safe, lovely and a bit on the perfumey side of things. I won't go there and say it's generic, but it's relatively linear. It's something I've already smelled somewhere in a perfume store. I get a lovely dose of sweet, fruity pear. Next, I'm getting a fruity rose, sweetened and creamy thanks to the orris butter.

Initial super sweet pear cloud settles close to the skin within ~20 minutes and dissolves in a big jar of, well, pink. While I can discern rose and iris notes if I concentrate on them, overall it's just smells super sweet, powdery and pink. It lasts (in a meaningful identifiable way) around ~6 hours, though the smell becomes more flat and one-dimensional after the first ~3.

It's very nice. The start is soft, powdery, and feminine. I want to be able to vote in accords, notes, longevity,ect...Don't know how to!?! I really liked this perfume! Unfortunately... it's not very long lasting!! Beautiful otherwise.

I thought I had already sniffed out all the interesting samples from my little treasure chest, and then while cleaning, I found this little gem at the bottom. Without high expectations, I poured a bit of the roll-on onto my wrist, and then the ZOOM effect. This fragrance has an absolute top note kick that, at least for me, quickly makes me terribly in love: the sweetest violet, dipped in Nivea Absolu, with a hint of gardenia in the background that quickly steps into the spotlight and shines creamy clean. The scent color is pure fabric softener white with a tiny bit of pink. Ah. I’m weak. As an old Iperborea fan, I like Eternity Summer 2011 at first sniff. And even in the following hours, it performs wonderfully - combined with today’s rain on the warm asphalt, it’s an absolute dream. In contrast to Iperborea, which is very similar, CK doesn’t develop as strictly clean, but tender and more floral. It fits better for a slightly younger target audience. The jasmine comes through nicely and gives this seemingly innocent little water a sexy undertone. Later, there’s soft clean musk, a similar tone to what you find in Rodriguez fragrances. It blends beautifully with the scent of my own skin and triggers compulsive, continuous sniffing of my own body. Conclusion: A very special spring and summer fragrance for all who have fallen for the "Nivea" note and enjoy it floral and soft. It feels very well-groomed and refined, making it suitable for really any occasion. It remains quite straightforward in its creamy-floral mood and has no "edges or corners." But that doesn’t always have to be the case.

Eternity Summer 2011...purchased by me of course in 2011, because I liked the bottle with the reddish flower so much. I'm not even sure if I really tested it properly. After that, this perfume sat for about a year in a closed box (wrapped in plastic) neglected in the bathroom. Looking back, I regret not paying attention to it for so long. Once sprayed, I am thrilled. It has a floral/creamy scent and in my mind's eye, I immediately see a large pot of Nivea cream. The longevity is also good for the price. I can only agree with Snowflake...a really great fragrance for every day and also for every season!!!

A fragrance that I like once again, and I find the Eternity summer scents great anyway. To me, it smells like lily of the valley with a creamy note. I can definitely see it as a purchase candidate. Nothing super extraordinary, but a great scent for everyday use.

I was a little confused at first when I smelt The Beat for Men. I was certain that I'd accidently sprayed a female fragrance instead. The scent was so sweet, with a touch of spice, woods and citrus. I now know that I hadn't been mistaken. The Beat for Men is not strictly masculine, I would definitely recommend this fragrance to both men and women. I get a lot of sweet, spicy woods, and I like it, a lot. Like Kevin from the NST blog mentioned, both the female and male versions of The Beat are supposed to represent the 60's era of Rock n' Roll. Well I don't get the booziness or the wildness, however I get a smooth, somewhat delicious scent, that is wonderful for a night out on the town. So many reviewers are saying that this fragrance is too harsh and too peppery, I find this fragrance more spicy than peppery. Perhaps it is just the way my nose perceives this fragrance. I also get a lot of violet and sweet, juicy fruits. The sillage of this fragrance is very strong, and the lasting power almost equally as powerful. I have come to the conclusion that The Beat for Men is a love it or hate it scent. Personally, I really like it.

I actually thought for a long time that apart from Brit and especially London, there was nothing at Burberry worth testing. But after today's test of The Beat, I have to partially revise that. This pepper scent with a woody-floral base is one of the best pepper fragrances on the market for a pepper lover like me. Very unconventional and certainly not loved by the masses - yet it has a great right to exist. At the very beginning, there is a citrus-sage note, and then The Beat quickly becomes very peppery. And not just a little; I have rarely experienced a fragrance with such a clear main theme. And since I always sprinkle my food heavily with pepper, I have no problem with it when it tickles my nose in fragrances as well. Besides the pepper, I perceive a lot of cedar, which in combination reminds me a bit of Terre D'Hermes. Very woody, green, bitter, and masculine. But definitely cool enough for true Britpoppers. I even smell something leathery in the drydown - very rock and wild. Similar relatives are probably Dirty English or Bang. Vetiver and the pepper make up 80% of this very dry scent for me. The bottle is typically Burberry, cool and full of detail. You can recognize Burberry fragrances from afar, and I really like that famous check pattern. The sillage is not exaggerated at all, but due to the piercing pepper note, one should still be cautious. Longevity is easily 8 hours. Does my collection still need a nearly pure pepper fragrance? Who knows. The Beat would certainly be one of the main contenders for that spot. Marc Jacobs Bang doesn't stand a chance against it!

In the book "Le Snob: Parfum" by Dariush Alavi and Patrick Hutsch, which has been recommended here before and I would like to do so again, the cultural factors in the evaluation of a perfume are discussed. For various reasons, the French often have less of a problem with darker, dirtier scents, while for Americans, it almost leads to heart rhythm disturbances. The British often associate lavender with grandma, for the Japanese, sea-inspired creations are equated with the concept of nothing, and us Germans? Allegedly, people here often tend to dislike perfumes that have a lemon base because they subconsciously remind them of harsh cleaning products. I had to chuckle while reading and was also somewhat glad because I might have found a plausible explanation for why "Burberry the Beat for Men" is so unsuccessful here. Perhaps the Brit is flying so far under the radar that he risks crashing to the ground - he has become suspiciously cheap. With what? Certainly not with justification! Be that as it may, anyone who smells cleaning products here has probably sniffed too much glue, because the fresh citrus note comes across as very natural, complemented by vetiver, which gives the Beat a more robust, slightly woody undertone. This is beautifully complementary or, overall, clean yet distinctive. A bit of spice comes through a pinch of pepper in the fragrance microcosm, and what on earth is wrong with that, as long as one doesn't overdo it, which is not the case here. This subtle sharpness is an interesting counterpoint that makes the game even more intriguing. While not many fragrant substances are used here, they are skillfully arranged. Nothing is exaggerated, but also not understated to the point of being uninspired. For me, "Burberry the Beat for Men" is fine understatement, a co-pilot that never becomes intrusive but certainly has something to say without being completely mute. A buddy you go out with who helps you flirt with the opposite sex exactly when needed, but never undermines your own presence. This blend doesn't necessarily create a personality, but it shapes it somewhat in terms of charisma. Domitille Berthier and Olivier Polge have created something here that is positively British; a gentleman maintains composure when necessary but never loses his charm. I could even imagine a modern James Bond wearing this Burberry, following the motto of being somehow "very British," but it no longer requires piercingly intrusive masculinity in fragrance form to represent a real man. At least beyond certain groups. This Beat for men is contemporary, simply in tune with the music, not overloaded, but accentuated.

To begin with, I should tell you how I came across this fragrance: A friend was wearing "Touch" by Burberry and I was smitten - it smelled heavenly. So I tested this fragrance as well (unfortunately without noticing that balsamic-warm-spicy scent on my skin) and took two other fragrances on the unremarkable test strip with me. Well, "The Beat" was supposed to fall into my target range. And my instinct did not betray me. The scent develops on my skin into a sensual, present, yet not at all intrusive canon of light citrus notes with spicy and warm undertones that remind a bit of incense (Benzoin Siam, high-quality frankincense) and honey. Without coming across as artificial, alcoholic, or forced in any way. Or even resembling the hippie-Esoteric-alternative cliché of patchouli-tainted air. For me, the fragrance has been a hit and I also think that women with an affinity for Farfalla scents should test this men's perfume. Since I do not own a television, the advertising campaign completely passed me by and I can proudly say that only my nose in connection with my skin was the reason for the love at first and later sniff ;-)

Many know this "typically British" song by the Beatles, which tells about a quiet street and its everyday occurrences. I think it’s great... And in a way, so is "Burberry's" Beatle-esque "men's fragrance." It is also very calm and immediately reminded me of this song. Why? Because "The Beat" smells very British to me, with a certain understatement, yet it holds its little surprises. The pepper and violet are, by the way, dominant at the beginning of the fragrance. And not shy. ...."he keeps his fire engine clean... it's a clean machine...." Yes, clean, and also fiery, the "fire" is doused with violet. But to think that it should stay that way is a misconception. Soon, geraniums and spices from the greengrocer's waft out of the open shop door. Fresh and inviting. That's how it should be. Mr. Bucksmith is happy to welcome every customer. If there’s one thing that should not be lacking in a nice, robust fragrance, it’s woods and vetiver. After a stroll through "Penny Lane," it continues into a damp, fresh green English forest, where one can completely focus on oneself and the surroundings away from the bustling life. Fresh, spicy air.

It is paradoxical, but even though I only moderately like the second of two scents from this company, I still like this brand. They seem to hire calm perfumers who are allowed to work with ingredients that are not too inferior. What I have smelled from Burberry so far has been somewhat dull over time, but crafted with a steady hand, coherent, and pleasantly unexcitable.

I haven't warmed up to Burberry fragrances so far. Of course, they are designed more as British understatement creations, aside from the hero offshoots. But the well-known spark just didn't ignite for me. The Beat for Men is no exception. In the relatively long-lasting opening, I perceive a somewhat passable synthetic intense lemon accompanied by a good amount of pepper.

Burberry Beat opens very citrusy, and quite sour indeed. This citrus note is accompanied by something herbal-green. At first, I thought of sage or tarragon. It is really very sharp and spicy. It takes half an hour for this character to change. The herbaceousness fades, and the citrus note suddenly is no longer lemon juice, but something artificial.

Sure, with The Beat you’re not just buying a fragrance, but a whole advertising campaign, consisting of a cool name, young conservative dandy types, Britpop (The Fratellis), the delightful Agyness Deyn (at least the model for the female version of the fragrance), and a very trendy bottle. Should one trust so much hipness olfactorily as well?

I have now ordered my 5th bottle from a very affordable online retailer! I have had the fragrance since it was produced. Nevertheless, I must say that I have received more compliments with this scent than with any other in recent times. This is probably because it has few wearers and thus seems almost unique at the moment or stands out extremely from the crowd!

If this perfume has taught me ANYTHING, it is not to trust my nose in store after already smelling a dozen fragrances. I tested a whole range of Jo Malone scents a few weeks ago, lots of florals and bright scents, so the sweetness of this one truly stood out to me. That day, I thought this was just a rich vanilla. I bookmarked it to buy but then decided maybe a decant first. Decant was a brilliant because this smells so different to a virgin nose. First sniff is tequila, very bright & strong, then quickly opens to a spicy cardamom. It took a minute for me to find the vanilla in the background. As it dries down, the sweetness comes out a little more and the woodiness develops. The vetiver smells like less grass and more like teak wood. After about an hour, I loved this one on my skin, although it is more masc leaning than I usually expect from a vanilla. A true unisex scent. In my collection, I think this will be GREAT for layering with vanillas that I find too sweet. I'm not sure if I will actually buy a full bottle, but maybe a travel size or just keep a decant on hand.

I like the concept: Oriental Vetiver. At first, it has a distinct cardamom note, making it spicy and immediately warm. The vanilla also comes in soon, rich and not too sweet, but the namesake sweet grass hardly comes through on my skin. That's a pity, as it lacks the cool-exotic counterpoint. Overall, this Malone strikes me as somewhat borrowed from ELDO's Fat Electrician upon the second sniff, although I prefer the latter because it has a clearer vetiver and the chestnut cream is more refined. As a base, there’s a slightly powdery tonka that makes an impression, but it again reminds me of JM's Myrrh Tonka. Oriental vetiver lovers will surely want to test this, but AugustA doesn’t need to have this one, even though it’s well made.

I love discovery packages! Why? Because they help me discover scents I would never have noticed otherwise. I am a staunch opponent of any vanilla, outside of the base where it’s hard to avoid. And even though I like vetiver, I would never have thought to pick up a tester, let alone spray it on my skin, that already has vanilla in its name. Oh, what I would have missed... The scent reached me within a discovery package and since the sink and Linda hand sanitizer were ready, I was brave enough to spray this sample on my wrist. What unfolded on my skin was not the dreaded vanilla bomb, but a sauna infusion, and I love saunas. Completely perplexed by how something with such a dreadful name for me can smell so great, I sniffed my wrist every 5 minutes for the next few hours. It really smells like a sauna infusion. I can almost feel the heat. The scent is warm, spicy, soothing, and surprisingly complex for Jo Malone, in my opinion. Although only cardamom is listed as a spice, which is clearly noticeable, I feel like I can perceive a variety of other spices underneath. The vetiver brings in a slightly woody note, completing the image of the sauna for me.

I have a special relationship with Jo Malone fragrances. I am a total fan of the ... (what do I call it)...purity (?) of the scents. I would describe almost all from the house as "pleasant." However, I haven't found one that I would personally like to wear as a perfume. I think it's the perfect decision that Jo Malone sells their fragrances as candles, because for me, most of the scents are somehow really "candle scents" (even though it almost feels like a "sacrilege" to call such pleasant fragrances just that, but that's how I feel...). But now to this specific scent: Vetiver & Golden Vanilla is one of the few fragrances from Jo Malone that I also see as a perfume. For me, it is a beautiful, warm spicy (rather masculine) vetiver scent. Nothing new, but simply pleasant!

For me, this is the best vetiver scent I have smelled so far. The vanilla is really only subtly noticeable and beautifully rounds off the whole experience. It's not particularly unique, but it is the fragrance for which I have received the most compliments from women in the short time I have owned it.

... not to buy it. Sprayed it in the store. Thought "oh this is definitely a men's scent, what a shame." Drove home. Regularly the bottle hung on my wrist, because now the vanilla was there. A warm, full vanilla. There is great annoyance, because the store is 45 minutes away from me. A week later, I can't take it any longer. Blissfully acquired the scent.

I'm surprised by Ange Ou Demon. Prior to testing this fragrance I had assumed it was similiar or along the lines of Armani Code for women and Thierry Mugler's Angel, however I find it much softer and in some ways more mysterious. Ange Ou Demon isn't as gothic and dark as the bottle seems to suggest. There's this undeniable softness and fragility which adds to this fragrance's allure. The scent is light and 'fluffy', almost airy with subtle hints of spicyness, like pepper or thyme. There is also a distinctive powdery-like quality to Ange Ou Demon which is reminiscent of some classic aldehydic fragrances. I enjoy Ange Ou Demon's spicy yet powdery scent, because like D&G for Women, this is a powdery fragrance that isn't sharp or soapy, instead it's inviting and sensual. When applied with a light hand, (as one should always do), the sillage is just strong enough to capture the people that dare to come close. I particularly like this aspect because it certainly adds to this perfume's mysterious appeal. Apart from the dominant notes of spices, florals and vanilla, I also sense a cinnamon note, which reminds me of Intimately Beckham Night, which is in some ways very similar to Ange Ou Demon. I'd say the lasting strength of this scent is good, however I fear this fragrance will be reformulated soon due to the oakmoss component. I highly suggest you try this scent while it is still in its original formulation.

While out walking a canine friend one spring morning, flowers bursting all over the neighborhood, I thought, "Man all these flowers smell amazing!" I quickly realized that incredible burst of florals was actually the Ange ou Demon emanating from my wrist. Wow! I had it applied only a small amount to one wrist to test, and already this scent was wafting around me. It is, indeed, incredibly sweet. But also spicy and exotic. The mandarin orange gives it a little punch, and the florals are dreamy and just dripping with sweet vanilla. The woody notes really anchor it and give it that notable sensuality. What a perfect name "Ange ou Demon" (Angel or Devil) - it's so versatile. It seems to perfectly conform to how you decide to wear it. A playful, sweet and feminine daytime fragrance? Sure! A seductive (perhaps naughty) nighttime perfume? Absolutely! Lastly, I disagree that it's strictly a cold-weather scent. I'd wear this any time of the day, any time of the year, it's incredible! Long lasting with incredible sillage, too.

Every angelic face hides a devilish persona ange ou demon definse that. it starts sweet and half a hour later transform to an deep intoxicating notes of dark florals and dry woods makes it a versitile frangrance for the ages. The opening starts sharp with a note of mandrian orange dries gracfully with the velvety feel of Saffron and dries the top notes with the innocent notes of thyme and White Lily, The middle section starts to become more deeper with the presence of dark orchid and the wisting scent of nocturnal jasmine bloom though the night. The drydown is an dry finishing scent of oakmoss vanilla adds to the angelic sweetness to the frangrance exotic brazilian rosewood and ends with the nutty accord of tonka bean. I just love the flacon design and color the coloring is reminisent of the sun setting though the twillight sky on a clear night i also love the jagged artwork of the bottle worthy of it's demonic edgeiness there is nothing soft about this scent this is for a girl who is sweet on the outside but deliciouslly bad from the inside.

Ylang ylang... Now we are talking about. When a scent contains ylang ylang flower in a big dose its becoming sometimes exotic fruity floral sometimes lux soft creamy floral. In both situations I enjoy that. Ange ou Demon edp gained so much disslikes in fragrantica. I think that scent doesnt deserve this. Beginning= Mandarin orange, very soft sweet floral with bit earthiness of saffron. I dont enjoy saffron generally (I hate mfk br 540 edp) but here its well-combined. Time to time-its rare-but I feel herbal thyme too. Then after hours vanilla+ tonka bean sweetness with soft florals= these are ylang ylang and lilly. I thought before my first smell its heavy scent because of saffron but it isnt! +I got Play doh smell too. :) Best season= Fall, winter and spring. If you insist, you can spray less in summer nights. Occasion= It gives me warm and cozy effect so lots of time its suitable. Home, dinner, mall, friends meeting, job meeting, with family or relatives... Compliments= I see some boys are crazy for this smell. I hope I can get compliment. At least my darling liked it. :)

Givenchy has a fine history of great perfumes. I love Ysatis, Amarige and Organza. Therefore I had great expectations when finally meeting Ange ou Demon. The name alone makes me expect a transformation of some sort or a very varied scent. However, this is not my experience. The white thyme and the mandarin orange start this scent incredibly well. After ten minutes the flowers appear and softens the almost minty-fresh expression, especially the Yang-ylang is strong here. Underneath there is a lovely vanilla and something spicy. The bottle is interesting. I like the way it changes from the dark top to the light bottom. If I saw it without knowing I would have thought it to be part of the Mugler collection. Nice scent, a bit anonymous to my nose, but I acknowledge that many parfumistas love it. To me it is could be the smell of angels. Definitely not demons. 90/365

This is what I can best describe as a "cologne for women" It is bold, alluring, hypnotizing. The perfume commands attention and declares "I embody sensuality" I waited for years to try this perfume but as soon as I smelled it, I bought it. It almost reminds me of an oriental chypre. One of the best perfumes in my collection.

Not a scent for well-behaved, conforming girls and nothing for young women who are still practicing flirting. No Chérie and no Lolita! Dark, deep, and extravagant, this fragrance belongs to the Femmes Fatales and the sirens among us.

Yes, why did I wait so long? That is exactly the question I ask myself in connection with my latest acquisition "Ange ou Démon" by Givenchy. Before Corona, I preferred to buy my perfumes at the duty-free shop in airports. I can't remember how many times I have hovered around "Ange ou Démon." Of course, the name intrigued me. I fondly remember a former colleague.

It was a crisp, cold winter day when I first truly took notice of Ange ou Demon. And since Givenchy as a brand of upscale mainstream and especially fragrances with a certain something already have a bonus for me, regardless of whether I like them or not, it was examined more closely.

Ladies and Gentlemen! In the left corner, angel "Ange" de Angelo, in the right corner, the opponent devil "Démon" Beelzebub. Gong! The fight has begun. Round 1 (Top Note): ------------------- A clamp attack from de Angelo: He tries to shove a juicy mandarin into Beelzebub's face. But he gobbles it up, and what remains is the bitter, spicy mandarin peel along with the skin.

That's what I think of the Euphoria EDT bottle. This is a nice little oriental floral with good lasting power. I've been on a quest for the past year to try everything with champaca flower in it and this one doesn't disappoint! I tend to love perfumes with green in them too, and this one opens with lovely green notes and peach. The peach is not as prominent as I wish it were, but you can't have everything I guess. This leans to the soft sexy side, but still I think it's a fine scent for the day time and work.

I found this randomly at the Duty Free in Antalya and bought it on a whim, as I had to leave quickly. Well, every time I smell it, I think of a futuristic Cyberpunk lady, sipping a cocktail at a bar with an amazing view of the city. The woman is young, just like this fragrance compared to the original Euphoria, which is more suited for mature women. It's like the original but a bit fruitier; despite everything, it feels somewhat heavy on the skin and has a metallic quality. I find it quite nice, but I don't wear it often because it's more suitable for specific occasions like clubbing or dates, rather than an everyday scent. I'm still a fan; I like the original just a little bit more.

This was the first Burberry fragrance that I didn't fall head over heels in love with. Usually I'm lucky with their fragrances because they're often flowery, light or sweet, however Brit Sheer was far too fruity for my liking. I enjoyed both the EDT and EDP versions of Brit, so I immediately assumed I would like this fragrance. I often find that if I have high expectations before smelling a scent, I am usually left disappointed. The pineapple note is far too strong and when mixed with the yuzu note, it creates something that is sour and acidic smelling. To some people this fragrance is refreshing and clean, however fruity or citrusy fragrances don't usually appeal to my tastes in perfume. I much prefer soft floral scents. Even though Brit Sheer isn't my type of fragrance, this perfume doesn't strike me as being anything special. It is far too generic and safe. The lasting strength is also a disappointment, not lasting any longer than 2 hours. Edit: I have forced myself to re-test this and I must admit that it smells much nicer on the skin. I'm beginning to sense a delicate, sparkling pink grapefruit scent. On a warm day this is quite refreshing.

This baby rose gem is a beautiful, citric fragrance with lots of potential. I got is as a gift many years ago and have been using it every summer. Just recently I emptied the bottle - the smell intact with all the volatile top notes (to my nose they are dominantly lychee and mandarin). I usually like the heavier fragrances with loads of spices, but I fell in love with the mix of sweet and sour notes. I have a weakness for peach and lychee, and in this perfume they combine so nicely. Bottom line to this Burberry Brit flanker is that it makes me happy when I wear it. It does not last long and sillage is poor but sometimes it is nice to wear something descreet and delicate. That is what you get with this fragrance. Eventhough I have lots of fragrances I would consider buying it again. (Day 1 of 365)

I was really excited for this perfume, as it has a lot of notes that i like, but I ultimately found that it was too bitter smelling, i definitely don't smell any pineapple or orange. I'm not sure if that's just how Yuzu smells but it almost smells like a sharpie or lemon cleaning supplies. I will wear again but probably layer it with something sweeter to balance the smell.

It’s light, fresh, watery notes make it smell like a shower gel. It’s not unpleasant at all. Not too fruity or sweet so it’s a nice balance for someone who wants to wear a scent but not overwhelm a room. The longevity was moderate and the sillage was very low. It was noticeable by me, but wasn’t traveling far or overwhelming.

I find check patterns absolutely terrible. Especially checked backpacks. And I’ve forbidden my husband from wearing checked shirts (not that he ever had that in mind, but better safe than sorry). The only thing I occasionally allow myself is my corset with tartan checks. But those stuffy Burberry checks should stay away from me. I also don’t really connect with the scents, even though my aversion isn’t quite as strong. The top note is usually still quite zesty, but then they often have something bland and generic. Brit Sheer is just such a candidate. The first 5 minutes I find really good. Yuzu and mandarin are pleasantly fresh and not piercing. A nice pick-me-up that I needed this Sunday morning anyway. However, the freshness soon fades, and next comes something fruity. Lychee and peach (to me, it smells more like the fruit than the blossom). It somehow feels very watered down, smoothed out... as if they want to make sure nothing goes wrong. Scents with lychee can be so beautifully energetic and zesty, but unfortunately, you don’t notice any of that here. Interestingly, the fruity notes completely retreat after 2 hours, and everything becomes floral. I rarely like peonies in fragrances. The scent is just meaningless to me. The peach blossom finally appears now, with a hint of Nashi. The latter is actually a fruit as far as I know, but now it smells more powdery and very floral. I find it almost intrusive, but that’s probably because I just don’t like the combination. That such a scent needs a lot of white musk in the base is somehow clear. For that ultimate clean woman feeling. The association that comes to my mind is STUFFY. But not in the sense of outdated and old-fashioned, rather the concentrated cliché of a perpetually smiling, overly friendly lady who wants to represent virtue in person, but somehow you can tell that something is off. Either she beats her children or has an affair with a married man, commits shoplifting, or drinks too much... take your pick. In any case, she floats in a cloud of Burberry Brit Sheer, wonderfully fitting her slick demeanor, but ultimately somehow discordant and annoying. The sillage is not exactly overwhelming but consistently present and doesn’t diminish even after half a day. The scent easily lasts throughout the day. If you like it, that’s really perfect. However, I can’t say how it develops in winter yet. However, it seems to me more suitable for a summer dress (of course pure white and perfectly ironed) than for a winter coat. To all those who appreciate the scent and the Burberry brand, I would say not to let my criticism ruin Brit Sheer for them. The quality is absolutely right for this price range. Whether you like the scent or not is once again just a matter of taste.

Today I looked for fragrance special offers at Karstadt - tried this and that, but wasn't necessarily convinced. There stood, shy and lonely, a pink bottle in the corner - of course without a tester. Brit Sheer. My attentive husband pointed it out to me, especially since he likes Burberry.

A few weeks ago, Burberry Brit Sheer was on the sale table in my perfume shop. I was actually there to get the original Brit, but because the bottle was so beautifully pink, I just sprayed a little on a test strip. The scent kept drawing me in... Heaven, it's so good! In the end, I bought Brit Sheer instead of Brit, and since I got it, I can't keep my nose away from it.

Burberry - fake scarves around the necks of the English working class and hooligans with that notorious check pattern on their baseball caps. That's what comes to my mind first about this brand. I have been rejecting scarves with their typical pattern for years, and the brand's fragrances as well.

At first, it smells quite nice, especially on the skin. But within half an hour, it quickly fades away and leaves nothing that could impress. Just an ordinary floral scent. :/ So, anyone who likes floral fragrances might find some enjoyment here.

Blind buy and I am conflicted and disappointed. I’ve worn Poppy & Barley for a few days now, and honestly, I just don’t... The violet note is really prominent and reminds me a lot of the violet in Insolence by Guerlain, which I can’t stand, it actually makes me feel a bit nauseous. Poppy & Barley isn’t as sweet, thank goodness. Even though I wouldn’t say the rest of the notes are similar at all, I can’t help but notice the extreme resemblance in the violet note. It’s super strong at first and starts to fade after about 20 minutes. That might not seem like a long time, but if you don’t like the smell, 20 minutes feels like forever. For those first 20 minutes, all I can smell is violet; it really overpowers everything else. After that, what’s left is this really tart scent that lingers until the fragrance wears off. I think it’s mostly from the blackcurrants. It’s not bad, but I wish it had more of an aromatic fruity vibe instead of being so sour. If that makes sense. My biggest letdown, though, is the lack of barley and powderiness. They’re practically non-existent. I was hoping for an airy, floral, fresh/fruity, and earthy powdery perfume, but this just isn’t it.

Sharp and clean overall impression, almost like a white tea. Initially I get a hint of that floral, but the fruit scent takes the forefront. Very light musk in the dry down, only smell a very subtle impression of barley or rye but not as much as I'd hope with the name. Guess that's on me, Jo Malone names seem straightforward but they're honestly never as complex as I want them to be.

It is shareable, but leans a little towards the feminine side (it has a delicate essence). Reminds me of a beautiful, classy, intelligent and educated woman. When I think of a woman involved (and asserting herself) with social projects and commitments to society, I think of this perfume. I can imagine this perfume with white clothes, satin fabric. I imagine a bride at the wedding with the presence of intimate people and the cake with champagne. The notes are distributed harmonically. The powdery notes are noticeable, a divine talc in the right measure. But the blackcurrant note is the one that stands out the most, as it gives a fruity touch (albeit fresh, not sweet) to a floral and powdery fragrance. It's a contained perfume that doesn't get to stay in the air. It is intimate, however, unique. It's almost a white wine tending to dry (without being exactly dry) from specific grapes that only grow in a certain region.

This is lovely clean, chic perfume. Perfect for everyday wear, it’s elegant and intriguing but not too sweet. To my nose it opens with a fresh floral of garden rose, violet and a hint of fig and blackcurrant blended so well that at first your nose struggles to differentiate the notes with a slight scratchy, dryness from the powder that pulls you in, intrigued to discover more. It settles on my skin lovely, with a soft fresh, green violet and garden rose and a light comforting white musk. The fig, now slightly creamy, dances with nutty salty bran that oddly compliments the blackcurrant. There is a little tingle of sweet and salty mustiness in the powdery dry down with the grains interacting with the musk, with a dustiness to it, that reminds me of paper pages in a really old book. I really like this perfume. It’s understated yet intriguing at the same time with a sophisticated yet practical vibe. Collection Status: First bottle was a gift a few years ago. It’s steadily been in my collection for a few years now and will remain.

When I had my first whiff of Poppy & Barley in store, it smelled pretty, soft and feminine. Unfortunately, once the fragrance was on my skin, (after purchasing a full-size bottle) it smelled terribly gross. Just did not work my skin chemistry at all. The only positive thing I can say about this perfume is that at least it lasts a strong 20 minutes with absolutely ₊˚no˚₊‧ sillage

I don't know what poppies and barley smell like in real life, but to me it's a sweet floral, almost honeyed scent with a sharp tartness, probably from blackcurrants. It's much stronger than you'd expect from a cologne. It lasts all day on me, and when I apply it close to my neck, it becomes intrusive. I save it for cold weather.

This is an extremely pleasant, dust-inspired scent. Think: you’re at the barn and just brought the horses in. It’s a dry day, so their hooves have disturbed the dirt in the ring and dust is flying around, but nearby sits a field of blooming flowers ripe with pollen and impregnating the air.

On my skin, I first experience the powdery, ionones of violet, immediately followed by light, sweet fig and juicy blackcurrant. These notes are tailed by musky barley, bran and wheat - musky and slightly earthy. The floral notes of the Poppy flower are there, more in the background nuancing, But every note and then coming through loud and clear.

'In the big red house down by the river lives Madita. There also live Mama and Papa and the little sister Elisabet, a black poodle named Sasso, and the kitten Gosan. And then there’s Alva. Madita and Elisabet share the children's room, Alva is in the girls' room, Sasso is in a basket in the hallway, and Gosan is in front of the stove in the kitchen.
Poppy & Barley is a fragrance that captivates me greatly. An atypical scent. It is related to Florabotanica . Not that it smells the same, but the style of composition is very similar.

On paper, Organza's list of notes reads like something I should run from as though my life depended on it, given the fact it contains every white floral in existence (okay, that's an exageration, but not much of one!), but because of its masterful use of all the other notes in conjunction with the florals, it is an enchanting, sweet, woody, nutty, slightly floral spice bomb with a very classic feel. There is SO much going on here, it really is one of those kitchen sink fragrances (as in "everything but the . . . "), with the very edible notes of nutmeg, walnut and vanilla, swirling together with all those flowers, citrus and woods, and yet Organza doesn't feel confused, nor does it suffer from too many disparate notes competing for attention. In fact, given the strong presence of white florals, this has to be one of the most masterful blending accomplishments in the history of perfumery, for me (bona fide non-white floral enthusiast that I am) to love it like I do, and it to feel as rich, cozy, warm and inviting as it does. A classic blend fit for a lady in a beautiful evening gown, or for a regular gal (like me) in office attire, sitting at her desk. It's all good.

Givenchy's ORGANZA is a gentle, pretty oriental floral with not-so-good staying power in the edp. This seems to be a part of a grand campaign/conspiracy in the mass industry: do not make strong perfumes, else you won't sell many bottles! Well, that was a bit cynical, but there is a huge difference between the staying power of a bona fide edp in the classical sense and edps ostensibly made for the so-called modern woman. Anyway, ORGANZA is a slightly spicy, mildly sweet bouquet with lots of woodiness in the drydown. This is a likeable fragrance--very wearable, but perhaps not terribly memorable... I truly dislike the bottle, which is rare for me. This seems like a case of trying way too hard, and all of the ornate weirdness--the woman's hourglass figure and flowing dress, the Grecian pillar effect, the curled-up edges of the cap/head--ends by leaving me with no real impression at all except that maybe the bottle is trying to compensate for its contents. Well, it certainly wouldn't be the first time that package was prioritized to product... ORGANZA is wearable, don't get me wrong, but I never really warmed up to it and eventually swapped my large bottle away.

I remember first time smelling this… my son had turned one year and I was dying to wear perfume again. During the first year of my son’s life I had not worn any. I was told that the baby recognizes the mother’s scent and wearing perfume would make it impossible and therefore worry the baby. So for a whole year I stopped using perfume. Now was the time. I found Organza at the local perfume shop. It was quite new at the time and I tried this among several others. I was sure at first spray: this was going to be my first post-pregnancy perfume. It has been in my collection since. I turn to it when I want to recall those first days of my new life as a mother. But it also smells great. Luca Turin puts it so well: A fine instance of vulgarity done exactly right. I could not have expressed it better. And being abstinent for a whole year - this was just what I needed. The most interesting thing about this is that my son, when smelling it, says that he remembers it very well. Apparently, it opens a door to memories he usually has no access to. The scent is warm and full, and I specifically notice the nutmeg and the walnut notes. These two notes add a rare feeling to the scent. A beautiful depth to the whole picture. Grojsman and Labbé have really made it this time. And the bottle? Oh my! What a masterpiece! It really stands out, adding to the whole experience. Serge Mansau must be proud of himself. 91/365

So, from my experience, the house of Givenchy has always specialised in making distinctly feminine perfumes. In the sense that the one this reminds me of (which my mother used to own) was Ysatis, which again was a very grown up and feminine fragrance. With Organza, I get a sweet honeyed jasmine with supporting notes of tuberose and gardenia. There's also orange flower and honeysuckle and this really comes across as another variation on a sweet, white floral. The vanilla, amber and nutmeg, along with the soft woods, really ground this fragrance and lend it a very smooth aspect. Well-rounded and complete - nothing lacking here, very polished. Overall, I think it's a beautiful smell. The really great thing here is that it's not really a cloying monster or a badly done fragrance in any way. It's balanced perfectly and with style. I could see this working for dates and nights out with a loved one. Not clubbing but very intimate and personal moments and occasions with a partner. I see it also as something of an evening perfume. I believe it's very sultry and womanly. I could recommend it as the quality is there. You would probably have to be okay with a white floral done well, with a hint of honey and warmth. For what it does, it hits the mark. Really quite good.

I was repelled by this back in the late 90's when I was a young 20-something. It was all wrong for me then, but then I scored a vintage mini-splash bottle of this over Memorial Day weekend for four bucks. This is so right for me now as a 40-something woman!!! This is nothing like Organza Indecence; they are totally different. This is all grown-up florals, with a strong amber drydown; very little vanilla comes through on me. Very heady, but not headache-inducing. Sillage is strong, and it lasted all day. I've never smelled Kai, but lots of celebrities apparently wear it because it makes them feel confident and as if they can succeed at anything. Organza is like this for me. I am so glad that I didn't let my past prejudice allow me to pass up this gorgeous beauty.

About 20 some years ago I was strolling through a department store and more bored than interested I tried Organza. Didn't do much for me, at least so I thought, and I went on to the movie theatre with my hubby right afterwards. And while I was sitting there, I couldn't keep my nose off my wrist. It was just the greatest aroma.

It was the 1996 when the beautiful model Yasmeen Ghauri appeared on the magazines wearing a very sexy white dress like a greek goddess: it was the advertisement of this wonderful perfume: a hymn to timeless feminity. I adored immediately at first smell this fragrance: first, the neroli and gardenia notes arrived to my nose, made spicy by the nutmeg touch.

I liked Organza at first. Initially it was quite sweet yet spicy at the same time. The combination was something that I really enjoyed. The opening was a delicate mix of sugary white florals, spicy nutmeg and zesty bergamot. I loved the richness of Organza, it was elegant and sophisticated.

Top Notes: Bergamot, African Orange Flower, Gardenia, Nutmeg, Green Notes. Heart Notes: Honeysuckle, Tuberose, Jasmine, Iris, Walnut, Peony. Base Notes: Vanilla, Amber, Cedar, Guaiac Wood, Woodsy Notes. After reading the many glowing reviews and carefully considering the notes, I blindly bought this, and I must say I am very glad I did so.

Just as sensual as it claims to be, Organza is a remarkably delicious, spicy blend of vanilla and white florals. The amber, wood and nutty notes really warm this one up, as well as provide a lot of its depth and complexity.

Eternity Purple Orchid is really nothing like the original Eternity. This flanker is not so clean and flowery, in some ways it seems darker and more unique. I was initially struck by how sweet and plummy the scent was. It was somehow rich and dramatic, yet light and airy at times. I enjoyed it because it had this interesting sensual and fruity soapiness, which was rather difficult to describe. The fruit notes, like the peach and plum are quite candied and jam-like, so when blended with the soft, soapy floral accords, Eternity Purple Orchid smells like a watered-down, flowery gourmand. If that is even possible. I guess the almond and vanilla notes towards the drydown further my opinion. Despite being a confusing fragrance to my nose, it was one that I quite liked. For the first few hours I couldn't stop smelling it. At times it can be a little chemical smelling and bland, but when compared to other Eternity flankers, this fragrance fares quite well. The packaging itself, with its eye-catching purple bottle, is quite alluring. It's hard to walk past such an interesting looking fragrance. I think in a weird kind of a way, Eternity Purple Orchid, while not an orchid based scent, is very 'purple' in its approach. What I'm trying to say is that the colour suits the scent's personality. Unfortunately the longevity is not all that impressive. I would have liked the fragrance to last just that little bit longer. But all in all, I'm happy to have found this fragrance before it disappears altogether as it was an experience in itself.

A purple darling and a wonderful flanker that actually smells very little like the original Eternity - which is a good thing since having the same perfume re-created over and over again is a bit pointless. When applied it bursts out in green notes and lots of florals, not in an overly floral way but in a warm, sensual way. I guess its due to the woodsy and musk note that almost immediately join the "purple" bouquet of flowers that unfolds. Halfway before the dry-down I smell something light and breezy (water lily?) and a hint of fruit that compliments this elegant, and fresh fragrance very well. A sensual and somewhat heavier formulation than the original Eternity. More suitable for evening wear. Elegant and sexy in a sophisticated way. Silage is: "elegant warm florals are all around me" - Longevity is great: 7+ hours of purple flower haze. If you can still find it try it. It's an Eternity reminiscent scent with a darker, warmer and sexier twist.

There's something about Calvin Klein fragrances that have never agreed with me. There's an alcoholic quality that seems to singe my nose hairs a bit, no matter how pleasing the notes accompanying the mixture tend to be. On the bright side, this is an upbeat almost citrusy, fresh smelling floral. When I go in to smell it, I think, "Well, that's not so bad!" And then comes the aforementioned alcoholic 'aftersmell' that dries the back of my throat, and gives it a soapy masculine bite that just doesn't agree with me.

With your best friend, you can usually talk about anything. Secrets are entrusted to her, stories about men are exchanged, and you like to go out in the evenings with her. Eternity Purple Orchid is the best Eternity variant I know. It is significantly more seductive than the original. The color purple perfectly matches the scent. The scent of the purple vanilla flower, also known as Heliotrope, and the aroma of fully ripe plums enhance the wonderful orchid character. Almonds and musk are also present. Woods, green notes, fruits, and water lily, as listed in the fragrance notes, I cannot perceive. The relationship to the original lies in the musk and in the Freesia that I love above all. Overall, it is a fantastic scent and a very successful variant for going out. Unfortunately, I cannot rate the scent higher due to its low longevity and scent intensity - what a shame! Like Eternity Love, this is a limited edition. Acquiring it is difficult, but not impossible. On eBay, it is often offered in a three-piece Eternity miniature set, especially in Great Britain. The purchase is worth it.

If violet were a scent... the color of the bottle and the fragrance match incredibly well here. It smells softly feminine, fresh, and a bit floral, but not too much. The green notes and woods capture it very well. A fragrance that has a calming effect while also being aphrodisiac. It has something mysterious and mystical about it. Aphrodite would surely have had it in her collection. I wear this scent when I want to express an extra dose of confidence and individuality. And yet, it also carries a creative, sensitive, and intuitive aura. Just very feminine. It's a shame that it is no longer produced or at least not available in Germany anymore.

It's a vibe rather than individual notes, which is something I've noticed with the other Kurdjian scents I've tried. It's clean, fruity, floral, soapy. What are the fruits and flowers? No idea, nothing stands out on its own. That's nice in some ways, it's pleasant, but it's also kind of boring? I think there are others in this category that I like better, like Diptyque or Ralph Lauren Romance.

Almost every Burberry makes me shrink. No, not into an old hag. As soon as one of them touches my skin, I feel myself getting smaller and younger, my voice becomes squeaky, the feminine.....uh....attributes disappear and within seconds I feel like I am 8 years old again. At most. Then I feel the almost irresistible urge to joyfully skip across a postcard-like flower meadow, to swing towards the sky like Heidi, and to roll down the hills with Peter the Goat Herd. “My Burberry Blush” takes it a step further. I sprout blonde corkscrew curls that gracefully bob up and down in sync while skipping through the meadow. Additionally, I suddenly wear a delicate white lace dress and matching, utterly adorable sandals. I feel sugary sweet and absolutely lovely. The only problem is - I find long hair terrible. Delicate dresses too. Especially with lace. And white even more so. As a child, I already loudly insisted on short hair because the long fuss annoyed me, and I would scream bloody murder when my mom wanted to put me in “pretty things.” That damned stuff itched, scratched, pressed, and pinched everywhere. I hurt myself pretty badly rolling down hills many years ago, swinging now makes me feel sick, and there are ticks in tall meadows. This fragrance is so cute, so pretty, so innocent, so fresh like the young morning..... and so not me at all.

... if it were here. Yesterday, my friend and I - dripping wet from the continuous rain - wandered through the department store and took a break in the perfume section. Oh - a new My Burberry! I had a rough start with the EdP back then - it was more of a love at second sight. But Blush is much more approachable and instantly evokes sympathy. This is what summer could be - if it were actually happening. But Blush pushes the gray rain clouds aside and shines out of the bottle. A very sunny English fragrance - although I have experienced its homeland in a similar way. Lemon and pomegranate start off fresh - mixed with crisp apple. Rose and geranium soothe, and the wisteria adds its exquisite note to round it off. Blush concludes with subtle British elegance. A familiar, positive scent - with good longevity, to which I can directly say Yes!

During my last city stroll, I sprayed My Burberry Blush and the scent somehow captivated me and hasn't let go since. I absolutely wanted to have it. Now I have it, and I still like it, but... somehow it's different from the other fragrances I know from Burberry. It's so pleasing and almost cries out: "please, please love me." I don't find that bad, as everyone wants to feel liked and loved. Still, I suddenly feel like something is missing. My Burberry Blush has no edges or corners. It starts with cheerful/friendly lemon and apple. Pretty quickly, rose and jasmine join in, and that's it. I can't really imagine a scent note under wisteria, and I don't perceive any other component. Nothing jabs or pricks, and that's probably exactly what "bothers" me. For me, it's just too perfect. I wanted exactly such a "good mood fragrance." Now I'm not satisfied with that either. My Burberry Blush is like Rosamunde Pilcher in a bottle. Cute cottages in Cornwall, pastel-colored roses, and apple trees with plump, juicy apples in the garden. We women are strange creatures. First, we wish for something, and when we get exactly that, we start searching for the fly in the ointment. Yet the scent is made for spring and summer. Maybe the weather is to blame. That must be it, for sure. My Burberry Blush probably just needs spring-like or even summery temperatures to truly unfold. It will definitely get at least one more chance (probably more like two or three), because it is really beautiful. I find the bottle really well done, which I can't say about the packaging of its checkered brothers and sisters. The 30 ml version lacks the pink ribbon, but I can overlook that. My Burberry Blush is clearly a women's fragrance, as I can't imagine a guy I would want to smell it on, and I also doubt that men want to smell like this. The sillage is rather weak or at least weaker than I'm used to from the other fragrances of the British traditional house. The longevity is also less than with the others. For me, it lasts about 4, at most 5 or 6 hours. Update 19.05.18 My Burberry Blush and I do not match, although I still find the scent very successful, but just not for me, and therefore I gifted it to my youngest daughter today. She was absolutely thrilled with the first spray, and it definitely suits her better.

I like powdery, soapy, shampoo-like scents and I fell for this one when a blogger spoke so beautifully about it. But no, this is not at all what I had imagined. It does give a fresh feeling, but it has too few flowers, too little powder in it, and simply smells sour (probably due to pomegranate and lemon). I miss amber and/or a little musk here. Such a shame. However, I find the bottle very pretty. Those who can wear this scent are lucky. I'm a bit envious;-)

I sniffed this at Douglas yesterday and fell in love immediately. I have been searching for a scent that smells like sunscreen for a long time. With this, I have found it. A friend immediately noticed this scent and asked if I had used sunscreen. The fragrance lasts a long time and is very intense. Anyone who likes the scent of Nivea sunscreen should check this fragrance out.

My Burberry Blush is the first fragrance from the My Burberry line that I quite like. "Quite like" - it's not the ultimate best perfume in my collection, and I wouldn't repurchase it. This perfume falls into the "smells like freshly showered" category. It starts fresh and slightly zesty, before gradually moving into a lovely floral direction.

If I could write stories and fairy tales, I would write about this perfume. I have many perfumes in my collection, from designer to luxury, and I really have a wide selection of perfumes that I can use multiple times a day. Perfumes are my passion, which has existed since my childhood. But there is one among many that has never left me indifferent, and that is Blush.

It took me quite a while to get my head around this one ... I generally don't like the Jo Malone fragrances but I've persisted here and to my delight have come to recognize a fair bit of uniqueness about this creation. I guess my newfound appreciation for Violet Leaf is tickling this particular fancy! I have a number of compositions in my collection containing this note ... Boucheron's Jaipur Bracelet, Gucci's Gracious Tuberose and Dior's Fahrenheit to name a few ... but not until Red Roses have I appreciated it fully. The crisp, almost metallic greenness my nose is presented with is most satisfying! Strangely enough, I'm not one with a fondness for the sweet powdery, woody-floral scent of actual violets, which is due to the ionones in the flowers. The scent of violet leaves is different ... they give off an intensely green aroma which resembles mown grass with a hint of cucumber ... tout à fait merveilleux!! The freshness of Red Roses is further exacerbated by the addition of Mint, which to some has lent this fragrance a 'toothpaste' mien. I don't get that feeling here ... rather just a slightly 'sparkling' idea, and a tartness provided no doubt by the Lemon. When all is said and done, however, Red Roses is all about just that ... big, red, velvety Roses ... speckled with dew and the vibrance of a summer morning. I can't be sure what the origin of this Rose is, but it definitely is big and blousy, with none of the earthiness contained for example in Damascus or Taif Rose. Hazarding a guess I would be more inclined to steer in the direction of Bulgarian roses ... and yes, I know that most roses come from this strain but where they grow vastly affects the scent. Roses grown in drier climes are woodier in fragrance ... at least to my nose! I could also be completely wrong and simply be experiencing a well crafted aroma chemical :). I'm glad that I stuck it out on this one, and while I haven't become a Jo Malone convert I am a Rose freak and this one is sufficiently different to have a place in my collection. The price Red Roses retails for is tragic (I have the bath oil too) and there are many 'less expensive but just as good' Rose frags out there. Unfortunately I am just a glutton for a well crafted Rose!!

Today I was given a sample of Red Roses with my Jo Malone purchases. I didn't expect to like it much after reading reviews, but I was curious. I have a friend who smells wonderful in Tea Rose. It's her signature scent and was also worn by her beloved grandmother. I've secretly always wanted a grandmother and I wanted to smell of roses. Red Roses opened better than I expected. It's strong and fresh yet not sneezy. The lemon is clearly a back up singer. It nicely supports the crispness of the rose. My nose didn't detect even a hint of musk or powder. Sadly, Red Roses gradually turns more and more "barnyard" on my skin. An hour or so after application I found my self wondering "what is that horrible odor?". I realized that it was emanating from my skin. Without too much graphic detail I can tell you that underneath the "rose" and after the lemon fades- I am taken back to my days as a pony clubber. I've smelled this very scent as I mucked out my pony Anastasia's stall. I adored my pony and spend my childhood summers smelling of her- horse hair, grass, and sometimes manure. Her name was Shannon when I got her. I thought she was a princess among ponies so I changed her name. As an adult woman, I'm more than a little horrified to smell of this cologne. It really smells disgusting on me for whatever reason. I've also left it on for almost 8 hours.... On purpose. It's made me feel both a little repulsed and nostalgic. I'm missing those carefree days of summer when Stacia and I spent our youth together. I grew too tall for her and ended up on a part thoroughbred gelding. I loved him too, but it wasn't the same. Stacia died when I was in my 20's. I don't think of her often, but when I do I cry. I feel silly about it, but the tears still form. I don't know why this "turns" on me but I do not recommend buying this unless you can try it first. The top was pretty but it morphed into one of the worst perfumes I've ever worn. Tomorrow I will wear Orange Blossom which stays fresh and pretty on me. Tonight I'm sleeping in it and hoping I dream of my childhood.

I believe Jo Malone when she says this perfume contains “seven of the world’s most exquisite roses.” When I first smelled it, I was idly paused at a perfume counter with a friend. The sales clerk handed a test strip of this to my friend and the roses leapt from the perfumed paper into the air and up my nose. I knew I would buy it. At once my eyes opened in surprise. I said, “What is THAT??” and could barely keep myself from snatching it from her hand. We each left with a bottle. I’m wearing it now, about to meditate, this ecstatic scent fit accompaniment for the other bliss I will shortly be in. Crushed violet, mint, honeycomb and lemon mimic the mundane aspects of the rose—thorns, stems, leaves—supporting, as claimed, seven of the most breathtaking rose petals on this earth.

This is such a delicious rose fragrance - probably one of the best, ever. It just smells straight-up like a rose without much else. It's not oldschool (which would be a very powdery, aldyhydic rose) or newschool (which would be a jammy and sweet rose). It just smells like you have happened upon a dewy, fragrant rose in a garden and have leaned down for a smell. I do get a hint of honey and citrus like the notes listed here but they're so harmonized with the rose that they barely seem separate. I see why people think it's boring because it's just rose and little else but it's executed so well and that's exciting to me. This is such a realistic rose fragrance that the first time I smelled it I had a powerful olfactory memory of being in a florist's shop with my Dad buying roses for my Mom. I have to wonder if this was my earliest memory of smelling roses - I think it may be as we didn't have a garden and in this memory I was very small. Fragrance alone, it's in my top 3 rose fragrances with Delina and La Fille De Berlin. However the performance is so bad that I don't even have a full bottle of this. On my skin it lasts about an hour before it turns into an unpleasant powdery floral that smells like it's gone off (but is barely detectable) and on fabric it performs better but I think the projection is really low (which could be bad or good). Jo Malone fragrances get a lot of criticism for being colognes with EDT/EDP prices. Some actually perform quite well - Lime Basil Mandarin has impressive longevity for a cologne and Peony Blush Suede isn't bad either. Fragrances in general have gotten weaker than they were 20-30 years ago when JM earned this reputation so I think the bar has lowered and some JM fragrances now don't seem like such a bad buy but Red Roses specifically performs so poorly that I can't give it the same benefit of the doubt that I give some other JM fragrances despite it being one of the best fragrances they've ever created.

Red Roses is 100% the only perfume on the market where I live that features the exact rose absolute I use to fall asleep. When I was younger, I would put a few drops of rose absolute essential oil in an ultrasonic diffuser to ensure I would drift to sleep in a dreamy haze. Every other "Rose" fragrance on the cosmetics market is either pulling their rose accord from Rose Hips, which are the developed seeds of rose flowers and smell completely different to the petals, or they are attempting to get the accord from the Tea Rose varietals which are in a different grouping of cultivars from the apothecary roses and damask roses. I'm not a rosarian myself, but I do understand that different varieties of roses release different molecules. This particular fragrance is a soliflore based only on the Damask Rose or Bulgarian Rose, depending on your familiarity. Rosa Damascena is hybrid between the Rosa gallica and Rosa muscena - the French Rose and the Musk Rose. Both parent cultivars are among the oldest cultivated varieties of rose. Red Roses comes close to the right region in a subtle and well rounded way. There is an almost citric note that hangs around the edge of the topnotes of this fragrance in a way that sort of dilutes the Roundness of the rose accord, which I imagine is a sort of alteration to the typical english fragrance palette. If Jo Malone produced this as an Intense, as they do with their similarly osmotically-shaped Rose and Oud, I would bathe in it. One of my friends and my own mother personally loathe the smell of rose absolute - whereas when I smell this and the essential oil I associate with it, I cannot breathe deeply enough to satisfy my rose lust. Their loss, I love this fragrance.

This opens up as a fresh garden rose bouquet. No green, no powder, no sweetness, just basic garden rose. It conjures up memories of the rose scented Barbie Doll accessories from my childhood back in the 80s. It's a basic rose Solifleur without much depth. It's fairly short lived. I got about 2-3 hours out of it. Jun 02 2014

As the name goes, Red Roses is quite all about rose, played in a way I really enjoy here. It’s fresh, green and breezy, probably one of the most bracing and crisp rose-based scents I’ve ever tried. It avoids any soapy-camphorous effect, far from any classic rose inspiration; rather enhancing the natural fruity-leafy side of rose (also thanks to some citrus notes).

Nothing can surpass the romantic aroma of a bouquet of red roses. If you have ever desired to scent your skin with such a fragrance, then Jo Malone's Red Roses Cologne will delight you in more ways than one. Red Roses is a fairly basic fragrance, but one that I find quite captivating.

Red Roses is a fragrance that truly embodies the essence of a fresh rose. It’s not just floral; it’s vibrant and green, like stepping into a blooming rose garden on a crisp morning. The scent is incredibly realistic, capturing the delicate balance between the petals' softness and the leafy freshness surrounding them.

Those of us a bit older know this saying! Well, do you remember? Right, the Golden Girls! Whenever Rose reminisced about her hometown of St. Olaf, she was silenced with this phrase. Now, what connection do I draw between Red Roses by Malone and this sitcom?
Cool fresh tuberose. Sweet milky white and metallic. Venomous as snake bite. Mutant spawn of Poison and Sécrétions Magnifique. Utterly audaceous. Insanely powerful. Totally unwearable. Fabulous.

A unique floral blend of ylang ylang ,gardenia and tuberose. This is spicy and yet sweet.Great sillage and longevity. It's a marriage of elegance ,femminity and class!Deep floral,hints of fruits based on woods and musc.It is sweet due to vanilla but not overwhelming or gourmand and balanced on spiciness of carnation flower. An orchestra of notes wonderfully blended together from the maestro of perfumes Dominique Ropion.5 stars!

My first fragrant love. Amarige. I initially laid my nose upon this glorious scent in the library of a school where my mother had a temporary role as deputy head. The head teacher wore Amarige. She strutted around shouting the odds. Had a real attitude problem, as my mother saw it. She was headstrong and aggressive in her demeanor. I thought she was at once hilarious and cool as all hell. Dry wood, warm yellow and white flowers. Bookshelves and plants. We went to IKEA and she had me trailing behind her pushing the trolley full of her pickings. Nothing, and nobody, stood a chance against the stench of Amarige. Love! Power! Independence! My second encounter was in the kitchen/dining area of my mother's childhood friend, Sheila. She lived atop a windy hill and her husband was a photographer specializing in black and white landscapes. As I sat on a long wooden bench beside her large wooden kitchen table, I breathed in the delectable scent of freshly baked bread mingling with Amarige. I asked, "What is that flowery smell?" My mother responded: "AMARIGE! I've always HATED Amarige! It's Sheila's signature scent!" Such venomous spite toward my beloved, Amarige!!!! The best tuberose and cedar-wood based concoction in the world. I will always return to my Amarige.

From the plethora of notes listed I can only really detect neroli, rosewood and cassia in the opening. Then the base notes emerge and that's where Amariage settles quietly on me becoming a woody-vanillary-ambery-musk. It's a pretty, comforting and well-made perfume that lingers for hours and reminds me of autumn leaves, but to my mind it's not an especially complex one. Judging by the wide range of responses here it seems that how you experience Amariage will have a great deal to do with your skin chemistry as Missk says.

I'm not very familiar with Givenchy fragrances as of yet, but this fragrance is certainly very memorable and beautiful, and is one of friend's signature scents.
