Like most people have mentioned here, this is a very strong floral fragrance. It's strong in an elegant and sophisticated fashion rather than being offensive and "in your face". The scent is rich and spicy with subtle hints of fruit, rather oriental and unique. The notes of orange blossom and peach are quite prominent, making it sweet and feminine. I absolutely love that my friend wears this scent well, it blends perfectly with her skin chemistry, making this classic fragrance smell exotic and sensual. However on myself, Amarige is quite powdery. Not terrible, but not as beautiful as when others wear it. I suggest that you try this before you buy to see whether it matches your chemistry.

3.4 edt bottle This is the biggest floral perfume in the universe. Its gigantic. Its over the top. It lasts forever. Its beautiful!! Sometimes, you just need a huge floral. Amarige is it. Note: This is the most long lasting epic room spray ever. My man said, "Oh u got a new shipment I see.I can smell a florist shop in the kitchen.

What else can anyone say about this beautiful fragrance? I’ve been wearing it since it was released. Amarige was in your face from the get go (even by 1990s standards) and there it remains, undefeated and undeterred. The strongest, most unapologetic floral with an absolutely ridiculous sillage.

White Gardenia Red Rose Succulent red berries Orchid delectable Peaches Spicy Carnations and Woods makes me imagine a 1957 Parisien Cafe with fire red walls Abstract Fernand Leger paintings on the wall Having lunch with Audrey Hepburn Jean Seberg Brigette Bardot Simone Signoret. downstairs plays jazz where all the chic Beatnicks hangout mixing with high class Sophisticates.

I found a 1oz. bottle of the new version in the bargain bin at a local discount store for $7. The box was banged up and was mixed in with a lot of cheap drugstore fragrances and body mists. I asked the cashier if the price was correct and she pointed to the pink sticker on the side of the box and said, “Yep, that's the price.” So, I bought it.

I was gifted Amarige in the early 1990s by a man who wanted to impress me with gifts. I loved the perfume, but I can’t remember the giver now in 2021. It’s a lovely floral perfume, heavy on tuberose, which is why I love it so. I must have lost the bottle at some point during my many moves, so now it’s time to replace it after all these years.

I was very excited for this when it just came out, but quickly lost interest in my sample because I was disappointed by it. Now, many months later, I'm giving it a final try to write this review. The problem with My Euphoria is not that it smells bad, just that it's very generic with a much more interesting sounding notes list. Especially the black sesame made me curious, but I detect absolutely none of it. I'd describe this as a warm, fruity, slightly sweet and slightly woody perfume. Blackcurrant is the most prominent note, but honestly, it could be any kind of berry. Next comes the powdery, vanillic orchid that works as a backdrop for the currant. And if you really press your nose onto your skin, you can also sense a slight woodsy sharpness that I guess is supposed to be oud. A clean oud, of course, and really not much of it. And that's the whole fragrance. It has not much in common with the original Euphoria. Sure, it's roughly in the same family, but it's really just a boring second cousin. If you want an updated version of Euphoria, please try Euphoria Intense, it's my favorite of the line and keeps the spirit of the original.

I chose to wear Burberry Red for the first time while travelling up north on a Christmas day. The lovely scent of tart rhubarb mixed with the slight tingle of spices filled the car, as we drove through the snow covered winter wonderland woods. My first thought was, ‘rhubarb pie and cranberries in the snow’, to describe the crispy feel of the scent. Half an hour later, I thought, ‘mmmm… rhubarb and vanilla’. Warm, spicy and tart, Burberry Red turned out to be a pleasant surprise for me. I was drawn to an unusual note of rhubarb when I bought it blind, but I was not sure what to expect based on reviews. I enjoyed wearing Burberry Red and I will be wearing it again during the holidays. However, I have to admit that both, my husband and I, got serious rhubarb pie cravings while I was wearing this scent. So be prepared to do some baking. So what is the recipe for a successful rhubarb scent? I know there are no cranberries listed in the pyramid, but I do smell something in the beginning that reminds me of freshly squeezed sour berries with a citrus zing. The rhubarb is complimented by spices and a gentle rose layer in the background towards the heart notes. Finally the crispness is replaced with a gentle vanilla layer turning the scent into a warm and fluffy rhubarb pie sprinkled with gingerbread spice to add a kick. The scent has pleasant presence – not overpowering, but noticeable. I am also pleased with its lasting power for at least of 8 hours. I would like to give Burberry points for creating a scent with an unusual leading note and making it successful. I think the charming ambience of this scent and the festive bottle with red plaid motif fit the holiday spirit like a glove. I was looking for something unusual and interesting to wear on Christmas day and Burberry Red fit the bill. Overall score 7/10.

So, so very beautiful. A sweet and mildly spicy vanilla fragrance which has all the class and sophistication of a true Burberry perfume. While most of Burberry's fragrances are casual and Summery, Brit Red I would dare to wear to any formal event. I believe that I could never tire of this exquisite fragrance. Brit Red is warm and comforting while at the same time it's incredibly sexy. It has all the appeal of a floral-scented perfume, yet the spicy kick from the rhubarb, ginger and patchouli makes this fragrance so different and so appealing. For the life of me I cannot understand why they are discontinuing this fragrance. I test many scents, yet it has been quite a while since a fragrance of this kind has grabbed my attention. I do hope to purchase this fragrance so that I can wear it during Winter next year. I must add that the lasting strength is amazing, lasted on my skin the whole day. The sillage is also good, not overpowering but heavy enough to leave a light trail. I cannot wait to get my hands on a bottle.

Ginger, vanilla, and... rhubarb! An unlikely combination even in the kitchen, but in a perfume? In fact, BURBERRY BRIT RED, against all expections (which were perhaps admittedly low...) smells quite nice to me. As its bright red plaid bottle boldly proclaims, this is a holiday scent: to be worn at most twice each year, on Christmas Eve and, perhaps, again on Christmas morning! Not to welcome Jesus Christ, mind you, but oh-so-secular Santa Claus. This is a likeable fragrance to anyone who likes sweetness in moderation, at least when it comes to wearing it on their skin... And I do appreciate the novelty of this scent, now and then. To be precise: twice each year! A good perfume to put you in the mood for... baking!

This went on my skin sour and tart and sometimes sweet - that's the rhubarb, I guess. It was firey, like a midnight barbeque, sweaty and smoky. Haven't yet found a perfume with ginger I like. Many hours later it did dry down into a pleasant vanillic and gingerbread smell but I did not enjoy this perfume. Don't consider blind buy unless you love orientals.

Brit Red is an atypical gourmand. It's citrus & tart, sweet & spicy, rich & delish, and full of depth & character. I can only echo all the positive reviews this fragrance receives, and I can't add much, except ... BODY LOTION. The BODY LOTION is outstanding, and the EDP spray and body lotion layer beautifully. Layering greatly improves longevity and sillage ... and gets raving compliments. Best for cool weather, day or night. Perfect for holiday parties & Christmas evening. I wear this exclusively in December. Even so, my 3.4 EDP will certainly be used up in the next holiday season in its third year. I rarely use up a frag, so that's an indication of how much I dearly love Brit Red. This was a blind buy because I adored Brit and was confident the rhubarb & spices would work for me. Unless you fall in that camp, it's probably best to sample first. Rating: 5 out of 5.
What do you get when you mix in Vanilla with Rhubarb?

Hi folks, I'm back and as always I have a new fragrance description for you. I recently tested a fragrance that should be fairly well-known and is absolutely not a surprise for anyone, especially since it comes from a mainstream brand that might be a bit underestimated because they have some really beautiful scents, namely Burberry.

Perfumes can preserve memories. One can see experiences again and again, process them, so to speak, set them aside, and then a small hint of the associated scent comes along, and everything comes alive again. Do we then see it from a distance, or do we dive into the feelings experienced? Hmm, it depends. 2005, it was autumn, Brit Red was my beloved companion.

A fragrance full of contrasts! At least that's what I thought based on the pyramid and the comments... At the beginning, there is a clearly recognizable, tangy, pleasant rhubarb note. Those who enjoy perfumes like “Aedes de Venustas,” “Ciel mon Jardin,” or even the rhubarb scent from Hermes will also be pleased here!

Brit Red was a blind buy! I was looking for a sweet winter fragrance and during my search about 3 years ago, I kept coming across Brit Red. It’s supposed to smell like gingerbread? - yes, great! That’s what I want too! Since it’s a limited edition and had long since disappeared from stores, I just bought it blind online. First spray "uhhh, what is THAT?!

One of my favorite Jo Malone scents, I find myself constantly smelling my arms when I wear this one. I could bathe in it—it has such a gorgeous warmth to it. The longevity and sillage are fantastic, so bathing in it wouldn’t be advised. It’s more feminine, but I can see some men wearing it with no problem. You have to love jasmine though, as it is first and foremost in your face. I don’t smell marigold at all, and didn’t know they had a scent. In any case, you think of tropical gardens while wearing this fragrance. It’s pricey, but totally worth every penny. Bring it on! It’s so sexy!

I love Jasmine and a fair share of white florals, but I can see how this one can be very intense and even head-y. It's a beautiful, classy powdery Jasmine perfume, with great lasting power. I was surprised to see this as recommended for warmer weather since I think the powdery and creamy quality makes for a comforting and yet alluring winter scent.

I feel torn about this fragrance. Marigold is one of the few flowers I really don't like to smell, but I heard so many good things about this scent that I still wanted to try it. And at first, I thought it was the right decision and that I would have missed out if i didn't. This smells so realistically floral, like a jasmine shrub at night in full bloom. It's sweet and creamy with an undertone of overripeness, borderline decay. Just like real flowers can smell! The ylang ylang and vanilla are quite noticeable next to the jasmine, they make the scent sweeter and warmer and keep the indolic notes in check. It's beautiful. Everything is good. That is until I finally notice the marigold. Ugh, no, I still can't stand this flower! It always smells musty to me. And it's such a shame, the rest of the scent is so natural, rich and hypnotic, the whole opening is stunning... And then the stupid old marigold kicks in and ruins it for me. I don't know how to rate this. I gave it a measly 6.5 because I got to be honest, I don't really like it as a whole. If you're into realistic florals and don't mind marigold, if you maybe don't even perceive it as a funky note in general, don't let that deter you. Jasmine Sambac & Marigold might be perfect for you. It's certainly a well-made scent, and I should have let the name be a warning to me.

This is the perfume that brought me to the joy of perfume collecting. It is also the one that made me realize my love for white flowers in general and jasmine in particular. It's such a deep, classy, sophisticated jasmine scent. I was obsessed with it the moment the Jo Malone store clerk in Rome sprayed it on my wrist. It was a hot, 42°C day. I was initially only curious about the normal cologne and tested the English Pear & Freesia and Peony & Blush Suade. I was not ready to buy a full bottle right away because of the price. But then, I saw the black cologne intense bottles. I asked what the differences were, and she sprayed this on me. It did not impress me at first, but then after a few hours, I came back to the store, asking the name of the bottle, then later bought it on my birthday. Even now, after sniffing the Tom Ford Jasmine Rouge, Diptyque Olene and Do Son, and Chloe Jasmine Nomade, this jasmine scent still leave a big impression on me. It's not a rich Jasmine milktea like Jasmine Rouge. It's not a bouquet of jasmine and other flowers like Do Son and Olene. It's not just passing by a jasmine on the way to a vanilla shop like Chloe Nomade Jasmine. This scent is more like an elegant mysterious lady with a calm voice you meet spontanously somewhere and cannot get her out of your head. For me, the scent is like that. I sprayed this when I'm nervous. Or before going to bed. Or simply for a night out. I think this scent could be overwhelming for those who are not into or get headache with jasmine. But for me, it's just perfect. It lasts around 6-8 hours on me, so the price is okay.

It can't be true that Jo Malone, or rather the previously unknown perfumer Mathilde Bijaoui, has created such a dreamy jasmine scent! I generally appreciate Malone fragrances for their natural quality, but until now, I have only found my luck in layering two scents - this one convinces me as the first Malone fragrance that works beautifully on its own. Today I tested Jasmine Sambac & Marigold and after the first sniff on paper, I immediately had it sprayed on my wrist, which cost me almost no courage in this case, as it already smelled fantastic on paper - warm and golden, yet equipped with fresh components, enchantingly floral with a certain "background!" In detail, this means that the golden jasmine sambac and the wonderful ylang-ylang flower immediately rise to my nose, subtly underlined by the mild-spicy freshness of marigold and lemon. Benzoin and amber provide a warm-balsamic foundation, which gains a pleasantly creamy note from the added vanilla. The scent strikes me as floral, rounded, fresh, and radiant at the same time. I could roll in it!!! As a lover of Dior's "J'adore" fragrances, it reminds me of J'adore-L’absolu and also of Dior's noble "Grand Bal." I also find Roberto Cavalli's "Roberto Cavalli," despite its lack of jasmine note, not too far off - only that "Jasmine Sambac & Marigold" lacks any showy, vamp-like note. It doesn't need it, as its radiant elegance ensures a wonderfully feminine effect. I can only imagine the scent on a man in exceptional cases. After five hours, I can still perceive it on my wrist, albeit slightly diminished, even the next morning. With a moderate sillage of a maximum of one meter, I find it pleasantly natural and unobtrusively elegant. In my opinion, it is well-suited for the colder season, but I can also easily imagine it in spring or on cool summer days due to its unobtrusiveness. “Jasmine Sambac & Marigold” is a not overly sweet, warm, vanilla-creamy, yet golden radiant winter jasmine scent that one can only dream of. With it, I don't feel like a vamp, but like a modest diva. I would love to buy it right away, but my allergy-prone life has taught me to first acquire a sample to test it thoroughly. I am looking forward to it!

You really have to like jasmine, but that should have been clear to everyone given the name, right? British understatement is not really the case here, rather typical British dreams of India - when they were still a colonial power - if it weren't for ... locals ... rebels ... heat ... tropical diseases ... The rest can be read, for example, in Agatha Christie.

Finally, finally, finally I have found the one jasmine fragrance. Jus de Rose, I thank you so much, it's amazing how similar our fragrance preferences are. For years, I wandered around the Elie Saab fragrances, and nothing ever clicked between us. A part of me craved them, while the other part rejected them. Since the moment I smelled the cap of Jasmin Sambac, I know why.

Just a tiny spritz. Close your eyes. Take a deep breath. I am back. I am back in that place where I was eleven years ago. The place whose impressions I had locked deep in my heart. Memories that I cannot summon in the hectic everyday life. With just one spritz, I am back, oh Kashi, you City of Light.

So… here it is, the new fragrance from Jo Malone. Or let’s say, one of the new fragrances, as quite a few new scents have been released this year, such as the English Fields collection. However, this fragrance is not limited, so it will be part of the entire collection. The fragrance is called Jasmine Sambac & Marigold. The name suggests a floral scent.

In 2012, I went out into my grandmother's garden; she was very crazy about flowers, which I loved about her. She had a greenhouse full of different flowers, and the first thing I smelled was jasmine; I fell in love immediately. After my grandmother passed away, it was this scent that always reminded me of her.

...and then being served a fruity & chilled cocktail while a gentle breeze allows some rays of sunshine to slip through the trees surrounding the lake. This is the only edition of CK One Summer I have ever had. I've smelled a few others but none seem to come even close to this fruity beauty. Like CK Be this to me is one of those highly addictive scents that I just love to smell, they're not similar scents but I find both extremely comforting and relaxing. CK One Summer 2008 is just summer bliss, it contains hedione (the which is extracted from jasmin blossom. It's quite apt that 'hedione' comes from the Greek word 'hedone' meaning 'fun' or 'pleasure' and this could also describe this CK fragrance perfectly. It's brilliantly suited to those long, warm summer days where you spend almost all of your time outside, having fun with friends, or even just chilling in a park with a book in the shade of a plane tree, or on a beach somewhere under a palm tree (watch out for any coconuts!). When I looked at the notes of this juice I was kind of surprised that it features no citrus. I always associated the most refreshing scents with citrus, but this has changed my opinion (I'm sure there are many fragrances like this too)! I could always smell the watermelon and cucumber though, which I guess give this stuff it's deeply aquatic feel. The dry-down is musky and there is an ever-present cool minty undertone which adds to the fresh feel. This is an enticing and special kind of scent in my opinion, which I think most people will find hard to hate and some like myself will find difficult to forget. It lasts a decent amount of time for a fresh summer fragrance (if only CK Be lasted like this!) and makes a great alternative to a citrus scent on those hot summer days.

I bought "CK One Summer 2008" because I found the design of the bottle and packaging so great (I think the gradient bottles of the other "CK One Summer" editions look cheap and uninspired) AND because it was very affordable at 22.50 euros for 100ml. But now... The scent. Wonderful! Summer, water, and LIGHT fruity notes. Right after spraying, I notice the very balanced aqua notes and a really nice hint of watermelon. After a while, mint and cucumber come through. Everything remains wonderfully light and summery. In the base note, the classic CK One scent reveals itself. When I smell "CK One Summer 2008," I think of summer, a fresh sea breeze, a minty mojito in hand, and nice "locals" selling fresh fruit on the beach... In the coming days, I’ll be going back to the crime scene :-) I need to have another bottle, one for enjoyment and one for keeping. It’s true: the perpetrator always returns to the crime scene.

Crisp green-fruity-citrus scent with no praise or blame – well, more blame than praise, quite on the synthetic/acrid side (a floor detergent, basically – imagine you’re using it to clean the tropical juice you’ve just spilled on the floor, here’s Weekend). Quite cheap overall, especially for the first minutes which are fairly loud and pungent; once it settles a bit on skin and finds its proper tuning, it’s a mildly enjoyable and exceedingly generic green-citrus-musky scent with those annoying metallic-pungent nonsense nuances many brands try to pass as “tropical fruity notes” – although luckily it’s more green-woody and citrus than tropical. Not that acrid anymore if compared to the opening, more metallic and “gassy” after a couple of hours, but still miles away from being something pleasant to wear. Anyway, linearly green and fruity on the lime-tropical side, and that’s all. Personally I’d rate this mediocre, to be generous; but if you’re looking for a summer fragrance and your pretenses are really (really, really) low, then here you go. 5/10

This is my all-time favorite scent. Make a list and it is a number 1. Here's why. I personally buy perfume based on my feelings, not on the scent or how they perform. When I was young, like very very young, my friend's brother used this one. He is very handsome but his style is free-spirited and fearless/carefree personality. I adored him so much and this Burberry weekend and D&G Light Blue are always on his vanity. I saw him spraying one or two before going out. He is always smelling so good, and this is the first scent that made me into the world of fragrance. Every time I wear this, it always brings back to my childhood. A good memory. A loving past. How many weekend bottles I used? 7 and I still have two 100ml as a backup. I love Citrusy fragrance so this is the number one, all the time. I don't care about whether the weather is hot or cold. But however, I might have 20 bottles to wear based on the occasions, but if it is the weekend, this is one, there is no other.

It's no secret that my favourite perfume of all time is Weekend for Women, so I was eager to see what the male version was like with the intention of perhaps purchasing it for my significant other. This cologne is not a floral like its female equivalent, which I consider a good thing, (I like my men to smell masculine). Weekend for men is quite fruity yet pleasantly sour, that makes this scent a fantastic Summer fragrance, as it is sharp and refreshing without being too overpowering. The lasting strength is not bad, however I'm speaking from a female perspective where many of our fragrances are eau de parfum rather than eau de toilette, so the lasting power might actually be fantastic for some. Weekend is so light and clean that it could actually be worn by a very daring woman. However, I do believe that this fragrance is very masculine. The only element of this fragrance that mirrors Weekend for Women is the honey note in the drydown, which adds warmth and a little bit of sweetness. My verdict on this fragrance; I love it yet I don't think this type of fragrance would suit my man, (he's more into dark and woodsy scents). However, I will consider buying this for some of my male friends when it comes time to buy them gifts.

It is a nice Fresh Citrusy fragrance, A Unique perfume for Hot weather. This is a bit mature and synthetic but it smells so good with reasonable price. It opens up with sweet fresh citrusy combo and green notes in the background then dry down is sweet musky woody. The Ivy note is dominant in this scent, Longevity is good. Rating : 7 / 10

At first I was pretty "meh" about Weekend. I got it for $20 on a whim, and wasn't too impressed after wearing it a couple times. Floral mixed with honey, not my taste at the time. Fast forward a couple years when I'm going through all my old scents during the summer, and I give it a shot. What was once floral-honey has transformed into freshly cut grass, with a good dose of sweet honey and a hint of citrus peel. Suddenly this fragrance makes complete sense, and paints a beautiful portrait of a leisurely Saturday during the summer- cutting grass, drinking sweet tea, and eating fruit fresh off the tree. I wonder how this fragrance would do with a base of Tobacco to complete this picture, however as it is Weekend is a great, low key scent for when you need a pick-me-up or want to smell good while working out on the yard.

This is the weekend of a man who is part of a couple, I'd say. There's a whiff of coffee from breakfast still hanging in the air, but now he's out in the garden mowing the lawn while she is quickly wiping down the house (the cleaning agent being Citrus Fresh). Later on he goes fishing: I smell an aquatic note that reminds me of fish fresh from the water.

Ive never felt so strongly about mediocrity. Burberry Weekend is the definition of 5/10, just eh, completely inoffensive, pleasant yet utterly univocative. It smells like a freshly ironed white button shirt. On days I dont want to think about what I spray on and I don't want it to last long so that I can choose something better later then I will choose this.

“Weekend For Men” is 24 (!) years old… Wow. You wouldn’t think so. And it is the first real hit from my big order of cheapies from last week that will probably stay beloved in my collection forever. And it might now even be my favorite Burberry scent. Much too overlooked, far too little written about. That has to change! Or maybe not. It can just stay mine.

...grapefruit are in my nose during a walk in southern Europe. But there is also the aroma of ivy, moss, and something woody in the air. It’s simply beautiful. When applying this fragrance, you first get lemons, grapefruit, and mandarin. The green of ivy joins in, along with a mossy note and a hint of woodiness.

Hinoki & Cedarwood was love at first sniff for me. I've been curious about Hinoki notes for awhile and this fragrance served as my introduction to the note while leaving me both impressed and hungry for more! This opens with a gorgeous cinnamon sprinkled soapy accord that makes me think of a high end, quiet sauna. The slight spice lingers as the strongest woody top notes begin to evaporate giving me a cola adjacent vibe on my skin. As the spices continue to fade, the soapiness remains and mingles with the light and distinguished woody aroma of hinoki. From there the fragrance stays linear as it dries down, keeping up the uniquely fresh and luxurious smelling clean woody accord. This is a great fragrance to wear when looking for something light, airy and fresh and is perfect for fall weather but can easily be worn year round. It's definitely not a strong, spicy woody fragrance, but rather a very peaceful, uplifting scent reminiscent of a breeze in a quiet forest clearing. I've shied away from Jo Malone in the past due to performance concerns but I find that this fragrance has impressive longevity for how light it is. While it sits close to the skin and does not have much in the way of silage/projection, I get about 7-8 hours on skin and all day on clothes. This is perfect to wear when looking for something calming, but relaxing. It's not like a Wūlóng Chá Extrait de Parfum that calms in an uplifting, invigorating way. This calms in a tranquil soft way that just leaves you feeling clean, clear headed and ready to find peace in your day. I'm happy to own this in my collection and will be reaching for it a lot this fall. Sample first!

Opens aldehydic, soapy, slightly aromatic. Hinoki wood and cedar wood are both "dry" smelling woods so it surprised me that the drydown here is decidedly "wet." Earthy and loamy rather than sharp woods and pencil shavings. I guess I was expecting a rich lavender with a smoky sharp hinoki and got old-timey soap and Clearwood (a "clean" patchouli aromachemical) instead. If you like this profile, I'd suggest trying New Look . It goes more all-in on the aldehydes, and I much prefer the gorgeous smoky frankincese as the background than this messy attempt at a woody accord. And the price is comparable too (New Look is $165 for 40ml while Hinoki & Cedarwood is $160 for 50ml). However it is MUCH more polarizing, but that's what comes with specificity.

I tried a sample of this. When I sprayed it on paper it smelled like a slightly woody, warm cinnamon. However when I sprayed it on my skin, it smelled EXACTLY like coca cola. I wasn't getting the woodiness or the cinnamon anymore, just straight coca cola. Not for me, but if you've been looking to smell like soda, this may be the fragrance for you!

I'm not sure if anyone has noticed but this one smells similar to the Fabuloso Lavender cleaner but this is one is less harsher on the nose and more woodsier. At first wear, I get an image of wet wooden spa with a hint of coconut for some reason. It lasted nicely on my clothes for the whole 8hrs. However, when I had to clean up the floors, I noticed I smelled something like Hinoki and cedarwood. To my dismay, it was the Fabuloso Lavender cleaner we had. I'm not so sure of buying the full bottle anymore though. I think I'll just finish my decant for now.

... the forest in the cool late autumn. Fir trees have been cut down, the branches stripped of their twigs, now drying in the lukewarm midday sun. Fir and spruce resin, still liquid and viscous, release their enchanting scent together with the light citrus notes of the fir needles. Now there's a hint of incense coming from afar. Does it bring that very, very delicate sweetness? No, it has already disappeared again. Did I just imagine it? Now something else is joining in that I haven't smelled before. A fresh breeze from the north? Yes, I believe so. It is now cool and fresh. The wonderful green with the juicy wood remains for a long time. I feel alive.

Hinoki & Cedarwood starts off very fresh with a surprisingly green forest note. Somehow, it reminds me of a lovely green spruce bath additive. Hinoki wood is said to have a relaxing and calming scent. Yes, this fragrance is definitely relaxing. It provides spa moments and is distinctive in its own way. The freshness lingers for a long time throughout the scent's development.

Hinoki&Cederwood starts with a green, fresh wood note that invites you directly to a forest walk or reminds you of a lovely day at the spa, where you enjoy the aromatic infusion in the tree sauna. It radiates an incredibly soothing note and calms you down.

This is what this perfume smells like. Very cozy with a lovely atmosphere. It gives me strong vibes of a beautiful cozy wooden cabin, with a sauna and fireplace. On cold autumn days in Scandinavia. It is a woody, sweet scent, with a hint of spices. If you have the chance, definitely try out the fragrance and also the perfume house, it's worth it.

First of all: I bought the fragrance blind. Cedar and aromatic notes have rarely disappointed me. I expected something similar to Tam Dao Edt by Diptyque. Hinoki wood was new to me. What can I say? The fragrance did NOT disappoint me (as expected)! However, I was surprised by a 'sweetness' that I did not anticipate after all the reviews/TikToks and YouTube videos I had read.

I bought this fragrance in Palma at Corte Inglés, sometime in the fall/winter last year. To be honest, I didn't really know Jo Malone before and approached it without any expectations. One spray - and I immediately understood where this journey is headed and why this scent is so popular. Hinoki & Cedarwood has a clear wellness character for me.

This opens up as somewhat of a fresh, spicy and fairly sweet orange, due to the mandarin orange, pink pepper, and nutmeg in the top (there is birch that I don't detect at the moment), and the vetiver in the heart is already making itself known. After 10 minutes or so, the spiciness begins to tone down, leaving a hint of the sweet mandarin orange (though definitely on its way out), while the freshness of the vetiver remains and the earthiness of the patchouli sneaks in. I think the patchouli carries a sweetness to it as well which keeps the fragrance slightly sweet, even after the mandarin has gone. There is cedar in the heart that I can't detect at the moment. Perhaps I just need more experience with woody notes...Overall, as the fragrance begins to dry down the scent can be described as a little soapy, and tad bit sweet, and slightly earthy/damp. Very clean and masculine, though subtle. Most definitely gentlemanly. Projection is already becoming a problem (currently 15 minutes into a decent spray on my hand. I can smell it from a max distance of 6 inches away...though more sprays on warmer areas tend to let it project a little better). After almost 30 minutes, I believe we make it to the base notes, which are allegedly musk and incense. I detect no musk yet, but I do get a slight smokiness from the incense. It makes this thing even more masculine as it continues to dry down. This scent stays linear in this fashion for a good while. 3 hours in, I clan say that the fragrance is at the end of its projection life (not sure if I'd call good and true projection though; again maybe actually wearing it would change that). I now get what I think is the musk note; if so, it is providing a slightly bitter and sweet element to the fragrance. It isn't off-putting though. It's still a little soapy, but not quite as fresh anymore. Still masculine and pleasant. Almost 12 hours later, I'm sure some has rubbed off in my sleep, but I'm still getting a faint presence: ever so slightly woody (there it is!), and the hint of a sweet soapy-ness. In wearing this one in the warmer weather before, I notice that heat makes it a little powdery, and a little off-putting to my nose. I think I prefer to wear this one in moderate to even cooler temperatures. I'd say it thrives in the spring and fall, and you could even wear it indoors during the winter. I would NOT wear this in the summer heat.

This is a very underrated fragrance that flew (continues to do so) under the radar. Its main issue is the time it was released and its marketing. Back in 2013, the commercial designer market was all about sweet, fruity, spicy, boozy fragrances, in a trend set by One Million and continued by many (your 212 VIP, Eros, Invictus, etc). There were also Dior Homme and La Nuit in their peak. The niche market was profoundly moved by Aventus and it's overwhelming success. The market had no interest in all-rounders, clean out of the shower scents. Bleu de Chanel was new to the game, and blue fragrances weren't a thing yet. In fact, Bleu wasn't hyped at all by the masses since it was (and still is) a somewhat likeable, versatile yet expensive scent. And the fragheads thought it was plain generic. In that context, Givenchy decided to update its classic Gentleman and released this jewel, Gentlemen Only. I believe the name fits this fragrance perfectly, but it angered fans of the classic, that were expecting a classic masterpiece like their beloved Gentleman. Gentlemen Only wasn't groundbreaking at all, and it certainly didn't appeal to the more mature fans of the original Gentleman. The masses didn't care much for it, either, since it wasn't the scent profile they favoured at the time. And so it was Gentlemen Only just didn't get much attention. Except by a few of us, that is, that weren't looking for something "trendy" and wanted a fragrance with a bit more personality. Like I said, Gentlemen Only is a protoblueish fragrance, if you will. Comes out fresh, green and a bit sweet, like mandarin tends to be. It's also spicy and woody, with a subtle incense reminiscent of bleu de chanel. There's certain depth here, but not too much, since it remains a rather simple (but not basic) fragrance. It's clean, somewhat sophisticated, correct and elegant on its own way. This doesn't scream for attention, and it doesn't need to. Much like any proper gentleman. Overall, a great everyday fragrance, that works well on pretty much any scenario, except night outs/clubbing since it hasn't the strongest performance in the market and will be overpowered by ambient smells and other fragrances.

An easy-to-wear spring fragrance, rich in masculine scents, dominated by the scent of pink pepper and violet leaves, really wonderful, but not suitable for hot summer days, and it’s not a summer blue fragrance, the scent of violet and birch leaves gives you the impression that you are in spring as the flowers begin to bloom. Suitable for men over 40 years of age and above (a sense of dignity). It’s not a youthful fragrance for lively young people. The performance of the fragrance is somewhat average: - Longevity: around 4 hours or little more - Sillage: around 2 hours The fragrance bottle comes in the famous shape of Givenchy bottles and the liquid comes in a very light violet color to signify violet flowers and spring.

This is a Wonderful and Lovely fragrance, Fresh, Clean, Refined, Unique, Modern and Complex. It is suitable for Rainy Days. A good perfume can change your mood and I must tell you honestly that I really enjoy it. When this scent develops on skin and its smell changes over time. It opens up with like fresh spicy , slightly sweet, spices and floral notes in the background then dry down is a bit smoky musky woody. The Pink Pepper , Violet Leaf and Incense notes are dominant in this perfume. I am glad that I have the chance to buy Givenchy Gentleman Only as It is truly a delightful Hidden Gem that should be talked out more ! Guys do yourselves a favor and at least sample it. Longevity is good, Highly Recommended. Two Thumbs Up. Bravo Monsieur Jean Jacques ! Rating : 9 / 10

The opening is actually really promising and pleasant - woody and boozy with a slightly sweet zesty mandarin note, very pleasing. After half an hour I get lots of pepper mixed with a vetiver-y vibe, which turns smokier into something incense-like, but very faintly in the background. This goes on for another two hours and after three hours, it's basically a skin scent. Strange thing is that the opening screams "springtime" to me, while the middle phase and drydown are very "fall like" in the mood - and, unfortunately, quite generic. Smells a little like a mix of several popular cheaper fall scents. IMHO I find it somewhere between "like" and "dislike" - it's not that I'd love to have it, but it's simply too safe to dislike. No reason to fear anyone getting annoyed by this.

The opening of refined flowers and dusty books brings a smile to my face, but unfortunately, it is fleeting. Within 10-15 minutes, this gives way to the baby oil note. This dances back and forth with the refined flower note, which I guess isn't a terrible thing.

A man with a well-manicured goatee, accented with 5-o’clock shadow, steps into his walk-in closet after a shower. He is greeted by a sea of jumpers, suits, and blazers - all in muted navy, grey, and charcoal black – with the occasional flash of pastel purple and French blue dotting the otherwise uniform white of his numerous collared shirts.

It's an interesting one, I get vetiver and incense and a little pink pepper. The opening is nice, but the dry down is very generic. It's okay, but it really could have been better. I would have liked to have seen more from Givenchy, especially after the classic "gentleman" of the past.

Today I bought some decant of this perfume. For those who believe it is similar to "YSL L'Homme Libre" I should say totally not. The top note smells a bit look like "YSL L'Homme Libre", Spicy and woody, but more intensive. After a while the cool scent turns to be more sweet and soap like descent.

First of all, I need to clarify: "Gentlemen only" is, in my opinion, not a bad fragrance at all. A total dismissal would also be quite bold on my part, after all, I acquired it voluntarily, without it being a blind buy, and I use it relatively often. I will come back to these points at the end of the comment.

Today I rushed to the fragrance dealer, with the firm intention of getting Emozione Dolce Fiore. But the smart young man makes a regretful face -- the desired fragrance is not in stock yet. Suddenly, his expression transforms into one of seduction and he reveals to me Euphoria Deep. He knows my preference for the Euphorias and feels he is on safe ground. Of course, I don't need to be asked twice, and I indulge in a spray. Wow - this is quite a fine thing, and I am instantly comforted - so soft and indeed "deep" envelops me the fragrance. I glide into Deep like into a smooth, snug silk dress that fits like a second skin without constricting. In my arm rest deep red roses that play into the black - like the "black Madonna". The aquatic note of Cascalone emphasizes the flowing nature of the fragrance, but does not rob it of its magical fullness. Musk adds shine to the scent and patchouli provides a hint of eroticism. Deep captures me immediately, I am almost euphoric, and I forgo the "test run" with the fragrance, because I can trust it blindly. I was right to do so, because now, hours later, it is still loyal and close by my side and shows a lot of feeling. It is the heart of my Euphoria family.

Undeniably a great fragrance that receives a lot of compliments but lacks greatly in performance. For this reason its an often underated fragrance. A lot of people tend to go for it due its value for money but are then disappointed by its performance, not something I would blind buy unless you test to see how it works on your skin. It opens up with with fresh and spicy notes before developing with a slight warmth kind of vibe. Its not something i would wear during the day. More so suited for evening/night or winter occasions. The strength of it is mediocre, once the scent has opened up and evolved, it becomes very bleak and lifeless. The overall performance is poor, skin scent for myself after 1 hour. Almost nothing after 3 hours

I like this one, creamy, sweet but not sickly sweet...maybe hints of fruit....I get something that smells a bit like a pineapple, but I think Grapefruit is actually what is in the note composition.....smells a bit like bleu de channel too....this is very versatile, you can wear this to work and its pleasant on my skin....this is one that energizes and longevity lasts the work day for me so 6-8 hrs, projection is not that great but in my opinion this is something you enjoy for yourself.....I wouldnt exactly wear this for somebody else

This is one of those fragrances that put smile on my face whenever i sniff :) So, Wow! This is more of a night time fragrance, it has perfect balance without being overly dark and not too bright either. Also it's not too sugary or not too citrusy.. It's modern, but without Ambroxan, major ingredient in this days fragrances. It has spices and flowers that is my impression, i can sense the flowers in it, this notes gives this fragrance freshness, not to fall into the dark. Longevity and silage is moderate, not too strong, just perfect! In one word, Lovely.

The Indigo flanker really impressed me lately. The EDT also seems quite decent during the sniff test. And since they have the EDP in action at Kastner right now, I quickly sprayed some on my wrist with the option to buy. And then I remembered why I decided half a year ago not to test potential candidates on my skin before work. I'm not particularly picky when it comes to men's fragrances. I wear Fahrenheit, I wear Antaeus, Habit Rouge, etc. But when it smells like I've just splashed a load of cheap aftershave on my décolletage and I suddenly feel the urge to fidget with my face in anticipation of sprouting beard hairs, that's where the fun ends. The problem seems to be less about the raw masculinity itself and more about this "proletoid" vibe the scent has for me. Just cheap aftershave of the brand "I-don't-wear-fragrance-am-I-gay-or-what". To put it more neutrally: I initially only smell tarragon. Way too much, way too much. Vetiver, cinnamon, and patchouli are ruthlessly trampled. Still, the whole thing feels quite flat. The longer I wear the fragrance, the more this aftershave-deodorant smell develops with that typical synthetic note often found in cheap scents. Burberry shouldn't have that anymore. After 3 hours, I still detect an amber hint on my skin and a somewhat shower gel-like freshness. Are you sure there's no white musk mixed in? Maybe the scent develops differently on male skin. Or in colder weather. For now, it's not an option for me. Unfortunately, I can't help but picture a totally embarrassing wannabe player. We had a guy like that in school who always tried to act like a cool hip hopper. Unfortunately, he was physically a bit developmentally delayed, and to compensate for his baby face and childlike voice, he always acted super aggressive. Of course, only towards those weaker than him. A real creep, and unfortunately, I associate Mr. Burberry EDP with guys like him. I'm sorry for everyone who likes the scent. You know it can smell completely different on you.

There is no other way to explain how this perfume could have come about. By now, I have discovered a few absolutely brilliant Kurkdjians in the niche sector that are undoubtedly masterpieces. However, his designs in the mainstream are often very strange (one might generously overlook the simply too often smelled and overly sweet perennial favorite "Le Mâle"). What this is all about hardly makes sense to me. "Mr. Burberry" could have been carelessly thrown together by any half-talented perfumer in 10 minutes; Monsieur K. didn't need to lend his name and waste time for that. Shower gel opening by the book, at least thanks to tarragon, it is felt to be 30% more original than the majority of new releases. But better? Not really, just a bit different. Tarragon-synthetic-shower gel, if you ask me. After a quarter of an hour, the aforementioned spice dissipates and what remains is a bland, flat, awkwardly fresh-trying little water that is, in terms of quality, slightly above the broad mass, because at least it doesn't overdo it with the lab hammer. Maybe a hint of watery vetiver in the drydown and remnants of tarragon, wrapped in a bit of synthetic. That’s it. Burberry called, Kurki came. And did what was expected of him. Nothing more.

After I found the Mr. Burberry Eau de Toilette quite good, I decided to buy the Eau de Parfum. Both are very similar, with the EdT being more interesting to me because it is more multifaceted. The EdP starts off unremarkably but develops very well from the middle and remains rather linear. I find the entire Mr. Burberry line to be quite successful.

...I come out of the shower and dry myself off. I pick out the clothes I want to wear. After putting on black jeans, a white shirt, and sneakers, I stand in front of my perfume shelf and am momentarily at a loss. And then I see him, Mr. Burberry. Dressed in black, and I think to myself, yes, this one is right for the club, and I apply it.
I have to say the scent smells really good. The bottle has no flaws and the perfume lasts a long time. The fragrance is very strong and I would describe it as aggressive.

Mr. Burberry starts off with that typical designer shower gel DNA that you feel like you've smelled a million times before. Unfortunately, it radiates pure boredom by now. Over time, it gains a bit of spice and moves in a slightly interesting direction, but it plays these factors too weakly, allowing this boredom to continue dominating the scent.

"Mr. Burberry Eau de Parfum" starts off very uninteresting, almost with an overly familiar average top note. Slightly fresh and spicy, but nothing special. Shortly after, it becomes a bit softer and definitely more pleasant. The "biting" sensation in the perfume fades quickly, as I perceived it. Unfortunately, the further development leaves much to be desired.

Givenchy Ysatis (1984) gives me some new thoughts on scent and memory. It comes from an era when I rarely wore perfume, and didn't pay attention to the state-of-the-art at all.  Still, I remembered it instantly when I found a perfectly preserved vintage specimen recently. Ysatis is more nuanced than Dior Poison, less car-alarmish than Givenchy Amarige, less cartoonish than Boucheron by Boucheron. There's no doubt it's cut from the same cloth, though. It's a classic 80s signature fragrance.  In the 80s, an era noted for valuing assimilation and aspiration, a signature fragrance wasn't one that made you stand apart, it was one that loudly signaled your inclusion with a group, or affiliation with a type. No one of these fragrances was fatal, but together, they were nightmarish. (note: At this time I lived in New York City, a city of public transportation and confined spaces.) They made me appreciate the ridiculous slogan of the era: Just Say No. So, memory.  I remember associating this perfume with the go-go sensibility of the 80s. It was a time of gross misproportion, of ill-judged dynamics.  The perfume and fashion of the era might have been set-dressing, but their were indicative, and Ysatis demonstrates the inappropriateness. Example:  shoulder pads aren't my style, but I can understand their use in suits jackets dresses. In the 80s, shoulder pads were used in short sleeve T-shirts. Imagine a T-shirt so poorly fitted that the bulk of the voluminous fabric hanging about your waist must be tucked into your high waisted jeans. Slapping some packaging material into the shoulders of this T-shirt does nothing to mitigate its inattention to the human form. In fact, it highlights it. The person who wore this T-shirt/jeans combination wore Poison in elevators. Wore Cacharel Lulu to brunch.  Wore clouds of YSL Paris on the RR. Wore Amarige to the gym. You get the picture. Ysatis shares the era's sin of volume, but it utterly typifies another great miscalculation of the time, which is the overuse of formality.  The market of smart sportswear had yet to be unearthed in the 1980s. The choice was often torn Levi's or a hideous dress, and the hideous dress usually won. A variation of an old bromide was reinvented for the 1980s: If it things worth doing it's worth doing... with ruffles, with chintz, with gris gris, with cheap adornment.  "Jewelry" was stated,"costume" was implied. Seen from later eras, Ysatis could be considered tasteful version of the big 80s perfumes. But what is the value of a slightly more tasteful monster?  It’s like someone kicking you hard in the balls, but not as hard as he could have. Dominique Ropion is a master of the highly calibrated floral perfume. But for current use, Ysatis lacks the camp of Opium, Poison, Giorgio. They are dated and caricaturish, but they’re fun.  Ysatis, Ropion's tailored monster, is so busy sucking in her cheeks and posing she doesn't crack a smile. from scenthurdle.com

To me, Ysatis is elegant, formal and moneyed. Black taffeta gown, Tahitian pearls, Walborg beaded bag. Ysatis is a gorgeous, classic Perfume with a capital P. Ysatis wears very similar to an oriental on me, just a tad sweet & spicy. The aldehydes & white florals (jasmine & tuberose) are too strong for my taste, giving me a headache. Warm weather is definitely not the time to wear a perfume such as this. I often see the words 'old lady' associated with Ysatis. I think a better term is 'old-school': Ysatis is a beautiful, old-school perfume, just like how perfumes used to be made. Turin says this is the first floriental, although it's technically a chypre. Nevertheless, give it a try. Sample first, buy second.

Ysatis is fascinating. Powdery, elegant, beautiful and classical. I had really expected something extremely outdated, strong and aldehydic, however this is no Chanel No.5, Ysatis is different. The fragrance opens with soft aldehydic notes, creamy coconut and refreshing citrus, balanced out by subtle spiciness. The scent throughout has a likable powdery-incense quality that is both unique and sensual. A previous reviewer mentioned the prominent honey note which adds a sense of happiness, which I certainly agree with. The honey, vanilla, coconut and ylang-ylang does create a delicate sweetness, however the galbanum, patchouli, cloves, civet and oakmoss, give Ysatis a damp greeness which can be bitter at times. Animalistic yet refined really sums up this fragrance well. I don't get much in the way of white florals here, it's more powdery and fresh than anything else to my nose. The lasting power is truly worth the price as its richness lingers on the skin for days. Ysatis is strong and powerful with a lot of character. I recommend.

I'm surprised that jasmine is not in the fragrance card i can smell pervasive amounts of it. to the skin it brings out a soapish scent with an opening of aldehydes the civet i think makes it heavy and oily i do notice a bit of coconut which suble but nicely done. the drying down turns into an warm reisen of galbanum with dry brazilian rosewood. the heart is hard to detect but i can smell a bit of an honey note the drydown is prodominly of sweet amber that is cloyish and strong amount of vanilla and also a wisp of black liqcorice.

A favorite of mine over the past twenty years, I've gone through too many bottles of this sweet juice to count! It's a shame that it has been reformulated and has lost a measure of lushness and oomph. (Still worth owning, but buy a vintage bottle with a gold cap if you can find one.) In my opinion, Elizabeth Taylor's White Diamonds was designed to emulate this exquisite fragrance....there are too many similarities for it be a coincidence and it came out 7 years later than Ysatis so it is possible. I can imagine ET falling in love with this somewhat pricey Givenchy scent and creating White Diamonds as a less costly version that could be afforded by the average woman.
I don't have Ysatis yet, but now after having red the review of "jtd" I want it, I will find a vintage sooner or later with "the golden cap" as "Matriarch" suggests.

This was the very first fragrance I ever received, strangely from my boss way back when as a birthday present (No, he had no intentions of any kind, as an editor-in-chief he got a lot of samples, and so us girls got either gifted fragrances of books he received for reviews, But I received the big bottle and used it up eventually).

Meeting the Ysatis in the late 80s was like a brief but very emotional and stormy love affair. I was in high school and a lot of my days were spent with the same people. We knew each other well so when something new happened we all took part in it. One day the class room smelled differently. It turned out that one of my classmates had bought a new perfume: Ysatis.

Exquisite honeyed flowers. It is magnificent but the aldehydes spoil it a little for my taste by providing a soapy side which will last for quite a while. If you manage to wait, this magnificent duo flowers/honey appears and the perfume becomes sublime. The new bottle is hideous while the old one was superb... Too bad.

A super erotic fragrance, it has a Tom Ford quality and feel to it. No wonder that I love it. There is a smoldering sweetness to this that, combined with the warm spice, brings pure sensuality to the surface. A real femme fatale in my opinion. I do not get the masculine vibe at all. For me it is not even unisex. She is a dark, super sensual lady. So fitting wearing an all black sexy outfit, fake eyelashes and big hoop earrings. Thanks so much to my swap partner bcars10 for allowing me to experience and own this gorgeous dream in a bottle. Like the saying goes: Someone's owl is another ones nightingale, and I found a nightingale in Liquid Gold, indeed!

I can definitely tell this is a Euphoria flanker. I have enjoyed the original since its inception, so I was intrigued by the listed notes to try this one. It is quite manly, but with an underlying sweet-fruitiness. The opening cinnamon note--which is what drew me to this, honestly--is very fleeting, sadly. Right now, I have a sneeze in my nose that won't come out! I'm thinking it's the orchid that's being so loud and screechy because, generally, I like sandalwood. Maybe the combination of orchid/sandalwood is what is making me sneezy?! Anyway, I do sorta like it, and I am hopeful that the drydown will introduce more of sandalwood's creaminess that I enjoy. I also wish more cinnamon would come into play again. My husband does not like this one or the original Euphoria because he says it makes me smell too masculine, and I would agree. The initial couple hours of the original are more masculine, but it smooths out eventually, and I am hopeful for the same on this one. I bought the bottle off ebay, and it is the gigantic one! It's going to last into next century because, honestly, I can't see how often I will choose this one. I still can't get the sneeze out. Sillage is impressive--fills my house! Longevity also seems to be there. If it changes, I will edit this review. EDIT: This has lasted over 12 hours, and still going strong. The screechiness has mostly left, but I can still detect it a bit. I think it gave me the headache I had today, so I might try it again to see what happens next, but I'm certain this will not make it to my top shelf. Too obnoxious. I like my perfumes to "flow," not "scream." EDIT (July 2107): This was the first one to make it to my swap list. It's just too masculine and screechy for me. I really can't stand it, frankly. But I will pat myself on the back for trying to love it!

I had to really control myself to give this an objective review, I just found it so plainly nauseating. It's just too much for me, frankly, and I've been able to tolerate other fragrances like Red Tobacco , Patchouli Magnetik , etc. and allow them to develop so that I can discover and appreciate them fully. This one, though...it's just cheap bling. Screechy, cheap sandalwood, burnt plastic-like sweet orchid, no cinnamon. And boy, is she loud! She'll trumpet your presence and leave a trail of lethal nerve gas behind you. User beware.

Perfumer Professor Nasus turns to his intern: "Listen, Hein, the folks at Calvin Klein want us to create a sweet perfume that all the young girls will wear. And as a special challenge, they want to see the results in an hour, after all, time is money. So first, dissolve the gummy bears in water." "Yes, Professor," said Hein and got to work. But since it was his first day as an intern and Hein wasn't the brightest, there was a serious misunderstanding. When the professor returned to the lab half an hour later, he threw his hands up in horror. "Oh my God, Hein, what have you done?! I said 'water'! Now the gummy bears are floating in my cough syrup! And we don't have time to make a new tincture." "Oh dear," said Hein, turning pale and wanting to make up for his mistake. He grabbed the cleaning cloth that was next to him and tried to fish the bear remnants out of the syrup. "Heeeein!" The professor's voice almost broke with horror. "Not with the dirty cloth in there!" But it was too late. In the meantime, the bear cough syrup had mixed with the moldy water from the cleaning cloth. "How are we going to explain this to the bosses at Calvin Klein?" the professor lamented. "They wanted to make quick money with this." "Oh, Professor," Hein placed a reassuring hand on his superior's shoulder. "They can still do that. They just fill the stuff into a fancy bottle, slap their brand name on it, and that's it." "Oh Hein. You're not as stupid as I thought," the professor beamed.

My Euphoria family stands neatly in a row on my shelf, and I find myself wondering if it really has to be Liquid Gold when I discover the bottle at my fragrance dealer. Hmm - without much hesitation, I bought it blind. At home, I quickly took a sniff - and I can answer my initial question with a Yes! The scent reveals itself as a subtle oriental that also perfectly fits the Christmas season with its hint of cinnamon. It harmonizes beautifully with my curvy, delicate black orchid, which brings simple yet stylish elegance to the windowsill in its golden pot. Of course, it only appears black from a distance - up close, it warms with a velvety deep red. And the understated fragrance is something to be appreciated up close, as it unfolds very subtly. The cinnamon note is prominent but completely unobtrusive. Likewise, the light orchid reaches me only gently and gradually. Smooth and "liquid," the scent is enhanced by the sandalwood. A careful, fine oriental - that fits well into the Euphoria family and suits me.
Today my package with the long-awaited Euphoria Liquid Gold arrived, and of course, I had to test it immediately.

~ Inspiration ~ After I became aware of "Euphoria Gold" in my search for honey fragrances, "Liquid Gold Euphoria" also made it onto my watchlist. I received a sample of both from the lovely Serafina for testing. ~ Bottle ~ The curved shape immediately indicates that this is a "Euphoria" offshoot - this time in a matte, opaque gold tone.

Comparing this to my new favorite, Kiss My Name by Monegal, which I wore last night. They both have a beautiful tuberose but this Jo Malone can't compare to the splendidly and luxuriously indolic version in Kiss My Name, enhanced by jasmine, neroli, balsam and cedar, as it is. In fact, Kiss My Name has usurped Creed Jasmin Impératrice Eugenie, my long-time favorite perfume. Tuberose Angelica doesn't speak the same language as these two greats. At best it speaks a dialect. Yet, it does appeal because the notes are so well done. Angelica does for this hypnotic perfume what lily-of-the-valley, narcissus or hyacinth have done for many a brilliant floral composition: sophisticated the sweetness until queens could wear it. I haven't explored Jo Malone scents much so far and don't own one, so I looked them up. They're a British perfumer, founded in 1994, and their website says the scents are designed to be layered or worn alone--a step up from Demeter? This no doubt accounts for the successful simplicity here. Tuberose Angelica lacks the projection of Kiss My Name, but it's no skin scent either. It's a quite good perfume, overall, not for a queen but it would suit the crown princess just fine. Guess I'll go out and get myself a bottle.

A little slice of heaven. She’s bright like the sun coming up over the flower garden and the dew is still chilled. I’m reminded of creamy wisteria with this fragrance at the beginning. The dry down is green with a touch of spice. She’s natural and aquatic. I love everything about this scent though the longevity for the price is stark.

I’m not getting Jo Malone (I so regret I did) anymore. Their scents are so cheap and linear. I was like a Virgin because it was the first niche, or I should say first fragrance brand that I exposed to. I didn’t like any fragrances before it. I first tried it and got this one. It smelled good at first because I was looking for something unique and bold. I didn’t know anything about fragrances. Their performance is bad too. Last only 2-3 hours and very weak projection. It also smells so mature. Once I found Kilian, Initio, Frederick Malle, Roja, MFK and Nishane then I realized how bad the quality of Jo Malone is. They are not cheap too. I rather spend a little more for these brands to get more unique complex scents and easily last double the time of Jo Malone.

When my father-in-law passed away, the sun was shining and the mirabelle tree in our yard was blooming in full splendor. He often got annoyed with this tree because it dropped tiny fruits in large quantities in the fall, which had to be picked up individually from the ground - but he always collected them before I could. Looking at the blooming tree, it becomes clear to me that I will never hear him on the yard again, even though that sound is so familiar to me. He no longer sees this beautiful, blooming tree, and perhaps it is only now that I realize that I have truly lost him. Today we lay him to rest, and we have two hours until the funeral to say goodbye. As superficial as it may sound: I thought about which fragrance I would wear after showering. For me, this consideration holds significance, as I know I will always remember my father-in-law when I wear the fragrance I choose today. I thought about Panthéa, because the scent is so clean and distant, radiating so much purity. In the end, however, I decided on one of my tuberose fragrances. I have a matching body cream for Tuberose Angelica, and I only envelop myself in this treasure on special days. Tuberose Angelica and her little sister, the cream, are as cloaked in black as I am, so simple, so serious. And above all: Of all my tuberose fragrances - and they hold, as some know, my perfumed heart - Tuberose Angelica is by far the most serious scent. Only it manages to bridge the elegance of the festive tuberose and the seriousness of the angelica. The green, herbal freshness merges with the tuberose from the very first seconds. I don't know what else should be in the pyramid, but I perceive the two notes in perfect balance. Thus, the opulent sweetness of the tuberose is drastically softened; there are indeed emotional worlds between something like "Love Tuberose" or "Heartless Helen" and the Jo Malone scent. It comes across as absolutely elegant, without being sweet, dreamy, or childish. It is an adult, serious tuberose and an elegant, fine angelica that come together here, powdery notes slightly resonate, cushioned by a fine, woody, restrained tone that radiates warmth. And it is, if I'm not mistaken, a Cologne, light. I believe I couldn't have chosen a more beautiful scent for this day, and I know that when I wear it next time, I will gladly experience the memory, for the choice is right. I didn't spend long on this comment, as it would have seemed disrespectful to me. But I felt the need to write down my thoughts about this fragrance that will accompany me today. My father-in-law, who was a father substitute for me during my marriage, since my own father passed away a long time ago, often spoiled me greatly. He liked it when his wife or I, the wife of his only child, were elegant. He would have been pleased with this fragrance. My husband gifted it to me along with the cream for Christmas. That would have particularly delighted him.

For days, it has been my faithful companion, day in and day out, unobtrusive yet present. I am so taken with its green-herbaceous playful tuberose sweetness, floral yet not at all opulent (even though I like that). Anyone who enjoys tuberose and angelica will find this to be a delight. It is by no means gourmand, not woody or earthy, nor sugary. Instead, it shines brightly, a picture of a green clearing where little elves dance, that comes to my mind. This fragrance makes (me) happy and invites dreaming. An ideal companion through stressful days, as it conveys lightness and joy. Such a beautiful clear, almost linear scent. The sillage is close to the body, present for many hours. For me, a spritz in the morning is enough on the skin, and I still catch a whiff of it 10 hours later - probably no one else does, as it is so close to the body, but if sprayed on clothing or hair, it lasts even longer, up to 18 hours, and still remains unobtrusive. I received a surprise decant from the lovely QueeN after this fragrance had been on my wish list since I first sniffed it last year in Munich at Beck. I think it will stay on my wish list and will eventually find a permanent home with me, as the decant is unfortunately almost used up.

In my opinion, Tuberose Angelica by Jo Malone is a fragrance for every season. For quite some time, I have been sniffing through all of Jo Malone's offerings in various selected perfumeries, repeatedly affirming some scents only to discard them later.

Tuberose Angelica is a fragrance that has stayed with me since my first visit to Venice. I tested it there for the first time and have since tried it numerous times in German perfumeries to ensure that this wonderful scent truly smells as good as I remembered. The tuberose dominates and provides a rich, creamy floral scent.

I was not expecting this one to be this good. With a desperate flanker name like "Parfum Intense" it just feels like they're clutching at straws for this line to be relevant. And honestly, it hasn't been since Hero Eau de Toilette was released, and that's only because that's a cut rate version of Dior Homme (2020) Eau de Toilette . The EDP and Parfum are just department store filler amberwoods. And admittedly, the drydown here is not complex and kinda just goes the same path as Hero Parfum . But the opening is crazy. Super smoky leather and vanilla - "Le Vestiaire - Babycat | Yves Saint Laurent" vibes, morphing into a really nice woody mid. There is always that sharp maltol sweetness lingering around though. Like I said, the base gets a bit generic, but holding it up to my nose I can still get the some of the smoky embers of the powerful opening remaining. Performance is quite good, projecting immensely in the first hour or two then settling on skin for another 6-8. Usually these kinds of smoky leather frags are not for youngsters but the aforementioned sweet maltol really youth-ifies it and I could see a particularly edgy teenager rocking this at school (like I did Bvlgari Black back in the day ). I'm sure this one's gonna fly right under everyone's radar because it's a blandly-named flanker in a super boring line but it is definitely worth a try. Edit: my pricing rating is based on what I'm predicting the discounter price to be at a few months from now. You can find Hero Parfum for around $50 on discounters and I assume this will be the same. Edit 2: this one stayed on me all night and well into the morning when I took a shower. Updating my longevity rating because this is BEASTLY

Burberry Hero Parfum Intense unfolds like dusty amber tobacco nestled in a mahogany humidor, cedar oils so intense they conjure a romance novel Fabio carved entirely from fragrant wood; golden resin pooling in the grain of his impossible biceps, abs you could grate cheese on if they weren't made of aromatic cedar, pectorals broad enough to land a helicopter if they weren't so heavily forested with sawdust, a sprinkle of black pepper-like errant chest hairs poking through his unlaced pirate blouse. Thighs like ancient oak trunks offering not seduction but the domestic comfort of a Snuggie, strong arms thick as timber promising Calgon-take-me-away escape, the performative masculinity of rippling wooden muscles dissolving into something unexpectedly nurturing, pipe tobacco sweetness without the acrid burn, fragrant wood shavings soft enough to curl up against those carved shoulders. Fragrance as guilty pleasure romance novel, the kind you read alone in Cheeto-stained sweatpants: Johanna Lindsey's never published My Lumber Lord's Love Log.

Hero Parfum Intense presents a rich, smoky, leathery, sweet, vanillic and woody scent that is ideally suited for winter and autumn. It is notably strong and carries a nutty undertone, with the leather initially giving off a gasoline-like aroma that gradually fades away. This leans towards the niche market, and many may not appreciate it, especially during the opening and mid stages. This fragrance is loaded with vanilla in the dry down and is quite heavy. A maximum of 3 sprays is sufficient, as more could lead to an overwhelming and potentially nauseating experience. I believe it might even surpass other well-known elixirs in strength. Although leather scents are not usually my preference, this one distinguishes itself as something rather different. The only downside is it's somewhat linear; I would have preferred a bit more complexity, but it still holds its own as it is. Initially, I received a tester sample and found it somewhat unexciting. However, I kept coming back to it, I couldn't stop smelling the tester strip; it possesses an addictive quality, especially for those who appreciate very dark fragrances.

a smooth leather, a fine black pepper, an incense-like spice, and nondescript woody base. no pine as the others have had, no coniferous scents, no dark green leaves or anything: it's a creamy leather with pepper and warm spice and not much else. its phenomenally strong, it lingers like smoke in the air, and clings to skin and clothes like no other.

I really enjoy this. This is a very nice mass appealing scent. It is quite smooth for a leather scent. The anamlic touch is very faint to my nose. It becomes more apparent in the dry down, giving it a masculine appeal. Overall very creamy, woody scent. In the air I almost get a sandalwood type vibe. If you removed the florals and added a masculine leather and pepper to Dolce the One EDP, you'd get close to this. That's just what I smell, I'm sure many won't agree with that. As far as performance, I could still smell it on my shirt the next day pretty well. Sillage appeared average but I received a compliment from a couple feet away after nearly 4 hours of spray. I think there is a fair amount of nose blind with it.

Pepper spray, cheap cognac and pungent sour pleather. Super strong and aggressive. Fills the whole room and then some from a single spray, stings my nose, makes me cough and struggle to breathe. Suddenly I'm a child again, holding mother's hair back while she pukes out of the taxi window. Revolting.

Yesterday I tried something new again and sniffed through Burberry's Hero line. On one wrist, the Hero perfume, a very pleasant start, nothing that stands out, nicely balanced but still not boring. Then the new Intense perfume on the other wrist - BAM! It blows me away. Leather, spice, a hint of woodiness, mixed with subtle sweetness.

All respect. Those were my first thoughts after the first spray, which were confirmed by the impressively long drydown. If Dior were to present this work, the praises from influencers would likely be unbearably loud. You are dealing with a wonderfully balanced oud/leather scent that expresses just the right amount of sweetness and spiciness.

The EdP Intense is a striking fragrance with a masculine presence. The wearer spreads his scent relentlessly in the room; one might think even through closed doors. Even outdoors, it is well perceived by others with above-average projection. Whoever wears it wants to be noticed and thus points to his masculine presence and sovereignty.

... at a small café on the Istrian peninsula. In front of me is a cappuccino and some Fritule (small balls). I can smell the scent of the cedar forest nearby. The sun is trying to warm me, but it hasn’t succeeded yet, and still, it is relaxing. Especially when the wind brings a breeze from the sea.

This fragrance does not smell bad at all, but unfortunately has some tinge in it that brings to my mind the smell of stink bugs. With that scent association I get, deal breaker for me. The smell of stink bugs I've read is some times compared to coriander. I don't see coriander as a note in this one anywhere, and the smell of coriander does not bother me at all, and does not bring to my mind stink bugs. But in any case, to me this fragrance does. I'd suggest smell before you buy, specially if you particularly dislike the smell of coriander and/or stink bugs.

This is my favorite pickup recently! Love the bottle and design of Givenchy, super classy. First spray is that woody, iris, coffee and vanilla. Main notes being coffee and vanilla. It reminds me of Mancera Amore Cafe with the coffee/vanilla, but clearly more masculine with the woodiness elements. The sillage is moderate, the longevity is moderate. The scent is so good. This is my favorite of the Gentleman line. It was hard to pick between this, boisee, edp, edt intense and reserve privee, but this is just so unique and versatile. This can be a great fall/winter/spring time signature and depending where you live, will do great under 80 degrees.

The coffee note practically makes this a gourmand. With the rest of the notes, the original Society is very much present, not in the background but alongside the coffee. Overall, it's a very pleasant fragrance. If you like Society or coffee notes, this is very much worth checking out. Definitely a Fall/Winter fragrance. Maybe a spring fragrance on a cooler day and maybe a rainy summer day.

For my nose and seemingly overtly feminine fragrance preferences, this is too strong, but surprisingly, I am loving all the notes together. It's fresh, sweet, rich, and gourmand, with an energizing opening. I find the scent masculine and sexy without being overwhelming. Unlike with many masculine-leaning scents, I don't sense too much spiciness or headachey sharpness. Gentleman Society EDP Extreme has more a powdery sweet ending that shows itself around 7-8 hours. This isn't one of those beast mode scents that you can apply for a night out and wake up at noon the next day with it lingering on your wrists. This doesn't quite hit the yummy sweet spot (quite literally) of my favorite masculine-marketed fragrance, Azzaro The Most Wanted, but if I met someone who was wearing this, I would give them a compliment for sure! It's just not quite the one for my own personal use.

I’m not exactly sure why I subjected this “Gentleman Society EdP Extreme” to a closer examination. Surely, the significantly higher and impressive price played a role, overshadowing all other Givenchys with ease. Or perhaps it was the minimalist metallic bottle. Or just coincidence. Either way: it was an instinctively good decision! At first, this particular “society” indeed comes across as somewhat… boring. Staid. Undefined. Sweet, nice, but without a unique selling point. Not a failure, but simply too wishy-washy. However, after a few minutes, textures, edges, and scent facets revealed themselves that elevate this “Society” to a whole new level. Essentially, a rough, well-equipped iris fragrance unfolded before me - but an iris like I’ve never perceived in this accord before! And that is more than enough of a unique selling point. Rarely has it scratched so pleasantly. Nutmeg and peppermint together tingle, crawl, and tickle. A (for the designer sector) very high-quality (but somewhat boring) vanilla in the dry down calms and smooths the edges. Then it becomes somewhat arbitrary, to be precise. But fundamentally, this socially acceptable gentleman is a splendid fellow. A very special, sensational iris. Bottle: thick glass base I like Sillage: rather dense than wide Longevity: 8 hours and often enough even double digits Conclusion: this “Society” takes a little time to understand… then it’s a scratchy-masculine iris (!), that won’t leave my mind, nose, and heart. A grower!

The Gentleman line from Givenchy is one of my favorite lines in the designer sector. So far, I find all releases from this line to be successful. The regular Society was the worst of this line so far, even though this "Society" concept had potential with its great DNA. However, I found the execution to be a bit lackluster, and the synthetic notes were a bit too noticeable.

The fragrance notes captivated me, I couldn't help it and had to test this scent, and what can I say: The facts do not lie. At first, the scent reminds me of hazelnut; knowledgeable perfume enthusiasts in the ticker told me that vetiver can sometimes come across as nutty. The drydown with the coffee notes, vetiver, iris, and vanilla sets in relatively quickly.

Many thanks to Carsten for the original manufacturer sample of Gentleman Society Eau de Parfum Extrême :-) This is now one of the very few fragrances from today that I absolutely cannot stand.
