This coffee-vetiver aroma is simply terrible and unbearable for me - sorry! However, the longevity on my skin is really strong.

... yes, the coffee aroma is there but unfortunately fades away very quickly. However, the chestnut comes through beautifully. When applying this fragrance, the first scent that hits the nose is coffee. Even though it's not listed in the fragrance pyramid, a chestnut aroma quickly emerges that stays throughout. This perfume is underscored by a dry and dark, very dark note.

The fragrance starts off strong with notes of chococcino, meaning coffee aromas paired with something chocolatey. I feel similarly about the classic A Men by Mugler. It could be due to the patchouli that it goes in that direction for me. It is definitely an unusual gourmand fragrance that I find appealing.

If I ever created a scent from scratch, this is how I'd want it smell. Fresh, exotic, sexy and bright. You can tell that this is a unisex scent, but that doesn't bother me. On both sexes this would smell absolutely amazing. CK One Summer 2009 takes me to my happy place; lying on a beach on a warm day sipping a refreshing beverage while feeling the sun soak into my skin. In other words this is a very beachy scent. The fragrance opens with the delicious blend of mint, cucumber, lime and bergamot. I can smell every one of these notes and let me tell you, this is the ultimate Summery scent. The scent is so unusual with notes like sea water, rosemary, rum and oakmoss creating something that you'd only expect to find hidden in a niche fragrance. I am highly impressed by this offering from Calvin Klein, it's a pity that it's a limited edition. I'm seriously considering buying this fragrance in bulk because I love it so much.

The 2009 summer version of CK ONE is a wonderful scent for hot days. The composition is interesting and refreshing with citrus notes, herbs and woody base. The scent would smell equally nice on a man or a woman. It is not too masculine but also not too feminine, so it occupies this wonderful territory of truly unisex scents. And the most important, it does not smell cheap but has depth, complexity and balance. CK ONE 2009 is my perfect companion for sunny days on the beach, power walks in the morning or simply relaxing in the backyard. I can put it on whenever I want to feel refreshed and relaxed. The opening of CK ONE 2009 has a lovely zing of lime, freshness of mint and relaxing cucumber. The mixture works great. I love both lime and mint here. The scent remains aromatic as it develops. In the heart notes I continue to smell mint and lime but there is rosemary and apple added to the mix. The floral notes of lotus are very gentle and not overpowering. I also enjoy how the woody base comes in pretty soon and adds lovely layer to the heart notes. The scent remains woody aromatic in the dry down but there is a drop of rum in the base. It is not too strong to be perceived as an alcohol but it gives very interesting and pleasant accent to the woods. The only drawback of this scent is the longevity. I can smell it for 4 hours tops on my skin, so I keep on reapplying. But other than that, I definitely recommend this scent if you can find it. I think it is one of my favorites CK ONE flankers.

I haven't had CK One (the classic) for a long time, after smelling it on everyone during the summer for years. The 2009 summer edition is wonderfully light, tropical, and reminds me of a beach bar in the Caribbean. After spraying it on, I first thought: Mojito to spray! Then it turned out to be more like Long Island Ice Tea in my nose. Well, rather a combination of both. The top notes of cucumber, lime, and mint create a desire for vacation, and with the heart and base notes, everything dissolves into even more pleasure, feeling clean, straight, and suitable for the whole day-the typical CK One scent. 100ml of liquid vacation to spray on! If someone is looking for me, I’m quickly at the beach bar :-)

beautiful composition of fruits and flowers, finely spicy! You can actually smell the cucumber; it radiates freshness. Every part of the heart note is recognizable, but with the water accord, I’m not quite sure what kind of scent that is supposed to be. The base note is very pleasant; however, I can't detect any rum, or maybe I've just been drinking the wrong kind my whole life - laugh! All in all, a successful summer!
I tried it yesterday. Unisex? Yes, definitely! Very summery, fruity scent. Rum notes are definitely present. Ideal for spring/summer, otherwise... maybe something else would be better.

This fragrance really smells extremely fruity and summery. I always take this scent when I go on vacation and we head to the sea in the morning. It immediately brings the right anticipation for a meaningful day by the sea.

At the beginning of the fragrance experience, the citrus notes of the top note emerge and then quietly remain in the background throughout the progression. I particularly enjoy the harmonious symbiosis of hibiscus and vanilla. They balance each other so excellently that neither the hibiscus becomes too floral, nor the vanilla too sweet. Jasmine and ylang-ylang also act here as a subtle accompaniment. Such an alluring composition that definitely guarantees compliments, and I see it more on a lady.

Expecting a real baby powder or baby cream scent "Baby Touch" was really confusing for me at the first hours of testing. But who knows? Maybe in another country, culture or continent the babies skincare is smelling like "Baby Touch"? I am just perceiving a not so gentle chypre in the first phase of the top notes. Because "Baby Touch" is starting with green and citrical notes and clearly more with the tangy scent of verbena than those of spearmint. I like it, really. But I do not consider it as a babies scent. I consider it more for adults and as unisex. But then is following a delicate and transparent blossom-mixture, more poudry than creamy. I would claim that "Baby Touch" has a gentle tea-note. This beautiful flowery scent is very long lasting. Nothing else is happening. The ingredients of the base notes seem to have the task to stabilize the heart-notes because I cannot recognize moss. And fortunately for me there is no milk-bar-scent with vanilla flavour. "Baby Touch" is an agreable female blossom scent with not exaggerating powdry and creamy notes.

Since I was already very enthusiastic about Zwitsal, I couldn't resist testing "Baby Touch" as well. Apparently, I've recently developed a liking for baby powder scents. Although comments like "smells like a baby or baby bottom" confuse me quite a bit. How does a baby actually smell???? (Comments from mothers are welcome) I don't have a baby. And in my circle of friends, it's not quite time yet. And I lack the courage to approach strangers with strollers to ask if I could sniff their baby. Just imagine the situation. ("What?! No, I'm not crazy!!! Why are you running away now? I just want to know how your baby smells so I can compare it with my new perfume.") Sorry, my imagination is running wild. :-) So "Baby Touch" is very nicely packaged. The cardboard box even has a press button. And the bottle itself is in a terry cloth pouch with a little sheep on it. I think that brings a little squeal of delight from every woman. About the scent: I admit, I expected something different. With this bottle and packaging, you just expect to be enveloped in a cloud of baby powder. Nevertheless, the scent did not disappoint me. On the contrary. Upon the first spray, I distinctly perceive mint and mandarin. Verbena and rhubarb round it off, so it’s neither too citrusy nor too sharp. Later, it becomes a bit more floral and powdery. But it doesn't change significantly (at least for me). I couldn't compare it to another scent. For me, it is a calm and fresh fragrance. Perfect for clearing the mind. It is neither intrusive nor loud. Although the sillage could be a bit stronger for me. I don't want to bother anyone with my perfume, but you really have to be quite close to smell it. The longevity could also be better. However, I recently acquired a 100ml bottle at a very good price, meaning you don't have to feel guilty about reapplying. For me, it is a fresh, slightly powdery feel-good scent. It doesn't lull you to sleep but wakes you up and makes you happy. A little help for a good start to the day.

Oh, what tender citrus accords open this fragrance so caressingly soft and gentle, I don't know citrus scents like this pure and clean fresh mint notes blend into the velvety citrus swirl and gently and softly transition to powdery soft white flowers, not exactly identifiable somehow washed out or veiled, they come through the base is vanilla milk, but not cloyingly sweet, rather very calm and thoughtful, cuddly soft mossy notes invite to relax and dream a mild scent suitable for every day with incredible longevity yet a low sillage for me, more of a relaxation and soothing fragrance I personally would wish for a laundry detergent and a fabric softener with the scent note

This one is very popular with me as well, I searched for it online for a long time and was glad to finally have found it. It was a blind buy, but since I knew I would like it, I ordered 2 right away. And I love this scent. I really like these baby powder scents and I am currently collecting others as well. It is a powdery but still fresh scent, so not "dry powder". It lasts quite a long time on me, especially when a spritz goes on my clothes, I can still smell it the next day. I also like to use this in the evening after showering/bathing to sleep. During my pregnancies, I didn't like any scents at all and I wouldn't have sprayed my girls with it either, they smell wonderful on their own unless the diaper is full.;-) I hope I can still buy this scent later, it seems to be not so often available in Germany anymore.

At first, it smelled to me like a simple cologne, a bit lighter and powdery... After reapplying it several times, since it lasts no longer than 5 minutes, a slightly musty scent emerged at the end, as if one had placed their powdered baby on a forest floor, just slightly, but I found that very disturbing. I am a lover of fresh, clean scents, but this one is far too short-lived, aside from the slight "damp earth smell".

...smells the baby perfume from Burberry. Very piercing, strongly synthetic like a laundry detergent that fades relatively quickly and transitions into a powdery softness. The perfume then smells very much like a baby :-) loving, cute, soft, innocent... It doesn't last very long and I had to reapply often. The bottle is super cute.

This fragrance is intended for babies, but I wouldn't perfume babies anyway, so HERE'S MY critique :)..a very delicate scent. It initially smells somewhat like a refreshing wipe, but on the skin, it reveals delightful surprises! Very subtle and actually gets better over time. Warm and lovable. Currently my favorite fragrance.

The bottle seemed to exude a lot of promise. The red could have represented something hot and sexy, or masculine and bold. In all honesty, Xeryus is a bit of everything. This is quite possibly one of the most intriguing male fragrances I've come across in the last few years. It's crisp yet fiery and spicy. Xeryus Rouge makes me think of all those men in my life that were so bad that they were impossible to resist. Both those men and this fragrance has me drawn like a moth to a flame. This fragrance is dangerous and exciting. If you're looking for a scent that equates to sex, look no further. This woodsy, spicy and slightly sweet scent is commanding, masculine and sensual. It gets me all hot just talking about it. I can really sense the red hot chilli in this fragrance, which gives off a rather warm yet fresh, invigorating feel. The scent can be a little sharp and tart-like at times, but only when smelt up-close. From a distance, Xeryus Rouge has a definite, subtly sweet smoothness. This fragrance is so unique that it almost puts what I hold as 'out-of-the-ordinary' to shame. All the complexity that is contained in this one bottle is quite breath-taking. The lasting strength is great, and let's be honest, this fragrance has the ability to suit practically every season and every occasion. Just make sure that you wear this during a passionate night with your lover, it will drive her absolutely insane and she'll remember this fragrance for years to come.

Very unusual scent (very unique). Smells different, in a good way. I find it suitable for a party cause i think that projects well and have a very good lasting power. PROS: - Good projection and lasting power. - Unusual spicy smell CONS: - Underrated - Not very "romantic" I want this in my collection cause i think if one of the best of Givenchy and unlike anything else. If you are a fragrance collector or looking for some different scent, try this, can be a nice surprise. Regards.

Very unique scent. In my opinion this is one of the best releases from Givenchy. Fruity and spicy at the same time, it's actually hard to describe it. Opens with a great cactus and kumquat notes layered over a peppery cedar base. The little sweetness is in the right amount. Sillage, lasting power and projection are high. Definetely a must have and big thumbs up! Updated January 2014

This red glass with that font type somehow suggests brutality, and made me curious, so I purchased it blindly. Well...Xeryus Rouge is absolutely different from what I expected. Instead of a supermasculine scent, I got a very bracing fresh woody perfume. The cactus note gives some bitter freshness, the pepper guarantees the spicyness, and the cedarwood is a perfect base. Nothing special, an all-weather scent for every age. To me this scent is totally up-to-date, it easily could be marketed as a new release, see No Limit$ Plein Super Fre$h which is truly similar, bur Xeryus Rouge feels much more refined. For 40€ that's a bargain especially if you are looking for another spring/summer scent, because you are f'ed up with the mainsteram. Absolutely recommended.

I'm enjoying this fragrance much more than I expected. By the reviews I assumed it would be more of a cooler weather scent but, for me, this could be worn every day of the year. And while I do agree that it is a unique scent, I find it difficult to believe many people would dislike smelling this on you. I was fortunate enough to find a vintage bottle that hasn't gone sour. The performance is much better than I expected.. you get decent projection the first 2 to 3 hours, but by hour 6 there's still a pleasant scent bubble that I notice off and on. I'm hopeful, but not optimistic, that the current formulation is at least half as good as the vintage. Because this, for me, is a signature worthy scent.

I was a teenager in the 1980s and by 1987 i started becoming interested in fragrances. I purchased many different kinds back in the day and the original Xeryus by Givenchy was one of my picks. I loved it and still do, although i refuse to buy the current formulation in the drab new bottle. Only the vintage art deco one will do.

This was a recent blind buy for me and I am glad that I purchased it. Xeryus Rogue has a very creamy wood, cactus and pimento cheese opening. A clean scent, but not a squeaky clean scent. Kind of like the good guy that knows how, and when, to be a bad boy. I find XR to be a sexy, classy and masculine scent that has good projection and longevity on my skin.

Not dated, but not youthful either. As opposed to the club settings most people recommend this for, I find that it works excellently in serious business settings, meetings, negotiations etc. where it commands your fellow attendants to pay attention.

Well, after giving Xeryus Rouge such a good review, I am back again. But THIS time, not so good. I thought I had found a new signature scent, but I was wrong. That raw (VERY raw) cactus flesh is a bit too much for me. (CACTUS flesh or ROTTING flesh?) I can certainly see why some people find XR disgusting. I find it almost tolerable on fabric, but definitely not on my skin.

I am immediately wowed by the smell of cactus combined with the orange and some hint of pimento. It's really gorgeous and refreshing. I was expecting it to be really dark because of the red vintage bottle but it's actually a nice 90 percent freshie. I'm using a perfume oil inspired version and I am so glad that I discovered this gem.

smells like a cold, fresh spring day. this is what i imagine persephone to smell like. it’s a bit strong at first but after a few seconds you get the flowers. as the description says, this is perfect for spring. no matter if it’s a warm or cold day. however, unfortunately the scent doesn’t last long on your skin. on clothes, sure but for the body you’d have to re-spray it every 2-3 hours or so. still, i really enjoy wearing it since it makes me enjoy spring much more than usual :)

Starts off GORGEOUS - drops of shiny tart, sweet pear juice plus gentle naturalistic floral notes as if you’re really floating through a spring garden. There’s also something cooling about it. Unfortunately all that beauty dissolves pretty quickly after the first half hour into some bitter undertones that didn’t sit well with me, because they reminded me a bit of old sweat + crushed pear stem. I think it’s this particular kind of musk note that becomes a bit too sharp/sour for me with the rest of the notes. (I normally like powdery musks - I wish I could get the powdery dry down that others seem to get.) Oh well.

So I was able to test it today, as I ordered it blind directly from Jo Malone. I cannot agree with the first review in that I own both Pear & Freesia and Nectarine Blossom & Honey. I layered both, and that does not correspond to the new Pea. This one has only a very slight sweetness at the beginning, but much more of a lightly tart fruity freshness. Like a pear that is not quite ripe yet. This fades fairly quickly on the skin, leaving a wonderful composition that I can hardly describe. Since I am not familiar with the scent of sweet peas, I can only say that it becomes more floral. But floral not in the sense of "being overwhelmed by so much flower," but very lightly, like the scent of a flower being carried away by the wind. The pear now remains very subtle in the background, as the musk as a base beautifully "powders" the scent. It even has a slightly creamy aroma, like when the sun warms up a moisturized skin. It stays very close to the body in an exceptionally balanced way. Those who know Malone know that they are all beautiful in their own way, but still - depending on the skin - sometimes only one scent note is much more perceptible. Not so with this one. The three: pear, sweet pea, and musk complement each other perfectly, and none takes away space from the other. null stands out. They play together like a perfect musical trio. Softly, with gentle tones. I can't say anything about longevity yet; so far, it has held beautifully for 3 hours unchanged. Can you layer it? Certainly. But whether you should, I don't think so. Because it is so well done on its own and so gentle that any other Malone on top could ruin it. My first thought after spraying was even that this is not a typical Malone. It is different, wonderfully different.

I had the chance to smell and test this fragrance in Edinburgh, and what can I say, this is once again a scent that reminds me classically of Jo Malone. The longevity for me was 6 hours, so nothing that blows you away, but also not as delicate as it can sometimes be with Jo Malone. But how does this new fragrance smell? For me, it is the lovechild of English Pear & Freesia and Nectarine Blossom & Honey. On me, it smells exactly like the layering of these two. The pear is 1 to 1 the same as the one we already know from English Pear & Freesia, but it brings the floral sweetness that you know from Nectarine Blossom & Honey. There isn’t much change in the scent over the 6 hours. Only the acidity of the pear diminishes a bit, and the floral notes come out a little more. So, anyone who combines these two fragrances only needs to buy one in the future. Those who already own both can leave this one aside, and if English Pear & Freesia was too acidic for you until now, you might find a new favorite here.

First comes the fresh pear, which is beautifully juicy green and not too sweet yet. I’m not exactly sure how scent peas smell. I can sniff out unsweetened flowers and freshly cut greens. But in between, it seems to me that notes of a bitter herbal tea or sun-dried hay tickle my nose. Overall, the fragrance develops floral notes, but definitely less sweet than I would have expected; towards the end, it becomes slightly powdery. Absolutely wonderful. For a moment, I have to think of the large flowering bush in my grandma's garden, whose branches hang down to the ground, creating a perfect hiding spot underneath. As a child, I spent hours playing there with grandma, beneath me a soft carpet of moss and grass, above me a protective canopy of dense green and flowers. Grandpa picked the pears and sometimes brought them to us for a snack, but only if he could find us in our secret hiding place at all. I’m already looking forward to summer again.

My first Jo Malone after an eternity, discovered by chance in Stuttgart while I wanted to show my good friend in Breuninger what I already own and love. There’s also English Pear & Freesia, which is a completely different scent with patchouli, and I only like patchouli in homeopathic doses; Sweet Pea is the successor. Released in 2023 and perfect for spring.

It is one of my favorite childhood memories: My grandpa built a two-meter-high wall of "rabbit wire" in the garden every spring. There, the peas would first grow, and after their harvest, the sweet peas would climb high.

The English Pear & Sweet Pea from the house of Jo Malone is a simple yet so perfect fragrance. The composition of just three scent notes harmonizes so well, as if they were made for each other. Here, the Williams pear clearly takes center stage. Wrapped in a sweet pea, accompanied by fresh musk, a sweet-fresh pear scent emerges that is addictive.

Burberry Touch is different to say the least. I'm not usually a lover of green and soapy scents, however this fragrance charms me. This fragrance opens with a sharp, green bitterness which tends to rather masculine. Despite being turned off by this opening I was intrigued by it and kept bringing my wrist to my nose to smell it over and over again. In a way I wanted this fragrance to turn creamy and slightly sweet, however in the heart it is mostly a powdery and soapy scent. The notes are very light, almost undetectable. It's like the composition has been mixed so well that it's hard to identify any particular notes. Some would call this powdery floral mediocre, but I find it to be much more complex than it seems. The way it settles on the skin is very delicate, it becomes a scent that isn't just perfume, it is like a natural part of yourself, a natural skin scent. This fragrance lingers on your skin for hours and I never get sick of it. It is so enticing that I can barely stop smelling it. The overall impression is a light, pretty and inoffensive fragrance best suited for daytime/casual wear.

You'll never read me saying - 'You're wrong, I'm right.' regarding any fragrance, ever. But...there are times when I'll say something akin to - 'I truly cannot understand what you guys are experiencing, and disagree with your perception entirely.' This is one of those times. I don't relate to any of the unsavory remarks about this perfume whatsoever. But, I was admittedly, more intrigued *because* of them (and not in spite of them). I went out to my car to check perfume sites and get a feel for what this might have in store for me before returning to Ross to purchase it. And FWIW, all of the perfume sites/resources I checked have conflicting notes (this is not an uncommon occurrence, but it's annoying...I have my suspicions as to which is more correct or incorrect, but I'm gonna stay quiet about that). All of this to say, reviews are all over about this, references disagree as to the notes, and it's seemingly a polarizing fiasco. Naturally, I was completely compelled and purchased it, hah! I love this. It's a seemingly incongruent batch of notes, but it works. It's not nearly as cedar-y or sharply woody as I anticipated, nor as fruity. In fact, I get barely any fruits whatsoever in the opening, and it goes STRAIGHT into a plushy, almondy, powdery sandalwood blend. I get NO pepper. No pink pepper. Nothing spicy and/or red. The entire composition feels 100% beige to me. People have claimed this is masculine. And...I vehemently disagree. I'm actually struck by how sensually femme it is. "Touch" is a FANTASTIC title. It's clean, feminine, dry (I'd love to wear this when it's rainy) and reminiscent of cleaned and lotioned skin. However, it's not a modern "your skin, but better" (I'm so sick of that phrase, gag me...), it smells dated (which isn't criticism, it's refreshing). Like lotion or body oils from the Y2K era. Weirdly, I don't find any references to orris, but it's what I would've bet money on it containing. This is the kind of scent I admired as a kid. I was either 8, 9 or 10 when this was launched (again, the sources on this are a mess and disagree). As a child though, I was exposed to this sort of thing, but never wore it. To to have this bottle now is a fabulous and nostalgic gift to myself (this was my bday present to myself). I'm very happy with this, had a great gut feeling about it, and I'm thrilled that I listened.

As opposed to some other reviews, I love the fresh vegital opening. It’s in the dry down where I run into issues. If I’m being honest, they should have skipped the addition of vanilla which seems not to blend well with the florals and fresh pepper note in this. There’s a celery aspect to the fragrance which would have been fantastic had things been kept fresh and fruity. Celery and warm woody vanilla is not a keen combo however.

By chance, I stumbled upon this fragrance in a perfume store. That was over 12 years ago. I had never smelled it on anyone else until I was in the hospital, after a long phase without it, and I noticed a lovely, warm, and subtle scent trail from a fellow patient. I followed her and was thrilled! She was a bit confused, but I was able to explain and we agreed that it is the best perfume in the world! Well, one of the best... for everyday use... After that, I was back "on it," had to buy it immediately! It is a distinctive scent that comes in a brownish-red with fine pink and golden threads. (Unfortunately, as a synesthete, I am most capable of describing a scent through color comparisons.) Velvety soft, slightly floral, enveloping, tidy, and yet subtle. Perfect! I just realized that my last ration of Touch is empty, so: Off to the "dealer" to get the next "fix"!

Today I continued to store my perfumes on shelves, and I must shamefully admit that there were also some freshly wrapped, unopened boxes among them. Among them was Touch. I finally uncovered its secret and was pleased by the pleasant, unexcited scent that gently enveloped me. Very subtle - very British. Just like the beautiful Burberry wardrobe and the lovely bags of this label, it is an eye-catcher upon a second glance. The orange and the blackcurrant are refreshing, yet the rose oil is wonderfully old school and reminds me of the well-kept English gardens that shine with their old Austin roses. Cedar and vanilla suggest cozy fireplace gatherings in country houses and make the scent comforting. Here, understatement is written in capital letters, and that is precisely what touches me. All Barnaby and Miss Marple fans will feel addressed and mentally stroll through Cornwall.

...because it reads a bit like you first get a sticky fruit basket thrown at you, then get rolled over by a floral wave, and because it was so nice, you are finally overwhelmed by all sorts of woodsy creatures. But that's not true!

My first encounter with the Burberry brand took place when it was still spelled with an apostrophe and an "s" - I still love that coat dearly, which is probably twenty years older than I am and is still in much better shape than I can claim for myself.

A nice wealthy family has left us their holiday home in Ain Soughna by the Suez. In the couple's bedroom stands Touch for Woman. I actually like the Burberrys, so I allowed myself a tiny sample on a paper towel. Just like back when I was training to be a hotel manager and worked as a chambermaid for a while, happily (turning red) sniffing the guests' perfumes.

I love spending time in nature, and a fragrance that could put me in that mood would be great. At first, the scent seemed like it could do just that... So light, fresh, unobtrusive... Like taking a breath of fresh air... with a hint of pine. Later, it became very close to the skin, extremely subtle and featherlight. Like forest air. So far, so good.

Recently, I was at the drugstore with the horse in the logo. This happens rarely enough, as I usually prefer the chain with the two letters. Since I had some time - why not see what fragrances they have. I had heard about Body by Burberry from a YouTuber and decided to test it. Hmm... Not really my thing.

beside Chloe EDP. Oh, it has been 3 years since I bought this pink treasure. CK fragrances have never blown me away. I once owned Eternity Moment. It was quite nice, just a bit too "fabric softener-like." And I really don't like the original Eternity.. Back then, in the summer of 2014, I was looking for a sweet, floral, and not too heavy scent for the summer. That’s when I discovered Eternity Summer while passing by. It was actually the bottle that piqued my curiosity. Yes! the typical Eternity bottle, but in pink!! and the bottom of the bottle was milky. It looked quite pretty. That drew me in. When I sprayed it on, I knew this was my summer scent! And yes, it has remained that way to this day. I mostly smell the peony, not sharp but cuddly and soft. In the background, the juicy watermelon and the water lily keep the scent from being too stuffy, adding an elegant freshness. Towards the end, the warm musk comes in and rounds out the fragrance. Eternity Summer is a rose scent, but not an overwhelming one. It is fresh, but also floral and perfect for summer, especially if you don't like aquatics (like me). Unfortunately, it was a limited edition. That’s the only downside.. But since I bought it in the 100ml version back then and it lasts relatively well for a summer scent (around 5 hours it wafts around you, then it becomes close to the skin), I still have 50ml left :) I can only hope that next summer, or the year after, a nice summer edition will come out that is reminiscent of my 2014 one :)

Strangely, the perfume smells strongly of lilac, even though there is none in it. Perhaps it’s the blend of peony and watermelon that you can faintly detect. The perfume simply smells like lilac in fresh water and makes me think of the swimming pool. The slightly woody base note keeps it from being too overpowering. Unfortunately, it loses its scent quite quickly.

I had already reviewed this fragrance, however, i didn't own it back in the day, and now, i do, and i will give you my impressions on the fragrance, as i have been wearing it back and forth in different climates, during the last five months. My first impression on the Gentleman by Givenchy, in the first time i tried it, around my birthday of 2021 and around a year before of actually buying it, was a modern leather scent, much like CH Men Privé and JPG Le Male Essence de Parfum, such. Along it, i tested the vintage Gentleman '74 (Which i originally did like more than the current) and the Gentlemen Only Absolute, which i found nice but didn't really interest me to like, buy it, plus the already mentioned CH Privé, JPG Le Male Essence, Dior Hommes and Polo green, which i ended up buying. Anyway, as i bought a fragrance of my choice in my birthday (July) of this year, 2022, i went to the store hoping to find CH Privé and pull the trigger, since it was one of my favorite scents. They didn't have it, and i really wanted to walk home that day with a brand new modern leather, date frag, and they had some Gentleman EDT 2017 gift sets at a good price. I bought a case, including a shower gel (Which i use to shave) and the EDT 100ml bottle. Gentleman (2017) by Givenchy is a fragrance that takes inspiration out of several tendencies in the fragrance world, current and past. First of all might be CH Men Privé by Carolina Herrera, as leather seems to be a path very appealing to one of the perfumers, Nathalie Lorson. However, the CH frag is based upon a kind of russian leather, as it has wood bark tar smoke, phenolic nuances, along petrol tones and an astringent whisky note in the head, along warm spices and tonka bean sweetness, while Gentleman has a more tamed down sweetness, its leather note is more refined and not as "in your face", and its booze nuances are lighter and more refined as well. To my eyes, the CH fragrance has a more appealing leather note than the Givenchy, however, having an extremely dominant and heavy leather note is not the purpose of this frag. I am guessing the purpose of Givenchy when ordering the creation of Gentleman '17, was making a versatile, modern, but manly fragrance, different than the already known "blue" fragrances that dominate the market today. This was done by the two noses creating a "light" leather scent, with a fruity head, cardamom spice and powdery floral nuances in the heart. This makes me think that, this actually has a bit of inspiration and structure taken from the original Gentleman from the 1970's, even though they go in completely different directions. To my taste, they share certain accords, if not the concept of the whole olfactive pyramids. In the opening, both possess boozy nuances, (Original: Animalic honey plus the civet in the base / Modern: Boozy aromachemical fruits) share a warm spicy and powdery heart (Original: Cinnamon, Patchouli and Orris Root / Modern: Cardamom and Iris) and both are dominated in their drydown by a leather note and sweetness (Original: Russian, dirty, smoky, brown leather with amber, plus the patchouli earth and civet rancid nuances / Modern: Refined, almost a suede - like leather, i am guessing based upon safroleine or violet like notes, with labdanum and resin nuances and pretty much no smoke at all, does have a castoreum ingredient but it is extremely tamed down, and has a vanilla note which softens the drydown a bit) When compared to either Gentleman '74 (Which i state once again, even when sharing the concept of their respective olfactive pyramids, don't smell nothing like the other) and CH Men Privé / JPG Le Male Essence, i would say the Givenchy perfume is way more refined and versatile, climate - wise, than the previously mentioned. While fall being the perfect time of the year for its use, can be worn in warmer winter days and fresher summer times. It is extremely sexy, and for that fruits, iris and refined leather combo, seems to me more elegant than some of its counterparts, when refering to the clothing to be used with it. If you ask me, wear a nice button up shirt, shave and put this on on a fall afternoon or evening on a date. She will love it. Bottom line: Good longevity, of some 7 - 8 hours, intimate projection which can either be a good or a bad thing (Being a leather based scent) extremely versatile for intermediate climates but still more elegant than casual IMO. I would advice to try it out, maybe you'll like it more than CH Privé for date use, it is very sexy. Greetings

This fragrance gets dismissed really quickly due to it being a very linear fragrance. It's a nice fresh scent, you get the fruitiness of the pear mixed with the lavender and iris while also getting the woody and vanilla notes at the base. The leather note is there but it's hardly noticeable at the beginning to my nose, but is does develop more around 30 minutes in. The description on this site is spot on by saying it's a powdery fresh scent, personally I would describe it as a fruity / sweet take on Prada L'Homme, it's a great daily business / casual fragrance, and at £60 for 100ml I would say it has a fair price as well, definitely one that will be a part of my collection for some time.

This cologne is light, fresh, aromatic and sweet. Not heavy, not try hard. It is a modern fougere with lavender, iris and geranium. I get the sweetness of the iris and the aromatic lavender at the same time. The lavender remains while the iris powderiness fades out into a mild vanilla and leather. It is deeply pleasant and well blended. No braggadocio. It’s agreeable and not overly challenging, appropriate for work and for date nights, and for smelling like an overall upstanding citizen. A current-day Clark Kent in the Daily Planet. Nanami from Jujutsu Kaisen. Definitely a white collar worker scent. Definitely attractive. Wear this if you’re a white collar worker who volunteers on the weekends. Wear this if you have drawer organizers. Wear this if you’re getting married and you want the family to love you. Wear this if you roll up your sleeves and you have nice forearms...but you're not flashy or anything. They're just there and you're proud of them. This is not a "beastmode pantydropper influencer blah blah blah" scent. Don't wear this if you're a flashy man. Wear this if you want to smell modern and quietly handsome. It's not an old-fashioned strong fougere. It's not a rough-edged, rugged man fragrance. It's a modern fougere for a guy who wants to smell good, but doesn't want to be the only smell in the room. It's perfect for a man aged between 20-35, and meant to be sprayed one to three times. It also would smell gorgeous on anyone...anyone of any gender would smell light, clean and fresh in this. Regarding longevity and sillage: My fiancé wears only one spray of the EdT at a time and it fades from a 6 inch scent bubble to only a light scent that you can smell two inches away. edit: I had originally left this review on the EdP which was incorrect.

Typical fresh opening, some fresh and fruity pear mixed with some freshness from the lavender, boring background woody/vanilla notes, nothing new here, same generic crap, but for a generic fragrance is nice, soft and clean, didn't bother me so the quality is ok, can't say the same for most designer releases this year that smell like deodorant and hairspray. Can't really say much about this one, it's ok, just that, ok... Hard to dislike so a safe bet and doesn't smell very cheap so, that's a plus now a days, actually better then most givenchy.

What I think about this one is that it's a safe option. I don't particularly think it's bad in any way, maybe just safe and pleasing. It's not one that would offend and I think it's a perfectly acceptable option for any man out there. I get that this is an update of an original fragrance, but this smells similar to many offerings out there. I get a great floral composition here. The iris and lavender (two of my favourite notes) are paired with leather - a fantastic combination, and coupled with what I think is hedione (the synthetic jasmine similar to Dior - Eau Sauvage). Other fruity notes may accentuate the composition which remains fresh and sweet. In summary, there is nothing wrong whatsoever with this fragrance, I find it very agreeable and pleasing, and I think people will like it. Longevity and projection are not great here so bear in mind to apply liberally. I think it's probably a better fragrance than Gentlemen Only however I must admit that the house of Givenchy has seen better days in the past.

Here we have something safe, harmless, "grab&go". I acquired it as a collector, the Gentleman line is one of my favorites and I find this EDT as the least favorite. What I like most is its opening, which rounds off a delicious fruity leather that quickly (too quickly) settles and shows off iris and patchouli slightly sweet from the vanilla.

We should be able to “smell” without “judging”, taking into account the experience of the perfumer in question, and go beyond what often “looks” but “isn’t”. It is precisely the judgment, and the tendency to judge the real obstacles, the absolute barriers to authentic communication.

I had given a 6 to the scent after the first try, but I am updating it to 8. The opening has a pleasant pear scent, at least on paper, and hope that also in your skin. Unfortunately not on mine. On me smells in an strange way, I can not describe it, I am afraid that my ph degrades the accord.

I think this is a little better than the rating it gets here and on another review site. Starts off really floral, which had me worried, but eventually settles to a lite sweet-ish fragrance. If there's patchouli and leather in there I'm guessing the pear, vanilla and lavender keep it very tame.

"Gentleman Only" (2013) was one of the last fragrances I purchased before my journey into the world of perfumes began. Before I became aware of my longing for olfactory completion, so to speak. :) In the months and years that followed, the fragrance, still at a good fill level, collected more and more dust in my collection.

Vanilla & Anise starts off with a strong anise/fennel note which is delicious! Sweetened slightly by the dry vanilla bourbon and a dash of Tonka in the middle...it is mesmerizing. This is definitely a gourmand scent for lovers of licorice, though not overly sweet, IMO. About 15 minutes in, I detect a "rootbeer/sasparilla" accord, which is akin to a creamy wintergreen+vanilla+nutmeg for those who don't have Rootbeer available. This seems to wear better on a Fall evening, as it blends with the surrounding smells of burnt maple leaves and crackling fire places. I initially tried it in the Spring and gagged- due to a hot cloying synthetic orchid note that stepped right out of Britany Spear's Fantasy (a.k.a., my personal fragrance nightmare...), but now on a cool overcast Fall day...I do not detect that at all, there is a touch of orchid but it is well behaved, adding just a little sensuous abundance and "eye of newt" to the cauldron. Vanilla & Anise seems softly alluring, reminding me of the excitement and thrill of dressing up in our coolest costumes of ghosts, warlocks and goblins and collecting free candy on Halloween. After about an hour this dries down into a lighter, watery version of something in the Hypnotic Poison/ Acqua Di Parma Mandorlo family, but with a double shot of Iso-E on the bottom. Though the sillage is about 3-6 inches (7.6-15.2 cm) radius- off of my skin maximum- this is typical of the Jo Malone Line, so if you've tried some from the line, you already know that they are fairly sheer. I think this is a mysterious, lovely vanilla and licorice scent, with a slightly haunting vibe to it that might layer nicely with JM's Nutmeg & Ginger Intense, Vetyver, French Lime Blossom-for the added freshness of a daytime scent or even Nectarine and Honey Blossom- if you have a real sweet tooth. Either way, you will have to invite this creature of the night across your threshold, it is not the sort of sillage monster that will lunge upon you, teeth-bared and ready to attack anyone in sight. It's a little sexy black cat familiar scampering across your path under the harvest moon.

Vanilla and Anise by Jo Malone is one of those fragrances that you hear about all the time, especially when browsing YouTube. I was of the opinion that I was missing out on something special, so I wrote it down in my 'for test' list, expecting to be blown away. Vanilla and Anise is nice but not breathtaking. It's not nearly as sweet and vanillary as I thought it would be. This fragrance is actually quite a light, spicy aromatic, with a hint of creamy tuberose and fluffy vanilla. The sillage is barely there. In that regard, it is quite an intimate and soft fragrance. I can guarantee that it won't offend a soul. I do however like anise and its green, licoricey quality, especially when used in this composition. I may have approached Vanilla and Anise expecting something along the lines of Lolita Lempicka, hence the reason why I was initially disappointed. For what it's worth, this fragrance is unique and classy. I would probably recommend using it more for layering purposes than to wear it on its own. Unfortunately, Vanilla and Anise is one cologne that failed to last on my skin. One to two hours and it was all but gone. It was a disappointment for me, but not a failure. Original review written: April 2013.

Sunday afternoon at the end of July. Barefoot, I wander through hip-high grass that crackles under my feet. It is hot, very hot - the air shimmers with heat. My legs are bare under the wide skirt, passing blades tickle my skin. Absolute stillness, only the buzzing and humming of insects fills the air. Being alone. Letting thoughts drift, lazy and aimless. I take a deep breath - the scent of the grasses rises to my nose, mixed with herbs and the hay drying in bales in the field next door. Bright red poppies dot the green, yellow and blue flowers whose names I do not know. My skin tingles under the sunscreen. A butterfly flutters ahead of me. Drops of sweat trickle one by one down my belly. The world seems to stop turning, should not turn any further. No wishes, no worries, no tomorrow. Happiness.

I love this scent. Generally, I am always on the lookout for vanilla perfumes, but there are only a few that I truly like. Most of the time, the vanilla is not soft enough for me, but rather comes through in a piercing way... Here, it smells pleasantly sweet, and then the spicy note of anise joins in. You feel wonderfully scented all day long without leaving an unpleasant trail behind.

Vanilla & Anise comes across really fresh and lively. I already find the top note great; the fresh bergamot and neroli create a wonderful contrast to the fennel and star anise. The scent is truly very floral with a subtle spicy note. I find it really fitting for spring right now. Jasmine, orchid... I always think of heavy perfumes, but that’s not the case with this one. Even the vanilla smells only very subtly. Today the sun is shining here, and I wish the tulip bouquet in front of me on the table smelled as amazing as this perfume. That would enhance my spring feeling even more, but they are just tulips, bought at the discount store... they look great, but don’t smell at all... I guess I have to get this perfume one way or another.

I purchased a bottle in 2018 at the store on Regent Street. The lady in the store confidently introduced me to the reissued edition, and what can I say: love at first sniff. Since then, I guard the bottle like my most prized possession and only spray it on special occasions.

"Body Tender" is a subtle little fruit that likes to run around naked. Okay, that sounds a bit intrusive. However, the scent is the exact opposite of that. A soft apple in the top note, a slightly soapy rose as it develops, and a velvety veil of musk laid over it - and there you have it, a go-to fragrance, an intimate nudist, a sexy clean scent. A fragrance between two lovers. At least in its most romanticized conception. This is how Disney princesses imagine the scent of making love. Extremely subtle, always stylish, the opposite of overloaded or intrusive. A beautifully whispering counterpoint in the usually screaming mainstream women's market. No sugar, no squeaking, no bling-bling, no in-your-face, no pick-me. Soft, silent, stylish. Flower-child sex in fragrance form. Not always necessary, but always works. Unmade-up, natural, and pretty. The perfect mix of wallflower, athlete, and ball queen. Love Me Tender! Bottle: a bit wobbly but nice. Sillage & Longevity: a skin scent lasting no more than 5 hours. Conclusion: soft, pleasant, unobtrusive, human - "Body Tender" is a powdery musk nudist that lives up to its name. Fine understatement.

Life is a quiz - and we are just the contestants… guessing, guessing, guessing. And among other things, we guess whether this blind purchase will meet our expectations and hopes this time? In this case, the blind purchase was indeed bold, because first of all, no Burberry scent has captivated me so far, secondly, certainly not Body (on me it’s sharp, prickly, rose-like) and thirdly, I have had little luck with blind purchases so far and have largely weaned myself off them. Exceptions confirm the rule, of course... With Body Tender, I simply relied on the comments. I bought it back in late summer, but now it really deserves a comment, as it is currently in use. What else can one do in a spring-like winter like this with 14 degrees Celsius, where the beloved winter scents just don’t bring any joy? Something heavy is too much, something summery is too fresh. So, a woman needs something soft, unobtrusive, nose-pleasing, and still warm. And that’s where Body Tender comes in just right. Nothing stings or pricks here, everything fits. The scent is soft and rounded, floral and warm, creamy and not sweet. The sillage is strong at first but soon weakens a bit. On me, Body Tender lasts quite a long time. With this lovely comforter and all-rounder, I feel just like that: comfortable and well-groomed, always and everywhere. When I really don’t know what to wear, I often reach for this one. Because with it, I can never go wrong. Body Tender envelops the wearer all day long with a pleasant, warm feminine aura. Exactly the right thing for this winter, which is a spring…

At first too citrusy, but then "Body Tender" transforms into a beautiful, soft fragrance that smells of apple blossom, pleasantly light with rose and distinctly of jasmine. A subtly spicy, woody note occasionally emerges. Later, the apple note becomes stronger and more prominent again, and the citrus note reappears, this time more subdued. Overall, the fragrance represents pure elegance for me in every situation.

This is my first perfume review and I ask for your understanding if I make one or two faux pas. Today I want to talk about my latest acquisition, Burberry Body Tender. Practically since Burberry Body hit the market, I have been a fan of this fragrance. Most of the time, I don't think much of the light summer variants of various scents - but not with this one. It starts very similarly to Burberry Body - strong and sensual with a hint of sweetness. However, after a while, the strength fades - what remains is a soft, slightly floral, fresh summer scent - yet it retains a slight heaviness. A bit freshly showered, but more with a cream shower gel and not with a fruity shower gel that you use after sports. It envelops you warmly and softly and feels grown-up. For summer, I love D&G Light Blue and Be Delicious, but this fragrance is elegant - not sporty, rather seductive - not girl, but young woman, something for the day, the evening, or work. However, be careful with the dosage. One to two spritzes are usually enough to enjoy it - otherwise, it quickly becomes intrusive and too present.

If Givenchy Gentleman is a "Stairway to Heaven" (although a slightly begrimed one), then Play Intense is "What goes around...comes around". And it's just as alpha male as Justin Timberlake compared to Robert Plant. It's also like the difference between entering a mouldy basement rehearsal room and entering a noisy mall with a greater than usual ratio of patisseries and sweet shops. Yes, there's noise and smells in both places, but only one of them has the potential to make a legend out of them. I don't know if that's the case with other countries too, but seeing samples delivered in cheap plastic sachets instead of glass phials (let alone miniature bottles) gets on my usually stolid nerves. Especially when they require a crowbar to be pried open. I guess that Justin's check swallowed all the glass available, just like those guys in sideshows of yore did. Or maybe it's just a hint that plastic is here to stay, slowly casting out all natural ingredients and burying them in polymer caskets. Now, I DO NOT like so-called gourmands. Don't get me wrong, I love the smell of coffee and all these little pieces of heaven that usually come with a cup. It's just the fact I believe that the only people who should smell like candy are the ones exiting a candy workshop, and that coffee without the smell of smoke is like Bonnie without Clyde. And I don't really understand why a fragrance containing coffee and caramel is a gourmand, while one containing lemon and sage isn't. Did herbs and citruses ceased to be edible at some point? Anyway, let's skip culinary debates and talk intensity and presence. Well, my take on playing intense goes like this. I still use an antediluvian CEC turntable and a Wharfedale amplifier/receiver for listening to music when at home. They both come from the '70s, and despite being heavy, bulky and by no means portable, they're made of wood and metal and they have something that no iPod will ever have. Soul. They behave in the selfsame way that their contemporaneous fragrances used to do. By filling a room with their presence. Visually, acoustically and olfactorily. Yes people, music does have a smell. Or at least it used to. It's the smell of the vacuum tubes being heated, the smell of air perturbed by monstrous speakers, the smell of a brand new vinyl record, the smell of sweat mixed with notes. Like the smell that once rendered Givenchy a linchpin of the fragrance world. Like the smell which used to foreshadow that something serious was coming our way. Like the smell which assured us that a scent's ingredients were born in the fields an not in test tubes. Like the smell that my Givenchy Gentleman bottles from the '70s pack in shedloads. Like the smell that Play Intense is the farthest cry from smelling anything like it.

I find Play Intense to be an entirely different composition when compared to the original Play. While Play was composed of citrusy and fresh notes, Play Intense is rather woodsy and dark, sometimes rubbery. I find many similarities between Play Intense and Bvlgari's Black. Play Intense is rather sexy. I doubt that I would feel out of place if I wore it myself to be honest. It's an interesting blend between smokey, dark woods and rich, syrupy yet masculine vanilla. It also has an earthy quality, particularly towards the heart, quite possibly due to the patchouli and coffee, which gives this fragrance the potential to be worn to night-time events. As a woman, that can often be picky when it comes to masculine fragrances, Play Intense is quite impressive and sensual. Due to its richer approach in comparison to the original Play, I find this release much more pleasant and wearable. Perhaps even a tad more interesting and not as generic per se. The longevity and sillage are relatively strong, and in some ways bold. I'm dismissing the fact that Justin Timberlake is the face of this product as I don't feel as if he suits this kind of scent. It's hot in a smouldering and mysterious sense of the word. I am thorougly impressed with Play Intense, and I feel that Givenchy has been a little daring with this, even though as a whole it's not particularly outstanding or unique.

For the longest time I avoided this cologne simply based on the fact that I hated the bottle it's in. I think it's immature looking and just plain ugly. A few weeks ago I went to a department store and was testing a lot of different colognes. The clerk was kind of pushy and was spraying a lot of samples on test strips that I didn't even ask to smell. null of them excited me until she sprayed this one. I can say that I was really shocked and surprised at how good the scent was compared to the bottle it was in. I just don't feel like the bottle is a good reflection of the delicious smelling cologne inside. I didn't buy it that day but the smell was good enough to make me think about the cologne until I decided I had to have it. I finally purchased it this week and all I can say is it's one of my favourites already. On the second day I wore it I had someone tell me how nice I smelled. I wish all of my colognes would get compliments like that but they don't. I can't stop sniffing myself when I have this one on. It just goes to show that you can never judge a book by it's cover!
The smell is very good. coffee with vanilla rocks. But for me the longevity n projection is not that good. It stays 3 to 4 hours, projection is good for first 1 hour then it gets close to my skin.

It opens with a citrus scent then dries down into a gentle spiced coffee scent. I would not say it smells really like coffee. In fact I haven't find something smells like real coffee in perfumes. But Play Intense does evoke an image of bitter coffee. It somehow also has an incense-like smell. I find it not very sweet, and clean. It's a versatile fragrance, not cloying sweet for summer and spicy enough for winter, day and night, unisex as well. That said, it still has its caracter. Its sillage is moderate and the longevity 7h+ on me. Originally written in 2013.

I will say this is a big improvement over it's father which to me smelled very flat. This adds more depth & feeling as I hoped it would since it is named intense! But if it were to compete against other gourmands in it's range I'd rank Play Intense dead last. It is not bad, but it is not great either.

Beautiful gourmand scent that definetely worth it. Despite not being unique, it's recommended because it smells great, the price aint high and has an average projection and lasting power. And yes, reminds a lot of Rochas Man. And yes, i find this more balanced than the coffee of Bond's New Haarlem (and it costs 1/5 of its price). Updated January 2014
i dont find this fragrance particularly gourmandish instead it shows a good ambery wood aspect that i really like ,easy to wear in a man during the working days ,warm in the skin with good projection

Finally, an Intense flanker that delivers on its promises without completely denying its Play roots. Clearly darker and suited for September to April. A dark gourmand coffee that outshines its lighter brother in every respect and can even hold its own against giants like Rochas Man or A*Men at times. Well done, Givenchy, it's about time!

So, I need to edit my comment now after a nice time during which I tested it extensively. I've already written a lot about the bottle when I wrote my Play comment. The scent itself is really a more intense version of Play. Some fragrance notes are very strongly accentuated. At first, I didn't really like it that much.

I’m learning that I’m a big fan of chypre scents. I absolutely adore the combination of florals and fruits, but especially when you add a patchouli or moss note. Even though I’m not crazy about moss, I’m seeing (or smelling rather) that when done right, it can add such beauty and grace to fragrance. The composition of Honeysuckle & Davana is very simplistic and the scent stays linear from start to finish, but it has a gorgeous depth. The davana is both aromatic and fruity, while the honeysuckle offers the bulk of the white floral/green scent that this has. Then the moss comes in and adds the gentlest touch of earthiness. It’s actually so stunning. I tried this at my friend’s place the other week, and I was shook as I continued to sniff it on my skin throughout the afternoon. It’s giving effortless beauty, old money, and quiet luxury, and I think it’ll be an absolute stunner in spring/summer heat and for cooler rainy days. Performance isn’t too bad either, especially for a Jo Malone. It’s not a huge projector, but it stays well on the skin for a good 6+ hours and carries beautifully with the wind. I’ll definitely be getting a 30 ml / 1 oz when it gets warmer out.

Super light, and airy floral scent! In my opinion it shines especially well during the spring months when the weather is still slightly cooler. In warmer weather this becomes slightly sweeter on my skin. However overall the fragrance has a very clean and fresh, almost soapy, sort of feeling! An easy reach and staple in my collection.

Yesterday, I had the luck to grab a bottle of the Turquoise at the Malone stand while passing by. It is not yet available for sale, I heard from the saleswoman, but I was allowed to test it. Since it hasn't been discussed here yet, I will give it a try. I certainly can't pick out the individual notes like many here, but I can convey my impression. I do enjoy floral scents, especially in summer, particularly when they come across as somewhat natural, which is also the reason why I liked Malone; I say liked consciously, as the last creations didn’t really excite me. Fortunately, this one is a bit different. The scent is indeed very natural, floral, I won't say: flowery, as it has a certain lightness that makes it fit well into summer. Without the familiar citrus opening, I still experience it as fresh. Honeysuckle, goat's beard smells wonderfully lush, almost a bit tropical; a plant of it grows in front of my window. In this respect, the scent seems to be truly captured here. Now, it is also said to contain Davana, no idea, so I consulted Wikipedia: pale-leaved wormwood. Well, I know kitchen wormwood, which is not exactly a fragrant herb that would fit a floral scent. But the description mentions a woody-sweet scent, also: warm mango scent, which doesn’t drastically change the goat's beard. Indeed, if you know it, you can imagine mango; there is certainly a slight fruitiness present. I actually like the opening the best, as the scent appears light and permeable without being banal. After that, it becomes greener; one would say that the stems and leaves have been added, which makes it a bit more angular. At this stage, it is also wearable by men, which I wouldn’t say for the opening. After that, the scent doesn’t change much anymore. The base is said to contain moss, but if you expect oak moss or something chypre, you are mistaken; the scent merely becomes a bit warmer. Very pleasant, slight sweetness, but not excessive. A lovely summer scent that surely won’t offend and is enjoyable to smell on a woman. However, it loses some of its naturalness over time, and it becomes flatter. In between, I thought of APOM, but that one is still higher quality, going deeper. However, it is not a twin. Longevity is not bad at all, for me over 4 hours, which is a lot for me, then only perceptible with the nose to the skin. I can only estimate the sillage, but it doesn’t overwhelm anyone as expected. Conclusion: finally, a Malone that I enjoyed, even if it won’t be joining my collection.

Hey hey and welcome to a new comment from me. Today it's about Jo Malone, a brand I have introduced several times in the past. I do like this brand, even though some of its fragrances seem quite simple to me. However, this simplicity is sometimes intentional, as the scents can be layered, but even on their own, some of these fragrances smell just great despite their simplicity. Aside from that, I always enjoyed chatting with the saleswomen in the Jo Malone section of the store (yeah… talking to saleswomen is something I can just about manage… *sigh*), unfortunately, there has only been a guy hanging around there for months now… argh :((( I always have such bad luck… at least this Jo Malone guy doesn’t try to make me sniff him like the Dior guy does, who sprays himself with the Dior Privée scents and then asks me to sniff him to see how great the fragrance would smell. Again, ARGH!!! :DD Well, Honeysuckle & Davana is one of the newer fragrances that was released last year. Regardless of my comments that the scent would smell so feminine and even a bit trivial to me, the aforementioned gentleman in the Jo Malone department was so enthusiastic about it that he kept trying to convince me how great this fragrance was… :D The Scent: I smell floral sweet notes at the beginning. Silly as I am with flowers, I still don’t know anything about the scent notes of flowers after over 1500 comments… :D That’s why I’m not quite sure which of the listed plants emits this slightly herb-spicy and distinctive scent, but I’m pretty sure it must be the Davana. Because alongside it, a sweet-floral note appears, whose sweetness reminds me of honey, and this must be the honeysuckle, as I just read that honeysuckle is said to smell like honey (and nectar). A few (few) hours later, it then smells continuously sweet-spicy until the honey-sweet scent in the base gradually disappears and the fragrance seems a bit drier. In the later base, it smells more herbaceous, with hints of earthy patchouli. I think that’s when it’s time to reapply the fragrance, as it comes across as a bit trivial to me personally. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is rather weak and therefore only really detectable from close up. The longevity is six to eight hours, after which you only smell a faint breeze of dry-earthy scent notes. The Bottle: The bottle is high-quality as always. It is rectangular with thicker glass and a large white label with a white frame, displaying the name and logo. The cap is oval-round and chrome-plated. All in all, quite nice. So, I referred to this scent as trivial during the scent description, but that doesn’t mean it smells bad. I also don’t mean that it smells generic, as it doesn’t smell like every other fragrance and has its distinctive points. It does smell quite nice, but it is also kept rather simple. Nevertheless, I think it should appeal to most ladies, as you sweet-toothed ones are known to be crazy about honey, and the fragrance radiates a light, beautifully honeyed sweetness without being overwhelming or too heavy-spicy. I like it too, but it hasn’t knocked me off my feet like some other fragrances from this brand. But maybe it can be nicely combined with other scents! And perhaps you will like it much better than I do. If you don’t want to layer the fragrance, then it is, considered on its own, a light scent that would be great for spring and summer, serving as a nice and good everyday fragrance. Therefore, I do recommend trying the scent, especially now that the days are slowly getting warmer again. So, that’s it for now. Let’s see what else Jo Malone will release soon, but I’ll probably have to chat with that guy again instead of a sweet saleswoman… *sigh* :DD I wish you a lovely evening, until next time! :)

My first Jo Malone. Sweet, flowery, powdery, inducer of good mood, white flowers, playful, awesome projection and durability. I would recommend to buy the small bottle because one only needs a little quantity for each use. I wear it pretty much all seasons, except the very hot days(it can become cloying). In winter it brings the long desired warmth when applied.

Superficially, the Mr. Burberry line was created in response to the current waning trend of marketing mass-appealing quasi-aquatic, quasi-spicy, quasi-fruity citrus woodies to fill the versatile needs of the common consumer. Despite the original Mr. Burberry being a decent, yet somewhat lackluster scent with a ‘gentlemanly’ twist, it seems as though the brand has been taking more interesting risks with each subsequent flanker. With none other than Francis Kurkdjian – mr. crystalline lemonmint himself at the helm, I found myself rather taken with the spice-heavy Mr. Burberry edp and seriously considered picking up a bottle, despite its lukewarm reception by the online community. It’s a fairly simple scent to be sure, but well executed for a designer freshie, and with very decent performance. So it was no surprise that I was interested in sampling Indigo when it finally came out. Unfortunately, nothing would prepare me for the herbal BLAST that met my nose the first time I smelled Mr. Burberry Indigo on paper. Blue? Indigo? Nah. The stuff wasn’t even green. Instead, it was so vegetal that it reminded me of grappling with my older brother in our backyard as kid and having my face rubbed into a clump of weeds. Nuthin’ but green plantstuffs RIGHT up my nose. Unbelievably brave for a designer to release something like that in 2018 and still manage a spike in sales. Needless to say, I was turned off - perhaps for good. But then, after having my eyes burned out watching droves and droves of cheap, sweet, woody ambers flood the market, my nose just couldn’t deal with the lollipop guild anymore. I needed something to balance the influx of saccharine – something more down to earth, green, fresh or herbal; something minty, something… And then I recalled that time I smelled Indigo and wouldn’t you know it, within a week I had a bottle. Yeah. It’s just how I remembered it. A great big herbal blast of violet leaf, rosemary and fresh spearmint in the opening with a bit of sour lemon kicking in the background. If you’re imagining a citrus opening, get that right out of your mind because it’s anything but. Instead, it’s like tearing out garden plants with your bare hands and feasting on greenery like some vegan maniac. Strangely enough, my mind is also instantly drawn to Acqua di Gio for some reason – not a surprise since they share 6-7 notes - but you’ll see this theme coming up again and again in the review. Ten minutes in, the rosemary begins to dial it back and you can smell the sweet amber in the background playing nicely with what’s obviously a driftwood accord (ala Original Penguin’s Premium Blend or TF’s Costa Azzurra) to give Indigo a subtle, aquatic touch. But the star is still the violet leaf – similar in scent to the clary sage you’d find in Ferragamo’s Acqua Essenziale Colonia – and balanced superbly with that spearmint. Altogether, I’m also somewhat reminded of Artisan Blu/Acqua from John Varvatos, but with a far fresher and less soapy outlook on account of the mint. So yeah, not exactly the most unique fragrance out there, but still very enjoyable. As the fragrance begins to peter out at the 3rd or 4th hour, most if not all of the mint is gone and what’s left is an ADG-esque drydown with driftwood on top of a base of iso-e and evernyl. Not the best ending to a fragrance out there, but certainly better than most modern sugary blue concoctions. There were even times when I wore Indigo and got Amouage Beach Hut vibes in the first 20 minutes! Although that fragrance is far heavier on the barbershopy amber and ivy (not to mention the longevity and projection!). Total longevity was about 5 hours, but that’s on par with what you’ll get with most modern freshies. Overall, I think Mr. Burberry Indigo is a lovely release. Simultaneously, it somehow manages to capture bits and pieces of several herbal freshies from the 90s all the way up to today, and masterfully blend them with mint in the way that only FK can. As a result, it also doesn’t exactly have a single identity of its own. If you’re looking for something with more citrus, I’d go with ADG; more soapiness, go with JV’s Artisan Blu; more barbershop vibes, go with Essenziale Colonia or Beach Hut; more Mr. Burberry, stick with the original. Instead, what we get is a vegetal violet leaf and sweet mint quasi-AQUATIC, with all the shades that the colour aqua has to offer. Wonderful for both the spring and summer, and sporting a nostalgic touch that children of the 80s and 90s could uniquely appreciate. As for it being a blue or indigo fragrance…I think not. More like a breath of fresh, garden air in a time of saccharine-induced craziness. Not bad. Not bad at all.

It's a nice fragrance, This is a fresh,herbal,woody scent. Top notes : Blackcurrant, Rosemary, Lemon. Heart notes : Violet leaf, Driftwood,Spearmint. Base notes : Amber, White oakmoss,Musk. It opens up with like fresh citrusy then dry down is green woody.It smells like ocean breeze. The Spearmint note is dominant in this fragrance. Best of the Mr.Burberry line. This perfume reminds me of Acqua Di Gio Profondo. I really enjoy it , I love Mr.Burberry Indigo and I'm so glad that I have it in my collection. Longevity is very good. Highly Recommended. Bravo Monsieur KURKDJIAN ! Two Thumbs Up. Rating : 8.5 / 10

The scent is a good one. It's not super common either. The opening and initial spray gives me scope mouthwash vibes, which I don't enjoy. After a few minutes though, that tones down and the rest of the fragrance comes out to play all at the same time. The citrus shines here. Towards the dry down the oak moss, musk and wood show out more. Not powerful or overwhelming in any way. About a foot of sillage, but does leave a slight trail. If U want something a little different but still safe, grab it. It's pretty affordable through discounters.

At first when I saw the 6.8 rating on here it shocked me because this is actually a really good fragrance. But then I thought to myself, the people who purchased this were probably looking for something mass appealing and approachable, since it is a designer Burberry scent and the original Mr. Burberry and its EDP flanker were pretty standard designer perfumery. Mr. Burberry Indigo goes a pretty unique direction. The opening is very green, herbal, and vegetal. If you are expecting sweet, bubblegum perfumery, I could see where this would be surprising in a bad way. But wow I really like this. I haven’t really smelled anything like the opening. When Indigo dries down, it goes into a spicy aquatic that smells very good in the air. My one critique of this fragrance is that on the dry down, there is a bit of a synthetic note that is giving it some SLIGHT sweetness. This note smells really good in the air, but right up close, it’s a little syrupy and fake smelling for my liking. Mr. Burberry Indigo has been discontinued and it’s an absolute shame. This was a very unique entry into the line and I respect the perfumer for taking a swing and not pumping out just another boring mass appealing blue or an Invictus clone. I was lucky enough to pick up a never used 100ml from Mercari for under $70, but I’m sure this will be one that will be listed on eBay for $400 in a few years.

It is Saturday morning in a German metropolis. The more arduous part of the week is behind me, the sun greets with an intensity unusual for this region, and the prospect of a day outdoors brings a broad smile to my face. Perhaps I will stroll through the weekly market. Maybe I will take the tram and go hiking in the countryside. If my location allowed it, I would love to set off for a walk on the beach. This feeling of freedom after a job well done, this sensation of having a multitude of options and being able to consciously choose according to one’s taste and current mood, this luxury of free time - all of this is wonderfully captured by the new men’s fragrance from Burberry. Mr. Burberry Indigo radiates blue skies, freedom, fresh air, and the scent comes with a zesty-citrusy top note. Indigo reminds me, in its composition of citrus fruits (here lemon, there grapefruit) and Mediterranean spice (rosemary instead of pepper) and the masculine oakmoss nuance, of Terre d'Hermés, one of my absolute favorite fragrances. Nevertheless, Indigo develops a character of its own, with the fresh spike mint clearly noticeable in the heart note. Woody accords ensure its longevity. I hadn’t really paid much attention to Burberry’s men’s fragrances until now, even though I find the iconic fashion of the British heritage brand very appealing. I find it particularly interesting that the classic trench coat is honored in Mr. Burberry Indigo: the bow that adorns the neck of the bottle, reminiscent of distinguished English gentlemen, is made of gabardine, the same patented material as the trench coat. The folding box also seems to be inspired by the relief of the trench coat. I am very glad to have discovered Mr. Burberry Indigo. No matter how my Saturday unfolds, Indigo will be my companion today!

Why am I testing another Mr. Burberry? Good question to myself... maybe because I still appreciate Kurkdjian? Because I like to give the checked luxury brand another chance? Because I like the bottle? Or simply because sometimes you need to smell flops to appreciate the beautiful fragrances of this world even more?

Isn't it beautiful, this transparent light blue - indeed Indigo - colored bottle with the bow on it? The chic bottle immediately caught my attention, and the color suggests a certain cool freshness, so I tried the scent right away. Scent The opening is fresh, citrusy, and aquatic. I particularly notice a strong note of sour cucumber.

When I read Francis Kurkdjian as the listed perfumer, I had to rub my eyes for a moment. But even after I opened them again, it was no mistake. The perfumer behind masterful creations like "Grand Soir | Maison Francis Kurkdjian", Oud Satin Mood Extrait de Parfum , and Baccarat Rouge 540 Extrait de Parfum ...

This perfume simply doesn't last long and feels extremely uncomfortable on the skin. It smells not just like aftershave but rather like a cheap aftershave. Wannabe perfume. I am ashamed to even own this bottle.

... the fruit and vegetable stand. I can smell the scents of lemons, berries, and fresh spices here. From the stand next door, a floral scent wafts towards me with a light breeze. Now I'm hungry and I make my move. At home, I realize once again that I bought too much. Oh well, it will be processed.

As others have already mentioned, this piece is one of the Spicebomb types and features vivid and distinctive cinnamon. I'd like to add just how Gentlemen Only Absolute differs from competitors like Spicebomb, Bvlgari MIB, L'Occitane Eau des Baux, and etc. 1. Not really boozy. So there is no impression of profligate or free-spiritedness. It is not as seductive or alluring as it is. 2. Not ostentatious. Once this scent itself is not very noticeable, and its performance is also. The longevity is sufficient, but the projection can only be recognized from a really close distance. 3. There is something like a vanilla-based creamy soapy water, and there is a coldness in the middle that almost feels metallic. Maybe Spicy Nutmeg. I really like this part. However, this soapy water is slightly old school, thus adding a mature vibe to the scent. I think GOA is too mature for people under 30. 4. And because of the above three factors, GOA is maybe suitable for day-time offices. But is it really a good scent in the office? Not certain. And also it's a bit modest to wear at clubs or social gatherings. In my opinion, it can be worn anywhere, but not the best anywhere. 5. Anyway it should be said that it has much greater general purpose compared to Spicebomb. It is okay to wear it now, which is mid-April, not winter. And it's a pretty good choice for Cinnamon fans who will always want to wear this kind of scent. 6. There's a shortcoming of course. Ambiguous rather than shortcoming. A sweet element that can never be said to be few. This sweet part is not very elaborate. I read some comments comparing GOA to 1 Million, and I don't agree with that, but I can fully understand that the assessment comes out anyway. This means that the sweetness of GOA is considered an ordinary cliché. 7. GOA's sweet type is yummy vanilla which reminds us of Givenchy Pi in part, with a soft and dark smoky flavor like a baked marshmallow. And I don't know why, but I sense some coffee. It may be a good factor for dark vanilla fans, but it gives me a younger impression too much. 8. So here's my conclusion: The use of scents and the age range of the main target of it are not clear. It is well-made enough, but it is a little old fashion for young people to wear, and it is too flat a sweet taste for mature adults to wear. At night time, GOA is certainly inferior to Herod, Mancera Red Tobacco, Spicebomb or so.
