It can only be a better choice than them in the office, but there are already many other good perfumes for the office. If you already have a few bottles of perfume, maybe there's almost no reason to include it in your collection. 9. Nevertheless I bought this, because I really love the scent of Spicebomb type. Despite being really fond of it, it is often difficult to wear this type of perfume. For example, I won't be able to wear them during light tea time or confession time (although it's been so long since I've been to the church, anyway). But GOA can share more of my daily lives than them, except for funerals.

This is a Gorgeous Fragrance, Elegant, Classy, Spicy, Refined and Warm. Unfortunately, It is hard to find and discontinued. Givenchy Gentleman Only Absolute along with Spicebomb and Bvlgari Man In Black are Suitable for the Cold Weather. All of them have a unique spicy Composition and Well-blended. It opens up with slightly sweet fresh spicy and spices notes in the background then dry down is creamy vanilla woody. This scent has High Quality in the dry down. The Cinnamon and The Vanilla notes are dominant in this perfume. I Really enjoy it and I'm so happy that I have it in my collection . Longevity is good. I have some availability,hit me up if interested.

Rating : 8.5 / 10

Soon my best friend has a birthday and I'm once again diving into men's fragrances to find a gift for him. My anxious question about whether my obligatory scent gifts would become boring was vehemently denied by my men, as none of them like to hang around in perfume shops - they prefer to leave that to me. Apparently, they all suffer from acute "time shortage" - but they do enjoy wearing fragrances. So be it. I already delighted Mr. Forester with Gentlemen Only for Christmas, and now I tried Absolute. This fragrance also carries the Givenchy signature, but it follows its own path. Woody, spicy, and oriental is how it is announced on the cover - for the "absolute" gentleman. I gladly endorse the adjectives, but the scent doesn't necessarily need a pinstripe suit to make an impact. It will also suit my biking forest man, who loves to wear his leather gear. Of course, he is an "absolute" gentleman in his attitude. Absolute is soft and deep, and very approachable. The fresh bergamot harmoniously pairs with the spicy nutmeg and the sweet cinnamon, emphasized by elegant saffron. The vanilla is soft again, and sandalwood wraps around it in a creamy way. A fragrance that signals closeness - and allows it as well. Just right for my rugged "cuddle bear". The oriental hints would fit better in winter - but the birthday falls in summer. Although it is another Gentlemen Only, Absolute will not bore the birthday boy, as it is more the cuddly version of the already existing Only. And even rugged men like to cuddle.

Leather jacket "young Romans" (by Falco and off we go. A masculine scent that even women in their 20s really like. A fragrance that shows women who the man is, but at the same time has a very pleasant and attractive effect on women. But folks, this scent is not for the insecure. This scent is pure arrogance.

This is quite something. Is this a Mediterranean-salty water with spices or a dusty gourmand in a nutmeg dress? I dared to grab this wonderful bottle and wear it for a day in summer. Mistake! It is not suitable for warm days. More for evenings in autumn. The aversion in the office was greater than I thought. The truth is simply that the scent is made for bold men.

Due to the positive reviews of Gentlemen Only Absolute and my search for a sweet fragrance for the cold season, I had a nice Parfumo send me a sample blindly - thanks again at this point to YuzuFan :) During my first test, I was already enchanted by this spicy-light woody sweetness.

With the Absolute here, this year has already seen the second new Gentlemen Only fragrance from Givenchy. The other was Parisian Break, which was tailored for summer and didn't really exude the typically known Gentlemen Only DNA, and while it was quite nice scent-wise, unfortunately, nothing more.

In search of a fragrance for the cold season, it is almost impossible not to notice this bottle, which stands out particularly with its red accents. It doesn’t always have to be a hand grenade, which everyone here in the forum knows how to appreciate, and it doesn’t always need to have an extravagant bottle shape that focuses more on appearance than substance.
Very nice autumn or winter scent that is well balanced; it smells fresh with bergamot and slightly spicy with a hint of vanilla, while the saffron prevents it from becoming too powdery.

I picked this up before I got into fragrances, and I didn't understand it was a limited edition. I used it every day and loved this to the last drop. Imagine my surprise when I went to repurchase! I've been chasing this scent high since that day, with no luck. I wish they'd do a throwback bring-back of this scent because it was amazing. Creamy, sweet but with a pang of freshness and nature. The only good thing is that it did introduce me to Mathilde Bijaoui as a perfumer, and surprise-surprise when I find new perfumes I love, she's behind them.

My husband insists that one never really gets rid of their "stable scent." He means this in a social sense - and he may be right. My mother put it more bluntly: You can't turn a chamber pot into a soup pot. I enjoy carrying the stable scent with me in two ways. On one hand, the aforementioned imprint, and on the other hand, the familiar scent of the horse stable that always accompanied me. That soothing scent, when my husband started the clattering oat mill, was a delight for me. The stables were permeated with the scent of oats, rounded off by the note of hay. And the horses stretched their necks in anticipation of their meal. And then afterwards their satisfied munching. I also loved wandering through our oat fields, where the blue blossoms of cornflowers stood out. The good soil exuded earthiness - and in the air lingered the nutty scent of hazel bushes. A piece of home. Oat & Cornflower is a natural, nature-connected fragrance that not only reminds one of the English fields but also of the fields and meadows in the beautiful Sauerland. Why wander far away - see, the good lies so close.

The underlying principle of Jo Malone's English Fields series is actually quite clearly anchored in its name: English fields. So, a green or at least botanical theme: each featuring a flower and mostly - in four out of five cases: wheat, barley, rye, and here indeed oats - a type of grain. This heralds summery scents - like a cheerful country outing through English hill landscapes with a well-filled picnic basket. Green Wheat & Meadowsweet, the first (and most beautiful) of the five limited edition scents I have commented on, still fulfills this expectation: a quietly cheerful summer fragrance full of wonderfully fresh June greens - uncomplicated, effortless. Honey & Crocus, which I described a few days ago, already diverges - as a scent of warm, buttered honey rolls, while still allowing its botanical name part - the crocus - to be recognized. With Oat & Cornflower, there is hardly anything to be found of its floral component - the cornflower. Instead, there is much more of its (processed) grainy aspect. Oat & Cornflower is the scent of breakfast flakes, leaning more towards Frosties or Smacks in terms of sweetness than Toppas. It also reminds one of oatmeal cookies - the American version, the size of beer coasters and still soft on the inside. Or of warm cake. Butter cookies. Its medium strength is quite suitable for summer. Conclusion: this cookie note is a bit one-dimensional. Where, for example, Serge Lutens' Jeux de Peau, which many also call a cookie scent, adds a noticeably organic, almost animalistic component that makes it interesting and experienceable beyond the grainy sweetness, Oat & Cornflower exclusively focuses on cereals (which sometimes have more calories than chocolate). For lovers of gourmands, it is a feast for the senses. But there is hardly a trace of English fields.

And here we go again with the new Jo Malone fragrances. The English Fields scents are fragrances that include, among other things, grain notes. But don't worry, anyone thinking that you might smell like bread with these is mistaken :D Although the grain notes in the fragrances are certainly noticeable (even if not particularly strong), they do not smell like bread or porridge or anything else you typically make from grains (... yes,... beer is also made from various grains, you thought of that immediately, didn't you?... :D). The fragrances are, of course, more perfumey, but the grain gives them a special, unusual note. I find that all five of the fragrances are quite lovely and should at least be checked out once. Now comes Oat & Cornflower, one of the slightly heavier and creamier scents from this line. The Scent: I don't know how cornflowers smell, but the scent starts off quite creamy, sweet, and floral for me. Then it becomes a bit nutty; I find the hazelnut is quite noticeable and reminds me, especially together with the sweet, creamy notes, of chocolate spreads like Nutella, well, at least a little. The creaminess remains, and you can perceive a bit of oat, although not very strongly, and the scent generally smells good, but also a bit heavy, at least for a summer fragrance; it might come off as a bit intense for some. In the base, the scent remains creamy and sweet with what I perceive as indeterminate floral notes. You can still smell the hazelnuts for a while before they fade away. I'm a bit unsure about the vetiver; it seems to be very weak, although some could detect this note better than I could, which means that vetiver is likely quite noticeable. And as Zitrönchen mentioned in her comment, there’s also a feeling that a light coconut note might appear. I think Oat & Cornflower is a successful scent as well. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is really good; you leave a nice, larger scent cloud and are therefore quite noticeable. The longevity is even extremely good. Sprayed on just before evening, around 5 PM, I could still smell the scent well on my skin the next morning after lunch. The Bottle: The rectangular bottle is slender and tall. It has a pale blue pastel look and looks nice. A special feature is the lower third of the bottle, which is rocky. Or rather, it has a rocky, grainy "wallpaper" that looks good and feels nice. A very beautiful bottle. Yes, I also really liked this scent from the English Fields line, but unfortunately, I find it a bit too feminine for me to wear as a man. Most of the scents in this line (unfortunately) come off as a bit too feminine, but for you ladies, they represent successful fragrances that you should check out. Oat & Cornflower has turned out creamy and sweet, smelling of oat and hazelnut, and initially, especially because of the hazelnut, it even seems a bit like a nutty-chocolate spread, so it really smells delicious, even if it comes off a bit heavier than the other fragrances. Of course, I would advise against using it as a Nutella substitute, even if your Nutella is all gone and you really want to snack on such a spread. Because no matter how delicious a scent smells, it never tastes like it smells, um... I'm not speaking from experience here... :D But you probably know that; on the other hand, I also know that you are all crazy addicts, capable of anything, so you never know,... :DD The scent is wearable in spring, but you might want to be careful not to over-apply, as it can come off as heavier, especially since it lasts quite a long time. By the way, this makes it very suitable for going out. So, as I said, check out this scent when you have the chance; maybe you'll like it too!

First of all, I like them all, the new and limited Jo Malones from the English Fields collection, but this one unfortunately comes in last for me. This may be mainly because it is incredibly intense for a Jo Malone fragrance. The Bottle Typical for Jo Malone fragrances in a limited edition, all English Fields scents come in the classic Jo Malone design with a twist. This time, the glass of the bottle is painted in pastel colors and glazed in a structured and contrasting color in the lower third. This creates a texture reminiscent of stone and porcelain, as if Jo Malone had teamed up with Villeroy & Boch. It is elegant and chic and fits wonderfully in the hand. The cap is made of plastic this time and is in the same color as the upper two-thirds of the bottle. The caps fit a bit tighter than usual, so the fragrance usually opens with a satisfying "pop" sound. As beautiful as the bottles are, they do have a drawback and an advantage at the same time. On one hand, the fragrance is somewhat protected from light, but even when held against a light source, the fill level can only be guessed. Furthermore, the transition of colors is not cleanly executed on all bottles, and some have a slight color shadow in the transition. Those who care about this should take a close look at the bottles before purchasing. The Fragrance Wow, this is a strong little potion for an EdC. At first, a rather heavy and floral note hits you with a slightly powdery undertone. This is apparently the cornflower, though I don’t remember its scent being so heavy and overwhelming. It’s almost as if you’ve just picked a large bouquet of flowers and are now burying your nose right in, and then the fragrance takes its time. It takes a relatively long time for the development to begin, as if you’ve leisurely set off on your walk home with the bouquet. Once there, freshly baked cookies are cooling on a plate and filling the house with their scent. Because after some time has passed, oats and hazelnut finally emerge, providing a creamy cookie scent. Nevertheless, the cornflower remains very present for a long time, vying for attention. The vetiver is only subtly noticeable, as if it doesn’t want to be noticed, but this also keeps the fragrance from going completely off the rails and becoming too sweet. In the end, a creamy, slightly sweet scent emerges, as if coconut or vanilla were included. Even after 8 hours, I can still clearly perceive the fragrance on myself. Conclusion This fragrance is something for cooler spring days when you long for the blooming of flowers, or for autumn when you’re not quite ready to let go of summer. It is surprisingly intense and long-lasting, and one should already enjoy heavier fragrances, as it clearly leans towards the gourmand direction. Those who like light scents like Wild Bluebell are in the wrong place here. However, those looking for a spring-like and lighter alternative to Black Opium with a cookie note that you don’t smell on every corner might find joy in this fragrance.

... beautiful! I am happy and sad at the same time, because with Oat & Cornflower I have found my new great love and my signature scent. It could be so wonderful if the fragrance weren't a limited edition from 2018. Now, let's talk about the scent: Cornflower or anything floral is not really perceivable here.

Burberry Sport goes on with a realistic fresh grapefruit scent mingled with orange; it has the zing of grapefruit and the heart of orange. Within ten minutes, spices come out to support it, and it smells great! The spices are well-blended with the grapefruit, so much so that you'd think that a spice-laden grapefruit had fallen off some tree, instead of two separate notes meeting for business somewhere. With a little sweat and time applied, it smells a bit astringent, more spicy-animalic. It loses its medium projection after about an hour or so, and by 4-5 hours, it is a skin scent. At times, Burberry Sport reminds me of a more mature John Varvitos; fortunately, it has conquered JV's horrific short-gevity. After 5 hours, it comes up around me now and again in an ethereal wafting way, much like Burberry for Men. Odd. As a skin scent, it's a spicy-grapefruit-animalic-aromatic deal with the grapefruit predominant. The animalic vibe is genuine; at the end of the day, one of my cats is licking my wrists right where this scent was applied. It lasts at least eight hours. I've not followed the sports fragrance market, so I can't speak with any authority on what they are supposed to do or not do; my general impression is that they are supposed to smell fresh and clean, and cover up light workouts. In this, Burberry Sport does a good job, although I'm hesitant to call it a pure sports fragrance, due to its interesting evolution. I would say it's a sporty fragrance, but it's not stereotypical or ordinary. The overall effect it has is one of energy, youthfulness, "in" without being snobby, a little daring, and masculine without being overbearing. Finally, the bottle -- although it's plastic, it's one of the most visually appealing and engaging bottles I own. It invites you to open it and hold it. All around, Burberry Sport is a class act.

I'm not too convinced that Burberry Sport for Men is indeed a sports fragrance. It's not as fresh as I thought it would be. In fact, this fragrance could be worn in Winter. Burberry Sport for Men is mostly fizzy and citrusy ginger. Grapefruit seems to be the most dominant accord in this scent pyramid, which smells fairly strong to my nose, especially in the opening. It has a very aquatic feel to it, mostly brought about by the rather synthetic sea water accord and the cedar, which resembles the scent of pencil-shavings. Luckily the ginger in this fragrance is pleasant and balanced. The ginger is slightly refreshing like ginger ale, and has a rather spicy edge. I can't seem to detect the wheat note. It doesn't register to my nose. Unfortunately I find this fragrance quite generic and boring. It's not something I'd particularly want to smell on a man in the gym. It leaves me feeling disappointed and uninspired. I do however like the bottle design. I find the black rubber outer-casing very handy and aesthetically pleasing to the eye. The lasting strength is relatively good, as is the sillage, which may perhaps be in certain situations, a little too strong and in-your-face. All in all, Burberry Sport for Men is passable in my books, but definitely not an exciting new release.

Well, I have my issues with the brand Burberry. So far, nothing from them has really appealed to me. My Burberry London - why on earth did I buy that - is languishing in the back row. And now, of all things, the new trendy sport fragrance is supposed to change that? To get straight to the point: This is something very simple, nothing grand. Very mainstream and right in line with other current sport fragrances. As such, this perfume primarily features a light, lemony top note that, in my impression, is enhanced with aldehydes. It’s not too strong, but rather quite watery. However, it is long-lasting. After all, it plays the main role - typical for its kind. It probably doesn’t have much to do with real lemon/bergamot. But it is pleasantly understated, fresh but not too sour. Thus, it likely appeals to (almost) everyone. In this style, I find it directly comparable to Cartier's Roadster Sport and perhaps also to the new sport fragrance from Gucci. But - then something else comes along! Namely, an elegant musk-moss?-cedarwood base. Very masculine, surprisingly old school, and stimulatingly physical. This contrast between synthetic freshness and animalistic physicality is probably why I lingered on it a bit. Not that I would buy it now. I own other, better perfumes. But it’s just OK. You can’t go wrong with it. Thus, it makes a great gift, as this scent pleases everyone. The respectable fragrance pyramid would certainly be ignored; I didn’t find much of that again. All in all, I am positively surprised; because in this category, there are worse options.

This is what a sport fragrance smells like to me. I'm not really a fan of sport scents, but today the Turquoise ones had this fragrance on offer. Sprayed it in the store, and it actually smelled quite good. So, I just took it with me because it was €10 cheaper than usual. Then I also ordered the ICE from Burberry, just received 3 calls from the nice ladies saying there are problems with the order, but now they managed to get something at the branch in Münster, and as compensation, I get a €5 discount, very kind of the ladies. :) So, back to the "Sport"..., um, excuse me, "Sport". I just sprayed it on and I'm trying to describe what I can smell. It definitely smells quite good. I perceive something fresh and pleasant. Citrusy or bergamot-like somehow. Nice and light, not a heavy hitter scent that has made its way into my collection. However, this fragrance seems familiar to me. I've been thinking the whole time about what it reminds me of. It’s probably some Adidas shower gel, right?? I don't know. If so, why would I buy something like that when Adidas shower gels seem too cheap to me? :D:D No, we don't want to bash the 3 stripes, to each their own. :) But, it doesn't really matter. Burberry Sport will probably, as our Apicius already wrote, please everyone. If someone has a birthday again, I'll buy them Burberry Sport for Men and they will be happy. Longevity is okay, I've had it on for about 3-4 hours now, it's still there and smells very nice. So, a good middle ground. That's it from Sport... :D

So, now Burberry has also managed to attach a rather dull plastic block and, as a bonus, a cheap rubber wristband with the unwelcome word "Sport." Considering that we are not exactly dealing with a niche representative of the high-price segment, one can certainly overlook the name; after all, "Weekend" or "Summer" have also been used up by Burberry. The first thing that surprises in connection with sporty freshness is the color red. One suspects already that the indicated marine notes do not play the main role here. A sigh of relief goes through the ranks of the Boss and Klein-wallet holders. Ah yes, red ginger and juniper berries! Not only does it sound good, but it also smells like it and brings a refreshingly fruity contrast to the well-known, slightly stale Burberry house note (yes, the corporate identity guidelines have once again been implemented exemplary here), reminiscent of Kenzo's Indigo playfulness with a dandyish laissez-faire. I sniff berries like blackberries, blueberries, and other berries that aren’t even present and see Grandma standing by the canning kettle with a blue-red smeared apron. So far, it makes a good impression, but I often have sympathies for Burberry anyway. You see, I have to bridge the time as the base note takes a while to show up. Extension after the first half, something new. The ginger/juniper duo holds up bravely, and the ominous marine note must be some high-tech gimmick because the persistently cool base mood at this late stage is quite surprising. With Cool Water and others, it worked with mint or menthol, but Burberry Sport has nothing green about it. Now it gets paradoxical, cool but still slightly cozy? As I read elsewhere, real experts don’t fumble around as clumsily as I do and speak of "spicy-ozonic." Thank you! Well, amber, musk, and cedar still seem to be stuck in traffic somewhere... a glance at the clock... the scent lasts, who would have thought? In summary, a welcome change in the locker room, less "Brit"-ish and more summery than The Beat. Burberry Sport cleverly avoids flat clichés and feels very modern without annoying with its certainly present but well-integrated synthetics. Well Wolfgang, here we have a bit of the free spirit you were looking for.

How does one envision the bottle of a sport fragrance? Fresh, clear shapes and colors, preferably in white or blue, round, pleasingly soft forms. Well, all of that is not what Burberry Sport is. Borrowing red and black from the classic beige-white-red-black Burberry check, it adopts the rectangular shapes of the typical Burberry pattern.

Whether Men, London, Brit, or Touch - the men's fragrances from the British luxury house have something for every taste without any real failures. I like London the most, especially during the autumn holidays. Only Sport, which I believe is becoming rare on the market, I had never had in front of my nose.

are supposed to give a hint of "left lane" to some small cars..... It looks the same with the bottle. On the shelf, it appears interesting. But when the plastic is in hand, you already feel the first disappointment. So now I turn to the scent. Having just tested Gucci Sport, I have hope that sport fragrances can indeed be something great. The first breath.

......wears the same, whether at work, in his leisure time with his beloved lawn sport involving several clubs and a small, usually white, "dimpled" ball. And he wears "Burberry Sport for Men" extremely sparingly (which he is not when it comes to strokes in golf).

So. I am starting again. Almost a year ago I finished a 365 days’ review streak; meaning me writing a review every day for a year. I succeeded and it taught me a lot; about my nose; about ingredients; even about quality, I suppose. I loved it - even when it was difficult, it was never so tough that it kept me from doing it again. Right now my collection consists of around 600 different fragrances. I have decided to reduce it to around half - maybe even less. I have even made a shelf named ‘Have to go’ and as I write, 290 of my beauties are now placed there with the purpose of selling in the near future - hopefully! They all deserve a new, loving home. I have read loads of reviews and looked into the ratings here on Parfumo. I have weighed every pro and con of all fragrances, looked at the bottles (I am a bottle-o-maniac), smelled and tested and then made my decision. The fragrance that starts this 365days race is carefully chosen. It is one of my newer fragrances, bought on a recent trip to Gran Canaria. I went to a perfume shop at a mall because I was looking for L’Interdit Rouge but ended up trying Rouge Ultime instead and… fell in love… This is NOT the “airport duty free shop kinda-love”. This is a love that will last for a long time. This perfume is carefully chosen for my collection. If you have not tried it yet, be ready for a blast - that is if you like sweet/floral fragrances. This one has everything you need. There is, to my nose, an almost minty note in the beginning; a freshness that took me by surprise the first time. And the second. And third… and then it starts blooming; a magical mix of jasmine and neroli. So seductive. So sweet. So intriguing. I was stunned the first time. It has a depth that is in a league of its own. And it just keeps going. The feeling I get with this fragrance is truly red. As red as the bottle which is so chubby it makes me smile every time I hold it - I love chubby bottles! I imagine a pair of lips with the most gorgeous red lipstick; glossy and perfect. If the colour of the bottle is a code for the juice I cannot wait to try L’Interdit Rouge, since it has a darker cherry shade. I suppose I will have to add a bottle of that to my collection as well. But here goes L’Interdit Rouge Ultime into my collection for good. So gorgeous… so red… so beautiful! Year 2, 1/365

Bubblegummy white floral in the initial spray, very much like the OG but perhaps with slightly more prominent orange blossom. Hints of cola as it settles, and just a touch of cocoa. Such a warm, dry scent, perfect for autumn or a chillier day in late summer. Probably the sweetest of the flankers. I wanted to like this, but ultimately found it too dry and sour-leaning for my tastes. Fortunately the original still has my heart.

God I want this so BAD. I test it literally every time it’s on display and it hangs around until I shower and wash my clothes. It’s sweeter and more creamy than the rouge & black bottle flankers but deeper and sexier than the OG or flankers in the clear bottles. Truly a masterpiece, so yummy. Peak dark feminine vibes

I don't hate this one, but I also am still on the fence with this one. It is super sweet initially. Today I mixed it with Azraq and I am testing that out. It is too sweet for full on summer, but it is perfect for fall. I am going to try to find the perfect thing to blend this with, to make the perfect concotion to take some of the sweetness away. I am in love with the Rouge and the Tuberose versions...

I recently reviewed the original "L'Interdit (Eau de Parfum Rouge) | Givenchy." Here follows a review of the flanker Rouge Ultime. According to Parfumo, this fragrance is a limited edition. Quite possible, as most (small) flankers tend to disappear over time. Sometimes quite quickly, especially with less popular ones. This one should be tested by women before it vanishes again. For me, this Rouge Ultime is the most beautiful in this line. I like all of them extremely well, but this one is one of the most beautiful women's fragrances I have ever tested. This is a scent that is very seductive and will likely appeal to men as well. In my eyes, it's a perfect evening fragrance that can impress women and make them feel good. The L'Interdit line is simply superb. The hallmark of this line is, of course, this wonderful tuberose note, which is even more dominant in the other fragrances of this line. Here in this Rouge Ultime, you get a wonderfully balanced mix of flowers, sweet notes, and a touch of pleasant mild spice. The tuberose has been somewhat toned down here, settling into a mix of jasmine, orange blossom, and a bit of neroli. The tuberose is still in the foreground of this floral mix, but as mentioned, it is perfectly balanced and soft. Alongside the tuberose, the cocoa shell is the star of this creation. A soft sweet cocoa note with gentle mild spice. It is followed by beautiful dark patchouli, which, in my opinion, perfectly rounds off this dark and mysterious vibe. A fragrance that captivates me and somehow draws me in. Also, this gentle woody note that becomes stronger towards the base is simply buttery soft and pleasant. Overall, for me, a fragrance with a lot of sex appeal. Performance is top-notch like all in this line. Tuberose fragrances are generally very dominant, and here it just fits. Not too overpowering, but clearly perceptible from a minimum of 8 hours of longevity. Perfect for evening activities, especially with slightly more elegant outfits. It is also not unbearable in everyday casual outfits. However, it shines much better in the evening. For me, one of my absolute favorite women's fragrances. It's a shame that this is only a limited edition. The original Rouge is, however, similarly good and also worth purchasing.

While L'Interdit Eau de Parfum Rouge comes with zesty blood orange and spicy pimento, making a sexy hip sway, L'Interdit Eau de Parfum Rouge Ultime becomes more powdery and cozy due to the cocoa, which makes it a wonderful going-out scent for autumn and winter.

This fragrance is the reason I ended up here at Parfumo. It suddenly triggered a desire to smell, sniff, and try more and more. But it all started with a mix-up... A few weeks ago, a perfume influencer suddenly popped up on my TikTok FYP, claiming that L'Interdit Rouge is THE women's perfume, irresistible, attractive, and so on.

Why is there now the variant No. 125 of a once beautiful fragrance (exaggerated, I hope the reader will forgive me)? Somehow, it has become a trend in recent years to produce always new offshoots. But are they different or better? You can decide for yourselves….. I am a bit disappointed. Not really surprisingly different.

My interest in perfume slumbered long and deep within me like Smaug in Erebor. One day, as I was lost in thought on my way home, a woman walked past me, closely followed by a large and heavy cloud of vanilla. But neither the woman nor the scent itself awakened the dragon; it was rather the thought - no: the longing to be a cloud.

With the regular Rouge, I find it a bit bothersome that the patchouli smells too extreme, making it hard to perceive other components. Here, you can smell patchouli, but finally, the other heart notes also come to the fore. The bottles look simply stunning and elegant.

Snowdrops...how do they smell, and do they smell at all? Snowdrops do not smell (at least I tried but couldn't feel anything), and I guess Jo Malone suggests her own imaginative perception how it would smell, and I agree with her. I don't want to break this smell in notes, I am taking it as a whole. It is beautiful and feminine, I see it wearing only in a fresh weather, and it is office safe. Bottle design suits it perfectly. You smell what you see. This bottle is my blind buying, and I don't regret at all, it is a diamond in my collection.

So, today I’m coming to a new Jo Malone fragrance from this year. This one is limited edition and will probably be gone soon, as is often the case with most limited fragrances from Jo Malone. It’s always a bit of a gamble… if the scent is popular, it’s gone in no time. If it gets less attention, you might still find it after a few months. I’m curious to see how long this fragrance will stay on the market. In any case, I always enjoy trying new scents from this brand. Over the years, I’ve found myself increasingly drawn to Jo Malone and especially find their limited fragrances interesting and wonderful. So… the last new fragrance from this brand, Honeysuckle & Davana (which, by the way, is not limited), really disappointed me. Well, it wasn’t a bad-smelling fragrance… but somehow terribly boring, just an everyday scent without any special features that you could practically forget right after spraying it. Well… now comes White Moss & Snowdrop. Let’s see how it smells. Hmm… Snowdrop means snowdrop, and snowdrop sounds almost like snowflake... Ah, Christmas is coming soon :D And don’t worry, even if I might be a bit cheeky (or perverse :D) here sometimes, I won’t ruin the song “Schneeflöckchen, Weißröckchen…” like Charlie Harper from the series “Two and a Half Men” by singing it like he does: “Schneeflöckchen, hoch das Röckchen!...” :DDD He he, now let’s get to the scent, and let’s all hope that we’ll at least see a few snowflakes this year,… hopefully for Christmas… *sigh* The Scent: The scent starts with moss, which seems a bit like oak moss to me, and therefore smells that way. Then it becomes a bit spicier on my skin (on paper, the moss seems stronger and lasts longer), while the moss slightly softens, and then I smell the wonderful citrus notes. The citrus fruits, namely clementine and petitgrain (for simplicity, I’ll just refer to them as oranges from now on, since you can’t really distinguish between clementine and petitgrain and the scent smells more like oranges anyway) don’t smell citrusy-fresh and sparkling here, but simply warm and beautifully reminiscent of the delightful Orange Bitters (also from Jo Malone, also limited,… unfortunately!) but are much lighter and less intense. Snowdrops provide a light, floral, and slightly sweet note, they smell nice but are a bit weak. The later sweetness of the fragrance mainly comes from the amber. Towards the base, the scent remains as described, but the fragrance notes become weaker and weaker. Only the moss seems a little stronger than the other notes and occasionally stands out. I can only smell the tonka bean very faintly, and only when I sniff very closely at the sprayed area. However, you can tell that the tonka bean makes the scent softer and slightly powdery. A nice fragrance, nothing new, but once again something rather unusual from Jo Malone, in my opinion anyway. The Sillage and Longevity: Hmm, since the scent can actually be well used in autumn and winter, the sillage could have been stronger. You have to get closer to smell it on someone. A bit of a shame, but still okay. The longevity is slightly longer than eight hours, but from about five hours on, it becomes rapidly weaker. At least that was the case for me. The Bottle: At first glance, the bottle looks like all the other Jo Malone bottles, even though the fragrance is limited (because limited bottles always have a different color or special design). Upon closer inspection, however, you notice that the bottle has a shiny surface that refracts light in all rainbow colors, which is very beautiful and you constantly catch yourself playing with the bottle under the light to see the wonderful, colorful reflections :) The knob-like cap is also gold-plated instead of chrome. And the label is lighter, as the frame and the writing are also slightly gilded. A beautiful bottle. Like almost all limited bottles from Jo Malone. So,… yes, the fragrance is not bad. I don’t necessarily need this one, but it smells good and is much better than the last Jo Malone fragrance, Honeysuckle & Davana, which, as I mentioned at the beginning, somehow smelled so trivial and totally boring, in my opinion anyway, and was more of a scent that would only be somewhat nice when layered with other Malones. By the way, I haven’t commented on that fragrance yet, well, maybe I’ll do that sometime. But back to this fragrance here. As I said, it’s not bad. It’s nothing excitingly new, but rather quite unusual for a Jo Malone fragrance, as I haven’t had a scent that reminds me of classic, more mature fragrances with its oak moss note from this label in quite a while. Additionally, I really like the warm-citrusy orange-neroli note here. It reminded me a bit of Orange Bitters, which is even more beautiful than this fragrance and would be highly recommendable. Orange Bitters is also limited, but as far as I know, it’s back in stores for the Christmas season. The fragrance is definitely unisex. Although, it actually fluctuates during the scent development :D Because when sprayed, it almost seems like a classic men’s fragrance to me. Over time, it becomes softer and slightly more floral and then appears more feminine. In the end, I smell more moss again, making it a bit more masculine again. I think both genders could appreciate this fragrance. Perhaps it could be layered especially with Orange Bitters? That would be worth a test. And this fragrance here would also be worth a test, it might appeal to some :) So… that’s it. Have a lovely evening everyone and don’t forget: Hope for a white Christmas. Of course, everyone who doesn’t want to scrape ice or anything will surely hope against it… *sigh* :DD

Snowdrop in a white dress cool freshness spreads wide. Moss man gently covers her Tonka & Amber bring warmth to it. … What a special scent! Snowdrops? What do they smell like? Like this? Really? I don’t believe it! Now, let’s take it slow… First of all, my sample only said “White Moss”… after some research (with Mantus, from whom I got it) we thought it was Private Collection Jasmine White Moss Eau de Parfum , but it wasn’t!!! Then we continued researching (mostly Manti, thanks again for that!) It turned out it could be White Moss & Snowdrop . So I ordered a sample and Tadaaaa … It is it! Now, about the scent… I am particularly taken with the top note. Citrusy-fresh with a dreamily beautiful hint of aromatic (from the moss), White Moss begins. Clear bright Neroli and Petitgrain, which you can smell well. And then the snowdrops sneak in (which I would never have recognized as such, but who really knows how they smell?!). Honestly, I am enchanted. The flowers are lovely and soft, almost even slightly creamy. Combined with the top note, it results in a floral-soft, somewhat herbal, slightly sweet, citrusy-fresh, lightly cooling, aromatic scent. In the base, however, a slightly warm note sneaks in (Tonka & Amber) that connects with the herbal moss nuance and brings a gentle conclusion to the scent. But it retains its cool aura. I don’t exactly know why this scent immediately captivated me. But even when I took the cap off the bottle and held my nose to the sprayer, I was smitten. I hadn’t even sprayed it yet. But Mantus already said he knew I would love this scent. :-) White Moss is a fragrance for every day and every occasion. Chic and caressing. A bit cool in its aura. But very pleasant in warmth. Now I just have to wait until snowdrops bloom again to check if they smell as beautiful as this scent!

Never thought that was possible: oriental and yet fresh. An atypical yet special Malone. Longevity for me is about 8 hours, it lasts longer on me than the other Malones. One shouldn't expect something like Wood Sage & Sea Salt or White Jasmine & Mint, of course. ;-)

Jo Malone is often too "ordinary" for me! But this one has made it into my collection. I love this feeling of freshness, pure and cozy! The scent is dominated by snowdrops and moss. I perceive it as freshly bathed, enveloped in a cloud. It really lasts a very, very long time, and I prefer to wear it in winter.

I’ve just received a small sample, and to be perfectly honest, my expectations were low. I never quite understood the hype surrounding the original fragrance, which to me has always felt rather plain and overly sweet. And yet… this flanker managed to surprise me in the best way. The vanilla here is sumptuous - creamy, rounded - with an almost liqueurous elegance that instantly brought to mind the texture of Baileys (and I stress the texture, not the scent). Raspberry weaves through it vividly, giving shape to a pairing that feels both harmonious and genuinely pleasing. In the drydown, a subtle suede undertone emerges, though what lingers most is still that enveloping vanilla entwined with raspberry. To my nose, this stands as the most captivating interpretation of Goddess to date. Well worth experiencing with an open mind.

At first this just seems like a much sweeter version of the OG. Just way more vanilla & fruity vibes than anything else. I liked it! And then I carried on walking around the shop, letting it dry down, and I noticed it started smelling like nail polish or nail polish remover? Not like acetone but the fragrance they put in it. Or maybe it’s hairspray, I don’t know. There’s just something in the dry down that reminds me of other generic cosmetic fragrance and it really surprised me

Pure sophistication. It opens strong with the leather, hints of vanilla, but dries down to more of a lavender than anything else.. After two hours, the leather-scent comes back. I actually really like this one, and it suits me. The original smells amazing, but unfortunately it was not good on my skin, so I was left with the impression that I don't like it. Today I got a sample of this new goddess parfum, and I was skeptic, but curious still. Both me and my husband thought it smelled really great and now I'm thinking to buy a 30ml of it at least. But, it strikes me as a bit strange that the bottledesign and colour of the perfume is all gold and warm. When I think of lavender, I think pastel purple, but then again, the leather is quite prominent.

This fragrance opens with a sensual, creamy vanilla that unfolds beautifully from the very first moments—soft, enveloping, and almost hypnotic in its gentle radiance. The vanilla remains present throughout, but in a subtle, understated way that feels elegant rather than overpowering. As the scent develops, the composition gradually reveals a refined leathery base, adding depth, contrast, and an unexpected sophistication. The result is a perfume with a dual nature: tender and luminous at first, then confident and shadowed, like a goddess with two faces.

I have to honestly say, I love Burberry Goddess extremely! From the very first spray back then, it was clear, it suits me! Warm, soft, feminine. In the evening, I really like to wear the Intense version. And that's why I was so incredibly excited when I heard that a new version is coming to the market. I jumped off the sofa in the evening and cheered. My husband sat next to me completely perplexed. But I have to say, I was very skeptical when I read the fragrance notes. Raspberry and leather? Isn't that somehow too much? Spoiler: after the first spray, I thought to myself, yes baby - give me more! But let's start from the beginning: The first spray, wow. Raspberry. Juicy, fruity, and fresh. I like it. Elegant and really beautifully balanced. Not overly sweet and sticky. (Fortunately) no childish sweetness, but perfectly dosed. Harmoniously balanced. Berry-like, noble, and liqueur-like. Then comes the Goddess EdP DNA, soft, creamy, as usual. But less sweet: Fresh lavender, very herbal, slightly spicy. A lot of character. Simply special - I like it. Almost magical, like a walk through a lavender field in the evening. Here, lavender does not stand for inner peace, but for feminine strength. Very dominant and less soft. The vanilla, darker than usual, richer, deeper. But still slightly creamy and not intrusive. No headache - nausea - scented candle - vanilla. Dark and elegant like a vanilla pod soaked in cognac. Barely sweet. And then the leather comes through! A smooth, soft, creamy leather. Like when you stroke a suede handbag. This makes the scent very exciting and grown-up. Wow, folks - I'm telling you. I'm not a big raspberry leather fan. But! In this case, I'm just blown away. The Goddess DNA becomes so extremely complex, noble, high-quality. Deep and sensual. Almost unisex. I love this contrast. Fruity, our beloved goddess DNA, and then this velvety leather. The raspberry brings that bright smile at the beginning - but then the leather lays over it and the scent changes. If the scent could talk, it would say: I'm not just sweet - I know exactly what I want. ;-) And now let's be honest, compared to the Goddess EdP and the Intense version. EdP: The classic scent is for me feminine, soft, and creamy. Vanilla meets lavender. I wear it constantly and love it. Intense: Here it gets warmer, deeper, and more drama baby. The vanilla is brighter but even more present, and the lavender is more herbal. Perfect for evenings or going out. (But I know, opinions are divided here. But I also find this very beautiful and something different.) Goddess perfume (new variant) Compared to the other two, I would say it is very herbaceous, unisex, hardly sweet, very herbal. Regarding longevity, I was really positively surprised, as the scent lasts for me 6-8 hours. No scent cloud, you don't pull the scent behind you for kilometers. But still present and with me. No boom - here I am! But rather a statement - I know what I want, I know who I am. The only thing I might criticize - the raspberry is unfortunately almost gone in the drydown. I would have liked it to stay. Conclusion: I really love all three scents. And all three scents are so different. But that's a good thing, because who needs three similar ones? The classic is definitely my daily companion and will remain so. The intense version is my power move, or when I just feel like something different. But only very subtly dosed. And the new version - my secret weapon when I want to leave a lasting impression. In summer and everyday life, it might be too much for me, but in autumn and winter, and in the evening, it will definitely be my secret weapon to turn a few heads. (Oops, I'm married, I just realized.) But girls, you know what I mean. I'm glad that all three scents are so different; for me, each scent has its right to exist, and I'm just happy with the new variant.

When I first smelled Burberry Goddess, it was quite a while ago, but I liked it right away. Now I had a sample of the "Goddess Parfum | Burberry." Since I usually evaluate or describe predominantly masculine or unisex perfumes, I wanted to test a declared feminine fragrance again. And what can I say... this is an absolute hit in my eyes.

Yesterday it seemed to be pleasantly warm for the last time, and when I was in the garden in the late afternoon, the sun shone in that typical autumn golden-yellow way and had a lovely warmth. And this feeling is exactly what Goddess Parfum gives me.

What a beautiful perfume. The first spray is lightly fruity-fresh but also warm and incredibly sensual. The term perfect femininity fits here absolutely. The bottle, a little treasure (as 30ml), then the warm-golden content and the fine fragrance mist transforms every woman into a goddess.

Sprayed in the perfumery and at first, yessss!!!! Then ordered, it arrived, luckily a free sample included, sprayed, noooooo!!!!! I can't do this to myself, sent it back in its original packaging. So far, so good…… Found the sample again after 2 weeks, sprayed, yessssss!!! Ooooaaa, don’t annoy me!!!!!!!

I really can't understand the negative reviews here. They truly demotivated me from even trying the scent. But when I smelled it for the first time, I was immediately in love, and I must say it has become my absolute favorite fragrance! I found the fragrance pyramid very interesting because it consists of very few notes. Yet they harmonize wonderfully with each other.

I tried this on strip and was impressed...on skin ehhhh. It starts out so promising, a dry slightly sweetened iris-tobacco. Then the amberwood kicks in and it's like "oh another amberwood. In 2025." They really need to give up on this same drydown they put into every single men's release. It's just laziness. I get that you can't make a completely different fragrance, top to bottom, for every single release, especially when brands are releasing like 5 scents a year, but there exist other DNAs to choose from. Dior Homme Parfum (2024) is so much better than this. Doesn't exactly smell 1-to-1 but it does the same thing essentially and you can use it in the same situations. If you want a nice mass appealing modern masculine iris, just stick to the Dior.

This is a Fantastic Fragrance ! Woody, Warm, Floral, Tobacco, Ambery, Complex , Opulent and Sensual. You can't go wrong with it. I tried it at Sephora store and I fell in love with it at first sniff. It is on my Radar and I will buy it. Givenchy Society Ambree opens with up warm spicy, green and floral notes in the background then dry down is semi sweet vanilla, balsamic, tobacco and ambery. At first I saw it on Instagram then I tried it , It smells so good and very pleasant. It is suitable for cold weather. Longevity is good. The Tobacco, Amber, Narcissus and Vanilla notes are dominant in this perfume. In my opinion, One of the best releases of 2025 so far. Highly Recommended. Second Edit : Finally, I bought it from HOLT RENFREW OGILVY today. I'm so happy that I have it in my collection and It is a New Scent for this year 2025. Two Thumbs Up. Bravo Givenchy! Rating : 8.5 / 10

I flat out love this fragrance. It's top 5 in my 400+ collection and I can't stop reaching for it. It's woody, smoky, and tones of sweet vanilla; it's fantastic. I also love Dior Homme Parfum 2025 don't like them YouTubers fool you about it. It's way better than that trash DHP. If you don't have this in your collection you are surely missing out. DHP 2025, Boss Bottled Absolu, GS Ambree all smells in the same family to my nose.

…but a bit overpriced. It’s got a good opening, semi-sweet feel that’s not overbearing, and not TOO sweet. I was bummed because the tobacco is so soft. I honestly barely get a hint of tobacco. It’s all about the amber in this. They made the atomizer douse you for a reason… it isn’t a loud performer. Sillage is minimal unless you spray 7+ times, and even then it’s barely got a 4ft radius. Sillage is also short as well. This is a great scent for a date or a formal event, but if you’re like me and like presence and sillage, you’ll probably be a bit disappointed. A nice scent indeed, but I should have went with my instincts and grabbed Insurrections Tobacco & Cognac instead. (That was what the in my head battle was). If you are looking for a tobacco scent like I was, this is NOT it, despite it listing tobacco as a main accord, and reviewers telling you it’s there. Good, but not worth $144. On to the next adventure.

A nice take on the juniper-sage combo that I’ve enjoyed in other scents. The tobacco in the opening is too much that I wouldn’t wear it personally, even though I appreciate the scent. Strongly masculine in my opinion. I picture a man in a suit as much as a camping stove in the woods. Despite its strength, the smoke doesn’t smother the juniper and clary sage notes, and within 10-15 mins fades away to let these two come forth, making the scent more aromatic, and a little herbal. The juniper and clary sage are much more within the top notes of Gentleman Society, whereas in my other juniper and clary sage frags such as Pineward Juniperus and DS & Durga Coriander, they are in the middle. They stay distinctly at the fore for another 5-10 mins before muddling off into a general smoky-wood scent with some sweetness as well. I think the tobacco comes back but lingers in the background. I occasionally still pick up some creamy clary sage on the fleshier parts of my forearm, which is also where the scent tends to be sweeter. Meanwhile, it generally gives smoking log elsewhere. Slowly, a bit of vanilla comes in but it is not very strong. Waiting to see if the vetiver comes into play.

It's interesting how this scent immediately reveals its full composition, opening with a delightful and engaging blend of tobacco, sandalwood, and vanilla. This warm base is balanced by sage and juniper notes, which introduce a fresher, greener, and more aromatic quality.

The Society flankers from Givenchy are a nice addition to the fantastic Gentleman line, but they haven't completely convinced me so far. With "Gentleman Society (Eau de Parfum Ambrée) | Givenchy," that changes. Here we have the classic Gentleman DNA, spicy, powdery, sweet, delicious.

... meeting at the Casino Partouche Nice Palais De La Méditerranée in Nice. First, I had a little something to eat at the bistro. Now I'm strolling through the boulevards towards the casino. On the way, I encounter elegantly dressed ladies who look at me just as I look at them.

Givenchy is gradually becoming one of my favorite houses. According to the info status of my collection, 7 Givenchy perfumes are now displayed. Just ahead of Dior now. Unbeaten is of course my favorite house Chanel with 12 bottles. Although I must say that I have 2 travel sizes from Givenchy, and I do not include these in my main collection.

Here we have a delightful all-rounder from Givenchy. The much-hyped Gentleman Givenchy Réserve Privée unfortunately didn't appeal to me as much, as the whisky note in the top was a bit too much for someone who doesn't drink a drop of alcohol.

Jo Malone's Intense collection is honestly not that intense for me. Her Saffron scent was one of my most anticipated but every time I tried it, the smell was gone in minutes. While there, it was a pleasant soft saffron with slightly spicy and creamy notes. I cannot really say much else about it: nothing stood out but the name. If it lasted longer I might have bought a small bottle but it did not do it for me.

As autumn sets in, I find myself craving dark fragrances. Scents that can be entrusted to the retreat inward, supporting the shortening days and lengthening nights. I am not the type who wants to hold onto summer for as long as possible, flying to the South Seas in winter or heading to the Canary Islands in autumn, where one might still expect beach weather. Every season has its mood, which I gladly surrender to and celebrate. Saffron is a perfect autumn fragrance. Not only is its noble yet somehow unpretentious bottle dark, but the scent itself is as well. However, it is not of a profound darkness - I could also say (morbid?) gloom - but rather a friendly, soothing darkness that provides a sense of security without becoming "cozy." One might expect a strong opening given the spicy-fresh-smoky top notes, yet I perceive Saffron as rather soft from the start; at least it hints that it will develop softly. Spice is certainly present, and strangely, a subtle leather-wood note emerges quickly, which I cannot quite explain. Perhaps my nose/my scent memory is already segmenting here, as I have noticed that smoky notes tend to develop more subtly on me, while woody and leathery notes do so quite strongly. Since there is no shortage of wood here, I am not particularly surprised, especially as guaiac wood often exhibits a certain intense, bitter strength that runs through the entire scent journey of Saffron. By the way, the slightly bitter-aromatic-earthy saffron note is always difficult to describe, but when I smell it, I recognize it well. Perhaps the interplay of wood & saffron hints at soft leather, but that is just my speculation. Iris & sandalwood act like softeners over the woody-bitter-spicy events, and this, in turn, makes this fragrance so appealing to me. It feels like warm, soft skin - and I do not mean just the fine velvety skin of the fairer sex, but also the well-circulated, yet not sweaty, warm, hairy skin of men. Here I can lean back with confidence and feel protected and secure; a man who smells like this radiates strength, warmth, and calmness to me, attributes that gain even more attractiveness for me in the dark season than they already do. The rather skin-close sillage is also beautiful and harmonious. Spices, wood, leather - these often have quite good projection, yet here the strength is very well regulated, without being too weak or diluted. The muted sillage adapts excellently to the dwindling energy of autumn and does not overwhelm. The drydown surprises with a certain sweetness - perhaps the woods have already expended their olfactory lion's share beforehand - amber with its special sweetness spreads out, but not too much and not too pure. Just barely, Saffron brushes past the aforementioned label of "cozy"; I would rather describe it as "sensual," as the skin-like quality is beautifully highlighted by a lovely hint of cool-soft musk. The longevity, however, does not last through a dark autumn evening, but given the overall rather restrained, quiet, soft, and somewhat elegant character of the fragrance, I find that quite fitting. I find scent similarities in Saffron to Carner Cuirs and Carner D600. This is interesting, as I know both well; Cuirs was in my collection for some time but unfortunately developed consistently woody and a bit too sharp and one-dimensional, as I realized only quite late, which is why it had to leave me. D600, on the other hand, is a lovely cuddler, also spicy, also leathery, also introverted, also velvety. But one must add a decent amount of sweetness to it compared to Saffron, which pushes it more towards winter seasonally and, in terms of setting, rather from the living room to the bedroom ;-). Both, however, have a special, slightly extravagant note that still does not seem exaggerated or aloof, but rather familiar and interesting at the same time. What I wished for was a fragrance that combines Cuirs & D600 and unites the best of both worlds. With Saffron, I have found it and will embark on a liaison with it during all the dark, quiet autumn evenings that are looming, and whose melancholic beauty casts a quiet glow on my mood.

When I wanted to use the €10 Parfumo voucher at Ludwig Beck yesterday, I took a proper look at the Jo Malone perfumes for the first time and almost ordered 2 small 30 ml bottles. First of all, big praise for offering this affordable size! But luckily, I didn't order blindly, which also applies to the Bal D'Afrique by Byredo that I was considering, but for different reasons (it smells like Vetiver Fatal, which I own). Today, I tested quite a few Jo Malones at the Douglas in Cologne, and that was good because now I definitely know more about the brand and their approach to making fragrances. So the voucher will have to wait. Saffron wasn't available for purchase, but it quickly landed on my skin due to the enthusiastic excitement of the saleswoman, along with Earl Grey & Cucumber. However, while the tea scent faded so quickly that I can't even properly evaluate or comment on it, the fragrance from the black, more expensive bottle held up. Luckily, it would be a shame if all JMs were such fleeting scents. But I will also spray the Earl Grey separately and test it thoroughly, even if it will only last about 20 minutes again. I'm not a fan of layering, even though the JMs are suitable for it and marketed that way, so I was hoping for standalone fragrances. Saffron is definitely that, offering far more than its name would suggest and is, to put it simply, an extremely pleasant, rounded scent. It is spicy and oriental due to the saffron, offers milky wood, a high cuddle & jammy factor, protects the wearer, and is wrapped tightly and gently. I would mention iris and incense as the closest notes, but it is a total work of art that has surprised me very positively. Unfortunately, there are also performance issues here, although seemingly less than with the lighter scents. Bottle: simple, but I find it prettier in black. Unfortunately, it is only available in 100 ml. Sillage: most suitable for cozy autumn, but also conceivable as a signature scent and very thoughtful. Longevity: relieving, although improvable, 6-7 hours. A mix of Amouage on cuddle mode and Olfactive Studios Lumiere Blanche. Snuggly, wonderful, warm, slightly masculine. Thumbs up!

After the wonderful comment from dear Gaukeleya, I must now also "add my two cents" to this masterpiece: I tested Saffron at our only Jo Malone counter, in a Douglas store in Vienna, among many others, and then bought Peony & Blush Suede as a daytime fragrance. However, Saffron and one of the Intense rose scents stuck in my memory, and I noted them down as "dark" evening fragrances, for going out, for example, to the casino. Recently, I managed to get a 7ml sample of Saffron and fell head over heels in love. I own only a few fragrances that are as balanced, multifaceted, and high-quality in appearance. When my spray bottle is empty, I definitely need to get the full bottle, even if it costs 115 euros (but it's worth it). I remembered the scent as oriental-spicy-opulent, but that's not quite accurate. Especially regarding the sillage. One mustn't forget that it is an Eau de Cologne (albeit Intense), and that lies below an Eau de Toilette in terms of perfume oil concentration. I prefer to wear it at home when I can enjoy a free evening, read a good book, and perhaps light a candle or two. Now to the notes: Upon the first sniff at the spray opening, the scent immediately reminded me of "Actrice" by Veronica Ferres. Because of the orange-vanilla-sandalwood combination. Unfortunately, Actrice has no wood-incense or other notes and is rather overwhelming-gourmand-like. When you spray Saffron, the interesting thing is that you always perceive different notes, depending on whether you are 10cm away from the skin or sniffing directly at the skin. From a distance, I can perceive natural wood, leather, and the orange/vanilla combination. When getting closer, intense freshly tanned leather comes to the forefront. Then the heart note soon arrives, with the typical saffron note, framed in (in my opinion) cedarwood. A fresh, lively wood. The scent becomes earthier, spicier, and eventually, you can also perceive the incense note. I find it like cold smoke or ash, but not biting, just cold and uninviting. At the same time, however, the vanilla note remains, which lulls you in. In the base, Saffron almost becomes a gourmand scent, with coconut notes like in Indian cuisine, vanilla, and musk. Very close to the skin and tempting, but not too sweet. However, the wood notes still persist, now leaning more towards sandalwood. It seems to me that Saffron smells different depending on the mood; you are surprised by it every day. The longevity is quite okay, the sillage rather weak. It is a close, cozy feel-good scent for gloomy, rainy days. Very high-quality crafted.

Jo Malone has a new one. And since I always find Jo Malone's scents particularly interesting (even if many of them wouldn't make it into my collection), I had to sniff it right away. First just on the card, as I was already wearing another fragrance. Saffron starts off fresh. That must be the bergamot, but somehow incognito. So this sharp citrusy aroma that you usually associate with bergamot is never really detectable. It’s more like a light fresh breeze that carries the other ingredients. In the opening, the pink pepper is also immediately noticeable. It basically introduces the spiciness in the fragrance, but it is still the lightest of the spices in the scent, as pepper also has something, yes, how should I put it, spritzy about it. Nevertheless, the fragrance is not a fresh scent, but thoroughly spicy, yet light. Gradually, the saffron emerges, which from now on weaves through the fragrance like a red ribbon and gains more and more intensity. The saffron scent is warm, soft, and gentle, and it remains present even until the base notes. Towards the end, the woody notes come through nicely. I really like the scent of guaiac wood because it has such a warm-woody aroma that is not aggressively spicy. When I now sniff the card after about 5 hours and try to imagine the wood I smell, a very elegant piece of furniture comes to mind. The wood is dark, almost leaning towards a reddish mahogany color, and when you run your hand over it, it is very smooth. Together with the musk and/or amber, the wood forms a beautiful base that definitely leans towards a slightly powdery quality. Of course, the saffron is always present. All in all, a very nice fragrance that I definitely want to test on my skin. In comparison with the other black scents from Jo Malone, I find that this one is one of the weaker ones, with intensity comparable to Oud/Bergamot or Iris/White Musk, although the latter is still a tad stronger. It definitely doesn’t have as much power as Velvet Rose/Oud, which I love on the card, but unfortunately doesn’t smell nice on my skin. However, that does not make Saffron any worse than the other blacks. If it had even more spice, it would be almost too much.

I love clean scents. I love citrus. And I apparently also now love floral scents, since this feels like the cleanest version of "home" for me. Initial small burst of citrus and ginger that morphs into flowers with a soft warm undertone from the amber and musk. Turns sweet on my skin and just smells fresh and cozy to me. A perfect everyday wear for me that both calms and elevates my mood.

Tested: skin and fabric over 8 hrs. TLDR: Citrus/spice upon application, slightly generic masculine, unisex if anything, inoffensive, dries down to rose musk. -As a huge fan of the original Burberry Her, let me say, these are nothing alike. If the sweetness and fruity red berries of the original do not agree with you, I’d give this flanker a chance! Upon first application, it was a blast of STRONG lemon. Immediate citrus. A little bit like spray cleaner. Shortly after, the ginger kicks in and it starts to remind me of a men’s cologne, the fresh and slightly spicy kind. Not at all overwhelming, if a bit generic. Not Old Spice or Axe. This part of the scent lasted only about 4 hours as far as I could tell. Great projection for about 30 minutes, I could smell it on myself. My non-fragrance hobbies coworker liked it, though she agreed that it was more masculine that what I usually wear. “Does it comes in a blue bottle?”, she asked. That made me laugh. I suspect she was thinking of D&G Blue - also lemon, spicy, and unisex. 8 hours into wearing is when I checked again. It had faded a lot by that point, and ultimately dried down on my skin to a soft rose musk that reminds me so much of Rosie by Rosie Jane. This is the part of the scent journey that is most agreeable to me. I didn’t catch very much floral until the very end, and I don’t see myself wearing it again, per my own tastes. I do, however, find it nice, light spice, and refreshing!

I can't describe it at all; ever since I first wore this fragrance, I can't stop thinking about it. I don't notice the lemon and ginger, but I definitely pick up on the floral notes and the musk. For me personally, it's the perfect scent for "every now and then." I don't own it myself, as I have enough at home and it's a bit heavy on the wallet. But whenever I pass by a perfume shop and see it, it belongs to me for the day. That way, I never get tired of it, and it can bring me joy from time to time. It will probably remain my little affair for a long time!

LVHM - do you really mean this? Givenchy used to be such a gorgeous brand. I'm still in awe of perfumes like "Organza", "L'Interdit", or my beloved "Givenchy III". But this new Dahlia-flanker is not in the least divine and very remote from anything I'd associate with "gold". "When gold meets fragrance" it says on my sample. And they call it a "lush floral woody". What? "Amouage Gold" is a lush floral - there is no way of comparing the noble Amouage to this watered-down nondescript floral by Mr Demarchy. (The guy runs the risk of ruining his repution if he continues to put his name under such bland fragrances). I can't detect any real flowers in "Dahlia Divin", just some artificial aromachemicals used by the knowledgeable chemist in order to mimick some kind of - "flower". "Dahli Divin" is extremely boring and even worse than the new "Black Opium", which I also dislike. LVMH still come up with beautiful perfume vessels and clever marketing ideas, pretty names and packagings. But the content? Actually, not even worth writing about. Another huge disappointment.

I am not a fragrance professional. I cannot write epic lengths about the composition and development of a scent, as others here can describe so aptly. But what I can describe is the effect of this fragrance, on me and on others. Backstory: For every season, I need two fragrances. Winter/Fall and Spring/Summer. Always one scent for everyday wear and one for going out. For everyday wear this season, I am using DKNY Fresh Blossom. But I still needed a scent for the evening, something seductive that would particularly charm my boyfriend and make me feel utterly sexy, feminine, and glamorous - without smelling "cheap" or like something generic. Sometimes, as a woman, you want that ;-) For winter, it was clearly Yves Saint Laurent - Manifesto Elixir. And since then, I was looking for a suitable counterpart for the warm season. I really stumbled into every little perfumery and Douglas (is that how you say it in plural ^^) multiple times. The staff has already looked at me critically, "What does she want here again?". But I never found anything or perhaps I wasn't well advised. Here in the forum, Dahlia Devine was recommended to me. Until then, I had never heard of this fragrance, and it was never suggested to me on-site either. So I went back to Douglas - once again - with a list of fragrance recommendations - once again! There, I tried this one alongside numerous other recommendations from this forum - and I was immediately captivated. My nose was already overwhelmed with various other scent influences and the somewhat counteracting coffee beans, but I perceived this fragrance very intensely. Long story short: I finally ordered it and wore it out on the weekend in the evening. The effect was astonishing and similar to Manifesto. No lie, I was approached by almost every second friend I hugged to greet. Everyone also took a second sniff. A very seductive effect on the outside world. But the most important thing: Once I applied the fragrance, it actually enveloped me, and for once, the marketing hit the nail on the head, like a couture gown. I felt completely prepared for the evening right away. When I came home that night or rather the morning, I could still perceive the scent on me. Conclusion: This fragrance has a magical effect both on me and on my environment. Whether I would associate it with Alicia Keys is another question ;-) But it is 100% glamorous without being overly ladylike. It suits every occasion - whether going out in style, bar-hopping, dining with friends, etc. - and leaves a lasting impression + has exemplary longevity. Basically, everything a fragrance should have in my opinion. I can only recommend it with the highest enthusiasm. The little plus: If you don’t have a circle of friends or acquaintances consisting of fragrance junkies or connoisseurs, hardly anyone knows it. Definitely not mainstream :-)

Now I have to tell you briefly about my new friend - her name is Dahlia, Dahlia Divin. I only met her a week ago and was totally enchanted by her in no time. She has everything you could wish for in a friend. We went shopping together and she made me feel so good. I feel appreciated and valuable. She put me in a beautiful light and I could really enjoy the time - she didn’t disturb me at all but was still totally present. After shopping, we took a walk in the park and it was just a lovely feeling of life with her. I felt elegant with her. My husband and daughter also liked her very much. Of course, I wanted to invite her to my home right away. At the next opportunity, I gave her a perfume shop voucher and invited her over. A few days later, she came. I was really happy and excited. But now comes the real kicker... she just bursts into my house and starts shouting. I feel harassed and overwhelmed by her. I almost get a headache from the noise. Yes, I almost felt sick.... Well, okay, I have to say I had met many other friends in the perfume shop during the day, maybe that’s why I got annoyed so quickly. In any case, I wanted to throw her out of the apartment right away (return slip had already been requested). Completely exhausted and annoyed, I lay down on the sofa with my daughter. Well, then my daughter told me how much she liked Dahlia and why Dahlia wasn’t with us every day. She practically threw herself around her neck. Strange, why was Dahlia so nice to my little daughter and not to me anymore? I decided to endure her for the sake of the child. Well, what can I say. The lady got back on track and suddenly became tame again. Finally, my friend was back, with whom I had gotten along so well and who had made me feel so good. Admittedly, she’s not particularly silly and you can’t pull off any wild stunts with her. But you can have a wonderful dinner, go to a musical, or do other nice activities with her. For the childish things, I have my new friend Candy - she’s quite silly, but you need that as a contrast to a lady like Dahlia. (About the scent itself: as many have written, jasmine stands out strongly. Patchouli and sandalwood make the scent very warm and totally pleasant to wear after a rather loud phase. In my opinion, it’s a fragrance for women from their mid-20s.)

The black dahlia is one of my favorites, so I was curious about Dahlia Divin. And I must say, Divin also has favorite qualities. How fitting that Alicia Keys is the face of this fragrance, because at the first spray, "Fallin`" immediately comes to mind - one of my favorite songs. Highly recommended to listen to while wearing this scent: I keep on fallin' in In love with you Sometimes I love you Sometimes you make me blue Sometimes I feel good At times I feel used Lovin' you darlin' Makes me so confused I keep on fallin' in and out Of love with you I never loved someone The way that I loved you Oh, oh, oh Never felt this way How do you give me so much pleasure And cause me so much pain Just when I think I've taken more than would a fool I start fallin' back in love with you And I too fall into this sensual scent, like into a soft luxurious feather bed. It is smoothly sweet, and also somewhat melancholic, like this confusing love that hovers between hope and fear, which Alicia sings about. Who doesn’t know these feelings? Yet Divin gives hope for a good ending, as it feels like a warm comforting embrace. After many doubts, everything turns out well - and one feels safe. This secure, sheltered feeling is also conveyed by the fragrance. The mirabelle is deliciously sweet, and with the white flowers, the sun rises. The jasmine is also bright and elegant, emphasized by juicy vetiver. Patchouli adds sensuality, and sandalwood makes Divin round and radiant. The scent has something of "arriving" after a long journey - and it may be an emotional journey. I press the repeat button and let myself fall into "Fallin`" once more.

Dahlia Divin is initially a rather fruity scent that later leans more towards the floral direction. I have had it for about a good year now. I believe it was winter when I bought it used. The start, as mentioned, is very fruity with beautiful juicy-sweet mirabelles. I really like the scent at this stage. However, it soon becomes too sweet for me. Jasmine Sambac and modern, current patchouli, as found in many of today's mainstream fragrances, come through strongly. This sweetness is personally too much for me. I prefer patchouli in the old-fashioned way, dark, earthy, even a bit grave-like. The scent doesn't last more than two hours on me, which doesn't bother me too much. It is not a bad scent in itself, but it doesn't quite match my taste, and I won't repurchase it. It goes a bit in the direction of Coco Mademoiselle, which I personally like much better because it is less sweet, or even a little like So Elixir. One thing I could still try: whether the cold of winter dims the sweetness of the scent a bit. I still have to wait for that. Unfortunately, it cannot compete with the great classics from Givenchy like Organza, Ysatis, Givenchy III, or Eau de Givenchy. However, Dahlia Divin will surely find its admirers.

My first encounter: I was once again in my trusted perfumery today :) I wanted to test some specific fragrances! But then there was this nice saleswoman all of a sudden. She had seen me holding the Tresor in Love... She had the same taste as I did :) Identical to every single perfume! And then she said she had to show me her personal favorite perfume. It was the Dahlia Divin!

Dhalia Divin is a very refined fragrance for me. Not overpowering, but well noticeable. The mirabelle smells sweet and ripe here, but no overly synthetic fruit note imposes itself. A very beautiful jasmine note is at the center here. In my opinion, this is simply well done. All the other notes just cradle it. It’s an uncomplicated, yet beautiful scent.

Dahlia Divin was, in a certain way, "love at first sniff" for me. Completely unexpectedly, I took the sample, giving myself a small spray on both wrists. The fragrance starts with delicious mirabelle, fruity, only minimally sweet and a bit sparkling. I like that. However, this opening quickly fades and floral notes come in.

~ Inspiration ~ "Dahlia Divin" landed on my watchlist after "Dahlia Noir" didn't quite convince me, and I was curious about this new variant. ~ Bottle ~ The square glass bottle with golden liquid/inscription and white cap gives an elegant impression. The name translates to "divine dahlia." ~ Fragrance ~ It starts with sugary, slightly tart, sun-ripened mirabelles.

Dahlia Divin is a fragrance that should definitely not be judged right from the beginning. Because then it would have received 100% from me. The start is really great, fruity-sour, just like how mirabelles smell. I could hardly take my nose off my wrist. I was tempted to buy the largest bottle right away. But then I waited. Which turned out to be a good decision for me.

Here we have a scent that seems quite simple based on the fragrance description or fragrance pyramid (well, it really is, but read on! :D). But when I briefly tested it on paper, I knew I definitely had to test it on my skin as well. Because right from the first sniff, it smelled to me like fresh carrots, which I found very delicious! If I hadn't tested the scent on my skin, I would have surely eaten the test strip… *gag* The scent: Oh, what a delicious start.
