You immediately smell the iris root, which strongly resembles grated carrots, giving the scent a very green impression. The violets take a while to become noticeable, even though they are listed in the top notes. The scent is quite straightforward, so it initially smells carrot-like, then becomes sweeter with the violets. A little later, the "carrots" gradually turn into powdery iris. Together with the sweet violets (which occasionally remind one of jasmine), the fragrance smells very nice, sweet, soft, and powdery. Sandalwood forms the base and is a bit weak. The amber is almost undetectable. Longevity and sillage: The longevity is somewhat low, with the scent lasting about five hours on the skin. The sillage is also not very high; especially at the beginning, the fragrance takes a little time to fully unfold. After that, it is somewhat noticeable for a short time before it gradually fades away. The bottle: The bottle is rectangular, tall, and black (but slightly transparent). On the front, there is the well-known Jo Malone label with the name and logo. The oval cap is chrome-plated. All in all, quite nice, though not particularly special. So, I haven't had a carrot-like iris or iris root under my nose for quite some time. Sure, I've tested many iris fragrances, but they were almost always just powdery (which this scent also becomes later). That's not bad, but I had somehow missed this carrot-like scent. It also makes the fragrance smell beautifully green. Since the scent becomes sweeter later on, while the iris starts to smell "normal" and thus the scent also becomes more powdery, Orris & Sandalwood has become a very beautiful, soft fragrance, where one would have wished for a stronger sillage, as it is actually quite suitable for going out. You can hardly stop smelling the sprayed area, so you must surely be like a burr on a lady (I specifically say lady, as the scent smells quite feminine)… and thus possibly be a big nuisance (*sniff* I hope not!). However, since it is unfortunately not very strong, it can instead be excellently used for relaxation… or, as it is sometimes called here,… as a cuddly scent or something :) You really have to test it; I found it truly wonderful, even if, as mentioned at the beginning, it is very simply constructed. The only downside (aside from the low longevity): The scent might come off as a bit too feminine for a unisex fragrance and therefore, once again,… simply smells better on women… (of course, you could also say whether you would like to smell such a scent on us guys,… you could let me know :D

“The room is almost empty except for the afternoon sun and the sounds of traffic, a few particles of dust floating in the beam of light. The room is almost empty except for the last boxes, with a few things you apparently don’t miss. I packed them for you. I won’t bring them to you. Now they do nothing here except cast shadows. The later it gets, the longer they grow. Distorted by time in the slanted light. And if someone asks me, I say I don’t miss you.” My song association with this fragrance, which I came to like a virgin to a child, as a latecomer to sharing, I dusted off the bottle that wasn’t particularly liked and am very satisfied with it. Not that I have a lack of iris fragrances, no… This one opens with a beautiful powdery-herb-fresh note, the kind of violet that is more commonly found in men’s fragrances, stripped of any spring-like floral innocence. Very soon a soft-powdery iris note joins in, of which I briefly fear it drifts too much into a make-up sweet territory for my taste, but it catches itself just before the fall and takes on a rather harsh, almost slightly sour-bitter touch, reminding me of vetiver, though according to the fragrance pyramid it probably isn’t. Perhaps it’s still a hint of violet, as in Arsene Lupin, where the violet also has a slightly bitter note. It doesn’t really last long; at least I perceive it on myself for only about 4 hours, after which I have to sniff again and go on a search for traces. Maybe that’s also why it reminds me of this song, of an empty room with a wooden floor and packed boxes, with shimmering dust in the air, somehow quite pleasant, yet with a slightly bitter aftertaste of farewell. Such is the scent, powdery, woody, delicately bitter, with a light gray tint, without metallic aspects, not bright and cutting, as iris can sometimes be. A bit melancholic. Beautiful, suitable for everyday wear, but also nothing spectacularly special that one hasn’t smelled somewhere before. For iris lovers, however, it’s a must-try, as in the realm of passion countless nuances open up that one might still want to experience. This one is very close to “Iris Prima” for me, in terms of the dust and the wooden floor, but a bit harsher and edgier. Dust gray. “The room is almost empty except for me. With my head on my knees, I watch the window crosses as they move from one corner to another on the ceiling. In the wandering of the light. And until it gets dark. I do nothing here except cast shadows. The later it gets, the longer they grow. Distorted by time, in the slanted light, and if someone asks me, I say: Nothing” (Dota)

This is the best perfume from Burberry, it's quality is fascinating, i love the combination of it, raspberries, vanilla, leather, cashmere wood, tonka bean and sandalwood, it's really good stuff, performance wise too, it's beast mode on my skin. i love the bottle's design too, it looks class! well done Burberry!

Every day, you show up to work and either accomplish a sufficient amount or look productive enough not to get fired. And when you've either crossed enough tasks off your to-do list or read the entire internet, you deserve to leave the office and get a drink. So how about a Manhattan cocktail for happy hour? To begin with, Burberry Brit Rhythm Intense opens with a blast of awesome wormwood-absinthe, which reminds me of Vermouth, a fortified Italian wine that has had a distilled spirit like brandy added to it. Imagine you are drinking a Manhattan cocktail for an aperitif, which smells spicy, sweet, and robust, and tastes heavenly. Like the Vermouth, some herbal notes get more prominent, and I smell cumin, mint, marjoram, and quinine. This robust, aromatic, and earthy introduction is completed by spicy pepper that reveals as soon as the boozy note calms down. After nearly half an hour, the heart announces as a more masculine and reinforced leather accent compared to Brit Rhythm. There are intense notes of patchouli and sensual amber fused with leather, a more modern mild and soft leather similar to Armani Code, neither dark nor rude. To put it very clearly, it is not the kind of raw leather you can smell in most of Ferrari's fragrances, which I like, of course. Ultimately, after the boozy and leathery phase, BBRI turns into work and comforting scent, sitting on the skin with lasting undertones of blonde woods and guaiac wood, with the sweet touch of the tonka beans- Recommended for cool and cold weather, from late fall till early spring, it is safe for office, intense but not overpowering, during the evening, and for your nights out, it is still going strong for the after-party. Please, be informed that sillage stays around your arms, but longevity is enormous if you smell your shirt or sweater the day after you can feel it, so smokey and sensuous. -Elysium

Spring is definitely here to stay. It might rain again eventually, but at this point, it would only be a summery rain. Its just monday, i have a trillion things to do, there is not, indeed, any particular reason to be happy but still i cannot but smile to the sunny day and i feel light, flirty and silly. The Insensé season is officially open. Insensé became part of my life when i was 15 years old and it has been a beloved spring/summer constant ever since. If i own a fragance that is crazy, fun, romantic and extravagant, it is Insensé, like something a maniac scientist would create by mistake. Take a big fat bouquet of spring flowers: magnolia, sheer iris, a touch of hyacinth maybe and the more dominant muget, wrapped in the shinny cellophane of aldehydes. A spark of bright citrus amplifies the heady effect of aldehydes; the refreshing touch of cool basil rounds this exhilarating opening, and you feel like high on infatuation. So far, this could have perfectly been a ladylike fresh-green floral, but then, the cornerstone of Insensé is an odd but comforting balsam fir, that veers the fragance into the realms of the mysterious and reassuring. Curiouser and curiouser. Insensé cannot be understood without this ingredient that is both sweet and fresh. So, lets say, that healthy dose of spring flowers and aromatic herbs, comes through the sweet/balsamic notes of conifers and lentiscus, reminiscent of the night stroll in the woods of Nuit Etoilée, creating daring unsmelled accords.Happy,insolent, masculine, glorious!

Insensé is one of the many fragrances I shamefully underrated for a long time, I guess for my lack of experience and proper taste. I always misjudged this in the past, always trying it quickly from samples or decants, and always ending up in considering it only a really nice albeit a bit boring and kind of heavy sort of “overly feminine fougère”; I am really glad I grabbed a deal recently and got a small 30 ml bottle of this some days ago, so that I had the chance to wear this at its fullest and give it a proper chance. And I got, as they say, a true “epiphany” about this – from mild enthusiasm to sudden devoted worshipping. It is indeed the hyped masterpiece many rave about, and the hype is fully justified. Actually, no, it even gets way less hype than it should. For me, Insensé has now jumped straight on top of the – however limited – chart of the best floral fragrances for men ever made, because it is hands down one of the best, if not the best one ever. And easily among the best masculine offerings in general ever made. Luca Turin once mentioned two key features of this, which perfectly reflect what I also strongly felt while full wearing this the first time: “melancholy and mystery”. It is exactly how I also view Insensé: this a dramatically romantic, rich and slightly decadent scent which stunningly blends decades of masculine and feminine perfumery in an enigmatic, completely new, clever, breathtakingly creative and above all, irresistibly good unisex floral blend. Which indeed smells mysteriously “different” from anything else. Like a prism, it reflects echoes of perfumes ranging from Cristalle, to Diorella, to Caron’s 3rd Man. The smell is complex but seamlessly beautiful: there is a rich heart symphony of green herbs and flowers refreshed by a subtle fruit-pine breeze, contrasting a deeply dark, smoky base accord of woods and aldehydes which provide “weight” and baroque gloominess to flowers and herbs. The overall feel is soapy, smoky, lightly waxy, aldehydic to the bone, floating between a nostalgic green-chypre powderiness and a fresher, more austere balsamic-woody feel of many classic fougères. Not simply a juxtaposition of different styles, just a true rewriting using selected key notes and accords from all those inspirations. It may sound simple or boring, it’s definitely not: as I said it’s truly a sort of triumphant gathering of decades of perfumery blending together to compose this incredibly handsome, unique mosaic. Distinctive, bracing and sophisticated in a quite peculiar, decadent way to say the least, probably also quite “gothic” to a certain extent: surely “not for the faint of heart”. Totally worthy the high prices. Leave that shitty niche boutique and save your money for this. 10/10

There was a very famous bank robber in Greece during the '70s, who used to enter the robbed-to-be bank with a sawed-off unloaded shotgun hidden inside a posy of sword lillies. And yes, bank robbers can achieve rock star status, cause banks, directed by vampires in expensive suits, are not exactly the most popular establishments. He also used to give the flowers to the ladies working in the bank, before running away with the money. He got caught, escaped prison, flew to another continent, got caught again, and during his deportation flight he gifted fragrances bought in the duty-free shop to every hostess on board, leaving them wondering whether he was a shipowner or an oilman. Or both. He died at the age of 35, following the "live fast, die young" motto to a tee. Every time I spray some of this short-lived quirky little gem on me, I feel like I'm ready to enter a bank along with him and run with the money. And on a sunny, yet frigid January morning some years ago, vintage Insensé on a paper strip was one of the two best things I've ever smelled in my life. Having the guts to do something just because you can, will always be a solid example of insolence yelled in the face of norms and poise. Insensé came and went unnoticed, scorned by the defenders of uber masculine fragrances, for it smelled like walking in a forest in early spring or late winter, while holding a bunch of blue flowers in one hand. The fact that a rifle was in the other didn't seem to be in its favour. All the more that it was not there for hunting. A brave little soul, which left its gentle mark by the pen, in a world echoing with the clang of swords and the roar of faddish waves. And despite its failure to smoothly conquer it, it will always be acknowledged for its gallantry and whim. For it did.

When I first obtained my bottle of Insense, I was expecting a floral assault of a fragrance. What I got confounded me - a green oriental? A salty pine-pastry? Must De Cartier over Anais-Anais? Well I can say I understand it now. I'm wearing it on a beautiful, cool, and dry day and it is enveloping me with its lovely aura. This is an aromatic fougere taken into abstract territory. Lily, galbanum, and a very intense Iris play nicely with the lavender and bouquet garni. This is a sunny miracle of fragrance. It's not so beloved because it is daring and pretentious - this is lovely because it is so carefree and beautiful. It's complex, but its beauty lies in the whole picture, not the details. This is the scent of masculine youth. Clean, innocent, and virile, in stark contrast to Kouros's unashamed sexuality. This is truly a singular study in perfumery. Nothing else even comes close. Everyone should try this before it's all gone.

I lucked onto this one. I’d read Luca Turin’s thoughts on Givenchy’s Insensé and was intrigued though I’d never tried it. While visiting San Francisco I found it in a tiny kiosk-sized perfume shop. Smitten. This is my favorite perfume. One slice of Insensé’s beauty is that I can smell the constituent parts even as I take in the whole picture with a clarity unlike any other fragrance. It’s floral, aldeydic, ambery, woody, herbal. I can smell its fougère shape. I can put together the bergamot, amber and moss and see the chypre. I can isolate the cedar. It’s not the new-style cedar that was about to become the Lutens signature. It smells like cedar essential oil, a high-pitched timber along with a sharp oiliness that reminds me of the sound of an oboe. The layering in Insensé is spectacular. High to low: galbanum & aldehyde, lily of the valley and basil, amber and cedar. But forget the bad attempt at description. The perfume you love sweeps you up, captivates you. This one grabbed me by the balls. Not my sole barometer of fragrance quality, but certainly telling. Here's my hypothesis about Insensé. Yes, a masculine floral is doomed to failure. But it would never have existed at all as a feminine release. It would have been less handsome. Odd notes like an oily cedar and a bracing basil would never have been included. The reach of the florals would have been curtailed. Maybe it didn’t fail because it was a floral for men, but because it was the best of classical perfumery (disparate elements, focused complexity, beauty greater than one-note prettiness) launched at the point in men’s fragrance where cool met sport. A note on reformulation. I believe there have been at least two versions. The first, in the Amarige bottle, is everything I’ve just described. Flawless. The second, in the rounded rectangular bottle, is lovely as well, but they clearly tried to butch it up a bit. Less aldehyde, less muguet, more amber. Still spectacular.

There is a kind of man that never can be reached. He is independent, solitaire, and tenderly aloof, his soul always on the edge. Everybody wants him, and he wants nothing. I'm thinking of Rimbaud in Charleville, young, adventurous, with an entire life to come; or in the magnificent character of Lord Sebastian Flyte, from Evelyn Waugh's "Brideshead Revisited".
*This is a review of the vintage formulation.
Today, thanks to the generosity of a colleague, I was able to try the discontinued Insensé.

Insensé by Givenchy probably is the most decadent fragrance I own: I only bouht it to perfume my black leather jacket (and selected leather handbags)... I love the combination of real leather and this warm fragrance of wood, black currant and resins!

A really interesting scent, a male flowery fougere. I can only recall Caron 3 Homme as virile flowers. Although this is not my kind of perfumery I was astonished by the positive vibes of the crazy Givenchy. I'm not a fan of bright aldehyde kick, but everything upon is magic.

A pond, calm and clear, covered with delicate lotus flowers, whose petals dance on the water like butterflies, surrounded by green, hanging gardens. The air is humid and clear, fresh and bright at this place in the early morning, infused with a gentle green, water droplets glide softly on the flowers and leaves of the plants. The flowers emit a delicate fragrance that mingles with the lush green of the leaves and the scent of green figs. The sun has just risen, the day awakens, the dew has settled over everything. The green unfolds and spreads joy and freshness.... _________ This image conveys to me Fig & Lotus Flower - and that is exactly what this fragrance is meant to express. Green, bright, fresh, cheerful. A hint of graceful lotus flowers, neroli, a touch of musk, a good portion of vetiver, and green leaves. The illusion of green leaves is likely achieved here through the molecule Stemone, which is combined with lactonic notes to recreate a milky fig leaf note. It is a fragrance that immediately takes effect on me. Even in a bad mood, it brings me a cheerful feeling, my spirits lift, and the fresh aquatic note clears my mind. *It's amazing what some fragrances can do.* However, it is not for everyone, as Jo Malone's creation is very green, hardly sweet, and this scent does not really change over time. I find it fantastic, especially in summer, a very refreshing creation.

First associations: green, wood, elevated, cathedral of tall trees. The scent uplifts me! Strengthens me! It fits the "Tree" posture from yoga: Well-rooted, upright, oriented towards the sky and light, inner calm, in harmony with myself and the world Can it be that a fragrance has such a strong effect on the psyche?

This fragrance underwent a longer, multiple test run today with interesting results: On me, it presents itself as floral green-fresh at the start and remains very smooth-soft and stable at first. The slightly herbaceous green (of the fig leaf? Assigned by the process of elimination, because to be honest, I've never sniffed the leaves of a fig tree) then seamlessly transitions into a comparatively gentle vetiver. And it stays that way. Very unexciting, but in its insistence on this herb-fresh-green note, it feels almost a bit penetrating to my nose. For my companion, it acted like a different perfume: similar at the start, but then clearly more development and less "smooth": The flowers flash and play with the slightly herbaceous green. Finally, it becomes distinctly woodier and warmer. The musk comes to the fore, which seems to be completely hidden on me. In this version, it's a really nice thing - interesting without becoming too prominent, rounded without being boring. Longevity is surprisingly good, considering that only "Cologne" is written on the bottle.

Burberry Body is a scent made for the stores. It starts out so great. It lures you in, whispering: I am so interesting. Buy me! And then after some time it becomes yet one more scent smelling of whatever… at least that is my opinion. If you buy it - buy it for the opening. Because this has a brilliant opening. I think it is the absint that makes it so interesting, since I know apple and peach and they are not at all dominant here. So, a lovely, new acquaintance for me. Then arrives the rose and the tea. They calm it down a bit and, sadly, it becomes less interesting. I do not get any iris but I do not think it would have made a difference. The base is okay but very subtle. All in all this is not one of Burberry’s best scents, apart from the opening. Since I guess it is the absint note that does the trick, I shall seek out other scents with this note instead. Perhaps they invite me on a more interesting journey. 38/365

A fragrance that smells fantastic ! Very bright, clean and refreshing. It can be worn to the office, dates, on a daily basis and so on. This won't do any harm, let's get this straight. Slight projection with 5-6 hours of longevity. This is that fragrance that you can pick when you want to be fresh and clean without "showing" it too much. Fantastic pick for a hot day. Citrusy, floral and a bit woody also. That kind of smell that you reach for after a cold shower on a hot summer day, for sure. At times, this is very cheap and I really recommend it for the smell but if you want a beast mode, you may reconsider. For me it's pure love even if it's not the greatest performer. Overall rating : 8/10

Is longevity really that bad? I've worn this a couple of time and I recall it lasting 4 hours the first couple of times, didn't wear it for a while (due to rotation) and today I decided to try it again so I did the usual 6 to 7 sprays (I'm an oversprayer) and went on with my day: working from home, walked the dog for a bit, lunch, more work from home and over 6 hours into my day my wife told me she could get my scent as soon as I walked into the room, that's a decent 7hrs longevity. I don't recall it performing this good before, perhaps maceration did it's thing I don't know but I'll test further cause this frag smell great and if you remove the performance issue from the mix we get a winner here.

This is a scent similar to Acqua di Gio, though more green, and a possible replacement for the classic. Apparently they included a little ambroxan, which frankly I didn't notice initially. Compared with AdG, it improved performance to almost a typical EDT level, though it's still on the weaker side. Quite powdery, but I do not really smell iris in this. Overall, a good summer fragrance.  of my perfume reviews at The Scent Stories: thescentstories.substack.com

First review on parfumo, i'll try my best to keep it a buck. The opening is a 10. Burst of lemoney (bergamot) freshness upon opening, the iris is worth noting as well (not as strong as prada l'homme's iris, more casual but refined). Although this sounds cliche, it honestly reminds me of standing amidst a field of flowers. There is a strange appealing aquatic feel to this scent too, reminds me of my days swimming, or coming out of the shower fresh. Very bright and inoffensive notes. I will admit i'm not getting rosemary at all. Simple fragrance make up , but as the bergamot leaves, you get the subtle musk lingering on. However the scent becomes no more than a skin scent after 1 hour on me. I do however, catching myself take whiffs off the back of my hand just to enjoy it, however it would be strictly a scent the wearer can enjoy. Longevity wise its not great, quickly goes into a skin scent after 3 hours and then fades more rapidly after. I've hear other youtubers say the same and occasionally the dissenting opinion that it may last 6 - 7 hours. This is one of the weaker scents by a long shot. He is the yamcha or krillin of the givenchy line when it comes to longevity and sillage, but he is a fan favourite. Not a great anime reference by a long shot, but you get me. Hard to say whether this is worth its price being 100$ aud. Bright citrus and aromatic is honestly the most generic accords of the fragrance world. But definitely try it before you purchase it. I loved it from its opening and i work in a very closed environment (physio) which is why i purchased it. If i were to go further, you can increase the longevity by spraying it on your collar as well as your sleeves; it's a clear scent so it wont stain. I would say that this would also be a perfect gift for others when you are not sure what fragrance to gift them (blind buy worthy if you can forgive the poor longevity and sillage). Givenchy did a great job at pertaining to a wider (15 - 30 yr old) audience with this one, but it's not as sophisticated and mature as their givenchy gentleman edp. I highly enjoy this scent, however it's not the greatest performer.

Hey, I'm currently at Douglas testing a Givenchy flanker. "How does it smell?" Hold on, … I just sprayed it. "And?" Oh wow, it’s super fresh - - nice citrusy - - - has something - - special - - - and is also - - slightly - - - spicy. "What? I could barely understand you, bad connection!" Strange, it shows all three bars on my end. Can you hear me now? "Yes, loud and clear, so again." Well, it smells - - - really fresh - - but - - also a - - little bit like… "Stooopp!" Nothing is coming through on my end." Well, … nothing is coming through for me either! "What do you mean?" Well, the longevity is so poor that you can't even finish a sentence without reapplying :) "So it’s not the bad connection, but this Givenchy?!" Roger … but the opening is really top. Nice citrusy, zesty, fresh, it instantly lifts your mood. Plus, there’s a fine spiciness that makes it wonderfully tingle, almost fizz, so lively is its freshness… it also has a special hue, as if there’s pear in it, very light, clear, and attractive. "And? Are you going to get it?" Nope, let me first apply it properly, I’m going to splash 3-4 sprays on my neck, on my wrist, and another amount on my shirt. That should be enough… "Okay, see you later then." **** Hey, it’s me again, about the Gentleman Cologne from Givenchy. It really starts off great, and after the superb top note, it also becomes a bit green-velvety-plant-like. But on my wrist, it was already gone after half an hour, and an hour later it was gone from my neck and shirt too! "What? Is that it?" Yes, and no trace of iris. "Huh?? I thought your girlfriend's name was Susanne." Very funny … oh by the way, that’s already over too. But speaking of relationships, I think I’ll get this flanker after all, it’s just ideal for Speed Dating!

It is often complained that there are hardly any real gentlemen left today. At Givenchy, this is definitely not the case. They are becoming more and more numerous. It all started in 1974 with 'Givenchy Gentleman', followed by the flanker 'Gentlemen Only' in 2013. Since then, old-school gentlemen have been multiplying like rabbits.

The original has nothing to do with this. But that’s almost the only thing you can criticize about this Cologne from Givenchy. Okay, the sillage and longevity are also poor, that’s true. But that’s it... almost. Because it’s actually just a thin copy of “Dior Homme Cologne” with a splash of “Paco”... Oh man.

After a long time of pondering and testing, I finally purchased a bottle of Gentleman Cologne. It has the characteristic of starting off explosively and then fading away incredibly quickly. It was no different during the testing phase. But I had to have it! It has something that other fragrances don't have. Don't ask me what it is. But there is something there!

The Givenchy Gentleman Cologne is a wonderfully green, fresh fragrance. However, it has that certain note that reminds me of a clinic. Clinically clean, just like the white color of the bottle, one could say. Somehow, I also detect green grass and Petitgrain or something similar. Although none of that is listed. The iris and musk are very restrained.
Due to the fact that this flanker of the new Gentleman Givenchy line is so hard to find, I believe it has been discontinued.

I kept checking the bottle label and sample and Sales Associate to make sure she hadn't mix these samples up! This is very light on the Nutmeg- so if that's what you're after (yeah, sometimes I like a fragrance to just tell me what it is in the name- Nutmeg & Ginger is a Summer sprizter, rather than a piquant spice blend. It is almost undetectable to my nose, which is typical very sensitive and literally begins to burn in the same room with someone wearing a single spritz of Amariage, Christian Dior's Poison or even D&G's the One. Well, this scented water sits on the other side of the galaxy, like a distance planet capable of sustaining life, but not currently interested in sustaining life. This is beyond tepid in its use of Nutmeg and Ginger...it's less gingery than Canada Dry Gingerale and less nutmeggy than a 10 year old nutmeg locked in a bank volt in a remote Inuit village thousands of miles away. What is in this big bottle? Sort of imagine a watered down version of green mandarine, grapefruit, lemon, petitgrain, clove, cinnamon, ginger, pink peppercorns, geranium, lavender- pinch O' wood- i.e "Diptyque's L'eau de L'eau". It is clean, transparent, zesty totally office appropriate, clean- did I mention clean? A unisex citrus splash with a touch of sandalwood in the dry down- which happens approximately 30 minutes after application. And then, the real magic happens- Presto! Et Voila! It completely disappears. Not a bad after shower splash on those hot humid muggy days- but not worth it and not going to fix my nutmeg and ginger addiction at all- I'll stick with "Origins Ginger Essence" for the Summer and Bois 1920's fantastically rich "Sushi Imperiale", Serge Luten's "Five O'clock aux Gingembre" or "Comme des Garçons Original EDP" for my ginger and nutmeg fix, Thanks.

This is one of my least favorite perfumes ever. It should have been perfect - I like all the notes individually. However, on me it had a horrible fakey chemical smell that only reminded me of the deodorizer used in the bathrooms of Greyhound buses here in the U.S.. Not a happy association. I even tried it again because I couldn't believe how bad it was on me, and got the same result. (I've tried other Jo Malones since & this must be a line that just doesn't agree with me, although the others weren't this bad.) I'm mystified & would love to smell it on someone it agrees with. (081809)

In the fall, I was in Ann Arbor. Ann Arbor is a medium-sized city in the Great Lakes state of Michigan, about half an hour west of Detroit, probably the most famous of the once-thriving industrial cities of the Midwest - in a curve from the Great Lakes to the Atlantic coast - which today, after its spectacular decline, they call the 'Rust Belt.' In Ann Arbor, there is no sign of that. Although it was my first time there - so I don't know the other seasons at all - I am sure that it is most beautiful in the fall. In October, hollowed-out pumpkins sit in front of the white and gray-blue painted wooden porches. And because Ann Arbor is a well-known university town, the tree-shaded sidewalks are populated by students with books in their arms - and bearded professors with patches on their elbows. In October, it smells everywhere of Pumpkin Spice, a spice blend of nutmeg and ginger, cinnamon, allspice, and cloves, which is typical for fall in the USA. From every bakery, every café, warm, comforting wafts rise into the street, transforming the city into a kind of surreal Midwest Stars Hollow, where everyone wears red, hand-knit wool scarves and falls into each other's arms while eating Oatmeal Raisin Cookies. Conclusion: this autumn warmth, this idyll, the muted light, and the omnipresence of coziness - all of this is captured by Jo Malone in Nutmeg & Ginger, perhaps THE classic among her fragrances. A scent that tells of steaming breath on coarse wool gloves, of glowing pumpkin faces, and friendly literature professors in worn tweed jackets on the streets of Ann Arbor. Home is where the heart is.

Nutmeg in fragrances always catches my attention. While not always welcome in food, I love the spice even more in perfumes. It often radiates a pleasant, even erotic skin scent. In Nutmeg & Ginger, however, ginger comes first, only slightly spicy, but quite sweet. More like sweetened ginger tea. I also smell lemon, not sour, but beautifully lemony with powdered sugar. The nutmeg is subtle here, but in the most beautiful connection with the other notes. What blows me away and comes completely unexpectedly is a wonderful creaminess. I once had a cream that smelled like this, but unfortunately, I can't recall the name and brand. This scent is so different from what I expected. While ginger-heavy, it has such a creamy, delicately spicy aura that I am completely enchanted. Here, a harmony like no other has emerged from fresh and citrusy notes combined with sweet and powdery nuances, which is simply fantastic. Postscript: When I applied Nivea cream to my hands in the evening and then sniffed the scent again, I became aware of the great similarity. It could therefore be the perfect Nivea scent.

I was on vacation and had planned to check out the Jo Malone fragrances. For this purpose, I had selected three or four scents that I wanted to test. Nutmeg & Ginger was not among them. While testing, the nice lady suggested that I could try this one too, as it is a classic (Jo Malone's first fragrance) and very popular. Well... I thought, let her do her thing; it was too complicated and exhausting for me to explain to her in English what I wanted. Once I smelled the fragrance, it wouldn’t let me go. I walked around on vacation for days. I had to have this scent. And now I have it. A fragrance that can be worn all year round. The scent begins. I cut open a ginger root. The first impression is citrusy. Very citrusy. Then the ginger becomes sharper and more like what one imagines ginger to be. With this image, I can't move forward. The nutmeg softens the sharpness of the ginger and gives the fragrance a slight sweetness. Sweet is the fragrance still far from. The woody base also reveals itself after a while and takes away some of the ethereal freshness of the scent. Throughout, the fragrance remains almost as it was at the beginning. It is only complemented by a few aspects as it develops. The lemony freshness, the sharp herbal-spicy ginger, the sweetish-herbal-spicy nutmeg, and the wood. The freshness lasts until the end.

****** * You can see from this fragrance how different perceptions and preferences can be. I don’t smell any cola, not at all. I also don’t smell any Nivea, zero and nothing. The scent is not sweet for me and not creamy either.

Nutmeg and Ginger Nutmeg and Ginger I don't know who else remembers the old wooden kitchen cabinets with a small door behind which several glass drawers held the spices, two large ones for sugar and salt, and several small ones for other spices, including a whole nutmeg with a mini grater, which was then grated over mashed potatoes, for example.

I am currently in a Jo Malone euphoria, I would love to have all the fragrances (even if it's just 1ml)....really all? No. There is one that I will probably return to, even though it is a brother of my favorites Saffron, Nectarine, Peony, and Dark Amber.
Like Chrisantiss, I perceive a strong resemblance to Nivea cream. I absolutely love this scent. It can be worn without hesitation for any occasion and season.

Ange ou Demon Le Secret is pretty, but not nearly as unique as the original Ange ou Demon. Although not particularly outstanding, this will be widely liked because of its inoffensive, simplistic and safe floral blend. I sense a majority of the notes listed. Peony, jasmine, green tea, soft lemon and white woods are all there, however the patchouli is very mild, not nearly as dominating as I would have liked it to be. Le Secret is sweet but not overly so. The fragrance is very balanced and feminine. It has an almost fresh and clean like quality which I do admire. Overall, the lasting strength and sillage is good, if not better than average. All in all, this is a lovely, soft floral which tends to be shy rather than loud. A very basic yet enjoyable casual scent in my opinion.

Nice run of the mill citrus-floral combo. First notes are lemony, nice and fresh. Then shortly after this fades somewhat and some rich berries poke up their heads. Florals come through in the middle, I am not experienced enough to distinguish one from the other. I don't get much woody upon drying down, just the tiniest hint of patchouli. Very thin and transparent fragrance, although pleasant. Very small sillage & longevity on me. Hardly lasts at all. Pffffft... 20 minutes and it's gone. Very suitable for daytime office wear - banal and light. Kind of boring, I agree with Sherapop.

Fun! Flirty! Soft! Sexy! Opens with an insouciantly festive rush of lemony green tea and ripe juicy cranberries wrapped in translucent veils of fresh jasmine, crisply clean peonies, and dew laden water flowers, all nestled in a tenderly feminine base of sensual white woods, spicy clean patchouli, and sheerest of white musks. Angelic in the lightly sweet, sophisticated opening. Demonic in the deceptively sensual softness of subtle white florals and tender, yet distinctly earthy development of woods, grasses, and musks. No sour acridity from the lemon, no overdone syrupy sugar development in the fruit, no fecalic indoles in the jasmine, no harshness in the wood, no dirt in the patchouli, and no sweat in the musk. On my skin chemistry this is PERFECT. I get the positive attributes from everything in this bottle. Sillage is perfect to my taste and longevity is adequate in my opinion at about 7 hours on my skin. Leisurely sophistication and relaxing, tranquil sensuality in a bottle for me. I am reveling in this! An utterly delightful concoction! I LOVE IT! Thank you Givenchy!

It took me about half my mini to figure out that ANGE OU DEMON LE SECRET is basically a dilute pinkish fruity-floral tea fragrance. Something like Diet Cranberry Snapple. Here are the notes according to Givenchy (sugar is not listed, so I'm assuming it's nutrasweet or sucralose?): top: Italian winter lemon, cranberries, green tea leaf heart: Jasmine, white peony, water flowers base: Blond woods, patchouli Yet another boring flanker. Every bit as inoffensive as it is forgettable.

I received a generous sample of Le Secret EDP from a large online seller. On paper, this is very pleasant fragrance to sample. Tea and citrus come out on on the top, with a bit of cranberry to follow. Overall, Le Secret is a bit sweet without being gourmand, slightly fruity without being fruit-based. However, on my skin, Le Secret wears completely different. The jasmine & lily rear their ugly head, as white florals so often do on me. The white florals cling to the back of my throat and in my sinuses. After 30 minutes I couldn't stand it any more and scrubbed it off. Unfortunately, this has been my experience with most Givenchy scents, notable exceptions being Extravagance, Indecence (original, unreformulated), & Hot Couture (original, unreformulated) - each of which I consider among my favorite fragrances. For those sensitive to certain formulations of white florals, Le Secret is a monster ... not in a good way. Not for me. Not at all. Unwearable.

The tea in this reminds me of a Litpon with lots of lemon and at least two full teaspoons of sugar, or a Long Island Iced Tea. It smells like tropical vacations to exotic beaches, where you sit at the bar in your bikini surrounded by the happy chaos of other beachgoers.

So... the juices from the Ange-ou-Demon line by Givenchy, I must say clearly here, are my absolute favorite fragrances. The "normal," rather sweet-heavy scent in the blue bottle, however, is completely different from this sparkling-fresh variant.

...the sky laughs. And this proverb was the theme today, as the gloomy clouds parted when I made my way to Le Secret. With the first spray, even shy sunbeams dared to come out. The little angel greets me warmly and offers me delicious tart cranberry juice, and, very thoughtfully, a cup of green tea, spiced with a few drops of lemon.

The fragrance starts fresh with a zesty Amalfi lemon.... it creates a perfect harmony with the cool green tea and the bitter-sweet cranberry. The water lily, jasmine, and peony blend gently, adding a touch of unobtrusive femininity to the scent, while the base note offers a modest dose of patchouli and light woods.

Ange ou Démon Le Secret was gifted to me. At first, I was skeptical; I prefer to choose my fragrances myself. My perfume collection is large, and my wish and note list is long; I probably would have never encountered this scent. I take a beautiful long walk with the dogs, of course, as they are always with me. It is a very warm afternoon.

I've only recently delved into the house of Jo Malone, and from what I've experienced so far, I'm impressed. Many dislike the simplistic nature of these colognes, and as a result, Jo Malone has been discussed frequently on our forums as not being worth the money spent. I agree that they can put a dent in your pocket, but I do enjoy them for layering purposes or even to spritz on when I don't want anything too loud or offensive. Amber & Lavender is a charming unisex fragrance. It opens slightly masculine, with rich aromatic qualities and a heavy dose of lavender. I love lavender and often use it for soothing purposes. I'm also one of the rare few that find the smell of it rather seductive and alluring. It's not all about the lavender of course, but it does feature strongly, particularly in the opening and the heart. I absolutely love the way Amber & Lavender settles on my skin; aromatic yet oddly clean. It's refreshing at the best of times and very easy to wear. There's a glorious, subtle hint of mint that really freshens up the composition, also making it suitable for the warmer months. Although I would prefer this fragrance on a chilly day, the options are endless as it's a fairly versatile scent. The amber accord isn't syrupy nor outrageously oriental like you may expect it to be. Every note in this fragrance is quite mellow and smooth. Patchouli and myrrh only add to this fragrance's beauty. Another wonderful thing about Amber & Lavender is that it lasts. This can't be said of every Jo Malone fragrance, so I consider it a big plus. I'm surprised that this fragrance isn't more popular. I can only assume that women may forgo this fragrance thinking that it is only intended to be worn by men. I personally think it could go both ways. You'll either buy it for yourself or for your partner.

Opens bright with lavender and soap. Continues to wear somewhat medicinal and clean. This feels like an old idea of a clean scent, aristocratic cleanliness, it's what you might have expected classic fragrances from Penhaligon's, Geo. F. Trumper, truefitt + Hill, Floris, et al. were supposed to smell like, but don't. This does.

Somewhere I read or heard, probably in Hamburg at the Jo Malone store, that these fragrances are those with clear statements. What’s in the name is right there in front. On the Jo Malone website, the description mentions only lavender and amber alongside petitgrain. The other details above come from an article from another source, yet they seem plausible. I came to basil myself, for example. Right after applying, I initially thought of fuzzy, unripe bergamot, but after a short moment, petitgrain actually seems more coherent; the citrus note is darker and heftier, also oilier than bergamot usually is. Still, a bergamot impression is not completely out of place. So far, so good; so moving on, so hm. I fear the combination of lavender and eugenol does not work at all on my skin. Lavender alone is often problematic enough, and to add that biting ingredient, which primarily resides in cloves but also lurks in nutmeg and some cinnamon… Oh dear! For hours, the matter oscillates back and forth, hence the idea of the daisy, with which I can pluck petals in the old-fashioned "He loves me…he loves me not…" manner between "It stinks" and "It doesn’t stink." Throughout the morning, the already diagnosed aftershave quality by the previous commentator emerges, which could indeed be called "quite classic," yet remains airier and spritzier than what grandpa’s waters allowed according to my childhood memories. I’m sure it’s a great thing for fans of classic fragrances to be served in such a light-footed manner. Amber takes over in the second half. As the fragrance has darkened a bit by noon, its appearance can now be described as "pretty classic." In style, it reminds me of Elite by Floris, which I find more consistent, fuller, and rounder. I certainly wouldn’t buy it today either. Yes, perhaps that’s the best comparison that comes to mind for me as a self-proclaimed non-expert in this fragrance direction. The final touch is provided by the gradual fade of Amber & Lavender throughout the afternoon. I sense musk there, which not only shows a similar character but also has a calm yet confident presence. Conclusion: It seems extraordinarily British to me. A recommendation for fans of such designed fragrances. I find it a bit boring and intermittently not very pleasant. I thank MisterE for the sample.

How I rejoiced when I unexpectedly uncovered the small sample of Amber & Lavender from the large brown envelope. I love the components included: amber, lavender, bergamot, myrrh, and patchouli; just thinking about these beautiful notes makes me want to roll my eyes in delight. Based on the fragrance pyramid, I anticipated a fresh, herbaceous-citrusy start, already underlined by warm notes of cinnamon, a hint of clove, and perhaps even a hint of amber and myrrh. My expectations for this scent were so high... ... and just as deep was the fall of disappointment after spraying it on. The top note was nearly pure biting alcohol, soon accompanied by a sharp, spicy clove note. The lavender then added a slightly herbal-medical flair reminiscent of cheap aftershave... But I remained patient; the warm notes from the base components had to come at some point... But no, even after 2 hours, there was still nothing to smell from them, although the aftershave stench thankfully began to fade. Well, I thought, maybe it doesn’t suit your skin chemistry... so I borrowed my sweetheart's arm as a scent carrier: with exactly the same result. And my sweetheart wrinkled their nose in disgust and went to wash their arm... Okay, I thought, the sample might be off, so I noted it on my testing list. What can I say? Even in the perfumery tester, it was the same result. Amber & Lavender can stay where the pepper grows... it’s not coming near my skin again, that stinker!!!

For some time now, I have been eager to test Jo Malone fragrances and I was lucky enough to enjoy my first sniff, and I am thrilled. I generally don't like lavender, but here it doesn't bother me at all. Especially bergamot and amber are clearly recognizable, with the lavender being very subtle and not intrusive. I find the scent on my skin wonderfully gentle and warm, but very masculine, in my opinion. This is how a man should smell... elegant :D My husband also said it smells great... is that aftershave *laugh*

For those who are interested in what the fragrance water smells like, there is only one word: Lush. My sister gifted me Amber & Lavender for Christmas. That means you could say it was a blind buy for me :D At first, I was very skeptical about the scent, as I consider Jo Malone fragrances to be the expensive version of toilet sprays or deodorants.

... of scents was presented to me today in my fragrance oasis - and I had the agony of choice. Burberrys always score points with me, so I also tried My Burberry EDT. The scent greeted me with a friendly "Hello," crowned with lemon blossom and entwined with beautiful sweet pea - but then it first wrapped itself in silence. My dear husband was present, and he demands quick decisions. Meanwhile, My Burberry celebrates British calmness - and takes its time. Once we had long left the store, the peony and freesia spoke up eloquently - and really getting into the swing of things, the full rose and soft moss entered the scene. If I had waited an hour, it would have certainly made it to the shortlist - because its development is remarkably beautiful. Good things come to those who wait - and so does the scent.

Do you know that feeling when you discover a bottle in a perfume shop, find it beautiful, and think: Wow, if the bottle looks this nice, how amazing must the scent be?! Well, if you know a bit about perfumes, you realize: The content doesn’t have to be anything special. Some scents come in incredibly ugly or very plain bottles and smell fantastic, while others are in beautiful bottles and smell awful. Unfortunately, this is the case with this Burberry. The bottle with the lovely bow and the large, heavy cap certainly looks impressive, but it smells like the rose soap on my grandmother's sink. Actually, it's even worse - My Burberry doesn’t develop softly and soothingly on me, as is sometimes the case with rose, but starts to sting and gives me a headache. Such a shame, because peony and peach blossom are exactly my thing! In the end, My Burberry doesn’t smell elegant or luxurious on me at all, but rather like a cheap drugstore fragrance. Sorry, I just can't find anything to appreciate about it!

I just between time to time when I want to buy a new, unknown perfume, I come here to see what the community is writing on specific perfume that I heared is good and worth to try. However, this is not the case today due to the low rating for this product. Before a while, I used just to follow the blind technique, buy it, and judge it by using your smelling preference. One of the perfumes that I bought with that technique, was the Givenchy pour homme, and I cannot tell you how I was lucky ( by the way it's something rare ). The scent is something unique, you will identify it easly if you smell it in the street, old fashion, mature, not for the millennials. Start with strong woody-Fresh smell, then everything be quite with the Fruity scent. The longevity is above average, I am unfortunately smoker, even thou, I still smell the perfume on me after 5-6 hours. Highly recommend it if you are searching for special scent.

My preconceived notions about Givenchy pour homme came from other reviews. Apparently this is a spicy, woody, fresh fragrance that is dated and more suited to the 35+ crowd (I'm 35). The way people were describing it made it sound like Old Spice aftershave. Upon first spray in the opening, this is NOT Old Spice. In fact, this is barely spiced at all, at least to my nose. I have an earlier version of the bottle with the built-in atomizer and the candy-red painted plastic piece on top. So what was I smelling? Effervescent, sparkling, cool ginger fizz. I guess ginger is a spice--just not the type kept in a spice cabinet. I'm not sure how ginger isn't listed on the note breakdown. It may be that the combination of coriander, lavender and grapefruit/mandarin is combining in a way that creates a ginger accord to my nose (like a slightly spiced, bubbly citrus). The woodiness is also toned down here, but present. Strangely enough, to my nose, this fragrance has less woodiness than something like Light Blue Summer Vibes (another Morillas concoction). I'm not sure if it's because of my batch or because of the fragrance itself. The woodiness is sort of in there hidden behind the bubbly ginger fizz and a bit of sweetness from the labdanum. So is this an outdated fragrance? No. It's actually incredibly modern, like many of Alberto Morillas' creations. It's refreshing, light, like a cool tonic water mixed with crushed ginger and a tiny dash of simple syrup. Givenchy pour homme would appeal to anyone that enjoys these types of fresh, cool fragrances. I live in a Mediterranean climate so these types of fragrances done right will always appeal to me. Maybe it's the incredibly young men who are just discovering fragrance for the first time that are calling this "old man spicy". Perhaps, compared to Invictus, Nitro Red, BR 540, sure. But this fragrance is also not old-school masculine like an 80's and early 90's aromatic fougère, nor is it in-your-face old school like YSL Kouros. I sort of put it in the same category as Tygar, as weird as that sounds. It's definitely a unique fragrance if you can get past the fact that it's not overpoweringly strong. I know a lot of noses out there need highly volatile scent molecules to sense what is going on. But, if you can get past the humble strength, there is a lot to love about this fizzy fragrance. It successfully straddles the line between cool and warm. This would work great in almost any situation--even in the most crowded of elevators and subway cars. 7.5/10

I bought a full bottle for $33 from Jomashop without testing a sample at home. It was not a completely blind buy as I had tested it while passing through London Heathrow Airport. When I sprayed it on my hand in the duty free airport boutique, it felt spicy and medicinal, but pleasant. When I tried the full bottle at home, it still felt medicinal but rather unpleasant. Vetiver, cedar and labdanum (?) are all pushed to the front and it doesn’t create a good feeling. I really couldn’t see much development in the notes. This combination might have worked two decades ago, but we have much better perfumes now. In addition, Givenchy Pour Homme comes in a very odd-looking bottle. Fortunately, I was able to send it back to the seller and get a refund. It is just too much and too little at the same time. Don't buy it simply because it is cheap.

A well-groomed scent, I must say. The longevity is also relatively good for me, lasting 7 to 8 hours. I find the fragrance works best in the office. You always smell like freshly ironed clothes; I know the same from Bvlgari Homme, but here it is even more pronounced and not as synthetic as with Bvlgari. I don't even know where this comes from; amber is often responsible for this "ironed freshness," but it doesn't appear in the scent progression here. Maybe it's the labdanum? What is that, actually? Does anyone know? Well, I like it very much and always feel very comfortable with the scent!

I love this scent!! It’s just perfect for summer. I had it back when I was 18, and now I have it again at 31 :-) I can only recommend it. It suits almost every occasion. It smells citrusy, elegant, and subtle. It really lasts a long time.

Price: mid-range; I paid €22 for 30ml Season: Fresh enough for summer, but the warm base is also suitable for winter Suitability: as it has a classic touch, a good scent for work, also okay for going out, as it is fresh and long-lasting Age: Givenchy recommends the fragrance "for the gentleman from 25 years old.

I received it as a miniature and was initially pleased with the bottle, as the eye is known to eat with the nose. Then I applied it and was very positively surprised by the scent - my wife even more than I was.

Givenchy has passed me by for quite a while among the fragrance labels, but since I have owned the "pour homme" in the red version since Christmas, I would like to give it a comment now. The fruity top note, where I perceive more grapefruit and less mandarin, can hardly put anyone off. Fresh, very pleasing, very pleasant.

What a bottle...a dream, from the spray head to the craftsmanship, it deserves my highest rating and immediately caught my attention for testing...and since I have hardly tested anything apart from Gentleman and Pi by Givenchy, this comes in handy...if only the scent were half as strong, it would make its way into my collection...

Maulwurf84 has already described the fragrance very well. So I will just add a few remarks. Givenchy pour Homme is an exceedingly pleasant, rather summery scent. It doesn’t match at all with the opulent design of the bottle. For me, a rather soft mandarin is dominant here. Everything else seems to literally dissolve into thin air on my skin.

I actually don't like this, at all. Burberry is my favourite fragrance house, however with this new release I am rather underwhelmed. It smells synthetic to my nose, a little rubbery like the bottle it comes in. It's true that it smells like D&G Light Blue, which I don't even care for, however, (I can't believe I'm saying this), I'd choose Light Blue over Burberry Sport any day. Salty plastic is all I can smell in the opening. The mandarin orange barely features in my opinion. The scent tends to become more aquatic as it develops into the heart. The honeysuckle and Carribean magnolia aren't as floral as I had expected. They seem to be un-naturally sweet. Musk overwhelms me into the drydown. There's too much of it for my personal tastes. Burberry Sport ended on a headache for me unfortunately. The lasting power is incredibly good, as most Burberry scents are. I am extremely disappointed however that I have come across a Burberry fragrance that I don't enjoy, which was something I thought was never possible until today.

Since Rossi is located opposite the DHL shop, I thought I might as well stop by for a sniff. The newspaper had announced Burberry Sport as a special offer, and I had never gone wrong with Burberrys before. So I decided to take a whiff. I expected something fresh and invigorating - but I am confused. I am greeted by a dull laundry detergent note reminiscent of Weißer Riese, with a hint of stain remover added. Does the cardboard strip distort the scent? So I bravely applied it to my skin. No, the impression remains biting and soapy, with a salty background. With good will, I can still detect a hint of mandarin, but the rest of the ingredients get lost in a kind of lye. This scent does not call me to engage in sports activities - if anything, then to do the "big laundry". I echo Churchill's words - no sports. P.S. Or was the tester old?

The first whiff was already disastrous: it bites the nose. Or did I just think I smelled the salt that is supposed to be in the top note? After 5 minutes: much better & somehow interesting (but why do I think: "man"). The conclusion after an intense sniffing session clarifies everything: too harsh, hard, powerful, and above all too masculine. I find that Burberry Sport exudes an aura of masculinity, especially at the beginning, which fades more and more over time, but the first impression just won't leave me (I really have the "For Woman" tester in my hand :-D). Nothing against powerful women's fragrances - quite the opposite - but for my taste, I would prefer something more oriental and sensual or heavily sweet. This is simply not the kind of fragrance I like, and Burberry & I have unfortunately never clicked.

It's quite funny and also very unique what everyone associates with individual scents. My friend and I once had the glorious idea to plan a spontaneous trip to Texas. We are both big fans of the USA and of course also "experts" on the USA ;) We did this in August.... Well, exactly in August! In the hottest month of the year with daytime temperatures over 40 degrees and sometimes 80% humidity. We drove for days through the dust-dry desert to finally reach the Gulf of Mexico and breathe in the fresh sea air... We were sweating from every pore, but when we arrived, everything was forgotten and only that moment at the sea mattered. And this moment is exactly what this perfume represents for me. It starts with a strong and powdery dryness... I can clearly smell the salty note, but for me, this note makes the perfume very unique. I really don't understand what this scent has to do with sports. For me, sport fragrances are very fresh and lightly fruity.... This one is not fresh at all. It also reminds me a bit of a less creamy version of Burberry Beat... Because some fragrance notes are indeed very similar to me.

Well... uh... here it is... *sniff* ... yes... hm... *sniff again* ... hm... yes... um... *???* I could go on like this indefinitely, but it wouldn't help anyone. So I’ll try to put my impressions into a bit more words than just points: To me, it absolutely does not smell like a sport fragrance. Especially not for a woman, I completely agree with Blanche on that. For a man, however, it feels way too floral. Who wants to have a spring bouquet with muscles and leg warmers running beside them... oO Not me! The problem lies in the fragrance notes - or rather their chosen direction and dosage: the mandarin is more sweet-sticky than zesty-fresh, and the salt is non-existent. The heart note is not perceivable individually and comes across as floral, dominating everything. In the dry down, you can smell musk, but only with a bit of imagination. And then there’s supposed to be cedarwood, but where??? Maybe you have to be sporty to like this scent. Maybe you have to be sporty to understand this scent. I, on the other hand, just can't warm up to this fragrance and have to rely on the old warm-up. I'd rather run a marathon than buy this scent. Sorry.

Hello everyone, You've been with us for over 12 years and my wife still likes you... You dear Sport for Women are not the best fragrance, you don't have fantastic performance and you certainly don't shine with the HIGH QUALITY of the fragrance oils used. But we still like you... I can't really say why exactly... It's intriguing for sure!

BS is a wonderfully uncomplicated, brilliantly light, zesty summer fragrance! Unfortunately, summer is taking its sweet time this year, and it's already fun to sweeten the anticipation a bit with this lovely perfume...

Burberry Sport smells to me exactly like Fa shower gel. This has never happened to me with any other fragrance so far. Fresh artificial mandarins in the opening, something salty tickles the nose (the only thing not found in the shower gel). The heart note reinforces the shower gel impression again. Honeysuckle and magnolia smell very light and fresh.

I tried this for the first time when I was in a local department store. I had wanted to test it for as long as it has been around. The minute I see the word "noir" in a perfume, the old goth in me immediately wants to try it! To start with I was encouraged by what I smelt. Floral, sweet and slightly juicy. Not what I imagined from something "noir" but it was very pretty all the same. I was tempted to buy it, but my other half was with me and dragged me away from the counter before I spent even more money on perfumes. I let him smell it on me and his first reaction was that it was "headache inducing flowers". I am always disappointed when he doesn't like a perfume because I feel I can't wear it around him. However, I hoped that it would improve and that my partner may, in the end, like it. Soon I thought I smelt something dirty around me. I realised it was the perfume when I smelt my hand again. Oh no, bad patchouli. I'm not a great fan of patchouli because, in my opinion, it is done so badly in so many perfumes and, unfortunately, this appeared to be one. However, iris is a note that I usually always love, but here it smelt very artificial and harsh. My other half said it smelt like toilet cleaner! So far I had lost the pretty opening and was left with dirty, harsh patchouli and artificial iris. I loath giving bad reviews to a perfume as everything is subjective, but I really can't be positive about Dahlia Noir. I love Givenchy so was very surprised by this fragrance. Even if I don't like a perfume, like Organza, I couldn't ever say that it was horrible, it just isn't to my taste. But Dahlia Noir, oh my, it's just not very nice at all. I'm grateful to my partner now that he didn't let me buy it!

I got a couple of samples of this because the notes sound luscious. The first few minutes had a bit of orange and a bit of powdery green mimosa, so I was expecting good things. However, at about 5 minutes, it dried down into something more like an inexpensive toiletry and stayed there. I would say that this smells like something in between Nivea Creme and baby wipes. Not an experience I'm eager to repeat.

Dahlia Noir (EDP) opens brightly with juicy orange and fresh mimosa, then swiftly becomes predominantly musky. A subtly sensuous, powdery, salty "clean skin" vanillic musk, with a smooth, buttery iris, providing a delectable backdrop for moist, crisp pink rose petals. At times I'm reminded of Astral body cream - the one in the big blue tub. If I had to compare this to another scent, I'd describe Dahlia Noir (EDP) as a modernized, fresher, zesty, creamier, far less suffocatingly sweet take on/version of Ombre Rose. (I personally find Ombre Rose to be somewhat smothering, too strong, too sweet, too linear, and a little bit (DARE I SAY?) dated. At times I can appreciate it, sometimes love it, but overall I'm far fonder of the fresher, zestier Dahlia Noir!) It's like taking a snooze after indulging in a whole tub of vanilla ice cream with honey drizzled all over it. Dahlia Noir (EDP) puts me in mind of clean, moist skin with a delicate layer of oil/sweat. I find this scent comforting and refreshing. A nice "pick-me-up" for days/evenings when you're in the mood for something a little more natural smelling. My best friend says it smells like dill. Strange but true, and I'm inclined to agree! Easy to over-spray, so beware; it's really not required. Better to top up in a few hours than to over-apply. Keep it low-key. It has relatively good lasting power (up to 8 hours on my skin), projects to arm length (with only a couple of sprays), and becomes skin-close after around 3-4 hours. (February 22nd, 2015)

Dahlia Noir is well blended?feels like chiffon. I can smell iris, pepper, orange, mimose and sandalwood. However, neither of them is overpowering. It's a powdery floral scent with a delicate sweetness. I think it works well in the three warmer seasons. It's tender and inoffensive, suitable for daily use in office. The sillage is pretty close to skin, the longevity is around 6h on me. Overall I like it, but do not yet have enough desire to own a full bottle. The bottle suits the fragrance well. The ad campaign is ok if focusing on the tenderness illustrated by the fluctuation of the chiffon. It's not the sort of mysterious powerful gothic "noir", that's for sure. However, it has a slight melancholic vibe. But still, I'm not fond of the name as it makes me think of something unpleasant. I agree with cedriceccentric, that something "Poudré" as name might be better. Originally written in 2013

Scentrack: Moloko – I Want You In my opinion Givenchy is one of the greatest fashion houses ever. However, many of their fragrance releases in this millennium were unworthy of this historical name. Dahlia Noir, created by Francois Demachy of Dior, gives a hope that Givenchy got it right. Personally, I really like Dahlia Noir EdP. It is elegant and modern, yet reserved with hidden old time grandiosity. Dahlia Noir opens with an unusually fresh burst of mandarin, accompanied by short-lived berrylike accord similar to Guerlain’s La Petite Robe Noire. Among this fruit interplay, one could sense some perfectly tweaked peppery and powdery nuances. After initial fruity playfulness, Dahlia gradually morphs into a flowery heart of iris and rose. The iris note is rather fresh, juxtaposed to damascone rose of both floral and jam-like aspects. This jam-like aspect is a perfect introduction to sweeter and almost gourmand base. Like every other part of the composition, the base is again very skillfully tweaked. Tonka bean, vanilla and woody notes are very carefully arranged to give a contemporary feminine touch to the composition. Dahlia Noir is a perfect example of hybrid contemporary-classic chimeras. All the contemporary aspects are skillfully paired to classical thoughtfulness by the perfumer. Very nice for professional environment, dinner or theatre due to its duality. Simply, a beautiful and well balanced creation that successfully avoids all the traps of modern vulgarity. Almost gourmand, yet classical. Almost unisex, yet so distinctively feminine. A beautiful work.

The fragrance Dahlia Noir by Givenchy reminds me of the country singer k.d.lang. 1. She plays a small role in the film The Black Dahlia (2006) by Brian de Palma and 2. the scent is like her music. Bittersweet, passionate, dramatic.

What on earth was the marketing department of Givenchy thinking when it came to naming this fragrance? Me!! By some coincidence, I let all the staff with gardening experience be on summer vacation at the same time, leaving only the nerdy shadow beings to discuss which flower had yet to be marketed with the attribute "black.

My grandfather had two green thumbs, and accordingly, his garden was a feast for the eyes. Not only did I admire the floral splendor that thrived in his refuge, but the entire neighborhood also openly acknowledged his paradise. Alongside his proud roses, I was drawn to his multicolored dahlias. Among them, I found the black ones to be an unusual gem.

Hey hey folks, how are you doing? I hope well, right? The weather is getting nicer again and people (especially the ladies) are becoming more revealing and… argh… okay okay, I swear on my honor: When I’m in a relationship, I’ll write less of such things… at least I assume so, but I can’t PROMISE anything,...

When I think of Black Dahlia, I involuntarily think of Glasgow Smile and Elizabeth Short. The latter was murdered in L.A. in 1947. Because of her beauty, she was named after the flower "Black Dahlia". But now let's talk about one of my favorites - Dahlia Noir by Givenchy! I’m not really good at describing scents.

All hail the The World's Most Okayist Fragrance! Alright, well, that's rude of me. But honestly, this is a perfume with lots of VOLUME yet nothing of substance to say. It's a brick wall of neon, magenta strawberry along with ambroxan. It's fun for a few minutes, but doesn't develop. I have nothing more to add, I'm merely tacking on some additional wordage to meet the review minimum. Typically my reviews are long-ish, but this perfume didn't inspire me to yammer on, which is case-in-point.

I love this one, way superior than Elixir. This is what I wanted elixir to smells like, a creamy fruity strawberry. I still think it has that "cloud" by ariana grande DNA but a better version this time, because of the sweetness and bright fruits! In my opinion this one is literally more feminine, sweet and fluffy. If you hated the sharpness in elixir, this one is better.

Man, where to begin? There's darkness that comes from the black leather, booze and castoreum notes but what I think draws the younger crowd and women is the vanilla, clary sage and sugar cane. If you've been collecting scents for a while you know the big negative mark with Varvatos scents is the lack of projection and short longevity. Dark Rebel may not be the boldest and longest lasting male fragrance but compared to its predecessors from this house this release is pretty good. In the world of perfumery it seems that oud is the big note right now, quite often it seems to pop up where you least expect it, though there is none here this Varvatos scent's dark start on my skin has me thinking of that note. Such a great concoction of many notes, what I think bridges the dark and sweet/greenish notes is the tobacco, definitely evening wear and for cooler temps. Impressive and not ridiculously expensive. This and Platinum from this house really stand out.

"What is that smell?" "Ah, is the smell of the beast that is London," he said. "Best prepare yourself, my lady. On a warm day such as this, the odour does not improve." His words were, unfortunately, prophetic. Still, the smell was not as overwhelming as she had feared it might become and not all of the elements that made up. - The Dark Knight, Elisabeth Elliot. Luckily, John Varvatos Dark Rebel is anything but a bad smell, packaged in a very bold, elegant, and unique way. The cap bears the exclusive JV mark embossed with an impressive silver Fleur de Lis, while a twisted rubber thread wraps the bright black bottle in rebellious fashion. When I first encountered this cologne, I knew immediately that I was drawn to it. What makes this fragrance truly exceptional? I cannot pinpoint a singular element, but after wearing it multiple times, I've discovered its mysteriously captivating appeal. Allow me to share my personal journey with this remarkable scent. JVDR opens with an intoxicating blast of boozy sugarcane rum, reminiscent of a well-crafted daiquiri, followed by an undertone of spicy cardamom and aromatic sage—the latter gradually becoming more dominant. Though lacking zesty notes, the opening remains surprisingly fresh, medicinal, warm, and balsamic. The spice journey continues as black pepper and beautiful nutmeg provide a seamless transition to the leather accord at the heart. Every black leather jacket I've owned carries this same distinctive smell—animalic with a touch of oiliness. The snapdragon's presence adds a darker jasmine-like quality and introduces a slight edge of danger. This particular aspect evokes the Dark Knight reference—it embodies the very essence I imagine when contemplating that character. The leather, made black and intensely dark through the masterful use of fir and styrax, establishes the fragrance's primary accord. The base reveals a lovely golden tobacco, expertly roughened by woody notes and the innovative Akigalawood—a softer version of patchouli with reduced earthiness and enhanced herbal and spicy facets. Both vanilla and cedar contribute creamy and buttery dimensions, creating a warm and enveloping dry down. This aromatic masterpiece blends boozy, woodsy, and smoky notes into a decidedly masculine composition that exudes mystery and excitement—highly provocative and bold without becoming overwhelming. Its longevity is exceptional, persisting for several hours, while the sillage makes a confident statement. JVDR is perfectly suited for nighttime wear and special occasions, whether you're embarking on a romantic evening or commanding attention in a business setting. The sophisticated arrangement of notes suggests this is a cold-weather companion, ideal from late autumn through early spring. -Elysium

Longevity and projection are always connected to this line, but I enjoy the John Varvatos line for the exact opposite reason that it gets heavily criticized - I don’t need my fragrance to create a scent bubble a 1/4 mile out while continuing to pound off me for 12 hours. For $30 bucks if it isn’t a synthetic mess and smells good then frag on baby. If I need 6-8 sprays then so be it. Dark Rebel reminds me of a more tobacco smoke forward Halston Z-14. It has a mild cinnamon sweetness in the heart and leather in the base. Z-14 is more complex, but the vibe is similar overall. 3.5 stars

I received a sample of this not knowing what it was, and ended up liking so much that I ordered a full bottle. Dirty boozy opening that settles down into a mix of tobacco and a campfire. This is nice for summer nights, and though I haven't yet owned it during a fall season, I imagine it will be perfect once that comes around. I'll have to give it a few more wears before coming back to rate its longevity.

JV Dark Rebel is probably one of the best releases from the whole house. This is the fragrance that would be worn by Killian Jones from Once Upon a Time. Notes of rum, sugar cane, leather, pepper, and tobacco conjure imagery of swashbuckling on the Jolly Roger. There is a note of castoreum in the base that gives this fragrance just a little bit of skank, but not nearly enough to call this challenging. Unfortunately Black Rebel suffers the same affliction that all JV fragrance suffer from. It lasts two to three hours before it is hardly noticeable. The bottle is one of the coolest I’ve seen with its leather wrapping and the cap with its fleur de lis. It matches the scent of the juice perfectly. Since JV is no longer producing fragrances, and this was arguably their best, it can only be found on resale sites these days. And you can expect to pay anywhere from $60 to $100 for a 2.5 oz bottle. I expect those prices will continue to creep up.

... if only this one could last me a few more hours... it kills me, these gorgeous leathery tones that fade away after a few hours... this guy has a signature to his style, he just runs and hides after parading around so loudly in the beginning...

They called him tough Joe. Everywhere in Perfume Land, he was known as the dark rebel in the leather jacket. As a rough fellow, he often had a bottle of rum at his lips. Here he indulged himself, and each time he "drank," he soiled his jacket anew, so that the leather always had a union with the rum.
