Amazing fragrance, Elegant, Classy , Sophisticated and Unique. It smells so good and very pleasant with reasonable price. One of the best men's perfumes. It opens up with like fresh spicy fruity, green and leather notes in the background then dry down is ambery, leathery, woody. This is a modern perfume with well-blended composition and perfect for the spring, fall and winter. I really enjoy it and I love a scent that can make memories come alive. I'm so happy that I have it in my collection. Longevity is good, Highly Recommended. Two Thumbs Up. Rating : 8.5 / 10

John Varvatos is a smooth, masculine fragrance. It's fairly inoffensive on the skin despite having an array of unique and bold ingredients. At times, John Varvatos can smell a little dark and broody. It's definitely a cold weather, night-time scent. This fragrance has quite an attitude without being too 'in your face'. John Varvatos opens with some pepper, lime and sweet plum, before settling into a mild leather and spice blend. The drydown can be rather powdery on the skin, but pleasantly so. I can detect a soft cedar note with rich amber. The plum and fig notes don't really add a fruity feel to this composition at all. They contribute to the fragrance's overall sweetness and warmth, but never detract from the masculine woods, spices and leather. From a female's perspective, John Varvatos is both approachable and sensual. Due to its subdued sillage, it would make a great gift for someone who prefers their fragrances soft, leathery and masculine. I believe that John Varvatos is fairly affordable overseas. This is not the case in Australian department stores. Over here it bears a fairly high price tag. To fellow Aussies, I suggest looking for cheaper options online. Original review written: April 2013.

Wow, I didn't expect that! A few weeks ago (and I still am) I was absolutely thrilled by Donna Karan's first men's fragrance "DK Men" or "Fuel For Men" and thought that its scent combination is absolutely unique.

Recently, I met my wife in a shopping arcade in Nuremberg. Since there was still some time, I took a seat on a bench and let my thoughts and gaze wander. I openly admit: Occasionally, I enjoy observing other people. While the colorful hustle and bustle unfolded before me, a peculiar thought made its way into my consciousness. What if I were to encounter myself?

how top-notch this little water is. Because then the moment would have come when I would consider leaving it on my skin. But let's start from the beginning... Somewhere while browsing the WWW, I discovered the fragrances of J.V. Immediately, I informed myself about them and read a bit about the fragrance world of J.V.

To be honest, I can hardly pick anything out from the fragrance pyramid. Yes, this JV really does smell like grape sugar. A bit tangy, as if it were blackcurrant or something similar. It could also easily pass as a pepper scent. A rather rare fragrance composition, but very interesting and truly successful. Best suited for spring & summer.

It's time to really champion John Varvatos, because the 3 fragrances I know from him (Vintage, Artisan, and this one) are all top-notch, interesting, sweet, and delicious. This syrup-like scent combines Vintage and the original; Vintage feels a bit more mature and not quite as sweet. Artisan is completely different and a citrusy representative for the hammock and summer.

Burberry Brit Summer may have a similar scent pyramid to that of the original, but I can't say that they smell exactly alike. I much prefer this Summer flanker. It's softer, fresher and fruitier. Anyone that follows my reviews, will know that I don't usually enjoy fruity fragrances. There are only a few fruit notes that I like, and pear and lime are two of them. These two notes, when blended together, create a scent that is sweet, green, juicy, soft and feminine. Thankfully nothing in this fragrance comes across as being too overbearing. Brit Summer is a really delicate fragrance. It is far more subdued than the original Brit, which often turned sharp on my skin. I would most definitely reach for this flanker during Summer. The heart is well balanced with sweet, mashed pears, green lime, soapy peony and sugared almonds. It's almost a gourmand, however I'd describe it as being more crisp and clean. The musky drydown is even more pleasant, striking me as being rather sensual and soothing. If only this Summer flanker wasn't a limited edition. It's one of my pet peeves when brands discontinue limited edition flankers, especially when they smell better than the originals. The sillage of Brit Summer is fairly light and inoffensive. The lasting strength could have been better, but it's certainly not disappointing. My word to the wise is to go out and test this flanker as soon as possible. I fear that its existence will be short-lived. Original review written: September 2012.

I love the original Burberry Brit EdP, but this one is quickly becoming a favorite. Burberry Brit Summer is similar to her mother; but it is lighter, fresher, and with an added tea note. The tea tones down the almond and mahogany, both notes that made the original Brit a little sharp around the edges. Lime and iced pear are more prominent here as well. My mind is playing tricks on me because I smell a pinch of cinnamon, but I may be confusing it for something else.

It doesn't always have to be citrus! And not always "ocean breeze"! That's the motto. Various nuts, fruits, and herbs can also contribute to enjoying a fragrant summer. Perfectly suitable for hot temperatures. Here it shows its slightly cool-rough side! And has a strong "cool-wind note"! Even in cooler weather, it can be worn just as well. The scent then tends to lean towards the warmer, slightly woody side, which also lifts the spirits. The delicate, light pink peony evokes a mild summer evening enriched with floral scents, enticing you to spend it outdoors on the balcony, terrace, or in the garden. Everything has a slightly bitter "retro note" reminiscent of fragrances from the 70s. An Eau de Rochas (1970) Eau de Toilette or an "Ô de Lancôme" could be mentioned as examples, even though they have a different basic concept. The longevity is actually better (at least for me) than rated above. And you are always surrounded by a "bittersweet hint of summer"! Better than initially thought! ;-))

I hadn't known Burberry before. And while searching for a new summer fragrance, I came across this one. Do you know that feeling? You spray it on and are instantly head over heels! That’s rare, especially since fragrances usually take time to develop... But this was love at first sniff. Completely different from so many summer scents - which always come off as overly fresh and aquatic - this one has that certain something: initially slightly citrusy, it gradually becomes pleasantly warm and envelops you beautifully - but WITHOUT being too sweet or heavy, with the lime making occasional appearances. It lasts all day and is truly a great alternative when you're looking for something different for summer!

Givenchy III dates back to the 70s, it has been available again as part of the re-edition-scheme since 2008. Givenchy III is probably one of the best green chypres with head-notes of lily-of-the valley, rose, jasmin and galbanum. The heart is woody, with santal and oakmoss. I love this fragrance from its beautiful topnotes to the drydown, which seems to contain a bit of patchouli, incense, citrus. Obviously the idea behind Givenchy III was to create a very fresh perfume based on a flowery, but green accord. I think it is a dynamic scent, uplifting, versatile scent, suitable for all occasions. The re-edition does not last as long as the original and contains less galbanum and less oakmoss, but I still prefer it to countless new releases on the market. My vintage Givenchy III is one of my most precious bottles - contentswise. I even keep it in my fridge.

Galbanum glorious galbanum! GIVENCHY III is one of a cluster of 1970s-era floral-chypre perfumes with a classic structure and line-up of notes. The scrumptious galbanum is green and waxy and chewy and just sharp enough. The oakmoss offers a gray and slightly dirty contrast. The iris, rose, and narcissus keep the whole composition from being too dark and depressing. This is an utterly beautiful creation. Perfumes such as GIVENCHY III are the ones which keep me a believer in perfumery as an art, not just another luxury business or crass mass-market cash cow. What I'm not sure about is whether GIVENCHY III is better than the other floral chypres of this type launched about the same time. I love them all! I am testing the vintage GIVENCHY III and have no idea how the reformulation came out, though I'm not all that optimistic.

I don't know about you, but for me the most mysterious and enthralling place in the house I grew up, was always my mother's chiffonier. Everything on it looked like it came straight from a fairy tale, or from the far-flung palaces of the Far East. Especially the small collection of her perfumes. I was totally convinced there was a genie living in one of the bottles, waiting to grant my wish and make me a grown-up in no time. All I had to do was finding out in which one it dwelled. So one of my most daredevil antics was to secretly infiltrate my parents' bedroom and dab myself with whatever was lying within my reach. My "commando" tacticts were of course immediately exposed upon exiting the room, cause the monsters my mother was keeping in there were traitorous enough to give me away every single time. My mother was always giving me funny looks after each accomplished mission, but I fancied they were about my glasses being dirty or my hair being uncombed. Until one accursed Saturday evening, a huge 240ml splash bottle of Givenchy III decided it had enough of abuse, and tried to kill itself by falling from my hands. It failed. I dont know if you've ever handled such a bottle, but rest assured its glass is thick enough to stop a bullet. My mother came flying upon hearing the thud and found me aghast, with the golden stopper still in my hand, watching half of the golden soul of Givenchy III escaping its body and speading on the floor. The other half was already spilled on my clothes. Although I was sure a legendary chiding was seconds away from being yelled at poor me, she didn't say a word. What she did however, was leaving me with the perfume reeking clothes on for the rest of the weekend. Till Sunday night I was 1000% sure that I would prefer having my 8 years old butt kicked and be spared the olfactory torture. It felt like I was tied for ages with mossy ropes to an oak, while green devils wearing gardenia leis were frenziedly dancing all around me, poking me with pointy sandalwood sticks and throwing orris roots (with all the dirt still attached) on my face. I was seriously pondering over begging my mother for a beating in exchange of a bath. But not being stoical enough, I just asked for the bath. She replied "Why? I love the way you smell!". Amnesty was finally granted at late Sunday night. I felt like a sinner been cleansed from all his wrongdoing. After she scrubbed me redder than a beetroot, my mother left me standing ecstatic in the bathtub and went to bring a towel. When she came back and approached me I threw my hands happily around her neck in order to kiss her and show her my gratitude. Imagine my horror upon realising that she was the one reeking with Givenchy III now... Many years later I found a very old 60ml splash bottle of Givenchy III in a tiny backstreet shop.

As soon as I smelt this one, it took me right back to the reason why you can't beat a vintage chypre. There's something about the fresh combination with the oakmoss and delicate florals done right that just allures and entices you. Truly a lot of French fragrances made during this era were exceptional, composed with care and artistry. I get a lot of the fresh floral & slightly fruity citrus top, with the galbanum and jasmine coming in, balancing the harsh bitterness and the dusty oakmoss with a vibrant hint of citrus and bright floral. The orris root, sandalwood, lily-of-the-valley and even coconut come together absolutely wonderfully here, with a honeyed gardenia note that compliments other white florals and even hyacinch. Really a fragrance which is multi-faceted and extremely well put together and enjoyable. It's a joy to wear and defies gender classification in my opinion. I'm wearing the vintage eau de toilette and it's really something else. I can't speak for modern formulations or versions but if you do get a chance to try vintage and you are a chypre fan just buy it. If you like Mitsouko and No. 19 then this is a great and unique companion to them. One which has to be experienced. Exceptionally good and what real perfumery is all about.

Vintage Givenchy III EDT! What a beautiful fragrance this is. This is very similiar to YSL Y! It starts off with a strong burst of citrus & galbanum! No need to dread, this dries down after a while but still remains at the forefront. The heart of the fragrance is pure floral along with the citrus & galbanum still lurking around. I think those two notes keep this perfume balanced from going into HEY I AM A BIG FLORAL BOMB! We are left with the basenotes of sandalwood, florals & oakmoss (which I do not believe is found in the modern version)along with some vetiver. It is a green fragrance to say the least! This stuff easily last 8+ hours on my skin & projects nicely for the type of fragrance that it is. I am not the biggest chypre fan out there, but I do believe every perfume collector should have at least 1 or 2 of these in there collection. Altho marketed as a woman's fragrance, this can be unisex without any question or doubt. It should fit any atomosphere except a bar/club as I do not see this as a heavy hitter for those types of meetings. All in all, Givenchy has done very well here. Some of their best work I think.

From all the photos in here I can see that the bottle I have is quite common: the splash one with the golden, circular sticker on the front. It is SO nice! The thick, heavy glass. The golden top with a true metallic feeling to it. The simplicity of the whole thing. That really works for me. The juice inside is also great.

from a vintage miniature purchased recently: okay, wow. i have two miniatures of this, the first one i now realised was quite obviously turned, having a bitter, dead / dried herb-and-grass-like scent to it that didn't really budge or do anything. smelling this from a second bottle, however, it's like a golden sun has risen, light and life returning.

One of the best classic green chypres out there. If you like the family and you happen to come across a vintage bottle of Givenchy III, grab it and don't let it go. You won't regret it. Even if the longevity isn't long, the pleasure on wearing this green floral chypre makes it worthy yo spray again. Perfume incarnation of french spring elegance.

Praise be to Givenchy for reintroducing this fragrance! It is now a good deal lighter and no longer quite so voluminous, somewhat drier too, but so what: one of the most beautiful Chypre fragrances is back - now that’s something!
Givenchy III is the first perfume I ever bought for myself. And I still remember being completely fascinated by what was coming out of the bottle.

I don't care what anybody says, this stuff is NOT Burberry London LoL. And let's be real - if you buy a Varvatos frag, you're also buying a travel atomiser. 'Nuff said. That's just how we keep the good times rollin'. And guys, Vintage is one hell of a good time, let me tell you. If you're a cowboy, this is your scent. If you're on the prowl for cougars in the nether-regions of a desert town, this is you. Mexican? Well...let's not stereotype... But if you've ever seen a John Wayne movie, everyone in there is wearing Vintage. Just look at the note pyramid and you'll notice that it shares 5 prominent notes with Ralph Lauren's Polo - tobacco, leather, patchouli, juniper berry and some kind of pine. So can you blame it for smelling so similar in the drydown? Sure you can! But to me, it's actually a tad smoother and more well-rounded - easier on the nose. That's why I like to think of this as Polo's little brother. And I just love it. It's basically 90s masculinity in a bottle. So if you're a fan of the original Polo formulation, but found it a little too sharp, you'll find something in here for you at like half the cost. Well, plus the atomizer.

John Varvatos always produces a good men’s fragrance. This is my 4th JV and you get quality for less $$ This is a great cologne for many reasons, natural smelling, no harsh opening, great bottle design, and is fairly versatile I’m thinking summer evening or controlled climate is fine. This is definitely a more mature man’s cologne but not over the top barber shop, but a little in a good way. Blind buy? Yes if you are 40+ performance is above average and it’s not an over the top beast. I get a whole days wear with it and people notice and comment.

My review is based on a sample. I usually start out by spraying a new fragrance on paper but will not make a determination until I spray the perfume on myself. However, with Vintage, I made an exception to this rule. On paper, Vintage came across as way too sweet with a subtle fruit scent. I would never spray this on myself. This is a unisex fragrance at best. I had to write this one off and will definitely NOT be getting a full bottle.

Couldn't find the "sweet" notes on this one, despite what says here on Fragrantica. This fragrance clashes old with modern, it does smells a little "old", which is nice, regarding the "Vintage" thing. (mostly due to the strong suede notes, I think) Something in it makes it modern too, can't say exactly why though. Probably some of the other notes. Good scent, anyway! Sillage is nice on the first 45 minutes, then stays soft for around 4-5hrs on me.

I've been collecting for going on 4 years now & as the title says, this was what started my journey. I'd had fragrances my entire life, but after my cat who I adopted at the age of 3 passed away 9 years after gracing my life, I needed something special that I could foster and watch grow. . Upon smelling John Varvatos' Vintage for the first time, and every time since, I was (and still am) overcome by such a beautiful scent, unlike anything else I'd ever smelled. Rich, luxurious, mature & masculine without any of the potential negative connotations that can be attached to such words. To my nose, it comes off somewhat sweet but far from edible. It evokes class, a certain calmness that imo only comes with age. Nothing about Vintage screams, it carries with itself a serenity that I don't think I've ever smelled in perfumery since. And yes, people tend to complain about the longevity. I tend to get 6-7 hours from it which is all I would expect from an EDT. And honestly, I don't know if I'd ever want or need it to exceed that. I truly feel it would lose a lot of it's charm if it was beast mode.

Scent Soft tobacco/cigar scent nicely blend in the fragrance. Vintage and classy mood are well-mixed in the fragrance. A bit musky at the bottom notes. Longevity The scent-hold is good in night and cold ambient. For non 4-seasons countries, it is suitable for night and cold weather (referring to rainy season).

I think I like Vintage just that little bit more than John Varvatos for Men. Tobacco and lavender, when blended harmoniously with one another, can potentially make me swoon. I love the sexy and spicy feel of Vintage. It's quite a daring and complex blend.

JV Vintage has a special place in my collection and in my heart. It is the fragrance that I chose for my wedding on a cold January morning. It is a warm and cozy masculine tobacco fragrance that smells timeless. It’s the smell of sweet unlit cigars in a cigar shop. The only issue is, this fragrance disappears shortly after it is applied.

An easy one to reach for when you can’t decide what you’re in the mood to wear. This frag will serve you well day or night. A similar vibe to Drakkar Noir, but toned down overall with less moss and the addition of tobacco in the basenotes. There’s no reason to overthink this one. A masculine fragrance at an affordable price point that just smells good. 4 stars

It's a masterpiece and the best of the John Varvatos line in my opinion! This perfume is elegant, classy, soft and sophisticated. It is so well-balanced that its actually difficult to discern any one note! You can't go wrong with it.

Two fascinating moments in perfumery happened within a few years of each other. They are the “road not taken” moments. When Thierry Mugler’s Angel hit the scene, women’s perfumery was changed irrevocably. Florals, chypres, traditional orientals were instantly ancien régime. It was a classic paradigm shift, an overthrow of the old order. The floral survived by evolving into Fruity Florals, Orientals were diminished and became Gourmands, Chypres, god help us all, became outlaws and now are effectively black market commodities. The specifics of how the men’s market changed in the 1980s differ in some respects from the changes in the feminine market, but the parallels and simultaneity of the changes make the similarities more important than the differences. Davidoff Cool Water was the masculine counterpart to Angel. To say the aromatic fougère was supplanted by the aquatic fougère doesn’t sound like much, but the the newer, more tailored aromatic fougères had just started to surpass the dominance of the 70s big boys like Paco Rabanne Pour Homme and Azzaro Pour Homme. It was the greatest height of the fougère since the release of Fougère Royale in 1882. Musky fougères (YSL Kouros, Paco Rabanne Ténéré, Dior Jules) floral fougères (Caron’s Troisième Homme, Xeryus) spiced fougères (YSL Jazz, Jacomo Anthracite, Laroche Drakkar Noir) were taking the genre in exciting new directions. The fougère is structurally tied to both the oriental (tonka, balsam) and the chypre (oakmoss and coumarin tethering more effusive floral and spiced notes). It is an inherently rich genre and many perfumers were using the fougère structure to find new ideas. It’s worth considering that Michael Edward’s, the most authoritative figure in the nomenclature of perfumery, placed the fougère at the center of the wheel he created as a visual analogy for categorizing perfumes. It is the ur-perfume. There were still a few great aromatic fougères produced, such as Partick by Patrick of Ireland (1999) a fougère in the chypre direction, and YSL Rive Gauche pour Homme (2003), but for the most part, after the advent of of Cool Water (1988) the aquatic fougère ruled with an iron fist. Dyhydromyrcenol made for the creation of fougères that would have the volume of the best fougère from the 1970s, but lacked the complexity and therefore matched the feminine counterparts that were becoming ever louder, ever simpler fruity florals and candied gourmands. Feminism’s effect on perfumery changed or waned, depending on your perspective, and the empowered feminines like Aromtics Elixir, Scherrer de Scherrer, Dior Diorella, YSL Rive Gauche became ‘Old Lady Perfumes’. Hypergender became a stylistic norm, and countless straight couples could be spotted on the town: her, with hair three feet high and rising dosed with Poison or Angel; him with slicked back hair drenched in Cool Water. I am sad over the loss of the pre-1988 aromatic fougère. It was just about to take off into some great places. Let’s not forget that these perfume were also the basic blue-print for the 1980’s mens’ power frag. Take a fougère, exchange the lavender for some more spicy elements, and freeze-dry the wood. Voila! Krizia Uomo, Chanel Antaeus, Patou pour Homme. Sometimes the player of a group known for largesse is the one to go for. Scherrer de Scherrer, a chypre that could give Aromatics Elixir a black eye is my go to green/leather chypre. Xeryus has some of that well-dressed thug appeal, seeming more like a perfume for Craig’s Bond than Moore’s. Or perhaps Dench’s M. Xeryus is becoming on you in the way it allows to you swagger a bit. It lends authority. It’s a remarkably detailed perfume that tells you not to sweat the details. It has a vaguely threatening edge at the same time it lets you be a pretty boy. Great combo of attributes. Definitely a perfume to play with.

After about 30 years, since the last time I used this fragrance, I decided to buy the last "version" still available. It remains an intense, powerful perfume, with the aura of the 80s. It remains a true powerhouse, aimed at an age group, I would say, from 35 years old upwards. It is a unique fragrance that competed with YSL Jazz, VC&A Tsar, among others, from the Yuppie generation of the late 1980s. It's in my collection and will be used on special occasions. Xeryus by Givenchy ... I highly recommend it for lovers of good perfumery. Nothing that compares to current fragrances, synthetic and excessively sweetened.

This complex fragrance with over 29 different notes is an old style fougere from 1986. A masculine creation with above average longevity. I wore it when it 1st came out as a teenager during the mid 1980s. I won't even look at the new bottle because i just know it's been ruined due to reformulations. The IFRA should be ashamed of themselves at how they've butchered these classic 70s 80s and 90s works of art. Still don't and WON'T understand the oakmoss restriction. I just won't, so i overpay for vintage but i don't care i want QUALITY. It's opening is harsh but good all the way to the drydown. I smell it all day long. Do yourself a favor and pick up a VINTAGE bottle asap. If you are a fan of classic REAL strong but not overpowering masculine scents from the golden age of fragrances then ebay will be your friend. The vintage bottle I own is just a fabulous piece of scented bliss and the performance is off the charts fantastic. I remember this being a beast when I was a teenager. It lasted all day well into the night and upon wearing it now 30yrs later it's STILL A BEAST!! I will continue to buy vintage bottles of Xeryus until I can no longer find anymore but I hope that's very long into the future. In closing I have to say that this is clearly one of Givenchy's finest fragrances hands down but I'll bet you won't find 10 people who'll agree and that's a tragedy. :)

Sampling this in the store, I loved it so much I bought some for myself.I wore this quite a bit in the late 80's. I especially loved the green notes, and the slightly oriental edge. I had the splash, so very little was applied, and just enough. Very sexy. Come to think of it, I should probably buy some for my husband.

Fantastic Fragrance ! Spicy, Soapy, Green, Woody and Complex. This review is based on the new reformulation clear bottle. Nowadays It is hard to find and very Rare. It opens up with soapy fresh spicy, green and spices notes in the background then dry down is mossy and woody. It is similar to the perfumes of 80's decade exactly, Old School, Barbershop style , Nostalgic and Classic. If you like Open Black and One Man Show, You will like this one, They are not the same but the same style. It is perfect for the spring, fall and winter. I'm so happy that I have it in my collection , Longevity is very good . Thumbs Up. Rating : 7.5 / 10

Rough, green, scratchy, soapy, spicy, bitter, floral, citrusy, fresh. And all of that at once within a few seconds. Take a breath, wait. Because the impressions come together, merge into one. Quickly, a whole emerges, and I am amazed at how many of the ingredients can still be distinctly detected despite a rounded and harmonious overall picture.

This morning, still quite dazed from the exhausting escapades of late-night perfume analysis. A call comes in from the caretaker of the residential complex that also houses me, where I play a bit of jack-of-all-trades for around four hundred bucks a month. I struggle to the phone, looking out the window. Damn: Winter Wonderland.

What one encounters at the flea market!!! There are fragrances that no longer exist. Except: at flea markets. A black bottle, opaque glass, with a scent that I have never smelled before. A strong citrus-floral opening, fresh and herb-sweet. Then comes a huge herb and flower garden, bordered by dense green conifers, almost a small forest. Then it gets even greener!

Taurus1967 has scored the first hit and given me the template, so I’m moving on to the second: I have the vintage version (early 1990s) here and will briefly report on it. "Xeryus" in this formulation opens with a bitter-citrusy tone that leans more towards mandarin and grapefruit, deeper and fruitily-sour than the often-seen bergamot-lemon note.

What? No comments yet on this supposed classic? That should change quickly with this. Plus, I can indulge in some delightful know-it-all-ness ;-) Did you know that Xeryus was originally born as Keryus? However, there was trouble with the people at Yves Saint Laurent, who had launched "Kouros" a few years earlier and feared too much confusion.

Scent Fresh scent. Feels like a combination of citrus scents and musky scent. The scent is more than an acqua scent and its unexpected. Longevity The hold of the scent is medium. For non 4-seasons countries, it is very suitable on day and summer season. The longevity can hold for only 2-4 hours. For the 4-seasons countries, the longevity is better which can be around 5-6 hours. Performance The performance is good on top notes. But fades away gradually within middle. Surprisingly, the base notes hold better even the scent is not so strong, but it is still there. Sillage The sillage is medium. The effectiveness is not enough. Uniqueness The uniqueness is on the bottle rather than the scent. Because it is in the family of John Varvatos Artisan, the scent is quite similar from each other, but the bottle is unique. Bottle Design The design is unique and attractive. With the mixture of modern design and traditional craft, it is a superb design of the John Varvatos Artisan Acqua fragrance bottle.

One of the things that I like most about Varvatos's colognes is the shape of the bottles and the admirable covers. In contrast, one of the things that I dislike most is the performance, as you should know, most of the Varvatos's cologne suffer from a weak sillage and longevity, although the overall redolence is gorgeous. Artisan Acqua is a flanker to JV Artisan, yet a bit of a different take on the original, and to tell you the truth, I was not charmed the very first time I tested it. The sharp barbershop, shaving cream, old school cologne, and aftershaves resemblance put me off quite a bit. But, when that powerful opening calmed down after a while, what I could not stop doing was to smell my hand, and the cologne positively captured my senses. To begin with, Artisan Acqua comes with an excellent presentation of all handmade and hands knitted rope, with a metal aged cap and medallion. The opening is just fantastic as I aforementioned, bright but bitter citrus blend, you definitely get the mandarin and other herbal notes, a few sweetness from the pomelo, and the aromatic lavender, something more than a usual aromatic and citrus opening. There is a lot of citrus and spicy in there, mandarin, unnatural paradisamide molecule, and angelica create a lemon-minty accord. After a bit, slowing emerging from the citrus aromas is a slight wood note reminiscent of bleached wood baking in the sun on the seashore. This bright, bracing, and somewhat salty heart note takes over Artisan Acqua for several minutes before it is overtaken by something I'll describe as floral, light, and semi-creamy jasmine and orange blossom white floral accord. The floral effect is fleeting and leads to hints of fir, soft moss, and subtle wood notes. Yes, it settles down into a greener fragrance, more old-school accord, rather than the citrusy accord that was first introduced to my nostrils. In my opinion, there is more greenness that comes down due to the fir resin, which adds depth to it. And yeah, there is something aquatic but not like Acqua di Giò, Nautica Voyage, or D&G Light Blue, just to mention a few. The dry down is balsamic and resinous, thanks to the lentiscus and fir balsam, ... It is freaking amazing, more than just what you aspect, not totally generic. I recommend for a casual as well as a business day, with a blazer, daytime. Definitely, for warm spring months or lazy days at the beach, by the pool during summertime. The performance could be weak from time to time, which a cons most of the times, but it could be a pro if you wear it in the morning and have no time to take a shower before dinner or night out, so you will safely apply a night cologne without any dangerous mix. Although it does not last nearly as long as I would like it, it's the scent. It is unique: it is citrusy and spicy and has a great bite to it. My overall take on JV Artisan Acqua is not the typical aqua fragrance! This is one hell of a scent, but I do understand where all the hate comes from. Not meant for the younger mass population crazy for Dior Sauvage or Bleu de Chanel crowd-pleaser lovers, and for that reason, I love this fragrance. This is a modernized gentleman's scent, the same school as Cerruti 1881 I would dare. Very intriguing. One would expect something fresh, tropical, and aquatic after looking at the bottle and ads. Artisan Aqua, however, is a clean, slightly soapy gem of a fragrance. It has a barbershop, shave cream vibe that is straight-up addicting. -Elysium

Fresh, green, somewhat pleasant, and classy. Classic Fougère with a modern touch. I find the old man's deodorant vibes in this fragrance as some youtube reviewer said. Sadly the longevity and projection are weak. I got a decent deal, 25 USD for a 75ml bottle before this fragrance went rare. Forgot to mention, the bottle is freaking amazing!

It was immediately clear when I saw it in the Duty Free area that I would not only test it, but also take it with me to Tunisia. The price and appearance were completely convincing, and the fact that no one knows it yet is also a plus. Additionally, I am a bit of a JV fan and own a few of their perfumes, so I am certainly qualified to write a first comment on Acqua. On the test strip, it seemed very tame, not really noticeable or detectable. But now on vacation, it has steadily become my most worn perfume - despite competition like Dior Homme Cologne or Tauer's Cologne du Maghreb. Acqua has little to do with the orange from the original Artisan, even less than the spiced orange from Artisan Black. This is commendable and scores points with me immediately. It almost has the vibe of the original John Varvatos, only sharper, saltier, and more watery. I also detect something vintage, but this time completely without leather. And surprisingly, it has quite good longevity, which is not a given for either Acquas or JVs. Acqua is very distinctive and does not remind me of any current Acqua scent, which will please and relieve many. Acqua is at least as cool as its bottle, a sharp, young, spontaneous sea scent that fits perfectly at the beach. A salty fruity note is detectable, or a fruity salty note, however you want to see it ;). Almost something chlorinated appears from time to time - but not disturbing. And before the comments come: not just because I am testing the scent by the pool ;). But the most important thing about Acqua is definitely its ability to merge with the wearer's skin. As a result, it has almost no sillage, but the entire skin smells salty, sensual, sexy, natural, Mediterranean with the right application. Finally, a summer scent that has completely convinced me, even in the Tunisia long test. Bottle: handmade Waterworld style - The most beautiful of the year? Sillage: super minimal, but meaningful & intentional in this case. Longevity: much better than the sillage, lasts a good 7 hours on me. Another very beautiful scent from JV, where the content almost keeps up with the appearance. Even though JV always has strange, self-created fragrance materials, I often buy into it. Because their scents are something special among designers, especially among those who actually target the younger buying segment. Therefore, I also pay respect to the JV perfumer here, as he has distanced himself from the orange juice Artisan roots, as well as from the typical summer, sport, or Acqua conventions. Bravo, it partly reminds me of extinct small oases like Guy Laroche's Horizon or the groundbreaking Bulgari Acqua. Even if this comment certainly contains a lot of initial enthusiasm and vacation mood!

Oh dear - who at John Varvatos came up with the name Acqua for this Artisan offshoot? It probably misled not just me completely. Of course, as an experienced perfume enthusiast, one should have no reservations or prejudices about the term Acqua, but with the multitude of offered fragrances, name and bottle can, at first glance, provide initial clues. But even the crocheted package string around the bottle doesn’t quite fit. From the very first seconds after spraying, it becomes clear: this is not an Acqua in the classical sense, but rather a citrus-fruity feel-good scent with candied lemon and a refreshing splash of mandarin liqueur. Perhaps not as concentrated as one would like, but rather a bit lightly ... um ... diluted, yet that is by no means a reason to name this offspring Acqua. As time goes on, our Artisan becomes a bit more serious, welcoming a fresh note of muscat sage along with a minimal hint of coriander, yet the sweet citrus approach remains, leading one to wonder if it resembles other fragrances or why no one else has thought to combine these themes so elegantly. If I bring my nose closer to the sprayed skin - yes, one shouldn’t really do that - it reveals a casual aura of sparkling powder and a diffuse light rose note. Perhaps not everything has a thoroughly natural atmosphere, yet it is absolutely tolerable. After a while, Artisan Acqua drifts into a subtly herbaceous-coniferous direction, without completely forgetting the two previous scent impressions. Is Artisan Acqua fresh? Definitely! Is the scent citrusy? Yes, but in a relatively sophisticated way! Is our candidate sweetish? Yep - especially at the beginning, the citrus notes are quite candied, but served without a sugar shock! Is it also spicy? Yes - and that makes it somehow so refined! And what about the name Acqua? In my opinion, it does not fit the scent at all - it is too substantial and too complex! Perhaps at John Varvatos, they wanted to indicate a fresh, carefree summer scent for marketing reasons to attract more interest. However, this could lead to a significant backfire, causing some potential buyers to be put off by the name. I myself am only a conditional fan of Acqua scents, but this one, which for me isn’t really one, I found absolutely likable.

Artisan Acqua starts off very refreshing, slightly sweet - fruity, but also a bit synthetic. Our dear Parfumo "Zirkeltanz" gave me the opportunity to test this fragrance with its sample, for which I would like to express my sincere thanks. A very refreshed sweet - fruity mandarin with a decent splash of grapefruit can be sniffed.

spring is here, and with it a fragrance that could not be better suited for this season. John Varvatos Artisan Acqua, yes, this is your time. From now on, you can come out of your beautiful, crocheted bottle. A scent that has few followers here. A mainstreamer, but completely without a stream? Is it even one then?
So sings the wonderful Annett Louisan with a wink at our endeavor to always be individual and unconventional, and a little bit rebellious - without leaving the safe comfort zone.

When I tested Artisan by John Varvatos back then, I actually stumbled upon this fragrance by chance. Because, as so often, certain bottles simply attract you, and the wonderfully braided (or is it maybe intertwined? Hmm… I can already see a certain friend or Parfumo laughing at this sentence, but well… :D) bottle of Artisan was just a real eye-catcher.

(A park in the dim light of an approaching evening; in the background, one can hear fireworks and loud children's screams, in the foreground, two gentlemen on a bench) Johnny Beton: Good evening, Hektor. I greet you. Hektor: Good evening, Mr. Beton. J.B.: Just Johnny for you. H.: Alright. Johnny. J.B.: We have gathered here today in this place to talk about...

On the verge of being discontinued... that's why I was given a full tester-bottle of "Givenchy for Men Very Irrésistible" for free yesterday. A tenacious fragrance with many components: mint leaf combined with a cocktail of sesame-mocha and hazelnut wood. The result is a woody gourmand which is not as smooth as you might expect. The chocolate-mint-note is a bit weird and the woody base quite synthetic boardering on the unpleasant. Very powerful sillage, but sadly not in the least irresistible.

I have to agree. This smells to mint chocolate. Or chocolate mint. There is indeed a variety of a mint hybrid (Mentha x pipperita `Chocolate Mint´) that is curiously mint-chocolate scented, but i have no idea if that is the one that was used in here. Strangely enough, the notes list doesnt contain cocoa, although, again, the illusion of chocolate is very vivid. In my research i found out coffee and sesame were also listed in other sites. Mystery solved. Coffee and cocoa are brothers... I personally believe that it might be the accord "coffee/roasted-hazelnut/oily-sesame" what gives this unmistakable mouthwatering chocolate scent. It starts as a fresh, green blast of citrus and mint, very cooling. Very soon the mysterious accord takes over: whatever it is, mint chocolate or chocolate mint, it reminds to the english "after eight" sweets, which are candies, yes, but to be eaten when kids are off to bed, and taste adult and sophisticated. And so, VI is a an adult, sophisticated gourmand at this stage. The nutty quality makes it specially yummy. Patchouli is noticeable in the background, rich and luxurious. After a while, the enjoyable chocolate (and the mint) are sadly vanished. Then patchouli steps out, along with some pencil shavings. I love pencil shavings, and i have a very high tolerance to caustic sawmill wood scents (which is not the case of Very Irresistible) but i find now the patchouli raspy and tiring. And i dont want to wear it anymore. Projection is remarkable. Probably many others would enjoy this, i admit, but i only like the first hour i am wearing it, when you know there is patchouli but is not all about it. Im torn: I love the after eight... but around ten o´clock, i dont like it anymore... I guess i am not a Very Irresistible guy.

The first thing I thought of when I tried this fragrance was that it was a masculine version of Angel by Thierry Mugler. Chocolate is really dominant in Very Irrestible for Men. It's like a gourmand fragrance for men, which is often hard to come by. They do say that bacon is a man's favourite smell, so why don't they produce more foody-smelling scents for men? I quite like chocolate on a man. In this fragrance it is rich and syrupy. Almost dark in a sense. The hazelnut and mint only add to its deliciousness, however the grapefruit in the opening gives this fragrance a bit of a zesty and fruity feel. The colour of the bottle tends to confuse me into thinking that I can smell a greeness in this fragrance, however when I sniff more closely I contradict that thought. The woodsy drydown with the now softened chocolate note is something to die for. I can safely define this fragrance as being very sexy. The lasting power is good, however it could be better. But despite all of that, I think that Very Irresistible is a very irrestible buy.

Why is there no chocolate/cocoa note at the top of this page? I believe it's cocoa I smell, or could better noses be telling me it's hazlenut? It is on the synthetic side but it is great and for choco lovers it has to be a nice aroma to take in while it's there. It projects, decent life-span and of course gourmanish-I think the ladies love it. Givenchy tends to be above average on the whole designer/brand scent charts so you should end up happy with your purchase if it is a blind one. I think it is an all around type of scent, not too dressy or too "dressed down" and the ladies at the office should love it. Cheers!

Minty hazelnuts with hints of chocolate. Actually a great fragrance that may be irresistible (or not). For me it's very unique and it has a good lasting power (over 8 hours), nice projection and good sillage. Sweet in the right amount. Great scent that deserves at least a try. Thumbs up! Updated January 2014

If you miss this fragrance then try Penhalligons 'Changing Constance' (a unisex fragrance). I have tried them side by side and they are close. I have a qtr bottle left and only wear it for the special person on my life. ...

A rich gourmand with surprising notes for a designer offering. The simple version would be naming it "After Eight" for men, but overall the scent offers a sweet minty hazelnut and coffee bordering on chocolate and sometimes it comes out just a bit earthy or herbal as well, the opening is even a tad boozy with added freshness (from grapefruit maybe?).

Very Irresistable for Men is a fragrance in my collection that I have truly owned for many years. It's been a long time, back when I owned less than 50 fragrances. I ordered it blind back then, when my fragrance know-how was still very limited. I must admit the reason for the purchase was the convincing and confident name of the fragrance combined with this beautiful bottle.

Very Irresistable for Men by Givenchy was for years the brand's insider tip for the younger generation, until it gradually disappeared from the market and nowadays can almost only be purchased online. I also got the smaller version there.

I must admit that I ignored this fragrance for years. The bottle is, in my eyes, not a product of creativity. It could just as easily have the names Mexx or Esprit on it, and no one would question it. Therefore, my interest in this scent was rather lukewarm to non-existent. A grave mistake!

I wish Burberry would bring this flanker back into production. It is divine, like most Brit flankers tend to be. If you love woodsy vanilla scents, I would highly recommend that you go to the effort of trying to track down a bottle. Not to mention, the gold packaging is exquisite. Brit Gold opens with luscious, creamy vanilla and musky orris root. This blend is both sensual and delicious. The heart is a tad richer with powdery sandalwood, syrupy amber and sweet benzoin. A subtle hint of black currant appears every now and then, and works beautifully alongside the dominant vanilla accord. I honestly wasn't a huge fan of Burberry Brit, but I have since fallen head over heels in love with Brit Red and now this one, Brit Gold. Brit Sheer was also enjoyable as a fresh, citrusy floral for Summer. Vanilla scents always make me feel warm and cuddly and Brit Gold is no exception. It smells a lot more expensive than what it's worth. It's such a pity that it isn't more readily available. I think that if it was still around today it would be a best-seller. The longevity is incredibly good, as is the sillage. Burberry often produces clean and casual scents for everyday wear, but Brit Gold smells like a filthy-rich goddess; pure luxury. I highly recommend. Original review written: September 2012.

This scent is entirely dominated by the vanilla & benzoin. Pleasantly un-sweet compared to many vanilla-heavy scents. Not that much personality, though. Over time, it ripens & becomes richer. It comes to remind me of the vanilla & wood aspects of my beloved Laura Mercier Nuits Enchantees. However, NE has additional mocha and spice notes that make it interesting. Because Brit Gold lacks those types of notes, it doesn't venture beyond comfortable and cuddly.

...and Golden Luxury promises this British elegance and powerful scent. According to my fragrance sample packaging, it was supposed to be limited edition and is no longer available in the German market. The fragrance notes listed above also seem to be incomplete; according to Burberry, printed in golden letters, it also includes Heliotrope and Patchouli. It is very warm and intense, requiring a lot of self-confidence and the awareness to captivate the environment. Fruits and flowers are very subtle; the fragrance stars are Amber, Patchouli, Vanilla/Heliotrope, and Sandalwood. A voluminous, sensual, oriental amber fragrance for women. Somehow, it takes me back to the old, traditional British society, while simultaneously merging with the modern world of today. Modern and vintage in one. A true work of art. It’s a shame that it was also not intended for the German market for long.

I knew regular Organza from its first edition, as I remember my mother received it as a birthday gift, and I kept using it sneakily until she let me have the bottle. Being a youngster I quickly moved on to other things, and somehow my paths never crossed with Organzas for many years to come. I missed the Indecence altogether. Ever since I started collecting vintage perfumes over a decade ago, I was aware of its existence, but again it never came into my radar. Meanwhile prices have become " indecent" and the perfume harder and harder to find. Last year I discovered Frederic Malle's Dries van Noten, and it was an epiphany- that anything produced after the year 2000 mark can actually sweep me off my feet. The perfect composition of light sunny spices and woods. I wore it all summer, disregarding all the others. Smelt familiar to another favourite of mine, the vintage Dior Dolce Vita, so I thought this must have been the ancestor. Little did I know that there has been another close relative , until last week when I actually managed to win a partially used bottle of Organza Indecence, and I never win on eBay, usually just "buy it now". I can't believe my luck , now that I have the three reunited, I can say that Dolce Vita seems to be the most cinnamon-y of them, Dries van Noten most delectably woody with my beloved guaiac wood note, and Organza most vanilic but In such an uplifting and not cloying way. There is still one more gem on my to get list, which is related to this family which is Shiseido's Feminite du Bois, and I can't wait to actually have it in my hands and see where it fits in.

When I first applied this it literally could have knocked my socks off!!! That's just how good it is. Thank-you to Digindirt for sending me a very generous sample of this in it's original miniature spray bottle no less! Had it not been for her kindness I more than likely would never have been able to try it. I am admittedly not a fan of the original Organza but this one is beyond gorgeous. On my skin I can really smell the rosewood mixed with the vanilla and amber. It's so intoxicating that I can't stop sniffing myself! Such a crying shame that it's been discontinued. I will cherish the small amount that I have and apply it with a light hand so I can stretch it out and make it last. One of the best perfumes I've smelled, EVER! Simply heavenly.

I have a sample of Indécence and was so thrilled to try this, hoping for something greater than the fabulous Organza. Unfortunately it's much 'less than' to my bitter disappointment. Organza was my signature fragrance when I was working at a restaurant in Los Angeles where the waitstaff were all drag cabaret artists. This was during the mid 90's and brings to memory a time of my life that was filled with the wonderful Gardenia/Tuberose/Jasmine/Vanilla that Organza used to be ... I couldn't get enough of it!! I say 'used to be' because the current reformulation is just heinous ... a mortal sin committed on the sanctity of perfumery! But I digress ... Indécence is about as risqué as a 'glimpse of stocking' would be during Mass on a Sunday morning. Now, please don't misunderstand me ... this is not a bad fragrance ... in fact it's quite beautiful if a little fruit with a few sticks of cinnamon is your thing. In fact, I find the combination very appealing in a fruity 'chai latté' sort of way. It's quite unisex too ... but indecent it's not. This fragrance reminds me of a watered down version of Costume National Homme ... which happens to be a fast disappearing favorite of mine. Indécence (now discontinued) commands huge sums on the Bay ... I wouldn't spend that kind of money on it. If you want this but only streets better, then go for the Costume National.

I acquired an original bottle recently and I am now adding Givenchy Organza Indecence to my top 5 favorite perfumes. It’s that good. It’s that memorable. It’s absolutely delicious. The odor of burnt marshmallows, the scent of match tip’s sulphur when you blow it out, the remnants of moonlit campfires smoking embers. Cinnamon and vanilla in a perfect creamy blend, amber tempered, layered with a mildly fruity plum, Indecence envelopes you with an earthy presence immediately that stays throughout the duration of the perfume. A sense of warm patchouli surrounds the notes to complete this very spicy fragrance. Organza is a season-less scent, full of smoky images. It’s thick and only gets thicker as the hours go by. Dab in your application or you will be overwhelmed. It’s an intense perfume.

It was in 1999 that Givenchy decided to create a flanker of the already very pretty Organza. Why a flanker anyway? Organza is a scent of white flowers, delicately spicy, Indécence is a spicy fragrance built around vanilla and cinnamon. The first is sensual but delicate, the second is imposing, provocative, sexy, carnal. In short, not similar... I always liked both but Indécence, ha... Indécence. So extravagant, warm, oriental... Cinnamon, powdery vanilla, plum, amber, atomic staying power and sillage; perfection in a bottle! And yet, it sells poorly. Not because it doesn't appeal, but because the public simply doesn't know its existence. Bad marketing I guess... So on one hand, you get stopped in the street because "You smell good! What's your perfume?" and on the other, Givenchy decides to stop this marvel. A new version will be released in 2007 under the banner “Les Mythiques” but will also be discontinued a few years later. Since then, all my attempts to find a dupe will fail because Organza Indécence is simply unique. Givenchy will probably never read this but I have to write it anyway; please give it back to us!

Organza Indecence didn't deserve to be discontinued, and it is often fragrances like these, that appeal to me due to their uniqueness, that get axed and torn away from our loving hands. In some ways, Organza Indecence can be slightly masculine, particularly in the opening, which is a rather dark blend of cedar, patchouli and syrupy, spicy vanilla.

WOW!!! This is going straight to my top shelf! Completely different from plain ol' Organza, which I've never liked. I passed over this one as a similar flanker--boy, was I wrong! I was looking for something warm and cinnamon-y recently...something to give my favored Liz Earle No. 15 some competition!
I already had organza and i really like it, it works well on me.
The original ORGANZA INDECENCE (don't know whether it has by now been reformulated...) really cranks up the spices, so much so that patchouli is overtaken by...cinnamon!

I am a little late in the game on this one, yet today I discovered a vintage mini of this now lost legend at an antiques store. In the 20th C. I revered Givenchy as one of my favorite houses. This one slipped by my nose, as it quickly disappeared from the market. Due to high on the prices, I avoided it before today. My mini was just $3. My first thought was PI.

Surprisingly, the house of Burberry disrupted the tradition of its fall and winter Brit and Brit Rhythm colognes and released this first aquatic and fresh summery splash. Well, Brit Summer flanker is sweet and floral, and Burberry Men is gentle and creamy with its many summer flankers. Then, Touch is green and aromatic; The Beat is woody and aromatic. Finally, Mr. Burberry is fresh and is wooden, and the Weekend is sweet and citrus. Yet there was no aqueous Brit so far. Here you are! Brit Splash is bright, beachy, and subtly floral with fruity notes. I'm going to start by saying this scent smells fantastic, it is oceanic, with hints of flowers and roses, in particular, has a slight lavender-like smell to it, it does have a tad of oakmoss, very clean smelling in my opinion. Best for summer days, the fragrance opens up with aquatic, fresh, and aromatic main accords. There is crisp green rosemary with its rugged, dry, chest-opening spice. Rosemary is a fantastic note in men's cologne because it has the herbal complexity to be featured all by itself, and when it is used in a blend, it can add a bold, refined, and earthy nuance to citrus and florals. Then, a tropical freshly cut green juicy honeydew melon and dark galbanum complete the blend. I promptly catch the fruity and watery feeling of Brit Splash, with the greenish touch of the aromatic rosemary leaves. Not later than quarter-hour, this bright opening turns into something more watery, the notes of the violet leaves and wild-type cyclamen blossom. The leaves give off an intensively green aroma, which is resembles mowed grass combined with a hint of cucumber, metallic, aqueous, and the watery accord alters the rosemary piquancy in the heart. This central stage lasts a couple of hours or so. As the middle notes start to mix with the warm and sweet notes, it transforms into a light, refreshing, and summery scent. Moss, musk, and vetiver round out the scent in the dry down, which results in a bouncy, clover-like moss note along with a woods accord, as a calming fade-out to this energetic, clean, and pure fragrance. As it starts to wear throughout the day and settle on the skin, it turns quite muskier and more of your typical masculine fragrance. It is a little spicy, a little sweet, with just the hint of floral and all-around extraordinarily unique and exciting scent. The entire composition goes about its business in a casual, brisk, and charming way, and its appeal is in its watery rusticity. If you lean toward the aromatic in your fragrance preferences, save this one for the weekend when just a little extra spice is needed before you step out the door. It is housed in a bottle with a light gray-blue tartan pattern embossed on the entire bottle, the cologne has weak to moderate longevity and soft to average sillage. It has a sophisticated, yet slightly trendy and urban feel. When you first apply it, it has an exciting combination of spicy and fruity notes, that you would think would be incredibly sweet and sultry, but the musky scents help to ground it and keep it quite masculine. -Elysium

My wife is largely responsible for bringing me here. She bought me a 12 cologne sampler from Sephora, for Christmas, and Givenchy Play happened to be in the box with 11 other heavy hitters. The fun thing about the 12 cologne sampler was you got to chose a bottle of the one scent you desired. I spent a few weeks testing the various samples and decided that I liked Givenchy Play better than Hanae Mori, and YSL L'Homme which were the other two that I was giving strong consideration to. After choosing Play, I went on a crazy run ordering samples and bottles left and right. I've probably sniffed around 100 things since December and it makes me wonder why people call this one unoriginal? I've smelled nothing like it save for the flankers of the line. Play Intense is a great scent which is a little more vanillic/caramelic vs. the citrus found in Play. Why am I trying to replace Play? It's longevity is very disappointing. I bought Play Intense and am much happier with the longevity but I don't quite like the scent as much as regular Play. Play Sport is also semi-interesting but the least attractive of the 3 to me with it's ultra citric content. I've found that layering Play and Play Intense is nearly perfection for me, but I don't like the idea of having to wear two scents at once. Finally, I'll never quite understand those who'll pan Play and praise Play Intense. I really don't find that huge of a gap between the two.

This is ok, for a low end synthetic . It is a citrus woodsy fragrance, that also seems to be powdery at times . This is the cheapest synthetic fragrance that I own . Mainly due to my better half . It is nice though . I usually don't like fragrances this light, but it does work well . Great to wear around the house, or to run quick errands .

This fragrance is the kind of citrus that I like on a man. The mandarin, bergamot, grapefruit and bitter orange work in perfect unison with one another. The opening is crisp and energising rather than sharp or headache-inducing like most citrus-based scents are for me. Despite the fact that Play is fairly unoriginal, it is extremely inticing. I must admit that I don't like the bottle design. It's strange like a remote or something, clunky and looks cheaply made, however the fragrance makes up for the odd marketing. The pepper and the coffee in the heart does not feature as strongly as I expected they would, however because this fragrance is primarily a Summer scent, the strength of these notes would have inbalanced the liveliness and crispness of the scent. Like many have mentioned before me, the lasting power is unfortunately quite poor which is a little disappointing seeing that this is one of the nicest male releases this year. I did however get the chance to experience the drydown before it faded far too quickly, which was an earthy and masculine blend of vetiver and patchouli.

Givenchy Play is a backstreet fragrance. What I mean by that is it hides in the shadows of so many other fragrances of it's kind. I am glad I only got a sample of this. It opens up synthetic with citrus, woods & some coffee. While this does not sound bad, it is due to the lack of quality that is produced in this fragrance. It should appeal to those teenagers whom are young @ heart, but I can not recommend this fragrance to anyone over the age of 20! Givenchy perfumes are usually a hit or miss with me as they will either last a nice while or will fade away rather swiftly. This is the case with Play. I get a max 3 hours then it fades to nothing. Projects? Not much if @ all. Intense would be a much better option than this. However the bottle is unique.

Play by Givenchy seems to me a youthful, woody and fresh fragrance. Wearing this fragrance made me think of a young person who wears a fragrance with just enough woods that doesn't make him feel too formal, but also doesn't fall into sportiness despite being citrusy. I think the heart notes are the ones that give the combination of coffee and tobacco flower its own personality, although I don't know what the cuaba flower smells like, perhaps it also contributes its differentiating share. It is a versatile and pleasant fragrance, as I mentioned, I see it as ideal for young people (perhaps the advertising planted that idea in my head). Duration on my skin greater than 8 hours.

Recently, the well-meaning perfume saleswoman I trust tossed a few samples into my stuffed shopping bag. Play was among them. I tried it - and in bright red letters, the message appeared before my eyes: Remember! Today, while out shopping, I came across it again. Tested it again, and the initial positive impression only intensified.

It is extremely rare for me to feel a genuine aversion to a perfume. Play is so far the only fragrance that holds this position, and so this is my first zero percent rating that I assign to a perfume. Even the much-criticized Joop Homme and Le Mâle fared better. That such an extreme rating requires justification is, for me, a given.

If I had been interested in fragrances back in 2008, the advertising campaign featuring one of my favorite musicians, Justin Timberlake, would have likely made a good impression, and I would have had high expectations... which would have been quite bitterly disappointed. But even so, it is not a good fragrance. It simply faded into oblivion very quickly.

More appearance than essence - this thought crossed my mind after Play had the chance to guest on my forearm for a few hours. The discrepancy between presentation and content is truly extraordinary with this fragrance. The bottle presents itself in a deliberately stylish manner, clearly aiming to awaken desires in target groups who are devoted to electronic gadgets.

I had to edit my comment a bit because I think I should address more aspects! Let's first talk about the bottle and the advertising figure of this fragrance: Justin Timberlake! First of all, I really like JT's music and generally like the whole person with style, etc. Initially, I read that JT helped create this fragrance! I was definitely curious when I saw it in the store!

Now quickly wash my hands with some good olive oil soap, after all, my stomach is growling. One cannot live by body alone, can one?

Awakening! So infinitely deep beneath the earth of the forest. The taste of the damp-cool earth still on the tongue and in the throat. Interwoven with the sultry moisture of the night rain. Awakening as if from a deep-traumatic sleep. Twisting and stretching towards the surface. There where the green of the ivy reigns. Breaking through the earth. Freeing oneself to scream,..to breathe. Separated and torn from green-brown umbilical cords. Embraced by loops of the most toxic juices. Born to olfactorily consume everything that has ever existed! Adorned and refined by the darkest creatures of the night. Marked with the secrets of desires. The nests of love crushed and rummaged through in the deepest foliage of the ivy. A cradle of lust on damp-sweaty and warm hay. Stained with salty sweat. Right there you will rise,…for that is where you belong! Covered in earthy patchouli and damp-dark earth and the fluids of the forest's lust. Here your toxic crown was woven in the darkest green. Right there you will be resurrected. In the kingdom of earthy-green beasts. And when you have finally found peace in the lap of the fleshy ivy. They will come to you in streams and lick your wounds. With their ecstatic, tender-painful tongues. And then from that very moment on,…you will know. I am crowned and will REIGN…! Conclusion That this perfume even passed at Burberry is nothing short of a miracle. Who could or would wear such a perfume? I certainly would,…but I am also very unscrupulous. Perhaps I am mistaken? But I think I know very well what animalic means. Too well! But what has been created here is a crazily bizarre symbol of that. What does it smell like? As if all the animals of the forest were embracing you, bowing down and paying their tribute. And this exclusively in bodily fluids! Yes,..it sounds repulsive. But only for those who cannot handle it. This perfume is only adorned with a bit of leaf green from salty-green ivy and gently grounded with dirty-dusty patchouli and a hint of leathery castoreum. Otherwise, it is infinitely overloaded with secretions from civet. And God knows,..deeply animalic musk. Salty, sweating, and sultry-breathing. Rarely have I encountered modern perfumes that go as incredibly deep as this one. Devouring and deeply enveloping. Brutally beautiful and highly (pleasantly) disturbing! Also disturbing is that it was made by Francis Kurkdjian. He, of all people, who ultimately banished his greatest animalic creation from his own house. I will probably never forgive him for letting Absolue Pour Le Soir die. One of the most animalic perfumes he ever created. Perhaps it no longer fit into his "Also,…so clean concept" of his own label. Shame on you, Francis! But despite that! Even if he doesn't "dirty" his own label, he can still do it with other labels. Like here with Burberry. One of the most conservative labels of its time, to boot. Which is pure irony again! He can still do it when the urge comes over him. And when he does, he becomes a beast! In my opinion, he has almost "overbred" this perfume olfactorily! Or let’s say he has created an olfactory Callisto effect. A completely new, monstrous species. So incredibly strong and so insatiably hungry. It could devour everything that had comfortably settled in the noble niches over time. And this just in passing! I have the feeling that Francis emotionally and technically unloaded himself completely with Ivy Musk. Perhaps too much animal-consuming energy had built up beneath the clean-polished surface of a Francis Kurkdjian. Suppressing his instincts cannot end well in the long run! I can’t explain it any other way!? Thus, he ruthlessly seized the opportunity. And so he poured out and unloaded himself unrestrained and created Ivy Musk…. A so sensual, brown-green and human-dark, toxic ivy of fur, flesh, and blood! I thank you from the bottom of my heart for the hunt, ElAttarine. We will meet again in the ivy…! I wish everyone here for 2024….. Love, fulfillment, and the crown that every queen and every king here deserves. Reign wisely, happily, and justly in 2024. And let it be said……! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hbY9NQ257Qk C A N

As the sun rises, the morning dew shimmers airy-salty-sweet in the ivy forest. The ivy-clad crowns of the ancient trees reach higher than the eye normally goes, their roots deeper into the earth than even the mushrooms, worms, and decay bacteria are tirelessly traversing. The light falls only softly and is repeatedly refracted through the ivy green. On the damp ground with its sweetish decay, the animals of the forest rise from their resting places, rubbing against each other and stretching their limbs. In doing so, the flattened ground releases the scents of the night, just as the furs of the animals in the air, warm, urinous, animalistic, desirous, desiring, sexual, wild. Wild juices and secretions of all kinds and all manifestations of life let their aromas waft. Here and there, birds take flight, soar higher, and settle down again. The gaze that follows them opens up the space above. Awe at the height of the treetops and the enormous expanse that arches over the forest. So you stand there, stretched between earth and sky, with your feet on the ground, in this immense space of life. From the earth cave at the very bottom to the airy heights above, where the ivy eventually stops striving further upward and forms flowers... There, where it is not far to the clouds. --------------- It is truly hard to believe that Francis Kurkdjian created this scent specifically for Burberry! Burberry, for me, stands for very controlled elegance, certainly not for pronounced animality. (However, I have encountered some eccentric wearers of Burberry clothing in Exmoor, Devon, for whom this would fit perfectly, sweaty and in rubber boots, out in the twilight on a binocular hunt for the “wild red deer...”). Neil Chapman, who in his review on “blacknarcissus” did not capture the scent in my opinion (whether mentally or emotionally, both are possible!), writes in his description of Ivy Musk : “Jesus. This is a monster. A joke. Surely. The pooiest civet I have ever smelled.” The civet here is said to be truly fecal and capable of turning one’s stomach. The fresh and ozonic green notes that overlay the “foul-smelling and truly shocking decaying Gorgon heart in a way that is simply unacceptable in modern society” remain inaccessible and incomprehensible to him. His reaction is accordingly only “olfactory horror and dismay,” the scent is at best suitable for stink bombs or terrorist attacks. --------------- I feel differently. My scent impression: A very brief beginning with airy-fresh-salty notes, clearly beautifully tar-bitter-sweet ivy, and immediately the whole animality comes in. It has a presence! I also catch a whiff of slightly hay-like grass, damp earth, the sweetish decay. From this point on, everything remains simultaneously present, clear yet complex. The strong animality is very, very pronounced and is, for me, consistently fascinating and at no point repulsive. There are many facets of the urinous and animalistic. But never repulsive enough for me to turn my nose away. And every spot smells different; I sniff and sniff like one of the animals, always fascinated by where I have sprayed or dabbed. There is nothing banal, boring, pleasing, or nice about this at all. Again, a scent that is not for the faint-hearted, but very special and wonderful! Yes, some scents require courage to wear - but actually, it is fearlessness or courage for life that is needed here. For life with all the creaturely aspects that come with it. And when nothing human is foreign to us anymore or we have gone through it and thus are as human as possible, then it is good... EVERYTHING is life. “And though worms destroy this body Yet in my flesh shall I see God …” (from Handel’s “Messiah”) Oh dear, I have completely succumbed to this scent; I don’t want to wear anything else. - Yes, yes, I know, I am always so easily excited. But this. This happened very quickly, and it had me. Thanks to @Can777 for leading me to this trail! https://theblacknarcissus.com/tag/burberry-ivy-musk-review/

I should have left it alone, as it is absolutely not my scent. It is beautifully presented, I will give it that.
