I look forward to the coming time and will wear it more often with joy.

Gentlemen Only is one of those fragrances that smells so good right after spraying that you just want to take it with you (which means buy it :D). After testing this scent a few times and finding pleasure in it, you eventually see an Intense version and hop joyfully, but with a certain skepticism, to the tester (but always ready to curse loudly if some guys have already emptied the tester). Skeptical because the so-called Extreme, Intense, or whatever else they are called versions sometimes have nothing to do with the original scent. Of course, one should sniff each fragrance as an independent scent, but unfortunately, it sometimes happens that an Intense version smells too different or even worse, and you are very disappointed, especially if you really like the original version. Fortunately, this does not happen with Gentlemen Only Intense. At the start, you can clearly smell the slightly sweet yet very fresh mandarin. A few moments later, the black pepper subtly kicks in, but it is really very weak and fades away after a few minutes or becomes weaker. It then becomes slightly earthy, and after that, you can smell the leather well. Almost simultaneously, the fragrance becomes sweeter due to the amber, and you also perceive the unmistakable, slightly powdery, and wonderful scent of tonka bean. These last two notes seem to dominate until the end, as you initially hardly perceive the leather or vanilla at all. In the end, you can still faintly detect the mandarin, and then the leather and vanilla come a bit more into play (or you might still be smelling the tonka bean and think it's the vanilla, I'm not sure here...), although still faint. The tonka bean remains in the foreground with the amber as mentioned, and this does not change until the fragrance fades. All together, it simply results in a great scent. The longevity is quite long at about eight hours, which is very good. The sillage is better than with the normal Gentlemen Only and radiates well. The bottle is rectangular with rounded corners and is quite nice, fitting well in the hand; the dark gradient gives the bottle a great touch and typically matches the expression "Intense," as many manufacturers seem to use darker tones for Intense versions. The cylindrical black cap looks good and fits well with the bottle. Givenchy Gentlemen Only Intense smells very good, the scent changes over time from fresh to sweet (with the mandarin still present until the end) and is therefore, in my opinion, a good all-rounder, although perhaps a bit unsuitable for summer.
Coincidentally the second "Gentlemen Only..." fragrance within a week and this one also doesn't bring tears of joy to my eyes.

Actually, it was just a "bycatch" when I included this one while purchasing several samples from Givenchy. I already knew "Gentleman Givenchy," which was too powdery for me. So, I didn't have high expectations. I was all the more surprised to discover the best gentleman fragrance I have encountered so far.

I really like Gentlemen Only; for me, it is an all-around pleasing, well-balanced fragrance that, although it lacks a bit of bite, can always be worn without feeling out of place, and it has a pleasantly "grown-up" vibe. Gentlemen Only Intense has the advantage that the bottle looks better. Period. That's it. In all other areas, I prefer the predecessor.

I tested this fragrance today, also at the Turquoise store. I’m not exactly sure why I tried this particular scent, as it was more of a blind grab from the shelf than a selection process. I was probably fascinated by the cardboard display that concealed the theft detector with the likeness of Simon Baker.

I had been on a quest for this classic and finally scored an 8.4oz bottle for $125! A steal if there ever was one. I remember when i was a younghan walking in the department store with my parents at the church on a Sunday afternoon in the winter. A nice lady asked me if I wanted a sample of this new fragrance. It was the best smelling men's cologne I had ever experienced up to that point and to this day I remember how good it was. I held onto that little sample as long as I could careful to fold the pouch it came in to tuck in all the fragrance. That thing lasted over a year maybe more, stashed away in the upper drawer of my dresser. I have never forgotten it. I have owned and smelled lots of amazing fragrances since then but very few have made an impression on me like this one has. I am sure Nostalgia and the lady made an impact as well, but this was just a great Symphony of notes, period! My young inexperienced nose newadvent and my old one knows it now.

On the recommendation of Burberry (Junior), I was to visit his old man Burberrys at his house in Belgravia, London. I had met Burberry (Junior) some time ago in a Berlin nightclub (admittedly, he was quite tipsy and even harder to understand!) and took the opportunity to ask about the whereabouts of his old man. So the Junior arranged an audience with the old Burberrys in London Belgravia. I was excited. I was going to meet a legend. Finally! My taxi dropped me off in front of the imposing entrance, and after I managed to climb the huge staircase to the entrance (which probably resembles a castle gate), I reached for the door knocker. Knock knock knock. After what felt like an eternity, an ancient, somewhat senile butler let me in (he first led me into a storage room until he realized his mistake) and draped me in a gigantic salon (from the Thirties? of the 17th century?). And then HE came! Burberrys in full life size! Elegant in a light gray double-breasted suit with a jacket (unfortunately with an overly bright green tie - British, after all) and - (oh dear) - with brown house slippers! (Ugh, what a turn-off for my awe). Gray, almost white hair without even a thinning spot (envy!). On his sharply drawn face, a very dominant graying mustache. Burberrys: You, uh, are? me: R. from DE. I am pleased to meet you, Sir. (He gives me a firm nuanced handshake - just before the pain threshold. Now he reminds me more of an old British colonial colonel.) Burberrys: Uh, yes... Mr. R from DE. My ah Junior has already announced you. Please - uh - sit down. Would you like a drink? I have an excellent - uh - mint liqueur here? (Without waiting for an answer from me, he turns to the door) Arthur? Arthur... Bring this - uh - gentleman a glass of the '81 - you know - uh uh -. I: Thank you very much, Sir. May I ask you something? Burberrys: Uh, sure, Mr. N? I: No R., Sir! How did the S at the end of your name come about? Burberrys: Ah... In the time when I was still a bit more active, it was considered -uh- noble to extend one's family name with this letter - uh uh -. Today it basically only stands for "Senior". (Or for senile, forms in my head. Arthur comes in and sets down two huge glasses, in which a puddle of green stuff swirls) Burberrys: Thank you, Arthur. (turning to me) Burberrys: Cheers, Mr. M. I: Cheers, Sir. (Urgh.. Mint and - wait, juniper?) I: This is quite good, Sir! (Lie!) Burberrys: Yes, isn't it? It is made exclusively for me by a very well-known liqueur manufacturer - uh-. Did you occasionally - uh - know that I have a - uh - very respectable garden? I: No. Are you a hobby gardener? (How boring. British cliché fulfilled!) Burberrys: Oh, I wouldn't go that far. I have very capable gardeners who cultivate a - uh - select variety of plants under my guidance - uh-.. But see for yourself, Mr. - uh - F. (He rises and leads me to a large glass door that opens into a park-like garden. My gaze falls on a branched tree with fleshy leaves) Burberrys: Beautiful, isn't it? This sandalwood tree from - uh - Ceylon. Isn't it a gem? I was honored to receive it from His Excellency the King. Back when - uh - Ceylon still belonged to us... The good old days indeed. I: How right you are, Sir. (Flattery) I: You also have a herb corner, as I can't help but notice? (Corner is no expression: A field full of lavender, pepper plants, and juniper bushes. Well, where the pepper grows...) Burberrys: You can't do without it these days - uh -. Basically, I cultivate the best lavender plants in the world - uh uh -. I: And in between juniper? (A probing look over the curling mustache falls on me like a ton of mercury) Burberry: What do you mean - uh? Juniper? That's for gin... I - uh - like to have a gin now and then and let my ration be distilled here - uh - a habit from my - uh - military days. (So indeed: A colonial colonel and a drunkard to boot! Probably already in India during Queen Victoria's time) I: And back there? The little corner with the carnations, roses, marjoram, jasmine? (A critical look sweeps over me. The left eyebrow arches up) Burberrys: My gardener said it would fit color-wise into the - uh - picture. Doesn't it fit, Mr. - uh - ? I: Yes, yes. Wonderful. It rounds off the garden. Burberrys: Let's go back inside. I have a - uh - lounge there. (We go back into his palace and through a few corridors into a much smaller dark room) Burberrys: Please - uh - have a seat. The leather armchairs are still from my time in - uh - India... (So indeed: a colonial uncle! On the other hand: Nice furniture, pleasant smell, and comfortable to boot.) I: You were in India? How interesting. It must have been warm there.. (I couldn't have asked him anything more stupid. India and warm - Does the bear shit in the woods?) Burberrys: You wouldn't - uh - believe how warm! I was also in Russia, after the - uh - Crimean War. There I hunted musk animals. A whole different - uh - climate. Do you see those little funny heads over there by the - uh uh - fireplace? I shot all of them - uh -. (Oops, a small animal killer too. I need to get out of here...) I: Looking at the time, Sir, please tell me why you have withdrawn. (A sad look from dachshund eyes sweeps over me, a twitch around the mustache... Nanana, is the old man getting sentimental?) Burberrys: Uh, you know, the - uh - times have become so fast-paced. No one has time anymore to devote themselves - uh - to the nicer sides of life. Even - uh - you, Mr. D, look - uh - very often at your - uh - timepiece. This - uh - eternal hustle and bustle does not suit me - uh - and is not compatible with my dignity - uh -. I said goodbye to the old Burberrys, not without feeling a bit sorry for him, the great old man. A bit crazy, excitable, and out of touch with the times, but in his time he was fully on top. I like him. And maybe he will dare to step out of his palace again - hopefully without a gun.

And already the next vintage OF has moved in with me... "Burberrys for Men" is both a typical and atypical English fragrance. Typical in terms of its fine and wonderfully balanced structure, which radiates warmth and "homeliness," and atypical due to its strength. Yes, even Burberry had to (or wanted to) step it up a bit at the beginning of the powerhouse era, composing fragrances that are more assertive and robust. Quite strong, this colleague is never intrusive. Rich spice and warmth are evident right from the start, making it hard for bergamot and lavender to hold their ground. It becomes wonderfully complex in the heart; new accords constantly emerge and fade away. A highly varied olfactory journey is offered here, before the accents beautifully unite in the base and let the fragrance fade away. A clear candidate for autumn and winter. Classic and of noble elegance. Certainly suitable for tweed, coat, and cardigan as well as for English drizzle.

The quiet beauty of a sunset evening. The cool wind, which brought from afar the aroma of fresh wet grass and bergamot, slowly walks through the fields, gently waving the stalks of lavender and wheat. Suddenly, speeding up, he suddenly reached a small garden with blooming irises and, enchanted by their delicate powdery aroma, calmed down, as if falling asleep, hiding himself in a velvet blanket of purple petals. Here, sour citruses, bitter, fresh-spicy herbs and neroli give way to tickling nose lavender, dry earth and soft powdery iris, wrapped in a weightless woody-vanilla flair and fluffy soft musk. Rimbaud Celine is a fragrance of fragile beauty dedicated to the French poet Arthur Rimbaud. His creative path was only 4 years, but in this short period he became famous throughout the world.

I barely smell lavender here. Instead, I mostly just get slightly powdery orris butter. It's incredibly simple and linear, but executed so incredibly well. It's deliciously warm and slightly sweet, while nowhere close to cloying. It also smells rather natural, unlike many powdery scents, which are often reminiscent of cosmetics. A soft and gentle perfume.

RIMBAUD starts with a powerful lavender opening….. The herbaceous quality is quickly joined by the powdery touch of a buttery soft iris….gentle sweetness makes its entrance…. After a few minutes - when lavender and iris butter have united - neroli joins in with a zesty-fruity sweetness…..and then immediately recedes…. The fragrance remains exceptionally soft and even intensifies its powdery facets……possibly the listed wheat acts as a kind of “powder-cream booster”……or perhaps it’s the now clearly perceptible fine clouds of musk……. The initial brute herbaceousness of the lavender has vanished……now it is pleasantly soft, rounded, and tender….. Together with iris butter and a beautiful, delicate, and natural vanilla, it becomes an impressively harmonious “whole”…… Especially noteworthy: Each new note that joins in during the course blends - after a brief, intense flash - immediately with the already present notes….. RIMBAUD is a delicate and elegant fragrance with a pleasant amount of sweetness and powderiness……. a skin scent with subtle sillage, yet it shows presence and endurance…. The often invoked lavender/vanilla duo reveals itself here in its noble, understated, and quiet side and never drifts into the depths of a sticky, syrupy gourmand……

Just two weeks ago, I rated Rimbaud a 9 and wrote a statement. In the meantime, the sample is empty, a bottle has been acquired, and I have come to the conclusion that neither the number nor a few words can do justice to this magnificent scent. Many of you surely remember that one teacher whose detailed explanations you wanted to avoid at all costs. Not because you didn’t like them or because you didn’t need the explanations. Simply because they enjoyed drinking coffee during breaks and indulging in a cigarette. I wholeheartedly wish that soothing break to everyone - unfortunately, this enormous scent mixture that these teachers exuded from their mouths afterward still evokes pure horror in me to this day. As a teacher of highly pubescent teenagers, I have very concrete ideas about how my fragrance should work due to this unforgettable olfactory experience. I do not want them to avoid my explanations. My perfume must not fill the classroom (the teens already take care of that with their overused body sprays). It must not be perfumey, loud, kitschy, annoying, piercing, fidgety, or intrusive. I want the teenagers to perceive only a pleasant, subtle, calm, well-groomed, and warm scent when I lean towards them. Only very subtly, perhaps even subconsciously. But still in a way that it remains a positive memory. Rimbaud meets exactly these criteria, and I am already sure that many teenagers will associate this scent with me. It certainly touches me. Rimbaud opens with a wonderfully authentic and natural lavender. It smells exactly like the pure lavender oil that sits on my nightstand. I love this naturalness and was a bit disappointed during the first tests that the lavender had already faded after half an hour. However, I can now perceive it very subtly in the background throughout the entire scent development. This perfectly fulfills my desire to wear a calm scent in the classroom. After half an hour, the familiar and highly valued "Celinade" takes the lead. Just like in "Black Tie | Celine" and "Dans Paris | Celine," I feel incredibly comfortable with this delicate, gentle, understated, noble, and well-groomed vanilla in Rimbaud as well. At the same time, I now also perceive the wheat. It is difficult to put into words. But it gives the scent that certain something, and I find it pleasantly soft and warm. The iris butter also contributes to fulfilling my wishes. Neroli, however, my nose does not recognize. The scent remains like this for several hours until it gently sneaks away over the vanilla. It is so close to the skin (even quieter than "Black Tie | Celine" and Dans Paris ) that I needed a few attempts to perceive it for longer than two hours. In the meantime, I can actually smell it all day long, and I look forward to that every morning.

Hedi Slimane can certainly not be denied one thing: that he works or has worked very successfully for his respective ventures and companies. Dior, YSL, self-discovery phases and processes, and now he is supposed to finally bring Celine into shape. This will also work, as he is now allowed to almost dictate everything (with) and is also leading the release of the new perfume creations of the house. His bottle design is classic - Chanel-like-private-influenced - and beautifully staged. Quality glass and a heavy magnetic cap adorn the latest offspring of the Celine family. I was curious not only about the beautiful other Celine perfumes but also about the fragrance named after the poet Arthur Rimbaud. Rimbaud himself: a consistently gifted individual, who throughout his life wrote poetry full of restlessness, adventured, and was also very successful as a businessman - always in search of a new identity. This may now also be found in the Celine portfolio: After the statements that the Celine scents under Slimane have definitely been able to set olfactorily (Celine DNA with vanilla and lily plant iris), Rimbaud starts off quite softly from the beginning. The cool lavender has enough space at the start to secure its place and brings one of Slimane's favorite plants back to the forefront for the first time. Caution: on plain paper, lavender remains dominant for a long time, but on skin, it is quickly overtaken by the iris - without losing its way. Memories of Eau Noire by Dior come to mind, where a bit more was dared - however, the two fragrances have nothing in common, I also do not smell the often-read DHI, as only the iris is associative... Neroli crouches off the path, the Celine vanilla grounds the cool, gentle scent and warms it towards the end. I was reminded of Miya Shinma's "Yuki," and a comparison with Tom Ford's "Lavender Extreme" would also be fitting, which is just much more lavender-forward and without the iris antagonist. The advertised wheat note I can only slightly detect here, perhaps it keeps the sweetness of the vanilla in check - Rimbaud does not become too sweet, after all. Slimane succeeds as the main responsible party in creating a beautifully light lavender iris, which quietly - but certainly - expresses its opinion and wonderfully showcases the interplay of both major ingredients, without being just a mild breeze.

Imagine you are in a beautiful place in nature. You let your gaze wander. There are many fields here. Nearby, a wheat field sways in the wind. You yourself stand in the midst of a lush, purple lavender field. The sun is shining. It radiates on your skin and warms you, it is so warm and cozy. Feel its touch, feel its warmth, enjoy it. The lavender has a rich scent.

Blind tests are known - they are often done to stimulate the senses... to judge without prejudice! But that is not what this is about today. It’s about samples that are sent without sender and labeling, which leave the recipient in despair... especially when they are participating in what feels like 83 sharings (you know how it is) and have ordered another 35 samples.

This fragrance is highly praised here. So I wanted to test it too. I don't like lavender (except for Goddess Eau de Parfum , where I hardly notice it) in fragrances. My nemesis is Mon Guerlain Eau de Parfum , which I really dislike, as well as all the flankers.
Rimbaud had been on my watchlist for a while, but I never actively sought out a sample.

In the opening, strong lavender paired with wheat. Lavender fields in France. The strong lavender quickly fades and smells pleasantly warm. Wheat is perceptible on its own, while the lavender takes a backseat. Musk, iris butter, and vanilla join in, making the fragrance very pleasant.

Pi Neo is like a fresher, more woodsy and less syrupy version of the original Pi. I find this fragrance much more wearable, and dare I say, much more unisex. Keeping with the futuristic idea, Pi Neo has sparkling citric notes and balanced, fresh woodsiness. I am particularly intrigued by this fragrance, even though it isn't what I'd call unique. This isn't really sexy, in my opinion it's a nice, cuddly and casual fragrance. It also has a rather clean feel to it, but not in a soapy or powdery sense of the word. I find the overall composition very refreshing, and certainly lovely on the right skin type. The ice-blue colour of the bottle actually represents the scent well. I find the scent rather chilling and icy. There is definitely less vanilla is this fragrance when compared to its predecessor. The lasting strength of Pi Neo is pretty good, however the sillage is quite intimate, meaning that it doesn't project strongly. Despite my obvious preference for Pi Neo over the original Pi, I do believe that those that love the original will most likely like this, even use it as a Summer version.

Actually Pi Neo is a step below the original Pi. Nothing innovative. It's a good scent indeed, but it smells inoffensive: weak cedar base with some vanilla and patchouli. I'd pass on this one and get original Pi. Sillage, lasting power and projection are weak-medium. Updated January 2014

After the original Pi is undeniably a very good vanilla fragrance, it was finally time to test Pi Neo. Thanks to Grayscale for the sample. Although you do see it occasionally in department stores, it has always slipped away from my testing fingers... However, I had very low expectations despite the original being a classic, and there were hardly any test stimuli. And Pi Neo once again proves how practical it can be for a fragrance when the test subject has low expectations that can hardly be undercut but can be quickly exceeded. For my taste, Pi Neo is a quite acceptable fragrance that doesn’t reinvent the wheel but certainly makes a decent impression. It reminds me, not least due to its similar cyber setting and marketing, of Paco Rabanne's better Ultraviolet. A bit worse for sure, but there are definitely similarities that can only be described as neo-cool. Pi Neo starts fresh, free, pious. Very youthful, cool, chilly, even somewhat metallic. A citrusy aluminum note, paired with powdery synthetic vanilla and woods that hardly see any pricks against the cold iron. I keep noticing that I like powdery scents, so it earns more points here. Unfortunately, you can tell in many corners that the fragrance was created with budget cuts in mind, making it often feel undercooled and much less warm and likable than the original. Also comparable is IceMen by Thierry Mugler, which offers a metallic-cool patchouli note. But with a reflective metallic look, all these perfumes share that trait. I was also reminded of some vanilla scents from the 90s like Nikos Sculpture or Minotaure. Bottle: not as beautiful as the original, but the Pi bottles are among the best on the mainstream market, walking a fine line between cool, beautiful, and kitschy. Sillage: due to the powdery base, it is quite assertive and strong for a summer fragrance. Therefore, I consider it more of an all-year-round scent. Pi for winter, Tropical Paradise for summer, and Neo for all other times - at least if you only want to wear Pi fragrances ;) Longevity: lasted a good 7 hours on me. Probably less in summer. I would never buy it and would only recommend it hesitantly. But two years ago, as a beginner in fragrances, I could have become very fond of this scent and wouldn't have gone wrong. Especially the fact that it appeals to average noses and draws compliments is a plus point that almost outweighs the high synthetic aspect as a downside.

The Pi Neo man is young, has a beard, and presents himself in a wide-open white shirt, backed by the Pi code. The bottle (designed by Serge Mansau) showcases a cool blue and, with its cap, reminds one of the big brother. The silhouette appears architectural, even mystical. A fresh, dynamic fragrance that targets the younger crowd. The scent feels sweet and cool. It reminds me of a white Mentos, perhaps not as sharp. I find it hard to describe the further development of the scent; it closely resembles Armani Code, and I can also detect hints of Fahrenheit 32. What "cosmone" is supposed to be remains a mystery. When I close my eyes, I also have the Andromeda Nebula in my mind; maybe that's because the original Pi was advertised with an astronaut... Edit: The fragrance comes from the company Givaudan.

For longer vacations, I like to buy fragrances that I have never used before, so that later I can associate that scent with the corresponding holiday in my memory. I treated myself to this fragrance in 2012 during a two-week vacation in the Midwest of the USA. The 30°C in California seemed to awaken a need for freshness and uniqueness in me, and "Pi Neo" fulfilled both. But after 2-3 months of use, it starts to become annoying. The synthetic must be the cause. At first, it’s interesting because it’s olfactorily unusual (where else do you smell Toscanol, Safraleine, or Cosmone?), but relatively quickly I became irritated by the artificiality of these fragrance notes. Nice, so I tested a cyber fragrance, but in the long run, I definitely prefer the many natural "classic" aromas of other men's fragrances.

when I first smelled the fragrance at Marionnaud in Paris, I found it totally likable. I bought it as a little souvenir, and when I returned from vacation, I couldn't stand the scent. I still used it a few times (rarely, but still a few times), after all, I didn't want to just leave the perfume sitting there. Over time, the scent somehow stuck with me.

Smells like the perfume department at Kaufhof just before closing time and has hardly anything to distinguish it from the hopelessly overcrowded market segment of generic and indefinable fresh waters. Yes, it’s fine, but is that enough? Citrus, wood, vanilla, yawn... The promised high-tech aspect eluded me; it feels more like it missed the train.

should perhaps test this fragrance sooner than someone who loves "Pi". Because this scent has nothing to do with "Pi". (about as much as "Sun Delight" has to do with "Sun" for the girls) A completely unique and significantly fresher and more modern fragrance. My recommendation. Just give it a try.

The presentation / advertising / website of Pi Neo clearly targets cyberspace users and aims to please all Keanu Reeves fans with its Matrix design... I recently tried the regular Pi and then the Pi Neo. If you own both versions, you’ve made it through the year quite well. For the cold winter days, the PI, and for the warmer season: PI Neo.

high school in 10th grade with my hated math teacher who tormented us with pi. Sure, it was his job, I hated it. Luckily, it was spring and we could open the window so our heads could cool off while we calculated everything in our heads. Yes, to the younger ones, I still belong to the generation that did the math in their heads. We all started to sweat.

A perfect cloud of powder and cream. So fluffy, so clean, never suffocating, dusty or sterile. This has the perfect amount of warmth and sweetness to not turn sharp and cold, but not more than that. I usually love vanilla, but I'm glad it wasn't added here. Orris is obviously the star of the show, and it's the buttery smooth kind. The rice powder adds another layers of powdery cosmetic cleanliness, and a hint of soft rose rounds it all off. This might not be the most original scent on earth, but it's so sophisticated and perfectly balanced that I don't mind at all. Céline does powdery scents very well in general, and Le Peau Nue toes the line between creamy and powdery flawlessly, leaning ever so slightly into the creamy site on my skin. This is very true to its name, it's the definition of a "your skin but better" scent. Like you just showered and pampered yourself with the most exquisite body butter and powder. Very easy to wear and more of a daytime scent, but with a subtly sexy undertone, like a suggestion of the clean naked skin underneath our clothes.

a stunningly beautiful combination of orris butter and rose. smooth as silk; powdery, but not in any way scratchy or suffocating. this is definitely on the makeup side of orris' many facets; the finest milled pressed powder, or the most creamy-soft and buttery lipstick. the rose tames it into a slick of pink and beige skin shades, lightly effervesced by the merest sparkle of bergamot in the opening. incredibly minimal yet executed perfectly. by the point of late dry down, the orris is less buttery and takes on a more traditionally musky-powdery facet. with the vetiver, which introduces itself gradually and subtly, the rose becomes dried and brittle, almost reduced to a pale powder itself. there is also a touch of vanilla as well that begins to emerge. it does seem to augment and sweeten the rose a touch, but again, only so far as to support the main duet and not disturb it. it is, overall, akin to the description, of being like watching a photo de-saturate from overexposure to light and age, or a memory gradually fade to white static. quite nostalgic and melancholic in a way. longevity seems amazing, but it mostly stays close to the skin aside from the opening. that aside, all in all, perfection to my nose.

i really didn't think i needed this; i have Fleur de Peau Eau de Parfum and it's one of my favorite perfumes of all time. that said, they do not compare. but i thought i had this "box" checked, is what i'm getting at. i'm really focused on keeping my collection one of only signatures, as small as possible. but i had a few of samples of this, and, as it would turn out, my memory of this scent was not at all correct...oh i needed this after another few testings! anyway--i haven't been reaching for FdP lately because it's just so strong and eternal, whereas this is much more delicate and light, and yes: it disappears eventually (though not quite entirely). FdP is also very DRY to me -- beautifully dry, it's texture is sort-of edible in a way i can't explain other than it's almost toothsome, like al dente pasta. this has a lightness and its lipsticky vibe is, and forever will be, a favorite of mine. neither one is better than the other, they are very different girls. this is by far my easiest reach. even when i don't want to wear anything, i can wear this. and i OFTEN want to wear nothing, but...that's not really an option (for the most part). nothing about this is overpowering or annoying to me. and, honestly, this is the MOST "Celine" of their fragrances, in my opinion (which is worth nothing). this girl is not expensive for the sake of being so -- she's classy, refined, she just knows no other way to be. somehow effortless, in that whole closet-full-of-neutrals way that i personally enjoy mimicking. it's almost like...OF COURSE something like this would be expensive. what i mean is, perfume is so expensive these days, ALL OF THEM! it's actually insane WHAT SOME JUICES COST and simply just aren't worth the cost of the cardboard box they haphazardly stuff them into. but this is deserving of its price tag: you literally don't have to think about it at all, and that's priceless. i get--and LOVE--the baby wipes association (am a mom). but the lipstickiness keeps it interesting.

The rice powder accord is really interesting at first. However, after a few seconds, all I smell is baby wipes. Powdery, clean, inoffensive, smooth, and unexciting. I don't want to wear it again. I was hoping for some more complexity: I don't smell any rose or vetiver in here. Or some more allure: I don't mind the scent of baby wipes, but I'm not drawn to it either. The second half of the drydown, after maybe 4 or 5 hours in total, is a lot nicer. The rice powder is pretty much gone by then, as is the powderiness overall. The orris butter then starts adding a warm sweet creaminess that finally moves the scent away from the baby-wipe profile. This stage of the scent I thoroughly enjoy — but still not enough to redeem the rest.

LA PEAU NUE opens with a wonderfully cool, yet incredibly sensual iris that merges with the skin like creamy butter…..infinitely soft, milky bright, velvety gentle, tenderly enveloping and caressing…… Fragrance becomes skin. Skin becomes fragrance. Fine rice powder lays like a gossamer veil over the entire scent…..giving it elegance and a touch of nostalgia…….bringing warmth…. The rose absolute, which kept me from testing for a long time, blends in, does not take center stage, and merely provides a subtle, classically polished appearance……. Vetiver and bergamot also remain subtle…….from their “cover,” they contribute just the right amount of freshness and regulate the sweetness…… Like all Celine fragrances, LA PEAU NUE is also very delicate and skin-like…….the longevity, however, is surprisingly good….. For me personally, it is an exceptionally beautiful iris scent that starts cool and becomes warmer over time…….caressing, bright, gentle, well-groomed, soft, harmonious, sensual…..and very feminine….. Addendum: After two days of “full-body fragrance” (so not just on the hand), I find that the scent - for me personally - develops a bit too sweet……I am, however, quite “intolerant” when it comes to sweetness…….I will still keep the overall rating at 10, because it is truly a great fragrance…….only my “personal” rating I would lower to 8.5-9……

"This smells like a noble cream" - with these words, La Peau Nue was sprayed on me at Celine. And yes, to a certain extent, I agree: the fragrance is very noble, powdery, and wonderfully well-groomed. But at the same time, it is also a bit strange, almost uncanny, but in a positive sense... The beginning is different from what I expected.

For me, La Peau Nue is a fragrance that combines cleanliness, freshness, powderiness, creaminess & innocence. The first image that comes to my mind when I spray the fragrance and sniff it is a clean, freshly creamed and powdered baby bottom or baby skin in general. The scent opens slightly fresh and zesty, although I personally hardly perceive the bergamot.

Since I am currently a bit reluctant to buy Guerlain fragrances, which have always been my favorites, I am looking for alternatives. The fragrances from Celine are absolutely not new to me, and I knew that I definitely wanted to add some to my collection. Briefly about why I don't want to buy Guerlain fragrances!

....sautéed in butter, was my first thought. The scent of rice is, along with a subtle zestiness, the first thing that wafts towards you. In my opinion, this zestiness lasts quite a while. So a few drops of lime over the fluffy rice. I hardly perceive the rose. At some point in between, it subtly greets and breathes a bit of elegance into the rice ball.

It was actually much too late to set out. The twilight had not yet begun, but the weather was so dreary and damp that it took all her resolve to take the lonely path over the remote weir. She had to. The frozen remnants of snow crunched under her feet, but she was glad to have made her way down the path so quickly.

I've had this bottle since it came out but hadn't worn it in years. I remember liking it when it was released, but for some reason, it was never part of my rotation. I wore it to bed the other night and it was wonderful. I was worried it might show signs of turning, but I think since the bottle is opaque, it is preserved well. When I first smelled this I was working the fragrance counter at a major retailer; I think I was the only one who liked it lol. When I wore it the other night, I was reminded of the same scent image I had 10 years ago: a great-smelling dirty ashtray. I know some may turn their nose at this description, but I love deep, dark, bold fragrances and the description fits. It's nice to remember that JV actually made good fragrances at one time. Sadly, this one, like almost all JV frags, is not the best performer. Having said that, I was surprised that I kept getting wafts of this throughout the night, but it was basically gone by the time I woke up. There are strong similarities between this and 10 ans, so if you are able to get a hold of either fragrance and love bold scents, jump at the chance!

As an addition to a SOUK, the Platinum Edition landed in my mailbox. Never heard of it or seen it before. The JV’s have not really impressed me so far, which is why my expectations were not particularly high. The bottle is entirely in chrome with a small leather loop around the neck and the JV emblem as a pendant. It looks simple and beautiful; there’s nothing to complain about. The spray unit is certainly not the best since the invention of the bottle; however, it does its job without "leaking" -> fits. Right after spraying, the scent is very present and unusual. A mix of fresh bergamot, light spices, and cinnamon, which gives it a certain pronounced sweetness in the opening. The bitter orange plays a very subordinate role and is somewhat of a scapegoat. The fresh components prevent the fragrance from tipping over or becoming too cloying. On a test strip, this phase takes some time to calm down and transition into the heart note. When sprayed on the skin, I found that the transition happens faster and more harmoniously. I find the opening to be quite daring and rather original at the same time. Heart and base notes work closely together. Leather, incense, and vetiver... One might think that these three components together are too much of a good thing. However, my personal experience is that vetiver, in combination with one's own skin, often exudes a certain flair of soft or gentle leather. At least, that’s the association I have. Yes, I sometimes think of soft, supple, black leather, and the small leather loop around the bottle fits in very well here. null of the three components is overly dominant to the point where the scent becomes too much for me. Incense only flashes up now and then. Rather, the heart note is accompanied by a relatively dry amber and sandalwood. Together, the fragrance exudes a certain sensuality and sweet warmth. It is truly not a run-of-the-mill Mr. Happy scent. To me, it feels warm, slightly dirty, sensual, and very interesting. I usually get headaches from such scents (probably more psychological ;-)) and primarily prefer clear, transparent fragrances. However, this one manages to keep my attention. You can't test every fragrance extensively. Surely, this one has been sprayed on a test strip by some and perhaps two seconds later went straight into the next trash can... JV written off (as I almost did too). On the skin, it exudes a certain charm from the very beginning. It clearly stands out from other everyday scents. It has a uniqueness that I personally appreciate. The fragrance is noticeable, even though it’s not loud. Sillage and longevity are good; both, however, are not overwhelming (thankfully). In summer, I would not particularly recommend the Platinum Edition. While it would certainly work, as the scent does not smell musty, etc. at higher temperatures, there are more suitable representatives in your perfume cabinet for the warmer time of the year. The fragrance is only available in the 125ml variant. Since 2013, it has been on the market as a "limited edition." There should not be any procurement issues yet. A handful of clicks on the web and done. I cannot explain why the fragrance has only received 13 reviews and one comment so far. It is for this reason that I took the time to type down my impressions.

It's a pity that there are no comments on Varvatos Platinum Edition yet, especially since the reviews so far have been quite good. I want to give it a try because I find this fragrance very remarkable. My first impression was: expressive, harmonious, delicious. Upon the second sniff, as I focused more on the top notes, I thought to myself: No, this is not working at all... But let's take it step by step: The fragrance starts off, as already hinted, quite intense and I would almost not call this scent a fragrance at first, as a mixture hits you that reminds one of smoked ham, freshly shoe-polished leather boots in a garage, or a turpentine rag - softened by a hidden warm undertone. The powerful and somewhat animalistic start lasts for a good hour. The sillage is quite pronounced. After that, everything softens and the fragrance gradually becomes softer, more harmonious, and rounder. From this develops an absolutely pleasant, warm, and gourmand-like scent that defines the true character of Varvatos Platinum and does not change significantly until the end. It is not sweet, rather dry and malty-caramel-like with very long lasting power (up to 12 hours perceivable on the skin). Compared to other fragrances, I would place it in the direction of Tom Ford Noir (Eau de Toilette) or the VW fragrance Petrole. It also slightly reminds me of the very last phase of Mugler's Amen. In any case, I have never smelled a fragrance that undergoes such a pronounced turnaround. I occasionally enjoy smelling it and delight in this transformation. Personally, I will not wear it, as I do not want to leave the house smelling strong in the morning, waiting for the fragrance to eventually change into something pleasant. Moreover, there are too many culinary associations (like smoked ham and dessert) present for me, and that doesn't quite fit with a perfume. Nevertheless, I consider Varvatos Platinum to be a successful and beautiful fragrance. An experimental work of art that challenges, is fun, and somehow "plays with your nose." Ambivalent, delicious, and fascinating.

Eaudemoiselle is a rather basic fragrance. It's more modern than old-fashioned or vintage in my humble opinion. I was surprised to discover how fresh the scent is. I think I expected something richer and perhaps more floral. The scent strikes me as being a watery blend of rose, lemon, subtle herbs and musk. In my country, Eaudemoiselle appears to be a limited release, only being sold in the major capital cities. I don't see how this fragrance is better than other Givenchy releases. In fact I much prefer Ange ou Demon, Very Irresistible and Amarige over Eaudemoiselle. The release has come at a good time as Australia goes into the hot Summer months, which is the perfect weather to wear this fragrance. It's a rather polite and inoffensive scent, not being overly strong in terms of sillage, but having decent longevity. I'm slightly underwhelmed to be honest, even though I didn't have much in the way of expectations leading up to smelling it. It's delicacy has left me cold rather than impressed. There's an odd pear-like note that I keep smelling which is the only thing that intrigues me, to say the least. Because I can sense the pear and rose, I will compare this fragrance to Annick Goutal's Petite Cherie, even though the latter is much sharper and fruitier. Written: November 3, 2010.

I really love this scent. It starts out herbal and citrus for me - very delicious and fresh. Soon comes the beautiful rose in the heart very strong, but creamy and buttery and smooth. As it tones itself down I get a sense of something rich and nutty almost. Is that the tonka bean? I think the citrus gives this scent a less girly feel at the start which I like, but that soon morphs into a gentle floral and becomes very sweet. I am not a huge fan of florals, but this one has a different edge to it. I would be totally feel like a queen in my frothy prom dress wearing this scent...

This is a lovely scent. It has for me a slightly classic vintage vibe. The opening starts fresh with lots of rose and lemon, there is also a bit green note , I guess thats the basil. The ylang is there but not prominent, this note normaly makes me a bit nauseous, but not here. It blends nicely with the other notes. The drydown is a soft powdery musky rose. I love to wear this in warmer wheater such as spring and summer are

Rose powder, fresh Turkish rose tincture, and a splash of lemon to counter the sweetness. Jardin de Tuileries in the sunshine. Pink roses on green grass. Cheerful. Refinely girlish, but not prim or dusty. Basil adds a leafy green spiciness. Then Eaudemoiselle, with its floral powderiness, increasingly reminds me of the scent of a filled makeup bag or lipstick, as it smelled back in the 80s. Does Malle's Lipstick Rose smell like this too? There is a parallel in this heart note to Chloe's Love, only here the rose dominates instead of the hyacinth; or also to the new Balenciaga, which achieves the makeup powder effect through violets. However, Givenchy definitely lays it on the thickest, without wanting to value that negatively. Towards the end, the fragrance completely loses its last trace of freshness and becomes warmer and sweeter, as if warmed by the sun - now through ambrette and tonka. Later, the base becomes a bit more interesting, which I unfortunately cannot define with notes. Here I have the association of an exciting nighttime city still heated from the day? (Edit: It must be patchouli and a bit of vanilla!) The 80s chic is undeniable here, but it feels modernized through basil and lemon. Somehow, the fragrance also radiates something typically French to me. Perhaps it is the rose, which also plays the leading role in YSL's Paris. As a teenager, I had Givenchy's Very Irresistible for a long time and see Eaudemoiselle as a twenty-something successor that is a bit more mature and complex. The sunny-cheerful aspect of this fragrance gradually also has something shady, deep, almost nostalgically melancholic, which I really like about this scent. Unfortunately, the wonderful top note does not last very long, and the base warms up too quickly. I often long for a longer freshness effect here, which is why I wear it only very rarely. Otherwise, a great floral with a certain charm and chic, perhaps also for those who are not typical rose lovers.

François Demachy has managed in recent months to rise to the top of my favorite fragrance artists. He gives his scent masterpieces a unique signature that always points back to him, no matter which company he lends his nose to. In his creations, there is always a subtle aromatic nod to his roots in Provence, his hometown Grasse. Only the perfumers of the Guerlain family, including Patricia de Nïcolai as Jean-Paul's niece, rank above him in my personal value scale. But this is open-ended and not set in stone. The house of Givenchy has never been known for loud fragrances; here, elegant understatement is rather cultivated. Thus, the "waters" of this brand also possess a unique charm. Even "Eau de Givenchy" has sneaked into my heart with its light-footed beauty. On those days when "nothing" is already too much, it is a wonderfully unobtrusive companion. But I have already acknowledged this pleasant trait with a corresponding comment (see "The Sister Named Water"). And now "Eaudemoiselle": how delightfully old-fashioned that sounds! It immediately reminds me of the scene from Gotthold Ephraim Lessing's "Minna von Barnhelm," where Major von Tellheim's former sergeant Werner meets Minna's somewhat coquettish maid Franziska for the first time: "Frauenzimmerchen, Frauenzimmerchen - I see, she is pretty and probably quite foreign..." For me, this "Frauenzimmerchen" holds nothing disrespectful; this address contains so much astonished tenderness and respect from the simple man towards this young woman, who seems unattainable to him. Thus, "Eaudemoiselle" is also an exceedingly wearable gift for all women. At first glance, it appears almost simple and youthful due to the freshness of tangerines and Amalfi lemons, like a delicate budding flower of femininity, but soon the herbaceous spiciness of basil hints at a very different, more feminine development of this fragrance creation. Did not Lampedusa already write in "The Leopard" about an alley in Palermo where basil pots on the windowsills indicate that the ladies behind these windows are not averse to a gallant intermezzo? Basil can therefore be much more than just the herb that gives pasta its Mediterranean flavor. In the heart note, "Eaudemoiselle" thus becomes a bit more mature, losing the delicate melt of this youthful freshness: the mentioned flower bud opens up. For the noble rose with its feminine charm makes this fragrance no longer seem so innocent. Especially after it surrendered to the fragrant embrace of ylang-ylang. Both develop a very special olfactory relationship with each other. The sweet warm sensuality of musk and tonka bean is thus the fitting conclusion for this fragrant "Frauenzimmerchen." Nothing here is heavy or intrusive; everything is light and carries the magic and unmistakable light of Provence within it. Fruity freshness and herbaceous spiciness meet fragrant floral beauty before they sink together into a warm embrace. Thus, "Eaudemoiselle" is a graceful fragrance being that charmingly and smilingly accompanies you through the day and brings freshness and joy with every spray.

There is nothing to add to the (positive) comments below. Floral, fruity, woody, powdery. In the floral accord, no particular note dominates. However, a jasmine accord was definitely used (at least HEDIONE, benzyl acetate, hexyl cinnamon aldehyde, and indole).

Due to the comments, my interest in this fragrance was piqued. And it is astonishing how differently it is perceived. I will now contribute my part with my somewhat different fragrance description. But it is precisely these confusions and uncertainties that make this scent so multifaceted and lovable.

I discovered this fragrance at Karstadt - pleasantly understated, but without a tester. Since I like to surprise myself, I took the plunge and made a blind purchase. At home, with the first spray, I was overwhelmed by a wave of honey. Strangely, it is not listed. However, the honey note is by no means sweet, but rather straight and confident.

Eaudemoiselle starts with an interesting, citrus-spicy top note. The citrus fruits do not come across as lemon-fresh, but rather in the form of spicy-aromatic peel extracts that harmonize beautifully with the herbal note. However, the top note lasts unusually short, as the fragrance quickly develops floral and then becomes quite sweet.

I tested the fragrance based on the very different descriptions here and because of the basil note, which I find intriguing. Not too impressed with the packaging, black-and-white model photos in old frames adorn the box. Well. The bottle feels very nice in the hand, the ribbed glass reminds me of old cognac glasses.

This Celine fragrance is the epitome of quiet luxury—understated yet effortlessly refined, like a perfectly tailored wool coat on a crisp autumn day. Designed for cooler weather, it wraps around you like a comforting embrace, subtly enhancing your presence without demanding attention. While it leans gourmand, it never ventures into overly sweet or cloying territory. Instead, it strikes a delicate balance—rich and inviting but never overwhelming. The composition unfolds smoothly, making it an ideal transition from day to night, seamlessly adapting to different settings. It’s not a perfume for grand occasions, but rather a sophisticated everyday indulgence, perfect for those who appreciate elegance in the details.

I don’t know what’s going on here- this is a total flop for me. I love Celine’s DNA and most of the line. 1. Celine’s gorgeous vanilla is missing here, replaced with a weird plasticky chapstick textured caramel/vanilla. 2. null of Celine’s wondeful Orris- okay. There is barely a whisper of powdery amber under this strange plastic vanilla toffee? This smells NOTHING like Shalimar Iris (a favorite of mine) not black tie or Dans Paris. There is also a tartness (maybe Tonka) that comes across like fruity pebbles or cereal fruitiness. I wish they pushed the quirkiness and amped up the projection, maybe I would enjoy it more. It’s like when your favorite band put out a flop- disappointing.

Celine, Celine - you’ve done it again. Although “done it” doesn’t quite fit with Celine. Celine doesn’t crash in, doesn’t overwhelm. Celine fragrances appear, float in, stroll.. So does this dream of a poem. When I read the fragrance notes, I already had a rough idea of what to expect, yet it still hit me hard when I joyfully ran to my wife to inhale the delicious scent in her slipstream. Celine can do vanilla like only Guerlain can. They have definitely created their own DNA, and in this combination with tonka, musk, and benzoin, which is by no means new on the market, they have delivered their masterpiece. Now some will complain about the short longevity or the lack of sillage, but I think it’s just right as it is. Here, less is more, clearly. You’re not overwhelmed; it’s still present for a long time, sometimes it disappears only to come back again, and in the end, it even becomes a touch more beautiful. Where Dans Paris was previously my favorite, now two divine creations from Celine belong to my favorites. While I love Zouzou on my wife, I wear Dans Paris in the evening; it doesn’t get better than that. Celine, Celine - you enchant me, stay true to yourself and surprise us again someday; I can hardly wait.

Zouzou has what I smell in Shalimar Millésime Iris as caramel threads, the airy, light vanilla from "Dans Paris | Celine," and a hint of powderiness from "Black Tie | Celine." I also suspect what dear Cardea meant with the Baccarat Rouge 540 Eau de Parfum interpretation: there is a hint of BR 540 (perhaps due to the caramel undertone?), but minimal and in typical Celine elegance (if there were more of it, I would quickly make my escape). Zouzou is clearly a child of the Celine family! So, first of all, there’s really nothing that I would need to want, as the scent is a kaleidoscope of many fragrances from my collection. On the other hand, there is something behind it that makes it different. There is something bitter in Zouzou, a slightly green accent; a handful of earth; a crumbled piece of dark chocolate. The fragrance constantly shifts between all its facets; sometimes sweeter, sometimes earthier, always powdery - just like a chameleon. So, to summarize briefly: a blend of other fragrances - all are present in muted form. And yet distinct with an exciting green/bitter/earthy/chocolatey background hum, which I find magnificent. Very successful!

Zouzou by Celine is a fragrance that surprises me with its diverse facets and has captivated me immediately. From the very first application, a harmonious, addictive blend of vanilla sweetness and seductive lightness unfolds, instantly enchanting. But let's start from the beginning... Milan, late August - it's hot. Too hot for a sightseeing tour, so we used the day for an extensive fragrance stroll. We visited many exclusive perfumeries and boutiques, but I particularly want to highlight the excellent advice at Celine Milano, which perfectly rounded off my fragrance journey. The knowledgeable and passionate guidance helped me discover Zouzou for myself - a scent that can be worn both in everyday life and on special occasions. Zouzou is playful yet sophisticated. The seductive sweetness of vanilla, paired with benzoin, gives the fragrance an inviting warmth, while the patchouli note grounds the scent and lends it a refined restraint. This balance between sweet sensuality and elegant modesty makes Zouzou an extraordinary olfactory experience that is not easily categorized. For me, it is a successful blend of Black Tie and Coromandel, a hint of nostalgia combined with modern sophistication. Zouzou is indeed vanilla sweet, but I wouldn't categorize it as a gourmand. I would describe it as a unisex fragrance with a slight tendency towards the feminine side. Surprisingly, my partner also liked it so much that we bought the 200 ml bottle in the Celine Boutique on the same day. Our first shared fragrance... The bottle is kept very simple, and I like the magnetic closure cap. With its subtle sillage, Zouzou is also suitable as a daily companion from September to May. The longevity could be a bit better, at least in terms of projection, but it lasts quite long when up close. For anyone looking for a perfume that combines playful sweetness with an elegant and mature base, Zouzou is a wonderful choice. However, one should like vanilla. A fragrance that adapts to any situation without losing depth and character.

Dans Paris has a big sister; her name is Zouzou . And as it is with sisters, they are related and share certain attributes; however, they are both independent individuals. They are usually raised by the same parents, but will develop differently according to their own character. Otherwise, it would be boring.

I am still relatively new to the perfume bubble and had both Zouzou and Black Tie sent to me as samples. When I first applied Zouzou to my arm, I was instantly in love. This scent means perfection to me in terms of fragrance. It is so wonderfully balanced and beautiful, it never bothers, is never overpowering, yet still present.

I was so excited about this fragrance and could hardly wait for the release! Because I love almost all scents from Celine and the fragrance notes really appealed to me. Upon the first sniff, I immediately thought: Typical Celine!

I had the chance to test this amazing fragrance at Kadewe today and I fell in love immediately. The powdery - spicy vanilla, like in many Celine scents, enveloped me. One could almost say it's the child of Black Tie. Unfortunately, the nice consultant mentioned that it hasn't been launched yet.

The first impression that many will have: I know this from somewhere! Admittedly, it does remind me a bit of Black Tie, Shalimar Iris, or Bois Dore. I can even somehow pick out Tonka Bodykon. For me, the scent is most similar to Iris Dragées. It is definitely warmer and more vanilla-like, but there is also an undeniable kinship of the first or second degree here.

(Old version) If you are looking for a "Vetiver," you might be in the wrong place. The now more popular derivative Vetiverylacetate, chemically produced from nature, is not found here. Guerlain once had a convincing variant with the mentioned substance, but today, after what one might call adjustments to the times, it appears significantly flattened and also thin. With 'Vetyver,' it's about Vetiver in its two essential variants, Bourbon and Java. One is radiant, woody, and clean, while the other is musty, heavy, and dirty. The transition flows from top to bottom. Simplicity is the program. Nothing is complicated, one might think. The base appears after maybe 8 hours with a beautifully chocolatey accord of Java and sandalwood, greeting the day even in the morning. In the middle part, there is - compared to the very first reissue, a slight reduction of the coriander. It was previously almost too heavily applied. Thus, the perfume can also serve as a very prosaic wardrobe fragrance, which has transferred onto the laundry, for which Vetiver was often used. Quite simple, always works, and is loved in its distinctly unique way, see above the base accord. So far, I have found nothing that matches it in concentration, calmness, and rounding.

Thanks to a great sample gift, I was able to test Givenchy Vetyver in two variations: 2007 and 2014, which are presented here - nota bene - without distinction. I wore both on my skin to get a clear picture. One shouldn't be afraid of synthetics nowadays, as otherwise a large part of fragrances would immediately fall under the test table... In the top note, there are initially hardly any noticeable differences; it smells intensely of pomelo with a slightly herbal background. After about 30 minutes, however, the scent diverges a bit: in the 2007 version, a noticeably herbaceous-spicy note emerges with only a subtle wood accent, whereas the 2014 version drifts more towards a delicate spicy-woody direction and actually has an undertone of celery. As it develops further, the divergence even intensifies a bit: the 2007 composition adds a bitter note and a fine smokiness, while the 2014 version becomes sweeter and grassier. Interestingly, both then come closer together again in the drydown. The ingredient list on the packaging probably reveals the secret: while the 2007 version still contained oak moss extract, this bitter ingredient is completely absent in the 2014 version (thanks to IFRA), which is clearly noticeable in direct comparison. Neither of them are sillage bombs, but rather of the 'close to the skin' type; the longevity is also situated in the middle range. To what extent the term 'reformulation' is appropriate is probably more of a philosophical question - a bit too close to deserve the attribute 'completely independent', a bit too far to be considered merely a slight modification. I give an 8.5 to the 2007 version, as I personally preferred the herbaceous accent a bit more; the 2014 version, however, does not have to hide with an 8.0.

I own several vetivers, all of which I appreciate in their great diversity to varying degrees. Now, I bought the Vetyver by Givenchy blind - based on the almost exclusively very positive reviews, I thought that nothing could go wrong. But now I have a problem: it seems that I am the only one who cannot handle this scent at all. - What I primarily smell is a mix of sharp kitchen vegetables that have been chopped up in a blender. - I cannot perceive any vetiver at all. The scent is extremely unpleasant to me, so much so that I have had to wash it off 3 times, after giving it plenty of time to develop into something more beautiful. Maybe someone here can explain to me what might be going wrong and if others also have these sharp vegetable impressions. Why can I not perceive vetiver? Am I possibly the only one experiencing this??? - Then something is wrong with my nose. This has never happened to me with any vetiver scent.... This is not a comment, but rather a very personal problem report. That’s why I also refrain from rating it. Maybe someone can help me figure this out?

After I felt like I had written 2 comments almost every day for nearly a year, I felt a bit uninspired and tired yesterday, so despite having time and tested fragrances, I didn't write any comments. I even considered taking a writing break for a week or two to recharge my motivation and inspiration... It would fit well with a city tour in Hamburg and the Cologne Carnival in between... Well, that didn't really work out, as you can see today. The Alsterhaus was just too impressive, and the hours spent testing there were overwhelming. I once again faced the question of what to put on my skin... The new Tom Fords? Exclusive Guerlains? Rare finds like Givenchy's Vetyver that are hardly ever seen? It's clear that every fragrance fan would agree: the latter! And so I tested this top-rated, otherwise rather unknown Vetiver scent on Parfumo, and as a fan of the genre, there was no big lamenting about it. A dry-classic, somewhat darker Vetiver for everyday wear, a cross-section through the history of this fine category! Not as citrusy as the Guerlain, but similarly classic. Not as dry as the Extreme version from Guerlain, but still rough. Not as gloomy as Sycomore or Encre Noir, but also not cheerful-sunny, rather gray marbled. Not as clear as the one from Frederic Malle, but still high-quality. Not as stiff as Grey Vetiver, but still elegant. Not as clean and green as Original Vetiver, but also not dirty, just a bit edgy. No matter how much Vetiver I test, pearls keep surfacing! Bottle: large, yet grippy, clear in its lines and stylish. Sillage: an all-rounder and light Vetiver mix. Longevity: still present as a skin scent even now in the evening in the Hamburg hotel room: 7-8 hours. Rightly highly rated, yet unjustly so unknown worldwide... While it doesn't reinvent the Vetiver wheel, it still belongs to the elite and is extremely balanced and refined, without ever becoming boring for even a second!

I tasted all Celine Exclusive line and i have to say i was suprise that in this period of “hey lets make a perfume, it is a good busness today” Period when new perfumes are falling on us like heavy rain, they still manage to create nice line. This one is my favorite. It is clean iris with fresh notes of some citrus and just right perfect not sweet sweetness. It stays on clothes days but very soft clean beautiful pleasant scent. It is nothing head turning. Its sopay clean (Infusion iris kind of) scent. No, it is not similar to Infusion iris but in same cathegory; expensive clean smell.

I can't decide which Celine fragrance I like best. Black Tie? La Peau Nue? This? Yes, maybe this one. They're all so wonderfully soft and fluffy, yet a the same time sophisticated and elegant. Saint-Germain-des-Près is the freshest of the bunch. It starts out with classic cologne-like neroli and petitgrain, and then quickly uncovers its pretty base of vanilla, sweet heliotrope and iris. Celine really does iris so well, it's clean and powdery here, very minimalistic without any hints of earthiness or lipstick. The rest of the scent feels very creamy. It has a perfect balance of warm and cool notes. It kind of smells like what I imagine luxury products for babies would smell like. Angelic. This would make the perfect daytime signature. I can't imagine a time or place where it would be inappropriate to smell like this cream and powder dream, except for a smokey bar or club. It's just way too innocent for that.

Despite the note breakdown, it is green and a tiny bit sharp up front from the Petitgrain, but that sharpness quickly dissipates, and dries down to a a slightly sweet lemon custard & marshmallow powdery vanilla. This doesn’t project very far, but I love the ethereal scent bubble it gives me. This would work great as a signature scent and is inoffensive but still high quality.

A sample of Saint-Germain-des-Prés came with my purchase of Dans Paris. From the notes, I expected to love this. However, that is not the case. The petitgrain opens very green, like crushed green leaves and some drops of tea sap. Reminds me to when I made some cuttings from my Philodendrons early in Spring. But there is something very sweet, very powdery, and very screechy accompanying the petitgrain here. I sprayed it on my wrist once, with the tiny atomizer from the sample, and it's so strong that after 5 minutes it gave me a headache lol. This definitely can't be more different compared to Dans Paris in terms of sillage! But for the price? To be honest the Un Jardin line from Hermes is much better if you're looking for some fresh green scents.

this does indeed evoke a powdery, soft sweetness akin to marshmallows on my skin in opening, but it's backed by a citric, slightly bitter and woody combination of neroli and petitgrain; it almost has a nuttiness to it not too far from vetiver. the citrusy notes die down quite quickly and the sweetness drastically tones down as time passes from the opening. the base is actually similar to what i find 'la peau nue' dries down to. (from memory at least, i haven't tested them side-by-side) it's certainly a reserved scent, to say the least, calming considerably from first spray. muted, powdery, slightly rooty notes (orris) with a shy hint of vanilla (hinting a little playdough / dollhead-like) persist on the skin for some time but at a 'nose-to-skin' level. it's perfectly pleasant, but this just doesn't take to me as much as 'la peau nue' did.

Paris! Ah! When one thinks of Paris, everyone has their own unique way of envisioning this city. There are as many associations with Paris as there are countless sights in this city. With such a plethora of options, describing the places, spots, and buildings visited can often be challenging.

Today I wrapped myself in Saint-Germain-des-Prés for the second time. One doesn't want to be hasty, after all.... First of all, I want to say right away: Saint-Germain-des-Prés is a wonderfully composed fragrance. Softly powdery-fresh, light green, graceful, gentle, and well-groomed.

I make no secret of it, I love clean scents. Not necessarily those that smell strongly of soap, or the typical fabric softener or "fresh laundry scents," it shouldn't be too powdery either, but Saint-Germain-des-Prés fits my preferences perfectly. It is simply a brilliant blend of green/fresh/creamy/soft/clean.

Soberly considered, Saint-Germain-des-Prés is probably just "merely" a well-groomed cream scent. But what this fragrance does to me is almost magical. This wonderfully unconventional, biting opening with bitter Petitgrain and clear Neroli - marvelous!

After my love for Rimbaud was so great and I reordered another 10 ml from a dear perfumer, I received a sample of this fragrance as a gift! The joy was immense! It performs similarly to Rimbaud... right at the beginning it is very green and floral... Neroli + Petitgrain say just like the lavender & wheat in Rimbaud: "Hello, WE are here now".

After being convinced and blown away by the 3 most famous John Varvatos fragrances (Artisan, Vintage, JV), I had to test the rare, discontinued (?) 10th Anniversary in the store today. And I bet, if it didn't remind me so much of the last masterpiece I acquired from Andy Tauer, L'Air de Desert Marocain, the anniversary edition would have immediately found its way into my collection. But the Tauer gem is indeed very similar, more complex, and better. However, I still fully stand by JV and am glad to own the 3 fragrances! 10th Anniversary starts off smoky. The incense hits me hard, paired with a leathery sweetness that once again reminds me of syrup. Not too sweet, not too bitter - just right, and the common thread runs through the JV fragrances (except for the 2 Artisans). Cinnamon, citrus fruits, and a few spiced woods round it off here and there. The incense reveals itself as patchouli, and it unfolds as gently as rarely a patchouli does on my skin. Delicious, spicy, straightforward, uncomplicated, playfully sacred, Arabic - and worthy of an anniversary! The bottle is really good, smooth, high-quality, and a real eye-catcher in any collection. Longevity hovers around the 10-hour mark, and the sillage was smoky and autumnal bitter for me. Another proof of the great work being done at JV and a festive anniversary full of incense and patchouli!

It just happened. I am so ashamed. But I didn't do it on purpose, it was ... careless of me, I know. But I want to improve. I've been blaming myself for hours and biting my nails, non-stop. How could I forget John Varvatos' 10th birthday? Shame on me. After all, the birthday fragrance is on everyone's lips, or rather, in everyone's noses and of course in the print media. It may not have reinvented the wheel, but the scent is quite successful and makes a good impression for the 10th; apparently, it heralds a promising future for JV. Sweet-spicy is the opening, the orange comes through loud and clear. The sweetness diminishes a bit - which is better! - in the heart note and makes way for a transformation from spice to sharpness. But it is not sharp in the sense of pepper, rather a fresh breeze of sharpness. At the same time, a leathery note comes in and makes the scent - macho! The base is dark green, but subtle. Spice, freshness, and leather until the end, none of them dominant, but very nicely balanced. Could become a classic.

I have never paid attention to the scents from Varvatos. Why, I can't explain for the life of me. Maybe it's because people have always tried to push these fragrances on me, which I can't stand. Well, yesterday during a shopping trip, the new silver bottle caught my eye in the department store. Oh, I thought, why not. I grabbed the silver bottle and sprayed a generous amount on the back of my hand. First impression: spicy orange over earthy heavy sweetness. After a little while, the patchouli heart comes through with a hint of leather and some vetiver. On a late spring day, it’s not necessarily a fitting scent, but still quite pleasant. The patchouli note lasts a long time before it transitions into a balsamic-woody finish. On this note, the 10th anniversary takes its sweet time before it finally fades away. Since I am not familiar with the other Varvatos scents, I was positively surprised by this one. However, it wasn't a sensational fragrance experience either. All in all, a sweet, well-made, and above all, wearable scent.

Well-crafted men’s fragrances come from John Varvatos, which are offered in exceptionally beautiful bottles. The 10th Anniversary, presented entirely in silver with a subtle “chain”, is worth its price just for that reason - a must for John Varvatos fans! The scent itself opens quite typically: dark, smoky, leathery. I already allowed myself to question whether this anniversary edition is even a new fragrance. Yes, it is, and that becomes clear as we go on. Contrary to what was indicated, I initially perceived the smokiness as incense. Well - maybe I was off there. Only gradually does the actual theme emerge: patchouli. From about an hour in, the 10th Anniversary is nothing else - a bright patchouli accord. It has something fresh, then at times something chocolatey, slightly sweet, and it determines the rest of the experience. The 10th Anniversary is thus the most oriental perfume from John Varvatos so far, but I believe the fan community will embrace it. Just the mention of such a mystical fragrance ingredient as patchouli is likely to be a selling point for many - and then there’s such a well-crafted bottle! The 10th Anniversary also has that certain Varvatos style: distinctly masculine, but not overpowering. In its relative opulence, I would recommend it for the cold season. That the 10th Anniversary is fundamentally quite one-dimensional is unlikely to matter much. It definitely earns sympathy points from me, although I - unfortunately, unfortunately - do not tolerate patchouli well at all. So I must leave the 10th Anniversary to others.

That was my first thought while testing. Pleasantly summery-sweet scent with mild rose and an eccentric fruity note of pineapple and - although not listed - peach or nectarines, with no trace of allspice and amber. Just a light feel-good fragrance that doesn’t want to be too heavy-handed. A few days later, when I was out to dinner with a friend, I realized why the scent felt so familiar: It smells like the Elvital dream length shampoo that she always uses... So it’s a pleasant scent, but you can also get it for €2.50 at the drugstore.

After a disappointing fragrance experience yesterday, reaching for Live was a relief. I also enjoy Very Irresistible - and Live is in no way inferior to it. A "good mood relaxer" comme il faut. Fruity, yet soft, the pineapple greets me - without any acidity. Then a full pink rose joins in - slightly citrusy like the Leonardo da Vinci in my garden, which I can't get enough of. The allspice note adds a piquant and very distinctive touch. Amber and musk make Live fluid and cuddly - like my pink summer dress that sways with every step. Sweet vanilla gently envelops me, providing a sense of security. A completely likeable feminine fragrance that allows for closeness and signals it as well. My husband chuckles, saying that with Givenchy, you can't go wrong. He is right once again.

..., to start an irresistible life! This is how Givenchy advertises the perfume, and I am excited to write my first comment about it. Live Irrésitible is a feel-good scent ... it puts me in a spring mood. It makes me crave a delicious tropical ice cream sundae. Sun, warmth... ah... perfect for a frustrating rainy day like today. The fragrance pyramid is a bit sparse here. There is much more in this tropical-fruity-sweet scent cocktail. Top notes: Pineapple, rose petals, grapefruit, tangerine Heart notes: Rose, pepper, passion fruit Base notes: Amber, musk, iris, patchouli, praline, vanilla. Now to the scent: Live Irrésitible starts fruity-sweet with a hefty dose of pineapple and a bit of citrus also comes through. I soon detect some pepper, and rose is also involved. The combination is successful. Pepper and the citrus fruits temper the sweetness. It doesn't stop at pineapple; it becomes even more tropical... The passion fruit joins in. The scent is not yet spectacular, but the base is quite something ;) Amber comes across as spicy and embraces the fruits. I don't detect iris, but patchouli is there, albeit only lightly with a fine praline note. Vanilla seems to shy away from my skin; at least I don't perceive it on myself. Personally, I think this doesn't harm the fragrance, as it is already sweet enough. For me, it's a fruity-sweet-tropical-ambered scent that is special and stands out from the sweet fragrance variety. The longevity is very good ... it lasts 8 - 10 hours on my skin. The sillage is not overwhelming but noticeable. The bottle is also very pretty to look at and has a nice grip. Naysayers claim Live Irrésitible is limited. I hope that's not the case, as it is a must-have, and I wouldn't want to miss it in my collection.

I sometimes argue with my partner… or perhaps we discuss. The thing is, that we seem to differ a lot in taste. Especially when it comes to perfume. I love the strong florals, which some would say are a bit out of fashion. He loves the light ones. On me. This morning he asked me what perfume I was wearing. Knowing this is code for: I do not like, I said that this is Boucheron. An icon, I added. But there is not need to argue. This is a great late 80s. No matter how you twist or turn reality, this is just really great. It has the amazing fruity-floral beginning, the warm floral heart and the spicy-woody ending. I love it. My bottle is too small, no matter what… you can not argue about that. 274/365

This perfume embodies the essence of understated elegance, making it the perfect introduction to the Celine fragrance collection. Its simplicity is its strength—never overwhelming, yet undeniably refined. The scent carries an air of quiet luxury, effortlessly sophisticated without the need for bold statements. It’s the kind of fragrance that feels naturally elegant, like a well-tailored outfit or a classic piece of jewelry. Ideal for daytime wear, it offers a light yet distinctive presence, making it suitable for both professional settings and leisurely outings. The balance of notes ensures that it remains fresh and inviting throughout the day, enhancing the wearer’s aura without overpowering the senses. If you appreciate fragrances that exude effortless grace and refinement, this is a must-try.

This is a fragrance I wasn’t overly impressed with initially, but it’s grown on me and become a favourite. It is very light, but I also find it uplifting. I really like the light, airy citrus and moss combination. This reminds me slightly of Gateaux Des Anges, not because it smells anything like it, but it has a similar airy quality. The dry down of Parade does have a metallic type of note, maybe similar to Valaya but it’s a 100x’s better than that scent imo! I can still smell the citrus notes and I do find this actually lasts quite a while on me. It did create a nice scent bubble that I was able to smell it for a good 6 hours.
