For me Parade is a beautiful, comforting, elegant, feminine fragrance. It’s the type of scent that makes you feel classy and put together. I can’t wait to wear in spring and summer, although I’ll still wear this all year round though.

Celine Parade is one of those fragrances that feels effortlessly refined from the first spray. It’s extremely well-balanced, every note melts together in a smooth, seamless way, with nothing sharp or overwhelming. The citrus opening is bright without being loud, and the musky dry-down is clean, soft, and quietly elegant. It definitely carries the unmistakable Celine DNA, but it never screams for attention. Instead, it stays subtle, polished, and beautifully understated, perfect for anyone who appreciates refined simplicity. I totally love it, but I agree performance could be a bit better.

Perfectly tuned in major, this fragrance composition from the brand Celine envelops you from the very first moment. It comes bright and friendly, cheerful and light-footed, not in step as the name "Parade" might suggest. Rather, it is a relaxed stroll and pause, a walk in the summery south, enjoying the warmth, surrounded by southern flair, enhanced by a gentle breeze that collects many scents and caresses softly. "Parade" is a skillfully assembled mosaic made from classic fragrance components, a kind of kaleidoscope of airy summer joys. Of course, bergamot is included, known for its sparkling and invigorating qualities. The neroli oil, named after the Sicilian princess Nerola, warms the heart with its aromatic magic and is therefore naturally found in the heart note, while oak moss, surprisingly light yet still spicy here, scratches at the perhaps still daydreaming senses, fully awakening them with vetiver in its well-known manner, before a delicately and artfully woven blanket of warm, animalistic musk is spread over this charming southern creation. "Parade" truly offers nothing new, but rather enchantingly arranged, stylish fragrance charm that knows no temporal boundaries and can therefore be a harmonious companion throughout the day, which it easily becomes with reapplication. For the sillage and longevity correspond to the lightness of summer with its well-measured fragrance notes here. "Parade" awakens my curiosity for other fragrance creations from this brand, which I have read and heard about repeatedly, but which I had not known until I requested two samples. But it is famously never too late!

If you are a fan of neroli, you will likely be very happy with "Parade | Celine." I really liked the signature. Additionally, the longevity on my skin is quite impressive at around 10 hours, and the sillage is in the medium range. I can't really pinpoint a top, heart, and base note, as certain aromas are always present. Above all, neroli triumphs, which is caressed by orange blossoms, a citrusy-refreshing bergamot, and a certain woodiness. Creamy, powdery, and greenish aromas also resonate. In the background, there is occasionally a hint of oakmoss. I find "Parade | Celine" truly beautiful and I sincerely thank Kamyar for the sample.

Parade has become a well-executed mistake purchase for me. Originally, I wanted to order Black Tie and in my haste, I actually didn't pay attention to the fact that I ordered something completely wrong. Well then, here it is. Now, oh well, let's open it and spray it on, maybe it will work out for us. And indeed, it does work.

Tension. The seat is upright. The reins are held high and the pent-up energy beneath me threatens to unleash and propel forward with a huge leap. It’s still early in the morning, just before there was a light rain shower. The ground still sparkles and a light mist lays over the dressage arena. Everything is calm and I can hear my horse's heartbeat. Concentration - PARADE!

I love everything blue in fragrances and I love American fragrances in particular because most of them are light on the nose and have innovative, non-imitation scents. John Varvatos is a fashion house that features innovative, high-quality fragrances at an affordable price. John Varvatos XX Indigo is a light, masculine fragrance that is acceptable to all and has above average performance. It relies on mint in the opening, geranium in the heart of the fragrance, and Himalayan poppy to give balance to the fragrance on a light base of vetiver and patchouli. A delightful, perfectly balanced fragrance perfect for spring and breezy summer nights. The bottle is of high quality and comes in a deep blue (indigo) color with a metal cap and a medallion with the John Varvatos logo. The scent of Himalayan poppy is very attractive, distinctive and completely unrepeatable. The fragrance does not resemble the famous Dylan Blue Versace except in the color of the bottle only. Final Rating: An unrepeatable, unusual, very enjoyable and deep fragrance that is worth trying and owning.

First of all, this smells nothing like Dylan blue. For me, it’s very similar to the Jon varvatos original, but a little bit fresher version. It definitely has the John Varvatos DNA. I can even see similarities between this and Artesian too. For me, it’s quite a pleasant sent my wife likes it And I get over six hours even though the last hour or two is closer to the skin. The presentation; some think it’s tacky but I think it’s a nice looking presentation and it fits well within my collection. It has a decent atomizer. It’s loaded with a Notes, and it has a great smell, and like I said, it lasts a decent amount of time on me. I also think you could wear this most anytime and anywhere. It probably would do a little better in cooler months, but if you’re inside and air conditioning, it should be fine. I think the name indigo is perfect because this is a little bit darker version of I also think you could wear this most anytime and anywhere. It probably would do a little better in cooler months, but if your inside and air conditioning, it should be fine. I think the name indigo is perfect because this is a little bit darker version of a blue cologne.

Perhaps I should have guessed from the ridiculous name that Givenchy HOT COUTURE would be a mess, and it really is. The opening smells like artificially flavored red cough syrup--could be raspberry, but it's artificial, so it could also be gaspberry... From there, unfortunately, things just get worse... The middle stage of HOT COUTURE edp smells exactly like a dirty ashtray. This is not a smokey but a dirty-ash smell. Although I am not a smoker, I love few things more than the scent of the smoke trailing off of a freshly lit cigarette or a just struck match. I even like the smell of pipe smoke. But I have zero tolerance for second-hand smoke or the lingering nastiness that infects my clothes when I have the misfortune of spending time in a cigarette-smoke-filled chamber. HOT COUTURE smells like that to me. It reminds of the time I had a facial done by a woman who had just taken a cigarette break and neither brushed her teeth nor washed her hands before our session. The drydown of HOT COUTURE does become more tolerable with time, but only because the scent diminishes in strength. No other fragrance I know of smells like HOT COUTURE. But that is for a very good reason. This is a big, loud "No!" to my nose.

This was a very odd fragrance indeed. I totally wasn't expecting what I smelt when I intially applied Hot Couture. The previous reviewers are not wrong in stating that this is a peppery floral scent. It's quite sharp and surprising to my nose. I know many of you will go crook on me for saying this, but Hot Couture really reminds me of Chanel No.19. It has a grassy/green quality to it that I can't deny. In my personal opinion, I don't think this fragrance would be very well suited to young women, it seems to take a more mature and sophisticated approach. Don't get me wrong however, I'm not saying this is an 'old-lady fragrance'. I don't actually get the raspberry and vanilla in Hot Couture, which I'm a little disappointed about. To be honest, I don't find this scent sweet or fruity at all. I'd choose Versace Woman as a better alternative if you're looking for a raspberry and spicy/herb scent.

Hot couture has been my signature perfume since 2ooo. There is an elegance and sensuality to it that I have not experienced in any other perfume that I have tried. I love the way the raspberry note mixed with vetiver and cedar dance so beautifully together. I would never call it green or compare it to Chanel 19 because it is spicy and woodsy and a tiny bit sweet. That is just my opinion and the way it wears on me...remember body chemistry is the final ingredient so I can imagine this might be different on different people or even in different seasons. A beautiful scent!

i blind bought this perfume based on reviews on youtube and i can't believe i hated it at first! after couple of days i started to like the scent and now i'm addicted to it. the amount of sweetness is just perfect for me and i love the soft smokiness of the edt version. i wear it in both summer and winter and i think it's suitable for all seasons.

I'v heard so much good reviews about H.C so when i finally got my sample and was disappointed expected something more juicier and with more projection but instead it's has a synthetic Strawberry Jam scent with a plastic drydown I don't see any sex appeal nor artistry I notice tuberose when it mixed with Magnolia it's a recipe for nausea Not even the etchings of a black pepper drydown can save this I tried to like this sorry to the fans of Hot Couture but it's not for me.

Long before the oud + leather + raspberry trend came Hot Couture in the early aughts with smoky raspberry. It was magnificent then and is still today. I love this perfume with the passion of a thousand suns. This was my first “grown-up” frag in high school that made me feel cool as hell and I still wear it nearly twenty years later.

Raspberry, pepper and amber. Sounds odd? But smells good! A fruity/spicy scent that’s off the beaten track. I don't understand why some people compare the peppery smell to the smell of an ashtray or cigarettes; I don't see the connection at all.

As little as runway fashion is sometimes wearable for everyday life, "Hot Couture" is indeed wearable, albeit perhaps with a wink. This fragrance has edges and corners for me and even a bit of sex appeal; it is certainly bold. Who would combine raspberries in the top note with a hefty dose of pepper and a good amount of wood in the base?

A fine drop. Although the base hints at cotton candy, the EdT is not very sweet; vetiver is responsible for a clean scent, absolutely feminine, yes, almost vintage. Round, warm, and soft. A wonderful ode to feminine beauty. Discreet and smart with a hint of my dearly beloved raspberry, unfortunately, it fades away too quickly. :(

...Jacques Cavallier often hits the mark with me. I already own several of his wonderful creations. Yesterday, this treasure joined my collection. I approached this blind purchase with a relaxed nose... with Jakob, it can't go too wrong. What I got to smell was not only not off, but very, very delicious.

I am starting to wonder whether the house of Boucheron has a conscious ambiguity agenda going, as INITIAL, like so many other perfumes of this house (with the notable exception of the original powerhouse BOUCHERON) refuses to commit to a category or even to exhibit any sort of consistency from wearer to wearer. To my nose, this creation begins briefly with a tangerine/mandarin-spiciness evocative of the openings of a number of florientals familiar to me. However, as INITIAL develops, a very strange mid-stage emerges, in which the pepper and cassis leaf (I presume) somehow combine to produce a dry cigarette-ash effect. It does not smell dirty here, as in Givency HOT COUTURE (which I do not like at all—in part because of the artificiality of the raspberries in that composition). Instead of smelling like a dirty ashtray, INITIAL mimics during its mid-stage (which lasts a few minutes) the scent of clean cigarette ashes—as oxymoronic as that may sound. But wait, there's more: in the drydown, this perfume morphs again--at least on my skin, and according to my nose--into a honeyed-almond layer which lingers on and on and seems to bear no relation to the dry cigarette-ash stage, although it's not completely out of synch with the citrus-oriental opening. Overall, I'd say that the identity of INITIAL is very difficult to pin down: it capriciously defies categorization and seems to manifest different notes to different wearers and even to the same wearer at different times. Given its manifest elusiveness, I'm not really surprised that this perfume was discontinued. The one thing that I can confidently assert is that INITIAL is both nonlinear and unique!

At first you get the scent of orange wrapped with spices and warm amber Cozy fragrant Imaginings of a Old Victorian Fireplace on christmas eve a rocking chair rocks back and forth comly listioning to the sound fire Crakling Misoltoe on top of the archway faint sounds of tinkling music boxes playing. or in the scene from The Age of Innocence when Madame Olenska and Newland Archer suble erotic chemisty or russia Before the revolution when Tsars ruled with Ambered walls decked with fine paintings of great masters Leo Tolstory with his Anna Karenina Onegin wondered though St Peter's Squaire Like a Person without a soul after his Doomed love for Tatyana. the sweet Soft sounds of the balakas playing. this was a world before Lenin Stalin and Communist Regime Distroyed it Forever. these are the thing i imagine when i wear this. a bittersweet Sojourn in a bottle.

...stands an abandoned mansion in a deserted park. Almost forgotten and a bit eerie. A caretaker looks after it and ensures that it does not fall into decay. An ancient housekeeper sometimes airs it out and still enters the bedroom of the baroness with reverence, who died in childbirth about 70 years ago. No one else is allowed to enter this room, and nothing has ever been changed. The furniture in the house is covered with white sheets, and the curtains are drawn. Only a small beam of light shines here and there. The great-grandchildren have renounced the inheritance, and no one wants to buy the villa because it is said to be haunted and the baroness walks there. Some claim to have seen her face at the window or to have heard her weeping. It is rumored that the baroness's death was not a natural one. At night, eerie veil-like beings are said to float through the park, and in summer, thousands of lights glow over the small lake. That they are fireflies during the wedding flight interests no one. After all, one does not want to spoil the mystique. The housekeeper places lily of the valley on the baroness's bed every May. A fresh bouquet every day, for in the morning the lily of the valley is always gone. In front of the bedroom window, jasmine and English roses bloom, which are already ancient and have not been tended to or pruned for a long time. Somehow, they seem to bloom with their last strength. The baroness used to dry them and put them in her trunk. On the nightstand, there is still a box with the beloved pearl necklace of the baroness. No one dares to touch it, wear it, let alone steal it. It is said that whoever touches the baroness's treasures is possessed by her spirit and condemned to wander the battlements at night. On the dressing table, there is still a box with cool, dusty powder. When the baroness glides through the halls at night, she always leaves behind a distant cloud of powder. From a suit of armor, patchouli wafts. Oh no, it’s mice, raising the next generation and their special scent.

This Boucheron presents itself in the form of an earring: A flawless pearl, set in antique silver, with a subtle gold rim. Simple and elegant, it draws attention to itself. Even mine, although I have never worn a pearl necklace or even tried one on. I don't particularly favor gold either, and if I do, then only if it already shows signs of wear. This is the difference between liking a perfume bottle and other preferences. The content of this piece of jewelry is also solid: It is a rather abstract scent, jasmine can at best be sensed. The individual notes flow seamlessly into one another, without revealing their secrets. Floral-woody, always with a very fine, almost bitter touch. After two hours, the scent briefly intensifies again, perhaps a hint of pepper? And Initial lasts surprisingly long, gentle, beautiful. Initial is a classic fragrance, perfectly crafted. A group of stylishly dressed ladies sits at a coffee table in a summer park, engaging in very refined conversation. Solid, nothing is ostentatious. That is Initial. However, it has not become an ignition for me. It is not a boring or interchangeable perfume. For me, it simply lacks a bit of bite. It’s like some jewelry that I admire in the shop window: It is beautiful, well-crafted, but I wouldn’t want to wear it. It does not awaken any desires in me: Too ladylike, too perfect.

This perfume truly evokes the most bizarre associations in me! It certainly doesn’t come across as feminine or even boring on me, Right after spraying: Spicy, cinnamon-like, like warm wood! It reminds me a little of the infusion in a (classic) sauna with wooden beams - as I knew them from my youth. Very pleasant! But shortly after: something citrusy, but no longer really fresh hits my nose. Like outdated effervescent tablets or - I can hardly bring myself to write this! - scouring powder! Could this be a perfume under the 50% mark? But luckily, this unpleasant phase doesn’t last too long. Then comes a phase where the comment from Medusa ignites my imagination: "...commode from the Gründerzeit...old villa, creaking floorboards..." In the village of my childhood, there was an old villa from the Gründerzeit in the middle of a huge park-like garden - in spring full of wildflowers, later the nettles grew as tall as a man. Because of the unresolved question of inheritance, no one took care of the beautiful old building; it was simply left to decay. Nevertheless, it radiated a morbid beauty! For us children, it was primarily an adventure playground! We called the villa the "haunted castle" and went on "expeditions" inside. Sometimes dubious figures would spend the night there, which made the house even creepier. Over time, the villa fell more and more into disrepair; you could see through the holes in the ceilings over three floors - it was certainly not safe to wander around there! Yet nothing ever happened to us. A few years after I moved away with my parents, the villa was finally demolished. What a shame! Initially, it really has something from a bygone era, almost slightly morbid, perhaps due to the patchouli. A spicy-warm pleasant note lingers on my skin, even after a hot bath. Now I wonder: how to rate this? The "scouring powder phase" was really not enjoyable! It will hardly become a favorite scent. But the fragrance at least threw me into a whirlpool and recalled old memories. And I find the long-lasting base quite pleasant. Therefore, 70%.

A wonderful autumn; an enchanting fragrance. Colorful leaves, warm sunshine. A radiant scent fills the air. Zesty bergamot has a brief play. Fresh juniper, forest floor, and a green, spicy veil. The scent - a celebration with melting iris butter, tames the juniper berries so they do not overpower. Cedar, not gnarled and dry, lands on the ground embraced by vetiver. A play, a dream, a fragrance!

My first association, especially from a distance: day cream. A very good, fine one with something fresh and spicy in it. Before me, I see a breakfast on a hotel terrace overlooking the garden on a cheerful morning after a restful night. Perfect mood. The creamy iris butter dominates over time the vetiver-cedar combination. The cedar does not come across as sharply synthetic or unpleasantly woody-ambery (a problem I often have with perfumes that list "cedar" as a note), but rather like the dry cedar woods for the wardrobe. When the freshness from the top note has faded, everything remains soft and rounded all the time. Really nice. The day unfolds after breakfast in a pleasantly relaxed manner. However, it is not very warm; a pleasant, yet by no means fresh coolness permeates the scent. The vetiver here has nothing green about it, which is a dimension I miss. Instead, a very subtle, barely perceptible smoky note develops in the middle of the progression, elevating the scent from the realm of the ordinary. In the dry-down, nothing of that is felt anymore. Fortunately, there is no excessive use of vanilla and musk. Thus, Bois Dormant never becomes sweet or fluffy, but maintains a certain objective straightforwardness despite all its softness. For me, Bois Dormant is a powdery-soft, woody perfume leaning towards the stereotypically feminine side, with masculine additions of spice and traces of smoke, without sweetness. I find it friendly, noble, and elegant. In terms of style, Bois Dormant, as hinted in the marketing text, fits better with a flannel blazer or linen dress than with evening wear or jeans. It is chic, subtly high-quality (this iris butter is truly great), but not haute couture. The sillage is unobtrusive, and the longevity is moderate: After two sprays on the wrist, there was almost nothing left to smell after six hours. So, one can easily apply another scent in the evening. What the name of the perfume refers to remains a mystery to me: La belle au bois dormant is Sleeping Beauty. This could hint at the almost sleep-inducing calm aspects of this scent, or perhaps its wintry ones. However, "bois dormant" can also be translated as "blendholz" (although "bois d’éblouissement" would be more common), which seems rather banal to me, but at least captures the fact that the wood contained in it is not at all forest-like. Qui sait. I wonder why there are so few statements and reviews about Bois Dormant so far, even though it is currently enjoying high attention: After all, four sharings of it have been completed in the last month alone. Presumably, people simply feel comfortable with it without paying much attention to it. At least that’s how it is for me. I know few perfumes like this. My relatively reserved rating is due to the fact that I prefer more pronounced scents. In its own way, Bois Dormant is nevertheless very successful. It will please those who enjoy gentle, woody fragrances with a coherent overall composition.

Even though I find the scent of vetiver very interesting, it has always been too angular and rough for me until now. But here is finally a vetiver fragrance that is very warm, soft, and rounded. Although the vetiver is always very present, it is somewhat tamed by the iris. Perfect for autumn and winter, but certainly also wearable in spring.

Similar in ways, but very different. I categorized both as cider scents. This one is kinda mentholated which is mostly what you'd find in "mens" fragrances here and there. It's a little sweet and resinous, but not gourmand. Unique and very affordable. The personality of this scent shines on a chilly night. Most people have said it smells sexy. I would get a back up bottle. Long lasting and projects. Very festive. Leans masculine.

Recently, I tested the Varvatos in the beautiful, cherry-red, shiny bottle at a luxury perfumery in the center of Vienna. The bottle enchanted me, so I had high expectations for the scent. However, I was severely disappointed. The fragrance starts off sugary-sweet, berry-like, with a slightly synthetic feel and background woods. This heavily candied berry scent is not really my thing. I almost mistook it for the brother of Jaguar Red. But then something unforeseen happened. I can hardly explain what occurred from the fragrance pyramid. Out of nowhere, a very strong, penetrating, unpleasant chemical note emerged - at first, I thought it was synthetic oud, which is almost found in every modern perfume these days. But no. That wasn't it. It was much worse. The piercing note somehow smelled like the chlorine in heavily disinfecting cleaning agents. The fragrance changed its character, mutated into a penetrating chlorine bomb, and remained that way. Rarely have I smelled such an unbearable, respiratory-irritating, unpleasant scent. Nothing for the faint-hearted. Something only for men who want to smell like the work gloves of cleaning company employees - like chlorine cleaner, sparkling clean, right? - if such men even exist. The longevity is above average - practically forever and hardly washable, with a correspondingly strong sillage. P.S. On the paper strip I took with me, I detected some maritime notes behind the penetration, but only the next morning when the scent had weakened. I didn't smell them on my skin.

Speaking of gimmicks, Givenchy PLAY FOR HER comes housed in what appears to be an ipod. Cute, I guess. The liquid, predictably, is adolescent as well. PLAY FOR HER smells remarkably similar to about twelve red jammy fruity florals that I've sniffed to date. In fact, this may smell like one of Givenchy's other recent launches. Perhaps they're pulling the Bvlgari trick of selling previously launched perfumes in new bottles. Anyway, PLAY FOR HER lacks any perfumic interest to this nose. It's almost too sweet and the overall effect is that of a jar of red jam. I don't know why there are no fruits listed among the notes, but this level of sweetness could not be accounted for without something more sugary than tonka, it seems to me. I am confident that this fragrance will work for those to whom it is being marketed. I obviously do not fall into that niche.

It took a few good years before I finally got around to testing Givenchy's Play for Her. I was consistently put-off by the MP3 Player inspired packaging, however since noting that this fragrance has many fans, I sought it out in my local department store and took a sniff. Play for Her smelt the way I expected it to smell; sweet, airy and predictable. It's pleasant but ordinary to my nose. A basic blend of sugary orchid, fuzzy peach, creamy orange blossom, zingy pink pepper and slightly foody tonka bean. It's kind of like a toned-down, more peppery version of Viktor & Rolf's Flowerbomb. They are not exactly the same, but there are some similarities. Thankfully, Play for Her is not sickeningly sweet. I'm assuming that this fragrance sells reasonably well, however I'm sure that Very Irresistible and Amarige are still Givenchy's top female fragrances. Play for Her cannot top the Givenchy classics. If you are searching for a 'girly' and light scent, then Play for Her would be the perfect choice. I find it to be quite inoffensive and suitable for all seasons. The lasting power is also not half bad. It's just a pity that Play for Her is so unoriginal and linear on the skin. It's not a particularly compelling fragrance, so I doubt that I could muster up the desire to wear it, even if I happened to own a bottle. Original review written: February 2013.

My girlfriend wanted to treat me to a fragrance today, and I also value that we choose it together. It should please both of us. We tried this and that, but unanimously kept coming back to Play for her. To my great satisfaction, as I have been hoarding the entire Play family - including the men's fragrance, which I even like, although I usually shy away from men's scents. And also for her competed with the mild sunshine that warmed the perfumery and our spirits. Despite the name, the fragrance is not playful, but rather mature and tends towards the elegant side - yet with a certain casualness. It is transparent, but lasting - a good all-day scent. The pink pepper has temperament and the orange blossom reflects the sunlight. Orchid and Tiare make the fragrance floral - noble, and convey a positive message. Patchouli adds depth and the tonka bean rounds off the scent softly and elegantly. This optimistic attitude is inherent in all Plays - and I like that. Uncomplicated yet full - monotony is not its thing. Play - I have to think of "Bread and Games" - because I am equally fond of the fragrance and a well-baked bread. It doesn't always have to be a three-tiered cake. Play is what it claims to be - without any hooks or loops. I like that.

of Givenchy. If I were them, I would quickly stop production and pretend nothing happened. I would cut off contact with Emilie Bevierre-Coppermann, Lucas Sieuzac, and Françoise Donche. And yes, the bottle is indeed somewhat "hard on the eye." Embarrassing, all of it. Edit: but if someone is interested in this fragrance and because I want to be informative: It reminds me quite strongly of "Femme Individuelle" by Montblanc due to the pink pepper in the top note. At first, I thought of "Cascade" by Chopard, but compared to that, "Play" really lacks any edges or corners - and "Cascade" is already quite cute on its own. The fruity note that comes from the blackcurrant in "Femme Individuelle" is provided by the orange blossom in "Play." The difference is surprisingly small. I don't know what is supposed to be African about this orange blossom. The orange, as we know, comes from China (ApfelSINE) and Southeast Asia. So even in the ingredient lists, the shoddiness begins. It probably aims to sound particularly exotic, just like the silly "bottle" is supposed to come across as particularly funky and young. So nice and unobtrusive, ideal for the office. Just like "Femme Individuelle" - great that the category of fragrance twins has just been introduced - the heart and base notes are even quieter than the top note. How the balsam tree ended up in the iPod bottle, I don't know. I only know that balsam trees are a separate plant genus, consisting of a mere 2 (two) species, from whose resin Tolu or Peru balsam is obtained. Givenchy opted for the balsam tree instead of Tolu balsam. Or rather, for other parts of the tree. Probably the odorless parts, which would explain why no balsam tree can be smelled. But it does sound like something, right? Just like the flower of the nonexistent African orange. Otherwise, in the heart note, there are exotic little flowers, "Femme Individuelle" does something similar, and where there is a bit of vanilla in the base alongside musk and patchouli, "Play" has called upon the tonka bean here. Conclusion: the similarity is striking; I would actually speak of interchangeability here. So, anyone looking for a pleasant, delicate office or clean fragrance with a bit of fruitiness should reach for "Femme Individuelle." There is hardly any difference in scent, and a bottle that can be shown off. "Play" is as unnecessary as cold coffee.

I became aware of it because of the pink bottle and the glittery stones. Actually, I'm not really into that anymore, but sometimes the teenage girly side of me comes through. I bought it blind (once again a blind purchase), which did not disappoint me. I imagined it to be much sweeter and can't quite understand why this fragrance is received so poorly. (Tastes are different, after all ;) ) The first spray is very pleasant; a fresh sweetness and later a bit fruity. A fresh fruity sweetness. It immediately lifts your spirits and gives a sense of lightness. Overdoing it with this fragrance should be difficult, but the longevity could be a bit longer. I really like the scent and the bottle feels good in the hand. It doesn’t feel like cheap plastic at all, rather high-quality and made with attention to detail ???? I'm glad to have this beautiful fragrance in my collection. A scent for the carefree days in life ✨

And indeed a beautiful, imaginative, somewhat "old-fashioned" one in a small town. Behind it, greenhouses filled with all sorts of colorful and fragrant summer flowers, freshly watered. And in the shop itself, alongside the colorful and green goods, a wooden counter, decorated wooden dressers, and some delicate decorative fabric drapes like canopies hanging from the ceiling.

~ Inspiration ~ After testing the EDT of "Play for Her", I wanted to try the EDP as well, and it landed on my wishlist. During a swap, I received a sample to test. ~ Bottle ~ The shape of a pink MP3 player fits quite well with the name (with a focus on the "play button"). ~ Scent ~ It begins fruity-fresh with peach, bergamot, and a hint of pink pepper.
After reading many comments here on Parfumo, I was already expecting the worst from this fragrance.

Man, I have already described so many fragrances here, and I thought I would finally get to know a special perfume from the Givenchy brand. But Play by Givenchy disappoints me a bit; where has the uniqueness of classics like Organza, Amarige, Ysatis gone? Those were perfumes that had a real signature scent!

Negative reviews are never fun to write, but I hope you forgive me - especially if this fragrance works wonderfully for you, then I’d rather not have said anything :) For me, this is a boring sweet-floral scent in a sadly very cheap-looking bottle. I usually like playful bottles, but this one seems to me like it was designed for a 13-year-old.

Miss Boucheron opens with a brief spray of bergamot citrus before a growing fruity pomegranate and raspberry accord joins a somewhat synthetic smelling rose and white musk tandem, with just the faintest whiff of underlying gentle pink pepper in the heart. As the fragrance enters its dry-down the rose and fruity accords both recede, revealing a slightly spicy woody base that combines with the remaining synthetic musk now acting as support. Projection is excellent and longevity is outstanding at well over 12 hours on skin. I bought Miss Boucheron blind due to someone mentioning that it smelled very close to Le Boise by Ginestet, a fragrance that I enjoy but don't get great performance out of. Unfortunately, I see little resemblance between the two and Miss Boucheron is a *much* sweeter fruity floral concoction. The noses behind Miss Boucheron are a couple of the best out there, and while their raw material budget may have been limited (as the fragrance definitely has a very synthetic vibe throughout), their skill is quite evident and it is clear they did the absolute best they could with it. My favorite part of the development is the dry-down, as the slightly woody facets of the fragrance finally are revealed. The bottom line is that while I am not the target demographic for Miss Boucheron (as it definitely has a distinct feminine bent to my nose), I am not disappointed in this blind buy at all as it is quite the outstanding value at its under $30 a full bottle price online, earning a "very good" rating of 3.5 stars out of 5 outright.

I have to admit I love Miss Boucheron. I have the original Boucheron which I wear on special occasions only but Miss Boucheron is one of my favorite casual perfumes. I love how the fruity notes are combined with the fresh floral notes and a touch of suede. The scent is modern, pretty and young but also chic. The composition is not complex or dramatic but it is graceful, light and sparkly. I get lots of compliments when I wear it. The pomegranate note is playful and lovely in the opening mixed with a nice doze of pink pepper. I love roses and I can definitely smell them in the heart notes but I think the lead floral note here is the cyclamen. I think it is the cyclamen that makes the heart notes to smell so fresh and gentle. The suede note is very feminine and soft here. It mixes lovely with the freshness of cyclamen. The dry down is similar to the heart notes but toned down a bit. The scent becomes lighter in the dry down but it lasts for at least 8 hours. Miss Boucheron is a lovely, sassy and casual fruity floral that I definitely recommend trying.

She arrived in a pink box wrapped in pink satin. When you open it, hip lounge music plays, and you see in the lid the image of the young, oversized Madame (not girl, not lady) sitting in the mini-town and playing with a pendulum. I take the pretty pink glass bottle out of the box. It fits well in the hand. It is heavy and well-crafted, only the emerald cabochon spray button with the golden casing, I would have wished for something a bit more high-quality. The scent starts fruity and sparkling fresh, only the pepper gives it a slightly spicy touch. The flowers, and I could swear I smell a hint of musk, make the fragrance very clean. After a while, however, a dry, powdery leather comes to the forefront but leaves room for the fruity flowers. Very nice, very understated. Fortunately, I am spared from the cedar, which often hits hard right from the start. I can perceive the scent well on my arm, but it is not overpowering. I find that the image captures the scent very well, I perceive it as young, feminine, romantic, playful, soft, balanced, and also exclusive. Although I usually like loud, intrusive fragrances, I really enjoy Mission Boucheron and find it very pleasant. I think Miss Boucheron will stay with us for now and will accompany me to the office and in my leisure time in the future.

Miss Boucheron is treading new paths. Unfortunately, so far not very successfully. Boucheron, the venerable house of round-cut jewels and equally shaped flacons, has long been synonymous with oriental fragrances for mature ladies of the world, or ladies who wish to see themselves as such. Miss Boucheron will already deter them as a flacon, because pink is more "Paris Hilton" than "Mrs. Mayor". But the pink flacon houses a non-pink scent. Not an oriental, not sweet, not even overly floral, it is quite a positive surprise. Even though the top note starts off a bit sweet-fruity, the scent soon shifts to a fresh-spicy profile with a slight leather touch. The base is warm-woody, making the fragrance a noble, slightly spicy all-rounder. Only the rose makes a slight appearance, but only late, and doesn’t linger long, as is customary with VIPs. So, it is indeed something for Mrs. Mayor, but only if she is not the twinset and pearl type.

The name Reptile and the description as a perfume inspired by rock stars and their outfits sound like this could be a challenging leather fragrance, but no. It has a noticeable leather note, but it's done in the typical Celine style: understated, soft, powdery, elegant. If this was a reptile, it would maybe be a friendly pet gecko, or even more likely: A fancy stuffed animal crocodile with real leather details. The kind you'd use as a decoration, not something for little kids to snuggle with, but still completely harmless and soft to the touch. Right from the start this feels like a fluffy cloud of musky powder. Black pepper gives it a dry, slightly savory edge that makes it interesting, but is not overwhelmingly spicy. The leather is a gentle suede, not tannic or sharp, and the tree moss adds a subtle woodsy earthiness, the same as it does in Black Tie. Reptile opens with a touch of sweetness that mostly vanishes in the drydown. All the current Celine scents are marketed as unisex, but this is the first one that I don't find more feminine leaning (I tried 5 of them so far). It's not really masculine either, just truly unisex. I like it a lot, even though I would prefer other Celine scents on myself.

When it comes to Celine, a lot of their works rely on/use Iris and because of that they might come across as more feminine to some people. This beast screams UNISEX. I absolutely can imagine everyone agreeing on that. It is called Reptile (and here I am theorizing) because it might smell like a lizard skin to people. To me, it is rather a bundle of different memories from my childhood. I’ve spent a considerable amount of time at my grandmas since we lived very close to her in the same town. The perfume opens up with every note listed on fragrantica, and the list is rather short here: moss, leather, black pepper, cedar wood, and musk. I can smell all of them at once but they’re not mixed together into a cacophony that no one understands. Black pepper here doesn’t smell like any other black pepper listed in many fragrances: it smells exactly like this one powdered black pepper I loved adding to a bean soup my grandmother used to make (she still cooks it for me when I visit her ). The combination of leather and pepper reminds me of the old and dusty vinyl plates she used to have, that’s how they smelled or at lest how my olfactory memory remembered it. I also can pick out some muskiness here which is not overwhelming and rather subtle. I love smelling it from other people. It has some (not a huge though) projection and I love catching a whiff of it when the wind blows. It is definitely “unisex” and would suit anyone. Must try for pepper/leather lovers :)

For some reason, I expected this to be a much "louder" scent, but I actually found it to be quite gentle. The black pepper note becomes less pronounced with time, reaching a point where it almost feels like just another facet of the skin's natural scent. However, I'd wager that someone who doesn't care for black pepper would probably be bothered by it throughout. Underneath the spice it's very clear that it shares the same DNA as other fragrances from the collection, which I personally find quite delightful.

Of the many scents that have come my way in recent years, the majority have elicited reactions following this pattern: “An XYZ scent, terrible!” “An XYZ scent, boring.” “An XYZ scent, interesting, but not for me.” I can count truly unique reactions, which I somewhat chase after, on one war-injured hand, as it only has three fingers. In chronological order: Grey Vetiver Eau de Parfum : Wow, this is THE scent. The one I smelled somewhere on someone and found incredibly good. Here it is, I want it. Ganymede Eau de Parfum : Instantly smitten. Convinced and fascinated from the first spray. Forever associated with a wonderful vacation. My first fragrance compliment from a complete stranger. And finally … … "Reptile | Celine": It smells like Mr. L.! Mr. L. was my neighbor in my hometown and a man I only really saw when he stood in the doorway of his row house smoking. Whether he smelled like Reptile, I cannot know, as we were not that close. Probably more like Nightclubbing, Celine's tobacco scent. When we saw each other in the front yard, we exchanged a few nice words, a hello, not much more, we both probably knew we had better things to do with our time. Long conversations were thankfully avoided. But why do I think of this now-deceased person when I smell Celine's Reptile? I don't really know and can only attempt interpretations. Scent, like a person, strikes me as incredibly elegant, mature, with a certain distance from the supposedly significant minutiae of everyday life. Like almost all scents from Celine, Reptile is a rather understated fragrance; anyone expecting “Beastmode” just because of the name will be disappointed. This subtle, yet distinctly masculine elegance abstractly resembles scents like Pour Monsieur Eau de Toilette and fits wonderfully with the image I have of my neighbor. A lawyer with a penchant for tennis and the finer things, with a vacation home in Italy and a wife who enjoys being given the floor. Compared to scents that indulge in the lizard-like (hihi) aspects of longevity and sillage, Reptile may seem boring to some. For me, it has a pleasantly detached quality: Who cares about such trivialities? What matters is beauty. And Reptile has plenty of that!

What a wonderful scent was hidden for 24 days in my 2023 Advent calendar! The fragrance DNA is not entirely unfamiliar to me. They haven't reinvented the wheel here, but they have perfected it. Reptile is a buttery soft, woody fragrance with a subtle spiciness. The soft wild leather note perfectly rounds off the scent. I usually don't like leather in fragrances, but here this note is so wonderfully woven that I actually enjoy it. The fragrance is listed as unisex. Personally, I can imagine wearing it, but I still don't necessarily see it on a woman. Longevity and sillage are once again subpar, and of course, that affects the price-performance ratio. Anyone who enjoys woody, soft scents should definitely give it a try :)

Masculine, very masculine..! Although it is marketed as unisex, I can’t help but say, even if it’s not politically correct these days, oops, I’m saying it anyway, I absolutely cannot imagine this scent on a woman. Way too peppery and way too spicy.. So how does Reptile smell??.. Almost exactly like my drawer filled with spices from around the world..

After months of consideration, I decided to finally buy the fragrance that had lingered in my memory from Celine for so long. I spent many hours pondering and racking my brains. But it had to be done, the Black Tie. After all, I get a large 100ml bottle for the price asked - I had already seen significantly more expensive fragrances on a per ml/€ basis.

On my skin it's too sickly sweet smelling and too strong. It also smells sickly synthetic. Not a bad fragrance at all. Just not for me. Crimson is my favorite. Intense XX lacks the cider/apple note. THE original XX had a strong coconut note that I LOATHED. Most people are saying this scent is week, but on my skin it is STRONG and has a powerful sillage. For me it's a Winter scent.

I discovered this fragrance in February at my regular perfumery... Varvatos was new, right in the corner by the door ...but the bottles! So I went over, a little curious cat, and started spraying... all nice but nothing special to my nose and then I took the XX first spray... fresh, lemony, green... Hello Summer, I thought, but then... a few minutes later, a very lovely tonka bean tickled the scent... not dominant but it didn’t want to be overlooked, so I bought it... Compared to the longevity of other fragrances, it holds its own in the midfield, it’s not a lone fighter, not intrusive, not a catcher like Halfeti (Penhaligons)... it doesn’t really know if it’s unisex or masculine... I wear it as a woman... but it’s good, suitable for every day, goes for summer as well as winter AND it’s the only one (compared to its predecessors) that comes as an Eau de Parfum and at a really solid price for 125 ml in a very nice stone bottle with cowboy stars... Conclusion: good for every day and for anyone who wants to be inconspicuously noticeable.

Eau de Givenchy is a fresh, light and uplifting floral fragrance. Its opening is bright and sunny with bergamot, sharp citrus and grapefruit. There is also an added faint touch a mint. Other fruit notes are supposed to be present but I can't say that I get them. The heart is a bouquet of flower notes: a very natural lily-of-the-valley is joined by jasmine, honeysuckle and rose. The lightness of this fragrance makes it ideal for warm, sunny Spring days. Longevity is average, but not bad at all for a light floral. The base is woody (sandalwood and cedar) with light touches of musk and moss which add a bit of depth to the drydown.

Eau de Givenchy was my very first perfume, and regarding that with the passage of time the packaging was changed, I suspect that the fragrance has been reformulated as well. I don't know the current version, sold as part of Givenchy's "Mythical" collection, my review refers to the 1980s original, sold in a simple high and square flacon with a dark-blue veined square plastic lid. At first, Eau de Givenchy smells fresh, delicately flowery, clean and rather cool but lightly spicy as well - maybe that is what some people perceive as soapy. It ist a clear, clean scent, not sexy, not playful either, but reminding of spring, pure and innocent, just like a cold mountain stream splashing through a meadow full of spring flowers. A virgin whose erotic powers are still sleeping. While the fragrance evolves, sensual notes emerge, a warm woodiness, warmer, more sensual flowers: Behind the cool aloofness sleeps a clear sensuality, but it remains a suggestion. All in all Eau de Givenchy is a rather cool and reserved fragrance, fresh, friendly and in no way brash or flashy - a fine fragrance for office and business.

I wish I could have many bottles of this one.Everything I own from Givenchy is vintage,I must say I have them since the year they came out.About this one the original formula is so aquatic, chic and fresh.The second bottle I bought that one with the golden top I must say I found it more flowery than aquatic and doesn't last long...sorry but they do keep doing reformulations and thats not good for those who really love a unique perfume as this one.

Eau de Givenchy was released a year before Giorgio, but it could have been a decade. It's rooted in the 70's and bears more than a passing resemblance to Givenchy III (1970). But the difference is, with a feather touch of mint and a dusting of castor sugar, Eau de Givenchy lowers the age profile by a generation compared to her older sister. O de G is somewhere between a green chypre, a white muguet and a sugary gourmand but it doesn't lean too much on any one style. It's a nice balance; carefree but not frivolous, old but not dated. With its light gourmand, O de G anticipates the more youthful perfume that emerged in the 80's. Young women had more disposable income than their 70's counterparts, and when this was allied to an extrovert fashion style, it promoted the use of a more flamboyant perfume than was the case in the economically challenged and somewhat drab 70's. For a sober skirt you might wear a chypre, but with a pink tutu the old codes no longer worked. O de G moved on from the classic trope of it's 70's sister, but what it didn't do was predict the intensity or direction of the themes that were about to emerge. These were - broadly speaking - reflected by the two big hits of the 80's, the hedonistic tuberose of Giorgio, and the gothic floral of Poison. O de G was more innocent than either of these, a pretty - and still wearable issue of a classic era. (Based on a vintage miniature)

The title of my comment should not be misleading - because Eau de Givenchy is definitely my thing. But should the Eau de Givenchy run low, my husband quickly ensures a refill. THAT is his thing. He won't let himself be deterred from buying Givenchy. Thank goodness, because we agree on this brand. So the Eau de Givenchy is always well-stocked. It has been my go-to for years - even though it is by no means a common fragrance. But it adapts - without being "adapted." It has its own character - without a hint of stubbornness. Bergamot and honeysuckle start fresh - green, and the grapefruit adds a slight bitterness. The jasmine shines bright and clear - with a touch of elegance, framed by creamy sandalwood. Actually, it has a manageable list of ingredients - yet it is finely balanced and speaks of style and class. Here you can see Givenchy's signature. Less is more - finds its application here. For a fresh eau, it is very long-lasting, and due to its subtle elegance, it is also suitable for the evening. Completely my thing.

The four sisters Fire, Earth, Air, and Water form a harmonious and important unity, yet each is an independent personality. Fire provides warmth, Earth nourishes, Air keeps everything in motion, and Water belongs quite naturally to this group: they were the four elements of creation.

I made this discovery and can't even remember the noble dispenser. Shame, but still, thank you! God yes, one might think, simple, pale little bottle, simple, pale scent. The pyramid doesn't contain much either, a total of 5 fragrance notes. It reads like a fluffy light summer scent.

For a long, very long time, I have owned a mini Eau de Givenchy. A pretty, square little bottle, with a blue plastic screw cap adorned with small, turquoise glitter specks tightly sealed and never opened until now. The label has been missing from the very beginning, so for a long time, I didn’t even know what treasure I had.

A women's fragrance? Honestly? Now I'm stunned. I would have thought it was at most a unisex scent, even more likely a men's fragrance. But if that's the case... ...it changes nothing at all. Givenchy is a good address for solid fragrances. This is not meant to be offensive. It just means that you can find some good scents there and the brand belongs to the mainstream.

Eau de Givenchy and its unique scent are inextricably linked for me to the country of France, more specifically the Cote d'Azur in the southeast of the Mediterranean coast. This almost indissoluble association between my olfactory and thought world can be explained by the fact that I actually received the first bottle of this perfume in Southern France.

This was gifted to me by a friend some time ago who knew I liked Boucheron femme. I still appreciate the gesture ofcourse, but hadn't tried it properly yet, afraid It might disappoint. Today I finally took the plunge and tried it after taking a shower after work. It's an okay scent to have in your collection, but I don't find it very special. I'm afraid I'm one of those women who are spoiled by the better perfumes made in the past. I can imagine younger people liking it though for it not being the usual fruity, sweet, average perfume, compared to most modern scents. It is a fresh perfume, suitable for summer for those who like it, but I would only reach for this when all of my other bottles were emptied. In a distance, there is a faint connection to Boucheron Femme, but only if you search for it very hard. Inoffensive and safe, that's for sure, but 'safe' is not what I am after, though I also don't like scents that are offending. I don't get the frangipani unfortunately; when trying this, I was hoping that note would be more prominent because I do love frangipani. Don't find it really citrussy or orangeblossom-y either. Just a fresh showergel-like scent, ready for office (if that's what one is looking for).

Actually, I wanted to wait to write this comment until I get LouLou under my nose again. But since that might take a while, I’ll go ahead and start. Actually, it wouldn’t have occurred to me to actively test a Boucheron, as the few I had tested always seemed conventionally boring (so boring that I sometimes confused Boucheron with Burberry, which I find even more boring, embarrassing!) But then this traveling package came along. Actually, I had paused with traveling packages for almost a year for several reasons, but this one caught my attention. And so it happened that I tested a Boucheron and I actually have to revise my judgment about the brand. This fragrance is great and anything but boring. The opening: Fresh bergamot in my nose. I love that! Many fragrances start like this. Still, I find it beautiful every time. But here, something herbal comes in immediately, herbal-floral. I immediately think: These slightly scratchy, nonspecific flowers that I can’t assign to any particular flower and that seem a bit like they’re from your science fiction novel, could also be from a Mugler fragrance: fascinatingly different and at the same time intensely and lushly floral. I’m already thinking of Aura EDP, even though Fleurs is actually quite different, namely softer and powdery and less green. The heart note mainly consists of these amazing, foreign yet familiar indefinable exo-flowers with a slight sharpness, a slight sweetness, and a lot of powder that is juicy rather than dusty. And now comes my association: This herbal tone that gives the fragrance an edge, a kick, I know it, but where from? Quickly it shoots through my mind: LouLou! But no, LouLou is much less pleasing and has much more potential for shock with its insect spray undertone than the softer, sweeter, and more powdery Fleurs. But a hint of it... I would really like to test it against that. Homeopathic insect spray traces seem to play a role in Fleurs as well. Thus, a heart note forms from science fiction novel flowers, a touch of Mugler's Aura, a little ball of LouLou insect spray, juicy powder, and slight sweetness with a dash of tonka, which is so wonderfully extraordinary, intense, and slightly trashy that I can only say: WOW! I want this! It’s something special. This is a fragrance that makes me marvel, enjoy, and laugh. It’s so quirky in this combination and yet wearable, it makes me grin! Actually a cheeky fragrance! Over time, Fleurs moderates a bit as vanilla and, as it seems to me, also a little cashmeran come in, contributing gentle, woody warmth. The powder remains. The Aura and LouLou edges are rounded off and lose their shock potential, so that Fleurs slowly fades out with sweet exo-flowers on woody vanilla. The longevity is enormous. I smell the fragrance all day long and intensely all day long. The next day, I could only wear my clothes again if I wore Fleurs again, as anything else would have been layering. In this respect, Fleurs is also very impressive. Actually, I wanted to buy no more fragrances until May, but only trade. Actually. Now I have ordered Fleurs. I had to do it, it grabbed me, and it’s currently available at an incredibly good price. Let someone come and say that the word actually is a superfluous filler word!

The classic "Boucheron" was not my signature scent for years without reason. The opulence and luxury of this impressionable lady still fascinates me. Just like the enchanting bottle, which cannot hide its origins: it is and remains a luxury creation; born from a world of gold and gemstones. Truly a piece of jewelry through and through. The classic reminds me of a diva who makes the opera or theater stage her world: far beyond the proscenium, she takes possession of the wearer and her surroundings. But I already mentioned that in my previous comment. The charming bottle remains, but the contents have been noticeably rejuvenated, slimmed down - the diva, who expects applause, returns to the mortals and here in "Boucheron Fleurs" becomes a delightful and modern woman. She is still beautiful, this lady! The mandarin is surprisingly lovely here; perhaps the company of the slightly syrupy pear juice does her good, and the splash of lemon creates a nice, lively fizz - fruity-sweet and not reminiscent at all of the often encountered fruit cocktail. No, the opening is simply beautiful and already joyfully hints at what is to come. I recall that frangipani must have been used much more frequently in fragrance compositions in the past: even as a child, I found the name so mysterious! Frangipani sounded back then like princesses in a faraway land - just as little girls imagine being a princess. Mysterious and delicately blooming is also the heart of this floral being; especially because one can rely on the enchanting orange blossom and the fragrant power of frangipani - neither disappoints. A feminine scent is already emerging, one that brings lightness and good cheer. Just as Gelis feels it too. By the way, thank you for this sample. Unremarkable yet noteworthy is the interplay of benzoin and vanilla. Here, both aromas have been so well balanced that a warm and creamy, slightly resinous-smoky beauty emerges, which elegantly adapts to the fragrance development. From fruity to floral delicacy to the final accord, "Boucheron Fleurs" develops into a very pleasant companion that effortlessly brings its elegance into everyday life. This younger relative of the great "Boucheron" does not expect standing ovations - she ensures that the day becomes brighter and friendlier, even if not with extreme longevity. This charming lady guarantees a few hours of joy; one should not expect more from her delightful nature. I was very pleased to make her acquaintance.

A really lovely initial fruitiness surrounds me. The pear juice prevents the mandarin and/or lemon from being sharp or anything like that. The opening is mildly fresh and fruity, and it also has a slight sweetness to it. Quite quickly, the floral heart note joins in. However, it is a blend that I cannot distinguish. Only the good mood factor tells me that orange blossom is involved. I also cannot sniff out vanilla and benzoin from the base. But they are likely responsible for the creaminess in the fruit-flower mix. Surprisingly, there is this light fizz like from effervescent powder in the dry down, the origin of which I cannot decipher, but it is somehow fun. Well, that's about all I can say about "Boucheron Fleurs." Maybe just this: longevity 4 - 5 hours, sillage initially in the medium range but quickly reduced to skin proximity. I can imagine having it in my collection someday, but it's not urgent. Regards + thanks to Süchtig

Hedi slimane has been for me the embodiment of good taste for more than 20 years (clothing, artistic quality of these creations, perfumes, etc.) a perfume with a pure smell of nicotine (no cigarettes or tobacco) coated with iris and vanilla very finely made. Indeed, I agree with the previous comments with the image of the guy sitting at the bar but not smoker, rather the one who gets the smell of tobacco that would come to him in the discotheque. The resemblance to jazz club is not very realistic in my opinion. Can be a signature perfume for me

A very long lasting patchouli resin amber with iris and smoky touch. This one is the fiercest of all the collection. People stood on the pavement of Chez Castel to watch the parade. Saint-Germain-des-Prés is boiling despite the cold of winter. The smoke from her cigarette makes the mascara sink from her blue eyes. The girl clings to the boy’s arm, laughing. The party begins between euphoria and future hangover. The Parisian youth sets fire to the dance floor. The heat is stifling, it’s hard to breathe, the air is saturated with alcohol vapor, make-up powder mixed with body perfumes, cigarettes and leathery patchouli. The bodies stretch out, look at the strangers between raw desire and fear. Attraction and repulsion. The night unfolds like a treasure map full of promise. Her body falls into his arms. The boy grabs her mouth and puts his burning lips on her. The flickering lights make them weightless. The girl suddenly escapes and comes back with her leather jacket. She approaches his ear and says, “Come on, let’s go home”. They cross the dark corridors to reach the exit where they kiss again. She puts on her black perfecto and goes down the street smoking a cigarette without looking back. A trail of Nightclubbing stays on the alley. The final drydown is not so far from Dior Homme Parfum.

Most of the Celine scents I tried are very powdery and fluffy in a refined way. They usually smell like iris and vanilla, calm and elegant. Nightclubbing starts a bit different. Rougher. Cool, dry, smokey and a bit leathery. I understand everyone who says it smells like cigarettes, even though it's not exactly the same scent. It's neither as biting as fresh smoke, nor does it have the gross trash smell of an ashtray, and it definitely doesn't smell like unlit tobacco at all. But something about it still feels cigarette-ish. After it has dried down for a moment, the familiar powdery Celina DNA starts to shine through. Vanilla, musk fluff and Iris butter again, this time a tad earthy leaning and with a noticeably bitter galbanum note. It's starting to feel elegant and refined and not as rough anymore. Some cool smokiness stays around, but it becomes quite wearable and nice. This is a clubbing scent for people who are out of their party phase, a stylized memory of smoke-filled dive bars and leather jackets. It does not smell like the kind of perfume most people would actually wear to a club. The vibe is too introspective, it doesn't exactly scream "let's have fun". Among the Celine fragrances I prefer others like Saint-Germain-des-Prés, Black Tie or La Peau Nue, but I appreciate that they tried something a bit more experimental here. Now if they could only get rid of their unbelievably ugly bottles.

A luxurious, chic, leather sofa at the center of an exclusive secret club. New wave, post-punk music plays in the background. The sofa's leather keeps the smell of everything that these wild nights could tell: tobacco smoke, erotic tension, spilled whiskey drinks. Even if cigarette holes cover its surface, that sofa it's still such an enchanting piece of interior design. Nightclubbing by CELINE smells exactly like this.

I’ve read the reviews in the past and was put off by the cigarette description and was assuming it would be smoky, heavy and an absolute migraine. So I was pleasantly surprised when I took a whiff of this at the Celine boutique. It screams wealthy rich Parisian girl. Much lighter than expected. To me it’s 100% unisex that’s more feminine leaning..maybe it’s the sweetness in vanilla? I don’t know if it suits me, but I’m addicted to the smell..i have a travel size just so I can huff it. This girl is sexy, sultry, dark and gorgeous.

The fragrance is very well-named with Nightclubbing. You get a smoky, resinous scent here, which is strongly reminiscent of a night out at the club. The fragrance is complemented by warm iris butter, which I like on the whole, but reminded me of my grandmother on rare occasions, which shouldn't be the case in the club setting.

Nightclubbing is the sophisticated older sister to Iris Malikhan by Maison Crivelli. They share a similar dna but where Iris Malikhan is loud and unapologetic, a little screechy and synthetic smelling, Nightclubbing is much more balanced and grounded, airy and elegant. No need to scream, you have to come closer and earn it.

It is the year 2000. I am a "sweet" 17/18. I never saw myself as sweet; my surroundings probably did. I was never an explicit club-goer, as I found it far too loud in such establishments, the guys too annoying, and I quickly got bored. What attracted me, however, was the dark atmosphere in clubs. This included: of course very dim lighting. Fog machines.

06:17 AM. I open the heavy door. Bright light comes toward me through the darkness. Gray, cool, and pleasantly fresh, I breathe in the morning air. My eyes are still struggling to adjust to the brightness - no wonder, as they have seen nothing but darkness and artificial light for hours. I stumble a few steps down the street, then I let myself fall onto the first bench.

After "Guilty Absolute pour Homme | Gucci," one should actually be prepared for such an aggressive leather accord, right? I think so, because Bronze Wood & Leather starts off quite citrusy, still with grapefruit in the opening, but at the same time, you already have the wood-leather accord from the fragrance kit in front of you, which slowly pushes the grapefruit aside in the drydown and allows the vetiver to connect with the leather note. Guaiac wood and chypriol also find their way into the base along with patchouli; at least I could gather that from an interview with Marie Salamagne, those must be the unspecified "woody notes." The overall scent impression seems to retreat relatively quickly on the skin, but lasts much longer on clothing. Today, I happened to put on my sweater from yesterday and thought: What smells so wonderful here, until I remembered it was the Bronze, Wood and Leather. No, it’s not as blunt and aggressive as the Gucci. There’s definitely a bit of style here, and the scent doesn’t hit you as hard. It is strong at first but fades relatively quickly, remaining a pleasantly leathery companion on the skin, and as I’ve noticed, even longer on clothing. I find it nice to choose whether you want to wear it subtly or project it outward. The bottle, as already described, looks like a black ink pot, and the silver cap completes the appearance. But that’s a theme that runs through the Jo Malone line anyway. Ultimately, with "Bronze Wood & Leather | Jo Malone," you have a tanned leather-wood scent adorned with grapefruit and vetiver. I intentionally left out the juniper because I personally can’t pick it out; for me, the grapefruit is in the foreground, and shortly after that, everything else happens.

This is the real black ink; it would suit the name "Encre Noire" better than the one it has. Even the bottle (in the 50ml variant) resembles an ink barrel (https://fraguru.com/photogram/rj/95/7Qp2tJzF5KCkCwQ0.jpg). At first, there is the noticeably sweet grapefruit, which already has a bitter quality that is intensified here by juniper. Together with the immediately noticeable more intense darker notes (foremost vetiver), it creates an opening of liquid, watery ink, deep black and all-consuming. It is not fruity or citrusy; it is really as if the characteristics of grapefruit are merely used here to create a chord of liquid-fresh ink - and it succeeds. This opening lasts only a few minutes (~5, if at all), drying as quickly as ink on paper. Now the spicy properties of juniper become more prominent, and the vetiver impresses with a distinctly earthy and smoky quality. For the next approximately 15 minutes, it is this intense and imposing bitter-spicy vetiver blend that I perceive as the olfactory event of an old, indeed ancient piece of paper being written on with this dense, black, liquid ink. We inscribe our name on an Egyptian papyrus scroll, entering a burial chamber. The guestbook of Osiris. From there on, the scent becomes increasingly drier; the smokiness recedes, now coming across as more dusty, the earthiness becomes more mineral-like, one might postulate lead. The latter only reinforces that it still distinctly smells of ink. Very slight woody notes emerge, softening the scent, while leather now makes a stronger appearance. Writing instruments and scrolls are likely stored back in their leather cases. I would not describe the scent as particularly mythical or mystical, contrary to the Egyptian imagery; it is striking and interesting, far from generic, there is indeed something mysterious about it, but it is so easily identifiable as ink that it does not hold me in thrall thereafter. That does not mean I like it any less: I love this ancient, dusty, earthy quality, the beauty of the musty, these are generally some of my favorite notes, and I also find that the concept of "ink" has been brilliantly executed here - so brilliantly, in fact, that I find it truly astonishing that this apparently was not even a concept. Well, whatever, for me, this is Black Ink & Leather, or rather Encre Noire. As a personal note, I would like to mention that this scent reminds me of one of my uncles. A gentle, pleasant, and naturally well-groomed person. This certainly helps to love the scent even more. I cannot say much about the longevity and projection of the perfume yet, as I only have a sample. However, I can definitely say that one should not be deterred by the "Cologne" label here: the performance seems quite solid in terms of longevity and sillage, should not fall short of many Eau de Toilettes. Perhaps I will someday come into possession of a bottle of this scent, and then I will have more details to report on this.

This scent is truly pure leather! And I love it! In my opinion, the warm note that resonates in the background has something vanilla-like (which, according to the listed notes, isn't actually present..). I am also surprised by the mentioned grapefruit note. On my skin, BW&L consistently smells of leather, vanilla, and wood, so overall very warm, heavy, and indeed a bit scratchy, which I attribute more to the leather than to a citrus fruit. I can definitely perceive it on myself all day long, on clothing for almost weeks, and others occasionally notice this scent on me, which is why I would classify the sillage as very strong. Of course, men can also wear this scent, as it is a unisex fragrance, but I find it even more fascinating on women! Something different that you definitely don't smell just anywhere.

...one mentally climbs, crawls, and fights when applying this beautiful fragrance. Once we reach a clearing, we first sit down by the campfire. The smoke smells spicy... someone must have mixed in some juniper branches with the wood. Against the warmth, a refreshing grapefruit counters - we have also brought some fruit for our picnic. This image forms for me after applying Bronze Wood & Leather. I would recommend the fragrance for the cold season. Thanks to the grapefruit, which is barely noticeable, the scent can probably still be enjoyed in spring. I was initially disappointed with the longevity, as I quickly became accustomed to the novel leather-wood molecule (which the perfumer mentions on JoMalone.co.uk), but the people around me say it is still noticeable after several hours. So it is indeed a true Cologne Intense. According to Jo Malone, these variants are comparable to Eau de Parfums. At first, I thought this fragrance layered well with other scents from the British house. However, I now prefer to wear it solo again. I had the impression that Malone's fruity-floral representatives overshadow this warm-hearted charmer. Update: After a long-term test, I am lowering my fragrance rating by half a note - the scent progression is unfortunately quite linear - the fragrance holds too few surprises for me :-(

It consists of several clichés but really well maded, and it is not bad in practice. I consider Gentlemen Only Casual Chic to be in the same category as Chanel Egoiste, A&F Pierce, PDM Percival and so on, but the exquisite shaving cream-like side of it and, above all, its pleasant powdery feel underneath makes it stand out a bit more. But sadly it has poor performance. It lasts two to three hours and disappears literally, and I, of course, add that it's not because my nose is tired. It's very much like Gentlemen Only, but compared to GO, it has no smoky animalic scent. So it gives a fresher and clearer feel, but actually in other words, it's a thing like GO, with the base notes removed altogether. It's certainly not bad, and if it had better perfomance, I might have bought it for myself. But at this price range, I can say about 3,000 perfumes that are better than this. I think it's as good as Egoiste considering its scent, but at best it's a little better than Ferrari Light Essence considering its performance.

I am rocking this cologne right now, I love it, so unique, so manly, so different. I was never turned away by the bad reviews, and I am glad I looked into this one. Gentlemen Only Casual Chic turns 4 years old now, it's a divine fragrance for men, and it's my second Gentlemen Only cologne together with the original one, of which is a youthful flanker, not heavy and in your face, closely akin yet featuring ginger, cardamom, and juniper. First thing first, the glass is the same English-style flask already used by the range, crystalline with a heavy metal cap, an orange straw, and a pale azure juice within that creates bluish reflections. On the get-go, it starts with green, balsamic, and fresh spicy elements without any citrusy accord, juniper berries are the leading note, with a so bitter, cool, bright, and piny redolence. The initial spray seems to have an element of orange for the first few seconds or so before the spicy and woody aroma emerges. It has an outdoorsy vibe that is topped by the ginger and juniper notes which creates quite an interesting combination. The heart and base are where this really shines. The balsamic and spicy aspects fade away and the woody notes come into focus. It isn't a one-note accord, rather a bunch of fresh spices like invigorating ginger and minty cardamom, greenish birch leaves that provide a soft leather accord, and mild cedarwood. Less prominent warm spicy and leather accords create fantastic depth to make you smell phenomenal, with just a little bit of mint. A minty smooth leather unconventional accord. The ginger note reminds me of Dior Homme Sport, although I would not say Casual Chic smells like Dior Homme Sport, and I find it to be quite ‘green’ and woodsy, like a walk in the forest on a late spring or summer day, but it doesn’t go full woods as compared to other scents. Then it starts to dry down into a still fresh, woodsy scent with a seductive tiny hint of vanilla staying close to the skin, presumably coming from the ambroxan, which keeps it warm and smooth without getting overpowered by the cedar. Ambroxan is as sweet as in Dior Sauvage, unquestionably. More, the creamy, woody, clean scent from the cedar and sandalwood combo is superb. Casual Chic is a very safe scent, classy, versatile, it can be worn to work, school, or on a day spent around town. You can wear this in the day or evening, but I think it lends itself better to daytime wear. The best season to wear this is in the spring and it can be worn in summer if you do not live someplace that's really warm. It's not groundbreaking, but it doesn't smell much like anything else in my collection. I receive a compliment nearly every time I wear this stuff. Not a date fragrance but you might impress someone at the office with this one and get a date that way, you know? -Elysium

At least the marketing people have done something right. Because when looking at the Gentlemen Only Casual Chic bottle, the extension "Only" can easily be overlooked. And whether it’s about "men" or "man"? The neurons in my limbic system don’t care; they dance the samba and send wave after wave towards the cortex, where many good memories reside, some of which are also connected to the right gentleman. It’s clear that I approached this test with a slightly positive mindset - which was necessary, as I only had a sample in the form of a small pouch, containing significantly less than half a milliliter. Usually, these things end up in the trash without a second thought, as you can hardly open them without spilling the entire contents over your hands and the floor, leaving nothing for more suitable places. I would have preferred a small spray atomizer. But well, once opened, there’s no turning back. First realization: Casual Chic has nothing to do with the Gentleman from 1974. But not bad! A promising, spicy, fresh, sweet scent reaches my nose. Ginger, but also a tiny bit of apple compote, I would say. Not quite as intense and much clearer than Boss Bottled, which I would like to place the Givenchy near. Of course, there are deviations, but these largely disappear with the sandalwood base. Overall, the sillage is somewhat more restrained, and with around six hours, the longevity is shorter than that of Boss, which is too casual for me as a business scent, while the Givenchy doesn’t seem casual enough for a purely leisure fragrance. Casual Chic starts lively and fresh. Next to it, the bottle almost resembles stale apple juice spritzer. The sweet impression, which dominates most of the development, becomes prominent shortly after the start. After about four hours, the peak has long passed, and the warm, woody base note typical of sandalwood spreads. Even though this isn’t particularly imaginative, I usually find these sandalwood bases acceptable. Chic but not really casual - rather lackluster, as nothing else happens during the course. Those looking for a straightforward scent and who like sandalwood with birch and cedar will be very satisfied with this little water. Unexpected nuances should not be anticipated. Even the Boss has more to offer. Nevertheless - quite suitable for business, appropriate for her and him, more of an autumn/winter scent. It wasn’t a lost "scent-test-day," but I won’t mourn the empty pouch - that is, the Casual Chic - impression either.

Recently, while testing at the big D perfumery, I noticed Givenchy's Gentlemen for the very first time. The bottles had probably been so inconspicuous and unremarkable to me until now that I simply always overlooked them. Well, I had discovered them and first had to orient myself to understand what the difference among the gentlemen was. Ahh, probably in the scent, even though I could hardly imagine it. But my nose taught me otherwise.
