Cedars sprout and shoot up at an unprecedented speed. I linger with my eyes closed for several hours, enjoying the silence, undisturbed even by my own thoughts. “We must learn to wake up again and to keep ourselves awake, ... through the unceasing expectation of the sunrise, which must not leave us in the deepest sleep.” * ---------- To say one thing upfront, I do not know The One and I have only smelled Le Male once ages ago, so no comparisons from my side here. Quatre pour Homme Absolu de Nuit starts with sweet lemon underlaid with lavender and a hint of sage. Quite quickly, this is overtaken by a soft, woody note, and I also perceive vanilla. That is probably the Akigalawood®. Fragrances with a ® make me skeptical at first, and yes, it does smell a bit artificial, but it is alright (much more pleasant than, for example, Cashmeran). As the scent develops, it becomes spicier (pepper, nutmeg) and gains a fine green component from vetiver and patchouli. Then there is the cedar. I really like the scent. At the very end, the Akigalawood® and the vanilla reappear, but only very close to the skin. The pleasure lasts on the skin for 5-6 hours, on fabric for 7-8. Quatre pour Homme Absolu de Nuit is not so easy to categorize: on one hand, boring artificial wood-vanilla, on the other hand, beautiful green-spicy cedar. Everything is quite smooth, without edges or corners; there could certainly have been much more in it. But it is also a nice, warm no-brainer for the colder season. ---------- * from Walden by Henry David Thoreau

I bought it because I was looking for a more pleasant Le Male "clone". I love the base note of Le Male extremely, but the synthetic quality of the top note prevents me from wearing it every time. This one initially reminds me a lot of Le Male and then shifts towards The One over time (as my predecessor has analyzed well). It is a good scent, very pleasant and also sexy with good potential for compliments. Unfortunately, it couldn't end my search, what a pity.

Despite the listed notes, 154 mostly smells leathery on me. It's got a sharp burst of lavender on top that mixes with something fruity to remind me of that "woody amber" aquatic smell, but it ends up as a semi-metallic quinoline-heavy piney leather with a healthy dose of basil and juniper berry. I think 154 is trying to smell like a modern men's designer scent on top and a classic masculine leathery woody chypre on the bottom, which sort of works, but ends up kind of unremarkable. As such, it's the kind of scent I want to like more than I actually do. Technically a thumbs up, but still kind of "meh".

154 Cologne is a hidden treasure, actually is the "masculine powerhouse" of the line. It opens with bergamot, rosemary and lavender. There is a slightly medicinal side to this opening which is to be expected from the camphoreous contribution of the herbs but a sweet beeswax note quickly offers comfort and body to the composition. The intense opening leads to a fragrant heart of spices and patchouli. Nutmeg, clove, patchouli leaves and warm woodiness. It is never sweet enough to be considered an oriental. Never dry enough to be considered a fougere. It is a beautiful old-fashioned, masculine chameleon of a scent, herbal, woody and spicy, with a hint of shaving lather accord. In the drydown a leather accord appears that incorporates the beeswax note. This is an everything-but-the-kitchen-sink kind of a perfume but it is extremely easy to wear, very warm, comfortable and confident.

I’ve had a few visits to the dentists in my time and the opening embodies the aroma. It smells more like the dentist’s than the dentist’s does itself. However, this is but the opening. The grapefruit begins to shine alongside the musk, and fuses to make this weird but wonderful smell of incense or candles, yet it is much sweeter. 154 dries down to be unmistakably natural, and this is made possible by the lavender and basil notes, which enhance the two stages of the opening and binds them together to make a respectable and clean scent. Hours later, near the end of the scent’s lifespan, the vetiver and patchouli begin to shine to create a different scent, but as this cologne is weaker than a dad joke, it’s not too relevant. On the whole, this is a very inoffensive, very unisex and very formal scent. Any hate this receives isn’t justified but it’s understandable, as this is one of the more mediocre colognes which Jo Malone has created. Definitely one for the workplace (preferably medicinal).

I've recently tested this fragrance on the paper strip imagining that it was the classic citrusy cologne, but I discovered a wonderful spicy scent , where the aromatic notes are well blended with the fruit and the warm base. I am a woman who usually wear sweet fragrances, but i fell in love with this cologne! Unfortunately, talking about the high price(about 100€ or more for a 100mlbottle), the longevity isn't so good and the sillage too could be better. Anyway, a great creation I added immediately to my whishlist!

The Jo Malone scent bars are almost impossible to overlook. I count 27 perfumes alone on their website, along with room fragrances and cosmetics. Every customer is helplessly exposed to the sales efforts of eager promoters, and they might suspect: not all of this can be good. Thus, the customer will have to be seduced - to those perfumes that drown out their colleagues in volume, perhaps Black Vetyver or Pomegranate Noir. A perfume as unassuming as the house number it is named after is likely to be overlooked. Yet, 154 is a charming little treasure. It is a patchwork scent: citrus-fruity at the top, fougère and spice in the heart, and oriental notes in the base - if one even wants to apply the traditional three-part division here. Because somehow, all the cited directions get tangled and woven together, leaving one truly unsure of what to expect. Just as difficult as determining a scent character is defining its gender. Herbal and sharp spice characterize the men’s fragrance, yet fluffy musk and patchouli pull it back - a men’s fragrance for women! I particularly enjoy a beautiful, transparent-ethereal note, slightly green and iridescent. I recognize it in a similar form from the wonderful Aventure by Il Profvmo; perhaps the same fragrance material was used. 154 doesn’t make much of an impression and can’t decide, yet I hesitate to speak of arbitrariness here. Because all in all, a certain character does emerge, albeit not an extroverted one. With this light perfume, I suspect it could interact strongly with individual skin chemistry, simply because it seems so light. Thus, 154 will surely remain reserved for the more discerning customers - those who can set aside the overly loud and unfortunately not always good fragrances of this brand with assured taste. After over 10 years in the lineup, 154 will not stand without friends. Thank you for the sample!

154 could be so beautiful! Could be, because the scent does not live up to what it promises (to me). On one hand, it is completely harmonious and perfect for my preferences as a daytime fragrance, because it is green, subtly spicy, rather cool than warm, and therefore there is actually nothing to complain about.

Admittedly: the first 154 seconds of this little fragrance feel relatively pleasant. It simultaneously smells extremely nice, fruity, and spicy - balanced, elegant, and even original. But shortly thereafter, the scent develops a sour, unripe, and ... let’s say herbally dry character - and thus is anything but pleasant.

And another one from my fragrance stick test series. Merci bien, mon cher (I just couldn't find the "roof"...and I have no patience to search!!) It lasts. And it's really good. Masculine. Almost traditional, almost fougère, if it weren't for the soft base with vanilla. I won't say much about the opening, it's relatively short-lived.

Yes, with its freshness and spiciness of basil, sandalwoods, and a hint of lavender, 154 smells exactly like I remember Cool Water. So far the first Malone that I couldn't wear, because for me it is not a unisex scent, but a classic green-spicy-woody-aquatic men's fragrance. Masculine, aromatic, and strong.

The Elixir version of Ange ou Démon Le Secret immediately brought to mind bubblegum, but not the childish pleasure of a yummy fresh piece of gum still in the wrapper. Rather, this conjures up a piece of gum that is quickly warming up in the mouth as the juicy artificial flavors are being rapidly released onto the palate along with a heavy dose of magical high fructose corn syrup. The type of bubblegum is a particular brand of individually wrapped candy I see in the US, rarely, except for around particularly around Halloween; has a distinctive Sasparilla (originally made from a blend Smilax regelii plant extract, birch oils and sassafras)- benzoin complex sort of like root beer flavoring, but here it is just a hint compared to the true rootbeer fragrances, such as Aqua Di Parma's "Mandorlo". That being said, this fragrance is not for those who shy away from sweet fragrances, like myself. This is also not an office appropriate fragrance for anyone, because it is totally distracting. This is one of those "Head Turner" fragrances for a night out on the town dancing with friends and anytime it's appropriate to yell "Keep Those Appletinis Coming!". It's the kind of bubblegum scent that smells better mixed with secondhand smoke, sweaty skin and desire. It is sweet sultry seduction in a bottle. As it dries down I get a clear image of Olivia Newton John Circa 1979 in 'Xanadu', sporting mini dolphin shirts and roller skates and all. Likewise, I imagine that this is what Blondie wished she smelled like while singing 'Heart of Glass' with her insanely metallic red glossy lip, feathered hair and the spandex clad 'Solid Gold Dancers' in the background, back in the 80s. If these references don't resonate, I apologize, I'm outdated, but this fragrance is definitely not...it's a bold, sweet, strong and naughty modern interpretation of a youthful bubblegum fantasy.

When I first tested on the paper, it was more like citrus and woody floral. I liked it but was not impressed. Then I accidently got a sample, and I must say it's much better on skin because the vanilla base was missing on the paper. I can pick out jasmin, tea, lemon, vanilla and patchouli notes. I didn't have grape/bubblegum like some previous reviews. The first hour reminds me of Alien EDP mainly because of rather intensive jasmin, but they smell absolutely different. After 3 or 4 hours it makes me think of Kenzo Amour maybe due to woody-vanilla base. Overall it's a powdery-sweet scent balanced with citrus and woody notes. It's not too sweet and kind of fresh. The drydown vanilla blended with tea and other woody notes is very comforting. It's sensual and still fresh. The sillage is close to skin and the longevity is about 7 or 8h. Originally written in 2013.

I forgot that this fragrance was a flanker of Ange ou Demon Le Secret. As a result, I spent the first few hours wondering why Ange ou Demon Le Secret Elixir wasn't a stronger, more vanillary version of Ange ou Demon. I have now come to the realisation that I'm an idiot. Ange ou Demon Le Secret Elixir is a dark, yet surprisingly fresh tea scent. I don't find it all that sensual, however it does have a rather mysterious feel. It's a good choice for a warm night spent outdoors. To my nose, this isn't an overly complex scent. I smell watery tea, dewy jasmine, a hint of lemon, musty patchouli and white musk. Unfortunately I could not detect the sweetness that some have noted in their reviews. It was just a fresh, green jasmine-tea scent on my skin. It's a much stronger scent when compared to the original Ange ou Demon Le Secret. The projection is pleasing without being too overpowering. The longevity is not bad either. If you already own Ange ou Demon Le Secret, there isn't any reason to go out and buy Ange ou Demon Le Secret Elixir too. They are quite similar, the only difference being, this version has a richer patchouli accord in the base and stronger sillage. Original review written: February 2013.

The top note opens with the unmistakable scent of jasmine, the heavy sweetness of orange blossom, paired with a good splash of lemon. Although the tea note is not prominent, it is still recognizable throughout the entire fragrance journey. I also see the similarity to Le Secret EdP, while I recognize the sweetness more from the "regular" Ange ou Demon. The association I have in the first hour with Le Secret Elixir EdP is a slightly over-sweetened fruit tea (rosehip?) with a slice of lemon added. A real base note does not establish itself for me. After that, the sugar content decreases proportionally to the scent intensity. For the fragrance to last 5-6 hours, I really have to spray it generously. This is not a problem with the 100 ml bottle (which, by the way, is quite hefty and relatively unwieldy); at first, the perfume also seems quite intense. However, this is labeled as an "Intense EdP," which I cannot confirm compared to the aforementioned fragrances. My surroundings also did not comment on the perfume when I wore it, so I conclude that it does not have a strong sillage. Nevertheless, I like the scent, even now in summer temperatures. Then I add a few ice cubes to the tea glass and enjoy the uplifting, sensual side of Le Secret Elixir on a warm summer evening. But I also find pleasure in it on cooler days, as it feels like a comforting cup of tea when you come home completely soaked on a rainy day. My only concern is that I might get tired of it relatively quickly.

I had to revise my statement. It read: "Fruity, floral, warm, way too sweet for me, yet it fascinates with its special, bitter charm. I’m even considering wearing it!" Indeed, Ange ou Démon Le Secret Elixir has a truly special charm and - I have now succumbed to it. I am no longer just considering wearing it; no, I have almost used up my sample. However, I am still contemplating. I am now considering buying a bottle. Surprisingly, I no longer notice the sweetness at all. I don’t reject sweet fragrances; I just don’t like it when the sweetness seems to cover up flaws in composition or ingredients, when sweetness becomes the main ingredient. This is definitely not the case with Ange ou Démon Le Secret Elixir. In the top note, Ange ou Démon Le Secret Elixir begins with a citrusy freshness. The tea prevents the opening from being one-dimensional and adds a soft background of neroli and lemon. For me, the top note is pleasant and well-composed, but not particularly outstanding. I really like patchouli and find it a great pleasure how patchouli here gently announces the base without becoming too dominant. Both musk and vanilla come across naturally and stay pleasantly in the background. But the base ultimately isn’t anything particularly new. So why have I succumbed to Ange ou Démon Le Secret Elixir then? It started with this "special charm" that emanates from the bitter-powdery heart note. Now, it’s not that I hadn’t smelled frangipani, jasmine, and orange blossom before. All three are even candidates that I sometimes don’t like at all and can even ruin a fragrance for me. So, the ingredient list for the heart note wouldn’t have particularly appealed to me just from reading. However, in Ange ou Démon Le Secret Elixir, these three flowers are perfectly coordinated: the orange blossom contributes the bitterness without becoming too harsh and demanding, the jasmine keeps most of its cloying stinkiness to itself and adds a floral warmth, while frangipani gives the heart note something exotic. All three together merge into a devilishly extraordinary, warm-bitter, and somewhat scratchy, novel powderiness that awakens me. The heart note lasts for a good five, maybe six hours. And since it keeps drawing my attention throughout this entire period, constantly challenging me in some way, the comparatively boring base afterward is wonderfully relaxing, almost relieving. Now the constant, interesting, but also somewhat exhausting challenge of the heart note has come to an end, and I can find peace. And thus, my change of heart regarding Ange ou Démon Le Secret Elixir is explained: The heart note is exceptionally special, but it is so curiously bitter and also somewhat demanding that it captivated me, yet I couldn’t really identify with it at first. It was too foreign to me. On the other hand, the top note and base were too normal for me at first, which now makes me particularly fond of this fragrance. The fascination for the extraordinary led me to wear Ange ou Démon Le Secret Elixir from time to time, and gradually it became more familiar. Will I ever really identify so much that I buy a bottle? Probably at the latest when my sample is used up....I think I can hear the demon giggling again.

Well, there are fragrances that truly have it "in them"! This is also true for this elegantly crafted "Calvin Klein," which represents a variant of "Euphoria (Eau de Parfum) | Calvin Klein." While the "original" was already very original, THIS one is in a heightened manner. What starts off quite harmlessly with fruity-tart black currant reveals more of itself as time goes on. The somewhat "heavy" flowers already cause a stir. Initially a bit too "overbearing" for me, they are later softened in their intensity by "earthy" patchouli. What ultimately makes this perfume so "eccentric" and magical is the "return of all fragrance notes in a changed order and always with different partners"! This means: When you think one of the components of the scent, for example the black currant, has been exhausted or is almost gone, it comes back with force after a certain time. Now paired with the darker ingredients, like vetiver and patchouli. Or when you think the dark "orchids" have given up their spirit, they suddenly pop back up in tow with the other ingredients. And from the outset, you can never say what will return when and in what combination. Mystical? Definitely! Oops!! The patchouli is making a comeback! What will it bring along? ;-))

Imagine there is this meadowsweet. A shy, charming creature that everyone always overlooks and has stolen your heart. And you’ve heard she is at this gathering with a few acquaintances. You know them, and you don’t really have anything against them, but you’re only going to the gathering because of this heavenly creature. And then the long-awaited evening arrives. You’re excited as can be, have thought of all sorts of things you want to say, what you want to find out about her, and so on. It’s a memorable evening: The grapefruit jumps out at you and doesn’t leave. It takes you over and chats your ear off. Then, fashionably late, the wheat arrives. He stands in the doorway for a long time and then finally sits down. The wheat is a cool guy, but rather reserved. And the grapefruit is chatting away the whole time. Then the vetiver appears. The only one you already know well, who can interrupt the constantly talking grapefruit, and brings about an interesting conversation with his buddy wheat and you. But you keep glancing at the door, waiting for the meadowsweet. Just before eleven o’clock, the grapefruit disappears. The wheat hops on his bike shortly after and rides off. At some point just before midnight, you finally understand - meadowsweet, she’s not coming anymore. And together with the vetiver, you sit depressed at the bar, drunkenly staring at the dusty bottles of schnapps. First just intense grapefruit, a brief interlude with wheat, and in the end only vetiver. No trace of meadowsweet - not even as a platonic idea. Unisex. Sillage okay, longevity average, price-performance ratio very questionable.

I am a happy man. Because I - at least this has always been the case so far - have generally been most satisfied with my current age. If I could choose, I would often wish to simply hold on to the present. With a few exceptions - those moments when I count gray hairs too closely and for too long in front of the bathroom mirror - I never wanted to be sixteen or twenty-five again. I am a happy man. Because I - and happiness is often only recognized when it’s gone - had a carefree childhood. That is one thing I sometimes think back to with longing - that this all-encompassing carefreeness beyond childhood never returned. Picking flowers in the meadow for my mother and looking forward to how happy she will be on the way home. A Mini Milk and half an hour of Tom & Jerry. And nothing else. The meadow where I picked flowers was not far from our house. It was not a special meadow. People took their dogs there. Buttercups and dandelions grew there - and further down, coltsfoot, dead-nettles, and meadow foam. I played hide and seek there, learned to ride a bike, and scraped my knees. This meadow was the kingdom of my carefree childhood, for which I am so grateful to have had. Jo Malone's Green Wheat & Meadowsweet is the scent of my lost kingdom. Although it was a Rhenish meadow and not an English one. Although I can’t really remember either meadowsweet or wheat. A scent of innocence and youth. It is simple and unadorned - and creating such simple and unadorned scents is often the most difficult. Fresh, green-bitter grass and a hint of honey sweetness. The meadow. Later a Mini Milk and Tom & Jerry. And nothing else. Conclusion: I am a happy man. And scents like this remind me of that. In case I ever forget.

Today I am writing again about one of the new Jo Malone - English Fields fragrances. As you may know, these fragrances aim to impart a special note through various grain notes. Today, I will comment on Green Wheat & Meadowsweet, which translates to Green Wheat and Meadowsweet. Although I have tried this fragrance before, I was able to test it more extensively recently during a Jo Malone event. Although the delicious snacks and free drinks were the real reason for my presence at the event (argh, I probably shouldn't mention that, now I'll never get invited to such events again…!), I did enjoy all the fragrances quite a bit :DD But seriously, the new fragrances from Jo Malone all have something appealing about them, and I believe that each one is worth testing; there should be a nice scent for almost every taste! The Fragrance: The fragrance starts off briefly fresh with a zesty grapefruit, which I really like; however, it seems to smell longer and more intensely on a test strip than on my skin. You can also recognize this grapefruit note much more easily on paper, as it wasn't immediately apparent on my skin (at least not on my skin), and this scent was simply perceived as "citrusy." In any case, green notes quickly come into play. These are just general green notes; perhaps one could also call them plant juices, which, in my opinion, smell really great. Gradually, the fragrance develops a dry, wheat-like note. The dryness feels like a plant that has been roasted or dried in the sun, so warm-dry with a slightly Mediterranean feeling. Overall, it is a lovely scent that, in my opinion, is not an everyday fragrance and comes across nicely. This makes the fragrance seem spicy to me, even though it retains a pleasant freshness. The only thing I'm unsure about is how the meadowsweet truly smells (or perhaps it is the meadowsweet that comes across as so dry). In any case, over time I detect light, sweet notes that seem to become more powdery in the later base, almost smelling vanilla-like. Otherwise, the fragrance is also somewhat dry in the (late) base, a bit green, and as previously described, slightly powdery or creamy sweet, even if that might sound a bit contradictory due to the dry notes. The fragrance seems generally not very complex, but it has something… something pleasing about it that one should try out. The Sillage and Longevity: The longevity is moderate, although it should radiate a bit stronger at first. Unfortunately, it is not a scent that will be easily detectable from a distance. The longevity is quite okay; you can smell the fragrance for about eight hours, maybe even a bit longer (but then only very faintly). The Bottle: Ah, the bottles of the entire fragrance line here are very beautiful. Strictly speaking, the bottle is actually just rectangular and slim. But the lovely pastel colors (this one is a pale light green) look great, and additionally, the rocky wallpaper in the lower third of the bottle greatly enhances its appearance, making it not only look good but also feel nice. In contrast, the rather discreetly placed name of the fragrance on the front seems unassuming. As I said, a very beautiful bottle. First of all, I must say that this fragrance, out of all five, really comes across as unisex, while the other four seem more feminine. This is probably because the fragrance, especially at the beginning, comes across as less sweet and more citrusy and, above all, dry-grain-like. The term "dry" might be perceived negatively here, but it is a lovely kind of dry-floral scent. It feels to me, as I mentioned earlier in the fragrance description, a bit Mediterranean. By that, I mean that wonderful feeling when you walk through meadows and fields with rocky-dusty hiking paths in sunny vacation spots in Mediterranean countries and perceive those dry plant notes. Later, the dryness of the fragrance subsides a bit, and the scent gradually becomes more powdery-sweet, although the sillage decreases significantly. But that doesn't matter, as the fragrance always smells nice and good to me. You can wear this fragrance well in spring and summer, especially during the day, as it has not become a scent for going out for me; however, I think it would also work wonderfully for evening strolls. In any case, I find the fragrance very worth trying :)

I can already tell you, I am in love with this scent. It is a dreamy companion for the warmer spring days and summer. The Bottle: But before I get carried away with my enthusiasm, let's first discuss the obvious: the bottle design. Typical for Jo Malone fragrances in a limited edition, all English Fields scents appear in the classic Jo Malone design with a twist. This time, the glass of the bottle is painted in pastel colors and glazed in the lower third with a structured and contrasting color. This creates a texture reminiscent of stone and porcelain, as if Jo Malone had teamed up with Villeroy & Boch. It is elegant and chic and fits perfectly in the hand. The cap is made of plastic this time and is in the same color as the upper two-thirds of the bottle. The caps fit a bit tighter than usual, making the fragrance often release with a satisfying "pop" sound. As beautiful as the bottles are, they do have a downside and an upside at the same time. On one hand, the fragrance is somewhat protected from light, but even held against a light source, the fill level can only be guessed at. Additionally, the color transitions are not cleanly executed on all bottles, and some have a slight color shadow in the transition. Those who care about this should take a close look at the bottles before purchasing. The Fragrance: In Green Wheat & Meadowsweet, three fragrance notes primarily come together. As a result, the development of the scent over time is rather minimal. It starts with a grapefruit that we have not encountered in this form from Jo Malone before. While the grapefruit in the namesake EdC was rather bitter, here we are greeted with a sweeter, gentler grapefruit that still hasn't fallen into the candy bowl and has nothing to do with a cleaning product scent. This grapefruit is delicate, sweet, juicy, and has just the right amount of acidity, without making you grimace when taking a bite. Here, neither the sour enjoyment nor any bitterness tugs at the taste buds, but rather a freshness kick perfectly suited for breakfast in the morning comes to meet you. Very quickly after the grapefruit, the green wheat and meadowsweet set in. The scent becomes softer, retains its freshness, and the slightly sweet, floral note adds a hint of creaminess. I can also easily perceive the subtle spiciness mentioned in the statements. It’s almost as if not just the flowers of the meadowsweet, but the entire plant has flowed into the fragrance, and it is astonishing how lovely a plant that can grow up to 2m tall can smell. By the way, it’s also a great medicinal plant. ;) After that, the fragrance does not change for me and clings to my skin for 6 hours, which I am absolutely satisfied with, as it is good just the way it is and does not need to change anymore. With this longevity, it ranks in the middle among Jo Malone fragrances for me. Conclusion: Grain notes and perfume, I couldn't quite imagine that, but it works. Every fragrance in the collection is enchanting, and this one is the freshest among them. My personal favorite, as it vaguely reminds me of Chanel Chance eau Fraiche, and it’s almost as if the slightly biting citrus notes have been taken from the Chanel scent and transformed it into a well-rounded experience. I can hardly wait for the warmer spring days to arrive so that this fragrance becomes my everyday companion.

It was 2015, just before my last vacation in Italy with my boyfriend. A year before my relationship fell apart. I was wandering around Douglas because I was still looking for a vacation scent, and the saleswoman suggested Eternity Summer. I took a quick sniff, bought it! I still remember that I found the longevity poor back then, but the scent itself was just perfect, especially in the heat. It is fresh, really fresh, and smells of citrus and Cool Water Woman. I used it up relatively quickly and only left a little for memory's sake. However, I eventually used up the rest quickly as it always reminded me of summer. Unfortunately, the fragrance was no longer available anywhere. Only now have I learned that the 2019 edition was released again. I quickly searched the internet and actually found it. It arrived today, I opened the packaging, carefully took the bottle out, and paused for a moment: What did it smell like in 2015? The last good years before everything fell apart, before a stroke of fate hit my life. 2015, the last year I was happy. I want it to be like that again. Then I sprayed the fragrance. I was startled! All the memories came back like a flash, it’s summer 2015 and I am happy! I just thought wow, fragrances can be like a time travel. Then I wondered if the scent could also make me sad. To find out, I wore it all day today, but no, it doesn’t make me sad. It reminds me of Italy, of summer, and of good times. I like it and I want it. It reminds me of myself. Of my old self that was happy, and I want to become that again. It reminds me that one can fight for their happiness and that life can be beautiful. It can stay, it must stay. I even ordered another bottle before it’s gone for good. It became clear to me today what power fragrances have.

This is the first Jo Malone scent I actually dislike. Honestly, I don't know what I expected but not this. I was hoping it would not be at least a bit fruity, considering "red currant" in the name, and it isn't. It is very aromatic (and not in a good way!), and the opening is very sharp, it gave me a headache. Do not buy this if you are looking for a fruity currant scent! There is exactly zero currant here. This is for people who love vetiver and the like. Grassy.

I like the scent of almonds and sandalwood, the blackcurrant adds a refreshing touch. The fragrance is well-made, becoming beautifully creamy on the skin over time, and it is not too strong, which I find pleasant. I find the color of the bottle downright terrible and it looks like plastic. It does not fit the Jo Malone brand at all. A regular clear glass bottle would have been much more valuable, what a shame.

I was pleasantly surprised by VERY IRRESISTIBLE L'INTENSE, having been rather underwhelmed by VERY IRRESISTIBLE. It turns out that these already meaningless flanker names mean even less than nothing, since they bear no clear compositional or category relation to the original whatsoever. As far as I'm concerned, they do nothing but sow confusion. Who can remember which of the flurry of VERY IRRESISTIBLE flankers they actually liked? Did I mention that "very irresistible" is like saying "very perfect"? Look, it's either irresistible or it is not. There are no degrees of irresistibility or perfection: something either is or is not. VERY IRRESISTIBLE, a fruity-floral in the same general category as The Body Shop CASSIS ROSE, posed no resistance challenges to this nose whatsoever. But I digress... Why do I like VI L'INTENSE so much better? The composition is simple, but it works: plum + patchouli + rose + musk. Not too sweet, and dark enough fruit to add some nighttime appeal. I wouldn't necessarily confer the honorific title of chypre upon this creation, but it's certainly not as trivial as most fruity-floral frags. Some people have made allusions to Calvin Klein EUPHORIA in connection with this perfume, but I find EUPHORIA far more woody and spicy (and, frankly, blunt) than VERY IRRESISTIBLE L'INTENSE, which really does seem to me to be a relatively well-constructed and pleasing four-note wonder: plum, patchouli, rose, and musk.

Very Irresistible L'Intense is a flanker that deserves to be on the shelves. I am rather impressed by Givenchy's flankers actually, I find there's a reason for each and every one of them. The thought of yet another Very Irresistible release rarely makes me cringe, because I trust that I'll enjoy them. This fragrance is on the darker side of the spectrum. It has rich and musky nuances of rose, plum and patchouli. Quite a sensual blend in fact. There aren't many similarities between this fragrance and the original, apart from the dominant rose note. The rose in Very Irresistible L'Intense is much stronger and in some ways, comes bearing more attitude. Think Midnight Poison by Dior, just less masculine. I'm a huge fan of patchouli and red roses, so naturally this is a fragrance that appeals to me. However some may find this scent rather off-putting and perhaps even a little too bold. I personally think Very Irresistible L'Intense is quite a stunning and edgy little fragrance, rough on the outside but warm and fuzzy in the middle. The sillage is quite strong, so a light application is advised, however the longevity was a little disappointing with the scent lasting no longer than five hours on my skin. I fancied this fragrance as a night-clubbing scent initially, yet I don't know whether it could manage to withstand a night of dancing and cheeky shots. Nevertheless, Very Irresistible L'Intense is a pleasant fragrance, perfect for a woman that is searching for a mysterious and daring scent to add to her wardrobe. I must add that I like the tattoo style bottle also.

I feel as though each note here does exactly what it should - there's no overpowering anywhere. I just go weak in the knees for that dark & spicy patchouli! Ugh, and that plum is just mouth-watering! It's self-described as 'edgy', but I'm not sure I agree with that. Though it's an undeniably dark, mysterious 'noir'-type scent, it's actually pretty gentle, mature, and quietly alluring. It rests on your skin waiting to be discovered, rather than alerting you to its presence.

Nice oriental with rose-patchouli-musk combination, sweetness appears later. Very longlasting 8+ hours, a winter perfume which can be used also during spring. Lovely bottle with silver tribal tattoo design. Reminds alot of Euphoria and Play Intense, a quality perfume indeed. Definitely a winner!

Plum, rose and patchouli, and very nice too. I would probably have bought a bottle, but I have Natori and this does it so much better than the Givenchy. Natori is the diamond standard and this is a little bit rhinestone in comparison. Still it is a very good fragrance and worth seeking out.........but it's not Natori!

Givenchy often surprises me. Be it the first EdP Verry Irresistible, which I loved to wear as a teenager, the wonderfully unconventional Ange ou Demon, or the beautiful, wintry coziness of Pi. There are no wishes left unfulfilled. A few weeks ago, I was lured in by the fascinating bottle. I love wearing black; it seems so mystical, radiates power, and combines wonderfully.

Good evening everyone, here I am again (…did you just start sighing?? Shame on you!! :D)! Today I would like to introduce Very Irrésistible L’Intense by Givenchy, a fragrance line from Givenchy that already has countless different flankers, none of which I have tested yet.

Today is Sunday and I was rummaging through my sample box when the vial of Irresistible Intense fell into my hands. I hadn't tried that one yet. I actually wanted to write a comment on Sensi, but that hurdle feels too big for me today. This one is easier, as the scent is much simpler. I like it a lot! This is how I like roses. At first, however, I smell plum.

A ripe, soft, dark blue almost black plum. No, there must be more. So intense, it almost takes my breath away. Overly sweet, it is a heavy sweetness that nearly overwhelms you if, like me, you aren't expecting it. This plum becomes elegant with the appearance of the rose. When I close my eyes now, I see a rock concert at midnight, the guitars booming.

Some time ago, I found a sample of this in the middle of a magazine. Of course, I had to test it right away. The only thing was that I flipped through the fashion magazine during my lunch break, and the test then fell into the following working hours. So the open sample bag lay on my desk, providing a wonderfully enticing distraction time and again.

Boucheron has a beautiful collection of perfumes, named unimaginatively as La Collection, that highlights one accord from its point of origin. Rose d’Isparta and Iris de Syracuse are the other two from this collection that I own. It is arguable if that note truly belongs to the city or location in the name. Though these perfumes are relatively unknown, they are very good, and some are even great. Michel Almairac and Clément Marx, two perfumers affiliated with Robertet, are the noses behind Cuir de Venise. The future of this collection is uncertain because of the complicated marketing arrangement between Inter Parfums and Boucheron. This review is based on full bottle that I bought from a US discounter. According to the perfumers, guaiac wood is the main ingredient that imparts its personality to this perfume. Guaiac wood and Palo Santo are used interchangeably by many perfumers and perfume websites to denote various woods from South America and the Caribbean. As both Almairac and Marx works for Robertet, I conclude that they are using Robertet’s guaiac wood oil from Bulnesia sarmientoi. Bulnesia sarmientoi is described to have a sweet, dry, woody, floral-rosy odor. When someone mentions guaiac wood or Palo Santo, it is important to identify the botanical species used to make that oil or extract. The notes listed for Cuir de Venise on the Inter Parfums website are cocoa infusion, cinnamon, ginger, guaiac wood, papyrus, patchouli, cocoa absolute and cedarwood. This perfume is named a leather, though there is no specific leather note listed. The leather accord is created using facets of patchouli, papyrus, cocoa and guaiac wood. The cocoa in the opening is perhaps the only identifiable note that is sustained throughout the life of this perfume on the skin. I also get a fleeting cinnamon note, but I don’t get any ginger. The heart notes – guaiac wood, cocoa, papyrus and patchouli - take over very quickly. Most of it is the lush, sweet smell of guaiac wood with some minor contribution from papyrus and almost of the earthy patchouli. I suspect patchouli comes up much later as the chocolate facet in the heart notes to act as a bridge to the strong cocoa in the base notes. The base notes on my skin are mostly cocoa, guaiac and cedar, with a hint of vanilla. As you might have gathered, Cuir de Venise is an olfactory chameleon. It starts with a strong and smooth leather accord that cedes its dominance quickly to a sweet woody guaiac wood, which ends in a beautiful cocoa accord. But it is still a harmonious progression as these transitions are not well demarcated. Cuir de Venise performs very well on my skin. It lasts more than 6-8 hours with strong sillage in the first few hours. It is not recommended for office settings, unless you use it sparingly. Certain notes like cedar stays longer on my clothes. Cuir de Venise is a wonderful perfume that I recommend strongly. I rarely wear the same perfume on consecutive days, but Cuir de Venise might be the one where I break this rule. It is made using quality components and it is relatively inexpensive. It cost me $85 for 120 ml from US discounter. Though it shares some notes with Guerlain Feve Gourmande, Cuir de Venise is essentially a woody leathery fragrance with cocoa base notes. As the future of the Boucheron La Collection is unknown, it may be prudent to get a bottle soon before it disappears from the market.

Taken by the included components, I tested cuir de venise. Eagerly, I wanted to sniff out the components, but I failed. I smell so much, but I can't define anything. Everything is intertwined. I waited for the drydown, but even then I couldn't unravel anything. I wore it overnight and found it smelled the same in the morning as it did in the evening; on my skin, there is no development even after 10 hours. Overall, it smells warm, rounded, and woody, slightly sharp. For me personally, it's too monotonous.

While strolling through a perfume shop, I bumped into a stand with the summer fragrances of this season, and thus I literally stumbled upon this scent. I didn't intend to buy any new summer editions, as I already have enough, but: this is not a summer fragrance for me. Nope. After I knocked over the stand with full force, I had to set some of the little bottles back up and straighten them out. A very nice and dedicated (and I mean this SERIOUSLY and LITERALLY, NOT IRONICALLY/CYNICALLY!) saleswoman rushed to my aid. We quickly struck up a conversation, and based on my scrunched nose, she could tell that I had no interest. She let me browse in peace, and so I cautiously rummaged through the store, as there were more shelves that could jump out at me. Somehow, I was magically drawn back to the previously knocked-over display - a criminal always returns to the scene of the crime. Thus, Eternity Summer 2012 made its way onto my skin. I waited, sniffed, found it to be a typical summer fizz-fruity water, and thus it failed the test, and I moved on. I was quite proud of myself for not letting anyone talk me into nonsense. A little while later, I was at the checkout to pay for my mascara. While I was flailing around looking for my wallet, a completely enchanting scent wafted towards me. Oh, what was that? I hurriedly thought about which body parts I had doused with what, and concluded that it was Eternity Summer 2012. Hm... That couldn't be right, as the scent had failed my strict test! Hm... Or could it? I sniffed my skin again and was fascinated by its scent development: while it smelled like any run-of-the-mill summer fragrance upon spraying, it had transformed into a creamy, balsamic, fresh dream of subtle citrus fruits and an elegant floral note. Oh, how much I liked that! You can guess where I sprinted off to! Yes, bingo, I had to get it! And: this time I did NOT knock it over... At the checkout, a lively debate ensued, as the saleswoman could hardly believe that the scent smelled so good on me. Quickly, all the ladies present were encouraged to apply the scent, and it turned into a colorful sniffing and comparing session. The result was that Eternity Summer 2012 smelled quite uniform on all the others, except on me. The scent strongly reminds me of "Musc Collection for Her" by Narciso Rodriguez, but a bit lighter and more subtle - if that's even possible. It would be a good alternative, as Rodriguez is quite a bit more expensive. This only holds true if your skin behaves like mine does... Further studies on skin chemistry will follow, both on parfumo and nationwide in Germany. It remains exciting... ;) _____________ Addendum: I have to deduct a few points, as the scent develops differently depending on the temperature. If it is very warm or even hot, the scent is as described above. However, if it is a bit cooler or cools down during a German summer day, the scent becomes musty and unpleasant. How unfair! So the conclusion is: only use above 25° C, and only if you know that no cold front is on the way... - > 25° C: 90 % - < 25° C: 10 % - Overall: 50 %

This one may surprise a few Jo Malone fans simply because it is not as prim and proper as her other scents. Intense Iris & White Musk is indeed a musky fragrance, a little on the dirty side of things. From what I've learnt over the years, musk in fragrances can go two ways. Firstly it can be clean, sensual and feminine, secondly it can be dirty, animalic and loud. This fragrance falls into the second category, something that I don't think anyone would have expected. Intense Iris & White Musk opens sharply with dirty and damp musk and a hint of sparkling aldehydes. The scent softens over the course of its development, rounding off into a somewhat soapy blend of iris, lily and musk. My ideal musk is Original Musk by Kiehl's, which may smell crude to some, but to my nose is sexy and masculine. Intense Iris & White Musk is a touch soapier than Original Musk, but equally as unisex. I am also highly impressed by this fragrance's longevity, which holds much longer on the skin than the average cologne. Intense is very apt in describing both this fragrance's sillage and lasting strength. I really like this fragrance, so much so that I have purchased a sample to test it even further, especially in the colder months. This is an exquisite fragrance that I think at least everyone should try, especially if musk is your thing.

Creamy soft milky iris along with orris root powder is delicately balanced on clean not so powdery dry white musk with a dry down that is slightly of buttery soft suede, a little linen paper/cotton note and a little dash of naughty warm musk (not Egyptian, like Narcisco Rodriguez, more like a drop of Kiehl's Original musk added to the mix like a single tiger roar- well more like a half-hearted house cat meow. This fragrance reminds me somewhat of Jivago 24K softened by an ultra fluffy version of Donna Karan's Cashmere Mist. This is cozy, feminine and warm- but not particular ground breaking. There are days when this is just perfect- like a Cashmere Shawl and an elegant intimate dinner of Fire-roasted Veggies with Buffalo Mozarella paired with a crusty bread and bottle of velvety round Malbec. (Sorry, I digressed).Iris & White Musk is quite wearable, and might easily qualify as a comfortable daytime Winter/Spring signature scent- effortless it gives me a sense of vulnerability and pampered elegance. Will it leave an impression on anyone else- yes, that will likely be "nice and un-offensive". I loved it for the first hour, was intrigued by it for the second hour, and then promptly felt neutral about it as a "FB/Must Have" by the third hour. I believe it is extremely well made and carries a bit more sillage and longevity than most single Jo Malone Colognes as part of the Jo Malone Intense Cologne line...but I've got moves to make, olfactory synapses to exercise and more interesting scents to get to now. Nighty-night.

Kleos Musk Series Part 23 Last year, I crowned Musc Bleu osmo (the oil) as my number one musk fragrance. And now there’s a tussle for the throne: Iris & White Musk is making its bid to become the musk king as well. Initially, I wasn't so enthusiastic after the first sniffs. I had sniffed this fragrance, but at first, it seemed a bit too masculine to me. My partner shared this opinion, yet was very taken with the scent, both on himself and on me. However, after frequent testing and even more frequent wearing, I now have a completely different impression. Essentially, I smell what it says on the label: iris and white musk. But especially at the beginning, there’s also something spicy that initially struck me as masculine. However, that dissipates, and I now perceive it differently. Then iris and white musk come into play, and it smells powdery and - in contrast to Musc Bleu - very warm! That’s the only small criticism of Musc Bleu - it’s a bit cool, so I tend to wear it on warm days. Iris & White Musk is “snuggly,” but without any sweetness, and I’ve already received compliments when wearing it. For me, Iris & White Musk is wearable all year round, equally for men and women. It’s not labeled unisex for nothing. It’s an EDC intense and lasts very well. The sillage is quite strong at first, but it noticeably weakens over time. Nevertheless, Iris & White Musk remains pleasantly detectable for several hours. In short: This could become my new number one and actually push Musc Bleu aside! But since there’s always a catch, there is one here too: Iris & White Musk has been discontinued. Unfortunately. So I will wear my new number one with delight and enjoy it until the last drop. My 100 ml bottle is still almost full, so it should last a while. And now, quiet down, boys. You can both take turns sitting on the throne. Always nicely alternating!

Iris & White Musk did not work on my skin; the test strip was enough for me. Therefore, just a brief note. "Pur" has iris root or solutions and emulsions with this fragrance ingredient, which, alongside the desired properties, has a characteristic smell of raw carrots. This is undesirable, and perfumers strive to cover or alter this without losing the desired properties of the iris root. This either did not succeed here or was not attempted at all. No thanks, this is not recommended!

... my new fragrance for every day. After my previous favorite scent, Pioggia Salata, was no longer available at my trusted perfumery, I have been searching for a worthy successor for quite some time, one that would become my constant companion from now on. It should be powdery, somehow delicate, smell like freshly washed laundry, and envelop me like a gentle breeze. Not too heavy to wear in summer and not too fleeting to be perceived in winter. During a visit to Berlin, I stumbled upon the fragrances of Jo Malone by chance. After testing several that I didn't like at all, finally, Iris & White Musk came up - with a healthy dose of skepticism on my part. But even with the first sniff on the fragrance strip, I thought to myself, this could be the right one. I confess that I generally really like iris. However, the composition of most fragrances tends to be either a bit too harsh or sometimes too sweet for my olfactory perception. But with the combination of musk and violet root, Iris & White Musk develops this fine, feathery light note on my skin that I love so much and would like to wrap myself in all day long. And here comes the small catch: Unfortunately, the scent doesn't cling very well and fades quite quickly. The large bottle (100 ml is the only size) is not suitable for daily carrying in my handbag, which made the acquisition of a new travel atomizer necessary. Since several people have already told me in the meantime, "You smell so good. What fragrance is that?", I think I have made the right choice for my daily fragrance well-being experience with Iris & White Musk.

I much prefer this fragrance over the original. I found Ange Ou Demon to be a little strong even for wear in the cooler months. This fragrance however, captures the essence of its predecessor and in my opinion, is much more pleasant. It's powdery, soft and delicate with subtle hints of spices and woods. Mysterious and sensual, this fragrance guarantees to intrigue and draw in the opposite sex's interest with ease. While the original was more grounded and dark, I find Ange Ou Demon Tendre to be heavenly, almost ethereal. For something unique, feminine and soft from the house of Givenchy, you can't pass up this wonderful scent.

The waves crash against the beach I ran through the water with my feet. Enjoying the sun together here no one can ruin our day. Relaxing in the sun on a lounge chair sand on my feet, what a delight. A cocktail quickly ordered now "On vacation" - how beautiful is the world. With a book I find my peace sometimes I even close my eyes. A boat glides swiftly over the sea the palms sway in the wind. In the restaurant, there are many delicacies God may forgive a pound too much. A sunset by the sea is beautiful who knows when I'll come back here. (yellowrose) . Ah, what a lovely scent. It conveys spring and especially summer feelings. Ange ou Démon (EdT) smells like pure summer and sunshine. Sprayed on, it immediately brings back memories of swimming pools, beaches, warmth, the sea, sunscreen, flowers, meadows... aaah, etc. For a long time, I didn't like it at all. I found it overly heavy. But no!!! It is wonderful, creamy, powdery, and soft. Orange blossom and heliotrope convey that "vacation/summer feeling," while lily of the valley and mandarin add a nice touch of "lightness," and patchouli - phew, thankfully there's very little of that - reminds me of meadows (not the scent of a green meadow, but rather like a rubbed meadow) where you roll out your beach mat or blanket and lie down. Sliding back and forth to finally find the right position *g* Rosewood and peony only come in briefly at the beginning. Unfortunately, they disappear very quickly. Get it, girls, it quickly brings the sun into your heart!

Simply beautiful. And pleasant. It reminds me of ... - cool spring and summer mornings - fresh air - sun rays - dew drops on the blades of grass - butterflies - flowers swaying in the wind - fog over the fields - clear water This fragrance is not only perfect for everyday wear, but for pretty much any situation. Work, leisure, day, night. It is simply very unobtrusive, stays in the background, and is very simply delicious and light, floral, very delicate and sweetish. And the great thing: all without coming across as boring. With this fragrance, you can't go wrong, but you also don't have to worry about carrying around something generic. Beautiful!

This delicate version of Ange ou Démon caught my eye at first glance. The scent is soft and unobtrusive, yet not boring, as it has a very warm and sensual accord and lasts quite well for an EDT. I would wear this fragrance more during the day and the EDP in the evening.

I have not tried either the EdP or the original formulation, so I cannot say how they compare. But on its own, Boucheron is a very friendly little thing. It doesn't particularly wow me the way other 80s floral-ambers I've tried do, but it does have one major secret weapon up its sleeve: it has a really, really good opening. There's such a good, juicy orange going on at the start of this. Downright edible. I meant it when I said orange creamsicle in the title, that's very much what it smells like. It's a little heartbreaking when it disappears, because what's left behind is a pretty standard amber, faintly floral in a powdery kind of way, like you're still wearing the remnants of a super-strong fragrance from last night. It's pleasant, because ambers are pleasant, but not really anything to write home about. But for about thirty minutes at the start, you're wearing liquid sunshine.

I already have the EDP (wrote a review on that also) and had read that the EDT was quite different. Loving the EDP, but sometimes longing for that one to be a bit more delicate and appropiate for more occasions, I decided to try the EDT as well. It is different, not so much in 'scent profile' but it is softer, more smooth and 'airy'. I think I prefer this EDT over the EDP. The EDP is more oriëntal and amber forward I think. The EDT is a bit more flowery with still a wink to the Oriënt, but at a larger distance. Less outspoken and therefore a little more inviting to sniff ones own skin and with even more happening in the development. Opening is quite citrussy and orange-y and after that wink to the Oriënt, the drydown is soft and tender. As with the EDP, the low price is unbelievable for such quality. As with many fragrances, I feel as though the EDT projects better than the EDP and that, on the other hand, the longevity of the EDP is better than that of the EDT.

The new year is already more than two weeks old, and many of the New Year's resolutions made are likely already a thing of the past. Human will is often weak, and the mind is inventive when it comes to satisfying its reward center. In line with the spirit of the times and long before the chancellor, I have already introduced a fragrance price cap for myself. If I desire a very expensive perfume, I buy a very cheap one alongside it, which results in an average price for both that is bearably below my fragrance price cap. I know that I am somehow deceiving myself with this, but it still gives me a good feeling and double the happiness hormones for my reward center. At Boucheron, a venerable company with a history of more than 150 years, we also find wonderful, high-quality fragrances in practice that would hardly exceed any real fragrance price cap. These quite affordable perfumes are available as EdT and EdP, often in a double pack, so to speak, and are true fragrance price brakes. Notable examples include: Boucheron EdT/EdP from 1988, Boucheron pour Homme EdT/EdP from 1989, Jaïpur Homme EdT/EdP from 1998, and Boucheron EdT/EdP from 2011. All variants are still available except for the 1988 edition. In each of the mentioned examples, the EdT and EdP are quite close together, particularly true for the women's perfume Boucheron from 2011. Since I prefer the slightly more sparkling EdT of this fantastic double whammy just a bit better at the beginning, this review is based on it. The 2011 edition is a very successful continuation or new development of the 1988 version. All fragrance notes of the 2011 pyramid are exactly where they were in 1988, and no new notes have been added. However, some notes from the old composition are missing. I do not know the 1988 perfume, but the scent of the 2011 version is fabulous and intense, a strongly fragrant bouquet of lush white flowers, subtly underlaid with spiciness and impressive feminine power and elegance. It starts with a sweet-floral opulence that can be enchanting. The full splendor of the intense aroma of orange blossom is flanked by a mild but noticeable sparkling freshness whose fruitiness is very pleasant but not long-lasting. In return, the flowers gain strength, and with additional jasmine, ylang-ylang, and tuberose, the floral component is broad and versatile. The complex sweetness develops in parallel with an agile, honey-like, and sensual temptation. Charged with this massive, wide-ranging floral power and propelled by the sweet, aromatic propulsion, the bazooka is now finally fired and cascades down as a dense cloud of sweet-spicy floral opulence onto the wearer, enveloping her robustly for many hours. The floral fragrance bouquet is never light-footed and becomes denser and heavier over time. The floral aroma largely remains strong, while the amber notes weave in a cozy warmth, and the scent takes on enveloping, seductive traits. The initially inconspicuous vanilla with its sweet-spicy, harmonious notes gives the perfume a touch of classic elegance in the end. Just as the EdT comes across as slightly more sparkling at the beginning, it remains somewhat more unruly at the end than the EdP, which adds an extra thrill to the comfort. By the way, fragrance price brakes with double whammy are not limited to Boucheron. Calvin Klein offers a double whammy of the extra class with Obsession EdP for women and Obsession for Men EdT! For firing the bazooka, precise aiming is quite important. Thank you very much for your company!

Unfortunately, too many uninformed customers buy these CK One Summer Editions instead of investing their money in a really good summer fragrance... At first, it is typically fresh like CK One, with a bit more fruit than usual and suitable for all genders...later it becomes a bit more masculine and heavier, musk & incense, too heavy for a summer fragrance, but with above-average longevity... Nice colorful bottle and noticeable sillage for about 3 hours, then it becomes very close to the skin... I would never let something like this enter my collection, but I can hardly criticize it for being mainstream...average!
The first Ck Summer that I like, citrusy but still with a soft, somehow woody note; whether it would be enough for a purchase, I don't know yet.

This summer starts off quite fruity with CK. The opening is citrusy with lemons and lots of mandarins, cool and refreshing, so we are in for another hot summer. CK knows that, yes indeed! What have we mixed in this year? Aha, definitely included are melons (whole fruits). I think there are watermelon and honeydew melon in there. Oh no - vervain? I don't like that. Well, anyway, it contributes to further cooling. For sure, Calvin has eaten all the peaches by himself and the bouquet of freesias is just sitting on his table. The base is a bit weak and frankincense...? - I don't know, it doesn't belong in a summer perfume, does it? No, I really don't like the dry down. We've had better summers. EDIT: Friend, you're asking about the longevity: no idea, I just got it earlier. So it does last, but not as much as it promises. As fresh as it announces its arrival, unfortunately it doesn't stay that way, it just becomes boring... Tears of disappointment pushed away.

When I wear "Silk Blossom | Jo Malone," I mentally jump into a fabric softener commercial. I imagine myself bouncing in a white summer dress over a flower meadow. Everything is peaceful, the birds are chirping, the butterflies are dancing with the bees over the blossoms, life is beautiful. The scent is a true clean laundry fragrance. Incredibly wonderful. Fresh, pure, delicate, and silky soft. Just like a fabric softener. But that’s not a negative! No, it’s enchanting. A little feel-good dream that I always wear when I long for purity and confidence. The pepper is hardly noticeable. But the silk tree blossom. And how ❥ I like it very much. It’s a shame that it’s no longer available for purchase.

i love this smell but, as all of this brand, unfortunetly it's too poor sillage for the retail price offered. It's similar to an EDT performance, with double of price :( I can't explain why they don't want to increase they're quality and performances, this will could justify the high prices. Hoping in the future they'll can solve this issue for all fragrances proposed.

Enflammé is one of the very best fragrances in the Givenchy La Collection Particulière. It is very beautiful, mature and elegant. Naturally, it does not project a lot, nor will it announce your arrival at a party. Visualize something your expensive lawyer would wear, and you will get Enflammé. Enflammé was created by Amandine Clerc-Marie, an inhouse perfumer for DSM Firmenich. The high-quality ingredients in La Collection Particulière typically come from DSM Firmenich. This review was based initially on a mini flacon of Enflammé, but I have updated it after buying a full bottle. Givenchy lists labdanum, coffee, tobacco, patchouli, vanilla and tolu balm as the main ingredients. The opening is an outstanding blend of coffee and labdanum, followed by the heart notes of tobacco and patchouli, and finally into vanilla and tolu balsam resin. But Enflammé is far more than the sum of these notes, because of the synergy created by Amandine Clerc-Marie. The different notes are exquisitely blended, and you will not find any note to be dominant. The olfactory progression is not clearly demarcated as you can smell most notes at all stages, though with varying intensities. So, it is not a coffee scent, a tobacco scent or an amber scent. Therein lies its beauty. You will not perceive the sting of tobacco or the earthy woody note of patchouli in Enflammé, though they are all there somewhere in the background. The dry down is similar, but the vanilla and resins float up a little bit. In the notes for Grand Soir, Francis Kurkdjian writes that the amber accord is primarily a combination of labdanum and vanilla. Though I agree with his statement, amber is better stated as blend of one or more of the resins (labdanum, benzoin, frankincense) and one or more of the vanilla-like accords (vanilla, tonka bean, coumarin). In Enflammé, the vanilla and labdanum appear in different parts of the olfactory pyramid, but they blend and produce an amber accord. I consider Enflammé to be a glorious amber fragrance with minor tobacco and coffee accords. The longevity of Enflammé is phenomenal on my skin and clothes. It is going strong even after ten hours. The sillage and projection are in line with the elegant mature personality of this perfume. This is a perfume for the board room, not the bar room. This is an unconditional recommendation from me, if you can afford it. But that is a big if. Currently a 100 ml bottle costs $345 on Givenchy’s website, and it is rarely seen on discounter websites. But you can get three 10 ml splash bottle of La Collection Particulière for $99. Givenchy will credit you this money when you buy a full bottle, making this a good bargain.

To me, this fragrance is so damn underrated. Its simplicity doesn't matter; to me, it's still so unique and intense. Such a beautiful fragrance! The bottle of the 200 ML flask is quite frustrating, though, due to its clumsiness. But in terms of scent, longevity, and sillage, it's just so damn good. Overall, despite the awkward packaging, this fragrance truly stands out for its exceptional qualities.

I don’t know how this fragrance isn’t popular , its literally the best thing I've ever smelled Am not exaggerating but this is just gorgeous its one of the few high end fragrances that deserves the price The notes looks simple but its about the blend and how high quality the oils used in this most of them are absolutes Note that not every note is listed on fragrantica idk why ,it has an amber accord and labdanum which is absolutely gorgeous along side that vanilla and subtle tobacco while the coffee note is just chilling in the background of all of this giving it a slight feeling of gourmandiness ( it is not a gourmand fragrance by anymeans but just a touch) , just wow and for some reason it gives a cinnamon-ish vibe ( it is not a note but more like its a same vibe accord-ish typpa thing idk how to explain it ) And the best thing in this fragrance is the performance man this is just crazy istg i sprayed it on a coat and i can still smell it after 100+ hours am not even exaggerating The best part is that its not an offensive smell rather its a really relaxing sweet but refined smell The performance is really crazy to the point where i used it one day , slept , woke up then at night the next day i used another perfume and after that perfume faded i could still smell enflamme clearly not low key This is worth every cent u pay for , yes its expensive but it is the closest u can get to being worth it

When I go to perfume shops, I sometimes prefer to be alone, without anyone presenting the perfumes to me. I also like it when I don't feel pressured to buy. During my last visit to BHV, I changed my tactic. I asked the consultant to show me the collection. And thanks to her, I was able to discover this gem. I was thrilled!!!! My wallet will suffer because I want it!!!! This is a scent that I love, with an excellent balance and a perfect blend of everything to give you an extremely chic and seductive fragrance. It is a mood-setting scent. I can easily imagine a romantic date. The only lighting should be a candle ️ and the fireplace. Terribly beautiful, both on a man and a woman. It has a sillage, but not in a harsh way. Not too sweet, and thank you for that. The vanilla is not too rich, so it is in osmose with the tobacco. The tobacco adds a slightly muted character without dominating or pushing itself to the forefront. The coffee is there, but it is not the coffee you smell in some perfumes. It is there to complete the picture. I have the impression that it is a beautiful contemporary dance. And every dancer dances, but they leave space for the others without putting themselves in the spotlight. I do not compare it to other tobacco + vanilla perfumes, because it has nothing to do with that. If you are looking for prominent tobacco and all those vanilla trends, this scent is not for you.. If you are looking for the scent behind the fashion, this is also not the right one for you. It is not the discovery of a new world. It is a fragrance that evokes emotions and stimulates the imagination, that is for sure. Perhaps it is something for those who don't need tricks to feel good. Those who like it appreciate it quietly, without making noise. I, for one, am overwhelmed.

You have "ignited" my love!!! Full blast of patch at the beginning and I totally love it. Gradually, the coffee comes in. More like a cup of milk coffee with vanilla topping. But patch and coffee blend together so brilliantly. A dream!!! You really have to be into patch in fragrances to learn to love this one.

I got this cologne as a gift, and it mixes well with my chemistry. Its sillage is subtle, and the longevity is about four hours. However, it does stick to clothes. The smell is refreshing. I would categorize it as an "after-shower" smell. It smells like a tea garden on a cool, humid day. The sweetness is herbal, rather than sugary. I wore this on a rainy day once, and the osmanthus paired really well with the ozone, so it's become my late winter/spring scent for rainy days.

This is my Summer Freshy No. 1. My absolute favorite from Jo Malone. Fresh, citrusy, sweet, and floral all at once. The first thing I smell is this mega delicious orange-osmanthus blossom, which simply smells incredibly juicy and tempting. I would love to have a few more spritzes of this fragrance! I can't imagine that one could easily over-spray it. Unfortunately, it turns slightly bitter on me after a short time, which is probably due to the woods included. After about 2 hours, the sweetness of the orange blossom has exited through the back door and has thus said goodbye...unfortunately. Now the woods come forward from the background and create a wonderful symphony with the osmanthus blossom. A symphony that incorporates freshness and purity with a hint of coolness. Now it could even be unisex, in my opinion. As the spectacle now unfortunately only takes place close to the skin after about 3 hours, I feel like having an encore. Applause to Jo Malone. I really like the scent and feel very comfortable with it in the summer - nothing bothers me about it. A fragrance without edges and corners...and I can't get enough of it and can't imagine ever getting "full" of it.

it always depends on the skin chemistry with fragrances!!! On me, the scent develops really well and definitely has "that certain something". My skin likes fruity scents with a lot of lemon, that might be the reason. I own a lot of fragrances from Jo Malone, and each one is unique in its own way. Depending on my mood, I wear them individually or mixed, but they are always special. They remain "close to the skin" and do not overwhelm the surroundings. Once the nose has gotten used to these scents, "normal" fragrances (at least for me) smell too artificial and too strong. At first, I definitely smell the freshness of the lemon (which I really like) .. then osmanthus comes into play, and it smells absolutely sensual (it has a certain erotic touch!!!!) but a certain freshness is still there. I definitely like this fragrance and can only recommend it. But as I said, fragrances should be tested on the skin... What I have also noticed... fragrances smell different on my wrist than on my neck. The scent develops best when sprayed on freshly showered skin. Once the pH level of the skin changes (which is inevitable throughout the day), the scent smells different.

I am a confessed Jo Malone fan... my collection consists of almost 50% Jo Malone and I always look forward to new scents from this brand, as you are usually not disappointed. I ordered the 30 ml on a whim and it arrived this morning. Full of anticipation, I sprayed a spritz on my wrist and sniffed. The scent starts off very citrusy, but not elegantly citrusy, rather biting and cheap (the famous toilet duck sends its regards at this point). After a short while, something sweet becomes noticeable, but the piercing citrus scent is still overwhelmingly present and almost soapy. After about 20-30 minutes, the biting lemon slowly fades away and something floral emerges. From then on, the scent is actually quite nice: powdery soft, somewhat sweet, faintly smelling of peach and a bit floral. The scent is "nice," but unfortunately not special at all and actually too expensive for that. Generally, this could also be a drugstore fragrance. After this initial testing phase, I sprayed myself generously with Osmanthus Blossom (5-6 sprays on neck and wrist for the extreme test) and I must unfortunately say regarding longevity that it is incredibly weak. Generally, Jo Malone fragrances are rather delicate in nature and have mediocre longevity, so I don't have high expectations, but this scent was already gone after an hour (!) which is unusual even for a Jo Malone fragrance. To make it short: I am disappointed. I don't know if I am willing to endure 20 minutes of a biting citrus bomb with drugstore scent character until the rather average nice scent appears, which then also disappears shortly after. Update from 09.05.2013: It has been bothering me, and I tested Osmanthus Blossom again on my clothing. And indeed, it smells completely different than on my skin. The lemon here is gentle and sweet, and it lasts for several hours. I would have never thought that skin chemistry plays SUCH a big role! I will keep it after all, as I quite like it now, but I will definitely NOT spray it on my skin again.

It starts off very fresh, with many green notes: cucumber with some herbs and spices and a very unusual citrus note that I haven't smelled before. I guess it's the mandarin leaf, as it has a green-citrusy scent reminiscent of plants/gardens, almost a bit like rain. The melon is unfortunately not sweet and red juicy, but rather green/unripe, and probably contributes to the freshness that I perceive as cucumber. Rhubarb is present and supports the spicy cucumber salad character. After 10 minutes, lemon verbena slowly emerges. I can't say that the scent is bad; it's just not my thing at all. I don't even like it as a room spray. Someone left the bottle in our hallway, and I think I will return it there shortly.

On days when you know you're still going to the gym and the tanning bed, you naturally pick out light test fragrances that are perhaps also easy to see through, don't last long, in short: just not that important. No complex Amouages or anything like that. Just such a candidate was the 2006 Summer Edition of CK One today. A few months ago, at the beginning of summer, I was really excited about these limited summer editions; somehow the Tequila 2014 version sparked my interest. Luckily, I only ended up getting the minty 2013 version, as they all resemble each other too much to own more. Still, today it was the version from our World Cup summer that was up, fitting with the current -euphoria in the country. The 2006 version is at least 95% identical to the 2011 version, which I had already labeled as boring, so there's already quite a bit written about it, even if I was probably a bit too harsh on that day. And of course, I was still far from as experienced as I am today when it comes to perfume. But then the rating should actually be worse than back then, yet it isn't. My CK One Summer fever is probably still not completely gone ;). But I can live with that, especially when I remind myself of the €30 per summer that you have to shell out every year. But here’s a brief description of what the 06 smells like: minty, powdery, synthetic-scratchy melons, with a bit of lemongrass, salty hints, and pleasant, CK One typical musk in the base. Bottle: one of the more boring CK One Summers. Sillage: only for the peak summer. Longevity: 4-5 hours of pure refreshment. A short refreshment, but clearly weaker for me than the 2 newest ones. Also annoying that some years resemble each other so extremely or are simply recycled due to a lack of ideas or courage. It can't be that hard; there are still so many summery themes that could be incorporated... if you need ideas CK, come to me ;)

- so I will just: This one is fruity, fresh, resting on a bitter base. The blend is, as with almost all summer CK fragrances, excellent. Well, if they had left out the 1 mandarin leaf, we would be much poorer. Joking aside: Since 2010, CK has really stepped back with their summer scents, even enormously (what 1 mandarin leaf can do...) I am a confessed CK fan and from 2005 to 2009, the summer fragrances were simply top-notch!

I genuinely love Désobéissant. It’s one of those fragrances that feels easy to wear, yet always makes me feel polished and confident. From the first spray, the cedrat comes through fresh and clean, but not sharp. It smells bright, smooth, and quietly luxurious. As it settles, the cardamom and black tea really stand out for me. This part feels warm, calm, and slightly spicy—very comforting, but still interesting. It has a classy, thoughtful vibe that never feels too much. The dry-down is where I’m completely sold. The pine and cedarwood are soft, woody, and elegant. On my skin, the longevity is better than average, and the sillage is just right—people notice it, but it never feels overpowering. What I love most is how natural it feels. It doesn’t try to impress; it just works. Désobéissant has become one of those fragrances I truly enjoy wearing again and again. Clean, refined, and incredibly satisfying. Overall, I highly recommend it 10/10

It’s a fragrance that immediately brings an outfit to mind. I can’t help it. A man or woman of slender stature, fine facial features, naturally styled hair, a fresh complexion, elegant clothing. Perfectly fitting trousers, a fitted shirt or blouse, a minimalist watch, and sunglasses. Everything you need to tackle any demands of the day. Without excessive effort or fuss. For some, it’s a meeting; for others, client appointments await. A young dynamic mom taking the kids to the movies, a father picking up his son from afternoon sports. A thousand different everyday situations. The wearer of Desobeissante exudes prosperity and stability, and above all, the sense of having life under control. But also style, taste, and elegance! Desobeissante, which interestingly means "indecent" but smells exactly the opposite, opens for me with almost all the listed notes. Sour fruity citron, the big one I often smelled in the Mediterranean region, mixed with the milky spice of cardamom (which for some reason smells like fig to me). The fresh black tea notes are also almost immediately present, and just a little later (10-15 minutes) the woods come in. Each note can be easily discerned here, and the mix is MAGIC! Sillage and longevity are in the medium range, so completely satisfactory, but the crucial aspect is of course the aroma itself. It is very, very beautiful. For me, an exceptionally well-made fragrance. I think after this decant, I will get the large bottle. This feeling when wearing it is simply wonderful! Thank you for reading. Alisa23
