The individual fragrance components are much more complexly intertwined here than in the reduced and simplified version from 2007 and can hardly be fully dissected except for a few distinctive notes. An unusually complex scent for its time of origin, which skillfully oscillates almost from the beginning between green-herbaceous marigold, slightly tart green mandarin, creamy orange blossom, and a fine woody base. The fragrance itself is more opulent, rounder, and overall more harmonious in its development than the younger version. All fragrance components flow harmoniously into one another; there are indeed breakpoints, i.e., changes in direction, but I do not consciously perceive them. Extravagance d`Amarige is a refined, elegant, and extravagant (in the sense of extraordinary) nose pleaser. Its younger relative, Les Parfums Mythiques Extravagance d`Amarige, is a charming and uncomplicated everyday companion. P.S: Since the version Les Parfums Mythiques Extravagance d`Amarige from 2007 was listed on Parfumo until recently, my originally placed comment here referred to that - as did the responses to it.

It was again one of my many blind buys that initially prompted the reaction "that's it, this is thoroughly off the mark." Well, today is a gardening day. I don’t need a great scent for that. So, Extravagance D'Amarige is being used. It does the job just fine. When I first sprayed it, I felt confirmed in my opinion that the scent was a misstep, primarily blaming the somewhat bitter-smelling marigold for that. Now the scent has been with me for three hours, and to my surprise, it is becoming increasingly likable. Because what follows in the heart and especially in the base notes is by no means the troublemaker of the beginning. The bitterness is gone, and the floral aspect of the scent becomes softer and gentler. Amber definitely warms the fragrance. It may not become my favorite scent, but it will surely be pulled out from the last corner more often. Conclusion: Give every fragrance a chance, it often pays off.

I just treated myself to it...in Spain, more precisely in Andalusia, where it’s still 30 degrees at the beginning of October and the sun smiles from a rich blue sky for days on end! What could be better? And this scent is pure summer-sun-good mood with a freshness kick that radiates dry warmth and leaves nothing to be desired. I really don’t want to go back to this horrid gray, cold, and especially light-poor Germany, and the autumn and winter time that is coming is anyway the worst for me....but this wonderfully light scent will make it a bit easier for me to wait for summer 2018 ;-) at the beginning, I perceive a nice mix of bergamot and anise, although you can only catch a brief whiff of anise. The desert rose doesn’t reveal itself to me, what a pity, I would love to know what such a wonderful specimen of bloom smells like ;-) over time, it actually becomes a bit aquatic, but never too transparent, rather refreshingly bright and cheerful, like a breeze at 40 degrees in the shade and a brilliant 35% humidity...the climate that I love so infinitely! I really like frankincense, but here it shows me the cold shoulder and rather shines through its absence, instead, sandalwood paired with a hint of delicious musk tickles my summer nose... Unfortunately, the sillage is rather close to the body and the longevity could be improved. I just keep reapplying, close my eyes, and am once again under the wonderfully hot southern sun, which simply means life and enjoyment!

Jo Malone's fragrances can all be layered together. But with White Jasmine & Mint, I don't dare to do that. I already find the interplay of the scent notes of this fragrance incompatible, so I can't imagine it won't be dreadful when layered. The top note smells like illness. Mint, chamomile, it reminds me of days with stomach aches and the like. The scent is absolutely piercing, and I would have preferred to wash it off immediately. Unfortunately, the mint from the top note also runs through the entire fragrance pyramid. The scent does become milder, but for me, the other scent notes are overshadowed by a huge pile of mint leaves. The little lily of the valley peeking out from under the mint is completely crushed. The other notes from the heart and base sound great, but I mostly smell mint. A sickly mint that, due to some note, doesn't smell fresh anymore but almost a bit rotten.

I’ve had it for about a year now but only wore it a few times because I found it too light and fleeting, lasting only an hour with low silage. I was also a little disappointed I didn’t smell Neroli, which was the reason I wanted it. I also don’t smell grapefruit, which is a blessing. Overall, it smells more like a citrus cologne with some floral, woody, and green notes, like the type used for freshening up. As a scent to use at the gym or some other active pastime, it’s great. Initial spray is very cooling and refreshing; and I continued to feel cool and refreshed for the hour or so it performed. The musky dry down gave a powder feel that contributed to the cool and dry feeling. As a scent to use as a perfume, not so great, though it did last longer in early spring, fall, winter, and cooler days of summer. It all but disappeared within an hour on a hot day. In fairness, not many scents perform well in hot weather either. This is a scent to use more liberally than you normally would, which I suspect is why it is also available in a reasonably priced 6.7oz. The inexpensive price could be due to the fact that it is really just a cologne despite the claimed designated strength of edt. Overall, I found it to be a pretty, refreshing scent that satisfies as long as you are not expecting more than it can deliver.

I couldn't really warm up to the two previous dahlias: I found the EdP to be a warmer amber scent with too much sweetness for my taste, while I remember the EdT as floral - fruity - unremarkable. But this one, I like a lot. This is supposed to be a lighter summer version, as the name L’Eau suggests, but don’t let that fool you. Because: this scent is not an EdC, but an EdT, and even for that, it holds up really well. Are they trying to justify the price with that? In my opinion, L’Eau is a modern chypre. Right after spraying, I smell wonderful citrus notes + neroli, which initially reminds me of a summery EdC. Then it becomes more floral, with the rose not playing a dominant role. And after that, a woody, powdery base sets in, where the lightness of the top notes still resonates. It seems to me that the whole thing has been spiced up with a few synthetic fragrance notes (Ambroxan & Co), which I personally like. Igli is right, the scent is feminine, but not only. Above all: it is not sweet at all. And it fits all seasons.

…at least for me. Why I, since I turned 40, now prefer light, green, refreshing scents above all else. The best years are now behind me, I've passed my peak. One struggles with slack contours, dry skin, and fine lines. The old, withered, gnarled self is crying out for the spring of life, which is years behind. And for me personally, all green, refreshing, floral scents represent spring, and I can’t get enough of perfumes like Dahlia Noir L’eau, which comes across so wonderfully fresh and green. In my younger years, I wanted to emphasize my femininity and allure. The opposite sex should be lured in with rich, sweet fragrances. At 16, I was bathing in Venezia, which now only brings me headaches and nausea. I’m curious to see what I’ll like in 20 years. Scents that smell like a crypt? Paloma Picasso, Montana Eau de Peau, Magie noire….??? Oh yes, Dahlia Noir L’eau is really great, not for teens, crisp green with recognizability… it didn’t remind me much of Chloe L’eau, I found that too grassy green…

Out of connection to the EDP, I also tested L'eau, and I was surprised that I couldn't find any similarity between the two scents. L'eau is an independent fragrance, which doesn't bother me. At the start, it greets me with a pleasantly green note, reminding me of a lush meadow that one walks barefoot on. The fresh citrus notes and the cool neroli are very invigorating. I think of a refreshing EDC that is enjoyable to wear in the summer. The rose comes in on velvet paws and gives the fragrance softness and gentleness. The cedar is slightly woody - smoky, but with a lightness that suits L'eau well. I spent a considerable amount of time with the fragrance, and the longevity is surprisingly good for this lightly composed perfume. So it's not an EDC after all. Still, I was undecided whether I should wander back to the perfumery to purchase it. During my next visit to the perfumery, it will be tested again.

Dahlia Noir LÈau in no way resembles its predecessor "Dahlien"; it is completely different, like a "warm summer rain". It is very light; I perceive it as very powdery and playful, yet not intrusive but very fresh. A wild meadow with various flowers and plants growing together as nature intends, the sun shines in the sky, a gentle breeze sweeps over the meadow and over the skin, dandelions dance through the air and tickle the tip of the nose, grasses and ears brush against bare legs, and the sunbeams warm the skin, a few woolly warm drops of rain moisten skin and hair. You lie in the grass and enjoy this unique summer day.... That is Dahlia Noir LÈau for me.

The scent has no connection to the previous "Dahlias." It smells somehow indefinably "fresh," but without a watery note. A hint of something anise-like occasionally appears (in the direction of CANTHOXAL) but only briefly and vaguely.

citrus? neroli? rose? no, I immediately smell the base note and it instantly reminds me of Gucci Envy or Peace, Love Juicy Couture... just not as extremely green. longevity is quite good, and in summer definitely sufficient. refreshing and feminine, only the price... outrageous! I really like the bottles of all three Dahlia Noirs!

While I always think of a delicate, creamy, warm, cuddly, and possibly sweet base with baby scents, this very green blend strongly resembles toilet cleaner. Verbena, mint, and rhubarb are very prominent, with no trace of the vanilla milk. As for longevity, thankfully the toilet smell is gone after an hour :p

Is this fragrance the trigger for my aversion to sporty scents? Currently, manufacturers are flooding the market with high citrus content fragrances, and every time I smell one, I shudder again. Last week it happened. While tidying up, I came across a nearly full bottle of this "creation". Not much needs to be said about CK One. Everyone knows it, and hardly anyone understands how such a success story can last so long. Every year, at least one (summer) variation of this scent is released, which are rarely successful. This fragrance probably came about in the same way. So I tried it again on a spring day last week, or rather, I subjected myself to it. Lemon and mandarin, the full citrus blast, which shows no signs of naturalness for me. Every toilet fragrance would be envious of such energy from artificial aromas. Fortunately, it drops off a bit in the heart note, so it doesn't push itself too much into the foreground, and the base becomes, then similarly defensive, like its big brother. I don't know what possessed me to buy this fragrance two years ago. But it must have been a terrible phase in my life ;) What should I do to get through the bottle?

Gold-green shimmering tea leaf, a hint of soap and citrus. A floating scent aura, yet quite present, with body. Jade as a stone generally stands for satisfaction, self-confidence, and balance. It has a shimmering, sometimes milky warm green. All of this fits the fragrance, which is more than just a refresher with a tea note. AugustA perceives it as translucent, yet physical. The scent initially spreads a pleasant sound and, with the use of resins and incense, is also good for sparking interest as a daily interruption and bringing a touch of elegance. It then develops rather herbaceous; I can understand the gentian connotation. That might be the mate accord. In between, there’s a powdery nuance that remains delicately in the background. In the long run, however, Jade Leaf Tea seems a bit too clean to excite me. The longevity of the fragrance is surprising, lasting many hours with a good sillage for a tea scent. All in all: A pleasant fragrance, but not overly captivating. However, it is certainly a recommendation for tea scent lovers to test.

I really love (green) tea scents. I quite like this one as well, but it's not my favorite. Unfortunately, the tea note takes a bit of a backseat in my opinion and is heavily overshadowed and displaced by a clean, soapy aroma. Also, the incense becomes a bit too strong for my nose in the long run. In between, I find the scent quite nice and pleasant, but I guess we won't become 100% friends.

a magical scent. transparent and light the opening is subtly herb-citrusy. then it becomes enveloped in a resinous-woody incense, fine fruitiness and soft aromatic herbal notes float in this vast space. it is balanced, artfully restrained. calming and refreshing. like a delicious cup of tea. so sensitive and delicate that I imagine it more on women... my absolute favorite from the rare tea series.

My Rare-Teas test series from Jo Malone continues. This time it's Jade Leaf Tea's turn, which with its very beautiful, jade-green fragrance liquid almost magically attracts you, making you want to try it immediately. Of course, you hope even more that you will find a great scent and, naturally, that you won't be disappointed. The first two fragrances (Darjeeling and Oolong) were already very good, so let's see how this scent is... The fragrance: The scent initially starts very fresh with a grapefruit, which is naturally citrusy as well. But right after that, you can make out a wonderful tea scent that reveals itself to be mate tea within just a few minutes and accompanies the fragrance throughout its development. Powdery notes also come into play, as the yerba mate tea gives the scent a soft and powdery quality. From this point on, the fragrance doesn't really change much. You can perceive pine resin or conifers a bit later, but this scent quickly fades and is replaced more by incense. Nevertheless, until the end, there remains a beautifully powdery mate tea scent that is not only powdery but also exudes a slight (but quite pleasant) sweetness, while the grapefruit lingers for a while (even if in the background) and doesn't just disappear immediately. Longevity and sillage: Yesss, these two points should be taken with caution here, as I was out on a not-too-warm day and continued wearing a T-shirt after spraying, so it could very well be that the scent is stronger and more long-lasting than I will describe here. So, I would initially state the longevity as four to five hours; according to the saleswoman, the scent lasts quite a while, but that needs to be tested again. The sillage is initially strong, as the grapefruit radiates well; however, it eventually fades, and the mate tea is not particularly strong anyway. But it will still be perceived by someone, especially if you spray it on clothing; otherwise, you can always reapply. The bottle: And once again, the bottle is rather gigantic. A 175 mL bottle, rectangular, tall, and filled with light green (or jade-colored) fragrance liquid. On the front, there is only the logo as a label; no name or anything else is written on it. The cap is oval and black. All in all, perhaps a bit simple, but still quite high-quality and nicely made. Sooo,… Aside from the low sillage, I really liked this scent. Maybe it's because I've somehow rediscovered mate tea for myself and like it more and more. But it is, of course, mainly because the scent is simply well-composed. It may not be a fragrance that evokes some kind of super-wow effect (although one could still exclaim "oooooohhhh what a beautiful scent!"), but it is really nice and suitable for warm days. Because it is initially citrusy and fresh, and later remains light and powdery with bright incense and a slight, woody note. If it were stronger, it could even be used for going out, especially if you're looking for something not overly sweet. It could possibly be compared to Midnight in Paris by V.C. Arpels, although Midnight is certainly a bit sweeter and stronger. However, the tea note here feels better and more authentic. In any case, it is a scent that you should definitely check out. And I… I have only black tea here again… although I see that there are also herbal tea, fennel tea, and cold tea (ugh) lying around… hmm, I think I'll stick to black tea for now!

I had avoided buying any of the Play line from Givenchy because I assumed, wrongly, that they were just going to be generic fruity/floral creations. My assumption came from the look of the bottle, which I felt was aimed at the teen demographic. I shall say now that I was very wrong and that, although I don't really understand the link between the fragrances and the MP3 player style bottle, these are beautiful and complex perfumes. I bought this version as I have a penchant for intense, dark fragrances and this delivers! There is a slight vibe of Very Irresistible L'Intense by Givenchy and I get the similarity between Play Intense and La Perla J'aime La Nuit, both of these are favourites of mine too. I had always shied away from perfumes with pepper expecting them to be too harsh, so I am glad I didn't check the notes for this perfume before I bought it. Play Intense opens with sharp Orange blossom/black pepper medley which quickly settles down getting darker as the patchouli and benzoin deepen. I can't smell much magnolia at all but definitely get the tiare and orchid which stop this being too masculine. The tonka bean rounds the fragrance off beautifully making it smooth and slightly creamy. Overall, I find Play Intense mysterious and gothic, yet elegant and feminine. I highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys the darker side of perfumes!

Amazing Oriental perfume, very long lasting and yet sweet and mysterious. I loved from the first moment, not too heavy and I believe suitable all seasons if you like orientals. The bottle is very unusual and modern mostly like a gadget. I love it.

One has a certain idea of all perfume houses. Of course, when thinking of Givenchy, elegant, floral, powdery, glamorous scents come to mind, like Organza, lively ones like Very Irresistible, and extraordinary ones like Ange au Demant. And for those who are a bit older like me, there’s a fond memory of the herb-elegant scent Givenchy III. null of these are world fragrances like No 5 or Shalimar, but it’s nice that they exist. And now this - the choice of the bottle already shows the first misstep, as it’s the same nonsense as with Davidoff Champion and its dumbbell. Here it’s a mobile phone, which probably won’t appeal to any existing Givenchy users. And the young girls who find this funny ask: Huh? Giwentschi? Who is that?? And they’ll turn away as soon as they see the price tag. As for the scent itself - it lacks personality as well. It’s fruity, sweet, and in the end powdery, and that’s it. I really don’t notice anything more. Whether Givenchy is conquering a new target group with this remains to be seen, but I doubt it.

This fragrance was shown to me yesterday at my local D. store on German soil. The young "lady" - sorry for the expression, seemed a bit overwhelmed by me. I had to first show her Miss Dior Chérie (2011), as she couldn't relate to it at all. She also had no idea about the Floral-Chypre fragrance family. So, I explained my fragrance preferences and their representatives to her, as well as the website of her employer. Then she showed me Play Intense for Her by Givenchy. The bottle does not appeal to me at all: More suited for party girls over 20. On Saturday nights, they head to the pubs and clubs in the clothes of the Swiss pink rabbit and in the party shoes from the Essen shoe giant. The phone is also stylish for their generation! The bottle could be a flat mobile phone that can easily be taken in handbags, and there is definitely a risk of confusion: After a few drinks and hours later, one might use "Play Intense for Her" by Givenchy instead of the phone for calling. The word Intense in the fragrance name is misplaced. It is weak, and the scent is consistently very vanilla and slightly creamy on my skin. A light sweetness can also be detected, but nothing intense, nothing striking, just everything very monotonous and boring! Sleep music from the bottle! And in general, this lady from the generation described above completely missed and misunderstood my wish!

Look, look, look, look here, here I am... come over here. You, you there, look, look at me. Come over here. Hey, hello, peekaboo. Or you there, come over. Look over here. Hello. Can’t you see me? Peekaboo, come on, come over here, look at me. WHY ISN'T ANYONE COMING OVER TO ME? --> Because you look like a purple cell phone and you smell like sh** too!! This could be the worst of all celebrity perfumes (if it were from a celebrity): too sweet, too fruity, too overpowering, too one-dimensional. Every drugstore scent is better.

I am one of those who first saw a mobile phone and not an MP3 player in the bottle ;-) For this reason, my description will also have to use a phone as a "red thread." A peppery floral medley with a restrained orange blossom, while the magnolia is much more present, and a hint of Tiaré sets the tone for this call.

Today I was in the mood for an impulse buy - and what do I always crave? Right - a fragrance! I looked and sniffed here and there, but nowhere did my nose linger with delight. Then my searching eye discovered an appealing purple box - Play Intense for her. No tester available. But I had a feeling that my mother once wore it, and I had liked it on her.

Unfortunately, I cannot understand the negative reviews. This warm fragrance is pure sensuality. Pink pepper and orange blossom initiate the pleasurable journey into this scent experience, followed by Tiaré flower, Amyris wood, and orchid. Sandalwood, patchouli, tonka bean, and benzoin provide an unforgettable experience. I can only recommend this fragrance!
I don't find it that bad at all.. but it's not new.. it reminds me of another fragrance I once had.. unfortunately, I can't remember the name of that fragrance anymore..

a fresh spicy aperitif in the form of a citrus-orange cocktail greets me first. Very delicious! The pink of the bottle matches it now it becomes fruity-floral, with a main tendency towards orange-ginger, later a bit velvety soft interesting scent note, reminiscent of the compositions of CK one summer. The perfume comes across as loud and strong, as is typical for CK, but unfortunately fades too quickly.

The annual collection of fragrances from Jo Malone is always eagerly awaited by me. This "Rare Teas" collection was released a few years ago - just like that in between - as a particularly noble fragrance collection. I first got to test it at the Jo Malone counter in our KaDeWe: while my neighbor once again couldn't decide whether to venture into something new or stick to the tried and true in her very own fragrance world, the always very nice salesperson and I enjoyed discovering these fine scents. Of course, only a hint of exquisite tea compositions remained in my memory; however, my interest was piqued. Now it happened that my ever-praised Parfumista (she knows exactly that she is meant!) had two of these "Rare Teas" samples in her inexhaustible, fortunately always "renewable" "to go" collection. These two naturally ended up with me. One of them is "Rare Teas - Silver Needle Tea": a very fine fragrance painting based on a very exquisite white tea. "Yin Zhen Silver Needle" tea is the most famous and simultaneously the rarest white tea in China. Only particularly beautiful aromatic, still unopened buds of the Pai Hao tea plant are hand-picked and carefully processed. Since Yin "Zhen Silver Needle Tea" hardly becomes bitter, it is not necessary to remove the leaves after brewing. On the contrary: multiple infusions of this tea leaf set are easily possible and even recommended. As a passionate tea drinker for decades - a friend from the mid-seventies sensitized me to the enjoyment of tea - I always welcome any finer tea base in fragrances - see also "Earl Grey & Cucumber," also by Jo Malone and commented on by me. "Rare Tea - Silver Needle Tea" is a very special fragrance blend that I would perhaps also like to have as a brew in one of my beautiful porcelain tea cups. Bergamot naturally first reminds one of the well-known and much-loved "Earl Grey" tea. But white tea is lighter and finer, simply more delicate than the well-known "herb" in the Earl Grey blend. Thus, this first impression quickly dissipates and is led in a completely different enjoyment direction by some herbs (which I cannot define more closely) and a nice dose of sage. Sage as tea and incense is always welcome to me; even if many people are always bothered by its somewhat peculiar, herbal taste; I like it! As a fragrance note and companion to the previous tea base, sage here provides a good framework on which the delightful aromas of the dearly loved mimosa and noble rose absolute can rest and "spread out." This floral freshness once again awakens the temptation to drink this mélange. Especially on very warm days, sage tea cools extraordinarily, and so such a cup of tea would not only be a special drinking pleasure but also a lasting refreshment. But this fragrance remains itself and on the skin, now surrounded by a light musky veil that forms the crowning conclusion of this "tea ceremony." Very skillfully, freshness is woven together with flowers and exotic elegance: "Rare Teas - Silver Needle Tea" is a very fine fragrance creation that is perceived as a pleasant whisper but never proves to be intrusive or even "old" in its scent progression! Jo Malone has once again created a fragrance that delights all lovers of fresh, clear scent artworks. The courage to combine the most diverse fragrance notes stands out particularly here. Many of the earlier fragrances, such as "Blackberry & Bay," "English Pear & Freesia," and also "Earl Grey & Cucumber," therefore belong to my collection and also to my life. I like this clarity in fragrance, which for me also represents a certain British understatement. "Rare Teas - Silver Needle Tea" will surely accompany me more often this summer. I look forward to many shared hours with this fragrant being, which turns out to be pleasant and exceedingly friendly - an ideal companion. Perhaps we will also go to the "English Tea House" in the Tiergarten; there, every summer, jazz is at home in the midst of nature: that would indeed be a fitting ambiance for this fragrance composition!

Jo Malone. A brand known for some wonderful fragrances. Tea. As a tea lover, do I need to say anything more? Combining both terms, one might think that something wonderful could come out of it. And yes, this assumption is indeed correct, as the Rare Teas from this Jo Malone collection are really good, and even the least favorable scent among them is above average to good. It really depends on which tea scent one personally prefers. And since I like to test my way through this range, I have now arrived at Silver Needle, well... let's drink... or rather smell :D The scent: The fragrance starts citrusy fresh with bergamot, but at the same time already has a slight tea note. Unfortunately, this tea note, which I am not entirely sure if I smell black tea or white tea, quickly fades into the background, as the scent soon takes on a floral character. This floral note (presumably the mimosa as indicated) is sweet, but also slightly stuffy, which I personally like a bit less. The stuffy notes become somewhat stronger, but fortunately, the tea also regains strength, making it more noticeable over time. The sweetness seems a bit honey-like to me, and combined with a light herbal scent, primarily sage, one almost feels like sucking on a sage-honey candy, or at least catching a whiff of its scent. I find it nice that especially in the scent cloud, the tea scent rises well and smells very good. The sillage and longevity: The projection is okay, perhaps a bit weaker than one would like, but you can still smell the fragrance at a short distance from someone. One should expect a scent cloud to be less prominent, as is often the case with such fragrances, even though the scent gives an autumnal impression. The longevity is good. The fragrance lasts more than seven or eight hours. The bottle: The large bottle, which holds 175 mL of light fragrance liquid, is rectangular and tall. It has only a small, square label with the brand logo on the front, which, despite all its simplicity, looks quite nice. The cap is black, solid, and oval on the sides. In the photo, it may look simpler than it is, but on the shelf, it must look really good. I like the large Jo Malone bottles. Okay, this fragrance from the Rare Teas collection is the one I personally liked the least, even though the tea scent itself is very nice. I personally do not like the floral character with slightly stuffy notes that much. This may sound misleading... because the scent is beautiful, very much so, but for me, it is just a bit too floral. However, if that does not bother you, you will get a very nice tea scent. Due to the somewhat too spicy-sweet character of the fragrance, Silver Needle Tea belongs more to autumn, but could of course also be used in spring. I find it a bit too heavy for summer, and for winter, a tad too light. It is suitable for various occasions, but I would use something else for going out. Despite my criticism, I am sure that the fragrance will appeal to the ladies here much more than to me, as you can surely relate more to floral notes than I can. This makes the scent smell a bit more feminine to me than unisex.

The Rare Tea Collection from Jo Malone, or rather the fact that it would soon be released, sparked immense anticipation in me as a fan of tea fragrances, and I could hardly wait for it to arrive. I was particularly curious about whether the promise that comes with a somewhat pricier exclusive collection regarding quality and uniqueness could be fulfilled. Often, the new releases I was especially looking forward to turned out to be not as great as expected. Let’s reveal this much: Fortunately, I was not disappointed this time. The first fragrance in the series is Silver Needle Tea. The first one, because the series is organized both by the intensity of the fragrances and by the length of the "infusions," meaning how long the tea has been extracted in alcohol. The fragrance is a clear liquid, which, like the other fragrances in this series, is reminiscent of the color of the respective brewed tea. Silver Needle Tea is a precious white tea that, although it gives the fragrance its name, is absent from the list of fragrance notes here. Right after spraying, "Silver Needle Tea" starts off zesty and bergamot-like, but there is a bitter note that I can immediately identify as tea. However, I wouldn’t have been able to say that it is white tea right away. Combined with the bergamot, it initially reminds me more of a fine Earl Grey. The zestiness from the bergamot quickly recedes and allows the powdery-bitter notes to spread out. Although I can't smell it directly, I strongly suspect that the musk contributes to making the tea note even more powdery, especially finer. Over time, the fragrance becomes a bit more intense, and you can tell that there are other notes beneath the tea notes that are essentially supporting it. It is definitely a floral base, but I can't clearly identify any note. It could possibly be a very light rose, although I am surprised that it is so delicate and backgrounded, even though rose absolute is supposed to be included. Well, fragrance pyramids are sometimes just smoke and mirrors. This mix of floral notes and the powdery-herbal tea remains intact until the end. The fragrance is fine and elegant, and I find it somehow special despite its simplicity. Throughout the day, I pleasantly perceive the fragrance on myself repeatedly. There is indeed a sillage, but due to the light nature of the fragrance, it is not excessive. Therefore, this scent is ideal for leisure on a beautiful, warm spring or summer day, as well as for work, even when working closely with many people. The longevity also positively surprised me. I can still smell the fragrance well in the evening. In this regard, it is definitely worth its price. I find the bottle very nicely designed. Typical of Jo Malone is the simple design of the glass bottle. The silver cap from the regular collection has been replaced here with a large black knob that is attached to the bottle with a magnet and feels heavy and valuable. However, the size of the bottle leaves me somewhat puzzled. 175 ml? 100 would have sufficed, or 125 if it was to be larger. So one has to be quite sure when choosing the fragrance that it will indeed accompany them for a longer time. A smaller size might also invite more to collect the collection, as the color gradient of the individual teas is quite impressive.

Givenchy AMARIGE MARIAGE bears virtually no resemblance to its namesake, AMARIGE, which may explain the negative reviews I've seen--a reaction to dashed expectations. If my vial were not a manufacturer-produced, carded sample, I could easily have mistaken this for a flanker of Thierry Mugler ANGEL. Lots of sweet patchouli in a pleasant floral mix, AMARIGE MARIAGE is essentially another patchouli frag among so many others which erupted on the scene post-ANGEL. The staying power is quite good, and the sillage pretty big, but I'd have to say that AMARIGE MARIAGE is more or less interchangeable with any among the entire panoply of sweet patchouli frags. Nothing remarkable or new here, but nice, if sweet patchouli is your thing (which is a big if...). The dominant floral here is jasmine, so perhaps that's the "link" to AMARIGE? Still, a pretty weak link, given that jasmine figures so prominently in so many floral frags. Maybe it's time to stop trying to make sense of flankers? The anagrammatic name is a clever twist. Better than a plastic flower cap that doubles as a bracelet, I'd say.

Spicy oriental slightly floral underneath all that oily spice. Coudn't do it, swapped it with Seatonica for Guess Seductive, which I can wear. If you like oriential spicy (I don't) this has good projection and lasts a long while.

The original Amarige may have been a sweet, white floral, but its flanker, Amarige Mariage is a sweet, syrupy oriental. I realise that this fragrance is not widely liked, hence the reason why it's often found in discount stores. I approached Amarige Mariage with a sense of trepidation, especially after having read many negative comments prior to testing. Much to my surprise and delight, Amarige Mariage is the kind of fragrance that I usually enjoy. The sweetness may be off-putting for some, but to my nose it's the perfect touch. Amarige Mariage is quite spicy and warm, with a unique bitter orange and fresh jasmine blend, adding a sparkling and delicate feel to an already heavy and rich composition. I'll have to admit that it doesn't strike me as something that I would wear to a wedding, or as a bride for that matter. It's more of a wintry, night-time scent. A fragrance I would enjoy wearing while sipping on a mug of hot chocolate in front of a roaring fire. The benzoin note smells almost vanillary on my skin, with the cinnamon adding to the slightly gourmand, delicious quality. I struggle to understand how people could grow to dislike Amarige Mariage, seeing that I'm enjoying it so much. The longevity is great, as is the sillage which radiates within an arm's length. I am most impressed by Amarige Mariage, and am even more thankful that it's still available in my area. Original review written: December 2012.

My friend gave me Mariage for my birthday - we sprayed it and reminisced about my wedding. My goodness, was I nervous! Would the wedding dress still fit? During the preparations, I had definitely lost some weight. Would the hairstyle suit me? Would I drop the bridal bouquet from my trembling hands? After all, more than 50 pairs of eyes were on me. But with the ringing of the sonorous wedding bells, I became calm. My friend recited: "It is what it is" by Fried in the church, and I was very moved. I don’t know what fragrance I wore back then, but Mariage would have been a lovely choice. It is as full and harmonious as the wedding bells. Bergamot and bitter orange create a lively opening, and the magnolia makes it bright and elegant. - Like a white wedding dress. The jasmine is radiant and the cinnamon note is subtly sweet. Patchouli and sandalwood add a touch of solemnity. Very harmonious. Just like the interplay of my sister with the alto flute and the organ. My dad gave a touching speech, and we all fondly remember that beautiful day. Thank you for the lovely birthday gift!

First of all: The original Amarige has nothing to do with Mariage. This was obviously another attempt to give a new fragrance a head start by "linking" it to a somewhat successful perfume. I still remember the launch of Mariage well. However, what the scent has to do with weddings was unclear to me even back then. The advertising posters featured a bride who was overly made up with bright red curls on a bright green lawn. And the scent is just as loud and fruity-sweet. It's all a bit too much, not to say, too inelegant. The bitter-orange top note might be acceptable, but then it turns floral-cinnamony, and now Mariage reminds me of an "Intense version" of "All-about-Eve" by Joop. It just needs a bit of apple in the mix. Amarige does have a more conciliatory finish, as the base becomes noticeably quieter and finer. Mariage apparently hasn't convinced customers either, as it is quietly disappearing from the shelves without much lament. We only carry one size now, and even that no one wants anymore. I actually find it a shame that Givenchy didn't handle the theme of "Mariage" in a more stylish and creative way, because I am convinced they can do better.

For a few years now, I've had a couple of little sachets of Amarige Mariage lying around. They contain exactly 1 ml of it. For you, I specifically opened one of them. At first, I found it difficult to get any of it onto my wrist. Somehow, it always splashed everywhere. However, I immediately noticed a scent that seemed very, very familiar to me.

....you will experience when you wear Amarige Mariage on your special day ;-) Thanks to a dear friend, I was able to test the fragrance through a sample. I can only faintly detect the orange, while the bergamot is a bit stronger. You can smell it immediately upon spraying. However, an extreme sweetness overwhelms you (and this is despite the citrus notes).

...spicy rush of mint in my nose with this fragrance. Upon applying the scent, the first thing I notice is the freshness of the mint combined with a spiciness from the thyme and juniper. A hint of woodiness follows with the sandalwood and cedar. The fragrance is rounded off with amber and musk. The perfume is masculine. The longevity and sillage are below average. On warm and hot days, this scent is easy to wear both at work and in leisure time. The fragrance is no longer in production.

...or "this summer is last summer". Today at Douglas, the tester was still in the basket of freshly arrived goods, and I asked one of the ladies to present this fragrance to me - although that is the wrong expression. A more accurate statement would be the clumsy one - to "spray" the fragrance on a paper strip. And I would gladly do that myself, alone. And the obligatory, attached sentence "would you like to test it on your skin?" is just as ineffective as the forced smile. Aside from the color of the bottle, not much has changed as expected. It probably spent too long in the tanning bed over the winter ;) The opening smells similar to its predecessor in 2011. Perhaps a bit softer than in 2010. The rest, despite differences in the top and heart notes from last year, feels to me pretty much the same. The base is completely carried over, just like every summer variant. In summary, familiar territory, but not bad - a nice, spicy freshness paired with a sensual rounding. Since I still have some of the 2010 version, I won't be getting it this year. I suspect the longevity is just as "short" as its brothers (a major drawback, because I really like the scent)...

... of 19 vintages and 19 summer fragrance creations from 2004 to 2022. A very special scent for me and undoubtedly the best CK One Summer ever made is the 2007 vintage. It has been 17 years since I last smelled it until today. A top note that smells as authentically citrusy, fruity, and bitter as no other CK One Summer. Orange, mandarin with bitter grapefruit, watermelon, and mint. You can smell everything. Not sweet. Sparkling, fruity, bitter, aquatic, fresh, and invigorating. Wonderful. Above all - no synthetic lab brew - my nose tells me! For me, this is what the olfactory perfect interplay of the components of a top note looks like - which does not vanish like today, usually after 1 to 2 minutes, but lasts and lets the nose enjoy. The fruitiness of the top note remains, as mentioned, for a long time and radiates well again and again. This sets the fragrance apart from other summer scents. Light aquatic nuances are also present. Later becoming slightly woody. It has relatively good longevity for a summer fragrance and unfolds beautifully. 4-6 hours without reapplying is easily achievable. Application area: at high temperatures in summer 25°-30°. By now, it is very hard to find or practically no longer available. A huge thank you to the nice parfumo who made it possible for me to add this treasure to my collection. I hold it in high regard.

...that smells good. The scent is strongly fruity but not sweet with a slight woody finish. After the initial wow, a pleasant feminine, subtly powdery yet fresh fruity fragrance lingers on the skin for a long time.
Really just a scent for warm days. I really like how the fragrance develops. About 2-4 hours after spraying, it smells the best.

The initial spray is very astringent. The citrussy solar floral is very reminiscent of a bathroom spray rather than an effortless hot weather cologne. It's got a disinfectant aldehydic quality that makes me feel like a sparking tile floor, when I wanted to smell like a sparkling seashell. It gets better as it dries, but the bathroom-cleaner accord gives me the same kind of headache you get after bleaching your bathtub. :(

Undoubtedly vacation-like and tropical, but without any coconut which was wonderful to me! I do have to admit that I wasn’t expecting much while going through my Jo Malone samples as we all know they have abyssmal performance and longevity, but I will admit I was surprised by how much I enjoyed this one. A soft, but fruity and bright lemon beginning paired with a watery, fresh jasmine. Doesn’t take long before frangipani takes the center stage. Its a lovely floral scent and ylang-ylang adds that tropical, slightly fruity, twist to it. The scent remains fresh and light, but there’s also a creamy facet that adds itself to the fragrance, giving off warmth and comfort. It does give off soapy vibes at one point, but nothing too overwhelming: it’s just a clean, fresh scent. It’s overall very soothing, but also elegant and discrete. Drydown becomes creamier and woodier with the sandalwood, but the floral notes remain until the end. I’d wear this when getting out of the shower or when I feel like wearing something light that’ll disappear after a few hours during the sweltering days of summer. I do have to admit I pondered for awhile on getting myself a full bottle (and I might ponder on it for a little while), but since it has such poor performance, I might have to pass up on it to avoid cluttering my collection with evanescent fragrances..

The lack of salt drove me to Galeries Lafayette. Yes, there is only one type of salt I use, and it's worth the trip to the gourmet department. Of course, it wasn't just salt: a piece of Breton butter with coarse salt crystals, goat camembert, and delicious fig bread also had to come along. And naturally, I strolled through the perfume department; I had time, so I could take a good look at everything and mentally match many of the fragrances lined up there with my existing scent samples. I hadn't been there in a long time. I realized how long it had been when I discovered a Jo Malone counter; in October, it will be a year at this location - how and where have I slept through all this time? Of course, the saleswoman and I got into a conversation. She, with already 31 years of experience in the "fragrance business," could still remember a lot: including the time of the "big fragrances" of the eighties. We laughed about our youthful sins with all those far too heavy, too mature scents that we poured over ourselves to make an impression. These "fragrance shoes" were indeed a few sizes too big for us. Now she has landed at Jo Malone, and our exchange of experiences about this brand was correspondingly intense. Before I left her, I got to know "Frangipani Flower" from the current collection. She said that we would suit each other well - and she was right! I encountered a fragrance being that, at first glance, fits well into the fifties and sixties. Like a light yellow, fragrant summer dress with a swinging skirt, "Frangipani Flower" embraces you. The special scent of these blossoms had indeed been almost forgotten for quite some time; my fragrance memory was not mistaken here. All the more delightful is that this feminine fragrance note is making a comeback in new compositions. A delicate, fresh lemon aroma corresponds excellently at the start with the heaviness of jasmine. Thus, something floral and elegant is created, which remains summery and buoyant throughout. The scent of the frangipani flower, in my perception, is a blend of a touch of vanilla, amaretto/almond, jasmine, and a hint of freshly grated lemon peel: so much fragrance beauty is united here in a single, enchanting bloom! This sensual magic lovingly marries with my special darling ylang-ylang. So far, this graceful lady is floral and buoyantly light; so light, it feels as if she is floating. A fragrance net of sandalwood prevents that and simultaneously gives a bit of contour. I find it a pleasant stabilizer, even though it can often be a bit stubborn or even bulky. "Frangipani Flower" thus also gains a touch of eroticism; until now, this fragrance creature was sweet, but also a little bit boring. That suddenly changes! Through sandalwood, a delightful, romantic summer scent emerges that not only feels feminine and buoyant but also flirts with the wearer and their counterpart. Therefore, an old song by Richard Rodgers comes to mind, which was already sung by Maurice Chevalier back then: "Isn't it romantic?" "Yes, it is!" Longevity and sillage correspond to the experiences made with other Jo Malone fragrances. They are all light-footed, and therefore I don't expect more than four or five hours of their company. It is precisely this lightness that makes them so charming. I am now only curious about what the mysterious new release in Germany on November 11/12 of this year will turn out to be! Apparently, even the employees of the company do not know what it is about. In England, this new fragrance is already being sold; the fragrance barrier seems to be surprisingly impermeable here. If I think about it, I will just stop by.

I wanted to buy a light summer perfume. Floral, light, not too subtle. Frangipani is that as well. Unfortunately, it doesn't last long on me. The scent itself is initially a successful blend of citrus and jasmine. The jasmine, which I really like, is light and fresh. Then the others quickly join in, but they don't stick around for long. So the enjoyment is only brief. What a shame.

That my predecessor mentioned that this scent has no similarities to the classic Ange ou Démon, otherwise she wouldn't have bought it, was crucial for me, because otherwise I wouldn't have engaged with this fragrance at all. The original Ange ou Démon belongs in my personal chamber of horrors and is locked away forever! But the description sounded like this limited fragrance could be MY perfect summer scent for 2014. Since I couldn't test it anywhere, I had to order it blind - a real gamble in this price range. But what the heck, no risk, no fun, and my ordering finger clicked. When the package arrived, I had sweaty hands. What if this blind purchase goes horribly wrong?? It wouldn't be the first time, but it would be the first time in this price league. The bottle with its gold-threaded content is quite pretty and would at least make a nice decoration in the bathroom. Squinting my eyes, holding my breath, I sprayed a bit on my wrist: Aha. Well. Ok, it definitely has nothing to do with the original. That's good, so it can't get worse from here. I immediately smell the pleasant lemon - no trace of a cleaning product aroma, but a really nice one - but it doesn't last long. Soon it becomes floral, and that's the part I personally don't like so much. It's probably the jasmine that bothers me a bit. I don't detect any salty accords, but all in all, this is a floral, soft, light summer scent. I particularly find the long-lasting base beautiful, as a hint of vanilla comes into play and makes the fragrance warm and creamy. The sillage is not overwhelming, and at first, I thought it didn't last particularly long. However, every time I move, a delicate scent still wafts around me even after hours. I had also sprayed quite generously, though. Conclusion: If I had tested the scent beforehand, I probably wouldn't have bought it due to the floral notes. It could also be a bit stronger for my taste. But since it's already here, I will wear it from time to time. And besides, I received my first compliment for it today - from my hairdresser. If that’s not motivation! When answering the question about the name of the fragrance, however, I had a knot in my tongue: “Angsch u dehmon lö sekret edizion kroasiär von Schivonschi” - it’s probably best if I record that and play it back if needed… And now I'm attending the self-help group meeting for blind buyers to share that this blind purchase was not, as feared, a total flop!

If you, like me, have been with Parfumo for several years and have had the opportunity to discover more and more fragrances thanks to many generous people here, then for most, there comes a point to consider letting go of another scent for every new one that arrives. There are several reasons for this: lack of space or money, or the fact that you already have similar scents and don’t need multiple that differ only slightly. Sometimes, however, the newcomer is just a little better than another very similar, wonderful scent already in the collection. And that’s how I feel about Ange ou Démon Le Secret Croisière. It will replace my beloved Ange ou Démon Le Secret Elixir. I have already written a comment about the Elixir. Even though I might write that comment a bit differently today after almost three years, I still experience the scent essentially the same way. I would just perhaps praise it a little less highly. That’s the downside of having discovered so many fragrances: you’re not as easily impressed as you were at the beginning. You become more discerning, more demanding, sometimes too demanding. I sprayed both scents in parallel for comparison: Right from the top note, the Elixir is fresher with much more orange blossom and also more jasmine. The Croisière is milder, noticeably softer, gentler, with Tiaré. This particular character of both fragrances remains throughout the entire duration. When I wore the Croisière alone a few days ago, Tiaré was far less dominant. It’s interesting how perception focuses on the differences and pushes the similarities into the background when comparing two scents: The Elixir clearly develops a sugary note in the heart, a bit like a love apple, just not as an apple but with a nonspecific fruit. The Elixir is spritzier, more active, sweeter, but also harsher compared to the Croisière, which radiates a lazy summer calm. This sluggish slowness is wonderfully relieving to my nose and reminds me of long lazy days with an exciting book in a beach chair, of total relaxation, of slowing down. While I like both, the harshness of the Elixir, which I attribute to the jasmine, is borderline, while the Croisière is particularly pleasant for summer and to unwind, without being a Tiaré bomb. And that is quite significant for me, as Tiaré scents, no matter how impressive they are time and again, have always annoyed me after a certain period. And that is not the case here. Both Ange ou Démon Le Secret Croisière and Ange ou Démon Le Secret Elixir have a pleasantly powdery accompanying note that is the same. It feels dry, slightly spicy, and somewhat woody. It is an essential component of both fragrances and so unique that it clearly indicates their relationship. When wearing one of the two alone, it is quite dominant. This note is consistently present in both and forms the main factor of the fading base at the end of about a 6-hour day. So, for those looking for a spritzy, fresh, active, intermittently sweet, but fortunately not piercingly sweet summer scent, and who are not averse to jasmine, the Elixir is definitely worth a try. For those like me, who tend to find jasmine problematic and who like a little, but not too dominant Tiaré and have a desire for a lazy, slowed-down summer scent, the Croisière is the right choice. As I read, the Elixir is no longer available and the Croisière is now called Riviera. I don’t know the Riviera, but experience suggests that it has also been reformulated.

Some time ago, I tried a Givenchy fragrance from the Ange ou Démon line, and I wrote something about how women can appear both angelic and devilish (or demonic), hmm… :D It seems that the devilish or demonic traits are always a bit more pronounced. Well, it’s just a feeling, and I could be wrong… (but I’m rarely wrong in this regard, mu ha ha ha). … phew, I shouldn’t be making “women are devils” jokes in this heat, as if it wasn’t already literally hellishly hot right now (aaaargh, I had a slight sunburn recently!!), no, if I anger you now, you might actually turn into devilish demons!! Or rather, even more devilishly demonic than you already are… aahh… okay okay, I’ll really be quiet now (for the time being)! But hey, you ladies… you guys constantly call us men “pigs” (… well, I was more often referred to as “piglet”… *sigh*), so it’s only fair that we’re allowed to describe or highlight the wicked side of you ladies in comments and such :D But alright, let’s get to a fragrance that seems quite nice, and I hope it smells that way too! The Fragrance: Right at the start, I smell a sweet floral note that also seems slightly fruity (like berries), so I’m guessing it’s the Tiaré. Otherwise, there are lemons to be sniffed, which are not particularly strong but appear refreshing from time to time, giving the fragrance a fresh vibe. However, they disappear again after a short while. Over time, the fragrance seems to become more floral; Neroli is barely detectable, just like the jasmine tea, which one (or I) wouldn’t have recognized without the fragrance pyramid. Salty notes can later be discerned a bit, giving the fragrance a slightly vacation-like feeling, but unfortunately, this doesn’t last long as it becomes sweeter again due to the amber, which doesn’t mean the fragrance gets worse; it just loses a bit of that vacation feeling. Amber is the main note in the base, so you can smell it combined with a rather understated vanilla. And as often, the vanilla gives the fragrance a slightly powdery touch at the end. A lovely scent, though a bit unremarkable. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is quite good at the beginning, as the sweetness is pretty noticeable. After not too long, it weakens a bit but remains at a good level for a summer fragrance for a while, so it should be reasonably detectable if you’re not too far from others. The longevity is okay at five to six hours. The Bottle: The bottle has the same shape as all Ange ou Démon fragrances and still looks to me like a spearhead with which we guys could be pierced :D On the front, you can see beautiful plant patterns, and in the background, this drop-like fragrance tube (if it’s a spray tube). The crystalline “spearhead” is transparent and represents the cap. I find the bottle very well done. So, I think this Ange ou Démon is quite successful as well. With its casual nature, it fits well into spring and summer, even if some might find the amber or the sweetness a bit too high for warm days. As always, it’s best for everyone to test the fragrance themselves. Yes, yes, the fragrance smells quite nice, almost innocent. When smelling on the wearer, one could definitely think that she has nothing bad in mind. Which could then be to one’s downfall if women are indeed more demonic than angelic :D The extremely hot weather right now could very well be a sign of the demonic, as it feels like hell has opened its gates, from which you ladies now emerge to hunt us poor guys, ufff… But it could also be that I’m just a bit paranoid :DD Yes, it’s just so hot,… some of my brain cells have already burned out, so I’m rambling nonsense again… :DD But still, I must mention that the fragrance has turned out quite nice and could definitely be worn on hot days despite its sweetness, as it doesn’t feel heavy. It fits both during the day and in the evening or when going out. It’s just that after a while, it becomes hardly distinguishable from other similar fragrances, which applies to many fragrances, especially today, where even the niche market seems to be flooded with countless scents, so that you could basically only come across a fragrance that smells completely different and innovative by sheer luck (which you might not like because it has a unique note like “one-week-unwashed-feet” scent note,… he he he). Be that as it may, in my opinion, this one is among the fragrances that you can try! … and the heat will continue until early August… better brace yourselves for a bit more nonsense from me here… :D

This "Limited Edition" from the Ange ou Démon family truly deserves to be called a summer fragrance. First of all, I must point out that this scent bears no resemblance to the classic Ange ou Dèmon, otherwise I wouldn't have bought it. This version, playfully infused with gold shimmer, smells of summer, sun, sunscreen, and the sea. Pure vacation feeling! I can't identify a great development of the fragrance; above all, I smell one thing, the wonderful Tiarè flower, in a soft, delicate manner. This scent can be generously sprayed on and carried in your handbag to refresh that vacation feeling in between. It is by no means strong or overpowering. And that’s exactly why this little gem will be my summer companion in 2014: overdosing is practically excluded, pleasant and summery for sure!

First of all, I must agree with my predecessors that this fragrance (thank God) has nothing to do with the other Demonies!!! Because they somehow remind me of "le petit robe noir" by Guerlain, with which I will never become friends in this lifetime! I strolled, as I often do, through my favorite perfume shop to find a new summer companion. Then I approached the Givenchy section with a somewhat disapproving glance... but ohhh, what is that sparkling hidden among the other bottles? So pleasing, so gold-creamy??? I have already noticed that I am first drawn to the warm, golden-yellow, beige flacons. That's usually where I find what I like. So, on goes the wrist and inhale.... Indeed! It has something! And once again, my intuition did not deceive me. It truly smells like lightly floral sunscreen with an exotic touch. Probably due to the Tiaré flower, which has often accompanied me in my work as a spa therapist. In addition, there is a salty, very subtly vanilla amber, a bit like salty caramel. I find that interesting and incredibly warming. It goes very, very gently in the direction of "l'ambre de merveilles" by Hermes, to which I will also comment on in due time. Because I use it reverently and sparingly, as it is simply beautiful... But now back to this edition... ah, not only beautiful to look at, it also transforms the skin into a real feast for the eyes. It gives the right summer glow without sparkling like a disco ball. All in all, a truly successful summer perfume that brings sun, beach, and sea right to the door, NO, into the house. A small comfort for me, because this way I always have "vacation to go." Thank you, Givenchy, for this edition. It has awakened new hope in me that you are on the right track...;)

...this fragrance is pleasant to wear. Upon spraying, one gets a light apple note even though it is not listed in the fragrance pyramid. This is complemented by the freshness of mint and citrus fruits. A very slight spiciness is emitted by the juniper berry. The thyme further emphasizes the spicy note, followed by a woody note. The longevity and sillage are below average. This fragrance can be worn for any occasion in summer. The perfume is no longer in production.

This smells like a forest after it had heavily rained, the sun is shining bright and it smells like damp soil+woods+warmth and something really sweet preventing it from being too green or too woody. Patchouli heavy but its so well blended but i recommend testing before buying. It smells like something an indie niche brand would create but wouldn’t sell out because it hasn’t found its target audience. As an arab this smells really rich and could be worn to any setting, but if you’re not a fan of heavy scents this would be a great open space evening scent. Perfectly unisex

"The fragrance is exclusively available on the Arab market." When this sentence is under a fragrance that you find interesting, the disappointment is great, but the longing to have it, to test it, is even greater. So what does a perfume lover do when they want it? They search and search and search.... and find! In a German online shop, and when you realize during the order that the price has just been halved (!), the joy is even greater! The fragrance arrives and everyone knows it: The packaging is not opened carefully, but ripped apart, torn, practically atomized. The main thing is to get to the scent. Cap off and go for it: "sniff sniff". Hmmmm... yamyam. The fragrance doesn't come across as heavy as one might think with some of the notes. A fresh, slightly sweet breeze wafts towards me. Date sweetness, yes, that fits. Solar note? No idea where that might be hiding or what it’s supposed to smell like. But I really enjoy this welcome! After the interesting start, it continues sweetly and creamy, but never dulls, instead retaining some of its fresh lightness. Ylang-Ylang, one of my fear components, as it often gives me headaches, is finely woven here with rose and orange blossom, so that it hardly stands out, but instead forms a beautiful creaminess. Neroli still provides the zesty companion, ensuring it doesn't become too monotonous. Almond here smells almost more like a light amaretto, just in the light version. I find almond scents somehow great, especially in winter. A total hit then ;) In the end, it even becomes a bit fresher and slightly woody, but remains sweet, creamy, with a very light hint of leather. Anyone looking for a leather scent will be disappointed. Those who find leather too "intense" will find a lovely example here, where it is finely woven into the scent and doesn’t strain the nose... I’m glad that this fragrance is available here too; I would have been disappointed if I hadn’t gotten it... Maybe I’ll get a backup bottle before it’s no longer available here... By the way, the bottle is a dream and the longevity for me is about a day, on clothing even several days! So be careful when spraying! ;)

With this perfume, it became clear to me again that although I wasn't fond of the ingredients, just as little as the bottle (which I don't think is really beautiful or elegant), this scent enchanted me with its entire composition. Powdery, feminine, and not really intrusive. It wears like silk. Smooth

Fresh like an unknown, but not sweet fruit or perhaps a vegetable, not watermelon, not cucumber, but comparable in freshness and with an unusually delicate, aromatic spiciness, Elderflower begins with a surprise. After just two minutes, it becomes increasingly spicy and now sweetish, but still bright and rather light; I find this impressive scent, after nearly 2000 tested, to be something truly new. It has such a light-footed, effortless harmony that it stands out pleasantly from other scents that are novel: Here, nothing feels forced, flashy, or demonstrative; instead, it simply gives the impression that someone had unrestrained joy in creating a wonderful fragrance and approached it with intuition and cheerfulness. In the heart note, the unknown, fresh fruit and the aromatic blend with a new, also fruity and mildly sweet, yet by no means sour note into a bright, warm, slightly creamy, effortlessly floating mélange that soothes. Furthermore, all the notes are ones I have not encountered in any other fragrance so far. The only thing I think I can recognize is a very delicate, light hint of heliotrope. And with that, we have something familiar to me in two ways: First, the heliotrope, and second, my Jo Malone phenomenon. I have yet to be able to trace the pyramid in any single Jo Malone fragrance. I have tested 11 scents from the brand, and only in one can I - distantly - discover what is listed as fragrance notes (in Tropical Cherimoya). Perhaps my previous disappointment with this brand is related to this: I do enjoy obtaining samples of fragrances whose pyramid appeals to me. However, this approach has not worked at all with the Malones so far. In the base, the heliotrope impression and the fruity notes increase slightly, and the very fresh notes from the beginning recede; otherwise, the character remains the same: aromatic, mild, bright, and completely new, fruity, without the fruit feeling familiar to me. The longevity seems average while wearing it, but the next day I can hardly get my nose off my leather bracelet, which must have received a spray. I appreciate both the scent of elderflowers, the juice of elderberries, and to some extent the pungent scent of elder leaves. I also like gooseberries. However, none of that is found here. This time, I have nonetheless received a dreamy fragrance with my choice based on the pyramid, which I will love and wear with great joy. Thank you, Geschpusi! I suppose I still need to search further for my elderflower scent. Edit: I should perhaps add that I tested the new version, that is, the one from 2021. I do not know the old version - should it smell differently.

I had already given up hope of getting Jo Malone's "Elderflower & Gooseberry." From the limited "Sugar & Spice" collection from the 2013 season, it is also only very rarely available. Unless one is willing or crazy enough to pay up to 180.00 euros plus overseas shipping for a nice scent intermezzo. So I was content with my decant: however, I guarded it very carefully. My more or less irregular walks here in the souk brought a big surprise: a leftover of "Elderflower & Gooseberry" was offered. A leftover is enough: even for me, there hasn't exactly been a great drought in terms of fragrance. Seen, written, and after a few technical difficulties bought on Wednesday afternoon. Hooray! I could already announce my decant of this calorie-free dessert to a friend. The letter must have been traveling at breakneck speed; from Horb am Neckar to Berlin in just a few hours: so that works too! Anyone who has an elder bush in front of their house knows how many possibilities the flowers and fruits offer. Already in late summer/autumn, picking and cooking the berries is very creative - and usually leaves the kitchen looking like a pigsty! Elderberry soup - always delicious warm or cold! -; fruit spread pure or with apples and, for example, a few mint leaves perfumed; fine and clear jelly and thick syrup: very good for summer and winter drinks. This syrup develops particularly well when mixed in a 1:1 ratio with a fine liqueur! (Bottled in pretty bottles, by the way, a popular and welcome gift or souvenir.) A good harvest keeps us well and healthy through winter and even part of spring. Because a few vitamins do survive cooking. Glazed or fried elderflowers are a delicacy: if you manage to get rid of everything that has legs and wings. Thus, elder is not only useful in the kitchen. No, as the so-called "guardian of the threshold," it should also not be uprooted or cut down! That brings nothing good for house and family; nature keeps a particularly protective hand over this plant. Not without reason have magic wands been cut at certain lunar phases time and again. Thus, elder should be honored as a whole. I love all types of berries, including gooseberries. The large, thick red ones are of course something particularly fine, but the small green berries can also be very tasty when ripe. And it seems that these small berries were used here. My grandmother had four gooseberry bushes in her garden, and since I usually spent some time with her during the summer holidays, I regularly managed to stuff myself with unripe gooseberries and then complain. She could talk, she could scold - I always believed: this time they are really ripe! (From time to time, my father's stubbornness does come through after all.) Later, we had rhubarb or gooseberry pies, tarts, and cakes at home - with and without meringue - for Sunday coffee or for birthdays. The acidity of the fruit and the sweetness of the sweetened, slightly caramelized egg white has something very special. All these kitchen magic tricks are united by Jo Malone, along with the very sweet lychee, in "Elderflower & Gooseberry." This scent, which is more sweet than floral, is truly a collector's item. It is a very special fragrance creation and therefore, with all my sympathy for it, it is absolutely understandable that this purely seasonal plaything did not make it into the standard program of this company (like, for example, "Earl Grey & Cucumber"). The longevity is average for Malone, here perhaps a bit longer due to the sweetness. For this collection, the well-known narrow, rectangular smooth bottles are used, in keeping with the English understatement. My joy in this scent is genuine: it simply brings good cheer. Jo Malone's "Elderflower & Gooseberry" truly spreads a calorie-free cheerfulness!

I'm going to write about this perfume as I could write about a beloved person I've lost. In fact, this fragrance was the mate of my 20years and it represents the springtime of my life. I discovered it and tested the first time in a drugstore in Brescia, Northern Italy, where I studied at the university. It was love at first smell: so flowery-fruity, so soft, so perfect for my Young age! I cannot forget the gorgeous rasperry top notes characterizing this scent as rich as a secret garden . Then, I remember the warmer and very feminin flowery bouquet revealing all its innocent sensuality. At the base, the unforgettable sweet vanilla notes lasting on my skin for hours without resulting too intoxicating or sweetish. The sillage was good and the result so ethereal and so perfect for a "jeune fille en fleur"! It was a little corner of Paradise, contained in a very romantic and refined bottle which was a little masterpiece to show on the bathroom perfumes shelf. A scent connected to the springtime , to the first ray of light of the day, to a bon ton and flowery dress , to pastel nuances. This paradise is lost not only because the oerfume was unfortunately discontinued by the Maison Givenchy (and I ask myself: Why?) but also because, changing my address and transporting too many objects, I didn't find anymore the precious 50ml bottle I owned and which was one of the last presents given to me by my mother for Christmas. R.I.P. dear "Fleur d'interdit"...I'll smell you in my best dreams!

After repeated, but alas, unsuccessful attempts to find a single drop of well-preserved vintage, I have to say: "Goodbye, Dear Friend!" May you remain in my memory as young, fresh and beautiful, born for joy and seduction, as your creator intended you to be. Apparently, you were too tender, time and conditions could not preserve your green and watermelon notes, some flowers in your heart have faded, sour shadows are imprinted on your profile and only the base reminds of what you were. You've aged, we've aged, but it's a natural process, albeit a little sad. You were unique, as evidenced by the lack of a large list of similar one. Your wonderful bottle I will tactilely remember always, in my memory you will forever be a favorite. And I will still look for you in new incarnations and hope that someday you will be re-released, rejuvenated and modernized. Goodbye my beautiful, my Fleur d'Interdit!

Like Xeryus before it (also Givenchy) Fleur d’interdit is an odd mixture of styles. It’s an aquatic - fruity-flora hybrid which re-jigs the classic feminine to appeal to under 25’s. There is red fruity sweetness jostling with bitter moss and thin aquatic notes, and a sour woody musk coming from the base; three different tropes at loggerheads... Needless to say, if you work on the principle of throwing enough muck at the fan - till some of it sticks - you won’t come up with a Jackson Pollock.

Today, on Christmas Eve, I am in a contemplative, yes somewhat sentimental mood, as so many dear people are no longer present for the family celebration. They are in another place. I have to come to terms with that - but I still miss them. But my thoughts are with them. I rummage through my scent memory box, which tells so many stories. Christmas is the festival of love - and completely unexpectedly, a fragrance comes into my hands that has a lot to do with the theme of "love". It is Fleur d`interdit by Givenchy. I had already resignedly saved it under "Had I" - but it is indeed still there! I wore it during the time when I fell in love with my husband, and he with me. He is not a fragrance fan, but Fleur had captivated him - alongside my humble self. This multifaceted scent underscored our getting to know each other until the wedding, like the film music of a romance. The beautiful flower may be forbidden because it is so irresistibly attractive. One cannot escape its charm, just as the sailors of the Loreley could not resist, and crashed their boats, intoxicated by the lovely song of the beauty. Hyacinth, strawberry, and melon taste so sweet that one cannot get enough. So it was with us - we had to always be together - and we still must. Violet, rose, and lily of the valley are unabashedly romantic, but deep oak moss and dark iris admonish and warn. Should one embark on the adventurous journey together - when one does not really know where it leads? But do we have a choice? I think of Erich Fried: What it is It is nonsense says reason It is what it is says love It is misfortune says calculation It is nothing but pain says fear It is hopeless says insight It is what it is says love It is ridiculous says pride It is reckless says caution It is impossible says experience It is what it is says love The forbidden flower has brought our souls together, and our little ship faithfully rocks through rough seas and calm waters. Sometimes we land, sometimes we move on - but always the two of us. The forbidden flower may possess magical power.

Some time ago, I wrote a blog post about scent memory. My example was Fleur d'Interdit. I assume my elementary school teacher wore it. This was in the mid-nineties, and back then, we still had somewhat rougher manners in elementary school, especially when the teacher - like my Mrs. F. - was tenured and couldn't be fired as long as she didn't hand out slaps. But otherwise, there weren't many limits to the cruelty. Luckily, she didn't have it out for me (thank goodness my mom sang in the same choir as her), but when I enthusiastically sprayed my Fleur s'Interdit that I had won on eBay a few years ago (I had no idea it smelled like Mrs. F., and I had completely forgotten about her), my hair stood on end. I spent about 20 minutes wondering why the scent was so unpleasant to me, and then it suddenly hit me like a ton of bricks. The teacher... And little Lisa in between, somewhere between fear and wanting to please, and aversion because she was always going after the best friend, who eventually broke down in tears, that wild boy, it was outrageous, and there was nothing to do but look down awkwardly and write his homework next time. That's Fleur d'Interdit. SO unfortunate, because actually, it's so beautiful... As I already mentioned in my blog, I wore it quite often to drive away the unpleasant memories. And it works. Somewhere in the back of my mind, she still lurks, Mrs. F., but I can now enjoy the scent for what it is. A - now - completely out-of-fashion floral fragrance, lush, elegant, detail-oriented, like you can't find anymore today. Exactly my thing! When spraying, there’s now a slightly sour note. My bottle must be about 25 years old, so it could very well be the signs of time. Looking at the top notes, that could fit as well. With melon, raspberry, wild strawberry, it can sometimes smell a bit sour, but the warmer it is, the less I perceive that. Even though Fleur d'Interdit is anything but a lightweight, it develops best in warm weather. I have the impression that the longer I wear the scent, the clearer the individual notes become. The flowers are expansive from the start. Lily of the valley, hyacinths, violets, lilacs... Everything grows wildly together. After about 3 hours, the fruit notes also become clearer. Strawberries, raspberries, with leaves in the sun. Green notes often seem cool and damp to me. That's not the case here. We definitely have green notes, but bright and sun-drenched. Really beautiful! Fleur d'Interdit lasts effortlessly all day with strong sillage. Careful dosing is advisable, also because the scent is so out of sync with the current zeitgeist. It can happen that you stand out unpleasantly. The base is rather inconspicuous, creeping in over time. Nice scratchy oak moss, cushioned by clean musk, slightly powdery, not really woody. This one really takes off, and as is known with many high-quality vintage fragrances, the overall picture changes constantly, and the scent remains lively all day. I like it more and more the longer I wear it. I prefer it on really beautiful summer days when it's warm but with a light breeze. If you like this type of fragrance, grab a bottle somewhere. It's really worth it. Fleur d'Interdit on my teacher was the first perfume I consciously noticed on someone, basically my prototype perfume. And I liked it a lot back then (Mrs. F. is mean, but she smells good). Now I'm very glad I kept the bottle and didn't sell it due to unpleasant memories. If you set those aside, it actually belongs to my all-time favorites.

...have just as much to do with each other as Fleur d'Interdit and L'Interdit or a Chypre! Sure, the comparison is a bit off, but I did not choose it lightly.
