Simple, to be sure but I feel like it delivers on the idea of what the name conjures up in your mind. Non-offensive, mild tempered spice with a creamy understated sweetness. I totally get the connection to the "Nutmeg Ice Cream" moniker. It's food-like without being too literal. I tried to wear Kenzo Jungle Elephant and although I appreciated it, I couldn't handle the strong food-like quality that it had. It was just too much for me. I gave my bottle away. This one would be a second cousin, twice removed of Jungle Elephant. Same kind of idea but less savoury, more sweetness and much more subdued in it's approach. If Jungle Elephant could be described as a nuclear bomb, Nutmeg Ice Cream would be a gentle rain. So far, from all of the Demeter fragrances that I've tested, this one is my favourite.

Background: The limited "Tea Collection" from Jo Malone is both very tempting and refreshing with all 5 scents. There are three so-called tea fragrances: Assam & Grapefruit, Earl Grey & Cucumber, and Fresh Mint Leaf. The other two scents, Sweet Milk and Sweet Lemon, are the layering components and can be combined with the other tea fragrances. It is meant to evoke the English custom of enhancing freshly brewed tea with a slice of lemon or a bit of sugar. The Scent: When I first encountered this collection, I was a bit surprised at how tea could be created as a perfume, but the saleswoman told the story so charmingly and lured me in with sweet pastries. Well, I can’t resist sweets….. The first thing that stands out is the obvious lemon, which isn’t too surprising given the name. The scent feels clean, and the bergamot and rhubarb add a delicious fruity note. This is later enhanced in the heart note with peach and pineapple, along with a small floral touch from the freesia. I wouldn't have perceived the base notes this way. Perhaps the cypress prevents the scent from becoming too citrusy. For me, the pineapple and peach remain very prominent. This makes the scent fresh, fruity, and ideal for warm summer days. Conclusion: Sweet Lemon is a lovely companion for summer, sun, and vacation. For me, it becomes extremely exciting when combined with Sweet Milk. It takes away the creamy sweetness from one and the citrusy aspect from the other. The result is a scent that I personally can’t get enough of, even if I’m not adhering to the original concept of layering. C’est la vie…. It reminds me of delicious fruit sorbet with a dollop of caramel sauce……

The pepper comes through very strongly in this fragrance, paired with aquatic notes. A combination that I would never buy again today. In my opinion, the scent fits very well into the early 2000s, but today it is absolutely not a crowd-pleaser.

Since the three bottles of this "London Blooms" Limited Edition visually appeal to me particularly, I had to test them, of course. After all, I like both peonies (mainly the flowers themselves) and moss as a fragrance note in perfumes. The first impression was simply that of peonies, well and naturally captured, but somehow also boring, just a nice peony scent. After a while, there was no significant change, so I had already written off the test for myself. I forgot the scent strip in my coat pocket until it came back into my hands a few days later, and I was delighted. What I perceived there was quite different and perfectly suited my taste. The peony note had receded into the background, and the wonderful moss note in the base harmoniously - yet still dominantly - came to the fore along with the other notes. The moss note strongly reminds me of the Goth Juice hair gel from Lush, just sweeter. Now the transformation into a truly beautiful fragrance was complete. But somehow, buying a perfume doesn't make sense when you have to wait so long for it to go from nice and boring to special and appealing. Such a divided fragrance is rare for me. Even two further tests consistently led to the same result. Really a pity, as I also find the longevity to be very good.

How can you best test a fragrance? I think when you have the original right next to it for comparison. In front of me on the table, there has been a vase with mimosas since the afternoon, filling the whole room with its spring-like and enchanting scent. Delicate little flowers like a thousand tiny suns are beaming at me, lifting my spirits hour by hour. Forgotten is the rainy and dreary day. Outside yuck, inside yay. And how could it be otherwise, reaching for the mimosa scent for my winter-weary skin that longs for spring is an insatiable need. Test subjects: Real mimosa, Amarige Mimosa de Grasse Millésime from 2005, and this one from 2007. Right off the bat, both Amarige Mimosas are quite authentic compared to the real mimosa. The difference is at most that the Amarige Mimosa de Grasse Millésime from 2005 exudes a warmer scent, as I can imagine a mimosa bush under the strong and warming sun. In contrast, this scent here is truly authentic with the contents of the vase. Fresh mimosas with stem, leaf, and bloom. Enchantingly intense, yet still very fresh and cheerfully yellow. In the sillage, both the real one and the one in the bottle hold their own. Both successfully compete for my favor. In terms of longevity, for now, the real one will win, but when it has lost its beauty and fragrance splendor in a few days, I will always be able to delight in my two bottles and joyfully celebrate spring. Whether it snows, rains, or whatever.

Mimosa is usually what one calls a sensitive being that always appears a bit awkward and cries at every little thing, right???? This Mimosa has taught me otherwise, because she is anything but "delicate"! Well, the girl comes from India and enjoyed the blazing sun and plenty of rainfall in 2007, which is not the norm in India every year. I actually expect a sweet, full-bodied, perhaps slightly creamy little Mimosa, just like I know from Mme Goutal. But even this line of thought vanished during my olfactory experiences with Mimosa 2007 in a dark side alley! Upon spraying, I immediately remember Amarige, the classic predecessor, "only" that in this fragrance the Mimosa is in the foreground. The scent power is comparable to that of Amarige, which simply means one thing: BAM! Fine, I think to myself, Amarige with Mimosa, is that it? But the girl from India has more to offer.... I don't have to wait long, as the dear one reveals herself to be a cheeky little rascal, rebellious and everything, but really everything other than shy! Fields, miles and miles of fields densely filled with Mimosa abundance exude a true scent power. Herbal-floral, this really present scent wave lingers on my arm, and I have to wait a while longer for the described sensual-powdery woody note, which, after the breathtaking appearance of the little Mimosa, turns out to be quite shy. But if I sniff deeply, I can smell the creaking, damp underbrush at the end of the fields that dries after a heavy shower in the sun.... ~ Conclusion: This beautiful Eau de Parfum is a knockout, truly impressive, but not for the faint-hearted! The dosage must be applied very sparingly, otherwise the sillage becomes a knockout for the surroundings! ~ INFO FROM THE WEB: Givenchy Harvest 2007 Amarige Mimosa is a perfume from the Harvest 2007 trilogy, which opens richly with a hint of mandarin leaves, neroli, and mimosa. In the heart note, the absolute mimosa from the Tamil Nadu region in India is present, while the base accords evoke noble woods, sensual and powdery. Compared to the original Amarige perfume, this is a modern, shiny, and sparkling variant. ~ Story: Native to Tamil Nadu in South India, the mimosas selected by Givenchy grow at an altitude of nearly 5,000 feet. In 2007, this tropical zone experienced exceptionally low temperatures and abundant rainfall. The essence obtained - both warm and powdery, and sheer and green - is the centerpiece of this collector's "Harvest" edition of Amarige. ~ Description: The green mimosa top notes melt into the neroli. In the heart, the floral notes of mimosa dominate Amarige. The woody base amber takes on a powdery tonality. Designed by: Emilie Coppermann, Symrise.

No, this mimosa is not delicate, I agree with Michelangela. To me, she appears as a fairy, such an otherworldly beautiful being, who looks fragile with her delicate, translucent wings, but nevertheless has a lot of substance behind her ears. The mimosa fairy is incredibly natural and doesn’t waste any time. She gets straight to the point. Bam, she flies right into my right nostril, swirling around so much that my left nostril gets a bit of a taste too. She is sweet, she is strong, and very enduring! At first, I wanted to lock this cheeky thing away again, but then she decided to let the green notes free. Now she starts to wrap me around her little finger a bit. And when I scold her for her direct attack, she sulks behind the next bush and acts all dignified. She almost had me wrapped up. What a wonderful rascal, this mimosa fairy, even if she doesn’t quite suit me. But for women to whom she does suit, I imagine this scent to be enchanting! And for those who love to sniff flowers, here is a fantastic liquid flower bottled up.

I have already encountered several mimosas. I personally own the Acca Kappa Mimosa, which has a very soft and delicate scent, and I have also tested the Annick Goutal Mimosa, which didn't really reveal its fragrance at all. Here I have a very special mimosa in front of me, a kind of noble mimosa. It’s not a headache-inducing scent, as one might suspect from the pyramid, because the mimosa, whose fragrance clearly dominates this composition, is accompanied by a green note, which significantly reduces the sweetness. This scent is definitely wearable, everywhere and on any occasion, even for going out. It changes a little over time, as the green note becomes softer and actually something like white flowers comes into play. However, I cannot identify these individually; in any case, they are fine white flowers, not overpowering, like gardenias or similar, but rather very carefully dosed jasmine and possibly even white violets. Once the scent reaches the base, it becomes clear that this is not a drugstore fragrance, but a very beautiful, thoughtfully composed creation, in which the fragrance components have been artfully arranged and, despite some edges and corners, show a lovely unity. Thank you very much, dear Michelangela, for enabling me to test this. Even though I wouldn’t buy it myself, the sample stays and will be used up. For me!

... with this introduction (the translation of its name) and an enthusiastic grin, my then favorite fragrance consultant introduced me to this Givenchy, and I was curious... curious about what a scent with such an exciting name could do and how I would like it. A few seconds later, I had it on my skin, and since then I love it! Love at first sniff, so to speak. I can only partially agree with the name; for me, it would rather be glowing hot summer days, when the sun slowly sets in the evening and the tanned skin is still pleasantly warm from the sun's rays, a light breeze, midsummer. A desire for life, a desire for summer, for adventure, simply beautiful and in such a way that it should never end... from May to September, I’m all about this little water; when it’s cooler or gets cool again, it doesn’t work - at least on me - as well, it’s missing something, probably the summer-warmed skin... The scent leaves an impression - definitely one of the top 10 fragrances, after whose name I have been asked multiple times while wearing it ;-) Out of sheer enthusiasm and slight excitement - after years of reading along and browsing, this is my first comment here - I unfortunately don’t have the individual fragrance notes ready, I’ll just add them later... .. I’m just so delighted that it still exists... AND I couldn’t quite believe that no one has rated it yet!

"London Rain" - this series name suggests something light and fresh. To get straight to the point: in this regard, "Wisteria & Violet" sails under false colors. It is also the only fragrance in my Jo Malone collection that stands out in this respect. The content delivers what the dark purple bottle promises at first glance: It is quite a surprise! Heavy, fully bloomed wisteria, spiced up with violet and water lily. - If you like it, you like it! I like it, and that’s why I have enjoyed this fragrance from the very beginning. Just a few spritzes and it envelops you like a voluminous velvet cape, warming and long-lasting. Therefore, it could also be the ideal fragrance companion for slightly cooler spring or summer evenings. (A little jacket wouldn’t be so bad, though!) Maybe there’s a cocktail in a matching color? That would really be something! Certainly not a fragrance for sporty women looking for a fresh kick. Also, the woman who chooses this fragrance should not be too young. In the office, "Wisteria & Violet" is better worn only after consulting with colleagues or in "solitary confinement." With public traffic, I advise: better "hands off!" I bought my bottle used almost two years ago and was somewhat shocked by Serafina's statement. I’m sorry to hear that. Hopefully, that won’t happen to me as well. Because I wouldn’t want to do without my cozy velvet cloak. After all, there is indeed the right time for it every now and then.

I can't pass by the Play fragrances from Givenchy; they have a special melodic statement for me. They remind me of musical pieces from my favorite band Coldplay, which invite you to sing along. The beautiful Intense has already found a home with me, so I had to try Play for her as well. The fruity opening - I recognize orange and lime - is like the sparkling piano intro of Coldplay's "Clocks". It has a buoyant lightness and an attractive sweetness. Then the tone becomes fuller and very beautifully creamy through Amyris - sandalwood oil. The white iris adds a bit of minor to the melody. Very expressive. Musk makes the fragrance shine and gives it a soft finish. A harmonious, melodious scent that immediately makes me want to pop in the Coldplay CD.

In my opinion all of these Pi flankers are far away from original. I can detect some herbals, an aquatic note and a very weak cedar base. This one smells very synthetic and has almost no projection and lasting power. Updated September 2014

Amazing fragrance with good projection. The Longevity more than 5hrs. Best summer scent i like ever. Dam good catchy smell which can easily attract everyone. I get lots of compliments. Girls Love this. One must own this for sure. Fantastic job by Givenchy. I Love it.

Bold and different from the regular Pi Neo. Smells strongly of coconut - the only perfumes I know that evoke similar associations are Set Sail St. Barts and Fire Island. Not suitable for the office, as it is too noticeable, but excellent for the summer months. Due to the vanilla sweetness in the dry-down, the scent lasts a long time, definitely 8-10 hours. The downside is the closure - it’s almost missing, so air always gets to the sprayer - in terms of longevity, especially for a limited edition that is no longer available, it's poorly designed.

This review is for the EDP concentration. I want to add my voice to the group praising Philosykos, this was my entry to Diptyque, and based on its strength I suspect I'll be adding some more through this season. Thanks to the previous reviews, I knew I'd be in for a nice treat when I went to smell this one; and a treat it was! I haven't tried any of the other fig-based frags yet, so maybe they just all smell this good, but this was a very welcome change-up from the usual cologne offerings. What I read on the open is a very fresh, fruity (fig), leafy top. This part is fantastic, and lasted around 30 minutes. I noticed that the fig retreated a bit after that and the coconut note came a bit more to the forefront afterward, providing a counterbalancing scent, as well as just a touch of sweetness. Based on other reviews, it seems that the EDT may have a more pronounced fig note, just as an FYI, but fig is definitely noticeable in the EDP as well. This one did evolve some during the heart and drydown, but never resorting to the tried-and-true powdery or musky notes I get in so many other scents - which can be boring. I honestly think I'd have a hard time describing this drydown precisely, because it's well-blended. In any event, it evolved "nicely", I'll settle for that. I know the "natural-smelling" catch-phrase is overused, but this one definitely strikes my nose as being more like something I'd smell outdoors in the Summer, than something that comes out of a beaker. Scent-wise it's top-shelf. Given that the concentration on this bottle is EDP, it had the expected, to maybe slightly less longevity, sillage and projection than I'd expect. It wore fine, but it's not a beast by any stretch. Probably 5 hrs good wear for me on the first couple of wearings in hot Houston, TX weather. The scent is unisex to slightly feminine, I'd say. No issues pulling it off, I think in a casual scenario any guy could, really. However, much to my dismay the GF didn't like this at all. Which was surprising, because she likes fresh/sweetish scents normally, likes coconut, and she's part Greek. Silly me, I figured this would be a homerun - just a word to the guys who are looking for a date day/night frag - this one might need GF approval first :) I wouldn't recommend this for workplace wear, it sure presents itself as a personal, casual scent. Recommended, and highly enough that I will be back at the Diptyque counter again, smelling some of the other little gems.

There is a fig tree in my back garden that keeps me busy all year round. Branches grow and extend all over the place and regardless of how many I manage to chop one year twice as many will take their place the following season. During spring the garden is taken over by bees and bugs and in late summer, once the figs start dropping from the branches like hand grenades the insects multiply. Any attempt at gardening will leave me bitten, stung and with plenty of decomposing fig pulp stuck to my soles. In autumn the massive fig leaves have turned brown and started to fall, waiting for the rain that will turn them into a wet and musty blanket all over the floor. Before winter arrives the last gardening tasks of the year are completed in preparation for the cycle to start again only a few months later. Philosykos brings me back to this garden every time I spray it: I can smell the wet leaves, the wood and branches as they go through the seasons: very green and fresh during the spring-like opening, more woody as the scent evaporates with the summer heat and almost earthy during the autumn-like drydown. It smells clean, transparent and natural but also at times milky with an almost rubbery feeling, bringing to mind sticky sap. Since the fragrance recreates the entire tree and not just the fruit it remains a perfectly unisex fragrance throughout, light and easy to wear by anyone almost all year round. One day I wlil move to another place and no longer have a fig tree to keep me busy throughout the year but I will always keep a decant or two of Philosykos to bring those memories back.

I am so attracted to fragrances with green notes that I often overlook the green qualities that every other reviewer mentions in their first sentence. Philosykos green? I hadn’t noticed. I think of Thymes Fig Leaf & Cassis or Jo Malone Wild Fig & Cassis as green, but Philosykos? To me it's all about being creamy, creamy, creamy fig (with fig being incomparable to any other scent except perhaps that of dates). The coconut adds sweetness without announcing itself individually. Philosykos runs fairly linearly, yet never strikes me as boring, which even the illustrious Lutens Feminité de Bois can be for me. The scent doesn’t throw far from the skin and is so subtle as to possibly be perceived by passersby only subliminally. I would wear Philosykos in regular rotation if my husband weren’t put off by fig in any formulation.

This is a fragrance where there is a huge difference between the EDT and EDP. I couldn't stand the EDT but love the EDP. I started out sampling but ended up buying a full bottle of the EDP. I'm going to admit that I don't really know what a fig smells like. I do know what coconut smells like and I don't get a heavy coconut smell out of this. It must be mixed very well, because neither the fig or coconut is overpowering. What I do smell is a VERY green fragrance. It reminds me of the smell of breaking open a new green branch on a maple tree in the spring. The fragrance is good but unfortunately, at least on me, it suffers sillage and longevity problems. Even with 6 or so sprays of the EDP, it's a soft fragrance with only moderate longevity. I bought it direct from the Diptyque website, so I'm sure it's not counterfeit and I highly doubt that it's old stock - it's just the way the fragrance is. If you like a soft, green fragrance with moderate longevity, buy it but as far as I'm concerned, I won't rebuy based on how weak it is.

Philosykos is very realistic and captures the feeling of eating a ripe fig while sitting on fresh grass underneath a giant fig tree. You get the fruit, pulp and peel and juice and all, plus the thick, almost gritty green leaves, a bit of the wood and bark, and even a hint of the dirt under the roots. This is how a squirrel or a bird experiences a tree redolent with ripe, juicy figs. The reason this perfume stays in such high demand despite how relatively odd it is, especially compared to other popular perfumes, even in niche. To me, it is a bit *too* realistic. It lacks something that would make it a scent I would like to wear on my body. I can recognize the craft that went into making it, and I can recognize how spot-on it is. It smells exactly like walking out onto my back deck when I lived next door to a massive, decades-old fig tree that was beloved by the local squirrels and raccoons. In the mornings, there'd be partly eaten figs all over the ground and the deck, and this is a concentrated version of that smell. If it were sweeter or maybe a little more floral I would like to smell this on myself, but as it stands it is a beautiful piece of fragrant art I would like to smell on others. It smells divine on my husband, even though I would say this is truly unisex since it just smells like a tree on a sunny day. If you have never experienced Philosykos, I would highly recommend it, as it gives a deeper glimpse into the art of perfumery. To my mind, it is a singular scent experience. I personally love fig notes so I am always happy when I get to sample this just for the sake of understanding fig perfumes better, but I will stick with scents that employ the fig as a motif rather than showing me the life cycle of a fig, from branch to dirt to return again.

3/5 of my Discovery Set: What set Diptyque off my radar was the existence of this scent. It seems that praise follows and trails behind this legendary scent across every corner of the fragrance aficionados. And what a scent it is. Like biting into a fresh fig, it perfectly encapsulates the essence of a fig - deconstructed down into its bare components.
Lads, ladies, and all romance-seeking beings in Hades, gather round, for I am about to share with you a deep and profound secret of perfumery. There is such a thing as...one of THOSE perfumes.

So I am biased on this one. We had a Fig tree in our house during my childhood, and I had a connection with that tree. I used to cover my eyes and blindly went up the tree. The first time I smelled this fragrance I was freezed. That tree with all the trunk, branches, leaves, fruits, and even a creamy resin was in this bottle. It's an instant LOVE.
Philosykos isn't exactly my favorite fragrance, but it's definitely my most worn fragrance by a large margin, because there's really no context where I *wouldn't* want to smell like this.

To me it smells like green fig trees, ripe figs and earth after the rain. Definitely refreshing, opens up a little different in each season. Perfect for days when you want to feel grounded, fresh, and just a little nostalgic. And after rain? Absolutely magical. It blends right into the air like it was always part of the landscape, I like it!

This fragrance is mostly carried by a beautifully realistic steamed rice note. More specifically, it carries the smell of the "sticky rice herb", or Nuo Mi Xiang, Semnostachya Menglaensis (I don't know any English name for it), which is sometimes used to scent teas. Here the steamed rice (or rather sticky rice herb) is combined with subtle roasted sesame and blonde woods, which creates an association with bamboo chopsticks and furniture. It is a bit sweet on my skin, like some rock sugar was added. If there is any paper here, like the name suggest, it is rice or bamboo paper. Or maybe it is the rice itself, delicious as it is, but asking to be painted with colorful condiments. After a while the white musk gains in prominence, although the sticky rice herb stays for a pretty long time as well. Near the end - after about 5 hours - it's mostly musk and bamboo wood. I don't think it projects very far after the first hour (unless you use more than two sprays), but it is not a skin scent either. It seems to hover about 20 cm above the skin for hours. It's hard to rate this scent. It's definitely interesting and something I did not smell in perfume before, but not for all-day or frequent wear. In any case, I don't see myself wearing this outside of my house or even when having visitors. However, I tend to associate steamed rice with childhood family cooking, hence making this a very soothing scent for me, especially the opening and the first hour. Even then, I tend to find the phase where the musk starts to overpower slightly suffocating. In sum, a very interesting fragrance to sample and try, but definitely not a blind buy.

A "your-skin-but-better" scent in the genre of Glossier You or JHAG Not A Perfume. That Iso E Super woody base note is prominent, but the steamed rice accord is savoury and cozy. The mimosa plays a supporting role, but definitely adds a slight uplifting freshness to the scent. Really easy to wear but comforting in the best way possible.

As much as I love Diptyque, I can’t defend this release. They already have the perfect “your skin but better” fragrance: Fleur de Peau. L’eau Papier is a waste of display space. Don’t be fooled by the fluffy musk and rice opening: a hefty dose of Ambrox-adjacent ingredients ensures that it dries down sharp and metallic. It feels like a half-baked attempt at AnOther 13. Its only redeeming quality is the beautiful abstract art on the label. Diptyque, PLEASE release minimalist and natural-smelling fragrances. That’s what your brand is known for. Don’t go down the route of musks and woody ambers.

Honestly, this is one of the best things I've ever smelled. I wasn't expecting much and knew nothing of this scent. First comes to my mind my solo trip to Berlin. this hotel lobby, cozy, small, decorated for Christmas. So subtle and soft, it makes me want to curl in bed or take a steaming hot shower. It's a scent that's hard to describe, but for me it's just the most pleasant toasty musc. The more it dries down the more it becomes a second skin, almost lactonic, and I'm transformed into another hotel in Scotland. They had original milk-musc soap there, and it's just so lovely. It's also holding up in this position for so long, I could still smell it's ghost on my skin a day after i sprayed it. What a beautiful experience!

One of the few renditions of white musk that really goes beyond merely smelling of recently washed clothes. This feels clean, but carnal, abstract yet almost tangible. I especially like the (shortlived) first few minutes which clearly evoke steamed rice.

This was a random sample and I fell in love with it straight away and bought a bottle of it. L’Eau Papier is a clean and fresh scent without being soapy or detergent like. It’s a cozy, soft, minimalistic blend which is mostly subtle musk with a feeling of hazy rice steam. It really smells like freshly boiled rice.

I had been eyeing this perfume for quite some time. There’s something magnetic about the dry, delicate yet slightly pungent scent of old books, newspapers, parchment, rice paper, or faded black-and-white photographs stored in tin boxes.

The combination of notes and accords on this perfume blend perfectly together and really transports me to a soft and warm embrace. This may also be due to the fact that my partner uses this a lot, and when I smell it I instantly feel safe and protected.

I feel overwhelmingly that this is the best skin scent I have smelled, despite it being a bit too reminiscent of warm porridge. I have it in one of the little travel vials. My younger sister fell deeply in love with the scent, I am saving up to get her a bottle. I do see that the scent slips away rather fast, but it's like a white rabbit hopping away tentatively.

I got this as a present two years ago and have worn it during summer ever since. The more heat, the more Philosykos gets better. I find it to be at its best when it's scorching hot. I haven't worn this outside of summer, but every now and then I pick up my bottle to give it a sniff. Every time I do, I exhale aloud with pleasure. Its freshness, creaminess and slight sweetness is just delicious, and a true delight to wear. Can't wait to wear for the heat to wear this.

Philoskyos from Diptyque is a scent I don't wear very often because I am not quite sure what to make of it...and I don't know how to pronounce it, either. It is meant to be a perfumed ode to the fig tree in its entirety, the wood, the leaves and the fruit, but to be transparent here, I have never eaten a fresh fig, and even worse I sometimes get confused about dried figs and dried dates, so I'm already at a loss. What I do experience from this scent is the milky sap from a broken twig and the fragrance of spring greenery, damp from a morning rain. Despite that, it still comes off as dry, and I would expect it to also be fresh and light, but somehow it's strangely musty. I wear this on days when I know I've got a lot to think about, to remind myself that it's okay to not know everything, and maybe never reach a conclusion.

Philosykos is beautifully effervescent, even on moisturized skin. The opening is fresh and juicy, combining the sweetness of fruit with the green of its leaves and twigs. Over time, the fruitiness dies down and the wood settles down with a pepper-like note. And then, it's gone. I usually get a good hour before it settles, and then it often becomes a skin-scent / scent-suggestion by the 5th hour. I couldn't tell you what it smells like on others, or if it subtly fills a room with its beauty and you just never notice. This one keeps to itself, and I guess that's fine. The only thing that arrests me from loving it is the constantly increasing price of the bottle. I would not consider this worth $200+, though the bottle is gorgeous as well. I say this, but I continue to buy it, because I love the very idea of it. It is an easy go-to, especially if you live somewhere temperate and/or humid and you get warm days throughout the year.

These days, I own the EDP, which is greener and woodier than the fruity EDT. The point is essentially the same, though – Philosykos is the whole fig tree in a bottle, leaf, sap, and fruit and all. It is an intensely naturalistic, evocative, vivid fragrance, and one that pushes the fig narrative with single-minded agression. It reminds me of sitting under my mother-in-law’s massive fig tree on the small homestead she owns overlooking Skadar Lake, straddling Montenegro and Albania. Spraying this scent transports me back there immediately. Always a happy experience, therefore, albeit one tinged with a bit of nostalgia for the Mediterranean, which I find becomes especially acute in the depths of an Irish winter.

I got a free sample of this at a local Diptyque boutique I went to in Spain. I loved the paper smell but was not certain this would be great as it seemed somewhat unwearable and more of a smell I would want on a candle or a soap. However, it was wonderful to wear. Super refreshing and green. Personally, I did not get any fig fruit notes and got only plant-like notes which was not bad, but it could have been any other plant in the marketing and I would have believed it. Sadly, it was gone from my skin and my clothes within 2 hours, which I spent outside with fresh air. Other scents I go noseblind to still whiff me in the clothes, but this one was just a total disappearance. A shame since it was so good. Compared to the other sample I got, L'Ombre Dans L'Eau, its performance sucks for both being on the lighter side of fragrances. Test before you buy.

Soft and creamy rain, freshly cut grass, and fig trees all around. Initial impression is a bit too grassy but when it softens to fig leaves and mild coconut, the scent is so calming and beautiful. The longevity is criminally brief and I am much too low-maintenance to bring a 75mL bottle around with me to reapply throughout the day.

Philosykos is a beautiful fragrance. It smells like nature, like the fig tree and not just a sweet fruit. The EDP is sweeter than the EDT and has more coconut. I am in a Northern European climate, so that may be different somewhere warmer. I bought a small bottle of EDT after using up my miniature version and was in heaven.

It smells like a tree. That's it. The fig does add a beautiful freshness, but the fig wood and leaf are VERY strong. When sprayed on MY skin it leaned very green & woody. I liked the woody smell since it was perfect during autumn or when it would rain. I didn't like this perfume that much probably because of how green it smelled, like a young tree whose bark was cut.

This is a stunningly beautiful fragrance. It is green, fresh, slighlty floral and fruity, but never cloying and barely sweet. It smells just like a freshly cut underripe fig. I found it to be fairly linear. It lasted 7 solid hours on my moisturized skin, and over 24 hours on my clothes (although I have a sensitive nose).

I was excited to try this, as I’ve never tried a fragrance with this much fig in it. Fig fruit, fig leaf, fig tree… I also tend to enjoy a coconut note. But I think the combination of fig, coconut, and other green notes blended very poorly with my skin, because on me, this stinks.

This fragrance opens with a delicate, almost edible vanilla accord. Simply delicious, the accord reminds me of a vanilla-lemon custard, or a vanilla-lemon cake. This gourmand impression is soon shattered by the appearance of juniper and elemi resin which I see as pepper and incense. The scent remains sweet and vanilla-dominated, but I'd place it now in the same category as the non-gourmand Vanille Insensee by Atelier Cologne. This Dyptique, however, has more presence and sparkle. The fragrance sheds most of its sugary and citrusy facets as it develops - the emphasis is now more on the vanilla, resin and smoky tea notes. The dry down can be described as a flat vanilla framed by a sheer veil of smoke.

I’ve never been a person to douse myself in fragrance. Maybe in high school. But I’ve always been appreciative of a relatively intimate scent bubble. My rule of thumb is: Don’t fill the room but be noticed. Eau Duelle EDT has pretty poor sillage. But it’s really part of what makes this shine as a fragrance. It’s a green, bright vanilla. The vanilla is specifically so similar to a pure vanilla extract. No sugar, all vanilla. The pepper and juniper are there but sit behind the prominent vanilla. Being a EDT lets these bright notes burst. It’s fun to layer and play with Eau Duelle EDT. L’Eau Papier is an amazing base for it. It dances with the steamed rice/ sesame notes and creates a signature scent worthy fragrance. Orpheon as well. It creates an incense-y vanilla with a woodier base. Eau Duelle EDT isn’t trying to be loud, and that’s exactly why it works. It’s proof that a fragrance doesn’t need to be beast mode to be beautiful. The way its pure, unsweetened vanilla hums close to the skin makes it feel effortless—almost like a secret.

For a long time, I never quite understood what a “green vanilla” scent was. Is it referring to a vanilla pod that’s unripe and picked early? Or is it referring to vanilla blended with green notes like leaves and herbs? If you have a definitive answer, DM me lol. Either way, I feel Eau Duelle is the first vanilla I’ve encountered that feels like a "green vanilla". Unlike the usual cozy holiday vanillas that are warm and gourmand, this is vanilla by day. It’s vanilla on a sunny weekend with no plans. Vanilla wearing a cotton shirt with a top button undone. It’s airy, light, and well, green I suppose. I tried both the EDP and EDT on different hands for a side-by-side comparison, and they both have this easy-breezy feel. I don’t think either version of Eau Duelle is cozy and wintery. While I’m glad to experience this green vanilla and try something new… it’s not really my thing. I guess the vanilla-coziness association is too strong and I keep wanting/expecting Eau Duelle to be deeper and more ambery (which it isn’t meant to be). For vanilla fans though, I can see it being a refreshing take on a beloved note.

This is what Link puts on before meeting up with Zelda for an evening walk around Hyrule Castle grounds. Light woody fairytale like scent. Love the piney juniper opening with the light incense and vanilla dusted wood chips. I also own G Water and Eau Duelle EDT lasts longer, has more sillage, wears lighter YET has just as much, if not more depth. Balsamic touches and light spices dance about underneath this soft cloud of vanilla. Wonderful understated creation by the house of Diptyque.
I have a sample of this and wow! - it's vanilla overload. There's nothing muted about it from the start. Imagine a very strong, creamy vanilla ice cream and you have Eau Duelle.

Eau Duelle is a spicy vanilla fragrance, but this spices are not ones you would typically expect in the style of the feminine orientals like Shalimar, Opium etc. Instead... Eau Duelle has what I call "green" spices, like cardamom & herbs. These feature juniper, pink pepper, elemi resin (which to me smells "juicy") and olibanum (frankincense).

When I went to a Diptyque store and said I wanted an ice cream scent, they said, "Then it's the EDP!" But I tried a sample first and was disappointed with the EDT. It doesn't have the richness of ice cream at all. Diptyque's EDT and EDP have different notes as well as concentrations. You shouldn't think that they are perfumes with the same atmosphere.

Ah, Dyptique. I was unimpressed by your offerings before and now more than ever, continue to be so. Why is your wonderful vanilla/frankincense composition so very weak? When I first smelled the EDP, I was mesmerized by the church incense note. The burnt vanilla was soft and wonderful. But after a few minutes, there is nothing at all!

Eau Duelle is a lovely light and airy vanilla, lightly sweet and a touch earthy/woody note. First spray is prickly spice with the hints of pink pepper, smells almost like green pepper to me. The dry down is the most lovely sweet and woody scent that clings to skin. Lasts well for Diptyque EDT but it does not project like most Diptyque fragrances.

Diptyque EAU DUELLE is a somewhat sweet floriental. Pretty inoffensive but also not very thrilling. I wore the liquid edt both yesterday and this morning, and I have now applied the solid perfume. Yesterday's wearing was, I have to say, entirely forgettable. I didn't even notice what I was wearing for most of the day. I'm finding the solid perfume quite a bit more appealing.

Orpheon is a very potent clean- fragrance, the type of fragrance that doesn’t annoy anybody near you and has well-blended and natural ingredients as components. For me, this smells like taking a bath infused with provensal soap, juniper berry , jasmin, and then laying on some clean cotton sheets. It has a strong sillage and also a very distinct lingering power in a room- the cloud remains even one hour after the person has left the room ( I experienced this before only with Bacarrat Rouge) . It does have a certain vintage feel to it, but it’s a rather “clean girl in the South of France in 1960 ” than an “grandma” type of vintage. Orpheon should get more attention that it does at the moment, for sure !

Orpheon is Fleur de Peau's younger, cheeky brother. They share a similar cocooning effect on the skin but Orpheon is somehow fresher, almost... crisp? Melancholic like a fall afternoon walk after the rain. Old, modern, both and neither at the same time - a beauty that transcends time. Simply dreamy. Fabric softener but make it Dyptique. I don't know why but I always imagine Orpheon being worn by a girl in her late 20s to early 30s strolling through the streets of Seongsu (or Yeonnam, Sinsa - honestly, any hip neighborhood in Seoul would do). She strictly wears minimal monochrome looks paired with eclectic accessories - an issey miyake asymmetric pleated shirt, a perfectly glossy hime haircut or big square glasses to frame her face, a collection of funky charms on her bag. Art book in one hand, half empty cup of iced coffee in the other (no sugar, duh). Exuding coolness at every step but, weirdly enough, it never looks like she's trying too hard. Effortless. Like it's second nature. I don't know if I'd rather have her or be her. Ughhhh

Wow I love this perfume. It’s strong without being overbearing, it’s clean, fresh, and a little sensual. The opening starts off very masculine with the blast of juniper berries. But then once the jasmine and the other notes come in, it helps to soften the overall vibe of the scent a bit and make it completely unisex. It never turns very sweet on my skin, but does develop a beautiful warms from the Tonka bean. The cedar adds a stunning touch of wood, making the scent very well rounded. It’s addictive, harmonious, and perfect composed - which makes its name ever more suitable. I wore it yesterday to work and right after I sprayed it on myself, my boyfriend took the bottle and sprayed himself too. We walked out my place smelling so beautiful. Like I said before, it’s quite strong with really amazing performance. Stays on the skin for 10+ hours easy, and projects for about 4-5 hours, but in a very subtle way. If Fleur de Peau didn’t work out for you, definitely give this one a go. It’s a beautiful way to do “skin scent” that would smell nice on literally anyone. This will probably be in my collection forever.

(Warning: I had a lot of controversial reactions towards this scent, so a lot of editing below, sorry for the inconvenience :-(.) So I went to a shop where they sell niche brands and they were so generous to give me two samples: One of Orphéon Eau de Parfum and one of Fleur de Peau Eau de Parfum . And now I remember: a co-worker in a former job smelled amazing and when I asked her what she was wearing, she only said: 'Don't know if you are familiair with Diptyque?' she didn't seem to be willing to reveal the name of the scent (don't know why), but I'm now sure it was one of these. And - seeing the year of production - it must have been Fleur de Peau. But they share some similarities. Now about Orpheon...Ofcourse I read the background story and in the opening I can relate to that a bit: Modern Jazz improvisations in a bar can come to mind, but after drydown the scent becomes the opposite of the opening. Opening is abstract, aromatic, herbal... The drydown however is beautyful, blushing skin asif the Jazz-singer sings a more mellow song near closing time, wearing powder and lipstick. Drinks and smoke still linger, but in the background. It smells clean...or...I don't think 'clean' is the best impression, it's 'skin but better' as from a healthy body after a workout (which does not represent me at all, but I find it very attractive to imagine it would - lol), not that musky kind of 'clean'. Very lovely. It did cut through a rather chilly wind when I biked home, wearing it on my wrist and I got very pleasant wafts during the ride. I will try Fleur de Peau tomorow, sprayed some on my hand and I think it goes more quickly to that 'skin-stage', a bit less sweet, more powdery (in a good way) and also soapy, but a bit more vintage-y soapy. I may like that even better, but I surely will get either one of these beauty's as a full bottle! Edit: First I thought I liked Fleur de Peau more, but after trying both samples and especially remembering my initial positive (understatement) reaction towards Orpheon, I decided to buy Orpheon, Fleur de Peau is also beautyful, but turned out to be a bit too musky and, in my case, this can be headache inducing. I also find Fleur de Peau a bit more linear and very persistent on clothes and I found it good on skin, but not so much on clothing. Edit II: I'm having one problem with this scent: It just won't leave my skin, I need to wash maybe 6 times to get it out of my system and clothes I need to wash two or three times. So I only wear this when I'm sure I'll be wearing it the next day too. A good thing for those who want to wear this as a signature maybe, but not so much for people who frequently want to wear different perfumes. Edit III: I bought Fleur de Peau too, now that the weather is warmer and it is easyer to spray on skin, avoiding cloths, both are lovely for separate reasons, despite some similarities. Edit IV: So sorry for all the editing, but....this scent is so very different with each wear that I just can't take the risk of spraying it any more. It's like russian roulette actually...and...my boyfriend, who doesn't care much about what I wear, really hates this...

I received Orpheon in a travel spray set. I wanted the rest of the set and this one was just along for the ride. On paper, it's nothing like what I'd choose. Even sniffing the bottle, it's not my style. However, once I tried it on, I was smitten. I'm still confused why I love it so much. I typically hate powdery, clean scents, but this hits the spot for me. It's actually the only one of the whole set I ended up buying in a full bottle size. It's a very cozy, almost fresh laundry smell. Luckily it doesn't go soapy on me. Based on the PR for it, I expected more of a night-out, sexy, smoky perfume. What I got was a day in, reading a book, and snuggling type of perfume. I'm pleasantly surprised and now I'm wondering what other fragrances I've missed out on due to not liking the notes.

I struggle to cypher the notes on this chypre. Smoky, musky, nuanced… chewy? It’s sweet in the way that salted black licorice is technically a candy. Moreso than distinct notes I get a distinct atmosphere. There’s history to this fragrance. Amidst the current wave of shower scents and clean musks, Orphéon stands an aloof anachronism.

I generally don’t like powdery notes in fragrances, but the sharp juniper top note, balanced by cedar and vetiver in the base, cuts through it beautifully. When I first tried this, I liked it at first but then wanted to scrub it off halfway through the day. Yet, for some reason, the next day, I felt drawn to it and gave it another shot.

Cedar soda with juniper bitters. Water drawn from a limestone well surrounded by briar and bramble, thicket and thorn. Aerated ice chips that shatter between molars. A single cypress cone crushed between fingers. Cigarette ash that never quite made it to the tray. The condensation ring left on wood that won't ever completely fade. Cold metal keys pressed against warm lips.

I wear this nearly everyday to work - it's inoffensive, smells great with powdery and woody notes with a bit of musk on the drydown. The juniper is more an initial hit, and Orpheon is a well-composed perfume by Olivier Pescheux (Rest In Peace).

The fragrance of my dreams, truly. I have always wanted a luxurious, powdery, spicy floral like Orpheon, and was elated to finally discover this fragrance on my trip to New York earlier this year. Orpheon is a fragrance that screams 'luxury' in the best way possible. It's very upscale and chic, but never too full of itself or too kitschy either (I'm looking at you LV!

Hello, first of all many greetings. I am new here and am trying my hand at my first comment. Hope I'm doing this right:-) Absolutely Givenchy is, in my opinion, a delicious candy for on the go. Although it is relatively one-dimensional and doesn't hide its somewhat synthetic notes at all, I love the scent. The passion fruit and apple come through very clearly, and with its light, fresh sweetness, Absolutely is probably something for every day. I would consider Absolutely a delicious, fresh alternative to GentleX L'Or, without the annoying gold glitter and without the "scratchy" notes... Unfortunately, it's relatively hard to get the scent; the 50 mL size was only available for a short time at the local Douglas (45 €), and otherwise, I have only seen Absolutely at the airport in the "travel sets" in mini format - a shame, because it easily outshines the more expensive mainstream scents, in my opinion. Best regards

I like Eau Duelle (EDP version) for many reasons, but perhaps the best reason is because it sets out to be an equal dance between two opposing elements (cold, spicy incense, and warm, clear vanilla), and in this, it succeeds effortlessly. The opening is cold and aromatic, fizzing with the sting of pink pepper and juniper berries. Hiding behind the aromatic spices and black tea is a warm, robust, but utterly unsweetened vanilla. The vanilla note pops its head out shyly at first, but then it becomes a dance of equals, the aromatics, black tea, and the incense dominating one moment, the vanilla the next. The two elements never merge, instead they develop along separate tracks, but wrap around each other at various points of the journey. It's worth pointing something out about the incense and the vanilla here. First, the incense here is not the smoking resins type of incense, but the cold, waxy, almost herbal/aromatic spiced air left behind in a church after incense has been burned but long since extinguished. This type of note is in fitting with the cold, open air feel of Eau Duelle in general. The vanilla is cold and clear, sharpened by a slight evergreen edge. There is a starchy, papery feel to the vanilla in Eau Duelle that makes one think of opened books. It is a cool-headed, intellectual vanilla fragrance rather than a sweet, foody one, and it's all the better for it.

Petrified forest vanilla. Strikes me as a tree resin sort of vanilla, like something you’d get from melting down Paleocine amber. Dry, peppery, honeyed, smoky. It still lays down malty and smooth, like a true vanilla extract. Queen bee of the “evergreen amber” family of vanillas. Perfect choice if you found Glizzy Water too flighty and cupcakey, or if you wanted more fire and spice from Architects Club. Does something parallel to Liis’s Bo but with pine and pepper instead of mallow and cedar. Or perhaps Babycat, evolved into a graceful cougar. Yes mother. Mental Snapshot: The kind of woman who would carry an impressively scuffed-up Birkin, the way nature intended. She’s an art historian, an elusive Pulitzer winner. Think hot archaeologist, like Rachel Weisz in The Mummy. tl;dr: elder amber

Oftentimes the initial stage of a fragrance is the most exciting part and it's rare –at least for me– for the fading drydown to beat an opening full of fireworks. Eau Duelle is one of such exceptions: a scent that requires patience in order to reach the proverbial pot of gold. The first few minutes may come across as too loud or agressive particularly for a Dyptique fragrance, usually so full of restraint. There is an abundant bright spice that is fizzy like ambroxan, and it combines with cypriol oil to create an almost sour accord that the most sensitive nostrils won't appreciate. Thankfully this stage doesn't last too long. Once the spice settles the real protagonist rears its head. It's a warm, slightly powdery and very pleasant vanilla –far from sickly sweet– next to some wood and incense. This is a much more enjoyable combo that comes to the forefront fully as time goes by, ending up in a sober, unisex vanillic woodwork smell with a hint of smoke. It's a perfume that could be categorized as spicy, woody and sweet but it never approaches gourmand territory. A few hours later most of the notes are gone and there is just a faint vanilla scent on the skin, so comforting that one wishes it would never fully fade away.

At first I struggled to smell it , I really don’t know why because now I can smell it correctly maybe because I were smelling other decants before this ( this was a decant too not in a spray bottle I just had to opened it to smell ) I was a little bit disapointed and gave it directly to my mom who were in love with the smell ( which I didn’t understand because I cannot smell it before ) but at the exact moment she put a little bit of juice on her wrist and I went to smell it I immediatly regret giving it haha and cannot stop sniffing her wrist ( which is a little bit ankward but I didn’t care haha ) I completely fell in love with it !!! this fragrance is just sooo good it’s smell exactly like a bourbon vanilla a spicy vanilla / smoky vanilla with so much warm in it not a sweet vanilla tho but a sophisticated one I think It will be perfect for the vanilla haters , then come the scent of incense and oh my god I don’t know if it’s because I always put incense in my home everytime I feel good but this note makes the fragrance more comfy more cosy ! I really have a instant hapiness when I just smelling it in the mini bottle I think It will be perfect for everyone and anytime especially for autumn because it got a cozy vibe to it but I really think I can rock with it all year long This is definetly a unisex perfume and will be smelling so good on a man ( unfortenetly never experience it yet :( ) Some people said the EDT smell better , according to the notes I really don’t know but I will try it and buy a full bottle of the EDP !! btw sorry for my bad english I’m a french speaker :)

It's a strong vanilla scent for vanilla lovers. For me it is a little bit to flat, a scent does not develope enough. It is the same from the beginning to end. Than after a few days rather boring. Like book which you begin to read knowing how it end up. Who would like to read such kind of book…

This perfume opens spicy and green on my skin. Then, it quickly develops into a resinous and expensive vanilla. The vanilla that was used here smells really rich and sophisticated. It's not a sugary vanilla, but rather a formal and elegant one.

I agree with every line of the last review, which I found remarkably accurate: this is a cold-incense, cold-forest, cold-green vanilla scent that warms my soul. Thanks to that review, I finally bought this perfume which had been on my mind for a year. Eau Duelle is neither an intimidating incense nor an overbearing vanilla.
For those who aren't into full-on gourmands but appreciate a hint of sweetness with complexity and depth, this might work for you. It feels luxurious yet sexy and comforting at the same time.

I once said I liked vanilla at a Diptyque store, and they told me to try the EDP, so I tried it. I also had them spray it on paper and put it in plastic, and I kept smelling it when I got home. At the time, I was impressed that it smelled like high-quality vanilla ice cream scooped up with a wooden spoon. The top smells like a warm bungalow.

Oh wow?! This is beautiful. I’ve never tried Diptyque fragrances before and I’m quite pleased that this is my first from them. The vanilla in this is very sophisticated, a little creamy and very smoky from the incense.

....use seemingly uninteresting, shadowy fragrances on the weekend when only unpleasant household chores await me after the work week. So also "Lovely Prism". I thought it was so unspectacular - I don't need to elaborate on it. Today, it is this fragrance from Givenchy. Well, it doesn't blow me away and doesn't transport me to olfactory heights, but it has a lovely fresh floral quality, for which I immediately received a compliment from my son. ("That smells good, did you just put on some lotion?") Unfortunately, the longevity of the EdT is poor. I've already reapplied three times. I'm not shy about it. Overall, a fragrance that deserves to be presented to the world on beautiful spring or summer days, should anyone notice it. You certainly won't be bothered by it, as the sillage is as meager as the longevity. So a recommendation for those who like it light, floral, and close to the skin.

I like "Very Irresistible" in spite of its stupid name and the bad reviews it often gets. Uninventive, boring, bland, nondescript, "utterly devoid of beauty" (Luca Turin!). Well. To my nose, VI is an uncomplicated, pretty rose fragrance. The Special Edition from 2010 features the lush scent of "rose damascena" and is much more expressive than the "regular". It's a "safe" fragrance, nobody ever objected to it, I never heard a single negative remark about it when wearing it, on the contrary, I always get complimented on the "wonderful perfume". If you love fruity roses and want a pleasant, flowery scent, this edition might be the right thing for you.

By day, she is cool. Distant. Her daytime makeup is bourgeois, understated, precise. Her skirt is knee-length, her blouse neat and high-necked. Her hair is tamed. Her aura: aloof, almost biting. Her passion: financial accounting. After sunset, she sheds her skin. She takes off her high-necked blouse and frees her tamed hair. Her dress: neat is different. Her evening makeup: only carnivorous women wear such. Her aura: You can close your jaws again! Her passion: everything that cannot defend itself. “Very Irresistible Rose Damascena 2010” is such a 2-in-1 woman. In the first hours, a cool, even frigid little rose that isn't even very rosy. Cool pale pink flowers based on alcohol. But at some point, after three or four hours: Cut! The total transformation! And what emerges is an unsweetened creaminess like no other. Almond-like, leathery, buttery, smooth, appetizing, sensual. Like tons of exquisite tonka bean, amber, musk from the best parents, and soft woods to go crazy over. A dream of a base that, to top it all off, lasts forever. Rarely has a seemingly unremarkable little rose surprised me so much. I have never experienced such a metamorphosis in a perfume before. Now I hope that this wondrous transformation is not due to my own skin chemistry. When I read the other comments, I am struck by the sinister suspicion that the little rose usually keeps her blouse buttoned up. Nevertheless: Thank you to the garden fairy for this surprising fragrance experience!

How is it that the rose lover didn't know this fragrance until now? Well, I already know quite a few rose scents, but I can't know them all. There are just too many, and unfortunately also too many bad ones. Rose Damascena by Givenchy, however, does not belong to the latter. On the contrary, it is a beautiful, albeit not necessarily natural rose scent. It rather showcases a playful form like those found in Les Parfums de Rosine. At first, a sweet, peach-melon-fruity opening creates a bit of confusion, but that dissipates as the rose unfolds. Initially, it blends its scent with the fruity notes, but then it becomes stronger and stronger, while the sweetness decreases simultaneously. After that, the fragrance hardly changes anymore. The rose blooms and competes with itself in terms of scent as much as it can. And it lasts quite a long time! This rose easily survives an entire day and only needs a little refreshment for the night to continue blooming until the next morning. Not bad for this Damask rose. But it lacks the edge, the character, the special something, the Irresistible!

I tried this years ago and did not like it. I just revisited Tam Dao, and I guess I have done a near 180. I still can't say I love the scent, but I at least like it now. I get some sweet sandalwood at the start that is quite nice, and then the scent turns briefly green. The green transition is brief, but a bit medicinal and unpleasant smelling. Finally the sandalwood returns, mixed with a strong incense accord. Neither the best sandalwood nor incense scent available, but worth a sniff if your tastes run to either of those notes. A mild recommendation from me at 3 out of 5 stars.

Much has been said about the sandalwood element here. Whilst I do detect the sandalwood vibe I must admit it is faint. I do notice the other woods here being more prominent, such as the cedar wood etc... Overall it probably shouldn't be looked at as an iconic sandalwood fragrance. Definitely a prominent woody scent but not exclusively a sandalwood one. Overall it's warm, very pleasant and the dry-down happens to be very nice. Unfortunately it doesn't seem to go anywhere else apart from smelling like high quality, freshly polished wood. In that way it's quite a linear fragrance. However worth a try, just not the masterpiece others claim it to be. But it is elegant and refined, definitely. If wood is your thing, you will enjoy, but it's not in any way ground-breaking in my opinion.

Cedar - that's what this fragrance is. I don't smell much of anything other than that. It's like walking around in a natural wood furniture shop or smelling freshly cut cedar. To me, that's wonderful! I like the smell of natural wood and cedar. It's not an overpowering scent and longevity is average at roughly 4-6 hours.

I couldn't decide what the opening of Tam Dao reminded me of until I found a review that gave me the answer: crushed dill! An odd note for sure, but very short-lived. For the most part, Tam Dao rides on the carrier wave of a white-musk molecule that my nose also detects in L'Artisan's Passage d'Enfer, among others. Cedar is definitely present, and sandalwood as well. Both are mellowed down by the white musk base that creates a waxy-smooth effect and binds the whole composition together. Progression is minimal over time, but the scent lasts on my skin for many hours. Despite the linearity, I find Tam Dao well-balanced, inoffensive and rather calming.

Review for the EDT in round bottle. Well, to be honest, I was a bit worried that there will be too much cedar and not enough sandalwood in the EDT version. But I can happily confirm that it's not the case! Tam Dao EDT is a beautiful sandalwood-centric perfume that's completely unisex. It reminds me so much of the sandalwood fan my mother used to have, it's almost the same smell, only the real wood was a bit sweeter and muted, while Tam Dao has quite an airy, spacious and solemn feel to it. Like a Buddhist meditation to find inner peace. Which is interesting because I do feel calmer and more meditative than usual when I wear this scent, so the suggestion works. The sandalwood is not milky or creamy, in fact it feels a bit raw and dry, as if freshly cut - but I do not get the dusty, wood shavings impression from it either which is what allows me to enjoy it completely. Behind the sandalwood, cypress and rosewood are great in their supporting roles, maintaining the exclusive woodiness and adding complexity and interplay. The cedar is also there among the crowd, but not a contender for the dominant note. It adds a touch of masculinity and keeps everything dry and airy. Overall, a true woody perfume and a wonderful way to relax and think more profoundly about the meaning of life. :) Sillage and longevity are moderate. A reapplication might be needed after 6 hours.

I am mystified by certain perfumes that receive so much adulation and adoration from its admirers yet leave me totally unresponsive to its supposed beauty. Diptyque’s Tam Dao is a prime example of these enigmas. This review is based on a sample I picked up at a Diptyque boutique.

The major downside to this is that you may get tired of it after a few wearings due to lack of complexity of notes. However, if you are like me and enjoy sandalwood, you are truly in for a treat. This immediately puts your brain into a serene mode. On days where you don't want to wear anything, wear this.

This brand along with L’Artisan Parfumeur has something that just makes it float a step above the majority of other niche brands. Tam Dao is another example. It smells very very woody, clean, dry, soft, smooth. A cloud of very clean and clear wood flakes with subtle things around.

The moment I put it on, I was hit with a strong, macho scent like vetiver and cedar. I was expecting a kind monk, but I got hit on the shoulder with a bamboo sword. I couldn't detect any rose or myrtle. It's probably a supporting role. A few minutes later, I smell a sweet cypress scent. It's the unique sweet scent you get when cutting wood. A little fragrant.

Nose err.. note picking can be fun, but in the end it is just a guessing game. In the completely irrelevant yet never-ending "Cedar vs Sandal" discussion, I find myself somewhere in the middle. A little bit of both, I suppose. Obviously, this is a straightforward, almost simplistic all-woods perfume.

“Very Irrésistible Givenchy Rose Centifolia de Châteauneuf de Grasse”: this is the name of the limited edition of the Givenchy fragrance “Very Irrésistible”. For this fragrance, the rose variety “Rose Centifolia,” which grows near Châteauneuf de Grasse in southern France, was used. Right from the first spray, you can immediately recognize the close relationship to the original scent. With the difference that this one is much rounder and more harmonious. It feels as if “Very Irrésistible” has been extracted for so long that only the rose note remains. And that is anything but bad. This slightly sharp and somewhat artificial note that always lingers in the background of “Very Irrésistible” is completely absent here. The limited version is harmonious, and the fragrance notes are well balanced. The “rose” also takes center stage; I would even say it carries the perfume entirely, while the other fragrance notes serve only to support the “rose,” making it softer, gentler, and more powdery. The rose note smells very authentic here, not artificial, sharp, or musty, but fresh and elegant. A very beautiful, unobtrusive, and at the same time modern rose scent. Unfortunately, it is no longer available, but Givenchy releases a special edition every year dedicated to a specific rose variety.

Tam Dao is a triumph of focus, showing what's possible in perfumery when a house lets itself celebrate and elevate a single note (or, well, ok, kinda two notes - more on this below). I spent huge portions of my childhood camping in the pine forests of the northeastern U.S., and while a northern white pine or balsam fir obviously isn't the same thing as an Indian sandalwood or Lebanese cedar, there's a reminiscent, coniferous quality to Tam Dao that brings me back to those days. It's a tremendous fragrance. Tam Dao is dry, warm, mildly creamy sandalwood and cedar. Think freshly cut wood drying in the sun, or a green branch you just snapped off a tree on a summer day. A previous Parfumo reviewer described it as smelling like a dry sauna, which is very accurate. And that's it. That's what you get here. This is stripped-down, linear, nearly photorealistic perfumery. There's no evolution over phases, no complex blend of notes, no interpretation needed. It's as uncomplicated as can be, and magnificent for it. It's tranquil, calming, and sophisticated. If you're looking for something more creative or interpretive or multifaceted, this will disappoint you. But if you can appreciate the artistry and sophistication in a tiny number of high-quality ingredients singing in absolute harmony, you will enjoy Tam Dao.

Boy if this is good. Now you need to really like the scent of a piece of spruce wood. It starts with a very high dose of Iso E super or something similar on a bed of javenol, its not so creamy but almost spicy (i guess thats the coriander but isoesuper is also quite peppery lets face it) With this I am not saying it smells synthetic but it reminds me of those molecules. I absolutely love it! It smells of a wooden chalet, the inside of a steaming hot sauna, woodchippings. Drydown is the best because i finally get the lime which adds this quirkiness, the olfactive accident I guess. Vanilla is there to reinforce sandalwood and add some depth. I am not sure what amberwood smells like but anytime i see it listed theres some sharpness and incredible longevity added to the fragrance ( I am thinking to L'homme a la rose MFK). Going to comparisons there was a moment (having tam dao in one hand and gypsy water in the other) in the beginning of the drydown which they almost smelled identical but opening and drydown are in completely opposite directions. Tam Dao is a fulfilling 360 degrees woody experience (actual dry bark guys) whereas gypsy water goes citrusy and and somehow sweet. If you are searching for something like Gypsy water i suggest Tulsivivah! from Miller et Berteaux which is a super happy and comforting sandalwood with oranges and lemon, that fragrance really needs more attention and love because its great! 10 out of 10 Diptyque again, never a disappointment in fact the accident is mirtle, which makes sense it enhances the smell of sandalwood. Last thing I promise, i dont get the name. Or I mean this could have to do with what we associate with smells, because of what i said I would think this as a very western oriented fragrance and instead it is made thinking to asian forests. Just great how we come to things from completely opposite angles of perspective

I like using a pencil since I was a little kid.. The pen also does the same job, but you can not correct what you have already written without making a smudge first and writing it again.. The pencil forgives.. it can walk on its toes.. it can transition from pale to bold depending on how much you are going to press it against the paper.. it can be silent like a ninja or ferociously loud.. A playful pencil that can draw black teeth on perfectly sterile posters or French moustaches on mythically expensive paintings.. just because it is fun to do.. A pencil next to a blank A4 paper on a beautiful thick wooden table and a glass of buttery milk.. I am 41 years old and I still use a pencil.. One of the most beautiful scents I have ever experienced.. 10/10 Ps A small piece of advice.. spray it on clothes rather on skin.. it lasts for days.

The EDT version Tam Dao Eau de Toilette has been a regular in my office rotation for quite a while. Its blend of cedar, sandal and cypress woods gives off a long lasting mellow mood. That really gets me through the day. More recently I stumbled upon a sensational sandalwood note in Bois des Îles Eau de Parfum and that triggered a new quest for a sandalwood perfume. Since I already had good experience with Tam Dao Eau de Toilette and I read that the EDP formula had even more sandal, it made sense to explore this one first of all. To my nose, the EDP and the EDT are almost interchangeable. Clearly, the components come from the same bottle. They form the same dry, barky woody dimension. More sandal? Not sure, that may as well be an effect of the increased concentration overall. One significant difference is how the EDP feels more 'spicy'. In the end, no doubt this is a great woody scent. If I ever finish my EDT, I will replace it with the EDP. That much is sure, but there is no point in having them both. Alas, I must continue my quest for an even greater sandalwood.

Tam Dao from Diptyque is a perfect poem of a scent that I love wholeheartedly and which others have most assuredly spoken of more eloquently than I could ever hope to. A dry, woody composition with notes of cedar and cypress, sandalwood, rosewood, and musk, it’s an understated and Introspective fragrance, evoking the meditative shifting light of the afternoon sun as it deepens into the melancholic shadows of evening as daylight dwindles. It recalls for me the oft-quoted line from beloved poet Mary Oliver’s The Uses of Sorrow: “Someone I loved once gave me a box full of darkness. It took me years to understand that this too, was a gift.”

Review based on a 2015 EDP version. Nothing bad per se, but nothing new or creative either. Nothing wow about this at all. And, on my skin, absolutely no sandalwood. Nothing even remotely creamy. This is all about super dry cedar (definitely high on iso e super), incense, black pepper and a very powdery-amber.

Unlike the EdT, which focuses mostly on the cedar and has some resemblance to CdGs Wonderwood, the EdP opens with a little lime and ginger and dries down to a rich and creamy sandalwood with only hints of cedar, a little bit of coconut and amber. The sandalwood is clearly of the Mysore kind and comes out very lovely.

My grandfather and grandmother have a farm next door to where I live, and although they weren't farmers themselves, the farm was once used for its original purpose. I used to go there every weekend when I was a child, but now it's a bit more complicated as I live on the other side of the country.

Tam Dao is not for everyone as it takes woodiness to the extreme. However, if you love woody scents, you must get your nose on this. Diptyque excels at making restrained “natural” smelling scents. Personally I love it as it manages to be both dry (cedar) and creamy (sandalwood) at the same time. It’s much more cedar than sandalwood, though.

Overall this scent is laconic and soft; easily wearable in my opinion. At first spray on skin all I got was sharp coriander (which was honestly off-putting for me personally.) Within minutes on skin it begins to warm up in the best way, and over time settles down to a dry, powdery, spiced sandalwood.

I was convinced that I was smelling a rich, natural jasmine in the opening of Diptyque DO SON, but jasmine is not listed among the notes. The note in question does not smell to me like orange blossom (which is listed), as it is not at all sweet. To my nose this is a big white flower bouquet, with tuberose as only one of the participants. I definitely do not regard DO SON as a tuberose soliflore, so it doesn't make a lot of sense to compare this composition to FRACAS, CARNAL FLOWER, and BEYOND LOVE, since it's in a completely different category. Someone has compared DO SON to Estée Lauder Private Collection TUBEROSE GARDENIA, which makes much more sense to me, since that creation has at least as much gardenia as tuberose--if not more. Needless to say, DO SON is a white-flower-lovers only perfume. Don't even think about getting near this powerhouse unless you are prepared to dive into a billowy abundance of white flowers! DO SON is like a huge feather bed built from white flower petals. They are soft and silky and slightly cool against the skin, and their scent fills the entire room. There is not a speck of dirt anywhere on this petal bed--it's as clean as can be, not at all sharp, and more fresh than creamy. ** Solid perfume compact review: Today I am testing the eau de parfum, but I own the solid perfume of DO SON, and I must say that it is a delight on all fronts. In fact, Diptyque's solid compact is probably my favorite of those of various houses which I own and have seen. (Putting Miller Harris, the worst of the worst packagers of solid perfume, to shame!) The vessel is a glossy black enamel covered metal with an engraving of the house graphic on the top which snaps onto the bottom half. The compact comes in a gray felt-like fold-over sleeve and is sold in an attractive black box. The presentation is incredibly sleek and weighty and, equally important, the texture and strength of the solid perfume are perfect. I've tried some concrets which are too hard and others which are too soft, but this one is just right. I highly recommend the solid format from this house. The black enamel-coated metal case would be worth having to look at and touch even if it had no perfume inside!

Diptyque described it as a "light, airy tuberose". I find that to be true. I get the whole living plant, still young. The opening suggests early morning dew on the petals and surrounding greenery, the drydown speaks more of a swealtering late afternoon when the only coolness to be found is on the river bank, where the tuberose are growing. Absurdly pretty and evocative, I find this fragrance gorgeous and enveloping, but light, like a thin gauzy veil with remnants of white flowers on the fabric. Good lasting power, too.

I am somewhat taken aback by how fresh and green this fragrance is. I find Do Son to be a very natural interpretation of tuberose and orange blossom, with an interesting and unique watery accord, which leans slightly towards an aquatic. For those that like their florals fresh and clean, Do Son would make an excellent choice for Spring and Summer wear. It's very likable in the way that the composition remains straight-forward and simple. While for some its basic nature may be off-putting, I find it quite refreshing that Do Son doesn't feel the need to constantly surprise me. While I enjoy smelling Do Son in my surroundings, it's not the kind of white floral that suits my personal tastes. Its light and crisp feel unfortunately reminds me of an air freshener. I can't seem to shake off this connection. The drydown, while still quite watery and floral, introduces a beautiful white musk accord. This blend smells rather comforting on the skin. I am pleased to say that Do Son holds its strength from beginning to end. A true sillage Queen. The overall feel that I get from Do Son is not unlike a Spring garden after rainfall, or an antique bathroom stocked with powder and floral soaps. It's a relatively 'pure' fragrance, hardly the suggestive type. Do Son's longevity is superb, and while I do enjoy the house of Diptyque, I am hoping that further exploration of this brand will lead me to something that doesn't remind me of an air freshener, which is not something that I aspire to smelling like.

With its sea-breeze note in in the opening, Do Son delivers that mini-vacation experience. Perhaps not all the way to Halong Bay, but at least a sunny place with salty ocean air and sand between your toes. The white florals in the opening are strong, heady. At the same time the whole is lightened up with a salty, airy breeze. This marine note fades after a while and the white florals remain. The jasmin-tuberose becomes orange blossom-tuberose, so that Do Son stays on the fresh side. Diptyque has successfully implemented salty freshness into a white floral composition, giving it a summery and fairly exotic touch. Shampoo and tanning lotion vibes are carefully avoided, thankfully.

An outstanding note of Do Son is Jasmine. It reminds me of the garden full of fresh bloomed floral in the morning. The scent is not too strong and it lasts long for more than 5 hours before it is faded and the feeling when you wear this perfume is warm and lively. It is the perfect choice for leisure occasion in summer.

I have Do Son EDT and EDP, each on a separate wrist. The EDT is a true white floral. It’s brighter with a more energetic personality than the parfum version. This one wants to be known and feels like it’s leaping off your skin for attention. Jasmine can sometimes be too sharp or soapy for me, but there’s a softness here that’s lovely.

This EdT smells like walking through a rainforest near the ocean and smelling the humid breeze of very fresh green leaves and white flowers. There is no smell of forest dirt or humus, though.
