I assume it's role is to temper everything. There are no sharp edges or green curves, and it smells borderline gourmand. The rhubarb doesn't technically go away, it just lifts off bit by bit over the hours. I would consider this fragrance to be linear in nature up until the end of its lifetime. The benzoin here is the same as in Benjoin 19 and Benjoin Bohème . B19 is a stripped back sweet Benjoin, and Lazulio is if you took it and added rhubarb on top. Benjoin Boheme is only similar in that they both have this caramel-like sweetness and that is where the similarities end. They are not similar AT ALL otherwise. Near the end, Lazulio is a benzoin perfume. The rhubarb keeps it interesting throughout, and I personally think it's its saving grace. I don't like Benjoin 19 by Le Labo, because I think it's boring. Lazulio is very, very pleasant. It is sweet, a bit earthy, doesn't smell synthetic, et cetera et cetera. I wish it was cheaper. I really do. I don't understand why this of all things is so expensive. It's not better than the normal Diptyque EDP lines. It's not stronger, it's not cooler, it doesn't use a cool exclusive ingredient to warrant it's price. All it is is fragrance profile that Diptyque hasn't made before, put inside of a new, flimsy looking bottle, and sold as an artist's interpretation of something that isn't perfume: a peacock's feather. I really really like the fragrance. I wish it was along the lines of Fleur de Peau or Tempo, delivery wise. That would've been awesome.

I first caught a whiff of this on someone else and for a moment thought it was Encelade, before learning it was a Diptyque fragrance by Quentin Bisch and before I knew what the notes were. When I tried Lazulio on my own skin, I discovered it’s much more floral and airy and far less woody and dense than Encelade. Still, the rhubarb + vetiver combination and that unmistakable Quentin Bisch signature are definitely there. The opening struck me as pleasant and easy to wear. The rhubarb, vetiver and rose are all clearly present in equal measure. For some, this balance might come across as a little too straightforward, especially if you enjoy hunting for hidden nuances in more complex, non-linear fragrances. But I can’t deny it’s a well-blended trio on top of the benzoin and a genuinely nice composition. At first, I didn’t get much of that vintage, powdery Diptyque character. Only after about half an hour did the rose start to shine more, bringing in a touch of that classic Dyptique feel. I particularly like that the tart, syrupy quality seems to come solely from the rhubarb, while the rose avoids any jamminess. Instead, it feels soft, dewy, creamy and velvety and it provides a beautiful counterpoint to the fruitiness of the rhubarb. The heart of Lazulio is where it’s at for me: an elegant blend of rhubarb, rose, vetiver on a base of warm benzoin. Unfortunately, the drydown (after 2–3 hours) veers back into familiar Quentin Bisch territory; glossy, metallic, almost Ganymede-like, which just isn’t my style. In short: Lazulio opens like an airy, floral take on Encelade, has a truly lovely heart, but ultimately dries down to something too Bisch-coded for me personally. Find me on Instagram for more scent thoughts @melanie.buist

A feathery rhubarb bouquet, dusted with resin. The opening is one of the most convincing rhubarbs I’ve ever met, and also one of the most convincing… cannabises(?) Must be something about the tart herbals paired with the vetiver, or maybe it’s how some rhubarbs play with my nose. (Gumamina’s Odette opens like a grapefruit edible to me). However, on skin, this completely vanishes within fifteen minutes to be replaced by a polite, roseate tea parlour scent. On fabric, a weedy ghost still lingers above the roses. If anything, Lazulio gave me an insatiable yearning for Prada’s Infusion de Rhubarbe (more candy, more carbonation - think flamingo pink) and got me re-spritzing with my beloved Odette (more tangy, more baby – think blush pink). If I had to call Lazulio a hue it’d be “dusty rose.” My synesthesia is at odds with Diptyque’s creatives, as Lazulio reads very coral and ivory to my nose, while Corail Oscuro gave me emerald and sapphire. Don’t get me wrong; I don't hate Lazulio. I’m just already betrothed to two other rhubarbs. Mental Snapshot: A floral-festooned drawing room, iced with curlicued moulding and padded with tufted silk. Beyond the lace-curtained windows, albino peacocks bask in the rose gardens. The Marchioness reclines on her divan and lights a fat blunt. tl;dr: Maryjane Austen

This Lazulio is a total flop for my nose. An acrid, sour scent that's absolutely vile and which made me wrinkle my nose right away; that’s clearly the rhubarb talking. I almost get a sweaty vibe from it, and honestly, I won’t be able to tolerate it on my skin for long - a proper wash is definitely in order. Rhubarb is notoriously hard to tame, whether in pastry or in perfumery. Here, it completely misses the mark, at least for my personal taste.

I’ve heard that you are supposed to combine the freshness of Tilia with the zest of "Delina (Eau de Parfum) | Parfums de Marly," and I promptly had to get a sample. This mixture just sounded too good… Thanks to the Parfumo Souk, I can test you no later than 48 hours later. I spray you on and immediately find myself mentally sitting on the terrace of a restaurant in the best weather and sunshine, drinking an ice-cold rhubarb spritzer. The zesty-bitter note lingers for quite some time - it’s not as short-lived as I feared… Now is not your time yet, but I’m already looking forward to you in spring. You simply bring good vibes!

That's how it should be. A friend's heart truly opens up to green scents. Let's take a stroll through the garden. First of all, gardener Pötschke has trimmed the greenery to a manageable height with the hedge trimmer. It could be ivy, boxwood, or even the ground elder that has spread out in the garden. The fact is, freshly cut brush is in the air. Juicy fresh, with a grassy touch. Let's stay in this garden and imagine ourselves in the rose bed. Fresh dew-kissed rose petals join the green section and give the scent a slightly soapy nuance. Well, if that isn't something! At this moment, the scent reminds me of Yardley's Heritage Collection Geranium. And the best part always comes last, when a gentle wood note adds a soft, rounded touch, and we take a brief seat on the woodpile behind the shed to admire the garden in all its glory. Eau Plurielle is by no means a thin little water, It is available in a large bottle, but I believe this scent has perfume quality. It lasts and lasts and lasts. The great thing about it is, as the name suggests, that it can be used in various ways. As a body spray, room fragrance, and even as a laundry scent. And I can tell you, I will make ample use of it. Diptyque has created a cheerful, friendly all-rounder here, that is never too much, but so delightful that I can't get enough of it. And then Diptyque has done everything right with their 200 ml bottle.

L' Interdit -- Forbidden. This review is for L'Interdit II EdT. Top Notes: Strawberry. Heart Notes: Bulgarian Rose, Jasmine, Freesia, Violet, Sunflower, Ylang-Ylang. Base Notes: Musk, Sandalwood, Incense. I recently purchased a bottle of this in what I believe is the newer formulation, a 3 2/3 oz EdT in the tall bottle with a metal cap that is quite similar to the bottles used for Ysatis and Organza. I could not stop myself from spritzing it right away as I am so enamoured with Givenchy's Ysatis and Organza, and overall I am quite impressed with L' Interdict as well, although it is vastly different from both Ystatis and Organza. I have worn it several times thus far, and my impressions are as follows. It is a gorgeous fruity, floral, woody, musky but CLEAN fragrance with NO patchouli--a welcomed difference. It is VERY feminine; very soft; and, very fruity upon initial application. Then it soon turns much more floral. I think the sillage, projection, and longevity on this one will be one of my worst, though, possibly worse then the current Apres L'Ondee EdT, but I hardly expected it to be a powerhouse, a heavy hitter like Opium for example. It is simply not that sort of parfum. It is the type of fragrance that once one gets a sniff of it, however, one would want to move in much closer to the wearer in order to get a better sniff. : ) I definitely get a fresh, red, JUICY but tart strawberry in the top. Then it quickly dries down to sandalwood and musk with hints of rose and probably violet peeking through the sandalwood and musk. It seems to be very well blended. I cannot tease out any sunflower, freesia, jasmine, or incense, and I definitely do not detect any ylang-ylang which is a note I truly enjoy. My nose it pretty untutored overall, though, so I may be missing some of the notes that more experienced noses could readily discern. L' Interdit has something of a "perfumey" vibe about it. It does not smell like any currently made accessibly priced fragrances of today which all tend to smell fairly sweet to my nose. This composition definitely seems to have a vintage vibe to it if compared with, for example, Madonna ToD Naked which is quite heavy on the honeysuckle, vanilla orchid, and peach blossom notes, and is thus quite sweet. L' Interdit's sweetness is of a different variety---it is less artificial, less synthetic, truer to nature, and I LIKE THAT about it! Within thirty minutes of application, L' Interdit pretty much begins to lean toward becoming a skin scent, albeit a very feminine, floral one. Projection could not be more than a foot at that point as far as I can tell, and I imagine sillage is very soft indeed. A heavier hand is definitely possible with this one. Thirty minutes after application, it is slightly woody, quite floral, but not at all either sugary sweet or balsamic. Actually, the strawberry makes it smell more tart than sweet from the very beginning. Overall, I really like it, and I am not at all sorry I bought it blind. It seems VERY spring/summer like to me, very fresh and very French. I do not think this L' Interdit would perform as well in cold weather, but I could be wrong. It is pretty warm here again today as I wear this parfum. In my opinion, L' Interdit is a fairly light, woody, fruity, floral that has a fresh, young, French vibe to it. I doubt anyone could possibly find this fragrance offensive. I believe it would work for both daytime and night time wear in virtually any environmental setting, including around children and/or elderly people. I think it would work well on a woman of just about any age, too. Although it is not synthetically sugary sweet, I bet its natural, authentic floral sweetness would attract bees and wasps if one wears it out of doors! Definitely recommend this one if you like fresh florals with a woody, musky base. Fragrance: 8.5/10 Sillage: 3/10 Projection: 3/10 Longevity: 4/10 All in all, this is another successful blind buy for me, and although I could not claim that this is a "sexy" fragrance, I definitely think it is a very cuddly fragrance that gentlemen would appreciate smelling on their ladies. As a floral, it is MUCH more sophisticated smelling than the florals from the very early 20th century. Definitely not a soliflore. Definitely VERY FRENCH. It leans toward the demure but very feminine side of the spectrum. I do not think this fragrance is unisex at all, though. Sorry gentlemen. ETA: In the very deep dry down, L'Interdit smells a little bit powdery but not overwhelming so. I am quite taken with this lovely fragrance. : )

I got it as a gift at the beginning of my collection. I never smelled anything quite like this before... To me L’autre is an Indian cook working in a crowded , full of steem, small kitchen , he’s on the third round of curry already, he sweated once, the heat in the kitchen dried him, he sweats again and he didn’t even had a shower in the past 48 hours... Of course I didn’t liked it when I got it, but I admired sincerely the fact that there is someone in the world that knows how to put things together to help me visualize a full, complete scene from a movie.

I was waiting to try it for weeks and then found here. I have no expectations as I never have contact with 70s formula. And yes, that is an adventure. Nobody is creating such fragrances these days, it is really unique. And not for wearing, at least for me. Let me be straight-forward: it is like going for a delicious curry to your fav Indian bar. Everything what stays afterleaving on your hair and clothes- you will fine in this beautiful bottle. The way all the ingredients mingle and make each other complete is just a wonder, however it is strong and can be not beatable esp in the first seconds. If you like cumin or caraway and you haven’t tried this perfume, then you know nothing about spicy fragrances

Every time I went to the Diptyque store, I smelled this fragrance. For years, I thought it smelled like a sweaty man at a Middle Eastern grocery store. It reminded me of Alexander McQueen Kingdom from the early 2000's. I went about my life with other fragrances and have now come around to appreciate L'Autre. I started getting bored with perfumes and L'Autre was suddenly much more interesting. It really is different! It's not trying to please anyone, it's more of an experimental art of expression. The opening is very much as I first experienced it, citrus and cumin, but it changes in a short amount of time into a fresh spice rack. It smells like a sexy kitchen. After many hours, it's a gently sweet, barely there patchouli. As with most Diptyque, smelling this on a card will give a totally different fragrance as opposed to on your skin. It's much better on skin. I lament that there are no samples given for this fragrance! I decided one day to go to the boutique and liberally use L'Autre not just on me, but on my partner as well. That was how I found out I love this fragrance on my partner more than on myself. I do wear it. It has such a nice dry down on my scarves. I bought it to spray on my partner who doesn't care about fragrance and I don't regret it. I think it is a wonderful fragrance on its own, but if you are feeling experimental, try layering with L'Eau des Hespérides and tell me what you think! *Edit to say do not layer it with L‘Eau Hesperides! Things went south very quickly and got soapy.

Finally received... the package from Paris with Diptyque's herb bouquet from the early 70s is on my table. Carefully, I worked out the completely intact cardboard packaging wrapped in foil from the transport protection made of x+n layers of bubble wrap, and I can hardly wait to finally get acquainted with "the Other"... Wow..... this is going to be love at first sniff, rarely have I been so instantly fascinated by a fragrance as I am by this one.... The cardamom note is very dominant, but in combination with clove, pepper, and in my opinion lavender as well as rosemary, it is absolutely harmonious. The scent gains even more spice and balsamic depth after an initially spicy-fresh opening. Patchouli and for me also a distinctly noticeable benzoin note round off this masterpiece with a resinous finish. ABSOLUTELY TOP CLASS!!! Unfortunately, it is no longer listed on the official Diptyque homepage, hopefully, they will remember this great formula a little at Maison 34, Boulevard Saint-Germain.

This fragrance has moved in with me while my previous commentator has moved out. I am very pleased about this and feel inspired to add a comment here to share my scent impressions as the female part. This is still the fragrance in the square bottle; I don't know if the scent in the now oval bottle smells the same. For me, the scent starts off lemony fresh after spraying. Whether it is verbena, lemon verbena, or ginger, I cannot say, as my nose is not that trained. In any case, this scent note is not mentioned in the pyramid, even though it is quite pronounced. That’s why I don’t look at the fragrance pyramid while testing, but rather make my own notes. This fresh citrus note lingers on my skin for a long time, but after a while, it recedes more into the background and makes way for the spice of cardamom and the herbal scent of carnation. I do not perceive pepper at any time. When the fragrance then transitions into the heart note after quite a while, a note is added that some do not like at all. Namely, that of cumin, not common caraway as indicated here, but cumin. The two have nothing botanically in common, except for the name cumin. Cumin thus mixes into the scent experience, with its note that many associate with sweat. I do not want to contradict that, but it is not unpleasant to my nose, as it is not the smell of old dirty sweat, but rather a fresh sweat note that we all probably have from time to time, and which fits wonderfully into this fresh, herbal, spicy scent. Additionally, coriander joins in, blending beautifully into the scent experience. Nutmeg, I say no thank you in food as well as in fragrance, and I am therefore glad that I do not perceive it in this scent. In the base note, when the fragrance loses its herbal-spicy strength, it indeed becomes balsamic soft, through a hint, really just a hint of patchouli. However, there is quite a portion of benzoin, also not mentioned, but definitely detectable. I love benzoin, and it is clearly present, as already described in the previous comment. All in all, for me, it is a herbal-spicy and ultimately also balsamic fragrance. Its seasons are spring and summer for me. Wearable by both men and women alike, so ladies, dare to try it. Longevity is good, I personally place the sillage in the middle range, but I am also pain-free in this regard; others may see it differently. In any case, I am very happy with this treasure, which will surely accompany me often through the warmer seasons.

For years, I was convinced that Julia Roberts and Brad Pitt would make the perfect couple, because they both looked like mice to me. Alas, it was not meant to be, I suppose. They are both married to other people and breeding like rabbits, but who knows what the future may bring? Since I am not the biggest Julia Roberts fan to begin with--indeed, I find her quite annoying for some inexplicable reason--I was not all that excited to get my nose on the new Lancôme fragrance, LA VIE EST BELLE, of which she is the representative, although her teeth take up most of the ad. I recall having read that Julia insisted at some point that no fruits be used in this, "her", fragrance. So it looks as though the marketing data won out in this case, because the composition opens with a fruity-floral pink patchouli complex very similar to many other recent launches. Or perhaps we can say that Julia's preferences were not vetoed, since LA VIE EST BELLE doesn't really contain any fruit. Whatever may have happened, this creation does indeed seem very similar to a variety of recent pink perfume launches, including La Perla J'AIME, well except that the big musk is missing here, and the patchouli is rather low key--at least by recent standards. The listed flowers are jasmine, iris, and orange blossom, but it's probably hedione along with other abstractions. LA VIE EST BELLE, however, morphs swiftly into another twenty-first-century hackneyed fragrance phrase: that pseudo-woody, pseudo-ambery "stuff" which forms the base of way too many perfumes today. It smells an awful lot to me like ambroxan, as in Le Labo ANOTHER 13 or Juliette Has a Gun NOT A PERFUME, and even has a tinge of what I have been thinking is oud in all of the oud-named perfumes, but perhaps I've been misidentifying it all along? All in all, LA VIE EST BELLE rolls a few trends into one bottle of pink liquid (that being one of the trends), and does not appeal very much to me at all. Abstract fruits, abstract flowers, a dash of patchouli (probably the only thing natural in the entire composition--but only because there is no cheaper synthetic substitute), some pseudo-woody, pseudo-ambery stuff, a somewhat sugary opening with a more unisex or even masculine middle stage and, as a grand finale, the opening sweetness making a come back in the drydown. Not for me. Lancôme redeemed themselves to some extent in my eyes by launching La Collection a few years back, proving that they could produce seriously good perfume. With this new bottle of gobbledygook, they've regressed to their former mass-market ways.

Top Notes: Black Currant and Pear. Heart Notes: Iris, Jasmine, and Orange Blossom. Base Notes: Patchouli, Tonka Bean, Vanilla, and Praline. I heard so much about this fragrance. According to my on-line research, it is the best selling fragrance in Paris, which I found truly surprising because after all, in Paris one can find every Guerlain, Chanel, and Dior in production, and all three houses offer outstanding fragrances. Therefore, I was very curious about LVEB, so I pushed myself to go to the shopping mall to test it. Although citrus notes are not listed for LVEB, I smelt pure citrus upon initial application, and citrus is all I smelt for well over half an hour---perhaps it came from the orange blossom? I soon began to wonder where were the sweet and warm gourmand notes everyone mentions as I could not detect any. I could not detect any black currant, pear, or iris, much less praline. Finally, after an about an hour, the base notes began to come through, and I was able to discern some vanilla and other sweet notes, probably praline. Projection and sillage were excellent. I could see that everyone around me noticed the fragrance on me, and I had only spritzed one good spray on the back of one hand! Longevity was outstanding to say the least. I could still smell LVEB quite strongly late in the evening before I bathed but after I had washed my hands a couple of times. LVEB has tremendous tenacity. I suspect it would last for days and days on clothing. Unfortunately, I am unable to understand why LVEB is so very popular. I certainly do not think the huge point of sale photos of Julia Roberts is what makes LVEB sell well. Yes, it is sweet and gourmand, which is one type of fragrance that I enjoy, BUT it smelt very synthetic. In fact, it smelt so synthetic that it actually made me feel a bit embarrassed as people noticed it on me. The only other fragrance I have smelt that was this synthetic was Jessica Simpson Fancy EdP, which I purchased blindly and then quickly got rid of it. If you like this kind of fragrance, then definitely go for Jessica Simpson Fancy as it is much less expensive than LVEB. I cannot say I hate LVEB, but I also cannot say I truly like it, and I would not purchase it even at half the price. If it were gifted to me, I might keep it just for the pretty bottle, but I could not imagine I would wear it very often--maybe only on exceptionally cold winter days. If I want a delicious, praline fragrance, I would use my Bath and Body Works Sensual Amber every time over LVEB. Sensual Amber smells so much better than LVEB, and Sensual Amber does not smell so synthetic. As a bonus, Sensual Amber is quite inexpensive, too. Some people have compared LVEB to Angel, and I certainly understand why the two have been compared, but I own Angel in both the EdP and EdT formulations, as well as Angel body creme, and I think Angel is far, far superior to LVEB. Angel does not have the strong synthetic vibe to my nose. I cannot say Angel smells "natural," but it certainly does not smell as strongly synthetic as LVEB, and Angel has a lot more development than LVEB. Therefore, if you want a sweet, gourmand with prominent praline/chocolate, my best advice is to try Sensual Amber first, and then try Angel second if you want to spend more money. If you want to stay within a low price point range, Sensual Amber is by far the best choice, though. Sensual Amber is so good that I cannot imagine ever not having it in my collection. As for LVEB, well, I am disappointed in the fragrance, but it does have excellent projection, sillage, and longevity. I only wish my Chanel Exclusifs had as good projection, sillage, and longevity as LVEB. Fragrance: 2.5/10 Projection: 10/10 Sillage: 10/10 Longevity: 10/10

~ This is not a review but simply one man's sweet first impression of this Lancome lady luv! I spent the noon time hour exploring new 'fumes when I came upon this pretty, popular designer. "Sexy, Sweet and more Sexy" is what I get out of this candy sweet gourmand! Nothing subtle here in my words or this scent. If head turning is acceptable in your world this candy/vanilla/praline scent will literally snap necks! I wore this on my masculine skin all day so there is definitely longevity and sillage to spare right down to the subtle hint of patch in the fading base now in the evening as I type. No fancy articulate words or evoking images with this soo seductive Belle just simply "Love!" Kind Regards, Plat ~ A side note when I first sprayed this it immediately reminded me of somewhere between coco~m & noir's opening dna....a true compliment to be compared to for certain.

It opens with some fruity scents then quickly dries down into praline, vanilla and patchouli scents. The praline is dominant. Though the patchouli tends to balance it with some earthiness, it doesn't seem to be enough. I find it at the limit of being cloying sweet even with one spritz. Plus I have difficulty to associate the fragrance with the supposed image of a 'beautiful life'. I'm not very inspired. But the longevity is 9h+ and the sillage is quite good. After I tested it again, I insist using it sparingly. Not only just one spritz but one litte spritz. This time I detect the fruits and floral scents much better and they helped a lot to pull the praline back from being cloying sweet. Originally written in 2013

I'm probably part of the target market for this fragrance so forgive me for being madly in love with this celebrity-associated, Flowerbomb mimicry. I can't help it: this synthetic gourmand fruit-chouli has so much cavity potential that it is absolutely delicious and addictive to me. And forgive me for comparing it to the Gourmand Queen - Guerlain Gourmand Coquin, but Gourmand Coquin was a somewhat disappointing experience for me after wearing La Vie Est Belle: I think that LVEB does the chocolate note better for my tastes and the longevity and sillage is better... less refined than the queen for sure but I've never pretended to be a refined lady. I'm more the girl next door than a elegant seductress. I love, love, love over the top sweet fragrances. Pink Sugar is right up my alley, as is Flowerbomb, La Petite Robe Noir, and Lolita Lempicka. I also love caramel gourmands like Molinard Vanille Marine and Laurence Dumont Tendre Madeleine/Xerjoff Lira. If these fragrances are your thing my guess is that you've probably already tried La Vie Est Belle and have an opinion on it. It's my absolute favorite in the chocolate-gourmand category.

Lancome La vie est belle is a very pretty, elegant smelling perfume for the younger set. I get the patchouli first, it's sweet and soft, not overpowering at all. It's a patchouli for beginners mixed with a candy-like flair. From beginning to end, La vie est belle is soft, never in your face, never too sweet.

I can understand why this is one of the top-selling fragrances, it’s sweet, feminine, and very strong. I use a light hand with this one, though. 1-2 sprays to the back of my neck and that really is plenty to get me through an average day.

I recently got a travel size of this at the thrift store. I actually like it! It is sweet but not sickly sweet. I think this is definitely a classic fragrance. It may be a bit overused or over hyped, but is that really such a bad thing? It can be okay to like things other people like. It has mass appeal and lots of people will like it on you.

This was my signature fragrance for many years. Got a sniff of it when it first came out, my mom had a tester and I just had to have it. Sweet, floral, fruity, powdery, patchouli, and most of all a vanilla perfection. My husband bought me a 50 ml and i wore it every single day, and I didn’t have to use more than 2-3 sprays.
This perfume was recently given to me as a gift along with it's miniature and body cream so I was a bit unsure if I would like it or not and I was partially right.

Wow. I love it. I’m going to wax poetic for a minute. I don’t know how to classify this scent. The coral here is a living creature, a chameleon. Marine-floral. Vegetal-mineral. Citrus trees spouting in a rosewater-spiked sea. Balmy, aquatic mandarin. The three chords I can discern are orange, green, and blue. Orange: imho, the mandarin is the star. I want to say the mandarin here hits the same note as The Body Shop satsuma body butter of my childhood. Eerie, sweet déjà vu. Green: I’ve always had a visceral dislike for jalapeño and bell pepper scents, so thank god I’m blind to it here. There is a bitter green spike to this scent, which reads chlorophyll-y to my nose. Like waxy, just-snapped leaves. Blue: I get a strong salty-sea accord. Not beachy/tropical, but more briney/oceanic. Harmonizes really well with the soft rose thread. Of Les Essences, Corail was the stoutest. This fragrance hit its high note straight out the bottle and played it strong and steady for over twenty-four hours. Three days out from original spritz and I can still catch an echo of it in my hoodie. I’ve never met a citrus that performs like this. My favourite Diptyque to date. I’m sorry, paycheque. Mental Snapshot: A stone-pebble beach, hidden off sandstone bluffs. Dappled sunshine through plump orange trees, clouds casting mosaics upon the satin blue sea. An Aperol spritz, maybe three. You’re a guest at the White Lotus in Sicily. tl;dr: 5/5 star Mediterranean resort, would recommend to friend

After initially writing a long-winded story, I’ve deleted it to say this: Corail Oscuro is ultimately a salt-accord scent with rose playing support. I suspect Symrise’s Sympep(R) is the major player here. I don’t normally like salt and mineral accords, and maybe it’s my bias for Diptyque, but I still find this a lovely scent. When I first tried it, it felt like a gust of warm air, slightly tropical and sweet from the mandarin. On the skin, the salt really blooms and takes centerstage. I think Alexandra Carlin did a wonderful job capturing that stony, yet aquatic quality of coral. It’s not my favorite of the five, but it’s interesting and unique to admire on someone else.

I love Diptyque. Other than Frederic Malle, they’re the biggest part of my collection. This new collection, and especially this fragrance, is almost making me swear off the brand for good if they don’t course-correct. Diptyque’s supposed to be about understated elegance. The fragrances are not overbearing, smell “natural”, and seamlessly blend into the background of everyday life, almost like atmospheric background music. Corail Oscuro is a synthetic, screechy mess that’s the antithesis of “natural”. It spits in the face of everything Diptyque stands for. One small detail that marks the erasure of Diptyque’s legacy: Lunamaris and Lilyphea do not have an “O” sound in their names. Every single fragrance released thus far has an “O” sound (usually in eau) as a nod to Diptyque’s ovals. Clearly whoever’s in charge of this collection has no love or understanding for Diptyque, just making decisions off market research. Diptyque seems to be losing its brand identity, its creative direction. It seems Diptyque is struggling to recover from the loss of Pescheux (RIP). Instead of slow, thoughtful releases, they released five fragrances at once, ranging from awful to mid. Their main lineup feels very fairly priced. At $230 for the quantity and quality, the EdP feel neither too expensive nor cheap. Trying to peddle far worse fragrances at $330 is a transparent money grab. There are plenty of other brands that release faceless mid fragrances. Stop trying to appeal to the general market. Appeal to your already-loyal customers instead of alienating them. Diptyque’s customers don’t want synthetic fragrances that last days on the blotter.

To me this is a strong perfume, probably because of the chypre. It’s all about floral and rather complicated to my nose. I honestly can’t discern between the Roses and the bergamot. Smells so 1990’s to me. The perfumes lays heavy on me. One squirt is plenty, and almost too much for me to handle. Unfortunately for me I bought blindly and have a full size bottle that I’m trying to wear every so often with hopes I begin loving it (or standing it). It’s headache producing for an hour. I want to love it, but it’s such a difficult fragrance for me. I have an aversion to oak moss, and it’s detected here. However, after an hour things start to slow down. The florals start coming out, not so harshly, allowing me to breathe again and enjoy the fragrance. Having said all of this, I wouldn’t have bought this perfume had I known I’d experience the discomforts of this scent bomb, but it’s manageable after a couple hours.

I decided to test out Idôle after trying out one of its flankers (Aura). I love going through originals and their flankers to determine the difference between them and see how they have evolved (and the thought process behind it all). Like others have already said, it's a nice citrusy, fresh rose, but there's not much more to it. I don't want to say it's basic, since it sounds insulting, but there's not much more depth to it. Idôle is perfect if you want to wear a feminine rose fragrance and not much else (which is totally fine). Since it is almost one-note, I'm pretty sure you could layer it with other rose products to add rose power to the scent or try and experimenting it with other perfumes for nice layering. It's not heavy or loud, it's not powdery and it's a nice floral with a hint of sweetness (probably from the jasmine). I'm glad I have bought a 10ml travel size because, although it is nice, I don't think I will be going for a full bottle. I've seen better interpretations of roses out there (I prefer the flanker Aura).

I usually don’t like rose, but it turns out I just don’t like it when it’s dusty or the main note in a scent. This perfume has a juicy mix of pears and roses, and there’s a strong vanilla accord that I can smell on the shirt I sprayed for six days after throwing it in the dirty laundry. Maybe I’m talking out of nowhere, but I feel like the scent kind of emanates a clean skin aura that makes you smell freshly washed and ultra feminine. This is a lovely perfume for any people who want to smell sweet and clean. It’s also not cloying to me. However, it might be too strong for an office with its insane longevity and sillage, unless you sprayed only once, very lightly.

Such a beautiful fragrance; an extremely elegant white floral and rose that's clean, paired with a vanilla bourbon base that is *very* lowkey yet pulls it all together. I think this is a fragrance almost any woman regardless of age can wear as long as their attitude is graceful and feminine. I absolutely love this one.

Many who already know me here know that I simply love the Lancome fragrances! :) Especially the la nuit tresor line :) I was very curious about Idole and was even more excited to test it! :) I was able to get to know and test Idole through a perfume sample. Admittedly, I am still extremely unsure about my opinion on this fragrance! It also reminds me a bit of Comme une Evidence L'Eau de Parfum by Yves Rocher (but only very subtly!). This time I decided to test Idole with my mother since I know from my grandfather that he does not like floral scents and would only say they are bad or boring... And I believe that would not have gotten me or anyone here anywhere... My mother, on the other hand, likes it a bit floral and fresh from time to time :) (which I can't really claim for myself :D) My mother and I dressed up nicely since we wanted to go out together; she suggested we could both apply a little of the fragrance and then see how it develops throughout the day. I thought that was a good idea! :) So I gave myself two sprays and she gave herself three :D. I must say that the H+S is amazing! It is perceived extremely strong and clear... I don't know it any other way from Lancome;)) So I will now simply describe how it developed on my skin and on my mother's skin :)..: On my mother's skin: For her, the fragrance was noticeably sweeter and softer than on me, in my opinion. I smelled a very beautiful and pleasant lightly powdery but still refreshing feminine rose note*-* The bergamot was also clearly noticeable on her, especially upon spraying, but then the note became lighter and more subtle... I found that much more pleasant! I could also smell the pear most intensely on my mother. It was not an artificial or piercing pear note! Much more a juicy and sweet pear that makes you want to bite into the person's wrist :D Musk gave the fragrance a certain something that I can't quite describe! All in all, she really liked the fragrance, which I could understand well! :) (No wonder it smells so good on her!) She gave the fragrance 8 out of 10 points... :) I also think that it smells very beautiful and special on her skin! :)) Now I will describe the fragrance development on my skin... On my skin...: So where should I start... I must say something!... On my skin, unfortunately, it did not smell as great as on my mother's skin... :(( Already upon spraying, I could smell an unpleasant mossy slightly sour note... :(( Which was unfortunately not a nice start for me! But well, you can't have everything in life! The rose note... it was personally too overpowering for me as it became more and more soapy and piercing... I would have wished for a lighter, more pleasant rose (on my skin) :( The pear note was the worst in the entire fragrance development! It was extremely synthetic and overwhelmingly sweet, which is a shame, I think! Since it was so beautiful on my mother!... :( The bergamot, on the other hand, was more bearable and pleasant. It took away the synthetic sweetness and refreshed the fragrance development :)) Which became more pleasant for my nose :)) Nevertheless, I realized that this fragrance is not for me! And once again, I learned how differently fragrances can be for each person! :)) But I must emphasize that the fragrance is not bad! But also not the newest! Still, I think it's better to test the fragrance beforehand and then buy it! Since it was not so nice on my skin, I give Idole 5 out of 10 points. H+S is, as already mentioned, very, very good! Idole lasted the whole day on my mother and also on me. This is very rare for fresh/floral fragrances. I hope the comment/text is well and accurately written as I put a lot of effort into it but also wrote it with great pleasure :) ❤

...this was confirmed today when I unsuspectingly took a spontaneous stroll through my trusted Dougi. There it was, the latest creation from Lancome, standing on the shelf like a phoenix from the ashes, framed by LVEB and the La Nuit Tresor diamonds. The impressive, super slim bottle immediately reminds one of a smartphone.

... and the scent on the hand. In the past, I always did the newspaper shopping for the family, as it also provided me with reading material. For Grandma "Heim und Welt", for Dad "Spiegel" and "Titanic", for Mom "Burda Moden" - and for me auto motor sport, Bravo and Fix und Foxi.

Now that I know what a "Chypre" is, I’ll say that this is not a "Chypre"! After skimming through some comments and statements here, reading some parts fully or just partially, and looking at the ratings, it seems that "Idôle" is more of an "everyday scent." Nothing special, maybe just "okay," or at the end, perhaps "quite nice," ...

Recently, I have been very cautious with blind purchases. I also haven't found anything I wanted to buy in the perfume stores. I became curious due to the comments about Idole. "Rose" and "Soap". For years, Chloe was my signature scent. My sister said Chloe smells like me. So, long story short: I ordered Idole blind.

With an order from the green D, I received a sample of Idôle, and my friend gratefully accepted it. She usually wears floral fragrances, which always suit her delicate blonde appearance, in my opinion. The scent did not reinvent itself after spraying and started surprisingly flat for the first few minutes.

My partner called this a lemony, Coca-cola like scent when we tried it in the store. I didn't get it then, but upon repeated wear, I'm seeing it more. There's something lemony, fizzy, and ginger-like about Rose Roche. Speaking in all honesty, it's a more dominant characteristic of the fragrance profile than the rose itself. Rose Roche might be built on rose, but when it's contextualized among the other notes, it takes on an almost unrecognizable quality. The ambrox (Firmenich's version of ambroxan, I add that note here not to sound pretentious, but for my own learning) extends the longevity immensely. I wore it before bed and woke up the next morning smelling it first thing. It also fills the house to the extent that my partner asks me not to overspray, lest he get a headache. As a Diptyque fanboy, it's lovely, but it's not my favorite of the Les Essences collection.

An unfortunate Jekyll and Hyde with my skin chemistry. On paper I got a delightful craft root beer: sassafras, ginger, and a lemon wedge. Truly effervescent, with a magical sparkly quality to the spice. Readily the most endearing opening of Les Essences. However, on skin I got something gnawingly spicy, which took to my sinuses like sandpaper until I scrubbed twice with dish soap. In this monstrous form, it became a tenacious and abrasive cardamom, ground up into a nostril-needling storm with desiccated rose petals. Can't speak on longevity, because I could only take an hour of it. While it does capture the raw, abrasive character of a desert rose, to quote the late, great Anakin Skywalker: “I don’t like sand.” Mental Snapshot: You’ve got a crush on the soda jerk at your local high-brow hipster haunt. Suspenders, sleeve garters, stick-n-poke roses flashing beneath their collar. They slide you a shiny copper mug. Moscow Mule, on the house. “But you mustn’t let them taste the passions of the flesh!” Your conscience nags. “Remember last time? You were lucky to escape with your nose!” tl;dr: Dr. Pepper and Mr. Migraine

Although "Eau de Lavande" is part of the "les florales - floral collection," this fragrance is definitely recommended even for those who are not fans of floral scents, as lavender, unlike most flowers that have sweet, heavy, and exotic notes, has rather herbal and green, fresh, almost camphor-like notes, with only a very slight floral aspect. Have I mentioned that I greatly appreciate lavender? And also Diptyque? Consequently, the announcement of "Eau de Lavande" raised my expectations, which were indeed not disappointed. "Eau de Lavande" combines lavender with various spices, of which cinnamon (which, in my perception, clearly comes from the cinnamon leaf and not from the bark) is the most prominent. This pronounced spiciness, however, never drifts into the sultry-oriental, as fortunately it lacks the unfortunately widespread addition of vanilla and/or tonka bean, and is always countered by the coolness of the lavender. Presumably, not only the lavender blossom was used, but also the lavender green. The overall impression is one of shady and cool, aromatic beauty, which also possesses a revitalizing warmth. You can never have enough good and convincing lavender fragrances, and "Eau de Lavande" is, in my opinion, clearly one of those.

I tested this perfume on my sister who has had a bottle for a few years. This scent is great, thick, sweet syrup. Very dark in tone, almost black. If colors had scents, black would smell like that. What surprised me is that in this thick syrupy scent I can pick out a few specific notes. When I smelled it for the first time, not yet familiar with the scent pyramid, the first thing I felt was licorice. I am very sensitive to this note because I love licorice and for me licorice is the star of this scent. There is also rose, very sweet, dark and intoxicating, you can also feel the earthy chocolateness, but mainly I smell the controversial licorice jelly which I ate as a child in Denmark and which many people hate. This licorice note is so strong here and I like it so much that I could occasionally go out with it to some elegant dinner or to the theater. I recommend testing it also men because it can look interesting on men's skin.

This to me smells like an alcohol-filled bonbon with a strawberry inside. It's also quite synthetic and the patchouli is definitely there. I do like the caramel in this one, whereas I normally hate caramel in perfume (Chopard's Wish has a terrible caramel note imo). The drydown on me is a mix between sharp patchouli and incense, with vanilla in the background. The scent gives of dark vibes and is perfect for cold temperatures. On hot spring and summer days this would definitely be too cloying and overwhelming. It is so strong that I can practically taste the perfume. It also lasts rather long on skin. Overall La Nuit Tresor is a like for me. It simply reminds me too much of boozy bonbons, otherwise this may have been a love. It lacks a little sophistication for my taste.

My taste is definitely changing… a few years ago I would have found this too sweet, but not now. I find this overwhelmingly delicious and a beautiful interpretation of the Black Rose. I have had the Tresor Midnight Rose, but it had the Raspberry note in the top as well, so it was too sweet-fruity. This is perfect. It balances so well with the Lychee Praliné, seductive and elegant. When I wear it I cannot help sniffing my wrist. It gives me such pleasure all day through, because this is a great performer. Endless hours of goodness, that is. Do NOT hesitate to try this if you like sweet gourmand fragrances! Year 2, 194/365

I tested La Nuit Tresor a while ago and was enchanted. An opulent scent that immediately drew me in like magic. But, you are all right, I already have Lveb and Black Opium here. The basic similarity simply cannot be denied. I’d rather go for a completely different fragrance direction if I have to spend money on a scent again. So the small sample was pushed to the back, and La Nuit Tresor was ruthlessly crossed off the wish list. Reason had prevailed. But, the dark side of the force comes relentlessly from behind and pulls you to its side. Whether you want it or not. Unaware, with no fragrance applied, I stand in a leather goods store waiting with my colleague for a saleswoman, while a beautiful, magical, noble, smoky vanilla trail wafts past me. Incredulously, I watch the wearer. What on earth was that, something so noble and perfect? The smoky, cool-distant, almost arrogant vanilla trail hits me a second time, and I am convinced that I have never smelled such a magnificent vanilla. It is the most beautiful flower in the whole land. I want to follow it to the ends of the earth. Now, as I said, we had another task, and the vanilla trail also had customers. So I left the store in love, with the certainty that I would return during my break to ask about this grand scent. At that moment, I was sure the answer would not make me happy. Surely a vintage or some extremely high-priced niche product. But, the answer made my eyes widen. La Nuit Tresor. Wow, my beautiful queen of the night. I hadn’t noticed you at all. I had you in my mind as dark fruity, warm, and caramel-chocolaty. That you carry the most beautiful bitter-cold, smoky vanilla trail behind you was like a revelation. I tested it again that evening, and indeed. There it is. The smoky vanilla note. On myself, I perceive the cool smoke much more subtly. The warm, skin-close notes prevail. But I don’t smell myself from the outside. :-P And right now it’s on sale. In a set with shower gel and body lotion for 38 euros. It must be fate. Away with reason. Bring on the most beautiful vanilla note. Or also: Come to the dark side, we have cookies.

Hey hey guys, how are you doing? Are you still sad that summer has said goodbye? Don’t worry, autumn has its good sides too. There’s Halloween, where you can eat sugary googly eyes! Or you can perfume yourself with wonderful autumnal scents, like here with La Nuit Tresor L’Eau de Parfum by Lancôme! Why this scent here? Because I don’t even particularly like the regular Tresors! Well, let me tell you this: There are a lot of crazy perfume enthusiasts here on Parfumo. And because of one such enthusiast, I was forced to test this scent! Here’s how it went down: Crazy Perfume Enthusiast: “Hey Don, this scent is soooo wonderful, you have to comment on it!!” Me: “Hmm, okay, I’ll do it sometime!” Crazy Perfume Enthusiast: “Nooooo, not sometime,… right now!!!…” Me: “No way!” Crazy Perfume Enthusiast: “Aaaaaaaa! Then soon, okay, OKAY?” Me: “Okay okay,… soon!” The next day: Crazy Perfume Enthusiast: “So? So? So? Did you try the scent today?” Me: “... you just asked me a day ago!” Crazy Perfume Enthusiast: “But for me, that feels like an eternity!” Me: “Argh, just be patient a little longer!” Crazy Perfume Enthusiast: “Waaaah! Hurry up!!!” Finally, the following day: Crazy Perfume Enthusiast: “Hu hu! Did you finally try the scent today?” Me: “NOOOOOOOOOO!!!!” Crazy Perfume Enthusiast: “Whaaaaaaat??? Screeeech!!!!!” Well, that’s how it’s been for almost half a year. And I thought, now that the days have gotten cooler, I could kindly try the scent for real. And of course, also to prevent the sweet but screeching enthusiast from completely losing it :DD And since I was in the city, the opportunity arose. I saw the scent on the shelf, but my hands were full of bags, so since I had accompanied my mother, I asked her to spray the scent on my arm. At first, I only got a few sprays, but I wanted more to be able to test the scent thoroughly. “Your arm is already dripping wet, why do you want more?” my mother asked. “I have to test the scent in every detail!” I replied. “And why is that?” my mother asked. “Because I’m in a fragrance forum. And for most perfume enthusiasts there, I’m a deity!” I explained. She then proudly sprayed the entire remaining content of the bottle on my arm, because honestly, which mother wouldn’t be happy that her son is considered a god?? :DDD So, with the contents of a quarter bottle on my arm, I walked out of the store and sniffed my arm repeatedly. And here’s my impression of the scent: The Scent: The scent starts with a delicious and initially fresh lychee note. However, sadly, a note comes in that I like a little less: orchid. It brings back memories of the scent of death (Black Orchid by Tom Ford), which I find truly repulsive. Here, the orchid is fortunately not nearly as intense, but it does exude a heavy floral aura. At least it doesn’t last too long, so after just a few minutes, the scent improves enormously. Because soon, the vanilla mixes in strongly, making the scent both sweeter and pleasantly powdery. Other sweet notes smell like a mix of praline and caramel and thus smell very delicious, hmmm… :) With the black rose, I present you with proof once again that I’m terrible with flowers… I mean, does a black rose actually smell different from “normal” roses? Because I don’t perceive a rose scent here. Instead, the floral notes that come after the orchid are not really identifiable for me anymore, rather heavy and thus autumnal, but perhaps it is indeed the black rose… argh, I really don’t know :D But let’s continue: It smells, as mentioned, increasingly sweeter, both vanilla-sweet and deliciously caramel-like. In the background, hints of fruity notes appear, which you can only smell if you sniff closely at the sprayed spot. So it can happen that you might perceive a slight orange, which then, together with the sweet scents, radiates both an autumnal and even a Christmas aura, which I naturally find great. Also in the background, there’s a bit of patchouli and thus earthy notes. In the end, the scent remains as described, mainly smelling of delicious sweet and powdery vanilla and caramel, with tonka bean added, which smells fantastic with the vanilla. The heavy florals are now more in the background, and the scent has a generally warm and gentle, but also quite sexy aura. A very beautiful scent, even if now and then a slight synthetic note can be perceived, which by the way becomes a bit stronger after about seven to ten hours, but is never bothersome. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is very good; the scent was easily noticeable on me. It’s even quite room-filling and should therefore be sprayed with care if you’re not going out. The longevity is very good, lasting longer than twelve hours. The Bottle: The bottle has the shape of the well-known Tresor scents and is therefore pyramid-shaped. It looks like a large, dark violet gemstone. A beautiful black silk ribbon in the shape of a black rose has been attached to the neck. All in all, the bottle is very beautiful, although the larger bottles are a bit unwieldy for smaller hands. So,… I have to admit that the constantly screeching enthusiast was absolutely right :D This scent is really well done. I usually don’t like the regular Tresor at all, but this one surprised me because it really smells good and very sexy, aaaah! :D In my opinion, this scent is a perfect going-out fragrance for autumn and winter, just to come across great. Yes, I’m sure you could really make a good impression with it, as it makes you look sexy and delicious, and… well, one would definitely want to nibble on the wearer of the scent and completely devour her, but not before giving at least 100 kisses :DD Want to be devoured? Then wear this scent. Want to enchant and captivate and then rip a guy's heart out and stomp on it? With this scent, it’s all no problem… *sigh* So, you can tell, I really recommend testing this scent… don’t let yourself be put off by the fact that it’s a mainstream scent with slight synthetic notes! Otherwise, you might miss out on something! And with that, I’m done for today! I wish you all a great evening, until next time! :) PS: All’s well that ends well? Pah… not at all, now I’m supposed to test La Nuit a la Folie too… *sigh* Sometime… :D PPS: And of course, everyone knows that I’m just joking when I call one or all of you crazy, right? I do love you… somewhat at least :D

This perfume is the most valuable item in my small collection. A few weeks ago, I discovered it while browsing and it hasn't let me go since. During the time between discovering and owning it, I could hardly walk past a perfumery without drenching my wrist and a test strip with this elixir. I could just roll around in it.

Yesterday I received La Nuit Tresor as a gift, which I gladly accepted, as I expected a midnight blue, mysterious scent in the style of La Nuit by Rabanne, which still ranks among my favorites. The little package promises: "A sensual night where lovers lie in each other's arms." Bring it on!

I was just in my perfume store and tested Tresor la Nuit EdP and the EdT. The EdT clearly falls short compared to this one, not only weaker, but also different and not nearly as beautiful as the EdP for me. The EdP smells gorgeous, more fruity than gourmand, very sweet.
( So I deleted my old comment about this scent because I just didn't find it good and accurate anymore!

It’s official! I have succumbed to the intoxication of scents. I assume I will find understanding among like-minded individuals here, but I will come out anyway. In my surroundings, I am often labeled as crazy for my rather unusual interests. Well, actually, that’s a compliment. I wouldn’t be me if the conventional interested me even the slightest bit.

And it’s worthy of the new $50 price tag (100ml). It’s quite soft on my skin, but the longevity is there (I get a good 6-8 hours). The projection goes maybe 1-2ft for the first hour or so, then it fades to a soft 6in-1ft bubble for the rest of the ride, and sillage is pretty soft as well, but the scent itself is quite nice if you like the sweeter stuff. It’s kind of a fruity vanilla that I get, with a soft hint of ambroxan. I will say that if I paid the full $90 for this, I’d be quite upset, but at this price, it’s a worthy grab. It’s a great up close, snuggle & cuddle juice, but don’t expect it to Bomb through at a bar or club. Some people compare it to Sauvage and Aventus, but I don’t get anything remotely close to those. It’s much sweeter and softer than both. I’d say check it out at Dillards or Ulta, and if you like it, grab it at TJ MAXX or fragrancex. Not for everyone, but good enough for me.

This is a well-balanced, versatile, very wearable scent that's a great value for your money at discounters, even if it's nothing to write home about. A little sweet, a little spicy, a little fruity, a little floral, a little woody, a little creamy, some pleasant vanilla, and a touch of leather. It's something you can reach for in just about any occasion, any time of day or night, and during any season, and not really have to think about it. Maybe not the gym or a beach/pool party, but other than that, it's an easy reach. You're not going to be challenged or inspired or transported to a different world, you're just going to smell nice to yourself and those around you, and sometimes that's exactly what you need.

Hmmm. Coach Platinum doesn't quite have the moisturising effect of Sauvage but it does a decent job if you're on a budget. Pineapple smells awesome (except in beta fragrances like Aventus) and it's no exception here. This is definitely a unique scent as you don't see this combination of notes too often. That cashmeran is off its head. Makes the vanilla overdose that I hate actually wearable. Can't believe I actually like something that is vanilla dominant, hope I'm not sick. This is nice to own because all the snobs hate it.

Coach Platinum opens up with pineapple, juniper berries, black pepper, and sage. Also, there is the ever present vanilla. It sort of smells like a spicier Dylan Blue mixed with Sauvage EDP, with an extra heaping of vanilla. Don’t worry, smelling like other fragrances, will be a common theme with this scent. I actually like the pineapple and juniper mix up top, its fun and delightful. However, the pineapple craps out pretty quick, and the juniper is left on its own. At this stage, it is a battle to smell like a mix between Sauvage EDP and Luna Rossa Carbon. It’s weird to have the Sauvage comparison, as there isn’t an ambroxan note listed. However, Coach Platinum does give off that effect. It goes back and forth between smelling like those two fragrances, for a while. Finally, it decides that it wants to smell like a version of Carbon, with vanilla, leather, and sage. The vanilla becomes the strongest note, with a smooth leather in there. The sage, along with other notes, substitute for the lavender found in Carbon. Gives Platinum a more aromatic spice, which I do enjoy. The vanilla and leather, sit on top of sandalwood, at the end. I have to say, this part is quite enjoyable to smell on my skin. I dig it. So, that’s it. Take Luna Rossa Carbon, add lots of vanilla, throw in some leather, and you have Coach Platinum for Men (for the most part). I don’t want to make it sound bad, as I like all of these scents, as well as Coach Platinum for Men. It is just that, I’m sick of this formula, that every designer feels the need to replicate.

This fragrance brings a classy, masculine edge that is super versatile. I found this fragrance to be a great fit for daily, spring, autumn/fall, and summer evenings. This almost copies the idea of a Pour Homme and gives it a softer yet light and fruity opening. This eventually makes Coach Platinum quite an underrated gem that could perform if you're searching for something versatile and classy yet still obviously masculine.

Personal: 7/10 – I like this more than I expected to. It’s warm, sweet, and woody with a slightly synthetic, almost metallic edge that keeps it from feeling flat, despite its weirdness. Mass appeal: 8/10 – Very approachable. Sweet vanilla and soft woods are easy to enjoy and broadly appealing, though metallic juniper isn't for everyone.

The original Coach for Men is undoubtedly one of my favorites for everyday wear and suits me perfectly as both an office and casual fragrance for spring and summer. A pleasant shower gel freshness blends with light fruity notes of pear and cake, creating a mix that is always appealing and inviting.

Coach Platinum is quite a successful fragrance. Unfortunately, it does everything well, but nothing really right. It doesn't fit into a specific direction. For the classification function, aside from smoky and animalistic, I actually indicated everything. At first, it smells fresh, floral, sweet, and fruity. Everything is very synthetic but not unpleasant.

I have had this Coach Platinum for a few years now, and it deserves a few lines from me. This fashion brand from the USA primarily makes clothing and items like handbags. This brand represents luxury, and the prices are quite steep, unlike the perfume department, which often falls in between designer and drugstore prices.

What can the most expensive Coach do so far? Upon spraying, a sweet fruit (pineapple, but not only) spreads. The longer the EdT dries on the skin, the more the fruity notes give way to the floral ones (geranium?), while the strong sweetness (vanilla) remains. The floral aspect gives Coach Platinum a certain mass appeal in terms of age.
Google images Castafiore to get an idea of the smell. An old propper rich lady smells like this. The oldest and the classiest one. This is an amazing creation that deserves all recognition.

I have organized another duel. I have struggled with rose scents for years. Most of the time, I get headaches or feel like an old lady. Rose is unmanly, my wife always tells me. Except with oud. So the wood is masculine and the flower is feminine? One could argue about that. Red roses. That always has something mature and is no longer so hip for the youngsters. Let's be honest. Fresh rose scents are sparsely sown and rarely really good or mixed with other flowers. Diptyque's Eau Rose is an exception. The "mature" rose scents that still have durability and quality to sniff out, there are already several, but unfortunately also unpleasant representatives. Two absolute highlights that no rose fan should miss are these two, which are quite similar. Today in my duel: Rosa Moceniga by The Merchant Of Venice vs. Essences Insensées (2016) by Diptyque. Both are for me authentic rose scents, as if freshly pressed from the leaf and embedded in amber or honey to make them last longer. It's all very feminine! Yet I wear them from time to time and receive the finest compliments. Both are long-lasting on the skin and radiate throughout the room without ever being intrusive. That’s quite an achievement for a manufacturer. Bravo. Rosa Moceniga is more on a vanilla bed and appears fresher, while Diptyque is clearly golden warm honey. Who wins now? Very, very narrowly Diptyque. It lasted longer and feels a bit wilder and deeper. Test it yourself. Men too, please!

I ordered the solid at Ludwig Beck in Munich based on the comments here - and I can only say, pure enthusiasm! My daughter is so taken with it that I ordered again right away. On my skin, the scent smells very intensely of roses from start to finish, and at the beginning, the red fruits come through lightly. I only catch a hint of the honey after a few hours. The longevity of this solid is very good; unfortunately, I don't know the spray version, as 100 ml seemed too much for me. The theme of roses from Grasse has been captured perfectly, the scent initially briefly reminds me of Roses de Chloé, but it lasts significantly longer than the roses from Chloé. I now wear Stella EdP in the morning and after an hour, I apply the solid scent from Essences Insensées - a - wonderful option for my nose! Stella and Essences Insensées blend wonderfully on my skin, creating shifting scent veils of roses - simply delicious! I will probably order the solid again - which, by the way, comes in a lovely pouch made of colorful fabric - so I can enjoy these wonderful roses for a long, long time. My grandpa had roses in his garden when I was a child, whose scent was similar. I am enchanted *g A little tip on the side for those who can never have enough roses: I apply the Weleda rose lotion after showering, then Stella, then Essences Insensées - and I am in a heaven full of roses.

As a young woman, I owned and loved Tresor for its sophistication and elegance and complexity and sparkle. Passing by the Lancome counter today, I thought to once again include it in my wardrobe. On a fancy, I sprayed Tresor on one arm and Tresor in Love on the other. Just like me, how Tresor has changed. It is now the screechy stink of rotting apricots left in the sun. It is absolutely rank, and it has been rank for the last 3 hours. It must have changed its genes. Or my skin has changed. Tresor In Love, on the other arm, went on warm, tea-rosy, powdery, blossomy sweet. After 3 hours, it is a sweet, powdery, dreamy, jammy-nectarine, woodsy delight. Much like my Kenzo Eau de Fleur de prunier - plum, which 50ml bottle I have just raced through as a favourite perfume.

I had a long-term relationship with Lancôme TRESOR, although I basically never wear it anymore. But whenever I catch a whiff of it, a flood of memories filled my mind, back from the time when Isabella Rossellini's image was ubiquitous. I approached TRESOR with some trepidation (for the purpose of writing this review), not wanting to disrupt all of my past fond feelings for this fragrance. But my worries were for naught, for I still, after all these years, love the sweet rose, peach, and vanilla concoction that TRESOR is to me. TRESOR, like it or not, was a trendsetter, perhaps the perfume that set off the explosion of sweet scents that have become so prevalent over the course of the past twenty years. TRESOR is an oriental floral in the sweetest sense of those words, for its vanilla infuses a slurry of pineapple and apricot--in addition to a double dose of peach--in which abundant rose petals float along with a few other diverse floral garnishes. TRESOR is oh-so-sweet, yet oh-so-loveable, a guilty pleasure hidden away in a cookie jar to eat when no one else is around... TRESOR may have been my first comfort scent, and for that reason I hold it in esteem, despite my belief that its allures are somehow superficial. But I still cannot deny, even after so many years, and no matter how hard I try, that I love the way this smells!

I love strong florals, even the headache-inducing, overpoweringly heavy ones. I assumed that I would enjoy this classic fragrance, however this was not so. When I first sprayed Tresor I had to smell my wrist a couple of times in order to clarify that it was perfume that I was actually smelling. It smelt like decay to me. Rotting fruit, wet sand, stale sweat and mothballs. I will add however that this was from an EDT tester bottle, so the EDP may be a lot nicer. This review may also be on one of the Tresor versions, so please correct me if I am wrong. Needless to say, I was shocked by what I encountered. A tinge of sweetness later on only made this fragrance more nauseating. Something tells me that this has to be a different perfume, perhaps even an off bottle. I cannot understand why anyone would want to wear it. In conclusion, thankfully, it's lasting power was very poor.

It is one of those perfumes that has all the personality that marked an era, without a doubt a tribute to the 90s. Inside it houses a majestic intensity, but with a subtle, delicate and velvety sweetness, like the skin of the fleshiest peaches and the petals of the most beautiful roses. It was the first perfume we had at home from a prestigious brand. In 1992 my sister went on a study trip to Paris and there she bought this jewel. I, who was 9 years old at the time, when I smelled it I was fascinated. My mother kept it in her closet, because it was obviously a present that my sister brought to our mother, but every time she left me, I sprayed a little of this perfume in my hair and I became the happiest girl in the world. . . . Later, in my teens, I also used it a lot, especially on special occasions. My mother left 7 years ago and in her wardrobe, in the same place, is this treasure, still with a bit of perfume inside, which she kept for special occasions and I can assure you that its aroma is still intact after 30 years. It brings back such beautiful and special memories of my childhood and adolescence, that I always have it in my collection. Trésor is a peach in its purest state, in its maximum splendor, at its most beautiful moment of maturity, surrounded by an exquisite floral group in which I perceive a velvety pink and a powdery tone of iris and heliotrope. The background evolves towards a vanilla that is not hostile and a soft, barely perceptible sandalwood. Personally, I think it is a perfume to use on special occasions, especially in cold times, but why not, also to wear it at any time you like to enjoy it (because it is a pleasure for the senses), for example, in front of a good fireplace reading a good book. As always, I speak from my sensory and personal experience. Obviously, there are opinions for all tastes and there will be people who this perfume gives a headache, as I have been told on occasion. That's why I recommend trying before you buy, because its intensity can be overwhelming. ....and if you like it, don't hesitate, you won't be disappointed.

This is the most feminine perfume in the world...It starts with the peach & rose presence involving sweet powdery nuances ....Soft and velvety stays at heart with delicate flower blossoms ! The drying down gets to the woodiness of amber and sandalwood ! I enjoy this scent because i love peach and rose combination in perfumes and this perfume is unique to this ! Romantic,powdery and tender.Three words that describe it the most. Perfect for romantic wear .It is long lasting.A five stars perfume for me!

I Think this has to be the most beautiful Bottle next to Chanel no 5 I Just love the coloring. it reminds you of the sun setting driving though the Fashionable Parisian district of Champs Elysees. Very Elegant. The first notes is very sweet Apricot Blossom Peach. and it dries down to Vanilla Amber And the last Sandalwood.

'Nose' Sophia Grojsman made some of my favorite perfumes, but alas, Tresor is not one of them. From all the pretty notes mentioned above, I only get wood that is burning. Not in a pleasant way like Cabochard or even Cabaret where the smoky wood sensation is teamed up with other notes that enhance and beautify it. No, it's a pile of moldy wood dowsed with bad fruit.

First of all, let me stipulate that I bought my bottle directly from Lancome's website, so I have no doubt it is genuine, and I am really shocked and disappointed by this perfume. This is the much acclaimed and much beloved Tresor??? How???? I think I must have sniffed the bottle in stores before, but I never tested it.
I tested today at my favourite drugstore the reformulated perfume: the bottle was in offer and it was disposable on the shelf.

One of the most beautiful perfumes of the 90s, in my opinion. Its understated beauty has stood the test of time, continuing to charm 35 years after its release. Trésor is a delicate blend of peach and powdery vanilla, with a soft touch of rose. The result is a velvety, caressing scent that feels effortlessly elegant.

Green, salty, cold-smoked herbs & a splash of Kiwi juice, a very refreshing, summery, springy fragrance that is easy to wear and can be used as a daily fragrance. masculine and very suitable for lovers of green fragrances. The most noticeable notes are kiwi, followed by rosemary and crystallized moss. To be honest, I also detect hints of ambroxan, even though it's not listed in the fragrance ingredients. The performance of the fragrance is above average, which was a surprise to me. The performance of the fragrance may last for several hours, perhaps more than six hours. - Is it a heat killer? Yes, it's definitely a refreshing herbal scent that's perfect for spring or summer mornings and provides exceptional hydration. - Is it a generic fragrance? Absolutely not. The use of the kiwi note is novel. I have not encountered it with such intensity in any other fragrance. - Is fragrance suitable for blind buying? Absolutely not; it needs to be tested before purchasing. Testing it will allow you to fully appreciate the unique blend of notes and ensure it aligns with your personal preferences. - Is it similar to the famous Luna Rossa Carbon Prada and Sauvage Dior? No, I don't think it's similar to the previous two, perhaps only in the ambroxan note that is not mentioned here. The bottle comes in a stunning gradient green design in the traditional shape of the Coach fragrance series. One of the biggest drawbacks of the Coach line is the atomizer, which is ridiculously made to release the spray weakly and leak when sprayed.

If you like the Dior Sauvage DNA you’ll like this. Coach Green is somewhat similar to Luna Rossa Carbon but not as metallic, and a bit fruitier, especially in the opening. The Kiwi note is barely discernible, and the fragrance tends to remain pretty one dimensional in the dry down, but it’s very pleasant. It’s a good all year round versatile scent. Longevity and projection is pretty average, so don’t be afraid to overspray if you want it to last. I give a 7/10.

I like the clean, fresh and green smell of the top notes made up of kiwi and green apple. The middle notes and drydown smells like eucalyptus hotel soap but it's actually the reason why I chose this for daily use. I just initially want to smell clean and not fancy during office hours. However, the performance is weak. The projection is average, but the top notes would last between 30 to 1 hour during summer (double of that during colder months). Due to this, I would usually spray five times every application. The drydown lasts longer than six hours in my experience. Also, because of the weak performance, I think it'd be good for field activities where I'd be exposed to the sun and perspire a lot so the scent would not meet the sun and mix with sweat. I bought the 100 ml version that comes in a thin cardboard box. The cheapness of the box is saved by the elegant bottle that is similar to a whiskey flask with rounded corners. It is colored by a gradient of greenness going clear towards the lower half, and with the Coach logo in the center. The leather tag under the cap adds an elegant touch. The atomizer can be closed by twisting it sideways.

Performance: 4-5 hours, more on the 4 side for skin, 5 side for clothes. Moderate projection in the first 30 minutes, then a close bubble for another 90 minutes, and it's a skin scent for the rest of the wear. Really an under-performer. You need to spray at least 8 times to get 5 hours out of it. Scent: There are two phases to this scent: the fruity phase, and the soapy phase. In the first 30 minutes, it's a fresh, kiwi-apple shampoo scent, but the sweetness pushes it almost into a candy direction. In the opening it's almost tangy in the way that candy can be. You get hints of the rosemary and geranium and moss and woods, but it really is candy-like. I don't think this is really a green scent because it's so sweet. But if it is a green scent, it's a green scent like candy is green. 30 minutes in the fruity, sweet opening starts to subside, and out comes the soap side of the kiwi-apple shampoo. Truly, if there's a kiwi V05 shampoo, it's like after you lather it and the soap side comes out as the sweet part goes away. There's nothing that special about this phase, but some of the "tang" does stay through the drydown. By the 2 hour mark, it's only a skin scent, and really only sticks around until the hour mark. I think this is a great crowd-pleaser scent, but it just performs so bad that I'd prefer some other fruity-fresh fragrance instead. Bottle: Fuck this sprayer. It's plastic in the worst way, and the part you put your finger on is skinny!! Who thought making less surface are for the sprayer would be a good idea?? And it puts out so little juice. The rest of the bottle is cool, but the most functionally-oriented part sucks.

This fragrance is a cheap designer beast omg. This thing is a fresh spicy sexy masculine kiwi beast. The longevity is around 7 hours but the projection is crazy I smell it around all day which for a coach fragrance is amazing serious is a must have. I couldn’t recommend it more. Reminds be of Dior sauvage but with a more tropical spin and better in my opinion.

This is a great summertime wear. . This fragrance is very simple but does its job the way you need it to. In the day time, you're looking for something easy to reach for. Something that's gonna smell good to most people, has decent longevity & possibly get a compliment. This is the fragrance you need. . Coach Green comes off, like a fruity/green like shower gel.

first 5 minutes are a synthetic bomb on my skin. after that, though, it smells pretty much like head n shoulders apple version. longevity is like 5 hours(projects around 1 hour, then its js a skin scent). man idk. bought this for 40 euros and im conflicted. i think its a pretty solid purchase and im gonna wear ts for school and as a basic everyday dumb reach.

In the 90s, some of my classmates' fathers worked at a nearby waste disposal company. When we boys, sweaty and dirty after a football afternoon, first trudged through the laundry room to take off our mud-caked football shoes, it smelled of cool floor tiles mixed with laundry detergent.

The scent is very clean. Almost nothing unpleasant emerges, except for a small slippery note that I also recognize from Aventus (and Fragr1Unisex4Evryb). A safe perfume if you want to appear well-groomed. I’ll ask around, what is that caraway/mint air that Coach Green exudes? From the rosemary? From the moss? Mentholated cedar? Wrigley's Spearmint fell into the pot?

… big impact. For me, one of the hidden gems in the lower price segment. Opening with a kiwi note, but also a distinct bergamot, it reminds me a bit of Drakkar Noir Eau de Toilette . However, it is much less strict and more modern. I read somewhere about 80s shower gel, and I can absolutely relate. You feel extremely clean, but not soapy.

A limited edition travel set that I managed to track down half way across the globe in my pursuit of the perfect tomato salad scent. The opening is promising - green, peppery, vegetal. There's almost bitterness and it's very rounded. Unfortunately, this beautiful crispness dissipates after about a minute and it becomes something so faint you have to really hold your nose to it and use your imaginations. It's slightly sweet, slightly floral, and faintly earthy from the vetiver. After an hour all that is left is a generic floral sweetness that has no resemblance to the juicy salad I was promised. The whole experience is like ordering a fresh Italian salad only to be served with a single salad leaf. It's a tease.

Venise is as if the velvety moss-muscled Masters of the Universe Moss Man toy found himself in a biergarten nestled in the midst of a forest of crooked pines &twining nightshade.
