Seating himself under the canopy of verdant flora, the green plastic henchman orders a moderately priced sampler of lambics and goses and other sour, seasonal ales (but he’s going to expense it to Skeletor anyway) and as he’s enjoying his tiny, half-filled glass of coniferous resin and lactobacilus-y fermented grains, he notices the plants stealthily creeping closer, surreptitious snaking sneaking vines with intent to strangle. For though Moss Man can camouflage himself in foliage and control all the plants on Eternia, on Earth he’s apparently powerless and our terrestrial vegetation views him as a threat. As the air becomes suffocating with the scent of sap-filled botanical defense mechanisms, Moss Man slips into unconsciousness wishing he’d actually ordered the full-sized stein.

EXTREMELY vegetal, piquant, and aromatic in the opening and the "Green Bell Pepper" accord has a bitter, indolic, greeness to it. What's odd is it later transitions to a somewhat rosy, floral, and green fragrance. So either my nose is not percieving this right or Diptyque isn't divulging the full list of notes. Just as in the case of their other new offering, Kyoto, the jury is still out on whether or not this is for me. And again, another HIGH quality offering from Diptyque.

Impressive. Warm. Luxurious. Gorgeous. Deep. Rich. Smooth. Perfection. Addictive. These are just some of the words that come to mind when I think about this beautiful fragrance. Decidedly one of the very best fragrances (and a flanker at that!) that Lancome has ever offered to us. (High praise indeed!) I can't find a fault with this beauty. It gives me everything that I crave for in a vanilla based scent. The vanilla isn't synthetic smelling to my nose but (to my delight), rather natural and the best part is that it's pronounced and stays that way through the entire wearing of it, never letting you forget that the vanilla is the star of the show. I can smell the juicy red currant and it mixes seamlessly with the vanilla. For me, that's what this is, juicy red fruit mixed with boozy, foodie, gourmand-ish vanilla. It is not overly sweet and is just so well blended that it makes you feel special and unique when you are wearing it. When your body heats up, this one gives off the most spectacular scent trail. You'll be fighting off the masses who will be lining up to bury themselves in you! They've managed to make a fruity/vanilla perfume that's mature, sophisticated and enticing. In a word, delicious! This is one that you'll actually crave. It deserves all the praise that it garners. The bottle is undoubtedly stunning, if a little impractical for storing/handling purposes (but I can live with that!) This fragrance was love at first sniff. Blind-buy worthy for vanilla lovers. Back-up bottle worthy. Unfortunately, it's not the easiest fragrance to find now. Here in Canada, they still sell it at Hudson's Bay (in-store and online) and on the Canadian Lancome website but I haven't spotted it anywhere else. It's also quite expensive so no back-up bottle for me just yet but when I can get a deal on another bottle, I'll be stocking up!

Everytime I wear it , many people notice it and compliments me for how amazing I smell.This is not a gourmand but somehow sexy on me,it is very elegant and is romantic in a maternal sort of way.This is a powdery amber vanilla scent that is sweet but not Pink Sugar sweet. Just right imo. The rose isn’t that prominent to me, and we definitely smell the fruity touch from the pear and black currant. I think this is “well blended” in the sense that you can’t smell a harsh transition from opening to the drydown. A warm, securing embrace by a large and fancy lady who is sweet and soft but also strong and supportive. I was disappointed when I heard the news that this is discontinued.

This looks like and is a gem to me. It smells like a sweet potion infused with redcurrant and spices. There is a cherry-kissed tonka bean sweetness and a magical red-fruit stinginess and twinkling feeling. The vanillic benzoin offers warmth and depth to the scent. The rose feels somehow chocolatey, sprinkled with cocoa powder, it sometimes even gives me chocolate truffle "illusions". Now if it could only be a bit more intense because what I get is so gorgeous that I can't get enough of it. It has a very strange property in terms of how it is perceived. It is such a deep scent that you have to look for it and go through an olfactory "digging" process. So the scent is potentially but not actually there and all the fun is about trying to "catch" it. Nuit Tresor a la folie is definitely a treasure worth to be found.

So, my fragrant little readers! Hmm… actually, more women will probably read this comment, after all it’s a women’s fragrance. So I’ll just say instead of readers, better you little reading mice :DD Today I’m coming to a scent that my perfume lady absolutely wanted me to test. And yes, it was the same perfume lady who wanted me to test La Nuit back then. She just wouldn’t stop until I had finally described the scent, and I thought that would be the end of it. But nooooo, she kept screaming because I absolutely had to try this La Folie here *sigh* :DD So, this has now happened, although as always in a really elaborate manner. The Tresor fragrances are sitting in a corner with really colorful or simply very feminine-looking bottles, and I always feel a bit shy about trying such a scent on myself. So, as usual, I went to the bottle, looked around, and hoped that the only lady standing in the distance wouldn’t come any closer to me. “Please don’t come closer!” “Please please don’t come closer!!” “…” “OH MY GOD SHE’S COMING CLOSER!!!” (and worse, even MORE women came, and even saleswomen, of course exactly at the moment AFTER I had quickly sprayed the scent on myself and was still holding the bottle…!!). Well, somehow I was smiled at by a few, after all, I was the only one who had sprayed something in the aisle, so I was giving off a very sexy delicious, but also feminine aura… I’m pretty sure they all thought I was… let’s just say, not heterosexual… but I’m a clever little guy, I knew immediately what I had to do about it. I pulled out my phone, pretended to look at other scents, murmured things like “what did SHE find nice?” and achieved what I wanted. While the faces of the saleswomen darkened a bit because they thought I was comparing prices online, the faces of the female customers became even more delighted, but not because they still thought I was gay, no, but now they thought I was looking for a Christmas gift for my girlfriend and that I must be a really nice guy because I was taking so much time to make everything right and perfect! If they had known that I don’t have a girlfriend at all, mu ha ha ha… that I… uh… don’t have… a… girlfriend… … … ;_; *seeeeeeeeeeeeeufz*… :DD Ah, let’s just get to the scent… The Scent: The scent starts fruity and powdery-sweet. At first, for a brief moment, the fruity notes (especially pear, but also a bit of berry from the pink pepper and currants) are in the foreground, then a powdery-sweet scent appears, which together with the fruity notes smells a bit like delicious fruitcake, but of course much more perfumey… but delicious is just delicious :)) The sweet notes mainly come from the vanilla, then a little from the jasmine. For quite a long time, it remains fruity, powdery-soft, and sweet, and everything combined just smells very nice and also sexy. The roses flash up now and then, but I must say that I hardly notice the roses at all. A little later, it is still fruity, but the fruitiness diminishes slightly as the scent comes across a bit softer and sweeter due to notes like benzoin and tonka bean. And it stays that way until the end, until in the very late base only powdery-sweet vanilla remains, which then lingers for quite a while. The Sillage and Longevity: The projection is very good, as one is enveloped by a large scent cloud that leaves a nice, pleasant scent trail while walking around. The longevity is also extremely well done, so that it even clings to the skin until the next morning. On clothing (e.g., scarf or jacket), it clings forever. My jacket still smells intensely of this scent, and that’s been over a week! The Bottle: The bottle is a darker and violet version of the well-known, gem-like Tresor bottles. A silk ribbon is attached to the neck, on which the name of the scent can be seen. The angular and square cap also looks like a gemstone, which naturally fits very well with the rest of the bottle. Everything is very beautiful, although a bit unwieldy. Okay, first of all: The eternally screaming perfume lady who constantly tried to push this scent on me was right. This scent here is great. Really, really great. Very sexy, very delicious, one of those scents where I would drool and run after every perfume lady and scare them away forever… *sigh* why does everyone run away from me? :(( In any case, the scent is really very nice. Especially for autumn and winter, it’s a great companion that you could use everywhere. A little less applied for the day, a bit more for the evening, as it also makes a perfect going-out scent. And although I, as a guy, constantly drool and talk about how delicious it must be for you girls, this time I was stared at with this scent,… unfortunately after I had fled to the men’s department after spraying it to analyze the scent in peace. Therefore, it was unfortunately a bit… irritating to be stared at by guys… argh! What the heck, definitely go test it, because I can definitely recommend it. Remember that with this scent, you could always be the center of attention. It’s just unfortunate that all the other girls might think the same, so that at the next party, 200 girls will show up with this scent, and then the one who might stand out will be the one wearing Alien (especially the new and also very great Alien Fusion), mu ha ha ha ha :DD He he, well then, I wish you all a lovely evening, a nice 2nd Advent, and see you next time :)

This perfume is certainly not the most suitable candidate for someone to try their first comment on. I dare to do it anyway, because alongside the abundance of comments, mine is not crucial, and because ... well ... La Nuit Trésor À La Folie and I do not have such a close and passionate relationship, but rather only come into (literally) contact on certain occasions. In other words, if I were "it" (La Nuit Trésor À La Folie) - I would feel totally neglected ... :( However, nothing comes from nowhere, and what we have, between us, has its reason, and when I look within myself, it is more out of respect than anything else. Through our interaction, La Nuit Trésor À La Folie embodies for me a special radiance and elegance and is neither an everyday nor a common perfume - La Nuit Trésor À La Folie is not hot in that sense, but rather like ice at first! The bottle made of thick glass appears almost massive, heavy, and very solid in - hinted at - diamond cut. The dark, gradient coloring between black and red is magically alluring, I feel like I am holding something extraordinary in my hands. The cap, in contrast to the bottle, is rather inconspicuous, yet very fitting, simple, and very flat, not disturbing or tearing apart the symmetry of the bottle. However, I see a kind of "flaw" in that it is not made of glass, but rather light and made of clear plastic, and thus does not equally transfer and let me feel the constant coolness of the bottle in my hand and fingers. Spraying left, right, wrists ... and then comes the reason why it is not such a hot love between us, because I perceive something smoky cold, slightly sultry, nothing sweet or warm is present. This may be the combination of the stated top note, and I discover something cool and burnt woody in it, perhaps from the base note. The first felt hour builds a certain kind of "coolness and especially distance" towards me despite direct body contact - I am not (anymore) looking to smell like À La Folie. Rather, it is like now and then through movements one makes, to perceive the perfume in its emitted peaks here and there, because À La Folie is and remains very close to the body. These "peaks" are then warm, slightly fruity, berry-like, and when I want more of it over time, sniffing again for the scent, I gradually realize how this cool distance fades and sweet, partly fruity warmth takes its place - the radiance and elegance still remain intact. À La Folie develops in its play a unique, special aura, which becomes more and more creamy, almost even feels so (in the mind) at the end. À La Folie is a special perfume in my collection. Compared to the others, it is not "straight" from beginning to end, but magically changing and remains enchanting, after all, it is the same perfume once applied. With À La Folie, I warm up anew every time, and I have long accepted that for myself, as I know no better going-out scent and simply play along with the melting game "à la folies"! Thank you for reading and until next time, perhaps! ;) PS: Formulating this here (also consciously for myself) in this comment has 2 consequences: 1. Adjustment of my rating by +0.5 and 2. out of the "Outlet" folder!

Yesterday, I tried Folie in the bustling Kstadt. This soft, full fragrance does not fit at all in this bright and loud location, as it speaks with a quiet, alluring voice, gently takes you by the hand, and leads you to a hidden place. Perhaps to a nighttime rose pavilion in the park - or to a secluded Chambre Separee of an elegant bar.

I have now tested a few fragrances from the La Nuit Trésor line, and I must say, this one is by far the best for me! I found the EdP really well done, but unfortunately, it wasn't wearable for me. The Caresse was okay, but that one wasn't good to wear either, and the EdT was rather disappointing. So, I didn't have high expectations here.

I haven't written a comment in a long time, but now I have to!!! As a packaging victim, I love beautiful bottles, and the Tresor fragrances are among the most beautiful for me. I've tried all the other variants, but they were all too "biting" for me. Something always bothered me. But La Folie... I sprayed it on my wrist during lunch break and forgot about it at first.

Thank you Lancôme, thank you for proving with this fragrance that the modern art of perfumery is not completely lost. I smelled this scent on a lady in the airplane. I don't know how much she sprayed, but her scent cloud was noticeable at least 2 rows in front/behind her.

Beautiful scent in a beautiful bottle! Right from the first spray, it’s different from the usual La Nuit. Softer and creamier. Vanilla and tonka bean compete with the freshness and fruitiness of the berries. For me, it’s perfect, sweet and zesty at the same time. I can’t stop sniffing my wrist.

There isn’t much to say about Demeter's "Mandarin Orange." Just imagine a blend of the white skin of mandarins and the popular canned fruits. "Mandarin Orange" is less sweet, rather bitter, and unfortunately incredibly fleeting. Yes, longevity has never been Demeter's strong suit, but this one is really short-lived. Of course, there are certain "tricks" to extend the longevity, but those are not an option for me. However, this fragrance is well-suited for layering. If you want to give a heavy, sweet scent a certain lightness, you can definitely try this. Provided you like mandarin. You can forget about sillage; close to the skin is the motto here. If you want something even more bitter, go for Demeter's "Pink Grapefruit"; if you prefer something sweeter and especially more long-lasting, take "Orange Cream Pop." That one is one of my absolute favorites from the mentioned fragrance house. I can only give a very limited recommendation. If you are generally interested in this type of fragrance... Take "Orange Cream Pop," as it has a hint of vanilla in it :)

This is one vanilla-based fragrance which I find utterly breath-taking. Hypnose is yummy and sweet without being overwhelming. This has no where near the same strength as Fantasy or Pink Sugar, to my nose this is light and much more grown up. This is spicy, but only mildly so. Hypnose is mostly soft and slightly powdery vanilla, jasmine, passion flower, vetiver and bergamot. I find this fragrance to be one of those scents that smell better on the skin rather than paper. On the skin it becomes very warm and soft, however on paper it can be rather sharp. The lasting strength and sillage are good, but I must advise you all that this fragrance should not be over-applied. Hypnose would make a lovely fragrance for the colder months and special occasions, however I would wear this casually myself.

The scents I am mostly picking up are the passion flower and some vetiver. We own some property out by a lake and there are passion flower vines growing on it. They smell fantastic, and I have always wondered if the scent was used in perfumes. So I was surprised and excited to find that this perfume, indeed had passion flower in it. Yes, there is vanilla in this but it's not a warm vanilla to me but kind of cool and icy with perhaps a little mint. I don't find the vanilla all that strong. Perhaps it's just me. With the first spray, I thought that this was too subtle. Boy was I wrong! In about 5 seconds the power of the fragrance shot out from me into the room. It's strong and has lasted now for several hours. It's fabulous!

My mother used to manage a Lancome counter when i was 14-17, so i am very familiar with most of their recent fragrances. When this came out i was given TONS of hypnose homme vials, and never really enjoyed them. I DID however sneak some of her Hypnose Femme vials frequently! ;) This is a primarily sweet fragrance featuring nuances of creamy florals, and soapy rough vetiver. The top: I get a mildy acidic bergamot, and mandarin orange rind(a generic start for many fragrances), and a harsh miasma de aniseed! :O If you're thinking the same thing i am, you'd be thinking this is VERY confusing already!...Almost Hypnotizing!!! *creepy hand shaking, along with wiggly fingers* The middle: The heart of Hypnose is primarily owned by an extremely powdery hard jasmine! Not that i mind, as i mention in many of my other reviews, i am a jasmine ADDICT!!! So if you are turned off by jasmine, head for the bloody hills with this one! Along side the Jasmine, i get a crazy dirty soapy vetiver, which is sort of like a good friend to the jasmine. Telling it to count to 10 before it blows a fucking floral gasket!!! The base: While being extremely vannilic, it is also remarkably barfy...Which isn't a bad thing. It's very VERY radiant...in all the WRONG ways, but smells completely RIGHT for this. Hey don't say I didn't f*kin' tell you this wasn't confusing. It's ok i'll see you in counseling soon. In the meantime, go out and enjoy this fragrance. Hell maybe even buy a bottle, it's pretty good! :EDIT: I had NO idea Annick Menardo had her hands in this, but now that i look at it, i'm glad i hadn't gone into this review with a biased opinion! She is the MASTER of sweetness!

I had it. I don't know why I bought it....maybe a special offer? I don't remember . anyway, after a few years I re-tested this scent and I found it too sugary. Not my cup of tea. Tastes change. The bottle remains a masterpiece, but what there is inside is something extremely sweet-synthetic. If you risk diabetes, don't try this scent!

I love green vanilla fragrances like this! Hypnose is sweet, warm and alluring without overwhelming syrupy sweetness that is everywhee these days (I am looking at you, LVEB and Black Opium!) Hypnose reminds me of YSL Manifesto, Guerlain's Angelique Noir, Dior Addict, also sweetish, floral, green vanillas that I can’t get enough of.

As a child I did not see my grandparents as often as I would have liked. They lived far away from us. But sometimes during the summer holiday, my father’s parents offered to let my brother and me spend a week at their place. And since they lived very close to my mum’s parents we often went there afterwards. Two weeks with grandparents - great!

Ooooh I see some people find Hypnôse too sugary, well I don't agree ! Yes, it's a sweet vanilla but perfectly balanced with the passion flower and with a hint of vetiver in the background. I always loved it and still do ! It has its own universe and absolutely doesn't resemble the new sugary perfumes of the moment. The bottle is magnificient, as is the name.

When I read the notes of this perfume I immediately went to try it on. On paper, it was a bit disappointing, beautiful scent but after a while it felt too much of a good smelling cleaning product vibe with a nice bottle. But; then I tried it on skin and I understood that I was wrong. It is a beautiful jasmine-vanilla with floral notes dominating.

and drove me back into your arms. I would love to stay a little longer and rub my nose against you. I need this sweet scent as much as sunshine and air... ;) Oh how I once loved this fragrance. About 5 years ago, it was my favorite perfume. No other scent surpassed Hypnose.

...have I only just discovered this fragrance? I was recently in the perfume shop and found the bottle hidden in a rather inconvenient corner, way down at the bottom...next to...I assume...other scents that are no longer so "in" and wondered what purple EdP smells like?! Well...I sprayed a little on my wrist, lifted my mask, sniffed it...

Coach sort of crept into my collection. I never paid much attention to it, since I got it in a great bargain with loads of gorgeous perfumes. When I finally got around to testing it, I must admit that I was disappointed. Loud raspberry and pear and not much else. That is not what I expect of a fragrance that bears the brand’s name. “Girly dreams” or “Fruit Basket” would be more appropriate and it would help me to steer clear of buying. Well, it is part of my collection and therefore it gets a review. But my advice is not to buy. 279/365

I used to force myself to stay in relationships that weren't good for me. You know, the one's where the chemistry just isn't there... But the individual is so cool/sweet. Somewhere along the way, I decided to be honest with myself. Staying in that relationship was not only a waste of my time, but it also it wasn't a kind thing to do to the other person. I also had to make that decision when it came to fragrances. I cannot tell you how many fragrances I tried to force myself to like... Sometimes because so many others raved about how much they loved it, so surely I HAD to love it as well. Or because I spent my hard earned money on a bottle... So I GOTTA wear it! But forced relationships are abusive. I feel this way about this fragrance. When it comes to this Coach fragrance... We're just not meant to be. Not because she's not a sweet person... We just don't mesh. I don't really like anything about this... Sadly, that's about all I can say. I will say that a 1 oz bottle of this looks so cute on a vanity, tho... That's about it... Shame.

I’m not going to write much about this perfume other than it has been headache producing each time I’ve tried to wear it. The raspberry is immediately harsh and stings my nose (pepper?). I’ve tried to single out the notes, but I can’t do it. We are opposites on opposing spectrums, I suppose. I always hope the next time will be better, but so far my experiment has been unsuccessful. It feels like many other fruit medley perfumes sold at the discount store. There’s nothing special here for me, so it’s time to allow this bottle a new family.

Yesterday I crawled through the city after an exhausting physio training and discovered in the window of my perfumery a little box with the inscription "Coach". Of course, my relentless trainer immediately came to mind, who had demanded unnatural contortions from me that still buzzed in my bones. No - standing under this impression, Coach aroused no interest whatsoever. But my scent fairy floated towards me with just this fragrance. My politeness forbade me to decline the offered spray. But instead of hard training, I was surrounded by soft wellness. Now I finally notice the beautiful carriage on the high-quality bottle that my displeasure had overlooked. I think of great-grandpa's old Landauer, which waited in the coach house under the riding hall. From time to time, I would remove the protective cover and let myself plop down into the cushions, causing the springs to squeak and gently bounce. How pleasant and serene it must be to rock through the countryside in such a vehicle! But there was often talk of harnessing, yet it was never realized. And I have no Antoine to whom I could command: Let the horses be harnessed! So instead of harnessing - better to relax. And the gentle scent helps me well with that. Pear and raspberry waft towards me on my mental journey - past blooming rose roundels. The soft suede rises to my nose, mixed with the noble wood of the valuable carriage. Nostalgic romance envelops me - supported by oval, sepia-toned photos from the old albums. An enchanting fragrance for those who dare to dream.

When I was younger, I always got to go with my grandpa to the beverage store in our village, and we would shop - mineral water, a crate of beer, juice... And for me, there was either a bottle of woodruff or raspberry soda. The former was neon green (back in the days when natural colorants weren't particularly in demand...), the latter bright pink. Raspberry soda made me think of Coach, which I recently sprayed empty. The scent is not an absolute innovation, but it is a lovely perfume. It complements the elegant leather creations that Coach produces. It starts off fruity and fizzy thanks to raspberry and pepper, and the rose soon makes it more classic and feminine. Coach is evolving, and I believe this is one of those candidates that develops differently on various skin types. It ultimately dries down to a woody and soft finish, and it lasts several hours on my clothing. The closure is a bit unusual, as it must be opened and closed by twisting - but it's actually not bad for a handbag or when traveling. Coach is not really playful or sweet, but rather a ladylike scent - yet still suitable for young women who are firmly grounded in life. It's the raspberry soda for grown-ups!

I like rose in fragrances and I also don't like overly sweet (!) berry notes. "Coach - Eau de Parfum" has some nice notes, I thought, when I checked the notes. Could this be something for me? No. Mega boring "fruity-floral" scent that we've all smelled before, one way or another. The beginning is definitely dominated by the loud, overripe raspberry. The pear adds to it.

I am working my way through my fragrances and samples. Here is Coach perfume. I had already seen the bottle at ..Türkise.. and almost went for it. Note that it is actually not particularly aaaaber it has a charm uiii new "trinket" for my key as my husband always complains. The shiny charm makes my magpie gene kick in.

The Moomins - friendly, troll-like mythical creatures with a hippopotamus-like shape - were not entirely unknown to me from my childhood, but apparently I was a bit too old for such series when they became more prominent on German television in the late 70s. I only just learned that the first books were written and illustrated by the Finnish/Swedish author Tove Jansson as early as the 1940s. The virtual home of the Moomins in the far north seems to have also inspired the Moomin perfume series by Demeter (alongside “Finnish Snowfield,” there’s also “Icelandic Aurora” and “Norwegian Wood”). “Finnish Snowfield” is, in my opinion, a delicate, light floral scent with hints of lemon-juice-spiced herbal tea. The association with a bright sun shining over a powdery snowfield seems quite fitting to me, but I also can’t help but think of the first spring flowers waiting for their moment to emerge beneath the snow. Therefore, for me, it’s a perfume for the waning winter. Moderate longevity, but at least it’s a perfume that is suitable for wearing and not just for “bringing to mind” certain scent images.

Although I rarely wear it, I admire Lancôme's Poème as a creation. This unabashed floral-oriental perfume has an integrity absent from many late twentieth-century perfumes and which explains, I believe, why no flankers of Poème have ever been produced. Poème needs no tweaking at all. The world doesn't need "Poèmette," "Poème leger," "Mon Poème," "Rêve de Poème," "Poème pourpre," etc. Poème is a perfume which deserves to survive in of itself and does not need to procreate in order to justify its existence. The opening is heavily floral, while the drydown is quite distinct and seems very oriental, in part because of the dominant floral note which somehow sneaks in to steal the show: the dark and mysterious neroli. The drydown is so spicy to my nose that I continue to believe--against all evidence--that clove must be among the basenotes, and this is perhaps why I rarely don Poème, since I have a low tolerance for clove, whether real or perceived. My own idiosyncrasies notwithstanding, I believe that Poème is a real beauty for real lovers of real perfume.

I finally bought it, lured by beautiful advertisements. It has a vintage feel because it smells full and rich, like a classy old lady. A golden honey scent with a little of linden, and after that very little change, it just stays on and does not turn nasty. It seems to be meant for special occasions and should be sprayed with a light hand. Most suitable for Fall and Winter - to go with heavier fashions - then it makes sense. The longevity is incredible. The scent stays and stays and will remain in scarves and clothes.

This giantess of a perfume is quite a difficult case to me. I guess that it's as hard to understand as its most profound namesakes, cause I'm sure that Lancôme didn't have Humpty Dumpty on its mind when "Poême" was chosen as a name. I was struggling with it since it was launched 20 years ago, and it took me nearly half of them to finally decide that I love the way it burns my olfactory receptors with its datura and narcissus mayhem, as opposed to its mimosa and vanilla comfort. And maybe this is the reason why its bottle always reminded me of a blasting machine, which of course would make a totally inappropriate vessel to contain a poem written with liquid gold. Unless this poem was a revolutionary olfactory manifesto. Well, was it? I'm not sure yet. Maybe Poême was never really meant to be thoroughly understood. Or maybe I was never able to handle its truth. Poetry is one of the most subjective forms of art humankind has ever created. Because it's just words, and this makes it just a fleeting whiff of air. Because you can't see, touch or hear it (unless someone is reading or reciting it to you, but this subtracts the personal connection). All other arts require one or more senses to be perceived, and they depend on senses to reveal their true form and meaning. Poetry requires just reading, and reading is not a sense. Yes, it also requires vision, but vision here is only the mean. It's the most private of all arts. But on the other hand, it's the only form of art that can quietly make you see, touch, hear and smell the things it deals with. Yet this befuddling elixir feels more like an incantation than a poem. But what it actually summons still remains a mystery. It's like a shapeless pulsating mist, which every time you take a step closer to it attacks you with such vice that makes you wanna run away, but when you turn your back and take the first step offward, it engulfs you with the most alluring and promising fantasies. Just like when you desire something with all your heart, but you're scared to death by what it'll take to have it. And all its qualities, whether good or bad, have a certain escalation. Like a poem which starts in a seemingly indifferent or incoherent way, making you think that it's not going to be anything more than yet another babble, and suddenly you find yourself sitting on the edge of your seat, enthralled beyond words, trying to understand what has happened and why you're crying. I have a very old bottle of this beauty, coming from the late '90s, and it has a deep amber colour, not unlike red gold. Every time I remove its cap, its olfactory assault hits me with full force, to the point of rendering spraying uneccessary. And in the rare cases of finally deciding to spray some on me, 24 hours is the minimum period it grants me its magnificent contradictions. Like stealing a full day and night of my life. I'm still wondering why such a successful and popular perfume does not have even a single flanker launched. And I have no answer to offer, except that some strange conjuncture may have decided that it will remain one of a kind till the end of time. I believe that it's the last truly great piece of high perfumery created by the once mighty Lancôme. And this makes it a landmark on the edge of "old world" perfumes. A last, yet perpetual reminder of a time when the most important asset in any perfume house was the lab and not the marketing department.

My oldest son was born in 1995. I remember being fairly sensitive concerning smells. All kinds. Through my pregnancy and after. Flowers made me sick, food made me sick, living in the city made me feel sick. I could not be in the same room with another person wearing any kind of perfume. Some days it was worse than others. When we reached his first Christmas we celebrated it with my parents. A Christmas tree was almost covered with presents, almost all of them for my son. I could not help cracking a smile when a tiny present was handed to me. I remember thinking that even though it was small, it may contain something nice. I opened it and looked at the box. Poême, it read. There was a tester taped to the box. I decided to save it for later, because I thought that it would make me sick like all other fragrances. Christmas morning I felt ok so I sprayed the perfume on a piece of paper. I thought it would be best so I could throw out the paper if I did not like it. The first whiff smelled so good. So spicy/warm/sweet that I could not believe it. I put the paper close to my nose. And I did not stop sniffing for a long time. It instantly became my favourite fragrance. Belletrud has once again made a masterpiece. A juice for gods - and for those who can still find it at reasonable prices. The bottle is gorgeous. This belongs in the spicy department - and on Lancôme’s shelf for huge successes. Bravo. 230/365

Poeme is a heavy, syrupy sweet white floral, and I absolutely love it! I can't stop smelling this one. It's a bit like Dior's Poison but much lighter, not as dark and more casual. I sense a lot of plum, tuberose, jasmine, orange blossom, vanilla, tonka bean and mimose in this fragrance. The white florals are quite honeyed. I picture Poeme as a thick liquid, trickling off my skin, it is in no way light, this fragrance is thick and intense. It has a definite oriental feel, which makes me conclude that this is an oriental floral with class. Seeing that the opening is rather strong, it's probably best to apply this fragrance lightly or spray the scent into the air and walk through it. It could easily become headache-inducing and cloying if over-applied. The scent lasts for ages which is really wonderful. Poeme appeals to me because I like fragrances of this nature, however for people that tend to dislike strong, heavy florals with a classic feel, this probably isn't for you.

This is what I call a “sunny floral”; whirlwind of white and yellow flowers, fruits (particularly peach and plum) and of course vanilla! There is a small hint of leather in the background which brings sensuality and warmth to the whole, but it blends in so well with the rest that it is difficult to perceive it.

Poeme is a yellow and white sweet floral that must have been made to seduce bees and everyone else with its lovely scent. Poeme was composed by legendary perfumer M. Jacques Cavallier-Belletrud and launched in 1995.

It's springtime and I am at my mother's. She has been cutting flowers from her garden and they have been in a closed up room overnight. I walk in the next morning. The air is dripping, cloyed, thick with the smell of her cut daffodils, freesias, more daffodils, narcissus, jasmine, hyacinth, flowering cherry, honeysuckle from the fence.

If color had a scent Lancome Poeme whould represent Dark Blue although the liquid from this perfume is Gold and the box is bright sunny Yellow. The top notes/Opening note starts off with hardiness of Leather a few seconds later dries to an softer femenine note of Blue Himalayan Poppies Succulant Plum i can detect a note of sweet Blueberries and peach.

What can you find inside the bottle? - A bunch of sultry flowers like jasmine, orange blossom, tuberose, rose and ylang-ylang spreading their heady and suffocating aroma between the landscapes made of honey and vanilla. - A meadow full of yellow flowers bathing under the golden sunlight. - Daffodils. The poisonous greenish aroma along the lines of Chloé Narcisse.

Bright, sweet, fruity tart opening. The early stages are definitely leaning to the fruity floral end of the spectrum. The pineapple leads the way and is fantastic. Reminds me of the same note found in Coach Platinum for Men. The pineapple is flanked by citrus notes, think lemon. The pink pepper is present giving it some further warmth and kick of spice. Fresh opening but the sorbet aspect of the pineapple, keeps Coach Floral feeling cold at the start. It will quickly turn into a white floral with sweet fruity highlights. The gardenia will actually play the largest role, to my nose. The rose tea is the second strongest and not the actual focus. Finishes into a fairly creamy white floral with woods and musk. Still sweet, just a pretty far distance from the opening act, but leans more tart to my nose. The shift from fruity/floral to the floral notes leading the way is fairly drastic, but it doesn’t completely change.

Hello there! I'm back again (… wait… did someone just sigh??…) and I'm rambling about a fragrance once more (… I'm pretty sure some of you are sighing!!!). Today, I'm once again talking about a brand I'm not familiar with. Coach. Do I need to know this? Is it weird for someone who writes a lot of comments not to know the brand Coach? I have no idea. It's funny though, that I often seem to have trouble spelling the word "Coach" correctly, as I almost always write Couch, you know, that seat thing where we put our butts :D Anyway, today it's the fragrance "Floral" that's up for discussion, which could actually make me want to run away immediately. On one hand, my knowledge of flowers is more than pathetic, as you know, and on the other hand, I always fear that floral fragrances will have stuffy notes in them, which make a perfume very unpleasant for me. But I'm going to test it anyway. On one hand, dear Parfuma, who sent me the fragrance, would surely complain endlessly if I didn’t test it, and on the other hand, you all need to be entertained during these Corona times, where you should actually be staying at home more (yeah, even despite the relaxations… don’t be stupid people :D Next week there’s still a mask mandate, but the masks do NOT make you invulnerable out there if you’re close to each other! :D), right? So sit down on your couch and read :D Yeah, good thing I used the right term here… I mean, you Parfumas could also sit on your Coach, but… I’d better not go into detail :DD The Fragrance: The fragrance starts with pineapple (no!!! NOT like in Aventus!!!!) as well as slightly spicy and above all fruity-sweet pink pepper. There’s a lot of jasmine, which adds another sweetness that is also floral. The whole thing reminds me of delicious chewing gums with berry and other fruity flavors, which I don’t mean negatively here, because it smells nice, spring-like, and also beautifully feminine. A little later, it continues to smell pleasantly sweet, and now roses are added to the floral notes. Although the fragrance list mentions rose tea, I only perceive roses, and there’s sadly no trace of tea to be smelled (what a shame…). Later, as is sometimes expected with such fragrances, it becomes a little stuffier. Fortunately, it’s not so extreme that you feel suffocated, but a small, stuffy-floral note is indeed present. Otherwise, the fragrance remains sweet, although the fruity notes fade a bit. In the base, the fruity notes fade even more, and the floral notes become more like "general floral notes," meaning you know the fragrance is floral without really being able to filter out the specific floral notes, as even easily identifiable notes like the roses fade and just smell, as mentioned, "floral." The sweetness of the fragrance now increasingly comes from the musk in the base, and the fragrance becomes a bit earthier due to the patchouli. A nice fragrance, although I preferred the beginning and the middle part a bit more than the base. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is average, neither strong nor weak, but detectable from a normal distance (so if you’re standing next to someone, but also a few steps away). The longevity is okay, lasting about six to eight hours, although the fragrance does become weaker over time. The Bottle: The bottle is rounded and filled with pink fragrance liquid. On the front, you can see the brand logo, which is a horse-drawn carriage. Between the neck and the bottle, there’s a pink, leathery, oval disc attached, from which a similarly leathery and pink flower dangles, which is golden in the middle and displays the brand name. There doesn’t seem to be a cap. All in all, a nice bottle. Conclusion: Ah, I’m glad I tested the fragrance. Not because I was afraid of the complaining Parfuma, but because I would have missed out on another nice fragrance. Sure, the fragrance had a slightly stuffy note, especially in the middle part, but it didn’t last too long and wasn’t really bothersome. The majority of the fragrance smells pleasantly floral and sweet-fruity. It’s one of those fragrances that doesn’t necessarily have a distinctive feature, as it comes off a bit generic (but like a well-made generic fragrance) or reminds you of many other fragrances, but it simply smells nice and belongs to the feel-good fragrances that you could use again and again in spring and summer for slightly casual days. The affordable price is also one of the strengths of the fragrance. So it’s definitely worth a test for me, but if someone has higher expectations and just doesn’t want anything mainstream, then they are totally at the wrong address with this fragrance. Well, that’s it again. See, that wasn’t so bad, was it? So I’ll surely be back here in a few days with a new comment (okay, stop sighing already!!) and yes, we’ll “see” each other! Have a nice evening :)

When I lived in the countryside, a wedding carriage was customary. The farmers already had horses - and somewhere a carriage could also be found. Even in our barn, an old landau was still slumbering under the tarpaulin. So the neighbor's daughter set off as a radiant white bride in the flower-adorned carriage. Flower garlands decorated the old vehicle, and the horses wore roses and jasmine on their harness. A romantic and nostalgic sight. I regretted that I hadn’t freed our old carriage from the dust and rocked my own wedding in it. But the cleaning smelled of a lot of work, so I opted for the car instead. But I enjoyed the floral-woody scent of the neighbor's daughter’s calash. Noble and elegant, it wafted over to me. I waved to the bridal couple with my gardenia bouquet in greeting. A harmonious marriage - preferably without boredom, should be granted to the couple. But even the return trip from the church was not marked by boredom, as the horses bolted, and the occupants of the wedding carriage landed in the fertile field. The wardrobe was ruined, which the bridal couple laughed off. They saw everything through the love-struck rose-colored glasses. And Coach Floral wears those too. Despite its refined statement, it exudes a positive, optimistic mood - one that it won’t let go of. I hope the couple has also kept their sense of humor.

Discovered at the Rossmann around the corner for €13. There was no tester, so I googled the scent notes and took it home blindly. It starts citrusy and zesty. But throughout the entire duration, absolutely no toilet bowl vibes! More like it makes your mouth water. And it never gets prickly or sharp. I believe this is because the jasmine adds a bit of sweetness and rounds it out. But jasmine does not take center stage; it is beautifully woven in. So it is not a classic jasmine scent. Especially in the first 10 minutes, I can clearly smell the gardenia. It is only that floral at the beginning. As it develops, the citrus notes and the pineapple remain. The pineapple leans more towards acidity and less towards sweetness - the term 'pineapple sorbet' really hits the mark. It doesn't smell like edible fruit to me, but like perfume. On my skin, everything stays citrusy and fruity until the end, with a slight hint of sweet flowers that makes it fragrant and wonderfully rounds it out. The longevity for me is up to 8 hours. For a citrusy, lighter scent, I find that really impressive! I find it super refreshing and invigorating in the summer. Overall, a very nice fragrance experience. It is definitely worth testing on the skin if you are looking for a beautifully rounded citrus-fruity perfume with very good longevity.

I love it! I can clearly smell pineapple, and the other notes create a harmonious base together, with jasmine fitting perfectly. Definitely not just one of the many fruity floral scents. An absolute mood-boosting fragrance, energetic, sweet, juicy. It is not citrusy and fizzy, yet very bright, sunny, but also cozy. The sillage and longevity are quite good for a fresh scent; I can smell it for hours.

My story/drama I promised that I won’t buy any perfume on February and here I am on 4th of February with a new perfume and a review on the first day and my man making fun of me that I can’t even keep a promise for 28 days! First of all, I want to seek redemption for my actions. I was really really disappointed by my last 2 perfume purchases whose smell was created in heaven but their performance was created in hell. I was looking for something with a good performance rather than a good smell but I found both today. Can you blame me? So today I was passing outside a department store which is usually super crowded (due to click away service) but today it was empty (1st lucky me) so I decided to ask if I can sample this perfume which is not available for purchase on their website. So they brought it to me and they sprayed my wrist and they told me they have it available, on sale and with a gift from Lancome (2nd lucky me). The perfume immediately got me under its spell. What is the surprising part, is that I was smelling it in the air all day at the office and I couldn’t smell the perfume I wore today because oud bouquets smell have vanished every other smell in the room. So I was like “to hell with my promise I’m buying it”. The smell The notes are so beautifully blended and you can tell the quality of it. At the beginning, you get an intense “metallic” woody rose smell. You can distinguish the praline smell and some “earthiness” from the saffron, after it settles 1 hour to your skin. The oud is not very intense but together with the vanilla, they provide a solid base that enhances the smell of the other notes. It is considered to be a gourmand perfume, obviously because of the praline. For me it is more like orientally gourmandish. It is sweet but not too much. The performance As I said before the performance is amazing. With one spray it lasted all day, it covered the smell from the perfume I was wearing and even now that I have washed my hands many times, I still get the smell. Season/Occasion Mostly for autumn and winter and early spring because it has a warmth in its smell. As for the occasion, anytime you need a smell with beast performance. Gender In my opinion, its mostly for women because it’s too rosy for a man to wear. I haven’t smelled it on a man’s skin. Maybe it responds differently than my skin, so I wouldn’t blame a man wearing it. A great combination of rose and oud for a man is Prada’s “Miracle of the rose”. In the pradas perfume, the oud is more intense and the rose more discreet. In oud bouquet it’s the opposite. Miracle of the rose (or OUD ROSE) is an amazing perfume for a man and oud bouquet for a woman. Conclusion Sorry not sorry, I broke my promise. It’s a lovely well blended perfume that has an amazing performance. Totally worth trying / buying it ! Thank you for your time. Be safe and smell Goud BOUQUET.

The first thing you're taken by is the filligreed heavy glass bottle. There is no plastic here (I'm looking your way Armani and Aerin) and the heavy magnetic cap clicks into place smoothly every time. The dark amber liquid shows through the golden metal filigree like an expensive liqueur. Next comes the smell: the most artfully blended vanilla with candied praline and a hint of rose. The oud is an abstract concept here: there is the appearance of a woody darkness but it is not the typical medicinal or strongly-pungent oud. It's a touch. The main concept here, as is illustrated on the other side of the beautiful bottle, is rose praline. This new Oud Bouquet is nothing like the unpleasantness of the old version with the same name. I see no drawbacks in price, longevity, sillage or appearance. Kudos to Lancome for creating an amazing array of fragrances in the Grands Crus collection.

Oh my Gosh! I felt in love immediately after the first Sniff. So classy, so deep so balanced, so warm. It is the bad day, good day, cold day, special day, night sleep, spoiling Fragrance for me. When I wear it, it become immediately noticed. Has a very good performence. A must be for every female.

This is by far one of the more talked about recent releases from the house of Lancôme. It has had some positive press from a lot of trusted reviewers and I was keen to see, or smell, what the fuss was about.

I found this beauty of a perfume when browsing through the Lancome.de website for offers because they have a nice discount currently. Oud and Rose, I said .. this is typically used combination and I smelled it with Silk Oud from MFK or Santal Royal from Guerlain, I wonder what is different with the Lancome´s OUD Bouquet, by Fabrice Pellegrin. I honestly can say that the first spray I applied to my skin was telling me about what high quality ingredients they are using, all smells absolutely natural, like pure rose oil which is not 1€ Shop sickly sweet and also not so overwhelming like in the MFKs. Together with the OUD, which is very wearable, not heavy at all .. it makes a very nice oriental woody type of smell which can be unisex more than Santal Royal which even if I like it, for me it is more lady oriented. The H/S is just out of this world, after 24h you still feel it on the skin, with one shower included .. on the clothes it smells like freshly applied even after few days. I did not know about Maison Lancome´s Haute Parfumerie but I am so happy I discovered it, they might have the best selling La vie est belle and lots of make-up, but their top range is also worth checking out.

... well, what can I say? This fragrance ... I bought it very quickly, perhaps a bit hastily, and I must admit I didn't discover it on my own. I'm currently watching various fragrance influencers on YouTube (in this case, it was Demi Rawling) who almost pushed me towards this purchase.

First of all: this is all absolute new territory for me, I have zero clue about all this stuff and nonsense. But what I definitely know: this stuff is deadly! It smells so unbelievably Ultra, I could just lay in it, rub it in my eyes, spray it on everything I own. I sprayed it in the air yesterday afternoon and swung my forearm through the cloud.

Deep and extremely low temperatures outside (like right now -12°C here in Bad Segeberg) should not tempt one, when testing a - as here extremely gourmand-sweet - Oriental, to be blinded by the sugar of coziness. "Ôud Bouquet," one might think based on the ingredients, would largely be the usual (as I recently wrote) standardized banal triad of rose, saffron, and oud.

From the first spray of my decant, the scent had me, I must honestly say. It smells so deep, so dense, so warm, and so special that I can hardly find words for it. The longevity is absolutely insane, spray it in the morning and still have some left in the evening (I've never experienced being able to smell the scent on myself all day long!), it’s truly a dream...

When I think about the fact that I can slowly no longer smell saffron and oud because I have simply gotten used to both notes over the years, one might rightly ask why this fragrance has now entered my collection? It is simply due to the incredible transformation that happens in the drydown.. I was out here in Hamburg at Alsterhaus to buy one or two fragrances.

I am usually not drawn to flowery scent but this perfume reconciled me with it. I would usually wear it as a daily scent as it is not too overpowering. When I first sprayed it, I was terrified of the dry down, but it was actually really good. It first starts as a citrusy scent and then dry downs as a beautiful flowery scent, I do not smell the vanilla that much but that is okay as well. Great fragrance for spring and summer.

I swapped for this fragrance and didn't expect much but hoped for a lot because I really love "Coach (2016) (Eau de Parfum) | Coach." This one, by the way, doesn't get much love but is really beautiful. I love reaching for it and feel pleasantly fruity-floral and somewhat long-lasting when wearing it (even though I can't for the life of me detect any suede in it...). Anyway, this is supposed to be about "Coach Dreams Sunset | Coach." So, it arrived, I sprayed it on, sniffed my wrist with interest, and thought immediately: I know this, I have it! So, quick sniff comparison and lo and behold: Dupe discovered! Specifically to "Sunset Hour | Goldfield & Banks." Only, Coach Dreams Sunset is more intense, lasts longer, and costs a fraction. It has a bit more jasmine/magnolia and a bit less coconut but more body than Sunset Hour and lasts easily 5-6 hours. I say, save yourselves the 150 euros and take the dream carriage into the sunset...so, now you know!

So or something similar was my statement last year about Coach Dreams. Compared to the previous fragrances from Coach, I liked its softness, apart from the scent composition. Not as squeaky sweet and fruity as the florals, not as piercing a top note as the original Coach perfume (although I do grow fond of it over time). I wrote this statement, not knowing that soon a new flanker would see the light of day. Admittedly, it took me a while with this one. As I said, I really liked Coach Dreams, which is why my excitement about Sunset was quite high when I saw it in the window of my perfumery. Oh yes, the box has a great color, not so pink, more peach (and I love peach!) - and the beautiful bottle has remained, I liked it so much last year. So, into the perfumery I went, and it was generously sprayed onto a test strip - thankfully. I do not like the opening at all on the strip. It is fresh-fruity, and I perceive that piercing note again, which I did not like in the sweet florals. Great, all my hopes have evaporated. The test strip goes in the trash. Several weeks passed since then; I am having dinner with my mother. She arrives a bit later (as always, couldn’t find a parking spot, yes, yes ;) ), sits down energetically next to me - and brings a real cloud of fragrance with her. “What are you wearing?” I ask. “Oh, I got a sample of the new Coach” - she doesn’t sound very enthusiastic. But I am surprised by the scent, so warm and vanillic, almost autumnal, I hadn’t perceived it that way at all. It is really very intense and accompanies us throughout the entire dinner. A few more weeks go by until I focus on Coach again in the perfumery. He gets another chance, cautiously a spray on my wrist, oh what the heck, another one on my neck afterward. And then he gets me, all of a sudden. On my skin, he is not nearly as piercing and bothersome as on the test strip. He has that softness again that I liked so much in the big sister. After about half an hour, I perceive the pleasant warmth of the vanilla, which is pleasantly muted in conjunction with the heart notes. And with that, this flanker climbs high on my Coach best list. I find the transformation it undergoes to be wonderful. The longevity is also good, on my skin easily 6 hours, on clothing even longer. For my standards, that’s almost a knockout. Due to the predecessor (and the name), I expected something different, but I was still positively surprised. I imagine Coach Sunset to be more of a golden hour in late summer when the leaves slowly turn colorful and the days get shorter, but you still don’t want to let go of summer completely. It did take a little while for us, but now I can overwrite my statement from last year - this is the best Coach for me (so far).

Here is the third of the Mumin fragrances specifically developed for the Korean market. What kind of scent do they associate with a polar light in Iceland? Something Nordic-cool or fresh? To me, the fragrance initially comes across as primarily citrus-fresh. The combination of citrus and mint does indeed remind me a bit of those ice candies, although I don’t perceive their typical synthetic note (which has always slightly repelled me, even though I generally like almost every type of candy) in the perfume. Later on, and this happens quite soon, the perfume becomes more floral-fresh, as I would expect from the floral blend in the heart note. This perfume is not particularly long-lasting on my skin; it gently fades after a maximum of two hours. A nice scent that is well-suited for spring or summer. Nothing extravagant, but very wearable. Of the three bottles, I personally like this one best in terms of design, which is due to my love for blue-turquoise tones.

Red and purple berries from all over the world escaped from a chemical lab and managed to unite in this bottle. So much about the top-notes. Should you be able to survive this berry-attack, you'll be given a nice reward: a vanilla-trifle treatment. Who is this aimed at? 8-14 year-olds?

I'm on the fence when it comes to Tresor Midnight Rose. I'm not a huge fan of the top notes, yet the drydown has me somewhat captivated. Either way, I find this fragrance unique, which is one very pleasant aspect, especially in regards to a modern mainstream release. Tresor Midnight Rose opens with a rather musty blend of pink pepper and rich, jammy berries. The overall feel is dark and mysterious, but perhaps a little too musky on the skin sometimes. A berry sweetness dominates this fragrance, sharing some similarities with typical releases from Escada to Mariah Carey. The rose adds a floral dimension to the composition, that certainly complies with this fragrance's femininity but doesn't cancel out the sugary aspect. I also get a strange cough syrup vibe. For most of this fragrance's development, it's a mish-mash of heavy musk, synthetically sweet berries and pepper. I can't say that I'm a fan. However, closer to the drydown, Tresor Midnight Rose shows signs of complexity, and sweetens even further into a blend that can only be described as powdered chocolate and blueberry flavoured jellybeans. Okay, so although it's still too sweet for my personal tastes, this rather captivating blend interests me greatly. In fact, I can hardly stop smelling it. It goes from a musky fruity floral to a rich gourmand in only a matter of hours. I'm kind of impressed. The longevity is great, as is the sillage which projects itself quite strongly. Of all the Tresor flankers so far, including the original, Tresor Midnight Rose is certainly the best, but then again it has its moments.

I decided to try this today, as had a lovely large sample. I have had Lancome fragrances in the past, and can't say I like them all, but this is the first fruity one I have tried. I have to be honest and say, I really don't detect Rose at all! But, Berries galore! First opening, a blast of Raspberry...followed by more berries..a hint of citrus, and still more types of berries. Too sweet for my liking, and didn't detect any cedar. It seems to last, but I find it very berry boring! The dry down is a bit of a let down, but perhaps this fragrance is geared more towards the real fruity (not much floral) fans. The bottle makes you think it will be more of an elegant scent..but, not in this case.

For me, this scent begins with very strong jammy and tart raspberries with a bit of rose. You can almost imagine you hear the bubbling of the rasperry and sugar mixture on the stovetop. As the top notes fade out the musk and vanilla become more prominent. You can also notice some green (cedar?) somewhere in the back ground. Although it's way too sweet for regular use by me, I really like it. Very feminine, sexy, yummy and pretty near edible fragrance. The sillage seems very good and the longevity is adequate (3-4 hours) for me.

Oh, how I wish the longevity of this fragrance lasted! Despite three generous sprays (the fragrance was dripping up my arm), this just didn't last on my skin. There's a hint of it on my clothes, but for me it was more like, MIDNIGHT POOF! Gone at the strike of 12 (applied at the strike of 11).

LANCOME Trésor Midnight Rose is mostly 3-note fragrance to me. I can sense black currant, rose and raspberry all the way to the drydown. Opening is very loud in a good way and immediately brings me to cold winter season with lots of snow on the ground and cozy rose petal jam on a toast laying next to cup of black raspberry flavored tea.

If you find Midnight Rose initially too sweet, cloying or fruity - stick around a while longer. It loses some of its fruitiness and gives way to a more sultry, spicy and mysterious vanilla-laced rose (as its name suggests). For me, it is powerful in both sillage and longevity, a small amount goes a long way.

This perfume goes on strong. I don’t get roses whatsoever the entire length of time wearing it, but instead I get a dark blackberry, fruity scent that smells great after a couple hours of wearing it. Longevity 8 hours. Sillage 3 feet at first, ending in a nice skin scent. I would not rebuy this perfume since the roses don’t come out in my skin.

Such a pretty bottle with a little rose wrapped around it. Alas, it left me very disappointed. I felt like all the beautiful notes of rose were overwhelmed by the loud berry chorus girls. In the end, it always gave me a headache as the raspberry diva sang too high. It’s a shame as I loved the concept. Sugary sweet rosy berry.
When I first spray this, it instantly puts me in mind of Britney Spears Midnight Fantasy. I think because of the raspberry top note. It smells like sugared, dark fruits to me.

I love this scent! I genuinely don't perceive the "floral" notes of this perfume and instead just bask in its sweet, juicy, strawberry deliciousness. Every time I pass the bottle when I'm home I spray some on me for a boost of seratonin. It's a great layering perfume due to it's mild, sweet scent-- I've paired it with stronger, citrus forward scents as well as muskier ones. This is a real compliment inducer, of the "you smell DELICIOUS" variety

------Blind Buy-------- I was on a hunt for a realistic strawberry, I was recommended this perfume multiple times. At first I really thought it was perfect but it's so faint that the scent of alcohol barely ever disappear? It kinda stays there for multiple minutes and overall you can't really tell how good the perfume is. Now, for the scent... It's a fresh strawberry, a light sweetness and not candy like, neither childish, bit woody and slightly floral (not to the point of only smelling the floral). Yep, that's good but I don't really know if that's a win?. The "perfume" is certainly not powerful enough to be called an edp, so no high hopes for this one.

people often talk about Strawberry Letter or Burberry Her as being true strawberry, but to me, they are strawberry with an intruder of some kind. Love is really super strawberry forward to me with a little hint of tea in the background. like others said, I also miss the florals mixed into this and get 95% strawberry, which is exactly what I wanted in a perfume. this isn't heavy on the nose and is easy to wear with good lasting power. I find a regular batch of 4 sprays lasts me 4-6 hours (depending on humidity and if I sweat, but that's normal) which is solid to me. great for the fruity/specifically strawberry lovers!

the wild strawberries here are synthetic, floral and soapy - not juicy and tangy at all. at the same time they are not too sweet, it's just enough to make this scent not infantile. it totally feels like taking a strawberry bubble bath with rose candles lit around you, maybe the soy wax ones with a wooden wick. it’s a very simple, cheerful, clean fragrance that might work well in spring. personally, i would rather choose a strawberry body mist from the body shop.

As a man who really likes the scent of strawberries and wants to smell like them, it’s not easy. This fruit is usually only found in perfumes for women, and often only in those aimed at teenagers. I have discovered a few "adult" ones, but they all have one thing in common: they tend to lean towards sweet strawberry shakes or strawberry cream. However, I wanted a sparkling fresh strawberry, and this fragrance has that, and it’s not too sweet, probably because they opted for a wild strawberry. It’s all pure synthetic, and the mandarin gives it a bit of a "children's sparkling wine" vibe, but especially in warm weather, it’s really delicious and refreshing, even though it’s not a typically fresh scent. I can’t complain about longevity and sillage either; I sprayed it 24 times this afternoon at 3 PM and I can still smell it around me, even though I was outside a lot and did some work, so I was sweating too. Yet, it’s still there! The reason I sprayed it 24 times is due to the major flaw of this perfume: the bottle is unfortunately very poorly designed. It seems they have crammed the already bulky plastic holder for the decorative heart so tightly under the spray head that it doesn’t allow for a proper press, resulting in a very weak spray. So whoever made that decision, that’s really bad! I don’t want to take it apart either because it’s so poorly made that it will probably break. For this price range, I expect more; even cheap dupes do better. It does take some courage and confidence for a man to spray on this girl’s scent, but I take it sportily like with niche fragrances, as I really don’t care what others say about it. I think it’s great and will wear it often in summer because it’s just so lively and sparkling and puts me in a good mood. The name "Love" fits perfectly!

No, I’m not completely crazy yet. It’s not my fault that Demeter/The Library of Fragrance produces such uncanny scents, To be honest, "Molasses" was probably one of the fragrances in Demeter's range that interested me the least from the whole background. However, since it was available at a bargain price, I ordered it to expand my already huge Demeter collection. Let’s get to the scent. Molasses is a sweet, no let’s say it straight up, REALLY sweet fragrance. Since Demeter scents rarely undergo a complex transformation, you get exactly what you buy. Anyone who knows this classic black spread in the yellow packaging "... Goldsaft" knows exactly what I’m talking about. The strange thing is that it actually smells good. As creepy as the idea of slathering oneself with sugar beet syrup is, it’s surprisingly wearable in reality in the EdT version. Alongside the overwhelming sweetness, there’s a slightly bitter undertone that almost leans towards licorice. However, this is really just a side note. Overall, Molasses is a sweet, rooty delight for the nose that is definitely not suitable for warm weather. Unless you’re in love with bees, etc. Then you probably have constant visitors ;) Longevity and sillage are quite good due to the sweetness. I classify the scent as unisex. In the autumn/winter, I will get a little closer to this guy. Let’s see what effect it has then. As hollow as it sounds to wear such a scent, I was amazed that it works. Not an overpowering scent, no sensation, but a nice sweet little fellow that shows the world out there: "I’m still here" You don’t have to do it, but you can :)

Lancôme's MIRACLE opens in a somewhat confusing way: I smell a mingling of flowers and ginger with the texture, not the taste, of a lychee. The squeaky feeling when you bite into a lychee is a unique experience and combined with a slight muskiness and magnolia--well, if nothing else, I must say that this fragrance is one of a kind! Magnolia is the dominant floral here, to my nose, but I would hesitate to characterize this as a floral scent, not only because of the slight sweetness imparted by fruits, but also because the early stages are relatively shortlived, and the drydown is entirely dominated by musky pepper. This creation has the pepper-scented fingerprints of Alberto Morillas all over it. Overall, I'd say that MIRACLE is probably my favorite gingery-lychee-textured magnolia-musky-pepper fragrance. (-:

Whenever I smell this I'm just mystified by the hate it receives. Certain perfumes almost seem to get picked on simply because they're crowd-pleasing. I understand bashing something like Angel or Black Orchid because they're strong, polarizing scents, but not Miracle. This is PRETTY. The florals are seamless...I'm struggling to distinguish anything specifically. They're non-indolic, clean white florals with some tasteful spice. Not earthy spice, but almost a cola tone? Sparkling...and a little zingy. The lychee isn't the same as it is in Delina or other newer releases, some different aromachemicals are seemingly used here. I know Lancôme is French, but this fragrance always feels American to me in personality. Bubbly, pink, suburban, a bit basic admittedly (the kids call it "normcore"), but in a comforting and nostalgic way - not bland. It's not something that I feel suits me (though I could wear it), but every time I've visited it over the years I'm pleasantly transported into the early 2000s emotionally.

I must have it for over 15 years now, and it just doesn't seem to become any less. I bought it way back when, because the sales woman was persistent that this was a great fragrance for me, and I liked it enough to cave in and purchased the 50ml bottle. I like it, but it is far away from love, and there are way more fragrances out there for less money that I enjoy just a much if not even more. So, Miracle is okay, and I would not crinkle my nose if someone would like to give me a nice present and buy me a bottle again down the line. I myself will very unlikely strut into a store to get another bottle myself, if I should ever get out of it. A BIG if, the way I use it, I'll most probably still have the same bottle in my drawer in another 15 years from now.

I was rather disappointed when I smelt this. I had imagined Miracle to smell sweet and flowery, especially since the pretty pink bottle had misled me. Instead Miracle is a strong burst of peppered fruits, a little like spicy orange juice I thought. In some ways it's quite sour and unpleasantly strong. I think it's one of those scents that rely on the wearer's skin chemistry. I've smelt this on a few people who've managed to make this fragrance smell softer and more flowery. On a more positive note, I like that Miracle is different. The spiciness mixed with the fruits is interesting and original. This fragrance would make an excellent Summer/Spring or casual scent.

An iconic huge bouquet of flowers! Perfect intense floral for a spring day. This is very feminine. If you could smell colors, this would be pink. It makes me think of Easter, wearing chiffon dresses to church. You know how after a late spring rain, the sun comes out and the flowers smell extra beautiful? That's the feeling you get from a few drops of Miracle.

At first a gentile breeze of pink floral and in a few minutes turnes fruity and at the end amber. this is a fememine scent very soft. very perfect for daytime and spring. but unfortunily this doesn't last long.

Ô de Lancôme is a scent that goes way back early memories, the first Lancôme scent I remember. Actually, Lancôme as a brand was to me for a long time truly decadent and luxurious. It has always been there and I have owned many of their fragrances and still do. Magie Nôire was worn by my mother in the early 80s as was ô de Lancôme. Later she wore Tresôr. She loved it.

I got to know and love Miracle quite late. My mother loves the body lotion, which is how I discovered Miracle as a fragrance for myself. In the meantime, it has become a subtle everyday scent for me that gently accompanies me throughout the day. I like its fresh opening, and I obviously enjoy perfumes with the top note of lychee. The freesia is very subtle.

Today, I want to dedicate a comment to my beloved Miracle. I first got to know Miracle in 2006 during a time that was anything but rosy for me personally. However, Miracle has always conveyed a sense of lightness during this difficult phase of my life when the day didn't go perfectly.

I received Miracle as a gift from a dear perfume-obsessed friend (beyond Parfumo :-) ). Unfortunately, she couldn't tolerate the scent and told me that it triggers breathing problems. This might also be a reason for the reformulation of Miracle that seems to have taken place.

Coach Dreams is a lush floral that has both sweetness and sharp edges from the bitter orange. I usually don't like florals that I perceive as sharp, but something about this draws me in. It feels so springy and refreshing! It's a clean and pure kind of floral, but it has the slightest honeyed undertone that keeps it from being harsh and sterile. I'm not 100% sure if I would have identified it as a gardenia and cactus blossom scent blindly, but it definitely feels white floral, creamy and not too transparent. I do not smell the pear from the top notes, and I don't miss it, every other floral already has a pear note nowadays. The bitter orange is much more interesting. Even though I enjoy it a lot, I don't think I'd personally wear it. The sharp and clean notes simply don't suit everyone, and I feel more at home in softer and warmer scents. But if you're looking for a floral that is fresh, but not necessarily light, I recommend to try Coach Dreams. In my opinion it's pretty unique, I can't think of another perfume in the designer white floral category that has such a strong and distinct bitter orange note. It's also rather loud and intense for a scent that feels so breezy.

Coach Dreams may be simple, but it is very pleasant. An ideal companion for spring: it contains notes of freshly cut grass, spring flowers, and a variety of fruits. This purity and freshness in the base is very rare for most modern luxury fragrances. Sweet, juicy, and cheerful, when Ambroxan comes into play, it becomes thicker, more enveloping, and warmer. Deserves attention.

I was just on a nearly empty bus for what felt like an eternity and three days, successfully passing the time with a Coach Dream sample (occasionally lifting my mask to sniff my wrist) ... On stage, a metallic-tinged gardenia immediately appears - a cool floral touch that I like - and then alternates with the delicious bitter orange. The cactus flower brings in a fresh-sweet background, and towards the end, it becomes a bit sweeter and creamier. Perhaps that ambrosial Joseph lily? The scent creates an urban strolling feeling for me, so I immediately added an extensive evening downtown walk through our old neighborhood with the beautiful Art Nouveau houses and a few English gardens... a whimsical companion for a short trip, with which one can and wants to experience some variety. It coached me well because it gives me butterflies in my stomach ;-) Just missing the old Petula Clark Downtown song ... or Diana Ross. Longevity about 4 hours - I've already reapplied.

Coaches have not disappointed me so far - I enjoy wearing the edp and the floral. Good mainstream fragrances with a nostalgic touch. Pleasant and nicely unobtrusive. They also appeal to my husband's sensitive nose. And so this open carriage feels like a relaxed overland ride in an old landau. You are gently rocked through the landscape - like in a cradle. You pass by orchards where the pear dominates. Clear and aquatic - emphasized by a delicate bitter orange that provides a good counterbalance to the sweet pear note. Floral notes linger in the air - and I dream of summer. I cannot detect any disturbing synthetics - the ingredients feel natural to me. A friendly companion for the day - even now in winter. I will place this charming carriage with the others in my coach house.

Oh, another Demeter. But wait, no. This time it won't be another test series (what a shame...), but just a single test because I kindly received a sample of this fragrance. Well, despite some oddly smelling fragrances from Demeter, I expect a good scent here. Hey, after all, we're talking about cookies. And if they smell authentic,... then happy munching! :D Alright, let's go! The scent: The fragrance starts off a bit powdery and sweet, but then it actually smells like butter cookies, and quite naturally, although a bit too strong. Yes, I don't think butter cookies smell this strong unless you're inhaling the crumbs :D But still, it's quite well done and really close to real cookies. The sillage and longevity: The projection is strong, but only at the beginning. It's almost as if you have butter cookies in front of you that are a bit crumbled, causing the scent to rise more intensely. Not bad, but unfortunately, it doesn't stay at this level for long. The longevity is okay; it lasted about six hours on me, maybe even a bit longer. The bottle: The bottle is as always,… uh wait… WHERE is the bottle? Someone took the bottle away and I only see the blue placeholder here, but even this drawing looks better than the original! No, not really… oh, it's hard to find the bottle online too, as it seems it hasn't been produced for quite some time… but if it still existed, it would be rectangular and practical as always with an overloaded label showing a bar in some color with "Butter Cookies" written on it. So, all in all, rather unremarkable, but that's just speculation :D Therefore, I won't rate the bottle here. Hmm, not bad. Butter Cookies is one of the scents from Demeter that doesn't smell bizarre. Moreover, it mostly smells authentic and good, but it's not perfect. Because something bothers me; I think it's because real cookies don't smell that strong. Well, you can give it a try, but I don't think you'll see the scent anywhere. But don't worry, that's okay because Demeter has other cookie scents (hmm… Chocolate Chip Cookie must smell great!). So what can you use the scent for? Maybe to say, "And whoever is nice gets a cookie!" he he. And then there will be complaints because it's a plain butter cookie and not a chocolate cookie, but hey, dipped in tea (or coffee, for that matter) butter cookies taste great, unless they break apart and turn the hot drink into hot mush! Buuuahhh… I bet that has happened to you too, right?
