At the very first sniff, the inner nature if Hypnose is already clear: a half-good work. Perfectly split in two parts: one is completely good, the other completely crap, and the clash is just... err. There are indeed some nice features: the mint note is fresh, green and realistically crunchy, avoiding the toothpaste effect; the spices are vibrant and lively, and overall, it surely catches that mid-2000s “metropolitan” masculine elegance played on amber-warm-sweet notes blended with spices and woods, here also added with a dusty layer of lavender and white musks, clean and classy like a freshly ironed shirt. The family, in broad terms, is the one of Dior Homme or Arpège pour Homme (to which Hypnose resembles a bit, just more pungent and spicier), that type of urban, office-safe, yet somehow feminine elegance which was in fashion some years ago. So far so good: lavender, spices, woods, a balsamic breeze. It would be a good perfume, but... the “but” here is quite a big “but” (sorry for the pun), and it's represented by a completely useless, unrelated, horrid metallic-ozonic-fruity note, or better say “feel”, which smells quite similar to that stuff they use to build tropical-sea notes (I just thought of Azzaro Chrome for instance, but you get it in many other scents as well). Basically some kind of pungent, moldy, metallic and completely weird spicy-calone aftertaste, which is fruity in a way, but warm at the same time. And as I said, completely separated from the rest, just sitting there like an elephant in a room – and I mean a real elephant into an actual room. Without this nuance, which to me is quite bold, it would be a good scent, a bit trendy and conventional but good; but as-is, it's just annoying. Such a shame! 4,5-5/10

Before i found out that this was going to be discontinued (in fact, it was discontinued recently) i bought a 50ml bottle of this. Not because i really love this but because it's weird and intriguing. This is a fragrance that has a good idea but was made with low budget. It starts off with a blast of sweet mint and cardamom. Sweet inducing and annoying. As it dries down, the lavender round things up a bit and links the sweet and fresh mint-cardamom combo with the shower gel amber and patchouli-musk base. Nothing is particularly good and the opening is definitely cheap smelling. But there's some interesting ideas and the overall experience isn't that bad and, in fact can be alluring in the right occasion. This was made to be worn at night. I tend to wear it on a dinner or a night out, but this isn't that strong to be considered as a good clubing fragrance. It's just a cheap fragrance that has nice ideas but on a budget. Maurice has better options even with low budget (Nautica Voyage). I compare this one with Ted Lapidus pour Lui which has the same problem but that one is actually worse cause it's just a Le Male done wrong. This is a nice fragrance if you find it for a nice price. Has some nice ideas and the overall smell is pleasant but it's cheap materials make me nauseated sometimes, specially the opening. Because this was discontinued, it may became a bit expensive and i will not recommend you to spend much money on this. Get La Nuit de L'Homme Eau de Toilette for a better night out/dinner fragrance. They aren't super similar but they do utilize lavender and cardamom and the YSL is miles away better. 3/5

Hypnosis, or hypnotherapy, is a state of deep relaxation and focused concentration. It’s a type of mind-body medicine. Hypnotherapy is a heightened state of concentration and focused attention. Guided by a trained, certified hypnotist or hypnotherapist, hypnosis allows you to be more open to suggestions for making healthful changes in your perceptions, sensations, emotions, memories, thoughts or behaviours. Thus, what makes it so hypnotic? At the opening, you immediately feel lavender’s fresh, aromatic, and herbaceous nuances, a massive dose, but it worked well. It is as if a bundle of lavender spikes had dived from the springboard into a tub full of well-dosed citrus juice, in which mandarin orange and bergamot are mixed, but I also smell a little orange and lemon. The presence of cardamom is noteworthy, a warm spice with its somewhat balsamic colouring that goes well with the citrus part, making it slightly acidic. For an instant, it seemed to me that I, too, had the same vibrations of Touch for Men Eau de Toilette and Le Mâle Eau de Toilette . There is something that smells the same without making one a copy of the other. Instead, the mint note is subdued, perhaps overshadowed by the lavender overdose. The more the fragrance grows, the more the citrus notes are lost. Instead, wet violet leaves’ metallic and dewy edges stand out with a slightly sweaty aftertaste, a very virile, masculine, hypnotic sweat. It’s not an ugly, nasty, disgusting, stinky sweat while remaining very close to the smell of the body, of clean and cleansed skin, which is attractive to many people. The cardamom continues its path, and having reached the centre, it joins the lavender, offering tea-like accents. The spicy aspect is very fragrant than piquant or pungent. Something even creates a hint of fresh, moist, and unburned tobacco. At this point, Hypnose differs from the two perfumes mentioned above. The dry-down surprises me with oriental, musky and amber accords. The fresh part was lost; now, the scent is warm and sensual, keeping that sense of sweat clean. A touch of patchouli, not overly damp rich, and moist, gently soil the more animal aspects of musk and the powdery ones of amber and coumarins. All in all, the perfume’s finish is moderately sweet, despite many sweetish notes. It also showed some creamy edges, which makes me think of hidden sandalwood. A splendid interpretation of the fougère family, to my nose significantly leaning towards the masculine universe with a potent combination of cardamom and lavender. Too bad it didn’t achieve the success it deserved and that it was discontinued; perhaps too much underestimated. It is one of those scents you either hate or love. The accords place it among the autumn fragrances, even if I suppose new nuances can be perceived if worn in spring or other warmer or colder seasons. It is a perfume with limited performance, the projection is intimate, and the duration is around half a day. Almost a classic; it never leaves its comfort zone. It is ideal for formal meetings, work, an outing with friends, or a dinner. Even though it’s rated for the night, I also find it suitable for the daytime. Such a lovely and hypnotic scent, I'd suggest to men of all ages, a perfect staple in my collection for when I want to give off an alluring vibe. I'm basing my impressions on a bottle I have owned since June 2019. -Elysium

Meh!! I got a bottle of Hypnôse Homme in a duty free shopping spree some time ago and in a bit of a rush this morning, it was the first thing I grabbed as it was unopened. "Time to try it ..." I said to myself. I seem to remember it being a nice Cedar. WRONG ... I must've confused it with something else on my arm. As fragrances go there is little to redeem this one in the way of being different. Nothing 'hypnotic' here I'm afraid. It's pretty much a bog standard rendition of a generic male fragrance that smells like dozens of others on the men's shelves today. This doesn't smell awful ... it just smells boring! Synthetic Lavender and Bergamot up top with with a vaguely amber/patch dry down does very little to inspire. Hypnôse Homme also has that 'tinny' Musk note I have no time for. 9 to 5 business suited men in middle of the road corporate jobs would probably have a lot of use for this ... it's inoffensive and smells like deodorant. YAWN ... It can go to my brother in law, who's an accountant.

Today I was able to wear this Lancome perfume. It is a good perfume, but, I expected something more complex, anyway, it is a beautiful fragrance and easy to dress. There is a fundamental pillar in this perfume, which is lavender, cardamom and amber, a warm aroma, spicy, sweet and very aromatic. This is the aroma that we will perceive throughout the life of the perfume, only that, at the beginning, it is much sweeter and more fruity, with a touch of precious mint. Then, the aroma lowers in intensity and stabilizes, disappear citrus and mint, to give greater presence to lavender and amber, with a little spicy cardamom, and the addition of patchouli, which gives body and a woody tone very pretty. This is how the aroma stays until it dies flush with skin, and in spite of its monotonous drying, it is a perfume that I like, it is warm, neat, elegant and very sensual. The perfume from the first moment you smell it, you seem familiar, I'm still slicing my brains to remember what it looks like, although it belongs to that line of fragrances with very generic fragrances and that smell very similar to each other, and therefore, I'm not going to eat my head very much, but at all times I've been thinking that it reminds me of something known, although, its aromatic generality does not mean that this perfume smells phenomenally good. In my skin the performance has been moderate high in duration, and moderate to dry in projection, remaining in skin for about 7 hours. Its use I see it more appropriate for the night, but it is one of those aromas that are very versatile and you can use it in any season or hour, except for summer, where I think that its sweetness could overwhelm a little, otherwise, I think a good perfume. Sorry for my bad english.

Hypnose Homme is mostly sweet amber and oranges to my nose. I'm unfortunately not experiencing the spices and rich green accords like everyone else. While I'm not blown away by the scent, I'm not hugely disappointed either. The scent is pleasant enough with a smooth, resinous feel, but it fails to move me in any way.

I did expect more of Roucel's work. This is a good scent, but nothing new added. There are some spices (mostly cardamon) in the opening laying in a cedar/ambery base when dries down. Longevity is about average, and projection and sillage are low. Updated August 2013.

Hypnôse Homme is a fragrance that I have owned for a while. After a statement some time ago, I decided to add this with a little comment. I remember that it was being sold off cheaply a few years ago, and unfortunately, I didn't jump on it back then. Since I preferred the more common designer men's brands, I only noted the offer without testing it.

That's right... I really am... :O How... what... why??? :O Well, the name is indeed fitting. I am hypnotized. ;) I've had this little gem for quite a while now, one of my first fragrances since I became a member of Parfumo, as far as I can remember... What makes Hypnose particularly special is that, despite having it for so long, I hardly used it! Hmm.

I stumbled upon this fragrance purely by chance while browsing the shelves in the perfume store. Until that moment, I had no idea about this scent, and Lancome was a brand that I primarily associated with women as the target audience. When I tried the fragrance on a paper strip, it could be easily described as slightly sweet and oriental.

This is a very pretty feminine fragrance with a hint of fruit and sweetness. I pick up on the rose but I wouldn't say it's a strong rose scent, it's nicely balanced by the other notes in this fragrance. I especially pick up on the bergamot on the initial spray. However, I don't really think it's anything particularly special. It does smell a little generic. It's definitely not my favorite, and I don't reach for it often. It's a nice scent to wear when it's colder, especially before bed or for a date. I don't think I'd buy again but if you like a simple, easy to wear and inoffensive floral this could be for you.

Lovely rose scent, very feminine and pleasant. It is a deeper rose scent rather than a fresh-cut rose scent. I love roses (the blooms, the smell, the colors, everything!) so this is a thumbs-up for me. This would be a great Valentine’s Day fragrance! My only complaint is performance seems to be lacking a bit for an EDP. Stays close to the skin. Not a bad thing, but I’m glad I didn’t buy a full bottle, just the travel spray.

At first dismissed this one as another BR540 knock off. It feels similar on opening with the strong ambroxan, and the two have similar silhouettes, but in the light you can’t mistake their differences. But given a few minutes it turns into its own signature of sweet, comforting, woodsy rose treat that makes me think of Turkish delight. It’s hard not to like it. It’s not groundbreaking but I quite enjoy it. Longevity is pretty good, 6+ hours before topping up, and lasts days on clothes. It’s quite affordable but has a rather expensive feel to it, making it a good value for money in my opinion. I live in a desert climate where our winter lows rarely get below 40 degrees Fahrenheit and it’s been wearing beautifully, it projects well enough & it leaves a nice sillage. It’s gotten many compliments. I suspect it will wear well in all but the hottest of weather. This is also one that I can smell on myself throughout the day, which is the best thing about a fragrance to me.

I didn't get much bitter or powdery almond in Jasmins Marzipane. The fragarnce is all about jasmine during the first 3 hours, and a very pretty one at that. The jasmine here is more full-bodied than those primarily relying on the green radiancy of Hedione, sweeter and with a noticeable indolic twang. But compared to Tom Ford Jasmin Rouge and Maître Parfumeur et Gantier Jardin Blanc, it's tamer and has a less complexe olfactory profile. The initial indolic and green nuances soon disappear after about 1 hour. The sweet floralcy of jasmine also becomes more and more nebulous with time. During the 4th and 5th hours, the fragrance sometimes smells very softy of caramelised wild strawberry, probably because the cashmeran becomes more noticeable at this stage, which I perceive as having an abstract berry and woody smell among other things. But ultimately, Jasmins Marzipane would resolve into a clean white musk infused with the vague sweet floracy of jasmine. The vanilla is never explicit on my skin to evoke a truly gourmand caracter, but serves to provide a smooth playground for the dainty jasmine. Jasmins Marzipane has a moderate to soft sillage, and lasts about 8 hours on my skin. Although the smell of Jasmins Marzipane didn't inspire the same awe as its splendid bottle to me, it's pretty charming and easy on the nose, and adheres to the conventional feminine beauty quite well. It's probably not the most innovative, interesting or realistic jasmine fragrances that I tried so far, but it does smells more natural and more sophisticated than a few mainstream offerings. I would recommend it as an easy-going everyday fragrance to jasmine lovers, or to those who are venturing into jasmine fragrances but are still unsure about how much indole one can handle.

I believe that this is the best jasmine perfume I've smelt. The reason is simple: it seems clean and simple but it is interesting instead. when it warms up it develops more deep with this almost leathery facets of the jasmine that are also verging on the almond facets. This would make an excellent bride perfume and I've reviewed it in my wedding appropriate fragrances video review that you can find here below.

Hm, I know a few good fragrances from Lancôme, but this one definitely belongs to the really good ones from this brand. Throughout this comment, I will mention that the scent offers nothing new and that many similar fragrances have been smelled before, but this scent still smells very good and is definitely worth a look in my opinion. I should mention that the scent feels delicious,… and your interest is already piqued :D Or perhaps,… you already know all my clichés where I write about how wonderful women with such great fragrances affect me, and you’re fed up and not even reading further :(((( (I think…. I urgently need new readers here,… he he he :D) But let’s get to the scent. The scent: The fragrance starts with a very beautiful jasmine that smells sweet, accompanied by a floral background. The scent is generally very gentle and soft while also being woody, which should smell pleasant due to the cashmere wood. Of course, there’s also the vanilla, which harmonizes very well with the jasmine (but is weaker in projection than the jasmine) and also adds a certain powderiness. In the far background, I also perceive a slightly fruity note that reminds me of oranges. But the scent is mainly delicate-sweet with vanilla, jasmine, and the soft, woody notes. The sweet jasmine is always the strongest note. And yes, as the name suggests, the scent also smells like marzipan, which I find very delicious. Later, some floral notes appear in the base that are a bit stuffy, but they are more in the background and therefore not so strong. The sillage and longevity: The projection is above average and will be noticeable to others. With a high dosage, there might even be a small scent cloud at first. Later, the scent is not as strong, but it can still be perceived by others. However, after just three hours, I find the scent quite weak… The longevity is not particularly impressive, as after five to six hours the beautiful scent notes have already evaporated, and the fragrance remains only floral and unremarkable. The bottle: Wow… what can I say about it. First of all, the bottle is rectangular like many others. On one side, there is a metal plaque with the name of the fragrance. On the back, there is a plaque with an image of jasmine flowers embossed, and you can peek inside the bottle through the punched-out areas. Since I couldn’t find a photo of the other side, I don’t know exactly what the front looks like, but if it looks like the Parfumo picture here, then the front is clear, allowing you to see the inner wall with the jasmine flowers that were embossed on the plaque on the back. The cap is cylindrical and chrome-plated. All in all, an excellent bottle. I really like the scent, at least regarding the top and heart notes. As mentioned, one must say that the scent offers nothing new and certainly smells like many fragrances with great jasmine, but this one from Lancôme has become one of the particularly good fragrances. It is very sweet and soft, but also feels somewhat elegant, so I can easily imagine wearing it for going out, also for parties and such, because it definitely makes a positive impression. However, one would need to reapply the fragrance for that. It is well-suited for spring and autumn/winter; in summer, it could potentially feel a bit overwhelming if the thermometer shows more than 30 degrees again. Aaaargh, I know you don’t like it when I say it this way, but the scent is delicious. Especially for everyone who loves marzipan, the scent will definitely make the wearer feel yammi yammi :D (Now you’re probably thinking, “aargh, I shouldn’t have read further, it’s always the same thing that DonJuan writes here….”… *sigh*) (And yes, for me, the scent is definitely feminine!) But it’s just delicious. My stomach is growling… and dinner was only a few hours ago…! But, a dessert should still be okay :D I’m craving marzipan,… great… and I just came back from running. Good thing there’s no marzipan at home… … on the other hand… …nooooo, no marzipan at home :(((((((((((((

I really have to keep it short today. I just tested this fragrance, which I received as a little extra from a very lovely participant. Unfortunately, it’s already quite late and my alarm will ring again soon. I was familiar with the name. I expected something different, but I have always been curious. So why not a little fragrance date before the bed cards are punched..? *pff*...hmm..okay? Wait...there! I don’t know why, but the first association: Escada! It smells like the good old classic by Margeritha Ley. I am a child of the 80s. Born in the 70s. In the 90s, I indulged in it. And why? Because it reminded me of something specific (don’t hit me). Perhaps some of you still remember those gumball machines that used to hang on house walls. And among all the colorful gumballs were little rubber figures. As a toddler, I was fascinated. And since I always had to smell everything, the olfactory impression remained. I am fascinated by many things that remind me of the good old days. Lilacs, the sea, apple shampoo, grass, and just things like gumball machine figures. And that’s exactly what Jasmine Marzipane gives me. How I wish I could describe things in lyrical words as beautifully as many of you do. But I tend to be more rational. Although - emotions are somehow involved here too. ?

Actually, I was drawn to “Orange Bigarade” from the same series during my lunch break - without much hope of actually being able to test it. But lo and behold: Our local Karstadt actually has the line! The really quite experienced saleswoman recommended that I also try “Jasmins Marzipane” after some targeted questions about the fragrances I like. I must admit, I was VERY skeptical. The name was really off-putting for me, and in my mind’s eye, I smelled sticky almond mixed with stinky jasmine - probably also with an overdose of vanilla. Horrors!! My (suspicious question) about whether the scent was very almond-heavy was kindly denied by the lady, who described it as “Naturally definitely a jasmine scent, but with a slight freshness that it retains until the end - and no, the jasmine is not stuffy or oppressive, but a very clear, pure scent.” I should give the fragrance some time to develop; at first, it might be a bit overwhelming, especially if you usually wear lighter scents. Hmm: Jasmine and clear and pure? I wasn’t really convinced, but I decided to sacrifice a wrist anyway. And what can I say: At first, it was already VERY overwhelming: A surge of jasmine, jasmine, jasmine - and additionally vanilla. I already saw my worst fears confirmed, but I took a short coffee break and gave the scent half an hour to sort itself out. And it does - and how beautifully! The jasmine really smells just like it does on a balmy summer evening when you sit a little distance away, and the wind gently carries the scent cloud over to you. Not at all like when you bury your nose in the flowers, making the jasmine almost take your breath away. Really quite clear, translucent, and radiant white. The musk is now also detectable - it’s a clean musk that gently envelops the jasmine. The woods serve only to provide flattering support, but they don’t push themselves to the forefront. By the way, I don’t smell marzipan at all - not even much almond! For comparison, I sprayed “L’Instant Magic” by Guerlain on the other arm. The scents are somewhat similar in their impression, and the cuddly factor is high for both. “L’Instant Magic” has this distinct almond aroma - and “Jasmins Marzipane” is more floral - a bit more elegant and mature. As the fragrance fairy at Karstadt promised me, the scent really is accompanied by a delicate freshness that smells a bit like orange juice from very mild fresh oranges. A creamy-powdery-floral scent symphony! A real blockbuster! Will “Jasmins Marzipane” now move in with me? Once again, I struggle with the fact that some fragrances are only available in these large sizes and at correspondingly steep prices. It will definitely be added to the wish list!

At the risk of stepping on some toes. I don't want to badmouth a fragrance that someone enjoys. Opinions, scent preferences, and "skin chemistry" are indeed very varied. This scent smells terrible on me, anyway. I can't really understand why so many people like it at the moment.

I have to say that there are really only a few fragrances that I like so much that I want to wear them myself. One of them is Jasmins Marzipane. Fortunately, I was already warned that the name is misleading and that I shouldn't expect a gourmand. In fact, the fragrance starts with a little jasmine bomb and then becomes increasingly cozy, softer, and more beautiful.

What does one expect from a fragrance with the word marzipan in its name? Something warm, soft, cozy... Unfortunately, I do not experience that at all with this scent. I even find the top note to be rather cool and intrusive. Once you get past it, it does develop into something a bit sweeter.

I first heard about Jasmins Marzipane when I was binge-watching YouTube videos at the beginning of my fragrance passion, and this name kept appearing in various top perfume favorites lists. At that time, I had no idea about a fragrance pyramid or even the individual notes, and for me, it was just "smells great" or "not my thing at all.

A very beautiful perfume with a light gourmet touch, it is very warm, creamy, and pleasant to wear. In the first minutes, the jasmine is very strong, but it fades slightly and gives way to sweet almonds, vanilla, and cashmere. The ingredients feel very high quality and are very well blended. It smells expensive and elegant, and the bottle is wonderful and very feminine.

I absolutely adore Coach Open Road. While it smells fresh, citrusy and aquatic on a test strip, that scent couldn't be more different on my skin. The cologne works with my skin chemistry in a way that turns Open Road into a woody, earthy, sweet, aromatic, and ever so spicy scent that is reminiscent of a more intimate version of Mind Games Gambit to my nose. Open Road being an Eau De Toilette causes it to sit a bit more intimately on my skin. Gambit is one of my favorite fragrances of all time so I love the way this smells. This cologne projects much less than Gambit since the latter is an Extrait De Parfum, however I can't deny that this works with my skin so well that it has become my signature for the summer. I adore the way Open Road smells. I've had it on my skin for about 3 hours now and it still smells just as great as when I first applied it on my skin, granted I did spray it about 10 times after testing it on my wrist to see how I liked the cologne as I had only smelled it on a strip before purchasing it. At the discounter price of $30 I find Open Road to be an absolute steal that shouldn't go unnoticed! It's an excellent fragrance!

I remember when I first got "K" edp by D&G & said..."This nice & woody with a citrusy blood orange background" ..... And after about 1 day I said, no its a big old SOAPY-woody fragrance that doesn't have much depth.... I am no longer a fan of it, atleast for the time being.... . Moving on, I find out Coach has this fragrance called Open Road & it's been described as smelling a lot like K but a little fruitier. & that made me hesitant to actually buy it but I seen the price tag & said, "oh what the hell" it's cheap. I got it & thought this is better than K I see the resemblance, but yes fruitier, smoother & more pleasant. It isn't so aggressively "Soapy", I dnt know why but I can't stand that & in this fragrance is much smoother. It may be the combination of the red apple, citrus & lavender but it is better to me for being way cheaper. . I'd wear this on a Saturday, in the spring or summer when I'm running errands and wanna spray a buncha of something fresh/pleasant & easy to wear on me. While I'm running errands on the "open road". It's perfect for work, the gym or just hanging out at the house. It really does work in a lot of situations but it doesn't project very loud at all, you'll catch slight whiffs, better to hit the pulse points & the cloths as much as you can. Easy buy, check it out

Coach made a quite interesting mix based on an interesting concept of an airy yet spicy and fruity profile. I initially viewed the fragrance skeptically (it smells like D&G K EDT), but I believe it deserves a chance. To me, it stands out due to the Sichuan pepper-Lavender-Vetiver mix as it also brings a slight "player" vibe. But it deserves at least a sniff, as I might not have the same opinion as you'd have for it.

When I purchased 'Open Road' by Coach, I was initially underwhelmed and disappointed. However, I've discovered i prefer this vein of scent over the blue aquatics for the warmer months. In this fragrance, I can see the maturation of preferences in scent. While I expected this to be an aquatic scent, I found 'Open Road' to remind me of 'Terre d'Hermes by Hermes, which i absolutely adore. The cons on the fragrance is in the initial spray and projection. I find it to be fleeting given it's composition and that is disappointing. I am a quite liberal sprayer when it comes to fresh and lighter scents, and I do not smell much trace of it unless I sniff my skin. I do not believe its anosmia, because some scents I can sense throughout the day. I hope at least I smell pleasant to others.

Jean-Christophe Hérault, known as the Ghost Perfumer of Creed's Aventus, has set the bar extremely high for himself with his now legendary masterpiece. "Open Road," which has been relatively sparsely advertised (as can be seen from its popularity), has been available for several months now. Described as a fragrance that is supposed to awaken the spirit of adventure and the desire for freedom (or something like that), it marks the beginning of a new line. Housed in a quite beautiful bottle that somewhat reminds one of Dior's "Homme" line with its central tube, but features a spray head that I find somewhat peculiar (the tester in the perfumery was already damaged), this good piece comes along. The scent development begins, as so often, with a citrusy opening that is particularly sour here. So those who, like me, are not particularly fond of purely lemony top notes will be disappointed. However, soon the red apple joins in, adding a bit of sweetness to the mix; the strong citrus note, as usual, recedes somewhat into the background but remains quite present. The lavender is well dosed and does not come off as scratchy, but rather modern and masculine. From start to finish, the fresh character of the fragrance remains intact. I couldn't really detect the sage, but one shouldn't always be able to pick out every single note - after all, the overall composition counts. In the drydown, woody notes join in without disturbing the balance - the fragrance retains its fresh and light profile. Additionally, there is definitely no noticeable synthetic quality, which is particularly noteworthy for a freshly released freshie (almost a tongue twister). By the way, with a bit of concentration and good will, there is even a minimal (in words: minimal) Aventus vibe here and there, which is not surprising given the perfumer. "Open Road" is a very light fragrance that, in my opinion, was released at the wrong time of year. As a spring release, it would have likely found a much better place, as its light and absolutely non-intrusive ease is perfect for warmer temperatures. Given the current weather, however, it is mercilessly overshadowed, and one won't fill rooms with this scent even in spring. The longevity is okay, but nothing more. In the current price and fragrance class, there are definitely more sensible alternatives. At a discount price, though, one might consider acquiring the fragrance. In conclusion, it can be said that "Open Road" doesn't really do anything wrong, but also nothing particularly special. It ranks in the upper midfield among the plethora of fresh fragrances flooding the market, without being a clumsy clone. Somehow, it just lacks that certain something. Yet its lightness, lack of depth, and at most slightly above-average performance are, to stay positive, just right for a flanker in 2023, which is surely already in the works. I predict a slightly darker liquid, a juicier opening, stronger woodiness in the drydown, and somewhat better longevity and sillage. Such a flanker would definitely be worth a look for me.

While the newer bottles from the leather fashion designer Coach have so far looked very sporty yet stylish, this time they have opted for a new look. The strongly rounded edges remain, but the cap, color scheme, and shape orientation (slimmer instead of wider) are new. The presentation remains modern and classy, and the thing is solidly crafted anyway.

I first heard about the scent in a YT video… when I was planning my USA California road trip, I bought this fragrance - I must say that I choose a scent for every road trip that accompanies me to create memories - the first time I sprayed it was in the morning after showering in Long Beach… and yes… wow… it delivered exactly what I imagined and wished for this trip.

A lighter version of Terre d'Hermès. Not as intense, less spicy, and much more aquatic. Similar in smokiness after the sharp and citrusy top note settles, but very pleasant and unobtrusive. The cedar base stands out the clearest. After a while, it also reminds me of the spicy notes of Roma Uomo, just less oriental. Overall, a good scent for the office.

How wonderful it used to be once upon a time! Even now it's not bad, just more diluted, definitely oak moss was removed from the list of ingredients. The original formula of Magie Noir is phenomenal, heavy, mysterious, full of colors and very elegant. At first it is very compact and dense, but after the first moment that seems a bit harsh, unfolds slowly until the mixture becomes smooth and velvety in the base. It starts quite grassy and aromatic and has from the start much charisma. A strong and vital smell, moist, almost cold. I am sorry for do not feel tuberose, rose instead is perceptible and take a breath with almost ethereal daffodil flowers over an animal-spice mixture. Flower power decreases over time and remains a hot mixture of resin and powdered spices. It is a perfume for strong women but with gentle soul

Grimoires and wands. Potions and philtres. Enchantments and charms. Spells and incantations. Imprecations and anathemas. Allure and enthrallment. Metanoia and lethe. Arcane and occult. Mesmerising and narcotic. Soporific and empyreal. The nemesis of light, the triumph of darkness. Pernicious and wrecking for Hermione Granger. Salubrious and hale for Bellatrix Lestrange. One to pulverise Harry Potter and his likes. One to resurrect Lord Voldemort, only with a full-blown nose this time so as to inhale even the faintest waft of its bewitching nefariousness.
This stuff makes me want to run out and have unprotected reckless sex with the guy you don't take home to mother even if I am way too old for such nonsense. A sex bomb of a fragrance. Luscious.

I considered Magie Noir to be one of my favourite perfumes of all time so what was I thinking when I decided that because I was so fed up with all my niche perfume sampling disasters that this would be safe blind buy (blind buy in the sense that I had not tried the reformulation). I set myself up for disappointment and disappointment I got; I only have myself to blame. I am not usually so unforgiving but right here right now I feel pretty cross that my son (I asked for it for my birthday) dolloped down £37.50 (are they selling this off as it is on offer everywhere?) for this bitter, soapy, watery mess. Old Magie Noir - spicey, woody, oakmoss, rich, deep, dry. New Magie Noir - bitter, soapy, hyacinth and narcissus. Maybe it is the way I smell some of the newer aroma chemicals but I don't call this Magie Noir. Old Magie Noir - develops as it wears on my skin. New Magie Noir - almost linear. Old Magie Noir - blackcurrant done right. New Magie Noir - a very pissy blackcurrant that wears for hours and hours, and dominates all else. Old Magie Noir - sweet animalic musks. New Magie Noir - no discernible animalic notes. Again, all of this is on my skin and of course on someone else or to someone else this new version of the perfume may behave well. For the opening I get a rather bitter soap with a sherberty bergamot, hyacinth and narcissus. It is a very high pitched perfume that does not develop to reveal base notes on me; there seems to be a lot of an artificial citrus smell. I don't get any sweet animal notes, don't find it spicey, and, most surprisingly, I don't detect any oak moss. The pissy blackcurrant kicks in around the 10 minute mark and that, as they say, is that. Extremely harsh, strong, acrid, overpowering. Lasts well over 16 hours on me. Yep, altogether super disappointed with this so I am going to write in indelible ink on my brain, 'Don't you ever buy a reformulation of an old love without sampling it first ever again. Just don't!'. To add insult to injury after a half hour or so it makes my skin itch and triggers migraine with nausea. It's going back. Thank goodness it was bought from a good quality department store with a no questions asked return policy. Eua de toilette purchased October 2016

Magie Noire was never a top fragrance choice for me. Through the years, it has become a cult classic, so I decided to revisit it and purchased a vintage bottle. I've worn it in two seasons before I've written this review, so I can feel I am accurately assessing my thoughts. Back when it was first released, I wasn't a huge fan of this or any of Lancome's perfumes. But with all of the accolades surrounding it, I decided to give it a go again to see what the hoopla is all about. It's definitely a cooler weather perfume. Wearing it above 55 degrees is nauseating. I've discovered that is one of it's flaws and perhaps why some absolutely abhor it. The temperature outside (or inside) must be cool enough for this perfume to work properly. This is a very strange potion. Its aroma wafts and wanes around you, circling its fumes in layers of clouds that hypnotize and entice and mesmerize. How do perfumes create such images? Some scents hit head-on with no looking back, some sit in a corner of a room expectantly, hoping for attention, and others are classics that need no introduction because they are simply elegant members of a family. But Magie Noire swirls around, dances and sings, appears light and floral one moment then impacts hard and deep as a chypre floral that's just very complex. This is not a try it once to decide if you like it perfume. It changes with the seasons, your moods and the climate. It's been called a witch's brew and the moniker fits it well. Although there are many that wear this, only a few can truly pull it off successfully. It's must be worn with an attitude, from the base of your soul , with determination. Heavy on spices and woods, burning with incense and myrhh, musky with patchouli and wrapped in a tight package with a civet's tail, this might or might not be for you. It is a Seductress' perfume, an Enchantress' fragrance, it will bewitch those around you if you are the Femme Fatale wearing it. Certainly not an everyday perfume, and definitely not an office fragrance, Magie Noire is wonderful for an evening soiree or a tete-a-tete supper. This is a strong perfume to use on your pulse points and let the heat of your skin bring it to its fire. Rita Hayworth, Sophia Loren, and Bridgette Bardot could all wear this perfume easily. Radiates strongly if you're not careful and lasts for hours and hours.

I am not a fan of wearing chypres. Plain and simple. I'm certainly intrigued by them and I have some in my personal collection but they are fragrances that often perplex me. Sometimes they even intimidate me. My chypres are the ones I grab most often, just to simply sniff and admire. I don't wear them often. They frighten me a bit in their complexity.

From reading about the evolution of Magie Noire from 1978 until 2011, I think that it has always been a grab-bag of a perfume. Early versions sound like they emphasized different facets than this most recent one. It sounds like they used to bridge the dark floral chypre to the spicy oriental via some old-school animalics.

"Magie Noire" is a bit daunting to review, most of us know it. It's the notorious sorceress among Orientals. Love or hate: indifference is in my opinion not possible with this scent. From the opening notes of heavy rose and jasmine we move quickly to a smokey amber with a faint but stubborn high note of bergamot in the mix.

This fragrance surprised me. I didn't actually recognise this fragrance because it was bottled in a green rectangular-shaped bottle. The way it had been packaged made me assume that it was going to be a citrusy/green scent. I was truly amazed when I discovered that it wasn't. Magie Noire is a soft, slightly musky and pretty floral fragrance.

This scent doesn't project on me. Though the top note is hypnotically entrancing--reeking as it swiftly does of 3 from my current magic combo (Jasmine, Tuberose, Lily of the Valley)-- it swiftly vanishes into the other notes and stays close to my skin. Since I wear perfume principally for my own enjoyment, the inability to smell one after only moments is a real downer.

I like the Coach fragrances. They have a touch of romance that reminds me of the tranquil country life and my youth. In our carriage house, there is an old Landauer that I would have loved to ride to my wedding. Time and again, I lifted the cover under which this gem rests, and time and again I imagined how it would look if it were freshly polished and hitched up. But it remained just an idea - for the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak. I would have had to spend days polishing the Coach. So I zoomed off to the church in the dented Range, which was also uncleaned. There was still some straw on the seats - but my beloved said: Straw makes you happy. But the Coach fragrances awaken my girlhood dreams again. And floral blush in particular. This soft sweetness mixed with berry notes has a hold on my nose. The wood note is also smooth and light. A country drive in bright summer - or in golden autumn. I again have images of Rosamunde Pilcher in my mind. Could we not make my dream come true? Reality reaches me on the phone: If you clean the Landauer - I will hitch it up for you. You know where the bucket and cloths are. That doesn’t sound like a Pilcher film - I think the romantic scent will be enough for me.

Summary: I would roughly describe the scent as floral-fruity and fresh. In my opinion, it is more suitable for younger women. It is not a special fragrance; it strongly reminds me of La vie est Belle EDT combined with Tresór - Midnight Rose. The longevity is not appropriate for the price and an EDP, in my view. Detailed Review: Maybe it’s my nose, even though the described 'notes' don’t have much in common: somehow this fragrance reminds me very much of La vie est Belle EDT with a hint of rose, only that the Coach scent is a bit fruitier and doesn’t come off as powdery. Furthermore, I find that the longevity of La Vie est Belle EDT [!] is much better than this EDP... I don’t know what Goji berry smells like 'in nature' - I certainly don’t smell it out ;-) *'Hint': somewhat 'spirity', rosy, sweet-berry [similar to the 'raspberry' in Tresor: Midnight Rose], maybe a bit of blood orange for the 'citrusy freshness' *Middle Note: Rose, raspberry - which peach? - since the scent fades very quickly, you hardly smell anything of this... *Base Note: Towards the end, if you can still perceive anything at all, a musk note remains... The fragrance is by no means bad, but it is also nothing special; you’ve smelled it a hundred times before - I would have expected more from the brand Coach, which is particularly known for good men’s fragrances... The Otto Kern: Commitment drugstore scent for less than half the price lasts longer. * Bottle: Typical design from Coach with a slightly different sprayer than other perfumes, pink-rose watercolor gradient. The logo is 'pressed' into the glass, under the sprayer is a pink plate in pink leather [look], to which a hibiscus flower charm in leather [look] is attached. Tastes can be debated, but it does seem a bit kitschy. In my opinion, there are prettier, more individual, and higher-quality bottles in this price range, e.g. La vie est belle, Versace Eros, Versace Dylan Blue.

“I've been everywhere, man, Looking for someone, Someone who can please me Love me all night long…” ok enough with Rihanna! All I want to say is that this is what I feel about this fragrance!! I don’t like summer fragrances or citrusy scents or aquatic scents which are more appropriate scents for hot weather. I sure enjoy coconut and fruity scents but everything I have found has some disadvantage which is usually the performance. I mean I know it can’t smell all day on my skin with 40 degrees of Celsius outside , but at least let me reach work place smelling it!!! If you have any suggestions for summer scents that last a decent amount of time, please feel free to leave me a comment and I would be very grateful!! This fragrance is a gourmand creamy scent with dominant peach and coconut that has a great performance! It can even last all day on my skin and clothes if I spray a bit more than usual! If you like peach, you will love it! It’s very well blended and gives a summery vibe without being a typical freshie scent. I remember I loved la nuit tresor but I haven’t smelled it for a long time in order to compare it with this. I usually don’t smell releases like this because they are copies of the original but this one didn’t remind me of something I ve smelled before! Since I started this hobby with fragrances, I don’t have a signature scent because I can’t stick to one fragrance for long! But this one I believe it will be my signature scent for summertime! If you love gourmands and peach you should definitely try it! Thank you for your time!! Be safe and smell great! Maria

Usually I like the Coconut note in perfumes as long as it is part of a mix. As a single note it can get too much. Terracotta Le Parfum by Guerlain, Alien Goddess and Hypnotic Poison are all three great loves of mine. Especially Terracotta has a rather distinct Coconut note among the others. I was therefore looking forward to meeting La Nuit Trésor Nude. But something about it bothers me and the only reason I can come up with is the nutty/creamy expression that reminds me of a special kind of hard brown sugar candy with some kind of spicy taste. I do not like these. Back when I was a kid I remember we used to visit a friend of my grandma’s. She always gave us this particular dark, brown candy and we were too polite to say no. I soon found a way to get to the bathroom and spit it out. It had a chocolate-y spicy dark taste - nothing I was used to. And I have never learned to like it. La Nuit Trésor Nude has a note that smells like this particular candy. I am quite sure that I will not learn to like it. But I have decided to give it a try since it so highly rated. Maybe it is an acquired taste. Maybe I will grow to like it… as with coffee, red wine, coriander and olives. Who knows? Year 2, 52/365

I admit - I don't like being undressed. Collective nudity bothers me even more - so much so that I avoided the family sauna at home. It was creepy during a vacation in Sardinia when the whole group joyfully stripped off their clothes on the beach. Ah - everyone was so free and carefree! And so natural! For me, it's not natural to run around and sit naked all day long - I find it very uncomfortable. I obeyed the peer pressure - but I found the back-to-nature behavior silly. Moreover, undressed people have a different scent than those who are dressed. And this skin note also greets me in Nude. The peach rolls sweetly over it and coconut veils the scent milky - but I still perceive this slightly sweaty note that doesn't want to keep its distance. I feel uncomfortably undressed - and I start to feel cold. Maybe I would like this phenomenon in summer - but today I set the Nude bottle aside - and instead bought myself a soft warming scarf.

Like a hortus conclusus, a closed garden often surrounded by walls or impenetrable thickets that refuses the gaze of the curious, La Nuit Trésor nude presents itself. A completely self-contained, delicious fragrance that only opens its access to the familiar. The hortus conclusus, a frequent theme in medieval art, thrived on what it wanted to conceal, thus stimulating the imagination of the observer. This little garden has always been a symbol of woman, of the unfathomable feminine, whether in sensual desire or in religious glorification in relation to Mary. The woman remained unfathomable, not revealing her innermost feelings, not losing herself in the chatter of everyday life. Understanding her, penetrating her thoughts and motives, was equally the desire of men and believers. Such a hortus conclusus is also La Nuit Trésor nude. At first, you feel transported into a beautiful, summery garden by the fruity freshness created by the skillful interplay of peach and bergamot. You lie under a large tree, its lush green foliage providing pleasant shade. Bees buzz, it is wonderfully warm, and the scent of blossoms spreads. Exotic hints of coconut blend gently with the scent of rose; you dream further into summer, to distant beaches, into foreign gardens. No scent dominates here, the coconut is extremely mild and only provides a gentle sweetness, which is further intensified by the multifaceted floral aromas of the rose, gaining depth. The fragrance is incredibly mild and soft, enchantingly subtle, calming, soothing, murmuring like the gentle splashing of a fountain in a garden surrounded by high, shady walls. The skin of juicy peaches, the delicate strips of fresh coconut, the roses all around provide a moment of greatest relaxation; you let yourself fall completely, feeling free and carefree in this moment. Velvety and fine, the fragrance lies above you, barely perceptible waves of vanilla and caramel approach you, a summer afternoon snack, a sweet moment. The fragrance is perfectly pure and balanced in its components, indescribably feminine and soft, for the unique moment you spend alone in the garden, in cozy warmth, in light summer dreams. A gem is also the beautiful bottle, whose soft colors and delicate shimmer perfectly reflect this mildness. There is a lasting durability over many hours, during which the fragrance enchants with a gentle, not too strong sillage. For me, it is by far the most beautiful of the series, because it is so incomparably mild and made for an hour spent entirely alone with oneself.

When I found out that a new flanker from the La Nuit Trésor line was soon to be released, I was on fire! I was practically obsessed with testing this new fragrance! :D I drove everyone in my family crazy with how excited and curious I was about the new Trésor flanker!

This is my very first comment here; I have thought for a long time about which fragrance to choose for this. Once I made my choice, I also wanted to find the time to do this scent justice. I am trying to do that now while my baby sleeps beside me, and her scent, mixed with a hint of "Nude," surrounds me. This blend is - with all due respect - simply divine.

I was as excited as a bowstring about the new Tresor. Finally!!!! no blackcurrant. How I hate that berry, it has ruined all La Nuit's for me. That extremely sweet-sour *shudder* ugh no. In Musc Diamant it’s not there, but unfortunately the raspberry (another one of my shaky candidates) was too present for me and the longevity and sillage were too bland.

Okay folks, you have to admit that you probably expected me to come up with a comment on this fragrance too, right? The screaming perfume that you surely know, which raves about these scents here, had long begged me to test this fragrance line (he he :D), but I came across the latest one all by myself!

When I read the first comments here, I immediately fell in love with the scent. It could only be a magical fragrance!! On the first day, I had little success... I couldn't find it anywhere here, some sellers didn't even know about this scent and looked at me as if I were talking nonsense... The next day, it was finally available, I wanted to buy it blindly, as I often do...

Maybe I had somewhat high expectations, but this was a hard no for me. I love my masculine fragrances just as much as my neutral and feminine leaning fragrances. They all have an appropriate mood for an appropriate time. Coach for Men EDP is masculine in a way that smells very dated and not in a good way. One can smell dated and still be classy. This however, smells unapproachable and unappealing to my nose.

i wish i could smell this and not make a comparison to anything else, but this is sauvage elixir's poor cousin. it's gently less sweet than elixir, with but it brings nothing else to the table, nothing new nothing exploratory. it's a generic men's freshy, perfect for the spring/summer seasons coming up

I really like perfumes that remind me of things. Since I find the concept of the Library of Fragrances cool, I thought I could order two samples, as there was a 2 for 1 deal on the homepage. I ultimately chose Lavender Martini and Provence Meadow. The scent notes listed by Demeter are: fennel, basil, thyme, lavender, and rosemary. However, the fragrance does not smell like that at all. Instead, it is an ode to a terribly overpowering, artificial lemon scent and alcohol. After the test spray, the guy asked me if I had a booze smell. A statement couldn't be clearer. The bottle now sits in our bathroom to eliminate odor traces when something has spilled again - after all, the bottle is recyclable and I can use it for other purposes later.

My mom LOVES Tresor In Love and I'm In LOVE with Tresor. :o) Could you go wrong with either one? I don't think so. They are both elegant perfumes, Tresor being the more original and mysterious, in my humble opinion. At first spritz my nose picked up the fresh fruity opening of bergamot, nectarine, peach, and pear. This wasn't as "wet" an opening as most Escada perfumes. This wasn't a lush, tropical opening. It was "almost" dry fruits (at least in my perception.) The slightly citrusy nectarine/peachy scent then stayed about 10 mins before the Turkish rose/jasmine kicked in. However, note that in this floral phase, the wonderful signature nectarine scent of Tresor continued and gave the flowers a VERY sweet but non-cloying edge. After about 2 hours, the base note, which is supposed to be cedar, was really mild (at least on my skin.) So it became a sweet, nectarine-ish, floral, ever-so-mildly woody fragrance. Staying power is poor and so is the projection. Fades away too fast. It also stayed too close to my skin; unlike its predecessor which has incredible projection, sillage, and staying power. If you find the original Tresor difficult/cloying/heavy to wear, you could try this one. It's an awesome fruity floral. But it's still not as unique as the original - which I STILL prefer.

I was delighted to realise that Tresor In Love smelt nothing like the disastrous Tresor on my skin. The only similarity is the peach note, however in this fragrance it is not dry or bitter smelling. In the case of these two perfumes we've gone from one extreme to the next. Tresor was unique but so different to the point that it almost made me nauseous, whereas Tresor In Love is likable and soft, yet a little too generic for my tastes. This fragrance opens with a soft, delicate array of fruits, with the pear and peach being most dominant. The rose and jasmine come through only seconds after the initial fruity opening, making Tresor In Love a very feminine yet predictable fragrance. While classic, elegant and somewhat romantic, I can't help feeling as if Lancome has tried to emmulate Coco Mademoiselle through the release of this fragrance. To me they smell quite similar. The drydown is a musky cedar blend, that settles with a slight sense of masculinity. Although I didn't expect to like this fragrance because of my distaste for the original Tresor, I guess I wanted something more from Tresor In Love that I didn't receive. I do like the bottle. The small black rose, made of ribbon around the cap is both classy and quaint. It is hard not to be enchanted by its design, however the scent leaves much to be desired.

Tones and Tones of roses very distinctive smell...violet and musk..i don't think it can be compared to Tresor because tresor original belongs to another category of perfumes that is very classical floral/peachy .. In Love is different ,refreshing (i can smell pear among all the fruits),romantic,elegant and rose-y ...perfect for all weather wearing , day/night and special occasion too!

This 2010 fragrance is absolutely sublime! It’s the perfect balance between light and strong. Nuanced top notes of nectarine, pear, pink pepper and bergamot form a heavenly blend that captures your attention but doesn’t sting your nostrils. The pear is the real stand-out and overall it reminds me of sweet herbal tea. Peach makes up some of the middle notes as well, but combined with rose, violet and jasmine is becomes less fruity and more floral. I can’t detect much of the musk in the base notes but the cedar is the best finish. The whole fragrance experience is unexpectedly beautiful and I can’t recommend it enough. Additionally, the bottle is charming! The little cloth rose is a nice touch.

Right on the first working day of 2022, I experienced a discovery and a crush: After the original vault seemed too bulky and overwhelming to me, and Midnight Rose was far too expansive and unrefined - I never showed much interest in the vault fragrances again. But yesterday, on my way home, I passed by the large train station M and saw a last bottle of In Love on the promotional table... the color attracted me, as I have been looking for a suitable peach scent for a long time. And I sprayed ... immediately, a refreshing and inviting, bright fruitiness enveloped me! I spontaneously took the last bottle with me and gave up something else for which I had actually come. Now I am testing it on both wrists in a delayed manner: The opening, as Schnuffi aptly describes, indeed initially resembles a fruit brandy - alcohol with pear. The nectarine indicated in the above scent profile is not distinctly noticeable, but I think it makes the pear significantly juicier and softens the sharpness of the emerging bergamot. The nectarine is there for a sweet rounding, no doubt. The sharpness quickly subsides with the emergence of fresh bergamot with a hint of soft floral notes behind it - I would have called it undifferentiated floral on its own, but reading the pyramid allows me to attribute the lovely, wafting quality to jasmine and to perceive a violet note flashing here and there. Now, for my taste, too much sweetness would unfold if a cheeky rose with stem and leaves didn’t appear to cool the aura with its proud demeanor. Here, for the first time, something subtly woody is added very quietly. This is really well balanced and forms a harmonious framework for the note that I have been seeking as the centerpiece of a good fragrance for years: the subtly peppered peach with its velvety, seductive melt. It reigns in the center of this scent composition: mild and ripe and creamy - la peche dominates, flanked by the violet, which modestly spirals around it, and unfolds this feminine scent into something very seductive that envelops the wearer softly while still radiating a calm self-confidence. It lasts for about 7 to 8 hours and gradually becomes less noticeable after 4 to 5 hours, retreating into a skin-close creaminess. With this perfume, one can feel revitalized, sensually and comfortably throughout the day, and make a feminine statement that is in no way intrusive. The opposite of shrill yet still fruity-fresh. A sophisticated everyday fragrance, by no means arbitrary. I am considering whether this could become my signature scent for spring and summer, as The Only One, with its coffee-violet note, is clearly made for the cooler season. But In Love can be worn not only in spring and summer but also well in autumn and winter. So anytime ;-) And who wants to sit sulking in their chamber, letting life pass by without any fruitiness, sweetness, and a touch of playful sophistication?

Since the "mother" Tresor was able to gradually, but thoroughly win me over, I gladly embrace her children. Tresor in Love is a pretty, delicate - and sensitive daughter. It is a thoughtful girl who loves to read and enjoys her daydreams. Unfortunately, I only know Paris from passing through, but this city touches me as well.

Personally, I don't like it when peach takes the lead in a perfume. However, if it subtly complements the rest, I find that very pleasant. I bought Trésor in Love after trying it only on a test strip. I fell in love with the scent. I've always liked the heavier original. But I was glad to snag a fresher, younger version that still quietly reminds me of the original.

Sorry, here comes a nose again, with two souls residing in its chest. On one hand, I would sell my father-in-law and mother-in-law for nude, clean, and tart fruity scents. On the other hand, I consider the original "Trésor" a stroke of genius made of peach, amber, and Lancôme.

"Trésor in Love" came to me through a blind swap. Until then, I had only had good experiences with the fragrances from the Trésor line and thought that with another perfume from the series, you couldn't go wrong. When the swapped fragrance arrived along with the other exchanged scents, I was astonished: I already knew this one!

I breathe you in and never out again Lock yourself in my heart Don't let yourself out again Thus begins a beautiful song by Philipp Poisel, and that's exactly how my love for Tresor in Love started. With the first sniff, I was done for. This wonderfully fresh bergamot-peach scent makes you so likable, jasmine makes you seem fine and delicate... ah...

I can't believe this is an La Vie est Belle flanker! Not that I hate the original or anything, but this is very different and so much better. It's a powdery and fruity scent that smells a bit like an expensive sheer lipstick, but with some extras. The most noticeable note right from the start is a fresh, natural raspberry that doesn't lean overly syrupy. I can also smell violet leaf clearly, and some of its flower, too, even if the latter is not in the notes list. A touch of soft leather perfects it all. I don't know if I would have identified the cacao butter on my own without the notes list, but as I know it's there, I can pick it up. Especially in the beginning and when sprayed on my skin. It adds a touch of warmth, a very slight cacao-ish scent, just like a cacao butter lotion would. It's a subtle, but interesting addition to this cosmetic-like scent. L'Elixir has some sweetness to it, but it's not a heavy gourmand like the original LVEB, it's more elegant, more floral, missing the patchouli and the fizziness that LVEB is famous for. I understand why some people voted for this to be similar to Guerlain fragrances like French Kiss, Rose Chérie and Insolence. It definitely goes into this direction! I find all of those more powdery though. They have Guerlain DNA and this is undeniably a Lancôme release. Maybe it's the rose note or something about the texture, I think you have to smell it and see the difference for yourself. To me, this scent feels special, it gives me a magical, sparkling, optimistic feeling I really didn't expect here. Think of an evening before a party, with the sky fading from pink to dark blue and the stars coming out, listening to a perfect pop song. I can't explain it any better, I just love it. A perfect balance of warm and cool, powdery and juicy, sweet and fresh.

The first time I tried this fragrance, I wasn’t sure. It was winter time and I felt the scent was too bright. Now that it’s warming up here, I can’t get enough of it. I love the fresh raspberry and violet combined with the warmer notes. It just may be my new #1 among a collection of many. I also love Soleil Cristal, but there is something about the freshness of L’Exlixir that I absolutely crave currently. It’s gorgeous!

I really LOVE this fragrance, it's very different from the others "la vie est belle", which are most of the time super flowery/fresh. The "elixir" flanker is a funnier version with a very sweet raspberry/ greenish violet twist. It has an incredible jammy-syrupy-soft raspberry and sweet, but green violet. Weirdly said, the perfume is made in a way of never becoming overpowering and always super soft. I can literally spray a hundred times and still be obsessed with that perfume (hopefully I don't spray that much lmao). Something about it that is SO addictive, makes it easy to love. I'm a fan of the juice color as well, so pretty.

nice sparkly raspberry opening. kind of like a soda. as it dries, it becomes more creamy and smooth, the raspberry still prominent. i am not a raspberry girl, it can quickly become cloying for me, but I can appreciate that it is done nicely. after the raspberry fades it becomes very light and ethereal. i imagine its what a fairy would smell like. I'm getting violet, powdered sugar, and something tart, grounded by the cacao butter. i can see why you would compare it to Celeste, but it is just a tad less nauseating without the lime - and not as vanilla-heavy. very similar to dama bianca too edit: I wore 2 sprays of this today and I had gone noseblind to it after a few hours; however, when I got home, one of my family members asked why it smelled like perfume. we weren't even in the same ROOM. one of my other family members said they smelled it on me in response. so other people will smell you a lot more than you will smell yourself wearing this.

I've been searching for the perfect sophisticated woman scent. I believe I've found it! I spent fall/winter of 2024 wearing this almost exclusively. I'm not certain if anything I say can do it justice. La vie est belle L'Elixir opens as if you've freshly uncorked raspberry wine. It unfolds into violet. Some days it smells like candy. Other days, it's similar to violet leaf. It finishes off with cocoa butter, rendering you practically edible. Leather and cedarwood provide balance, though to my nose, they stay behind the scenes. I don't personally detect rose or bergamot, which is great (I hate bergamot). L'Elixir is exquisite. It is nothing like the original La vie est belle or the other flankers. She is the true diva, one that commands attention when she enters the room. (Seriously, a few dabs are enough. A full spray can be too intoxicating.) Her only downfall is her headlining show is limited to the colder months. She would certainly risk overexposure if she appeared in the spring or summer. I do hope she'll stick around for years to come.

This rose-raspberry combination is very well executed and the perfume feels charming and feminine. I don`t know what the original Vie est Belle smelled like, but I quite enjoy this. The raspberry is fruity-sweet, but lacks its dose of Vitamin C, making it more candy-like and less astringent. There was a touch of citrus in the opening, but it disappears almost immediately.

I am typically a fan of "sweet" scents, think Good Girl Glam, Angel Nova, Black Opium over Red... that sort of vibe. I was interested in LVEB Elixir after seeing the scent notes, even though the OG LVEB I'm not a fan of. I received a sample of Elixir and on initial sniff, I thought it was going to be an instant success. Sprayed on (once!

I personally enjoy the original LVEB and have owned it several times, though it isn't a staple in my small collection. I haven't really gravitated towards any of the flankers, either, but happened to come across this version at Ulta and gave it a try a couple times.

Most of the time, the La Vie Est Belle line is a miss for me, and it's entirely the fault of the patchouli that is included in almost every scent. There only three flankers I've tried that are an exception to the patchouli rule: Vanille Nude, Rose Extraordinaire, and L'Elixir; of those three, I own the latter two.

This perfume isn't excesively sweet. At the first spray, I feel a blast of raspberry with some drops of liquor. I definetly smell the boozyness but it is perfectly delivered. Is not the alcoholic blast that you smell in different perfumes at the beginning. I really like this perfume. it is a raspberry liquor with some flowers.

I do not understand why the reviews do not match what I smell (no gummy bears, no cough syrup), and I do not understand why patchouli is not listed here and not mentioned in the reviews. It is what makes this scent distinctive to me. The sillage is lovely, and it is pleasant. I love Jasmine in perfumes, and that note comes through here. Not “florals” but Jasmine. On the other site they mention rose. I heard Parfumo has the accurate (company’s) notes not some crowd suggestion, but in this instance I think it is lacking. What is listed here seems inaccurate to what I smell as do the reviews. Anyhow, I discovered it this summer, and it performed well in the heat. I will keep wearing it in the winter since it is an easy reach. Delights me each time.

Coachd dreams moonlight is like let's throw everything into the cauldron and see what happen and they stopped right before it turns bad, it's weird but not weird weird it's kind of a goop of synthetic and nondescriptive scent that playing hide and seek with you To me this smells like if you take a sweet cough syrup and pour some floral water into it and garnish it with gummy bears and now we have one ticket to tummy ache town but it smells rather nice. This smells kind of synthetic and medicinal to my nose with a touch of vanilla, something vaguely floral, white floral and it is all mushy and mellowy feels like what a sleeping potion would smell like but rather than gently luring you to sleep this would be one sip and you're drop to the floor

I love Sicily, and especially the city of Messina. I enjoyed wandering through the streets and alleys there, feeling transported back to ancient times. What stories might the old, well-kept houses have witnessed? Perhaps Goethe strolled and lingered here? It is already dark and the moon hangs silver in the sky as I board a carriage drawn by a beautiful white horse. Slowly and leisurely, he takes me through the evening city, past white villas that dream in the lush Sicilian gardens. Floral scents mixed with bergamot reach my nose, and the swaying of the carriage gently lulls me. There is something sweet in the air. Could it be tonka? The melodic sound of hooves comes to an end; we have arrived at our destination. I thank the little horse and the coachman for this lovely journey.

No initial blast of alcohol when sprayed which is quite nice. I'm greeted by a fresh uplifting bergamot zing. It quickly fades in the background as I'm swept away by the feminine, soft, light, airy and ethereal roses. I was pleasantly surprised: the roses are not too young (sickeningly sweet) or too old (powdery), they're just right. No wonder this perfume is a staple and a classic. I could also smell a bit of salt note, but I felt it was there to add an intricate and delicate layer to the star of this fragrance. Jasmine does appear shyly to impart a nice creamy aspect as the fragrance moves towards the bottom notes. I'm finally left with a nice drydown composed of vanilla and musky accord. It's an overall nice feminine fragrance and a lovely interpretation of salted roses with vanilla. I'll probably be getting a travel spray for my collection!

This smells like a beautiful bronze goddess eating Turkish delight by the sea; her hair is effortlessly wavy, and her skin smells sunkissed, salty, creamy & warm. I like the sweet and salty aspect of this fragrance, out of the Idole line, it’s the only one I enjoy. The hot weather brings out the best in this fragrance. It smells so different to me right now that the temperature is cooler; the salt and solar aspect aren’t as present but instead smells more like milky rose water.

I received a sample of this perfume in the mail and loved it so much that I caved and bought a full size bottle. I find that the longevity is actually better because I spray more than I could with the sample bottle and it stays on my clothes. It is a lovely rose vanilla fragrance that I enjoy a lot more than the original Idole. The bottle itself could be better, with perhaps a little bit of iridescence on it. The price point is good.

Sometimes I get a salty rose that it is comfortable to my soul, other times I get some fresh dill and sometimes for some reason I get watermelon. She is a bit of a black sheep when it comes to the other flankers and the OG, but I love her nevertheless. I am a fan of salty, vanilla notes that are not too thick and overwhelming (looking at you, Olympea ) so this hits the spot for me.

The salty vanilla compliments the fresh, almost solar rose notes very well. This was the first time I had a perfume give me a scent association, which was twofold: the various beaches my family had visited on vacations past, and the beautiful bouquet of fancy “Princess Maya” roses I had ordered myself for my 30th birthday. Those roses were absolutely gorgeous and the longest-lasting flowers I’ve had to date, with an amazing fragrance. Idôle Aura made me crave another bouquet, and another trip to the beach. It made me feel nostalgia and wanderlust at the same time; with a sprinkle of romanticism. Out of the three Idôle flankers I own, this one is perhaps the weakest when it comes to longevity, but that also depends on how well I moisturize and what the weather/air around me is like (dry, humid, hot, cold, etc.). The bottle is still the iconic thin Idôle rectangle, but with a pretty white fog/ombré that symbolizes the salted note well. It isn’t quite as pretty as the peach ombré on the Now flanker, or the rainbow sheen on the Nectar flanker, but I do still like to look at it. I do think this is primarily a summer scent, being so beachy and solar, but it can chase the winter blues away any time you need a mental break from cold, grey, dreary weather. I know I’ve used it for a sensory escape now and then.

Finally, a salt fragrance for women where the salt truly stands out! It is accompanied by a floral creaminess with roses, woods, and jasmine; only in the base does the vanilla appear lightly and the musk abundantly. The scent also clearly reminds me of 'Olympea' with its blend of salt, vanilla, and a somewhat sultry and stuffy floral note.

I tested all 3 Idoles. During the first testing, I liked the intense the best. The Idole Aura came across as very salty to me during the first sniff, which I don't particularly like. So I ordered the intense online, and... here it comes - it came with a 5 ml sample of Idole Aura. I thought to myself, okay, I'll give the sample a chance and test Aura more thoroughly...

Since I like the original Idole, I was very pleased to receive the Aura sample. I sprayed it out of curiosity - but unfortunately in the dim lighting of the living room, so the first spray landed in my right eye. Ouch instead of Aura! With tear-filled eyes, I reached the saving bathroom, where I first gave my crying eye a few splashes of water.

On my YouTube channel, I made a comparison to the other two Idôles (in English) and described this new one here. I would be happy if you stopped by! This scent has a very interesting twist due to the salt note, which gives it a certain spiciness without being spicy in the sense of classic spices.
Surprise, this Idôle. Two compliments on the very first day, that doesn’t happen too often. And it imparts a certain buoyant cheerfulness without coming off as superficial. Very French!

And I love it. I was in Ulta perusing the fragrance section. I saw the Coach Gold display and the pretty gold bottle. I looked at the description which states an “ambery-floral parfum, inspired by sun-drenched brilliance. Pink peppercorns, almond blossoms, vanilla.” I wasn’t sure what to expect because that’s not typically notes I gravitate towards. Other than Amber and vanilla. But I sprayed it on a test strip and liked it quite a bit. I decided to spray it on my wrists and try it out for the day. I couldn’t stop lifting my wrists to my nose to smell it. It’s somewhat similar to Burberry Goddess, Xerjoff Lira and other similar fragrances, but doesn’t have the distinct lavender. I really liked the vanilla and amber notes with a hint of pink peppercorn and a light floral blend. This might be my new favorite 2025 release.

I have heard interesting stories about how this fragrance smells from person to person. I initially loved the way it smelled on paper and the associate suggested trying it on. My elatedness and surprise were equally scaled. Coach Gold is my favorite designer release of the year. While Coach for Men EDP was a major disappointment, the women’s release had such a great impression on me that I purchased it for myself. On my skin it opened up similar to Mercedes Benz Club Black, then transformed into something very warm in the family of Guerlain Spiriteuse Double Vanille and Akro Glow. It is surprisingly unisex. There is a whisper of fruitiness after time, but the composition is not at all fruity. There also aren’t enough flowers to constitute a floral presence. Traditionally, this is what you would call an oriental vanilla. Vanilla and Amber are key players all the way through and if not for the pink pepper, it probably wouldn’t have been as appealing to me personally. Louise Turner does wonderful work with vanilla such as, Blanche Bête by Liquides Imaginaires, TF Lost Cherry, Musc Infini by Ex Nihilo, I Want Choo Forever Jimmy Choo, Eau de Star by Thierry Mugler and Good Girl & Good Girl Supreme. A great collaboration for this release.

Let me start with saying that I live too far away from a perfumery and usually buy samples to test fragrances. But if I have the opportunity to visit any kind of perfume shop, I want to take a full advantage of it...if you know what I mean... This fragrance captivated me with its simplicity, which managed to charm me with something among at least a dozen of scents that I tested that day....and to be honest, if I were to choose that fragrance based on its notes, I would never even buy a sample of it. Why? Because the notes totally fail to convey the magic hidden in this bottle...only the name of that fragrance fits here perfectly.. Gold is simply beautiful, clean, cosy, creamy and somehow addictive. It's something I've been looking for for a long time, but nothing has met my expectations...until that day. Usually such fragrances are soapy and boring to me. This one is different. This one definitely deserves more attention. And I think, I don't need to add, that Gold is now in my collection

I am not going to launch into the whole philosophy behind Demeter single note scents. They are wearable, inexpensive and when you want to smell, very specifically like Watermelon Jollyranchers, Lobster, A Crust of Bread, Pruning Shears, Fire Flies, Church Incense, Hot Toddy or Dirt--- this is the best collection for that niche. These are low risk and great for experimenting/layering...although they never satisfy my deeper need for Art Bottles and Niche fragrances- they do come in handy at times...need your house to smell of fresh baked breads, yummy tea time treats and an English garden? Demeter's Earl Grey tea, Gingerbread cookie, Lavender, Greenhouse and Ivy will weave a delicate ol'factory extravaganza that will fool all your guests! So, Saltwater Taffy was something I didn't order or request that just showed up in my last order from Demeter and in spite of all that, I find it noteworthy. It is obviously sweet and I must say, I am not a fan of cloying sweet fragrances in general. In spite of this... I find Saltwater Taffy is wearable and even alluring because the dry down is a fairly believable toasted coconut and buttery powder cloud.
