I personally wouldn't pay much more than free for this time of composition, but since it was free...I am going to wear this this summer and enjoy it as I enjoy cotton candy, ice cream and roller skating in the Summer but never really admit it to any one else. What do I detect in this bottle? Toasted coconut cream pie (an edible note as opposed to a synthetic suntan lotion coconut) an carmelized spun sugar note- that is subtle-not overwhelming or nauseating and a salt air note that is again, not too synthetic of over-the-top salty so it never veers into "Low Tide by the sea shore" territory. Overall- surprisingly good for layering and I am definitely going to wear it this summer. Strictly for Cooney Island and Boardwalk fun, but...Give it a try!

This fragrance is absolutely wonderful. Superb in fact. I had chosen the perfect day to test O de Lancome. A rather humid Summer day in the centre of a busy and steamy city. I must say that at first the citrus notes came on quite strongly. It was very green and lemony. Although not entirely unpleasant, I was expecting the worst seeing that these fragrances don't seem to agree with my chemistry or my nose very often. I was about to write this scent off the list when I brought my wrist up to my nose for another sniff. I was met with a delightful, fresh and cheerful blend of honeysuckle, various herbs/spices, jasmine and mild citrus notes. On my skin the heart and drydown was soft, slightly soapy, musky and feminine. I can't say that I understand the masculine references. To me O de Lancome is girly and somewhat sweet, in other words something I can't imagine a man wearing. I had no idea that this was a fragrance from the 70's, it is very modern and could easily pass as something being produced today. The lasting power is average, around 7 hours. I do recommend this.
Dark citrus with a touch of florals. After a regular cologne, the moss in Ô makes it feel like sunglasses on a bright day.

From a very young age I remember Ô de Lancôme. To me, it is the smell of summer. A smell of freshly cut citrus fruits and of chopped herbs. The sandalwood and oak moss ground the scent so it does not disappear instantly. Every summer I went to see my grandparents. Being at their place was an endless row of days with sunshine and loads of exciting things to do. Or so I recall it. My grandparents lived outside the city and they had a huge garden and an old garage with an attic full of things, such as old magazines, a piano and hundreds of jazz records. My brother and I spent hours going through all this. We played the piano and listened to the records. We read loads of Donald Duck and Superman. No one came to check if we behaved. It was great! My grandmother wore this fragrance. She always smelled so good and she wore it all year round. It stood on the shelf in the bathroom and I went there many times during the day just to smell it. She passed away way too early - she was in her mid sixties. At the funeral - I was ten years old - I thought I could smell the perfume in church. It is so strongly attached to my memory of her that it sometimes makes me cry. Ô de Lancôme is my grandmother. 363/365

As Parfumo doesn't like when I try a suggestion of revision (I can't no longer suggest a revision anyway), I wanted to add here that I bought this exact bottle directly from Lancôme this morning. it's available on their French website and last time I checked at a local department store (something like 2 weeks ago), it was there too.

It happened recently while I was tidying up. Once a year, let's say, I organize my books. I dust them off. I see if maybe I should part with a few of them. I almost never do that, though. On the upper shelves, which require a ladder, are books that I have almost forgotten about, under - sometimes - twelve months of dust. (I am a good and decisive thrower and sorter, but not when it comes to books: the respect for the written word - as silly as it may sometimes be - runs deep in me.) And then - quite suddenly - I had it in my hands for the first time in at least twenty years: Enchanted April, written by Elizabeth von Arnim almost a hundred years ago. I then sat on the edge of the sofa with the dusty book and read its nearly three hundred pages in one go. Enchanted April is what one would commonly call a 'women's book.' So what? Von Arnim tells the story of four very different ladies - Englishwomen like her, too happy to call themselves unhappy, but too unhappy to be happy - who together rent a wonderful villa on the Italian coast for a month - that very April. And how each of them comes a little closer to happiness in her own way. Von Arnim revels in light and colors, tells of sunshine, flowers, scents - in a language that is light-footed and airy, but never simple-minded or banal. And when I finished reading the nearly three hundred pages - partly leaning on the sofa's edge, eventually sitting, while the already sorted empty bottles stared accusingly at me from the hallway - the villa by the sea and its little happiness felt very close. The same lightness and airiness, the same faded charm and the same fragrant colors, the same slightly old-fashioned but loving and careful language - and sunshine, flowers, scents, told lightly but never trivially - I find in Ô de Lancôme. Ô comes from a time when it was common to clearly categorize a perfume as a women's or men's scent - by today's standards, its classification as a women's fragrance seems almost anachronistic - being a delicate hesperidic chypre. It is nostalgic and a bit old-fashioned - yet youthful and eternally young. With an almost watery herbaceousness - dry, but not bitter, serious, but not solemn - it reminds me of those four very different people whose souls unexpectedly regain wings in the Ligurian spring sun. A lot of kindness and longing - and joy in the little happiness. Conclusion: Moments like my leisurely afternoon with 'Enchanted April' have a calm, unexpected, and sudden beauty. And Ô de Lancôme has that too. For women. Men. People.

Oh my Papa, … was a wonderful person! Oh my Papa was a great artist! Oh my Papa was a handsome man! My Paaaapaaaa...... I listened to the song again on purpose. It’s actually called: was a wonderful clown. My Papa passed away in 2017 and we had him laid out in an open casket. I will never do that again when a loved one of mine passes. The images still haunt me today.
What one might expect when reading the fragrance pyramid and trying to picture it would be ... a citrusy freshness that would come rushing towards you, supported by the bittersweet bergamot,... ...

Phew! - Breathe easy!!! I just successfully auctioned a brand new bottle of "Ô de Lancôme" on eBay, and I am genuinely relieved that this little water will soon be out of the house for good. The background of this rather intense emotional reaction has become clear to me by now.

Hello, fragrance lovers! Here I am, as often, with a new comment. Recently, I tried the scent "Ô de Lancôme," which I thought I had already described here long ago, but that wasn't the case, so I tested it. The term "Ô de" probably means "water of..." as always and is a classic designation for a fragrance, but since it is not written as "Eau de...

O and I met many years ago. The occasion was unfortunate. I had to go to the hospital for a few days due to an operation. It was summer, and I was looking for a fragrance that would refresh me during this time. It should, of course, be subtle and delicate, appropriate to the occasion, but still fresh. In a large perfumery, I looked around. I prefer to do that alone.

Easy to wear and inoffensive. Fresh watery floral with a hefty amount of fruit, some citrus and sweet, and a pleasant soapy powderiness. The soap is more than a suggestion, so if you have low tolerance for it I would suggest skipping. I like it even more with Rose as the florals here are not especially pronounced and identifiable. The bottle is very charming. I especially like the nod to clasps in the design of the locking sprayer nozzle.

I do find Coach POPPY FLOWER to be more floral and less acrylic/vinyl than its namesake, but to my nose this fragrance, like so many recent floral launches, toes the line between household cleaning products and perfume. I believe that the "wet ivy" and the "water lily" are contributing to the overall aquatic feeling here, but the peony is also fairly dominant. This composition is definitely more of a floral than a fruity-floral fragrance to my nose, as I do not actually detect any of the fruits listed as notes. Since I did not really enjoy POPPY, I'm neither disappointed nor surprised to find that POPPY FLOWER is also not for me. This one might work for those who like the offerings of the house of Clean.

I think I like this better than the original Idôle and Idôle Aura, but it still can't hold a candle to the gorgeous Idôle Intense. The popcorn note in the opening is recognizable and nicely blended with the fresher rose and soft vanilla. I was a bit wary if Idôle's clean floral DNA would maybe clash with such a strong, warm gourmand note, but it works. Unfortunately the popcorn doesn't last forever and the drydown doesn't get as caramel-like as I hoped it would. After a while the rose turns a bit jammier and a white floral creaminess emerges. The base is very similar to the original Idôle, but a tad sweeter and more vanillic. If you love Idôle it might be just the twist you need, if you want something more gourmand with lots of caramel and popcorn it might be disappointing. I find it pretty, but it doesn't blow my mind.

Was gifted a small bottle by a friend of mine. The bottle itself is so pretty! The warm pink corners and the orange fluid reminds me a bit of the lesbian flag :) Unfortunately this isn't gourmand in the slightest :(( I do not get the caramel top notes, nor the vanilla base notes. For me this is almost entirely a very fresh, rosy floral. I do get the popcorn notes on the drydown, though it's less of a warm, buttery movie theater popcorn and more a plain popcorn. It's almost giving "clean" smelling to me - not like, kitchen cleaning solution clean, but like, getting out of the shower type of clean. It's certainly not a typical combination, but not an unwelcome one. Very pleasant. Just not for me. If you're looking for something more gourmand, look elsewhere.

This fragrance had been on my wishlist for so long that I literally had a dream about it. Which I know sounds ridiculous. So it pains me to say that I did not like it as much as I thought I would. I disregarded the reviews and thought I would have a different experience with the scent, but unfortunately the Rose note is truly so overpowering that you can barely smell anything else. It’s like a very syrupy rose. Not quite as gourmand as I expected. I don’t hate it, but I don’t like it enough to continue using it either. Lasting power is very long as I could still smell it the next day and on whatever it touched.

I've been on the hunt for my Christmas Perfume (aka the full bottle fragrance I'm gifted every Christmas) and the main requirements have been 1.) lesbian flag colors in the bottle and 2.) girly smell 3.) mass appeal bc I work in an office and also 4.) I actually like it. This one fit the bill! It's so silly, just a silly idea for a perfume. Not the bottle, obviously, but the notes. Popcorn? Roses? Vanilla? Sure, why not. After testing it at Ulta, I was waiting for the letdown, but luckily it never came. I really like it! It's sweet and salty and rosy. Like if a perfume was a glitter-obsessed high femme lesbian... so me, I guess.

I don't know why, but the normal Idole has NEVER stuck in my mind - no matter how often I tested it. However, the word Nectar made me sit up and take notice, because I am a victim of opulence! The scent smells a bit heavily composed, as if the notes were not given enough time to unfold. At first, it smells deliciously zesty (sweet mandarin?), then it transitions into a very intense combination of rose and veeeery sweet caramel, which adds a bit more depth to the fragrance. On my skin, the scent becomes beautifully vanillic at the end, and you can detect a tiny hint of popcorn. I would have wished for the popcorn note to be a bit smokier, like in La Belle by JPG. The rose gives the fragrance a touch of lipstick/vintage cosmetics without becoming outdated! I believe the scent is deliberately aimed at somewhat younger women (who basically grew up with the face of the advertising campaign). The fragrance does not come across as very mature. Those who like Rose Gourmand by Zara or Si would probably also warm up to this one.

Among all the other scents I tested that day at Müller, Idôle Nectar stood out clearly. It has something very special. No other fragrance smelled like this. So I bought it on a whim. To me, it smells rosy, clean, and sweetly dry. A beautiful, rounded fabric softener rose. Nothing pricks me. The longevity is very, very good. About 10-12 hours.

Once again something for the ladies. L'ancome is a great brand for me that simply produces appealing mainstream fragrances for girls and women. L'Oreal is generally aimed at the broader audience, and you can definitely tell that in the pleasing creations. But that's not always negative; you get crowd-pleasers that most people will enjoy.

Since the rose all-rounder fragrance Idôle already surprised me positively, and as a big fan of vanilla and gourmand scents, I found the popcorn and caramel notes so interesting, I decided to get the Lancôme Idole Nectar in 25ml. I was not disappointed; it is the perfect mix of floral, sweet gourmand, with rose kissing sweet caramel and bourbon vanilla.

I have to say that I didn't like the original Idole at all. Way too watery and bland. By chance, I then tried the new Idole Nectar and fell in love immediately. It really is a nectar. A beautiful sweet, playful rose scent with a hint of popcorn and caramel. The DNA is the same, but it comes across much nicer here.

I love it. I tested it at Müller, alongside many other perfumes. I left the store, smelling my arm throughout the day, which was sprayed with about 5 different scents in various places. Again and again, my nose was drawn to the Idôle Nectar. It smells so sweet, delicious, floral, and fresh. A wonderful fragrance, for which I would love to have a larger sillage.

I’m not generally a fan of the La Vie Est Belle line, but I picked this up as a (heavily researched!) blind buy after reading that this particular flanker isn’t super similar to the original. I can confirm, it is indeed not very similar to the original LVEB. This is a summery orange-ish floral to my nose, I get mostly the ylang ylang with orange and a hint of coconut in the background. It has tropical vibes but is not aquatic or fresh. There is still some sweetness but it’s not overwhelming, in my opinion. It actually does last and project, which is not always the case with “summer”-coded fragrances! And I really like the bottle, it’s super cute and the flat design means it will be easy to pack for summer adventures.

I get a bit of the OG la vie est belle right at the beginning, but it goes away to quickly. It is really it’s own scent and I really like it. On me it’s powdery iris, vanilla and coconut with a bit of a tropical touch in the background. Perfect summer perfume, and I would love to bring it for a hot tropical vacation right now.

I have just welcomed La vie est belle - Soleil cristal into my collection. You read a lot of negative opinions, but I think that comes from disappointed expectations, not from the actual scent itself. It is not a zesty summer refreshment nor a sunscreen fragrance. I really like it. For me, it evokes the following mood: vacation in Italy. You spend the day at the beach, feeling rather sluggish because it’s so hot. Sun on your skin, only slightly cooled by the wind, occasionally bathing in the sea, grateful for the refreshment and a bit of movement. Tired, with still heated skin, you head back to the hotel, perhaps resting a bit on the cool white sheets, while sounds of increasing evening activities filter into the room through the closed wooden shutters. You shower, let a hair treatment sit, apply lotion, do your makeup, because you have a dinner reservation at a fancy garden restaurant with a view of the sea, a bit away from the tourist crowds. And now you sit in the garden, wearing a lovely flowing summer dress and sandals, you are perfumed, wearing lipstick, and enjoying an aperitif, perhaps a cool Fragolino. It’s still very warm, but a breeze picks up, and you look forward to a lovely evening in refined company, with delicious multi-course meals, chilled wine, overlooking the sunset, the landscape, and other guests who are all well-groomed and elegantly dressed, behaving discreetly. Nothing is shrill or loud, the leisurely rhythm of the day continues and transitions into the night. All of this is captured for me in the scent, a lot of warmth, but also a light sea breeze, a Mediterranean garden, warm earth and stones, the scent of cosmetics and a light fruity wine. I can really only recognize iris and vanilla, once the citrus-heavy top note fades and transitions into the white flowers. I perceive coconut and patchouli more as a texture than a scent; the coconut gives a creaminess reminiscent of Raffaello, while the patchouli creates a dark, slightly crisp base. For me, this is definitely a vacation scent, a carefree time where you let yourself drift gently, find peace, enjoy, without chasing from one highlight to the next, but simply allowing things to happen. I usually like scents that make me feel longing, but this scent embodies for me the existence in the here and now - and that is exactly what I long for ;)

I would have liked to like you so much.... Based on the fragrance pyramid, I imagined a wonderful, delicious, fruity, creamy summer scent that would be just right for me. Full of anticipation, I took the first spray from the beautifully shimmering bottle, thinking it could only be good... But then came the pure disappointment! I smelled a scratchy, piercing, bitter/sweet note of citrus fruits and a strangely roasted (more like burnt coconut) scent, not the delicious creamy coconut note I had expected :(( Because I actually love coconut, but... What is this?! This can't be right.... Maybe it's just at the beginning, I thought, let's wait and see.... Again and again, I sniffed at my wrist in the hope that it would develop into a nice, pleasant summer/vacation scent. Slowly, the vanilla joined in, which became a bit more pronounced towards the end, but unfortunately, that piercing, scratchy, biting smell remained present until the end, which truly repulsed me and gave me a headache. So I had to come to the conclusion that unfortunately, this won't work out between us and you won't be joining my collection :(.....What a shame. Thus, the search continues for the perfect summer scent!

Finally tried La Vie est Belle Soleil Cristal today. And it is really beautiful. A summery version of the original, less sweet, even slightly salty (I prefer it to J'adore in Joy, it goes slightly in the direction of Olympéa Intense but it is gentler) and very Ylang-Ylang-focused. The mandarin gives it a fresh touch and the vanilla is tropical, and the overall impression is beachy, but in an elegant way. I would say I like this even more than LVEB la Vie en Rose, which had been my LVEB favorite until now. The patchouli of the original is softly perceptible and really pleasantly realized. Anyone missing Womanity should at least try Soleil Cristal once. Beautiful!!

... was the first sentence in my French book. And since the sun is shining mild and friendly today, I reached for La vie est belle Soleil Cristal in the perfume department. There was no tester available, but since I always get along well with the La Vie est belle fragrances, I wanted to take a chance on a blind purchase. First, I got 30ml.

A lightly synthetic summer-sun feel-good scent, anyone?--- HERE it is! Yes, life can be beautiful! With a perfume that truly shows its crystals. In the form of bitter peppery-citrusy semi-precious stones. Best compared to sparkling quartz shards.

If I had guessed what Coach was likely to have as its namesake fragrance, it would have been something evoking horsiness (see its insignia)with a touch of chav. (I'd assumed it was a British company, but checked its website & found out that it was founded in NY.) I'd have been surprised to read this description on its website, because it doesn't really fit the brand image to me: "a blend of soft, fresh fruits and florals with a heart of fragrant yellow blossoms and warm hints of amber and cedar wood." And I'm more surprised still to smell this scent. In a blind test, I'm not sure I could tell it from E. Lauder's Brasil Dream. Like ELBD, it's all about the guava and jasmine. It smells like it also has a fair amount of gardenia, although it's not listed. The mimosa, which is the only "yellow flower" listed, is sadly undetectable. It's not unpleasant if you're looking for a tropical white floral, but be prepared for its initial trumpet blast of scent to be nearly undetectable in two hours.

This perfume goes on screaming “Citrus!” I smell oranges and a hint of Waterlily. It keeps screaming for about 15 minutes. And she’s loud! Wow! At that point, I smell jasmine and tea. There’s still citrus behind the tea though. She likes to play center stage. And she’s fresh. At the end, which is rather short-lived, is a woody nod. You know, the thing men do when they pass in the hall without saying a word. The bottle is absolutely gorgeous! However, I’d likely not wear this perfume again. I don’t usually fall for a citrus perfume.

Tested yesterday cause i went at printemps shop . I had earned about this lancome collection and décided to discover them. So i began by figues and agrumes. At the opening a great odour of neroli which reminds me prada day n night or ysl trench. Then after 20 minutes a coconut odour which reminds me soleil blanc tf. After 1 hours,the copy of balade sauvage and fu.... fabulous tf. A fragrance of summer perfectly unisex. Seller told me it will be discountinued. Doesn t matter there are balade sauvage and tf

Figues is so so beautiful. It’s one of those perfumes that everyone likes. Totally unisex. It has flowers such as jasmine. A scent of fig green whit a somewhat sweet background. It is an elegant, fine perfume, suitable for any time. A wardrobe staple without a doubt. When i put it on, i get a smile. It is cheerful, Fresh at the same time it cozy. What more could you ask for.

Hey you snot-noses! No wait, I meant you sniffing noses :D How are you doing? Have you already evaporated or are you still sweating? Yes, yes, the weather has once again become extremely hot, and this is just the beginning, as temperatures above 32 to torturous 36-37 degrees are yet to come, not to mention hellish heatwaves with 40 degrees and more. But apparently, we now have a few days to catch our breath, as the weather has become more bearable again (thunderstorms aside). * sigh * I really don’t like summer when it gets this extreme. Yes, yes, it’s not just because I’m single and we singles are known to suffer even more in summer (and that despite the lightly dressed ladies with endless legs,… uh you know what I mean :DD), but also because of the heat, especially on rainy days when it becomes unbearably humid and you stick to a leather couch more than if you were covered in super glue... Seriously, how can anyone like summer?? Well, if I had a girlfriend (with endless legs :D), I might think a little differently, but I’d probably still complain about the heat, I think… heeeeeeeat!!!! :DD But alright. What belongs in summer in terms of perfume? Hmm… since it seems that quite a few people are listening to me here, I could, as a single, turn into a movie villain and claim that at 35 degrees heat, one should wear heavy oud fragrances, especially with ylang-ylang, coriander, and opulent tuberoses!! Mu ha ha ha, suffer with me!!! :D But you’re lucky that despite all the complaining, I’m still somewhat nice and therefore present you with a true summer fragrance, namely “Figues & Agrumes” by Lancôme, which sounds quite refreshing with notes like fig and citrus sorbet! So let’s see how it is! The Fragrance: Oh, the beginning is great. Light, airy, citrusy-green, and thus refreshing. Before I perceive the figs, the citrus reminds me of the refreshing effect of Concentré d‘Orange Verte by Hermès, only a bit milder and sweeter. And I also think that here, citrus doesn’t just mean lemons, but rather oranges, because the scent really smells like (bitter) oranges. When the citrus calms down a bit (but is still very noticeable), you can better perceive the fig, along with floral-sweet jasmine. In the heart, the fig becomes significantly more intense and then becomes the main scent note, as the citrus notes recede a bit into the background. There’s still sweet jasmine, although the sweetness of the fragrance is rather low, yet in my opinion, it is perfectly dosed to simply smell very pleasant. In the base, however, not much changes, except that the projection of the fragrance becomes a bit lower, so that the scent gradually fades after a few hours and is just waiting to be reapplied, which you should definitely do, as especially the top note smells really delicious and zesty! The Sillage and Longevity: Summer fragrance = low sillage. This equation does apply here, but generally speaking, the sillage of this fragrance seems to be a bit higher than that of most summer fragrances, which is great, but overall, it’s still a weak scent :D I found the longevity of about 5-6 hours to be quite good for a summer fragrance. The Bottle: Ah, the bottles of these Lancôme fragrances are, in my opinion, among the most beautiful bottles ever. It is first of all a rectangular bottle with rounded edges. But the two gilded plaques make the bottle simply look wonderful. There’s the lovely plaque with the delicately appearing cutouts that create a beautiful illustration of a fig fruit including leaves. Since this golden plaque is only visible on the front, it appears greenish from the other side due to the green fragrance liquid, which is also very nice to look at. The next plaque has been placed on one of the side edges, where the name of the fragrance can be seen. The cap is appropriately gilded as well, so everything harmonizes well together and simply looks great. Conclusion: Wow, what a beautiful fragrance! I really like figs and here they come with citrus notes, which I particularly appreciate in summer! The interplay of these fruity scents is delightful, as the fragrance refreshes especially in the top note, but also remains light on the skin throughout the rest of the fragrance journey, making it a scent that can be worn well on really hot days to smell good even on those exhausting days. So if you’re melting away in the heat, then use fragrances like this one here. If the heat is unbearable, but you still want to smell good, then use fragrances like this one here. If you’re sweating endlessly and longing for a sparkling refreshment, then strip down… no wait, I meant to write again: then use fragrances like this one here… he he, hey have mercy, it’s too hot, and I can never think clearly when the sun is frying me or I only see endless legs everywhere… *sigh* :DD So, this fragrance is usable… come on, you’ve probably already guessed it, in summer! :D I would then use it for all sorts of occasions, although you might need to reapply it occasionally when going out, as it does lose strength noticeably after just a few hours (at least in terms of projection, the longevity is surprisingly good!). In any case, Figues & Agrumes is a recommendable fragrance that, unfortunately, seems a bit overpriced, but smells very good. If you’re looking for a comparable scent that is significantly cheaper, I recommend checking out “Fico di Amalfi” by Acqua di Parma, which is one of my personal favorites in summer. That’s it again. Have a pleasant evening and see you then :)

I actually just wanted to give a short statement, but that didn’t seem enough for this beautiful fragrance. I have been watching Figues & Agrumes for a long time, considering whether the pyramid listed here might be a perfect match. But somehow, I never had the opportunity to test this scent nearby. While I’m not averse to blind buys, it just never worked out here. Then, recently, when I was in Hamburg with my husband at Alsterhaus, I suddenly stood in front of the object of my desire. Sooo fresh and green, I never thought I would like these notes so much. And the figs, simply dreamy. After about half an hour, the scent on my skin becomes wonderfully creamy, and it stays that way for hours. Even after 7 or 8 hours, it is still present, fresh creamy fig. A small bottle has moved in, maybe one day the 100 ml bottle will follow.

Delicate, sweet, creamy figs with blossoms and notes of citrus fruits as well as grated green leaves at the beginning. The opening is soft, then feminine, mysterious, peaceful. The perfume transforms into a thick, creamy, enveloping sweet fig scent. For me, it is the most delicate, the milkiest fig. And when it rains outside, the magic happens - the humidity gives it a strength in which every note of fig-citrus-flower sounds even more harmonious.

I highly doubt that anyone will absolutely abhor this fragrance, it's fun and fancy-free. But there is no olfactory lesson in this bottle, it imparts no deeper message or knowledge. I find it very similar to "Nine West Love Fury". Likewise, I consider this a casual Summer fling- not Love, actually. Coach Love is youthful, carefree, almost calming in its lack of originality, as a daily fragrance is not bad at all. It has some fruity notes, I detect mandarins and blackberries-ripe and ready to be eaten. There are also notes of violet, magnolia, freesia, jasmine and a synthetic gardenia complex. A dash of sandalwood and vanilla notes. There's a bit of soft musk finished with Caramel (a la Jessica Simpson's outrageously and mysteriously successful "Fancy") and the other Caramel greats of the last few years. It manages to not be cloyingly sweet, nor is it a sharp fruity floral- it's quite wearable. It has a certain commonality with Gucci II (2) in its composition, almost like the innocent prepubescent sister of Gucci II, that makes this office appropriate. This is sheer but has decent sillage of about 1 meter (3.28 ft.) and it last for a good 6 hours on my skin before disappearing (off to a Coldplay Concert, with her friends- no doubt). Coach Love was a bona fide fragrance, but ultimately, I used the rest of the sample to freshen my kitty litter box.

I was once handed by an SA a ceramic tester heavily sprayed with Lavandes Trianon, and I was not thrilled at all by its dense cloud of generic gourmand tonka vanilla. But when I got around to try it on my skin, the result is much better. It opens on my skin as a vivid purple lavender. It's not at all like the metallic, ultra-clean note in certain mainstream masculine sport fragrances. Here, the lavender is aromatic and herbal in a gritty, earthy, deep and resinous way, sometimes even a bit like burnt rubber. As the fragrance enters into the dry down, the latter nuance shifts gradually into a soft burnt caramel and dried hay undertone thanks to the quiet arrival of vanilla and tonka bean. The initial lively herbal vigour is also soothed by the comfort of vanilla. I was a bit wary whether its commercial gourmand vanilla-tonka base previously observed on the ceramic tester would take over the fragrance. But as long as I'm careful with the amount applied on my skin, Lavandes Trianon is foremost a lavender soliflore, and the vanilla and tonka bean in the base behave more like a filter to soften the contour in a picture. Although Lavandes Trianon is mostly linear, its tone does shift from the opening to the dry down. If the opening is a field of lavender at dusk, releasing its aromatic yet resinous redolence after bathing under the Mediterranean sun, this field is then caressed by the vanilla like a balmy summer breeze of early evening. I get a moderate sillage during the most part of its 8-hour longevity. While Lavandes Trianon might not be the most complex lavender fragrance, it does display a wide range of earthy, deep nuances that are rarely featured in mainstream offerings. Its gourmand base also manifests in a measured manner as long as I don't overapply, which helps to avoid triggering gourmand fatigue too often. Personally, I find it more "lavender" and less gourmand than Rochas Man and Mugler A*Men. Although I would hesitate to recommend it to fans of fresh lavender fragrances, Lavandes Trianon would be an interesting option to consider if one ever wants to venture into gourmand territory, and vice-versa for lavender-phobe gourmand fan.

I found out about Lavandes Trianon and the rest of the Maison Lancome Grand Cru collection after most were discontinued. Many, including Lavandes Trianon have a cult following. I read it was one of the best lactonic gourmand fragrances. Prices for some of the discontinued MLGC go for over $400 a bottle! So when I found a 60% full bottle for $100 I went for it. It arrived and I ripped open the packaging. I sprayed once on each wrist. Uh??? Where’s the magic?? I smelled a creamy, rounded lavender but not much sweetness or caramel or vanilla sugar. I was disappointed. I decided it’s going on the swap list. Many in my fragrance groups quickly messaged me about buying it and that made me smell it again. I sprayed more liberally this time and it clicked!! A pot of heavy cream, sweetened with vanilla and sugar; warming on the stove with sprigs of French lavender steeping in the cream. As it warms, the entire house fills up with the aroma of this lavender pot de crème! That’s exactly what happens on the skin. The lavender starts off potent but rounded. The opening is it’s most aromatic but it’s soften, edged removed. It’s almost fuzzy like tonka. As it warms on the skin, it becomes sweeter, richer and the vanilla comes forward. The deep dry down is a delicious gooey soft caramel that feel runny. The lavender stays throughout the fragrance. I find this had amazing siliage for hours! I love wearing it to bed. I can smell it all night long and I’m the morning it’s there until I shower. I fell in love. I found a full bottle for $160. Now I have 2 bottles. I never want to be without it; I haven’t smelled anything like it yet. Not Mon Guerlain or Mon Guerlain intense not Libre or Libre Intense. All are beautiful lavender fragrances but none have the lactonic magic that Lavandes Trianon have.

This is beautiful. I was scared/nervous when I ordered this blindly because a lot of the reviews here reported a realistic, herbal lavender, something likened to an essential oil. I don't love a pure lavender smell, even in a lavendar bar of soap, I always prefer it alongside something else, preferrably vanilla. This perfume is not cheap (even though I did get it for a decent price) so I felt like I was taking a risk by ordering it before I had smelled it but luckily for me, my experience was a positive one. My fears were put to rest upon first spritz. It is a realistic lavender scent but I didn't find it tremendously herbal or medicinal (thankfully.) The lavender is perfectly tempered with a creamy, fluffy sugar-coated vanilla. It's as if someone had baked a vanilla cake and thrown a handful of dried lavender in the batter, then as it bakes it gives off this soothing, comforting, calming aroma which makes you feel zen. It's strength and lasting power wasn't an issue for me. I could smell it all day on myself and when I awoke in the morning, I could still smell it. This fragrance is ethereal and altogether magical. I am an anxious person by nature and I was hoping this scent might help tone that down a little. I'm happy to report that it did. I am enamored with this beauty and will treasure each and every drop.

This is a very vanilla heavy milky lavender, It is fluffy and on me it is BEAST mode so spray one to two sprays MAX , and don't even try this in the summertime. I love the sillage that floats off of my skin, it's a cloud of vanillic lavender. This is not herbal like some say but does have a lavender cake quality.

Since I really like the combination of lavender and vanilla, I got a 10 ml decant of Lavandes Trianon from a dear perfumist here and out of excitement, I even considered ordering a full bottle right away - I was so enchanted by the scent notes and the comments. Now I've been testing it for three days and I can say - we will not become friends. The lavender always comes through beautifully on my skin and I also like the vanilla - but unfortunately, I can't agree with the rest. After two to three hours, my perception of the scent is just annoyingly sweet, sticky, and way too much of everything - except for the lavender. Moreover, I also miss a bit of refinement - after three hours, only vanilla and lavender linger, and that's it. I'd rather get the Eau de Parfum "Lavande intensif" by Leblanc - 12 ml only costs 9.90 euros - and to my nose, these two smell quite similar. For the times when I'm in the mood for a cozy scent, that will suffice *g

Lancome describes "Lavandes Trianon" as a "fresh gourmand." On me, the fragrance opens fresh and aromatic, but unfortunately also piercing, with a slightly soapy, slightly herbal lavender, steeped in sweet vanilla cream, all covered with a thin layer of cling film.

Well.... I heard such WONDERFUL things about this fragrance. Things that made me feel as though I just HAD to give it a try. But looking at the price of this now, due to it being discontinued... There was no way I was going to pay $200-300 for a blind buy bottle. Fast forward and I run across a sample box of Coach mini dabbers that included this fragrance, so I jumped on it. Sighs.... Of the 4 dabbers included, this one is my least favorite. I mean, it's not horrible... It's just lackluster. I think it would be perfect if you just wanted to apply a fragrance that wouldn't draw much attention. It's a little powdery, woody, soft, and warm. Maybe it smelled better back in the day, but as I type this review today, it's nothing to write home about.

Ôponé is a fragrance so revolting you’d think someone was joking, that it couldn’t possibly be real. But it is real, and I have a sample of it. It’s a vile cocktail of the following: a freshly-opened bottle of goopy, boozy-but-not-nearly-enough booze bitter berry Robitussin Maximum Strength Cough and Chest Congestion (possibly the one with Dextromethorphan and Guaifenesin), the most repellent, unpalatable artificial fruity-sour energy drink on the shelf with the most outrageously obnoxious packaging, the one so disgusting and foul that even the people you think might be into it would never buy, and the saddest long-stemmed fake rose wrapped in dusty crinkly plastic at the gas station. Nobody wants any part of this. Throw it in the trash immediately.

The rose in the opening rushes by too quickly for me to check its origin by ID or otherwise. It takes a back seat to dusty-bitter-spicy saffron and intense licorice, contributing only a subtle aroma close to the noble rose. This somewhat watery quality often bothers me, especially when it is turned up too loud (à la Montale). However, in this case, it seems to be the key to understanding the first hours of the fragrance. The charming contrast of rose and licorice has a surprising effect: Just as sugar acts as a flavor turbo (or alternatively - pretender) in a lemonade for the sparingly present fruit, the sweetness here enhances the relatively weak rose scent into something surprisingly refreshing. However, nothing becomes cloyingly sweet; rather, the newly invented licorice-rose lemonade comes across as herbaceous and grown-up. Great idea. I’ll sign up as a test customer right away! Moreover, Ôponé caters to fresh, oriental, and borderline gourmand cravings equally. Strangely enough, it does so without giving the impression of being just any interchangeable opportunist. On the contrary, the Diptyque comes across as distinctly idiosyncratic. From late morning onwards, it gradually steers into curry territory. For this, licorice and saffron enlist not only completely unsweaty cumin but also remind me of the combination of licorice and strawflower from Amouage’s ‘Fate Man’. After all, the Italian strawflower is not called ‘curry herb’ for nothing. However, it doesn’t become entirely edible, as the consistently watery-fresh rose remains involved, still on the threshold of the noble rose and clearly a supporting actress. And where elsewhere, in the course of the afternoon, a mellow aging might set in, Ôponé strikes again. The licorice expands its dominance. It takes on a slightly piercing, almost animalistic note, underpinned by bitterness. Harmless is not the word. Consequently, it is accompanied by worthy companions: birch tar and, towards the end, increasingly stronger smoke - until late in the evening, licorice more or less closes the curtain alone. Very nice. That the rose still remained a character-defining presence in quiet persistence has led my wife to declare the fragrance rather feminine. I don’t see it that way, of course. A fine little piece and a clear test tip. I thank Ergoproxy for the sample. PS - regarding Seymour's statement: Celeriac is, of course, nonsense. It is undoubtedly about celery stalks.

When I first tested Ôponé during my early days here at Parfumo, I was completely taken with it and wanted to have it. Unfortunately, the fragrance was no longer available at that time, and I quickly lost track of it. Recently, Ôponé has been produced again as an EdP within the Collection 34. Even during my first test of the EdT, I noticed a certain contradiction that the new version of the fragrance also exhibits. Unfortunately, I do not have a sample of the original fragrance to make a comparison. Ôponé is, in my opinion, a linear scent, meaning it does not have a significant scent progression. The focal point is a slightly sweet rose note around which the other components have been composed. In addition to rose, saffron is the most noticeable for my nose, which consistently gives the fragrance a slightly powdery bitter note. At the start, I perceive the rose scent as slightly metallic for a brief moment, and towards the base, the rose in Ôponé becomes somewhat spicy and smoky with hints of dry wood. My nemesis, cumin, has been so well incorporated here that its spiciness can only be subtly sensed. Ôponé is, for me, a "but still" fragrance. It is somehow old-school, but the bitter powdery note makes it very modern. The longevity is top-notch, while the sillage is rather moderate even at higher dosages, which I personally find fitting for the fragrance. I also think the bottle is great, reminding me of a 70s whiskey glass with a shattered look. In hindsight, I have noticed that I like most creations by Olivia Giacobetti (some of which I have or have had in my collection), and I am now looking forward to more fragrances from her hand. What I unfortunately could not clarify is what Ôponé means. The common translation sites were not much help to me.

I gifted myself Oranges Bigarades last Christmas. It was a blind buy based on such an enticing description that I simply had to treat myself to this fragrance - albeit only the small version. And it did not disappoint me, quite the opposite: I didn't wear it much last winter, but this year it has become one of my absolute favorite winter scents! Yes, that's right, I don't see it in summer and not necessarily in spring either, but rather in autumn and winter. However, during those seasons, it suits me perfectly! I also cannot fully agree with the classification as citrus-fresh. Citrus yes, fresh only to a certain extent, rather spicy, in that regard I definitely agree with the description from Duftsucht in their comment. The opening features a very prominent, juicy bitter orange, which, together with bergamot, offers a wonderful citrus-herb fragrance experience. A slight sweetness becomes perceptible in the background as it develops, but really just a hint, so the scent never comes across as overpowering. After a while, the aroma of black tea joins in, and the fragrance becomes spicier. And so it remains relatively long-lasting for me, enveloping me in a lovely, warm veil. It is a truly wonderful composition with a high recognition value, perfectly balanced, nothing is too much and nothing is too little. If you are looking for a winter fragrance that smells of oranges and completely avoids gourmand notes and Christmas baking - here it is!

Angua's comment on "Oranges Bigarades" sounded so enticing that, seized by a fierce desire for fragrance, I rushed to Karstadt during my lunch break. Without much hope of actually finding the exclusive line from Lancome there. But lo and behold: Another prejudice must be laid aside, there they stood in rows and lines: The bottles in all their golden-floral splendor - and Oranges Bigarades quickly made its way onto my wrist. The scent begins with quite a powerful top note - nothing shy about it: But cheerful and buoyant for sure. The bitter-citrusy smell of candied orange peel (called Aranzini in Austria) fills my nose, but not scratchy, rather juicy and spiced with a distinct hint of bergamot. This immediately lifts my spirits and gives me a real boost of energy. After a while, the scent becomes a bit more bitter, the tea comes to the fore: To me, it smells like Earl Grey mixed with very strong black tea. Bitter, but not harsh - and again, it’s an additional component that keeps the scent fresh. Woody pepper also mixes in - and I think I can smell ginger too. Citrusy-green doesn’t seem like the right classification for the fragrance direction. For me, it would be citrus-spicy - woody. An extremely fine, balanced, unobtrusive fresh scent with a high recognition factor - rightly described by the saleswoman as a “first-class wellness feel-good fragrance”! Since I was testing “Jasmins Marzipane” from the same series on the other wrist, which completely blew me away, “Oranges Bigarades” had a tough time in this test. However, it passed the challenge with flying colors - and now I have a decision problem and two more fragrances on my unfulfillable, constantly growing fragrance wish list!

Hello you sniffers and welcome to my commentary on Oranges Bigarades from the exclusive Lancôme fragrance line "Maison Lancôme". I received a sample of this scent and I must say that just based on its notes (the fragrance notes listed), it could very well suit my taste if it’s well made. Because I like… well, I think I don’t need to emphasize this anymore, you know that I’m into tea scents, and also notes like oranges, hmm… That’s why I particularly enjoy testing this kind of fragrance, because there might actually be something for me in it instead of always just something for you (ladies), when I present another women’s fragrance (which I always do just for you, you ungrateful monsters! :D). And especially tea and orange sound absolutely perfect for warm days, like we have more often in spring (Yes! It’s true, even though the last few days have been cooler and rainier, we are surely just a stone's throw away from the next heatwave! :D). So I hope the scent is great too! Although my feeling is generally positive, as the Maison Lancôme Collection often offers good fragrances. So, let’s sniff! The Fragrance: At first, I smell citrus notes, especially oranges. These smell like the delicious pulp and therefore do not have that slightly bitter scent of the peel of these fruits, even though bitter orange should be listed here (at least that’s how it seems to me). In addition, there is a wonderful tea note that you can actually smell well, which makes me happy, as tea sometimes comes across as quite weak. Pepper adds a small, spicy note. It is subtle, so it doesn’t come across as sharp, but you can still perceive its scent, even if only for a short time. For a while, it stays that way, with the pepper gradually fading away. In the base, the fragrance doesn’t change much anymore, as I can still smell oranges (now a bit more bitter) and the tea, but everything is just quite weak. Overall, a rather nice, fresh scent. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is above average and thus, at least up close, still somewhat pleasant to smell, although not for long. The longevity is quite okay, on me the scent lasted seven to eight hours. The Bottle: The bottle is rectangular and made of thick glass. The fragrance liquid is pink-orange. On one side, there is a golden shimmering metal plaque with the name and brand. On one side, there is another plaque, but this one has beautiful floral patterns cut out. Viewed through the bottle, these patterns also look very nice. The cap is cylindrical and white. Like all bottles in the Maison Lancôme line, this bottle is also very beautiful to look at. Conclusion: Yes, I had already thought that this fragrance could be a great scent and yes, I was not disappointed. Sure, the sillage could, like with all fragrances of this kind (i.e., tea and citrus), be much more intense, but well, that’s just how it is, and one must live with it, like it or not. But still, the scent is very, very nice and fits perfectly as a casual or everyday fragrance for spring and especially summer with its fresh, relaxed scent. A test is absolutely recommended, unless of course, you are brain-dead and don’t like the scent of tea and oranges… how can you not like it? Ugh, instead, you prefer something disgusting like cumin or coriander, yuck! :D And that’s about it for today, I know my comment was short this time, but hey, I can’t always write lengthy texts where half of it is just complaining about you ladies, can I? Unless you give me permission to do so, mu ha ha ha :DD So then, have a nice evening :)

What I particularly like about Oranges Bigarades is the invigorating bitter freshness of a strong, not overly steeped black tea. I can clearly smell a good dash of bergamot, which gives the tea its Earl Grey freshness. Orange as juice or fruit takes more of a back seat, but it seems to me that orange blossoms very subtly and gently make their presence known, along with a hint of bitter neroli. The most exciting aspect of this fragrance for me is the sweetness. I am very cautious with sweet scents; they don’t suit me. However, the sweetness in Oranges Bigarades comes across to me as a very light and non-sticky sweetness, somewhat like glucose that dissolves quickly and provides energy. It is completely different from the syrupy or dessert-like sweetness found in gourmand fragrances. Speaking of which: I don’t find the scent creamy and I also don’t detect any vanilla. I deduct a few points for a slight artificiality in the later development of the scent. For me, it’s not just a summer fragrance; it works all year round.

Summer is taking a break! It hasn't spoiled us too much so far, and now, gallantly as it is, this summer gives precedence to the "sheep cold": It even opens wide all the doors for it! The cold west wind, often in hurricane-like gusts, makes me shiver and actually makes me search for a warm, smoke-filled fragrance cave; but I am defiant and therefore rummage through the pouch with the lighter, summery scent samples. So I finally find "Oranges Bigarades" by Lancôme; not really my favorite brand, but it's worth a try: "I can always grumble if necessary!" growls the diva in me. But, oh! What is this delightful scent? A cloud of wonderful, lightly spiced Ceylon tea with Black Pepper surrounds me, and the harmoniously intertwined citrus aromas bring pure cheerfulness! Just the right dosage: not too sweet-sticky, too zesty-biting, but balanced by a cleverly added portion of bitter oranges into a very charming summer cocktail that makes you crave more! Thus, a light, transparent summer fragrance develops that simply spreads joy and is not too fleeting, but possesses a pleasant richness of aroma. This fragrance experience lifts the mood (even if not the outside temperatures) and has already achieved its goal for today: My mood is improving a bit! And for the hopefully still upcoming summer days, this not so meager sample of "Oranges Bigarades" will be a cheerful, not so everyday companion.

,,Orange Bigarades’‘, it says on the packaging, one thinks this scent is simply fresh. No. An unexpected kind of orange with vanilla that you perceive from the very beginning. Very surprising. You are sitting in the restaurant of a legendary luxury hotel and you are just being served by a very attractive waiter. A thick - sweet orange with vanilla cream.

At first, the tea note reminded me a lot of "1 - Bergamot, Tea Leaf, Sandal Wood | Rosendo Mateu - Olfactive Expressions." The orange is very prominent in the opening, but then it fades a bit, and it seems to me that a mint along with a hint of marshmallows takes over. So picture this: a mint tea with a slice of orange as decoration and marshmallows on top.

Masterpiece from my favourite perfumer – that is ESSENCES INSENSÉES. Icing sugar peach lilac – the first breath, as your olfactory would be bombarded with shining, happy notes. If you take a deeper breath, it is easy to detect some biting spice, most probably the pepper (what else could be?). The fragrance is strong, confidently fresh, and 100% natural. The best face of niche – written here just to annoy GothicHeart :D On the ground that I do not know all of the notes for sure, my nose makes easily mistakes, e.g. I feel chamomille. The scent of health. Bravo! This flower withers so fast... Dry and dead chamomille - The scent of sadness and too early farewell from life. If that was the intention, then bravo. If not, then: why the hell do I have to feel such grief at this stage??? ...Especially after and before the beautiful springtime of head and base? Till the end of heart ESSENCES INSENSÉES is the same with different body chemistries. The scent revives on lucky skin, and shows petals floating on clean water. Another drydown path is paved with herbs (mate?), is a bit sour, and shows in the last few hours a pretty, feminine and a bit boring mimosa. Where is the beeswax? In the head. Where is the vanille? In the head. Where is the violet? Mimosa kidnapped her to accompany her in the base. As you can see, this fragrance involves me emotically very fast and deep, it is wonderful, and I can not keep myself away from the feelings that it makes arise. ESSENCES INSENSÉES is enough possessive to engage my thoughts for hours, nonetheless it is easy to wear. I like it. I love it. I hopelessly want to grab the volatile fineness of it.

Translating the name 1:1 from French raises the question of why? Why are fragrances referred to as nonsensical essences... Has the manufacturer already supposedly enough sensible essences on the market and wants to market their formulations that have been languishing in storage under a slightly misleading name? No idea. In any case, all 3 fragrances launched under this name so far are anything but nonsensical; each one is something special with a specific target audience. In 2014, mimosas were highlighted, in 2015 jasmine, and this year the rose has been put in a special light. The two fragrances from 2015 and 2016 are successful, but not to my taste. The first formula from 2014 is different. However, one must have a certain preference for the quirky, tingling mimosa scent that runs like a red thread throughout the entire fragrance progression. The fragrance starts green and slightly metallic; the violet blooms here only very briefly, as it does in nature, most of the time the small violet spring messengers are gone after a sunny day. The pink pepper also listed in the top note may be somewhere present, but is hardly noticeable. The mimosa is already present in the top note and intensifies in the heart note. Anyone who has ever stood under a blooming mimosa tree in spring by the Mediterranean will immediately have this image in their mind. The mimosa scent personally always reminds me a bit of blooming linden trees, which is why I would like to compare the fragrance a bit with Tilleul by D'Orsay. The beeswax note in the base further emphasizes this association. Farnesiana by Caron also caters to the same fragrance direction. For me, the fragrance is the most successful of the "Nonsensical Essences"; it is subtle and not overwhelming, yet it has good longevity and a pleasant sillage. Essences Insensées 2014 is unisex, which I cannot attribute to the other two fragrances from 2015 and 2016, as they are more suited for women. Anyone who likes green floral scents, especially mimosas, should definitely test this fragrance; I am not sure, but I believe it is no longer being produced, as it is very rarely found.

To start on a positive note, this fragrance smells like summer. Just like in the last few days, very very hot, many people at the outdoor pool lying on the grass and using plenty of sunscreen. It initially starts very green, like freshly cut grass, the lawn in the morning, still dewy and freshly mowed. I seem to miss the violet and pepper. But after just a few minutes, the sun rises mercilessly hot, and something sweet joins in, gaining more and more dominance, very sweet-almondy, almost like baking aroma, while being powdery vanilla-like. Spicy not in the classical sense, rather radiating the spicy sweetness of acacia honey. Here I really wondered why I perceive no flowers at all, and did some research. Heliotropin, which is used in perfumery, is described as powdery, vanilla-like, and almond-like; it is said to have a relaxing and comforting effect. That describes it very well, as it is the scent profile that absolutely defines and dominates this fragrance for me. Heliotrope also means: turning towards the sun. I don't know how mimosa smells, but the scent essence from it is derived from a type of acacia, which is said to have honey-like facets. I am a little reconciled with my nose again. And then...? Unfortunately, nothing more comes. Grass and marzipan continue hand in hand in the height of summer and eventually make themselves comfortable on a blanket. There they stay, turned towards the sun and very relaxed. I hope more comments will come, as I cannot assess the longevity; as you all know, fragrances that you don't like are very hard to wash off, so I find it quite long-lasting... Anyone who loves sweet gourmand fragrances, vanilla crescents, and especially marzipan should definitely come and sniff this! It is not my scent at all; I am not a heliotrope lover, and the aroma seems a bit overdosed-artificial to me. I will trade the remaining sample for a second comment! :-)

La Nuit Trésor Musc Diamant is part of an impressive range of flankers for the original La Nuit. Being pretty inventive with the naming of all of these (I count 13 in the directory), this one is named Musc Diamant. I am not sure I understand why - the musk note is present in all three stages but diamant? Well, I suppose some has made a clever choice at some point…? At the time of writing this I own three of the La Nuits of which this one has the lowest rating, 7.6. Compared to the other two this is way more withdrawn and mild, which could be the reason. The La Nuits have got quite a reputation for being dark, seductive and berry sweet. But in this the berries are subtle. The quality of this is the powdery feeling which is backed up by the sweet vanilla. But do not expect the La Nuit DNA in this one. It would be like going to a stadium concert with Metallica and ending up in a pub listening to the local Irish folk band. On my skin this lasts between 3-5 hours. I consider this a moderate performance but it is still worth wearing. Just carry a purse spray with you. Sillage is well behaved so you can wear it for work. The bottle is white with a baby pink shade on the edges and the ribbon rose around the neck is white. Quite delicate. I like this one. Go try it - but hesitate to buy it blindly. Year 2, 20/365

Hmmm...When I first tested Tresor Musc Diamant, the scent of violet and raspberry from the top notes lingered for quite a long time on my skin. It reminded me of my favorite vape juice "Mora Violetta". And I loved it...combined with musk, it felt really cozy and unique. The second time though all that I could smell, after hours of having tested it, was a faint vanilla-musk-patchouli scent. Ιt really is a nice, soft perfume, but with so many musky perfumes out there to choose from, I won't bother buying it.

If pureness femeninity and innocence was a fragance it would be this one. So delicate! I would not recommend to women with strong character because this is a pretty soft fragance. The opening its pretty sharp but it softens A LOT . The dry down gave me imediately the image of a bride in her wedding dress with her flower bouquet.

Today, I set off with my husband to Kstadt because I wanted to call Eli Saab Resort my own. It is a limited edition, and there was only one bottle left on the table. Even my husband noticed that. But despite sharpening our pupils - the desired bottle seemed to be lost. My face grew longer and longer, and I claimed: It doesn't matter. However, my husband stalked a saleswoman and didn't let her go until she had dug up the sought-after Resort from some corner. Proudly, he held the find under my nose - and turned to leave. But then I discovered Musc Diamant a few tables away. Just taking a look. The first Tresor was a gift from my dear mom, which I initially regarded with skepticism because I didn't quite share her taste in fragrances as a teenager. Arpege, No 5, Soir de Paris, Byblos didn't appeal to me back then - although they suited her well. But for me, they weren't the hit at that time. Therefore, I was pleasantly surprised by the dear to lovely character of Tresor. In the meantime, I also host many flankers - and I wouldn't want to miss any of them. And Musc Diamant is also a treasure. A sweet web surrounds me - fine like cotton candy - but without being sticky. A white musk cloud floats in, and one wants to take off. The soft cloud drifts over fields of flowers and almond trees, accompanied by a hint of vanilla. Despite the delicious ingredients, Musc remains feather-light and cloudily transparent. I am actually not one to waver - but I find myself teetering. Resort or Tresor? My husband scores points with logic. The Saab is limited - and Musc will probably be available for a longer time. Well combined, Watson - I praise him - and postpone the treasure for later.

He he, hello and welcome to a new comment from me. And although this is a comment on the La Nuit fragrance line from Lancôme, this time the screaming perfume you surely know has nothing to do with it :D She recently just said that she would scream in my ears if I didn’t try the EDT of these fragrances at some point, but I chose to test this Musc Diamant all by myself. After all, I’m currently on this fragrance line and secondly, it’s also a relatively new scent. Testing this time was much easier, as I went to the city quite early, where most people were still at school, university, or work, so I could test the scent a bit more calmly. Of course, there were still some ladies present with the fragrances, but they were more busy looking for Christmas gifts rather than paying attention to me. However, I paid a lot more attention to them… what I noticed is: Are leather pants back in fashion? Many are currently walking around in these tight and somewhat shiny pants, and I must say that these pants are even very… um… butt-enhancing. Argh… yes, I’m sorry, but that’s how it is. While testing the fragrance, it happened again. I’m sniffing my arm and looking at my phone to read the fragrance notes here on Parfumo. But with one eye, I’m automatically glancing at a lady wearing one of those tight pants and I’m just thinking “Wow”!! And then this lady wants to look at the cosmetic products on the bottom shelf. But instead of kneeling down, which is always healthier, as doctors always say,… she BENDS down and it looks like the pants are about to burst!!! Ohmygoshohmygoshohmygosh!!! That sight… those are the kinds of things a man doesn’t forget quickly and therefore gets easily distracted. I’m lucky I didn’t drop the bottle from my hands!! While I’m still analyzing the fragrance, a little later another lady comes by in tight leather pants (this time in red),… but she does it right this time: She kneels down to look at the lower fragrances. And do you know what? It really doesn’t matter whether one (or actually, one should say woman) bends down in leather pants or kneels down, the curves are emphasized either way, and I… seem to be drifting further away… argh, I actually wanted to describe the fragrance here!! I better get to the fragrance before I’m finally thought of as perverted, if that hasn’t already happened… argh,… *sigh* The Fragrance: The fragrance starts with the listed raspberry note and a lot of musk. Regarding the fruity part, that is, the raspberry, I must say that sometimes it even comes across to me like a cherry. It fluctuates between these two fruits, but it might just be me. The musk, on the other hand, is noticeable throughout and is the main fragrance note from beginning to end. The indicated violets are rather weak and probably contribute to the slightly powdery aura of the fragrance. I smell even less of the roses. The middle part is basically just like the top note, only that the fruity notes become significantly weaker, so that the musk stands out even more. In the base, a little vanilla joins the musk, making the fragrance even softer and more powdery, and it also lasts longer. Overall, you mostly smell musk and later the vanilla-powdery sweetness, making the fragrance consistently beautifully distinctive. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage has been toned down compared to some other La Nuit fragrances and is therefore not immediately filling the room. The fragrance is still good to smell, but not over longer distances and thus not really comparable to other La Nuit fragrances that usually create huge scent clouds. The longevity also seems to be a little less, but is generally very long-lasting, so it can still be smelled on the skin after ten to twelve hours. The Bottle: The bottle has the well-known gemstone-diamond shape, so the shape fits very well with the nickname “Diamond.” The bottle is white-milky this time, with the top shimmering reddish depending on the light. As always, there is also a (now also white) silk ribbon around the neck with the name of the fragrance on it. A beautiful bottle as always. So… wow, the ladies in those tight leather pants were quite a sight,… uh… wait… actually, I didn’t want to bring that topic up again since I described it quite detailed at the beginning… but… why don’t you perfumes come to a Parfumo meeting dressed like that? No matter if a young “thing” in her twenties or… uh, a woman in her prime (uuuh, I hope that can be said!), such pants would look great on everyone :D But okay, back to the fragrance. Despite my fixation on behinds, this fragrance fortunately didn’t turn out to be a total flop. On the contrary, it’s actually quite nice. However, I must say that compared to the other La Nuit fragrances, it comes across as significantly less bombastic and sexy. One reason for this is that it has a lower sillage and generally seems a bit more harmless fragrance-wise. Instead, it is more elegant and, like all La Nuits, quite seductive. Furthermore, the fragrance feels less heavy, so it could not only be worn in autumn but also well in spring. By the way, this fragrance can also be used well for going out, although it is also suitable for daytime wear. So, you don’t necessarily have to have it unless you collect the La Nuit fragrances (like a certain screamer among you ladies here :D) You can definitely try it, especially if you find the other La Nuits a bit too sweet or if you’re into musk. Well then, that’s it again. I wish you all a nice evening, until next time :)

Don't expect a dirty bear scent! I was misled as well. How could one expect that from Lancome? They stay true to the previous theme. Namely sugary and sweet. Here I first smell the same base note as in Folie. Sugary, fruity, berry-like, but the musk is also present. Just sweet as well.

I spray and spray and am enveloped in a very fine and delicate mist, musk and a noble rose join in, rounded off by gentle vanilla. I love it. I find the scent very fine, very delicate, almost tender. I really like the Lancome fragrances, but this one, despite its beautiful notes, unfortunately does not last very long.

So I deleted a text again because I didn’t find the old one good enough anymore... Why? Because I changed my mind once again, as I now perceive the scent much more and better. In the old text, I described how it smelled far too strong of musk... But now all of a sudden, my nose perceives this scent MUCH better and more accurately...

This fragrance is actually what brought me here. I've always enjoyed sniffing around in the perfumery, but I never really understood what makes these scents what they are. Fragrance pyramid? Nope. Longevity? Nope. What the hell is a sillage? Yes, that's how it started. Until my friend and I went sniffing one day and this fragrance crossed our path.

First of all, the bottle in diamond shape, iridescent in white-pink-purple, is beautiful! It caught my eye immediately in the perfumery. I quickly tested it and was delighted! Fruity raspberry welcomes you, paired with a white musk cloud and a hint of vanilla. A delicate, light, sweet, and powdery scent veil surrounded me.

This body spray perfume will totally have mixed reviews as it´s citrusy/grassy/really herbal but has a smell of a mosquito repellent - indeed at the Diptyque shop they said that it was the actual idea to make it so. So if you are traveling to Nordic countries or lakes during the summer, I highly recommend to take this with you. It´s a light perfume so the scent in my bottle changed with years, so it´s the best to try to use it up during one season, but I still love it, it´s special.

Coach Leatherware & I did not have a good relationship... This is a fruity leather scent that is shall we say boring... The quality of this fragrance, is decent, not spectacular. It opens with zesty grapefruit & it seems on me at least, the fragrance goes straight towards the base notes. Leather, pathchouli & oakmoss appear. I don't see this being a serious staple in my collection which is why I sold it. The lasting power is 4 hours & it projects arms reach. You could do much better than this & enjoy a fragrance of this type that last longer considering it being a EDP.

So many mixed reactions surrounding this perfume, like: "grandma perfume" "not a vanilla" "super strong jasmine". Well... most of them are wrong, especially "grandma". Are we forgetting that grandma's were baddies in their youths? that stupid description is NOT stopping me from trying anything. I really came in the shop with no needs of trying it, but since I was there, why not? The vanilla slapped me. Straight up soft - creamy vanilla harassing my nostrils with some ice cream type of goodies. I told you, I got slapped so hard my credit card slipped and I (sadly) had to buy it. Now, the perfume is a very good mix of vanilla and jasmine. At first, the vanilla is very much prominent and I could smell the delicate scent on my wrist. When it fades, the jasmine is way more present and it tends to be powdery as well. I agree that after multiple hours, it's way more into a generic type of jasmine, I'll say it can disturb many, but I'm fine with it. The dry down also reminded me of "Le Temps des Secrets - Amande & Fleur de Murier | Jeanne en Provence" like a powdery bitter almond without removing that incredible and warm vanilla. I really love Lancôme DNA and never once thought it was "too old" or "grandma". I 100% recommend vanilla lovers to take a sniff !

A warm, soft, fluffy cloud of vanilla icing, speckled with jasmine flowers. Very delicate, light, and airy. Very feminine. Definitely more ethereal than the original, with only the barest hints of that DNA. While there is a good hit of vanilla in the initial spray, it turns muskier as it settles. Not necessarily a bad thing, as I found the vanilla a touch synthetic for my tastes, at least to begin with. I don’t pick up on any sandalwood, nor the coconut some other reviewers mention. Longevity is good for such a soft scent, still detectable on my skin almost 8 hours later. Projection is intimate. This is a pretty scent that I’m glad to have tried. It grew on me over the course of the day more than I initially expected it to.

A beautiful vanilla with a non-indolic jasmine opening that makes it truly pleasant and almost refreshing. But, to me, there is still a problem: while it may be an absolutely wearable and tasteful fragrance, it retains the DNA of the classic La Vie Est Belle. There's no point ignoring the elephant in the room: that DNA is there, it bothers me incredibly and ruins what could have been a perfume I would have appreciated and perhaps purchased. If, on the other hand, you're a fan of the raucous progenitor of this family, you'll probably find it adorable. It's still a cute vanilla with a slightly powdery touch to adds delicacy to the whole composition. Excellent persistence and significant sillage. I think it will sell well.

This latest LVEB flanker opens as a bright fresh floral vanilla with a hint of powder and musk and stays pretty linear throughout its life on my skin. It’s nothing like LVEB OG, in fact, the minute I whiffed it, my immediate thoughts were “This is Lancôme doing a gentler Libre”, and that’s it! Where YSL Libre is a nuclear bomb of lavender, bourbon vanilla, orange blossom, jasmine and musk. LVEB is a toned down version of these exacts notes except they went easy on the lavender.. but, to my nose, there’s defo lavender there despite it not being listed. And there’s a little hint of neroli dancing with the orange blossom too. And you know what, it’s absolutely beautiful and delightful. Where I struggled with the overpowering Libre that causes me headaches if worn indoors, Vanilla Nude is extremely easy to wear and a joy to wear. It’s bright, clean and feminine, beautiful and extremely comforting everytime a whiff catches my nose with its slight envelope of powdery musk that makes it very much a gorgeous perfume. It’s beautifully blended, as to be expected of a Lancôme but this was also created by one of my fav perfumer collabs, Anne Flipo and Dominique Ropion. I find whenever they work together that Flipo tempers some of Ropions loudness to create beautiful, wearable popular fragrances. So would I get a full bottle? Well, there wasn’t anything that really jumped out at me and made my brain go ‘I need this IMMEDIATELY’. It’s a perfect office, day wear scent and if I was gifted a bottle I would happily use it up. I would certainly reach for it more readily than my LVEB OG with its strong, sensual praline dry down (I think I’ve worn that once this year). So looking forward to wearing this sample a few times, I could see me falling for this as a new office scent.

First whiff was mediocre. Strong LVEB scent surrounded by a cloud of vanilla. It became interesting around 10min after. It’s been 4 hours and the dry down is a stuffy vanilla scent, nothing else remains. Not in a cookie or fresh vanilla pod kinda way but like some people said, a bit like a vanilla scented candle or one of those scented car things. Binning the sample I got.

Years ago I had a delicate shimmering body powder with a charming little squeeze bulb - it left a subtle golden glow on the skin, but its real magic was the scent: a perfect blend of vanilla and coconut. When it was discontinued, I was a bit sad and spent years searching for a replacement.

The opening slips past my senses—pale impressions of sunlit freshness without clear definition. In time, soft florals emerge, lending a touch of sweetness, yet it is the base that truly captivates: a sensual, creamy vanilla that appears almost unexpectedly and lingers for hours.

As we women are, something is always being sold on classifieds, I am quite the repeat offender. And my husband has to stand at the door and hand it over, because you never know who is coming. It was again one of those evenings. 7 PM - on the dot, the little table is picked up. My husband takes over, I "hide" behind the hallway.

I just bought a 30ml bottle at my local perfumery - it was on sale for €52 including a beach towel as a gift. The scent is very strong - like most in this line (even though NOT all LVEB flankers..). It strongly reminds me of the typical, quite synthetic vanilla scented candles or room fresheners - sounds rather off-putting.. and yet, strangely, it suits the scent well.

At first, I found the scent extremely unpleasant. I was literally overwhelmed by a penetrating wave of synthetic vanilla that immediately connected with the all-too-familiar sweet perfume cloud of La Vie est Belle. It is scratchy, biting, and in a strange way unpleasantly sweet - almost artificial and too intrusive. However, after a while, it calms down.

How do I begin? Best to start with the bottle. When I saw it here on Parfumo, I was smitten. What a beautiful design! I love crystal. And it’s supposed to smell like Tiare? Frangipani? South Sea associations? Hmm, that could appeal to me too. So I rushed to Diptyque, while these limited bottles are still available. The bottle immediately caught my eye in the store. And hmm, it was disenchanted. Yes, unfortunately. Not as beautifully sparkling as I had hoped. Pressed glass, sure. But really just pressed glass. And how does it smell? My scent memory didn’t take long to tell me "I know this one." And yes, for example, Rem by Reminiscence smells like this. Summer-light, aquatic-vanilla. Essences Insensees has a slightly more floral scent, maybe a touch of wood, a bit sweeter. But Tiare, Frangipani? No, sorry, I don’t smell any of that. So if possible, please test and check it out yourself. After all, it would be a larger investment .

Dear community, I like the La Vie est Belle - series! So, now it's out. (Oh dear, do I see the angry mob with pitchforks on the horizon?! *ducks away*) For many of you, this, especially the classic LVEB, is the epitome of boredom. Uninspiring, or worse: The ultimate mainstream! *shivers* But I stand by it and was of course completely thrilled when I first heard about the latest flanker "Intensement." The desire to test it was awakened immediately, and at the first opportunity, I jumped in blindly. Shortly after spraying, you perceive the familiar LVEB DNA for a minimal short time. However, this quickly gives way to a sea of red fruits. In the top note, it is said that raspberry is responsible for this. However, I can't specifically identify it. Rather, it seems as if all kinds of red berries have agreed to a flash mob. Well, what can I say... From this moment on, you wait eagerly but unfortunately in vain for the scent to change again. Where are the red iris, the red vanilla, or the benzoin? It seems as if they just managed to get to safety in time. Safe, from the invasion of the red berries! The floral notes of the heart note have also (warning, pun!) heartily decided to stay away from the event.
