At most, a slight powderiness drizzles down on the fruit bombs towards the end of the scent's progression. However, these cannot be properly contained. I am really disappointed. Only the pretty bottle in Bordeaux red can excite me. Aside from that, this is a narcotic red fruit soup that robs me of my senses. Thus, I will stick with the predecessors LVEB EdP Intense and L'Absolu and patiently wait for the next flanker. Because it will surely come!

A dear perfumer recommended that I test Intensement - and I am very open to tips. At first, I had avoided La vie est belle because I didn't like the artificial woman Roberts in the commercial. But then I couldn't resist a special offer - and LVEB made its way into our home. A good deed, because the fragrance truly conveys the feeling that life can be beautiful. There followed several flankers - all of which are independent but carry the genes of the original mother. So it is with Intensement. It is the beautiful life in the orchard, surrounded by raspberry bushes. It does not deny its kinship to the original scent - although its theme is the soft sweet raspberry. Although vanilla is added, Intensement does not become too sweet - and certainly not sticky, as jasmine and orange blossom float above it. A welcome garden feeling that I enjoy indoors, as the drizzling rain is pounding on my beds outdoors. The fragrance fits well in autumn, due to its ripe fruitiness. This flanker also finds its place in the La Vie est Belle family.

When I first sprayed the perfume, I didn't have the different notes clearly in mind, which is why I had no concrete idea or expectation. I suspected it would be sweet, and my only hope was that it would smell different from the original LVEB, as I unfortunately didn't like that one at all. The first note I perceived was the pear. It immediately made me think of La Belle.. The second perfume that came to mind was La Nuit Trésor à la Folie. For me, it is a blend of the two scents. After that, I really wanted to check the notes, and lo and behold, pear is not listed, but raspberry is. With this knowledge and some time that has passed, I also distinctly smelled the raspberry, and the 'pear aroma' had vanished. What raspberry definitely has in common with pear is the strong sweetness. The LVEB Intensément clearly stands out from the original, which is why I like it much better! I was not disappointed.

By chance, I discovered you. I wasn't quite sure what to think of you. You were sweet, initially much too fruity, but in the base so soft, vanilla-like. I had to try you again and again and never knew if we would become friends. During a very oppressive time, I sprayed you on and since then I feel embraced, safe, protected by you. Over and over again. As if a very good friend were comforting me in her arms. I don't perceive you constantly, but now and then you show me that you are there and send me a nice gesture, and I know you are by my side. You have elicited a compliment from my dearest person, and thus I associate you even more with happiness and love. You are my absolute number one. I keep coming back to you. I hope we remain friends forever, I hope you always look out for me!

First of all, I want to note that yes, it is a beautiful, fine, and life-affirming fragrance! Now here comes the but.... for an Intense, it definitely does not last long enough for me; after 4-6 hours, there is only a light, quite pleasant and fragrant little perfume left. Life's joy should burst with energy and should also be a bit louder. It adapts to its predecessors as it is pleasing, will appeal to many girls of all ages, and the house of Lancome still has that French flair. The bottle looks very nice, feels good in the hand, and is an eye-catcher with its cheeky little red scarf. I find this scent floral-fruity with a sweet base. Patchouli has hidden itself well - it only peeks around the corner cautiously..... it seems a bit shy to show itself. The development feels to me like a fruit basket sitting outside on the table in summer, next to it a large bouquet of wonderfully fragrant flowers, and as a third element, a big bowl of melted vanilla ice cream. You sit at the table with your eyes closed, and all the aromas mix and rise to your nose. It smells very pleasant, delicious, and I feel comfortable in this overall picture. That's how I would describe it. It is well-suited as a gift for my friend as a reminder of our fun girl talk in a wonderful summer location.

La vie est belle is a fragrance that, although often encountered on people, has never bored or annoyed me. I own it myself, like it, and wear it from time to time. While I appreciate flankers like LVEB En Rose as a fresher, fruitier variant, Intensément does not score points with me.

Sugary aroma of raspberry jam. In contrast to the original LVEB and the intense version, this version lacks the same tonal depth that would elevate the strong sweetness. In sweetness, it is almost comparable to Aquolina Pink Sugar. In the base, the situation improves somewhat, a pleasant powderiness emerges, but it takes a while until I reach the base notes.

Yes, as mentioned before, I am not really a fan of La vie est belle, but this nuance with patchouli and sandalwood in the base is just totally my thing. I recently received a sample and have to say, the scent lasts incredibly long. I think it's great what Lancôme always does with the bottle.

The iris blossom, floral-powdery-leathery-smoky, is the star here, and already noticeable in the top notes. All the other notes are the garment that makes it appear femininely sweet and pleasing despite its edges. On the skin, the sweet soft vanilla quickly reveals itself.

Actually, "La Vie est Belle Intensément" has theoretically "everything I need" in terms of notes. But that's the fascination with perfumes, just like with music, so many surprising results can arise from the combination of different notes. At the beginning, it smells floral-fruity and overall very subtle.

I find Cuir to be definitively leather, but so unlike most of the other leathers I know. There is not a trace of scratchiness that I usually associate with leather scents such as Bandit, Aramis or Rien. In fact it’s hard for me to consider Cuir and Rien in the same category. Cuir is a sweet, smoky floral leather (I get a lot of iris.) I can’t quite point to the source of the smoothness. Perhaps it is simply its well-considered moderation. Cuir has the nose feel of an emollient, viscous but not sticky. It makes me prick up my ears waiting for that roughness that the composition tells me is coming. But then, no, it’s more like a low-pitched vibration. The growl is implied, but what I hear is a purr, with all the sly contentment that a lounging cat suggests. Overall, I find Cuir very sophisticated. I tend to love rough and angular fragrances. Cuir is certainly not one of them. That said, Cuir does make me sniff my own wrist more often than any other perfume I can think of. I suppose I’m always listening for the growl. If Cuir is a bit of a tease, I’ve fallen for him.

Lancome Cuir is familiar & comfortable but feels affluent. I imagine a well-breed aunt who dresses in a Chanel suit yet always welcomes you with a hug. On me, Cuir opens as a slighty dark - almost smoky - leather scent that warms, mellows & lightens as it drys. The leather in Cuir is smooth, buttery and pliable, like a pair of kid leather gloves in taupe. As Cuir develops, the florals become more noticeable. I don't pick out jasmine & ylang-ylang, but something else ... perhaps the saffron & the hawthorn, plus a powdery characteristic likely from orris. Lancome Cuir is a soft, floral leather which could easily be worn by a guy. It lacks the astringency and potency of other femme leathers such as Bandit and Cabochard, so it makes a good introduction to leather fragrances. It's also available at a price-point to-die-for (about 40 USD). Cuir is unique enough to smell niche and high-quality enough to smell lux. Simply, it's too gorgeous to ignore.

I only realized I would miss the scent after I had given away my sample of Cuir de Lancôme and, in a moment of impulse, made a regrettable purchase. It was almost acute: while my regrettable order was on its way (a reckless detour into indole), I enjoyed the sample that had been sent to me and wore it intensively for 2 days, with everything that everyday life currently has to offer... and it came to pass as it had to: I was properly annoyed by something (not hard, given everything that everyday life currently has to offer) and the previously softly animalic flowers combined unfavorably with my annoyance into an irreversible indolic penetrance... Even before my order arrived, I was done with it. Now a comforting scent had to be worn, a confidant with an everything-will-be-okay function, one that grounds you, brings you back to your center - thematically best one that is close, human, quiet... somehow like that. But I had just paused my search for a suitable musk scent. While I turned to some of my favorite scents in my collection to regulate my disappointment, I remembered that I had recently tested this discontinued Lancôme scent... it had been beautiful. But indeed discontinued. Even with a leather note... without leather being in it... it had been truly exceptionally beautiful... Where is the sample?! Oh no, I don't have it anymore - I actually don't like leather scents... But it had something... with very delicate patchouli... Ah, patchouli would be great now. Soft, not cold earthy. And besides, it's a SKIN-REFINER! Why did I give away the sample again? Oh right, it's discontinued. Wasn't there recently in the souk...?! Yes! And it was still there! It had patiently waited for me! Today it has arrived with me. And I can't get enough of sniffing it! It has everything I need right now, and I'm sure it can offer much more than just comfort. With heartfelt thanks to Parfuma, who let me have it, and to Gaukeleya, who once again hit my taste perfectly - and this time I had to sniff twice to realize that this is indeed the case. _________________________________ The scent opens briefly fresh, only to then create a spicy and simultaneously buttery soft leather illusion from saffron, patchouli, and flowers, with a gentle smoky quality in the periphery for me. Beautiful, clean, soft leather, sometimes smooth, sometimes velvety, like those popular hippie suede jackets that we used to wear with jeans with holes in the knees in the 80s (back when holes in pants legs still had a rebellious, alternative vibe)... One can also imagine an elegant-luxurious leather glove understatement during a convertible ride. Over time, Cuir de Lancôme becomes increasingly smoother, softer, and creamier. If you want, you can catch a whiff of a few flowers, or simply continue to inhale the beautiful leather note. The scent embraces you, and the very mild hawthorn animality makes it almost merge with the skin, feeling somewhat human, while you feel well-groomed throughout, but not sterile-clean. The birch doesn't come through strongly for me, the iris feels rather rooty and, together with the styrax, forms a very subtly sweet base (without the support of vanilla, benzoin, or tonka). Wonderful - and why was it discontinued again? My rating has now been corrected from 8.5 to 10. __________________________________ Regarding the regrettable purchase: since I still find that this one is beautiful and it really can't do anything for my unfortunate conditioning, I don't want to go into detail about which scent it was. It taught me two things: even delicately presented perfumes can enter into an unfavorable liaison with one's own mood, so occasions for wearing newly discovered scents should be chosen carefully... AND: Ms. UnderValue, stop with the impulse purchases!

A tiny hint of mandarin teases briefly, but the actual opening is immediately dusty leather, which comes from the patchouli corner, supported by saffron. Bright and delicate. Within a minute or two, a touch of eel-smoked aroma forms alongside it. Not overpowering, but finely spicy. Exciting! It smells as if the namesake leather is meant to be varied. A few minutes later, a diffuse floral veil has settled over the fragrance. Very distinctive - so far, I am definitely not (at least not exclusively) in the "women's fragrance" category. Slowly, the focus shifts towards sweetness. Nothing from what is indicated matches my impression; I think of a mild, lightly honey-sweetened herbal tea. But the friendly, calm rain remains the equally nuanced and extraordinarily noble leather note, which has just the right portion of smoky tea to still be considered thoroughly elegant. I am thrilled. Behind it, the presumably hawthorn pricks and stings, but in the overall picture, it is neutralized by the still-present addition of subtle sweetness, for which I still have no reasonable suggestion. A hint of throat lozenge (similar to what I know from the violet corner) can be diagnosed from the second hour onward. This would support the thesis that a range of leather variations is being showcased here; thus, it may be somewhat wishful thinking on my part. In the late morning, a gently vanillated amber note appears, optionally ambered noble vanilla. This means: wonderfully distinguished. The leather idea, on the other hand, takes a backseat. This (as will become apparent) interlude culminates around noon in a chocolaty patchouli note. In the afternoon, Cuir de Lancôme finds rest in softly smoked, sour leather with a pinch of resin alongside restrained throat lozenge sweetness. Vanilla increasingly becomes prominent as it progresses. Depending on the dosage, the fragrance fades in the eighth to tenth hour. As a final remnant, I imagine amber/vanilla. Conclusion: Great! And essentially unisex. I thank Turandot for the sample.

I love the scent of leather, which is why Cuir was a must for me. Cuir is a fragrance of subtle yet penetrating notes, "understatement" comes to mind. Cuir is not a scent for a grand entrance; it does not belong to the bold, strong leather category, which I also quite like. Cuir is light and delicate, soft and rounded; it doesn't step on anyone's toes, is reserved but noticeable. My association is a dainty, cream-colored leather couch in a sunny, bright conservatory filled with many colorful flowers. A fragrance that makes me feel comfortable, that doesn't draw attention but is still perceived, that grounds and calms me, and fits many situations. The sillage is rather close to the skin, and the longevity is moderate for me. I find Cuir most beautiful in spring and autumn, although I wouldn't limit it to seasons. The bottle is simple, easy to handle, and I like it a lot. Well, I don't wear it often, but when I do, I enjoy it all day long. And only while writing this do I realize how much I appreciate it.

Somehow I came across Cuir de Lancome: I wanted to explore leather as a fragrance note in perfumes, the scent was available online at a good price and was also considered a modern classic by many. At first, I was a bit disappointed because Cuir seemed harsher and less gentle in its leather note than I had hoped.
The shy Lady D. had become the wife of a significantly older and very wealthy nobleman as a scion of a impoverished British aristocratic family.

Of course, Cuir de Lancome is a leather scent, even if it doesn't state so in the pyramid. The leather note is very beautiful. Here, one experiences a very clean, smooth, and new leather. I almost thought I could sense some oud like in Montale's Oud Cuir d‘Arabie. However, the leather note in Cuir de Lancome is much more subtle, skillful, and refined - simply beautiful.

A truly special leather scent because it is so refined. The moment when the fragrance transitions from a slightly resinous-fruity accompaniment of the leather to a fine and not at all sweet base that only slightly reminds one of vanilla is simply dreamy. Never heavy, but always more like a textile with a hint of leather dust powder, inviting to the touch.

First of all, a huge thank you to the donor of a true flood of samples of women's classics... This will be a real education in terms of perfume. Because even the first testing of this little sample armada left an impression. Even though many smelled similar at first whiff, some even extremely old-fashioned and requiring getting used to, the positive impressions prevailed.

This is a perfect fragrance. Not only is the longevity on this from just one spray insane (24+ hours) but every single whiff I get is an absolute pleasure. A mouth watering fruity gourmand all day and night that does not get boring. If this isn't available anymore it's a damn shame, even though I'll never get through my bottle for how little is actually needed for each wear.

...there was a girl named Belle Absolu. Belle Absolu came from the royal family of the great kingdom of Lancôme. But although she was of royal descent, Belle Absolu had a hard time, for her father was missing and her mother, Lavieé Belle, was an extremely imposing and equally revered as well as hated princess, whose widely shining and magnificent banner drew the eyes of the people throughout the streets of the vast kingdom. Belle Absolu had several sisters who also led a submissive existence in the shadow of their powerful mother, but Belle Absolu not only remained in the shadow, but most people in the kingdom didn't even know of her existence. Belle Absolu, whose full name was actually Lavieé Belle L'Absolu, had realized over time that it was rather disadvantageous for her to tell strangers her full name. Either people broke into praises about her wonderful princess mother and tried to use little Belle to gain favor at court, or they regarded the girl with disdain - she could hardly be less ruthless and self-satisfied than her ubiquitous, intrusive mother and some of her eagerly pushing sisters. Thus, the girl had no real friends. However, little Belle was quite different in character from her mother. At first glance, she seemed similar, starting with the fact that she also wore the royal robes of her house with the fine, transparent gray scarf and her noble figure. Her eye color of dark amber was almost the same, as was her tendency towards fruit and sweets. But after just a few minutes of getting to know her, it became clear to the few who didn’t immediately look away that Belle Absolu was much more refined in her restraint than her mother. She was also milder and gentler in nature. While her mother, with her preference for sugary and sharply roasted, sour fruits with jasmine, seemed rather loud and biting to many, Belle Absolu loved ripe and juicy fruits along with a large bouquet of powder-blue iris. She liked sweets just like her mother, but she had, as befits a good dessert, never forgotten the pinch of salt. In fact, it was not just a pinch, but so much that it reminded one of salted caramel. Last but not least, if one had the patience to truly get to know little Belle, one could eventually discover her preference for exquisite, delicate, and at the same time powerful leather, which she would wrap herself in quietly in her little chamber for the long night hours. Thus, little Belle Absolu not only stood in the shadow of her mother, was not only exploited to gain access to the court, was not only rejected outright by the haters of the Lavieé Belle family, but was also overlooked because of her inherent restraint. No wonder she felt unloved and lonely. One day, the girl met a blind man. He treated her completely differently than she was used to, so unbiased and open that she cried all night out of emotion. The very next day, she devised something she would henceforth call her "Blind Test": She dressed in the very simple robes of the common people and spoke of herself only as Belle Absolu. How surprised she was at how friendly and appreciative people were towards her under these circumstances. People suddenly became interested in her, in her alone, in her as a unique person! Some sensed that she had received a royal education and asked her if she came from the house of Guerlain, known for iris, or if she was related to the Salt Caramels from the kingdom of Shay & Blue. Others claimed to recognize in her the genetic line of the princes of Bottega Veneta, known for fine leather. Sometime in the distant future, Princess Lavieé Belle, like so many celebrities before her, will probably have undergone a multitude of cosmetic surgeries. Once she is no longer recognized by her admirers, the royal house will likely send her into retirement, as seems to be the fate of once radiant princesses. Perhaps then will come the hour when Belle Absolu can step into the spotlight. However, that is very unlikely. Much more likely is that once again a more dominant and larger-than-life person will carry her banners through the streets. Ultimately, though, that would not matter, for in the meantime, Belle Absolu has found a number of true, loyal friends through her "Blind Tests" and has become happy in her own way. And if they haven't died, they still live today.

I have always kept my distance from La vie est belle, fear of mainstream was the reason, having sniffed it once and since the launch, you can smell it on every 4th to 6th woman who can afford it. It was simply unsympathetic to me. Today - oh my goodness! Just because I was strolling around and saw the beautiful color of this little water, I dared to try it. I sprayed l'absolut... And ... Fuck yes! It hit me - kaboom! That happens rarely - I fell in love. As a devoted Guerlain fan, this almost shocked me! This spontaneous love for a Julia Roberts protégée (in absolu ;-)). From the very beginning, it smelled on me like salty sweetness. I can't describe it any other way. I have to constantly smell my wrist and sigh every time in delight and astonishment at the same time. I'm not a gourmand lover, more one of the oriental fetishists... But the punch - folks, test it if you have the chance. It surprises. I wish you good luck and a punch .... By the way, My Visa is crying, 60,- for 20 ml is quite hefty, but L'Absolu, 2 sprays and it's enough for a day and a night. Sweet and sour. I love Halloween and I love this punch.

“La Vie est Belle” - a modern fragrance classic. Whether you love it or hate it, its success is outstanding. For years, this scent has topped the “charts” and is a true bestseller. I also own a large bottle of the original flanker, but I don’t use it too often. Why? It’s often a bit too scratchy for me. Too loud and biting, a bit too much sweetness and not enough depth. Too syrupy. I like the fine praline note in the base, which even slightly reminds me of popcorn. However, the overall composition sometimes feels a bit too restless. Nevertheless, I really enjoy it when I spray it into the air and walk through the mist. Then I’m surrounded all day long by a cotton candy-like cloud, which I find truly beautiful. The concentration of the spray mist is the secret. - The other fragrances in the “LVEB” line have never really interested me. As I said, I like the original scent, but it’s not one of my favorites. However, I did test “L'Absolu” in a perfume store a few years ago. In winter, December. A spritz on my jacket sleeve. At that time, my sense of smell was already overwhelmed, so I hardly perceived anything and went home. I quickly forgot the scent, lay down in bed, and fell asleep. The next day, I was greeted in the hallway by a wonderful fragrance. So sweet, soft, and warm. I felt as if I were standing in the middle of a Christmas market. Throughout the day, the mentioned scent kept wafting into my nose, and I constantly wondered what smelled so wonderful. At some point, it clicked, and I realized that my jacket sleeve was the scent messenger. For the next few days, I left the jacket hanging in the hallway because the scent just wouldn’t fade. For days, I had to hear from my family and guests how lovely it smelled in our wardrobe. Only after 3/4 days did the scent dissipate. It was immediately clear: I had to have it - and so the “L'Absolu” version moved in with me shortly after Christmas. For me, “L'Absolu” is a complete version of “La Vie est Belle,” which possesses much more warmth and depth. The scent feels significantly softer and rounder. I find the top note extremely interesting: powdery iris and dark ripe berries nestled in a sweet cotton candy cloud, along with slightly earthy patchouli. Perhaps it’s this note that triggers a “lipstick association” in me. Alongside the truly beautiful sweetness, I perceive a slight lipstick note. I wouldn’t call it overly disturbing, but I’m glad that this impression is only really present in the top note. In the heart, the powdery iris dominates in connection with the sweet and warm base. The information regarding the fragrance pyramid for this scent varies greatly depending on the website. Often, “praline” and “tonka” are also mentioned as part of the base. I too find that the base reminds me of tonka and chocolate. Also of roasted almonds. A Christmas market in a bottle. Without any scratchiness, but with a lot of warmth. The sillage is very strong. 1-2 spritzes are completely sufficient to envelop yourself in a sweetly warm cloud. Just like with the original scent, I prefer to spray 2 spritzes into the air and walk through the mist. This way, the fragrance is best expressed, and it doesn’t diminish the projection. The longevity is truly outstanding. On the skin, it becomes intimate only after 9-10 hours and dissipates after 13/14 hours; on clothing, it lasts for days. All in all, a really beautiful scent for cold winter days. I usually wear it at Christmas.

The first thing that hits me when I spray it is a caramel cloud, even though there’s nothing of the sort listed in the fragrance pyramid. Those who compiled the list must have been completely dazed and deprived of their senses to forget this note ;-))) Such burnt sugar needs to be digested first! I absolutely do not mean this as a devastating critique; rather, I completely understand these ladies and gentlemen, as I feel the same way about the opening. A perfume cannot start more spectacularly! As if a squeaky pink fairy is hovering above me, pouring buckets of equally pink icing over me. Until my gray clothing is completely covered. And the crazy thing is, I don’t even want to scold the fairy. With every bucket emptied over me, my mood rises. Orange and jasmine set the bar high. Who can keep up with that? This duo is something else! The rose, in any case, tries to keep up, but I think it remains just a try. The others are too strong for that. However, those who succeed, in my opinion, are more Cashmeran and praline. And they really put in a lot of effort. I feel like I’m in a baking show, only that it’s not the bakers competing to bake cakes and other treats, but the ingredients challenging each other for the top spots. It gets even more exciting when pear and currant join the race. They manage to slow down the initial sugar rush a bit and fight their way to the front. The tonka bean catches the sweeties that have gone off the rails and prevents them from overheating and sticking somewhere. The bakers are still standing around completely stunned, watching the scene with skepticism. They have simply been relegated to extras, and the shock runs deep. But who will be awarded the prize now? I think everyone has performed equally valiantly and is a winner. Because the result with all the ingredients is a single, sensual masterpiece! Intense in a positive sense is the longevity of this colorful fireworks display. A drop here and at most half a drop there, and you can sense it all day long. For the office, I would still share the half drop. But in the evening, it can stay whole. The affiliation with the La Vie Est Belle family is undeniable. You would immediately recognize it among all the other similar and sugary followers. The Absolu variant is sweeter, softer, and stronger. In the end, Cashmeran returns with its woody note and rounds off softly, whereas the Eau de Parfum still shows some herbaceousness. The Absolu then remains as it is and does not change further on my skin or on clothing. The intense and heavy scent, in my opinion, is made for cool temperatures. And the colder, the better. It definitely has what it takes to drive away the grimmest yeti and let the sun shine. This is how I imagine the scene: a beautiful winter landscape, everything thickly covered in white, the snow crystals glimmer kitschily in the sun, like trillions of diamonds, the air is icy and pure. I am warmly bundled up in coat, scarf, and boots. No sound can be heard, everything is peaceful and still. I sit on a bench in the midst of this dream landscape, soaking in the view once more and closing my eyes. Then I take a deep breath of my Absolu. In that exact moment, I feel: La Vie Est Absolument Belle.

I have struggled with the entire "La vie est belle" line until now - for me, they have always been offshoots of my beloved "Flowerbombs". In my opinion, the original version smells exactly like the purple bomb, perhaps a bit sweeter and without the woody notes present in Flowerbomb. Also, in terms of price, "La vie est belle" would have been a good alternative.

When I discovered the small darker La vie est belle bottle in my perfume shop, my heart skipped a beat. I tried it on my wrist. You immediately notice that something heavy, intense, and very sweet is coming your way. A La vie est belle that is stronger and more beautiful than ever before. I am a confessed fan of the EdP and the EdT.

~ Inspiration ~ I became aware of this version here on Parfumo. I first received a sample from Bluebird, and shortly after, Pepper81 gifted me their bottle :) ~ Bottle ~ You can immediately tell by the thick glass bottom and gray-silver ribbon that this is a "La Vie est Belle" offshoot.

Admittedly - the question may seem oddly out of place as a title for a perfume review. However, it is important to know that this review came about as part of a blind test. The lovely First put together a wonderful travel package with 9 fragrances, from which each of us in the group could choose one to keep - of course, without knowing which scent it actually was.

It is a gloomy, rainy day and I think already in the morning : Today it has to be chocolate. Not much, just a small piece. I go to the bathroom, see the beautiful bottle with a bow and the reddish-brown liquid - why not spray a little? The opening is already very rich. Orange blossoms and jasmine create a sweet, creamy melt.

A pretty, bright, light perfume from Coach. Nothing extraordinary, but nice none-the-less. It's more of a woody floral to my nose with a hint of citrus to keep it fresh. Best suited for spring and summer, though I like to spritz myself when I'm feeling down for a nice pick me up. I can smell the Coach Legacy and Signature in the composition. I find it a bit more mature than the Poppy line so if you like the Coach vibe, but need something a bit more grown up then give Signature Summer Legacy a try..

Rose and woods? That's totally my thing. Unisex and not too intrusive? It is. A winter fragrance? Not really. At least it doesn't keep you warm. It has something icy cold about it. The pink rose for me starts fresh and cold, slightly sweet-bitter in the middle where powdery ambrette wood is waiting. Almost gray on gray, dry, noble, soft, and yet somewhat dusty rustic. Powdery dried grasses. This is how an old bedroom in Naples might smell at 5° degrees above outside. It somehow reminds me of my childhood. An aged modern scent? Is that possible? I discover yellow and white flowers. Along with leafy green. Fresh but still dusty undertones. Pepper is bright and pleasantly restrained. It only tingles a little. At least I didn't have to sneeze. Vetiver is fresh, green, fine, and slightly sour. Sometimes I think of Nemer by Boadicea and white musk plus plastic oud. Prada also had something similarly powdery. I think of Luna Rossa Black! Just without the rose. I also get centifolia wrapped in fresh Chinese plastic. Plastic smell. Sounds silly, but it's beautiful and at the same time somewhat disturbing in its notes. But that might be my skin. As always. Somehow I feel very drawn to it. Its dry down is beautifully delicate and also woody-powdery. I would rather wear it in summer. In the evening at a restaurant. It lasts 8 hours and is only available in 100ml as EdT. So if you're into a soft, cold, dusty green rose scent, this is the right one for you. But beware. Limited.

What a radiantly beautiful, fresh, clean, dewy-green, orange blossom floral! This lovely flanker opens with a splash of dewdrop-fresh citric greens embraced by a warmly lush heart of neroli, clean jasmine, and headily smooth creamy orange blossoms. The tenderly soft base of clean, light woods and benzoin envelops everything in a tenderly soft cocoon of warm elegance and subtle sweetness. This is a delicately intoxicating haze of clean, white seduction. Feminine in extremis. I am enchanted.

Upon first spray, I was immediately reminded of Alien from Thierry Mugler. Maybe not the Eau de Parfum, but a cleaner version. Perhaps the Alien Eau de Toilette or Alien Aqua Chic? I desire to call it, "L'eau de Alien". I believe this is due to the way in which the jasmine is used or breed of jasmine. O de L`Orangerie craftfully uses more citrus and benzoin opposed to amber. This is a very fresh, well balanced floral where all of the notes equally share the bottle.

If you love orange blossom as much as I do, this O de Lancome flanker is worth checking out. I turn to wearing fresh orange blossom scents at the start of every Spring. It's my way of avoiding fruity or citrusy scents, and sticking with florals. O de L'Orangerie is so light and fresh on the skin, that it's perfect for those hot Spring and Summer days. It's also a tad sweet, in a way that compliments the rest of the composition. The scent in its entirety strikes me as being rather cool and crisp. The mint-green coloured bottle really does suit the scent, as it's quite fresh yet feminine. It may never live up to its classic and unique predecessor, O de Lancome, but this flanker does have the ability to stand on its own two feet. Its zesty approach to orange blossom intrigues me, and is also what makes it so universally pleasing. It's unfortunate that O de L'Orangerie is a limited edition. The only stores that still stock it tend to be duty free, and I fear that after this year, it will become increasingly harder to find. O de Lancome, O de L'Orangerie and the accompanying flankers are some of the very best from Lancome. Although the projection is a little weak, the lasting strength is surprisingly good. I tested it before heading off to work and still caught wafts of it after I finished my shift. I recommend. Original review written: November 2012.

I came across this fragrance yesterday while searching for another scent from which I wanted to fill a sample. There isn’t much more to say about this fragrance; some say it’s boring, others say it’s beautifully refreshing, both are true. When summer in the Rhineland is hot and sunny, when heels get stuck in the tar on the street, when the air shimmers before your eyes, and the thunderstorm and rain drive the humidity even higher, then it’s time for Ô de l'Orangerie. With this fragrance, I primarily perceive fresh, juicy orange, not sweet, not too sour. The jasmine hides from me, the scent remains beautifully orangey-citrusy, is a bit bitter and greenish-herbaceous, and after a while becomes softer and slightly woody. An ideal, rather linear fragrance for hot days, which, alongside its freshness, also conveys a wonderful impression of cleanliness. The big sister, Ô de Lancôme, was also in my collection years ago, but today I prefer the little sister, as she is not quite as citrusy-sour as the older sister. Longevity and sillage are quite weak, but when used with the body lotion, both are acceptable. Additionally, the price is quite reasonable, so you can confidently reapply. The ribbed glass bottle is aesthetically pleasing and, despite its size, fits well in the hand. Although O de L’orangerie is classified for women, I consider it quite suitable for the stronger sex.

At first, I couldn't really warm up to the scent (*waving over to Lilau*). I was probably just disappointed that, as a little gourmand fan, I wasn't catered to as hoped. What I imagined was: a big, juicy Capri-Sonne Orange would be presented to me. Or Sunkist Orange. Delicious, fruity, sweet-juicy, ready to bite into (or to enjoy sipping). Far from it! Here, a bitter, herbal, alcoholic adult beverage is opened. The orange is not pleasing, but rather very brittle. By the way, I can clearly smell it throughout; the floral notes never really dominate, despite the finely radiant jasmine at the heart. I also find the scent rather dry. As it develops, the orange becomes more agreeable. Initially bitter enough to make you cough, it gradually loses its harshness and becomes softer. But never, really never, is it sweet. The base is delicate and pleasant, cool and soft, the bitterness has evaporated. The longevity is surprisingly good for this type of summer fragrance. Yes, it outperforms its garden competitors from Hermès in my cabinet by a long shot in this regard. Those who don't find aquatic scents refreshing in summer (like me), and who find citrus scents too quickly exhausting (like I do), should definitely give the Orange-Ô a chance.

Spring is just around the corner. Even if you can't really feel it (yet). However, if you look at the shrubs and trees, you can see it directly. Many of the leaf buds are already plump and waiting for their moment in ambush. Hazels and alders are already sending their first pollen into the land.
I can't even come up with anything original for this review. It's just arbitrary, nice, and thus completely unnecessary.

Yes, I purchased this Lancome fragrance two days ago, without knowing how poorly it had performed here. And that’s a good thing, because I really like this fresh, orangey, and slightly bitter scent, and I have to comment on it immediately, or I’ll burst.

Aaaahhh, the peels of citrus fruits. Sour, slightly bitter and zesty, in short simply great, as long as you don't have to eat them (baaah, then it's toooo bitter!). You surely know it when you peel oranges, mandarins, and similar fruits, that afterwards your fingers are yellowish and smell of the bitter peel.

...be mine...again and again. It rarely happens that I actually repurchase fragrances. Thanks to Incienso, Ô de l'Orangerie has made its way back into my perfume shelf...and is looking forward to summer with me, which hopefully will come?! Admittedly, this fragrance had it easy with me. The first time I quickly bought it as a light summer perfume and then off on vacation!

This is one of those perfumes that mix several popular scent profiles into one. In this case, it's the dark, syrupy sweet La Nuit Trésor DNA blended with a slightly Delina-esque fruity rose and an on-trend cherry note. So, it's not the most original scent, but I got to admit it smells extremely good to me. I love all those accords on their own, so why wouldn't I love a good olfactory remix of them? And it is nicely done. Juicy cherry and dewy, sweet rose floating on a sensual, deep vanilla base that keeps the scent from going sour. I definitely get some of the base notes from the original La Nuit Trésor, like caramel and patchouli, even though they're not listed. A big difference is that this doesn't have the smokey incense of the original. The newly added almond milk note is very subtle to my nose, I can't really separate it from the cherry. The "Intense" naming isn't very fitting here. I don't find this weak, but it's lighter and fresher than the original LNT, just not what one would expect from an Intense version. On the plus side that also means that this flanker is a little more versatile and less of an night time/winter only scent. Some find this similar to the discontinued La Nuit Trésor à la Folie, but I wouldn't recommend to get this as a replacement. The sour cherry and general bright fruity vibe make it quite different from the ultra-warm, ambery À la Folie. Sure, they're both from the same line, so they're not complete opposites, but I don't find them that close either. Each one is lovely in its own way. I wouldn't mind having both.

This flanker of the line la nuit tresor by lancome is a definite drift from the original perfume. Here the dark cherry and the almond milk are the stars in the opening and introduce us to the Isparta rose. For more details please watch my Youtube review linked here below. Hope you will find it helpful!

With the first spray, unaware of the fragrance pyramid, I am immediately struck by the scent of cherries. The opening is undoubtedly characterized by an intense, sparkling cherry note - somewhat dark, sweet, and very intense. As in many of the popular cherry fragrances, I perceive the cherry, especially black cherry, as syrupy. At that moment, I thought I had found a perfume made specifically for those who love cherry scents. But then, after about 15 minutes, something changes. A familiar note joins in, and I feel my nose wrinkle. The scent seems to age by the second and then mutates into an "old lady scent." I love roses as a fragrance note, but as often happens with rose, it can easily drift into that old-fashioned direction, and that’s exactly what happens here. It stays like this for about 2 hours. Towards the end, the rose becomes a bit less dominant and even reveals a hint of tuberose, which reminds me of N.R. For Her Musc Noir Rose. That’s a nuance I actually like. Unfortunately, this nuance is only the transition to the base. The lingering scent is vanillic, but not marked by almond milk, rather fruity. Somewhat boring and synthetic like a flavor in candy. All in all, my experience with La Nuit Trésor Intense is like a bumpy ride. This perfume seems unsure about which audience it wants to appeal to, and the various nuances are not harmoniously connected.

Where should I start.... Well, as some know, I am a big fan of La nuit Tresor, especially since this fragrance direction has always attracted me and spoken to me until now. Every flanker that has come to the market so far has been a unicorn for me, yes, love at first sniff! The original La nuit Tresor has been my signature scent for 4 years now, the fragrance that makes me the happiest but also amazes me every time I spray it or even just sniff the bottle!:)) Let's just say it's MY BABY;) When I found out that a new flanker from my favorite fragrance line was soon to hit the perfume market, I was, in any case, excited:D My grandfather was also eagerly anticipating the new La nuit Tresor fragrance with me:)) The scent notes sounded wonderful, almost too good! My grandfather and I ordered a sample of it, which unfortunately did not arrive, so we decided to drive to the perfumery instead, and we were lucky! As soon as we entered the perfumery, the delivery of the new La nuit arrived. I hopped and giggled like a child to the tester, and my grandfather just shook his head and said, "Just spray it already, then we'll know more:D" It felt so special to hold and admire the new bottle in my hand*.* I silently prayed that this one would blow me away but also immediately tempt me to buy it.... Now from here, I can say let's start with the scent description;) Let's get to the nice part;) The scent description!:D The scent... Starts with a very syrupy cherry note that dominates the entire scent progression on my skin. At first, I thought, well, let's see how it goes... However, my grandfather was already very disappointed with the scent progression from the start, but I didn't give up hope and prayed it would get better... Before I tested the scent, I thought it might go in the direction of La petite robe noir since the scent pyramid of La nuit is almost identical to La petite robe noir, but I didn't know how wrong I was... If some of you think it goes in the direction of TF Lost Cherry or Rouge Smoking by BDK, you are completely mistaken! Also, the word Intense is unfortunately more of a deception than reality... I was hoping for a much more intense and darker version of the original La nuit, but my disappointment was greater than my joy... Don't get me wrong, the scent itself is really beautiful BUT it is not what I had imagined.... My grandfather also had higher hopes since he loves La nuit just like I do, but he found every flanker from the La nuit line beautiful until now; only the Intense he found not as interesting in terms of scent progression as the previous La nuit flankers. After the cherry, a bitter almond note followed, which didn't seem very rounded to me. The almond became more intense and subtly aromatic over time. I was hoping for a creamy almond, but this almond note somehow has too much rose; I unfortunately can't smell it at all because I believe it could have saved the scent progression, but on my skin, it wasn't present for a second. I also smelled a note that kept bothering me, especially when I brought my nose closer to my wrist. Only I unfortunately don't know what that note is:(( The vanilla note that I know from the La nuit Tresor line/flanker I could smell on my skin the next day because it is so beautifully creamy and dark, but at least the vanilla could bring a comforting smile to my face the next day. For longevity and sillage, I can only say positive things, as with ALL La nuit Tresor fragrances EXTREMELY GOOD! On the skin, it is detectable until the next day, and on clothing (sillage) it is still perceptible for three days and longer. My conclusion: a beautiful scent, but you have to like syrupy cherry notes/fragrances! I am considering getting it, but since I haven't warmed up to the scent itself yet, I'm hesitating. What do you think?? Should I buy it even though it didn't blow me away, or should I let it go?

Although in November one tends to indulge in mandarins, one would certainly not reach for "Eau Mage" these days, nor would I have, had I not simply confused the bottle with that of "34, Boulevard Saint Germain"... well, this is how a long-overdue comment on this rather idiosyncratic "magical water" comes to be. :-) Created as one of three fragrances for the 50th anniversary of the company, Diptyque, in my opinion, did not delve too deeply into the trick box; the actual anniversary scent, which bears the name of the address of the headquarters, surpasses "Eau Mage" by far in terms of refinement. When I spray it on, I always think of opening a bottle of lemonade from "La Mourtacienne," which also comes in a mandarin flavor - and just as sticky-sweet is the first impression of "E.M." ...magical... well, E.M. then develops into a herbal-spicy scent, but the mandarin always remains present with residual acidity... similar to heartburn after the aforementioned lemonade.... However, whatever rose oxide may smell like.... hmmm.... Rusty roses are at the gate to the botanical garden.... but that is certainly not to be understood that way. Rosy notes unfortunately do not reveal themselves to me in the slightest. "Eau Mage" is a summer fragrance, subtly nice and unobtrusive. Those who find the blood orange of "Eau de Tarocco" too strong, and who enjoy slightly sweet citrus notes, will surely appreciate the mandarin of "Eau Mage." However, do not expect too much... it is certainly not Diptyque's best composition in this genre.

I was not impressed by how Tubéreuses Castane smells on the paper: a cloying, excessively creamy vanilla-tonka bean-tuberose trio, unabashedly gourmand and one-dimensional. However, the opening on my skin features a surprisingly vivid roasted chestnut accord. During the first half hour, I can smell a warm, smoky woodiness, recalling the shell of roasted chestnut without sounding the alarm of acrid woody amber aromachemicals, and an untuous nuttiness evoking the chestnut cream on a Mont Blanc dessert. Moreover, the green camphor of tuberose creeps silently around the edge like poisonous ivy. Combined with the nuttiness, it sometimes even veers towards bitter almond/cyanide, hinting at a potential danger beneath this alluring delicacy. Sadly, what I smell on as the fragrance dries down about 1 hour later, is the true face of Tubéreuses Castane on my skin. As the fragrance dries down, the nutty and woody smoky aspects disappear, and the greasy vanilla-tonka-tuberose trio takes over. There's no indole, nor green earthiness of tuberose to keep a natural sensation. Instead, the tuberose is more like a buttery, vague floral facet to complement the thick, creamy sweet vanilla. Tubéreuses Castane remains as such from then on, and it's not dissimilar to other gourmand tuberose such as Isabey Lys Noir and Tom Ford Orchid Soleil. The sillage is heavy to moderate during 3 hours, it then stays closer to skin. I got an 8-hour longevity. Iinteresting and evocative as its roasted chestnut accord in the opening may be, the generic dry down of Tubéreuses Castane is a let down for me. The lack of nuance and the heavy, sweet creaminess make it feel like a tedious drag on my skin. Nevertheless, Having said that, I think the opening is worth a try to those who are looking for a realistic nutty accord, and I suspect that Tubéreuses Castane might be more appealing to those who enjoy creamy gourmand fragrances, rather than to those who enjoy a more floral, natural tuberose.

Tubéreuses Castane is such a beautiful, fabulous fever dream of a cocktail... an elderflower-forward sparking sweet Riesling with a musky, caramelized chunk of amber floating in the wine, along with a luxuriant dollop of rich chestnut puree and a generous dash of spicy ginger liqueur. It's heady and hypnotic and a little weird but it's not too cerebral or precious about it and lordy be, it is a friggin glamazon. Hot dang y'all.

I wanted to live this and I should have! The notes all look great. This is as realistic a chestnut fragrance you’ll ever find. It’s definitely smells roasted. The issue is that’s all I could smell. The tuberose was completely downed out and there was nothing creamy or milky or floral about it. Maybe if I find a bottle for an amazing price, I’ll give it another try but all I could smell was very strong, very oily chestnuts.

Here, everything is roasted to the max! But are those chestnuts? Unfortunately, this cannot be filtered out upon first spray, rather burnt starch, roasted grains, charred sugar, malty nuances. However, this unpleasant note disappears after a few minutes, giving the stage to a completely atypical tuberose. Where this plant was previously known to me as a sweet-powdery tropical dream, it now continues in a floral-fresh and citrus-spring-like manner. The heaviness is completely absent, and yet the perfume is already very loud and noticeable at this stage! A slight twist towards nuttiness is also present after half an hour. It could continue like this, as the scent is beautifully composed up to this point... The fresh sourness gradually fades, and then a fallen-overripe fruit lingers in the background... Perhaps a (canned) PEAR??? A certain reluctance sets in for me, as this scent is quite demanding in its loud overpowering presence. After two hours, the presence softens somewhat, and I could swear that the pyramid has concealed a hint of sweet guaiac wood from us... What am I saying... No hint! But a whole truckload that simply refuses to go away. Even in the seventh hour, it is a monothematic guaiac radiance. All freshness or floral notes have disappeared. The scent is sweet-dull and very rigid in its projection and is now seriously getting on my nerves. And it takes until about seven hours for everything to become softer, creamier, and for the beautiful initial nuances to shine through again. A strange progression that naturally only reflects my own perception. Nevertheless, I consider the perfume to be well-made, noble, and very distinctive. Unfortunately, the scent did not resonate with my taste, as the three nuances 'Roasted', 'Fruit', and 'Guaiac' are simply not my thing. For fans of guaiac perfumes, such as Palo Santo, this may be an absolute recommendation to test. Conclusion: A rather dominant yet softly flattering perfume for a grand evening appearance, or - when dosed more discreetly - usable as an exquisite daytime scent. For ladies only! No words are needed for the brilliantly beautiful bottle with a magnetic cap and golden metal ornaments. One day it will be in a museum! Thank you, Miss Piggy, for the great sample! Unfortunately, it didn't work out for me to overcome my roasting material phobia!

The air is still, as if barely breathing, And yet rustling, near and far, The most beautiful fruits fall from every tree. O do not disturb them, the celebration of nature! This is the harvest that it holds itself, For today, only what falls from the branches Is what the mild rays of the sun touch. Christian Friedrich Hebbel Autumn! Autumn in a bottle - what could be better! Golden leaves, sunlight with that special hue, scent of last blooms and ripe fruit... The first spray of this fragrance brings to mind roasted chestnuts. Delightfully warm and nutty, deliciously sweet and floury - I immediately crave Purrée des Marrons! The tuberose is sweet as hoped, but not piercing or headache-inducing. Mild, sunny, like a midday in sunshine. Although a floral nuance, I have an idea of ripe fruit like mirabelles. The entire fragrance radiates gold-yellow, warming and caressing. The longevity is magnificent; after 4 hours I still feel well-perfumed on my skin. Even at about 30 cm away, delicious clouds rise from my arm and reach my nose. While the top note is already warming and radiant, the heart develops into something even more delightful. Roasted aromas, nuttiness, and creaminess create a comforting envelop of extraordinary roundness. Somewhere within is a tiny touch of "aquatic" hidden, just enough to cool the sweetness a bit. As the heart note fades, tonka appears, and nuttiness or roasted chestnuts come forth stronger. I perceive the entire progression as relatively evenly swinging between the creamy sweetness of tuberose and the more bitter nuttiness of chestnuts. Now and then, this unknown fruit shines through, refreshing the fragrance, which never slips into being sticky. For autumn, I am now well-equipped - I expressly give a sniff recommendation!

Hm, what does one do in a spring that doesn’t feel like spring at all, as it is once again icy cold, rainy, and in some parts of the country even snowy (or once was)? Quite simple: No, I’m not talking about drinking black tea, although…, yes, that too (but please without milk!

Well, - beautiful bottle - sometimes one feels compelled to buy a perfume just for its beautiful exterior, its presentation, so -, even if it sounds odd - "I buy blind because it apparently appeals to me" -. Now I was also inclined to do this here, until a sample included could take the decision away from me - !?

I was already used to warmer temperatures, and when it was icy cold in the mornings this week with a strong wind blowing, the sample came back into my hands... I love walking through the colorful leaves in autumn, enjoying the warm rays of the sun and the play of colors, collecting chestnuts.

I love chestnuts. The smell of freshly roasted chestnuts on Bahnhofstrasse in Zurich in December is heavenly. Therefore, this was a blind buy. And it smells exactly like that at first! No artificial vermicelli scent - no, smoky warm chestnuts meet tuberose. The combination of nutty, malty, and floral notes works surprisingly well.

Tuberose and I harmonize - that's nothing new. Tubereuses Castane practically embraced me on this rainy day. In the bottle it smells a bit old-fashioned, but once sprayed - oh my! It smells warm and spicy, a little sweet. The chestnut seems to come through quite subtly at first, but lingers. It has an autumn-winter vibe without directly shouting Christmas market.

First of all: I really don't like the regular version of LVEB at all. However, for some time now, I have noticed a version on the subway worn by other women that didn't have that stuffy note, but was simply fresh & sweet. After a few tests, I ended up with La vie est belle en rose and OH MY GOD, this scent is exactly what I was looking for. I have a date. I just want to smell feminine and not too overpowering: This scent is JUST right. I'm not a fan of vanilla. Other favorites of mine, like "Delina Exclusif | Parfums de Marly," can feel too heavy on certain days and in certain moods. The LVEB DNA makes the rose in the scent feel a bit outdated, but it makes me feel like an adult, modern woman when I wear it.

I admit that I am not immune to the effects of advertising. So I rushed to Opel after the cute Fred Flintstone commercial, where little Pebbles exclaimed Corsa! Corsa!, and bought myself this lovely little car. Two of my friends followed suit - and from then on we were a Corsa! Corsa! trio. And my American friend Sharon and I couldn't stop laughing when the Rama Girl in traditional clothing suddenly appeared out of nowhere, offering the tasty margarine to the breakfasting family. What is she doing? Where does she come from? --- I don’t know. I still eat butter. But advertising can also ruin a product for me. I always quickly switched channels when Ms. Roberts woodenly stomped through the Lancome ad - trying to convey to me that life is beautiful. So I also kept my distance from the fragrance she promoted for a long time - until I couldn't resist a special offer one day. And lo and behold - La vie est belle appealed to me - and I like it a lot. Several flankers joined in - and En Rose also speaks to me. It carries the genes of the original within it - but makes its own floral statement. The opening is fruity sweet - yet subtle. Peony and rose are freshly cut and also have green facets. Sandalwood hugs closely - and rounds off the harmonious scent. My husband has no objections to En Rose either - and soon it will be Christmas. Then Pretty Woman will surely be repeated for the umpteenth time - sorry - but not with me. I don’t need to put myself through that much Julia Roberts.

I really like this scent, it is not too heavy and not too sweet. The rose scent is very pleasing to me, it becomes slightly sweet later on, but not too overpowering. A very tolerable light fragrance that can also be worn in summer with 2/3 sprays. I noticed while showering that as soon as I wash it off, the scent becomes very sweet for a brief moment.

lasts on my skin for only about 2 hours and then - no trace. I have tested other EDTs that last significantly longer. Otherwise, a very nice scent, smells like sunshine and a rose garden. Perfect for a spring date =)

This scent is a circular skin scent on me. At first I smell a sweet tobacco, then vanilla, then tobacco, then vanilla. The dance continues until the base where they stand arm in arm exhausted and calm. The entire time I could smell both at the same time. Very well blended and beautiful, but did not last as long as I had hoped.

Oh no, no, no, NO! This fragrance had me cringing from the very first spray. Sure, Magnifique is unique, but perhaps Lancome took their new daring approach to making fragrances a little too far this time. I really expected Magnifique to smell magnificent; rich, elegant, powerful and almost regal. Honestly I don't find anything wonderful about smelling like a piece of burnt plastic and synthetic flowers. The alcohol is so strong in this fragrance, it almost wipes out the notes completely. I have smelt cheap drugstore deoderants that smell better than Magnifique. If you can manage to get past the overly strong opening notes without washing this scent off, the scent does improve slightly. Magnifique becomes a woodsy fragrance, yet I'd say it is more masculine smelling than feminine. I very rarely get headaches from fragrances, yet Magnifique has succeeded in giving me one. I think it's because of the strong caraway and vetiver notes. I don't know if I could ever recommend this fragrance, I'm rather glad I don't work behind a Lancome fragrance counter, otherwise I'd have to lie and don a false smile everytime someone bought this fragrance.

In 2011 I turned 40. I threw an informal party and invited a lot of good friends, colleagues and family, and I still remember this a great day with lots of love, laughter and music. Just the way I like it. One of my presents was Magnifique. I had not made a wishlist, so everyone was free to bring a gift or do whatever they wanted. It was a dear aunt that gave me this gem, knowing about my expensive and eccentric hobby. While handing the gift she said: “I asked the lady in the store to find something interesting. This is what she gave me and I would like to know what you think”. Already wearing a different perfume I told her, that I would give her my opinion within the next week. When spraying it the next day I knew I had found myself a long life companion. It starts out really crisp with an almost chalky sharpness and yet with a rosy note. The combination of saffron and flowers makes me think of berries - I do not know why but it is pretty fruity to my nose. Then Vetiver and sandalwood makes the fragrance a lot more spicy and this stays for many hours. I love the bottle. Simple in a beautiful colour. I love this design, which looks a lot like Oriflame’s Amber Elixir, only taller. Luca Turin rates it with two stars and writes “so two-years-ago”. I do not always agree with Mr. Turin. I am amazed that Lancôme have not made a series of flankers for this one, since I find it one of their best perfumes. I have not tried the edt, but according to the ratings the edt is way better than the edp, so I guess I shall try to get my hands on it. Unfortunately, I only have about 10-15cl left in my edp bottle. Sad but true. Oh, btw: I did call my aunt the next day. I told her exactly how I felt about the perfume : marvelous, wonderful… Magnifique. 149/365

This is a review from a 2008 formulation, not the newest formulation It opens with a strong saffron and a bit of powder (just a hint from the rose I think). There is a slight spice but not distinct enough to say for sure it's caraway. I actually think it may be the cypriol oil. I don't get any of the rye bread caraway scent, anyhow. There is definitely that synthetic thing going on that others have complained about but it's not too overpowering to ruin the scent for me. I wish there was a bit more warmth in this though. The opening has an unfinished feeling to it. Now we get to the magic of this one. The heart. I checked back in after an hour of application and I am getting a sweet rose. Very similar to the rose in Tresor, I can see why people compare the two. But unlike Tresor there is Saffron behind this rose cutting the sweetness and adding more depth to this composition and grounding the sweet rose. It's lovely. The warmth I wanted in the opening is here in the heart thanks to the saffron and spice (maybe caraway most likely the cypriol oil, but I still can't say for sure). The spice is subtle and soft, a very goldilocks amount. Not too much, not too little. Perfect. The synthetic thing is all gone now too. I'm checking in on the dry down nine hours after application. It's definitely a skin scent now but it's a beautiful soft sweet floral with a slight hint of sandalwood. There is also a memory of the saffron and spice that sits behind the sandalwood and rose. Yea. I love it. Nov 15 2014

Having never tried it in the stores when it was available, I became curious after viewing the notes and reviews so I bought a mini of Magnifique. You can imagine my surprise when found that this is actually an immortelle bomb with a fresh rosey almost verging on peony aspect to it. Saffron and caraway are easily discernable but the base is syrupy, caramelized, spiced, immortelle through and through with maybe just a touch of sandalwood. Up close it is all you can smell on the skin. Eight inches to two feet away the fresh rosey aspect which I would have identified as peony is very prominent with only a hint of the caramelly spiced based. Overall Magnifique has an interesting and unusual composition. The listed notes here made me think I might be in for an overtly Middle Eastern styled rose scent but that's not what I got at all. After smelling it for myself and identifying the immortelle note, the disparate reviews make sense to me now. I like Magnifique, but I don't know that I love it. The dichotomy of fresh floral and then sweet spicy then fresh spicy in one perfume while unique is a little unsettling. I can't think of anything that resembles this. Given that uniqueness I think this would make a remarkable signature scent for someone you loves it regardless of gender.

What i notice about Lancome perfumes that they have an distinct scent apart from other fragrances lancome has a sweetish light and woody texture notice Poeme Miracle Hypnose Tresore and Hypnose senses all have this sweet vanilla and woodsy scent that is sort of their trademark.

I received Magnifique by Lancome as a Mother's Day gift from my daughter in 2014. I tested it back then and liked it. My daughter was probably there too. In any case, she also tested it and found it good. It was very generous of her to save up so much money to make her mom happy. After all, it's not a bargain for a teenager.

Tonight, late in the evening, I was alerted by a rumbling and crashing. Thunderstorm? No, it suddenly struck me, it was the Night of Fireworks that I almost missed! I hurried into the garden, and there unfolded a spectacular display in the sky of sparkling, fiery cascades in all the colors of the rainbow.

Of course, after testing thousands of fragrances in the men's section, some recurring patterns in the perfume market have long since gotten on my nerves, as I have encountered them in all colors, shapes, types & qualities. But in the women's section, there are also trends that come around every few years, which you can't escape, that are annoying, that are overdone.

At the beginning, Magnifique greets me with a strong, slightly sharp cloud - the saffron makes its presence felt immediately, but is soon enveloped by rose and may rose, which warms it up. At this point, jasmine is not yet distinctly recognizable to me. That will not change in the course of the fragrance.

As someone who prefers scents that are more personal over the kind that announce themselves to the whole room -- Orphéon is perfection. Clean, powdery, and sophisticated, with a light, floral sweetness to it, but without leaning toward laundry, and with a woody base underneath. It's so well blended that it's difficult to think of an example of what this smells like. I've seen people describe it as really fancy soap and while i do get that, i also feel it doesnt quite do it justice. Airy, creamy, smooth, luxurious. Orphéon is soap the same way a thunderstorm is rain. Every time i break this out i wonder why i dont wear it more often. I havent smelled the edp version so i cant speak to how they compare, but from what i gather the solid leans slightly more woody/powdery, but less spicy, and as expected the longevity and sillage is lower, but i personally find that to be a plus rather than an issue. It becomes a more subtle scent, more for yourself than anything else, but still lingers nicely on skin and clothes. Lasts the whole day without issue, and i usually catch a whiff of this on my shirt the day after. The compact itself is stunning and surprisingly heavy. It, and the refills, cost a fraction of what a full bottle would so it's nice that the packaging is still good quality and made to last. All in all a budget friendly, and more than worth the price, option.

I first purchased the solid version of Orphéon as a more affordable way to experience the fragrance, and it didn’t disappoint. While it shares the same essence as the 75ml bottle, the solid perfume has its own nuances. To me, it feels softer, more powdery, and less spicy than the liquid juice. The projection is quite minimal, making it an intimate option—perfect for layering or a subtle, close-to-skin scent. It complements the 75ml bottle beautifully and serves as an excellent introduction to the fragrance without the full price commitment. Whether as a standalone product or a pairing with the bottle, the solid perfume is a versatile and budget-friendly way to enjoy the world of Orphéon.

Rose Extraordinaire is a very rose forward flanker to the La Vie est Belle line. It stays true to the orginal's heart, while remaining slightly airier and fresher. It doesn't dig quite as deep, nor does it linger in the same gourmand territory. The opening is a rush of sweetness - indulgent - exactly the way fans hope it will be. Sugar gleams for a moment, before softening, settling into its floral nest. The rose has different facets. There's clear rosewater, which paired with iris lends a clean freshness. Then there's a more processed rose: beautiful candied petals, sugar frosted around the edges - the way you might imagine them in a luxurious winter ad or delicately perched on top of fancy pastries and cakes. Rose Extraordinaire lasts for hours, but when it starts to fade, the rose is the first to disappear. I used to love L'Elixir even more after sampling it in the summer of 2024. But when I bought a travel size in spring 2025 it felt like a different fragrance altogether. Revisiting both has shifted my perspective. Rose Extraordinaire is now, without hesitation, my favorite flanker.

A spritz of this new creation unexpectedly transports me back to my childhood, which was quite some time ago. Once a week, my mother would put my little sister in the stroller and take my hand. We would walk to a drugstore that was in the neighborhood of our previous apartment, but the longer route was worth it, my mother knew, and I knew. In 1970, we still didn't have drugstore chains like we know them today. The shop was smaller, and the interior was entirely made of dark wood, with shelves and many counters. There was no self-service; every product had to be announced, and it would then be placed in the shopping basket, with advice available upon request. On one of those counters stood a large glass jar full of sparkling treats, tiny fruit candies wrapped in cellophane. And with each visit, I would receive one of those: delicious blackcurrant would fill my mouth in this environment that smelled of rose soap, cream, and baby food. This association fills me as soon as I spray LVEB Rose Extraordinaire. At first, I think of an Eau de Cologne, with no high fragrance concentration, a bit of refreshing bergamot that also brings warmth. The blackcurrant takes a little time to develop, then it suddenly appears, dominating the scene, and then a creamy base unfolds, a face cream with a light, transparent rose scent, that’s my impression. Slowly, a bit of lipstick, some wood, and a touch of smoke mix in, and I am reminded of summer in the Veneto, when you drive through the countryside where the air smells of sugar beet processing, furniture factories, and burnt garden waste. The iris gradually reveals itself, and the consistency changes from cream to powder. But there is nothing sultry like in an actress's boudoir; I rather see the well-groomed housewife waiting for her husband in a tidy home after his workday. The fragrance doesn't undergo much more development on me. It stays in this blend close to my skin for hours, only then does the musk dare to come forward a bit. After five or six hours, I would like to re-spray. However, a base remains on the skin that I can still perceive even after twelve hours. So I wake up in the morning still smelling sensually well-groomed. The scent has a very mutated LVEB DNA; it has retreated into the private sphere. It is not a statement for a grand appearance, but rather my little secret to feel comfortable. It is the evolution from LA vie est belle to MA vie est belle, so to speak.

One strolls through the Vienna Prater on a summer day, buys a pink cotton candy, and then continues to wander through the people and all the colorful surroundings. Afterwards, one sits on a bench in the green and cooler shade, flirts a little, and enjoys. This is roughly how my associations with this fragrance go. The top note has a bit too much cotton candy sweetness, then comes rose, and later musk. The latter two have absolute classic potential and a lot of everyday wearability. In principle, the fragrance can be worn regardless of the situation and at any time of year, however, it doesn't fare well in high summer temperatures, as the sweet cotton candy becomes a bit too overpowering. All in all, a good rose fragrance, but the sugary sweet top note is strongly dependent on personal taste. For those who enjoy this, the perfume is a good choice.

I have been eagerly awaiting this new flanker. Now it has been mine for a few days, and I have thoroughly tested it and - fallen in love! First of all - I spontaneously gave it a 9 for the scent. I am raising it to 10. It will surely be my most worn fragrance in the coming months. It is my favorite LVEB version! It sits between La Vie est Belle en Rose and La Vie est Belle Intensément . It is more "binding" than La Vie est Belle en Rose . It is less present and much more pleasing than La Vie est Belle Intensément . On the other hand, La Vie est Belle L'Eau de Parfum is significantly more praline-like, edgier, and "special" than this one. Here is its progression: It opens very fresh, slightly green, but above all modern-rosy. This lasts on my skin for about 20 minutes. Then the typical LVEB DNA comes through, but much less praline-like, for about 1 hour. The rose remains. After that, a wonderful, soft, sweet-cloudy, slightly herbaceous (raspberry?) musk fluff lingers. This fluff lasts on me for up to 10 hours, but increasingly close to the skin. The rose lasts about 5 hours. After that, I definitely get some Nivea vibes. Occasionally, a very subtle smoky note comes to my nose. But really just very subtly... Overall, it has moderate sillage. This lasts for about 2 hours, after which you have to get VERY close to really smell it. I find that totally pleasant because I want to smell like myself, but not overwhelm others. But I do want to be noticed a little. :) Perfect for me! What remains after 5 hours can be beautifully layered if you want something different for the evening - or you can reapply, because this scent always works! It works for any season, although I believe I will reach for "cozier, spicier" scents (e.g. Sì (2023) Eau de Parfum Intense ) in the fall. Even on really hot days, I can imagine reaching for something else, we'll see. I would like to a. promote it everywhere so that it stays in the lineup for a long time, but at the same time b. actually just keep it for myself! I have a strong suspicion that this will be my signature scent and I look forward to the opinions that will gather here in the near future. I have already layered or sprayed it side by side (upper arm/lower arm) with White Tea Eau de Parfum - I find that a great combo, a bit fresher than just alone. I also found Signature Eau de Parfum at another body spot to be a great complement, but I will probably test that again in the fall, as it feels too "cozy" for now. La vie est belle, douce, florale, joyeuse - et légèrement plaisante! --------> Enjoy it, my dears. PS. I find the bottle of the OG okay, but boring. I like this one much more!

If you are into intense, spicy, and oriental aromas, you should definitely try "Santal Kardamon | Lancôme." I also find this scent to be quite unisex. The longevity on my skin is impressively strong at around 24 hours, and the sillage is convincing as well. The top note starts off exceptionally spicy and oriental with aromas of cardamom, nutmeg, allspice, pepper, and saffron. There is also a hint of something menthol-like. The heart note offers a strong leatheriness. The base has a sweet, woody, resinous, creamy, and balsamic scent of sandalwood, Bourbon vanilla, amber, cedarwood, and benzoin. I find Santal Kardamon at least intriguing and quite successful. Does this fragrance DNA suit me? Probably not. Nevertheless, I thank Tina for this interesting sample.

A year after I started my training as a healthcare and nursing assistant, my hospital launched a new training course where trainees from various cultures came together. There were also some refugees from Syria, Afghanistan, and other countries. Around Christmas time, there was a joint project. All the trainees were to organize a Christmas party together. It was meant to be an opportunity for mutual exchange, to get to know other cultures and their ways of celebrating. Everyone brought specialties and music from their culture. The new trainees brought pastries with rose water, couscous and rice dishes with various spices, and date cookies. And among all the new treats for me, the cardamom coffee has probably stuck in my memory the most. Beautifully strong coffee, brewed with whole cardamom pods. The gentle spice blends with the aroma of the coffee. A warming, rich, and intense drink. That day, I learned to appreciate a lot of new things, especially the scent of cardamom (which incidentally led me to purchase "Cardamom Coffee (Perfume) | Lush / Cosmetics To Go." Unfortunately, not such a pleasant experience). Santal Kardamom fits perfectly into my preferences. And yes, the scent smells heavenly of gentle sandalwood and spicy-warm cardamom. It does not veer into the soapy, piercing, or sharp territory, as can sometimes be the case. I perceive a very gentle, spicy warmth that envelops me and brings something cozy to the cold February. I can only perceive the pepper very subtly, and the mandarin not at all. But they are not necessary to achieve a beautiful, rounded scent. However, one thing is missing for me in the fragrance. It simply does not have the intensity and depth of the coffee I once had the chance to try. Santal Kardamom is more of a gentle spice cloud, a quiet companion. I personally would have wished for a bit more "oomph," more strength and depth. It is still beautiful, though.

Noble sandalwood fragrance with a very warm aura, worn like a cozy wool jacket on cool days. Oriental spice meets delicate woodiness, creating a true wow effect. A little bit of orange-glowing citrus notes, a hint of pepper also evokes an exotic market just like cardamom. Or even spiced pastries. And a magical forest, where sunlight diffuses through the canopy and paints swirls of light and shadow on the ground. All in all, wonderfully "noble-chill" with an almost psychedelic lullaby effect. One can and should embrace this when hustle and bustle threaten to fray one's nerves, in order to approach things with calm again, no matter how others rush around (it brings much better results in "creating") Or simply to unwind in the evening after a tiring day with dreary weather.

Santal Cardamom. So a scent that apparently could somehow smell like sandalwood and cardamom. Wait, did I just say cardamom or kardamon?? What is the correct term actually? Well, why are you asking me? First of all, I’m a total foreigner here, and secondly, I’m not exactly a language genius.
