The aquatic mineral note lasts forever on clothes, and the performance is about whats expected for a fragrance in this category. This is ideal for those looking for an aquatic thats different from the usual and a real delight to wear. Everyone is entitled to their opinion, but I don't know how anyone could think this smells bad. It is just such a pleasant orange aquatic that is different enough to be noticed and appreciated. I love it. I have a decent, but not huge collection, but I've been thinking/reaching for this one the most since I got it. I will be buying a bigger bottle, and maybe a backup as well. I also look forward to wearing this in the cooler months, I think the scent is versatile enough for it. . .

Guys and gals, I totally get the rotten eggs analogy; and for a long time, I was in the same boat. Everyone raves about the performance of this sucker, but it's probably because this is a neroli incense BOMB. BITTER orange? Ahhhhh YEAH - because of the patchouli and incense. And for some reason, my skin don't do incense. Nuh-uh. It turns sour and can easily remind me of rotten eggs. But there's more... You know that trademark Aqva backbone? It's in here, and with the neroli, it makes this stuff grown up and sexy. The incense just provides some spiciness in the sillage. Just make sure not to get in too close - that was my biggest mistake - it's not one of those scents. It's more of an outdoor beast when you need the performance. The scent itself is simple. It goes from an authentic dark mandarin incense, into a neroli incense - and goes on and on and on. I'll say this - it smells of quality and kudos to Bvlgari for making a fragrance that is absolutely true to its notes. Jeremy's description of this is the "brutal strength of the ocean", but I think a more apt depiction would be the emotions he expresses when making that statement. Notice the grimace and the unmistakable urge to punch something. That's it. Why? Because it's how Amara makes you feel. That initial blast of incense can be off-putting, putrid and can make one act out violently. Hahaha. But believe me, it's MUCH BETTER at a distance - intriguing, unique and even alluring. Give it a few wearings and you'll see what I mean. Cheers.

If you know me well enough or happen you read any of my reviews, you know that I don't believe the hype and instead test and review any scents by myself. Amara is the best Aqva spin-off I've ever got, I didn't expect to love it, but I do. After liking and wearing the original Aqva pour Homme, which in my opinion was one of the best marine and aqueous scent out there, I got a bit harassed by Aqva pour Homme Marine. I have fallen in love initially, but then since there were too much synthetic seaweed, marine grass, and salty things in there, and purposely did buy neither the two Toniq flankers nor the most recent Atlantique. It is not that bad per se yet too much closely akin to Dior Sauvage that I've got in many shapes and dupes, no need for another one in my wardrobe. But Aqva Amara is a different story. It is a must-have summer fragrance, a nice one with no more seaweed, yet sourer and interestingly flavored. The master perfumer Jacques Cavallier did a great job here, and I like the way it has been conceived, it doesn't feel like an ordinary aquatic at all. Quite weird to say, Aqva Amara has been stored in my closet for more than three years now, it miserably never took part in the summer rotation, but this year it deserved it. Hence, this morning I woke up feeling like wearing it, and here you're my first impression. Allegedly made with just five main notes, namely tangerine, neroli, water accord, incense, and patchouli, the initial burst is made of bright and salty citrus, Aqva Amara, or Bitter Water, is the proper name of it. It is full and fresh citrus peels with a light neroli and a hint of patchouli from the base, which creates that pleasant minty vibe. It's notably pleasing at least to my nose and smells like an orange sprinkled with salt. Very powerful, with somewhat of an ocean and salty, watery accord, but it is not aquatic. I'd say more like fresh saltwater drenched in citrus and white sands vibe. Marvelous and vigorous. The heart is all about orange blossom, or neroli, with a musty, salty mineral note, so wet and ozonic without being too aquatic. The neroli note here is bitter, slightly green, and not as sweet as in other scents with a dominant indolic white flower tone. The synthetic molecules meant to reproduce the watery accord create an evanescent coolness akin to spring water in summer. On the dry-down, I do get hints of the typical seaweed accord as in the original Bvlgari Aqva, yet not dominant, mixed with smoky frankincense and modern patchouli. But the great thing about this fragrance is that the tart orange note lasts throughout the whole life of the scent, and the olibanum in the base balances the oceanic citrus exceptionally well. When it comes to performance, the sillage is stable, while longevity is above average, about over 8 hours. The durability far exceeds the original Aqva and is one of the strongest for a citrus-based cologne. Overall this is a beautiful iteration of the orange and neroli note, mixed with an aquatic ambiance that is rare, try to imagine Terre d'Hermés in its watery shape, Eau d'Hermés with wet seawater in place of mineral pepper. A unique summer gem, in my opinion. The strength of the ocean. I'd dare to say it's currently one of the best summer fragrances for men. Long-Lasting, compliment getter, unique smelling, and is best suited for mega high heat daytime casual, as well as office wear. -Elysium

This is a really nice one. A creation by the master perfumer Jacques Cavallier, this one is great. I do love the way it has been done. Done in such a way that it doesn't feel like a typical aquatic. With bitter orange, patchouli and possibly some cardamom and herbs, this is a good one. I would happily wear it. It reminds me of the beach and sea, and warm skin. I think it's a masterful fragrance, and really clever for it's genre. With another perfumer this could've been a very generic scent, but with Jacques Cavallier it became something unique and intriguing. I think this is definitely one to try for summer nights and hot, beach vacations. Really well done and it surprised me in a good way.

Well, another excellent perfume that has inexplicably become discontinued. Its output is very sharp, with a predominant bitter orange, which little by little softens and mixes with aquatic and, above all, floral notes, which once dry gives a fresh and clean sensation that is maintained until the end. A daytime perfume, ideal for spring/summer, different from what most wear. Its duration and sillage are remarkable, above average for this type of "fresh" perfume. I read here that it has a similarity to Terre D'Hermes, and the truth is that at the start they do have a certain similarity (especially due to the bitter orange), but after a while they go their separate ways. For me a very good option

Somewhat polarizing this one. I love it, but I totally understand if you don’t. I also enjoy Terre d’hermes with its bitter/tart orange. This one is sharing that feel, yet still an aquatic feel to it. Also there are some floral notes in the heart of this one. I get about 7-8h longevity with 3 solid hours of projection. Not bad for a summer frag!

this is simply awful ,aquatic rotten eggs in a bottle ,don't waste your money on this ,i didnt think it should b possible to make something most terrible than the prior aqva that i simply neglected but indeed they succeded to give an even more awful rendition

This was a love at first sniff for me. Aqva Amara - translates to bitter water. The first thing that caught my attention was the bottle it is stunning the golden/bronzy colour how it looks like a pebble or drop of water just drew me in even now every time im trying to decide what to wear it catches my eye and always i must smell it and marvel at this glorious creation.

"The Strength of the ocean" the best nick name that i have for this fragrance, that salty air when u go to the beach, that warm, sand smell, acquatic vibe, all in a bottle Acqua amara is the best in bvlgari acqua line The performance is very good 8h+, sillage sometimes 4-5h woooow! A must have fragrance for summer hot days!

This has to be one of the top summer/warm weather fragrances there is. An absolute masterpiece. This fragrance just makes me feel so refreshed and it is a compliment getter for sure Uniqueness: 10/10 Longevity: 9/10 Sillage: 9/10 Versatility: 10/10 Presentation: 8/10 Overall: 10/10

Out of all the LNT flankers I have tried, Dentelle de Roses is one of the closest to the original EDP. It has a lot of the same notes and accords, even though not all of them are listed. Beautiful raspberry infused rose, a sweet base of vanilla and patch are what I smell in both. I even get a hint of the smokiness of the EDP here, but it's toned down. The same goes for the fruity notes. In this one I really only get a berry note, which is intertwined with the rose, no lychee and other fruits like in the original. The overall feel of the scent is a little drier, less syrupy. I find it a little gimmicky that they added velvet to the notes list, as the fabric doesn't really have a distinct scent per se, but I can see why it's there. It describes the character of the scent quite well. Maybe they should have listed suede instead, that would more sense to my nose. While the original is very much like a nighttime only party scent to me, this feels a little more versatile and grown-up. Even though it's still extremely appropriate for a night out, I can also imagine it in other situations. Generally I would say it's clearly more of a winter fragrance, but I have also once sampled it on a hot summer day and found it surprisingly enjoyable with one light spray on my arm.

Some of you might have noticed how much I wanted this fragrance :D But some of you also know that I collect the La Nuit Tresor flankers, and not because of the bottle but because of the scent itself! The fragrances from the La Nuit Tresor line simply smell good! Especially the original La Nuit is my favorite!*.* When I saw here on Parfumo that a new treasure from the Tresor family was about to hit the market, I was immediately excited :DD I jumped up (and no, I'm not lying) and started screaming with joy... My mother and my grandfather almost had a heart attack that day because of me... Oops... BUT well, both are still alive ;D I knew right away that I HAD to have this fragrance NO MATTER WHAT! Especially since it is also a Limited Edition... And yes, I was also ready to buy the new La Nuit blind! The bottle also appealed to me a lot as it symbolizes femininity and sensuality at the same time ;)) When I finally saw that it was also available in Switzerland, I ordered it without any second thoughts. And I haven't regretted it for a second! ;)) When my package arrived, I was as happy as a child :D I opened it, and I was already enchanted by the design of the box; this beautiful lace pattern was simply dreamy!*.* And the bottle with the lace pattern on it is a work of art for the eyes! I gave two generous spritzes on my wrist and was IN LOVE! (Just as expected) I know many of you are now curious about the scent description :)) Rightly so! ;)) So let's start with the best part :D The scent... starts with a refreshing berry note; the raspberry note is neither sour nor too sweet/synthetic! Much more pleasant, yes sweet but not too sweet, rather juicy sweet. The raspberry note dominates lightly on my skin over time, but it is still noticeable as it is perfectly woven with the other fragrance notes :)) The finest part is the heart note!*.* I was personally just amazed! Because it smelled sooo good of caramelized rose petals paired with a creamy and light cream note... I could just lie in it because it smells soooo wonderful! The rose petals are so feminine and sensual at the same time, laid in the finest subtle smoky dark caramel liquid.... On top of that, there is a fine but very light cream note *.* For me, it smells like a mix of La Nuit Tresor Caresse and a la folie. The Caresse is wonderfully berry and creamy while the a la folie has this fine creamy note that comes from the vanilla. Many find that the original La Nuit is very smoky and heavy... Understandably, as the incense note is very present in the scent progression, but here with La Nuit Tresor Dentelle de Roses, that is not the case! Sure, it has a subtle incense note, but it is never as intense as the original! With Dentelle de Roses, as the name suggests, the rose note is in the foreground BUT there is no soapy or even synthetic rose... It is the finest rose note I have ever smelled, as it has been caramelized so finely and also offers this interesting dark note subtly. This scent is also creamy (especially on my skin) due to the hidden cream note :)) In my opinion, this scent is a perfect Valentine's Day gift for newly in love couples, of course, referring to the lady ;)) It smells very feminine and sensual; this scent is also sexy ;)) For the man, it is a little seduction and joy at the same time ;)) Which man wouldn't want his partner to smell good and seduce him at the same time? ;)) The sillage is EXTREME like with the other Tresor scents! Especially on clothing :) Not to forget the opinions of my mother and grandfather ;)) Mom: Smells beautiful and pleasant to her. Doesn't overwhelm but leaves a fine scent trail behind the wearer ;)) For her, as a rose scent lover, it is a must in every rose perfume collection ;)) Grandfather: Loves all La Nuit Tresor flankers and this one too, as he perceives it as very feminine and seductive :)) He thinks this scent is perfect for a chic night out with a loved one, paired with a long black elegant dress, smoky eyes, and cherry red lips ;)) Yes, my grandfather knows a thing or two about cosmetics thanks to my grandmother :D What is your opinion???? :))) I hope you found my description good :)

.. in a beautiful bottle. As the owner of several treasures, I absolutely had to try the latest flanker. The scent notes sounded promising, especially the raspberry syrup, which captivated me, and the velvet made me even more curious, so I couldn't resist testing it :) Right after spraying, I notice a wonderful, juicy mandarin that makes my mouth water. The rose stays more in the background for me. Just a short time later, the raspberry flashes through, making the scent very fruity. It reminds me a lot of raspberry jam, which I find incredibly wonderful and delicious. After a while, I perceive a note that really reminds me of velvet and somehow makes the scent feel "soft" and "creamy." The beginning might be a bit too sharp for some, but after a while, the scent develops incredibly softly on the skin, which makes it so unbelievably seductive and sexy. With this fragrance, I feel so comfortable and not overwhelmed. The smokiness from the original La Nuit Trésor has been toned down a bit here, making the scent absolutely suitable for summer. But here too, less is more. The scent lasts a long time in the hair and on clothing, while on my skin, it has a moderate longevity. The sillage is also in the higher range, but it doesn't overwhelm anyone. Once again, a successful flanker and an absolute must for the La Nuit Trésor collection :)

Actually, I don't like gourmands. Well, at least I thought so. They usually smell great and delicious - like a dessert. But do I really want to smell like that? Recently, my answer to that has been: YES!!! And in this case, it’s raspberries... and what raspberries! At first, something in the top note bothers me; I initially suspected a pear (which isn’t officially listed). Maybe it’s the mandarin. I have no idea, something is tickling my nose... and annoying me - or maybe not? Irritated, I wait it out - and then it becomes really delicious! I perceive the raspberry very naturally. I make myself a muesli every morning and it usually includes berries! Raspberries, blackberries, strawberries (I love berries). And because I can be a bit lazy sometimes, the muesli bowl just sits around for a few minutes (or hours)... and smells berry-like. Just like the perfume! Is my muesli lying around here somewhere?! Sweet is the scent in my opinion, definitely a bit sticky (as berries are), but surprisingly, I don’t find it unpleasant. Furthermore, the sweetness is somewhat muted, I mean by patchouli or vetiver; definitely by something herbal. I can’t perceive a great scent development; however, the scent loses some sweetness over time (but it still remains sweet enough!). Sillage is strong, a few sprays and the whole household benefits from it. And the longevity... folks... well, I have a sensitive nose, but SERIOUSLY?? I still perceived the scent up close after a whopping 36 hours! Now I’m in a dilemma...

As the owner of the complete La Nuit Tresor line except for Nude, I was really looking forward to this fragrance. Raspberry, velvet, rose? Sounds exciting. I ordered it immediately upon release. The scent: The top note is super raspberry. There’s a slight sharpness in the background, not as bad as in Midnight Tresor, but not as soft as A La Folie. But it’s definitely raspberry. As the scent develops, the sharpness fades away, leaving a strong raspberry compote. And that’s it. The fragrance is a blend of the fruitiness of the original, the softness of A La Folie (without the famous vanilla), and the raspberry scent of Midnight Tresor. Conclusion. Do you need it? Maybe not. If you’re looking for a seductive, raspberry fragrance for the night that is mature, then it’s a good choice, if not the best in my opinion. Lancome can create fruity scents like no other, and this one is proof of that. If you’re a collector, this one should not be missing. However, you must keep in mind that it’s just a mix of the three and therefore nothing innovative. If you have a thousand raspberry fragrances, you might want to think twice. It is, as mentioned, “ONLY” a simple raspberry scent for the night. I find it well made again, but there’s no applause; it’s just very simple and not interesting, yet it is incredibly delicious. I find Midnight Tresor much more interesting. 7/10

The most beautiful scent I have found after months of testing new releases. If only it would last a little longer... Love, softness, sweetness, a smile, and a sparkle in my eyes were bestowed upon me by this fragrance after the first spray. And a lighter wallet. Fruity, sweet, juicy, gourmand with the rose at the center. You can almost taste this scent when you smell it.

I know the original La Nuit Tresor. My mother received it as a birthday gift. And as a little perfume addict, I of course didn't have to ask long before my beloved mom, who knows my addiction all too well, sprayed 3 generous spritzes on my arm... To not digress too much, Tresor really smells good if you like this type.

I am a fan of the La Nuit Trésor line. That’s why I had to test the latest flanker, Dentelle de Roses, of course. Dentelle de Roses definitely has the same fragrance DNA as the original La Nuit Trésor, but in my opinion, it differs enough from all the perfumes in the line that it’s worth purchasing Dentelle de Roses.

I perceive this scent as a distinctly gourmand perfume that unfolds on my skin like a warm, velvety, and rather heavy fragrance cloud. The composition feels enveloping and soft, yet so intense that I almost feel like I can hardly breathe while wearing it.

There seem to be tons of incense perfumes by now. I have the Comme des Garçons Incense series, which covers a lot of dry incense ground. Annick Goutal ENCENS FLAMBOYANT offers a new twist on incense: dampness. Never has a perfume reminded me more of the scent of the inside of a medieval cathedral after a rain. So, yes, I'd call this a novelty scent. Do I want to smell like the inside of a medieval Catholic church all damp and musty, like cold concrete and stone mingling with purple smoke? Not really, to be honest. Perhaps ENCENS FLAMBOYANT would work better for the gents, although I wonder whether it might morph into some sort of body odor scent. Probably depends on the guy. Try before you buy. In any case, I enjoyed the memories elicited by this perfume, of my trips around small towns in France where I invariably dropped in for a visit to the local church or cathedral and often smelled something like this scent lingering in the air. It's odd, I suppose, that an agnostic should enjoy visiting the cathedrals of France. I also like cemeteries and catacombs, perhaps for the same reason.

Encens Flamboyant is supposed to be the most incensey fragrance in the series, however I'm not feeling it. This fragrance is much more subtle than Myrrhe Ardente and Ambre Fetiche. Despite its lack of incensey goodness, this fragrance makes up for it with its unique blend of pepper, woods and smoke. I totally get the 'Christmassy' feel that some reviewers have pointed out. The combination of spice and fir, is like scent recognition for me, it's Christmas in December all over again with every sniff. In some ways, Encens Flamboyant is musty, but not in a bad way. Its mustiness is what adds to its mystery, like an old, forgotten room, locked up for decades. Encens Flamboyant often strikes me as being an aromatic, as I sometimes find myself dazing off into space when I casually smell it every now and then. Although I do find this fragrance unisex, I'm more likely to recommend this fragrance to men more than women, however I haven't managed to pin-point what makes this fragrance more masculine than feminine to my nose. Being mostly dry, yet occasionally musty and damp, Encens Flamboyant is a very unique fragrance indeed. It is certainly worth checking out, even if you don't think it would be your type of scent. These Les Orientalistes fragrances are masterpieces that will hopefully be sold for many years to come.

An incense perfume, with a thick and peppery opening. Somehow I expected it to be sweeter. Not so. This is a lovely brooding incense with fir, cardamom and -o bliss !!- a sweet hint of red berries. For once I am happy a scent -which I really love- is not at all heavy in sillage (be sure: I sprayed and sprayed again). It probably would have been too much if it were. Being as mild in sillage as it is, I find it absolutely delicious and bewitching at the same time. A combination of two adjectives quite applicable in general to Les 4 Orientalistes.

This one is very nice. An incense which has a lot of "forest" type notes. I can pick up birch wood and fir balsam and a host of other notes. This really reminds me of the very good incense perfumes I've smelled before. I really enjoy it. I have enjoyed many of the perfumes in the Les Oreintalistes series from Annick Goutal. This one is no exception. Recommended for lovers of incense fragrances.

Wednesday. Bath day. I remember that in my childhood - after a ultimately unsuccessful, albeit heated discussion with my mother about the necessity of basic personal hygiene - it always brought me great pleasure to generously distribute the viscous contents of a bottle of "Pine Needle" bath foam into the slowly filling tub. This was the essence of bath-time fun. Once the container, not unlike those of today's fabric softeners, had been emptied to a certain extent, it was time to linger a bit in the dark green emulsion and wait for three handbreadths of foam to settle. Afterwards, I would attentively watch as the tub's contents gurgled away down the drain. The inevitable question of whether I had washed myself properly everywhere was answered with eager nodding while wrapped in a thick terry towel. The scent of the bubble bath lingered in the bathroom the next morning. Green, shifting, slightly balsamic. This foundational tone is also present in Encens Flamboyant. I mean this in an absolutely favorable way. I perceive the opening of the fragrance as pleasantly unexcited. A bright smoky note, at best identifiable in nuances as incense, is restrainedly sacred, slightly earthy, and socially compatible. Following this, the aroma of fresh pine needles subtly overlays, providing a pleasant, intimate experience. Shimmering green nuances alternate with the bouquet of fine, brittle wood. After a while, a gentle, balsamic base note remains, lingering and discreet. Encens Flamboyant exudes a restrained, calming aura and conveys a sense of security. Whether in the morning when spraying it on, or later in the office. A fine companion.
Can you see how heavy the snow rests on the branches of the fir trees? They bend under its sparkling weight, and the night air is fragrant with the harsh frost that is yet to come.

Substances for expanding consciousness open up many strange associative spaces. Wildly surging waves of ecstatically dancing hippies, rolling in the mud of Woodstock, embracing trees, people, and sounds, as disciples of Albert Hofmann encounter themselves in self-dissolution in the light of orgiastic music, staggering in the fog of perception.

Now I have you in my hands, a fine cylindrical bottle. I open you, smell you, and relaxation washes over me. After a trial, I needed some time to understand you; it was not love at first sight. I had expectations of you, opulent, sacred.

Recently, I received a few new samples that I've been carrying around in my bag for days. Always hoping that an opportunity to test them would arise during the day at the office. Unfortunately, that wasn't the case; on days with meetings, I avoid strong scents or testing unknown samples. And every day was something different.

Annick Goutal's fragrances never cease to fascinate me; also because they tell stories. Sometimes, indeed, because they tell me my very personal stories. I got to know "Encens Flamboyant" because FvSpee pointed it out to me after my comment on "Ambre Fétiche." A heartfelt thank you for that!

I have several Tygar clones and a small sample of the actual fragrance but decided today to pull the trigger and get a full bottle (discounted). Of course this is a fantastic "FANTASTIC" fragrance. It's a warm, spicy, fruity, aromatic fragrance, with notes that are sweet and sharp. It’s a balanced fragrance that gives you earthy and bright. The note breakdown emphasizes grapefruit in the opening and while I got that, I pick up ginger immediately and it’s what carries it into a wonderful dry down that is very ambroxan forward. The transition is smooth as is the fragrance overall. It’s said to have vetiver in the base but if it’s there it missed my nose, but I really didn’t missy it. This did fine for me without that note. This stuff lasts a long time and its projection while not room filling is very “in the house”. Having said all of this and I love this fragrance, here comes the "but" pay the full retail price can’t be justified because there are so many excellent clones that come so close that only an expert could tell it’s not the actual Bvlgari fragrance. So, paying 4 bills when the same aura and aroma can be gotten for a fraction of that just smells bad lol.

Tygar is good, but it’s boring, and overpriced After having tried the below perfumes, it just feels crude and uninspired compared to them Given how much more expensive it is, there is no reason for me to even consider it Aqua de Dora is a straight, significant upgrade in terms of scent, creativity, complexity, performance and price Ingenious Ginger smells a LOT better, and is much more interesting. Performance isn’t a whole lot worse, and it’s half the price Forever Love (Pana Dora) doesn’t smell hugely similar, but Tygar reminds me of FL if they forgot to add half the ingredients Roja citrus perfumes aren’t very similar either But I found Burlington 1819 and Isola Blu all WAY more pleasant scents, made at higher quality and with more interesting dna 8/10 - a good perfume but simply not as good as competitors

It smells (very) pleasing, the best way i could describe this perfume is a: Fresh & candied orange with a very high concentration of Ambrox of very good quality and small dose of woods. I like to wear it when it's sunny but not too hot outside (as the ambroxan can be a little overwhelming in the high heat). It projects like a monster and the longevity is out of this world for a fresh fragrance, i wore it a couple days ago, i got complimented over ten hours after applying and was told that it smells strong so... It's simplicty makes it very pleasing, but for 340€ it's a bit high of a price for such a simple formula it's not refillable like the LVs and it's 100ml, a fair price for this perfume would be 260€+- (same prices as Dior & Louis Vuitton perfumes)

Right amount of ambroxan addddicccctiveee musky citrusy fresh scent i love it. Cannot stop smelling it nothing comes close. People think this is similar with LV- L'immensité but LV is much rounder and if i had to describe it i would say L'immensite reminds me a 20-28 age group man who enjoys his BMW and goes to the gym smells clean fresh, good looking. Bulgari Tygar on the other hand is BUSINESS... a man who has done it has a big family. Drives his Mercedes S- Class. Not playful its more mature, classy and SHARP.

This is the best fresh scent Ive ever smelled. It’s bright, its clean, uplifting, and smells like a grapefruit exploded. Overall scent wise this is what a fresh everyday scent should be. Its like Blu de Chanel but way brighter Now the only issue is I wish it lasted longer. Its a bug 4.2oz bottle so you can just respray it. You can always get Turathi Blue as a dupe. Lasts just as ling but its cheaper. Or get Sospiro Vibrato which is a more beast mode version of this DNA that lasts (and most people prefer) The fact this fragrance has inspired versions of itself speaks to how good it is. Masterpiece Fresh Fragrance right here

Tygar from Bvlgary is a masterpiece, it is fresh, clean and smells luxurious. It is amazing. It lasts long despite the fact that it is a blue fragrance, and these kind of fragrances usually last for only a few hours. Comparisons with L'Immensite from Louis Vuitton (which I also own) are obvious but I prefer Tyger over L'Immensite with no doubt.
Imagine putting Afternoon Swim scent profile on a ginger woody base borrowed from L'Immensité ; So if these two heavy hitters from Louis vuitton house had a baby, it would be Bvlgari Tygar!

Can’t seem to understand why the longevity is only a 7.9! For me it was Ridiculously long lasting, sprayed it yesterday at 5pm and can still smell it today at 2:30 pm after a shower as well! Projection is perfect, people will smell you but you won’t over power them.

First of all, I should mention that I blind bought Tygar. When I first received it, I hadn’t smelled that many perfumes yet — around 40–50 niche fragrances, most of which were winter scents. I opened Tygar with excitement, sprayed it in the air and on my arm, and immediately noticed how expensive it smelled. It was like bitter grapefruit mixed with a sharp soapy vibe.

There is understandable controversy around Bvlgari Tygar. $400 + tax to smell like a candied grapefruit? It's a hard sell. That being said, it's a nice scent with decent longevity for a citrus freshie. Playful enough for leisure but mature enough for professional wear. Any comparison to Louis Vuitton L'Immensite is simply not true.

I find this fragrance bears a strong resemblance to the original LVEB, yet I think it smells much more synthetic at first. On the skin, however, it smells more pleasant and smoother. The scent somehow reminds me a lot of a lip gloss, as it is so fruity-sweet. Nevertheless, I would recommend it if you are into distinctly sweet fragrances.

Karstadt had sent me a discount voucher - and of course, I wanted to invest it in a fragrance. Since I like La Vie est belle and its flankers, I reflected on the new Oui. Unfortunately, there was no tester available in the store. But since the flankers had not disappointed me so far, I also dared a blind purchase of the new Oui. Besides, I like to surprise myself. I hope for a similarity to the original, but with a certain something. And the fragrance delivers on that. The signature of the sweet, powdery original is unmistakable, but it gains flair and lightness from the fresh, sweet raspberry note that pleasantly brightens the scent. Ylang is enchanting, yet remains ethereal - just like the gourmand notes. The softly smoky finish is interesting and subtly elegant. I say Oui to this approachable fragrance that conveys closeness.

I liked the original La Vie est belle from the very beginning. However, the scent was always a bit too much for me. Especially towards the end, a bitter, punchy vanilla note developed. That's why LVEB was only an option for me in the colder months. Now in March, it would be time to "store it away" until next winter. Last week, the saleswoman at the perfume shop slipped a sample of Qui La vie est belle into my paper bag. So far, I found the annual reinterpretations quite nice, but none ultimately convinced me to buy. But with this one, it clicked right away. Freshly sprayed, the scent immediately reminds me of the original LVEB. But then it quickly becomes fruitier and somehow lighter. And there it is, my LVEB for the warmer months from April to September. A floral, sweet scent that smells to me like delicious raspberries and ylang-ylang. So it only took 2 days for me to return to the perfume shop to claim a beautiful, sparkling bottle as my own. The longevity and sillage are very good for me and not as intense as the original. A successful scent for the anniversary of La vie est belle.

I believe that cologne, rather than coca cola, is “the pause that refreshes”. Its dynamic combo of freshness and cooling properties are a no-brainer for summer. Although my favourite eau de cologne, the Chanel Exclusif, is deeply gorgeous and relatively complex (the musk, oh the MUSK!), it is still just that; a cologne, and is by definition short-lived and quite basic. But colognes refresh. But what if you want that refreshment with some real perfumery pizzazz? Annick Goutal’s masterpiece, Eau du Sud (EdS) refreshes. And sparkles. And delights. For hours. It is no garden variety citrus cologne, nosireebob! It’s one of the single most compelling reasons to even have a summer. It’s that good. Every single time I apply EdS, especially in the anti-climatic summers of Holland, I’m teleported to a place I never want to leave. In the land of EdS the birds are singing, a plethora of Mediterranean herbs – basil, rosemary, lavender and mint - are fecund and ubiquitous, the Sicilian lemons & grapefruit are freshly squeezed by a bronzed beauties and the sky is wide open and endless with heat shimmering through the ether. It’s perfume voodoo and this voodoo is the key reason most of us fume junkies are so committed to – it evocates a very specific context of where we really want to be. The first hit of EdS is ALL of these elements smacking you upside the head like a warm sirocco wind. It has a close affinity in vibe with the timeless classic Chanel Pour Monsieur but with just more everything. The citruses do dominate at first but the grapefruit – unusually – takes over from the juicy lemons and bergamot. And what is doubly remarkable is that the grapefruit lasts for a full hour, outlasting even the excellent Guerlain Allegoria Pampelune. Then there’s the mint & basil, which I believe truly sets EdS apart as a unique experience. They simply sing together in perfect fifths as in an elegant, rustic choir. Furthermore, it is this herbal bouquet that gives EdS its claim to greatness, because they act as the basis for the unmistakeable chypre vibe you get after maybe 15 minutes on the skin. Some say EdS is like Diorella and Cristalle among other aromatic citric chypres, but I emphatically disagree. They all have some degree of moss in their composition, whereas EdS relies on its gorgeous herbal accord to provide the chypric foundation. The longevity of EdS is another of its extraordinary features. There is no cologne on earth that can last for 8 hours, no matter how hard Malle might try with his latest Indelebile. You can apply EdS at 8am, where it through a stanking hot day and it just holds up all day long! Whether you are on vacation or stuck in an office with the AC on the fritz, its power to evocate a happy place will never let you down. There is the faintest, almost imperceptible waft of labdanum and vanilla in the base that I hold responsible for this legendary longevity and is one more reason to admire the skill of the late lamented Ms. Goutal; this was among her final masterpieces. The great asset of EdS is that even if you are in the midst of a brilliant summer, it enhances that reality, kind of like certain substances enhance the reality of certain music. Its chypre quality allows you to enjoy throughout the year for a quick and dependable pick-me-up, casually or for formal occasions. But it is in summer where it teleports most convincingly. My bottle (and its 2 backups) is a “vintish” one, produced before the fairly recent take over of AG by a Korean parent, Amorepacific. You can easily recognize it as it doesn’t have the soulless conformity of bottle that the new ones do. From my experiences, this event has really affected the best AG frags in a depressingly familiar negative way, and honestly I won’t even try any more after a traumatic whiff of the reformulated Mandragore and Sables…. Luckily you can still find this fair weather gem on the usual sites and I hope you do. You may never be as satisfied with a mere cologne again….

Unlike other reviewers, I didn't get much in the way of citrus in Eau de Sud, despite it being a citrus aromatic. I find Eau de Sud perhaps more herbaceous and soapy. Almost peppery, especially in the opening. I like the fresh characteristic of this fragrance, however I find it a little too sharp at times. I'm not really a citrusy or soapy person, so this fragrance isn't really my cup of tea. But for the sake of it being a fragrance from my most loved perfume house, I'd say it is one of the best. It's lightly feminine on the skin which is something I absolutely adore. For that fact alone, I agree that Eau de Sud would make a lovely choice for those particularly humid days. Robin on her blog, Now Smell This, mentioned an interesting smokiness, being quite distinctive, which emerged quite prominently in the drydown. Although I had not noticed this initially, once reading her review and returning to this fragrance, I must agree. The smokiness disrupts the soapy sharpness, which ultimately smoothed out the scent considerably. I find some similarities between this fragrance and Chanel's Cristalle, although they are not complete replicates. The lasting power of Eau de Sud, in the eau de toilette concentration is pretty weak unfortunately. This is also one of Annick Goutal's lighter fragrances that don't depend upon the wonderful sillage to create a beautiful aura. Eau de Sud is a fragrance for those that enjoy their soft, clean and crisp scents.

For me, Eau du Sud is all about the basil and the verbena. I love them in concert here. But let's start at the beginning. In the opening, you're hit with a wallop of citrus, and a handful of fresh crushed basil. In trying to identify the citrus notes up top, I get grapefruit and lime. But as my nose follows the trail of the citrus, what soon emerges is lemon verbena, not a true citrus, but herbal, like the basil. That's the experience for me at the heart of Eau du Sud: basil and verbena. A few hours later, a lovely light, soft chypre base emerges, although brief wafts of the verbena remain. I think Eau du Sud is lovely, especially for spring and summer, but if you don't like basil, or if even a gentle chypre base turns you off, you won't like it as much as I do.

Its no surprise that a modern Nose should draw inspiration from Eau Sauvage - and produce something like a streamlined working of Roudnitska's reference cologne-as-chypre composition. Eau du Sud cuts the fibrous iris-floral heart of Eau Sauvage right back, and promotes, with lime, the juiciness of citrus in its place; revealing the desiccated woody bones of the structure at the same time. It's as though Annick Goutal took Eau Sauvage, exposed it to the sun and winds of the garrigue 'till only the essentials were left; she then juiced it up with lime to give a skeletal, lime scented Eau Sauvage. It's a decent woody citrus in its own right, which, when stripped of the original's floral baggage, becomes less grand, but more at home in todays climate of skin and bone masculines.

I have always been intrigued by the Annick Goutal offerings which are sold in both the standard feminine bottle and the rectangular masculine bottle. For a while I thought that they were two different formulas, but someone disabused me of that false belief. EAU DU SUD is one of them, and systemeD graciously sent me a sample making it possible for me to try this fragrance out after having wondered about it for quite some time... To my nose this is a fairly sharp green citrus fragrance. I'd say that it's about midway between Parfums de Nicolai COLOGNE CEDRAT and Bond no 9 CENTRAL PARK. There is not nearly so much greenishness in this composition as in the latter, but it has a slight spiciness which makes it feel more masculine than feminine--at least in the drydown. The quality seems very high and I'd put this in the EAU D'HADRIEN neighborhood, not only because it's primarily a citrus scent, but also because it, too, seems like a fairly simple creation--at least when compared to the more complex feminine perfumes of this house. We've reached the end of summer here in Boston--a turning point marked by my donning of socks today for the first time in months--so EAU DU SUD is not something that I'm in any hurry to acquire, but I'm sure that come May I'll be considering this bright and cheerful citrus cologne once again.

Short and sweet. Eau du Sud, to me, is very similar to Eau Savage, which I have always loved on my husband. Unlike me he doesn't keep an arsenal of fragrances and so I don't step on his toes and wear one of 'his' signatures. Now I can. Other reviewers note a similarity to Cristalle in Eau du Sud.

A few years ago, when I first traveled to Nice and stood on the beach of the Baie des Anges on the first evening under a full moon with my ice cream from Fenocchio in the flavors of lavender and orange blossom, I wondered why I was only now experiencing this for the first time: "How foolish were you, really?

After the daily question "Which fragrance will I wear tomorrow?", I dug out Eau de Sud by Annick Goutal again, and this in late autumn/winter. Until now, I have actually only worn Eau de Sud, which I have owned for several years, in the summer. It is generally recommended as a fresh citrus summer fragrance.

Every year, I meet up with the core group of my graduating class at the Christmas market in Düsseldorf, our hometown. The meeting point is the Sternchenmarkt, right by the mulled wine stand next to the children's carousel, where we drink egg punch or mulled wine and chatter away until we feel dizzy.

Eau du Sud is a wonderfully old-fashioned aromatic citrus fragrance that has borrowed more than just a few ideas from the classic Detailles Aeroplane. Both have a complex citrus note underpinned by basil, mint, patchouli, vetiver, and oakmoss.

This fragrance for me was very different after I spent the day smelling many fragrances that were particularly 'perfumey'. Omnia Crystalline is more watery than anything. It's refreshing, light and oceanic. I'll start by saying that floral aquatics don't suit my skin chemistry nor my personality, but with that being said, I can appreciate them and in some instances, I do rather like them. I'm on the fence in regards to Omnia Crystalline. It opened nicely on my skin with a delicious pear note and watery lotus, however the tea note is particularly strong which doesn't agree with my nose. Throughout the transformation on the skin, Omnia Crystalline becomes ever so slightly soapy and clean. I must admit that if this fragrance was overwhelming or heavy I'd probably detest it, but in this case, seeing that it is so delicate and light, it is very pleasant. The lasting strength is pretty good, excellent for such a light scent. The warm weather I've heard really brings out the beauty of this fragrance. I'll be interested to see how it fairs in Summer at the end of this year.

I love this scent. The first time I smelled it I was captivated and bought it. I identify with it and my friends say that this fragrance smells like me. It is like being in a forest, sitting in front of a crystal clear lake with lotus flowers. At the beginning I feel a watery freshness that is composed of pine and green tea, intertwined by dried peel of sweet mandarin. The drydown evolves towards a dry woody (more intense than in previous editions) with nuances of incense (my perception feels like the one they burn in the church). In general, I think it is a perfume that few people dislike, because if something characterizes it, it is discretion and softness. It lasts more than acceptable on my skin, as well as on clothes. Again, apologies for my bad English.

The opening of Omnia Crystalline is a rather interesting and somewhat unique experience, at least when compared to other popular perfumes. It’s light, clean, and has a bit of a soapy quality to it but with a distinctly Asian influence. Lotus, tea, and a pear-like smell (provided by the nashi fruit) are the main attractions here, which gives this Bvlgari perfume a floral-plant type of outdoorsy scent. Omnia Crystalline is quite a feminine fragrance and doesn’t seem to include anything that could be considered heavy or overwhelming, which should make this one a good choice for the warmer months of the year. The tea note really reminds me of a men’s cologne that I cannot quite recall the name of (maybe by Roberto Cavalli?), it’s really distinct and green, in it’s aroma. I also detect a hint of Alien Aqua Chic in this composition. However, the major player here is the lotus note…so, if you’re not a fan, look for another perfume. It does have a different feel than the usual rose, iris, violet notes that are so often found in other ladies’ fragrances. There is a slight musk which gives it some warmth and body. The dry down is woody and green, with some remaining fruit sweetness, but mostly that lotus flower as the focus of it all. Bamboo and a bit of moss coming through.

Pretty, light, and clear, exactly as promised. Opening is floral-fruity, with a bit of a throat-scratching green flourish for a minute after the first spray. The first hour or two consists of that watery accord -- lotus and a fruity gesture that you could call ya pear. The thing that elevates it is a touch of smooth herbal green -- the tea note I think. The result is pleasant, luminous and clean and oh so gentle. After about two hours, the drydown becomes more powdery-floral, and the whole experience lasts 3-4 hours total. It reminds me of L'eau d'Issey, but feels less likely to overwhelm, and is more careful along the way (but don't get me wrong, I love L'eau d'Issey). I feel torn about Crystalline. On the one hand, it absolutely delivers on the premise, and does it with delicacy -- though perhaps too much delicacy, since it's a committed skin scent after about an hour, and doesn't last as long as I'd like. And -- I may be ridiculed for this, but every time, the smell makes me imagine a target demographic of rich white women who wear a lot of white, who talk about feng shui and meditation and decorate with Buddha statues. It has that sheerness, and a calculated combination of notes to make you think "zen." I obviously can't know the thought process behind how this perfume was formulated, so I that's just my impression. In short: it's pretty, I tip my hat, but it could be more, and it ain't for me (The line in the title is from "Crystalline" by Björk!)

I had high hopes for this, but there’s a really pungent and horrible undertone in this perfume that seems to dominate over everything else. This actually smells like Veet hair removal cream to me. I don’t get clean from this at all, only burning hair. Maybe it’s the guaiac wood, but it’s a definite pass for me!

In the beginning this one intrigues me. Only three notes are listed, but when I spray it my nose tells me that there are more. I sense a musky note which perhaps is from the balsa wood - but to me musk. I sense a tea-ish note as well. And something watery. All notes that must appear because of the notes combined in this creation.

This is a really clean, very green scent! It has a soapy, almost laundry vibe to it and you really smell the bamboo note. Very safe choice for the office since it's quite inoffensive while still being more on the mature side. While I feel this type of fragrance doesn't really suit me, I think I would really like smelling this on other people!

This is so well blended that it feels difficult to distinguish the notes from each other, it just flows from minty/tea watery coolness to soft floral and a bit woody. I've been wearing it through summer but I feel like it will be loved just as much in the middle of winter.

this is lovely and i think this can be worn in the daytime in any season! if i worked in an office this would be my pick. i find it very very similar to Kayali Musk 12 but this is far better in terms of complexity, longevity & sillage. so if you like the scent and overall vibe of Kayali Musk but want something that actually performs and is a bit less boring, give this a try!!

Omnia Crystalline by Bvlgari is a timeless floral fragrance that carries an unmistakable sense of quiet sophistication. It conjures the image of a modern, refined woman who embodies understated elegance and effortless affluence—someone dressed in the subtle codes of quiet luxury rather than overt display.

I wanted to love it so much. Rose, musk are a dream for me. Unfortunately, the scent comes across as oddly sour to me. And it's not a nice sour, fresh, and crisp but rather an unpleasantly artificial sour. Not a fine sweetness that settles on my skin and wonderfully wafts around me, but rather a persistently annoying presence around me. I think I don't like the Lancome Rose. I had the same problem with Roses Berberanza and Parfait de Roses or La Nuit Tresor Musc Diamant. The same annoying fermented sour note everywhere.

I find the scent very pleasant and soft. Pure femininity. It is also long-lasting. However, the fragrance strongly reminds me of L'instant Magique by Guerlain, just with less sillage. It could also be that I am mistaken. In any case, I am happy to have it in my collection ????.

The scent is like a large bouquet of bright red, finely fragrant noble roses that have just opened their heads (but not the overbred ones, rather the wild-growing ones that can still determine their own growth and shape). Over this, a large, bright silk veil is gently draped, allowing only delicate traces of the rose aroma to penetrate through the fabric - like a young woman who blushes softly because her first kiss has been stolen from her, awakening the deep sensuality that has been slumbering in these seemingly harmless beings. After about half an hour, a large, white, initially innocent-looking clean-sensual wave of musk rises, which one would love to fall into. Simply divine this progression; I find it very feminine, appealing to the recently awakened very young female enchantresses or the more experienced seductresses who have been around longer. This perfume is in no way clumsy, artificial, or cheap, but rather noble, a bit luxurious, and for me, like a sprayed compliment to femininity with all its facets. It lasts easily 7-8 hours and leaves behind a hint of this very pleasantly fragrant fresh-sensual-erotic musk. The roses are very well wrapped in white musk and benzoin, a dream come true for a long day or a captivating night that promises everything is possible. As usual, the price is not cheap at 220 euros for 100 ml, but you need only a little, and then this very fine bottle with its enticing contents lasts forever.... For me, an absolute favorite to recommend for a long time.

Annick Goutal PETITE CHERIE is an excellent example of why people who fall for this house really fall for it. Everything is here in one package: freshness, fruitiness, greenness, florality. That may not sound so amazing in these days of lab-produced perfumes, but in the case of PETITE CHERIE, it all smells entirely natural and not at all abstract. I suppose that the peach in this composition must be synthetic--that's what I've heard about fruit notes in general--but it smells fresh, like the fuzz of a fresh peach plucked from the tree. The peach has not been sliced open, and the sweetness is further contained by the significant greenness, summed up in the note hierarchy as "mown grass", which I interpret to mean "grass clippings". I myself do not find the green here to be as loud as the scent of just-mown grass--this is nothing like Robert Piguet FUTUR or any other grassy green perfume I've ever tried. Still, there is a greenishness, which I find to be about half-way between the scent of grass and that of hyacinth. The flowers in PETITE CHERIE--to my nose, pink roses--are just as important as the peach and the green, but they, too, are gentle and blend in with the rest of the components to create a perfectly balanced perfume. Can there be a natural-smelling fruity-floral perfume? Apparently so, given the existence of PETITE CHERIE. (I should say, though, that this is very, very different from FERRE edp, which I recently reviewed and raved about as a sophisticated fruity-floral perfume.) Despite the name, I do not find PETITE CHERIE to be juvenile in any way. It is friendly and has a sort of innocent or guileless quality to it, as there is nothing dirty or skanky whatsoever, and it's also not overly complicated. I find it endearing without being "cute". Perhaps the best expression to apply would simply be "effortlessly pretty". Think of a freshly washed face with the skin still moist from water and the cheeks slightly pink. That image matches my feelings about PETITE CHERIE.

It's easy to fall in love with a scent such as this. Classic yet simplistic, Petite Cherie has shown once again why I love Annick Goutal fragrances so dearly. Although primarily fruit-based, with pear being the most notable accord, Petite Cherie proves to be quite refined and elegant, which are rare qualities in a fruity floral. I find the scent to be very rich and insanely addictive. My mother happens to love this fragrance with a passion, so it looks to me like I'll be buying her this for Christmas. Petite Cherie is Spring and sunshine in a bottle. The refreshing pear note blended with rose, gardenia and peach makes this fragrance so very juicy and green, especially with the almost grassy-like note in the drydown. Unfortunately, like many have stated, the lasting strength is very poor. I'm determined to find a giftset where a lotion and shower gel is included so that the scent should last a lot longer.

How have more people not mentioned the MUSTY smell in PETITE CHERIE? Yes, it has a girlish, flirty flounce, sure, in all that fruit. But it's very hard to miss the bookish dank musty library in this! Also, it doesn't last. Pure and simple as that.

It took me a while to finally get to testing Petit Cherie as for some reason I thought that it will be too childish for me. Well, I tried it this morning and I love it a lot. The fruits are done so right in this scent. They are natural, vibrant and beautiful. I was able to smell the sparkly pear without even looking at the notes, so I think it is the most noticeable in the composition joined by the delicious peach and just a touch of a rose. There is also a nice, luscious green note that I quite enjoy in this fragrance. The scent smells like a lovely smile of spring, sunny and fresh. Petite Cherie is very happy and delicate perfume and I can see why Annick Goutal dedicated it to her daughter, Camille. This perfume will make a beautiful gift for young ladies or anyone young at heart. I just love how the sunny side of life is captured in this scent. My only complaint is the lasting power. Unfortunately the scent disappears way too quickly for me.

Dainty, delicate and delicious. I enjoy this soft delectable somewhat reminiscent scent. I think it would be perfect for a new mother. The notes meet my nose and taste buds with velvety softness. Nice balance of fruit-flower. Fades away too quickly though.

First thing to hit the nose is a distant fruity sweetness (more peach than pear), and then immediately – grass. A moment of excitement. An unexpectedly realistic and pleasant surprise. Then I notice the petals. As rose petals grow stronger, I lose sight of the grass and my excitement soon fizzles out.

Recently at the flea market: Spring, 22 degrees, sunny, light wind (the hair was in place) - it was wonderful! Then my eye spotted a small bottle of Petite Cherie with a little bit left, probably enough for about five applications. Annick Goutal was familiar to me (how could I ever forget Songes...

Dedicated to my friend Rike. "Petit Cherie" is, as the name suggests, a little treasure. A spring-fresh bouquet of meadow flowers, and a delightful, enchanting fruit basket, where a slightly riper peach and many green pears rest. Yes, pears, with their delicate, lovely scent. Their fine white juice.

This is how young girls should smell! This way and not otherwise (and I don't just mean the upper-class daughters, but ALL of them). Not like hairspray, not like smoke, and not like Bacardi Breezer burps. Also not like the sugary slush from Playboy. They should smell like their youth: Somewhere between clean, juicy, and flirtatious. Cute, but with style.

When I brought the aroma to my nose, I smelled rose, peonies and a little pepper. From the very beginning one can feel the presence in the garden, filled with the scents of flowers. Moreover, the rose fascinated me so much that I could not get away from it and apply it to my hand. At the beginning I smelled mint, a little bergamot and grapefruit. The aroma becomes very similar to a grapefruit mint candy, but at the same time it was sweet and fresh. Rose and peon open up in the middle, and I also smelled some watermelon wateriness. Very cool, balanced, floral-fruity middle. It feels like a garden of flowers, and in the middle there is a fountain, quite large. Well, at the end it starts to smell like raspberries, pink pepper and a little rose. The aroma becomes very soft and delicate, bitter, fruity and somewhere fresh.

I don't smell anything from the soap/shampoo note described here. I smell rose, raspberry, and pink pepper...beautiful, floral with a kick. This scent reminds me of Delina by Parfums de Marly. It's not a dupe, by any means, but it has a certain similarity. However, it is fresher and lighter, well-suited for summer (which Delina, in my opinion, is not). The longevity on my skin is not particularly good, a maximum of 3 hours, on clothing a bit more. The problem I have with this scent is that it smells sour on my skin when I sweat :(. On clothes, it smells great. Yesterday, when I was walking in 30-degree heat with this scent, after an hour I felt like I had a glass of vinegar-pickles poured over me... :( That makes me sad because the scent itself is very beautiful.

Aqva pour Homme is an aromatic aquatic fragrance for man released in 2005 by luxury market company Bvlgari, having Jacques Cavallier as its creator. Aqva it's a marine frag in its essence, with all the strength and depth of the ocean amazingly blended between its notes from top to base, to create the perfect aquatic scent. Energic a vigorous as an ocean storm, not as an ocean breeze or a walk on the coast line. The Original Aqva is big waves and stormy sea. It's a ship battling a storm in high ocean water and finally getting sunk into the depths of the ocean abiss. Aqva fills your nose with notes of Mandarin Orange, Petitgrain, Lavander, Cotton Flower and Seaweed, probably its most unusual note but also the one that gives this fragrance its charisma and uniqueness. All of those top and middle notes wonderfully backed up by a woodsy base, Patchouli and Amber giving it an incense like dry down. Salty and fresh with a punch of character and complexity, Aqva is the perfect summer scent, perhaps even all year round scent if you live near the coast line. It's a weird, moody, strong and mysterious kind of fragrance, wrapped with a little darkness and probably what your Zack Snyder's Aquaman smells like if you have to make an analogy with a known character. Out of all the Aqva Bvlgari line the original might be the one with more presence and definition, the more luxurious and sophisticated. Performance gives you 7 to 8 plus hours on skin with great sillage for 3 to 4 hours. If you spray it on clothes it stays forever and it explodes in humidity or summer rainy weather. Top: Mandarin Orange, Orange, Petitgrain Middle: Seaweed, Lavander, Cotton Flower Base: Virginia Cedar, Woodsy notes, Patchouli, Clary Sage, Amber This review reflects personal opinion and is not sponsored. For more follow me on Instagram @daysleeper_alchemist

Bulgari Aqua opens with a blast of artificial smelling orange with tons and tons of calone immediately peeping through early. The aquatic calone chemical remains into the heart of the scent now the star, with the initial orange remaining in support joined by woody cedar rising from the base that grows as time passes and the calone recedes during the dry-down with the scent staying relatively linear from there on out. Projection is excellent and longevity is average, lasting 6-8 hours on skin. I can't say I am a big fan of calone-laced aquatics, and Aqua pour Homme is no exception. It is highly synthetic smelling, and in this case that is in a very bad way. Unfortunately Aqua is just another "me too" generic aquatic offering from Bulgari that is bested by many others in the genre that are much more pleasant smelling (and many for less money to boot). I recommend seeking others in the genre if you want this kind of scent, with excellent options being vintage Cool Water, Bellagio for Men or New West for Him among many others. The relatively poor smelling Aqua pour Homme gets 2 stars out of 5 and an avoid recommendation.

I am attempting to write this review without being biased. My boyfriend wears this on a daily basis, so it's become less of a perfume for me, and more the smell that reminds me of him. I will begin by saying that when I first smelt Bvlgari Aqva, I was a little underwhelmed. I'm not a huge fan of anything aquatic, even though I do enjoy its freshness on a man's skin. However, in the case of Bvlgari Aqva, I began to fall in love with its salty sea water note and its rich, earthy patchouli which lingers underneath the juicy orange. I'm actually not surprised to read that there are many women that wear this also. It's masculine, but not strictly so. I find it a fragrance along the lines of Cool Water, Acqua di Gio and CK One, but perhaps a touch spicier. My boyfriend wears this all year round, which is sometimes strange because I think it suits Summer weather a hell of a lot better. He also owns Gucci's Envy for Men (a gift I gave him) and CK's Eternity for Women, however Bvlgari Aqva is what he chooses above anything else. On any other man, this fragrance would not turn me on, but on my boyfriend's skin, the combination is extremely sexy. It gives off this clean, 'fresh out of the shower' type aura that I really adore. Bvlgari Aqva is a touch woodsy in the drydown, sharp almost. The rich amber only re-instates its masculine qualities. In some ways I'd call this a fierce aquatic, there is nothing subdued or soothing about it. The longevity is great, especially on my boyfriend's skin which tends to soak up a lot of scents. Bvlgari Aqva is right up there as one of my favourite fragrances for men.

This is a joint review of Aqva Pour Homme and Aqva Pour Homme Marine. Both of these are fresh scents that work well in summer. Aqva Pour Homme opens with a refreshing burst of strong citrus. As it begins to dry down, an aquatic accord appears that is rather subtle along with a slightly green accord. I wouldn't say it's a very strong aquatic scent. After about 20 minutes or so, it takes on a very synthetic accord that's slightly plastic-y, which I didn't care for. It wasn't awful, but it wasn't great. Aqva Pour Homme Marine doesn't open with strong citrus, despite the top notes. More obvious was a stronger melon like scent. As it dried down, the melon scent was reined in along with the appearance of a subtle woody note which gave the impression of an aquatic or marine scent. Marine is definitely the more aquatic scent than Aqva Pour Homme. I also found Marine to be slightly less synthetic and no trace of a plastic scent. As is typical with most freshies, performance overall was mediocre although Marine had a slight edge. Longevity was about 5 hours tops with reasonable projection for about an hour. My preference is for Marine. Both are rather expensive for what they are.

I think it was Dillards where I first smelled this back in 2005, and a song by the Carpenters was playing over the speakers. (Strange, the things you remember that others consider insignificant.) Now, every time I think about Bulgari Aqua, I think about that. At first sniff, it smells nice enough with that orange opening, but later becomes almost plastic-like (yes, I tried it on my skin). But still, despite that plastic, fishy smell, there's something about it I like. It seems sophisticated, and is certainly not pure fish like the Aqua MARINE flanker.
One of the best and unique Aquatic - Summer fragrance. Its smells amazing, projection is not so great but you don't need to choke everybody in summer, 6 sprays will be enough to have like 5-6 hours.

I love blue aquatic fragrances, and they have a dear place in my soul, Most of my fragrances library contain fragrances with aquatic scents, but I don’t really know, This fragrance doesn’t belong to this category, Who has classified it as an aquatic fragrance? The fragrance tends towards refreshing green, herbal fragrances, not blue at all.

But just like most of his flankers, the longevity leaves you longing for a little more. The oceanic feel that this one gives is second to none. A “deep sea” vibe that you either love or hate. It’s definitely not for everyone. I personally love the way it feels... it gives the vibe of being out on the ocean, with a sort of cool, fresh feeling added to it.
Going back to 2015 when I bought fragrance because I some random female youtuber recommended it to me for summers. When I put it on for the first time it felt like an aquatic bomb...

Personal: 7/10 – Salty, aquatic, and slightly bitter-green. It’s pleasant, but it's not my favorite. Mass appeal: 8.5/10 - Very safe marine citrus fragrance. Seaweed is not at the forefront. Performance: 6/10 – Okay for an aquatic, but not a powerhouse. Fades after a few hours.

It is quite annoying to see reviews of people, characterizing this particular fragrance (and others) as unsuccessful, purely synthetic or even generic!.. Well, it is probably not the most traditionally made aroma out there, but it is absolutely an interesting and nice smelling one. Also, it's name "wood essence" gives a pretty good idea of what to expect in terms of smelling experience : woody enough for someone who likes that category of fragrances. Of course, the "woody" aromas aren't always the preferred choice in comparison with other types (as spicy, or aquatic) but are still a good choice for rho who like that type of fragrances. So, for that particular category the Bvlgari Wood essence is really a very decent representative! If you are a fan of woody fragrances, then this is an excellent choice!

Immediately after spraying, the fragrance is filled with an exquisite smell of freshly cut wood and forest. It is not an olfactory complex fragrance and If you do not like woody fragrances, this fragrance will not be to your liking, the smell of wood is very present. In the drying of this fragrance the magic happens, the smell of wood decreases and a Citrus-sweet smell appears along with the Bvlgari base. Here's the difference with many woody fragrances. An ideal fragrance for young adults, It does not smell like a mature adult, like the case of Man in Black, nor does he fall into the vice of sweet fragrances for young people who don't know if they are for men or women. It is a 100% masculine fragrance, but it screams youth. In my opinion it is very positive, but if you are looking for a woody fragrance that projects maturity and firmness, again, this is not the fragrance for you. The duration of the fragrance is Excellent, the projection not so much. If you put it on your clothes or on blotting paper, the fragrance will last for weeks. On skin about 8 to 12 hours The projection of the fragrance in the first 2 or 3 hours is very good but then it fades a lot. This is the weakest part of the fragrance. In some perfumes with low projection, you could apply about 10 sprays and with this you would solve the low projection. But this is not the case with wood essence, if you apply 10 sprays, you could flood an entire auditorium with smell, it would be inconspicuous. Indeed it is an Edp, on the skin it feels slightly oily. Ideal for use in spring or autumn during the day or night.

I tend to like Morillas' creations, and love several of Bvlgari's releases but this? I was excited to try it since I'm a sucker for woody fragrances but damn, when was the last time Alberto visited the woods?? Let me start off by saying that this isn't anywhere near a WOOD essence, more like a generic, money-grab, blue fragrance release. It starts off very sweet and synthetic pretty much like any other scent of this kind, shampoo-ish. That stays until the very end it is a very linear scent until it somewhat becomes a skin scent that smells of clean musk. That's it. They could've done much better stuff with this idea. Big pass.

The first hour or so I'm reminded of Davidoff's Good Life which is a definite Spring and Summer scent. It starts off green and figgy though I don't see fig in the notes list. The middle life turns to cypress and vetiver. I have to give this a few more wearing to better describe the tail end of Wood Essence.

This is for a man that is comfortable in he needs and obligations, he does not rush nor does he have much to worry about, for someone that appreciates the artistry of a fine handmade umbrella, quality paper, ink, indoor fireplaces and a single glass of whiskey. Softwood notes morph into woodsmoke as the hours progress, further adding a mellow, mature and refined atmosphere to the man that wears this. Zest and corriander is pleasently noticeable, early on but gradually fades and subtle woodsmoke takes over. This is a very mature scent, think of a man that wears woolen turtlenecks, owns many leathergoods and has a pair of genuine sheekskin seat covers on the seats of his vintage mercedes benz.

The scent of sugary citrus fruits (I preferred that there was no sugar) that releases into the air as soon as I spray this fragrance is that of oranges and lemons which, when attenuated, allows the freshness of the cypress to be fully perceived, unlike of the coriander leaf which is not distinguishable.

I discovered this perfume through a miniature in 2018. it quickly stood out it is a perfume that has an unusual smell. I Didn t find an equal rater than i smelled around 500 fragrances. I clearly qualify it as a masculine summer perfume, it is a fresh woody scent. Ideal for the end of the afternoon.

Lovable coriander leaves opening. Sleek synthetic cologne below. Initial cloud engulfs the room, but soon settles in the wearer's immediate vicinity. An arm's length worth of sillage for the first ~2 hours. Settles close to skin afterwards. Fresh cypress, artificial cedar, dull vetiver and a splash of nostalgic sense of melancholy. Huh. I wonder what that one's about.

Really. The 40-minute drive after I innocently tested the monstrously advertised new men's Bvlgari in a shopping arcade was honestly an olfactory nightmare. What is this? I haven't encountered something so annoyingly bulky, irritating, and artificially disgusting in a long time. Coriander? Cypress? Amber?

In the past, everything was better. This isn't always true, only when making a very specific comparison to devalue something new. Well, 20 years ago, maybe even 10 years ago, you could reach into the Bvlgari shelf at random and get a really great fragrance under your nose. Unfortunately, I haven't felt that way for several years now.

Sables follows a classical drydown arc: top, heart, basenotes. The real trick though is that is that it takes you from one genre to another over this progression. Starting with immortelle dissolved in amber, Sables gives you either a strictly sweet maple syrup candy, or a sweet and savory curry with fenugreek and raisins. It’s up to your nose. I get the latter. Either way I find it principally gourmand. Where Sables winds up, though is in the sandlewood/amber range. While the spice-like immortelle fades in the heartnotes, by drydown, there is a light, peppery sharpness that gives the amber drydown a mineral/dry inflections not miles from that of Ambre Sultan’s scent of hot stone. Sables is the only fragrance I can think of off the top of my head that isn’t categorized so much as a hybrid (eg. floriental, leather chypre…) but as a fragrance that starts in one genre (gourmand) and ends firmly in another (amber/oriental.) A gorgeously constructed fragrance, appropriate across the multiple (and I believe there really are many) genders, but would be a smart statement of devil-may-care appreciation of prettiness on an assured straight man.

I am an unconditional fan of the aroma of “Immortelles”. Not because the Greeks used it to crown images and statues of Apollo since the plant symbolized love. But first for the beautiful and unforgettable olfactory memories that I associate with it. When in the late afternoons in summer I returned from the beach along the dunes of the Alentejo coast, in front of the pessegueiro island (Porto Covo - Portugal), I was blessed by a warm breeze that carried the comforting smell, at the same time spicy and relaxing, of “Immortelles” with small golden yellow flowers. As a result, I have been a fan since the first hour of “Sables” by Annick Goutal, released in 1985. Probably the first fragrance in history in which everlasting flowers took center stage. The great reference among fragrances centered on “immortelles” or “everlasting flowers” ​​that was conceived as a declaration of love from Annick to her husband (Alain Meunier) trying to reproduce the sublime atmosphere of the days spent in Corsica during the summer. I still have a bottle of the 2nd reformulation. Without a doubt the original Sables from 1985, with a very interesting refreshing black tea note (which disappeared in later versions) is much better than the 3 subsequent versions. Super dry, curry-like, a little bit creamy and sweet. Overpowering. A masterpiece and perhaps the brand's best fragrance ever. Rating 10. The 2nd version is powerful and masculine and also very good but more “earthy”, drier, hot and wild. Like the previous version, it has fantastic projection and sillage. A true Simum of the desert. Rating: 9. The latest version (I think it's the 4th reformulation) is lighter and with a slightly citrusy opening. More wearable, less intense and without the masculine splendor of the first 2 editions. However, the current Sables remains interesting and has a recognizable personality. Rating: 7 Comparing the notes between the 1st and the last one better understands the reasons for the differences. Notes from the 1st edition (1985): Top notes: Immortelle and Cinnamon Middle notes: Black pepper and Black tea Base notes: Sandalwood and Amber. Notes from the last and current edition: To notes: Bergamot, Mandarine Middle notes: Jasmine, Black pepper, Oakmoss Base notes: Immortelle Sauvage, Santal d'Inde, Ambre

There are some fragrances that create so much with so little. Super straight forward, they want to replicate some moment/place or just the smell of something. Goutal is a great classic brand that newer noses don't care and/or don't even know about it. And I don't blame them because today's standards are different from 20 years ago. Youtubers are the main sources for new hyped fragrances and the whole market are centered on fresh and sweet versatile scents and the niche houses are no longer niche brands but just high end designers clones, with higher price tags. Fortunately, there are still some classic niche brands that does things right. This classic '85 release is a proof that we still can enjoy some different and quality fragrances with a good price and stand out while smelling appealing at the same time. Created to his husband, Goutal wanted to replicate the smell of sand in Corsica beaches. And to do that, she choose to use immortelle. A big flower, with yellow tones and a strong smell (like burned curry). Very common in dunes and dry sandy places. Sables has, right at the opening, a strong immortelle presence. Super dry, curry-like, a little bit creamy and sweet. There's also something sticky and sweet in the opening, that will evolve into a more dry, creamy and relaxed sweetness in he drydown. The main player here is, of course, the immortelle but I also can detect some dry and sweet cinnamon and a creamy sandalwood. That's it. Super straight forward composition. But it's so beautiful, powerful and majestic that it works perfectly. A true piece of art, but still, very wearable and comforting like a warm coat. Winter is the best time to wear it due to his great performance and presence. Although I also can wear it in spring, on a walk on the coast side. 2 sprays will fill a room and will last all day (10h+) All in all, a beautiful and magic fragrance that is a must-have and deserves more attention. Hopefully, will be available forever for us to enjoy, like the immortelle itself. 5/5

It's no secret that I adore Annick Goutal, however I must admit, despite my eagerness, I wondered whether or not her male fragrances would captivate me in the same way. Fortunately, Sables is outstanding, incredibly desirable on a man and something I wouldn't mind wearing myself. It's a little sharp at first. Sables begins with a strong burst of pepper, woods and smoke. Although masculine, I thought it was a little too much, somewhere along the lines of the ruggedly masculine yet rich and bold Yatagan by Caron. Thankfully Sables settles into a divine, sensual blend of woods, spice, caramel and burnt golden syrup. It's almost a gourmand for men with its distinctive deliciousness. I love how the burnt sugar accord doesn't make this fragrance feminine or too sweet. It's perfectly balanced and very sexy, something that I would never tire of smelling. The longevity and sillage are rather impressive, with this fragrance clinging to the skin for almost a whole 12 hours or more. I highly recommend.

Take a red herbal liqueur of cherry, dried apricot and salted plum. Mix with burnt sugar and spice. Pour onto hot dry sand. Observe that while the liqueur drains away, the blocks of Helichysum, peppery amber and sandal do not change much.
