Opening with a burst of citron, immediately the vetiver and leather are apparent and sting your nostrils slightly. The drydown is beautiful. Unapologetically masculine and assertive woody earthy goodness. It's very nice, but I can see how it can fall into that pit of being on the one hand not shocking enough to fans of Guilty Absolute and Terroni and being too bold and brash for the fans of TdH and its ilk. For me, I slightly prefer Guilty Absolute since I like "going all in," as it were, on the ostentatiousness of the Woodleather synthetic but this is definitely a good backup in case that one gets discontinued/becomes too expensive.

This fragrance is so damn unique....... . Location is Venice Beach, you been walking along the beach & have only been in town for only an hour or two.The first thing you notice is the heat, it's dry & it is intense. You choose to go grab yaself something cool to drink, at the shop off on the corner. But before you walk in, you get a very distinct smell of Cannabis that almost smells earthy yet pungent. Very pleasing but you continue into the store, get a COOL BLAST from the ac. You get a chance to really breath, & in the faint distance, the store owner is burning a slightly spicy incense. You grab yaself a nice Arnold Palmer, taste of the citrus & ice tea really helps quench your thirst. So you're back out in the heat & you start to take your walk out onto the main street & see all the activity, a food truck in the distance. & you can see the heat coming up from the concrete. The heat wave has started & you have a great weekend ahead of yourself. . Naturally you end your afternoon, in a dispensary & go relax until the night falls. Happy hunting
After Bvlgari initially startled me with the cacophonous "Wood Essence," I did well to give this "Earth Essence" a chance despite everything. Because this one is really decent!

Ladies and Gentlemen, today we are talking about the new fragrance by Alberto Morillas, which he designed for Bvlgari, namely Bvlgari Man Terrae Essence. Foreword: Since I really like Acqua di Giò Profumo by Alberto Morillas and Uomo Urban Feel is also quite decent, I decided to get Bvlgari Man Terrae Essence as well.

Once again, I cannot understand a rather poor review. The title is inspired by a fellow reviewer, whom I found to be just perfectly fitting. The Bvlgari Man Terrae Essence impresses me mainly with its masculine, woody character, which can particularly shine in summer through its understated elegance and uniqueness. Subtle citrus gives it the finishing touch.

First of all: I haven't been in the perfume game for very long, and this is my first review. Why did I choose to write my first review about this fragrance? Because this scent has shown me that there are fragrances that you only come to appreciate after wearing them for a longer time and more often. I received this Bvlgari shortly after its release.

This fragrance starts off a bit intense, the citrus fruits are somewhat heavy, but not overpowering. It feels a bit smoky, earthy, and it develops over the next few hours. The scent lasted about 5-6 hours with 5 sprays. It has an average projection of about 40cm on my skin. I don't find it too synthetic.

La Vie est Belle L'Éclat L'Eau de Toilette starts off refreshingly sweet - fruity, but also subtly citrusy - herbal. At first, a sweet and fruity note can be perceived, which gives the top note a "soft" quality and is thanks to the mandarin. At the same time, the mandarin is underlined by another fruity note, which is responsible for giving the top note a somewhat illuminating quality and comes from grapefruit. These two notes are enveloped by a lively, peppy note that provides the top note with a pleasant refreshing feeling and originates from pink pepper. In the background, a fine subtle citrusy - herbal nuance of bergamot can be detected, which further enhances the "refreshing feeling". The entire top note is carried by a typically tea-like aura, which brings a hint of hibiscus and lotus, giving it a pleasantly uplifting quality. Already in the top note, a "hint" can be perceived, which unfortunately becomes even stronger in the heart note. This constellation is perceptible on my skin for 20 minutes before the heart note unfolds. Now, a sparkling, floral, and very bright note is noticeable, which gives the fragrance a pleasant lightness and is thanks to the neroli in combination with orange blossom absolute. These two notes are enveloped by very pleasant floral notes, which bestow a very intense femininity to the fragrance and come from jasmine absolute. In the background, a deep and also captivating floral note can be perceived, which gives the fragrance a pleasant substance and originates from Turkish rose. All of this smells remarkably good; however, the fragrance is slightly overshadowed by the hint from the top note, which becomes increasingly evident the closer one gets to the skin: Namely plastic, which retreats almost completely after 3 hours, but unfortunately not entirely. The heart note is perceptible on my skin for 5 hours before the base takes over. Now, a very fine and subtle powdery - floral note can be detected, which gives the fragrance something "beautiful" and is thanks to iris concrete. There is also a slight earthy, sweet nuance that provides a certain depth and is due to patchouli. These two notes are enclosed by a clear and transparent note, which comes from ambroxan in combination with musk. La Vie est Belle L'Éclat L'Eau de Toilette is a pleasant companion in the spring, summer, and autumn months for younger and older women who are looking for a light, bright, floral, and flowery fragrance and can overlook the hint of plastic. Overall, the fragrance lasts 8 hours on my skin. The sillage is designed from the beginning to be clearly noticeable at arm's length, and this is maintained for 3 hours before it gradually reduces until the fragrance finally fades completely.

...it's starting to feel a bit eerie ;-) because: I usually don't get along with LVEB due to the cotton candy or praline note (which ruins the 1st EDP). The L'eclat EDP was the first LVEB that I liked right away despite the still present sweetness, probably because it already had that beautiful zesty citrus combo in it. The EDT finally has even more of that zest! Although I wish the sweetness had completely disappeared in the EDT, unfortunately it is still slightly present depending on my mood. The scent itself starts off citrusy-fresh-herbaceous for me and then quickly transitions into a light floral note that transforms into a lovely creamy note by the base. Depending on my nose's mood (or hormones), the aforementioned sweetness comes into play or not. In the former case, you can clearly recognize the LVEB DNA, while in the latter, you might think more of an Eau de Cologne. Then the scent is unbeatable for me, reminding me of the 70s and a great time! The fragrance carries exactly the aura of that era (yes, I believe in such things :-)) into the here and now. The bottle is also beautiful, reminding me again of the 70s (probably because of the sparkling disco balls ;-)) and fits wonderfully with the scent and name, in my opinion. The sillage and longevity are also decent, so one should be careful with the dosage. I'm curious to see how it performs in summer; so far, I could only test it up to 10 degrees Celsius or in freezing temperatures. Here, I already notice slight differences, especially when the air is more humid. In cold, dry air, it feels distinctly cool, the warmer and more humid it gets, the softer and more charming it becomes. For a rather synthetic fragrance, this change is quite unusual, but it allows for some "playing" with it. All in all, LVEB L'eclat EDT is an absolute recommendation for all lovers of floral scents. For LVEB fans, it might be the first flanker that doesn't resonate as well as its predecessors or one that you need to get used to.

This fragrance is really lovely and fresh. It's Summery and pretty without being overloaded by citrus notes. My skin really soaks up these kinds of scents. Eau Parfumee au The Blanc sits on my skin like a lightly scented lotion, creamy and polite. It's very inoffensive and as I imagine, wonderful in the warmer weather. Many say that this fragrance is soapy, and I somewhat agree, however I think it smells more like an expensive, soft, floral-scented shower cream. I also sense a creaminess that reminds me of icecream, however vanilla isn't present here. On my skin, Eau Parfumee au The Blanc is extremely feminine, however I would like to see how this fragrance wears on a man's skin. I do believe it has the opportunity to be masculine. The muskiness in the drydown is very nice and subtle. I urge those that are afraid of a strong tea note or pepper note to not give this fragrance a miss. Those notes don't tend to dominate. I'm not surprised to hear that Bvlgari has produced a shampoo and conditioner range using this scent. The scent is truly delightful. The lasting strength is good for a cologne concentration, and the sillage is fairly intimate. Overall a lovely unisex fragrance for the individual that doesn't like anything too 'perfumey' or strong.

There he stood lonely and alone In the midst of all the autumn leaves Wrapped in cold autumn air Wrapped in cold fog Enchanted by the freshness Enchanted by the distance There he stood lonely and alone Stubbornly spicy-comforting Again like a little forest sprite Like himself, the little dragon Estragon So he jumps in the freshness So confused in powder clouds Like a lazy pirate of the skies Like a little jerk in the distance So he remains So he spews So he haunts in this scent Our little dragon Estragon Addendum to the scent: Actually a crazily beautiful scent. Just for me so herbal, so spicy, just like a little forest sprite, just like the little dragon Estragon.

A whole decade we have shared together, you and I, a decade full of madness and melancholy, fireworks and ocean depths, heavy metal and soft tones. Tears by day, laughter by night, chimes at odd hours and hours dripping by far too slowly. A decade with a black sun and a red moon, with magic rays in the night sky and a return to the womb. Did you think that we would experience all this and much more together, back on that day in Simone's perfumery? There you stood, cool, clear, subtle, and very elegant - I already knew your big green brothers, the red one was not yet in the world. I liked you, I took you with me into that time when a love affair swept me away, that lifted my world off its hinges, washed my brain, and flicked my soul to Venus and back, letting me plunge without a straw into a wild sea that promised to swallow me, to drown me. You witnessed all of this, silently, reserved, never joining in, always keeping a distance from my feelings, my longings, my memories. Two years later, the tornado spat me out, leaving me behind with twisted, shattered limbs, breathless and without will. Do you remember? You watched me as I picked myself up and fell again, as I crawled and stumbled blindly, walking slowly beside me on the long path back to myself. You were there, bright and cool, never touching me, not my head, not the heart that was just minced meat, and yet you never left me alone, never. Eventually, many days, weeks, months later, I was well again, the survival mechanisms had kicked in and banished the dark fog from my brain. You were still there, still - many of your brothers and sisters had to leave, had found another home, because I could no longer bear them, not the images, the memories, the deep pain that their scent revived again and again. You remained with your citrus cheerfulness, the restrained floral sweetness, and a gentle yet distinct tea note that kindly stimulates and calms at the same time, cooling and restraining my blood. You never wanted to become herby with me, a bit scratchy perhaps, as your namesake can be, the white tea, if one dares to treat it wrongly. And I know that you will punish me with silence again, and yet I must again think of Calvin Klein's famous One, which becomes so similar to you on my skin with that aquatic nuance that closely intertwines with the citrus notes and relegates the tea to second place. Of course, you are finer in your composition, more fragile and cooler, softer and more mature, calmer, more grown-up than CK One, but still... What is so wrong with mentioning you both in the same breath? Don't forget that he, the healer, wore that very Calvin at our first meeting, who perhaps didn't really fit him, but also didn't disturb and certainly didn't prevent anything. It will soon be eight years since then. He is still there, warm and firm and constant, my rock in the surf, my ripcord on the parachute, my crackling fireplace when the storm howls through the trees outside, my lifeboat when I have once again played Titanic, my I-am-with-you. He is there. Just like you.

Many criticize the 3 Bulgari tea fragrances for smelling too much like a sanitized hotel room, but I don’t see that as a disadvantage. I have been in many luxury hotels, but it has never smelled this good! Maybe in heaven, because I have already fallen somewhat in love with the 3 fragrances - each has its own face and character, but all 3 are teon, clean, and relaxing with different interpretations of the tea theme! The Blanc is my girlfriend's favorite of the series, and I find it increasingly difficult to pick a winner. The Blanc is the lightest, simplest of the 3, but often simple is indeed genius, and that is the case here. There is a great similarity to the Vert, but Blanc is even more citrusy and sweeter, with no green notes to be detected. Pure lemon, the lightest white tea ever, a bit of spice from tarragon and pepper, but hardly noticeable, and in the end, just as pure white musk. A fragrance cannot be whiter - heavenly and fitting to the bottle and name! Cloudy, naive, lovely, pure, baby-soft, slightly powdery. One easily starts to dream and fly! The bottle may be unassuming in color, but with the ice effect and the changing surface upon touch and warmth, it might be the most beautiful of the 3 stunning Bulgari bottles! Sillage is hard to overdo and always remains light and airy. Longevity never exceeds 5 hours. These 3 fragrances are a class above everything else in the Bulgari house, please do not discontinue!

This is my first attempt, which I naturally want to dedicate to my "great love"! Eau thé blanc is for me the first and only fragrance that has accompanied and fascinated me even after 10 years, just like on the first day. The only one I have repurchased countless times. I wear it in summer and winter, and I haven't done that with any other scent. Why, how, and why I don't know, but this is my fragrance. This is me. It belongs to me, and I can't imagine a life without it anymore. So, if Bvlgari ever (which I hope they won't!!) gets the crazy idea to discontinue the production of my "beloved," I see myself forced to take out a loan, rent a cold storage facility to buy up and store all remaining stocks on this planet... For me personally, it was love at first sight. The bottle is straightforward, without much frill, yet not simple, but of stylish, timeless elegance. We met for the first time in a small perfumery. I looked at it, and its outer appearance made me hopeful. It exceeded my expectations. I could already see from the outside what was inside, and it did not disappoint me. The scent is clear, light, fresh, somewhat lemony for me, but not sour, surrounding me with a subtle light sweetness, a little powdery, and eventually becomes warm and slightly spicy but discreet, without deviating from the actual fresh line. On clothing, it lasts forever for me. I feel truly elegant and stylish when I am surrounded by its fresh-powdery, velvety scent. I prefer to wear it in winter in the evenings when I am dressed all in black, and in summer, I prefer it with white. It has the elegance needed for the evening in black but also the freshness for the cool white linen pants with a top in the summer morning. When I take the bottle and sniff it, the first image that always comes to my mind is of the lovely sun shining through the window on a summer morning, blinding me, and a still cool, fresh breeze wafts in through the tilted window. The second thought is then a cozy dinner in winter, with lots of snow outside and a crackling fireplace; I am wearing a soft, black cashmere sweater. Ah, what would I do without it? We have already experienced so much together. If we hadn't met, I would probably still be rushing through life today, hoping to encounter "THE ONE" someday. But luckily, we found each other, my love.

Oh, many beautiful declarations of love on this page. Hopefully, it’s not too bad that I approach the fragrance in the following not quite as intimately. I still find it very, very beautiful! Read here why The first minute for me is pure glue.

Just as I enjoy testing Jo Malone's Rare Teas, I also like to explore the tea fragrances from the Bvlgari Thé collection, and I've just arrived at the White Tea. I just realized... I haven't had white tea in years (note to self: remember to buy white tea. How can I best remember that??...

tea fragrances.... High-quality white tea is also known as the champagne of teas. It was once reserved only for the emperor and his servants. No other Chinese tea is produced in such a natural way as white tea. In traditional Chinese medicine, white tea is considered one of the oldest remedies.

This fragrance is so clear, so pure, so wonderfully delicate. It invites me to dream. Dreams of a vacation by the sea with fine, warm breezes that gently caress me, lull me, and give me inner contentment and serenity. I feel refreshed in its softest form, for despite its pure freshness, it is a warming scent, likely due to the pleasant spiciness of tarragon and pepper.

White tea originally comes from China and is characterized by the fact that the fermentation, which influences the aroma, is interrupted shortly after harvesting. This gives the tea leaves a lighter, whitish appearance, and the high-quality tea remains bright and clear, with a mild, rounded taste.

Lancôme's "Trésor" is a classic - one of these powerful florals created by the great Sophia Grojsman in 1990, a peachy rose on a woody and vanillic base with a strong sillage. The latest flanker called "Eau de parfum Lumineuse" has no sillage at all. It stays very close to the skin. All I get out of it is a musky praliné note with some rosy overtones. The advertising blurp on my sample tells me: "a new olfactory signature created by one of the great Fench masters perfumers, as the fresh and delicious imprint of a kiss". The master perfumer is Dominique Ropion - but this is by no means his new masterpiece. Roja Dove once said, "Never believe the advertising of a perfume. It is always a lie." (Would he exclude his own advertising here?). The new "Trésor Luminuese" is no "new olfactory siganture" but an attempt at making "Trésor" more accessible for a younger audience who has been brought up with light, flowery-fruity scents. The praliné note is not in the least new either, it simply adds a gourmandy touch. Perfumers have returned to the "gourmandy rose theme" countless times, but this new attempt is just average. I'd be keen on hearing Sophia Grosjman's opinion on this flanker.

I discovered the original Tresor rather late - but all the more sustainably. In the meantime, many fragrances from the Tresor family have joined, and I was very curious when I discovered Lumineuse. At the first spray, I immediately sensed the family resemblance, but Lumineuse does develop other enchanting nuances. The subtle praline scent captivated me right away - so unobtrusively mild. Accompanied by the gentle Damask rose and alluringly rounded off with violet absolute. This fragrance has a lightness like Grieg's Morning Mood. The spiciness of woods evokes thoughts of a sunrise in a forest clearing, where the air is still clear and cool, and the birds faithfully announce the new day. The light is white and soft, bathing the forest and meadows in pastel colors. While I enjoy wearing Tresor in the evening, Lumineuse is made for the dawning day. It is a mood-enhancing fragrance - the light figure among the Tresor scents.

For a long time, I thought this slightly lighter "Trésor," which stands right next to a big bottle of the original (belonging to my girlfriend), was just a smaller version of it. Until I tested both extensively, wore them, and placed them side by side, and could clearly sniff out - this is a new, completely different version, a flanker! Bam, read under the bottle: "L'Eau de Parfum Lumineuse"... It's not so easy to distinguish these many "Trésors," especially without the packaging... "Trésor Lumineuse," as I want to call it for short, remains true to its mother scent but introduces new facets, finesse, and colors. The base still features a delicate hint of musk and vanilla, but the forefront has been clearly adapted to modern times, sweetened and presented in a crisper, livelier way. The roses come across as more green than red, blooming on a damp, chilly meadow in the sunshine. Additionally, there is a woody, praline-like fruitiness in lilac tones and definitely a few more (synthetic) prickly thorns than before. You have to like that; it makes this "Trésor" less cuddly, but more agile, sprightly, younger, more naive, and youthful. Also a bit more transparent and sparkling, fitting the name. I almost like it more than its predecessor and flagship. It has a cheeky sparkle in its face yet wears an evening gown. Perhaps nothing underneath. And it invites you to take a closer look at the many other little Tresors... Bottle: just as beautiful and shiny as the original! Longevity: just as long-lasting and effective as the original - 8-9 hours! Sillage: a bit softer and lighter than the original. Conclusion: a great facelift for "Trésor" without completely losing the character and soul of the original. Very elegant yet everyday enough. Shiny, indeed.

Tresor lumineuse came to me as a gift from a friend who used it but found it too sweet and heavy. The original Tresor can be sensed, if you know it, in the spicy expression of its notes. Tresor l. is soft, heavy, sweet gourmand. So in that part, it is the opposite of its big sister. I smell fruity notes in the tart radiance of blackcurrant. Floral notes of rose and violet resonate as well. However, it is the praline in the top note and the vanilla in the heart note that set the tone; together they provide sweetness, while musk and woods give the spice to this sweetness. The scent is heavy, almost a bit cloying, more suited for autumn and winter and for the evening. It is only office-appropriate if well dosed. Sillage is strong. The bottle is like the original Tresor. I don’t find it bad, but I fear that its heavy sweetness might get on my nerves over time, just as it can quickly happen with LVEB. But I need to finish the gifted bottle as well. I don’t actually think it’s bad.

Just sprayed it on and initially thought: oh, this doesn’t smell as nice as it did when I sniffed the bottle earlier. So I was a bit disappointed at first. The scent had something that bothered me a little. Now, after about 30 minutes, it actually smells quite good again and stands out positively to me. A mix of powdery and "freshly washed" meets vanilla and "woody" notes, along with a light sweetness mixed with flowers (roses). So in the end, I actually like it quite a bit. What annoys me a bit about the Tresor perfumes is that it's hard to distinguish which one you have if, for example, you received it as a gift or want to repurchase it after a long time. With this model, for instance, there is already some confusion if you’re not deeply into the subject. My wish would be to clearly label the name or to design the bottle a bit differently.

Every day a different scent, depending on my mood and feelings, that's how I've been doing it for a long time. What you can evoke with that! I love the sharpness found in the blackcurrant, the delicious warmth that the praline brings, and the overall sensation that shifts so comfortably, appearing and disappearing like Lancome can do.

What is there not to like about Bvlgari pour Femme? This fragrance is pure elegance, perfection and class. Appropriate for any occasion or season, you'll feel instantly feminine and beautiful when wearing this glorious fragrance. Bvlgari pour Femme opens with a fresh and clean bouquet of flowers with subtle citrusy undertones brought about by the bergamot and orange blossom. This scent is mostly floral from beginning to end, fresh and pretty carnation, violet, iris, jasmine, rose and lily-of-the-valley. Slightly powdery in the drydown yet somewhat rich and woodsy, this fragrance concludes beautifully. The lasting strength was wonderful in my opinion. Although Bvlgari pour Femme isn't entirely unique, there is something very sensual and expensive about it which should appeal to those that seek a sophisticated and distinguished fragrance.

There are two version of Bvlgari pour Femme one is Eau de Parfum and thr other one is Eau de Toilette. However They both great and classic but there is some differences in the smell. If you love the intense Violet try the EDP version, and if you do not like violet to be intense, it is better to try the EDT version. Bvlgari pour Femme EDP is one of the best Bvlgari perfumes for Ladies :)

BVLGARI POUR FEMME edp is one of only a few perfumes which I wore in the twentieth century and still wear today. It seems not to have changed. I've drained a few bottles and my current supply, a back-up 100 ml purchased pre-Y2K, holds a scent very similar to the small purse spray which I received in December 2012. So that's good news: no reformulation appears to have taken place, and that is probably why I am still wearing this creation even though nearly everything else from the 1990s is history. I mean literally a part of my perfume history, like old friends from the past whom I have no intention of meeting up with again. This creation by Sophia Grojsman has not grown dated or uncomfortable since it was launched nearly two decades ago. Every bit as appropriate as it was back at the time of its launch, BVLGARI POUR FEMME is a sweet violet rose composition similar in some ways to both L'Artisan Parfumeur DROLE DE ROSE and Miller Harris COEUR DE FLEUR. They are all united by their violet-tinged, water-washed rose. The big distinction made by the Bvlgari violet rose is that there is a substantial clean musky base which imparts a decidedly perfumey quality to the composition as a whole. It smells almost resinous to me, and in addition to making BVLGARI POUR FEMME seem more like an elixir than a watery sweet floral, it also adds a kind of golden shimmer. More formal than both DROLE DE ROSE and COEUR DE FLEURS, BVLGARI POUR FEMME is also very distinct from Frédéric Malle LIPSTICK ROSE, yet another fine violet rose creation. The Bvlgari perfume, apparently the first in its olfactory neighborhood--and another iconic idea generated by the great Grojsman--strikes a balance between formality and informality. Wearing this perfume is like getting all dressed up in satin pajamas to spend the night at home.

This fragrance should come in a bottle shaped like a powder puff. It's feminine and pretty, and the dry down is one you want to linger on your clothes. The violets add the powder, and the rose is just enough sweet kisses before bedtime, before your kind mother shuts the lights and wishes you sweet dreams. POUR FEMME is exactly that, for a lady.

This is a very feminine fragrance. Not my favourite but I acknowledge the work of Grojsman and Lorson - particularly Grojsman usually knows what she is doing. She is the nose behind Organza, Paris, and Tresor, so kudos to her. However, this fragrance just never catches my attention. The opening is fresh and very fruity like the bergamot and orange blossom opening usually are. Lovely, but to me in this fragrance, a bit too much; somehow cloying. When the first notes disappear the scent becomes way more calm, especially the mimosa in this one is so beautiful and delicious. Luckily, this stays for several hours and becomes a lovely yet very subtle companion. To me a bit too subtle. I simply forget, I am wearing it. The base is nice, lovely notes that I know, but again way too subtle. I am not saying that I love to reek of the fragrance I am wearing but I feel anosmic when wearing this. The bottle is lovely, very feminine and heavy. I have the 100ml and it feels great in my hand. 41/365

I never could vibe with this perfume. It's never been something I'd ever choose for myself, it was a gift from a needy guy who was way too nice and way too boring. So, I had to accept it with grace and even try to tolerate wearing it a few times. Barely tolerable fragrance to my nose. There's just way too much stuffed in here.

There are days, and days. His started well, mine too. Days before, I had rummaged through my box to see what else there was to discover. There was a small sample, with a residue that was almost dried up. All my pleading, my upside-down sample maneuvering, my come-on-don't-be-like-that didn't help at all. The rest just wouldn't cooperate as I wanted it to.

Bvlgari - many may not warm up to this brand here. For me, however, it is one of my favorite brands. I know almost all of the men's fragrances, but only a few of the women's. Those I know all have something special. Jasmin Noir, the entire Omnia range... and also this one. With over 20 years under its belt, this one is actually already considered a classic.

A few years ago, my then-boss invited the entire office to dinner at a Lebanese restaurant in the old town. There was a good reason to celebrate; he had been appointed the second managing director. We sat down at a beautifully set table with about 15 people.

Do you remember? Long ago there was a place, that no stranger ever saw, that no word ever named. Where the fairies go to dance, moonlight flows silver, diamond dust in the grass shoots like lightning cascades. You and I alone saw it, just for a glimpse, chosen by Oberon - incomparable luck! Alas! The moment passed. The sun gleams in the room.

The initial cloud is gigantic and, for a lack of a better word, oppressive. For the first few hours you will be able to smell the wearer before you enter the room and see them. Very straightforward, just as synthetic. Rose flavored shower gel, but dialed up to eleven. Still, at this point it's not too bad. Just meh. But don't worry, it gets worse. After the first ~2 hours woodiness starts peeking through from underneath the rose veil. It's subtle at first, slowly transforming the rose shower gel into rose air freshener. Not great, not terrible. Around the ~3rd hour mark sillage becomes a bit softer – it still envelops the wearer in a cloud, but only becomes apparent an arm's-length away from them. Meanwhile, as rose mellows out, the overall scent continues getting worse. It's faint at first. Something is wrong, but it's hard to put the feeling into words. You are ~4 hours in. As rose continues mixing in with the wood, the unpleasant undertone becomes more apparent. A lightbulb moment happens about ~5 hours in. Cat piss. Aggressive artificial rose flavor still hides it quite well, but it's now undeniable. Somewhere in a corner where you usually wouldn't think to look – a cat flavored puddle is seeping into the floorboards. The soaked floorboards flavor becomes more and more apparent as time goes on. Around ~6 hours in it becomes the main note, pushing rose to the sidelines. Luckily, around the same time it finally settles close to the skin. ~7 hours in – it's the only thing you can think of when you accidentally put your hands too close to your face. I scrubbed it off in a shower and breathed out a sigh of relief ~8 hours in. Will probably avoid Lancôme for a while after this.

opens with an intense rose and slightly tart green apple, juicy and floral, with a very gentle woods nestled in the base. that is, unfortunately, all that it seems to present. that simplicity, however, is beautifully crafted, but leaves much to be desired. as it sits it gets progressively smoother, more cream-like it is enormously strong, while typing this up i can smell it as if it was still next to my nose.

I got a free 1.2ml tester of Idole Power and it's grown on me a lot. I didn't have high expectations after testing Idole Nectar due to the popcorn note and slightly cloying roses. However, I'll never turn down a free fragrance tester. I tend to love any fruity/floral fragrance and this was no exception. The tartness of the apple balances the sickening sweetness of the signature Lancome Rose that I often struggle with. Together, the apple and rose make for a bright and fresh initial spay. After a few minutes, you're finally grounded with the sandalwood. I really enjoy this scent, but it is almost too strong for me. Usually when I spray on my neck or chest, I go nose-blind after an hour or so, but this scent lingers and tickles your nose for HOURS. I've been sneezing but at least I smell good. This scent feels a little bit mature (maybe for the late 20s early 30s age group) than what I'm used to, but I can definitely see myself purchasing a small size of this in the future. I can't imagine finishing a full size bottle of this since a little goes SUCH a long way. It's a really lovely scent, and my favorite from the Idole line so far.

When I hear the name of Bvlgari, what come to my mind is class, elegance and quality. Though my relation with their fragrances never passed the stage of one spray at the store counters, this scent surprised me rather pleasantly. First of all let me state that I don't dislike their perfumes, they are wearable and elegant yet they miss to make me crave them. So when I had in my hands the bottle of Mon Jasmin Noir I was rather sceptic, I was expecting another jasmin white floral to be honestm and the nougat tone was troubling my mind a little as I am not the biggest fan of confectionary notes. The initial spray was very pleasant, sweet citruses embrace you with the pretty smell of the lilly of the valley, ultimately girly, after that it becomes a floral musky scent on me, very nice and airy, with a hint of saltiness, I cant figure out where I get that from, may be it is the musk combined with the nougat. As for the nougat, I wouldn't say it is dominant, it is there but not in your face, not sickeningly sweet. In a way it reminds me little girls who sneak and wear their mommies' shoes and put their make up on. Girly and elegant with a hint of child. All in all, I can't hide that I enjoy wearing this fragrance when it is cold and sunny outside and I am wearing a dress, it just feels right and pretty. Last but not least the classic bottle with the adorable cute bow is to die for.

I adore most Bvlgari scents, they are all pretty bottles full of quality ingredients and enchanting fragrances. However: not all scents compliment every nose and/or chemistry. And Bvlgari is no exception. (alas) To my nose Mon Jasmine Noir is the little less sophisticated sister of Jasmine Noir (in the black bottle) MJN is lighter, breezier and with a fleeting character and less sex-appeal. Now, I can't deny that she's pretty! She is. She has that wonderful jasmine note that we like, a hint of nougat and even a far cry of patchouli. But whereas her big sister JN is a sexy seductress that leaves no doubt about her intentions and that she is sensual and long lasting. MJN is more 'shy', and eager to leave rather than to stay and to seduce. To me, MJN is for people who would like a lighter more office friendly version of JM - and don't mind refreshing it a couple of times. (the silage is wonderful be it far less noticeable to JM -- but the longevity is a bit short) Bvlgari scents are not the cheapest, and for the price & the -usual- Bvlgari quality, I am somewhat disappointed about the shy and fleeting nature of this scent? But, perhaps my nose gets too quickly used to it? My best advice? Try this one on your skin and let your nose and chemistry tell you if it's worth the price-tag since I am not sure if my nose gets too used to it too quickly -- It has happened to me before that I couldn't smell scents very quickly after application anymore, yet others could. Since I wear fragrances for MY pleasure far more than for others. I dislike scents that don't give me a whiff of: "Hello! I am still here!" now and again throughout the day. So I have to say, this one is not for me. Better luck to you : )

I am enjoying Mon Jasmin Noir far better than the original Jasmin Noir. It's soft and refined in a polite manner, that is inoffensive but perhaps a little too discreet, at least in my opinion. It's not necessarily fresh like I thought it would be, instead there tends to be more white floral accords, particularly that of the lily of the valley. The jasmine is quite pretty in this composition, reminding one of an old-fashioned tea party taking place upon the immaculate lawn of a period-style mansion. It's a delicate, somewhat vibrant fragrance with citrusy undertones and a rich, earthy patchouli base. Pleasant, but not all that unusual. I am slightly turned off by the clean bathroom feeling that this fragrance seems to remind me of. Not that a clean sensation is a bad thing, it's just not my cup of tea. The sillage is rather intimate, with the lasting strength being surprisingly good. It's perhaps not as gothic or sexy as Jasmin Noir was perceived to be, however this lighter reincarnation is enjoyable nevertheless, and a far deal more wearable in my opinion.

Mon Jasmin Noir Smells best when it's hot. The jasmine then smells delicious and gets a touch in my nose every time I move. Really amazing. So many compliments with this smell and for me a scent I bought many times. Recommended.

With Bvlgari you never know what you are going to get… I have five of their perfumes and they all seem to surprise me. Especially the BLV Notte is a really interesting scent, but I especially like their bottle designs. The Jasmine Noir is a really likeable scent. It starts with the delicious citron note, not to be confused with lemon, that gives the lily of the valley a new and refreshing expression. I love the way it keeps going, and after half an hour I start wondering if the scent will ever reach the heart. It does, eventually, losing the citric freshness and developing a way more Jasmin-y vibe. Beautiful but I like the opening better. It goes on for a few hours and then something new happens. The nougat note makes the base really interesting. I love the woody notes but the nougat makes me want to eat the scent. So deliciously smelling. It does not last for long, unfortunately, and I must admit, that after such a great start it is a bit disappointing. But Polge and Labbé have done something interesting here, I think. The bottle is shaped like other Bvlgari fragrances such as Bvlgari pour Femme and Rose Essentielle. It is a likeable design with a cute detail, the black ribbon with golde n tag. It suits the fragrance, and I think it gives it an exclusive look. 40/365

Do you know the commercials with Kirsten Dunst for this perfume? Here is the film from YouTube with the lion. But there is also a second one, without a lion, which I always refer to as the "Fog Film." I find both very beautiful and especially very fitting, very elegant. The music feels very melancholic to me, it almost brings me to tears, I don't even know why.

I unfortunately have two clear opinions about Mon Jasmin Noir. Of course, they are incompatible, how else could it be? I am a novice when it comes to fragrances. Mon Jasmin Noir was the first of its kind that came under my nose. On a Kleenex - the consultant used this instead of test strips. I was blown away.

Good evening folks (that means Good Evening, you ignorant ones!) :D I really don't need to write much about why I'm here, I mean, you know that whenever I show up, there's always a new comment from me, right? Or do you not know me that well? Hey, I've been rambling here for years and the only thing that sticks with you are my dirty fantasies when I write about ladies again.

Actually, I wanted to test Mon Jasmin Noir together with the regular Jasmin Noir, of which I should also have a sample at home. But since I must have misplaced it somehow & couldn't pack it in my work bag, today it was only Mon Jasmin Noir. Since both are said to be hardly similar, this circumstance is probably not too tragic.

At the moment, there isn't much to laugh about. Parents are becoming frail, and even in the circle of friends, the topics of "back" and "knees" are being discussed. Instead of comics, pharmacy magazines are circulating, and instead of hot phone numbers, people exchange the addresses of good physiotherapists.

This house of Lancôme is absolutely amazing and offers great fragrances, especially, in the Private Collection. Very underrated and only known for Ôud Bôuquet, which is great, too. This one is very alluring yet creative. A Patchouli that doesn't smell like a pure Patchouli, at least is not very powerful. The Sage dominates the first 4-5h. Is fresh, clean and aromatic. A note that isn't very common in the front of a fragrance but more in the background giving an aromatic nuance. In this case, is very prominent yet pleasing. Gives this almost clean bathroom vibe but, along with the other notes, has a sweet and elegant vibe. The drydown has a sweet patchouli borrowed from Coromandel which is quite awesome. The result is refined, very alluring and pleasing for everybody. You'll be noticed for sure and everybody will compliment you. It's easy to wear yet distinctive, with great longevity (12h+) and heavy projection and sillage for the first 4-5h. The only con is the fact that the fragrance is quite linear but, for a night time situation, fits very well. A great fragrance made for both genders and with excellent quality. Recommended! 4/5

So now the new Maison de Lancome Patchouli Aromatique is in the house. Super fast from Douglas for a quite acceptable price. Since then, I’ve been sniffing at my wrist. It’s very hard for me to describe it! According to the description, there are only three fragrance notes. Patchouli, vetiver, and sage. Quite puristic. P.A. is very modest, calm, charming, genuine! With the first spray, the patchouli immediately comes to the forefront; I only know sage from cooking in the kitchen. And I love it with chicken, in herb butter, and in saltimbocca or even in candies. I even bought a little bag of sage to be able to describe the scent. The scent of the leaves is very fresh and citrusy. I only catch that at the very beginning. Patchouli and vetiver blend well together. A bit mossy, woody, resinous. Even after showering, I can still smell P.A. On me, the scent lasts about 6 hours. The bottle is rectangular, and the golden paper cut makes it look expensive and elegant. All in all, despite the name, the patchouli remains charmingly elegant in the background. I like it!

The title says it all. The grapefruit up top is gen-u-ine. Bright, zesty and delicious. Then you get that trademark Bvlgari sophistication from a mass of pleasing notes (cactus? Wha?). But after that, it settles into a nice, spicy vetiver (from the cardamom) with just a hint of wood and amber to smooth it out. It's NOT heavy, nor does it scream. It's just a perfect businessman's everyday - sophisticated, pleasing and uplifting - like a big boy's ADG. No surprise, since Morillas created both. Out of the entire Bvlgari line, I consider this to be the best and safest freshie - Amara, if you want some incense - and Man in Black for evening wear. That's a winning trio. But give this one a try if you enjoy citrus or vetiver.

its not same as bvlgari man at all . very sharp and clean , citrus woody spicy notes. great longevity and sillage is good too. i can use it in spring , summer , fall and winter. its a good fragrance with a fair price i like it .

This is a gorgeous scent by master perfumer Alberto Morillas. It opens fresh and citrusy and evolves into a woodier scent. That being said it performs as awful as other Morillas’ fragrances like D&G LB. This is a great example of companies where the marketing team is not in the same page as the perfumer since there is nothing extreme about this scent unless marketing was going for ‘extremely disapponting performance’. Fragrance is great for whatever long it lasts

It is an excellent fragrance with Cactus note , Fresh, Clean, Elegant and Unique. If you like a fresh citrusy perfume with Unique note, you will like this one. It opens up with like fresh citrusy , cactus note , spicy and floral notes in the background then dry down is green woody. This is perfect for the spring and summer. Longevity is average. I really enjoy it and I like Bvlgari Man Extreme EDT . Thumbs Up. Rating : 8 / 10

A very nice summer scent in the vein of Versace Man eau Fraiche, but with much more power on the zesty grape and bergamot side and sweet starfruit quickly followed by a background layering of vetiver. The opening is REALLY great and super fresh, simply made for that hot summer day. Still, I'm finding it ironic that this is called extreme as longevity isn't very extreme, it lasts only a good three hours on me. If you're into the fresh citrus/bergamot colognes of the Acqua di Parma line but can't quite afford them, this is a very decent alternative.

Bvlgari is a fragrance house I have some issues with. It is not that they make terrible fragrances, but for the majority of them, they do not last on my skin. Extreme Man which there is nothing extreme here is a fresh grapefruit, woody, slightly peppery addition to the many fragrances done in this composition.

This lighter and sportier version of Bvlgari Man, has the same DNA but in a different way, a light, refreshing summer fragrance excellence that everyone accepts easily. A very wonderful scent mixed with extreme professionalism, when you wear this perfume, you will feel refreshed and ready for life's adventures. Suitable for youthful and young men and in the summer at most.

Bulgari has long been a rather elusive brand for me, but when I tested a few perfumes, a nice line and a Bulgari DNA quickly revealed themselves. Fresh, wet, noble, luxurious, understated. Bulgari Man was really good in terms of scent, but one of the loudest fragrances I know; the statistics like longevity and especially sillage were catastrophic and ruined the rating.

I like fresh scents, sometimes even very much. They are wonderfully unobtrusive, giving me a feeling of ultimate grooming, attractiveness, and effortless charisma. Their only downside: they are largely interchangeable. Wanting to stand out from the crowd - partly from cheap imitations as well - is a high demand.
Bulgari is also one of those brands that hasn't really impressed me in terms of perfume so far. It somehow feels too watery, weak, interchangeable, and insignificant.

This is much more of a rose than a magnolia scent. It smells very "pink" to me, at first sight it seems like a typical mainstream designer rose, maybe with some peony and red fruits or berries. There seem to be two notes lists for this floating around, one is the reduced form from the packaging that Parfumo uses (rose, magnolia and white musk), and the other contains some more notes like saffron and suede! I definitely get saffron here, it adds a medicinal bitterness that takes the scent out of the completely girly and pretty territory. It's a little heavier and warmer than it seems. And the magnolia? It becomes somewhat noticeable in the drydown as a hint of slightly creamy and slightly watery floral freshness, but it really isn't the main star here. All in all this is a nice perfume, but it doesn't wow me, especially not in comparison with the Maison Lancôme scents that came a few years before (Oud Bouquet, Lavandes Trianon etc.).

Tested at printemps shop this week. I was worry cause i dislike magnolia. Finally it s was a good surprise. A good and different rose from others fragrances in this style.i can feel there a lot a work to create this elegant rosely fragrance. I will buy for my wife its sure. More for spring cause the hold is weak around 3 hours. The bottle is really wonderful A few known but it disserves more

I owned Omnia before I knew anything about gourmand fragrances. The reason I bought it? Quite simply, I liked it. When the SAs at Sephora encouraged me to try Aquolina Pink Sugar, I recoiled on first sniff but I also was intrigued by the sweetness, which was unlike any perfume that I had worn before. So I did my own research, and I ended up with Bvlgari Omnia ... and Escada Magnetism. I've since emptied a bottle of each, and I replaced the Omnia, not the Magnetism. Omnia's chocolate, coffee, almond, spices, and vanilla are all very well blended. It's sweet, but it's not Pink Sugar. It is a spiced fragrance, but more like a well-mannered chai with almond milk than a classic oriental. A smooth white chocolate is there but it doesn't dominate. This is a gourmand for adults who prefer local coffee & tea houses to Starbucks but also aren't pretentious or cliquish in their patronage. It's a unique, accessible ragrance that could also be worn by men. Although I have added many gourmands to my collection since those first 2 bottles, when I want a gourmand and I don't know which one, I reach for Omnia. I love Omnia, and it loves me back. Thank you, Alberto Morillas.

While I had been anticipating to try this frag I was let down twice. First the bottle is shall we say different, & while it is appealing the container itself is plastic. It would have been better if it were glass. Second, I am VERY dissapointed with the longevity of this scent. While it is very nice, & the white chocolate is very smooth, it is somewhat spicy & a little floral. It should be an EDT! As this does not last more than 4 hours on me. Such a waste for a nice fragrance. This gets a neutral from me, more so on the negative side due to the lack of longevity given its suppose to be an EDP!

The one gourmand that I adore all autumn/winter long. I love coffee and chocolate, in fact all the ingredients are to my 'taste' in one way or another! It's a yummy, spicy, sensual and unusual scent. A bold character and must be tested before purchase, but, hmmmm if you like it you might get addicted. A cozy hug in a gorgeous bottle. It smells like the best aromas in 'Cafe de Flore' in Paris *memories* The silage is: "yummy, I smell wonderful" and the longevity is great. A warm and unusual treat for those cold days.

I seem to be having a woody season—probably the only logical answer to the dry, brittle cold wave we're having. Either that or none of the gourmand-y stuff registers with my nose. I didn't even know "white chocolate" has a smell! Omnia gets softer and softer as it develops, never imposing, never harsh. Just *there*, not shouting to get noticed, standing with her head held high. I just keep sniffing the back of my hand for that lovely creamy sandalwood. This is not the raw wood of Santal 33; this is creamy, powdery, a tad sweet yet not too dry, and just fresh enough to be friendly to the casual sniffer. I'm betting its beauty is the reason why it was discontinued as Mysore sandalwood is now endangered and prohibitively expensive for use in middle-market mainstream fragrance. When I find a bottle, I'll buy it, and hope it passes the family and friends test because this is going to be on me for a while. If you wanted a woody, spicy yet soft oriental, you could have done a lot worse.

My first impressions of Omnia was that it was a lot lighter than I expected and probably not as rich and spicy as I had hoped. However with that being said, I am not disappointed by this fragrance in the least. It's very unique and quite modern. Although this is a predominantly foody fragrance with strong notes of coffee, chai, chocolate, spices and nuts, don't assume that this is a gourmand. Surprisingly Omnia tends to be quite woodsy and the lack of sweetness makes this scent quite masculine, especially in the opening. Omnia is a rather dark fragrance and strangely sexy too, however it is not your typical sexy, it has more of a mysterious aura. I'm not usually a coffee lover, however in this fragrance the added spices make the scent somewhat exotic and unusual. I can certainly see this fragrance adapting well to both men and women. It is unfortunate that they have discontinued this fragrance in my country because I feel that unique scents like these should be more readily available. I must say that although I like this fragrance's subtlety, the lasting power did let me down. Perhaps layering this fragrance with a matching lotion would help with the longevity.

Walking through a woodland, wet and mossy underneath, brushing cardamom leaves aside, hint of ginger and spices. Earthy and woody and softly, gently spicy, wet woodland becomes whispering dry. not sweet (except for the cinnamon) or floral. Very close to the skin. Yeah, good thing you didn't tell anyone about it 'cause it's already gone.

Powdery, oriental, full of spices! Saffron combined with cardamom and ginger give a bitter spicy texture at first . A few minutes later, changes to a sweet combination of almond, chocolate and woods ... I do not know exactly what it is, but the flavor has a strong character but powdery and simultaneously emits a woody, slightly spicy aroma.

Coconut! It really surprises me that coconut is not listed in the notes. I was expecting so much more from this. With all the notes listed I was expecting maybe a boom, bam, pow! Oh well, it's pleasant enough...just not impressive. Here's what I get: creamy coconut, lightly spiced, slightly edible. But, wait, where did it go? Ah well, it's nice, just not for me.
Lovely Scent! I receive a lot of incense. Green oriental maybe? I do not smell most of the notes they have listed. Unfortunately It only lasts a couple hours on me.

This is a really successful fragrance. The list of notes is long, and a lot of the notes are spices, that I appreciate. I love cardamom, and finding it in the top is really pleasing. It starts the scent with power and sweetness. The ginger note makes it even better. What a beginning! Then in the heart I notice almond, cinnamon and nutmeg.

Tea scents have been experiencing a hype wave for quite some time now and are on everyone's lips, just look at Imagination for example. This is not surprising, as they are usually unobtrusive, pleasant, and a good option in any weather. I also really like them and have had a few in my collection. Therefore, I am quite astonished that no one is talking about Jasmin d'Eau, as there is a true gem hidden here. I was recently in Dubai and had a vague recollection that Lancome might discontinue this line or has already done so. Some made it onto my watchlist anyway because I feel that Dubai is always a bit behind when it comes to new releases and discontinuations. And indeed, I was lucky enough to test and buy Jasmin d'Eau at the more inconspicuous Dubai airport. The fragrance starts off very zesty; I look at the notes and am surprised to find no lemon/bergamot or similar, but only a bergamot tea. If this brings such authentic zestiness, I am already impressed at this point. This sharp zestiness is then accompanied by the elegance of jasmine. This is not an overwhelming jasmine, but a very delicate, balanced, and somehow transparent jasmine for me. Even people who might not usually gravitate towards jasmine should give this a try, as I have not smelled one like this before. A slightly fruity note is also noticeable. The notes indicate that it is peach. While this is often overly present in fragrance notes and somewhat shampoo-like, here it is just as delicate, balanced, elegant, and unobtrusive as the other notes. Above all, the tea note holds its protective hand. And I really feel that this is not just any 0815 tea note but something special. I find the longevity to be great for a tea scent; I get through the day well and can always smell it around me. I have had worse candidates. The sillage is appropriate for the character of the fragrance, noticeable but not overwhelming. I don't know what this treasure originally cost or if it is still available. But anyone who has the opportunity and is inclined towards tea scents should definitely test Jasmin d'Eau.

I am really indifferent to this one. The grapefruit note overpowers everything else on my skin. I like grapefruit, but am not a fan of it as a dominant note... Longevity is pretty good, and sillage is average. Pretty much an average scent that is not bad, but so forgettable like many others. Not recommended, unless you find it super-inexpensive, and love smelling like a giant grapefruit. 2.5 to 3 stars out of 5.

I dunno but the first time I smelled this, I got a 90's formal business man in a suit on a bright early morning. He could also be in Finance, Accounting or a Mathematics lecturer. This scent has a very potent green tea mixed with some grapefruit which makes the opening very intense and green. As the scent develops, I get an oakmoss accord similar to the one present in Azzaro Chrome EDT and Creed Aventus. I was hoping that it wouldn't turn into CREED Aventus because I wasn't a fan of it surprisingly, but as I continued wearing this scent, it grew on me and I liked it (although I almost returned it). If you love 90's scents like Silver Mountain Water, Chrome by Azzaro EDT and the likes with a dash of green tea, you will most definitely enjoy this. I could tell that this was Jacques Cavalier's style as Pacific Chill has a slight resemblance to this for a few minutes. I actually wore the two scents together and I really enjoyed. I would love to try it out with Silver Mountain Water next.

The first ever fragrance that blew my mind, how could anything smell so good!? This is a nice and classic scent that is refreshing and calming. You have tea and musk in the notes which is blended perfectly. I still own a bottle and get compliments now and then. Definitely a must own for any serious fragrance collector!

What now? No comments? Still nothing? Well then, I’ll finally dare to introduce you to my secret tip. "Bvlgari pour Homme Extrême" is for me an adult, extravagant, and oriental unisex fragrance. It starts fresh, cool, and very classic. At first, it has something of cologne. It unfolds in an incomparably ethereal and very intense way. The balsam fir is very dominant here, and for my part, I also smell a fresh bouquet of basil. The scent feels very Mediterranean; it smells of nature, forest floor, and noble woods. It clears the mind and is not heavy despite its intensity and is consistently unsweet. As the fragrance develops, it only becomes a little warmer and woodier; the ethereal aspect recedes into the background but remains until the end. The longevity is above average. In short: An "Acqua di Parma" by Night. To me, the fragrance has a simultaneously cool and extremely attractive impression, making it suitable for mysterious seducers. I would most closely compare its effect to candidates like "Égoïste" or "Black Orchid" and "Boudoir," even though it doesn't really resemble them. It is warm and cold at the same time. Balsamic, gentle, yet somehow strong, dangerous, and dominant. Very stylish. In any case, this fragrance demands a character with its own style and a strong self-confidence. It is not an old man's scent; on the contrary: The soft accords make it quite wearable for women and younger men as well. Nevertheless, it requires a certain maturity and presence. At least, I wouldn’t buy this scent for just anyone. Very "hip" types would likely make themselves look ridiculous with such a perfume. I find it extremely attractive and erotic, especially because of its coolness. It’s for seducers and seductresses; for gentlemen and divas - not for pick-up artists and machos.

I only moderately liked the original, found Soir unnecessary, and online there are even more opinions suggesting that the original is the best of the three. Additionally, there are only 2 comments here, both very complimentary and from women. But despite everything, something drew me to Bvlgari Pour Homme Extreme. It probably wasn't the price, as my 50 ml bottle wasn't extremely cheap. The bottle was more so, but that's what you expect from Bvlgari, such sparkling pure beauty. Some fragrances just have an aura, an attraction, out of nowhere. In the back of my mind, I had the lovely tea note of the original, which fits all three well in spring, and Extreme was supposed to be the most bitter, woody, and masculine version. However, it was also mentioned that the citrus note was simply intensified and that it comes across as more generic. Complicating my decision was the fact that I hadn't smelled the original in a long time and that both are said to be very similar. It was high time to shed some light on the darkness and take the risk myself. Since I didn't make a direct comparison, I will focus more on the perfume itself rather than the comparison with its predecessors or relatives. But from memory, the original seems very similar, a bit more transparent and less bitter-woody. The spice and seriousness have been turned up, while the citrus is less pronounced. Extreme is much darker, more suitable for autumn. Still a good office scent and Cartier understatement. An invisible piece of jewelry, after all. Extreme is an extreme natural scent, actually subtle but a nose-teaser up close. Tree bark, cold wind, earthy tea, and a splash of citrus fruits come across as cool, composed, and almost dominant. However, the environment perceives it less, only during testing and when the nose is directly on the wrist does one notice the gray bitterness, the rough diamond wind that blows. Almost as hardcore as in the original, the musk here also allows for a wet feeling similar to Narciso Rodriguez and spreads a bit of an animalistic flair. The pepper tickles, the musk delivers, the citrus opens, the woods underlie, the tea calms. A thoughtful blend, elegant and from a luxurious house. The scent often reminds one of a hot tea in an autumn storm outside in nature. After showering, the high musk content can be somewhat off-putting and smells like a wet dog. Bottle: like a piece of jewelry. Sillage: strongest Bvlgari PH, yet still mediocre. Wearability: 6-7 hours is not a full workday. I believe it was the right decision, as I like the more masculine Extreme more than the original or Soir, both of which I should remind myself of now that I am getting to know Extreme inside and out. The first wearing attempts were already friendly to cheerfully serious. Which one do you prefer? Where do the differences lie?

Happy New Year, dear community! It's time for a new comment and especially for a new comment on this extraordinary crowd pleaser that not everyone wears. Dear JoHannes, your blog “Mann Mann Mann - Männer Männer Männer” speaks to my soul in many ways. And I hope I was allowed to use a quote from your blog for my title.

It's morning, five o'clock. He comes home after spending the night drinking and smoking at the club and throws a peppermint in his mouth on the way home so it doesn't smell too bad. That's Bulgari Extreme for me, and I love the scent. Initially, I could only smell it on my colleague, but I couldn't help myself and got it for myself as well.

Shortly after its release, I received "Bulgari pour Homme" in the regular version as a gift from my then-girlfriend. It was my first encounter with the brand at all. To this day, I practically always have a bottle of this fragrance on my shelf because it possesses a unique fresh aura in my nose.

After years of reading along and gathering impressions, I finally mustered the courage to philosophize about one of my absolute favorites. Unfortunately, it's for a sad reason, as the last remaining specimens are soon to be gone and will only be available at horrendous prices. Out of pure nostalgia, I have decided to pay this price nonetheless.

I was really NOT looking for a new fragrance. I was on a flight to Beijing from Dubai. Emirates Business Class, toiletry bag, the finest life, and then… BOOM! This little 10ml bottle was inside, next to various mini BVLGARI items. I smell it and immediately get the feeling: Fresh shirts, polished shoes, perfect hairline, even though I had a Sunday hairstyle.

when I first rolled this onto my skin, I got a hint of vanilla, but then it tuned down to a soft powdery and slightly citrusy magnolia scent, which I really like. also you can’t really smell it unless you get really close to the skin..

The only reason this fragrance isn’t stealing the show is because its “furball sibling” somehow charms the crowd with its feline antics. But make no mistake, the real alpha of the jungle is Kobraa (with a double "a" for maximum alpha energy). I can appreciate the merits of Tygar, and I tip my hat to its clone, Turathi Blue (shoutout to Afnan for that "gem"). Still, Kobraa operates on a whole different level. Sure, the scent profile is relatively simple, but its genius lies in making a notoriously tricky note - frankincense - surprisingly wearable. Paired with geranium, it achieves a sweet, smoky incense accord that's versatile enough for all seasons. Just remember to dial back the sprays during a heatwave unless you want to fumigate your audience. Performance? Absolutely stellar, 10+ hours. It’s has a good projection, enveloping you in a scent bubble that is equal to Tygar's. Unfortunately, it also mirrors Tygar’s price tag, which, while reflective of its quality, still feels steep. Thankfully, I managed to snag a smaller bottle at a reasonable price, or I’d never have had the pleasure of meeting this hypnotic serpent.

If Interlude Man is the Blue Beast then this should be considered the Green Beast. They both take the same spine of herbal/spice, incense, and oud in different directions. And by god are they both potent! While Interlude is dark and brooding, introducing leather, patchouli, and amber in the base notes as the scent opens up, Kobraa is surprisingly fresh given the note breakdown. As other reviews have stated, there are surely many notes missing from the official pyramid. The peppery-floral geranium top note is joined by some citrus (or maybe it is the lemon-y nuances of the frankincense?) and an herbal note, perhaps coriander or rosemary? I also detect a camphoraceous pine or eucalyptus. Olibanum dominates the heart of the fragrance, but it is not overly smoky like Search . It smells closer to distilled frankincense oil rather than burning olibanum resin, for example in a censer. The incense note is supported by oud, but nothing fecal or animalic. Soft woods, more like a sandalwood or cedar, give the frankincense longevity. And such longevity! You will be smelling this all day if it is applied first thing in the morning. Overall, Kobraa is a very high-quality powerful fresh incense fragrance that makes a statement. This is not a daily wear or dumb reach. Another reviewer said that it "spreads a feeling of aloofness" (translated from the German "verbreitet ein Gefühl von Unnahbarkeit"), and that is a perfect description for it. You wear this scent for yourself and not others. Let them think what they will. A Kobraa doesn't concern himself with the opinions of mice.

I will tell you a little story. I smelled this fragrance for the first time half a year ago and it blew my mind. I have smelled a lot of fragrances but with this one i felt as the first time i smelled interlude, back a few years ago. This one opened my mind and created the need to get a bottle. I spent the next six months trying to get a good offer for a bottle until the opportunity rose a few days ago. Three official notes. Geranium, Franquincense and Oud. Of course this is a lie but oh my god, what a lie. I wish more fragrances lied to me like this one does. This is a picture of a funeral pyre (minus the body) geranium flowers above and below the oud and the incense that burns Dark, seductive, addictive

MOVE LIKE A SNAKE!!!! What an interesting green scent. In a way it kinda smells this a gym where it has that metallic funk and fabuloso cleaning product scent to it But on the other hand it does smell green and a little smoky. Like you’re in safari or forest temple as Laura croft or Jumanji. Not your typical fresh scent, and its pretty versatile too. I definitely like it. Little but of an acquired taste. Fresh but a lil dirty. Nice stuff here

I was hesitant to try this bc I tried most of the Le Gemme line and was very underwhelmed. This is the only one that’s worth trying imo, and it’s the only adventurous one where the rest feel very commercialized. Kobraa reminds me of the sexy snake in the jungle book adaptations. Unfortunate that it doesn’t whisper dirty things in my ears . God that snake is hot. Anway.. Kobraa is elegant, it’s seductive, very serious (it smells almost black - if you’re one of those people that associates perfumes with colour) . A refined and rich smelling heavily spiced incense perfume. I get a lot of citrus and pine resinous notes as well. It also feels very vaguely floral to me - but an earthy floral rather than powdery. It feels quite 'niche' for a Bvlgari perfume, which is a very good thing. Kobraa is brazenly confident without being overbearing, seductive and sensual without being crass. Extremely versatile and will make you stand out in just the right way at work or on a date, I love this stuff. The bottle is absolutely gorgeous too. Compared to something like Interlude and Black Iris, this is much less difficult on the nose. So much so that this is one of my favourite work perfumes. While I do slightly prefer Interlude (og) and Black Iris, because they are so much harder to wear than Kobraa, this is a much safer & more versatile pickup. The performance is good but nothing crazy - it’ll last a full work day which is my personal benchmark. I think a bit of entry level perfume fan glaze has inflated the numbers a bit - the performance isn't anywhere near interlude's, and this is definitely not a good value pickup. Like the rest of Le gemme its extremely overpriced, but it’s an excellent pickup 2nd hand or from a discount seller. Especially if you can find a 30ml :).

My first comment in this community will directly be the first comment for Kobraa. So far, I have never felt such an immediate urge to put my feelings into words and share them with you regarding any fragrance. I enjoy associating scents with character traits, mentally connecting images, memories, places, and situations with a perfume.

......is undoubtedly Margret Rutherford for me. As Miss Marple, she was unbeatable. I loved those black-and-white crime films with stories that were never boring. And she was cool, nothing could rattle her. She was tomboyish, had a cheeky mouth, and was incredibly funny. Agatha Christie didn’t think so, but that didn’t interest any fans of the actress.

Basically, I have never been a fan of incense. Too heavy, too dark, too resinous, too something. Through the nasal tasting of a lovingly sponsored sample (many thanks to Nicole), I had the pleasure, and I mean pleasure, of experiencing the original from Bvlgari. How can I describe the scent experience? Actually, I would say: sauna.

26.10. my birthday. Traditionally one of the few occasions in the year when I treat myself. This year it was two fragrances, both from Bvlgari's Le Gemme line, Tygar and Kobraa. I already knew Tygar, for me the best summer fragrance I have ever smelled, a gift from Nikolaus. Kobraa, on the other hand, was a blind buy.

Well, the Le Gemme - Kobraa completely surprised me. While there aren't many particularly complex aromas to discern, the overall scent is totally harmonious and beautiful! Additionally, the longevity on my skin is fantastic, lasting nearly 24 hours, and I would describe the sillage as very strong.

I asked a member for a sample of this perfume and she graciously sent me some. It was love at first sniff!!! I am enthralled by the beautiful damask rose its very dewy and wet. Then when this gem starts to warm up on my skin the magic begins when the amber and vanilla start to mingle doing a little dance as I say... Then this gorgeous musk appears out of nowhere and I am hooked! I thought I was going to lose my mind if I could'nt find this frangrance... I have searched and searched and with the help of some wonderful friends and networking, I soon will have this incredible bottle of magic for my very own!!! It's so worth having!

Right after its release, I did a rather random scent test. And what can I say: Roses as far as the nose can smell. Beautifully lush and unrestrained. I used up two oval bottles and then turned away from it, as it became too much for me, very prominent, and it also caused slight headaches.

I received this fragrance as a gift from my mother years ago and I miss it dearly. I still had the oval bottle, which was a true delight to hold. The scent is easy to describe: A rose garden on a hot summer day. The top note features small tea roses with a hint of vanilla. Sweet like vanilla ice cream. In the heart note, the classic garden roses are accompanied by a base note of dry earth. After many hours, the base consists of long-stemmed, dark red roses on musk. The evening after a hot summer day, with sweet promises for the night. The fragrance is still noticeable the next morning. Although Mille et une Rose has such a rosy scent, it does not annoy those around you. It is, however, a constant companion throughout the day.

Bulgari lounched the series of "Teas" for quite a long time and I always avoided even trying them because I do not like to smell like tea or coffee or chocolate. Recently I received a sample of Eau Parfumee au The Rouge not in a vial, like all those samples they give you with a purchase, or a small tissue square like the Fragonard samples, but in the size of a small towel. I am not kidding. And since it was a small towel I used it after the shower just to get rid of it. The next second I thought I was smelling Behr paint with primer in the mix. It was as if I went back to the day when, out of curiosity to see if I was able to paint a room all by myself, I did it successfully with that kind of paint. Do not ask me what my thoughts were about Bulgari's Eau Parfumee au The Rouge! And what if this smell of paint lasts for a day like the Behr? Next thing was to run to my Parfumo.net and write an acidic review about it. I even settled for the title: " Not my cup of tea!" How wrong could I have been, my friends and how much the first impression does not always count! In less than five minutes, a beautiful, warm scent was calming me down. The Rooibos tea smell receeded and the sweetness of orange, the freshness of bergamot rounded the composition. Perfection. A scent for cold evenings, for cool mornings, for those days when stress is unbearable. Before the musc settled the foundation, the almond scent came strong and beautiful. Beautiful. Longevity? Good. Unexpectedly good. Sillage? Not so much but I did not care because I wanted to keep it close to my skin and not share it with anybody around. I think this is one of the longest reviews I wrote about a perfume and I coul keep on writting but it is a review and not a blog. Happy to share with you my discovery.

I find this perfume very nice and unique. It's deep without being heavy. It's warm and I detect a soft spiciness on my skin. It's also very nutty smelling (walnut) which gives it an earthy feel to me. My favourite part about this scent is the red tea vibe that's going on. I really love it. It smells like an authentic tea and not chemical smelling at all. I know a lot of people don't like the fig note in perfumes but I do. Any perfume I've ever tried that has fig in it, I have liked a great deal. I love this fragrance so much that I bought a back-up bottle a week after I bought the first one as I know it's discontinued now. Definitely unisex. This would smell great on a man or a woman but I do find it a tad more masculine rather than feminine. I could see how this fragrance wouldn't be for everyone so testing it out first would be a good idea before buying a full bottle.

We're having a hot spell here, with a heat index that could well reach 105F/40C. I'm avoiding going outside as much as possible and am so grateful for the invention of central air conditioning. One of the first things I thought on waking up was that I needed to douse myself in Bulgari Red Tea. I like my iced tea strong. I think that, to be the most refreshing, it should be potent black tea that almost curls the edges of your tongue the way a lemon does. Then, one should add just enough sugar to create a contrast. This is my iced tea in perfume form. A potent tannic note (enhanced by the walnut) centers it, making me think of a tall, cold glass of chilled tea that's almost as dark as coffee. The fig is that scant teaspoonful of sugar, like a little life raft in an ocean of puckery intensity. Perfect for this heatwave!

This is a very nice frag.. From start its a burst of tea & fig! Thats all I really smell! This is by no means a bad thing, the fig is there from start to finish. As it dries down it becomes a lingering sweet scent with a fade of the tea lurking in the background. It last approximately 4 hours on me @ most.. If you spray on you shirt, you will smell it all day. 1 of the better tea offerings from Bulgari! Nice scent I give it 7.5/10

First of all, Rouge Bvlgari has NONE of the notes that I don't generally like (tobacco, leather, amber, or vanilla), but it has tea, fig, pink pepper, and orange notes that I prefer. And as another reviewer said, it smells hot! Very rouge/red. There's nothing about this to NOT like. In fact, it has already earned it's place on my "love" shelf. I just got my 2ml sample Friday and have already almost used it all up, such an addictive smell. And so perfectly unisex. I don't say this too often about any fragrance, but Rouge Bvlgari is certainly worth buying a full bottle.

If you want rich, dark, concentrated tea, look no further, you can't get much more tea-like than this. I thought I was smelling something by Demeter when I first tried Eau Parfumee au The Rouge. It was tea bags alright, a heady, thick aroma of a cup of tea, minus the milk and sugar.

Tea. Once again a tea scent. And one that smells so good that you would almost want to drink it. Yes, it's true, as soon as the fragrance fully unfolds, it smells so wonderful, as if you were enjoying a cup of real tea. As I mentioned before, the Bvlgari fragrances almost passed me by because I didn't pay attention to them back then.
The Lotus Position, Padmasana, is a type of cross-legged sitting for advanced practitioners and one of the classic, if not 'the classic' sitting postures of yoga.

I treated myself to all 3 Bulgari tea fragrances, and I did it blindly; I somehow felt that I would like them and that they might soon be discontinued. They are also usable by my girlfriend, as they are labeled unisex. Although Bulgari has not been able to convince me with their regular men’s fragrances so far.

This starts out with a big blast of pink pepper, so it's dry and spicy at first, but the peony and rose are already peeking through. Basically it smells very true to the name: It's a springy, fresh, pretty peony scent and not much else.
