There is some confusion about the base note, which was listed as "Chantilly rose" in English, but as "chantilly de rose" at the original French Lancôme site. The latter means rose flavored whipped cream, and I was a bit excited to smell something creamy and delicious underneath the peony and pink pepper, which isn't really there. There is a hint of sweetness, but nothing pronouncedly lactonic or gourmand, so if you're looking for that, don't get your hopes up. I think Lancôme changed the direction of the Maison line a bit in 2019. The older fragrances were mostly gourmandish or floriental leaning, the newer ones are mostly lighter and more floral. I wonder if that's one of the reasons the whole range is out of production now - I prefer the old style by far. This one is nice, but it's only a simple like, nothing close to a love.

First of all, I have to say that I find the design incredibly beautiful. The elegant gold on the back paired with the floral elements and the simple shape of the bottle... Just stylish and a bit fancier than some others in my collection. When spraying the fragrance, a rich rose scent spreads, as if you are holding a bouquet of various types of roses in your hand. An authentic rose is clearly perceptible, just as it should be, but with a refined spiciness that comes across as a bit rough. The pepper definitely adds some edge. The scent is more feminine to me than unisex. Regarding the "age" of the fragrance, I must say: definitely not a young, lively scent, but it feels mature and serious. Overall, it has certain parallels to Delina Exclusif by Parfums de Marly, but it is much less sweet in the top notes and lacks the complexity of Delina Exclusif. A certain light sweetness comes into play later on. As a little pastry lover, I found this development wonderful. The drydown reaches a scent of fluffy, whipped buttercream with rose aroma. This must be the "Chantilly de rose" listed as a note by the manufacturer. When you enter this term in Google Image Search, pictures of small, cute cupcakes and lavish cakes adorned with rosettes from a piping bag appear. Trés délicieuse! (Sometimes I think I would fit in well in a baking forum, but unfortunately, professional indulgence is not feasible for me in terms of my figure, so I prefer to stick to perfume.) Despite this development, I would not classify this Eau de Parfum as a gourmand. Since this is my first fragrance that leans more towards niche, my crowd-pleaser nose perceives a certain unconventionality. It provides a nice change from my playful, sexy juices in my collection. Because the fragrance blend is so exquisite, I will wear it at my wedding in the spring when the rose bushes bloom in May. Pivoines Printemps truly takes you on a journey. When you close your eyes, you get the impression that you are on vacation and taking a dreamy walk through a Victorian rose garden. At five o'clock, you meet comfortably in the white-lacquered pavilion and have some tea. Light pastries with rose cream are served with Earl Grey and a splash of milk. (I'm having a flashback to the Bridgerton series marathon. Those who have watched it on Netflix might know what I mean.) Simply fabulous, this little vacation for the senses.

Who could think that pistachio could be so attractive in a perfume? I certainly did not think so until I tried this little gem with its unusual composition of fragrant peony, woods and of course very sophisticated and delicious pistachio. Green Jade captures the allure of green, floral and refreshing without being too sharp. It is certainly a summer scent for me and it does smell lovely and natural but surprisingly it does not remind me of a natural wilderness. Green Jade rather captures the modern and fashionable style of an urban environment. It is all about balance and moderation. The composition never appears too strong or overpowering but provides a lovely but discreet aura of sophistication that feels both, modern and chic. The fragrance opens with lovely notes of mandarin orange. The pistachio note is quite noticeable right from the start. The heart notes develop into a nice bouquet of peonies and jasmine. The pistachio note still shines through and gives the composition depth and warmth. The dry down is mostly woods and of course the pistachio again. Bvlgari certainly created a nice and easy to wear scent. It is perfect on a hot summer day for going out to shops or to restaurants or even to a business meeting. The perfume has close to the skin sillage but I do get compliments while wearing it. I re-apply it throughout a day multiple times though. The longevity is not that great.

I usually detest floral aquatics. They always seem too acidic or too sythetic to my nose. Omnia Green Jade was a nice change, something that if I was given it as a gift, I would definitely wear it every now and then. Somewhat similar to other fresh, green scents on the market, like Miss Dior Cherie L'eau and Versace Versense, Omnia Green Jade embraces the new, modernistic and very popular Summer scents of today. Although it is nowhere near unique, I do like this fragrance. Simplistic in its nature, it's nothing out of the ordinary, but it is rather pleasant. Fresh and 'cucumbery' in some ways, it seems like more of a clean, musky and green Spring scent rather than a scent for Summer. Although I have mentioned above that it isn't as synthetic as other floral aquatics, I will mention that there is a subtle green chemical note hidden in the heart, that can be unpleasant when inhaling deeply. I was only beginning to enjoy this fragrance when it began to fade rather quickly, showing poor signs of longevity. I am somewhat disappointed in the whole Omnia series for this reason alone.

With OMNIA GREEN JADE, Alberto "Chemical Albie" Morillas finally made a believer out of me: in induction. Three out of three green liquids created by him induce feelings of queasiness and anxiety in me. Three out of three OMNIA edts which I have tried have been less than FB-worthy, to put it mildly. Clearly, Mr. Morillas and I represent a perfume marriage made in hell. As he is the creator also of both MANIFESTO and INTUITION, in addition to HOT COUTURE and AQUA DI GIO, I can say that we have deeply conflicting chemistries. But that's okay, since not everyone is meant for everyone. There are people who like and even love each of these compositions, including OMNIA GREEN JADE. As for me, I was driven by my trial (literally...) of this fragrance to go eat a packet of Sugar Babies. It's true, then, it appears, what I learned back in Psych 101: under conditions of extreme distress, animals will seek refuge in comfort food and often exhibit irrational eating patterns. Désolée!

I sampled this at Macy's when it was launched. I used a heavy hand, and I thought it was stifling. Duh! Now, a couple years later, I dabbed rather than sprayed. I get a clean & green top, and I clearly sense the pistachio and peony. Unfortunately the jasmine doesn't sit well with me and this goes cloying, irritating even. At least I didn't spray this time! I adore the original Omnia, but I don't understand the place of this flanker in the Omnia line - it's out of place. In fact, I think none of the flankers in the line are true to the original, although I also adore Omnia Crystalline. I usually love Alberto Morillas's creations. This isn't one of them. Feb 19 2011

Ah yes, I still remember exactly how I came to "Green Jade" :-) back then (almost exactly 10 years ago) I was 20 years old, just before the graduation trip to Vienna and still a bit shaken from my first real heartbreak. As one knows so well, in this situation you need something new. I was completely satisfied with my hair, so a new perfume was in order. An expensive scent at that time, with a limited training salary, that not everyone had. Nothing from Christina Aguilera, Naomi Campbell, or Kylie Minogue. In a magazine, I found a paper sample from Bvlgari. Never heard of it, not garishly sweet, clear lines, that was exactly what I was looking for. I had also matured since the end of the relationship and had gained a certain vision, even if I wasn't fully healed yet. I immediately tested it, deemed it good, and bought it at the next drugstore. This fragrance marked the beginning of a new era of growing up. "Green Jade" starts aquatic-green with a splash of mandarin. Relatively quickly, pear and peony join in. The base is really beautiful, I mostly smell the light wood and the pistachios here. The scent reminds me of a day at the Baltic Sea, but not a hot day, rather sunny-warm with a clear sky. I see myself sitting on a piece of driftwood, the spray foaming and splashing, and I can take a deep breath and exhale. The sea is in motion, wave after wave rolls onto the beach, but it is not rough and aggressive. For miles, there is not a soul in sight. My mind becomes clear, and I can see beyond things. My heartbeat slows down, I can relax and unwind. I find the longevity to be quite good; in the evening I can still perceive a fresh green veil. Even today, I still like it, although I usually prefer gourmand-sweet-fruity scents. Thank you, Green Jade, for accompanying me into a new chapter of life :-)

When I received a sample of this fragrance a few years ago, I first wondered if it was even a women's scent. The color and the name didn't necessarily seem feminine. I didn't know any fragrances from Bulgari and couldn't imagine what it would be like. The surprise was great when I applied it: Fresh, yet soft! Green, yet warm and creamy! Elegant, but not overpowering!

Actually, I wanted to tidy up. But then I came across some notes I sometimes make about fragrances. About fragrances that I get to test from friends, acquaintances, or even neighbors. If I was lucky, I sometimes even got a small sample.

Yes, I did it. First: This is my first Bulgari fragrance. That means, I have tested almost all of them, but I once gifted the Omnia and the Jasmin Noir is a candidate for purchase. I can only imagine the tea scents after the sauna. Second: I prefer to avoid anything that looks green. Unless it's in orientals or chypres.

I love this perfume....it is one of my absolute favorite scents! It smells fresh and at the same time warm! Musk, rose, and citrus fruits are present in ALL of my favorite fragrances.... Coco Mademoiselle; Tresor in Love, Euphoria Blossom, and Gucci envy me or j'adore (or even Britney Spears Curious; -))! If you like those, you will surely love this amazing perfume too!

And here we go with Bflgari… Bvlgari… yes, as I mentioned before, when I didn’t know the Bvlgari brand many, many years ago, I always pronounced the “v.” So, you can have a little laugh now. Laughed? Good, then let’s continue! :D This is now the fourth Omnia fragrance from Bvlgari, and it doesn’t sound too bad to me based on the notes.

La Vie est belle was launched when my daughter was 11. We saw ads for it everywhere, the face on them beautiful Julia Roberts (need I say Pretty Woman?) Both my daughter and I were curious about the smell so we went to a shop and tried it. I suppose we both wanted to like it. Done spraying we sniffed the whole afternoon and evening. I could not get my head around it; to me a strong note of something kept annoying me. I asked my daughter and she said, that she thought it smelled good. I decided that it was probably just me. Not all scents are for everyone. I bought a bottle for my daughter the same Christmas. Just a 30ml but she was very happy. She used it up quite quickly and I planned to give her one for her birthday in October. When she unwrapped the present she look a bit tired and said thank you - but my mother’s ear is tuned to some frequencies not hearable to other humans so I noticed the disappointment. Later that week I asked her if she would have been happier with another present. “You know, mum, there is this strange smell in the perfume that keeps annoying me - and I liked the smell of the perfume in the beginning!” I could not help smiling - perhaps preferences are inherited. I bought the bottle of her and kept it in my closet - for a long time. A few years ago I tested it again with the same result so I got rid of it. But then I got my hands on L’Eau de Parfum Légère and this was a totally different experience. The base makes the change. Less sweet and loud. I can wear this without getting a headache and that is an improvement. Sometimes flankers are the better version of a not so likable juice. It just takes some time to find it. Year 2, 19/365

I was given a Bottle (1/3 full) of this fragrance, so decided to give it a full days wearing. Well,, here goes..another boring berry clone. I was surprised at how very similar to Midnight Rose this fragrance is. Black currant is listed in the opening..a very synthetic berry it is. Has an overpowering fruity feel, throughout the whole wearing experience. The cloying sweetness is most likely due to the supposed addition of praline and chocolate. Even the jasmine and iris are hardly detectable ...they too seem false somehow. Considering the bottle design...heavy and expensive looking), the actual juice is a real letdown. It may appeal to the younger collectors, who seem to enjoy the very fruity fragrances that seem to be all the rage. I don't find this a soft scent either. It has an almost jarring quality to it...it doesn't seem to have any stages what so ever...it basically has the same bland berry scent from start to finish. It does have lasting power...it stayed with me for several hours, which is quite a feat on my skin! I won' be testing any pinkie colored fragrances for awhile now...I'll just stifle my yawn, and move on!

I was particularly excited about "La vie est belle L'Eau de Parfum Légère," because I still have the original in my mind... and I think I remember not liking something about it. However, I must also admit that my taste in fragrances has changed significantly during and especially after pregnancy. La vie est belle smells wonderfully delicious and currently performs better for me than the original, because the blackcurrant, although categorized as a top note like in the original, is at most just a hint, as I have never been fond of overly fruity scents. La vie est belle starts off quite sweet, very vanilla-like, and the scent of praline immediately tickles my nose with the warm chocolate note (which I usually don't like, but here it is simply perfectly balanced) with a floral touch that beautifully refines the gourmand and makes it something truly special, really very delicious and elegant at the same time... yes, I would almost call it ripe. I would say it is a fragrance that, while it has some notes that would fit well into teenage scents, as vanilla and chocolate are often treated rather poorly in fragrances... but here they come together to create a unique scent for the lady... that I must truly admit to being a big fan of. After a while, I find the scent a bit mystical, which I would attribute to the jasmine... because in combination with the praline, it comes out particularly grand. I don't see this fragrance on very young girls... but from around the mid-20s, I think it is an absolute treasure.

"La vie est belle L'Eau de Parfum Légère" smells wonderfully delicious and performs better than the original, as the blackcurrant is barely noticeable. It starts off sweet and vanilla-like with a hint of chocolate, really very tasty. There’s also a slight smoky scent, almost reminiscent of incense.

What a shame to have this brand image, this beautiful bottle ... everything to succeed ; but what a mediocre execution and what expensives prices ! . It seems that it won't last too much but it does at a low profile , the problem is that the smell lacks presence, grace, shine, quality. It's , like almost everything one finds on the shelves , very safe-mode , as to take it to the office and reapply in the middle of the day . For unpretentious circumstances . I detect spices , musks , but the problem to me is that I find a prominent note which reminds me of ambroxan that I usually don't like . It isn't listed in the pyramid but for me it has a very clear feeling . Being so minimal , I should try it more times and without interferences to give more details buuuut , NEXT in every ways .

tested today at the sephora in Lyon part dieu. I had heard about it without more so it was the opportunity to discover it, especially with the very hot day an icy effect was welcome. except that this perfume is neither fresh and even less icy. It smells good, a smell that I don't remember having ever smelled. Synthetic, pleasant but nothing more. ideal for a person who does not have a huge collection and who is looking for a perfume that can match almost every season and stand out with a rare but not tenacious smell because after 2 hours the perfume no longer smelled.

Opening is super pleasant. Fresh, juicy, icy blast that really refreshes you. Not a very common scent either, would make a great office/everyday choice. Everything after that falls off a cliff tho. It's mostly just dry musky woods but done in a slightly unpleasant way, and stays more or less linear from the end of the opening all the way until it fades. Performance is quite weak overall, everything after the opening is just a skin scent, tho that's probably for the best. I can't see a reason to buy this, tho it is a bit of a different choice the drydown kills it

Masculine, clean, cool, calming, pleasing, a waterfall of freshness, summery, and very suitable for everyday use. The name Glacial perfectly expresses the content of the fragrance. One of the creations of the famous perfumer Alberto Morillas. The strange thing is that Glacial Essence does not have any DNA of the original Bvlgari Man. The fragrance is based on a completely dominant note of juniper berry, but here in a fresh, aquatic form. This is followed by notes of ginger, which give a slightly pungent scent, then sandalwood, on a noticeable base of clearwood. I also did not notice any synthetic note. I've read a lot of negative comments about the fragrance's performance, but my opinion after extensive use for several days is that the fragrance has a high performance for a summer fragrance, and I received many compliments. I can say that the longevity is no less than 4 hours and the sillage is up to 2 hours or more continuously, noting that the fragrance comes in the form of an Eau de Parfum. The bottle of the fragrance features the traditional shape of Bvlgari Man series bottles, but it is designed in a beautiful light blue color with a white top head that perfectly expresses the essence of the fragrance. Pros: * Unique * Classy * Eau de Parfum form * Noticeable projection Cons: * A little pungent * Somewhat high price * Not suitable for blind buying Rating: A distinctive fragrance, but not the best in the Bvlgari Man line 8/10.

Bvlgari Glacial Essence lives up to its name, delivering a distinctly fresh and cold sensation that's quite surprising. Despite an initial impression of citrus, this scent feels remarkably minimalist, even more so than its sibling, Rain Essence. Both share a kinship with the crispness of Silver Mountain Water, thankfully without any inkiness, though Rain Essence leans closer due to its green tea note. Glacial Essence centers around a prominent, almost sterile white musk, reminiscent of molecular musk-focused fragrances like Caron's Musc Oli or Ajmal's Amber Musc. While it successfully achieves the sought-after ice-cold effect perfect for summer – and commendably avoids the harsh chemical edge that often plagues similar scents – it ultimately lacks depth and nuance. I find myself wishing for a touch of complexity, perhaps the invigorating mint of ELDO's "You or Someone Like You," layered with this glacial coolness. Alas, for those of us who prefer single-wear fragrances, that perfect summer concoction remains a dream. Glacial Essence isn't bad; it's a "pleasantly cold" experience, just one that ultimately feels too straightforward.

Personal: 8.5/10 – Fresh, icy, and aromatic. I don't usually like juniper, but here I do. I really enjoy this fragrance. Mass appeal: 8/.510 – Clean, fresh, and bright. Most will enjoy it, but juniper is a bit divisive. Performance: 6/10 – Moderate longevity and projection. Not terrible for a freshie, but not remarkable either. Value: 6.

Normally, I try not to be impressed by the marketing campaigns of perfume manufacturers. In the case of Glacial Essence, I only partially succeeded. Mountains and glaciers, along with the promise of a very icy-fresh scent, were enough to make me want to test the new Bulgari. So I quickly sought out a sample and off I went on the (ski) ride...

I really like the Bulgari Aqua line. Fresh, aquatic scents that suit my taste very well. Glacial Essence sounded to me like it would also head in a similar direction. This is only partially true. Glacial Essence starts off fresh, evoking associations with glaciers and ice. Quite quickly, one perceives the sandalwood and the artificial cypress as well as Clearwood.

You stand on the Jostedalsbreen and look at the icy water. The fresh, cool air caresses your face, you are well bundled up and carry the sun in your heart, which is why you can enjoy all of this. You take a deep breath and it feels like you could breathe in forever and everything.

Pleasantly fresh summer scent, perfect for everyday use at the office/school/university. A fragrance for when you simply want to smell nice without standing out too much. The scent doesn’t hit you in the face, with a sillage of 6/10 mMm, but that’s perfectly fine.

This fragrance is a little like the original Miracle, yet much more flowery and sweet. Although there isn't rose listed in the notes, I can definitely smell roses in this perfume. This scent is much better suited to its bottle design than the original. So Magic is certainly a 'pink' fragrance because it is so light, feminine and pretty. This fragrance would make a perfect scent for the warmer months as it is fresh and energising. If you're like me, and couldn't take a liking to Miracle because of its strong spicy notes, then this fragrance could be more suited to you.

After I raved so enthusiastically about L'Instant Magic by Guerlain, I wanted to know what the magical flanker of the Lancôme Miracle is all about. Is it like magic? Will I finally be awaited by Tom Hanks on the Empire State Building when I wear it? Honestly, things don’t look good for my relationship with Hanks. Miracle So Magic! cannot work magic. Fell for it again. But as a fresh little fragrance, it’s quite nice. The top note is super fresh, so fresh that my nose wakes up. The heart note is floral-floral with a kick of creaminess. The base is warm, cuddly, and barely sweet. Since I don’t like daffodils, I’m glad they’ve hidden from me. All in all, the only magic that MSM exerts is that it is pleasing and suits everyone, and if you gift it, you won’t get the bottle thrown at your head. A nose-pleaser, a little charmer.

My dear husband is not a shopping enthusiast - especially not when I enter the perfume store with a sparkle in my eyes. But he is not a spoil-sport and bravely accompanies me. Recently, in my olfactory paradise, when I was once again lost in scent experiences, he held a fragrance strip under my nose that immediately piqued my interest. So Magic! Oh, orange and pink pepper. Caressing and cheeky at the same time. Then again softly enticing through the rose and a bit strict through the daffodil. Somehow controversial and exciting. The impression is rounded off by musk and cedarwood. Still, it is an unconventional scent. Would we become friends? The slightly metallic finish made me hesitate. But my beloved convinced me. Rightly so, because by now the scent has captured me - and we both enjoy it when I wear it.

At first, I was thrilled with Miracle so magic, then I was a bit torn about whether it smells noble or cheap, but now I am totally excited again, because whenever I use it, I receive compliments upon compliments every time. Recently, I was even asked by a bank employee about the wonderful scent I was exuding.. It is a charming floral fragrance, framed by a bit of green and just a hint of vanilla.. It is very suitable for spring, as it radiates energy, floral notes, magic, and a desire for more. It is appropriate for any time of day and has relatively good longevity. Since I initially treated the scent rather dismissively, but now know its effectiveness as a compliment magnet, the bottle is already dramatically emptying. In addition to the fragrance notes mentioned here, according to Lancome, it also contains violet, hazelnut, pepper, rose, and cedarwood. Furthermore, it is said to contain rosehip. I love such complex fragrances, as they make them unique, mysterious, and exude a certain magic. Thanks to Schnuffi for the great tip and thanks to Lancome for the wonderful scent. The bottle is wonderfully handy, practical, and yet in a lovely girlish pink-rose - I like it!

I had So Magic a few years ago, and I really liked it! Maybe it will come back into my collection someday ;) I found it very beautiful back then, as it was sweet-floral, without woods, but purely floral with a white musk note :) Sweet-scented jasmine, lily of the valley, daffodil, and a hint of vanilla and white musk made Miracle so magical ;) I also managed to sniff out some violet here, which is not listed. So Magic also has good longevity. A successful fragrance from the house of Lancome, which is also great for summer, as it is not overpowering! One should dare to try So Magic!

In front of me lies a refreshing wipe like no other. Made with elaborate handwork and visually so what from magic in its silver space foil ;o) Miracle is in my nose a pink-green floral bouquet, it smells incredibly young, fresh, pious, and spring-like, that it almost pulls me out with sunscreen onto the garden lounge chair, but WAIT! All just show.

I stumbled upon this perfume by chance. One day, 5 years ago, I was just about to buy the regular Miracle variant for a friend, which I personally do not like. Of course, new and unknown scents always draw me in magically, and I have to test them immediately. It was the same here. On that very day, I bought the perfume and have been using it for over 5 years now.

The reason I have a decant of this relatively new perfume is that a brand rep came behind the Guerlain counter when I was there and walked by, holding this bottle. It's a beauty so it did catch my attention. When I asked what it was, he didn't say Goldea, that I recall. He started talking about Cleopatra, said the bottle mimicked the crown Liz Taylor wore in the movie. So that's the name that stuck. I kept searching our database and online for Cleopatra by Bulgari and didn't find it. Tonight I picked up the vial and tried to make out the scrawl on the hand-applied label. Ah, Goldea! It's in our database. So why was he telling me about Cleopatra, which I think would have been a much better name. Perhaps because he knows the name Goldea is a dud. Or maybe they originally planned that connection, but abandoned it. Hmmm....let me take a look at the attached video. Oh, okay, it has Isabeli Fontana walking up a pyramid wearing a snake necklace and bracelet. Now I get it, but I do think it's misnamed. What does it smell like? To me, many Bvlgari sents have a waxy, synthetic note--something that threatens to choke me or close my nose if I smell too long. Jasmin Noir is an exception, as I recall. This one is more like the Bvlgaria Omnia scent I bought but will never wear. Goldea is not candyish like my Omnia is, the notes are potentially lovely, including the Egyptian papyrus that's strong in the base. I just think Bvlgari needs to use a bigger percentage of natural ingredients, or use better synthetics than they do. For those not nasally afflicted by Bvlgaris, this is a warm, mature oriental. Goldea vaguely reminds me of J'Adore, but this is a better fragrance, IMO.

Goldea isn’t what I thought it would be. Alone, it’s fruity and musky. It’s warm and pleasant, not one is buy a large bottle of, but nice. I would consider this a summer fragrance because of the warmth. During my experimentation I also put on Elizabeth James Nirvana Rose and the combination is incredible. I will definitely layer with these two fragrances. Longevity is four hours. It becomes a skin scent after two hours. Layered it lasts a bit longer.

To me, it's a sweet creamy scent with some floral notes. This is my first try with sweet-ish perfumes and I can only bear it on really cold cold days. Otherwise it's too strong for me as a person who always goes with a splash of white florals and subtle scents. Respect to everyone who loves this perfume but I would recommend it to mature ladies.

Hm... Goldea doesn't seem to be getting much love here, and I really don't think this beautiful scent deserves that. For a long time, I hesitated whether I should rather get Olympea because I quite like the salty vanilla in it, but then I realized that I'm not really into Paco Rabanne, and the many types of musk listed in the fragrance pyramid didn't help either. There's no vanilla in here... but I still perceive that salty-sweetness. I immediately think of sun, beach, and sea with this scent. Yesterday, in my little regular perfumery, I couldn't say no anymore and got the 25 ml bottle during the 30% off promotion. Summer doesn't want to show itself this year, and I'm really frustrated. It's nice that there are scents that can at least give you a little summer feeling. Goldea is such a scent. About the scent: Goldea starts sweet-fresh, which is probably thanks to the combination of bergamot, orange blossom, and raspberry. The musk is also slightly noticeable. As it develops, a hint of flowers comes in... but I wouldn't call it floral. More musk... but rather as if the musk brings some depth. My sense of smell doesn't allow me to differentiate between crystal musk and golden musk. Just musk. Towards the base, I perceive the patchouli, which tempers the sweetness a bit, and there's something spicy that I attribute to the amber. Even more musk comes in :) ... I find the musk never overwhelming but really beautifully integrated into the scent. There's no coconut listed... but somehow a coconut note is always subtly present. The longevity is about 7 hours. The sillage is rather average. However, a nice scent aura is present. You smell really good with this ;) My little hand-friendly bottle is just as pretty as the original bottle. Both fit excellently with the scent. I can imagine Goldea as an all-day fragrance, especially in summer. Only when it goes above 28 degrees, I would prefer it for the evening as a going-out scent. Conclusion: Goldea ... similar to Olympea ... but a tad more elegant. Warm, powdery, sweet with a hint of coconut. But also a bit fresh. Sea, sun, vacation ... fits! A golden scent for the longed-for summer!

Almost two weeks ago, I met Joyce. We were the only ones on the flight from Chicago to Los Angeles with an empty seat between us - and during boarding, we had silently vowed with our glances that the very large man in the sleeveless shirt, who usually manages to plop down into such free middle seats at the last minute (often sweating profusely because he just ran to the gate), might just barely miss out this time. When it became clear that the seat would indeed remain free, Joyce ordered a whiskey and cola - and without asking, she got one for me too. Joyce was somewhere between sixty-five and a hundred. It was hard to tell because she had had quite a bit of 'work' done and was otherwise heavily made up. But the blonde Dolly Parton wig and the fact that she was only wearing shorts and a top - had she just come from the airport? - suggested that she found nothing wrong with her window-leather décolletage and dark caramel thighs. She was charming and very cheerful, talking a lot and happily, and although I usually don't enjoy long conversations with complete strangers, those unexpectedly entertaining four hours flew by. Joyce shared that she lives with her husband in a gated community (a fenced-off suburban village where only similarly styled houses are allowed) in Palm Desert on the edge of the Sonora Desert. I imagined her meeting with other women between sixty-five and a hundred in pink leisure suits for 'Make America Great Again' bingo, while the men stayed home cleaning their rifles. But then she mentioned that Palm Desert is apparently no exception in traditionally Democratic California, and I thought: okay, they have to grow old somewhere... When we landed, Joyce opened her huge bag (white leather with a braided handle and plenty of bling-bling) and pulled out a still-wrapped bottle of Goldea by Bvlgari (it had been on sale at the Duty Free in O'Hare - I had seen that too). She tore off the plastic and generously sprayed herself with it - which is basically a cheeky move on a plane - and a glowing cloud of silvery - pardon: golden! - sweetness flooded towards me. And I thought: 'But that should surely be a gift for your great-great-great-granddaughter, who is waiting for you at the gate - and not for you?' Goldea is not a bad fragrance. However, it is very much a product of a consumer-oriented present - and not one that claims to leave a historical footprint in the world of perfume. It lives off its alluring and radiant top note - sunlit and sweetly soft - and chooses, beyond that, a largely interchangeable amber-patchouli-musk dry down, like so many others have. I had ample opportunity to study its progression - as I stood closely behind Joyce during the endlessly drawn-out disembarkation, while she reported live to her family on the phone about which row she was currently at. Conclusion: a bright, light fragrance for here and now and for the moment. Not one that whispers of yesterday, and not one that anyone will remember tomorrow. Joyce's great-great-great-granddaughter will surely be very pleased - if she indeed received it. But maybe Joyce kept it for herself?

As a woman with a fondness for many of the Bvlgari fragrances, I naturally had to try "Goldea." Maybe I'm a bit biased, but I don't find this scent as bad as it's portrayed here in parts. Sure, it's not a top achievement in perfumery. But does it always have to be? How often does the truly "big hit" really happen?

I have too many sample vials, it hit me last night with a loud bang. The sample glass on my makeup table, where another sample glass was parked, shattered last night around 2:30 AM with a loud crash. I was scared to death by the noise at my feet. My boyfriend, who had been peacefully sitting at the desk, stormed in to locate the source of the noise.

I was pleased with the Goldea sample, as I can associate the name with the golden autumn. And the scent is indeed mildly autumnal. It exudes a slight warmth - like the low autumn sun, and the aroma of ripe sweet raspberries still lingers in the air. Above it hovers the pleasantly citrusy orange blossom absolute.

~ Inspiration ~ When I discovered "Goldea" by Bvlgari here in the new arrivals, it immediately landed on my wishlist. During a swap, I received a sample. ~ Bottle ~ The delicate, round glass bottle is set in a narrow, golden ring. It features a double-stranded, dainty chain around the neck and a large, yellow-gold cap on top, giving it a luxurious appearance.

Goldea came to me as a sample. For a long time, I was skeptical, set it aside, and didn't spray it. Today I tested it and would like to share my impression with you. Goldea reminds me a bit of other Bvlgari fragrances in the dry down, like Jasmin Noir.... in my opinion, it cannot deny its fragrance lineage. Goldea is warm, soft, and does not smell to my nose like La vie...

I like salt. Most of the time, I season a dish without having tasted it beforehand. I admit it. Now, of course, I know that too much salt can harm the body. That's how it is with the little "vices." The dose makes the poison! In the world of fragrance, however, spices can be used in any quantity and according to preference. Without a guilty conscience. All the more joyfully, I welcomed a new addition to my collection today: Ô Zenith by Lancôme Those who know me might be aware that I'm not necessarily the biggest fan of citrus-fresh scents. Too often, I've associated them with cleaning products or refreshing wipes. With Ô Zenith, however, it’s completely different... The refreshing citrus is balanced here by gentle florals and a tropical vanilla note. I've read online several times that this scent is often compared to "Alien Goddess (Eau de Parfum) | Mugler." I do not agree. Rather, I can faintly recognize similarities to "Olympēa (Eau de Parfum) | Rabanne." Here, however, in a much lighter, summery variation. Like Olympēa, Ô Zenith also has an incredibly pleasant salty note that immediately catapults me mentally to a deserted island: tropical climate, white sandy beaches, and summery fruity cocktails. The salt of the sea on sun-kissed skin. As it develops, the scent becomes pleasantly sweet, and the citrus gradually fades away. What remains is a veil of salty vanilla that carries you into the sunset. The longevity is quite appropriate at around six hours for a summery EdT. The sillage is rather close to the skin, yet you can still catch a light whiff of the fragrance now and then. I am very much looking forward to sunny days with this thoroughly friendly scent. Wishing you all a wonderful summer! :-)

Master perfumer Dominique Ropion, who has already created numerous wonderful compositions - from popular designer fragrances like the Alien series for Thierry Mugler to L’Interdit for Givenchy, Babycat for Yves Saint Laurent, and niche fragrances like Akoum for the perfume house Reine de Saba - once again demonstrates his fine intuition and talented nose here. With Ô Zenith, he aimed to create a “sunny, cheerful fragrance that captures the lightness and warmth of a perfect summer day.” And although the scent may not represent an olfactory revelation, it is exactly what a summer fragrance should be: light, unobtrusive, yet present. The opening is fresh and invigorating, without being too sharp or citrusy - rather pleasantly zesty. As the scent develops, it unfolds harmoniously soft: The heart of jasmine absolute brings a gentle floral note, while the wonderful, sweet monoi accord in the base evokes memories of vacation, sun, and sea, instantly lifting the spirits. The entire Les Ô collection from Lancôme is designed to promote positive emotions through fragrance. It is not a scent that shouts loudly - but one that brings a smile to your face. In my view, Dominique Ropion has accomplished the mission with flying colors.

This is a very pretty fragrance. I wasn't sure how mimosa and iris would work together, as it seemed like a very unusual combination, but I am surprised to find that they complement each other very well. The mimosa starts out sweet, but the green notes and bergamot keep the sweetness in check. Then iris joins the mix, adding a lightly powdery, clean facet. I love the addition of violet leaf in fragrances, finding it adds a lovely garden-fresh dimension whenever used. It is no different here, giving this fragrance a freshness that's not typical of iris dominant perfumes. This is not the usual powdery iris fragrance with the obligatory vanilla note, so if you expect that you may be disappointed here. While I like those Iris fragrances too, this is very different. It's bright, light, and crisp and has an upbeat quality about it. Performance wise, I get excellent silage and longevity. Not beast mode, but I was aware of it most of the day. While this is a strong like right now, it has potential to become a love.

Truly an incredibly beautiful, gentle, soft, and tender iris scent. I was sure I owned all the great iris perfumes in my collection. Wrong thought, this enchanting iris is so beautiful that I immediately ordered a bottle. The great thing about this iris is that it doesn't come off as dusty-dry, but rather lovely. It gently hugs the skin, without anything scratchy or even dark. You can smell the iris very well and almost nothing else. Probably the raspberry gives this slight sweetness. But it doesn't come off as cloying; instead, it perfectly supports the delicacy. I cannot perceive sandalwood or vetiver. The tonka bean is also present only to a small extent, probably just to make the scent a bit more lasting. Since the iris flower or iris root cannot be harvested in the first year of life, this makes iris perfumes very expensive, but this price here is, in my opinion, very acceptable. It's worth testing, but I warn of extremely strong addiction potential.

Thanks to a dear friend who recently showered me with a bunch of fragrance samples, I am currently enjoying the luxury of testing a new little indulgence every day. Today it was "Splendida - Iris d'Or". I had not yet had the pleasure of experiencing Bvlgari, so I was all the more curious about this noble drop. A spritz here, a spritz there..., eyes closed..., cautiously inhaled... INSANE! What a fragrance! Enchanting, intoxicating, sublime, liquid gold. It is truly the perfect scent for a proud aristocrat with plenty of charm and heart, made for the nobility. Absurdly, it still did not feel out of place on me in my simple T-shirt/jeans combo. It felt more like this fragrance had elevated me from my bourgeois status for a fraction of a second and ennobled me. Pure decadence, but with so much soul. I was easily swept away and succumbed to the temptation of holding my nose close to my pulse to inhale the captivating scent... Wa wa wa Wum!! As if I had run into a wall or plunged into the depths of an abyss filled with sweet, heavy blooms and warm, soft aromas that instantly buried me. For the next 20 minutes, my head throbbed as if struck by an olfactory sledgehammer. Stupid curiosity! I decided to keep some distance, tilting my nose slightly upward while sniffing to increase the distance from the scented skin areas. This made it much more bearable, and immediately this slightly diva-like fragrance regained its magic and allure, starting its siren song once more! But I had learned my lesson, knowing now that the temptress bites when you press too hard, so I kept my nose respectfully at a distance from then on. And then it finally became clear to me why the nobility must often be so haughty! For with a nose held high, "Splendida - Iris d'Or" is one of the most beautiful perfumes I have encountered so far!

The Spendida line is truly successful! First, I was captivated by Jasmin Noir - then I started eyeing Rose Rose. Bulgari is creating competition within its own ranks. Now, I am enveloped by the lush Iris d`Or. Yes, I find it to be the most substantial of the three - suitable for evenings and the "big appearance." In the theater or concert hall, it will certainly make a good impression. But it's better to book a box, as the sillage is not to be underestimated. The bitter violet leaf is clearly present, delicately accompanied by fruity raspberry. I can't detect any sweetness. Iris - and mimosa absolute deepen the bitter tone - but remain creamy. This might be due to the sandalwood, and tonka also has soft curves. Vetiver grounds the elegant fragrance - with a tendency towards heaviness. During the day, I wouldn't wear the "golden iris" - it's too full-bodied and significant for that. Even simple clothing is not its domain - evening attire must be pressed for it. That's why I keep an eye on Rose Rose, as it is more suitable for everyday wear - just like Jasmin Noir. But when the patent leather shoes are polished, it can be Iris d`Or.

Anyone who, like me, loves "Bvlgari pour Femme" will welcome this new radiant-elegant family member with open arms. After encountering "Bvlgari Splendida Iris d'Or," I naturally had to try it. And the longer our acquaintance lasts, the more enamored I become. After a delicate yet intensely fragrant introduction - there was no skimping on Heliotrope here - a heart of perfect beauty unfolds: Iris and Mimosa shine brilliantly against each other! If both weren't pleasantly muted by their inherent bitterness, it would almost be too much of a good thing! Because here, they really went all out and didn't hold back! Sandalwood, Tonka bean, and Vetiver complete an elegant women's fragrance! Only exquisite ingredients were chosen, thus splendidly "dressing up" the classic "Bvlgari pour Femme." The goldsmiths send their regards. In my opinion, "Bvlgari Splendida Iris d'Or" is a typical Italian; a rich golden veil that makes the woman it envelops beautiful and desirable. A fragrance for "Le Donne sotto le Stelle"! (Even without the Spanish Steps.) Whether it will become a classic like "Bvlgari pour Femme" remains to be seen. In any case, the "golden iris" is going on my wish list.

From the very start, I am greeted by the powderiness of heliotrope and iris, with a delicate touch of raspberry adding a fruity note. However, the violet leaf quickly introduces a certain bitterness (too quickly for my personal taste). And so it remains for now: softly powdery, gently bitter, a decidedly elegant fragrance. The sillage is not very expansive for me.

This fragrance is the "reinterpretation" of the classic "pour femme". Bvlgari's statement: The scent is now even more precious, they have intensified the iris note, increased the concentration, and at the same time established a new fragrance line with "Splendida". Now my opinion (identical to many "old customers"): Iris d'or is a disaster!

I deleted the old comment/text about this fragrance because it wasn't very precise and was also way too short! I must admit that I haven't written a text in a long time :) I have to confess that I also had a hard time these last few weeks and didn't find the energy to write a new text... Anyway, to get to the point, YES, I have fallen in love with a Lancôme fragrance again... To be more specific, from the La Nuit Trésor line :D Who would have thought :D Probably no one is surprised by this news anymore :D But okay, I at least admit that I am a big fan of the Trésor line :))) Since I absolutely LOVE the La Nuit Trésor EDP, I wanted to test the EDT version better and more thoroughly ;))) I was familiar with the fragrance but not as well as my beloved EDP ;) I got a small perfume sample of this scent from my favorite perfumery to test it more closely and calmly. At home, I tested this fragrance with my grandfather, who also thinks the La Nuit Trésor line is fantastic ;D Before I sprayed the fragrance on my wrist, we looked up some information here on Parfumo, and the fragrance pyramid sounded very promising already :))) So I didn't hesitate and applied two sprays on my wrist. The fragrance... Right upon spraying, you could smell beautiful but also somehow very pleasant berry notes... The berry notes remain present throughout the entire fragrance journey. They are neither artificial nor annoying berry notes! Much more, they are extremely feminine but also slightly sweet and pleasant berries :)) (For anyone looking for a good berry fragrance, this scent is perfect!:))) My grandfather also loved the berry notes :D He said that many berry fragrances he has tested so far smelled like jam to him... But he found this scent here extremely pleasant and very good :)) Once again, we both agreed :D. I must also admit something! This version is fresher but not as sweet as the EDP. So, if someone found the EDP too strong, they might really like this version here :). The rose note gave the fragrance a certain lightness but also freshness... Which is very pleasant to wear in spring :) The berry + rose notes harmonized so wonderfully and at the same time so beautifully with each other!*_* The Tahitian vanilla note was also too beautiful to be true! So creamy but also pleasantly sweet! :))) It is somewhat similar to the vanilla note that you can smell in the EDP, but this note is much lighter and not as strong. My grandfather found this note one of the most beautiful, as it simply stands out for him neither too strong nor too weak! And I can only agree with him! What I want to emphasize clearly is that this fragrance lasts on me, just like the other Trésor fragrances, almost two days! I also find this fragrance very romantic but also very playful and, of course, extremely feminine! :)) A fragrance that you can wear everywhere, as with the right dose, it is simply beautiful and very attractive! Great fragrance! ❤ P.S.: The EDP remains my favorite ;D

The L'Eau de Toilette from La nuit Tresor is more transparent than its opulent predecessors. The slightly sour black currant is clearly recognizable in the opening, taming the sweet notes of raspberry and lychee. The rosy heart notes flash briefly, with a trace of Damask rose still detectable in the base. After that, the perfume becomes sweet gourmand with patchouli and a soft vanilla note in the background. The L'EdT is definitely a scent of the 2010s, but due to the more subtle dosage of the gourmand notes, it has a slightly mysterious aura reminiscent of perfumes from earlier years. For me, it is clearly the most beautiful version of the La nuit series.

During extreme heat, I appreciate simple and unpretentious fragrances. Here: just lemon and sandalwood - and that's enough! I would never wear this ODT for a special occasion, BUT: for everyday errands, doctor visits, at the playground with the grandchildren, at home on the couch, etc. etc. - for these very normal occasions, I love this scent! It doesn't always have to be highly complex - one can also appreciate and celebrate simplicity!

Tested at printemps shop this week. What a fantastic i surprise i was worry to find a clone of rose d'Arabie armani. Not at all,this is thoughrougly different, it s like a shower fresh of rose ,really féminine . Light and flowerly its ideal for end of spring and beginnong of summer. The longivity is poor just 2 hours and the sillage weak but doesn t matter the scent is the strong point of this flagrance. Thanks lancome for this masterpiece

This is a fragrance that -in my opinion- improves everything good about Man in Black - the famous previous flanker - and solves all its weak points, taking the original olfactory idea to its maximum artistic expression - without leaving its series, of course -: - Creamier, more mysterious, more refined… better blended, better performance, better sillage... If you like MiB, it's hard not to like this one; it also dispels that inconvenient “drunken scoundrel” reminiscence of the first: Black Orient replaces MiB's tobacco with cardamom, orris with Taif rose and benzoin with oud, creating a fantastic olfactory composition albeit a little darker, more enigmatic and elegant. Unfortunately it wasn’t cheered on YouTube as happened to its sister who became the bet of the brand, discarding the rest of similar iterations. If you like MiB and you can get this, you shouldn't hesitate, although I don't advise paying collector's prices either. So I see the shelf with the fragrance bottles and I reach out and pick up the black bottle crowned with gold, knowing that with each new breath, it draws closer to its dark destiny…

I bought this one to test it because of good reviews, and I was happy with it the scent is good a bit harsh ( so not everyone will like it) it's not really spicy maybe more leathery. The performance : to test it out I did one spray on my arm and continued with my buisness as usual So for the first 02 hours I could smell it really good and it projects really well; after that it drawdown a bit. For longevity : 08 hours on my skin, I could even smell some traces on my arm after more than 12 hours.

Enriched by the rum note, although it is not sweet or cloying at all. The liquor point quickly fades, entering a very smoky, dry and linear phase that remains unchanged until the end. Leather and oud remain shy, close to the skin. The sillage isn't amazing, and the longevity is downright short on my skin. It has a slight similarity in its middle phase with Midnight in Paris, by Van Cleef & Arpels, but I love that one and I don't find a point of originality or character in Bvlgari Man Black Orient that would invite me to buy it. It reminds me of the rest of the Bvlgari Man flankers, although it has the outstanding smoky character as a novelty. This could please those who enjoy this feature in a perfume. I don't think it's a bad fragrance, although I'm not convinced because it lacks something to be round, and even more to be special, I don't know... It lacks body, projection and intensity.

An exquisite composition including oud from natural origin this treasure is now doscontinued and very hard to find. It has something form the old Guerlains Les desert d Orient collection. Amazing quality, 12 hours longevity and good projection. Grab it if you find it at a resonable price, unfortunately the prices are insane nowadays. Happy to have it in my collection, a true masterpiece given to us from Alberto Morillas.

Sadly discontinued (what are you doing, guys) masterpiece by morillas. Great rum, leather and cardamom combo, uber masculine and elegant, amazing presence and projection. I don't understand how this got discontinued. Maybe some IFRA BS. I hold my last 10ml as if it was liquid gold. Legendary scent

Yes, I have given this fragrance top marks, not without reason. A modern and oriental scent, very well combined, simply genius. It smells very spicy, strong, and intense from the very beginning. Wonderful, I am very satisfied. In the middle part, a bouquet of the finest roses comes in. Wonderful. Can it get any better? Yes!!!

Right from the start, rum and tuberose engage in a neck-and-neck race. A fantastic sillage that lasts for about 2-3 hours. Then it becomes weaker and closer to the skin, but still better than many other fragrances. I would describe this scent as oriental, masculine, heavy, spicy, and actually not sweet. The dominant note is definitely the rum, which is never overpowering.

I had already written a brief comment back then and now I would like to elaborate on it and present it differently. Differently, because I have had the opportunity to test significantly more perfumes since then, and as a result, perceptions change. We all know this; our beloved first fragrance suddenly doesn’t seem so wonderful anymore once we’ve smelled other things.

Man in Black Orient is for me just like the original Man in Black a great fragrance. I find both to be very similar. You can tell that it has the same base DNA. The twist of the Orient for me is that it is noticeably less sweet to almost not sweet at all. This fragrance is also masculine and slightly dark.

After spraying, one immediately notices a distinct rum note, mixed with a slight spice note of cardamom. A minute later, the leather emerges, accompanied by flowers in the background, which I personally find not so harmonious.

The English word "nondescript" beautifully summs up my impression of this scent and come to think of it, I should actually refrain from paying any more attention to this new flanker of "Mon Jasmin Noir" bearing this ridiculously arrogant name of "L'eau Exquise". I can't perceive anything remotely exquisite in this scent - and - to make matters worse, I am not a fan of Kirsten Dunst, photographed with a lion. What does the lion represent? There used to be actresses of natural style and grace ... when was that? Well, decades ago, women like Cathérine Deneuve or Grace Kelly. Nowadays Kirsten Dunst aspires to be a vamp. But I shouldn't digress. "Mon Jasmin Noire L'Eau Exquise" is a weak, faint Cologne-style scent with slight allusions to "Thé Vert" (also by Bvlgari). The tea note is altered by a jasmine touch - and there you go, a quiet whisper... fini. How can the fragrance be linked to the lion and Kirsten in the advert? The fragrance is a kind of olfactory mini-purr belonging to a soft-toy cat. "Eau Exquise" is gone after 30 min. I don't regret it.

Today again the Friday "must round" through the city - with my dear friend. For me, the perfumery is a must - for my friend, a chic boutique. First, it's the fragrance paradise's turn, because then one can stroll on well-scented. Among the tested fragrances, Mon Jasmin noir L`eau Exquise enchanted me particularly - and it ended up in the shopping bag. With this scent, the beautiful song "In the Prater, the trees bloom again" came to my mind - and my stroll back then at the big fair, which is also surrounded by magnificent jasmine bushes. This floral, bright fragrance accompanies me to the legendary Ferris wheel - "The Third Man" and the zither music from Karras send their regards. Soft almond scent wafts from the "treat stands," mixed with green tea. The old trees exhale their woody aroma - a scent mélange that accompanies me into the carriage and high above the rooftops of Vienna. Unfortunately, the suave Orson Welles is not on board - but my green, dewy fragrance surrounds my nose - light and buoyant like the zither sounds, emphasizing the airy feeling. I want to pack my little bag and visit my friend in Vienna - for a stroll in the Prater among blooming bushes and trees. At least I will write to her.

After being overwhelmed by L'Eau's on the market, I'm having a bit of a crisis. *Rolls eyes* Everyone is bringing their summer scents to the table, and help, which one is the best for me? Well, that's difficult. I could just say that L'Eau Exquise smells like Mon Jasmin Noir, only lighter, and that would be that, and you could picture it. But it's not quite that simple. I actually really like L'Eau Exquise as a fragrance, soft, a bit fresh, lightly floral, gentle, and slightly creamy, a true all-rounder. Not as powdery and jasmine-heavy as the previous version, slightly almondy and only lightly sweet. You can't go wrong with this scent; I just wish it had one or two citrus notes to spice things up a bit. Some might even call it boring. It's actually quite a harmonious, fine, exquisite drop, as the name suggests. But, as is often the case with Bvlgari, it disappears after an hour. Of course, a light summer scent can't last forever, but it doesn't come cheap either. It didn't even say a proper goodbye, the exquisite L'Exquise. I'm begging the perfumers here, please release something that lasts more than two hours, and I would be your biggest fan. I remember L'Eau de Chloe lasting better; that lasts at least 4-5 hours. So, it is possible.

So, I dare to write my first comment...... With this fragrance, I experienced love at first "scent"!! Just close your eyes and.... You walk through a blooming summer garden, where the dew drops sparkle like stars in the sun. A light scent of jasmine, white tea, and lemon blossoms envelops you. Floral, but not too heavy. Fresh, but not too cool. A fragrance for women who radiate joy of life and a connection to nature. For me, one of the most beautiful summer fragrances I know...

~ Inspiration ~ After I liked "Jasmin Noir," I coincidentally received a sample of this and was curious about the lighter version. ~ Bottle ~ The bottle made of thick glass looks very elegant and fits well in the hand. The liquid is in a light mint green, which promises a fresh scent. ~ Fragrance ~ Pink pomelo and green almonds create a citrus-fresh, zesty opening that carries throughout the entire fragrance journey. Jasmine remains gently in the background here. White tea adds a slightly bitter note, beautifully rounded off with white musk and woods. ~ Longevity ~ Unfortunately, it lasts only 3-4 hours on my skin (a bit longer on clothing and hair). The sillage stays close to the body; reapplying does not extend the longevity - otherwise, it quickly becomes too scratchy. ~ Occasion ~ A refreshing, unobtrusive scent for warmer days in spring and summer. ~ Conclusion ~ A nice change from my other fruity-sweet perfumes. I like it very much, even though it is green-citrusy and woody-bitter.
Even if it's sleeting, cold, and snowing... For me, spring begins, and that includes L'Eau Exquise...

Thirsty and glowing, I drag myself through the hot desert sand... the sun shimmers... sand cements my dry eyes and nose.... I crave water... shade... I won’t be able to survive much longer in the heat.... One more step and another... I hardly notice that my boiling body is sinking into the hot desert sand..... Days later I awaken...

The notes of this fragrance fit perfectly into my preferences, and my predecessor had me heavily and successfully hooked, so thank you for that. A sample soon found its way to me thanks to the lovely Springflower. The keyword "summer rain" made me very curious, and therefore my expectations for this delicate lightweight were quite high, which wasn't exactly wise.
Somehow, this nicely packaged sample found its way to me, and I was very pleased because I really like Bulgari Jasmin Noir.
..and I can't perceive any jasmine either. Still, it's a nice, light scent - however, in my nose, it bears no resemblance to Jasmin noir. To me, it smells more like Un Jardin sur le Nil.

If the original Idôle Eau de Parfum is a clean rose shampoo, then Idôle Eau de Toilette is a fresh cup of zesty green tea served in a dewy rose garden. This flanker loses most of the sweetness that is found across the rest of the range, but it does have a much brighter, citrusy pop at the beginning. Thankfully, though, the bergamot does not present so sharply as to turn the fragrance into a generic citrus or "cleaning product" scent profile. The tea and rose combine very well, in such a way that it evokes the mental image of young roses on green stems, still just a ways from full, mature blooms. The blend is fresh, invigorating, and has surprising longevity for an eau de toilette, especially seeing as it doesn't have any officially listed base notes. I can still smell traces of it on my skin past the 4-hour mark, though it does become a skin scent. The projection is also soft, but such is the way with EDT's. Idôle Eau de Toilette feels best-suited to spring and summer; this could easily be worn in casual, office, or even some sport settings, though I personally do not have the best luck with bergamot notes when I have been exerting myself and sweating. This is a classy, clean-feeling, easy-to-reach-for rose fragrance for those seeking something light but fleeting. Tea-lovers would likely enjoy this as well, for the realistic green tea note. For those seeking a slightly more unisex fragrance, or for those who love green tea but do not enjoy rose notes, I recommend Proad Green Tea, which is a bit sharper and has a bolder citrus note (lemon), but falls into a very similar scent category.

I'm surprised I like Idole EdT as much as I do. Upon spraying the rose overpowers for the first ten minutes. After that it blends nicely with the green tea. The bergamot is somewhere in the back, barely noticeable. As time passes, the rose slowly disappears and the green tea and bergamot start coming out more and more. Wonderful freshness that turns the rose light and airy instead of heavy and stuffy. It makes me feel both young and classy. A perfect scent for the transition of young girl into strong and feminine woman. Personally, I've always had trouble with rose fragrances as I find them overbearing. The original Idole EdP is much too heavy on the rose for me, so ordering a decent of the EdT was quite a gamble for me. This smells a bit like "Pure DKNY - Rose / A Drop of Rose | DKNY / Donna Karan", except Idole EdT is an even more pleasant blend. It is not too overpowering and quite fresh thanks to the green tea, which makes it a good choice for warm weather. It lasts surprisingly long for an EdT too, going strong for well over 6 hours. It's a far cry from the original Idole EdP and most of its flankers, but very enjoyable nonetheless. A rose fragrance for those of us who are scared of rose fragrances! I do think it is too expensive for an EdT, but then again I live in a country where fragrances have been becoming more and more expensive. Might be found for a decent price in other countries.

That "other" website has fragrance notes not listed here or on the official Lancôme site and I really wish I took that information to heart as I do not like vanilla or patchouli. I don't think it's overbearing and it does smell expensive, I just can't stand when those notes are prominent. I don't detect any green tea or bergamot. I haven't had much luck with green tea, but bergamot has never been difficult for me to discern, so it may be that my splash sample has lost its top notes. The heart and base of the fragrance is a little green, rosy, powdery, sweet, and cedar-y, with a hefty dose of patchouli and vanilla. It feels very similar to Le Parfum Eau de Parfum . It's fine for what it is, but it's not to my tastes.

Alcohol & Vetiver leading forthright to a focus on a "fresh", effervescent and zingy mandarin orange. Maybe here an orange by any other name is a "quince"? Possibly with a slight sprinkling of this so-called "salt" in the opening. No seaside. No cookie, but it does take the biscuit, and it's certainly not cricket. Nice but boring. Fresh, fruity, woody. Not salty. Edit on the seventh of August 2017: I began to doubt my initial opinion of this scent. I retested it and got the same result. This is, from top to bottom, as before, mainly orange peel and vetiver. Nothing else worthy of mention. I get no salt. No ginger. No floral. No beeswax. I'm not about to say I smell something just because it's written in the notes. Edit 10th of January 2017: Got this at a bargain price and am testing on skin for the first time. Other notes are coming through - some fizzy sweetness - and this is slightly more enjoyable than my tests on card, but orange rind is still the prominent dominator here. Smells like it could possibly squeeze into the lighter side of the Hermes Eau de Merveilles family. Overall I personally feel that this was already done far better by Montblanc with Presence d'une Femme. Funnily enough, the bottles are conspicuously alike also.

This reminds me of Autumn nights on Padre Island, bonfire ablaze and the air heavy with salt on a pulsating breeze, tiny crabs running sideways here and there and the shore dotted with seashells like pearls in the sand. The crisp ginger and sweet, juicy quince dance in a unique accord over the depth of the wood and sweetness of the amber in the base. She does remind me vaguely of my husband's Aqva Pour Homme (the shared DNA is quite obvious to my nose) and I love that one, though like someone else has mentioned, the Pour Homme is by far a stronger, larger-projecting fragrance. For this one I suspect the warmer it is outside, the more she will completely unfold and shine. As it is on this cool Spring morning, I am nostalgically transported back to the Gulf Coast shores, surrounded by friends and the gorgeous salted air. Scent: 9/10 probably 10 in warmer temps Performance (longevity): Moderate. Fair enough. Value: Good. No complaints about the price for what I've received in exchange. Sillage: depends largely on application. With 3 sprays, moderate. A small caveat worth mentioning: I oversprayed this once and made myself nauseous so start out with this one cautiously. She is a beauty, though. Just be careful, folks. ♥

Today I am wearing Aqva Divina through the kindness of a friend, and it is one of those feminine perfumes, that even feeling delicate and tender, has that subtle woody touch, which makes it possible for a man to dress without problems. A fine, fresh and delicate fragrance is not invasive or annoying, on the contrary, it is extremely refreshing and relaxing, very pleasant, where, for me, the protagonists are ginger and quince, on a light background of amber of woody warmth , with very nice floral and salty nuances. In general this is the aroma, except that, at the start, the bergamot gives it an extra touch of momentary freshness, but it is light and lasts a sigh, and then, in the final drying, the amber woods have more prominence, otherwise, the perfume is a fresh quince, juicy, tender and spicy by ginger, with a slight floral aura, exquisite, and all about, the aforementioned, subtle bed of woods, warm, ambered and sweet, really nice . You can see the hand of Morillas in this, the king of subtle and delicate aromas. The yield is moderate, it is not a pump, but it is compliant, and above all it is very cool to cope with these heats, so you know, it is a very good option to dress during the day, in warm and warm seasons. It is not the typical unisex perfume, you can see its feminine execution, but if you are open-minded, it is an easy scent to wear, yes, any man will not like it, but that's like everything, to taste the colors, but if you have it at hand, and you want to try it, go ahead, it's a very good option to try new things and get out of the routine. Sorry for my bad english.

Even after my recent doctor's visit, I found myself back in the perfume department of Karstadt. I needed to treat myself and browsed through the Bvlgari fragrances. There, I had begun my journey into memory the previous week. I wanted to continue wandering in those footsteps. At the very bottom of the shelf stood a somewhat shabby box and an even shabbier tester. But what a beautiful surprise it contained: "Aqva Divina"! This goddess painted a summer day for me in a house by the sea: in the air, a hint of salt dances with the scent of bergamot. The sharpness of ginger harmonizes in a pleasantly sparkling way. A slightly salty, fresh, and peppery opening. Very lively! The floral aspect of this fragrance only emerges later. The delicate aroma of waxy white-pink magnolia blossoms mixes in; the quince remains a bit in the background; it stays more of a suggestion. Well, the beeswax does remind one a bit of furniture polish. However, I love freshly polished wood, gleaming and lightly fragrant. This makes the illusion of my house by the Mediterranean perfect. Thus, a thoroughly harmonious scent image is completed. A watercolor with softly flowing colors, without hard lines, hardly any shadows - a bit impressionistic. The longevity is quite compatible with the name part "water": I didn't expect more. "Aqva Divina" invites for reapplication and also for lingering. I met a goddess who lightly, almost weightlessly surrounds herself with a veil of fragrance.

I had been away from Aqva Divina for a long time, but I found the idea of salt incredibly exciting. After all, I often find aquatic fragrances quite boring, and salt could add more substance to it and be the salt in the soup. The first impression of the scent is radiant, fresh, full, bright, Mediterranean, and invigorating. Truly an aqua. However, within a very short time, the true character of the fragrance reveals itself, and for me, it is profoundly feminine, mature, sensual, classic, and not as light as one might expect, even though it is not a heavy scent. I don't immediately detect the salt, but it gives the fragrance something intimate. The substance that I usually miss in aquatic scents is already present. The penetrating quality of bergamot with ginger disappears after about half an hour, and the fragrance becomes more powdery with a dominant magnolia. Always in the background is the quince, which gives Aqva Divina a beautiful, delicate sweetness. I find the beeswax in the base surprising, but it grounds the scent very pleasantly along with amber. Woody components are almost completely absent, which is quite unusual these days. Overall, I really like Aqva Divina, and although the fragrance pyramid reads rather unusually, it is still a pleasing scent that is suitable for all occasions, but certainly not a little-girl fragrance. The longevity is good, and the sillage is moderate. I think Bvlgari has once again created a fragrance with the potential to become a classic.

Who would have thought that opposites like sweet and salty could harmonize so well? This works not only in food but also in fragrances. The scent notes of Aqva Divina intrigued me from the very beginning. Accordingly, I was totally thrilled when I received a sample. At home, I had to spray it on immediately. I really perceive the salt combined with bergamot.

~ Inspiration ~ It actually landed on my watchlist only because of the beautiful bottle, as the fragrance notes didn't particularly appeal to me... During a swap with Jenny05, I received a sample for testing. ~ Bottle ~ You can already tell by the round, flat shape, which looks like a polished gemstone, that it is a Bvlgari.

Today I received a small sample of this fragrance and tested it throughout the day. I had no preconceived notions about the scent components and approached this creation completely unbiased. Like my predecessor, I thought that "Divina" is more unisex. After about an hour, the heaviness dissipates, and I inevitably have the following associations: India. Temples.

When I first encountered Aqva Divina, I was uncertain. I felt torn back and forth - similar to Marni. Both start with bergamot and ginger - only Divina culminates in salt, while Marni ends with pepper. But I practiced patience. Divina also takes a milder turn once the initial waves have settled. The salty note lingers longer, deepening the impression of foamy waves.

Even though it seems otherwise in the reviews "above": The beautiful scent lasts a very long time (around 8!) .. it also has more sillage...(between 7 and 8) and is not a bit "watery". It does have something of seawater: The crisp freshness and the salt. I would also describe it as "floral," but not in a sweet way. Pleasantly tart-fruity as well.

Released in 1982, Trophée is a sporty green scent; and - as such - is in the same family as Lauder’s Alliage (1972) which was marketed to women. It’s a fresh woody-citrus, which has a lime head and a small jasmine heart, and because it has both masculine and feminine tropes (woody citrus, floral) it’s possible to read Trophée as a mixed scent. This reading is backed up by an advert from 1983, where a bottle is flanked by two golfers; one male, the other female. 1982 was the year when Vanderbilt was released for women, and Quorum was on the guy side of the aisle. In this context, we can see how the Trophée’s citrus and jasmine doesn’t fit with the gender stereotypes of the day; it’s neither a heady tuberose Amber nor a barbershop fougère. In fact, in this regard, Trophée has more in common with the citrus, green tea and florals of cK One; which in 1994, rejected ‘his’ and ‘hers’ perfumery by declaring itself androgynous; a shared perfume for him ‘and’ her. Trophée was around long before that, and even though its gender positioning was subtle, almost below the radar, Trophée was, to some extent, a pioneer of the modern gender-neutral perfume. In terms of its structure, with it’s light character and short persistence Trophée lies somewhere between the cologne and an EdT. In this sense it feels like an earlier release from the same house, Ô de Lancôme (1969). Trophée is a light and pleasant Green scent, which is not the easiest thing to do in perfumery. Credit should go to the unknown perfumer who worked on it, they did a good job. I hope the 2002 version is the same, but with moss in the formula it’s likely to be different.

It opens with a citrus note, not far from Eau Sauvage, followed by lavender with some basil and jasmine. Along with the jasmine I also get a pretty clear note of marigold though it is not listed, which gives it just a tiny tiny resemblance to Hugo Boss Sport. After this, it dries down to a great grassy-green chypre on a musky base of vetiver and patchouli with a decent shot of moss, which actually smells like another kind of moss than oakmoss, not sure what kind it is ? The scent is big, but not loud and very well-mannered. Overall, an excellent scent in a somewhat quirky bottle. Sillage is good and longevity is excellent, even if the bottle is some 20 years+. An impressive piece of work.

are two of the most famous comic characters by Walter Moers. I must admit that I don't know his comics particularly well, and yet I choose the 'little asshole' and the 'old sack' as an analogy to comment on the latest addition to my collection - Trophée Lancôme pour le Sport - a truly wonderful new addition that I already can't imagine living without, to give that away right from the start. The 'little asshole' because rarely (or never?) has a fragrance - especially one that I have never really smelled before - driven me so persistently. I am a confessed bottle buyer - ugly bottles do not enter my house! - and although it is quite old-fashioned and quirky in design, especially the bottle has captivated me - the stylized golfer on the front, the little golf ball as a screw-off cap - I find it simply delightful! It reminds me a bit of those hand-drawn brochures from the third quarter of the last century, where radiant families laugh down into lush valleys from sun-drenched terraces, and their gaze reveals: 'Your family could be this happy too!' And although I am not a fan of splash bottles, it was clear from the beginning that the far less iconically designed spray bottle (boring shape and no golf ball on top) was never seriously considered. Every few months, it crossed my path again - mostly here, sometimes elsewhere - and each time I thought to myself: 'Damn it, I want that!' And since this is a fragrance that has been discontinued for years - if not decades - I couldn't smell it anywhere beforehand - it was either a blind purchase via the internet (something I had never done and never wanted to do) or nothing at all. So my first blind purchase and: hooray! And now I come to the 'old sack'. It's a bit like cooking with perfumes - if you have some experience, you can quite well estimate how the result will smell or taste just by reading the ingredients. So I knew that Trophée Lancôme pour le Sport would smell old-fashioned, a creation of the late 70s and early 80s - and how a thirty-five-year-old fragrance - presumably my specimen would be almost as old - has survived the years, one cannot say. But my boldness was rewarded, because this is a truly fabulous fragrance - my first (and probably only) one with 'Sport' in the name, by the way. It is herbal like sun-warmed hay - with a gently underlying fougère accord that clearly reveals we are dealing with a true gentleman here. The lack of citrus freshness may be due to its age, and the diffuse sweetness in its green-golden heart tells of a sun-drenched forest floor and picnics by the shores of a glowing blue lake. From the peaceful idyll of days gone by - Rock Hudson and Doris Day at the country club - past, but not so long ago that no one remembers it anymore. A dreamy warm, grounded, sovereign fragrance. And yes - even the 'Sport' in its name can be left as is. Conclusion: it was a little asshole, and it is still an old sack. And the new secret star in my collection - one with 'Sport' in the name, who would have thought?

My father not only brought beautiful gifts in the form of perfumes into the house, but he also brought his own sillage across the threshold for me. How I loved to sniff him during the greeting kiss! The scents always matched the simple elegance of his clothing perfectly. One day, I noticed a particularly fresh green scent on him. It smelled as if he had just come from a golf course - like green grass surrounded by lemon trees. Refreshing, yet subtle. After a while, the mysterious tonka bean wafted over, mixed with dark moss. I praised the beautiful scent, and he told me that unfortunately he could no longer find it anywhere. I couldn't accept that.
