I searched in various perfumeries and finally found a bottle of the matching shower gel. At least. I proudly presented my find to him, and he was truly touched by my effort. Even today, I still keep an eye out for Trophee pour le Sport - as a memory of my father.

First-class scent that catapults me back to the 80s / my youth. It smells like business trips, briefcases, business, and success. Not too much business, because today there’s no tie over the shirt, and in the afternoon it’s off to the golf course. Exactly like the little man on the bottle! At first, a fantastic fresh note, in the middle (which lasts forever) a cozy warmth with the carefree spirit of the 80s, which then gently fades away by evening. I wear the scent explicitly in my free time, because it’s too precious for work, as it’s getting harder to find!

When worn, Gyan is a sexy cloud of resinous smoky patchouli with a sweet jasmine sambac radiating from the center. The patchouli is not that "hippie smelling" patchouli, this is a rich and refined patchouli. Gyan is a smooth non-cloying fragrance (unless you really over do it) that can be worn anywhere - Black tie events, office, out with friends, or on a date with that special someone. Gyan gets a lot of unsolicited compliments and smells fantastic. Gyan projects around 2 meters (6ft) and leaves a nice smoky sweet jasmine trail of fragrance in your wake. As far as I am concerned, this is a year-round fragrance. Hot or cold weather, you will always smell great. Gender-wise Gyan would smell great on men and women 25+. Younger people that prefer fresh scents will probably not appreciate this as much. Gyan as well as the rest of the Le Gemme collection can only be purchased at a Bvlgari boutique online or in one of their brick and mortar locations. Yes the Le Gemme men's line is a little pricey ($310 for 100 ml) but honestly, you are also paying for presentation as well as the amazing juice. The box is very nicely padded. The sleek black bottle is topped with a blue gem. Each Le Gemme fragrance has its own gem color. I have tried each one and all are worth trying out. Gyan is a solid 10/10

Smells fantastic, blend is unreal. Oranges jasmine clean patchouli, some woods in base and incense. All year round fragrance. Performance is extremly bad, like extremly with bold letters. Turns into skin scent after 2 hours. Longevity 4-5 hours at max. Can be worn any season any occasion. Dumb reach. Got mine for 45€ for 30 ml bottle. Definetly not worth of the enormous retail price.

Personal: 7.5/10 – I have darker taste, so this isn't entirely for me, but I do like it. I would definitely wear a clone of it. Mass appeal: 7.5/10 – Incense and patchouli are polarizing but this is a fairly clean, safe take on them. Performance: 8/10 – Solid projection and longevity, though not beast mode. Value: 3/10 – This is a luxury priced line from a jewelry house. It's a great blend that's very approachable, but for over $300, it's absolutely bonkers. Uniqueness: 7.5/10 – Incense/patchouli frags are common, but Gyan’s blend is particularly smooth and clean. SCORE: 67/100 Full bottle buy? NO, disqualified on price alone, honestly. Blind buy? NO, patchouli + incense is divisive, and the price is WAY too steep. Recommend? YES, if you want a very polished, light incense and patchouli frag. Date night? YES, in upscale, formal settings – it’s refined, not seductive. Office safe? NO, incense still reads a bit heavy for close quarters, but in the winter you MIGHT be able to pull it off. Pros: Smooth, refined incense and patchouli. Well-blended, luxurious, elegant. Cons: Extremely pricey. Generic DNA despite the price tag. Somewhat unique, but not groundbreaking. Bvlgari Gyan is part of their high-luxury Le Gemme line, and it smells like it belongs there. It's very smooth, resinous, and clean, despite the patchouli and incense base that would otherwise make this bottle lean dark. I actually think it's a fairly bright, warm-ish weather fragrance that on cooler days, could even work during the summer. It opens with a darker, greenish burst of patchouli but is calmed by white florals immediately. It has a warm, somewhat spicy, very resinous base that lasts fairly well, and smells great the whole time. Really, at half the price, I think this would be a great buy, but for around $300, it's impossible to fully endorse, unless you REALLY want THIS fragrance specifically. And if what you want is a clean, polished, very wearable patchouli fragrance, maybe this IS what you really want. Smooth, clean, likable, polished patchouli and incense. Not your usual fragrance, but not your usual price tag either. Review #109 in my fragrance journey – this fragrance I own as a decant

Where do I even start ! This is beautiful. This is one of the most beautiful, refined, classy scents I have ever smelled in my LIFE. Like any other Le Gemme release, notes don't show the depth of the fragrances. But to keep it simple: this is Bleu de Chanel Eau de Parfum , but made 10x more elegant. I can go as far as calling Gyan a "winter freshie", thanks to its own type of freshness, which suits a well-dressed gentleman on a formal occasion during the colder season. The moment this smell hits the cold air, it turns magnetic. You keep wanting to smell more of it. The sweet, smoky, incense-y jasmine in the scent trail, along with the earthy-clean patchouli. Its so weird to describe ! Because this doesn't make sense. We don't deserve such a fragrance. This is so well done, its perfect. You can't quite put your finger on what you're smelling. Easily one of the best fragrances in my collection, and out of everything that I've smelled so far during this journey.

Today, I would like to take you on a journey. A journey to the origin, to nothingness, into pure darkness. Into a world where we realize that we know nothing at all. That we are just a tiny part of something incomprehensibly vast. I have always found the exploration of the universe to be very exciting.

This Tresor was not a flanker, but a distinct perfume. Sophia Grojsman wanted a collaboration wotu Dominique Ropion and ...voila: L Absolu Tresor. A stunner, an exquisite potion made only from.raw materials and absolutes, 100%. It jas been produced only few months in 2013. The price - $150 for the unique amount 50 ml was not so comfortable for the customers. The production costs were huge, the selling poor because of the price, so, in the end of 2013, few months since lauching the production has been stopped and Tresor L.Absolu discontinued forever. It is a beautiful lerfume with the Tresor vintage DNA, but with a leather velvety hint in it and a fumé vanilla absolute, that makes this fragrance a stunner. It is unique as smell, the bottle is also gorgeous...so...a masterpiece with a very short life unfortunately.

I have been enchanted by the classic Trèsor scent since the first time I smelled it. No, I should rather say, since the first time I wore it on my skin. This fragrance only develops fully and in its true splendor when worn on the skin. It needs body heat and soft skin to completely unfold. I discovered this new version one day on the internet. I found the bottle quite impressive with its black-tinted glass. Although it has the same shape as the classic Trèsor, you can tell there is something mysterious and dark inside. It is a dark, deep, and mystical dark red, almost black rose. No, there are many of these beautiful Damask roses. They exude a deep, almost intoxicating scent, with a heavy, spice-laden sweetness. The sweetness is that of a dark rose liqueur, or that of a heavy perfume oil. For me, it is by no means too sweet and not too heavy. It is not sticky like syrup, or oily but deep, powdery, dark, and fine. All in all, the scent is simply very pleasant. This version reminds me in its basic structure of the original Trèsor, completed with new, darker facets. The L'Absolu de Parfum is for me the perfected version of the great classic. It is the epitome of a perfume for me. This is exactly how "my perfume" should smell. It truly lacks nothing. The formulation is completely perfect and beautiful as it is. But the dark, spicy rose is not the only thing that impresses me. The fragrance also includes bright, pink roses that create a play of scent impressions in the heart and top notes. A bright, lovely scent impression accompanies the Trèsor. In combination with the jasmine, they make the scent brighter, lovelier, and more erotic. Benzoin and vanilla provide the dark rosy accompanied, balsamic-vanilla base. As a gourmand, I would not describe the scent at all. There is no risk of confusion with a sweet treat, although the aromas are very delicious. If I had to live with only one perfume, it would be Trèsor L'Absolu de Parfum. I hope it stays and is not taken off the market as quickly as various flankers. Unfortunately, I do not detect any leather, and I was really looking forward to leather. But it is already complete as it is. The longevity is extremely good at 14 hours. I applied it in the evening, had the scent in my nose all night, and still perceived it until noon. This is now my Absolute No 1.

I waited a long time for it and ordered it blindly, as scents with a leather note always pique my curiosity. Unpacked with great expectation, sprayed on... And was disappointed. Piercing, typical Trésor. Pack it up, send it back? No, I won't give up that quickly... The lady has an invitation to a candlelight dinner at a nice restaurant. She only knows the gentleman from the internet. What does she expect? What does he expect? First, play the innocent, not too revealing clothing, rose scent with a hint of peach is perfect for that. The two take an immediate liking to each other, the conversation during dinner becomes more private. Warm spices mix with the rose, they get closer and forget the time. After dessert, the obligatory question: "Are you coming back to my place?" She quickly convinces him to come with her. She unlocks the door, her apartment is bathed in soft light. The air carries a light scent of vanilla, mixed with a bit of patchouli, the atmosphere crackles. The rose that the gentleman gave her was left in the taxi. She goes to the kitchen to get the champagne from the fridge. When she reappears, the gentleman's breath catches. She has swapped her high-necked dress for a leather corset... What else might the evening bring? Those who have enough patience will be surprised by the scent. Waiting it out really pays off, as the warm leather note remains well hidden for a long time.

Today was a beautiful day. My nose behaved quite normally, and I had the opportunity to try "l Absolu" for the second time. The first attempt was on a very hot day; today, at 12 degrees, it was significantly cooler. Following the last test, I sniffed my clothing for days; I was truly longing for this scent. All the more surprising is that it leads a nearly undiscovered shadow existence here; I can only imagine that many are deterred by the name Tresor. Well, the similarity is undeniable, and one should not have completely rejected the original (not the current chemical version). Then, however, it can begin, because even with the second test, I can only confirm my first impression: this scent is a dream! Immediately after spraying, a huge, magnificent Damask rose blooms on my skin. Velvety and dark with a somehow oily but not heavy, deep sweetness...trrrrreamy. Not gourmand, not sticky, not girlish. This scent is mature, a refinement of the original; with it, I can simply be a woman, feminine, sensual, but with class, romantic, yet not playful. It wraps around me, envelops me; it is, in the truest sense of the word, delicious. A wonderful composition. You can let yourself fall into this scent. I notice nothing of the listed patchouli; the leather also passes me by, not a problem, I couldn't imagine it more beautifully. Rose (but not Dr. Hauschka rose oil-too true to nature for me, more like rose liqueur!), spices for depth, vanilla finely dosed, sophisticated and "biteable" at the same time. The sillage is enormous but not overwhelming; even in warm weather, it was not too much for me. I perceive it as a kind of chameleon, as it adapts to all situations. With it, I can go to the office, read a book on the couch on Sundays, pick up my child from kindergarten, or play at the playground; just as well, it dresses me for a visit to the opera, indeed "my little black dress for every day". A real discovery that quickly makes its way to my wish list; I thank Sonjoschka very much, for without her comment, I would have never tried this scent. Hhhmmm...and now my nose sinks back contentedly into my turtleneck, a lovely evening to you all:-)

Treasure L'Absolu had already caught my attention positively at its launch in 2013. Recently, I hadn't seen this version in the perfume shops anymore, so I wished for it for Christmas. The day before yesterday, at the Christmas brunch, it was handed to me. I opened the packaging and held the elegant bottle in my hands. My brother spontaneously said, it looks like Darth Vader :-). But all jokes aside, I can only echo the comments here: L'absolu is a richly darker version of the classic Treasure scent. Fruity notes (peaches), which dominate the base chord of the classic Treasure in conjunction with roses, play no role here. The roses in L'absolu are darker and silkier and blend excellently with the balsamic notes of benzoin and later vanilla. The fragrance also never veers into sweetness, as the spices and patchouli accompany the entire scent journey, giving the perfume a dark chord. A fragrance for special occasions, perfectly suitable for going out.

What a glorious rose! I definitely did not expect to find a rose scent of this calibre from such a well-known, mainstream brand. Rose Essentielle is pure loveliness. Being absolutely perfect for Spring and Summer wear, this is a sweet and slightly powdery take on a pretty, pink rose note. Classy, feminine and smooth, each and every note in this composition works in unison. With most rose scents, the rose note tends to become too sharp and somewhat tart-like throughout the fragrance's development. In the case of Rose Essentielle, this is not an issue. This fragrance is easy to wear and effortlessly pretty. It's lightness and subtle berry sweetness only adds to its widespread appeal. Initially this fragrance goes on rather strong, with a rich, jammy rose, highlighted by the berry notes and the violet. After a few hours the scent settles into a delicate, powdery rose, which is thankfully not the soapy kind. Lady-like, refined and romantic, this fragrance encouraged me to get in touch with my feminine side. The lasting strength is very good, especially for that of such a soft, light fragrance. I can see Rose Essentielle being worn well in every season, both casually and formally. It has just the right amount of realistic roses and complexity to make this fragrance absolutely outstanding.

Initially I was quite pleased with my acquisition of Bvlgari ROSE ESSENTIELLE. I ordered a large tester bottle of the edp scent unsniffed because I am a huge fan of the original BVLGARI POUR FEMME and had read that there were overlaps between the two. And there are. The rose and the violet and the mimosa, for starters. However, there are also differences. ROSE ESSENTIELLE has a much more synthetic feeling. In some ways, I find it closer to Costume National SCENT GLOSS than to BVLGARI POUR FEMME. This synthetic quality becomes especially marked when I liberally apply ROSE ESSENTIELLE, at which point I begin to feel a bit as I do when I over apply MISS BOUCHERON. In both cases, what starts as a likeable perfume starts to become somewhat irritating to my lungs. I do think that the synthetic quality is not gratuitous--as with the perfumes of Costume National, there is an artistic point to this. The concept of an abstract rose looms large in this composition. Still, I would caution those who are sensitive to synthetic florals to try before they buy.

I wanted ROSE ESSENTIELLE to be different enough from BVLGARI POUR FEMME to warrant buying a bottle, but the two are too similar after only 15 minutes. That said, both dry down beautifully (and the same), and smell gorgeous on clothes. But if you own one, you basically own the other.

Starts as a powdery rose. The Rose fades and more powder moves in. When the powder becomes bored and moves on the rose finds its way out again. Lasted over 12 hours on me and I am STILL smelling the (powdery) rose!

This could be Yves Saint Laurent Paris offspring. This would be its contemporary and modest (maybe even a wee bit shy) granddaughter. Where YSL Paris is a bombastic (but delectable) explosion of roses, this carries overlapping dna poured in a more subdued and rounded form. Where YSL Paris turns heads and commands attention, this rose is very sweet and well mannered. Very nice I must say, but not necessarily groundbreaking (but is that always necessary?) In the drydown it deviates more from YSL Paris as the violets ard more prominent and a sweet freshness is what is left (YSL is more tangy). Good to use on very hot days if you're in the mood for rose paired with some violets or when you want to wear a good crowdpleaser.

Dear Dr. Sommer Team! I have a problem that I feel a bit ashamed about. I don't want to burden my parents with it. My siblings have similar difficulties, but it's not as bad for them as it is for me. I come from a good family. But not everyone speaks well of me. Many have noticed my weakness. My classmates always look at me that way.

Since I know that Floris's Rose Post is already waiting for me at the post office, I have to practice a bit on a rose fragrance comment. This rose fragrance is very straightforward. I smell rose and that's it. So I’ll try to describe this rose to you: It is very sweet and has something artificial about it.

No fragrance has enchanted me about women as much as this one so far, unfortunately, it is rarely smelled. Truly a wonderful composition that includes style, elegance, an oriental-mysterious essence, and also a huge dose of sex appeal.

If you’re not into heavy rose scents, you should give this little rose a try. It’s a rather light rose fragrance. Floral, powdery, fresh... those are the keywords that come to mind. For me, however, it’s just a bit too light and inconspicuous. I’ve experienced some much more impressive rose fragrances ;)

If you like rose scents, you can't really complain about the scent of Rose Essentielle at first. It is a cute, sweet rose fragrance that is successfully composed with other notes. However, this rose is neither proud nor vain. It is delicate and girlish and completely harmless.

I immediately detected petit grain upon applying Annick Goutal DUEL, and what I thought was vetiver! According to the notes, which apparently include gaiac wood, not indicated above, what I am perceiving as vetiver is an olfactory illusion created out of wood and maté. However, maté can be quite bitter, which this composition certainly is not. DUEL is smooth and calm, and as it dries down, it feels ever-so-slightly leathery, but not in the off-putting, rubbery, synthetic way in which so many in-your-face leather fragrances are today. To my nose, DUEL is neither masculine nor feminine. It is quiet and conservative, not at all a loud cologne guy frag or bracing citrus slap in the face. I rather like this creation and although I do catch wafts of pencil shavings along with the leather, the overall effect is very light and pleasing to my nose. DUEL reminds me a bit of the scent of sand and the sound created by walking along a pebble-littered path, as odd as that may seem. It find this creation quite serene. The quality is indisputably niche. Another fine fragrance from the house of Annick Goutal.

Duel is a nicely done aromatic fragrance with hints of leather, citrus, tea and rich tobacco. It's subtly done, and is a wonderful choice for Spring and Summer wear. Annick Goutal tends to make rather bold orientals or sharp citrus scents, however Duel is not so 'in your face'. Although masculine, it's not strictly so, preferring to adopt a unisex feel, which is both elegant and unique. While I think Sables has more character, I like Duel's refreshing approach. It's clean and light but not in a boring aquatic or citrus after-shave sense of the word. It doesn't smell generic or for that matter, like anything you'd find the average man wearing. It's quite cozy and lovable. The tea note stands out the most for me, followed by smokey tobacco and subtle hints of lemon and lime. It can be quite linear at times, however I'm not too bothered with its lack of development. I enjoy the scent nonetheless. Perhaps its only disappointing aspect was its lack of lasting power and strong projection. I'm used to Annick Goutal's male fragrances being lasting and bold. In regards to price, Duel is rather cheap when compared to other fragrances from this house. It may be worth trying if your man, or even yourself, wouldn't feel cheated if the fragrance only lasted a few hours and required touch-ups during the day.

Since I am currently in an Annick Goutal frenzy, I took the plunge. Blind, so to speak. A bottle of Duel was offered. Now it’s mine. The first sniff was a bit off-putting. Tea! Doesn’t it smell a bit like green tea? The theme is actually mate and mate tea, which I haven’t drunk in what feels like centuries. Two days later, I sprayed my new AG again and took it to the office for further testing. The initial bitterness of the tea fades after a while. Then it becomes warmer with a hint of petitgrain freshness, a trace of leather, and a little bit of hay. Further down, the scent was compared to gold. I gladly agree - the scent progression is golden-citrusy-warm-fresh. Can you make something of that? I don’t really perceive the other mentioned notes. It may be that they develop differently on women’s skin or specifically on mine. But I have noticed something quite strange for myself: It is a comfort to me. Can a scent be comforting? A magical substance or a memory of cozy childhood moments? Recently, I felt terribly bad; heartache with tears flowing. At night, I woke up and longed for the scent of Duel. Does anyone know that feeling? I was sure that this very smell on my skin would carry me safely through the next day and allow my soul to recover. So I did just that. It may be that this comment is of no use to anyone, but I was comforted.

A quote from the official Goutal site: "Duel is the fragrance for the man who lives his life boldly, fearlessly, and courageously..." Rarely have I read such a silly, almost "reputation-damaging" nonsense from a manufacturer about its own product. Luckily, I was not familiar with this saying or had just successfully repressed it in time when I bought a bottle of "Duel" a few years ago. Otherwise, I would probably have disregarded it with a "just too bad" attitude. I can be particular. And that would have been a shame, because I would have missed something: The scent of a vast landscape, whose fresh, natural aroma the wind carries along - yellow-brown like dry grass, olive green like dry leaves, and reddish-brown like dusty, warm earth. The scent of the South American grass steppes, the Pampas. The main theme of Duel is "Mate" - a traditional, bitter-herb infusion drink of the South American indigenous people. With colonization, it became a popular drink, especially in Paraguay, Argentina, and Chile. It is made from the dried leaves of the mate tree, which, due to their caffeine content and high tannin levels, have performance-enhancing and appetite-suppressing effects. Traditionally, mate is prepared in small gourd calabashes, which are refilled with hot water throughout the day, and it is drunk through metallic straws with a filter at the bottom, called bombillas. To return to the opening quote: With "Duel," no duel can be won. It is anything but "fearless and bold," and the only courageous aspect is choosing an ingredient like "Mate" as the main theme for a perfume. It is neither loud nor powerful nor in any way "back-strengthening"; on the contrary: the longevity is modest, the sillage discreet, the scent delicate. Nevertheless: With "Duel," Annik Goutal has once again proven that one can bottle a feeling, an image, a landscape in perfume bottles. In France, there is the term "Terroir" for this - a concept for which there is no German translation for the underlying idea. It states that high-quality (agricultural) products, e.g., high-quality wines, carry the individual taste and character of the specific region in which they grow: its climate, its mineral soil composition - the scent of the landscape. Annik Goutal achieves this with her perfumes. Recommendation? Recommendation!!

Duel is a scent that actually isn’t really there. It is one of the particularly subtle perfumes. You don’t need to use it too sparingly. Here, you can spray generously and occasionally reapply! Duel is very difficult to describe. Upon spraying, it is only briefly slightly lemony, probably from the Petit Grain. Then comes an indefinable smell reminiscent of a certain type of plastic. I thought I had a chemical cocktail à la Comme des Garçons in front of me. Then the scent becomes a bit greener, but not juicy green, rather like dried leaves. Oak leaves that have already fallen from the tree in the dry August heat, a dusty, sandy smell, even slightly smoky. Annick Goutal evokes the image of underbrush in the forest, but I do not agree with that. Except perhaps a forest in the southern France, after a long period of heat and drought, when wildfires are imminent. What is it? Well hidden, you can find the answer on Annick Goutal's website - it is mate! Mate is the theme of this fragrance. A long time ago, I drank mate tea. I just believe that this fits. In addition to mate, iris root and leather are mentioned. Both are not prominently present. What is to be made of this? Duel is certainly a very unusual men’s fragrance. I don’t know any other men’s scent that revolves around mate. That is something special and also confuses experienced noses. Duel can thus be considered a very individual scent. I see Duel as a fragrance for daily use on any occasion. It is extremely subtle. I think it gives the wearer a certain presence without the surroundings necessarily attributing it to the use of a perfume. However, this also indicates that it is a very demanding scent that one must engage with and give time to. In this respect, it is hardly suitable for perfume junkies - today Le Male, tomorrow A*Men and the day after Duel, that just doesn’t work. In its restraint, Duel requires a few days to merge with the wearer, their clothing, their aura, and thus fulfill its purpose.

It hasn't been long since anything was written here! Yet this is such a beautiful fragrance. I have had Duel for several years now, and there is still some left in the bottle because I also wear other scents in the meantime. I got Duel after a long search at Oberpollinger in Munich, recommended by a very nice saleswoman.

With mate, I immediately associate Birkenstock sandals, nettle cookies, and scratchy cotton sweaters. Everything feels a bit eco-friendly and bursting with political correctness. Additionally, I connect mate with something medicinal. Perhaps this is also the basis for the titular Duel, a fragrance torn between being half sick and almost healthy.

It is indeed a challenge to comment on "Duel" by Annick Goutal. It is as elusive as my counterpart. Does he have his hand on the pistols? The contours of the gaucho blur in the shimmering midday heat of the dusty pampas. I catch a whiff of old, dry leather. This impression fades after a few minutes - and then the gaucho disappears like a mirage.

There are fragrances that, in my opinion, have somewhat inappropriate names for the scent. I mean, Duel is a tea fragrance! Delicate, gentle, fragrant, somewhat polite. Why should such a scent be called Duel? Well, anyway, it was pretty obvious that I would test the fragrance, because you know I’m totally into tea (without any milk lemonade)!

First of all, I must say: I appreciate and love many Goutal fragrances, even though they are (almost always) rather short-lived on the skin and are not exactly the kind of scents you buy "just on the side.

Lancôme is a brand of great diversity. Looking at the timeline it has released so many different fragrances with different expressions: Ô de Lancôme (one of the freshest citric scents I know), Magie Nôire (the black magic of the eighties) and a long line of other triumphs such as Miracle, La Vie est Belle, Tresôr and Hypnôse - just to mention some of them. I then would have expected that a perfume named Attraction would have more to offer. This is a very kind and polite perfume. It does not make a fuzz or shouts out loud. It stays close to the skin and keeps sending out floral notes. It stays like that for a few hours. When it fades, I often think whether I sprayed too little. Did I spray at all?! Well - Attraction will not make it to the history books, I suppose. 201/365

It does not really smell like any of the individual listed notes, because they are all blended together so much that it just becomes it's own new thing. Very sophisticated. Manages to strike a balance between something that you have smelled before and something very unique. This smells the way I imagined a classy lady would have smelled twenty years ago. Hypnotically beautiful. If you can get your hands on a small bottle, do it... this could be worn in any season for any occasion. A gorgeous classy woody floral. Like real gold or diamond jewelry that is dainty enough to be worn daily.

Not bad, but not wonderful either. My opinions on this fragrance keep changing. One minute I'll dislike it, the next minute I'll be somewhat intrigued by its scent. When I first applied Attraction to my wrist I was really confused as to why the gardenia, neroli and ylang ylang blend smelt so spicy and almost bitter on my skin. I guess it's a matter of chemistry although my friend also had the same reaction. Finally when the intial blast of the top notes pass, I am left with a rich and heavy blend of flowers, which in my opinion is pleasant but not very soft or feminine. When Attraction begins to fade and transcend into the drydown the scent becomes sweet and 'vanillary'. This drydown makes me like this fragrance, yet for the first hour I really did not enjoy Attraction in the slightest. To purchase this fragrance simply because I am 'attracted' to the drydown is silly and a waste of money, especially when this fragrance is extremely overpriced. I'd say that overall Attraction would have many positive responses, yet for me it just didn't have the 'wow-factor'. The lasting strength was phenomenal, I guess that's one good point, however I'm not surprised that Lancome has decided to discontinue this fragrance.

to present myself to your wrist? I am curious which beauty, boldly named attraction, hides behind this little fragrance. I spray on: Help, a toxic screeching gardenia leaps at me, provocatively stabbing my nose multiple times. Behind her limps a musty-smelling ylang lady, trying to lull me with stale chatter. Barely wafting past me follows a bunch of hectic, sweet giggling jasmine girls, whose childish screams give me a headache. From afar, 2 little roses wave desperately at me - no chance, they cannot reach me. A plump patchouli girl stomps past me, huffing loudly. Exhausted by so much femininity, I treat myself to a breather. When I cautiously sniff my wrist again after 10 minutes, a pretty one rides past me on a musk ox, she is almost transparent, with sawdust in her hair and a faint whisper of amber. I know, beauty lies in the eye of the beholder, but I wonder: was she really worth the wait? Definitely not for me!

Instead of taking the easy way out of designing a "Rain" fragrance with petrichor. Morillas played with ingredients, and gave us this gem right here. Musky, calming tea, with a citrus opening and a woodsy musky dry down, come together to simulate a feeling of raindrops falling on the windowsill. I'm a big fan of this frag, interesting composition. Clean without effort and without smelling like a shower gel / blue fragrance. Great alternative for those actually. Not gonna project as much as projection junkies would like it to, but that's the point of this, it's clean and you can smell it only if someone comes close to you. Does it smell like rain? In an interesting way, yes. It reminds me of waking up on a rainy morning in clean sheets and I have a self care day. As soon as I get my hands on a good priced bottle I'm picking it up.

tested today at the sephora in lyon part dieu. we are really on a mid-season perfume. Neither refreshing nor warming. It is the same smell as the Margiela Sunday Lazy perfume that I had already evaluated on the site. There is also a similarity with Dior Private Collection Balad Sauvage. There is a smell of figs that stands out a lot, so it is a fruity perfume. discreet sweetness. the cheapest alternative to margiela and especially to dior private collection.

Upon application, I thought: "Wow, this is a really good fresh-aquatic scent. It could be worth a bottle!" But I don't go to the perfume store and test a fragrance just to buy it right away; I also give it time to unfold. For better or for worse. Bvlgari Man Rain Essence starts off beautifully fresh and is very lightly, non-spicy aquatic. A bit like one would imagine a water scent. I would have wished for petrichor to adequately capture the rain theme, but okay, dozens of pseudo-rain fragrances have already failed at that, and one doesn't want to be too demanding. Unfortunately, the fragrance becomes spicier over time and thus takes on a standard aquatic note. I am absolutely not a fan of white lotus, and this particular note starts to bother me more and more as it develops. Additionally, Bvlgari Man Rain Essence also becomes subtly green (the tea) and thus loses its lightness. It becomes somewhat of an average scent. Nice, but a bit boring. I am a little disappointed. It is suitable at the beginning for sports, everyday life, and leisure. Later on, it is more for business. The sillage is solid and dissipates after about 3 hours. The end of projection for me is reached after about 6½ hours. The bottle is, as with the entire Bvlgari Man line, great. What do I do now with this fragrance? Great start, not (quite) so great development. I jumped on it when it was at its cheapest. But will it eventually fall victim to decluttering? Have I let myself be too seduced by the refreshing start? Perhaps I have. Anyone still searching for a scent that smells like fresh rain will not find enlightenment here, that much is certain.

During our summer vacation in 2023 in Büsum at the North Sea, we decided to visit the island of Helgoland for the very first time after all the years we had kept returning here. Anyone who knows Helgoland is aware that there isn't much to see. A nice town center (if you can call it that), surrounded by various duty-free shops. Since I buy a fragrance as a memento on every vacation and associate it with that trip forever, I naturally had to go into one of those stores. So I sniffed my way through all the shops and pretended that there wasn't basically the same selection in every store. At that time, I was still a complete beginner when it came to perfumes. I had just started to really engage with scents, but I had already smelled just about every type of fragrance. Therefore, it was always something special for me to smell a fragrance that was completely new to me. And there it was, the Bvlgari Man Rain Essence. A bottle that I personally didn't find very attractive, surrounded by a younger couple who were just being recommended the fragrance by a saleswoman. I listened in discreetly and decided, after the couple had passed on the fragrance, to give it a spray. I didn't expect much, as I said, I didn't find the bottle very appealing. But the scent convinced me right away! It reminded me of the generally rainy day on this beautiful little island. For me, it was like the scent of Helgoland to take with me. When I wear the scent today and close my eyes, I see myself in a light drizzle at around 23 degrees, with my favorite music in my ears, sitting in a beach chair by the sea in Helgoland and enjoying the moment. So much for my not really objective opinion on this fragrance. Thank you to everyone who actually read this through. :D Objectively speaking, I find the scent really nice, but not particularly special. By now, I have smelled several fragrances that were at least similar. Unfortunately, I find the longevity/sillage to be very weak. This was my first review on Parfumo, so please don't be too harsh. :D

I knew it from earlier, specifically the vintage bottle, but I couldn't quite remember what it was like. Now, a little bottle has moved in with me again, and yes, it leaves me speechless. I haven't smelled something this good in a long time. Reading through the fragrance pyramid, one might think that so many different ingredients would be overwhelming. But not for me; on the contrary, I could constantly douse myself in it at the moment (though I only have 30 ml, so caution is advised). So how does it actually smell? If only I could describe it. Here, one wishes to be a poet or at least a writer, because I simply lack the right words. Yes, green notes are definitely present, but which ones? You can also smell a bit of honey, just enough that it doesn’t become overpowering. It also has floral elements, but these never take over. Animalic components are also present, but they somehow fit into the overall picture and never come to the forefront. Everything is unobtrusive, enveloping you with a gentle hand, sometimes green, sometimes floral, sometimes a little woody. This is true perfume artistry, blending everything together so that in the end, you don’t even know what you particularly like, what you love the most? The version currently available for purchase, I also have, but it doesn't come anywhere close to this scent. And once again, it’s such a shame that fragrances of this kind no longer exist and probably never will again. Therefore, we enjoy what we still have.

Lancôme Magie Noir opens the fragrance altar for you, takes you into a dark magical world, full of surprises waiting to be discovered. You find yourself in an enchanted forest, surrounded by berries and dark flowers. Earth with moss and animalistic weight, patchouli also does not fade into oblivion, no one will get in your way so quickly. Her special sensual aura won’t let you go, this composition in the black bottle is simply fabulous. As the fog lifts, you awaken, then you quickly realize: was it all just a dream full of black magic? You have quickly explained it to yourself, this journey was worth it, to dare something new and to carry the dark magic from now on.

Magie Noir was my mom's scent. Tonight I'm still sitting outside, don't want to go inside, don't want to let summer go. I made a fire, it warms my feet. The sky is starry, I'm thinking of you, Mom. Where are you. The song Let it all Go by Birdy and Rhodes makes me endlessly sad. You passed away in November two years ago. We didn't have much in common, but you were my mom. I don't have your scent Magie Noire in my nose, it's in my heart. It's no longer available, you're no longer here. HE was you for me. Patchouli. My fire is quietly fading, I send you a greeting into infinity. I'm thinking of you, Mom.

We met for the first time in high school; we were friends for more than twenty years. It was only after 1989 that we lost sight of each other for good. Two very different young women: Petra - tall, long-limbed, and dark-haired: I - small, petite, and in the end, blonde again. It was not a "We stick together through thick and thin" kind of girl friendship. We had too many personal interests of our own for that. We rarely discussed very private or even intimate matters: that was not our style. Perhaps also because it was not common at the time to constantly "come out". My most intense memories of Petra encompass the time when we were both in our thirties. There were many shared activities, even a two-week vacation at a beauty farm. Yes, that’s what it was called back then: wellness temples had not been invented yet! I still vividly remember her perfume: "Magie Noire" - Black Magic! For a dark-haired woman like her, it was a wonderful scent: full, warm, and sensual! But it is also a fragrance of its time. A time of opulence: Clothing and fragrances were often luxurious; "unisex" had not yet cast its shadow. A woman was a woman - she dressed accordingly and she smelled like it too! "Magie Noire" opens with a wonderfully fruity-green medley: black currant and hyacinth play an excellent role here. Next, honey takes the stage: warm and a bit viscous. It envelops the following flowers, mainly from white spring blooms, with a special charm. Ylang-ylang adds sparkling light accents. So far, it is a very lively fragrance composition. Sensual-erotic, yes, even a bit animalistic, a base of noble ingredients completes this scent. Particularly, oak moss and patchouli dominate here slightly. But everything harmoniously blends together. "Magie Noire" develops very femininely, at times even alluring. The above-average longevity typical of many fragrances from that time accompanies this one as well. "Magie Noire" is no exception: this scent and the woman who wore it were simply present! The bottle is very impressive: black with bold colors! I still remember that it felt very good in my hand; even with my small paws. I will never forget the scent mixture that revealed itself to me when I opened the apartment door after I had once again taken Petra to the taxi late at night: a fine hint of good food, cigarette smoke, her "Magie Noire," and my "Chloé"! That was a truly magical scent! For we often sat together for hours at my place: ate more than enough, drank a little too much, smoked countless cigarettes, and talked, talked, talked. As the evening progressed, we would also sit in silence together: we could afford that; we knew each other very well! "Magie Noire" is for me the scent of a friendship that somehow faded away. What a shame! And yet beautiful again: the memory remains and so does this scent!

Contrary to Eau d'Hadrien, I can barely smell any lime or lemon in Bois d'Hadrien, only a vague suggestion of a fresh fruity opening. And in a sense true to its name, Bois d'Hadrien indeed feels quite woody. However, these woody notes don't really have any charming characteristics of specific wood, either, but more like an abstract fruity woody note with certain similarities to Cashmeran. And it even turns a bit aridly smoky in the dry down, somewhat similar to the unpleasant effect of certain woody amber aromachemicals quite common these days. Probably thanks to these potent molecules, the projection of Bois d'Hadrien is rather heavy, and it can cling on skin for at least 10 hours. But in return, I find Bois d'Hadrien lacks urgently the subtle, poetic beauty of previous creations from the house of Goutal. As a result, I would not particularly recommend this fragrance, especially if you happen to be fan of Goutal's offerings before 2012 which feel completely different in style with Bois d'Hadrien. As a side note, the spray mechanism of the new packaging is much better than the older Goutal sprayer! It gives out a very uniform spray and is much easier to press.

This is quite a unique creation, at least to me it is. The quality of the ingredients will let you smell every single note individually, a trade mark I noticed with Goutal fragrances in general, something I can't say about other houses. Very bright lime with sticky sweet balsams, a combination I haven't seen before. Oh, and the sprayer is absolutely magnificent, just 2 or 3 sprays and you're good to go.

Yes, it is warm: summer has returned with force and intends to settle down for more than just a moment. As a summer creature, I welcome it, but I also know that it can be a burden for many. Thus, the right light wardrobe and a corresponding fragrance are all the more important during this summer time. Nothing constricting, nothing heavy that swings the scent club. No, now is the time for "waters" in various compositions; everything called Acqua Leggero is welcome: a fresh, cooling breeze that pleasantly surrounds and does not constrict. Already during the first very warm days, I tried many "freshies" from my decants. Now, after the morning trip to the Gulf of Sorrento with "Sorrentina," I consciously reached for "Bois d'Hadrien": spicy freshness and successful wood aromas envelop me! It is still warm, but the evening feels like it is descending over a gently hilly southern landscape that seems to breathe softly. I sit amidst the warm aromas that the cypress and pine emit, on a slope. This mixture makes me relaxed and peaceful. Aromatic and spicy underbrush spreads its own slightly rugged charm, and a light breeze brings the fine fresh scent of nearby lemon/lime plantations. The magnificent image of a Mediterranean landscape emerges here. A fragrance painting, an idyll that dispels tension; gently untangles the strained thoughts and smooths them out kindly. A scent being with a light step and gentle hand is born! Camille Goutal succeeds here in translating the harmony of a summer landscape into a fragrance image. "Bois d'Hadrien" is a hybrid fragrance: not masculine, not feminine - it adapts effortlessly and is immediately present. Nothing needs to develop first, nothing hides or arrives late: "Bois d'Hadrien" is here now and immediately; complete and personal for everyone. Its lightness is elegant, yet not too casual. For several hours, this seemingly light yet refined fragrance creation accompanies me; surprisingly long for a scent from this house. My trust in the name Annick Goutal was not disappointed here either. However, I find it hard to warm up to the shape of the new bottles; where are the sensual curves of the familiar bottles that fit so beautifully in the hand? "Bois d'Hadrien" sends me on a journey into a special fragrance landscape. Its gates are opened to me anew with each spray, and I enter with great joy and love to linger there again and again!

I don't know Eau d'Hadrien, but I can imagine that Eau d'Hadrien plus wood results in Bois d'Hadrien. For me, Bois d'Hadrien is mainly lemon (or lime, if you prefer) plus wood. It could be cypress wood, but it could also come from the hardware store. This might sound like a harsh critique, and honestly, I find critiques much more entertaining than praise. However, Bois d'Hadrien has proven to be excellent for me at work. So far, it is best suited for work alongside (untitled) l'eau and Blanche (Byredo). I should mention that I get quite close to people at work, and it's good if I smell fresh. Additionally, I comfort and cheer myself up at work with the perfume I wear. At first, Bois d'Hadrien blew me away; I found the scent so wonderful. I must attribute that to my inexperience. Then I didn't buy the bottle because I found the scent one-dimensional. Lemon. Wood. If I had been fair, I should have at least counted lemon and wood as two-dimensional together. But it might also have been due to that terribly hot summer. Perhaps Bois d'Hadrien doesn't work at 30°C plus, but hits differently. With the wood on top, it’s not great at all. When my sample runs out, I will definitely need a bottle for autumn, winter, and spring at work, alternating with the other scents mentioned above. I consider Bois d'Hadrien to be unisex, and it can probably be worn on other occasions as well.

I recently discovered Bois d’Hadrien. I have known the Annick Goutal brand for a while and I really like it; I am fond of natural ingredients. I became aware of Bois d’Hadrien while browsing in an upscale perfumery, and I found the duet of lemon and wood very appealing from the outset. However, the prices were also quite upscale… Fortunately, through a nice perfumer, I was able to acquire a decant, and I now treasure it like a gem. It is a wonderful fragrance that starts off with a strong, zesty lemon and immediately brings a woody undertone. Over time, the woody note becomes stronger while the lemon remains. At the same time, a wonderful powdery warmth emerges, and it develops into a very beautiful scent that lingers on me for hours. I indeed have an association with wood or trees, but not in the forest, rather in the garden. Trees are being pruned (I love gardening!), wood is being stacked, there is digging in the earth, and on the table, there is a lemon cake and a carafe of mineral water with lemon slices and mint leaves. It is a robust scent that still has a certain softness in its depth, making it neither harsh nor strict. I believe this fragrance will accompany me for a long time and soon become a regular guest in my collection. It is a very beautiful, indeed special scent for every day, also suitable for the office, less for an elegant evening, but still stylish, and for every season. The lemon refreshes in summer, the wood warms in winter - perfect!

With Bois d'Hadrien, what you see is what you get. No frills, no unpleasant surprises. Here, quality counts over quantity. A simple, but perfect harmony - from the natural, juicy-sour lime at the beginning to the subtle, herbaceous ivy leaves, all the way to the woody, sweet-spicy base.

.... in between everything that feels good. Quality over quantity - when it comes to the ingredients. It doesn’t just come across as summery. Yet it handles all temperatures from Nordic cold to Southern warmth and plays on the keyboard of the senses. Green expanses and ivy-covered forest floors. Nordic conifers and Southern citrus fruits.

Here we are again! I'm going to write about Bulgari perfumes and the problem is always the same: the sillage. This fragrance is light and pleasant, the rose notes give it a particularly feminin and soft touch. It's the perfect day scent in springtime-summer....but the sillage is too weak. It's a pale rose scent in a precious and expensive bottle.

A truly beautiful rose, fresh, radiant, and kissed with a touch of pomegranate that adds a playful spark and a hint of modernity to the composition. This is a perfectly balanced fragrance: neither too classic nor too daring, just the right blend to smell good, feel good, and give off an air of effortless elegance. For rose lovers, this is a real success: easy to wear, refined without being overdone, and above all, a real joy to experience.

The bottle is huge and heavy, especially for a 1.7oz. Can’t even imagine what the 3.4 is like…It’s classy yet gawdy at the same time? Mixed feelings here. Anyway, BEAUTIFUL fragrance! I adore fresh rosewater scents and this one has just the right amount of warm woodiness making it rich and clean, without ever becoming heavy or dark. Very reminiscent of Paul Smith Rose but with wood notes instead of green notes. Actually the two smell fantastic layered together! This is creamy and clean, floral and bright, but also serious and sensual. I have a few different Bvlgari fragrances and not a single one is a powerhouse but I think that’s just how these perfumes are, beautiful watercolor fragrances. Elegant and primarily for your pleasure. Edited to add: Eight months later after finishing my 50 ml, I bought a larger 100ml bottle. Yeah, the bottle is huge like I thought it would be but I don’t care because I have fallen madly in love with this fragrance.

Bvlgari's first fragrance already put the rose in the spotlight - that was 22 years ago. Then came the flanker "Rose Essentielle," a rose jam-like, liqueur-like, sweet scent that certainly had its charm. 2016 is obviously the year of the ROSE, hardly a new release, hardly a flanker that doesn't bring the rose theme. YAWN. "Rose Goldea" is what I would call "pretty": really lovely and by no means a showstopper or polarizer. One might find such a fragrance banal and clichéd, but you could also like it because there’s nothing disturbing about it. Personally, I still prefer the first Bvlgari (is it called Classique now?). However, I really like the bottle of "Rose Goldea," and the scent is very nice, so wonderfully rosy. But the longevity of the new one is unfortunately poor for me. After 2 hours, I can hardly smell anything anymore. What a shame. After all, the price is not in the "I'll-just-grab-this" segment. Update August 2019: If you wait, you can often snag a bargain after almost three years. In the meantime, there are more rose fragrances from the series, the flankers of the flanker... Therefore, this one is currently very cheap online. I have now integrated it into my collection and will wear it when I don't want to stand out too much.

Today I picked up the chic miniature of the new No 5 L`eau at my perfumery - and of course, I couldn't help but look around a bit - since I was already there. The marketing concept works perfectly for me. But I'm not upset about it, because I discovered Rose Goldea. Goldea already has a "Heart of Gold" - and the Rose is no less impressive. In the intro, I am greeted by comforting sweetness - a real balm for the soul on reflective days like these. The full, soft rose fits perfectly - reminding me of the filled Leonardo da Vinci. My mom's favorite rose. The sweet rose is the theme here - skillfully accompanied by bright jasmine. Sandalwood makes the floral aspect of the fragrance creamy, and light incense adds a certain depth - and profundity. A soft, gentle scent - that brings the melody of Neil Young's "Heart of Gold" to my ears. I click on the song on YouTube - and think of people who have their hearts in the right place.

Perception A fragrance that reminds me of an elderly lady's country cottage in summer. From a bubble bath in the antique bathtub, the view overlooks a densely planted rose garden in full bloom. Fragrance Description Right after spraying, I get a slight impression of Cologne 4711, which quickly fades and is overtaken by the actual scent. The rose makes a strong entrance.

The bottle caught my eye right away; it is heavy but looks very feminine, noble, and elegant, just like the perfume it contains. It comes packaged in a pretty box that feels as delicate in the hands as a swan made of rosewood.

A summer evening, walking through a Mediterranean village. Your gaze wanders through the alleys. You notice a beautiful woman, and your eyes linger on her. She has her back to you, next to her a large rose bush. A red dress obscures her contours. Suddenly, she turns around and your eyes meet. An incredible feeling. She smiles at you.

This fragrance has been with me for several years. It reminds me of a walk in a rose garden. Right from the start, I perceive the rose very strongly in the top notes. Shortly after, the floral jasmine joins in. For a long time, I only smell these two components. A perfect mix of a light sweetness, the powdery rose, and the fresh, floral jasmine.

Miracle Homme opens with a pepper-green-woody and slightly aquatic accord which smells really astringent, dry, bitter, with a peculiar sort of austere and almost boozy woody note (like mahogany) sweetened by a slight juicy tea-red pepper note on a fresh, elegant, formal and quite conventional cedar-vetiver base – that “hi everyone, I’ve just been hired here” type of office-safe elegance. Nice contrasts though, and a peculiar, interesting sort of sour, dry sharpness all over, perfectly contrasted by a fresh feel (not a matter of specific notes, just more literally a “feel”). Then, once Miracle starts to “warm” on skin, it brings cedar and vetiver to a prominent position, making them more “round” and warmer than the opening phase, pairing them with something smelling like a sort of powdery, gourmandish, dusty suede note on the very base, which I guess may be the coffee note. No oak moss at any point to my nose. What interests me here is that there’s some creativity in here, nice contrasts and shades, masterfully concealed behind a conventional look; you do feel this “fresh woods” are definitely, entirely “2000s designer”, but still there’s something more, some elusive hints you keep coming back to smell. Maybe it’s that coffee note, which – if I detect it correctly – is just more of a sort of mellow, kind of roasted but also sweet and silky-powdery gourmandish suede note, as I said above. Or that sort of syrupy and fresh “tea-red pepper” note that comes and goes. All I can say is that this scent is... odd, in a positive way: it smells kind of dull at first, but if you pay attention and make some (well, actually “quite many”) efforts, it reveals a really interesting and complex texture. It smells like a conventional aromatic-fresh “boisé” at first, with a nice warm feel, and it’s undoubtedly a pleasant, effortlessly elegant crowpleaser: but there’s something which makes me think there has been quite some creativity and attentive craft behind this. It’s like if all these “conventional” notes are slightly displaced from their usual perspectives, making them all smell just a bit different. The fact that this hides behind an almost dull look, I don’t know if it’s intentional or a “faux pas” though. I still consider this compelling enough, pleasant and cozy, not boring at all, even if we just take it as a dull mainstream woody scent – the quality is good the same. The main flaw of this scent is that it is really too light and “thin” to make you able to appreciate all its qualities at the fullest – and it surely would deserve that. I appreciate the understatement here and overall I consider this a tad more intriguing and compelling than most of other “office woodies” to which this may be compared to; but still, it would have definitely needed a boost. 6,5-7/10

It's a great fragrance, Fresh , Woody with very Sensual overtones. A hidden gem, I agree with that : THIS IS A TRUE MIRACLE ! This perfume has a masterful well-balanced composition, All notes are in harmony with each other. Too bad this is discontinued! It opens up with like fresh , slightly spicy, and bitter coffee in the background then dry down is semi sweet woody. It smells so good and very pleasant. MIRACLE is perfect for the spring, summer and fall. I really enjoy it and I love it. You can't go wrong with Lancome. Bravo Monsieur KURKDJIAN ! Two Thumbs Up. Rating : 9 / 10

Such a shame that this men's cologne was discontinued. I find it to be such a nice, comforting scent. Pleasant, warm and understated. It's non-offensive smell makes you feel wrapped up in it's cozy aura. I looked for this cologne previously with no luck. Finally I was able to find a bottle of it at a discount retailer. They only had one bottle and it had once been a tester. It didn't have much out of the bottle and it had the cap so I didn't hesitate to snap it up. Happy to finally have this soothing scent! If you have the chance to buy it, get it, you won't regret your decision!

Lancome Miracle Homme is not a perfume that tells a story - here one can be brief. MH smells subtly “modern perfumey” with notes of fruity-sweet foliage and a hint of bitter coffee bean of the non-gourmand variety, garnished with a bit of moss and paprika (I suspect that the notes mentioned above are a translation error: red pepper = Paprika, not red pepper). The dominant, unusual foliage note has a nutty and an apple-sweet component - and smells surprisingly good. The paprika also fits neatly into the usual array of scent components without seeming odd. Kurkdjian's composition successfully combines bright and sweet motifs of modern men's perfumery with classic, more austere notes. But it doesn't help: unfortunately, Miracle Homme is short-lived on my skin, with limited projection. While MH avoids the chemical shallowness of Hugo Boss and the like, it is still not exactly a character player in its restraint. With MH, one is unlikely to cause any stir, but equally, it won't evoke any enthusiasm. Miracle Homme is, like a piece of soap, a decent and solid worker in terms of personal hygiene, not a masterpiece for perfume lovers. Overall, it is wearable, even if MH runs out of steam too soon on the skin. For whom? Office workers who want to be properly but not overly fragranced.

...a beautiful fragrance. Yes, it is not terribly complex, and really only suitable for spring/summer or early autumn (if it is as warm as 2014), but then it is all the better... Fresh/fruity, unobtrusive. Sometimes that is simply enough, and for that, "Miracle Homme" fits really well. A classic "go-to," not too sweet, not too synthetic, not too generic, but also not a weakling. It could brotherly unite with some of the recent creations from Lanvin that also go in this direction. Fresh, natural, and rather light. As a vintage, it is not that easy to find; not a fragrance that one must absolutely have right now, but certainly not one to be scorned either. As I said, it doesn't hurt anyone, even though it is unlikely to provoke the strongest reactions. Very solid, and that simply has to be enough, right?

Whenever I wore this fragrance, it always reminded me of a meadow in summer, shortly after a rain shower. I had the scent of damp grass in my nose, a lot of green, and also the association of wet hay. Strange, because I can't find anything in the fragrance notes that I would expect to find in a meadow?

The scent of mimosa is something I'm very familiar with. I grew up on a property where this stuff bloomed everywhere. I played under it as a child and delighted in snapping off branches of the stuff, yet as I got older, it gave me dreadful hayfever. Le Mimosa is close to the scent of my childhood, but unfortunately it has been overshadowed with syrupy peach and sugary musk. I see this fragrance as being a delightful, bright little Spring scent, but I'd be lying if I said I didn't expect more from this release. At times this fragrance is a little powdery and honeyed. To me it doesn't smell like mimosa, instead it smells like the inside of a beehive or another flower altogether. It's pleasant and unique so to say; very sunny, bright and yellow just like mimosa blooms itself, but still to my nose, this is not mimosa. In all honesty it's mostly peach, powder and a dash of icing sugar. It's unfortunately quite linear and predictable after a while, which leaves me a little lost as to how to describe it. It's a fragrance that's trying to follow in the footsteps of the sugary and pretty Songes, but somehow it fails to live up to its proud predecessor. The drydown is quite musty, yet it's only then that I sensed a glimmer of sweet wattle tree blooms that made me long for home. My first full-blown fragrance love, which I find reminds me of home more vividly, is Burberry Weekend for Women. So for fellow Australians like myself, that long for that beautiful, homely scent, Burberry Weekend might soothe some of your cravings. Le Mimosa was unfortunately poor in terms of longevity and sillage. It's times like these that I tend to curse Annick Goutal, even though nothing has come to rival it as my favourite niche house. I will use my Le Mimosa sample, but I won't be buying a full bottle anytime soon.

A few years ago, I owned a bottle of Petite Cherie. I loved its transparent nature, its green freshness, the succulent pear, and understated florals. Unfortunately Petite Cherie was a bit too juvenile & thin for me, so I swapped it because I wasn't wearing it. I've since regretted that decision and wished I kept it, not to wear it but to sniff it on occasion and enjoy its playful, uplifting nature. Since then, I have been looking for a fragrance to replace Petite Cherie. Finally, I found it - Le Mimosa, which is Petite Cherie all grown up. First off, let's face it: Le Mimosa is a fruity floral. There I said it. If that category is on your "I'll wear a fruity floral over my dead body" list, then move along because there is nothing to see here. If you don't harbor disdain for the concept, perhaps even wore fruity florals 10 or 20 years ago, then Le Mimosa might be worthy of sampling ... and reading on. Like many AG femmes, Le Mimosa is transparent and has AG's signature accord. I think that characteristic of the AG femmes is soothing and soft, yet distinctive. It was something I craved after I let go of my Petite Cherie bottle, and I love that about Le Mimosa. The green is not as bright & long-lived as Petite Cherie. Le Mimosa is not as thin as Petite Cherie, and it's more balanced, with clean musk in the base, a hint of woodiness, and a touch of naughty. Compared to Petite Cherie, the fruit (peach) is more present, more persistent and more impressive, so much so that Le Mimosa could have been named La Pêche. As others have stated, Le Mimosa is not a soliflore mimosa. Rather, it's an AG impression or interpretation of mimosa, which apparently is peach-tinged. Le Mimosa is an appropriate fragrance for summer & spring, and I struggle to think of anyone who would be offended by it. That's another way to say it's office-appropriate. It also would be appropriate to wear to warm-weather gatherings like weddings or family picnics. It's an understated & effortless fragrance that exudes niceness yet remains memorable. Like many femme EDTs in the AG line-up, Le Mimosa is close-wearing and is short on longevity. But I forgive it - it's not that type of fragrance. I'd love to have Le Mimosa in body products, such as a body powder, so I could envelop myself in the scent without over-spraying. I think Le Mimosa would most appeal to those who like transparent peach and pear scents such as AG Petite Cherie, Fresh Sake, and Keiko Mecheri Peau de Peche.

Annick Goutal LE MIMOSA is quite sweet. It lists aniseed and iris among its notes, but there seems to be violet or vanilla or perhaps both as well. In fact, the sweetness level is on a par with some of the Laurence Dumont LES SENTEURS perfumes. Basically, if you do not like sweet perfumes, you will not like this one. That said, I find LE MIMOSA to be entirely natural smelling. This a mixture of a few different flowers, including mimosa, with peach, and the peach becomes more and more marked in the drydown. I like this composition, but it is very simple and reminds me of something that might be produced by Jo Malone or found in the Demeter All Naturals collection. People looking for a mimosa soliflore may be disappointed with this perfume, so I'd definitely advise that you try before you buy. At the same time, I'm pretty sure that this would make a good gift for someone who is used to wearing mainstream fruity-floral fragrances, as this one smells much better than those.

The opening stage of Le Mimosa is the most floral moment throughout the whole development. I can smell the powdery iris. Regarding to mimosa, I'm not familiar. Thus I'm not sure. Then comes the sweet and slightly ripen peach, and it soon becomes the leading role. At this stage, Le Mimosa is more like a peach fragrance balanced by floral notes. The sweetness is delicate, and the whole scent feels casual and carefree. After 4 hours it then turns into a gentle sandalwood and musk trail with a hint of sweetness, and last for another 4 hours. The sillage of Le Mimosa is soft. It actually is a comforting peachy floral fragrance and easy to appreciate. I like it, but am not motivated to purchase a full bottle.

Le Mimosa is an impulse buy. A small owner-operated perfumery in Hamburg recently had a big sale, and which perfume lover can resist the temptation to sniff around? Perhaps it was the cold, gray winter weather that led me to finally grab Le Mimosa at the end of my shopping spree, as mimosa always evokes for me a full-bodied summer day, warm, sunny, yellow, lush without heaviness. Unfortunately, my skin was already doused with many other test candidates (and I had another purchased scent in my bag), so only the test strip remained for Mimosa, which initially revealed something very girlishly floral to me, something I found somehow inappropriate for myself, as "too young." But I took the strip with me and kept testing it throughout the day. And what can I say: it captivated me. So I had to go back to the store and buy Mimosa without another skin test ;-). ********************* And this is what happens to me when I apply Le Mimosa to my skin: The wonderful summer of 1982 rises to my nose. I was 14 back then, the World Cup was on (Germany lost in the final against Italy 1:3), I had my hair cut like Kim Wilde and was ready for many things. We were on vacation at my grandmother's in a coastal Frisian village. New neighbors had moved in: two sisters, one 15, one 16 years old. Over the garden fence, we shyly made contact, and then followed a magical country summer filled with a series of endless sunny days, balmy evenings behind the house, visits to the outdoor pool with harmless, but for us at the time, incredibly exciting flirts with the lifeguards there, evenings filled with fantasies about romantic moments with the young gentlemen, as well as endless joint analyses of signs of their affection (possibly), and in the end, a few days of heartache when the summer vacation was over. Everything was underscored by the scent of warm earth in the vegetable and fruit garden of the neighbor girls, from which we simply pulled out young carrots and ate them after a quick rinse under the rusty old faucet by the shed, picked and devoured strawberries, inhaled the scent of the swaying cornfields around us, and listened to the summer wind, which brought with it only a pleasant whisper along with occasional seagull cries, cow moos, and the rumble of a farming machine. The sun tanned us dark brown, and our skin smelled of young girl skin, slightly singed, but still sweet, warm, tender young girl skin. To increase our chances with the lifeguards, we had bought lip glosses in the village drugstore, which sparkled in light pink and smelled of peach and apricot, blending into this olfactorily rich teenage world. I think of all this when I wear Le Mimosa now, and strangely, I don’t feel silly or teenage or "too young" for this scent. Perhaps because it fits so naturally into my life story, because this summer didn’t just dance for one summer, or because my friendship with the two sisters still exists today, and we meet once every summer ;-) under the fruit trees in the garden to drink tea and eat fruit cake, ice cream, and melon. * And how is the scent itself? The opening is surprisingly powerful, anise, anise, anise, along with a hint of delicate flowers, something green even, and quickly joining in: the juicy sweetness of peach. It smells "rural," of straw, hay, sweet, dripping, sun-warmed apricots and peaches, spiced with a sharp sweetness from the anise. This note lasts surprisingly long until it finally leaves behind the slightly cow dung-like impression of country air and allows the sun fruit with its sweetness to assert itself. The sweetness is pleasant and well-measured; Le Mimosa retains a certain lightness, luminosity, and naturalness despite the increasingly powdery and sweet notes, not feeling stuffy or "thick," and to speak of opulence would be completely out of place. Surely this is also due to the rather weak sillage; I can certainly smell myself without having to bring my nose to my skin, but there is no cloud trailing behind me, rather it is a very delicate veil. One must want this, and it must suit one - it suits me quite well, and therefore I do not necessarily see it as a drawback. The delicate mimosa glows finely and golden yellow from the skin, it is so friendly, so warm-hearted, so natural, so unobtrusive, yet still present. A quiet but intense presence, strengthened by the anise note, which accompanies the scent throughout its entire development (at least on me). This gives the harmlessness a cheeky, almost stubborn quality, but just enough so that the pure fruity floral and sweetness does not come across as too boring. In the end, creamy sandalwood and soft, skinnier musk remain on my skin, beautiful, just how I love it! The longevity is rather in the medium range, but that may be different in summer, and I swear, I will test this extensively and simultaneously breathe in the magic of summer 1982 and the melting of my youth once again. For Ina & Petra from Z.

In 2011, a video advertisement from the four-letter furniture store was released, in which a girl - optionally a very young woman - emphasizes verbal... uh... expressions of displeasure through the intensive use of various movable parts of the kitchen furniture. Surely everyone has seen it. Funny, right? My wife and I smiled through the pain. It felt all too familiar.

Shivering, she pulled her delicate shoulders up. The thin little dress is suitable for warm summer days, but it's far too cool for autumn temperatures. Sadly, she lowers her head. It will be so long until summer returns to the land. Dreamily, she lets her gaze wander over the autumn garden.

A typical Sunday afternoon in July in Rome. On the Piazzale Napoleone I, Roman families dressed for Sunday and, of course, tourists gather. They are not only recognizable by their various cameras; the Sunday does not play a role in their summery casual attire. What a pity! For Romans, this large terrace is often a place where they celebrate family festivities.

In an unexpected way, "Le Mimosa" found its way to me. A bright floral scent… wrong address, I thought, and after the first spray, I was convinced that my prejudiced mistrust completely matched the scented reality: Very nice, but indeed a bright floral scent with a decent portion of fruit and white musk. Even after the second spray, I was still sure.

God, you are such a sensitive little plant. Not that I'm unfamiliar with mimosas. I know, you fold your leaves together when someone just touches you. I have no intention of touching you, so feel free to come out. First, you send out a peach, no not one, a whole basket full of ripe, juicy, sweet peaches - simply irresistible.

I absolutely love the first hours of this. An uncommon blend of fruity and balsamic notes. The copaiba balm is noticeable right from the start. It's warm, creamy and slightly medicinal. I find it similar to Peru balsam, which is found in fragrances more often. The mandarin is sweet and juicy and adds a gourmand mandarin cheesecake vibe to the scent. I assume the tonka also plays a part in that. Unfortunately the scent turns very powdery as it dries down. After a few hours the warmth is not completely gone, but covered by a thick layer of cooling powder, which makes the drydown quite different from the opening. It's still nice, but it doesn't blow me away. I would have loved this if it dried down warmer and more balmy. The way it is, it's more of a like. I'm not too sad, it saves me some money, but I hope I will someday find a perfume that smells like Rubinia's opening all the way.

We all have them: The categories into which we classify fragrances. In addition to the categories: I don’t like it, it’s okay, I like it, and I love it (the highest level so far) I have discovered a new category for myself with Rubinia: “So beautiful I could cry” And as cheesy as it may sound... it’s true. I would like to introduce you to this red beauty: As part of the Le Gemme collection, Rubinia is meant to embody the ruby. The ruby is considered one of the strongest healing stones for love and sexuality, as it is said to have a dynamic and revitalizing effect. The gemstone is supposed to give courage to live out these desires, but it is also said to promote sensitivity in relationships and is therefore considered a lucky stone for love. About the scent: Rubinia starts fruity-creamy. I perceive the mandarin, it is by no means citrusy or fresh at all! Rather, it is a balsamic mandarin, and I could swear I’m catching a whiff of a cherry note. Later, a powdery vanilla note joins in, which must be due to the tonka bean. After a few hours, Rubinia noticeably decreases in sweetness and remains powdery-vanilla without becoming dry/dusty. Overall, it is a beautiful creamy/powdery vanilla-tonka dream. (That was long haha) The scent does not have a particular development, I must admit, but Rubinia doesn’t need that. Bvlgari has created something magical here. Rubinia embodies not only the ruby with its bottle but also the meaning of the gemstone in esotericism with the scent. For me, the scent is the embodiment of feminine seduction. Rubinia is incredibly feminine, sexy yet uniquely special; not only would men turn their heads when a beautiful lady walks by wearing this fragrance, leaving a cloud of scent in her wake. With this scent, I envision an elegant, seductive woman wearing a velvet nightgown in blood red. Around her neck, she has the beautiful gemstone, adorning her décolletage. She knows exactly what she wants. She is aware of her effect, and she enjoys it. Rubinia could not better emphasize her essence. Oh yes, it is seductive, but still suitable for everyday wear in my opinion, and who says that one cannot smell seductive in everyday life? ;) However, I would stay away from it in very high temperatures, as it can indeed come across as quite heavy. I may still be a novice when it comes to the world of perfumes and have only been able to sniff/test around 140 fragrances, but I have come to love Rubinia like almost no other scent so far. So ladies, you must try it :)!! Thank you for reading.

Hello my dear sniffers and welcome to a new comment from me :) (Unbelievable, after all this time and so many comments, I am still being read!!... :D) Today, I will describe the wonderful scent Rubinia from the Le Gemme collection by Bvlgari, which is one of the more premium and exclusive fragrance lines of this brand. I received the sample from a very dear perfumer, and apparently, I had to test the scent since she said something like “Test the fragrance or I’ll throw the bottle at your head!” which seemed like a gentle threat that she would hit me if I didn’t test this, admittedly wonderful scent. So it seems I have no choice but to ramble on here. You see, I’m not always to blame when I have to ramble on to you (…unbelievably, “ramble on” is now also spelled with three “L”s… :DD). So, Rubinia then. You know that the Le Gemme fragrances are supposed to represent a specific gemstone, which is why they carry names of gemstones and minerals (or names inspired by them). Rubinia comes from ruby, a gemstone that is formed from the mineral corundum, which contains some chromium. Chromium-free corundum minerals have different colors like blue or green (due to iron, titanium, or something else inside) and are then referred to as sapphires. Anyway, ruby is therefore red and is considered the strongest healing stone of all (how fitting, in case I do get my head smashed by wild perfumers… :D). But a ruby also has many other magical properties, at least in esotericism, and is also regarded as a stone of joy, strength, vitality, and of course, primarily love. And… well, you should look up more about it yourself, as the stone seems to have a lot of properties. Whether one believes in it is another matter, but it all reads very interesting nonetheless :) But now I finally come to the fragrance description! The Scent: The scent starts off lightly fruity sweet with a mandarin, which I wouldn’t have immediately recognized if it weren’t listed in the fragrance notes, although you can smell that the beginning is quite fruity. I quickly detect beautiful, sweet-powdery vanilla that harmonizes very nicely with this mandarin.
