There’s also a light spice, which should be the indicated saffron, but it quickly recedes a bit into the background. I also smell a light, clean-soapy component in the background. Later, you still smell the wonderful fruity-sweet mix of mandarin and vanilla, with balsamic notes that make the scent even softer. A bit later, this softness is further enhanced by the tonka bean. The sweet notes also seem to come additionally from jasmine. Towards the end, the scent actually remains as it is, mainly powdery and sweet from vanilla, tonka bean, and balsamic notes, although the fruity scents recede a bit and the fragrance seems to become even softer. All in all, a very beautiful and very feminine scent. The Sillage and Longevity: I find the sillage quite good. At first, when sprayed, it might seem that the strength of the scent doesn’t quite come through, but it develops better soon, enveloping you in a nice, even larger scent cloud that is easily detectable by others. The longevity is enormous, as the scent lasts ten hours on me. The Bottle: The bottle has a cup-like shape and is black with golden accents. The base of the bottle is smaller, which means it could wobble or tip slightly when touched, so one should be a bit careful. The disc-shaped cap is, as always, the highlight of the bottle, as it is also black-golden but additionally carries the color of the respective gemstone, in this case ruby red with a beautiful golden star-shaped decoration. A very beautiful and noble bottle. Wow, I think Rubinia is one of the most beautiful Le Gemme fragrances I have tried so far. It smells sweet, powdery, and soft, making it a very feminine scent that comes across as very passionate, sexy, and elegant (and in these cases, it always makes me want to bite a woman wearing such a fragrance, aaaaahhh…..!). Due to the stronger sweet and powdery notes, the scent is a bit heavier and thus best suited for autumn and winter. Applied lightly, it could be used daily, but it is even better for the evening, to simply appear heavenly, elegant, and above all, seductive (and of course… you know me and what’s coming next… especially delicious :D). It is just perfect for going out or for dates (of course not with me… *sigh* how mean!) and simply for making everyone who perceives the scent say nothing but “WOW”! Therefore, I find that this scent is definitely worth a test! To sum it up briefly: You ladies would be really silly if you didn’t at least try it once :)) Yes, I have reached the end and wish you a lovely evening, until next time :)

Since the first test spray, Rubinia has been on my wish list and as of the day before yesterday, it is now in my collection. This is the reason for my comment, although I cannot share entirely new or differing impressions from my predecessor's comment. The scent touches something in my soul, which is why I feel the need to write about it. I rated it 9.0, even though I can't say that I like it unconditionally and exclusively. This may sound strange to you readers and I hope my further explanations will make it a bit clearer. Alongside the scent perception, attributes come to mind such as special and unique and different, yes sometimes even peculiar. This is due to an exotic note that blends into the otherwise predominantly balsamic-almond scent. I still do not know if it is primarily due to the copaiba balsam, as I have not encountered it in its pure form yet. It is probably just the interplay of many elements. This many for me is: - Tonka-almond to the same extent - Sandalwood-creamy somewhat less - Jasmine-floral and Mandarin-fruity and in between also - creamy-powdery I do not notice a significant progression; the scent remains quite consistent on me, aside from the powderiness, which I perceive only temporarily and much stronger in warmer temperatures than in cooler ones. For me, it is a scent for the upcoming season, autumn, possibly also winter. Additionally, it is 100% feminine; I absolutely cannot imagine it on a man. The longevity, in contrast to the other Le Gemme scents I have experienced, is extraordinarily good. I always find it difficult to evaluate the sillage, but what I can contribute is that I can perceive the scent well for up to 10 hours. For that, 2-3 fine sprays are sufficient. Rubinia is more a scent that evokes well-being for me than a perfume. So I do not even know if I would wear it in everyday life, during activities, or in company. In any case, definitely not to smell good for others. No, I wear it when I feel the need for deceleration, security, and calm. Then Rubinia provides a comforting feeling, as Gandix has already aptly described in her comment with 'familiarity' and 'balancing-harmonizing.' However, it is not a sofa-cuddle scent for me, nothing for lounging in sweatpants with a piece of ready-made pizza in hand. Not at all, because the other qualities I attribute to it are a kind of sublime beauty and elegance. Wearing Rubinia, I associate with a well-groomed evening accompanied by relaxing music, where one dresses casually yet carefully, even if alone. Or with a visit to an art exhibition at a time of day when only a few visitors are there and one can enjoy in silence. When I started writing this comment, I felt I had not much, especially not much new, to say about the scent. Then this line from a song by Reinhard Mey came to mind: “What I still have to say takes a cigarette and a last glass while standing.” Strange how one remembers certain songs from earlier times that one never hears anymore. I then looked up the lyrics and find that many lines from it fit quite well in this forum. I would like to conclude my comment with these: “… Thank you for the time I've spent chatting with you And for your patience when there were more than one opinion For never asking when I come or go For the always open door, where I now stand …”

I had previously known Bvlgari more as a "purveyor of the mainstream." When I was wandering through the city again last week, searching for a new scent (my wallet doesn't like it very much, but what can you do..), a saleswoman recommended that I try the Bvlgari "Le Gemme fragrances," and before I could refuse, she sprayed Rubinia on a test strip and handed it to me. Internally, I was already rolling my eyes and thinking, "surely just another 0-8-15 Bvlgari fragrance (sorry to all Bvlgari lovers ;) I took the test strip and ... and ... and.... was enchanted...! "What’s it called again and what’s in it???" This scent smells like a chalice full of happiness and rubies ;) WOW! Of course, I couldn't help myself and had to try Rubinia on my skin right away... At first, I could clearly recognize the mandarin... but a creamy and not so fruity mandarin (?) and somehow cherries... Red juicy cherries, something like amaretto... (I know, it’s not in the fragrance pyramid, but that’s how I perceived it). I’m not usually a fan of fruity scents, but Rubinia is somewhat fruity, yet somehow also "unfruity"... I don’t know how to describe it exactly... strange, but strangely good! The saleswoman gave me a sample and I left the store... After a while, more creaminess came through, tonka bean was definitely playing along, and then it became powdery for me! I love powder, and Rubinia is really wonderful... not dusty powdery, but rather "creamy-powdery" I kept smelling my wrist over and over.. Rubinia smells on me unsweet-cherry-creamy-powdery... incredibly wonderful and very extravagant, something I hadn’t experienced in a fragrance before... Days later, I tested Rubinia again at home in peace and had the same impressions as during the first "test"... "unsweet-cherry-creamy-powdery" I thought about the price... 350.- Swiss francs... phew, I’m definitely going to have a fight with my wallet... But I could get another sample? (shame) So I went back to the store and started chatting with the Bvlgari saleswoman. "Today there’s 15% off everything!" she happily informed me, and then I didn’t hesitate any longer and took my chalice full of happiness and rubies home with me ;) Oh how wonderful, I have my Rubinia ♥ ♥ ♥

Rubinia is a perfume by Bulgari, and their core competence lies more in designing jewelry. But no prejudices; always test first and let the nose decide what we have in front of us. Appropriate for the season, it starts off citrusy with mandarins and a slight bitter note, along with the association of Christmas. Mandarins and Christmas.

Picnic For dessert, there was fluffy almond cream the almond note at the beginning even slightly marzipan-like, which transitions into pure almond cream, but retains a very slight hint of bitterness. I am lying on a blanket, next to me a few flowers bloom, delicate, fine; my daughter has her head close to me. I can subtly smell her light make-up.

The fragrance is only available as remaining stock, released in 2018 as part of the Le Gemme collection and thus priced in the league of Tom Ford Private Blend, actually higher. The bottle is not my style at all, meant to symbolize sensuality and feminine curves. Sweet, floral, and powdery.

There's something dark & dirty about Lancome Magie (La Collections). She's not for a modern girl, but for a classic woman. Magie opens unisex but dries femme. I like Magie, but I don't care for the way the jasmine develops on my skin and how the fragrance sweetens as it wears. I do like that quality in Cuir, I don't like it in Magie. I might be wrong, but I think it comes down to the relative amount of jasmine. Ladies who love mysterious woody fragrances might just fall for the reissued Magie. I love sampling the reissued La Collections, and I applaud Lancome for resurrecting these fragrances and bring them to market. Magie doesn't speak to me in the same way that Lancome Cuir does. However, the entire line is sample-worthy!

I really enjoy the current formulation of Magie Noire by Lancome, so when I discovered that there was another fragrance that came before it, I ordered a sample almost straight away. Magie is one of those classics that really need to be brought back. The scent is heavy, powerful and reeking of confidence. It's quite a powdery scent, but not necessarily clean. I find it more animalic and slightly earthy. Magie tends to be rather sensual too, especially towards the drydown. This fragrance smells relatively dark and seductive on my skin. There's also a subtle note that resembles dirty fuel, that I must admit, intrigues me greatly. It has obvious unisex qualities, a fragrance that would wear just as well on a man as it does on a woman. Magie reminds me of Chanel No.22, however it's much dirtier and a tad more masculine. The opening is bitter in some ways, and also heavily concentrated in terms of aldehydes and musk. As it settles, the amber accord is more apparent, bringing to light a hint of beauty and superiority. Before the drydown, Magie is at its most animalistic stage with a thick muskiness combined with unsweetened amber. I should also add that the sillage at this point is rather soft and intimate. So this is in no way a loud and offensive blend. Despite the fact that Magie doesn't contain a leather accord, I think many women who adore leather-based scents will love Magie. It has a similar rough 'biker-chick' feel to it which I personally love. I'm very much taken with the drydown, which was a beautiful and smooth ambery incense blend, suiting a cold Winter's night perfectly. I highly recommend.

Magie Conjours a esoteric mystery Opens with the darkest and the most animalistic note of amber pure and unsweetened, Walking though a dimly lidded cave on a nocturnal moment threads of Calligraphic Arabic verses of gold Dangles with an Ethereal glow, Elusive jasmine grows in the Rock's crevice elegantly grows on the on the bare walls with sinuous beauty with it's leafy vines. I detect Civet in it's purest form adds to the Dark Exotica of this scent Wisp of incense smoke pierces though the utter darkness of the cave following the smoke until you saw where the smoke is burning from a beautiful incense burner etched in the shape of a dragon burns with the note of dry sandalwood, as the incense burns your transfixed by the smoke dancing revealing our Inner thoughts. Magie is a dark beauty delighting in sensual pleasure a bit of danger with Civet and meditation with amber.

Magic was the predecessor of the now reformulated Magic Noire. It was briefly revived a few years ago in the "La Collection" series by Lancôme, along with Cuir, Sikkim, and a few other earlier successes of this once-great perfume house. I even believe that the current formula comes very close to the original, if not identical, as the fragrance carries the charm of the 50s and 60s, which is not meant to be a devaluation, quite the opposite! It has the euphoria, the class, and the opulence of the great fragrances that accompanied it for a few years: Jolie Madame, 1953, Fath de Fath, 1953, L'Interdit by Givenchy, 1957, Caleche by Hermes, 1961... Great fragrances that are still loved and worn by wonderful women today. Magic has not lost its magical allure. I too felt helplessly surrendered to it when I smelled it for the first time. An aldehydic top note, comparable to many of the aforementioned classics, announces the fragrance quite impressively. Neither fresh nor overwhelming, perfectly balanced. The heart note has more to offer: Violet and jasmine provide only a light floral note, which remains in the background; the main element is the amber. It dominates the fragrance for a long time and extensively. It makes it animalistic, makes Dioressence look old in comparison, wild and untamed. The heart note has the power of two hearts. The base has the soapy freshness of musk with a green, slightly woody background. The longevity and sillage are predictably ka-boom. Girls (and guys who like heavy classics)..., for this fragrance, you will sell your soul!

I didn't know for a long time that there was Magie. Until the day I proudly presented my Hypnose "Hexenzauber" Elixir to someone, and she said... it reminds me of my childhood, of magic... I interrupted her speech and immediately said; No, Magie Noire is from MY childhood, from '78, and not from yours, you are twice as old as I am-- No, Eva. Magie, from the fifties, belonged to your grandma. Oops. This will be something for me. It smells so old... so dusty, like an old satin dress that can no longer be worn, it will disappear, collapse in on itself, decay. I recognize light aldehydes from the top notes, which can have many variations between soapy and musty, and are unmistakable in so many old perfumes. And then- come the sweet oriental jasmine and violet - lovely to excitingly floral. And the opening is sensual amber and musk, not easy to describe, nor necessary, we know it as the skin-like fragrance base of several perfumes. It is an EdP, with a very nice intensity. Today, EdP. Many years ago it was EdC and just as dark and intense. With Lancôme, I have no doubt that something will smell off (until the completely new pink escapade, that is). Perfumes are Lancôme's specialty and they are simply good, and definitely limited. Only the truly obsessed must have it. Or, enchanted, witch, and ancestor. Others will manage perfectly well with available editions.

This is the most atypical, shady, low down smelling antithesis of all citrus colognes you could ever imagine; the Evil Twin of Extra Vielle; cologne from the Dark Side. After the most perfunctory of citrus fanfares, Eau d'Hadrien EdP keeps only the most tenuous relation to citrus via an herbaceous and choppy textured note of lemongrass. But this is a fig leaf, there to give a surface cologne-like respectability to the caustic ginger that struggles to control its temper, and a dark bitter liquorice molasses that's found brooding in the depths: these are the ones who rule here, so make no mistake. All those who imagine Eau d'Hadrien to be a sunny Mediterranean sketch of citrus and cypress - think again. And then, you may wonder; in one hour! ... where did it go? [Distant, booming Comedy Villain voice comes vanishing from the depths] 'No poxy white musks here! Ha ha haaa ... '

Hadrien starts with that tricky yellow lemon, that I have grown less and less fond of - after trying a few too many lemon-centered old-timers. Immediately, I fear this is going down that yellow-lemon-with-the-usual-herbs road. But as soon as the other citrus species kick in, I realize I was put on the wrong track. This is anything but typical yellow lemon. Bitter citrus with a sub-layer of also a-typical herbal impressions make this a fascinating and highly enjoyable refreshment. Performance is in the "notoriously brief" range. The enjoyable experience does easily make up for that, though. Pretty sure I can welcome a full bottle to my collection soon.

Invigorating blend of bergamot and bitter citrus, sparkling but brief, with a hint of cedar below. So bright without being astringent. Like most citrus fragrances, it is not very long lasting. The citrus began to fade after about an hour and continued to linger close to the skin for another hour after that. I didn't get the base notes listed. This fragrance would be attractive on any sex.

.. is this Eau d'Hadrien indeed. But when is a fragrance actually special? Perhaps when it sets a record: According to CelebrityFragrances.com, this scent is worn by more Hollywood stars than any other perfume in recent times. A proud 21 mentions can be found there, including some great legends of American cinema (N. Kidman, L. di Caprio). It is only surpassed by Chanel No. 5 with 30 mentions - this fragrance is, however, over 60 years older and thus out of competition. The beloved Aventus only has one mention :) Another superlative is the number of bottle variations. After the renaming of Annick Goutal to Goutal, the bottles were redesigned. Additionally, there is a Homme variant (square) and a Femme variant (oval) with identical contents. I have not seen anything like this with any other perfume so far. Now let's get to the actual scent: Released in 1981 (as EdT), it is one of the first perfumes by A. Goutal and can be considered the flagship of this house. The EdP, which I am discussing here, came a bit later (1988) and lasts a bit longer than the EdT. Due to the higher concentration, it smells even more intense than the EdT. However, the longevity remains below average. At the beginning, you get a strong freshness kick. This kick comes from the citron (Cedrat), which smells a bit more citrusy than (regular) lemons. Some find this scent reminiscent of toilet cleaner or citrus cleaner, and I must admit: sometimes I also find it a bit too piercing. Nevertheless: a wonderful Mediterranean scent that is meant to evoke the lemon garden of the Villa Adriana, where Emperor Hadrian once resided. The late Annick Goutal, who passed away in 1999, left behind a fragrance of superlatives with Eau d'Hadrien, which is even above comparison with toilet cleaners. Your Frankfurt Fragrance Lover

Oso stood before the small table with the Latin inscription. Again and again, he had to read the lines, for although he did not understand Latin, these sparkling and fluttering syllables were for him, even as mere sound, a poem, a musical language. He had descended deep into the cool tomb chamber of Emperor Hadrian in the Castel Sant'Angelo and read the few lines on the tablet, carved in the finest Antiqua: ANIMULA VAGULA BLANDULA HOSPES COMESQUE CORPORIS QUAE NUNC ABIBIS IN LOCA PALLIDULA RIGIDA NUDULA NEC UT SOLES DABIS IOCOS. He knew the meaning of the words that the dying emperor had penned, which were of such painful beauty, especially since they had stood over his grave for almost two thousand years. No translation could even remotely capture this simultaneously so lively and sorrowful, this affirming and farewell-taking, this fluttering butterfly of a poem. The lines meant approximately the following: Soul you, wandering, tender, Companion and guest of the body, Now leads into the gloomy realm Shivering shadow your way, And you will no longer jest as before... After Oso had been unwell for a few days due to a bothersome cold, he thought during the time he still spent in Paris about what this attack on him or Elena could have been about. Although he was feeling better now, this last incident had taken quite a toll on him. Were they really Aventists? Or was it someone who merely wanted him to think that? What else could the rider figure on the assailant's hoodie mean? He no longer wanted to impose on Elena's hospitality, as his presence could pose a danger to her. His scholarship from the Olfactory Academy was not designed for constant travel across Europe, but he managed to snag a cheap flight and flew to Rome. He told Elena he would get back to her soon, and she accompanied him to Orly Airport in the morning, where she slipped him a small, already opened bottle as a farewell gift. She said it would surely be suitable for a lemonatic like him. But he should only try it out in Rome, at the best possible place for it, namely at the grave of Emperor Hadrian. So, after stowing his things in a guesthouse in the San Lorenzo district, he soon made his way to the Castel Sant'Angelo. The city was simmering in oppressive summer heat. How pleasant it was to step into the coolness behind the thick walls of the mausoleum. It became his own little ritual. He waited until the three visitors who were with him in the tomb chamber disappeared back upstairs and took out the small square bottle from his pocket, spraying it once into the air, then once towards the grave, and once onto himself in the open collar of his shirt. He felt that this homage, this dedication from the perfumer, the fragrance of Hadrian, was being transformed into reality, so to speak giving the emperor what belonged to the emperor. A hint of freshly grated lemon peel filled the air. Tart, vibrant, and very authentic and natural. Like the fluttering little soul from the poem, the lemon scent surrounded him, never distracting from its main theme. Didn't it wonderfully fit the essentialism or even the asceticism of the emperor, this restriction to the essential, but of course, a restriction in abundance, which was merely a refinement of an even greater kind? A clearer taste that distinguished Hadrian from the love of opulence and excess of many of his contemporaries, but perhaps also merely showed the vanity or extravagance of his highness. Lemon, lemon -- what could that possibly mean? Oso knew better than anyone that one always needed a interplay of several notes to create the illusion of something singular. In the coolness of the mausoleum, the lemony top note unfolded almost in slow motion and did not explode, as it would have in the heat above. But Oso now went back upstairs and constantly murmured the Latin syllables like a mantra: "Animula, vagula, blandula, animula, vagula, blandula…". Almost not knowing how he had gotten there, he crossed the bridge, sniffed grapefruit and wood, and followed the street into the houses, he wanted a coffee and a glass of ice-cold water, for after just a few minutes, the coolness of the tomb had vanished and the refreshment was gone. But the scent showed in the heat how unsweaty and dry the lemon was held by the wood note. Oso had to think of his old master from the academy, to whom the essences obeyed and always led to the effect he had previously announced. Oso entered a small bar, and behind the counter stood a man with a curly full beard in the Greek style and a simultaneously sensual and sensitive expression around his mouth. Oso ordered a glass of mineral water, and the man asked him with a smile: "Con Limone?" "Very gladly," said Oso, wondering where he recognized the handsome face of the man behind the bar from. He had just seen him; he had been carved from stone. It was Emperor Hadrian.

"Hey - are you still feeling fresh?" This is how unreasonable actions or thoughts are commented on here in the Ruhr area. Fresh and free from the soul. I like this straightforward way, which always carries a touch of warmth. However, since I prefer to be "fresh," I reach for Eau d`Hadrien, as it protects me from comments like these.

Like every year in summer, a citrus scent must move in with me; I love lemon fragrances in the summer, they give me so much cool freshness, a holiday mood arises, I dream of the south with lemon trees under which I linger. This year, after a long time, it is once again Eau d'Hadrien Edp, pure lemon, the little sweetness probably comes from the hint of mandarin.

Anyone who looks at the scent notes of this perfume already knows what to expect. And it's full throttle! Citrus, freshness, warm weather. Three terms that are inseparable in Eau d'Hadrien. And the citrus makes the perfume excellent! Absolutely not sweet, but rather bitter, the scent penetrates through the hot and sweaty air.
A very classic, Mediterranean (summer) fragrance. Elegant and casual at the same time, fresh and clean. In short: always works and for everyone.

Think of Shalimar (Extrait) with booze and a harsher citrus note, minus the Jasmine, and enter the cacao. Clearly not as rich and well blended, but definitely inspired. Manlier. I didn't catch it until I recently acquired the Extrait version of Shalimar. I kept on thinking it vaguely reminded me of something and then, boom: this. There's no way Alberto Morillas didn't draw the comparison, even if it were inadvertent.

Gardenia, like lily-of-the-valley, needs to be built from the ground up in perfumery. As fragrant as the flower is, it doesn’t yield a gardenia essential oil. Building a flower that combines elements of green, creamy, and umami is hard enough. Then to make it dewy should be a nightmare. Maybe it was for Isabel Doyen. But we don't see the sweat, just the smooth end product Un Matin d’Orage does smell a bit like a gardenia, just enough to make the allusion. This isn't a gardenia soliflor by any means. The success is not just in the likeness to the scent but in the odd balance of forcefulness and frailty the gardenia flower suggests. Using the ghost-gardenia as a launching pad, the image of a forest floor at dawn actually comes true. Because the gardenia's scent suggests both soil and plant it is the ideal basis for this olfactory image. The watery notes have an ambient feel: misty, dewy, even muddy. Very nice work. I found an unlikely kindred spirit to Matin d'Orage in PG's Psychotrope. Matin's sweet-forest has a water-color version of Parfumerie Generale Psychotrope’s electric Jolly Rancher & leather accord. Both perfumes leave me with a very clear olfactory memory. I can call both of them to mind very easily. from scent hurdle.com

Un Matin d'Orage is one of those really feminine and dewy white floral scents. It reminds me a little of Kai, however this fragrance is much lighter and more green. This fragrance is most likely going to appeal to those that enjoyed Songes and Le Jasmin. The dominant gardenia note, while crisp in the opening, especially when alongside the citrus, becomes creamier and buttery towards the heart. The gardenia and the other floral accords in this composition, smell very naturalistic. One can imagine an exact replicate of this scent in a luscious, Spring garden. Un Matin d'Orage can sometimes be a little too one-dimensional, especially since it doesn't develop too well. The lasting power is also very fleeting which is another slight disappointment. In the drydown, it becomes increasingly soapy. Not to an extent that it's unlikable, however it does resemble a somewhat generic bar of sweet gardenia soap. While I do honestly like this fragrance, I would have aimed to improve it by making it longer lasting and perhaps more green.

Annick Goutal UN MATIN D'ORAGE is, to my nose, essentially a gargantuan gardenia (GG) perfume with a few twists and turns thrown in for good measure, but the gardenia note is rather strong, so be prepared. I see that gardenia is not listed as a note, but are not gardenia notes always constructed? I believe that champaca and magnolia are substituting for what is often tuberose, but jasmine, another key note in big white florals, is present here as well. The spiciness imparted by the champaca is a nice touch, and there definitely are some notable green and woody elements moderating the gardenia as well, especially moving toward and in the drydown. From the name, I think that I may have been expecting something along the lines of something in the Hermes UN JARDIN... series, but UN MATIN is a very, very feminine fragrance, as I should have been able to guess by now from my earlier AG experiences... I like this slightly oriental, slightly green and woody, big gardenia composition and recommend it for gardenia lovers as an alternative to MARC JACOBS or KAI. UN MATIN D'ORAGE is spicier and more complex than both, with big sillage and excellent longevity on my skin.

To me, this smells nothing like a stormy morning but a bouquet of lilies in a closed room; sickly sweet, oppressive and borderline nauseating. It’s shallow, insincere ... sentimental in the worst possible way. If I met a matron wearing this I would be instantly on my guard. (By the way, I should say, I hate lily perfumes and anything that contains Lilial : Butylphenyl Methylpropional, it -literally- makes my toes cringe.)

Rain on a flower garden. Green hints, which leave room for a riot of incisive, strong floral notes. The kind of floral that unfortunately I don't like is the presence of gardenia which I hardly appreciate (de gustibus) but I wouldn't be able to wear it. I see it well on a young, innocent, soap and water girl. Spring. “Young Girl with a Bouquet of Flowers” painted by Perrault.

It's smooth, I'll give it that, but its a smooth bald tyre, worn out and down, no tread, no traction. I can't find the enthusiasm for this AG even though I thoroughly respect the intention. I was no fan of the original Chloe and this reminds me of it for some reason. Can't buy in to the story, this is not an Carolinas answer to Apres L'Ondee.

In one of my boks on perfume, Annick Goutal is presented as a brand, that makes fragrances with a story. Both Annick Goutal herself and later her daughter, Camille, have made perfumes, that are widely recognized for their quality and creative composition. I am not convinced with this one. Unfortunately, this is the only Goutal I have met so far. The ginger is very dominant.

Un Matin d'Orage opens like a blooming gardenia under the rain. It's creamy and intense, as if it's enhanced by the rain. Some characteristics of jasmine and magnonlia can be detected though they never take the leading role of gardenia. This strong gardenia phase lasts around 2 hours then gradually mellows. It seems to be linear.

It is high summer and already early in the morning it is very hot. A thunderstorm is approaching and lightning and thunder, accompanied by a heavy downpour, sweep across the land. People have all retreated into their houses. But after a short time, the thunderstorm is over, and it is only 10:30 AM and still morning.

It is raining: the sun is still shining faintly, hardly a breeze can be felt - the rain falls softly and balsamically on the already far too dry ground. This is the current situation on this evening in this city. Admittedly: The exact opposite of what "Un Matin d'Orage" by Annick Goutal conveys.

Only a few days ago I was thinking that Bvlgari was one of the fairly" safe to blind buy from" . And that I always at least liked or tolerated their scents even if I wasn't head over heels in love with all of them. I must have jinxed myself. On my skin Paraiba opens with mashed bananas ( baby food) with a side order of artificially flavored and colored banana candy ( recall those hard candies shaped like the flavors they were supposed to be? Those.) A few minutes drydown reveals a " tropical floral " heart --unfortunately it strongly reminds me of some bathroom deodorizer spray ( green can Glade? Febreeze?) which my dad uses whenever he's let off a big stink bomb in there. Honestly I dislike this " tropical " stuff so much, I'd rather smell the stink bomb. Base is beginning to appear--a clean musk and freshness of vetiver . This part is rather pleasant, if it didn't have the ( repulsive to me ) top and heart notes overshadowing it. I'm reviewing from a sample I acquired free from Sephora, thankfully NOT from a blind bought bottle. Enough of this,I'm off to scrub.

"Omnia Paraiba" is an excellent, young, and playful cocktail fragrance. For the Caribbean, for the South Seas, for parties like beach days. Whether Brazil or Curacao, whether the Dominican Republic or the Maldives. With this turquoise grin in flacon form, the sun always seems to shine. Probably the final and youngest of all Omnias. The latter applies to both the target audience and its release. The scent is primarily sparkling, fruity, and colorful. You can almost taste the passion fruit, and it rocks every place, hut, beach bar, or pool. But what makes this vacation scent better than many of its peers, mostly flankers or summer editions, is its backbone. Fine vetiver makes it almost unisex. Simply refreshing and sporty, delicious and positively naive. A lively find, with which you can never go wrong during summer vacation. Only very occasionally does it come off as somewhat artificial and lab-like, at least when you bury your nose too deep into the skin. But no normal person does that. Only we perfume enthusiasts from time to time. Flacon: if there wasn't so much plastic involved, it would still be one of the most beautiful designer flacons on the market. Sillage: no aggressive punch, rather a decent drink. Longevity: this beach club lasted 4 hours. Conclusion: the definition of easy-to-wear. Especially on vacation. You just have to pull the stick out of your backside. Then you have fun! Unforced, likeable, exotic.

.... I would like to sing that if I could only sing, but let's leave it at that. I just came home from a little jogging round. It’s cold and yet I’m sweating a bit, so I was looking forward to a hot shower. And what do I see: A package is lying in front of the front door, the scent is here. I AM EXCITED Omnia Paraiba, WHAT a name. (No idea what that means, I should look it up). A fragrance that, as a layperson, I imagine scents to be, just like it might smell on a Caribbean island. Fruity and floral sweet, that’s how it actually smells all the time. I can’t detect a scent progression, but that doesn’t matter because this composition is simply brilliantly made. It delights my heart and my soul. I can’t say more about it, nor do I need to. Try it out for yourselves, even if you’re not a fan of fruity notes, this one will please you. And not just in summer, even now it creates a feeling that blissful sun, fragrant fruits, combined with friendly floral-sweet bundles fill the air. Ah - you really start to dream, at least I do Take care (Hopefully you don’t think I’m crazy, dreaming of the Caribbean during the Advent season) tz tz tz

Today I fished a turquoise cover out of my surprise bag. Aha - Omnia paraiba. This fragrance immediately set my thoughts sailing. I don’t like being in the water - but I do enjoy being on it. Above me, the azure sky shines, and the white bow of the proud ship plows through the choppy turquoise waves. On deck, a cool breeze caresses my sun-warmed skin, and the rise and fall of the ship is extremely soothing. I think of my great-uncle, a well-traveled sea captain - and how I, a passionate non-swimmer. In his view, the best prerequisite for a good sailor. The ship is like a large cradle - and the wind sings the lullaby. It brings distant Curacao orange with it, and the relaxing aroma of passionflower. The gardenia blooms fully on the shore, and the scent of cocoa wafts from the galley. Safety in the vastness of the sea. Sweet vetiver lingers in the air - the ship begins to gently roll, and I feel pleasantly drowsy. Up - down. Up - down. In my dream, I am a daring pirate maiden - and the brave conqueror of the seven seas.

Bvlgari "Omnia Paraiba" is for me a pure summer fragrance. A scent that embodies sun, beach, and sea, and a lot of Brazilian feeling. In my imagination, "Omnia Paraiba" develops into a nice summer cocktail: a base of Curacao bitter orange (a few alcohol percentages get the circulation going), adding passion fruit and flower, as well as a considerable portion of candied, intensely fragrant Brazilian gardenia. Now everything is shaken a little for the first time! Cocoa beans and vetiver give this liquid beach magic a bit of longevity, a certain foundation. Add crushed ice and shake well; then strain. Perhaps a little sparkling, bubbly addition - and serve with a fun "drinking straw"! Salute! "Paraiba" is a bit of an outlier, even in the rather adventurous fragrance series "Omnia" by Bvlgari: for me, its fruity sweetness is somewhat out of the ordinary. It really only fits the height of summer: with short summer dresses, warm nights, and lots of samba, à la Copacabana! Like many of the Bvlgari fragrances, "Omnia Paraiba" does not last very long. When reapplying, please do so with a bit of feeling! On well-warmed skin, otherwise a certain "double wow" effect could occur! (This was even the case for me with "fish blood".) The bottle again consists of the well-known two rings: this time inspired by the color of the Paraiba tourmaline. This gemstone is found in the state of Paraiba in northeastern Brazil and shows, besides green and blue, many (soft to radiant) intermediate tones. Whether it’s such a radiant turquoise as here - I don’t know. I have been experimenting with the "Omnia" fragrances for a while. As a classic Bvlgari fan, they are all a bit of an adjustment for me. So far, only "Crystalline" has truly managed to win me over; however, with "ringing play and fluttering flags"! Surely "Omnia Paraiba" will find its admirers. I will not be among them, but I find it quite entertaining and amusing. Just as a summer intermezzo should be!

Floral soap, flowery and pleasant. I smell flowers ... floral soap or a perfume? Maybe a perfume & soap in one? ... still very pleasant, the heart opens ... a meadow full of flowers ... without grass or "greenery". In the middle stands a citrus tree ... bitter orange gives a fresh kick and keeps you awake and fit ...

Rose and patchouli last for several hours, the liquid version is also "spritzier" in a figurative sense. I use the perfume as a daily driver or for layering with fresh scents. Perfect for the office, as the solid scent simply takes up less space. The case is heavy but compact, robust, and the hinge with magnetic closure is absolutely high-quality. The solid inserts are relatively inexpensive, and the scents can be changed.

For me, a dreamy blend, it starts like a summer garden after the rain, fruity with blackcurrants and green. The tomato leaf accord used is also a new development, I think, as it generally smells more like wild greenery and not so strictly like tomato leaf. ...Then the sun comes out and it becomes more floral with jasmine. I love jasmine, but I also have phases with it. In summer, it suits me well. A lightly fruity sweetness and a bit of green remain, and I perceive the monoi note (floral-creamy-sweet) as an exotic bonus. Total mental escape from everyday life. Like sitting in that garden and performing a hair care ritual with monoi oil. Even in the drydown, no disturbing harsh notes emerge. Longevity and sillage are stronger than expected; I actually intended to use it as a body spray, but I force myself to a maximum of 7 sprays. What is too much for many is just perfect for me. I don't find the name very fitting.

I don't think I could ever refer to Eau de Charlotte as being a gourmand. To my nose, this fragrance is more of a rich fruity floral rather than being particularly 'foody'. Nevertheless, Eau de Charlotte is a lovely fragrance. It's a surprising scent to say the least. In the opening it's very juicy and intense, however in the drydown it becomes soft and powdery. Eau de Charlotte opens with sweet berries, which almost resemble the scent of home-made berry jam. Very delicious indeed. I began to predict that this fragrance would mellow slightly and end with a musky drydown, however, as I said before, Eau de Charlotte is surprising, you can't preempt how this fragrance will develop. In the heart, Eau de Charlotte became quite flowery and feminine. The combination of both mimose and lily-of-the-valley is crisp and refreshing, bringing me to conclude that this would make an excellent Spring/Summer scent. The vanilla is pretty much all I can smell in the base notes, which certainly isn't a bad thing because vanilla settles on my skin beautifully and just happens to be one of my favourite notes. Overall, Eau de Charlotte is unusual, classy, relatively long-lasting, wearable and very enjoyable.
Blackcurrant jam on toast beside a jar of daffodils. Occasional visits from other flowers and some suntan lotion. Lovely and simple.

I don't love lillies, but in Eau de Charlotte they hold hands with the mimosa and skip rope together on a sunny spring day in Jardin de Luxembourg. This powdery freshness goes really well with a pleated skirt and ballerina shoes. To my nose it's not a sweet gourmand, I feel like the cocoa is kind of bitter and the vanilla is just a barely detectable shadow in the base. Like a lot of other Annick Goutal perfumes, if you want better silage and longevity, I recommend letting it macerate for a year or so before using it. I prefer to spray it on my hair, because it seems to last longer that way compared to my skin. Absolutely beautiful spring fragrance.

I can't detect any vegetable notes like soup greens in Eau de Charlotte, but I can imagine that the lily is to blame here, as it has a nuance that I could certainly describe as musty, harsh, or bitter in a more concentrated form. Thankfully, it is used so subtly in Eau de Charlotte, just as I would have wished for Penhaligon's Lily&Spice. I also don't perceive blackcurrant, especially not the tart black variety, and I believe that is not even intended, since the pyramid mentions blackcurrant blossom, not the fruit. It's nice to know that A. Goutal's daughter likes blackcurrant jam, but in my opinion, that's more of a marketing strategy. All in all, this perfume is a delightful unsweetened floral scent without the obligatory citrus note at the start and without berries and fruits that often give floral perfumes a sticky quality. Here, on the other hand, the bitter cocoa tempers overly girlish romance with a powdery seriousness. Even though the scent is said to be created for a young woman, it is quite mature and radiates calm elegance. Thus, it would also be wearable for me, although I would have preferred an even darker base.

..then I put on Eau de Charlotte! Tinkerbell is wearing her green dress, Lillefee is a dream in pink, and my dress is purple. A delicate purple! With white lace fringes and pom-poms on the sleeves. Tinkerbell has her hair up again, Lillefee has little curls, and I've braided my hair. Sweet, the three of us blondes at the doll table with colorful dishes. Little cupcakes with currants are on the table, and we are enjoying our tea. Hmm, somehow I think there are way too few currants. We are cheerful, goofing around. Then Lilli tells us about some stupid guy from the other fairy clan! He stood her up. Lilli suddenly has to cry. We cry along. All three of us are such softies. But sweet softies. Enough crying. Our favorite boy band "The Fairy Stealers" is playing. They are quite the naughty ones. With a bit of kohl and all. A secret among the three of us is that we secretly like really baaad boys. But we won't tell anyone. We prefer to drink tea with our dolls. Just as you would expect from three fairies. Two skinny ones and one chubby fairy. Cute. If you can picture this now, then you also have an idea of how I perceive Eau de Charlotte. It starts off very delicately. You definitely can't talk about lush floral bouquets. Delicate, mint-green floral rays let the fragrance start off sunny. Really fairy-like, as the floral veil unfolds around me. Good vibes are in the air. Smiling, like lovesick teenagers, After a while, the scent on my skin becomes almost creamy. I feel as if I have rubbed myself with a body lotion sprinkled with fairy glitter. It provides a cozy, delicate feeling of protection and the belief that in the fairy world, everything is good except for stupid boys. And to make that feeling last longer, I applied some body powder at the end. The powder is cream-colored and has cocoa on the logo. I would have preferred if they had left it off the logo and packed more into the powder. If I didn't know that cocoa is in it, I probably wouldn't notice it. Well, I’ll have another cup with Tinki and Lill'! It's a shame that our tea time is always so short. Charlotte always disappears after three hours. A short but lovely pleasure. What a pity. I like tea time and the scent. Both should last longer. So, I have to fly home now. I need to feed my unicorn and then do my homework. I don't like homework. Tomorrow I have to ask Tinkerbell again if that guy has apologized to Lilli. And if she is still sad, she'll just get a spritz from Charlotte. Then we'll listen to the kohl boys, wave our star wands, and everything will be alright again! Thanks for reading!

Eau de Charlotte was a blind purchase for me. I had the unique opportunity to snag the EdT online at such a low price that I was almost compelled by an inner urge to place the order. The fragrance pyramid also sounded very tempting and "safe"; blackcurrant blossom, vanilla, cocoa,… Beautiful! When it finally arrived, I could hardly wait to spray it on immediately.

“Eau de Charlotte” is the counterpart to “Eau de Camille” In both perfumes, Annick Goutal has made a small gift to her daughters. Actually, there are two Camille scents, as the pear fragrance “Petite Cherie” is also dedicated to her.

With my fragrance, I thought it had gone off. So Snoopy kindly sent me a sample of this little water. No, it IS like that! I find the top note really extremely strange. Very sharp-spicy, it leans a bit towards ultra-bitter licorice. There’s not a trace of fruitiness in my nose, at least not in the first few minutes.

The first whiff that hit my nose after the test spray was - Maggi! After a few minutes, the Maggi became warmer and smelled very herbal, dry-musty, and like soup greens. Like the little bouquet that you put in the broth when you want to make vegetable stock. I also smell dill, fennel, and dry savory. I can forget about the pyramid. Did Annick Goutal not like her stepdaughter?

I just got the sample. First impression: The scent isn't really exciting. My first associations are, blue Pacific wave (ok probably heavily influenced by the title) and the smell when vitamin effervescent tablets dissolve in mineral water. The opening is as expected fresh fresh fresh and citrusy bright with a bit of sharpness. The scent doesn't really change much after that, although it does lose some freshness. The fizzy impression intensifies and sometimes drifts towards a slightly sweet laundry detergent. Mhh overall, the scent feels iridescent and somewhat metallic, minimally spicy and fizzy ?!. If you're simply looking for a fresh summer scent that isn't overly sweet, you'll find it here. It's not particularly exciting or complex, and the smell is familiar, although perhaps more from men's aftershaves ;)

Looooove Goutals. [*strict-look-and-long-pause-to-create-awkward-feeling-for-the-other-person*]. You are on the right track. The way back. We agreed that we wanted to forget your chemical madness called Vent de Folie as quickly as possible. A sentiment that, by the way, apparently some have joined, considering that the… hm, little water doesn’t quite fit… uh… Hediönchen is already occasionally found in the cheap spots after just about a year. And now? You’ve been caught. You tried to disguise the stuff as mandarin peel, but you won’t play that game with me! I noticed it immediately. Aha, you want a slow withdrawal. And I must admit, there is indeed a resemblance to the smell of citrus fruit peels. Let’s leave it at that without resorting to Erlenmeyer flasks and Bunsen burners for proof (Alright, I did beat around the bush a bit above…). With the next fragrance, you’ll return to your old virtues, especially your once inimitably natural sprightliness, for which Eau d'Hadrien is somewhat the exemplary type. Agreed? Despite the gloomy weather, I chose the new Goutal creation one morning for a test. First of all, I had become very curious after DOCBE’s comment (including the appropriate appreciation of the indeed language-baffling mandarin volcano) and quickly got myself a sample. Secondly, the office day would only be half a day and would kindly transform into an HH city center day in the afternoon. And there, as we know, there’s more to test. I don’t need an endless fragrance in the morning. I just like to prepare carefully. I even wore my half-day shoes. They are a slightly tight pair that I wouldn’t risk on a full office day. Mandarin and citrus notes are fine. My above comments don’t mean that it doesn’t smell citrusy, where hesperidins always emit a slightly synthetic scent anyway. The highly regarded Eau d'Hadrien is, by the way, no exception in this regard. Osmanthus seems plausible to me as well. Due to lack of pure knowledge, I’ve always had to piece that together from other sources (especially through Osmanthus from TDC). Without announcement, I would have initially recognized the tea in the scent only with difficulty, which is similar to what the esteemed opening commentator experienced. On the contrary, the synthetic component becomes stronger for me over the course of the morning and creates a deep furrow on my forehead. I only unmistakably perceive the tea in the late morning, although I’m not sure which one it is supposed to be. Something aromatic. I find that simply annoying. And then, of course, this chemical stuff (unfortunately only that) lasts longer than expected, namely about six hours (*scrub, scrub*). I have nothing against decent longevity, but not like this. No, no, dear Goutals, there’s still a proper piece of the way to go. Back, of course.

And I do! Because this is the most phenomenal scent I've had in a long time. The offer was good, so I bought a 100ml bottle for men, more or less blindly. That was about a week ago. The first 15 ml are already gone. And no one else has gotten any of it. This scent can be worn excessively. In the morning, at noon, in the evening, at night, every day. For walking, shopping, working, cuddling, having coffee... just all the time. And that even if you're not a citrus fan. It is present but not intrusive, only unfortunately it disappears far too quickly. Now I wish I had bought 3 or 4 bottles at that great price, but the discounted little bottles are unfortunately all gone, and with my consumption, I'm struggling with leaving 100 bucks or more at the dealer. Especially since my cabinet is full of fragrances. But now let's talk about the scent: A lot has already been said, and everyone perceives the scent differently; it develops differently for each person, and everyone likes something different. That's a good thing. I was a bit afraid of the 100 ml after what I had read. And yes, it's true. The 4711 alcohol note at the beginning is indeed disgusting; no one can deny that, but then! Then follows this wonderful, natural tea note. I perceive it more as white and green, not black, maybe brewed for 10 seconds too long and therefore a bit bitter for a green or white tea. And along with that, fresh mandarins; I love the scent of mandarins, especially during Christmas when everyone is eating mandarins (except me, because I really don't like eating them, just smelling them). Occasionally, light flowers join in, rounding off the tea scent. Since the longevity isn't that great, I like to reapply after 2-3 hours, even before everything is finished. And when reapplying, the best part of the scent comes out. I smell very delicate natural honey and a hint of bitter chocolate that joins the tea. Not long and not abundant, but just as if you quickly lick the honey spoon while enjoying the tea and push a tiny piece of dark chocolate behind it, letting both linger on your tongue until they are gone. You can really feel comfortable, and it also makes you happy. I don't perceive it as synthetic at any moment. What is actually missing is the "gammel" note that many Goutals like to leave on my skin, which makes me happy. With all my love for the scent, I also enjoy a "simple" fragrance that doesn't challenge the nose. Although I don't find L'Île au Thé boring either. By the way, I am a passionate coffee drinker and a citrus hater, but I enjoy a cup now and then with my brother, who is a tea junkie and pays prices in the hundreds for 100g of tea. Maybe that's why I like the scent so much, because I had no specific expectations for it, but I had already had quite a bit of tea.

With Annick Goutal's fragrances, there are obviously only two opinions: you either like them or you don't! I like them, but I also know which scents from the large collection do not suit me at all: I stay away from those! Or I discover them at a later time with great astonishment! But then I have changed, not the fragrance! I have loved "L'Île au Thé" from the very beginning. Perhaps it's also because I really enjoy Osmanthus tea. This is the main ingredient of this scent. How many cups of this wonderful flavored green tea have I already enjoyed: a drink for lovers of the extraordinary. This Annick Goutal fragrance opens pleasantly lightly with several citrus notes and a hint of recognizable fresh ripe mandarin. (Although mandarin always smells a little synthetic to me.) Right after that, the scent characteristic of Osmanthus flowers develops, which is slightly supported by white musk. Without it, this fragrance composition would be too light, too insubstantial. But as it is, it is surprisingly lively: sparkling and effervescent like a glass of champagne! Or two? Or even more? "L'Île au Thé" lifts my spirits, making me a little addicted to "more"! That certain lightness of being - no problem: here it is! Especially in early spring, when there is still a wintry lethargy within me, this addition is very welcome. Since this one, like many Annick Goutal fragrances, does not last very long, it is a pleasure to indulge in a little "more" again and again. The very sensual glass bottle invites me to constant touch anyway. How tempting it is then to spray a little "more" right away ... "L'Île au Thé" is like a little buzz - just without the hangover! I promise!

The start of the fragrance is aquatic due to the mandarin - and then it becomes zesty citrus. A beautiful invigorating beginning, as I was still so sleeeepy. But the intro is not a cold hostel shower, but a room-temperature soft rain shower that gently leads into the here and now. So I cheerfully take care of my things, only to cuddle up at home on the sofa. Now comes a surprisingly calm turn, thanks to the Tea Absolue. Supported by noble osmanthus, Earl Grey envelops my nose - and it has been steeped for a long time. The now calming effect of the tea sets in - and I become pleasantly drowsy. A misty gaze through the wet panes into the winter garden - and the dream fairy takes me away. I find this effect simply wonderful. A trip to a shimmering island - behind my eyelids. Afterwards, I wake up refreshed and eager for adventure. A tea elixir from a magic island.

Okay, a fragrance that translates to "Island of Tea" certainly piques my curiosity, as you all know, I'm totally into tea. I can easily imagine an island where different types of tea grow, just waiting to be "picked" and brewed. Though... the island would need to have some freshwater, otherwise, you only have the salty water around the island to make tea *gag-endlessly-gag* eww.... But, I don't want to judge too quickly and will spray the fragrance on. The excitement builds... The scent: Oh, this is great. I smell pure black tea, mixed with strong, citrusy notes that are both refreshing and make the tea smell a bit like green tea (which is also great). However, the scent later does smell a bit like black tea again. Unfortunately, the lovely tea scent is somewhat clouded (for me) by floral notes that seem a bit stuffy, which I personally don't like as much. Fortunately, this doesn't last too long (even though it remains slightly stuffy in the background, unfortunately), as the musk likely makes the (tea) scent a bit better again, and also sweeter. The sillage and longevity: At first, the scent is quite strong. It hits you with a real tea fragrance, as if you had stuck your nose (or your whole head!) into a tea bag to sniff the dry leaves. But unfortunately, after a short time, the scent weakens more and more, until it eventually becomes quite close to the skin. This naturally also affects the longevity, so I could smell the fragrance on me for about five to six hours. The bottle: The bottle has the familiar beautiful shape of most women's bottles from Annick Goutal. It is cylindrical with a thicker middle part. The bottle is surrounded by grooves and topped with a large, golden cap. The label is attached, as always, to a piece of shoelace-like cord that is wrapped around the neck of the bottle. All in all, very nicely done. First, I want to reassure everyone who thought of salty notes because of the term "Island of Tea" as mentioned in the introduction. Because such a thing does not occur here at all. Phew... However, when thinking of tea and island, one might also think of Great Britain! Even though the scent occasionally smells stuffy, it offers a great tea fragrance. The scent is also refreshing due to the citrus notes, making it suitable for spring and summer. Nevertheless, this fragrance is still not outstanding and smells like many other (good or above-average) tea fragrances, so everyone has to test it for themselves. For me, it's okay, maybe a bit too floral, so there are definitely better tea fragrances for me. But I don't find it as bad as some describe it here.

I tried the scent last summer but soon set it aside because I wanted nothing to do with musk. Now I have opened my horizons a bit again, and I am giving this fresh fragrance another chance despite the winter season. My first impression is that of an Eau de Cologne. This is not my first choice even in midsummer, and at this moment it feels irritatingly cool.

This is stunning, the perfect amount of dry, rubbery oud and spicy resins to balance the boozy vanilla. There is absolutely something in this formula giving it brightness- almost like a tea note. Not too sweet for daytime/casual wear. Great longevity, not a room-filler but consistent ~2ft projection throughout the day. To the folks who say this isn't unique enough to justify the price, I hear you- but you are not the target demographic. Sure, you can find vanilla/oud scents for less (albeit none that smell like Orom), but out of dozens of decants in this scent category none have matched the quality and effervescence of Orom.

I was eager to try Orom, as I have smelled all other fragrances from the le Gemme line (except Kobraa!). Well, my first impression is.... ok. It is quite soft and introvert, with an emphasis on a dusty oud, rather than vanilla. The vanilla is unmistakenly present, though. It reminds me of Mancera's Vanilla Oud. This sure isn't a creamy gourmand, what I was hoping for. Not bad, but nothing special. 7/10 Today is my first full wear. Ok, it was a tad bit better than I expected --> 7,5/10 :)

I don't know why this fragrance is among the lesser-known Le Gemmes. Maybe the oud note scares people from trying this? An oud fragrance I adore is Atkinson's "Oud Save The King". It smells suede-y, powdery, suave, confident, has a very magnetic Earl Grey Tea note, and the oud is not animalic, barnyard-y or fecal in any way. It's giving sweet, synthetic (in a good way), velvety-woody. Orom shares the same base as Oud Save The King. Same type of sweetness, same oud, this one is slightly more resinous though. But not as resinous as, lets say, Grand Soir. Orom is a very comforting, elegant, masculine-leaning fragrance, which I would wear, but at this price point, i would personally go with Oud Save The King, or Penhaligon's "Babylon". This doesn't stop me from giving Orom the rating it deserves. It's done very well.

“Orom” is a fantastic new addition to Bvlgari's Le Gemme collection. Very wintry, soft, and wonderful. A leather gourmand that is anything but off-the-shelf. At first, it almost feels like a tamed “Tuscan Leather” with much less or no fruit at all. This pleasing sweetness is taken over by an expensive vanilla. The leather is distinct and bright. A beige dream to dream about. But certain oud notes provide a dark counterbalance. Overall, it has an otherworldly fluffy Milky Way aura. Leather has rarely been interpreted as creamy and cozy. In conjunction with the presentation of Le Gemmes, it is indeed a play of beauty and luxury, of armchair and shoe, of pastry and the Orient. Brilliant, but I think I would wear it too rarely for the price. Nevertheless, a feel-good fragrance from the highest shelf. Bottle: pure class and beauty Sillage: noticeable and assertive (outward), but never overpowering Longevity: 7-10 hours, but with a wide range in extreme cold Conclusion: useful both as a leather scent and as a vanilla crescent. More than that. Luxurious, noble, different, pleasant. Alien cuddle romance.

Finally - an Oud fragrance from the Le Gemme collection that doesn't smell synthetic and unbalanced. After my reviews of Le Gemme - Falkar and "Le Gemme - Onekh | Bvlgari," I was a bit worried about "Le Gemme - Orom | Bvlgari." That worry was unfounded - Orom is a dream, and here are the reasons why: - Le Gemme - Orom opens with a beautiful vanilla-oud-benzoin note, which is soon complemented by a soft leather. Everything smells perfectly coordinated, a real dream. Strong, potent, yet cozy. - Gradually, warm sandalwood joins in, and the sweet vanilla note remains but slowly fades into the background. The oud and the bright leather linger in a lovely blend on the sandalwood, creating an extremely pleasant, potent base in the drydown. - The projection is very good but not overpowering; such a beautifully balanced fragrance simply cannot come off as overwhelming, in my opinion. Really top-notch! The longevity is truly fantastic - the scent lasts a long time, easily throughout the whole day (10H) In summary, a truly beautiful leather-oud-vanilla composition that is not as piercing and abrasive as "Tuscan Leather (Eau de Parfum) | Tom Ford," nor as fruity as "London | Widian / AJ Arabia" or "Oud Maracujá | Maison Crivelli," but simply elegant and perfectly balanced with creamy vanilla, bright leather accord, and the tamed oud. The only thing that would hold me back from a blind purchase is the hefty price. Therefore, definitely test it before a possible buy!

The Le Gemme - Orom is a very masculine-tinged fragrance. As a woman, you really have to be quite self-confident to wear this. Truly a spicy-leathery beast in a bottle!!! And that brings us to the point. The Le Gemme - Orom is indeed a purely leathery scent with strong spice. Vanilla peeks through only very slightly.

First of all, a great fragrance. It took me quite a while to categorize all the notes. At first, it was a leather bomb for me with a hint of wood and vanilla. Now, a couple of hours later, I must say it has become very versatile. In the opening, it is very masculine meaning smoky, woody, leathery, resinous, and a bit of vanilla, which rounds it off very well.

My new love!!! I didn’t expect to like it this much, but wow ! The mix of tea and fresh notes smells absolutely amazing. It’s soft but striking, refreshing and elegant. Such a unique take on rose for me and I am not even into rose perfumes to be honest, but I am completely obsessed with this one now!

tested at the Printemps Lyon store as part of my search for new gems in this brand. rose or die reminds me from the start of a perfume from the old collection, the 1001 roses, a rose refreshed by notes of lemon, a perfume very clearly for summer or spring. it's fresh then the tea takes over, reminding me of rose Milano then peony suzhou from the Armani Privé collection, lighter and almost no longer smells after 3 hours. Tonic and energizing already felt, already known, with a price difficult to justify given the performances

A lovely raspberry, peony, and rose fragrance. Natural, youthful, sweet, and flirty. Light and pleasant, works well in warm weather. The raspberry comes off natural and not too sweet. I didn't expect to like a raspberry scent because I've only experienced it as a cloyingly synthetic note in cheap body sprays. But it's really delicate and beautiful here. Rose Pompon EDT is a lot of fun. I'm curious about the EDP now.

Today, my husband and I had a dentist appointment - a trip to Canossa for both of us. In a bad mood, we were wandering around and were very taciturn. On top of that, we are also suffering from a nasty cold, and we are coughing and wheezing in competition. My husband called the practice and told them about our unfortunate condition. And - lo and behold - the doc would rather not see us! A wise man. A weight lifts off my heart, because "the test has been postponed". Our mood rises back to operating temperature, and I spray Rose Pompon with gratitude. Ah - this friendly, cheerful scent lifts the spirits once again! Vibrant pepper mixed with delicious raspberry gives me energy. I dance to the radio, and Richard Marx is singing "Right here waiting". A heartfelt soft song that matches the velvety rose aroma, over which a delicate, bitter tea scent gently lays. The tart blackcurrant is now making itself known - combined with noble smoky cedar. Despite my runny nose, I can enjoy the scent - and also the optimism it radiates. Indeed, that pesky cold has spared us from the dentist. Everything is always good for something else. Should the "trip to Canossa" be on the agenda, I will arm myself with Rose Pompon, as it belongs in every fragrance home pharmacy.

Annick Goutal bottles are not only beautiful, handy, and practical (since they are refillable), they also catch the eye - just like this one. I have fallen for it and had it on my "want" list. Luckily, only on the list! Because thanks to a very, very dear parfumo friend, I was able to test it now... The opening is wonderfully beautiful and it makes me crave a Kir Royal! The black currant smells simply lovely and surprisingly natural. This note lasts quite a long time and is truly a delight. Then the rose should actually come; Bulgarian and Taif rose - no sign of that, peony and centifolia - yyyyyyes, at least for a short while. After about an hour, I have rose soap on my skin and ONLY rose soap. Nothing of real roses, but also nothing from the base notes, just soap, soap, soap - with a slight rose scent. Rose Pompon - what a name! When I think of pompons, I always think of cheerleaders and see them bouncing around. Ultimately, it fits, because cheerleaders are usually young and this scent actually suits young girls. It reminds me a bit of Lipstick Rose. If someone gave me the empty bottle, I wouldn't say no, I would clean it and fill it with my favorite scent. However, I will not buy Rose Pompon, as it does not meet my expectations of a beautiful rose scent.

On a rather gray day, I discovered this fresh scent for myself. It is fresh like spring, floral, slightly sweet, fruity, and it doesn't overwhelm. For me, it is romantic, far from kitsch. Something special. It is sour-fruity and softly floral. The peony is fresh, authentic, but also somewhat distant. The scent seems youthful at first glance, but it is mature. The Taif rose shines, but subtly. A fragrance like a botanical garden just coming into bloom, in the middle of spring, just before summer. Rose Pompon feels very natural and is, in a narrower sense, a peony scent, behind which lies a nice idea that has been skillfully executed and poured into a beautiful bottle. Not a soliflore, but a fragrance that contains few ingredients and still expresses something.

From the beauty of the English rose garden of Atkinsons’ “Rose in Wonderland,” my rose fragrance journey now leads me to Provence. Pompon roses surely also bloom in the beautiful rose garden of Christian Dior at his estate “La Château de la Colle Noire.” There, the varieties “Pompon de Bourgogne” and “Pashmina” must be blooming as well, whose flowers are not only beautiful to behold but also smell divine. This is not to say that the experienced perfumers Camille Goutal and Philippine Courtière from the house of Annick Goutal need to draw inspiration from Christian’s gardens; they manage just fine on their own! Their creation “Rose Pompon” clearly demonstrates this. But just the thought that the two ladies might meet there with François Demachy, my favorite perfumer of recent years (including from the house of Christian Dior Parfum), for a chat over a glass of wine is “très charmant”: A relaxed exchange of ideas among fragrant roses! “Rose Pompon” is also très charmant as an Eau de Toilette, soft pink and light-footed, exceedingly feminine and very buoyant: "A little Flirtation" is captured within it! A pink-raspberry opening, supported by stronger aromas of blackcurrant and pink pepper: A fruity-spicy top note emerges, leading into the pink floral world and then into a sensually warm base. For we are immediately surrounded by the enticing aromas of numerous precious roses and the pompon-headed, feather-filled, heavy peonies that I adore! A wave of true delight for rose fragrance lovers, not at all overwhelming or cloying, but summer-rich and full of exuberant southern cheerfulness! Thousands of fragrant roses seem to sway here in their special dance, surrounded by transparent scent veils in different color and fragrance notes. They float on a refined base of moist-earthy patchouli, silky-aromatic cedarwood spice, and plenty of warm white musk: These noble fragrance ladies could not have chosen a better dance floor! In “Rose Pompon,” everything simply fits, and this fluttering and flirtatious lightness of scent and feminine grace is, of course, reflected in the sillage and longevity. Translucent scent gauze woven from thousands of flowers dresses summerly and extremely charmingly, albeit known to be fleeting: An Eau de Toilette, and nothing more! I find here a rose fragrance that is fuller and more sensual than “Rose in Wonderland” by Atkinsons, but just as enchanting when it meets the right skin on the right occasion! “Madame Rose Pompon” flirts and floats, while “Lady Rose” only makes a quiet appearance with English understatement and a reserved smile. Both are lovable companions in their own way and can surely become good friends. There is indeed this ancient bond between women and roses! And my “Rose Journey in Fragrance” will continue: No worries, there is only one more stop ahead; where Rojas’ rose garden will surely reveal interesting and fragrant insights into the world of these noble beauties. A little summery rose magic does change the October gold somewhat, making it appear richer and warmer; we travel back once more and soak up cheerfulness and laughter. Both will be needed in the coming months, and that’s why it’s good that we have discovered our fragrance world, in which we can immerse ourselves and from which we can draw light and strength every day anew.

Beautiful and spring-like is the first impression that the new rose fragrance from Goutal makes on me. Previously, I was drawn in by the familiar ribbed bottle with its lovely gradient, which suits the delicate peony scent it initially emits. That’s exactly what it is, the scent of the magnificent bright red blooms from the garden of my childhood.

Blv, why Blv? I can't get over it! Bvlgari Blv pour Homme has been my signature cologne when it was released barely 18 years ago, and I don't think I'll ever get tired of it. It smells fresh and clean, but not in a fruity, ephemeral way. It's very unisex, actually, almost soapy and chilly powdery. I share other opinions stating it smells like baby powder, similar to rosy-cheeked posh kids decked out in clean sports gear. I don't understand why it isn't rated higher. I wouldn't say this is a super sexy cologne to wear on a date, but it does the job of making you smell better than you would without it. Beautiful, lagoon-blue bottle. The scent is a mix of cool and warm, ginger, mint, green freshness with cool tobaccos, green leaves, sandalwood... the overall effect is a very unique and powerful cologne unlike any other marketed towards men. Bvlgari Blv pour Homme is a spicy woody cologne built on top of three central elements: the balmy Cardamom, the fizzy Ginger, and the creamy Sandalwood. Indeed, it features a few other eerie notes I've never smelt before, such as Galanga rhizome, Ginko leaves, and Tobacco blossom, for an invigorating aroma that draws attention from anyone nearby. Creamy and citrus is the top of my list, I get a sort of lemongrass, the ginger is so fizzy in the opening that it fooled me into thinking that some citrus also featured in this fragrance. In that sense, it does have a very fresh, almost citrusy feel to it. Not the everyday ginger as in YSL l'Homme or Davidoff Horizon, yet this has a mellow tone to it, like the kind of ginger embedded within a bar of chocolate. I absolutely love ginger, particularly when it features in a male fragrance, such as Blv pour Homme. While there’s a clean, soapiness to it, there’s also a sweet-spiciness that keeps it from being yet another smell-alike fragrance. The ginger notes that dominate Blv can be love or hate for some so beware. The creaminess stays into the drydown but the citrus is gone quickly, just turns into a clean, soft scent. But the opening does not end here... There are spicy cardamom and rich sandalwood supplementing an exotic, masculine atmosphere that instills confidence almost immediately. Ultimately, the opening is a very calming scent that is bright and fresh. Middle notes of rare galanga, sharp juniper, and elegant ginger enhancing the aroma with their enriching botanical element. Galanga plant belongs in the same family as ginger with which it shares the piquant, spicy facets. Hence, it is pretty clear now why Blv's ginger is so different from other colognes featuring the same root note. The dry-down is smooth and mellow as well, a cool creamy base like face makeup or body lotion and the faintest hint of spice. The tobacco appears and says: "I’m here to make you elegant without annoying you." To close the door with a golden key we have delicious and balanced notes of solid teak wood, white tobacco blossoms, and ginko green leave that complete the concoction for a cool, uplifting cologne that’s original and satisfying to both the mind and body. The ginger occurs in initially and the foundation is tobacco with a tinge of sandalwood. It is creamy and a bit powdery but not over powdery at all. It is extremely well blended. One of the best aspects of Bvlgari Blv Pour Homme is its versatility. It’s a fragrance that will work at the office, on a date or even a formal dinner also. I love to wear this on hot days, especially to work. It's pleasant in every way and has modest projection while lasting for most of the workday. Because it’s a relatively clean and natural scent, it feels at home in most situations. It also has a sweetness which I usually think of as appealing to younger men, however, it’s just spicy and clean enough that it doesn’t feel like it’s exclusively for young guys. Seriously, I am 55 years old and we go together well. It always draws compliments from people as it's a very clean smelling fragrance, I'd love to own a vial of the pure perfume of this, I think I'd carry it everywhere. This isn't a real manly scent but it would really suit the right kind of person. I adore it! So soft, nostalgic, fresh, beautiful. -Elysium

It's been a while since I have seriously worn a fragrance and unfortunately, BLV Pour Homme only survived a single outing, so I won't be able to break down the notes in any detail. It smells better on the sample strip than on my skin, and that was the first disappointment; however, on my skin, it wasn't terrible, just a bit unexciting. On me, it was a clean, fresh, nearly aquatic sort of scent mingled with a bit of baby oil (disappointment number two). I'm not a fan of the latter note, but my wife found the scent to be engaging. It is a linear scent, so if you don't like it in the first hour, you'd better get thee to a scrubbery. It does last for at twelve hours, so you definitely get your money's worth in that department. With all that said, I might have kept the scent around for occasional use, but as it turns out, I cannot wear it at all, because whatever is in the base is a major allergen to cats. After sitting in my lap a minute or so, our grey tabby started turning his head to side and scratching his ear, to the point of looking like he had a neurological disorder; he has not reacted that way to any other scent I've worn. The better half and I freaked out and after we tried various things, I went to scrub the scent off, and voila`, the cat returned to normal. BLV Pour Homme is a decent scent on the whole, but cat lovers beware!

Well, as my comment’s title - this fragrance is a bit confusing. As a tester, it was a dream for my taste: fresh, clean, spicy, soapy.. woah, its just wonderful! As a bottle it was.. a bit different, because I used it on myself day after day. Positives: The frangrance is a real lady-pleaser, most of the women noticed the BLV and I got tons of compliments because of its freshness. The scent also really useful for office and daily use, so its really easy to use it. Negatives: Two times my colleagues got allergic reactions from the BLV (eye itching problems), and its not a small problem with a frangrance. The fragrance has an amazing top note, but a really borung soapy base note - and after hours of use you just probably realise there are tons of better picks than this one.

I absolutely love ginger, particularly when it features in a male fragrance, such as BLV pour Homme. The ginger was so fizzy in the opening that it fooled me into thinking that lemon also featured in this fragrance. In that sense it does have a very fresh, almost citrusy feel to it, and because of that, I recommend this fragrance for the warmer weather. I must admit that the fragrance started off quite generic, however before I could yawn, BLV pour Homme developed into something rather woodsy and enticing. There was also a subtle spiciness that I really enjoyed. This fragrance is sexy without being too bold or offensive. It smells absolutely amazing on a man I must admit. I'm a little wary to try it on my own skin in case it disappoints. This is yet another pleasant and casual male fragrance from the classic Bvlgari line, who are in my opinion the gods of modern yet simplistic scents.

Ah, who wouldn't want to smell like this! Initially fresh and fine cardamom, along with sandalwood in the top note, something completely different. The heart is thoroughly spicy with juniper berry - perhaps a bit sweet, ginger - peppery and certainly very aromatic - and also galangal, darker and somewhat cinnamon-like.
