But I hold green tea in zenlike regard, greatly preferring Japanese varieties such as sencha, bancha, genmaicha, kukicha (green), and of course matcha, which are really destroyed by adulterants such as lemon and cream. Setting aside concerns with the name of this perfume for the moment, EAU PARFUMEE AU THE VERT EXTREME opens beautifully with a blast of bitter greens. Very lemony and very green, not in the sense of tea, but more in the sense of grass. The opening reminds me a bit of Bond no. 9 CENTRAL PARK, but after the opening this unique creation becomes a very different kind of scent. A mild green tea drydown is where this composition finally ends. Light, refreshing and, yes, zenlike, as if to offer a therapeutic reprieve from the exciting Sturm und Drang opening. EAU PARFUMEE AU THE VERT EXTREME smells nice through all of its various stages of development, but the opening and drydown really seem like two completely different perfumes, and those who love the excitement of the opening may be bored by the finish. Those looking for a zenlike green tea fragrance, on the other hand, may be alarmed by the somewhat jolting opening of this one. I like both stages a lot, but it would be rare to be in a synchronic state of mind so as to be able to appreciate both the opening and the drydown in the sequence in which they unfold in this unique creation.

I am not familiar with the original edition of The Vert, which seems quite appreciated. All I know is that this Extreme version smells... this close to a nightmare, for me. I get a really little “tea” note out of this, but it’s entirely drowned in an unbearably plastic and harsh blend with coriander and cardamom above all, something citrusy, something synthetically greenish and a bunch of really pungent spices. And just other stuff I can’t recognize. This smells at the same time complex and really simple, harmonically screechy and completely disgraceful on skin. More than “notes”, it’s just olfactive noise, a weird and rough spicy-sweet-green-tea mess. I can’t explain why, maybe is just a subjective issue, but this really makes me physically sick. Tremendously bold and linear, and as if wasn’t enough, also tragically persistent. A proper “scrubber” for me. 4/10

You probably know this: You stick your nose into a bouquet of violets, sense an intense scent - and suddenly nothing more. A few moments later, having already irritably given up hope, the floral aroma nudges you powerfully again - abruptly fades away - returns… There is an explanation for this: The ionone responsible for violet flower scent, a substance from the group of ketones, is perceived by human noses only at a certain concentration. Only when a certain amount of air dilutes the ionone do we smell "violet." If there are too many fragrance molecules per liter of air, we smell nothing. And if the concentration drops below a certain level, our sense of smell is overwhelmed again. What does this have to do with "Eau Parfumée au Thé Vert Extrème"? Nothing - because although there is certainly more in the bottle than stated, violets haven’t even passed by from afar. Everything - because the scent behaves as mysteriously as that of violet flowers: seemingly long gone, it suddenly resonates again from nowhere, it comes and goes, a whimsically floating airy one. It begins with a bright green fizz, a breeze sweeps through young beech leaves. The sun is still low, casting long shadows; the morning is cool, yet it holds the promise of a warm, cheerful day. Fast-moving clouds in the blue sky constantly change the light, and with it, the color of the fragrance transforms: Quickly it turns green-gold. A delicate, yet shimmering hue, like fine silk chiffon: transparent yet vividly colored; weightless, reshaped by every gentle breeze. Nevertheless, warm and enveloping, stable, even able to withstand storms: silk, no matter how gossamer-thin, should not be underestimated; it can bear the heaviest loads (not by chance do tailors use it as sewing thread). The further development of the fragrance unfolds at a slow-motion pace. As if the perfumer, who chose green tea as the guiding motif, took its long, flat effect curve as a model for the rhythm of the scent. Slowly, very slowly, copper mixes into the green-gold. Copper? Yes. There is sweet jasmine white and the typical rose-red scent of velvety dark red, almost black roses in the heart note. But it does not turn into a marzipan confectionery pink. For well-measured spicy aromas darken the sweetness with a hint of bitterness, chestnut instead of flower honey, warmth with a nice pinch of bitterness. And then there is also the base, which comes into play very early and tempers the citrus aromas of the top note as well as the floral heart: green tea. But is it really just tea? I doubt it. To confirm, I lifted all the tea canister lids in the kitchen (there are quite a few, and the contents smell diverse, sometimes surprisingly strong): Yes, I am sure there is more in the bottle. But what? The scent's conclusion - again in a leisurely tea rhythm, a Central European long sunset, where copper gradually turns into deep, soft dark red and then fades into bluish infinity - reminds me a bit of the beautiful sandalwood notes in the finale of Creed's "Silver Mountain Water." However, those are much earthier, denser, coarser than here. In the green tea essence, the perfumer has accomplished the feat of giving the base of the fragrance grounding while still allowing it to float, silk-fine, glassily iridescent, glowing bittersweet. Riddles, fairy tales, magic… This mysterious scent music resonates for a long time (distant string quartet? - no, there are also English horn and clarinet involved - and what you hear is "classical" with wit and flair, not dramatically expressive - more Mozart than Beethoven): In the first test, dosed with the caution typical of EdP, it accompanied me for almost twelve hours. In the second test, I was a bit more generous, and now, after about nine hours, the finale is just beginning - for an Eau de Toilette, the longevity is astonishing. The scent will become mine; I find it dreamily beautiful. Why does it still only get 90 percent? Because I classify it as a "day scent," but not as a scent for every day, due to its unusually calm rhythm, which one must engage with. And because I want to get to know it properly first. (Then I could still adjust the score if needed…) _______ Update 15.03.2012: My affection for the green tea essence remains unbroken. But by now, I have encountered so many fragrances that I find just as good or even better that I am correcting the rating for the sake of standards: 80 percent.

...often comes as one knows. Right at Christmas time, I had the unexpected opportunity to get to know one of my new favorite scents, Bulgari Thé vert (extreme). According to fragrance classification, it is categorized as a spring and summer scent. In a highly recommended wellness hotel in Hesse's Frankenberg, there were baskets in the bathrooms for hotel guests containing exclusive body care products in mini sizes from various renowned perfume manufacturers. Most of them were familiar to me, but not necessarily preferred by me. There was only one type that I had not yet encountered and eyed with skepticism - Bulgari Thé vert. Curiosity won. I tried the shower/shampoo, hair conditioner, and body milk. Even while showering, I enjoyed the new scent very much, and when applying the body milk, I was completely captivated. I was instantly fascinated; the scent remained present throughout the evening during the extended gourmet menu. It caressed me, beckoned to me, seduced me. It was immediately clear to me that I had to have this scent. The body milk from the E.d.T. Bulgari Thé vert is almost more intense in scent diffusion than the E.d.T.. The combined use prolongs the fragrance pleasure, as the longevity of this wonderful scent is not very strong. Due to the longevity, after testing both variants (Thé vert and Thé verte extreme), I decided on Bulgari Thé vert extreme. This morning I sprayed it around 7:00 AM, and now at around 4:00 PM, the scent is still intensely perceptible. I also enjoy wearing Thé vert extreme in winter; surely it is a scent with a fresh green note, but it has something warm and comforting for me. As has already been very enlighteningly highlighted in other comments, it is more complex and multifaceted than one would expect from a green tea scent. For me, it is both stimulating and calming. I cannot perceive a changing scent progression. After spraying, waiting, and drinking green tea, the scent remains unchanged for me; perhaps my nose is not sensitive enough. The fact that there is no exciting scent progression in Thé vert extreme does not bother me further, even though I usually find it very exciting when a fragrance unfolds from top to heart to base notes. I find the scent enchanting, a masterpiece. The balance between green-bitter, mild-spicy, and floral, golden subtle sweetness is perfect for me.

Hey guys, how are you? Welcome to my latest review, which is once again about a tea fragrance. It’s quite fitting for this time of year, isn’t it? I mean, it’s winter and people tend to drink warm beverages more often. And besides the ever-popular coffee, tea is also a constant favorite with its various types… or mulled wine, but that’s another story :D Now, I’m coming to a tea fragrance from Bvlgari. A few years ago, I already presented all the Thé fragrances here (argh, I just realized that I still haven’t tested the black one! I really need to catch up on that!!), and I found them all really great. However, these fragrances were released with years apart, so it’s not like they all came out within a few years or even all at once. While the green one, Thé Vert, was released back in 1992, Thé Bleu, for example, only came out in 2015. Anyway, today I’m talking about the now-discontinued Extrême version of Thé Vert, which hopefully has a slightly more intense scent. Because as lovely as all the Thé fragrances are, they all share a common flaw: they all have a terribly weak sillage *sigh* Soo… arrrgh,… damn, before I can spray the fragrance, I have to remove the tape from the cap, aaaargh, why do you keep doing this… *grumble grumble* Such a hassle again… The Scent: Okay, the scent starts with a nice and fresh green tea and also has a soft powdery scent. I can smell orange blossoms, although the tea is the stronger note. Pepper and cardamom create a bitter-spicy blend. I wouldn’t say that you can really smell both notes, but I assume that the slightly spicy aura is "caused" by these two notes. The green tea even becomes a bit more intense as it develops, which I find nice. It smells distinctly of green tea, but still, the fragrance is very perfumey as it also has a powdery and creamy scent. In the base, the green tea is thankfully still present, and you can smell it quite well. The mentioned other notes like powdery and creamy scents also linger a bit, so the whole fragrance smells very good from start to finish. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage remains weak as usual for this fragrance line. Whether the scent is significantly more intense than the normal version, I unfortunately cannot say, as I don’t have the normal Thé Vert available, but it might be that there’s at least a slight difference in sillage, which doesn’t mean much since the Extrême version is also quite weak. The longevity was okay with a few hours, around four to six hours. The Bottle: The bottle is cylindrical and tapers at the spray head like a lipstick, onto which the neck attaches. This looks like the shaft of a column, on which a similarly column-like, chrome cap sits (so the cap is basically the capital of the column). In contrast to the normal Thé Vert, this one has a dark green fragrance liquid. All in all, a nice bottle. Soo! You might already guess it, but I’m also thrilled by this fragrance! Although the green tea flavor-wise only ranks lower for me (I find that over time, the green tea somehow scratches my throat, do you know that feeling too?), I find its scent in fragrances very delicious, refreshing, and lovely. The Extrême version of Thé Vert is therefore a very successful fragrance that certainly smells stronger than the normal Vert, but overall, it is still quite weak, but at least you can really smell the tea consistently. I also like its gentle side, which makes the fragrance pleasant but also a little bit feminine. I would now say that the Extrême would have been the better choice among the Vert fragrances, but unfortunately, it has long been discontinued. If you should happen to "encounter" it, I would definitely recommend giving it a test, as it is an excellent summer fragrance that can be used for refreshing on hot days, or of course, to smell pleasant on hot days, since many fragrances can feel overwhelming in the heat if you choose the wrong one. But since it is no longer available, you’ll just have to test the normal Thé Vert, which is also worth it, just like all the other Thé fragrances from Bvlgari. Soo, oh do you actually know why tea is still so frequently encountered in winter? Yaaa, of course, especially during the Christmas season, there are a lot of advent calendars available, and besides the popular chocolate advent calendars, with which you all stuff yourselves (though I hope you wait for the respective day and don’t just barbarically rip open all the doors :D), there are also various tea advent calendars, which is also a very nice thing :) Well then, that’s it again. I wish you all a lovely evening and hopefully, we’ll "see" each other again next time :D

At first, I think I must have grabbed the wrong bottle, because initially, it clearly smells like 4711 Eau de Cologne. But the zesty and radiant scent stream is quickly subdued by coriander and pepper. The two make the opening of APATVE somehow ...

I bought this fragrance towards the end of my studies. It was a lot of money for me. I lingered around it for a long time and thought it over thoroughly. The result is that I have found a scent that I still love, one that I will never get tired of. And one that I will definitely buy again. I am surprised that it has received so little attention here.

Thanks to the dear "nose," I became aware of this fragrance. Somehow, "Eau Parfumée au Thé Vert Extrême" slipped through my fingers, well, whatever. I was already familiar with the "normal" Eau Parfumée au Thé Vert by Bvlgari, which I always found too light - it's just an Eau de Cologne - that's why I never bought it.

The citrusy -bitter note of bergamot and green tea helps to keep a cool head on hot days. The spicy components, I mainly perceive the pepper, give the fragrance strength and expressiveness. Rose and jasmine provide depth and volume. The orange blossom somehow gets lost, but I don't miss it.
I once had this Eau de Toilette.. It smells very natural, not artificial or overpowering!! Imagine a beautiful, slightly cool, misty morning in summer, and then this scent!

This is a more refined, tailored or gentrified version of the original Black EDP. Less biker bad-boy feel to it. More like a black Bentley, with clean hair and ladies around. You can wear this with a suit with great effect - just like Lorenzo Viotti in the advertisment. Be warned, this projects not, it prefers to sit close to the skin, to linger, and occasionally send out wafts of its dark quality scent. Personally, I love this, except the dry-down which can be rather generic (tonka-ish). And it has to be said, the opening is rather lightweight because of the cinnamon heavy overture. However, do not listen to crybaby-boys. It lasts, a LONG time. I have it since it came out, 1,5 months, maybe. 36 hours ago, I sprayed this on my wrist, then, after 2 showers, this morning I sprayed Laudano Nero on the same wrist. Again, 12 hours later, in the shower, Laudano Nero was washed down and there came Black Parfum back from under it and radiated in the bathroom again - for a short time, though. It comes alive when wet. On clothes, it stays 3-4 days, easily. Make your bets, gentlemen.

This one starts super spicy. If the EDP was similar to Spicebomb Extreme, this one is even closer to it during the first hour. Compared to the original, I'd say this one is spicier, less Iris and something that feels to me like a... resinous vanilla or cinnamon at the base? Forget about the leather, the tobacco, and the rum, It's no longer here. Definitely feels like someone in Bvlgari went through all the "This feels like an ashtray" type of comments of the EDP, and decided to remake the original fragrance for today's market. If you want more sillage (1-2h, then stays close), compliments, and duration... get this one. I don't want to say the other one is obsolete, but, I find it hard to see people going for the EDP when this one is next to it unless they love the tobacco note or they want a more mature scent. I find the OG a more interesting pick, but, this one will work better on the market and for the average buyer.

So, the new Parfum is at 79% Alc. barely at the Parfum limit, assuming that only 1% is water inside it will have around 20% Perfume oil. I hightly doubt that, though .. so it means that on the same line of Elixirs (which were actually EDP), this one is not what it leads it to believe that it is. I enjoy the scent, it is very nice, manly and dark .. I remember the EDP quite sweet and uninspired, because there is also Spicebomb smelling similar. But this one here, it´s quite nice and unique for my nose .. Master Morillas did a good job and I will gladly have this novelty into my collection.

In this category, it is my current favorite among designer fragrances. I am just a huge fan of oriental, spicy scent notes. Only a few niche fragrances like Initio Oud for Greatness or Kilian's Straight to Heaven White Crystal as well as Editions de Parfums Frederic Malle Promise create an even more beautiful feeling. However, this perfume is in my "everyday collection" and rotates with the others. Thus, for me, it is an everyday scent that smells special and is therefore also suitable for an evening event or special occasion. The longevity is moderate (I changed this afterwards, I originally rated it better), after half a day I have to reapply. With a pure perfume, one could expect a bit more. The sillage becomes somewhat more subdued after about 3 hours, but is still pleasantly noticeable. It suits my taste. Better than the longevity in my opinion. However, I also adjusted the movement here a bit afterwards. I quite like the bottle. What other color could it have been but black? And in elegant contrast, the golden lettering. With the rotating spray head, you also don't have to worry about something accidentally ending up in your toiletry bag while traveling. Top note: starts off directly spicy oriental. To my nose, it smells like pepper in combination with the Philippine elemi resin, which reminds me of incense. It lasts relatively long. Heart note: to be honest, I find it a bit difficult to detect the iris and/or tuberose absolute note here. I think it remains rather spicy/oriental, but becomes subtly more restrained than in the top note. Base note: it feels like the patchouli note comes through in the form of a subtle smoky and very fine earthy aroma. But still spicy oriental from top to base note.

Costa Rica produces some of the best coffee in the world, but when you order it prepared in a cafe there, it is usually served in a diluted form which effectively destroys what would have been an excellent cup of coffee, if only it had been prepared with about 20% of the water that was actually used. This lamentation about how what held potential as delightful can be ruined through dilution is fully relevant to Bvlgari BLV II, which boasts some of my favorite notes in its line-up but is so weak that I find myself wishing that I could distill off all of the extra solvent. There is but the slightest soupçon of benzoin, licorice, violet, tonka, anise, labdanum, etc., in this composition. Even the patchouli is very difficult to tease out. What a beauty this might have been, if only the notes had been combined in sufficient concentration! When I smell something this flimsy (and an edp at that!) I wonder whether the perfumer may have been trying to protect the wearer from overapplication, a protection which we perfumistas really do not need. Thank you very much all the same for your misguided paternalism. Désolée. For the record, BLV II bears nearly no resemblance to BLV, and I have no idea why it was marketed as a flanker. The only overlap I find at all is that both are unisex, not feminine fragrances.

Testing BLV Eau de Parfum II for the first time was met with utterances of approval and thoughts along the lines of, "yes, I would definitely wear something like this." I held this fragrance in such high-esteem that when I went to smell it again only a few hours after application, I was horrified to have found it vanished into thin air. Despite its poor lasting strength, BLV Eau de Parfum II is one of the most unique fragrance releases in the last year or so. The candied violet when mixed with the rich, licoricey anise and mandarin orange is divine. The opening was both likable and different, being both clean and pretty at the same time. Unfortunately the scent becomes much softer and more watery as the fragrance develops. The fragrance loses a lot of its concentration, with the patchouli and vetiver being so diluted that they're barely there. A shame really, seeing that this fragrance had so much promise. The drydown was only slight evidence of its former glory. Musk and tonka bean tended to dominate, but only for a few seconds before this fragrance disappeared completely. This fragrance was a much improved, more balanced and a heavily powdered version of the original BLV. A pity that this fragrance didn't have the same amount of longevity.

First= powderies very violet, mini iris. Then= potato fries of McDonald's. That smell reminds me McDonald's coupons, mall food hall, childhood. Makes me hungry, really. I think this fastfood effect comes from= licorice+star ???? anise+powdery violets with bit of iris. :) Not much longevity, sorry. Just couple of hours.

This fragrance is absolutely a fragrance for spooks. Not a jump scare, overt, aggressive or notably dark ghost...no... This is restored/refurnished Victorian homes uptown spooky. This is early 20th century lace. Satiny sheer curtains. Doilies, claw-foot bathtubs...a woman sequestered upstairs with a faint countenance to deteriorate and wither in melancholy to her early death at 33 years old...haunted. (*Ahem*, it was laudanum the whole time but her family did nothing to help.) She's never left her room at the top of the stairs. Some say a dim lavender colored light can be seen through the window before dawn in early April mornings. It's beautiful, frail, waifish, vintage (not truly, just in essence) and depressing in a very specifically poised way. It smells like spring, but it lacks the liveliness and vigor necessary to even get out there and enjoy spring (indeed, this is silenced in anything aside from indoor or balmy air). I smell the violet and licorice/anise (something in between the two), and a watery, echo of lily-of-the-valley. It's quite blended, very soft, very, VERY classically feminine I truly don't get much in terms of resins...whatsoever. The light laundry musk might be modern if it wasn't underpinning so much antiquity. But it smooths this out nicely. I really enjoy this and lament it's discontinuation. Maybe you won't get the same story from this perfume at all, and that's totally fine, but to me I have some pretty vivid associations.

I just came from the oral surgeon - and on my tense nerves, one could hold a violin concert. It was just a harmless preliminary discussion. Nevertheless, I stopped by the nearby luxury perfumery to calm myself. Visually, the water-blue box of Blv II already appealed to me. And the old-fashioned lovely violet in the opening won me over immediately. Boring? No - calming. Exactly the nerve balm I was looking for. The licorice note is finely dosed and comforting, and the frosted mandarin is exceptionally refreshing. Like a cool compress on my hot forehead. The lily of the valley is also soothingly cozy. The Texas cedar adds warm spice, and the Spanish rockrose provides that touch of exclusivity. It is precisely this calmness and the mild "easy going" of the fragrance that I like. BlV II is a perfect wave smoother in exciting times - with a decent longevity.

It must be something like a sense of adventure when I order a fragrance on a whim. I've come to know several Bulgari scents and have used some for a longer time (e.g. omnia amethyste). BLV 2 was available at a very low price just before Christmas at perfumetrader, and so I went for it, just like that.

Since I am currently in Switzerland, but my perfume addiction is not diminished abroad, I snagged Otto's 50 ml for 50 francs. Blind purchase due to the lack of a tester. I can't really pick out any of the notes listed here; it smells fresh and a bit spicy, and I think it resembles an expensive scent for a lady.

the scent is fresh.. and also pleasant.. but as my predecessors have already mentioned, there isn't much to say about it.. slightly floral, minimal sweetness can be detected.. the longevity is also quite limited.. fresh and light.. but yes.. just average.. not a must-have.. doesn't stick in your mind.. not something you need, and has no recognizability

Well, this scent is really nice and fresh, nothing extraordinary, that's true, but you don't look a gift horse in the mouth ;)... actually, you could use it daily... unfortunately, it lasts for me only a maximum of 1 - 2 hours.... that's quite disappointing - especially at this price...
It's a very fresh scent, but for my nose, it's nothing extraordinary. It's a nice fresh fragrance, but somehow it totally gets lost.

With the first spray of this fragrance, I had a déjà vu experience, it's... you know it from somewhere...!? But of course, is it Narciso or not? In fact, the scent is very similar in the opening and also in the further development, but there are a few small differences. At first, I was very surprised that the only overlap in the fragrance pyramid is supposed to be musk, which astonishes me given this similarity. Patchouli Tentation opens rather cool, but soon the white peach flashes subtly, taking away some of its initial severity. Powdery and enveloping, the fragrance reveals its wonderful heart of iris on fluffy musk, and that is the part I like best about this scent. I feel gently enveloped, delicately powdered and creamed, yet it is not an entirely sweet fragrance; patchouli sneaks up from the shadows on soft paws like a shy cat and grounds the scent. But.......... the theme has partly missed the mark, as anyone expecting a darker patchouli scent based on the name will experience a moderate disappointment. In my opinion, the theme is more about iris and musk; I even suspect some cedarwood in the background, even though it is not listed in the fragrance pyramid. Despite all the kinship to Uncle Narciso, this fragrance becomes softer and less strict over time, always retaining its fine powderiness and wearing gently like a delicate silk scarf, yet with very good longevity. Conclusion: I really like this fragrance despite the misleading name, which somehow doesn't quite fit this beautiful scent and only delivers the themed patchouli in very fine doses. The white bottle fits very well, as it is a bright scent, clean and creamy with subtly fruity nuances, but certainly not a dark patchouli representative, which I forgive Bvlgari, as that is not my preferred fragrance theme anyway.

For some time now, I have enjoyed reading the fragrance descriptions in this lovely community, and now I feel like writing something myself again. My first test candidate is the Patchouli Tentation from the Splendida series. It starts off very cool, distant, subtly floral, a patchouli in a winter coat. Peach is hardly noticeable. Then the scent becomes very clean, it smells like freshly showered skin. The iris is probably to blame for that. Soon it disappears again, and the white musk makes its appearance. This becomes increasingly delicate, subtle, and finely powdery. A fine, discreet, yet still special fragrance for every season, except summer. That would need to be tested first to see how it performs in strong heat. Oh yes, in my experience, it is particularly important with this fragrance series to let them breathe; they often develop surprisingly.

...a sense of nostalgia winds through my veins, melancholy pulls a silvery gray ribbon through my hair, and I wish with all my might to slow down the river of time, if only for a moment. I want to hold onto the warm gold of those last days, the deep yet radiant blue of the sky, the almost imperceptibly fading splendor in my garden, the silky touch that caresses my still slightly tanned skin and soon, oh so soon, loses its softness, becoming cool and damp, strict and sometimes even harsh. He always comes too early, the man with the reddish-brown hair and deep gray eyes, who can be so aloof yet also so friendly, so heartfelt, so warm... Every year in September, my gaze falls on the amber-golden, gently warm-promising bottle of "Aroma Sun." A soft glow emanates from it, not fiery, not warning of burns - the colors of late summer, the dark gold of the sun when it is already low over the rooftops, the orange and yellow of the first leaves on the paths seem to be captured in this flacon, which appears simple and unpretentious yet somehow comforting. At no other time of the year am I drawn to it so much; no other time seems to suit it better than September, when the time for light, fresh summer waters has passed, and I still cannot bear, do not want to bear, the powerful, dense, heavy, fur-lined, and full-bodied powerhouses, not yet ready to submit to the inevitable, the unavoidable. When the time is right for those scents that Jil Sander paved the way for with her equally passionately loved and scorned "Sun." "Aroma Sun" is not a fragrance for the really hot days when one can barely move from fatigue, when every movement provokes endless sweating, and only "Eau d'Eau" seems truly bearable. Days when fragrances can trigger nausea and headaches, even those we love hotly and dearly on other days, regardless of whether they are aromas wafting from a garden brooding under a heat dome, the scent of simmering dishes from the kitchen, or olfactory phantoms in bottles. On days like these, wearing a fragrance like "Aroma Sun" would be an unbearable punishment for me - this scent seems predestined for more temperate climates, when the skin no longer needs sunscreen and yet one still wants to smell a little like it, like the sunbeams that warm the skin and elicit that very special scent that no perfume, no cream can ever truly capture and portray. When one sits outside Lorenzo's café after hours in the office, sunglasses on the nose and next to them the overly large ice cream sundae with coconut and vanilla ice cream under the huge dollop of whipped cream, for which one skips dinner, watching the wilted leaves that a gentle wind swirls across the square. When we pull cardigans over our T-shirts and curl up in cozy socks on the sofa in the evening. When we dream of sandals and polish our boots to a shine to combine them with 40 den tights and short skirts - then is the time for "Aroma Sun," for its golden, shimmering warmth, light and airy like sponge cake and as delicious as the mirabelle compote on my stove. Every year in September. And always when I wish for a little late summer.

I recently told a colleague that she smells very delicious - the next day she brought Aroma Sun and gifted it to me - almost full! I really like the scent! Sweet, but not overwhelming with a very, very beautiful coconut-peach note that is nicely balanced by woody accents. I find the fragrance to be very rounded; there is nothing that bothers my nose, and that is rare! The longevity is also very good!

This is nice. It smells quite " soapy" on me but that's fine because it reminds me of freshly washed skin. The unfortunate part is that is simply does not last very long at all. Fades really quickly. This is one that you will have to reapply many times throughout the day. The bottle itself is simple and classy looking. Not a "love" but a solid "like" for sure.

I've struggled to like this (gave up on loving it after the 1st 5ml) and after 40ml of a 50ml bottle I'm looking forward to giving up the attempt. the jasmine is a bit of a nothing - not fresh and green and sweet, I don't get any jasmine at all - just a lily of the valley and light synthetic sour lemon smell, soon overtaken by an unpleasant, dull, thick musk. I don't get any light, fresh, sweet or jasmine, no sweet fizzy honey mimosa/wattle, nothing nice at all. Very musky. Even if I use 15 sprays the whole experience is (thankfully) over in 2 hours. But, that's Bvulgari.

Bvlgari actually makes some pretty decent jasmine based fragrances. I'm not referring to Jasmin Noir which I found a disappointment, I'm throwing into the arena the relatively new Mon Jasmin Noir and this fragrance, Voile de Jasmin. I like my jasmine scents light and airy rather than heavy, so Voile de Jasmin's subtlety appeals to me. Along with its freshness, this jasmine is clean, crisp and green. Especially in the top notes, bergamot compliments the fresh jasmine with a zesty and citrusy finish. The heart sees this floral become quite musky, however bright and sweet mimosa keeps this fragrance light and flowery rather than bland. The sillage may indeed be very intimate and soft, yet the longevity, at least on my skin, is not what I'd call disappointing. Voile de Jasmin is very much a Spring and Summer fragrance. Its slightly watery quality makes it perfect for hot weather and those days when you want to wear something light and inoffensive. It's like a whisper of a fragrance, and very beautiful in that regard. It may not be the most exciting fragrance that you've come across, and you may enjoy Bvlgari's stronger scents in preference to Voile de Jasmin. I'm a little surprised by how much I like this perfume, and I've come to the conclusion that I'm very much taken by its simplicity and refreshing jasmine accord. However I must admit that Mon Jasmin Noir has eclipsed this fragrance in terms of what I personally prefer.

In my childhood, I spent a large part of my summer holidays in Wrocław with my grandparents. They have a wonderful allotment garden. To this day, my grandparents grow all sorts of vegetables and fruits themselves, and there is always a lot to do. I fondly remember the time in the garden, especially the smell. It always smelled of grass, sun-ripened tomatoes, cherries, and strawberries. It smelled of earth and all the flowers my grandma had planted. The makeshift little house, which threatened to collapse with every gust of wind, surprisingly withstood even the harshest of storms. On the side of the house, jasmine climbed up the wall. I loved the smell. Adorned with cherry earrings and jasmine flowers in my hair, I climbed the apple tree one afternoon. It was very nice weather that day. I made myself comfortable on a wide branch. It had such a great shape that you could even lie down on it. I fell asleep. I woke up to the booming thunder directly above my head. The sky darkened, and it quickly cooled down. A quick glance into the garden revealed that everyone else had already sought shelter. But I was still perched in the tree… Well. I got a bit wet, but not too much, as the apple tree provided enough protection - and it wasn't much worse than the ruin of a little house… It rained and rained. The air became increasingly pleasant. A crystalline freshness hung in the air. Wonderful! It smelled of all the flowers that were thirstily soaking up the rain. And then - poof - the rain stopped. The sun greeted me so kindly, as if it had never been gone. It shone right in my face. I climbed down from the tree and walked towards the hut. But then I paused, turned around, and closed my eyes. I took a deep breath. Right behind me was the climbing jasmine. It smelled so wonderful! Jasmine has a very intense scent, especially when it becomes "ripe." At that moment, it simply smelled fresh and light. This is exactly how Voile de Jasmin smells! An incredibly wonderful, fresh jasmine scent. So delightfully light, like no other. If jasmine perfume is usually too musty and heavy for you, you might give this fragrance a chance. Rose and lily of the valley are hardly noticeable, but they are there. For me, the bergamot does a great job here, providing that wonderful freshness. The scent is absolutely unique. The only downside is, as with its other siblings, the longevity. However, it performs better compared to Bvlgari pour Femme and Rose Essentielle. Just at the moment when I opened my eyes again, the sky filled with a beautiful rainbow. I will never forget that moment.

Yes, men will think, I know this... it often is the case, but ultimately one is to blame for it oneself. Since I got to know Voile de Jasmin, I can no longer let go of this scent. In the top note, one is greeted briefly and freshly-florally, with the subtlest bergamot note I have ever encountered in a top note. Then of course jasmine, beautifully caressing the skin, but so delicate and powdery that a jasmine lover like me can only be enraptured. Lily of the valley and rose are just small starlets in this jasmine performance. Sparingly used bright clear musk (not the animalistic heavy direction) in the base combines with the radiant jasmine and warm skin in the most sensual way, creating a feeling of well-being for me. One can certainly attribute clean eroticism to Voile de Jasmin. No pee direction, which many fragrance lovers have struggled with when it comes to jasmine notes. By the way, musk can also be blamed if the dosage has been excessive. This scent is expensive for me because I apply it extremely generously, like a body splash. I can watch the liquid level in the simple transparent bottle rapidly drop after each fragrance shower, and I have already gone through several bottles. An overdose is, by the way, impossible with this bright, elegant little scent. Voile de Jasmin will therefore remain my expensive fragrance love!

I was quite curious about the jasmine scents from Bvlgari, as I have already fallen for the waters from this company twice. Since I like the scent of jasmine, I decided to give it another try and hoped to finally have a successful experience with Bvlgari. As you can probably guess, it didn't work out for us this time either.

With jasmine scents, I am extremely cautious. There is one from Crabtree & Evelyn that is far too overpowering and has a strong "aftertaste." Yet jasmine is one of the most beautiful and delicate floral scents. Voile de Jasmin does justice to the flower, if only it would last as long as the bloom itself.

Voile de Jasmin was tested by me together with Jasmin Noir by Bulgari. The surprising result: I like Voile de Jasmin better (with Jasmin Noir, I find the jasmine too intrusive, it "jabs" somehow), even though I thought the heavier variant would be more to my liking. With Voile de Jasmin, I associate: delicate, light, elegant, pure.

I tested it today in our little perfumery after Blanche recommended it to me in the forum. I was told that this scent is very light and very delicate. It is the absolute counterpart to Jasmin Noir, which is a winter fragrance. The first impression of the fragrance is sweet-fresh, gentle, and fragile. (in the sense of fine).

I have had this fragrance for a while now, and it's finally time for me to share my thoughts. Voile de Jasmin is a lovely scent, but not a standout for me. It starts off zesty, fresh, and at the same time, sweet. Jasmine dominates the heart note, yet remains as delicate as one rarely experiences with this flower in fragrances.

I have tried now, several times, to wear the edt instead of the edp. it does not work for me. The edt is somehow shrill and thin but not in an edt way. I suppose it is due to the concentration. There is nothing left of the dark and sweet expression you get in the edt. This is not for me. The edt is divine, btw. 205/365

A perfume worth of Jacques Cavallier-Belletrud's name. It is a sweet, but not gourmandy vanilla perfume with a burnt sugar facet. There's something "umami" like about this scent, in the way creme brulee or peanut butter fudge or very creamy and fatty vanilla ice-cream smells and tastes. I feel like I want to bite into this perfume, but it is not gourmand in the literal sense. I think it is gorgeous, especially for autumn and winter.

This perfume is my favorite from the Allegra line. It has a very fruity stop, but not fresh fruity, rather carnal, creamy fruity. Next we get a Gardenia whit notes of vanilla. Súper súper creamy. The drying in my Opion, although i don’t declare it, I notice a creamy, half-lactonic sandalwood that, together whit Amber. Makes This perfume an addictive elixir for me. Vero good duration by the way.

I did not test it with another essence (small candies), as he recommends. But I don't need to, as I was already satisfied with this vanilla. I find that this scent is much more sophisticated than it appears, despite the few notes listed. I'm not sure if he has revealed the entire fragrance pyramid. It is a very seductive floral-vanilla-amber scent, incredibly creamy, without being too heavy or flat. The blend with gardenia makes it perfect; it has a feather-light creaminess. It is the perfect combination that keeps the vanilla from being too sweet and cloying. With the amber at the end, it is so soothing and seductive, absolutely amazing!!! I catch a hint of rum, but I think it's the blend of notes that gives me this impression. For me, simply a great love.

I bought this perfume blindly this year, in February. I did not show suspicion despite the price when I had already been very disappointed with onekh from the same range. I had heard a lot of good things about this collection, and I also discovered 2 nuggets in it that are in my top 3 discoveries this year out of more than 100 tests. unfortunately this one will not have convinced me completely, we would say an old-fashioned cologne with greenery. it brings a certain elegance and refinement. nevertheless, I find that it is aimed too much at a more mature category among men, from the age of 45. I can easily imagine a politician or a member of the Senate wearing this type of opulent fragrance in the summer. the advantage of this perfume remains a singular rare smell, almost impossible to find. a little in the same style as erolfa de creed but better. not sticking to my state of mind I sold it after 1 week. not the best of the collection the gem but the worst either.

…you should also be able to lift your leg. Regarding the pricing of the Le Gemme series, I admit I had a certain fragrance image as well as prejudices in mind: - Bottles with gemstones on the cap - High-quality ingredients - More is more - often rather opulent scents for specific occasions - Poor availability - Sometimes more (money) appearance than reality Point 1 is already fulfilled with the Le Gemme series. Quote: “Malakeos - The radiant gemstone is a symbol of splendor and abundance…”. However, malachite neither passively nor actively glows and, strictly speaking, is not considered a gemstone. Schnitzel Wiener Art is also not prepared with veal, which explains the price difference. Thus, point 5 is also fulfilled regarding the bottle. Last but not least, one must of course search for sources and may end up in a Bulgari boutique. Of course, with a prior appointment (point 4). After having laid down a significant sack of gold coins for a sample, the account decreases and the anticipation rises. The spray finger moves nervously and reverently towards the spray nozzle. No, stop! First, sniff at the said spray unit (since it’s a used original sample). The first impression is characterized by a short “uhh,” quickly followed by a drawn-out “oooh” and simultaneous distrust in the stomach area. So completely different than expected. I spray the fragrance on my wrist, still full of anticipation, wait, waaaait, and bring my nose close. What reaches my nostrils at the same time were the following 2 impressions. 1. What, off? 2. You know that one! I could have sworn there was verbena/moss in the opening. I only know this combo from Irish Tweed, and at first, I thought the scent was off here too. A green-bitter note wafts towards me, which personally irritates me but does not completely deter me. In the case of Green Irish Tweed, scent transitions become recognizable afterward. In the case of Malakeos, I perceive not transitions but musk. Admittedly, the combination is interesting. I find musk beautiful. However, I can only wear a few musk-heavy fragrances for an extended period, as they seem too monotonous to me over time. With Malakeos, the green opening fades a bit but remains consistently in the background until the base. Musk becomes very present after about 30 minutes, but due to various, very prominent scent molecule pillars, it feels prickly and slightly penetrating. This impression also makes it impossible for me to distinguish lavender in the scent progression. And with Malakeos, that was already it for me regarding the scent progression. Even though this malachite proves to be persistent, the projection, fortunately, remains very moderate, and that is a good thing. My initial positive impression had thus quickly turned into its opposite. I also want to draw an honest, personal comparison regarding the scent character. Even though I don’t want to offend anyone here. Otto Kern Signature Men makes no secret of its synthetic nature, comes without a gemstone, and the 50ml costs under €15. In my eyes, both are quite similar in character. However, in the medium term, the packaging material we receive for the 21 Otto Kern bottles will certainly cost us more than a small Malakeos. So, if you have the necessary pocket money saved up and like the scent, please indulge without a guilty conscience and enjoy having something special in your collection! I wholeheartedly wish it for you from the bottom of my Parfumo heart. As for me, I lost money on the sample but gained insight in return.

If the intense green of malachite - which one experiences in nature - is meant to evoke the healing power, well-being, and lush greenery of the endless coniferous forests of the Urals - then, yes, you are in the right place if you like it fresh, lavender-like, green-woody and perhaps are looking for a Fougére that is both modern and timeless at the same time…. I was unexpectedly struck by the sampling (olfactorily) recently! While "Orage" was my (green) discovery of 2018 - since then, I have been actively here for you and would like to thank you emphatically for any help, tips, and simply outstandingly nice contacts - should another fresh green come along in 2019. Mr. Dublee - thank you very much! - recently sent me some samples. “Malakeos!? Add it to your cart, the 'Le Gemmes' have been calling to you for a while and Jacques Cavallier-Belletrud produced 'your' Orage after all.” I can already tell you that the first spray truly doesn’t knock you off your feet; perhaps some Parfumo will wonder what is so outstanding about this scent!? Well, I might not know myself. It is simply exactly what I have been looking for. Malakeos is without lemon-fresh, presents itself quite traditionally as #fougére and places the whole thing on a modern pedestal, reinterpreting it. Perhaps due to my feeling of dry coolness. That might capture it best. Russian Ural forest coolness in sunshine! I haven’t been to the forests of the Urals yet, but I have looked at some pictures. Evocative associations: “Juicy needles, steaming moss, heather swaying in the wind.” Sensually green plant freshness. It could also be the barber shop. Or shaving foam. Shaving foam with lavender - unsweetened-fresh, with a bit of green wood at the back. In my statement, I also wrote quite lyrically “there a river, here my mountain.” Yeah, when I look at the bottle and weigh it in my hand, it brings more than a pound of ground meat on the virtual scale. What a block. Nice: The spray head itself atomizes wonderfully. 3rd place after Vuitton and Dior. And for Lars: that thing is magnetic!! No. Yes! Ohhh! I have found my green in 2019, this time a rather classically structured, very versatile one. "Here is my mountain"!

I got this perfume today and i immediately recognized the scent..it smells very similar to Marilyn a hairmask from Lush..in the opening especially..and in the drydown it gets more powdery but it still smells a lot like Marilyn. I find it very comforting and sweet but not to sweet.I'm glad i discovered this pretty little gem

I met Nora back at the luxury fragrance department store. Dressed up in a black and blue outfit, she stood there on the shelf.. The saleswoman handed me a test strip and I was gone! Noorah knocked me off my feet (in a positive way, of course). I quickly took a sample home and tested it: The opening alone is like a sunrise on Christmas for me... it starts with a very natural earthy iris, slightly spicy and rather cool... Over time, the iris becomes stronger and stronger, slightly green-mossy, but without being intrusive or annoying - NEVER :) The scent development is somewhat limited... not much happens for me :) After about 5 hours of beautiful iris, a slightly sweet vanilla joins in - but the iris is always clearly in the foreground.. The listed "tobacco" comes across for me more like sweet shisha smoke…. For me, Noorah lasts what feels like an eternity (yay) - with a solid 8.5 hours, I find the longevity quite good. The sillage is, in my opinion, moderate.. (unless you completely drench yourself in it ;) My heart opens every time I'm with Noorah :)

The opening is initially very alcoholic (rum?) with a dry-metallic iris, a bit earthy; it lasts at most 10 minutes, then it becomes spicier, you can imagine patchouli and cardamom, also shisha tobacco, and it becomes a bit softer. However, all of this is not too intense. I put on a jacket, rolled up the sleeves after a few minutes, and it was gone, or almost. I had to sniff very carefully. You think, is that it? And then it comes back, initially delicate, but becoming clearer until a wonderful sillage develops. Not abundant, I have to get within 10 cm of my arm to smell it myself, but every now and then a gentle breeze wafts into my nose. And this is truly exquisite. Soft, creamy iris, intertwined with benzoe, spiced with cardamom, the wood is only very subtle. Vanilla makes the scent even creamier, but it is more of a companion and does not take center stage. The tobacco note has actually completely disappeared. The galbanum also contributes to the creaminess. This spicy-creamy, even subtly powdery phase then settles in and lasts and lasts... That was in the afternoon, at around 20 degrees. Now at half past 9 in the evening, I sprayed again to remind myself of the opening, and now the scent smells significantly more intense. It seems to depend on the temperature how strongly it comes out. Ideally, it is much more pronounced in cooler temperatures and rather delicate in warmth. Very interesting and I like it very much in any case.

Bvlgari is known not only for its fragrances but also for colored gemstones, which is why the exclusive line is named "Le Gemme." The line started in 2014 with 6 fragrances that were meant to represent a kind of journey around the world. Each fragrance is supposed to reflect both a country or its way of life, as well as a gemstone. "Noorah takes the turquoise as its model, the gemstone of the nomads, inviting you on a journey along the ancient Silk and Spice Road. A gemstone that reminds one of vast horizons. The name means 'light' and reflects the atmosphere of endless expanses." So it says in the little chic booklet I received back in the perfumery when the fragrances were newly released. The scent itself is described as "Enchanting shisha accords underscore the oriental richness and refinement of Noorah." I like tobacco as a fragrance note, so this scent was one of my clear test favorites. Like all the other fragrances in the Le Gemme line, "Noorah" is also stored in a black amphora designed to protect the fragrance from light. This bottle shape is also meant to emphasize the preciousness of the scent, as everything valuable was stored in amphorae in ancient Rome. The cap is modeled after the respective gemstone, here the turquoise, and its shape is not chosen randomly: it is meant to represent the cabochon cut of this gemstone. It certainly makes a statement. The opaque bottle has the advantage that even when empty, it remains beautifully decorative. Now let's embark on the scent journey: On the skin, Noorah initially starts off fresh, but immediately powdery, which is likely thanks to the iris. I smell the cardamom and something green, which could be from the galbanum. The iris becomes increasingly voluminous and soon receives a visit from the tobacco. However, this is not smoky or dry, but rather reflects the moist, soaked shisha tobacco very well. A slight sweetness is also perceptible here, but it does not make the scent sticky in any way. It seems to come more from the tobacco, like in vanilla tobacco. The iris remains present and continues to give the scent a powdery component. In combination with the moist tobacco, this is not too dry. Not much happens after that. Since the tobacco is not overly sweet or smoky, the scent might also be suitable for those who want to ease into this note. I like the scent well; the shisha illusion is well captured. But personally, I feel like something is missing for me to actually purchase the scent, especially considering the price, which is around €300/100ml, placing it in the higher mid-range of exclusive lines. The longevity is very good; sprayed on in the morning, I can still perceive a hint of it the next day. Unfortunately, the sillage is very low, and the scent quickly becomes close to the skin. I find that a bit disappointing personally; I would have wished for an oriental fragrance in this price range to be a bit more dominant.

the most beautiful and magical perfume I've ever smelt. This is what I'd expect Morticia Addams from The Addams Family to smell like, this is what a Vampire & Vampress smell like. As someone who was born in Halloween and grew up loving the gothic and loving Halloween, this the one, this is it, my favorite rose perfume maybe even perfume ever. To all my Vampires & Vampress il try to describe the smell, Imagine the darkest crimson or darkest indigo purplish rose that fell on boiling lava of golden amber, and the rose burning with smoke. It's so dark, and magical. This isn't melancholic roses, like Portrait of a Lady, which is still beautiful, but for me it's too sad and all i smell is the Ghost of the Lady in the Portrait, but it's mostly the Portrait that you can faintly get a whiff of the Lady in the Portrait. But Garanat is straight up Portrait of a Lady, a healthier one that moved on, and is strong and dark. this is Morticia, this is Gomez. Straight up 10/10, the gem collection is hella slept on too.

Words can not put into perspective how much I love this perfume. This was a blind buy for me and man am I glad I picked this up. I was fortunte enough to not pay retail for this (around 200€) if I remember correctly, it is also in the old 100ml bottles which I prefer to the newer ones. Performance on this is beyond amazing aswell, a truly 10/10 fragrance. If you love rose and incense do yourself a favour and try and smell this.

Imo, this is the best TRUE rose fragrance for men on the market! The olibanum here only accentuates the manlier facets of rose, but make no mistakes, this is through and through rose! If , like me, you ever sampled Lyric Man, or any rose marketed fragrance for men, and thought them to be too "femme" or not rosy enough, well, not here. A woman will have a challenge wearing this, imo. And that's a lot to say of a ROSE dominant fragrance. To me, this is appropriate for all but the dog days of Summer. And is appropriate for dress up occasions and work, but hey, that's me. Overall, this is a REALLY good, 10/10, fragrance for me. I think, due to the price this is seldomly talked about, but if you like rose or want one of the best rose for men in your collection, you need this. Please sound off about this if you own it. Let's hear your take! PS: Garanat > POL... not as complex but a better overall fragrance...

Nanu? No comments yet on this lovely fragrance? Well, it’s about time! ~Bottle~ Typical Tresor. However, this time it’s not square but shaped like a diamond (top view). Under the spray head, there is a clear ring. The fragrance is in a clear rose color, which fits very well with the content - young and soft. ~Occasion~ Somewhat elegant. Depending on the personality, suitable for leisure or even work. It’s also suitable for going out, but it’s not a powerhouse; it’s delicate. ~Scent~ It starts with a hefty dose of powder. Please hit your face thickly with the powder puff! But that’s only for the first 10 minutes; then it softens to a moderate, pleasant powder note. Once the powder punch eases, you can also smell the mild bergamot and peach top note. Not citrusy, rather a very ripe, sweet fruity peach with a hint of fresh bergamot. The top note diminishes somewhat after an hour but remains very softly present in the background, giving the fragrance a youthful, fresh charm. Rose (35%), Freesia (20%), Patchouli (35%), and Sandalwood (10%) harmoniously share the scent as it develops, merging like an orchestra, with the rose occasionally taking the lead, and at times the freesia taking the melodic voice. ~Longevity and Sillage~ As mentioned, it’s not a powerhouse. It’s not skin-close either! With three sprays, it is clearly present but in the background. On my skin, it lasts a pleasant 7 hours, during which it doesn’t gradually lighten, but rather drops off sharply in the last hour. CONCLUSION: The resemblance to the original is definitely undeniable! But where I find the original somewhat old-fashioned and older, this is the younger, softer, and more harmonious version. A beautiful and elegant fragrance. Those who like Tresor will surely enjoy this one too! (Here again, a thousand thanks to Nuitdete1; thanks to the lovely person, the fragrance can finally move in with me :D)

This is like a DEEP orange-y smelling fougere with sandalwood and musk. The vetiver's here to add a green grassy element which complements the orange-y smell. Perfect for spring. I know Bvlgari's being cagey with the note breakdown but I definitely smell vetiver. Smells expensive as does every one from the Le Gemme line that I've smelled. Definitely doesn't smell like anything I've smelled before and for that reason I wouldn't recommend blind buying this. At this price point you want to confirm your purchase. Lol. UPDATE: Albeit I stand by my initials words on this, I grossly under sold the point of how GOOD this is. I typically don't drop the "sexy" word when describing a fragrance, but, man, there are little other words I can use to describe what it is. The orange in here is so real and juicy and the vetiver is lending this earthiness to the fragrance that is out of this world in the dry down. Disclaimer: the opening can leave one with the distinct impression that this may lean feminine and is too loud and unbalanced. I mean the orange is like a bomb in the opening as well as the sandalwood. Initially those two notes do fight it out and are admittedly LOUD. But as it settles...my oh my... This becomes decidedly masculine and you'll find yourself lifting your shirt just to smell it again (and again) to confirm that the wafts you're getting is in fact emanating from your person's. Every one that I've smelled from this line has over exceeded my expectations. A fantastic line of masculine, chic and ritzy fragrances. Too bad they're so exclusionarily expensive... That's not a word but you get the point lol

“Yasep” has truly enchanted me. One of the few fragrances where I find myself quite distinctly at odds with Taurus. No mediocrity - but a gentle fragrance festival! For me, “Yasep” has nearly everything I want in a (signature) perfume. It really deserves more positive attention or even a hype! But for now, I have it all to myself… A very mineral mandarin creamy, caressing and delicious! Young and versatile. Expensive but worth it. A fluffy musk that lingers. Stylish and unobtrusive. It flows easily, can do anything. Fit and invigorating from toe to hair tip. Without ever coming close to the typical summer freshie corner. Perhaps slightly “boring” and straightforward, without real twists or wow effects in the middle. Hence the minimal deduction despite my promising title. But fundamentally, “Yasep” is for me a single wow effect! Perfect transitions. A great whole. Many solid individual components come together in harmony to create something new, something wonderful, a star! Like deodorant from a foreign, friendly planet. The Sicily of Saturn. Lightly salty skin, very sunny and close to the sea. Without ever becoming a true aquatic. The (still) better “Acqua Amara” for me. A harmony orchestra in sparkling nirvana. Pepper keyboard of Zen. The square of the price. The fruitiest vetiver, playful yet masterful. Orange and yet completely different from other citrus fruits. Zesty magic dust! Bottle: Bvlgari’s flagship line - what more can one say… Sillage: softly strong Longevity: 6-9 hours, doesn’t handle heat super well over time Conclusion: a perfume cocktail that reminds me equally of deodorant as it does of cloud 7, of mandarin minerals like jam, of an empty wallet and a satisfied scent soul. For me, a dream!

Attention: after I finally wanted to know what the name Yasep is all about, I must once again play the explanatory bear here. After all, I don't want to withhold the results from you after my research. And of course, you also learn something about the scent. Of course, I first googled it, but under Yasep, you find almost only entries related to Bulgari or the fragrance. On the Bvlgari website, there is at least a hint under the name pointing to Jasper, a variety of the mineral quartz. In Persian, the stone is called Yashp, in Hebrew Jaseph. It comes in different color tones, which are predominantly used as gemstones. I think the cap of the extremely tasteful bottle is a reference to the red variant of quartz, which is said to emanate an irresistible life energy. Olfactorily, this is supposed to be expressed with glowing sandalwood and woody musk. A fine pinch of Sichuan pepper is also included. More is not listed in the fragrance pyramid on the official website. The strange thing is: Fragrantica additionally mentions Sicilian mandarin, cedar, vetiver, and Amyris Balsamifera, the latter being the term for sandalwood from Venezuela or the West Indies. So much for the theory, but in practice, one actually perceives a slightly sweet mandarin, which one might associate with diluted fruit juices. Relatively restrained, but definitely present. In between, there are one or two nuances of sandalwood, and later in the dry down, it becomes a bit woody. Official musk and unofficial vetiver do not come through for me. Nevertheless, it seems okay so far and goes well with the mentioned theme of life energy, but given the - and I can't avoid addressing this - rather high acquisition costs of 300 € for 100 ml of EdP, Yasep does not seem as exclusive to me as Bvlgari wants to suggest with its Le Gemme Collection in the stylish bottles. While the longevity and sillage may be more than decent, the scent, in my opinion, does not exceed good average. Unfortunately!

You're in the right place if you love oriental fragrances! I first smelled this in the Bvlgari Boutique, but unfortunately it was sold out, and also in the store next door it was sold out, so I could only manage to get a sample. The scent doesn't hit you in the face directly, but feels light and elegant. When I smelled it, it transported me to another world and strongly reminded me of the desert nights in Dubai. Almost mystical, I began to dream about all the scents I perceive. For me, it's a very harmonious fragrance that, fortunately, is still quite unknown at the moment. My partner is usually absolutely against oriental fragrances but found this one very beautiful! If you know this problem :)

Tropiques was once again an absolute blind buy. Since I already have several perfumes from Lancôme, I thought I couldn't go wrong. The name and the bottle immediately reminded me of a Caribbean vacation, of a sultry beauty with long black hair, with a sweet-smelling flower in her hair, or of the delicious tropical, exotic fruits that I can't get enough of on vacation. And that's exactly how this fragrance is. It brings a touch of the Caribbean back to me. It starts fruity sweet, and fortunately, neither is overwhelming, but in the right balance, and it finishes with a slightly creamy note. The fragrance doesn't undergo significant changes, but I find that perfectly fine. The sillage is well-defined but pleasant. I like it when I can still perceive the scent for a long time. The longevity is noticeably longer in high temperatures, lasting about 6 hours for me, while in cooler temperatures, I don't smell much after 3 hours. So it fits the name as well. A fruity, sweet summer perfume, perfect for the evening hours. I have no regrets about the purchase and enjoy wearing it from time to time.

Ce Soir ou Jamais translates as Tonight or Never. A beautiful name for a stunning rose fragrance. I will never use this as a casual perfume, because this is not a casual perfume to me. For me it is like experiencing something beautiful and extraordinary. I love many other Goutal’s creations but Ce Soir ou Jamais has a special place in my heart. I have read that it took years for Annick Goutal to perfect the formula for Ce Soir ou Jamais and I think she really put her heart into this perfume. It is a monumental, complex and unique rose scent with a beautiful and passionate soul. It says on Annick Goutal site that the composition for this scent has over 140 ingredients. And I agree that it is not a rose soliflore, though it is rose-dominated scent. The opening is like rose petals dipped in sweet fruits. I think that I smell pear and lemony notes in the opening. The scent quickly transforms into a bold and strong rose and hibiscus bouquet with fruity and spicy accents. The opening and heart notes are strong and complex. I would even call them sharp at times. This is not a tender rose water made for those who want a delicate rose scent. It is more like a rose elixir. The scent stays linear until the dry down when it transforms into slightly sweet, almost honeyed and cozy rose. The lasting power is great. Ce Soir ou Jamais is a magnificent rose scent. Tonight or Never… The world stops, nothing else matters accept for this one moment, one chance to experience something extraordinary – the rose in full bloom. Annick Goutal managed to capture this feeling and the scent in Ce Soir ou Jamais.

In my neck of the woods niche fragrances are well nigh impossible to come by, apart from a few more mainstream lines kept here and there. I was lucky enough to discover Etat Libre d'Orange and a few others via these avenues, but say "Goutal" down here and people reply with "huh?". I've had a few samples in swaps but when this one presented itself for sale by a fellow perfume junkie I jumped at the chance! Ce Soir Ou Jamais, in a word, is "ravishing"!! This is Rose at her very sexiest, all slinky in marabou slippers and form fitting silk satin ... not quite the femme fatale but no blushing bride either! She offers an ultimatum ... it's "now or never" and in doing so becomes completely beguiling. The opening burst of this fragrance is heavy with a fruitiness that recalls over-ripe pears, but this effect is short lived as the central idea of Roses in full, sweet, velvety bloom begins to assert itself. It's as if one is approaching an immense arrangement of them from a distance, their scent becoming all the more enveloping with each step closer. The Goutal website maintains that Ce Soir Ou Jamais is made up of more than 160 ingredients. 150 of those must be various forms of Roses from different places ... the intricate layers of Rose from delicate and charming to impossibly sweet and honeyed are simply astounding. I'm not sure what Hibiscus smells like, never having had the pleasure ... but there is a somewhat tropical aspect to Ce Soir Ou Jamais, as well as a slight smokiness, no doubt as a result of the Amber. Traditionally composed of Benzoin, Labdanum and Vanilla, this Amber is muted and respectful of it's minor role as a supporting cast member in this Rose Extravaganza. I don't know why I bother rating sillage and longevity ... my perfume munching skin makes a mockery of most fragrances. On me, the lifespan of Ce Soir Ou Jamais is sufficient at a little over 4 hours but a full wearing is in the offing to establish the impression of others. This is not a fragrance that the average male would be comfortable wearing ... but if one is a Rose addict (I have a lifetime membership in this club!) then not at least sampling Goutal's Ce Soir Ou Jamais would be remiss. This beautifully crafted fragrance should carry the label "for Rose lovers only".

I had read somewhere that Ce Soir ou Jamais was one of the late Annick Goutal's favourite fragrances. I find all of her scents to be lovely creations, however if I were to choose my favourite rose from her collection, I'd also say Ce Soir ou Jamais. Rose may be this fragrance's most dominant note, however the additional frangipani, jasmine and musk add extra colour and complexity to something that could be straight-up, pretty, pink roses. Had I smelt this particular scent a few years ago, I may not have appreciated it. It was on my twentieth birthday that the allure of a owning a rose scent really grabbed my attention. For those that associate rose to that of an old lady, which I once did, needs to open their eyes and experience something as beautiful as Ce Soir ou Jamais. The delicious rose note in this fragrance is almost dewy, being fresh and exotic in a very appealing sense. It is a tad 'antique inspired', however it does not seem so rich and ancient like it's big sister, Rose Absolue. Ce Soir ou Jamais has a rather youthful impression, which I feel is brought about by subtle fruity notes, like pear, that tends to linger softly in the heart. This fragrance is a little bit like Quel Amour!, yet perhaps not as Spring-like and fresh. I read a beautiful article on the Perfume-Smellin' Things blog, that portrayed Ce Soir ou Jamais as being in 3-D. I have to agree that this fragrance has the ability to bring a rose note to life. I have only experienced this fragrance in the EDT concentration, and from that I would say that the lasting power is quite good and the sillage light yet detectable. As in regards to the EDP version, I have noticed that some feel it too wine-like, quite intense and boozy. For a delicate rose like I have described I'd probably lean more towards buying the EDT.

A delightful, flowery fragrance, featuring the very substantial oil of the Turkish rose with "honeyed" overtones. A rich interpretation of the velvety floral notes, a "nocturnal garden" with a lingering heart of roses and a beautiful drydown, slightly reminiscent of "Joy", but not as grand. If you love this type of fragrance, "Ce soir ou jamais" might be an alternative to "Joy". A beautifully romantic perfume.

If Vita Sackville West had harnessed her knowledge of flowers and writing to a penchant for perfume what reviews would have graced The Observer? Imagine Sissinghurst Castle as an English Givaudan. Vita would have loved Ce Soir ou Jamais. It defined her life. “Tonight or Never” she told her lover, Violet Trefusis. They left their respective husbands and fled to Amiens, where their husbands, having flown in on a two seater plane, intercepted their plans. It was 1920. Absolute scandal ensued. Her garden was overblown with roses; she reported herself ‘Drunk with Roses.’ What rose perfume would Vita have loved? Her son wrote a book and called it ‘A Portrait of a Marriage’ Would Vita have loved Portrait of a Lady? Yes, I think she would have. She loved Souvenir du Docteur Jamain, deepest darkest blooms of Damask, prone to blight. Paris?...Without doubt. Perfumer’s Workshop Tea Rose? Yes, she would have worn that in the garden and kept Ce Soir for the twilight. Would Sa Majeste from Serge Lutens have found its way into her tower. Yes, she would have worn it during the winter at pruning and burning time. Ce Soir ou Jamais is nothing but a thick jammy rose but it’s not what you’ve got, it’s how you use it.

that you take me to; Who needs paradise? I'd rather have you! From what I read here, I hardly dared to hope that I would ever be able to own this treasure. I'm constantly looking for the scents that I would like to have, so I search the internet "up and down" and found what I was looking for yesterday.

Before writing anything else, the title of my review is very important: there’s emotional connection with the first perfume that led you into niche perfumes. Rose always has been one of my favorite notes, it’s timeless, it’s classy, it can be so many things.

She had been looking forward to this experience so much: picking roses! In the midst of the fragrant fields, surrounded by the sensual scent, harvesting the almost still-sleeping blossoms: she absolutely wanted to experience this!

My darling, my true all-time favorite. It's quirky, I know, but for my nose, Ce Soir is a real magnet. After spraying, I am almost overwhelmed by a rich, juicy-sweet apple cider note. Clearly, overripe, slightly fermented apples, as delicious as thick apple cider.

In the year 1770, a 21-year-old lad named Johann Wolfgang von G. (we'll keep his name confidential for reasons of discretion) was in Strasbourg for study purposes to earn his law doctorate. Together with his Alsatian friend Friedrich Leopold W., he undertook extensive excursions into the surrounding area.

The Goldea fragrances appeal to me greatly because they are extravagantly relaxed. So I gladly let my husband spray Absolute on me, as I can rely on his nose. Soft and creamy, the plum greets me - gently sweetened by soft vanilla. A caress - a flatterer, cushioned by mossy notes. Jasmine brightens Absolute and provides a certain clarity and lightness. A walk in a forest clearing leading to white jasmine bushes. A calm, gathering scent that appears full and round, yet remains subtle. It maintains privacy - but is easily noticeable. My husband made a good choice - and Absolute will adorn my birthday table.

When I brought the aroma to my nose, I naturally smelled rose, flavored with musk and vanilla. When I applied the aroma to my hand, I immediately felt the alcoholic spice, only after a few seconds I was finally able to discern the beginning: white pepper and a little mandarine. A little later, the aroma of tarragon (drink) began to be felt. I really liked this start. In the middle, the Bulgarian rose opens and, as I understand it, the wild rose, although the Bulgarian rose stands a little further away, and the aroma acquires freshness in greater quantities. The aroma is quite sweet, but as for me, the sweetness was not overdone, the aroma is also a little fresh and green, but somewhere there is still the aroma of tarragon as a drink. At the end, vanilla, musk and ambarette begin to smell. The aroma turns into a very soft, floral and enveloping, plus there are still spices.

Year 2000 I remember was brightened with “ 2000 et Une Rôse”. Creators used three types of roses in order to celebrate very special moment in history. I ordered mine directly from Lancome’s online store. It felt like millions of roses were collected in cute, small bottle. Oh, well, not a million, but 1001 to be exact. If you ever need perfume with unique rose scent, look no further and try to find this discontinued gem. New formula is not the same. “Mille et Une Roses” have about the same notes, but they all came in completely new scent. This scent always will be kept in my heart.

The perfume is exceptionally long-lasting! A play between fresh rose and musk. Those who miss the scent will find a similar direction with Chloe & Co. Nevertheless, it is the pioneer! Beautiful color of the liquid and an inconvenient bottle that can only lie down. Still, I think the bottle is something special in the shape of morning dew; it reflects the scent like a water droplet on a rose.

I have a sensitive nose and get headaches, but this doesn't do it at all. This scent is really weak. It smells like cologne. It's full of natural fragrances and is an eau de toilette, so I think it will wear off quickly. I think even 100ml will wear off in no time. But the scent is amazing. The indole component of neroli has been removed to make it a fruity neroli. There is almost no base note, it seems to be a single note. It also has an atmosphere like Santa Maria Novella. It's very bright, honest, and not gimmicky. It's a simple and elegant scent of natural neroli. But the scent is very weak. It's closer to orange blossom than neroli. The green and herbal scent is not that strong. But it doesn't have the "candy" or "marshmallow" scent of common synthetic orange blossom. I feel like it means a dreamy moment. It's definitely a daydream-like, hazy scent. It's euphoric, and the cosmetic scent that I don't like doesn't linger for even a moment. Considering the price, it's a very luxurious scent, but I think they didn't want to lose this transparency. If you like LUSH's Orange Blossom, you'll definitely like this, but you might find it a little too subdued. I didn't know that Goutal was under Amore Pacific! This is the first time I've heard of it! I won't be buying a bottle as it's too extravagant for me, but I will probably use up the sample.

Sweet candyish orange blossoms, somehow both bright and airy but also quite sugary and seductive, verging on cloying. Unlike any other orange blossom note I've experienced so far. Before reading the notes, I thought it was honeysuckle, or jammy rose plus powdery iris. I don't detect any of the other notes listed here. Le Temps des Rêves is very lovely, but simple, linear, and rather short-lived.

My French teacher stands in front of me wearing a "Call me Friedrich" T-shirt and shouts with spit bubbles: "Come on, finally start the conjugation of rêver!" For some reason, I am silent. It could be because he is carrying a chicken under his arm, or because Steve Martin is whispering dirty jokes in Bavarian into my ear. "Je rêve,..." I begin hesitantly and look desperately at Shaking Stevens, who is swaying his hips in the corner of the classroom. "tu rêves, elle..." "This is taking way too long, it's already the 6th period for me!" the teacher snaps at me, while a toga-clad Roman strides down the aisles. And through the window, 'Cool and the Gang' blares with "Fresh". Shaking from sensory overload, I glance at the door through which a bold Frenchman strides in, takes me in his arms, and while walking proclaims, "What is always in the mind is almost never on the lips."
