I will never forget the expression on the saleswoman's face when she sprayed Eau du Fier onto a card and held it under her own nose after some back and forth.

I stumbled upon Eau du Fier quite by chance, namely in the Goutal Flagship Store in London. The display was so striking that this name caught my attention, and I thought it was strange, as I already know the "male" Goutal fragrances, and I asked the (gay) French store manager, somewhat puzzled.

For me, this was immediately a harmonious and pleasing scent. Peachy-fruity Osmanthus meets a leathery-bitter blend of smoky Lapsang Souchong and turpentine-like birch tar. To my nose, this works perfectly together. Osmanthus alone would be too sweet. The smoky-lacquered notes would be too harsh.
... I admire you who can describe this eccentric fragrance event so beautifully and in detail!

This smells about 90% like Pink Flamingos. It has that same hairspray, aerosol lift and texture with a Cherry and Rose heart. It isn't as sharp or fruity as PF. But definitely smells synthetic and candy like though, rather then Natural and organic. The Tuberose is Fuzzy and the Cherry gives it a nice sweetness. There is also a slight fruit nuance from the Pomegranate. It doesn't really mellow or morph much as It dries to a kind of Cherryade smell. Much prefer Heliotrope and Almond to create an Organic Cherry accord rather than synthetic cherry note tbh. It's not horrible just a bit cheap and tinny smelling.

I did expect a lot of this, since one of the two top notes is ginger, a huge favourite of mine. Unfortunately, the ginger in this is not really working like I want it to. My nose experiences it as a bit 'oily' - hard to explain. I would expect the mandarin and the ginger to perform fresh and citrusy - but it becomes a bit cloying instead. After half an hour it moves on to the flowers and surprisingly becomes better. The base is hardly there at all. As with the Cyclades, this is underperforming. It is definitely not one of Lancôme's best scents. Usually, they make really good products. I recommend you spend your money on something else. 238/365

This is extremely pungent. The Jasmine is lovely and naturally sweet in the opening blast. Then it settles into the smoky bed of Incense and earthy sweet Oud. It has nuances of Infusion d'Homme with that hazy Incense but the Oud is the focal point here. This is the first palatable Oud fragrance I've smelt. It's challenging but so well blended. It's smells very masculine to me. Without the Jasmine it would be too skanky but the magic creamy white floral sweetens and cleans it all up.

Yesss… hardly do I mention in my comment about the Bvlgari fragrance Eau Parfumée au Thé Rouge that a dear perfumer, whom I also know personally, wants to push all Bvlgari fragrances on me, when I soon find myself dealing with said perfumer, who has read the comment… *sigh* Of course, when we meet again, we also look at a few fragrances and, seemingly quite casually, we stroll back to the Bvlgari fragrances (what a coincidence…) and stop at the Le Gemme fragrances, to which two new ones have been added. And as soon as we are there, she hisses: “So, so, you’re telling people on Parfumo that I want to force these fragrances on you!” “Um… yes, but I didn’t formulate it like THAT!!!,” I stammer slightly nervously, with a few beads of sweat on my forehead, which could also be the result of the hot weather. “Good…,” she says. “I’ll give you one more chance to pull your head out of the noose.” The beads of sweat decrease, I breathe a sigh of relief and wait to see what this opportunity is. The perfumer looks at me with a smile and finally says in an angelic voice: “Soooo, either you test this fragrance here… or I’ll hit you! It’s that simple!” Before I can even make a decision, she is already armed with the chalice-like bottle. Her eyes pierce through me and I can read her thoughts: “If you choose the hitting, you’ll regret it for the rest of your life!” she seems to think, and it becomes clear to me that I will get the bottle to the head if I choose to be hit… … It is also clear that I would rather let myself be sprayed with the Bvlgari fragrance… Again… The fragrance: The fragrance cannot be classified into the classic top, heart, and base notes, as it does not develop and therefore smells the same from beginning to end. At first, you smell a smoky oud cloud, which is not as piercingly strong as one might assume due to the oud. This may be due to the frankincense, which makes the fragrance feel lighter and airier, softening the oud. The sweet jasmine also contributes to a more pleasant scent. However, the fragrance does not offer any distinctive features and smells like many other smoky, airy fragrances. Oh, and also, the fragrance is slightly powdery. The sillage and longevity: The fragrance has a fairly good projection and is particularly strong when sprayed on clothing. Nevertheless, it is somewhat gentler compared to some other oud fragrances. The longevity is quite good, and the fragrance lasts at least eight hours, as is often the case with somewhat stronger scents. The bottle: Like all Le Gemme bottles, this one also looks like a chalice or a modern interpretation of an ancient amphora. The main color is black or anthracite, with gilded details. The upper part and the top side of the cap are blue like the gemstone lapis lazuli, which this fragrance also represents. In addition to most other Le Gemme fragrances, the cap, or the top of it, is also adorned with gilded patterns that almost appear delicate. Overall, a very noble and beautiful bottle. Yes, the fragrance doesn’t smell bad, but I find it somewhat rather ordinary, at least for a Le Gemme fragrance. I also don’t associate it with a gemstone but rather with nothing at all… it’s just slightly sweet, smoky, and powdery. Quite nice, but nothing more. It feels wintry, but it’s not as heavy as one might think. Nevertheless, it is probably best used in spring and autumn. As an occasion, it is more of a daytime fragrance than one for going out. It’s worth a test, but the other Le Gemme fragrances smell significantly better. Soo,… after testing the fragrance, it was soon time to say goodbye to the aforementioned perfumer. But I had to promise her to definitely test a fragrance that she apparently picked out just for me. Of course, she didn’t come with me since our paths had already separated, but somehow she had sent me directly into the lion’s den… what that means, you’ll find out tomorrow, in the comment on Laura Mercier - Tea Menthe Citron… To be continued…

I would never have thought of testing a Trésor flanker on my own. The original was too loud for me and had an undertone of something unbearably intrusive that I had not encountered in any other fragrance. In that respect, I was initially disappointed to see a packaging labeled "Trésor" in the surprise package from Simetra. Then I noticed the term "Eau Etincelante," which I had never heard before. Strange. No EDT, no EDP, no previously seen flanker - what was this? Oh, before I start browsing the web - I quickly sprayed it on... Ah, yes. I recognize a delicate hint of what I would unmistakably classify as THE Trésor character. But what had happened to it? I am reminded of a comparison between two sculptors: One chisels a rough structure from the stone, which is quite positively impressive due to its mass and presence, while another shapes a finely crafted, elegant figure from it. And it is the latter that I grasp with Trésor Eau Etincelante. So, I had to Google the term: Aha, this fragrance is supposed to be sparkling and bright. Indeed, it is more vibrant and lighter than its mother Trésor. Bright - well, I wouldn't exactly call it a clean scent; there are too many flowers and fruits involved. And again, it becomes clear to me that something must be off with the information in the pyramids. I clearly recognize in Trésor Eau Etincelante the DNA of the original Trésor from the 90s. I can’t remember if I had the EDT or the EDP back then. With the EDP, Trésor Eau Etincelante shares rose, heliotrope, sandalwood, and musk, while with the EDT, it only has rose and sandalwood. But I am quite sure that the Trésor DNA does not come from these components, but from something fruity. Well, let me describe the fragrance as if it had no famous ancestors: At first, it is citrusy-fresh, then moving towards a slightly bitter bergamot, and after about two or three minutes, something light and floral comes in. I can't necessarily perceive the floral note as rose; rather, I sense a hint of violet and heliotrope. And if someone had asked me, I would have said there is also a little jasmine in it. And a fruit. Spontaneously, I would have guessed on an not unpleasantly artificial peach, but when I read pear, I can also smell it as pear. Trésor Eau Etincelante remains light and translucent. It is not unsweet, but I wouldn’t call the fragrance sweet either. A bit of herbaceousness comes in over time: labdanum. But also heliotrope, which I seem to perceive strongly even in small amounts, adds a slightly biting quality that prevents Trésor Eau Etincelante from drifting towards being light and trivial. Over time, the fragrance becomes softer, the bite fades, and a friendly, feminine lightness envelops me. Just as Trésor Eau Etincelante balances sweetness finely, this also applies to warmth and cold. Here too, there is a floating between extremes, and I recall the saying: In the middle, it is light. The violet lingers for a long time and gets to showcase its soft gentleness, while remnants of bergamot and pear maintain the freshness without having the very sparkling quality of the very first minutes of the top note. Trésor Eau Etincelante is anything but unisex. I find it to be a very feminine fragrance that is suitable for any time of day and fits almost any occasion with its understated elegance. Only for very cold days in winter might it be a bit too light. The longevity is very good despite the lightness. After eight hours, it is still clearly perceptible. Some artificial musk notes are my nemeses. Here, musk is very subtle and not unpleasant for me in its nature. Musk and patchouli seem to blend so finely with sandalwood that they form an undifferentiated but pleasantly soft base that gently cradles the last remnants of violet and fruits to sleep. Thank you, Simetra, for opening my eyes to this beautiful Trésor despite my prejudices regarding its famous ancestors!

Years ago, when I stumbled upon the Bvlgari Aqva series, the Toniq didn't exist yet, only the original Aqva and Aqva Marine. As a dedicated fan of aquatics, I tested the two against each other several times (since they are quite similar) and ended up sticking with the Marine, which was simply fresher and lasted longer on my skin. The following summer, I discovered the Toniq and was blown away! A (admittedly initially acquired) bitter note that develops wonderfully and keeps the fragrance from sliding into the "shower gel triviality" like many other aquatics. In my opinion, it's the most exciting from the Aqva series (at least among the turquoise-blue flankers - I don't know the Amara) and is hopelessly underrated with a 6.5 here on Parfumo.

I think it's so great!! I found it at my sister's place; it belongs to her husband, and I immediately sprayed some on myself. I just love to sniff this scent. I didn't find the others in this line nearly as exciting.

Finally, I have time to write again. Bvlgary Aqua Marine pour homme is the fresh and zesty version of Bvlgari Aqua and a limited summer edition. On the international homepage of Bulgari, it states that it contains Posidonia, the Neptune grass. Sounds exciting and exotic. I have often rushed to Douglas, Marionnaud, Müller, and drugstores to spray myself with it. Since people started to recognize me, I had to change stores every now and then. *g* For a long time, I searched for a fresh scent that wouldn’t immediately evoke the toilet block in me. This happens to me with many designer fragrances that use aggressive lemon and poorly blend with other fragrance molecules. Here, Cavallier has created a super creation or reinterpretation. Who would have thought that pear would harmonize so well with grapefruit and create such a light Mediterranean freshness? In Kenneth Cole's "T-Shirt," there was also pear in the top note, which spread more of a purely fruity association. The freshness gradually gives way to the aquatic accord of Posidonia and a "Frozen-Water-Accord." It all sounds a bit mystical, and it is. The transition happens rather gradually and flows smoothly into the heart note. I would say it’s a smooth transition, and everything ends in a solid base of sandalwood and white cedar. The longevity is very good. 1 spray on paper strips: 10 hours! On clothing (2 sprays), almost 2 days. On the skin alone (with its warmth), you can expect about 7 hours. This fragrance is not intrusive, not sharp, chemical, and/or piercing like many discount fragrances that are supposed to smell fresh. You can tell not only by the longevity that this is a noble little water. Obtaining Posidonia as a fragrance ingredient is also a labor-intensive endeavor. Aside from that, Bulgari is synonymous with luxury, and I treated myself to it. 50ml costs €56.90 at Douglas, and the double amount is about €75. That was a bit expensive for me as a student, so I often had decants made. But on my return flight from London to Graz, I saw an irresistible offer at the airport: 100ml for £45! That’s only about €52! I jumped at the chance and am now the proud owner of this (commercial) luxury fragrance! My mornings now always begin with a splash of freshness, and the day can start. My classmates are thrilled and say I am so refreshing. I recommend testing the fragrance and simply trying to smell the components while applying it. It’s very interesting to detect the Posidonia. It works with a little effort, too. :) I see the fragrance as suitable for everyone aged 18 and above because it is fresh and sporty. But older students can also wear it in the office. It evokes youthfulness without coming across as silly. For the evening, I recommend the original fragrances. The tonic is more of a daytime scent, in my opinion. Unless you’re going to a beach party. *g* Have fun testing! :)

Anticipated with excitement and yet disappointed - at least puzzled! With this fragrance, I unfortunately have to pass - my nose must be playing tricks on me!? I smell the familiar... with the Toniq variant, just like with the Aqua Pour Homme Toniq, I detect the same notes as in the original versions. Everything feels the same, just a bit softer, milder! Therefore, I see the Toniq version(s) more as summer variants than as new compositions - but test it yourself and let me/us know ;)

Michel Almairic has designed a variety of perfumes for Bond no 9, so it's interesting to see him listed as one of the perfumers for Chloe CHLOE, as this composition reminds me very much of some of the Bond no 9 abstract floral perfumes, including CHELSEA FLOWERS. These sorts of compositions work well for many people--except when they don't, obviously as a result of some sort of chemical incompatibility. They strike me as highly synthetic, so I do not recommend them as floral perfumes, per se, and such creations must be tested on skin, otherwise one risks finding oneself at the wrong tail of the bell curve distribution of chemical compatibility. CHLOE is a watery, abstract rose-esque fragrance which smells clean and fresh and appears to be intended specifically for public space. There is the slightest touch of shampoo-like cleanliness, similar in this regard to CHELSEA FLOWERS without a doubt. I am reminded also of some of the cleaner perfumes in the Victoria's Secret prestige line (NOT the Secret Garden collection). I do not find CHLOE to be that good as a rose perfume, but it is a friendly fragrance which will work well in today's open cubicle office environment. No one will be offended by this clean watery rose-ish scent. I think that it's probably only necessary to own one such scent, so possessing both LOVE and CHELSEA FLOWERS or any of the other abstract watery florals now on offer--they seem to be especially prevalent at the Sephora level--would be redundant.

There was nothing to dislike about this fragrance, yet nothing to make me fall in love with it either. Chloe is a light, clean, pretty and feminine floral scent which is not offensive nor extremely unique. For the price tag it was dissapointing that this fragrance smelt like so many other cheaper fragrances. I had actually first tried this fragrance earlier in 2008, when my perfume obsession had only just begun. At the time I thought this fragrance was divine, but after 12 months of writing reviews and smelling other fragrances, Chloe no longer appeals to me. I believe that your own personality will determine whether or not you like this fragrance. If you're a little like me and enjoy intense, unique and sexy fragrances which help you stand out in a crowd, then this fragrance may not be for you. However, if subtle, clean and pretty scents are your thing then this fragrance could be your next big winner.

rose!? ... now let's be honest here... roses bring to mind a more mature wearer. a lady who lunches in pearls, Chanel suits and white gloves. honestly, when i smell rose in a perfume, i just... can't. no no no. nope. But this. THIS. this is not your grandmother's rose perfume. this is turkish rose and tropical fruits like lychee. this is flirty and curious. this is light and sexy. this is something i would actually wear! it smells like sunshine and barefoot strolls through english gardens. it smells like YOUTH! OH MY GOD CHLOE WHO ARE YOU PEOPLE? SORCERERS!? YOU MAKE MAGIC HAPPEN! give it a chance, take it from me, this is some good juice baby!

I tested this today at the drugstore. For some reason the first thing that came to my mind was "hospital." To me, this reminds me of what a hospital smells like. Kind of like the stuff that the janitor mixes with water and mops the floors with. Cleaning fluid type of smell. I just don't like it. Not for me.

The most feminine of feminine perfumes there is nothing masculine about this it's all girl to the notes and the design. The opening starts with an air of peonies with it's petals delicate releasing a sweet aroma floating through the breeze light purple freesia joins and gives a airy scent gentile and innocent, Litchi dries the top notes and with it's sweetish notes adds sexiness. Powdery rose is noticed here with a bit of a spiciness scent with delicate buds of lily of the valley just glades though the the notes magnolia similar to rose also brings spiciness but with an honey accord. i dectect a faint note of sandalwood for the basenotes and with the distinct warmness of amber i can't pick up any scent of cederwood. Chloe Conjours for me an field of daisies and a blonde girl lying upon the whole vast fields of them on a warm sunny day she grabs an stem from the daisy and blows and all the delicate petals float into the blue sky, when you wear this you get a sense of innocence and brings to child within you.

Chloe was one of the first fragrances I bought myself. Light, fresh, clean and yet unmistakable. I keep smelling Chloe on others as I walk by and am delighted every time, even though the scent is neither new nor rare, because for a few years (between 16 and 18) it was one of my signature scents. For me, it's clearly dominated by a powdery rose from the moment I put it on.

Chloe is my signature late winter Jan-Feb scent because smells cold and bright. It almost has a sort of ozonic, watery note to it. It makes me think fresh snow sparkling in the sunlight, or that cold air in the first few weeks of spring. This fragrance is also one of the few fresh fragrances I have tried that has some serious projection and lasting power.

Chloé is the essence of effortless femininity. A soft, clean floral scent, it opens with fresh peony and gentle magnolia, unfolding into a delicate rose heart that feels airy and graceful. It’s like freshly washed linen kissed by spring blossoms, elegant, modern, and timeless. Ideal for everyday wear, it leaves a subtle yet lasting impression of sophistication and charm.

This is a dew speckled flower bouquet. The opening has this really distinct sweetness that almost feels like it's going to lean into something vanilla or gourmand, but then the florals emerge and bring it back to this very light, wet, flower shop.

It has been consistently in my collection since 2008 and though it has been reformulated a little over the years, the heart still smells the same. It smells warm and powdery clean. The combination of the rose and lily of the valley play together beautifully. It is not a crisp and freshly picked rose on me but a softer, deep bourbon rose like Gertrude Jekyll.

This is a gorgeous musky-ambry-fougère-y confection. Unlike in Gucci's Bloom Acqua di Fiori, though, the musky-ambry and the fougèrey are balanced from the outset, and also the fougère-ity is nowhere near as wild. In this one it's more like, indeed, a fern, or a bit tobacco-leafy; but in that one it's, well, a bit like you've just cleared an overgrown plot of land with a power-strimmer! I do as a general rule like the juxtaposition of green and amber in a fragrance - but it's difficult, and shows forth the skill of the perfumier if it is truly accomplished, to make of that juxtaposition a true synergy. That is precisely what _is_ done here - it's like a rope braided of green and amber chords. And it's got that ubiquitous Chloé 'signature' too: I cannot adequately parse it - the best I can offer is that it's kind of the olfactory equivalent of polished marble. And it's as durable as that: it's low-key, but it just stays & stays. Or sardonyx rather than marble - more durable.

I blind bought this as I like all Chloe fragrances. I really liked it at first. Now I think It smells like an aftershave on me. The opening is a pretty, feminine and fruity floral, unfortunately after about an hour it dries down to a masculine musky scent. Sillage and longevity are enormous. It stays even after showering the next day. I dont recommend blind buying Nomade.

Edit: I realized the fragrance I had previously reviewed here was actually the ADP version of Chloé Nomade. I am now updating my review because I found the EDP and it's absolutely enchanting! The EDP is actually everything I had hoped it would be! The plum note in this version is much more subtle and fresh. It's still there, but less of a punch in the face and more of a subtle fruity note. This fragrance is so special and different from most fragrances you'll find at the big box stores. The mossy note makes it feel a bit retro, green and earthy. But it's still massively appealing. It has great longevity and sillage. It smells fresh, fruity, and clean. This is definitely a grown woman's fragrance and I am here for it!

This beautiful scent was a love at first sniff. I'm a sucker for plum notes and Chloe Nomade has such a bright, juicy plum heart that's elegant, flirty, and alluring. The opening of this fragrance is a gorgeous blend of all the citrus top notes which blend together to almost smell like a freshly-squeezed cup of citrus juices, more sweet than zesty. As the citrus notes fade, the heart of rose and jasmine really come forward—with the peach adding a juicy edge. The entire lifetime of the fragrance is supported by a smooth, creamy woods base accompanied with a soft musky facet, a tinge of greenness from a smooth and earthy patchouli, and a slightly scratchy distinct oakmoss. If you're a femme who dislike oakmoss or think it automatically makes a fragrance masculine, Nomade is absolutely going to be a no for you. But personally, Nomade taught me how oakmoss could be used to add a confident, earthy, head-turning edge to a perfume. All of the notes come together to create a perfectly-sweet, juicy and fruity floral fragrance with an extremely long-lasting musky-woodsy moss base. Probably 1-2 hours of 1m projection, then another 2-3 of 1 foot projection, but lasts on your clothes 8+ hrs at intimate distances. This would be a fantastic signature scent and is appropriate for just about every season but winter, where she would be better replaced by her older and richer sister, the now-discontinued Nomade Absolu de Parfum. Would be a head-turning but still safe daily reach which could fit the office just as well as running errands or a little cafe date. Probably a little bright and peppy to be a good nighttime scent as well. This is a hidden gem from Chloe and deserves more love. I'll probably always keep a bottle of this or the Absolu in my collection.

If Nomade piques your interest, and it should if you are a chypre-fan, check out Blackglama's Epic, which is a virtual unknown that can be had for much, much less than Chloe. I try not to get triggered when I encounter "similarities" in fragrances, but Nomade treats oakmoss & patchouli in a manner that is so similar it feels like a copy. The only difference I can detect is that one front-loads with fruits, the other with aromatics. Sweet or dry, take your pick. It is nice to see this classic style sneaking back into the mainstream. (copied from my basenotes profile Cardozo's_Ghost; review date 9/2018)
Chloé Nomade opens with juicy succulence of Mirabelle plum, sweeter, sunnier and less astringent than regular purple plums.

Firstly, I don’t have an experienced nose, which will likely become plain. Neither do I have the incredible way with words that many reviewers here do, but I am so charmed by the journey this took me on today that I wanted to write it down.

a burst of fresh citrus, like breaking the peel with your fingernails: bergamot, lemon, orange. followed immediately by a fruity peach and white floral, intertwined with a deep moss, patchouli, and woods. as it sits, it sheds the citrus and nestles gently in a nest of moss, earth, and coniferous woods, with an almost minty undertone woody, enchanting, alluring.

Nomade is a superb modern fruity-floral chypre. It opens with a sweet white floral note, reminiscent of honeysuckle, and a juicy stone fruit accord that falls somewhere between an apricot and a plum. There's also a noticeable dose of oakmoss, which is impressive given the current restrictions on its use in perfumery.

I have a part time job where I sell perfumes along with having my own business on the side. I feel like I have to get that out there, because I keep saying I'm done with designer fragrances, but I end up trying them anyways. I have the option to smell many fragrances during a shift, which is why I keep falling for trying new ones.

I once met a girl. She was out of my reach for so many reasons. The path seemed so rough, bummpy, uninviting but I decided to give my best shot, no matter her reluctance and the cold shiver of the poisonous phrase: "I can't see this thing working beyond of just a casual friendship." The beginning. I tried to give her my phone number one day, but she told me she wasn't carrying it with her to write it down. (way later on I found she wasn't lying, but I didn't know at that point). So I figured out a nice way of giving her my number the next time I accidently bump on her while she would walk her dog in a near big forest in our neighborhood. (I also have a dog) My phone consists of ten numbers so I made a total of 10 origami with a number on them. Each time we run accidently on each other, I was giving her one. (I was carrying an origami with me everytime in case I would see her. Had to be also extra careful not creasing it in my jacket's pocket) Couple of weeks later after the last origami was given, she figured out that the numbers on the origami was for a phone and sent me a thank you message. Now I had her number. Our (dog) encounters stopped being accidental, but she was still very absolutely intrasigent about being anything but friends. Less than three months later, I had conquered her mind with all the things I did for her. Our first night together. Ha.. don't expect any saucy details, but I can so vividly remember how much she wanted me and ofcourse her scent that night. In some other circumstances I wouldn't like this perfume. It was like a pungent greeny slightly flowery savage pachouli which had been meticulously laundered and then persistently ironed just before the point to be burned. God.. all that night's imagery, and that smell. The transformative smell of a woman's no to a yes, using your mind, your soul and your imagination. Conquer her mind and from that point it is really downhill. true story people.

Love Chloe is lovely, lady-like and sophisticated without being a floral-bomb. It's a beautiful, powdery rose that is simultaneously classic and contemporary. I know, I know - Love Chloe is composed of purple flowers, not roses. However, it leaves a rose impression. As it dries, the rice accord comes out. Although it sounds odd, it's really lovely. At first, Love Chloe seems strong & synthetic, and I imagine this turns off many customers at the sample counter. However, good things come to those who wait. Love Chloe chills in the 20-30 minute mark on me. Then it begins to meld with my skin, and it only gets better through the wear - It becomes a 'my skin, only better' fragrance, and on me it is amazing. Love Chloe lasts amazingly long on my skin -- in the 8 to 10 hour range. It's a comfortable fragrance and one I especially like for bedtime or the office - both as a light mist walk-through with a directed pulse point spray for yours truly. Love Chloe is an ageless fragrance that could stretch from 20 to 60 years with ease. Longevity is amazing, even when sprayed lightly. It's especially delightful in the lotion, sadly which is difficult to find at a good price. I think Love Chloe makes a great office-friendly fragrance, and it could easily be a signature for the right wearer. Although it's mass market, Love Chloe is unique enough to be niche or luxe. It's nothing like the original Chloe, nor like the newly reissued Chloes. I highly recommend sampling for rose fans and powder & soaps lovers. Note that patience with the fragrance is a must - don't give up on the opening, and try it several times. It grew on me, and it just might grow on you too.

There are hundreds of powdery fragrances but about solid hit pure powder it is a rare trend, so seize it! Chloé Love is a pure powdery opener with brittle floral nuances and soapy tidy hint. It's clean and cleansing, fresh, calm and promising of a rather cleaner musky undertone that appears much sooner than expected. Musk is essence of love with all its carnal affairs and while pure musky fragrances usually bring retro air up, Love links the material to today's taste. It's a posh powdery musk, timeless classic, simple, and a straightforward good-smelling fragrance. Good longevity, fine projection, satisfying. But what I love about Love is refined freshening dry down. 3/5

Metamorphosis in a Bottle "how a caterpillar turned into a butterfly" In this case How Gravel turns into Silk, Love Opens Harsh with a Blast of Orange Flower and Pink Pepper Underpinning starts it off a little Boozy and sharp As Love dries the scent turns Silky smooth and supple Like Second Skin Heliotrope Come Steeping though Giving Love a Vanillic Sweetness Lilac is Subtle but Noticeable, As Love Nears it's Ending Musk opens bringing with it an air of Animalistic Touch Iris Gives it a Cold Metallic Tinge what i can Pick up The Note of Leather I Do Notice a Good deal of it to my Nose Dominating but not Cloying The Leather brings out a good Base in this Fragrance, Rice gives the Scent an Avant Gardness Just Picture White Rice Floating on Glossy Black Leather, The Bottle may look simple but the Notes are a Work of Art.

Upon donning CHLOE LOVE, I was caught offguard. The scent was very familiar to me, and I struggled to attach a name: was it BVLGARI POUR FEMME? Certainly LOVE is a sweet and resinous floral, so I had to be close. Could it be Miller Harris COEUR DE FLEURS? After another couple of minutes, it suddenly dawned on me: LOVE is the cousin of FERRE edp, created by Pierre Bourdon. The iris perfume for which Bourdon is far more famous is Frédéric Malle IRIS POUDRE, which is less fruity and more aldehydic and formal than FERRE edp, but the similarity between the two is patent. In the case of CHLOE LOVE, I find the similarity even more striking, and looking at the notes it becomes clear why: iris and rice. This unique combination, sweetened by either fruit or heliotrope, shines through the composition in both cases. I have to conclude that these cousins are just as close as are the two iris-centric perfumes created by Bourdon! I am pleasantly surprised by this creation. Of course, I love FERRE edp, so naturally I'm inclined to like any perfume which bears a close resemblance to it. The main difference which I find here is that the drydown has a muskier demeanor, but it seems to be rendered more textured by the "talcum powder" note. Really? The final result to my nose smells an awful lot like ambergris (not labdanum amber...). Rather than fruit, the sweetness of this composition appears to be imparted by heliotrope. Now that I know how close LOVE is to FERRE edp, and precisely because it is slightly sweet but not fruity, I might consider adding a bottle of this creation to my collection, despite the fact that it is produced by Coty Prestige, which as far as I've seen (reading labels) adds BHT to all of its perfumes these days. I'm not in any hurry, though, as I have an ample supply of FERRE edp to fill my iris-rice needs for the foreseeable future.

First smelled it off a magazine fold over or a peel off. In the past, such samples in between pages of glossy ads always struck me as identical. With Love, Chloe, however, I experienced a moment of “just hold on, gotta take this name down.” It does exactly what I look for in a perfume - which is to make you smell good rather than like a “perfume.

A very beautiful perfume that opens up with spicy and transparent citrus that puts me in a good mood immediately. It's like that first "zing" you get in your tummy when you fall in love. For me the flowers take the main stand, hyacinth and lilac being the dominant ones.

I read all these reviews prior to testing Love by Chloe, so the strong baby powder note did not take me by surprise nor did it revolt me. What I did not like about this fragrance was its strong, almost sharp, powdery presence. The brand Chloe is really not for me. I didn't like the new Chloe and its flankers, nor did I enjoy this.

one of the few things i really liked recently is this new creation named chloè love ,very chic and feminine ,elegant and classy even for a young woman and why not even for an outrageous man .... ? soapy but not invading the room around you ,floral and powdery in the right way , i smell orange flower and hyacinth mixed in a sensual way .

Is it just me, or does Love, Chloe smell like a rose? How can it be that there are no rose notes listed?? I'm a big fan of florals, but this one just didn't wear well on me- in the same way that I would prefer a tailored men's styled white shirt to a ruffly blouse- this just smells too "frou-frou!

Eau de Monsieur was Annick Goutal’s first release and it’s hard to imagine a more quietly confident debut. It’s a citrus-mossy woods in the style of the existing models: Pour Monsieur de Chanel and Eau Sauvage, but it takes a different direction to those, with an amber note that warms the woody baseline, and a theme like star anise, pink rubber candy & ice cream wafer. The rubbery note harks back to Knize Ten and the work of Coty, and the anisic note is a clear reference to Azzaro pour Homme. But, despite the weight of tradition, (along with l’Artisan’s spiced coffee scent Eau du Navigateur that soon followed) Eau de Monsieur opened up a modern gourmand sensibility. This put Goutal in direct opposition to Roudnitska’s anti-gourmand over-ripe melon theme, and way beyond anything in Henri Robert’s non-gourmand Pour Monsieur. Goutal clearly had the imagination to hold her own against the likes of Robert and Roudnitska (perhaps it was her training as a concert pianist that gave her the power to interpret a given theme) but as a neophyte she didn’t have the technique of a grandmaster and Eau de Monsieur was well blended but rather straightforward (at least compared to Eau Sauvage). Nevertheless, it had a warm woody citrus and somehow (spicy) biscuit allure – a bit like gourmand Eau Neuve de Lubin crossed with Yohji Homme; subtle, low odour-yield but nice. Being the product of a conservative industry, perfume progresses in baby steps most of the time, and so it would be easy to write off Eau de Monsieur as just a pleasant tentative masculine that’s none too remarkable. But as Colbourne mentions in relation to l’Eau du Navigateur, this was 80’s niche, or possibly proto-niche from today’s perspective, and the masculine gourmand, which may now seem rather tame was probably quite radical back then. Regrettably, the original version was replaced by another formula in 2013. The gods giveth and the gods taketh away.

I can't see how anyone could dislike this, but then again, there's that saying "each to their own". Eau de Monsieur is a citrus-based scent blended just the way I like it, meaning it's less focused on sharp citrusy accords and refreshing in both a clean and herbaceous manner. Annick Goutal's Eau de Monsieur opens with subtle and clean lemon, complimented by an array of aromatic herbs. It is masculine in some ways, but I tentatively call it so, preferring to place it in a unisex category. Once settled on the skin, Eau de Monsieur takes on a powdery-like quality. I'm testing this in the midst of Summer, yet this somewhat warming scent is comforting enough to be worn in the cooler seasons too. The ambery drydown also adds to this likable warmth. I was quite disappointed by the lack of lasting strength, especially since I was enjoying the scent on my skin so much. After about three and a half hours this fragrance had pretty much vanished. A real shame. The sillage was also rather weak, nice in an intimate sense but a little too light for my nose to detect. I like Annick Goutal's approach when it comes to her masculine fragrances, most of them being easily worn by women too, but I'm not impressed with their lacklustre longevity.

I was lucky enough to snag a bottle of the "old" Eau de Monsieur at my trusted perfumery. It was a bargain at half price because it was a leftover stock. This was still the one with the ornate, handwritten-style label. The new fragrance was next to it, and both scents had testers available. The new Eau de Monsieur was too light, nondescript, and too citrusy for me. I was about to turn away from the fragrance, but I sprayed the older batch on my other wrist. Positive surprise: it smelled completely different. Richer, fuller, and rounder, plus much stronger. Above all, moss! Yum! There’s also a fine hint of wood, of the mild, delicate kind. Sniff sniff! This was exactly my direction when it comes to this scent. It doesn’t have a huge sillage, but I can still perceive it well on myself after a few hours. Eau de Monsieur evokes in me an image of a forest in light rain, where the plants exude a subtle, fine fragrance that allows for complete relaxation. It is also well-suited for female lovers of such somewhat rugged scents, as the smell is by no means "masculine" or even "animalistic." A subtle companion for every day and many occasions.

I had a sample lying around that I avoided because I HATE the regular LVEB. Yes, it’s too powdery for me + reminds me of bad times (yes, a personal issue). I’m glad I finally tested the sample because I didn’t expect to be enveloped by the wonderful scent of melted chocolate. The praline comes through super well for me and smells really delicious, or rather the mix of praline + tonka + vanilla. It definitely dominates, even though the LVEB DNA comes through after a while. I guess I’ll have to get the bottle.

Very different to other Nomades. In my opinion very unique I haven't smell anything like this before. I absolutely LOVE this. When I wear this on a warm summer day I feel like I'm summer goddess. I haven't been in Morocco or Egypt but I imagine there would smell like this. Date and vanilla is amazing combo. If you love gourmand fragrances you have to try this out. The bottle is also very pretty. I can't complain about performance either. Chloe Nomade Naturelle will always be a part of my collection.

Got a sample of this and to my nose it is very much in the vain of scents like Terracotta and Bronze Goddess. I own "Terracotta Le Parfum | Guerlain" (the one from the Les Legendaires line though) and feel like I don't need this. Terracotta does dry down more interesting to my nose. I tested Bronze Goddess Eau Fraiche and that one is very much like this one: a tropical summer scent without much else going on than Jasmin and vanilla, I don't find the vanilla as disturbing as in many other scents and this scent is certainly not bad, maybe even good, but still...it just doesn't thrill me. When it comes to Jasmin for summer, I much more prefer Gelsomini di Capri Eau de Parfum a true, uplifting, refreshing Jasmine that avoids that 'semi-euphoric' character of many tropical scents.

To me this it's the fall/vinter version of Nomade. The Nomade Naturelle is not similar to the original Nomade, this is sweet, cosy, warm and not as earthy as the OG. I get a warm, sweet and spicy vanilla with dates and i really enjoy it. Can't wait to put on a big cozy cardigan, doze myself in this and snuggle down to a movie when the weather turns colder.

Jasmine, sandalwood, vanilla and mirabelle plum. Nomade Naturelle is a warm and comforting scent and even if the date brings a fairly present sweet side, everything remains pleasant. The perfume remains quite delicate, perhaps a little too much in fact because I find the staying power and sillage quite light. Pretty nonetheless.

Well, does anyone still remember when you just pack away the samples that relevant fragrance and beauty companies send you into a drawer? Because they are always a bit too oriental and heavy? Hardly any variety, so that you don't even hold them to your nose anymore? I definitely do. I can do well without musk, but I'm not a fan of heavy syrupy orientals or melancholic perfume sweetness in general. In light of this, Nomade Naturelle was already on its way to becoming a room spray, and suddenly I smelled something unusual. Familiar sample sweetness with… leather? Oak moss? What was that? For once, I spared a wrist and was surprised. Briefly a fruity coolness, quickly something creamy-nutty that lingers, herbaceous and fruity, then sweet-mossy-leathery-woody, almost tobacco-like. It smelled like a lazy day at the beach during summer vacation, salt, musk, and for the third time slathered in sunscreen with sunscreen stains on the book where the sand sticks. Cozy. And this despite the fact that, if I had to choose, I would rather go to the cold than the Mediterranean. So, no inner memory that I often recall with longing. I can also relate to the association of others with desert wind and dates. This scent smells warm to me, fruity enough not to be too heavy. Warm, but rather heated like one feels after a sunny day in a sun-drenched land, when the heat of the day slowly fades and you still - or finally - smell the exotic flowers, ethereal oils, musk, and the rest of the warmth in the air. A great perfume, definitely noticeable and sweet, but unique, not a cotton candy scent. Also something for women who usually prefer it more herbaceous and grassy. For those who usually jump on the sweet fragrance pyramid: Do not order blindly, this one might not appeal to you. All Nomades are, in my opinion, very unchloéesque, so if you like the classic Chloé, smell it first, these are very, very different. If you are not a Chloé fan (read: me!), you will appreciate the absence of the often overpowering rose. For me personally, one of the first sweeter scents that I like. One that makes me long for summer in spring and for winter in autumn. Successful.

Once again out and about in the perfumeries of our city. On my free Tuesday morning, with my better half in tow, who now knows the exact route and my plans. "Now you probably want to go to the D..... first and then to the M.....

Yes, this perfume radiates pure zest for life. Perhaps it’s also because I prefer to wear the scent in spring or summer - or maybe it’s the association I have with jasmine flowers and dates. But let’s start from the beginning: In the summer of 2022, I tried several fragrances in the turquoise D.

Anyone who has ever been in a sandy desert knows that wonderful moment in the evening when the sun is just setting. Everything that lay still and motionless under the relentless sun during the day and hid in the shadows is now moving. Gazelles come to the watering hole, birds seek out their trees, and beetles crawl over the dunes.

I can remember the day I first smelled "Nomade (Eau de Parfum Naturelle) | Chloé" as if it were yesterday. In reality, it was in March of this year. A day trip to Freiburg with my loved ones. I was wandering through the city center with my youngest, and of course, I was drawn into one or another perfume shop. Then I tested it, the scent that has not left my mind since then.

... this fragrance has captured me! Somehow, I haven't really warmed up to Chloé scents. Except for Chloé Naturelle. And now this fragrance. Love at first spray. Soft, creamy, warm, and the date gives an incredibly lovely oriental sweetness without being spicy. The scent evokes an immediate sense of well-being in me, as if it had been waiting for me.

Chloe Love Story is a beautiful fragrance and I am glad to have tried it. The original Chloe EDP doesn't suit my skin nor my tastes all too well and sadly many of her flankers pose the same problem as they smell too alike. Chloe Love Story could be considered a stand-alone fragrance as it bears very few similarities to its predecessor. Chloe Love Story is a clean, somewhat soapy interpretation of neroli, stephanotis, rose and pear. It has a similar fresh laundry vibe like the rest of the Chloe range, just without the fizzy peony and litchi notes. Chloe Love Story was recommended on a few bridal websites as the perfect garden wedding scent. As a soon-to-be-bride myself I am placing Chloe Love Story onto my rather exhaustive shortlist for my big day. I adore neroli dominant fragrances and am looking for something refreshing and pristine with this fragrance ticking lots of boxes. I am a little concerned however that Chloe Love Story is soon to be discontinued if not already. My local department store now only carries the original Chloe EDP, Chloe Fleur de Parfum and Roses de Chloe, with Chloe Love Story already relegated to the discount stores. If this is to be my wedding day fragrance I will have to make my decision quickly to avoid disappointment.

Since I have heard from many people that the Chloe fragrances are good and sometimes very romantic, I went to the perfume store to form my own opinion about the Chloe scents. I tested every Chloe fragrance... I simply find that 99% of Chloe's scents smell like soap, or am I just imagining it? The saleswoman said that Love Story is one of the most popular Chloe fragrances because it is supposed to be very feminine, so I gave Love Story a chance. With Love Story, I also only smell soap and rose, which I find really disappointing! The Chloe fragrances are not the cheapest either, and at a high price, I think not every scent should smell like soap or rose. I was just disappointed and gave up on these fragrances; I believe I had too high expectations. The scents are indeed feminine, but nothing really special either. The fragrances have neither a special scent progression nor highs and lows; in short, they are just boring for my taste! And with Love Story, I smelled only soap and rose throughout the entire scent progression; only at the end could I detect a slight note of orange blossom, nothing more. I would be interested in hearing others' opinions on this fragrance because I find it just strange that I only smell soap and rose... The longevity wasn't great either; I could only perceive the scent on my skin for 4 hours.

Although I am generally a niche lover in olfactory terms, there are still some well-known fragrances that can pleasantly surprise me. This recently happened with Chloé's relaunch of Love Story. I love the classic from the house and know very few women who do not appreciate the powdery scent. When I first saw the beautiful advertisement featuring the wonderfully authentic Clémence Poesy, I knew: this is going to be a love story. The way she strolls so effortlessly and French along the Seine, with that romantic bottle in hand, oh..! Floral essences of orange blossom and neroli paired with soft cedarwood may not sound like the most groundbreaking composition at first glance. And I suppose that’s not what Love Story aims to be. It is an incredibly clear fragrance, gentle and girlish, very pure and elegant. In the past few days, as I step out of the shower, the thought immediately crosses my mind: today I will wear Love Story! The perfume is so wonderfully uncomplicated and fresh, just the right amount of scent that one would like to wear during the day and still find exciting while dancing in the evening. I would really love to know where my liaison with this bottle comes from, was it perhaps the beautiful Clémence? Or the almost kitschy setting of the perfect commercial? I don't know, but one thing is clear: for my next date, I want to smell just like this! Like delicate, freshly bloomed flowers that subtly settle in the nose and evoke a cozy smile the whole time. A perfume made for falling in love and perhaps the beginning of a truly great love story?

Now I have to tell you something about my Valentine's Day gift. I really like all the scents from Chloe, some more than others. I am less open to new things these days, as nothing really blows me away anymore. This new delicate breeze is not exactly a fragrance bomb, but I still like it very much. Why? Well, I see this Love Story on a spring day, you wake up and are immediately in a good mood. The sun is shining and the first spring flowers are greeting you. Cheerfully, you start the day with this fresh and floral scent, radiating energy and enthusiasm. I notice neither sharpness, pungency, nor toilet cleaner; I usually have that impression with citrus scents. When I first tested this new fragrance, I noticed a slightly soapy note, which I no longer perceive after some wear time. Well, it’s nothing terribly new that we’re encountering here; Neroli, orange blossoms, and flowers are currently delighting many perfumers and are being translated into new fragrances. By the way, I just had to Google Stephanotis; you can’t know everything after all. It’s a type of flower from the wreath vine that exudes a captivating scent. I would have said I smell jasmine, that would probably be simpler. If the rose in the regular Chloe, EdP, bothered you, you might want to take a closer look at this scent, fresh, cheerful, and simply enchanting. And completely without rose. A very light, pleasant breeze surrounds you constantly; Love Story certainly doesn’t stand out negatively. My husband really likes this scent on me. I smell so good! The only downside is that the scent doesn’t last all day. Reapplying is necessary. At this price, that stings a bit. So, how does my Love Story smell exactly? In short, fresh, floral, not sweet, but not bitter, with a woody finish. You should like orange blossoms, though. Fresh yet sensual, skillfully conveyed. I think I can still sense a hint of musk at the end, not bad. It’s also well-suited as an office scent, and I see Love Story as ageless. Anyone who likes it can wear it. So, that’s my personal Love Story! What you make of it is up to you.

And again we have a love story here… at least by the name of the fragrance. As I mentioned with the EDT recently, I unfortunately can’t tell a love story, well, due to the lack of a girlfriend and all, mu ha ha ha, I could at most talk about a few romantic movies, but I’m not so good at that either, since I don’t really watch such films often… unless there’s a totally charming actress like Audrey Tautou involved… *siiiiigh* :D Since I’m talking about the French… oui oui, they are now world champions, the game was great and quite goal-rich, but the games are over now. So you surely have plenty of time to read all my silly comments where I constantly whine and annoy everyone :D So, back to the fragrance. Recently I introduced the EDT of this scent here. Today I’ll try to list the differences to the EDP, even though at first sniff both fragrances should smell quite similar. The scent: The scent actually starts almost the same as the EDT. You can smell beautiful neroli, light (and indeterminate) flowers, as well as a slightly sweet note, which is stronger here compared to the EDT. Hmm… Stephanotis?? I have no idea how this wreath plant smells, but since it belongs to the jasmine family and is supposed to have a strong scent, I assume that the sweetness radiates from this plant, which is why the fragrance has a somewhat more intense sweetness than the EDT. Later in the base, I also smell a lot of neroli and floral scents; the sweet notes are still present, but have now weakened (and continue to weaken) and resemble more the sweetness of musk rather than jasmine. And almost typical for a base note, you can also clearly smell the cedarwood here, which is a big difference from the EDT, as cedar or any woody notes are not present in the EDT. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is somewhat higher than with the EDT, at least especially at the beginning. After a while, however, both fragrances can seem equally strong again. The longevity is a bit higher, so the scent lasts just over eight hours. The bottle: The bottle is great as always. It is rectangular with grooves in the glass and a chrome-plated top "edge," where the brand name is engraved. The bottle might remind one a bit of ancient buildings, which I find pretty cool (somewhat similar to the Roma bottles, although this is more obvious with the Roma fragrances, and here it just seems to me that the bottles look like ancient buildings). There is no label; the fragrance name is printed on the lower part of the bottle. There’s also the swingable handle thingy (what do you even call that? :D) with a nice silk ribbon in the same color as the fragrance liquid (light pastel green). A great bottle, although the EDT looks a tad prettier due to the pink fragrance liquid. So… first of all: I don’t quite understand one thing here… the EDP was rated significantly worse than the EDT, hmm… sure, there are some differences between the fragrances, but as long as one doesn’t mind a somewhat stronger radiating neroli in the base (which makes the scent more citrusy-sour than the EDT), I find both versions of the fragrance equally successful, which is also the reason why I rate both fragrances the same. Like the EDT, this scent is absolutely great for spring and summer; I would even say it’s more suited for summer, as the fragrances are not so strong in their radiance and will surely unfold better on warmer days, rather than being blown away at the slightest breeze :D For going out, the fragrances might be too weak, but one could still give it a try, as they smell nice. Those who have the dilemma of choice should simply test both extensively. The EDT is generally warmer and less citrusy, while the EDP radiates slightly stronger and smells more of neroli or orange blossoms, even in the base. Both are lovely fragrances that, while simply constructed, come across nicely. So, now there’s still the Eau Sensuelle left (which surely smells great, I’m already excited to test it)… and I bet that by the time I test it, I still won’t have a “love story” to tell… aaaaaaaargh and *siiiiigh* ! :DD

“When I saw the advertisement for it, I thought of you.” With such a wonderful promise, I received Cloe's “Love Story” as a gift. Which woman wouldn’t feel flattered by this comparison and THAT name? 'Schatzi' and my children are the only people in the world who are allowed to see me differently than I am. Nice. Soft. Maybe I am that too.......with them.

TOP NOTE: Neroli! (And a lot of it, excessively!) HEART NOTES: Orange blossom and Stephanotis (Jasmine) BASE NOTES: Musk and cedarwood "Love Story" is clearly inspired by Paris as the city of love. The perfumer here is Anne Flipo. The opening is like the entrance to a garden full of orange blossoms, brighter grasses, and colorful, sunlit flowers.

I have now been to my trusted perfumery 3 times... Each time I sprayed Chloe Love Story on one wrist and See by Chloe - Si Belle on the other! Both smell really good and much more pleasant than Chloé Signature. But in the evening, I always forget which one was Love Story and which one was Si Belle... is it the same for you? I also can't say yet which one I prefer!

Top note: Fresh. Heart note: Smells a bit like Armani Code pour Femme to me, meaning the orange blossoms are clearly dominant. Base: Beautifully woody, slightly powdery, clean. Thanks to the unsweetened base, it's a good fragrance for the warmer season; due to the flowers and freshness, it's less suitable for winter, at most on warm autumn days.

I must preface that Chloe's, Love Chloe's, and their flankers play in a league of their own for me. I simply love them, every time I wear them...always love, for some at first sight, for others on the second glance ;) Love Story is also such a fragrance for me: Bottle: very successful, it symbolizes a lock that lovers attach to bridge railings as a symbol of their love.

Annick Goutal NEROLI blends a variety of non-neroli notes in with the dominant neroli to produce a gorgeous neroli perfume--this is not a cologne! According to other sites, cypress, petit grain, and cedar are all implicated, and I do believe this to be true. NEROLI offers the perfect combination of greens and woods and citrus and neroli such that the whole is much more than the sum of its parts. There is also something resinous in the base to sustain the whole composition, as this is not at all an evanescent creation. Also perfectly unisex, I recommend NEROLI before nearly every other neroli-named fragrance I've tried. To my nose, this is one of the best Annick Goutal compositions, right up there with EAU D'HADRIEN. In fact, they are close cousins, with the neroli here dominating the citrus, rather than the reverse. Both NEROLI and EAU D'HADRIEN have an important dose of woods and greens to smooth the way. I definitely recommend this creation to anyone who appreciates EAU D'HADRIEN, and I regret that my decant will soon be gone!

I shouldn't be comparing this fragrance to other neroli based scents, however only seconds before trying this fragrance I had tested Le Lebo's Neroli 36. Had I not smelt a much sweeter and more feminine Neroli 36, Annick Goutal's Neroli may have been delicate to my nose too. The orange note is certainly obvious in this fragrance. It's not overly citrusy, more pulpy and juicy with a dash of herbs. It does have a masculine quality to it, however I wouldn't go so far to say that it's unpleasant. The scent tends to be very light and airy at times with a touch of greeness and a likable bitterness. Unfortunately the lasting power is extremely poor, I could barely smell it after an hour on my skin. Neroli evokes a strong sense of Summer in my mind. Lots of sunshine, cool drinks and warm breezes. It's pretty, but like I said, disappointing in the longevity department. I wanted to see how it would develop further. Vanilla does play a part in this fragrance's drydown, giving Neroli a somewhat sweet aspect that still manages to smell very natural. What I do admire about this fragrance is its ability to smell like a blossom picked fresh from a garden. This is an all-natural interpretation of a beautiful orange blossom.

Neroli:the symbol of purity, innocence, fertility and eternal love. This fragrance was created as ode to medieval Italian Princess Neroli. A pure essence of orange blossoms full to my senses.The poetic spring white blossoms of orange trees blooming as the sun rays touch them Fresh,ethereal and magical scent.It was the first niche that i added in my collection.One of the most natural blends of neroli i have ever encountered. It's worth trying/buying.Highly recommend it.

This is my favorite neroli/orange blossom scent. Very nice balance of citrus/green notes and florals. The opening is citrus and somewhat sharp. Quickly a soft floral undertone emerges for a wonderful combination of delicate florals and zesty green notes. Would be perfect for summer, but I wouldn't necessarily limit it to that season. Lasting power is also good. A must for neroli and orange blossom lovers.

L'Eau de Chloé (2012) is an odd little fragrance. It opens bright and sunny with notes of citrus, then it transitions to a subtle rosewater. The patchouli is there, but it's dry not wet, green not brown, neutral not sweet, and subtle not demanding. At drydown, this fragrance becomes a green, soapy aldehyde on me. It feels like a throwback to the 1970s, and it has much more in common with Y by Yves Saint Laurent than it does with Chloe, original or new. L'Eau de Chloé is a mature fragrance. Oh, how I hate using that word but it's appropriate. I imagine that the target market might like this at the perfume counter, buy it, then despise it after a longer wear. It is getting a lot of mixed reviews, and that's one guess as to why: The fragrance when wet is completely different from the fragrance when dry. The fragrance when wet is a good quality lemon-rose cologne from Demeter. The fragrance when dry is a vintage find from the charity shop. Perhaps I should say that L'Eau de Chloé is a fragrance for an experienced sniffer, in particular someone who appreciates classic fragrances but tends to wear contemporary ones. I put myself in that camp. I can't wear Y and I struggle to wear Chanel 19 (new or vintage), but I _can_ imagine myself wearing L'Eau de Chloé. It's a contemporary take on a green, soapy aldehyde. Anyone who likes classic fragrances, or at least appreciates them, might want to sample L'Eau de Chloé. I purchased a mini for a song on the bay. I like it, really like it, but I need a bit of wear before I decide whether it's full-bottle worthy.

Since the disappearance of Chloe (1975) and Chloe Narcisse, all modern releases from this brand have left me dissatisfied. L'eau de Chloe has thankfully come along and saved the day, renewing some respect that I had lost for Chloe over the last few years. This fragrance is all fresh and inoffensive. Finally I've met a Chloe fragrance that doesn't jam itself right up my nostrils and cause me to reach for my inhaler. L'eau de Chloe has very little in common with the original Chloe fragrance, (by which I mean that strong and soapy rose inspired perfume, whose popularity I do not understand). The pastel green bottle design, reflects how this fragrance smells. It's fresh, green (of course) and Spring-like. The citrus opening is bright and breezy, but never overpowering. Its projection is pleasing to say the least, settling intimately on the skin. According to the perfumer Michel Almairac, this fragrance is "supposed to evoke the scent of frozen lemonade", as reported on the Now Smell This blog. Surprisingly I can smell this idea reflected in L'eau de Chloe's composition, and I think that's the main reason why I've come to enjoy this fragrance so much. I like the carefree approach that this fragrance has. It's very easy to wear, and even easier to enjoy. To some finicky reviewers, L'eau de Chloe may strike them as being linear and plain. I for one, don't mind the basic citrus and green, leafy blend. The rose and patchouli in this fragrance are so watered-down that they barely even feature. I found both the sillage and longevity to be equally pleasing. I think I also prefer this flanker's packaging over and above the other Chloe releases. I'm giving L'eau de Chloe my personal tick of approval.

"L'Eau de Chloé" is a refined femininity inspired by cosmetic scents, perfectly embodying the new Chloés. Its role within the Chloé family: cool sovereignty, slightly distant, slightly factual, slightly sober. However, being entirely Chloé, this delicate green "Eau" is categorically sovereign and cool, but without the governess-like strictness of most straightforward women's classics. Even more so, it lacks the herbal-bitter exclamation marks of many vintages or the pinched mouth corners of traditional colognes. It also forgoes the claws of icy, green-bitter chypres. It hints at all these "don't-touch-me" characteristics, but in a Chloé translation. Upon spraying, these immediately come to life: decidedly green citrus fruit spreads out, more dry than juicy. Soon, a dark, very cool iris unfolds-which isn't really an iris at all: sterile rose and especially dry patchouli create a cold-bitter iris (like in some iris soliflores where the iris can easily double). This wonderful fake iris eventually fades into a sea of freshly washed linen: slightly rough, but always clean and cozy. In this sense, "Eau de Chloé" may be too rough, too bitter, too dry, too straightforward for one wearer. For another, it may be too little of that. For one, it will be too little Chloé, for another too much Chloé. For many others, however, the "Eau" will be just right-precisely sovereign, un-playful, cool, and pure. And still Chloé enough. Just like for me. Thanks, Hasi!

I rarely wear updos. I don't own a pearl necklace. I don't have a Chanel handbag. I don't have manicured hands. I don't have a Dior suit. But I will wear the green Chloé! The previous comments hit the mark - I also have these associations in my mind. L'Eau de Chloé is different from its siblings, but somehow not really. It doesn't stray too far from the line. I don't necessarily associate the other Chloés with punk girls, but rather with elegance and style confidence, deluxe understatement. To me, L'Eau de Chloé smells like a mix of all the other Chloés with a few fresher ingredients. In other words: 30% Chloé EdT + 30% Chloé EdP + 30% EdP Intense + yellow Nimm-Zwei-Bollos + something green = L'Eau de Chloé That's roughly how it smells to me. It is just as light and creamy-balsamic as the EdT, just as floral-rosy as the EdP, has about the sweetness of the Intense variant paired with a bit of citrus and a green touch, somewhat like that from the Un Jardin line by Hermès. For me, a successful composition, where the wheel wasn't reinvented, but it speaks to me very much. L'Eau de Chloé is worth a try for all Chloé fans! And: whoever has my address and wants to get rid of any of the above-mentioned items that I DO NOT have, go ahead... A new watch wouldn't be bad either. ;)

I discovered and tested L’Eau de Chloe in January 2014 during the Christmas clearance sale. This Chloe captivated me immediately, and I treated myself to the small "My little" bottle with 20 ml. And I still love it. I have always liked roses as flowers and rose scents. This Chloe is a rather simply constructed but effective rose fragrance, delicate and refreshing, but without the teenage note that often bothers me. It starts with slightly citrusy notes, pleasantly soft. No sour lemon punch that makes your eyes water. The lemon reminds me more of lime and lemon balm, perfectly dosed and finely woven with fresh rose petals, still damp from the morning dew, which are just opening in the mild temperatures and yawning a bit sleepily into the young day, releasing their first hint of rose. The citrus notes and the rose petals unite here in the most beautiful harmony. A drop of patchouli grounds the scent and has also been perfectly integrated, so that it is only barely perceptible and does not overpower the citrus-rose combination, but rather gently supports and reinforces it. Everything is perfectly balanced here despite the simplicity of the fragrance. There are many fresh rose scents, but this one is my favorite among them. Some are just too similar. And in many, a teenage note reminiscent of black tea dominates too strongly, which spoils the rose for me. Thankfully, that is not the case here. L’Eau de Chloe is different, perfect for me when I want to wear a delicate fresh rose. I also cannot complain about the longevity. I applied it yesterday before bed and can still smell it in the morning, though only faintly. I like the ribbed bottle with the light green ribbon and the pale green liquid best in the "My little" version. I will definitely repurchase L’Eau de Chloe as long as it is still available, and I have already saved a backup bottle.

For some, a fresh scent - for me, one of the most unforgettable scent flirts of my life. It all began in one of my regular spots, in the perfumery I trust. I probably wouldn’t have noticed this shy little bottle with the modest ribbon. Until the saleswoman I trust insisted on introducing me to it. Hmm...

...now you are mine! I discovered perfumes for myself not too long ago. Many well-known brands are usually too heavy or too sweet for me... or even both. Or you smell them quite often despite their not affordable price. But the green has captivated me. So far too expensive, I had relegated this scent to my wish list.

Chypre par excellence! One has become accustomed to the fact that a slight variation of the name of a well-known fragrance produces a completely new one of its kind. Familiar, yet still different from the others. The Chloés are beautiful, like sisters. They resemble each other vaguely but have completely different character traits.
L’Eau de Chloé. A scent I am quite curious about, as I have experienced one very good and one rather insignificant fragrance from Chloé so far. I started with Love Chloé Eau Intense.

My friend and I had settled in at the Chloe stand at Karstadt - and we both enjoyed the fresh floral notes of L'eau. My garden in the morning dew, when the scents gently weave like a web around my nose. The citrus notes feel pleasantly cool against the calm rose in rose. The transparent fragrance gains depth through patchouli.

This is an outstanding tuberose soliflore. It is bold, strong and it walks the line of being a bit too much for me but yet I find it is to be quite remarkable. There is something raw, powerful and exotic about this fragrance. I still think that Carnal Flower by Frederic Malle holds the title of being the sexiest tuberose ever but this one also has this deep sensuality that only tuberose can deliver. It makes me feel like an ancient and powerful goddess with a beautiful tuberose lei on my shoulders. The tuberose note in this fragrance is very vibrant, natural and realistic. The fragrance has pleasant sillage and average longevity. I definitely recommend it for tuberose addicts.

Here it is finally in its most beautiful, fleshy-floral depth, my absolute dream tuberose! :=) For a long time, I avoided tuberose-heavy scents. I found them musty or urinous depending on the supporting components. After several years of fragrance experience, it suddenly revealed itself to me. I could appreciate it in scents like Michael Kors, Nuit de Tubereuse, DSH Tubereuse, and my then favorite, the grass-green Carnal Flower Tuberose. But somehow, there was always a certain distance (a bit too piercing or too dull-musty :) Then, by chance, a sample of the Goutal fragrance came under my nose. PHEW!! WOW! So this is Tuberose Absolue?? Nothing else to mask/intensify, etc?? Here, the tuberose has a soft fluffy powdery face, but still made of flesh and blood :) I can't compare this scent to anything familiar; it leaves me speechless.. it is a bit earthy, floral, buttery, and powdery, and indeed tuberose-like, but how do you describe tuberose to someone who has never smelled it? Unfortunately, I can't.. but I hope that many more tuberose lovers will get to know and enjoy this scent. And unlike many other Goutals, this fragrance clings to the skin for a long time (almost 7 hours on me). Bravo!

Well, if you ask me, the rose. But that's not what this is about. Des Lys is a typical Goutal, the brand is instantly recognizable, even at the first sniff on the skin. One could almost call it a Goutaliade... It starts with a very dark green opening, somewhat bitter and woody. But that only lasts a few seconds. Immediately after, the lily opens up, and it is the white lily. Delicate and light, it dominates this fragrance for quite some time and is beautiful. Bright, clear, unique - a soliflore, at least in this phase. Later, a green note joins in again, no longer as bitter and dark as at the beginning, but enough to take out the sweetness without suppressing the scent of the lily, so that the lily in the base is completely unsweet. A stunning development and for me a lily scent that I would love to wear. That's why it’s also going on my wish list. The sillage is remarkable here, the scent can be nicely perceived from over 60 cm away. The longevity is also good, with 6 hours I can't complain, and it still smells quite distinct. For a Goutal, that's a good result.

‘Cedrus’ is another fragrance from ‘Atelier des Fleurs’ by Chloe - and like the rest of the line it’s subtle and very personal for the creator Quentin Bisch; a childhood memory of a bouquet of branches given by his father to his mother. The fragrance opens with a green fougere accord - there are fresh herbs, fresh green leaves and a fine spicy note - before the more milky powdery side becomes more prominent. The slightly spicy character remains - not spice in a culinary sense but rather like freshly cut flower stems or branches where you can still smell the sap. There’s a certain crispiness about it; like an early morning walk along the edge of a forest, where lush meadows meet the first shrubs of the woods. To me there is also an aldehydic note - becoming especially strong after a few hours - clean, light and soapy but without being synthetic. This ‘Cedrus’ has in common with another superb Bisch creation - ‘Bois Imperial’ for Essential Parfums. Starting as a fougere scent ‘Cedrus’ morphs into a soft woody one - that change is done very skilfully and feels very organic, just like a freshly cut bouquet would subtly change over time. As with other ‘Atelier des Fleurs’ fragrances the projection is moderate - so it’s best suited for someone wearing perfumes as a personal experience. The longevity is surprisingly decent - even after an entire day I can still smell the base notes; albeit faded there’s that clean powdery aldehydic scent. It’s a gentle fragrance - I wouldn’t classify it as either particularly masculine or feminine but rather a mood scent that puts me at ease and reminds me of the simple joys in life.

I really enjoy this collection and already own Vanilla Planifolia, Ylang Cananga, Jasmine Sambac and Herba Mimosa. I love every single one of them, but was a little unsure of Cedrus. "Cedrus | Chloé" is a nice woody, versatile, all year round scent. Cardamom is a note I struggle with and find nauseating. While I can still detect the cardamom, it’s balanced well with the wood notes making it much easier for me to wear. It’s also light without being overly woody, especially for someone like me who isn't keen on woody fragrances in general. I also found Cedrus lasted longer than Cedrus Intense. Cedrus Intense has a gorgeous opening of citrus and woody notes. I wish it stayed throughout but, while not listed, I get a strong and overpowering Cardamom note in the dry down. Cedrus Intense also has the addition of rose, which makes it nauseating and unwearable for me. So the winner for me is "Cedrus | Chloé" Great on its own or layered with other scents.

The first splash that hits the nose when I spray it is delightful. As if I'm smelling some ancient chypre perfume from a rich lady's private collection as she puts it on. Green, damp, aromatic, almost forest-like and with a surprisingly elegant mossy note. But in barely ~10 minutes the magic dissipates. The lady has errands to run, so now she's gone. I am a child again, left alone in her giant empty house. Awkwardly sitting on the couch, afraid to touch anything. What's left is woody, very clean, almost soapy. There's a fleeting hint of powder – homely, slightly sweetened. There are no flowers listed in the notes, but I feel something undeniably floral at the edge of my vision. It's all very casual and effortless, yet almost... uncomfortably expensive. Polished wood furnishings, fresh white flower bouquets in every room, odd statuettes mounted on cabinets and coffee tables that feel like they will fall off at any moment if I dare to even look at them wrong. The air itself is permeated by an aftertaste of that vintage signature perfume. Very beautiful, but no matter how much I'm told to relax and feel at home – I just can't do it. I'm all stiff and can't wait to get back to my parents' house and breathe the mold in, lol. It never travels far from the wearer, and becomes a complete skin scent in ~1,5 hours. The ~5,5 hours that it lasts (the same rich people's house from start to finish, just fainter and fainter) pass by in a melancholic trance that I struggle to snap out of. Feels like an unproductive therapy session. I will not be coming back to it.

Mossy creamy cardamom with warm woody notes. I get what people mean when they say that this is soapy, but when you see it being described that way, don’t think that it necessarily smells like literal soap— it just has a very clean and creamy facet it to it. OH OH this smells like Chloe Nomade but way way toned down and “cleaner”. This is the only full bottle perfume that I have ever blind bought and thankfully, it was a win. There is a soft elegance to it that makes it addicting and I’m so happy that the fall and winter are here so that I can enjoy this a lot more. I will say that the projection of this perfume is extremely disappointing, specially for somebody who loves a strong scent. Part of my joy in wearing and testing perfumes is catching whiffs of it throughout the day and just enjoying what I’m smelling and unfortunately, this perfume only does that for about an hour. I will say, though, the longevity is good; it can linger on your clothes for at least eight hours. If you like a clean woody scent and like a cozy intimate scent, this will be an absolute gem to have.

Initially feels like I am sitting inside a soap bubble. Then it’s like the bubble pops (after about 15 minutes) and I find myself in the most beautiful mossy woods with a few sweet flowers underfoot as well. I’m a vanilla girl yet I absolutely love this. It’s clean yet not sharp or “hand soapy”. It’s unisex but i feel the dry down leans feminine. I thought it didn’t project much but I got a compliment the minute I walked into work wearing this. It makes me feel clean and sophisticated. I spray it on my sheets before bed as well, it’s peaceful and relaxing. After almost returning it when I first began testing (because I didn’t love the soapy opening), I now consider this in my top 5 fragrances. It also helps that it can be found on discounter websites occasionally (I paid $89 for my bottle).

“Do you know this one?” --> Whenever I hear this sentence from my colleague at the office, I know that I’m about to get something wonderful to test… just like this time.
