PSSSST. HELLO! HELLO YOU! CAN YOU HEAR ME? Did someone just speak to me? HERE, HERE UP HERE I AM! Huh? Am I going crazy now? YOU JUST NEED TO LOOK UP! SNIFF ME! I KNOW YOU'LL LIKE IT. My heart races as I look up. Next to Chloe EDP, my absolute favorite, stand its siblings. AAAAH. FINALLY YOU'RE LOOKING AT ME. COME ON! YOU WANT IT TOO! TAKE ME!

When I read the great comment from Peanut, I knew I had to have this fragrance :-) so I went out....sprayed it in the perfume store, took a few rounds through the city and I was done for. I sniffed at my wrist and what I smelled was enchanting.

For the upcoming dark, cold, long months (grrr), I embarked on the arduous search for a snug skinny cuddle-comfort fragrance. I also asked for your help in the forum. A big thank you to everyone for the great scent ideas and sniffing suggestions! The very first idea from a lovely Parfumo user was Chloé EdT or EdP. I immediately took the following position: "Oh no.

This is my absolute favorite among the three Chloé fragrances in the bottle style of a pleated blouse. It is also the only scent that I wanted so badly when I first noticed it on another woman that I asked her what fragrance it was.

Today I discovered a bouquet of long-stemmed dark red roses in the supermarket, which whispered to me softly: Take me with you! I listened and paused. Has this red, enchantingly fragrant splendor been overlooked - or even forgotten? No, I cannot leave it alone in the cold neon light.

....It's probably like with Mon Guerlain Sparkling Bouquet ....we want to try something completely new and hide the DNA...okay, that worked...I don't perceive the typical LVEB, instead there's a synthetic air accord...if it weren't for the pear, I would have thought I sprayed Bright Crystal Eau de Toilette . Fresh clean scent, a bit of pear in the opening, musk in the dry down. A little peony...hm nice but unspectacular.

Do you like green noted perfumes? If yes, this could be an interesting addition to your perfume arsenal. Not at all sweet, but somehow still airy and feminine, with this perfume Chloe set out to make a perfume out of 100% natural ingredients derived directly from nature. No synthethics. As your scent options therefore are limited in this situation, what resulted is a very green, very light scent. The projection isn't large and neither is the longevity, so you would need to overspray. The perfume is so green its a bit sharp in its green-ness, but not screechy. Its a fun experiment in perfumery, and once you know the story behind the scent, the smell of it makes sense. But you've got to be into green notes to like this, because its almost all green, with a very light, ozonic touch and just very light overall, with a sharp, dare I say, almost bitter note. It opens on a greenish citrus note, that fades quite quickly. I personally don't get much of the rose in it, neither the mimosa or neroli. What I mostly get is that citron, blackcurrant and cedarwood accord. It's not my personal favourite, but I can see it fit for the minimalistic, organic, sustainable lifestyle oriented person who likes to wear whites and linens. Suitable for all ages maybe except teens. Definitely a daytime scent, it's and easy grab-and-spray that you don't have to think too much about, suitable for free time, picnics, walks on the beach, you know, fresh things. Could maybe even be fit for a nurse as a subtle, clean green scent. Did I say green a lot? I think you get the idea. :)

CHLOÉ Eau de Parfum Naturelle comes in the usual Chloé bottle with a ribbon and looks very beautiful. When sprayed, there is a brief hint of roses. The scent itself is quite fresh, like just out of the shower, and has a woody base note but no wow effect. It is more of a fragrance that you might spray on quickly when you don't have anything else at hand. On my skin, the scent shows significant weaknesses in longevity. After a few gentle attempts, I tried with about 8 sprays, but unfortunately with the same result. And my surroundings don't notice the scent at all. Unfortunately, it does not meet my expectations, and I will not repurchase it.

I really like your opening. Pleasant citrus and freshly mowed, but dry grass. For anyone who grew up in a small town: the top notes of Chloé naturelle smell like childhood in a bottle! But then, really just 5 minutes later, the somewhat scratchy, typical Chloé rose comes through. The meadow associations are gone. Instead, there’s grandma’s rose soap: nice, neat, but terribly boring. The longevity and sillage are really so weak, I have never experienced anything like this before: after a maximum of 2 hours, not even the rose is perceptible, let alone any of the base notes. Neither on test strips nor on the skin. Very unfortunate, but this flanker was really unnecessary.

As the days get warmer and buds let their first juicy leaves sprout in the sunlight, Eau Naturelle also opens its fragrance buds. The opening is citrusy-bitter, with candied lemon clearly dominating - it will accompany us throughout the entire fragrance journey. The blackcurrant bud joins smoothly and gives Eau Naturelle a soapy direction. I am a bit irritated, or is this the typical Chloé character? More soap bubbles than nature.. After a few minutes, the Bulgarian rose shines through the soap, warming pleasantly and weightlessly. It takes over tactfully, green notes follow it into a pastel green scent spectacle.. Light neroli adds feminine notes.. I feel like I am in a compressed flower meadow. Dew-fresh, flower by flower opens, mimosa now sprinkles in powdery notes. Now I wait.. and wait, oh cedar? Where are you..? Either it is a very young, shy cedar or it disappears under a soapy-green-floral-pastel pink foliage.. I cannot identify a clear cedar note for the life of me; it could just as well be hazelnut. Gradually, mimosa adds a warming sweetness.. Very shy branches emerge from this fresh-floral green, laying it in a silky base.. Fresh, romantic, green-beautiful. Conclusion: As the rose bloomed in the fragrance journey, I began to like Chloé's Eau Naturelle more. I don't know if I could cope with the soapy character of the fragrance (probably the citrus combined with the floral), which ultimately reminds me a bit of diffuse hairspray notes. I just can't warm up to that. Perhaps I would layer it with 2Wood for her to achieve a stronger woody base. I guess I am simply not a Chloé type. :') Those who resonate with Chloé in its fundamental character will find pleasure in Eau Naturelle.

I wanted to get the Chloe signature, but this one caught my eye as I went to the store. Nice ribbon and first thought that came with the scent - very cozy for some reason. I can't quite put it into words, but the composition feels a little sentimental to me. Lots of rose, a little of raspberry (but still very visible). When I got the perfume on my skin, I smell woody notes - the raspberry remains as a sweet little addiction to the rest, as it sets as a fresh, earthy rose (not the usual rose you get in the perfume, I would say). It lasts for a nice few hours - maybe 6-8, I'd say. They could last a little longer for this price, but they stay on clothes for longer though. Nice scent, however I don't think I will buy this again after finishing the bottle.

I absolutely love this. I always keep smelling my wrist when I spray this so i don't understand bad reviews. Classic and feminine rose with woody notes. Just ordered my second bottle. I really like rosy scents and I think this is perfect rose for colder weather. Raspberry fades away very quickly tho, but it doesn't bother me.

This was a blind-buy for me (not recommended) and my first time trying Chloe perfumes in general. The raspberry is very prominent, making the opening fruity and a bit tangy, even. This lasts about 1-2 hrs. The rose is somewhat powdery and I would describe the overall quality as classy and feminine, more suitable for evening. It is quite intense, lasting even longer on clothing into the next day. I don't like the dry-down... On my skin it turns smelly, unfortunately. It is not a sharp woody cedar smell, but just odorous, and somewhat musty :(

A large cloud of very artificial raspberry. The other notes hide behind it at first, but I can already feel that there's rose down there and it's not good. And something else, not sure what, that is still somehow worse. An almost... oniony undertone? It even hurts my eyes a little. Bonus points for full immersion, I guess. Takes around ~30 minutes to settle in my immediate vicinity. Projects around an arm's length away, but becomes very sharp and noxious as you get closer. Rose is becoming stronger and it's just as I imagined it at that first sniff – synthetic with a hint of cat piss. My partner comes home and confirms the "something else" part. Something in this perfume transforms on my skin into a scent of oniony body odor. Yay..? It is, in a very specific and negative way, a very well-rounded composition. "Synthetic dupe perfume from a corner shop" top notes. "Cat pee infused clothing" heart. "Onion breath and musty body odor" base. Just spray it once to immediately recreate a very specific type of stranger you would try to quickly get away from on the street. Takes ~3,5 hours to settle on skin. At that point body odor and onions mostly fizzle out. The rose takes centerstage and clings to you for the rest of the evening. I could still feel a faint synthetic sweetness on me ~5 hours later as I was entering the shower. Are you serious, Chloé? What is this? Is it my fault for expecting better from you?

but I didn't want any synthetic notes, where is the promised raspberry? Did someone mention disinfectant x 2? No, that's strange, it's just alcohol mixed with Baccarat… Chloe, you have disappointed me. At first, there was a piercing, irritating, burning, sour note, but it doesn't last long, then it's just Baccarat, but washed in a washing machine. Huge disappointment, the raspberries must have been sold out.

Recently, while browsing, the new Chloe caught my eye - I really like the Chloe Rose, and I wear Love Story from time to time, so I wanted to test how I feel about this one. The bottle is appealing, and the red bow is nice too. The name is somewhat ambivalent (L'eau = water, so fresh/light, Intense the opposite), but that's typical for flankers.

The fragrance starts with a pleasant combination of fruity notes, primarily raspberry, which also brings a strong sweetness. At first, the soft Chloé DNA resonates, giving the whole a familiar base. However, after a short time, the rose pushes to the forefront - and not subtly, but with full force.

I must admit that I’m not really fond of Chloe fragrances; somehow, it always ends up being something rosy. The last Chloe perfume I bought was back in 2015, which is almost a decade ago now. It was Chloe Lovestory, which I ended up giving away after less than half was used because I couldn’t stand it anymore; I actually felt nauseous when I got near the scent.

I find the scent beautiful. Elegant, feminine, heavy yet somehow clean and light. It can overwhelm you if you spray too much, which happened to me last time, so I had to take a break for a few days. It shouldn't be too warm either. As for the scent, you definitely smell rose, ambrox, and synthetics. It definitely has a Chloe character, but more mature and less playful.

And that doesn't reconcile me either. Ambrox synthetic, cheap hairspray, thorny rose, raspberry rather unripe. This type of fragrance creates a scratchy throat for me, teary eyes, not out of joy. Synthetic note, Bulgarian rose water. Too bad Chloe, I'm used to better flankers. Short and sweet, the longevity seems to be very good but I immediately feel the urge to wash it off!

Creamy vanilla with a hint of rose jam – feels more fruity than it does floral. Not much jasmine, if any. A hazy sweet cloud in the wearer's immediate vicinity. A twinge of balsamic ambers close to their skin. It smells okay, but every step it takes is hesitant and moderate. There's no spark within it. If you know a girl who would repaint her walls "eggshell white" instead of "light beige" and then tell you about that as a story of her being quirky and adventurous – this should be a safe gift for her. A type of scent for a pretty girl background character. She's not meant to be remembered. As a matter of fact, I already barely remember her at all. It settles on skin in about ~2 hours. Becomes simpler as time goes on. Past the ~4 hour mark most of it is gone. There's still some vanilla left, but it becomes unpleasant on drydown – like a pudding that stayed out of the fridge for too long and now smells funky and is starting to look suspiciously fuzzy around the edges. That lasts for about ~2 hours more. Yikes. But don't worry! Overall it's so boring and faceless that come tomorrow you probably won't even recall that you had felt any particular way about it at all.

I mostly loved this when I sprayed it on at Ulta. It started as a lovely very light rose then after about 10 minutes or so I noticed a very slight cloying note at the end of every whiff I caught. It mostly smelled nice, sort of like a baby wipe in a very pleasant way, but it was just slightly off at the very end. About an hour or so later it dried down to a really pretty warm amber that completely dissolved into a strong wood 5 minutes later that I wasn't a huge fan of. I'm so conflicted and would probably need to test it again to really determine how I feel about it.

This is a beautiful classic amber-vanilla-jasmine. I could see this being a great "first big girl" perfume, a gift for a new mother, a wedding scent, or a lounging-at-home perfume. It is a little more traditional floral than I enjoy, but I'm so glad I sampled this little lovely -- it is absolutely signature scent worthy! ETA: I had to buy a bottle, this grew on me so much as the weather warmed up. I wear it to ballet class because that’s the vibe - effortlessly chic and graceful, sweet and refined. The balsamic notes in the drydown remind me of rosin powder and warm wood floors. My favorite amber-based perfume by leaps and bounds (or jetés and fouettés).

Where is Chloe and what have you done with her?! Those expecting the typical Chloe DNA will be disappointed here. I have tested Lumineuse several times over the past few days and I am not warming up to it. From the rose, which I usually find successful in Chloe, I personally smell nothing. I perceive amber and a powdery-dry, synthetic vanilla, underlined by jasmine and a fruity nuance that I interpreted as orange before I read the notes. The powdery synthetic remains consistent and reminds me of a note I have often noticed in perfumes lately; in "Un Jardin à Cythère | Hermès," dry grass is mentioned as a note, and in "Memori - Coeur Azuki | Kenzo," rice/vanilla. In the dry down, only powder and a slightly resinous scent remain. I would like to like it, but unfortunately it gives me a headache, even though the notes actually fall exactly into my preferred category.

After a long search - more out of curiosity, not because I am a dedicated Chloé fan - I was finally able to test Chloé Lumineuse yesterday. Directly on my arm, paper is a waste of time for me, as it smells completely different. Now, I am actually not a Chloé fan; my only fragrance from this brand is Rose Tangerine, because in that one, the rose is not the overwhelming note (at least not for me), and I only like rose as Narciso Rodriguez interpreted it in Poudree. Or in Musc Noir Rose. That said in advance. Lumineuse is, as others have already noted, also not a flanker of the Signature line for me; it doesn't fit in there at all. They should have created a completely new name. I thought that with the fragrance notes it is advertised with, this would be a Chloé scent that I would really like - if only it would unfold that way! I do not smell the typical Chloé rose, which was supposed to be reinterpreted here. Jasmine is also not recognizable to me. I can't really identify the rest - except for the vanilla, which I only find at the very end as a weak base that I can only notice with my nose directly on my wrist. In fact, there is something that I find in my test set from Kenzo Memori, I just don't know which fragrance it is. Most likely Poudre Matcha. Maybe also in Coer Azuki, as Scandinavica has already described here, or perhaps Nuit Tatami. (By the way, I was also not so impressed with the Memori set that I would buy one of them in full size.) However, Lumineuse has a bit more sweetness, but I don't find it as overwhelmingly sweet as one can read in the statements. Sweet would not have been my first association. So, how does this fragrance smell on me? I don't know. Maybe it's called "balsamic." It's not heavy, but it's not fresh either. I don't find it bad, but do I need to have it? I don't know... considering the space in my perfume cabinet ;-). As an everyday scent, it's okay if you free yourself from the thought that it should be a Chloé Signature scent. It is rather independent. What I also notice: While today's fragrance world is largely synthetic, Chloé still made a big exception for me, as you can definitely smell the completely natural ingredients in the Signature line. With Nomade, I would no longer agree. I don't warm up to the Nomade line at all; it's too sticky and artificial for me. I also find Lumineuse quite artificial. My expectations were not met here, as it turns out completely different than I thought.

I understand my predecessors, NEVERTHELESS I must disagree on some points. First artificial, yes, but it also has something absolutely fresh and summery delightful. The balsamic notes stand out clearly in the foreground and overshadow everything quite a bit. However, not in a negative sense. This makes it not refreshing, but round and embracing.

With this fragrance, I began my journey into the world of perfume last year. After never really being interested in the topic of perfume, suddenly the desire arose to try it out. But how do I even start? At Douglas, the selection was overwhelming. So many perfumes. Some have almost the same name, look almost the same, but are apparently different?

In my impression, this fragrance is a very sweet blend of fruit and flower, accompanied by a powdery undertone. The rose is clearly perceptible to me, while the rest comes across as very synthetic. It aims to please, perhaps a bit too much. Unfortunately, it's very generic, not my cup of tea.

...Chloè fragrances like the plague...a huuuuge plague. I don’t like them. Period. It’s like with Chanel. I don’t like them. Period. Buuut...in my last fragrance mail, there was a sample of this scent included. It was hot that day, the day was stressful, I was slightly irritable (but just slightly), and I still had a few things to do on the computer. Unfocused and disinterested (and irritable) as I was, my gaze fell on the tester..."oh, what the heck" I thought to myself and sprayed it on my forearm. Ooooyyy...this mandarin...instantly, my spirits were lifted. So beautifully fruity, yet light like a white curtain in the wind, paired with a delicate rose, on whose petals the morning dew is still visible...wonderful. Later on, a cozy amber joins in, and that’s about it. This scent isn’t exciting, it doesn’t have a spectacular scent progression, but it is well made. It invigorates, refreshes, lifts the mood (probably due to the mandarin), and is a summer fragrance for daytime. It’s not a room-filler and doesn’t last long (at least not on me)...unfortunately...

The husband bought a flat screen TV - the size of Holland. Two strong young men carried the thing into the house - and hurried away. So the husband set about setting up the high-tech device. His initial excitement diminished considerably, and he offered me to read the instruction manual - I was the reader in this household. I clarified to him that this had nothing to do with literary reading - and also hurriedly left the house. Destination: Karstadt - perfume department. And a new offshoot of Chloe caught my eye. I have always cherished and valued the Chloes - and there was even a tester available. I was curious about the ingredient tangerine - but could only perceive mandarin, which appears fresh and not sour - keeping the scent transparent. The rose also seems white to me - lightly citrus-tinged. I see the elegant rose "A Whiter Shade of Pale" before me, brightening and adorning my garden. The blackcurrant is subtly tart - and also leans towards freshness. Light and bright, cedar mixes in - gently sweetened by amber. A bright positive scent with casual elegance that also fits into autumn. Cheered up, I drive home again - where the husband is still brooding over the instruction manual. His gloomy mood, however, bounces off the cheerfully tuned scent - which I carry into the house carefree but distinctly. Tangerine lands on the wish list - Christmas is coming soon.

Even at the first spray, the typical Chloé signature is recognizable in Chloé Tangerine, the light rose scent that gives all Chloés its character. ROSE TANGERINE, however, is more self-assured, modern, and feminine than its predecessors, particularly with the addition of a fruity and lively mandarin that gives the fragrance its name. Yet, it loses none of the typically romantic, playful elegance of the Chloé house. Delicate rose is the first thing that the nose perceives. I enjoy rose scents, but they shouldn’t be too "intense," as is the case with MFK L'Eau de la Rose. The rose in Chloé's fragrances is, in my opinion, perfectly dosed, as it is light, feminine, and sensual, always giving its wearer a touch of cool romance. Surprisingly sweet and quite suddenly-after about 10 minutes-the fragrance turns fruity. Zesty mandarin and blackcurrant join the rose. For those who found previous Chloés too rose-heavy, this could offer a more fruity-floral alternative. In my eyes, Rose Tangerine provides a very good entry point for Chloé fragrance beginners. Rose Tangerine is not a scent that overwhelms. For people who prefer very prominent fragrances, Chloé Rose Tangerine is definitely not for them. Like all fragrances in the line, this one is also very close to the body and subtle. What is exciting about the fragrance, in my opinion, is that it changes again about two hours after application. When warm woody notes of cedar and amber come into play, Rose Tangerine gains some character and more presence. Even though Rose Tangerine reminds me a bit of the EDT from 2009, the fragrance has a completely independent temperament, with more sweetness than its predecessor, which was more powdery-something Rose Tangerine does not offer at all. The fragrance is suitable for any occasion, for everyday wear, festivities, or the office. Since there are so many different scents, every woman of any age can find her matching Chloé fragrance without having to forgo the typical Chloé signature. Like all the fragrances I own from Chloé, Rose Tangerine is also perceived as pleasant and seductive by those around me. The typical Chloé note also reveals to my surroundings-without saying a word-that I am wearing Chloé. I personally appreciate this about Chloé fragrances very much. Sillage and projection are rather moderate. The texture is soft and delicate. The bottle is handy and elegant, and with the bow, it is a real eye-catcher.

For those wondering why there was no 10th door yesterday, the comment on Miller Harris - Lumière Dorée was already written; I just added the video. Now, onto today’s 11th perfume Advent calendar door: A long time ago, I wrote a blog titled “The Confusions of the Nose.” In it, I described what my nose occasionally actually smells in relation to the listed fragrance notes. This list emerged: Roses combined with citrus fruits: Dill pickle water Cedarwood: optionally pencil shavings or ham Saffron: paprika Fig: cat or coconut Blackcurrant: definitely and almost always cat Lily of the valley in oriental combinations: soapy, piercing lab chemicals Chocolate: wet dog Aquatic notes: fish Fresh notes: banana Patchouli: valerian Vanilla: mushroom I should experience one of these nose confusions during my first testing of Chloé Rose Tangerine, but first, a few facts about the fragrance: Chloé Rose Tangerine was released this year as a women’s fragrance. Created by Sidonie Lancaster and Michel Almairac, who was also responsible for the creation of the popular Chloé Eau de Parfum and co-developed my beloved Chloé Eau de Toilette. I sprayed both just before the first test of Rose Tangerine and must say that I really enjoy smelling the Eau de Parfum on others; however, the rose sometimes seems too woody and distant to me, and it quickly becomes soapy on my skin. The Eau de Toilette starts icy-fresh for me, with a cooler but less woody rose, and gains an aromatic cedarwood note as it develops. So, boldly and with prior knowledge, I approached the test: Ah mandarin, squashed mandarin…… green mandarin ……. and wood………wood? Green wood???.........Dill, I can hardly dare to smell further because Tada, you guessed it, there it is again: DILL PICKLE WATER! …………….hidden way back and very small is a woody rose à la Chloé. But my nose simply cannot get past that wicked herb. I managed to hold out for a few hours during the first test, but then washed it all off and couldn’t perceive anything else in the drydown, so I am now bravely repeating the test a second time. Here are my second impressions: Juicy mandarin, slightly artificial, something aromatic in the background (dill? I can hardly dare to say it, because if I don’t say it, maybe I’ll smell something else this time). The roses are strongly faded, similar to Roses de Chloé. The mandarins also dry up quickly. The dill remains in the background today, but I am sure they simply used dill instead of baby’s breath when binding the rose bouquet….a slight soapy note comes through in the drydown and subtly reminds me of the Eau de Parfum. One thing is clear, my fragrance will not be this one. Even though the dill pickle water is tamer today than during the first test, I cannot completely avoid smelling the herb. So be it, one less fragrance I need to add to my collection, even though I find the idea of mandarins and roses very beautiful.

I’ll keep it short: noble-floral-fresh - slightly herbal experience. There’s not much more to say about it. Personally, I find the longevity very good. With a bit of Vaseline, the scent lasts even longer on the skin. The fragrance is also perceived by others and described as very pleasant. I wear it during the day - in summer/spring I also like to wear it in the evenings. For those expecting a sweet scent: no chance! I get a fine herbal rose, fruity noble mandarin, fresh currant, and in the drydown, the cedarwood and amber come through.

Chloé (2007) has been my signature scent since its release year. Of course, you have to like roses; otherwise, there's no point in looking at the line at all. And since I love the original and I love mandarin, I thought that Rose Tangerine would simply be the perfect blind buy candidate.

An extremely pleasant, high quality and well blended musk fragrance. Aldehydic start (and I could swear that pink pepper is involved?!). Discreet florals, discreet wood, discreet incense. And just a pinch of very well fitting ambrette to soften the jasmine and transfer everything smoothly to musk by its silky and light powderyness. Pressing your nose against the skin there is a slight animalic touch as well. And speaking of skin: it’s definitely not a beast mode fragrance, but it stays close to you for at least 8 hours. Quite different from my other bottles in the Le Gemme line. Is it groundbreaking or exciting? No. But very well received as an office fragrance or just that one bottle when Myths Man is a bit…much. Way too expensive at full retail though and I would never recommend it at over 400€… But I scored a 100 ml for 130€ and at that price it’s a solid 9!

The scent lives up to its name at least at the beginning. It smells strongly of rose, or rather like a rose garden, as the lily of the valley and grapefruit (thankfully only very subtly) are noticeable and make the fragrance a bit more diverse, making it truly feel like standing in a garden for a moment. That's nice, but I still miss that certain something, something special/exciting. The scent is pleasant, but it just drifts along, heading towards forgetfulness. Cedarwood knocks briefly, but then unfortunately after 20 minutes the scent becomes a bit piercingly powdery.

This EdT from Bvlgari smells so fresh and soft. The fragrance embodies romance, elegance, and yet a touch of playfulness. It is not at all overpowering and leaves a fresh, powdery floral scent. Perfect for spring and summer! Some people find this floral scent a bit too intense, which I personally cannot understand, as it smells very light and clean. Perfect for the Clean-Girl vibe!

Fruity perfumes are often cloying on my skin and therefore I don’t wear many. I received a sample of Allegra - Rock'n'Rome and was delighted to find I enjoy wearing it enough to purchase a large bottle. The apricot is soft with a powdery base and delicate osthmanthus below it. It’s really that simple. It’s fresh and perfect to wear during spring or summer, particularly while on vacation. The bottle is charming and fun, albeit expensive. Longevity 4 hrs and sillage is close, not excellent but appropriate.

A brief note upfront: those of you who are less interested in my allegorical framing story can feel free to jump straight to the section "about the bottle" for my olfactory impressions. Under the category "new and noteworthy" on the Parfumo homepage, the five cheerfully colorful Bvlgari bottles from the Allegra series immediately caught my attention at the beginning of the year. Opinions on the classic candy-shaped bottles may vary greatly, but I personally identify with the group "love at first sight." In terms of color combination, Rock’n’Rome appealed to me the most, and fortunately, the fragrance pyramid also piqued my greatest interest. At the end of March, as I slowly began to recover from a physically and mentally taxing illness (you might guess, I was indeed hit by that nasty Covid-19 virus), I could use every possible positive feeling for the healing process. My range of action was still severely limited at that time, so I delighted in three online purchases. I chose a colorful summer dress, a gray metallic leather bag, and Rock’n’Rome. According to perfumer Jacques Cavallier, each fragrance in the collection represents a specific Italian way of life. And voilà, since we all know the secret of the space/time travel magic of fragrances, I found myself in my new dress on the terrace of a cozy café in the historic center of Rome. It’s a warm spring day, I’m in pleasant company, and my gaze falls on an ancient piazza, in the middle of which a picturesque fountain produces pleasantly soothing splashing sounds; in short, I’m right in the midst of la dolce vita. The little glass bottle with thick yellow-golden nectar, which I have long desired from previous trips to Italy, stands before me and exudes its fruity, enticing apricot scent. Alongside it, there’s a hot chocolate that lightly wafts a smoky aroma to my nose. In between, I sniff at my new soft leather bag. My companion remains pleasantly calm by my side, not demanding my attention but enjoying this wonderful sensory moment with me. About the bottle: The 100ml bottle surprised me with its size-it is among the largest bottles in my collection, measuring 13 centimeters in height and 5 centimeters in width. The color is just as beautiful and vibrant in person as it appears in the pictures. The design leaves nothing to be desired and is intricately crafted with its gold and glass elements, giving it a very high-quality feel with the heavy stopper. The spray is easy to use but quite strong, making it somewhat difficult to dose, although you can hardly overdose on the fragrance-but more on that later. About the scent: Rock’n’Rome starts with a sour-citrusy note that transforms into a fresh fruity note within seconds. My nose detects the authentic scent of apricots, which are accompanied from the very beginning by a subtle leather note. Although the bottle might suggest otherwise, the apricot scent does not have a squeaky sugary sweetness; instead, it truly smells like juicy apricots. Perfumer Jacques Cavallier describes Rock’n’Rome as liqueur-like. I can’t quite relate to the idea of liqueur in the sense of alcohol, although I do occasionally believe I can detect one or two overripe fruits during a certain phase of the scent's development, but fortunately, this light hint quickly passes. However, if he means the thick consistency of a delicious apricot nectar, I find that very fitting. The fruity-floral scent of osmanthus creates a very harmonious blend with the apricot as a powdery peach note. Unlike in Le Gemme - Coralia, the leather note of osmanthus here is very soft and subtle and certainly not prominent or synthetic. I can only smell it when I hold my nose directly to the scented spot. Otherwise, it likely contributes to a certain elegance and elevates the fragrance above the realm of generic fruit perfumes, which can easily drift into girlishness. As the scent transitions towards the base, the apricot relinquishes part of its presence to the benzoin. Rock’n’Rome then takes on a certain balsamic note that fits wonderfully and adds a grounded and cozy quality to the fragrance. When I sniff directly at the scented spot, I can perceive a chocolate aroma. But… For all those who enjoy wearing statement fragrances, I cannot recommend this one. Rock’n’Rome is truly a very subtle scent. It is a beautiful fragrance, balanced in its components, with an interesting progression, but its sillage is definitely weak. It is a quiet companion that is there for you and delights you when you consciously turn to it, but otherwise tends to remain in the background. Longevity is present for a few hours, but it requires a conscious focus after some time to perceive it. However, for those seeking a light, unobtrusive fragrance for the warmer seasons, this one is quite suitable. Perhaps the weak sillage is indeed intentional, as the five colorful Allegra bottles were launched alongside five so-called Magnifying Essences (50ml, white, also in candy form). These are designed to complement or enhance the perfume with specific notes-available are musk, bergamot, patchouli, vanilla, and rose-to make it more personal. For me, Rock’n’Rome is a very cheerful and vivacious fragrance that fits perfectly into spring or summer. It exudes lightness and carefree joy and, despite its understated presence, has the power to evoke pleasant childhood memories or catapult us right into la dolce vita as described.

I haven't had or tested any perfume from Bvlgari until now; this is my first one and I am very satisfied even though I bought it in winter. It is wonderfully fresh and not too citrusy. I don't perceive cinnamon at all; it is simply beautifully refreshing and somehow cooling, probably due to the mint. After a while, a slightly floral note comes in. In the base, it becomes a bit warmer and leaves a lovely scent trail on the skin. I am already looking forward to wearing it in summer :-) Small addendum 7.8.13 : Unfortunately, the scent has not developed well on my skin in warm temperatures; at first, it is wonderfully fresh and slightly floral, but unfortunately, the base is a bit too spicy and bitter for me. I perceive it more as a unisex scent, and indeed it smells wonderful on men's skin, like freshly washed :-). Therefore, I have let it go.

… that such a beautiful, charming fragrance has no reviews yet. I would never have come across this scent if I hadn't received a surprise package last week. Dear Missol, thank you once again for your incredible idea of sending me these beautiful fragrances just like that!! It made me very happy and also touched me. Now to the scent: It's rare for me to like a fragrance from top to bottom (or base). There's usually a hitch with one of the notes. Normally, I have issues with the top note, as it often comes across as grand and pompous, only becoming the actual scent when it reaches the heart note. Ma'magnifica is something you want to hold onto with the first spray. You feel… yes, this is exactly how a woman wants to smell. Fragrances that I don't know, I test blindly. I want to be influenced neither by reviews nor by fragrance pyramids. I completely disregard the brands. And I must say: this fragrance in no way reflects what I read. My impressions: Rose First slightly fruity Then minimally woody Iris Very pleasant and understated After reading: Spicy (a bit), floral (I can confirm), earthy (none!!!), oriental (I'm looking for), woody (mild sandalwood, pleasant, similar to iris). A thoroughly inconspicuous, pleasant, enchanting scent that lasts but does not project (and I mean this in no way negatively, quite the opposite). The bottle In short: I don't like it. I would have preferred a classic bottle for this fragrance. Longevity: Average, I can perceive it for 5-6 hours Sillage: Rather understated but enchanting Absolute recommendation for testing, and I am very happy that I could test this beautiful fragrance quite incidentally … and wishlist

I have rarely had a perfume that smells different every day when sprayed on. Sometimes it’s vanilla cake, then play dough, then baking vanilla, and today inexplicably watermelon? Maybe because of the leather notes... But in the dry down, it always turns into a beautiful powdery vanilla that simply smells like fresh pudding from the pot (and I can confirm this because the scent made me want to cook some). However, I’ve noticed that it performs very weakly overall. The longevity and sillage are terrible, and I find it too weak for layering; it gets lost on me. But I love how it smells; I really wish it would perform better.

what must a fragrance be like that I perceive as precious? bright, balanced, as if it gently makes the wearer glow. and that is what splendia does: with a floating, radiant magnolia, that lasts for hours has a fine creaminess and a distinct freshness and a depth, that is light and delicate and gently joyful, as if one were looking into deep, clear water. a fragrance jewel.

...while reading through the individual fragrance notes, I asked myself.. "What does a maple leaf smell like...?? Answer: "No idea but -live broadcast- Damn delicious!!!" This little scent is so incredibly tasty-- it immediately reminds me of those wonderful scented candles that one always wishes for as a perfume but can never find. Especially during the cold season, when you stroll through the (divine) decor department in furniture stores and suddenly perceive this aroma coming from some shelf..! it smells so deliciously cozy, vanillic, warm... like cookie dough!! Then you look around and search for the stand where you can buy these roasted almonds, macadamia nuts, love apples, gingerbread, etc.. But no, they are only outside in the cold in front of the entrance... ...it must be scented candles...! :D Just as shamelessly delicious smells Hotkiss - sweet talker.. Intensely spicy with all the "Christmas" spices. No one gets a sugar shock here because everything is perfectly blended. The ingredients are balanced, not overloaded, not loud! But rather close to the body and long-lasting. Simply sweet Unsweet. Must-have for ALL sweet tooths!

Anticipated with excitement and yet disappointed - at least puzzled! With this fragrance, I unfortunately have to pass - my nose seems to be playing tricks on me!? I smell the familiar... with the Toniq variant, just like with the Marine Toniq, I detect the same notes as in the original versions. Everything feels the same, just a bit softer, milder! Therefore, I see the Toniq version(s) more as summer variants than as new compositions - but test it yourself and let me/us know ;)

I don't know what it is with all these perfumes. Either my nose is so spoiled by really good scents that I can no longer tolerate these generic waters, or they are all really as bad as I perceive them. Here, a very nice fresh top note stands out first, which I would describe as quite successful. But that does not deceive my nose about the very synthetic base that comes through relatively quickly and gives the heart no chance to unfold. This does not immediately cause severe headaches (for me, mind you!), but I wouldn’t want to wear it.

I’m not a huge fan of Bvlgari perfume in general. They’re usually too strong for me or make me sneeze, so I was hesitant to try Riva Solare. I was sent a small sample and tried it one afternoon. Expecting the worst, I was shocked to experience how incredibly lovely this perfume is! I noticed the scent of osmanthus more than anything, but it is balanced by orange blossom. The musk is there, which is what makes it so lovely. Without it I’m not sure it would be so appealing. Comparing it to Jo Malone Osmanthus Blossom I actually like Riva Solare better. Osmanthus is a hit or a miss; it can be too much of a good thing. Here in Riva Solareits balanced quite nicely. Sillage is good, about 3 feet. It’s not overbearing, but simple. Longevity for me on a hot day is 4 hours, but I can still smell it lightly for up to seven hours. I would actually buy this one!

Not a fresh musk..I mean. It is the smell of comfort, of feeling good. The smell of cotton in winter. It's a warm, very warm smell.. it releases an incredible power of pure peace. That's what this little gem makes me think about. P.S.: Magnifying what!?!?.. I will spray it solo to enjoy it as is... its a forceful satisfaction!

I stumbled upon Magnifying Bergamot completely by chance right at its launch in an expensive department store. I was actually just there because I was waiting for someone and was boredly wandering through the brightly filled shelves full of "who's who" brand names. An equally bored saleswoman spotted me, and we decided it made more sense to pass the time together rather than politely ignoring each other. So she brought me one fragrance after another. But it quickly became clear that I did not belong to her classic target audience. Just as we were both about to give up, my gaze fell upon the brightly colored, candy-like bottles from Bvlgari, next to simple white bottles. Above them was the text: "The new Allegra Collection. Your personalized fragrance experience starts here." Aha. More out of curiosity (and to give us both a little success), I surprisingly reached for the inconspicuous Magnifying Bergamot. "Boring bottle, but with bergamot, not much can go wrong for me," I thought. Almost embarrassed, the saleswoman interrupted my thoughts: "Oh, this is something very simple, actually only meant for layering, not to be used separately. The colored bottles are the real stars. This one is nothing special, it doesn’t do much, and it’s quite expensive." (Ouch, so much for her assessment of my target audience suitability...). Well. But sometimes less really is more. And sometimes "simple" is actually damn expensive. So this is the little story of how this rather unknown perfume from this well-known house came into my life to stay forever. To start: Magnifying Bergamot is not a complicated fragrance, and it is indeed simple. But therein lies its genius. It has no thousand frills, is neither kitschy nor intrusive, but clear, pure, honest, zesty, and ageless. It reminds me of home, of an Italy, without having to resort to shallow clichés or fulfilling a picture of the country and fruit shaped by poor marketing. Thus, this perfume becomes a small white pearl in a vast sea of bergamot fragrances: unique, without being offensive. That’s why it also perfectly fulfills its original layering purpose. I wear it (sorry, not sorry) shamelessly over Chanel, Nishane, Widian, Xerjoff, etc. or quite classically over Molecule 01. This gives everything an elegant, juicy bergamot note, that certain extra that makes it my "Francesca fragrance". Unfortunately, like many freshies, it doesn’t last particularly long, but that doesn’t diminish my enthusiasm. Because every time I perceive the fragrance on my skin, I feel like I have found the pure essence of what I love most about a perfume. It resonates with my essence so much that I sometimes think bergamot has long become part of my DNA. I (and my bank account) would now find it only fair if Bvlgari would finally sponsor me. Not only because I have certainly contributed a significant part to the sales of this rather unknown fragrance (and not just through my own very decadent consumption). But also because many people in my environment have now become consumers of this expensive little water themselves. You don’t believe me? Let me tell you: I get approached about my fragrance so often when I wear Magnifying Bergamot (whether alone or layered) that I have now saved the link to the perfume fixed in my notes app to be able to airdrop it directly.

I am an enthusiastic fan of Bvlgari. This perfume was recommended to me, but when I looked at the notes, I wasn't convinced. I had thought of a light, floral fragrance. Until the day I was able to try it. At first, I thought the consultant had suggested the wrong bottle, and I looked again and sniffed at the cap. It was indeed "Passeggiata". What I smelled did not seem like a light floral scent. To my nose, it started to feel like a tropical fragrance. With notes of honey, frangipani, and quince. It is sunny! Creamy. In no way as simple as the fragrance notes wanted me to believe. It's a bit like "Beige de Chanel," but in an intense version!!! Very rich and sophisticated. I feel like I am inhaling the air of a tropical island full of flowers with floral nectar and very ripe fruits. I can even smell the sun. It will gradually settle to remain sparkling and musky. Definitely, I love these candies more and more. Regarding the bottle: The color truly reflects that you have the content. I love it. Thank you, Nicole, for recommending me this candy.

At first, an alcoholic start that transforms into freshly washed white cotton. The clean impression is supported by lily of the valley and ends on a creamy base (woods & musk). The sillage could definitely be better, as the scent is versatile and suits anyone who wants to feel clean and refreshed! Therefore, in my opinion, it is not a going-out/evening fragrance.

...oh dear...piercing, biting. I thought this was nail polish remover...oh no, my acetone-free one with peach scent smells more pleasant. A completely unhealthy synthetic, like something for disinfecting the toilet. As unnaturally blue as the liquid looks, it smells just as terrible. Moschino Cheap&Chic has this color too and to make matters worse, it comes in a bottle that looks like a glass cleaner spray...and smells like it too. However, this piercing note fades away, well what remains is an attempt at a Clean Girl scent heading towards the Muse or Blanche...who knows...In conclusion, you can buy nice scented candles at H&M (white meadow) but stay away from "perfume"!

The scent resembles the popular "T-Shirt | H&M," which is almost identical to buy. I am very glad about that because I always quite liked it for those days when you’re not really sure what you want to wear. At first glance, this might sound a bit negative, but that’s not how I mean it. Quite the opposite. The scent is synthetically fresh, has no development, and is absolutely unobtrusive, although I can perceive it on myself for 5-6 hours. For the price, I find it remarkable that the synthetic quality here is, in my opinion, better than that of some significantly more expensive counterparts. Freshness for me is really only in the sense of cotton. Here, in contrast to "T-Shirt | H&M," there are a few additional fragrance notes listed, none of which I can detect. No citrus either. Just cotton, nice freshly washed laundry that is still slightly damp. Well-groomed, pleasant. It works for me always. And I actually catch myself quite often with both scents, reaching for them on those indecisive days despite not having a small selection. Perhaps a short story about how this little "love" even came about. On that day, we were heading off on vacation, everything was packed, and I had even written a little list in the days before of which scents from my collection I wanted to decant and take with me. Well, then we realized 3 hours before departure that my ID was nowhere to be found. Of course, chaos ensued. Unfortunately, I didn’t get to decant my scents. But since I absolutely couldn’t go on vacation without a fragrance, I quickly threw the small bottle of T-Shirt into my suitcase; it didn’t take up much space, and I had brought it along out of curiosity to test it, thinking that for the price, it wouldn’t be a loss if it really got damaged or lost. So it happened that I ended up wearing it every day and for every occasion the following week, which surprisingly always suited me quite well. By the way, I received my marriage proposal during that vacation, so maybe that’s why I like the scent so much. :D Anyway, since then, it has been my personal value-for-money hit. And since they are virtually identical for me, this applies to both bottles.

With this fragrance, I have once again come across a very interesting "patchoulist." Not only was it composed for a fashion retail chain, but it is also surprisingly well-made. At first sniff (which one shouldn't judge too quickly!!), it smells like many others. If I let it unfold for a few minutes, things look quite different! It then presents itself with a slightly floral, earthy aroma. It seems rather smooth and pleasant, but what soon emerges is something slightly "fidgety." As if something is bubbling beneath the surface. And a kind of "hair" stands up, slightly scratchy, as if wearing a sheep wool sweater. Comforting and pleasant, but subtly rough and a bit "quirky." This remains the case for a long time until the previously almost imperceptible bubbling rises to the surface, intensifies, and a distant dark red glow comes closer. As if one were standing at a safe distance from a volcano that begins to spew slowly flowing lava. A mix of tension, fascination, and coziness envelops the "observers." This "base" lasts for hours and culminates in a warm earthy-woody afterglow at the very end! I find this "fashion house fragrance" very well done, and it outshines some more expensive ones ;-))

A subtle hint of lemon over a sweet and cashmeran cookie dough vanilla and toffee. It's a really enticing gourmand and doesn't verge anywhere near being sickly sweet, juvenile, or over the top. For someone who doesn't find gourmands as easily cloying as I do, I even think this could work year round, because the citrus and florals really balance it out and keep it from getting too food-like. One of the very few perfumes I've actually been complimented on; my coworker said I smelled "really good, like chocolate or something." :) So I'd say the sillage is pretty good! Longevity isn't bad, though the scent bubble definitely becomes personal after a little bit, I could still smell it on my sleeve a few days later. Absolutely worth the ten bucks! I'd be lying if I said I haven't considered buying another bottle for a backup, since it's such a cheapie.

I find this fragrance far more favourable than Love by Chloe EDP. The original made me sneeze with its bold sillage and sharp, almost fizzy powderiness. Thankfully, Love by Chloe Eau Florale has a much softer presence. It's really pretty and flowery on the skin, with the familiar powder note found in the original. The lilac has been replaced with sweet pea in this flanker, and the overall feeling is more fresh and airy. A subtle tea note in the drydown, provides an interesting green quality. It's what makes this fragrance so suitable for Spring and Summer. Love by Chloe Eau Florale has surpassed all my expectations. I enjoyed it enough to recommend it as a wedding day fragrance to one of my dear friends. Here's hoping that she'll use it for her special day. Fans of the original Love EDP will be pleased to know that Love by Chloe Eau Florale has much in common with its predecessor, however the softer aspects may find this fragrance some new fans. I know that I personally would choose this flanker over and above the EDP and the Intense version. Actually, make it my pick out of the entire Chloe range. The packaging is as always, very classy and chic. The lighter pink bottle is a nice touch. This flanker has my personal tick of approval. Very nicely done. Original review written: March 2013.

Love, Chloé didn’t stay long in my collection. I love the floral-powdery opening, the vintage touch, the immense, feminine aura of the fragrance that spreads gently yet firmly. I was so looking forward to the scent, but a harsh, intrusive, and unpleasant note destroys the delicate weave. I can’t even say exactly what it is. Probably the interplay of the heart notes themselves. Such a shame, because I really like wisteria. The neighboring house from my childhood was almost overgrown with the fragrant plant, so the scent of the blossoms puts me in a beautiful, nostalgic mood. Love, Chloé Intense, on the other hand, develops wonderfully on me, but in my opinion, it doesn’t really fit into summer. I see it more as a sensual winter fragrance. But since I don’t want to wait that long, I brought Eau Florale into the house. Thanks to dear Dusnatli. Hooked by Gruftikatze’s comment, which resonates quite well with my feelings. The opening presents itself in good Chloé fashion: fresh and soapy, weightless and airy. Very delicate powder appears, very pleasant and only slightly voluminous. Somehow, the pyramid seems sparse to me; there must be much more in it. I think I smell a transparent rose, including soft, powdery, honey-sweet pollen. Along with the finest, almost transparent scent fragments of my beloved wisteria. A very floral opening. Fresh like a March morning, infused with winter cold, while the first golden rays of sun already warm, feathery white veil clouds adorn the flawless blue sky. A cooling breeze sweeps through the young, light green foliage of the trees. The scent provides a peaceful and deep sense of well-being in a very pure form. Unspoiled and optimistic, bright and clear. It creates a really good mood and brings a smile to the lips, a rosy touch to the cheeks. At the latest, when the fragrance becomes increasingly lovely, softer, and the attribute "floral" is earned with flying colors, it has touched my heart. In a simple and honest way. It is dreamily beautiful; my nose keeps seeking out the scented spot. Although the fragrance is very powdery, it does not feel dusty or oppressive. It is a very fluffy and light powder. Not compact, but loose. Effortlessly, it swirls softly in pale pink and gentle. Airy and free. It reminds me of the dance of a ballerina, a gifted soloist. Ballet has always fascinated me. This body-focused aesthetic, the discipline, the beautiful figures. A grueling sport, associated with much pain and daily, hours-long training. Yet it ultimately looks so light, so effortless. So spontaneous and free, as if it were not choreography, but merely danced out of passion. So perfect and complete, graceful, elegant, and stylish. Then all the equipment, white, pink, light gray, satin, silk, tulle, lace, glitter, and feathers... that seems to be my world. Unfortunately, I never became a ballerina. My mother thought she had to protect me from it, as it ruins your whole body and is incredibly expensive. It’s quite possible she is right. But as ambitious and relentless as I can be, I would have certainly become the Swan Queen... Well, who knows what good it was that I wasn’t allowed to take that path. It’s also irrelevant, because with Eau Florale, I have found my white swan. One that accompanies me through the day with rustling tulle, theatrical makeup, and much romance and budding passion. The projection is above average but not too loud. For hours, I revel in luxurious floral powder, feminine and grown-up, without being matronly or stiff. A very beautiful progression: from fresh and soapy, through delicate-sweet and petal-soft to wonderfully powdery and fluffy-creamy. White musk is definitely part of it, of the clean and floral kind. Perhaps also a bit of cedarwood; the base definitely invites dreaming. A romantic and tender conclusion, vulnerable and lovable, yet far from being pale or weak. Just like the ambitious and tough soloists, who at first glance may seem very slender and almost fragile, they carry within them much strength and endurance, a strong will, drama, and a lot of feeling. For spring and summer, a fine little fragrance; in autumn, the big sister Intense will celebrate her debut. I am very happy to have discovered this powder dream for myself. Hopefully, more perfumes will succumb to its romantic charm; the fragrance is unjustly ranked in the back places.

For my mother's birthday, I gifted her the EdP of Love, Chloé. She loves it, but I find it too intense. I think it has a sharp note that pushes too much to the forefront. That's why I wanted to test Eau Florale. However, Love, Chloé Eau Florale is NOWHERE to be found in my hometown and surrounding area, which is why I bought the fragrance online, also on iparfumerie.at, "blind." I don't regret the purchase for a second. It was love at first sniff. I've never encountered such an incredibly beautiful, powdery, feminine scent before. So clean and fresh, definitely not synthetic. I also notice a light (clean!) floral note, quiet and in the background. I want this fragrance in my collection forever, a true treasure! Love, Chloe Eau Florale is long-lasting, with a medium sillage. I don't limit myself to a season, but I believe the scent is wearable at any time of the year. It has something soft and warm about it, without being musty. I've never been able to say this about a fragrance, but for this one, it is true for me (!) - The scent is perfect. The bottle is also beautiful and elegant. The soft pink color matches the feminine, delicate content, and the golden chain is an eye-catcher. (And ordering online was a very good idea, I want to add. Ordered Thursday evening, the fragrance arrived Monday morning. Additionally, I have the advantage of not being looked down upon, as is common in perfume shops due to my dark appearance. At 18, do I not have the right to be treated with the same respect as others? Am I not allowed to smell good just because I like to dress darker?) Conclusion: Feminine, pure fragrance with recognizability. Powdery and clean floral, suitable for any occasion.

My grandfather had a wonderful garden that was admired and marveled at by the neighbors. In the center was a magnificent rose roundel, consisting of noble polyantha roses, which I loved to circle around as a child. But in one corner of the elegant garden were the inevitable trash bins, which already troubled my child’s eye back then. So, I gave my grandfather a little bag of sweet pea seeds for his birthday to green over this "eyesore". He was very touched by my thoughtful gift and praised my ingenuity. And just a year later, the modest little bag had turned into a floral splendor that eagerly covered the unsightly trash bins. The yellow and white flowers looked at me like friendly eyes - and their scent was enchantingly beautiful. They competed with the proud roses and were in no way inferior to them in fragrance. Their twists and curls reminded me of my colorful gleaming pictures that I loved to admire on the garden bench. These little pictures, often depicting garden idylls, were treasured by me like a treasure. And this scene, where I sat lost in thought in front of the fragrant wall of sweet peas, is awakened in me again by eau Florale. Along with the spicy scent of mate tea that grandma had brewed. The powderiness of Eau Florale is like a soft focus that bathes the memory in a gentle light. A romantic floral fragrance full of poetry and a piece of childhood.

And I don't regret it ;) I was intrigued by the comments about Chloe Love Eau Florale and was tempted to buy the fragrance blind (thanks to the lovely Navuc) I'm not really the best at sniffing out individual components of a fragrance. For me, it’s more about "smells good" or "smells bad"... maybe also: powdery, green, woody, warm, floral, herbal, sticky, sweet, etc. I'm also not a fantastic storyteller like some others here in the forum whose stories about a fragrance are quite good ;) Okay... enough blah blah: I really like the scent. Fine and lightly powdery, delicate and floral, but not sharp or headache-inducing. Not a crazy floral scent that overwhelms you, and not cloying or old, but fresh and fragrant. And very pleasant. I'm glad that it now resides with me ;)

In recent months, I have learned to love Chloé. No other perfume is as soft, as powdery, and still has that touch of fluttering flowers. I am in love - completely. - Scent Comparison - The Chloé Love Eau de Parfum is heavier. Heavy not in the sense of oppressive, but heavy in the sense of intense.

I have to say that no Chloè has convinced me so far, and I didn't even want to test it at first, but the powdery notes lured me in. Finding it was not so easy; most online shops didn't have it, or didn't have the desired size, or something else. The perfumery here locally didn't even know that this perfume exists and couldn't order it either.

For winter, I really liked the Intense version of Love Chloé - and I liked it a lot! Now, due to the reviews from my predecessors, I became curious about this version and ordered it "blind" online as well... ...and I am absolutely thrilled!!!

This fragrance is a thick, oily tropical floral with a hint of coconut and an aquatic accord. It evokes the scent of Monoi Tiki Tahiti Tiare oil, created using the traditional Polynesian method of macerating tiare flowers in oil to extract their fragrance. The scent is reminiscent of lotion and sun tanning oil, with a touch of aquatic melon. The melon note is slightly sweet. Tiare is the main/dominant note. This fragrance is a great alternative to Guerlain Terracotta Le Parfum and also brings to mind Phloria by PHLUR. The scent of warm skin covered in monoi oil, conjuring the image of a morning walk on Waikiki Beach. While it doesn't have great longevity, it projects well while it lasts.
Damn sweet, striking, sticky ;-) Should only be worn by ladies. I find that the scent has a certain similarity to Daim Blond by Serge Lutens.

I often struggle with Jasmine forward fragrances as they can sometimes turn dirty on me or be too heady, but I have been on a hunt to test different ones and find one that works for me. Nomade Jasmin Naturel Intense works for me probably better than most other jasmine forward fragrances I have tried and that's partly because I feel like despite Jasmine being in the name, it's not 100% a jasmine perfume. Firstly kudos to Chloe for releasing a designer fragrance that to my nose feels unique. Chloe moreover seems to have been able to perfectly capture the wanderlust and feeling of a nomadic heart within a bottle. This really triggered the recognition of something familiar in me that was almost startling the first time I smelled it. The first time I smelled it in store, I thought, "This reminds me of something I used to smell all the time but haven't smelled in years. What is it?" The more I have worn it, I realized that it smells like Colorado horse pastures. Not in a gross way and there isn't anything animalic to be found here. But this is a fragrance that conjures imagery for me nonetheless. It's a warm fall afternoon, the sun is shining down, the Rocky mountains are off in the distance. I am eating date bread in wide open brush pastures, a slight waft of fresh hay and horses grazing nearby is in the breeze -- but in the most pleasing way. Life is peaceful and there's a feeling of freedom in the knowledge that you can go anywhere. IYKYK. I was a horsegirl in my teen years and there is something in this perfume that I just find transportive back to that time. (I'm being dramatic I am aware, but this fragrance is proving to speak to me more than I expected.) Make no mistake though, this isn't a childish perfume, it's a grown up scent that also isn't too mature. I see this on women 20-40s age range, but really anyone could wear it. Jasmin Naturel is also not a heavy, cloying, indolic perfume in my experience. It's really quite beautiful actually and I struggle to describe it note by note and if it wasn't clear can only really explain it emotionally. I don't see Sage listed as a note, but I feel like I detect a bit of it here or perhaps it is the patchouli coming through. This isn't a dirty patchouli by any means, but it is earthy.I also know the original Nomade had oakmoss but I don't see that here. Still maybe that is an unlisted note that still helps give that earthy vibe. The dates, vanilla and sandalwood add a sweet, soft and creamy undertone. The Jasmine provides some brightness and freshness, but it's really just a well blended scent. Wonderful fall scent that's highly versatile. It can be casual, formal, office appropriate, day to night. We stan a versatile fragrance and I very much could see this being someone's signature scent. After trying in store for a day I bought a 30 ml bottle for testing and when I've used it up I think this may be full bottle worthy. Chloe really knocked this one out of the park.

I love the scent of jasmine. That’s why I also have a lush jasmine bush in my garden that delights me year after year with its white flowers and intense fragrance. It is called Snowstorm because of its abundance of white blossoms. So far, the color pink has been predominant in my garden, as the almond tree is blooming so eagerly. But it only has a delicate scent. I still have to wait for the Snowstorm. Nomade Jasmin intense comes in very handy, as it shortens the waiting time for my jasmine bush. In Nomade, the floral scent is paired with fruity pear, rounded off by soft date and sweet vanilla. Sandalwood feels woody and creamy, and embraces Nomade intimately. Not only jasmine fans will enjoy it, as it also conveys extravagance and elegance. Still, I welcome my Snowstorm in the garden.

Oh damn. At some point at work, I served a customer who smelled unbelievably good. A bit fruity, clean, subtle & super feminine. And with an amazing sillage. When I asked her what she was wearing, she mentioned Nomade Eau de Toilette . Wow - what a fantastic scent I had never encountered before. When I was expecting my order of two new fragrances today, there was a sample of the new Nomade Jasmin Naturel Intense included. Ohhhh was I excited, as I did not expect that. A small (just good) spray on my wrist & then I dared: For heaven's sake. What is this? I can't sugarcoat it, but in my opinion, it's absolutely not okay. It's so overpowering & unpleasant. I feel like I'm in the Neustadt, an alternative district, surrounded by lots of esoteric people who run shops where you can buy colorful scarves, wooden elephants & incense sticks. Please don't get me wrong, I do walk through there sometimes, it's all good. But these smells give me unbelievable headaches & make me feel a bit nauseous. After smelling Nomade Jasmin Naturel Intense , I feel like I've had to walk several rounds through such shops. And then I’m supposed to meditate for another 5 hours. I couldn't even stand it as incense sticks for the bathroom. The scent is so exaggeratedly spicy, oriental, piercing & exhausting. I think the sillage & longevity are good, at least I had to literally scrub the scent off. But unfortunately, I find it quite dreadful. Really a shame, but that's just how it is. For that, the regular Nomade Eau de Toilette really blows me away.

As a second review, I almost hesitate to write. Especially since my nose is still in the elementary school of scents. So far, it is neither particularly refined, nor can I distinguish or name individual fragrances. But still, I want to support it. Nomade Jasmin Naturel Intense is my latest addition. Bought a bit too quickly, but my hands couldn't hold any more test strips and my forearms and hands were all occupied. Since Jasmin Naturel Intense was the most dominant and screamed the loudest, it became the one. Admittedly, freshly applied, it is very intensely oriental. Patchouli and sandalwood do a great job here. However, if you have the latest creation, Nomade Nuit d'Egypte Eau de Parfum, on the other arm, you don't notice it at first. Nomade Chloe edP on the back of the hand is hardly noticeable anymore. It indulges heavily and intensely in the white flowers and becomes lighter after a few hours, but remains sweetish. Perhaps the date supports the vanilla.

First of all: I perceive this fragrance as fundamentally very different from how others perceive it; I do not think it is a very heavy scent. She is so sweet and innocent, her smile like fresh jasmine. There she stands with open sandalwood hair in a vanilla-colored, unpretentiously elegant silk dress in front of the mirror. Clean, yet somehow romantic, and everything about her is somehow beige, gold, cream, and vanilla. Today she wants to be wild! Leopard pumps on! She shakes her shiny flowing mane and grins mischievously behind a strand of hair at her reflection in the mirror...uh...hm...maybe not soooo wild after all! She takes off the pumps again. She arranges her hair and combs it into a smooth ponytail. Sweet as a date, she stands there. Pear date caramel cream. Only in her smile does a hint of cheeky patchouli sometimes flash through...she is well-behaved, innocent, and charming...with that certain something that only still waters possess. Golden, elegant, unpretentious fragrance with a touch of woody extravagance.

Chloe Intense, is a stronger yet not so different version of the original Chloe. If I had to describe the scent, Chloe Intense is an old-fashioned bar of rose scented soap or that refreshing and homely smell of freshly washed linen. This is a rose scent that has been emulated and ultimately popular for many years. Despite its very feminine and somewhat classic appeal, Chloe Intense cannot seem to capture me or make me fall in love with it. It has a strange fizzy quality in the opening that actually makes me sneeze. After that momentary allergy, I become almost anosmic to this fragrance. An hour later, once settled, I can smell the prominent soapy rose which doesn't develop much further from this. Chloe Intense is a pretty, one-sided fragrance, that appears to be too conservative and too lady-like for my personal tastes. I did, however enjoy wearing this fragrance for the duration that it lasted, which was well over six hours. I don't think I'll be re-visiting this one again though.

This is the most intense variant among the Chloe fragrances, but that doesn't necessarily make it the best, as it is purely a matter of personal taste. There are three variants: the delicate and fresh EdT, the warm and powdery EdP, and the peppery and slightly oriental Intense. These three variants reflect the maturity of the rose bloom, which is the central theme at Chloe. It goes without saying that Intense represents the final stage of the rose bloom with maximum intense fragrance aura. While the pepper is quite dominant at the beginning and especially close to the skin, the scent develops into an incredibly deep-rosy fragrance with a bit of distance. This scent is quite true to nature, but due to the monoculture rose imports today, it is rarely found anymore, except perhaps in a special rose garden where fragrant roses are cultivated. Caution, a rose is not just a rose. This one is really something for power women who love to be obviously perfumed. For those who prefer a subtle floral scent, I recommend the truly light, delicate, and yet rosy EdT. Overall, Chloe Intense is rosy, peppery, woody, and oriental. It does not have the stuffy powderiness of the EdP, as the pepper knows how to prevent that. My favorite remains the EdT in first place and the EdP in second. Intense is excellent, but alongside its other sisters, for me, it is only the bronze medal winner because it is personally a bit too intense for me, but that doesn't make it any less good :-) while the EdT smells more like white roses, the EdP like pink roses, Intense most closely resembles deep red roses. I need to say a few words about the bottle. I found it very unattractive until now that the metal parts tarnish no matter where you store the bottle. This patina can be reduced by wiping it away, but it always returns and gives the bottle an undesired antique touch. Now I have learned that this is intentional, as these metal parts are plated/coated with real silver, so a patina is desired. Furthermore, the bottle designer was inspired by a Chloe blouse in pleated style, which can now be beautifully recognized on the bottle. Chloe must be tested; for me, it is one of the best perfume lines with a consistent theme that has ever existed!

We met by chance, as the bottle appealed to me very much. A small spritz on my wrist (even though I was looking for Estée Lauder's Sensuous) and shortly after, I think that my good friend Lene must be nearby! I smell my wrist and instantly know what Lene uses in her daily life - at least it came back to me, just that my love uses the EdP version without "intense." On me, this Chloé smells almost identical and I am absolutely thrilled. Grandma has also had the chance to try it, where the rose becomes more prominent for her and gets very warm. That was the effect I wanted to avoid, as I don't like those sweet rosy scents on my skin. They always grab me by the throat, but I like it on Grandma. Fortunately, Chloé Intense develops surprisingly cool on my skin, which makes it a welcome change from my cozy scents. It becomes soapy and gives me the impression of having bathed everything in rose detergent, without being intrusive. I have rarely felt so fresh and cheerful! Previously, I had already been eyeing Jil Sander's "Eve" and "Love, Chloé" in the EdP version, but they were too powdery for me, and as a walking fabric softener, I really don't want to come across that way to my surroundings. The perfume in the Intense version gives me that clean scent I have long desired, and I would agree with anyone who calls this scent "Grandma's rose soap," but for me, this soap piece belongs to the somewhat more qualitative ones, wrapped in the finest silk paper, sealed with a beautiful sticker, nestled in a nostalgically printed box, and adorned with elegant satin ribbon. A gift! Just like Lene, who visits me from time to time (though far too rarely) and enchants me with her scent. What I also like is the slightly smoky sandalwood touch and the tonka bean that sensually lingers until the next (!) day. However, I don't know how pink pepper smells, only that I enjoy wallowing in this one "rose soap." Grandma and I are just good buddies.

I didn’t pay much attention to rose scents during the first half of my life. I’m increasingly noticing that my fragrance preferences have fundamentally changed. This is probably related to getting older and the fact that “ladies” often only start to appreciate classic rose water at a certain age. It’s a pity that such a classic and ethereal essence of rose is attributed to a “grandmother.” I still have many squeaky sweet scents in my closet, but my recent purchases, with a couple of exceptions, no longer belong to that category. Now they lean more towards powerful amber-patchouli or floral-woody-musk scents that are fresh, powdery, aldehydic, and elegant. And that is also Chloe Intense. The fragrance is monothematic and exclusively revolves around the rose. Pink pepper gracefully accompanies it at the opening and throughout the development without being sharp, and the sandalwood is very subtle. This is the first fragrance I know that contains tonka bean, but it only quietly resides within. I don’t detect any trace of tonka, just a minimal warmth, and I find it overall a bit rounder in the base than Chloe. It is a very feminine, elegant, noble, and fresh rose scent, and as has already been mentioned here, a well-groomed clean scent. I really like it.

"A Rose" Some say love it is a river that drowns the tender reed Some say love it is a razer that leaves your soul to bleed Some say love it is a hunger an endless aching need I say love it is a flower and you it's only seed It's the heart afraid of breaking that never learns to dance It's the dream afraid of wakin that never takes the chance It's the one who won't be taken who cannot seem to give and the soul afraid of dying that never learns to live When the night has been too lonely and the road has been too long and you think that love is only for the lucky and the strong Just remember in the winter far beneath the bitter snows lies the seed that with the sun's love in the spring becomes the rose I love this song by Bette Midler. When I first got to sniff Chloe Intense, this song immediately came to mind. It is melancholic, yet very powerful. It envelops you maternally, offering wise life lessons and advice along the way. No matter how hopeless a situation may seem - one should never give up. From the small seed grows the proud rose - one should not underestimate the strengths that lie within - they just need to be lovingly coaxed out. The darkest of all the Chloe sisters is very warm and expressive, yet romantic with the right dose of rose that I love so much. For me, it is an absolute dream.

A very ambivalent scent, this Chloe Intense. On one hand, it smells very sensitive, almost graceful, like a noble wedding where the couple has just come out of the church and is being showered with roses.
My favorite perfume since 2009. Now they have decided it is no longer good and it has simply been taken off the market. I can't believe it! Please bring it back!!!!!!

I have known the scent of Chloé from the very beginning. One of my daughters has repurchased it twice; she loves it. For me, it was just too weak, although I really liked the cleanliness of this little water. I was very happy when the Intense version came out. For me, it’s just right; the scent lasts all day and you really feel good wearing it.

To begin with, I would like to apologize to the ladies for the forthcoming harsh and ignorant words of a rough man who knows nothing about intrusive, sweet rose scents. To me, it smells like Elfriede Müller on a Sunday afternoon in front of the souvenir shop at Porta Westfalica. So, go ahead and hit me.

I will now sit down. I’m really sorry, apparently Chloe Intense has many fans. I would love to be one of them. I really tried. I am a fan of Love, Chloe and I find Chloe at least quite nice, although not a big hit. So I was excited when I found a sample of this one while sifting through my samples. I usually like Intense fragrances.

I first tried Nomade in the EDP version and immediately knew two things: I had to have this fragrance, and I could not handle the EDP. Once I discovered that the EDT version existed and had almost identical notes, I moved forward with a FB purchase without even testing it out. A lot of times the EDT and EDP don’t have much in common with each other, but with this one I had faith, and my bet paid off. Nomade EDT is nearly identical to the EDP from start to finish. I can’t really detect the lychee in the top note. I’ve seen this described as a fruity scent but I can’t say I agree - it is much more floral than fruity.
