The dry down, however, leaves an addictive scent that lingers for a full 24 hours on skin and is truly the reason I love this perfume. If I could skip the first few hours of wear and solely capture the dry down alone, I would. It’s slightly sweet and woody. While Nomade EDT is much lighter compared to the EDP, this is still a strong fragrance. It’s a single-sprayer for me and one I only reach for in cool/cold weather.

I always find it fascinating when I read the statements and reviews here about how extremely different fragrances are perceived or how they develop individually on the skin. First, I must mention that I actually do not like powdery, feminine scents at all. My skin tends to turn most fragrances sweet, and I hate vanilla. Therefore, I prefer green to unisex perfumes, but I really wanted to own a "noble" lady... but not a grande dame, rather a 40-year-old Grace Kelly. Since "Nomade" is one of my favorites, I didn't want to leave Rossana's review, which I believe does not do justice to the fragrance, hanging in the air :) - because my perception of this EdT is really completely the opposite: @HappySunny compared it to an extremely expensive/noble body lotion, and that was also one of my first associations. Lychee or fruity is never present for me, freesia (and I would even say soft warm suede - which is not listed in the pyramid) is clearly noticeable and lasts forever. And then there's the oak moss. This is by definition not a real chypre, maybe the little cousin, and that's a good thing because it lacks the old-fashioned, heavy quality that has kept me away from most chypres so far. I could have sworn it has at least a bit of musk in the base, but apparently it doesn't, strange... "Nomade" is not for hot days; it overwhelms me then. In the evening, rather in the cooler seasons or when I simply have the need for an extra portion of feminine white-beige cashmere-cuddle-luxury, I reach for it. I also find it hard to understand the comments about poor longevity. It lasts forever! And it needs to be dosed carefully! I have even treated myself to the body lotion, and the combination lasts 12h+ (an additional thumbs up for the existence of this combo). I tested both the EdP and the EdT, as my little luxury ego wanted to indulge itself. I do not like the EdP at all, and only thanks to the good persuasion of the saleswoman at my trusted perfumery did I give the EdT a chance. The EdT is less fruity/sweet/floral; it does not overwhelm me like the EdP. So definitely try both and see which one you prefer. I find the price top due to its great performance, certainly not a drugstore bargain, but it is often on sale, and you don't have to sell your left kidney to afford it. Oh yes - there is a 30ml version, a size that I find incredibly great and that is unfortunately only available rarely. The bottle fits: simple, noble, pleasing to the overall concept (and hey, I like the leather strap or the small ring on the cap, it feels so beautifully soft).

Quite boring, little character. A scent for daily wear, so as not to stand out. Very fleeting, light, and unobtrusive. One forgets it quickly. Too bad, the bottle is quite pretty, the little leather strap is nice as decoration, but also unnecessary. Rating 4.

H&M launched an insane number of new fragrances in 2018. That something decent can come out of it is proven quite successfully by Zara for several years now. So, it's definitely interesting. And when a fragrance has something to do with chocolate, I obviously have to give it a sniff. My fragrance description for Choc is rather brief. It simply smells, who would have guessed, like - chocolate! Nothing more and nothing less, just pure dark chocolate. But the good kind, with a high cocoa content. Delicious, warm, creamy. The scent development is absolutely linear. Longevity and sillage are not outstanding, but perfectly fine, especially for the price. And the similarity I mentioned in the title with Montale's Chocolate Greedy? A bit of clickbait. Yes, the two fragrances do indeed go in a very similar direction. No, Chocolate Greedy cannot pack its bags. But: If you just want a great chocolate scent and are willing to make compromises on the orange note, the bottle design, and longevity, Choc is absolutely satisfying. For that, it is also significantly more affordable. So, from my side, it's a definite recommendation! And to quickly throw in another chocolate scent: I find that Choc is also very similar to La Perla's Dark Extacy, even a bit more similar than it is to Chocolate Greedy. And since Dark Extacy is known to be discontinued, Choc can certainly be considered as an alternative. Chocolate fragrance lovers should definitely grab this one!

When I read the pyramid of Fleur de Parfum, I expected a full romantic rose scent, with a touch of nostalgia. But this rose that awaits me here is white and slightly citrusy, and it unmistakably reminds me of my radiant Snow White bush in the garden. Its aroma is refreshingly lively, almost sassy, and not as dreamy as that of the old English Austin roses. The vervain further emphasizes the fresh - green impression without overshadowing the rose. The cherry blossom softens the slightly prickly start and merges delicately with the almond. However, the scent does not turn into a marzipan note. A vibrant, floral morning scent that lively guides you into the day. I like its casually elegant dynamism. But reapplying is necessary, as Fleur is somewhat fleeting. I don't mind doing that.

Hm… if I write "fabric softener" in my title, it might well scare some people off right from the start, because there are certainly perfumes (and also parfumos) that don’t like soap and prefer to be little dirt birds :D Well, a fabric softener is not soap, but the term does imply something synthetic, which can also be off-putting for some. And it's okay if you're not into certain things, but I think Fleur de Parfum is a scent that isn’t all that bad and could at least be worth a try. The scent: The scent starts with a slightly powdery (and somewhat synthetic) verbena note, which could be better described as citrusy fresh lemon balm or verbena, thus also having a slightly bitter edge. Then you smell roses. These are light and also smell a bit artificial, but that’s not a problem, as it smells more like nice fabric softener with "rose aroma." However, the scent can occasionally come off as biting, which is something that unfortunately comes and goes and occasionally disrupts the scent progression. Even late in the base, I mainly smell these softened roses and still the lemon balm. I can’t find any almonds at all… After about six hours, however, the scent only smells average, as the fabric softener note with the roses is almost gone and the scent only smells of lemon balm. The sillage and longevity: The projection is above average. At first, you can hardly smell anything, but then the projection suddenly unfolds, so you could even make the mistake of overapplying. But that doesn’t matter at all, as it calms down a bit later on. Overall, the projection keeps decreasing. The longevity is only four to five hours. Even though you can still smell the scent for a few hours after this time, I don’t count that as usual, because you would really have to press your nose against the sprayed area to smell anything. The bottle: This bottle also has the basic shape of most Chloé bottles, which, with a bit of imagination, look like ancient temples with columns. The chrome upper part contains the brand name, the fragrance liquid is light pink, and as always, there’s a nice bow at the neck. All in all, a very nicely made bottle. Hmm…. somehow I’m currently in a drugstore. Yes, that’s right, drugstore, not perfumery. Because, as we all know, you can smell everything (especially you parfumos and parfumos should know this!). And besides the scents themselves or things like scented candles (yeeah, Yankee Candles, there should soon be Halloween specials again :D), you often smell shower gels, shampoos, and indeed fabric softeners. And that’s exactly what this scent reminded me of, as it smells very much like nice rose fabric softener alongside the lemon balm. And even though the scent itself isn’t very extraordinary, it should appeal reasonably well to those who enjoy these clean notes. However, the slightly pungent sour scent is a bit bothersome, which unfortunately brings the fragrance down. Without this annoying note, the scent would have been even nicer, which one could consider for spring and summer when looking for something nice for the day or leisure (as it’s unfortunately a bit too weak and short-lived for going out). If the synthetic aspect doesn’t bother you too much, you might want to check out this scent. Unless, of course, you’re not into that clean feeling and, as I mentioned earlier, prefer to be a little dirt bird :D

I'm back. I'm buying Chloé Absolu blind. And why? Because I read the statements and comments that describe it as much more beautiful than the original. And because it’s limited and discontinued. Immediately, I fall into the familiar Raff and hamster mode. Normally, I don't like Chloé at all. Way too soapy and sharp, even the flankers. And in general, I prefer to admire roses in a vase. But I did it anyway. Just ordered it and let myself be surprised. And you won’t believe it: it is actually a little bit soapy. But I like it! It doesn’t completely blow me away, but that’s okay. I actually find it much more beautiful than the original. Softer and rounder, nothing jabs or bites, not even the soap. Classic, well-groomed, clean, and pure. A fragrance for many occasions, although many people probably know it. The main theme here is also the rose, which probably contributes to the slight soapiness. And although I am very sensitive to soapiness in fragrances, I find it just pleasant in this scent. Then it becomes soft, I think due to the vanilla, which is only delicately dosed and makes the fragrance beautifully rounded. It’s not sweet, but it radiates a certain warmth. The little bottle is also pretty to look at. Chloé Absolu is always wearable, a classic go-to that doesn’t clash anywhere. Whether in the office, at the doctor’s, at family gatherings, in a restaurant, or at a funeral: with this fragrance, you won’t stand out unpleasantly anywhere. But that’s probably exactly what might annoy some: little development, pleasing, classic, nice, and clean, pearl necklace and twinset. I don’t care. Sometimes a woman just needs exactly such fragrances.

First of all: long intro full of uninteresting life story! Here it goes: As a teenager, I wore "Chloé (eau de parfum)" and didn't like it. Tempted by a pretty, oversized, and no less impressive, far too perfect face on a rose gold advertisement and a harried saleswoman who rightly suspected a lost, directionless person like me to be an easy target, I bought this bottle without much hesitation from my hard-earned Christmas money. I wore it extensively, regularly, almost obsessively, always carrying the perfect face in my mind, full of hope to transfer some of that beauty onto my lackluster appearance, perhaps to convince the right man for life that I was a top candidate. But we never really matched. And it worked, as one might suspect, only in my head. Several years have passed, the time for searching for a partner is over (thankfully! Hopefully?), and Chloé became a forgotten relic of another time in my life. Until I found a sample of this fragrance here. It had sneaked into my collection despite being on the watchlist and was already threatening to lead an unnoticed existence until I read more closely. "Absolu" ah... probably like the original, just with a lot more volume. Or like so many Absolues, Intenses, extraits, and whatever else is out there, just throw in vanilla and tuberose, shake vigorously, and re-market. Nevertheless, I tested the sample. Just like that. And I was transported back to another time. Uncertain, full of overwhelming emotions but also full of passion. And like me, Chloé has grown up. The Absolu presents itself clearly but not strictly, minimalist but not overly structured, warm but not lulling. Like a woman who has simply let go of much that she long believed she needed. The Chloé DNA, that typical strict rose, shines through clearly and doesn't lose itself in the fragrance, yet the vanilla softens it right from the start, rounds off the edges, tames the thorns, and gently accompanies it to a grounded, unspiced, and soft base. Don't get me wrong: the fragrance is still clean, it fits perfectly in a dentist's office, an office, or a car dealership. It's just that it's no longer the pretty lady with a center part, pressed blouse, and white nails at the reception; she's more like the warm, friendly, and well-groomed woman from administration, the one everyone likes to have around, who always has an open ear and occasionally brings the best cookies for everyone. But one doesn't really know much about her life, as she always remains professional and clear. I find it dreamy. And it's the first fragrance in my life for which I will probably get a bunker.

In my opinion, the absolute is more mature and simpler in structure than the EDP. Clean, classic & unobtrusive. This is what I understand by rose! Somehow, the composition is kept simple and has thus gained. It is modern, minimalist but not necessarily exciting, which is also okay. I love the scent of fresh roses. Often, I have been disappointed by rose fragrances because I secretly expected the smell of my grandmother's roses in the garden. They smell regal. Even after hot summer days or days of continuous rain, I always perceive the scent as delicately subtle and pure. Unfortunately, most rose perfumes smell to me just synthetic and stuffy or start to smell almost 'modern' on my skin (if this makes sense)... I don't like it when too many floral components are crammed together because the rose doesn't need that at all. It simply gets lost.. Despite the vanilla, this one is by no means sticky, just appetizingly pure and fresh. Patchouli grounds the fine roses here, and they stay comfortable. With this scent, I feel at ease in a room full of unfamiliar people; it is beautifully discreet and stays close to the skin. It is definitely a good choice for the office. On the skin, the scent only changes slightly over time, perhaps becoming a bit creamier and finer. Unfortunately, the longevity is disappointing, an estimated 5-6 hours before it completely disappears on me. I love it nonetheless. My thoughts when I first smelled it on my skin were similar to those I had with Rose d'Arabie by Armani Privé (for me, the best rose scent). I thought: 'Wow! Yes! Clearly, this is it, I’ll take it!'... This is how I want to smell when I hug someone. Definitely test it if you are looking for clean scents and like them.

When I first saw this 2024 fragrance line from H&M, I was immediately more than thrilled. Such great, high-quality looking bottles, and I find all the names very appealing. Finally something new. Fortunately, the fragrances themselves are not only inspired by designer and drugstore perfumes, but also draw some inspiration from niche scents. This little gem is no exception: Adventure Seeker is apparently inspired by Gris Charnel, and it actually gives me vibes of that, especially in the top notes. The fragrance starts off pleasantly spicy-sweet-peppery, and then becomes creamier and milkier in the dry down, feeling really well-groomed and lactonic. It retains its sweetness, but gradually loses the spiciness from the beginning. In terms of performance, the perfume leaves something to be desired, as it quickly becomes very close to the skin, but what can you expect from a fragrance for under 10 euros? Just reapply. Let's go!

This scent seems to be a little divisive? it's easy, it's cute, it's inoffensive and hard to spray too much, but scent has to deliver on fantasy and with so many scents this one might be passed over for more exciting "stories". But what I get from this fragrance is not just the clean creaminess of the base that I get whiffs of throughout a lazy summer day, or the deep breaths to get the spicier notes which can almost become meditative in any scent, but for me it reminds me of those weird little ambient cd's I saw in health stores in the 2000s (like Anugama or something). It's vaguely oriental in its suggestion of an "exotic" place, and hardly delivers on that front, but when you see it for what it is, an enjoyable piece of music or a truly delicious scent, you can see the beauty in that too. The marketing does this scent no good, so try to ignore it. When I wear this perfume I can hear a small stream, water clattering against rocks and I'm burning a little bit in the sun, and I have nowhere to be and nothing to do. To me this scent is very calming, that's why it's a perfect "summer day scent" to me. Yeah, this smells really good to me! It's creamy and smooth without being edible, it lasts a long time on me (~8-10 hours), when it's hot it becomes kind of coconut/banana like, and I like that I can disappear into my wrist when I smell it and I can hear that stupid Anugama cd and the nostalgia of that does bring me a lot of joy.

I purchased this without sampling, wasn’t really sure what to expect as this flanker seems to be getting some mixed reviews. Well, it arrived today and upon first sniff, I fell in love. It is so beautiful and classy. I actually like this better than Nomade Nuit d’Egypte, which I also have. This Lumiere flanker is honestly not really similar to Nuit, this is a light, fresh, kinda aquatic, elegant jasmine with some noticeable green notes. (Whereas Nuit is more of a sweet, vaguely spicy orange blossom and vanilla.) Lumiere apparently has the same “spice” backbone as Nuit d’Egypte but I’m not really picking up on it. This will be a perfect spring/summer daytime fragrance.

I really like Nuit d’Egypte, and I can sense the same base here - a sweet, balsamic balm that I find very appealing. But there’s also a clear aquatic touch and a fresher jasmine, which make this fragrance better suited for warm weather (although I wouldn't mind wearing it all year round). So Lumière d’Egypte is a creamy, sweet oriental balm with a fresh edge. I see it’s not very popular, but personally, I really like it - a warm breeze along the banks of the Nile.

Ancient Egypt themed party at an indoor kiddie pool. Plastic lilypads floating on chlorinated water. Soft drinks – cold and fresh, yet syrupy sweet. Playing pretend. Having fun. Going to bed and smelling newly changed sheets. The scent of fabric softener – synthetic and a bit harsh, but it transports you further into fantasy nonetheless as you drift off to sleep. Much fresher than other Nomads. Childish. Lovable. The 12-year-old me would die for it. But then (about an hour into the experience) blue lotus starts fizzling out. Sandalwood becomes more visible – fresh, almost... unripe in a way? Pleasantly resinous beneath. It's pretty, like a summer evening coming to an end. And melancholic, like growing up. Another hour and its youth comes to an end. And what's left suddenly smells like pickles. Not in a figurative sense. Literal honey and vinegar pickles. And don't get me wrong, it's not too bad. I personally really like pickles. But it's not what I'm looking for in a perfume. Then again, I suppose that's adulthood for you, lol. Over the next few hours it slowly gets softer and eventually withers away. Fun and memorable as a one time experience! Wouldn't wear it again.

Those familiar with the Nomade line will discover a new facet here. Nomade Lumière d’Égypte remains true to the signature style: warm, elegant, and natural - but it features a surprising aquatic opening that makes it airier and fresher than its predecessors. While the OG Nomade Eau de Parfum has a more earthy presence with its oakmoss-plum combination and Nomade Absolu de Parfum sets spicier accents with wood and leather, Nomade Lumière d’Égypte is undoubtedly the subtlest and softest variant in the line. Not loud, but with just the right balance. After the fresh start, a subtle, warm jasmine-wood note follows, adding a creamy, slightly floral depth without being intrusive. Sillage? Close to the body. Longevity? Typical for Chloé, up to 6 hours. So it’s a fragrance that is present but not screaming. Conclusion: This scent is perfect for the office or for anyone who loves understatement.

Not a typical wow fragrance that immediately overshadows everything, but rather one that stands out with its calm, elegant nature. Right after spraying, you feel a light freshness, a bit aquatic, a hint of lotus - it reminds me of morning dew somewhere far away, perhaps actually in Egypt. Then it slowly becomes warmer, more floral, with jasmine, but never too sweet or heavy.

Here we have a woody, spicy candidate. This special lotus note, which dominates the opening like in Rituals Karma, is not for everyone. A special sweetness, a bit tea-like. In the middle, the fragrance develops into an Egyptian potion through myrrh, cinnamon, and jasmine. Those who appreciate woody, fresh candidates will find this one satisfying.

Last week, I acquired a beautiful fragrance by Cécilie Motton. Chloé Orchidée de Minuit touched me, and I found the composition of this perfume to be above average. Unfortunately, this fragrance Nomade Lumière d’Égypte by Céline Motton leaves me cold. After Nomade Nuit d'Égypte, I was looking forward to this scent.

This is not what i thought it would be, but in a positive way. It's very woody and creamy, really lovely. It sits like a soft veil around you, a comfortable cozy scent. I don't detect any of the famous Chloe rose in it, which for me is a good thing. It was a surprise and i glad that i blind bought it and have it in my small collection.

A lovely start! Rosy, with a tangy bergamot note that doesn't feel citrusy – just refreshing and green. Reminds me of Schweppes – sparkling, fizzy. You know there's a ton of sugar in it, like with every other soda, but once you taste it – it's sour and bitter. Fresh. Delicious. Has soft sillage at first, but in about ~1 hour settles close to the skin. Slowly loses the fizziness, but remains pleasantly green. Rosy woods. Simple, but elegant. In another hour all that's left is just soft creamy woods; and in one more – just your own slightly sweet skin. Still lovely, even if it's not much of anything. It's good, but it also firmly sits in the category of girly designer perfumes for girly girls – the ones you sniff and immediately know their main job is to make the wearer smell even more feminine. I'm not its target audience. I already know I'm a woman, I don't need more of that, thank you. But out of all woman-forward perfumes I've encountered – Rose Naturelle Intense is the best one I've tried so far, I think. If someone kidnapped me and forced me to wear something femininity-enhancing, I'd choose this one.

Wow, what a great scent. I approached the test without much expectation. Honestly - anyone who knows the classic Chloé (2007) Eau de Parfum knows that you get something nice here. That’s it. Nothing world-changing. Not a mega scent. Just nice. You can wear it - but you don’t have to. And that’s exactly the expectation I had when I approached the test. My first thought: “Wait wait - you’re a Chloe? No way!” It was so completely different than expected. At first, it’s very lightly floral and slightly citrusy, relatively unsweet. After a few minutes, a beautiful, very soft velvety sandalwood scent comes in. The scent develops with the skin into a beautiful creamy fragrance. Milky - creamy - woody. Minimal sweetness. Not a typical Chloe floral water. The typical Chloe DNA comes through very lightly. What a wonderfully refined scent. It slightly reminds me of Santal 33 Eau de Parfum and "Blanche Bête - Eau de Peau | Liquides Imaginaires". I think this is a very successful and lovely scent. Even if you can’t relate to the typical Chloe, look forward to testing this one.

It's been a long time since I last felt the strong urge to have a new fragrance as my companion. Not too heavy, fresh but also floral/rosy with a touch of uniqueness. My new little scent should fulfill exactly that. The search began. I stopped at Chanel Chance eau Tendre: fresh, white floral - innocent! A bit further on, then Gucci Bloom: heavy, warm, and too opulent for me in everyday life. So I moved on to Narciso Rodriguez Musc Noir Rose: oriental, sweet-rosy - more of an evening scent. I had almost given up hope when Chloé Rose Naturelle Intense caught my eye. I was shockingly in love from the very first moment. It’s hard to describe this fragrance and do it justice in my eyes! It is, in one word: beautiful! But also graceful. At first, very floral with a hint of green. A light sweetness slowly emerges and finds its end in a light and very pleasant woodiness. But by no means a heavy or oriental woodiness; a slight creamy note also blends in. For me, the scent is the perfect everyday fragrance, but it can also be worn in the evening or on special occasions. I wouldn’t necessarily assign an age to the fragrance. For me, it’s a timeless scent. Those who don’t like roses will find little joy in this fragrance. I immediately took the 50ml bottle and will soon acquire the 100ml refill! I haven't been this happy about a new scent in a long time, which almost feels like it was created according to all my initial ideas!

The man sits next to me in the car and looks at me. "Why does it smell like whisky here? Like cheap whisky? No way." I hold out my arm to him, "it smells good here, over there it smells like alcohol." Uff. And yet I really like the scent because it cures my rose scent issues. But there it is again, the way guys describe fragrances. After jelly pudding with Juliette, now it's whisky - recently he said it was Jacky-Cola. And yes, he has a point. The citrusy opening reminds me of the smell when the lemon slice slips into Bacardi, but this scent doesn't have the woodiness of a whisky. Once the top notes have faded and the rough edges have smoothed out, the rose comes through. It's not the typical Chloe rose, but a woodier one. Oak, sandalwood, and cedar create a slightly soapy base. I like the scent because it's so untypical for Chloe. It's rosy-soapy, but has something herbal and creamy. I find it has something alcoholic, but it doesn't smell like cheap booze, and that alcohol note fades away, leaving a slightly soapy-creamy rose scent on a woody base.

Chloé usually falls within my preferred spectrum of fragrance creations, but this one has completely captivated me. This Chloé stands in stark contrast to all the gourmands I typically wear, yet it is perfect for my diabetic nose. I tested it purely by chance while accompanying a friend on a fragrance shopping trip.

Growing up in Mississippi where the Magnolia is the state's flower, I've had first hand experience with the beautifully unique/waxy smell of this delightful flower. I will say that this rendition is rather excellent in capturing the essence thereof. Very delicate and lighthearted. My only complaint is that this is very overpriced and the longevity is rather poor.

This was a blind buy fail that I had big hopes for. I have been on the hunt for a good Magnolia forward fragrance but, with my skin chemistry at least, this is not it. I know magnolia is a waxy flower but this actually feels like a light wax coating on my skin as it dries down. It smells nice and realistic for about 3.5 seconds and then it turns into the dirtiest, saltiest bad BO fragrance. It's not as offensive to me as the new Prada Paradoxe Intense (one of the most offensive things I've sprayed on my wrists to my nose) but Magnolia Alba is surprisingly close. The performance is very weak with this fragrance as well so thankfully at least, it doesn't linger in the senses. I really wanted to love Magnolia Alba, but I think when it comes to magnolia dominant perfumes, I would much sooner reach for Gucci Gorgeous Magnolia any day over this . (It does help that I actually like wearing Gorgeous Magnolia.) Like anything though, YMMV. The only nice thing I have to say is that I love the packaging. ETA: I just realized that the perfumer behind this is behind Replica: Lazy Sunday Morning. I like the scent of Lazy Sunday morning and I've owned it in the past but it gave me a headache. I wonder if this perfumer and I just have very different noses/senses.

Top 3 Magnolias ever. The whole flower, seed, leaf, stem is in this. You are literally in the blossom. It’s absolutely stunningly gorgeous. Finally a real magnolia without any other white florals nudging it aside. It breathes out with perfect sillage and projection. Présentation, price, and size are all wonderful.

Very good. A feel-good scent. Pleasantly fresh and uplifting. Citrus summer or spring fragrance. I would consider it more unisex and it's really good for the price-performance ratio. Unfortunately, it doesn't last very long.

Love Story… mu ha ha ha! You seriously don’t expect me to have a love story to tell, do you? *sigh* Unfortunately, I don’t have anything like that in store for myself *sob* If I did, I might have annoyed you with it just as much as with my stories about the cat, or any nerdy stuff, or other craziness :D But I just don’t have anything to say about love, waaah! *another sob* :DD … However, I can at least try to describe this fragrance here, which is also called Love Story, and compare it to the EDP. Admittedly (for me) this is only a small consolation, but at least a few women are reading this, unless everyone prefers to watch the semifinals in football, which could indeed be very exciting today :D The Fragrance: So, the fragrance starts for me with citrus notes, with Neroli being quite pleasant. It is a little sweet (which is also a small difference from the EDP, as the EDP starts off significantly sweeter) and floral. I don’t know exactly how plum blossoms smell, but even though a fruit and its blossom can smell quite different, there’s still a hint of a plum scent (at least to me), which is also a difference from the EDP, as I perceive this note much less in the EDP. In the base, the fragrance smells mostly of (still not really identifiable) flowers, which are not cloying but light, making it well-suited for spring and summer. Neroli is still somewhat present, but much less than at the beginning. This is a difference from the EDP, where you can still smell the Neroli or orange blossoms quite well and intensely in the base. Another difference from the EDP is the woody notes like cedar, which are completely absent here in the EDT. Oh, and the fragrance also gives off a slightly clean or fresh impression, even though I wouldn’t necessarily describe it as soapy. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is rather low, so you have to get quite close to the wearer shortly after spraying to smell it on her. The fragrance radiates a little better around oneself, but this doesn’t last long either. The longevity is about six to eight hours, but in the later hours, the fragrance is very close to the skin. The Bottle: The bottle is rectangular and has grooves in the glass. The chrome strip at the top of the bottle, where the brand name is engraved, gives the bottle a somewhat antique architectural look. There’s also a swiveling mechanism mounted at the top that acts like a carrying handle, with a ribbon hanging from it that has the same color as the fragrance liquid, which is pink. The cap is round and transparent. Like most Chloé bottles, I find this one quite lovely as well. So, I liked Love Story EDT. It is a gentle (albeit quite weakly projecting) fragrance that comes off as fresh and floral. It is not very sweet, so it should appeal to those who are not into sweet scents. It fits wonderfully into spring and summer, and I think the fragrance would unfold best on warm or even hot days, as I feel it could quickly be blown away or hardly noticeable on cold or windy days. Due to its low projection, in my opinion, it is more suitable for daytime use than for going out; on the other hand, it would surely be good for open-air events and such, where you might quickly reapply. The fragrance is also a bit clean and fresh, thus coming across as particularly feminine and also sexy, and I’m quite sure it must smell wonderful on your skin, ladies, although a man would have to get veeeery close to appreciate it… if he dares!!! Aaaaaaaaaarghghgh! :DD As I said, I find the fragrance quite successful, so I would recommend giving it a try!

Love Story EdT does not tell a complete love story, but focuses on the introduction, the phase where you get to know each other and form delicate bonds. Everything is feather-light - and the head is spinning. You can't forget the beloved face, have endless interest, are curious - enchanted and uncertain. The orange-yellow nasturtium warms the heart and thoughts in a tender way. Yet, you can't help but think. Mild orange and plum blossom are the softeners for the suddenly so perfect everyday life. You are in love - not only with this person but also a little with yourself, and the tingling feeling that surrounds you. Will it become a multi-volume love story - or just a short story? How will it end? You don't know - and enjoy this uncertainty in suspense. As Goethe says: When it buzzes in your head and heart - what more do you want? Who no longer loves - and no longer errs let them be buried.

This is a really fun scent. It's young and playful. It reminds me of a Green Apple Jolly Rancher mixed with the Blue Raspberry Jolly Rancher. A candy lovers dream. This was such a steal, the price was only $5.99 US dollars. Get your nose on this if you can. You can check out my review of this along with the two others in the collection.

I blind bought this one and didn’t know what to expect. I can’t say I know what Mimosa smells like, although I do recognise the scent, To me this smells of clean sheets hanging on a washing line, swaying in the summer breeze. This is gorgeous! It’s a clean, almost cotton fresh type of scent. I love it! I can’t fault this collection at all. I’ve been really impressed with most of the Atelier perfumes and have many from this line already. I love them all.

After finishing my bottle of Highgrove Bouquet by Penhaligon’s, I decided to search for a different mimosa based scent and, because I have no willpower or self-discipline, I blind-bought this one. It’s not a fail, really, but not a success either. The mimosa is definitely present but is very weak and fleeting. And that’s all there is to it, a weak mimosa that will need to be layered with another perfume.

I love Mimosa and I love this perfume. This and Tom Ford's Mimosa and Cardamom are two of my favorite Mimosa fragrances. Neither have the greatest lasting power, but that is OK... They are both still so very lovely. Perfect for Spring and everyday wear. So pretty! This scent is a real pick me up in a bottle. Really puts me in a happy mood. 7.5/10

Chloé's Atelier des Fleurs line is a wonderful collection of clean, straightforward fragrances that seem to come straight from nature. Nature is a precious source of scents. For my nose, there is nothing more beautiful than nature. Capturing this is an art, and this art can be found in Herba Mimosa. Clear, bright, fresh, green, sparkling, refreshing.... like a mountain stream, its water bubbling over mossy stones; like green, freshly cut flowers; like a freshly bloomed mimosa flower releasing its fragrance. All of this makes me smile and brings me bliss. Pure nature. The scent begins with a fresh breeze that refreshes with a greenish bitterness on warm days and becomes tender with a fully bloomed mimosa as it develops. It then fades pleasantly woody, bright, and clear. Herba Mimosa feels very aromatic and natural to me. The green conveys the impression of freshly cut flowers, and the mimosa is unsweetened and fresh. The green beautifully blends into the delicate scent of the woody-soft base. A wonderfully crafted perfume that unfortunately lingers for far too short a time. However, the price is incredibly high. The Atelier des Fleurs line scores points with the beautiful ribbed design of the bottles. In my eyes, this does not justify the price, though. There are more affordable alternatives. I prefer to use my "Truth (Eau de Parfum) | Calvin Klein," which, although it doesn't have this lovely mimosa, still has a similar character. Despite the price, a fantastic scent that is definitely worth trying.

The Chloé scents are of course quite classic and you have to love them, but I think many people can really appreciate the Love Story scents. I must say that I was not immediately sold when I first smelled this one. She smells rather classic and a little old-fashioned. This scent really needs time to develop on your skin and after that it is really a very nice and warm scent with nice longevity. As for the perfume itself, it's a suitable update to the original and I think she's very sensual. The orange blossom and heliotropes give the top and heart notes of Eau Sensuelle an addictive wanna-bury-your-nose-in-it kind of warmth. Love Story Eau Sensuelle also differs from its siblings in that it comes in an Eau de Parfum concentration – which naturally makes the scent a little heavier and longer lasting. I think this one's a great scent for everyday, but it works best on cold days that call for a soft and musky floral perfume.

...is the highest form of arrogance. This aphorism crosses my mind when I observe how difficult it is to please my husband. He always needs nothing - or - it is not necessary. So my friend also racked her brain about how she could repay him for helping her out with the computer. No - he declined. I understand her concern, though, because no one wants to be in debt to the other. So we decided together that I would receive a gift from her instead. And we quickly found Love Story Eau Sensuelle. This mild, friendly scent also fits well with the theme of modesty. But here, modesty is an adornment. The orange blossom and heliotrope shimmer in competition - but do not dazzle. A hint of mint clarifies and gently refreshes - soothed by creamy sandalwood. Of the Love Stories, this one is my favorite, because it is the brightest and most transparent. But also the most individual - despite its fine restraint. I was so "immodest" to joyfully accept this gift - and my friend was relieved as well.

Doesnt worth the money. Boring, plain rose water scent. So expensive for a rose water. Not new thing. I dont recommend to anybody. I can buy million times cheaper rose water if I want smell and use it in Turkey. Nothing new.

My blind buy and fail. Admittedly, I thought, what could possibly go wrong with Chloe? I had almost all Chloe fragrances so far and liked them all. A fresh, fruity rose is always a good choice, I thought. From the data sheet, it has a great composition. I have sniffed the scent here and hope that’s not the issue. For some reason, the fragrance smells sour and rancid to me, even though there is no rhubarb in it, it almost exclusively smells like rhubarb on me. It might also be the combination of grapefruit and lychee. There are hardly any fragrances that I want to wash off immediately, but this is one of them. For now, it’s stored in the cool cellar, just to be sure it smells the same in autumn/winter. Sometimes there are surprises depending on the season in both directions. The recognizability is reflected in the elegant bottle made of pleated glass, available since 2019. This time, the face was Haley Bennett. I expected a green-fresh start, powdery, rosy, crisp, fresh, sparkling, and instead I got a cleaner association. Later it becomes a bit softer, but a piercing plastic note remains. It has a certain synthetic, scratchy severity. Biting rhubarb rose, if I liked the scent, it would be the only Chloe unisex. Still, it wouldn’t have anything to do with Chloe Rose. I will avoid grapefruit and oak moss for now.

After I liked Ur L`eau, I was interested to try the new version. Can it keep up with its predecessor? I think so. Here too, I am greeted by the floral freshness of my morning garden. The blackbird sings the new day - softened by cool night mist. The magnolia unfolds its delicate pink scent - accompanied by the full pink of the Leonardo da Vinci rose. The jasmine has also awakened and begins to shine. Oakmoss behaves discreetly and acts only as a framing element. L`eau is transparent and intense at the same time - and puts me in a romantic mood. A good moment to play something soft and delicate on the piano. Maybe - Morning has broken? The gentle melody and the equally melodic scent form a beautiful unity. For me, a worthy successor to the original version.

I have found that the word 'opulent' as used by perfumers (Amouage, Ineke, et al.) in their marketing literature is actually code for soapy/aldehydic floral compositions, and I'd have to say that Chloe INNOCENCE fits right into that category. This is a fairly sharp, very soapy green floral perfume reminiscent to my nose of Dior TENDRE POISON. The hyacinth is dominant, but the squeaky clean quality of this creation is what is most striking of all, above the flowers and everything else. When I donned this perfume today, it occurred to me that it may very well have been the inspiration of the entire CLEAN line. Strong and declarative (potential headache alert...), and a bit cold, I'd say. I realize that aldehydes are not listed among the notes, but INNOCENCE is closer to WHITE LINEN than it is to most floral greens, it seems to me.

A sort of sugar-water pink peony, with jasmin, grannies violets and orange flower, but even notes like grapefruit, banana skin, green notes and a dark bitter iris can't restrain an powerful sugar rush. For a massively sweet-toothed profile it handles the syrup quite well, and by holding onto a watery texture it stays on the breathable side of glycerine. It comes as no surprise to see the adverts for this showing a pale, blue eyed, blond girl, the super-sweet scent points directly at the teen market. The saccharin simplicity of Innocence is a remote descendant of that first great puberty perfume - Anaïs Anaïs, and both must be held responsible for prizing open the bedroom door to those morally (and aesthetically) dubious phenomena, Celebrity Perfume and perfume for girls. Chloé - not so innocent.

The mid 90s, to me, is a period with an overweight of beautiful linear fragrances with few notes. Simplicity and back to quiet. I suppose some may disagree and this is not the whole picture, but this is how I remember it. At least I remember a change from the 80s’ strong flower-bombs to something way more quiet. It was like fashion turning down the volume. Innocence is in my opinion a typical mid 90s’ scent: Sour, flowery, powdery… that is Innocence to my nose. Not much ado. The sour comes first. Not a bad, but a different sour. Like sharp citrus fruit, the feeling of picking the peel of a lemon. Then especially the rose and violets come to play and that combo is even more odd. It stays sour but in a flowery way. Finally, the warmer, more powdery feeling ends the journey. All in all a great tour… But… Actually, the fragrance is not the reason why I bought this. It was, as often before, the bottle. Minimalistic, organically shaped an opaque. I really like it. I do not know how to describe the shape of the bottle. It looks hand crafted by a glass blower, a sculpture of some sort. A work of art, definitely. 113/365

I have always liked Chloe Innocence very much and I even bought 2 bottles - far too expensive - online. It's a pity that this fragrance is no longer produced! It smells soft, like freshly washed, and wonderfully unobtrusive. I wanted to share my find with you, a fragrance that, while not smelling exactly the same, at least resembles Chloe Innocence: Narciso Rodrigues Essence The fragrance is described as: “floral powdery musk” with iris, rose, benzoin, amber, and musk notes. It is marketed as a daytime scent that is both clean, like “liquid sunshine”, and sexy. Since many people are still searching for this fragrance, I thought this information would surely be helpful.

So was the title of the piece by TLC that accompanied the commercial for this fragrance back then. In the ad, you saw cuddling girls in a milky white setting, neo-David Hamilton. This may have contributed to the US market having a problem with the scent, and it never really took off, not even in Germany. The strange, uterus-like bottle also drew mockery and ridicule, and so the fragrance, which followed the ultra-floral, then-successful scent Chloe Narcisse, did not become one. I thought it was great back then. The music was hip, the ad was hot, and the bottle, well, it was just a bottle. But the scent was excitingly different, hot-cold, sweet-fresh, crazysexycool. The hyacinth in the top note knocked everything that smelled like it or after it down. Still, the fragrance had a freshness kick and also a slight powderiness. The sillage was rather sweet-floral and slightly sharp. The longevity was a bit of a letdown. I am now a bit older and wouldn’t wear it this year, but I sometimes sniff my remaining bit or its weaker scent twin (Energizing Fragrance by Shiseido) when I want to be reminded of the mid-90s.

I came across Innocence by Chloe rather by chance. I bought two other fragrances used, which I no longer remember, and received this one as a bonus. I didn't even know this scent. But since I like the Chloe brand, especially the very old classic Chloe, I was pleased with this addition. However, it has nothing to do with Chloe from 1975.

Yes, that is how the hyacinth is referred to in the language of flowers. I had Innocence in my youth and found it extremely heavy - even though it contains only white flowers. "Innocence" is supposed to embody the scent? Really innocence? Well, if it refers to the bottle and the bright, floral aspect, then that fits.

With the fragrance group of rather delicate, light perfumes, I usually don't have much in mind. I like this one extraordinarily - but it doesn't belong to that category at all! The name is misleading. Chloe Innocence is not an innocent country girl, but quite a cunning thing.

When I bought this fragrance years ago, I always feverishly thought about which spring flower it reminded me of. I didn't think of hyacinth back then (and Google didn't exist at that time, at least I didn't know it). Still: none of my other fragrances with hyacinth smells like this one, a bit piercing perhaps at first, but definitely floral. O.k.

Innocence smells innocent, pleasantly green, like a hidden garden with a fragrant sea of blossoms. I see a virgin rising from the sea, then again a spring queen among the Celts. And the dream of Kätchen conveyed to us by Heinrich von Kleist! Cause of love: Count von Strahl: "What binds you to my steps? Käthchen: My noble lord! You ask too much of me.

Let's put it this way: You get what you pay for. Whether you like it or not is, of course, a matter of taste. I liked the scent from the very beginning - despite the H&M stamp... it actually smells like sweet plum schnapps, with a smoky vanilla note. It strongly reminds me of the vanilla Impulse deodorant from the 90s :). You have to like it, though. More suited for autumn and winter.

I have been really impressed with this collection from Chloe. So far I have Vanilla Planifolia (which I absolutely love), Jasmin Sambac, Ylang Cananga, Cedrus (the only one I’m unsure of) and I’m now awaiting Magnolia Alba & Herba Mimosa to complete all the scents I wanted from this collection. I find them very light, airy and feminine. Jasmin Sambac has a beautiful, soft, freshness to it. It actually reminds me a bit of Angeli di Firenze by Santa Maria Novella, which is one of my favourite spring scents. This is softer and not as soapy, but overall this is a beautiful scent. I’m pleased to have it in my collection. My favourites from this collection are Vanilla Planifolia and Ylang Changa, with Jasmin Sambac coming in 2nd. I have blind bought Herba Mimosa so hoping that it’s as good as the others.

Yup, it's me - I don't like jasmine and I have it in my collection. This one is completely different than any jasmine perfumes I know. It's very elegant and will stay with you all day. I think that the whole Chloe Atelier line is really good and worth to try. Magnolia, Chedrus, Immortele and our pretty Jasminum are my TOP 4.

Fresh, delicate, green, and in the background, veeeery softly indolic. However, not unpleasant but realistic white jasmine blossoms in misty cold air. Those who are very sensitive to it should test it 2-3 times beforehand. The scent is perfect as a spring perfume for anyone who loves white flowers in a gentle and unsweetened way, and year-round for all jasmine lovers. I smell the jasmine from Le Jardin de Monsieur Li without the citrus notes coming through. Longevity and sillage are roughly similar.

I love jasmine. I think everyone knows that by now, whether they want to or not. If I could, I would walk around all day with heavy, intoxicating jasmine scents and give everyone headaches. But I'm not that mean after all. After some fresh and inoffensive jasmine fragrances for the day have moved in with me over the past few months, I've been thinking for a while about a slightly more voluminous and expressive jasmine scent. I could wear it in the evening. Just for me, at home, no one has to know. My partner has a terrible sense of smell anyway. In my niche perfumery, I've been eyeing "Atelier Versace - Jasmin au Soleil | Versace" for a while. This extremely sultry headache candidate is only sold in 100 ml bottles and costs a whopping 350 euros. Moreover, the enchanting jasmine scent is disturbed by a very persistent freesia. So much greater was my joy when I managed to get a decant of "Jasminum Sambac" at the souk - many thanks to Needlesoup for that! With the first spray came the revelation - pure, intoxicating, pure jasmine! All alone, completely undisturbed and without annoying companions in the foreground! I am in love! Chloe does it like no one before! The jasmine is everything, there are no other fragrance notes needed to disturb this intoxicating spectacle! I am left completely satisfied and happy. I have found my jasmine scent.

The best lavender I have ever smelled. Most perfumes with lavender tend to be more masculine for me. This scent is more feminine. At first, it is fruity and green… maybe lemon? The fragrance develops and you can smell lavender, which is very soft, creamy, and also a bit powdery. This is a scent for calmness and security.

I was looking for a light, feminine lavender scent - preferably niche - that isn't boring. I love Mon Guerlain Intense - but for everyday wear, it's too much for me. Definitely. I honestly didn't think it would be so hard. Long story short: I eventually found myself at the Chloé counter. I had little hope. Chloé is not really my brand; I almost completely gave away my bottle of Normade to a friend a few weeks ago. And the first spray on paper of Lavanda? Quite scary. Just a sharp, cleaning product green and no lavender. I was persuaded to test the scent on skin. And lo and behold: The top note, or the first impression, is still very NEON GREEN (grass and lemon for me) and unfortunately, I don't smell any flowers. Sorry! The sharpness thankfully fades quickly. The scent remains predominantly green for me, but it softens, the lavender shines through, and a few flowers join in. It has a bit of a wildflower meadow vibe, I would say. Later in the dry-down, the scent is undoubtedly close to the skin, more floral, and powdery - which I personally find very sexy. Lavanda deserves a chance: please don't judge it directly at the counter and on paper. The discrepancy was very large in my case. PS: I’m still very open to ‘sexy lavender’ tips. ;)

Sweet, creamy with that banana ylang smell that I love and was looking for in a fragrance. Ylang ylang nosy be has it but it quickly gets ovefpowered by vanilla and fades. This one, however, is just right. It is a perfect tropical ylang that is fun to wear and I think it will be pleasant for those around because it is light.

What a gorgeous, fresh, tropical scent. This to me is a happy fragrance. It’s bright and sunny. The ylang-ylang is soft and inoffensive. I blind bought this based on all the ratings I could find and it’s definitely a winner. Perfect for spring and summer. A 10/10 for me. I don’t mind that it doesn’t last long either. For 50ml these bottles are really well priced in my opinion. Love it! So far I have Vanilla Planifolia which is another love, Jasmin which I find is a beautiful refreshing scent, Cedrus which I’m still a bit unsure of, and I’m now awaiting Herba Mimosa to complete all the scents I wanted from this range. I’ve been really impressed with this collection. All the fragrances are light, airy and feminine. I love that these can be layered to make different scent combinations as well.

Love Tuberose but with Ylang instead of the Tuberose/white florals! There's a bit of citrus in the top notes that give it a fresh effervescence, quickly followed by a skin-salty, ever-so-slightly-sour ylang custard cream. (There's absolutely no camphor, which I love in my ylangs but its absence doesn't hurt this at all) It only lasts about 4 hours on my skin, but much longer on clothes/hair. I was a little concerned it would be too sweet, but it's well balanced and I love it. The sweetness is measured and (the entire cream/sandalwood/cedar base really) very comparable to Love. I'm not sure that it would be a safe blind buy for someone who isn't a ylang fan; but if you love the "custard pudding" style ylangs honestly I say just get it. I will add though that I think it’s a little overhyped for what it is, possibly because it can be difficult to find in the US

For me, it is a beautifully enveloping summer fragrance that smells intensely but pleasantly of Ylang Ylang and reminds me of a luxurious summer body lotion that you want to bathe in. The longevity could be better in my opinion, as I already have to reapply throughout the day to continue enjoying the scent.

I don't understand the negative reviews. If the bottle had Chanel or Tom Ford on it, everyone would go crazy for it. I (unfortunately) only ordered a small one, and was surprised. It smells sweet, but definitely not cheap. There is this 'cozy' feeling, when it's cold outside, this perfume warms you up (I couldn't find it on the H&M website anymore :( ) A beautiful scent for a ridiculous price. P.s.: It doesn't always have to be expensive to be good.

I read the fragrance notes and expected a tasty gourmand. When the bottle arrived, I found the choice of a bright pink color a bit strange. One does not expect a gourmand behind such a glaring magenta. To start, I don't think the scent is bad. Unfortunately, it is somewhat misguided by the listed ingredients. Some, like jasmine and tuberose, I can smell and they definitely dominate. The top note is very floral and there is a slight creaminess hidden behind it. It can definitely be worn, but I see this scent more suited for a younger, female clientele - as it is also quite sweet. After about 10-15 minutes, the scent becomes creamier and something that reminds me of Vanilla & Chestnut comes through. The floral aspect is still present, creating this slightly discordant note. It’s as if the scent cannot decide. Am I a floral freshie or do I want to be a creamy gourmand? I’m not upset with it, especially not at this price. I think the 30ml bottle will be used up quickly, as you have to reapply several times. However, I definitely won’t need to buy it a second time.

Because I am enamored with Chloe Love and Eau de Fleurs Capucine, I am making my way through Chloe fragrance line. Next up ... Eau de Fleurs Lavande. The opening is nice but a bit over-powering and artificial. Eau de Fleurs Lavande is not the masculine lavender that I feared, the masculine lavender which is common in fragrances such as Roger & Gallet Lavande Royale. However, Eau de Fleurs Lavande isn't overtly feminine or floral either. Instead, it has a neutered characteristic that is consistent with Yankee Candle room sprays & BBW air fresheners. As it dries, Chloe Lavande melts with my skin and becomes a soapy, clean scent. It has a slight sweetness to it, and I sense vanilla and sandalwood although neither are listed. I get a bit of violet, some green and citrus, also the musk in the base. However, the clean, soapy aspect defines the scent, not the lavender accord & supporting notes. Someone looking for fragrance like a lavender flower may be disappointed with Eau de Fleurs Lavande. In that case, I'd instead recommend an aromatic lavender oil, or exploring a soliflore such as Demeter Natural Lavendar which is vintaged by harvest year. Eau de Fleurs Lavande is marked EdP & wears like an EdP but has the presence of a dried down cologne. Lavande actually passed the overnight test. The next morning the scent was barely on my skin as a whisper, but as my skin warmed and as I moved about, I could smell Lavende wafting up from where it was applied. So, Lavande -- especially when over-sprayed -- has longevity; it just doesn't have a lot of sillage. Chloe Lavande strikes me as a skin scent. The color of the juice is a barely there beige, which seems quite appropriate for the fragrance. I think it would work well for the office or for bedtime. It also would work well on those days when, for whatever reason, you just don't want to smell like much of anything. Chloe Lavande is a fragrance that fits within the American aesthetic of squeaky clean skin and freshly laundered clothes. If I didn't know any better, I would have guessed that the juice in this vial was B. Clean Relax by Benetton, although the Chloe is better quality and more complex.

I'm in two minds over this fragrance. Eau de Fleurs Lavande is beautiful in a discreet and natural fashion, however I think I'd prefer it much more if it was slightly stronger, like Eau de Lavande by Annick Goutal perhaps. The top notes are when the lavender note is at its most prominent in the composition. It jumps off the skin in a feminine and watery way, somewhat aromatic, but also quite understated. I liked the opening the best. The heart tended to become more discreet and airy, with subtle tea notes, zesty bergamot and fresh violet leaves complimenting the core. The rich lavender diminishes slightly, a little too soon in my opinion. The sweet almond accord, although unique and pleasant, disappointed me as I wanted more aromatic lavender rather than sugared nuts. I think this fragrance is so focused on smelling elegant and refined that it loses a lot of its character and rawness. Eau de Fleurs Lavande started off as my favourite from this series, however by the drydown it's my least favourite. It's just too fleeting for me and I grew tired of it far too quickly. I acknowledge its purity and softness, but for me it was a little boring and forgettable.

Well, first of all, I strongly considered whether to write any comments at all. Here, there are non-commenters who think they have to leave a negative "comment" on every post but don't have the guts to address anyone directly. As long as they can throw in their two cents or press DR out of spite. Well, I think I can rise above that. * I received Eau de Fleurs Lavande from a lovely perfumer after my first Parfumo meeting in Munich. Unfortunately, it is now rarely available, and when it is, it’s very overpriced. * Eau de Fleurs Lavande is delicate and "purple." It immediately reminds me of a lavender field in summer, with a pretty woman standing in the middle. She wears a white, flowing dress and a white straw hat adorned with a light pink ribbon. Her arms are stretched out to the sides, and her palms touch the tips of the lavender flowers. At first, EdFL smells cool and very much of tea. Slightly bitter and a bit sour. Then it quickly becomes creamy, soft, and silky. As if you are looking at the display of a confectionery, where pralines lie waiting to be tasted and purchased. You can almost taste each one. I mean that creaminess, the slightly "fatty" glaze before you bite into the interior. Not sweet - just creamy. Do you know lavender pralines? An acquired taste, but delicious. Lavender, delicate, fine, and Mediterranean. EdFL then becomes increasingly clingy and hugs the skin like a second layer. Cashmeran, soft and flowing, musk for the well-behaved "animal" in you, and vetiver and cedar for the fluffy herbal-green. You can wear this scent anywhere, at any time of day. It is gentle, unobtrusive but present and elegant. Almost girlish - although that sounds a bit too playful. Let’s put it another way... for a shy woman who wants to awaken the protector instinct, it’s just right. But of course for anyone else as well. A very fine fragrance. Lavender is the dominant note, but without a whip!

Eau de Fleurs Lavande is a delicate, uncomplicated floral scent with a light (!) lavender focus. I find it to be a typical Chloe - soft, floral, fresh. I am almost inclined to call it an innocent flower, but that does not do it justice. The fragrance is excellently composed, no note overwhelms the other, none stands out sharply; all components gently blend into a beautiful harmonious veil of scent, semi-transparent and enveloping. A quiet, gentle companion for all occasions. At the same time, it has a certain presence - just not a "whoops, I'm here" presence, but rather a clean, flattering one. This Chloe creation gains depth from warm amber and a soft woody musk note. The longevity is surprisingly good for such a delicate character - though in a subtle, skin-close way. Even during an 8-hour workday, I didn't feel the need to reapply. Eau de Fleurs Lavande is a perfume for wearers who do not necessarily want to stand out with a strong scent. It is quiet, harmonious, and supportive.

Usually, I test all new samples I receive briefly on test strips to get a first, very general impression. Then I also enter my initial rating here and mark it as tested. The samples then go into my to-be-tested bowl and are tested on the skin during a day as needed and desired. Sometimes, I also test them over 2-5 days before writing the review, depending on how quickly I can access the perfume. Eau de Fleurs Lavande had slipped all the way to the bottom of this bowl, and I was very surprised to see that I had given it a solid 90% on Parfumo after the first test months ago. It must be my kind of scent. No wonder, I really like lavender. The name is a bit misleading. Of course, lavender is the (shy) main actor, but it is only through the wonderfully arranged supporting actors, the locations, the composition, and the gentle effects that Fleurs Lavande becomes a recommendable release. The heart is formed by lavender, powdery and creamy, together with buttery iris. Beautiful, not too green, hardly sweet, classic, soft, refined. A light tea note gives the fragrance a slightly smoky-soothing quality, while vetiver and cedar add a slightly rough character and pull the scent away from the feminine corner. Citrus and indefinable floral notes, especially at the beginning, round off the overall fragrant pleasure. Bottle: looks simple, but extremely fine and elegant. Sillage: one can hardly speak of real sillage or projection. Longevity: already better than 7 hours. A clear unisex scent for me and a pleasant lavender interpretation, which often moves in the gray background, but does so with class and elegance. And for lavender fans, it’s a must-try. It greatly improves my opinion of Chloe and makes me eager to try the other two Eaus from the brand.

Is there really lavender in here? Since I discovered Jicky, I have been fascinated by herbal lavender scents. And I would love to have exactly that in its pure form. Today, I came across this perfume. Immediately, I hoped to find a lavender scent like the one described above from Chloe, who indeed produces decent fragrances. I was mistaken. And yet, it's a hit!
For me, the scent is nothing special and I find it rather inconspicuous - perhaps even a bit too sweet. But on many women, it smells great. That must be acknowledged without envy.

Hey, Parfumo's assistant reminds me that I know Le Mâle and should write a review. Truly? I mean, I had it, I have it, and I definitely will have it, and I haven't commented on it? My bad. People have already spent a lot of words on the torso bottle design or the metal tin box, so that I won't say more. Instead, let me tell you this is one of those perfumes that I think every guy has owned, and if you don't have it, you should have it and keep reading the review. The scent is a clean, sensual musky sweat, like a man's squeaky skin. It is an aromatic and desirable type of fragrance, which has nothing to do with other dirty things designed with sinful and raunchy male fluids in mind, like Kouros Eau de Toilette . A kind of barber's perfume, which befits a handsome man. So disruptive, trendy gay clubbers and straight men alike welcomed it with enthusiasm--I would swear a lot of women wore it too. Le Mâle was everywhere in the late '90s, and it still smells great today. Le Mâle is back to its golden age. It is a cologne that revolves around mint, lavender, and vanilla blend. If you missed it, Francis Kurkdjian is the perfumer behind it, the same one he created Baccarat Rouge 540 Eau de Parfum . Sophisticated yet playful, sensual yet fresh, it is still modern. They've reworked it over the years, so if you still remember it from the mid-90s, it's worth a second sniff. Subsequent releases have reduced performance, but the essence of the perfume is still there. Fresh mint is a symbol of strength and characterizes its delicious opening. Ignoring the other aromatic and spicy things, like bitter mugwort and green cardamom, and a touch of powdery bergamot that adds a citrus twist to a freshly spiced start, but my nose picks up a powerful hint of mint. It may seem like some intense opening, but it settles down pretty quickly. When the heart arrives, a traditional soapy note of lavender, which remains prominent until the end, announces it. The blue flower shares the stage with a sweeter citrus bloom, orange blossom, I bet, and a punch of spices. While I don't take too much of the sweaty cumin, I sense a lot of sweet cinnamon barks. And then, the coumarins give warmth and tenderness to the dry-down. Both powdered vanilla and toasted tonka are featured and blended with a salty, honeyed amber. The base also features some woods, creamy sandalwood contrasted with a dry cedar. Overall, the amber, woody, and creamy cocktail create an oriental accord. It has a kind of barber vibe but is slightly off the classic fougére shade we're used to. It still retains the combination of vanilla and lavender with a muted spice and the remnants of a strong mint. The original luxury of Le Mâle made me prefer to wear it in the cold months of late autumn and winter, for the evening or the night. Both the sillage and the longevity were indescribable. They are moderate nowadays, although that won't stop me from keeping Le Mâle in my collection. Clean, woody, and fresh, but with wonderful warmth, this fragrance is incredible! The recent target has changed from clubbing to everyday use. However, it is a delightful scent to revisit from time to time, as it brings back many positive memories. Finally, I have Le Mâle Eau de Toilette on my right wrist and Cuba Gold Eau de Toilette on my left wrist, and they have many points in common. I base the review on a 75ml bottle I have owned since March 2018. -Elysium

I can't say the word wonderful enough when it comes to describing this amazing Jean Paul Gaultier creation. I don't know where these so-called 'homosexual' and 'metrosexual' terminologies come from. I'm not one for throwing a fragrance into a particular category, Le Male can be either masculine or sweet with a feministic touch, it all depends on how you interpret the scent. Because vanilla and musk are dominant notes in this fragrance, I can see why some men might think that this lacks masculinity. Let me assure you that when worn by the right man this has all the potential to make me swoon. Le Male is sweet yet refreshing at the same time. Some have noted an almost soapy and powdery quality, which is certainly there, however I quite like it. I particularly love that for a fragrance which is so popular, it is so unique, one of a kind. The lasting strength, is honestly, out of this world. It has the ability to last and last. I must add that I rather like the bottle. I like its bold and straight-forward design. It's beyond me to understand why someone would be ashamed of displaying it.

There's not many fragrances that are still relevant and carismathic after 30 years. This is one of them. A classic, a must-have, one of the best creations and super influential. I remember being a young guy and a friend of mine was wearing Le Mâle. back in the late 90's early 00's. I was not into fragrances although i always like to spray on whatever my father had. Usually Original Eau de Toilette , Black Eau de Toilette , Don Algodón para Hombre Eau de Toilette , Pull & Bear Eau de Toilette or Springfield Eau de Toilette . But this smell stuck with me and years later, i worked with a guy that took baths with Le Male. Everytime i entered in his car i would be drowned by his scent. I knew the scent but never asked what fragrance was. In 2015, i started collecting fragrances and in one of the first perfumery stores i immediately picked up Le Male and recognized the smell. Since then, i have Le Mâle and wear it often. Everybody knows it already but to sumarize it, it's fresh, sweet, powdery and a bit spicy-earthy in the opening. Mint, lavender, vanilla, orange blossom, woods tonka beans... The combination is perfect, mind blowing, iconic and still influential. You can hype the new flankers but none can reach the greatness of the original. They all smell similar to Le Mâle, but aren't as good as the original. The only one that is very good is Fleur du Mâle which was created by FK and has a nice floral twist on the DNA. Le Parfum is a really nice flanker too but like the new Elixir, falls flat, although I prefer Le Parfum over Elixir. Overall, the fragrance still performs well, has depth, uniqueness, an iconic smell and it's pleasant. A must have masculine scent. Youtubers always criticize it saying it's played out. It's just a way to get money from the newer stuff that they hype. This is great and i even go further saying it could be considered a masterpiece. Forget the new flankers. go to the original. A legend. 5/5

I have seen this fragrance being talked about or referenced so much since I dipped myself into the world of perfume. So, I had to try it, but I was shocked to find out that this was released back in 1995 and was Kurkdjian's first creation. This is the perfume from the ’90s that’s still relevant to this day, just like my beloved Issey Miyake’s L’Eau d’Issey Pour Homme from 1994. For context: 1) People associate this with a ‘daddy’ or old-man scent, since it was released decades ago. I, for one, have never been into the perfume world until recently, so I have no idea what the scent trends were back then. More importantly, I wouldn’t be affected by nostalgia. 2) The term 'barbershop scent' is a Western-centric concept, rooted in what Western or European barbershops traditionally smelled like. To me, especially in the Southeast Asia region, we have a different idea of what a 'barbershop scent' smells like. Spoiler alert, Le Male doesn't exude barbershop scent to me Now that that’s out of the way, Le Male is my new favourite. It opens with a fresh, powdery scent and a clear cardamom note. My nose kind of went wonky at first because it had never experienced something powdery fresh yet spicy. It almost rejected it right away. But once it settled down and my nose got familiar with it, I started to warm up to it. It then transitions into a clean scent, almost like ambroxan but not quite. Maybe it’s ISO E Super? It eventually settles into a warm vanilla base. I didn’t get any old-guy scent from it or any barbershop vibe, but it is clean and mature without smelling synthetic. It’s powdery, spicy, and honestly kind of addictive to sniff. Le Male may be nearly 30 years old but to my nose it still feels bold, clean and entirely relevant. I came in with no expectations or nostalgia and it still managed to win me over. Sometimes a scent does not need to follow trends. It just needs to catch you off guard in the best way.

I think not. Nor should popularity be a sin, but it is this, what "Le Male" is being blamed of quite frequently. And yes, this fragrance is a "weapon", in terms of intensity only excelled by "Joop! Homme" to my opinion. And yes, this a commonly used fragrance and it is used by a lot of people I cannot identify with (nor do I want to) and – even worse - who cannot dose properly. And yes, I sensed it even in the office the other day and this is hardly the right place for Le Male. Still, it is a magnificent fragrance – the oriental sweetness, supported mainly by notes of mint and cinnamon in combination with an exhilarating seasoning is special and does appear "crispier" than in all other fragrances I know of. This is why I still like to wear it, when I go out and am in the right mood for it.

Scentrack: Skee-Lo – I Wish Le Male opens with a short shot of bergamot and mint, followed by synthetic lavender reminiscent of classic fougere fragrances. The lavender is complemented by strong cinnamon note and almost dirty white flowers of orange blossom and jasmine.

I'm talking about phrases or opinions that certain people constantly repeat—things like, "This is outdated," or "Don't buy this, someone's dad wore it, so you shouldn't." There's nothing left to say about this wonderful scent. Classic and timeless, definetely a must have for any fragrance lover. A wonderful mix of lavender, vanilla and tonka bean (mainly) that lingers for a long time in your skin. Thumbs up! Updated January 2014

I bought reformulated bottle of Le Male in 2019 and I have to say that it is still pretty good fragrance. Due to its reletively low cost, synthetic vanilla has been used in this fragrance, which makes the initial opening quite bitter.

this is an Amazing fragrance!, it has a very nice projection and longevity. if you like sweet fragrances this is "a must have". very nice combination of vanilla,mint. i cant give this fragrance any other than a 100%!, this fragrance never gets old, its 18 years since it was introduced on the market, so i guess you can call this a Classic and an oldie but a Goldie!

I had high hopes for this one because I love the combination of rose, orange blossom, and vanilla. But here, I’m disappointed. The opening is very sweet and vanillic, with a vague impression of white florals. After a few minutes, a hint of orange blossom pushes through, but where is my precious rose? I can’t find it, what a shame! To me, this perfume feels like an overly sweet, rather generic floral, lacking originality, and nothing like what I had imagined: a bold, striking duo of rose and orange blossom. Disappointing.

A winter dream for Chloé fans? I would have wished that the then Chloé Absolu de Parfum had more depth. The new flanker (like many others) is solid but not a revelation. It doesn't have to be, as it can smell just right for everyday autumn wear. Well-groomed Chloé DNA but with warmer notes; tonka bean and light vanilla come to the forefront early on. The listed citrus notes are only faintly noticeable to me, and they could have been omitted. More spice and punch are missing. The O-flower is more present, while the typical Chloé rose only flashes here and there. The O-flower also reminds me of Nomade Lumière d’Égypte For me, it's better than Chloé L'Eau de Parfum Lumineuse (which made me feel a bit nauseous ^^). But both are not necessary. The Chloé L'Eau de Parfum Intense is the best of the new releases, but for me, it’s not suitable for the cold season. Interestingly, it reminds me just a bit of Classique Intense … that one was great… Longevity on me is good, like all Chloés. It's okay for everyday wear, but not a milestone. You won't stand out with it, but you don't always have to (wink ;) Rip Love, Chloé … when will that be brought back from obscurity?

Last summer, I embarked on a fragrance journey exploring scents at the Macy's flagship store in New York City. Among the vast array of fragrances, a few stood out among the various fragrances that were offered as samples. Jean Paul Gaultier's Ultra Male was one of them. As the hype surrounding this fragrance has died down since its release in 2015, this presents the perfect opportunity to assess whether Ultra Male truly lived up to its earlier acclaim. ---- Ultra Male's opening is a familiar blend of mint and lavender that is reminiscent of the original Le Male fragrance, but it comes with an added twist. The infusion of a juicy pear note adds a fruity touch to the fresh introduction that is impossible to ignore. It is a surprising, yet welcome shift. During the dry down, Ultra Male ditches the freshness for a sweet and gourmand profile because of the cinnamon and vanilla notes. The presence of lingering amber notes adds to the fragrance's overall sweetness. null of this is a surprise, as this is also present in the original Le Male. Overall, Ultra Male attempts to be a daringly sweeter adaptation of the iconic Le Male scent, and it succeeds beyond expectations. Whether you are a lady or a gentleman, if you have an affinity for sweet fragrances, this scent will leave you absolutely enamored. Conversely, if sweet scents annoy you, encountering Ultra Male can be a nightmare. ---- It is hard to discuss the Jean Paul Gaultier Ultra Male bottle design (and by extension, every Le Male bottle) without bringing up the iconic mannequin bottles with their distinct crotch bulge. I do not have strong feelings about the bottle design, but it is notably divisive. Some individuals love the unique shape that differentiates itself from other bottles. For others, the bottle design is enough to turn them away from the fragrance. At least the midnight blue opaque coloring is a pleasant touch. That being said, the functionality of the bottle takes precedence over its aesthetics. With Ultra Male, simply pulling the pin and pressing the nozzle produces a satisfactory mist with minimal effort. Ultimately, while the bottle design may not have universal appeal, the functionality of the spray mechanism is commendable. ---- For performance, Ultra Male is a standout among designer fragrances currently available on the market. With just two sprays, this scent projects throughout a moderate-sized room for 4-6 hours, leaving behind an impressive sillage trail that lingers for at least 15 minutes after the wearer has left the area. Also, Ultra Male's longevity is simply unmatched, lasting on the skin for an impressive 12 hours - enough to see you through an entire night with ease. On one hand, if someone seeks a subtle fragrance, Ultra Male is NOT that scent. However, for the attention seeker, it delivers a powerful performance and is sure to leave an impression (positive or negative) on those who experience the potent projection and remarkable longevity. ---- With seasonal use, Ultra Male presents an interesting dichotomy.
