The scent profile is a fascinating blend of sweet and fresh notes should make it a versatile fragrance across different seasons, but that is not the full story. Its strength and intensity make it ideal for cold weather, and it works exceptionally well in winter. However, the fresh and fruity aroma of Ultra Male also makes it an excellent choice for spring or during summer nights, where it can add a touch of sweetness to the warm weather. That said, Ultra Male's sweetness can be overpowering and cloying when worn during the summer daytime when it is hottest. Similarly, the fresh scent can work in the fall, but even as a sweet scent, it can feel somewhat out of place with the autumnal atmosphere. While using a strong fragrance like Ultra Male in certain social situations such as the office or the gym might not be the brightest idea because of the strong sillage, it truly comes into its own in other settings. For instance, during leisure time spent outdoors or at a large indoor party, this fragrance is an absolute showstopper that draws attention and helps create a vibrant atmosphere. Perfect for people who want to stand out. And while Ultra Male might not always be a surefire hit on a date night. It is a winner if your partner loves sweet fragrances. (If not, well, you have a charming personality, right?) ---- I must note that the fragrance world is currently moving towards fresher, more subtle scents, which is why Ultra Male fell to the wayside. However, in my opinion, the hype behind the fragrance was genuine. However, the hype is meaningless if you are not a fan of sweet fragrances, or you seek a scent that is more intimate than attention-grabbing. In these instances, Ultra Male is not the right scent for you. That said, if you are in the market for a year-round sweet and fresh evening fragrance that will turn heads when you enter a room, then Ultra Male may be just what you are looking for. Those who appreciate this bold, attention-grabbing scent are sure to be equally impressed by its longevity and impressive performance.

Tl;dr: There are haters who are giving this fragrance an unfairly low rating, but if you set aside your preconceived notions, you just might find you really like Ultra Mâle. After more than a decade of not wearing any fragrance, I got the urge to curate a small collection of fragrances for my personal use. I set out to examine fragrances independently, without regard to brand renown or general popularity -- in other words, to do like Toucan Sam and "follow my nose." Because when you're out and about giving meaning to the existence of your fragrance, allowing yourself and others to experience and enjoy it, they neither know nor care what shape bottle it came from or even which brand it is. All they care about is what their nose is telling them about the scent you exude. That's the simple fact of wearing and enjoying fragrances. My methodology was to sample each fragrance at the opening, put each tester strip in a separate Ziploc bag, and sample it again after the dry-down. And so it went with approximately 300 samplings over the course of a couple months. As the samplings went on and my confidence in my favorites grew stronger, I began forming my collection. Special thanks to big sales before and after Mother's Day and Father's Day 2021 in the U.S., such as 30% off sales from Lancôme, YSL, and Mugler, as well as a couple 40%-50% discounts on other individual fragrances. Which as a side-note serves as a reminder that patience and strategic/opportunistic buying can save you a lot of money while curating your collection, especially if you buy from retailers. Back to my review of Jean Paul Gaultier's Ultra Mâle. I loved it. Before I even sampled it, I immediately hated the bottle. I mean, the dick bulge is just too much -- what heterosexual male wants to hold that bottle and have his fingers brush up against a dude's crotch? But again, I didn't allow myself to care about the bottle because that was only for the eyes. And in this olfactory journey, the nose was to be judge, jury, and executioner. The judgment: an overall 9/10 on the scent. Both during the opening and dry-down, it was sweet and inviting with no trace of questionable or off-putting smells. So, why is this not rated more highly in the Parfumo community? My theory is that there are two reasons. First, many people don't like the bottle, so they exact revenge on the fragrance for a marketing issue. Not fair. And second, people overreact to hype in a negative way. Maybe if you never heard of the fragrance, you would have given it an 8/10, but because everyone else said "OMG 10/10 MUST BUY!!!", you feel the need to take it down a peg so you rate it 6/10. Again, not fair to the fragrance itself. In case you want to re-examine whether you have fairly rated Ultra Mâle, maybe you can take a look at the nose behind the fragrance. Did you ever think about who created this? Hm... it's Francis Kurkdjian. Of Baccarat Rouge 540 fame. And like 540 and dozens of Kurkdjian's other fragrances, Ultra Mâle is a high-quality work of art. Maybe you can perform the mental exercise of disassociating the fragrance itself from its bottle, from its alias ("The Clubbing King"), and from its hype, and simply let your nose decide. I guarantee the reviewers who gave this fragrance an unbelievably low 0.5 rating for the scent would realize they were just "taking it down a peg" and would admit their rating is artificially suppressed. And hey, maybe overly-sweet isn't your thing and it's only a 6/10, but you are doing others an injustice by fraudulently manipulating the ratings by giving it a 0.5/10. Because as a statement of objective fact, a rating of 0.5/10 would apply categorically to the worst smells you can possibly imagine -- literally raw sewage or worse -- and I cannot conceive of a human who would ever rank this fragrance as being anywhere near the worst smells on earth. In summary, it is my opinion that the ratings should be higher, and each individual should try this fragrance for oneself. Forget about the bottle, forget about anyone else's opinion (unless you're wearing it primarily for your "special someone"), and just let your nose decide. Beyond that, you might already be aware that the sillage and longevity are considered to be on the higher end of the performance spectrum, so you merely need to determine whether the price/value proposition is right for you. Already have five other sweet frags? Maybe skip this. But for me, starting from zero, I happily added this to my collection.

This perfume really introduced me to the world of perfumery. It's definitely for noses that appreciate sweet perfumes! Those who aren't used to fragrances like this might think, as mentioned in some reviews, that it tends more towards the "feminine" side, but I don't share that view. The opening is wonderful, with notes of pear and lavender, then evolving into a more vanilla/cinnamon side of the fragrance. In my opinion, this perfume continues to be "different" in the world of sweet masculine perfumes today. As for performance, I would say that the old batches stand out and, within the Jean Paul Gaultier house itself, Le Male Elixir easily surpasses this one. It's a perfume with great projection, "announcing" its arrival wherever it goes. I would say that it can be used without fear on colder nights (winter/autumn), but for warm climates it's not so interesting, as it can become quite cloying for the people around you! A great perfume and a reminder: you have to like sweets!

So i was a little bit afraid when i ordered online a 125ml version of it. When it arrived the first thing that came to my mind when i smelled it was: PURE POWER. At the first sniffs it is a very strong pear and bubblegum bomb. It has a very good sillage for around 2 hours then it slowly becomes skin nearly with the time. And that is the period when this scent becomes the most pleasing. It slowly turns into a sweet and sophisticated vanilla type scent. The thing i love the most about it that it isnt linear.. it has so many faces as i mentioned. I think it performs the best in a little bit windy weather. It can be also worn in summer imo, just use 1 or 2 sprays bc otherwise it can be overwhelming. If you love sweet type fragrances, then it is a must have for you, also a great clubbing fragrance. Its bottle and packaging is very unique. I got a 125ml version for aroudn 70 euros so i think its ok price for this quality. Edit: This masterpiece received the most compliment on me.

SO, SOO SWEET! Sugar overload. I had to wash it off because it was too much for me. I'm prone to creamier, smoother sweet perfumes. It is strong and bold, colorful and playful. Fruity, yes, but synthetic fruity, like a fruity bubblegum. Even though it is so sweet, I don't find it cloying or sharp. It is a nice perfume if you're into it and I think it is worth the price tag. It is better blended than its dupe 9pm .

Usually I’m not into sweet fragrances, yes I do enjoy an ocasional vanilla/tonka one as muchas the next guy but that’s as far as I go with sweetness. Ultra Male dares turn sweetness up to 11 which should make this annoyingly sweet and unwearable but it somehow works perfectly. Seductive, daring and unique, the ultimate clubbing fragrance.

I remember the first spray and was in amazement! The fruity smell like cotton candy to me! I was like "Yes!!!". Thanks to one of Jeremy Fragrance's videos. Jeremy tends to overhype some brands, but this one was right on the money! I also love the dry down and how the sweet smell morphs into a clean slight fresh soapy smell, simply amazing! I love it!

This fragrance is an interesting one to me. It feels like it should trend young, but somehow does it without feeling unprofessional. Bottle: (??/10) I don’t know how to feel about this design. It’s incredibly iconic, but I feel silly having something that looks like this on my shelf.

I really like the opening of this one—that fruity, sweet pear smell that jumps out and says, “Hey, look at me.” You get hooked straight away. But it's so damn weird, though. And you have to keep in mind: I just said in my previous review that Le Male is a staple every man should have in his collection. In my opinion, Ultramale doesn’t really compare.

Vanilla and cinnamon are not felt intensely. It only helps to spread the fragrance. I don't find it to be a sugary scent in general. It smells more like aftershave, softening detergent, and freshly bought clothing fabric. It's not a niche fragrance. It is probably a scent that has been imitated hundreds of times and has therefore become a classic.

First impression is of a fuzzy and vaguely floral makeup powder that gets sweeter and sweeter by the minute. Takes ~10 minutes to completely open up and suddenly it's as if someone has blown a cloud of perfumed powdered sugar into my eyes. Not the worst thing I've tried, but still very much not my preferred experience. Surprisingly moderate sillage. One spray feels like a dust storm when you're in the epicenter of it, but someone standing an arm's length away will only sense a sweet floral whisper. Takes about an hour to settle down and become breathable. Sweet makeuppy earth. Mellow spice. Sharp honeyed orange blossom. It lingers, unchanging, for another hour; then slowly fades out over the next ~4. Florals fizzle out first, then spice intermixes with dirt and becomes indistinguishable. The drydown lasts into the night and tastes like boredom, sweet dirt and mild disappointment.

Nuit d'Oranger smells like burying your nose in the heart of a flower and sniffing hard, pollen flying in your face and all. It's a very warm scent that brings to mind a sweltering summer afternoon or a hot summer evening following an even hotter day. The floral notes are heavy and heady, accompanied by honeyed sweetness and odd powderiness that to me creates the impression of flower pollen flying around. The warmth and sweetness are highlighted by a hint of hard to describe spiciness that I can't find in the listed notes. It's absolutely *not* fresh, clean or airy as many others in this line are (say Cedrus or Magnolia Alba). Mate and patchouli are not clearly discernable, instead they serve to add structure to the fragrance, creating a very discreet, unsweetened, dry and woody backdrop for the floral-powdery-vanillic main act. I find that it performs well in 24-25 degrees Celsius but starts choking me once we hit 30. It's definitely not meant for extreme heat nor extreme humidity and could easily bother people around the wearer. It opens with a huge, startling burst of projection that recedes over time. In about 3 hours what remains is only a little stronger than a skin scent, although it projects slightly better from fabric (pairs well with flowing fabrics if you enjoy having your scent noticed by those around you). As the bottle and the name seem to suggest it works best for summer evening outings, whether casual or elegant. Personally I find Nuit d'Oranger interesting but not really worth the price. However I don't care for most floral-forward fragrances so don't let my bias stop you from at least trying it out. I wouldn't call it blind-buy safe or a safe gift material, since some folks might find it cloying. My patner for example (coincidentally a person allergic to pollen) was very much not impressed by my high heat wear test.

An incredibly wonderful scent for the evening. Spraying it on is almost like slipping into my favorite evening dress - I feel beautiful and confident in it. The fragrance has something very mysterious and almost animalistic about it; you can't quite put your finger on what it is, but you want more of this seductive elegance. A dark orange, not innocent at all. Definitely addictive.

This scent is a time machine: I am 6 years old again and in my grandmother's bathroom. She had a body care line called Cleopatra (the same brand, not the perfume itself). The bubble bath was in a blue bottle with a golden cap and always stood at the edge of the bathtub (or was it the lotion?), and the matching bar of soap lay by the sink. This scent from Chloé totally reminds me of that bubble bath/lotion, the smell of which I thought I had already forgotten.. I am not good at recognizing individual notes and then sniffing them out according to their composition in the pyramid. Others seem to do that better. But I will try to convey my impression of the scent as best as I can. Primarily, I think of soap and bubble bath. The scent is not citrus-fresh in the sense of colognes (despite neroli and petitgrain), but conveys the feeling of being freshly washed, clean, and creamed (orange blossom). This creaminess remains well perceivable throughout the entire scent journey and becomes denser. The DD smells rich/lush; I suspect this is due to the patchouli in the base, which blends into this dense orange blossom cream. Despite this fullness, I do not find the scent overwhelming or even intrusive (this may be due to my positive association with this smell). In any case, I am glad that Chloé has brought this beautiful memory back to me :) The predominant scent direction of citrus & fruity indicated here does not make sense to me. But that's how perception is.. Edit: The longevity is above average (which is not too surprising for this dense cream dream)! I applied the scent yesterday around 5 PM (on my upper arm) and I can still perceive it there today, the following day, shortly after 7 AM.

Some sequels are mainly big flops .. see the Montblanc Explorer line, Star Wars or even the latest Thor. However, when you have an ambitious young man who wants to study parfumery, even if he is not a chemist only by chance and the good will of Jean Guichard from Givaudan - we now have such gems like Ganymede, Le Parfum and now Le Male Elixir. If you smelled Carlisle, Le Parfum, Delina or Bois Imperial .. you will know what the master perfumer does well: Projection and Performance! When I samples Bois Imperiale, it was literally choking me from the jacket in the next day. Apart from the huge performance, the scents are also very well blended and thought through. Many houses and perfumers like to play it safe, for the sake of the stakeholders .. but not Mr. Bisch, he will do what he needs to do and do it well. • Longevity: It will project abot 4 hours then stay close to skin for the whole day of wear and some more. • This is a playful, sweet scent and if it´s your first JPG bottle then you can´t do anything wrong starting with this one, Bisch does very strong, projecting nice scents and this one is great. I believe this is a must try scent, maybe the hardcore fans of Le Male will not like it, but it is modern, sweet and has a hint of Code Absolu. It will be perfect for office and business wear, but also with jeans and a white t-shirt. I love my Le Parfum bottle and I do not feel the need to buy the Elixir, however if you do not have any of the Le Male into your collection, this is the one to start with. For me it is a one of universe´s mysteries how does PUIG allow such a wonderful creation to come out from their group, when their main target is to create mainstream spams like Phantom, Invictus and such.

Ever tried Tom Ford Vanilla Sex? This is like transfusing that idea for a honey-rooted fragrance. It's a beautiful gourmand that doesn't waste your time with all sorts of unfinished mixes or stupid excuses but instead delivers an obsolete sensual powerhouse. It's probably one of the fragrances that'll get everyone complimenting you. However, there's a big problem with it. It's really overused. I mean, every time you go to a slightly more formal event, there will probably be two to four different guys wearing this fragrance, which would kind of make you feel like an NPC. However, I believe that this fragrance is rightfully overrated, as it definitely delivers.

This is one of my favorite fragrances. Especially the opening is awesome. It is one of the best openings I've ever smelled. It is very sweet and I love sweet fragrances. The longevity and projection is like a beast. The presentation is also great. You get a strong honey and vanilla note with this fragrance.

Wow, so many things happening here. First, a burst of lavender and mint, then, it starts to get warm, a bit sweet. Tobacco appears, vanilla, a kind of black licorice accord too... Then, the honey makes it appearance together with the resinous part of the fragrance. It's weird, because it is fresh because of the lavender and mint, but warm and cosy, because of the honey, benzoin, tonka and tobacco. I'd wear this at cold or rainy days, and at night, while hanging out at bars or a terrace. But, to be honest, it would not surprise me in any other situation. It is noticeable, but not as cloying/bomb as other Elixir fragrances. It is similar to Le Parfum? A little. Is it similar to Xerjoff? A little too. This scent is kind of in the middle ground of sweet scents, you can recognise a couple of accords from different parfums. It is not something completely new, but it will stand out from your collection. When it is dry, a beautiful rough tobacco (similar to Bvlgari MIB in my opinion) softened by a sweeter honey, while all other notes swing around making it a "What's that, let me smell a bit more" kind of scent. Overall, warm, calming, really wearable, made to be like by the masses, stands out (but wont make you the "another Sauvage elixir guy arrived at the club") and it lasts long enough (8-10h). Unisex? Yes yes yes. Safe blind-buy? Well, if you hate sweet, no. If you tolerate it just to a certain point, and you are not afraid of a tobbacco note, you like spices, lavender, mint, and you've been around slightly resinous scents, then yes. My favourite JPG so far. Oh, and the bottle, what a masterpiece, easily new part of the decoration at home.

Yet another juvenile and overly sweet creation by Bisch... seems to be all he does lately. Then again, this is exactly what's hot and trending. It's a tonka/vanillic fog that all the kids are chasing after. nowadays. The blending is actually a disaster here. Perfect if you want to smell like a teenager that is trying to get attention anywhere he can.

I have recently purchased a perfume I was very excited to try. On paper this sounded exactly what I needed . A stronger , maybe even more masculine , long lasting parfume from Jean Paul Gaultier The bottle seemed like it would deliver all that but unfortunately it left me a bit dissapointed. However , that disappointment quickly made me appreciate this parfume even more.

I was very much looking forward for this release, hoping for an amazing debut and long term success, however left blatantly disappointed. I’m going to be very honest here. This fragrance is a mess. Tries very hard to reinvent, amplify, and revolutionize its backbone Le Male dna, unfortunately for me it is a very sad fail.

First of all, this is somehow compared to Versace's eros EDT. The only comparison I can find is that they are both sweet (So are 90% of Fragrances, and they both went through the frat boy timeline ) REVIEW 10/10 performance and looks People say they smell this all the time, which is hard to believe because I've smelled this maybe once.

Best version The scent is beautiful and has a slight difference from the EDT and Le Parfum, but the Elixir version is more beautiful . Some say it is similar to Naxos and Pure Havana, but in reality there is nothing similar between them, they are completely different.

My relationship with fresh laundry scents is a bit divided.. I really enjoy exploring these scents on a test strip, as a fabric softener they are wonderful or as a room spray top.. but so far I never wanted to smell like that myself. For me, they often just aren't skin scents. Chêne starts off as sharply synthetic as The Muse or Love-O-Matic (with The Muse definitely taking the cake). This biting clean scent lingers for quite a while and lily of the valley is distinctly noticeable. This little, inconspicuous flower can pack a punch and clings on.. and that is also the case here, and I was already close to washing it off.. After about an hour, however, the scent calms down and becomes very creamy. I find creamy clean scents quite exciting. From now on, nothing bites anymore; it becomes increasingly vanilla-sandalwood and soft. I can definitely smell the orange blossom as well, but it blends in nicely. However, alongside the vanilla, I also smell a very DISTINCT coconut note that isn't listed. This makes the whole story quite tropical and takes a turn that one wouldn't expect at all.. at least I didn't :) In my opinion, one should appreciate both the fresh laundry vibes and coconut/tropical notes for this scent and be able to handle a certain level of synthetics. The scent positively surprised me with its twist, but for me, a fragrance ultimately needs to fit from start to finish, and that is not the case here.. still, an interesting scent for this category!

The fragrance is very pleasant without any disturbing notes. A woody note is noticeable, yet it remains feminine and soft, as if you were snuggling into leaves. The sandalwood adds a slight creaminess. It could be a bit more long-lasting, but precisely because of its unobtrusiveness, it is very suitable for everyday wear and work.

…. in a spa in the middle of the South Tyrolean Dolomites. Some might think "how nice for her," but I should point out that I am not at all a spa enthusiast. Sweating in the sauna is a horror for me. But now Chêne comes into play…. I close my eyes - breathe in and smell herbs, lily of the valley, and warm, very warm wood. Creamy vanilla joins in and something I always long for in everyday life: relaxation. Maybe I should go to the spa with Chêne more often…… And for some critics, I should note: I was all alone and didn’t bother anyone with a Chêne cloud.

Le Beau Le Parfum Intense, these are my first impressions... Like eau de toilette, with that tropical touch, although lowered, with the coconut less marked and with other notes accompanying, such as pineapple or subdued woods especially noticeable in the drying. The bad part (for me) and the reason why I have almost automatically discarded it, is the tonka bean. F** mania of the brands in loading their current perfumes with this stinging note. What do we get out of it? Turn what could have been a denser tropical fragrance, with more body, perceptible nuances, evolution and "fine", into something "rough", dominated by an excessive sweetness, strident, a global something repetitive, trite, disco and typical of a teenage and noisy age group, like Scandal (never better said). The drying after about 3 hours is more pleasant and bearable with that woody / amber base, where sandalwood is well appreciated, perhaps what it should have been from the beginning (personal taste) and avoid that amount of tonka bean so sharp that, far from improving, covers everything else. I stay, by far, with his sister eau de toilette, who did not invent anything new, which yes, is also sweet, but certainly does not make you diabetic after using it. In any case, if you like very sweet, fruity / woody perfumes with that type of profile, try it

When I hear JPG, the first thing coming into my mind is the awesome Le Male by Francis Kurkdjian, which brought the brand to the big beauty houses table, IMO. Many other attempts have been done, but the Le Male is still the icon of the brand and therefore, hardly anything can even come closer. I owened the Le Beau, because it fooled me in a perfumery .. the top notes were awesome so I ordered one right away, little did I know that it had the longevity of about 1 hour, max. Now I got a sample of the new "Le Parfum" Le Beau, and after the Le Male Le Parfum awesome experience, created by Quentin Bisch .. I thought that the new flanker should be a good one. Oh well .. one should smell a scent first, rather than read reviews or the name of the perfumer: The scent is a fruity cocktail, something you woul experience if you go to an all in holiday at the sea. I liked Le Beau EDT but it had a miserable performance, Le Parfum is performing very well instead but I find it too simple for my taste, just like a one time summer hit.

Coconut, the tropical fruit of the sparkling seas with burning-feet hot beaches aligned perfectly with palm trees, while having a carefree state-of-mind. That's my association with this scent. It's creamy, it's woody, it's tropical, it's delicious. I could almost eat or drink this fragrance. My experience so far with Jean Paul Gaultier fragrances is a good one. Most of them seem to be sweet, fruity and warm. And I suppose I discovered that I really like that at the moment. Le Mâle is cardamom-vanilla vibes, Ultra Mâle is ultra sweet and warm, Le Parfum is Ultra Mâle without the fruity-sweetness and more spice. Although, if tropical sweetness is not your thing, then don't even consider this one. So, without further ado: Do you like woody, creamy coconut vibes? Kind of like a shower oil or in sunscreen? Then get it! The scent opens with a fruity-fresh coconut, which develops into a creamy, woody base. Probably the pineapple and ginger in the opening, and the coconut, tonka bean and sandalwood in the dry-down. Lastly, I want to emphasize that everyone's nose is different and that this review is of course an interpretation of mine. Always sniff it yourself and then decide! Have a fabulous day.

Le Beau Le Parfum takes the classic JPG DNA and runs it through a blue filter. The result? Clean, mass-appealing, and very familiar. Like most blue scents, it’s hard to pinpoint individual notes. They all seem to mishmash freshness, sweetness, and syntheticness together. It opens fairly synthetic but becomes more tolerable and wearable as it dries down. Still, it never fully escapes that feeling. It’ll definitely have you smelling nice and fresh, and it’s hard to go wrong with it. But in terms of uniqueness, it doesn’t move the needle. Blue fragrances tend to stay in the same lane, and this one is no exception. You’ve likely smelled this a dozen times before, and you’ll smell it a dozen times tomorrow.

It's fun to read the reviews here. Our experiences and impressions of perfumes can be so different. For example, someone wrote this is a masculine coconut. Sure, it can be more "feminine", but I would never use the masculine to describe the coconut here, or Le Beau in general. Another user wrote that coconut is less marked here compared to the EDT version. I feel it's precisely the opposite. This one is nothing but coconut with a few slices of pineapple. Instead of "authentic", I'd rather call this coconut synthetic. What I agree with is that it lingers on clothes for ages. Personally, it's a turnoff for 2 reasons: firstly the perfume itself is very linear, becoming dull after a while. It's very creamy, there's nothing refreshing about it. Secondly, it makes me wonder what chemicals are in it that enable it to last so long on clothes. I bought a decant and that's enough for me.

Awesome yummy scent, might give some certain people a headache though. Do not wear this during very hot summers. This is a sweet fragrance and might choke some people out during scorching days. This is a very nice scent, pineapple doesn't last long though, which is a shame. Creamy, woody, sweet afterwards. Also for some reason, I don't get the best longevity on this one.

Starts slow but then is so radiant. Creamy, little sweet, not heavy more on the light side and with that coconut touch. You can feel the 'le Mâle' skeleton if you're used to this brand. Casual style but very sexy. Great longevity and sillage. Perfect for spring, may be a little too much for summer days (but great for night outs).

This is a bad perfume. I recommend you try any other designers before you think about buying this. I own a full bottle of this and I tried really hard to like it, but it's just... eugh. It smells cheap, synethetic, unoriginal and not how it is marketed. The bottle is crass and crude. But like the perfume itself, it doesn't have anything interesting to offer.

The quintessential naughty scent for summer nights. Very tropical and sweet woods and coconut with a light touch of iris. The pineapple is minimally perceptible at the open, but it's there to open the mouth. Outstanding longevity for the price, projection is highly temperature-dependent, but generally heavy; if it's cooler, it's more moderate.

Usually, I do not make reviews when I get a cologne, but I will make an exception for Le Beau. This fragrance is one of if not the most underrated of all time. Maybe I'm just a sucker for coconut, but when I smelt this I nearly ascended into the heavens. When I went home after I smelt this and fell asleep in my cozy bed, I had a dream about Le Beau.

This fragrance is WIERDDD but also kinda grows on ya (for better or worse) Sweet, salty green body wash. Not bad. However it’s synthetic and the sandalwood in this one is polarizing. Kinda reminds me of Gris Charnel where its a synthetic fig fragrance thats mass appealing. Definitely spray it on skin cuz on paper it wont give you the full speech Definitely the more you smell it the more you’ll either like it or hate it. Paradise Garden still keeps that sweet coconut DNA from the le bayt line. It Opens like a green body wash, but dries to a fruitier more playful le beau le parfum. Overhated. I give it a 7/10

Smells like 3/4 Armani Stronger With You Absolutely and 1/4 Kenzo Homme EdT Intense for the first hour, then for the remainder of it, the ratio is reversed and it smells mostly like Kenzo with a dash of Armani. Very strong, cloying and generic. Lasts literally three days, and is impossible to scrub off. I sprayed my hand and wrist for a total of three sprays, and even after several attempts to scrub it off and shower it off - six attempts in total - at first on fervent command from my partner who couldn't stand the scent, and then from my own accord becoming sick of the smell and wanting to get rid of it - it still is a faint skin scent on day three. This is jet fuel performance, and I wish I had never sprayed it. It fills the entire room and you need to open the windows to air it out. To call this a summer fragrance is in my opinion wrong. It has nothing to do with summer. It is heavy, dusty, boozy, cloying, way over-powered, radiant and room filling. Not what a summer fragrance should be. There are way better (summer) fragrances out there, and even as a fall or winter fragrance this just fails. It's too generic to be bothered with. It is too heavy for summer, but too tropical (fig) to be a winter or fall fragrance. I think this was a misstep from Jean Paul, and seems like a rush job to get a summer flanker for 2024 out and also get on board with the ongoing green / herbal trend. To sum up; It is generic, forgettable and regretable.

I decided to test this out because I'm intrigued with Quentin Bisch's works and I do love a fig perfume. It's a very interesting scent tbh. On my skin, I find that it has similarities with Santal 33 (or perhaps Piano Santal?) but this is more coconut-y and creamy. There's also something in here that makes me nauseous for some reason. It's something I find in most male designer perfumes. Perhaps an unlisted ambroxan? I would say a more elegant counterpart of this is Maison Marie no 13 Novelle Vague. That one shares the same vibes as this but it's more aquatic and fresher.

I got this from a buddy for $50. I’ve smelt it before and I wasn’t gonna spend over a $100. But for $50? Yeah, of course! I’m gonna layer it with other things. Like my Al Haramain Amber Oud Carbon Edition (Synthetic GIT clone) to elevate both of them. Try it. Anyways I get the coconut, tanning lotion, sweet vibes. That can be annoying after awhile until you put something that might compliment layered over it and see what happens

Smelled this on paper and loved the mint note in the mix of the coconut and lime. As I wore it several days, I found it was too sweet for me and I couldn't find the difference between this and a women's coconut lime lotion. If that's what you like, go ahead, but you can take a trip to Bath and Body Works for less than half the price to get the same scent.

Yes, another review about another average Gaultier scent that’s so overhyped because of gaultier fanboys and sponsored/dumb youtubers. Aquatic, green and coconut. Yeah. sounds a LOT like many other scents but It’s Gaultier! It should smell better right??? Hell no, fragrance is synthetic. It’s not horrible but pretty average.

I was curious about this scent as I saw the controversial & mixed reviews on tiktok and youtube, so i got myself a sample from notino. First you get a majestic dose of what i think is a nice pineapple smell and i was wishing this is how the fragrance stays, it smelled exactly like a pina colada.

Here's a perfume that I didn't expect at all, and it surprised me very positively! Le Beau Paradise Garden is a tropical, fresh, saline, herbal, green, fruity, and sweet fragrance in short. Of course, Paradise Garden maintains the DNA of the traditional Le Beau, which is that fruity smell of a natural coconut.

Why has this fragrance been so popular since its premiere? I don't know. Although the Le Beau series is not a world championship, I like the other two fragrances and compared to them, Paradise Garden is quite pale and inferior. The green notes that are in the opening come out very vegetal on my skin. I smell fresh cucumber and dill.

This fragrance really seems to be a love it or hate it kind of a scent, personally I think it smells great, nice fresh minty coconut scent. it's a winter scent but can also be easily pulled off in summer!

When I first tried this at the shop, I loved it a lot. The second time I passed by and tried it, I didn't like it. I preferred Cedrus more and purchased it and got a nice free Chloe bag with it. The guy was also kind enough to give me a sample of this to take home and test, but I still didn't like it. I suggest you test it a few times before buying.

As some who enjoys Black Opium (Le Parfum) I don’t think this is similar at all. This opens with a very vintage smell. I don’t know what notes I’m smelling, but it’s not to my taste. The dry down is a bit better, but it does become a skin scent relatively quickly. There’s a note that just doesn’t agree with me. I find this scent really dry and a bit nauseating. To me this smells more like an old fashioned tincture to cure an ailment, more than it does a perfume. Maybe it’s the styrax and cloves, I’m not sure but it’s a hard pass for me.

Orchidée de Minuit is this sexy floral scent that makes us appear mysterious. When you wear this fragrance, you know its effect. It starts beautifully floral and then becomes spicier and darker. I don't pick up the rum strongly. The vanilla comes across as creamy and soft. I am almost hypnotized by this scent DNA. It is a fragrance for seductive evenings and more suited for colder days. But still, I will wear it in the summer months as well. Sexy, sexy, sexy!!!

Is Orchidée de Minuit a groundbreaking new fragrance? No. Will it appeal to many? Unlikely. For me, it is the bolder Black Opium, it dares more. The patchouli plays a dominant role here and gives it more grounding or depth. For me, it’s not musty; in combination with the clove and styrax, it evokes more of a licorice association, in the best sense. Equally intense is the jasmine note, and it is not overshadowed; rather, it becomes “darker” through the rum and patchouli. This makes it mystical, sexy, bold, and seductive for me. An absolute fragrance for nights and evenings when women are fully aware of their feminine allure and want to play with it (while Black Opium is “let’s see what happens,” Orchidée de Minuit is “it will happen, and I have chosen you to be a part of it”). Over time, it becomes “quieter,” “closer to the body,” which for me completes the allure of the fragrance. The vanilla is, of course, a key note from the very first second, but it does not overshadow everything in this perfume. It connects the individual parts into a velvety sound. From the new blue line, my favorite. Longevity is above average for me.

"Le Beau" by Jean Paul Gaultier is a simple but alluring release: It's all about bergamot, coconut shell and tonka bean... And even the bergamot is just a little bit to introduce and balance the scent. . So not much olfactory complexity here (apparently), although - IMO - it has an original and genial vibe. It's a very well made fragrance. Sometimes simplicity is all you need to wear, and here you have a very nice charming scent with a little wink of wizardry. - Longevity & Projection: The performance of this release is OK, about 6 to 8 hours with average projection first (+1h) and moderate later. - Occasions & Mood: For me it's best on warm days, but not too hot (22° - 27° C): Warm spring & fall afternoons and refreshing summer sunsets. Good for dates and hangouts with friends; chill, casual..."Le Beau" has a comfy tropical vibe that fits very well on these occasions. - Conclusion: An easy, sweet and tropical-woody scent. Very cozy and a prominent seducer.

Very good scent. At first I can feel coconut flakes, and after a while the scent smooths out into a sweet and creamy coconut-tonka base, which lasts until the end. Its simplicity is only an advantage for it, a very pleasant comforter with good parameters (clearly noticeable 8h+). The perfect choice for someone looking for a coconut scent clearly on the masculine side.

Changes in men's perfumery happen so slowly they make glaciation look precipitous. Eau Sauvage was king for 22 years before Cool Water stole his Fresh crown, and it was 17 years before Le Mâle replaced Azzaro pour Homme as the go-to fougère. Bleu de Chanel has been around for thirteen years, so we may not be stuck with millimetric adjustments to its Spiky Wood formula for that much longer. However, in the mean time; the flacon of Beau may resemble Le Mâle but the juice inside is pure Bleu.

Definitely a perfume to seduce. A Fragrance reminiscent of a coconut-based tropical drink. Therefore, it combines a lot with the climate of my South American region. And it gets me compliments. Regarding the lasting, it lasts wonderfully on my skin, an average of 10 hours. Regarding the projection, it has an intense projection in the first hour and a half, then it gets closer to the skin, but always noticeable, it creates a kind of aura in me.

TLDR: If you're under 25 and live somewhere that its warm out more often than not, this is a no brainer as far as designer goes. (Overspray it though it lasts long but doesn't project without doing so) For my proper review: Le Beau, especially the edt is what I would consider to be the best scent on skin if you can say yes to 2 questions. 1. Is it over 60 degrees out? 2. Are you younger than 25? If you check those 2 boxes, this is going to be what I would say is the best readily available fragrance from the designer market. This, Valentino uomo Born in Roma, and Prada L'homme L'eau, are what I would consider to be the 3 best designer fragrances. This isnt because of their scent though, I consider them the best because they provide something that is either unique, or lost. To brush over the other two, with Valentino Uomo, you get what is essentially Invictus aqua 2016 but made into something younger guys can pull off in any occasion and season. With L'homme L'eau, you get an undeniably unique yet inoffensive scent for work or school. The reason I believe Le Beau to be the best thing from a designer for younger guys is because of 2 reasons, the first reason being that its so oddly versatile considering what it is and what its notes are. The coconut is strong at the top but you also get that tonka bean bringing it back down to being wearable in cooler temperatures, by no means does that mean this is the best option for fall/winter, even in the morning. But regardless of better options for those seasons its still absolutely wearable around that time (which is where age comes into play). My second reasoning is that Le Beau is just genuinely my most complemented designer fragrance, and not only is it my most complimented designer fragrance but it even stands up to some of the niche fragrances in my collection. Le Beau really does punch above its weight and even if its not the greatest thing I own scent wise, for some reason girls around my age range (sub 25) all absolutely adore it, Ive had friends of friends, acquaintances, all kinds of people who have told me that it smells gorgeous completely unprompted. This fragrance even earned me the coveted "Getting stopped by a random woman in public" award at the grocery store a couple months ago. As for the review I'm going to keep it simple and sweet cause that's what this fragrance really is. Le Beau opens up with an absolute blast of coconut and some subtle tonka bean which balances out the coconut. The bergamot isn't immediately noticeable in the fragrance but if you look for it, you'll find it. The bergamot is pleasantly received, but does not overstay its spotlight. Its still there for the heart but what you really get is that now woody coconut stepping down and making way for gorgeous tonka bean at the base, this is where this juice really shines. However, and my one gripe about this fragrance, is that its a beast that runs on adrenaline. And when that adrenaline fades, you're left wishing you sprayed more of it. This is the one fragrance that I decide to wear beforehand even if its still what I would consider to be casual, and that's because any time I wear it I make sure to spray at least 8+ times depending on the occasion which in result means I need to give it around 30 minutes or so to calm down, in spite of it not performing well in the department of projection. Anything you spray this on more than 1 time will smell like it till its washed pretty much. In summary, this is the best from the JPG Line and arguable the best designer fragrance relative to what it offers and what it brings to the table and really is a tried and tested complement puller.

This fragrance gets a lot of hate for some reason. I really enjoy this one from jpg. It’s like scandal edt but more fresh. Is it the best jpg? Hell no, but it still is a solid one! Got my 75ml bottle for 50 bucks! I wouldnt really pay more for it because there are indeed better options like le male parfum or even the intense version of le beau. But for what it is its great!

...not a masterpiece, actually rather simple, and totally not the kind of scent I'd usually wear - but surprisingly, especially since other JPG scents except for Fleur du Male have not been to my liking, I found myself enjoying it quite much.

I saw this parfume in numbers of videos, so i gone to sephora to review the scent, and at first i didnt like it, but in 2/3 minutes the scent gone high and higher, summery, you’ll hear coconut, some woody stuff, probably the palmwood coconut, and something like cardamom. Thats what “le beau” sounds on me, i genuenly love it, try it and buy this banger.

Le Beau is the definition of how to mix coconut with both gourmand and citrusy elements. It's a great early spring or evening scent for someone who wants a tropical masculine edge with some sensuality. I truly love it, however, there are some things I want to point out, and that is the lack of ideas for the mix.

First, the bottle. The iconic but more sculpted and angular shape of a barechested torso compared to previous editions is the same already used for Le Mâle Essence de Parfum, here the bush is covered with a golden vine leaf. The juice inside is emerald green, so vicious, so luscious. The sailor Querelle from Brest is now Adam in the Garden of Gaultier.

Is it just me, or are sport flankers getting better as the years go by? I was expecting to be bored silly by Boss Bottled Sport, however I'm surprised to admit that I'm actually enjoying it. Boss Bottled Sport opens with a gloriously refreshing grapefruit accord. This grapefruit top note is less sour than it is in other perfumes, and is quite sweet and invigorating on the skin. Most fascinating to my nose is the appearance of the aldehydes, which provide a soft, powdery quality, that somehow works. Cardamom and lavender in the heart keep this fragrance smelling masculine and spicy. I adore the scent of lavender on my men, so this fragrance works a treat. I am almost tempted to suggest Boss Bottled Sport to my boyfriend this Summer. The original Boss Bottled is a real hit with the ladies, so it's no surprise that Boss Bottled Sport evokes a similar reaction. I'm actually shocked that this flanker isn't more popular. I believe that many men may be avoiding it just like I did, thinking that it's just another boring, sport-inspired flanker. Not so, folks! Like any scent that is gym-appropriate, Boss Bottled Sport has a fairly light projection, however the longevity is applaudable. To my female nose, it smells both fresh and sexy. I highly recommend. Original review written: October 2012.

It seems to be an ironclad rule that every mainstream brand has its sport fragrances. Hugo Boss has just released one, specifically in the Bottled line. The Hugo Boss brand strongly connects with the scent experiences that people have with shower gels from Axe and Co. This is mass-appealing, always works, and in some cases, the commissioned perfumers have indeed achieved great things in this field. The Bottled fragrances are not that bad, especially Bottled Night has rightly gained attention on Parfumo. After such a good predecessor, one is eager to check out the new Bottled Sport. Well, unfortunately, Boss Bottled Night cannot be compared to Sport. It’s a dilemma with sport fragrances - if you know one, you know them all. Again, it’s a thin, synthetic note with a citrusy touch that characterizes the scent and only slowly fades away - accompanied by a boring, ordinary, and somewhat scratchy background. I don’t feel much development beyond that - the fragrance feels static and lifeless. Just something to tick off, this is by far the weakest scent in the line. I don’t want to smell like this, and I don’t want something like this near me. Fragrances like Boss Bottled Sport are the cheap filler sold to the uninformed and inexperienced. However, Hugo Boss can do better. Those who generally like the direction represented by Hugo Boss and are looking for something light and fresh would be much better off with Boss in Motion Edition White. It has already survived for 3 years and is - unlike other variants of the In Motion line - still in the range. Quality usually prevails, even at Hugo Boss.

Yuck, it’s sticky! Even with the rather arbitrary topic of sports, one of the most annoying scent suppliers fails miserably. Forget the pyramid you see above; in this overly sweetened generic slush, you won’t find either lavender or vetiver, and unfortunately, not even sport. Sport fragrances may not be everyone’s cup of tea, but most of them have at least adhered to the honor code of providing a fresh breeze for fitness enthusiasts. Not so with Boss! The latest flanker of the already questionable original scent smells like a mix of last year's Boss Orange and asleep feet, so the same recipe of fermented mushy fruit and clumsy chemistry lab concoctions that fogs up the Dougis and Müllers of the republic year after year. As usual, slightly cheesy and pre-warmed. Of course, we knew not to expect much here, but such nonsense is truly extremely annoying!

Actually, I’m not a fan of sports and I agree with Churchill: Sport is murder! But since today, there’s an exception: Boss Bottled Sport. And actually, I’m not a fan of sport fragrances either. But again, there’s an exception today: Boss Bottled Sport! It’s brand new on the market and fresh is its keyword! Well, fresh is probably what all sport fragrances are, but the new Boss is particularly so. I tested it today at Müller completely unbiased and ... Woooooow!!!! The grapefruit opens it with a sporty, fresh breeze. I immediately think of the sea ... High waves, beach, sun, and cool cocktails. Boss Bottled Sport inevitably reminds me of Cool Water in its base note, just that it’s not as heavy and overpowering. I also perceive a touch of Chopard’s Heaven. It also reminds me of Nightflight before the reformulation. However, it has nothing in common with the original Bottled and the Night version. It could just as well be a completely new Boss fragrance. Then the lavender comes to the surface and gives it a certain fullness and seriousness that I miss in many sport fragrances. The longevity, however, is not really impressive, at least on my skin. I tested the fragrance around 4 PM and by 9 PM, there was almost nothing left to smell ... However, I still perceived it very intensely on the test strip for a long time. I did find one negative point: the price! About 74 euros for a 100 ml bottle at Müller seems quite steep to me. Were the original Bottled and Bottled Night also that expensive when they were first released? Otherwise, the new one from Hugo Boss clearly stands out from most sport fragrances for me. I would rather describe it as a summer fragrance than a pure sport scent. Soooo, now summer can come ;)

Now I would like to express my thoughts on this long-lost and forgotten fragrance, although I will be defending my position quite alone. As bad as the reviews are here, I must say I do not find it that way. But hold on! The gallows shall wait until I have spoken. It all began with me as a child, who always stopped at the fragrance shelves of the drugstore. But this one captivated the little boy in the duty-free shop at the airport, while waiting for the long-awaited first flight. And so it happened that I finally received this masterpiece after one of my father's next long business trips. It was my first perfume just for me, and I was correspondingly proud to wear it every day. To defend my father here, I must mention that he was never as much of a fragrance enthusiast as I am, and thus he simply bought this scent for me after I expressed my liking. So this perfume was my daily scent for the next few years, which I would not have traded for anything. But over time, I started to collect a few more drugstore fragrances, so this one was not used as often anymore. Thus, I eventually got on the right track and began using higher-quality perfumes. But I hope you understand now why this little scent from Boss cannot simply be dismissed with a wave of the hand. It has simply carved out its own place in my nose and brain. This fragrance is linked to so many memories for me that it has probably been rated too highly because of these two points. However, I find this synthetic fresh start very pleasant. It radiates familiarity for me, just like Acqua di Gio probably does for many others in connection with their father or grandfather. And yes, it quickly transitions from the fresh start to the skin-close phase, as is known with many Boss fragrances. The transition from heart to base note also happens extremely quickly, and after a short time, I only smell a mixture of lavender, vetiver, and a bit of tonka bean. After about 4-5 hours, it’s over, and you have to start all over again to enjoy it once more. No, joking aside, I can understand if someone does not want to own this fragrance. And I wouldn’t either if I hadn’t experienced so much with this scent. But it is simply too important to me for me to part with it. Moreover, I find the bottle simply too beautiful not to look at it from time to time. Now you know why this strange fragrance is in my collection, along with some relics from the drugstore. Don’t worry, you don’t have to endure this scent yourself, as it has not been produced for quite some time. So now that I have shared my thoughts and explained my journey to perfume, it’s up to you to either pack the gallows away or let it reign. I really hope it is clear why I feel this way about this perfume; perhaps you also have a "nostalgic scent"?

Okay, it's not so bad that you scream Igitt or Puuuh, but Buuuh is definitely allowed! It smells like any generic Fa, Rexona, Axe, or whatever shampoo, really weak and pathetic for Boss to think they could so easily jump on the sporty fragrance bandwagon... why even jump on at all?^^ The train is heading straight for a wall...

At some point, the folks at Boss must have realized that after discontinuing the green Hugo Sport, they no longer had a dedicated sport fragrance in their lineup. As the entire competition launched one fresh sport variant of well-known scents after another, Boss found themselves under pressure.

Anyone who thinks that freshness and gourmand are a contradiction in terms should be enlightened by Boss Bottled Sport. The fruity top note is already refined with a distinctly noticeable nutmeg spiciness. The fragrance has that radiant freshness of Cool Water Game by Davidoff, but combines it with a cozy warmth (gentle memories perhaps of d or dunhill edition).

This perfume is masterpiece. Congrats Quentin Bisch really. I like his perfumes. I smell tasty pear, and a lot of HAZELNUT cream, caramely nutty effect. In here Vanilla is helper note. You dont smell directly vanilla its with pear. Im not always a gourmand lover(I dont like Lancome La vie est belle or THİERRY mugler Angel). But perfume needs at least 1 try At Sephora shops. Very good staying on my clothes. 4-5 days, exactly. Dont overspray it maximum 2-3 spray. Delicious, peary, hazelnuttish(nutty) , gourmand. Drydown has vetiver touch.

I really love this scent. To me its a pear and vanilla dessert, it’s sweet but with a freshness to it. I blind bought it because of all the hype this perfume gets on YouTube, and now I can just agree, love love love! I think it’s a crowd pleaser and signature worthy all year rounder, will stay in my collection as long as it exists.

I’m pretty indifferent about pear notes in fragrances, but I absolutely adore the pear in the JPG La Belle perfumes. I also love the intense flanker to the original, but this review is for the OG. La Belle starts off with a very loud and strong syrupy blast of pear and vanilla. You don’t get much else until a few minutes pass and the floral notes and amber come in. The leather and vetiver aren’t super perceivable here for me until the late dry down when the the sugary sweetness has had time to really wear out. It’s STRONG, SWEET, super feminine, slightly fresh, and a wonderful crowd pleasing scent. Men and women alike absolutely love this one and i must say its definitely sexy. To me, this is very much a gourmand but done in a grown woman way. It’s playful, it’s sensual, it’s delicious, and it lingers well on your skin and clothes for hours and hours. I think the OG works well in all seasons besides summer, and is appropriate for day / night use. Would make an excellent date night / sexy night out scent, but can also be worn more lightly during the day. I decluttered this at one point and just recently got it back because of how much I was missing it. She’ll always have a spot in my collection.

Everything has been said about this perfume, so I’m writing this for me as a memory. The perfume is a gourmand. To me it smells like marshmallows toasted over an open campfire. There’s a bit of smokiness to it and it’s very cozy when worn. I would consider this a winter or fall perfume for myself. I also believe this is a unisex fragrance. The bottle is beautiful. Sillage and longevity is excellent. Probably worth a 9 ml buy. I would not buy this in a larger bottle because I would not wear it every day.

This fragrance is sweet enough to make anyone want to take a bite! I don't necessarily smell pear as much as a synthetic cherry/licorice type aroma. It smells "sticky" but there is a barely-there-impression of smoke and leather that gives it that slight bit of edginess. This could be dangerously addictive! However, I could also see it being cloying to some, especially in hot weather. Best to stick to the cooler months with this one.

Upon first spraying La Belle EDP, I immediately think that this is the female version of Ultra Male, by this designer. Two different scents, with overlaps, and really the same concept. Juicy pear and bergamot kick things off here.

sweet, smooth and juicy. like eating roasted pears with sugar during date night. not so sweet that you feel disgusted but not as strong as i had expected. i was pleasantly surprised and i seriously think this can be signature scent worthy. at least on my skin, it seems to need two spritz per zone. overall, this is a delicious fragrance.

I discovered this fragrance rather late, and after reading so many glowing reviews, I must admit my disappointment. On my skin, it leans excessively sweet, with a dissonant undertone that recalls burnt rubber. Perhaps it's the leather note creating this effect, but the result strikes me as overly synthetic and unrefined.

after smelling it from the cap in a store and thinking it's quite pleasant, i got disappointed during the wear-time. the pear here is not a fresh, juicy one that I'm looking for, but rather dried and candied, or like a pear compote.

This perfume reminded me of a romantic evening in Morocco because it is sweet, spicy, woody, and a bit oriental in scent. The first note I perceived immediately upon spraying was warm and resinous with a slight undertone of vanilla. Then, along with the fruity, sweet raspberry, a woody, earthy elegance unfolded. I find this scent to be very occasion-specific; personally, I would only wear it in the evening when going out to a restaurant.

Sweet fruity raspberry scent full of energy and zest for life. At the same time, it has a woody warmth that envelops its wearer. A lovely delicate vanilla nuance makes it sensual and very attractive. Overall, an elegant, eye-catching fragrance that I enjoy wearing very much. What I particularly like is the long-lasting quality, and that it suits any occasion. Although the scent is strong, it does not come across as overpowering. It seems to appeal to both the women and men around me, as I am often complimented on it. Whether young or old, it seems to please. Perhaps it simply matches my personality and thus feels harmonious. In contrast to Boss Alive, I find it more robust and somehow cheekier, stronger, and even more suitable for the confident woman.

I liked the beginning; however, it was also a note that I encounter quite often - red effervescent powder. Effervescence lifts the spirits, but I don't need it in 100 versions, as it already appears in Absolutely Me and lasts longer there. The scent quickly became very creamy. Creamy fragrances are great, but even there, one or two are enough to be soothing, like a cashmere blanket, like Nivea cream when I was a child. Effervescence and cream - both are great, but neither is new, and I don't need both in duplicate. I would have appreciated a scent that I haven't experienced on my skin in this form before, as some comments hinted at something different :-)

Dear perfume lovers, Normally, I am not a fan of the BOSS line, as they all seem to fade away too quickly and often lack something special. But something prompted me to test BOSS Alive, and it immediately found a place in my collection. It has a wonderful freshness. Raspberry and benzoin are very dominant, but the vetiver also subtly makes its presence known. I am surprised by the longevity and sillage. I enjoy wearing this fragrance at work, as it is not too overpowering, yet I still receive compliments on my wonderful scent. I have become quite a fan of it: whether in everyday life, at the beach, or in the office, it always creates a cozy and relaxing atmosphere. To my own surprise, I really like it!

Sophia was a dreamer. She loved wandering in the realms of scents and letting them caress her. One day, she discovered the enchanting fragrance of Australian sandalwood. Silky soft and creamy delicate, it enveloped her senses and transported her to a world full of harmony. The scent was subtle, almost a bright aura surrounding her. It began with a gentle citrus note at the top, which gradually unfolded into a blossom. Sophia couldn't help but surrender to this fragrance and enjoy it to the fullest. But there was a catch. The scent was so gentle that it lasted only a maximum of five hours. Sophia knew she had to make the most of this time to fully immerse herself in the world of this sandalwood. She let it guide her as she wandered through the world. The people around her noticed Sophia's presence. They felt the hint of sandalwood that surrounded her and were touched by its grace. Sophia became the muse, the embodiment of the fragrance that was so much more than just a perfume. In those five hours, Sophia felt angelic. She was one with the scent that enveloped her and allowed it to lead her into a world full of charm. It was a brief but intense time in which Sophia could indulge in her dreams. As the time ran out and the scent of sandalwood slowly faded, Sophia returned to reality. But she knew she would never forget this experience. The fragrance had shown her that it was possible to dive into another world for a brief moment and be enchanted by its beauty. ____________________________ Beautiful it is, the "Atelier des Fleurs - Santalum | Chloé" - although very expensive. For the 5 hours it lasts, it is a dreamily beautiful sandalwood scent that I could easily fall in love with. I am still struggling with myself whether I really want to spend so much money on it. However, I like its calm, subtle nature, as there is nothing brutal in this sandalwood scent, unlike many other fragrances of this kind. This is a truly fine, very naturally elegant woody scent that, in my opinion, has no synthetic undertones. It is silky soft, creamy delicate, bright, filigree, subtle, and caressing. Definitely worth testing. The bottle is also very pretty - typically Chloé.

Chloé 2022. One more in the Infinite Collection, they said in marketing. Australian sandalwood? What can one think of that? In any case, after today’s wearing, I feel rather puzzled. I don’t know why I always associate sandalwood with strong and loud fragrances. Not the one from Tom Ford with all the fanfare. Also not the one from Perris Monte Carlo, which came across as rather subtle and molecular to me. Here, I experience a soft and bright floral scent. Subtle sweetness and even subtler wood. It is cozy, fleeting, calm, and sensitive. One-dimensional, yes, but very pleasant on every nose. I think of cream pudding, light musk, Nivea shower gel for Women. Quiet and close to the skin. It lasts 5 hours on my skin. I like it, but it lacks “punch.” I personally find that a shame for the price. Maybe someone will still go for it. It is truly angelic and innocently beautiful.

Gaultier 2 is delicious, but not so much in a gourmand sense, rather I liken the scent to something quite boozy, like vanilla flavoured rum. It smells dangerous and sexy, as well as being quite warm and comforting. Vanilla and amber dominate this fragrance, however I sense subtle hints of tobacco and powder as well. It's a fragrance for both men and women. I feel so empowered wearing Gaultier 2. It unleashes a lot of sensuality and confidence which is often hidden within me. I think on a man, this scent would be uber-sexy. I must add that the lasting power on my skin is very impressive, withstanding some showers even. Because of its richness and potency, I can't guarantee that everybody will love it, let alone find it inoffensive. It falls under an oriental category, and I'll agree that at times, it can be a little heavy. I have grown to love Gaultier 2, and I'm quite satisfied with my little mini of it, however it's probably not something I would want to own by the gallons.

I really like this fragrance, as it is simple based upon the 3 notes listed, I would also say it is complex as it gives off 2 different illusions for me. 1 is a grape note that appears throughout the fragrance. The smell reminds me of the bubble gum called Bubblelicious! ( GRAPE ) flavored.. It smells really nice as I love the smell of grape. I also get a nice boozy whisky accord that is mixed with the vanilla to create a cappuccino smell. It has GREAT longevity & it leaves a nice trail to follow. Last all day. & is sure to get you noticed regardless of people may like it or not. A nice gourmand that is perfect for clubs, bars or weekend activity.

You know, there are times when a unisex fragrance is truly unisex. Unfortunately, this is not one of them. There's a whole heck of a lotta woods or patch in Gaultier^2, the kind of woods and patch that wears like an aftershave or splash cologne on me. Women who have difficulty crossing over to the other side should steer clear of Gaultier^2, which is all male on me.

Fellow fragrance traveler Awesomeness sent me an adorable mini of Jean-Paul Gaultier Gaultier² a while back, and unfortunately I did not notice that the top became loose in transit. While ferreting through my sample queue this morning, I discovered that most of the liquid had evaporated! All that was left was a small amount of extrait of extrait: thick, dark brown, and a bit scary looking. Undaunted, I added water and shook it up, then used a sprayer to apply the resultant solution as I would any eau de parfum. I have to say that I'm glad that I did! Gaultier² is a simple yet appealing fragrance with a thick somewhat in-your-face sweetness and labdanum amber combined with some kind of woody components(s). To my nose, this is more feminine than masculine. Although it is strong and quite far from being subtle, it smells very good and would make a great wintertime fragrance, as it fits well into the comfort scent category occupied by the likes of Chôpard Casmir, among many other creations which I do not wear that often but enjoy when I do. Perhaps I should not be surprised, given the perfumer, Francis Kurkdjian, but I have had limited experience with this house, and it was negative, so I did not have the best of expectations in donning this fragrance today. I am not sure that I need a bottle of this particular creation (although I'm sure that I'd wear it now and then, if I had some), but now my perspective on Gaultier has been changed, and I'll have to try some more of the perfumes of this house. Thank you Awesomeness!

This is definitely an interesting one. I get sweet, boozy vanilla, and a hint of orange blossom (I hear that orange blossom happens to be a signature of the perfumer Francis Kurkdjian). There is also a hint of something fruity there, like a blackcurrant/grape note (some people mentioned "bubblegum"). What this strikes me as is a burnt caramel/rum-drenched vanilla vibe but I also get the amber in the background. I would say it's predominantly vanilla, but not in a creamy way, this is more of a dark, almost burnt, vanilla-rum kind of smell, a lot like the vanilla you find in Guerlain fragrances (i.e. Shalimar). Overall I think it's sweet and a little gourmand but not overtly so. To me it's quite sensual and blends well with warm skin, giving off a very warm and inviting vibe. Would smell great on men or women, I find it quite playful and flirtatious. Very alluring, and although some may find it sweet, I find it actually balances perfectly, it's on the "darker" side of gourmand-sweet really (cognac & crème brûlée). Definateley a cozy, sexy scent for colder nights with loved ones by the fire. Very warm and very nice.

This one really grew on me. I did not like it at first, found it a bit cheap or ordinary/trashy smelling. But I kept sampling it, again and again. I felt some similarities to Amouage Reflection Man, but only at a certain point. Reflection was softer, this felt heavier. But I grew into liking it.

First I would like to thank all the enablers on here for piquing my curiosity about Gaultier 2 and finally getting around to blind buying this with confidence after the reviews. The fact that Kurkdjian was behind this was also a selling point for me, I have yet to dislike anything he creates. This is truly a beauty and true to its note pyramid.

I soooo wanted to like this. After reading several reviews and based on the notes, this looked like a total winner to me. Vanilla, amber, musk, what could go wrong? Right? Well, a lot actually. There must be many more notes in this composition that aren't mentioned and one or more of these just don't work for me. Right after spraying, I gagged. The first note is awful.
Gaultier 2 has a nice opening, but then turns to a musky bubble gum smell, which it's actually good, but not my cup of tea. I guess its more suitable for woman. Updated January 2014

To be honest i really don’t understand the hype. Gaultier 2 is just another of those perfumes that died the way it lived: as a perfect unknown and unimportant. It’s sickly sweet and sirupy, very similar to Joop Homme and with some classic Le Male vibe.

What can I say about Scandal pour Homme? Well, what is scandalous is the number of compliments I receive with this fragrance… As simple as that. I don't know how the hype for this doesn't reach the stars - maybe the famous reviewers don't go out at night anymore - because the results in me are frankly scandalous: Pretty much every woman I meet gives me at least one compliment. It might smell especially good on me, but I don't think that's the case. Let's be clear, I'm not a teenager anymore and I don't go out on that plan. Also, I usually wear a suit (more casual, but I like suits, period) and clearly I don't look like a youngster. So let's demystify prejudices: - Some famous reviewers say it's for teens: FALSE. I'm over 40 and I’ve received very positive attention from women under 30, women in their thirties, and women over 40. - Smells great, but it's generic: FALSE. I’ve tried all the new designer fragrances. null have given me anything remotely similar. The key, and this is the real key, is how it smells in the air… This potion is pure magic. - It’s extremely sweet and dense: FALSE. It’s very sweet, especially if you smell it in a tester, but when it dries on the skin the scent has an effect that is close to animalic without being so; it remains clean, sweet, creamy and inviting. In addition, the tangerine induces a considerable freshness that lasts a long time. Fragrance details: Above-average projection, with a heavy trail and great longevity: The performance doesn’t disappoint. Excellent. … What else do you want? Do you also pretend it to change your life or revolutionize the world? Age: Well, I already talked about that. Unisex? Although a woman can wear it, it isn’t a scent that I would recommend at all: There’re much better options for them. Occasions? For me, this is a perfume that I see exclusively for cocktail parties, clubbing and date nights. Contrary to what many reviewers say, I see it more striking in well-dressed men, not in adolescents (for them I also think there’re better proposals). So only twilight or night… That’s all. I wouldn’t wear this perfume on any other occasion. Finally: You can already read the notes of the fragrance, there is nothing special about them apparently. But listen, it gets addictive… And in my case, the effect is ​​scandalous (like that inspired song by Prince).

Scandal must be what fragheads refer to as "screechy". The caramel sweetness combines with the aromatics to create a nose-tingling and head-splitting concoction. The bombastic opening is reminiscent of Paco Rabanne Phantom. I am not a fan of sickly sweet scents such as these but I would pick Phantom over this if I had to. These scents smell like something children would wear but apparently adult men wear them to go clubbing and to impress the ladies. If I understand correctly, men wear sweet scents only because women like sweet scents and they want the ladies to move in for a whiff. To that I say, it is a good thing men do not have to dress like women to attract them.

Since I was planning to buy some samples of Scandal pour Homme Le Parfum and Scandal pour Homme Absolu , I felt obliged to try the original Scandal pour Homme as well, purely for reference and comparison to the other two when I'll test them and write their reviews. So, what I get with Scandal pour Homme is an immediate synthetic blast, mixed with some pumped up creamy sweetness from the tonka bean. There's also a caramel in there somewhere, but it's not very prominent. I get more of a toffee kind of smell, which I guess is somewhat similar to caramel. The clary sage note adds some freshness and herbaceous feel, as well as a clear lack of balance to the composition, but after a while it dissipates noticeably. The vetiver tries its best to bring some of that earthy/woody dryness, yet it's a difficult task when you're engulfed in syntheticness and bothering sweetness. The fragrance also lacks proper development. It's pretty much the same from start to finish. And in terms of quality, I thing the couple of times I mentioned 'synthetic' should be enough to give you an idea of it. I imagine someone rebel, cocky, and scandalous would smell like this, which I suppose that's who this fragrance was made for. For an eau de toilette, Scandal pour Homme did quite well in terms of longevity. I got around 8 hours until it would pretty much vanish from my skin. And projection-wise, for the first hour I had a solid one foot bubble around me, but afterwards this bubble would pop and settle down plenty. Given its synthetic nature, I also went nose-blind quite quickly to it. So I did need some help from a couple of friends in order to determine its projecting power and longevity. So in terms of sprays, I wouldn't really put on more than 5, really. For occasions, this pretty much falls into the daily/leisure wear category. I wouldn't wear this to more special situations since it's too synthetic, immature, playful, and bland for most events. Sure, you could definitely rock this at a party/club, but personally, I don't think I'd want to smell like this - synthetic and sweet - in those situations. No, actually, I don't think I'd want to smell like this in any situation. It's just a generic, annoying, poorly-executed fragrance. And what really makes Scandal pour Homme redundant is the fact that you've got many better options out there. Many better in this same ballpark of designer-ish sweetness and genericness, but also many that are simply better executed. There's certainly people that will like this, for one reason or another. But I still stand to my point: there's better options out there which just make Scandal pour Homme not worth the money, nor a consideration. Overall Rating: 5.9/10

Scandal pour Homme revolves around three keynotes—clary sage, caramel, and vetiver—later joined by a fourth, the tonka bean. Like D’Artagnan joining the three Musketeers, tonka completes the ensemble and gives this review its title. Dumas’s tale of camaraderie and character feels like the perfect parallel to this scent’s own alliance of notes. But instead of retelling his story, I’ll share my impressions of one of Jean Paul Gaultier’s more recent creations. Scandal pour Homme is an amber-woody-fougère with soft, spicy undertones. Its sweetness shines brightest, lending the fragrance a smooth, lighthearted charm. The opening may feel familiar—evoking memories of a Paco Rabanne composition. It’s not revolutionary or daring, but rather a well-polished evolution of Le Beau Mâle —swapping milky coconut for burnt caramel. And that’s perfectly fine; solid craftsmanship has its own appeal. On skin, Scandal feels persuasive, sweet, and quietly sensual. The opening reveals silvery clary sage, brushed with a touch of citrus brightness. Sage leaves and mandarin peel intertwine to form a creamy, slightly metallic accord, soon joined by tonka’s warm, ambery depth. The tangy freshness fades quickly, making room for something more indulgent. A chewy, burnt caramel heart soon takes center stage. Smoky, salty, and buttery tones flow together without tipping into dessert territory. Beneath the sweetness lies a faint powdery nuance—perhaps from violet leaf or iris root—adding sophistication. A soft suede-like leather hums in the background, tempering the sugar with texture and warmth. Despite its gourmand elements, Scandal remains balanced—sweet, but never cloying, unlike Ultra Mâle. In the drydown, roasted tonka beans emerge, releasing cozy whiffs of vanilla and talc. Vetiver joins in with its cool, earthy, and slightly smoky accents—clean and green rather than dark or inky like Encre Noire Eau de Toilette . The result feels like the gentle warmth of a firelit room: inviting, round, and slightly creamy. Scandal pour Homme performs best in cooler months—autumn through early spring—when its sweetness feels comforting rather than overwhelming. It suits evening wear, nights out, or simply moments when you want a soft aura of confidence. It may not break new ground, but it wears its style with grace and reliability. A bottle I’ve owned since October 2022 has only deepened my appreciation. Scandal pour Homme is not a rebel—it’s a well-dressed companion, charming in its familiarity and steady in its warmth. -Elysium

Based on the notes listed I expected Scandal to be sweet and chocolatey, something like Paco Rabanne Pure XS Night. In reality, it opens rather sour, almost like 1 Million. After a few minutes the scent becomes mostly nutty, and it stays like that. It's nutty, sour, and aromatic, with little outright sweetness. It's more salty than sweet.
