Scandal is similar to 1 Million Parfum, although with differences (not as all over the place, no florals, nut instead of the coconut). It's similar to Valentino Uomo, if I remember correctly. Lattafa Hayaati Al Maleky also comes to mind, although it goes all-in and overboard on the fresh-nutty combo. Scandal is cleaner, sharper, and more reserved. I would say it's not very scandalous, more like weird. It's also more cold than warm. The drama, if any, is of the courtroom type, not the orgy type. Overall, a decently pleasant scent, sharp in a good way, somewhat shocking. Suitable for a Christian Bale psycho stock broker type. The greyness of the bottle fits the scent pretty well. Not sure about the gold. This fragrance might be too cold for winter, and too heavy for summer. I'm curious how it would feel for spring and autumn.  of my perfume reviews at The Scent Stories: thescentstories.substack.com

So, Jean Paul, we immediately recognize your "paw"... So this Scandal is, let's say, deja vu. Neither good nor bad, neither brilliant nor disgusting, but deja vu... Like we take a bit of what's already been done, and add a pinch of this, a touch of that, to end up with a "new" perfume. So to me it smells like a million other perfumes, not better, not worse...

I tested it on both myself and my partner. I was lucky – the upper notes dissipated from me pretty much immediately and the aggressive faux caramel scent only lasted through the first hour. Then I got ~8 more hours of plain boring vetiver. My partner was less fortunate – sage and caramel clung to him for at least ~5 hours. Sweet, but in an oddly artificial way.

Absolutely incredible—just as the title promises. This fragrance leaves a lingering trail so captivating that even after you’ve left the room, people will know you were there. It shares the top spot as my all-time favorite alongside Althair. I first received it as a gift from my mother, and it holds a special place in my heart.

"Dennis, what is a scandal for you?" "Well, let me think... so yesterday, I read that Coke Zero isn't healthy... artificial sweeteners can harm the liver and pancreas... but, well, a real scandal... that's something else." "Mia-Chanty, what do you think?" "Rescue at sea." "No, let's not get political now! We want to make a podcast about a new perfume, people.

There are these fragrances where the product marketing just doesn't resonate with me, and I find myself standing in front of the local perfumery's shelf with my mouth agape, my entire body language signaling despair and helplessness.

I visited a Macy’s in New York City with a friend recently and was looking at fragrances and talking about some familiar ones to consider. Because of the employees' aggressive sales tactics, I purchased nothing. However, the sales team sprayed three fragrance samples that piqued my interest. Bottled Marine, the latest fragrance (at the time of this review) in the Hugo Boss Bottled line, is the first of the three fragrances. ---- The Opening is apple and mint, which is identical to Nautica Voyage. The mid notes are where things divert slightly. The smell of sage is more noticeable than cinnamon. Combined with the patchouli and cashmere wood base note, the fragrance is smooth, fresh, and sweet for the entire duration of the scent. Overall, the fragrance is a soft and masculine touch. However, more notable is the significant relaxation effect. Mint, sage, patchouli, and cashmere wood all have stress or anxiety-reducing effects. ---- Hugo Boss Bottled Marine has above-average performance for an eau de toilette. The sillage and projection are average. This will not break doors open with fanfare to announce a person's presence, but a second person passing by or entering their personal space should notice the fragrance. The longevity of the fragrance was about eight hours. This is an excellent performance for a warm-weather eau de toilette under normal circumstances, as that will get a person through an entire workday or an evening event without a respray. ---- In terms of social usage, Bottled Marine is a fragrance that is wearable to any person (regardless of age) in most situations without serious scrutiny. If longevity in cooler weather is a sign, Bottled Marine is a fresh fragrance useable throughout the year. This could allow a person may stand out during the winter months when people switch to spicy or gourmand notes. Bottled Marine can work as a solid date night fragrance, but there is a proviso for first dates. Using the fragrance may trigger a memory of another man, such as a parent, sibling, or ex-lover. Such memories can lead to a mood shift depending on how the person's date associates the fragrance. That said, the best situation to use Bottled Marine is during a leisurely moment. Whether you are enjoying the cool waves on a beach, reading a captivating book outside, or getting ready to rest, Bottled Marine enhances those moments thanks to the relaxation notes that are prominent in the fragrance. For the same reasons as leisure, Bottled Marine can also excel in a demanding office environment. ---- Hugo Boss Bottle Marine is a solid fragrance. It smells pleasant and smooth, and it is typical of many fresh summer fragrances. The relaxation vibe is also undeniable. However, for anyone looking for a unique summer fragrance, or wants a fragrance that stands out from the crowd, Bottled Marine would be a waste of money. Even if someone likes the fragrance and does not care about uniqueness, a comparable fragrance is available for less than a third of the price — and that is with Bottled Marine being at a reasonable retail price, which is under $100.00 for a 100 ml bottle. For these reasons, I can see Bottled Marine going to the discount racks within a year, where it may shine as a hidden gem. However, if you are looking for a fragrance that has a similar profile to Nautica Voyage, but with better longevity, or simply a fragrance that is a good option for calming down stress and anxiety, Bottled Marine is a worthwhile purchase.

Bestsellers in the men's segment have received more flankers in the last 15 years than Leo DiCaprio has supermodels. You may like it or not, but rarely do truly great and lasting fragrances emerge from this trend. However, I've written enough about this trend already; one could easily write master's theses on it. "Boss Bottled" is undoubtedly a pioneer in this regard. Has anyone counted them? Does anyone say stop? With its "Marine" version, the latest offshoot comes between salt crystals, corporate offices, and carnival apples... "Bottled Marine" is undoubtedly one of the clearest and most classic "Bottled's." Sweet apple with creamy overtones. You know it, it attracts. Alongside this, there’s a never intrusive, slightly synthetic sea breeze that sometimes truly reminds you of the ocean, but also of typical showers, changing rooms, and shampoos we three-legged beings of this world use. "Bottled Marine" is never overly sweet, never teeny, never cheap or too ordinary. That’s good. It relies on the strengths of its family and is a pleasant, reliable companion. For the white T-shirt, for leisure activities, for after-work sports. Not for impressing. But you don’t always have to do that… Bottle: dark blue and not really a showpiece Sillage: present without fuss Longevity: more craftsmanship than art - 6-7 hours Conclusion: slightly salty, slightly generic, slightly great - you can rely on "Boss Bottled" (with tempered expectations), from the office to the sea!

To put it simply, here's what kind of scent you can expect. It is a creamy sweet apple with cinnamon + a refreshing "icy" note in the background. This likely comes from the mint. However, don't be misled by the fact that mint is only listed in the top notes. Because the freshness in the scent lasts the whole time. Overall, Boss Bottled Marine smells relatively consistent from start to finish. The fragrance hardly changes. You just get a bit more mint in the opening; afterwards, it plays a more supportive role in the background. If you don't like the scent of cinnamon, you should definitely stay away from Bottled Marine. One could say it smells "more mature" and spicier than its brother Boss Bottled + as mentioned, with the noticeable freshness. I got about 2-3 hours of sillage with 3 sprays and around 5-6 hours of overall longevity. So it's not a performance monster. However, I did receive a compliment at work right away. It really smells unique with the apple cinnamon + fresh combo. In the air, it is truly very "delicious," but without being too gourmand. One could really say it leans towards niche fragrance now without wanting to step on anyone's toes. It smells nothing like synthetic as its other brothers do. The only downside, in my opinion, is the performance.

Summer vacation in Italy, a little road trip with my girlfriend. Stops included Florence, San Remo, and Lake Iseo. Dream scenery and dream weather. The Italian climate helped my troubled nose, and after a long time, I could finally perceive scents intensely again. While strolling through Florence, my girlfriend wanted to quickly stop by a well-known cosmetics chain. She eagerly tested 3-4 fragrances and wanted me to sniff them too, but I said no, it doesn’t make sense, I can never smell anything. Suddenly, I realized I was completely wrong, the scent she showed me smelled wonderful like lilac, and I knew, now I am captivated by fragrances. I marched straight to the men’s fragrances to sniff my way through the range. Sure, it’s not exactly informative, but I just couldn’t get enough. In the high temperatures, I particularly liked the Valentino Uomo Born In Roma Yellow Dream and this Boss Bottled. Still, I couldn’t bring myself to buy it, as I didn’t want to make a significant dent in the vacation budget on just the second day, and good things take time. At the second destination, San Remo, I was the one who headed to the local branch of the chain. I then sprayed both fragrances again to test them and let them work on me for a day. In the end, I chose the Boss Bottled Marine Edition, as the scent was simply a bit fresher and more aquatic and suited the moment better. Great aquatic notes, paired with a light freshness and acidity from the green apple. I don’t really perceive the middle notes as indicated; maybe you can sense the cinnamon if you already know it’s there. But after a while, the apple note diminishes a bit, and the woody notes join in. The longevity and sillage are nothing extraordinary; it’s a rather short-lived fragrance. After about 2 hours, it’s only close to the skin, and after 5 hours, the whole magic is over. The bottle is sufficiently well-known, kept here in a matte blue, fits the theme but isn’t a showstopper. All in all, a very summery aquatic with a hint of synthetics, which doesn’t stand out but also doesn’t make anyone wrinkle their nose.

Boss Bottled is well-known as one of the most popular fragrances, and rightly so.... And this version definitely belongs to the most beautiful ones ... the scent is very pleasant, a creamy freshness, very soft and aquatic... The sillage and longevity are good .. performance is better than that of many EDPs.. I particularly like the fragrance because it has a very unobtrusive mildness and softness, but also a very fresh quality with good performance.

The Boss Bottled Marine is an interesting designer aquatic with a little twist. It starts with apple and mint. The apple is more pronounced here than the mint. Together, they create a good fresh-aquatic opening. Next comes cinnamon and sage. The freshness is maintained by the sage, and the cinnamon adds a touch of sweetness. You don't get much of the woods.

Neroli is not usually a note that I enjoy. Most of the time it presents itself as being too green or too bitter, which turns me off most fragrances with neroli as its dominant note. This fragrance however, is far more pleasant than any other neroli based scent I've tried so far. It's a rather delicate and subtle, orangey-soap smell with a touch of sugary sweetness. It's not breathtakingly unique, however it's very appealing, at least in my opinion. It opens with bright, Spring-like citruses that at first reminded me of cleaning products. Thankfully that clean, antiseptic scent disappeared leaving a pleasant sweet and soapy orange note with an underlying spiciness caused by the sage and rosemary. Unfortunately I think I'd tire of this fragrance rather quickly due to its lack of lasting strength and linear composition after the heart. It loses a lot of its character after a while, but if subtle soap scents are what you crave, certainly go ahead and test this entire range. Although Eau de Fleurs Neroli left me uninspired and wanting more depth, it certainly reigns supreme as being a classy and elegant fragrance. Many fragrance releases over the last few years lack these qualities, so I'm truly glad to have found at least one fragrance that has managed to achieve this successfully.

Is it even a fragrance? Isn't it much more like a refreshing wipe, used to clean the snotty noses of the little ones after a 5-hour drive on the highway and many messy snacks? Is it one of those bath additive lavender(!) balls that you only throw into the muck after Grandma and Grandpa have taken their swimming test in it? Or is it perhaps the base note of camphorated alcohol that subtly spreads in the bathroom after the weekly pickling binge? The latter is supposedly said to relieve headaches, body aches, and tension. But Eau de Fleurs Néroli triggers all of that for me. 4711 in sweet, medicinal, and ancient.

delicious - the original scent from Chloé is almost overshadowed, but I find the neroli note very tasty and natural. The fragrance is spring-fresh and feminine. Only the longevity leaves something to be desired (2-3 hours on my skin) =(

Today I had the chance to test the Chloé creation. The name lives up to its promise. In the opening, the scent is a bit "sharp" and has a slight medicinal character. In the later development, however, it becomes pleasantly light, floral, but not too heavy, with a distinct neroli note. In the base, it even becomes a bit soapy. Neroli is said to have mood-lifting effects. That may be true. For me, it's a feel-good fragrance.

Jean Paul Gaultier himself described his first fragrance like this: “One part dusty loose powder, like my grandmother wore - think it was old Coty; one part that smell you get when you are sitting in the front row of the theater - for me, I think of going to The Chatelet when I was 12, and the curtain goes up, and the hot lights are on the costumes, wigs and sets, and you breathe it all in. And, just to be modern, one part nail polish remover!” I completely agree with his interpretation - it does smell incredibly powdery and very vintage, very sexual in a somewhat old-fashioned, pin-up model way. The fragrance is sensuous, seductive, dramatic, theatrical in a way - it smells like nothing I've tried before. The soapy impression it gives is tempered by the oriental, somewhat darker undertone that comes to complement and enhance the composition to make it daring and provocative, yet still classy and posh. Classique perfectly evokes the high-class, well-bred woman that likes to give in to the physical pleasures from time to time and is not afraid to fully explore her sexuality. She is powerful and smart and she does not fear the erotic, passionate side of her.

Early in my perfumista journey I vowed never to own a perfume housed in a female torso bottle. So much for vows. I don't even know why I like this, exactly. Maybe it's the utterly intoxicating top note that makes me close my eyes and yearn for far-off sunsets, the unusually successful Iris/Orchid accord. The base is certainly stellar simplicity. I just know once I smelled this at the counter today, no way I was leaving without it. Maybe I'll just hide the bottle...some place invisible but quite near so I can spray this beauty at heartfelt will and dream.

Really nice scent. A little powdery, definitely has a prominent vanilla. Not a gourmand vanilla but the more vintage inedible vanilla in a lot of 80s-90s perfumes. Anise is at the forefront and I wish it remained more prominent in the dry down. It almost reminds me of root beer. The orange blossom remains strong throughout. There's something soapy as well. An orange blossom, vanilla root beer soap? It sounds weird, but it is really pleasant, really warming and feminine. I see some similarities between Classique and Poeme as well, with the latter being more balmy and yellow floral. I find that I go nose blind to it easily though, which is really disappointing.

The review is for edt version of Classique. The scent starts very vanillic ,incense-y orange blossom. Incense and vanilla sweetness stays from opening until the dry down. It's the kind of incense like infusion d'Iris Prada but this is very vanillic smelling and the florals that picking out the whole are orange blossoms and rose. The package is unique and distinctive -the femme's nude body-like the male's version nude body... It's very good wearing more of the young ages and i would say very good for the evening nights out. I categorize it to floriental vanilla and the longevity is very good (more than +8 hours).

It lives up to its name: a classic! One of the best JPG perfumes in my opinion, completely timeless and ideal for all ages. It smells mainly of vanilla and orange blossom, it's powdery, it's neither too much nor not enough; perfectly balanced. The bottle is awesome, today we're used to it but imagine a bottle like that in the 90s, damn original and above all provocative! I will never cease to love it and will always have a little room in my collection for this wonderful bottle.

Back in the 1900s...lol....you know back in the day. Some of THE best of TIMES... Ahhh MEMORIES. This was groundbreaking in my humble opinion. So much so that it was, as I like to say, "Too big girl" for me. I was rather intimidated by it.... Yet I kept my bottle and from time to time, I'd sneak a spray. Just ONE! So spicy, so bold, so unique, so beautiful....
Sexy scent in a God-awful bottle but a big warning to all of who wants to purchase the E.D.P apply on small doses because this is an siliage monster J.P.

Perhaps this is simply a case of inflated expectations induced by the provocative packaging, but Jean-Paul Gaultier CLASSIQUE just seems to me like another synthetic, slightly sweet woody oriental among a dozen others.

One of the samples I got yesterday and I gave it a full wear today. I can't place this in any era and still there is something familiair in this fragrance. Something vintage but then again it is not vintage in the way my Guerlins or Diors are. I guess it is the powdery drydown that give it this slightly 'vintage vibe'.

I have a bottle with only Jean Paul Gaultier on it, not "Classique". I assume it is from the 1990s. Its a luscious, heavy and beautiful epic that was the watermark of its day. It seems somewhat synthetic at first, almost unnatural on the first few outings. Then I let my nose adjust and reconsider this marvel. I love neroli and this has more than anything I have experienced.

Yes I like this but, nope, not really a "Sport" scent to me, maybe I've grown accustomed to 90's and newer sport fragrances that are pretty much aldehyde/citrus/marine note bombs. This shows its age in being such a strong oakmoss/lavender smeller. I'm actually wearing this as I write and cannot help but picture a barbershop and shaving cream products. It's a classic, maybe for the over 30 crowd, nice projection and life on my epidermis.

Reviewing the EdT : Boss Sport is dry and herbal and well rounded by the slight sweetness of the tonka. Blended with loads of different notes, but the marigold (or actually tagetes, the french marigold) mixed with oakmoss gives off a piney and "dirty" sensation and the juice itself has a thick, almost oily feel, that's how concentrated it is. It actually does come across as a little soapy. I'm not really sure why you would call a flowery fougere "Sport", but in my memory this is kinda how "sporty" guys smelled back in the eighties, not the citrus/aquatic sweet scents of today but heavy on the oakmoss and kinda industrial cleaner-like - weird stuff really. Most prominent notes are marigold, oakmoss, tarragon, sage, lavender, patchouli, geranium, vetiver and tonka. Unfortunately it gives me a slight headache wearing this, but definitely worth a try. Projection is average on me, but longevity is great.

We owned a disused pasture when I was young. Each summer it became overgrown with weeds, brush, and wildflowers, so a man came by to Bush-Hog it almost down to the dirt. The smell of that field being mowed on a hot Midwestern day is indescribable. Boss Sport evokes that heady mix of fresh vegetation indiscriminately chopped down at the same time, and it's a thing of beauty.

There are simply ideal days for a particular fragrance. Today, for example, was one of those: sun-drenched, filled with warmth, spring is unfolding its splendor. And yet, you can still feel the freshness of the season. The first half of the day is marked for hours by the coolness of the night. A hint lingers in the air. On such days, Boss Sport is recommended. I find the unpretentious appearance of this fragrance to be a breath of fresh air. Nothing feels forced here. Boss Sport caters to a spicy aromatic, green spectrum that presents itself as multifaceted yet transparent. The balancing act is consistently successful, even if the individual phases of the fragrance development are quite distinct. The freshness is moderate and pleasant. In the first hours, a restrained sweetness emerges, skillfully providing variety. Later, mossy aspects prevail before the fragrance fades into a subtle bitterness. 1987, that feels like an eternity ago. I indulge in nostalgia, which tends to romanticize many things. And yet, I dare to claim: That was a great hit back then. Fresh, green, composed without fuss, definitive in its statement. A coherent concept that still convinces me today. Perfectly suited for early spring days when everything seems possible.

About two years ago, a member of Parfumo kindly sent me the Boss Sport as a miniature (see picture below). It immediately went into the acrylic display case, but a few days ago I finally wanted to write a review about it, so I first had to check how the scent still holds up. I was surprised in two ways. On one hand, the already quite aged Boss Sport smelled as fresh as if it had just come from the store. No signs of any degradation whatsoever. On the other hand, I was instantly reminded of Lacoste Original, even though I last enjoyed that fragrance in its original version (I only know the reissue fleetingly) over 20 years ago. Nevertheless, the connection was immediate. Boss Sport has exactly the same slightly sharp minty-citrusy opening, which, with its crisp freshness, is suitable for both scorching summer days and athletic activities. However, here it deviates from the usual citrus waters and, with the numerous additional ingredients, forms a warm spicy base that makes it clear to everyone that it means business and has quality. However, Boss is not necessarily a brand that immediately makes you think of sports. Accordingly, besides this offshoot, whose bottle design strikingly resembles Boss Number One, they have only released the inconsequential Boss Bottled Sport. In contrast, Lacoste with Lacoste Original was far more authentic and thus managed to launch its arguably best fragrance.

I still have the moment in my mind when I discovered this fragrance. The bottle with its green color attracted me like magic. When I tried the fresh, spicy scent, I immediately knew, this is it: the incredibly unique fragrance. It was indeed my favorite for several years, until it was no longer available on the shelves.

I got it, the 125ml bottle. I sprayed it on and immediately had a flashback: Yes, this is it, the scent that the big guys wore in the late 80s and 90s when I was young, when it got warmer or we were on a ski holiday. It was far from what we today have as “citrusy sport waters.

Sport fragrances are as plentiful as sand on the beach. What unites them all? They all smell quite similar, as they convey a similar message. The man in sports pushes himself, showcases his masculinity, and ultimately radiates the clear victor. And on the winner's podium, he must look impeccable, as if he could immediately head to the victory celebration in the evening.

Yes, yes, the old lament about the discontinued. What can you do, the song must go on when so much good is senselessly switched off. Boss "Sport" presents itself as a very green, extremely herb-fruity sports fragrance of the old style, almost the serious counterpart to "Lacoste Original".

The dear "scent stick" suggested a few days ago - well-meaning - that I should look "forward" and focus on "new things". Well, the "new" often takes a long time to arrive or is often a disappointment. true to the motto - not everything that glitters is gold.

Meanwhile at Jean Paul Gaultier headquarters: -Lets make a new fragrance -But we dont have much time to think -just put inside what you have in front of you -I have Vanilla, Tonka bean and I am eating a pear -These will do... and... "BOOM"....Magic happened! I guess this is how this fragrance was created judging from its simplicity. It is a very simple yet an adorable, DEEP sweet, warm cuddly, seductive scent, a typical beauuuuutiful womens fragrance. We knew vanilla and tonka bean do miracles together so this is one of them. The performance of the perfume is great compared to other designer fragrances. On me, it stayed for about 6 hours (warning: I overspray). On my clothes it stayed all day (without overspraying them)! It can be worn in any occasion because it is not intense, it doesnt turn heads! It is discreet, elegant and beautiful. Its a safe womens choice for any occasion and especially for dates. Also it is only for cold weather. Personally, I feel that something is missing from this fragrance...Maybe an acidity or an incence, or something spicy, would make this fragrance more interesting. I dont know if I am used to more complex perfumes and this seems too simple for my nose. This fragrance misses something in order for me to say "wow". I have also layered it with Xerjoff Lira and for my surprise, Lira didnt cover la belle as I was expecting, since Lira is nuclear. It was a good layering and I think I ll try some more layering with this perfume. To sum up I keep 3 words for this fragrance: Simple, deep, elegant. Thank you for your time! Be safe and smell great!

This perfume is much more than what the notes are describing. It's impossible to believe its captivating scent comes from that simple pyramid. It's slightly smoky/incensy, resinous and balsamic sweet with a hint of floral, and a fruit compote with probably a pinch of cinnamon and other spices, maybe some clove. For more details, please watch my Youtube review linked here below.

It’s SWEET. It’s got a prominent pear note, but the kind of overripe sticky pear that drips all over when you bite into it. It’s so sexy, so mature, and one of my favorite nighttime perfumes. It’s very rich, very feminine. I think the bottle is perfect for it, what the black to red gradient and golden necklace on a female torso evokes as an image is exactly what it smells like. It’s also one to spray lightly, as it is very very very sweet. Sillage 10/10, Longevity 9/10

One of the sexiest scents I own. It’s a blend of sweet vanilla & warm, reminding me of those cozy vanilla candles you smell at Marshall’s. I wore it on a date night, and my boyfriend couldn’t stop asking what perfume I had on & that I should wear it often. I’m usually an over-sprayer, but with this fragrance I try to be more careful because it can definitely give you a headache.

Pear, jasmine, and vanilla. Sweet and syrupy, with a background of incense smoke. Very sexy, feminine, and alluring. Strong and long-lasting. Definitely a scent that will get you noticed. A peak autumn/winter scent for me, just perfect for cold days. Also a great gourmand, and fabulous for date nights.

To me, this smells just the same classic JPG I wore when I was a teenager. I think this is better suited to a younger generation. It’s a nice perfume, but it doesn’t scream sexy to me personally. Maybe if I hadn’t worn JPG as a teen 25+ years ago I’d feel differently about it.

As per usual, this house never fails to disappoint, even when it comes to ladies' fragrances! Awesome yummy fragrance. Perfect for late autumn/winter occasions. Actually, I could argue this has a powdery feel to it, I think it's because of the pear. But still. Edible and creamy fragrance. Good longevity and projection.

La belle original is far greater than this one - very heavy where tonka bean takes over everything else. This horrible mash up leads to an old not freshy pear in decomposition. La belle the original on the other hand - is sweeter, fresh where pear can be noticed directly. I wouldn’t recommend, bling bought it, sent it back and ordered la belle instead.

La Belle Le Parfum by JPG is a delicious, warm, sweet fragrance that reminds me of an delectable pear tart with a caramelized crust, served with a scoop of melting homemade vanilla ice cream. Yum, yum, yum. I love gourmands and I love this scent. It's a sexy, grown-up fragrance, perfect for a winter date night. Marry me.

She is an eternal goddess. Canned pears in syrup with vanilla. The barest hint of jasmine, and Tonka for days. Lasts 3 days on my clothes. Chronic oversprayer and I only spray this 3x. Definite rebuy. I literally spray this on my shirt and I can still smell it AFTER ITS WASHED. go-to date night smell

I received this sample at Pieper with my Dior Jules purchase and thought it was the men's version I was already familiar with. But then I noticed that it said EdP on the label, and it might actually be the women's Eau de Parfum. Luckily, I decided to try it out, and it is clearly not the average men's orange. I haven't tested the women's EdT yet, but this brand-new EdP is quite impressive and a reliable everyday companion and all-rounder for all stylish and spontaneously modern women. However, one must like sweetness, as both apples and crème brûlée are not exactly shy when it comes to sweetness and sugar. The slightly modified Boss Orange bottle fits well in the hand and is not unattractive. Sillage and longevity are, with a bit of luck, just about in the middle of the league, rather on the decline, as it is a rather thin, shy scent that fades away quickly, after about 6 hours. So, a bit more could have been added here, especially as an EdP. But by now, it should be clear to everyone that EdPs often do not match the strength of a true perfume. Alongside the sweet green apple in the top note, in the sugar-laden crème brûlée base, there is an extremely inconspicuous heart note with a floral meadow that somewhat reminds one of fresh laundry with a hint of orange. But it's as subtle as a brief breeze at 42 degrees. A good everyday companion that comes across as stylish, calm, sweet, and naive, showing hardly any perfume strength. For the younger, sweet, inexperienced female generation, it will surely be well-received on normal days and won't hurt anyone. It's just a pity that it doesn't last the whole day, not even a workday. One shouldn't expect miracles, but with a tempered expectation, one won't be disappointed, rather surprised! Because the scent is a lovely intermezzo for all dessert lovers.

Unfortunately, I am not a health-conscious fruit eater - unless the fruits are sweetened afterwards or deliciously prepared. So, Mama's crispy apple pancakes, topped with cinnamon and honey, always lure me into the kitchen. I also like to have a scoop of vanilla ice cream with it. Not exactly what you would find in the Brigitte diet book. But I am not a diet apostle - rather a connoisseur. This is where Boss Orange EdP comes in handy for me, as the delightful scent of my favorite dish has been well captured in the bottle. The apple is warm and soft, wrapped in cinnamon and honey, complemented by a dollop of tart plum jam, surrounded by sweet vanilla. The orange blossom adds a touch of freshness to the treat, and the olive wood gives an interesting spicy finish. The scent is subtly gourmand - without being overwhelming. It has nothing greasy about it, but remains beautifully transparent, even though this is not a case of simple cooking. Moreover, the longevity is good, and I can enjoy the appetizing aroma for a long time.

~ Inspiration ~ Last year, my first comment here on Parfumo was about "Boss Orange." Now I came across a sample of the EDP. ~ Bottle ~ The modern shape of stacked gemstones has been retained. This time the color is a warm rose gold, suggesting a more intense fragrance. ~ Scent ~ Like the EDT, it primarily smells of oranges and vanilla. Sweet apples, orange, and other white flowers give it a subtle, fruity-floral aura. Sandalwood and olive wood, together with crème brûlée, create a soft, warm, slightly gourmand scent with a caramelized base note. ~ Longevity ~ On my skin, it lasts about 4 hours (on clothing and hair a bit longer). 2-3 sprays are sufficient, as otherwise it becomes too sticky sweet and synthetic. ~ Occasion ~ A sweet fragrance that fits warmer days in spring, summer, and autumn. Also suitable for work, as it is not overpowering. ~ Conclusion ~ I can't notice a big difference from the EDT.

Recently, when I made a detour to my little local perfumery, the saleswoman I trust approached me with a Boss Orange tester while I was wandering through the store. I wished I could be invisible, because my first and only encounter with the Eau de Toilette from Boss Orange is not exactly a fond memory. Since then, I have always kept a wide berth from it, because who carries a face mask all the time!?! The only thing I remember in hindsight after that shock was HAIRSPRAY; it took my breath away, and I left the store in a daze... I have often wondered how this scent can be so popular and beloved that it belongs to the bestsellers. Am I that different? Well, she came up to me with the tester and must have seen my crouched, curse-promising posture, and waved her arm directly, saying: "No, no, don't be afraid, just try it, it's different from the Eau de Toilette!" It was obvious to her that I had "fear" of it *smirk* Hmmm, I would usually spare myself such things, but since she has my trust, I laid down my weapons to give it a chance. And I must say, it did nothing to me. It started fresh, apple-like, and then transitioned into a delicious, initially fruity, then floral, slightly sweet, caramel crème brûlée; I can only agree with my predecessor on that. It's probably not a total knockout, but I think it could be an unobtrusive, slightly fruity-floral, deliciously sweet everyday companion. In any case, I did not find it a punishment, unlike its brother, which is already something. And I will now take a closer look at the EDT, despite my bad memories. Sometimes it also depends on my mood, the season, or the time of day, and upon a second glance, it can actually be quite nice. Let's see, we will experience it.

I had a sample of this little fragrance in my Box of Beauty December. The scent starts with a distinct apple note. Then I smell just a hint of flowers, and right after that, the apple falls into the Crème Brûlée! Sugar - caramel - applesauce with a touch of vanilla and sandalwood. Unfortunately, it's a short pleasure. The scent doesn't last very long on me.... It's a quite nice gourmand fragrance, but unfortunately a bit weak in terms of longevity. The bottles from the entire Boss Orange line are really not my style. But taste is what you like. Best, Kitty17

It is a creamy, green Iris scent that I very much enjoyed. In my opinion it's an unisex scent, to me even feels more masculin. I don't get any coconut in this one so I'm kinda confused with the comments here. The first spray got me, with such a fresh and uniqe openning, in half an hour it lost its strong herbal feeling and it became very delicate and gentle soft scent (at least on paper not sure if it would act the same on skin) It could have better performance in means of longevity but it is still very pleasent to me.

The very first moment of JPG Scandal sprayed from the nozzle is a saccharine cloud of medicinal raspberry, typical of gourmand fruitchouli. What ensues is a nutty, tropical tart green accord over a fuzzy gourmand vanilla, which reminds me of a similar combination in Mugler Aura. Only that the vanilla is more subdued in Scandal, and a fresh, aquatic, almost laundry-like facet is more emphasised here as well, which is frankly quite nauseating to me during the first 3 hours. I can hardly detect anything in a natural floral way. And although I can occasionally perceive the tart, juicy blood orange, it's mostly drowned in the archetypical fruitchouli mess with a scratchy praline on top. The final dry down after about 10 hours is more acceptable for me, with a honeyed patchouli similar to that in Mugler Eau de Star, and adorned with some roasted nuts sprinkled atop. But unfortunately, the squeaky clean laundry musk and irritating synthetic sweetness still haunt in the background. The sillage is mostly moderate, while the longevity exceeds 12 hours on me. With the overwhelming synthetic fruity vanilla sweetness and the brazen laundry musk, Scandal unfortunately places two of my least favourite olfactory elements in the center. Although I think it fits the general "sexy sweet yet fresh clean" trend dutifully, I don't find it original or exceptionally well done. Therefore, I personally would not particularly seek it out.

There will be no scandal! The perfume opens with citrus smell. Fresh, clean, juicy. Then, after a few seconds the honey enters the stage like a primadonna. Now it is it turn to show what it can do. From now on it is all about honey. A sweet, intoxicating honey. Because the citrus smell does not disapear completely, honey is not so syrupy. It has a sparkling touch that gives a fresh feeling. This removes the sticky trait of honey. It is refreshing, pleasant and full of joy. It suits a woman capable of awakening burning passions, eager to always flirt, independent and free as a bird in the sky. This woman will always leave behind a trace of scandal. Maybe not outside, but surely inside. The perfume remains like this for a few hours. The dry-down is a patchouli with honey. It has a good longevity, while the sillage is pretty good too. Scandal perfectly adapts to market requirements. It’s what ?s been looking for, what many women wear. It is in the trend. So, if you are looking for a honey fragrance, softened with citrus and settled by patchouli, you can try Scandal.

I revisited this one last summer and I can honestly say that this is a total love for me. When I first tried this in the cooler weather, I liked it a lot, but I wasn’t sure if it was something I’d want to wear often. Honey and beeswax can be difficult notes for some, and in Scandal, they do come off slightly animalic. But I think they add to the raunchy, dare I say, slüttiness, of this scent. This fragrance definitely oozes sexy appeal. You can also definitely pick up on the licorice, so if that isn’t a note you enjoy, I’d probably avoid this one. The licorice doesn’t bother me at all, and adds a nice soft, spicy touch to the fragrance. It’s perfectly floral and sweet. The ratings suggest this fragrance for cold weather, but to be honest, I think this fragrance needs warmer weather for all of the notes to fully shine. From my experience wearing it now during summer compared to during the fall / winter, I can smell all the florals and fruits much better. Overall, I think the scent wears better on a spring / summer night than it does in the cooler weather. I think it’s appropriate to wear in the cooler seasons during the daytime, but works perfectly in the warmer seasons for nighttime use. I’ll definitely be wearing it more before summer ends, whether it’s for date night or to go out with the girls. The performance is spectacular and the scent carries stunningly in the wind. While the scent profile may not be everyone’s cup of tea, it’s definitely for me and has made me a fan of honey + beeswax notes in fragrances.

I’ve never smelled a honey fragrance so I was intrigued by this. Can confirm it definitely smells like I have just smeared some honey on my arm. When I first spray, I get a huge sweet blast of honey and blood orange, and the honey sticks around as it settles, but some beeswax and florals come into play as it dries on my skin. It is indeed very sweet, but in a natural honey way, not an artificial “candy” way. I’m picking up on some slight animalic tones as well - maybe that’s how my nose is interpreting the honey? - but that just gives it some depth and very flirty and sexy vibes. This is a powerhouse fragrance, as others have said. I’m sitting here with just one spray on my arm for sampling and I can really smell it jumping off my skin. Definitely for cool weather only, in my opinion, and best applied very lightly (1-2 sprays, otherwise I think this would be headache-inducing for anyone in the vicinity!). This really screams “going out/nighttime” to me, but I think this would be ok for daytime wear in cold weather if used conservatively. It is one of the more overtly sexy fragrances I’ve smelled, so I would definitely NOT wear this to work, for example.

Top note: pure acetone Heart note: headache-inducing jasmine Base notes: still headache-inducing jasmine, lilac, honey mixed with motor oil, echoes of acetone. I was taken aback by the blatant attack of nail polish remover that straight up stabbed my nose. The longevity is exceptional, but I'm not sure how nobody else has mentioned the acetone - it's overpowering. Maybe my nose is broken, I dunno. This perfume feels violent.

This scent is one of the most permanent and high-silage scents you can see in your life. The scent starts with a citrus bomb. It is so sugary that the blood orange is recognizable. If you know the difference between a blood orange and a regular orange, you'll know what I mean. The smell can make you faint because of the sugar, so it should not be squeezed too much.

The initial blast of blood orange gives place to the honey, jasmine and gardenia the I love.. After a few hours you are left with caramelly beeswax and patchouli that I love.. And what can I say about the scent bubble? Let's say you'll be noticed for sure, so if you'll be stuck inside make sure you won't choke anyone else out let's say this one is Not office friendly.

Maybe there is something wrong with my nose but I swear the patchouli is strong in this – but not in an off-putting way. I find this very palatable, but slightly mature. Like, when my sister smelled this she said "that smells like [our auntie]" lmao. The sweetness from the honey (and tbh I swear I smell beeswax) make this very pleasant to smell.

... and it's sweet too, let's just compare it to La vie est Belle and its counterparts, even though we have such a trained nose.... but sweet is just sweet, and honey can sometimes be cotton candy. ;-) Even I, as an absolute fragrance novice, can clearly smell the similarity to Jean Paul Gaultier Intense, which I actually had in my collection for a long time.

(Title inspired by Evelyn Hamann's ruthless self-critique as revue-dancing Dr. Margarethe Tietze) These days, it’s that time again everywhere: up and down the country, the annual unavoidable company Christmas parties are being announced.

It's no secret that the original Scandal pour Homme wasn't that good of a perfume. It was synthetic, sweet, bland, and it just didn't really feel like a high quality, well-put fragrance. The flanker here, Scandal pour Homme Le Parfum , doesn't stray far from that either, but it is "better", to say the least. The opening will still have some of the synthetic punch of the original, but toned down a bit. With Scandal pour Homme , the tonka bean sweetness would immediately push through, blending with the synthetic accord messily. But it's not the same with Le Parfum. Here, I get a much more prominent geranium, which gives the fragrance a spicy and citrusy undertone. It fits much better than the clary sage, in my opinion, as it doesn't blow things out of proportion. The little tonka bean that there is here smoothens things out with a mild creaminess. And as the fragrance settles, you get that woody, musky, slightly spicy vibe from the sandalwood. It does feel somewhat better blended than the original Scandal pour Homme , but I also seem to go nose blind to it much faster than with the original. While I would say that it does smell a bit nicer and better put than the OG, I'm still far from impressed. There's still that synthetic part in the background which just makes this a rather annoying scent. It's al worse when blended with some of that sweetness. And again, there's hardly any proper development, just like with the OG. The fragrance falls flat, staying largely the same from start to finish. Thankfully, quality/blend-wise, it's slightly better than the OG. The longevity here does impress, though. The fragrance held on for about 10 hours on my skin, which is again, a bit better than with the original. Projection is also praiseworthy for the first two hours, leaving a nice trail behind and filling the rooms I entered. But after the first two hours, it was very tricky to tell just how much more was it still projecting. Since I went nose blind to it rather quickly, I needed a couple of friends to tell me from time to time if they could still smell it. But it seems that they also faced the nose blind issue, and after the first two hours, they could barely feel it anymore. But given how good projection was initially, I doubt that the fragrance became a skin scent so quickly after, so my nose blindness is to blame, and I'm sure that it was still fairly noticeable for those who weren't constantly around me and smelling it. In terms of occasions where you could wear Scandal pour Homme Le Parfum , the same ones that applied to the original also apply here. Leisurely, daily wear, work, parties, clubbing... you could even rock it at more formal gatherings if you'd like (I wouldn't, though). It's a pretty versatile fragrance, and given its mild (but noticeable) improvement over the original, I'd say that it's much easier to wear to a broader selection of scenarios. But still, I'm not a fan of this DNA. It doesn't smell terrible once it settles, but it certainly feels generic and boring in every way possible. It's better than the OG for sure - that geranium and sandalwood make for a slightly better impression. But it's far from "Yeah, I'm getting a full bottle" type of impression. So again, I don't think this is truly worth the money. Too boring, too generic, too "designer-ish"... Overall Rating: 6.6/10

Amazing Fragrance, More mature, deep and less sweet than the EDT Version. This fragrance is amazing, different from everything else out there. Love at first sniff hhhh ! I recommend it during a night out or evening events during the year ( All seasons ) . 3, 4 srays of it are sufficent. Beast performance and great longevity.

To me this fragrance is very underrated. I can see what people mean when they say "looks like One Million, The Most Wanted...", that's kind of same family but Scandal is the Big brother of this family. Much less sweet, more mature, sexier, darker. You will wear it during cold days or night time. It's so masculine and very modern (not old daddy) at the same time. Give it a try guys and let your nose be the judge.

The boy turned into a man! Scandal Le Parfum is a much better fragrance than its predecessor, Edt. This time Le Parfum no longer has that cloyingly sweet, synthetic base of Scandal Edt. Le Parfum has these notes of geranium, tonka bean, and sandalwood very well connected here in this fragrance. The scandal LP has a more mature sweetness, and the sandalwood here has a more liqueur side. Overall the perfume is more mature, sexy, and at the same time mysterious. And I'll tell you a secret! He is king of compliments! The performance is worthy of the house of Jean Paul Gaultier, that is, high level on my skin for 10 hours on average. And with a strong projection of 2 hours, and then it becomes golden on you. A true Club night perfume!

Scandal Le Parfum is a stunning release from Jean Paul Gaultier. It’s deep, sweet, floral, dense, mysterious, dark and seductive. It’s definitely like the original, but made more serious and dark. Fragrance opens with a coconut-like smell that I’m not a true fan of, but after a few minutes the coconut smell turns out to be dense geranium-tonka combo. In middle the parfum becomes less sweet, more floral and deep, the more sandalwood starts to show, the better fragrance gets. The fragrance is for more serious gentleman who’s still seductive, In my opinion confident women can definitely use this fragrance as well. Season wise it is suitable for Winter, Fall and Spring or even for the cold Summer nights. This fragrance shines in the night, This fragrance is for seducting people. If you want to buy an everyday fragrance, Le Male’s would be a better option. Performance is BEAST. Even close to Le Male elixir while being less sweet. Lasts more then 12 hours on my skin, easily fills a room without overpowering someone. A head turner for sure. I bought it for 70 euros 50ml, Imo definitely worth it but I’m sure you can find cheaper offers for the fragrance. Le Male Le Parfum was my favorite from JPG, but after smelling this fragrance, I just found my signature scent. Definitely smell before you buy it, It’s a very dense fragrance that needs to be tested first.

Actually, I already knew after seeing the promotional displays of the "Scandal-pour-Homme" line that this would not be a fragrance for me. A longer stay in the orange drugstore chain with the big "M," prompted by my better half, led me to try a few "scandalous" sprays due to the somewhat limited selection in that specific store. I close my eyes and ... whaaaam...

With the name "Scandal," the pompous appearance, and the provocative marketing - I would have never expected such a boring fragrance. I mean, just read for yourself: "The King of the Ring is back! This Eau de Parfum intense is more addictive than ever and promises even more sensations. Geranium, sandalwood, and tonka bean ensure bulging muscles.

... yes, you could wear it well on a Christmas stroll. Everywhere there are marzipan potatoes, candied apples, roasted almonds, and caramelized nuts, Scandal Le Parfum feels particularly at home. Synthetic woody-warm smoke of oriental spices surrounds the wearer throughout the day at a rather penetrating level on a cloud of doped cotton candy.

First thought: “Smells like JPG Le Beau Intense, just without coconut and less summery.” A first hint of disappointment, since that one is already in the closet. But oh well. It was a Christmas gift and you don’t want to step on anyone’s toes. So let’s give the crowned bottle a chance. Next day: Let’s see what Scandal can do.

My first Jean Paul Gaultier fragrance! It smells similar to JPG Le Beau Just without coconut and more wintry. You could actually wear it in the summer evenings as well. It lasts very well on my skin I would say it lasts around 12 hours! In my opinion, it's a really great sweet winter fragrance. A great scent for people aged 13-25.

Boss Intense, magnificent perfume even more better than I expected. It is deep and fresh at the same time. Perfect for all seasons and much nicer than deep red which is more lemony. It is very long lasting with perfect and noticeable sillage. The spice notes are so wonderfully blended with the orange blossom and the result at the end is superb. High class perfume with a very distinguished bottle. I was very pleased with my choice

This is currently my bed-time scent. It's not something I'd probably wear out, however its clean woodsiness is very soothing on a cold Winter's night under the blankets. Boss Intense has an almost masculine feel to it. Not that it bothers me, I gender bend fragrances all the time. Some people refer to Boss Intense as being similar to Deep Red, also by Hugo Boss. I own both, and while I see the similarities, Deep Red is much sweeter and more tasty. Vanilla does feature in this fragrance, however it's not sugary or particularly feminine. This fragrance has an odd bite to it, being rather bold and resinous in a way. I feel powerful when I wear this fragrance, hence the reason why I recommend this fragrance for the tom-boys and those dominating types of women. Boss Intense was a gift given to me by a friend, and even though it doesn't strike me as something particularly me, I will use the bottle up until the last drop. This fragrance can be overpowering at times, and has a habit of sticking to fabric, especially my sheets. This fragrance really has to be applied lightly for it to be appreciated.

At the risk of being excluded from Parfumo for disregarding a code of honor, I will still say where the fragrance currently stands: in the toilet (yes, exactly: not to freshen up before leaving). I want to briefly explain this ultimate humiliation. It’s not that I find the fragrance itself incredibly bad, but for a few years now, I just can’t connect with Hugo Boss anymore. Every fragrance lacks that certain something for me. The scents feel too business-like, too smooth, and there’s a spark of femininity missing. Even Deep Red wouldn’t make it into my collection today (and I used to think it was great). Right now, I prefer either delicate or intense - forest fairy vs. nose fireworks - and Hugo Boss is really right in the middle.

~ Inspiration ~ This perfume from Boss was missing from my Tested series, even though it has been on the market for a while now. The commercial reminds me a bit of those from "Bruno Banani". ~ Bottle ~ The slightly tilted bottle with an intense gradient from silky red to velvety black makes me think of sexy lingerie. ~ Scent ~ It starts off a bit spicy with kumquat and other spices, immediately presenting a somewhat bitter yet sensual character. Roses, jasmine, and vanilla provide an underlying creamy floral note that gives the fragrance a refined character. Finally, it concludes warm with sandalwood, amber, patchouli, and benzoin, featuring the typical Boss note. ~ Longevity ~ On my skin, it lasts about 6-7 hours (even longer on clothes and hair). 2-3 sprays are enough; otherwise, it becomes too scratchy for me. ~ Occasion ~ A going-out fragrance for the cooler evenings in autumn and winter. ~ Conclusion ~ To my nose, it smells like a mix of "Deep Red" and "Boss Woman".

I have been using this perfume for years. And every time I wear it, my man asks me he: hmmmm... what scent is that, it smells guuuuuuuud? I: not again he: what do you mean? I: never mind, the one with the red bottle? he: what’s it called again? I: Boss Intense ;-) Boss Intense is a hot scent that is very well received by men. It smells very intense, as the name suggests, a bit bitter, floral, and sporty. At first, it smells quite exotic and fresh. Once the scent develops, it smells wonderfully spicy and vanilla-like (Vanilla Orchid), and in the end, it is intensified by various woods. It definitely smells warm and sweet, no no... not like the other sweet heavy perfumes, no... a really good-smelling perfume that fits anytime and anywhere. The bottle is quite extraordinary; it looks as if the glass has been twisted. This blend of slightly floral and bitter with a mix of vanilla is, in my opinion, a successful composition, my absolute favorite scent. The only downside, in my opinion, is the longevity; I would have wished it to be a bit more intense :)

Many years ago, this dark red bottle smiled at me in Douglas. I immediately reached for it, and this unique scent enchanted me right away. I had never smelled anything like it before or since. The spices immediately rise to the nose, but not harshly, as they quickly blend with kumquat. It creates a spicy fruit that lays velvety on the skin.

Next to Deep Red, one of my favorite fragrances. During the day, I spray just a little, as it smells intense on me and lasts all day. In the evening, I happily apply more. It smells sweet but at the same time fresh. My best friend also owns it and finds it heavy and bitter.

...that is Boss Intense on my skin. It is definitely different from other women's perfumes - there is nothing that reminds you of a bouquet of flowers or a fruit basket, but also no heavy oriental scent that narcotizes the surroundings within several meters. But it is definitely for women, although not for everyone.

I really like it. Just to start. The opening is spicy-floral and slightly fruity, that must be the orange blossom. Quite bitter and hardly sweet, but definitely for women; I know and own other fragrances that lean more towards unisex. The spices become more intense over time; I think there’s some kind of pepper in there.

..I find it almost subtle (and that's meant positively)... It is not feminine in a sweet sense, but rather consistently spicy and woody. I smell a cloud of spices all day, which I perceive very positively. I only notice rose and vanilla, as well as patchouli, at the very beginning; afterwards, only the spicy (nutmeg!

From the moment I smelled the opening years ago, I liked it. In fact, the opening is just awesome - a drier and slightly spicier Le Male - still with plenty of sweetness - albeit with "more mature" slapped all over its chiseled torso. Unfortunately, the disappointment came in the drydown. On my skin, the original Le Male backbone in Essence de Parfum loses its muster quite quickly - about an hour in, to be exact. The sweetness fades, to be replaced with a super dry cardamom, subtle leather and vanilla combo, all the way to the end. It's definitely a decent scent, but just a tad dry for my tastes. For months, I was turned off by how the cardamom was being used in this composition - unlike the sweet, smooth and fully integrated nature of the spice in YSL's La Nuit de L'homme or CH Men Prive (both obvious competitors), the cardamom in Essence comes off a little brash and astringent when combined with the leather. There's simply not enough tonka and vanilla to balance it out. Perhaps the addition of a denser wood or amber would have been more appropriate?... In either case, I've come back to it after a couple years of disillusionment and still enjoy wearing it sparingly on cool autumn nights and rainy spring days. Damp environments tend to bring out the sweetness a bit more. And compared to the overly sweet / fruity / ambroxan heavy men's releases in the past two years, Essence de Parfum is actually a breath of fresh and elegant air, dry cardamom 'n' all.

A superb perfume, probably the best "Le Male" that you can currently buy. However, it's not the most suitable perfume for the habitual public of JPG fragrances (typically young people, avid for attention and compliments). It's less "playful" and that may cause confusion... ("Does this thing smell like... Leather? And... Sweet? OMG...") Ok, just wear it and you've got a high quality scent with a truly modern olfactory proposal: It makes a young man more interesting and seductive, and a serious man, more charismatic and appealing. Sounds good? Well, it smells fantastic. So you don't need me to tell you its notes, because you can read them, right..? What you need to know, is that it's wonderfully composed and has a beautiful interplay between them. Longevity: Easily 10h. Sillage & Projection: 2h average, the rest moderate. Lifestyle & Mood: This fragrance masterfully contrasts several concepts: manly but sweet, adult but fun, urban but refined, polite but wild, modern but traditional... You see it..? It is c.r.e.a.t.i.v.e. "Le Male Essence de Parfum" is simply what a great "designer" perfume has to be.

I don’t get any similarity to the original Le Male in this one. Ultra Male? Nope. Essence stands out with a darker, more masculine, leathery sweetness. It’s a very full scent, but it sits closer to the skin. The sillage trail is definitely there (people will know when you were in the room after you’ve left), but it’s not an exploding projector. It has about a 2ft radius of projection. The scent itself is very nice; not being similar to the original Le Male or Ultra Male in how the sweetness flows. Those two bring more of a feminine, soft sweetness. The Essence IS indeed sweet; but with more of a leathery, dark, and confident vibe. Maybe the “bad boy” of the Le Male family? Don’t get me wrong; the leather note gives more of a “brown leather cowboy” feel. It’s definitely not a “black leather jacket biker”, if that makes any sense. I get about 6-8 hours performance with the projection radius, and a great sillage trail for about 3-4. It’s not a blind buy, but I’m happy I grabbed it.

While smelling quite similar to CH Men Privé, the nuances of the opening and the way the leather is constructed differs heavily from one another. CH Privé has a slightly smoky macho leather, on the other side this Le Male Essence de Parfum is more refined and elegant, the leather on it being pretty much a hyperrealistic suede. The cologne starts with a potent herbal and cardamom opening which reminded me of frags from the 1980's. In the drydown we got a suede type leather and some vanilla. I think this is far better than the Carolina Herrera frag, which on my skin smells like plain Coca - Cola. (Not kidding) However, the scent has been discontinued and it had already been reformulated. The one i tried lasted half an hour projecting, unfortunate that Puig destroys their own creations.

I wore the original Le Male in the 90’s and to be honest, smelling it now feels outdated. But this one, while have a little of the original dna, really does deliver maturity and sexinesss without being redundant. Highly recommended!

It was 2014, my family and I were looking to spend the Eve of Christmas in our favourite Italian restaurant within my city. The cold air made our breathes observable and the feeling of joy accompanied by the smell of rough yet pleasant and recognisable nutmeg-y spice hit me once I stepped into the eatery.

I think everyone knows it - the original Le Male - which seemed to be smelled on every street corner, in every café, or even in every club at some point. Please don’t get me wrong, I found and still find it quite good. Yes, I would or even will wear it myself, if it weren't so "overworn.

Le Male intensified, yes essenced? A few years ago, some would have put on gas masks at the thought & dug out the bunker. A few reformations later that steal strength & projection, the situation looks different now... But the name is misleading: "Le Male Essence" is not necessarily the essence of the classic, not the more concentrated EdP version.
Actually, I don't test Gaultier anymore, as not a single one has convinced me to this day. Was it the reworked, more premium-feeling bottle that made me reach for the spray head?
I must say, I have never been a Gaultier fan... if I have commented on a Gaultier fragrance somewhere, my comment about the scent probably starts similarly... but that's just how it is.

In the 'mare magnum' of tuberoses, I would say that this one has decently found its own niche. The combined effect of the notes succeeds in giving vigour and meaning to this interpretation that would otherwise be merely another variation on the theme. Let me be clear, we are not dealing with an epoch-making innovation, but I believe that the combination of pepper, osmanthus and sandalwood succeeds in breathing new life into the composition. Specifically, the three notes respectively give a clear spicy opening, a fruity nuance and a soft undertone. In conclusion, a solid choice for those who love fragrances with a retro and important feel.

A remote town behind the border to Mexico. It is night, the white tuberoses release their scent into the darkness as if it could glow. And it is hot. In the Titty Twister, the table dance bar, she dances with a white snake around her neck and body, in slow, lascivious, erotic movements. The music is just as enticingly slow; the rhythm anticipates sex imaginatively with her movements. Her headpiece, which she slowly removes later, and her skimpy bikini are adorned with gemstones. Her gaze is dark, seductive. Tempting, but revealing nothing of herself. Like a distant fire deep behind her eyes. The (male) audience watches her hypnotized. Selma Hayek as Santanico Pandemonium. Most of them do not yet know what awaits them when they succumb to her power… ----- “Tubereuse Lazuli” could be the scent for this scene from Robert Rodriguez's “From Dusk till Dawn” (1996). For me, it is a night fragrance and of course only suitable for tuberose lovers. The main character is a very distinct, yet highly elegant tuberose, hardly indolic, which I initially found a bit disappointing. Nevertheless, or perhaps precisely because of this, it is very seductive. Chypre-like, as indicated in the classification, I do not find it at all; the bergamot in the top note hides from me, at most the beginning is slightly aldehydic. And then it goes straight into the tuberose, whose floral scent appears very authentic here, with jasmine mixing in to enhance it. I wouldn’t have thought of osmanthus, perhaps it contributes something soft that I like here. Overall, the fragrance combines something both gem-clear and yet soft. In the end, a beautiful soft sandalwood base awaits. Only a trace of earthy-smoky patchouli can still evoke the dangerous - knocking on devil’s door… ----- Tuberose is always a very sensual scent that can dissolve inhibitions - perhaps even those one would rather keep in everyday life… Therefore, it is understandable if it is rejected due to its disinhibiting effect. It originally comes from Mexico, but has long been cultivated and used in India, among other things in wedding ceremonies. The Hindi name is “Rajnigandha,” the scent that comes from the night. In Europe, it was banned in the early modern period because it was feared that it could corrupt young women and trigger spontaneous orgasms… “Tubereuse Lazuli” (2024) is not really a new scent, but of good quality. It belongs to Chloé's Fleur-de-Nuit collection. On the website, it says: “Fresh and green in the early morning hours, the scent of tuberose becomes denser and more intoxicating in the evening. To capture this intoxicating sensuality, perfumer Jean-Christophe Hérault has combined Indian tuberose with intoxicating jasmine.” Interestingly, the same idea underlies Bulgari's “Splendida - Tubereuse Mystique” from 2019, as explained in an interview with perfumer Sophie Labbé from 2020: “In India, where the plant grows and is cultivated, necklaces made from its buds are used in religious ceremonies. The flowers are picked in the morning before they open. This was also the method used for the flowers intended for perfume production. Inspired by the color of the bottle, the perfume team came up with the idea to shift the harvest time to dusk, the famous ‘l’heure bleu’. A test harvest showed: The difference is enormous. Labbé has two samples ready for the journalist: ‘In the morning, the scent is fresh and green, in the evening much creamier, more intense, and sensual,’ says perfumer Labbé.” Unfortunately, I am not yet familiar with “Splendida - Tubereuse Mystique,” so I will have to conduct further tuberose fragrance research soon… “Tubereuse Lazuli” has good but not excessive longevity, which is almost a quality sign these days. And the sillage does not radiate atomically, which I find rather good in the case of tuberose and makes the scent more wearable. And more seductive. “I'm not going to drain you completely. …Welcome to slavery!” Clearly, this is the music for it: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UTCbnJLYQA8 And here with Santanico Pandemonium's dance… https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1-g2LECVXgc NZZ interview about Tubereuse Mystique (Bulgari) from January 5, 2020: https://bellevue.nzz.ch/mode-beauty/die-tuberose-fuer-den-neuen-duft-von-bulgari-wird-abends-gepflueckt-ld.1530004

I've come to expect things from Hugo Boss. First mistake, I know, but with such a knockout scent as Hugo Boss Hugo (try saying that five times fast), I thought that the house had some fragrance mojo goin' on. Alas, it is not to be. Hugo Boss XY goes on like high-end hotel soap -- very clean, vaguely oriental, and slightly fruity. Then, depending on your fortunes, it may achieve another movie parody name -- Gone in 90 Minutes. Even if it hangs around, this scent is the king of intimate silage. Within an hour, it's a skin scent. Now it doesn't smell revolting, but neither is it interesting. It's like hotel soap meets harem oil with a few pieces of citrus arranged in the room for feng-shui power. Anyone want a slightly used sample?

Sometimes I should not be so quick. Especially when it comes to buying a fragrance. Unfortunately, that was the case with XY as well. The scent has a certain component that immediately appealed to my nose. But instead of asking for a test vial to take home, I pulled out my wallet right away. XY is the male counterpart of a conceptual Hugo Boss fragrance pair. There isn’t much to it, except that the two fragrances share the bottle and the chromosomes XX for the female and XY for the male name are used. Then there’s a little variation in the color scheme (silver and gold), and you have two different bottles for two quite different scents. The box of XY is, as is often the case with Boss, very simple, silver as the base tone with subtle red and black lettering. The bottle is supposed to reflect a spray can, hence it is simply cylindrical with a discreet print on the clear glass container. The liquid is slightly smoky gray in some versions, while in others it is clear. A massive silver cap seals the bottle at the top. Simple, but not stunning. Pear leaves provide a green opening for the scent, which soon receives a very fresh boost from mint and a little bergamot. Basil adds even more spicy-green notes. In the base, the velvety soft, almost balsamic cedar is dominant; I cannot discern patchouli or musk. That’s it: fresh-spicy-woody. Initially, I was very attracted to the mint, which floats on a green base. However, a very superficial wood note follows, and over time, the scent feels too one-dimensional, too weak for me to truly enjoy. The projection is quite OK, but when the mint disappears after about two hours like chewed gum, the sillage decreases significantly. Overall, the scent does not last longer than four to five hours. For a summer fragrance, that might be acceptable, but unfortunately, it’s too little for me in the long run. And for a sport fragrance, it also lacks the necessary base besides the citrus component. With its minty-green notes, it’s a nice summer scent, but unfortunately a bit weak.

I find this scent very cool and fresh, which in my opinion is caused by the mint. The first impression after spraying it was like a "standard" scent, but this fragrance takes just a short moment and the cool freshness captivates you immediately. Thus, the scent has a good recognizability. I am very enthusiastic and love this minty fresh fragrance that makes you feel truly alive. This will be my next purchase ;)

The name Boss certainly suggests pure dominance, yet most Boss fragrances are rather reserved. The true puppeteers prefer to remain discreetly in the background :-) In my opinion, XY also does not stand out in the lineup of Boss fragrances. The scent is pleasantly spicy. I perceive basil most distinctly. By the way, it's one of my favorite spices in the kitchen *g* Still, I can hardly find anything appealing about XY. It doesn't smell unpleasant, but that's about it.

Aside from the price, there is little positive to say about this fragrance. When I read the reviews from other people here, I wonder if we smelled the same scent… I understand that some people are attracted to this green scent character and would label this fragrance as a fresh summer cheapie, but I don’t understand how one can be undisturbed by this medical synthetic note. The green freshness lasts for the first five minutes, but then it shifts into a spicy, mineral mess. This fragrance reminds me most of Curryking + disinfectant that ended up in the same bin. One thing I understand even less is why one would choose this over all the masculine Boss fragrances. One would think that if you are looking for a masculine freshie, of which there are more than enough at Boss, you would find something better than this synthetic mix, which I will definitely wash off after this review.
a very challenging and individual scent from Boss. pear leaves, mint, and cedarwood are from the party and give the fragrance something very dominant. I really like xy!

This is the original with a few tweaks. . This scent is amazing! First, I loved the original 2005 version. Really was amazing when I was 20 years old and now still amazing when im 33. I was so scared when I first bought this because I didn't think it would give me all the feelings I got when I first smelled it that young. BUT BEHOLD, IT HELD ITS OWN & GAVE ME THAT FEELING! . You first spray you get a big dose of Vanilla & Jasmine with amber. The musk is present more in the background. . It last very long. It's 40° where I live today, in December & i sprayed it on at 1:30pm & still smell whiffs clear as day now were at around 730. It gets a little woodier & muskier the longer it sits. But the vanilla and amber are still present just more of a backseat presence. The Jasmine really is there but not the way the Cedarwood took over. Can be worn by men or women easily. Because whoever you wear it for, or occasion, it's gonna have someone or that "someone", saying how damn GOOD you smell! Wear it in spring, fall or winter. Preferably spring and fall ...... . It's back & just as good as ever, so get ya hands on this fragrance!. . I also have a great review to check out on this fragrance & it won't take all day to watch

Attention, dear ones! There are at least two new Gaultier2 versions, and the batch codes are also different. I was surprised that the notes on the Gaultier homepage have changed as well, but it was indeed not just marketing! According to the packaging: 2022, floral, as in my original review. Family: Woody, Floral, Powdery Jasmine, Sandalwood, Ambergris 2023, closer to the original. Family: Woody, Amber Musk, Vanilla, Amber New review: The 2023 formulation is indeed closer to the original and almost exactly the same! Just like before, I cannot detect any jasmine or floral notes! After some maturation, both fragrances have become more intense than right after purchase. Nevertheless, neither of them matches the 2005 version in terms of sillage or longevity. In the souk, everyone has to see for themselves what might suit them better, as not only the "old" versions vary greatly in batches but also the new ones! :D The 2022 is a bit sweeter & more feminine due to the floral notes & definitely very well done. Due to the international rush for the reissue, the 2022 version is likely to be rarer & harder to obtain. Moreover, it is now somehow a special addition & for me a great collectible! Those who wanted the original are definitely better off with the 2023 version. On the test strip, I cannot detect any difference in sillage between both new releases. In terms of longevity, the 2023 has improved a bit. Although it doesn't last for days, it is a little longer to smell. Due to the absence of floral notes, it feels a bit "more" unisex to me than the 2022 version. The scent is and remains a sweet powerhouse :D I hope my review helps some of you a bit. Since it is my signature scent, I feel compelled to test the 2024 version as well. If I notice any differences, I will continue to update. Original review from 2022: Finally, it is back, even if only available online. The original Gaultier2 accompanied me through numerous party nights. It stood out and compliments poured in. Even if the disco was packed, it overshadowed almost all other scents, established itself, and stood out as the clear winner in the crowd. Having been heavily wounded in my preferences, I tested just about every dupe available on the market until I crowned my favorite. I was accordingly over the moon when I found out it was coming back! Ordered at release, I could hardly wait, and it was delivered this morning.. The expectations were high, and I was literally afraid to open the package! I haven't been this nervous in a long time :D So many positive memories are attached to this scent! The good news is, I am not disappointed! It clearly contains the same DNA as the old Gaultier2 and it smells good. However, it is different. In the past (in the first versions), it was heavier. The sillage lasted for hours within a 3-meter radius, and it left a heavy vanilla mist in its wake. This has now shifted to a more modern-feeling, quite fitting, but lighter floral note. This will make the scent more wearable for many in everyday life and allows it to be integrated into all seasons. However, it is surprising, this decision. It is unisex! And for a unisex scent, it has also been worn by an above-average number of men. Due to this now more subdued decision and the jasmine accord, it suddenly feels a bit more feminine. More feminine, for me, is not a problem. However, for my taste, I would have liked it to be a bit more. Also floral, this power can! Spraying the Gaultier Fleur Terrible, it fills the entire room with its aura and says to everyone, hello, here I am! And that for hours. With the new Gaultier2, I would have wished for exactly that again; one of the key carriers of its fame is now missing. Now, like with many scents, you have to go in for a cuddle. I have to get within 30cm of the scent to sniff it.. It is simply less bold, less loud, but rounder and more adapted. What a shame! Because I like to stand out and enjoy wearing scents that can be a bit edgy. It smells soooo beautiful.. But it now makes it very difficult for my fellow humans to tell me so!!! :D The memory of youthful emotions, unfortunately, cannot be brought back to me like this. However, it has become a great scent again. Even though it has to take a back seat in comparison, I can recommend everyone to gift themselves this scent. I still have a glimmer of hope that a few more weeks of aging will turn things around a bit, so I remain curious =)

Recently, Gaultier² (2022) experienced a huge hype again. Of course, this made me curious: What is so special about this fragrance that it is celebrated to such an extent? I had added it to my wishlist and nearly forgotten about it until my dear friend "Northlight" discovered it there and kindly offered me a sample. I was extremely happy, especially since I even received two more samples along with it. Thanks again for that! I imagined the scent to be vanillic and floral, and that is exactly what it turned out to be. The opening strongly reminded me of "Reflection Man | Amouage," albeit in a sweeter variant. The jasmine note is very similar to that of the Amouage. In the top note, jasmine initially dominates, but gradually the initial sweetness becomes more pronounced through the vanilla, which can be well perceived in the base along with the jasmine.
