After about ten minutes, I also notice amber, sandalwood, and especially musk. However, for me, it is the jasmine that sets the tone here. In the end, the combination of jasmine and musk develops a slight bubblegum note for me, accompanied by the sweetness of the amber and vanilla. From the dry down, the fragrance indeed leans a bit more feminine (W60%/40%M), although I would still classify it as a unisex scent overall. Surprisingly, I find the performance to be strong. I perceive it very well over a long period, which I absolutely did not expect, even though I didn't overspray it. The longevity is also more than decent, hats off! What can I say? I am extremely grateful that I got to test it. However, the "Reflection Man" vibes bother me, as I do not like the Amouage at all and am strongly reminded of it here. But for those who celebrate this fragrance and are looking for a slightly more feminine version, they will clearly find it here.

18 years old … Taking public transport to pre-game with the guys. Hair and outfit are on point. Which fragrance? Yes, which one now… Dior Homme Intense (2007) ???? A lot of people are really wearing that right now…. So Gaultier² (2005) …. 1.2.3.4.5.6.7.8 sprays to make it last all night. So here we go in my amber, musk, and vanilla scent cloud. So many wild evenings and nights spent with you, until it was discontinued and I was left with only the half-full bottle that I cherished like a treasure. This powerful scent that still smells so soft and sweet. Simply incredibly wonderful on a man and so different on a woman, as if it adapts to the wearer. Now I’m 32 … the evenings are still wild (now they are evenings where the little daughters don’t want to sleep, or the very little one can’t find peace due to colic). When I heard that Gaultier 2 was coming back, I was curious. Many fragrances that return are usually a bitter disappointment. But not here. Gaultier 2 still impresses with its incredible scent DNA, yet something is different. It smells floral, grown-up, no longer so wild, but more suitable for everyday wear. Musk and vanilla have been replaced by sandalwood and jasmine, making it more mature and less sweetly conspicuous. Nevertheless, it impresses with an amazing sillage and longevity. All in all, the new Gaultier 2 is a modern interpretation of this classic that is wearable for both men and women.

I recently secured the reissue of this icon from the official Jean Paul website, the stallion, after there was such a stir about the re-release in the forum, without me ever having smelled the fragrance. So much for FOMO (most probably know this term in connection with the stock market, which, by the way, usually doesn’t end well...)! At the same time as the fragrance, I ordered a sample here in the forum to test how the scent really smells, before I fall into ecstasy for about 10 seconds while removing the cellophane from the original packaging, as I always do (who doesn’t know that?). I must admit, I ordered the fragrance blind but didn’t really expect much. Why is that? I was recently tempted by a hype surrounding Égoïste Eau de Toilette on a well-known deal platform, where Égoïste was praised to the skies and also received very good reviews here on Parfumo. (WARNING, now comes quite a bit of text about Égoïste, but this is necessary to ultimately establish the connection to JPG2): I did something similar to what I did in hindsight with JPG2: I had ordered a sample of Égoïste at the same time here in the Souk. When I sprayed the sample, I was overwhelmed by a gag reflex-like state after a relatively short time. I actually had to wash it off, even though I didn’t want to, because I couldn’t imagine that the scent could trigger such a reaction in me. Many are probably cursing me now for saying such things about Égoïste. Because I didn’t want to accept that, I sprayed it again a few days later right after showering, to really wash away any "remnants" of previous perfumes that could possibly cause a cross-reaction with the scent. However, I experienced exactly the same thing. In my opinion, it is only suitable for Ü50 parties. I had the same concern when I ordered JPG2 due to FOMO, even though there is a decade between the release of Égoïste and JPG2, they are somehow both "vintage" and therefore to be approached with caution by the "modern clientele," often being labeled as "old man scent." However, when I sprayed the sample, I was on cloud nine. It is the complete opposite of Égoïste and doesn’t smell like an old man scent at all. My skepticism changed abruptly into euphoria and bliss! I don’t know how the old "vintage" version smells, but I immediately thought of "Reflection Man | Amouage," just much more ambry. A real dream! In my opinion, this is a Reflection Man 2.0, purely from the fragrance experience. In the drydown, I also clearly smelled vanilla, even though it wasn’t listed in the fragrance notes when I checked at that time. Now, as I write this review, this fragrance note has strangely appeared on Parfumo (previously there were three fragrance notes, and at the current state of my review, there are five; vanilla and amber have, in my opinion, been added, exactly the two fragrance notes that I strongly detected from the scent without having read the notes here on Parfumo). Especially in the drydown, I really smell almost only vanilla, which is why I couldn’t understand why there was (initially) no vanilla fragrance note listed. In my opinion, it has two development stages. Jasmine, sandalwood, and amber in the first hours, and later it becomes more vanilla or actually almost only vanilla. In my eyes, it only goes through two development stages. Today's developments in fragrances with multi-stage evolutions are actually rather modern, which can be both advantageous and disadvantageous. I’ll compare it to "Nefs | Nishane," which seems to go through 10 developments (but also costs five times as much). A very strong contrast, which, of course, stands in absolute contradiction price-wise (I wanted to exaggerate here intentionally). However, the fragrance has one major disadvantage: the longevity is really poor. On the day of this review, I conducted a practical test until just before midnight. At 8:30 AM, I sprayed about 4 sprays on my left and right forearm (T-shirt in the home office) and 3 on the front of my neck (since I’m in the home office, I didn’t spray anything behind my ears). For the next 2-3 hours, I was internally moaning about how great it smells. But by noon, it became weak, and I had to press my nose to my forearm. So I reapplied, but only a little, because at that moment I didn’t see the need to spray as much as I did at 8:30 AM. By 3 PM, I could hardly smell anything anymore. Since I then went shopping, put on a jacket, and didn’t want to "contaminate" it with the scent, I sprayed another 3 sprays just on my neck. While shopping, I could still smell it very well, which made the supermarket trip quite an experience, but by 6 PM it was all over. Everything was gone from my arms, and I couldn’t even press my nose to my neck, as I’m not Marilyn Manson, who had a few ribs removed to be able to bend down further than usual and... well... do something "good" for himself. :( Conclusion: The fragrance is simply fantastic, purely from a scent perspective. The longevity is poor, yes! Now it depends on what is important to you. Personally, longevity is secondary for me, as I wear fragrances for my own olfactory experience, and then I’m happy to reapply. And if it happens three times like today, then it has to be that way. It’s a shame, and there are deductions for longevity, but if a fragrance smells this good, I just can’t do without it. If long-lasting performance is the top priority, then this fragrance is the wrong choice! And since I didn’t want to end the review on a negative note: I love the Gaultier times two, hüüüüüa! :)

At first moment upon application, this scent is very feminine, but it does not remain so. The femininity lasts only a few minutes, and then a warm scent of vanilla and musk emerges, which holds steady and gradually becomes a bit weaker, later blending with sandalwood and amber, making this fragrance wonderfully warm and sweet with a floral accent.

My beloved Gaultier 2. My absolute favorite fragrance. I was so sad when I found out a few years ago that they were discontinuing it. For me, it was and still is, without a doubt, the best fragrance there has ever been (!!) Now you already know how I feel about this perfume. When I found out that it would be coming back on the market, I could hardly believe my luck.

The 2005 version of Gaultier² was already quite a powerhouse. It's a shame it was discontinued - what a stroke of luck that it has been resurrected as the 2022 version. Long-time wearers can immediately tell the difference. Others may not even remember the original version or only have a vague recollection. At first sniff, both seem identical.

Is the hype real or just a little hype? We'll see, but first, you should smell it. What is it like? Imagine the following: You take the powderiness of "Le Male." Add a bit of "gummy bear sweetness" like in Joop Homme (EdT) or in "So Scandal" - with a certain synthetic touch.

It was released in 2005 and has certainly remained in the minds of many perfume enthusiasts who had it under their noses. I would even say that in the following years, it almost enjoyed the hype of "1 Million (Eau de Toilette) | Paco Rabanne". Unfortunately, it was discontinued a few years later, but it gained many fans, myself included.

A sample - a new fragrance from "Chloe" is also new to my nose. I have hardly smelled anything similar, despite many years of fragrance experience. So far, I am only familiar with the two classics from the 1970s: Fleur de Narcisse and "Chloé (1975) (Eau de Toilette) | Chloé," which are true olfactory "hits." This "Atelier de Fleurs - Immortelle | Chloé" is a fine, versatile floral scent that knows how to take subtle "adventurous" paths. It plays with the seasons, which do not always unfold in chronological order here. There is the very early spring, characterized by cool citrus fruits. At the same time, I can recognize the flowers of summer right in the middle! Leading are jasmine and a bit of tuberose. The "full spring" is, however, taking its time. For it seems to be autumn first! Here, the silvery-leaved immortelle is fragrant, together with woods. But then, when a delicate "aquatic" and slightly salty note appears, the "full spring" at the seaside with its pleasant temperatures and slightly humid air becomes a delight for the nose. Much later, after the blooming summer becomes stronger again and the "immortelle woody autumn" creeps in, winter approaches. Characterized by warm vanilla and a bit of orange. And soon the "circle of seasons" closes with awakening cool citrus fruits of early spring... Finesse in the bottle :-))

I have never smelled Immortelle before. Either I was vacationing in the wrong areas or simply inattentive. However, the Italian strawflower looks quite inconspicuous - scruffy, green-gray foliage and yellow flower clusters; nothing you would put in a vase. Here in the forum, the scent of Immortelle seems to polarize a lot. There are certainly many, as I have now read, who find it unbearable. How fortunate that I completely unsuspectingly acquired a sample of Ateliers des Fleurs - Immortelle in the souk. I like jasmine and tuberose, which is why I found the scent interesting. The first spray hits you with a burst of citrus - BAM. If you weren't fully awake before, you are now. The salty notes come across as somewhat "quirky" without me being able to identify them. Shortly after the somewhat aftershave-like opening, the flowers unfold - and now begins a highly interesting fight between the bitter-spicy Immortelle and the soft-sweet white flowers jasmine and tuberose. For a longer stretch, the battle remains undecided. Even more: The scent notes unite into a slightly soapy, fresh, and herbal-floral triad that is extremely attractive in its contradictions. The perfume becomes more peaceful when sandalwood and vanilla soothe the Immortelle and harmoniously unite the contrasts. A friend remarked while sniffing on my arm that this is the scent for an unconventional, self-confident, and quirky artist. Although I am not an artist, the adjectives do fit quite well. However, on dreary, damp autumn days when the heart is a bit out of tune, I prefer to reach for another perfume, as Ateliers des Fleurs Immortelle needs a strong ego and plenty of sunlight to fully unleash its revitalizing powers. Therefore, it is a spring and summer scent for me. Longevity: Average. After a few hours, the fire has burned down and only smolders quietly. Price: So far my most expensive perfume. Is it justified? I think so, because this is not a mainstream scent that will have high sales numbers. Bottle: Classic, rather inconspicuous, but somehow fitting. The closure is practical, made of roughened plastic, which can also be easily removed with cream-covered fingers.

I have a tester of Boss Orange Sunset to one side of me, and a glass of tropical fruit juice on the other. The similarities are pretty surprising. Boss Orange Sunset is one of those typical fruity scents that attempt to emulate the scent of shampoo and sugary fruit juice. I didn't mind the original Boss Orange, which despite its sweetened and synthetic orange note, had a delightful creaminess. This Boss Orange Sunset however is too strong and juicy for my liking. The lasting power and sillage are pretty amazing. For those that adore the smell of this, the quality is a plus, however for those like me that find this fragrance a bit of a headache-inducer, it can definitely get on your nerves. Like I mentioned before, the orange is pretty dominant in this fragrance, so is the sugary note. There are some subtle floral accords, however they don't seem to be present until the drydown. I'm a little underwhelmed by this fragrance, not that Hugo Boss is known for making anything outstanding but I like most of them. I will be interested to see how well this sells this Summer.

The color of the bottle initially made me hesitate. Somehow, it suggested the scent of cloves/gingerbread to me. I was very pleased when the fragrance finally unfolded on my skin! Fresh, warm, powdery. I like it a lot! ADDITIONAL NOTE 23.01.2011: I can no longer stand by my previous 70%. It now comes across as too synthetic to me. It's nice, but nothing more.

...floral...fruity...sweet... I distribute my clicks listlessly when categorizing this scent. How often have I clicked on "floral-fruity-sweet," and how often was the tested fragrance much better than this one...?! Often. Very often. And it's synthetic too, oh yes... Hello-ho! The fragrance is called Sunset! SUNRISE!!! A new day begins, first with timid sunbeams, then with a dazzling bright sunlight. Carpe diem - seize the day, it seems to call, the sun, this warm, radiant bright orange-yellow-white sphere, without which our planet would be surrounded by eternal night, without which life on Earth would not be possible. One shakes off the fatigue despite a slight chill in the limbs and starts the morning in a good mood. THAT would be, for example, a sunrise. Life without this fragrance, however, is very much possible compared to the sunless variant. For something like this, I don't get up; I'd rather draw the curtains, turn over, and continue snoring. It comes across to me as so annoyingly synthetic that I would prefer to wash it off. It is simply floral-fruity-sweet. Boring, unpleasant, synthetic. I can't smell any mandarin, no flowers, no freshness that should actually be somewhere. And the vanilla is just irritatingly cheap. As much as I like the original Boss Orange Woman, this one is simply unnecessary. So nothing sunset, rather a mental blackout.

"BOSS Orange Sunset" is a fragrance that perfectly suits the winding down of a summer day for me. The heat of the day slowly fades away. You feel tired from a long, but very lovely summer day at the beach or by the pool. A refreshing shower has washed away sweat, sunscreen, chlorine, and salt smells from the body, and it’s time to sit on the terrace in a light, flowing summer dress, enjoy the last rays of sunshine, and then let the day come to an end in the glow of torches and lanterns. For these hours, in my opinion, there is no better fragrance than "BOSS Orange Sunset." It is a soft, warm, gentle scent - I don't smell bergamot at all, but I do perceive the mandarin very strongly. The rose and white flowers can also be detected, but they remain pleasantly modest in the background for me, allowing the cheerful, sweet scent of the mandarins to dominate until the end. Vanilla is only hinted at, but it gives the fragrance a soothing delicacy. The scent is subtle, and the sillage is hardly present. "BOSS Orange Sunset" is therefore not a summer night party fragrance. But for calm, warm summer evenings in the company of family or a few close friends, where you just want to lean back in a lounge chair and enjoy, it is the perfect fragrance.

Today the sky hangs gray and heavy like lead over the city. No, not a sky full of violins, but full of rain clouds. My friend suggests a sniffing tour, which I willingly agree to. In the store, I aim for a beautiful orange-gold-yellow shimmering bottle, which truly glows when I hold it up to the light. Orange Sunset. And the opening of bergamot and mandarin captivates me for it. Citrusy - but warm. The also warm rose brings a hidden violin in the sky to life. The image of the sun rising from the horizon in the morning comes to life before my eyes. I hum Golden Brown by the Stranglers: Golden Brown texture like the sun lays me down - with my mind she runs Throughout the night No need to fight Never a frown - with golden brown. The sweet, soft vanilla that hovers over the scent truly smooths the frown off my face. This fragrance is gentle and tender, like the mild rays of the morning sun after a long night. I treated myself to a bottle of this confident morning mood.

Another blind buy, I actually wanted to get Boss Orange at the duty-free shop, I had already tested it extensively and I must say I am quite a little Boss fan :-D especially of Deep Red, but Orange has also captured my interest. Well, at the duty-free there was a super special offer, just from Orange Sunset, so I saw it and bought it.
sunset is quickly described: smells cheap, way too sweet and synthetic. those who like this will also find options in cheaper price ranges. every wearer may forgive me! -end-

As bad as the scent comes across here, it's really not that bad! "Orange Sunset" starts fruity-fresh, with the mandarin clearly recognizable. It's actually not my taste to be too fruity or too fresh, but I find this opening quite successful and somehow... relaxing. Then the flowers come into play and make the scent softer, rounder.

~ Inspiration ~ I was curious about the "Sunset" variant of Boss Orange, as I find both the EDT and the EDP quite nice. ~ Bottle ~ The stacked gemstones were also used here as a distinctive feature. The gradient from red to orange to yellow skillfully reflects the sunrise, as the name already suggests.

If you already own any one of the following fragrances — Le Male Le Parfum, Le Male Elixir, or Le Male Elixir Absolu — then purchasing another from this trio is, quite honestly, unnecessary. The scent profiles are incredibly similar, to the point where the differences are barely noticeable in daily wear. While each version may have slight tweaks in notes or intensity, in real-world use, they all deliver a nearly identical olfactory experience. Le Male Le Parfum brought a darker, more mature twist to the original DNA. Elixir added a touch more sweetness and density, while Elixir Absolu is marketed as an even more intense and luxurious version. But when sprayed side by side, the nuances are extremely subtle — and mostly apparent only to trained noses or hardcore fragrance enthusiasts. In terms of projection, sillage, and longevity, they all perform excellently, lasting 8–10 hours with ease. For the average user or even the moderately invested fragrance fan, it’s hard to justify the price of buying all three. The bottle designs are attractive and collectible, which may appeal to fans of the brand, but if you’re looking for variety in your scent wardrobe, these aren’t distinct enough to warrant multiple purchases. In short, unless you’re a die-hard collector of Jean Paul Gaultier fragrances or want every limited edition release for display purposes, you can confidently skip buying the others if you already own one. You won’t be missing out on anything groundbreaking — they all smell great, but they smell pretty much the same.

For me it's like le male elixir plus a fruity, synthetic plum with from time to time a light coconut*ish note. Similar to the scandal absolu Plum / coconut*ish accord. Pretty similar to the elixir in smell and performance. So kinda redundant but it's also quite apart with the distinct fruity note. But that's almost the only difference for me. Maybe it's also a bit less harsh compared to the elixir, probably because of less tobacco. Pretty good I like it. But seems maybe even a bit more sweet and juvenile than the elixir. And also even a bit more unisex. So I think I still prefer the elixir although both I'd say are pretty good.

My first JPG was Le Male, bought when it was first released. For years, it was my favorite perfume. What I found in this new release has something that reminds me of the original Le Male. Now amplified and showing itself with more impact in a more intense and sophisticated version, combining the stronger facet of Elixir. Initially, it is explosive, as if shouting loudly: "I've arrived!". A very striking aroma made to capture all the attention immediately. The opening is marked by the refreshing lavender, alongside the plum, creating a fruity and juicy sensation. In the background, after the initial explosion, a sweetish tone emerges that envelops us, almost warm, leading us to the tonka bean surrounded by vanilla. Amber Aromatic profile, very radiant, made to stand out in the crowd, clearly for a young and modern audience who like striking perfumes and are not afraid to attract attention. It sins by excess, which makes it too heavy and ends up saturating.

… I grabbed it because I’m a Le Male loyalist. Is it “groundbreaking”? Nope. Is it a “must have”? Absolutely not. Do I regret it? Hell no, I’m a Le Male fan. That’s how you have to look at this. If you have a bunch of Le Male and aren’t a loyalist, you’ll find this a bit redundant. Yes there are some SUBTLE differences, but if you have or recognize the Elixir or Parfum, you’ll smell the similarities. Performance wise, just like all JPGs, the scent projects and performs well. A 5+ft radius scent bubble that leaves a lingering sillage trail that points directly to you and where you’ve been. Longevity is 8-10+ hours. It’s a bit sweet for formal events, but otherwise it’s flexible for usage. Not very different than the more recent releases, but that’s how JPG plays the game. They want you to recognize the family DNA. I’m happy with it. Enough said

While this is *slightly* linear, its got a bit of complexity to it. The sweet components work really well together and is very smooth. Tonka bean, benzoin, the random whiffs of plum in the air.. its beautiful. The spices are soft, its a very warm cinnamon and cardamom feel that give a lot of personality to the fragrance. I would usually prefer my spices to have more texture to them, but its simplicity works here. Within the spices, there's the supporting notes that fill in the gaps and make it more smooth and complete. It's a woody labdanum and patchouli, and the smooth davana really connects the woodiness with the fruity sweet notes. I don't really detect artemisia or bergamot, the ambrette gets a lot more prominent the longer its on skin, giving a lot of texture instead of just smelling something sweet at the end of its life. Quentin Bisch made something really amazing here, definitely an improvement on the original Elixir. It's a lot smoother, less in your face, and it makes the wearing experience so much better. If you liked the smell of Elixir, but hated wearing it, I think there's a good chance you're going to like this one.

Elixir Absolu opens up different yet familiar to the original JPG Le Male Elixir. It doesn’t have the cooling the mint note. Instead you get a good deal of that lavender, with some warmer spice, and a new addition of a sweet plum. To me, the plum actually isn’t too heavy in the start. It’s much less of a tart note and sweeter than I thought it would be.

Rainy day in Maryland, but this scent matched the mood perfectly. Elixir Absolu opens with the familiar lavender, but it quickly shifts into something warmer and spicier, with cinnamon standing out more than I expected. It’s less sweet than the original Elixir, leaning richer and more refined.

Fragrance Notes Top Notes: Lavender Mid Notes: Plum Base Notes: Tonka Bean. Fragrance Review: First thoughts, it starts off boozy, mixed with plum and dries to a vanilla/tonka bean scent. Le Male Elixir Absolu has a dominant boozy, plum fruity sweetness is similar to Carolina Herrera Bad Boy Cobalt. I sprayed a total of 5 times.

So, I've tested Elixir Absolu on my left hand and regular Elixir on my right, both with two sprays on the same spot. I first smelled Elixir Absolu and I liked the opening much better than Elixir because it wasn't harsh, but...

As soon as I sprayed it, only one thing came to mind: wow, it smells like makeup. I started rummaging through different makeup products to understand what it reminded me of specifically, and in the end I realized that the scent closest to it is cocoa butter and lipsticks.

As good as the scent smells… I am very disappointed with it. It doesn't last at all for me and almost disappears immediately. It smells very fresh, berry-like, and fruity… somehow also like orange blossoms, but unfortunately I can't detect much more as the scent fades away very quickly and is lost. The bottle, on the other hand, looks nice and has a beautiful mysterious design. But it will definitely be sorted out from my collection!

This fragrance appealed to me much more because of the color of the bottle than the classic "The Scent" ever could. I actually didn't like the classic scent at all. But this time I applied both, as I happened to have a sample of the classic The Scent and received the new "The Scent Magnetic." I then scented one arm with one and the other arm with the other. At first, the scents couldn't be more different. The classic The Scent smells fruitier, while the Magnetic has a strong Osmanthus scent. This makes it smell more floral and initially much more overpowering. After a while, the scents develop, and then I can hardly smell a difference. With the Magnetic, I still slightly perceive the musk note in the background. But you really have to smell directly on the skin to even notice the minimal difference. In the end, the scent is not really new to me. It is personally more pleasant at the beginning than the classic The Scent. But neither fragrance is my world. They are simply too floral for me in the end. And also too similar for me to pay the extra price for the new product.

I had originally written a statement about it but felt I needed to explain a little more. Divine is an exotic/marine perfume. For me, no meringue nor white flowers but a very strong smell of coconut and pineapple surrounded by a salty/sea breeze. What strikes me as odd is that it's undeniably salty but also sweet and in a way that I find very cloying. To be completely honest, I should point out that I usually don't like sea/marine smells even if sometimes they can suit me. But Divine... I just can't stand it. Too salty but also too sugary, I don't know... It's a mess that's not very pleasant to my nose. On the other hand, I really love the bottle.

First and foremost my favorite thing about this fragrance is the bottle! I got a sample size in a kit from Sephora and would almost redeem the voucher for a full size of this because of the bottle alone. I'm a huge anatomy geek so needless to say I'm a big fan of Jean Paul Gaultier's bottles :) The fragrance itself isn't bad but it's not something I'd find myself reaching for very often. In a lot of my reviews I talk about how I'm very picky about my white florals because they often come across as cloying. This almost steps into that territory as the fragrance warms up on my skin but the first sniff or two is wonderful and as it fades I like it more. It's not unbearable or bad at all but could easily be something I'm not a fan of in the right circumstances. I'd love to see more floral gourmands because I feel like those have interesting potential but this just *barely* overdoes it with the white florals.

I was able to get my hands on a bottle of Gaultier Divine just a few weeks ago and I love it! One of the few perfumes I blindly bought and I couldn't have chosen better. It reminds me of my summers spent in Saint Tropez and on the southern coast of France. Tropical fruit, vanilla and sea breeze. I find it elegant and playful at the same time. A modern and refined perfume. Not for everyone. In Italy it is difficult to find, mine comes from Germany, but I am happy with it, because I love it so much that I would like to be the only one to wear it. I hope it never becomes too widespread.

Did you ever wonder, "What would it smell like if a watermelon threw up?" Wonder no more! Gaultier's Divine is anything but. This should be balmy white flowers and fruity beach vibes in the tropics, but there's a sharp, sour, acidic undercurrent that turns the whole perfume to the back alley behind a dive bar. Have you ever held a girl's hair in a nightclub bathroom, wincing with your eyes watering, studiously pretending not to hear the sound of her prayers to the porcelain god? Oh, my friend, you will intimately know Divine. It's the fragrance of a going out top, three too many Skinnygirl vodka sodas, and texting your ex. This...is the smell of hot girl bad decisions. I know, I'm being harsh. But legitimately the opening of my sample smells so bad, so much like actual fruity floral vomit and leftover tequila salt, I almost wonder if it's gone off. I suspect the meringue is the problem on my skin, because I also own VS Tease Creme Cloud which shares the same note and both have the same party-girl-but-sick element in common. I adore other Gaultier (La Belle, my beloved!) but on me, this is ABSOLUTELY horrendous. I am SO jealous that it smells nice on other people. -- This review previously appeared on another site under the name "PrincessPrickleson." That's me! I'm moving my collection to Parfumo.

First off, a few notes are missing for this one. Here is the full note list for this fragrance taken from the Harrods website: Base notes: Meringue, Patchouli, Musk Middle notes: Lily, Jasmine, Ylang-ylang Top notes: Calypsone, Pink berry, Bergamot Second off, from first sniff, I knew I’d like this as I love white florals. Every JPG I’ve tried has been a HIT for me, and this one is no different! Divine is a sweet and salty white floral scent that doesn’t smell anything like the Fleur Terrible flanker. This has a noticeable marine note and while it’s very floral, the meringue note sweetens it the overall scent profile up quite a bit. It has that JPG DNA running through it, but the overall vibe actually reminds me of a Mugler fragrance, especially with the jasmine and patchouli notes in there. It’s so beautiful!! The sillage and longevity on this one are very good! The one small spray I did on the back of my hand with projecting with every movement of mine and I’m very impressed with it! Most JPG frags have great longevity as well, so I expect the same from this one! While the scent definitely gives a summer vibe, I think this would be appropriate to wear year round, day or night. Don’t let the bad ratings or bad reviews scare you! This is a beautiful scent, especially if you’re a big fan of sweet white florals. Quentin Bisch has done it again!

this scent is lovely, reminiscent of a very creamy and luscious dessert by the beach... but then a massive wave comes and leaves your mouth full of sea water. if they ever release a version that's similiar but without the salty note i'd instantly buy it. from a distance it's bearable i guess but still too salty. NOT a safe blind buy + testing on skin is a must.

the opening notes on this are delicious, fresh and slightly aquatic - mostly white flowers (i find it reminiscent of the lily pollen) and red berries. the fruits disappear after around an hour, leaving behind a deep, elegant florals with just a hint of sweetness. while it is a beautiful smell, i get really tired of it after couple of hours.

this surprised me by smelling absolutely incredible on skin (and clothes for that matter). it’s a very sweet, slightly salty floral with incredible sillage. my fiancé said i smell like gummy worms. unsurprisingly, this gave me a headache ETA: after taking a migraine abortive and letting the perfume (and myself) chill.....i've come back around to enjoying this quite a lot.

I was so curious for this. Lily and meringue with a touch of salt sounds gorgeous and quite original to me. I mean a sweet, summery floral that doesn't rely on the usual jasmine, tuberose or tropical, sunscreen-esque flowers? Count me in! But as we all know, high expansions can lead to disappointment.

I hated this one from the first spray. For me, the aquatic/marine notes are completely overpowering and not in a good way. This smells like if a floral shop opened up in an old fish market. It got even worse when applied to my skin. I had to wait to shower for a few hours, and it only got worse. It is very strong, and, to me, migraine inducing.

Allegedly, there is only one fragrance note here: daffodil. Narcissus Poeticus is, for me, a white floral composition with jasmine, orange blossom, and neroli. It could also contain some tuberose. Very soapy. Not as powdery and straightforward as Infusion D’Iris, my long-time signature scent. At first, I like the fragrance well, the nostalgic soapiness, melancholy, and tenderness, but in the drydown, it becomes too retro for me. The daffodil smells almost honey-like or even a bit "musk-like" here. After 10 minutes, everything revolves around soapy, clean, powdery white flowers - similar to the style of Santa Maria Novella. The drydown reminds me of Jo Malone's Tuberose and Angelica, although this one is more powdery and less sweet. Overall, it smells chic and elegant. It fits perfectly with a well-groomed, feminine, understated vibe. The scent is meant to evoke spring. The daffodil flower brings a honey-like scent, inspired by childhood memories of perfumer Philippine Courtière in the Jardin du Luxembourg. Floral-fresh, powdery, slightly sweet, and creamy - a fragrance that leans more towards a nostalgic, delicate direction. A moderate presence and longevity. Character: Pure, fresh, powdery, and floral with subtle elegance and lightness. Perfect for spring. Ideal for everyday wear. This is something a Trad Wife would wear; Nara Smith probably smells so innocent in front of the camera. Rather reserved. At first, I thought of mimosa. Mimosa is often used in powdery and romantic fragrances (e.g., with violet, rose, or iris). It is frequently found in soft, feminine compositions or in fresh spring perfumes like Prada Infusion de Mimosa, Hermès Jour d’Hermès, or Fragonard Mimosa. Style: Elegant, feminine, and yet with a nostalgic twist - "perfectly chic and classy." Fairy-like.

I had very high expectations for the fragrance and was really looking forward to it because of the daffodil. Unfortunately, I was bitterly disappointed. The perfume unfortunately does not remind me of spring and daffodils at all, but smells like cologne. For the price, you can get much better scents. The longevity of the fragrance is (in this case unfortunately) very good, it clings for a long time. A scent that my grandma might wear instead.

I loved it, despite the negative reviews, it's a great fragrance, the oud and saffron mix nicely, without being too heavy, it lasts a long time, it's unconventional but very pleasant. Looks a bit like kalan from PDM, not for a blind buy but weirdly nice and addictive, yet it is the worst of the three special editions. For me the best is "Oud", followed by "Aromatic", which has a great resemblance to Fleur de Male from JPG and Custo Man.

This is one of the best beginners ouds. Strong, manly yet rosey oud. Oud is a particularly strong wood note, that smells wet, and alike to a damp animal. This stuff is very well blended with synthetics to create a masterpiece oud. While there are ALOT of rose oud combos, this is very safe, as compared to something like Luna by ATH. If your scared or want a safer oud experience, this is nice!

Granted, I am not a big Boss fragrance fan and my second favourite probably is Boss Number one (the real vintage one) but Oud Saffron stands out to me! I love both the darkness, deepness of Oudh and the spicy components of Saffron. This has both and plenty of it. The slight sweetness to it might or might to be the indicated rose. Probably is, because it in itself has a certain spice or metallic feel to it. Maybe a rose oxide or something similar. To me, this is as close of a master piece as you might get from a house like Boss on designer perfume shelves. Only caveat is, I do not think you can wear this in summer. This is dark, heavy, full bodies and radiates warmth. One of the very perfumes of which I purchased a second bottle to keep for the future.

As a long-time admirer of the classic Boss Bottled DNA and a seasoned explorer of Oud fragrances, I finally took the plunge and blind-bought Hugo Boss Oud Saffron after a positive initial impression years ago. While it doesn't disappoint, those expecting the familiar Boss DNA will be surprised. This is a distinct and powerful Rose/Oud composition in its own right. Forget any rumored plastic opening; on my skin, it's an immediate and potent burst of Rose, quickly followed by a touch of saffron and then the undeniable richness of heavy Oud. The dry down is where this fragrance truly shines, evolving into a lovely and long-lasting scent. Projection is beastly, easily lasting over 12 hours on my skin. For a winter fragrance from Hugo Boss, I find it easily worth the money. However, a word of caution: unless you have a genuine love for prominent Rose and Oud notes, this is probably not a safe blind buy.

When I first read the notes of Boss Bottled Oud Saffron, I was immediately captivated. A combination of sweet, alluring rose, elegant saffron, and masculine oud. A simple yet convincing and beautiful combination. I was fully convinced and immediately sought out a whole bottle. A bit reckless, the blind purchase. I realized this in hindsight. From this mistake, I learned to always test a perfume beforehand. What did I get? I would describe this perfume as one for teenage girls. You get a very, very, very sweet and unfortunately also chemical rose scent. Saffron and oud, in my opinion, hardly play a part in the orchestra. To be fair, I must say: this fragrance has received a lot of positive feedback here. Perhaps my bottle was a Monday product or something is wrong with my sense of smell. I respect the voices of the lovers of this perfume, but unfortunately, it is not for me.

the scent somehow reminds me of my childhood vacations in Turkey. it gives me those vacation vibes. yet, it’s actually not a summer or vacation fragrance. saffron, rose, labdanum, and oud are the notes. I must admit that I wouldn’t have been able to identify a single one of these notes. to me, it smells primarily sweet, spicy, and somewhat leathery.

I was at the airport and had a little time to kill, so I immediately headed to the duty-free area to check out the perfumes. Once there, a red/transparent bottle caught my eye. The Hugo Boss Oud Saffron. Arrogantly, I thought to myself, oh really? What can a Boss Bottled fragrance do? However, the Oud/Saffron combo had already captivated me.

"Coumarin is a fragrant organic chemical compound in the benzopyrone chemical class, which is a colorless crystalline substance in its standard state. It is found naturally in many plants, notably in high concentration in the tonka bean, vanilla grass, sweet woodruff '(etc. etc ...)'.The name comes from a French word, coumarou, for the tonka bean. It has a sweet odor, readily recognised as the scent of new-mown hay, and has been used in perfumes since 1882." Paraphrased from Wikipedia. I've been wondering of late whether the immediate acquisition of Fleur du Mâle upon its launch in 2007 has caused my growing interest in cologne-like fragrances. Quite possibly so, because if anything, this fragrance with its high levels of Petitgrain, Neroli and Orange Blossom could very well be a long lasting EDC, were it not for the addition of Coumarin in its base. Fleur du Mâle is a sweet fragrance ... but not 'toothache inducing' sweet, more like walking through an orchard on a cloudy Spring day. A vanillic milkiness is quite evident here, exacerbated by a very fragrant Chamomile note drawing the mind in the direction of tea ... a steaming cup with a spoonful of demerera and a cloud of milk :) ... quite the desired effect of Coumarin! Without this note Fleur du Mâle would probably be just another 'orange flower water' ... its addition here is simply inspired! Even the promotional material for this fragrance, featuring an extremely handsome man submerged in a tub of cloudy water scattered with white rose petals alludes to this milkiness ... a modern day Mark Anthony at his bath? I personally find Fleur du Mâle to be a marvellous idea and I really enjoy wearing it too. Pushing the envelope by creating a floral fragrance directed at men is a great way to break down the social taboos of gender specific fragrances, imho. I've never been one for worrying about how a fragrance is marketed, I simply wear what I like. Wouldn't it be wonderful if one didn't have to choose? Fleur du Mâle has, in true Gaultier form, wonderful sillage and longevity. I get a good 8 to 10 hours from it with sincere compliments every time I wear it. I find that the more I sample the work of M. Kurkdjian, the more I conclude that he is a genuine genius of the modern industry. A fragrance such as this should not only be something that comes out of a bottle ... it should be a lifestyle.

Looking back, Francis Kurkdjian’s Jean Paul Gaultier Fleur du Male marks a time when Kurkdjian was pivoting his career from work for designer labels and the more rarified niche lines to his own line. Fleur du Male was released in 2007. 2009 saw the first perfumes from Maison Francis Kurkdjian. Designer, but with a twist, Fleur du Male Fleur du Male matches and surpasses the Gaultier brand which had beaten its enfant terrible schtick to death and by this time had become its own catch phrase. Kurkdjian breaths new life into a tired marque and gives Gaultier a perfume that speaks to his base while also attracting new buyers. Technically a flanker, Fleur was released 12 years after le Male, also by Kurkdjian for Gaultier. Matching the Gaultier sensibility, Fleur du Male is an effusive fragrance that speaks with waving hands and superlatives. Any lack of enthusiasm I have for the Gaultier’s brand in general, is sidelined by Fleur du Male. Daring and lovely, it’s a strong statement that breaths some beauty back into a dull mainstream masculine market. The fougère makes it masculine, the huge orange blossom note makes it fey, the locker room sensibility makes it gay. It feels boisterous and affable, typical of the fougere genre. The enormous floral flourish ties in with a sweaty, steamy locker room vibe. The result is a fragrance tailored to the gym queen sensibility of the 1990s and early millennium. It feels as if it was intended to target a middle-aged gay set who remember the 1990s nostalgically as a time when gyms were the new bars, steroids surpassed poppers and the cruising took place in the showers showers more than the dimly lit bars of the previous decades. The perfume bottle is recognizable from le Male and both are derived from the Schiaparelli Shocking bottle (1937 ). It is a sort of trophy, a nude Oscar, a robotically idealized male form in white. It's a nod to the clone look/life that fits hand-in-glove with gym queen-dom. It gives the impressions of some sort of fetish, in all senses of the word, at the same time that it looks like an insertable sex toy. Where it's easy to dismiss the cheap eroticism of the le Male bottle, the same shape has a new meaning in Fleur du Male. The white marble-like bottle, a young male nude in a standing pose, is a salute to the kouros. The perfume it contains, a musky, orange blossom fougère, is a nod to YSL Kouros, its predecessor. Nice touch. Fleur du Male hints at some of Francis Kurkdjian's later work for his own line where woody, spicy and floral notes were used to bend traditional forms to convey more contemporary tastes. The allure of recognizable classical perfumery draws the wearer closer and then comes the twist, the surprise. It's a smart, successful use of the 'change from within' strategy, a that trend continues in Kurkdjian's own line. from scenthurdle.com

Jean Paul Gaultier's Fleur de Male is aptly named, as this fragrance is quite flowery. But don't let the florals put you off guys, because this fragrance is quite sexy. The composition is mostly soft, milky and soapy floral accords, with a hint of rich, citrusy orange blossom and aromatic herbs. Yes, it does smell a little feminine at times, but I found it more unisex than anything else. I'm really enjoying it actually, when I thought that I wouldn't. I'm very finicky about men smelling like 'men', and although this fragrance is flowery, it gets my blood running in a way that I never expected. It's comforting yet seductive. Not a clubbing scent by any means, but one that helps put the wearer and his lady at ease. Although clean smelling, the herbaceous notes add a hint of masculinity, which makes it a little rough around the edges. I placed a tester card of this fragrance under my man's nose earlier, and his observations were that it smelt like soap and brown sugar. Some days I think he has a better nose than myself. I'll agree that Fleur du Male is a difficult scent to pull off, but for those men daring enough, I think it could smell very appealing. Well-dressed metrosexuals are more than likely going to be the perfect men to douse themselves in it and smell amazing at the same time.

I live in hot & sunny Florida and while I own, wear, and love many "heavy" scents, every now and then I just need something light and summery (but still rich enough for my tastes) and this is where Fleur Du Male comes in. A clean, powdery, floral with great longetivity and sillage. Is it kinda feminine and flowery? Well, I guess I can see how certain guys might have a problem wearing this, and that's OK for them. As for me, I'm secure enough to wear what I like, when I like. And I like Fleur Du Male very much.

This is lovely. What a wonderful combination of masculine and feminine. I was so afraid that I wasn't going to like this. I was expecting something heavy and smothering. When I sprayed it on, what I picked up right away was a bitter "green" blast with something powdery. The initial blast settles down fast and slips into something that is somewhat of a contradiction in terms - bold yet soft. The star of the show here really is the orange blossom and it's done so well, mixing with the other notes flawlessly. I am not a huge fan of the original, over-exposed, Le Male. Something about it irritates me and turns my stomach. You can smell a little of the original in here at its base but it's understated and kept at bay when mixed with the other notes. Not every man will like this. In fact, I don't think the average man will. You have to be in touch with your feminine side and be comfortable in your own skin to pull it off. I only needed one spray and that sufficed nicely. I believe that this scent is best suited for the cooler weather. I can't see wearing this in hot weather. I think the heat might make it a little aggressive and obnoxious. Different and unique as far as men's cologne goes. A modern throwback! Head and shoulders above the original. A classic in its own right. Highly recommended for the self-assured, confident man!

Up to now, the best "Le Male" flanker, has nothing to do with the mother fragrance, except for some reminiscences in the final drying, of Kurdjian-style musks, which are evidently inspired by the original, but nothing remarkable, could have been an independent perfume perfectly.

even if I feared it being too feminine with all the floral notes. Maybe I was also tempted by the fact that I'm pretty sure the name was meant to play with the outrageous title "Les Fleurs du Mal" released by Baudelaire in the 1850s. It was not quite how I imagined it but again, florals for men aren't that common these days.

Punchy, vibrant, and type of "hey I'm here" perfume! Opens with deeply overripe orange blossom. It is late spring, the blossoms are falling down and leave the smell dot of fruit behind. The ground is covered with mesmerizing white blossoms. Decay is set in. They are about to spoil and the smell is turning rotten and chemical.

Flowers. Sweet flowers. This should be called "Flowerbomb" instead of V&R's one. Deep and sweet, tends to be more feminine. Lasting power, sillage and projection are hazardously high. Thumbs up! Updated January 2014

daring masculine but totally feminine perfume. Only the most daring will enjoy this great work of the master francis kurdjian. bestial duration, bestial projection. I love it. perfume for winter and for women and men.

Autumn is here, winter is coming, and who even thinks about a typically summery fresh Neroli scent anymore? Maybe for 2021? Or the “always works” fragrance for notorious orange blossom lovers? There are thousands of them. Most, however, are not that great and can be had for cheap. More expensive versions really need to impress. BVLGARI has tried it, and Tom Ford long before that. YSL, Chanel, Prada, and others are happy to sell us €200 Neroli bottles from their exclusive lines. Is that really necessary? Personally, I know and have had what feels like 50 different yet often very similar Neroli fragrances. Ranging from €10 to €300. Those who know my reviews know that I always like to pit near doppelgängers against each other. Today: Néroli Oranger By Matière Première VS. Atelier des Fleurs - Neroli By Chloe. Result? Matière Première is clearly weaker in terms of sillage and longevity. Chloe lasts a solid 6 hours. Chloe feels more feminine, less green, and not as herbal. Honey yellow seems to be Néroli Oranger. Chloe is more orange with pink. It feels powdery, more elegant, and less “4711 Cologne” like. It would be more suited for women. Chloe simply has the edge in comparison, although I don’t find that “old-fashioned nostalgic” feeling in Néroli Oranger. It feels more modern, but also somewhat chemical. I only sense Ylang Ylang in a homeopathic way. I think I would go for the Chloe. Unfortunately, I already have a Neroli favorite from V&A. That one is and remains unmatched.... for now! Location of the duelists: Hamburg Alsterhaus and the new Douglas next door.

This one took me by surprise, literally! Based on the modern ad campaign and bottle design I expected a fruity fresh crowd-pleaser. But when I sampled this I was blown away at the almost vintage beauty this scent unfolds on my skin! It's definitely in the league of Fragile and/or Sensi. On me, the rose, jasmine and something sweet but not cloying (black currant?) is making this a beautiful and elegant perfume with a velveteen-smooth amber base that only enhances it. The bottle is misleading, this darling is elegant with a vintage vibe and should be in an elegant and feminine looking flacon, not in a modern sporty bottle. But the bigger your surprise when you test it! Silage is: "wonderful whiffs of slightly sweet flowers and sensual yum" -- Longevity is: an amazing 8+ hours in which it dries down to a warmer version of the fresh opening and the rich smelling middle stage. YUM!

Predictable, pleasant but boring, Hugo XX won't be getting any rave reviews from me. This fragrance is so light that it takes a lot of sniffing and inhaling to even be able to describe what it smells like. Hugo XX has quite a simple opening with blackcurrant being its most dominant note. It's fruity yet it lacks that fruity punch which would've given this scent more character. The heart is just as bland and boring as its opening, with the jasmine and rose creating a scent which has been done and re-done many times before. The floral combination is soft and pretty, yet it has that all-to-familiar soapy quality which I really dislike. I never got to the drydown because this fragrance disappeared in only 30 minutes. It's possibly the worst lasting scent I've come across so far. I don't recommend this fragrance unless you like to be ordinary.

My dear colleague recently came around the corner with a box. You like perfume, right? I have a few bottles here that I bought over time and some of them I never used. Take a look! Otherwise, I will throw everything away! So I did, and took the box home. There was quite a variety inside. Among other things, there were perfumes that had turned and were in not-so-nice colors in the bottle, that just by a quick sniff at the spray head almost made me lose my hearing and sight. I bravely tested some, but the maggot note lingered stubbornly. Sorted out. And there was also a half-full bottle from Boss with XX. Doesn't ring a bell for me. Boss XX EdP starts off really nicely summery fruity and puts me in a good mood! A lovely mandarin and lychee, I wouldn't have picked out the blackcurrant so easily. Unfortunately, the top note doesn't last as long as I would like, because I find the fruits to be zesty and summery, but by no means too intrusive. Once the scent settles, a mild rose and such an incredibly beautiful creamy note come to the surface, a little dream. Although I am always a bit cautious with jasmine, everything blends wonderfully together, nothing is intrusive or too much. I perceive this subtly fruity-floral scent for several hours, even though the fragrance settles relatively quickly and doesn't have a very strong sillage. But that doesn't matter at all. Especially when it's warmer outside, you can wear the scent without being over-perfumed. In the soft, purring base, a rather sweet amber and a restrained musk dominate, yet the fine rose and the creaminess remain subtly in the background. Very fine! Throw away?? Seriously?! This one stays with me, I really enjoy wearing it. I removed the layer of dust and uncovered a little treasure. A sensual feminine aura surrounds the scent, I believe it is no longer produced as EdP. Which is really a shame, because it always hits the mark, I am already looking forward to wearing it in the fall. Then I will have a very nice summer memory of a bottle that I saved from the trash can! My daughter has snatched up two other rather sweet scents, and I found another Burberry that we fought over. I won, she already has the girly scents :-)

~ Inspiration ~ I think the Hugo Boss fragrances are great. You can wear them anytime and anywhere. As soon as a new scent is released, I want to try it out. ~ Bottle ~ Simple yet present. The nude tones match very well with the gentle fragrance. The gold accents add a touch of elegance. ~ Scent ~ Feminine, delicate, and loving. A subtle, understated fragrance that has a positive effect on me. The floral nuances are perfectly rounded off with very restrained fruity and slightly spicy notes. ~ Longevity ~ On my skin, it lasts well, about 8 hours (longer on clothing/hair). A few small sprays are already sufficient. ~ Occasion ~ With this perfume, you can never go wrong, anytime and anywhere. Not intrusive, subtle, yet still perceptible around you. Suitable for every season, any time of day, and for all ages. Not for women looking for a bold and strong perfume. ~ Conclusion ~ I am thrilled with the scent! It completes a well-groomed appearance and leaves a good impression on others. You can't go wrong with this perfume.

I bought XX because of the irresistible blue eyes of Jonathan Rhys-Meyers, who stepped into the boxing ring with a female model in the commercial for this fragrance. This rather dance-like fight was probably meant to symbolize the battle of the sexes. It certainly caught my attention. However, XX is in no way aggressive, but very soft and feminine. Lychee and mandarin provide a very fruity, fresh entrance, and jasmine and rose are mildly sweet. A charming blend. With amber, musk, and sandalwood, a touch of sex appeal is added. But very subtle. This fragrance is really more about a promotional dance than a fight. Armed like this, I would have loved to step into the ring with blue-eyed Johnny.

Hugo Boss has been with me for almost 5 years. He was already there when I hadn't yet developed my interest in perfumes. He is my go-to. When I don't know what to wear, I reach for XX. On my skin, he develops lightly, fresh, and creamy. I feel like I've just stepped out of the shower with him. He is not at all intrusive.

I was at Müller today and this perfume caught my eye. I bought it immediately. Once I got home, I had to try it out right away. The scent is simply fantastic. The perfume smells incredibly good and I fell in love with this fragrance today. I will wear it to work on Monday. I'm curious to see what my colleagues will say.

The scent was a gift from my husband; I had never immersed my nose in any Boss fragrance before. Upon spraying, the orange note hits my nose first, and it lingers for quite a while before the warmer components come in, with the sandalwood eventually dominating and becoming somewhat unpleasant if over-applied, while the fruity notes maintain a very subtle undertone.

Hugo XX is a truly sensual and graceful fragrance that awakens the senses. It is a modern, pleasantly elegant companion. Two sprays are enough for the whole day; this scent lasts a long time. Even in the evening, you can still catch a whiff of it, even though it is an Eau de Toilette. This fragrance can really be worn for any occasion.
It is a provocatively sensual perfume. Basmati rice and Sambac jasmine come together to create a floral, intoxicating, soft heart note that exudes a seductive power that is hard for a man to resist.

Gorgeous citruses and blood orange sweetness combined perfectly with neroli and orange blossom, complimenting each other in great harmony without stealing the spotlight. A base of musk and wood adds the perfect support to this bright ensemble. The bottle design with its little crop top is adorable, charming the open-minded and sparking reactions from those still not quite ready for the 21st century.

it has nothing of the classic le male, or for the female version le classique, and perhaps for this reason its rating is so low... the truth is that it is a masterpiece, citrusy, persistent, wonderfully fresh, sparkling and floral, and finally, at a ridiculous price, I managed to get it. for all citric lovers a must have.

I was initially conflicted about this scent. Another flanker, I thought. But I also thought: Actually, JPG makes pretty good flankers. Consider Ultra Male or Superman. Still, I approached this fragrance with great skepticism. When I finally smelled it: Awesome. That was my first thought. It smells fresh, fruity, and the blood orange is very prominent right from the opening. It smells similar to Mandarino di Amalfi by Tom Ford. However, with a blood orange in the fruit basket. Otherwise, like with MdA, it has pure sunscreen and vacation vibes. You can run straight to the beach with this. And yes, it does have a bit of a reminder of "On the beach" - however, "On the beach" has more of a "fresh laundry feeling" going on. I would rate the sillage and longevity a 7/10. I get through the workday well with it. For such a bright and fresh designer fragrance, that's a really good performance. In general, the scent is also in the unisex sweet spot. It can really be worn by anyone. My conclusion: Anyone looking for a summer fragrance for 2022 and/or perhaps annoyed by the price or longevity of Mandarino di Amalfi will find a really good alternative here. You get a strong, summery, and cheerful scent for quite little money. I'm curious to see when the hype for this will start. You can find more in my video about it.

Hello everyone, yes, we are TALKING again for what feels like the hundredth time about a flanker from the legendary Le Male line. I’ll be honest! When we TALK about a new or expanded fragrance direction from Le Male, unfortunately, there have been very, very few that stood out. Exceptions for truly good ones were: - Superman + Popeye - Ultra Male - Le Male Le Parfum - and ... Aside from Le Parfum, nothing really new has come out, and I have always found that very unfortunate. The new Pride... is something I have been waiting for a very, very long time and I am really excited about it, because on one hand it is NEW (not a classic Le Male) and finally the first one that can be worn 100% in the high summer + summer. I LOVE Popeye + Superman and both definitely have that light and fresh TOUCH, but still carry the slight spiciness and sweetness of the Le Male DNA within them, which makes it a bit challenging after 2 to 4 hours (with the transition from top to base note). That’s why those (JUST FOR ME fragrances are good up to 23°C). With the new Pride, it’s different; a mix of bitter citrus notes with neroli makes it generally bitter - citrusy - light and refreshing, and after 4 hours it basically turns into a "clean man scent" with light woods + musk. A Le Male that is really great for the warmer days of the year, I’m glad I get to experience this ;). Seriously, respect JPG. An absolute insider tip from me and in my opinion, this release is one of the best we have seen in 2022.. Best regards

It is mid-May 2023, and for many weeks now, one cloud after another has been drifting across the sky, almost every day brings rain, and the temperatures remain clearly below 20 degrees. It is still time for the heavier scents, the long rainy season allows for good preparation for the warmer days. And so, we allowed ourselves the fun of blind testing summer fragrances in the family. Louis Vuitton Imagination, Le Mâle Pride Edition 2022, Roja Elysium Cologne, and Parfum. And behold, the clear winner in the fragrance competition during the rainy month of April was... Le Mâle. This scent is truly great; it opens up with an incredibly zesty note of fresh blood orange that you can effectively pinpoint. At this point, you don't suspect much of the classic Le Mâle, but over time, that changes, and the citrusy freshness gives way to the Mâle fingerprint of a slightly sweet, yet still fresh and captivating musk note. I find the longevity and sillage for a fresh fragrance to be quite good; Le Mâle Pride Edition 2022 easily wins against the Roja and Louis Vuitton fragrances, which evaporate much faster and project less. And all this at an unbeatable price. All in all, a fantastic fragrance, and for those who are bothered by the cardigan: it can be removed, leaving a classic, purist Le Mâle flanker.

I had this Pride edition on my radar for a long time, especially due to the fantastic feedback on Parfumo and its similarity to significantly more expensive fragrance twins. From a marketing perspective, it probably wasn't the best move to launch a Pride flanker with a rainbow. Many heteros will not even test this unless they happen to be on Parfumo reading these reactions.

This fragrance opens with a pleasant Mediterranean citrus note that brings a gentle fruitiness. As it develops, the floral components of orange blossom and neroli become more prominent. The initial citrus freshness diminishes, and the scent transforms into a predominantly floral composition.
...that’s exactly the question I asked myself after seeing how many people noted the similarity to On the Beach by Louis Vuitton. During a sale, I decided to grab 125ml of JPG for about €74.

The Le Male Pride Edition is an absolutely brilliant fragrance for summer. This scent fits perfectly with the sun, beach, and sea. It starts off with a beautiful blood orange note, which is really prominent. Additionally, there is a wonderful, finely tuned neroli note. The orange blossom adds a very subtle floral touch. Simply genius!

A citrusy JPG scent with Pride marketing - shut up & take my money! It starts with a bitter blood orange. Citrus lovers will get their money's worth here. This bitterness quickly fades and develops into a pleasant rainbow of flowers, citrus fruits, neroli, musk, and light woods.

This perfume is very feminine. The aroma is floral, even slightly intoxicating. Then the flowers give way to a soapy aroma. In such a palette of pleasant flower aromas, I personally find it difficult to separate them into individual components. Although jasmine still comes to the fore here. After such a beginning and middle, I was very interested in what would happen at the end. The flowers have begun to bloom sweet pine nuts and sandalwood. This scent for me is a vintage classic of women's perfumery.

My now sadly empty 7.5 ml bottle of the perfume "Chloé" is inhabited by many golden glitter particles. These were very generously included during the final phase of the program "Magic of Butterflies" at the Dream Theater Salomé! It's been a long time, but they are well preserved there and always remind me of beautiful and entertaining hours. Like with the "KL," the smaller bottle here is much more charming, as it is better proportioned than the "bigger brother" with the 15 ml filling. As an Eau de Toilette lover, it was inevitable that I had to own the perfume as well. There were probably only a few women who didn't fall in love with this extraordinary bottle. And so, I also received "Chloé" as a perfume one Christmas a year ago. The two of us - the perfume and I - were shining in competition! In terms of radiance, this surpasses the Eau de Toilette by far. It may be hard to imagine, but it's true! In a well-balanced fragrance fullness, bright aldehydes and a bouquet of white summer flowers greet you: fragrant lilac, large-headed hyacinth, climbing honeysuckle, the slightly waxy orange blossom, and the bergamot that always slightly dampens the scent. They skillfully unite with the inherent sweetness of coconut. Additionally, there is the fully ripe peach and the sparkle of the always beautiful ylang-ylang. Here, everything shines a little deeper and more golden than in the Eau de Toilette. Musk generously envelops a balanced and precisely dosed blend of amber, benzoin, and sandalwood in the perfume. Oak moss adds depth, and cedar provides additional full spice! Thus, a perfume is created, as thoughtfully and artistically composed as a grand symphony of scents! Against this backdrop, it is unnecessary to think about sillage and longevity: both are simply incredibly rich. Touching up was done purely out of joy for the scent, never out of pure necessity. With this fragrance, Karl Lagerfeld made an extraordinary gift to the house of Chloé. The name, which will always be associated with him, to which he successfully laid the foundation, continues to be used. Whether successfully, I do not wish to comment on here. For me, at least, "Chloé," in whatever concentration, has been an important and very personal fragrance milestone and will likely always remain so.

This is literally a wrist sniffer. IE, you can't smell it unless you sniff your wrist. Tired of not being able to smell it on me, on the weekend I soused myself in 20 sprays. 5 minutes later, another 20 sprays. Still no trail. It's only to be smelled if I sniff my wrists. That isn't what I wanted. For such a faint scent, it does manage to last 4 hours but what's the point you can't smell it unless you sniff it. As to the cyclamen reference, intrigued, I went and smelled my intensely flowering, hot pink, cyclamen, and it does have a warm, softly spicy, and a fine but definite petroleum scent - like a water lily or orchid - this petroleum scent is in my cyclamen flowers pretty strong in the morning unlike the perfume which is not strong any time. The perfume is warm, nutty, a hint of gingerbread biscuits. I am a lover of marzipan, and I could not smell marzipan. Sometimes there is an out of place soapy, lemon waft. Then a soft suede scent intermingles with a warm, fuzzy/heathery/woolly scent. The dry down smells like a handful of pot pouri thrown on a slow combustion oven in the tack room or the engine room/machinery shed where the old saddles are kept. A warmed up undifferentiated pot pouri, leather and soap smell. I bought this blind, hoping for a violet and/or marzipan scent. It wasn't there.

Pure Purple is more of a gourmand to my nose, not so much a fruity floral in my humble opinion. This fragrance is indeed delicate and sweet, but not in a sickening way. When first applied, Pure Purple smells like gingerbread cookies. There are hints of sugar, ginger, spices and almond. Just sniffing it was making me hungry. In the heart, the scent continues with its sweetness. Candied violets and white cyclamen with an overload of sugar. Nectarine makes a brief appearance right before the drydown, rather than in the top notes, however the leather overshadows the fruitiness of the scent. The leather in Pure Purple is not like the leather in let's say Bandit by Robert Piguet. This is leather that can appeal to a younger audience; synthetic and subtle. The lasting strength is really good and the sillage not very strong but not subtle either. I find Pure Purple to be a little different, not exactly what you'd expect from a mainstream brand. Purple doesn't seem to be the right colour for this scent. I'm thinking a reddish brown or even black would compliment this fragrance better.

The deciding factor for reaching for the bottle about eight years ago was its similarity to Hypnôse by Lancôme. My signature scent back then. I was curious and perhaps a bit annoyed. Why such a blatant copy? But never mind. Now it’s part of my collection and I’m very happy about it. Another scent that has never left me cold and unfortunately isn’t so easy to find anymore. A heartfelt thank you to Ronja for the nice souk deal. While the also twisted bottle of Hypnôse is simply very elegant to look at and has a beautiful emblem on the cap, Deep Purple feels urban and chic. The edges are slightly rounded and it features a color gradient from crystal clear to dark purple. I like the color and design. It also fits well with the contents. At first, it starts off a bit rough. I perceive marzipan just like my predecessors from the very beginning. At first, it reminds me more of amaretto, but don’t worry. As a schnapps enthusiast, you won’t be labeled as such when wearing it. This impression, as interesting and strange as it may be, doesn’t last too long and makes way for a very authentic marzipan scent. Spontaneous salivation, how delicious is that? It smells just like opening a bag of marzipan potatoes. Sweet, incredibly fine, perhaps a bit too foody, but who cares. Because shortly after, a powdery violet enriches our dessert. A really pleasant combination. The marzipan takes a bit of a back seat and gives the floral notes more room to breathe. A clean and sometimes slightly piercing note floats subtly along. I suspect it’s the alpine violet, which sometimes appears a bit too clean for my taste. The scent is still sweet. However, the marzipan has lost its firm consistency and gives the fragrance a certain smoothness. Still, it remains biteable. I can’t describe it as particularly fruity. The nectarine hardly stands a chance against the gourmand notes. A sparse fruity and indefinable nuance can be detected, which fortunately doesn’t negatively affect the progression. In fact, the long-awaited suede also makes an appearance. Butter-soft and cream-colored. Very feminine and smooth. It’s a pity; I prefer my leather a bit rough and grippy. Similar to Cuir Cordoba. Perhaps those latter attributes would be out of place. This leather here wraps itself advantageously around the marzipan. It supports the lovely and powdery violet. Creates an elegant stage for the shy amber. There aren’t any major changes from now on. From amaretto to fine marzipan, garnished with a violet that may seem a bit naive at first but finds an interesting partner in the leather. For the sillage to be satisfactory for me, I have to apply a bit more. It will never be room-filling, but that’s a good thing. Marzipan overkill in the office sounds quite uncomfortable. I find the longevity to be good. It easily withstands a long workday. For the evening, however, one should spray a bit more. Except for high summer or for sports, Pure Purple can be used in many ways. Especially now, during the cold autumn storms, it provides warmth and security. Still, it radiates something cheerful and light. It may be that it’s a bit too girly and sometimes too squeaky and edible for me. But I don’t care. When I feel like this calorie-free and terribly delicious marzipan grenade, I just reach for it. Perhaps not the best choice for moments of dark cravings. But it has to adapt to me. I simply give it a purple ribbon. Anyone who doesn’t want to gain a few pounds during the pre-Christmas season and compete with the Christmas goose for the rising weight should give this scent a try. A treat for sweet tooths and it definitely satisfies the craving for marzipan potatoes.

Today I had a dentist appointment. Such dreadful activities strain my nerves, and I need a calming scent to waft into my nose in this inhospitable place. I rummaged through my collection and reached for Pure Purple. Yes! The delicate scent of marzipan immediately soothed me - accompanied by juicy nectarine and a serene violet. On top of that, a fine leather scent lays itself. My purple cloud, in which I was enveloped, prepared me well against the biting clinical smell. In my ears, Prince intoned emotionally and slowly: Purple Rain. What can I say - the treatment was bearable. I was well prepared, after all. Even my doc seemed in a good mood. Somehow, Pure Purple is a harmless sedative.

Also for me: Love at the second sniff! At first, I could only smell the alcohol somehow, but just a few seconds later: "Oh my goodness, this is delicious!" Yes, sure, the scent is floral. But I simply cannot explain or (and do not want to) understand that there is supposed to be marzipan in the base. It is so incredibly present. You smell the fragrance for the first time and the gentle, by no means exaggerated, marzipan scent comes right at you. I haven't smelled something like this in a long time. I am really excited. I don't like to eat marzipan at all. But I obviously love to smell it. The fragrance is not intrusive at all. Not particularly sweet. Not particularly floral. I wouldn't have expected this from Hugo, but somehow everything fits for me here. The blend makes the scent so special. My goodness, this is quite possibly the most beautiful thing I have tested in a long time. Hearts are swirling above my head... that smell like marzipan. People, if you like this kind of thing, then you MUST try it, promise me that! Unfortunately, I can't say anything about the longevity at the moment, so I will leave this review out.

Well, I must say, I like quite a bit from Mr. Boss. You can all say what you want. Pure Purple I also like *stamp*. However, I could swear that the marzipan does not belong in the base (I completely agree with you, Wölfin!), or not just there. I smell it right in the top note, right at the beginning. Really delicious.

~ Inspiration ~ "BOSS Purple" doesn't really fit my usual preferences due to the leather accord - but I was intrigued by the marzipan when I swapped samples of Violethaze. ~ Bottle ~ The design reminds me of "Hypnose" by Lancôme, just a bit clumsier. true to its name, there is a (violet) lilac liquid in the twisted bottle.

I received this perfume for my birthday last year. Even though I have many others (my boyfriend already thinks I'm crazy), the bottle is almost empty. I think that says a lot. For my taste, simply delicious; I smell marzipan, marzipan, and more marzipan.

sweet, marzipan-like but subtle. I enjoy sniffing it. I also don’t find it heavy, so I definitely wear it in the summer. I don’t smell leather as such, at least not as pungent as I imagine leather to be. could last a bit longer.

About a year ago, I had to buy a sweet fragrance for someone very special... the "nice" design of the bottle caught my attention back then! After a short test, I knew this was it! The presentation delivered what it promised! The gift was well received! ;-)

Scandal pour Homme and Scandal pour Homme Le Parfum were, in my opinion, quite unimpressive. Their reliance on that synthetic-sweet structure was simply a turn off for me. Hence, I don't have big expectations for Scandal pour Homme Absolu . However, this is the best on in the line, in my opinion... but, as always, there's a 'but'... And that's because the opening of Scandal pour Homme Absolu , the absolute best part of the whole fragrance, is short-lived. Immediately after I spray the fragrance, I am met with a pretty delicious and creamy chestnut, along with a small dose of synthetic and slightly harsh citruses. The caramel note sweetens things up further along with the tonka bean, and the signature Scandal clary sage starts pushing through just minutes after spraying, which I'm not the biggest fan of, but it does seem better integrated than on the OG Scandal pour Homme . As for the Mirabelle plum note, I got little of it in the opening, with a mild fruity-floral accord hiding through the creamy sweetness. But then, it's all gone. As things settle down rapidly, the woody accords of sandalwood and cedar push through, along with the tiniest bit of vetiver, which make the fragrance instantly reminiscent of its siblings, Scandal pour Homme and Scandal pour Homme Le Parfum . Then I also meet the now-iconic synthetic undertone of the line, which was always there; it was jut a little better masked on the opening here. There's also some of that chestnut/caramel sweetness from the opening still present, but it's more tonka bean after some minutes. But... here comes my main issue. That initial beautiful blast of chestnut, arguably one of the nicest openings of a fragrance I've smelt so far on designer territory, fades away in less than two minutes, at least on my skin. And from there on, it just gets fainter and fainter, in the end leaving me with about 70-80% clary sage and sandalwood, and 30-20% of some smooth sweetness of tonka bean with some chestnuts sprinkled on top. If that chestnut lasted loner... But hey, at least that tonka/caramel sweetness does a better job at hiding that synthetic DNS than Scandal pour Homme . I did have relatively high hopes for the longevity of Scandal pour Homme Absolu , seeing how its other siblings did quite well in this respect.
