And while it's far from terrible, it's just borderline decent. I get about 6, maybe 7 hours of longevity on my skin. I can live with that. But what I don't accept is such a soft projection. For the first hour or so, I got 1 feet at best of silage, after which it would settle down just as quickly as the chestnut accord did. Fair, I'm also to blame for my bad skin chemistry; many fragrances don't perform that well on my skin. But Scandal pour Homme Le Parfum , for example, actually held on for quite a long time, and so I just hoped that Scandal pour Homme Absolu would also last that long, given they both share the same DNA at the base. But nope, not on me. So personally, I'd go with 6-8 sprays. For occasions, I'd say that Scandal pour Homme Absolu works for leisure wear, family gatherings, or for winter parties/clubbing. If the fragrance performs any better on your skin than on mine, I believe that it could get plenty of attention (if that's what you're after). Searching for the Scandal king, I have finally found it, but it does not wear the crown anymore. Scandal pour Homme Absolu has one of the most delicious openings of a designer fragrance that I have ever smelled. Caramel, tonka bean, some citruses, and a hyper-realistic chestnut, all aided by the classic Scandal clary sage, vetiver and sandalwood combination, which I'm honestly not a fan of. Lamentably, disappointment is still what I find. The chestnut rapidly fades after the first few minutes, becoming a memory somewhere in the background, leaving you with largely just a sweeter/creamier and less synthetic interpretation of the OG. And the projection of the fragrance, at least on me, is disappointing and quite soft after about an hour. All of these cons just do not justify buying a full bottle. In the end, the throne still awaits for its scandalous king, and the crown keeps collecting dust on a pedestal in an empty hall. But there might be another entrant, another contestant for the throne... Might Scandal pour Homme Intense be the much-awaited king? Overall Rating: 5.7/10

Scandal Absolu is likely my favorite JPG fragrance overall. It’s a beautifully crafted scent, blending a rich, warm, and sweet smoky chestnut with hints of caramel. The performance is outstanding, lasting about 11-12 hours on my skin, with strong projection for the first 6 hours. You seriously can't go wrong with this. Insanely good for this cold winter weather.

I've had this one for a couple of months now, to me it smells like a very potent but nutty crème brûlée. When I first smelt it I new I had to get it, I've gotten several compliments for this, from young and old people. If you enjoy a long lasting vanilla and hazelnut-y scent, I suggest you look into this one. It's definitely a masculine scent, but I wouldn't mind it on a woman either. Scent: 8.0/10 Longevity: 7.6/10 Sillage: 7.2/10 (3 sprays) Bottle: 9.1/10 Value: 6.7/10

Scandal Absolu is the third in the scandal pour homme line, and I can easily say that it is a good fragrance. The fragrance opens with Mirabelle that screams “I wanna be a boss fragrance!” which is REALLY unnecessary since mirabelle has NOTHING to do with the scandal line, but it smells good too. Exotic, even aphrodisiatic, later the fragrance turns to Armani stronger with you edt thanks to the chestnut and later sandalwood shines and smells exactly like OG scandal (notes listed here is wrong, mirabelle, chestnut and sandalwood are the only notes listed by Gaultier) Good for winter and Autumn, has a very strong performance; people were still able to smell me after a 10 hours long flight (yes I tested in duty free). So overpriced, I would pay 70 euro max for 100ml. This is the least characteristic scandal in the line for me, both scandal Le Parfum and OG scandal is more characteristic and better fragrances in my opinion. Still, I would have liked this more if it was the first scandal that I have smelled. Would recommend to test in a store or buy a sample before a purchase, since it is really unnecessary if you have scandal edt, le parfum or stronger with you edt.

Emporio Armani - Stronger With You Parfum but much more sweeter. It doesn’t smells like Christmas like Emporio Armani - Stronger With You Parfum , but in the same time doesn’t give anything more than SWY Parfum. I can’t say is bad , because actually smells good , but if i was you i would buy Emporio Armani - Stronger With You Parfum

I fell in love with it the first time I ever tried it. I hate caramel in fragrances for some reason but something with this one makes it just right. I feel like luxurious wearing it, it's a very gourmand and overwhelming fragrance but a little less sweet then the standard one (better for winter).

The third JPG release this quarter; I'm going to be broke :D Scandal pour Homme and Scandal pour Homme Le Parfum are both in my closet, so of course I had to get the new one as well. I prefer the OG of the first two, as it is simply a bit fresher, more on point. The development in Le Parfum didn’t add much value for me.

Scandal! Another new fragrance from Jean Paul Gaultier. Is this already the third release in 2024??? The flankers keep coming, and this time "Scandal" gets its new cash cow. "Scandal pour Homme Absolu" is hitting the market! "Le Parfum" is not even two years old yet, and "Scandal Absolu" wants to take the throne. At least: it is the best in the series!

...a beekeeper suit. In front of me, the bees are buzzing. From the beehive comes the scent of honey and wax. Accompanying this is the fragrance of fresh lemons, a bit of wood, and chestnuts. The bees are relaxed, and so am I. Upon application, an incredible sweetness of honey greets you. Very faintly in the background, there is a freshness and fruitiness.

I already have the Scandal EDT, today I sprayed the Pour Homme Absolu for comparison. I find the Pour Homme Absolu to be a bit more mature compared to the EDT, as the fragrance components are a little better harmonized. Here, honey stands out nicely, which makes the sweetness appear more rounded compared to the EDT.

The best of the "Boss the scent for her”. warm, sexy and creamy. You have to be in the mood for it but it is interesting with the akigalawood vetiver blend. So grounding, calming and creamy. love love love I'm glad 'Le Parfum For Her' stays with me from sunrise to sunset. Lasting power is extremly good. so happy to own this masterpice bottle.

For years, I searched through the niche world, because designer fragrances just don't come into the house anymore, for whatever reason I thought that?! And where have I ended up? At least lately. With this one right here. My current everyday companion. Sugared pepper and some flower, I don't care! It has captured me! I will continue to search for my signature scent, and until then, this bottle will definitely be empty or will be repurchased, who knows!

Powdery, sweet, delicate. Got a sample of this one last summer in Paris. I like it better this year than when I received it. A nice, subtle everyday fragrance. But unfortunately doesnt project or last much. If I was to buy the full bottle it would soon be empty because of all the touch ups needed.

This blind buy gift from my husband immediately reminded me of Hypnotic Poison, but not—It’s smoother, with no playdoh note, and it’s less heavy. It’s more of a vibe that tickles my brain in a similar way. I love them both. I like to rotate my fragrances, but I find Scandal LP easily fits most occasions, so I find myself choosing it several times a week. Today, it’s my shlump-around-in-sweats scent, and I keep smelling my arm. My husband calls it “the sexy one,” so it’s perfect for date night or cuddles, too!

Scandal Le Parfum by Jean Paul Gaultier is the latest flanker (2022) of the well known Scandal line. This perfume is sweet and floral in the opening, with a caramel heart and a delicate salt that is barely there, probably coming together some sparkling touches. If you are interested into hearing more details about this perfume, please watch my review on Youtube.

I'm not the biggest fan of Scandal, but I still tried all the flankers. This one is my favorite so far, along with Scandal a Paris. While that one was a light, fresher version, Le Parfum is as rich, sweet and opulent as the original, but in a different way. There is a touch of the honey-infused Scandal DNA in this, but the sweetness here is less sticky and the honey gets tamed by the other notes. It feels very smooth and quite floral. I don't just smell jasmine and lots of tuberose. The caramel in this is very creamy without any burned aspects and only a little touch of salt. Vanilla rounds it all out. A lot of people compare this to Hypnotic Poison, but I don't really get it. The vanilla might be similar, but HP has so much almond, a rubbery note and even some spices, all which Scandal LP doesn't have. Instead it's much more floral and a bit honeyed. Weirdly I get a hint of Black Opium in the opening (without the coffee), but that vanishes away in the drydown. At first I wasn't too impressed by this, I thought it was just another unremarkable sweet designer floral on a vanilla base. A weak like, nothing more. But it really grew on me while testing. If I had a smaller collection, I'd buy it. I think it's the subtle salted caramel and the super smooth blending! Also, this is the type of perfume that gets better the longer its on.

This reminds me a bit of marzipan with vanilla, yum! I do sort of get those “vanilla play-doh” vibes with this, but it’s not bad - just makes it feel very cozy and comforting. Yes, it IS a sweet fragrance, but it’s not sickly or cloying in my opinion. Wearing it in the right weather (i.e. cold!) definitely helps it perform at its best. Some of the florals come out in the drydown on my skin as well and give it more dimension, it’s definitely not a simplistic “one note” fragrance. Is it sexy? Yes, I’d say it definitely has flirty vibes. In my opinion, you could also get away with it during the day, but only in the fall and winter. This will be a strictly seasonal scent for me.

This perfume is the descendant of several other Scandal perfumes. Scandal by night, scandal, so scandal, so scandal intense, however, this perfume has drawn me to its side. You are not immediately overwhelmed when you spray it; it is more of a gentle awakening.

Tuberose makes the start, lovely and sweet. Honey gives it that powdery shiny note, which wonderfully merges with sinful tonka bean and a beautifully soft vanilla. Salted caramel adds a bittersweet note to the fragrance, for which I can only find one word: luscious.

I’m sure I’ll make some enemies now, but I find it quite surprising that the scent seems to be received rather well. :D Yesterday, I quickly sprayed it on my wrist out of curiosity. Since the year 2000 (I’m getting old...) I have been using and loving Hypnotic Poison EDT by Dior.

This is not a fairground scent and not a simple children's fragrance - it is an ode to salted caramel. To salt, to the sea, to sweet caramel, and in the base note, gentle sandalwood that only shines through over time. Combined with amber, the perfume smells soft, warm, and creamy, without being too sweet, thanks to the salt note.

Scandal fragrances are variations of jasmine - and Scandal Le Parfum is particularly soft and has no patchouli in it (or almost none). While the very dominant green scent dominated the first three Scandals and reminded one of the '68 era, this perfume is reserved and woody-sweet, vanilla-like, but not boring: because it also smells distinctly salty!

Of course, this is a so-called designer fragrance, and I usually don't like them. But this one was surprisingly good. Perhaps a stroke of luck among the many different yet so similar Boss perfumes. I can't quite relate to the listed fragrance notes. For me, it revolves around synthetic musk, but maybe I'm mistaken about that as well. As a perfume for everyday use, it is definitely recommendable.

White is the new black. This is not just a statement, it is a fact. Smartphones, cars, furniture, clothes, everything, even milk sells better when it is white. Who should recognize this trend better than a big fashion label? Why not wrap the crowd favorite 'In Motion' in a white garment? I really like this silky matte, soft white with the orange belly band and small orange belly button. It also feels good in the hand. However, like many white items of daily use, the signs of wear are unfortunately hard to overlook; greasy fingerprints become immediately apparent. Therefore, the testers in perfumeries often look quite dirty, which is not a real invitation to want to test the fragrance here. Fortunately, the scent is just as I imagine it. A not too offensive variation of the original, the original character is not betrayed. Still, there are enough different accents to make you want to have this fragrance if you like it. There is a bitter, not too sweet blood orange that subtly supports the basil with spicy-green notes. Pepper and cinnamon create aromatic peaks time and again. Vetiver provides the necessary earthy-woody anchoring. All of this is solid craftsmanship, but one searches in vain for surprises or even revelations. One also searches in vain for the fragrance after a mere four to five hours, as it has then disappeared. The sillage is quite decent until halfway, although fortunately not intrusive. However, the longevity is disappointing; the too narrow base cannot hold on after the blood orange has evaporated and dies a quick death. With the bottle, you are fully on trend - if only a bit more attention had been paid to the scent and its longevity. But as a sport fragrance, it’s okay.

So here's a comment from a lady:) I gifted this fragrance to my boyfriend! I bought it blind because I liked the regular motion and the white one looked even more beautiful and was on sale. I am very happy with this purchase! I love the scent so much! To me, it doesn't smell really sweet. Maybe a bit sweetish! An everyday fragrance. It's so cozy and warm! It smells different from the regular motion. Somehow cleaner and creamier... just white! It has something unique! I recognize this scent immediately! And I can't get enough of it! Simply a wow fragrance for me! To me, it smells warm, as if there is musk and some tobacco in it, but it's not listed in the fragrance pyramid.

The perfume smells sweet and is more suitable for younger men (17-22 years). It fits well in spaces where people are close together (like a disco, for example). Due to its sweet scent, it is not as overpowering as heavy fragrances. In short: Top note: Lasts about 5 - 10 minutes. Heart note: about 3 hours. Base note: from the 3rd to a maximum of 5 hours. I can recommend the scent to those who often go to discos or clubs and are no older than 25. Otherwise, the fragrance can still be worn in spring and summer. It is not suitable for autumn and winter.

If the top note is meant to entice the valued customers to make a purchase, then Boss has thoroughly missed the mark here again. White is not the elegant, smart BOSS suit wearer for me, but rather Max Mustermann. The initial idea with basil and blood orange is not bad in itself, but please not so synthetic!! The transition to the heart notes becomes more tolerable for me, and I could even warm up to the base notes. For me, it's one of those fragrances that a man could wear but shouldn't necessarily. Okay - outside of my vicinity, I don't care so much anymore ;-).

Honestly, I don't find it that bad at all; as a 16-year-old, I didn't think 'in motion' was so terrible either, despite how it's sometimes looked down upon here. I find the bottle practical and fairly well-designed. The longevity for me is about 4.5 hours, unfortunately only average with a decent sillage and a slightly orange-toned but still not fruity scent.

A perfume saleswoman handed me the scent with the words ''something fresh''. Well, to me it smells like walking into a biker bar, full of sweaty, overweight guys all wearing leather jackets. Admittedly, I have never been to such a bar, but I imagine it exactly like that.

You better be ready quick ! The big "money shot" in Kokorico happens in the Opening credits. A sharp, acrid green of distilled fig leaf... poured over a pungent plot of patchouli... Complete with garden soil, (as played by the double-duty cacao). A compelling accord that borders on the grotesque AND the sublime. (Very Annick Menardo). Everything after that, is rather anti-climatic. Simply, charming after-sex banter between gruff patchouli, and alluring cacao (now, the velvety hot chocolate powder variety)... still entwined on a bed of vetiver, and cedar. true, the dynamics of this duo may wear off for some before the scent does. But Kokorico's cacao note alone, continued to drive me "cuckoo for Cocoa Puffs", long into it's drydown! (and that's NOT a bad thing ; ) I can see why the much maligned Kokorico wasn't a big hit. Both the Opening, and concept, may be too audacious for the mass-market: A scent that dares to repel as much as it beckons. But the rest of Kokorico proves to be a quirky, huggable, masculine scent. A good alternative for younger cocoa lovers who may find DHI and L'instant, too dressy or mature. Distinctive, and easily the most fun to wear in my wardrobe. Longevity:9/10(in base) Projection(Fall temp):7/10(in mid) Art/Creatives:8/10(bottle,concept, composition)–A preposterous surrealist bottle worthy of Dali. How:Casual,anytime,fall,winter, date,snuggling,signature.

The name is so silly that I would certainly consider a man who'd display a bottle of "Kokorico" on his bathroom-shelf a trifle weird. "Doodle-doo" or "Kokorico" in French is a men's perfume released by Gaultier in 2011 - and this fragrance was given considerable attention because because of its bottle, its name and the advertising campaign related to it. In Germany, the image of the faucet does not evoke positive feelings, especially when the word rooster is used as a synonym of the noun "man". (In English, of course, the word "cock" has yet another meaning I don't want to expand on). Expressions like "vain rooster, cock of the walk, cock fighting" are normally not loaded with positive significance. However, the cock, the Gallic rooster, is indeed the symbolic animal of France. Always ready to indulge in fights of all kind, an alert and active type, the French rooster embodies key French qualities of a guy like former President Sarkozy (who is planning a comeback). But the marketing of fragrances has to operate on an international scale today, and I doubt that German, British or Chinese men or women consider the rooster's wake-up call a plausible name for a scent. Nevertheless one could argue that Gaultier used a clever marketing-strategy, taking into acccount the fact that costumers need certain visual stimuli. The bottle is designed to stir the interest of the client who has to cope with the grotesque bottle before spraying the fragrance. And what's it like? The scent itself? Is it a wake up call, a scream of masculinity? Well, I'd say it's an "okay fragrance". In most forums it has been compared to "L'Instant pour Homme" by Guerlain, but I personally think that "Kokorico" is only distantly related to the Guerlain fragrance. "Kokerico-doodle-doo" is no revelation to me and offers nothing new. It starts quite strongly with loads of fig and patchouli. The often mentioned cocoa-note is present in the background, it is primarily the patchouli that dominates. Therefore I'd call "Kokorico" a scent devoid of surprises. Who has not smelled a strong patchouli-fragrance before? When either my husband or I yearn for patchouli, we can rely on many offerings of this variant which are superiour to Gaultier. Staying-power is mediocre, too - after two hours you're done with your "mating call". Other men's fragrances reveal their beguiling potential only after two or three hours... I guess the whole concept of "Kokerico" is kind of a gag with the bottle having been modeled according to a portrait of Monsieur Gaultier himself. The famous French satirist Coluche once said that the rooster is the most suitable symbol of France. Why? Because it is the only animal that continues singing happily when its feet are already deep down in "la merde". I'd call this stamina or "résistance". But unfortunately, "Kokorico" is no good example of this adorable quality.

On Wednesday Manchester was a wash with Kokorico Mania, fifty foot high posters every where depicting the Gaultier model In all his glory. It got me all of a flutter with excitement so Into Selfridges we all ran. Once Inside I had to fight my way through a sea of social reprobates and chavz In their track suits and hoodies, alarm bells began to ring. Imagine the scene, security guards were twitching nervously and the orange faced perfume sellers where goggle eyed trying to stop the shoplifters, Immediately It cheapened the product and I was right, Oh dear Mr Gaultier. On first spraying what you get Is a TM Amen rip off, sad but true. After about two hours It began to smell like Elnett hairspray, yep just one big disappointment I just couldn't believe what I was being put through. Anyway the lads from social housing and the unemployment dept seemed to like It, the drug addict shoplifters also had a field day, you could get the fragrance on Deansgate by three that afternoon, £10 a 50ml bottle, still In the tin.So It seems this seasons fragrance for trackie lads Is Kokorico, football grounds will stink of the stuff, council estates and the job centre will never have smelt better, so If I were you I would just stick to the Amen or If your me....Tom Ford Tobacco Vanille.

Perhaps one of the best "designer" releases of recent years. Surrounded by "products of the type" "Hugo", "CH" or "1 Million" (I can continue to infinity ...), aimed, rather, at a teenage audience, this perfume was a pleasant surprise for How different and daring it is. Its predominant notes are patchouli with cocoa, vetiver and little else. It may have some wood, but the rest are very light notes. It is a very daring aroma, in the sense that it comes out of the most common of these days, with an earthy touch and above all "different" (YES, that is just the seal of J.P. Gaultier). With a very good duration but a soft sillage rather stuck to the skin (I think that, in this case, it is not a bad thing). I see it more focused on people close to or over 30 years, since you have to have a certain character to carry it, simply because of the different or "shocking" that can result. Kokorico, I think he has had a great flaw. It really smells like many components of what it declares, such as classic perfumes, that is, the patchouli smells like patchouli, cocoa with cocoa and even the vetiver, gives it an earthy hue, as it should be. All this, clashes with the perfumes of his time, in which to find a note that smells minimally sharp and decent, it is like looking for a needle in a haystack. Without looking like any masterpiece, but if it seems remarkable, because of what I mentioned before and because unlike many of his time, like 1 Million, Kokorico is balanced in all its phases. In summary: Gaultier's excellent perfume, which has already been discontinued, I understand that because of its low sales, but hey, "Twilight" was No. 1 in sales and we are alive and so happy. XDD

After the HUGE success of Le Mâle, JPG wait 16 years to introduce a new Men's fragrance and it happen to fail commercially. Kokorico, created by (probably my favorite perfumer) Annick Ménardo along with Olivier Cresp (Angel, Light Blue). A dream team basically. The fragrance, is a great aromatic and powdery patchouly complemented with fig leaf. The cocoa from patchouli is very present, creating a sensual chocolate feeling with dusty woodiness. Not much moving between opening and drydown but the result is great, masculine, sexy, woody aromatic goodness! The problem, i guess, was the time. It came out in 2011, when thins like Bleu de Chanel, Aventus or 1 Million were dominating the trends and this came as an woody aromatic with strong patchouli and kinda similar to other stuff that came before (LIDG,LIDGE or even Play Intense). This turned out being a failure and the fragrance was discontinued 5/6 years later. I really enjoy this because i find it very aromatic with the fig leaf, which i'm a fan of, and the slightly sweet and dusty cocoa is a perfect combination. Different from LIDG which has a more spicy feel to it with the anise, and more interesting that Play Intense, this could be a classic if it was been released 5 years before. If you never smelled it, try to find a good deal on it and you'll be surprised on how good it is. The prices aren't that high so you can still find good deals on 50mls or even 30mls. I don't find it a true masterpiece or a must have but if you like woody aromatic compositions in a limbo between classic and modern, this is a great example with a twist. Another great work by Annick Ménardo, bravo! 4/5

Here is another example of an underrated and under-considered fragrance that literally drives me crazy. It was discontinued miserably. I really like this fragrance. I got it on a whim with a discount, there were only two red metal boxes left, and I wasn't disappointed. I had no expectations other than knowing it was gourmand, dark, and woody.
I didn't have much expectations for this one as it's poorly rated and it went by with no guts nor glory.

Cedar and patchouli, a masculine-feminine mixture. In the first hour I find it rather feminine, very green. Spring green. Then the cocoa appears, bringing even more contradiction to the combination of aromas At the drydown, the perfume takes a surprising turn and becomes woody and masculine, with that clean smell typical of cedar, although patchouli lingers for hours.

The name evoked a memory of my childhood begin 90's in my uncle's barbershop, where I would always choose the Coco Rico soda. The bottle evoked a comparison to a Moorish head symbol. Then this scent evoked a vision of a masculine embraced male who couldn't care less about being criticized by the noise an unheard herd.

"Can I have that?" he had asked, the man next to me. "Can I have it when you're done testing?" It sounded hopeful, it sounded like he really wanted it - I had to ask to make sure I understood him correctly. "Yes, yes, it's great!

I blind bought this one, it is a very unique scent. Someone described it as a middle eastern bazar. And that is true. The first day, I disliked it. After 1 week, I start to get used to it and like it a little. After 1 month, I hate it. The scent is a mixture of spices and oud. It is going to be only very especial night occasions that I would wear it. I think I am gonna keep having this one for years as it will never end. However, the performance is really great. I can feel sillage even after 9 hours of wearing it.

I was also surprised when I saw this bottle for the first time. I cleaned my glasses with a used cloth, just to make sure that this really is a Boss Bottled OUD fragrance. And indeed... My eyes were not playing tricks on me. There is actually a bottle from Hugo Boss in front of me that contains Oud. Cautiously, I sprayed a bit of this EdT on my skin. Somehow, I couldn't imagine what to expect. I mean: Hugo Boss and Oud, can that work out well?... Oh yes... and how. I dare say that this fragrance is one of the best, if not the best Oud designer fragrance currently on the market. My God! I have fallen in love with this scent. This woody and slightly spicy note... my nose was in tears of joy ;) The Boss Bottled DNA that I love so much is no longer recognizable, yet this EdT is very successful!

When I first sprayed this on I thought "uh oh." The first blast is a bit overpowering but I find it dissipates really quickly. Ahhhh, instant relief! It turns into something really special and beautiful. I can see why so many people have this and love it so much. They sure named this perfume well. It certainly smells like a "classic." It's smooth, warm and rich. Smells "high class" to me. I can smell the vanilla, rose and amber on my skin. It seems to stay linear throughout which I don't mind at all as I love the smell! I love the Eau de Parfum version but I don't like the Eau de Toilette version at all. That one smells sharp and stinky to me. This one is so much nicer. I don't find it too strong or overpowering at all. Simply gorgeous!

The bottle design is absolutely perfect for this scent. Classique smells the way high-end lingerie looks. I save my bottle for use on special occasions, the kind where I hope to get very close to a particular person. I get the orange blossom quite clearly, the vanilla, the ginger and the tuberose. But this is so much more than the sum of its parts. Sweet, warm, powdery, slightly old fashioned in feeling without seeming dated or from any particular era. Just "the past", said in a wistful nostalgic way. If this perfume were a person, it would be a woman who has spent a good deal of time getting dressed for a special night. She has applied various lotions, powders, her makeup applied with the attention to detail of a geisha. I even smell hints of the heated rollers and the material her stockings are made from. I beg you to not waste your precious drops of Classique on those who won't appreciate that you are a goddess.

To clear up any confusion that this review may bring about, I have tried the EDP concentration of Classique, in a woman's torso shaped bottle with intricate, lace-like detailing. From what I've heard, the EDT and EDP are two entirely different scents. This fragrance is a warm floral. It speaks to me as the essential feminine scent, one that is indeed very classic in its appeal. It does have a rather oriental feel, possibly due to the anise, ginger, plum, vanilla and amber. Classique is often difficult to describe. It's recognizable in the sense that it's a popular scent, however when worn on the skin it stirs up so many different opinions. I enjoy Classique, I also find it worthy of its acclaim. This fragrance is heavy, but show me one fragrance that has lasted decades which isn't. It's a mixture of rich floral accords, subtle spices and an interesting creamy sweetness. While I do love this composition, I must admit that the sweetness doesn't work too well with my chemistry. A wardrobe classic but also perhaps a little overworn, Classique is in my opinion, a love it or a hate it. The same could be said of its male counterpart, Le Male. It's thankfully everything I hoped it would be; sexy, rich, floral and feminine. The perfect fragrance to represent a true woman.

Classique is a fitting fragrance for a classy lady. One that proudly wears a cherry red lipstick, black liquid eyeliner and black high heeled shoes. Somehow it reminds me of a 50's Barbie doll. I do not have many opportunities to wear her, but when I do, it's with a cherry red lipstick. Somehow I feel with her no other lipstick will do.

An absolutely beautiful perfume from Jean Paul Gaultier (JPG). This is such a gorgeous scent. It's orange blossom-dominant which is one of my absolute favourite fragrances, and just a few sprays on different pulse points goes a long way indeed. The sillage is excellent, radiating out at least 4-5 feet from the body if not more, so a little goes a long way. The divine fragrance also lasts for between 5-6 hours, if not longer, with the scent lingering on the clothes on has worn. This is a perfume which will turn heads, and it's a divine fragrance that, just by spritzing it on your skin, will uplift your mood, and envelop you in a feeling that you're floating on cloud 9! I'd been eagerly awaiting its arrival by post this morning, and have definitely been rewarded with a heavenly fragrance. As soon as it was opened and I sprayed upon pulse points, the scent was a sweet, spicy, syrupy honey-like ginger ale. It was very heavy and dense and yet the sweetness was in no way cloying or too much. There's a honey-like texture, almost caramel. Intriguingly, it's somehow both thick and sparkling and bright all at the dame time!The ginger is well balanced by the orange blossom and the aldehydes which alone carry a vanilla-like scent. The vanilla lets one know it's a Classique but the Essence is more vanilla-based and spicy with the most gorgeous orange blossom, along with actual whipped cream, honey, almonds and some beginning notes of jasmine as the mid notes slowly begin to appear. The mid notes became evident as creamy white florals appearing on my skin and, in the notes, there's jasmine and orange blossom. The orange blossom's definitely more noticeable which is one of my favourite scents alone let alone in this gorgeous swirl of aromas. I thought there was a hint of tuberose but that's not part of the official list of notes so maybe it's the mix of benzoin with tangerine. The florals are full and rich but never cloying, and they're sweet and slightly powdery. Also in the mid range, there's a wonderful very creamy texture. In the notes, whipped cream is listed and this gives us whipped cream with very sweet vanilla, orange blossom, and other beautiful floral notes. There's also benzoin which gives a honey-like, syrupy, caramel-like texture. And one can still smell the ginger spice. This beautiful perfume is an orange-blossom heavy floral, with spicy oriental gourmande quite literally with vanilla and whipped cream on top! The dry-down of the perfume is extremely smooth. It smells quite similar to the mid notes on my skin. As mentioned earlier, it's quite long-lasting, easy to wear and an incredibly sexy and sophisticated perfume. It's reminiscent of Alien Essence Absolute by Thierry Mugler in the sense that just as the former feels so rich, deep, dark, thick and heavy, so does one get that feeling here. So, if you like Mugler's Alien Essence Absolute, you'll very likely love this perfume as well. In the drydown, it's still very sweet and creamy. There's notes of musk and a type of juniper called cade wood which provides even more sensuality. The scent of spicy white florals sits atop a woody base that comes very deep in the drydown. This is definitely my favourite perfume not just in the Classique line, but from Jean-Paul Gaultier. I just discovered that there's a Classique shower gel and a moisturising body lotion, so those wishing to layer the scent can definitely do so. I definitely intend to purchase the gel and the lotion in the future. However, the perfume alone is quite powerful, and a little truly does go a long way. If you're looking for a sweet, syrupy-like florental gouramande perfume that's extremely easy to wear and which will delight the senses of others around you, then this fragrance is for you. It's an absolutely divine perfume, and I've had compliments from strangers who've wished to know the name of the perfume. It's suitable for any time of the day and any season although I do believe it's likely at its best during the cooler months and in the evenings. JPG's Classique Essence EDP is a sophisticated, sexy, absolutely feminine perfume that will leave you feeling like a goddess as soon as you spray it on. If you're in need of a 'pick me up', this fragrance will boost your mood and your confidence. It will attract attention, in a good way, so be prepared for people to stop and ask you if you'd let them know what perfume you're wearing!

I love the lingerie clad 'torso', and I love Gaultiers taste and sense of style (I'll even forgive him that he 'borrowed' the design for his torso ladies from a favorite vintage of mine: Shocking by Elsa Schiaparelli.) The truth is; I would forgive him anything because he is a scent-genie! I would love to own all his perfumes (if they only were a bit more budget friendly!

Classique EDP walked - no, strutted - so that LDBS could run. This has the sweetness, the animalic sexiness, the floral maturity... but with rose in lieu of orange blossom. I treasure my vintage bottle (from 2016, right before reformulation) and hope I never run out. If I want that flirty-sexy-ultra-feminine vibe of LDBS but I want to smell totally unique, I pull this out.

2012: Evening. Driving in my car, going somewhere I have forgotten. Listening to the radio. Hit after hit. I am not paying attention. New track. Slow and laid back, almost careless or hesitating... A female voice, deep, sexy, playful. Beautiful. Original. Singing 'It's you, it's you, it's all for you - everything I do'... I focus on the music.

So, as you can see, I'm commenting on a women's fragrance again. But this time, everything went much easier than usual! No, I didn't have a sample of this scent and had to test it normally in the city, right in the midst of the female public. So far, so bad! :D However, luck was on my side for once, as the store was being renovated, so there were fewer customers around.

I have tested the EDP Classique by Gaultier several times. I always asked myself: do you actually like it? I am still undecided. The opening is intense, heavy, opulent. It feels as if you are thrown bound into a flower bed and then lie there, faint and dazed, buried under flowers whose heavy, sweet scents take your breath away.

La Belle Fleur Terrible by Jean Paul Gaultier is an aquatic amber floral that makes you travel with your sense of smell to a tropical lagoon on a hot humid day after the rain. The lagoon is adorned by beautiful floating blue water lilies and you are drinking a ginger ale to refresh yourself while your skin is warm and sweet. Around you the humid and hot nature exhales smells of sweet creamy flowers, fresh herbs and green leaves. If you are interested into hearing more about this beautiful scent, please watch my Youtube video linked here below.

This is a beautiful, fresh, and floral focused flanker to the OG La Belle, by none other than Quentin Bisch. I love almost everything this man creates. I must admit, Fleur Terrible is an interesting name but I’m not French or anything, so I must not be saying it right lol. Anyways, this fragrance is a few things, but one thing it’s not is weak. I was shocked at how much this one was projecting all over the place when I wore it to work today. The performance is on par with the other La Belles but the main difference with FT is that it’s floral, powdery, and slightly aquatic. I was surprised to see iris in the notes, but here, it adds a gorgeous and soft powdery touch to a nicely sweet and watery scent. Oddly enough, I am getting the coconut vibe people keep talking about even though there isn’t any coconut here. I wonder if the water lily is causing that or what… either way, it’s beautifully blended and instantly boosts my mood when I smell it. It’s calming, fresh, and gentle, but still has a sensuality to it. Not only is the juice beautiful and performs well, the bottle is absolutely stunning. I love all aspects of the bottle, from the blue color, to the floral neckpiece, and of course, the sexy and classic La Belle silhouette. I just love it and it elevates my experience when using this perfume. This is one that’s great for the spring and summer, but I couldn’t see there being an issue if you wanted to bust this out during fall and winter days when you’ll be indoors. It’s pretty, strong, but still subtle enough to wear whenever. I’ll admit, I can understand why some people wouldn’t be keen on this. The notes are quite simple, but the scent profile itself is complex and unique. Too bad it’s been discontinued.

opens very aquatic. im getting juicy watermelon (albeit a pretty synthetic scent.) its fresh and sugary sweet. then comes the iris, which almost always reads as dust to me. the sweetness of the opening lingers throughout the wear. if you are looking for a soft, dewy floral scent then you will be disappointed. this is the smell of a cold shower with a sweet watermelon shampoo in your hair EDIT: this longevity is crazy lol. i applied it yesterday after showering at around 9pm. its now 2pm the next day and its still there. i even applied another perfume this morning and I can still smell this fuckass watermelon on my wrist. its not on my clothes/hair.

Gorgeous aquatic floral. I definitely pick up on the iris note, it is very well-done in this perfume. It lends a slightly powdery note but does not go into “old-fashioned” territory (iris is a note that can feel a bit dated to me sometimes). The fragrance overall has a light, fresh, watery, modern but still soft air. I don’t think watermelon is a note, but to me Paradise Garden almost has that same “watery and slightly sweet” watermelon quality of the (sadly discontinued) Guerlain Coconut Fizz. (They are absolutely not dupes! But as someone who owns both, I will say I do get similar “sweet aquatic” vibes from them.) Furthermore, what I love about JPG scents is that they have actual staying power and sillage, and this is no exception. It is hard to find fresh spring/summer perfumes that last and project! So that in and of itself makes this a “win” for me. Lovely fragrance, great staying power, and a beautiful bottle.

Oh you beauty! Oh you terrible one! Can't live with you, can't live without you. We don't go together, I secretly knew that from the very beginning. On the other hand, how could I have resisted you? You looked just too good in your turquoise bustier, along with your necklace made of colorful crocheted flowers... You smiled at me so charmingly and said: "Don't take everything so seriously!" And back then in November, you brought a dreamy smile to my face. You instantly brightened up the gray monotony of everyday life. But you also started to annoy me right from those first minutes of our acquaintance. With both, annoying and delighting, you never really stopped. So, what helps? I am captivated by you, precisely because of that and despite everything. Your cheerful scent of tame vanilla and sharp ginger, of zesty bergamot and sunscreen-like ylang swept me away. You whisked me away on a freshly washed, colorful, flying beach towel to a landscape of turquoise swimming pools, rather heavily chlorinated, (that's how you like it, you say, synthetic-hygienic). You like to refer to this pool smell dramatically as "the scent of blue lotus." Quite undramatically, you cheerfully mix cocktails at the pool bar, always with Batida de Coco as the main ingredient. Often you spill, more or less intentionally, a splash of your beloved Coco-alcohol stuff into the pool water. You don't care that you might attract attention. Being ignored is not your thing. You sing (e.g., about beer that doesn't exist in Hawaii) and talk a lot and loudly, and it takes hours until you finally start to quiet down. Deep conversations, soft tones, you want nothing to do with that. You are a seasoned party girl. In homeopathic doses, almost a beauty, yes. In larger quantities, an enduring nuisance par excellence. Once you’ve gotten involved with you, you won't be rid of her so quickly, and you express yourself with a dissonant note (chlorinated pool / alias blue lotus, plus Batida de Coco) and all things sharp-spicy and delightfully creamy and refreshingly colorful floral around and about. It may be that this written engagement with you is the beginning of the end of our liaison. My children don't like you. My husband thinks you are at least quite OK. But, don't be mad, you don't exactly knock him off his feet with excitement. However, I am simply not strong enough at the moment for a separation from you, my colorful scent bomb. After all, you are a "Limited Edition," so what if I were to change my mind again? Could I even bring you back? And if so, at what price? No, no. I will just try a little longer with you, dabbed and not sprayed, and I assume: We will, even if we don't really match, still have a lot of fun. Despite everything and precisely because of that.

I admit, most JPG fragrances in the women's body bottle do not harmonize with me. However, the announcement of "Belle Fleur Terrible" piqued my curiosity. The apparently simple and fresh composition matched my taste perfectly, along with the marketing and the look of the bottle - I had to test it! Joyfully, I opened the sample package and couldn't spray it fast enough.

The long-awaited bottle arrived today. I quickly tore open the envelope and, full of anticipation, sprayed some on my arm. That was about 5.5 hours ago, and I'm still getting a little cloud when I move my arm. For me, the longevity and sillage are fantastic, as it still hasn't lost its strength. In my opinion, it's a truly wonderful summer fragrance.

Hello, fragrance fanatics, and welcome to a new comment from me. Yes, yes, it was time for me to write again; I really had other things to do lately. But now I've stuck my nose into things that don't concern me… I mean, I sniffed a new fragrance so I could present something to you here, he he. Today, we're talking about the Gaultier fragrance "La Belle Paradise Garden.

In the opening, lotus, the typical La belle pear flashes briefly. Probably due to the iris, there is a short lipstick scent association, it runs slightly powdery. It has tropical vibes without becoming too stuffy, slightly aquatic without being "shower gel-like." More in the direction of "Aqua Allegoria Coconut Fizz | Guerlain," just sweeter.

For me, this is the ultimate vacation scent, my first high-end fragrance and my first Gaultier. And also a blind buy, how bold. When I spray it, I am greeted by a hint of sunscreen that then transforms into a tropical cocktail.

Boss hasn't made any good perfumes for a long time. Aside from Boss Bottled, they only have rubbish in their lineup. Not worth the price. Absolutely zero artistic ambition. Often poor copies of other bestsellers. No courage, no innovations... And so on and so forth. All theses & opinions about Boss perfumes that I had already stereotypically laid out for my test of Boss Pure. Everything set aside for now, because surprisingly, I find it absolutely not bad, quite the opposite. Boss Pure from 2008 is an aquatic fragrance full of synthetics, chemicals & laboratory feel. This doesn't necessarily have to mean something bad, as Comme des Garcons regularly shows, but it is simply an undeniable fact here. The scent often reminds me of the highly praised Nautica Voyage - but what apparently goes unnoticed or is even rated positively there, is torn apart here & dismissed as synthetic nonsense. I can't & won't understand that. Even if a brand releases a lot of unnecessary products, one should give every fragrance they test an unbiased chance. And I like Boss Pure, despite the metallic aqua-jogging in the lab basement. This aquatic impression is completely different than, for example, Cool Water or Acqua di Gio. Boss Pure goes its own way with melons, metal, mandarins, chlorinated water, aluminum foil, cucumbers, light woods, and white flowers. Fortunately, the fig is used more than discreetly and serves only as a loose framework. However, one should note that completely detached from the sillage, such synthetic bombers can quickly become migraine-inducing due to acute overdosage. Bottle: simply fitting & fittingly simple. Sillage: somewhere on Nautica Voyage level. Longevity: don't expect more than 5 hours with it. Conclusion: a pleasant surprise & a solid summer synthetic fest!

Boss Pure was recommended to me by a saleswoman when I asked for "something that smells similar to Cool Water Deep." So it should be something fresher, aquatic. After several attempts, which I found neither fresh nor aquatic, she finally handed me Boss Pure. I liked it immediately, so I took it with me. A blind buy, because my previous perfume was completely empty. The scent is somewhat aquatic as well. However, I'm sorry, it smells very much like melon to me. I only find the scent fresh in the first 5-10 minutes; the watermelon (please forgive me this bad pun...) seems to stick around quite stubbornly. And eventually, I get this strange, almost sugary, heavy sweetness that I find so unbearable that I just want to take a shower. It could be that mine has gone off. But this unbearably sweet scent was already the reason three years ago why I let it gather dust on the shelf shortly after purchasing it. Still, I don't want to tear the scent apart. It does have components that I like. Maybe it smells really good on someone else. On me, however, it does not, and that's why I unfortunately can't get much out of Boss Pure.
I recently tried Boss Pure - a great scent! It definitely has its own character. The freshness is just right, with no trace of being overpowering.

I once had it as a shower gel, unfortunately the EdT cannot really distinguish itself olfactorily from that. As shallow as the bottle and the advertising, so is the scent. "Pure" starts in a rather compulsive way with a slightly powdery, somewhat synthetic wave of freshness. Fig may indeed be a component of the heart phase, some fruity elements join in, but in terms of sillage, it is very airy, very light-footed. The synthetic aspect hovers over everything the whole time, "Pure" also comes across as somewhat annoying in its almost provocatively casual attitude, wanting to be floating-aquatic and invigorating. The fragrance world doesn't really need this.

This Boss creation really starts off very fresh. Very citrusy but not with a fruity round note like, for example, Dior Homme Sport; rather, it has a somewhat bitter scent like grapefruit or, for me, even more like a very sour pomelo. After a few minutes, it becomes quite aquatic with typical cucumber/melon aromas. I don't really recognize the fig; perhaps it is the cause of the now rising light sweetness. A slightly herbaceous/dry floral accord slowly emerges. My nose convincingly tells me that this is a floral scent, but I can't identify which flowers they are. I'll rely on the pyramid and believe that it is hyacinth and lily. The citrus notes are now only perceptible in the background. In many fragrances from recent years, such a citrus opening often disappears without a trace after just 5 minutes. Not here; the citrus scent is still slightly present, and the aquatic "cucumber freshness" is still right in the mix. Together with the floral scent and the minimal sweetness of the fig (or is it the Massoia bark responsible for that?), a lightly herbaceous, minimally sweet floral fresh scent emerges after a relatively short development, which characterizes this creation. And so it goes on. Sillage: rather subtle and close to the body but not entirely weak. Longevity: quite decent for a fragrance with this profile. The bottle is one of the most successful examples from the BOSS portfolio for me. It comes across as stylish and definitely looks elegant. The clear and sober/unexcited design language fits perfectly with the content. Pure calmness, as my predecessor wrote. I agree! No high recognizability; for that, you really have to know it well. Not a fragrance that you get directly approached about, no "Wow, I want that" effect. But that is exactly what I find very successful about this scent. A universal fragrance with a very pleasant note that really stays fresh. And at no point does it become unpleasant to my nose; quite the opposite. I can't relate to the strongly overpowering sweetness mentioned here. Often you hear that with such inconspicuous fragrances in this price class, you can just as well find something in the drugstore. I don't think so; the "fresh and simple" waters of the lower price range that I have tested so far either have significantly worse longevity and are gone after a maximum of two hours, or what's left doesn't match the actual scent at all. I'm glad to have found this Boss; there are plenty of occasions where you can do without a character fragrance. And that's where BOSS Pure fits perfectly!

For years, I have been searching for an exciting scent from Hugo Boss. There used to be a few here, but most of them have unfortunately become extinct. Let's see what comes next. The advertising promises an aquatic scent with Pure. Hurrah, maybe this will be something. However, the packaging is too light, too pastel, too soft for that.

Here, name and scent have come together well: pure and unpretentious. It is certainly not a fragrance that stands out for its complexity and depth; rather, it is a - if not applied too heavily - pleasant everyday scent, where freshness and straightforwardness unite.
I'll buy it again someday. Very fresh, slightly tangy scent. Good for everyday wear.

Like all the fragrances from Boss in recent years. Please don’t try to make something special or extraordinary. It would be nice to create a real fragrance again. No, the real fragrances remain Hugo and Bottled. After that, not much has come (except for those who are loyal to Boss), and it will probably stay that way.

"I met him out for dinner on a Friday night He really got me working up an appetite He had tattoos up and down his arm There's nothing more dangerous than a boy with charm He's a one-stop-shop, makes the panties drop He's a sweet talkin' sugar-coated Candyman A sweet talkin' sugar-coated Candyman" - Christina Aguilera I recently gained it online for an absolutely fantastic price, blindly, trusting the fact I love both Le Mâle classic and Ultra Mâle. I can't believe my eyes, Le Mâle Airlines' Eau Fraiche is an oxymoron, a really fresh and delightful fragrance at the same time. The ultra-fresh notes of mint combine with the ultra-candy notes of chewing gum, it's like eating a soft and juicy Big Babol with mint! Do not let the guy in tank top bottle fool you into thinking that Le Mâle Airlines Eau Fraiche is just marketed to a particular generation of men. Jean Paul Gaultier made this suitable for everyone with its slightly sweet and very fresh profile, and Le Mâle Airlines builds around a sexy fabric softener accord, clean linen laundry smell, fresh like an impeccable tank top that you slip into. A few notes are dimmed, and some are amped up, but overall this is a summer version of the original thing, so read on if you're interested. It rises heavily for me, but I can tolerate experiencing a delightful mellowing down into something fresher and sparkly. A blast of minty crisp, neroli blossoms and something airy opens the dance. Aldehydes are involved; however, I do not get them like in Chanel n° 5. Perhaps, the blend of aldehydes and neroli contributes to the uplifting airy bubble gum accord. I got big, and I mean huge, chewing gum vibe. As if it smelled like the original, but with a fresh chewing gum feel, I loved it. Nathalie Gracia-Cetto developed this new interpretation by using ingredients with impact wrapping the mint in a swirl of aldehydes and ozonic notes, with the mint grounding the less earthbound notes around it. That's the part that's lighter, so you don't know yet what to expect later. The orange blossom leads into a heart dominated by sage, a place where keeping it lighter makes the overall effect better. Sage and orange blossom are brought to you on a warm breeze. Both sage and clary sage, here called Sclarene, are blended to release a woodier and herbal accord that works very well, especially for a summer perfume. If your nose is trained enough, you will catch Ambroxan in the background, and together with the aldehydes, add a delicate airiness and salty depth to the blend. The more massive, powdery sweetness comes in next and dominates into the sensual dry down. The fusion of woods, tonka, and vanilla are still here from the original, with the Ambroxan as the principal source of woodiness. The vanilla and tonka beans are always there to make it close enough to the sweet woody foundation that defines Le Mâle. I guess that trinity is a Le Mâle DNA. Of course, a touch of creamy sandalwood cannot be missing, that's why I also get some light woody notes throughout. Le Mâle Airlines is something substantial! It has the same DNA as the original, no doubt, when you catch a whiff you can not associate it with Le Mâle classic, the similarity is too substantial. An interpretation of that hit that overall it feels a bit of lighter, and updated through the addition of ambroxan. It smells like a very refreshing combination of mint, tonka bean, and vanilla. Even though it is aimed at the warmer seasons, it might be too cloying for some like myself in too hot weather like Italian summer. In fact, it has the typical bubblegum vibe of modern fragrances, such as Paco Rabanne One Million and Invictus, Rochas Man, Nikos Sculpture, or Versace Eros. Le Mâle Airlines is a sweet fresh scent, but not cloying, very playful that shines from early Spring throughout late Fall, casual daytime and not too sweet for warm weather. It's not a powdery scent to me, it's definitely on the watery side, but you won't find marine notes either. It might come as a bit naive, but like I said, it's a fun fragrance, something for fun events, parties, summer activities, etc. The bottle is pretty shabby, but the juice is excellent and lasts a long time, longevity is very good for a summer fragrance, and the projection is reliable, so beware of over-spraying! Do not blind-buy this one if you do not like the sweetness in modern fragrances, or you are not intimate with Le Mâle species. Sweet and fresh, what else? This review is based on a Le Mâle Airlines tester 75ml I own. Stay well; stay healthy. -Elysium

Year after year, Jean Paul Gaultier releases a flanker. Almost simultaneously with Le Male Essence de Parfum comes this Eau Fraiche Popeye Edition. One must say, many flankers are quite insignificant. I haven’t tested all of the seemingly 1 million flankers, but some were indeed very unremarkable. Besides the original, I own Fleur du Male, which I love and have used often. The rest is often an attempt to make the fragrance classic relevant again with a flanker. As with many classics, this rarely succeeds. I absolutely wanted to test this Popeye because the concept is quite interesting. Since this is a limited edition, you never know when it will disappear again. It comes again in the well-known metal tin. The most famous bottle in the world greets you. The Popeye image looks slightly trashy, but I find it quite cool. It has something. Popeye is a likable character, popular with young and old. It appeals more to the younger clientele, as Popeye represents strength. After the first spray, a strong mint note dominates. A very fresh bubble-gum mint. It becomes clear that this was primarily created for the younger audience. Due to the mint, it reminds me of Versace's "Eros." The sillage is similarly good. This sweet mint is a commonality with Eros. Whether this was intentional, one does not know. Furthermore, the typical Le Male note is immediately recognizable. Quite well executed and well modernized for the year 2016. Neroli and sage are not very noticeable. As for sclarene, I must say I don’t even know what that is or how it smells. Later, the tonka bean comes in, adding sweetness to the whole. I like it, and the teenage girls and young ladies will surely like it too. Also wearable around the age of 30, but it has to match the style. It definitely doesn’t fit with a shirt and suit... For me, it is certainly not just for summer. Since it can be quite intense in sillage and scent, it can also be worn well on somewhat cooler days. 1A-suitable for parties as well, since it has some similarities to Eros. Thanks to the mint, it is a fresh scent for warmer days. Not necessarily suitable for all activities. Sillage and longevity are similarly good as the original Le Male. The sillage is reminiscent of Fleur du Male. It radiates similarly. Comparisons can also be made to Eros, but due to the Le Male note, it clashes significantly less. Conclusion: Those looking for a young, modern scent and have no issues with the Le Male note might find this interesting. If you like Eros, you might enjoy this intense fragrance. A successful flanker of the greatest fragrance classic.

I am so tired of the minimally different summer versions of major perfume bestsellers. Almost more than the people who punish a flanker like this one before they have ever seen, smelled, or held it. So, two good reasons, along with the little hype around it, to test the new Le Male Popeye Edition more closely. Without spinach or Olivia, but at 30 degrees in bright sunshine, while eating ice cream & in the gym. It is a summer scent, no question about it. And a powerfully potent, intrusive & high-pitched one at that. But I somehow like it for its brash, piercing synthetic overkill style. It combines the Le Male mint-tonka combo with the currently popular frozen bubblegum chic - resulting in an extremely bright, citrusy & artificial refresher that should appeal greatly to those under 20. It redefines the word cool, combining it, in my opinion, somewhat with the word "cheap." But as I said: it’s a Le Male, it’s better than reheated summer nonsense & it’s hip, sleek & easy to wear. So hats off briefly to Ms. Gracia-Cetto! No flop, no hit, but also not worth any of its hasty criticisms. You might not like it & find yourself too mature for it, but as a scent, it comes damn close to what young women find sexy these days. Bottle: the Popeye gives the already somewhat kitschy Le Male bottle a run for its money... not very pretty anymore. Unless your name is Geissen. Sillage: strong, especially because it will mostly be worn in summer. Longevity: due to the sweet base, it even lasts over 6 hours at 35 degrees. Conclusion: those who are young, have a brutal taste in perfume & consider themselves good-looking due to excessive self-confidence shouldn’t go wrong with this Mr. Spinach. And one should generally not be averse to Le Male. Definitely better than the fifteenth summer version!

My title refers to the Superman edition of this fragrance, where you can see Superman on the bottle. Otherwise, it is of course the same scent as the Popeye edition. Anyway, I had a sample of this fragrance from a nice perfumer who knows I like comics. I think Superman is quite alright, even though he shouldn't be my favorite character (that's Batman!!! :DD), but I still enjoy reading the occasional Superman comic,… and I must admit, I especially like Supergirl… from the new TV series,… I could endlessly rave about the sweet actress… *sigh* but well, I’ll leave it at that :D Well, be that as it may, before I bore everyone with comics (although… this is a men's fragrance… but okay, I’ll refrain from mentioning them further *sigh*…), let me get to the scent, of which I don't expect much, as I have never really been a big Jean Paul Gaultier fan and most of the fragrances from the Le Mâle line haven't appealed to me much. The scent: The fragrance starts with fresh notes. There is relaxed neroli, mixed with mint, which provides a nice start, if it weren't for the synthetic aftertaste that is already noticeable from the beginning. That said, sweet notes quickly blend into the fragrance, which are clearly coming from the tonka bean. However, despite the tonka bean, the scent is not heavy-sweet, even though the sweetness should continue to rise. The mint keeps the fragrance smelling fresher for longer, while herbal notes (sage and generally herbal scents) contribute to a more spring-like or summery atmosphere. Overall, the heart note and initial base still smell quite nice. The tonka bean gradually mixes with vanilla in the base, which increases both the sweetness of the fragrance and its powderiness. Normally, this scent combination, the "dream team" of tonka bean and vanilla, is often a very nice combination for the base. Unfortunately, the synthetic notes, which can be very clearly smelled in this fragrance, become extremely stronger now in the base, so that the scent starts to become less pleasant from the base onwards, which is a shame, as this phase of the fragrance lasts the longest. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is quite good, and thus the fragrance can be smelled from a distance for a longer time. Even though the fragrance is not particularly heavy, one should still be careful with the dosage, especially on warm days. I also find the longevity very good, as the fragrance lasts easily over ten hours. The bottle: Since I tried the Superman edition, I will of course describe the Superman bottle instead of the Popeye bottle. So, the bottle has the well-known shape of the male torso from the Le Mâle fragrances and is shiny silver or chrome, except for the lower part. On the front, you can see Superman as if he is about to break through the bottle wall. It’s a nice motif for Superman fans or comic lovers. As is often the case, these bottles have no cap, fit well in the hand, and are easy to spray. And of course, there is also the "tactile" feature at the bottom, which didn't necessarily need to be sculpted that way :D And as I said, I tried the Superman bottle edition here, so the expression "The Man of Steel" takes on a whole different meaning! :D Hmm… so how do I find the fragrance now? To quote the (disappointed) words of Caesar from "History of the World, Part I" by Mel Brooks, after receiving an alabaster bathtub: "Nice. Quite nice. Not wildly exciting, but nice!" That's exactly how the fragrance feels to me. A scent that initially smells somewhat nice, but due to its rich synthetics, in the end, doesn't really appeal to you, unless you have lower expectations or are still quite young, as this fragrance could certainly be a good going-out scent on warmer days for younger people. Without the distinct, even (at least for me) annoying synthetic aftertaste, the fragrance would surely have turned out much nicer, but as it is, it’s simply not my scent, and therefore I cannot really recommend it. I would anyway suggest the wonderful Essence de Parfum, which smells many times better, but unfortunately, that fragrance is not suitable for warm days and can only be used in autumn and winter… … alternatively, one could also consider Nikos Sculpture, which smells wonderful, also contains orange blossom and tonka bean, and is somewhat suitable for summer and parties. Of course, Nikos is also a bit synthetic, but it is also proof that synthetic fragrances can be well made… at least in my opinion :)

I have now spent a few days with the new Le Mâle Eau Fraîche Superman, which is supposed to smell just like the Popeye version! Now, if it were up to me, I would call it Le Mâle Eau Fraîche Spiderman (since it sticks quite well to the skin!) or even Le Mâle Eau Fraîche Superboy. I find the names Popeye or Superman, as well as some reviews of the fragrance, exaggerated; I would expect something stronger, more distinctive from Popeye or Superman (which is not the case!). At the start of the fragrance, a sweet mint greets you, which initially reminds me of women with hairspray and chewing gum, but that fades away in the first 5 minutes. After that, the sweet mint becomes more subtle, and tonka and sandalwood slowly come to the forefront. Another scent development only occurs after hours on the skin; after 5-6 hours, I perceive the typical Le Mâle DNA (just with a bit more vanilla). Le Mâle Eau Fraîche Popeye / Superman is certainly not a bad fragrance and will find some lovers here. Even though it is primarily designed for summer, I wished for slightly better attributes, so it’s quite nice but unfortunately not a top fragrance (especially not a powerhouse or beast mode scent). Longevity: on my skin about 10 hours / on fabric a bit longer (but no comparison to Le Male / Vintage) Sillage / projection: for the first 30 minutes, it can fill a small room, after 45 minutes it’s only close to the skin (for me).

At the end of September, vacation, 34 degrees, a great opportunity to test 3 fragrances. As a fan from the very beginning of Invictus (not Aqua), I simply love these sweet, fresh-synthetic bubblegum scents. From the souk, I got 10 ml samples of Le Male Popeye Edition (also known as Superman Edition) and Rasasi Hawas for Him. Thanks to Shuqush.

* This review is for Le Mâle Eau Fraîche Superman Edition + Le Mâle Eau Fraîche Popeye Edition * Hello everyone, today we're talking about one of the "thousands of flankers" that exist for Le Mâle Eau de Toilette . Short and sweet - these are, in my opinion, the 5 best!

The limited edition of Le Mâle with a maritime look impressed me right from the purchase, but it ended up in my bag purely by chance (and not by design). Le Mâle is likely a familiar term for many of you, but what Jean Paul Gaultier has released for summer is a somewhat outstanding fragrance, thanks to its maritime character.

At first, one can perceive a very intense and strong sweet floral note, which carries a very strong soapy powdery tone and, the closer you get to the sprayed area, it exudes a gum-like aspect thanks to the neroli.

I first smelled Le Male Eau Fraiche on a friend and thought it was quite good (the scent). So I was even more excited when I discovered the Limited Edition "Superman" at Duty Free in 2017. Bought it blind - I knew it. At home, I joyfully sprayed it for the first time, but somehow I remembered it differently. Fresher, more masculine.

... for so long and I still don't know if I like you or not. When applying this fragrance, you get oranges in your nose with citrus and green notes, followed by slightly spicy aromas. The musk makes it slightly creamy, there is also a woody note and vetiver makes it dry. The longevity and sillage are moderate. Can be worn by young, middle-aged, and older people; it works for both work and leisure. If you like a spicy orange scent, this is the right one for you.

This is my absolute favorite fragrance for men. I have been using it for a long time, sometimes switching it up, but I always end up coming back to it. And maybe that's why the scent feels so familiar and close to me. It is a wonderful option for the modern, energetic man, filled with notes of strength, courage, energy, and hints of masculine charm that are hard to resist. According to classification, the fragrance belongs to the woody-oriental scents. The opening note is bergamot, which immediately grabs attention, but there are also floral notes, nutmeg, and cinnamon, sandalwood, and cardamom. All these ingredients create a great composition that refreshes and invigorates, igniting passion and generating a strong flow of energy. A scent for real men who cannot settle for less and want it all at once. Tip: Use it sparingly, the scent is intense and requires only a little, then it will attract the women around you and make them crave you.

Today I had the excellent idea to travel south - specifically to the southern part of Bochum. The area is picturesque - and the Ruhr flows through forests and meadows. Unfortunately, hundreds of others had the same idea - 90% of them cyclists. They were commuting, wobbling, and zooming along the walking paths, forcing Hundi and me to dart into the underbrush like hares. With arrogant good-people faces on their bike seats, because they are doing something for health and nature! Hundi had his tail - and I had my head tucked in. Scandal! I rummaged through my bag for a white flag - but found, fittingly, Scandal by Night. The first spray cooled my pulse down - but at the same time boosted my self-confidence. The soft honey note smoothed my frayed nerves, and the tuberose creates presence. Tonka rounds it off, and patchouli has a strengthening effect. Hundi and I crawl back out of the underbrush - and stroll side by side along the path. We take up the space that is rightfully ours - and by Night creates our comfort zone.

I absolutely wanted to test 'Scandal by Night'. Why, actually? The somewhat embarrassing answer: Because I am an incorrigible packaging victim. 'Scandal' and 'night' are both buzzwords that reflexively pique my interest. As a goth and chronic night owl, I unfortunately always feel addressed when perfumes carry names like 'night', 'dark', or 'noir', only to be overwhelmed far too often by cloyingly sweet mush. Apparently, in the minds of many perfumers, the night is quite a sticky-sweet affair. I was additionally lured by the television advertisement that caught my eye yesterday (or rather both of them). The ad itself, in which a long-legged model tiptoed through an upper-class restaurant wearing only an oversized men's jacket and flashing lingerie, while the restaurant guests and waiters whispered in outrage, dropping their lobsters, monocles, and other items, could not have interested me less, despite its bourgeois-artistic black-and-white aesthetics. But the music - the waltz from Khachaturian's Masquerade Suite, one of my favorite pieces of music ever! Of course, I had to test the scent... with somewhat disappointing results. The nocturnal scandal is not bad. To be honest, Pure XS for Her, Olympea, the regular 'Scandal', and this little flanker here are for me sisters, between which I notice no significant difference. In the top note, all four start almost identically for me, with a sweet honey melon note, heavy but not too cloying, quite suitable for summer. Especially compared to Pure XS, I can't really discern any difference at this stage, at least from memory, since I don't have a sample or a bottle for direct comparison here. Then, however, the fragrances develop apart. While Olympea becomes increasingly salty-vanilla and Pure XS takes on that popcorn note, Scandal by Night reveals more and more honey and tuberose after a while. The scent loses its initial summery lightness and becomes a bit more cozy-sweet. Compared to Olympea, I find it more boring, weaker, uninspired - and I also find Pure XS, although it can be a bit annoying, still has more character. One can give 'Scandal by Night' credit for not being as cloying as the fragrance pyramid suggests. The honey is not sticky and does not trigger diabetes spikes. For me, it is more of a honeyMELON, a bit fruitier-fresher, at least at the beginning. Tuberose, which can often chase me away, especially when it goes in that disgusting, artificial gum direction, does not smell artificial here at all, not like gum, and for its standards is almost subtle, not scratchy and clawing, but almost cuddly. Tonka? Well, maybe a hint - and the patchouli is almost nonexistent for me. It takes a while before it even dares to show itself. I am a bit puzzled that some find it overly sweet, heavy, and cloying, and especially unbearable in summer. I myself am quite sensitive to that; an overdosed sweet, heavy women's fragrance in summer in a cramped train compartment or a poorly ventilated, narrow room and I could vomit. But I believe 'Scandal by Night', if dosed sparingly, would not particularly annoy me or upset my stomach even in the height of summer in the mentioned situation. And I am actually very, very intolerant: LVEB at 30 degrees Celsius outside and I develop urges to push the lady in question out of the bus at full speed. ;) Still: 'Scandal by Night' delivers nothing new or surprising, it feels to me as if I have smelled it a hundred times before. Honey, tuberose, a bit of patchouli, a bit of tonka, a song as old as time. But I really don't find the scent bad, as long as it is not overdosed. If someone were to gift me a bottle, I would probably even use it up, but I would never buy it. Anyone who has Olympea or Pure XS does not need this one as well. P.S.: I don't know if my skin has recently become a scent eater, but I definitely cannot endorse 'Longevity: 8.9'. It has crumbled away quite quickly on me.

JPG rarely holds back. And with a perfume named "Scandal by Night," it could only get thoroughly naughty. And the red juice undoubtedly meets these expectations and prejudices. An extravagant night-out scent for young girls and young-at-heart mothers. Very juicy, very moist, very flickering and igniting. More of a honeyed seductress than a sweet little thing. Almost an even more feminine successor to Gaultier². Very aggressive and self-assured. But mostly without tipping into the disgusting and catty. Wayward youth. Let them live it up! Long live the flesh. Love for all. Sex sells. It is and will always be so. "Scandal by Night" leaves no cherry in the village and goes straight through the dance floor ceiling. The scent sits in a red evening dress at the semi-fancy bar. With equally red makeup. The lips are visible. She gives no F and yet had them all. Warm and monstrously captivating. A lady on the street but a freak in the bedroom. PILF. To me now, a bit too penetrating, exhausting, and clingy. But 15 years ago, I would have definitely fallen for it. Bottle: she was only wearing shoes Sillage: potent power-packed seductress Longevity: 7 hours to double digits - depends on how much you sweat Conclusion: a tuberose honey cherry explosion that takes your breath away and comes right in your face - this JPG knows no shame and is wonderfully kinky!

Man and woman Parfumista might wonder, what do these terrible, taste-bud-offending alcoholic drinks and a perfume have in common that they stand side by side in a title? The answer lies in my individual reaction: Of all three numbing impositions, I felt nauseous. So --- for those who find this - admittedly pointed - summary sufficient, you may stop reading here and retreat with an "oh, what a pity" or "I knew it" to beloved scents or positive olfactory surprises. For those who hesitate, here is my experience with this new (really?) fragrance from JPG in more detail: I was careless enough to open my sample on a Saturday evening and quickly apply it to my wrist. At that moment, the scale read: xxx kilograms. Immediately, sweet scent notes conquered my nose and for tenths of a second, the prevailing olfactory impression was: floral-sweet. So far - so predictable. But instead of a delicate floral dream, the obviously aggressively formulated scent molecules added up to a syrupy, honey-laden scent carpet, well, let’s say - coating, which had nothing to offer besides an enormous intensity of great penetration: As with Scandal, one searches in vain for tuberose and patchouli, at least notes that deserve those names. But I wanted to wait and see how the scent would develop. Perhaps it just needs a chance, some time to connect with the skin and reveal its true character? Unfortunately, SBN rather revealed a commercial character: All cards already played, even bubblegum smells more differentiated. With each passing minute, I felt increasingly that I had eaten far too many honey buns, many, many, many heavy honey buns with cheap industrial sugar honey stuff. A glance at the scale confirmed: xxx kilos plus 3! Within just 10 minutes! I had to act! So to the sink, where water and fine olive soap should put an end to the sweet overkill that was already threatening to glue my brain: Everything appeared to me tinged with honey-colored yellow. Yikes. Back at my workspace, I opened the windows and let out into the night what remained of the scandalously overdriven mono-scent still clinging to the precious oxygen elements. Now the nuisance should come to an end, I thought, and sat down. Instead, a sweetish cloud wafted through the room again and reached for me. A sniff test on my wrist confirmed: At least the longevity is (unfortunately) above average good.

Which perfumery came up with the idea of delighting me with a generous sample of Scandal by Night, I no longer remember. It would most likely never have crossed my mind to acquire a fragrance called Scandal by Night. Not because I am so prudish, but because I can imagine what awaits me. Thanks to the sample in a spray bottle, I now have the opportunity to test my prejudices for their validity. Based on the comments, I assumed that I would be overwhelmed by a wave of honey sweetness.
