Whether it would be sticky sweet or surprisingly light and bearable. However, the honey remains very discreet after I spray it on. Instead, I am flooded by a wave of floral scent, which I soon identify as tuberose. An old acquaintance. I know her from Poison, Hypnotic Poison, and Loulou - all creations from the 80s and 90s, when heavy scents were favored. I owned all three. Loulou is still in my collection. When I received Hypnotic Poison by Dior years ago as a gift from a Swiss pen pal on a date, I unfortunately already knew that I couldn't handle so-called "hypnotic" fragrances. (I still "used it up" because I had it after all...) I recognize and understand their message: They seem exotic. One feels transported to a magical nighttime jungle in Tahiti - although I have no idea if there are jungles in the South Seas. Not without reason is the white-flowering tuberose a night-blooming plant. Its scent is enchanting, heavy, sweet, sensual, seductive. And that is exactly what Scandal by Night aims to be. Fragrances of this kind have "always" existed and have been popular among many women. Gaultier consciously plays with the sensual note of tuberose. The bottle, in which a lady seems to be trapped, of whom one only sees the wriggling, well-formed legs with high heels, fits the image just as much as the supposedly scandalous name. The fact that the nighttime scandal has something to do with sex is conveyed more than clearly. As is known, Jean Paul Gaultier likes to provoke. Okay, I get that. It's fine with me. What bothers me is that the message of the perfume is brought to me too overtly. I prefer something subtler. But Gaultier has no intention of that. He wants his fragrance to be loud and stand out. And that is probably what most women who wear this perfume want as well. And they don't just wear it, but - even intentionally - flaunt it: Look how sexy I am... I am irresistible... I will cloud your senses, enchant you, seduce you... This is what Gaultier tries to convince his target audience about the effect of this fragrance. I find that too blunt. I don't want to walk around as a female seduction machine, nor would I - as a man - respond to such an overly blatant sensual scent. But I am sure that many - especially younger - women feel more desirable with this perfume, which is of course a chimera. I can imagine that some men would rather take cover from this scent wave than let themselves be conquered... But maybe I am being unfair. Surely many ladies also wear the perfume simply because they like the scent and not because they want to appear erotic and make a conquest. The scent is too heavy and too sweet for me. Tuberose is said to have a relaxing effect. That has not occurred for me, just as the supposed scandal that the perfume wants to express has not. What is offered here is simply too little. The scandal is, according to the scent, not even a scandalette - at most for those who let themselves be convinced of it. In reality, it is a rather conventional tuberose scent, of which there are many. The sensuality comes, so to speak, with a sledgehammer and can be quite annoying if one does not appreciate such a sweet, enchanting heaviness. A fragrance can also create an erotic aura in a different way - finer, more refined, more exciting. As mentioned, the very one-dimensional message also includes that the scent undergoes no significant changes on me. It remains, so to speak, as it is. Only that it becomes weaker over time. The scent may annoy some because it is so intrusive. That it is above average long-lasting and cannot even be removed with oil by those who want to get rid of it, I cannot quite believe. For me, the longevity is average. The sillage appears impressive at first but soon diminishes. It is clear that this scent is not made for everyday use. In professional life, it would be completely out of place. It is clearly an evening fragrance that I can well imagine in discos. I cannot identify with it. Not because I no longer go to discos, but because my preference, as mentioned, lies with subtler fragrances that have an exciting scent development and are more interesting or profound and perhaps innovative. Fragrances with a touch of avant-garde like some molecule perfumes or something more "sophisticated" simply suit me better. Others may see it differently, of course. Since the scent, in my opinion, radiates little elegance, I see it most likely on ambitious disco queens in their 20s. The tuberose may smell intense and striking as a flower. As a scent on my skin, I find it too intrusive. This applies to all fragrances with this note. I love hyacinths and their strong scent, but in perfume, it soon becomes too much of a good thing for me. But that is a matter of taste. I don't want to say that I fundamentally cannot relate to tuberose. I could imagine that this note can be very stimulating in fragrances if it is not overdosed. Unfortunately, I have yet to come across a perfume where it is not - apparently, there are many fans of tuberose overdoses. I feared that the honey in this perfume might be too much for me. In fact, I find the tuberose so dominant that it gives the honey no room to unfold. Tonka bean may give the tuberose a certain vanilla warmth and that typical sensual almond aroma, but it actually serves only as a supportive base and never comes to the fore. Conclusion: too sweet, too heavy, too intense, too intrusive... Not for me.

A gray, cold day in the north. The view out the window initially dampens the mood. A few spritzes of Scandal by night and the mood lifts again. Suddenly, I feel all warm inside! I go to the kitchen and make myself a tuberose tea. I add such a big spoonful of delicious, sticky, sweet honey that the tea almost only smells of it. Yummy!

Storytime: Last year, I went power shopping with my best friend. It was incredibly warm, and the shopping frenzy made me melt. I had neither deodorant nor anything else with me, terrible! For me, it's the worst to "smell." Before heading to the next store, we had to bring back what felt like 100 bags to the car because, as I said: nearly dying!

Today is Friday, the weather is damp and cold, and even though it’s already May, it feels like November. My gaze drifts out the window, and somehow the inner desire for warmth and comfort arises. Scandal by night is for me such a fragrance, fitting for this mood, and suddenly there’s an olfactory embrace.

Today I was in the perfume shop... I just wanted to test THE scents that I didn't like at all a year ago or rather, that I absolutely hated... Scents that I was always sure I would NEVER test again... Wrong! My aunt always has a saying: NEVER SAY NEVER! So today I can agree with her 100% on this saying!

I love this scent! When I read the composition, it was already too late for me: honey and tuberose! What a combination! As a declared tuberose fan, I couldn't get the scent out of my head. Still, I decided to look for a honey scent and went for Spirit Intense by Boadicea the Victorious. But today in the city, I had so much time... so off to D... sniffed around...

Early summer! A garden near a large body of water. The first fruits are already ripe: Black currants. Shiny blue-black. Slightly tart, with a delicious aroma and very juicy. The last, late daffodils are still blooming. Cheerful scents of floral and spicy freshness. By the pond behind the bushes, the deep blue of irises glimmers. Lined with "water grasses" that love to grow at the damp edge. Powdery-floral and "green-grassy" summer aromas galore! But the nights are often still quite cool! Just right for the long, delicate gray-green moss drapes that grow on the branches of the gnarled, ancient oak. Its trunk already shows "age wrinkles" in the bark, with some sap oozing out and smelling aromatic! Exactly the right "olfactory partner" for the other delightful scents of this garden. The days are cheerful to cloudy, with an occasional brief shower. Then the currants smell particularly aromatic. And of course everything else does too. Floral-cheerful, temptingly "berry," finely mossy. And with the "right wind direction," even slightly "aquatic" scents from the nearby large lake join in. Delicate-cool and moist! Delightful early summer at its finest!

Okay I saw this fragrance recommended on the perfume guy Sebastian thinking oh yeah I’m about to get a banger. Went to the World Trade Center mall Hugo boss and they didn’t have this fragrance for sampling and they didn’t have it available. That should have been the first red flag because who doesn’t have their fragrance available at their store. Anyway at first spray you literally smell absolutely nothing but it’s not a bland nothing it’s a synthetic nothing. It doesn’t smell good it doesn’t smell bad but just nothing. It has no opening there is literally no dry down just nothing and the synthetic nothingness aroma disappears after like two hours. I like Hugo boss but having the audacity to charge $275 for a synthetic nothing smelling fragrance is just outright disrespectful to the consumer it’s a direct insult.

Upon applying "Magnetic Musk | Hugo Boss," I was immediately impressed and also thought of Dior Homme Intense (2011) right away. The longevity on my skin is about 11 to 12 hours with a successful sillage. The top note starts very powdery, spicy, and sweet with a lot of beeswax. In the background, I also catch a hint of citrus from lemon peels. The heart note remains powdery with floral and creamy nuances of iris, violet, and tonka beans. The base offers woody hints of sandalwood with a touch of musk. Yes, Magnetic Musk is truly a great little fragrance. Many thanks to Carsten for the sample.

A three-year-old fragrance from a well-known designer label that has neither a review nor a statement is somewhat surprising. I was also taken aback when I recently found this more exclusive Boss line at Galeria an der Kö in Düsseldorf. It was beautifully presented with photos and chic "scent sticks," but somehow almost inconspicuous. After all, there is quite a large selection of creations in this line, and almost all of them are indeed more than decently made. In particular, this Magnetic Musk has a stunning attraction, as it releases a good amount of beeswax alongside the slightly sweetened musk that gives it its name. It comes across as dry, somewhat bitter, and a bit animalistic, and one might think that there is also some suede leather involved - but that's not the case. The powdery iris initially strongly reminds one of Dior Homme Intense in this combination, but the more the wax comes through, the more one has to chuckle at how misled one feels. Sage plays the least significant role among all the notes. The gentle tonka bean and a bit of sandalwood unfold a little better towards the end. The most dominant accents are set by beeswax, iris, and musk. All in all, it is very high quality, unusual, and brilliantly executed. Wearing it gives one a soothing and elevated feeling, and I think Magnetic Musk is nearly perfect, especially in autumn and winter. But have we already talked about the price? Boss charges over €200 for the The Collection series as a 100 ml EdP. This raises the question of whether this is bold or already megalomaniacal. For my taste, not only should the projection and longevity have been more opulent, but also the bottle, which is reminiscent of the Bottle series and features a significantly thicker glass base and a more textured, higher-quality label, but otherwise does not signal that one wants to compete in the expensive perfume segment. This could be considered understatement or purism, but I would have wished for a more creative bottle for The Collection series. The olfactory result should not fail due to its success, but I am a bit skeptical about that.

Here I am - bored, alone, and with a pile of testers that are just piling up. A lot of Boss, a lot of Diesel... What the big retailers tend to give away. But let's get to the scent: It's short and sweet... Really good! Does it win an award for creativity? No, absolutely not. Nevertheless, it is pleasant, relatively high-quality, and "pleasing". It smells like a cocktail I was served years ago. Champagne mixed with a wine tonic from Austria... VinTonic. It starts off very sparkling and fresh, but becomes more floral and creamy over time. It lasts on my not-so-hairy male arms for about 6 hours and projects quite admirably. Not too much, not too little... Actually perfect for the office and the occasional party if you apply a few extra spritzes. It impresses me so much that I will order it for a good friend’s birthday. The price is more than reasonable with discount codes and is actually a completely safe bet. I can't think of a young woman who wouldn't like this scent. Well done Boss... You can occasionally create quite decent fragrances.

When the new school year began, a big attractive girl appeared as a "repeat student" in our class. She wore her brown hair down to her waist and calmly looked around the classroom with her big eyes. And - oh - she sat down next to me. I felt flattered, as she radiated such self-confidence. She was smart, but not diligent - and when the teachers came at her sharply, she shot back. I was also under her personal protection, and she threw herself in front of me like a lioness in front of her cub when a teacher confronted me. She liked to stand out - and had a charming yet provocative way about her. Moreover, she was never at a loss for words - which annoyed the teachers - but also impressed them. I emulated her - and soon we were both unpopular with the educators. But she taught me to stand up for myself - regardless of the authorities that wanted to make an "x for a u" out of me. So Scandal would have suited her, as she was neither conflict-averse nor did she shy away from confrontations. Because this fragrance also makes its statement - while remaining likable. The tuberose makes a statement, but is softened by the sweet raspberry milk blend. The bright jasmine is prominent and puts its wearer in the spotlight. So Scandal has a mind of its own - without being outright stubborn. By the way, my Anne has become a teacher.

“Scandal” is a fragrance that I have been confronted with for years. My mother wears it often, and it packs a punch: sugary honey galore, making every bee envious. Now, I came across a sample of the new flanker “SO SCANDAL!”... and then also under my nose. The expectation was clear: it will be sweet and heavy, like its predecessor. I was not to be disappointed. As soon as the first whiff of the fragrance hit my nose, an association immediately came to mind. Raspberry bubblegum. Fruity, somewhat synthetic, and sweet. The typical bubblegum note that should be familiar to everyone. After about 15-20 minutes, the scent becomes a bit warmer, a bit more mature - the essence of the predecessor “Scandal” becomes more recognizable. Just without the heavy honey - in “So Scandal,” it’s the raspberry bubblegum note that takes center stage. So the fragrance lingers on my skin. The longevity is perfectly fine - I can still smell it on my skin for 6/7 hours. The sillage is also good, although “Scandal” seems to be a bit more enveloping. "So Scandal!" feels a bit softer to me, the sweetness is less piercing. Nevertheless, the fragrance is only for those who can appreciate scents like "Scandal," "La Vie est Belle," or "Sì." It fits seamlessly into the "sugar bomb" category. I find it quite pleasant; it reminds me scent-wise very much of "Poison Girl" by Dior. Fruity, sweet, warm, playful, and a bit cheeky. Girlish with flair. A good choice for all night owls.

Actually, I was in the mood for vanilla. Sweet, anyway. Preferably distinctly sweet. Autumn is coming, and it’s getting cold and gloomy. One needs a bit of comfort. I tested various fragrances from Jean Paul Gaultier, the two La Belles (also very nice), but the only fragrance without vanilla won the race: So Scandal! Sure, in a way, the scent is a common designer tuberose and nothing you’ve never smelled before. But it’s really beautiful, no overly sweet top notes, not too sticky, no trashy fruitiness in the drydown. Just a creamy raspberry candy that brings joy because it’s so cheeky and uncompromisingly sweet. I can’t help but grin every time I spray it on. I hesitated briefly to buy it, as I’m no longer 20 and wasn’t sure if something like this would suit me. Isn’t such a sweet little fruit a bit overly loud and inelegant? It reminded me of an impossibly neon pink fishnet tights I saw years ago at H&M in London. I instinctively reached for them, but my fun-resistant super-ego wanted to hold back: “They don’t match anything else you have! You’re over 30. What do you want with those?” But I bought them. And I wore them often and loved them madly. They were just fun and made my legs a real eye-catcher. And So Scandal! is just like that. The fragrance is simply fun and frees me from any boring, proper super-ego judgments about what I should appropriately wear. Just follow the intuition of your nose and wear what brings you joy! It’s easily noticeable, lasts well into the day, and is never intrusive. I perceive the milk note subtly as cool and creamy. And it’s not entirely without elegance; sometimes it reminds me just a tiny bit of Rouge Malachite… well, the affordable, more girlish H&M version of it, so to speak. And the bottle! Cheeky, unique, and somehow funny, like a crazy dive into a barrel of perfume. For me, it also represents this slightly absurd passion for perfume that has taken hold of me for a few months now. It’s so much fun and so unreasonable, perhaps even a little scandalous for the “inner accountant” in me, and I can’t stop. What can I say? So Scandal!

I have to say, I have absolutely fallen for JPG fragrances, especially lately. Each one I have tested so far is truly something special and always worth a "head-turner". And So Scandal is no different. While browsing in the perfume store, I casually sprayed it on my hand and moved on, as I was actually looking to snag a different fragrance that day. But on the way back, I kept thinking, "hmm, it smells so deliciously like grapes here." Yes, to me it actually smells like grape candies. So good. I've been searching for something like this for a long time. Grape flavor/scent is unfortunately much too rare in candies, etc. 1-2 weeks later, the treasure was also in my collection :D Now that I read the notes here, it must be the raspberry that I smell so intensely. Paired with jasmine, this creates an unbelievably sweet and seductive scent that makes me feel sexy and well-groomed. When it gets to the base notes, it even becomes slightly smoky-woody. Longevity and sillage are, as one is used to from JPG, simply strong. I can only recommend it to you :)

I tested so scandal because I like raspberry and milk and knew those were ingredients. I was not disappointed. So scandal is mega fruity and smells incredibly strong. You really don't need to spray much. This is also the only scandal I like. For me, so scandal is for spring/summer, while la Belle is for autumn/winter. Anyone who likes sweet and fruity should definitely give it a sniff.

This scent is very present and should not be overdone. This perfume is quite the cheeky little fruit. Right from the first seconds, a delicious fruity sweetness spreads. But not like the original scent "Scandal | Jean Paul Gaultier," no, this fragrance is much lighter and also "younger." It smells delicious, the raspberry really fulfills its mission well and scandalously!

And once again something with orange blossom... I can't stand it in many fragrances, especially in combination with tuberose... it can sometimes come off so stuffy and old-fashioned... I wouldn't have even looked at this scent again, even if it contains raspberry and milk, I would still be unconvinced and further put off, especially since I can't stand the regular "scandal.

I dedicate my first comment to a fragrance that is very special to me. If I were asked for a short statement about the scent without personal associations, I would probably say: The scent is just as annoying in the long run as the corresponding song: "pink fluffy unicorns dancing on rainbows" Or maybe "Smells like pink children's bath concentrate.

Pleasant yes, nice too. Sweet...sure...flattering. You definitely won't offend anyone. An almost "always wearable" scent. Except at 35 degrees in the shade. It has a slight pencil note on my skin, which I don't find disadvantageous. However: I unfortunately don't smell any raspberry. The longevity is average for me. I don't perceive a nice development, on the contrary.

I tested it for the first time in summer and the scent had something. I found it good and interesting. Now in winter, during the 2nd and 3rd test, I found the scent simply piercing and synthetic. Completely unpleasant and I was very surprised that a scent can become so negatively affected by the weather. I have never experienced such a drastic change before!

That is, what should be all fragrance flankers, an interpretation of the original. No, bring to the market flanker that have nothing to do with their mother fragrances, just to take advantage to sell the name or the prestige created by the origin fragrance. "Le Male Terrible" is the original aroma with a few touches that are fresher, lighter, a less complex fragrance, but of an olfactory quality comparable to the original "Le Male". From the beginning you can see the DNA "Le Male", that characteristic vanilla lavender with warm touches of precious amber, but at the start it is fresher for the grapefruit, even fleetingly fruity and pungent for the pink pepper, then the aroma melts with a touch of vetiver, but nothing remarkable, being at all times the protagonists of the aroma lavender, vanilla and amber. The truth is that, not to be a lover of the original aroma, I liked it, it seemed simply more versatile and fresh. The performance is very good, being quite durable on my skin, with a duration of about 8 hours or so, and a moderate wake from the beginning, although a little more noticeable in the first hour of application. For me, it is much more versatile than the original, being able to use it at any station and time of day, in this aspect I do not see any noticeable glitch. One curious thing is his name, "Terrible", and that's why I expected it to be more intense than the original, but it has not been like that, it's much cooler, so I do not understand what "Terrible" is, anyway, it's a very recommended perfume. Very good Flanker of "Le Male", but the best. Sorry for my bad english.

Le Male was a milestone in the fragrance world, a fragrance that is relevant today however, it became a victim of its own success and was also damaged by constant reformulations. It's been copied by everyone and overplayed. Le Male Terrible keeps the DNA but changes just enough to make the fragrance new and exciting. The note breakdown is far simpler and replaces the bergamot in the opening with a very noticeable grapefruit that shines in the opening but . Longevity is above average, projection is good but the scent is what really brings me back to Le Male Terrible. Just as the bottle, this fragrances is an edgier version of Le Male

Francis Kurkdjian, the creator of Le Male, recently modernized his Fleur du Male, also released by JPG, and launched it as Custo Man under a different brand. Apparently, JPG could not win him over for the modernization of the long-running Le Male. Here, Aurelien Guichard took the reins, who has made a name for himself with Andy Warhol's Silver Factory from Bond No. 9 or the Unidentified Fragrance Object from Kenzo. And Le Male is in dire need of modernization. Just recently, I encountered it again at a gas station, where an alcoholic was drinking his cheap beer. His exhalations mingled with a penetrating Le Male cloud. Le Male is as dead today as this person will sadly likely be soon. In the facelift, Aurelien Guichard has borrowed or drawn inspiration from elsewhere. On one hand, from the new Infusion de Vetiver by Prada, and on the other, from Mr. Kurkdjian's modernization of Fleur du Male. But let's take it step by step. Right from the first spray, I noticed a similarity with Custo Man. Specifically, a certain fresh cologne note. This is also present in Fleur du Male, where it takes on an opulent floral direction, while in Custo Man it develops fresh and green. Clearly, Le Male Terrible takes a step towards Fleur du Male/Custo Man, and that's not a mistake. Cologne notes are top notes, and so it is here. It's just the starter. What remains, however, is a green touch from the vetiver noted here as well. This initially takes a back seat in the fragrance development, only to present itself again in the drydown. Some cedarwood could also be involved in this note. Just like with Infusion de Vetiver, with which Prada recently modernized its successful fragrance Infusion d'Homme in such an interesting way. This idea is simply too good to be limited to one fragrance. So far, so good. But Aurelien Guichard has set further accents for which I can't think of a template. I perceive a distinctly animalistic note. Whether this is due to the interplay of vetiver and the Le Male base accord, I cannot say. Civet is not listed, but this smells, especially in the heart note, a bit like the Cologne Zoo, department wild cats. Moreover, there are traces of a fruity acidity that endures through the top and only disappears in the drydown. However, I perceive it less as grapefruit - as indicated. It is fruitier, more like apple cider. And this creates an interesting symbiosis with the vanilla component of the Le Male base tone, somewhat like the acidity in Montale's Boisé Vanillée, which is otherwise a completely different perfume. In the drydown, which begins after 2 hours, the vetiver note significantly modifies the Le Male base accord. I have the impression that Le Male Terrible stays much closer to the body and does not tend to form clouds like the original - a blessing for the troubled humanity! I want to return to Infusion de Vetiver. I described it in my comment as the ideal office variant of Infusion d'Homme. Does this also apply to Le Male Terrible in relation to Le Male? Well, only in emergencies, and for two reasons. On one hand, this variant is also clearly Le Male and as such simply too expressive for boring offices. This is especially true for the middle part of the fragrance development. On the other hand, the drydown with the vetiver dominance sets in too early for me, namely after just 2 hours. The great thing about Infusion de Vetiver or the similarly designed English Breakfast by Mark Buxton is that you have the freshness in the morning and in the evening, the cedarwood-vetiver power delivers another energy boost. But for that, Eau de Parfum strength is needed, and Le Male Terrible does not have that. It is not up to this brilliant office fragrance concept. Thus, Le Male Terrible leaves me somewhat perplexed. The name is pure marketing, as it suggests something even crazier than Le Male. For that, the wild cat note should have been more pronounced. Le Male Terrible is a Le Male that reaches out in three very different directions: noble cologne-freshness in the top, animalistic in the heart, dark vetiver-wood note in the base. Not that all of this doesn't harmonize well - but it is too complex to be labeled. It is not a functional fragrance (office, evening, etc.). I think Le Male Terrible is best suited as an alternative for die-hard Le Male fans who critically view the strong proliferation of Le Male, yet cannot let go of it themselves. Sorry for the many name drops, but it had to be done here.

Then I’ll get started on my first Parfumo comment. A little backstory: I am a big fan of Le Mâle (even though this masterpiece is often ridiculed in the Parfumo community ;-)). As with every birthday, my mother gifted me a bottle of this elixir, hoping to bring me a little joy. She succeeded! I was surprised back then (2010) by the razor blade around the sailor's neck, but I placed the bottle, unopened and unnoticed, next to my nearly full 200 ml bottle. Months passed, and so did my Le Mâle supply. But then my mother's gift smiled at me, still sitting unopened. My practiced fingers opened the bottle, and a spray of the magic potion clouded my neck. Question marks. Silence. Something was different. I examined the packaging and saw that it was Le Mâle Terrible. In the room was a familiar yet unusual scent. There was a daring citrus note that I didn’t know from the standard work of JPG. Like the good old black leather jacket that turns a banker into a daring and mysterious stranger in seconds. Now and then, I treat myself to a spray of this three-day stubble in a bottle. It doesn’t turn me into a daring stranger, but it transforms my beloved Le Mâle into an olfactory leather jacket.

"Terrible," French for: Bad, terrible, awful, fantastic, great, sensational, cool, dreadful, fearsome, massively intense, grim - severe, devastating. I think you can criticize the fragrance for many things, as some do: swimming through the sweetness of the mainstream, being quite similar to the original, being a bit weaker than the original (vintage)... But one thing you cannot accuse it of: that it doesn't live up to its name. And I don't mean that negatively at all.. I have had this fragrance for quite a while (in terms of my Parfumo time..). I must admit, I haven't worn it for a while, but I've always known that I wouldn't part with it; it has a fixed place in my collection. When I tested it "hardcore" back then, I wore it heavily - even overdosed while exercising (alone, not in the gym or anywhere where I could torture people with it..), which I sometimes do with fragrances to find out where their soul lies. It works great with sports because the heat and sweat bring the fragrance into a different working area; perfumes really come alive and express themselves, as if you were breaking them down. And from that experience, I can tell you, you CAN overdose this fragrance. I find it even easier than with the original Le Male. Back to the name and the fragrance. The name and the design of the bottle (translucent blue with worn stripes) and the box (in black) already tell its story; it's supposed to be a dirtier "Bad Boy" version of Le Male. Like torn jeans or something.. RogerWilco put it nicely, I think: "Leather jacket and a cigarette in the corner of the mouth." And that’s exactly what the fragrance represents for me. It has this vanilla-lavender-amber trio that makes it somehow pretty and beautiful at its core, but here it has been enriched with grapefruit, pepper, and vetiver, which makes it a bit rougher, edgier, and less likable than Le Male. Beautifully "edgy"... Le Male, on the other hand, seems really smooth and lovely to me! And I don't know if the reduction in performance (or adjustment to the weak reformulated Le Male performance) was intentional, but for me, this fragrance would be too intense if it were stronger... As it is now, you can distribute it a bit better with several sprays over the body, achieving a more even distribution. I have just rediscovered it after a long time, and I find it really, really cool. It is somehow different due to this olfactory plot twist, and its casual nature makes it really interesting to smell. I completely understand this "Terrible" term; if you apply a bit too much, you still want to keep smelling it because the notes are somehow addictive - but at the same time, it's too much and somewhat intrusive. Because then a citrus sharpness cuts through the vanilla, which can be a bit cloying. I really believe this is a fragrance that could draw a lot of attention through its sillage, because you feel even more than with "Le Male" that sensation of "WHAT WAS THAT SMELL? WHO WAS THAT? I NEED TO SMELL IT AGAIN." Please don't take my words too literally... but I find it really underrated and timeless. With its slightly fresher appearance, I could also imagine that it would be very useful in summer. And now that "Dior Sauvage" has made pepper mass appealing again, you probably get twice the recognition from people as before. Whether that matters to you or not, it's just the fashion phenomenon. I think if Le Male Terrible could express its opinion, it would say, "I don't really care if others like me... I don't even want everyone to like me." *Grins, lights a cigarette, and leans coolly against the Shelby Mustang GT500* ;)

After I extensively tested Le Mâle recently, I couldn't resist trying its younger offspring Le Mâle Terrible and the limited summer edition Le Mâle Summer 2015 today. And both can be recognized at the base by whose children they are - the tried-and-true vanilla that has made Le Mâle appealing to men in mass.

At the beginning, I would like to wish all readers - and of course the entire community - a pleasant Good Friday. After a somewhat longer abstinence from parfumo, I thought I would write another review comment following the "Reflection Man 45" comment. Now it's vacation, I have a bit more time, and I can finally get down to business here in the forum ... on Good Friday.

When I started my new hobby of perfumes a year ago, Le Male was of course well-known and liked, but I had never owned it. However, it was such a classic that it was clear that at some point, the blue sailor bottle had to adorn my perfume display; it is a must-have for every perfume collector to have owned it at least once.

Well, Le Male still evokes a lot of controversy. When Le Male Terrible came out, it was touted as an extreme version of the original. Although I never really liked Le Male, my curiosity was very high, and I tested it. I liked it right away. The bottle hasn't changed much, except for the razor blade as a necklace. It still looks very kitschy and gross, but the sprayer is great!

Off the beaten paths of the seaside, only entrepreneurial risks lurk. So, Gaultier has now crossed his headless bust with the commercial art genes of the "fresh" type to also reach the last, still unconverted fragrance customers in the vanilla pod core business.

Here it is, the offshoot of the original. But can it hold its own against it? The opening seems to be a bit fruitier than in the original DNA. Quite pleasant, and that remains the case for quite a while. This fragrance stays almost consistently true to its line and changes very little. Only much later does it appear spicier to me due to the leather note, which gradually takes over without standing out too much. And now I really like it. It feels pleasant to me; one could almost call this development of the fragrance boring. For me, it is not; I appreciate its clarity, and it is a nice companion for daily use at work. The sillage and longevity are not outstanding; after about 3-4 hours, it is only perceptible close to the skin. In my opinion, it does not come close to the original, but it is certainly a noteworthy little brother!

Postscript: ..........Could it simply not suit my skin chemistry? Has the manufacturing process been altered or has it always been different here? The other scents and Bosses have never been convincing on my skin either.... Please keep this in mind, but: a review is a review after all. Now, to the point! A hint of disappointment, or rather a hint of nothing? The description of the sample tells a tale of "sharp interpretation of the oriental original," "stimulating ginger," "sensual suede accord." Admittedly, there is sharpness, and the accord is pleasant. But let's take it step by step! I spray it on and smell diffuse, unrecognizable, fruity sweetness. The aroma of the Maninka fruit is said by some sources to be like strawberry and chocolate, while others claim it resembles passion fruit and rum. My skin reflects none of that! Unrecognizable fruit, certainly no stone fruit, none of our native berries, really nothing identifiable......and along with it, a sharpness. No, even the ginger is not very recognizable; the note tree could almost indicate chili instead. The top notes, nonsense, the scent itself doesn’t last long anyway, close to the skin in less than an hour. Luckily, sometimes a dusty, almost scratchy acidity emerges. Shy as it may be, the drydown is pleasant, reminding me of Valentino Uomo. Thanks to Yatagan for this! The tip to test more on paper helps to better understand the scents. Pure Accord shows a noticeably more pleasant opening, a bit more sharpness alongside a beautiful citrus bouquet. Still feels half-finished, as if a counterbalance has been forgotten. Fortunately, here it is so weak that it hardly matters. In short: (For me?!) An indecisive little water with little presence. What do you think? Is it the skin chemistry? Lack of creativity in the industry? Having tested it negatively multiple times, at least I am ;D

Without being a lover of "Le Male", and not for fragrant reasons, but for saturation. I know a friend who wore it in large quantities, and not the watery formula of now, but the original primal, imagine what it was like to be close to this friend hahaha, that's how I ended up, hating it. Well, the fact is that Le Beau Male I like it, it moves away from the original proposal to offer us a more herbal and fresh aroma, although it does not lose that imprint of the original that makes you know what you are wearing. In the beginning, he presents his DNA "Le Male", and offers us a mixture of lavender, mint and some absinthe that is very reminiscent of the original, but less sweet and somewhat greener. Then, little by little, the orange blossom and sage are taking body on a bed of musk, which, along with a touch of lavender and residual mint, create an illusion very herbal and fresh, something soapy and pristine cleanliness. In the drying, the musk is winning the battle to the rest of notes, increasing that sensation of aromatic cleanliness, and without many more changes, the aroma finishes dying flush of skin slowly. The perfume I liked, starts with a certain resemblance to the original and then take a different path, much cooler, but something happens with it, and that being a flanker of the original, and being one of the most imitated perfumes and copied from the world, I get the feeling that I carry a bad imitation of any house that has tried to copy "Le Male", I do not know, it's just a sensation and it does not take away any merits, just that I have that impression when I wear it, in fact , my brother bought an imitation of "Le Male" from a well-known franchise and I think it looks more like this "Le Beau Male" than "Le Male" himself. The performance is moderate in both cases, with a duration between 6 or 7 hours in my skin, and a very noticeable wake in the first half hour, then down to moderate and there it stays, gradually falling to die level with skin. The proper use of this perfume I see between spring and summer, taking the warm part of autumn, it is a fresh and very diurnal aroma, but that is already a matter of everyone. I, honestly, if you are a user of "Le Male", and you want to continue using it in the summer, with the current reformulation you have to spare, this perfume seems redundant and dispensable, even though I like it. Sorry for my bad english.

The funky wormwood opening will probably shock those expecting just the slight variation which is common for quite a few of the Le Male Flankers. Somewhat animalic musk is the star of the show supported by a sweetish green warm mint. Drydown is addictive if musk is your thing. Reminds me of A&F Fierce and Creed GIT. Was ridiculously good VFM until discontinued (bought 75ml BNIB for like 25USD shipped in July 2021), now it seems to be more tricky to find and prices are way up. This one, Superman Eau Fraiche and Fleur du Male are my favorites of the line. Francis Kurkdjin stepped out of the box a bit with this one and it is all the better for it. Under appreciated scent and I would not be very surprised to see this one become sought after over time.

I don't get why LBM gets so much hate, I actually wanted to hate it because of its bad reputation but since I bought it last week it's on speed dial (December is very sunny in Costa Rica). It is simple and linear but that's what I expected and it's fine consindering how nice the opening is. A nice mint and lavander splash, very refreshing Update I got awful performance when I first got it or so I recall but I'm getting 7 hrs out of it with decent projection so no complaints in the performance field. A good addition to the Le Male family

we are in a completely different world smelling the original le male that was a real perfume with a certain karma and credibility during the years ,if this is intended to potentiate a men sex appeal and erotic potential i stand astonished .... chemical means erotic ? in wich way ... this is an horrible ,incredibly sinthetic perfume i can't believe a mature and sexy man could wear this kind of crap ,imho another poor sibling of the awful acqua di giò

I got this as a sample in another frag's order. I have to say that I am a little underwhelmed. To me ,it just smells like a generic 80s cologne that has a shower gel vibe and and fresh impression. Nothing full bottle worthy. But again, it's just my opinion. I have definitely smelled this before on someone I just can't recall where and who

I tested this out at the drugstore today. Smells very generic and boring to me. Really nothing special. The scent is like a million other colognes out there right now. Something new and unique would have been nice. I'll pass on this one!

Since this fragrance is, in my opinion, unjustly rated so poorly, I would like to share my thoughts on it here. I really can't understand why there are so many negative reviews for this scent. I think it probably has to do with the obvious comparison to the original Le Male, which is loved by many.

A new Le Male fragrance, and this time personally from Kurkdjian. This is definitely one of the biggest events of the still young perfume year, and I have finally tested it. Le Male is a classic, Terrible is still good, but opinions differ on that, and there has been very little change.

Now one can no longer claim that the Le Mâle variants are as alike as two peas in a pod. To my knowledge, for the first time, JPG has packed a completely different fragrance into the sailor torso. There may be overlaps in the target audience, even in the concept, but not in the scent in the strict sense.

With Le Mâle, the French fashion designer Jean Paul Gaultier has probably released the most successful and well-known perfume of recent years. Hardly anyone can say they don't know the scent! Moreover, there are several fragrance copies from other manufacturers.

Sweet, spicy date, party, and club scents for men are as plentiful as sand on the beach (well, business freshies are even more common). So what could Hugo Intense possibly add? The opening is very typical. Spicy with a decent dose of sweetness. Cinnamon is clearly present, but the remaining notes don't explain the scent impression. But then: What is that? Something green? What is that doing here? It comes across less as old-fashioned and rough, and more as refined and grassy. It complements the composition - and quite well! Here, modernity meets classic, and they enhance each other excellently. A regular scent with a cool twist. As it develops, the green note increases and becomes more robust, while the sweetness decreases; the spiciness remains. It's a shame, because this shifts the balance towards the old-fashioned and makes it significantly less enjoyable than the refreshingly different start. The sillage is really good, no surprise for an EdP Intense. It lasts a solid 6 hours, then it fades, and after 9 hours it is gone. The bottle is definitely one of the cooler ones in the Hugo Eau de Toilette line. The dark red background with black accents works great. The bottle itself is a matter of taste. I still find it okay, but elegant is (of course) something else. Hugo Intense is a successful, because unusual scent for parties and dates. It complements the selection of different scents for these purposes quite well. However, in my opinion, the development should have better maintained the balance between old and new. Therefore, I will not be getting it. nulltheless: Those who like sweet-spicy scents but have been missing a bit of green should give the new Hugo a chance.

Recently, I tested the Hugo Boss Intense EDP at the local perfumery, but I didn't arrive at any conclusion that satisfied me. So the salesperson gave me a sample to take home. First of all, yes, if any perfume should ever live up to its name, it would be this one. Intense might even be an understatement here. Even Joop Homme smells conservatively unobtrusive in comparison. In the perfumery, I sprayed a small puff onto a test strip. At that point, I wasn't completely overwhelmed by the sweet scent; I even found it quite pleasant. However, when I used the sample at home and sprayed it on my skin, it behaved quite differently. In no time at all, I transformed into a walking perfumery. The sweet, fruity scent quickly turned into something very overpowering. This results in a scent trail that is definitely noticeable to others. To achieve a truly acceptable result, one really has to be careful with the dosage. The scent is definitely long-lasting, and Hugo Boss Intense has no intention of leaving you anytime soon. For me, it was simply way too much all at once. The EDP has potential in itself. A slightly less intense version I might even consider successful. But as the scent stands now, it is absolutely not for me. It lacks elegance and a certain maturity. The EDP smells too much like adolescence and not like an adult man who has already traveled some miles in life, which is a shame.

The scent is rated much too poorly in some reviews, I think it's a fantastic designer fragrance. The opening is very sweet, yes also synthetic, but I find the scent so lovely after a few minutes... in the drydown, thyme and leather also come through... very successful, I think it's a beautiful thing...️ I can easily imagine that this will become a frequently worn daily fragrance for spring and autumn... bravo Hugo!

After reviewing the Narcisse Eau de Toilette today, I now turn to the Narcisse Parfum . In the end, I am definitely more taken with the parfum. I find the scent to be more intense, but also more oriental and spicier. The longevity is really good at 8 hours + X. After showering, I can still smell a pleasant breeze up close. The sillage is also quite decent. The top note offers a strong stone fruit in the form of apricots. It again smells soapy and beautifully floral with daffodils, frangipani, and jasmine blossoms. In the heart note, alongside fruity, soapy, and floral hints of orange blossoms and rose water, there is also a spicy oriental touch in the form of cloves and cinnamon. Unfortunately, the scent comes across as somewhat piercing and earthy at times. The base is again soapy and fruity with aromas of bourbon vanilla, tolu balsam, sandalwood, and an animalistic musk note. If the heart note hadn't been so earthy and somewhat unpleasant, I would have likely given an even better rating here. Overall, it is still a pretty good scent.

When my girls and I were out and about, we played the cheerful game: People Watching. This means - we observed our fellow humans - especially the gentlemen of creation. So we sat - like jurors - in our box - that is, club seating - and exchanged our judgments. Andrea was always very engaged - and if she liked a man, she would pinch me - ouch - in the arm and purr like a cat. If a gentleman did not meet her taste, she would make a face and grumble: A cold sip of cocoa. We didn’t always agree - but with The Scent Intense, we did. This fragrance is definitely a "warm sip of cocoa" - made from the bittersweet cocoa powder from Bensdoorp. Dark chocolate envelops me richly - without being sticky. Soft peach is drizzled with honey, and noble osmanthus provides casual elegance. Mild vanilla floats above - forming a harmonious unity with the bitter cocoa note. An unusual, interesting scent - alluring, with "snuggling" tendencies. Not a gourmand - but still very appetizing. The husband acknowledges it with a nod - and Andrea purrs in response. Music: The Year of the Cat by Al Stewart

This comment won't please all the highly demanding perfume enthusiasts who seek their scent salvation in the complexity of various fragrances (especially niche ones, as hard to find as possible and definitely not mundane), but I don't care. It's a shame that this cozy scent is received so poorly by many here. Yes, it is sweet (you can see that right away from the fragrance pyramid). Yes, it is simple (it consists of only 5 fragrance notes). And yes, it does not undergo any development. All completely correct. But does that make it a bad scent? No. It is exactly what you expect. Predictable. It is cozy, warm, and sweet. And exactly what is criticized about its development is what I like so much about it. I spray, I sniff, and I like it. Right away! And just the same. And half an hour later still. What good is a scent that I don't even want to smell on myself, freshly sprayed, just because it might "develop so wonderfully" at some point? Anyway, I like it very much, and my husband even more. The only downside is its rather lower longevity and sillage. Boss unfortunately hasn't noticeably improved that with the Intense either.

The original "The Scent" already captivated me in some way - I bought it last year in late summer and used it for weeks afterward; while it’s not a perfume that blows you away completely, it still received many compliments and I felt great wearing it. I even bought the matching shower gel. When the bottle was empty, I knew: You have to get this again; preferably in 100ml size! :-) A few weeks ago, "Boss The Scent Intense" made it onto my wishlist and I knew I would buy it anyway... Although Boss fragrances are often dismissed here as boring, uninspired, mainstream, poorly lasting, annoying - in short, just bad - I have to disagree. I have also been using Boss Femme for over three years and as long as it remains in the lineup, I will continue to repurchase it. Long story short: The Scent Intense smells almost exactly like its predecessor, just stronger and sweeter. The peach hits hard and overall the scent is very sweet - the longevity and sillage are stronger than in the EdP 1. If you don’t like the first one, you shouldn’t even bother testing this one. The first edition is considerably more subtle - but this one is called "Intense" for a reason ;-) See the title - the peach is slightly tipsy and sultry. Fruity-sweet for summer/late summer and autumn. Also very fitting in spring. Not so much for cold days. It’s also suitable for spritzing on boring Sundays while lounging on the couch. In my opinion, Boss fragrances are perfect for everyday wear; they are certainly not perfumes that stand out greatly or make you want to know their names after someone walks by wearing them. Still, they always fit. You definitely don’t need both The Scent editions. When my 30ml bottle is empty, I will consider which one to repurchase. Have fun testing :-) _______________________________________________________________________________ This perfume is very well received by those around me; many have already asked what I’m wearing... And that’s how it should be ;-)

Why do they dump a truckload of sugar or syrup to all their fragrances? Original Le Male isn't too sweet but after that: Ultra Male, Le Parfum, Elixir, Lover, etc... they are all kinda good but so sweet they are almost unwearable, specially for summer frags. I love Le Male, Terrible and Eau Fraiche though. This one would've been awesome if they toned down the sweetness in like, half

Ahh, another year and another release after release from Gaultier. I really do not care about the other people’s comments especially for Gaultier. Gaultier m…riders are the only people that possess even more uneducated noses than Sauvage edt glazers. Sure, Gaultier has some amazing fragrances like Le Male Le Parfum, Scandal Le Parfum and Le Beau Le Parfum but also has some fragrances that are just overhyped. Ultramale is a over-sweet, extremely offensive and synthetic mess, Le Male Elixir is again over-sweet and extremely offensive mess but actually smells good, Le Male OG is an outdated barbershop fragrance and scandal absolu is a armani you ripoff. So, I was excited for Le Male Lover because those m…rider gaultier fans probably couldn’t like this fragrance because it was not a synthetic and over sweet mess but actually a good one and… I WAS RIGHT! Le Male Lover starts just right amount of white pepper that gives a fresh-spicy feeling, then becomes a cold and sweet fragrance with ambergris and leaves it’s place for classic Gaultier vanilla. So simple yet so good. Performance is also quite good, lasting slightly more than 8 hour mark with a strong projection. Fragrance will be ok for any season and any occasion, even though I think it might smell a bit too sweet for high-extreme weather. The only con I can say about the fragrance is it’s just right on the middle in terms of characteristic. Does this fragrance wants to be a summer or a winter one? I don’t know. Is it versatile? Versatile enough to wear it on both summer and winter. Also, in terms of “syntheticness” ambergris here is clearly made through processing ambroxan but you wouldn’t expect a designer brand to use real ambergris so I guess that’s okay. The price is REALLY expensive, I am not going to pay more than 100 euros for a 125 bottle. (The price I saw was 112 frank in Switzerland which worths about 117 euro.) if you can find it for cheap, I would recommend a purchase. But since it is a limited edition, it is not even available in my country. Maybe I will get a sample from a tester bottle when I visit another country. This fragrance was the one that should have gotten the hype, not coconut, aquatic green synthetic sweet fragrance that screams “Cool Water Intense ahhhhh” fragrance called Le Beau Green Paradise.

A new year, a new Le Male flanker. For me as a JPG (Bisch) fanboy, that's not bad news, as my fan heart jumps a little higher with joy. I just love JPG, let me be! Currently, the fragrance is still relatively hard to get, as it is not available through the German JPG website or German online/offline perfumeries. And although I have seen some video and text reviews from mostly English-speaking critics in the meantime, which have all been rather mixed, I thought to myself, "Oh come on, what the heck, I'll just order it quickly from Italy and test it myself." Said and done, and to give a little preview: I'm glad I did. Because no review has yet captured the scent for me as I perceive the new Le Male Lover. And we will get to that now. Right when I sprayed it, it shot through my mind: "Huh? You know this scent? I wore it a lot in winter?!" Confused, I tried to connect the smell with a fragrance from my collection. And then it clicked: "Invictus Victory Elixir | Paco Rabanne"! The opening and the middle remind me of a slightly fresher version of Rabanne's Victory Elixir. The same vanilla/coconut note that reminds me of some vanilla-scented candles. For me, it's incredibly great, just a bit fresher than the "original." If you don't know the Rabanne scent: Cool Water Intense also goes in this direction, but the Rabanne scent is much closer than the Cool Water, as it has more vanilla than coconut. In the middle to dry down, my nose also picks up a bit of "1 Million Parfum | Paco Rabanne," fruity bubblegum sweetness with a slight peppery freshness that smells minimally minty. Great combo. Imagine Mentos. A new flavor of Mentos: Vanilla Coconut Mentos. And they consist of 3/6 vanilla-coconut, 2/6 are the old classic fruit Mentos, and 1/6 are the classic mint Mentos. And voila: Le Male Lover Mentos is created. I like it, because I really enjoy both 1M Parfum and Victory Elixir and consider them the best of their respective (commercially available) lines. But Rabanne doesn't seem to fare well in general, judging by comments and reviews; I just wonder how the fragrances manage to be so mainstream when no one likes them; but that's another topic. After I had sampled the V Elixir, I immediately had to get a bottle. I find the vanilla note in it very great, and even my wife, who is really the number one critic when it comes to fragrances, approved of the scent because it reminds her of scented massage candles for adult use and thus associates something pleasant with it. What more could a man want :D But back to Le Male Lover: Actually, this is not surprising at all, because Rabanne and JPG share some of the same perfumers with Raynaud and Bisch. So I simply claim that 1M was created with Le Male as a model, Bisch then refined 1M Elixir into Le Male Elixir, and now finally found "inspirations" in Victory Elixir and mixed it with his 1M Parfum into the new Le Male Lover. Do you believe this story is true? On the other hand, it could also... While everything from Rabanne comes across as "coarser," the JPG fragrances seem a bit finer and more balanced to me. The only downside is: Rabanne seems to be setting the trend now (or the perfumers are experimenting), and JPG picks up the ideas and refines them. Of course, mass-appeal DNA is its great-grandfather, but: not very innovative. On the other hand: Le Male Lover replaces two Rabanne perfumes (Victory Elixir and 1M Parfum) for me in one fell swoop. Because honestly, I would prefer to wear Le Male Lover over either of the two, as it simply comes across as more interesting and refined, not so youthful and in-your-face. I see Le Male Lover in spring/fall and possibly still in winter, rather than in summer. For summer, then only in the evenings/nights, during the day the scent might be too heavy/sweet even though it radiates a bit of tropical vibes. Longevity for me is more than okay with 6+ hours for the price of 85,- (including shipping) for 125ml, and it lasts significantly longer on clothing. In the first hours, it also has good projection (about 2-3 hours). Here, the two Rabannes unfortunately have the edge, but they are also significantly sweeter and less fresh. So it's somewhat understandable. Did JPG do themselves a favor with the packaging and presentation? Because it rather reminds me of a blue, fresh aquatic; and in my opinion, you get 0.0% of that here, as the scent is vanilla/coconut/fruity sweet and only offers minimal freshness through the mint. I believe a different branding like Le Beau (tropical green) would have suited it better. Although the original Le Male is already green (and Aviator) and would probably have raised false expectations again... And the name itself is somehow... difficult? If someone were to ask me what I'm wearing, I find the answer with that name somehow "unintentionally funny." Especially since "Lover" also suggests that one loves Le Male and it might be a homage/reissue to the OG; which it definitely is not. Le Male Tropical, Le Male Springbreak or something along those lines would have been more sensible names. For marketing, this time it's a flat 6, fail, missing the point. To sum up: Le Male Lover is for me a great spring/fall scent and is indeed the link between Elixir (winter) and Le Beau Paradise Garden (summer). Not innovative at all, but for me the better version of the two originals from Rabanne. Unfortunately, Le Male Lover has little Le Male DNA (except for minimal peppery mint subtly in the background of the vanilla/coconut/fruity bubblegum sweetness) and rather reminds me of a very good Rabanne scent. If you want Le Male, you will be disappointed; if you want a good, mass-appeal scent: Cheers Le Male Lover. One thing is as certain for me as Amen in church: I need at least 1-2 bunker bottles of this limited edition. I would be quite sad if it ever runs out and is no longer available, and I haven't said that about InTheNavy, Aviator, and OnBoard. However, Le Male Lover is also not an Eau Fraiche. Those expecting that will also be disappointed. But for anyone wanting a "Best Of" Rabanne for spring/fall from the house of JPG: You are in the right place. Puig won't care anyway, they own both :D And I'm just happy that I like a scent, innovation or not, because as the saying goes: Better well stolen than poorly made yourself.

I break a lance. Le Mâle Lover currently stands at 7.1 and enjoys little enthusiasm - yet 'Lover' is truly a great fragrance! I unmistakably perceive the modern Le Male DNA, which I know and love from Le Mâle Le Parfum ! Masculine sweetness, no Bubble Gum, but mature, established sweetness. Dominance flanked by motivation and seduction. Self-assured, attractive, not abrasive, but pleasing. Le Mâle Lover is an all-rounder that, in my view, always works - although in the depths of winter, Le Mâle Le Parfum might indeed take over. In a manageable dosage, Le Mâle Lover works in the office and, at higher concentrations, of course also in the evening hours. Even in the scorching heat of summer, I can easily imagine it - it will be tested live this year! So why the previously weak rating? Yes, the initial impression is 'shower gel scent' - but that's just the first. The second is directly a seductive Le Male. But it is indeed simple, and that doesn't always suffice for an experienced perfume nose. Its simplicity also makes it so versatile. Every weakness is also a strength... Don't let yourself be framed, ignore the rating, test the fragrance once and again, and I am sure that Le Mâle Lover will please many. Let's see if we can still reach 8.X over the course of the year! EDIT: Regarding the coconut: Yes, there is definitely a coconut accord noticeable. However, it is a creamy coconut, not a fruity one like Virgin Island Water .

Hello everyone, A few weeks ago, I learned that there is a new flanker (once again^^) of the Le Mâle Eau de Toilette line and, well, I'm less than impressed, because how many more years can this go on? And somehow my expectations weren't that high... Besides, I saw the fragrance pyramid and thought (based on that) it would go in the direction of Le Mâle Terrible ... Resolution - no! He hasn't reinvented the wheel and there are no innovations or anything memorable... nothing. And now for the BUT... It's good, not damn good, not exceptionally good, it’s good! It’s pleasant, nice, has (of course) a current Le Mâle Eau de Toilette vibe + a certain light vacation/well-being note of Le Beau Mâle = just really nice and better than Le Beau Mâle ! It has something fresh, something clean, and a slightly sweet but not annoying touch, and I personally consider it one of the better releases from the house in recent years. When + where? Almost always and for any occasion, well, maybe not at 30°C and above, but otherwise it really works anytime. And my experiences at work (both genders, tested for 2 weeks as always) were very positive! So I can't report anything bad! Do you absolutely need it? No? NO, but you definitely won't go wrong with it. (So I do like it...) If I really weren't convinced, I wouldn't recommend it to you! (At least for a test) And now have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______

Let's start with the bottle: A beautiful blue bottle with black tattoo patterns. The sprayer doesn't really match in silver. I would have found it brilliant to make the sprayer in the blue of the bottle. But you can't have everything. The packaging is, as always, simply fantastic from Jean Paul Gaultier and belongs to the few outer packages worth keeping.

Le Male Lover doesn't do anything groundbreaking, but it doesn't have to. It smells solid and quite good. I can't really recognize the typical Le Male DNA, but there is a twist to Le Beau. At least that's how I feel with this sample. The fragrance starts off slightly refreshed, but immediately with a certain sweetness.

New Day, New Flanker. The Le Male Lover is an interesting scent - positively put, it is versatile; negatively put, it doesn't know what it is. Original Le Male DNA: at most 20 percent. Without the same bottle and the knowledge, it wouldn't have occurred to me at first.

Here, vanilla creaminess alternates with sweet spiciness - and still leaves room for subtle nuances that everyone (apparently) interprets a bit differently. It is not extremely dominant, but long-lasting and quite pleasant to wear, especially during transitional seasons. For summer, however, it is a bit too spicy for me.

I remember spending my hard earned babysitting money on a bottle of Chloe Narcisse for my junior prom in the late nineties. The advertisement for this one was very romantic and included a smelling strip. It's a heavy fragrance and to me it was very grown up. Perfect for prom, right? Years later I would find another bottle of it and realize in retrospect that I probably wore far too many sprays of this super potent daffodil concoction. The thing about Narcisse, it is far too mature for a seventeen year old but never the less... there I was, dripping with Chloe Narcisse in a backless red satin dress with my hair piled high on my head (a feat that took the salon stylist 2 hours and hundreds of bobby pins to achieve). Such memories this scent stirs up!

It's a great surprise because I hate the original which I find very synthetic. And this one is really very good ! The fig becomes coconut to my nose, the honey is deliciously creamy and this touch of sandalwood is just perfect ! Ideal for spring and summer thanks to its sunny side but frankly, I wouldn't mind wearing it in autumn/winter mainly thanks to its honeyed side.

A very sweet gourmand fragrance with a hefty dose of honeyed peach in it. Heady white florals. Fig on the sidelines. Something lovably herbal too (davana?), but it's unfortunately rather weak and brief. But peach is the obvious star of the show that steals your attention the moment you relax and stop trying to sniff out each separate detail. My partner got a sneezing fit as soon as I sprayed it. I was laughing at him at first, but then started sneezing myself right after. Not great. The whole room soon became peachy and sweet, while the air in my immediate vicinity became bitter. For the first hour I could taste this fragrance on my tongue if I made a mistake of breathing it in through my mouth. The scent may be different, but bitter chemical taste was the same one would feel if they sprayed a lot of air freshener in a tiny enclosed space. It settled closer to me in about ~1,5 hours, and finally became easy to breathe in. At that point – still a very sweet composition with an emphasis on peach. There was something powdery deep within it, which made me feel almost as if I was petting the fuzzy peach skin. Pretty neat if you like that feeling, but me personally? I hate that texture, it always makes me itchy. In ~1,5 hours peach fizzled out and left just the sweet vanilla base on my skin. Another ~2,5 hours later vanilla faded away too. Eh. It's whatever. I tested it the next day after the original Scandal while the memory was still fresh, so if I had to base my score on that comparison – this one would easily win. It was both more balanced and much more interesting. But in general, compared to all other fragrances of this kind that exist? If someone asked me for recommendations of peachy/gourmand perfumes, this one wouldn't even get a honorary mention.

I didn't know what to expect from this as it was my first Scandal fragrance, but the notes looked so good to me, so I ordered a sample. Immediate love. Sweet perfume -- by no means a scandal! -- but the Fig, honey, and Peach just combined with the white flowers was just so lovely. And then, 3 hours into the wear test, something on my skin smelled like spicy BO. I was so disappointed! I am going to give this another shot before giving up, but disappointing how skin chemistry can turn something so delightful into "I swear I took a shower and put on deodorant!" Great perfume though, even if my skin says it's not for me. Edit: Yep, tried it again, and the spices were even faster (and stronger) to come out a second time! Alas, this is just not for me. A shame because it is a great fall/winter perfume.

Like with Scandal Le Parfum, I find this Scandal equally pleasing. The scent is warm and creamy. The honey here is very pleasant, and the sweetness with the fig is not overwhelming or artificial. In fact, the color gold perfectly matches the fragrance. The tuberose also smells wonderful here and not old-fashioned. Really a very beautiful perfume! I like it better than Le Parfum. I love the original Scandal, and apart from the honey, I can't see any similarities. JPG has delivered again. Even in continuous testing during absolute heat on summer vacation, it convinced me with incredible longevity! With the coconut note, it's a true summer fragrance! I’m already looking forward to autumn and winter. Has potential to be a signature scent and is wearable year-round.

I don't know if it's because the fragrance is still relatively new on the market or if I have a unique preference, but for me, this flanker from JPG hits the mark completely. The scent is liquid happiness for me! When I wear it, I think of a sunset on the beach, in front of me a delicious dessert of grilled figs, vanilla ice cream, and honey. Carefreeness, letting go, "everything is good." It is sensual, romantic, seductive, warm, and velvety. I really hope it gets more attention in the future, because it absolutely deserves it in my opinion. The longevity/sillage is average to good for me. I spray it once in the morning and once in the afternoon, preferably on my décolletage, and then I actually perceive it permanently and very pleasantly around me. No headaches, as often happens with other perfumes. In short: For me, a rough diamond and my favorite fragrance for a long time!

I’m trying my hand at my first review. First of all: I am an absolute lover of sweet scents and a true Gaultier fan. Therefore, I thought, THIS is my fragrance. The written statements and reviews have reinforced that belief. Very positively for me: The longevity and sillage are truly above average.

It starts fruity-sweet and smells exactly like peach iced tea to me, I can almost taste it. This lasts for quite some time, only after 25 minutes a slight floral jasmine note comes in, bringing a brief excursion into powderiness. Only after 40 minutes do I smell some sandalwood, it is now overall less iced tea, but the peach remains fruity and present.

I've always liked Boss Bottled; the problem is that here in Spain it's a fragrance with an overwhelming success: Almost every time there is an occasion when people are wearing suits, you smell Boss Bottled. The same for Boss Bottled Intense, too. Finally, this 'Absolute" iteration comes out and I have to say that it's really good: More modern, classy and refined than the OG & Intense. Also, it has a different vibe... Which allows you to wear it next to the others and not smell the same. ... And I'm not going to say better or worse, but different enough; I've read people who say it smells the same and this isn't the case at all. However, if you aren't able to discern the nuances, don't buy it. The Scent: It opens with apple, bergamot and plum, masterly blended in a gentle balance expanded with cinnamon and subtle woods. All of this is sustained and harmonized with a soft musk and other notes that add depth and a watery - but not the typical aquatic -vibe. The final blend is sophisticated, elegant and modern. Mood & Occasions: -Boss Bottled Absolute is a very classy signature scent to wear with a suit on all occasions involved. Of course, it's an attractive and sensual fragrance, without losing an iota of confidence and class. Best seasons are Fall, Spring and Winter; Summer if it's not too hot. - Longevity & Projection: It lasts long enough, but it's a smooth projector (6 - 8h). This is the type of fragrance that I use for long days with all kinds of situations, including a night out. In these cases I usually have the bottle on hand or carry a decant in my pocket... For me, this is better than a strong fragrance which can be excessive at various times of the day. Conclusion: A modern and elegant signature scent. Excellent choice for executives, even at formal events... But for other types of uses and scenarios, you may prefer Boss Bottled Intense.

In the past, I mostly bought or received perfumes from Hugo Boss. For my nose, there was generally always something suitable, or I hadn't had any negative experiences yet. This variant is fundamentally not bad either. I find it great for everyday use or work. However, I miss the "WOW" effect for a better rating. The longevity and sillage seem rather low to me. You feel the need to reapply quickly. Overall, I find this version too restrained. The opening is pleasantly fresh, and I find it more intense than it becomes in the heart and base notes. But as I said, it's great for everyday use or work. Top note: starts with fresh bergamot and lasts relatively long. Then briefly transitions into the plum note. Heart note: the fresh note fades, and a light sweet cinnamon note emerges. However, it becomes relatively subdued quite quickly. A hint of wood subtly comes through. Base note: the wood note becomes more pronounced and then dominates the field. In the end, I still have the feeling of being able to perceive a slight sweetness.

I haven't smelled the Boss Bottled line, but in the cold late November, Absolute was introduced to me. It starts off like shampoo and champagne - sparkling apple and high-quality grooming products for men. A little later, a slight gasoline note comes into play. After that, a green, sour plum takes the lead, framed by cinnamon and plums. Fresh snow smells like watermelon rinds, and Absolute seems to flirt with the same theme. The fragrance works very well in cold and damp weather; it feels invigorating, uplifting, and somewhat depressing, literally keeping you from losing your human face with its soapiness.

After finally getting my little tester for the fragrance today, I was really surprised... You can already smell the similarity to the regular Bottled, only this one is infused with a hint of slightly synthetic oud and Gaultier's Ultra Male. Sweet woody, perhaps even slightly musty on some skin types. However, this somehow makes these sweet spicy scents... more mature. The longevity is decent (6 hours), the sillage is about the same as Bottled Intense, but with a bit more oomph. However, it's not annoying. I can't really evaluate the bottle, but since Boss has always had good craftsmanship, always has the same functional sprayer, and only changes the color, I find it quite chic. If you already have Intense, you probably don't need this one. But if you're looking for a mature interpretation of the classic, you should grab it when it’s available at a good price. The Bottled variations generally appeal to most people's tastes anyway.

I found 4 50ml 'snowglobe' bottles of Fragile tucked away on a bottom shelf in a duty free shop I frequent on my incessant travels. Having recently found out that it is an INCREDIBLE Tuberose I bought one (ridiculously inexpensively) and it is fast becoming one of my favorite frags of all time! I'm passing through the same shop again in a few weeks and will definitely buy the remaining stock! This thick and creamy white floral bounces off the skin with a fizz ... the ginger in the top undoubtedly responsible for this phenomenon! The Tuberose here is lush and plentiful ... and lasts at least 10 hours on my skin. In fact, this fragrance is so well composed (even the musk which I usually abhor is very well behaved) that it's discontinuation boggles the mind. It's not overtly feminine on me. If you like Tuberose and you haven't tried this you are surely missing out on one of the most beautifully crafted white florals of the turn of the century! Yes, it's heavy ... yes, it throws back to the late 90's ... yes, it'a a sillage monster!! YES, YES, YES ... it has all the things I like in a perfume. Simply wonderful!!! Bravo Mons. Kurkdjian.

This wonderful fragrance, in its unique bottle, felt like a gift of golden glow when I first received it. It had just been released, and from the start it was something precious to me. I remember sitting by the window, shaking the tiny golden flakes that floated through the thick liquid, watching them drift around the little figurine inside. In my mind, she was a Hollywood diva from the 1930s, frozen mid-pose on the red carpet - timeless, glamorous, and utterly untouchable, captured in her world of light and luxury. I was still very young at the time and while I already liked the scent, I instinctively knew I had to grow into this perfume. I wasn’t trying to become a diva, yet I instinctively wanted some of that glamour and excitement she seemed to embody. I’d place it back on its shelf, where it seemed to whisper softly: “You know where to find me.” Growing older, as occasions came up to wear Fragile, I’d spray it onto my wrists and behind my ears, and it felt as though the lady in the bottle came to life - lending me a touch of her charm, her confidence, her shimmer. On special evenings, perhaps even more than a touch. I associate this perfume with so many luminous moments - evenings of laughter, days filled with excitement, memories gilded with its scent. I never wanted the bottle to empty, so I wore it sparingly, and I’m glad to still have it with me, even if the liquid has considerably darkened over time. Fragile is a perfume that’s both bold and delicate - radiant and very present, yet tender at its heart. Heavy enough for everyone around you to notice, but graceful enough to never overstay its welcome. Simply put, it’s glorious. I only wish it weren't discontinued.

My father always brought me something beautiful from his business trips - chocolates, perfume, and snow globes. As a teenager, I was relatively indifferent to scents - the chocolates appealed to me much more - and even more so the snow globes. I could daydream for hours about the little scenes encased in glass. I was the lady who circled the Eiffel Tower with her poodle - and occasionally, I let it snow down on my alter ego. Or I stood as a little photographer in front of the Colosseum - right in the middle of a snowstorm. It was only later that scents accompanied my fantasy journeys and even inspired them further. That was when my love for fragrance was awakened. Of course, I was drawn to the Fragile bottle, as it combined my preferences. I was that delicate, elegant lady upon whom golden rain fell. And the scent touched me too - for it spoke of glamour and fame. Proud rose and enchanting tuberose and ylang-ylang. Very sensually, vanilla and cinnamon were added. This fragile lady behind glass was a femme fatale, a heartbreaker, and the star of the Moulin Rouge. And whenever I held the bottle in my hands - I was HER alter ego.

First of all, a thousand thanks to dear LA for the sample of this dreamy perfume. And believe me, I tested Fragile 3 times today, in different places - so to speak, with full body commitment - to do justice to the scent in a comment. But also because the top note initially puzzled me. But I figured it out. Fragile starts with a noble, mysterious sprightliness. With a hint of sparkling sharpness. As if you were mixing grated ginger, a pinch of coriander, and oranges with a good, dry champagne and pouring it over your skin.
