The champagne bubbles burst one by one, providing a tingling intoxication on the skin. However, not loud, but erotic and playful. Rose and tuberose make their presence known clearly and audibly. Yes, the heart note is almost dominated by the tuberose. A floral ecstasy. But even here, I get the impression that Fragile is hovering around me, and I was afraid that this dreamy composition would float away. Like in a dream that is so beautiful that you don't want to wake up. But the dream remained; it did not dissipate. The awakening was ambery, powdery, gentle, yet very present. I would describe it like this: Like a very beautiful woman who is delicate, appears very fragile, and yet carries an unexpected strength within her. LA, you know that I don't like cloying scents that hold no secrets, and you hit the nail on the head here. THIS is not Fragile. It holds all the secrets. This will definitely be my next perfume. Kiss Medusa, who hovers on scent pearls.

Or also known as Jeanne-Antoinette Poisson, Dame Le Normant d’Étiolles, marquise de Pompadour, Duchesse de Menars (copied from Wiki). I wouldn't choose any other "calculating" scent for this clever woman. Dominant yet submissive. Gets what she wants without pushing or having to use "force" and intrigue. Turns her enemy into a friend.... a seemingly still water that knows exactly what it wants. Fragile is just like that. Loud with orange blossom, jasmine, ylang-ylang (unmistakable!!) and coriander. Engaging with bergamot, rose, and star anise. And as a crowning touch, the "soft" notes of amber and musk, dusted with a hint of cinnamon. This fragrance has absolute recognition value, is completely vintage, and is a "bang" that demands courage, self-confidence, and a certain degree of cheekiness. Fragile is bursting with floral splendor. But not like a bouquet, rather like a lush palace garden full of flowers, arranged in various patterns and colors. Framed by fruit trees and bushes in the hottest summer. Humid, heavy, powerful. A floral-fruity scent that fades with a herbaceous-green finish. Here it’s a case of "less is more" and the longevity is typical of vintage scents -> enormous! The bottle is classy, albeit a bit kitschy. Unfortunately, it is also very awkward to spray. But the scent is very striking, and Fragile surely manages to outshine one or two competitors ;-)

What a bottle! Personally, it's almost too playful for me (& definitely difficult to spray), but still: extraordinary, iconic, elegant. Only JPG dares to do something like this in the designer realm... and just for such designs, I am glad for the brand & its success.

fragile, sensitive, delicate. The bottle, a revelation of elegance. A chansonette in a black evening gown, a nobility spécialement, the poise of a diva who is aware of her vocal power. Around her, the magic of a moment in the form of golden soufflé. Gracefully she stands on her stage, alone, all eyes on her. The fragrance, an homage to the magic of an exquisite scène.

Fragile, I treated myself to in winter 1999, it was even my New Year's Eve fragrance and the scent of the new millennium for me. Everyone knows how eccentric and extravagant Gaultier's fragrances used to be (the current ones are, with few exceptions, all ordinary and interchangeable).

The beginning admittedly startled me a bit, as it is spicy and hazy. Somehow pulsating... I am catapulted to an old attic. The afternoon light shines through the old, veiled windows. You can see the dust shimmering and sparkling like gold. It is mysterious what I smell. There must be a secret hidden in this attic. Many old and beautiful things catch my eye.

Today I had the chance to test this fragrance. Ouch! I wish I hadn't. The opening is very fresh, like sparkling lemonade in yellow. However, it quickly develops such a harsh synthetic note that I narrowly avoided a severe headache. I also lost the desire to search for any individual ingredients. This is another candidate for the notorious Ata-Attack!!

I have a soft spot for many of the Boss flankers and I happily acquire the older models one by one to test how they were. Boss United is Boss's take on fragrances like Invictus Eau de Toilette and Bad Boy Eau de Toilette - regardless of how one feels about it, this flanker simply did not turn out well. There is hardly any fruity component to discern, just a sweet synthetic mix right from the opening. Barely any freshness despite the mint, rather musty and artificial. The fragrance does not develop at all but remains in this realm of artificial sweetness without definable components. I truly do not smell the Boss DNA at all. This could have been any drugstore fragrance. Fortunately, the longevity and sillage are not too strong.

The fragrance starts with a pleasantly fresh blood orange, which is soon complemented by a nice breeze of mint. After 15-20 minutes, an extreme sweetness develops that comes from the patchouli. This sweetness reminds me of a very artificial melon chewing gum, even though there is no melon or anything else listed among the notes. This melon chewing gum then lingers for me until the end, still accompanied by a hint of mint. Overall, I would say that the fragrance strikes a relatively good balance between sporty freshness and pleasant sweetness, even though it smells distinctly synthetic. Due to all its characteristics, I wear this fragrance mainly for sports. For the rest of my leisure time, it suits my taste less, as it is too synthetically sweet for me. The longevity is unfortunately disappointing; after 2-3 hours, the fragrance is hardly even detectable on the skin. The sillage is still okay in comparison, but nothing more.

Very sweet. Creamy, like coconut milk. Salty and a little aquatic, but very... uniformly so, as if the salt is completely dissolved in the milky liquid. Resinous – in a slick buttery way rather than gooey. Floral. Very yellow. Leaves a thick lasting trail, but needs a fair bit of time to engulf the larger space in your immediate vicinity if you sit still. The type of scent that's too heavy for its own good. Feels like eating desserts at a seashore café. The idea of sitting on a terrace outside sounds genius until the wind rises and suddenly your exorbitantly priced piece of sponge cake with wilting berries tastes like sand and sea water. Falls into a category of super sweet and heavy summery perfumes that are meant to invoke a "tropical vacation" feeling in the wearer. Welp, at least it doesn't smell like sunscreen... Takes about ~3 hours to dry down to the base. During those 3 hours makes me feel weirdly uncomfortable. Like I'm an unspecified anime girl in a filler beach episode. Washed ashore at a picturesque tropical island that has a single abandoned hut in it full of nothing but hundreds of cutesy skimpy bikinis to choose from. It's hard to put the feeling into words, but while it smells pretty good, there's something... ingenuine about it. As if the composition is saying "look at me, everything about me exists for your titillation". I personally don't find that feeling in any way enjoyable. The drydown is mostly gourmand. Powdery in an "old crumbly merengue" way. It lingers for a few more hours, but at that point it's a skinscent that I can easily ignore by keeping my arms away from my face. Objectively – it's decent. But personally? I'm very much not its target audience.

Gaultier Divine was, for me, underdeveloped and totally unharmonious on the skin. Now with "Gaultier Divine Le Parfum | Jean Paul Gaultier," everything has been improved and what can I say... BOMB! Why not do it this way from the start? About the scent in advance, it is very strong and lasts for hours on the skin and days on clothing. Not for weak noses! It smells elegant, floral sweet, and slightly salty. This version is totally balanced and really rounded. Through the base, I find the Le Parfum also rich and dark. Not an 08/15 scent and a woman definitely stands out. Wearable everywhere and in every season. Potential for a signature! Definitely a candidate for testing!

Divine Le Parfum didn't immediately convince me upon first application, to be honest. I had the same effect with the original Gaultier Divine . Both are pleasant scents, but nothing that blew me away right away, typical Jean Paul Gaultier DNA, after all. But then, after a few minutes, it started to develop on my skin, and that was the moment I understood what makes it so special. Love at the second spray, so to speak. The fragrance opens with a fresh note of bergamot, which is zesty and light. But then the salty accords come into play, reminding me of a walk by the sea. This blend of freshness and salt is incredibly pleasant and gives the scent something unique. In the heart note, delicate white flowers join in, making the fragrance seductive but not overpowering. Jasmine and rose provide a floral depth that feels very elegant. And finally, a warm base of amber lingers softly on the skin, giving it a pleasant, soft warmth. Gaultier Divine Le Parfum is a fragrance that, with its combination of freshness, floral notes, and a hint of salt, is perfect for those looking for something special, not too overpowering, yet still seductive. For me, it is an absolute must-have in my collection and a lovely, more intense version of the original!

I definitely have to write something about this Divine Le Parfum. The perfumer here is once again the talented Quentin Bisch, collaborating with Givaudan. I am a big fan of this perfumer, and you can't really go wrong with any of his works. For some brands, he creates more creative pieces; releases like Paco Rabanne or these Divines from Gaultier are, of course, much more mainstream and tailored. At Puig, they want to appeal to the broader audience. However, I find this Divine series, consisting of "Gaultier Divine | Jean Paul Gaultier," "Gaultier Divine Elixir | Jean Paul Gaultier," and this Le Parfum, quite successful and not just one of many. This DNA is catchy and stays in the memory. It's a fragrance that can be worn throughout the year, as these notes are very versatile. It might be too cloying for the extreme heat, but otherwise, it's really well done. I haven't tested the Elixir yet; this Le Parfum feels a bit more elegant than the original, but it is also a bit heavier. I like both and think they are worth it, especially if you're looking for pleasant but not generic scents. A very modern fragrance that fits well with Quentin Bisch's style. The box is pretty with golden highlights, and the bottle is truly out there. It goes in the Classique direction with the torso, but here it's a bit wilder with this corset. It's definitely an eye-catcher, whether positively or negatively is up to each person's taste. Prices are typical for a women's designer release. Available in 30, 50, and 100ml. A refill is also available. Divine Le Parfum has only fragrance notes, no pyramid. Since this scent has little evolution, this is understandable. As usual, it starts off a bit wild but becomes tamer as it develops. What I like about this fragrance are the exotic notes. You find many summery flowers here like Frangipani, Ylang-Ylang, Lily, and Jasmine. A wonderful floral freshness that is slightly sultry but still manages to be worn in summer. Creamy notes like coconut and a solar note are added. Coconut is not in the foreground, so it is perceived more as an exotic note. The sea salt note brings a summery vibe that really spreads a pleasant and casual atmosphere. Akigalawood contributes that typical woody vibe that Bisch likes so much. A bit of warmth and sweetness comes in with amber, benzoin, and sweet meringue, which naturally intensifies towards the end. This fragrance is not too heavy, but in extreme heat, it might be a bit much for me. A great scent profile that you get here. Well suited for fans of modern designer fragrances. Performance is typically good for a Puig fragrance. This Divine Le Parfum definitely lasts for 10 hours. The sillage is good, and the scent has a nice projection. Overall, a great appealing women's designer fragrance that works year-round. For the evening or not-too-hot days, it's always a great choice that stands out from the crowd. I particularly enjoy the salty sweetness.

I ordered the perfume blind because I have found all the scents from Jean Paul Gaultier to be excellent so far. The fragrance components sounded very interesting, but I was somewhat put off by the salty note. I ordered it anyway because I wanted to try something new and had never been disappointed by Jean Paul Gaultier scents. The first spray was a completely new experience for me as I had never encountered such a scent before. My first impression was: it smells like parsley. On the skin, in my opinion, the salty note becomes quite prominent, but as the fragrance lingers on the skin, this note fades and a powdery scent remains. Overall, it's certainly not a bad fragrance, but there is something about it that bothers me; it's somehow an annoying scent, a scent you don't become addicted to like with some other Jean Paul Gaultier fragrances, such as La Belle.

... is still standing at the dock with his white bouquet and the meringue in hand, watching as the boat arrives. She jumps onto the dock, and he catches her and spins around with her. She takes the flowers from him, smells them, smiles at him, and says it's a different scent than salt and fish.

Yes, I really like Boss fragrances. I haven't smelled them all yet, but I've tried quite a few. Most of them I find quite well done. Boss Orange for Men - Feel Good Summer absolutely belongs to my favorites. It's a pity that this is probably a limited edition. It starts off very fresh and citrusy, with a sweet note that remains at least through the top notes. After a while, a slightly herbal note (black tea!?) comes in, without losing any sweetness. There is a certain similarity to the regular Boss Orange, but this one is much more citrusy and fruity. Makes perfect sense for a summer edition. I would recommend Boss Orange for Men - Feel Good Summer for leisure and work; for going out, I find the regular version better, as it somehow seems more elegant. The fragrance has a strong sillage and longevity. It lasts on me for at least 8-9 hours. Even after 7-8 hours, I can still perceive the scent on myself without having to sniff myself. I haven't experienced this pronounced longevity with many summer fragrances so far. All in all, I can only recommend the fragrance, just give it a try.

In search of a fruity summer fragrance, I sought unbiased advice in the perfumery. The friendly saleswoman sprayed several scents on test strips and handed them to me for comparison. I had at least five to choose from and ultimately decided on this one. Now, let's get to the headline. It was indeed an impulse buy based on the impression of the test strip. At first, the scent is really very fruity and summery. However, over time on the skin, the fruity notes quickly fade away. The fruitiness transforms into a mix of moss and tea, which remains perceptible on the skin for a few more hours. There are scents that I cannot tolerate on myself, but this one I can. It’s nothing special. I will use up the bottle, but I don’t think I will repurchase it.

Okay, with the name of the perfume, I couldn't help but think of James Brown's hit from 1965. But one has to admit: the scent is so pleasant and relaxed that it really gives you a good feeling. A feeling of something summery, almost party-like. I had only tested the scent casually, as I'm not really into Hugo Boss at the moment, and I never thought I would like it so quickly. The scent: A fruity-fresh beginning runs through the top note. It is a pleasantly relaxed scent with a hint of lemon and a bit more apple. The scent remains casually fruity, and soon you can smell the pear, while the cucumber and black tea noted in the heart are hardly noticeable. Now the scent reminds me of something that might surprise some. The scent smells a bit like those little shots with vodka and fruit flavor. It's almost as if I would down one of those little bottles and have that fruity aroma in my mouth. Even in the base note, this impression lingers a little, probably because the actual scent notes in the base are quite weak. The amber is the most noticeable, while the moss and patchouli are hardly present. After the tea sets in (which at first smells more like a fruit tea, turning into black tea only an hour later), the scent slowly but surely comes to an end and eventually disappears completely. The longevity is somewhat longer than typical summer fragrances. Depending on skin characteristics, probably between 4-6 hours, on test strips as always a few hours more (which should never lead anyone to assume that the scent lasts that long. But you can always spray the scent on your clothes to get more longevity out of it). The sillage is quite okay; it's not as weak as I had assumed, you can perceive it well, and the surroundings catch a bit of it too. The bottle is quite nice and almost looks like a bar of chocolate. The liquid is orange, the cap is elongated and silver. Everything is quite modern and also quite alright. Boss Orange Man Feel Good is a nice summer fragrance, light, relaxed, and pleasant-smelling. It holds up reasonably well and should definitely be tried if you like fruity notes. Unfortunately, in my opinion, it is a bit too expensive, but maybe you can get a smaller bottle if you want to alternate between several summer fragrances in the summer. But definitely worth a test!

What kind of summer scent do I want? It has to be fresh, fruity, a little green and spicy, with a gentle base. It should provide refreshment, capture the fruits of summer in its scent, reflect the spiciness of fresh herbs, while being subtle and not too overpowering. Light and yet with a certain, lasting volume. The fragrance comes from the Boss offshoot Boss Orange. The name is a concept, as is the orange box with its playful lettering. The bottle is a variant of the original Orange bottle, the segmented ribbing has been retained, thankfully the metal ring has been omitted, and the liquid has a pleasant, not too toxic coloring. The bottle is OK, but not really eye-catching. Let's see if one can feel summer. Lemon, apple, and pear open up, fresh, fruity, juicy, unfortunately with a slight hint of artificiality. After a while, bitter and green notes follow, the garden cucumber is clearly detectable, the tea can be sensed. Moss is prominent and provides a bitter and herbal aftertaste, which settles into a warm base. This sounds quite like what I initially wished for. But unfortunately, it doesn't quite meet my expectations. On one hand, there are the slightly synthetic hints, as I have smelled and tasted too often from various apple and pear sweets. Unfortunately, I also find it lacking in volume and complexity in the development of the scent. The projection is already OK, initially moderately strong, but then it fades very quickly for me. The longevity is a bit better, lasting just under six hours on me. I lack the assurance to get through the day in summer temperatures. Unfortunately. I also miss the masculine notes in the fragrance. It is a bit too soft and weak for me. “Feel Good Summer” is a modern, youthful feel-good scent that one would certainly enjoy smelling in summer. Unfortunately, it lacks a bit of substance.

I received it as a gift many years ago, but it sat in the cupboard and I never used it. I am so surprised. A light, fruity scent that emphasizes my casual side. It brings good mood to everyday life. Subtle, but noticeable. Boss Orange is like a refreshing breeze that lasts all day. Its subtle longevity ensures that I feel refreshed throughout the day. Sometimes I wish it were a bit more intense.

I had a highly unpleasant experience with this scent in a perfume store. I wanted to test it, but it wasn't available. The ladies working there tried to convince me that Eau d'Amour is the same scent as Gaultier2. They wouldn't be swayed by anything better. I haven't been back since. And Eau d'Amour is fortunately, man, am I glad about this, NOT the same scent as Gaultier2. I was able to bid on a half-full bottle. I would have really been annoyed because Gaultier2 develops on me like toilet blocks. This scent here, on the other hand, is wonderful. It's lighter to wear than the classic Classiques, which I also love - and, that's the great thing: it doesn't smell like toilet block on me! Eau d'Amour starts off sweet and fruity with a subtle spicy note. This intensifies as the mandarin fades and harmonizes in a very sensual way with the amber and the constantly present vanilla undertone. From there, I understand why this is labeled as a unisex scent; what remains afterwards is spicy, warm, and not too sweet, which men can also wear. So, men who don't have a pronounced feminine side... The top note, on the other hand, I find very feminine, very sweet, as I said, I can hardly imagine that. I might have to spray it on my boyfriend, perhaps. It's great when Classique is too intense for me, and I'm very glad that I trusted my ...uh... gut feeling and gave it a try without testing it beforehand.

For this comment, I need to refer to two other fragrances from the house of Jean Paul Gaultier: On one side: Gaultier². I found it to be a pretty crazy creation right from its release. A fragrance made up of just three components (amber, musk, vanilla), and all of them very warm. Very simple, very moving. Why look far away, sometimes the simple things are the best. The perfume smells great, but I could never bring myself to make a purchase. On the other side: Classique. THE women's fragrance that divides the nation. Either you love it, or you hate it. But it is undisputed that the scent is also a stunning creation and has now become a classic. The same base as Gaultier², but with a citrusy top note and a floral-spicy heart. I have never owned this fragrance either. Eau d'Amour is the perfect blend of both: the citrusy fresh start and the spicy heart of Classique, along with the warm sensual base idea of Gaultier². And I HAD to have THIS perfume immediately. This is truly a beautiful scent. So rich, powdery, creamy, floral, and sweetly sensual. It could also fit well in ET's drawer of "jogging pants fragrances." Slow down, switch off, cloud the senses, feel good.

Ah, I am simply enchanted... Gaultier² is, as already mentioned, a knockout. Gaultier² Eau d'Amour is no less impressive, on the contrary. The two fragrances could be twins, although not identical. Eau d'Amour is fresher, citrusy, somehow creamier, and has a powdery undertone. Interestingly, Eau d'Amour only has this creaminess on me; it smells completely different on my husband... there it is again, the scent-works-on-everyone-else effect. On him, Eau d'Amour is very animalistic, warmer, and very sensual. I have no idea how Gaultier manages this, but he is a genius. Both sillage and longevity are just as enormous as the original; you get to enjoy the beautiful scent for a long time and intensely. Another advantage: Eau d'Amour fits any occasion, whether it's a party or a casual night in.

My absolute favorite perfume!!! I got it in 2008 as a Valentine's Day edition and have never been able to let it go since! When I go out, I usually wear this scent, and so far I have only received compliments. For me, this is the most interesting fragrance composition I have ever smelled. At first, it smells herbaceous and powdery on me, and after 2 hours it smells completely different, somehow sweeter. And that's exactly why I love it.

At first, I perceive intense lemon and orange aromas. Then the fragrance becomes floral - perhaps that's the coriander, as there are no flowers mentioned in the description. I also think I can detect a distinct honey and pollen note. In the end, a bright, sweet note remains with dark (woody?) accents - that must be the vanilla with the musk. Eau d'Amour smells distinctly different from Gaultier²; it is also lighter and fresher. I think that those who like Gaultier² will not automatically like Eau d'Amour, and vice versa. Therefore, I don't understand why it was released as a flanker and not as an independent fragrance (probably just in the expectation that both would be purchased together).

I didn't even know until recently that this fragrance existed at all. Well, I’ve tested it now. It’s true, fresher and lighter than the regular Gaultier². Oh but sooo beautiful! Wonderful, not too heavy, I really liked it a lot.

I find this version of Gaultier2 much better than the regular one. It offers a lot more freshness, especially due to the citrus notes. Absolutely recommended! The idea with the magnets is also sweet. You get 2 bottles in the set that stick together magnetically.

so now I will dedicate myself to this variant-------- 1. After an evening, I tested this version of Gaultier 2, but I cannot agree with my two predecessors I prefer the original version. w I will test the fragrance for at least a week and report further.
than the original (gaultier²). this scent is also available in a two-pack. the two bottles are held together by two magnets - such a sweet idea from jpg!

Jean Paul Gaultier Classique does not list jasmine in the official notes yet it smells like a glittery jasmine vanilla powder bomb drunken dance floor. It recalls an evening I visited a friend and without telling first, she had agreed with other friends that we'd all meet up and go to a club. Being a brutally shy homebody, that's the last thing I EVER want to do, but as a visiting guest, you're sometimes trapped into these things, and I am also a people pleaser, so there you go. And there we went. The ladies room was filled with tipsy club-goers fixing their hair and makeup, and our mutual friend pulled a whole-ass bottle of perfume from her purse to refresh her scent. Even me, being the perfume obsessed weirdo I am, thinks that's strange. A whole bottle, wow. Anyway, it was this Jean Paul Gautier scent, and to this day it makes me think of boozy nightclub cocktails and the jasmine-scented tears of strangers in bathrooms telling me they love me just moments before puking on my feet.

I was in my twenties at the time and working in a thermal spa. One day, as I walked between the changing room stalls, I suddenly caught a heavenly beautiful scent in my nose. It smelled so sweet, delicious, and somehow sexy; I was magically drawn to this fragrance and had to know what smelled so good. The scent trail eventually led me to a lady who was drying her hair at one of the tables. Next to her cosmetics bag, she had also placed a perfume, which I tried to sneak a closer look at. I recognized that the bottle was a pink female body with a strange decoration on it. Of course, I couldn't read a name anywhere, and I didn't dare to ask the lady about her perfume, as I didn't want to disturb her as a guest. The scent haunted me at home for the next few days, and soon after, I went to a perfume shop with my then-boyfriend and explained to the saleswoman what I was looking for. She brought me various fragrance samples, and I recognized "my" scent again. It was Classique EdP by Jean Paul Gaultier. My then-boyfriend later gifted me the Classique EdP for my birthday, and I fell in love with the perfume, the beautiful feminine pink bottle, and my boyfriend. I wore the scent for all occasions: parties, dining out, at night, during the day, just always and everywhere. We were young and full of dreams; it was an exciting time. Then, as it had to happen, I suffered from terrible heartbreak and could not and did not want to wear the Classique EdP, "my beloved scent," anymore, as it was so closely tied to my then-boyfriend. I gave the bottle to my mother because she also liked the scent very much. From time to time, I would smell the bottle during visits to my mother and attempted to wear the scent again, but it failed every time, and I stood there, wistful, longing, and with bittersweet memories. Then I forgot about the Classique EdP. After a longer break from perfumes, I started to become interested in fragrances again and stumbled upon la Belle by Gaultier. This reminded me of the Classique EdP, and on a whim, I ordered the perfume. The excitement and joy when the package arrived were immense, but the disappointment was even greater when I sprayed it on myself. It was no longer my scent! Something was different; it smelled different, or was my memory deceiving me? Then I noticed the bottle...a red corset?! Mine was pink and had a delicate lace corset on it. Unfortunately, I don't like the new changed version at all. I find the scent unremarkable. It smells sweet at first, then becomes quite soapy on my skin very quickly, and in the dry down, I get a barely noticeable vanilla with soap. The scent barely lasts an hour on my skin before it evaporates. I can no longer smell the beautiful rose and the delicious rum that were special about the older version. It's really a shame what Gaultier has done with this reformulation.

It's a shame that Gaultier is altering or removing all of his good fragrances. Longevity is also a hallmark. Especially for big brands. The predecessor in its prime was truly beautiful! I no longer like the modern version. The main thing is to produce new fragrances like on an assembly line. Bye bye Classique

What the hell happened here? I love the EdT, I loved the old EdP, which I unfortunately never bought. Naive as I sometimes am, I recently ordered this version without much thought. I hadn't noticed any reformulation and thought I couldn't go wrong. How wrong I was! This "fragrance" may be called Classique, but it doesn't deserve that name at all. It is neither elegant nor beautiful. This water in the wrong guise is utterly useless and it deeply disappoints me. How can such a thing be allowed to pass? :⁠-⁠( What comes out of the bottle is not Classique. If you look closely, you might find a very faint note, but it could also be a cheap dupe. It smells like cheap soap, like an unpleasant composition... and somehow more like a men's fragrance. I am so disappointed, I can't say anything more about it. This is outrageous. The bottle is, as always, very beautiful, but the contents are not. I have now layered two sprays of the EdT over it to endure it, but I think I need to take a shower during my lunch break.

This is not the standard Classique (Eau de Toilette), but this is the Eau de Parfum - and as such, it is not just a higher concentration, but a truly different scent. It smells sweet - which may be due to the mandarin and vanilla. I personally always associate it with Christmas and cookies. Additionally, it is also floral, and I personally detect a woody note, probably sandalwood. I like it, but somehow it is too cookie-like for me - therefore, I always recommend the standard Classique EdT.

I have loved the original Classique for over 20 years, having repurchased it multiple times. By chance, I came across the red bottle. As a little fragrance addict, I absolutely had to smell the scent. Now the lady in red has moved in, wow. Definitely similar to the classic, but somehow rounder. Great S+H .... if I had to choose, I would pick the red lady....

Might feel "not-so-special" at retail price, but as a blend I think it's very nice and the "coolness" and watery effect is successfully achieved by calone-citrus-iris-mint for the bigger part of the evaporation, no nose-raping woody ambers but instead a mellow fruity-floral-woody unisex drydown.Delivers the marketing promise (coolness, jeans & white tee, anytime/anywhere, laid back). Top: At the very first spray the Calone/Cascalone/Scentenal hit my face with that marine and egg whitey olfactory mass, but the next second your nose adjusts and in few minutes this scent turns into what I can only call as a "potential future summer cheapie" that smells quite nice with undistinguishable citric top notes. I liked the fact that it doesn't abuse you with nuclear woody ambers and I'm a strong believer the last decades amber-wood overdose trend will die out soon and men's fragrances will do a flashback to millennial era. Mid: So here the transformation goes in the direction of iris, though not listed in the notes but you'll notice this carrot seed, musty iris rhizome effect that provides a peculiar coolness which fits the marketing story of this perfume especially when combined with the obvious menthol freshness. I surely get a slight non-gourmandy, more-fruity/floral sweetness which I can only assume violet/pear notes (ionones and esters) in combination with muguet/cyclamen type transparent fresh and watery sweet florals (hello 2000s) and also popular in laundry detergents forever. I think I get the vetiver here too but really not distinct. Base: After 20 hours on test strip the scent is more floral-sweet (clean fresh laundry muguet/cyclamen and violets), honeyed orange blossom, even lavender, almost feminine/unisex, right out of 90s-00s, will feel familiar to those perfume heads since 90s. The effect of woods must be there but honestly I can't "pick out" individually the sandalwood or vetiver again but it doesn't mean they don't play an important role in the effect overall.

My best blind buy. Let’s get straight to the point. Sometimes I develop a love for the unloved and forgotten flankers of fragrance lines. I try to appreciate things and discover treasures that may have flopped for others. Often, I come up empty and get frustrated - but sometimes I stumble (I) upon treasures and enjoy them even more. Hugo Jeans is not a popular release - no matter which platform or YouTube video you ask. I got it solely because of the notes breakdown and because the house of Hugo Boss almost always hits the mark for me when it comes to fresh scents. The result: Hugo Jeans is a favorite in my entire collection. The opening is beautifully fresh, with grapefruit, a bit of mint - nice and clean out of the shower. Very quickly, the main player comes in: the juniper berry. Certainly synthetic at this price, but incredibly delicious, at least for me. Sweet-fruity, with just a hint of acidity. I know I’m swimming completely against the tide here - but I have rarely smelled anything more delightful. Accompanying this in the drydown are subtle woods - however, this base is very understated. The prominent berry note lingers on the skin for about 2 hours before slowly fading away. The scent neither becomes sweeter nor shifts in any other direction. This blend of fruity-fresh without being too sweet makes it wearable for me in spring, summer, and autumn. I can imagine wearing it both after a workout and before a meeting. Dress up or down - it works for me in both scenarios. The combination of versatility, fragrance notes, price, and longevity results in a very good scent for me - if you like this kind of berry note. And if it’s not for you? Then at least it’s something different - not yet another lemon, then tonka, then vanilla to finish. For me, an absolute sleeper. It probably hits my sweet spot, even though it’s objectively terrible. But that’s exactly why everyone is their own person.

I love the original Classique for women with its delicious oriental feel and sexy floral accords, so when I saw this new Classique X flanker with the raunchy adverstising, I expected something sexier and richer. I find Classique X a powdery, softer version of Dolce & Gabbana's Light Blue. Disappointing actually, as I don't like all those citrusy, lemony accords. It's a mixture of sharp citrus and soapy florals on a rich, woodsy base. Not particularly sexy, but refreshing to say the least. When it comes to the warmer weather I'd be more tempted to reach for Classique Summer 2010, (which was a lovely soapy and flowery scent), over and above Classique X. I think the intention of releasing this fragrance was to have it appeal to women who were not fans of the original Classique. Although I don't entirely understand the craze over fruity and citrusy scents, they do tend to sell well and are usually big hits for perfume companies. Despite my dislike for this bitter, uneventful fragrance, I have no doubt that there are some women who are quite enamoured with it. Although the lasting strength is quite good, I've come to the conclusion that I much prefer Jean Paul Gaultier's orientals and masculine offerings. Classique X has missed the mark with me and left me quite cold and unimpressed.

It was a damp, cold, gloomy November day when I first encountered him. I had sought refuge from the lashing rain, the biting wind that swirled my hair like autumn leaves and caught it in the windbreak of the bus stop. The bus was late, once again - I was cold and the shop behind me was a sanctuary of light, warmth, and scent. There he stood, the torso, right at the top of the shelf. A damp dream of satin glass with a wasp waist, the bust in DD. I was wearing jeans and a parka, at 25 just a Cup B. Ten minutes later my bus arrived, I dashed out of the shop with the torso in tow, wrapped in gentle softness and warmth, late summer light on apricot skin. From that moment on, I kept running into him. He took the bus and train and sometimes even rode a motorcycle, he went through thick and thin with everyone he wore. He flooded the disco, the pub across the street, the supermarket, and even the hospital. He was omnipresent and eventually too much for me - I no longer wanted to taste the sweetness of a Hubba Bubba, let alone smell it (afterwards), so I filed for divorce and tried to avoid him. As best as I could. Twenty-six years later we met again. I was still wearing jeans, still a parka, at least when it was cold, now and then. The torso wore an X instead of a corset, the bust seemed not quite as large anymore. "How have you been? Come on, tell me." He had become calmer, lighter, finer. A little greener for the greeting, the brightness dimmed. Still the character of his youth, still sweet, still chewing gum - but more oranges than their blossom today, a bit of acidity, a fizz here and there. Relaxed friendliness, a charming wink, no more push-up, no more piled hair. Recognizably "Classique", a bit also "Ma Dame", no longer quite young, yet not too grown-up. A late spring, an early summer morning when the sun soon warms the garden. Close to my skin, he does not flood rooms, not even the car, no one takes flight. A scent for gray as well as sunlit days, for bare arms as well as for furry muffs.

Pink and black combined, I can recognize it from a great distance in the perfume store. But it has to be this delicate pink like the bottle of Classique X. So that's already a great success in my opinion. The scent starts with pure Vitamin C (I can't identify which citrus fruits are present). After the citrus top note, I experience a scent lull; for a while, I smell nothing (I've tried this several times) - somehow a blind spot. Strangely enough, the people in the room with me still smell the full blast of the top note for quite a while. Maybe lemons with wings... I don't know, it's strange. However, my sense of smell comes back. By the way, my introduction to Classique X took place in a perfume store that still does 1. decanting and 2. even in small spray bottles and 3. for free. I also bought my Coco M. there, but still, very commendable. From the middle, Classique X becomes really beautiful. The orange blossom comes out nicely on my skin. A fresh floral quality unfolds, very intimate (but not sexy, sexy is different). However, X does not remind me at all of my beloved Classique EDP (bottle with a copper-colored tip), but that’s okay. X is uncomplicated, fresh, and suitable for days when it doesn't need to be so special. For summer, X is perfect. However, women should plan to reapply - the longevity leaves something to be desired. Personally, I believe that I lack a certain scent nerve for Classique X, as my fellow humans apparently experience more of this fragrance than I do. It may hold better on textiles than on my skin. Yes, one more thing, for an EDT, I find the price really steep, 63 - 65 € for 50 ml... Those who love this scent will, of course, buy it!

After testing Classique and Gaultier2, my new acquisition has turned out to be a tiny dose (20 ml) of ClassiqueX. No decision for the B-solution! Because it is a very distinctive initially fresh scent that then develops a bit of fruity depth and ends up smelling powdery. The scent progression may not be truly harmonious-rounded, but that doesn’t bother me. Since I also appreciate Roma and Light Blue, I find in the X scent nuances that correspond to my preferences. I can very well imagine that the fragrance will accompany me at least for a season starting in spring. If I should be mistaken, then I’ll just have a small decorative torso in my collection, which is also fine.

Classique X is for me a kind of middle ground between Classique and Ma Dame, just much lighter, fresher, and unfortunately also more fleeting. The scent starts for me with a hint of citrus freshness, then this "Gaultier-esque" element from Classique joins in, and my nose picks up nuances from both of the mentioned fragrances. Classique is heavier, Ma Dame is stronger and much fruitier. All in all, a really beautiful scent, if only it would last longer. I can hardly perceive Classique X after about 2 hours, I have to get my nose right up to my wrist. Still, a nice fragrance that can also be worn well in spring and summer.

I am surprised. I had suspected I would get a tired copy of the well-known Classique. But it is not like that at all. It is not a "vanilla bomb," like the regular Classique. This one is a fresh version, which also has a slightly floral touch from the beautiful peony note. A lovely, floral summer fragrance with a tiny hint of freshness.

When I wanted to test the sample, I immediately thought of the regular classique, which probably everyone who knows a bit about perfume is familiar with. But I was mistaken. Very much so. But in a positive way. It smells fruity and light at first and after a while, floral. Not as sweet as the original, suitable for spring and also summer.

I smelled it for the first time in the perfumery and didn't know what to make of it. The first impression was rather not good. It smelled so "boring." But when I smelled it a second and third time, I liked it more and more. I then just ordered it. It arrived today. I tested it right away and now? I don't even know if I like it anymore.

so I love Classique, I have been wearing this fragrance since I was 16... so for 13 years. Classique X I find boring, unremarkable, and way too light. I was expecting a nice, soft, warm scent but unfortunately that was not the case. I will stick with my Classique EdT. But I am curious about the Extrait, unfortunately I haven't been able to test it yet.

Of course, an Elixir had to be added to this Gaultier Divine and Gaultier Divine Le Parfum from this line. Often, when Quentin Bisch is involved as a perfumer, an Elixir comes out. Name aside, if the flanker is good, one can overlook it. And this Elixir delivers in my opinion and is, in my taste, the best of this line. The other two and the base DNA of Divine already appeal to me, but this flanker from this year is the most interesting interpretation for me. In the last two years, the trend among summer designers has already been heading towards tropical and exotic, especially with Jean Paul Gaultier. I like it, as I find this exotic style quite appealing. The Divine line is already very mainstream, but still, this series has its own twist thanks to this wonderful salty note. Since the tuberose also comes across as slightly heavy and a bit cloying, you can easily wear this even in autumn, although I see it best suited for temperatures starting at 20 degrees. At the recommended retail price, 100ml costs a hefty €170, which I find quite outrageous. Niche prices have arrived in women's designers. One should really only buy at good offers, around 50% off. Additionally, this fragrance is available in 30, 50, and 200ml. The bottle and packaging are a bit of an acquired taste with this bottle resembling Classique with the female torso. This tin can also follows that direction. The perfumer here is once again Quentin Bisch, in collaboration with Givaudan. Three notes are indicated here, which is of course not true. The pillar of this fragrance is the floral heart note that also dominates this scent with slightly cloying tropical notes leaning towards tuberose and ylang-ylang. Additionally, there are wonderful fresh white flowers in the form of clean jasmine. This floral framework is already very harmonious, if one overlooks the somewhat overpowering start. In the opening, there is also a wonderful salty freshness combined with marine notes. It fits well and contributes somewhat to that beach feeling. Moreover, subtle citrus notes complete this combination in the first hours. The sweetness from the base sets in noticeably earlier: vanilla and creamy tonka notes, which of course also remain until the end. There are also gourmand touches and a bit of patchouli. A great fragrance that already seems interesting and is also very mass-appealing. The scent is wearable during the day, but it can also shine in the evening with wonderful sweet-seductive notes plus this exotic touch that has slightly mysterious vibes. Performance is typically good for fragrances from Puig and also for Quentin Bisch as a perfumer. This fragrance easily lasts around 10 hours, with a sillage that is really good and has endurance. You won't get lost in the crowd, even if you don't dose heavily. Overall, a great designer fragrance that should still drop significantly in price. At the recommended retail price, it is certainly not a recommendation, but it is a solid choice that should appeal to many and stands out from the crowd.

I have been a fan of this sun perfume for years now. The first Divine by Gaultier was a very sweet-floral scent for me - almost like a flower meadow in southern France, near the sea. The salt remained somewhat in the background for me, overshadowed by the floral scent. The second Divine, Le Parfum, brought out the salty-aquatic notes more distinctly and was no longer quite as sweet and floral. Here, the Divine accord truly shone for me: the sea association became more present and pronounced. With the third Divine, Elixir, I still find the basic idea of a summer day by the sea completely palpable - the salt remains, but the scent becomes earthier, leatherier, and visually fits the browner bottle. After spraying, I sense alongside the sweetness a leathery-earthy accord that almost leans towards tobacco. For me, the aquatic and salty notes are still clearly present, contrary to what some reviewers claim. It feels like a different place by the sea: less floral meadow, more warm earth, leather, and sun on salted skin - perhaps even with a hint of sunscreen. I really like this new, exciting direction - sweet, salty, aquatic, and earthy all at once. A great addition to the Divine line!

Unfortunately, the scent is not perfect yet. It is significantly better than the EdT. It is not bad for a lady who doesn't want to smell too overpowering. The fragrance is pleasant to smell, even if you can hardly distinguish it from others once applied.

... belongs to Lovers. This Patti Smith hit came to mind when I discovered Boss Nuit pour Femme intense. To this music, we used to "dance our legs off," as my friend always beautifully put it. But this fragrance has no pounding rhythm, rather a gentle melody. Definitely an evening serenade. It suits evening strolls in the park, while exchanging thoughts hand in hand with your beloved. You can still sense the outlines of the shimmering white-flowered bushes, and the scent of jasmine lightly brushes your nose. You walk over soft moss, and the woods exhale their warm spiciness. Not a pitch-black night, but a gentle, moonlit twilight. In a bustling disco, Nuit would indeed be out of place - its notes are too delicate and sensitive for that. It needs a moody environment to shine - and then it weaves a delicate yet effective spell. It was as if the sky had quietly kissed the earth - that she must only dream of him in the shimmer of blossoms.

Scandal Intense offers an extremely smooth and velvety scent, I’d even say downright milky. There’s a slight hint of honey, but what stands out the most is the ylang-ylang, making this new release a great pick for summer. As for the cardamom, I honestly can’t detect it at all. That’s a shame, since I tend to enjoy perfumes with spicy notes - it could have added a nice little twist. It doesn’t bring anything new to the world of perfumery, but I still find it pleasant overall. I really like the purple bottle, though I still can’t stand that cap with the legs in the air…

Nothing alike like other scandals that didn’t stand out for me. But this one, it’s something else, original : it’s amazing. Best combination of my favorite flowers ylang and cardamoma. It makes it sweet without being extra gourmand. It’s subtle but yet a pleasant light and perfect mixture ; its projection was intense for first few hours and longevity great. I can see why so many people are disappointed : i first tried out of a tester from the store, the fragrance was really intense, but once i bought it and i got to try it from my new bottles. Performances were nothing alike and much weaker; perhaps because the tester in the store havr « macerated » enough since there for few days already. I can’t wait to reach my it’s full potential. I would advise you to go in a store and try it out ; not to judge directly out of the new blind-ordered box.

Might not be groundbreaking in uniqueness but this is a really intoxicating vanilla/cardamom combo that I loved at the first sniff in the store. I had to go back and buy a bottle even if the price was steep and I promised not to buy anymore full bottles! I wore it today at work and everyone around me was wondering what that beautiful scent was, I got endless compliments - and it's not like people don't know I love wearing all kinds of perfume every day. I agree with the other reviewer who wrote that the tester in the store smells "stronger". I think it's easy to go nose blind when you personally apply the scent on yourself, but obviously it projects amazingly! I own both Scandal Le Parfum and Scandal Absolu - but Scandal Intense is not much alike them.

It’s marketed towards women but it’s more unisex imo (as is all fragrance, inherently, just wear what you like). We tried this in boots when it first came out and it’s also the scent that made me change my mind on a lot of JPG. It’s simple but rich, deep, and comforting. Perfectly balanced between sweet, spicy, and floral so it doesn’t really lean any particular way.

Scandal Intense enters the room as if it owns it. High heels, honey lip gloss, a laugh that’s a bit too loud - but that’s exactly what it wants. It wants scandal - but delivers more reality TV than classic French film. The first spray is like a sugar shock, I only smell honey. “Subtle” is a word this fragrance does not know, “loud” is its first name. Unfortunately - and I’m sorry to say - it gets stuck on the sweetness. The complexity is missing, and while I hope for some depth to develop, all that remains is a sweet carpet that soon becomes too sticky for me. Like actually all the other Gaultier fragrances (to my nose), this one is also too much of everything. Jean Paul and I - it’s not going to work anymore.

The name fits perfectly! What stands out immediately: - The scent is ultra sweet and heavy, with honey, vanilla, and a slightly cherry-like note that really hits hard. - It starts off really loud, almost overwhelming - but once you get into it, it becomes really cozy and sexy.

Thank goodness not the well-known scandal of synthetic honey DNA. I smell coconut, perhaps the combination of ylang-ylang paired with cardamom gives me coconut. While testing, I think, wow, I actually don't mind this at all. The coconut note (not Bounty, not a scented candle) disappears and we have a heavy sweet vanilla...cardamom, which I desperately searched for...

The range of Boss colognes is quite broad, with Hugo Man a recognizable scent thanks to its fresh notes and its gourd-shaped fiasco, so much a classic that it was followed by many flankers, and Urban Journey joins the collection. It stands out for its fresh side and its green and watery notes. A flanker that stick out from the Hugo Man original composition by having its own olfactory universe. The bottle, inspired by the cans of the soldiers, this time is adorned with a smooth bluish-grey dress, whose texture is reminiscent of that of concrete and stone like it's coated in sand, the urban soil I bet, same screw cap with a black ribbon. There are many notes stated in the olfactory pyramid, and Urban Journey is not a linear perfume, though a woody aromatic cologne, which ranges between a floral head, an aqueous and leathery heart, and a woody and mossy base. Urban Journey welcomes you with a very pleasant and reasonably balanced floral and green accord. The combination of zesty orange fruit, with a hint of spicy cardamom, and the citrusy freshness of the rare mountain Himalayan whorlflower blossom produces an aroma that has some Hesperides facets, quite close to that of tangerine peel. It's a bit tasty and reminds me of most of the original Hugo Man's DNA. However, it opens up citrus and fruity, the cardamom is nearly perceivable, it's addictive. The heart unveils aromatic facets of fresh black tea tinged with drops of aquatic freshness. It has a strong, slightly bitter smell, with a smoky overtone. The result of organic black tea and synthetic cascalone, an aroma chemical that adds a sea breeze or marine note to the concoction, is gorgeous, still green, with the soul that comes from the vibrancy of the Indian tea leaves, I did not expect it. Finally, the dry-down delivers fairly discreet woody notes of creamy, slightly rosy, with honeyed-sweet sandalwood, which matches with raw guaiac wood, a robust incensed tone lightly smoky and waxy-oily. But the base is not all too woody, there is a tinge of mossiness given by the oakmoss, or better the artificial substitute of it. The overall base is comforting and quieting, it does not scream boisterous. In the final phase, the fragrance retains a citrus presence. Still, it feels different from the traditional notes of grapefruit, lemon or orange, staying close to a slightly salty cold water and ozone tint, with some warm sections of musk. I don't think it is all too artificial or scratchy. It grabs the attention without being too loud while relying on the subtle blending of its few dominant notes. Both sillage and performance are averages, more than half a day on my skin and clothes. The fragrance does not fill the room but moves when you move. Perhaps, it is targeted towards a teenage audience. Still, I do like it. The incredible freshness makes Urban Travel suitable for milder months, Spring and Summer seasons fit the best. It is a daily safe, sophisticated, and casual fragrance, for leisure time, sports, as well as office, or school, why not? Urban Journey is just right, neither too bold and heady for this climate, not too airy and not long-lasting enough. This review is based upon a 75ml bottle I own. Stay well; stay healthy. -Elysium

When applying my sample of "Hugo Urban Journey | Hugo Boss," I was initially not as disappointed as the reviews on Parfumo suggested. Unfortunately, as the fragrance developed, I gradually became quite intimidated, as the ending was not very pleasant. The performance is also quite lacking. The longevity on my skin is around 6 hours with a rather subtle sillage. The top note starts off quite refreshing, fruity-citrusy, sweet, maritime but also rather synthetic-alcoholic thanks to orange grape sugar, lemon peels, and a shower gel aroma. The heart note is spicy but also a bit greenish. Here I detect cardamom, black tea, algae, lemon balm, ozone, and violet leaves. The base offers a rather musty and not particularly pleasant as well as indefinable woodiness with a hint of oak moss. It's a shame that Hugo Urban Journey ends so musty - there was definitely more potential.

Do you remember Giovanni Trapattoni's rant? It would fit perfectly here: "There is currently this company, ... ooooooh! ... Some perfumes ... forget what they are! First: there is no Boss perfume that smells good like Creed. Second: I explained, ... with this example, after Hugo Iced ... maybe needs a break. I have seen other perfumes, ... on the market. A user is not an idiot ... there were two, three or four scents that were as weak as an empty bottle!" Sorry, ... please forgive me, but an "empty bottle" would have been quite alright with me, because unfortunately, it was even worse. Here are the facts: Recently, while on a business trip, I used my lunch break to buy a perfume, and there were a few samples included as a bonus. After that, I completed my appointment and sprayed Urban Journey on myself back in the car. A great testing opportunity, I thought, since I still had a three-hour drive ahead of me. What a mistake! The opening was still somewhat okay, as I at least tried to interpret it as "somehow fruity" - albeit quite synthetic and not further definable. But after barely fifteen minutes, the "scent" completely flopped and showed its true face: pure chemistry, hardly bearable! Therefore, it would be better if "Aggro" stood on his hideous blue shirt instead of Hugo, because that could easily happen ;) My problem: although I was finally able to wash it off at a rest area after another agonizingly long 20 minutes, some of it had also gotten on my shirt. So I had to endure this completely botched Hugo for a grueling 2.5 hours, sending up 150 desperate prayers to heaven "no traffic, please no traffic," and I arrived home never happier, ready to finally quit Boss. Sorry, dear fragrance fans, but for me, it is almost forbidden to discuss the individual notes of this Hugo in detail, which is hardly possible anyway. Because the completely overdosed sweetish chemistry of the aquatic Cascalone® simply overshadows everything, so you can only name the other ingredients by exclusion, foremost cardamom, sandalwood, and oakmoss: not present. I am done! But maybe this comment can still be turned into something positive, because I learned a lot: 1) Never spray unknown fragrances directly on your skin or clothing, at least not in the car, or your steering wheel might bear bite marks. 2) A "Limited Edition" does not necessarily mean "valuable due to scarcity," but could also imply the manufacturer's ability to cleverly and very quickly take a perfume off the market at any time. 3) Not every boss is aggressive, but this boss certainly is ;-) 4) Some things are even uglier on the inside than their appearance suggests, but everything is relative - according to 5) 5) Even though this consolation is mean; others have had it worse, e.g., with Sécrétions Magnifiques. Because against this brew rated 3.1, including adrenaline and blood, Hugo's chemical accident seems like a harmless company outing ;-) And yet I gladly forgo it and wish Urban Journey was as "weak as an empty bottle." In other words: What does Boss allow?!

All of the entries from the Scandal pour Homme line have disappointed me so far. The original Scandal pour Homme lacked smoothness and was simply a mishmash of synthetic sweetness, Scandal pour Homme Le Parfum toned down that synthetic edge a bit, but still failed to impress me in terms of scent, and Scandal pour Homme Absolu left me down due to its disappointing performance and short-lived delicious opening. Simply put, none of them are worthy of wearing the crown and occupying the throne. But now we've got another contestant, Scandal pour Homme Intense , which can either save the Scandal line for me (nothing left to save, really), or it can join its cousins in the pit of shame... Immediately upon spraying, the OG DNA comes upfront - synthetic sweetness. The clary sage brings that sweet, herbaceous, floral, and musky mishmash, which isn't necessarily bad on its own, just lacks balance. The synthetic undertone which is the signature accord of the line and on which all of the notes are built upon just kills it for me. Also, I do get some slight hints of some creamy tonka bean in the opening, which appears to be more and more prominent as things dry down. As minutes pass by, the synthetic aura takes a slight step back, making way for even more prominent tonka bean sweetness, while the vetiver mildly shows up. It adds a dry and woody aroma to the composition, but it's hardly earthy, which is one of the key accords of vetiver, meaning that there's not much vetiver in here, really. Frankly, you really got to dig through the scent to just get the slightest of that unmistakable vetiver aroma, which here is quite cheap and as "safe" and bland as it gets. But you know what else you don't get a lot of in here? Leather. When I initially saw Scandal pour Homme Intense added in leather, I admit, my expectations rose a nudge. I adore leather, and I hoped that this would finally be the ingredient that might save whatever's left of the Scandal pour Homme line for me. But boy, was I wrong. The leather here is some of the faintest, most subtle, softest, mildest, barest leather that I've smelt in a fragrance. There might be something which reminds of leather, but hardly so, and it appears like 10-15 minutes after spraying. Let me be clear, though: there's little development here. The syntheticness dissipating a bit since the start gives you the feeling that there's development underway, but really, everything smells very similar from start to finish. There's no story being told, nor much quality at the door. On a more positive note, longevity here is excellent, at least on my skin. I get a minimum of 12 hours, with some cases reaching even 15 hours, which makes it the Scandal with the best longevity on my skin. Of course, by those marks, all I sense is a very faint, warm leather woodiness, which frankly, I much prefer over the loud synthetic-sweet opening. As for projection, I got about 2 feet for the first hour, settling down to about a 1 foot bubble for the next few hours, and reaching a skin scent somewhere around the 5 hour mark. Not bad at all. With occasions, Scandal pour Homme Intense pretty much falls in the same bowl as most of its cousins - partying and clubbing. It can definitely work as a daily too, or even for evening dates. But honestly, I would never recommend this or any of the other fragrances from the Scandal line to someone over 25 years old. Even though Scandal pour Homme Intense will be seen as the more "mature" Scandal purely because of that misleading leather in the notes pyramid, it's still very clearly aimed towards the younger demographic. The whole line has that youthful edge, mainly because of that synthetic sweet combo and that weird "bad boy" vibe I get from the Scandal line as a whole. So, it's another unfortunate candidate. The scent resembles the Le Parfum flanker quite closely, which is definitely not something I missed, and the leather is not really there, which adds to my disappointment furthermore. However, I'm more disappointed in myself for having any sort of expectations from this. The only pros here, in my opinion, are the performance and the marketing. This (and the whole Scandal lineup) is clearly dedicated and marketed towards the youth, teenagers, Gen Z, etc. So in the end, if the fragrance finds its right fanbase (and it will, since anyone more invested in perfumery and niche will stay away from this), then it will also find plenty of success. That's pretty much all most companies care for these days. nulltheless, I think Scandal pour Homme Intense concludes it for me - the Scandal line is not for me. It never was and it will never be. Overall Rating: 6.5/10

Scandal Intense has an aromatic woody sweet opening with a touch of Leather, but it's very subtle. I also got a few whiffs of Tonka Bean and Cardamom in the opening The longevity is very good, it lasts approximately 12 hours on my skin. This fragrance projects great with about a 6 ft radius for the first hour, and a skin scent after. (Depends on skin types ) Overall Rating (8,5/10) In my honest opinion, it's a redundant release if you already own the previous Scandal flankers. It's not really a leather fragrance, but more of a "fresher/aromatic" version of the original Scandal.

The scent starts off zesty and pleasantly sweet, reminiscent of its brothers (with the big difference that thankfully nothing is sticky here). However, the youthful burst of freshness fades after just a few minutes, and more maturity takes the reins. As it develops further, for me, nothing but dry wood takes the lead, although I also believe I can detect some nutmeg as well as a decent portion of tonka (similar to Code edp). Leather is announced, but it is hardly discernible or can only be constructed with imagination: in fact, earthy, subtly animalistic accords join in, which could remind one of leather. This one has very little in common with its predecessors, which may be a relief for some. Note: definitely test the scent on skin - the test strip delivers drastically more synthetic notes and sweetness than my skin.

I had this fragrance as a sample with another purchase and initially thought nothing of it, but after just a brief test, I was immediately surprised by how wonderful the scent was. I was completely taken by this DNA and had to keep smelling it again and again in the following days. After a short consideration, I decided to buy it because I was simply addicted to it. It does smell quite synthetic, but not unpleasant and interesting at all. Otherwise, I unfortunately can't categorize the scent well, which adds to the factor of mystery for me.

So this fragrance is quite simply structured. The top note is sage ... In the heart note leather ... and in the base vetiver. Apparently, I really like scents with leather and vetiver because I find this one really good. Scandal Pour Homme Intense honestly pleases me a lot. I have to say it does come across as slightly synthetic but not at all disturbing. Not in a way that makes you think, wow, what a cheap fragrance, but it really smells good. You can really notice the leather, which I find very pleasant, and I truly believe leather is my thing when it comes to perfumes. It's a fragrance for young people, I think, who go out partying, etc... The price-performance ratio is also really good. The bottle is beautifully made, just as you would expect from Jean Paul Gaultier. I don't even know what else to say about it. It's just a really solid fragrance, especially for the price. You can easily wear it in everyday life, whether it's summer or winter. It's just a scent that always works. And it's not like the fragrance bothers anyone or anything. I believe it doesn't disturb anyone when you wear it. It's simply a fragrance that smells nice but isn't overpowering. Very masculine, in my opinion, with no room for unisex or anything like that... For me, it's definitely a good all-rounder that I enjoy using.

I really like this scent; you can clearly recognize the Scandal line in it. Very present but not intrusive, with good recognizability. The leather is hardly noticeable to me, which I actually like. The Scandal line continues to impress me time and again. I find the longevity top-notch; you can still perceive it in the afternoon.

Looking behind the facade of "Scandal pour Homme Intense | Jean Paul Gaultier," it could rightly become scandalous: Here, someone is trying to imitate leather, but the obvious synthetic quality reveals a sweet insecurity.

The first time I tried Byredo's Bal d'Afrique a few years ago I thought "meh … just another EDC parading around as an EDP". Then a fascination with Neroli began and I had the opportunity of smelling it on a friend … and found it lovely! Truthfully, this is a very expensive fragrance for what it is … in fact, the entire line is overpriced imho, but I suppose it all comes down to what one is willing to pay for. I was lucky enough to secure a 'once sprayed' bottle from a friend who was spring cleaning her collection at a very decent price. Replacing it once it is gone will be a bit of an issue :). I was completely amazed to find that this fragrance contains buchu, which as a South African I know very well in the form of the vile concoction 'Boegoe Brandy', a sort of snake-oil-cure-all remedy used in this country for centuries. I suppose it tastes a bit like Jaegermeister … but a lot rougher. The plant smells vaguely minty and camphorous with a fresh, berry-like note. It's not indigenous to where I live in the North East occurring primarily in the West of the country, but I have had occasion to smell it in it's natural state … once I made the connection it became quite obvious that Bal d'Afrique contains a good dose! It's quite unique smelling, but this fragrance also contains a sweetened Vetiver, which I love! Neroli essential oil is VERY strong, but it is well controlled here in concert with the other top notes. I do get quite a lot of Violet from this frag bringing a soft sweetness along with it. I'm of the mind that this is what might be taming the Vetiver and keeping it from being overly root-like. My biggest issue with Byredo is the cost proportional to concentration. This is marketed as an EDP, but it must be at the very bottom end of the oil-to alcohol ratio, because even if the sillage here is satisfactory, longevity is an issue and overspraying to correct that proves costly. I've had quite a bit of success spraying my clothes, however, so that's one way of increasing the lifespan of Bal d'Afrique. I recommend this fragrance to anyone who enjoys a different take on the classic EDC. Bal d'Afrique is interesting and unique … quite a joy to wear! A note about cost: 100mls of Bal d'Afrique costs $220 from the website. I love the simplicity of the bottle, but I guess a substantial part of the price resides in the exquisite, but imho, unnecessary packaging. An outer sleeve plus an inner box with a cut out space for the bottle AND a card with the marketing blurb are irrelevant. I'd buy loads of this if it came less expensively packaged. I feel the same way about byKillian. Strangely enough, fancy packaging always makes me wonder what the product is lacking … food for thought!

Bald Freak she is not, as this is the scent of the most luscious hair I can imagine. Most people seem to brand BdA a citrus, but to my nose she smells like an artisanal shampoo made of marigold blossoms. Bright, zesty, complex, with a “cosmetic-y” core. Like the scent of a celebrity after being gussied by an elite beauty team. However, I feel like she could complement wearers of any age, in any season. Astute reviewer @heliotrope72 said it smelled like “a type-A person on vacation,” and yup, I see it. I've never smelled anything else quite like BdA. She will probably be the next Byredo I buy a full bottle of because I'm on my fifth tester vial. Lifespan is, alas, mid. The things we do for the beautiful… Mental Snapshot: The morning starts with a neroli oil deep tissue massage, followed by a cocoa butter Lomi Lomi. Every cuticle is caressed, every hair coaxed into skeins of silk. As you recline in your chair, you’re primped, powdered, spritzed, styled, and maybe even titivated. You’ve never been Photoshopped once in press. Not when you look this good. tl;dr: A-list salon

In a brand full of crowd-pleasing fragrances, Bal D'Afrique is probably the most crowd-pleasing-est of them all. People love this fragrance. And damn it, I love this fragrance too. It's kind of hard not to. I like to think of it as a sparkly, sunlit version of Vetiver Tonka, made all giggly with forest fruit, violets, and lemon. It is one of those perfumes that seems to be all things to all people. Some describe it as musky, cedary violets, some as a creamy lemon scent, and some as a fruity, nutty vetiver. And truth be told, it's all of those things, and more. Nothing about Bal D'Afrique stands out and that feels like a deliberate decision. Nudged more firmly in one direction or another, it could easily have been pegged as a vetiver fragrance, a woody violet, a fruity floral, even a foodie amber. But Bal D'Afrique contains a touch of everything and doesn't press down too hard on one particular note, so it ends up playing like a low-key medley of tunes you hear in a cocktail lounge - wonderfully pleasing but sparkling at a low enough wattage so as not to distract from conversation.

Unless I find something better on my perfume journey, this will be my signature scent. I love it the most among the other perfumes in my collection and wish list. It is very unique, recognizable, well-blended, and non-offensive scent. I can’t complain about the longevity and sillage; it lasts quite a while on my skin. It is expensive, but considering the quality, I think it's worth it.

This fragrance is very well blended a mixture of soft vetiver with a little sweetness, and a bit floral. Perfect for a summer day and one of the few summer fragrances that really stand out. Performance could be better but this is not a screamer. 3 hours in it becomes a skin scent. Very pleasant soft and unique.

When I saw the hype and the hysterical love for this scent, one can only wonder how is it? After I got my sample with an order from a lovely German shop, I thought that maybe is a girly scent, proper for someone liking "Santal Complet" type of sun tan lotion smells. But then I realized that this can be so much more.

Story Time: Back in 2019, I was on my honeymoon in Switzerland, and I stayed at the Sheraton in Zurich. They had this amazing set of soap, shampoo, and lotion called Le Gran Bain. It was like a little slice of heaven! The occasion was romantic, and the Swiss countryside was just breathtaking.

I took an immediate liking to Byredo BAL D'AFRIQUE but was confounded as to what this perfume reminded me of. It was on the tip of my tongue, but I could not figure it out. Then I took a look at the other site and saw that five people had listed Hermessence VETIVER TONKA as a smell alike. Then it dawned on me: they were right!

I love the initial burst of bright fruit before the floral and woody notes come through. It smells like summer but somewhere hot and dry like Arizona or a desert rather than somewhere tropical and humid. The citrus notes come and go for a few hours, before the earthy and woody notes take over. From time to time, a slight powdery note appears.

I’m underwhelmed by this influencer-overhyped and overpriced fragrance. For me, Byredo’s Bal d’Afrique is a rather boring and predictable citrus scent. The opening is a slightly metallic neroli jolt followed by a softly cloying floral. I find the silage limited and the longevity on my skin is around 4 hours.

Today I report once again from my humor course, to which our partners were also invited this time. Despite some mild surprise, everyone showed up, and the course leader explained that it would again be about "involuntary comedy." For the first exercise, all couples were to sit opposite each other at a table and exchange ideas as if they were having dinner in a restaurant. It seemed strange to us, but we did it. After five minutes, he asked us to simulate an argument over a trivial matter, which displeased some - but hey, we wanted to learn something... Then, after a short while, the instructor interrupted our bickering and said: "Can you now imagine how funny it sometimes looks to a third party when you are eating together?" Instantly, there was silence in the room, everyone thought for a moment and had to admit that this witnessing of their own whining had happened more often than they would like to admit. But none of us laughed about it. Why should we? Silence. Our course leader then became increasingly nervous, muttering to himself for motivation "involuntary comedy, involuntary comedy..." under his breath, and was then momentarily relieved that he thought of an addition: "and when the couples are just two, they sit next to each other in silence after dinner! and observe the other guests for another hour, haha." Silence. Still silence. Then a murmuring... until it slowly formed into a grumble that was now directed at the course leader by all participants. He quickly fled the room with the remark "I need to step out for a moment." But it took so long that it seemed like his bladder was a cistern. So in the meantime, I’ll share my notes on Hugo Now: Since this boss has a much too short lifespan on the skin, I had to spray it on my shirt, where it seems a bit more intense: The first 5 minutes are quite fresh, fruity, citrusy, and with a hint of aquatic - nice for summer, I thought. But already in the next 40 minutes, this Hugo reveals itself to be a relatively thin, albeit spritzy little water. I hardly smell any cardamom or lavender, but the mint could provide the bright freshness effect. Then a bit more green comes through, the vetiver, which makes the scent a bit deeper. Unfortunately, that doesn’t last long, and the Now falls back into its slightly fruity "aquazone," which is far too synthetic to be truly enjoyable. Overall, this top note blender seems to be geared only for quick sales in the height of summer. Because its H&S are rather poor. But why not? After all, it’s called "Now" and thus stands for its short usage. And not everything has to be eternal. But that’s how the 20 minutes felt until our instructor finally returned from the restroom. Everyone had calmed down again. But still, once again Silence. Until a course participant suddenly stated: "Thank you for the great examples of your involuntary comedy." I could only agree, and so my conclusion for today’s lesson is just like for our course leader and this Hugo Now: Dynamic start, but weakling :)

Hugo now, after the very good Hugo Extreme. What a run, what a great strategy to continue this success story. At first, one is thrilled by the surge of lightness and southern well-being that emerges. After that, nothing more. Can this be? After about ten minutes, there is simply nothing left. Is it the crisis with the current coronavirus and the house arrest, or is the sample over? It can't be, as this little bottle landed on my table about three weeks ago. Such a disillusionment for such a well-chosen name hasn't happened in a long time. For Coty and the many good products at the moment like Cool Water Intense, Joop Wow for Men Intense, or Boss Bottled Oud, the products have been on quite an upward trend. Unfortunately, this jester ruins the spring mood, as one can expect more, since it only comes with mint and a bit of vetiver. For fragrances that have relatively few ingredients, this Now is completely off the mark. A cologne would be acceptable like this, but a normal eau de toilette borders on unfair competition. The Mäurer&Wirtz products from Baldessarini even last a bit longer, or even the unspeakable Diesel are more noticeable. It's a shame and unfortunately absolutely not recommendable for a fragrance that one wants to perceive for at least a few hours. Not being able to recognize anything after such a short time is the wrong way for the younger Boss or Hugo fragrances, which is very regrettable.

This fragrance does not need to hide! This morning, I sprayed a spritz of "Hugo Boss now" and "Dolce & Gabbana light blue intense" on my wrists.
