In the first 3 hours, "Hugo Boss now" was very noticeable. In particular, the fresh, aquatic, and citrus notes came to the forefront. Personally, I really like the scent. It feels extremely refreshing and is, in my opinion, very suitable as a summer, office, or sports fragrance. I can also imagine that this fragrance will receive many compliments and is "easy to like." At this point, I even found the scent better than "light blue intense." Although the longevity of the fragrance is truly outstanding for an aquatic perfume, it does change over time (after hour 3) unfortunately. After a while, it smells less citrusy and more minty, but also more synthetic. The scent is still not bad, just unfortunately not as good as in the first hours. However, "D&G light blue intense" does not change as much and still smells very fresh and good after 7 hours. After hour 7, "D&G light blue intense" unfortunately started to fade slowly, while I could still perceive "Hugo Boss now" for about 9 hours after spraying. In summary, "Hugo Boss now" is, in my opinion, a super fragrance. It lasts long and smells really good, especially at the beginning. At least in the first hours and after hour 9, it can easily compete with other summer fragrances like "D&G light blue intense"!

Today I sprayed and tested Hugo Now on my wrist. About the scent: The fragrance starts off very refreshing and invigorating. Super fresh and aquatic. To put it briefly, I am simply thrilled with Hugo. Is this really from Boss??? A lot has been said about this fragrance, but there’s one thing I absolutely have to mention. As I said, I was positively surprised because the longevity of this perfume lasted quite a long time. From experience, I know that many Boss fragrances unfortunately struggle with longevity. Please correct me if I am wrong in your view. This Boss is truly a Boss, a Boss of Refreshment! Who is this fragrance suitable for? This scent is an all-rounder. Ideal for spring (in nice weather), especially better in summer, on warmer days it feels very refreshing. Conclusion: Really highly recommended, fresh, invigorating, and sporty. This fragrance has good performance. About 3 hours have passed and I can still smell it well. I haven't found anything as long-lasting, invigorating, and refreshing since Frozen Cologne. Super Boss, keep it up! I hope that when new flankers come out, they perform just as well as this one. This flanker is worth buying. Clear purchase recommendation.

Even though Hugo Now is no longer blue but green (the liquid), the scent is still the same: fresh, aquatic, a bit green. Lemon and mint at the beginning, later aquatic notes (possibly Calone) as well as some vetiver and fresh lavender. For me, it's a nice freshie, very clean. I like to wear Now in combination with sports activities or in my leisure time during the summer. It also works very well after showering. Of course, it is weak in performance, lasting only 2 hours and having no real projection. However, that's not what this type of fragrance is about for me. If you see it as a fresh all-rounder that you can easily reapply, then it's a great release. I got it for €29 for 75ml at the drugstore. At this price: Definitely grab it or at least test it!

Hugo Hugo Iced was an interesting case. Super mono - pure mint but well executed. Ultimately, however, it is too monotonous for me to be more than a mini refreshment. Here, the concept is taken and given an aquatic touch in the opening. Cardamom at the beginning with citrus notes for spice and simultaneously a slight fruitiness.

Opening - Sharp ginger and lemon, extreme 4711 vibes. Unfortunately, it doesn't stop at the top note but rather runs consistently through the entire scent development for me. I was really looking forward to sweet, creamy, slightly powdered marshmallows, but they unfortunately get overshadowed too much. Through the screaming, shrill ginger-lemon mixture, which I can still perceive on my skin even after 24 hours. The longevity here is absolute "Beastmode," as one would now say in an "influencer" way ;-). It really lasts a long time. Anyone who likes the scent has a 24-hour companion here. There is indeed a certain similarity to LDBS, yes. But LDBS does not have this screaming ginger-citrus note for me. However, it must be said that LBDS also doesn't shine as much. Those who like this fragrance direction may have found an even better, especially cheaper companion in Pin Up. Unfortunately, this Pin Up doesn't resonate with me and I hope it makes someone else happy :)

I believe it’s no secret that I worship marshmallow scents!:D The first marshmallow scent that continues to blow me away to this day is Kilian Love Don't Be Shy... I don’t think I need to say much more except that every time I spray or wear this paradise scent, I float on cloud 7 and am simply happy and content all day long:)) The Princess is also a divine and seductive marshmallow scent, but it is lighter and creamier, as well as fluffier than the LDBS. Dragee by Reminiscence is indeed an almond scent, BUT even though no marshmallow note is listed in the fragrance pyramid, I can smell the hidden marshmallow note much more intensely than the almond note. The Dragee is also a beautiful and delightful marshmallow scent that leans heavily towards Kilian LDBS, but it is not a dupe. Giorgio Armani Si Fiori is also a beautiful and fluffy as well as very, very creamy and noble marshmallow scent, accompanied by very feminine and soft floral notes. So why am I listing all these treasures now? To make it short, I know from many, as well as from myself, that Kilian Love Don't Be Shy is simply very expensive or doesn’t fit into the budget.... I wanted to find a scent that would truly convince just as much and smell almost 1-to-1 like the LDBS. And as always, this is a challenge to find a dupe that really smells like the beloved perfume that one cannot or does not want to afford, or even worse, when the scent is no longer produced/sold. Of course, no scent smells 1-to-1 like another, but this difference is hardly noticed by our fellow humans, much more by ourselves or better said, by our scent noses;D Be that as it may, the search was fun (for me at least:D) as I was able to discover more scent treasures on this fragrance journey. (I mainly searched for marshmallow scents) I found what I was looking for through a very, very dear and esteemed perfumer, namely the lovely Elenasmom:)) If you’re reading this, thank you so much again for the great recommendation:) I got a hint that Classique Pin-Up by JPG is a good dupe (if I may call it that) or at least a very good alternative to Kilian LDBS. Admittedly, at first, I was very, very unsure whether this scent would appeal to me since I had read several times that the ginger note was more prominent than all the other fragrance notes. The annoying thing about it is that Classique Pin-Up is/was a limited perfume and I missed out on it... But I was able to snag a decant of it, so I can at least test it:)) Since I still have a good amount of decant from Kilian Love Don't Be Shy and now also a nice decant from JPG Classique Pin-Up, I can make/write a little comparison:)) I will now compare both to see if the Pin-Up is really a good dupe for the LDBS:)) The scent... JPG Classique Pin-Up (Top Note): Starts with a very prominent ginger note that, while it tickles a bit in the nose at first, can be very refreshing, for example, in the morning;)) The lemon note gives the scent a very fine freshness:) Kilian Love Don't Be Shy (Top Note): Also starts with a refreshing orange blossom note that wonderfully brings a fine juicy nectar note with it.*.* The marshmallow note doesn’t take long to appear and presents itself in the top note from its most beautiful side. JPG Classique Pin-Up (Heart Note): And finally, the hoped-for marshmallow note arrived!*.* I must say I am speechless! Soooo wonderfully creamy, fluffy, subtly creamy and milky at the same time... The marshmallow note in Pin-Up merges with the skin just like in LDBS. In LDBS, the marshmallow note is accompanied by a dark caramel note, whereas Pin-Up is a pure marshmallow scent with LDBS DNA. The orange blossom gently approaches the marshmallow note, which I personally like very, very much!*.* Although no rose note is listed, I think I can smell a very soft but also velvety and delicate rose note, BUT as already mentioned, in Pin-Up the marshmallow note is the most prominent and intense to smell. Kilian Love Don't Be Shy (Heart + Base Note): Marshmallow, velvety roses paired with a dark caramel note that brings a mysterious depth with it. The orange blossom is still present and merges with each individual note into a magical and sensual progression like hardly any other! Especially on my skin, it feels like a spell that touches my soul anew every time!*.* JPG Classique Pin-Up (Base Note): The marshmallow paradise on my skin is also unmistakable*.* I can also slowly perceive the vanilla, but very softly and powdery. Vanilla powder is sprinkled over the marshmallow, and next to the marshmallow mountain, fine but fragrant orange blossoms are placed.... I can only say it’s addictive and downright seductive!:D I can only say one thing, both are worth being included in any perfume collection! Especially if you like sweet scents, particularly if, like me, you have a great love for marshmallow scents.:)) And yes, the Pin-Up is a very good alternative to the LDBS, especially if you like to save. The longevity and sillage are very good, especially on clothing, lasting until the next day. I can only say I am simply happy to have discovered such a beautiful scent that brings me great joy every time I spray it, but also seduces me!;))

Since I took the plunge into the rabbit hole of fragrance arts three years ago, I have discovered quite a bit. For a long time, all fragrances smelled the same to me - no matter what I sniffed in the standard perfumeries, everything was basically La Vie est Belle L'Eau de Parfum to me. Thanks to Parfumo, and the great samples and sharings here, completely new worlds opened up. I tried countless brands, niche - from Amouage to XerJoff - and indie, extremely expensive fragrances and extremely hard-to-get scents (Hello "Kiste | Slumberhouse"). I fell in love countless times, saw new horizons and fragrance notes that I had never smelled before. Yet, I never found the ONE fragrance that captivated me so much that I only wanted to smell it. Then, quite unexpectedly, after a question about possible relatives of "Mon Précieux Nectar | Guerlain," I was recommended Classique Pin-Up in the forum. Okay, why not order it - after all, I had already bought fragrances in completely different price categories blindly. I liked the Guerlain, this one should last longer. The reviews are okay. Why not test it - if necessary, sell it in the souk. When it arrived, the bottle was already very kitschy and the lemon-ginger note at the start was a bit strange. But at the same time "strange." Everything that followed was grandiose!!!! An adult marshmallow hint with pleasant vanilla and gentle feminine orange blossom envelops me. Carried by amber, my favorite fragrance note, which I perceive here in such a way that it subtly makes me addicted without being animalistic or intrusive. Still, it is not banal or standard. It could definitely be niche quality. Pin Up is ME! Soft, friendly, sweet without being sticky, cuddly warm, but completely without kitsch! Not intrusive, just wonderfully fluffy without being childish. A pure feminine dream. And this, despite the fact that it is not hyped at all. It lasts all day on me and is noticeable, but never intrusive. It has a fine sillage, but completely within bounds. Perfect! A go-to fragrance that works just as well at work as it does for cuddling. I just want to smell like this all the time. Thus, it came to pass that Mrs. Silverwheel chose a banal designer flanker as her signature scent after a 3-year fragrance journey. And this, after she has never tolerated JPG fragrances and long since renounced the topic of "signature" due to the variety of scents ("why should you only wear ONE fragrance?? How boring!") Sometimes, there is no rational answer to the question. You just wear the fragrance so often in 2 months as others do with their "favorite fragrances" in 2 years. Sometimes a fragrance simply finds you and takes hold of you. You no longer wonder what you want to wear in the morning; you spray automatically. And you indulge in the fluffy bliss of your great fragrance love. Okay, occasionally I still "stray," but I always come back by evening at the latest. ;-) I am curious how long this great love will last. One thing it definitely deserves: a dedicated review!!! Therefore, I warmly recommend Pin-Up to anyone who loves soft, feminine-cuddly, agreeable, yet extraordinary fragrances - especially now in autumn. I think we will have a lot of fun together.

This fragrance is the perfect combination of fresh and sweet, woods, incens, lemon and vanilla are the stars here. Very unique and works in all seasons and situations. even thou it doesn't last long or project that well, the weak performence works for this fragrance thou because it makes it more appealong and intimate for the special someone.

I love casual and down-to-earth scents which convey feeling of being outdoors, but many of them are so harsh and chemical. Gypsy Water is such a beautiful exception in this category. The scent is a natural, soft and creamy combination of woods and vanilla spiked with ever-green needles and juniper berries. It has a perfect balance of being casual but not boring, linear but not simple. Gypsy Water is my jeans and sweater companion to cuddle with on cold November nights. Lovely, easy to wear and natural, I could never go wrong wearing this scent. The lemon and bergamot opening makes me think of a windy day outdoors – refreshing and natural. Yet, right away, the warm rays of sandalwood and vanilla shine through the scent making it soft and comforting. The iris adds just a touch of powder and pine-tree and juniper berries keep the composition winter fresh. The scent has a bit of a linear quality but it does not bother me at all, as the composition is absolutely lovely. It is a soft scent, which makes it a great every day casual scent. And though it is quite light, it does lasts for hours. Gypsy Water is not the scent that will shock you with its super complex composition or fireworks of notes. But it is a scent that I will take with me on a winter skiing trip, a walk in the park or everyday at work. It was such a pleasure to wear that I finished my sample in no time and now craving for the full bottle. Overall score is 8.5/10

Sometimes I miss Gypsy Water so much! So enjoyable, so subtle, so pleasent... but for its longevity it's on my black list :D Really, I don't know any other scent that lasts on skin for 20 minutes and diseapper! I know that I'm not the only one, so this is not my skin's fault. I spent a lot of time looking for a good dupe but I didn't find one yet. Such a shame!

... But dissipates quicker than any perfume I've ever tried! It truly smells like you're in a nordic forest, picking juniper berries. It smells so delicious. However, it quickly disappears. Not just the sillage disappearing, but I couldn't even smell it off my arm or even my clothes. I've never had this happened before and I've tried countless perfumes like a lot of you, from body mists to niche fragrances way out of my budget. I'm so perplexed by the poor longevity, and it's not being anosmic to it either. I don't mind fragrances having no sillage as long as I can smell it on me, I wear fragrance only for me, nobody else. But when I can't smell it myself, what's the point? :-( So the sample was enough with this.

Why did they have to name it like that??? Culturally insensitive name aside, this is a very nice and complex scent. From a very realistic pure lemon with a spritz of bergamot in the opening, it develops into a softly somewhat creamy fruity/citrusy light sandalwood. I think the frankincense creates a lightly smoky twist to the citrus notes but for me it is not really noticeable. A very nice fragrance, different to a lot of other popular byredo scents, which mostly for me are far too sweet and usually a fruity mess.

I was reminded of two perfumes upon donning Byredo GYPSY WATER: Giorgio Armani ACQUA DI GIOIA and Fresh BROWN SUGAR. It's less sweet than both and certainly better made than the former, which can become quite sticky, if liberally applied.

There is something enchanting and cozy about gypsy water that is hard to describe. But the performance is bad and it really clouds my judgement to rate this well. I get the bergamot, oris root, vanilla, and sandalwood the most and it’s a cozy, yet an uplifting scent that I think could be worn in most seasons.

My god. There's something about this perfume that is so alluring - don't wear it in my presence if you don't want me following you around like a truffle dog. I mean, there's a reason why it's so popular: it's just the perfect blend of woody aromatics and non sweet vanilla. Not trying hard, she's just naturally like this.

Gypsy Water was love at first sniff. I sprayed it at an airport duty free and my first reaction was "Wow, this feels unique to me." I am not normally one to love super citrusy perfumes, but this one I like. The citrus note doesn't turn into a more sour body odor scent the way a lot of others do and I have to say I really love the combination of vanilla, incense and juniper.

I really like this perfume, it’s like wearing Gin&Tonic in a good way. It’s fresh, spicy, woody and powdery. And it’s easy wear, you can’t go wrong with this. I have thoroughly enjoyed of this perfume. Unfortunately the longevity and sillage are extremely poor even when overspraying.

Tested today at the Nocibé perfumery. I had seen it released on the website. The opening reminds me a lot of Boss Just Different, then after an hour, a deep freshness is revealed, sometimes reminiscent of Chrome Legend. Generally speaking, this is a fragrance that appeals more to a teenage audience or young men under 25. An all-terrain, all-season fragrance that will suit many, especially since the sillage is decent and the lasting power is between 8 and 10 hours.

The way it develops and evolves has me SMILING. It’s as if they removed all of the “old school minty barbershop” notes and left everything else behind... hard to describe the notes... familiar, but I can’t quite remember where I’ve felt it before... It starts to sweeten up as all of the brothers do, but with a different swing in style; think right handed, not left handed, if that makes any sense. I’m getting an almost leather vibe here as it dries down. You can recognize the family, but it’s not the same father... a “half brother” if you will. It feels rather soft in projection, and that is unfortunate, because I really, REALLY love the way this one develops... Sillage is decent; but as with most of the Le Male line, you’ll get obligatory fatigued, and left uncertain if your trail is still there. I’m happy with my purchase, and I’ll wear it regularly, with pride.... now if I could get my hands on the “Le Parfum” my life would be completed.

Arrived today, ripped from the packaging, sprayed on... and initially very disappointed. "What a dud!" was my first thought, partly because the scent strongly reminded me of classic cucumber (don't ask me where that comes from, everyone has their associations - and "cucumber" isn't exactly something that makes me jump for joy). Fortunately, it didn't stay at those cucumber-like exhalations; the scent has really developed strongly over the last three hours. Sillage feels strongest after about an hour, and the fragrance shifts from cucumber (prominent for the first ~3 minutes) to herbal, until eventually the geranium shines through (which I really love) and is now replaced by a rather minty scent (that might be the violet leaf combined with the other notes, as mint doesn't appear in the fragrance pyramid here). I can't detect the tonka bean, although I thought I sensed something in that direction earlier... but now it's gone. So far, a very pleasant scent that doesn't bother me, but also doesn't blow me away, as it comes across as quite simple; it's acceptable for the price, but not a must-have. The bottle is typically JPG-masculine and I also really like the tin can! All in all, a solid purchase that reminds me a bit of Eros Flame (probably due to the geranium). PS: I am positively surprised by how much my girlfriend likes the scent - so from now on, a bit more fougère.

Le Mâle was and still is my most frequently repurchased perfume ever. As far as I can remember, I received my first bottle in 1998, and since then, I have always had a bottle of this fragrance in my collection. Now there are so many extensions of Le Mâle that it's almost impossible to keep up... I still have a bottle from 2007, which I cherish very much! The best extension of Le Mâle for me so far has been the Popeye Edition and the Terrible, both truly fine descendants of the original, albeit somewhat altered, which I enjoy using from time to time. But one starts to think that it should be enough, yet it seems they will continue to milk the Le Mâle cow, and it seems to be worth it ;) I sprayed this one quite unprejudiced last week at Müller. Crazy, but I felt a bit transported back to 1998 when I held my first Le Mâle bottle in my hand. The typical DNA is now very well detectable here in Aviator, almost like back then... With the difference that Aviator is initially a bit fresher, like the Popeye Edition, and there is less cinnamon, with a slightly herbal/green note coming through. However, it quickly shifts towards sweetness, thanks to the tonka and vanilla. Even though lavender is not listed here, I believe I can still smell it quite well. Another difference is the longevity and sillage. These are significantly reduced compared to the original from back in the day, which I consider very good, as it allows you to wear the fragrance wonderfully at work without overwhelming anyone ;) In summary: An extension of Le Mâle that (in my opinion) comes very close to the original from the early days, yet is somewhat fresher/herbaceous/greener with less punch, making it suitable for everyday wear. Oh, I am happy that there is the Le Mâle Aviator; it at least somewhat replaces the original from back in the day, and I no longer feel like I have to chase after a rare bottle from the 90s for many euros ;)

Hmm... Well, if you want to play the good son-in-law and are out of your adventurous times, this is the right choice for you! Very green, fresh, and with just a hint of Le Male in the air. I think there are much better fragrances in this scent and price category.

I personally quite like this fragrance and wear it regularly at work and in my free time. It is not a wild Ultra Male that you would wear in a club, but rather the slightly more mature Le Male. It is an elegant and pleasant everyday scent that won't knock you out with its intensity.

New day - new flanker. This time with Aviator, a truly rare scent by now - difficult to even get hold of. Even though it has absolutely nothing to do with flying, the green color of the bottle is a hint of where it’s headed. Le Male DNA: 10-20 percent, again very low. Without the series connection, I wouldn’t have been able to recognize any relation here.

This will not be a long review. Upon trying this fragrance today my nose was assaulted by a chemical soup in which some bright spark thought it would be rather grand to make jasmine flavored vanilla ice cream and serve it in a freshly carved wooden bowl. YUCK!! I very seldom react this way to fragrances, loving the art form of perfumery as much as I do. There is, however, a limit as to what I would shell money out for … and I find it completely shattered by Boss: The Collection - Silk Jasmine. As a costume designer, I was intrigued by the combination of fabric and fragrance … until I smelled this. Vanilla and silk have nothing to do with each other … freshly spun silk smells raw and sexy, not smooth and sweet, which this chemfest fails dismally at anyway! Avoid at all costs!!

This is a WONDERFUL fragrance. Silk & Jasmine is part of an exclusive line of fragrances that are available only through Nordstrom's, Harrod's or the Hugo Boss website itself. There are five fragrances in this line, which is named "Hugo Boss: The Collection". The five fragrances are: Velvet & Amber, Wool & Musk, Cotton Verbena, Cashmere Patchouli and of course, Silk & Jasmine. Silk & Jasmine is fresh and sweet with a very light powdery scent. The honey and vanilla are blended together beautifully, creating a smooth finish. It's classy and perfect with anything, anywhere. I'd consider this an excellent scent for the office, since you can spray it on yourself several times and not worry about it being overwhelming, because it's light and stays closer to the skin. Sillage and longevity are average, so expect to get 4-6 hours out of an application. Even though it's considered a men's fragrance, it's easily unisex and no doubt would smell wonderful on a woman as well. The only downside is the price. At $140 for a 50 ml bottle, it's quite expensive and difficult to find. The Nordstrom's location close to my house didn't have samples or bottles available. I had to go through customer service, who transferred me to a store in California where they did have samples. The fragrance counter manager was kind enough to send them to me and in the end, I placed my order through him, so his counter could get the credit for the sale. If you're interested in getting samples, contact the fragrance counter at Nordstrom's at the Los Cerritos, California location or email Hugo Boss directly, through their website.

...,the experience is truly enchanting. Immediately after spraying, one is enveloped in delicious trails of honey and jasmine, delicately seductive, silky, and sensual. However, by the second minute, the fragrance wraps itself in silence. A noble silence, indeed... but it is silent. At best, a deep breath near the wrist conveys a vague hint of what was intended as the heart and base notes. Gentle creaminess, subtly spicy, a cautious shift towards hand soap. This is not unattractive, but somewhat arbitrary. I generally like to identify myself as a lover of finely crafted accents, but here the action is so silent that the term "olfactory experience" is actually inappropriate. "Stay a while, top note, you are so beautiful...!", one wants to call out to the fragrance. But hardly has it been said, the magic has already dissolved into thin air.

Mojave Ghost is one of two Byredo fragrances that I deemed full bottle worthy. They just do subtle and clean smelling fragrances better than a lot of companies out there. The opening to MG is pretty unique with the sapodilla fruit note. It then goes into some florals in the heart and ultimately dries down to a very creamy sandalwood. Clean, natural, luxury are the words that come to mind when I smell it. It’s perfect for the office or daily wear. It’s for someone who doesn’t want to announce to the world they are wearing a fragrance, but wants to smell nice for themselves and their loved ones when they give them a hug. Most of the moaning and groaning about the performance is confusing to me. I’ve never personally had issues with Mojave Ghost disappearing on me too quickly. I had someone compliment me on it at work about 7 hours into my shift and I’m not an over sprayer. One spray on the back of my neck, one spray on each forearm, and one spray on my shirt. Gives me about 8 hours of longevity with moderate projection for a couple hours and light projection the rest of the wear. I’ve noticed it is a pretty unique scent profile, so even in the latter part of the wear, if you walk past someone it gets noticed.

Actually, there is Sapodilla or Nesberry in the top notes. This tropical fruit note brings lingering sweetness to make sure MG doesn't turn into just another musky woody perfume. Then violet comes; adding this shadowy, floaty and a little mysterious vibes like a "ghost" vibe! and the name "ghost" suddenly makes sense! It is soft yet adds some depth to this perfume making it charming. MG shines so bright in hot weather. It clings to your clothes for a solid 24 hours and floats around you like a sweet little aura. This is very unisex, imo. Musky and woody notes balance the feminine energy that violet and magnolia bring while the Sapodilla keeps it vibrant.

Mojave Ghost from Byredo is a wistful floral. A little milky, a little woody, a little sad. With a gently soapy violet aspect to it, more like laundry soap than handsoap. Something that you might use to clean a dusty Edwardian frock. It first calls to mind the girls in their frothy ivory dresses from the film Picnic at Hanging Rock, and their mysterious disappearances. It makes me think of ruffles and lace period, I suppose, worn by people who’ve yet to encounter loss or grief. A child who one moment has no concept of death, and then in the next second when they learn of their missing sister who will never return, or their terminally ill relative or a grandparent who died in their sleep...and then with that knowledge that none of us will be here forever and eventually we’re all going to shuffle off of this plane of existence... things are just different. Perhaps we’re not going to disappear into a massive and uncanny geological formation, possibly ushered along by unseen forces (like the Hanging Rock girls) but that our lives will one day end is a certainty. Mojave Ghost smells like the moment just after you’ve come by this information, and you know you are never again going to be as happy as you were before you knew it.

What can I say about Mojave Ghost that hasn't already been said? Usually, I'm left feeling underwhelmed with "clean" scents. Why would I pay a premium just to smell like body wash or laundry detergent? But Mojave Ghost pulls it off. It's snuggling in the fresh sheets at a high end hotel, while eating a bowl of exotic fruit (I've never tasted prickly pear, so don't know if it's like that, but it's something like watermelon/pear/raspberry -- something of a tutti frutti quality to it). The longevity is solid -- about 3-4 hours of moderate projection, before settling down and eventually disappearing at the 5-6 hour mark. Really, this lightness is part of the charm. It makes me feel light and put together, ready to take on the day. In a very rare moment for me, I bought a full bottle a week after only smelling it in the store, without going through a tester decant first to make sure. I guess it truly does haunt you.

This is one of those you have to experience to understand that the scent notes are not enough to really decide where the scent will take you. Luxury hotel lobby is what comes to mind when I wear this perfume. It has a clean, floral sweetness and cozy feeling that makes you feel warm. It’s not overly sweet though, it’s more creamy and toned down which ends up affecting the performance. Byredo is for people who don’t want or care for others to smell their scent. I don’t mind a skin scent every so often, but this is way too weak unfortunately.

"mojave ghost" is such a suitable name for this fragrance. every whiff you take is captivating and ephemeral, yet the memory of it is gone in a blink. i've never smelled sapodilla before, but i imagine that's what makes this perfume so unique and addictive; it's green, fresh and sort of floral... very light on the nose. regardless, it is SO expensive!

My interest in unisex fragrances is growing. Perhaps it is due to a change in taste when it comes to different notes. Perhaps it is because I find them less complex, even though a lot of them are not. From Byredo I have Bal d’Afrique which I find absolutely stunning (review in the making) and I have Mojave Ghost, warmly recommended to me by a fellow parfumista.

The perfect white tee of fragrance. Dress it up, down, to work, to bed, to the gym. My most-worn scent to date. It’s even the scent I go to if I have a headache. MoGho is a cool rooftop evening in a bottle. Calm, airy, and perfectly unisex, without a hint of the “laundry” notes common to most clean fragrances.

Either this is the world's shortest lived perfume, or I'm completely amnosic to it after about 15 minutes. Probably the latter, as other people seem to smell it just fine, but I've never had that reaction to a fragrance before and it was wild to experience.

I have a dupe of this and its my most worn and favourite fragrance so far! It was amazing to wear this in the spring time and I will wear it in fall as well. For the hot summer time it was lacking something citrusy or aquatic for me but it totally blooms between temperatures 15-25 C degrees. The main note I get is ambrette which I absolutely love.

I want to say first that I’m not familiar with Jean Paul Gaultier, and I have never worn any of his fragrances before now. I’ve never tried the original Kokorico flanker, which sounds very dry and interesting, but when I heard Kokorico by NIGHT features cocoa and rhubarb together, I HAD to sample. (I won’t take time to explain my fascination with that tart smell of rhubarb, I don’t really understand it myself. All I know is, to me, it smells healthy.) But Kokorico by Night, as somebody else already said, smells like La Nuit by YSL. After wearing for awhile, off-and-on for a few days, on skin AND clothes, I have to agree. And I have decided Kokorico by Night isn’t unique enough or fascinating enough to hold my interest. That nice, tart rhubarb opening doesn’t last through drydown. Honestly, KbN reminds me TOO much of YSL La Nuit, which I consider headache-inducing. Nothing bad about KbN, but nothing special, either.

I found the original Kokorico to be somewhat neat: it’s pleasantly chocolatey with a slight tendency towards bitterness. Not a showstopper, but still quite acceptable and appetizing. In contrast, the night version feels like it was designed on a marketing drawing board. Surely, it was also inspired by L’Instant de Guerlain pour Homme Eau Extrême. But while the Guerlain fragrance is finely lemony and well-balanced, deserving of the gourmand label, Kokorico simply seems to be a mix of whatever can supposedly sell. The opening reminds me a bit of the fruity-sweet top note of 1 Million, before slowly revealing the dark chocolate. There’s also an interesting slightly soapy note in it. That would be relatively okay. But as it progresses, the fruity component increasingly takes over, causing Kokorico to suddenly mutate into another Paco Rabanne fragrance, namely Black XS. That one also has a strong strawberry/rhubarb aura and sells quite well. Whether one can still claim that for the Kokorico flanker, I doubt. Like some previous reviewers, I also don’t quite understand to what extent the designation “by Night” is justified here. The fragrance feels far too bright, too fruity, and almost too summery. Admittedly, the label “Sport” would also be too ridiculous for the Kokorico concept - as a “Summer Edition,” it would have been more believable. Especially since the fragrance doesn’t exactly boast great longevity. It certainly won’t last through a long winter club night until the rooster crows - even if it finishes with a typical sweet, soft vanilla/tonka bean note. An exciting scent journey with flirt factor is something else! Of course, Kokorico by Night is aimed at younger buyers, but I doubt this target group wants to grow old with this fragrance. I already predict that in a few years, no rooster will crow for it anymore!

I find the regular Kokorico good, but it clearly falls short in the chocolate gourmand perfume category compared to the competition from CK Shock or Guerlain LInstant. It would never make it into my collection; one simply expected much more from the good JPG. It will not become a classic, that much is already certain today. However, there were many buyers at the launch, that is also a fact, so this reissue came extremely quickly. Too quickly for my taste, but well, that’s how it gets tested. And surprise: It passes with flying colors, is liked better than the original, and even makes it onto my wish list! The bottle is fancier due to the play of colors than the already extravagant original. The longevity is very good at 9 hours. The sillage is average, about on par with the first Kokorico. The chocolate DNA is clearly noticeable here as well, but it does not stand alone in the forefront. The citrusy bergamot holds its own well, sometimes even taking the lead. Later, tonka mixes in slightly, but the two really settle it among themselves and blend wonderfully. I don’t smell rhubarb; I don’t even know what it should smell like^^. The name by Night doesn’t really fit, as the bergamot clearly brightens rather than darkens. The Kokorico in black is definitely more suitable for parties and going out than this variant. It’s a very nice mix that will please everyone who likes, for example, Rochas Man. Here, the bergamot and chocolate notes create a truly unique symbiosis. A pleasant surprise! It fits well, although it’s a simple combination, but nice to smell!

The original "Kokorico" is one of the most usable and balanced Gaultiers for me - with its sticky tear-off sailor notes and the absolute sugar cherry ice horror "Gaultier2," it can stay far away from me. "Kokorico by night" now presents itself as a rather unnecessary follow-up fragrance to the original. Constricted, aromatically dry start: it begins cocoa butter-like, somewhat dull and sweet at the same time. After a little more than three-quarters of an hour, a slightly tart rhubarb finally brings a bit more excitement into the mix, the scent opens up a bit but remains relatively close to the skin and aromatically constrained. Unfortunately, that's about it for the development of aromas; I really don't need to write a novel here. The drydown feels craftily usable, the sweetness fades away, leaving a gently acidulated cocoa butter, slightly drifting into bittersweet territory, with a hint of plum puree attached.

I discovered the fragrance by chance at Becker in Düsseldorf Central Station - so I immediately put it on my hand! At first, I found the top note to be unpleasantly bitter and piercing (it reminded me of wilted salad greens), and I was close to giving up. At some point, plum with coriander crystallized out; however, in such an overdose and so one-dimensional that it is definitely not a treat for the nose. If you still manage to be patient, the fragrance eventually becomes more bearable and bearable - it clearly shifts into an oriental-spicy direction. Clove, cinnamon, and rose set the tone, and the fragrance even has a slightly velvety quality. In the base, there’s the balsamic (benzoin) tinged chocolate note that is already so typical of the original Kororico, along with a strong pinch of sandalwood, which is so powerful here that it not only serves to round it out but also dominates the fragrance in a borderline way. The hint of leather and licorice, on the other hand, is pleasant, as it softens the somewhat "broad" sweetness. The promenade blend of "Opium pour Homme" and "Allure Homme" gets a wild touch of "DKNY Men" or "Egoiste". In the end, I am quite reconciled, finding the fragrance not particularly innovative, but quite pleasing. It is nice to wear, but on one hand, it could be a bit rounder, while on the other hand, it lacks that certain something that could truly excite me about it. For the quality of the ingredients, I find it rather expensive. To me, it has something of a masculine counterpart to "Coco Noir".

So so.. Kokorico by Night The main thing is that something new has been created! Pure disappointment and a complete waste of time, so I can't say much more about the scent.. but something must be said!! The fragrance starts off like its predecessor with a nice cocoa accord, but everything else that follows is just too sweet..

First of all, I actually own the fragrance and it is the original. A perfume that really surprises you. It is truly a good scent with medium sillage and good longevity. (I even tested it on my skin). I also own many other JPGs and can only say that those who like the JPG fragrance DNA will probably really enjoy Kokorico by Night.

just very briefly, he said, and I don't want to buy anything, just need a little funnel ... he said ... and the hair has to go, he said .. then I'll just quickly go to Friesen Hansel and be right back ... he said .. but he knew ... that the perfume dealer ... this woman L. ... right next door ... he knew it .... and she is even working ... he knew it .... in short, 3.

So, one thing upfront: This by night Kokorico has almost nothing to do with the night. The regular Kokorico is much more fitting. Well, maybe one could say that with this fragrance, you make the night involuntarily into day. The bergamot is for me at the beginning really just a very brief flicker. After that, the cocoa comes immediately and runs a bit parallel to the rhubarb.

the old flower water. Fortunately, I haven't encountered it in a long time, but with "Hugo Woman Extreme," it is really extreme. I don't know what this has to do with women. The perfume starts off quite pleasantly: fresh, classically elegant, slightly citrus-floral; the boysenberry, a hint of jasmine. For the first few minutes, it reminds me just a bit of "Chanel Chance Eau Tendre." For a moment, I even suspect a deliberate copy, as the bottle looks quite similar. But then it suddenly tips into that unpleasant smell of old flower water that I am familiar with from some perfume tests. Is it the ragwort? Or does it come from the mix of jasmine and black tea? Because when I sniff closely, I can break the scent down into these two components. But in the overall blend, it consistently produces a very unpleasant result. Over time, strong leather notes emerge.

Today I find a sample, wrapped in a pretty pink cover. Hugo Woman Extreme. Pink always attracts me - like the special paint job of a friend's limousine, which gave the rather staid body with a star a real flair. A wonderful surprise effect! And the scent also holds surprises. After the intensely sweet boysenberry, surprisingly a warm woolly note reaches my nose - but not scratchy. I consult my wool hat - and when you subtract the distinct sweetness, the scent is similar. Interesting. Did my dear Aunt Anne wear this scent while diligently knitting? Or the nice saleswoman in the shop "Wool Delight" from which she sources her "raw materials"? Or was this unusual note intentionally blended into the fragrance? Questions upon questions. I don't perceive any other ingredients - but I never thought this seemingly harmless scent would turn out to be so enigmatic.

"Clean girl". Perfume reviewers always use that, don't they? As their defining compliment: "She's a clean girl". Clean girl is cool. Clean girl is game. Clean girl is clean. Clean girl never gets pissy with a skin scent. She only smiles in a crisply-veneered manner. And then presents her mouth for her next nude lip balm du jour. She likes what the trend cycle likes, so evidently she’s a costalgrandmother-cottagecore-angelbaby who loves blueberry-milkshake-ozonics. If the cycle likes alpine-tradwife-oldmoney, she's a lactonic-bubblebath-gourmand babe who talks white linen notes and layers with three other vanillas. When I met Blanche I knew I wanted to be "clean girl". And for this scent, I'll admit: I was willing to try. I applied no-makeup makeup. I drank artisanal spring water watching videos of skincare ASMR. I removed all colour from my house and bought a Restoration Hardware cloud couch. I went to reformer pilates, semi regularly. I slept on silk pillowcases. I was fucking game. I can't say I didn't enjoy some of it. tl;dr: clean girl

There was a Disney Sleeping Beauty doll released in 1994, that came with a small bottle of "lily of the valley" perfume. This smells almost identical to that perfume, just a slightly more grown-up version. Although this doesn't match the notes, here's what it smells like to my nose: - lily of the valley - baby doll head (powdery/soft plastic) - creamy rose - faint iris It's all very creamy, soft, and well blended - feels like a fluffy lilac-colored cloud to me. I saw someone said it came across as more "screechy/synthetic laundry detergent" on their skin, and that's exactly what happened to me too for the first 30 minutes - literally like huffing generic dryer sheets with a too-sharp synthetic accord. While the opening is screechy and lasts a while, the dry down is worth waiting for!

I came to Byredo BLANCHE with zero preconceptions about this house, and my immediate reaction was "reminds me of Costume National SCENT SHEER." So, yes, it has that white noise, minimalist vibe. This composition seems a bit more complex and slightly green. The violet here must be violet leaves, because it is not at all sweet. The musk is clean, but this is not really my kind of thing. To me this is a unisex scent in a somewhat negative way: rather sterile and uninviting. I'm sure that others would like this, but to me it smells a bit like laundry starch. Try before you buy.

Blanche is clean, comforting, pure, and soft. It's evocative of taking freshly laundered white linen sheets that have been drying on the line in a cottage garden on a beautiful, bright spring day and wrapping yourself in them after you've had a long, luxurious Sunday morning bubble bath Performance wise, it is a moderately intimate scent. It's great for places you don't want your scent to be obtrusive. This is a perfume that people love to smell on you when they hug you because you just smell so clean and comforting. Yes, it smells like laundry detergent or white bar soap, but in the best, most luxurious way. If you wear perfume for the aromatherapy, this is ideal for calming you down and bringing peace. 9/10

Lovely fresh clean laundry scent. Very aldehidic and acuatic. A bit creamy. Calming and comforting, it's one of those that I wear to bed, spray on my linens or use in those ocassions where I need to stay calm (like a job interview, although I would advise to wear under the clothes in those moments, it projects a lot on my skin). Similiar to 724, but a bit more femenine than 724 I would say, also less crisp, more calming.

Those who like aldehyde-fresh fragrances should definitely try this. I don’t particularly enjoy soapy scents, hence the low score, but this is one of the best scents I’ve tried among soapy fragrances. It is very refreshing, and the other notes are not overshadowed by the aldehyde. Maybe this is why I don’t dislike this one as much as I dislike other soapy fragrances.

I’m an absolute psycho for clean linen aldehydic scents so I might be a bit biased - since most don’t, but if you’re scared of a sharp, astringent detergent scent. Fear no more. This takes 724 and Lazy Sunday Morning and tones up the aldehydes, and takes out some musk and rose - more emphasis on peony and violet.

As someone who doesn't like white floral / aldehydes, this was surprisingly inoffensive. It's light and clean. Not something I would reach for, but does not repel me either unless over sprayed. It is kind of a like a laundry detergent smell, or a judicious (by which I mean light handed) use of dryer sheets.

Yes this is a pretty consistent laundry scent, it has the exact same smell the laundry shop has - or the laundry spray they use on clothes. It doesn't have an evolution imo, it stays the same. It's clean, it's soapy, "white", crisp, pure but cold and 'distant'. Almost impersonal, detached.

Now, I love Byredo Blanche. Airy, light, clean. But I couldn't put my finger on what this familiar smell was until I was lathering up in the shower, and there it was, in a mist of hot steamy clean around me: Head and Shoulders Classic, not mint, not aloe, not 2 in 1. Classic. There, solved it, itch scratched.

After my husband pleasantly surprised me with Boss Femme - it has now become part of my signature scent collection - today Essence also caught my attention. My perfume dealer conspiratorially whispered to me: Take this one! It’s no longer available! And he was preaching to the converted! Essence is also characterized by an enchanting, serene femininity. Like Femme, it is creamy and soft, topped with a melting blackcurrant that has no compote character at all. Freesia and lily make the scent gently bright - and the rose adds a touch of velvet. Apricot skin is slightly mild-bitter, captured in warm sandalwood. A close scent - it sits like a second skin - without pressing or pulling anywhere. You slip into it, like your favorite soft ankle boots. Essence is like a reunion with the flawless Femme, just a bit deeper - a hint more mysterious. I wouldn’t want to miss either scent, as both emphasize my femininity - one more during the day - the other more in the evening.

"Aha, Hugo Boss, the suit tailor. Hugo Boss, the one with Boss Bottled and that macho advertising. Well." That's roughly what I thought whenever I encountered a Hugo Boss fragrance. So I avoided engaging with it at all. Until, yes until I was offered Essence de Femme and bought it more on a whim. Sure, I tried it, and at first I thought, okay, you didn't pay much for this, and for that it's quite good... Then I tried it a second time. And what greets me there? A wonderfully sparkling glass of champagne with a good portion of cassis. A Kir Royal as it should be! I really didn't expect that. Well, let's see how it goes on. And it continued just as beautifully. A fresh, aromatic mandarin/freesia scent, not sweet as expected, but fresh and green. I like this, I like it a lot! When the lily joins in with its full bloom and the jasmine shyly throws in a few blossoms, I am already more than satisfied with my purchase. No, I really didn't expect this from Hugo Boss. A real surprise. And I love such beautiful surprises. As it becomes fruitier again, I expect the cassis, but no, it's softer, sweeter. It's early summer in Barcelona, those delicious, small, firm apricots that are very light but incredibly aromatic and sweet. At the same time, the scent becomes calmer, warmer, and more intense, as amber kicks in and turns the Kir into what it really is, a KIR ROYAL. Well then, cheers. I'll gladly take that, even if the fizz could last a little longer. P.S.: the base lasts very long, it still smells this morning!

Boss Femme appealed to me from the very first moment; for me, it is a very noble floral scent. The name Femme is very well chosen, as it is not for little girls, who should rather buy Orange. It is very soft and feminine, this Boss, a truly beautiful composition of floral and fruity notes. When Essence de Femme was released, I was very curious and just as disappointed. My nose detects no difference, and there is no sign of the promised stronger intensity and longevity for me, really a shame.

Be warned that this is a fall/winter scent as heat affects the scent very much. Bibliothèque becomes very sweet and fruity and the notes are flattened in warmer weather but if worn during cooler days, you’ll get everything it promises to deliver. I find the notes listed are incomplete. For me, the opening is a burst of peach, patchouli and bergamot. 10 minutes later, it’s a pronounced parchment and musty old books, an old bookstore that has taken over. The vanilla and leather appear and interweave with the old books, plum and raspberry in the background. I get hints of incense and vetiver. The problem for me is the drydown where a peony powderiness takes over. No leather, no fruit, no smoke. Just old books and Victorian bathroom talc. Overall, Bibliothèque is a dry, dry, dry scent. As with most Byredo fragrances, the notes are detectably synthetic, which may or may not be a deal breaker for you. Just make sure to keep it cool if you plan to wear it.

As others have said...not actually for people who love books, libraries, and the scent of those things. Opening reminds me of Marc Jacobs Decadence. I love plums and other stone fruit in real life but apparently not in perfume. I felt like I was being dragged down by a dark, oppressive cloud of sweetness. Sickening and not in the good way. Gave me a headache and I could not wait around for the dry down. Scrubbed it off. In general Byredo fragrances are too sweet for me and this was no different. In theory I like the fruit notes. I wish they were juicy instead of smothered in high fructose corn syrup and synthetic leather. I imagine a leaner, fresher, less opulent interpretation would those notes shine.

Bibliotheque has an inscrutable character of discovery and familiarity. In that ambiguous sense, I can see how it resembles a library: a third place simultaneously dedicated to quiet comfort and deep growth. But beyond that, I find the comparison rather limiting. I perceive her as leathery-juicy but not in a gourmand, fresh, or chewing tobacco kind of way. (Get used to negative definition in this review.) The opening is old but resilient pleather and powdered juice mix. As overbearing as that sounds, it actually packs the punch of a feather. Enveloping but not overpowering. From this distance, the dissonant accords of leather and fruit basket appear natural, congruous. The mind tricks do not stop there. In its heart, Bibliotheque’s fruity character takes on a subtle aquatic sensation. It is not oceanic or river-fresh. It calls to mind Softsoap brand aquarium hand soap. Thematically consistent with the paradox of a library, this aquatic tint is sanitized but with an uncannily cozy charm. Like the fruit, leather too has not fully disappeared, only taken on a new energy. I find the leather note here wanders across a continuum of woody, spicy, and smoky. In the heart, it leans woody with a hint of green sweetness. Overall, this phase reminds me of first playing Galatea by Emily Short. The dry down is the weakest part of the fragrance—which by all means should not be the case. For some reason, Bibliotheque picks now to veer hard right into a sugary, synthetic quality that hasn’t had prevalence since the opening. Grape cough syrup and musky vanilla woods try and fail to synthesize into something not vapid. With leather nuances absconded, I am left with a fragrance on par with Claire’s perfume. Forgetting this unsuccessful finish, I am in awe of my first Byredo. It’s unconventional and enigmatic without resorting to anything off putting and remixes some of my favorite notes in striking ways. I hope the dry down is something that grows on me because I would love to add a bottle of this to my perfume shelf.

This scent is wonderful and evokes two strong images for me, and so I will share those rather than delving into the notes. The first and probably the reason I love it so much... My grandpa was a cigar smoker and this scent reminds me exactly of a humidor. The old wood mixed with dry tobacco leaves is a scent that brings me joy and this fragrance, presumably accidentally, NAILS it like nothing I've smelled before. If you know what a humidor smells like and enjoy it, regardless of whether you are a smoker, you will enjoy Bibliotheque. Second, and probably more to what Byredo was going for... anyone remember that episode of Avatar: The Last Airbender where the gang visits the ancient library hidden below the sand in the desert? This fragrance smells like that library. I'll leave it at that. Lovely.

Wow! This scent is very, very weird to me. It smells like two songs or two movies playing at the same time. One is youthful, sweet, juicy, and bright pinkish purple. The other is spirituous, antique, the warm amber color of an expensive aged liquor. Or perhaps this fragrance has a background and a foreground. The background is dusty and evocative of a library (but only if we're talking about a private library in a big old chateau where the beautiful antique furniture of an eccentric duke is gathering dust.) It's also very alcoholic, like cognac or whiskey. The foreground is bright fruit candy, almost too sweet, and clashing so much with the background as to be dissonant. This is actually the first Byredo fragrance I've ever smelled. Are all of them this weird?? I'm so intrigued.

A gothic still life. A Caravaggio chiaroscuro of overripe plums, brandy snifters, inkwells and fountain pens. Bibliotheque is the fine art PhD twin sister next to the avant garde concept artist one that is Pulp. She's fruity in an almost fermented way, like a splash of elderberry schnapps, but freshened with a bite of violet pastilles.
Well...when I first wrote this review originally in that one perfume database run by lunatics, I really loved this one. I said: "The only perfume in my life, so far, that I have re-bought.

At first this smelled like a sweet artificial peach, but after the dry down it really does smell strongly of... dust?? It’s true to its name/inspiration, so I’m impressed. But for some reason the dusty smell (probably the leather and violet) is super overpowering to me and almost gives me a headache.

Opens with a crisp peach, much more than the plum for me. The violet adds that oddly comforting note that when combined with patchouli and leather smells just like it does in the book stacks of the library. As a graduate student, I’ve spent so many years in them that it’s a scent I absolutely crave for comfort and concentration.

Bibliotheque reminds me of Vintage Radio by Lataffa but then sweeter and with a stronger plum note. Fruity but also comforting. It has some funky sweet wine-like note though that confuses me a little bit. Suitable for date nights and dinners out, more for winter and fall than the hotter months and leaning feminine to my nose.

Well, I certainly don't have the most refined spice tester, and I usually find it very difficult to identify individual fragrance notes. But with this scent, there is clearly one note that emerges, reminiscent of preparing a pistachio ice cream mixture from lightly roasted pistachios, slowly but persistently spreading throughout the kitchen. Very appetizing, almost festive, I must say! This note dissipates after a short time and makes way for a balsamic-woody, slightly sweet yet very fresh scent that develops over the next hour. While vetiver scents usually bother me after a while, everything here just harmonizes very well for my taste. This is probably also due to the labdanum and cashmeran in the base. Points are deducted for longevity and intensity/sillage - at least my nose gets used to it very quickly, so I always feel like it doesn't last long, but the scarf that has come into contact with it still carries the scent for several days from a short distance - especially if one uses a relatively generous amount, which makes this perfume unfortunately run out quickly. Nevertheless, I wouldn't say it's a bad price-performance ratio. I simply love this scent too much because it is very harmonious and works very well with "my chemistry." The fragrance has both a Mediterranean and a festive quality, making it quite wearable throughout the year, in my opinion. Not least because of this, it has practically become my signature scent, and I would always invest that not-so-small amount of money in it again.

Black Saffron was the first leather themed fragrance I ever experienced. It is so peculiar, because it takes me right back to my partying days in my 20's. This smells like a goth guy, I was dying of laughter when I first tried it! It's like smoke break at the goth club and you're all huddling together in front of the door with freezing fingers, and someone has boozy cherry schnapps still on their breath. I smell a leather jacket and cold, night-time air. It's the sweet smoke from a clove when it gets absorbed into someone's hair, and that someone is wearing a black leather biker jacket. It feels like it's time to go reapply my black lipstick. When you finally get home at four in the morning, your clothes smell like last night's shenanigans. Glorious.

Byredo BLACK SAFFRON is not at all what I was expecting. It opens sweetly, like a floriental, reminding me of something along the lines of Linari or maybe one of the new Keiko Mecheri Bespoke perfumes. After a couple of minutes a dominant ash note comes through, reminding me of Boucheron INITIAL. At one moment in the trajectory my thoughts turn to Caron LE 3eme HOMME and ELdO JASMIN ET CIGARETTE. But the sweetness then has a resurgence, and suddenly I do believe that I am in the midst of raspberry, as is listed among the notes. The saffron is not very evident to my nose in this perfume, at least not the scent of saffron as I've come to recognize it in perfume--or in cooking. Nor do I find this perfume to be very black. It was only on my third wearing, as I reached the bottom of my generous house-produced sample vial, that I realized what BLACK SAFFRON seems to my nose closest to: Givenchy HOT COUTURE. The raspberry-cigarette ash connection is unmistakable. The big difference is that, while sweet, BLACK SAFFRON is neither cloying nor overly synthetic smelling, and the ashes smell clean, not like a dirty ashtray. Given the manifest similarities between the two compositions, I would definitely recommend BLACK SAFFRON to anyone looking for a higher-quality perfume in the spirit of HOT COUTURE.

Black Saffron lives up to its name during the first few minutes. Dark, spicy, prickly with hints of citrus and then suddenly... there's a fresh floral emerging from the smoke. Could it be juniper?? As you're trying to adapt to the unexpected turn this fragrance has taken, leather surfaces and sends juniper back from which she came. This sudden change has given Black Saffron similarities to Tuscan Leather. This is truly a fragrance of metamorphosis and each phase is undeniably exhilarating.

A very Good Composition. I will compare it in my review with Tuscan Leather by Tom Ford and Parfum de Marleys - Godolphin. I tried it side by side one week with Tuscan Leather and Godolphin as they are all really close in composition! What I can Say is that Tuscan Leather is more smokey and les raspberry while Black Saffron is less smokey and more raspberry sweet. A femininer Version of Tuscan Leather. I dont get Leather at Byredos Scent. It is very sweet an more fresh. Here some specs(max 4 Stars for strengh): +Tuscan Leather = Smokey Raspberry Saffron leather ** Thyme * /////////////////// +Black Saffron = Smokey * Raspberry Saffron Leather (none) Vetiver / Lemon/ Juniper mix ////////////////// +Godolphin= Smokey Raspberry Saffron * Leather creamy/ flowers/ musk * In total it last 4 to 6 hours. Less then Tom Ford and same as Godolphin I would say. Try it yourself! I prefer Godolphin still. Will update maybe in future my experience. Memos - Italian Leather soon enters the ring! It is kinda close too.

I find juniper to be a tricky note. For instance, I like it in By the Fireplace because it's overpowered by the smoky notes, but I can't stand it in Emporio Armani - Stronger with You Intensely because it's too scratchy and cloying. In Black Saffron Eau de Parfum , it doesn't have an annoying presence at all. It's rather well blended in the background of leather and saffron, but gives them a pleasant sweetness together with what I'm guessing is the Pomelo note. The performance is also strong compared to most Byredo fragrances. Overall, it's a pleasant leathery-fruity scent that can be worn daily. Not sure it's worth the full price.

Sultry, smoky, and sweaty for a Byredo. The punk-pop younger sister to Bibliotheque. She’ll shift into Eau Rihla once she gets a mortgage and an AMG. Dominant notes are crushed raspberries and supple black leather. There’s the faint musk of cigarette smoke, but without the ash or tar.

The first niche fragrance I ever bought was Black Saffron. Then, I traded it for Tuscan Leather. Then, I sold the Tuscan Leather and bought another bottle of Black Saffron. This is, perhaps, one of the most beautiful fragrances ever made. Soft, sweet, smooth. It isn't in-your-face loud or standoffish, and works for nearly all social occasions.

Black saffron and blanche are the two most challenging byredos for me. I hardly ever escape from a fragrance but these two… They really hit me hard. Leather, spice, sweet notes, florals, sour notes, woods. Everyting thrown in and i simply cannot tolerate those clashing. The berry sweetness, that tart aspect of it really ruins it all for me.
A nice perfume, very well made, which may please many. For me, however, Black Saffron is too sweet. If the raspberry could be turned down a notch, I feel sure a great perfume would present itself.

It has such a strong note of vetiver, to the point where it almost smells like mint, a cooling note that smells like menthol, not lemon or green but sinus passage opener, in a medicinal or male aftershave way. Shame because I enjoy all the other unusual perfume notes.

I couldn't find this scent in any perfume store and ordered it blind! Then I sprayed the fragrance and it exceeded my expectations. A spicy opening with mint support in the background, a little later amber comes into play while the mint remains pleasantly noticeable and stable in the background, then an oriental scent joins the amber and all elements stay very balanced, meaning no component overdoes it, it remains very pleasant, I feel like I’m in a bazaar in Turkey where it smells similarly spicy, amber-like, and minty. Clear recommendation!!

I feel like a joyful smiling nurse, with my white freshly washed - ironed uniform, ready to kindly serve and take care of my patients, always with devotion, pure intentions and heartfelt joy. Oh no, I am not a nurse in real life, in fact I don't even fancy hospitals or clinics, la tulipe gives me the feeling of a sterilized but bright joyful person who's on a mission, determined to carry out her/his duty, making others happy with her pretty perfume trail.

One of my favourites and my parfum of choice during spring. It's flowery, green and watery. Very photorealistic freshly cut tulips, you can smell the creamy flower and the greenness of the cut stems. Lovely during rainy days, as it has some acuatic notes. A very clean, fresh and happy scent. It's absolutely lovely in spring but a tad heavy for me during the day at the warmest point of the summer.

You know when you walk into a florist (a real florist, not one of those boutiquey places that pretend) and you get hit by the scent of chopped off stems, a bunch of florals and a little bit of damp? That's La Tulipe. The florals aren't overwhelming, in fact for me the green-ness of it came out the most.

He looked at the cream-white silk square in front of him; he had already stretched it onto the appropriate frame. His tools: brushes and paints, the small mixing palette - all of it was ready on the little table beside him. Nothing was missing. Nothing - except for the all-important inspiration! Lost in thought, he gazed out of the atelier window; saw the rooftops of the city center; the gray where there should have been blue sky and sunshine. How was he supposed to paint a new silk scarf here and today? The bad weather phase had lasted too long, and the deadline was approaching fast. Sighing, he dreamed himself into spring: he saw sunshine, lush green, and the first blooming flowers on heavy dark soil. He would use the dark green for the large rhubarb leaves that fit quite well into the corners: he could almost sense their somewhat stern scent. Fine reddish veins ran through these leaves with their wavy edges. Yes, a beginning had been made! To the dark, somewhat sternness, he now needed something sweetly fragrant and light: a few nests of yellow, fragile freesias joined the green. And cyclamen! Yes, cyclamen: the small, wild ones that grew in whole clusters and lifted their proud little heads. Of course, he needed the classic light violet-tinged red for that: during his now confident, elegant brush strokes, he felt surrounded by a fine breath of spring. The world smelled, it was alive again! And so was he: inspiration pulsed through his winter-weary body! A glance at what he had created so far showed: now tulips had to come! Tulips in the most varied colors; best the fringed so-called parrot tulips. They would fit wonderfully into this picture. Also important were these curved stems, which uniquely find their way to the light. His brush flew across the bright silk! Proudly, he stood before the frame on his little easel: Not only did the colorful, hope-spraying colors please him, but he also felt the lively breath of spring. But he also sensed that his artwork - for it had become a small work of art by now - needed a bit of calm and depth. This colorful kaleidoscope of shapes and colors needed to be toned down a bit. His spring also included the woods: some still bare, some already intertwined with fine leaves. And what a spicy scent they already emitted in the light spring rain! His brush almost blindly found the sought-after shades; he perceived them as fragrant nuances. It was done! His highly developed sense of smell suddenly began to vibrate; his colorfully spring-scented silk painting received a special touch: his wife had just entered the atelier. As usual, she smelled familiar of vetiver! What a sensory masterpiece was created in that moment in this sparse attic space! The woman would finish the silk square with fine rolled hems; she was skilled at these delicate handworks. Who would buy it from him this time and thus bring a little money into the household? Hermès? Ferragamo? Our artist does not yet know that these true works of art on silk will later be sold as foulards for a lot of money and will even achieve a cult status! "La Tulipe" is such a fragrant painting: not a high-quality or elegantly composed work of art; but still the result of a solid craftsman with a lot of imagination and love for what he does. It promises spring in an uncomplicated way, brings much joy, and reliably accompanies its wearer for several hours. It bids farewell slowly and politely - a light whisper remains on the skin. And the longing memory of what spring means: light, air, and cheerful experiences! Thus, "La Tulipe" earns its place in the great world of fragrances - as a friendly spring greeting!

I love the morning. By noon, I’m always somehow tired, the morning and afternoon are filled with work, and the evening is for relaxing - but the morning is everything to me. The earlier, the better, especially in the warmer season. It basically starts as soon as it’s light early in the morning - then I love to get up and go outside. Whether it’s just with a coffee on the balcony, having breakfast in the garden, or taking the dog into nature - it doesn’t matter. I love to see the fog rising over the river and the vineyards lying in shadow, only individual patches illuminated by the sun. I love the absolute silence, interrupted only by the chirping of birds. Above all, I love the crystal clear cold air on an early, sunny spring morning. This clarity, this purity, the sun still too weak to warm the air, so that with every breath I deeply inhale this diamond-like air - that is the metaphor for new beginnings. Whenever I have the chance for such a morning walk in sunny cold, I reset my life and start anew. Plans, intentions, goals - suddenly everything seems feasible, achievable. In the crystal clear morning, the geometry of my life unfolds in a completely logical structure - and I draw upon all the hope I can get. On such mornings, there are only two spring fragrances for me that reflect this complete purity and clarity - one of them is La Tulipe by Byredo. It was through this fragrance that I first became aware of the niche segment. When I smelled La Tulipe for the first time, it was like a revelation to me, and I had high expectations of Byredo - an expectation that, unfortunately, has not been met for me with the other fragrances of the brand so far. They often seem synthetic and constructed away from nature. Quite the opposite is La Tulipe: The very first moment, the top note, is so perfect, so clear, so pure, so harmonious, so round. The perfect scent, crystal clear like fresh, cold spring water, floral-pure and deeply nuanced, without sweetness, without harshness. A completely soft, pure floral scent, a symbol of growth, a symbol of the moment when the bloom presents itself in all its delicate beauty. For the absolute freshness, it is the cyclamen and especially the freesia that are responsible; I know this note from other spring fragrances as a freshness carrier. However, the freshness does not give me the impression of fresh laundry; I cannot find the slightest, tiniest similarity to Blanche by Byredo. While Blanche really smells like the starch in my freshly ironed bed linen, La Tulipe is the freshness of pure spring water in the mountains. Then, when the tulip joins in the heart note, I can only agree with my predecessors: A real tulip is relatively odorless and cannot achieve the effect here. I also perceive a hint of lilac, but in a very, very moderate form and not to be compared with the sweet heaviness that lingers in the air from the lilac in my garden on summer evenings. The tulip here in La Tulipe is primarily a symbol of the materialized spring, of clarity, new beginnings, and purity. It is a wonderfully beautiful, round fragrance that is by no means synthetic in any way, which is only later softened by slightly harsher, woody notes after many hours. Perfectly fitting this experience are the completely simple bottle, the white label, and the colorless transparency of the perfume. In this regard, I personally consider La Tulipe to be the true, underrated masterpiece of Byredo, to which no other fragrance of the brand can compare. How could it? No other symbolizes pure, fresh water as much as La Tulipe.

A kingdom for a tulip? Well, an entire realm had to believe it, as many a house was exchanged for a tulip bulb. The bulbous plants, which today are sold cheaply as mass-market items, enchanted not only emperors and kings in the 17th century but also drove wealthy merchants to ruin.

Commotion in the flower bed... early morning in the garden. Snowdrops ring in the first round. The freesia enters the spring-decorated ring and plays the role of the number girl. Rhubarb, as the referee, wants to announce the contenders but doesn't get a word in. La Tulipe, the challenger from and to Byredo, naturally introduces herself. Then Viola appears...

First of all: I am new here, 42, female, only been intensely interested in fragrances for 2 years and experimenting. This is my first comment. Please forgive my clumsy description: La Tulipe starts fresh and within seconds a floral-sweet, juicy and pink!!! tulip breaks through. Beautiful. Noble, pure and clear, not powdery.

..tulips from Sweden... Uh, yes. I guess I wasn't quite sure about the lyrics! But I just couldn't resist this introduction. I am surprised that this floral scent doesn't give me a headache. The fragrance theme isn't really my thing, but I don't think this Byredo is bad. This tulip opens with a chord of freesias and rhubarb.

Once upon a time, tulip bulbs were almost as valuable as gold. There was a huge hype around these little plants. Everyone wanted a piece of the pie, and people bought and bought, investing all their money in tulip bulbs because the demand was so high and everyone thought they were ideal investment objects.

Unfortunately, I discovered you much too late. By chance, I was able to make your acquaintance in a drugstore. As a lover of the entire Scandal line, I am of course enchanted by you as well. The typical DNA is unmistakable here, and this light bubblegum note :) that's what I call it. I read "cheap and artificial" here, and I don't find that to be true either. Every skin is different, and fortunately, you develop wonderfully on me. Anyone who has been to Paris will find your name choice fitting. For being an EDT, you have real power, and 1-2 sprays are enough. A very sweet pear briefly appears, which is then replaced by a honey/jasmine mix. The pear here is also rather crisp and fresh. In "La Belle | Jean Paul Gaultier," it is more Christmassy and warmer due to the roasted notes. Personally, I think this Scandal flanker is very suitable for spring and summer. Theoretically, it could work all year round, but I prefer vanilla scents then. Sometimes it is incomprehensible why a perfume was discontinued. For those who find the regular Scandal just too much, this would be perfect to take along. The flankers Scandal Le Parfum or Scandal Absolu really don't fit into the line. They have hardly anything to do with the original Scandal. Different names could definitely have been chosen. The series with "Scandal | Jean Paul Gaultier," "Scandal by Night | Jean Paul Gaultier," and Scandal à Paris really made sense! What a shame, Mr. Gaultier

I have had this fragrance in my collection for quite some time. When I was testing the Scandal line at my trusted perfumery, I found Scandal à Paris to be the most convincing in terms of scent. Although I quite like the new Scandal Le Parfum as well, it smells completely different. But back to the EdT: To start with, I love sweet fragrances and have an aversion to patchouli. With this scent, I perceive a candied pear right from the beginning, and thankfully, I don't smell any patchouli at all. It is either very subtle or gets overshadowed by honey and pear. For me, the fragrance still smells the same after several hours; it doesn't develop on my skin at all. However, I find the sweetness of the fragrance not too overpowering and consider it suitable for any occasion. It is also not 'in your face' sweet, but rather keeps a bit subdued, possibly a result of the patchouli. The longevity is excellent; the perfume lasts all day on me and is also very well perceived by others. For a scent that is "only" an EdT, the longevity is top-notch. The bottle is extraordinary; I had to buy the 50ml just because of the legs.

The Scandal series is - unlike what some write here - a truly exciting continuation. Although many describe the Scandal A Paris scent as sweet, I must say that it still belongs to the first fragrances in the series that all have patchouli in the base note. This strong scent almost overpowers the pear, I think - this fragrance smells of patchouli with sweet pear and soft flowers. However, those who do not like patchouli should rather reach for So Scandal! or Scandal Le Parfum.

This fragrance was my first blind buy and my first step in a slightly gourmand direction. Actually, I’m more of a floral type. I do smell plenty of flowers in this scent, but also the honey. This honey note, combined with the pear, always reminds me a bit of a cake my grandma used to bake, and I instantly fell in love with the fragrance. My boyfriend doesn’t like it at all, but I don’t care. The floral notes unfortunately don’t last particularly long on my skin, but the honey seems to stay forever, and I can still smell it long after. The soft scent gives me a feeling of security, and for that reason, it’s also a good fragrance for sleeping and during tough times. However, I must admit that the sillage isn’t particularly impressive. At least not on me. The bottle with the bare legs dangling at the side does have something scandalous about it. But I can’t exactly say the same about the fragrance. Overall, I like it very much, especially in the cold season and when I want to feel secure.
