Not even a replica like in Oud Immortel. Nothing of the sort follows later (in the famous “Where-is-Behle?” question from Bruno Moravetz, Jochen Behle at least showed up). However, this doesn’t bother me at all. I am satisfied with the so-called leather accord, especially since the wannabe Oud in the accidentally mishmash Oud Immortel didn’t really excite me. But perhaps I should start earlier: Blackberry. Aha. Count me out. Alternatively, a consumptive one. Saffron gives the leather a dry, rough elegance that I quite like. Regarding rum, a quote from my favorite colleague: “Rum…hm…I can convince myself.” Nothing to add to that. Sage (while I’m already checking things off): Not explicitly, more as a bitter addition in the background. For patchouli and powdery musk, however, a ‘cheers’ to my colleague, who - unlike me - identified both in the third hour, and without any announcement! For me, a leather note develops practically immediately, reminding me of Cuoio by Pal Zileri. Nice. After a few hours, I feel somewhat at home, as the leather note takes on that throat lozenge-sweet licorice quality that is pleasantly familiar from other Byredos. The fact that I can tolerate this well should not disguise that there should be some variety at some point. Nevertheless, I do not share the largely unanimous disappointment. I find the prevented Leather Accord quite decent. It spares me that often intrusive fruity note that has apparently been compulsively part of too many corresponding fragrances since 2007. Gradually, it glides from rough to sweetly subtle and remains appropriately persistent. After spraying it on at seven in the morning, the leather note was still distinctly present until around 3 PM, although it became distorted in a typically Byredo manner (see above) towards the end. Eventually, I also smell the musk, finally, I might almost say. By 4 PM, it’s practically over. I find that perfectly fine. Whether it is a candidate for purchase, I do not know yet. It might be a bit too plain overall. It’s enough that I work in accounting. I don’t need to smell like that.

Right from the start, the scent is difficult to describe and can only be formulated in images. It begins wonderfully leathery, but not just that. With a dried-fruit depth, Accord Oud smells old, not necessarily antiquated as the scent is modern. More like old furniture, very old dark brown wooden furniture, the kind you discover through the haze of dust stirred up in your grandparents' attic. They are simple yet possess an undefined elegance. The scent evokes for me a sense of the past and loneliness. Nevertheless, it conveys a muted elegance, not so much a dull thud but rather pulsating and awakening. It is a craftfully great composition. You can feel how raspberry, rum, and leather notes enter into a symbiosis here, but you can't really smell it; this scent is too intertwined. When I am in my parents' attic during the height of summer, I feel the stuffy dry air in my throat, the unbearable heat, and the longing for a refreshing fruit ice that only dries my throat out more. That's somewhat how Accord Oud is. Dry, dusty with a hint of withered fruitiness. Around me, old wood and old armchairs. The transition to the top note is very subtly progressing. The sage gives itself completely to its light note and smoothly replaces the fruity dry notes of the top note with equally dry but wood-heavy notes. A bitter, harsh note sets in and firmly establishes the end of the top note. Accord Oud somehow comes across as a constrained scent. It doesn't fully open up and hides itself more and more as the scent develops. It also becomes weaker. Cinnamon is supposed to be in there as well. I actually smell nothing of spicy cinnamon and saffron. I probably missed that. After a promising start, I was also waiting for something to be expected. Nothing. The scent becomes downright boring. The dry down is merely a subtle patchouli. The oud, as the name promises, is found in a new interpretation. Formerly the prima ballerina of the scent, it is here very subtle and shy. You can smell the resinous, sultry wood character with an earthy undertone. Unfortunately, I don't know Oud Immortel, but both are said to be "exaggerations" of original ideas. But read for yourself. Ben Gorham on Accord Oud: “I got to know the smell of oud in India and the Middle East. Its distinctive and intense character impressed me greatly. I felt the need to focus entirely on the uniqueness of this raw material and create a scent that draws exclusively from the character of oud. During the development, I found that different facets of this complex wood type were even more pronounced when combined with other essences. In the end, I liked two very different interpretations the best, and I decided to present them as a pair. In both cases, they are exaggerations of the original idea.” Although I find the idea to be great in my opinion and nose, the execution leaves much to be desired. It's as if the perfumer lost interest after the heart note. The realization of the idea is too simple and too unremarkable for me. More than up to the top note doesn't reach me; after that, Accord Oud loses itself in woody pseudo-minimalism. Accord Oud feels unfinished, going from initial greatness to being unremarkable. The opening was so promising, the ending so unremarkable.

In the world of music, a chord is understood as a harmonious combination of at least three tones. Given the mentioned oud, which does not officially appear in the pyramid, I assume that Byredo is referring to the idea that the interplay of the individual fragrance notes is meant to create an illusion of oud.

So how does one start writing about a perfume that is simply outstanding?! The first time I came into contact with Byredo fragrances was in the spring of 2014. After a brief test, I found them quite peculiar and rather unremarkable.

So. Seminar paper submitted and straight to Ludwig Beck: Accord Oud !!!! First, the Flui's scent bulb perceives apple spritzer. Golden apple spritzer, (could also be a Bavarian wheat beer in terms of color from the food designer) that has a bit of fizz. I find AO also has a slightly sweet-herbaceous quality, a slight reference to Davidoff Champion, to that dumbbell bottle.

Thanks to AdAstra72, I was able to test this fragrance, which I wouldn't have been interested in at all based on the listed notes and comments. Parfumo is really a fine thing - it allows you to try scents that you wouldn't have paid attention to otherwise and constantly provides new impressions. But I'm sure I'm not alone in this opinion.

Well, to start on a positive note: Fortunately, "Accord Oud" presents an oriental leather-oud forest fruit that doesn't drown in amber or other sweetening aromas. We don't see that very often. However, the shift into the counteroffensive is quite abrupt. This fragrance does not want to be your friend; it has a mind of its own and likes to rub you the wrong way.

Sometimes we convince ourselves that we can do everything on our own, without the outside help of another. I admit, I have never read the accompanying instructions before testing a fragrance, but in this case, it is highly advisable. Jean Paul Gaultier's Monsieur Eau du Matin is not a fragrance in the EdC, EdT, or EdP strength. It is, in the German translation, a "Revitalizing Fragrance". Uh, I don't understand that at all! The Dutch(?) "Geparfumeerde Lotion" sounds much more familiar. It is a full-body fragrance lotion to spray on. From the English, I gather "toning properties," so a kind of tonic, and clearly: "Rub over the body for a discrete fragrance." Anyone who sprays the fragrance only on the back of their hand and around their neck, thinking they have a going-out scent, will of course be disappointed - hence the puzzled comments and statements. This "Uppfriskande Doft" or "Frescor Estimulante" (no idea which languages) can be generously applied after showering (and don't forget to lightly rub it in - of course, the purest exception regarding fragrance rubbing). It may not be summer yet, but when I return from work in the afternoon slightly sweaty and can't jump straight into the shower, I just take off my shirt and apply it to my upper body. It keeps me fresh for several hours until I can shower, and no one runs away from me. Yes, it is fresh, with a dose of citrus fruits, and definitely cucumber green. It reminds me most of carafes filled with water, in which some cucumber slices are floating. In short, cucumber water, which I find very refreshing in the summer. The wall bottle - simply top-notch! So don't dismiss it right away, but read the instructions first. Then it will work out with the neighbor too.

When I saw it at the airport for €20, it was clear that it had to come with me to Tunisia. It seems to be similar to Paco by Paco Rabanne, now a pure airport scent that can only be purchased in duty-free zones. On the strip, it could not have disappointed me so much that I would have left it there, as I was aware of the higher online prices, its obscurity in the community, and its absence in regular stores. Also, the names JPG and Kurkdjian were not exactly arguments against pulling out the debit card. Here in Hammamet, however, Monsieur is not used very often, only occasionally in the evenings after showering to help me sleep, as that is mostly what he is. I would have never expected such an unspectacular, somewhat bland scent from the two previously mentioned big, rather extroverted names. And then there’s even the green soapiness known or borrowed from bestsellers like Original Vetiver or Mugler Cologne. That is a bit disheartening. However, Monsieur is not a stinker, not at any time. He comes across as calm, green, soapy, spicy, and above all, clean. But compared to that, some L'Occitane body lotions are true scent explosions. The woody finish is barely perceptible; before that, you smell something like being bathed in herbal broth. Bottle: simple with the wall style, but not ugly. Sillage: 6 Longevity: 2 hours at most is among the least I have experienced with a perfume so far. Not all blind buys can be winners. This Monsieur is not a loser, but no more than a green refreshment for in-between. No comparison to other Monsieurs, Mugler Colognes, or interesting refreshers.
A very subtle scent from the new JPG care line for men. The perfume is extremely understated, you smell like you just stepped out of the shower. Suitable for full-body application :)

Today, April shows its "fresh" side - and it is raining in torrents. Nevertheless, there is a green floral scent in the air that invigorates and delights the nose and senses. A detergent manufacturer once coined the term "april fresh," and this describes Ma Vie florale well. It is, like April, floral but still cool - without being distant. One enjoys the gentle caress of bright jasmine and budding yellow tea roses on the forehead, and it urges one to go outside - even with a rain jacket. The cactus flower creates a mild exclusive tone that provides casual elegance. The cedar softly embraces the sandalwood. I want to step out of a London taxi like Gwyneth Paltrow, the well-chosen face of this fragrance, with flowing hair and stroll through the soft English rain. Casual naturalness and style go hand in hand here. One walks optimistically forward - even if one splashes into some puddles.

This smells like a green tea i used to drink. Bitter herbs, fresh flowers with a fruity sweetness when i first sniffed it. After, i get an ambery resinous smell that, with the fruit, just makes this warmer, like a dried apricot, but the musk i only get towards the end, a very clean one, well mixed and blended with the orris root. In fact that is what i get from this: well blended and also dynamic. All the ingredients seem to work together in an effortless way but they also change and morph.

Smoked sage, varnished wood, eucalyptus mist, dry menthol, green tea. Imagine if Aesop branched into the occult. My favourite scent of all time to date. Full stop. Instant aromatherapy. No matter the time of year or my mood, I keep coming back to DLS. It's aromatic, green, boreal, vespertine. Airy enough to feel clean, but without treading into soapy spa tincture, and herbal enough to have a bite of earthiness, without feeling mulchy. A sage stick, without the acridity of smoke. It's a true unisex scent with admirable longevity for a Byredo; I spray it on my travel scarf before long-haul flights and it will last the whole slog through to the return flight. I promise I'm not a shill, but I own two large bottles and several of its candle formulation (Sweet Grass), and live in low-grade anxiety that one day they'll retire it and I'll need to empty my savings to secure a larger stockpile. Since meeting De Los Santos, I compare every scent that's followed to it. Mental Snapshot: You're a herbology professor in haute couture. You frequent places like old Catholic churches, which have been converted into a steam saunas, or teahouses in a modern art galleries. You can guess strangers' star signs to 89% accuracy. tl;dr: modern witchy teahouse

Another simplistic fragrance from byredo. Starts with sweet floral notes, there is a delicious fruity accord. Quickly settles to a rosy-ambroxan smell. From top to middle notes, the sweetness is very well preserved. As the smell matures, you get plenty of clean ambroxan with soft musks. I could never detect any palo santo which was a note i was waiting to get. After that opening, i expected a much richer fragrance. Well, i think the top notes are pretty good. De los Santos gives a great fruity note at the start. After that you get a rosy ambroxan and musky ambroxan. If you don’t mind synthetic base notes of clean quality, you may like this. Nothing really special here.

At first sniff, my nose recoiled a bit, too "minty," "herbaceous," almost "healthy." But then, an almost magical development. The scent melts away, becoming soft and sensual, like a second skin. It is full of contradictions, pure and clear yet warm and sensual, cheeky and velvety at the same time. It reflects the crisp coziness of winter just as much as the warm breeze on a bare summer arm. Intangible yet always present. I don’t want to be without it anymore.

I have to defend "De Los Santos" now. Yes, the fragrance is not straightforward and will not appeal to everyone. It starts strong with aromatic sage followed by cistus and orris root. For me, there is also incense in it, even though it is not listed. I only catch a brief whiff of mirabelle at the beginning. The heart of this fragrance is aromatic and somehow exotic in the sense of being unusual and fascinating. The Ambroxan makes the scent slightly sweet in the drydown. The longevity is superb for a Byredo. After 8 hours, it is still quite noticeable, and even the sage from the top note is still recognizable (apparently not a pure top note). The sillage is strong for 2-3 hours and then slowly becomes a bit more intimate. What I appreciate about DLS is that it really smells extraordinary. It piques curiosity. One wonders who might smell like this. At the same time, it is very calming and aromatic, so for my nose, it stands out but is not unpleasant. If I’m already spending a lot of money on niche fragrances, I want to wear something that not every designer has already offered in a similar way for a quarter of the price. So my conclusion: De Los Santos is a very successful, special creation without the typical Byredo H/S weaknesses. It certainly doesn’t suit everyone, but that’s exactly what makes it so good. Thanks for coming to my TED talk. ;-)

Summer 2022, just acquired another perfume from the brand, my first niche perfume & I receive this sample of “De Los Santos” - the first spray hits my nose and then becomes very dry. From the right, the sage hits me in the face and I feel refreshed. Nights follow in which I dream of the scent, it haunts me so much. A few days later, it’s still 36 degrees in my city.

I was very curious about this fragrance, as it sounded exciting and unusual. Upon the first spray, disappointment set in: diluted sage tea and a few artificial-sounding woods. Hm, too bad, let's wait and see. I kept sniffing at my wrist, but at first nothing happened. Then after about 20 minutes, it started: the iris root came through, giving it a floral touch.

… there was a lumberjack who one day woke up with terrible sore throat. Before he left the house and made his way to the sawmill, his wife gave him some candies for relief. Not just any candies, but the refreshing sage candies from Dallmann's, in the small yellow paper box.

A heavy sweet scent of sun-warmed grasses, I seek the shade of large trees and breathe a sigh of relief, finally some coolness. Indeed, this perfume gives me exactly that, the sigh of relief after a long, hot summer day. I perceive warm wood and notes of grasses - perhaps the rockrose? The clary sage is wonderfully refreshing, I love it.

As a big fan of Mexico, its culture, and its people, I was indeed curious about "De Los Santos," even though Byredo's fragrances have not been my thing so far. The promotional photo, featuring a Mexican woman holding the bottle with a confident gaze, also appealed to me in some way.

This time, Jean Paul Gaultier has chosen the St. Andrew's cross as a bold decoration for his body bottle. Although the ingredients of this EdP are actually simple, they are composed in such a way that they come across as sultry and erotic, which is the art of a perfumer, and I believe it must have been a perfumer in this case. The scent starts off with a berry note of raspberry with a touch of lemon, then becomes floral with orange blossom and various roses, and finally turns a bit more robust in the base with iris and vanilla. However, I don’t perceive bergamot and lemon balm - but this often happens to me, that I search in vain for listed fragrance notes and simply can’t find them! "Classique X" may not be exciting, but it is somehow arousing and stimulating. As mentioned, it has something sultry, sinful, indecent, and disreputable... It may sound strange, but I imagine it on a woman wearing a corset and straps. Am I a bad girl for thinking this?

I didn't get much typical coconut in Byredo Velvet Haze, at least not anything cloyingly plastic like some coconut-flavoured products can be. Instead, it's creamy, warmly sweet, slightly honeyed and animalic, evoking a bowl of hot milk to me during the first 20 minutes. Then, something vaguely inky and metallic, yet still somewhat velvety, starts to infuse the hot milk and cools it down. It felt familiar, but I wasn't able to name it until 1 hour later, when it firmly dominates and the sweet milk becomes merely a facet of it: a clean, vegetal white musk, halfway between the musty one in Byredo Blanche and the brighter, more floral one in Narciso Rodriguez for Her EDT. The main difference being the addition of the sweet milkiness, Velvet Haze feels kind of like a semi-gourmand variation on the clean white musk theme. From then on, Velvet Haze doesn't change much anymore. Sometimes, I can smell a bit of coconut milk within the mix, but it's mostly just abstract velvety milky sweetness among the inky white musk. I don't detect any distinct bitterness of cacao or patchouli on my skin, although the spikiness of the later was detectable during the middle phase on the paper. I get a medium sillage during the first 3 hours, and it stays close to the skin for another 6 hours. Without digging into any musical or cultural background, the name itself actually summarizes well how Velvet Haze smells to me: a velvety, hazy white cloud of clean inky musk with a subtle creamy sweetness, which fits well into the abstract, modern artificial style of Byredo fragrances that I tried so far. I would recommend it to those who enjoy clean, abstract fragrances, especially to those who'd like a warmer, more creamy version of Byredo Blanche or Narciso Rodriguez for Her EDT.

Velvet Haze is indeed an Egyptian musk fragrance. Sure there's a strong resemblance to the NR line, but the same would be said about literally any Egyptian musk fragrance nowadays. Velvet Haze is not a dupe by any means. The opening is unpleasant to my nose. I don't love the way the lactones were executed here as they don't fit smoothly into the composition and that's usually what they are supposed to do. Instead I find that there is an odd juxtaposition between a bitter dirt accord, and a strangely milky overripe fruit accord. This unsettling push-pull character lasts for the first half hour of wear and then slowly fades as the Egyptian musk accord comes to the forefront: it's all lived in musk and tamed patchouli. I like the dry down very much for it's familiarity rather than for any compositional innovation. Aside from the opening, Velvet Haze is easy to wear and easy to love. It's probably a big seller for Byredo. However for my personal preferences, I strongly prefer the composition of NR for Her as it's more overtly femme while Velvet Haze is solidly unisex and monolithically musky.

I liked this perfume the instant I smelled it , it's warm, inviting and natural in a way like a skin scent. I smell a lot of musk and patchoui but in a very muted ,velvety , hazy, creamy way , as the name suggests. It might be somewhat odd for some in the first 5 minutes but then warms up into a sweet creamy haze. Let coconut not worry you if you don't like it. I would say it's more milky , like the sweet smell of real coconut milk ,not like the strong odor of simulated coconut suntan products . I am in love with this perfume and will definitely re purchase when I get lower. One of Byredos best !

There's something about patchouli and cacao/chocolate notes together that sounds awful but works beautifully to my nose (see also: Strangers Parfumerie Cachouli and Fresh Cannabis Santal). I don't pick up a lot of flowers or fruit in Velvet Haze; they seem to be more of a supporting cast compared to the stars of the show: musk, patchouli, and dark, bitter chocolate, adding creaminess and warmth to the overall composition. Velvet Haze is a perfect scent for when I want to feel cozy but don't want to smell like dessert.

With Byredo, I don't always have it easy ... most of the brand's fragrances have completely failed with me, the only one that made it into my collection is Bal d'Afrique. I was more than curious about Velvet Haze ... the pyramid sounded great :) At the perfume meeting in Munich, I briefly smelled it on a test strip and found it terrible. I had already participated in the sharing and still waited impatiently for the decant ;) Finally, the moment arrived and I was a bit stunned! Narciso For Her EdT ... but different ... and the name "Velvet Haze" ... fits perfectly! One thing upfront ... you should like musk, and the somewhat strange-scratchy opening is quickly overcome ;) About the scent: Why does Velvet Haze start so scratchy? It might be due to the ambrette seeds, which are said to smell musky-herbaceous-peppery (and that's exactly how I perceive the opening!) I am quickly reconciled with the not-sweet coconut that joins the musk. (nothing gourmand here!) Patchouli is now also mixing in ... not earthy as one often expects. It adds dark-smoky accents to the scent progression. The whole thing is dusted with cocoa powder and an extra dose (!) of musk is added. A sensually intoxicating scent ... not new yet still different. Similar to Narciso For Her EdT but never the same. The creamy-clean base is slightly soiled (sexy) ... and I find it lovely that coconut and cocoa keep flashing through. It should be mentioned again that we are not dealing with a gourmand scent here :) This is how I like musk and this is how I like Byredo. The Velvet Haze is intoxicating and addictive. I believe that Velvet Haze is wearable almost all year round except for the height of summer. Unisex? ... hm... I'm not so sure (I can't really imagine Narciso on a man either) but the gentlemen have to decide that for themselves ;) The longevity is about 8 hours. The sillage is not overwhelming but well noticeable. We all know the simple Byredo bottles. The 100 ml bottles are hefty and heavy ... the 50 ml bottles are really cute :) Conclusion: Coconut, patch & plenty of musk dusted with cocoa powder. Intoxicating haze! Creamy-clean base... Narciso waves in :) For me, as a musk and Narciso fan, Velvet Haze is a brilliant new discovery ... I recommend testing it ... you definitely have to sniff it at least once ;)

A little coconut water? Or quite clearly a musk magnet? Perhaps a female patchouli pirate? What is "Velvet Haze" then??? A bit of everything. "Velvet Haze" is a hyper-modern hippie. The color purple spreads in my mind, and it is of course velvety. The great art of dying. A circular saw of hugs.

Everyone probably knows the scene from "Asterix the Gaul," where Centurion Gaius Bonus wants to test his superpowers after drinking the supposed magic potion. However, since it is actually a hair growth product, he naturally fails with the bigger challenges, and his attempts ultimately end with a - relatively speaking - pebble. A similar fate may befall 'Velvet Haze'.

I am often astonished by what others smell and what I myself then perceive. Sometimes there are worlds between them. This is also the case here. After Sweetsmells' beautiful, extremely enticing comment, I immediately got a sample. MUSK! And then also fine patchouli, a scent note that I am just starting to love (as long as it doesn’t come off earthy and grave-like).

After being hooked by Byredo's wonderful 'Rose Noir', I bought two 12 ml original bottles of 'Gipsy Water' and 'Blanche' at a bargain price on eBay and immediately fell in love with both after the first test. As a bonus, I received a sample of 'Velvet Haze', but help, what was that? The two hefty sprays that I joyfully applied to my forearm left me quite puzzled.

Some fragrances you spray on and immediately feel "at home," even if it's an oriental or a incense figure. Others remain neutral or take you to a distant land where you like to linger from time to time. It’s difficult with perfumes that primarily feel "foreign" and evoke the sensation that you are in the wrong film - uh - scent. The name intrigued me so much.

Here I must say that I actually prefer the slightly modified reissue even more than the original! It seems to me somehow softer, lighter, and more pleasant to wear - that sour note that bothered me a bit back then is now gone, and what remains in the reissue is a beautifully radiant, soft fragrance that lasts an eternity. I would almost describe it as linear, with a simple yet unique composition. How thrilled I was when I read that MaDame is back!

I wanted to be in my late 20s when I first bought the fragrance. Back then, I associated Madame with something rather conservative and imagined a woman in a suit, high heels, and a pearl necklace with perfectly styled hair. Madame hit my (fragrance) heart 100% back then; the scent reached me directly, even though it contains rose. Finding summer fragrances has always been difficult for me, but Madame was so pure, clean, and yet special - like freshly hung laundry on a summer meadow. I associate it with wonderful memories of an unforgettable time...young, independent, spontaneous, rebellious, loving, searching, sensitive, loving, creative, emotional, exciting, clear, different,...the fragrance fit perfectly back then and still does today, and it will always remain something special for me. Last week, a large bottle moved back in with me. I still find it fantastic and love this fresh, clean interplay of the individual fragrance notes.

I had put it in my shopping cart so many times, and so many times I left it there. And then a dear friend got me excited about it again, and I had to order it immediately. I loved "Ma Dame (2008) (Eau de Toilette) | Jean Paul Gaultier," I bathed in it. My heart bled when it was taken off the market. Ma Dame Eau de Parfum was available for a while longer here, but it couldn't compare to the eau de toilette. So I just opened my package and was catapulted 15 years back into my youth. Guys, Ma Dame (2024) Eau de Toilette comes so close to its predecessor!! I find the scent is more floral. But that's not a bad thing, it smells a bit more grown-up, and I have grown up too. And yet, the girlie vibes are still there. Dreamy! I can't say anything about the longevity yet, but the sillage is already great.

I’m already gearing up for summer and am in the testing phase. Ma Dame is somehow simple, almost linear, no corners, no edges, no detours. Fruity sweetness, without being squeaky or annoying. A candidate that you won’t tire of, no off-note. Unfortunately, I often have that, where there’s some note that bothers me...that’s probably why my collection doesn’t grow, but changes weekly. Let’s talk about the scent: early summer in the city, orange, I would have guessed something berry-like with peach, and here I even like the rose from the house of Gaultier. Musk not comparable to Arabic perfumes. I need this scent...now I know why: three notes.

Bought blindly I had seen few comments and comparisons with this perfume which aroused my curiosity. what a disappointment, this perfume is boring, it just smells like sandalwood, simple and ordinary, nothing more, I could easily find an eau de toilette in a pharmacy for €10 with the same smell. intense eau de parfum? a real joke, the sillage is weak, the staying power does not exceed that of a classic eau de parfum for around 7 hours but is weak. really gone your way this reference has nothing more than another but so much less than many others. the price is unjustified.

Since the nineties, when the two Elements fragrances adorned my collection, I have had some encounters with the scents from the Boss brand, but nothing has truly excited me. The Bottled series relies too much on apple for my taste. Here, they make a strong effort to incorporate every state of this fruit, from branch to blossom and unripe state, all the way to its musty liquefaction, into their fragrances. The rest is, for me, no better. A year ago, however, the Collection Edition caught my attention. The notes of the Energetic Fougère appealed to me. I didn’t want to order “blind,” so I set off to a retailer that carried this fragrance in their promotional portfolio. Since the scent was not in stock at the location, they promised to request a sample, which should arrive in two or three days. A few days later, I received the sample, which was not much, just filled in a tube without a spray nozzle. I then transferred the sample into a travel spray and tested it. What I perceived was quite pleasing. So I will skip the fragrance experience I had up to this point and pick up again with the receipt of the fragrance shipment. The first impression is always the visual and tactile perception of the product. The scent comes in a round cardboard box that gives a rather high-quality impression. After removing the protective film, the cardboard bell is lifted off the base where the fragrance bottle rests. It reminds me of the sailor fragrances from JPG, but without me having to wonder whether using a can opener would be advisable. The bottle is quite heavy. It is simply designed, has a thick glass base, and a cap that fits well. The spray nozzle has the right effectiveness and makes a solid impression. Overall, it is very understated. Since I am interested in the scent and not so much in the packaging, this is perfectly fine and appropriate. Quiet luxury, it doesn’t have to be flashy. Now I come to the actually interesting part: How does it smell? The fragrance opens with a sweet, green note. To me, it feels “wormwood-like.” This is likely due to the mugwort and the oils from the angelica seeds. This impression is immediately supported by the present but not overpowering note of sandalwood, which contributes its own gentle woodiness and subtle creaminess. The sandalwood accompanies the fragrance throughout its entire duration until it fades away. As it develops further, the geranium and rose introduce a herb-fresh floral aspect. These scent impressions give the fragrance a few light, fresh, fougère nuances. Overall, the fragrance feels sweet, woody-fresh, with a slight bitterness contributed by the rose and geranium. The framework is formed by the sandalwood, which is always very present. The classic characteristics of a typical fougère, such as herbaceous citrus bergamot and earthy mossiness, are sought in vain here. To me, it also feels quite “blue.” Not that it is very marine, but it conveys the freshness of spring water. This fragrance reminds me of my childhood. Outside the village, there was a forest pond that, upon closer inspection, revealed itself to be a spring pool that had carved out its place and flowed into a stream. It was clear and not very deep. Thus, the little sand fountains caused by the rising water were very beautiful to see. There was so much movement in this little world that aquatic plants had no chance of settling. Only on one side was there a small urban corner where a few cattails grew. On a lighter side of the spring pond, a few wild herbs grew up to the shore, and a few roses, which someone must have planted and forgotten, broke through the lush green. The springs were fed by the surrounding highlands, and the pond was surrounded by pines, smaller firs, and ferns. A small waterfall, resulting from the outflow of a spring that was a bit higher and hidden in the woods, completed the scene. Energetic Fougère reflects the olfactory impression of this pond, which felt very fresh and not musty, very well. Everything feels natural, gentle, and harmonious. Present but not intrusive. The longevity and projection of Energetic Fougère depend greatly on the surrounding temperatures and the physical activity of the wearer. On average, it lasts about seven hours before the scent is only perceptible very close to the skin. For me, that is perfectly sufficient. I hope I was able to give you a little insight into the fragrance world of Energetic Fougère, which adds a bit of blue to the green and thus is not a “real fougère.” A modern and successful interpretation of the theme “fougère.” I like it!

I’ve smelled every single fragrance that Byredo has released and I’ve always come back to this one. Something about how simplistic it is, it’s intoxicating. It’s abundantly fresh but not in a blue or green fragrance kind of way— rather like stepping into a pool of pure ISO E Super, assuming where the name of this fragrance comes from. Many have compared it to Molecule 01, which I haven’t smelled so I can’t speak on it, but I find myself in love with the minimalism of this scent. My only real qualm with it, which to be fair is a very notable one when purchasing a fragrance, is its longevity and sillage. As incredible as it smells, it’s much more for your own enjoyment than it is a room-filler or crowd pleaser, because it has very limited range. I’ve tried spraying a comical amount onto myself and in half an hour the smell is gone. If this had more longevity and sillage, however, I’d own 20 bottles of it. If someone is close enough range to get a whiff of it, I’ve always received compliments on how nice it is, but don’t buy this expecting to be noticed as it’s a very subtle statement.

“Small is big for the smaller” - Mehmet Murat ildan Is it a perfume? Is it a plane? No, it's Byredo's Super Cedar… sorry, I couldn't resist. Now, what do you want me to tell you about this "perfume"? I will start with the positives: Pleasant smell? Check Funny minimal packaging? Check Interesting name? More or less Check. And that's it, because the Super Cedar "kryptonites" are many and strong. Let's start with originality. It smells too much like MS Molecule 01, which only means one of two things, either I have my nose totally wrecked or it's full of Iso E super. Now, let's talk about performance. Time is the enemy of all linear fragrances, but this one in me is completely "destroyed" in a blink of an eye. 30 minutes after application and the initial, strong, tall cedar trunk turns into a musky toothpick, with notes of vetiver… skin scent is his middle name. Finally, the price. 110 euros for 50 ml of Iso E super? If EM 01 price is already an outrage, this one is even more “pornographic”. This "super thingy" is nothing more than a little thing pretending that it another thing completely.

My favourite Byredo. It's very difficult to describe it, since for me it has very synthetic smell of a plastic. But at the same time it definitely smells very woody and creamy, which makes it very wearable and interesting. And funny that it has a rose in the pyramid, but i usually don't like roses in perfumes, here i don't smell it.

I understand that some people are anosmic to ISOe. So if you are, I totally get why this is not working for you. I detect it plenty, apparently, since I actually find this sharp and assertive. For me this perfume is cleverly named. Super is a nod to ISOe, obviously--which has a cedar smell. The brilliance is the rose note that quietly floats around and then when you least expect it, it jumps to the forefront and supersedes the cedar. It's a fun wear.

Pro: Very soothing scent. Cedar is very noticeable, but it is not cold or aggressive, it is calming and a little miky. When it is completely mixed with your skin, musk and vetiver makes it seems like that it is your natural body smell. This is just Magnificent. Con: it doesn't last long although it is an EDP.

Super cedar starts with a blast of white musk, evolves with a hint of cedarwood accord, and dries down with white musk. All in minutes though... Well and wow... No projection and sillage at all. Tried to wear from 4 to 12 sprays myself and zero existence, tested it with many other people but no joy.

Title describes my experience Headache inducing, heavy synthetic smell. Barely lasts 1 hour on my clothes, skin is non- existent. I bought it because I still had a old test sample (really old) , from when they released it, and I finally tried it. The Cedar on the sample is stronger, woodier and it lasts and projects far better.
Byredo Super Cedar is in my opinion a very light noted woody fragrance. The impression is very positive when tested on paper however as wearer unfortunately I didn’t experience much of it.

This is a good introduction to byredo in my opinion. A cool, sophisticated musk that has a lingering rose note and a woody note that is perfectly balanced with the musk and rose. If you mostly wear masculine leaning fragrances and want to dip your toes into florals, I would highly recommend this to start a floral journey with.

It's a lovely woody fragrance that combines rich cedar notes with a modern, synthetic twist. It's warm and inviting, perfect for any occasion. However, the scent doesn't last as long as some might like, so you may need to reapply throughout the day!

A game changer for the 1990s, l'Enfant Terrible launched this distinctive floriental for "gen X-ers". I detected it everywhere in the day. The entire composition was creative and the bottle shocking. Oddly I found everything strangely familiar, like a half-remembered dream. It is quite quirky and very elaborate. It's hard to describe. Cranky opening notes like nail polish and hairspray, lavish white florals with neroli dominating all and creamy vanilla caramel base that last for days! It was one of those beauties that you cannot forget even if it's not your thing. There is a peculiar bitterness hidden in there. After the dust settled, the memory lingers...where have all of the years gone? I have to get out my Bjork records.

This is truly an extraordinary perfume. As I have mentioned several times (or maybe not), I received an astonishingly extensive collection of older fragrances as a gift, and this beautiful bottle was among them. So folks, I can't detect anything sweet in this. It rather smells of bitter flowers. Flowers that probably don’t even exist, but that’s how I perceive it at first. So it’s more sharp and somewhat green, completely opposite to the impressions described here. For me, the opulent freshness of orange blossom predominantly reaches my nose, and when I read the ingredients here, it could be ginger that pairs so incredibly well with it, making it slightly bitter-spicy and zesty for me. In my opinion, it has nothing liqueur-like or fruity about it; it rather reminds me a bit of Twilly. Pear is listed, but I don’t smell it, nor do I detect the rose, and there’s no trace of plum even though I do like the scent. It is also supposedly a PARFUM, not an Eau de Toilette, so it must be this version that is depicted here. My bottle looks exactly like that, and it probably doesn’t differ much from the EdT in terms of ingredients, only the intensity is - of course - stronger, but sweet, no way. And I initially didn’t recognize the bottle as a splash bottle, but it is indeed one. (Many thanks to Pollita for the clarification) Since it probably hadn’t been opened for years, it was very difficult to open. Especially since the upper silver thing is really very small and hard to turn. A small towel, dipped in very hot water and placed on the bottle opening for a minute, finally allowed me to open the bottle and present its unusual scent. It certainly wasn’t tilted, as tightly as the little bottle was screwed on. And I am amazed and amazed even more; somehow the sillage seems familiar to me, maybe I had it as a sample before, but I didn’t remember. So if there’s supposed to be a lot of floral notes, they are not detectable to my nose. But it doesn’t matter, I really like it and will use it often. And since it is a limited edition, I will cherish it and enjoy it gladly.

Classique and I came together more than 25 years ago. I had just finished school and was preparing for a new chapter in my life. I was young, enjoying life, the prospects were still not really clear, and my heart had been broken multiple times. Experiences that we all probably went through in a similar way as young people. I wore it for a long time as my signature scent. At first, I kept reaching for my mother's bottle. Later, I got my own. I loved this sensual orange blossom, which initially garnished with a sweet pear gradually mingled with various other flowers. A bit of garden rose, a hint of iris powder, but also tropical ylang-ylang give the fragrance depth and opulence, before this wonderfully warm, cozy amber and musk base gently captures the orange blossom, gradually distorting it and promising a long-lasting, dreamily balsamic finish on the skin. Until the next morning, this fine base always remained and gifted me wonderfully sweet dreams after nights of dancing, wild parties, and painful farewells. I hadn't thought about this fragrance for a long time. Yes, partly I didn't want to. Many years had passed. I went through various stages of my life and forgot some things along the way. Not just with perfume. Even the music I loved, which always held a special place for me, faded somewhat into the background. Much faded into a veil of gray. After diving deeper into the world of scents again in 2019, sniffing many beloved and familiar fragrances, buying and selling some, falling in and out of love, I wanted to have him back. My Classique. With Safanad, a similar representative had already found its way to me. It revived many memories, but it was only similar. When I discovered this wonderful extrait from 1993 here in the souk, I simply couldn't resist. I had never smelled it before. As a student, I couldn't have afforded such a noble fragrance back then. But this scent seemed to want to return to me. To call my name. And I treated myself to this jewel, which immediately managed to bring a radiant smile to my face. Pleasure and bliss, but also the rather sad moments that have their place in every life, were suddenly back. This composition is incredible. Classique in its most beautiful form. Even more depth than the EdT, even more intense and sensual. Even softer and more balsamic in the finish. Finest perfection. For me, a masterpiece. A dream. And a piece of my life, in fragrance form. Yes, the heart knows what it wants. And a true love for fragrance never fades. The same has happened to me in recent years with my beloved music from the past. I listen to it again, the old CDs. I enjoy them. The colors have begun to shine again. And a fitting lyric from the Backyard Babies from 2001 immediately comes to mind: Some things are not just black & white Somebody's gotta shine In colours and it could be me Out of the Jungle Into remedy A heartfelt thank you to DANA17 for this wonderful fragrance dream

Without the ginger note, the scent would be simply stunning. Unfortunately, it is perceptible for hours and is just too pungent for me personally. I also notice the gentle creamy scent component, but unfortunately only very faintly in the background. With a little less ginger, it could have really been a great fragrance, but it is too unharmonious for me, thus too pungent.

Every year we get a new Boss in Motion summer fragrance. This is quite nice, but I always get annoyed when I can no longer repurchase this seasonal item once it's gone. But that's life, and next year there will be another new summer scent, another fragrance will be pushed through the perfumeries. The packaging appeals to me a lot, the box has a slightly metallic orange sheen, and the Boss Orange logo is prominently displayed on the front. The bottle shines even more, with a subtle white belly band and a matching belly button providing a slight contrast. I really like this, the bright orange ball is a true eye-catcher. And here it is, the familiar In Motion orange scent. Only this time it's a bit more subdued, as it's layered with a sweet passion fruit. In my opinion, it's a bit too sweet, almost overly sugary, as I appreciate the passion fruit precisely for its acidity, which has unfortunately gone missing here. However, a very nice mint compensates for this, not too much like chewing gum or toothpaste, but natural and mild, yet still long-lasting and aromatic. The geranium adds floral-spicy notes, while the patchouli follows with herbaceous-green accents. That's about it, no great magic here. One searches in vain for a refined scent development, as well as for an opulent fullness, but all involved do their best to make this a beautiful summer fragrance. And it is, with its fruity-fresh and spicy-green notes, it has everything one needs, plus the combination of passion fruit with mint is relatively rare in the men's section. The sillage is not excessive, but the longevity is quite acceptable at just under five to six hours for a summer scent. For a summer scent release, Made for Summer presents an interesting fragrance. Not really exciting, but quite appealing and attractive for a season. I like it!

So innocent and ladylike. Nothing heavy. It reminds me of a woman who's always nice. She writes thank you notes on engraved personalized stationery. She's always carrying an umbrella, in case. She's prepared, never careless, always on time, always forgiven. But she chews her fingernails, and despite what's in fashion, she always prefers things simple. Her fish is grilled, and her favorite flower is the Daisy. This smells like sunshine, like a little girl delighting in matured weeds.

Opens with a watery blend of green and floral notes. The accord is sweet (rose) and fresh (freesia) the perfect opening for a spring/summer fragrance. However, much to my surprise the scent gradually takes a turn into a sweeter, denser territory: once the top notes vanish I see a magnolia-enhanced lily of the valley-accord. The powdery, creamy qualities of magnolia contrast nicely with the acidic dewiness of lily of the valley. This play with contrasting sensations like crisp/smooth, acidic/sweet, powdery/watery, dense/gauzy makes Inflorescence really special. Additionally, the central lily of the valley accord is very well-made not too artificial/functional fragrance-like. The base is made with a heady jasmine and a silky woodsy musk; they anchor the fragrance to my skin and conclude its story with a luminous floral dry-down.

Like huffing hundreds of tiny white blooms, while staring directly into the sun. Muguet takes the centre stage here, with jasmine close behind. This fragrance is airy, ozonic. There’s a slight greenness that grounds it, like the chlorophyll-infused water in the bottom of a vase. It’s bright and ethereal, but I usually prefer my white florals with a side of citrus. Longevity is solid (~6 hours) for a clean, cloudless-sky scent. Mental Snapshot: Lay in the middle of the park. Gaze into the summer sky until your retinas bleach white. Ditzels of hot, vivid light dance behind your eyelids, forming a pixelated bouquet. tl;dr: sun-bleached blossoms

Inflorescence opens with a nice fresh rose and freesia, green and dewy, very lovely. Very soon, it becomes very lily-of-the-valley centric. It's mostly lily-of-the-valley and a very mild lemon, a lot of it, for a fairly long time. It's lovely and fairly realistic, but I find lily-of-the-valley hard to wear in general. I have similar feelings with regards to Dior Diorrissimo en Dior Lucky, two other very well executed lily-of-the-valley scents, which are lovely to smell but somehow not appealing to wear.

Inflorescence transports me to a forest clearing, where the air is thick with the delicate scent of lily of the valley in full bloom. At first spray, Inflorescence may come across as a bit harsh. Yet, this it quickly gives way to a soft, powdery a subtle undertone of green freshness, reminiscent of newly sprouted foliage. What I truly like about Inflorescence is its photorealism, closely resembling the authentic fragrance of lily of the valley. While some may perceive its singular focus as lacking, I personally adore it. Each time I catch its scent, I am transported to a field of lily of the valley in full bloom.

One must give credit to the brand Byredo, the fragrances are very diverse. Well, not every creation could captivate me, but which brand can achieve that? I must admit that when reading the notes of Inflorescence, I didn't expect much. I anticipated some generic floral scent or worse. Think again! Mr.

Byredo's little backyard garden in a bottle makes everyone shine. As I sprayed the sample on myself, I was immediately captivated by the freshness and greenness of this fragrance, and subconsciously, I had to smile. It instantly brought back memories of a small herb garden from my childhood. In this little garden, there was simply everything.

I received a little box, the label of which I hastily deciphered as "Influenza". Not a tempting title for a fragrance - so I put my glasses on. Oh, Inflorescence. It must be the essence of flowers. And immediately, I am enveloped by a full green floral scent, where the foliage has been incorporated. Fresh and alluring.

By a wonderful coincidence, I came across a sample of Byredo Inflorescence and it was love at first sniff. This fragrance will always remind me of my vacations in France, where I first wore the sample and during our second trip, I got myself the bottle. Spring in a bottle with a powerful inflorescence. The name Inflorescence = flower cluster fits perfectly.

At first, the scent enchanted and surprised me - it doesn't fit my usual preferences at all. But the opening is fresh, green, and incredibly lively. I felt as if I were sitting in a garden, surrounded by blooming flowers. A fantastic bouquet! Are those the freesias? I don't know, my nose is still too inexperienced for that. My late grandfather, however, loved freesias...

I love the bottle, I think I bought it just for that reason, but I am not disappointed. On the contrary, I find that this one smells better than the original; it is lighter, rounder, cozier, more pleasant, simply more refined. Really well done. It also lasts a very long time, which I noticed on my brother, but on myself, I can only smell it for 2 hours... at most, then it's over. As I said, I think the tattoo pattern is really well done, an eye-catcher. Just like the can. And I believe the price is reasonable for the fact that it contains 125ml.

I really like Le Male, it is for me one of the 5, maybe even 3 great classics in the men’s fragrance category that shaped my generation and still do. However, it hasn’t been in my collection yet. But this weekend I was here in Cologne celebrating on the rings and I must have perceived it almost 10 times that evening, really incredible, only One Million comes close. I find it funny to walk through the streets and now, after almost 18 months of dealing with perfumes, to recognize the scents of people. Not so easy, but it works surprisingly well. And of course, such a golden cow will be milked until there’s no more to give. Besides the interesting offshoots Beau and Terrible, which still remind me of the original, but then also dared to create something new and beautiful. Especially Beau is a successful summer version, so to speak THE summer version. And then there are of course the real summer flankers, like this one here. And it’s okay, but definitely remains the last one I test, because it’s really not worth many words, as it sticks so closely to the original. The original is more opulent, even sweeter and more benzoin-heavy, therefore better suited for winter (although the fans don’t care at all, it seems to be heavily sprayed even in the height of summer^^). This tattooed summer flanker is a bit more reserved, watered down. Like Diet Coke, somehow unnecessary and only half as fun. Besides collectors and hardcore Le Male fans, I have no idea who is supposed to buy this summer flanker. They don’t even look better than the normal torso, I’ve rarely seen such ugly tattoos^^. To briefly describe the scent again: cool vanilla. Mint, lavender - typically Le Male, perhaps here with a bit more musk and more sunshine. The bottle is still good, but the cheap tattoos make it extremely trashy and not chic. The sillage is strong for a supposed summer perfume compared to the competition. No wonder, as it’s simply just a masterful, extremely potent winter perfume watered down. Longevity is also above the summer average at 8 hours, even far above. Overall, I’m not impressed when something perfect is copied 10 times just for the sake of good money. So just stick with the original and don’t support such things... at least not directly! As for the brilliant Joop Homme Wild, which has perfectly matched my taste, I can only guess parallels. Both are sweet, but Le Male always has this cool vanilla character, Joop Homme Wild was once again very different with its cherry-coconut accord!

It's quite difficult these days to keep track of all the men’s fragrances, but it must have been this one that I had on my skin today among the Turquoises. At JPG, we have seen a desperate effort for years to maintain the hype through ever-new facets of their flankers. Apparently, the strategy is working! So we repeatedly see light versions, or those that pretend to be one. It is rarer for the base ingredient to be tinkered with, as in the case of Le Mâle Terrible. More often, a facet of the original is particularly emphasized and highlighted, while other aspects are omitted. This year's Le Mâle Summer can certainly be counted among the latter group. It is well done, but only at first glance can it truly be called summery. There is a noticeable lightness, the absence of a certain opulence that is characteristic of the original. Surprisingly, the existing fresh aspects are almost overshadowed by a very dark fruity-floral note. It has an almost medicinal character and somewhat reminds me of cough syrup and dark berries. I liked it, but it also felt familiar. It significantly alters the basic character of the sailor - so much so that there is a distinct individuality to Le Mâle Summer. After a while, the penny dropped: It is exactly the same accord that was recently used by the competition in Joop!Homme Wild. I find it very pleasant that here this note is balanced out by the fresh and cooling sides, while in Joop! it tends toward the candy-like and opulent. If I had to choose between the two, it would clearly be in favor of JPG. Well, competition is known to stimulate business. Currently, in terms of advertising intensity, Le Mâle Summer 2013 is clearly lagging behind the new Le Beau Mâle. But summer isn't here yet, so let's wait and see what rolls in. I find Le Mâle Summer a remarkable change, an absolute must for all Le Mâle fans. For everyone else - probably not.

I keep reading here that Boss fragrances don't fare well in reviews, and probably not without reason. Jour eau lumineuse came to me as a special offer, as an everyday scent, a loyal companion through normal days. And today I am wearing it. It smells lemony creamy on me with recognizability. The longevity is longer on me than I thought, it lasts 9 hours. Boss Jour is beautifully powdery soft, a fragrance that doesn't stomp around everywhere, leaving a statement with warm, slightly fluffy freshness. I wouldn't have bought it at full price, the price-performance ratio seems to often be skewed with Boss. The level of price and the level of perfume then create a gap that is hardly bridgeable. But at 50% off, it's a steal. Jour could become my signature scent for days when I want to smell pleasant and discreet. Who wants to attract attention all the time? It's not as bad as I feared. As a deal, it's a good buy.

Yesterday, three fragrances caught my eye: the long-desired Especially Escada, the enigmatic B Balenciaga, and the unfamiliar Boss Jour Lumineuse. And lo and behold, during the "first tasting," "the bright day" was my favorite. I had actually gone to the store for the Escada. But Lumineuse shines at me so vivaciously that I am immediately drawn to it. So first, I took all three fragrances for a walk and subjected them to a "long-term test." The Boss invigorates with its citrusy start of lime and lemon, and I stride along cheerfully. Freesia and lily of the valley shine brightly - and the osmanthus is the noble factor in the scent. The iris is slightly powdery, and the white birch is naturally green. I rummaged extensively in the bookstore - but, oops, where is my cheerful companion? While its competitors still flaunt on my wrists and gain momentum, my Boss - the back of my hand is empty! It reminds me of my puppy, who one moment is charmingly frolicking on the sofa and then suddenly lies down and falls into a deep sleep. This trait touches me about little Kira - but I feel abruptly abandoned by the Jour. I value loyalty and consistency - even in fragrances. So the interesting and lasting B wins the race - Especially has to wait - but remains on the wish list.

Lean made of Robitussin, vanilla coke, and violet pastilles. Opens with a forceful tablespoon of cough syrup, before swooning you into the backseat of a vintage Cadillac and dousing you in Coca Cola. It’s a boozy amber after that. Sappy, malty, balsamic. Though the medicinal cherry and tobacco-y leather still linger. It’s like a Tootsie Roll distilled to liqueur. Potency is upper quartile for Byredo; this is very much a nighttime elixir, but the one time I dabbed it on in the morning I still went to sleep smelling of Slow Dance. It’s a funny one. I don’t hate it, but I don’t think I’ll be returning. Mental Imagery: It’s prom night, directed by David Lynch. Victory rolls, poodle skirts, a sentient disco ball. You steal a slug of Jack-and-coke from your flask. A jukebox plays Elvis, backwards. “You’re dancing too slow,” Your date croons. “Must be time for your medicine.” Your date is the school nurse. The school nurse is Elvis. Shouldn’t have gone to prom with the flu. tl;dr: cough cola

I had ordered a backup bottle of Besos, as mine was running low. The nice online perfumery included 2 Byredo samples, Slow Dance and Inflorescence. I was just in the process of packing a perfume package, I can't remember if it was for eBay or parfumo. Anyway, the samples came as a welcome addition. Something inside me whispered: "At least give them a try." Alright. Slow Dance on one wrist, Inflorescence on the other. I perceive Slow Dance more strongly from the start. I sniff around my wrist. Somehow interesting. My inner voice says: "Okay, interesting. But you would never wear it, right?" Me: "NEVER!!!" Inflorescence smells quite nice. By the way, I had already included both samples in the fragrance package. Everyone knows what comes next. Again and again, Slow Dance wafts into my nose, and my nose wanders back to my wrist. I shyly admit to my inner voice that I might actually wear it ... O.k., the recipient of the package doesn’t know what I was planning. Inflorescence can stay, but Slow Dance is staying with me, sorry. I need to test it all day long (instead, another sample goes into the package). Ah, it’s somehow very beautiful! I haven't read any fragrance description or notes and I smell raspberry, rose, vanilla, something like incense and leather, it’s sweet but not too sweet and simply melt-in-your-mouth. I tested it all day long. Then it became clear that I had to have it. Found a good deal, jumped on it - et voilà. In this scent, I feel strangely at home. I have (too) many perfumes and use them quite variably. But sooner or later, the longing for Slow Dance grabs me again. It's very me - I can't say it better.

Maybe I’m alone in this peculiarity, but it happens to me more and more often that I choose my fragrance depending on the material of my clothing for the day. So, there are my favorites for silk blouses (Molecule 01, Etro Musk), my cashmere team (Amour by Kenzo, Abel odors Cobalt Amber, Frederic Malle's Dries van Noten,...), white shirt scents (Infusion d´Iris, Ambrette 9), and of course, there are the crossovers that come into play here and there. And then there’s the leather jacket team. Right now, Molecule 234.38 together with Slow Dance (ideally layered) is at the top of my list. I LOVE the combination of these fragrances with the natural scent of my suede jacket. The crunching sound with every movement of my arms, perhaps accompanied by the delicate minty scent of a chewing gum pack from my jacket pocket...and all of this with a cold autumn wind in my hair...this combination makes me utterly happy. Slow Dance starts (for my standards) surprisingly sweet. But not sugary, not delicious, not like something edible. More cool sweet, abstract, and somehow from the very beginning...cool. Just like my leather jacket. The geranium adds a grassy and moist, somewhat classic touch along with the violet. And then the labdanum, the skin-close warm vanilla, the slight and not at all earthy patchouli touch. Now this Byredo becomes really cozy, soft, and comfortable, without losing its coolness. But what blows me away the most is its ability to be reactivated by water. I like to spray perfume on the nape of my neck. Preferably on the lower hairline. With every shower, a captivating scent, a vanillic, resinous breeze comes to me that I would love to make my signature.

At first, it reminds me of incense but with a creamy character, then it becomes floral - no, that's the wrong word, rather softer and rounder, the often piercing quality of incense is completely absent, and that's a good thing, it's more like Slow Motion. I find it has a slightly sweet note but not candy-sweet, more of a fine floral-sweetness, unusually new, different but very flattering for my spoiled nose. Violet, vanilla, and patchouli - what a blend - very, very beautiful. After about 1 hour, it has a pleasantly warm quality; one might think there's a hint of cannabis. Nothing to do with peace and all that. No, I really like the blend after 2-3 hours, it fits perfectly into autumn. A fiery tango with close body contact fits right now, or cuddling up in a blanket with your loved one in the evening, looking deep into each other's eyes and letting yourself fall into those trusting arms. It remains very close to the body, not a loud bang but a quiet whisperer. Two sizes are available; I believe it will quickly find its admirers - rightly so! It has something very erotic about it, surely wonderful on a rugged man. This development into the sensual and daring suits it well.

This is the name of a great track by the band Cake, and I always think of it when I smell Slow Dance. There’s a verse that goes like this: While Frank Sinatra sings Stormy Weather The flies and spiders get along together Cobwebs fall on an old skipping record Slow Dance smells just like that: old vinyl records, cozy evenings during stormy weather, and in the background, the Rat Pack is playing. Pure nostalgia and romance, but completely without kitsch. The fragrance brings together the carefully selected notes in perfect balance. Everything is just right, and nothing is too much. When I first tested it, I was still skeptical, but as is often the case with Byredo, love grows with each wearing, and now Slow Dance is probably one of my absolute favorite perfumes. Longevity and sillage are decent, only the price personally hurts me. But what can you do? true love has no price. An old man sits collecting stamps In a room all filled with Chinese lamps He saves what others throw away

Two days ago, a manufacturer sample of Slow Dance reached me as a surprise addition to a swap (Thank you, my dear ️). Those who know my taste are aware that I no longer lean towards squeaky-sweet, floral fragrances.

The Byredo creations have all seemed too artificial-chemical to me until now, but the listed notes of opoponax and vanilla tempted me to give it another try and swap for a sample. A heartfelt thank you to the lovely A.! There is already a decent amount of sugar present, and combined with the artificially clean patchouli, it initially comes off as mainstream and hollow.

I want to write something great, something significant, poetic. There’s a sensitive heart hammering inside me, damn it! But also voodoo, soul, and hard karate: Because I got to know HYDE by Hiram Green...

The resemblance to Bibliotheque is undeniable. Slow Dance is more present, louder, on the way to "1996," but less spicy and less unisex. The patchouli in it is very restrained, by no means earthy, and together with vanilla, it highlights the delicate violets. They appear more self-assured through labdanum.

As you obviously could realise this is the summery version of Jean Paul Gaultier Le Mâle.For a strange reason many years ago I had grabbed three(!) flasks of this(probably I was living the last three days of the world and I did n't know what to do with my money).Even better I had unboxed all of them and recently I was informed that these flasks are collectible with a remarkable price,but as all of them are used ,I would n't have any possbility to sell at least one of them.LOL! Anyway, after all I feel experrienced enough to leave a comment for the scent.Of course is very similar with classic JPG LM but weaker in longevity and sillage and less complex.In my opinion it could be a four season fragrance (not only for the summer) for several occasions excluding sports and the very cold days.It is a sweet,fresh and less powderly and woody scent.The prevailing notes are levander and musk followed by fine vanilla and sandalwood.Grass is minimal. The bottle is funky and I like it. TIP : If you are interested for the fragrance and you can not find it,just buy the Ford Mustang Perfomance EDT.It is quite similar in a ridiculous price(check my review for Ford M P )

Today at the "turquoise friend," I once again engaged with J.P.G. Particularly with his new summer fragrance. Le Male Summer 2012 should be imagined like this: you are talking to someone who is currently chewing a pack of gum (mint) and wearing Le Male ;) The mint has the advantage of making the perfume very fresh. But I'm not really a mint fan, so it wouldn't be for me. However, those who like mint will love the scent. I think J.P. has brought something new here... you don't smell a fragrance like this on every corner. However, I can imagine that the mint in the top note will quickly disappear, leaving just the regular Le Male... and then you have another scent that so many men smell like... But it is definitely worth testing!

Forgive me, yesterday, by mistake, I placed this review on the perfume sheet of Elie Saab Essence Nº3: Ambre, but it is already corrected and I put the review in its correct place, excuse me. In my obsession with resins, incenses and wood, I came to this "BOSS The Collection", and I found a perfume of amber and vanilla with balsamic nuances, which I like, but that does not convince me. From the beginning to the end, amber, vanilla and resins are present, it is a velvety aroma, delicate and extremely fragile, I see it as unisex, but with a female vocation, that is, it is a perfume that I would prefer to smell in a woman because of its fragility and Delicacy, although, of course, is totally unisex, this is only a personal appreciation. Despite containing few notes, a linear perfume is not felt, because depending on what phase of the perfume we are in, one note will stand out from the others. In the beginning a balsamic leave stands out, with an almost citrus sensation, which stands out against a very elegant amber and vanilla background. Then, that balsamic leave loses intensity and highlights the amber, sweet and resinous, on a sweet background of somewhat medicated, but mild vanilla. In the end, amber is relegated to the background and what remains on the skin is a fine vanilla with some resinous and balsamic nuances. The perfume as a whole is pretty and elegant, but it is sweetly generic, nothing original and with an exaggerated softness, too ethereal or thin, it lacks body, I don't know if I explain myself, but since I applied it I have that feeling. The performance is regular, in me, the duration has been about 6 hours with a moderate-low projection, almost flush from the beginning. An aroma of fresh or temperate climates and for both day and night use, although due to its softness it is more appropriate during the day. The perfume has a magnificent packaging, the box and the bottle are beautiful and quality, but I think it is just a mere ornament to direct attention to the other side and that we do not notice its mediocre content, Eye! I do not intend to offend anyone with this, I just try to objectively comment on a particular product. The aroma is sweet and pretty, but somewhat generic, so I recommend your test before purchase if you can afford it, because otherwise, I do not recommend it, there are better alternatives in the market and at lower prices. Update: From what I have been able to read in different places, the batches from 2015 of this collection have undergone a reformulation, losing intensity and longevity, they say they feel diluted. My perfume decant is from 2017, so you have to take it into account when assessing it and possibly the cause of such unfortunate performance.

The Boss Edeledition fragrances and I are unlikely to become friends anymore. After the booming, petrol-like "Damask Oud," "Velvet Amber" also fails to convince me. Pleasant and agreeable, yes, that at least. But for well over €100, I expect much more complexity. The scent drones on shallowly and milky from start to finish. As mentioned above, only lightly vanilla-tinged amber notes really dominate the experience. There is absolutely no evolution happening. A soft, slightly sweet softie. Nothing more. It doesn't really come across as a men's fragrance either.

It was probably in mid-2011 when HUGO BOSS decided to launch an even more exclusive special series of fragrances within its already exclusive "HUGO BOSS SELECTION" series: "The Collection" Essentially, tailor-made fragrances that are meant to reflect the experience of high-quality materials. These are: Cotton+Verbena Silk+Jasmine Cashmere+Patchouli Wool+Musk and Velvet+Amber This review will focus on the latter: First, one must ask, what do I get for a hefty 110€/50ml?! A lot, I think!! Packaging: Even the packaging celebrates the fragrance. Each of these scents comes in a box approximately 30x20cm in size, with the front adorned by the material referenced in the fragrance - in this case, velvet. When you open the sleeve, a small pouch with a cord reveals the real crystal bottle - simply wonderful! The Fragrance: In contrast to Cashmere+Patchouli, HUGO BOSS did not choose the main ingredient in its almost pure form for this fragrance, but instead paired the amber with a strong vanilla and a hint of tonka bean. Thus, the entire scent profile feels very oppressive, sweet-creamy, almost dark. There is no top, heart, or base note. This fragrance is there from the very first second in its almost overwhelming opulence! This Velvet+Amber is an assassin. Slowly, yes very slowly, the amber-vanilla scent complex increases its intensity until it mercilessly suffocates after about 30 minutes... Longevity: Loooong, very long. 24 hours is no problem for Velvet+Amber. Conclusion: Those who enjoy opulent-sweet-spicy men's fragrances will find their Elysium in Velvet+Amber. Everyone else will meet the vanilla death!

Just got a sample. REALLY good. And I'm not too keen on vanilla fragrances. This is done tastefully. Not too sweet, opulently smoky, unisex/feminine leaning... yeah. This is good. Unique? I'm not too sure. It reminds me of something I either have or have smelled. In it's defence, how many ways can you do vanilla until it's all been done? In any event, this is vanilla done right! Fbw?? For me, no. Only because I know I will own it and not wear it. I have enough sweet fragrances should the rare need or occasion call for it. However, if I smelled this on a woman at some fancy gala or even club, I would be 100 percent intrigued.

I enjoy this almost as much as Seven Veils, which is more of a sensual vibe. There are 3 main entities here that fight for the spotlight. Piercing through a very warm and consistent vanilla is the cashmere wood and cistus labdanum. The note of plum certainly adds a plot twist that makes the transformation more exciting. This is almost the perfect vanilla. After further analyzing, the tenacity and projection of Vanille Antique is lacking a bit for an Extrait, but interesting while it lasts. Sadly my hunt continues for a signature vanilla.

Vanille Antique captivated me not only with its beautiful and dreamy name but also with its scent elements. I first got a sample to test it thoroughly. After several disappointments, I have refrained from blind purchases. VA comes with a very pleasant and warm embrace. For me, the first notes that are immediately noticeable are amber and vanilla. The vanilla is not intrusive or artificial. The warmth of amber. In the drydown, I smelled plum and vanilla in interplay. It is a subtle scent that is not loud and does not want to be. The fragrance was perceptible to me for up to 8 hours. Towards the end, it became woody and the vanilla disappeared. However, the warmth and slight sweetness remained in the scent. So much for the scents. When I apply VA, it takes me on a journey. A journey into the past. More precisely, to the Silk Road. Arriving at many junctions, I smell the entire spice world of the Near East and Asia. I let myself be carried away by the many different merchants and their goods. Eyes closed and nostrils flared, so as not to miss any nuance. I sit by the roadside and enjoy my mint tea. Merci beaucoup Byredo.

Anyone who loves Arabians Tonka by Montale will love this even more. At the beginning of my journey through the diverse world of perfumes, I eventually came to the Extrait de Parfum by Byredo. At first sniff, I wasn't impressed; I was only used to generic scents, sweet, fruity, and not long-lasting at all. After the second and third spray, I was in love. The scent is simply sexy, best suited for going out in the winter evenings or on summer nights. Woody, spicy, interesting, and exciting. I love this scent more and more every time I wear it; I completely lose myself in it. The sillage and especially the longevity are overwhelming, and the price definitely reflects that... A perfect and successful fragrance.

Unfortunately, I can't describe the scent... but I would still like to share my experiences with you. The fragrance was a gift from my girlfriend for our first Christmas together. My first thought was: what could I have gotten with this budget for 50 ml... My girlfriend liked it so much before the purchase that she just assumed I would like it too. As someone who loves vanilla scents, I was initially disappointed after the first sniff. I couldn't really pick up on a classic vanilla scent... After using the fragrance 2-3 times, it became indispensable in my collection. I really can't describe what it smells like, but it's just incredibly good. Every person I've shown this fragrance to couldn't stop sniffing the bottle. The scent is simply unbelievably UNIQUE That's why I only use this fragrance for special evenings to smell correspondingly special. The sillage and longevity are good, but given the price, they could definitely be stronger.

... between Arabians Tonka and Instant Crush and 9 months later "Night Veils - Vanille Antique | Byredo" was born. I will now go into a bit more detail about the fragrance notes. At the beginning, I perceive a slightly metallic note, similar to the top note in Instant Crush. However, I cannot clearly assign this note to either the iris or the plum.

I stumbled upon this fragrance by chance, and it completely blew me away. I really like the vanilla; it’s very pleasant. Unfortunately, it’s a bit expensive, but it lasts really well and is especially great for evenings. It's definitely worth testing out - you can find it at Breuninger, Oberpollinger, or sometimes at Pieper.

I am often a huge snob when it comes to summertime or sport-inspired flankers. A majority of the time they either appear pointless or smell less than pleasing on my skin. However, every now and then, I am proven wrong. Classique Summer 2012 is one Summer flanker that I actually like. Although it shares similar accords with the original Classique, I find them slightly different. This Summer flanker is less sweet and surprisingly muskier in the base. It's also less elegant and more casual. The main notes to my nose are sweet, pulpy clementine, feminine orange blossom and musky vanilla. It goes on rather smooth and floral, despite the citrusy opening. I am most impressed by this fragrance's composition, although I must admit that it is rather simple. Classique Summer 2012 is too good not to be worn during Spring and Autumn as well. I couldn't bear the thought of this flanker going into storage every time the seasons change. Everything seems to be pointing me in the direction of a purchase. Even the bottle design is oddly alluring. I love all versions of Classique, but it's this flanker's fresh orange blossom opening, and grounded, musky vanilla base, that causes me to lust over this fragrance alone, and leave the original in the dust. If you need more convincing, I'll add that the lasting power is good, and the sillage fairly strong, but nowhere near as heavy as Classique EDT or EDP. I believe that I'll be wearing quite a lot of Classique Summer 2012 come this December. Original review written: October 2012.

So, here it is. The new summer fragrance from our Paule. What do we expect when we test this little gem? Right. Good mood, summer feeling, carefree enjoyment, umbrella drinks.
