Zenne, which represents the character of a beautiful and flirtatious woman. To be honest, I was afraid of blackcurrants when testing the fragrant pyramid, as I don't find them particularly special in perfumes. Blackcurrant is very irritating to me in some fragrances and is close to my tolerance limit.

….I am a nameless hero. I am the reflection of the marginalized. People don’t think about me; I belong to the “Others.” My everyday life is marked by dramas, tears, and pain, accompanied by my passionate dance performances. I am yours, I am a part of you. I belong to the We. And we are all kneaded from the same dough.

Many thanks to Niklas for the manufacturer sample of Zenne :-) This is a really beautiful women's fragrance that would also work great in the colder season. The longevity is really good at 9 to 10 hours, and the sillage is impressive as well. The top note starts with a lot of rhubarb, a fruity sweetness, and a hint of blackcurrants.

I have tested Zenne over the past few weeks and must say that the fragrance is another Nishane that is unjustly flying under the radar. The trend of "clean girl vibes" includes many mainstream scents, but Zenne is nowhere to be found, or only very rarely...

This is a combined review of Hacivat and Hacivat X which I tested from samples on consecutive days and also compared directly. I've never tried Adventus, so can't compare these to it. I do have and enjoy Montblanc Explorer. Hacivat is a really nice, strong and masculine fragrance with a great pineapple-citrusy opening. The dry down does have some subtle old school vibes with the oak moss and woody accord. Hacivat strikes me as much smoother and less woody than Hacivat X and Explorer. Overall scent is people pleasing and is a definite versatile easy grab for most any occasion. Longevity is very good with strong sillage. On to Hacivat X. The major different between it and the OG is that X has a much more pronounced woody accord, the pineapple/citrusy opening is not as prominent and X comes across as sharper or less smooth. The OG seems a bit sweeter than X. I'd also say that Hacivat X is closer to Explorer, although Explorer is even sharper and more woody. X is also a very masculine fragrance (perhaps more so than the OG) with the same great performance as the OG. In the final analysis, Hacivat and Hacivat X are both great fragrances, so it just comes down to personal choice on which you'd prefer. My preference leans towards the OG and it isn't redundant seeing that I also have Explorer (they don't smell alike). Hacivat X would be redundant since it's much closer to Explorer. My recommendation would be to start with Hacivat. If you want something woodier, go with Hacivat X.

Hacivat X Like the og opens op with pineapple and citrus and you get that oakmossy vibe only this time it’s like a smoky vetiver. like smokey birch style like oakmoss. This time the pineapple is accompanied with a lime note making it a touch sweeter and more creamy i think because of the lime and maybe some jasmine or hedione touch. this for my first impresions is still like 85/90% like the og it smells very very nice. The legendary hacivat dna is still here. It’s hard to talk about perfomance because the samples spray so little it can’t be compared to a real bottle atomizer. But i think its good in the power department. Haci X dries down and keeps this creamy oakmossy vetiver while it lingers to softness. If you love the og you will also love this.

I tried this at the store and had a good enough first impression of it that I decided to go for the bottle. On skin I feel it's fantastic, absolutely perfect summer fragrance. The pineapple I'd been told about is there but a little more subtle, a kind of lime/bergamot scent seems to take center stage instead. On the dry down it does take on more of a warm sweeter side I've come to associate with some other Nishane fragrances. Very happy to have this

I am surprised that this is classified as "fruity" because I am definitely not getting fruit from this. I am also not picking up any of the floral notes. I would say this makes for a great chypre fragrance. The top is spicy with the pink pepper and a hint of bergamot. I maybe get a hit of the lime in the middle but it is easy to miss. Mostly, the Haitian vetiver dominates this scent from the start. Its little bit smoky and very woody. That paired with the sandalwood and patchouli just makes this scent very woody to me. Its good, just kinda disappointed that the other notes are lost. It lasted on my skin about 6 hours and projection was about 4.

First of all, I want to say that I have been using the traditional Hacivat for years and know the scent DNA very well; also the surrounding themes like Creed Aventus over several batches/years. Why do I start with this comment? Well, from my perspective, an extremely large number of reviews are strongly based on false expectations - what does the community expect from a anniversary edition? - If they had pushed the performance with even more oakmoss and Ambrox, comments would have flown in like "Hacivat has released an elixir, little innovation, who needs more performance, expected more" - If they had completely changed the scent DNA, it wouldn't have become an anniversary version, but rather a new line hidden under well-performing brands; I can already see many opinions coming in here You see, no matter what the niche houses do, we always find reasons to criticize what has been done, and everyone with their personal expectations or, even worse, the personally-influenced opinions of others. The idea behind Hacivat X is, in my view, not to get closer to Aventus (sorry, but anyone who knows Aventus batches knows that Hacivat X has absolutely nothing to do with any Aventus batch), but to bring a "more mass-appealing" variant of Hacivat to the market that a) gives niche lovers enough "niche" but makes the scent more suitable for everyday use in the office, etc. b) does not give newcomers the full blast of oakmoss; that is really challenging for many Now to the scent itself, finally: - I find that Hacivat X is quite similar to the original, the Hacivat . The additional bergamot takes away the already aggressive, rather piercing pineapple note in Hacivat a bit. The opening is therefore not so "harsh," but much rounder - The drydown feels more harmonious, rounder, and a bit more floral to me. The big difference is that the base is now more woody, slightly floral-fruity; Hacivat hits hard with full oakmoss and woods here - The H/S is really good, of course not as extreme as with Hacivat, but we are talking about significantly above-average projection and longevity; whether one really wants to project for 24 hours is the question. If the goal is to show that one has spent a bit of money and needs the performance - well, then it's better to reach for Hacivat. But anyone looking for a pleasant companion for everyday life will be very well served with Hacivat X - The price - well, known to be high at the beginning, far too high. I think prices will adjust drastically once the scent is fully retail-ready, the ideal price point for the 100ML, in my view, should be around 200-220.- - Comments on sophistication; well, was Hacivat really more sophisticated? It is much harsher, edgier. How do you even define sophistication? Roja has a high level of sophistication, but then we complain about the performance :) Overall, a successful scent for me, and unfortunately, I cannot agree with many comments here. But that is not my goal or my mission; objectivity is much more important to me here. Just enjoy the scents, and let the fragrance affect you without thinking in every direction.

Hello everyone, As I read the statements here so far, they mostly lean towards the "meh" direction... But does that really do justice to Hacivat X ? In my opinion, no! (And I will, of course, explain it - in detail) A new Hacivat , can it be good?

HACIVAT X is a standalone creation that clearly differs from its predecessor "Hacivat | Nishane." Unlike "Hacivat | Nishane," the pineapple note is no longer in the foreground, although it is distinctly noticeable in the opening and quickly retreats. This change gives HACIVAT X its own unique identity.

I was visiting a friend in Rostock this winter and strolled past a really beautiful, newly opened perfume store in the pedestrian zone. When I spotted the Xerjoff bottles, I just had to ask my buddy for a "quick detour." The owner, a really nice guy, took a lot of time to let me sniff through his selection.

Honestly, the purpose of this Hacivat offshoot escapes me. The original has become almost a classic and is largely very popular. So why would one change the formulation to create a variant that now leans much more towards the original "Aventus | Creed," yet lacks any of the Aventus charm?

I actually find the scent good, but there is a certain note that bothers me. Unfortunately, I can't pinpoint it exactly. It could be the Haitian Vetiver that is bothering me. It's just too "vetivery" :D. But those are my impressions of this fragrance. I thought it would be better than Hacivat, but I was sadly proven wrong.

I really wanted cherry mist for my VS collection. When I saw it for the first time in 2024 I unfortunately couldn't buy it cause of it's biggest popularity then. But when it recontinued in a new design, I was really happy! Rocket Pop smells like sour cherry in lemon juice. It literally smells like sour belt candies or cherry lemonade. To be honest, I like the design of 2025 more than the previous one. The bottle main color looks like a pool!

So fresh, fresh, exciting, this fragrance is so exciting to me. So fresh fresh exciting, like a lemon verbena shower for meeeeee. Exciting, her little development is so exciting to meeeeee. I've been thinkin' 'bout peppermint by the way. Baby, uh, I like the way you refresh me. She's fresh, fresh, exciting. This fragrance is so inviting to me, yeah. Tell you somethin' this is really fresh for meeeeee. A refreshing scent with way too little longevity. Therefore, it’s already time after a short while. Hit Repeat (spray, pfft pffft) and sing So fresh, fresh, exciting, she’s so exciting to meeeeee.

Is there anything more beautiful, more refreshing than a summer rain? I love the scents of nature, and one of the most beautiful is the smell after a heavy rain shower in summer. When the trees and bushes are in full bloom, they emit an incredibly lovely fragrance as the rain pours down on them. The earth also has a pleasant and very characteristic scent when it rains during the summer months. The air, previously hot and unbearably humid, cools down and carries entirely new olfactory impressions. Especially where trees are present. Whether in the forest, in the home garden, or in the park. A fragrance that comes very close to this impression is Verveine Menthe by L’Occitane en Provence. The scent of verbena and citrus notes reminds one of fragrant trees and bushes after a good downpour. The mint enhances the impression of the still damp air before the ground quickly evaporates the moisture again, and a muggy heat builds up once more. The mint also makes the fragrance feel slightly cool upon spraying, a delight on hot days, especially right after a shower post-workout. The wood and musk tones in the base are exactly to my taste. Bright, delicate, and completely free of annoying synthetics. The musk is so finely balanced here that the freshness remains, which only very few summer fragrances manage to achieve. Many tend towards a laundry detergent or fabric softener scent with floral undertones of musk. That is exactly what we do not have here, and it makes the fragrance unique. Unfortunately, the pleasure lasts only as briefly as a summer rain does. Verveine Menthe is a very fleeting fragrance. If I hadn't known that we were dealing with an Eau de Toilette, I would have guessed it was an Eau de Cologne. At the latest after three hours, one should reapply if they want to catch a bit of this delicate hint of summer rain. I have heard that the fragrance is now supposed to be available for regular purchase again. For that, I can only express my great praise to the charming brand L’Occitane en Provence. Not many fragrances return to the market after being discontinued. It cannot be ruled out that some houses occasionally take a look here and read along. After all, the fragrance has quite a few fans. Lastly, I want to thank Floyd, who introduced me to the fragrance and even gifted me his bottle afterwards. A true enhancement for hot days in my collection.

He comes, the flickering cool mist. It swirls on the horizon, rushing over the hot summer fields of Provence, rocking sparkling verbena and fresh mint, making them dance among the bright citrus trees. I close my eyes and let it happen. Its breeze makes my clothes flutter, I feel its tiny mist droplets on my face, the refreshing coolness on my skin, in my soul, dreaming myself for a few short hours into a shady little grove of light woods, settling gently with the green and citrusy freshness on soft musk. Yet it is always very close to me. When it has then gone after three to four hours, dried by the heat of the day, evaporating over the concrete of the city's canyons, I call for it again. And it comes, the flickering cool mist.

"One values dust, a little gilded, far more than gold, a little dusted.” (William Shakespeare) Summer scents are my favorite. Bright, pure, and sun-drenched … They are hard to describe, for what words can one find for all the brightness, all the light, all the warmth on our skin? How does one find words for the scent of summer? Green-golden and citrusy it is, this fragrance. Fresh, cool, and clear from the very beginning. A light, bitter hint of mint wafts along, like a gentle breeze … lending a quiet, finer tone to the cheerful radiance of the lemons, green and enchanting. This scent is airy, refreshing, without being loud. It accompanies us, stays with us like a good friend. With a subtle warmth after a while, bright as the sun itself. This is how groves smell there in Languedoc, at Pic de Canigou ... Often the good suffers who seeks better. (William Shakespeare)

Awesome fragrance. Smells fantastic, expensive and high quality. Very unique for me, but I have not tried the two Penhaligon's in the 'smells similar' list. Relatively dry - little sweetness - quite masculine. To simply describe it, I'd say mainly spicy, with some lavender and resinous base. But, it's by no means a simple fragrance. Performance is powerful. Seemed to last forever. Left with a pretty strong scent on my skin after 12 hours. Sillage was quite good for about 3, maybe 4 hours. Its strength would probably limit its versatility for some guys unless you are quite confident. I usually don't attribute any emotions to fragrances I wear, but I found Papilefiko to be strangely uplifting for me. Brightened me and my day. I'm putting this on my full bottle shopping list. Price is reasonable at discounters.

If you’re familiar with Dominique Ropion’s spicy creations, you’ll catch a similar vibe in Papilefiko. Does that make it redundant in a collection? Maybe for some. But for me—not really. Before picking this up, I was already enjoying Costume National Homme, also by Ropion. The openings? Definitely cut from the same cloth. But while CN Homme leans a bit synthetic and stays pretty linear, Papilefiko feels smoother and more dynamic—it actually evolves on skin. Plus, it wears lighter, making it more versatile. Blazing Mr Sam comes to mind too—it shares that spicy kick in the opening. But Mr Sam opens heavier and dries down richer, which makes it more of a winter scent in my book. Papilefiko, on the other hand, works nicely in fall and spring as well. So yeah, similar DNA, but each one has its own lane.

Very linear, sweet pine and lavender juice. A fragrance I thought would be great for summer, but it would disappear 2 hours after application. In cooler weather, that sweetness was absolutely vile and sickening. Linear, sweet, boring, disappointing. I find the "Similar" suggestions on Parfumo really out of left field, so few of them have anything to do with anything for a lot of perfumes I have tried.

So first, the story behind the review, as that seems to be mandatory here. I had Papilefiko in my Advent calendar - yes, I received an Advent calendar with 24 (25) niche fragrances to test. That was really, really nice! Unfortunately, it led to me spending way too much money on perfume in the last few months, if that's even possible. I initially had Papilefiko as a 1ml sample and was blown away from the very first moment. I was instantly thrilled, and so it made its way onto my wish list. But as it goes, other princes come to the dance and you test, sniff, buy, and get influenced. First, it was "Tony Iommi Monkey Special | XerJoff," which had to move on quickly, and then "Oceania | Roja Parfums." Well, and about 10 other niche fragrances. But luckily, Papilefiko lost its glass slipper on the stairs and thus stayed on my mind. So I went on a search, in the souk, in perfumeries, and everywhere it could have been hiding. And fortunately, there were still the magic nuts, and suddenly it appeared as a fragrance mail in my mailbox. I sprayed it, and the fascination was there again. That beautiful feeling when something just fits. And this time, I won't let it go again! For me, a fragrance that simply doesn't get enough attention here, and what bothers me about many contributions and statements are the endless comparisons. "Smells like" xyz + abc. "DNA already exists" here and there. "Longevity is better/worse than," "The dupe is better than the original," etc. "Perfume is art," a wise person once said, and it's not a competition or race. Try to capture and understand a fragrance for yourself! And yes, fragrances can only be perceived subjectively, as they trigger emotions in the brain, evoke memories, and that's a good thing! About the fragrance itself: For me personally, a clear 10. Especially in the top notes, a very nice fruitiness unfolds in the combination of coriander, cardamom, citrus combined with jasmine notes. Not overpowering, but enough to stay in your mind immediately. After some time on the skin, the spiciness comes forward and achieves a really beautiful and long-lasting softness with fir balsam, lavender, and moss, with just a hint of sweetness. The lavender supports and remains present the whole time, but is not intrusive. In contrast to many other comments and statements, I consider Papilefiko a masterpiece, as it is incredibly well-balanced and has just the right dosage in terms of sillage and longevity. A beautiful fragrance that I have rediscovered after a long search and have embraced in my heart. There aren't many fragrances that I spray on my skin and, in that moment, bring total relaxation, well-being, and enjoyment to my mind. Definitely worth testing!

Such a day full of surprises doesn't need a perfume. Or rather: no Parfumina. A woman needs a little love, a small gesture, or simply a scent. A scent like "Papilefiko | Nishane," which gently caresses your soul, calming your heart with lavender. I immersed myself in a sea of flowers to let go, to be "me." A fir balsam for the spirit, with spices as an ingredient for more happiness and relaxation. On that evening, the fragrance was a revelation for me: “Don't let your shine be taken away, just because it blinds others.” Thank you for allowing me to test the fragrance.

The Papilefiko is a fragrance for relaxing and feeling good. This pleasant balsamic note is really beautifully crafted. In addition, there is pleasant lavender, a light freshness, a nice sweetness, slightly green and subtly resinous/vanilla-like due to the balsamic flavor. The fragrance starts lightly fresh, greenish, and with a subtle spiciness.

I discovered Papilefiko by chance during my trip to Dubai, and it has accompanied me ever since as the scent of hot days. Another masterpiece from the hands of Dominique Ropion. Those who know his creations understand that they play in a high-quality league, and this one is no different.

I was finally able to test several fragrances from the Time Capsule Collection by Nishane (Papilefiko, Tero, Kredo, etc.) and I must say that this line is massively underrated! These are truly beautiful and unique scents, each with its own character!

To complete this Time Capsule collection of reviews, I’m giving this Papilefiko one as well. At least the 4-pack that was released in 2022. Another one came out last year with Deziro, which I will definitely test as well. This Papilefiko is already quite popular and is definitely the best-known one in this series.

This is my first Nishane fragrance that I am testing more thoroughly than just a quick sniff on a strip in the store. So far, the brand hasn't really made it into my consciousness. A souk partner had the fragrance in his lineup. Average rating 8.0, coriander, lavender, and fir balsam, sounds good! Let's go! Top note, wow! It feels very oriental!

Smells really goood Is floral, kinda citric, fruity and sweet I think is perfect for Spring or even summer Perfect for daily, leisure and evening. I would give it an 8/10 cuz Im not so into floral perfumes, but this one is really good! I love ittt You may find it by $20 normally if there's no special offers!

It was one of those days in February 1975 when spring seemed just within reach. It was still cold, the sky was gray and heavy, and only a few snowdrops were stretching their fragile green from the chilly ground. A cool wind blew my braids around my ears as I tugged at my mother's hand, eagerly stumbling over my own feet, wanting to go faster, wanting to be there soon, my parents, my sister, and I, where it was loud and colorful and fun, where the carousels spun in circles until I got dizzy, where it crashed and clinked and screamed. The fair had been in our town for days, and for days I had been pestering my parents, whining and annoying, begging and flattering, until it was finally time, until it was said: "Put on your coats, girls, we’re going to the fair!" It didn’t matter that my hands and feet were cold, that I had to wear the silly hat that I had secretly stuffed into the bag my mother wanted to donate to the charity. It didn’t matter that I had to stand in the corner as punishment today because I had punched Robert, the idiot, in the nose until it bled. He deserved it; he shouldn’t have called me "Pippi Longstocking." It didn’t matter that I couldn’t join in the rubber twist, that we had pea soup for lunch and my sister got to eat more pudding than I did. It didn’t matter at all - all that counted for me was the fair, into whose fairy-tale world I was diving at that moment. It was loud, very loud. Music blared from speakers everywhere, there was clattering and crunching, and every bang at the shooting booth was met with cheering comments. A long howl came from the ghost train, followed by rattling and screaming - involuntarily, I gripped my mother’s hand tighter, which now stopped at the cotton candy stand. Shortly after, a pink-and-white mountain blocked my view, sticking to my nose, cheeks, and chin, seeming more delicious than anything I had ever eaten. We rode bumper cars, bumping into every vehicle, the smell of rubber, metal, and roasted almonds in my nose, beside me the best dad in the world. I rode in circles on the unicorn, one hand on its mane, the other holding a thick, red-glazed candied apple, indescribably happy. At some point, it started to rain, twilight set in, and we walked home in the encroaching darkness, the gingerbread heart around my neck, the slowly fading screams of the fairgoers in my ear. My mother washed the remnants of cotton candy and roasted almonds from my hair, then she tucked us into bed. I dreamed of ship swings, giant teddy bears, and popping popcorn, of the calls of the stall owners and the organ grinder. Four months later, I woke up. It was white around me, white and warm and very quiet. The bed I was in was not mine. I didn’t know the black man in the white coat who was leaning over me. His eyes were friendly, his mouth smiled - then he moved it, as one does when speaking, but nothing came out. Nothing at all. Not from his mouth, from no other mouth, never again. On that day, the little dove was born. "Déliria" strikes me right in the heart. No scent has yet been able to conjure the smells and the atmosphere of that very special day, to make the old images come alive as if almost forty years had not passed since then. The sweet and the cold, the hard and the soft, the delicate and the coarse unite with light and dark in a fragrance that I cannot say whether I like it, whether I would want to wear it beyond the test. I am torn back and forth, a little frayed too - and at the same time very grateful for this unexpected journey into the past. PS: Franfan - thank you!

Déliria! What an apt name! After using this fragrance, I feel close to that state which can be understood physiologically as a delirium, a state of confusion, an etiologically nonspecific organic brain syndrome: disorders of consciousness, psychomotor disturbances, changes in perception... At the forefront of my (still somewhat present) perception is the promised metallic note, which is horrifically pervasive, cannot be displaced even by a hesitantly emerging base note, and disturbs me more and more despite or because of the contrasting sweet undertones (is that the rum, the candied apple, or the cotton candy, in any case something sticky, gooey, sugary?) so that with each of my tests, I could not resist the pressing desire to wash off this uninspired mixture. I cannot recognize any real development, whether in a positive or negative sense. The fragrance does not change significantly until I wash it off my body and perceive with relief the healthy scent of fresh water that rinses away the sticky-metallic soup. How could this happen? L'Artisan creates a new line (Explosions d'Emotions: not really a successful marketing gimmick, this loud name), lovers of this brand (to which I expressly belong) become curious and are all the more disappointed by the modest, indeed failed product, and this applies in my opinion to all fragrances in this new collection. What remains as a summary? I am hardly willing to sacrifice more lines than necessary for this mediocre fragrance - and this may astonish some and please others, who have often accused me of excessive epic breadth. Hardly any fragrance I have discussed here has left me so perplexed. The manufacturer of Timbuktu, Fou d'Absinthe, and Navegar, as well as many other great successes, perhaps one of the few truly serious niche brands, has made several olfactory missteps here, for which one can only hope that they will be history by the next season at the latest and that none of the great treasures from the truly significant historical portfolio of the brand will be displaced. Fin!

... just give it a good shake and what happens is roughly what occurs in the Menthos in Diet Coke experiment - a quasi-explosive reaction ;-) Dear folks, I'm not really a fruit freak, but this falls under experimental chemistry, right? Squeaky sweet, synthetic fruit aroma, loads of sugar - wow! With this mix, I also know where the metallic note comes from... from the falling dental fillings! A bit later, a bitter note comes in, maybe because the nose and brain shut down the perception of "sweet"?! The sillage is fortunately not too abundant, but the stuff sticks like caramelized sugar syrup on the skin! Warmly recommended by money-hungry dentists ;-)

I also tested "Déliria" freely without looking it up here, just like "Amour Nocturne." And when I called up "Déliria," I was surprised by what others perceived. I do not disagree with that and do not doubt it either. However, I had noted that "Déliria" is something you need to get used to. At first, I smelled a very intense aquatic scent. With such a start, I tend not to expect too much and feel a bit disappointed. Because such a scent, even here, smells synthetic. But then "Déliria" becomes enriched with green and slightly herbal notes, bright and light. After a relatively short while, the fragrance turns slightly sweet and fruity; I was convinced, and I am convinced, that it is Osmanthus. So, a floral scent with a fruity note that I really like. Yes, when I think about it, this Osmanthus smells just slightly like an aromatic apple, not artificial. During the progression with the Osmanthus-apple scent, lightly green, the aquatic note disappears. Gradually, as noted 10 hours ago, "Déliria" transforms into a greener and denser tuberose note, similar to the floral scent at the beginning of "Amour Nocturne." Since I was simultaneously testing "Amour Nocturne" on the other wrist and still have it, my preference shifted between the scents. I couldn't and can't decide which one I prefer. Then my attention was directed to other things for hours; after all, there is more than just perfume. When I sniffed "Déliria" on my wrist again around 3 PM, it smelled floral, delicate, and a bit like heliotrope, but much softer than the real flower smells. By now, "Déliria" had developed into something a bit sweeter and more lovely. By around 5 PM, I could also perceive vanilla. Although "Déliria" has weakened after 12 hours, I still smell a light vanillic floral scent, namely heliotrope. I found the sillage to be close to the body and light. I believe that "Déliria" is a feminine fragrance.

Oh dear, I think I'm feeling faint. I smell blood, blood, and more blood. I'm already feeling weird while typing. Unfortunately, I can't detect the delicious candied apple or the promised cotton candy. The rum is there at the beginning, but the bottle full of rum quickly and relentlessly fills up with fresh blood. The sillage is quite strong. I can't comment on the longevity because I will soon try to wash it off. For lovers of metallic scents or for a vampire on Halloween, this fragrance is certainly the right choice ;-)

I like it. I don’t like it. I went back and forth quite a bit with Deliria. In the end, I find myself somewhere in the middle and would never recommend it, let alone buy it. For me, the perfumes from the "Explosions d'Emotions Collection" are all just scent experiments. Everything from nice to unbearable and terrible is included.

Scents, colors are as sensitive as words. Sometimes you can find them, but very often they remain hidden from us. Can scents be described? We can depict our emotions, write poems, reviews, treatises on fragrances, but we cannot simply translate the language of scents. If it were possible, we would have long had an app for our iPhones.

The visitors at the fair are captivated by the fireworks and do not notice that a sailor in a blue dress is sneaking around between the stalls with a bag in hand, searching. Yes, now he has found the stall he was looking for. He looks around, no one sees him. Quickly, he pours the powder from his bag into the cotton candy machine and adds a few green-and-white rings.

I find little about the Zara fragrances here. So, I would like to describe Zara Night, as there are certainly interested parties. The notes must have been mixed up, but I can't find anything more precise about it online either. The scent is very warm, soft, vanilla-like, sweet, and musky. I suspect a large amount of heliotrope and musk combined with amber. There are subtle almond notes coming through. Possibly something fruity is involved as well. I would guess strawberry or something dark and sweet. I don't perceive any light floral notes like peonies or roses at all. I know the spring fragrances from Zara and their notes, and this scent is more suited for winter. I don't want to say that it smells particularly high-quality. No, it doesn't. Zara Night reminds me of the musk bombs from my childhood that gradually disappeared from the market. More like an overly dosed fabric softener or a vanilla deodorant from old times, but certainly charming and pleasant. I like it very much, and that's why it got to come home with me. Zara Night also has a vanilla-powdery touch but is not dusty or dry at all. Well, the bottle with the glued-on gold-colored studded band all around is no longer that trendy. Studs are actually out again, and all bottles that hold some value now seem to feature rose gold, I've noticed. But that doesn't bother me; I care about the inner values. Zara is always worth a visit for women's fragrances. I'm not so fond of the clothing, but there are one or two scents that have convinced me. One shouldn't be deterred from testing if one happens to catch a sweet fruity water right at the beginning. Eventually, one will come along that pleases. The fragrances are all different from one another. null resembles the other. They are especially wearable, and I use them regularly and with pleasure. These fragrances do not gather dust in the closet, like some that lack the right occasion. I will also wear Zara Night during the day in winter. In spring and autumn, rather in the evening. But the sillage is pleasant. It is not a screaming scent, but a warm skin caresser that accompanies me for many hours.

-Oh my...! Did you see that? A grapefruit the size of Mount Everest just fell from the sky! -Yeah. It seems it was hunted down by this even bigger jasmine that's following... -Do you think we should run? -Probably, but having just eaten this delicious exotic dish with its slight dose of cummin and all this pepper, I don't think I'll be able to... -Yeah, me too...The damn dessert was so loaded with cinnamon and cloves, that my stomach debars any thoughts of running. -So what shall we do? -I don't know. How about play nonchalant and go pick some juniper berries? I think I can smell some nearby... -Agreed! They would make a fantastic finale for such a surreal day!

Onde Sensualle is a captivating spicy fragrance that goes in opposite directions. The beginning is harsh with the Juniper berries, saffron and ginger taking center stage. More than obvious how big and overwhelming it is but as the fragrance dries is when the magic happens. The drydown is heavenly as the jasmine amber musk and agarwood come to the surface. This fragrance starts off harsh and i almost went to take a shower in an attempt to scrub it off but i showed some patience to see if something different developed and it did in a beautiful way. The last couple of hours smell almost completely different than in the beginning. Some fragrances are linear, this beauty sure is not. Can be picked up for a pretty good price too and the bottle is kinda cool. Even though it's a unisex fragrance it leans female but it's not the end of the world nowadays.

First of all: This scent has its own kick. The reason I don't wear it is solely that it doesn't suit me. "Onde Sensuelle" is full of tension and warmth, coolness and relaxation. Yes, it sounds contradictory now, but somehow Bertrand Duchaufour is simply the perfumer who manages to bring together seemingly incompatible elements with a few clever twists. The end result is always so homogeneous that it feels entirely natural, yet it is conceived and still effortlessly light and authentically organic. He is a master of improbable connections, of deliberately placed stimuli that hardly anyone else thinks of. I have the utmost respect for that. So what is this scent? It is very fresh, fresh and warm. That's already a beautiful contrast that is skillfully bridged in flight. The freshness is prickly, due to the juniper. Its counterpart is ginger, which appears here in a rather soapy-fruity, exotic-meaty way and is not very sharp. Just these two notes are so beautifully combined, playing off each other so wonderfully while still interacting, it's a sheer delight. The spices are partly on the fresh side, partly on the warm side. They often seem to switch flanks, resisting and then finding their way back, nudging and caressing each other. Overall, this scent has a truly beautiful rebellious sparkle that quickly exhausts itself in words but can create true enthusiasm in the nose. Everything is jumbled together yet is masterfully choreographed. Yes, this scent is brilliantly conceived and crafted. And yet it wears poorly. I can imagine that on some skins it could create irritating impressions. As much as this perfume is a small work of art, it behaves rather combatively on a warm person. I can't quite describe it, but while wearing it, there were always significant elements that did not correspond at all with my body scent, and others that blended perfectly with it. Perhaps it is the fate of this fragrance, which has so much within it, that it doesn't fit well anywhere. Attractiveness and repulsiveness are combined here, but in such a beautiful harmony that together they result in "Wonderful." It leaves one quite perplexed. I'll let it sit for a bit and see what happens. Unconditional sniff recommendation!

A very dear parfumo user has sent me an original sample of Onde Sensuelle, and I can only thank them warmly ;)) I am greeted by a gentle wave of citrusy juniper. Even though the pyramid shows nothing citrusy - it definitely smells citrusy. Like a wonderfully ripe, freshly cut lime. Right next to this lime are freshly picked, not yet dried juniper berries, which still hold all the power of the juniper bush, including its woodiness. I can't really perceive much of the other spices, even though I know each spice very well and even have them in my kitchen. They merely form a spicy, warm background for this fresh citrus juniper. Simply delightful. It is truly a pleasure to enjoy this L'Artisan. If it weren't for the price, this sensual wave could land right with me!

Juniper is an exciting spice: Fruity with a citrus direction. Piquant-fresh like coniferous wood, just not woody. A cool spiciness, without being herbal. Warm facets that contrast with the aforementioned cool aspects. So complex, it can also be unwieldy and not so easy to use in cooking. It goes well with sauerkraut. However, its true calling seems to be the classic Sunday roast, whether from pork or game. Here, the complexity is highly welcome, as the savory aromas temper the unwieldiness. In terms of quantity, the flavoring of spirits with juniper is probably more significant, not just since the gin and tonic revival of recent years. There are some perfumes that create a gin impression with juniper as a note, whether it's Oliver Cresps' "Juniper Sling" or seemingly every second Geza Schön scent. I really like that, but I always have concerns about whether this spirit impression should prevent me from wearing it at work. "onde Sensuelle" is undoubtedly a juniper scent. With curiosity about whether Bertrand Duchaufour would serve us a gin cocktail, I approached the fragrance. Initially, I smelled mainly rhubarb. However, juniper quickly becomes dominant with all the aspects described above, each enhanced by other notes: the piquant-freshness with the mentioned rhubarb, the fruitiness with a juicy-sweet mandarin that can be sensed even in the base, the cool spiciness with cardamom. Early on, the fragrance becomes warmer through saffron without its sometimes present dustiness. The whole thing rests on a warm, fluffy musk base that is just dirty enough (animalistic would be an exaggeration) to not feel too clinical. Furthermore, the base is simultaneously warm and fresh, so I suspect a strong dose of ambroxan is uniting these rather contradictory characteristics. This combination of juniper with notes that overlap with its scent impression leads to an exciting effect: when I casually smell "Onde Sensuelle," I notice only juniper as a note. However, when I concentrate on the perfume, I perceive the juniper aspects separately - a fruity mix with mandarin, a fresh one with rhubarb, a cool-spicy one with cardamom, and a warm one with saffron-musk - and through this unfolding, I no longer recognize the juniper as such. A bit like Heisenberg's uncertainty principle. This may sound exhausting, but it is not at all. On the contrary: this keeps "Onde Sensuelle" varied, and I don't seem to get used to the scent so quickly. Another consequence of this type of composition that should not be underestimated: I never have the impression of having a gin flag. Or of being a Sunday roast. And that is not the worst thing for a juniper scent.
Hm, I have already tried several L’Artisans, but I haven't encountered any in the, let's say, different or special bottles yet.

This artisan is, firstly, quite rare in collections. And secondly, somehow "exotic" - which probably results in the "first" point. And the exotic nature of it is precisely what makes it exciting. Here, both "temperatures" and "colors" can be sniffed out. It probably arises from the straightforward ingredients that this is the case.

A really nice vanilla scent that's a dupe for Wrapped in Vanilla but slightly less gourmand and more of that bubble gum note? It is a great vanilla to wear year round and actually lasts pretty well for a body spray. I actually prefer these bottles to the BBW bottles! I'll be sad when I'm finished with this one.

First off I find the name of this fragrance kind of confusing since theres another VS body spray called Pink - Vanilla & Dreamy that came out at the same time yet their very different scents. To the point where they are not comparable at all. Aside from almost having the exact name, I like this scent. To me this is a very cake edible gourmand vanilla. And it has that vanilla extract to it. This is sweet but not overly sweet and I think this would be a crowd pleaser. It is very light so you may need to over spray this one. All in all I think it's nice and this is one I think I may try layering with other scents.

I feel like Shem has been flying under the radar for most people. Either because of the ridiculous high price tag or the dominating rose note, I rarely to never see it mentioned. It is definitely not a fragrance for everyone; quite the contrary, the rose + cypriol combo can seem unusual and overpowering to inexperienced noses, especially the way it is done here. But to me, this whole blend is both addictive and prestigious. I like the way @Static titled his review just below - "Business class". I feel like that's a very fitting evocative label for Shem , for this does smell high-quality. However, I certainly did not expect it to be as sweet as it is, almost candy-like. The Turkish rose unapologetically dominates the scent right from the start, with a very rich, sweet, velvety aroma, with hints of spice, smokiness, and even a honeyed edge. It is warmed up by the cardamom accompanying it, which is also responsible for the lemony/minty undertone. It could just as well be the geranium, though, as its complex herbaceous rose-like attributes include a slightly citrusy twist. nulltheless, the opening is intense, yet beautiful in every way. Dark, sweet, complex rose, blended with warm spices and aromatic touches. Soon, the cypriol takes on the scene, which adds this slightly smoky, spicy odor, with nuances of woodiness and earthiness. It also seems to be the one responsible for the alleged "faint cigarette smoke scent" that my dad picked upon. However, for me the osmanthus steals the show at the heart due to its impressive complexity of fruitiness and florals. It basically reminds me of peaches, but with a stronger sort of floral creaminess on top, like a mix of jasmines and orange blossom. As for the amber, it's not very pronounced, mostly warming things up while taking a step back, leaving the rest of the notes shine through. At the base, this very prominent lemony scent with balsamic and fresh, spicy qualities of the elemi resin completely overshadow the rest of the base notes. The rose, cypriol, and osmanthus, which persist for most of the wearing, aid it further in diminishing the smell of vetiver, of which I can barely pick up any, and leather, which takes it a while to properly show. And even after it shows, it is still quite mild (to me), struggling to properly identify it. I mostly get some warmth which I can associate with leather. Overall, great blending and quality - richness and depth throughout the whole wearing. But I will say it strikes as a little linear; that strong rose/osmanthus/cypriol overpower mostly everything else right from the start and through most of the wearing, so there isn't a lot of development at first glance. In terms of performance, I was expecting this to follow the lead of most other Nishanes on my skin and fade away by the 5 hour mark. But to my surprise, Shem stuck to my skin for somewhere around 9-9.5 hours. And I was also pleased to see it deliver pretty good projection and sillage, with 2+ feet for the first two hours, after which it would take a step back and form a one foot bubble around me for like 1-2 more hours. Somewhere around the 5-6 hour mark, it would turn into a skin scent. Overall, quite solid. It should be clear by now that this isn't a fragrance to be worn daily, nor to your usual getaways or at places where you have to keep it lighter (e.g. gym). This feels like it was made for special occasions, like weddings or similar dressed-up situations. And for men worrying that the rose in here might give the fragrance a more feminine lean, rest easy - this is rose done in a more masculine way. Not overly so, however; it is still definitely unisex. So in the end, you won't see why I like Shem until you try it, or maybe you won't see why it isn't talked about more until you give it a sniff. It's really a love it or hate it affair, but if you enjoy fragrances with a dark, sweet rose being the main protagonist, then it's well-worth sampling Shem . But is it worth getting a full bottle of? No, I don't think so. Its retail price of around €450-€550/50ml is simply exaggerated. And while I believe the end product is definitely high-class and rather underrated in Nishane's catalog, it's not really worth what they ask for it. But hey, if you can afford business class, I guess that this should be pocket money for you. Overall Rating: 7/10

This is a fragrance with character, elegance, sexy, it has a green shining vibes, like the color of its bottle, but at the same time warm, sophisticated and refined, it reminds me of those gala dinners at night, when you want to draw attention but without screaming, because you are phenomenal in a natural way, you are already like that, this is truly a neck breaker, Shem means candle, because when you use it you shine like thousands of candles around you and you make yourself noticed and with this fragrance I feel powerful, elegant, opulent, sexy and unique, and of course, I consider this scent very unique, and obviously when you wear a scent like this one, you want to smell different and unique to those around you, and others will know it, they will know that because you’re shining on everyone around you. The flowers are giving that refined and elegant touch, its green and earthy notes that are distributed on the three levels are giving that powerful aromatic touch that together with the amber gives that warm and smooth creamy temperature that it needs to make it powerful, opulent and outstanding to finalize its leather note that It gives a soft animalistic touch but without offending, that feels so rich and makes it sexy and very unique. Regarding its performance, we are talking about an Extrait de Parfum, which is a high concentration, on my skin has lasted 12 hours, taking care in the sprays, but in general it has a decent performance of 10 hours, however if you love to overspray like me , this fragrance becomes a beast mode and you could easily reach more than 10 hours, it has a projection of 2 meters easily, in conclusion a decent performance, personally it fascinates me when a fragrance lasts more than 8 hours. I could consider it as a night fragrance, but please, use it when you want, this conveys greatness, if you feel like this and want to project it then use it, and always use the fragrances that make you happy! It is for us and to convey to others how incredible we are, just be careful with sprays in warm places. Thank you very much for reading my review, I invite you to try this fragrance, it is worth a lot, I wish you good health and blessings.

Close the doors, dim the lights and enjoy! Feel the relaxation , sink peacefully & dream away. Experience high quality ingrediënts wich instantly creates hapiness. This is entertainment at the highest level. A discovery of “re”newing elegancy & luxury in every sense of the way. The price tag? I imagine they said to Lucas Sieuzac ….”No limits, just create”. Creamy leather with a superiour touch of vetiver. This is realy up, up and up! Just the name “Shem” i find not suitable here. Candle, light out of darkness? No not at all! This is gold! Next level niche! ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️

Shem wasn''t a love at first sniff for me. It came over as a bit muted, introvert. Also I did not like the composition. But there was something about it. A few times I just suddenly thought, without actually smelling it, about the scent profile (without knowing that I was thinking about Shem). So I was jus walking somewhere and I thought: "oh yeah that is a good smell. What is that again? .... It is Shem!" I ended up buying it and it is great. Thick, daring, bold. I think one spray is enough, I dont think I will ever wear it to the office.. :)

Hello everyone, today I would like to TALK about a fragrance that deserves many expressions, the underrated, the overlooked, the black sheep of the family, or the evil brother of Nefs - and I will explain why. Underrated + overlooked: As of now - only 51 people here (!) have the fragrance, so I don't know how meaningful the ratings can be. In my perception, they give a rough direction, as it is relative how one evaluates something (my opinion). But I also think that many do not know it effectively because of the price of Shem , more on the price and my recommendation later. Black Sheep + Nefs in Evil: I chose this point deliberately because I see it this way and I will tell you why. When you look at Mana + Nefs , then Shem is all that (NOT) what Nefs is. It has zero sweetness, absolutely none. Shem primarily works only with cardamom, cypriol, and leather; the other notes like osmanthus, amber, rose, and so on are just side appearances that briefly say HELLO but are quickly gone again. And Mana works even more with rose, saffron, incense, oud, and labdanum. And that's why, in my opinion, it differs massively from both! It is dark, evil, and consistent in what it does and wants to be! (A small note from me regarding this, Shem resembles my old 2019 Layton Exclusif very closely after about 4 hours! Dark, smoky evil - I just wanted to mention it!) Performance: Anyone who says it doesn't last 12 hours, I can only heartily recommend going to the doctor (really!). Applied yesterday around noon at 12 o'clock, showered in the evening at 11 o'clock, and now around 3 o'clock I can still smell it very noticeably! It stands up to Mana , Nefs , and Hacivat Oud in terms of pure longevity, so all in all a 10 out of 10! On the topic of sillage: It is "somewhat" quieter than the others, although that is also relative! I perceive it as not so brutal regarding projection - my wife and I were separated yesterday by 5m - 6m (as the crow flies) and she noticed it extremely while I only took 2 sprays... - so you could say yes, relatively! For whom and when to recommend: This is always very, very difficult to say with such special fragrances; some would say work, some would say dining out - I would say YES YES, but it is a matter of dosage, as it is strong. Primarily, for me, it is a STATEMENT FRAGRANCE, it is one as it is written in the book, it is very CONSISTENT! And when October to March comes, it is really good in my opinion! Is it worth the money? This can only be evaluated subjectively and relatively. If I say yes and you say no, or I say no and you say yes, it really doesn't matter in my opinion. I like to evaluate a fragrance based on what it can do, what it offers, how it is made, and so on. And with this fragrance, you can really notice the quality, and that is no lie! Nishane always delivers in terms of quality, and you often see what is feasible and implementable, and I would say, you should definitely test it! How does it come across and what role does cardamom play? I admit, I was a bit apprehensive here because the fragrance has 0 (!) sweetness (from Nefs ) or soft aspects; it moves forward, a real statement fragrance, so I thought, well, that's okay... But I forgot that there is also cardamom here, and anyone who doesn't know what effect cardamom can have on women (can - not for everyone) should google it briefly! 99% of people have liked / loved the fragrance so far, but only with a subtle dosage of 2 - 3 sprays; otherwise, it gets modest here :P ! Recommendation: If I really weren't convinced, I wouldn't recommend it to you! (At least for a test for sure, and if you like this direction, then congratulations on your new Shem ) And now have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______

One of the strongest scents I have ever tested-stayed on the paper strip for weeks. With Shem, I couldn't detect any ingredients at all. There was just this intense smell that penetrated my brain-nothing delicate, nothing subtle, just this sting-I was addicted. Friends and family reacted to the paper strip like this: “Yuck!”, “No way!”, “What is that?!

Shem by Nishane. For me, a new dimension of perfume - simply because I have never had a fragrance like this before. I am thrilled! An impressive presentation of the high-quality bottle encased in a metal lattice. It definitely meets the expectations that the (steep) price evokes.

Before I take a short break from perfumes due to vacation, I would like to introduce you to "Shem | Nishane." I actually like this leather-rose scent quite a bit. However, I find the price a bit exaggerated. The longevity on my skin, on the other hand, is really great, as Shem lasts well over a day! The sillage is correspondingly strong.

À Fleur de Pêche is perfectly pleasant fruity patchouli, but it's hardly unique. It smells almost exactly like Britney Spears Believe--I even tested them side by side to confirm. The L'Artisan version is a little airier and cooler but also more short-lived. Considering the Britney bottle was $16 and the L'Artisan runs closer to $200, I think I know who wins.

There’s some peach in there, but it’s more like peach blossoms mixed in with other spring flowers. Light floral, but not peach fruit to my nose, which is what I was hoping for. Still like it for springtime though, or for an event where I need a light floral. I imagine more of sitting at a garden party in April than a peach grove.

I had the chance to try out this one when I went back to Etiket. I'm quite happy I got the chance to try out a new arrival, as I often feel like I'm a bit late into the niche game. I don't have a lot of experience with peaches in perfumes (I only have one in my collection as a travel size), but the notes called out to me and I was curious to see how they'd turn out on my skin. This is a really beautiful peach fragrance, showcasing all the different facets of a peach. At the start, I get this Fuzzy Peach kind of scent. There's sugary sweetness, like biting into a fresh peach right off the tree. After awhile, the scent shifts its focus towards a fresh, aquatic-like fragrance with a predominant jasmine note. Ambrofix is probably the culprit for the aquatic freshness. I don't have a lot of experience with aquatic accords yet, but it was lovely. I had a feeling pink pepper also played a role in this refreshing twist. Jasmine overpowered the rose to my nose. There's a soft earthy vibe coming in from the patchouli, but it never veers into the woody territory. Overall, when smelling this fragrance without trying to overanalyze its note, you get a sweet, fruity, fresh and aquatic peach, stunning in all of its facet. It's a soft, refined feminine interpretation (quite classy) that has great lasting power on my skin. I'm still debating on adding a bottle to my collection, but I have the impression it's more about my personal scent preference (what I want to smell on my skin during the day) than the perfume itself.

I got a sample of this for free. Well... I had to pay for shipping. When I saw the notes, especially the Tonka Bean...I thought '...could this be in line with Tom Ford Bitter Peach', ,,which, digressing, caught me by surprise with how much I loved Bitter Peach. (...Peach is not a note I favor) So I was surprise, and wonderfully so, when the first blast was not what I expected! My nose immediately picked up the floral component of this. It now became more in line with a Christian Dior J'adore than Bitter Peach. This of course was how it acted on test paper. However, on my skin, I began to picked up the sweet notes, but it never veered towards the sweetness of Bitter Peach. It is still very floral, fruity, soft, giving it a refinement with the added delicacy of sweetness. It's a well done scent; good peach fragrance. Worth a try ( if you can or are willing to pay shipping)

This is a very unusual peach scent to my nose. It's neither edible, nor like powdery peach skin, nor the big syrupy peach some of us might remember from 90s fragrances. The opening feels cool and artificial, a white peach surrounded by floral and woodsy aromachemicals. It's sweet and even a little juicy, and unmistakably peachy, but not a realistic portrait of the fruit. Texturally it feels ozonic, but also dense in its sweetness. I never had a diet white peach soda, but that's what comes to my mind when I smell this peach note. And to be completely clear, I'm talking about the old-fashioned stuff with aspartame, not some modern sugar free flavored sparkling water. The base of the scent is creamy and woodsy, with a lot of very clean, softened patchouli. There are definitely some florals involved, too, but I don't find them defined enough to single out anything specific. In my opinion, this is a weird release for L'Artisan. They're fragrances usually have something natural, sometimes quirky going on, but this is just on-the-nose synthetic cleanliness and sweetness. I would rather expect that from a designer scent or newer, trendier niche houses. I have nothing against intentionally synthetic scents, but this one feels a little off to me. It's a new take on peach that makes me appreciate the old takes. Even though something about it intrigues me and makes me want to retry it, it's ultimately not something I would want to smell like.

I made the mistake of trying it on skin before getting in a bus for 3 hours... While I liked it at first, the very sweet notes gave me nausea very quickly... If you like peach, this is definitely for you although I find that it is a relatively synthetic smell.

Tried it in Paris today. Lovely! Natural peach smell with loads of jasmine in the middle and base. Very refined and natural, silky, smooth as usual with L’Artisan. The peach is more of a dry peach peel, with salty nuances, not really a sugary fruity peach. Then the jasmine makes it really creamy and clean, floral.

This is a perfect ode to peach. It’s got the fuzzy peach skin, the syrupy juices, earthy pit, and a natural breezy quality. It is French summertime embodied. Like eating a freshly picked peach in a garden in Plovan, with fresh white sheets drying around you. A crisp air breeze, a basket of stone fruits, dreamlike.

If you want a juicy ripe peach scent this is not your girl. However, I think this perfume is lovely. The peach note is more like when you’re at the store and you are trying to find a good peach and so you’re smelling for ripeness through the skin.

So, on my skin, the jasmine takes over, and it's almost as powerful as the jasmine in Mugler Alien. I don't mind it but I was hoping for more peach, which is also present and is lovely in this scent, but is immensely overshadowed by the jasmine. Overall, this is a well done scent but heavy on the white floral, and not fruit.

OOOO-WEEEEE. WOW. Opening is quite fecal and challenging. Afrika Olifant is one you want to apply about 1 hour before heading out. But after it dries down - oh man - is it great. It's in the same league as Kouros, El, Juste Filthy and Hyrax. Kinda a difficult to describe. If you think of all these scents as having their animalic component and everything else (spices, florals, amber, etc.), on one side you have Kouros which balances it in favor of the 'everything else'. On the other side of the spectrum, there's Hyrax which puts the emphasis on the animalic component. I'd put Afrika Olifant sorta in the middle together with El and Juste Filthy between Hyrax and Kouros. Hyrax seemed pretty useless to me - not much of a fragrance outside of an off, mild leathery scent. All the others are real fragrances that are versatile and wearable. I'm definitely adding this one to my shopping list. Performance is quite good. Got a decent 10 hours of longevity out of Afrika Olifant with a skin scent still remaining. Sillage was strong for about 3 hours. WARNING: Afrika Olifant is not for the cotton candy callants or bubble gum boys. Your balls have to hang low and heavy to carry this one off. This juice is testosterone in a bottle.

I don't understand why Afrika-Olifant has such a poor reputation. While it has a tantalizing animalic undertone, the key players are warm resins and a superb leather accord. There's nothing dirty or indolic about it; Jorge Lee's genius mixture of musk compounds comes off as a clean, powerful musky volume. Think of it as an animalic fixative that elevates the raw materials and greatly improves the wearing experience. The opening is loud and spectacular; myrrh and frankincense kick the door down with their boozy, fruity, honey-like, smoky and spicy nuances. Labdanum and ambergris add another fruity/sweet layer similar to ambrarome in Lustre - something between cherry, caramel and coca-cola. Once muskiness starts coming to life, you end up with a luxurious fragrance which oozes decadence. Initially, castoreum and labdanum provide their usual dry leatheriness. However, 1.5 hours into the wear, a different kind of a leather note pops up. This one is incredibly rich and oily, rounding out the scent in an arousing fashion. The drydown phase is an interplay between leather and the powdery remnants of musks and resins. Performance is solid, it lasts for up to 12 hours on my skin with moderate to soft projection. Given its captivating and borderline seductive scent profile, it's a good choice for date night. That said, it works fine as a daily driver during the colder months. If you love amber/leather perfumes and don't mind the musky aspect, grab a sample of Afrika-Olifant.

MUST HAVE fragrance and at least MUST KNOW for Zoologist's pet fans. So there will be a lot of skins, thick skins and hair. It smells like a combination of the scents of different animal skins (musk, civet, castoreum) and combined with agar and smoke of roasted resins: labdanum, myrrh and olibanum - that's not bad. I do not recommend the perfume to people who avoid animalistic notes, although the smell in my opinion does not give the impression of "animally repulsive", on the contrary. Rather directed (in my opinion) towards male skins, and especially THICK-SKINED creatures (ha ha), although ladies who want to mark the area with their presence will also interestingly subordinate the surroundings, especially those consisting of bearded individuals in tubular and short pants, who are looking for places in the woods where gluten-free dumplings live.

Do not let the listed notes scare you off, for Afrika-Olifant is anything but a blood-thirsty animal. It's a tamed, gentle, docile beast, misjudged by many from the distance. Even I was reluctant of approaching this creature, believing it would bite me harshly. But I was terribly wrong, and now I cannot stop coming back to it to pet it. Upon first spray, I get an addictive warm, ambery sweetness from the labdanum, accompanied by an ever-so beautiful blend of spicy and balsamic accords, with a bitter undertone, enveloped in light smokiness - all attributes of the unmatchable myrrh. The frankincense adds more to the warm, balsamic accords, while also unleashing a dominant resinous scent, which is just magnificent in combination with the rest of the ingredients. The ambergris further aids the ambery-warm section of the composition, while also bringing a musky accord somewhere in the background. Simply put, a delightful resinous-forward opening. You'd be inclined to believe that the dry down is where the beast starts growling and showing aggression. Notes like castoreum, civet, and oud are hardly beginner-friendly. But the intensity of these notes in Afrika-Olifant make it probably the best starting point for anyone discovering animalic fragrances. There's just a subtle animalic base, overpowered by the resinous, ambery, sweet opening. There's no sign of a fecal odor, which can sometimes accompany animalic notes and/or oud; all I get is warm, musky, and sweet animalic scent. Hardly any leather either (to my nose, at least), which is anyways rather difficult to point out on its own in a warm and sensual blend like this. Once the resinous sweetness from the opening begins to settle down, the base notes - civetone, muscenone, muscone, thibetone - offer a calming and soft finale. All of these brought together just make for a musky, warm finisher with an animalic tonality. To me, the way everything comes in play just evoke two words in my mind: elegant sensuality. Or, to keep the gentle beast metaphor alive: tamed animal. There are unfortunate downsides to owning such a creature, however. But these don't apply to most out there. The sample I obtained of Afrika-Olifant could be part of a bad batch, which would explain the rather disappointing performance I get on my skin compared to many others out there rating it highly in longevity and projection. So keep that in mind; I might be an unfortunate exception, either because of a bad batch or because of my skin chemistry. nulltheless, I get about 6-7 hours of longevity at the very best, which is fine, but I do wish it extended to at least a solid 10 hours. For projection, it's decent for the first half an hour to an hour, sitting somewhere around 1 foot and a half to 2 feet of sillage. But after that, it rapidly declines, becoming a skin scent by the 3 hour mark. Quite disappointing, for I was very hopeful that I would get the expected performance here. Seems that "a gentle beast" fits as an even better description than I imagined. Yet again, if you were to judge Afrika-Olifant just by its note pyramid without actually trying it, you'd struggle to find a social occasion where you could confidently wear it. But well, things are turning out quite the other way around. I would wear Afrika-Olifant nearly anywhere, aside from leisurely or as a daily (money would be the problem, primarily). Sure enough, I'm speaking for myself here, for if you get better performance out of this one, its versatility could take a hit. Still, it won't make you smell like an animal, even with good projection, for the terms "gentle" and "tamed" many reviewers use refer to the understated animalic accord of the fragrance, and not necessarily to its soft projection. In my case, it applies to both. Afrika-Olifant rapidly made its way onto my wish list, and if it weren't for its poor overall performance on my skin, a full bottle would've been a priority. The dominant resinous and sweet aspects of it, with that tamed animalic base that added some depth overall, made me fall in love. It's smooth, it's sensual, it's delightful, contrasting an expected pungent, rough, barnyard odor if we were to judge just by its notes. So in conclusion, never judge an animal by its fierce, menacing aspect. It can turn out to be the exact opposite. Overall Rating: 6.9/10

Spices, resins, incence, oud maybe? And the most important, the overdose of animalic notes. The easiest way to describe this is the way the lion's den in a zoo smells. Dirty and fecal in a good way, sweetened just enough to make it more palatable. Very distinctive from anything else I have smelled. Longevity and projection is beast mode, 14+ hours on the skin.

Hands down one of my favourite fragrances of all time! It has very high quality ingredients and the skill from the perfumer is very apparent. The scent mixes classy deep oriental notes of myrrh and smooth sweet resins complemented with gorgeous animalics like civetone, Oud and other musk molecules.

Though not outwardly too animalic, I can see why Afrika-Olifant is not one of Nishane's most popular. The combination of notes can be a little rough for newbies: a mélange of (mostly synthetic) animalic notes combined with spicy resins and leather. The spiciness in particular doesn't show up in the notes listing, I mostly get a sharp cinnamon, perhaps also with some clove.

If this is an elephant, it must be Benjamin Blümchen. Tempted to leave it at that. There's not a hair on any animal that I have ever encountered that this perfume smells even slightly similar to. Iow, there is absolutely NOTHING animalic here.

Out of all my collection , (atleast 100 bottles) Afrika-Olifant is the only one I’ve completely emptied. I’m now on bottle number two. I’m a lover of animalics like Leather Oud , Hyrax etc. This is right in the same league. This fragrance is the perfect blend of resins, and musks. Starting so smooth and then drying down to a more textured musk.

This is one fascinating perfume! I was slightly terrified to try my sample because of the polarized reviews. I’m glad I did (though I’ll be honest, I sprayed a very small amount on my skin just before I was going to have a shower, in case I hated it). I didn’t hate it, not at all. There’s something very attractive about it and something repulsive about it too.

A double zesty zing of Citron and Petitgrain - liquid sunshine - open this, accented by mere hints of Coriander. Drying into the heart, green Shiso and the green floral of cyclamen comes into play. Musk is my major player in the base, followed by grassy vetiver and dry, woody notes. Sillage on my is decent, but longevity is severely lacking, but this an EdC so.... I also could be a bit dehydrated, so that would reduce longevity as well.

So much in advance: For Mr. Duchaufour and the company Puig, department "L'Artisan Parfumeur", it was not a fireworks of creativity to name this fragrance "My Number 9". For this name, I only give one point. The fragrance deserves a bit more. Details now on this channel. L'Artisan Parfumeur is - similar to Villoresi from my last comment in this series - a moderate luxury label, albeit one that belongs to a large corporation, and one where various big noses can let loose. With this label, you don't necessarily think of colognes, and yet LAP even offers a series with six waters, of which at least 4 also meet my personal definition of cologne (the others are tendentially floral colognes without citrus or otherwise fresh notes). This is the first one I am testing. In my (superficial) first test some time ago, I found the fragrance unspecifically nice, gave it 8 points, and wrote a somewhat inspired statement. Yesterday, I tested it more deeply and was (then immediately) thrilled. A fragrance that reaches me in the heart and evokes childhood memories, in this case memories of overnight stays in mountain huts and hikes in the Alps: Sprayed on, and shutters are thrown open: Bright, dense, citrusy yellow sunlight streams in, but not the glaring, harsh light of southern latitudes, nor Mediterranean radiance: This is the strong, rich morning light on a mountain pasture. The hesperidic notes immediately blend with the herbaceous, damp scent of straw from the hayloft, and a steaming green (mist veil of dew-soaked meadow; perhaps also that it rained during the night). Everywhere is also the scent of flowers, fertilized and then trampled by cattle, with a hint of violet bitterness yet still enchantingly gentle. This mélange of muted citrus-fresh with herbaceous-floral, damp-green, and earthy-herbaceous notes creates a wonderfully composed whole, a dynamic nature symphony that is stretched somewhere in my coordinate system between Eau de Campagne by Sisley and Valeria by Harry Lehmann (which is a great compliment for me). By the way, the scent impression does change in the first two or three hours, with sweeter and resinous-balsamic tones coming to the forefront, but the overall impression, including very resilient citrus notes, remains intact. I was inclined to sing the praises of Master Duchaufour once again and raise it to at least 9 points. By the way: A green-herbaceous natural cologne (remotely related to HL's New York); despite cardamom and coriander, it is not a brown spicy cologne. Today, a third test with just a small remainder, which I only sprayed on my wrist, under everyday conditions. And a certain sobering set in. Because "Number 9" proves to be not only very long-lasting for a cologne (five to six hours), but also almost enervatingly projecting and, unfortunately, not beautiful anymore in the final phase. AndYouAndI in her comment from five years ago is completely right! The fragrance is only beautiful as long as the lemons play along! In the drydown, this is no longer the case, and then Number 9 becomes strangely, disharmoniously sweet-floral-earthy, yes, I even find it at times to be piercingly cool and artificial. Very unfortunate. This could have been a love affair. So, a descent into the valley, a return to the city, and a sober evaluation: Just under 8. P.S.: Price 120 euros for 100 ml.

“Mon Numéro 9” was a total blind buy. It’s not really my style, and it usually goes wrong. The brand and the perfumer were decisive factors, and not least the fact that summer is approaching and the ingredients sound quite appealing. After the first spray, I hopped around the apartment in joy - could my blind purchase turn out to be a real hit? The citron is super zesty, but it doesn’t come off too sour; instead, it is initially accompanied by a bitterness that I find exceptionally pleasant. This start is quite delicious! To be honest, I can’t get enough of it; it’s such a “I-want-more!” fragrance experience. As is fitting for a true citron, it doesn’t remain solely sour or bitter, but brings along an underlying sweetness that makes this scent incredibly tasty and pleasing. Soon, I smell the rhubarb leaf, although I would never have guessed that’s what it is, but you can definitely smell the green, and it fits well with the start. And then, after not even an hour, the super delicious citron unfortunately runs out of steam, and - yes, I know, it’s an Eau de Cologne, that’s how it can and should be, and for all I care, it’s even appropriate - I am a bit disappointed. The green bitterness lingers for a while, and the resins slowly shine through, giving the scent a somewhat woody, coniferous quality. Nevertheless: The harmony of this (and surely not just this) fragrance, according to my nose, clearly lies in the interplay of top, heart, and base, and the scent loses a lot of charm as soon as the (extremely delicious!) top note disappears; it brings about the great silence in the woods. That can be nice too. The good thing is: you can reapply, and then everything is back, and it all smells wonderful, really, incredibly tasty. Still, I have to replace the originally awarded 90% in the excitement of my blind buy with 80%, and this beautiful Eau de Cologne truly deserves that despite the mentioned weaknesses. I have become curious about all the other Numéros and am already toying with the idea of a bunker bottle of “Mon Numéro 9” for the summer. Longevity: Unfortunately, the top note weakens quite quickly here, but overall you get a good 3-4 hours of the scent. Sillage: Quite decent at the beginning, but with the departure of the citron, it becomes rather close to the skin. Target group: Completely unisex, bam! Occasion: Spring, summer, everyday - the scent is very pleasing, absolutely suitable for work, for me it’s not a date or going-out fragrance, but a daily all-rounder. Don’t forget to bring a refreshment! Conclusion: An absolute test recommendation for all Cologne and citrus fans. I am very curious about more Numéros from Duchaufour!

Citrusy, green, and fresh scents - I often don’t get lost in this fragrance direction. Of course, one enjoys smelling fresh, but most scents in this category are too one-dimensional for me, touching neither my emotions nor my imagination. Quite the opposite of this one, which reminds me of my time in South America two years ago when I visited my brother. The story is slightly adapted to emphasize the scent associations. I stroll through the streets of Cusco, Peru. The air is thin, my lungs have not yet adjusted to the altitude, I had just overcome my mild altitude sickness yesterday and had to get out of my hostel bed. It wasn’t late yet when I was drawn to a bar on the slopes of the former Inca city. A hidden gem according to Lonely Planet, one of the most popular travel guides. And so the hidden gem was no longer a secret, as one backpacker joined the next. A room full of young people, thirsty as they were experiencing the most exciting time of their lives so far. Strangely enough, this bar had a very Western vibe, tequila shots were being prepared. The usual mess of lemon juice, alcohol, and salt was hastily wiped up with a bunch of crisp green twigs by a bartender in a dusty jacket, who was far too old for this party. You could see it on him, and you could smell it in his Eau de Cologne, which was far too classic for this place. Something familiar yet forgotten, leaning towards Fougere. Repelled by the backpackers, although I was one myself, I was drawn to the back corner of the bar with my Pisco Sour. I observed the little man, his wrinkled face, stretched with weather-beaten skin. What was this man doing here? Was it just a job, or did he feel comfortable in this place that didn’t quite fit Peru? What had his life been like before the great tourism and travel boom that so drastically influenced this country? And was he satisfied with the change? I didn’t stay long at this bar, I didn’t care much for the music and was still a bit wobbly on my feet. On the way back to the hostel, the memory of the old Peruvian's cologne had long faded. The scent doesn’t directly have anything alcoholic, but the well-crafted citrus makes me think of cocktails. Really nice for summer. And unlike most good scents from l'Artisan Parfumeur, this one is not yet discontinued. Sillage and longevity are not as low as described here on average; for the fragrance direction, it hits the average. Thank you for reading my comment.

Zesty, fresh, herbal, Mon Numéro 9 comes along and instantly brightens my mood. The freshness develops into a pleasantly woody note after a while, which, at least for me, is perceptible for at least 6 to 7 hours. Unobtrusive, natural, and friendly. An incredibly beautiful scent. For me, the best *blind buy* of this year, thanks to your review! Rose? I couldn't recognize it that way. But then again, I'm not a perfume specialist. :)

Nanshe is yet another Nishane that I don't fully understand. It is marketed as unisex, yet I feel it leans heavily feminine.
