And I've got my mother to back that up, this being the only perfume that she has ever complimented on me, and she only compliments perfumes that she would wear too. nulltheless, extra points for that. The opening of Nanshe is the only part of the fragrance I genuinely find interesting, with a pleasant but not overly-strong burst of citruses from the bergamot and yuzu. The cardamom immediately brings some warm spiciness to the play, as well as some subdued sweetness. The carrot seed, however, gives it that interesting edge. It brings an earthy sweetness with a warm and spicy undertone, but it is all kept at bay, so it's not very potent. The fragrance then smoothly progresses to its flowery heart, with ylang ylang being the most prominent to my nose - richly floral-sweet, hints of honey, custard, and even banana. Then there's the jasmine, with its iconic rich sweetness and musky undertone. As for the rose, I do not get much of it on its own. However, there is a certain floral freshness here, with a rather noticeable aquatic/watery edge. Of course, that's tied to the aquatic flowers note, from which I didn't expect much. But I must say that they add a rather nice touch, especially in tandem with the watery fruits, which further accentuate the watery accord, plus adding a faint fruity sweetness. Although listed as a base note, the powdery notes are detectable right as soon as the top notes start dissipating, which is like not even two minutes after spraying. It's a makeup-like powderiness, which is the key element to the feminine lean of the fragrance. The rest of the base is rather simple and soft, with a classic blend of musk and warm sandalwood. Can't really detect any patchouli, nor the iris on its own as expected, given the powdery notes. Longevity was significantly better than expected, although also a bit confusing. The most I got was about 7-8 hours, which is pretty good for a Nishane. However, other times it seemed I got like 4 hours at best, and I can't exactly tell if I was just going nose blind to it or if it was something else that made it fade away faster. Either way, I'm to blame - either my allergies got my nose stuffed and my olfactory receptors down along the wearing, or it was my sweat that washed away the fragrance off of my skin (what do you want me to do in 30+ Celsius?) I did get a better idea of its projection, thankfully. It's just decent for the first hour or so, projecting about a foot and a half. After two hours, it settles rather close to my skin, borderline skin scent. Sillage did prove to be a stronger point of Nanshe , though. It was after two hours on my first wearing that I got my mother complimenting it. But oh well, I guess a soft projection has its upsides too. And that's versatility. You won't be offending anyone with this one (unless you put on 10+ sprays), regardless if you are at work, at school, at the club, or at a wedding. But again, let me remind you that Nanshe leans feminine. And although I don't believe that it's completely unwearable for a man, it's definitely not something that I'd reach for. But nonetheless, do try it out; out of 188 users who own Nanshe here on Parfumo, 53% (about 100) of them are men. But for me personally, even though it smells nice, Nanshe won't be finding a place on my shelf. Powdery-floral fumes are just not my vibe, yet Nanshe still managed to get a 6.5/10 from me, so that says something. Also being the only fragrance that my mother has ever complimented on me says a lot (more specifically, a full bottle is demanded :D). Overall Rating: 6.3/10

For someone unisex, for me a purely feminine scent - the scent of purity, close to the scent of a woman's face, powder, make-up. It goes into the chypre style. There is a very fine powder and musk in the perfume. Inside the body of the perfume is a dark rose - complete, with leaves and stem. And cardamom and carrot seed are also running around. In the end, it all looks clean, like a freshly made-up lady who just came back from the bathroom with her make-up on. The perfume has great staying power and projection that goes the way I like it in gusts of air, in waves. Not every woman or confident man may like this fragrance, although I think it suits a woman better. But I think it is a very well made fragrance from the Turkish factory Nishane.

I started with a lot of expectation, as this perfume comes from the creator of Ani. But the different accord groups stay separate like oil and water in this perfume. In other words, the notes are not very well blended. For my nose, the yuzu and bergamot family of notes cannot be easily blended with rose, Jasmine and iris notes. It could have worked if the citrus was prominent in the opening, giving way to rose and floral in the middle or dry down. This development is what I like with Mefisto. However, Nanshe just bombs us with all the notes creating an olfactory confusion. Also, it muddles the personality of the perfume. It may work for someone else. But I am going to give this a hard pass. There are so many other perfumes before I would buy a bottle of Nanshe.

The opening was strong on spices as expected of Nishane, with a powerful wave of cardamom wrapped around a bouquet of feminine florals, especially rose. Lasting power was weaker than most Nishanes, but I liked the softer, powdery yet syrupy gentle rose scent that came out in the drydown. It smelled similar to a milky bandung drink for those who are familiar with Southeast Asia. Beautiful and feminine but I won’t purchase a full bottle as I think there are more suitable rose scents for me out there - I’d prefer more edge and spice and wetness.

I was overjoyed when I held the Discovery Set from Nishane in my hands for my birthday. I had wanted to try Ani and Woolong Cha for a long time and was also curious about all the other treasures. Because one (and only one) would be allowed to move in with me as a full bottle. Which one would it be? My heart was captured by Nanshe. It was my soul scent. Do you know that feeling? Most perfumes are like a pretty costume. With one, you feel a bit more feminine, another sparks activity. Yet another soothes or inspires. And then there are those that just don’t seem to fit you at all... Nanshe, on the other hand, belongs to those scents where I feel that I and the fragrance are one. Not forced. Just a second, more expressive version of myself... Nanshe reminds me of a fair-trade shop or an oriental knick-knack store. A bit dusty, the air heavy with the sweet scent of incense sticks. But not scratchy. More powdery soft. The dry down is super warm, sweet, and there’s something fruity in the air without acidity. At the beginning, it has a hint of overripe banana for a few minutes - I actually don’t like that very much - but that’s just a moment of 3-4 minutes. Then the fruity sweetness remains and wraps itself in this oriental woodiness. Powdery. Gentle. I’m not a fan of the bottle. It looks very bulky and I don’t like the color. I would have preferred gold, red, and orange instead of this beige... But I’m not going for a walk with the bottle; I’m just taking its wonderful contents for a stroll... My conclusion: Ani will probably have to move in with me as well, but this Nanshe had to be the first. And it’s also the only fragrance I’ve ever been approached about. However, I wouldn’t recommend it as a blind buy.

The Nanshe truly feels special and is not just a fragrance that you spray on and then forget. It stays in your memory, inspires, delights, and lifts my spirits, which is something I personally value highly in a perfume.

I really liked the "Nanshe | Nishane," as I found it to be very lovely, always unobtrusive but also beautifully crafted. The longevity on my skin is 10 to 12 hours. I would also describe the sillage as successful, especially since the scent picked up intensity again in today's heat, and I was positively approached about it even after hours.

In Sumerian mythology, Nanshe was the daughter of the earth and mother goddess and the god of freshwater. Nanshe's functions as a goddess were diverse: she was, among other things, the goddess of social justice, fertility, and clairvoyance. Her sacred animals were geese.

Nanshe is a challenging scent for me. It starts loud, with carrot seed, a bit of bergamot, yuzu, and cardamom providing a touch of freshness. It quickly becomes soapy clean and then transitions into a dusty, dry powder. It remains clean, but then the rose comes in, which is extremely piercing and unfortunately becomes more so as it develops.

Wow, that was love at the second sniff. The discovery set from Nishane has been with me for a while, How could I have overlooked it? Maybe because I usually don't like cute scents, I thought until now.... The fragrance pyramid wouldn't have appealed to me either, but once again I realize that the listed notes don't say much.

I'm in a garden in summer, the sun is shining down, everything around is green. I'm picking a pea pod straight from the plant, open it up, and it smells incredibly appetizing. That is how Iris de Gris starts: bright, refreshing and oh so natural, it makes me smile within seconds. Reminds me of the days I was little, and the best thing about going to my grandparents' garden was that pea veggie bed, where I could enjoy those young crisply green pea pods. Not long after, the iris appears. Not the thick, powdery kind, but the light and breezy, grass clippings scented whiff that reminds me of garden air. The world around you suddenly appears drenched in sunshine, the air is cooler and greener, everything feels ripe, juicy, and full of life. Well, it doesn’t last forever, projection is soft, and longevity is short. But I actually love that. It gives me the chance to spray it again during the day and get a refreshing dose of happiness. Another blast of garden breeze, another relief from the heat, another smile. This perfume makes me smile, brightens my day, and gives me an instant boost of energy every time I spray it on my skin. It was not love from the first sniff, but the sample ran out way too fast, and I ordered a full bottle, because I couldn't imaging summer without it anymore.

Iris de Gris is a shade of green fragrance unlike the others I’ve tried. I am not even particularly drawn to green fragrances but this one arrived as gift sample during a deep dive into iris fragrances and bewitched me. Crisp, fresh, gentle and persistent. We have a simultaneously crisp slightly watery galbanum-green pea accord with a soft iris-musk. Iris-musk is popular and not something I am particularly drawn to. The iris-musk here doesn’t skew too “laundry” which is often what happens to me. It seems mostly to support the green pea accord with some rooty—perhaps ever so slightly carrot-y qualities—and a lovely sheer freshness. In combination with a bright hint of citrus (mandarin?) and mint, the iris-musk in Iris de Gris strikes an evocative balance that I find wonderfully comforting and unique. I am a lover of green pea and this hits the mark for me. Though I never imagined I would want to wear it as a fragrance. The mint in here becomes more prominent after a while and makes me love the fragrance even more. A gentle fragrance with a joyful, life-affirming verdancy. Ideal for Spring and Summer. I love it after a shower or as a way to shift gears after a long day.

Tried a sample from the house, which u can purchase from l’artisan’s website (2 samples with delivery for 7,50€) The green peas pod is what i smell at the beginning. Is the peas “folder” :-) So you get this very green earthy smell and the iris contributes to this earthiness. It’s pleasant and surprisingly elegant, but still too green for my tastes. Just not my thing but a very interesting creative juice. Try it if you’re a frag nerd. The cardboard also says musks and vibrant woods.

IRIS DE GRIS is one of the five fragrances from the new “Le Potager” collection….. “Le Potager” means: The Vegetable Garden…… As the name suggests, the focus here is on a vegetable…….such as: Cauliflower Tomato Leaf Fennel Beetroot Pea In IRIS DE GRIS, it is the pea. Consequently, the fragrance starts with exactly this initial scent impression…..a crisp-fresh green pea, whose rich green and distinctive aroma are highlighted by a generous portion of galbanum. At the same time, a citrusy-minty freshness unfolds…....however, there are different reports regarding the citrus fruit used……L‘Artisan Parfumeur mentions blood orange, while other sources refer to bergamot….. My nose would lean more towards bergamot here, as I perceive the citrus note as slightly bitter….. Gradually, the “vegetable” scent impression weakens a bit and gives space for a completely unsweetened iris to unfold….. For my nose, IRIS DE GRIS only becomes a “real perfume” with the appearance of that iris…..it brings its own veil-like, softly powdery touch of elegance to the fragrance experience…….in the earlier stages, I would rather call it a “smell”…..pleasant, yes, but merely a “smell”….. Unfortunately, IRIS DE GRIS has also been “enhanced” with a minimal trace of Ambroxan, which I find particularly unpleasant…….however, the dosage is within a range that should not be noticeable to most who are not as sensitive to it as I am……so it is definitely NOT an Ambrox bomb…… All in all, IRIS DE GRIS is a thoroughly green fragrance with sprightly-fresh elements and an elegant, unsweetened veil of iris in the first 1-2 hours…..especially the latter is something I usually appreciate very much…… I perceive the aura of the fragrance as delicate and, starting from the heart note, minimally or very subtly powdery…… Those who dislike powdery scents need not worry about encountering a powdery fragrance here…..it is certainly not that……and it is not sweet either…..for that, it is initially far too green…. “I initially say” because IRIS DE GRIS becomes completely close to the skin after about two hours……..there is hardly anything left of the preceding scent notes…..no green, no pea, no citrus, and only a very minimal iris…..what remains is a pleasantly soft - albeit diffuse - scent veil that smells of nothing concrete anymore (similar to some molecular fragrances)….. Do I like this fragrance..? Well, it is quite appealing…..especially the beautiful unsweetened iris has captivated me……and I am generally quite open to green fragrances…… Do I need to have this fragrance…? No. On the one hand, because it loses its distinctive character quite quickly and drifts into the - only faintly perceivable - diffuse…………on the other hand, because I find it outrageous to incorporate the cheapest ingredients like Ambroxan in a $210 fragrance…….not to mention that I don’t like it ;-)…. PS: Samples of the 5 fragrances from the new LE POTAGER collection are available directly from L‘Artisan Parfumeur….

As far as tea fragrances go, I've never had any big expectations from them. It kind of goes without saying that such type of scents would turn out rather weak, inoffensive, and ultimately boring. Wūlóng Chá Extrait de Parfum , however, proved me wrong, showing me there's more to a tea-centric fragrance than meets the eye. And so, I came to Colognisé hoping I'd meet another soothing cup of tea. But all I got was a stale (albeit qualitative) cold cup. The opening feels like a generous squeeze of effervescent citruses in your cup of herbal green tea, with a realistic zesty lemon being the most prominent. The grapefruit adds a hint of tangy sweetness, while a clear sweet, floral jasmine starts to show. The green tea aroma is not as strong as I'd like, but it is definitely enough to be easily identifiable. Once the citruses settle down and the cup of tea starts getting cold, white florals take over, with the already mentioned jasmine being paired with a clean and slightly soapy lily of the valley. They both create a pleasing soft, delicate, floral freshness with remaining hints of citruses from the opening; hard to hate, but it's also not something to phone home about. The base brings some clean muskiness along with a lively neroli, adding more to the white floral structure, reminiscent of orange blossom with its orangey/citric attributes. The vetiver takes a very good while to show itself, and when it does, it doesn't take center stage. It adds a lightly grassy earthiness which is very inoffensive; seemingly made for people who can't stand vetiver. Overall, the only thing that saves Colognisé in my eyes is its raw material quality and blending. But as the scent itself, it feels very simplistic and a little stale, which is not necessarily a bad thing, as many people appreciate and prefer such compositions. With all that in mind, I expected performance to be terrible. And in terms of projection, it is one of, if not the softest Nishane I have yet tested. But as for longevity, that musk-neroli-vetiver base managed to push the scent to about 6-7 hours on my skin, instead of the 4-5 hours I expected. Projection did not take such a turn, and it proved to be pretty mild, with about a one foot bubble around me for the first 30-60 minutes, then turning more intimate and becoming a skin scent after about 3-4 hours. One good thing does come out of all of this - versatility. And unless you want to stick out and invade people's noses, Colognisé is really hard to fault. As wearable as it gets; wear whenever, wherever. Apart from someone who really appreciates softer, inoffensive, delicate tea scents or someone who can afford to get Colognisé as a gift for someone who's not really into fragrances (blind-buy safe), I don't see any other reason to get Colognisé . It's just your regular pleasant yet unimpressive fragrance. If you want a more distinct tea fume, then Wūlóng Chá Extrait de Parfum or maybe I-III Russian Tea are more worth considering. Sure, Wūlóng Chá Extrait de Parfum is significantly more expensive than Colognisé ($150 vs $250), but if you can't justify paying that much, then I don't think Colognisé offers any better value for money. Overall Rating: 5/10

Colognisé starts with a fresh whiff of green tea, a note I truly adore, accompanied by bright jasmine and uplifting zesty citruses. It's not something that has never been done before, but I did like the overall accord at the beginning and I wished it had stayed longer. After awhile, there's a powdery grapefruit that jumps in, turning the perfume into a fruity, clean and soapy scent. It stays light and fresh, but with an added tinge of green coming in from the white florals. The green accord becomes stronger on my skin as time passes while citruses fade away. I thought the dry down was going to be a warm and green floral scent, but unexpectedly, vetiver started to grow stronger. It became so strong that it crushed the floral note underneath it. The drydown became this solid block of green spiciness with a hint of citruses and the shadows of the florals that once were. If the beginning, with its freshness and white florals, leaned feminine (or unisex) to me, the drydown leans fully masculine, like a men’s spicy cologne. The bottom notes is the reason I won't be getting another bottle and will be trying to sell the one I have. Overall it's not bad, but for the price it ain't it. I was fortunate to get it during Boxing Day at 75$ off with an added discount of 15%. I find the sillage and longevity quite weak for something so expensive and I have other perfumes in my collection that have better performance than this one (and they don't lean as masculine).

This is lovely. I don’t think of it as a freshie, despite the citrus; to me it’s more of a pretty floral. There’s a sweet delicate jasmine and a little neroli in the drydown. I don’t really get much lily of the valley at all, but the base is nicely rounded out and warmed with some musk and vetiver. Really pretty and pleasant.

This was a relatively safe blind, as it's a genre I usually tend to like. Although it has all the hallmarks of a cologne, I would highlight the opening, which I think is the best part of this perfume, with a remarkable citrus harmony. This olfactory paradise only lasts a few minutes, however, and we soon enter a base that I would say has a more animal touch, probably due to a good dose of ambroxan in the composition. I would say that from a light, citrusy, floral and aromatic opening, we move to a more ambroxan base, which therefore lingers for a long time, but in this more animalic register. I've never had a negative reaction to it on my skin, although some people complain that it makes them sweat. I remember my sister saying that this perfume smelled like a father. It seems to me to be a fragrance to enjoy, especially on hot summer days.

If you like citrics, tea notes and green perfumes, I'm pretty sure you'll love Nishane Colognise. But careful, because there's another Colognise from Nishane that is saffron-centered and doesn't have the same peppy freshness or appeal like this one. Colognise is not a complicated scent, but it's awesome for summer. It tries to bring back the classic Turkish colognes that you would run into everywhere in Istanbul in the form of wet napkins at the baklava shops, small bottles of disinfectant which used to be free on buses, or those classic colognes you could buy in Turkish pharmacies. Maybe it sounds pretty ordinary, but for me this brings on nostalgia for summer vacations in Turkey. It reminds me of a more masculine version of Chanel's Cristalle Eau Verte, but as a woman I love wearing this, too. PS-I think the reviewers who are complaining of this as not being fresh or being too animalic are most likely writing about the other version of Colognise, the one with saffron. Pretty dumb marketing both these fragrances with the same name and bottle design. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Daca iti plac citricele, notele de ceai, si parfumurile verzi, sint mai mult ca sigura ca o sa te potrivesti cu Nishane Colognise. Dar mare atentie, ca este si o versiune cu note de safron care arata exact la fel, se numeste tot Colognise, dar nu are nici pe departe aceeasi prospetime sau atmosfera. Nu este un parfum foarte complicat: Colognise incearca sa recreeze clasicele colonii Turcesti care ti-se ofera peste tot in Istanbul in forme de servetele umede la cafenelele cu baklava, sticlute mici de dezinfectant de mana care erau gratuite pe autobuze, sau coloniile traditionale care se gaseau oriunde in farmaciile Turcesti. Suna cat se poate de obisnuit, dar pentru mine Colognise are nostalgia vacantelor de vara in Turcia. E proaspat, usor, curat si perfect pentru canicula. Pentru mine se aseamana cu un alt favorit, Chanel's Crystalle Eau Verte, dar Nishane are o persistenta mai buna si o latura un pic mai masculina, care este totusi abordabila si pentru femei.

Colognise is a wonderful fragrance from Nishane, a simple citrus and white-floral scent that is worth every penny. I got a full bottle from US grey market seller for $69, after testing it using a discovery set. In my humble opinion, it is an undervalued perfume. Nishane has not disclosed the nose behind this perfume.

On paper: bitter. On the skin: an intense citrus note of bergamot and lemon or candied lemon with a very dense texture. At the heart, the zesty citrus note sits firmly in the saddle with a touch of floral sweetness above and, of course, vital freshness.

In summer temperatures, I truly enjoy Colognisé in my daily life. On my skin, the scent is still subtly noticeable after about 12 hours, even though it noticeably diminishes after 6 hours - but for a cologne, that's absolutely fine.

Central white flowers, light citrus in the opening and more woods and vetiver towards the end. Simple but well made. More masculine than unisex and a bit old-school, but not too outdated for me. It has a calming, down-to-earth quality for me. I like to wear it when I actually don't want to wear a fragrance, or strangely enough when I go to bed.

I love the scent of Nishane Köln because it is so simple. In summer, I often just want a fragrance that smells pleasant and doesn't overwhelm the entire room. That's exactly what you get here. A light, zesty citrus scent that immediately gives you the refreshing feeling of summer. However, the longevity is relatively short.

My mom has this and on her it smells exactly like TF Eau de Soleil Blanc, it's so sparkly and bright, the mimosa is really noticeable to me. It's sunscreen-y but not in a bad way, it's like an energizing bright sunscreen. Can't speak on the longevity as it's my mom's perfume but at least on her I can always tell when she's wearing it. Very classy, elevated and elegant lady at the beach vibes. Sure, you can find this profile for cheaper, but this does feel like a more expensive-smelling alternative to a sunscreen scent.

There's not anything wrong with this fragrance except the fact that it borders too much on the functional aspect of sunscreen to me. Other than that, this one is gentle, discrete and lovely (if it wasn't for the sunscreen vibe I get). Lemon and bergamot give it a sweet, fruity vibe while ylang-ylang becomes the star on my skin. It's a carnal flower, well-rounded, a bit thick, tropical and ever so fruity. This is probably the main culprit for the sunscreen vibe. Mimosa adds a bit of sweetness to everything while benzoin gives it warmth and deepness. Vanilla appears at the end, imparting the distinct sweetness we've all come to love with vanilla notes. At times it does smell like lemon and cream and at other moments, the scent shifts towards this tropical fruity sunscreen. It's a pleasant fragrance, one that can be worn during summer for that extra warm, your-skin-but-better vibe. It,s pretty linear and lacks a bit of that oomph I'm searching for which is why it won't be added to my collection. nulltheless, L'Artisan Parfumeur has created a good niche perfume that steers more towards the mainstream crowd. A nice crowd pleaser.

I just received the sample and i’m testing it right now on my hand. This is really beautiful, very rounded and creamy, upon first spray it reminds me of Soleil Blanc by Tom Ford, with lemon and mimosa added. Seems like it has tuberose, but it might be the ylang ylang that gives that creamy summer vibe. The mimosa is starting to appear after some minutes and makes it more yellow. Very very good one, i feel like it leans a bit more feminine but nothing that i wouldn’t wear. It’s solar, bright, feel good vibe and very refined, makes me miss the sunny seasons. Will try more in the upcoming months.

Thanks to a nice swap with the lovely Jessica/Stinkekatze, I got to test this amazing fragrance. What an incredible stroke of luck for me! The scent is simply a 10/10! At first, it’s pure citrus, but over time it becomes creamier. Even after six hours, I could still perceive it well on my skin (albeit closer to the skin now). The sillage is also convincing. Not a beast, but you will definitely be noticed as you pass by. In short, it’s a fantastic lemon cream fragrance that sweetens your day for 6-7 hours.

Histoire d'Orangers is arguably a rather simplistic fragrance: a breeze of fresh neroli soon lifted by a fluffy, inky white musk, while ambroxan extends the fragrance further into the dry down. However, there are enough nuances to keep it pretty and natural-smelling. The neroli in the opening is fresh and transparent, with just enough green bitterness to evoke the natural feeling, and nothing sharp or soapy at all. A delicate honey casts golden shimmers to the neroli, just enough to add a touch of sensuality and suavity, and nothing sticky or cotton candy-like, either. The musk is clean and slightly inky, luckily without any connotation of sharp laundry powder to me. Its fluffy texture complements the feathery neroli perfectly, and lends an expansive sensation. The scent as a whole, is like an ethereal white cloud of neroli and musk, shined upon by the golden sunlight of honey. These first 3 hours are my favourite part of Histoire d'Orangers. Afterwards, ambroxan becomes more and more apparent, and eventually dominates the perfume and pushes the neroli to the edges. I usually perceive ambroxan as slightly salty, but mostly musky sweet with a vegetal/mineral nuance. Here, the vegetal facet does link with the neroli nicely at times. But once the ambroxan completely takes over, it's just ambroxan and nothing else, which eventually bores me in the end. Histoire d'Orangers rather whispers its story close to the skin, and lasts at least 7 hours thanks to the extensive dry down of ambroxan. Like many L'Artisan offerings, Histoire d'Orangers is very easy to appreciate and have a certain natural feeling in the opening. As an orange blossom fragrance, it's clean and fresh, but not as bitter herbal green as traditional cologne; it's fluffy and honeyed, but not as sweet as cotton candy or too indolic. It embodies the innocent nature of orange blossom perfectly. However, its overall simplicity and its extensive use of ambroxan may not jibe with everyone. I would mostly recommend it to those who happen to seek for a soft, non soapy neroli fragrance.

L'Artisan Histoire d'Orangers is the very gothest orange blossom. If you could distill all the words in every language for "melancholia," capture the essence of a flick of heavy black eyeliner, or bottle the resonance of a sorrowful minor chord, that would sum up this perfume. It's the poetry of abandoned orange groves at twilight, their spectral blossoms an incense of Saudade, Sehnsucht, of Mono no aware. For those moments when you long to wrap yourself in a tremulous sublimity of sadness, to revel in the exquisite pain of being achingly alive in a world that's always slipping away. I'm aware this is the biggest, corniest cliche you've ever heard, but as a Florida goth awash in perpetual summertime glooms, I don't know what else to tell you.

I've smelled my fair share of neroli and orange blossom fragrances. Fruity, sweet, fresh, green, citrusy, I think I've gone through most of 'em (in broad categories). I didn't really have any expectations going for this one, but I was interested to see how white tea and tonka would play out. The fragrance is fine, but what sticks out the most to me is its abyssmal performance. It's a skin scent after 15 minutes and, even then, I'm being very generous. Might be a skin chemistry problem. As for the fragrance, the opening is beautiful. Delicate, light, fresh and citrusy. White tea gives the opening an ethereal, soothing and almost calming aspect. Wish it had lasted longer on my skin. After a few minutes I get a warm, slightly spicy accord (helvetolide maybe?) with a fresh, floral orange blossom. It finally morphs into a powdery, almost body lotion vibe with a warm and synthetic accord. Like I said, it's fine. It doesn't have stellar performance and it's relatively safe for a blind-buy. The only thing is: do I wanna pay that high of a price when better alternatives exist? I don't think so. The rest is up to you, but it won't be making it in my collection.

This is an instant CLASSIC. The best orange flower in my opinion, such a classy, refined, soapy musky clean perfume. Longevity and projection are huge, when the bottle arrived and first days not that much, but as usually happens with L’Artisan, they grow and grow week after week since u spray them for the first time, like they begin to get more dense and rich... you smell like a 5 star spa soap, such a mouthwatering orange blossom and musk. This projects very very well and lasts a lot on the skin! Wonderful, wonderful, wonderful, 10/10

If you love the smell of orange blossoms and want to feel like you're walking through a grove of flowering orange trees, then look no further. A lovely, soft scent dominated by orange blossoms with hints of sweetness and a bit of musty and green notes. The neroli and ambrox give good balance to the otherwise fresh, floral, and citrusy smell. There isn't a ton of evolution here, at least for me, but I think my skin isn't the best suited to this fragrance (my skin tends to dry out most smells). Projects close to skin after the first hour, but lasts as a delicate, intimate aroma for 5-6 hours. A straightforward, orange blossom dominated fragrance with some subtlety giving it impressive lasting power for generally delicate notes.

Hello everyone, I'm back! Are you happy to see me? To be honest, I’d rather not know your answer :D Anyway, today we’re talking about the fragrance “Histoire d‘Orangers” by L‘Artisan, and as you might already guess from the name, the scent means “The Story of Orange Trees.

In search of a refreshing yet softly cushioned summer fragrance - or let's say: an affordable alternative to the unmatched Bigarade concentree - I now have HISTOIRE D'ORANGERS on my skin. It became clear very quickly: This is not going to work for us.

Pachuli Kozha (Patchouli Leather) opens with noticeable chamomile along with a green/herby accord which I assume is the mugwort. Didn't get any florals. As it dried down, a musty, blended woody accord appeared. The scent didn't strike me as a strong patchouli but more of a blended combo of patchouli, leather, incense and honey. When I smelled it, it immediately recalled a specific incident from a couple of years ago. At that time, I volunteered along with a friend to help a church remove their old pipe organ which needed repair. I think it was about 70 years old. Anyway, the wooden boxed airways on which the pipes stood and the pipes which were made of wood all smelled like Pachuli Kozha. Weird, eh? It's not an unpleasant scent - sorta like musty dusty varnished wood, but not something I want to smell like. Masculine fragrance. Performance is a beast with very good longevity and projection, but not for me.

Beautiful patchouli (not herthy patchouli, but a boozy patchouli) with floreal accord and a touch of incense leather balanced by honey notes. The note of chamomile and ylang ylang are also perceptible, when opened it almost seems to be boozy. Very persistent perfume, it has an excellent sillage and unrivaled quality/price. Highly recommended

The fragrance in my opinion is one of the best of this perfumery. When it comes to uniqueness, quality and projection, next to Ania, Spice Bazaar, Sultan Vetiver and African Olifant - the best. To me it smells like darker patchouli combined with sooty incense leather and doused with balsamic honey. A very interesting and unique combination of fragrances in such a way that it is a warm, spicy, incense, and at the same time slightly sweet fragrance. The scent has a large projection and the vitality is a real monster. I highly RECOMMEND, at least MUST TRY. Oh ... translated from Bulgarian and Turkish nomads - KOZHA is leather ;-)

oh my..! what a beautiful patchouli. A crazy balance of notes that often crash one with the others. Honey: check. herbal notes: check. spices as well.. I can also smell a beautiful never heavy leathery scent. After 15 minutes, an amazing incense comes up. Personally speaking, I would have preferred an extra hint of flowers, but it is really well structured. It is so pleasant to smell the skin with this perfume on. It gives calm and peace sensations, despite the aggressive feature of each note! Maybe a bit masculine leaning, but it is wearable by women too (same sensations as for Patchouli Ardent .) Super approved nishane!

After a long consideration, I have finally decided to write a comment about this extraordinary fragrance. It found its way to me through a roundabout route. A perfumer discovered it for herself and raved to me about this "Oh-my-God-Patchouli scent." She sent me a small sample and I was immediately smitten. However, after my research, the price made me forget about this fragrance a bit. But what was that??? Suddenly, it was offered in the souk by that very same perfumer. I could hardly believe it. What happened??? Of course, I immediately contacted her and she revealed to me that SHE still finds it wonderful, but her husband is running away from it. Well, .. the decision fell in favor of the husband. And I got to enjoy having Pachuli Kozha as my own soon. I was overjoyed!!!!! What can I say? Love it or hate it..... After three days, it finally arrived! Upon opening the package, I was also thrilled by this beautiful box that contained the fragrance. Black and elegant! It’s almost a little ceremony to open this to get to the scent. Immediately after the first spray, earthy patchouli greets me. Quite a bit of incense joins it right away. Chamomile? Not for me. Instead, honey of the finest quality. It makes this scent very wearable for me. After about half an hour, leather comes into my perception. My nose is glued to my arm. It comes across now much much much much better than I remembered from the sample. OMG!!!!! And it is now mine!!!! If you don’t have tolerant colleagues, you should probably avoid wearing it in the office. Mine have gotten used to my perfume passion and are quite tough about it. Whether I will wear it in the height of summer, I doubt.... or will I????????????? And almost forgotten: The longevity is exceptionally good!!!! This delicious scent accompanies me all day.

Similar to animalic nuances; Patchouli is certainly not for everyone. And when both come together, it really makes a noise... I have always found Patchouli in all its possible gradations to be fantastic - apart from the Patchouli scent that one slathered on in liters on their poncho or band hoodie when they were fully grunge.

Patchouli is certainly not to everyone's taste - mostly somehow earthy, strangely woody-herbaceous and yet also somewhat balsamic-sweet, it often reminds me of wet earth in a wonderfully fragrant forest.

The Pachulí Kozha by Nishane is a special fragrance; yes, special because its focus is so extremely on patchouli; not exactly surprising when you read the name of the scent. I actually like patchouli when it is well and subtly crafted.

Many thanks to Niklas for the many Nishane samples :-) Unfortunately, Pachulí Kozha is really not my thing. Even at work, I didn't receive any compliments for it; my best friend even said: "It smells really cheap oriental." He was a bit shocked when I told him how much this perfume normally costs.

Earthy-woody patchouli powerhouse with a sweet honey/resin finish at a solid lover's price. After yesterday's Papilefiko disappointment, today brings a glimmer of hope on the horizon and what a strong start it has ... (!) ;-) Immediately after spraying, a real patchouli-chamomile punch hits you.

This is a beautifully dark, incense-y rose with spices, dry woods, and a hint of smoke. Many comparisons have been made between this and Le Labo’s Rose 31 and they’re indeed similar. Arcana Rosa is a more polished alternative, with the woods here (more sandalwood than cedar) being less screechy, the vetiver less scratchy, and overall has a more velvety feel.

She is a somewhat aging former beauty. In her youth, she also modeled and competed with Twiggy, after all, they were born in the same year (1949). But Twiggy was more of a photographic model, while our pug lady (let's call her Suzette) strutted down the catwalk in Paris. All of this was eons ago. She has been widowed for a long time. Her late husband was a big shot, which also explains her well-off circumstances. She has 2 daughters, whom she claims look like Brigitte Bardot and Romy Schneider. The latter has been six feet under for quite some time now, and I believe she wouldn't be very pleased with that comparison. Her loyal companion is the aforementioned pug named Merguez (Sausage), and the dog cannot deny a certain resemblance. I myself am not necessarily a fan of pugs. I mean the dogs, dear readers. But they can't help it. Our Suzette regularly meets with 3 friends at a café near the Eiffel Tower. All the same age, all with their dogs. There’s Nadine with her miniature pinscher, Adele with an indefinable creature that always clings to her handbag, and Claudette - lanky and tall - with her Saluki (sighthound, 70 cm shoulder height) who often races with her and usually wins, Claudette. Today there’s yet another discussion about Suzette's fondness for perfume and her almost fanatical love for roses. Nadine: “Say, Suzette, have you marinated all your underwear in rose water again?” Suzette: “No, that’s my new perfume!” She waves her arms, fans herself with her little Chanel blouse, and jingles her pearl necklace. Clouds of Arcana drift across the table. Adele: “It smells like the perfumer distilled the stems and thorns too. You do know that real pearls and perfume don’t mix, right?” Claudette, always very sarcastic: “Yes, and he probably had a wooden leg and a toupee that he glued on with resin.” Suzette pouts. She is in rose heaven. They have no idea, those old bags, especially Nadine, that matron. She recently dropped her clingy rat into the crème brûlée. Offended, she flounces away, trailing a flag of spiced roses behind her. For rose fans, this is certainly a treat. It scents every room, as the sillage and longevity are remarkable, or you can feel like Sleeping Beauty.

Floral Morning Dream body mist is just okay for me. I usually prefer fruity florals, but this one leans more towards a pure, classic floral scent. However, on a cloudy morning when I want to feel like I'm in a jungle flower garden, it works. It's not that I dislike it, but it's not something I reach for often from my wardrobe. The floral scent is quite green and very mild, with poor sillage. To improve it, I've combined it with Nykaa's Wanderlust Himalayan Hemp body lotion, which made it better. If you enjoy a strong jasmine scent, you might want to pair it with Nykaa's Hawaiian Jasmine body lotion. Personally, I find pure jasmine fragrances to be headache-inducing, so I avoid them. Overall, Floral Morning Dream is fine for occasional floral moods, especially if you like green florals. For a detailed review, you can check my YouTube video on Floral Morning Dream

As I said in the title, this tuberose fragrance is not for the fain of heart. If you don't like the note don't even think about it, but if you do, oh my God! It is beautiful. It starts with a beautiful sweet orange combined with the freshness of the orange blossom. It is divine! This formulation is thick, like there is substance to it. It must be the amber combined with the vetiver in the base. The sandalwood keeps the formulation creamy and it goes hand in hand with the white flowers. Tuberose is my favorite note on my girlfriend. It is so beautiful and pure. I feel that Tuberoza is a more feminine fragrance but a man can pull it of if used in the right situation and environment. Longevity and projection are above average 12+ hours. The most potent tuberose I have ever smelt. Great value for the money!

To me, Tuberóza Extrait de Parfum seems like the epitome of a white floral fragrance. And although admittedly, I'm not the biggest fan of white florals, Tuberóza Extrait de Parfum is one of the few of such blends that I can appreciate, but can hardly wear, as it leans in too feminine for me (as with most other white floral scents). nulltheless, what does it smell like? Well, immediately upon spraying, it is made clear what direction this fragrance takes. An intensive dose of a soapy, slightly citrusy orange blossom, mixed with the forever complex ylang ylang - floral, balsamic, sweet - creates an intoxicating opening very reminiscent of banana, which lingers throughout most of the wearing. If you try hard enough, you might also pick the mugwort hidden in the background with its touch of green, minty, aromatic accords. Once at the heart, we receive the bouquet, composed of jasmine, gardenia, Mexican tuberose, and tagetes. The unmistakable floral sweetness of the jasmine, the Mexican Tuberose that accentuates the intense floral aura, the gardenia and its zesty floral scent with a hint of greenness, and the tagetes with a fresher floral burst - all blended in a intensely rich, creamy, fragrant odor that makes it so difficult to tell each apart. As things gently dry down, some powdery muskiness pushes through, hardly strong enough to stick out in the white floral field that we find ourselves into. Then, a smooth, slightly sweet warmth with the faintest woody backbone shows up, along with a touch of balsamic softness. These are the sandalwood and amberwood notes at the base, which frankly, are quite subtle, being easily overpowered by the overall floral composition. As for vetiver, I barely get any; most notes after the opening are quite the challenge to pinpoint on their own. Nevertheless, if it wasn't clear by now, anyone with a white floral affair will most likely adore Tuberóza Extrait de Parfum . The quality is pretty great, with a smooth blending. However, a little linear. It's most definitely a feminine-leaning scent, but I think that men can also get away with it rather easily (not me, though). And here's why: its soft projection and short-lived lastingness. On my skin, Tuberóza Extrait de Parfum turned from a lively, intensely fragrant bouquet of dozens of white flowers to a single stem with few petals left dangling by the 4 hour mark. Many others seem to find Tuberóza Extrait de Parfum as quite long-lasting around here, but it's just not the same for me, even after numerous try-outs. And projection is also hardly impressive, although not exactly inappropriate. I don't know about you, but I find overpowering floral fragrances that you can sense on someone from 5 feet away simply nauseating and headache-inducing. And so, given the strong emphasis on the floral accords here, a softer, more intimate projection seems the better fit. And on me, I got about 1 foot at best for the first half an hour or so, after which it would rapidly settle to a less-than-half-a-foot bubble around me. So indeed, you cannot call this good projection in any universe, but I'd argue that it's quite fitting. It's like it invites you to discover this beautiful bouquet from up close. In terms of occasions, I feel that Tuberóza Extrait de Parfum would make a solid case for itself in pretty much any context. Work, school, dressed-up events, dates... and any other place where you'd want a pleasant, but subtle floral scent. Definitely not clubbing or partying, as not only it might be too soft for those seeking to grab attention, but it is also not the type of fragrance that fits those messy, loud contexts. This is intensely floral, yet still delicate and sophisticated, and it should be worn as such. But in the end, I can't get myself to give it any more than a 7.5/10 in terms of scent, simply because I'm just not the biggest white florals enjoyer. That doesn't mean I hate it. On the contrary, I'd enjoy an ever so dim whiff of this composition in the air, but just not coming off my skin. It doesn't fit my style, aside from also leaning in heavily feminine, and so I don't really enjoy wearing it. But if you find it the other way around for yourself, and you can justify its steep price tag, then I suppose you should grab onto this bouquet. Overall Rating: 5.7/10

One of the most seductive flowers of all is undoubtedly the Tuberose. Of the legends surrounding this flower, think of it, native to Mexico and belonging to the agave family, which amplifies its narcotic scent at night, I have already spoken amply, but I can easily say that the one in this fragrance is absolutely the most carnal and overwhelming one I have smelled. It is a flower that makes its scent felt from afar, like this perfume, which is so intense, and which I consider unfailing in the collection of lovers of this note so precious in perfumery. I, for those who have realised it, prefer it in other interpretations, less provocative and more green, but I can't help but consider it one of the best tuberose creations there can ever be. Of a shameless sensuality, excessive, but incredibly beautiful, magnetic, just like Marilyn Monroe, whom I cannot fail to mention in Andy Warhol's iconic portrait.

This review is for a sample of Tuberoza that I received as part of the Nishani discovery set. This discovery set it a mixed bag of perfumes with very different tastes and personalities. It is perhaps worth ordering individual samples of the perfumes you are interested in. Tuberoza is one of two tuberose scents in the Nishani discovery set, the other being Hundred Silent Ways. Tuberoza is a cleaner tuberose like Givenchy’s Desinvolte or L’Interdit, presenting itself as a tuberose-dominant white floral. This is the key distinction from Carnal Flower, which is a green perfume with tuberose notes, albeit a very lovely perfume. As its name implies, tuberose is present all times in the olfactory pyramid in Tuberoza. The opening notes ylang-ylang and citrus add a greenish personality, though barely lasting an hour. I confess that I cannot distinguish all the notes listed in the opening notes. The orange note in the opening is beautiful, but also very fleeting. The heart notes - tuberose and jasmine mostly - take over completely after the first few minutes. These notes endure for 8-10 hours before disappearing. The base notes and the dry down that remains are vague - mild sandalwood and musk - more like a skin scent. The performance is very good with moderate sillage and a longevity of more than 8 hours on skin. On clothes it lasts longer and continue to smell like the heart notes. So, I would recommend one spray on your clothes as well. In summary, it is a good perfume if you are a tuberose enthusiast. You can get 50 ml for about $100, though I would prefer it to be around $75 or less. Similar to my opinion on Carnal Flower, I would hesitate buying Tuberoza if you have another good tuberose perfume in your collection. Carnal Flower is a better tuberose in my opinion, if you don’t mind the opening green notes.

I like this a lot! One of my favourites from the Nishane sampler set I received. It has a beautiful opening, floral with some mild citrus. It smells vintage 1980s to me, but without being dated. It was still lovely over an hour later. I'm trying to figure out if it was the ylang ylang that I liked so much from this.

This fragrance isn't much of anything. Its not memorable, unique, or even worthy of hate. It just exists and does the bare minimum. It is a heavy white floral with some citrus in the beginning and that is about it. You pick up some of the wood during the dry down but even then the white floral is the strongest note.

Many thanks to Niklas for the original manufacturer sample of Tuberóza Extrait de Parfum :-) This is a truly wonderful fragrance that I would associate much more with women. It is so sweet and delightful. The longevity is quite good at around 10 hours, and the sillage is nothing to hide from.

Most people say that the scent is a pure women's fragrance, which I understand but still have to say no to. I received this fragrance in a mystery box and was initially disappointed because the scent notes didn't appeal to me, and it is marketed for women, rarely seen on men. However, I must say that I fell in love with the scent immediately upon the first spray.

This is undoubtedly a JPG Le Male clone. It is impressively close to the original. If I had to quibble, I would say that the opening is a little bit less complex, with less mint than the original. It also seams more linear, with a drydown that can be a bit cloying at times. But my sense is that most people would not be able to tell the difference.

Then I will dare to write my first review; until now, I was just a diligent reader, but now I want to contribute a little to this wonderful site! My first review, however, will not revolve around a scent that everyone knows, but rather the lesser-known "Zara Sport 675". First, one should be aware of what to expect for the price; sillage and projection are, of course, hardly comparable to the well-known high-quality fragrances that, of course, also cost many times more. In my opinion, this is a super nice scent that, at least at the beginning, clearly reminds one of Le Male; this fragrance could thus represent a serious alternative for many (young) people! When I was younger (at 21, I still am), around 16, I only owned 2-3 great fragrances that made it to me over Christmas, so I used them very sparingly, but soon one feels not quite "complete" without a accompanying scent; this fragrance is perfect for that! The term "sport" should not be given too much significance here; in my opinion, the scent takes a much more oriental path rather than an aquatic, citrusy one, as one might expect! So if you plan to shop at Zara in the near future, give it a try and form your own opinion about the scent. Let me summarize: - affordable Le Male clone in the top note - good "everyday scent" - limited in scent volume and possible transformations - together with "Zara Night," my favorite fragrance from their range

To me this is a minimalistic masterpiece by Giacobetti. It is a very linear trip between the opening of a mandarine - the ripe- to the heart of a mandarine - the juice - Very last units left. I would strongly recommend you to get your own. Sillage and longevity is almost non existing. The scent lasts the time it takes to eat a mandarine. Full circle.

Mandarine is a vibrant and refreshing scent that captures the essence of the mandarin fruit. L'Artisan Parfumeur's original description of Mandarine provides the most fitting summary of the fragrance's inspiration. “The challenge for perfumer Olivia Giacobetti was to explore this fruit as it ripens, extracting from it three essences at different stages of maturity… green, yellow and ripe, Mandarine is strikingly tangy, zesty and sweet.” The opening notes burst with a photorealistic tangy, fruity aroma, evoking the sensation of peeling a fresh mandarin. As the fragrance settles, a natural sweetness emerges, balanced by a subtle spicy warmth from ginger. Late into the drydown, Mandarine lingers on the skin with a soft, smooth cedarwood and only a hint of citrus, like the scent left on your hands after peeling the fruit itself. Mandarine is an uplifting and joyful unisex scent, bringing warmth and energy to any day, whether it's a sunny summer afternoon or a cold winter morning.

Ah, I love mandarins. But not because they are healthy (yes, yes, always eat some fruit) or because they keep my cat away from me, but because they taste good and smell particularly nice in perfumes. Here too, in the scent from L’Artisan, they smell great and above all natural, unfortunately, the scent hardly lasts... The scent: The scent doesn’t start off very citrusy with a still green and slightly unripe mandarin, which seems to have been stored with spices instead of in the fruit bowl, as there is a slight spicy note detectable, that of ginger. The good thing is that everything smells very natural and therefore real. In the heart note, there is indeed a very light floral note discernible, however, a slightly sweeter mandarin is again the main note here. The spicy ginger from the top note seems to become a bit stronger as well, although it weakens a little in the base. In the base, not much changes. Although orange is listed in the fragrance pyramid, it is weakly present and the scent blends with that of the mandarin, as the mandarin no longer smells sweeter or more pronounced, making them hardly distinguishable from each other. In the background, there is cedarwood present, but that’s about it. The longevity and sillage: The longevity is about as long as the time it takes to peel and eat a mandarin. Well, let’s say... three mandarins... but no more! There is hardly any sillage, so the scent becomes practically skin-close immediately after spraying. The bottle: The bottle is, as always, the typical seven-sided little flask with the narrow label on which the name of the scent is printed. It comes with a golden, also seven-sided cap. Everything is done really well as always. So, I had to test this scent because I really like mandarins as a fragrance note. Therefore, I was even more disappointed because this scent has almost no sillage to offer. Sure, the scent is nice, even quite beautiful (even though I felt that the spicy notes occasionally overshadow the mandarins), but it dissipates so quickly that you would actually be busy re-spraying the scent the whole time until the bottle is empty. And that, especially with a brand like L’Artisan, which generally costs a bit more than other fragrances, is very unfortunate, so in my opinion, the purchase is hardly worth it, unless you are a hardcore mandarin fan and have no problem re-spraying the scent every half hour. I find that your fingers smell longer of this fruit after you have peeled it (and sometimes you have orange fingernails afterward, yuck...). This scent is therefore unfortunately not suitable for going out. However, I find it nice that the mandarin can be smelled as a whole, at least that’s how I felt. What I mean is that you can smell not only the flesh of the fruit but also the slightly bitter peel as well as the leaves a bit. You can take a look at the scent; I would still recommend the scent from Hermès (Eau de Mandarine Ambrée). Even though that from Hermès is also not particularly strong, it still gives (in my opinion) an unmatched beautiful mandarin scent for at least two hours. But I am always open to further tips, especially mandarin unisex fragrances!

or: Baking Butter Cookies with Mom (Cookies = Biscuits) ;) This is a delightful little fragrance! It really smells just like when my mother grates orange peel into the fresh dough for butter cookies during the Advent season, and thankfully, she still does it. That's why I simply have to love this scent! Or ... here comes another image ... butter cookies lying together with mandarins on a treat plate ... *melting away* I really don't need to say much more about "Mandarine" - except: This delicacy is definitely something for brave men as well. Unfortunately, it disappears almost as quickly as the delicious cookies.

It's a shame somehow, especially for me! Today, on Monday 21/06/2021, I used the last sprays from the bottle. In these summery high temperatures of recent years, this Eau de Toilette was an excellent refreshing option. Maybe it had a flaw regarding longevity on my skin, but that might be due to my skin type. The fact was, after about 40 minutes, the scent was practically no longer present on me. No matter, I just reapplied it from time to time! On the positive side, the reactions from people who noticed this EdT in close proximity were generally very good. “Oh, what a wonderful scent you have!” was the often-expressed reaction. It didn't matter whether in the elevator, on the plane, in the train, or tram, etc. It makes me even sadder that I can no longer repurchase this special EdT because, after the sale of this French perfume brand to the Spanish perfume and fashion giant PUIG, the major assortment cleanup began. This also included the discontinuation of “Mandarine.” Until now, I had no opportunity to test a fragrance from the “Histoire d'Orangers” line. But orange is not mandarin! But … well, time will bring me something new!

One of the most peculiar scent I've ever smell. Not in a bad way, it's just very surprising for a VS mist. It's caramel-y in a weird, non sweet way, almost smells like molasses. It's a heavy, seductive scent that opens with a liquory cherry, not at all what I was expecting, a true, cherry, not the syrupy, overly sweet and artificial one. it's a black, juicy and ripe cherry dipped in rhum. It's a mature cherry. Sometimes when it comes to cherry perfumes, we expect a very young, borderline "coquette" adaptation of the fruit. Not in this one. After that it settles in a scent that reminisces me of marzipan, there's something quite almond in the dry down. The cherry almosy disapears, and it's juste that mix of molasses and marzipan that lasts quite a bit on the skin. But don't be fooled, it doesn't project much, and it doesn't last too long. It just kinda settles in a skin scent after one hour. A bit disapointed there. Edit: I know what it reminds me of: The well known liquor cherries coated in chocolate from Mon Chéri. It's a photorealistic Mon Chéri scent. I can even smell the chocolate. I hate those with a passion, but the smell itself is divine.

I've never smelled Tuscan Leather, so can't compare. Suede et Safran opened for me with a big burst of leather, even though it's not a top note. It then evolved within seconds with the leather pulling back and a green accord popping up followed by a somewhat sweet floral accord which I assume was the ambrette. Really kinda amazing how the scent evolved within about 15 seconds. Finally, the sweetness pulled back somewhat and everything started to settle down into a dry, suede type scent with the saffron. I didn't get any ginger. Longevity was very good while the projection was more average. Overall, didn't really care for it. Seemed kinda flat; not much there.

We are in Morocco, in Marrakech, a city where a highly prized type of leather is produced: the Moroccan. With this postcard Suede et Safran, "suede and saffron," wants to pay tribute precisely to the artisans who create this uniqueness. Leather and saffron is one of the accords I most appreciate in artistic perfumery: the roughness and toughness of leather is blended with saffron from Iran, which softens it almost to the point of mellowing. Ginger and ambrette seeds, finally, contribute a spicy hint to the composition and make it very elegant and perfectly wearable.

Composition that basically the smell is suede and saffron, all accompanied by ginger and musk. Taking advantage of the fact that it is a bit cold today, I dress with her. If you find an offer and you like leather fragrances, don't hesitate. Uniqueness: 6/10 Scent: 7/10 Performance: 7/10 ♂️▫️▫️◾▫️▫️♀️

Suède et Safran is one of those fragrances that feels instantly familiar to me, or at least to me in this composition. Nevertheless, I had to ponder for a long time and even use the search function regarding the two main players, leather and saffron. There is certainly plenty of that, and eventually, I figured it out. But I want to keep the suspense a little longer and reveal the scent ... or rather the scent family members later. What struck me about Suède et Safran is, alongside this somewhat overly softened leather interpretation and the very subdued saffron, this sneaky fruity note, which is not listed but can exhibit something berry-like. Or is it perhaps a woody peach note or peach wood? No, more likely blackcurrant if not even raspberry. And at the latest here, some might start to connect the dots, as the similarity to Tuscan Leather by Tom Ford is undeniable (unless my sample is contaminated with something else). However, the aforementioned Tuscan Leather is simultaneously rougher in leather and, I believe, more recognizable in saffron, and it has that smooth raspberry note as a cultivated counterpoint, while Suède et Safran flirts with the edge of being artificial and slightly penetrating. Well, the scent is harmoniously crafted, but at the same time very linear, making it a candidate that could become annoying over time, especially since the longevity goes to extremes. And when I see what prices Nishane is asking ... everyone can think for themselves. On the other hand, I wonder what Suède et Safran would have become if there had really been more (the promised) ginger taking the lead.

For all leather scent lovers or those who have not yet dared to try leather fragrances, this Nishane is highly recommended: Soft, understated but present in terms of the leather impression, beautifully intertwined with saffron notes and warm spiciness. Prolet or Rocker Girl vibes? Never! In this form, the Nishane scent is even sexy, suitable for everyday wear - even in the office and among people who will appreciate its strikingly noble character. It comes across as soft, spicy, slightly fruity, and wonderfully creamy. In some way, it is also sensual. Of course, it consistently smells of pleasant, light leather. A creamy leather mixture that flatters the nose. The longevity is good, as is the projection and sillage - although a noble restraint seems to be integrated into its DNA, which is somehow fascinating. The certain kick is included, not just for men, but also for women. Ergo: Leather kick with a statement. I mean: Beautiful!

Nishane has some top fragrances that are not in the Top 100 for nothing. Here we have a somewhat lesser-known scent from the house, a saffron-leather fragrance. This fragrance composition is nothing new anymore, but it still works very well.

Suède et Safran is my third fragrance from the house of Nishane - and I am sure it will not be my last fragrance from this house. I like the presentation of the fragrance: high-quality packaging, lined with fabric on the inside, and a really great bottle. The whole thing radiates class without being over the top. And then there is the fragrance itself.

Suède et Safran combines lightly spicy saffron with a well-captured wild leather note into a rather soft combination and clearly distinguishes itself from other leather fragrances, also because no fruity or synthetic scents mix in.

The Suède et Safran could not have been named more aptly in terms of branding; from the first spray, you can clearly smell these main components of the fragrance. But how does the scent perform, and can it really be compared to other leather fragrances like Godolphin and "London | Widian / AJ Arabia"?

Reading reviews prior to testing, I got the opinion that Cote d'Amour was going to be a 'straight down the line' aquatic, with all those oceanic qualities that I personally find irritating. I was really pleased to discover that this was not the case. It does have aquatic tendencies, but it's not an aquatic in the traditional sense. At first spray it smelt like fresh, watery cucumber and pink musk sticks. Amazing combination I must say. The sweet muskiness stays on throughout the composition, and I believe this scent is brought about by the immortelle flower, (which I have never smelt in real life). The heart introduces some unique smells like herbaceous rosemary, rich, woodsy pine, zesty grapefruit and a hint of powdery rose. The way in which they blend is almost phenomenal. If Summer always smelt like this, I swear I would enjoy the hot season more than I do. Cote d'Amour does tend to be on the lighter side, especially more towards the drydown, however the soft sillage did not reflect the lasting strength, which lasted a good eight hours on my skin. What I thought would be a scrubber turned out to be a fragrance that I loved wearing for the rest of the day. I give Cote d'Amour the big thumbs up for its unique composition, and another tick in the box for the way in which it kept me perplexed, yet under its spell. L'Artisan hasn't made a mistake with this fragrance, no not at all.

Côte d'Amour is a really uniqe fragrance. Quite fresh and creamy, and maybe rosemary makes it smell as paprika, but only for 1-2 minutes. The sequel stage is more impressive and sweet, even though the sillage is so weak, that my skin get pressed from my nose, if I want to feel something. I would like to feel this interesting, refreshing and thougth-provoking fragrance, but unfortunately I am glad, if it stays 2 hours long. Some perfumes don't mind if I lay another perfume on them, and after dissipate they consider to come back for a last leer. Côte d'Amour does not belong among those perfumes, even if you pray, it will not last longer. (I tested it from sample vial, without spray.)

When I first smelled the decant before putting it on, it was a pretty salty-mineral smell very similar to Ms. Ellena's earlier Sel de Vetiver. But when I put it on, it's just a pretty, gentle woody-spice scent of no particular artistry. It could easily have been concocted by someone less talented, blending essential oils at home. Most perfumes last very well on me, but this is gone in less than an hour. I want to like these "natural" perfumes, but perhaps I've been spoiled by the artificial ones? If this sort of thing interests you, go for her gorgeous Sel de Vetiver (The Different Company) instead. (090609)

When they first met in their youth, George, the Parisian intellectual, and Gauvin, a Breton fisherman, had no idea that this encounter would change their lives forever. Soon ignited by love and passion for each other, both are aware that a shared future in terms of living together, family, and daily life is not possible for them, as their environments, backgrounds, and goals are too different. Despite all obstacles, they still live their happiness, stealing moments together, even though both have their own partnerships, often not seeing each other for years, and yet, it is love that endures into old age and only finds an end through death. To love means to remain two, to the point of being torn apart, writes Benoît Groult in her 1992 book, originally titled Les Vaisseaux du Coeur, the vessels of the heart. Vaisseaux also means ships. George and Gauvin are like two ships that meet in the night, only to follow their own course again. Côte d'Amour, the coast of love, could be the fitting scent for this Amour Fou. A refuge just for the two protagonists, a place beyond time and everyday life. Initially minimally citrusy, here salt, sand, and sea air are the main themes. Caressing breezes, by no means artificial or piercing, as I unfortunately have to note in other fragrances of this category, gently embrace the nose. Dune grass, coniferous woods, and even faint rosemary provide soft undertones and ensure balance and well-being, before a delicate floral note emerges, evoking thoughts of the way home from the beach, past blooming front gardens. A lovely break from everyday life and a summer-sun longing fragrance that I would not have discovered so quickly without Hasi and her wonderful giveaway.

I hesitated for a very long time before purchasing this fragrance. But since it is no longer available regularly, I bought an OVP bottle in France at a really good price. Because my coast of love lies by the Mediterranean! Undoubtedly! The opening contains the complete fragrance collection of the Mediterranean: it smells of salt on sun-warmed skin, rubbed with sunscreen, it smells of immortelle, that creamy soft-scented coastal plant, of jasmine from the gardens near the coast, still faint and delicate, as it will only unfold its full scent at night, of sea and sea foam, of sand so hot that it is hardly bearable to walk on, and of pines that defy the hot sun. It smells of ripe, sweet (citrus) fruits, of wildflowers, and of wood. After a rather loud but beautiful opening, Côte d'Amour becomes soft and creamy and melds directly with my skin. This is a fragrance for summer, truly beautiful from 25° C upwards. Once the fragrance has developed - this happens within the first 15 minutes - it doesn’t change much anymore. After a few hours, it only becomes slightly woodier in the dry down. Nowhere else does it smell like this, as it does by the Mediterranean. Nowhere else is the light as radiant as by the Mediterranean. Nowhere else do I feel the same as by the Mediterranean. Nowhere else is it as beautiful as by the Mediterranean. My bottle is much more beautiful than the one pictured above, and the fragrance is a knockout. I really cannot understand why L'Artisan has taken this fragrance out of their range. Anyone who likes this type of fragrance should - if offered - grab it immediately!

Cliffs, rocks, wind, rough salty sea. She has found a place among the stones. Her gaze wanders over the endless expanse of the sea. Today she awaits the return of her beloved. Everything is prepared in the house for the visit. She has made a good meal and a pitcher of lemonade for refreshment. Her hands still carry the scent of the fruits.

YES! At least for me. I had been eagerly anticipating this Coast of Love and immediately tried it out impatiently upon its arrival. But what was that? I had never experienced anything like it: A rather generous amount landed on my skin. As the liquid made its way, I capped the bottle and wanted to sniff - but there was nothing! Absolutely nothing!!

Côte d'Amour is an interesting little fragrance. I once vacationed in Ireland; and I must say, this scent behaves quite similarly. The top note is citrusy for just a few seconds; I perceived more of the salt and rosemary. The development then moved towards gorse, cypress, and dune flower; coconut or rose completely faded away.

Thematically, it fits. The name "Côte" absolutely does justice to the ingredients. Anyone looking for something reminiscent of a Mediterranean beach that also exudes a certain beach party atmosphere might find what they're looking for here. A lively start, where refreshing mandarin, subtly coconut-exotic, and lightly spicy-salty nuances create a harmonious interplay.

I came to this fragrance because it is Ecocert certified and thus one of the few perfumes that complies with natural cosmetics guidelines but doesn't smell like a witch's brew. If one didn't know that it is an organic perfume, they wouldn't guess it so quickly. The scent itself starts fresh and citrusy.

This is an easy, everyday wear if you are looking for something quietly inoffensive. The scent itself is not very strong. It is a light, powdery floral that almost runs away from you. I don't think I ever got any fruit on opening, just soft white flowers. At the end, though, it rests on a nice, warm bourbon vanilla that I can definitely pinpoint. This could be a good scent for layering, though it doesn't last very long.

I'm a Heavenly/Dream Angels Heavenly fanatic and have tried almost every single release/reformulation. I compared them to this newest release, and this one: - is not the same as the OG Dream Angels Heavenly formula (in the tall, tapered, slightly-curved bottle with the white heart cap), or even the more recently-released Heavenly formula (the one in the chunky/"rectangular gold gem" shape) - is missing a LOT of notes from the OG Dream Angels Heavenly + newer Heavenly formulas (see previous Heavenly reviews) - smells cold, synthetic, and flat; does not have the musky, clean, "sexy soapy" DNA we all know and love over the years, regardless of which version/release - does not last :( *TL/DR: This is not the same as previously-released versions :( * P.S. I recently bought the OG formula on a resale platform, and it smelled just as beautiful and vibrant as before - hadn't turned at all. Read all 3 to see the differences, listed in order from oldest to newest: - Dream Angels Heavenly - Heavenly (2013) Eau de Parfum - Heavenly (2023) (this one)

Oh my, is that Nishane or Amouage? Once upon a time it blows from Greece to the Middle East...a thick flow of fragrant molecules. I think the wind is calling for beautiful silky non-tea bergamot, soft oily pepper, supple stems of cypriol, luxurious herbal hay for Arabian thoroughbreds, drying damp clover, the polished wooden stable of the sheikh and the polished horse air-conditioned by the savannah breeze. I blush slightly, I read about the scent, it is also about roses.

I bought this fragrance as an addition to my Rose-Oud collection, also Nishane is one of my favorite niche-brands and I love a lot of their fragrances. Synthetic florals make for a fake fruity experience, smells cheap and screechy. It gets better in the dry-down but I’m disappointed in Nishane. My nose can’t make out one particular floral note or even a clear rose note at all. In complete it does smell kind of oriental but that is it. I’d say this is kind of similar to Blue Sapphire Parfum but definitely smells WAY cheaper.

It was a morning when the world still seemed to be half-asleep. The sun had just begun to cast its first rays over the rooftops of the city, and a gentle breeze played with the curtains of my window. I applied Favonius to my wrist, unaware that this moment would be forever etched in my memory. At first, there was the freshness of bergamot, as clear and vibrant as morning dew on leaves, interwoven with a hint of pink pepper that made me smile with a slight tingle. Then the rose unfolded-not the usual, slightly sweet bloom, but a rose full of depth, spicy, majestic, carried by incense that wafted through the alleys like a soft breath. As I walked through the city, the air suddenly felt denser, richer, filled with stories from ancient times. The oud and wood notes at the end of the fragrance gave me a sense of grounding, of strength and permanence. At the same time, everything felt like a dance: the wind played with the blossoms, the sun reflected in the windows, and I felt like a part of an eternal, elegant flow of light and scent. Favonius was more than just a perfume for me that morning. It was a companion, a whisper of nature, a touch of luxury, and at the same time a reminder that even the most fleeting moments can be full of beauty. I could still smell it hours later on my clothes, and every time I lifted my hand, it seemed a small part of that morning came alive again. It was as if the fragrance itself preserved the memory of that moment-the freshness, the warmth, the delicate power of the rose, and the quiet, venerable breath of the incense. Favonius was not just a scent, but an experience, a fleeting spring captured in a drop of perfume.

...(at least at the Nishane stand). Maybe also in the Xerjoff Lounge on the sixth floor, probably next to Floraiku. But definitely at Nishane. I've been to Harrods three times to try the Harrods exclusive fragrance Favonius at the Nishane stand. Always found it brilliant, but never bought it due to the rather steep price. In the last few days, I was back in London and this time I did it. It hardly hurt at all (the credit card bill will come in a few days, and then the tears will probably flow). For now, however, there were only tears of joy. Joy over this fragrance, which for me not only belongs to Nishane's best but is probably one of the most beautiful rose-oud combinations you can buy. If it weren't so expensive and complicated to purchase (only at Harrods or by ordering from Istanbul), I'm sure it would be Nishane's flagship. As it is, it remains a little secret of the brand. When I first tried it, however, it was not love at first sight (more like "at the first sniff"). That day, I had done a little perfume tour through London, and not only were my legs exhausted after 40,000 steps, but probably my nose as well. However, I caught myself sniffing Favonius again and again from all the test strips I had received in the following days. Back in Munich, I left the tester in the car at first. The next day, I was greeted by the full inhalation of Favonius when I got in. That probably says it all about the fragrance's performance. It lasts easily a week on clothing, and on the skin, it radiates all day. So what does it smell like? Somehow, I still can't say exactly. I smell cherry and berries, even though there aren't any according to the fragrance pyramid. You might catch a whiff of incense and definitely the bouquet of flowers listed. Rose and oud come more in the combination known from my dearly loved Oud Satin Mood (just in a less intrusive way than with Maison Francis Kurkdjian). Thank goodness it's not cheesy and musty like Oud Silk Mood; that would drive me away. All in all, perfectly rounded and balanced, probably unisex (at least I, as a man, am now diligently spraying it on) and somehow a shame that it gets so little attention.
