With Oudous Lux Solis , cosplay perfumer Jordi Fernández is taking some (!) inspiration from his work under both Maison Crivelli as well as Ex Nihilo with their hero franchises, those being Oud Maracujá and Blue Talisman Eau de Parfum . Beyond that, it's hard to express where this hodge-podge of notes and accords actually ends up at. With Oudous Lux Solis , we have a fresh-fruity-sweet and synthetic open. The initial feeling is that Fernández has taken the tropical fruity accord from Oud Maracujá and aligned with both a synthetic-aquatic accord (designer-like calone quality) and a synthetic-woody accord (akigalawood). The structure of the scent, given the fresh-fruity-synthetic opening, features significant overlap with the manner in which Blue Talisman Eau de Parfum is shaped. There is a prominent candied sweet fruitiness in the initial few moments alongside that tropical fruity accord which is likely the reason why I am seeing comparisons to "Le Gemme - Tygar | Bvlgari" and/or Vibrato , but this is clearly (!) not a scent in that realm. When I first smelled it up-close, the structure itself reminds me of other fruity interpretations of akigalawood that we have in the market, most notably Blue Talisman Eau de Parfum and Castley . Relative to the PDM, there is a lack of fresh spiciness and the fruitiness features more prominently in this scent. Somewhere in the first 5 minutes, I do pick up on mild Ani X type qualities, offering some of those melon & vanilla-like nuances. The first red flags start to appear thereafter as the tropical fruity accord begins to break into various parts. The fruitiness goes in various directions and the listed patchouli note begins to pop more. Similarly to Hacivat Oud , the execution of the patchouli is poor as it comes off a bit like paint remover. In the ultimate dry-down with no fruitiness remaining, we arrive at a very underwhelming product. While this scent is not meant to be inspired by Xerjoff's Erba Pura and scents in that family, the ultimate composition ending at white musk and mild fruity tones isn't doing it any favors. That is to say the scent ends up somewhat barebones after the first hour or so and most of the notes/accords shielding this poor blending fade away. I think one relevant comparison here could be Tropiques from Fragrance du Bois which has some of that Erba Pura-style, but in a more tropical fruity direction than the Xerjoff. In the final stages of this scent's evolution, I think it's fair to say that this is among the worst products I've ever put on my skin (and by almost any objective measure, it's worse than the any of the aforementioned comparables). For what it's worth, this scent never smells of oud and I have to assume people are voting for "woody" as an accord strictly because of the akigalawood, albeit that note's actual main accord is just synthetic. Final accords: synthetic-fruity-sweet-fresh So where did we end up at? Unlike some others, I don't want to imply that many of the problems plaguing niche perfumery today are strictly applicable to today's scene. In the past, there was a time when Alberto Morillas would drop the same garbage aquatic fragrance for more than a decade straight and people thought he was a genius. Yet to me, this type of behavior in the niche market feels egregious. For the last couple of years, one-trick-pony perfumer Quentin Bisch has been at the forefront of this with takes of both Ganymede as well as Guidance and Fernández' recent lack of originality isn't that far from Bisch's, building on the success of existing IPs such as Oud Maracuja and Blue Talisman in his catalogue (and London, Gris Charnel, Town & Country and others outside of it). But in most cases, the perfumers aren't the ones deciding the creative direction of the product(s) they're working on. The ones at fault are the brands who feel like they are competing for finite resources, whether it be customer spending, views, engagements, you name it. It's a lot easier to generate revenue with IP that already has some recognition in the market, meaning all the perfumer is asked to do is to make a quality take of it. But this obviously raises the question as to how Nishane ever signed off on this absolute trash that Fernández put together. It's going to take a lot for this to not end up as the worst of 2025.

What should I say to you? First of all, I want you not to be misled by the Erba Pura comparison. Unfortunately, I can't support that. What I can understand more is the comparison with Oud Maracuja and the usual suspects that go in the same direction. Fruit with Oud, after all. However, I don't want to keep you in suspense any longer and reveal why I chose this headline. Well, as you have probably already seen, the Oudous Lux Solis is a Harrods Exclusive. I ordered it just like I have ordered many other Harrods Exclusives. Among them is also the Exclusive from EldO. And I immediately noticed a parallel: An honestly half-bad fruit-Oud blend for a solid chunk of money, which both fragrances are definitely NOT worth. Well, here it might be the "tropical fruits," not the strawberry (EldO), but still a parallel. I don't necessarily want to dissuade you from this fragrance, but I want to emphasize that this is a typical case of copy-paste, where ChatGPT might have changed it a bit (). And if you then say: Wow, this IS my fragrance, I need it, I want it. Then at least consider again briefly whether you want to pay a huge amount of money for a mid-range product. Best regards

The sun had just risen above the horizon, and its first rays fell like liquid gold on the rooftops of the city. In this quiet morning hour, I stepped into the studio, a room filled with fabrics, colors, and long-lost inspirations. But today was different; today she was to create something that not only touched the senses but also the soul. I reached for the small, shiny bottle that lay in her hand like a treasure: Oudous Lux Solis. With the first spray, a vibrant play of mandarin, pomelo, and a hint of ginger unfolded-a radiant spark that filled the room with energy. It was as if the sun itself had lost a fragrance that it now wanted to return. The heart of the perfume blossomed like a mysterious garden: honey and cistus merged into a warm, almost magical shimmer that filled the air. Ela closed her eyes and envisioned a quiet, sun-drenched courtyard where golden petals danced in the wind. Every breath was an invitation to immerse oneself in this moment, to forget the hustle and bustle of the world outside. But then the base emerged: oud, Indonesian patchouli, and Akigalawood. Dark, earthy, and yet fascinatingly metallic, it framed the light that had previously been so clear and pure with a mysterious aura. It was as if the sun itself carried a shadow that made its radiance even more intense. I knew: This fragrance was more than an experience, a small cosmos of light and shadow, warmth and depth. A scent that transformed the moments of everyday life into something precious and took the wearer on a journey-from the morning sun to the golden evening light, from joy to quiet reflection. As I applied the last drop to my skin, I smiled. Oudous Lux Solis had told its story-and I was ready to share it with the world.

'Once Upon a Wood', but is that really all it was? This fragrance stands at the crossroads of two worlds: that of wood, with its deep and natural notes, and that of the field, where the earth offers echoes of fresh grains. Despite its evocative name, the fragrance might have worn the title 'Once Upon a Countryside' more fittingly, as it would have captured its cereal soul more faithfully. This fragrance doesn't seek to shake up conventions but rather to create a pleasant universe, albeit somewhat predictable. It transports us, yes, but not with the grandeur of an epic. More like a gentle stroll, a quiet countryside scent, unpretentious.

My most loved vetiver and dark green scent, hands down. Not only that, but it's a fragrance that I would totally wear to work or to an event. I'm a huge fan of green profile scents and love them in all their different aspects from light, fresh vegetal greens (think Synthetic Nature ) to dark, mysterious greens like Bandit (2012) Eau de Parfum or its sunnier sister, Le Sillage Blanc . However, not all of these are perfumes I would invest in for daily wear because quite frankly, a lot of these are statements, or art works that are not exactly suited to the ordinary situations in which a woman would find herself in everyday life. "Il Était Un Bois | L'Artisan Parfumeur" however is something I could see myself wearing a lot. "Il Était Un Bois | L'Artisan Parfumeur" is the perfume from a Brothers Grimm fairy tale, the ferns and grasses growing under a dark European forest canopy, a seldom trodden path through the Black Forest, Red Riding Hood hurrying through, throwing quick glances behind her as the sun is slowly dropping on the horizon. There's a peppery, herbal vibration of something slightly mentholated, like anise or eucalyptus. It's dusky, mysterious, slightly humid, superb. My only pet peeve, why is it so hard to get your hands on these? Their European site at Harrods only accepts UK issued credit cards (royal bitch, please!), the customer service is totally clueless, and the websites are clunky and don't load properly. C'mon, L'AP, show some professionalism and concern for your clients!

It's masculine. It's woody. It's kinda fresh but in a balsamic way. It does remind me a bit of Mechant Loup and Fou d'Absinthe, but just a slight vibe. It definitely transports me into a cold forest, with fresh cut woods and cold air. It's great, would consider buying it if i'd only use one perfume cause it smells like a signature fragrance of a nice 40/50s man. Still studying it though, tried only one spray on my hand. Will write more if i catch up something more. EDIT: Tried again and it definitely has vetiver all over it. it's a vetiver prominent perfume. I like it a bit less.

a perfume named "once upon a forest" ...very beautiful, I think, but still sad the thought of not finding a forest "like this" someday. Beyond the beaten paths, moss-covered trunks. Fog whose dew reflects on the leaves. Sun desperately trying to fight its way through the mist. Pale light that makes the forest appear as if in a fairy tale. Everywhere, the tiniest water droplets glisten on the delicate blades of grass that make their way to the light through the fallen leaves. With every step, the crackling of dry, rotten branches, small wisps of fog rising up through the warmth of the sun.... This scent perfectly reflects these images within me. The earthy vetiver and cedar, paired with the gentle warmth of buckwheat. A beautiful composition. Spray it on and let your soul dangle. A scent that allows us to escape from everyday life, everywhere there are no enchanted forests. I assume this is why this scent received exactly this name. ....once upon a forest.... I hope so much that such forests are not destroyed. That careful consideration is given to how such oases of tranquility can be preserved, for us and for future generations. There are no more beautiful places of peace than the forest. This scent should not become a scent of memories but remain a scent of comfort. It is not a scent that overwhelms you immediately. It unfolds really slowly. I love this slightly warm, earthy, woody, green scent. Somehow it always brings you back down to earth when you are about to lose it. The longevity of "Il Était Un Bois" is very good. This scent is truly worth a little journey. A journey into an enchanted forest .

Shinanay is a bold unisex fragrance that opens with aldehydes and blood orange, leading to a heart of white florals like tuberose and gardenia. The base combines sandalwood, oakmoss, and civet, adding depth and complexity. Rating: 8/10 Longevity: 8.2/10 Projection: 7.8/10 Versatility: 6/10 Best for: Evening / Fall-Winter

First off, I’m a big fan of Nishane; it’s arguably my favorite niche house. Kredo is my signature fragrance for the cold weather, and I plan to buy Wulong Cha as my summer signature. You can probably imagine my excitement when Shinanay came out. The timing coincided when I started using Souk, and I got Shinanay via a Split. When deciding how much to split, I was hesitating between 10 vs 5 ml. The heart wanted 10 ml, and kept reminding me all my previous beautiful Nishane experience. But the brain was telling me to not rush. Eventually, the brain won, and I feel very lucky about it now. Here is why. Shinanay is NOT a conventional smell. While the orange note in the opening brings some freshness, an animalistic note (probably the Civet) quickly pushes out and dominates the stage thereafter. In Kredo, there is also a slight offness and animalistic sense, but it was not dominant and is quite enjoyable for me. However, in Shinanay, the note is dominant and unpleasant. The scent itself is complex, and, with more wear, I start to pick up different layers. While it may be interesting, I‘veI never found it desirable. If Shinanay is an art, I am not a good enough artist to appreciate it. Lastly, the moral of the story: when sampling a new fragrance, start small!

You've lived in the woods your whole life, have a pet wolf and chop trees in your spare time. This is what all the alpha males preaching to you on your social media platforms would smell like if they lived the lives they claimed. This is also what I imagine that the men who wore scents like polo green in the 80's thought they smelled like. Shinanay is much smoother (and overall way better smelling) than a polo green however. This is an unapologetically resinous fragrance that I can see being a signature scent for an overwhelmingly confident man's man. If that isn't you, then this must be worn intentionally or rest assured that it will wear you. From the opening to the end of its 8 hour lifespan it makes itself known with a good projection and sillage. If you love the house of Nishane and want to get into animalic fragrances, then this may be the easiest wear that they have to offer in that style. While I think this is an amazing scent (that I wear it at home from time to time), it is ultimately too animalic for me to wear as often as I would like.

Civet and beaver bring their three little zibers to dear Ziber Grandma for a little chat before they head off to the disco they run into the neighboring forest where the little ones were just playing in the cedar forest and are full of resinous oak moss. But Grandma is clever and has already filled the bathtub with soapy foam, so she carefully places them one by one inside and starts to rub them down. Afterwards, they are creamed and powdered, and after a little smoky citrus spritzer, they head to the freshly made cuddly soft sandalwood bed. Grandma tells her favorite story about the evil blue goblins who become greedier and hunt the kind-hearted, empathetic goblins, but they are not interested because they sleep through until Sunday morning. ------------------------------------------------------ What a bombastically brilliant opening celebration after the first contact, I thought I was in the seventh Chypre heaven citrusy mossy truckload full of all the flowers in the world meter-high soap foam mountains green woody lavender soft and still pine bath like as a toddler, I find it like at Grandma's, musky soft bed linen cuddly soft, oak moss fresh, the old wooden wardrobe ventilates through and Grandma's cream and powder are everywhere, the lily of the valley calls loudly for water. The scent is more than vintage, everything from the past is there, musk very tame, the scent is really well blended and feels very rich, it radiates pure luxury, is enchanting and seductive, exalted and all-encompassing like a scent ball. There are very sweet goblins here, everything fits, no poking this time. Thank you to the very dear Gandix for the testing opportunity ️

The word Shinanay or actually also " şinanay " comes from Turkish and has many meanings; it is often associated with playful themes and is also versatile in its application. I connect the motto with the fragrance as well. The start begins green, somewhat Fougere-like, with a bit of the vibe of aftershave, and then shifts into a Chypre direction. I have tested an extreme number of fragrances from this house and was literally shocked that such a step was taken. If I were not aware of which label the scent comes from, it could very well be a "Bogue" fragrance, with the fine difference in complexity. With the Chypre character, the drydown also begins; tuberose is no longer at the back of the line... My concern was confirmed! It keeps pushing further and further forward until it characterizes the scent very dominantly. Thus, a mixture of 50% tuberose / 50% greenery emerges. The drydown did not go over well in my friend circle because I was visiting a buddy at the time, and they commented on it haha :)) And now to the end, after about 3-4 hours, the tuberose pulls back a bit and the notes of the ingredients listed below come in, which I personally liked the most. It gains a new scent character through civet & co. All in all, I find the fragrance very well made. However, I am, from the bottom of my heart, an enemy of tuberose, which is why it finds no parking space in my perfume cabinet. The tuberose is somehow and somewhere present every second, sometimes more, sometimes less... Nevertheless, "good job"!

Shinanay is quite a special fragrance. The edges and contours of the scent make it unique, but this can manifest positively or negatively. I think you generally have to like something like this to find it appealing. Otherwise, you really need to give the fragrance some time.

This scent is good. Not great, not bad, just fine. Why? It lacks a bit of depth. I've smelled my share of neroli fragrances, realized it's a flower I do love in a fragrance if it's done right. In this one? They've done it nice , but haven't done justice to it. At the beginning, neroli is floral, sweet and citrusy with a tinge of green freshness. It's soft and lovely, perfect for the warm weather ahead. After a few moments, it turns a bit more spicy (still stays in feminine territory) with a warm musky and ambery undertone. It's like a neroli flower getting heat from the rays of sun during spring. I don't really get what oxygen or solar notes are supposed to smell like, so I can't really share an opinion on those. Since it doesn't have a lot of notes, it lacks the depth I need and crave to add it to my collection. Overall, it's a nice skin-scent, clearly in the clean-girl aesthetic, It'll make you feel freshly showered and ready to go. Unfortunately, there are better fragrances out there for a fraction of the price and the sillage is so so soft, it reminded me of a fragrance mist. Not worth for the price.

I hadn't looked at the fragrance notes before testing, so I was hoping for a fresh, green scent reminiscent of grasses and herbs before spraying it on. That is not the case. It's much more of a (very) light, (very) beautiful Neroli scent. (Very) delicate. Too delicate? I'm not a fan of fragrances that seem to linger even after two days and at least one shower. I don't think my scent needs to be smelled from 3 meters away. Sometimes, it almost ruins a fragrance for me when I can smell it continuously over a longer period; it creates a sort of saturation feeling. BUT I would like to enjoy the scent myself for at least 2.5 - 4 hours. Even with an EdC, I think 2.5 hours should be achievable. When I rest my head on my hand, I appreciate a whiff of the fragrance. If I hug someone during that time, I want my scent to be at least perceived peripherally. During my first test, after an hour, I could only smell something when my nose was pressed against my skin. So I sprayed on more and waited again. This time, I could perceive the scent quite closely for about three and a half hours. I find that still okay, but I had to initially apply quite a bit of perfume for that. It's a nice scent, but at least today, it’s not enough for me to make a purchase.

I sold my Wild Palm and kept the BG one cuz they are so similar but I prefer lighter options for summer that I can just add more if needed. I didn't need 2 of the same fragrance. A more youthful version of Tuberoza but very recognizable as its sister. I think the violet makes it lean more candy-ish while Tuberoza is straight sweet white floral. I like X, and I'd recommend it especially for people branching out from college student gourmand tastes but not quite ready for mature floral bombs. I still like the original more for myself.

The Tuberóza Extrait de Parfum unfortunately shows me once again that tuberose, especially in combination with ylang-ylang, is simply not for me. The opening is exhausting, has something metallic/lacquer-like in the tuberose-ylang-ylang mix, and brings few 'surprises' as it develops. For me, it's a "No, thanks." One step at a time: As mentioned, the fragrance starts with a tuberose and ylang-ylang punch that hits you hard. The scent is loud... very loud in the opening, but weakens towards the end. In the opening, there is one note that ruined it for me: something metallic or lacquer-like. Based on the fragrance pyramid, I can only guess it's a €2 lipstick. I can only vaguely make out the outline of a mandarin; for me, the opening consists solely of the above 3 components. After 20 minutes, the metallic note fortunately fades away, and it becomes more pleasant. The intense, strong tuberose remains dominant and loud. Ylang-ylang adds a good dose of creaminess. Despite the loud tuberose, it becomes noticeably more harmonious and calmer after 30 minutes, evolving into a floral-creamy "sweetie." After 1 hour: A certain peppery/spicy note comes into play. Just very lightly, and you really have to sniff closely. Could it be a spicier musk? Very likely, because the fragrance pyramid wouldn't suggest anything else. The drydown, which is basically composed of tuberose and ylang-ylang, is rather boring, as there is hardly any change or surprise. A hint of sweetness (amber?) emerges, but the scent is already very sweet, almost powdery. After 3 hours: Not much has changed. The musk and the spicy note become more pronounced, but still perhaps only account for 20% "market share" - the rest is claimed by tuberose and ylang-ylang. I don't sense any of the (sandal)wood presented here. That would have made it more interesting! In the time between 2-3 hours after spraying, I believe the most beautiful side of the DNA shows itself: no longer so loud, beautifully floral-creamy with a slight sweetness. What was initially overwhelming now becomes a more refined spectator in the second row. After 5 hours: The longevity decreases significantly, and you can only detect the Tuberóza Extrait de Parfum close to the skin. It would still project well on clothing; however, all my tests have been solely on skin. Not much has changed scent-wise - everything just gradually becomes weaker. After 9 hours, most of the ingredients have faded, but are not gone. Honestly, I find it most pleasant now, with the last remnants of power, simply because the tuberose is no longer so dominant and has developed into a kind of sweet licorice-tuberose-vanilla. After 11 hours, it is only perceptible very close to the skin. The longevity has been above average! ---- Conclusion: For me, the fragrance has once again shown that tuberose in this high, intense concentration is not for me. Ylang-ylang is used to tame the tuberose beast and make it creamy. The metallic note in the opening and the generally rather boring drydown lead to many point deductions combined with my dislike for tuberose. Important: However, those who love an elegant, creamy tuberose will get their money's worth here (!) Unisex? Probably not. I clearly see it on a woman. Season? I can imagine it well in late winter, early spring, when such loud fragrances can be worn. Occasion? Even though it lasts through a whole workday, I wouldn't wear it to work or even in the office. It radiates too much. Its use is found after 6 PM; I could also see it as a feminine date scent. The price of €230 comes from one of the most expensive ingredients of its namesake: the Indian tuberose in highly concentrated form. For lovers, it is an absolutely justified price - it's not for me. tl;dr: Can be done - but not by me ;-)

This scent is for me the classic form of a typical tuberose perfume. By nature, tuberose fragrances are sweet-creamy to me and often have a slightly synthetic or gummy quality, which does not bother me at all here. The gum is not sticky or chewy, but simply sweet and milky, perhaps more like a colorful fruit chewy candy. For all tuberose lovers, this is an absolute go! The question of whether I would classify it as classic or modern leaves me a bit stumped. The tuberose itself feels somewhat old-fashioned (here: "lipstick-like"), but the Ylang Ylang adds a summery creaminess that "modernizes" the scent in a way.

This was awarded the best gourmand niche fragrance of 2020 and for a good reason. The combination of coffee with the passion fruit is just divine. The coffee in here is more like a cappuccino, a bit more potent and noticeable that in the intense café. The chocolate gives it this almost edible quality that makes you want to like your hand :D. It is based on a beautiful ambery vanilla, which combined with the musk smoothens up the formulation but at the same time keeps it sweet. The coffee and passion fruit stays with you throughout the whole duration of the fragrance. The projection is average with above average longevity 12+ hours. Not as potent as Nishane Ani but close. The only sad thing is that this is officially discontinued so if you find yourself a bottle get it while you still can. Worth the retail price? If you are a Nishane fan like me, yes!

A piercingly bitter sour fruit opening, passion fruit fits in my opinion and a thought of grapefruit is also acceptable. The third in the supposed trio would be coffee. On this topic, I need to elaborate a bit: With some good coffees (for visitors to Hamburg: www.die-roesterei.com), it is clearly noticeable, as long as we don't ruin it with milk and/or sugar, that the coffee bean is a fruit, the aromas are so sour-fruity. I do not perceive such here… unfortunately. I went a bit too far, heh. Let's forget that. Instead, I smell a kind of bitter almond aroma note that guides me out of the citrus-sharp opening. And where to? To the gas station. The scent, despite all its sweetness and floral notes, takes on a gasoline twist, and I can't get away from the baked aroma in this regard. The whole thing also develops - supported by the citrus-and-co fruit remnants - a somewhat synthetic, but still fresh-green, latently plant-juicy touch. It is indeed conceivable that coriander has a certain share in this. Chocolate is, at least according to our understanding of it, indeed absent, and I already align myself with what has been said. In this context, I rather recall my test of "Piment Brûlant." That also had little to do with chocolate and shouldn't have. Because the Xocoatl ("bitter water") of the Aztecs, which Duchaufour explicitly refers to in L'Artisan, was a mixture of things like water, cocoa, corn, vanilla, chili, and salt. And that the cocoa was fermented back then as painstakingly towards chocolate as it is today can be considered questionable. I gradually feel like the "Advocatus Angeli" (the content-wise correct "… Dei" would be quite a stretch) of the manufacturer: I am making too many justifying thoughts. There is no indication that the people at Nishane intended such. The scent is simply mediocre and could be described with a more malicious mindset as prickly-sweet-sour-penetrating. In the late morning, a stinging, floral or heliotropic vanilla spreads, surrounded by our leftover fruity-sour freshness at the threshold of the watery, for which we can be grateful at this point. Interestingly, at some point, the heliotropic synthetic reminds me unexpectedly of Africa by Tesori d'Oriente and even Joop's Nightflight. In the afternoon, the prickliness recedes and finally reveals a quite decent vanilla, which still benefits from a balancing fruit residue, although it is increasingly approaching canned fruit. Overall, however, the scent is retreating; about five hours have passed. Nevertheless, it lingers in a significantly diminished volume for quite a while. Towards the end of the evening, patchouli scratches around. Conclusion: What is offered stands in what I consider an unacceptable disproportion to what is demanded (160 euros for 50ml). That the name might also mislead chocolate fans is annoying.

It is known that cumin in fragrances can smell little bit like bo, but for Spice Bazar it is not the case. Still, the cumin in here can be a bit divisive. Very palatable in my opinion, together with the yuzu and the ginger it gives that Nishane fizzy opening that we love from Ani but with loads of spices and just a hint of sweetness. I don't know how a spice bazar smells like but for me, as a hardcore niche lover, this fragrance is amazing. I would say best suited in spring and autumn but it can be work all year around. Jorge Lee did amazing with this one, his best work for Nishane in my opinion. Sadly it is being discontinued. It is not a blind buy, sample first. Longevity and projection above avarage, 12+ hours.

Yes, that's what you can call him, the Shy One. He has everything my patchouli heart desires. But he is sooo shy. I work with him because he actually needs a bit more self-confidence. Come on, come out of your shell. A little bling bling and hair slicked back. Wouwwww, see, that’s better. No, seriously. Múnegu is a wonderful, warm - earthy patchouli scent. Unfortunately, it doesn't get the recognition it deserves here. Considering that patchouli was once a healing herb and is still used as such today, one can actually be happy if one likes a patchouli scent. Well, it was mainly used as an insect repellent. That makes perfect sense to me when I think of patchouli scents that smell sharp and cold. The smell of patchouli was also a sign that, for example, goods that were to be shipped to another country were sprayed with it. If a carpet or a coat didn’t smell of patchouli, it wasn’t “real” or came from somewhere else. Now, patchouli is not just an insect repellent or healing herb. Oh no, it also has magical properties. It is said to awaken love, desire, beauty, fertility, and passion. In magical or witch circles, patchouli oil is used for fertility magic. Although fertility is a very broad term for me. It doesn’t always have to be about sexual fertility. One can also use fertility, meaning growth, for success or courage or whatever one might be lacking. Fine, but Múnegu has not only patchouli; it is simply beautiful with its enchanting liaison of woods and earth, warm amber, and spices AND strong flowers like ylang-ylang and geranium. Cumin, which always has the property of making all scents a bit sweaty and animalistic, is completely overshadowed here. The fruity-citrusy start of the fragrance brings a smile to your face because you just didn’t expect it. Delicate veils of incense and steaming tobacco smoke give the scent a slightly masculine touch, but that’s fine too! For me, Múnegu is a shy, lovely patchouli scent that could definitely be a bit louder. Because for the price, Sylvain Cara - who usually breathes something extraordinary into his fragrances - could have given it more power. Otherwise, well done!

This is bitter, fresh, herbal, gentlemanly but not overly masculine, slightly sweet and floral. What a beautiful concoction. I wore this at a wedding in the summer and got tons of compliments on it. It is a fresh aquatic without going in the blue fragrances direction. The amber in here is used very clever, similar to the way it is used in Ambra Calabria but here it is not the star of the show. The kelp note makes this fragrance marine but without giving it an overly fishy vibe. Imagine a walk on a beach that is surrounded by green vegetation and flowers. Stunning gem from Nishane. It is sad that this is being discontinued. Much better fragrance than Ege in my opinion. Longevity and projection are above average 12+ hours. Very potent for a freshie.

First of all I like this. But, if you have ever smelled D&G Light Blue Intense you don't need to buy this. I might have had an olfactory malfunction but I really find it very similar and the D&G cost me less than £30. This is perhaps longer lasting but that doesn't matter when I can spray the D&G to my hearts content. Shame

I have had Florane by Nishane on my watchlist for what feels like an eternity. Actually, ever since DaveGahan101 wrote this statement and compared it to Bal d’Afrique. In the meantime, I had long sorted out Byredo, but my curiosity about Florane remained. Not even in Zurich at Spitzenhaus could I test it. They didn’t even know it there! Well, it is what it is. There are lovely Parfumas and Parfumos. And thanks to dear Connie, I was finally able to test it. So, I tried it and to be honest, I am a bit torn. I would categorize it as a scent that I like, but not necessarily on myself. I had it with me this morning while running. As usual, just a few drops. And even though dear Connie has a different opinion, I think it projects quite strongly. So for the first half hour of my run, I had Florane constantly in my nose, which is usually almost too much for me with such a small dose. However, it performs really well while running. It has a very strong, almost slightly stern floral deodorant freshness. If someone wishes to feel fresh with power and also loves flowers, then Florane is definitely the right choice. The Nishane brand is known for its perfumes not exactly scoring points for shyness. This one certainly doesn’t either. This slight sternness that makes me think of deodorant is also the reason why I don’t see it on myself personally. I prefer flowers to be softer, fluffier, cozier. You can cuddle with Florane too, but it requires a bit of patience. After my run this morning, I had a soft, wonderfully creamy scent on my hand. And I can even understand the comparisons with Bal d’Afrique, as the jasmine here strikes a similar chord. But I also thought of Eternity by Calvin Klein. Another floral that knows how to excite me, but just like Florane, I don’t feel it as my own. Those who know Eternity know what I mean. With CK, there are also lily of the valley, violets, and jasmine hitting you right in the face. And for those who can withstand the floral storm, there’s a cozy, soft cuddly base with warm amber tones as a reward. It’s exactly the same here. When discreetly dosed on someone else, such a scent can be a blast for me. Overdosed, however, I tend to pick up the pace when running away. That works quite well again! I have trained hard :) A heartfelt thank you to Connie for allowing me to finally get to know it. It’s high quality, it’s beautiful, but personally, it’s just a bit too much for me. Eternity fans will adore it. I’m quite sure of that! And Nishane could definitely bring it more into the spotlight. I find it a shame that it is so extremely hard to find.

A very very beautiful creamy/floral and very special scent. Although it is floral and creamy, the fragrance smells very niche due to the unusual combination with the false cypress. I can hardly detect the fruits; to my nose, the violets are very prominent. Lily of the valley and jasmine are also noticeable but play a supporting role. A super interesting note emerges from the drydown, the cypress, which in a fantastic way adds a slightly greenish but very very beautiful creamy quality that makes the scent so special. I don't know any other fragrance that smells similar. It is the kind of scent that is simply super pleasant, very refined, and very very creamy. It is slightly sweet and smells like the most expensive cream you can imagine... When I sprayed it on, I saw a beautiful woman in front of me. It is summer in Italy, she is wearing a long white dress, her sunglasses in her hair, holding her long blonde hair together. She wears flat shoes and sends everyone a smile in a light and carefree manner. Unfortunately, the scent is quite close to the skin and the longevity is only mediocre; if it were different, I would have to have the fragrance immediately. So, anyone who enjoys "more intimate" creamy, summery scents should definitely test this fragrance.

~ Inspiration ~ After I was able to test "Midnight Dare" and "Pure Daydream" from Jeli, other Victoria's Secret Body Sprays also made it onto my wishlist. I received a sample of "Midnight Exotics - Forbidden Vanilla" from the lovely Delica. ~ Bottle ~ The plastic bottle contains 250ml. A dotted mesh pattern, reminiscent of tights, forms the background with a gradient from purple to pink. ~ Fragrance ~ Creamy-sweet vanilla meets velvety dark teak wood, giving it a sensually warm aura. ~ Longevity ~ Unfortunately, it only lasts about 2-3 hours on my skin (not much longer on clothes and hair). The sillage remains very close to the body, and one should keep in mind that it is a body spray and not to expect a perfume. You can comfortably use several sprays. ~ Occasion ~ A delicious, unobtrusive scent for the mild days of autumn and winter. Perfect when you don't want to smell too strong (e.g., as an office scent with sensitive noses), as it really only leaves a hint behind. ~ Conclusion ~ I quite like it, but unfortunately, it fades away so quickly! It somewhat reminds me of a milder version of "Pink Sugar Sensual" by Aquolina.

Welcome back to this year's closing coverage. In 2025, Turkish niche house Nishane has launched 4 fragrances, incl. 3 products with exclusivity to various boutiques: A Date with Oud , Oudous Lux Solis and Oudous Cerasus . While the Harrods exclusive Lux Solis sits at the bottom of my 2025 rankings as of early November and has been there since I first smelled it, Oudous Cerasus delivers a pleasant experience with a good depth of notes and accords. In the top, Oudous Cerasus opens spicy-fruity and slightly synthetic. You just instantly know there's some akigalawood mixed in. Much like with Oudous Lux Solis , I can pick up on the Oud Maracujá style dark woody/leathery accord very quickly as well. Unlike Lux Solis, the structure is done well in Cerasus: the calone doesn't pop up at all and the main notes in the air are the cherry, the cistus, and the two woody notes (akigala and oud). The structure here is very much reminiscent of the opening of Xerjoff's recent Milan exclusive Via Manzoni 20 . As always, the initial impressions are merely a reflection of what I am smelling. When I compare it to the notes/accords, I'd place the product somewhere between the Xerjoff and the recent Triptych collection from French niche brand Vilhelm who figured releasing 3 different takes of Ganymede was a good idea in 2025. The wearing experience in the heart of the scent clearly places Oudous Cerasus in the realm of scents like Fernandez' hero franchise Blue Talisman Eau de Parfum . For me personally, I like the comparison to the opening of Via Manzoni 20 the most. I would also bring attention to the patchouli which does add an earthy smell to the on-skin composition in the heart and dry-down. As for floral tones, I cannot spot any personally. The performance is quite a bit lighter than Lux Solis: I never really get more than average-to-mediocre sillage with my initial longevity assessment being about 6 hours. Value's a hard one to assess with it being exclusive to Selfridges at £310/100ml, but I don't want to give it more than a 4/10. The title of the review reflects the views that I generally hold for fragrances driven by akigalawood: given the note's prominent synthetic nature, I refuse to rate it high in my system. However, I have rated Oudous Cerasus on par with Blue Talisman Eau de Parfum after I recently revisited the Ex Nihilo and revised it up from a 6.0 to a 6.5 (not as synthetic as I had remembered). That is to say this is a fragrance I could see myself wearing, but all-in-all, it falls short of the highs Nishane has achieved over the years, from Ani Extrait de Parfum to Nefs . At the same time, Nishane should consider themselves lucky to not have released a cherry twist on Lux Solis' synthetic DNA.

I am starting to get a bit confused, and I don't mean to be harsh... I tried this today at Selfridges. Yes, it has a rather non-descript cherry opening but it rapidly veers into a oud maracuja x erba pura vibe. I really don't understand why Nishane is getting into this kind of releases. I guess that big exclusive contracts (i.e. £££) are at play, especially when you have a successful perfumer behind your creations. The silver lining is that if you are a fan of Nishane as a brand, you don't need to despair. In my opinion, these "Oudous" exclusives are just not worth it. Get a sample if you can, and judge yourself.

London's major department stores are known within the perfume community for carrying exclusive fragrances from big brands that can only be purchased there. However, the exclusivity of the perfumes (and the quite high price) is no guarantee that they are exceptionally good scents. With "Oudous Cerasus | Nishane," however, Nishane and Selfridges have hit a home run with me! At first, a cherry-strawberry jam with honey is noticeable - similar to the scent that wafts up when you spread some jam on a still warm roll. Warm, fruity, sweet, a little sour. Quickly, the Oud joins in. It pleasantly steps into the foreground without any animalic notes or being overly present. In the background, a certain citrus note can be perceived, which lightens the overall scent and provides a nice contrast to the fruity-sweet Oud + fruit combination. The longevity and sillage are also impressive. Definitely 10h+ - on clothing, much longer. With this fragrance, one is very strongly perceived; I would strongly advise against overspraying. Oudous Cerasus is quite dense due to the sweetness + Oud and might be a bit overwhelming for some over time. However, for Oud beginners (like me), it is definitely recommended, as the Oud used is really very pleasant. Thanks for reading :)

At first glance, I was hoping for a Eros Energy clone (see ZARA-HP: "A dynamic fragrance that radiates energy and character..."). However, that was obviously not the goal (see also fragrance notes). The opening is really nice, citrusy-peppery. I like it a lot, but it is by no means as striking as in very citrusy fragrances (e.g., Eros Energy). The drydown is then characterized by sandalwood and musk, with the apple adding a touch of sweetness. It smells fresh and clean to me. It fits quite well with sports or similar activities. Longevity and sillage are rather moderate; even when sprayed on clothing, the scent completely disappears within 9 hours, and on the skin, it goes very quickly, just a few hours, depending on the person). The bottle is nice with the frosted glass, but the spray head is poor for me (it dispenses little, has a strange pressure point, you first slide through, and then something comes out late).

As most of nishanes i have tried this perfume is a beast on longevity. The sillage is Aldo very good but the smell is subtle so It is not very noticeable. The note that i can smell the most here is the osmanthus flower. For me this is a perfume based un osmanthus with a background of different White flower and oatchouli and incense which makes the perfume deeper and more intebse. I find It a totally versatile perfume, unisex and weareable un every season and situación. Perfect for those Who are looking fora White flowers perfume without the tipical jasmine and tuberose.

First of all, a huge thank you to the lovely Irielle for this wonderful surprise! :D This fragrance is like a young woman who wants to seduce a man.. At first, she reapplies her lipstick - and whether you believe me or not, I can almost taste the red lipstick! - but she doesn’t show her sour side yet.. not yet ;) It starts off very, very raspberry. A raspberry that has fallen into vanilla yogurt.. and then it becomes a little game, a flirt.. sometimes you can catch a light breeze of bergamot, then you only smell ripe adult raspberries that could also be cherries, and at other times it just smells of vanilla with musk... this fragrance really leaves me with question marks.. :) But isn’t that what a man likes? The uncertain yet familiar? The slight naivety and yet somehow girlish..?! You could wear whatever you have nearby, sprayed on at a campsite or an open-air concert, and suddenly you become the cheerful heart girl.. So as a contrast, I could imagine wearing an open checkered shirt.. CONCLUSION: a nice, balanced fragrance that is fruity-floral-vanilla and yet somehow isn’t.. and from the lipstick, it has turned into a lip balm... :)

Beautiful rose - when I first tried it, it seemed normal, I don't know - maybe I didn't have the right day. We tried it again after 2 years - I don't know - maybe it has matured, or maybe I have matured. We went out - it was summer weather and my friend asked me, is that the Nishane?? It smells like fresh roses on Petrin Hill - where there is a rose garden. It's in Prague and it's a beautiful place - iconic. Full of roses. Yes there was a cloud of fresh roses around me and green chopped tones of rose stems and leaves - I was pleasantly surprised. Maybe it was a coincidence - I don't know, but since we only had a sample - I'll think about a whole bottle if it's reasonably priced. I was thinking - it will be one of those scents that is beautiful for a trip, just to go out, I probably found it too harsh at home, but outdoors - beautiful.

Very Sexy Now The Beauty of Brazil Victoria's Secret is a staple fragrance in time. I just started wearing it again after finding my confidence in wearing perfumes in my fragrance journey. Yes, it has a warm tropical beachy coconut (maybe coconut milk?) scent that’s equally mixed with papaya, preventing it from being too coconutty. The orchid note is merely a vessel to keep the fragrance going. In fact, after a first initial spray, I was afraid the orchid was going to remain strong after it took over for a moment. It faded to an ever-present support note that carries the subtle, almost expensive suntan lotion smell with a heat that slightly reminds me of honey. I look forward to the day we can all travel freely about the world again, and I can wear this while spending warm sunny days on the beach and exploring coastal cities I dream of visiting. I hope Victoria’s Secret brings this scent back, even if it is repackaged/rebranded, as the remaining perfumes available on third-party sites like eBay are expensive. Everyone should have the opportunity to experience this perfume.

It's Juicy Sexy and Delicious the opening starts with succulent Papaya Intoxicating Orchid and velvet Red Hibiscus with it's vibrant hue and milky coconut brings out the exotica from this perfume i just love the pink sunset color from this bottle I can imagine taking this with me to the islands of Bali with it's vast white sands clear turquoise Oceans acres and acres of Palm trees and a red sunset descending among the horizon between heaven and earth while an Ancient Temple wedges in the center. This scent is pure paradise.

During storms, trees, branches, and roots fall into rivers, and float down into the ocean, and then are washed ashore by the waves. The salty sea water transforms the color of the wood from brown to silver white. Sometimes, there is so much driftwood on the sand that the sand is invisible. Often this debris forms driftwood forts where one can shelter. But mostly, people build them by stacking logs like a pup tent. The driftwood filters out sound and sunlight and provides a sense of peace. Sandalwood Driftwood is a rare, discontinued perfume that has never appeared on markets outside of Spain. Little is known about this perfume, and the keynotes are unknown, apart from sandalwood and driftwood. The rest is all up to the wearer’s perception and sensation. This perfume was a revelation for me, bought blind on Vinted from a Spanish seller, since ZARA has never launched it on the Italian market. N°02 in the Jo Malone Ocean Collection, I would have expected something with a marine inclination, like Zara Ocean Nº1 - Salty Ocean Bouquet sibling. Instead, it surprised me like Zara Ocean Nº4 - Saffron Orange Flowers and Zara Ocean Nº3 - Caviar Bergamot, which are fresh and light like water, but without marine inflections. Specifically, Sandalwood Driftwood has whispers of salinity, but neither seaweed nor salt are the dominant theme. Bright, brilliant bergamot and bitter, tart lemon open this Jo Malone creation. It is vivid, pungent, like smelling the aroma of freshly cut green citrus. But this is not a citrus fragrance and the citrus accord lasts only for a few breaths, just long enough to awaken the senses from a momentary numbness. Little by little a slightly salty and woody accord rises, like the scent you breathe on a beach on a windy day, with the waves pushing the lifeless trunks of the trees adrift towards the shore, floating in the sea for an infinite time, and now they are beached on the shoreline. The more the perfume settles on the skin, the more the sides emerge sharp notes of sandalwood, which here closely resembles that used in other ZARA creations inspired by Santal 33 Eau de Parfum . This is a dry sandalwood, which those familiar with ZARA fragrances will have no trouble recognizing. In the heart there is they also feel some hints of straw and hay, probably due to a dried lavender, made less aromatic and more herbaceous. Surely there are slightly floral, spicy aspects, but I would say more than anything balsamic. And along with these woody accords, there is also a salty accord in the background. For a moment I doubted that the fragrance would take an aquatic direction, with strong influences of calone and algae. But fortunately, the marine accord is salty, that of ambergris , and all the modern molecules that reproduce the smell of salt. Adding a dewy facet is the rose, or a pink geranium, which here appears fresh and moist, not at all sweet and gelatinous. When the fragrance has reached the apex, and begins its descent towards the dry-down, delicate greenish, foliage accords emerge. The sandalwood takes over the whole scene, but instead of the creamy and warm traits, here it appears pungent, vigorous, which at times resembles wood shavings of cedar, with those typical slightly resinous nuances. On my skin this fragrance seems like a layering of Santal 33, the Sandalwood, with a marine and salty accord, the Driftwood. I don’t mind it at all, and I’m glad it has turned my fears and biases on their head. The best thing is to discover new sides from time to time that I hadn’t smelled before. As I interpret it, this fragrance is suitable for spring and summer days. So light, dry, and fresh it is perfect for both work and leisure occasions. If used indoors and during sports, it should not bother those passing by. The performance is excellent, as almost all of Jo Malone’s creations for ZARA. My interpretation is based on a bottle I have had since December 2024 (BC 13260). -Elysium

I have tried this perfume some month ago. I had no idea what nishane was but i felt un LOVE at the moment. This is one of the best Violet perfumes i have ever tried. It is very nice, sweet, intense and lasts forever. This is one of the most longlawting perfumes i have for sure. I recommend to try It yo all the flower lovers, this is a very good flowery one. It is not cheap but Two or three sprays are enough to smell It almost the whole day. There are oeople Who think that this scent is more in the femenine side but i find It totally unisex and i use It with no problems. I have even recived compliments wearing It. Very good job from nishanes House. Scent: 10 Longevity: 9.5 Sillage: 8 Versatility: 8 Quality/price: 6 (150€/50ml but very good quality extait de parfum) My personal raye: 10 (one of my favourite perfumes for sure) Average rate: 8.6

If I had to buy a bottle of anything from the Victoria's Secret range, Supermodel is the one I'd pick. Although a fruity floral (my least favourite fragrance genre), it is incredibly easy to like and wear. I find it nicely balanced and well-composed. It opens with a slightly sweet and syrupy peach schnapps accord and rich, red berries. It has an underlying hint of sensual and spicy vanilla throughout this composition, which is partly the reason as to why I enjoy wearing Supermodel so much. Although I agree that Supermodel is a somewhat cheesy name, I quite like it. After all, the faces of Victoria's Secret runway show are the world's most beautiful supermodels, so the name kind of fits. If only this fragrance had the magic ability to transform me into Gisele Bundchen with one simple spritz, then I'd be happy. I dare say, this fragrance is quite sexy. I could picture myself wearing this out clubbing or when I want to feel shrouded in an element of warmth. You won't hear me say that very often. So far, so good. It lasts reasonably well, and projects nicely. Not too loud nor too soft. The sweetness is well-balanced too. I think a few perfumistas, if game enough to try Supermodel, may find themselves pleasantly surprised. I urge anyone and everyone to give this fragrance a fair chance. I hear rumours that it has been discontinued. If that's so, then they need to bring it back. I can't see why any teeny-bopper in their right mind wouldn't buy this.

Encouraged by the green version with pistachio from this series, which does not smell like a children's perfume at all, I also tested this fragrance which was supposed to be in the JPG Le Beau style. And it already smells like a perfume for children, very childish. The opening hits with a very sweet bubble gum, from the notes I conclude that it is orange bubble gum - mega sweet, childish candy. This sugary bubble gum stays until the end, only weakens with time. When the top note fades, the orange is replaced by artificial, sweet coconut. It is a bit better later, orange blossom gives the scent quite bearable creaminess and smoothness at times, it softens this cloying sweetness, but what good does it do when it is already a stage very close to the skin when the scent fades. Generally, it smells a bit like bubble gum, a bit like candy, a bit like some artificial cookie. More for girls than boys. The scent is simple, very sweet, kitschy, but I don't rate it the worst for trying to smooth out the composition with creamy orange blossom. I recommend the version with pistachio in a green bottle for testing, which smells very similar to Moonlight Whisper and also to Kayali Yam Pistachio and has better longevity.

Sexy Little Things Ooh La La is a rather fun and flirty fragrance. To be completely honest, I'm not always in the mood to wear a scent like this, but whenever I have a sweet craving, this fragrance becomes a guilty pleasure. Sweet, sugary vanilla with a touch of pulpy mandarin orange, pretty much sums up this fragrance and the way it smells on my skin. If you don't mind the occasional toothache you get from something so sweet and gooey, then Sexy Little Things Ooh La La is perfect for you. Although a tad linear, this composition is not all that bad. I like its feminine and frivolous approach. Funnily enough, while wearing this fragrance today I had a sudden craving for a strawberry flavoured milkshake. I believe it was the scent's doing, as I'm not one to have those sudden food cravings. To my nose, Sexy Little Things Ooh La La is a vanilla gourmand. Many will find this fragrance sexy, perhaps even being a hit with most men. It's nothing totally unique, but still captivating. The vanilla accord is light and fluffy, the way vanilla should be. In terms of anything sweet, I find this fragrance tolerable. It will ultimately appeal to the younger segment of the population, however I think older women might enjoy wearing this one too. The sillage is fairly strong, and the longevity, although a little temperamental at times, lasts a fair while. I'm quite surprised, in a good way.

Victoria's Secret SEXY LITTLE THINGS OOH LA LA is a minimalist vanilla fragrance which essentially features vanilla. No development here, just mild vanilla flanked by mild citrus and very mild floral (I would have been hard pressed to identify which floral: cherry blossom, according to the listed notes...) . Not too sweet, nor overpowering, OOH LA LA is a pleasant scent which would be welcomed by some vanilla lovers. Now the burning question: are any of the Sexy Little Thing perfumes by VS really "sexy"? No doubt the concept is open to interpretation, but I found SLT, SLT NOIR and SLT OOH LA LA to be pretty, accessible, and amicable. These are not sizzlingly sensuous scents by any stretch of the imagination... (IMNSHO)

~ Inspiration ~ While browsing through the Victoria's Secret perfumes, I also noticed "Sexy Little Things - Ooh la la" and promptly added it to my wishlist. I received a sample from Mia777 in a swap. ~ Bottle ~ This simple glass bottle isn't particularly pretty; it looks more like a drugstore fragrance. The name of the perfume is written in a simple, slightly slanted script on the front, with a curled ribbon underneath. ~ Scent ~ It starts off fruity and zesty with mandarin oranges, until cherry blossoms give it a subtle floral expression shortly thereafter, and it finishes sensually, warmly, and slightly gourmand with creamy vanilla. ~ Longevity ~ On my skin, it lasts about 3-4 hours (a bit longer on clothing and hair). 3-4 sprays are appropriate without being overwhelming. ~ Occasion ~ It fits well into the mild and cooler days and evenings in spring and autumn. It also works as an office scent without being too intrusive.

There's a cult-like following for this, and I can see why - it's a pretty powdery-floral vanilla. Blended well so no notes stick out. Cozy, sweet, comforting. But... there are two fragrances that are more affordable + much easier to find + very similar to Parfums Intimes - Cashmere: Vanilla Jasmine : 1) Anatomy of a Fragrance - Orchid Vanille - although I don't think they meant to create a dupe, this is identical! Don't shell out more money for Cashmere Vanilla Jasmine, without testing Orchid Vanille. Plus it lasts forever, with strong projection. 2) Fresh Vanilla Blossoms - not identical, but still super similar. In my opinion, it's even prettier than Parfums Intimes - Cashmere: Vanilla Jasmine and Anatomy of a Fragrance - Orchid Vanille . Yes, seriously! So don't spring for Parfums Intimes - Cashmere: Vanilla Jasmine (super hard to find and expensive now!), without trying these two first.

Cashmere Vanilla Jasmine is a beautiful and cosy fragrance. Just like an expensive cashmere robe, the scent is warm, luxurious and soft. It has turned out to be a lot better than I originally expected. I really like the concept behind this series, and I think the name is well-suited to this fragrance. The vanilla and jasmine go together perfectly, with a smooth muskiness that somewhat resembles another cashmere inspired fragrance, Donna Karan's Cashmere Mist. Although casual and relaxed, Cashmere Vanilla Jasmine could be worn just about anywhere. I personally find it to be rather sensual, so wearing it on a romantic date is not out of the question. The vanilla in this fragrance is not sweet, but more smooth and cuddly. Without smelling like soap, Cashmere Vanilla Jasmine does have a slightly clean quality, which is pleasant rather than offensive. I think many will enjoy this subtlety. So far, this is my favourite Victoria's Secret fragrance. I am so very disappointed that it has since been discontinued. I do hope that it's still available both online and on Ebay. It was one crazy move to get rid of this fragrance, even if it wasn't a best seller. The sillage is intimate, however the longevity is good. If you're like me and enjoy the scent of vanilla and/or jasmine, then you're sure to be impressed. The two dominant accords have been blended beautifully in a way that is both breath-taking and wearable.

Wood, wood, and more wood... and it's a fluffy, soft wood that I absolutely LOVE... and I don't even like wood! Lovely, sweet, non-indolic jasmines wafting along with the vanilla. No foody stuff, no over-crowding of too many notes or an ambition to be oh-so-different... Just a clean, silky wood and that beautiful fragrant, vanillic flower. This is a bewitching perfume I cherish with all my heart. Some may balk at it but that sort of makes me happy. That way I can have all the left over bottles of this discontinued gem all to myself!!:)

Originally reviewed on April 15, 2012: Victoria’s Secret has a way of taking fragrant gems and trading them in for of-the-moment pop fads and diabetic-shock-inducing confections that last no longer than a year. I understand the company does have to expand and change as its age demographic expands and changes but too often they throw out the babe with the bath water. In this case Breathless is the precocious babe with much potential that got tossed on its rear to make way for something generic and sugar-berry scented. At the start Breathless is a relatively authentic orange blossom-y fragrance amplified, thanks to a heavy dose of orange blossom (not listed), neroli, and citruses. Nice, but the same can be said about Sung, Henri Bendel Orange Blossom & Jasmine, Sanborn’s Orange Blossom Cologne and many, many more. Wait it out a few minutes and be rewarded with the most sensual—if not flat-out sexual—your-skin-but-infinitely-better musk. It’s reminiscent of J. Lo’s Glow. However, Glow incorporates the scent of freshly scrubbed naked skin, the towel that is wrapped around the naked skin, the dryer sheet that’s still attached to the towel, the moisturizer on the naked skin, the shampoo, the conditioner … to the point the wearer has forgotten about the naked skin. Breathless is about freshly washed naked skin, out of the shower without a towel, and a significant other who cannot keep his or her hands to themselves. It’s naughty and fun, as should be expected from Victoria’s Secret, purveyors of lacy, silky, sexy naughtiness. Breathless is satisfyingly long-lasting and thank goodness for that; I love the subtle sweetness of my skin, but better, here. It leaves a sexy trail that will have many asking, “What is that bewitching scent?” I found myself catching whiffs of this scent, smiling, and feeling a million times sexier than I felt before I put this on. Surprising myself on October 9, 2023: Why am I surprised? My thoughts mostly remain the same for this. I was annoyed that VS got rid of this, a scent that didn't smell like an umbrella-adorned alcoholic frilly drink or candy. This smelled like something that matched perfectly with the bras they were selling. The only theory I can come up with: it was analogous to Glow and Glow was in danger of being dated and "old fashioned," thus Breathless was dated and "old fashioned." I loved Breathless . I might have been talking out of my backside when I claimed the neroli/orange blossom/citrus was natural smelling. There are citruses aplenty here in California, so I know how they smell. Breathless is hardly natural smelling. That said, it opens with unmistakable neroli/orange blossom/citrus. If that's your kind of thing, this provides a fun ride. Above all, Breathless is all about musk. The musk is simultaneously clean and skanky—what is eluded is post-shower coitus muskiness. This is the kind of musk you spray on before you put on your lacy VS bra and undie set. I'm sure spraying said lingerie set was encouraged. It's a great marketing ploy, so why they discontinued this is beyond me. I still have a large bottle. I don't wear it often but I can't bear the thought of getting rid of it. Sometimes, I'm in the mood to wear it; sometimes, it's too skanky for my taste or it's too frilly and twee. Sometimes, it's all of the above and I pass over it for something more neutered and unisex, like Aqua Allegoria Forte Mandarine Basilic . For anyone who enjoys something like Aqua Allegoria Mandarine Basilic but wants more sex in their bottle, go for a reasonably priced Breathless on eBay.

This not easily obtainable gem landed in my hands on the occasion of my birthday; I had been waiting for it for a long time and was anxious and nervous about whether this little potion would meet my fragrance expectations. Unfortunately, I didn't have a chance to test it beforehand. It was a relief that the scent is exactly what I had expected (after extensive internet research). This is a summery citrus bomb. Surely some of you may have a toilet spray association with the initial burst - and even for a few minutes afterward. You really have to like that. The scent reminds me of Malibu Lemon Blossom by Pacifica, but with much better longevity. What is listed in the fragrance pyramid as mandarin actually smells more like lemon to my nose, and that scent lasts from beginning to end, supported by a sweetness from a few white flowers, but always juicy and fresh. I can't wait for the hot summer days when this fragrance will be the perfect companion, but I've already used it now - for a refreshing kick in between and for the feeling of just stepping out of a complete wash cycle from the washing machine. Clean and cheerful and fresh. In my opinion, Breathless is an atypical representative of the Victoria's Secret genre, where you usually find sweet fruity-floral scents that are more youthful (and, as I see it, interchangeable). This "clean" laundry lemon dances a bit out of line. Much to my delight. Anyone who loves citrus-fresh can confidently go for it. However, those looking for a complex scent will find themselves in the wrong place - what you see is what you get :).

The smell is one of the only VS Pink body sprays I've found that I like. I feel like it's a typical body spray; basic scent and barely any lasting power. The smell is strong with sugar and cinnamon, and there's a back scent of pastries and butter that gives it a little more complexity. Works really well as a before-bed scent - not too strong or long-lasting to disrupt your sleep! If you know what to expect from a body mist, I'd say this is a pretty good scent to try.

After seeing the new release, I was so excited. It arrived and... This has nothing to do with the yummy notes writed on the bottle (soft serve, shortcake crumbles, candy coating) , the scent is neither candy-ish nor strawberry scented. This is soooo synthetic!! it even reminds me of sweet like candy by ari with a minty note, it's synthetically sweet and weirdly minty - fresh. The worst disappointment ever, coming from a strawberry lover and collector...

I'm a citrus snob. Growing up around citrus trees raises the bar for citrus fragrance expectations - sometimes making it difficult to find accurate portrayals of citrus. Luckily, "Bombshell Amalfi | Victoria's Secret" is a very realistic citrus - but there's more to it than that. It opens with a true-to-life tangerine, but not just the juice: you get the whole fruit - with sun-kissed, slightly-bitter rind intact. It's very refreshing, and I imagine picking a ripe tangerine straight off the tree - with freshly-juiced/zested tangerines nearby. Very quickly, a sweet musk moves in. Based on testing/comparing the notes from the other flankers in this line ( "Bombshell Santorini | Victoria's Secret" and "Bombshell St. Tropez | Victoria's Secret" ), I'm guessing this is meant to be a creative interpretation of peony. But it's not the typical peony note Victoria's Secret is famous for, as it lacks the watery/aquatic quality like previous note iterations. It's more sweet than floral, and the touch of musk seems to be a new addition. Interestingly, the musk does make it feel more "beachy": something that feels sandy, and a bit like sunbaked skin. This last element was drastically different between the tester strip and my skin, so "your mileage may vary". On a tester strip: a subtle driftwood became present in the dry-down; very dry and quiet. On my skin: the woody note felt more like subtle driftwood, paired with a very loud and heavily-animalic sandalwood. This blend was so animalic that it skirted the line of feeling like body odor, and dominated the citrus (to me it was a breakdown of 60% animalic sandalwood/20% tangerine/10% sweet musk). One spray on my wrist, and the sillage + projection were both very powerful. Even covering my wrist up with a long sleeve jacket, I could smell it through the fabric strongly - and couldn't seem to escape that animalic accord. When it was finally time for me to shower, I ended up needing to scrub my wrist multiple times with Dawn dish soap afterwards to fully remove the fragrance - and could still smell faint hints of it. The next day (a full 24 hours later), it was still strongly present on my jacket sleeve - despite only spraying on my wrist, and not the fabric. So if you're looking for a "skanky"/animalic citrus blend for summer with performance, this might be a great choice! But if you're like me and generally avoid animalic notes, I'd strongly recommend testing this in store like I did - to prevent any skin chemistry surprises. P.S. If you're looking for more refreshing citrus scents for summer, I wrote a blog post about this: https://www.parfumo.com/Users/Gourmandgrl/Blog/Article/sweet-citrus-scents-for-summer

Mirabilis is a complex yet simple noted, modern fragrance that challenges traditional perfumery with its molecular approach. • Dominant notes: Ambroxan, synthetic musk, and vanilla • Subtle undertones: Incense and earthy elements • Texture: Soft, powdery, and abstract • Performance: Moderate sillage and longevity The scent opens with a sweet vanilla embrace before evolving into a blend of synthetic musk and earthy tones. It’s described as ethereal yet grounded, evoking images of vanilla skies and modern boardrooms simultaneously. Mirabilis is an ambiguous fragrance that elicits mixed reactions. Some find it comforting and easy to wear, while others perceive it as clinical or sterile. It’s designed for those who appreciate abstraction in fragrances, requiring multiple wearings to fully grasp its nuanced layers. Overall, Mirabilis is a whisper rather than a shout in the world of perfumery, inviting wearers to discover its secrets through contemplation and repeated use.

Crepusculum Mirabile is a sensual dance between jasmine and creamy sandalwood, a perfect harmony between floral freshness and woody softness. From the first notes, jasmine opens with all its richness, but it’s in its meeting with sandalwood that the magic happens: creamy and round, it wraps the jasmine in a comforting and sensual warmth. It’s a fragrance that asserts itself as a calming, magnetic presence. A warm beauty, a tranquil sensuality, like a sunset drowned in the colors of the night.

I suspected I didn’t care for jasmine scents, and I think this was a reminder. The opening is a sharp jasmine, but it softens in time and smells lighter/soapier. It’s a bit non-descript, I guess. With so many options for jasmine fragrances on the market, I definitely wouldn't choose this one. I’m sampling the La Botanique range, and it’s my first experience with L’artisan Parfumeur. It seems to me that all of them are pretty weak in sillage and longevity. They peak very quickly and are essentially indetectible in 30 minutes. I hope to find a few with more staying power. My boyfriend: “It smells generic. I have no thoughts on this.” Lol

You can never go wrong with fewer notes than more and this is proof of it. L'Artisan parfumeur spotlights jasmine as this floral beauty that unfurls its petals to the nose of its wearer. At the beginning, she's sharp and floral, with a facet of fruitiness like white-gold. She borders on indolic and powdery territory, but avoids going in too deep. After awhile, it's the creamy facet of jasmine, paired with sandalwood and tonka beans that appear. There's sweetness, a slightly woody aspect and the powdery floral jasmine takes over. All in all, it's a pretty linear fragrance that is light, almost soapy with florals and a touch of woody sandalwood. It's a safe blind-buy and a more refined, adult version of Flora Gorgeous Jasmine . I also really love the Botanical collection bottles which I find classic with a touch of elegant refinement. I'm not the biggest fan of wearing jasmine on myself which is why it won't make it into my collection, but I'm glad I got to try this quiet but sophisticated fragrance!

I learned from this perfume world that when a perfume has low ratings and not hyped it’s gonna be very good :-) This is another case, omg, this house is just a step above the majority of other niche houses, everything they put out is so classy, natural, refined. This is a milkshake of jasmine and soap. I can’t describe it better. Very soapy clean and creamy and the jasmine is so beautiful and natural, like when you walk close to a plant of jasmine. The best way to imagine it is a cream of soap, jasmine and soft woods. Absolutely amazing. Not for the geeks of strong dark perfumes with oud ambar patchouli rose etc etc, this is white, clean and creamy.

The unexpectedly spring-like weather in Boston must be what is driving me to don violets, violets, and more violets. Usually April is all about frozen rain, but not this year. Violets are the perfect springtime flower. Clean, slightly sweet, natural-smelling and refreshing. Violet soliflores are a perfect alternative to colognes. In fact, violet soliflores really are colognes, especially when they have the longevity of L'Artisan Parfumeur VERTE VIOLETTE! I love this scent, but I have to say that the longevity is the poorest of the nineteenth-century-style soliflores familiar to me, including Borsari VIOLETTA DI PARMA and Berdoues VIOLETTES DE TOULOUSE. This composition is very close to those, according to my nose, and so anyone who likes any of the three will like the others as well, it seems to me. These are all slightly green and not at all sugary, while still being a bit sweet. Pricewise, the Borsari and the Berdoues are the way to go, but I picked up a large bottle of VERTE VIOLETTE at the recent L'Artisan sale, and I do not regret having done so. The bottle is labeled eau de toilette, but to me this is a cologne. Of course, I feel the same way about the Borsari, which is labeled eau de parfum! The problem may be with the ionones used to reproduce the scent of violets. Apparently, they block olfactory receptors, masking the scent to the wearer. It's possible, then, that others can smell this on me, though I do not smell anything at all after a couple of hours.

This one felt "eh". It's a violet leaf soliflore nothing exciting or special. The price you pay for this scent is not worth the incredibly small amount of time you get with it. There are way cheaper alternatives to this scent. Edit: It's a little less "eh" after it warms up and the Iris comes out to play, shyly. I still don't think it's worth the dough but if you like a soliflor of violet leaves with a hint of Iris before it fades, and you can afford the reapplications, then you might want to give it a go. Oct 25 2013

When Verte Violette was still in production, the L’Artisan Parfumeur website had categorized it as a violet soliflore - a single-note violet perfume. Described as a "green violet" fragrance, this scent beautifully balances delicate, sweet violet flowers with the fresh, green essence of violet leaves. The violets are complemented by a subtle, powdery iris note that adds depth and softens its overall character. Verte Violette's simple, classic charm makes it a cute and timeless scent that’s always in style.

This fragrance opens with green yet powdery violet. The unique green freshness is almost melon-like and vaguely reminds me of Fleur de Liane. Violet’s powdery floral smell is often plasticine-like and I detect a faint trace of this particular aspect in the background of the fragrance. It works rather well in this composition, as it tames the melon-y freshness. This part of the accord gradually loses intensity though never disappears from the development. A subtle woodsy note takes its place as the main base for the violet. Light and unobtrusive – diametrically opposed to Balenciaga Paris – this scent is well-suited for a warm spring or summer day. Lasts roughly four hours on my skin.

...lovely chimes" - in storm and rain, in cold and darkness, spring has suddenly arrived. It closed my eyes, tickled the corners of my mouth, sneaked past my scent receptors on its way to my heart, the shimmering blue-green speckled ribbon fluttering behind it, floating and caressing, gently stroking my soul and stealing me away from time, from the reality that shakes its head at me and admonishes me to stay in the here and now, at the beginning of winter, on the eve of the 1st Advent, in the darkness of my room with my nose on my wrist, humming Heinrich Heine's little spring song... Infinitely delicate, infinitely soft, infinitely clear and pure, a violet blooms on my skin, so distinct and powdery and creamy in its scent, that I cannot believe, that I do not want to believe, that I am dealing with a figment of my imagination, a mirage that will disappear as soon as I reach out my hand to touch it, the fine violet-blue petals, glowing in the mild, warm spring sun, whose rays warm my skin after the long, cold, gray winter. There are ball gowns that are adorned with crystals. There are luxury houses and villas that immediately reveal their owners belong to the "higher society." There are situations and things that compel a person to dress in a certain way, to behave "properly," to own certain brands, to prefer certain resorts, and to smell of beautiful, expensive, opulent perfumes.

Glittery pictures of chubby angels, hand-painted bouquets (or alternatively Ottifanten), "In all four corners love must be found" and of course: the sayings. Tried a sample (which btw has a really horrible sprayer and you can’t enjoy the fragrance and check its performance properly) and yes, it’s similar to: - Tuscan Leather - Suede et Safran - Mirsaal of Trust - Ombre Leather - La Yukawam - a huge etc… The only difference is the raspberry note which is very prominent, sweetier and fruitier than the others. The Cuir Grenat is a beautiful soft leather scent that unfortunately lacks durability and sillage. At least on my skin. The fragrance is compared to Tuscan Leather Eau de Parfum and "London (Extrait de Parfum) | Widian / AJ Arabia," which I cannot confirm. No, the Cuir Grenat stands on its own but carries a similar DNA. Only 3 fragrance notes are listed here, and those are exactly what you perceive. In fact, nothing else. You have leather, raspberry, and ambrofix as a fixative, and that's it. The scent starts with the leather note, which is very nicely balanced. There is no overpowering leather note here, and in the drydown, which is reached after a few minutes, the raspberry joins in but is by no means in the foreground; rather, it acts subtly in the background. The whole thing is perceivable close to the skin for 2 hours on my skin, and then the scent disappears. And that is very, very unfortunate because the balance of the notes is very good. The fragrance itself is also perfectly unisex. It is suitable for anyone looking for a scent that is more in the background and only perceivable close to the skin. Delicate and fine.
