I wouldn't buy a bottle because personally, I find it lacking in power and performance. Fragrance 8/10 H/S 5

First off...I Love Irises. true beauties of my garden they pop, on their own schedule and delight me with their robust color in the fullness of late Spring. They are tall slender and truly gorgeously indigo...I would love to be reincarnated, at least once, as an iris-divine! Additionally, they impart such a fantastic array of clean, powdery and earthy-carrot-like notes to many of my favorite fragrances. But...Alas, this was definitely not my HG Iris. It was very stifled dusty and rigid and immediately images of 'Downton Abbey' started to pop into my head. This is a very stately and complete composition, don't get me wrong. However...it was so constricting, formal and unimaginative, I felt very saddened upon smelling it. I just want it to go back into the crypt from which it came and disappear like the old "Anne of green Gables ", "Upstairs, Down Stairs" or "Brides' Head Revisited" Sagas on BBC. I guess, from my various Television references you get the picture of the mood this portrays. I felt as if this fragrance had been stored in someone's Grandmother's belongs chest and sunk on the titanic and some how kept dry very dry, in fact and then just opened and exposed to fresh air seconds before I sniffed it. There was nothing innovative, sexy, kinetic or even remotely artistically inspiring about this fragrance...which is so unfortunate, because I believe iris is one of the most beautiful flowers, as well as, fragrance notes; however, its light has not been ignited in this composition. Blah!

L'Artisan Parfumeur IRIS PALLIDA is a beautiful woody iris composition with the emphasis on the iris rather than the wood. The iris showcased is the flower itself, not the roots, so this creation is not dark and earthy at all. Instead, it is light and limpid. Among the niche iris perfumes I've tried, IRIS PALLIDA may be closest to TDC BOIS D'IRIS, but the latter is far more woody. IRIS PALLIDA seems relatively simple and linear, but the notes are perfectly blended. I would like to be able to say that I love IRIS PALLIDA, and perhaps I do for the short duration of its existence on my skin. After a couple of hours, however, not even the faintest trace remains, making this a no-go for me. I wish that L'Artisan would take seriously the ubiquitous criticisms of the ephemerality of their offerings. The quality here is beyond dispute, but I expect much better longevity than most of the L'artisan line-up delivers.

Actually, I usually write comments only after I have gotten to know a fragrance a bit. But this time I am making an exception and describing my very first encounter with this scent. There is a reason for this: I haven't particularly liked iris fragrances so far, as the powdery sweetness often gives me headaches. But this fragrance has gently introduced me to the theme, even though the confrontation at the end of the exciting scent development is quite direct for me. For anyone needing a 'crash course' in understanding powdery iris, I can warmly recommend 'Iris Pallida'... ;-) The scent meets my skin, a rush of anise comes towards me, causing me to almost flinch for a moment, then I curiously sniff at my wrist. But by then it is already retreating, leaving behind a briefly shimmering silver-gray light trail in the morning twilight and then blending into the overall composition of the morning air. I follow the trail and find myself in front of a lake. Thick fog hangs over it, a dark green, damp, moldy smell of violet leaf and iris root rises from it. Slowly the sun begins to rise, obscured by the fog, a light gray glow full of mystique and magic. After half an hour, the sun gains strength and the dense, humid clouds gradually lift, but the air remains hazy, a delicate mist lies like a gossamer veil over the lake, as if it does not want to fully reveal its secrets. A gentle, powdery scent rises, and now I can see it - the iris. It unfolds its petals and radiates ever more brightly in the light. I look closer and recognize a nymph; she is enchantingly young, has velvety white skin, yet radiates something ancient. She never sheds her veils, but they are so diaphanous that every curve of her sensual body can be sensed. It is slowly getting warmer; after another hour, woody notes dance around the powdery mist that now fills the entire air. The scent invites me to linger, and I step onto the freshly dried cedar wood dock that leads slightly out over the lake, where the green, marshy smells of the shore are no longer perceptible. The nymph is not shy at all; curiously, she comes closer and lies down beside me. Two more hours pass, during which I can feel her presence and the iris scent becomes increasingly prominent. It is pleasantly warm, not hot or humid, more like a beautiful sunny day in late summer. A very gentle patchouli and a hint of vetiver bathe everything in golden light, which, over the next 1.5 hours, is increasingly overshadowed by white musk. Are her veils what smell so intensely of musk and iris? Playfully, I drape a corner of the veil over my face; the light around me becomes ever brighter, it does not blind me, but I can no longer perceive the lake. I feel enveloped by the veils, losing my orientation and getting a headache. So much iris and white musk, it is simply too powdery for me. I try to free myself from the veils, and then the nymph takes my hand and pulls me close to her. It has now probably been a total of 6 hours, which is why the scent draws me so close to the skin - her skin, which is so thin that it appears translucent and shimmers light violet. She pulls my head onto her shoulder, and I can relax. Suddenly it becomes clear to me: the iris is a heart scent! It is not about hot love and burning passion, but about a very warm, enduring, golden glowing joy in the heart that spreads within me almost like liquid fragrance. With a jolt, my headache disappears; I gently detach myself from her embrace, only occasionally bringing my wrist to my nose to seek out that heart feeling again. Then the musk bids farewell, and the nymph lies down to sleep in a bed of vetiver and patchouli, where she slowly fades away.

super cute! i don't typically love scents like these since i'm not a fruity scent lover, but this is a nice guilty-pleasure kind of fragrance. to me, it's like a milder version of the og, which is too sharp to me. i wouldn't say any of the notes are distinctly recognizable to me, it's just a very sweet, slightly tart fruity scent. it's definitely a juvenile scent so it's perfect for girls in middle/high school but this is the kind of scent i don't see anyone actively hating. longevity and sillage are average, but that makes this perfect for a year-round scent--it's not too overwhelming for warm weather but it's sweet enough for cool weather

This is a very western rose, so its smell is very fresh, airy, it’s not a heavy dense middle eastern rose. I thought it was going to be feminine but for me no. The citruses make it very sparkling and fresh. As everything from the house, smells very natural, refined and classy. Smells like you’ve atomized water on fresh garden roses. I’ve smelled a lot of rose perfumes and they share a lot of similarities, so this is nothing innovative or very different, but i would wear this rose instead of others, cause it smells natural, fresh, light and wearable for a man.

After testing a sample, I learned that this fragrance had been discontinued. From the opening, I detect very green and heady notes, like aniseed, perhaps verbena, or green notes, or both combined, which dominate the other notes. The fragrance remains at this stage until the end, which is linear and unusual. The sillage is quite strong and the longevity is respectable at around 10 hours. Ideal for summer if you are looking for a sweet and fresh fragrance, which is rare. Do not buy blind. A discontinued product which, in my opinion, is not a great loss.

On one of my regular visits to Zara just to smell their fragrances, I decided to go take a look at the children's ones. Anna from Frozen smells deliciously good, despite being classified as children's I bought it for my own use. It opens fresh with the declared floral notes of orchid and peony and then a creamy and non-synthetic vanilla persists, very pleasant to wear! I think every fan of the vanilla note should try it. It's an uncomplicated scent and sometimes that's what you want to wear. It gives me warmth when drying.

I've got to admit, this one is a pretty unusual fragrance. Tested it out at the Rennaï (a new shop that opened at the RoyalMount in Montreal) and was pleasantly surprised by it. Sought out a sample at Etiket and here I am. At first, I get sweetened citruses. They're more on the subtle side than on that tangy, fresh zing you often get from citruses. Doesn't take long before tonka bean appears and this time, it's on the almond, almost powdery side. I don't really detect cauliflower, but the fragrance remains in the fresher territory, never going too sweet or too cloying. It's kind of hard to describe exactly how the scent goes. I'd say it's in the same territory as Lumière Blanche : almondy, powdery with some lovely citruses. Not quite a skin scent, but certainly not a strong fragrance. It has that soothing, calming quality to it and brings me comfort when I wear it. I'll be testing out my remaining decant and pondering on whether I'll get myself a full bottle. A very lovely discovery from L'Artisan Parfumeur!

Oud Wood. This is without a doubt my favourite fragrance from the Tom ford Private Blend Collection. Now I know many people roll their eyes when they hear any mention of Tom Ford's famously over-priced fragrance collection, however though I have to express my love for Oud wood which stands out on its own as something which I believe is incredibly sexual and conjured up images of Eroticism and Passion. The initial spray on to my skin is a very creamy oud which is unexpected because I was expecting something harsh and very masculine, i was expecting something very spicey and very "hard" but instead it seems as though the Oud and vanilla have created a marriage which has resulted in the Oud transforming into something very creamy, as if it were literally dripping vanilla. Rosewood, Tonka and Pepper further heighten the fragrance offering something a bit more complex and alot more "adult". Oud Wood isn't the most original scent but it wins points with its incredible and unashamed sexiness and its fantastic lasting power. This fragrance is a testiment to what I love so much about fragrances, because it communicates with me not only through my nose but through my emotions. I cant help but feel like a naughty school boy all over again when I wear this. It makes me want to be mischevious, it makes me want to be passionate, it makes me want to be physical. Whilst i believe that some of Tom ford's scents are severely over-priced. Oud Wood is worth every single penny.

Oud tends to be the gorilla in the room in a fragrance that uses it as the principle note. Oud being both potent and distinctive, the challenge is how to make an oud-centric perfume fundamentally different than any other. This isn’t only Tom Ford’s challenge. Oud is the It-Girl still, and here lies the other problem. The oud trend has been going on for long enough that its moment is getting a little long in the tooth. The smart niche companies that were touting oud for the past 4-5 years are moving on, but the high end designer lines (Dior,Versace, Armani) and the niche lines that don’t see themselves as niche lines but (trumpets...) Houses (Killian, Kurkdjian) missed the memo. My point is not at all that the perfumes are bad, but that seeing the trend as a function of marketing, the glass house of exclusivity and taste is looking a little fragile. All the $200-$500 exclusive ouds are competing with each other, but they’re also competing with much less expensive, well-made oud perfumes also available. Exclusivity is a fiction that style-merchants are constantly busting their asses to maintain, and the market is famously fickle. My bet is that the oud star is falling. An large part of the above scenario is price. Rare Vietnamese oud, ancient Cambodian treasured oud... You’ve never heard anyone refer to rare ethylmaltol, and for good reason. Where is all this oud coming from? Oud isn’t quite ambergris, whose formation is measured in decades to centuries, but you don’t plant it one season and harvest it the next. As with every other quality of smell that we refer to in perfume, oud, the note, and oud, the material are not the same thing. A product that is much more expensive than its direct competitors (a $400 by Killian perfume v. a $100 Parfumerie Generale perfume) require a certain justification, and whether the company is Chanel or Whole Foods, the rare sourcing of botanical components is the contemporary grail of sophistication among the consumer. Ivory, gems, elephant skin, milk fed veal. The exclusivity of Empire has given way to exclusivity AND ethics. ‘Please don’t spill your acai martini on my ipe wood floor and cause a stain. Though it’s sustainably grown, I’ve spent years monitoring the webcast of the organic, high altitude farm where I commissioned its growth. Don’t put me through THAT again.” And here we have oud. All the sophistication of ambergris, none of the ethical indecision. We’re perfect prey for the oud-mongers. Tom Ford’s Oud Wood starts out much like many other eponymous oud perfumes I’ve smelled, but from the very outset has a quality of softened edges and rounded tones. [ Caveat: I don’t have much of a nose or mind for dissecting the notes in oud, although I’ve smelled many oud perfumes. I’ve even had the opportunity, thanks to a friend sharing his stash, of doing a comparison sniffing of a number of quality pieces of Vietnamese and Cambodian oud wood whose very specific provenances were know by the person who collected them. I tend to take oud in as a whole. It’s a lovely, sensual experience. But in my case it also means I’m not much of an analyst.] This is a perfume that makes me question the difference between modulating something very particular and strong (oud), and going mainstream. At all points in Oud Wood’s progression it reads as within normal limits, a nursing expression used to describe a quantity not low and not high. Within normal limits: is that the goal? If so, it’s achieved. This fragrance would appeal to a large population, perfume fans and otherwise. Normally I would deride a goal of normalcy-above-all-else, but Oud Wood is wonderfully constructed, and despite the oud name, is a principally woody fragrance that modulates sweetness, smokiness, firmness and softness. It’s blended but specific, and smells like an imagined wood in the way that an abstract floral fragrance like Heeley’s Ophelia or the classic Patou Joy suggests an idealized flower. Does Oud Wood have all the brutal smokiness, bitterness, and slap-in-the-face often associated with oud? No, but find this modulated quality refreshing given the ‘my oud’s bigger than your oud’ competitiveness that characterized some oud fragrances released around the time of Oud Wood (2007). The most appealing use of oud in a perfume is to make it a note among many (ie. Guerlain Habit Rouge edp). Perfumer Richard Herpin pushes oud more to the center of the stage than this, but applies moderation deliberately to the composition and gives us the subtle but forthright Oud Wood. from scent hurdle.com

I've tried oud wood off and on over the last 10-15 years and its progressively gotten weaker and weaker and weaker. My most recent bottle, which was given to me as a gift (wasn't going to spend my own money on it) lasts AT MOST 30 minutes on my skin before it fades away to nothingness and can hardly be smelled. Forget about projection, this fragrance has 0 sillage, nothing, zilch, nada. This bottle was from Nordstrom, so it's authentic. The fact that they're charging $400 for this watered down garbage is disgusting and the definition of corporate greed. the one upside is that it smells absolutely incredible, and i've yet to smell anything else like it. Do not spend your hard earned money on this trash in 2023.

Oud Wood is more about woods than oud; it opens with a balsamic, somehow cold and almost “piney” blast of aromatic wood, supported by a quite realistic almondy tonka note, vanilla and just a shade of oud. The wood here is really invigorating, fresh, much aromatic too, in a way I almost never smelled it before. Plus, the texture is really peculiar in my opinion: Oud Wood is not as much sweet or “rich” as it may seem, on the contrary it appears to be really sharp, clean, thin, “woody” in a realistic, but slightly “industrial” meaning, if that makes sense (think of Ikea furniture). The name as I said is a bit misleading to me, as the oud is far less detectable than the wood; and also it has the same features of the oud in M7, which means it’s not the usual dark-rubbery-smoked and “animalic” note we’re used to, but here is rather more oily, nutty, slightly medicinal, and more “bright” than you may imagine. It is a bit smoky, but in a far more gentle way than usual. Overall Oud Wood is a really pleasant, versatile, masculine and easy going scent: it is classy, but at the same time “generic” enough to be safe for anyone in any situation. Actually perhaps one of the most generic and less creative among the Private Blend line for what I’ve tested so far – I don’t mean to say that with a negative connotation. Finally, I must agree with what several other reviewers stated on the Web: it is quite close to skin and the longevity on skin is really unacceptable for the price, while on clothes it lasts longer and projects quite well. A nice fresh and refined Oriental woody scent unworthy the cost in my opinion, but a nice one I’d keep and use if someone gave it to me as a gift. 6,5-7/10

I've tried Tobacco Vanille , which I know many people love, and I love this even more. I think it's sexier. This is (arguably) worth the hype and even the price tag. It is beautiful, it's seductive, it's quality, but I find it more intimate (and definitely more sensual..) than Tobacco Vanille. I can't see how many people would dislike this. It's quite appealing. The fragrance is based around an oud note, but I think it would be unfair to expect a loud blast of agarwood a la Arabesque, or in real Arabian style. No. This is Oud for western sensibilities, almost tuned down for people who don't like loud, in-your-face oud. To be honest, I don't expect this to be loud, it's very subtle, very sensual, and very sexy. It sits very close to the skin and doesn't project so far, so it's more of a scent that people who come up really close to you will go "wow, you smell incredible" kind of thing. What I like about this is that it isn't your average rose/oud combination, it's oud but done with tonka bean, lavish vanilla, sandalwood and amber, coupled with a beautiful, beautiful rosewood note. I do recommend this one a lot. The only drawbacks in my opinion would be the projection. It's an Eau de Parfum and it sits very close to the skin. But, it's not one to announce your presence, it's an experience to share with that special person in your life, when they are close enough to smell and feel the warmth of your skin. It's a "melt in your arms" kind of scent. In one word? Romantic. Worth it? I think so... just really nice stuff.

I re- bought Oud wood few months ago (22 batch if i'm not wrong) and unfortunately the performance (especially the projection) is not good compared to my 2017 batch.. Actually the new bottle has a very bad performance.... Very sad for such a nice fragrance! ........................................................................................................

Excellent Fragrance, though I did not like it on initial application, seemed another boring woody / Oudy composition but after a few wearings it becomes the most favourite Tom Ford replacing TF Extreme. Don't Know about others but I do get a similar vibe with Amouage Dia in the far drydown. Lovely blending and quality material probably from Givaudan.

I've heard rumours that oud wood was reformulated, so that oud wood parfum is the original oud wood (with great performance), and the performance of this was brought down. No way to confirm this, but Aaron Terence Hughes seems to circulate this theory in his review of the fragrance.

I'm surprised that nobody's mentioned the fact that Oud Wood smells a lot like Dzongkha. Specifically, the oily, rubbery cardamom that adds a green, celery-seed-like note to the composition in both fragrances, setting their character dial at once to the savory (as opposed to sweet).

From the 1st time that I've smelt this fragrance I was blown away. It somehow reminded me of something else, old and refined and I was like "I must have smelled this before". Very gentlemanly, a bit mature, very well balanced woody, a bit smoky, dark and mysterious kind of smell. A bit sweet, but not so sweet, seductive, just like a smooth criminal.

It's funny how the name "daffodil" connotes to me a sort of country bumpkin, hoi polloi flower, which some tobacco-chewing hick might pick to give to his sweetheart. "Narcissus" conjures up, in contrast, the image of a regal princess adorned in lavish purple velvet robes and covered with jewelry made of gold. Perhaps this is peculiar to me...??? Anyway, L'Artisan Parfumeur FLEUR DE NARCISSE smells a lot like daffodils to me, as it has a marked dirtiness that I'm not accustomed to sniffing in the creations from this house. Even their leathers always seem so gentle (and genteel...), but here I find some seriously dirty daffodils, their roots all covered with soil. This composition also has a slightly sour cast, which definitely makes it seem more complex than a little bunch of freshly picked daffodils, but I'm not sure that I really like what I smell. In an effort to determine whether I actually like FLEUR DE NARCISSE, I decided to do a side-by-side with Caron NARCISSE NOIR, which I have not worn in a while. The verdict? I guess that I'm just lucky, 'cause I very much prefer the sweet narcissus of the Caron to the dirty daffodils of L'Artisan. (Phew, what a relief!)

This is such an outstanding extraordinary creation! I love every single note I smell! Right from the beginning until it dries and settles down. The enchanting aroma of narcissus sweetened just a little bit by mimosa. Tobacco is striking you in an intense way you can hardly resist! Hay tones are also there, to form the whole composition in a unique way! I have a small decant spray of this masterpiece, I wish I could obtain the magical bottle! Even though the sillage is not good, the longevity is quite normal and satisfying! Highly reccomended!

Fleur de Narcisse goes on citric and bright, a little sour, fresh, and slightly green. I do understand the "vinegar" accusations, but it's closer to a light lemon or perhaps even cranberry to my nose. The core is a diaphanous floral note. I am not going to say it's not narcissus, but it reminds me far more of freesia than any narcissus I know. It airy, cool, and transparent, and completely lacking any heady, narcotic properties. The drydown emerges slowly, and after many hours, the florals morph into a delicate tobacco accord that's sheer to the skin. I don't know that I'd call this a chypre, but there is the faint, glassy shell of one around the floral core; a twang of citrus, and a dab of moss. It's all very understated, but exquisitely proportioned.

This fragrance opens with a strong alcoholic root-y note, reminiscent of a herbal tincture. What I see can be described as vegetal/herbal, sweet yet bitter at the same time. As the fragrance progresses it gradually softens and I detect traces of hay and smoke mixed together with root-y florals. If I had to associate a colour and a texture to this scent, it would be a dark amber and gooey. Unusual and complex, this fragrance is quite hard to wear. However, should it agree with your skin chemistry it is a very sophisticated scent.

As far as I know, Fleur de Narcisse was a perfume that was limited to 3000 bottles in 2006. It's a real shame, I must say, because this scent is truly incredibly beautiful. A very authentic reproduction of a real floral scent. When you wear it, you feel as if you have your nose permanently buried in a daffodil bloom. For me, it is therefore one of the most perfect spring and summer fragrances I have ever smelled. I also gave it to my girlfriend to test. She liked it very much as well, and I even considered giving it to her as a gift until I read about the limitation. However, there seem to be significant differences in sillage and longevity with this fragrance. While the scent was omnipresent but not intrusive for me, it was almost unnoticeable on my girlfriend. I had to be right at the spot where she applied it to perceive anything. Maybe it has to do with her skin chemistry, I don't know. But that doesn't matter too much now, as she also liked Fou d' Absinth - so I will probably gift her that one instead. Still, it's a shame that L'artisan limits their fragrances at all, and when they are as well done as Fleur de Narcisse, it makes it all the more bitter.
This is a very light, subtle scent for everyday wear when you want to hint at the approaching spring. You run no risk of smelling overpowering. However, it is also nothing really new.

This scent is definitely more heavy on that honeycrisp apple. The vanilla caramel is really noticeable, for me the only time i was kind of smelling it was HOURS later and it was very soft. I was hoping for more of a “caramel apple” scent but i really just get clean apple roomspray. If you like clean apple scents with a barely there sweetness, this would be for you.

Tobacco Vanille is widely loved by many who are fragrance aficionados. There are probably just as many who hate it for its straight-up tobacco note. Regardless, Tobacco Vanille is masterfully blended and will probably go down in the annals of fragrance history. Tobacco Vanille is a combination of three predominant notes. First and foremost is Tobacco. The tobacco note is clear, pure tobacco leaf, fresh and slightly spicy. This tobacco note conjures up visions of men swaddled in velvet smoking jackets, enjoying a pipe filled with fresh, aromatic tobacco and sipping a glass of brandy. Second is vanilla, smooth, warm and nutty. The vanilla creates a richly layered base note and complements the dry aromatic tobacco perfectly, slightly sweet and natural. Third is just a hint of opulently sweet, pure chocolate positioning itself in the background. This chocolate note even has a slightly fruity quality giving the it a broader dimension. The remaining players in this creation help bind the three predominant main notes together making a cohesive statement. The tonka bean, which appears in the heart notes, supports the vanilla note with strong hints of cinnamon, clove and almond. This gives texture to the vanilla and balances its sweetness with a little bit of spice. The tobacco flower provides a slight floral note but also a bit of woodiness to the predominant tobacco note. This is no masquerade, Tobacco Vanille is exactly what the name implies. It's a great fragrance for the fall and winter, perhaps even spring. You will probably not be comfortable with it in hot climates. You might find it a bit cloying, unless you're a tobacco farmer. Longevity and sillage on this fragrance is very good. Just like some of the other offerings in the Private Blend series, this fragrance can be detected even 12 hours later on the skin. Whatever you do, don't over-spray. This is a tobacco and vanilla monster, and moderation is required. Hats off to the Tom Ford and the mystery nose behind this fragrance. Tobacco Vanille is definitely a masterpiece.

That's a masterpiece. A warm and comforting blend of honey and sweet tobacco, rounded by warm vanilla. Rather a linear scent, but very well blended. It's unisex and has a great sillage, lasting power and projection. Updated January 2014

I know, this review puts me in a distinct minority, but I don't like such sweet perfumes, make me feel seasick...So great expectations because of the reviews but... Sorry guys but is my honest opinion.The sugar is overwhelming and mixed with tobacco... guess what? Overrated, overpriced perfume. Just test it before buy it.

Well, what can I possibly say to describe this amazing fragrance that hasn't already been said? To me, Tobacco Vanille is sex in a bottle. This fragrance seems to be edible, however I wouldn't classify it as a gourmand. I've grown up surrounded by the scent of tobacco, however I am never repulsed by it. The smokiness of the scent seems to be a comforting medium for me. When combined with the rich vanilla in this fragrance, the tobacco really takes on that soothing feel. It feels rather 'homey'. The scent is very strong at first, very rich and tobacco-y. If you've ever smelt a packet of cigarettes you'll find that they have a slight raisin type smell. This certain smell has been emulated in Tobacco Vanille's opening. The vanilla is sweet, yet not too sweet. This is certainly something that would smell amazing on both men and women, a true unisex fragrance. Expensive, yet well worth the money spent. Tobacco Vanille has amazing sillage strength and lasting power. I'm talking in terms of days. Since this is the only fragrance from Tom Ford's line that I've tried, I am very interested in testing them all.

TOBACCO VANILLE is the fourth Tom Ford creation that I've had the pleasure of sniffing, and I see a governing aesthetic coming into view for this house. I would compare it, texture-wise to gourmet caramel. Thick, rich, relatively homogeneous, made of only a few simple yet very high quality ingredients with a great deal of heft--these are not lightweight frags. I'm not saying that Tom Ford produces caramelly perfumes in the sense of "foody" or gourmand. No, I'm saying that they share a common aesthetic of delicious voluptuousness. TF perfumes wear the way caramel rolls over the tongue. Just as well-made caramel sauce is a pleasure not only for its taste, Tom Ford perfumes offer a similar combination of comfort and seduction. They are so directly sensual, particularly in the early stages, that I would not recommend them for office wear--possibly too much (though it would depend upon where one works...) TOBACCO VANILLE opens slightly sweet and lusciously rich but dries down to a more and more masculine fresh pipe tobacco scent. I know this because it reminds me of my stepfather, who carries a pouch of pipe tobacco with him wherever he goes. (Little does he know that he smells like the drydown of a Tom Ford perfume!) Although I initially found TOBACCO VANILLE a touch on the feminine side, as the sweet vanilla subsided, ceding to a dominant tobacco drydown, the overall effect seemed quite a bit more masculine to me. More masculine, in fact, than Creed TABAROME and certainly less feminine than Trussardi JEANS--two other tobacco perfumes which I esteem. The viscous rich caramel texture which I love in the opening of TOBACCO VANILLE makes me wish for more of the same, and since I prefer the opening to the lengthy drydown, I'm probably better off with the TF ORCHID and PATCHOULI perfumes... Like the other TF compositions I've tried, TOBACCO VANILLE has extraordinary longevity, but I do feel that it may be better suited for men.

I make it short: Tobacco and Vanilla well synchronised. I would say like a warm Honeymilk on the first sniff. Catching and hypnotising. Huge positive projection. Never to sweet nor cheap. lasts up to 12 hours and Sillage is huge. A hotel lobby will notice you! worth the money? For me every penny. scent: 9/10 I am SOLD to it!

I'm lounging in an Eames fine leather chair in front of a live fireplace. Crackling wood and flying embers. Lighting a Stadivarius Churchill, sipping on Legacy Rum. Flickering candle-fire from the Madagascan vanilla candles shift from wall to wall. An olive complected woman lies bare on a Persian carpet, picking fruit from a bowl. Tobacco Vanille is so beautifully composed.

This one is not easy to describe as just "Tobacco" and "Vanilla", I find it much more complex than that. To me this opens up with a huge wave of honey. Honey and dried fruit, coupled with boozy vanilla, almost like vanilla extract. It's very much in gourmand territory, and I think people who like gourmands will like this one.

I am a big fan of Tobacco Vanille smell, and after trying affordable alternatives like Phaedon or Al Haramain, I bought a Tom Ford. My thoughts behind the purchase - This is a very sweet and special scent, which is combining sweetness from Vanilla and Dried Fruits with dry Tobacco.

As many others have said, this fragrance smells exactly like the name... Tobacco and Vanilla. I have found it to have above average longevity on my skin, but below average silage. The scent is nice to be sure, but I think it is the association I made of it smelling just like a Las Vegas casino that really hooked me in (as I *love* Vegas).

Soft focus and romantic, Au bord de l'Eau is a rendition of Après l'Ondée. The difference is, Au bord de l'Eau uses lemon and bergamot to structure the marzipan-violet requiem. It's sad, but has a dignified poise that keeps the sorrow at bay. These slight changes make Fabrice Pellegrin's homage (if that's what this is) harder and fizzy, more wearable in the everyday, not just for wakes and funerals. It's a good thing that l'Artisan have done this, I love Après l'Ondée but it's too lugubrious most of the time. Keep Après l'Ondée for funerals . Wear Au bord de l'Eau in the garden - and feel happy to be alive.

A short review but a bit longer than a statement...a wonderful citrusy yet powdery scent. Absolutely no sharpness or association with cleaning products. Very much reminiscent of Nivea or baby bath/shampoo, which I personally like a lot!!! A light pleasant rosemary in the background. A great fragrance that I have never perceived here before. It was a real bargain in Strasbourg ;) Longevity is good at 5 hours, then rather close to the skin. Unfortunately, I couldn't test it in the heat due to continuous rain (yet), but I imagine it to be very pleasant and clean!

I was quite curious about this EdC because I read from someone that layered with "Premier Figuer" it creates a wonderful blend, and PF is supposed to last longer as well. So I immediately ordered a sample. Unfortunately, I was quite disappointed. At first, it almost smells like an essential oil. For a short time, it is nearly biting in the nose. It smells very powdery; I feel strongly reminded of perfumed talcum powder. I associate the scent with lavender, perhaps due to the blend of rosemary and bergamot. The talcum powder scent remains for now. I find it trivial. Sillage is hardly present. After an hour with one spray, there is almost nothing left on my skin. Three sprays last longer. The talcum impression fades, but the powder remains. In combination with PF, it is indeed nice. It rounds the scent off a bit and makes it softer. However, the difference is anything but huge. The longevity does seem a little bit longer to me. Overall, quite nice, but for me, it is never worth over 100 €. PF is already so beautiful; this EdC is not needed. I think there are nicer ones out there!

Water Mist does what a lot of more expensive fragrances fail to do. It gets closer to salt water than many scents can. It also does this without the crutch of florals. It's not just another citrus neroli or frangiapani or coconut. It just smells like salt and wood. Unfortunately once it dries in like 10 minutes it has a bit of a baby powder smell. Then it disappears completely. That being said, this otherwise unassuming body mist sitting amongst countless gross PINK mists is a standout. Discontinued, but a real one. If you can find it secondhand, you might get it to last through 2027 before it completely turns into alcohol.

I don't know how it happens when a top seller house falls in quality, it sells more! Tom Ford has fallen after discontinuing the most brilliant members of Private Blend and you see how powerful the brand became! Furthermore, the sales policies is so high; you see bold difference between Private Blend and ordinary releases of the house such as Noir, For Man, etc. Noir Extreme, for the first time I tried around five months ago, was a great let down. It still is. Someone really should give end to this oriental vanilla genre. Primarily, the title is totally unfit to the context of smell. It would be Pink Extreme. Seriously, if there is a certain definition of "man" which Tom Ford uses it as in classic creations which used to separate genders, and I believe Tom Ford personally would deny that definition, this perfume is totally out of that boundary. If he insists on gay culture and conceptualizes it by perfume, then naming a perfume "man" is a market-focused trick. Noir Extreme is an intense syrupy sweet lollipop with very punchy candy smell mingled with spicy air. It's more like crude home-made replica of a famous oriental vanilla by an untrained perfumer. A pimpy kinky medicinal sweetness that lacks the very character of every sweet smell: happiness. Longevity: 6/10 Sillage: 4/10 Scent: 2/10

Spring and summer carry the scent of blossoming flowers, summer rains, ocean tides, and sandalwood. A feeling of optimism and adventure permeates the air. It is invigorating and fresh and leaves a sense of optimism. But once fall approaches and heads into the crisp cold of winter, we crave something warmer and more homely, like spices. It is not uncommon for me to fall in love with a fragrance at first sight. Considering Extreme Noir was a blind buy, I can't help but feel satisfied. And it has the right amount of spice to suit the cold months. It is a genre of cologne that shares similar vibes with Spicebomb Extreme , Potion Eau de Parfum . The fragrance begins with warming spices and settles on the skin with an embrace of amber and sandalwood. The opening of Noir Extreme is a deluge of fiery spices. A warm cloud of delicious notes of nutmeg and the more mentholated notes of cardamom add the warm spice. I also sense that familiar, slightly leathery but not dominant saffron smell, along with the aromatic clove buds. Even though the olfactory pyramid does not mention it, the first note that reaches my nostrils is the smell of clove, which reminds me of mulled wine. Perhaps it is the eugenol that is present in nutmeg, clove, and cinnamon. Instead, the notes of neroli and orange blossom come to me subdued. It is a warm and complex start, with assertive spiciness and an underlying citrus sweetness. Yes, the spice is pretty intense at first, but it quickly becomes much sweeter. The heart reveals sweet flavours and creamy edges. This is because of the mastic resin and what I presume to be kulfi, an Indian frozen dairy dessert for which I have no framework for what it should smell like. I feel something nutty like pistachio and floral like a rose. The flower's queen compliments the kulfi note. At this stage, it has an excellent gourmand aroma, a warm amber undertone, and a delicate balance of floral notes. Some rose and jasmine come out of it, but neither is so distinct within the composition that it dominates or overpowers the other notes. When it dries, it turns a little powdery. A smooth, creamy base emerges, with milky woods that solidify the fragrance and add depth. The base is modern and gourmand, soft with sandalwood, a hint of vanillin, and a bit of amber with that genuinely unique gourmand accord and floral tones. Luckily, it is not another ambroxan bomb. Strangely and unexpectedly, projection and longevity are acceptable but not extraordinary, as I expected from a Tom Ford perfume. It stays close to the body and lasts for a few hours on my skin. Within moments, the boldness of the start gives way to the fragrance of the skin. Seasonally, I would reserve this for autumn and winter, mainly. It is beautiful in cooler temperatures and would be fine in warmer ones. Overall, do I like Noir Extreme? Yes, definitely. I base my opinion and review on a bottle I have owned since October 2022. -Elysium

Tom Ford usually take some risks, specially on his first releases back in the 00's. Black Orchid, Tobacco Vanille, Oud Wood and Tuscan Leather were pretty much pioneers and they still stand unique to this day (despite some clones and very "inspired" creations around there). This one is kinda unique but more mainstream and less daring than the previous i mentioned. It's a vanilla based scent but not strong enough to be a winter killer, more a Netflix and chill, a cuddling scent, around the house or by the fireplace kind of a fragrance. The main player here is the vanilla, as I said before, but along with that it has an interesting freshness due to some citruses and florals. The citrus here are not strong, not in your face. Just gives a slightly juicy sweet mandarin orange feel with hits of orange blossom. During the heart of this one, the florals became more pronounced but the vanilla is still pretty much on the front. The cardamom helps the vanilla become more tamed and spicy, more interesting and less sweet. A really delicious warm vanilla ice cream. It will not change much during the lifetime on your skin. A warm vanilla fresh and spicy ice cream! The longevity is average to good (around 8-10h), and the projection is average to low. Again, I prefer it to be like this. Is a feel good scent for cuddling and Netflix. Not your typical vanilla sweet bomb, ambery or medicinal. It's unisex and appealing to everyone. Not masculine and a complement magnet. Just a good smelling scent that will fit indoor enviornments during colder weather. I recommend it if you like sweet yet fresh vanilla scents with personality. Not groundbreaking or masterpiece territory but still, a great frangrance for indoors in winter time. 3/5

I have only tried the Eau de Parfum version of Tom Ford - Noir. I can say that the original in Eau de Parfum is stronger than this fragrance. Although this is labelled "extreme" I don't get anything loud here. What I do get, is a sweet, spicy woody oriental, which is very well suited to cooler weather. I personally would wear this to work or formally. I can see it being worn at night or even on a date. I love the ambery, resinous vibe mixed with the pistachio etc. However I wouldn't consider this a gourmand in an overt way. It's subtly sweet. I pick up some peppery like nutmeg and woods too. I think it's blended together well but feel it's performance slightly lacking. I do think it's more versatile than people think it is and I think in the right setting this could work very well. It's one to have around for the right occasion.

No wonder it's called "Noir". This has an interesting dark, slightly mysterious depth to it, and it's a beautiful combination of high-quality materials. So, Noir Extreme begins with a slightly spicy and sweet blast, combining the warmth and sweetness of the nutmeg, the spiciness and dark, leathery (but not too strong) saffron, the balsamic, woody and invigorating cardamom, and the slight hints of mandarin in the background. A beautiful start. All of these make up the main star of the show, and that is the kulfi note, which in case you don't know what that is, it's sort of an Indian ice cream made with dairy, cardamom, saffron, pistachio, and rose petals. As the fragrance dries down, it becomes a bit creamier and smoother, but also a touch more floral, with the rose, jasmine and orange blossom notes making it into the scene. But don't believe that this turns into an intensive floral fragrance. Not at all, the floral notes sit more in the background, being overpowered by the sweetness and slight spiciness of the initial notes. What the floral accords do is mostly smooth things out a bit and decrease the sweetness just a smidge, and they do so just right. Once Noir Extreme settles down completely, you get a touch of warm woodiness and some slight vanilla sweetness, along with a bit of amber warmth. The kulfi note slowly dissipates throughout the wearing. It's overall a pleasant gourmand fragrance. It's dark, sweet, complex, spicy, mysterious, and downright delicious. It's fairly well-blended too In terms of longevity, it's not bad either. I got about 7-8, maybe 9 hours before it would disappear from my skin, which isn't beast-mode, but still quite great. Projection-wise, it had a solid 2 feet of projection for the first two or so hours, after which it settled down substantially, not projecting much more. For occasions, Noir Extreme is actually more versatile than I thought. You could rock this at formal events, parties and clubbing, gatherings of all kinds, and even at work or school if you reduce the amount of sprays and if you are confident enough. Just make sure you wear it during the colder weather, otherwise you will be getting complaints, not compliments. Still, even though you could make it work in a variety of situations, I would retain it to parties or more special occasions. But regardless if you like the way everything sounds so far, if you haven't first tested it, don't blind buy it. Even though it's a very nice and interesting fragrance, it does not mean it will necessarily suit your taste. It's pretty different from other typical gourmands. It's not all just some sweet chestnut and a heavy dose of vanilla. This is a complex, spicy and dark-type of gourmand and even though it's a very acclaimed and beloved fragrance by most, you could just as easily fall into the category of people that just do not enjoy this. And although I do like it, gourmands are not really my thing. But for those with a sweet tooth, I can whole-heartedly recommend this one. Overall Rating: 7/10

Noir Extreme is one of those fragrances where the notes don't really do it justice. I could go on and on about cardamom this and kulfi that, and orange blossom this and mastic that, but it's really the combination of the spices, gourmands, florals, and amber that come together and make something more than the sum of their parts. This juice is blended to perfection.

Tom Ford Noir Extreme somehow manages to achieve a dark sophistication while also pulling off a mature, playful sexiness. It's a perfect scent for those who are self-assured but have a tendency towards introversion. Scent: I mostly get spicy cardamom and nutmeg at the top, creamy (what I have to assume is) kulfi in the mid, and vanilla and sandalwood in the base.

Two days before I made a blind buy on this perfume because I saw lots of youtube reviews which says Noir Extreme is awesome, special, manly and Beast. The shopkeeper does not had a tester for this perfume so again I have to make a decision for blind buy. The projection is very poor so that someone has to rub his nose on my body to smell it.

the fragrance starts strong with tangerine and cardamom. then floral notes develop but which remain light. after half an hour a milky sweetness settles in the middle of the spices. however for me the latter dominate all along the side ice cream is pretty discreet on me.

As the only drawback, I would say that it seems more feminine than masculine to me, even so, I wear it with pleasure. Tangerine, jasmine, rose, vanilla, etc., come together in this sweet fragrance, but without being heavy and unpleasant, resulting in a very pleasant, soft aroma, a little feminine I would say and completely versatile, both for hot and cold climates.

Fables d'Orient is a fragrance that knows how to stand out with elegance. It begins softly with iris, a subtle powder that gently caresses the skin, like a promise of refinement. The heliotrope, delicately vanilla-scented, adds a cosy touch. Then, amber and spices come in to warm everything up, bringing depth that gives a mysterious and sensual edge. The musk in the background invites closeness, without being pushy. A perfect balance, all softness and subtlety, leaving a discreet but lasting impression.

What a wonderful oriental perfume, powdery nutmeg with sexy musks and amber to give it a sensual background sweetness. Definitely warm and cozy, sexy winter stuff. Reminds me of Rosendo Mateu 5 but this is lighter and more pleasant, less feminine. I’m not into these kind of smells but L’Artisan can do everything perfectly. The only bad thing is its price.

Sweet cyanide syrup. Druggy bitter almond and drunken black cherry. Alluring and aloof, indulgent and narcotic. A molten morphine lollipop, flavoured fake blood. The cherry pulls medicinal, but this is a dose I want to savour. It takes a lot for an artificial cherry to overcome the childhood Robitussin PTSD (I won’t even touch red Starburst), so I have to admire Lost Cherry there. Love to see a weird girl go popular, even if it might make a villain of them. I can’t rationalise a full bottle but every tester I get my grubby little paws on is sucked dry within a month. Partly due to the longevity, which is oddly fleeting for such a thick scent. And partly the i-c-wot-u-did-there name, the glorified Duplo block vessel, the absurd price. Not going to fall for your tricks, Cherry. Mental Snapshot: Maraschinos steeped in Snow White’s poison, a vampire night nurse, a smooth-talking roulette dealer promising better luck on the next whirl, or the whirl after that... You know she’s fake, but you’ll happily fall for her trap. Not a red flag, but a ~ crimson ~ one. If I ever buy a bottle of Lost Cherry I will be entering my Anna Delvey arc. tl;dr: red dye 69

When Chet Baker crooned, “Let’s get lost, in a romantic mist…” clearly he was singing about Lost Cherry. The Cherry is there from the first blast then poof! She’s lost. But wait, what’s this I smell on my skin? She is still there, only found. There within the deep Balsam of Peru, lost in the rich Tonka Beans. Subtle wafts of that top note lost to almonds, roses, and everything sweet still yearn to be found with every sniff that comes just when you think it’s gone for good. Such a flirty little scent this Cherry is! Why must she always remind me that she’s still there when I begin to think she’s gone? And what comfort it is to realize she’s still there! How calming and cloud-like she tickles my senses, so sweet she is without sickening me. I do think we will get lost together…

Don’t get me wrong, I love this scent. But no perfume will ever be worth $350 unless it makes my celebrity crush of the month magically appear when it’s sprayed. This isn’t a candy-like cherry, or the kind you smell in cherry soda. This is real, fresh cherry. It’s perfect and I want to drink it. But Tom Ford can get lost if he thinks it’s worth over $300. Maybe I’m too anti-capitalist for this hobby. Oh and also this lasts like 3 hours maximum. Sure, you can reapply, but at this price point? It’s a yikes from me.

I am Ukrainian, and sour cherries are nostalgic for me. We had cherry trees growing on every corner, and cherries were used in jams, compote, wine and pierogi fillings. To me, Lost Cherry smells fantastic, I don’t get any synthetic cough syrup, instead, I smell a mix of realistic cherry syrup, amaretto liqueur, and a subtle smoky note. I bought a travel size spray and use it for special occasions. While it don’t regret the purchase, it’s not a FBW for me, mostly because of the price.

I have a friend who says this smells like cherry cough syrup on her, and I have no idea how that is possible. I think it smells like the most divinely realistic cherry perfume that there could ever be. Pure cherry and perhaps a bit of musk in the base. The cherry is the perfect blend of sweet and tart. It's a delicious fragrance. If not for the price tag, I likely would own it by now.

I bought this perfume for my beloved after hearing that it was a "vampiric cherry" type of flavor. I agree it is definitely a mature scent that evokes warm liquor in cold nighttime air. The cherry is very photorealistic and gives way to a disciplined mix of warm spices. I find it perfectly mysterious and self-assured, and a great accessory for an evening out.

Yummy sundae with the cherry on top. A bright red, delicious, sweet and tart finish to the dessert after a wonderful meal. In the case of Lost Cherry Eau de Parfum , it is the meal. However, much like a dessert, it is short-lived, fleeting, and leaves me wanting.

Not gonna waste any time on how I feel about this one. This is one of the best things I have ever smelled but it just fleets immediately. This didn't stop me from buying the bottle as the natural cherry scent with rose nuance was one of the most magical experiences I have ever had with a fragrance.
I don´t know if you can fall in love with a perfume, but probably this is it. Couldn´t stop smelling myself and am super aware when i wear it. A sweet but also sexy gourmand.

Well, that sure is cherry. Sweet gloopy cherry liquor that's made by fermenting ripe cherries with a giant heap of sugar. A very floral backdrop. A bit of jasmine, a lot of rose. Just overall... a lot. Initially engulfed the whole house in a giant thick cloud. Took ~1,5 hours to settle in my immediate vicinity.

Even though they're not listed in the pyramid, Champ de Fleurs strikes me as a foremost tuberose-gardenia fragrance. The initial opening of the softly bitter grapefruit pith quickly reveals the fleshy heart of tuberose and gardenia. The creamy sweetness is very restrained here, so much so that it feels almost like a nutty sweetness when the cedar starts to whisper in the background later on. The cheese-like butteriness of gardenia purrs quietly under the blanket of clean white musk, just enough to provide a certain intrigue but far from threatening the overall lighthearted mood of the fragrance. The sillage of Champ de Fleurs is mostly intimate, and it lasts around 6-7 hours on me. I initially thought of Champ de Fleurs as very similar to La Chasse aux Papillons EDT - one of the most successful L'Artisan Parfumeur offerings, and last year's Roger & Gallet Tubéreuse Hédonie, all three composed by Anne Flipo. After comparing them side by side, I still think that they're interchangeable to a certain extent, as all three share the similar tuberose heart and all three fill the same spot of a pretty, girl-next-door type of tuberose fragrance. But there are still noticeable differences, with Tubéreuse Hédonie being the closest to a tuberose soliflore, exchanging the buttery cheese aspect of gardenia with the vegetal and somewhat chalky undertone of tuberose, while the hay-like nuance of linden blossom in La Chasse aux Papillons becomes much more apparent in comparison. As a result, Champ de Fleurs turns out to be more creamy, more musky and less vegetal, even though marginally so. It's certainly a very wearable, everyday type of tuberose fragrance. Adequate for sure, but I'm afraid it doesn't have much anything new to say, and I doubt it would make much impression to hardcore tuberose fans.

Field of flowers. Flower meadow. Thematically spot on. But it feels like an old, yellowed photo. Like from a distance and slightly dried out. It lacks liveliness. One could say positively: romantically idealized. However, a feeling of happiness does not arise, as the ingredients do not seem convincing enough. Consisting of a generic, sweet-fresh floral note that is overly overshadowed by a clean, dry-powdery-woody, slightly synthetic laundry musk, and a spicy-grassy tone that reminds me of the wonderful Tokyo Bloom, but significantly paler and also dry. Together, they create the impression described above. Or that of a flower meadow that has been a bit too much in the sun, whose scent molecules are mostly already decomposed and have mixed in a diffuse cloud, blurry and shimmering above the green. This certainly has its charm and is a really nice scent in its projection, but when wearing it myself, I miss something special, clear - something distinctive.

As a confessed fan of Timbuktu from the same house, I had to test this new creation. So I got a 1.5 ml tester directly from the manufacturer and off I went… The first spray revealed cedar wood in its most magnificent form, powerful and hefty! But just a few seconds later, it turned in a sadly different direction, as the scent suddenly became dark and bitter. Although the cedar is still minimally recognizable, it is unfortunately pushed in a direction by saffron and nutmeg that I don't really like, and after a few hours, only an indefinable herbal paste, additionally garnished with cumin, is perceptible, which partly also reminds me of curry sauce. Unfortunately, the sillage is not really good either. It feels to me as if the cedar has been trapped in the bottle and immediately seeks to escape after spraying… For me, this is definitely not a masterpiece. Maybe my expectations were too high, but from a fragrance that has "cedar" in the title, I expect cedar and not an indefinable spice combo! Addendum: after about 6 hours, the cedar returns and has almost completely displaced the herbs. However, it is only recognizable up close!

As Omnipotato said, Ombré Leather is the standard by which other leather fragrances are judged. Sonia Constant uses black leather that doesn't smell creamy or animalic, but rather like the leather seats in a new Mercedes. Combined with a sweet and earthy backbone, this is a powerful scent, but it's also warm and inviting. How does it compare to the direct competitors? Tuscan Leather Eau de Parfum is more masculine and challenging, with raspberry and jasmine to combat slightly animalic leather. It also has a mild ashtray nuance due to frankincense. Needless to say, Ombré is tame and mass-appealing compared to its older brother. Godolphin ditches the pungent notes, keeps the raspberry at the top and adds more florals in the heart. Therefore, the leather is easier to digest than in the other two scents. The fruity and floral notes eventually fade and Ombré has a sweeter drydown. Back to Ombré. The opening is challenging, perhaps even too much for some. I enjoy the way Sonia uses a mixture of spices and florals to provide a lift and some balance to notes that would otherwise be nauseating. I enjoyed it in Noir Extreme Eau de Parfum where she used cardamom, saffron and florals to smooth out the cloying kulfi. You can expect the same thing to happen here, except with dominant leather. The spices give it a bit of airiness and shift your focus while jasmine works its magic and balances the thick leather with its fresh and sweet floral quality. Drydown is where things get intruiging. Leather is around, but the overall scent profile is more sweet. The amber base blends with patchouli and moss, giving off a vibe that I can only describe as dark. It's resinous, earthy and dense, with hints of leather. There's more character and intrigue than in your average amber base. Performance is solid, I get at least 10 hours on skin with my 2023 batch. Ombré also sticks well to a leather jacket; I usually do like 2-3 sprays every other week. I recommend getting the 50ml bottle, as 3-5 sprays will last you a whole day.

Hardly in need of an introduction nowadays. Whether it is from that one cool uncle of yours or from a random stranger passing by with 10+ sprays, you've smelt Ombré Leather (2018) Eau de Parfum before. Everyone has, and everyone loves it, which is why it has become the signature scent of so many around the world. The opening strikes with a not-overly-spicy dosage of warm, sweet cardamom, dare I say a little camphorous as well. It is supported nicely by a beautiful sweet white floral aroma from the jasmine sambac, which strikes as 'fuller' and more pronounced than regular jasmine. Then the star of the show starts peeking through - black leather. A rich and slightly sweet realistic leather smell with hints of woodiness, done in an easily-recognizable fashion here. However, while not listed in the notes pyramid, there's also a prominent red berry fruitiness on top, similar to raspberry. It brings just the right amount of tart, sweet fruitiness to the blend to make it even more iconic. Oh, and for those worrying about the animalic comments that Ombré Leather (2018) Eau de Parfum gets, it's fictional nonsense. There's no true animalic facets here, and if you feel it does, then let me tell you, you don't know what animalic smells like. Try visiting rural areas more often. Might help. The patchouli and amber make for a nice duet here, although there's not a lot of patchouli. Mainly, just a little of its musky/spicy/sweet attributes in the back. The amber adds a rich and warm sweetness, with the mildest undertones of resins. Vetiver takes a step back and just contributes with a touch of smokiness and woodiness, although it's hard to properly pinpoint as everything is sitting under a sensual, sweet dark leather, which is further complimented at the base with a touch of mossy dampness. It might all sound like quite a complex scent, but really, it all feels like a single unified creation. Peak of French perfumery? Maybe, maybe not, but it sure is the peak of mass-appealing elegance. And thankfully, performance is remarkable too. On my skin, the fragrance easily surpassed the 15 hour mark. Of course, a skin scent ever since around hour 7, with projection also leaving me satisfied during this time. For the first hour, a very solid 3 foot bubble around me, with nice sillage as well. Things would gradually soften to around 2 feet of projection up until hour 3, after which it would close in with lighter (but consistent) pushing power until the skin scent status. Very dependable overall, which is why I still love to rock it at weddings - I know that it will carry me throughout the whole day without issues. Outside of special occasions, Ombré Leather (2018) Eau de Parfum would do just as well in any other scenario. Minding the sprays according to context, you could rock Ombré Leather (2018) Eau de Parfum anywhere, anytime. An easy signature scent. It's no mystery how Ombré Leather (2018) Eau de Parfum got its success. The way it makes leather its core identity in a mass-appealing way without toning down the intensity of the leather as others do + the sheer addictiveness and elegant aura that it brings = worldwide blockbuster. At one point or another, this will probably be your favorite fragrance. And I believe that most fragrance enthusiasts reach that point early in their journey. As @Merlotsupern said below, Ombré Leather (2018) Eau de Parfum is a milestone in leather perfumery which no one should skip. Is it the best leather fragrance? No. But it will likely sprout a love for leather and a desire to find the "ultimate" leather fragrance that will hunt you for the rest of your smelly journey... Overall Score: 8.1/10

The mother of all contemporary leather fragrances, and effectively a milestone to compare against. If you are willing to develop your taste around leather, this is probably the best starting point - the price is reasonable at discounters. My best practical advice is to avoid any "clones or inspired by", and get this. Brutally, I would ignore the other flankers because this achieved the perfect balance between animalic facets, leather scent, ambery sweetness and overall performance. You'll find plenty of good reviews around, so I won't waste your time any further.

"We made vows inside the church to forgive each other's sins. But there are things I have to endure, like the smell of another man's skin. If that's not loving you, I don't know what is."--Sting, Loving You, The Bridge. Last night, as I was returning from the office, I listened to Sting's recent work, The Bridge, specifically the song Loving You. The lyrics made me think of the cologne I had been wearing since the morning: Ombré Leather by Tom Ford. Yes, because the way the perfumer treated the leather here is like the smell of another man's skin, a verse extracted from the text. I love leather accords, no matter if they are suede, Nappa, or rawhide. It's stronger than me. Here the skin is not brittle or demanding; it is soft and inviting. Ombré means having colors or tones that blend into each other, faded into color. And I like to imagine that in this context, it means shaded skin. When I smelled the paper on which I sprayed the essence, I really liked the fragrance I was smelling. And I'll tell you why. Ombré Leather opens my skin with an enormous freshness, like morning dew, with a slightly more indeterminate greenish tip reminiscent of dusting violet leaves sprouting around the blackened skin. An alcoholic and camphoraceous voice denotes an inky and leathery soul similar to black shoe polish. What you get instantly is cardamom, but the keynote is leather, a smooth and pliable suede. The opening is a combination of fresh spices and some flowers too. The nose has granted the spicy and minty tone of cardamom in a rumba with the sweetish flowers of jasmine. It has a smoky, slightly tarry, and dry smell. The nuance of the skin is not that of a new jacket, a briefcase, a wallet, or a new pair of boots, which lingers a bit in the air, makes you close your eyes and take a deep breath, but a rubbery, inked, and with an oily machine shop environment feel. Powerfully animalistic, earthy, and with a touch of smokiness. A light sprinkling of spices hovers all around, mainly consisting of saffron with a slight peppery smell. Saffron smells strong, leathery, earthy, hay-like, reminding slightly of rubber. I also have a kind of creaminess, which sounds like a contradiction, I know. An excellent suede effect feels beige and marks the fragrance as a much softer and calmer version of its holder material. This inviting overture slowly morphs into a heart of earthy and slightly pungent leather notes that is well tempered with a hint of amber in the bottom to keep things light, airy, and a little sweet. A drop of indole jasmine envelops the black leather, lightens, adds a floral sweetness to the composition, and allows Ombré Leather to become more unisex. The amber note brings warmth and color, while the airy jasmine gives a diffusive intensity, creating a bold and luminous clash of leather and flowers. It is not an old cracked leather jacket or the side of the horse's saddle. The leather is soft and buttery, with only a simple hint of smoke and dryness. This is leather that offers comfort because it is wrapped in a veil of pale amber and patchouli. Eventually, the skin fades into the background, allowing mosses, woods, and amber to take center stage. Slowly it smoothes to a salty and musky with a little earthy spice in the base. A masculine cut. What's left on you is patchouli, which isn't very heavy but adds some depth of character to Ombré Leather, an all-day greenish moss, with small patches of earthy vetiver similar to Encre Noire Eau de Toilette . The notes blend quickly and read more of a generalized green at this point. The amber here is honestly not that intense, even if it's an old-school composite amber note. It hides in the background without being intrusive and provides friendly support. On me, I get jasmine, white musk, and leather as important notes, the scent of leather is powerful. Even if the consensus for this fragrance is more oriented towards the winter months, I am making the most of this splendid scent by enjoying it in the evening and in the day's cooler autumns. This is my new fall fragrance to count this year in my fall rotation. It's so sexy and sophisticated and not overwhelming at all. But it's not subtle either; it stays in the air when someone passes by and smells so good. If you care about longevity, it lasts all day on my skin. It's a very dark type of fragrance but not an overwhelming monstrosity with heavy, opulent spice. Ombré Leather is definitely unisex with a masculine, dry and warm cut, Overall, it's an ideal type of perfume, but it has that rough-dirty side. If you can't stand leather, then this is obviously not for you. I base the review on a 100ml bottle I have owned since April 2021. -Elysium

With a couple of minor twists here are there that made the composition more clean and wearable, Ombré Leather basically smells like Tuscan Leather. The difference in the price tag between the two is big enough for me to recommend you go straight for this release in case you want to save some bucks and still smell practically the same. Here are my 5 quick takes: - The best suede leather fragrance on the market - Created by Sonia Constant in the 2018 as a replacement for discontinued Ombre Leather 16 - The best fragrance release of the 2010s and one of the best designer releases ever - Best worn during the colder months in business, night outs and dating scenarios - Pricey for a designer TOP NOTES Upon smelling the Ombré Leather for the first time, you will be reminded of Tuscan Leather and Ombre Leather 16. No matter what the brand is trying to push saying there is no raspberry here, it is well present, although, less pronounced than in Tuscan Leather. That familiar fruitiness is unmistakably here. One more “hidden” note that seems to be avoided from mentioning is saffron. Numerous high-end fragrances use it, and anyone experienced with the aforementioned note will sense it straight away. HEART NOTES The fragrance warms up in the heart notes with the introduction of jasmine Sambac and dusty amber. The floral sweetness feels addictive and is on the same level of quality as in Chanel perfumes. Being the pure leather scent, the classy floral aspect never takes the center stage, and the fragrance dances on the perfect line of being completely unisex while I do feel like it leans just a bit more on the masculine side. BASE NOTES Progressing from the top to the base, the scent is clean, well-blended, and it can get difficult to distinguish different notes except that “to die for” leather. In the dry down, it is closest to how does Tuscan Leather smells like thanks to the lack of “ashy” note found in Tuscan Leather. I find it personally the best suede leather fragrance on the market. The one I have the most experience with, and the one I could see almost anyone wear. Get it while still available in its first formulation. *Check out my Parfumo profile to find out how can you read full reviews on my website.*

This is a combined review of Ombre Leather EdP, Ombre Leather Parfum and Eau d'Ombre Leather. I've been looking for a mild and versatile leather fragrance for those occasions where a strong leather scent won't work. Tested from samples. I had really high expectations for these, seeing how well liked they are.

While Ombre Leather is not the easiest fragrance to pull off, what it brings to the table definitely offsets these difficulties. An explosion of new-car leather aggressively leads the way before slowly unfolding into a harmonious balance of sweet florals, smokey woods and warm spices. This stuff projects like crazy during the opening but mellows out over time.

As an androgynous woman who tends to prefer unisex scents, this is my go to fragrance hands down. It is simple, enjoyable, and gets compliments from all genders. This is a very genuine leather scent. It reminds me of sitting in a new, sun-warmed car with leather seats. Like being chauffeured in a luxury vehicle.

A absolutely sexy stunner of a fragrance that will make you smell like a member of the billionaire boys club. And someone who has just stepped out of his expensive leather upholstered sports car for a night on the town. As soon as you spray this on you are enveloped with the most plush and luxurious aroma of jasmine and supple plush leather.

When you feel like you want to smell like a person that got His/Her leather jacket and hit the road with no destination set, this is your fragrance! Ombre Leather smells like if you are hit with a leather smell from a new car with leather seats or a plain leather jacket...Raw leather with a bit of a fruity vibe that just take it to a really sexy rank!!

Well i have to disagree with most of the overall thoughts about it, i absolutely love it. I have to admit that when i first tried it, it was just ok and simple, and performance wise i was a bit disappointed. Then it settled for some weeks and wow, the game changed. The incense is so beautiful and natural smelling, i'm from southern Spain and the smell reminds me so much of the streets of Seville and the holy week. The pepper and cedar make this so so wonderful and not like you're a walking censer, to me this wears more masculine because of those woody aromatic and spicy background. And yes, the performance changed so much after some weeks, it's really well done and to me this is the best incense based perfume i've tried so far. They told me at L'AP this is the first of its own new collection which will feature other incense fragrances, i'm looking 4wd to see what they will do next. If Bertrand Duchaufour makes one, i could die Last but not least, if you layer it with Seville a l'Aube is just to die for, as well as some neroli or some vanilla.

I don't know, the scent is okay, I bought it at the beginning of my journey and sold it after I designed my perfume collection because I came to the conclusion that the scent is nothing more than nice and its longevity is short for a leather perfume and the sillage doesn't work well either. Yes, it has something unique, an aromatic leather scent but if we look at the whole complex of the scent, the performance and the price – it's not worth it and for this price you can find much more worthy perfumes. Tom Ford has such great potential to make really high-quality perfumes but they only choose good scents and everything else (performance) is below average and you can say that about a lot of their perfumes. 7/10.

Tom Ford fragrances are so unpredictable. Each one has its story to tell, its characters, its audience of lovers and haters. So far, all the colognes I blindly bought from this brand have not let me down. "Black Orchid (Eau de Toilette) | Tom Ford" , Oud Wood Intense , Tobacco Vanille Eau de Parfum , Sahara Noir , and Ombré Leather (2018) Eau de Parfum are all damn good and unique. Fabulous is not what I supposed it was, though it is very dramatic. It has a soapy, creamy, and powdery take on leather that I have never met in others. In fact, this perfume is unlike any I own. I want to provide an overview that reflects what Fabulous represents to me as much as possible. The fragrances are so personal, and everyone collects distinct notes. Scents smell differently on everyone, and everyone has different preferences. I can only let you know my feelings about the fragrance, and that's pretty much it. Aromatic, herbal, and slightly sweet accord welcomes me when the cologne touches my pulse points. There is no harshness in that blast but a fresh green burst from the bitter clary sage and the soothing lavender. In the initial stage, and on my skin, the cologne takes a masculine slant, no matter the mellowed coumarin presence, and the leathery nuance is still dozing and weakly perceivable. Right off the bat, you can associate Fabulous with a kind of fougére, very herbal. It takes quite a few moments before reaching the middle stage. Notes of bitter white almond and powdery iris are the first things I smell from the heart. The blend of milky and dry notes creates a soapy-like accord, which blends gracefully with the leathery nuance now getting more apparent. It is a brushed suede-like leather, velvety, tamed that grows and grows. Not at all off-putting; I can get small whiffs of it throughout the wearing. A copious touch of the leather changes the rather dominant, sharp, and sweet blend of tonka and almond, relatively dirty. Luckily, the almond does not smell on a par with Hypnotic Poison Eau de Toilette because it annoys me and gives me a bit of sickness the way it smells in there. The roughness becomes noticeable in the drydown when the cashmeran kicks in, and the leather takes on a shoe-polish aroma. A creaminess takes the stage with a rugged tonka that gives an additional depth. The trail is luxuriously self-indulgent. Close to the skin, I catch the mossy face of musk, animalic, and not in a clean laundry style. So, these come together under the soothing scent of dried clary sage, lending a lightness to the entire symphony. Performance is excellent, certainly not near the beasts of the Private Blend line, but strong on projection for a few hours before softening out and overall having outstanding longevity on the skin. Does it smell f@king fabulous? I am afraid not. But, if you like spicy, leathery lavender with hints of vanilla, amber, and bitter almond, then it smells fabulous, absolutely. To my nose, and those who have smelled it on me agree, iris root and clary sage add a masculine breeze to the first spritz. I enjoy wearing this kind of genre during cold months. Fall suits better, but even winter seems good. It is a nighttime cologne for evening and events out. I base the review on a decant I have owned since January 2022. -Elysium

I don't like negative reviews, i prefer to form my own opinion. And that's what happened with this FUCKING FABULOUS. I have read so many reviews, negative comments of all kinds that it sometimes seemed ridiculous that i had to necesseraly defend this olfactory gem. In order to silence the bad tongues, i am going to give you here my own olfactory experience, honest and without false notes. If I had to sum up this FUCKING FABULOUS in one word, i would say, as the name suggests, F A B U L O U S !!!! Fabulous in the sense that this juice is unlike any other. It is absolutely unique, its olfactory pyramid is nothing extraordinary but doesn't looks like anything you have been able to test. A subtle blend of refined leather, bitter almond, Tonka bean, powder vanilla with all the same a clear predominance of Tonka and sweet powdered almond of any beauty. A premium fragrance for the daring, to wear with pride. Do not put in the hands of inexperienced noses because this juice can disturb the uninitiated. It is needless to mention that the marketing and advertising genius of TOM FORD played a decisive role in the popularity of this fragrance by setting, as usual, the bar very high. Let us return, however, to the protagonist concerned. We are dealing here with a real olfactory treasure, marvelously mixing a composition clearly standing out from the competition and immediately recognizable among a thousand. It's sweet, luxurious, sophisticated, powdery, silky, slightly sweet... The top notes open on an almost toasted almond rolled in sugar and vanilla. Then it dries and becomes soft with a hint of very warming, smooth and creamy leather accord. To give you an idea, it looks like vanilla ice cream in a butter churn mixing chunks of almonds that melt in your mouth as you sit on a vintage leather armchair... Then the whole calms down a bit, like powdered baby powder... We attack the heart notes with the Tonka that oozes everywhere but in a seductive way to add a creamy character to which everyone refers. Once the weather is at rest, a kind of Tuscan style leather makes its appearance, both alluring and daring. The arrival of the base notes once again reveal a heavy Tonka, amber and musky, with a very persistent leather. The final drying shows a faded Tonka and tempered leather with woody notes. All this set requires a time of adaptation to be tamed, and will not suit everyone. A perfume to wear every day? Mmmm... I would say no. So reserved for unique occasions.
