Longevity and projection are bordering on cruelty to the people around you. Needless to say, the longevity on clothes is just phenomenal !!!! I get a lot of compliments and people ask me what that divine smell is. I tell them that it is TOM FORD FUCKING FABULOUS. Most of the time, they don't know it... Despite everything, some "gaps" are to be remembered: The price, 300€ for 50ml. The tendency to no longer smell the perfume on oneself after 2 hours despite a huge sillage. And the sensation of embalming baby powder after several hours. So, is this FUCKING FABULOUS really fabulous? It is for me because NO other juice looks like it. I noticed a longevity of at least 8 hours in my case. For most of you this will be i think a mixed opinion... However, this is not the scent i expected. To be honest, this FUCKING FABULOUS curiously reminded me of the Dolce Gabbana Intenso... Nothing to see you tell me but this is undoubtedly due to the presence of amber and clary sage. The matte black bottle is sublime, similar to a magnificent square piece of chess. Having the uncensored version, know that there is a "censored" version with the word FUCKING crossed out in red. (Censorship sucks) As the name suggests and for my own experience it is a fabulous, unique scent, a real olfactory killing, but not exceptional either to the point of falling from your chair... A good advice, test it before you start blindly, because only the price will make you put the bottle back. Young people and sensitive noses sorry but you will have to go your way. The Woww effect is very present, the olfactory pyramid is unique, although more masculine than feminine, this juice is from many points of view, an olfactory treasure. Conclusion: If you are like me, a TOM FORD perfume addict and a fan of liquid arrogance, don't miss it, because it is a centerpiece in your Private Blend collection. For all those who doubt it, never judge a book by his jacket... Only one solution, buy it. For others, i hope you like it as much as i do. My rating: 9/10

its not a "bad" smell, but it really does smell cheap for how ludicrously expensive it is. $400 for 50ml is beyond disgusting, thats even worse than creed pricing. to my nose, its just so synthetic/chemical smelling. I guess i was expecting something a bit more refined and natural smelling for how much they're charging and because of the name. Smells like cheap, scented baby wipes

I suspected that I would find this to masculine, and now that I had the opportunity to try a sample, I know I was right. This is a very aromatic scent. Sage and lavender are the strongest notes to my nose, especially sage is very easy to single out here. Then comes leather, which is very dry here, a bit rough, but cool and not animalic. Orris might add to the cooling effect. The tonka in this leans hay-like instead of creamy or pronouncedly sweet, and the almond and vanilla just act as supporting notes for the tonka bean and don't stand out much. There is also something in this that smells a bit like anise or black licorice, not sure where this is coming from. To make this scent truly unisex, I think they should have amped up the sweeter notes. The way it is, it's a nice, non-scratchy men's fragrance to me. Of course, women can wear this, too, I just don't think that people who usually wear fragrances marketed to women will be drawn to it. I personally would prefer it on someone else, not on me. Regarding the name, which ruffled a lot of feathers at first: I find it juvenile and a bit cringy, but not really offensive, as the word "fucking" is not directed at any person here and therefore cannot be insulting. My biggest problem with the name is that it raises high expectations, but I guess "Pretty Nice" isn't as catchy.

In this video you will find my first impressions review for Tom Ford Private Blend Collection release Fucking Fabulous. The name says it all but is it really Fucking Fabulous? Please watch to find out. Thank you.

Fucking Fabulous is basically a gentle, creamy, aromatic tonka bomb with an underpinning of bitter, doughy suede. It starts out with a lot of lavender and sage, which gives it a fougere-ish feel, but the plush, brushed-suede texture of the tonka envelops the herbs so completely that it never feels fresh or too foresty.

First of all my English is terrible and sorry about that .. so Let’s begin when i smelled this for the first time immediately i closed my eyes and i start to smile like a little kid met his hero knowing this is it this is it this is it …………………..

I've come to slowly appreciate leather in fragrances when it's done well and smooth. I'm not a fan of smelling like the interior of a brand new car. This scent is just the epitome of the interior of a brand new sports car. I can't fathom how people enjoy smelling like that and it's just not my thing. Leather is very sharp and dark, it takes up almost all of the place.

After testing the last perfumes that I had not smelled from the house, Amber Absolute and Moss Breches, I can now say with confidence that this is the masterpiece. The scent is so unique, creamy, leathery. and luxurious. It makes you feel confident and in charge, but it also can take the stress away. Every time I get a whiff of this I simply cannot hold my excitement back.

Despite the name, this is less an oud scent than a woody vanilla scent. Anyone expecting a powerful pure oud will be disappointed. However this is worth considering if you’re looking for a cozy wood scent for fall/winter. I usually stay away from vanilla forward fragrances but this is not too sweet. There’s more warmth than sweetness here, and there’s a hint of leather and more than a trace of smoke throughout. It’s beautifully nuanced simplicity and I can see this layering well. If you’ve been disappointed by the mixed performances of L’Artisan releases in the last 10 years, the longevity on this is excellent, reliably lasts 12+ hours on my skin.

I am completely digging the sample i ordered. It’s a gorgeous dark and smoky vanilla which has a lot more than those 3 declared notes. And no, don’t worry, it doesn’t smell of Oud, there might be a drop in the whole composition but is undetectable. The first seconds are strong, very middle eastern, but it quickly fades into a damn sexy and elegant dark and complex vanilla. I can smell suede in this, cedarwood, pepper. I would describe it as a moving point in a triangle where the corners would be Babylon, Babycat and Rosendo Mateu 5, made with l’artisan’s unique refine and class. Spot on. The price? Too much.

There's a cream note in this, so maybe that slight lactonic component is enough to steer this away from the tropical coconut smell. Honestly, that's kind of difficult to pull off! It reminds me more of a coconut sorbet, but not so decadent and sweet that it's like coconut cake. Kind of a cool, genius scent. But alas, still a short-lived body mist. Gotta say this is one of the better scents in the "We Mist You" holiday wreath set from PINK.

this is a very special cologne. actually "Special" is a fit word to explain scent of TUSCAN LEATHER. in my idea everybody should smell "tuscan leather" to understand the real concept of "special" word. the people's feedback toward this scent is a shock, first. everybody say this is a very unusual scent. nobody can say i hate it (some women can say it, because the Tom Ford's Perfumes are so heavy). but many of people can definitive say this cologne has a perfect scent. the collection of suede and raspberry and leather and saffron feels so clearly.

One of his coolest perfumes, beautiful and which once made me soooooooooooo dated and which ... I don't need to have. But why? Because, in my opinion, they are better than them, richer and longer-lasting perfumes - yes, yes, I would never expect that the student .. 'copyist' surpassed the master. And this is what happened in this case (anyway, history knows cases of painters, students and copyists who painted better, deeper and .... their works hung in art galleries and national museums as originals). Okay ... and what perfume are we talking about, if it's better than Tom Ford? About Rasasi- La Yuqawam perfumes. Richer, longer fragrant and cheaper. Just take it, buy it, don't regret it. If sometimes Polish online perfumeries lack them, or crazy prices - you can go to ebay or amazon.de, so as not to overpay. To sum up - beautiful Tom Ford perfumes that you can have, but you don't have to - because they are better than them ... sorry..... Mr. Ford.

This scent is historic. Its spawned many inspirations and copies from PDM Godolphin, Widian London, CC Woody Leather, Black Saffron, and more. And you know after trying a lot of them? I still like like original the most. Tom Ford does the whole leather thing the best. No house comes close This isn’t for everyone. Its a masculine scent that men love more than women do. So its not a crowd pleaser. Definitely let it grow on you before you judge it or comeback to it later in your fragrance journey since leather isn't love at first sniff for most. But if you do you'll find this is a very flavorful and well made leather scent that’s addicting Acquired Taste Masterpiece

A pleasant and nice scent indeed, as much leathery as tons of other contemporary leather-based scents (suederal-safraleine type), without any particular twist that lets this stand alone in the crowd. Classy and refined for sure, in a rather safe and tamed down way though: "brownish", smoky, crisp and clean like a new pair of leather brogues. Not bad, actually rather pleasant, just a bit overpriced for the quality. And in fact there's quite some cheaper alternatives which do the same job: Godolphin by Parfums de Marly, Golden Boy by Dueto for instance. 6,5-7/10

I discovered this masterpiece last year, during my trip to Prague when a nice consultant from Douglas offered me a sample, I worn the hell out of that sample and honestly that gave me a strong desire to buy a bottle. Then I discovered Parfumo and I noticed the alternatives, the cheaper options, the "better alternatives"! and spent a lot of money on Rasasi, Godolphin and also Sapphire London .. in the hope to find my "alternative" to TL. But, after trying all of the above, I realized that eventually it makes no sense to use "alternatives" when after all I like and want to wear and own the original, the one which started the whole hunt. It has a very particular smoky smell which I like a lot, ashtray would come to mind but aromatic one and not simply burnt tobacco smell. With fruity Raspberry, which apparently is a JCB trademark, he used it very successfully also in Ombre Nomade from LV. Below you can see me talking for over 10min about Tuscan Leather. Thank you for watching.

I recently enjoyed Tuscan Leather, and without knowing it, I had in my collection three perfumes that smell similar, Arabi Cana from Kolmaz, Attar Mubakhar from Swiss Arabian and Mukhalat Barq from Swiss Arabian, I guess inspired by him, or not ..., no I know.

Tuscan Leather is equal parts Easy Rider and Indiana Jones in fragrance. So, how do you know if this fragrance is for you? You ride a Harley or an Indian? - Tuscan Leather was made for you. You ride a Ducati? - You should overspray some Xerjoff. You ride a Vespa? - Pick up a bottle of Pink Sugar. 2012, the first time I got my hands on a decant of this fragrance.
One of the first Tom Ford Private Blends I ever tried. It began a whole exploration of leather fragrances. Is it still one of the best on the market? Is it still worth the money?

After more than a decade of not wearing any fragrances, I began a side-quest in life to rediscover fragrances and to eventually curate a small collection for myself. Approximately 300 samplings and a couple months later, I discovered some things. I discovered I enjoy fresh scents and gourmands.

Tuscan Leather is the "first real" leather perfume I ever tried a few years ago. Spoiler right at the beginning: to this day it remains in my first place. It's true - in the last 15 years or so, an incredible number of Tuscan Leather imitations or copies have appeared on the perfume market.

Soleil Blanc interesting stuff. The opening has a fresh, kind of ozonic/aquatic vibe without smelling like calone or citrus or cucumber. On dry down most of what I smell is a huge dose of lactones which smell milky, round and rather opaque. These lactones mix with a tuberose and ylang ylang notes, a sheer and bright cardamom note, white musk and a smidge of something that reminds me of polysantol. To me Soliel Blanc doesn't quite smell like suntan oil because of the cardamom and the fact that it doesn't actually smell overtly of coconut. This is exceedingly well blended and it is hard to pick out individual notes even after becoming familiar with it. It certainly smells 'white' to me, and there is a facet that reminds me of the smell of opening a rice cooker when you've cooked high quality jasmine rice. Very nice and highly wearable.

I am delighted and at the same time intrigued by this perfume. When applied, I feel bergamot, but it soon evolves into a harmonious combination of coconut, flowers and tonka. The part that intrigues me is that after a while all I can smell is sunscreen. An expensive, fancy sunscreen, if such a thing exists. But when I smell it near where I sprayed it, I can smell the sweet, creamy coconut along with the flowers. At first I was a little strange, but as time goes by, I smell it all the time, completely addicted to the beach scent of Soleil Blanc. But this beach is not tropical, it's European. I feel like I've been transported to Santorini, Mykonos or the Algarve. Moderate projection for 4 or 5 hours and longevity of 14 hours. It's already become one of my favorites for the summer, it's definitely going to be one of the perfumes I'm going to use the most this season.

If you’re looking for a light, summery perfume, this one might be the one. It smells of coconut, sweet, like a drink, but not too sweet. It’s nice to wear all summer, particularly when outside. The sillage is low and unfortunately the longevity is short on me, so I have to reapply every two hours. Because of that it makes this a very expensive perfume for me and I probably won’t buy it again. It would be nice to wear to a wedding or church when you need a scent, but don’t want to call attention to yourself.

Creamy, fresh, bright and elegant. Hard to get something creamy and fresh at the same time but this is it. Perfect for summer and spring, even autumn maybe. I love the balance and how pleasant the fragrance is. Yet, even though I love how light it feels on my skin it disappears less than a few hours , such a shame.. The scent is probably my favorite from Tom Ford but it doesn’t worth for its money at all.

Soleil Blanc is my absolute favorite from Tom Ford. It is warm, creamy, and fresh. It's full of summer vibes-soft, beachy and smooth I love how it’s not too strong but still lasts well and gets compliments. It’s perfect for summer, but I wear it all year when I want to feel a bit of sunshine. Beautiful and addictive!

There was an episode of Seinfeld where Kramer comes up with the idea that there should be a perfume that smells like the beach....then Calvin Klein makes it in the episode. This is exactly what I would imagine that smells like. Reminds me a little of the brand Hampton Sun, their SPF 15...but without the plastic / chemical smell that you often get with sunscreen.

Tom Ford Soleil Blanc is a weird one. But it's also ...not? I'm having a hard time reconciling this. Imagine if you will, Dior’s Poison. Or, at least the melancholic honey-stewed, midnight-harvested orange blossoms and jasmine flowers portion of it.

This was a very generous Christmas present from my mom. As I have worn Soleil Blanc over the past few months, I have become utterly smitten. true to it's name, Soleil Blanc feels like summer sunshine in a bottle. This scent is absolutely beautiful. Soft, sweet, and creamy it feels very feminine. I actually think this would make an incredible bridal scent.

I'm starting to think the Tom Ford DNA is not for me. Another scent that won't be making it into my collection because there is something in there, an accord, a note (or notes?), a chemical bonding that my nose is picking up and dislikes. The beginning is strong on the tuberose. Powdery, white floral, and even a bit carnal (animalic?). Maybe too strong for me.

One of the pioneers in niche perfumery, L'Artisan Parfumeur differs in its main line from the approach that ended up consolidating and defining the sector in recent years. I perceive that its line has a more abstract and creative face with less focus on both the author and the note itself - even perfumes named after a certain material (such as Premier Figuer) are still more complex and abstract compositions than what often appear in other niche brands. With the Natura Fabularis line the brand seems to go in a direction that unites what has been done in the market with its identity. It comes to me mainly tje influence of two major competitors of the brand in the niche sector in aspects of the line. In Natura Fabularis L'Artisan seems to channel the focus on the perfumer, something that has consolidated and became part of the identity of Frederic Malle. At the same time, it uses the numbering in the identity in a similar way to Le Labo, however indicating the number of attempts of the perfumer until arriving at the final result. Finally, the brand, even if it looks at the abstract, turns more to something concrete, an imaginary garden working in different textures and seeking to evoke romantic and dark sensations (in the same way as Givenchy in its Gaiac Mystique). All this conceptualization does not fail in 2 Violaceum because the perfumer Daphné Bugey does an excellent job in capturing an ephemeral and fragile violet. Violet is a note more versatile than it looks in the perfumery, being able to be worked in directions like powdery, green, aquatic and even leather. The perfumer finds a way to balance the most melancholy and retro side of sweet powdery violetwith the darkest leather aspect of it. For this, we have the carrot giving a certain earthiness and balancing the powdery and sweet side of the idea while the saffron gives a dry spicy aura and a nuance of leather. Secondary green violets nuances are present along with an aura of musk to give depth to a linear and harmonic scent on the skin. It is an idea that has its beauty in the simplicity and harmony of the elements and that certainly works by the fine adjustment of the composition and not by the novelty of the proposed elements.

Subjective individual preferences aside, you might agree that lavender and amber could rank among the few greatest fragrance notes of all time. To the great credit of Antoine Maisondieu, Tom Ford's Beau de Jour gives these two fantabulous notes a vast canvas on which to paint an illustrious image. Beau de Jour pulls off very skillfully something that a lot of fragrances aspire to but can't always achieve: being classic yet modern, subtle yet impressive. As the notes suggest, it opens with a burst of vintage barbershop lavender which is made more modern by the mild sweetness from the base notes. Green, fresh and masculine, as fougeres come. I do also get a little bit of cardamom, although I don't read it on the notes listed here. The high-quality ingredients and smooth cameos from patchouli and basil offer a vibe that has classy written all over it. To me, the best part of the fragrance is that transition from lavender to amber where the latter opens up over time to a wonderfully creative effect. At which point it extinguishes any remaining doubts about whether this fragrance is 'old school'. A note of appreciation for the versatility of this scent as it works all year round, really. Particularly good for spring and fall. Not to mention suitability to a wide variety of occasions from work to dates.

I revisited Beau de Jour and tested with my remaining sample after having tested it in March. This time, I also have Zino for comparison. First off, BdJ is a beautiful barbershop fougere that's been modernized by a subtle touch of sweetness that's apparent in the dry down. This also makes it slightly more floral. I noticed in the opening, as I did in March, a hairspray scent. It didn't last and disappeared in about 15 minutes. Zino is very similar but not the same. Zino has a coarser or rougher opening than BdJ. Also has that whiff of hairspray scent that retreats in about 15 minutes. On the dry down, Zino lacks the subtle sweetness that BdJ has, making it seem less floral overall. Where Zino and BdJ are identical is their performance. It sucks for both. Longevity about 3 hours. Projection good for first 30 minutes to an hour, then a skin scent. I kinda expect that with Zino. Having read all the complaints about it not being as it was, and only a $20 fragrance, I wasn't surprised. I expected much better performance from BdJ, given that it costs about $120 more than Zino. Scratching yet another Tom Ford off my list because of poor performance.

I'm glad this doesn't smell like Davidoff Zino because that smells like an old man. Instead Beau De Jour smells like your rich uncle that always slips you a $50 when he visits. Later in life you realise how cool that uncle is and you'll follow suit. Cool job, hot wife, childless, big house in the country. That's going to be me one day soon. And it will happen because of Beau De Jour. Save this for when you attend a wedding and you know there will be fun bridesmaids. This fragrance requires your best suit and a clean shave then the bridesmaids are all yours. Gentlemen, we owe Tom Ford a big thank you for this one.

Excellent move to transfer it from the private to the signature collection. The differences are minimal, the private is a little more woody in the finish while this remains green & fresh. Strong opening with excellent masculine aromatic lavender that fills the room then marries with strong dusty patchouli and discreet sweet amber. It has a vintage fougere feel but so well made, attractive and modern that in no case you can call it dated or grandpa smell. From beginning to the end it exudes a sense of class, freshness, noble and quality. A masculine aromatic paradise. A lot of compliments from men and women. I consider it to be the top designer fougere at the moment compared to the other fougeres or the reformulations of the old ones. It is easily worn by all ages (25+), in all occasions (office, leicure, events, evening, night out, formal, casual) and in all seasons (except high heat). Performance is excellent for fresh fragrance, duration 10-12 hours with strong projection and sillage for 4-5 hours on my skin. I highly recommend it for testing and especially now that it is still in its original formulation.

Review based on the Private collection Classy but yet modern, suitable for all men. Can be used formally or casually, all four seasons. Smooth but prominent, herbal, spicy yet sweet. To me the green spicy rosemary, basil and mint are the stars in this scent, makes it more modern and casual than other scents in this genre Rock this in a suit or dress it down with jeans and sneaks Signature scent worthy

let's take us back a year. early 2024, i'm reading the ripliad novels by patricia highsmith (the talented mr ripley, etc.). i'm sitting in bed, and wondering how tom ripley, a sauve, classical man, who lives in a chateau in france (at least from book two onwards), who enjoys the finer things in life, would smell.

An old school classic Fougere with a touch of modernity. I own the Private Blend version, for me, what I perceive the most is lavender, herbs, Patcholi and ambar. In comparison with the signature version, I find the PB version darker and more ambery, and the new version fresher and greener. That is only in the opening, I find them identical in the dry down.

This is a wonderful creation by Tom Ford. TBH, I was disappointed at first, when I smelled it. It came to me like a very typical and casual shaving foam for men, that was it. A shaving foam with a vanillic aroma. Anyway, the main idea is that this was pretty boring and "meh" at first. After a while, I've decided to buy a decant and try it again on the skin. Wow!

Beau de Jour is one of my favorite fougères and smells like a beautiful day indeed. A mellow and modern fougère compared to Houbigant and Guerlain releases. Lavender and rosemary are very attractive in the opening, but when the patchouli and amber envelopes the top and heart notes it becomes very refined. It’s smooth, green and very sophisticated.

In keeping with the extreme minimalism and linearity which I've come to associate with much of Jean-Claude Ellena's work, LA HAIE FLEURIE hits me as a straightforward jasmine soliflore. This one is right in the middle of the genre: not too dry and not too indolic. There may be loads of other notes in here, but honestly what I smell is jasmine--not honeysuckle, nor tuberose, nor x, y, or z...! If I needed another jasmine soliflore, I'd definitely consider adding this creation to my collection, but I don't, so I won't, especially since this one has rather poor longevity for what it is... Usually jasmine soliflores last virtually forever on my skin (well, at least until my next bath), but not this one. Smells lovely--while it lasts!

Honeysuckle, daffodil, and orange blossom promise a heavy, enchanting floral fluid that certainly does not suit everyone, and especially not at all times. It reflects the flower-laden atmosphere of a warm summer evening. However, it was a surprise for me to see these notes combined into a perfume by J.-C. Ellena. This piqued my curiosity, and my expectations were not disappointed. La Haie Fleurie is not sweet and lush, as honeysuckle might suggest, but rather, in conjunction with the fully ripe mandarin and oak moss, it is intense but not overly sweet and more aromatic. No rose gives this fragrance a feminine touch; and no lily of the valley or violet allows La Haie Fleurie to drift into the sweet realm, instead, the scent remains serious and resonant, albeit almost somewhat narcotic. As it develops, I briefly discover a somewhat peculiar leather or rubber note, not unpleasant, rather surprising, but it does not change the character of the perfume, especially since it does not stand out and blends into the dark finish. Is this a typical Ellena scent? To be honest, if I hadn't read it, I probably wouldn't have guessed. But now that I know, I do recognize parallels, particularly with Kelly Caleche. Well, there it is the tuberose, here it is the honeysuckle; La Haie Fleurie is also significantly heavier, but that leathery note, the aromatic volume, both share that in common. The perfume does not align with my fragrance preferences, but I found it very interesting to experience J.C. Ellena with a different theme.

Based on the pyramid, I expected something completely different here. Something floral-spicy and sweet. But La Haie Fleurie - in German, Blooming Hedge - is definitely not that. A long, long time ago, there was a fragrance from Papa Yves Rocher called Chèvrefeuille, or Honeysuckle. I loved that scent back then. It was light, fresh, cheerful, and floral, not very sweet, and very easy to wear. La Haie Fleurie continues this scent fantasy. Here, jasmine is also present, which can form a white hedge just like the honeysuckle. Both flowers complement each other wonderfully and can only be perceived individually on the skin. I cannot detect narcissus. The sillage carries a wonderful, white, and radiant floral scent into the room. Later, the orange blossom and vanilla add softness and a little sweetness. However, the fragrance remains bright, radiant, and fresh throughout its entire development. A green woody note joins the base, very faint and pleasant. The longevity is not bad at around 5 hours, but it's not great either. However, it's sufficient for me. Although my expectations for this fragrance were not met, I am not sad about it at all. Because what I received is a beautiful floral scent that I had not encountered before and that is a lot of fun.

My first impression of this fragrance was surprisingly not "blooming hedge," but Diorissimo light. Now, after the scent has been on my skin for 2 hours, I think more of Serge light, specifically "À la Nuit." À la Nuit is my favorite jasmine bomb, but sometimes bombs can be too bombastic. One has to hold back a little with oneself and one's fragrance so as not to leave too much of an impression (or, in the case of some scents, NOT Serge - lasting damage). La Haie Fleurie is one of those. It starts off quite floral-jasmine, but not headache-inducing. Jasmine can sometimes be like the nasty lily of the valley, which strikes out and mows down. The heart note then becomes diffusely floral-heavy, jasmine is no longer discernible on its own, and it’s a bit sweet. Delicious orange blossom. Not too much, rather lovely. The base is woody and greenish, but also slightly creamy. Super. A balancing act that must have required a lot of finesse, very wearable, balanced-floral, and beautiful.

Here you get a very ripe mandarin that is not citrusy at all. Garnished with daffodils, the nose has to get used to it. Fine flowers like honeysuckle, jasmine, ylang-ylang, and African orange blossom frame the whole thing. The vanilla is unobtrusive, the sweetness natural and subtle. The whole thing is served on a bed of moss.

The opening is a photorealistic apple pie, with a very warm, sugary, mouth watering buttery crust undertone to it, it's very gourmand but not in an overly, nauseating way. Then it settles in a generic vanilla only to completely disapear in 20 minutes, even when sprayed on body lotion or vaseline.

This is one of my favorite fall gourmands! The bottle claims a "Ruby apple" note, but it's more of a Fuji apple - cider-y sweet, nothing tart, but still much more dimensional than a Red Delicious. The apple note is enveloped in a cushy, creamy robe and finished with very soft and well-blended sugary-sweet spice (really does feel like a "crystallized ginger" as the bottle notes claim). To me, it's a vanilla-flavored Moon Pie (a treat layered with soft graham cracker cookies, vanilla marshmallow fluff creme, and dipped in a vanilla frosted coating), but also injected with a little bit of apple pie filling. It's not bursting with flavor, the spices won't awaken your senses (no burning cinnamon here) - but it's not meant to: it's something sweet, soft, and comforting to sink your teeth into - enjoying every last bite while huddled under a fluffy blanket, with a cozy candle on a rainy autumn night. P.S. Longevity is excellent as far as mists go - I can still smell it after a few hours. For projection, it creates more of a "personal scent bubble" - but it's a softer fragrance profile in general, so it's great for what it's meant to be (cozy, not loud).

I hardly expected to find love on the tube in London...but my heart missed a beat! The tube is a good place to encounter smells, but usually they are not the pleasant kind....this time I got lucky! A striking, long-limbed, beautiful black woman was sitting not far from me. She was captivatingly beautiful in an androgenous, artsy, Shoreditch way. I was deep in conversation with my boyfriend when my head snapped round, my nose on full twitch... a stunning deep, treacly, oud rose with a woodsy twist filled my nostrils. The dark bottle she was holding was unmistakably Tom Ford.....but which??!! Poor girl. I hope I didn't come across as too much of a perfume psycho. I received a beautiful bottle of Noir de Noir this birthday - some love from my love. To me this is a scent of real, deep love. Not first love or infatuation, not maternal love, nor passionate love, but intense, romantic love. Beautiful. Timeless. The scent is blended to perfection & smells like liquid gold pouring over molten woods & love letters scattered with the darkest of rose petals. The oud is present, but not over-powering & the deep, ambery sweetness is tempered by some patch-love & an earthy herbal twist. I am an oriental-lover & chypres can sometimes turn my stomach, but when they are done well I tend to adore them. Noir is mixed perfectly. Great sillage & lasting power - but not to the point of vulgarity. Just enough evolution & interest to keep you on your toes but not so much as to be loud, unclassy or confused. Inky black with a touch of scarlet, flecked with gold leaf. “The rose speaks of love silently, in a language known only to the heart.” A dark beauty & a real heart-stealer.

Noir de Noir is part of the Tom Ford Private Blend collection. It might be of interest to those of you who love a layered rose scent. It starts off with an opening that is very much about saffron. Noir de Noir is smoothly blended, so much so that the saffron is mildly detected under the sweet rising heart note of semi-sweet chocolate. There is a bit of an alcohol wave here that is like a candied dark liqueur, warm and smooth. Once the liqueur sensation gives way, Noir de Noir opens up to a brooding, dark rose and truffle scent. The heart notes take their time settling in, and it isn't until the dry-down that you can appreciate the blending of the vanilla, rose, truffle and chocolate hovering over a slightly earthy patchouli. There was some confusion by Noir de Noir in the beginning by its imposing dark and mysteriously sweet personality. This fragrance walks a fine line as being unisex and is just a tad more feminine that Tom Ford would like you to believe. Sample first, but it might be love at it first sniff.

~ I have never read reviews or watched video opinions on this TF before other than what I have seen on forum replies and the chain of notes above. I have this on my arm now as I type and I am completely neutral in my initial impression of testing. Of course I get the rose, chocolate (and red wine perhaps?) and it appears to remain the same and linear in the last two hours I have worn it. It is a touch sweet as I am getting more vanilla but perhaps too rich for the type of scent I usually enjoy. The dominant rose here no doubt will be the redeeming factor for my final opinion because I do enjoy florals. It definitely smells well blended and like it's price tag, expensive! My initial impression is this could be worn by a mature, elegant, confident woman or a man of the same but not just any man. He would need to be well dressed and well spoken and with this sprayed on his lapel would be complete! Kind Regards, Plat ~ - I have seen this mentioned in "sexy scent" threads but to my nose this is more about power and magnetism in a bottle!

When Tom Ford created the private blend line i wonder sometimes what did he envision. I've noticed that many people that dont assosiate themselves with the fragrance world find Tom Ford's fragrances "weird" .I feel like its their way of saying they are over done. Thats the thing with TF ,fragrances with rich notes, and amazing blends of ingredients that you would never imagine they would match.Fragrances that with time change as more notes pop out as the day goes by. But here we have Noir De Noir the prime example of an amazing blend ! The rose ...the saffron ...the truffle , I have yet to find something better.Black Orchid parfum came close with the truffle ,but nope Noir De Noir remains the king .Silage and Longevity is something we do not need to talk about ,its incredible,this fragrance lasts all day and projects to a 2-3 foot range for 8 hours at least. The scent on the other hand is something addictive that makes me want to take more sniffs so I can absorb and comprehend all its notes ,the analogies and what stands out to me the most .For about 1 hour all I can smell is the Saffron ,hints of Truffle and Rose and with the combination of floral notes. After that ,all the hints i mentioned pop out more with the oud and vanilla setting in and making it a more intimate fragrance .In my opinion its one of the best Unisex Fragrances. Sometimes I wish it was moved to the signature line so it could recieve a revamped parfum version .I really like its DNA and with a modern take i believe it could be a major hit on the market .

Looking at the list of notes here, I expected Noir de Noir to be an earthy gem built on moss, oud and patchouli, with some full-bodied rose for balance, and a little saffron adding exotic interest to the top notes. Instead, what I find here is just about the exact opposite of that: a sweet, sheer, unobtrusive floriental built mostly on a natural smelling rose note and some gentle vanilla. Earthy it is not. Noir de Noir pairs rose and vanilla beautifully, and carries from top to base a hint of ever-so-slightly tart fruit that doesn't seem to be explained by the notes listed here. It is lovely, and is what all smooth and pleasant rose/vanilla collaborations should aspire to. Rochas Tocade *wishes* it were Noir de Noir. :-) Rose is a note that I seem to enjoy most when it plays a subordinate or supportive role within a bustling ensemble. Chanel No. 19 comes to mind. Which is why I was hoping the patchouli, oud and moss would be louder in Noir de Noir, much, much louder. For anyone madly in love with la diva Rose, however, I think it's a must-try. It's not your grandma's or your mama's rose perfume. It's young and hip and au courant.

He says, "I'm smelling something I don't normally smell when I come into your office. Feet? Dog? What's that smell?" I scramble for skin, shove my wrist to his nose. He says, "That's it, I should have known better." It was Tom Ford Noir de Noir.

Scentrack: The Cure - Lullaby Although not being a rose fan, I must confess I admire how realistic and complex this rose is. A fresh rose merged with dense and dusty chocolate. Like this rose grew from the compost of moist and dark patchouli, priceless tuber and oakmoss, while viscous oud is dripping from the nearby tree.

I was introduced to Noir de Noir by a sales assistant as I was testing Black Orchid. He claimed that this fragrance was similar, yet richer. I'm not so convinced. I'm surprised to discover that some find similarities between this fragrance and Bond No.9's West Side also, which is a fragrance I am very familiar with. I honestly can't compare Noir de Noir to anything.

There's this really cool quote by the late English actor and general wankered raconteur; Oliver Reed. I cannot find it. I really want to find it because I think it perfectly encapsulates the essence of what I look to do with my life and...its a shame I cannot find it.

I will do not be in lace with this Noir de Noir... It's a real olfactive killer, one of the best TOM FORD of the Private Blend collection. As much acclaimed by women as by men. (Although in my opinion more masculine than feminine). Noir de Noir is the perfect combination, the meeting of the dark, the sensual, the opulent...

It is multifaceted, has its citrus, floral, herbal, aromatic and spicy side... The top is citrus with grapefruit and Sicilian lemon (and tangerine?), in addition to the completely refreshing mint leaving a icy sensation in the applied area. Then I feel floral nuances of orange blossom and jasmine along with light green and herbal nuances. In hot or torrid weather, silage reaches half a meter for three hours or more. However, at mild temperatures these numbers are lower because the fragrance does not exude as much. There are many fragrances with the same vibe as this one, but the naturalness of the notes contained here makes it a masterpiece.

The beginning is juicy, perfectly acidic and laced with hints of currant leaves - natural, green leaves infused with sugar and chlorophyll, not chemical mutants straight out of Lacoste Essential. These leaves aren't literal either, because if it weren't for the list of notes, I probably wouldn't have guessed their presence right away. Their scent is slightly shifted towards mint and green freshness, and the dusty nuances have been completely wiped away. Tom Ford again shows that he can play with citrus brilliantly. This is the third fragrance (after Neroli Portofino and Rive d'Ambre) in this climate that knocks me out. It's not some over-complicated fragrance and doesn't develop on the skin in a surprising way. But the upside is that Ford has kept a moment in Mandarino di Amalfi. This moment is dedicated to the tangerine. And it is wonderful! To be a little more reliable, however, I will write that later, after an hour or two, the tangerine slowly transforms into orange. The green note, on the other hand, loses its organic and tart overtones. It becomes a little more dull, woodsy, mossy even. A delicate touch of vetiver appears. But this is a minor detail that I noticed after using this perfume several times. The scent is best described in three words: ‘the green kingdom of tangerine’. Simple, brilliant and sincere. Highly recommended!

It's summer, some breeze is helping you out with the heat, and with the breeze comes the beautiful and natural scent of lemons. You breath deeply in and out. Some leaves and green in the background. That was a well spent afternoon with Tom Ford

Ι love this summer scent, it's very citrusy fresh, well-balanced, crisp and vibrant. I mostly feel mandarin, grapefruit and mint but it also has some sweetness too. This fragrance makes me smile and dream about sea breeze and drinking cocktails on a beach bar while wearing my white soft linen shirt!

This is a fragrance that confused me at first. I didn't like it at all, initially. I was getting an old grandma's closet vibe, with a smell of freshly washed clothes with a cheap detergent mixed with an old, woody furniture vibe, also owned by the same old and poor granny. After a few wearings, the fragrance started to bloom and evolve into something beautiful. More citrus, more acidic, more refined and crisp. I was really start to enjoy it. Since the first wearing It felt like a different kind of a freshie but I wasn't sure if that was in a good/bad way. Now, I know its worth. As I said, very citrusy, fresh, acidic and crisp, refined. This will be exceptional for the day (in my humble opinion) but if you love it that much you can also give it a shot for the night time. It sure gets very positive attention (this hapenned to me almost every time I wore it) and the performance is part of the show. Not a shy fragrance, it stays with me for 7-8 hours, with a 7.5/10 projection (it still projects after 4-5 hours and I was getting told that even if I could barely smell myself at that point). I am really enjoying it ! Pretty versatile for the warmer days, it can be casual/formal/intimate but I think it's a beauty and deserves more than casual usage. The price is so&so. I still have a decent amount of it (I mean a generous decant) and I won't buy a full bottle soon. It smells very nice and it's not your daily/typical freshie. You should try it ! Overall score 7.7/10

Favorite scent. If you don’t like the smell you probably bought it on discount/fake. It lasts long if you put more than 2 sprays. I put 4-5 sprays and I can still smell it on my clothes after a day of wearing it. I bought the last 100ML bottle on from Nordstrom . Com for collection purposes and there are only 50ML bottles left. When I was 16, or 15, I went to south of France with my best mate at the time and his brother and his brother's best mate. We slept on the beech and ate shit from the supermarket and well..it was a typical teenage adventure. Anyway it was early 90s and I remember that summer holiday because of three things : 1.

It's decidedly gentler than the usual orange juice, whose bitterness still keeps any enjoyment it could give me out of reach. I discovered this perfume at Sephora Lyon in 2018. typical light fragrance for summer, fruity and fresh. nothing new or fantastic for someone who has already tested hundreds of fragrances. it smells a bit of orange, citrus fruits and eau de cologne. it lasts a maximum of 2 hours on the skin, the sillage is weak.

There are plenty of citrus-based summer perfumes. This one is special as it the closest one to mandarin I know, even though heart note says orange blossom. Unfortunately, longevity is very low, while a lot of summer scent does not last long this one is leading after like 30 min it goes away. This is a pity as the scent itself is not bad.

When you first apply "Fleur de Lune | L'Artisan Parfumeur," a delicate veil of floral notes unfolds - jasmine, magnolia, perhaps a hint of osmanthus. They feel light, almost transparent, yet so intense that you simply cannot forget them. But Fleur de Lune is not a typical floral fragrance. Behind this fine, almost vulnerable bloom lies something deeper - a quiet, melancholic warmth. Gradually, the leather and saffron emerge, not loud, not heavy, but like a memory. It's as if you wanted to give flowers... and then forgot them in a leather jacket. The rain has stopped, the night smells of moonlight and decisions. The blooms are still there, but different - warmer, quieter, somehow truer. I remember a meeting... It had rained lightly, and he stood there, in a black leather jacket, with these flowers tucked inside. No neat bouquets, just loose blooms he wanted to give me. But I turned away, took a step forward, and looked up at the sky. The moon was clear above me, silver and calm, and in that moment I knew I could let go. Fleur de Lune carries for me exactly this feeling: delicate and strong at the same time, bittersweet and liberating. A fragrance that gives me the strength to be there for myself - not looking back, but continuing on my own path in the light of the moon. Like a memory that you let go of to find yourself again. (I perceive the scent distinctly - perhaps not screaming or kitschy, no, but soft and present for a good 5 to maybe 6 hours. I know that may be too little for some, but those who know L'Artisan Parfumeur fragrances understand: these scents never scream. They whisper and remain unforgettable because of that. Thank you for reading. Yours, MissMystre)

My first impressions are not that good. I was hyper excited about this, and it's what probably made me feel disappointed. The scent turned into a much more masculine direction, with an unexpected overdose of woodines that will make you remember Bois Farine or the more recent Il Etait Un Bois. I feel like they used the same core or one or more accords of it. The first minute is 95% similar to the Original, but then it turns completely white woody. I don't smell any pepper, a very small touch of incense in the middle of its development, but then it's all about clean woods, like you're in a forest, with a very shy presence of a green and more pungenr neroli compared to the creamy and bright orange flower of the OG. I feel like they boosted the performance quite a lot, but if you love the OG like i do, this might disappoint you. Not because it's bad, it's a very nice fragrance, but it smells different from the OG. Might give it some other tries, trying to wear it as a stand alone / not a remix scent.

For years, I struggled with a neroli trauma, and as is often the case, the trigger lies in childhood. The culprit is quickly identified: my maternal grandmother. (Sorry, Grandma!) She was a strict woman who tolerated no frills and knew nothing of sophistication. However, two fragrances were always found on her dresser: Tosca (Winter!) and 4711 (Summer!). The latter, in particular, was considered a kind of panacea, and so it happened that I, as the firstborn granddaughter and thus the only potential victim, was occasionally sprinkled with it (for refreshment!). I hated it, but for diplomatic reasons (family peace!), I never told her. From then on, neroli was to remain a disruptive factor that spoiled many otherwise beautiful scents. At least until recently. L'Artisan Parfumeur has achieved with Histoire d'Orangers Extrême what many have failed to do before: I feel reconciled with neroli. That really means something, as this fragrance revolves - not surprisingly - around the duo of neroli and orange blossom. Yet these two main actors are excellently complemented by delicate incense and a bright musk. Additionally, I also perceive an amber note. An overall harmonious ensemble that fits well in a restrained dosage for (high) summer, but will certainly flatter on cooler autumn days as well. Unfortunately, I cannot make a comparison to the non-extreme original version. However, I would recommend a test sniff to anyone who enjoys warm, sweet, and creamy fragrances with a subtle spiciness. Longevity and sillage are simply fantastic, which is why I would advise everyone to use it in moderation.

A hot and bright summer day that's finally started to mellow out in the late afternoon as golden hour approaches. Heavy, sun-kissed limbs from a day spent outdoors, walking along the beach or playing in the pool, and the promise of nothing left to do that evening but relax. Pure insanity to me that the first time I smelled this, I didn't like it-- I guess it pays to keep your samples around, because smelling this now is heaven. It's all creamy, sunscreeny, soft coconut and subdued white florals goodness. Instantly makes you wish you were at the beach, or at the very least, planning a trip there. The easiest summertime reach you could ask for.

There are certain afternoons when time feels like it slows down, as if the earth itself is drunk on the languid sweetness of the sun. Tom Ford’s Eau de Soleil Blanc captures that very feeling in a bottle. It opens like a thin mist of coolness — a gentle spray of neroli and bitter orange, light and glimmering, just like the air shimmering above hot sand. The first notes don't shout. They move softly, like the whisper of a palm leaf in the breeze. As the perfume settles, the world seems to thicken with a sleepy kind of richness. The soft sweetness of coconut and the creaminess of pistachio seep into the skin, mingling with the golden dust of bergamot and ylang-ylang. It’s the scent of sun-warmed skin, of fine grains of salt left behind by the retreating sea, and of sunblock lazily sprayed from a white canister, melting into your pores. Somewhere nearby, someone laughs over the rim of a cold Caipirinha, lime and sugar swirling in lazy circles at the bottom of a glass. By the time the heart notes emerge — jasmine, tuberose, and orange blossom — the boundaries between yourself and the afternoon have blurred. You are neither wholly awake nor asleep. You are simply being, suspended in the hazy warmth. The drydown is soft, almost imperceptible — a delicate tracing of amber, benzoin, and a hint of tonka bean — like the memory of the sun pressed gently into your skin after it has slipped below the horizon. In the end, Eau de Soleil Blanc is not so much a fragrance as it is a state of mind: a slow, radiant surrender to a summer that seems, for a few fleeting hours, as if it will never end.

I haven't tried Soleil Blanc yet, so I'll review the Eau on its own merits. To me this doesn't smell all that coconutty as some reviewers around the web say, instead of I find orange blossom to be much more prominent here. This is a creamy white floral that recalls expensive sunscreen lotion, but has some layers that make it more sophisticated than that. It has a vanilla base that warms it up and keeps the floral and citrus notes from going too screechy, but there is also something cooling about this. The cardamom and pink pepper are quite dry and almost woodsy leaning, which works beautifully with the creaminess of the other notes. It's all so smooth and soft. Cardamom is really noticeable to me, I guess my nose perceives this scent a little different than the majority. But I definitely think it fits the marketing, it's a light, summery fragrance and absolutely smells like the color white to me. The only thing I was a bit disappointed about is that the pistachio note is so subdued, I can only smell it for a moment in the opening. Nevertheless, this is a gorgeous summer dream.

A smell of vanilla, coconut and citrus. But it's quite difficult to say because my skin literally refused this edt; the smell was very faint and it disappeared almost immediately. I had to spray it several times to be able to smell it, totally crazy! In summary, I would say that paying so much to have a perfume that has such poor staying power and which literally smells like sunscreen, well... it's not for me. Cheaper alternatives exist.

You know my stance on Tom Ford fragrances, but for some reason I cannot seem to stay away, because his fragrances are that good. When smelled from the bottle, that is. On skin, it's a whole 'nother story. This summer, I seem to have been on a tropical hunt chasing pineapple scents and those reminiscent of exotic coastlines. Naturally, I was interested in Eau de Soleil Blanc. Eau de Soleil Blanc has a huge composition of notes, on Fragrantica, and I'm not even going to try to write them all down, but all I need to know is this: citrus, coconut, petitgrain, vanilla, benzoin, tonka and amber... I'm sold. So how is Eau de Soleil Blanc? A powerful citrus burst at first spray! Yum! Soon after, I smell the white florals, the coconut, the sunshine, the tropical island. Tom Ford has a way of luring you in, but will this fragrance last at all? In all honesty, Eau de Soleil Blanc reminds me of Unforsaken by Kerosene, which is on my wishlist. It's been almost a year since I've smelled it, so I'm not completely sure, but I keep revisiting my old review, because I remember it making a big impression on me. Eau de Soleil Blanc might be a more generic version of Unforsaken, a more digestible one. I keep getting hints of tiaré, which is probably the white florals in combination with the coconut. After dry down, there's something Monoï by Yves Rocher about it too... What I thought would be a unique fragrance is actually not that special at all, it seems. Eau de Soleil Blanc is also more soapy than the other two, but I wore it on a 7 hour shift and I am pleasantly surprised how long I could smell it on me and taking my jacket on at the end of the day, I got full whiffs of it. Never thought that would be possible with a Tom Ford!

Tom Ford Eau de Soleil Blanc was released several years ago as a flanker to Soleil Blanc, fittingly lighter, fresher, and less dense than the original, a light-and-creamy fresh floral that has a hint of sunscreen, the main notes being citruses, a parade of white florals (tuberose, jasmine, ylang ylang), and vanilla.

For some reason i really want to like this 2018 offering from Tom Ford but sadly i can't I just don't even though i wear it often. Makes a lot of sense doesn't it?? Anyway the summery beachy smell grabs you by the swim trunks and reels you in. The down part is that's about all it does.

I adore Tom Ford’s fragrances. Three of which I have rated 10 for the scent. And I am not done with testing yet. There are still so many gems to be found among his many combinations of notes. I admire his ingenuity and courage. He delivers interesting and breathtaking perfumes and I have to own them.

It smells expensive (because, well... it is), but more importantly, it feels like luxury. Think: designer sunscreen, private villa, golden hour. It’s soft, sunlit, and perfectly androgynous. I have already tried to describe it in my comment on Soleil Blanc, the big brother of this Eau, and in so many other comments about Tom Ford Private Blends as well: that diffuse woundedness and fallen nature that I discover behind the seemingly self-confidently radiant facade of the fragrances in the small, vaguely apothecary bottle-shaped flacons.

For over 30 years, the point has been made, the boundary drawn, the argument formulated: “Mûre et Musc” has a truly parfum-historical function, serving as a milestone of modern perfumery and the foundation of what is called “niche.” Jean Laporte went ahead in 1978 and articulated in the language of scent what time it was: Confident, challenging, and one hundred percent synthetic, only one fragrance motif was placed at the center of a perfume. Without softening it, making it more pleasing, or diluting it. Without embellishments, without frills, without compromise. Musk and blackberry. Period. All other ingredients served only to emphasize this simple and clear main motif. For the first time, not even a little attention was paid to the majority taste and the current fragrance trend; rather, the laws of art were placed above those of the market. Thus began what would (somewhat paradoxically) develop into its own market: The niche. 30 years later, a child of this niche perfumery celebrates the fragrance, its creator, and its own freedom: Bertrand Duchaufour creates an extrait for the anniversary of the great scent that is completely rooted in the present, while simultaneously being a jubilant homage to the late seventies fragrance. Since the point has been made so clearly and for so long, Duchaufour does not need to fundamentally, dogmatically, and with artistic defiance formulate something unique that marks the spearhead of the avant-garde and contradicts all supposedly valid rules… that was already taken care of by Laporte back then. No, Duchaufour can go ahead and highlight the beauty of the classic with friendly and pleasant, quite mainstream means. He can improve the not-so-optimal longevity of the first “Mûre et Musc” and he can close the circle to the perfume history of the 20th century with a proper dose of oak moss in the base. A successful performance, a joyful and beautiful celebration! The main note of “Mûre et Musc” is also the pivot of “Mûre et Musc Extrait”: It’s all about this one musk-berry accord. But in the homage fragrance, it is staged richly, playfully, indulgently, and quite extravagantly. All steps of the original are made slightly more pronounced and simultaneously harmoniously combined. The beginning is a bit more citrus-fresh and emphasized with pepper, the middle is overflowing with floral notes, pleasing, radiant, and the base is a bit heavier, better anchored to the ground, and more sensual. The extrait celebrates the original with applause, wit, and a super-happy underlying mood. What emerges is melodic, well-proportioned, and beautifully complete. Nevertheless, the original is always clearly detectable. It is not questioned or improved; rather, it is truly celebrated. “Mûre et Musc Extrait” does not relativize “Mûre et Musc,” but pays tribute to the beauty, as well as the importance of the milestone. And it does so in a smiling, harmonious, and contemporary way. Pure intertextuality. ____________________________________________________ My jubilant homage goes to Lolle, to whom I owe this beautiful fragrance. :-)

This morning I thought to myself, hey, 'you have all day, you can test a perfume thoroughly again. But sometimes it happens that either your own inner rush, usually caused by a neurotic imbalance, or, even worse, the longevity of the chosen scent messes up your all-day testing plans. null of this applies today. Everyone wants to take a look, everyone wants to pinch its rosy raspberry cheeks. But I protect it, let no one near. They all just want one thing. Its time. Just quickly away! Time is Berry!

I don't tend to like peony but that violet is special and I don't get that cheap A Thousand Wishes peony scent. Been wearing all day and also spritz it on before bed. Will be bummed when it runs out. Even if i see the resemblance with Guerlain´s vetiver, i wouldnt want to have a bottle of this last one, meanwhile i am surprisingly very fond of Tom Ford´s. I say surprisingly because i normally appreciate a touch of weirdness in a fragance and Grey Vetiver is extremely civilized and classic in spirit. This could never scare anybody. A clean, luminous vetiver, that veers to the green rather than the earthy, is the core of this fragance. Opening with lemon and bergamot, this is not an extremely bright one: the sun beams are diffused by a thin white fog, since it is not too cold nor warm. Grey Vetiver is tepid, fresh and foamy. The herbal, citrusy opening is very pleasant, but is the heart and evolution of the perfume what i find so wonderful. There is a salty aspect in Grey Vetiver, that makes me think more in dolphins and other cetaceans´skin grayness rather than the color of a gentleman´s tailor-made suit. Probably the amber listed is no other than ambergris. Actually, this lukewarm saltiness is similar to Hermes´Eau des merveilles (based on ambergris) and probably even more to the also vetiver-based Sel Marin by Heeley. A residual hesperidic nuance enlightens, and a balmy touch of tonka sweetens, the cool, silver vetiver. Buttery orris gives a thick, smooth powderiness. Grey Vetiver is sublte and elegant sea escapade for everyday. Would love to own a bottle!

~ This is one of those negative reviews that rarely get written but I write it with "all due respect" to those that do enjoy this one. After ordering a sample and wearing TFGV for a few days having even tried to train my nose with multiple wearings to smell past the opening and dissect the few notes in the chain alas it is just not for me. Much like with TdH I just can't enjoy the combination of vetiver and citrus. To "my nose" it is just far too green, sharp, bitter and earthy perhaps? But this is definitely aptly named with Grey because that is exactly the color it evokes in me. ~ Kind Regards, Pt1 (with a nod to performance) Sillage ~ Perfect 8/10 Longevity ~ All work day 9/10 Scent ~ "IMHO" 5/10

This one is an inoffensive, respectful and clean frag that is just perfect as signature scent. Wear it to the office, to meetings or even to wedding... it just works without shouting “HERE I AM!”. The vetiver is very prominent without being “dirty”. This is a clean vetiver frag, a soapy one. I prefer this over th EDT alltho that one is fantastic as well. To my nose this is a more fuller version and the edt is more light and citrus. However I don’t have the need to own both, but maybe you do?

Grey Vetiver is a good contemporary vetiver, “grey” in fact as regards of its sort of urban and discreet elegance, with a subtle smoky undertone well contrasting the luminous head notes. Clean and sharp, but also showing a pleasant feel of “dark” refinement. Simple, versatile, safe in pretty much any circumstance: a compelling modern version of a classic vetiver cologne, that sort of fresh-woody stuff you can bath in any time of the year always smelling nice and elegant. Surely not that unique or groundbreaking, but classy, well made and highly enjoyable. 7/10

Tom Ford has a thing for recreating older, classic fragrances for a modern-day audience. Here, he took the note of Vetiver, a note with a history of use in men's fragrances (ever since Guerlain's classic in 1959). Because of this, he also associates Vetiver with male tailored clothing & style, as well as money. I think this is what he was aiming for here with his Grey Vetiver, a modern take on an old classic note. Grey Vetiver opens up with a citrus top of Grapefruit, Orange Blossom and Sage, but the Veitver is there from the start. This is also a somewhat linear scent, as the Vetiver note is present from start to finish. I also get Nutmeg, Pimento and a dry, almost powder-like Orris note in the background followed by Oakmoss and some woods in the drydown. I see this as something of a "suit and tie" or "corporate boardroom" type of fragrance, and I think it would work better on men than women, but could also be worn as unisex. Ultimately, for me... Having tried the Guerlain Vetiver before trying the Tom Ford, I find that I like the Guerlain version more (to me it smells more natural), but that doesn't mean Grey Vetiver doesn't have it's place. For one thing, it's in Eau de Parfum concentration, and does smell "modern" to most people, while the Guerlain can come across with mixed reactions from many people. I think this is great, fresh, work fragrance but in my opinion it could also be worn in a casual setting. I also think that for people who don't like a deep, smoky type of Vetiver (or for people who don't like Vetiver as a note) would find this easier to warm up to and appreciate (and ultimately wear). Overall I would say, if you didn't like the Guerlain, you will probably like this one, and if you did like the Guerlain, you will find this more accessible to wear in the modern day (ie it will "fit in" with modern trends). I do think this is a "safe" fragrance, but at least it's an extremely well-made one, and one which I wish more men would wear thesedays... instead of the tiring, boring aquatic nonsense which has flooded the male market so recently. A good "modern" male fragrance. Well made and up-to-date.

Very delightful and sweet fresh dusty vetiver that opens yummy and goes through foggy fresh ultrachic pattern. This fragrance is much favorable for fans of designers; a trap to draw you into niche fragrances. Grey Vetiver reminds me a doctor, probably optometrist, in steamed up shirt and perfectly shaves face, very decent very polite!

I agree with the previous comments about this being a more modern take on Guerlain's Vetiver. That can be either a good thing or a bad thing depending on how you feel about that scent. In my case, I don't care much for it and the same goes for Grey Vetiver as well. Grey Vetiver is super fresh and inoffensive.

This is a wonderful vetiver based scent, definetely a must have for who likes this note. Not as dark as Encre Noire neither as sweet as L'Occitane Vetyver, this scent is a very well balanced vetiver-based fragrance - i would say this is a soft vetiver. The sage in the opening and the moss in the base turns really make it different from many vetiver-based scents.
If you love Vetiver by Guerlain but feel it is dry or sharp Vetiver, so you have to try this one. I believe you would love it, if you normally love Vetiver smell with a hint of Citruses.

This begins like Beethoven's violin concerto: a few gentle taps on the drums - one might think the drummer is merely testing his instrument. Then the strings entering, almost like a morning mist rising from the surface of the river. And then it's enveloped you, perhaps before your conscious mind has even fully formed the idea that it has begun atall.

I'm still sort of reeling from no 8. I tried it yesterday due to the generosity and perfume-camaraderie of perfume critic Katie Puckrik, whom I bumped into while perfume shopping. A celebrity sighting! No 8 starts with an iris root so carrot-seedy that the two notes actually seem distinct. They converge slowly and a throaty, rich iris-dominated floral picture comes into focus. Just into the heart, whammo! An exceedingly strong, exceedingly gorgeous soapy note grabs the wheel. (I kind of wondered about Katie's "shower day plus one" comment at this point.) Soon, in a convincing juxtaposition, a musky, ripe, body scent starts creeping through the soap and brings back the root-like, almost mucky feel of the iris/carrot seed bit. While not similar in scent, no 8 captures that clean over dirty intimacy that is the heart of Amouage Gold Man. I've only smelled it on a strip, but where most perfumes are a statement, or perhaps a simple question, no 8 is more like an argument, an assertion, and I'm completely persuaded. I’m certain I’d have the urge to nuzzle up to anybody wearing this.

This is the first neroli perfume I bought for my collection, I really like its smell… but unfortunately the performance of this perfume is just terrible. The longevity is below average and the sillage is not exciting either. With all my love for the fragrance, I sold it and bought this perfect perfume instead: Néroli Oranger which is both very similar in scent and also performs better. It's very disappointing that Tom Ford doesn't invest in the quality of their product other than the scent itself. This perfume doesn't last more than 4 hours. 7/10.

Tom Ford's exclusive line is how niche perfumery should not be. It consists basically of a monolithic marketing concept, optimized by special perceptions of sales psychology. The outcome is a fancy scent bar with numerous, quickly developed perfumes. In the past, the real maîtres among the perfumers allowed themselves years and years of development before they finally decided to release a scent to the public – but at Tom Ford, they simply buy what is quickly available for money. All perfumes of Tom Ford's exclusive line that I have come across so far are optimized for quick sale: the customer is presented a spectacular head note, but with not much behind it. Just like this is Neroli Portofino: the start is overwhelmingly good – one is pleased with so much delicacy and refinement. Airiness, freshness, but also considerable orange-y volume mingle together in perfect balance. Any possible customer can easily see the difference between Neroli Portofino and a Neroli-cheapie like 4711. However, a slight glance on the packaging should make you suspicious: A neroli scent, labeled as “Eau de Parfum“? Usually, neroli is not very enduring. As a flowery, citric note, it is mainly being used as top- or maybe heart note in many traditional colognes. After this short period, it fades away. And for this reason, neroli is the center of many simple, short-living Colognes – such as Guerlains' Eau du Coq, a true gem. But since a few years, we sometimes find neroli notes with monstrous life period. Examples are Colonia Essenza by Acqua di Parma and the number 201 from Micallef's Art Collection line. Did they find means to fix neroli? Or is it some chemical replacement of natural neroli oil? I suppose the worst since I came across this neroli type of scent blown into the air by a room freshener machine. Basically, Mandy Aftel writes in her book about the advantage of natural perfume oil that the batches all slightly differ from each other, since the oils are never completely pure. On the other hand synthetizised scents smell like „dead“. You may put this aside as the thoughts of an esoteric natural perfumer – but as far as neroli is concerned, I can very well follow these thoughts. To me, Neroli Portofino is just as dead as the central cemetry of my home town. Once the interesting top note has settled there is only sweet and sticky kind of neroli with maybe some amber. This is so solid, it does not move an inch! And it never leaves you alone, just like unwelcome relatives. I can only describe this as an olfactory tinnitus! With Neroli porofino, you seriously peril your sensitivity for scent. It is just the attraction of neroli that it is fleeting. One should never even consider holding it! Whoever wears Neroli Portofino in a certain period of time will surely develop an averseness against it. So, this is also another way to put off customers. The marketing concept of Tom Ford is just as sustaining as the deforestation of the amazonas region. At the Tom Ford scent bar, customers' interest is being exploited, not aroused. They will not return to the perfume shop for good.

I have a problem with Tom Ford's Private Blend Collection ... 90% of it is pure bilge! Smoke and mirrors ... there are perhaps two that I would consider owning (I've diligently tried all of them)... and then only if they were on major markdown. Neroli Portofino has to rank as one of the biggest ripoffs in perfume history. I buy litre bottles of Eau de Cologne to add to my bedding laundry for less than $10 a pop ... even that has better projection and longevity, and SMELLS better too! Pretty bottles and creative marketing do not a great fragrance make, and in this case they don't even make a good one! This is a less than mediocre sub par attempt at a classic cologne ... with a whopping price tag! Amber? Where? Vanilla? I beg to differ. Cheap orange blossom with a touch of Bergamot and a huge dollop of Iso E Super (to my nose at least) ... c'mon!! With any luck this nasty phenomenon that has the cheek to include itself within the revered halls of niche perfumery will just go away. On the other hand, I'll never be spending any of my money on it :) ... so I'll just ignore it 'til it disappears.

Neroli Portofino is one of the main problems that I have with Tom Ford's Private Blend Collection. Whilst many of the scents within the collection smell expensive and interesting- Neroli Portofino comes up smelling quite childish almost, it has a distinct freshness to it that will absolutley appeal to many people but it just doesn't justify its ridiculous price tag. Neroli and Bergamot dominate this fragrance, they offer a very strong- very potent citrus, fruity smell that borders on being annoying. Add to this a very staunch and synthetic smelling mandarin which sort of takes the fragrance into very cheap smelling territory where the fragrance takes on a deodorant like consistency which frustrates me because its evident, already that this fragrance is not worth the price. I won't go into to much detail about this fragrance because it is very basic. Its a Synthetic Neroli explosion which just does not do the job that an Eau De Parfum should. It lacks in depth, originallity and quality. All things which Tom Ford normally likes to associate himself with. Neroli Portofino is just another example of laziness at a very high price. To its credit, the lasting power is fantastic, but its composition is just awful, its not the kind of scent i'd want to smell all day long. After 20 minutes I hopped into the shower and scrubbed this off my body.

I wasn't fully aware that I love orange blossom as a note in perfume until I stumbled upon this beautiful emerald bottle with its rather sexual ad campaign. In fact, contrary to what everyone's been saying, I would definitely wear this to arouse my loved one, no doubt about it. Neroli Portofino may smell summery and clean, but there's something about it that puts a smile on my dial, makes my eyes roll back in my head and feel like a goddess both inside and out. Yes, Neroli Portofino smells like soap, but an expensive bar of luxury soap. I get a massive load of orange blossom in this fragrance complimented with a sweet and citrusy-green bergamot accord. To be honest, I find this fragrance sweet and feminine on my skin. I'm surprised that this is a unisex fragrance, however it may smell very different on a man's skin. Everyone's saying that Neroli Portofino is just an overpriced Acqua di Parma cologne. Really? I've smelt almost the whole range and I can't say that I found any of them as appealing as this. Colonia is a smooth, crisp lemon scent to my nose, no orange blossoms there I'm afraid. Give this fragrance to me wrapped in a big, white ribbon and I'll happily wear Neroli Portofino as my Summer signature. Even better, the longevity is superb, nothing like those Summer colognes that my skin enjoys eating until there's nothing left. I highly recommend.

Neroli Portofino is Tom Ford's take on the classic eau de Cologne type of fragrance. That is, orange flower blossom, citrus, herbs and amber. This is a very simple recipe, and it's one which is available in many forms. This fragrance is just Tom Ford's take on it. It opens up extremely fresh and soap-like. It's one thing I love about this fragrance.

The price discussion. I face it with all the Fords as well as many other costly perfumes. Will you pay, for example, $250 for a quality perfume when there are other comparable perfumes at a fraction of the cost? There is a market for costly perfumes, and if people are willing to spend big bucks, more power to them.

There’s little left to say about this fragrance, that other fragrance snobs didn’t say already. Neroli Portofino is a mildly pleasant, incredibly overpriced citrus-neroli cologne with a musky-herbal undertone and a sort of “laundry” soap feel. Just place it anywhere in the Dantesque limbo between 4711 and Acqua di Parma citrus colognes.

In eighth grade, I wrote a report about Sun Myung Moon and the Unification Church, and I've been thinking about cults ever since. They arise with remarkable frequency in Western civilization, in virtually every, even the most unexpected of realms, including perfume. Just look at the excitement generated by the recent release of Tom Ford's new Private Collection fragrances.

Sometimes you meet a fragrance which is a bit simple and yet offers just what you need. Tom Ford's neroli portefino exactly does that for me. Some of you think that neroli portefino is too simple, but I absolutely don't agree with that. I prefer sweet-spicy oriental scents in the colder seasons and white floral fragrances and woody-aquatics in summer and spring time.

"Mon Numéro 4" is the exclusive fragrance from the Mon Numéro series for the London L'Artisan Parfumeur store, and a distinct "Britishness" is also evident. The inspiration here comes from the scents of classic barbershops; Bertrand Duchaufour himself describes the fragrance as a modern fougère. But this scent is not only suitable for a visit to a barbershop or an English club with heavy leather chairs, but is generally a fine fragrance primarily for autumn. Right from the start, you are confronted with lavender, this beautiful and classic fougère top note with its aromatic old-fashionedness, but also a green spiciness that does not come across as herbal here, but rather with a cool elegance. Vanilla, this note I fear, which can easily spoil a fragrance, is subtly noticeable from the beginning, becoming stronger later on, but fortunately lacking any heavy and exaggerated sweetness. The meeting of the velvety warmth of vanilla with the silky coolness of lavender evokes the typical powderiness of a fougère. The leather note is sometimes hard to grasp; here it lacks the repulsive scent of leather jackets for me. I see it here as a foundation of the fragrance, creating depth and establishing the connection between lavender and vanilla. Classic and distinguished, aromatic, subtly fresh and powdery, soothing like a well-tailored suit (the latter a modified quote from L'Artisan Parfumeur), also calming through the aromatherapeutic classic lavender, this favorite note of mine, and definitely: For Gentlemen and Gentlewomen alike.

This smells like the most delicious peach dessert ever! Sweet ripe peaches, a tiny bit of booze, quite a bit of patchouli, delicious warm spices, woods and some fresh grapefruit to give it a kick in the opening. What a masterpiece! Longevity is good, stays in hair for even longer (2nd day I can still smell it). It doesn't smell like ice tea. Ice tea smells cheap, this smells expensive. It better! Because this baby is VERY expensive. You MUST love peaches and patchouli in order to like this. Good scent option for intimate nights, as any good gourmand scent would be.

I looooooove alcohol in perfumery. It smells like a juicy cognac-filled peach, covered with red orange juice. In autumn smells so magic, but for winter it smells weaker. But Tom Ford is literally overpriced for my boudget, so I got good analogue of it. It remains me a time before I went to hospital with pneumonia.
