I was so excited for this because people said it reminded them of cinnamon rolls - but this wasn't even close to cinnamon rolls unfortunately. To me, this is cinnamon toast crunch that you left out in a bowl where the milk turned warm and spoiled. It's got a distinct, "yeast-y" note that just doesn't hit the mark. I have yet to find a realistic cinnamon bun in a perfume, so if you have a recommendation please let me know - but as a side note, BBW's "Pumpkin Cinnamon Bun" is the most realistic cinnamon bun fragrance I've ever smelled in a non-baked good. Has the cream cheese frosting, bun, and spices all rolled into one!

Anyone who has thoroughly explored a liquor store has likely seen bottles with the word "solera" sprinkled on the label. Suppose the aging solera system is a foreign concept to you. In that case, it's easy enough to understand, primarily if you paint a picture of the process in your head. A solera system involves rows of barrels stacked on top of each other. The lower row of barrels, called the solera, contains the spirit that has aged the longest. When it comes time to bottle some of that spirit, it's taken from this lower row of barrels, say about a third of the content. Then, part of the liquid from the row above is transferred to the barrels of the rows below. And so on, up to the upper barrels, filled with brand new un-aged spirit. The complete system can develop, and the process repeats itself repeatedly. But what does the solera method have to do with this perfume? Simple. There is a woody alcoholic mention of brandy among the ingredients, which releases intensely during the bouquet's opening. This aged brandy accord immediately made me think of the expensive bottles of liqueur produced with the solera method. Changing the subject, I started my Penhaligon journey with "Trade Routes Collection - Agarbathi | Penhaligon's" a few months ago. I recently had a little bit of luck and bought Lord George decant blindly, only for the presence of distilled and soapy accords. Was it worth it? Absolutely yes. Would I do it again? Yup! And I'll explain why. As soon as I spray it, I let the greenish juice melt with my skin, and a wave of cask liquor aroma slowly unfolds. It is the impression of a warm, mature, and luxury brandy aged in American oak barrels; I imagine a Cardenal Mendoza, Lepanto Oloroso Viejo, or a Carlos "I" Solera Gran Reserva. Other than the nuances above, what struck me the most is not listed on any of the websites or immediately on the Penhaligon website. And that thing is woody, and not just a hint, a good amount. A nice dry note, somehow fumy, maybe cedar? The underlying woody nuance is dry, smoky, woody, very close to the aroma of pencil shavings. When the initial booze bomb subsides - it's almost gone in the first few minutes - the scent takes a turn that I'm sure I've encountered before. I'm not surprised at how much I like this one. I think it might have something to do with the barber vibe, particularly early on. It has a kind of creamy sweetness, which could be tonka, and it certainly isn't cloying. Lord George is a stunning modern twist on a classic fougére. While wearing it, something sharp about it reminds me of pelargonium. Still, overall, the scent is very woody and sweet. It's like a geranium leaf floating in an aged brandy glass. The fresh soapiness of neroli paired with sweet, sexy, and smoky undertones from tonka beans provides just the right amount of depth and intrigue. When that distinctive flavor lingers and mixes with the drink, then it's at your fingertips. Soap is like barber foam, the one my father made every morning by dipping the shaving brush first in hot water and then in the soap bowl. Just think of cutthroat razors and old-fashioned aftershave in the best possible sense of the word. It is chiefly delivered, and there is no question for me that anyone wearing it exudes class. The more the perfume enters the intermediate phase, the clearer the resemblance to Amber pour Homme Eau de Toilette the original before reformulation. The two smells share the same soapiness and dustiness. It is precisely the cologne I had in mind when I first smelled the smell. From this moment on, however, it is as if we were at a crossroads: the two perfumes each continue on their path, moving further and further away from each other without ever finding each other again. As it dries, it gets slightly less creamy and soapy and a little more amber and musky, and miserably that drydown happens sooner than I'd like. It is a sweet amber with salty and musky undertones. And this sweet, boozy amber lingers on my skin for hours and hours. The base of the booziness and soapiness is a soft tonka biscuit that hints at a dark caramel or molasses, with a hint of freshly baked bread. My final word, success. An exquisitely blended cocktail of alcoholic, amber, and woody nuances. From the first note of perfume comes an overwhelming sensation of splendor and luxury. It is precise of the aristocracy, which takes you to the days of luxurious royal concerts, luxurious palaces, and classical music, as if you were among the guests at that elegant ceremony, at that moment. This perfume blends elegantly and profoundly on the skin; it is pretty linear, although it goes through three distinct phases: alcoholic, soapy, and mushy during its growth. While it may be a little overwhelming at first, it soon becomes something more pleasant, a scent closer to the skin, intimate. I don't get great longevity and not even a ton of projection. But I don't mind at all. Traditionally leaning towards the masculine flavor, I find myself attracted to the fresh, soapy, and sweet notes that develop over time on my skin. A perfect partner to wear from day tonight. However, if you want to layer it on any other oriental woody scent, it doesn't clash in the slightest. I should reserve this fragrance for the best, preferably in the evenings, although the longevity could be better. The fragrance is surprising, rich, dark, smoky. I would have no problem wearing it in the office, on a date, or just around town. Just don't go to the club with it. I base the review on a decant I have owned since November 2021. -Elysium

Holy tonka moly! That is one beautiful tonka blast for a top note! Impressive. The next phase of warm-boozy tobacco-amber is a bit too alpha-male for me, but I admit the quality is good. Pretty soon everything dissolves into tonka-ambrox nothingness, only vaguely reminding one of the opening notes. This does not last long enough to function as a date night scent for youngsters wanting to smell mature and classy, but scent-wise that is how I would classify it.

A fragrance so British it doesn't even get asked for its passport at the border. A fragrance so British that the Kingsman casting director turned it down, claiming it would steal the show from the real star (Colin Firth’s suit). When I sniff the cap, a vivid image strikes me: I smell a perfume — not just any perfume, but an Earl Grey tea. A tea so British that... well, you get the idea. This impression lingers on the skin, but only for a few seconds. Then the woods arrive, followed by the bright cleanliness of ambroxan, all wrapped in a dark, almost mysterious vibe, carried by a rather unusual tonka bean accord. Insta: switzer_scent

Let me start by saying this is not a bad fragrance at all. I actually think it's pretty decent. Not the best and certainly not the worst. Not groundbreaking either. The main player in this fragrance from beginning to end is the soap note. Initially, you get ivory soap and some spiciness. IDK why the pyramid has rum listed as a note because it's completely non-existent. Then after about a half hour, the Tonka starts to creep in. THAT'S IT for the next 5 hours..... Tonka and ivory soap with the ivory soap as the dominant player over the Tonka. You really have to pay attention to get a whiff of the Tonka. All-in-all, The Tragedy of Lord George should NEVER be purchased at full price. Buy discounted. Spicy Ivory soap in sprayable form. You will smell clean and properly bathed guaranteed.

Damn, this is expensive where I live! So, I took my time, trying to figure out why it would merit that hefty price tag. Honestly, I can't say I did. It's not bad, it's pleasant, but I don't know, it lacks that special something that would make it great, or even good. It's a slightly above average scent of soapy rum that evolves into a heavily synthetic ambrox note which dominates the entire composition. Average projection, average longevity. Not blown away.

Reminded me more of tequila – fun and lovely for the first 5 seconds, but then you blink and suddenly taste asphalt with your face. Not a great time. I did love the initial cloud! The first whiffs of rum were delightful. And then nigh immediately soap hit me like a brick. Just pure soap. Gigantic dreadful cloud of it. And then it got in my mouth.

Lord George is promising something divine. Woodsy notes, brandy, tonka and amber? Sign me up! However, on paper, Lord George opens with a much drier and less sweet accord than I initially thought it would be. It is instead spicy, dry and woody. Quite masculine and fairly enough so that I don't feel like wearing it on skin.

This is the smell of a man who goes to an old school barbershop, where they use straight razors sharpened on a strap of leather. Where they create a thick lather from expensive soap and apply it with a soft brush. The smell of his cheek when its just a little damp but freshly made smooth.

Comfortable scent. Romantic, a little mysterious, a small dose of sensuality, but in my opinion it is not a perfume to seduce. It has to fit you, it's a perfume for someone classy, but very restrained. It sets and projects very well, almost like a second skin, following Penhaligon's house rule.

I'm not particularly well-read on alcoholic drinks, so Lord George to me is a cozy dry wood/tonka bean combo with a soapy slant. Props to the marketing, since I've since associated this scent with either a dimly lit library with a barely touched glass of rum, or a sad old british man.

Some of my favorite memories are of my time in the Navy, standing on the topside of a submarine in the middle of the Ocean. A spec in the vastness of nature. That is what I'm reminded of with this photo realistic aquatic. Oud Minerale is unlike any other aquatic in my collection or any that I've ever smelled for that matter. It makes the average aquatic seem... well average. Like quick lap in a pool compared to a full day at the beach. Both have their place, but one is an experience. Where most aquatics are easy grab citrus bombs that quickly fade into nothingness, Oud Minerale is a hyper performer with great projection and even better staying power that dictate it be worn with a purpose. Much like the Navy, this won't be for everyone. Hell, as a kid from the inner city it might not have been for me without the memories it evoked. That said, brilliant fragrance. 10/10

Wow, quite an experience. Oud Minerale is quite unique for an aquatic fragrance. Contrary to some of the reviews below, it didn't strike me as a knock out aquatic or marine scent. I did get a rather strong turpentine type of scent initially. It pulled back as the oud became more prominent, but not stand out either. After it settled, I'd describe it as oud/mineral with the marine/aquatic component coming in third. Even with the oud, Oud Minerale comes across as quite fresh, so it would work well on hot days. And yet, I'm testing it in winter and it's totally in place in the cold weather. Very versatile, very masculine. Longevity is quite good, while the projection is moderate. Projection would probably be better in warmer weather.

I recently picked up a 85/100ml 2nd hand bottle of this for 80€ (retail is 190€). I wasn’t sure on the scent when I first smelt it (only on wrist) so I almost didn’t buy it, because I have a tendency to buy things that are a “good deal” and than they sit. Thankfully here I said “what the heck” and bought it. Im so thankful I did. I always had issues with summer fragrances. I tend to find them uninspiring and very boring. Its either deodorant like or a citrus bomb, but thiss….This is by far the best tom ford Ive tried. When you actually wear this and not just spray it on wrist and take a whiff you get so much more out of it, so wear it when you try it. You wont get the right idea if you don’t . This to me is ocean in a bottle. Its fresh, green, aromatic and deep with this amazing salty smell enveloping it and making it flow beautifully from the top to the base. You also get a tad of this almost rotten smell in this, that you also get from the sea, so I can understand people who don’t like it, but if you love the smell of the ocean this is sensational. It also stays on skin forever it doesn’t project massively, only in the first 3 hours, after that it becomes a skin scent and as a skin scent it lasts and lasts. Not long ago, I wore this in the evening when me and me girlfriend went on a date and she still smelt it on me the next morning at around 10am and asked me if I woke up earlier and took a shower because I smelt so nice. This will definitely be my go to scent for this warm weather season.

Oud Minérale opens with a sea spray note that is iodised and mineral, like sand and pebbles by the sea, which strongly reminds me of the similar accords in L'Artisan Parfumeur Un Air de Bretagne and Hermès Eau des Merveilles Bleue, both released in the same as Oud Minérale. However, unlike the other two that breath air into this sea spray accord with sparkling citrus, Oud Minérale is sturdy and relentless, without much else to support the iodised accord. As I'm not that into marine accords in general, this head-on crash with the sea spray opening does not appeal to me personally. As this mineral and marine accord mellows with time, other nuances begin to make themselves known starting from the 2nd hour, with predominantly the aromatic pepperiness and fresh aquatic cucumber ebbing and waning from time to time. All of these rests on an abstract and very lightweight resinous woody base, and I don't recognise any oud in natural or popular synthetic reconstructions. Oud Minérale then just keeps getting more nebulous and becomes a slightly salty, abstract skin scent. The longevity is at least 7 hours, while the sillage is mostly close to skin. As a new generation of aquatic/marine fragrances, the mineral sand/pebbles effect itself is quite refreshing to the genre. However, after smelling three marine fragrances with this very similar accord in a row, while Oud Minérale is certainly adequate, I did not find it significantly more interesting than the other two. A rich oud could have been a very interesting, if not challenging, companion to the marine accord, But instead, Oud Minérale plays safe and lays a vague, soft woody base. If you're looking for a slightly masculine, iodised marine fragrance and has less limit on budget, you may want to try Oud Minérale. However, I would not recommend it as an oud fragrance, because it plays only a minor role at best in this fragrance.

So here goes my first review for a perfume here on Parfumo so please be patient with me :D, I was excited when i knew that i had the chance to try this perfume. I really love the Oud Wood and expected of course this to be similar, but don´t get fooled. To my nose, Oud Minérale is a peppery, salty woody/oudy, (not s strong oud note but detectable), which could be used in spring and summer weather in my opinion. It´s a nice clean fragrance, but not the same creamyness like Oud Wood has. Me personlly prefer OW!!

Tom Ford Oud Minérale encapsulates the essence of a niche fragrance. As with many things, it's either loved or hated. After all, the concept of minerality has always been somewhat challenging. The initial scent is striking, an immediate love-it-or-hate-it affair. But as the saying goes, familiarity breeds contempt.

I went into B&G hoping to get a sample of the parfum version of Oud Wood and was given this. I've never smelled Oud Mineral. So at first I was a bit miffed, however, after sampling this I was literally stunned at how good it is! I kept deeply sniffing the crux of my wrist all throughout the night; even when I woke up in the middle of the night.

This is by far the most realistic 'marine' scent out there! A unique blend that combines the rugged and unforgiving elements of sea with a refined woodiness creating that high level of sophistication we have become accustomed to from Tom Ford. In my eyes this creation has pushed the boundaries of the aquatic genre in an intriguing direction. 9/10

The whole beauty of this amazing, unique fragrance is the idea of water and fire, contradiction which breeds perfection. Oud and seaweed are the main parts of this fragrance, they coexist in a way I could have never imagined and have created something which could never be cloned outside of tom ford, it is a true masterpiece in its own respect.

I bought this today on the back of one spray from a sample bottle. I left it for an hour between spraying it and going back for the purchase and only in that short period of time, I went from liking it to disliking it and then back again. To say this is a unique scent is an understatement. It feels so incredibly refreshing but at the same time dark and almost sickly.

Can a reformulation be better than the original? In this case, yes! Olivia Giacobetti's L'Eau de l'Artisan was launched in 1993 as an Eau de Toilette. I have been a fan for a long time, as it is one of the few fragrances that smells of meadow and hay. Therefore, I was all the more curious whether the reformulation in 2018 would bring something good, especially since the Eau de Toilette version was taken off the market. I want to say right away: Olivia Giacobetti has succeeded in reinterpreting the fragrance and bringing it into the modern age without changing its fundamental DNA! Now to the scent: It starts fresher and more citrusy than the Eau de Toilette. Lemon and verbena are the perfect start, transitioning to meadow and hay accords. The base is characterized by woody accords that remain gently in the background. Overall, a Cologne masterpiece by Olivia Giacobetti! And all without sharp citrus and with a watercolor-like lightness that knows how to enchant. The longevity and sillage correspond to that of an Eau de Cologne. But one is happy to spray more.

Every time I spray this, I can't help but think of the Ron Burgundy quote, "I'm very important. I have many leather-bound books and my apartment smells of rich mahogany." That's precisely how wearing Halfeti makes me feel -- luxe, sophisticated and comforted by leathers, resins and the absolutely stunning woody notes. I wasn't really prepared to love Halfeti as much as I do and I understand why Penhaligon's pumps this outside of it's stores -- it's somehow an utterly charming scent. I first smelled Halfeti in an airport duty free and was blown away. I didn't buy it then, but it did kick start a sampling of a few different ouds including Tom Ford Oud Wood, Thameen Carved Oud, MfK Oud Satin Mood, Initio Oud for Greatness and of course Halfeti. Halfeti constantly came out as the clear winner of them all to my nose. The opening is quite masculine but the dry down softens and sweetens up to a totally unisex scent. A very dry, smooth and warm dark woods that just feels comforting on cold fall and winter days. Allegedly inspired by black roses that grow in the city of Halfeti, I don't actually get all that much rose. While it is undeniably present in the background it's the cardamom, saffron, oud and cedar that stick out most prominently to my nose (I am not mad about that!) With a light hand, Halfeti can be day time and office appropriate as the sillage and projection do settle closer to the skin (though watch the sprays, it is very possible to overdo it). The longevity of Halfeti is excellent and I can get about 8-10 hours out of it, though it will last over a week if sprayed on say a coat or scarf. Overall, I am really glad I ended up adding Halfeti into my collection and it's been one of my heavy hitters this F/W season.

This is an essential every day, all purpose cologne. If you had this and a fresh fragrance you would be set. The opening is a bit spicy in a kitchen spices kind of way, and not super amazing, but the dry down (takes about 20 min) is phenomenal. The mixture of woods and resins take the stage, with the spices providing background support. The scent has the character of an oud fragrance without a super noticeable oud scent, if that makes sense. In a way this reminds me of a much better version of Haltane / Oud for Greatness, which in my opinion are both terrible and poorly blended. Halfeti is blended in such a way that there is no dominant note, and individual notes would be difficult to detect if there were no note list. I will note that I don't detect any vanilla, this is not sweet to my nose. When I wear this, I feel confident in my own skin. I think this is a great signature scent because it's unique enough that people will associate you with this.

I heard only good things about Halfeti but never had the chance to test it, until I made a sharing and I was blown away how good it is. For my taste, is quite understated and will not project too much, nut the nice spicy character will last for many hours, even if not loud. In a span of few years after its launch, Penhaligon´s came with a few flankers which I think are also worth considering. Overall, the Halfeti smells very nice and expensive and if the old school bottle is not for you, you can get Mr. Sam which smells identical (to me) and comes with the nice personalized bottle. Enjoy the video :) !

Halfeti by Penhaligon's has a superb oud. It is an amazingly balanced unisex fragrance; it is neither too feminine nor too masculine. The fragrance has noticeable notes of cypress, oud and cedar. It is very light despite being so wood-heavy. Halfeti reminds me of going mushroom hunting in late September, in the early hours of the morning when the forest is still foggy and cold. The crisp morning air and pine trees are bottled up in this notorious fragrance. The base of vanilla and tonka isn't overbearing, to me it is hardly noticeable, but the sweet gourmands accompanied by the lightness of bergamot are what keeps this oud fragrance in check for me. On my skin, Halfeti opens with a strong liquorice note, not my favourite. The fragrance is much more masculine and I am quite surprised how differently it performs on paper than on my skin. After dry down, Halfeti is an elegant oud and a couple of hours in, it sweetens up and the vanilla becomes the main accord along with leather and saffron. On paper, the fragrance deepens as well over time. Saffron gives the fragrance an element that I also find leaning more towards a masculine fragrance, especially in combination with all the other notes. It is no wonder that Halfeti is so famous, it is a beautiful, continuously evolving fragrance, but it performs very differently on skin than on paper, which is why I would recommend trying it on yourself first. Be forewarned, you cannot help but love it.

Sweet, spicy, and masculine leaning. I really like it. This is what I wanted Maison Martin Margiela Replica Jazz Club to be. There’s a touch of leather but it’s not overwhelming; what I smell the most is the bergamot, rose, cardamom and nutmeg, which dries down beautifully to amber woods. Lovely. I can see why it’s polarizing, but personally, it’s a winning combination for my skin.

Halfeti is oud perfume created in arabian style. For me oud is always more masculine than feminine scent. But this one is warmer with some kind of ascetic elegance. When overhelming oud evaporate, remains fresh and subtle touch of roses. For me it is always difficult to wear oud scent. It somehow irritate me, make me dizzy.

Halfeti is one of the most wearable oud fragrances I ever smelled. I can smell that grapefruit cypress right away which freshens up this whole composition. Spicy heart of nutmeg and cumin intertwines with the best flowers like saffron, violet and rose. Leather, oud and resins blended with perfectly balanced tonka, vanilla and creamy sandalwood. Masterful blend by Mr.

Notes: Grapefruit, Bergamot, Green Notes, Armoise, Cypress, Cumin, Nutmeg, Violet, Saffron, Rose, Jasmine, Muguet, Leather, Oud, Amber, Resins, Tonka, Vanilla and Sandalwood Perfumer: Christian Provenzano A gorgeous, warm, inviting and an opulent scent.

The saffron and bergamot comes out fast blending into a rather nice smell with sweet and sourness. You also get some leaf-like notes from both the cypress leaf and artemisia After the first couple of minutes the rose has started to appear. The leather comes with it giving it this more masculine approach than before.

Halfeti is pure elegance in a bottle—a fresh, green, and woody masterpiece that instantly evokes a feeling of royalty. It’s the kind of scent that makes you expect a butler to appear with afternoon tea! This fragrance truly shines on cold, wintery days. On my skin, it wears beautifully as a unisex scent, though individual chemistry will always play a part.

Sartorial demonstrates the difficulty of story-telling in perfume. Penhaligon’s own press, and a number of reviews popose that Sartorial paints a picture of the British bespoke tailor’s shop in the 21st century. Take apart a well know reference, reinterpret it with a contemporary smirk, change the context---classic postmodernism. The equation of tailor’s shop with fougère is understandable. The late 19th century was the era of the fern and the Victorian gentleman’s tailor. Then to fuse the fougère with scents one might find in a tailor’s workroom is a more tenuous step. To my mind the story of the tailor’s shop is a bit of schtick. It also serves to create an expectation that can’t help but be frustrated. Perfume can conjure and it can evoke, two words I’ve read about Sartorial. But it simply can’t tell over the lengths of paragraphs the same narrative to each person who wears it. Truthfully, marketing department, full paragraphs aren’t needed. In this case the fiction is told with very few words. Simply to mention a British bespoke tailor’s shop ties together fantasy, aspiration and fetish in a few short words. But then to tell us about the cloth, the cabinetry, the wax, the thread… Oy gevalt. It’s like Ralph Lauren / GQ porn from the 1980s. All the above would matter less if the fragrance told me its own actual story, or took me a on bit of a journey. But I find Sartorial an unpleasant fragrance. The starch-and-steam-iron-like note up top can be an attempt to elicit the image of a steam iron in use, but it smells out of place and metallically flat in its floral/spicy setting. As Sartorial progresses the sweet overlap of notes of patchouli, waxy honey, and caramelized lavender (all long-lasting) turn it into a bland gourmand-like fragrance. Pardon my blunt, rather lacking description, but I don’t get much more from Sartorial. I’m a great fan of Bertrand Duchaufour, but to me, Sartorial is the latest cut of the emperor’s clothes. The fragrances of Etat Libre d’Orange share the conceit of fantasy-narrative, but their approach of story or hint of portraiture are more successful than Sartorial’s full-blown Victorian fantasy. (To be fair, ELdO’s laughably pretentious, simply bad text is far worse than Penhaligon’s here. Enough so that maybe it’s easier to dismiss.) But Tom of Finland gives you a loaded, iconic image and a fragrance. Rossy de Palma gives you an actor and a fragrance. The rest is up to you and the perfume. Please measure the above with the fact that the fantasy that Sartorial wants to give you, that of a 21st century world of people who frequent tailors, has no appeal for me. Maybe if it did I might enjoy Sartorial. Who knows?

This is a fragrance which I have no problem loving. As soon as I smelled it I realised it pleased me. For me it's honey and beeswax and lavender, surrounded by green herbs and mossy woods. A very grown up, very "gentleman" like fragrance. This one gives me the impression of being clean and groomed, like trying on a brand new suit in a shop, which I guess was the intention, given the brief and description of the fragrance (ie that it should smell like a tailor's workshop). I would happily wear this formally. I find nothing wrong with it whatsoever in terms of style and character. It gives me a good feeling to wear. The feeling it gives is gender neutral. Just a lovely, impressive aroma of brand new fabric and of wearing nice clothes. I do find it would suit a well dressed man perfectly, but a woman could pull this off too. Some people say the smell is old fashioned. I don't. I think it's quite modern. The use of aromachemicals here is very cleverly done, and by a very talented perfumer (Bertrand Duchaufour). I would recommend this one to gentlemen for formal wear, and for anyone who not only likes to be well dressed, but who would like to smell like that too. Very well made. Impressive.

At first i didnt like Sartorial. But after wearing it some times now i do love this scent because it shows newer facets while i wear it. Very complex and well balanced, i smell different notes each time i wear it, and always with a decent level of sweetness. Smells old and modern at the same time, this one of my most loved scents ever. It has a nice barbershop vibe that makes it very masculine. Longevity, lasting power and sillage are medium-high. If you like Rive Gauche, you'll enjoy Sartorial. If you like Brut, you'll fall in love for Sartorial. Updated January 2014

Scentrack Variety Lab – London in the Rain When I visited tailor workshop for the first time I was totally shocked by its spectrum of smells. Metal, textile, wax, steam... Very unique smell. Master Duchaufour perfectly translated it into perfume. Sartorial is complicated and masculine scent that reminds of Brut. But it takes the best of Brut and amplify it on the whole new level. Interplay of notes is incredible, unreal and so incompatible and cacophony expected, but eventually perfectly mashed. Metallic notes, aldehydes, wax, honey, Proustian linden blossom, lavender, flowers... perfection. Fantastic, formal, masculine, regal, dignified, well mannered. The essence of Britain. A work of a genius. Rating: 8.5/10 More on Scentimental Words

A mild thumbs up from me for Sartorial. I like its opening that really is a nice aromatic blend of citrus and spice, but then the scent calms down to a kind of barbershop fresh vibe at its heart that stays for the rest of its duration that I feel like I have smelled before. A well done scent to be sure, but a somewhat sub-par effort from a great nose like Duchaufour who has created so many truly outstanding scents. From almost anyone else I might call myself impressed with the results. 3 to 3.5 stars out of 5.

From penhaligons.com: ______ Sartorial is a contemporary interpretation of a classic Fougère; the traditional notes of oakmoss, tonka bean and lavender have been exquisitely stitched together with woods, ozonic and metallic effects, leather, violet leaf, honey and spices to create the perfect illusion of a tailor’s workroom. ______ Sartorial is a very complex perfume.

I have this thing that my ick is the categorisation of fragrances; work, party, dates, gym, shopping, clown orgy, bar mitzvah etc I hate that shit. Just that waste of a fragrance just to save it for a certain occasion or situation. I bought Tom Ford's Grey Vetiver for work, wore it to work about three times. Waste.

If a mad scientist offered to send you back to the 1950s, I’m sure your first question would be: “Which perfume should I bring with me?” Good news: you don’t need to wonder anymore — Sartorial is the answer. This fragrance embodies the timeless man — one who shines in any era, any place.

Great example of me buying a fragrance sample without realizing that it's "for men" and then coming to understand it does not matter. This isn't overly masculine, it's more just fresh and unisex, slightly soapy herbal. The lavender and metallic accords are a brilliant match here.

Lovely clean barbershop fougere. Not too heavy or old fashioned although it does give me a nostalgic vibe which I really enjoy. It does resemble to Brut, or niche version done just perfect. So rich and smooth. I love it. 10/10

This is the pear cousin of Mure et Musc Idea: simple, straightfoward and focused on a single fruit. But instead of Musc, you get a good dose of pollen-like flowery aroma. I confess that i'm not so fond of pear fragrances because they usually smell very functional to me, like a shampoo aroma or a ironing product. But on this one the pear seems more realistic, like ripe pear, and when it starts to go into the functional direction the mimosa aroma gives it the floral edge needed to make it like a sophisticated fragrance. I don't notice much vanilla on me, maybe it's used on small amounts to round the fragrance, but if i didn't knew it was vanilla i'd thought it was musc. I don't know if this collection is still sold, but when it was it had a more exclusive distribution which i think it's not coherent with this fragrance.

I confess that I sometimes get a little annoyed by those members of the fragrance hobbyist community who go on and on and on about performance. I don't need every fragrance to last nine days and announce my arrival to everybody within a 20-mile perimeter. I don't WANT my fragrances to do that. Getting 6-8 hours of gentle projection out of most fragrances is a perfectly acceptable, even preferable situation for me. It lets me easily change things up between daytime and evening, if I want; if I need it to last longer, I can always reapply. ...but there's a line, even for me. And Costa Azzurra is on the wrong side of it. Let's start with the positives: I absolutely love the fragrance itself. This is a beautifully mineralic citrus. It's briny and oceanic without going fetid or funky. It's one of the most genuinely "coastal" fragrances I've ever tried. The opening is dazzling - it leaps and fizzes off the skin when you first spray it, lively and playful. You get a heady and potent rush of salted lemon and a strong sense of sea air. It's a more complex lemon than most: it's bright, yes, but with a little bit of dark depth behind it. As it dries down, you get minerals and woods. It truly is evocative of the seaside: I almost feel like I can hear seagulls every time I spray it. And then, within an hour, it's gone. The first time I tried it was from a tester in a store, and I figured it was just a badly-abused tester. So I tried a sample decant, and figured maybe it was just the decant. But I still liked it well enough to splurge on a bottle at full retail (from an authorized retailer, so I know it's the real deal) and, sadly, have the same problem. I'm not exaggerating, either. I cannot get more than an hour out of this. It's the shortest-lived fragrance, by far, in my collection. I don't just mean in the air: even as a skin scent, there's nothing left. I don't just mean that I've got anosmic: I've tried it on test strips and clothing and left them in another room far away from me, and when I went back an hour later and stuck my nose in, they were gone from there, too. If this was an inexpensive, reasonably priced fragrance, I'd say "hang the expense." I'd douse myself in it every hour on the hour on days I wanted to wear it, and cheerfully enjoy the experience. If the aroma was SO overwhelmingly magical that nothing else even came close, I'd say "it's still worth it." But as good as it is, it ain't all that. And at Tom Ford prices, even through discounters, I just can't find the value proposition here. I love it. Don't buy it.

It gives what it promises: a French-Mediterranean scent mixing lemon, cypress and oak wood, all of it in an amalgamation of marine notes (despite not being declared) This is what a man with a white linen shirt, a gold watch and a considerably big boat would smell like while anchored in front of the coast of Nice, feeling the mountain breeze blowing upon the board. If at discount, this is a good bang for the buck, and a step up from other over the top citrus linear fragrances.

F** me, I love this. I am no fraghead, just a regular guy trying fragrances. And I loved this one instantly. Smells like what you think linen suit-wearing men in the 30s in Monaco smell like when chilling on a yacht in the golden hour. Fresh, spicy, woody. Personally I could wear this all year round for all occasions, but I see why people feel it's a summer fragrance.

I was super excited to get Costa Azzurra as soon as possible when it was launched and finally got my bottle in early September 2021. After looking at so many included notes, and imagining what it would smell like, I have to say that this one is one of those familiar yet supremely done aromatic woody fragrances with touches of sea smell. One thing that kept my excitement at the normal level was Costa Azzurra Acqua which I sampled one year before and was not overly impressed by the composition. TOP NOTES Upon the first spray, the fragrance opens up with a burst of juicy citruses, smelling natural and well refined. Looking at the listed top notes, this may come strange due to the whole different note listing. Anyone worried about the infamous oud note shouldn’t be worried since that note is non-existent in this fragrance. The citrus, of which I mainly get mandarin orange, and lemon are intertwined with aromatic herbs that transport you to the Adriatic coast. HEART NOTES The heart notes keep on the pleasant and sunny vibes while the notes step into an aromatic and woody territory. Cypress takes the main role, and if I had to imagine a picture of what it reminds me of, it would be a stroll through the Dalmatian villages, near the sea, where cypress and orange trees grow. The citrus notes never really back down, and the gentle whiffs I get wouldn’t bother anyone. The issue I have with all of this is the missing notes that are either non-existent or mixed in the minimal amount of concentration. BASE NOTES The base notes mostly consist of citrus, and aromatic notes present from the beginning with additional resinous woodiness from the generic woody accord, and incense that is mostly present in the higher outside temperatures. As someone who knows what the actual driftwood smells like, I’m sad to report that the driftwood present here is just a combination of vetiver, oak, and seaweed. *Check out my Parfumo profile to find out how can you read full reviews on my website.*

You have to toe the line my friends. Not all aquatics were made equally and Costa Azzurra pushes back against the little boys wearing Invictus. Silly fools, sweet accords only lead down a path of misery as everything blends together. This will remind you of a bushy, dry beach which fights against my pro-hydro stance. However the thought of rolling around in the grass will get the sprinklers going. At least it worked for my missus when she got me this for Xmas. Sucked in collector boys, I got an OG 2014 bottle. She did good and was rewarded accordingly.

Gentle marine perfume with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice in it. Summery, fresh, not too sweet, has a lovable funky saltiness to it. I do not like it. Out of the 6 perfumes in my Discovery Set I think I like this one the least. There's a peculiar quality I've noticed in all six Tom Ford fragrances I've tested – they all smell perfumey. This isn't necessarily a bad thing.

a pop of clean and fresh lemon and is almost immediately juxtaposed with what reads as a gentle earthy patchouli note, combined with a salty ocean accord and a musky, salty skin scent. has a green aromatic portion to it, but is largely a blue marine scent: salty and oceanic with a gorgeous lemon note.

It can be considered the best fresh perfume of Tom Ford compared to its other creation. This scent is dominated by lemon which mainly characterises. It can be a signature scent for men in summer and spring especially when you go to the anywere in summer night as Tom Ford Costa Azzurra is a ideal scent to accompany.

Costa Azzurra, the azure coast, is - unlike its French namesake, the Côte d'Azur in the south of Provence, suggests, not even close to it, but instead located on the Adriatic - right at the top of the coast of Friuli Venezia Giulia at the end of the Gulf of Venice - and not far from the Italian-Slovenian border.

Definitely a perfect fragrance to start your journey in the niche/luxury world. One of the least “British style” of the Portrait’s collection. I feel like the story telling (go check it out if you’re interested, it’s a marketing masterpiece) is spot on. Fresh and warm spicy goodness. Tobacco and vanilla. Patchouli (wet wood) and cedar wood (dry wood). Mr Sam really is a fragrance of contrasts with a double personality. I won’t get in too much detail, but a barista chased me down the street at night to ask me the name of this fragrance. Then, it happened again with a girl in university. And then it happened again. It’s truly “blazing”. Not a masterpiece, it’s a people pleaser, Parfums de Marly style. I’ll always be grateful for the confidence boost it gave me when I was feeling down and for the great conversation starting power it had when people smelled it on me. My first niche/luxury purchase ever, thank you for the memories. When I grow up, I wanna be like Mr Sam.

To me, this fragrance is very... round? Does that make any sense? Looking through the notes, you see tobacco, cardamom, black pepper, saffron, cinnamon... it looks like it could be a beast, punchy, and sharp. It isnt. It is so pleasantly rounded. The blend is smooth, and it is so easily wearable and enjoyable to all. My fiance doesn't enjoy smelling smokey and tobacco-ish scents on me, but this is her favourite fragrance on me. Because it is so wonderfully comforting. As time goes on, it becomes sweeter, and the spices begin to fade. The opening hour to my nose is filled with cardamom, tobacco and a little bit of vanilla and cinnamon. Its a very inviting and inoffensive scent. Projection is pretty good, and fades to a skin scent in around 2-3 hours for me. But i almost feel as if it being an intimate scent is appropriate. It feels like an elegant, more so masculine scent. I cant see anyone disliking it! im a fan!!

First of, I have learned not to be too excited about the notes in Penhaligon's before trying them (*cough* Changing Constance), however, Mr Sam is promising something very nice! Hot and cold spices, patchouli and creamy cedar... I might even hope that I can try it on skin, but alas, we've been here before... Just seeing the notes of cardamom, cinnamon, saffron and vanilla makes my mouth water. So, Mr Sam, on paper... Yes, yes, absolutely yes! Warm and sweet. Masculine, but not far from unisex. After dry down Mr Sam... Dries down! The fragrance is less sweet and more of a spicy, dry perfume. Still very warm and ambery - I absolutely adore it! Honestly, I cannot stop smelling it. I've been through a couple Penhaligon's fragrances now that I really dislike and my nose finally feels at ease! It is perfect for this season, the spicy cardamom and cinnamon allude to walking down cobblestone streets during Christmas. It is cold, the air is crisp and the small booths filled with Christmas delights like roasted almond fill the air with wonderful spices.

You know that nice feeling which we have sometimes for a few minutes when something seems familiar to us but we do not know from where and what is it? This is how Mr. Sam started the acquaintance with me, leaving me confused for a few minutes .. but then, I realized that we met before, in another context - I will explain. Penhaligon´s, which is a company owned by PUIG is one that can be called many names but for sure not boring or bland -> they have the lovely portraits collection with esquisite bottles, they have the history and they have an interactive website which can take you to the history of the brand. Mr. Sam here is the twin brother of Halfeti, also created by Penhaligons under the crafted hand of Mr. Provenzano, I would not wonder if Mr. Sam is also his creation, even if the perfumer´s name is not present here nor on Fragrantica. If you know and like the spicy character of Halfeti, with its notes - then Mr. Sam is the same, and if you do not know them, I can tell you that they start very strong with cardamom and almost cake like cinnamon, followed by a peppery feel and then they follow into a goodness of sandalwood with aromatic notes. And the longevity is better on Halfeti, for some reason. Enjoy my long video :) !

A green spicy fougere, almost aromatic, is the frontman of this scent, with a backdrop of vanilla sweetness, and inoffensive drop of tobacco and oud. After the projection fades, only vanilla remains on skin. Sillage and longevity are above average. Like other Penhaligon's fragrances, this is super wearable. I don't love it but close enough. I might gift this to my father.

This is the smell of a man with good and expensive taste. He sits in velvet chairs smoking and drinking, he smells like spice and like good whisky. He could find this same fragrance for cheaper and at the same quality but he won't. He wants to tell everyone he is wearing Penhaligon's, its a status symbol.

tested at the beginning of the year through a free sample, this allowed me to validate a good first impression when I had tested several perfumes of this brand at istanbul airport in September 2022. this perfume had already stood out from the others when I first discovered it. I find it really refined, fresh and neither too powerful nor too light. Ideal for mid-season.

cardamom in the opening similar to LNDL by ysl, a bit of tobacco that dissipates quickly, balmy vanilla and chocolate-y patchouli wrapped up in a generic drugstore shower gel freshness. In short, it smells like any other 3 in 1 shower gel marketed towards men with a ridiculous price tag.
Fragrances as a mirror of personality, or at least as a counterpart to it. A beautiful thought, although firstly difficult to implement and secondly rarely encountered in practice.

A golden bull's head looks at me and captivates me. As some have already written before me, the bottle is a unique eye-catcher. The entire series invites you to start a large collection. When you delve a little into the brand, Penhaligon, you realize that the creators behind the scenes have taken a lot of time for the extraordinary and interesting stories.

To write the first review... how do we get to the 9.3 here? I would barely give it a 2 out of 10. First Love?? They say: you never forget your first love, doesn't that connect to positive memories? This scent is simply cold, perfect for distant personalities. Lily of the valley... yes, but those that have experienced night frost. Somehow there’s a bitter note, a bit aldehydic and herbal, somewhat like green tea that has been drawn out too long, forgotten in the cup, and is now cold.

Aloha...the first review of this fragrance...DPD delivers the box to my freezing cold hallway....I unpack and my heart warms immediately. The typical VS packaging, in the case of Tease Dreamer, a white box with a few palm trees and a blurred turquoise and soft pink sky. OK, the bottles always look a bit DIY self-made. But that doesn't detract from the fragrance. If anyone talks about synthetic here, I can confidently refute that! The opening reminds me of Alien Goddess Eau de Parfum , but thankfully that typical Alien synthetic note fades away like magic. The longer the fragrance stays on the skin (body temperature), the creamier it becomes. No annoying synthetic coconut, it reminds me of my coconut body lotion. But it doesn't have those "saturating" sunscreen vibes; I think more of this coconut water that you drink best ice-cold in summer...how else would you get the sea salt note into the fragrance? Magnolia/Tiare/Frangipani...ah, few things can be so simple and good. With this lovely Dreamer, you won't annoy anyone around you even at 35 degrees and more. Since I couldn't test this fragrance beforehand, I'm satisfied with the "blind buy.

WHAT IT IS A sundowner in the wood-paneled piano bar at a 5-star hotel somewhere in the Southern Hemisphere. This opens with a spicy burst of smoky ginger before settling onto an absolutely posh, luxurious, Oriental base of cardamom-sweetened woods. Periodic hits of a fun creamy cola-like tonka come and go, but mostly this is all teak furniture, palm fronds, white button downs, good grooming, and refined manners. Sits relatively close to the skin and lasts a good 6-8hrs. Very true to the image of Tom Ford (the man, not the brand) and a cool weather staple. WHO IT'S FOR You've outgrown overly sweet, youthful "bangers" and want something more sophisticated, mature, and upscale. Skews masculine and 35-40+, but would pair well with a long black dress and some Louboutin heels. An easy, winning reach for date night. ALTERNATIVES The original Noir Extreme is sweeter and more youthful without the spiciness of the ginger - it's excellent. YSL La Nuit de L'Homme is arguably the exemplar of spicy, cardamom-forward fragrances and is more versatile, but doesn't evoke such an instant mood as Noir Extreme Parfum. JPG Le Male le Parfum is a workhorse in this category, but smells unsophisticated and synthetic by comparison. Valentino Uomo Intense has a stickier vanilla note on top of clean suede; a great choice if the cola accord in Noir Extreme Parfum is off-putting. FINAL THOUGHTS I've avoided buying Tom Ford fragrances because the value is off in my opinion. F*cking Fabulous, Soleil Blanc, Oud Wood, Lost Cherry, etc all smell great... just not "$200-400+ great" when there are better options from MFK, Diptyque, & Byredo. Even cheaper bottles like Beau du Jour and Ombre Leather, while excellent, lack the X factor of $100 bottles from Dior, Guerlain, and Chanel. The Noir line, to my nose, stands apart: a wonderful good-better-best progression of modern Oriental fragrances, the latter two being some of Sonia Constant's best work.

This is my take on this version compared to the Noir Extreme. This one starts off with a smokiness ,which if you make the mistake of smelling it close up you initially think what the hell No! But if you wait a little for the other notes to catch up, you realize the complexity and maturity of it, whereas in the Noir Extreme you only smell the sweet and spicy part of it. I like the more complex fragrances so I opted for this one. The longevity of this perfume could be better to be honest for a Parfum, which is also one of the reasons I opted for this one instead of the Noir Extreme. The bottle other than the color looks a bit cheap if Tom Ford hadn't been written on it. Still one of my favorite in my collection and could wear it every day !

The original Tom Ford Noir turned into an air freshener for me on the dry down which put me right off. TF Noir Extreme EDP was a lot better but I thought the fruity, Gourmand like effect was a bit powdery and not very dark. This one…. This hits just right. It’s rich, powerful, masculine straight off the bat and then as it dries down it starts to smooth off but with still a bit of spice and depth. Ordered a bottle after one day of wear. I know I will go back to this again and again.

Note: I've updated this review so please take not of the addendum at the bottom if you're using this review as guidance! I was extremely excited to try this fragrance, the notes looked amazing and the idea of a more masculine Noir Extreme sounded great because I find Noir Extreme to be 95% sweet Kulfi smell. Well, I'm not sure if I got a bad bottle or something but this smells almost identical to Noir Extreme but somehow even sweeter and with *less* leather. I don't understand how people consider this to be a masculine fragrance at all, it's a few leaps away from vanilla body spray. I'm genuinely hoping there's something wrong with my nose or that I had COVID or something because this left me feeling legitimately quite down. EDIT: I've got to update this, after a year either my nose has changed or this has really opened up and matured. The rich, lactonic Kulfi is not only making its presence more apparent but is far more elegant than the initial, somewhat simplistic ethyl maltol sweetness I had interpreted it as. The cardamom is subtler but also somehow more pleasant and expansive at the same time, unfurling itself and allowing the other notes to play out above it. The ginger and sandalwood have a gentle tug of war with the gaiac and cedar playfully oscillating back and forth, bobbing and weaving in a sinusoidal dance to the diapason of the Tonka, the final harmony that serves to animate the whole ensemble. I'm so glad my partner suggested I give this one another try, my initial review truly doesn't do it justice.

This perfume is one of my most recent acquisitions and has quickly become one of my favorite perfumes (even using it with temperatures around 20ºC / 68ºF). In Portugal, especially in the southern coastal areas, the temperatures are never very low (it is very rare for temperatures to drop below 10ºC / 50ºF in the peak of winter) so we have to adapt the use of "colder weather" perfumes to mild temperatures for most of the year (just don't overdo the number of sprays). The first time I tried the Noir Extreme, I wasn't impressed (I liked the smell but the performance left much to be desired, considering the price of this perfume). Later, I tried the Parfum version and, despite the opening notes being a bit strange to me (not in a bad way), it was "love at first smell." I tried it in local stores a couple more times before buying it, and I consider it one of the most charismatic perfumes I have smelled to date. It is not overly sweet and emanates a distinct personality compared to most current perfumes (whether designer or niche). The longevity is quite good too (more than 8 hours), whereas a significant part of my small collection doesn't last long on my skin (especially the perfumes more suited for summer).

I'm not convinced that I can tell how this is wholly different from the EDP. I know I am know I am not thinking that I would be disappointed if I had requested this but had been bought the EDP instead. Its the same with Ombre Leather. I don't know if there's enough in either the fragrance notes or the performance to be a completely different fragrance.

I really like the profile. For me, Noir Extreme is better. I bought this from a discounter so not really sure what I am working with. When I tested it in a department store, it was awesome. Straight from the strip for several hours. Really nice. Yet, the bottle I have now seems off. Or it may be my skin chemistry. The scent is the same. Projection is weak to moderate.

Idk if this is fake or was stored improper, but this stuff lasts MAYBE 3 hours, and is a skin scent in 30 minutes. Purchased from FragBuy.com. also got the Limmersine dupe called Jean lowe immortal, that stuff is AMAZING, but I digress. This TF ENP is horrendous performance. I won't make a real review, based off maybe it was not properly stored or cared for.

Never cared much for the OG noir extreme, was a bit too sweet for me, leaned very feminine to my nose. This, however, is a different beast…more masculine, more rough, less sweet. The leather, suede, Tonka bean and tobacco notes really help make this a much more seductive, mature, dark scent.

As a fan of both fragrances - Noir Eau de Parfum and Noir Extreme Eau de Parfum - I could hardly wait to try the new flanker from the house. Noir Extreme Parfum starts off surprisingly and somewhat irritating. In the first few seconds, I didn't like it at all. After a while, the fragrance calms down, and its true face reveals itself.

In the basis, this is a boring cashmeran-floral with vanilla-maltol sweetness. The course of the fragrance is quite a ride, though. Penhaligon's really played around with that basic formula and created something interesting and fun. I think it is the cardamom that makes the difference. It opens the fragrance with a big bright flash before dipping underneath that maltol sweetness, only to lift it back up on its shoulders. Meanwhile the florals and the cashmeran have fully bloomed and the scent has changed from bright-spicy to super-sweet to comfortably floral-musky within a few minutes. This is way too sweet for me, but it was a fun ride for this one time. I am starting to like Penhaligon's a lot. I always thought they were a dull traditional house, being British and all, but it turns out they have a great sense of humor.

I am in dire need of a pick me up! We started off so well with the Portraits Set, but I had to go through three florals to get here, to a beloved Amber Vanilla! Caramel, warm spicy, vanilla, tobacco, salty... What's not to like! On paper, Changing Constance is giving me Lush fragrance vibes. Simple, not the best quality (sorry, that's the experience I had) and quite frankly, cheap. Constance, why are you doing this to me! We were supposed to finish off big! Well, there's nothing else to do than try it on skin. From the whole set, I was looking forward to Changing Constance the most, but I am still reminiscing about Yasmine, which was a far more elegant take on cardamom. Constance is weirdly composed, monotonous, linear, boring. Just a sweet blob on the skin. I am so confused and struggling to describe it. Where's the caramel? The saltiness? The warm spicy notes? To me, this is as monotone as was Grand Soir, Absolute Aphrodisiac and Angel's Share (if I remember correctly on the latter). And I stand by my Lush remark. I'll give it a minute and reapply. Nothing's changed. What a snooze. This could be a great layering fragrance though - it is warm and sweet, perfect base for other fragrances that need some depth or sweetness, but alone? It just doesn't do it for me. I need more nuance in a fragrance, especially the ambery and gourmand kind. Oh well! The boys are up for testing now, which one should I start with?

I'm a guy and I love wearing this in cooler/rainy weather.nnIt really feels like a warm blanket (*expensive blanket).nnI wish performance was a little better but thats a trend with most of the fragrances from the Portraits Collection. Smell amazing but doesnt project. It lasts long on skin and clothes tho. But imo not everything needs to be beast mode, especially not this onennGreat for more intimate and cozy moments like a cafe session or movie nights nnIf you like this, you'll like Minuet et Demi or Magenta Tanzanite but those are a bit stronger, spicier, and harsher. This is just so well blended and delicate

This smells so incredibly good. Sweet but not a typical gourmand. The cardamom, tobacco and pimento help balance out the salted caramel, which is the main star. The notes unfold one by one, adding a sense of structure and complexity. Unfortunately, none of this lasts. The scent is completely gone on my skin after only half an hour. A shame, really, because this is one of my favourites by the brand. I'll use up my decant and cry, while reminiscing about our good times together. Alas, all good things must come to an end.

SEXY caramel, gourmand without too much sweetness. The cardamom and caramel are most of what I get, but I am sensing a hint of the tobacco underneath, adding a little dryness and preventing it from going too buttery and saccharine. Doesn't morph much on the dry down but the throw is definitely low, as seems to be the consensus. Even so, it's so beautiful I'm tempted to pick up a full bottle. Smells like a beautiful woman standing eating a piece of butterscotch - what's not to love?

Probably the most beautiful gourmand. Usually, salt+caramel perfumes are heavy, too much sweet, plain and cosy but boring... But not this one. It is sweet and creamy but in a light fashion. The pimento gives a very special touch that makes this perfume stands out. It also has facets of a musky floral, I can totally imagine a vale full of white flowers in bloom.

Wore it twice just to be sure it wasn't my nose the problem. The scent is very subtle and I have the feeling either I have some anosmia or my skin chemistry gobbles this fragrance up. That, or Penhaligon's fragrances have low performance (which I'm inclined to believe since it's the second one I've tried).

Penhaligon refers to Constance as a "very modern woman." A woman with no regard for custom and does as she likes. This description would give me the impression of a young woman who travels the world, tries the local food, and full of energy. That is not the impression I got.

Hello and welcome to the second episode about the scents of the Hogwarts common rooms! Now that we all know how it smells with the cunning Slytherins (Marc Jacobs - Decadence), the lovely Constance has burrowed into my fragrance memory so deeply that I associate her incredibly strongly with the Gryffindor common room.

Hello dear readers (no, I am not Lady Whistleblower - for all Netflix fans;-)), While browsing on Parfumo, I came across the beautiful pictures by @Parfümlein. I particularly liked the mood in the images. Then I realized that the depicted animal head is actually the cap of the bottle. What kind of perfume is this? Aha - Changing Constance! No way, my name is on it.

At first, I’ll admit the Gourmand trend felt a bit excessive to me—cloyingly sweet, heavy, and often bordering on juvenile. Too many feel unbalanced, with syrupy notes drowning out any structure or restraint. But Noir pour Femme is in a league of its own. Crafted with an exotic finesse by the supremely talented Sonia Constant (a personal favorite), it’s a fragrance that wears its opulence with grace. The opening bursts like an overturned spice rack—Cardamom, Nutmeg, Ginger, Cinnamon, and Black Pepper tumble forth. On my skin, the Ginger, Nutmeg, and Black Pepper take the lead, cutting through the vanillic sweetness with a fiery edge that’s both bold and elegant. Then, something lovely simmers underneath—like hints of apple pie or dried raisins. A whisper of a Grojsman-esque Rose tiptoes in, flanked by airy Orange Blossoms, buoyed effortlessly by a dash of Hedione. And just like that, the fragrance begins to bloom. The presence of Lily of the Valley brings a creamy-soft floralcy that polishes the rough edges and smooths the transition into an indulgent heart. It gradually deepens into something richer, creamier—true to its kulfi-inspired soul. There’s a lactonic silkiness here, woven with soft musks and a suggestion of sandalwood (perhaps a touch of Javanol). Musks like Ethylene Brassylate or Musk-T may sound unassuming, but in this context, they’re magic—powdery, vanillic, and quietly radiant from top to base, extending the wear and bringing a dreamy softness. true to early Tom Ford tradition (think pre-Lauder refinement), this is a suave, unisex gourmand that doesn’t shout—it speaks. Elegantly. If you love gourmands, this is an easy yes. And even if you don’t, try it anyway. It’s not brash, not too sweet, and never overbearing. Just a beautifully balanced spicy-sweet-ambery creation that proves why artistry still matters in perfumery. 9.5/10

This is a stunning woody Oriental floral. Starts out very heavy wood on me, but it is soon joined by spices and florals and a creamy sweet vanilla. I didn't even know what Kulfi was but kept getting this lactonic creaminess that is super rich. Doing a search, I was surprised to find that it is a form of Indian ice cream. Wow, that really comes across to me here. Indian ice cream must be very creamy, like gelato, because that's what I'm getting here. Though the woodiness dissipates as the fragrance dries down, it is always there in the background, but that sensuous spiciness comes forward. I am not picking up the florals as strongly here, possibly because the spice and woodiness has captured my attention -and my heart! It doesn't matter because this is gorgeous as is, and the combination of spices, and vanilla, and kulfi is just intoxicating. Performance wise, I found this to have heavy projection with just one spray. Within 2 hours the silage had gone down considerably, but it did last for a good part of the day, which is not the best time to wear this as I think it is way too sexy for day wear. While I only have a travel sprayer right now, I am considering a small bottle. But since one spray did the job, and I wear it so infrequently only when going somewhere special, I think this sprayer should last quite a while.

First I observed the objects on her dressing table, the lotions she uses, the accessories. I took them, looked at them. I held her little watch, turned it, stared. Then I peeked into the closet. Dresses, many dresses, ornaments... All these things that make a woman complete aroused in me a terrible feeling of loneliness, sympathy and the desire to be hers. Orhan Pamuk about love, Kemel and Fusun, Noir pour Femme takes us on such a journey full of feelings with the beauty of the Bosphorus and the smell of kulfi in the air, as if you are in a time where the smell brings nostalgia for more relaxed times.

Tom Ford Noir Pour Femme is a big-boned, 90s style floral vanilla in the style of Givenchy's Organza Indecence and the original, pre-reformulation Dior Addict (but quieter). It's a very competent piece of designer work that aims for a particular target and totally lands it. For women yearning for the va-va-VOOM of 90's vanilla powerhouses built with Jessica Rabbit-style curves, this will be your jam. Noir Pour Femme opens with a bitter orange and stale milk chocolate accord, briefly recalling a Terry's Chocolate Orange, and then slides into a heavy, plasticky vanilla that owes all of its cues to the orchid flower and none to the vanilla bean. It's sort of Black Orchid-lite at this point, minus the repellent tuber and cucumber notes. The vanilla is musky and floral, and it might fold over under the weight of its own voluptuousness but for the waft of bad-gal cigarette and the sour tang of fresh ginger root acting in consort to cut the cream. The trajectory from opening notes to the base is rather short, but I'm not blaming Tom Ford for doing what every other designer is doing, which is to frontload all the rich notes and leave the heart and base to deflate like a balloon (the attenuation happening just after you've already handed over the credit card, of course). The base here is a typical ambery, woody oriental affair  nothing too exceptional but (to give credit where credit is due) nothing even vaguely synthetic-smelling in that Iso E Super or potent woody amber aromachemical way. The whole shebang is a Greatest Hits tour of some of the high points from Tom Ford's own stable of scents (the plummy ginger from Plum Japonais, the vanilla from Tobacco Vanille, the heavy, musky orchid from Black Orchid, and the bitter orange from Sahara Noir) as well as from the powerhouse vanillas from the 90's (the orange vanilla from Organza Indecence, and the boozy, smoky floral vanilla from Addict). There's also a distinctly sleazy, morning-after-the-night-before quality to Noir Pour Femme. If you've ever yearned for the days when you stumble home from a nightclub at 6 in the morning, lipstick smeared and your lips stained with cheap wine, smelling like last night's smoke and wearing some random man's black leather jacket, the Noir Pour Femme is for you. Or even if you still do that. I'm not judging.

An embrace. An elegant creamy white merino sweater. A Christmas cookie. A whole night by the fireplace in the softest of sofas, cocoa and rum in the cups… Tom Ford’s Noir pour Femme makes my fantasy go crazy! When I spray it I know exactly what happens: a lot that I did not expect. Just like when I spray Chanel’s gorgeous Cuir de Russie EdT. NpF and CdR are both imagination triggers. Tom Ford has surprised me positively many times during the last ten years. Until then I found the fragrances a bit overpriced and I managed to steer clear of them for a long time. Until I met Black Orchid EdP. And Violet Blonde. I knew then, that TF Fragrances were something special. Noir pour Femme is no exception. With NpF I get never ending pictures and short films in my head, mostly about the themes I mentioned in the start. It is such a cozy smell. It makes me feel ridiculously great. And the best thing is that longevity of this is amazing. When I spray in the morning I can enjoy it all day, in the evening and the next morning as well. And whenever I pay attention through this journey I get impressions of comforting and pleasing things and scenarios. What is not to like?! This is a keeper. I can only repeat myself: Wauw… a long lasting, insisting one of its kind. Year 2, 185/365

I'm writing this for me i don't care what no one thinks. I had this perfume half of my life this perfume. I had it since i was 11-12, i cant believe all the years i wore it and i still have a lot left i rarely wear perfumes.

Being honest, this perfume surprised me. Lactonic notes can be tricky in perfumery, some smell like heaven, and others can smell rancid. Luckily this one is the first case. The creaminess in it was a pleasant surprise. to me this is a cozy winter afternoon at home, reading a book with some tea. This is it

I spontaneously tested Noir pour Femme in my little regular perfumery. I didn't find it bad, but it wasn't that outstanding during the first test. Later, when I got into my mom's car, she said, "you smell like gingerbread." It had to be the Noir since I hadn't tested anything sweet otherwise. The scent didn't let me go either, as the sprayed spot smelled wonderful.
How did I manage to overlook this amazing scent all these years?! I have constantly confused this unbelievably good perfume with Tom Ford's Black Orchid for some reason.

For weeks, I've been sneaking around this specimen. An original sample eventually found its way to me. Long overlooked, I brought it out every now and then. With each wear, I liked this charmer more and more. Sprayed once in the morning, it greeted me in the hallway still at noon. On the skin, it was still softly present in the evening.

I’d classify this perfume as a fresh-floral. They are top notes of all sorts of citrus which just makes it super fresh smelling and unisex at first. Next are all the florals, but the citrus is still there, though ebbs. It’s slightly sweet, but I’d never classify it as such. Rose is absolutely there after ten minutes and smells heavenly. It’s the main scent note for the duration of the perfume. It is more of a skin scent on me—very much neutral so that it can be worn for any occasion. This perfume is a breath of fresh air. I love it! Longevity fair, sillage good.

I feel this perfume enchant you or let you super meh, not in between feelings. The first time, in winter, I feel the second. I only smelled a common citric-woody perfume, I didnt understand what conexion there is between lemons and the moon. Today, a very hot spring day, I tried my decant again and I can't believe how beautiful it is what I was smelling. A beatiful light purple night sky appeared in my mind, evoquing a moment of wonder very few perfumes have made me feel. It smelled more like I remembered The favourite instead of what The favourite smells to me right now This wonderful moment of feelings dissapeared the moment my brain recognized it was like smelling a luxurious rose+lemon soap and the enchant faded away, but it is still very beautiful and pleasant. It also has something orange leaning in the opening It lasted strong in my skin at least 2h. Now that they have passed 5h, it smells more your typical unisex woody fragrance with the Penhaligon DNA I am getting used by this point.

As most people know, citrus scents are not my thing. I'm really happy that I've found some fragrances with clear citrus aromas that I really like. Luna is one of those few, another beautiful is Ultima Storia and of course unique Burlington 1819 which was the first citrus scent which caught my eye and which I find hard to wear myself though. Luna is at its best on hot summer days, after a shower or when your mind is heavy and you feel like you have too much to think about. It might also work in the gym, but despite the citrus, Luna is a relaxing and calming scent. It is fresh, soft, gentle, incredibly balanced and well blended. The rose and jasmine tie the notes together so well that the citrus is present until the end. Contrary to the initial impression that the citrus notes seemed to disappear quickly, they last very well throughout the long life of the fragrance. Of course, they perform more strongly at the beginning and then level out immediately afterwards. A subtle aromatic essence permeates through the citrus, but I still wouldn't classify the scent as aromatic. The juniper berry also doesn't make the scent sharp and it doesn't conjure up images of a drink. The musk and ambergris base makes the scent clean and sensual, yet innocent, while the Fir Balsam adds depth to the freshness, and together with the juniper berries and citrus, it creates a unique refreshing composition that I haven't found in any other fragrance. The scent is clear, transparent, breathable and soothing. It's no soapy nor shampoo like. What's also special about Luna is its longevity: it easily lasts all day, which is rare for such fragrances. It projects in the nice way as well. Luna is totally unisex imo. If citrus isn't my favorite category, Penhaligon's isn't one of my favorite houses either, but I think I could find others in this collection that I like. I’m absolutely in love with this scent. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

Although this is EDT it is a slightly more substantial, lemon-y version of Juniper Sling that performs better! The hint of rose is also beautiful and subtle! I admit that I've learned to value lighter but soothing and mellow scents that aren't as noisy in creating a sillage around me. When I tried this for the first time in November, it just smelled like lemons to my underdeveloped olfactory senses so I didn't appreciate it. But now that my nose has become more sophisticated with a collection of 100+ perfumes, I can appreciate a work of art when I smell it. I came across part of a 5 ml sample that had some juice left in it, and the herbal lemon with the undertone of florals was just beautiful. So I had to replenish my stock with a 100ml bottle someone was selling for a massive discount on Ebay. I think this might soon become my new signature scent. Penhaligon's keeps coming out with masterpieces and this one is no exception.

This is the first proper fragrance I bought myself, entirely based on my love of jasmine. The sales associate recommended this to me, and I fell in love! It’s watery due to the EDT concentration, which creates this lovely sheer, sparkly quality. It smells to me, like a rose-lychee martini, with a very juniper forward gin, in an ice cold glass. It is sat amongst giant Douglas firs, under a waxing moon.
Luna is one of the perfumes which I got as a sample when I visited Etiket. It's a lovely ethereal, light, airy, fresh citron and rose perfume.

Luna is a soft fragrance with a freshness that makes it easy to wear. The citrus notes bring a light, sparkling touch at the opening before giving way to a classic floral duo: rose and jasmine. Bright, clean, and effortless, but nothing groundbreaking. The composition is pleasant and well-balanced, yet it doesn’t stand out. Its main flaw? It doesn’t last.
You’re eating a dainty iced lemon cake at the spa, with light aromatherapy going in the background. And like a spa, Luna is beautiful, gentle, serene…and just a little impersonal.

Frilly gin tonic from seasonal menu with too much rose jam in it. Fizzy, watery, sparkly. Honeyed, sweet. Far too sweet. The kind of cocktail I'd take two sips of and then give the rest to my partner to finish because the flavor is too aggressive for me. The rose note itself is nearly identical to the one in The Coveted Duchess Rose .

Opens up super lemony, very acidic, bright and astringent, then becomes a bit floral but overall smells like a sparkling lemon and a Christmas tree, very pine-y yet not anything masculine or conventional.

Blenheim Palace is a well known house in Oxfordshire – nothing petite but a respectable country estate which evaporates a certain grandezza. It is the ancestral seat of the 11th Count of Marlborough who belongs to the higher aristocracy within the English hierarchy. As a fan of the folding bike, of course, Blenheim Palace is known to me, since the annual “Brompton Foldingbike World Championship” takes place there – an event that can really count as typically English. It is a cross county race on tiny Brompton folding bikes that have only 18'' wheels. The participants are asked to dress themselves according to the noble event – cycling shorts and jacket, shirt and tie or bow tie are a must! But Penhaligon's, rightly or not, adorns itself with borrowed plumes by using the name Blenheim. Years ago I noticed the mostly positive reviews on Basenotes. Blenheim Bouquet seems to be something like the fragrance reference of this brand. Anything else they do is likely to get compared with Blenheim Bouquet. Blenheim Bouquet is basically citric. It is a straightforward lemon with only some green and herbal echoes. I suppose, before the aquatics were invented, it was those green citric scents that men would go for instead. By regarding this style as conservative and outdated you would not do justice to Blenheim Bouquet. This style is robust and gripping. It is the sports fragrance for the modern and athletic gentleman of 1902! The more the lemon fades away and the green notes come forward, the better I like Blenheim Bouquet. But I am not convinced about the fragrance note “pine”. I do not see dark coniferous woods here – like i.e. Acqua di Selva. Musky notes and also some vetiver rather give you the impression of the amiable English landscape park that surrounds Blenheim Palace. I do not understand that vetiver is not part of the known pyramid. After about two hours, I get lots of it. Blenheim Bouquet may be a fragrance of the past, but also today it would make a good company on a stylish outing in Oxfordshire. Who knows – one or the other participant of the Brompton Foldingbike World Championship may complete his appearance with a few spritzes of Blenheim Bouquet!

I know some people find it astringent or harsh but I definitely don’t. It’s a soft sweet fragrance on my skin.
