The scent is very thick with pink pepper layered over sesame milk and some powdery iris with oakwood. But overall the scent is a bit bland, some people have described it as a vanilla-forward version of Dior Homme Intense. Like many Penhaligon's perfumes, though, I think this is quite unisex. But still too foody to add to my collection.

The opening caught me off guard. I was expecting sesame oil but this is more like putting your nose in a handful of sesame seeds: slightly powdery and vaguely reminiscent of yeast. I can’t tell if I enjoy it for the first hour or two. It isn’t unpleasant, but it’s so unusual that I’m caught off guard and unsure if I want to smell like this. Eventually the orris and vanilla kick in, adding depth and warmth to the yeasty top notes, and suddenly it all clicks into place for me. It’s warm and cozy and comfortable, and I can’t stop pressing my nose to my wrists. It’s unusual without being alienating, interesting but extremely wearable, arguably gourmand (my least favorite fragrance type) but not at all cloying. It doesn’t project strongly but longevity is solid: 9 hours later and I still get whiffs of warm, creamy vanilla sesame bread every time I move my arms. The marketing blurb claims this has “smoky, rum-like and leather hints” but I don’t pick up any of that. The reviewer who compared this to a sesame baguette is right on the money: it’s a sesame baguette dipped in vanilla and oh so tasty.

I don’t know what took me so long to discover this, but I cannot contain my excitement for this absolute sleeping beauty. Everything about this perfume is so well-thought out: the bottle design, the name, and the scent concept. Iris is a note that only recently can I admit to loving, and mainly because I’m not a powdery girl. But if it’s one thing I’ve learned about myself, is that I love a *sweet*, gourmand leaning iris. Mister Thompson showcases a traditional purple iris, in all its powdery/floral/earthy glory, paired with a savory sesame and some sweet vanilla joy. There is a bite of spice, but it’s only really noticeable in the opening. The scent feels cozy and friendly, but it holds power, intellect, and makes you feel grounded. The same way elephants move about in this world. Omniscient, emotionally intelligent, gentle giants that are not to be messed with. Interesting enough, elephant herds are typically lead by a matriarch, so this scent being marketed / named for men while smelling totally unisex is kinda funny. It’s a beautiful and complex scent of many trades, and I feel graceful, brilliant, and reassured when I wear this. Soft enough to wear year round (maybe not in hot hot summer), and kind enough to wear on many occasions. Definitely an underdog from the portraits line from Penhaligon’s and one that deserves way more love.

Tested at printemps shop last week i earned a good reviews of the release. After smelled i was between a good surprise and the disappointement. Dissapointed cause its the same scent of dior homme intenseso nothing of news. And glad cause i can have again this odour after dior homme intense was reformulated and 2011 version discountinued. But the price is little bit more expensive and it will grow up in january 2024 ,so i buyed it immediatly. Its a fragrance masculine perfect for winter ,which has already made his prouf.

Somehow for me the notes in this sometimes create the most delicious waﬄe cone accord to my nose. Love it. I don't get floral or powdery, but gourmand, vanilla dominant, caramelized sugar, bordering on a lighter more traditional take on the burnt sugars found in, for example, Kerosene's fragrances. One of the distinctive gems in the series.

Creamy Iris. I don't get a super noticeable vanilla note, but more of a caramelised one. It develops from this to a more spiced mode (Cardamom). Makes me feel it's made for formal situations. Something nobility would wear in the past days. Sadly longevity is not that good on skin for me. Used for a couple of days in the cold and maybe reached the 5-6 hours.

This perfume is creamy and comforting on my skin. Like many in the Portraits collection, its projection is subtle (weak), but last for 8+ hours on me. The sillage is close, about 20 - 30 cm, making it an intimate scent. Which makes sense with the imagery Penhaligon's gives: Mr. Thompson, a figure who sees and hears everything without being noticed, while exuding class.

Despite being omniscient, Mr.Thompson is quite the curious creature. To some he is this beautiful Iris beast, powdery and subtle. To others he is a gourmand king, vanilla and sesame ruling over all. For me he is the latter and I love him for it. On my skin Mr.Thompson is a warm vanilla and sesame bomb, garnering me compliments and the oh so loved 'What are you wearing?

And you, Mr. Thompson? I was so looking forward to meeting you. And then this: You seem almost inconsequential, so simple and straightforward is your nature. So terribly unexciting and quiet, you almost blend into the background. One could almost forget you. Almost. But I did not, I could not.

Tom Ford's Smoky Cherry perfume is an olfactory masterpiece that effortlessly captures the essence of sophistication and allure. From the moment it graces your skin, this fragrance unveils a symphony of notes that dance together in perfect harmony, creating an intoxicating aura that is both elegant and memorable. At the heart of this enchanting fragrance lies the captivating cherry note, a focal point that sets Smoky Cherry apart as a true gem in the perfume world. The cherry accord is meticulously balanced, neither overly sweet nor cloying, but rather a nuanced and sultry embrace that lingers throughout the wearing experience. It's a revelation in the realm of cherry-centric scents, proving that subtlety can be just as impactful as boldness. The smoky undertones add a layer of depth and mystery, weaving seamlessly with the fruity notes to create a scent that is as complex as it is inviting. As the fragrance evolves on the skin, hints of woods and spices emerge, enhancing the overall allure and leaving an indelible impression. Tom Ford's dedication to quality is evident in every facet of Smoky Cherry, from its carefully selected ingredients to its refined and luxurious packaging. Wearing this perfume is more than a sensory experience; it's a journey into a world where sophistication and sensuality intertwine. In a market saturated with fragrances, Tom Ford's Smoky Cherry stands out as the pinnacle of cherry-infused perfumery, a timeless creation that captivates the senses and leaves an indelible mark on the wearer and those lucky enough to catch a whiff. It's not just a fragrance; it's an embodiment of elegance, making it the best choice for those who seek a scent that transcends the ordinary.

I love this scent, its a perfect blend of cherry and smokiness. Its not too sweet, but still fruity. BUT, my partner absolutely despises it because it smells so similar to the artificial cherry flavouring in medicine. If you are looking for a hyperrealisitic cherry scent this might not be the one for you. Given the price I don't reccomend blind buying this, wear it for a few hours before purchasing the full size.

Not my outright favourite scent, but it's the one that anchored my to this hobby. The cherry opening hits hard, but it burns out quick. What remains is smoky and leathery but altogether less impactful. I can't afford to keep buying it, but its fleeting nature does add to the mystique. It's the one I come back to whenever I wonder what I'm looking for in a fragrance, it's in those first 3 seconds.

I got a 5 ml decant of this fragrance, and initially all I got from it was leather. Disappointed, I put it away into a dark drawer. Weeks went by, I decided to try it again. To my surprise, cherry made its appearance. It is a beautiful, mature, sophisticated cherry and leather blend, very smooth, very suave. Zero smoke on my skin, though, but I don't mind, I love the scent nonetheless.

smells like my mom and thats a positive: newports and jergans lotion. reminds me of summers in alabama where i'd float in the kiddie pool while my mom smoked and listened to back to black on repeat. one of the 3 tom fords i actually want to have full bottles of but i likely never will because of the price. the smoke adds just enough depth overall to the scent to make it interesting.

If you love Cypriol like I do, you will love this. It has some of the most vivid and 3D Cypriol notes I have ever smelled in a fragrance. Absolutely great stuff. There is also definitely Frankincense in this, but it doesn't become highlighted until the drydown. The cherry here is toned down and mostly used as a "color" note to an otherwise smoky earthy composition.

This perfume is thick and dark. It's also a little smoky. It smells like sweet smoky old wood. Cherry Smoke represents the alluring world of the night. It evokes the feeling of being close to danger. Imagine being in a dim light bar half-finished cocktail in hand surrounded by strangers.

To be honest, I don't have an original perfume because of value. But I have an cheaper, but high-quality analogue of it. Saffron + cherry = medical cherry scent. It reminds me something frm childhood - something vintage, but new. It's dark, but sweet. I'm interested in gothic culture and in my opinion, this perfume is exactly for winter for gothic women... and men

The 'cherry' accord will probably be one of those that we will only remember in ten years at the latest - some with nostalgia, others perhaps with a shudder - as a trend and a whim of the - broadly speaking - 2010s. Cherry (or what is considered as such in perfumes) is not one of the 'classic' perfume ingredients, and it will not become one either.

Estee Lauder is not only raising prices after the acquisition of Tom Ford. No, they are quickly turning high-performing fragrance bestsellers into flankers. The cow must be milked! Electric Cherry and Cherry Smoke are released by marketing. 190€ for 30ml? Ambitious! Douglas gave me a sample of Cherry Smoke in Hamburg. Electric Cherry is not available yet.

Oh, Malabah is one of my absolute favorites from Penhaligon's. I get lemon tea at the opening, but that is quite brief. I can definitely perceive both the orris root and the rose in the heart, but on me, the ginger and cardamom really stand out. There's a gorgeous woody drydown, with the spices abiding long into it. This one is a spice lover's dream.

I tried this about a year ago, and it's been on my short list for possible fb purchase. So glad I bought a sample. It's not working for me at all. It sort of reminds me of L'Or Torrente, but without the warm coffee note...leaving lots of hollow pencil shavings and orange rinds tossed about the floor. I get a rustic kind of coriander, ginger spice mixture and I absolutely abhor it when people say that a fragrance smells like "A GrandMa/Old Lady" fragrance- since I am getting up there in years, not only is it not really descriptive- but my Grandmother with her sex bomb "Youthdew" and Vetyver fragrances, seemed to rock my Grandfather's world for 70 years...possibly longer since they lived to be nearly 100. So, I am not going to comment on the appropriate age group for this fragrance or gender...it's All and Both. It's just not for me. I felt it was too cedary, too orange-rindy and too Ambergrisy for my taste, but like everything from the House of Penhaligon, worth sampling. Inspite of being too much of some key notes, the sillage is watery but detectable about a ft. (30.48 cm) away when you move through space and it last for several hours at a lower volume adding a dry, woody, cinnamon and gingery pepper note to the skin- somehow though, the combination just doesn't excite me like Diptyque L'eau or Jo Malone's Nutmeg & Ginger, or Molton Brown's Black Pepper, all of which, "If I were a Rich Man...yada dada da da da..."I would be wearing right now...all day, every day. Seriously though, there is a bit of stuffiness and British refinery in this that really screams "Cucumber Sandwich, crumpet, Earl Grey...haberdashery." In spite of the spices which cool and blend into a trunk of antiquities, the orris root and musk behave rather politely on the right Gal or Guy- this probably spells of Kasbah markets fragrance with curry blends, rich hand carved woods and the finest silks.

I love and worship chai tea. I am a cardamom-obsessed weirdo. I want to eat it and smell like it at all times. That being said, Malabah is one of the best cardamom chai perfumes I've come across. It starts out fresh with citrus and tea, but it quickly becomes creamy with a touch of smoky amber for depth. It's the smokiness here that I really swoon over and that "makes" the perfume. My screen name isn't TeaWithMilk for nothing! I'm on a quest for the best tea fragrances I can get my hands on, and this is way up there on my list. The only think I can add is that I *wish* it were stronger. If this were a sillage monster I would truly be in heaven! The notes above are incorrect--it's cardamom here, not cinnamon, says the Penhaligon's website. SUMMARY: Sipping real Indian chai and eating rasmalai--my cardamom heaven

Malabah is such a beautiful name for a fragrance. Here I was captivated by its name and imagining a rich, spicy tea scent with an element of exotic sensuality. This fragrance, to put it nicely, is too polite and refined in my opinion. It's simplistic, inoffensive and rather plain. Malabah opened with some interesting accords which had me hoping this fragrance would develop into something magical. The lemony tea opening was about as interesting as it gets. The heart is a combination of sweet and spicy, with such weak sillage that one may wonder if they're wearing a perfume at all. I've had my fair share of spicy rose scents, and Malabah has left me underwhelmed in that department. For my spiced tea fix I usually turn to the beautiful L'Artisan's Tea for Two, not Malabah. I like strong, in-your-face kind of fragrances, and this Penhaligon's offering is far too lady-like and quiet for my personal tastes. I find it very British. The lasting strength is pretty poor, struggling to last half the day on my skin. It was far too discreet and lacked serious warmth and distinction. It's pleasant, I'll say that much, but exotic is not a word that comes to mind when describing Malabah unfortunately.

This is a beautiful light tea fragrance. Lemon and ginger form the tart pungent top notes, quickly paving the way for the astringent notes of steeped tea leaves - Earl Grey Tea to be exact. Hints of cardamom and nutmeg tantalize from a distance, adding a bit more spiciness to the ginger. A light, sweet rose adds a bit of floral beauty to this, and is accented by powdery orris. Warm amber and musk, commitments by bits of sandalwood round this down to a beautiful base.

Sweet candied fruits, the old-fashioned kind that are chewy and have sugar crystals on them. You can only get them in a candy confectioner's shoppe. And each one is sitting in a little white paper wrapper. The flowers and spices join in after a bit, creating quite a full-bodied fragrance. All for a few minutes.

Once again, a fragrance that I would have assessed quite differently, as the name would have led me to expect something rather heavy and cloying. Various vendors speak of opulent floral splendor, intoxicating scent, and an explosive (!) formula. But... :) This fragrance is something truly fine! And I mean really fine, delicate, and unobtrusive.

Malabah is, according to Penhaligon’s, inspired by a journey along the (undoubtedly historical) spice trade route in eastern India. What role Earl Grey tea, which traditionally contained Chinese tea, may have played there is known only to the manufacturer. If the drink is meant to allude - benevolently? - to the British... uh...

I took a long time to write this review, even though it is one of my favorite fragrances. I can't dissect/analyze a scent as precisely as most of you here, my descriptions are a bit simple, but I hope it helps you a bit anyway. So: Malabah has nothing in common with the usual summer scents.

Penhaligon's is not exactly a brand whose fragrances particularly impress me. So I was quite surprised when I received a sample of "Malabah" for my birthday. But what was right for Queen Victoria, who appointed William Penhaligon as "Barber and Perfumer to the English Court" towards the end of her reign, should not be dismissed untested "from my bedside.

This is how I would define this creation by Tom Ford, which I would have called Poudreux. Why? Because Métallique has a very little metallic vibe, it is an ephemeral illusion that lasts only a few moments. Then the perfume takes off its mask and reveals its true soul, the powdery and vanillic one. Métallique welcomes me with a great explosion of powdery, sweet, but above all, soapy accords. In my mind, the image of a creamy soap made with sweet peeled almonds takes shape, like a cuddly almond cream soap from Dove, not only for the scent of the soap but also for the creaminess. The dusty feeling is there, but it has nothing to do with that the buttery iris rhizome. I can barely perceive the flavour of the bergamot, which appears and lasts like the blink of an eye, or the spiciness of the pink pepper, which is a little more prominent. Instead, the opening is all aldehydes, so crunchy, like the pungent air on cool, humid autumn and winter mornings. The aldehydes used here give me a sense of fresh snow, away from the sparkling hairspray vibe of Chanel N°5 or the cold metallic vibe of Chrome Eau de Toilette . However, aldehydes are very modern and do not give an old-school vibe to the fragrance. If there is a metallic reminiscence, that lasts only a few minutes. From now on, the perfume takes an extraordinary twist. Métallique is heavy on the heliotrope nectar. The smooth scent of the flower is reminiscent of almond with a hint of vanilla. The almond border comes out eagerly during the middle phase. So dominant that I hardly recognise hawthorn and lily of the valley. Another perfume that I have possessed with an overdose of heliotrope is Deep Vanilla , and these two give me the same sensations without being clones or imitations. Also, in the heart, there is a hint of anise, which could be because of the white flowers, but I could mislead by the almond note from the heliotrope. When Métallique reaches the finish line, it does not change a lot compared to the middle stage, though the nutty and flowery accords slide towards a warm and sweet base made up of creamy woods and greedy spices. A note that I hardly perceive is the ambrette seeds. I don’t clearly feel that musky aspect of it that drives me crazy. Instead, a balsamic aura emanating from the Peruvian balsam now warmed for a long time by the skin surrounds the comforting vanilla and sandalwood. It smells like soapy vanilla. It seems strange to me that no one else has found a certain resemblance to Hypnotic Poison Eau de Toilette , especially when the almond notes of heliotrope blend with those of sandalwood and vanilla. The result of this mixture is very similar to what we find in Hypnotic. There are many facets that I perceive in this perfume. If I had to summarise Métallique in three major chords, I would say aldehyde, talc, and vanilla. On my nose, the notes that stand out most in the three phases are aldehydes, heliotrope, and vanilla. Métallique seems to me more suitable for the cold seasons because of its sweet flavours; the balmy and vanillic base does not suit the hot weather. Men can wear as easily it. It is alluring regardless of gender. Performances are average, I can smell it all day long, and it stays close to my body, not offending nor cloying. I base my opinion and review on a decant I have owned since Oct 2022. -Elysium

I have no words to describe how I feel about him. He is the one I never knew that I needed, and now he is the one that I can't live without. I find myself neglecting all others just to be with him and I think about him constantly when he's not there. I love being surrounded by his fragrance day or night, any time of year. I don't even know how to describe him to others, I'm just lost in his aura. He is my Metallique.

A beautiful, cold, sweet, floral vanilla with a hint of metal. Métallique feels both elegant and edgy. It's quietly cool and quirky without screaming for attention. Performance: about eight hours on skin or 12 hours on clothing with moderate projection. The enduring popularity of vanilla plus the recent aldehydic "clean" trend should have made Métallique a roaring success. Unfortunately, it was recently discontinued. Maybe it was ahead of its time in 2019. I will treasure my bottle until it runs out. There's nothing else quite like it.

I really think this fragrance would work better for me as a layering fragrance than as a scent on its own. While it is nice, I already have something in my wardrobe that reminds me somewhat of this to a degree. That peppery citrus vanilla opening reminds me of Alien Eau Extraordinaire's opening as it uses the same notes, but I like the note profile following the opening of AE better than the note profile used here. I must admit though, I really love the Hawthorne, and the lightly powdery heliotrope is pretty too. But despite the floral notes this is really all about the powdery vanilla, and to be honest, while it is okay, I really would like something a little more complex than that. Even though aldehydes are listed, they are very lightly done and just add a light airiness to this scent. So, if you have an aversion to that, you need not worry about that here. Personally, for an aldehyde vanilla fragrance, I prefer Dame's Vanilla Farfelue simply because there is a lot more going on and I find it very versatile and wearable any time. Though I haven't tried it yet, I'm not so sure how this would perform in other seasons as it has super low silage now. I fear it might just disappear under certain weather conditions, but I'll just have to wait and see on that front. Metallic? To me, not really, but I always have a hard time finding that accord in any fragrance that claims to have a metallic note anyway. Right now, I only have a 3ml.rollerball of this which I will use it to layer with other fragrances. I can think of a lot of fragrances in my wardrobe where this might work great in adding a little something special to a scent, but I will not replace with a bottle after this is done. Surprisingly, compared to other scents from this house, it is pretty reasonably price, which I suspect is due to its simple profile.

Months ago, I was gifted many Tom Ford fragrances. One of them was Métallique. By just taking the cap off, I could smell vanilla, but also an unquestionable note of something metallic. The note is so unique and realistic that it is more of a sensation. Like having bitten your lip and tasting the metallic taste of blood in your mouth. Métallique is very unique and I dislike and like it at the same time. I honestly cannot have enough vanilla fragrances, but even though Métallique is largely based on vanilla, it is so unique that I wouldn't consider it a vanilla fragrance. Upon first spray, Métallique opens with a fresh citrus note of bergamot. I do love my citrus vanillas, but a note of something green keeps Métallique a freshy rather than a sweet gourmand. The green note is strongly meddled with heliotrope making the fragrance lightly floral and powdery. On skin, vanilla isn't as prominent as it is from the bottle. Sharp citrus is the main accord along with aldehydes. The vanilla on skin is very dry and solely serves the purpose of grounding Métallique, so that it doesn't become a classic aromatic, green, cologne like fragrance. The dry vanilla is honestly the only thing that makes Métallique unisex, whereas without, it would have been leaning masculine. I have to give this another go, but I feel a slight headache creeping in. I don't usually have headaches, they are always a result of a fragrance too strong for my liking. The metallic note isn't as prominent on skin as it is from the bottle, which is prefered. I cannot imagine how it would smell if it lasted on skin and how I would feel about it. Smelling as cold and sterile as metal does. I am honestly unsure whether I will reach for this fragrance. It is a citrus, yes, it has vanilla, which I love, and absolutely adore together, but it is done in such a way that I don't feel completely comfortable about it. However, after complete dry down, an hour or so later, Métallique is calm, delicate and a mellow version of what it was before. I would still describe it as a dry vanilla, but it is delicately floral, aldehydic, slightly powdery. You know what? An actual treat!

I'm in the camp of "this just works on my skin". Signature worthy stuff to be honest. It's constructed around vanilla mostly, with some balsams and flowers. I definitely get a soapy aldehyde note with a hint of freshness from the citrus. But it's mostly the flowers and vanilla that dominate.

This is a very nice new Tom fords releases. As It happens in most of the new releases of this brand the performance is not great and It have some issue un longevity and sellage, but as It belongs to the signature collection has a good price so It can worth the purchase if you like the smell. The smell is good, not very original.

Ah yes, Metallique. It appeals to me, Ford always needs to be tested anyway, even if I don't really find much in it. But let's just see if a second Black Orchid comes out of this. Spray, what do we have here? This is, well, what is it? Swimming pool? Chlorine? No, it's not chlorine. But why swimming pool?

“Metallique” by Tom Ford combines the synthetic theme of metal, lacquer, color, workshop, technology, coldness, perhaps even a hint of chlorine and chemistry, with a warm, powdery vanilla core somewhere between gingerbread, powdered sugar, and Christmas market.

As a metalhead, I would like to share a few words about Tom Ford's "Métallique." I don't want to create a false impression, but we met secretly - in Düsseldorf - even though I was supposed to meet someone else. On a Saturday morning, I entered the Breuninger department store and strolled straight from the side entrance towards Tom Ford.

Opens with a sweet fruity rose that swiftly fades into a straightforward candied rose. If there are woods or vanilla in the base, they’re too subtle for my nose — it’s just rose all the way down. Projection and longevity are ehhhh who cares, you’ll get bored well before it wears off or anyone else smells it. I’ve smelled this same profile in a thousand other (more reasonably priced) fragrances. If you told me this was a designer scent you got on clearance, I wouldn’t bat an eye. To be clear, I’m not hating on designer frags (there are some bangers out there) BUUUT Penhaligon’s markets itself as a high quality, upmarket, niche perfumery, and frankly this ain’t it. In a word: underwhelming.

I wasn't expecting too much out of this fragrance. There aren't many notes and it's a pretty straightforward fragrance. Syrupy, sugary sweet roses with a subtle hint of freshness make up most of this fragrance and then I get some woodiness somewhere after the one hour mark and the sweetness of vanilla. The drydown is a non-descript woody sweetness that's pretty faint. The thing is, why would I pay such an exorbitant price when there are better rose fragrances out there that perform better? 410$ CAN is absolutely insane for a fragrance that becomes a skin scent after about an hour and a half (at least on my skin). Hard pass and a sign of relief from my wallet. On to the next!

Y'all know how I feel about rose scents... Alas, it is in the set and I will give it a fair chance. From the first spray, this is giving me Chloé vibes - pure and clean florals, however, a little more mature and a little soapy. Yet again, this is more of a spring scent than for autumn. Though I dislike florals, I have to say Duchess Rose is more inviting to try on my skin than Lady Blanche was. On skin, Duchess Rose has the same Chloé-esque quality to its florals. Somewhat soapy too. It is quite light and airy for a rose scent. It is in fact a fine fragrance, light, feminine and soft. Duchess Rose is so light that I reapplied generously just after it dried down. Even though I was generous to begin with! In all honesty, the fragrance is barely there. Very personal and only those passing you by or standing next to you, would be able to smell it. I usually wear a fragrance for some hours and write my final take then, but I completely forgot. Why? Because Duchess Rose is so faint and lasts only a few hours. I can only smell her close to skin. What I do smell is a pleasant, light take on a classic rose.

Penhaligon describes this as a scent for a young bride brimming with passion for her negligent husband. I think this scent is for an even younger audience. I imagine more of a young girl who is barely in her teens, who is walking through a rose garden while eating sweets, rubbing the excess sugar off her fingers onto the rose petals. This is a candy sweet rose, like it was plucked at its prime and coated in a thing layer of sugar. Its a very young and very pretty rose. I didn't pick up much of the wood. This is another fairly weak fragrance from Penhaligon. It lasts a little over 3 hours on skin and has little to no projection. Like most Penhaligon fragrances, its expensive. They offer 75ml for $315. Its a nice rose but not that nice.

Sweet, fresh, delicate rose swaddled in the ethereal smoothness of Iso E Super's clean woods, and Iso must be why many people find this perfume to be little more than the ghost of citrus-rose. Which is a shame because the way the citrus and rose are haloed by the Iso creates this incredible longevity of mingled notes balanced to perfection.

Vanillin sweet, though not sugary sweet, and syrupy, It's got the same vanillic base that's been used in "Eau the Audacity" from the Potions & Remedies line by the same brand, a bit fruity in the opening instead of citrusy, think of sweet and ripe plums with a bit of something like pink pepper yet not much rose.

On Wednesdays at five o'clock tea. With cakes, sandwiches, sherry, and sometimes a little whisky. Mylady married the snooty, haughty Lord Worcester many years ago. He became rich through the production of the eponymous sauce, which is particularly good on ragout fin or egg dishes. She would have preferred to become a duchess, but the lord is only a baron.

Penhaligon’s background story for “The Coveted Duchess Rose” is about a duchess who, due to her unhappy marriage, is in search of fun, frivolity, and the occasional affair. The design of the bottle is a pictorial representation of the English word “vixen” (Old English “fyxe,” German Füchsin).

I am surprised to read about the man-devouring Duchess, whose Duke, if we are to believe the story from Penhaligon's, has not exactly turned out to be "l'homme idéal." She is certainly desirable. However, I find it quite unlikely that Rose throws herself at the necks of her lovers.

Majestic opening with the iconic antagonistic note of chocolatey sweet and delicately bitter earthy truffles of Black Orchid Tradicional here soaked in rum, bringing an alcoholic vibe that already makes clear a slightly more masculine and full-bodied posture than its predecessor. In this olfactory reinterpretation of the classic from 'TF', the sweetness of the ylang and the earthy chocolatey patchouli were in my view amplified while the rum and plum became even more prominent and thus increasing the sensuality in relation to the original Tom Ford Black Orchid perfume EDP version. The floral accord is added with the arrival of the fantasy note of black orchid enhancing the dark and nocturnal facet characteristic of this famous composition. Black Orchid Parfum lost complexity in relation to the Traditional and thus gained versatility and is more "wearable", but the formal, refined, sophisticated and luxurious appeal continues in this edition. Black Orchid in Parfum version is a Unisex Floral Amber Alcoholic Perfume; From an intense experience of one of Tom Ford's historic lines, it celebrates the iconic legacy of its classic world-class and timeless fragrance. With excellent performance!

For so long i stayed away from this and thought it was bad because of the mass appealing affect but then one day. i gave it a try and man, i fell in love with this scent. even tho it has a mass appealing effect, it is still very outspoken and has something bold. In the opening it might be a bit to loud and sharp but give it 30 minutes to an hour and how it transforms and develops into this spicy, rich, deep, sweet, gourmand yet very woody and spicy scent is what makes you addicted. you want more and more, i have to keep myself from reapplying the scent because i love the transition. When it comes to performance it is amazing, longevity as well as sillage. on numerous occasions i've had people walk into the room, and say what smells so good in here??! to which i happily replied; me?? For the people that know me they tell me that they could smell me from in the hallway and liked/loved the scent. Summed up i would say, if you like spicy woody sweet fragrances give this a try, and with that i mean wear it not just one time, but give it a couple of days to a week. And for the mass appeal part, i see it as a plus it is still a pretty bold fragrance and outspoken but when people smell it, instead of finding it polarizing, they end up loving it. Superb.

Spraying this perfume always gives me a very dark purple impression. That plum note, the truffle, orchid…it just triggers thoughts of that shade of purple. The opening is actually quite earthy and spicy. Truffle and the patchouli notes are huge here. It’s not my favorite, but I think that this does get better in the dry down. The orchid is apparent with its own spiciness/chocolatey nuances. Plum is also a prominent note. It’s paired with rum, which gives it a very interesting and further spiced quality. Plummy rum doesn’t sound like it’d taste that great, but the smell is nice. That opening blast will calm down after 10 minutes or so. The plum feels more defined and the balance of the composition is a lot better to my nose. That truffle sticks around, but the patchouli and rum will back off in intensity. So, it’s earthier rather than a blend of earthy and spicy. Still, you have that sweet boozy quality and the ylang-ylang really begins to come into play. At this stage, the orchid is superseded by that ylang-ylang. There is a creaminess to the blend. It’s funny, because it does have a dark chocolate-like aroma, but also an earthy almost dusty touches to it. Parfum strikes me as a very dry perfume. The end is a ylang-ylang and truffle/patchoui mix. The other notes just sort of blend together into a sweetish dark concoction, that’s really attractive.

This one is a way better version than edp, especially in the opening. When i first tried BO, didn’t appeal much to me because it was mainly an earthly sour dry woody fragrance - where i couldn’t envision directly all of the beauty. I gave up on it BUT during the dry down started to get different whiffs of it where i became almost addicted the- truffle. So instead of going for edp, i thought why not directly blind buy the parfum since both go in the same direction. Well, everything that made me like the OG, i found it in the parfum from the opening to its end. The emphasis on the truffle note is significantly more proement, it’s less earthy but softer, well rounded, less sharp in the sourness. The truffle note is really what makes this fragrance exceptionnal and unique - while the OG takes some time to get there, with the « parfum » you directly get to the beauty of what BO firstly intended to be. The plus the EDP has, is that during the dry down, chocolaty note appears (sweetness) which way more foreward than in the parfum which eventually counterbalance the initial flaws of the opening (which i believe what scares most of people who say to dislike this fragrance). No more sourness, no more dry earthy but instead it becomes a luxurious deep and richer than le Parfum, which remains truffle forward and boozy, lacking this profoundness. The EDP is unisexe in the opening before becoming feminine. The parfum is more feminine, sweeter from the begining. Hence, while liking strong truffle, i am glad having the parfum. But i couldn’t be without the edp, because then i was lacking of the profound aspect of it. So now i layer both by applying them together. Both perform great even though the parfum, seems to do better. EDP OG : 8.5/10 (i really have to wait for the dry down to benefit from it) Le parfum : 9.5/10 (could be perfect on its own but knowing edp, i was missing a slight part of it)

I sprayed this on and immediately went "whoa". It's a very deep, in-your-face spice at the beginning. This smells like something you would wear to the will reading for your rich husband who died under mysterious circumstances.

I tried this a full year ago and I disliked it a lot. Today, I decided to give it another try since I had a feeling my opinion on it would definitely change. I couldn't have been more right. On my skin, it developed beautifully. That earthy truffle that I previously hated turned into a delightful dark mysteriousness.

It’s been a few weeks since my return to Switzerland and my discovery of Ombré Leather, which I absolutely adore. From the very first wear, it was a revelation: Tom Ford makes the best fragrances in the world, full stop. No other brand is necessary, because I’ve found the Holy Grail. And I intend to become an expert in the field. I need more.

There is something so special and complex about black orchid. It’s a very sexy and domineering fragrance. It’s a huge confidence booster and a total head turner. I will say it is incredibly divisive. I was gifted this perfume by a former friend who received it for free and gave it to me because it “smelled like absolute shit”.

The highest mountains in the world are over 8000 meters high. There are only 14 of them; all others are lower, but by no means easier to climb. Just like with fragrances, there are scent pyramids that vary in height and structure depending on the compositions.

Every now and then I dutifully trot up to the Tom Ford concession at a local high end department store and I gaze at the wares on offer, almost willing them to shout "BUY ME"!! As of yet, very few fragrances by this house have entranced me enough to spend the ludicrous asking price on them. Jasmin Rouge, however, is one that may possibly make it to my collection. I will more than likely talk myself out of it a few times still :) ... because this fragrance is an Alien 'wannabe' to my nose, and I'd rather spend the money on a bottle of Essence Absolu at the moment ... teehee. JR is very similar (and costs nearly double in this country) to the Mugler ... with approximately similar sillage but less longevity. "Why then own it?" you would ask. Well ... it does have it's merits. Firstly, Jasmin Rouge is a very smooth ride. A sparkly opening of spices leads quickly to a very lush and creamy Jasmine note displaying a very muted indole ... enticing! It's a lot gentler than the almost mind shattering effect of Alien (which I happen to enjoy) with the similarity between the two resting squarely on the shoulders of Cashmeran ... an aroma chemical which both fragrances contain. My nose tells me there is absolutely no doubt of this ... here it is called 'woods' ... House Mugler is more up front about it and simply calls it what it is :). The deep dry down here (at about 5 hours) is a very nice Van/Amber but stays rather close to the skin. A solid application under clothes would probably amp it up a bit. I do like Jasmin Rouge quite a lot ... it's smoother and more elegant than Essence Absolu and would definitely serve a purpose in the right situation. I'm just not sure that it wouldn't always play second fiddle to my beloved Alien ... time will tell :).

Jasmine Rouge comes in a pretty red bottle, which is what initially caught my eye at Saks Fifth Avenue. I spent an hour sniffing miscellaneous perfumes until my nose could no longer take it. Coffee beans didn’t help, but I persisted until I found the one I wanted to buy, as this juice isn’t cheap. Initially I left with a different bottle, but the sales person sent me home with a small sample of Jasmine Rouge because I was torn between two scents. I went back the following week to buy this one. It’s pure jasmine on my skin, a lovely, sexy, warm scent that has great longevity and reach for me. I have so many perfumes that this one doesn’t get used as often as it should. It reminds me of summer love, warm nights outside, tropical breezes. Just magical.

The jasmine has probably received the solifor treatment more than any flower in perfumery save the rose. There are plenty of types available and at the full range of price points. Serge Lutens‘s solifloriental A la Nuit and leather solifor Sarrasins. Badgely Mischka’s fruity soliflor Fleurs de Nuit. Mugler’s chemo-soliflor Alien. Etat Libre’s woody soliflor Jasmin et Cigarette. Green, indolic, sweet, doughy, sweaty, pretty, naughty? There is such a wide range of tones that by highlighting or downplaying specific notes, a perfume may take any number of turns. That said, jasmine solifores tend generally tend toward the crass. Jasmine Rouge is not more tactless than, say, A la Nuit, which is my favorite jasmine soliflor, largely for its hearty embrace of crassness. Jasmine Rouge has an effusive opening, with a kaleidoscopic cycle jumping around from green to sweet to tart-indolic to spicy-floral at any given moment. It even has a bit of the yeastiness that jasmines and tuberoses sometimes have. It’s not unattractive by any means, but jasmine topnotes seldom are. Others have noted that it falls apart by the basenotes, and I disagree. It does become less distinctive over time, and a bland sweetness smothers the other topnotes, but it manages to keep a sketch of its overall shape. Would you pay $250-500 for a a beautiful perfume that you love? Tough question. Would you pay it for a tolerable one? Counterintuitively, distinctiveness is a risk in a luxury design product. Recognizability has as much greater value, and is typically found sitting in the middle of the road. Jasmine Rouge winds up feeling more like a place holder in a perfume line than than a perfume that someone had a great desire to make. It captures an inherent obstacle to launching a line rather than releasing a perfume. How inspired will a perfume be if its goal it to fit a category and fill a slot? It’s a question that comes up with each perfume in the Tom Ford Private Blend line. from scenthurdle.com

This is all about the packaging for me. The bottle is the star of the TF upper tier collection. More brilliant than the cool turquoise of Neroli Portofino, this high quality red glass would look simply divine on my dresser. I won't lie, I've been itching to justify a TF in my collection, for over ayear. I need more time...especially at this price point...I want to get it right. That would mean that I am as head-over-heels about the contents as the bottle itself. That is NOT the case with Jasmine Rouge. I find Jasmine is undeniable, I can't hate it even if I tried. It is the perfect flower of seduction, beauty and I feel their are so many interpretations of jasmine- there is a Jasmine for every season, every mood and the gamut runs from Etat Libre d’Orange's "Jasmin and Cigarette" to the iconic "Carnal Flower" by Frederic Malle to Serge Luten's "Á La Nuit" and all the way across town to my drugstore bought beloved Healing Gardens "Sensual therapy Jasmine" which is perfect refrigerated in the muggy summer heat, FYI. But I must say, after all the pomp and circumstance displayed by the sales associate to even let me pick up this bottle and the momentary pause he gave before allowing me to even sample this one...I was expecting something special. Jasmin Rouge is a beautiful pure Jasmin, with moderate sillage of about 1 meter , but so incredibly linear! Ugh. I was left with a hollow sense of deep inner sadness and questioning...is this all there is in the universe, Mon Dieux?! Perhaps, that's a little melodramatic, but I was definitely underwhelmed. Jasmin Rouge can't hold a candle to "Carnal Flower" or even to the little bottles of pure jasmine oil concentrate available for sale on the beaches of Barbados for a couple of USD to all tourists during Spring break. It was just a mirage wrapped in a very pretty package. Quel dommage.

Jasmine Rouge Jasmine rouge is a modern seductive, animalic jasmine scent. Its one of the few Tom Fords I really enjoy and can wear. Its sexy, deep and has a luxe feel. Superb for the cold night air of winter. If you enjoy jasmine on the naughty side, check this gem out. Superb longevity.

I'm loathe to dismiss a scent that is a favorite of so many. So as a disclaimer, I think this is a pleasant, wearable spicy jasmine that smells nice and (as my friends who are JR fans attest) makes people feel sensual and confident. But I've increasing found something a bit stale about it and ended up giving my bottle away.

I don't know what's behind the "rouge" part of the name, other than the bottle, because nothing about this scent evokes "red" in my mind. The image that I get is a petite, dainty little waterfall carrying an array of jasmine petals. This aquatic note isn't salty at all, and mainly just contributes a feeling of "fresh air" to the fragrance.

I love Jasmine, but when Jasmine is indolic for me it can be too much and I tend to prefer the non-indolic Jasmine scents, this falls into this category to my nose. Though it has a spicy side that gives it structure and makes it sexy, it’s also a creamy rich and beautiful Jasmine that leaves a beautiful sillage.

Jasmin Rouge is a pedestrian jasmine fragrance with warm, creamy facets, a dose of honeyed sweetness, and a smooth amber base. While that doesn't sound terrible on paper, it's much duller than you might expect, and overall a mild disappointment. It opens very fresh with a naturalistic jasmine sambac note, accented by a light caress of warm spices.

I tried this scent because I love so much the jasmin note and because I was attracted by this minimal but sexy red squared bottle reminding me an old chemist's potion : well, immediately a cloud of intoxicating spicy Jasmine came to my nose, made richer and fizzier by the citrusy touch at the opening .

On the bank of the Euphrates once lay one of the ancient world's most influential cities: Babylon. It was the capital of Babylonia in southern Mesopotamia. Today, that's about 60 miles south of Baghdad, Iraq. Mentioned in the opening book of the Bible, the Book of Genesis, and often dismissed as a mythical building, they have also associated the Tower of Babel with well-known Babylonian structures such as the temple of the foundation of heaven and earth. The story of its construction appears to be an attempt to explain the existence of several human languages. The Babylonians wanted to name themselves by building a mighty city and a tower "with the top in the skies". God interrupted the work by confusing the workers' language so much that they could no longer understand each other. The city was never completed, and the people were scattered across the face of the earth. "Come, let us go down and confuse their language so they will not understand each other. So the Lord scattered them from there over all the earth, and they stopped building the city. That is why it was called Babel — because there the Lord confused the language of the whole world. From there the Lord scattered them over the face of the whole earth." However, Penhaligon's Babylon is not another Tower of Babel. Instead, it is anything but confused or scattered. It is a harmony of spicy, earthy, woody accords, all rolled into one. Babylon opens with a robust spicy deal, a fragrance for spicy lovers, a blend of the holy trinity of spices - coriander, nutmeg, and saffron. At first, I get a blast of spicy, woody, and herbal accords, with a whiff of camomile, dry flowers, hay-like nuances. Then, I perceive the slightly leathery note of saffron with a slight citrus hint of bergamot that fades quickly. I even feel notes of blanched almonds, like almond paste, not as sweet as the marzipan. I adore this mysterious fragrance because of its unique personality. Oriental notes of spicy potpourri open the door to that magical oasis that we have rarely seen before. Soon, the warm spicy nuance twists into something smokier, and I think it's cypriol oil. The effect is intensely dry and smoky, like a burning brazier on which spices are roasted. The aroma converges into the earthy notes of cypriol in the heart, which is very dominant here. Cypriol oil blends with cedar and sandalwood, reproducing a picture of ancient times, hanging gardens, making rugs and oriental beauty. Although the cypriol adds a slightly leather nuance, the cologne never takes the leathery way. At a certain point, the perfume takes on a scent that recalls the smell of dried figs from Turkey. It is a nuance that does not resemble the classic milky fig, but is much closer to the caramelized fruit, cooked and dried in the sun. This is a nuance that I like and did not expect. Wrapping the wearer at the base is a decadent blend of coumarin and creamy woods. I get good deep and lasting base notes of warm vanilla, sandalwood and cedarwood. It is like an amber veil that covers my skin for many hours. It might be me; however, I perceive little vanilla. Yes, there is, but it's not a keynote, as many others have said. I don't find it a vanilla scent. It's not the edible type, at least on my nose and on my skin. This is a very welcoming and comforting spiced vanilla. No sugar sweetness here. I get a lot of spiciness at the beginning, then a dry smokiness in the middle, and finally a woodiness with amber reflections. The creaminess of the sandalwood blends with the dryness of the cedar shavings, and the result is impressive. Babylon is a fragrance that slowly grows on me, and my skin is pleased with this elixir. The formula and scent are simply divine, and I love the warm amber note combined with the woody base. It feels like a long, warm, comforting hug from a loved one. I rarely like gourmand vanilla on my skin. Still, the spice and bittersweet undertone similar to caramel and almond come together in beautiful, sweet harmony. I find it a perfect choice for fall, and as we're heading into winter, I feel this is an excellent addition to the winter rotation. The duration is ideal, while the projection is a bit contained. I base the review on a decant I have owned since November 2021. P.S. After wearing the perfume a few times, I can say that in my opinion, Babylon differs a lot from Horizon Extreme , in which the aromatic tones of rosemary prevail. Instead, I noticed a certain resemblance to Lalique Le Parfum Eau de Parfum , especially in the drydown where they bestow the same spiciness and creaminess. While not clones of each other, the two perfumes share some sensations and vibrations. -Elysium

Penhaligon’s is a brand that’s known for their nice, mass appealing fragrances. Very gentle, always drawing within the lines. I bought myself a couple of samples because, even though I love myself some stank every now and again, I work in an office environment where that’s not always appreciated. Most of my samples I had already smelled in the stores, so I knew more or less what to expect. This one I hadn’t smelled yet. But hey it got pretty high scores so what’s the chance for disappointment right? Well with Babylon we have ourselves an exception to the Penhaligon’s rule. Right off the bat it smells extremely aromatic. The woody smokiness is really something I didn’t expect from this brand. I sprayed it on about one hour before going to dinner and I remember thinking: “oh yeah this is awesome!” But in like 30 minutes or so it turned into a nightmare that gave me flashback of my worst childhood memories. You see, I grew up in the 70’s where literally everyone smoked. My mom was a first class chain smoker. And I don’t know if you’ve ever experienced sitting in a car as a non-smoker, and it’s just blue inside from all the unfiltered, exhaled shag? That nauseating feeling? That’s what I get from Babylon. And the evening had yet to begin… There’s no smoke or tobacco accent to be found, so I wonder what it can be that’s choking me out. I saw reviews complaining about burning rubber tires, I’m not sure if that’s because of the nutmeg, or maybe the vanilla. Boy, even thinking about it gives me a migraine. It lasted about 4 hours on my skin and that wasn’t because the stuff had lost it’s power but because I scrubbed it off.

First impressions: warm, dry, dusty, cosy, festive, spicy, classic, familiar, woody, sweet, fluffy. Babylon is a beautifully balanced autumn and winter fragrance. It has just the right amount of spice, wood, and sweetness and everything feels seamlessly blended. It smells classic and familiar, but not boring. The opening of saffron, nutmeg and coriander gives it a comforting feel, like an old leather jacket or the dusty shelves of a library. Cypriol adds an aromatic lift that keeps it from becoming too heavy or stuffy. The vanilla is soft, creamy, and slightly fluffy, almost like marshmallow. Sandalwood and cedar in the base add a dry, grounded warmth. I’m always happy when I smell an oriental-style scent with wood and spice that avoids the sticky, resinous, ambery notes that can feel cloying on my skin. It’s strong (just one spray lasts all day) and if I overdo it, the sweetness can start to feel a bit nauseating. So I think I’ll especially enjoy this outdoors; catching whiffs of it during long, crisp winter walks, browsing Christmas markets, or listening to carols in a cosy village square. I just got a new decant and in the middle of the current summer heat, it’s making me long for the colder, cosier months even more. Babylon will definitely be one of my holiday go-to scents. For more scent thoughts (and glimpses of my daily life with my dog), find me on Instagram @melanie.buist

Lovely gourmand that reminds me a bit of the now discontinued Traversee du Bosphore from L'Artisan Parfumeur. Not at all like most ambre fragrances, much more like gourmand vanillas. Nothing sour, nothing animalic, and not cloying as some ambers can be - just gentle vanilla and spices with a light woody background.

Is Penhaligon’s Babylon meant to evoke Babylon, the den of iniquity and pinnacle of sin? Or perhaps that groovy Satanic prostitute, arrayed in purple and scarlet, decked with pearls and precious stones, with her golden cup spilling with abominations and filthiness? I’m not sure this softly-spiced, velvet-wooded fragrance is as outrageous or dramatic as all of that. Imagine that golden cup, surely sensationalized to pique public indignation, was instead some sort of humble, unassuming vessel, a bowl of roughly carved but fragrant sandalwood, filled with a milky liquid, redolent of honeyed saffron, the aromatic, earthy warmth of nutmeg and coriander’s peppery-aniseed camphor, and delicately resinous, subtly smoky vanilla. If you’re a fan of Dior’s Hypnotic Poison, but don’t love that obnoxious root beer note, I think you’d find Babylon a more tasteful and understated option. I do enjoy this scent immensely, but I’d still like to smell a more vivid and exuberant perfumed interpretation of this apocalyptic beauty.

I bought a small sample for my husband, but ended up wearing it myself, too. Babylon is an oily, deeply spicy vanilla fragrance that has amazing longevity. The sillage goes through my mask, so it’s also decent. I imagine it’s perfect for warmer weather, when one’s body heat might activate the spices even more.

I discovered this perfume in the spring on boulevard Haussmann in Paris this year. It is one of the penhaligon perfumes that are still marketed. It's an excellent perfume but it looks too much like a babycat, so it's a rather masculine perfume and for winter.

Last Christmas I wanted to try this perfume but I couldnt because I had already put on myshelf so much perfume I don't have more free skin, but from the bottle I could smell a beautiful sweet and confy vanille, so I have been thinking all this this time this one was going to be my signature... Yesterday finally I could try it and it isnt what I was expecting. At all.

Babylon is a gorgeous gourmand, crisp in its opening notes, but also deliciously sweet. It has a notable resemblance to Santal Carmin by Atelier Cologne, because of the prominent notes of sandalwood and saffron. On paper, Babylon remains more fresh and crisp, whereas the fragrance quickly deepens on my skin and becomes more of a spicy gourmand rich with vanilla.

Since I am currently in London, I thought I would revisit some of Penhaligon's newer creations, as the brand had somehow slipped my mind. On the 6th floor at Harrod's, the luxury perfume department of the store, I was told that Babylon is exclusively available there, so after a quick test, I made an impulsive purchase. I regret nothing!

Terrible teddy is the only full bottle I have from penhaligons because when I first smelled it I absolutely loved it! Terrible teddy is a spicy, resinous and smoky perfume that many people do find very pleasant. Longevity is around 8-10 hours on my skin and bottle is outstanding with the beautiful cap! Fairly priced scent but not a great choice if your on a budget.

I am surprised at Penhaligons. I find the portraits collection to be a bit boring and have poor performance for such an expensive brand, but I was able to say that each fragrance is well made. Until I came to Terrible Teddy. This is a dry, harsh, spicy and woody fragrance that you would expect from a cheap department store. The generic harsh opening will eventually ease into a generic soap spice and woody fragrance but again, this is a scent I expect from regular ole' men's body wash at the grocery store. Except for the intensity of the harshness, this is mostly a linear and boring fragrance that lacks personality. This did last on my skin for about 6 hour. It does project in the beginning but that isn't necessarily a good thing in this case. It eventually mellows into close scent bubble. Its $315 for 75ml and its definitely not worth that price. There are smoother and more interesting fragrances that are way more affordable.

Notes of leather and incense promise something wonderful, but I am side-eyeing the ambroxan. I have a tendency to become anosmic to it, so I hope this won't be the case. Definitely leathery - Terrible Teddy is spicy at the opening, but I've just sampled Mr Sam and the two have a completely different note of spicy. Mr Sam is a classic, warm, spicy fragrance of cardamom and cinnamon, wheres as Terrible Teddy is a leather fragrance with the sour and spicy (also almost peppery) note of leather. I am not getting the incense to the degree that I'd like. It only smooths the leather a bit. Have I made a mistake looking up other reviews? Maybe, because I agree with them that Terrible Teddy suddenly became a woody fir fragrance. I now find it woodsy. I wish it had more charm. It is wonderfully made, but I am not blown away.

tested at the Printemps store on Boulevard Haussmann in Paris. I took advantage of this passage to discover many references of this brand as you can see by going to my profile if you need to get an opinion. I had a lot of hope of being conquered by the terrible teddy, nevertheless the verdict concerning this perfume was quick. a big disappointment, it just smells of pepper, which is surprising because this ingredient is not present in its notes. at more than 150€ a perfume that smells of pepper is of no interest to me and given my collection. nevertheless it will suit those who are attracted by this type of scent which gives it an exotic and oriental side as if it reminded the transport of spices with the company of the Indies. it also has a refreshing side, more of a mid-season scent. Hope this review was helpful to you.

This whimsically and charmingly packaged fragrance from the British manufacturer has already been described in great detail by many here. Several use the expression "sweet fir." Yes, I can agree with that, certainly. But as a resident of the Alpine foothills, I would like to make a clarification: ZIRBE!!! Exactly THIS conifer is what I perceive here. It develops a few minutes after spraying. The Zirbe enjoys high esteem in folklore - its scent is said to ensure particularly restful sleep, which has led to the existence of everything from Zirbe essential oil for capillary sticks to pillows made of Zirbe wood to entire bedrooms constructed from Zirbe in the Alpine region. There is also a cult liqueur that is made with - not so easy to obtain - still unripe Zirbe cones. It is not only produced industrially but is also the subject of fiercely contested competitions among amateur producers. And who knows, maybe one could score a few extra points in such a review if one puts on the Terrible Teddy beforehand??

Simple but good! More woody-smoky-resinous than leathery. The scent reminds me of untreated pine wood, slowly unfolding its dry, sweet-resinous aromas in the sun. On me, the fragrance lasts a long time and I just feel good when I wear it. :)

If there are sweet-smelling pines, they might smell like our Teddy here. At times, it reminds me of "electric wood" by room 1015. When I first smelled it on the test strip, I was still skeptical. But now on the skin.... damn!... it's really delicious. I would even wear it at home, just to feel good in the cloud.

Hello hello dear perfume lovers, the title already hints at where this is going. First of all, I must say how incredibly high-quality the bottles of the Portraits Collection by Penhaligon's are. I almost bought the perfume, even if I didn't like the scent at all...

Currently, this is one of my absolute favorite perfumes. A very unusual masculine autumn-winter fragrance. A very powerful, expressive, profound perfume for men. I perceive the scent as smoky, resinous somehow with a certain freshness and sweetness, simultaneously dark and mystical. It smells like a Christmas market in the pine forest, in the late evening.

Beautifully restrained, woody, moist, not at all Christmas-like. I don't smell leather or smoke. I find that very lovely and feminine. It's on my list. I love Diptyque Paolo and this scent is even more delicate, for me it has a mega beautiful cooling effect. I think it's gorgeous.

After a longer break from commenting, here I am again. I simply have to recommend this fragrance. It is so good and very, very affordable for Tom Ford standards. I'm not a big fan of extremely high-priced fragrances like the Tom Ford Private Blends, even though many are of extremely high quality. I usually treat myself to several fragrances for that price, especially with summer scents. 1. Because most fresh fragrances don't necessarily have better longevity in higher price ranges, and 2. because I like to use fresh scents quite generously on warmer days. 6-8 sprays are not uncommon with not too offensive fragrances. For that, the Tom Ford prices would be too high for me. Luckily, there is still the designer line and some Acquas of the summer fragrances. I also jumped at Eau de Soleil-Blanc. The affordable version of Soleil Blanc. I can also highly recommend this one for just over 100 euros for 100ml! A little preface about the original, which I have known for a while: After the first tests, I was totally thrilled, unfortunately not by the price. It has a lot of class and is just so beautifully juicy with this mix of mainly mandarin and orange blossom. I was very impressed, but due to the price, it didn't make it onto my wish list. I was also considering whether to possibly buy the affordable 30ml, which aren't too expensive. Then I found this Acqua, which according to many statements is supposed to smell very, very similar. After a blind buy that wasn't too risky, I can confirm this. A really good deal. 100ml for just over 100 euros. The original costs more than twice as much, even though they are strikingly similar and have hardly any differences in performance. The bottle is beautiful in milk glass and a stunning blue. Perfect for the scent. It smells like vacation and good mood. The name says it all: One of the most summery mandarins I have ever smelled. Simply beautiful and also very well rounded by orange blossom. A seductive composition, as this endlessly juicy mandarin with gentle orange blossom and also slight aquatic notes simply reminds one of vacation feelings in the south. It also slightly reminds me of Aqva Amara by Bvlgari, which, however, has significantly fewer edges and is 100% unisex. Note de Yuzu by Heeley also slightly resembles this scent. I love this mandarin-aquatic theme. Compared to the original, this Acqua is very close to the original but a bit fresher and more sparkling. In terms of price-performance ratio, it completely outshines its predecessor, even though the Eau de Parfum has its justification for existence. According to the label on the bottom of the bottle, this is an EdT, which scores similarly well with many hours and decent sillage. As I said: With fresh, unobtrusive fragrances, I like to spray more. With about 6 sprays, this is a great companion that lasts a minimum of 6-7 hours with good sillage. Top, and this one truly has summer signature potential. Also, in terms of scent type, a true crowd-pleaser that will hardly find any enemies. Nevertheless, it has that certain something that you don't often smell. In conclusion, I can say: Test it or buy it. A real enhancement for summer. A fragrance that I would definitely buy a 200ml version of if it existed. In everyday life, during sports, in leisure time, on a date... this one is always suitable. For me, a clear 10. Italian flair. Arrivederci!

is one of the unmistakable quotes from the unique Zsa Zsa Gabor, in German: 'Es gehört viel Erfahrung dazu, wie eine Anfängerin zu küssen.' One hardly thinks of 'beginners' when it comes to a Tom Ford Private Blend, as most of them - especially those in the non-blue bottles - are confident creations, some of them downright drama queens: complex, high-strung, capricious. They always give their wearer a stage, but in return, they demand attention and sulk when they don’t get it. Tom Ford Private Blends are the complete opposite of beginners. Mandarino di Amalfi Acqua, however - perhaps the Acquas among the Private Blends overall, which come in the frosted bottles - is a light-footed summer freshness with just enough sweetness to remain pleasant. The DNA of its big brother is noticeably present, but it is lighter, cooler, more delicate, far less demanding, holding back - in volume, sillage, and longevity - which gives it a lot of youthful charm and a completely unspoiled innocence and freshness. And yet, the complexity of the house's signature is still felt - one must simply practice for a long time to create a fragrance that appears as innocent as a beginner. Conclusion: it saved me once - this summer at a birthday party. Endless, hours-long traffic jam in scorching sun on the highway, no time to freshen up at the hotel, changing clothes in the parking lot behind the open car door, sponge bath in the restaurant restroom. In the outer pocket of my toiletry bag, I usually have a few perfume samples, and by some miracle, he was among them. Two sprays on the left, two sprays on the right - and the car ride was forgotten, the endless traffic jam was forgotten. The party was one of the best of the year and one that I will remember. And so will I remember Mandarino di Amalfi Aqua.

Hello everyone. Nice to see you! Well… actually I can’t see you, only your profile pictures or photo albums if you show pictures of yourselves there (don’t forget: In summer, short clothing is a MUST!,… um, just a side note…. Um… yes… :D). Today I’m talking about Tom Ford's Mandarino di Amalfi Acqua. A scent that not only sounds citrusy beautiful, but the first version of it, without the addition of “Acqua,” I liked extremely well, as it radiates a truly wonderfully zesty and delicious mandarin, which can be EXTREMELY refreshing right now in the hell… oops, I meant in the heatwave (or upcoming heatwaves), as it not only refreshes but also smells incredibly good. Thus, Mandarino di Amalfi belongs to the summer scents that, in my opinion, can always smell good even on those hellishly hot days, and this without annoying anyone with the scent (well, maybe just the cat, who really doesn’t like zesty scents!). I have always found it very unfortunate that the scent was so weak. Just shortly after spraying, it became almost skin-close, so that you could constantly reapply it if you wanted to enjoy it longer. Such a thing can of course empty the bottle very quickly, resulting in a rather miserable price-performance ratio given the already expensive purchase price. Well, then a few years later this scent appeared, and I thought: “Yeeeey! A new scent, maybe it’s stronger now!”. But then my own consciousness insulted me by saying: “You idiot! What didn’t you understand about the term ‘Acqua’??”, and I finally realized that due to my enthusiasm for Mandarino di Amalfi, I had hardly thought that the Acqua must indeed be a diluted and thus an even weaker scent. And yes… it turned out just as I had assumed. A wonderful scent, where Tom Ford managed to make it smell just as wonderfully (since the olfactory differences between the two scents are actually quite small), but the scent is now even weaker, so that you would literally have to bathe in it for anyone to smell it on you… or even yourself… *sigh* The scent: So,… as mentioned, I find the differences between the two scents quite small (now aside from the intensity of the individual notes). This scent also starts with a very nice mandarin, which comes across as authentic, fresh, and delicious. However, I find that in contrast to the other scent, the mandarins here seem less zesty, which may be due to the even looser sillage. Of course, there are also other fresh notes like grapefruit and especially a nice mint that make the scent more summery and thus fresher. I can hardly perceive the notes from the heart. I don’t smell any black pepper, coriander, jasmine, or anything like that; the scent continues to smell just as it began, quite fresh and mandarin-scented, only now the mandarins smell significantly more intense and less diluted (yet still quite weak!) and that with the neroli, another beautifully orangey note comes in. All of this basically applies to the base as well, as I primarily smell the mentioned citrus scents like mandarin and orange, a bit of bergamot and mint, as well as neroli from beginning to end. In contrast to the regular Mandarino di Amalfi, I find the mandarins here at the end a tad sweeter instead of citrusy-sour (which might come from the jasmine). In the background, there seem to be slight herbal notes, otherwise, the base remains as described, and the scent smells 80-90% like the regular Mandarino, only much weaker and with the few mentioned differences. The sillage and longevity: … so really, the regular Mandarino di Amalfi already had a terribly weak sillage, which I found very unfortunate. Now the whole thing is made even a bit looser and thus weaker. This scent here is really, really weak and thus quite close to the skin, which I again find very unfortunate. The longevity is, however, just as long or short as the regular Mandarino. So about four to five hours, although the scent is so weak upon spraying that it seems much shorter. The bottle: The bottle is, like most Tom Ford bottles, once again a feast for the eyes. It is rectangular and tapers towards the neck, where the cap sits, which looks like a column from the Doric or Tuscan order (I think…). The color of the bottle is now milky blue and also looks nice. The label is light blue to match, which even looks nicer than the golden label of the regular Mandarino (well, it’s a matter of taste). All in all, a high-quality and, above all, beautiful bottle as usual. Yes folks, as I said, the scent is actually not much different from the regular Mandarino di Amalfi. The only real olfactory differences are that the mandarins come across as less zesty and the scent generally comes across as slightly sweeter and warmer. The scent smells, as always, wonderfully, really really wonderfully; anyone who loves citrus scents, especially with mandarin notes, will surely enjoy this just like the regular Mandarino di Amalfi, as long as they don’t take their nose away from the sprayed spot and reapply at regular intervals. Of course, scent perceptions are always different, I’m aware of that, and there are also people who might perceive this scent more intensely, but for me, it is indeed really extremely poor in terms of sillage, so that in my opinion, it is absolutely not worth it, especially at the high price. I would much rather recommend the regular Mandarino di Amalfi, which is also quite a weak scent, which is a crying shame *sigh* Otherwise, these scents are of course pure summer scents, with which you can smell quite good even in the hottest and most exhausting summer, which is always a small art in itself on hot days, as scents and very high temperatures can be quite tricky, especially for the poor others near the scent wearer :D Well, that’s it from me again. Until next time, and have a nice evening everyone :)

As last year with the TF "verts", another stay in NY was used to discover new creations in advance. At Bergdorf-Goodman, with its excellent perfume department, one always finds something at the expense of the credit card... With Mandarino di Amalfi Acqua, TF hasn't reinvented the wheel - just like with Sole di Positano - but has instead complemented its existing summer fragrances with new variations. One could criticize TF for not coming up with anything new and for relying on mainstream, but why shouldn't we allow him to improve and further develop what already exists? All car brands operate this way, selling new niche models or developments within a corporate group based on an existing platform. And so, TF has once again created a perfectly tuned summer variant of the "la Dolce Vita" feeling with Mandarino di Amalfi. Upon spraying, the olfactory receptors immediately switch to high summer mode, as citrus scents, beautifully accompanied by fresh mint and fully ripe fruits, make the heart race and transport you to the middle of an Italian market. It’s brilliant that you are not overwhelmed by a crushing citrus/fruit bomb, but rather that various herbs subtly give the whole a balanced Équilibre. With satisfaction, one notes the light vetiver notes and enjoys the fact that the scent changes to a balsamic base. Personally, the best TF summer fragrance so far, with the realization that what already exists can mature leisurely to inspire anew.

“Summer, palm trees, sunshine what could be more beautiful? With you alone, it can be even more beautiful...” the doctors already sang. And what could be even more beautiful? With you alone in summer by palm trees and sunshine. This very memory is preserved in this scent. Together in Italy on the beach. Il dolce far niente, lounging by the sea. This scent is vacation, and it has found its way to me at just the right time. Andrà tutto bene - Everything will be fine! Just like back then: carefree, joyful in beautiful Italy on the beach. My nose is currently glued to my wrist and my thoughts are in the memory. The scent starts, as expected, fresh and citrusy and then drifts into the fresh aquatic - the sea is, in my perception, clearly and constantly present. There are no surprises, no spectacle, and the scent is neither masculine nor feminine. And I don’t know if my enthusiasm can be shared if you have never been to the sea in Italy. Because simply put, Mandarine di Amalfi Acqua is just a blend of Italian sea air, sunscreen, heat, zest for life, and the certainty - Everything will be fine!
Probably used so often in corresponding shops, the scent immediately reminds me of various concept stores with luxury fashion, Prada, Givenchy, everything you could possibly look for in that area.

There are some iconic images of George Clooney, but one keeps appearing over and over again. It shows him on (his) boat on Lake Como, standing, one arm casually resting on the boat's windshield, the other hand coolly on the steering wheel of the boat. If a picture expresses both casualness and elegance, then it is probably this one.

"Mandarino Di Amalfi", it is exactly what you get, a mandarin juice mixed with herbs and soap, the overall result is really good, but it really needs to be tested beforehand, as it is not suitable for everyone, precisely because of this soapy scent. The longevity is okay.. on me, the fragrance lasts about 4-5 hours, and it is not overpowering.

Alongside the Costa Azzurra Acqua, I recently got my first whiff of the Mandarino di Amalfi. I had wanted to test the Mandarino di Amalfi for some time and see for myself its quality. This is because I wasn't keen on the Neroli Portofino based on its reviews and comments.

I was full of anticipation to test the Mandarino Di Amalfi Acqua. Unfortunately, I was completely disappointed, and it has been a long time since that happened. The scent is by no means bad, no question. However, it doesn’t smell particularly special or high-quality at all. For me, we have a shower gel scent with mandarins and generally light citrus notes.

Santal Blush is a woody and floral at the same time. Opens with a lot of cinnamon and other spices, then joins the ylang and a huge note of jasmine. This opening phase remembers a lot of Versace Crystal Noir. The sandal itself is creamy and, as said here, has a coconut smell, which turns it into a fruity smell in the middle notes. This phase remembers me of Black Orchid after some hours. I wish there were more sandal in it. I mean, i did want it to be woodier than it is. Definetely a great scent, but not in my top. I'd stay with Chanel Bois des Iles instead. I can say this is an unisex fragrance, but tends to be more feminine. Sillage, lasting power and projectium are medium in my skin(around 8 hours).

I didn't expect to like this given the cumin, fenugreek and carrot seed notes. Sounded like a recipe for a great curry, but not a perfume. Cinnamon is also a note I tend not to like in a fragrance. When I put it on, I was pleasantly surprised that it was much more woody and less curry-like than I had feared. I did not pick up any cinnamon at all, and the cumin, fenugreek and carrot seed really seemed to augment and enhance the woods nicely and not just make the perfume smell like stew. There was also a very nice rosey undertone to the scent. About 15 minutes into the development of the scent, though, two things happened that turned my enthusiastic like of this perfume into a disappointed dislike. First, I picked up something similar to the incense note that made Lotita Lempicka not work on my skin. Second, I got a distinct plasticy, artificial smell that sadly made me think of bad mass market perfumes. This sharp plastic note did subside a bit as time went on, but then strangely reappeared, then disappeared again, then reappeared and so on.
