While the beautiful wood forms the gentle base of the fragrance, the musk emits a nice, sweet scent that even comes across slightly clean in the background. In the later base, it remains as described, soft and beautiful, with no trace of licorice and the bitter almonds gradually fading away. The woodiness then becomes a bit more pronounced and intense, also reminiscent of cedar wood. All in all, an extremely beautiful scent. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is strong, so the scent can be smelled well and for a longer time. One leaves a decent scent cloud for a while. The longevity is also quite long, lasting over ten hours. The bottle: The bottle is cylindrical and features grooves. In the middle, there is a section where these grooves are interrupted and the glass is clear again. Here, you can see beautiful bird patterns that have been embedded into the glass. The bottle is rounded at the top, and a black cord or “scarf” with golden ends hangs from the neck, on which the fragrance name is written. There is also a nice, golden pump ball that can be unscrewed. If you don’t do this, you can place a round cap on the spray head. All in all, a very beautiful and very feminine-looking bottle. Okayy, so… wow. Yes, really, wow! The scent, which initially starts off a bit intense and, as mentioned, might not appeal to everyone (among other things due to the strong licorice scent in the top note), soon develops after spraying into a very lovely, truly feminine, very sexy, delicious scent. I know that I have to be extremely careful with “delicious” scents not to repeat myself for the thousandth time and write something about being delicious, kissable, and biteable or whatever about how you ladies could appear with this fragrance, but somehow all these descriptions are still much better than if I were to write things like “hot” or even “bangable,” right? He he he :DD And no, I’m not saying that, so stop clenching your delicate hands into hard fists :D But seriously, the scent is really very nice. It smells truly sexy, but without coming across as girly, in case you were worried about that. It is one of those perfect companions for the evening and going out (in autumn and winter). Therefore, I give it an absolute test recommendation! So test it when you have the chance, because everything here is just right, from the scent to the bottle! And with that, I’ll also come to an end, my dear fans (who surely would still prefer to pound me with their fists, right?? Yes, yes… I know it exactly!!). Well then, have a nice evening and see you next time! :)

Luna Rossa Black is a well composed likable fragrance, and I have no doubt it will have a solid success on the market during next three to five years. In my opinion, it is nothing revolutionary – it takes the idea behind legendary Bvlgari Black and reshapes it for a contemporary audience with some Ambroxan undertones. It opens with just a touch of bergamot and immediately goes to Bvlgari-like eraser rubber. Personally, I am a big fan of these rubber accords that reminds me of school. I can sense also some lavender touch as a hommage to Gaultier’s Le Male. Beneath this main rubber accord are hidden some vanilla undertones with benzoin and Tonka as a more pronounced notes. Possibly, these two notes are responsible for this amber-like olfactory mirage plus some shady and contemporary Ambroxan touch. Rating: 7/10 More on Scentimentalwords

I can't believe it i used to hate this fragrance! When i first tried it made me physically recoil. I even gagged... A year later im in love. Vanilla is not my favourite note but here it's done in very unique way in my opinion. Musky, little bit aromatic, powdery and ambery vanilla done beautifully, very well blended. A very sexy take on vanilla without making it gourmand or overly sweet. The performance isn't the best but for scents like this i don't think it really matters. Lasts long enough and projects enough for my need but don't excpect more than 6 hours after that i can still detect it as a soft skin scent but obviously it wont project well after the first few hours. Sad to see it getting harder and harder to find, i hate being late to the party but it is wath it is. Seen a lot of people call it a date scent but i think this could easily be daily, very versatile in my opinion. This fragrance is another reason why Prada is the best designer house in my opinion. Sensational scent, must try while you can.

I think this is the best Prada. Kind of a dark and alluring scent Some ppl say baby powder, but im kinda getting a little bit of pencil shavings from it too Not bad but prada in general is kinda basic and isn’t very special. But its a very safe neutral brand. It isn’t overly costly or offensive. Great safe colognes to get someone who isnt very familiar with fragrances, or as a simple date night or work scent Unfortunately all of prada’s best stuff for men is either discontinued or incredibly hard to find

So, this scent is on my radar since about one year but I just did not had the chance to try it properly. And only with the help of two samples received from various orders, I had my chance to test it and understand what is the hype for ? Well .. I do not want to be the party breaker but this scent and I will not be friends. Initially I thought that I might have the Covid, because the scent was barely noticeable after 4-5 sprays on the strip and I was recording to make a First Impressions video but it was not possible to get anything than some ambery sweetness, something Grand Soir would smell like after 4,5 hours and you reapply some bergamot and patcholi scent on top. The first recording was deleted because I did not have good things to say about it and I do not want to post negative videos, if I do not like a scent, I will not upload a review for it. But I considered that I can give it a second change and used the second sample. My thoughts about it, you can see them below, thank you.

This one shocked me a little, I think I was expecting a warm slightly spicy cold weather fragrance. Slightly sweet and powdery during dry down. Patchouli, amber, classy, and fresh. Solid projection and the longevity lasted easily 10 hours when sprayed on clothing (6-8 sprays)

I had the privilege of immersing myself in the enchanting olfactory world of Prada Luna Rossa Black, and I was captivated by its enveloping complexity and magnetic essence. This fragrance is an ode to sophistication, a symphony of notes that dance together in harmony, creating an unparalleled sensory experience.

This is a carbon copy of White musk for men by body shop. It's pleasant. But basically sweet Tonka and musk with a peppery edge. A little too raw and rudimentary for me. Something a bit skanky puts me off. I think its the angelica and bare tonka. Would have been better with some florals to soften it and smooth it off a little

I received this bottle as a gift one or two years ago, and it has been a staple in my fall and winter rotation ever since. It's hard to describe what this actually smells like. It has some sweetness with a powdery texture, but it's also a bit dark.

A badass scent from the Luna Rossa line! It's warm, sweet and has a hint of herbs, all thanks to the main ingredient, coumarin. This scent is perfect for when the days are getting shorter or just at night. It's a great transitional scent that's not too overpowering, even with a generous spray.

This was my first "proper" designer fragrance that I bought at the beginning of my journey, I wanted something that resonated with me and smelled nice to others as I wanted to wear this to both school and dates with my girlfriend, and she absolutely LOVES this stuff on me Prada LR black was an instant love.

such a beautiful first impression...and then...it stays that way...nothing more comes. Really a lovely scent. Pleasant without the slightest disturbing factor, not sweet, not piercing, also lasting, everything quite "perfect". Except for the small detail that it doesn't say the slightest thing to me. No magic, no development, no mystery, no shock, no extra, no...nothing! Just nothing but "beautiful". Even with the movement of my arm, after two hours, I am still surrounded by exactly the same "beautiful". And even then the same "beautiful" when my nose hopefully asks, "are you still there? What are you doing?" then the scent says: "Yes, I’m still here. And doing the same as before..., as before..., as before..., as..." Tell me, what’s the point of that? Ah, I got it....You are not alive! You remind me of the beautiful, big, great talking doll with real hair that I had as a child and that sat on the wardrobe, nice to look at. I only liked her because she was beautiful, but she always said the same thing in a strange voice. Is that necessary? For what? Well, maybe it’s a scent for the open-plan office? Sort of disturbance-free for everyone and yet present.

I was eagerly anticipating the moment when the postman finally delivered the promised package. The bottle was already beautiful in pictures, and unfortunately, there wasn't much to find about the scent online. "I wonder what that's about?" - I asked myself. Today I know why, the fragrance is unremarkable. Do you know that feeling when you encounter a beautiful person? And in your mind, they are a perfect person, radiant appearance, great voice, … a dream bubble. And then this person talks for no more than 5 minutes.. and the dream is over? The bubble has burst. That's how you should imagine my feeling with this scent. Unfortunately, I don't smell any of the notes mentioned above - it's a jumble of woody notes - it could be Ambroxan that remains. The longevity is mediocre at about 4-5 hours - with the last hour being very close to the skin. The sillage is hardly present at all - the scent does not radiate. What a shame, more appearance than reality.

A whopper of a gardenia entrance with a touch of indolic honey. Big resin wafts playing around the sweetie garden. Reminding me of the largesse of Jungle Gardenia Touvach a little. It might be one for a future side by sider trial one day. Gardenia is not an easy flower to render as a perfume and normally I'm not particularly keen on Mr Fords creations. However here, I make an exception because without a real gardenia here to compare it with, This is pretty spot on to a memory of one. It has a slightly skanky side which is not easy to pull off well. One can even get a genuine feel for the pollen in the centre. As it progresses, the gardenia is morphing gently into an indolic and rather plastic nuanced jasmine. Possibly the labdanum pulling. The sweetness is never overwhelming but the perfume is certainly no shy angel. If you are a fan of floral whoppers like Joy, then wear this and light up a nice fag... this will be right up your smelly street. I'm pleasantly surprised by Mr Ford here. This type of perfume really isn't in the slightest way my cup of tea either.... but gardenias are extremely hard to do... and this certainly is a truly skanky one. I am quite shocked to find that I really quite like it.

Opens with a bitter gardenia accord dominated by green and mushroom-like nuances. The creamy/fruity sweetness I like so much in Chanel's Gardenia and Une Voix Noire seems not to be present in this fragrance. Only when the top notes are gone I start to see it, rising gradually from the background of the composition. Velvet Gardenia is a more realistic gardenia rendition than the Chanel Exclusif, but more realistic does not necessarily mean better. I understand if some people find this fragrance challenging to like or wear. However, I appreciate the artistry and elegance of the composition and give it 7 out of 10 possible points.

I'm sorry, but I can't write a politically correct comment about this "fragrance" without stepping on toes or offending someone in the slightest. I haven't written a bad review in a long time, but this stench doesn't deserve anything else. Diarrhea! In German, Durchfall, the runs, or simply loose stools! I expected a gardenia scent, as I like gardenia fragrances. Velvet Gardenia? Velvety Gardenia? Don't make me laugh! Was it standing next to a cesspool? Or was it adorning the windows of the wooden toilet (with hearts on the door and real windows, so you don't get bored while doing your business) that surely still stands somewhere in Hintertupfingen. Wiped with the newspaper! Instead of velvety gardenias, I smelled as if I had an accident in my pants or somewhere else and was trying to cover it up with some perfume. Forget the pyramid above. Maybe that's somehow in there. I would gladly give away the sample of this monstrosity. The stuff lasted like a charm and bravely survived several scrubbing attempts. In the end, I was so desperate that I was about to scorch the remnants off with a Bunsen burner, but self-immolation is better left to others. Please, the sample can leave quickly, very quickly!

'...linger on! You are so beautiful! Then you may bind me in chains, then I will gladly perish!' The gardenia - native to the old-world tropics, intoxicatingly fragrant and waxy white, similar to jasmine but botanically unrelated, the eternal boutonniere flower of the dandy and the bon vivant - Tom Ford pays tribute to it with this fragrance. This tribute is an exceedingly weighty, serious, and yes - somewhat challenging scent - one that may require a certain life and fragrance experience to truly appreciate. Velvet Gardenia - Tom's velvety gardenia - is a heavy, perhaps almost otherworldly fragrance. Those who love jasmine and lily will find here a related and intoxicatingly dark luminous scent accord - and all the grace and beauty of transience, in which one can lose oneself if one wishes. Lily of the valley and jasmine - both not lightweights - accompany the namesake gardenia and bloom with it in silent, porcelain-like, and springless splendor. And what in this white, unblemished heart is initially a vague suggestion, still fleeting like a shadow - materializes and condenses in its worn, endless base. There is something melancholic and sluggish, something of wax and honey and bitter resins, that pushes up from a dark bottomlessness beneath the blooming white like a black, slowly rising tide lifting water lilies without destroying them. This is a fragrance for Orpheus, who is allowed to lead his beloved back to the light from the realm of Hades but ultimately fails to do so. A fragrance for Hero and Leander, who drowns in the darkness of the sea as the light that ignited their path goes out. A scent like a night of love with someone you know will be killed by the first ray of sunlight. A fragrance like memory, like reading old letters - one that tells of transience and something precious lost long ago. A scent like a Thestral, the lean, black winged horse in the world of the wizarding student Harry Potter - which can only be seen by those who have witnessed death. Conclusion: in a time when Tom Ford's discontinued Private Blends must be guarded like Fabergé eggs, this dark fragrance - equally clad in black velvet as it is crowned with lily of the valley - is a precious jewel.

High Mass Sacre Cœur. That's what I always think of when my brother wears this fragrance. And because he likes it so much, he wears it a bit too proudly for my taste at almost every family gathering. Easter, Christmas, birthdays. This scent not only makes me sleepy, it almost puts me to sleep. Most of the time, I can't manage to follow the conversations when I sit next to him at the table - I go straight to bed afterward. Too much Pope, too Catholic, no oriental fire, no spice. And above all, so terribly proper. I can't help but tighten the bedspread and fold my arms neatly over it. Drill in the girls' boarding school, thanks to the nuns. Oh, there's something else, somewhere beneath, behind the incense, a hint of bloom. It could be the gardenia named in the title and perhaps a touch of lily of the valley. I can't say for sure. I'm lying in an incense coma and am very grateful when my husband wakes me with the kiss of true toothpaste the next morning. My brother is usually already on his way again, and at the breakfast table, there's still a delicate scent of beeswax lingering. Well, that could also be the wood polish.

So far, the Private Blend fragrances have been quite a disappointment. Tuscan Leather reminds me of a slightly sweeter, warmer Maserati from La Martina. The idea of not inspiring leather in a gloomy way is similar there. However, I actually prefer leather to be hard and edgy. If it's leather, then Duro :). Oud Wood was dusty... old spices, nothing special.

When I bought Amber Absolut, I also had a few samples filled, including this fragrance. Unfortunately, I have to say that this one doesn't really appeal to me, probably because I've noticed more and more that I don't like floral perfumes.

For now, just a short comment from me - a quick first impression. I sprayed the scent on my arm about half an hour ago (thanks for the sample, Bekos!). I have no idea if the summer temperatures today are suitable for this. But whatever. The opening is very, very floral, just the way I don't like it at all. But what is this now?

Velvet Gardenia starts off intensely - floral - flowery, but also fruity - sweet. The fragrance comes from the travel package of our perfumer "KingLui," and I would like to express my sincere thanks for the initiative. At first, one can perceive a very intense - floral note, which I really find extraordinarily pleasing and is thanks to the lily of the valley.

Such a nice scent to throw on for absolutely any event and any season. This will be one that I will be replacing once it is empty. Its a very very nice scent, but I wouldn't describe it as formal or a very adult-ish. It has a hint of scent that smells like I would have loved to use it every single day in high school. I still really love it though. It is a very recognizable smell and would probably fall into a summer-y category for me. Kinda smells like the Victoria secret store.

Prada L’homme Intense starts off with that familiar iris note, with its powdery aroma, and a warm amber plus smoothly rich leather. It’s very nice and has a noticeable darker profile than does the original L’Homme. This scent is clean, warm, and sweet with the inclusion of a roasted tonka bean note for good measure. I like how dry the composition is and how the amber sort of soaks the iris. Further along in the wear, we get to hit a base of sandalwood and patchouli. I really appreciate how subtle these later notes are and how they simply enhance the overall vibe of an already fantastic smelling cologne. It’s really at this time, that I am reminded of Dior Homme and Dior Homme Eau, as L’Homme Intense fits right in line with that series. However, this is stronger on the iris and doesn’t have the leather to the same extent, nor any cacao. The overlap isn’t too extreme. What it ultimately dries down to is an incredibly rich blend of mainly the iris and tonka bean. It’s so classy and smooth, with the leather and amber, being the next most powerful notes. Though, I’d put the amber at number three. From here, it is pretty linear, and doesn’t develop much beyond this. The powdery iris and the mix of woods, sweet notes, and leather are truly fantastic together. Not a super complicated fragrance in its development, but is definitely enjoyable throughout.

My first Prada perfume was Amber pour Homme. I still remember when that light purplish water came to store, its powdery-sweet-soapy-fresh accord drew me instantly. There were no iris in there, yet the dustiness, creaminess, and butter-ness were so dominant, the kind of redolence that floods the room where you stayed, with no comparable siblings at that time. In hindsight, I realized I was going through Nirvanolides molecule, with its intense musky, fruity, powdery, soapy odor with lactonic nuances. So, today I have another record from the Prada range of men’s fragrances, and one of the flankers to the original Prada L’Homme: Prada L’Homme Intense. A more deep version of the original fragrance, this is an alluring woody scent for men, floriental I would say. It's creamier, for one, and much more pungent and heady while the first was light and almost ethereal. It has the equivalent DNA of the original, yet three assertive notes stand out, viz leather, patchouli, and roasted tonka. Even though the last years saw new original releases from the major designers (Dior Sauvage, Saint Laurent Y, Prada L’Homme), they have been tormented with practically no creativity. We’ve been seeing the same focus-group approved crowd-pleasers that smell mostly the same, with main notes that turn around synthetic ambroxan and iso-e super. Of course, I love both, yet the different designer scents, in the end, result in a sort of deja-vu. L'Homme Intense begins with that familiar buttery iris note, with its powdery aroma, and a glowing amber accord plus smoothly rich leather, which makes it fascinating. More, there is a touch of patchouli and the blend smells unusual in a good way. It’s very nice and has a striking darker profile than does the original L’Homme. The initial notes of L’Homme Intense smell surprising good. The quality iris is unmistakable in the opening. The middle notes of leather and patchouli give it a distinctly masculine smell. It’s so classy and smooth, with the leather and amber, being the next most powerful notes. Though, I’d put the amber at number three. From here, it is pretty linear and doesn’t develop much beyond this. Further along in the wear, I get to hit a base of sandalwood and tonka bean that finish it out with a hint the orient. Sweet tonka takes over. The accord is pleasant but I didn’t expect it to dominate the composition so quickly. I really appreciate how subtle these later notes are and how they simply enhance the overall vibe of an already fantastic smelling cologne. Unexpectedly, I detected a faint scent of creamy iris. It's subtle and unobtrusive. Anyhow, I smell a stronger presence of vanilla, likely the listed amber accord. This scent is clean, warm, and sweet with the inclusion of a roasted tonka bean note for good measure. I like how dry the composition is and how the amber sort of soaks the iris. Projection wise, I find the sillage to be on the upper end of moderate. It’s not a heavy scent, but it projects well, just not crazy so. The performance is very good, regardless, and you or other people will notice this juice on you. The longevity for me hits around several hours, which is great for just about any purpose. Seasonally, L’Homme Intense strikes me as a cold-weather scent, with the ability to be worn in more mild warmth. I do feel it is a bit more limited than the original L’Homme, in this regard, but if you want to wear it at its absolute best, it should be colder. I think it is an amazing fragrance. It’s got enough closeness to the original to be familiar, while also adding new elements, to stand on its own. -Elysium

Hits every spot great sweet enough for the winter and fresh enough for the summer and all year around just smelling good and having a hint of sexiness essential cologne Even though the performance is mid Good for school good for office good For formal occasions 5-7 sprays Sad, this is discontinued. Pick up as soon as possible!

when i really got into scents almost 2 years ago, my 1st (fragrancex) purchase of 3 bottles covered 3 criteria. my order included an all-rounder/easy grab (dylan blue), warm/daytime scent (artisan pure), & prada l'homme intense (pli), which was chosen for cool weather/evening wear. the initial pli spray was more than satisfactory & just what was required on that rainy evening. i imagined the light evening fog as my (slightly) sweet, iris-scented bubble. the powdery facet was like being in a warm, fuzzy cloud. this stuff is awesome. the dense, but very clean scent reminds me of opinions i read suggesting that pli's classy, laid back vibe was well-suited for a groom. i agree, but this works casually also. ------------------------------------------------------------ i will give a light breakdown, as i'm not yet "nose-worthy" enough to be more detailed. scent: 8.5 sweet, clean, fresh, powdery, dense, gentlemanly/classy, evening-suited iris projection: i dunno longevity: approx 3 hours total scent bubble, then skin scent for remaining 5 hrs versatility: 6/10 exclude warmer weather & sporting/outdoor activities age group: 35+ wearing: from casual button-up or sweater with dark denim/slacks (no baseball cap or athletic sneakers) up to tuxedo sprayer: 10 a spray is 1 ft long, 7 in wide, 0 drip bottle: 6/10 nice style, but 4pts off for opacity overall: 8/10 *pli was recently axed...glad i grabbed 1

This iris fragrance is a bit creamy from the sandalwood and sweet from the amber. Ultimately the result smells a bit like marshmallows, but in a totally refined and sophisticated way The performance on this is nuclear, if you do two sprays it'll be too much unless you wait a bit before being around other people.

L'Homme Intense is the only fragrance from Prada I've properly worn so far. The fragrance notes are simply iris, patchouli, tonka bean, amber, and sandalwood. What I get is a blast of powdery iris in the beginning that does not go away. As it moves along, L'Homme Intense becomes a tonka bean takeover.

My friends, what an elegant perfume! I have a decant of Prada L'homme and at the first opportunity I bought the bottle of Intense. From the first spray I really liked the scent. It starts with this "bomb" of a very nice and elaborate iris, giving the fragrance an air of lightness and freshness.

Prada L'homme intense is an absolutely irresistible iris fragrance, exuding an air of refined elegance and sophistication. Its smooth and alluring essence, complemented by a subtle hint of sweetness, makes it the perfect choice for both romantic dates and exciting nights out. Moreover, it effortlessly transitions into a remarkable signature scent for everyday wear.

This Fragrance is a masterpiece. The best of Prada and one of the best winter fragrances in the market. Very well blended notes make the fragrance classy and elegant. The iris is the main note and it is used in a balanced way . The performance is good as well , longevity 8-10 hours with 3-4 hours projection.

I will probably try this one several more times just to be sure, but so far, I'm only impressed by its mediocrity. WTF, Tom Ford? For the price, you could have come up with something that didn't dissolve the eyeballs and strip the paint off the walls for hours after application! I think that the idea behind Musk Pure was to come up with something that was a bridge between SL Clair de Musc and SMN Muschio d'Oro. But instead, we have paint thinner, chalk and ... Farts. All whipped up in a frenzied bilious swill of rage and bitterness masquerading as "skinlike softness" behind a mask of what was meant to be "powdery" but is really closer to mustard gas. I wish I were kidding but I'm not. Thankfully discontinued, this olfactory insult with a scathing price tag will make its wearer the butt of every joke in the perfume industry. I can't tell you how much I enjoyed scrubbing this one off... it took no less than a 45 minute shower, 3 soapings and 2 generous applications of body oil to get rid of this stinker.

In search of the perfect musk fragrance part 16 Well, folks, this is not going to lead to the perfect musk scent! This fragrance would have belonged on the winner's podium in my personal ranking, but it missed out on a medal because it has been DISCONTINUED and is now only available at astronomical prices. So, it takes fourth place now. Serves it right. A very dear perfumer gifted me a sample of Musk Pure when we met in person. I took my time testing it, but now I'll keep it brief: I like this scent exceptionally well! Musk Pure contains exactly what it promises, namely a decent musk fragrance, where I can clearly smell the musk. It is sweet, warm, soft, creamy, flattering, and blends beautifully with the skin. Musk Pure is not a clean white musk, but certainly not one of those "darkest corner behind the train station toilet" types either. It sits somewhere in the middle between light and dark. I perceive it as somewhat viscous, golden, rich, and a little bit sultry, and that's meant in an absolutely positive way. I was pleased not to detect the listed flowers. The sillage is pleasant, does not bother others, but is still noticeable, and the longevity is okay at five to six hours. I would primarily wear it in autumn and winter or on cool spring days. If only I HAD it! Because now I will have to make do with the remainder of my sample, which is unfortunately dwindling. A small consolation is that my beloved does not appreciate this fragrance treasure as much (Philistine!). And he should enjoy sniffing it on me… Thank you, dear Aura, for this beautiful fragrance experience that I was able to have with this precious drop. You really know what discerning queens desire. That was a very nice GESTURE… ;) (Insider!)

Musk - essence and archetype of the beastly-animalistic, originally derived from the gland of a small, rather inconspicuous deer - often has a polarizing effect in perfume and is usually either revered or hated. Tom Ford once dedicated an entire series to it within his Private Blends - in white or clear bottles, with one of the four - White Suede, precisely the only one that still exists today (albeit in a brown bottle) - containing no musk. All four are labeled as women's fragrances, yet all - some more than others, perhaps - can also be worn by (some, certainly not all) men. And each one of them - if one can still get hold of them - is worth an intense engagement with it. Musk Pure, which - as its name suggests - is presumably the closest to musk among the four 'white' Private Blends, is also likely the most physical, sensually carnal, or - to put it vulgarly - the hottest among them. The musk here is sultry, almost heatedly arranged and embedded in nothing but trembling promise, in resinous-warm confectionery - just like an unsuspecting insect is lured into the depths of a plant in search of nectar, from which it cannot escape. A bright waxy accord gives the only casually perceptible flowers a certain formality, stripping them of innocence and any floral quality, and orchestrates them with the sugary sweetness and the almost disturbing corporeality of the musk into an invitation, primal like the scream of a cat on a sleepless hot summer night. And at the same time, it is intimate and tender, only hinting at what others have already revealed entirely - like a warm thigh accidentally pressing against the flank, and moist breath promising sensuality and desire. Conclusion: 'And she bangs, she bangs!' sang Ricky Martin fifteen years ago about a woman who - teetering on the edge of cheapness, but miraculously just not crossing that line - drives men out of their minds. This is a scent quite capable of bringing innocence to its knees - or, to stay true to Ricky Martin's uniquely profound poetry: 'cause she walks like she talks, and she talks like she walks!'

Dear First has now brought me to my first blind test in the form of a traveling letter. I just received the reveal and I had to grin. Is Musk Pure actually the scent she has chosen for me! With my vague guess, I must have been wrong :-D But read for yourself! One spray and it feels like sunshine is shining on my face. Everything is bathed in white-yellow light. Sparkling warmth. Crackling aldehydes dance with lemons. This is made for radiant women. I see them before me - with a citrus smile and softly powdered cheeks. For a brief moment, I think of citrus cleaner. But who can blame the radiant woman for having a subtle cleaning note at this moment? Soon I am sure that I am dealing with the sunny side of a Chanel No. 5... Only this No. 5 has been given a lemon face! A gentle soapy undertone makes itself known and allows the radiant woman to blink elegantly in the sun. A refreshing citrus blink! The lemon is reluctant to leave its sunny post at the radiant woman, who is now slowly pulling the crown of aldehydes from her hair and hanging it over her shoulder like a handbag. But still: it remains yellow and somewhat juicy! Sweet flowers linger on the journey at the hem of the radiant woman and quietly cover the lemon with powder... So it takes a seat for a while. The flowers need time, as they are being observed by citrus fruits and accompanied by the aldehydic veil. The observers and companions allow no sugary blooms, as they want to refresh elegantly! Done! Before the sun leaves only warm shadows behind, the radiant woman sits on a wooden bench, relaxes her head back, and enjoys. The evening breeze brings a subtle green-woody musk breeze with it and gets lost in her smile.

I had this one under my nose before and forgot to comment on this scent. I’ll make up for that now, right? I can’t help it, but this musk scent somehow feels unfinished and especially very 70’s. My mother had a friend who used Musk by Alisha Ashley, and this scent reminds me exactly of that. Musk pure remains the same from beginning to end. Nothing changes except for the intensity. It is subtly sweet and has a restrained bulky soap note. I would only wear this scent to a 70s themed party, and that in combination with a glam rock outfit. So, scruffy-crazy flared pants, a wild top, and platform shoes. So, now I’m putting on T-Rex!

I can still vividly remember the musk perfumes of the 70s (which were often adopted by ladies like my mother in the 80s) and 80s. The eye-catching advertising for The Body Shop's musk fragrance "White Musk," a fragrance oil for a sensual appearance, resembled more the display of a rutting stag for me.

When I first applied this scent to my arm, I immediately thought of a hairspray or hair styling product scent. This is probably due to the benzoin and orris root notes. After a while, the musk and tonka bean join in, but very subtly; they create the delicate warm and slightly velvety aroma. But fundamentally, I perceive the fragrance as pure and clear.

Intensive clear white cosmetic musk note in the style of The Body Shop. Light spicy aldehydic iris note and white lilies, intense sweetness with coumarin and vanilla. Possibly a hint of amber and cedarwood.

My first encounter with this fragrance took place in Monte Carlo. I was on vacation there and felt like wandering through the shops one afternoon. That’s when I saw a range of white Tom Ford fragrances. Tom Ford had never been particularly appealing to me.

What an extraordinary aquatic molecular fragrance. Modern, delicate, yet opulent and playful. The combination of water jasmine, melon, and iris was already a poetic and bold mix in my imagination. The cashmere wood, pink pepper, and vetiver give it a green, slightly tart, and woody undertone. It feels as if heaven, sea, and forest converge in this creation or as if one were lost in the deepest blue eyes of this world. This scent is probably more of a spring or summer fragrance, but for me, it's wearable all year round. It is truly a noble, fresh, floral aquate and lasts well. For me, it's unisex, although it is marketed as a women's fragrance. And with this perfume, the bottle is noteworthy for me (which I usually never mention). It is an elegant companion for this scent - blue, white, rose, and gold, satin glass with a rectangular relief, wooden cap, good spray head - it appeals to me very much. So, put on Billie Eilish's Ocean Eyes, test it, and dream yourself to tropical places…

Despite my inexperience with Lalique fragrances, I am writing a comment on this one. Here we go. At first, you smell melon, which is sour fruity like rhubarb, but without rhubarb. Then a bit of jasmine, a bit of musk. You’re lying on a mat and snacking on fruits. Or are you rather walking through an orchard? Or is it a summer afternoon and you’re being served fruit salad for dessert? In any case, it is clear that it’s not just about melon here. What you get is much more a combination of several juicy little fruits, all dripping with juice. It doesn’t come across as powdery to me. The initial sprightliness of the fruity components gradually transforms into a soft, musky women’s scent.

Seems like toned downed mix of black orchid parfum&edp. Less intense, less performant but also more versatile : might appeal to the ones wishing of making of black orchid a daily fragrance/signature (the other flankers might not be suitable for every occasions being too strong). I wonder if « reserve » word here stands for « a more reserved » fragrance for that matter, would totally make sense. Earthiness through patchouli and boozines are plumped up compared to « parfum », truffle is still there. Less earthy than edp, and more feminine. While the previous flankers keep their BO dna during the dry down, here the base notes are more pushed forward to a more basic vanilla - tonka. It’s like a better alternative to the edt : i know many people out there were hoping to meet a more versatile black orchid, that still keeps the edp/parfum dna. To be honest, i will still get it while having others ; sometimes BO might feel a little too heavy or inappropriate for some occasions but I would still be craving for that smell. That’s when Reserve plays its role to perfection My ratings of the flankers : 1) - Black orchid « parfum » : 9.5/10 perfectly executed, lacking perhaps a little bit of profoundness. Nuclear performance. 2) - Black orchid « reserve » : 9.25/10 signature worthy, a lighter fragrance, reuniting best aspects of all black orchid flankers. 3)- Black orchid edp : 8.5 harsh opening, too heavy, dry down is where it happens. Good performance, but doesn’t overperform « parfum ». While you could substitute edp version by the « parfum », getting yourself a better one. You can’t substitute « reserve » with the « parfum », because they both play different roles while delivering best aspects of what black orchid has to offer

Gorgeous floral orchid opening shifts into musky/floral heart then a delicious chocolate a la Black Phantom - Memento Mori . Definitely feels higher quality than previous Black Orchid iterations, though I can’t do a detailed comparison unfortunately since I’ve only smelled them on strip and it was a long time ago. Might be a bit too floral for me, but there are definitely lots of guys out there that would love to rock this.

The black OG has always been my winter favorite. The golden one I also have, but it's too floral, too light for me. I was initially hesitant about the Reserve, as many find it earthy and the price is really quite steep. However, since I love Tom Ford, I bought the 50ml blindly. And it was worth it; my old love has blossomed again. I don't find it earthy at all; it's a bit darker than the OG and has a slight note of dried fruits for me. It's a shame I didn't buy the 100ml.

I originally smelled this on paper in store and really liked it. Floral, candy like, and somewhat youthful, but not overly sweet. More like a suble sour candy you can suck on for hours. My girlfriend wears this all this time and its absolutly intoxicating and one of my favoriate fragrances of all time. I don't understand the low ratings besides maybe leaning generic, but I can recoginze it every time.

[...] A sweet, obnoxious mess. So, she's gone, I don't have her anymore and all I have to offer is this photo [not added here]. I think it's the first time I'm just posting a photo without a review. And I don't like it. I only remember that I laughed out loudly when I smelled it the first time, because of the backstory of the name, Paradoxe, whereas the fragrance has nothing to do with opposites at all. No duality, nothing contrasting, nothing special. It was so sweet and monotonous I washed it off after a couple of hours, because it was so bad. I honestly remember the jokes I was cracking about it better than I remember how it smelled, because it's so unmemorable.

I enjoyed the bourbon vanilla base, but everything else about this perfume was so typical, yet screechy. You'd find more unique, pleasing scents at Bath & Body Works. It smells like the perfume area at a department store. I'm going to finish the little sample size I have of this, but it's not worth a purchase imo. There are notes in this I love in many of my favorite perfumes, like pear, jasmine sambac, nectarine, tangerine, white musk, and benzoin, but the white florals are overwhelming combined with the extremely synthetic rendition of pear. It's extremely strong in my opinion, but I do have a sensitive nose and get headaches from fragrance more quickly than average (daily wear is 1-2 sprays max for moderate sillage perfumes).

Disappointing useless basic synthetic and other bad adjectives to describe this perfume with a weak combinaison of florals I feel like I already smell this years ago on women who dont smell good at all when they pass through you and I still smell this kind of fragrance everyday my god that’s what happen with some of these designers fragrance ( not all of them hopefully) and considering the price we can say that the devil won’t perfume himself with Prada It’s so boring that I forgot the smell (and I’m glad about it) Not even for a teenager

Paradoxe is quite the misnomer - where one might expect a surprise, it simply replays an all-too-familiar tune. A bouquet of white flowers, sunlit citrus, soft vanilla, and sugar. The problem isn’t that it smells bad, but rather that it’s just another variation on the same theme, with an extra dose of sugar for good measure. A safe fragrance, free of missteps, but also free of real personality.

The poster child of post-COVID capitalism in the fragrance market: genetically engineered to be incessant (lasts for hours and hours, even when it transfers to others when you hug them) but docile enough to ensure wide appeal. You can't say it's bad since it's been focus-grouped to death and iterated until clinical perfection.
So sad to smell this new perfume by Prada and finding nothing memorable in it. Just another unremarkable and unoriginal safe clean pear floral vanillla combo.

The opening of Paradoxe is a little too “perfume” for my liking (though it is fruity and fresh, not offensive) but man oh man after an hour this is a delicious scent to live in. Completely paradoxical to the citrusy opening. A warm vanilla that reminds me of the glaze on Krispy Kreme. Or translucent white rock candy. Yet mixed with a gentle fabric softener.

Not terrible, but you can definitely find similar at a less wallet-emptying price point. It's a nice blend of the sweet, floral scents (that have a slight aquatic undertone) and the citrus, sharp scents. As time goes on, it gets a bit more musky. That's not my particular vibe so it's not my favorite scent to reach for.

Hmmm… I get nervous sometimes that the creative noses of the perfume world have developed a fear of producing something new and stunning and go for the recipe that everybody uses. Too many of the new fragrances smell of the same. And no! It is not me getting old and grumpy, thinking yesterday’s perfumes were so much better.

This may be one of THEE WIERDEST fragrances in my entire 150+ bottle collection. Now, I like Odd/Unique fragrances and DO NOT care if a fragrance smells "Synthetic"" as long as I like the way it smells, but Lalique's Infinate Shine? Its just a bit too"Chemical" and artificial smelling and Im now seeing here on Parfumo how many artificial/chemical type notes are actually in it, so it sorta makes sense, Now what I will say that the "Chemical smell" does calm down a bit after about 10 minutes or so, yet itl'l still remain throughout the life of the wear just not as prominently. I also think its EXTREMELY musky (NOT a negative) with a slight "non-descript" fruityness (Probably the Rasberry) a bit Floral, a very slight Coconut/Sunscreen like smell in the far background, ZERO spiciness and then your left with a soft Sandlewood in the drydown. It is also veeeery Linear, has very little sweetness and wears quite close to the skin once it dries down with little projection. One way Id describe Infinate Shine is as if Lalique made a fragrance composed of ONLY supporting notes, but leaving out the one or teo "Main notes" that would've given this dna some direction or identity bc for now Id just describe it as a "Synthetic Woody musk fragrance." Now, although theres hardly any oil sheen (Like at all), oddly enough it does seem to lasts quite a while on skin (7 to 8 hours) and I can smell it for days on clothes when taking a close whiff. I think its meant to be one of those "Your skin but better" type of fragrance, but I must say that Infinate shine was a VERY RARE dissapointment from the house of Lalique imo. Also, when I'd initially sprayed it, it didn't even have a smell to it along with practically ZERO oil sheen? I was totally convinced Id recieved a total fake. But after a few weeks went by an actual scent began to emerge and so the "Maturation process" really opened the scent up taking atleast a month for it to fully become what its meant to be. I have a bunch of mens and womens offerings from Lalique, but Infinate Shine is my least favorite sadly. Cant believe this fragrance goes for over $200 Retail!! I mean my head would've EXPLODED if I'd blind bought it for that amount! Bad enough I spent over $70 for it. Oh and I do consider this "Unisex" leaning slightly Feminine, but guys can most def wear it no problemo as it really does become like a personal musky fragrance which does improve further into the drydown.. Unfortunately I can NOT Recommended Infinate Shine. Cant believe Im actually saying this about a Lalique! Lol. Oh well, cant like EVERYTHING right?

Sampling Tom Ford Amber Intrigue, a 2024 Private Blend line release that is exclusive to Harrods in the UK, which fittingly has a resinous component but should not be confused with Amber Absolute, for example, as respects the amber dominance, depth, and uniqueness. Amber Intrigue has some spices and dried fruits that, for me, conjure an outdoor market, while also having a medium-bodied resinous center that’s a little smoky, a little creamy, and just the tiniest bit animalic in the background. The official note listing includes dates, olibanum, labdanum, sandalwood, and vetiver, which roughly tracks with my experience of the fragrance. In fairness, there’s not really anything else (that I know of) in the Private Blend collection that smells like this, and it’s different enough from the sweeter, darker, denser Amber Absolute that it merits a separate fragrance, but I simply don’t see it as interesting as AA or even Myrrhe Mystere, the more recent resin-focused release from 2023. The price on the Harrods website is $400 for 50ml, more or less typical of the higher end of pricing in the US for the Private Blend line. Setting aside tariffs, it’s fairly pricey at retail. Overall, I’m happy to try this out but am not especially moved by it. It’s good but not great, which is generally fine, except for products in higher-priced lines. 7 out of 10

I imagine a room with a beam of dusty light coming in from the window and illuminating a table on which there is a large sandalwood bowl. The inside of the bowl has been sprinkled with a layer of silver incense and gold benzoin grains, and on top have been placed large fresh rape palm fruits, juicy and pulpy dates of the Deglet Noor variety. The air in the room, warmed by the sun, is filled with sweet, boozy, resinous, smoky nuances. Fingers of light embrace and caress everything. That is how I imagine this perfume. Amber Intrigue is a dynamic scent that starts with fruity and spicy nuances, touches a warm woody heart and culminates with a powdery amber trail. It can be unpleasant if you overdo it with the spray or smell it up close too soon, as happened to me. Otherwise, it opens with a deep note of dark dates, complemented by spicy and smoky accords. For a short while, the mix of the alcohol and spices gives a boozy accord akin to the Kraken Black Spiced rum. You might be surprised, as I was, by how realistic the date scent is. I expected a hint of citrus as an introduction, but it starts right away with saccharine and dense notes of date pulp, dark, sticky and opulent. The taste of a Deglet Noor date is similar to brown butter and has a very nutty finish. Maybe it is overly sweet, syrupy, cloying, or a date jam, but I am not sure if it is my cup of tea. But I let this sugary jubilation settle down and slowly something magical happens. First, I smell something reminiscent of Big Babol gum, thick, gooey. Then, a smoky and resinous accord accompanied by a warm spicy accord bursts in and invades the sweetness with an army of cinnamon bark and golden grains of olibanum. The date does not give up, but takes a back seat, leaving only its fruity side to be perceived. The more the perfume grows, the more I feel that I like it. It’s like a video game where you have to pass the first stealthy level, after which it becomes intriguing at each subsequent level, revealing secrets, hidden doors and pitfalls. So, a first level that offers a sweet and spicy opening. It takes a good hour for the heart to open up and let the woody tones of vetiver and sandalwood emerge. Now on the skin, there is a creamy mix, at times earthy but mostly powdery thanks to the addition of violet leaves. Overall, it remains smooth, the date is still distinguishable, and the powderiness is not comparable to talcum powder. And the incense, which is now alight and burning, spreading its smoky notes over all the other notes of the choir. Thus, the middle stage is all about woody and warm whispers. The fragrance fades and ends with a rich amber accord. It is not the salty ambroxan that has been overused in recent years and we found in "Erba Pura | XerJoff" for instance, but a vivid brown amber accord courtesy of vanilla to create dustiness, tree resins such as frankincense, myrrh and benzoin to add smokiness and musk to balance with softness. Those notes add a kind of intimacy and sensuality to perfumes and pair well with spicy and woody notes that give dark but soft powdery facets to the composition. When smelled close to the skin, it releases balsamic and smoky nuances. Overall, it is much more than a classic amber fragrance, which stands out for its weighty character on glues such as dates and resins. Despite the explosive opening, the perfume then takes a calmer turn, with exceptional longevity I would say, remaining on the skin and clothes for many hours. It is still an intimate perfume, which does not fill the spaces while making itself noticed. I like to wear and smell it during the day, on relaxing weekend days, but its placement is that of elegant evening events in the colder months thanks to the warm, resinous and spicy accords. I like to say that I have a few fragrances featuring dates, but none of them are as heavy as this accord, and perhaps that is what makes it unique for me. This feeling comes from a bottle I've owned since January 2025. -Elysium

Now the Christmas season is coming to an end. Or rather, in my case, it has long since ended, because as much as I enjoy playing Feliz Navidad in November and setting up my annual Annick Goutal Une Forêt d'Or candle - I really don’t want to see any of it after December 27th. There have even been years when I tossed all the stuff out on the 26th. The Swedes traditionally dispose of their Christmas tree on Knut (that's twenty days after Christmas, and the throwing-out-the-window part is just a legend). I could never wait that long, but on the other hand, it should be worth it with everything. To be 'worth it' in the sense of 'getting something substantial for your money' applies to Amber Intrigue as well, which Tom Ford just managed to launch in time for the Christmas shopping season (although I haven't seen it widely in local stores yet). The approach of thinking that an expensive fragrance must have impact and performance is, as is well known, foreign to me. I believe that a high-priced fragrance can and should be quiet and subtle, if it is a beautiful 'subtle and quiet.' However, here there is nothing subtle and quiet, and those who love Christmas and its scents and Tom Ford's 'a lot of everything' will likely be thrilled here. I am indeed a fan of seasonal fragrances, and I own explicit summer and winter perfumes. However, to focus so pointedly on a limited season seems a bit 'de trop.' Amber Intrigue plays so much with the scent notes of Christmas - roaring fireplace, buttery pastries, and other sweets much more than oriental and desert accords, as date and amber suggest - which is a shame because Tom Ford can do desert - that the thought of wearing it outside of the Christmas season feels difficult. And it smells like Christmas anyway - do we really need a similarly scented perfume for that? Conclusion: here you really get something for your money, if that’s what you want. No less than rich Christmas opulence in a pretty bottle. And nothing more.

Prada has become well-known for its charming "Infusion" series. Amber pour Homme was released about two years before Infusion d'Homme, and it must be seen as its direct predecessor. The personal touch of the perfumer Daniela Andrier is evident in both fragrances. For me, Amber pour Homme is all about violet, and violet pastilles - although these are not listed as a note. I don't know if this impression is caused by Nirvanolide – but it is remarkable and special. This dark floral appeal is also a little candy-like and sweet, but not overly sweet. It is distinct enough to place Amber pour Homme next to sweetish colognes like Le Mâle, Fleur du Mâle or One Million. However, Amber pour Homme's violet presents itself a lot more distinguished than those fuel-like musks. If only more people would use Amber pour Homme we should have similar arguments going on as we have about Le Mâle. But it is simply not widespread enough to evoke those love or hate controversies. Although Amber pour Homme is highly recognisable it can still go through as an individual perfume, and maybe a good choice for those who are looking for a Le Mâle alternative. It is still available in some shops but there is no advertising any more. No matter if you choose the omnipresent Gaultier cologne or Prada's Amber pour Homme: Be aware of what you are doing! I saw a statement on the German Parfumo from one guy who complained about his colleagues. They had asked him to immediately stop wearing this at work. Obviously not the best office scent. Amber pour Homme starts a bit undecided during the first seconds on skin but then the violet pastille note evolves quickly. Behind that, there is a nice cleanliness that points directly at the later Infusion d'Homme. Unfortunately that cleanliness soon gives way to a dark and dusty amber accord. I have to admit I find the amber base the least remarkable part of the fragrance. While the violet accord is so individual, the amber base is the kind of indefinite greyish amber note that one finds in so many mainstream perfumes. It is just background without lots of own character – just the opposite to the very distinct top and heart. And so, the name Amber pour Homme was not a lucky choice IMHO. It does in no way reflect the main character of this fragrance. In case of Amber pour Homme, I really don't know how to refer to the fragrance note pyramid; I smell nothing of that. Please do not confuse Amber pour Homme with the later Amber pour Homme Intense. That is a totally different fragrance and as boring as the name implies. They dropped the violet pastille note and replaced it with nothing special. The original Amber pour Homme is much more intense than the flanker. I regard Amber pour Homme as a stage of development towards the successful Infusion d'Homme. The cleanliness of the later fragrance is already visible in parts of it. The idea of an attractive and somewhat special sweetish-clean-powdery appeal is already present. In fact, the violet pastille note and the powdery iris touch of the Infusion are somewhat close to each other. The indefinite dark amber base is later dropped for more elegance and a lighter style. And any links to the Le Mâle world still visible in Amber pour Homme were cut off. Due to its distinctness Amber pour Homme is a bit difficult to wear. It is out of question that the successful Infusion d'Homme is the better perfume. Nevertheless I still like Prada's first attempt in the world of gents' colognes. Daniela Andrier created a unique style for Prada – something not many designer perfumes show. It is a pity that this style has been dropped with the release of absolutely 100 percent mainstreamed colognes such as Amber pour Homme Intense and the Luna Rossas.

A soapy sophisticated saffron sandalwood Masterpiece! I love the purple juice in it's classy chic clear glass and silver top bottle! I enjoy Amber's luxurious unisex floral opening almost as much as the slightly more masculine sweet musky patchouli dry down! This may never be rated a top sexy date scent but I feel right at home in the church pew or even at a job interview with no fear of wrinkled noses just smiles of appreciation! 10/10 all the way around! :)

This is the first male fragrance that I've tried that I can actually classify as luxurious. Prada Man is sophisticated rather than overly masculine or sexy. I'm not saying that it isn't pleasant, because it most definitely is, however its cleanliness and subtlety is what I find differs from other scents. There aren't any particular notes that stand out in this composition. They all tend to blend together nicely, creating an almost soapy and creamy-like quality. There is a subtle hint of sweetness, particularly in the drydown, that is more natural than sugared. I'm certain that this fragrance's simplicity would garner many compliments from men and women alike. When I first sprayed this on a card, I had to spray a few times in order to smell it. Fearing that it would be like Prada L'eau Ambree, which I could not smell for hours, I over-applied. Prada Man does take a while to settle, so it's best to wait it out before coming to a conclusion. Prada Man lasts quite well and the sillage is moderate to average. I do believe that this fragrance is geared towards men who want to be conveyed as being conservative and classy.

AMBER POUR HOMME is another excellent soapy unisex perfume from Prada in the spirit of INFUSION D'HOMME. The two share the very same soap note, which also happens to dominate both compositions, so if you like one, you'll like the other, and if not, you won't! I happen to love this soap note, but if it clashes with your particular skin or nose, you'll be in big trouble, since it is the focal point. The other components are a bit different from L'INFUSION (which is a composition around iris). Here the labdanum + vanilla = amber (this is not ambergris, nor did anyone claim as much, as far as I know..) combine with saffron and leather in a pleasing blend. I love this particular soap note, I love labdanum amber, and I love saffron and leather, so this one is naturally a winner in my book.

Now, there's nothing wrong with soap. It washes away dirt, it keeps you clean. It's great. So Prada here under the direction of Daniela Andrier on the theme of Amber, an imaginary accord composed of Vanilla, Benzoin and Labdanum. I get all of these in different variations. I also get neroli and orange blossom (used quite a lot in soap) as well as geranium, an ingredient used in men's soaps of the past. This is also combined with myrrh and patchouli, sandalwood, coumarin, and hints of cardamom. Overall, it's a great achievement. Even though I identify it as "soapy", it is is an incredibly high and good quality. It's worth the money. Because it's a long lasting fragrance that develops from a clean burst of elegant, expensive soap, into a wonderful second skin scent. I cannot recommend it enough just for this fact alone. Great longevity and above all, elegant. For the price it can't be beaten for freshness, cleanliness and elegance. It may be soap in a bottle, but it's probably the best soap you've ever had.

This smells great to me, smells like an expensive soap. The performance is extraordinary, I were this fragrance to impress ( very formal wear, suit & Tie type of fragrance) .Perfect for all year, and for people over 25+ in my opinion. Yes is nice. I could see on a woman this would be incredibly stylish, and very chic. But really the price is too much to pay for something that just smells "nice", and is a little safe (and which only lasts a few hours). That is, unless you are rich, and one of Tom Ford's exclusive clients. Jasmine Musk has been discontinued... don't bother looking for it. Buy Samsara instead.

A fragrance family that I sometimes find a bit foreign is that of tropical or South Sea scents. On one hand, most of these fragrances are quite similar (and often rather simply made), and on the other hand, they often rely on Tiare (or 'Tiaré'), a strongly scented flower from the gardenia family, which is processed with coconut oil into Monoï, the famous beauty product from Tahiti. Monoï has an olfactory recognition value that is extremely high - something you either like or don’t. The species used as Monoï-gardenia are 'Gardenia tahitensis' and 'Gardenia jasminoides', loosely translatable as 'Jasmine-Gardenia', where the notes of gardenia and jasmine are fundamentally not dissimilar. A few years ago in winter, I was in Hawaii, the only kingdom that has ever existed on the territory of the USA - and in its capital Honolulu on the island of O'ahu lies the Iolani Palace, the only 'American' royal palace. For nearly a hundred years, a queen and seven kings ruled the Kingdom of Hawaii - five of these kings were named Kamehameha. The most famous among them was Kamehameha I., after whom a club in the Hawaii-based series Magnum is named. Like Tahiti, Hawaii belongs to Polynesia (which is noticeable despite its undeniable affiliation with the USA), and you also encounter Tiare and its intoxicatingly sweet scent everywhere there. Tom Ford's Jasmine Musk is the scent of Polynesia and the scent of Hawaii. It is dazzling like sunlight right at the start, and then there are flowers - white jasmine flowers, enchanting and almost intoxicating - that speak of South Sea beaches and the gentle rustle of palm trees. Nothing here is shy, nothing fragile. A hint of musk joins in - like fresh body moisture on the skin, hastily evaporating in the sun - accompanied by a soft scent of warmth and sunscreen, which briefly flashes and then sinks back into the white flower rain. And behold: the Tiare is opulent and beautiful here. Jasmine Musk is lush blooming everywhere and shimmering, silvery sea. It is opulent laissez-faire at the Royal Hawaiian in Waikiki, a cool cocktail in the shade of white umbrellas, comfortably languid in its bright pink splendor. And then up the Likelike Highway to Kailua and further towards North Shore to the famous surfer beaches, and to Hale'iwa and Waimea. It becomes lighter now, playful, almost fleeting, and salty-balsamic like driftwood on the beach. And still, the sea of white flowers remains, intoxicatingly heavy and wonderful. Conclusion: fragrant Tiare without its notorious fangs. Nevertheless: one should probably like its scent a bit to love Jasmine Musk. Brightly shining South Sea dreams, overwhelmingly arranged. Kamehameha - a king.

Now once Silver starts going into the mid it really does become much softer, leather and Vetiver dominant and closer to the skin creating more of a strong personal "Scent bubble" vs projecting strongly. I spritzed some on the back of my hand just before writing this review and as Im now sniffing it the gorgeous, sweet Lemon/Cardamom with faint touches of smokey Vetiver is just really intoxicating to me. Soon it'll transition into a more masculine "Leather dominant" fragrance while still retaining some of the opening notes and man! Does Lalique's Les Compositiones Silver smell FANTASTICO! Although I find Lalique Silver to smell very unique, it does smell quite a bit like a much stronger Salvador Dali-Le Roy Soliel Extreme and upon comparing the notes they both share the notes of Lemon, Cardamom and Haitian Vetiver. Luna Rossa Ocean Eau de Toilette doesn't strike me as a primarily aquatic scent. Its opening is pretty synthetic, but that doesn't last long, as it immediately turns into a spicy and fresh mix of bergamot and pink pepper. Minutes after, the fragrance brings some herbaceous notes into play, like the sage and mugwort, and you also get a nice lavender and iris undertone. But as for the saffron or suede leather, my nose can't pick either. As it settles down, the musk, vetiver and patchouli, a classic combination of notes, take over to make for a dry, fresh and musky finisher. It's pleasant, overall; inoffensive, spicy, citrusy, fresh, but also pretty boring. I've smelt much more interesting and pleasing fresh fragrances. Longevity is pretty decent, actually, especially for an eau de toilette concentration. At least on my skin, I got about 6-7 hours of longevity. But by the 3 hour mark, the fragrance had already turned into a skin scent, so I'd go for about 6-8 sprays on a wearing, especially since projection (for me) is very poor here. I constantly asked friends around if they could smell my fragrance, but the only way they could feel it is by shoving their nose onto my neck. Only the first half an hour to maybe an hour you get some better projection; around a feet or so. But in the end, fresh fragrances, especially eau de toilette concentrations, aren't known for beastly projection or extreme longevity. For occasions, I'd say Luna Rossa Ocean would be great for everyday wear during the summer and/or spring. You can wear it leisurely, at school, at work, or at sports/gym. Given its poor projection and simple, fresh, clean scent, it won't offend anyone. But if you are looking to get people's attention, then this is definitely not the fragrance you're looking for. However, I do believe that there are better fresh fragrances out there that can be had for the money. Better fragrances that stick out more and nail the aquatic, oceany type of feel better. If you enjoy Luna Rossa Ocean's DNA, but wish for better projection, then maybe the Luna Rossa Ocean Eau de Parfum might treat you better. But I can't say much regarding that, as I haven't tested the eau de parfum variant. Regardless, this is a decent fragrance for casual, summer wear, but it's forgettable, and it's just not good enough to justify itself over the many other options out there. Overall Rating: 6.1/10

Soleil Neige is a fragrance of radiant beauty. From the very first moments, it unveils a sense of purity and softness, with an airy burst of bergamot, orange blossom, and vanilla. It’s both powdery and creamy, pure and sensual, leaving a gentle and light impression. I’m pleasantly surprised by the result, creating a sensation of freshness and comfort without ever becoming too sweet. This fragrance perfectly embodies the balance between softness and lightness, a true olfactory caress.

So, what should I say. When you are as "crazy" or rather "obsessed" as I am, you sometimes think: "Oh, I'll make a blind purchase." After all, I could always sell the fragrance again if I don't like it. The mind tricks you with all sorts of reasons and makes you believe that this was a good decision and a worthwhile purchase. Perhaps this also explains the many 9 ratings here. :) - ultimately, as always - "Greed devours reason." If I were to give this fragrance a 9, I would have to have quite a few 10s in my collection. But in my subjective perception, that is definitely not the case here. Tom Ford in the old way stays true to itself here: What is successful gets reissued and sold at an extremely high price. But well, this time it’s successful, I would say. The Soleil Neige in the perfume version starts with one of the most beautiful openings I have ever experienced - a wonderfully balanced mix of mandarin (a fresh and juicy mandarin), orange, and bergamot. Unfortunately, this dreamy opening fades after a few minutes, and the floral notes come into play. From this point on, the fragrance strongly resembles "Masculine Pluriel" or at least has some parallels to "Lavender Extrême." That’s also well done! As I evaluate for myself - I personally place great importance on a harmonious balance of the components, and here everything feels rounded and balanced. No note overshadows the other. (Just for the record, in case someone is reading along!) In the drydown, unfortunately, some of the magic is lost, but it remains appealing. However, in my opinion, the fragrance does not justify the high price - I would rather reach for MFK. Nevertheless, it is worth a test. The sillage is okay, rather close to the skin up to about a meter. So, not a beast. The vanilla and amber are subtle but noticeable in the drydown and round off the fragrance pleasantly. My conclusion: An expensive, typically Tom Ford inflated fragrance. The opening is great, no question about it, and overall the fragrance is successful. Still, it lacks that certain something to be truly spectacular. Thanks for reading :) Peace and out.

A majority of women may disagree with me on this point, but I find Prada Candy boring. Despite the fact that I dislike loud and sugary gourmands, I'm kind of wishing that Prada Candy was one of those fragrances, because this subtle whisper of caramel and musk leaves me feeling uninspired and disappointed. Prior to smelling this perfume, my fellow fragrant friends kept encouraging me to smell Prada Candy, and in turn give them my honest opinion. Well, here goes: while I certainly don't find it repulsive, it is generic and plain. Prada, while attempting to appeal to the younger market with its sweet accords, has made this fragrance subtle as a means of remaining classic and stylish. The two don't go hand in hand. I refrain from labelling Prada Candy as a gourmand, because while it's sweet and gooey, it doesn't smell like something I would want to eat. The caramel note actually has a slightly burnt edge, which many have noted as being off-putting. A hint of spiciness tries to steer Prada Candy towards 'oriental land', but fails. Candy-land is where this fragrance is from beginning to end. I unfortunately find this fragrance headache inducing if I smell it for too long. I am only grateful that this fragrance doesn't have a cotton candy smell. I agree with Eilismaireg (on Fragrantica), Prada Candy is indeed one of those fragrances that have been "done to death". Nothing original and exciting to be found here I'm afraid. Despite being amongst the targeted age range for this fragrance, I'll be happily passing up Prada Candy in hopes that there are people that appreciate it far more than I do.

If you're looking for a candy fragrance, don't bother with this one, you will be sorely disappointed. Why Prada named it Candy, I'll never know, my guess is someone in their marketing department needs to grow up past highschool. Which is not to say that I don't like it: I happen to love this perfume! Past the initial opening, it's actually not sweet at all, it's more of a salty/powdery/musky/woodsy slightly caramelized concoction. But not like candy at all. And it dries down to a barely there veil of scent, occasionally warming and wafting up throughout the day when you get active, this is not a sillage monster that leaves a trail so thick you can see it, either. But it gives the skin a very sensual aura, with a delicate powdery edge and a trace of yumminess. And in that, Prada did a fantastic job. They just need to fire the juvenile cretin who named the fragrance, lol.

Musk, Caramel & Benzoin at a ridiculous price. Absolutely no benzoin or musk came out, but some sweetness did for a brief moment before it dissipated into thin air. Prada Candy seemed more like a body spray than a perfume for me. Packaging is cute and appealing for a certain demographic, and many enjoy this fragrance. It just doesn't work with my chemistry for it's longevity or mix. I feel there are many other gourmands on the market that are far better mixes to choose from whether on the low-end or high-end that will give you more bang for your buck. I am a fan of (gasp) Pink Sugar, (yes, I admit it), I adore vanilla and something that is sweet but I also need others in the mix to tone it down or make it interesting for me. I really don't mind if the packaging is or isn't to my liking. I don't invite strangers to my boudoir, after all. The bottle is cute for those that like it. So are the advertisements behind it. But try as I may, warmer weather and cooler, I just could not get much more than sweet candy out of this frag. Oh well. A good mixer, then.

Caveat: While I love drag queens, I tend not to like dessert-like gourmands. Just not my thing. Prada’s Candy is in many respects a super-gourmand. It’s cotton-candyish, it’s caramellic, it’s vanillic, and it gains sweetness as it goes. Much seems to have come out of Prada’s PR about the benzoin and therefore the oriental genre. Yes, there’s benzoin, but the name of the perfume tells you about the perfume’s true affiliation: the dessert/gourmand category. I see people referring to Candy as complex, the complexity implying a big, successful outcome. I find Candy more of a kitchen sink gourmand. It’s a busting-at-the-seems stuffed perfume. It hits the prominent notes of the big players in the gourmand game from the past few years. But if you’re trying to capture Candy by describing its scent, you run the risk of giving a description that might apply to any other dessert perfume. Here’s how I see it: If you liken a sweet gourmand perfume to a straight, femme women, then Candy is the glam drag queen. The femme gives a certain portrayal of gender. The drag queen and Candy both take that same femininity as a starting place, then turn up the volume until the distortion sets in.

Candy by Prada reminds me very much of Inside by Trussardi. Inside is a gourmand favourite of mine, but to my nose Trussardi is the more grown up version and Prada's Candy is the sweetheart with a wild-side to her. Candy in crème brûlée that is begging you to eat it....with your fingers. Why not? Finger-food is yum once in a while. Silage is: "I am dessert in a 5* restaurant" -- Longevity is a bit short: 3+ hours. Sniff before buy! A fun scent for those who love it enough to spend this much for something that is not everyones cup of tea....erm...Candy. But perfume should be fun too! Right?
