bought in 2009 shortly after its release at the end of 2008 (at the same time as the one milion). for me it is the best neroli that I have smelled out of about thirty brands. fresh and ideal after the shower in the middle of a hot summer afternoon. it smells clean, it is a powdery perfume with a minimum of character so as not to confuse it with a feminine perfume.

It’s one of those days again when I indulge in myself, that’s what I call it when I take care of things I’ve had for a long time but have slipped my mind. Today I thought I’d take a look at my perfume collection from the "back section." And my gaze fell on Nilang without a cap, which I had received from a dear friend because she no longer wanted it. I had in my mind that it somehow smells "old-fashioned," a young fragrance enthusiast I know would probably call it "grandma-like." So I thought I’d just put it in the souk and wait, maybe someone would want it. And reflexively, of course, I sprayed the scent on my skin... and a whisper went through my senses. More like a small explosion... Whoever casually describes it as fruity/floral usually deals with shower gels - and YES, it is floral and YES, a bit fruity. But rather paradisiacal. That’s how I imagine a park in India, by the Taj Mahal, an intoxicatingly beautiful scent... I only smell a fruit very faintly, maybe a bit of bergamot, freesia a little more, but the jasmine... and in my mind, images of fantasy flowers from the Garden of Eden arise, combined with a slowly emerging powdery sweetness (blessed be "Your Graces Amber and Sandalwood"), which one can endure (you should know, I mostly have unisex or men's fragrances). Dr. Google now abruptly leads me back to reality: of course, the fragrance has been reformulated, the bottle completely changed...

I find the Tom Ford body sprays to be fantastic, as they represent a great affordable alternative to the EdPs. I have already purchased the Noir Extreme Body Spray twice, and I like to use it when I want to freshen up in between. In my opinion, longevity is not the priority for such body sprays; rather, it's simply an uncomplicated alternative that fits well in any bag and is easy to take along. In terms of price, these sprays are definitely an alternative if you don't feel like spending around €100 for the EdP. This designer line is still acceptable, although the Private Blends are also available as body sprays. After the Noir Extreme body spray, I also wanted to test the Ombré Leather (2018) Eau de Parfum spray, as I really like the EdP and it leans slightly towards the Bad Boy vibe with this leather. Nevertheless, this scent DNA is extremely suitable for everyday wear and doesn't clash as much as some other leather fragrances. Definitely a scent that you can wear well when it's mild and not too warm/hot. In terms of price, this product is significantly cheaper at €50/150ml. Online, you can find this spray in many shops for around €30. Fair. This spray comes in a deodorant-like packaging. Not very pretty, but quite practical to transport since it can't really break and fits in any bag. The scent of this spray is, of course, identical to the EdP as usual. Due to the concentration, this version is a bit toned down, but it clearly smells like the original. In the air, this body spray performs really well. This black leather note is beautifully dark, mysterious, and has its own edges and facets. This leather is, of course, always in the foreground, just like in the EdP. This leather is accompanied by a slightly smoky spice with the finest saffron and cardamom. Patchouli adds some darker vibes to this leather. Jasmine makes this scent soft together with a warm and sensual amber note. There’s also a bit of soft wood. Overall, it’s very rounded, and this body spray is a bit more linear than the EdP. You don't get much development here, but that doesn't bother me. You can spray it on your body and on clothing, which is really noticeable. A great choice for when a long-lasting perfume isn't necessary. Performance isn't bad, but of course, this scent doesn't last nearly as long as the EdP. On clothing, the longevity is really okay, and it performs for a few hours on the skin. Overall, a great alternative to the EdP. Everything comes as expected, and you get a wonderful option for this fantastic leather scent. After Noir Extreme and Black Orchid, this is the third body spray I can recommend in this variant.

Prada La femme is a perfume that brings together several things: it's clean, slightly soapy, tropical, put together, sensual. It is a very versatile perfume and I would recommend it for most occasions. I also find it suited to a wedding and I have reviewed it in my youtube video on wedding appropriate fragrances, that I am linking here below.

Prada La Femme is one of those tricky scents to describe. It's a rather complex mish-mash of notes where no note tends to dominate. I enjoy smelling Prada La Femme however I am hesitant to buy it. On my skin it's a warm, slightly sweet tuberose fragrance which dries down to an even smoother, creamier and somewhat clean floral. Due to its crazy, busy composition my nose tires quickly and I find that I am having to reach for the coffee beans more often than I'd like. I am unsure as to where this fragrance fits in the current market. Its sweet vanilla-honey scent would appeal to the younger market, however the bottle design and advertising points it in the direction of more mature, classy, brand conscious women. Despite the fact that I quite like this honeyed, creamy and tropical interpretation of tuberose, I have grave fears for its future. It's definitely unique, I'll give it that, but in saying so it's also a confusing, hard to wear fragrance. At this point in time I would highly recommend testing on your skin first, as Prada La Femme is not something that anyone should be blind purchasing. Prada La Femme is definitely not a white floral. I would categorise it as an oriental floral although it's not particularly ambery nor spicy. In lots of ways it's nearly as controversial as the 2004 Prada Amber.

I got a decant of this to test it out before committing to a full bottle and I'm really glad I did. This is a *very* soapy, waxy, spicy fragrance with a slightly sweet edge. The florals in this really all blend together extremely smoothly to become a very smooth, generic soapy scent instead of having really identifiable facets from each floral note. The iris definitely sticks out a little bit, but the yellow and white florals really all meld together to make a pretty bland floral soapiness, which makes up the majority of the scent profile. It's rooted in a sweet base from the beeswax and vanilla while adding a warm spicy kick from the spicy notes in here. The vetiver in this is really smooth and mostly just offers a slightly woody facet instead of the characteristic "scratchy" edge it often adds. The bergamot is only there for the first 20-30 minutes to add a bright citrus facet to the top I see this as being a really great office-safe choice, but I also can't really find anything interesting about it. It's clean, fresh, and inoffensive, but it loses so much character in the process. The notes are almost so well blended that it's hard to pick them apart without a lot of concentration. It's perfect to smell freshly clean, but it lacks the "wow factor" I tend to look for in fragrances. It's not a bad fragrance, it's just a very elegantly-mixed soapy scent which isn't for me. If you tend to like soapy fragrances, this is probably a pretty safe blind buy you'll enjoy, but it's not going to be the right DNA for my fellow gourmand girlies or vanillic sweet floral fans. Great for daytime wear, but doesn't have the impact to be a good daytime or night out scent. Pretty fair value for the money; you can find bottles of this at discounters for less than $100 very easily.

When elegance And femininity come together, the result ís this perfume that ís also balanced and executed. Here we havelt’s a white floral sweetend by a very fine honey. Where the projection is not a beast but you do feel it in every movement You make. I love it for spring days. Where it shines whit exquisite magic.

One of my all time favourite fragrances, actually in my top five, is from Prada: Infusion d’Iris. One of the best Iris interpretations ever made, in my opinion. Everything about this perfume is a success: the bottle, the wrapping, the scent. Just beautiful. Therefore I always tend to expect something extraordinary from Prada. Right now I have four bottles: L’Eau Ambrée, Amber Pour Homme, Infusion d’Iris and La Femme. The latter I just bought the other day. My partner used to wear L’Homme Intense, which is drop dead gorgeous. So I was really excited to receive La Femme. The bottle somehow tells that we are in the same league as with L’Homme Intense. I am not so sure after testing. To my nose there is an almost watery/floral vibe with this. Maybe a lightness - watery may be the wrong way to explain. The frangipani and the beeswax combined make a different sweetness - lighter and more versatile. I was expecting something loud but instead I got this very delicate expression. It lasts two to three hours which, for me, is a bit short. I would have expected more but looking at the notes, it is mostly the Vanilla that may have the ability to perform longer. I do not know. I shall keep it, though. It has that really beautiful frangipani note, and that makes it worth it. I wear Kenzo Amour for the same reason. La Femme will be a great substitute. Year 2, 54/365

I have smelled it several times before. And whenever I did, it was always the same type of woman wearing it. Friendly, open-minded, reliable, determined, strong, and somehow also a bit of Everybody's Darling.

Casual, cheerful, bright, relaxed, self-confident, attractive, and extremely likeable. These are the qualities of La Femme that make it an absolute all-rounder for me. La Femme is, to my nose, a subtle, fruity, waxy-sweet fragrance that comes across as stunningly feminine and self-assured.

La Femme is one of those scents that I tend to overlook. On a quick test, it’s quite nice, but nothing really sticks. Once again, it’s something feminine-floral-creamy and totally unexciting. But since I’ve been a bit fixated on exactly this kind of scent lately (at least when I let it sit on my skin), I finally had to give La Femme a chance...

This fragrance made its way into my collection via a small detour. I can't even remember where I first heard about it, but I was eager to test it, which I did - once again on my way back through the city from work - at the perfume shop. First spray. Meeeeehhhhh, SUPER floral!

...will finally be good. Ohhhhh... how I have disregarded the sample of this fragrance. To be honest, I had a tremendous respect because tuberose is honestly a nightmare for me. Almost all fragrances that contain tuberose are candidates for nausea and dishwashing - and the latter usually doesn't even help - for me. So it lay there for a loooong time, ignored.

I already know the perfume and this one smells very similar to Prodigieux - Le Parfum for me. However, when it comes to the price, one must say that it's better to reach for the Nuxe. Unless you are particularly inclined towards Tom Ford and absolutely must have it. Probably only then because of the bottle or just the name. I managed to get this body spray in a swap game and of course had something in mind: to definitely pack it in the beach bag for the next vacation. During my last visit to the fun thermal spa, it was already put to use. A truly excellent body spray that certainly has a long-lasting effect. Smooth sunscreen vibes, diving into the cool water, bringing along a lot of lemons, meet here with a gentle tonka bean that spreads delightfully on the warmed skin and forms a beautiful duo with the jasmine. The scent is absolutely not intrusive, rather reserved. One would think it has nothing to do with Tom Ford, but exactly this unobtrusiveness fits particularly well here. The body spray is not shrill, not sticky, it is exactly as I expect from a body spray. It should simply be a relaxed, albeit shorter companion for the vacation mood! Over time, it takes on a slightly woody character, with tonka bean and jasmine being the main theme. Beautifully creamy, almost buttery soft, it lasts until the last breath. You can confidently reapply, as you don’t need much of this scent to bring some sun for the soul and stroll slowly through the sand with warmed feet, letting the wind caress your warmed skin..

This perfume could be similar to a White silk shirt: minimal, but very elegant and classy. Iris notes are noticeable and the ensemble is well balanced and pleasant. It's a powdery scent, but not too much because neroli and citruses give a particular modern freshness. The price is high, but the product and the bottle too are very very good

The first and probably the last "women's" perfume I bought for myself, I randomly walked through a perfume shop and saw Prada and among all that I was interested in iris of course and one spray and I was in zen, wow I fell in love with this fragrance and the other day I bought it. I see that many people write and I agree this is unisex, this is a timeless classic that has nothing to do with gender, this is iris perfection. I have Prada L'Homme and I consider it one of the best men perfumes ever, but this one is a little different, more gentle, more romantic, more dreamy ... For me a perfect intimate scent of purity, smells like a white clouds in the sky, I think that if there is a place like heaven, it must smell like this there. It’s a unisex iris perfection in the bottle. Take into account that I love and prefer old school men's fragrances like Drakkar Noir, Azzaro PH, etc., this is somewhat the opposite. just like everything in life is Yin and Yang, it's the same with perfumes, this is the gentle side of men. I guess I'm not the only one who likes "real" men's fragrances on the one hand and iris "feminine" on the other :)

Remembered I smelled this in the past and regretting that I didn't buy it then (still regret that because I think it was a bit cheaper then), it was a long time ago though, so I sampled first to see if I would still love it and, oh my, I do!!! Bought a full bottle immediately. And really: I think I'm ready now, this completes my collection, in fact this could well be my signature. I find this scent beyond gorgeous!! It actually is what I love in Chanel 19 but with something kind and feminine added that I sometimes miss in Chanel 19 (guess I should have bought the 'poudre' version of Chanel 19 maybe, but I don't need to bother now, having both Chanel 19 and Infusion d'Iris). Love the sillage of this, I get these beautyful, enchanting wafts with every movement. It is so clean in such a beautyful, angelic, versatile way! Opening is a little citrussy, but in a soft feminine way, not sharp. Then that lovely Iris come's through, not the paper-kind of Iris and not the too sweet/powdery Iris, but a fresh Iris, perfectly balanced between those two. Oh, such a lovely powder this is, a cool, not stuffy powder. Uplifiting but also calming. Soft and gentle but not aloof. Sillage I find much better than rated and I can smell it many hours after spraying. Perfection! So happy with this scent! Edit: Really LOVE this, woke up to the beautyful smell this morning, it really has way better longevity and sillage then rated in my opinion, or maybe it's my chemistry, but usually perfumes don't last on me this long. And the scent is lovely at first spray, but even gets better and better, the longer it is on my skin! Edit II: Still love it, but I've noticed one shouldn't overspray this scent and not too close to the nose because this is a scent one can easily get nose-blind to. I guess that explains the relatively low ratings for sillage and longevity. Edit III: Problem solved with Ceravé Intensive Moisterizing bodylotion as a base, I could smell it all day.

This one has got to be the most comforting iris I have ever smelled so far. I mainly get some faintly sweet citrus and like an expensive baby powder. It also feels like you're being hugged in newly washed sheets. Leaning a bit vintage for some reason but I don't mind at all. Surprisingly has decent longevity (around 4-6hrs on clothes) for a clean scent. I think this is a good entry point for people who aren't familiar with iris.

This is a scent I've been chasing in my mind, for a long while. God truly knows for how long, since I can't remember anymore. Iris is such a delightful note that can have so many shapes and presentations, and i became obsessed with it. For my birthday, i decided to buy some decants of perfumes with prominent iris notes. This perfume, of course, had to be part of it. I just needed to try this one. At first spray, the scent reminded me of old people tastes in perfumery, but in a good way: the vintage feeling of thinking of my grandmother, and what she might have smelled like, if this existed back then. Then, as if the perfume knew that i am not old enough, the scent turned into something sweeter, the benzoin became stronger (which is natural on me, as my skin chemistry turns sweet notes and intensifies them). As it started to wind down, the musk and cedar appeared, making this an excellent closing moment. This is not a sillage monster, compliment-getter, lady-magnet that will make you rich because a rich man smelled it on you on a fatidic day. This is calm, relaxing, simple, unassuming. It only wants to bring you comfort. Great scent for when the world is too harsh.

The initial cloud smells the way a cottage cheese bar tastes. Is it even a thing outside of post-Soviet countries? It's basically curd cheese blended with sugar, and usually covered in chocolate. It's a rather gentle sweet flavor with a peculiar freshness to it. Creamy, but with a somewhat crumbly texture. Ugh, now I want one. Or five.

Iris is one of those notes that can leave me entranced for hours when done beautifully like this one. Elegant slightly fresh cause of the citruses, gentle, powdery and a tad soapy. A perfume that makes me feel put together and ready to go, or that can relax me and makes me feel cozy: I just feel comfortable with it, it evokes calmness and balance.

Lately, I've been acquiring fragrances that I wouldn't necessarily purchase myself, if at all. I have been blessed to be #gifted so many that I am grossly behind on reviewing them and taking photos, but one that really stood out was Infusion d'Iris. Besides the beautiful bottle, many of you have recommended it to me as well.

As I am a bit of a junkie when it comes to Prada's Infusions (especially the iris variants have captivated me), I had to test the 2015 Infusion as well. And I went straight for a full bottle, no samples for me. I'm not shy about it!

...And how many? .....that's how I feel about this great scent from Prada. Prada Infusion d'Iris, 2007, I have rediscovered it for myself; it is, for me, almost a pheromone-laden fragrance that completely merges with me, mixing with my hormones, present yet not present, but it has an effect.

This is - after the original Neroli Portofino and the recently added Acqua - my third comment on Tom Ford's azure blue - yes, indeed - classic, which (apparently) is so wonderfully debatable. Debatable because it arranges the inherently fleeting neroli oil in a way that is more enduring than its nature would suggest, and thus perhaps artificial or even distorted. And also debatable because a seeming similarity to another fragrance using the neroli accord is hard to deny - and Mr. Ford would like to charge more money than the ladies and gentlemen from Cologne on the Rhine. Regarding the first point: in none of his four neroli perfumes or the variants of the original Neroli Portofino is the bright accord of the essential orange blossom oil not beautifully orchestrated. In all of them, there is a kind of noble firn - that artificially elevated quality - that gives its freshness solidity and grandeur, and a snow-white prosperity that the Cologne waters (and I am a passionate lover of all things Cologne!) will never have. It has tenderness and mischief, has sensitivity and verve, and a delightful southern carefreeness that makes every moment a little bit better than it would be without Neroli Portofino. Just briefly on the second alleged point of contention or criticism: because he can. 'La pulce d'acqua' - in English: 'the water flea' - is the title of a song by the wonderful Italian bard Angelo Branduardi - perhaps his most beautiful, undoubtedly his most famous. It is a friendly, cheerful song full of lightness and carefree joy - just like a water flea jumping across the surface of the water on a sunny afternoon: quietly content and free of worries. I smell southern herbs in Neroli Portofino Eau Fraîche - and a tranquil pond, which lies quietly and cheerfully, barely shaded by low-hanging willows. Dragonflies dance over its water and a butterfly flits by, water lilies rest on the green-blue surface, and darting between them - there goes the water flea. Conclusion: a small, cheerful fragrance full of lightness and zest for life - as if one were watching the water fleas doing nothing by the pond for an endless afternoon. And yet: Tom Ford through and through.

Tom Ford, the luxury fashion designer from New York, who first revitalized the GUCCI group with his trendy and youthful ideas, founded his own fashion label in 2006 and has since created several fragrances for both women and men. Last year, the luxury body care line TF Neroli Portofino was added, consisting of the following products: Body Moisturizer (150ml), Body Scrub (200ml), Body Oil (250ml), Soap (155g), Shower Gel (150ml), Eau Fraîche Body Splash (250ml), Candle, Neroli Portofino EDP NEROLI, also known as neroli oil, is a distillate obtained from the blossom of the bitter orange tree, an essential oil. Traditionally, the origin of neroli is attributed to Sicily; according to legend, neroli got its name from the Sicilian princess Nerola, who adored this scent. About one kilogram of neroli is obtained from a ton of blossoms. The essential oil is produced through steam distillation. In TF Neroli Portofino, real neroli oil is said to have been used. PORTOFINO, a small town near Genoa on the northern Italian Mediterranean coast, forms the second part of the fragrance name. Even Dior drew on the charm of this little town's name for the scent Escale à Portofino, which stands for pure romance and wealth. This is where high society vacations. Here is a quote describing Neroli Portofino from the marketing perspective: "Tom Ford Neroli Portofino, the reimagining of the classic Eau de Cologne, impresses with a Mediterranean mix of orange blossom oil, bergamot, lemon, mandarin, lavender, and rosemary. Rounded off with a sensual amber note, you dive into the world of Portofino, a resort on the Italian Riviera, internationally known for its blend of enchanting beauty and the glamour and tradition of the 'Old World'. The bottle is designed in the typical Tom Ford Private Blend style. Tom Ford was inspired by the glass bottles used in pharmacies and perfumers' workshops for the packaging of NEROLI PORTOFINO." The TF Private line has not appealed to me so far; the oud fragrances that I usually love seem too feminine here. With Neroli Portofino, I was already taken by the packaging and its color before I even smelled it. This fresh turquoise is relaxing just to look at. The bottles from the Private line are also very successful, classic and timeless. Two weeks ago, I finally had the chance to experience the turquoise scent for the first time. It was clear: straight onto the skin... It was a very hot day, and I was rewarded:-) This cool, refreshing, yet also powdery, mysterious, and even elegant neroli note enveloped my nose. I can understand why Princess Nerola loved it too. Of course, I immediately thought of 4711, one of the first fragrances in the world, made in Germany. But is it really bad to create a modern homage to this masterpiece? I see it more positively that one still orients itself to this milestone, even in the prestige range. Americans are known to love our tradition and culture in Germany/Europe. I see it as a great compliment to have developed Neroli Portofino in memory of 4711. I was so excited that I immediately had to get the body lotion, body oil, and the Eau Fraîche, a delight:-) The body splash can be used either as body care or like an Eau Fraîche as a refreshing scent; you can wonderfully decant it from the 250ml bottle, which costs €119, into a small spray bottle. The body lotion is incredibly economical and makes the skin feel like silk after just one application. The body oil does not grease or stick at all. All three products hold the scent on my skin for up to 7 hours; I am very satisfied. Some EdPs can't manage that. A luxury Eau Fraîche to enjoy, refresh, and relax.

Scentrack: Montefiori Cocktail – Anonimo Veneziano Prada Infusion d’Iris was released in 2015, as a replacement for Infusion d’Homme which I used to wear. Personally, I still prefer Infusion d’Homme which was a little bit more masculine orientated, possibly due to enhanced smoky vetiver note. Infusion d’Iris Cedre is a tweaked predecessor to fit in a relaunched unisex Infusion line. Infusion d’Iris Cedre strictly follows Prada’s fragrance aesthetics, it is clean, cold and totally unisex. It opens with just a touch of piercing neroli, and goes straight to iris. This iris is Prada’s signature - cold, powdery, retro and slightly chemical. Not the iris we can encounter in Dior Homme. Woodsy notes of cedar give the slight masculine touch. The warmer benzoin gives this composition needed touch of human warmth, while the incense somehow stays cold and archaic. The overall composition is clean, unobtrusive and little bit retro. Like a retro soap or a bubble bath. I can smell north Italian roots of Prada company (Milan, but also Bologna or Venice). It is an ideal fragrance for office, and one of my favorites for that purpose. To more appreciate this composition, one should have some gray hair. It even garners compliments in situations where compliments are rare. This is not mind blowing composition, but a very solid one in the Prada’s portfolio. Clean, sophisticated, professional and Italian.

Infusion d'Iris Cèdre is now named and available as: 'Infusion de Cèdre' (in the Netherlands at least) but the notes listed on the packaging are: Cèdre; Mandarine, Encens, Benjoin. It has that same ethereal quality as Infusion d'Iris (2015) Eau de Parfum (in the opening you wouldn't be able to tell the difference), in the drydown it is different: more fresh and 'white shirt-ish' and a bit more uni-sex. Nice, but I don't smell any Iris in the drydown. Don't know if it is projecting more than Infusion d'Iris (2015) Eau de Parfum because of the strength or because it has that different scent-profile in the drydown, but - as far as I can tell now - it seems a bit more potent (a bit more 'piercing' maybe and therefore more noticeable?). I feared it would be too woody, but the cèdre just gives it some 'body' without it being too 'pencil shaving-ish', though on clothing the woody notes are a bit more prominent. Definitely a scent for warm spring and summer. Edit: I love Infusion d'Iris much more, it is more fluffy and powdery and comforting. Actually I doubt Prada's claim that the renamed version (Infusion Cèdre) is the same as this (which I can't find anymore)

This Infusion d'Iris Cèdre is a beautiful, clean and dusty aroma, which pleases everyone, is one of those aromas, which, although not being generic, is designed to please the masses, and therefore I do not find it original or groundbreaking, but yes, very beautiful and pleasant. Its aroma is a dusty iris surrounded by flashes of cedar and neroli, very pleasant and well orchestrated, and all this, on an ephemeral base of sweet benzoin and incense, which, despite being almost imperceptible, provides the just and necessary warmth, so that the aroma does not become excessively linear. Everyone who has given it to smell has liked, being its greatest virtue, that characteristic smell of clean, expensive soap, freshly washed clothes with a good fabric softener, who does not like to smell like this, after a shower? Well, that I think is his great claim. A nice and pleasant perfume, but I am more intense oriental, I think it is not for me. It has a moderate performance, its longevity is between 5 or 6 hours, with a moderate projection from the beginning, but, for a perfume of these characteristics it is more than good, although, yes, too expensive for what it offers. Unisex perfume of warm and temperate climates and to enjoy it during the day.

This is the same scent of infusion d'homme with edp concentration. Very natural product, very discret fragrance with a clean sensation. This is a perfume very easy to use everyday in office or in your daily Life. Impossible not to like it.

As others have stated, this perfume has been renamed (at least in the US) as Infusion de Cedre. After a long text chat with Prada directly, and not a small amount of confusion on their end (too), it was confirmed that only the name has changed and the formula is the same. I can’t vouch for this. But under the new name, I smelled a healthy dose of doughy Iris right off the top (same as in Infusion d’Iris). So I can—at least—report it still does contain Iris. As it dries, it does become quite powdery and musky and loses much of its iris personality. A pity. As an iris lover, I was sad to see it fade. That’s not to say the perfume is bad at mid through base; it’s clean, soft, powdery. Pleasant. The cedar does give it a slight “baby wipe” note at the mid. Compared to other Iris cedre perfumes (Affinessence Cedre Iris) this does fall short. Iris does make a reappearance at the base. Yet, for a clean, uncomplicated scent, it does it job.

If you love the "old" Infusion d'homme and you blinly smell this fragrance you recognize it immediately. The ingredients are the same, maybe the result is a little more powdery , but there's no doubt. It's Infusion d'homme "reloaded". Maybe the name has changed because This scent musn't be only for men, but for women too.

Anyone who thinks Prada's bestseller, "L'Homme," is already cool, distant, and possesses a certain cyber DNA, clearly hasn't tried "Infusion d'Iris Cédre." Regarding the so-called "cyber DNA," it refers to the extremely smooth, somewhat technized scent character that radiates aloofness and is quite far from warmth. Yet, it is precisely this that can create allure.

Ridley Scott's film Blade Runner (1982) is considered a stylistically defining science fiction masterpiece. The equally brilliant novel was penned by the perpetually doped-up SF multi-writer Philip K. Dick, who saw parts of the film shortly before he died of heart failure in March '82. The film, featuring a gruff Harrison Ford in the lead role, was not a box office hit.

Oh yes, our ever-popular washing plumber Klementine from Ariel would be jumping for joy like Hans Rosenthal if she knew how clean and pure Infusion d'Iris Cèdre smells, and the Persil man would say, "You know what you have, good evening." And..... They would be right, and how right they would be!

Cargo De Nuit....Silvery musk, woody notes, mineralic notes all like fine threads of scent woven together in a thin sheen silken fabric. Futuristic, hazy yet oddly familiar with the cozy and soft coumarin shavings. This is an elevated more focused and structured Luna Rossa Black. What even is it? Hard to describe other than pretty words. The high ratings are justified, though the price is just absurd. 9/10 and only knocking a point for the price

In a widely known online encyclopedia, it states: “An appeal, also known as an Appellation, is a legal remedy against a judgment of the first instance.” I am appealing my own initial judgment on Cargo de Nuit. Just a few weeks ago, I rated it a seven and a half, accompanied by the now-deleted statement that it borrowed certain elements from White Musk (Bodyshop, a tenth of the price), but unfortunately did not show much more than that. I blindly signed off on the weakness that is often noted. Then my vacation got in the way. Milan. A city full of temptations for fashion enthusiasts (not me) and fragrance fanatics (a bit me). A city that sucks in money and makes it disappear into nothing with the entry of a four-digit PIN. At the end of August, a relatively empty (summer vacation), sweltering hot place. Off to the air-conditioned perfumeries and department stores! There was so much to discover … … including the Olfactories line from Prada, priced high like the Parco Palladiano line from Bottega Veneta or the La Collection Privée Christian Dior. Hmm, there was something, I thought to myself. And there it was, Cargo de Nuit, that fragrance I had rated as mediocre with the ringing, strange, intriguing name, of which I still do not know whether it alludes to a French hit from the 80s - by a certain Axel Bauer - or has any connection to Midnight Train and Moonlight Shadow from the same line. “Freight Ship of the Night” - or how should one translate that? Sounds a bit like McDonald's naming a new burger “Melancholy of the Pampa Beef”; one could philosophize about that for a long time. Be that as it may. After my first acquaintance via Parfumo sharing (thanks to Niklas), I wanted to give the night freight ship a second chance. In the basement of a large perfumery, which also creates its own scents and is known, among other things, for an Aventus “clone,” I was able to test Cargo de Nuit again on my skin and my shirt, as well as on a paper strip. First at 22, 23 degrees, then outside at 32, 33. Yes, I still perceive a dominant musk impression, which likely comes from the ambrette seeds (Bisameibisch, Abelmoschus), which according to research are often used as a substitute for animal musk. For me, however, this has nothing animalistic about it, but rather something pleasantly soft. I personally would not describe it as “clean” like, for example, Infusion d’Iris Cèdre, although I understand why this association might easily arise. By the way, Prada itself lists musk instead of ambrette seeds. Complete: musk, aldehydes (very generic), woody and mineral notes (very generic), amber, ambroxan (which does not make sense to me at all), coumarin. Again: be that as it may. It’s all about the scent - and it can be “realized” in various ways, just as the fragrance notes usually seem to be more associations than necessarily ingredients. Many here have a woodruff association, which likely comes from the coumarin. I am a bit torn on that. In a nearby herb garden, I picked a handful of woodruff and compared it several times with Cargo de Nuit: fresh, after about an hour, after six, half a day … My impression: This slight sweetness, “floating,” not at all harshly spicy quality in Cargo de Nuit may be coumarin, but not woodruff. However, I admit that I once smelled the fragrance with a half-stuffed nose and then suddenly thought of woodruff (I find it fascinating how differently, almost strangely and newly, scents can smell then). Nevertheless: Those looking for woodruff should rather continue their search elsewhere. But a dominant note of this perfume at least heads in that direction. The mentioned coumarin note can also be detected in Luna Rossa Black, although there it is, in my opinion, dressed in too much distracting intense woodiness (?). In Cargo de Nuit, Daniela Andrier weaves primarily these two fragrance notes - something musky and something coumarin-like - into a quiet, subtle scent sound, which likely failed to impress me at first because it is completely unspectacular and unobtrusive, and only becomes not just “nice,” but truly beautiful when one smells it very closely and surrenders to it. Cargo de Nuit is then (at least for me) a wonderful, soulful, cozy fragrance, a scent mist in the forest, so delicate that it resembles a transparent, soft green powder cloud. Yes, it envelops, yes, it makes blissful. And yes, it is absolutely not loud. With, for example, Infusion d’Iris Cèdre, it shares subtlety and seriousness, but is warmer, more approachable, while the latter fragrance, in my opinion, seems a bit more artificial and distant (which I find very nice there). All of this makes Cargo de Nuit for me a fragrance that can be wonderfully worn at work, especially when one has a lot of contact with other people. This functionality is indeed characteristic of many Prada fragrances (e.g., numerous Infusiones or L’homme). Cargo de Nuit fits almost always. At work, in leisure, on a date. Only for a “loud night out” would it be too quiet. I also find it, compared to many “infusions,” truly unisex, or let’s say: gender-neutral. Once, on a cool summer evening, I sprayed it on a cozy-soft sweater. And there, a whole new magic emerged. For me, Cargo de Nuit is quite fleeting on the skin (or I adapt too quickly), but on clothing, it is oddly like a persistent, gentle cotton candy cloud, delicious and unobtrusive, softly sweet yet entirely ungourmand. A dream, albeit not one with the greatest longevity. Despite all the joy from the abundant sunshine, I am already looking forward to the fresher, cooler days when this fragrance will magically create an impression of coziness, comfort, snugness, cosiness, hygge, or however one might call it. Is it worth its elevated price? Standard answer: That’s something everyone must decide for themselves. I must honestly say: Probably nine out of ten interested parties will be disappointed after a thorough test because they would have expected “more” for the money. I understand that. Only for me, it unfortunately fits quite well. It is not spectacularly loud, no wonder of the world, no work of art. But it is simply very well made - and with the necessary patience, it showed me its entire gentle subtlety. I will gladly wear it, especially in autumn and spring, at work or afterwards to relax, to be cozily scented.

“Cargo de Nuit” is my personal sea of the moon. My only 10 here on Parfumo. This fragrance expresses a special mood within me like no other, which I can hardly describe. It calms, it strengthens, it carries - me. Certainly, Daniela Andrier has conjured up substances here that bring lunar associations to light. I actually don’t want to overanalyze this scent; too much expertise (I don’t just mean my acceptable one, but also your outstanding one) would lift too much of the enjoyment’s floating state. Coumarins have a calming effect, cedar and sandalwood notes are universally beloved materials, and the trick magic of the ISO-E-Super universe shakes hands. The iris, which I like to see, peeks through the fog wall for a moment. This makes Cargo de Nuit a versatile fragrance, almost always wearable, and despite the moon and Prada’s night connotations, it warms rather than refreshes. It warms like an intimate embrace. A quiet one, though - but a familiar one. Perhaps I like it so much because I discovered it for myself back then, without having read much about it here. It felt like a rare treasure find. One that you only have once every few years. Maybe also because it seems beautifully understated (!) - that is probably completely out of fashion (#beast / #sillagemonster), just like the very restrained sweetness. It moves me to inner stillness - just as I imagine it would be on the moon. Vacuum noise, vast white, and weightless shadow. A self. No you.

This night is not starry. A calm fog hangs over the waters, iridescent, ambrette-smooth, gray-violet. The ships still find their way. not getting too close to the large freighters at night the ships glowed, pushing off from the water's surface delicate sea rolls slowly dissolved their matter created a space beneath the seabed drawbridges, streams from the land, it was a rare light This light shines through the fog walls, muffling the occasional dull honking of the ships to a gentle sound. The smell of gasoline is mixed here and there in the fog. The light also penetrates through the water beneath the ships, along the ship's walls down into the depths, where it gradually becomes less and less. The waters are calm, moving very slowly. The soul follows the movement into the depths, beneath the seabed, dissolving into the oceanic. Peace. immerse yourself in the movement of the water that light mixed with the light, creating their connection another light, kinship of escape and understanding a middle thing between gas and liquid ----- The scent of "Cargo de Nuit" is a soul fragrance. At the same time, it very modernly refers to the movements of large cargo ships navigating through night and (for me) fog. In November 2021, I was at the Laeiszhalle Hamburg for the fascinating premiere of the piece "ships glow at night" by Leon Zmelty, based on the poem of the same name by Nico Bleutge. Unlike in the video below, it was performed there by the great Landesjungendorchester, and it represents for me, along with the poem, the mood that the fragrance also conveys. ----- A very synthetic, very well-made scent. With Ambroxan & Co., one can also create the impression of light that is dimmed and shines through the darkness. Yes, it really does smell like fog, which is "a middle thing between gas and liquid." Additionally, I have a slight gasoline note here, powdery iris, very soothing delicate coumarin (no candy woodruff), and something very delicate and creamy almond-like. The woodiness is also very soft, most like sandalwood and a hint of cedar, combined with feather-soft musk. I find the whole experience very calming, as if the scent truly wants to pull me to some place deep beyond the seabed, where all tensions are lifted. And at the same time, fortunately, on the surface, this soft glow of the lights mixing in the fog remains in motion… ----- Thank you to Seejungfrau for the sample! Quotes from Nico Bleutge: ships glow at night Leon Lukas Zmelty's composition "ships glow at night": https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oofTS4DqmBU (from 1:00:21)

I can't describe it. It's a feeling. A feeling like "Geste" by Humięcki & Graef. A fragrance that radiates contentment and creates a cozy feeling. Almost maternal. Woodruff/Coumarin, as it grows wild in the forest and only begins to scent when it is rubbed between the hands after drying. Not sweet, rather sweet-green-velvety.

Once you have immersed yourself in the world of fragrances, it is hard to come back out. At least when the desire has taken hold to find the perfect scent or to create the perfect collection. I have spent a lot of money on samples. My search is over for now. I have never written a comment on this platform, but if any fragrance deserves it, then this one does.

What does one do in this time when there’s really nothing else to do but go out to work and shop? Well, what else? Order perfume, of course! ;) And I’ve also planned a spring cleaning. To be honest, I’m not really a fan of the Prada brand. I once had Candy, but it was so boring, and after I finished it, I didn’t want any more.

Ah, these Olfactories have truly captivated me. This one is also a dream. I particularly appreciate this pleasant sillage. In the past, Prada was mostly associated with being overly opulent for me. But not the Olfactories. This one is certainly noticeable on me, but it wraps around me like a second skin, so rather subtle and quiet. The longevity lasts easily all day.

Hello everyone, how do I even start this review..., so many things are swirling through my mind! If you are looking for a sweet feminine or a masculine (woody -oud) fragrance, you can leave this review right now, because it is certainly not that. Foreword number 1: I did not know the fragrance - absolutely not! I associate the brand with the theme of "clean"...

The name suits it well, it’s bright, cool, and clean. It’s a true fresh/aquatic with a bit of brightness from the citrus but it’s so well balanced that it neither leans too household cleaner, nor too sweet/fruity. It reminds me a little of Giorgio Armani Ocean di Gioia, but less floral and more subtle. The only downside is that it doesn’t last very long, so you would need to reapply a couple of times throughout the day. Or this may be a great option if you’re sensitive to fragrance and don’t want anything too heavy or overwhelming. IMO This is the perfect scent for your gym bag, or pool/beach bag to refresh during the day or when it’s hot outside

Powdery, clean and elegant. Definitely a sister (not twin) to Infusion d'Iris, but the younger, warmer and more playful one. Even though neither are listed, I smell iris powder and sparkling, soap-bubbly aldehydes in the opening. The almond note is sweet and smooth, it reminds me of candied wedding almonds. There is a slight milkiness to them, too. Tonka and heliotrope aren't really distinguishable from almond here - this doesn't have the spicier facets of tonka or the doll-like aspects of heliotrope, everything just smells like sweet almond dragees. I forgot that this had a star anise note when I was testing it, but thought that it had an anise-like undertone, so I'd say this note is more prominent than the votes suggest, though still subtle. I personally prefer scents like this to be a little creamier, so I wouldn't chose this for myself. Nevertheless I like it a lot. In my opinion it's would make a perfect work scent for someone who enjoys gourmands and very feminine scents, but wants something understated for the office. It's not quite as serious as Infusion d'Iris, but not overtly girly either. The light blue hue of the packaging fits the scent very well.

I love this Scent. It opens with a sparkly, spicy cherry vibe. That has an uncanny resemblance to Dr pepper and Amaretto and coke. Which is so warm and delicious. It also has a well rounded powdery smoothness very much like the original infusion that oozes class and gives the smell a lovely softness. It really shines in the outdoor air that's when it projects the most I've found. Thanks to DonVanVliet for the recommendation. This is just gorgeous stuff :) Scent 10/10 Sillage 8/10 Longevity 7/10 Bottle 9/10

I tested right now and I was expecting the usual medicinal bitter Almond I find for example in Hypnotic poison. I realize that is totally different: the notes are perfectly balanced and the bitter Almond is soft and pleasant. It's a mediterranean classy fragrance with gourmand accent without being too sweet . An elegant and clean perfume I recommend.

As an ardent lover of most things Daniela Roche Andrier and Prada, I naturally had to go out of my way to try the new Infusions. Infusion d'Amande (IdA) strikes me as about the half way point between two pillars of the brand: Infusion d'Iris and Candy. IdA starts with a realistic blast of green almond and sweet musk. As it dries it gets progressively less sweet and more powdery clean. This doesn't ever really get to gourmand despite the notes. IdA is musky, warm, inoffensive and verges on baby-powderish without smelling like Teint de Neige. Like many Pradas there is a sheerness, a transparency and weightlessness to composition that makes this inherently easy to wear and easy to like. That being said, this isn't much of a statement maker. I like it, but I don't need a full bottle.

This Almond Infusion opens with a warm, almost pastry-like sweetness, evoking the comforting scent of frangipane. It's cozy and inviting, like a delicious dessert that's just been taken out of the oven, soft and delicate. The fragrance has a comforting, almost nostalgic quality, like being wrapped in a cozy blanket on a cold day, offering an indulgent moment of warmth and sweetness. There’s nothing sharp or overpowering here, just a gentle, enveloping presence that feels soothing and reassuring.

There are brands that simply attract attention with the brilliance of their names. Whenever I read that, for example, Guerlain, Armani, Dior, or indeed Prada are launching new fragrances, I can't help but perk up my ears, and such an announcement often finds its way onto my watchlist. Prada's new "Infusion wave" should be no exception.

After the last rather questionable fragrance experience, which are experiences that must be included, I am turning back to something pleasant-smelling. I recently got to know the Prada Infusions, although I had had some of them on my watchlist for quite some time.

Sometimes it's quite strange... one thinks they want at least one from the Infusion line by Prada in their collection. I chose Infusion d'Amande because I really like almond scents. In the Souk, I found it and boldly snagged (me and my blind buys... grin) thanks to a lovely perfume friend a leftover bottle :) I had cautiously asked her if it was soapy...

With an order I placed, a nice sales associate included a sample of Infusion d'Armande. I sprayed it on and immediately found the scent pleasantly warm. The light, bitter note, like a fine bitter almond, which I liked so much, was replaced after a while, and the fragrance became slightly spicy and then sweetly powdery.

What a scent. I received a huge swap package filled with samples, and among the first three fragrances to test was this one. While two other high-end scents (Wulong Cha and Lira) left me completely indifferent at first sniff, I was instantly smitten with Infusion d‘Amande. My first association was Deluxe Baby Powder, delicate cream, soft and fluffy like little cloud sheep.

I have to admit I bought this one for the name alone. In the store it smelled slightly masculine and intriguing. However, after dousing myself in it at home my stomach turned. It’s absolutely disgusting. And expensive. Fortunately, I only bought the body spray in the smallest size so it didn’t hurt my budget much. But it would have been money better spent on a more pleasant scent. For now, the bottle is sitting in my bathroom cabinet gathering dust.

My poor dear, I am so sorry. I know people speak ill of you. They just don't understand you, Prada. But as your good and loyal friend, I must tell you that it's your loud and unbalanced opening that puts people off. You come on so strong at first, and sometimes it's just too much. Your crazy, unexpected shout of greeting can be jarring to those who don't know you like I do. When you screech like that at me, I know it is because you're glad to see me, and I also know from long experience that you'll calm down quickly. You know, Prada, after you stop acting crazy, I can see a bit of resemblance to your more refined cousin, Coco Mademoiselle. But do you know what else I think? Your heart is sweeter than hers. And after we have been together for a while, your elegant, rounded patchouli-drenched vanilla sandalwood base is a thing of beauty that I can not help but love. Oh, Prada, don't pout. You will never win Miss Popularity, but that is not a bad thing. It means you are not common. Your true friends recognize your quality, and of course, you'll always be a cherished friend of mine.

I like this perfume very much and I feel it fits me better than many others. The feeling I get from it is an inexplicable union between the urbane sophistication of a lively city and the wild call of a foggy, humid faraway forest. There is something enchanting about it, somehow poetical, like a melancholy feeling on a rainy autumn's day, looking through the window at the wet streets outside, watching the falling leaves dance as they swirl towards the ground. It makes you want to dream away, to lose yourself in a perfect emotion, a perfect state of mind. The scent itself is quite versatile, in the sense that it manages to compliment a wide range of styles and personalities. It's a modern classic, cosmopolitan and sophisticated, sexy but intellectual, wise, intuitive, feminine and sensual, warm and deep but still free and untamed. Prada is basically a woody oriental blend of rich amber and labdanum, sweet earthy patchouli and creamy vanilla. There's also a thick, rich sandalwood in the composition, somewhat similar to that in Samsara. All in all, very complex, dense and balmy.

Prada and I got off to a rocky start. When I first tested PRADA AMBER, I overapplied it and was frankly overwhelmed by the dense, dark, wine-like fruity opening. It's not quite the scent of wine, because it is much less sweet. But I'd say that it does come rather close to wine dregs. Suffice it to say that the opening is very intense. My first encounter with PRADA AMBER was through a decant sent to me by a fellow fragrant traveler in New York City. Since she is a woman who in my estimation has excellent taste, I suspected that my problem with this perfume had something to do with me. With time, I realized that I needed to give PRADA AMBER another chance, and I am very glad that I did. I now regard this as a fine fruity amber perfume with a great deal of depth and complexity and a gorgeous labdanum drydown. There is much, much more labdanum here than vanilla, so much so that it actually smells to me closer to a straight-up labdanum than an amber perfume. Unlike many amber perfumes, the vanilla is not even detectable to my nose as an isolable note. The labdanum is central to this composition, and the patchouli is fairly strong as well, but again this is not a part of the post-ANGEL sweet patchouli pack at all. PRADA AMBER is unique. I ended up liking this creation enough to eventually pick up a 50ml bottle, and I continue to pine for one of the stunning atomizer models. It's only a matter of time before I find one at what seems like an unbeatable price, at which point I'm sure that I'll snap it up. The Prada aesthetic is top notch when it comes to packaging. Fortunately the perfumes smell very good, too! PRADA AMBER was selected along with eleven other perfumes by Chandler "Contingency Plan Man" Burr to be included in the Art of Scent exhibit currently being held at the Museum of Art and Design. On the other hand, PRADA AMBER was not so favorably received by the authors of The Holey [sic] Book, who appear to hate the house of Prada and every perfume they ever produced. I applaud Burr for having the guts to float as masterpieces of olfactory art a number of perfumes derisively dismissed by Turin & Sanchez as failures. Prada obviously does not jive with the Royal[ties] Couple's taste, above all their hatred of clean scents (Dolce & Gabbana LIGHT BLUE was awarded one star) and all things amber. Since everything from this house is either ambery or has a decidedly clean demeanor, it did not fare well. Burr has done much to resurrect the image of this perfume house, and I do not believe that it has been only a result of the fact that Puig is one of his major funders. Though I'm also quite certain that it didn't hurt. What Burr's radical disagreement with the other two self-appointed "experts" shows, it seems to me, is that in fact, when it comes to olfaction, beauty does indeed lie in the nose of the sniffer! According to me, Prada has produced some excellent creations, and PRADA AMBER for her is certainly one of them, although it is not an easy perfume to wrap one's nose around, as it defies most of the usual categories. The quality of the materials is top notch, and there certainly could be much worse things than increasing the global sales of this perfume through proclaiming it to be a masterpiece of olfactory art. It's a good perfume, no doubt, but labeling it a work of neo-romanticism may be stretching things a bit. Did the perfumers, Carlos Benaïm, Max Gavarry, and Clément Gavarry, and the house conceive of this perfume as anything more than a perfume when they launched it back in 2004? Of course not. Why we should appropriate the language of visual art for ephemeral scents is far from obvious to me. But that's a another story. The bottom line here, again, is that this is a fine and original oriental perfume.

Prada is an extremely unusual fragrance. I certainly did not expect something like this from a popular and mainstream brand. Prada is intense, spicy, rich, crisp and woodsy. The fragrance opens with sharp woods and subtle hints of citrus. It immediately reminds me of the scent of freshly polished rosewood furniture. The heart of this scent is somewhat crisp and fresh, yet the amber and spices balance this fragrance out nicely and add a delightful warmth. It also tends to have a grassy-like/damp forest finish which although odd is strangely appealing. I'll agree that the amber and patchouli are particularly dominant in this fragrance, however the green notes and the honey soften the scent. I wouldn't recommend this fragrance to overly feminine women, to me this isn't your typical flowery or sweet fragrance. A woman who wears Prada is edgy, confident and strong. I find some similarities between this fragrance and Euphoria by Calvin Klein, however Prada lacks the sweetness of Euphoria and is much stronger in both sillage and lasting power. I recommend that you try Prada if you're searching for a fragrance that is original, refined, classy, spicy/woodsy yet modern.

This has a milk and honey kind of a scent i find this very impressive since i'm not a fan of honey and milk notes but i really like this. Like rain soaked Patchouli in a early morning dew with gentil wispers of Oakmoss and willow then you smell the sweet scent of honey buzzing around your nose when you first apply it to your skin you smell a fleeting fruit note then it turns musky milky and honey. but the drydown doe'snt last eather consists of fiery sandalwood and benzoin sweet amber and patches of musk. Ok i only tried two Prada brands this and Infusion d'Iris prada has a talent for using natural ingredients in their perfumes never synthtic just stright Florals Woods Reisens e.t.c it has a refinedness that is a rarity in today's perfumery a maturity that can't not be compared to the others.

Prada Amber is a scent that reminds me of Dior Addict, and not because they really smell similar, but they're both woodsy, sweet, resinous scents that take up a lot of space. They are voluminous, they envelop you in a wondrously dreamy cloud of fragrance ...

Amazing, I've got a very old, very cherished bottle. It smells divine. The honey really is they key player, followed closely by the amber and musk. It makes for a sexy fragrance that is too heavy when the suns out, but in winter and at night it is amazing. I would also really love to smell this on a man, I think it can be unisex for sure.

In my youth, which admittedly was quite a few days ago, there were these perfume oils that were a hit for us teenagers. If you didn't smell like musk from ten kilometers away (me), you smelled like patchouli (some others). Interestingly, the musk faction thought that the patchouli wearers stank and vice versa. Very few liked both.

With this perfume, my long search for a pleasant patchouli scent has come to an end. Patchouli is a tricky note. It can quickly become too harsh or mixed with all sorts of sweet ingredients, thus distorted. An alternative would have only been the patchouli scent from Etro, regardless of the concentration. However, I found that one a bit too harsh.

"Prada Amber" is a peculiar scent - peculiar in the sense of interesting and good! I quickly sprayed it on myself in passing between two appointments, quite curious about this fragrance. Always spurred on by the Parfumos and their comments here. Dear people, your enthusiasm is dangerous!

I tested Paradigme before reading how much hate this had received, and am shocked to see how much it's been dragged. I understand it might not be the most innovative or unique blend - but while I wouldn't wear this for myself, I'm actually kind of obsessed with it! I would definitely want to smell this on a significant other, and it's also now among my favorite "masc-leaning" discoveries of 2025. To me, the bourbon geranium is the star of the show. This is only the second time I've tested bourbon geranium in a fragrance, and I'm absolutely in love with it here. It's present throughout the entire composition - and creates an ultra-velvety, subtly-mentholated/minty feel. Combined with the peru balsam, it brings a slightly-sweet and vanillic quality to the mint. It elevates the entire blend, and makes everything feel silkier and more refreshing. I get smooth, comforting spa soap + barely-sweet mint aftershave through Paradigme , and it pulls me in. On my personal "chili-stirring" scale, this fragrance somehow stirs but also simultaneously calms me. It has somewhat softer projection for a while, but that adds to the comforting appeal to me. (Projection noticeably increases in the base, when the amberwood becomes more pronounced.) The man wearing this would be understated, even-keeled, and reliable. He's planned his life, and made sure you're part of those plans. No games or cliffhangers here, so it's just soothing safety (from the fragrance AND man). So, no - predictable doesn't have to be boring... it can actually be (and is at least in my case, with Paradigme ) extremely attractive. EDIT: Longevity on fibers is nuclear (and is mostly the amberwood base) - I'm going on day 5 of it sticking around strongly on a tester strip. So if you spray this on clothes (rather than skin), be aware!

The name of this fragrance has surely got to be a joke. “Paradigme” implies a shift of paradigm presumably towards the future, but this fragrance is going backwards if anything. A fresh aromatic amberwood with slight fruity notes, it stinks of the same AI-generated slop that Phantom was supposedly composed with. Like how AI “creativity” works, it seems to just be an amalgamation of every popular men’s fragrance over the last 10 years. Bland doesn’t even begin to describe it.

The title here is not referring only to Paradigme . It's a perfect description of the current market of designer fragrances. Lackluster, boring, unoriginal compositions, money-grabber releases, and hardly qualitative fumes have taken over designer camp, with the competition looking more like who can make the most uninspiring fragrance rather than the other way around. And Paradigme is yet another great example of the current state of designer fragrances. The opening is, of course, represented first and foremost with a synthetic blast, only to reveal a chemical bergamot with its low-quality citric tones, and a side of warm, sweet muskiness. This immediately reminds me of Myslf , only there is no 'clean laundry' continuation. It might also remind of the scent of an apple, only it lacks that juiciness and realism. Instead, a rosy, sweet floral heart pushes through, with herbaceous undertones from the geranium. The rose here clearly lacks that depth and realism of a well-put together rose scent, and it isn't very strong either, seemingly struggling to overpower the musky accords. But no worries, the synthetic structure is still present, carrying the scent forward (or backwards, better said). Ah, but now my "favorite" part - the base. Paradigme progressively sweetens things up as it dries down, losing a little of that musky/synthetic accords. Then, a mishmash of sweet amberwood with a warm, vanillic inclusion from the benzoin bring a vivid memory in my mind... The memory of every single other sweet designer slop out there. There is no true woodiness in here; it's your brain which is tricked into believing that you smell some woody aspects due to seeing amberwood/Guaiac wood in the notes pyramid. But truly, all there is is just a nondescript, bland, sweet sludge which you've smelt a hundred times before. However, it seems a little thicker here, probably due to the Peru balsam. I also do get some similarities with wet baby wipes, or even diapers sometimes deeper in the dry down. "Sophistication & Avant-Garde in a Fragrance" says some of Paradigme 's marketing, all for a fragrance which smells the most like designer slop out of all designer slops. On a more positive note, although arguably, in this case, it's not a positive aspect, longevity is pretty good, at least on my skin. It lasts for around 9-10 hours, with projection seemingly not as good, but still what you'd call decent. For the first hour, I had a very solid 2-3 feet of pushing power, with a prominent sillage too. Afterwards, it would settle to around a foot for about 1.5-2 hours more, and then it would mellow down up until a skin scent around hour 5. Versatility is basically guaranteed with most designer fumes, and Paradigme is not excluded. Apart from maybe the high heat, this is made to fit the daily/leisure categories first and foremost. Outside that, such as special occasions or formal events, this is the last thing you'd want to wear. But even as a daily scent, this will literally have you smelling like every other passerby on the street. So if a touch of uniqueness is what you're after, you couldn't have chosen a worse fragrance. Be weary of social media influencers who might (and will) hype Paradigme . The only thing worthy of praise here is ... and maybe also ... Truth to be told, anyone who values perfumery and puts a little bit of care in what they wear will not dare to look at something such as Paradigme . While it's not the most expensive of designers, coming as low as $90 for 50ml, in my opinion not even $40 would cut it. The 100ml and 150ml variants do go up to $120 and $190 in some places, so the only reasonable conclusion we can pull here is: stay away. There is nothing new, nor good to see here. Nothing worth the money. If we thought that either Bleu de Chanel L'Exclusif or Y Le Parfum (2025) would definitely take the "worst release of the year" title, we should think again, for Paradigme makes a very enticing case for itself as the worst designer of 2025. Overall Rating: 5/10

I believe Prada had some leftovers of Phantom. They added some extra sweet and dense benzoin to it and pored it in a fancy bottle. Voila, that’s modern perfumery! Come on Prada you can do better than this! Your whole line of Luna Rossa can be a better base than Phantom! So to if even this concise review was too long, here’s a TLDR: it’s crap.

Certainly modern, fresh and green, like a green musk without the musk being overbearing. Versatile, and safe. Performance is average. Not the same, but if you like Myslf you would like this as it’s a little more crisp with less sourness. For the rest of us that have been in this hobby for a while, there’s nothing to see here. I love Prada, but this is extremely uninspired. Since its a new line though, perhaps this goes the way of Luna Rossa with some excellent flankers?? It smells good though and if this was my first fragrance I’d buy it. But because my nose has smelled so many similar things there’s no reason for me to pick up a bottle. This is marketed for the masses though and with the good smell, it will likely do well.

This new release from Prada will definitely remind you of other things. Some say it smells like YSL MYSLF Le Parfum, and sure I can see it a little. On first spray, I get YSL MYSLF Le Parfum freshness, mid I get Valentino Uomo BIR Intense sweetness, and Boss Bottled Parfum woodiness (minus the spice).

Am I buying a bottle of this? No. I already own ATH Legend, Icon and Supernova....and this is right in that wheelhouse. But the sillage and longevity on Paradigm is pretty poor. nnNot sure why people are so passionate about rating it a 1.0. It isn't THAT bad. It's what you'd expect from a designer....

When Y Le Parfum launched four years back, I was into it. There was a bite to Y LP that I couldn't put my finger on until I looked it up, and there it was: geranium. It's an odd flower if you haven't sniffed one up close: there's a complexity to it at first, but there's something strong, sharp, biting about the middle of that scent that can knock you off your feet.

Preface: This perfume smells completely different on the skin compared to a testing strip. The opening is quite fruity with a perfect amount of sweetness. The aroma strongly suggests cleanliness with a twist of fruit and lavender. Initially, I thought it would be a fresh, daytime, hot-weather scent, but it shifts.

I got this body spray because I really wanted to try something from Tom Ford. When I used it for the first time, I was immensely disappointed. So it stood lonely, lost, and unnoticed in my perfume collection. Today, I wanted to give it another chance for one of the last workdays before Christmas and sprayed it generously. What can I say: at first, it was just like back then: a somewhat ordinary scent and the big disappointment. I just got home from work and, to test the longevity, I sniffed my wrist. Wow! I smell a juicy peach with smoky undertones. I could just dive into this scent. So Bitter Peach: you will definitely get a third chance from me.

With this fragrance, you get exactly what the name promises: a bitter peach. Over time, this bitter peach becomes a bit sweeter without losing its bitterness, and a few smoky notes join in. The longevity is rather lackluster, which I unfortunately also noticed with "Lost Cherry (Eau de Parfum) | Tom Ford." However, since I enjoyed the scent so much due to the unmistakable peach and I don't feel the need to watch every drop because of the body spray format, I found this to be a good price at around €60 to enjoy this fragrance.

The bad ratings for this are interesting considering this intense flanker of Paradoxe is better than the OG (subjective), but I guess the notes in this aren’t everyone’s cup of tea. I’ll be honest, I wasn’t going to bother with this because moss usually doesn’t play well on my skin, but I’m glad I took the leap of faith. The main difference between PI and the OG Paradoxe is that the original is a very linear, white floral + citrus combo that’s been done over and over again. It’s inoffensive (kinda boring tbh), soapy, slightly sweet, and very bright. This new Intense flanker, on the other hand, has a depth to it that just makes it better and more appealing to me. The moss adds a dark, earthy, bitter bite to a relatively bright and floral fragrance. The increased vanilla in this version is also what appealed to me and mixed in with the amber notes, it’s creates a beautiful base for the neroli and jasmine to sit atop. The dry down of this is spectacular and lasts the longest throughout its wear. I wore it for the first time yesterday and can attest to the performance being phenomenal. Strong sillage and lasts over well over 8+ hours on the skin (probably even better on clothes). As my collection continues to change, I find myself gravitating to niche fragrances more, but this is an excellent designer flanker that I’m happy to have tried and truthfully enjoy. It’s definitely worth a try.

I confidently sprayed this right on my skin based on how many people love it. Big mistake. It smelled like feminized men's cologne on me, and ventured into headache-territory. It feels like it's trying to be bold and confident, and it definitely is. Very floral with a mossy, deep dry down. I do have the gene to smell ambroxan, and the ambrofix is STONG which is what's making it smell very masculine to me. If you can't smell ambroxan I bet this just smells like confident florals!

MUCH better than the original due to added depth from earthy notes like moss. This scent lasts incredibly well - I applied it at 3:20pm and the base notes were still on my body when I smelled my wrist at 10am the next day. This fragrance is a matured version of the original, which I found unremarkable. Paradoxe Intense isn't particularly interesting or unique, but it is a likeable, rich scent that I'm sure plenty of people will like.

Oh boy, this took me on a ride. The opening I sort of liked. It was super sweet fruity floral and I did quite like the pear. Then the dry down started and it smelled like straight up dirty pleather. This is why you don't blind buy, kids. What a mess this was. Disappointing because I actually really love the bottle design.

everything you hear about Prada Paradoxe is true of its intense variety. I've never gotten more compliments on a perfume than I do with this one; one time a guy on a crowded bus stopped to tell me how nice I smelled while he was walking by. if you want people to compliment your perfume, this is the one. it opens as a very sweet mandarin orange, and dries down into an almost jasmine-y note. it projects like crazy and, to me, smells exactly like the color of the liquid -- that pinky orangey color. I would absolutely recommend trying this one out.

Floral, fresh, a touch fruity. Very jasmine-forward, accentuated with the bitterness of bergamot and just a hint of syrupy pear. As it settles the dankness of the moss comes through; definitely a deeper, darker, more intense version of the original Paradoxe (although the underlying DNA is still present). It’s sweet, but not too sweet.

This came in a sampler kit and I wasn't a huge fan of Paradoxe Eau de Parfum but I sprayed it on to test it and so far I really like it! The pear and vanilla are quite lovely (and I can actually smell the vanilla in this version yay!) and the white florals stay in the back where they're not too overwhelming for me.

I sampled a bunch of popular women’s fragrances recently and this was the scent that really stuck with me. I quickly purchased a full bottle and have been wearing it most days since then. I find this perfume addicting and powerful but without a ton of character.

I recently reported on the regular "Paradoxe | Prada." This beautiful flanker also deserves a review. Moreover, in my opinion, it is rated a bit too low here, but that's a matter of taste. Like the regular Paradoxe, this one clearly goes in an extremely mainstream direction, which personally doesn't bother me.

Prada's Paradoxe is already more of a mass-market fragrance in its original form, one that can be found similarly from other designers. With the new Intense, I had hoped for a mainstream scent with an original twist. To my regret, the fragrance has been "improved" in a worse way. The new Intense is now even sweeter but at the same time much fruitier.

Now for a review of a body spray from Tom Ford, the Noir Extreme. The body sprays from Tom Ford are quite famous. Especially those from the Private Blends, as these are naturally quite pricey in the EdP concentration. So far, I haven't heard much negative about these body sprays, and from my own experiences, I can absolutely recommend them. 150ml body spray is already a great addition and also super for the gym bag or for traveling. Or as a cheaper alternative. As a fan of the Noir Extreme Eau de Parfum and the "Noir Extreme Parfum | Tom Ford," I now have all the variants from this Noir Extreme line. An absolutely wonderful sweet scent that is really well received and is good for a compliment or two. Moreover, this designer line is, in contrast to the Private Blends, quite affordable. In terms of price, this body spray is not cheap at 50€, but you can already get it for around 30€. A price at which you can jump in, especially if you're looking for a little "refreshment" in between. A great alternative to conventional perfumes. With this body spray, you can easily spray yourself, even on clothing. This can says not to spray on the face, eyes, and forearms. I don't quite understand why forearms. However, this spray also works very well on clothing. The packaging is nice and very similar to that of the perfume. This "deo can" doesn't look so great in a beautiful flacon collection; for me, it's more for on-the-go. Overall, this can is quite chic and makes an impression with its black color and golden lettering. There isn't much to report about the scent itself, as it is quite close to that of the EdP. Perhaps it is not quite as rich due to the concentration, but the "original scent" is clearly recognizable. A wonderful gourmand scent with sweet-spicy notes. Cardamom, nutmeg, saffron, kulfi, and vanilla play the main role just like in the EdP. This vanilla-kulfi note is simply wonderful and has something of fresh vanilla pudding. A lovely soft scent that is easy to like. There isn't much development in this scent. This body spray doesn't change much either. It retains that spicy-sweet vanilla-kulfi note. The performance is, of course, significantly worse than the other two perfume variants, but the sillage is still quite good, and you will be noticed. Longevity is absolutely not bad for such a spray, especially on clothing. Overall, a great alternative, especially if you want to smell good for a few hours in everyday life. For special occasions, a great EdP is indispensable. This body spray can also be well combined with the EdP.

For a body spray, the performance is really impressive. Longevity easily 8 hours.... And the sillage is decent as well. Now to the scent. For me, it is a very smooth, slightly spicy/oriental-tinged vanilla fragrance.... Nothing more and nothing less. To be honest, I expected more.... But at 40 euros for 150ml, you can't complain. I will probably test a few more of these body sprays from Tom Ford. The price/performance ratio is really top-notch.

Luna Rossa Extreme was a blind buy. One of those quiet leaps of faith where you trust the instinct, the bottle, the name—and hope it leads somewhere good. It did. And somehow, over time, I’ve come to love it more than I ever expected. It’s so damn dark. Not in a menacing way, but in a way that conjures old velvet, books that have held thoughts for too long, and jackets you find in the back of a closet still whispering the memory of nights out. It creates an aura of lived-in things. Familiar. Ghostly. Beautiful. I had Amber pour Homme Eau de Toilette once—a sweet-clean, powder-smooth kind of elegance that lingered for hours, leaving a soft trail behind me like a perfectly tied scarf. Luna Rossa Extreme isn’t that. It's stranger. A flanker, yes, but it doesn’t behave like one. It stands miles apart from the original Luna Rossa, which sails cleaner seas. This one dives beneath the surface. Some notes echo the original’s DNA, sure, but they’ve been shadowed, thickened, turned sideways. It isn’t extreme in the way you'd expect—it's subtle, it simmers. A quiet kind of intensity. Like the way nightfall doesn't shout, it just happens. I have the EDP. It falls into the oriental-spicy family, but that barely scratches the surface. On first spray, there’s a flash: fresh pepper—sharp, awake—with clove dust and a whisper of licorice, all swirling through a curl of bergamot. For a moment, it smells like the spice drawer in a dream kitchen. Or like a cake that remembers being dangerous. Creepy, dark, a little strange—but mesmerizing. There’s lavender up top, too, curling around the pepper like smoke from a candle that's just gone out. It's modern, yes. Sophisticated, yes. But more than anything, it’s curious. This scent wanders. The dry-down... ah, that's where the real transformation happens. After ten minutes, the harshness fades, and suddenly, it’s smooth. Golden. Amber laced with vanilla, rich and deep, like light pooling at the bottom of a glass of brandy. It gets close to tobacco, but not quite. It wears leather like memory—faded, warm, maybe even animalic, but always tasteful. The soapy undertone—Prada’s signature—is still there, a thread that keeps the entire thing from falling into chaos. It gives structure to the dream. As it wears, it becomes powdery in a way that isn’t cosmetic—it’s more like the scent of skin that’s been somewhere, done something. Not baby powder. Not clean linens. More like an old photograph. Grainy. Faintly sweet. Very human. To me, it’s elegant and masculine in a way that doesn’t try too hard.
