Casual, but in a cashmere and candlelight kind of way. It feels made for evenings—chilly air, dark wood, breath turning visible in the cold. Fall and winter suit it perfectly. And though other notes exist, it’s the pepper that frames them all. Pepper on the top, pepper in the air, pepper in the spaces between the notes. Like a ghost of spice haunting the whole thing. This one lasts. Eight, ten hours, sometimes more. I wore it last night, and I still smelled it in the fibers of my coat this morning—soft but unmistakable. People notice. Compliments come without asking. There's something magnetic in its blend—something that invites and lingers, like someone who doesn’t say much, but always leaves a trace. Luna Rossa Extreme is more than a flanker. It’s a dream stitched together with spice and shadow, drifting on skin like a secret you don’t need to tell. — Elysium

Bold, manly, bear-like. There’s a sticky- sweaty armpit quality (not necessarily a man’s pit) throughout that is honestly kinda charming like the rosewood in Alexandria II. I love that designers used to hit you with edt intenses and extremes rather early on in the flanker series. Y’know really flesh out the story while it’s still fresh before doing spin offs. Having the gift of retrospect I’d say Prada had the conversation long ago of developing androgynous perfumes like ocean and sport so LRE would conflict with that. Rn it’s going for babycat prices and it’s just not worth it. The DNA is undeniably there though so if you’re a purebred Prada boi then where else are you going to drop coin to get this? The Juniper is the best part of this to me, it’s sparkly like in journey man. Paired with LRS facial moisturizer the sandalwood really comes out and is rubber butter too. It’s sexy, it’s memorable, and it was a moment. Now give the waves a rest.

This is one which is an all round pleasant experience. I get pepper, lavender and vanilla, with a hint of florals in the background. It's traditionally masculine but I can't see why it wouldn't be suitable for a woman as well. It reminds me of other fragrances with a lavender and vanilla combination. The addition of pepper and spices also serves to make the fragrance a little different in it's approach. I do like it, and would wear it from time to time. I have been impressed so far with the fragrances I have tried from Prada. This one is no exception.

Luna Rossa is my signature, so I was very much looking forward to this one. But it doesn't have the "magic" the original had for me. I'm not talking longevity or sillage, just the scent itself. Extreme starts off with peppery lavender. The lavender is also the only note that it shares with the original Luna Rossa. Anyways, off the bat it reminded me a lot of L'Occitan by L'Occitane En Provence, which is also peppery lavender. But as it dries down, the Luna Rossa vibe comes through, as well as some sweetness from the juniper berries (and vanilla, but I can't isolate that note). It becomes this amber-y sweet-spicy lavender in the end. When people said that Luna Rossa was "nothing special", I never understood that because it worked so well with my skin. With the Extreme however, I completely understand! It just doesn't do anything for me. Truth be told, I did find the combination of lavender with both pepper and sweet notes pretty weird while reading about this scent before I tried it. I guess I'll have to stick with one or the other instead of mixing them. Also, despite it being called Extreme, it doesn't seem to have a bigger longevity or sillage on me... Overall, it's a nice scent, but I'm not putting it on my buy list.

I'm always surprised when a flanker tickles my fancy … not that Luna Rossa Extreme is much to write home about, but it does surpass its predecessor. Astoundingly, this very 'so so' creation comes from the nose who created the INDREDIBLE Infusion d'Homme, which, it must be said, took me quite a while to become enamored of. I think that once I'd started understanding what the Infusion collection was all about, coupled with a love for Neroli and Iris based frags, I was able to choose a couple that worked for me and I enjoyed wearing. Luna Rossa was a big disappointment, but the extreme version does have a couple of redeeming qualities. Firstly, the longevity seems amped up sufficiently … a pity that the same cannot be said of the sillage. Having said that, I was always under the impression that the projection of my beloved Infusion d'Homme was also relatively sketchy … but it proved itself not to be on numerous occasions. I may be wrong … I'm not always a very good judge of my fragrance wake!! Luna Rossa Extreme is mostly all about the classic base combination of Lavender and Vanilla. There is a slightly boozy quality from the Juniper while the mystery of Labdanum is more like a spoiler alert and the Pepper up top quite indistinguishable from many similar men's offerings of late. The base is nice … but I prefer to get my Lav/Van kicks from ELDO's Antihero's. This one would be an unnecessary addition to my collection (I'll stick with my favorite Infusions from Prada), but I am sure many will like it.

At least on me... what I get is black pepper, amber, a slight lavender - and not much else. No vanilla vibes getting through on me. It's very spicy and almost leathery, but not very soapy IMO. Thanks, but not for me. Love the bottle though !!

Recently, the new releases from mainstream brands have really come under fire. Especially the so-called flankers. No wonder - as consumers, we have a strong suspicion of being seen more and more as cash cows, to whom any weak fragrance can be sold, as long as the brand and the packaging or bottle are right.

I have worn and tested Luna Rossa Extreme several times without owning it. The reason for this is that my brother owns this fragrance. I find the Luna Rossa line, including all the flankers, very interesting. The original is rather unremarkable. The flankers Carbon, Sport, and this Extreme are really well done and special in their own way.

Anyone who has been involved with Parfumo for a while knows that the community experience often follows a similar path. Sometimes you buy way too many samples, then you discover sharing options and swaps, and before you know it, your cabinet is way too full. I speak from experience (as a quick glance at my folder "Samples" reveals).

After I really liked Luna Rossa, unlike many others here, I of course had to test Luna Rossa Extreme around this time last year. A classic case of expectations being clearly different from reality... just like in normal life... I had expected a more intense version... similar to Terre EDT/EDP. At that time, I was very disappointed... because that was not the case...

A niche fragrance hidden in a designer bottle, a true surprise from Prada in 2024. It opens with a burst of refreshing lemon, awakening the senses. At its heart, saffron adds a spicy richness, giving the perfume depth and character. The drydown reveals the best part—an ambered, woody scent crafted from smoky oakwood and Amber Xtreme molecules. In short, it’s a harmonious blend of freshness, elegance, and sensuality in a bottle. With a lasting power of around 10 hours and an exceptional projection of 4 hours, this fragrance leaves a striking and memorable impression.

For me this is an fragrance that really got messed up in the process. The initial opening to this is an citrus bomb, you can literally not smell anything else and its just too much. When you let it dry down you get this sweet feeling to it with the saffron combined with the lemon notes. Overall this is an good fragrance if you can just overlook the initial opening.

It’s fresh and sweet but has some dark woods. Reminds me of those Cuban cigar colognes from back in the day, but way better quality. It’s Prada so it still has that clean soapy touch to it. Not like Prada Lhomme soapy, but just fresh smelling with woods and sweet citrusy and saffron? (I’m not gonna act like I can decipher each note) Idk I’m going based off what’s listed. I get a sweet, citrusy, woody yet fresh tobacco like fragrance and it just works for me. Now when I say tobacco I don’t mean like spicebomb red. It actually doesn’t remind me of any of the similar fragrances listed. Maybe Layton but hardly. Like I said it reminds me of the Cuban cigar colognes. I love it. Works great in cold weather but can wear during summer nights also. I wore this to work (hospital) and got 3 Compliments. I feel like if I can wear a fragrance to a hospital and nobody complain, then I can wear this anywhere anytime. Hope this helps

Purchased from : N/A Price : N/A Method : sampler vial sprayed onto right arm Ok y'all. This was given to me by a generous salesman at Dillard's. I purchased a SpiceBomb sampler set and he threw in half a dozen samples without a single word from me. He was my hero for the evening, because I love trying new scents. This is going to be my first time ever smelling this. I've not even tested it at the store. Let's snap open the package here and pull out the tester. I'm going to just free-type this. The open reminds me of Cuba, instantly. So much lavender and tobacco. Man it's Cuba all the way. Lavender, honey, ylang-ylang, tobacco, vanilla...oh, now leaning sort of A*Men-ish? Am I getting chocolate-caramel-peppermint here?? Very much so. Okay, now this is A*Men, essentially, or rather Cuba's version of it. Like a cleaner, louder, slightly more assembled Cuba Prestige. Maybe that IS "A*Men". Haha. Projection BEAST alert!! I'm getting huge jump from this one off the skin. Approach and about 5" away you have to back up. After 3 minutes on the skin it's giving me some patchouli, mandarin orange, ruby red grapefruit, and damp moss in exchange for some of the volume of the earlier notes. It gets more aligned but more complex. Note this is still smelling like a Cuba frag. (If anything that tells you how crazy good and unique they are for what they cost, Prada is imitating this age-old company). I honestly don't get any of the listed notes, scrolling up. I got what I got, not going to erase a thing. The full dry-down gives me more Prada Ocean signature notes and has a sparkly, moving, quality about it. I am finally getting some of the sweet lemon, but that's the only note listed above that I can perceive. Besides the massive Cuba Prestige/A*Men vibes I get, my experience reflects exactly opposite of what's listed for top, middle, base notes, if you can puzzle it together that way. The warm notes come first, and the bright notes come last. Did they change it? I can't appropriately rate the longevity YET but I can only tell you it's probably going to be great because of how huge it is right now. I'll update the score when it fades. Overall this seems like a pretty awesome A*Men substitute and pulls a lot from Cuba frags. That'll make some of you mad but I don't care, this is what I've got going on right here. Considering the influences, and how freely you can get these notes from other far less expensive colognes, it's probably not worth its price. Still not a bad scent, I'll gladly wear the rest of the vial.

A round and striking amber-woody citrus scent. Everyone likes this, and no one who smells it will dislike it. In my opinion, it's a must-have if you want to get started with perfumes a little more complex than a supermarket cologne and load up on a bottle of Axe Dark Temptation every time you go out to dinner, have a drink, or go to work with people around you indoors. Very masculine and perfectly wearable if you already have at least a teeny mustache.. Of course, as soon as the thermometer starts to rise above X temperature, it's time to moderate. If you're going with 10 sprays as a base, then stick to 2 when it's hot, and that's great, because you can made it flexible and for every occasion

…mostly yes! If I had to compare the new fragrance from Prada, I would say it is very much reminiscent of Luna Rossa Ocean Eau de Toilette . In some moments, especially in the transition from top to heart notes, I can also clearly see parallels to Luna Rossa Sport .

Prada has done it again. I must say that some Prada fragrances hold a special place in my heart for various reasons. I'll focus on the Luna Rossa line: I love Luna Rossa Black because it sends a very masculine, spicy pepper-vanilla scent into my nose for hours. (Isn’t it supposed to be short-lived? I perceive the sillage on myself for several hours!

Such a beautiful composition. In my opinion, it is the best-created masterpiece from Prada, right alongside Prada L' Homme Intense. Spicy sweet, it reminds me of a blend of Bleu de Chanel and Ambre Nuit by Dior.

Luna Rossa Ocean Le Parfum the big brother of the Prada Ocean series. Is he also a good big brother? For me, the Luna Rossa Ocean Le Parfum was the only one in the Ocean line that convinced me to make a purchase.

At first, I didn't like this perfume, but I gave it a second chance and it made the most of it. It is a warm, woody scent with fresh, citrus, spicy, and sweet elements. It starts off fresh and citrusy with lemon. On my skin, it initially smells like window cleaner, but (thankfully) that doesn't last long.

~ Inspiration ~ While browsing through the Victoria's Secret fragrances, I also came across "Forbidden Fantasy" and received a sample from Delicia. ~ Bottle ~ The design in turquoise and dark purple evokes associations of underwater for me. ~ Scent ~ My first impression was melon! I was all the more surprised to learn that there is supposedly none in it? In any case, this combination of passion fruit (maracuja) and jasmine smells like melon to me :) ~ Longevity ~ On my skin, it lasts only 1-2 hours (on clothes and hair not much longer). You can comfortably use several sprays, as it is a fleeting body spray and therefore not very intense. ~ Occasion ~ It fits well into the warmer and hot days of spring and summer (also suitable for the office, although I find the longevity too weak for that). ~ Conclusion ~ I was surprised by the slightly green-aquatic melon note, yet I quite like the light, fruity scent for an occasional spritz.

Orange Blossom, for me personally, tends to remind me of soap and bath products. Occasionally this flower sits well with me, yet other times I crave that little something more. Something not so clean. Infusion de Fleur d'Oranger is simplistic yet beautiful. The soapy accord is most certainly present, however it gives me a sense of being clean yet sweet and flowery at the same time. If I were to bathe in a tub filled with petals, and the aroma of the bath water soaked into my skin, this fragrance is what I'd imagine I would smell like. It's a really fun, warm weather scent, light and inoffensive on the skin. It opens with zesty bursts of neroli, mandarin orange and a hint soapiness. The heart is mostly floral and a touch sweet, with a slight drizzle of honey. I find Infusion de Fleur d'Oranger such a well balanced composition. It's neither too heavy nor too light. It's just right. I actually wore this fragrance to bed last night, and my boyfriend complimented me, however it did take him some time to realise it was a perfume and not the scent of my freshly washed sheets. The longevity is good on my skin, and the more I wear this fragrance the more excited I am for the season turn-around, where light, Spring-like florals will soon dominate my wardrobe. This fragrance met all my expectations and for that, I'm very pleased.

I remember when buying this one; I thought it was wonderful, - light, fresh, summery. I still have these impressions, but when I wear it, I find it almost cloying. A small sprits on my wrists takes my full attention for most of the rest of the day, and it is simply too much. It is not the sweetness, I think. When compared to SLs orangeblossom, the latter is even sweeter, but I do not have the same reaction to that one. Maybe the Prada lacks something in depth? I've worn it only in spring/summer/autumn - maybe I should try in cold weather (Seville is by far best on me in winter!) So, you see, mixed feelings on this one.

This has a nice refreshing citric bitterness from the neroli and Orange Blossoms that has a fuzzy cloudy texture on top of a base of dirty jasmine and tubereuse that has a bit of a slight sewage/ animalic smell. But it doesn't get too skanky as the sweetness and tartness of the top notes balance it out. I like it. Don't love it. Edit. I love this now. It has a lovely cotton soft dry down from the Jasmine that's so gorgeous and plush.

My first impression was very pleasant, light and refreshing. Unfortunately, the drydown exposes the soapy angles of orange (in this case, I'd say of orange peel) and the scent seemed too bitter on my skin, whereas my daughter (20) loved this very aspect. Thus I happily gave her my bottle - so much about different perceptions. "Infusion de Fleur d'Oranger" is a good summer fragrance for those who like the whole spectrum of the orange to be represented in a perfume. Its good breeding (I like the packaging&the bottle design) places it well above the usual clamour of many other light citrussy summer scents. Btw, we couldn't detect any tuberose in it (as mentioned in the pyramide).

Very nice scent. Tuberose stays in the background, thank goodness, and doesn’t act up as it often does. But I find the sweetness of the orange flower moves into a kind of tartness - like the spray of orange peel into the flame of a candle. All in all I quite like it.

I love the Prada Infusions, in general, so it's no surprise that I like this one, in particular. INFUSION DE FLEUR D'ORANGER offers a clean, somewhat soapy orange blossom with a definite family resemblance to the INFUSIONS D'IRIS but also the soap note of INFUSION D'HOMME.

Orange blossom is a flower that one usually associates with light and airy summer compositions. However, sometimes these gentle flowers could grow in a full-fledged cooler month note. The latter happened in Prada Infusion de Fleur d’Oranger - a relaunched version of the original Infusion de Fleur d’Oranger.

I am currently on the hunt for the perfect clean orange blossom perfume. Reviewing based off of a sample and in store testing so I don't have an intimate knowledge of the scent but this can be treated as a first impression review. This is a charming and cheery orang creamsicle type of scent. I wasn't expecting for it to be so powdery and that surprised me on first spray.

The opening feels a bit pungent and sharp, but it calms down soon enough. Then we get some lovely orange blossom. It feels quite clean, almost soapy, with neat undertones of musk. But that's just about it. I do like orange blossom quite a bit, but nevertheless I find myself underwhelmed.

November is the epitome of a gloomy and dark time that regularly weighs on the mood. And even though, as has happened more frequently in recent years, sunny and mild days break through this gray, the numerous days of remembrance and the grave decorations found everywhere in stores signal that the light and cheer of summer are a thing of the past.

Infusion d´Iris Absolue is not a higher concentration of the eau de toilette, as i thought. Since i love orris fragances i like both of them, but i can imagine someone loving one and totally disliking other because the moods are, if not opposite, very different. The eau de toilette is cool, green and dewy, very spring-like. The absolue is more oriental, warm and enveloping. I would say they just share the iris. The way it starts is very much my cup of tea. bitter, rooty iris, probably enhanced with carrot seed. Rich and thick. The neroli is not so evident, but it gives off a freshness that you notice when its gone. Same happens with the orange blossom. It never steals the attention from the orris, but the concoction is dense, bitter and has an oily floral edge. As the fragance evolves the iris is more powdery and, definitely, polished, but still veers to the bitter and the vigourous. Mastic resin and benzoin are quite noticeable, making the Absolue a resinous, balmy take on iris. I catch a bitter almond-like whiff too. So far i love it. Vanilla and tonka make some sort of inflexion in the developement of the fragance. It gets sweeter, the bitterness and resinous quality fade. When this happens i find the fragance more, hmm, average, and i loose interest. Is like the sweetness from the vanilla kind of neutralizes what i found thrilling in this "infusion", not completely though. Truth is that the more it stays on the skin the more sheer and "pleasant" it turns. It becomes a comforting, safe scent on one hand, that still smells good. But on the other i find it uninspiring, older and, well, boring. I appreciate the drydown is still about iris, but is so powdery and ambery and tame that makes me wonder if it is the same perfume i sprayed. Still i come back to it sometimes, because the first couple hours i enjoy it very much: the orris is very intense and the warmer approach to it makes it suitable for colder days.
Take Infusion d'Iris edp & add Benzoin Oppoponax (Manoa from Memo) A bit of mastica Concentrated vanilla (vintage Shalimar) Very very nice.

Rock solid performer from Prada, better than the original Infusion to my mind. There's something Chanelesque about the way it wafts and wends its way around you and the mistake would be to think you could wear it every day, where I fear you would become a little anosmic. I qualify that by saying that the longevity is not as durable as the original and as others have noted the carrot goes before the stick, the iris (carroty orris butter) fades quickly to the golden benzoin afterglow. It's quite a romantic little number though and the acid test is whether or not you reach for it when pushed for time. I confess that I do and I that I have a back up. I have bath salts in the original Infusion D'Iris and a new bath, one of those Victoria and Albert ones that I have waited to be a grand old age to own, after a lifetime of acrylic monstrosities. Add Iris in all its forms to create the most luxurious bathing experience followed by Man style pyjamas, a dressing gown with a braid revere and softly scented breath on skin. I didn't say whose.

This bizarre naming trend, adding misleading adjectives and nouns such as "essence" and "absolue" to the names of successfully launched perfumes, generates lots of dashed expectations, as there does not seem to be a lot of attention being given to the meanings of the words being attached by marketers casting about desperately to generate names as quickly as new perfumes are being launched. One might have thought, for example, that the "absolue" of a perfume would be its extrait. Not so, in the case of Prada INFUSION D'IRIS ABSOLUE, which is not just a stronger version of INFUSION D'IRIS--no, not by a long shot. As someone who has managed (unbelievably enough) to drain an entire 200 ml bottle of Prada INFUSION d'IRIS edp and is making inroads into an even bigger jug of the stuff, I feel eminently qualified to pronounce on the difference between the latest Prada Infusion in the line-up, INFUSION D'IRIS ABSOLUE, and its namesake. First off, it is different. Those who detect no difference between the two compositions are probably working from memory. Yes, they are more similar than either is to, say, CHANEL NO 5. But they are distinct compositions, without a doubt. My initial impression upon applying ABSOLUE was that this version was quite a bit more resinous than the original, what I see borne out in the hierarchy of notes above, where not only benzoin but also "mastic resin" is listed. This version also seems sweeter and inches in the direction of Guerlain L'INSTANT. It also conjures up in my mind memories of Kenzo FLOWER. One review mentions the Prada baby oil accord and, yes, I'd have to agree that it is much more pronounced in this version. The biggest effect of the increased resin content is that ABSOLUE seems less clean and airy than either the eau de parfum or the eau de toilette, and also less green. The resins start to get just a bit gunky on me in the drydown, something that never happens with any other of the INFUSIONS. In fact, my favorite part of the entire series, the original, the eau de toilette, INFUSION D'HOMME, INFUSION DE VETIVER, INFUSION DE FLEUR D'ORANGER, and INFUSION DE TUBEREUSE, is the slightly soapy or clean edge in all of them. The only one which I do not own and have not tried is INFUSION DE ROSE, which I have never seen for sale anywhere! All of the previous members of this series familiar to me are not too sweet nor do they have any dirtiness whatsoever, which makes them boring to some reviewers. For them, the ABSOLUE may be a welcome change. As for me, I'll stick with what I know.

It has taken me two full days of wearing this, before I could write this review. I bought this fragrance blind, but had a brief sample sniff of the regular Infusion D'Iris from a friend. I was really looking forward to this fragrance, as wanted something floral, but a bit powdery for Spring. With the first few minutes, upon spraying, I was taken aback with an almost metallic, leathery note. Not very pleasant, but gratefully didn't linger too long. Then the nice notes started coming to the surface, a soft orange, and the lovely soft iris flower. This is when the powdery vibe kicks in). The drydown, for me anyway, is the greatest part of all. A lovely vanilla, drifting in and out amongst the floral. But, here is the disappointment. Not much lasting power at all. I do have a problem with lots of perfume no lasting a long time on my skin, unless it's a real power house scent), but this is too damn short. Projection is slight. Had to ask several family members if they could smell it. My son did, . only when I asked him to sniff my wrist, and neck. His comment was, "It's nice, but pretty old fashioned", They are more used to me wearing bold perfumes)So, all in all, I like it, after the first few minutes fades inwards, would wear it a lot, especially during the day, and a good workplace fragrance...but staying power is quite short, and don't think it has much of a sillage at all. A close to the skin scent, for sure. Also, a bit pricey, due to the short lasting power.

Dry iris, scrubbing iris, smoked iris. Iris raised to the power of two, no, of four... But after three hours, ovation please, burlesque queen Vanilla is coming! She's still slightly high after yesterday's party, but she did not forget to powder her nose ... and at that moment I fell in love.

Where the original is watery, cool, and crisp/bitter, the Absolue is rich, sweet, and warm. The iris is also much more evident to my nose in the Absolue version than in the original - it is rooty, thick, and almost bready.

This has the same lush powdery fuzziness that envelopes you as Prada Amande. This lacks the spicy top of Amande which also has a lovely soft fresh cotton musk dry down. This is more golden Ambery and Vanillic and a little less sweet. This leans more Resinous, Creamy and buttery with hints of caramel.

I am Infusion Iris fan, from the beginning when it came out until now.. i have odp and had odt and absolu More i have cedre/homme, amande, rose Plus i have their special edition from 2007 Iris N1 30 ml perfume(More oriental but still very Infusion iris odp) There is same dna as infusion iris odp but this one has something that bothered me. I gave it away.

If you were an instrument, then a viola. If you were a piece of music, then a nocturne. If you were a painting, then one by Modigliani. If you were a medium, then a handwritten love letter. If you were a fabric, then a heavy velvet. If you were a color, then a muted, matte gold. If you were a time of day, then the late afternoon.

A mature aromatic-balsamic fragrance for confident men. Strong patchouli with a green bergamot starting notes may seem 'oldish' to some people but the drydown after worth waiting for... You will be rewarded with a delightful oriental aura, not too strong, but smooth, warm and distinct, because the amber/myrrh/vanilla combination is doing a really great job here. Nothing harsh, slightly soapy, overall a sexy long-lasting and inviting smell for fall/winter seasons. My personal rank 9/10, recommended.

Prada Amber Pour Homme Intense takes a different angle on it's older brother, Prada Amber Pour Homme. It's sophisticated, elegant and seducting scent blended with the highest quality ingredients. It was born from Daniela Andrier passion, closed in the sleek black bottle with shining golden Prada logo. Original Amber Pour Homme is a really clean eau de toilette that brings wearer a feeling of just taking a shower. It's very classy and definitely not for everyone. Prada Amber Pour Homme is a little bit different story. All begins with a bergamot note that goes deep inside your nose. Just a minute later this perfume begins to effuse it's true identity, the mysterious, dark, yet alluring aura. Amber, Myrrh and Patchouli that are very prominent describe the men that knows what he wants and knows how to get it. When I close my eyes and smell Prada Amber Pour Homme I imagine a man with a nice tailored suit. This fragrance is a definition of luxury and good taste. This Prada is an eau de parfum which is not so common in male perfumery. It lasts all day on my skin, the vanilla accord accompanies me to the very end of the day. On the other hand this eau de parfum is strong and subtle at the same time, as it stays rather close to the skin. If you're looking for perfume that definitely gets some attention and smells like "wow" Prada Amber Pour Homme Intense is definitely for you. It's uncomparable to anything else on the market at this moment. Truly beautifull and unique creation!

Darker and heavier than Prada Amber, this intense version smells wonderful. One of the best designer's release in my opinion. It's a bit linear, with lots of patchouli and a bit resinous due to the myrrh. It's sweet in the right amount. Actually there's a bit more of amber added here, but still not a true amber based scent. Sillage, lasting power and projection are medium-high. Thumbs up! Updated January 2014

It is an Awesome Fragrance, A Modern perfume with the shadow of classic style and well-blended composition , similar to niche High Quality scent. This is Elegant, Classy, Sophisticated and Complex. It opens up with a bit soapy zesty , warm spicy, balsamic and resin notes in the background then dry down is slightly sweet, smoky, dark green ambery , It is not strong but it is soft, smooth and clean. The Myrrh, Patchouli and Amber notes are dominant in this fragrance. The art of bottle design with the plate of notes is very wonderful. This is perfect for the fall and winter, l'm so happy that I have it in my collection, I really enjoy it and I love it. Longevity is very good, In my opinion Prada Amber Pour Homme Intense EDP is a MASTERPIECE, Highly Recommended. Two Thumbs Up. Bravo Prada ! Rating : 9. 5 / 10

This is my first wearing and successful blind buy of Prada Amber Pour Homme Intense, the 2011 flanker to the original 2006 Prada Amber Pour Homme, which I only just tried for the first time last week and loved, and Intense is similarly very nice. Whereas the original is more of a soapy fresh amber, Intense is slightly spicier, albeit still fresh, but less soapy. Intense’s note listing is relatively straightforward: bergamot, myrrh, vanilla, patchouli, amber. I frankly get a bit of the champagne fresh spicy cologne vibe of YSL Rive Gauche with some of the darkness of Armani Attitude, and I sense some lavender without it being there, though perhaps I’m just smelling the bergamot and patchouli. Like the original, it’s not an amber fragrance in the sense that it’s especially sweet or thick or animalic, but has an amber base with some other additives. Intense has a good balance of resins quirks—namely, some spice and some smoke—with just a hint of sweetness, to complement the fresh and green vibe of the bergamot and patchouli. Like the original, Intense is very reasonably priced on the secondary market, about $65 for 100ml on FragranceNet, and it performs decently well, though the original perhaps performs better, despite the greater concentration of Intense (EDP, to the original’s EDT). Overall, I’d say that I prefer the original but enjoy the Intense as a darker, slightly spicier variation. 7 out of 10

Prada is my favourite designer house because of top level of perfumery like this. Sweet vanilla, myrrh, amber & patchouli with a gourmand chocolate drydown. Clean, soapy, spicy, masculine, sophisticated, rich and complex, very similar to the original but much darker. A beautifully blended true masterpiece, Prada at their best.

I'm not one to seek out fragrances designed specifically for men, because in my experience they're usually too masculine for my taste, often at the hand of some domineering bergamot. So, had I read the list of notes beforehand, I would've probably declined an offer to sample this one out of hand.

First, there is a hit of sweetness for just a short period of time. Then depending on weather, you can feel what I like to call wet patchouli notes, so sweetness goes away and you are left with a wet basement, wet soil, definitely on a darker side. It is the first ride.

OK, I'm gonna keep this short : PAPHI is a rich, dark and warm balsamic scent, especially good for colder weather. Two things make it less appealing to me though : First of all, even though as an EdP the longevity is great (8-12 hours easily), the sillage is rather low and after wearing it maybe 15 times, no one has ever complimented on it.

The only Prada I have managed to review thus far. This one was a blind buy from a couple of years ago based on it's good price, critical reviews, and note descriptions that appealed to me. Successful? Hope you enjoy the review and thank you for watching.

The name of Prada L'EAU AMBREE makes it sound like a watery solution or cologne strength version of an amber perfume, but to my nose this composition seems more like a thin golden veil. The amber is not animalic at all, and there is a slight touch of the Prada house soap note, almost as a sort of identifying mark or scent print. This is a very subtle composition, with extremely light and quite fleeting citrus in the opening followed by the veil of amber. The rose and patchouli are not at all heavy and, to be honest, barely detectable. But all of this is by design. Daniela Andrier appears to have set out to create the world's lightest amber, and I do believe that she succeeded! People who enjoy thick, viscous golden amber with an olfactory texture similar to caramel, or those who like the metal mesh effect of ambergris perfumes, may be disappointed with this creation. I however like it. L'EAU AMBREE is elegant, sleek and clean, and not sweet, despite the vanilla listed among the notes. Because of all of these features, this composition is perfect to put on after a bath and before going to sleep, and may induce in the wearer regal dreams! The bottle is the same gorgeous one used for PRADA and PRADA TENDRE with the glass thickness varying along the bottom, and a metal plate on the top, with the primary notes of the composition embossed. I now own both the regular and the bulb atomizer version. In a gift set, I also received bath gel, body lotion, and scented dusting powder with a charming powder puff. The powder smells splendid. The first time I reviewed this perfume, I was basically on Miss K's page (see below). Since then I have come to appreciate the subtle virtues of this noble creation.

A perfect summer oriental. Perfect in the sense of being elegant, refined and soft. This has been on my testlist for a long long time and I must say (as a niche devotee) I am perfectly happy to have it in my collection. L'Eau Ambrée has that typical Prada high class touch and it is now my favourite of the house.

L'Eau Ambree is on my wish list. The first spray is a harsh and jarring very short lived note of citrus. For me that note fades quickly within a minute or so. Thereafter lots of muskiness and patchouli and herbs. I get an odd undercurrent of something earthy that smells of dusty rocks or the crypt in an old stone church. Very soon after it becomes very powdery and sweet for me. The ghost of insense comes to mind also - that may be the 'opopanax' note that refers to sweet myrrh (I had to google that one...). Fades to smooth powderiness. But fades really quickly for me. A beautiful and complex scent for a winter's eve.

Prada L'eau Ambree didn't start off too well with me. I had first sprayed this on a card, smelt nothing. I then applied to my skin, still nothing. I even sprayed into the air around me, absolutely nothing. I honestly could not smell a thing, and my nose is very sensitive. I was wondering how on earth I could write a review when I couldn't even tell you what it smelt like. Thankfully I could begin to smell a subtle hint of citrus and patchouli after an hour had passed. Well, this fragrance is certainly not loud or offensive. It is extremely intimate and very subtle. Unfortunately it tends to vanish on the skin quite quickly. So the moment it appears, it's gone again. Throughout the duration of this scent, all I had managed to detect was the patchouli, the citruses, soft amber and delicate, powdery vanilla. I concluded that Prada L'eau Ambree smelt very much like an expensive bar of soap. Very clean and feminine. This fragrance was certainly not unpleasant, however it was disappointing due to all the hype surrounding it. I much prefer the original Prada as a unique and characteristic fix for my amber cravings.

I love perfumes with balsamic and vanilla main accords that carry a good amount of sweetness, and if they have depth and facets, I love them even more. Prada L'Eau Ambree falls into this category. I am usually not much of a patchouli woman, but here it is blended in so beautifully, that it enriches the facet aspect of this fragrance in a very interesting and delightful way. Sometimes sweet fragrances can be boring, just because they are nice and sweet, but don't add much else to the stimuli. Not so with L'Eau Ambree. This is a scent that keeps me entertained long after the initial spray, when so many other sweet fragrances lose their draw for me. It is deep enough for the evening and light enough for the daytime. I will be wearing this lady quite a lot for sure.

Amazing how noses can perceive fragrances differently. To my nose, this has no citrus fruits or lemon at all. But it has loads of the other notes mentioned and this makes a delicious cocktail, so warm, spicy and enduring that it has my interest and respect. I love to wear it. The warmth of the fragrance is outstanding.

No scent has made me as giddy as this one. I don't know much about Prada and have never paid attention to it. What a mistake. Now I'm sitting here trying to collect myself. For two hours I've been running around like counterfeit money, messing everything up. Of course, it's L'Eau Ambrée to blame, which I must have right now, or I'll die.*gg* What is there to say?

This Prada is different from other fragrances; it takes some getting used to at first. It is not a classic fresh lemon scent that one could guess from the top notes. The lemon is creamy, balsamic, elegant. Opoponax, patchouli, and amber transform the citrus notes into an extravagant fragrance that smells elegant, warm, and expensive.

At the beginning I would like to say that I'm not a big fan of this powdery/lipstick iris vibe of L'homme line. But every single scent in this line is amazingly done and I enjoy smelling them from time to time. Often flankers are a pleasant alternatives to their original brother. But sometimes there are flankers like A*men Ultimate, which completely lost the DNA of original A*men and sometimes there are flankers that are even too similar to their predecessor. And that's what Prada L'homme Water Splash is. My question is: Why Prada made a scent that is exactly the same as L'homme L'eau released 2 years before? Or should I ask, what is the reason to buy L'homme L'eau when Water Splash does exactly the same but at a cheaper price? I know that maybe I'm overreacting, but in my honest opinion, L'homme line of Prada became a little bit boring by this time. I hope that in the future they would give us something more interesting and slightly different in this line. Nevertheless it is a very solid spring/summer clean scent, don't get me wrong

I am a big fan of the Prada L'Homme line. I owned and loved the original, wearing about half of a 100ml bottle until it tragically tumbled from my shelf and broke, making my room smell luxuriously clean and powdery for a long while afterwards. I have tried L'Homme Intense on a number of occasions and plan on purchasing it at some point. But it was Water Splash which drew my eye when I was on the hunt for a new grabber for the warm weather. I won't deny that 90% of my reasoning for picking this one up was the bottle, which is super dope. The remaining 10% was because of my love for the original, and because I managed to grab a 5.1oz bottle for ~$50, give or take. It is no surprise that I love this one, given my affection for the original and for iris fragrances in general, and I think that if you like iris or the original Prada L'Homme, this is a safe blind buy. I haven't smelt Prada L'Homme L'Eau, so I can't speak to its similarities with Water Splash, but suffice it to say that most of the fragrances in the line are variations on one another, except for Intense. Anyway, Water Splash has that smooth, warm, clean, soapy vibe of the original, but freshened up. I'd say the primary difference between this one and the original are: this one has a more lipsticky iris vibe à la Dior Homme in the opening which was absent in the original; there is ginger, coupled with citrus (not listed), that provides a bit of zing; and the Mandarin leaf/petitgrain gives this a greener, more bitter, and more herbal vibe. If the OG Prada L'Homme was orientated towards the office and indoor spaces, Water Splash feels airier and more outdoorsy. Mind you, this is not some frontier adventure sort of scent. This takes me to a terrace of an Italian villa where you relax languidly in a wicker chair beneath the shade of orange trees in your oatmeal linen Mao collar shirt, bermudas, and jute espadrilles. The indoors is not very far away, and with the stirring of the breeze you occasionally feel a waft of cool ACified air from the open French doors leading out onto the terrazza. You thought that you had turn the maid to turn it off when the doors were open, but oh well, you have money to spare. There is a laid back, relaxed vibe about Water Splash, whereas the original was a bit more buttoned up. Both are pretty versatile scents, though, and well suited to warmer weather. Water Splash is just even more suited to warmer weather. The drydown goes deliciously creamy and luscious, a warm, cozy, and inviting skin scent that lasts for a good while. Performance is not amazing, but better than you might think. 5-6 sprays last me for about 6-7 hours, especially if you spray on clothes. The projection is always moderate, but detectable, and keeps up for around an hour before dying down to the skin. This isn't, and was never intended to be, a beast mode kind of a scent, so I'm fine with that performance. This is intended for relaxing around the house or running errands on a warm summer's day, and should be just enough to last you until night falls, and you spray something else on before quitting your luxurious villa and going out for a night on the achingly beautiful Tyrrhenian seaside town. Overall I'm quite pleased with my purchase of Water Splash, and will be wearing it often in the upcoming summer. This is exactly the kind of vibe I like to give off: calm, cool, clean, elegant, relaxed, cozy, and inviting. I think it's easily unisex too. Wear this with white linen and an air of sprezzatura and you'll be golden. I might not be a relentlessly handsome Italian stallion that summers along the Mediterranean coast, but by god I can pretend to be. 8.5 beige linen suits/10

First, a brief but necessary digression. Fragrance notes and scent pyramids are a minefield. We read: There is ginger in it. So we search for the ginger until we find it. Whether it is actually present or not (this could probably only be partially determined in a lab). Sometimes, however, it can be the other way around: We smell something that apparently isn’t included. A prominent example: Layton Exclusif. Until a correction suggestion based on the official manufacturer’s site, everyone probably thought that the fragrance contained the notes of civet and oud. (Allegedly) Not at all! The "animalic" note that even my amateur nose thought it detected is (allegedly) not present. A quick comparison of the scent pyramids of Parfums de Marly fragrances with those from the manufacturer revealed: Almost all of them would need to be revised, and thousands of perfumers and perfume enthusiasts have sniffed out "things" that are (allegedly) not included. Psychological science offers numerous explanatory models for this collectively misguided olfaction. But perhaps the problem also lies on the other (manufacturer) side. Why this introduction? For two reasons. On one hand, because this observation has generally made me cautious regarding fragrance notes, and I have come to the conclusion: The scent pyramids of manufacturers are likely heavily driven by marketing and may even be adjusted afterwards - one should primarily trust one’s own nose and those of other "end consumers." I also no longer believe anyone who claims they can "roughly imagine the real scent" based on a scent pyramid, no matter how many thousands of fragrances they have already tested. A fragrance is more than the sum of its notes - and one apparently cannot always rely on the stated ones. On the other hand, looking at the fragrance notes - to finally talk about Water Splash - one might suspect that this L’Homme flanker is entirely different from the original, which has already ascended to classic status. Because: They only share neroli and cedarwood. But: Any nose that hasn’t been blocked can spontaneously sniff out at three in the morning, even when abruptly awakened, that these are two very, very closely related fragrances (see numerous statements below). Conclusion for the best explanation: A flanker can be sold better with significant differences in fragrance notes on paper. Nevertheless, in my opinion, Water Splash is an interesting fragrance for at least the following target groups: 1) All those who do not yet own L’Homme or other flankers and would like to acquire a very similar fragrance for a fraction of the price from the same manufacturer and officially the same perfumer. Currently available for about €0.33/ml, really inexpensive. 2) All those who greatly appreciate L’Homme but find it a bit too "distant" (yes, this is a completely subjective impression). Water Splash adds a delicate, slightly bitter-citrusy fruitiness to the L’Homme DNA, which makes it for me a crucial nuance "warmer," "more vibrant," and "more summery." (Like an Aperol with mineral water vs. one with mineral water and a splash of orange). 3) All Prada fans who simply want to own every Prada fragrance (which could get quite expensive). 4) All those looking for a serious, not boring "business scent" that can also be worn in leisure time without hesitation, and who can warm up to a 150ml bottle. 5) All those who would like to take a seat in David Hockney's famous painting "A Bigger Splash" on a day with a brilliantly blue sky on the empty director's chair at the edge of the swimming pool in front of a luxurious Californian flat-roof bungalow, to witness the titular "splash" after jumping from the 1-meter board, and who value being appropriately scented for the context.

I consciously refrain from saying "Jeremy," as I would rather not divert the interested reader to weinkenner.de, Horse&Hound, or other lowbrow reading material. However: L'Homme is so incredibly present in the videos of the aforementioned fragrance influencer that I now want to contribute my two cents to the soap king, even though pretty much everyone should have an opinion on Prada's flagship, and I have already dedicated a comment to the OG. The DNA can never be bad, as it is predominantly graciously accepted by the more discerning connoisseurs here, which is akin to a nobility for mainstream designers. I can summarize my general thoughts on the L'Homme series as follows: 1. I have never, truly never, smelled a soap that smelled like #L'Homme. Not at home, not in a hotel, and certainly not in Abu Dhabi. But then again, I have never been there. 2. The DNA definitely creates a fresh-clean connotation for me, despite presumably high-quality ingredients being synthetic, floral, and slightly sweet, but primarily - clean. L'Homme has a high recognizability and clearly differs from Prada's other iris candidates. In particular, Amber pour Homme Eau de Toilette comes across as much more organic, likable, and warmer, though also a bit more old-fashioned. L'Homme Water Splash is the freshest and lightest flanker compared to the original and L'eau, but still very close to the original DNA. Mandarin and ginger give it a summery zest. Neroli is now a bit more prominent, and the sweetness that I still clearly perceive in the OG seems only peripheral here in the background. Iris is no longer included in the fragrance pyramid, but I believe I can still perceive it clearly. The longevity drops slightly in comparison, but that is by no means a flaw, as Watersplash is clearly intended as a cologne for the hotter days by its name. And it works excellently. I also feel that I don't come across as so distanced-cool, dismissively professional, as with the original. Water Splash is more playful, innocent, more casual - and that is what ultimately makes it more attractive to me than "L'Homme | Prada." And for those who like the original, Watersplash offers an excellent and also affordable alternative for summer. If someone wants something closer to the original, but still fresher, more universal, and with a bit more projection and longevity, they should go for L'Eau. In my opinion, all three complement each other perfectly and expand the DNA with real alternatives for different tastes.

This release is already 2 years old. I only just got my hands on it. It has been sold out in many shops for a long time, which makes me suspect that this is a limited edition. Luckily, I managed to get a 150ml bottle for just over 50 euros. The last one in this shop. In some lesser-known shops, you can even find it for under 50 euros for 150ml. Definitely "Bang for the buck".

The Prada L'Homme line is, for me, one of the most successful from a mainstream designer in recent years. Even the Absolu flanker, which is positioned between the regular and the Intense, has its justification in my opinion.
Smells really good and the scent is quite similar to that of the classic Prada L’Homme.

And then to fold my arms and turn the corners of my mouth down. My 6-year-old self is not getting his chocolate ice cream. The Intense differs beautifully and strongly from the original. Darker and "intens-ier". The l'eau is beautifully blue. Watery. Fresher. "L'eau-ier". It's logical what I hope for from the Water Splash, right?

So, since I have both l'homme intense, l'homme, and this one, I dare to share my opinion here. The scent is quite similar to the original l'homme but has a nice, really only super light but very noticeable freshness. I can't pick out ginger or the woody base here! You can wear it both at the office and in your free time, ideally in spring & summer.

Iris Pallida, according to the box, is the sort of Iris that was used for this earthy green floral. Now, i don´t know what is the olfactive difference between the varieties, but this white flower iris smell here rather pale and transparent. Don´t get me wrong. I am a huge admirer of paleness. The pre-raphaelite women are pale, and so is the fur of my cat. Pale is the light of a rainy day (just like today) and i could write a long list of many favourite pale things. Infusion d´Iris is very watery and a bit melancholic. On my skin, the lily of the valley is the dominant note. This is a rain soaked lily of the valley, very fresh and transparent, and pale blue-tinged, thanks to the violet. It is a beautifl accord, how the scent starts muget and finish violet, over a distant, clean iris. Neroli and galbanum are refreshing and sparkle like ice cubes falling on a glass. This flowers are so wet, it smells a bit musty, but just the tiny bit to make it interesting. In this first stage it is tender and delicate, and even it can be perfectly shared, it is closer to the femenine. Of all the versions on Infusion d´Iris, is the most flowery, and my second favourite after the Absolue. For the ones who like their tea strong, they will probably wish this infusion had settled a bit longer. Someone who look for a subtle, unintrusive scent will be pleased with this dewy wild flowers. The drydown is so beautiful and unoffensive i can hardly imagine someone disliking it: the clean iris is now the dominant. It keeps the characteristic earthiness, but all impurities and dirt have been washed away. The iris is rounded with a mild cedar wood note.

This is my sleep good, feel good, cozy perfume. I just love it, could baaaathe in it. Iris and a hint of violet, more I usually don't smell before succumbing to sleep. Every night, as I am surrounding myself with it - sometimes I light up the candle too - the whole room smells good. If I am not already sleeping by the time the base notes come out, there is a touch of neroli and something woody. But all in all, the scent is full of the wonderful powdery and creamy iris. There is really no comparison with the Eau de Parfum, in my opinion. These are two entirely different scents! While the EDP is built around the orange, the EDT stages the iris. So, the EDP is warm and spicy. This one, however, is fresh and powdery. Longevity is not great with either one. Strangely enough, the Eau de Toilette lasts longer on my skin. And now, have a nice little dream!

Quite close to Infusion d'Homme without the orange but with violet and Lily-of-the-Valley florals instead that gives a freshly laundered bedding kind of vibe . And has a little more sweetness from the heliotrope. Also quite creamy like dove deeply nourishing body wash.

When the darkness, like a part of the night, suddenly awakens within you... Remember, remember this... All the iris vintage powder dreams of your youth. All the faded legends that surrounded you, like ghostly sheets washed with violet fabric softener. All the cleanliness and strength that made you who you are. Remember. Remember this... All the cherished memories that shaped you. All the vintage myths that gnawed at your nerves. All the things you thought would destroy you. Remember. Remember this... When the darkness, like a part of the night, suddenly awakens within you... Remember. Remember this... That the magic lies solely in a pure heart of fragrance. Remember.

Since the collection is never complete, I was looking for a fresh-ironed-clean-laundry scent for those times when I just want to smell clean or when my nose needs a break from my beloved heavy fragrances. Ideally, it should also be softly powdery. And so, during my search, I stumbled upon the Infusion again, which I had actually written off for myself. I had definitely tested L’Eau, the EDP, and the Absolue, but I wasn't sure about the EDT. Unfortunately, back then, all the Infusions developed extremely soapy on my skin, with the exception of the Absolue, which also didn't manage to convince me. As I said, I wasn't sure about the EDT, but the comments sounded like it was exactly the scent I was looking for. So I took another chance and tested it again, this time with a decant. And what can I say, it worked! The EDT develops on me just as it should, as it was described, and as I had hoped: softly green at the beginning, fresh, dry, clean, bright, powdery, and beautiful, without the piercing, annoying soap - just freshly ironed... The whole thing has very good longevity. Two sprays are enough for me to smell pleasant almost all day long. Not bad for an EDT. And since the decant is almost empty, there was a whole bottle under the Christmas tree. The big bottle. Life can be so beautiful…

I’m into powdery scents. Not the sweet ones that are like dental fillings, but the fresh ones. The airy, delicate ones. And thanks to a dear friend at Parfuma, this fine gem has moved into my cozy home. Thank you again, dear First, my spring has become something special because of it. (Maybe summer too!) The scent: It starts off fresh and tingling in the nose.

The proof that you don't need to list a long list of ingredients for a classy scent is this one. Magical seven ingredients. It starts off fresh and floral right away. I know heliotrope as a gemstone or an addition in cosmetics. I boldly derive Helios, the Greek sun god, for myself. Because the sun rises for me when I spray this fragrance.

This wonderful little fragrance has a permanent place in my (relatively extensive) collection. The reason is quite simple: because it never annoys me and yet doesn’t bore me. Because I can even bear it with a headache. Because I feel tidy with it, without its freshness making me shiver. Because it is so predictable. I cannot detect a significant scent progression.
Prada's Infusion d'Iris as an Eau de Toilette is softer, gentler, and less spicy, harsh-vegetal, and green - the last bit that had bothered me about the EDP over time is no longer present here.

Infusion d'Iris gets 10 out of 10 stars from me. Why? With this perfume, in my opinion, you can't go wrong at all. Because anyone who loves the scent of freshly washed laundry or the fragrance character of fresh cream, powdery, clean, should not only take a closer look at this creation but seriously consider giving the scent a chance.

Candy Florale has little in common with the original or l'eau. Benzoin and caramel are nonexistent in this juice. All I can smell is floral notes and lemon ice in the drydown. I had high hopes for this one, but it smells awfully similar to Estee Lauder Pleasures Pop. This sits close to the skin and is veeeeery light, appropriate for springtime.

To me this smells like a jasmine-scented (I know it's not listed but it smells like it's there) hairspray, that dries down to a powdery indistinct-white-floral hairspray. Nothing else, not very memorable - pretty generic and synthetic. There are a lot of beautiful white-floral fragrances out there, and this wasn't one of those for me. Definitely sample this before buying a full bottle!

This is hardcore a shampoo scent. Smells like the super popular girl in high school who would gel scrunch her hair back in the early 2000s. I love it, but I love shampoo fruity florals. Dylan Blue Femme is one of my favorites. I was surprised how strong this was, four sprays and my entire kitchen filled with the smell and everyone could catch it feet away. But within an hour you couldn’t smell a thing. Even on my skin and clothes there is just this hint of honeyed floral lingering. However, this bottle is still pretty new so I am going to give it a month and revisit. Any type of lemon notes don’t really agree with me and thankfully, I can’t smell them at all in this. It is very floral. Not gourmand at all. One negative, when sprayed on dirty sweaty skin it almost smells like wet dog. No idea how or why, but I was out doing yard work and before running to the store quick I sprayed some on me and it went terrible in about twenty minutes. It never does this when I use it in the morning after a shower.

...there's a boy at school whom I find really sweet. He is a bit older than me. We've talked a few times, and he was really nice! Of course, I've found out a bit about him through friends, but unfortunately, I think he doesn't even know my name. Sure, I'm also way too shy to approach him directly. Now I've learned that he will be at a party at a friend's house soon. She has promised me that she will introduce us then. Hopefully, it works out!!! Can you please give me some tips on how to behave that evening without it coming off as awkward? What should I wear and what should I do with my hair? I would really wish that we could get together! He looks really sweet, and we would match perfectly, my friends think so too. Please, please help me! (Melanie, 15) Dear Melanie, it seems like you've really got it bad! Of course, you're a bit nervous when you meet your crush 'for real' at a party for the first time. It's really sweet of your friend to arrange that for you. I have a few tips for the big night - but the crucial step can only be taken by you! If you look pretty, you can emphasize that with a few sexy accessories. But don't overdo it! If you don't look so pretty, you should keep getting him beers. But don't overdo it! To boost your confidence and really wrap him around your finger, you can also reach for a very special secret weapon - perfume! Why not try Prada Candy Florale, it's made for girls like you. 'Candy' is English and means 'sweetness', 'Florale' is French and means 'floral'. And 'Prada' is Italian and means 'not cheap' - so you've already made a statement! You show him that you're really a sweet girl and that you like flowers! And you also show him that you're not cheap - that's especially important if you don't look so pretty and have given him a lot of beer to drink. Nothing can go wrong at the party, right? From us, anyway, good luck! Conclusion: what a beautiful time that was. And also not.

After I clumsily and embarrassingly struggled with the cap of the bottle for quite a while, I finally received the first spray. Forale is not as sweet and caramel-heavy as the original Candy, but it is attractively fresh and summery. The Limoncello Sorbet is more cool than citrusy, which I like very much. However, the peony is definitely in the foreground. It exudes a floral - clean scent, slightly soapy - but not biting. You feel like you are dressed in a bright white, freshly ironed summer blouse that doesn't weigh down the skin and cools slightly. A drop of honey and a hint of caramel have been added to the ironing water, which conveys a certain cheerfulness and lightness. The musk is smooth and creamy and clings to the skin. Nevertheless, Florale is not a cuddly scent - it dances freely through the world. Although "Made in Spain" whispers to me: Vive la Liberte!

Attention all die-hard Prada fans: you may be a bit disappointed, but you will still find a very beautiful fragrance... and all Candy opponents: give Candy Florale a try, you will be very astonished and surprised, and find a completely different scent here that has almost nothing in common with Candy and also Candy L'Eau.

Prada Candy - a sugary calorie bomb with lots of caramel and plenty of vanilla, that's how we know (and love...?) the original. Since I own that one, I didn't really look much at the other Candys. What else could possibly come? Until I tested Candy Eau Florale. I find that it has not much in common with the original Candy; the sweetness and heaviness are completely missing.

I'm not really a fan of the X-versions that have been thrown at us for years in addition to the original, trying to convince even the last reluctant buyer that the scent is just right - somehow, maybe in the L'eau or the L'eau fraiche version. Or the Summer Edition, or...

And once again, a Prada fragrance. You can (almost) be proud of me, because I dared to spray this girly women's scent on myself, and that in the city! It wasn't even discreet, as I don't just spray a little on my wrist for a test, but have to spray my whole arm. And since it's still cold outside, I had to take off my jacket and such in front of the shelf or fragrance.
Candy Florale is, in my opinion, also a typical Candy in spirit, but it is the summer interpretation - which translates from Miuccia and Daniela to: Limoncello (yes, it really smells like that!

I liked this perfume when I first tested it--a light floral with a twinge of sweetness, as opposed to the many loud fruity florals that Victoria's Secret offers. I was about to buy it today when I tested it again and POOF! Gone from my skin within 5 minutes of walking around the store. It's sad, since they're charging a pretty penny for the 1 oz bottle alone. I don't see this flanker lasting very long and will probably end up in the semi-annual sale bin this upcoming January/February.

Clean, fresh, and airy floral. Its name is apt, as it smells like something fleetingly glimpsed or imagined. The kind of floral a computer might have created; a digital rendition of a flower. It quickly turns musky and a touch powdery, with the neroli and jasmine remaining very much in the background. It’s a good every day easy reach that doesn’t require too much thought. A very pretty, feminine, captivating scent - and one that in a way almost feels liminal in its too-good-to-be-true unnatural perfection. Update 19/12/25: I recently found out that this is an AI-augmented scent, and I find that simultaneously both interesting and unsurprising as there is something ephemeral and (as I noted previously) almost too perfect about it that’s difficult to put into words. Apparently the perfumers used a programme called “carto” to create a “jasmine AI accord” from a micro lab of 1000 vials of jasmine variations, essentially creating something that doesn’t by itself exist in nature. An intriguing use of technology for sure, although one I hope doesn’t ultimately come at the cost of human creativity.

"Paradoxe Virtual Flower" by Prada is a jasmine scent through and through - which actually scares me and is not my thing. But somehow something admirable has happened here and it clicked between us... I don't know the other two "Paradoxe" or only minimally. This is the first detailed test from the series. And I am amazed at how powdery, wearable, and fine Prada interprets and combines jasmine here. It can really be appreciated - across weight classes! Jasmine is so clearly, sparklingly, and beautifully accompanied by neroli, musk, and bergamot that I barely smell the diva-like aura of the floral scent I often avoid. It remains a jasmine perfume - but very modern, summery, and positively charged. Not heavy or sweaty at all, not meaty or overwhelming, not annoying or thick. Quite the opposite. This is fun, this is elegant, this is energetic, this is young. Without being too synthetic, which I had prematurely assumed given the name. I really like this. Without completely uprooting trees. But it does its job. Bottle: more lying down than flying Sillage: delicate & consistent Longevity: 7 hours and more! Conclusion: one of the few designer "jasmine" scents that I like - (not too) sultry and (quite) beautiful!

I bought the fragrance blind after seeing it several times on Instagram. The scent is modern, floral, and synthetic, just the way many people love it. Now here comes the BUT: Do you know that typical fragrance direction that mothers wear to events and accordingly use before long car rides? This fragrance, which is initially okay/good, but after ten minutes in a closed car makes you feel nauseous? Here we have one of those scents. Outside, it works perfectly, exactly where fresh air, movement, and distance are present. But indoors, it's too much. I wouldn't say I regret the purchase, because as mentioned, you can wear the scent outside. But the hype is not understandable for me! I would neither recommend it nor buy it again.

I like perfumes, I like flowers. Paradox is what I was looking for, it lasts and lasts, two sprays and it holds for five, six hours. Then it came on strong, I expected the first one, but stronger, more persistent, sharper, none of that, disappointment. And then this one came. I can only say that those who love the Muse will find this one their favorite. Clear, airy, floral, seductive, summery, it gives a sense of well-being, cleanliness. Doesn't necessarily have to be part of the Prada collection, the first version is enough.

... has gotten ready to go out. But first, she needs to hang the white cotton laundry on the line. She hangs up the blouses, shirts, and summer dress on the clothesline. Everything exudes a fresh scent. She takes off her apron, puts on her high heels, grabs her handbag with the apartment and front door keys, and heads to her car. The lady who wears this fragrance first gets a fresh, citrusy, modern scent in her nose, which is quickly replaced by feminine floral accords. The perfume becomes clean, powdery, and the whole thing is underlined by a lightness and cheerfulness. This character lasts until the end. The longevity and sillage are average. Here we have a women's fragrance that can also be worn by young ladies. Guys, you need to try it out for yourselves to see if you can or want to wear it; it is not so feminine that it would be impossible. It is definitely very wearable on warm days, but it will also make a "bella figura" on cold days. During the day in a suit, in jeans with a blouse, or just casually, as well as in the evening in a summer dress, evening wear, or even just with something very ... this fragrance works well. Anyone who enjoys a fresh floral sweet citrusy clean powdery scent is exactly right here, all with a certain elegance.

I really like the Prada Paradoxe line. Even though Prada has drifted away from this noble and slightly niche direction through L'Oreal, this line offers something very suitable for everyday wear with a bit of sex appeal.

....said my friend...yes, the original Paradox, we will never be friends just like any NR flanker, Voce Viva, Burberry and so on. How did it come to pass that I had to have at least a generous decant of the latest version in my collection....some online perfume dealer just included a manufacturer sample for me....so for me, #The Muse is just adorned with flowers.

By chance, I encountered the fragrance and I was actually taken with it immediately. It is currently difficult to find scents that do not ride the vanilla wave. Unfortunately, that is not to my taste. The beginning is pleasantly fresh and lightly floral. Quite nice for spring, actually. But quite quickly, the scent becomes one-dimensional and for me, boring / plain.

Imagine a light pink flower, similar to or perhaps exactly like the summer-blooming peony that many remember. Anyone who has ever been captivated by such a wonderful creation of nature may have held such a bloom or flower head in their hands and, if they were detail-oriented enough, dared to explore those delicate petals between their thumb and forefinger.

Incredible Daring really surprised me. On my skin this is a true fruity floral. The notes listed calls out for only the orange flower but to me this isn't just a citrus perfume. My nose detects orange, apricots, pineapple and pear in the top notes. It isn't citric, rather a soft juicy fruit medley that leads to a heart of freesia. The dry down is much more than just musk and freesia. I smell tonka beans, musk, vanilla, and amber. This is a slightly complex fruity floral bordering on the gourmand side on my skin. It got me compliments right away. My only problem is with its longevity; 3 hours the most. But it is such a lovely 3 hours!! :) Recommended for anytime wear, especially close quarters or warm environments.

I constantly bleat on about the Infusion series from Prada being 'too light' and 'too expensive' for what they are. I am happy to report that I find my critique incorrect, especially when it comes to Infusion de Vétiver! I have no idea what has prompted this turn around in my perception. Suffice it to say that of late, I have been hankering for something that is both present and pleasant to spray on my skin ... something that doesn't necessarily trumpet it's existence but makes itself known with delicious wafts of 'fresh from the shower' goodness for longer than just a couple of hours. I have found it here! I've always enjoyed a healthy dose of Vetiver in fragrances ... I find it uplifting. The beauty of this note is further enhanced here by the clever addition of two rather pungent spices ... in a completely non-pungent way. The Pepper and Ginger here serve basically to make the Vetiver in this 'fume sparkle, like so many dew drops in the morning sunshine clinging precariously to blades of grass. The Tarragon in this composition brings a simple, herbal quality to it, further enhancing the feeling of freshness. Infusion de Vétiver presents the nose with a superb soapiness and doesn't demand any attention in it's own right. Rather, it enhances and compliments ... perfect for hot weather! It radiates cool confidence. Far from being a 'men only' fragrance this one falls into that 'never never land' of unisex creations. I personally feel that all fragrances should live in this world, not being one to connect gender to a bottle of perfume. I like everything about this fragrance, from the funky packaging to the simple, elegant bottle which has a lovely heft and sits easily in the hand to spray. It's taken me some time to 'get' the idea behind the Prada Infusion series ... now that I have, I couldn't be happier!

Yes it does smells like Infusion D'Homme, but they're quite different though. This one is more earthy/green because of heavier vetiver note. Actually i prefer Encre Noire or Etro's Vetiver instead of this. Anyway, it's a safe vetiver scent, very pleasant. Sillage, lasting power and projection are average. Updated January 2014

As a fan of both the Prada Infusions and vetiver, it did not take much to persuade me to spring for a scent-unsniffed bottle of Prada INFUSION DE VETIVER, and the deal was sealed by the endorsement by one of my dear Canadian fragrant friends, RRCOOLMAMA2, who not only has superlative taste in perfume, but also owns a bottle of this noble creation! Like the other Infusions, INFUSION DE VETIVER offers a refined and light linear layer of lusciousness. In this case, the lusciousness is leafy green tarragon--which does not smell exactly like culinary tarragon, but is also very different from grass green--combined with pepper and ginger, both applied judiciously, all of which complements the gorgeous vetiver very well. In keeping with the aesthetic of this series, nothing sticks out from INFUSION DE VETIVER. Unlike many ginger and pepper perfumes, these notes blend seamlessly with the tarragon and vetiver so that one does not (at least I do not!) immediately peg this as a pepper or a tarragon or a ginger perfume. Even the vetiver is shrouded in mystery in this composition. Yet it all smells so natural and nice and wonderful. And completely unisex, I should add. The texture reminds me a bit of EAU DE CARTIER CONCENTREE, which is a big, fat watery violet leaf perfume. The notes here are very different, but there is a similarly aqueous (I don't want to say "aquatic", because this smells gorgeous, not gross), demeanor. I am happy to have acquired a big bottle of this appealing fragrance, and so is HRH Emperor Oliver, as you can see below. Fortunately, in his magnanimity, he has decided since that photo op to share this lovely source of royal redolence with me, his Chief of Staff. Which makes a lot of sense, actually, since he benefits, too, from the delightful scent which wafts through the air each time that I don this refreshing perfume.

Prada Infusion de Vetiver is a glorious fragrance. I'm not usually the kind of girl that swoons over fresh scents, but this particular composition has everything going for it. Vetiver is a really unique note that appears every now and then in fragrances. In nature it can be quite dry, bitter and dusty. Most fragrances that attempt to tackle this note, often present it as being smokey or oriental. Infusion de Vetiver, takes a different road. This fragrance is clean and refreshing, but certainly not bland. The dryness of the vetiver is still rather apparent in this fragrance, especially on the skin, however the clean, soapy accord balances the vetiver out nicely. It's not grassy, just light and somewhat crisp. It's difficult for my words to do justice for this fragrance. All I can say is that I find it very alluring and it would compel me to approach a man that smells like this. The blend of freshness and earthiness really works for me. Prada makes some very classy scents, and while Infusion de Vetiver is one of them, it isn't strictly so. I'd encourage any man, even the casual men that feel awkward wearing suits, to give this fragrance a go. It'd smell just about perfect on any man, at least in my opinion.

Luca Turin expresses a rather scathing opinion about the big brother 'Infusion d’Homme': it is a "cheap iris," nothing more than a pale, misguided imitation of Lutens 'Iris Silver Mist'. He concludes his critique with a crisp "Avoid!" I take the criticism into account, but I still appreciate 'Infusion d’Homme' - and I find the comparison with Lutens' iris composition completely wrong. In my perception, the Prada fragrances from the Infusion series are very well-made lifestyle products that do not pretend to have an artistic attitude. Instead, they represent an olfactory perspective that, under the heading "Light Powderiness," offers an almost weightless alternative to the comparatively cloying sweetness of some mainstream fragrances in the men's segment. In doing so, Prada follows a (somewhat soap-heavy) path that has been successfully developed into the company's signature in recent years. That I myself have been hooked by this particular scent character still surprises me: I actually don't care for this powdery stuff at all. At least, I thought that until recently - and I had to be (willingly) educated otherwise. Of course, I also secured 'Infusion de Vetiver' before the last remaining stocks are sold out. According to Luca Turin's logic, I should now compare it to Guerlain's 'Vetiver', but I will spare myself the search for parallels; they mostly exhaust themselves in the name anyway. Prada's vetiver shows us a finely ground, powder-soft version of sweet grass free from that typical earthiness usually associated with vetiver. At best, in comparison to 'Infusion d’Homme', one might attribute a hint of rootiness to the sweet grass here, but even that thought is forbidden: the sweet grass in both fragrances comes across as too artificial. Their significant similarity seems striking to me: 'Infusion de Vetiver' almost leaves me with the impression that the homeopathic dose of sweet grass from 'd’Homme' has been slightly intensified while simultaneously dialing back the sweetness factor a bit - et voilà: the vetiver brother is ready. (That the iris is not mentioned in any fragrance pyramid surprises me: I would swear that it also plays a not insignificant role in 'Infusion de Vetiver'...) The comparatively less sweet top note is likely due to the use of pepper and tarragon; especially the spicy opening makes 'Infusion de Vetiver' a touch greener right from the start than its brother. Various associations with cut grass have been described here; in my perception, the powderiness of the scent quickly dissipates this idea - leaving behind a bit of hay. This creates a strangely dry freshness - and provokes thoughts of a handmade herbal soap adorning the designer sink in an almost sterile high-rise apartment: a hint of country life in a cleanly styled urban chic.
