Aaaaaaaaaaaaahhhhhh! Yessss!!!! Olééééé!!! (okay, I'm currently playing a game with a Mexican theme, it really rubs off on you :D). It's that time again, a new Prada fragrance from the Infusions line has been released. I can never wait for a new scent to come out, and so recently, just according to my Parfumo motto ("Time will tell, scent will come" :DD), a new fragrance has appeared here! With these scents, it’s usually the case that basically all of them are good. Well, more or less, and of course depending on personal taste, but for me, they are very good and very beautiful fragrances that also wonderfully prove that synthetic scents can be really great. However, one should know this: Since these fragrances have a certain trademark almost all Prada scents share, namely clean and soapy notes, the scent is not necessarily suitable for those who do not like this type of fragrance note (and whom I like to refer to as dirt birds or grime balls, who apparently run away from any soap like Pig Pen from the Peanuts :D), as they will likely not connect with these fragrances. But still, I would of course always recommend giving one of these scents a chance and at least sniffing it, as it could definitely be worth it. So, the new fragrance here includes mandarins, which makes me particularly happy, as I quite like mandarins in fragrances (and of course to eat)! Well then, let me start sniffing :) The scent: So, the scent starts as indicated with mandarins, oranges, and neroli. Actually, you don’t immediately smell the mandarins, as I could perceive the neroli better at the beginning. It takes a few minutes before you finally notice the mandarins. From these little citrus fruits, you mainly smell the slightly sweet and deliciously fragrant flesh, while from the oranges, you can smell the more bitter-scented peel. As the mandarins become a bit stronger over time and later are the strongest citrus notes in the fragrance, the scent sometimes even feels like you are drinking a fruity fresh lemonade with mandarin flavor (well, at least it briefly reminded me of the Turkish refreshing drink "yedigün" with mandarin flavor... oh, just Google it, it’s basically just the Turkish version of the Spanish Miranda drinks, only with mandarin instead of orange). Even in the base, the mandarin remains, which is great, as in most mandarin fragrances, the mandarin note quickly evaporates, but here it really lasts for quite some time. And of course, there is the typical Prada note that gives a fragrance a clean and fresh aura with slightly creamy-powdery notes. However, this "Prada DNA" comes in quite late and is also noticeably weaker here than in the other Infusion scents, but it is still present. All in all, a weak sillage-wise, but olfactorily (in my opinion) very beautiful summer fragrance! The sillage and longevity: Unfortunately, the sillage is quite low. Although you are used to most of the Infusion scents not being particularly strong, this mandarin scent is among the weakest in the line, so you should get quite close to smell it on others. The longevity is surprisingly okay (for a citrus mandarin scent), as I could smell it well on myself for almost seven hours. The bottle: The bottle is rectangular with slightly rounded edges or corners. On the front, you can see the familiar Prada metal plaque. The fragrance name is on a narrow orange label on the side of the bottle, while on the opposite side, another label lists the fragrance contents. The cylindrical cap is surrounded by the typical Prada synthetic leather, which this time is orange. At first glance, it resembles the yellow bottle of Infusion de Mimosa, but as mentioned, it is orange here. As always, a very beautiful and handy bottle. Oh, the scent is wonderful! Yes, yes, of course, this is just my opinion, especially since I really like mandarin scents and the Infusion fragrances from Prada in general, but for me, after the slightly disappointing (but still somewhat nice!) Infusion de Mimosa, this has become an extremely great scent from this line, which only has two actual points of criticism: First, the scent is unfortunately quite weak in terms of sillage, and second, strictly speaking, the scent is nothing really new, meaning you shouldn’t expect anything extraordinary. Although the latter is not really a criticism for me, as long as the scent smells good. And it is indeed very well made, smells very nice, and that is always the main thing. Anyone who loves citrus scents, especially with a slightly sweet (but still citrusy) mandarin and orange note that can also be a bit creamier, should definitely check out this scent. Even those who usually shy away from soap can approach this scent, as it has a less pronounced soapy note :D You still don’t want to? Hmm… Maybe I can encourage everyone to take a closer look at the scent if I write that it gives you a very pleasant feeling, as if you were sitting in a cozy cloud high up in the blue sky, snacking on mandarins. "Yes, yes, one could just fall through the clouds," some might say now, but I’m trying to tell a imaginative, beautiful story, damn it! You know, sprinkle a little fairy dust, swirl around some cat hair, build up a mental movie, spread joy, stimulate the imagination, and so on and so forth… but no, you still fall through the clouds and land on your bare bottom, right? (and just don’t ask me why the bottom has to be bare :DD). Tsss… well, fine, then don’t test it :D But you would miss out on a totally great scent that would fit perfectly into summer and is also very wearable on really hot days. Due to the weak projection, however, as is often the case, it is only suitable for daytime or leisure use, as you will hardly notice it when going out. Well… if necessary, you can always fill it in mini sprays or travel sizes and occasionally reapply :)

It's time, I'm writing my first review. For this, I chose the fragrance that surprised me the most recently. Prada Infusion de Mandarine. The scent: From the moment the first spray comes into contact with the air, a fresh breeze of green leaves greets you, subtly accompanied by notes of pomelo and grapefruit in the background. These are quickly overshadowed by a joyfully laughing mandarin that instantly evokes the most colorful childhood memories. Meanwhile, almost unnoticed in the background, the clean white blossoms of a mother watching over her children blend in. These heart notes slowly fade away like a dissolving dream, leaving behind a warm sweet freshness that inspires you to embrace the day, still hearing the laughter of children in your ears. Longevity: As is typical for citrusy, very fresh fragrances, this one is not the longest-lasting. On me, the scent lasts about 4-5 hours, and then even the base disappears. However, if I have used some moisturizer before applying, the fruity heart note lasts noticeably longer. Sillage: What surprises me is that the scent is noticeably perceived by people I talk to (1-1.5m away) for the first 3 hours. After that, the scent trail diminishes relatively quickly. Bottle: A rectangular bottle with an embossed Prada metal plate. The cap has an embossed band in matching pastel orange. Overall, it's a nice design, but nothing particularly outstanding for me. Price/Performance: I ordered the 100ml bottle for €65 and find that a good price for a perfume that is often refreshed. Conclusion: For me personally, it's a clear must-have scent. With its focus on orange citrus fruits, especially the mandarin, it is a particularly cheerful summer fragrance that never feels too young or playful due to its powdery clean undertones. The simple fragrance structure invites layering experiments, the results of which I am very curious about. I hope I was able to give you an idea of how this scent affects me, and perhaps I inspire one or the other to dream ;-)

Sometimes I think that perfumes have different compositions - depending on the mood. I don't smell burnt rubber tires - thank God. Nor a swamp or dog pee. A little rubber, yes. And indeed, this scent reminds me of Haribos with gummy bears and licorice mix. (I love it!) And of course my dearly beloved BR540! In fact - and I might be the only one - I also detect Mancera's Instant Crush here! A soft and high-quality leather jacket has also been mixed in here. I hope this is a fitting review, as I often struggle with the individual notes. I don't pick up orange here and I'm very glad about that. Definitely the saffron, which might also contribute to the similarity to BR540?! Overall, it has overtaken my favorite BR540, as this scent is more versatile, definitely more unisex, and has an extremely strong addictive potential for me! Thanks to Spirito Fiorentino, I am now sorting through my modest collection, because this one came racing in with a leather jacket, cotton candy in hand on a brand new Harley at such a speed that I didn't need much time to adore this scent! Exactly, divine! I believe I have finally found my fragrance. BR540 and Spirito Fiorentino - haaaaach Thank you for reading ???

My headline says it all. I received a sample today (unfortunately 10ml) and had to test it immediately. I almost peed my pants from excitement. Unpacked the sample, one spray on my wrist (left, right done). OH MAN WHAT IS THAT SMELL? It smelled directly of swamp and burnt rubber tires (very burnt tires) and a bit of MFK 540. Totally shocked, I remembered a YouTuber who said you should give the scent about 30 minutes, then the burnt tires would burn off. Unfortunately, it only got worse. I actually felt nauseous :-( On my skin, this burnt smell unfortunately remains mixed with something swampy and somehow also earthy. There is a specific smell after a summer rain in the city, usually smelling of dog pee and warm earth. That's what I keep perceiving on my skin. Unfortunately, nothing sweet developed for me. MFK 540 was only very, very faint at the beginning. Now, 8 hours later, my wrists still stink of it. Which speaks for its longevity. I wanted to test it since Baccarat often ghosted on me, but I’d rather get the Extrait now. Unfortunately, I don’t understand the enthusiasm from the YouTubers. I definitely do not want to smell like that and I don’t want my partner to smell it either. Totally terrible.

Release date 2018, a completely justified average score of 8.5, yet no one has felt compelled to dedicate more than a mere 140 characters to this fragrance poem until today. If one were to take the time to investigate the reasons, one might conclude that an accusation of plagiarism could possibly be the reason for this shameful neglect. However, I believe this approach simplifies the matter too much. Those who have followed my contributions in the past, due to a lack of personal hobbies and too much free time, know that I have been constantly circling around Kurdjian's Baccarat Rouge. It is important for me to mention that I am referring to the Extrait version. This fragrance fascinates and moves me. It can quickly lift my spirits, yet I use it rarely enough to have always refrained from a full purchase. But what is the reason for that? Do I find it too feminine? Not at all ... in stark contrast to the EdP, I see it as completely genderless. So what is it then? Well, I think MFK has simply pushed perfection to such an extreme that I subconsciously miss a note that gives beauty a lovable "flaw." Visually speaking, I am probably looking for something like Cindy Crawford's beauty mark, a distinctive reference point that, in very few cases, manages to make something absolutely beautiful even more beautiful through something seemingly "bad." The absolute roundness of the original seems almost surreal, and it lacks the crucial impression that credibly stamps the original, let’s say, as if it were indeed from this Earth. I always have the impression that I must be at least the best-dressed person in the world to create a coherent overall picture in connection with B540. That sounds not only complicated - and probably silly - it is. Thus, I am constantly searching for less perfect alternatives and am very pleased to have already found two. The somewhat distant cousin Kalan is, in this context, what one would nowadays call the NoBrain alternative. It works all year round ... always, everywhere ... fits perfectly, but does not reach the quality of BR540, nor does it aim to. Spirito Fiorentino, on the other hand, operates on absolutely equal footing, in the top premium segment, but has - warning, pun intended - Cindy's (liver) leather mark above the upper lip that I found so attractive in the 90s. It manages to not present the supposedly sought flaw as such, but transforms the perfect roundness into something like the perfect oval. Many may not believe a perfect oval is possible, as they only know round or square, but from my perspective, one can also act too ambitiously when trying to evoke a sensory impression. Some see this additional leather twist as a disturbing factor; I have read about burnt rubber with the maximum raised eyebrow. However, for me, it is clear ... it’s not a bug, it’s a feature! A very fairly priced bottle is currently on its way to me. The hope is very high that I have found the perfect imperfect fragrance. The 10 disguised as a 9, which gives me significantly more range of use while remaining special enough to maintain absolute equality.

Spirito Fiorentino first made its way to me last year in a package with various samples. At that time, I wasn't aware of what to expect from this fragrance. Once it arrived, I eagerly sprayed it on a test strip, waited a moment, and sniffed: The first impression hit me like a ton of bricks, and I initially thought, "Wow, this just smells like pure alcohol, how can anyone like this?" A bit disappointed, I waited a few hours, but even then I couldn't find anything appealing about the scent on the strip, which is why the sample ended up back in the drawer. Big mistake! Some time later, I tested it again, this time on my skin, where all the nuances of this wonderful fragrance creation began to reveal themselves to me. Smoky, sweet with a gently resonating leather note and a beautifully balanced saffron. An absolute dream, how could I have misjudged it so badly on the test strip? Bought it immediately. The bottle is a real eye-catcher and absolutely high-quality, which you can expect in this price range. Longevity and sillage are really good on my skin. The scent projects extremely strong for at least 4 hours, then becomes a bit closer to the skin, but is still well perceivable for 10-14 hours. It lasts forever on clothing. A true beast even with fewer sprays. With this fragrance, you truly draw attention to yourself and make a statement. I wore it at a birthday party last summer and was really approached very often, simply because it is really exciting, unique, and above all potent. Hence the quote from the title. In summary, one can say that for your money, you get a true masterpiece from the house of Tiziana Terenzi. It certainly won't appeal to everyone, so definitely test it beforehand (best on the skin ;-) )!

Paolo Terenzi is known as a talented and highly professional perfumer. The high-quality fragrances he has created, which largely enjoy respect and recognition in the perfume community, are more than proof of that. Spirito Fiorentino is definitely not a clone or dupe of BR540, but a completely original scent.

I accidentally "stumbled" upon a sample, or rather, headed towards Terenzi, and somehow most people are here to find THEIR scent. A fragrance that gives you that last bit of confidence. I haven't been at this for long, but I find it hard to believe that something will come along that will blow me away even more. But let's start at the beginning.

Spirito Fiorentino is a fragrance I have known for ages. I wasn't quite sure: Do I need this or is the scent not worth a whole bottle? I won't even come close to finishing a whole 100ml bottle, but this fragrance recently found its way into my collection. If you like this Baccarat Rouge DNA as a man, in my opinion, this is definitely the better solution.

Spirito Fiorentino and I have been together for 5 years now, and I never want to live without him again. We found each other quite by chance when I was looking for an alternative to BR 540. In many reviews, I read that it is said to smell like burnt rubber tires and is simply unbearable.

I had my eye on Spirito Fiorentino for a while. Since many people claim it resembles Barracat Rouge 540, I want to point out that I cannot provide comparisons to BR540 because I have not worn that hyped fragrance myself and therefore do not know how it smells. Two days after receiving the sample, I applied it around 9:00 AM - without knowing what my plans for the day were.

Well, now we are talking… My yesterday review was on Prada La Femme. I was not overall convinced that I wanted to keep it since it has a watery expression on my skin. Not a bad perfume, just not interesting enough. Luckily I have a tester for Prada La Femme Intense, and the word Intense hits the spot. This has way more power than the original. Even being a linear with just three notes, tuberose, ylang-ylang and patchouli, this puts on a show. A show that lasts for seven-eight hours. And all the way through I am really entertained. All three notes are highly appreciated by me and together they make an outstanding trinity. I must say that I get a little anosmic, but that is a well known fact with the linears and me. This is so feminine and delicious that my partner keeps sniffing my throat when I wear it. So who cares if I cannot smell it after a few hours? This will swap places with La Femme. Year 2, 55/365

Hello everyone, Today, I would like to share a few words about a very special fragrance at this late hour and one of the "least noticed / subtly underrated fragrances" available for women (personal opinion). My wife and I are really big fans of "La Femme | Prada," but it has this noticeable sweetness... and that’s not a bad thing, not even close! But there are days when you just have less of a "desire" for something sweet, and exactly this moment occurred a few months ago when my wife and I were looking around here, and I quickly found "La Femme Intense | Prada." I had briefly smelled it a few years ago, but I only had a vague memory of it, and luckily there was a sample (a very large one) available here in the Souk, which I ordered right away...! And how did my wife and I find it? She thinks it’s soooo great that it will soon be joining us when the current bottle runs out (it was a bit more than 9ml back then), but she only wears it once a week (if at all) and very subtly, meaning 2 sprays. I really thought for a while about what it reminded me of...., but more on that in the next point. How does it smell and what are the differences from the regular La Femme ? The La Femme is bright floral, creamy, with a light + clean bee honey note, with musk = a very nice and great designer fragrance for women, and my honest opinion is that it is one of the top 10 everyday - work fragrances for a woman aged 18 - 65 in the designer category. The La Femme Intense has less of this floral touch and no sweetness from the honey; rather, it is creamy, unsweetened, very composed, mature, and has certain vibes from the past - which I recognize as an old Chanel lover = I mean those powdery vibes of the old school that have a slightly vintage feel but are 0 bothersome...! I am a very big fan of this fragrance and can recommend it to women over 30 who are slowly moving away from sweet scents. Because the fragrance is consistent and not playful! I find the longevity and sillage to be good to very good! If you find a leftover bottle or a sample here and see yourself reflected in the review, I can only recommend this wonderful fragrance to you! And now, have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______

I had recently been leaning towards delicate floral to green scents - perhaps because spring is blossoming. But then I thought of Prada again - a brand that suited my mom well. She always smelled so elegant and stylish. And I wanted to emulate her. So I reached for Femme intense - and this straightforward scent lives up to the addition "intense." I don't find it sweet - but the tuberose is strong and enchanting. Ylang is also not holding back - cushioned by patch. A truly elegant fragrance that radiates confidence - but also conveys it. Not a scent for every day - but when I need a boost, it is the go-to choice. Then I gladly take a slice of its confidence. It is the scent against weak moments. It would also be suitable for a theater visit, as it remains close to the skin despite its intensity. Practical, unglamorous clothing is also elevated by it. Still, I can better imagine it on my stylish mom.

* sigh * I sometimes really struggle with certain Prada fragrances. I mean testing them. La Femme is not my favorite line from this brand, but the Candys always give me a headache about how I can discreetly test them… and I see that a new Candy, Candy Sugar Pop, is already on the way… * sigh * :D But I had a certain hesitation with this fragrance as well, though I still dared to spray it on myself right in the middle of the women's department. And for comparison, I even sprayed the regular Prada on my other arm! That's quite an achievement, isn't it? :D Okay, I have to admit that the women's department was empty… he he he, unfortunately, the cash register was right behind me, which was NOT empty and which I only noticed AFTER spraying. I thought I would get caught spraying… aargh, aaaah but: That was not the case! Because I tested the fragrance in a drugstore that has many other things as well. And since there has been terrible weather with wind and rain outside for a few days now, everyone was busy looking out the cash register to see how strong the wind was, generally complaining about the weather, or briefly looking for new umbrellas and hats, so NO ONE saw me. * sigh * I bet that the next Prada fragrance, especially the new Candy, will have the store packed again... :D But now let's get to the fragrance... The Fragrance: The fragrance starts off heavily floral, but also somewhat sweet. A Prada DNA, which you know from the old or other fragrances, that clean-soap feeling is not immediately recognizable, but only becomes apparent over time. Although the fragrance does not become really soapy, a small, clean feeling does emerge slightly later. The beginning differs from the regular La Femme in that it smells less floral (or has fewer floral notes) and is earthy with the patchouli. The sweetness (presumably from the tuberoses) comes gradually. In the heart note, the patchouli seems to fade a bit into the background, so that both La Femme fragrances (by both I mean the regular La Femme as well as the Intense here. I do not count La Femme L’Eau, as I do not know it yet) now smell somewhat similar. But then, a little towards the base, more differences become noticeable again. The Intense fragrance is generally heavier and more humid at first; I find the ylang-ylang smells significantly stronger here. The regular La Femme smells a bit looser and fresher here despite a little beeswax. Additionally, the patchouli returns in the Intense, giving the fragrance an earthy note again (which is completely missing in the regular Femme). Overall, the Intense is, as mentioned, heavier, more humid, and thus also seems a bit more mature. Overall, the fragrance is quite okay, but I simply find the regular La Femme more beautiful. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is okay and about as strong as the other Femme. This means that at a normal distance, it can be smelled for a while, but it does not necessarily leave a large scent cloud. The longevity is better, as I could smell it for at least ten to twelve hours. The Bottle: The bottle has the same shape as all the new Prada fragrances. From above, it looks like the letter "D" in shape. The front features the Prada/Milano inscription along with the logo embedded in the glass. The back is adorned with a burgundy artificial leather, which I find nicely done. The cap is T-shaped and gold-plated. As always, the bottle looks high-quality and great; I really like it, and even though it looks so massive, it fits well in the hand. So, I didn't like this fragrance that much, at least not as La Femme. It's quite okay, yes. And I would recommend it for a test, but personally, it came across as a bit too heavy and humid for me, which I don't really like. Although it resembles the regular Femme a bit, the regular one is looser and simply smells better than this one. However, I am sure that this fragrance could appeal to you ladies much more than it does to me. For those who enjoy heavy-scented fragrances, especially with humid or stuffy ylang-ylang and (sweet) tuberoses that together also seem a bit more mature, you might want to check out this fragrance. I, on the other hand, would still recommend the regular La Femme, as it simply appears more beautiful and has the same intensity, even though this one carries the name "Intense." By the way, I think La Femme Intense has become a fragrance for autumn, while the first La Femme also comes across quite well in spring. Well, now the L’Eau is still left from this line, but it probably hasn't been released yet, has it? At least I haven't seen it, but since I really like the Prada brand, I am very curious about the fragrance. Well, let's see... I hope by the time I test it, the store is empty again, so I can test it in peace :D

Cassiopea was an impulsive airport duty free purchase but it's a scent that was love at first sniff. This is one that I think fans of Xerjoff Dama Bianca may enjoy because Cassiopea has the same fruity-meringue plush pillowy feeling of Dama Bianca, but unlike the Xerjoff, Cassiopea is undercut and supported by a nice current of clean-robe softness too. It almost gives it expensive shampoo vibes and I mean that in the best way possible. I see this marketed as unisex but I have a hard time imagining this on a man. To my nose this is an unabashedly feminine fragrance that would work well for a bride and more formal events, but I think it also could be a signature scent for some as it's a fragrance that can be worn year round. Performance and longevity are both good, though I do find it eventually dims to a skin scent (which I'm not mad about but I know that bothers some people.) I don't always comment on packaging but here, I must. The presentation from Tiziana Terenzi for this line is incredible and Cassiopea may just be my favorite bottle design in my entire collection. Luxurious doesn't even begin to describe the way it feels in the hands. Honestly one to pick up as much for the bottle as the gorgeous juice inside. Eta: My unabashed love for this continues. However I wanted to update though as I've gotten to know Cassiopea more. I perhaps redact the comparison to Dama Bianca. Cassiopea is soft and fruity yes but the musk in this gives it a very different texture that is sort of hard to explain. It's not a dirty or animalic musk by any means. It is a decidedly clean musk to my nose but there's a quality and, as I said, a texture to Cassiopea that I find a little bit flirty and maybe even a little saucy? In any event if I had a signature scent, I think this would be one of the ones that would qualify as worthy. Pretty and appropriate any time, anywhere I always feel clean, pretty, confident and feminine wearing this scent. Works year round too.

Cassiopea is definitely a female fragrance. I could not imagine wearing this one, but I find it quite potent and sexy on my wife. As one can anticipate from the notes list, this fragrance is very fruity, sweet and floral. Top notes are relatively fresh, with passion fruit being the most prominent one. Generally I like blackcurrant in perfumes, it is quite an unique note, but I can hardly detect it here. After the initial fruity blast one can smell the sweet-floral heart on a creamy woody-musc base. To me the fragrance smells very natural and well blended. The longevity and sillage are great so be careful on the sprayer. In the same time this could also be a negative thing. My wife actually gave up of wearing this one because it is too strong and "aggressive" even with only a couple of sprays so that she doesn't enjoy wearing it. I would not agree that it smells fresh and clean. For example, if you imagine Chanel Chance eau fraiche being a fresh fragrance, Cassiopea is nowhere near. It is much sweeter and heavier formulation. We should maybe give it a one more chance, but it could be that we are going to get rid of this one. Oh yea, the presentation and the bottle are great, but I think that you really have to love this fragrance to get over the price tag.

I ordered a sample of this fragrance last month. My first test of a scent from this expensive brand. A brand that has many fans here. Also someone I enjoy writing to and we often have similar tastes. Even though some of this brand seem interesting to me, I decided on this one. I am extremely fond of fruity-floral fragrances, and the fact that it is listed as unisex piqued my curiosity. Since I also like to test for women, it wouldn't have been a disappointment if it were only feminine. And so it is. Only the base or the dry-down has a slight unisex touch; until then, it is a sensual women's fragrance. The bottles and packaging look luxurious according to the price. Especially the Luna Collection with its beautiful golden cap and elegant label. The fragrance is, as mentioned, primarily a fruity-floral scent. I love these two characteristics in women's fragrances. Not necessarily all of them, but here they are perfectly executed. Especially this stunning top note. For fruit lovers, it is an absolute must to test this. These fruity notes are definitely not run-of-the-mill. This mix of passion fruit and blackcurrant at the start is simply heavenly and very alluring. It slightly reminds me of chewy candies like Maoam. Not Maoam, but the more exotic ones that I used to enjoy snacking on. Yes, very delicious! Even when the floral notes come in, it remains at this high level. Very feminine and seductive. This wonderful fruity note paired with the floral notes is a mix that attracts me magically and makes me dream. It takes a few hours for the base to set in. It is soft and standard. Musk-tonka-sandal, nothing special, but quite pleasant. Some of the top and heart notes linger longer, and the DNA remains intact. The performance is really good as well. I haven't checked it precisely, but it should last around 10 hours with good sillage, especially at the beginning. Suitable especially thanks to its sensuality for flirting, dating, nightlife, and also simply for the beautiful and special moments in life. Despite the fruity notes, it also suits more mature women due to its noble execution. But you simply have to like and love fruity notes to wear this fragrance.

Well, you actually don't fit into my fragrance world at all. Your fruit. It is so delicately creamy, it is so puréed, it is so strained. There are no seeds, there is no pulp. You don't come across as artificially sweetened to me. Sure, you are sweet. Much sweeter than I usually like. There’s nothing bitter, no moss or anything like that. But I don’t feel like you’re clogging my pores and nose. Your dark berries also bring me a bit of pear. And I have the feeling that one or two small green leaves might have been whirled through the mixer as well. But just briefly, as they were probably well strained afterwards. And while I’m still on the fruit cream, flowers come in and merge with the fruit. They have such a fine aromatic spice nuance. And I must say, it suits you excellently. You become a little warmer. Not that there was even a hint of coolness before. No, a softened vanilla note is added. This happens quite slowly. You take your time. And for me, you also show a hint of amaretto. Not that you have any kind of alcoholic scent. No, it’s more like just the smell without the percentages. And you also appear a bit creamier to me now. Actually. Why actually?

The bottle: A dream of quality! Typical of Terenzi, one might almost say. You almost feel bad wanting to wear this fragrance without having dressed up nicely beforehand. The scent itself: Dominating for me are the musk and the passion fruit. Then the sandalwood. The other notes eventually join in. For whom is the scent: It is indicated as unisex. At the first "sniff," it suggests a feminine direction. This is the common and current opinion about this scent. But for me, this fragrance is just as wearable by a man. Is this scent, to pick up the title of this article, pure masculinity? No! It is not. Is pure masculinity, masculine or something desirable for a man? Absolutely not!! Because.. We all know the symbol of Yin and Yang (except my phone, which constantly tries to turn my Yin into a thing…). We also all know the extended form of this symbol with a black dot on the white side and a white dot on the black side. The "Taijitu," which represents the individual Yin and Yang. I want to take this symbol for my upcoming explanation and elaborate: Referring to the two (most common..) genders, this symbol represents the man on one side and the woman on the other. The dominant color on each side stands for the main attributes of both genders. For the man, and this is my own definition, so I have no idea if this is really the case, but knowing myself, it should be true: It is assertiveness and boldness. For the woman: The ability for empathy and intuition. The respective points symbolize that both sides also possess a bit of the opposite side. And they turn the supposed antagonist into an ally, ultimately creating a unity that leads both sides to interlock like two puzzle pieces. The result: Harmony. It also shows us that we must stand fully in our respective energy and its attributes to allow a bit of the other side. A good example might be Christopher Columbus; who could boast many masculine attributes like courage, recklessness, assertiveness, a bunch of unrefined and unwashed guinea pigs, and the ability to separate from the safe harbor of family and loved ones (which is what most fairy tales are actually about, by the way, and not about slaying dragons or waking up some chicks) but in the end, thanks to a feminine attribute, was able to lead his journey to success. Namely: Intuition! The fact that he got lost and ended up completely somewhere else than he originally intended only confirms this in the end. And when you look at the paintings showing how the ships park… but back to Cassiopea by Tiziana Terenzi.. So if you are a man who stands fully in his masculine energy, and that is never "pure" masculinity, you can wear this scent, my friend! Treat yourself! Fine!

Cassiopeia was the wife of King Cepheus and the mother of Andromeda. Moreover, she was an arrogant and self-absorbed woman, making sure everyone felt it and never missing an opportunity to express it. Unfortunately, this self-absorption eventually backfired. She claimed to be the most beautiful of all, even more beautiful than the Nereids, the Greek sea nymphs.

Here is my comment on the second Luna fragrance by Terenzi. I like this one a bit better than Draco, as the initial fruity notes smell so wonderful. One is also meant to imagine a journey to the moon or be reminded of traveling to similarly imaginative places. And unlike Draco, this fragrance allows for a better imagination of exotic and fantastical locations.

As can be easily seen, this fine favorite is my signature scent. I still remember the first time I got to test it in a small, exquisite perfumery. As is usual for me, I tested well over 40 fragrances on such a day. Accordingly, I was quite dazed after a while. However, with this scent, I became as clear as rarely before.

Cassiopea is my second Terenzi fragrance, and I must first say that it is my absolute favorite, especially in the current weather (quite humid and high humidity here). But beware: Cassiopea is not a conventional fragrance cocktail soaked in coconut and bergamot/lemon & rum. Rather, it is a fresh, clean, slightly soapy summer scent.

A basket full of blackcurrants and passion fruit. The sky is blue, sun rays warm my skin, and the birds are chirping. A gentle breeze provides a little coolness on this warm day, soaked with all the scents of the garden. Floral, fresh, sweet but not sticky. I want to keep smelling it and have the scent forever in my nose.

This is a wearable patchouli fragrance, there is not more to add. Texas cedar? More incense to me! Opening is harsh (spicy), but when it calms down (after 1 hour more or less) it becomes a decent patchouli without annoying people around you. Must say well blended (drydown is good), but not worth a full bottle.

The Midnight Train has completely convinced me. Honestly, I didn't have very high expectations for this scent, but I was proven wrong. With Midnight Train, you get a wonderful patchouli fragrance. Lightly earthy/dark and pleasantly spicy patchouli. Furthermore, there are these super beautiful woody facets. Over time, more and more sweet impressions emerge that create the impression of smelling a kind of patchouli liqueur. There are also very mild citrus accords, which are really very subtle. However, they fit so wonderfully with the fragrance that the overall combination of all the accords creates a fantastic overall picture. I even had the impression of perceiving some slightly floral nuances that give this fragrance a certain elegance. However, no floral accords are listed. Midnight Train truly radiates a wonderful elegance, a certain seriousness, and it constantly gives you the feeling of smelling really good. You have to keep smelling yourself; you look forward to catching a whiff of your own scent cloud every time the fragrance projects. The start of the fragrance might not appeal to some people. I found the beginning to be nice, but it becomes more beautiful over time. If I had liked the start as much as the rest of the fragrance, I would definitely rate it at least a nine. Make sure to try out this relatively unknown fragrance. Especially patchouli lovers will find pleasure in it. Even patchouli haters might find something to like here.

One thing upfront - the name of the fragrance is almost perfectly chosen. However, I would rather give it a bit more love or desire in the name instead of a heavy tone. "Caresses" fits well, as the scent is extremely cuddly on the wearer and truly knows how to seduce. It fits into the dark time of day, as it smells pleasantly warm of earth and thick, syrupy patchouli notes. Already with the first inhalation, the warmth settles in. I applied the fragrance after an extensive day at the spa, where I literally sweated out the toxins and everyday stress, including weeks of burdens, in the sauna. A thorough shower followed, where I rinsed away all my thoughts under a hard stream. Sometimes you just need that, especially after a tough time. It takes a while for everything to build up, but as they say, it eventually comes to a breaking point. It was already night when I came out. Arriving home, I wrapped myself in my blanket. The scent had become even more cuddly. It somehow calms you, gives you a sense of security. A gentle note of lemons tickles my nose, basking in the very last beat of the sunset. Earthy facets envelop the whole thing, with plenty of warmth still present. The scent of patchouli is not too heavy; it flows seamlessly within the perfume. Everything feels well-balanced. Sensually, I perceive resinous aspects that wedge themselves under the skin. It’s all so fluid, as if the fragrance was made to bubble. The -I feel good in my skin- feeling is emphasized here. Longevity and sillage are in the upper range. At midnight, it was still there. The caresses were not over even after waking up. Probably in my dreams, the scent broke through my hazy dreams, because I hadn’t had a night like that in a long time, where I slept so deeply that the next morning I didn’t know which planet I was on. You surely know the feeling, waking up and confusing day with night. Or the other way around. Once, I went to school at 8 PM in early summer because I thought it was 8 AM. :D But that’s another story. What I want to say is that the fragrance snatches away your sense of space and time, allowing you to fully immerse yourself in its caresses. There aren’t many transitions. It’s a steadfast warmth that runs from beginning to end. With lots of caresses from patchouli, warm, spicy earth, shining in the shadow of lemon. I love it and it’s going on the wish list. To the unknown donor of the sample: Thank you very much!

First of all: I belong to the patchouli admirers, but I am a critical one. It must not smell like perfume oil spilled on ponchos in the 90s, nor should it be overloaded with citrus accords. Patchouli can smell so good - and so unbearable. For years, I searched and found nothing that truly appealed to me in the way I envisioned a patchouli perfume. Years ago, Bois 1920's Real Patchouli came close to my idea (though it was a bit too vanilla-infused for my taste). Close. Then a few years ago, Tom Ford's Patchouli Absolu came along, and I was immediately smitten. That was exactly the scent I had imagined for years. Still one of my absolute fragrance favorites! In the meantime, over the last few years, I have occasionally sniffed and searched for another patchouli scent that would blow me away - or at least please me. Highly recommended in various forums and perfumeries were, among others, Etro, House of Oud, and Perris Monte Carlo. But even there, everything smelled too altered for my nose. Etro was too oriental and incense-like for me, PMC was too citrus-heavy, and HOU basically only smelled of (synthetic) rose; and that in almost unbearable intensity. When I then had the opportunity to test Midnight Train, that feeling was there immediately. I was in love with a scent. Yes, here too, the patchouli is blended with other (wonderful) accords. But everything fits together here, and the dark-warm patchouli keeps coming to the forefront despite all the other facets. This is my first review, so I’m not quite sure how to ultimately describe the scent or conclude the evaluation. Midnight Train is a dark-warm and earthy fragrance. It smells woody, of trees, firs, and cedars, and bittersweet honey. And beneath and above all this hangs a mist of that very dark-warm patchouli. Past: Alone on the train to nowhere. In the middle of the night. The tracks lead through the fog-covered autumn forest. Here and there a ray of the rising sun. Great scent, I've already ordered the 100ml at Selfridges and I look forward to every spray!

To create a composition as structured and layered as Laudano Nero requires an intricate understanding of raw materials, something the Terenzi family, with their long history in candlemaking, appears to possess. While the brand’s reputation may be tainted for some by its more commercially successful, but perhaps less nuanced, creations like Kirkè Extrait de Parfum , Laudano Nero stands out... and I suspect that there will be a few more in their catalogue, which I will need to sniff soon! Laudano Nero opens with a dark and boozy accord of absinthe and cognac, warmed by a smoky/leafy tobacco. This initial burst is complex, and you may need a few wears to understand what is effectively happening. After 1 hour or so, the scent evolves into a strong note of ash and a dry slate accord emerge, creating a rather unique stony texture. This is balanced by a subtle sweetness from acacia honey and a touch of rose, which adds a velvety quality without becoming overtly floral. As the fragrance settles, a rich resinous base reveals itself. Incense, labdanum, and a woody oud provide a deep foundation, while oak and vetiver contribute an earthy, grounded quality. The overall profile is an oriental spicy fragrance that has almost a "gothic feel". I usually avoid associations, as they may be very personal... but on this occasion I can make an exception. Laudano Nero evokes a feeling of walking through a dimly lit, historic street on a rainy autumn night, with the scent of wet stone, old wood, and embers in the air. This is a perfect fragrance for autumnal weather. Considering its composition's complexity and maturity, exceptional longevity (12+ hours on skin, 24+ hours on clothes) and strong projection, Laudano Nero is nothing short of an olfactory piece of art, a dark masterpiece.

Talking about amber perfumes wintertime is the best time of the year for taking them out into the cold world. At the end of November when winter starts to show its teeth I’m bringing out of hibernation my big dark ambers: Tom Ford’s discontinued Amber Absolute, Opus VI from Amouage and Ambra Mediterranea of Profumi del Forte. I love them all but, in my opinion, they are all still missing some sweetness that can bring softness to these beasts so I’m in a permanent quest for that big dark and sweet amber, my cashmere amber. Laudano Nero seems to be close to my ideal amber perfume. More than that, I think it’s the most complex amber scent I ever tried until now and it’s dark, really dark. It really deserves the word Nero The first notes burst very strong on my skin bringing out a boozy amber, cognac being easily recognized, with tobacco and some herbal touch of rosemary giving just a bit of stringency very well balanced by the sweetness of wormwood. There is also a hint of coffee in the top notes beside the cognac and tobacco and some licorice creating an almost gourmand sweetness. As the perfume further evolves the stringency from the top notes completely disappear and Laudano Nero becomes sweeter with a delicious chocolate note. In the same time a dark powdery vibe like cocoa dust appear on my skin making this perfume an ambery gourmand one surrounded by darkness.There is something vintage in this scent , it reminds me somehow of vintage Shalimar extrait not in the sense of having similarities in the way they both smell but in the sense of giving to the wearer the same feeling – sensuality and mystery. After the boozy amber and the dark chocolate accords another key note of Laudano Nero – the oud enters the stage. Far from having that medicinal sour smell the oud plays different in a soft manner. It contributes to the woody character of the base together with sandalwood still keeping the sweetness from the first notes and the softness with the help of vanilla and laudanum. During the first 2-3 hours it is a strong scent but in time it looses the strong character, after 6-7 hour changing into a skin scent that still lives for other 6 hours on my skin. Laudano Nero can be defined as a dark amber scent with gourmand and vintage vibe having oud facets. Compared with Tom Ford’s Amber Absolute which acts on the skin like a monothematic amber scent, Laudano Nero it is complex amber, evolving on the skin, in a constant change from the first masculine notes to the final soft and feminine notes. The feeling wearing this scent is like wrapping into a soft black cashmere blanket sitting in front of the fire place. In spite of the fact that is marketed as a masculine scent Laudano Nero is much more than a unisex amber, women who love amber will like it, its darkness lending to the person wearing this perfume a mystery aura. Amber lovers looking for a gourmand amber to keep warm during winter please do give a try to Laudano Nero and you will not regret.

Holy moly, this is awesome juice. Dark, masculine and smooth, but with just the right amount of bite. Laudano Nero opens with a sweet boozy tobacco. As it dried down, the sweetness pulled back (good thing) as did the booze. It became a very nice blend - not too sweet and not too boozy. As it further evolved, it became even drier/less sweet and the tobacco started to disappear as well. In its place, incense and woody notes became more prominent with a touch of vanilla. The incense did not stand out in a rough sort of way (i.e. Interlude Man) but contributed to the whole. Throughout most of Laudano Nero's life, it impressed me more as a woody scent. The tobacco retreats and disappears. There were occasional whiffs of the boozy note, but it wasn't obvious all the time. Very enjoyable to experience the fragrance as it evolved. Longevity is very good. It was still noticeable the next day, 18 hours after applying it. My morning cardio reactivated it and I had another nice scent bubble surrounding me. After a shower, it was still detectable, nose to skin. Sillage is strong with projection out about 6 feet or so. It wasn't beast mode/filling the room after about the first hour, which can be a good thing. Also, quite attractively priced. I'm going to pick up a bottle for myself.

Ahh, what a smell ... Mr. Terenzi (Tiziana's brother) is a genius. I do not know a stronger and more lasting fragrance that develops and changes so beautifully. The beginning is very strong, pungent, narcotic alcohol-tobacco, wood-incense ... after a dozen or so minutes you can feel wood, sweetness, resin, incense and conifers and delicately passes to the smell of oud, incense (but how beautiful and ambiguous) and musk. A wonderful, rich narcotic and addictive transformer. It is often compared to Black Afgano. For me, there is something to it to some extent - this power, darkness, transformation and the sweetness of resins that appears, but LAUDANO NERO is different and unique in its version. After various tests, there are similarities to John Vervatos-Dark Rebel, but the Dark Rebel can smell for 2 hours, and LAUDANO NERO is a MONSTRUM that can smell for more than 12 hours and has a rich fragrance. The smell is definitely not easy - if you like Black Afgano, Fortis and smells lined with oud and tobacco (Oud Wood, Tobacco Oud by Tom Ford, Leather Blend by Davidoff, Dark Aoud by Montale, Versace Oud Noir) and darker fragrances - it's worth buying , and especially when the price will be bargain (there are cool sales of this masterpiece). Otherwise - it is worth trying the castings / samples.

The King invites those to his realm to wed his daughter if they can produce a fragrance that will overpower and overwhelm those who smell it to beg allegiance to him to know its secrets. He is beautiful, he is overwhelming, he is inviting you back to keep being overwhelmed. He is natural so to not be repugnant, he is sly as to sneak up on you and make your anosmia make you think he isn't present in every corner of every place you have walked. I get it, this could be a scent any middle eastern person would poo-poo, however those in the west do not get their olfactory senses on anything like this 99+% of the time. This is not the one to rule them all, however, this one rules them all. Period. If you want to make a statement, this will make it. If you want to be the only one, this is the one. If you want everyone to know you, this will be the target on your back, your neck, your forehead and chest. No one will un-notice you for sure. You want attention, spray this twice, you want to overwhelm a room, spray this thrice, you want to own every single lung in the vicinity, spray this quadruple and await the response. Dark, alluring, sweet, deep. This frag is many things but fresh or citrus. Forget any mall scent and I granted, I have not indulged in designer dark scents, but I went straight to the dark side. Laudano Nero, if you know, you know.

Tiziana Terenzi is an Italian brand with a catalog that will overwhelm Guerlain and Dior with its numbers. I am still debating if Terenzi is a creative powerhouse, or a glorified dupe house that makes perfumes resembling popular fragrances in the market. But if you search hard, you will find excellent perfumes in their collection.

"The most bohemian stop on this unforgettable journey is the mythical Paris during a rainy autumn day, but warm with winding watercolours, blended as in painting by Renoir. The smell of the rain beating on the slate roof mixes with the stone streets lit by dim lights. A small fire at a crossroads of Montmartre heats musicians and acrobats that await tourists after the rain.

Black Laudanum historic medicine containing approximately 10% powdered opium by weight. And yeah there is something narcotic here. There is much of everything here, the opening is so rich that it is overflowing, sweet notes of alcohol, quality one like brandy, cognac with notes of gum, hot plastic.

My skin does reject the labdanum note, so I was surprised when I could smell something with this perfume! Then I took a look at the notes. Ah, of course. No labdanum. But it smells very great anyway, I'm a sucker for absinth. It's very gothic, very persistent, very sensual.

better step aside A lotta men didn't, a lotta men died So goes it somewhat martial in the great song "16 Tons" by Tennessee Ernie Ford. A hefty 16 tons of resin, wood, and smoke were processed in the creation of "Laudano Nero." The nonchalantly delivered hardness fits perfectly with this black labdanum, which effortlessly slices through my skull with a perfidious smile.

Don't be fooled into thinking that Prada Tendre is just a lighter version of the original. They are completely different compositions. While Prada is rather heavy and oriental, Prada Tendre is mostly soft woods and lively citrus resting on an element of fragile femininity. I like that this fragrance is smooth and easy to wear. It is unique without being too strange and 'in-your-face'. Gentle is a word that comes to mind when describing Prada Tendre. Prada Tendre starts off quite green and fresh, with the citrus signalling that Summertime is around the corner. Soft and sweet jasmine rounds the scent out nicely in the heart, where the vetiver and tea notes add variety and prevent this fragrance from smelling too predictable and common. The amber, which makes the original so popular, has obviously not been disregarded in this fragrance, however although it is still a dominant note in the drydown, it is not as strong. The patchouli however does give Prada Tendre that earthy feel that the original Prada succeeded in so well. I can't say that this is the best fragrance in regards to lasting strength, but honestly I'm not too fussed so I see no point in going on about it. Overall, Prada Tendre is a pleasantly sweet and feminine fragrance, which for some will be a Spring/Summer alternative when the original Prada proves too heavy for the warmer months.

Prada Tendre does its name justice. It is soft and warm from the beginning. Very harmonious scent which lingers quite long, even after washing my hands it is still there. But after about 2 hours I can not get rid of a certain memory. I know this scent from somewhere…. It’s not directly Angel, more Lancaster (the bath series). The amber-vanilla-very soft musky background is softer, not quite as strong as in the Lancaster but very similar. And I like it. What could you say against Prada? Exactly….

The Prada Tendre is my absolute favorite among all Prada fragrances, but unfortunately, it is only available in Germany as leftover stock from a few perfumeries online. The scent starts off very citrusy, somewhat green, cool, and fresh, but quickly transitions into a slightly spicy, warm note. The jasmine remains calm. The base is powdery sweet, but not overly sugary; it is subtly enhanced by the benzoin resin that emits a vanilla, honey-like scent and warm sandalwood. Cocoa doesn’t seem to be present, though I perceive it very subtly. Tea leaf, vetiver, and cedar give it a green character, which is rounded out by the warm notes. It’s actually difficult to describe, but all in all, it results in a bitter, warm, subtle, powdery fragrance that I have never smelled before. It smells expensive, elegant, and is not overpowering, even though it is very intense. With this fragrance, I feel secure and comfortable at events in a "more refined environment," and I have made no mistakes in my choice of perfume. An extraordinary, elegant scent with an aphrodisiac effect on the gentleman in a suit, it is a true "Prada masterpiece," as we have come to expect from Prada!

Prada Tendre's top note is hardly tendre (French for soft), as it bursts with elegantly sparkling citrus notes. This first impression of the fragrance reminds one of the initial spray of colognes and thus has a slightly masculine touch, and perhaps for some, a slightly conservative vibe - greetings from 1811. After about two minutes, the citrus notes almost completely fade away, allowing the tea leaves to become noticeable, which, together with jasmine, etc., smells complex yet somehow simple, fresh, light, and transparently herb-spicy. Over time, the fragrance gains a bit of sweetness and thus also a sprightly femininity, which becomes increasingly powdery in the dry down until one is gently enveloped by a soft-fresh-woody aura, in which the patchouli can also be quite well recognized. (On my skin, I do not perceive the strong sweetness and heaviness described by others, nor the cocoa note.) Prada Tendre is one of my absolute favorite scents. It has surprising similarities in the base to Coco Mademoiselle, which is not negative for me at all, as Coco Mademoiselle has been something of my signature scent for years. Prada Tendre is a more robust and lighter fragrance that still has a more pronounced tomboy edge already known from CM. This makes it overall less playful and more mature, giving it the best chance to replace the young Coco for me. While the young CM winks and calls: "Look at me...", her big sister Prada Tendre is more serious and subtle in her art of seduction. The word "sophisticated" hits the nail on the head, in my opinion. Ultimately, Coco becomes a scent for special occasions, going out, and particularly colder temperatures for me. Prada Tendre, on the other hand, will be my daily, fresh-powdery companion - one that simply always fits! Those who prefer it less discreet and like it to sparkle and shine should generally reach for the more radiant Coco Mademoiselle in my opinion. Prada Tendre smells to me like the perfect fragrance for young, modern women in everyday life. One will not find overly sweet, rosy femininity here, but only subtly floral-spicy freshness. Usually, the most beautiful and beloved scents are the hardest to describe, and I seem to lack the right words for the impression that Prada Tendre conveys to me, so I wholeheartedly recommend testing it. Just a little note: Prada Tendre is particularly inexpensive online (e.g., the beautiful large refillable bottle with the lovely dark red vaporizer starting at 55 euros) and is therefore, especially considering that Prada always uses very high-quality ingredients, a true bargain!

Finally, I have Prada Tendre in my collection. It is no longer available everywhere and is hard to find. The top note starts off herbaceous-citrusy, which could last a bit longer; a moment later it becomes floral-spicy, although I don't really pick up on the jasmine. It becomes milder, powdery, and softer, developing into an elegant, understated scent. Hats off to such mastery. I told you, it's Prada. The base is similar, but only the base, as with Coco Mademoiselle, I must admit, I just find Coco M. a bit fresher and more unique. Patchouli and sandalwood let this scent fade out without sweetness, by no means too strong or too woody. Rather subtle, yet present. Prada Tendre is for me a spring-summer scent; in winter it would be too light for me. The classic Prada is better suited then. Regarding longevity, I would wish for a longer wear time, but since this scent is meant to be more understated, it could also be that I no longer perceive it myself, while others do. It is wearable every day and suitable for all age groups. Definitely a scent worth trying and not an ordinary one!

~ Inspiration ~ I really wanted to press the spray pump :D ~ Bottle ~ Elegant and classic. It is kept simple, but with the spray pump, it’s a real eye-catcher. The pink color only matches the scent once it has fully unfolded. ~ Scent ~ When sprayed, it is very citrusy and spicy. Unfortunately, it’s not really my thing.

I received a few samples of this and tested them, even though it is a pure women's perfume. I know Prada by Prada, which is good but a bit intense. With this fragrance, I strangely perceived a strong cocoa note. Not sweet at all, just like, for example, dark chocolate or very fine cocoa powder. That came through very quickly. I perceived the top note as citrusy.

It really caught me off guard back when it was launched. Sprayed it on. Well, okay then. But then. Fresh, warm, the cool-delicate combination of jasmine and cardamom, the woody warm ambered drydown. I love this scent. My big problem: it’s no longer available. But, my bottle is still half full....for special moments.

Prada Tendre is once again a perfume that I really like. I would definitely recommend this perfume to fragrance fans who love citrus-floral scents with an oriental-spicy touch for a test!! As far as I can remember, it resembles Prada v. Prada (I tested it when it was released;)), although it was more intense and spicier!

I imagined Prada Tendre quite differently - a touch lighter would have been desirable. The scent also feels somewhat familiar to me. However, I am searching for the chocolate. Admittedly, one encounters a sweetness from the vetiver, which, combined with some citrus notes, can remind one of orange dark chocolate with a lot of imagination.

A very fresh opening with the Bergamot, Orange and Ginger medley, sitting on a soft subtle Rose which adds more to the pungent blast of freshness. The Vetiver adds a grassy, smoky texture which rounds off the sharpness from the cocktail of citric elements and always stays as the most prominent note. A little too prominent for my liking as it smells a bit too grey, smoky and a tad synthetic. This smells like a more polished D and G the one Grey. Not a lover of it though. But it's a well blended scent. The overdose of Vetiver ruined it for me

Had a terrible day? Is the weather really disgusting? Then a few spritzes of Infusion de Vetiver are just what you need. I guarantee: a sudden uplift in mood, a spreading sense of well-being. Vacation feelings and euphoric states cannot be ruled out. All very desirable side effects of this infusion! Prada hasn’t just brewed any old vetiver water here, but has created a small olfactory masterpiece of a short vacation. Zesty ginger, invigorating citrus components, bergamot, rose - all of this hits my nose practically immediately and triggers a fireworks display of wonderful associations. Vacation, sun, warmth, a glass of wine in hand, wind rustling through the grasses, serenity, relaxation. I’m sticking my nose to my wrist and letting my soul dangle..

The travel exodus has begun - and the last stragglers are at least packing their bags. I belong to those who stayed at home, tending to the familiar soil. But trips to the perfumery are a must. What do I come across? A vetiver from Prada? I wouldn't have expected such a bright, clean start. The vetiver note is downright fizzy on my skin - pleasant like champagne. The ginger is spicy and not sharp, and the neroli cools. Champagne in an ice bucket. But slowly the vetiver dims down - through the addition of dark red roses. A beautiful, interesting progression, interwoven with light bergamot. Even here in the coal district, I smell Mediterranean landscapes. Why wander far - see, the good lies so close. Thanks to Prada for the short trip!

A forest, bright and friendly. Birches and beeches grow there. The light trunks reflect the sunlight. The soft rustling of the leaves, which move with every breath of wind, fills the air. It smells spicy, lightly of iris and rose, and a little earthy. The opening of the fragrance Infusion de Vetyver by Prada has something dynamic and fluid about it. As it develops, a gentle calm sets in, reminiscent of a pleasant, mild afternoon in the woods. After an extended walk, you arrive at a log cabin that invites you to linger. You sit outside on a clearing on wooden benches and tables, enjoying afternoon coffee. Aromatic, bitter, mossy, earthy autumn air surrounds you. The bark of the trees and the grass and herbs of the clearing release this scent, which encourages you to breathe deeply and savor it down to the last molecule, allowing you to relax. The rustic yet playful aroma of Infusion de Vetyver also has something refined, even elegant about it, which made my nose "perk up," so I would love to add this perfume to my collection. Now that it’s getting cooler, it would be a good opportunity to lift my spirits into a cheerful autumn mood. Autumn is already one of my favorite seasons because it is so colorful, often mild, and always varied and diverse. A fragrance like Infusion de Vetiver perfectly captures this mood for me. The Eau de Parfum has very good longevity and sillage and becomes softer, slightly powdery, and rounder. With autumn roses!!!! A very successful fragrance variant by Daniela Andrier, who has already hit the mark with Infusion de Iris (which I have) (Spring)!!!

WOW is my reaction whenever I wear this perfume. It is exquisite from the very first spray right until it fades. Delox is EVERYTHING I wanted Gentle Fluidity Gold to be and then more. Yes, it is similar to Intense Cafe/Roses Vanille etc, however more refined. Please note that I do love Roses Vanille and this scent profile in general, I just think Delox has a refined edge to it. The honey note adds just the right amount of nuance to the fragrance and mixed with the vanilla + coffee creates this airy sweetness. The perfume is sweet without being juvenile! I can totally see it working in different settings/seasons. The performance is beautiful! I also think the price point is fair for what you get, and even better when bought discounted. Delox has quickly made it into my Top 10 and is likely to remain there. Absolutely stunning!

This perfume by Tiziana Terenzi is a great addiction to the amber roses perfumes with coffee. Here though we can also smell honey and the quality ingredients. For more details please watch this Youtube video here below where I am reviewing it and comparing it to Montale Intense Cafe and Intense Cafe Ristretto. I am also commenting on similar amber and rose perfumes. Hope it's helpful!

Delox is a conventional rose vanilla from Tiziana Terenzi, designed by Paulo Terenzi. Tiziana Terenzi is a brand that feels very confused and confusing. From the notes listed on their website, many of their perfumes seem assembled robotically without a clear sense of direction. Is their business model to be a clone house that makes expensive copies of well-known perfumes? However, as the infinite monkey theorem states, you can produce some masterpieces when you make a large number of perfumes. Delox may not be a classic, but it is definitely very good. This review is based on a full bottle I bought from Jomashop for $68. The opening notes listed on the website are iris, hyacinth and coffee. You will miss the coffee note if you blink. Apparently, there is some similarity with Montale Intense Cafe because of the coffee and rose notes. But the coffee note is so fleeting that I would just delete it from the olfactory pyramid. Many reviews and the description on the website made me expect a coffee scent, and I had to check the bottle to make sure that it was really Delox. However, the opening is interesting for its own merit. I get rose, vanilla and a davana-like accord in the start. I assume that this davana note is coming from hyacinth and iris, but it subsides quickly. There is also a wine note in the opening, which may be familiar to some from Frederic Malle Rose Tonnerre but without the sourness. The heart notes are primarily rose and vanilla that continues strong for many hours. The myrrh that is listed as a heart note is not perceptible to me. When we get to the base notes and dry down, both the rose and vanilla are still present in good amounts. But I can smell minor hints of amber, musk and woody notes also. The performance of Delox is very good. I can smell the rose and vanilla for 8-10 hours on my skin. The sillage is good at a few feet distance for the first 3-4 hours. Remember that most others will smell this as a rose vanilla. Finance theory states that the markets decide what a product is worth, based on supply and demand. Delox is worth the $68 I paid, but not the price listed on their website. I recommend Delox for someone looking for a vanilla-scented strong rose, with some minor ancillary notes. This choice can be an issue if you have other rose perfumes. I have Elie Saab Essence No. 1 Rose and Bon Parfumer 106 that are nearly identical to Delox, as well as Rose Tonnere, Portrait of a Lady and Noctambule that are roses with very different personalities. So many roses, so little time!

I got a 2ml sample of it. I like the scent because it just smells identical to Intense Cafe. I love Intense Cafe and its lasting power. I got a full bottle of Intense Cafe already. So I won’t be getting a full bottle of Delox. I don’t want to get 2 bottles of the exact same smell of perfumes in my collections. Delox has about the same performance of the Intense Cafe. Not any better or worse. Seems they’re just clones of the each other (I don’t know who cloned who). Maybe when I finish my Intense Cafe then I will consider getting it.

By now, I know so many fragrances that smell quite similar to "Delox." So far, I have tested several scents from Tiziana Terenzi. I liked and still like them in their opulence. There’s no fidgeting or half measures. Terenzi fragrances are straightforward; exuberant and lavishly used ingredients, well composed yet almost grotesquely exaggerated, the perfumes feel altered, even surreal. You either love it or find it dreadful. That’s my perception. There are "no prisoners taken," as they say; either you fall for it or you are enchanted. Now, here comes "Delox." But as often happens with fragrances whose descriptions I read from the vendors, I am disappointed. No, "Delox" is not a shallow little water. But I wonder why this brand has brought out such a scent only in "powerful." Below, it states in a statement that it is identical to "Lira" by Xerjoff. I can partially confirm that. What I smell first are very sweet fruits, definitely with acidity and a lot of vanilla. To my nose, the fruity scent is the fruity-floral Osmanthus. These two scent components remain strongly present throughout. Then I immediately smell cumin and hope that woody notes, bitter roasted coffee aroma, and resinous elements will develop. But only the acidity intensifies, although a bitter floral honey note holds its ground. Acacia honey could smell like this. (not to be confused with Robinia honey, as robinia is often referred to as acacia). I do not smell coffee. Only a somewhat quirky beautiful powdery-creamy floral blend that occasionally reminds me of Ylang-Ylang and Labdanum. Rose is also an option. I list all this. However, the progression of "Delox" is such that the individually described scent notes and groups do not behave like a pyramid but rather repeat themselves. Sometimes I smell the sour Osmanthus with the strong vanilla, then more of the flowers, then it smells more of cumin again. But basically, summed up, it is for me a strong version of all those fruity-gourmand fragrances that are currently "en vogue." From the "Prada Candy fragrances" to "La Vie est Belle" or the "Lira" by Xerjoff mentioned in the statement below. The list can be extended. Certainly well made, "Delox" leaves nothing to be desired in terms of clarity, longevity, and sillage. Also, "Aoud Velvet" by Montale goes in that direction, but surprisingly, I liked it right away. I find it, however, more austere, subtle, and not so aggressively gourmand. Whereupon the knowledgeable saleswoman, based on her assessment, not unreasonably gave me a sample of "La Vie est Belle" to take with me. (Do I hear someone laughing or wrinkling their nose? Well, I left the LVEB sample for room service with a corresponding "steel stamp with numbers" underneath in the hotel room; it’s not a cheap scent. Maybe someone enjoyed it) I also cannot grumpily claim that "Delox" is an unpleasant perfume. But "Delox" is really too intense for me. Above all, I actually miss antagonists like woody notes, resin, something bitter. It is stated as an intention in the pyramid, but unfortunately, I do not perceive it. Without a doubt, "Delox" is a feminine perfume.

My first niche fragrance.... Simply unforgettable like first love, first own apartment, or first drive without an instructor ;) Delox catapulted me quite roughly into the world of precious perfumery. At that time, I couldn't really recognize the individual notes of the pyramid, and so my first thought was "Noble!

LOVE! When I first had a tester and tried it out in winter, I noticed during my walk that these little scent clouds that kept rising suddenly enchanted me. Such a sweet floral honey scent with a subtle coffee note. It left me speechless.
First of all: I love the fragrances from Tiziana Terenzi! They all convince me with their quality, intensity, longevity, and sillage. "Delox" is an oriental fragrance (like all of Terenzi's scents).

How different our noses are! I definitely smell Gentle Fluidity Gold by MFK here, my husband smells Spirito Fiorentino by Tiziana Terenzi. However, we both have scents that remind us of it, and therefore it will not be joining us. Anyway, it smells very good. I don't smell coffee, but rather lightly honey-soaked flowers. Sweet but not overpowering.

A review is needed for this fragrance. Absolutely … because this scent deserves it (and just to be clear: even though it won't become my fragrance). I'll start from the back: The bottle is high-quality, heavy, fits well in the hand, and sprays nicely. Longevity and sillage are gigantic.

Yes, it resembles the Dolce & Gabbana Light Blue and to a lesser extent Fierce (imagine 70% - 30% mix). Obviously, it is an unfair comparison: the above two frags are designer while Paolo is working with a different budget. Very Italian, citrus-floral-aromatic-slightly woody with a pinch of ozonic and slightly airy salty accord. High quality, no chemical overload here, very natural smelling. Not very original, due to the above resemblance but very nice, easy to wear, likable scent. Great performance, unlike current formulations of the two above. So if you like D&G Light Blue and Fierce, blind buy safe. If not, you still might like this but try first.This also reminds me of Percival but I strongly prefer Foconero to the above, really. :)

Foconero opens with a citrusy blast that's quickly replaced by a generic floral scent. Looking at the notes, I can imagine that it would be combo of lily of the valley and hyacinth. Not particularly attractive. Dries down into a generic woody scent. I supposed Foconero can be called light and fresh because there's nothing there. Projection is almost zero. However, as a skin scent almost from the get go, it does have decent longevity around 7 to 8 hours. Although the bottle price is OK, I'm rating it expensive because it's not worth that much. More along the lines of $20 tops.

Foconero is different from the typical summer scent, it's a little bit citric without being a citric perfume, it is a little salty without being marine, it has class, elegance, body, nothing garish, for me it is the sensation that leaves a cocktail of these thick with a little citrus peel, and the salty edge. I don't know if the full price is excessive to be honest, as a perfume I find it very cool, elegant and wearable, but apart from that it brings back memories of when I was visiting Milan one June and we had a cocktails evening, with people well dressed, on the terrace, with the river, the music, the good vibe, that's Foconero. But there will be people who will find one more salty fresh perfume.

Salty citrus with an aromatic spicy herbal side. This is a straightforward and stiff scent with strong sillage. People comparing it to cat piss are not wrong. This is a niche fragrance and not a safe blind buy. It is somewhat similar to Parfums de Marly Percival, but different in character: Percival is quiet, this is rather aggressive.  of my perfume reviews at The Scent Stories: thescentstories.substack.com

Something new from me. The Foconero from the house of Terenzi. This brand is really cool, even if some people don’t quite warm up to it. Stylistically, this brand has its own signature that you have to like. In my opinion, perfumer Paolo really knows his stuff. Creations that are simply very catchy and usually have bomb performance as Extrait de Parfums, even freshies like this one. This Classic line in black with the wood look is still the "cheapest" line. Some cost over 600 euros, most around 200 to 300 euros for 100ml. The Classic line is regularly available for 175 euros, but often between 50 and 70 euros cheaper in some online stores. Definitely worth it, as these are Extraits that perform well. I bought this one at the end of last year. Pretty much in winter, but this one works all year round. Even though it probably works best on warmer days, you can't go wrong with it in any weather. I also recently bought "Percival | Parfums de Marly." It is listed here as a scent twin, but I don’t see it as closely related to this Foconero. Nevertheless, they fall into pretty much the same genre: a pleasant daytime scent that never strays too far from the norm. Fresh, spicy, pleasant, and cheerful. Definitely scent types that you can use daily and not just wear 2-3 times a year. If you want a more agreeable, noble scent, you should definitely reach for Percival. A great scent that is less abrasive and simply accompanies you pleasantly throughout the day. Now back to the Foconero: I tested this a few months ago via a decant. I like these Fierce Cologne -like scent types, although the original doesn’t convince me as much anymore. The initial notes are quite pleasant and predestined for a daily freshness. Since one often orients oneself to twins, I ordered a small sample of this Foconero. At first, it wasn’t love at first sniff. However, over time, I liked it significantly better. It spreads good vibes and is simply a great companion. I couldn’t find significant similarities to Fierce and Percival; scent type yes, DNA no. I rather recognize vibes from "Vodka on the Rocks | Kilian," along with classic vibes like those of "Insensé Ultramarine (Eau de Toilette) | Givenchy." Overall, very unique and not too similar to any other scent. Foconero has quite a large pyramid. It smells a bit more complex, but without being overwhelming. An easy-to-wear scent with Italian influences. Lots of citrus, juicy, juniper. As it develops, a maritime-salty freshness comes into play. Very interesting and pleasant. Additionally, a subtle spiciness and a lot of soft wood. For me, it’s thoroughly enjoyable. Similar to "Kirkè | Tiziana Terenzi," this one also has nerve potential if you don’t like the Terenzi signature. Similar to Kirke, Foconero is a scent that comes across much better in the air than when smelled up close. You should definitely test it, as a blind buy would be quite risky. Much riskier than the more agreeable Fierce & Percival. In the statements, I read about sweat notes. I can't confirm that. Perceptions can vary greatly with many scents.
