The drydown after many hours is a bit dull, but I couldn't detect any sweat. The best thing about this scent, in my opinion, is the performance. It’s annoying how these wonderful top notes in the freshness category fade too quickly. It can be very useful in leisure time, but for a daytime scent, it’s rather bothersome if you don’t want to keep reapplying. The Extraits deliver, and this one does too. It easily lasts 8-10 hours with mostly grand sillage. Recommended. Unisex, I can agree, although it will appeal more to masculine types. A great choice for everyday and sporty activities. And that all year round. Worth a test if you like Terenzi and are looking for a scent with good performance in the freshness category. Between about 100 and 120 euros for 100ml, it’s definitely worth grabbing. Quite unique.

Italian flair, a beautifully thought-out fragrance that is very complex yet simple for me, because: Yes, the shower gel image is accurate. But I wonder what the problem is? (It's a matter of taste, of course!) Anyone who has ever used the shower gel "Duschdas For Men" (the blue one) might agree with me that there are great similarities, which I find very cool.

I have really tested quite a few aquatic fragrances. The result was mostly disappointing. Often, they were somehow scratchy, synthetic, or even musty. However, I prefer aquatics to be softer. In my youth, I wore Fierce very often. Unfortunately, it is now just a shadow of its former self, and I can no longer stand this scent.

I have only come across a few samples from Tiziana Terenzi so far. Therefore, I was eagerly anticipating a surprise, and that’s exactly what I got. With Foconero, I find no comparison to other scents I have tested. For a fougère, it is very well done. The layers are clearly recognizable to me.

Since Kirke completely missed the mark for me, I now have to write a review about Foconero, as it is a fantastic scent. I can describe it with a single word that couldn't be more fitting: Aquatic! But let's start from the beginning: At first, Foconero unfortunately doesn't blow me away. The lemon is there, but very artificial.

Foconero is a fresh-woody perfume that mentally transports me to a beach bar in Sardinia. The Extrait de Parfum begins with a splash of beautifully blended green and aquatic notes, laden with juniper and authentic citrus fruits like bergamot, lemon, and lime. As it develops, a tangy lemon and a soothing herbal tone remain present.

Sunshine in a bottle. It's lovely and uplifting with the refreshing Mandarin and sparkly Anis opening. Melded Into a creamy Soft Rose Base. Like a hybrid of Amande and Infusion Rose. I do get that suntan lotion vibe with the fluffy floral Mimosa . It's very feminine, slightly fruity but mainly floral fresh. Soft skin scent with moderate Sillage and Longevity.

Latest addition to "Les Infusions de Prada" to complete and round the circle of an absolute coherent concept. A small semi-niche collection of seven perfumes that had their beginning with the highly acclaimed Iris (possibly one of the cleanest perfumes created in the last decade). The nice thing about "Les Infusions" is that they all smell the same and different at the same time. This one smells like yellow flowers floating in cotton. Definitely a unisex fragrance for the soft and bold.

Anyone who knows me is aware that the mimosa, not just in scent, is a huge favorite of mine among plants. In fact, it leads the list of beloveds even before the rose. The sweetness, which is muted - not covered - by a certain bitterness; the fragility of the leaves - whether as mimosa or acacia - and the yellow spherical flowers: all of this represents the mimosa for me! But where is it in Prada's "Infusion de Mimosa"? In my opinion, it is dominated, if not completely overwhelmed, by the strong star anise aroma! I admit: I also avoid star anise in my kitchen; I don't like that certain scratchiness. Neither in sweet dishes nor in hearty meals. There are only a few fragrances where I can tolerate this spiciness. It happens. So, the mimosa is pushed into the background in the fragrance creation named after it - what a pity! Instead, a fresh, again slightly synthetic mandarin stands beside the star anise: both seem to want to demonstrate their camaraderie from Christmas recipes. Only a full-bodied rose scent can compete with these two; this makes the fragrance softer and less scratchy. The magic that makes the mimosa special for me is simply not present. I am very disappointed! That does not mean that "Infusion de Mimosa" is not a wearable fragrance. To claim otherwise would simply be unfair! Very clean, very pure, it envelops the wearer. The memory of a soothing bath followed by a generous application of fragrant body lotion comes to mind. The illusion of a long-lasting freshness, of cleanliness, is conveyed quite well here. Despite all its perceivable prickliness from the star anise and mandarin, "Infusion de Mimosa" is full-bodied and also has an average longevity. I do not wish to judge whether the price-performance ratio is right. It also turns out again that I have great difficulties with some of the Prada fragrances, even if they come from a similarly themed series. However, in this case, I personally resent how the mimosa has been "castrated". Why does this fragrance bear the name of a plant/flower that then has to take a backseat to a spice? There are surely lovers of "Infusion de Mimosa"; I will place my sample among the travel testers. Of course, I would be happy if it found its way to someone who appreciates it! This fragrance certainly deserves it - just not with me!

Okay, I really feel bad. I'm writing a comment here about a Prada fragrance for 80 euros and concluding that for me it’s actually more like a light body spray. The punchline: I've already written such a comment once, about a scent from the Aldi brand Anna Biondi. The two have one thing in common: they smell great, but not intense and certainly not long-lasting. Now, you can overlook that in a perfume for 4 euros, but for 20 times that...? I don't know. That said, I find the scent really beautiful; the enchanting mimosa is supported by fruity-sparkling mandarin (wonderful in summer!), feminine thanks to the totally unobtrusive rose, and finally rounded off by spicy-soft anise. I love anise in all variations, but I've already mentioned that in one of my previous comments. So I'm repeating myself! Prada Infusion de Mimosa could really have the potential to be a repurchase candidate and a go-to scent; in principle, it fits the office, leisure time, but also quite well for the evening. However, when I spray it on in the morning after bathing, I can hardly smell anything by the time I arrive at work. Very unfortunate! The infusion seems to consist only of NaCl with a splash of active ingredient.

It's been a long time since I tested a Prada fragrance. By that, I mean one of the Infusion scents, as there are already two new fragrances from this brand, L'Homme and La Femme. No, I'm talking about the wonderful Infusions, where you can immediately perceive the typical, slightly synthetic and slightly soapy-clean Prada note upon the first spray, which some philistines scream "Eww, soap!" and run away from. When I saw Infusion de Mimosa here on Parfumo, the fragrance immediately went on my watchlist, even though I had some concerns, as I normally expect a rather floral-stuffy scent from a mimosa. But after all, it says Prada combined with Infusion, so I'm still extremely curious about how this scent will turn out. I suspect, as always, that this fragrance will also reveal soapy components, which means that soap haters should already prepare to run away screaming :D The scent: There it is again. The unmistakable, clean Prada DNA that you can't smell in any other fragrance, just as I expected. This scent also starts with anise, which comes across as a bit unusual for those who aren't fond of anise. Nevertheless, the fragrance is also soft and slightly powdery (or rather creamy) and has a very light, sweet note in the background. Then you can soon smell the mimosas, which give off a floral-sweet scent, but do not smell stuffy as feared. The anise still has a slight presence, but most of it has long since faded away. The clean note smells, as always, like a fabric softener, but as mentioned, rather floral with a "mimosa flavor" instead of rosy, as I can't detect any rose notes at all. A little later, you still have a slightly floral mimosa scent under your nose along with the Prada DNA, but the fragrance then feels quite light, and you get the impression that something is missing, like a hint of sandalwood as a base, which could have benefited the scent. Unfortunately, a bit later, the Prada DNA completely bids farewell, leaving behind a slightly watered-down floral scent, which is nice but no longer special. Well, then you can just spray it on again. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is rather subtle, as with most fragrances here. Okay, the anise provides a slightly stronger start, but really only for a very short time. Otherwise, the fragrance is only detectable up close. A little later, I even find it somewhat close to the skin. The longevity is somewhat better, and you can smell the fragrance for eight hours, although, as mentioned, it becomes very weak later on. The bottle: The bottle has the same shape as all the Infusions. It is rectangular with rounded sides or edges and is filled with mimosa-yellow fragrance liquid. On the front, you can see the metallic Prada plaque. The cap is cylindrical and has the typical Prada "fabric cover," this time in yellow. The label is, as always, placed on the left (or right? Depending on where you look at the bottle from :D) side, which lists the fragrance name along with the ingredients. As always, a beautiful bottle. It seems that Prada never seems to go wrong with all the Infusion fragrances. Sure, there are one or two scents that some may not like as much, but overall, most are excellent fragrances that will appeal to those who have no aversion to being clean :D Unfortunately, with this scent, the sillage is weaker than the usual Infusions, and the well-known Prada DNA fades away a bit too quickly. At least, that's how it seemed to me. But well, it's suitable for summer and might come across better on warmer days. If it is still a bit too weak for someone, they can always create a decant for re-spraying. As usual, one appreciates not only the (soapy) cleanliness but also the soft side of the fragrance, as it initially smells creamy and then powdery. However, this is also something that saves the fragrance. Because if this Prada DNA were not present, the fragrance itself would still be nice but would come across as a bit too banal (as a simple but well-made floral scent among many). Mimosa lovers who are not dirty-minded (by that, I mean those who have nothing against soapy scents :D) will surely find pleasure in this fragrance. A test is still worthwhile for everyone.

freshly bloomed mimosa, delicate as a butterfly fluttering away in no time what remains is a filigree green rose & a hint of anise spice. Cheerful & bright, creamy-fine it sneaked into my heart. _______________________ I like the mimosa, a beautiful delicate flower. Its scent is not intoxicating or seductive.

this would be my absolute favorite fragrance ..... if it lasted longer than 2 hours. Since I can no longer smell the scent within a very short time, I also sprayed it on my clothes - after 2 hours, there was nothing left of the enchanting fragrance here either. Such a shame about the money, the perfume is not cheap.

First sensation is that we are smelling something serious, full of quality and complex, like a mix between the sweet oud sensation of Kemi by Kemi and Black Phantom. The opening is balsamic, leathery, with a sweet touch, some earthy feeling, it is sweet but not too much, and with oud, it has a green touch, bay leaf and pepper are noticeable, all very balanced. He manages to mix and create something, not just a succession of notes, as as it progresses he tends to a tobacco, with jacket-type leather and a pinch of honey. It seems that it may be an excessively heavy perfume but it's not, the balance is so good that everything is well integrated and it is one of those that surrounds you. Projection and performance, without complaints, high, you feel bursts all the time. It's a difficult perfume to classify, enveloping, a little sweet, a little fresh, a little dirty, trying it is very worthwhile.

Like the name says Chimaera (from Latin, from Greek Χίμαιρα - Chimaira) is a creature of Greek mythology. It is a monstrous creature, composed of parts of several beasts, parts of a lion, a goat and a snake And like the scent its very complicated you will smell so many things but ohh so nice. First spray is more spicy like black pepper, thyme, bay leaf and some lemon. As it settles, there is more of amber and iris, magnolia, honey and peony. Then, the dry downs to tobacco, patchouli and woody essence of some kind of a balsam and cashmere wood. I would say more of a men’s perfume Love this one, definitely worth to try.

I consider it a mass pleaser - many people notice it in the air and ask what it is. A bit too sweet and artificial/chemical for my taste, yet it's not that bad. But is this one really man-made? I cannot imagine a real person creating this. Also, "no oud" would play better than "cheap oud" in this case.

I have long been in possession of it. Chimaera,..the scent that is so hard to describe. The scent that harbors a primal force and whose complexity is very difficult to grasp for untrained, but also for very trained noses. For a long time, I have been toying with the idea of writing a comment that does this perfume at least some justice and conveys an impression of what one is dealing with here. Let's try it with the following scenario! Imagine! You are walking along a volcanic beach on a Mediterranean coast. Everything looks black and matte on the beach until suddenly something catches your attention in the sun. A fist-sized piece of lava that is completely different from the others iridesces in the sun because it is semi-transparent and consists only partly of molten lava, but also of amber-colored resins. When held in the sun, you can recognize various inclusions within it. But what makes it most unusual is the fact that it has a scent. This unique piece has absorbed everything that it rolled over as glowing-hot magma and has miraculously preserved it olfactorily. It smells of citrusy sage and various Mediterranean herbs like thyme, bitter bay leaf, and different spicy pepper varieties. Mineral notes can be detected like dusty-hot sand heated by the sun. Robust and dark honey mingles with floral nuances of waxy-soft magnolia and bitter-herbaceous saffron. Balsamic resins flow from cistus and creamy-buttery benzoin accompany. Patchouli in earthy-chocolate tones flashes through. Everything is enveloped with smoky tobacco-incense notes and powdery-soft cashmere wood. And ultimately wrapped in a leathery-satin layer of golden-glittering caramel. Conclusion Chimaera is like a fossilized piece of lava found on a Mediterranean coast that seems to live within and overwhelms one immensely with its multitude of olfactory wonders. Deciphering this scent is not easy, as the fragrance is highly complex and opulently structured. Chimaera is truly like a chimera or an illusion because you always perceive something different but never quite pinpoint anything exact. A legion of notes trapped in a core. Spices, flowers, resins, and woods sink into the smoky-charred caramel and are bound within until only a fragrant sound emerges. A continuous, constant, olfactory metamorphosis. An interplay of scent notes and impressions. It fits perfectly into the winter season, but it also works very well on a warm summer night or during a vacation on tanned skin. Even then, it is very changeable and adaptable. It is comparable to a chameleon. I personally wear-or let’s say “endure”-it more in private, as it calms me and almost dominates me. It almost forces me to let go. I have long since given up trying to understand it. Chimaera cannot be controlled or understood, but this fact makes it incredibly beautiful and mysterious! Perseverance is the chimera of love. Luc de Clapiers Vauvenargues

Paolo Terenzi has betrayed me. I saved Chimaera as the last sample from the special collection case because I thought it would be exactly my type. Pepper, leather, incense, iris, oud, and all the other delicious notes. But Chimaera smells quite different from what I had imagined; that's just how it is with fragrance pyramids. Nevertheless, Chimaera is beautiful, very beautiful indeed. I don't find it overloaded or "too much," as everything feels incredibly rounded and balanced; almost on the verge of becoming boring. Right from the start, the scent is spicy and sweet, with a slightly bitter nuance that I actually find very nice, creating a balance. After a while, nothing bitter remains. All the hard, spicy, earthy, smoky notes simply become caramelized. Pepper, leather, oud, and incense - these nuances can be recognized, but they have almost lost all contrast on my skin. This does not make Chimaera any less beautiful. Everything is very harmonious, noble, and pleasant. However, an Aha effect or a certain tension is largely absent; for that, it is certainly easy and uncomplicated to wear. The base reminds me a bit of a light leather couch, on which "Sahne-Muh-Muhs," or caramel candies, were eagerly eaten. In the distance, perhaps a slightly spicy-oriental scented candle is burning, but the couch-caramel candy scent dominates. Chimaera is wonderfully harmonious, cozy, and comforting. However, I find €285 instead of €135 for the other Terenzis to be unreasonable, as it doesn't seem to perform any better on me.

I am overwhelmed. A fan of simple scents. Perplexed by the number of ingredients in the fragrance pyramid. Exceptionally excited before the first spray of the sample. Excited because the fragrance pyramid alone does not provide any information about what scent might be hidden behind it. Oud, incense, caramel, patchouli.

Thanks to dear Aunt Lilly, I had the pleasure of experiencing this very exclusive fragrance. It’s the first time that I raise the white flag and capitulate in front of a scent due to its complexity and jumble of notes. However, I still tried to carve a path into the fragrance... during the first test, it blew my mind... there was a blue screen in my nose and brain...

At first, the opulence of this fragrance literally takes your breath away. It is unfathomable, so multifaceted and simply impossible to grasp. Due to its complexity, Chimaera is for me a fragrance kaleidoscope: constantly changing, always different, with new facets emerging. Chimaera is like a mischievous sprite that joyfully transforms itself.

After being quite taken with Tiziana Terenzi's "Orion," a sample of this highly-rated fragrance from the same house found its way into the ALZD package. I actually didn't want to test anything else in the evening, but a bit of variety was necessary, and shortly after it was on my skin, it became clear: I have something special here.

I was sooo curious about this fragrance, especially since so many interesting ingredients are represented.... Thanks to a dear perfumer, I was finally able to test the scent: The opening is very citrus-heavy... An absolutely authentic lemon note surrounds me, delicate, fresh, and not unpleasant....

Absolutely awful. Sickeningly sweet, like a cheap, nutty paste overloaded with sugar and artificial additives. No offense to anyone, but I honestly think it smells terrible! On top of that, it has nothing in common with the original Paradoxe fragrances, they might as well have released it as a completely new perfume rather than a flanker. I’m completely baffled — both by the scent itself and the logic behind it. A real shame, because the bottle looks stunning in this color!

A heavy floral opening rooted in neroli and orange blossom, which then transitions into photo-realistic salted pistachio against a background of creamy sandalwood. It’s rich, for sure. A touch bittersweet. Not really a gourmand in the highly dessert-like way that most are presented these days. The warm, floral undertones endure throughout and pick up again in the dry down, with just a hint of the OG Paradoxe DNA peeping through. I do feel like this scent was released at an odd time, because to me it’s natural season would be winter. At its heart it’s warm, smooth, and long-lasting, and just perfect for cold, crisp winter afternoons. I also feel like “unisex” might be a bit of a stretch, depending, of course, on your attitude to sweet florals. It is to my nose quite a feminine scent for the most part, except for the initial 40 minutes or so where I agree it strays quite far into more neutral territory. One to revisit later in the year. Update 20/12/25: Revisiting this one in winter, and (as suspected) I’m enjoying it much, much more. Its overall richness and salty, creamy pistachio are so much better suited to cold weather. A hug in perfume form.

If Paradoxe is Anastasia and Paradoxe Intense is Drizella, then Paradoxe Radical Essence is Cinderella. Outcasted, overlooked and hated on; yet unlike any of the others from this line. The stepsister so to speak. Radical Essence is the more interesting of the Paradoxe releases in my opinion. I don't acknowledge Virtual Flower, because I am against AI based formulas such as Phantom. This new edition of Paradoxe is unapologetically gourmand with a heavy pistachio note gently hugged by white flowers, neroli and orange blossom. Thanks to the nutty note and sandalwood I find this to be very unisex, but leaning slightly feminine in the dry down. It is unique in this market of designer fragrances, which appears to be a problem for many people. What's considered "nice" or worthy of hype is almost always safe, familiar or boring. The moment brands decide to do something avant-garde and out of the ordinary, people lose their minds. I have heard comparisons to feet, corn chips and other things I care not to mention. Fragrance IS subjective at the end of the day, but fragrance is also an art and cannot always be familiar or mass pleasing. Often, I'll say something is not for me and that doesn't necessarily mean it is a bad fragrance. Radical Essence is one of my favorite designer releases of the year, because for once L'Oreal Luxe did something a little daring.

I organized a sample of this new Paradox flanker Radical Essence and have already tested it extensively. My expectations were not very high due to the low ratings, but I was surprised. Here, Prada has once again done a really good job. Since Prada has been marketed by L'Oreal, things have shifted quite a bit into this mainstream direction. In the past, this brand had significantly more charm, but now and then, good things come out of this combo. The Paradox line is of course extremely mainstream, and the sales figures of this line make it really popular. But it is still a great line when it comes to mass appeal, trends, and also likability. Established women may not always be drawn to this Paradox line, but girls and young ladies will be well served here. This new Radical Essence has nothing to do with the original DNA but naturally uses the fame of the line. Here, as mentioned, a few words of praise for this flanker. The flanker naturally uses this bottle like all in this line, here in a slightly darker red. It's quite cool, but also very typical mainstream. Prices are still quite hefty like all new releases in the designer sector, especially for women. However, they will certainly stabilize. The scent uses a pyramid with 4 notes. It seems modern to release small pyramids with 2-4 notes, but secretly more is included. Roughly, this pyramid captures this scent. The star is of course the roasted and salted pistachio. Pistachio has been the hype note in fragrances in recent years, likely due to the Dubai chocolate hype. Regardless of trends, I find this warm note very beautiful and also timeless. This slightly salty note has a great interesting touch and is not only suitable for the colder season. Additionally, there is a wonderful soft orange blossom note that brings this feminine floral note into play. This floral note is very modern, soft, and also sensual. More freshness is brought in by neroli, and these neroli-orange blossom combos harmonize very well anyway. There is also sandalwood in the base, which produces a well-groomed, sensual wood note. Even though this scent is rather linear, there is certainly another sweet component present. The sweetness is more soft rather than sticky or too heavy, making it quite suitable as a transitional scent. The scent is also relatively synthetic, but I find it well made and not much worse in this regard than other designer releases. Overall, it is very coherent and also a crowd-pleaser. Performance is quite good like all in this series. You get a minimum of 8 hours, and the sillage is quite good. Great for leisure, evening, and also for everyday wear when it fits. Overall, a great release that is a bit overpriced for what is offered. If the prices drop a bit, I can recommend this release, especially for younger ladies. Certainly not niche quality, but this scent does its job very well and is made more for the masses.

I was really excited about this version of Paradoxe and finally got to test it on my wrist today. Right after spraying, the pistachio comes through with full force, which I really liked. Then the Paradoxe DNA joins in, pushing the pistachio note into the background, making it very overpowering for about 5 minutes. The impression might also have been influenced by the weather, as the air was humid and warm. After that, the scent becomes increasingly gentle and in the drydown is beautifully nutty-creamy, no longer reminding me of the original Paradoxe, but rather a wonderful pistachio-sandalwood blend. I kept my nose close to my wrist to catch the scent :) I think on cool days in autumn/winter it will be even more beautiful.

... a young Greek woman goes to the Pistachio Festival in Greece. She walks through the various stalls that are there with different products made from this little nut. Cheese, ham, liqueurs, schnapps, or even bread and butter. The aromas are simply enchanting.

I love this perfume. It is definitely something special and has really nothing to do with the original Paradoxe anymore. It smells gourmand, nutty, creamy, and just delicious. Very profound. And not too sweet. Longevity and sillage are good. I find the price way too high. The bottle is great.

Today, thanks to a sample, I had the chance to test the new Prada Paradoxe Radical Essence and was curious about how, or if, the salty pistachio would harmonize with the floral notes. It harmonizes. Very well, in fact, I think. Right from the first spray, you get a pistachio cream with a hint of salt in your nose. However, this is overall a very short pleasure.

I'm currently wearing a sweater that still smells of burdèl; I sprayed it on my wrist 3 days ago to compare or test 2 or 3 fragrances, as I often do :) And the perfume is still very noticeable on the sweater. I do this from time to time with all kinds of scents and samples I have. But how does Burdèl smell? Opening. Shortly after spraying, it smells as wonderful as hardly anything else. Bergamot, fresh spices, a bit cool, lightly sweet, and in the background, those woody notes. It already strongly reminds me of "Oud Stars - Alexandria II (Parfum) | XerJoff"; the oud remains woody, dry, clean, and never goes in a barn-like or dirty direction. Thus, even oud newcomers will enjoy this scent. You immediately notice the high concentration of the perfume; it leaves an oily film on the skin. The opening is, for me, the most beautiful part. A solid 10. The further development. The freshness and fruitiness slowly fade into the background, and the woody and spicy notes come to the forefront. However, Burdèl always has this fresh bergamot in the scent development, at least on me. And this is exactly what distinguishes it from "Oud Stars - Alexandria II (Parfum) | XerJoff". Together with vanilla, a slight sweetness comes in, but it's beautifully done. Very elegant, yet sexy. Never intrusive or too much of a good thing, although the performance is truly convincing. The delicious lemon cake description fits it well, as many describe. This perfume is almost perfectly balanced. A 9 Drydown In the drydown, it only changes marginally. It remains woody, slightly fruity, sweet, and above all, sexy. It radiates something that I find very attractive and erotic, especially in the drydown. You keep smelling your arm; at least, that's how it is for me :) It could be the cardamom with vanilla and the oud that makes it so delicious. Conclusion. Burdèl clearly reminds one of "Oud Stars - Alexandria II (Parfum) | XerJoff" (provided, of course, you know the XerJoff) :D However, wearing both simultaneously allows you to recognize the differences better. For me, it is more masculine, fruitier, and fresher, thus having that certain extra that I felt was missing in AlexII. It is not a dupe, but rather a new interpretation or further development. The similarity doesn’t bother me; I am, of course, more than satisfied with it, as you can gather from my review :) The XerJoff is a wonderful perfume. And I love the scent. Nevertheless, TT has managed to improve an almost perfect scent with Burdèl. Personally, that was exactly what I felt was missing in Alex. If you own Alex, you don’t need to rush out to buy Burdèl. With Alex, you have a unisex classic that will always be special. People who didn’t like AlexII will also not like Burdèl. They are too similar. The bottle is beautiful, the sprayer average, the presentation excellent. The price on sale is unbeatable. (Please don’t pay €390 for it) Performance well above average. Almost wearable all year round; in too warm temperatures, I would recommend something else. Unisex - masculine. Age from 25 - XX Disco, bar, restaurant, or whatever. Almost always wearable. For sports or grocery shopping, it is too fine and special; better to take something lighter and cheaper for that :) It will probably never become as popular as "Oud Stars - Alexandria II (Parfum) | XerJoff", but those who can discover it will certainly not regret it :) Thank you for reading Best regards, Deniz

I want to address the headline right away as a preface. The word Burdel unfortunately means brothel in Polish. Although the perfume has an accent on the E, I still find the name poorly chosen and it surely has led to some strange looks from certain people. Burdèl was a blind buy for me, as there are simply no decants of Burdèl available in the Souk, and it is truly difficult to find a decant or sample of Burdèl otherwise. The packaging is, as is typical for the Anniversary Collection, very lavishly designed; whether that is necessary, I doubt, especially since the lettering on my packaging was already peeling off a bit. These huge packages lead to a completely different problem for me. I’m slowly running out of space for all these large Tiziana Terenzi packages. But I’ve bored you long enough, and it’s finally time to talk about the scent. Burdèl is truly exceptional. Everyone knows the usual bergamot or citrus top notes, which we have all probably smelled countless times. Burdèl combines the bergamot note with a hefty dose of spices. I particularly like the Syrian cumin combined with cardamom. The top note is absolutely unique and perfectly combines freshness with spices. As it develops, the spices increasingly take the lead. However, after about 1 hour, a gentle oud note also comes into play, which brings a bit of sweetness through amber and vanilla. This combination makes Burdèl suitable for people who do not like oud. I cannot really recognize the notes of the heart; Burdèl rather makes a leap from the top note to the base note. The performance is really very good; I could still perceive Burdèl even after over 14 hours, and the sillage remains detectable at arm's length for 7-8 hours. For me, Burdèl is definitely wearable even in higher temperatures, making it perfect for all seasons and never annoying, except perhaps at temperatures above 25 degrees.

I definitely need to write a review for this beauty: the Burdèl from the Anniversari collection by Tiziana Terenzi. Even though it is rated very highly, it always stands in the shadow of the hype surrounding Xerjoff. Competing with Xerjoff is already difficult given this hype, especially since the Tiziana Terenzi brand receives quite a bit of hate. Not everyone can handle the signature of this brand, but I like it. If you don't fixate on "Alexandria II (Parfum) | XerJoff," you can save quite a bit of money here. The MSRP of the Burdèl is also €400, but you can already get it for around €170 for 100ml. Supply and demand dictate the prices. In my opinion, this fragrance is a perfect alternative that even has some advantages, such as the slightly fresh undertone that makes it easier to wear. What surprises is the packaging: you get a huge box. It definitely justifies the MSRP of €400. The LED light that turns on when you open the packaging is impressive. This light shines on the golden decoration on the cap. I'm thrilled. Even if it probably looks more expensive than it is: I call this decadent and original. A clear 10/10 for this packaging, and the bottle is also very pretty in black and gold. As I said: Anyone looking for a top alternative to Alexandria II will not be disappointed. It's not 1:1, but I can't pick a favorite between the two as both have their advantages. The Alex II is, of course, a bit more beast mode and significantly more oriental, while this Burdèl has an Italian charm with a hint of citrus. Right in the top note, you immediately get the Alexandria II DNA. This fragrance twin is certainly recognizable but feels lighter and more citrusy from the start. This scent can be worn more easily in everyday life than its twin. Cumin and a wonderful citrus creaminess are present from the start. It's kept quite fresh, yet has this slightly heavier spice blend. Wood and balsamic notes also come in early, making this fragrance very elegant and lovable. The Laotian oud is shared by both Xerjoff and Terenzi. A pleasant oud note that is anything but barn-like. From start to finish, it is extremely pleasing without being too ordinary. Those who like the Alex II vibes will most likely love this one as well. The base is also beautiful with soft wood, some delicate musk, and a lot of sensual sweetness. A well-rounded composition. Performance is good but doesn't match Xerjoff. That's not a problem since Xerjoff is already the ultimate. Here you get a fragrance that theoretically can also be worn in everyday situations if the occasion allows. The sillage is pleasant, longevity is top-notch, and in the double-digit range. This review has already involved quite a bit of comparison, especially since this fragrance is likely sought after by those looking for a more affordable alternative. This is by no means a cheaper knockoff but has a lot of individuality, especially due to this citrusy start. Both fragrances are worth it for me. With Alexandria II, I only managed to get the 30ml travel version, where for that price you almost get the 100ml here. Definitely worth checking out. In any case, a fragrance with a lot of sex appeal for both ladies and gentlemen.

Read a lot and in the end tested it myself! I agree with all the comments here, especially the positive ones. - Alexandria 2 Dupe? No - A completely reinvented scent? No For me, it’s more of a better, fresher, and more summery interpretation of Alexandria 2. It’s 7:30, I’m sitting at my desk, drinking coffee, and trying to find a fitting description for the scent, and I keep coming back to Alexandria 2 because it lingers in my nose. I briefly smelled it on my wrist and realized: it’s not just this scent, there’s so much more behind it. Close to the body, I perceive much, much more than just the oriental-spicy and woody notes. It’s fresh, slightly minty, simply fabulous!

…he wore Vans, baggy jeans, a hoodie, and a backpack. But since it was already clear that he would one day become a "big" guy, he would hang his shirt and blazer outside for some fresh air before leaving the house and polish his Derbies to a high shine for one of the events that were becoming more frequent in the evening. Since the boy Alex doesn’t want to spend too much time and energy on a wide fragrance wardrobe, he recently decided on Terenzi's Burdel. Because it starts youthful, citrusy, fresh, and cheeky, even sporty; only to later develop into a mature, woody-oriental masterpiece that subtly yet unmistakably makes its alpha ambitions clear to everyone in the room! At some point, when Alexander has stood up to his full height, another fragrance will take the place of this one. And this story will then also be worth a short narrative and record. And how it will be! Until then…..

First of all, I am not familiar with "Oud Stars - Alexandria II (Parfum) | XerJoff". I got the sample of Burdèl from a nice Parfumo because Alexandria 2 is praised to the skies and I just had to test it. Once home, I sprayed the sample of Burdèl and immediately noticed that this is definitely a completely different quality compared to most mainstream fragrances.

Alex II is considered by many to be the nearly perfect fragrance. To be honest, it felt a bit too “old” for me to wear. This is exactly where the Burdèl comes in. In the opening, you get a beautiful citrus note, while in the background you can already clearly sense an Alexandrian breeze wafting around your nose. The first impression immediately captivates me.

Why I chose this title for my review is hardly debatable. Yes, the Burdel resembles the "Oud Stars - Alexandria II (Parfum) | XerJoff". Nevertheless, one can clearly see that the Burdel is a distinctly unique interpretation. The Burdel actually starts quite fresh, citrusy with a cooling menthol-like note…. It takes some getting used to but is by no means bad.

Burdel starts extremely citrusy, and I mean not a natural lemon, but synthetic lemon soda. Some herbs and caraway join in. However, these scent notes blend together so much that I can definitely say: I have never smelled anything like this before. The opening is almost fresh, like a cold lemon herb soda.

At first, you are greeted by citrusy fresh notes combined with a woody oud base that immediately reminds me of Alexandria 2, simply amazing! But only the woody/oud part! No rose or fruity notes! But in addition to the full load of freshness, you also get a fresh minty menthol note that I really like and is the best part of the opening.

The rhubarb note is fresh, tart, crispy, zingy and photo-realistic. It took me back to my mother’s kitchen where she would prepare the fruit for a slow boiling with sugar so we could finally wolf it down with custard. The green tartness of the rhubarb offsets the sweetness of the rose and the fragrance dries down to a soft rhubarb-rose glow. It’s the perfect fragrance to wear to bed or when you’re feeling nostalgic.

Delivers exactly what it promises: rhubarb. Sweet, tart, clean, and candied rhubarb with a heavy hand of silken rose petals. Has that sparkling/carbonated texture to it, which I crave so much (adding to my growing file of “soda scents”). Similar to the grapefruit-rose seltzer of Odette by Gumamina, but this is much greener and does not have an ounce of powder. The aldehydes here add a sense of clarity to the juice, rather than any soapiness. I associate most “infusions” with flavoured water, but this potion wears pretty opaquely. I’m two days out from my last spritz and it’s still wafting strong on the cuffs of my jumper. It’s linear, but I can’t fault it when it lands such a lovely note. Mental Snapshot: Prim and pretty, but in the most unhurried way. Gingham sundress, barefoot in the grass. Crisp red lip, windswept curls. Picking berries with fresh French tips. A giddy picnic party, for a Vogue photoshoot. tl;dr: rhubarbie

The opening note of green mandarin is faint and short-lived and the scent quickly develops into acidic, juicy, clean, red rhubarb. This is very similar to Eau de Rhubarbe Écarlate but the Prada Infusion is a much better performer. I compared the two side by side, and the rhubarb note in the Hermes one disappears in about 30 min whereas Prada's rhubarb has much better longevity. I can still smell a faint rhubarb after several hours of wear. I mean, this is not the scent profile that you can expect amazing longevity or perfomance from, but this is pretty OK. It feels quite natural smelling overall. This will be one of the summer staples for me. The only thing that I am annoyed about is the color added to the juice. I wish brands would color bottles instead of the fragrance itself, which makes it unsprayable on light colored clothes.

An elegantly understated everyday fragrance: The green mandarin is neither juicy nor prominent and fades into the background somewhere among the stalk vegetables. In contrast, there is the zesty authentic rhubarb freshness at the start, which remains at the center of the scent. This well-groomed good mood is completed by rose & musk. There are no unpleasant or innovative surprises here, just solid fresh "femininity" or "masculinity". I can live very well with that, but not with the longevity. I can hardly smell anything after 30 minutes. My wallet does not appreciate that.

bought blind to give as a gift to my wife for the feast of aid el fitr. the bottle being in itself a treasure, I did not worry too much about the smell. I still looked at the notes. finally the smell is really incredible, perfect for summer, light, fruity, Citrus. a remarkable identifiable smell, very pleasant. I recommend it if you are looking for a rare and light perfume for the summer. It is clearly a feminine perfume. hope this review was useful to you

I wanted to see her smile. She was so far away. Too far! She cried a lot in the last few days. I did too, but rarely in front of her. We were both very scared. Yet we knew about the "thing" in her right breast that shouldn't have been there. On the day of her birthday, there was the examination. In the evening, when everything was over, she received her gift from me. I handed it to her with the words that it should be her lucky star. I gave her a star named Telea. A star for a star,...my only and brightest star! I turned off the lights in the room because I knew that in the golden box a light would begin to burn when opened. When she opened the golden box and her face lit up in the dark, she started to cry. But not out of fear of losing me, herself, or us, and thus also life and love. No, she cried out of happiness and beauty. And so she said softly to me: I didn't even know that something so beautiful existed!? And after a long time, I saw a smile on her face again. We both moistened our skin with Telea that evening and began to dream. And instantly, Telea carried us away. Far, far away! Telea took us on her turquoise-golden flights to an exotic place that is like paradise. To our honeymoon that was a long time ago. To the Raa Atoll. To the Maldives! Telea Telea smells like an unreal-beautiful atoll in the Indian Ocean. A lonely, green island in turquoise-blue water. It smells of freshness, purity, and lightness. The air is clean and light, and the warm wind carries the scent of citrus fruits and exotic flowers with it. Zesty notes of oranges, juicy pears, and citrusy-bitter bergamot bring an incredible freshness. Accords of exotic flowers gradually mix in, and Telea becomes slightly sweeter and more floral. Like a warm wind that lays floral and softly green over the skin, it smells of bright jasmine and nectar-like, almondy heliotrope. As if it were coming from the floral depths of the island. Lightly underlaid by herb-spicy and slightly rough vetiver. Telea is as bright as white shell sand in which the bleached, almost white driftwood shimmers in the sun. Woody notes of the lightest and almost crystalline patchouli and oud refine it in a charming way, as if the notes were almost clinking and singing in their bright purity. Nothing is overloaded or heavy in this perfume. Telea becomes increasingly woody in its presentation towards the end and bids farewell with the feeling of tanned skin from warm-creamy mahogany woods and a sunset of fine, resinous-golden amber. This is how a piece of paradise could smell. Or rather. This is how it smells for me! Conclusion Telea is difficult to fathom and explore. The perfume is highly complex and very fine and delicately woven in its composition. It spreads its hypnotically exotic scent over many hours. If not even days. Telea is as light as sunbeams dancing around the skin. But also as rich as an exotic-floral flower garden after a monsoon rain. It is a constant interplay between fruity, floral, and warm-woody notes and accords. Telea is dazzling like white sand in the sun, green-floral, fruity like exotic vegetation, and woody-crystalline like clear, fresh air from the ocean. The oud that has been woven in here is so fine and pure in its quality that it almost appears like a woody-glassy veil of crystals. One of the purest and clearest patchoulis does its part to further underpin the transparent purity. Whether it is worth its price. In my opinion, it is! And it definitely belongs to the most dreamlike summer scents of 2021. One way or another! Perfumes can heal. They go deeper than some physical sting, cut, or pain. They go deep into the soul. To where one never reaches. They heal wounds that are sometimes not visible to others. Perfumes accompany us on beautiful and also difficult paths. They take us to distant, very, very distant places. Telea accompanied my wife and me during the days of waiting for findings and results. Telea was with us every day and brought back the smile for her and me. Telea enveloped us, comforted us, and held us in dark hours. I gave a star a star,...a lucky star named Telea. And this lucky star ultimately brought happiness to her and me as well. And yes,...it also healed. The body and the soul! https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=38E3u49BlOI

Fact report. This happened on December 10, 2021, in wild Brandenburg. Drive straight from the west and then turn right, where the bank is. I was so curious about Telea. After all, there are notes in it that the Medusa's heart desires. At least in the top and heart notes. I actually love such scents where the perfumer thought: "Just throw it all in, that can go too!" But at the very beginning, I almost liked it, even though I already thought that with hawthorn and heliotrope, it couldn't become too sweet of a little flower. I also didn't want to be biased, because agarwood, rosewood, or whatever it's called, can smell balsamic-sweet, smoky-bitter, or earthy. There must be something to this stuff if it's being praised so highly. The nice flowers faded quickly, and I had a feeling... I then laid down on the couch for a midday nap and snuggled into my huge plastic fleece blanket. I dozed off and dreamed. Characters in my dream: 1 Gorgon 2 Binturongs 1 Klingon newt a herd of water buffalo several white-handed gibbons 1 illegal logger with stomach pain and sweaty feet 1 spice owl with a sleep mask (zoological name unknown) 1 tiger The logger sits on a tree stump and brews a concoction of oak bark against his stomach rumblings and flatulence. Cooked oak bark helps, but smells like fermenting leaves. His feet stink in competition with the brew, so much so that his socks have already run away. The smoke rises into the tree above him. The owl in the branches tears off its sleep mask. Always this noise with the chainsaw, and it also smells like gasoline. It lets out a rough call and flies away. In the distance, the gibbons sing a sad song about the loss of their habitat. The Klingon newt bubbles air bubbles in the puddle and wishes he were as big as the one from Star Trek. Stinging vapors waft up to me, and I dream under my blanket that 2 binturongs are fighting with each other. I wake up because a herd of water buffalo thunders through my living room. Oh no, it's my cat that jumped off the shelf. The logger slurps out of the forest. A tiger follows him.

My nose and I are still quite inexperienced, and Telea does not necessarily match my fragrance preferences. But a review that deeply touched me still piqued my curiosity about this scent. So, I ordered a sample of Terenzi's Telea from Essenza Nobile. Unfortunately, our encounter was not love at first spray: very special, but for me too fruity-sweet, too intrusive, too different, and the sample was initially sorted out as not really my thing. But for some reason, the scent wouldn't let me go. Maybe I wasn't in the right mood at the time of the test, maybe it was too warm, too cold, or whatever? In the end, after a few days, I unpacked the sample again. And only then did I truly engage with this unusual and extraordinary scent for my nose without reservations and hasty decisions. And not just once or twice, but again and again. To my surprise, it gradually became more beautiful: still sweet, but not sticky sweet, rather exceptionally bright, radiant, fresh floral and fruity sweet, only to later settle more and more into a comforting, warm-woody direction in the base. It was not an easy start, but this special scent steadily and increasingly touched and conquered my heart. Telea is for me a starfish that emerged from the depths of the ocean, initially appearing spiny and unattractive, and only upon closer inspection could I recognize it in all its splendor and beauty. It was not love at first sniff, but by now I can proudly call a 100 ml bottle my own, thanks to a very nice perfume friend! I am very happy with my starfish! Telea is not quiet, but also not brash or superficial, rather it possesses an extraordinary depth and persistence. Telea is radiant, bright, sunny, friendly, enveloping, and warm. Telea embraces you, gives you time, and welcomes you. Telea is long-lasting and stays on my scent-hungry skin for a good 8-10 hours, and the sillage is, for me, quite strong and requires some getting used to. Telea is sunbeams, joy of life, and optimism! Love at second glance! Addendum: you are extraordinary, but we simply do not match! I feel uncomfortable and disguised with you! Ultimately, you are too loud, too sweet, too fruity, and too geared towards youthfulness for me. You are probably made for younger noses. I let you go. All the best!

Tele was a blind buy for me. I really just relied on the fragrance pyramid here. The excitement for the postman, who delivered Telea to me yesterday, was of course huge. The postman probably thinks I'm some kind of weirdo because I was already waiting at the door when the postal truck turned into the street. Now, let's talk about Telea: Telea is truly a vacation in a bottle. Compared to Orza, which I described yesterday, Telea is more like swimming in the sea in the Caribbean. Telea has a very light aquatic note. In my opinion, a similar aquatic note to that of Atlantide was used here; I would point to a gentle use of tuberose, which is not mentioned in the fragrance pyramid, but to me, this note seems to be present. I must say, however, that I cannot perceive over 50% of the fragrance pyramid at all. I can smell pear, orange, bergamot, gentle rose, musk, soft vetiver, jasmine, ylang-ylang, amber, and a gentle oud outline, but I really cannot identify any woody or floral notes here. I would see Telea more as fruity fresh rather than fruity floral. The similarities to Erba Pura and also Kirké I do not see at all here compared to Orza. Somehow, I have the feeling that everything fruity is always compared to the two most well-known representatives of this genre. Someone who does not like Erba Pura and Kirké can also enjoy this one. There is also none of the dreaded hairspray note that many fear. Telea manages to create an allegory of vacation for me, especially during the pandemic, such a memory of vacation in distant lands brings a smile to my face. Sure, one could say that the scent of Telea is too linear compared to a Roja, but that really doesn't bother me at all because simple can often be very beautiful. The longevity is in a good range for me at 10 hours. The sillage is just over an arm's length for about 6 hours, and from the 8th hour on, Telea is almost skin close for me. One thing I must get off my chest: Apparently, some suspect that I am sponsored by Tiziana Terenzi. I can clearly deny this. I evaluate everything with my personally tinted opinion, which represents my personal feelings about a fragrance. For me, Telea is one of the best fragrances in my collection, and I always feel like wearing Telea because it simply makes me happy and gives me a sense of freedom.

From the same collection, I have already tested "Orza | Tiziana Terenzi," which I find incredibly beautiful, but the price is far too high to explain the title upfront. In any case, after Orza, I decided to also test the other fragrances from the Sea Star collection. Telea was supposed to excite me similarly, although it doesn't quite reach the level of Orza.

Telea had long been a candidate that stood very high on my wish list. When I found a promising listing in the souk, I jumped at the chance without thinking twice. I had read the fragrance pyramid up and down and thought it could be a perfect match. In my mind, I imagined what awaited me and my nose.

A somewhat newer addition to my collection: The Telea from the Sea Stars collection. A fragrance I have been eager for a long time, but there were issues with the offers. The MSRP of €560 is, of course, absolutely unacceptable in my eyes, although it does show absolute class. The offers in the common online shops are really good, especially regarding this brand.

A feast for the eyes of a bottle that promises sea, ocean, water, or beach, but unfortunately not for me. I thought it would be a bit powdery because of the heliotrope, but it’s just dusty-dry magnolia with white flowers, hard for me to inhale. A lot of citrusy fruitiness with a decent portion of vintage musk; all in all, it reminds me of hair spray with "Tropical Flavor.

The opening has a pungent blast of medicinal freshness. Comprised of Orange and Carnation. Which has a strong Clovey, Basil like aroma which is very herbal and eugenol heavy. Underneath is a creamy mix of Sandalwood and earthy sweet Patchouli, all softened by an underlined musk. Its very well blended and unique to the other infusions. I'm not a lover of cloves so it's not my favourite Infusion . But can appreciate it's a very well melded and natural scent. It's like a Clove and Patchouli bomb.

If you look at the pyramid, you might think to a warm and spicy scent. No. It's totally different. It's a cold infusion with incense touches , fresh and powdery. It could be a "meditation" scent in aromacology. Very clean and classy, in its minimal but very elegant glass bottle , it's a scent I love and I recommend, although the price is high.Another masterpiece by Prada.

Soft but sparkling carnation. Happy and summery, a good choice if (and only if) you like carnation note with a modern twist. I like carnation scents, both vintage and new, there aren't so many new ones though. The other one I own is Etro's Dianthus, which is slightly more classic and which I find very tender and cute. This one is fresher and less creamy. Daywear, safe, moderate duration and sillage,

Atop the Infusion line's signature very soft powder, slightly soapy base, this opens more clean and powdery than most of its siblings except Fleur d'Oranger. On initial spray it smells of fizzy florals and bright musk, similar to Infusion Mimosa, but quickly reveals a sandalwood backbone dusted with freshly ground cloves. A spicy woody floral, but with a clean soapy undertone. In short, it's carnation + sandalwood splashed with soapy water. Sweet and warm, yet light and airy enough that it still smells relatively fresh and clean. Sort of a hot 'n' cold thing going on. Could be a summer flanker of Xerjoff 1888. I get better projection from this than the other Prada Infusions, with moderately strong projection for 2-3hr, longevity 12hr+.

As soon as I "slip" into the New Year, I feel a longing for spring awaken within me. This has been the case for as long as I can remember. I am on the lookout to discover small harbingers of the warm season. "The days are already noticeably longer, the sun is much higher now..." After the spring-like temperatures over the holidays, winter has unfortunately caught up with me. Bitter cold and snow have thrown a wrench in my plans. I acquired Infusion d'Oeillet last summer. I was already so taken by the delicate hint of carnation back then! However, it has overwhelmed me now on these icy cold January days. I don't even have to close my eyes; I can already see myself sitting in the garden, it's green, warm, and sunny. The birds are chirping, the bees and insects are buzzing and humming, and from the corner of the rock garden, the lovely delicate scent of the little colorful nails wafts over to me. The little heads in white and rosy tones stretch their faces towards the sun just like I do. Taking a deep breath all the way to the tips of my lungs, absorbing the lovely, unmistakable scent into my heart - that is my world! The fine sandalwood note gives Infusion d'Oeillet the finishing touch, making the scent even more elegant. It almost seems to me as if the little carnation ladies in their delicate colorful dresses are gracefully sitting on a wooden bench, enjoying the beautiful days. Now and then, one of them smooths her skirt, bounces her little foot, and smiles coyly. In a mysterious way, their appearance and scent enchant. The longevity is moderate, the sillage is rather close to the body, and in my opinion, overdosage is simply not possible. I suppose I still have to wait a little before I can turn my face towards the summer sun. But dreaming about it is at least just as beautiful.
Ah, finally another scent from the new 2015 Prada fragrances. I believe, aside from the new Vetiver and d’Iris, I have now "ticked off" all the new Prada scents.

I JUST RECEIVED SMALL SAMPLES OF PRADA'S INFUSIONS AT MY PERFUMERY AND TESTED THE D'OEILLET; it smells wonderfully spicy like clove fields, and creates a beautiful and somewhat mysterious atmosphere; which I find extremely pleasant right now in autumn: the last mild warmth of the sun's rays, a light that appears so subtly only in this season.

This pale lilac-pink bottle really fits perfectly with Infusion d'Oeillett. However, here you don't get a lush bouquet of lavender or lilac, but rather a few subtle impressions of a land carnation, as the name suggests. Primarily, the typical powdery notes for Prada, or specifically for Daniela Andrier, make themselves known.

Gold Rose Oudh opens with a dominant slightly raspberry jammy rose light as air supported by sharp green bergamot citrus. As the composition enters its early heart the airy rose remains the star, now supported by a relatively refined Oud and patchouli tandem with hints of underlying green fir and some of the slightly sweet honey rising from the base. During the late dry-down the rose and Oud slowly recede though never completely disappear as the slightly sweet honey takes over as star with subtle dry amber support remaining through the finish. Projection is excellent to outstanding and longevity excellent at about 12 hours on skin. The rose, Oud and patchouli trio is such a classic combination that it is hard not to yawn when yet another rendition is released (no matter how competent). It is all too easy to dismiss Gold Rose Oudh as just that... but there really is more to this composition than its surface classic structure indicates. The first thing notably different than the norm is its sharp green underlying nature immediately noticeable at the open through the deft use of bergamot citrus in an unexpectedly different way, furthered by an infusion of coniferous fir later in the early heart. Just when one may feel the composition has revealed all its secrets the late dry-down comes seemingly out of nowhere, turning it into a dry honey and amber driven affair through the finish. The bottom line is the $145 per 100 ml bottle Gold Rose Oudh does little to plow new ground for the crowded classic rose, patch, Oud genre, but its brilliant execution and subtle nuances throughout distinguish it, earning the composition an "excellent" 4 stars out of 5 and a strong recommendation.

Tiziana Terenzi Gold Rose Oudh A rich rose Oudh I wore GRO for a third time, trying to decide what to do with this blind buy. They say the third time's a charm, and I guess it is because wow, it finally hit me what a beauty she is. The first two times I tested GRO I applied it shyly, one tiny spray, and the result was an animalic opening with dark bitter sour roses and it just didn't work for me (I struggle with rose notes in perfumes and cosmetics). Today I sprayed a little more generously, 3 sprays, and this brought out her true beauty. Yes, sometimes more is better ;) GRO opens strong. The top is deep dark bitter. Imagine a rose dark as blood, dried blood, almost black, with a thick stem and the darkest green leaves you've seen, standing in rich wet soil, that's the image that comes to my mind. That rich earth is probably the patchouli and oud. I remember smelling some high quality Oud oil a few years ago and it transported me to winter walks in the forest I used to make as a kid. We'd play hide and seek, making yourself tiny, crouching behind trees and shrubbery. That smell of rotting leaves and wet soil, sometimes still covered with patches of snow here and there, mixed with the dark green pine smell, there's something very comforting about it. In this fertile setting stands a lush dark rose with a powerful deep and rich aroma, on the bitter side, not sweet. I didn't pay attention to the evolution, but suddenly I was thinking gosh, I love this. In the dry down the play between the rose and the Oud (soil note) is perfectly balanced out, it has softened, become more dusty or powdery, more smoky, whilst hiding some sweetness under that smoky cover, and it's captivating. I can't keep my nose off my arm, and boy am I glad I held on to my bottle and didn't swap it away as soon as I got it. This may have just joined the ranks in my personal best and most loved rose and Oud combo fragrances.

The opening is bright with bergamot and has a slightly camphorous, bitter green edge from the fir, which has the effect of snapping you to full attention. The oud used here is dry and woody, with none of the overtly medicinal overtones of the Montale-style oud, and it explodes in combination with a fleshy rose and a rich, chocolate-like patchouli. Everything about this central rose-oud-patchouli accord is rich, bright, and vivid. I tested it with Black Aoud on my other wrist, and I can say that the central difference is this: whereas Black Aoud has an impressive start, it drifts off into a soapy-white musk drydown that feels a bit flat and one-dimensional, whereas Rose Gold Oudh stays golden, resinous, and vibrant from top to tail. Surprisingly, Rose Gold Oudh is also far more animalic in feel and tone than Black Aoud. The drydown is a gorgeous and pleasant surprise. Unlike many of its peers in this category that end in a soapy, musky, slightly boring place, Rose Gold Oudh has a drydown characterized by a dry, resinous amber-benzoin combination and warm honey. It's not the usual place for a rose-oud to end up, but it feels like a very good idea. It is sensual, rounded, ambery and 'full' in feel. In other words, while somebody certainly didn't stint on the quality of raw materials used in this fragrance, it is also clear that there was a skilled hand here in guiding this fragrance through its transition from its bright, camphorous start to its animalic, rich, woody-rose heart, and then finally into its amber-honey base. In a corner of the crowded rose-oud-patchouli field, someone decided not to just phone it in.

State of emergency in Flui's nose. The alarm bells are ringing. A sharp scream. SOS. Out! A gigantic, sharp, ultra-thin arrow strikes right into the heart. As targeted as a needle prick. Completely smooth and clean. Unexpected, like the perfect killer. The scent kicks off like Black Aoud by Montale. A lipstick accord hits hard. A battle begins with an unknown, invisible, unavailable enemy. What to do? One is lost in an unfamiliar labyrinth, aimlessly driven. The nose goes haywire like a gear without a grip, without resistance (my physics teacher once chewed me out for spelling resistance with ie :D but never mind). Fortunately, the rose becomes slightly smoky over time, making it more bearable; I couldn't detect bergamot at all. The harsh and whipping notes of the top are slowly fading. However, the bitter battle is not over yet. GRO, however, has taken the fiercest edge off. The sand and the fir, at least I believe these notes are responsible, even if I can't identify them exactly, somewhat extinguish the blazing fire. The fiery oud is also calmed down. The fire-filled labyrinth becomes passable. The individual scent notes cannot be identified alone; everything is contained within everything. However, patchouli might be stronger in the further course of the scent than the rest, thus everything becomes more muted but GRO is still not tamed. The scent can only catch up with itself and work through itself until it calms down. In the end, it has exhausted itself and slowly collapses in on itself, becoming milder and milder, quieter and more subdued. The lipstick accord comes out a bit stronger again. Hmm, a small part of Flui's olfactory sensorium cautiously sniffs to see if the air is clear again. It is.

For a long time, I couldn't connect with rose-oud fragrances. I found them mostly too medicinal-dark, strict, or simply unpleasant. But either my scent perception has significantly developed, or I am increasingly discovering interpretations that make me learn to love this theme as well. I think it will be a combination of both factors.

My second fragrance test from the Terenzi Fire series. As you may know, the idea is to convey the symbolism and power of fire through perfumes. While XIX March had hardly anything to do with fire, being fresh and woody and hinting at the beginning of spring, you can definitely smell fiery notes in Gold Rose Oudh, which is quite interesting.

Roses as far as the eye can see, noble in many shades of red. Behind, in front, and all around, the darkest forest. In the distance, a glow and shimmer. Purple, edged in orange. Also violet with a bluish-green sheen. The sand-colored ground plays with the light, while the moonless night brings forth bright stars.

Before I tested or even smelled Gold Rose Oudh, it was already on my wishlist. However, since I never really got my hands on a sample or wanted to buy one, I had to wait. One day, I received a package with a fragrance sample of Roberto Ugolini 17 Rosso, and I was in love; what a beautiful rose scent, even though I thought rose was more for women.

Now I have sprayed the last remnants from the decant, actually just a bit of scented air, on my wrist: From the beginning to the last whiff, it is a strong, lush fragrance. When checking whether I had already listed the scent as "had," I initially didn't even want to keep "Gold Rose Oudh" on my watchlist. Gold Rose is an opulent sweet fragrance.

The opening of this is heavenly. You get a gorgeous fresh waft of Mint, Neroli and Orange blossom. It is so smooth and natural smelling. As it dries the powdery sweet Oleander Rose and Iris come through more with a hint of LOTV. In the drydown it has that lovely soft cotton laundry musk that is in most the newer infusions. The only downside is its pretty light, airy and transparent. But not bad longevity for an EDT.

Ah, this is so wonderful. My wish to test most (or actually all) of Prada's infusion fragrances has come a step closer thanks to one of my dearest friends. With a small sample from her, I was finally able to test and comment on the fragrance with the almost cumbersome, double-barreled name d’Iris L’Eau d’Iris (almost similar to Chanel's Sport Cologne Sport). Of course, all soap opponents (dirty dirty...) should now look away or not continue reading, because the scent does smell soapy, yes, but as I have written about some Prada fragrances before, it is NOT just soap. *sigh* Actually, I should feel sorry for the dirty little ones... I meant the soap opponents, because they are missing out on a beautiful, very pleasant scent with this one, whose only downside is the somewhat weak sillage... which is why it unfortunately misses a higher rating, but still, 8.5 points is pretty good and already falls into my "buy category"... The scent: At first, before one can even identify any of the notes, you immediately perceive the absolutely typical and wonderful Prada DNA, which always exudes a clean feeling. Then the top note consists of mint and neroli, with the mint being the stronger note. This makes the scent quite fresh. Additionally, you can also smell something slightly sweet, but I'm not quite sure where this sweetness comes from. Maybe from the lily of the valley? In any case, in the heart note, the neroli becomes noticeably weaker, but the mint remains fairly strong. Light and (thankfully) non-stuffy floral notes come into play. But as always, the iris gives the fragrance a wonderful note that makes it beautifully powdery and soft. At every moment, you can smell these clean notes that give off the typical Prada soapy scent and convey a great feeling of cleanliness. In the base, not much seems to change, as the listed woody notes in this fragrance are weaker and hardly make an impact. The musk may give off a slight sweet note, but you can also smell it quite weakly. I could hardly smell any vanilla either. Thus, the fragrance remains soft and powdery in the base due to the iris, slightly floral and slightly sweet. All in all, a consistently excellent fragrance. However, the scent does lose a bit of the Prada DNA starting from the base or rather becomes weaker. Longevity and sillage: The fragrance belongs to the infusions, which unfortunately do not last as long. At least on my skin, it barely managed four to five hours with effort, as after that it was really only extremely weakly present. The sillage is actually also a reason to cry *sniff* Because it projects little and will only be detectable at first, before you have to get very close to the lady to sniff her scent. For oneself, the scent lingers a bit longer in the nose, but even here it soon seems weak. The bottle: And again, we have the beautiful rectangular bottle, which has the well-known (but this time pink-tinted) Prada plaque on the front. The bottle also has a lovely light pink gradient, while the bottom becomes greener. The cap is cylindrical and covered with a pink fabric. As always, a very beautiful bottle. Hmm, with all the beautiful Prada fragrances, it's really hard to decide which one I prefer. Even though almost all have the typical Prada DNA, they (the d’Iris fragrances) each have their own scent, so they don't all smell the same or very similar. With the Infusion d’Iris (from 2007), for example, I had the feeling that it smelled stronger of vetiver. Here, however, we have a scent that is also iris-powdery, but seems more relaxed and floral. But: Both smell wonderful! Since the L’Eau here has turned out to be too weak in projection, it is more suitable as a fragrance for leisure or as a daytime scent. So a scent that is more for oneself and thus should smell good to oneself, while the lady using the fragrance also smells wonderful to everyone else up close. But as I said, you have to almost hug her to notice the scent on her, but maybe that could also be given as a reason to give someone a tight squeeze ;-) In any case, the scent fits well in spring and summer; on colder days, it would dissipate too quickly... I am really glad that a dear friend introduced me to the world of Prada fragrances, otherwise I would have missed out on something wonderful. So, now I just need a few more of the infusions... who will help me complete my comments? *looking very sweet* :D What? No one?!... just soap haters here...

I confess, I did it again.... another blind buy moved in with me yesterday. And it was Infusion d'Iris L'eau d'Iris. Why this one in particular, even though soooo many others are actually higher on my list of notes and wishes, I don't know. Maybe karma, because for me it was an absolute hit. About the scent: after my eager spritz, my first thought was: wow, this is strong! Full of fear of having another mucous membrane killer in front of me, I sniffed again cautiously...my nose detected something still quite unusual, namely mint. Fresh and a bit like mint gum. Please don't take this negatively; I perceive it as a very pleasant note. I'm not a big fan of aquatic scents, so this mint scent is a great solution to make a perfume into a summer fragrance. After about half an hour, the flowers join in. Mainly lily of the valley and iris, at least for me. These add a certain powderiness to the scent. And L'eau d'Iris remains true to this line. It becomes increasingly powdery and softer, maybe due to the musk?! Because I hardly smell vanilla. I would almost call it a cuddly scent...but that's not entirely accurate, as the mint note never completely disappears. Even if only slightly, I still perceive it throughout the entire scent journey and I'm glad about that. Because it is exactly this mint that ensures that the scent doesn't sink into floralness and become a boring mainstream floral, but rather remains interesting. One could also say it gives it its very own character. I find the longevity to be quite good--applied in the morning for work, I can still smell a light hint in the evening. Sillage is present but not overwhelming and breathtaking. For me, a true stroke of luck. A noble feel-good scent with a very personal touch that never feels out of place. Great :-)

Good interplay of all fragrance nuances = I can't specifically identify anything except mint. Interestingly, I occasionally perceive a nutty note in the sillage. This L'Eau is fresh, floral, and somewhat creamy, and somehow also gives off a bit of warmth. I don't understand how this fragrance could be considered a twin to "Eau Parfumée au Thé Bleu," which for me is mainly powdery. A nice scent for spring and summer, suitable for any occasion. I would say that thanks to the mint and bay, the gentlemen can also give it a try. I thank Clarabella for the opportunity to test this.

Hi guys and gals, after reading along here for a whole year and finding your reviews very helpful and also amusing, it was time for me to register myself and hereby write my first review. Although I am a true perfume freak and store more than 150 fragrances in their original packaging, cool and dark, I do not have a super nose to recognize and distinguish all fragrance notes. Maybe I can do better when I return from the Côte d'Azur in October this year and fulfill my dream of visiting a perfume factory in Grasse. But now, let's get straight to this scent: Right upon spraying, I clearly smelled the loyalty of the Infusion line. The Tubereuse, for example, was very strongly different and represented a completely unique fragrance, but this edition is very close to the classic Infusion. However, I had expected much more mint; instead, I was immediately "overwhelmed" by the floral scent of lily of the valley, which is classic for Prada fragrances. I find that the iris is somewhat pushed into the background by the lily. Since I had an appointment and did not want to show up with this lily of the valley scent, I tried to have it removed by the saleswoman with a cotton ball soaked in alcoholic tonic. However, this did not really work, so I assess the longevity on the skin as top-notch. However, I can't say much about the base. Since I have had initial difficulties with all Prada fragrances so far and they all count among my favorites today, I will give the lily of the valley another chance; perhaps the base will help me overcome this in the heart note.

I am the owner of this perfume, as the infusion of iris captivated me. At first sniff, there is hardly any difference to be recognized, but it is brighter and softer, as I have found out. I can smell mint and bay leaf, and also very slightly some vanilla. Above all other ingredients, the iris clearly dominates.

It’s a burden for me, with Ambroxan and me. A large, dark, heavy burden. As big and dark as the love that hit me like a sledgehammer, back then in Sentifiques "Testostérone". It made me sniff and yearn for this black, heavy substance, so powerfully masculine and spicy, that chased indecent thoughts through regions in the North and South. I kept encountering it on my own skin and others', again and again, more and more often - and from power it became overpowering, from desire it turned into pressure, the dense darkness increasingly took my breath away and drove love far away. For this Ambroxan seems all-powerful, domineering and possessive, unwilling to let go of skin and especially hair - olfactory stalking comes to mind, which is an exaggeration, of course, but that’s how it is sometimes when love departs. A fragrance that contains Ambroxan conveys to me and my nose only this: Ambroxan. "You shall have no other notes beside me!" It may be flowers and fruits, woods or resins, sacred or tarry smoke - they stand no chance of unfolding on me, reaching my nose and my brain. At the very beginning perhaps, just for moments - then there’s something bitter-green, a hint of fine floralness, a bit of aldehyde, whatever may be listed. Two breaths, maybe three - then the dark weight rolls in, a tsunami, a hurricane, covering everything, everything, until nothing remains but dark-spicy-smoky-sharp. This is how it always goes for me, again and again, this is how it goes for me with "Andromeda" as well. Such wonderful notes the pyramid shows me, such delicately tender flowers, such juicy-sweet fruit. I can read them, I would surely love them, if we had the slightest chance for a rendezvous. At the very beginning, there’s a hint of green, of stem green, rasp green, bitter green - but only very far from me, at least an arm's length away. That may be the man who shares body and soul with me - "that smells like gardening, quite hard work, and skin that then needs a shower." But when he comes closer and even closer, he too only smells "piercing-dark poison - go, wash that off, that’s not healthy!". All of this lies, I know well, with me, with my skin - with that love that Ambroxan seems to have for me, which I, however, can no longer reciprocate. It’s too much, too big, too deep, it takes too much possession, doesn’t let me go. It claws itself into skin and hair, for days, for many showers, more so in heat than in snow. That almost hurts a little. And I am not Anastasia.

Andromeda, as the daughter of Cassiopeia, had to suffer for her mother's actions without any fault of her own.
