As the kingdom faced the threat of a flood and the sea monster, her father sought advice from an oracle. The oracle proposed that the only way to appease the sea monster was to sacrifice Andromeda. Without hesitation, she was chained to a rock and was to endure a cruel fate. But fortunately, Perseus rushed in and saved her. However, he demanded that she become his wife. The parents agreed, and so he defeated the monster with Medusa's severed head and intended to marry Andromeda shortly thereafter. As one might expect, Andromeda was one of those classic pawns of ancient Greece. Originally, she was promised to her uncle Phineus, who, in light of the changed circumstances, demanded his niece's hand back and sparked a battle at the wedding with his followers. But here too, Perseus defeated the attackers thanks to Medusa's head and turned Phineus to stone. Here, the scent resembles its namesake. It is fresh and youthful, initially very green and unripe. Drenched in dew with a revitalizing effect. It is like a delicate bud that still needs to bloom. It must take shape until it becomes what it is. At this point, indeed still innocent and unwritten. The delicate carefreeness that cannot cause any harm. Yet, its possible downfall is also present. The danger of the floods gnaws at its legs, but it does not succeed in swallowing her. Well, every plant needs water to thrive. From the bud ripens a juicy fruit that surpasses the beauty of its mother and allows for a positive ending. With Perseus, she leads a happy and long life until death. She became a better and more selfless woman.

What do you do when it's horrifically raining outside? Exactly, you stay at home and cheerfully test fragrances. So, the Luna collection by Terenzi continues, this time with the name of the constellation Andromeda. The inspiration for this scent lies in the sibylline mountains, where Terenzi observed the constellation Andromeda and was confronted with the blooming period of the flowers on the mountain, which speaks to the many floral notes this fragrance has to offer. The scent: The fragrance starts off fresh and fruity. You can smell some bergamot, passion fruit, and a hint of sweet jasmine. Although it smells good, it somewhat reminds me of hair foam or even shower gel. The indicated cut grass is unfortunately not very perceptible. In the heart note, it becomes, as expected, significantly more floral and also sweeter. I can't distinguish the floral notes very well; I think I can best smell the rose here. Additional fruity notes come into play. I'm not so sure about the pear, but the peach is quite noticeable. The base notes are warm but generally weak. There's a bit of amber, possibly tonka bean, and some powdery notes, but I can't pick out much more than that. Longevity and sillage: The longevity is decent, lasting about eight hours. The sillage is okay but later becomes merely average, neither very noticeable nor barely perceptible. The bottle: This fragrance also has the same bottle as all the moon scents from Terenzi. It is white, round or cylindrical, and features a beautiful, narrow label on the front with the name of the fragrance in golden letters. It also has a large, gilded cap with a moon cycle motif on the surface. Overall, very nicely done. First of all, you can easily imagine Terenzi's idea of this place with the flowers, as the scent indeed smells of floral and slightly sweet notes. Unfortunately, everything feels a bit like a shower gel, or even like foam for the hair, as I described in the fragrance description. Furthermore, this gives the scent a slight synthetic note. I find this fragrance absolutely not suitable for unisex wear, but rather more feminine. There are too many floral notes that simply suit a lady better than a man. With the fresh beginning and the rather warmer end, I believe the fragrance is an all-rounder and can be worn at any time, although it may not be perceived as well in winter (outdoors). If it weren't for the aforementioned flaws, I would find the fragrance much better, but I would still recommend a test, as it might appeal to some. Among the Luna scents in general, I personally find Ursa and Cassiopea much better (unfortunately, I don't know Orion).

Frustrated that there is no store near me that sells bdk, I was looking for an alternative to Gris Charnel Eau de Parfum I wanted something elegant yet suitable for everyday wear, something feminine without being too girly. Something for every day. I ended up in a really great perfumery with an even greater saleswoman. The fragrance was the last one she let me try, and I was instantly captivated. At first, I get this fresh, grassy note, and then I quickly pick up on the peach, which is very pronounced. Not a sweet candy-like peach, but rather a refined peach. Despite that, it’s not a fruit bomb for me. I immediately said it smells like I just spent 200 euros at the hairdresser. To me, it has a hint of expensive shampoo but also a bit of spa vibes. If you don’t like that scent, you might want to pass, but for me, it was exactly what I was looking for. I don’t pick up on coconut and vanilla at all; it becomes more woody. It can be classified as unisex, but for me, due to this distinctive peach, it leans more towards the feminine side. Andromeda can be a beast; you really have to be careful with the dosage. If you don’t, I understand the comments calling it “piercing.” It might deserve a second chance and a bit of variation because then it truly becomes elegant and versatile. When well-dosed, it’s a fantastic everyday scent that gives me a bit of “Boss Bitch Vibes.” It also works for evenings or going out if you apply a bit more. The bottle is the most beautiful I have seen so far. It’s heavy and high-quality, and all the golden details are a dream. On the topic of price-performance, phew. Sure, it’s a significant amount, but it lasts so well, the craftsmanship of the bottle is excellent, and for 100 ml, I find it almost acceptable again. Occasionally, I just stare at it reverently, and my little heart beats with joy that Andromeda is mine.

Hello everyone! It's time for a comment regarding a TT fragrance! I first got to smell this fragrance when a good friend of mine was looking for a niche scent for herself. Her boyfriend already owned Kirke, so the decision was already made. The fragrance notes are very much aligned with Kirke, but leaning more towards the floral and peachy direction. You smell like freshly washed hair, as if you just stepped out of the shower and used hair mousse. The longevity and sillage are out of this world. On clothing, the scent is perceptible for a good 2-4 days, and with 3-4 sprays, there's a choke-out risk for friends. In my opinion, the fragrance leans more feminine. I can hardly imagine a man wearing it. But for those who have the balls to wear it, RESPECT! I also find that the fragrance doesn't develop much over time. It tends to become brighter and more floral, which, as I said, makes it lean more feminine. I think it's a shame that, in my opinion, not many women dare to wear this fragrance. I can really imagine it as a club banger or as an everyday scent if you only use 1 spray;) To all the young women looking for a fresh, sweet, and floral all-rounder, you will find it here. Definitely better than all those overused women's fragrances like Chanel Coco Mademoiselle or YSL Black Opium. It's no fun when almost every woman smells the same. But please test it beforehand, because this fragrance is way too strong for a blind buy!

I received it as a gift from my boyfriend while on vacation in Rovinj. He smelled it and said, "this is the best perfume I've ever smelled, this is how you should smell!" and with that, it became part of my collection. Like all Terenzis, it is of course dominated by synthetics, but so beautifully balanced with jasmine, pear, and grasses.

Then I will try to dedicate a few special and individual lines to this fragrance.. because this little wonder is definitely worth it! So, here we go.. A scent, as noble as the moonlight seems, envelops the senses, gentle and fine. A bottle round, wrapped in pure elegance, the beauty of the perfume fills the hearts.

With this fragrance, it's a constant back and forth for me. I stumbled upon this scent in a small perfume discount store, and what can I say... I was instantly smitten. However, I was advised to let the fragrance develop first. Once at the gym, I held the scent under my training partner's nose.

Tiziana Terenzi Andromeda is as beautiful as the heroine of Greek mythology. The perfume is inspired by flowers that grow in the mountainous regions of Italy. It touches the heart with its versatile accords that resonate anew each time.

Spraying Andromeda is always a surprise for me, as I perceive it differently each time, with different notes dominating, especially in the later stages. At first, I notice a bitter-fruity-sweet scent. Sometimes the peach dominates more, and then again the pear. The bitterness probably comes from the grass note.

I blind bought it because of its hype and people said it’s a thicker better version of Straight to Heaven and last longer. I have STH already and I love the scent but wish it could last longer on my skin so I got Ursa without trying it. I am disappointed! I only like the scent, not love. The scent is almost identical to STH and it is thicker with better longevity but I think the scent is not as good as STH because it’s too medicinal to me. STH is more linear like others said but the scent of STH is more straight to the point, less medicinal, smoother and warmer. I should try a sample first and regret getting the full bottle of Ursa.

Smoooooooth, as a baby's bottom. Patchouli, leather and tobacco are tame while oud, to me, is not intrusive throughout Ursa's development. This scent comes across as an example of a great republic, each and every one of the notes seems to have a say in this scent's existence. truly unisex, for all to enjoy
THIS STUFF IS INDESCRIBABLE! what your gonna get is a creamy oud mix with some boozy Rum the quality is there also the blend is magical!!! iam happy to find you Ursa (MASTERPIECE).

One of my fave notes in modern day perfumery is LEATHER. It was on this pedestal, that curiosity got me and I blind bought Tiziana Terenzi's URSA. This leather-themed fragrance effortlessly bespeaks undisguised affluence, influence and elegance. It's strictly for men (and women) who exude unadulterated class, style and panache. With notes of rhum, patchouli, tobacco, vetiver and oud, Ursa is versatile enough to be worn to office, church, red carpet, gigs, etc. It projects really well & is very long lasting! I love how this frag exhilarates me each time I wear it!

Based on some reviews of Ursa, I was expecting some sort of animalic monstrosity. Well, it definitely isn't that. It opens with a strange musty (with a "t", not musky) smell. Sorta resinous-musty. After a short while, a sweet fruity boozy accord appears. That remains for a while, with the sweetness pulling back some. The musty/woody/resinous smell comes back stronger with an occasional whiff of booze. Longevity is pretty good. Was still going strong after about 8 to 9 hours. Sillage and projection are more moderate after the first hour. I have yet to try Straight to Heaven so can't comment on similarity. I don't care for Ursa, not because it's challenging but because it's just a meh scent. Really nothing special. Not impressed and no wow.

I often relate my fragrances to fictional characters, situations, experiences, and real people. I was given a tiny sample of Ursa, but put off trying it for months. The notes in this perfume aren’t ones I normally fall for and it has to be the right moment. Apparently today was the day. I used a small amount of it on my wrists in case I hated it.

Gives a very heavy sweet barnyard open with booze and dried fruits. It dries down to the most beautiful and soft Patchouly I’ve ever smelled! It’s my favorite frag, I tried my sample for one day and went home to buy a bottle, I do not regret months later! It he bottle is also super sleek and heavy.

Or is it more like a bit of fermented baby... and so on. So I really don't want to tear apart a fragrance with a comment. But what good are all the fine praises if they lead unsuspecting blind buyers to their doom (as has happened to me far too often - precisely because of the great comments). In this case, thank goodness it was only a small sample.

Kallisto, a nymph from the retinue of the huntress goddess Artemis, was seduced by Zeus. The forest nymphs were bound to chastity in the presence of Artemis, yet this did not stop Zeus from seducing Kallisto due to her beauty and impregnating her. Out of fear, Kallisto hid the misfortune until it could no longer be concealed and was immediately banished by Artemis.

Another fragrance from the "Moon Collection" by Terenzi. This scent was also created in Italy, this time by Lake Como and the Fiumelatte River. According to the description, the rocks of the cave there smelled of vetiver and wood, along with earth, roots, and the scent of water.

This is a semitransparent oriental amber perfume, specifically a hyper polished sweet leathery amber scent. I can feel benzoin, a few micro powders and a bit of chocolaty patch on a perfect bed of musks and soft wood. Very classy and beautiful, discrete but long lasting.

Ordered this as blind buy, only based on notes... I know It was risky, many times blind buys go wrong, but not this time! I couldn't be happier with this blind buy! To my nose, Nero Oudh opens with blend of leather, saffron, and geranium. Very strong I have to say, maybe too strong. Make sure you let it settles before getting in a closed environment with others, you can choke someone! Despite there's nothing wrong with the opening, I have to say I almost gave up on this, cause I'm a bit fed up with roses, but then it started to dry down... Here is where this thing starts to shine, the roses gets tamed and oud starts to show up, and what a gorgeous oud! Not skanky, nor cheesy, just the best parts of oud! After a couple of hours we get a well blend of leather, saffron, oud, woods and a bit of roses. This reminds me an upscale men's clothing store, imagine that wooden furniture, the new leather belts, shoes and jackets, and a subtle floral touch. It keeps like that all the way to the end, slowing fading into a wonderful oud-leather combo. Performance is beast mode! Easily achieving 12 hours of sillage, but if you go to bed without bathing, you can still feel a trace on the morning. Amazing!!!

Nero Oudh is one of Tiziana Terenzi's fragrances that never really interested me. Nero Oudh features rose, saffron, and plenty of oud in its fragrance pyramid. This is actually not my usual preference at all. However, since a few Terenzi fragrances have managed to convince me when I didn't expect to like them, I decided to test Nero Oudh. Today around 11 o'clock, I received my sample of Nero Oudh. Of course, I had to spray the scent on my arm immediately for testing. Right after spraying, a strong oud note emerges, but fortunately, it doesn't smell like a barn or anything similar. The oud is framed here by orange and mandarin, along with a light vanilla note. I can only perceive minimal saffron and rose, which I really like because I don't enjoy rose and saffron as notes at all. Nero Oudh is very linear; I can't really detect any change. Oud is clearly the main note here. I think Nero Oudh is very interesting for oud beginners or fans of Xerjoff Fars. Here you get a nice oud fragrance that also works well in everyday life and doesn't attract negative comments, as some oud perfumes do. Yes, Tiziana Terenzi can do oud, and they do it very well. I can give an absolute recommendation for purchase here. The price for 100 ml is also acceptable. Regarding longevity, I can say that the scent is still noticeable on the skin even after 8 hours. I think the skin scent will still be perceivable for about 2-3 more hours. Nero Oudh should last around 10-11 hours or more. Perhaps I will adjust the rating a bit since I am wearing Nero Oudh for the first time today.

Nero Oudh smells exactly as the bottle looks: mysterious, elegant, and so dark that it practically absorbs light. It not only captivates the light but also me and everyone who comes too close. Contrary to what one might expect, it is never too heavy or intrusive, let alone animalistic. Still, I associate it with black marble slabs in a luxury house made of dark wood in the mountains, heated by a pompous stove. Next to the stove stands a subtle vase with red roses. Film character: Batman would wear this scent, and a dark cloud of Nero Oudh hovers over Gotham City!

You can imagine the scent similar to Ombre Nomade, just without that sweet note that LV has. Furthermore, I find that you become somewhat addicted to Nero Oudh; with each wear, you like the scent more, and this also applies to the environment you are in… When I sprayed it on Friday afternoon for a company party, a colleague told me that the scent could still be detected in the bathroom until the following Tuesday (so much for longevity) in my opinion, this is the best "bad boy leather jacket scent" there is… My absolute favorite perfume; I think Nero Oudh simply smells of pure toxic masculinity.

Once again a blind buy and once again I am very satisfied. When I first sprayed the fragrance, I actually got immediate Ombre Nomade vibes, but that faded quite quickly. The best way to describe the scent is, as already mentioned, like a high-quality car interior. You smell leather with a certain plastic note, which is delicious and very high-quality. On top of that, there is oud and other woody notes. Somewhere there’s also a hint of citrus fruit. The longevity is good - very good, and I find you can wear the scent up to about 25°C, so it’s still quite suitable for the cooler summer days. In short: I love the scent!

... immediately came to mind after spraying: smells fresh, a bit leathery, rather inky, woody, floral, intense, and masculine. Never smelled anything like this before. What sets this apart and makes the fragrance so 'unique' are Cypriol, Ylang-Ylang in the top notes, Gurjun balsam and cedar in the heart notes, and perhaps the iris root as well.

Every time I smell this fragrance, it strangely brings a smile to my face even though I have no association or memory with this scent so far. Nero Oudh has something dominant and elegant at the same time. A dark yet fresh composition woven with floral notes. Very interesting! This scent reminds me of the interior of a new car with black leather seats.

At first, a very strong smell of alcohol, which personally left a stinging sensation in my nose. But this strong alcohol scent, which I never would have believed, changes after a few seconds and develops into one of the most beautiful rose oud fragrances I know.

oh wow...this oud product is definitely not for the faint-hearted...a brief hint of mandarin...the short sprightliness is quickly followed by smoke, leather, or new car scents...smoke...yes but restrained we imply a dark leather interior here...a hint of vanilla and tonka bean is detectable...and rounds it off...

Nero Oudh opens strongly with woody aromas (Nagarmotha) and Ylang-Ylang adds floral notes and a bit of sweetness, hmm creaminess? A light rose scent is also present, though I can only sense it here. After the first spray, this combination enveloped me and brought a smile to my face ;-) .

I didn't expect to love this as much as I do but I'm blown away. The beginning strangely reminds me of sweet booze and after a few minutes it turns into pure powdery sweetness - something I absolutely love about the Prada Candy line. I'm slightly worried about the longevity compared to its price tag and it's not something I could see (/smell) myself wearing everyday.

This is potent one, i know it better be for that price they ask. I don’t justify price I don’t think it is ok. But quality and beauty is there. You wont smell any synthetic “today” molecules. It opens with raspberry and kind of mix of vanilla and fruit, it has smell like you enter in summer to icecream sweets shop ... but that goes away later and remains beautiful creamy make upy powdery (not dry) lipsticky scent. Whole room where do you spray it will smell beautiful for day. Projection is great and longevity average.

The brave are said to own the world, and so I am not entirely averse to blind buys. However, I usually do not venture into the price range of “Olfactories - Tainted Love.” When I read "lipstick accord" in the fragrance pyramid, it regularly blows my mind. I wonder where that comes from? Perhaps because it reminds me of my little cosmetic laboratory under my bed, where I mixed various creams and perfumes as a little girl? The psychologist in me shows me a different picture from my childhood. It’s carnival time, and my mother paints my cheeks with lipstick that smells of lipstick accord ;-) princess cheeks. Yes, it probably has to do with those scent associations from rare and special occasions when my mother was close to me. Anyway, in the fragrance pyramid of “Olfactories - Tainted Love,” the lipstick accord is written in big letters; it practically jumps out at me and gives me a kiss on the cheek. I like the bottle; I generally like Prada fragrances, I’ve worked enough lately, and thus there was no problem overriding the rational, sensible part of me. Said-Ordered. My idealistic fantasy held a "Prada infusion scent" with a lipstick note under my nose, a divine combination, so to speak. To reality: The bottle comes without outer packaging, but with a colorful patterned fabric pouch in 60s style. Unfortunately, I flooded it with coffee shortly after unpacking. Goodness, but at least this time it wasn’t the notebook. The bottle is substantial, made of thick glass with a magnetic closure. I really like the combination of the salmon pink liquid and the blue, slightly ribbed label. The first spray of “Olfactories - Tainted Love” is a revelation for lipstick scent fans like me, the ultimate “everything is good” note. But as already mentioned in the statements and stubbornly ignored by me until then, it quickly fades away. Then it becomes herb-fruity; it strikes me as a mix of plum, cherry, and raspberry. Good, also nice. At this point, it also becomes clear that the scent does not contain any “infusion DNA” and that it is not sweet and girly. Shortly after, however, I completely lose the scent. As if it disintegrates into not really compatible components. Rather herbaceous, a bit powdery, the musk almost jelly-like, then there’s also a nasty slimy association; you remember that orange or green goo in the little plastic barrel, slightly metallic and quite synthetic at this point. Actually, one could say it’s an advantage that I couldn’t perceive the scent particularly well. Oh no, I think, and yet I keep spraying and spraying and spraying, as if more of the same would yield something different. After about an hour, a herb-powdery scent remains, reminding me of “Misia” or “Angel’s Dust.” Both had not occupied much space in my collection for long. I do this for two days until I decide, with a heavy heart, to let the scent go. I would have liked to like it so much and had imagined it so beautifully with the two of us. So I place a sales offer in the souk and go to the gym. An overload of “Olfactories - Tainted Love” applied earlier in the day comes along out of necessity. And then something completely unexpected and highly delightful happens. Obviously, the scent undergoes a real transformation due to the warmth generated during training. The resulting dense-warm powderiness now reminds me a bit of “Brooklyn” by Gallivant, just without the orangey-citrusy notes. And the best part: the lipstick note comes back, is literally switched back on, and stays. I even quickly interrupt my workout to take the scent back from the souk. All’s well that ends well; the princess in me is beaming. It is clearly a scent with edges and corners, which, after a certain time, stand in a meaningful relationship to each other and paint interesting scent facets. It is not an easy sweet girly scent; it takes time to fully reveal itself, which makes it quite interesting. And above all: it clearly needs warmth to unfold. A clear recommendation for testing, then, for the warm-blooded among the lipstick scent fans and for the warm season.

I first saw Orza in a YT video, described as one of the best vacation scents. Given the price, I probably wouldn't have noticed it at first, but the positive review convinced me to test Orza after all. Fortunately, in hindsight. Short version Fruit cocktail Deep, versatile, complex Not really synthetic Innovative bottle and great packaging - Thank you for the extra cost Vacation vibes Best fruity scent from the house The scent Orza was a fragrance that immediately piqued my interest. Based on the reviews, I almost wanted to buy it blind, as I still had a voucher for an online retailer. However, when I saw the selling price, I ended up only getting a decant. I was a bit overwhelmed when I first sprayed it. I definitely liked what I smelled, but I had so many different associations that I couldn't quite categorize the scent. I can smell the berries, mandarin, slightly floral and sweet notes. All of this mixed together creates this wonderful fruit bomb. For some, it might be too much, but that makes this scent very special for me, as you can still perceive the individual notes if you really test it over several hours and focus on the individual notes. In the already mentioned complex top note, I can clearly identify the following notes: green apple, mandarin, coconut, raspberry, and blackberry. The heart notes and base notes are perceivable to me at the same moment. Slightly floral notes as well as vanilla, caramel, amber, and light musk, along with sandalwood. The fruity notes from the top note do not disappear in Orza; they remain throughout the entire progression. The progression is rather linear. At the beginning, I mentioned that this scent evokes various associations for me. On one hand, it reminds me of fruity cream candies, and on the other hand, simply of vacation and beach with many tropical plants. It also reminds me of cocktails, a fruit basket, or even classic shampoo with berry scent that I used as a child. All things that I enjoy smelling. This scent really has a lot to offer. I'm lucky that I like all the associations that the scent triggers in me. Anyone who doesn't like fruity scents will probably not like this one either. Orza has managed to distinguish itself from other well-known fruity scents through one or two fragrance notes. Especially coconut and apple in the top note set it apart from the well-known fruit bombs. The base combination of amber, benzoin, and caramel adds a lot of depth, certain creamy notes, and especially due to the caramel, Orza is different in the base, as in other fruity scents, vanilla and musk are usually the most dominant. This creates a slightly darker, sweet, and creamy base that I find incredibly appealing. Comparisons Here, one could mention many others; I will focus on the well-known representatives. Personally, I notice the following differences when comparing the scents. With "Erba Pura | XerJoff," the orange is more in the foreground; the other fruity notes are not recognizable, as if they had been thrown into a blender. Orza is a bit more complex. Erba Pura feels a bit younger to me. Regarding the H/S, both are similarly strong, but the Xerjoff scent projects better over a greater distance. In the drydown, the musk note is a significant difference. This is more dominant in Erba Pura, while in Orza, many more base notes are recognizable beyond just musk and vanilla. "Kirkè | Tiziana Terenzi" seems to me, in contrast to Erba Pura, somewhat more similar to Orza. Especially the raspberry and blackcurrant in the top notes make the two seem quite alike. However, in Kirke, the peach and pear are the strongest for me. Qualitatively, Orza is at a much higher level than Kirke. Orza also has significantly more depth. The biggest difference is also in the drydown. What makes Orza better compared to Erba Pura and Kirke is the simple fact that the scent is not so overloaded. The fruity notes in the two well-known fruity scents are sometimes too strong; this extreme is not present in Orza, making it less overwhelming for most noses, at least that’s how I would describe it. It is much finer and has no edges. All three scents are absolutely unisex for me, with a tendency towards the feminine direction. Bottle The overall presentation is a bit too much for me. When unboxing, it’s a one-time fun to struggle through this pompous packaging, but afterward, this giant block just sits around. I find the design of the bottle quite beautiful; it’s something you haven’t seen before. Visually and color-wise, the bottle also fits ideally with the content. But I find the quality of the bottle to be good, yes, but nothing more. The spray head, like in the other Terenzi scents, is not very nice; they could really improve that. Very little comes out with each spray. The cap does not sit 100% securely on the bottle, so you can't lift it by the cap. Longevity and sillage The H/S is truly extreme. Longevity of 10 hours with a long noticeable sillage. On clothing, it lasts for days and is noticeable. However, I still find the sillage not at the level that occupies the room. The cloud around you is very strong and present, but at a certain distance, you can no longer smell it, which I find ideal. Occasion I definitely see Orza on vacation; I have rarely had such a vacation feeling before. Otherwise, it can be worn in warm temperatures. It also works at parties. In the office, one spray is enough; here, the weak spray from Terenzi is quite good for dosing. In winter, it feels too much like a vacation scent for me; it doesn’t really work then. Reactions It was mostly well received. At a perfume tasting a few months ago, Erba Pura was the scent that almost everyone liked. At the last tasting, it was Orza. I believe these fruity scents are extremely well received by most people between 20 and 30. Price/Performance As much as I like the scent, the price is quite exaggerated. Even though it has been significantly reduced since the release, the current 450-500€ is simply too much for me. Especially since Terenzi offers so many fruity scents, I see, from an outside perspective, only the bottle + packaging as the reason why this line is so expensive. Kirke, Andromeda, and Cabiria, for example, are all cheaper. Whether more expensive oils are used in Orza, I cannot say; at least, it is not advertised that way. Fortunately, you can get it, although very rarely, in resale for significantly less. Conclusion What should I write here? In my opinion, the price is the reason why this scent remains under the radar. Orza is such a beautiful scent, but most will understandably be put off by the price. It is unique, for me the best fruity scent, but it is definitely not worth the extra cost. Such a shame. But for those who have the money to spare and want to test it - I can only recommend it.

it's time - spring is upon us - the feeling the real thing - also known as the opening for the drydown of summer when we were all still feeling great, the planning began with warnings to adhere to the suitcase weight today it’s all or nothing - just scratch that or because it will be nothing again with your vacation not due to the weather - but the crisis report one of many practices abstinence - but that's not me - because I get my little light from the message in a bottle. whether you believe it or not - or think I’m not quite right - I make my journey a daily obligation yes - even when the wind turns with tutta la forza - I grab my borsa and enjoy a bit of orza - because every fan knows them - the siblings Paolo and Tiziana Terenzi - from Cattolica to Sao Paulo - the scene recognizes them - this time with a starfish and the bottle looks really fancy ___________________________________________________________ ;) what a brilliant and high-quality presentation - the series consistently shines with an elaborately crafted golden starfish on the cap and even the packaging surprises with its built-in lighting. You even have to screw Atlantide out of its own water tank - now that’s what I call ingenuity. but here’s orza - what a work once again from the truly virtuoso master Paolo of the brand Tiziana Terenzi. I had the pleasure of personally meeting this really likable contemporary and can only tell you that besides his grand abilities, he is simply a true gentleman. There were plenty of funny and highly interesting conversation topics along with glimpses behind the scenes of the industry, and I have this special encounter in the best memory. We got along incredibly well, and there was even an invitation to Cattolica that I would love to accept when the world finally turns back to its long-missed rhythm. Until then, I enjoy using his creations as travel tickets, and it is therefore a very special pleasure for me to present to you today this first-class variant. So let’s get back to the scent - many classify it as a fruity gourmand and consequently rather for the colder autumn days. Personally, I don’t think much of these imposed restrictions - you should just wear whatever you feel like and what you like - everything else is just outside opinions. Of course, mine is included - but I personally find that this scent simply fits fantastically into the current springtime. But fundamentally, it can also be worn all year round and across genders without exception. this indescribably harmoniously composed fruity scent - which captivated me right from the first sniff. I tested a few from the series relatively briefly - Telea and Atlantide were missing - but orza simply stood out immediately from the rest, and I was instantly absolutely thrilled by this composition. so here you get, in addition to the mentioned packaging advantages, simply an amazing, potent, and long-lasting scent whose various development phases are simply kneeling-worthy. If you have even a little love for fruity vanilla scents, in my opinion, it will be very hard not to rave about this one... :)

Orza is one of the Terenzi fragrances that I have known for a while. My girlfriend has been wearing Orza for some time now, and recently I have also been wearing it more frequently. I want to point out right away that I do not see Orza as a dupe of Erba Pura or Kirké at all. Orza has more depth and is more complex. I find a more fitting comparison to be the following: they are fragrances of the same genre or direction, but for me, that is the only similarity. Orza is basically the next step for anyone looking for something more high-quality than Erba Pura or Kirké. Orza opens with a powerful burst of fruits: In the first 10 minutes, I smell apple, raspberry, plum, blackberry, and a hint of coconut. I don’t really smell the floral notes here. To be honest, I don’t detect the heart notes; for me, it goes straight to the base notes: caramel, vanilla, musk, sandalwood, and a bit of amber. Orza remains very fruity the whole time but becomes increasingly sweeter and less fruity after 6-7 hours. As for the bottle, I can only say again: it looks great, but I wouldn’t need it because these huge packages take up an incredible amount of space. The longevity is really impressive at 12-13 hours. The sillage is also very strong for 6-7 hours; I would advise against using more than 3 sprays because Orza only becomes very close to the skin after just over 10 hours. I can recommend everyone to try Orza, and if you can get the fragrance at a good price, it is a great alternative to Erba Pura and Kirke, especially for those looking for something with more depth and a feeling of a tropical beach.

Here, the bottle is as beautiful as the fragrance! Although there is no peach in the scent, it still reminds me of "Kirkè | Tiziana Terenzi" or "Andromeda | Tiziana Terenzi" with its creamy fruitiness. One cannot smell the apple or the raspberry, which is a pity since these are great fragrance notes. It is a fruit cocktail that reveals no recognizable notes. A very light floral and vanilla aspect emerges later on and remains. If money is no object, then of course I would buy this fragrance because I want that amazing packaging! However, I wouldn't pay so much just for the packaging, so I would rather opt for one of the cheaper versions. For my part, I don't need two, three, or more fragrances that smell almost identical.

The first time I came into contact with this fragrance was through its glamorous bottle. It immediately caught my attention, leading to the first sample of the scent. This captivated me right away with its fruity top note consisting of raspberry that is well perceived, as well as plum. You can smell this for a while, and then the fragrance becomes smoother and softer in the dry down, lasting on me for a good 10 hours and even longer on clothing. I can recommend this scent to anyone who has a little money to spare and enjoys fruity-sweet fragrances. A masterpiece by Paolo Terenzi.

It is a mega fruit bomb. My wife wears the scent and I want to smell her all day long. 2 small sprays and everything in the room smells wonderfully fruity with a hint of vanilla. Super strong and very long-lasting fragrance. Even after several hours, it can still be immediately noticed when passing by. Whoever says it doesn't last long either has no original or a bad batch.

As my birthday approached, I did something daring - a blind purchase of a sinfully expensive fragrance that I had been longing for. After much research and reading, I was sure - it would be fantastic. I had been eyeing the stars from Tiziana Terenzi for a while and absolutely wanted one; just the beauty of the bottle made me drool with desire. When can I buy you?

L'Homme Absolu was missing from my collection for years, because this is less common, and rarely appears at Parfumo souk or buy&sell groups. Now I found one for a very reasonable price (75€ for a 99ml bottle), actually it was cheaper than the Intense version, so immediately grabbed it. My first impressions: D'oh! This is a blend of Intense(90%) and L'Eau(10%). Absolu is a big big disappointment to me. I expected a little bit more creativity from Prada, and now I understand the reason why Absolu didn't became popular. Because it barely differs from Intense (which is much better btw).

As a fan of the L'Homme fragrance DNA, I have now tried all the flankers of the original. And even though there is much debate about the necessity of the various flankers, I believe that all the "reinterpretations" of the L'Homme line noticeably differ from one another. This is also true for the Absolut. It comes across as spicier and more intense than the original, but it doesn't overdo the sweetness, which I think is the case with the Intense. Although the scent development of the Absolut is, in my opinion, not particularly exciting, but rather modest, it impresses mainly with its excellent performance. This is already unexpectedly good with the original, but the Absolut reaches a whole new level. For me, that means: sprayed on in the morning and still clearly noticeable in the evening. Especially on clothing, this scent seems to never fade away. Wonderful. Especially now in the colder season, this scent is a perfect all-rounder for me. Unobtrusive yet something truly special. As mentioned in the title: For me, the perfect choice for someone looking for a true all-rounder. Especially in the colder season. So, if the original is a bit too weak for you and the Intense is a bit too sweet, the Absolut is a very good option.

I ask my predecessor Maltek to consider this not as a contradiction, but as an extension of his remarks! His comment certainly reflects the opinion and taste of many, if not most people here, regarding the Prada L'Homme line. Unfortunately for me, L'Homme Intense is a scent that is too sweet and unruly, lacking any counterbalance. (See my comment on that...) I was all the more curious when I realized that there is indeed a more intense "half-brother" of this fragrance line, quietly released! :) In one point, I must agree with you: If you know one Prada L'Homme, you know them all. The DNA is unmistakably present in all of them, and in any blind test, I would recognize each one as Prada L'Homme. For me, however, Prada L'Homme Absolu is just a little less sweet than Intense, which is necessary, and with the cardamom (or whatever it really is), it has just a bit more counterbalance to the sweetness, saving the overall impression for me. Absolu is therefore more balanced, and unlike Intense, it is truly wearable and enjoyable for me, even though the difference to its closely related family members is really not that great. So let's say a small but decisive difference for me! For the average consumer of uninformed nature, who buys a sweet fragrance for the winter season on the advice of their partner once every two years, the difference when testing in the department store is probably questionable... L'Homme, Absolu, Intense, are primarily more intense in ascending order. The slight difference in the notes and the tuning is more for olfactory enthusiasts. For me, both aspects apply: the intensity in Absolu is on the edge of what is possible in this composition without overwhelming me. And I like the slight spicy note so much that I would have wished for significantly more of it. However, I find that the additional spice is not limited to the fleeting top notes; it quietly but noticeably radiates in the heart and base of the fragrance as well. Yes, that would be it for me overall. So, a sweet-woody, slightly spicy iris scent, with a bit of freshness in tow. And indeed the iconic Prada L'Homme DNA, if you will, as the foundation. For me, these are the two, L'Homme & L'Homme Absolu, that I would acquire from the line or will acquire. Even though one can still say that all flankers of L'Homme carry a certain redundancy, thus deserving the label "For Fans," from my perspective. I simply find the original to be the best, and it is perfectly balanced and tuned, and should not be missing from any modern man's collection! ;)

Prada L'Homme has made a name for itself beyond fragrance enthusiasts and is selling quite well. The reaction from the marketing department was predictable, and so one flanker after another is being pulled out of the hat: L'Eau, Intense, this Absolu, and Watersplash. The bottle resembles the Intense in shape and color but has been adorned with a pattern on the back. Personally, I find that quite nice. The color suggests a familial relationship, and indeed, Absolu is very similar to Intense. While the regular L'Homme was too feminine for some men, the Intense introduced a darker, "more masculine" variant. In Absolu, the Intense is complemented by a hefty dose of cardamom. I’ll be honest with you: I’m a sucker for cardamom, one of my absolute favorite fragrance notes. It really comes through here and accompanies the scent throughout its entire progression. This naturally means that it is sweeter. However, it starts with a lovely freshness that lasts for about 15 minutes. Aside from that, though, that’s about it for the differences from Intense. Projection and sillage are really good, as is longevity. For me, the scent radiates at arm's length for two to three hours, and the overall longevity is around nine to ten hours, so really very good. You can definitely wear it at work, but due to the sillage and performance, I see it more for the evening hours. Generally, I would rather wear its fresher brothers in warmer weather and during the day. Do you need the Absolu if you already have the Intense? For me, a clear yes and no :P. If you’re not totally into cardamom, the Intense serves you well. For a friend, for example, the Absolu doesn’t last nearly as long; I’m really blessed with my skin.

As many (actually all) have already noted, the Absolu is the middle ground between L'Homme and L'Homme Intense. If you already have L'Homme Intense, you really don't need to test this one much. However, I believe that the different versions of L'Homme do have their justification.

I spent one and a half year with using a quite similar perfume, Ô DE L'ORANGERIE by Lancôme. I know, it sounds funny, but I had a perfume-allergy. When I smelled strong perfume-odor, I suffocated and had a nonstop cough. Perfumeries were life-threatening for me. When I used perfume at my neck, near to my face, or at my wrist, I had ugly red rashes. I had to chose in this terrible period of my life a very subtle fragrance, that was the Ô DE L'ORANGERIE. Now I found this scent with a more refined, more natural version in the WHITE FIRE. It is an elegant, citrus- and chypre-like fragrance, which recalls that horrible season, that had only one good point: it was soooo easy to choose perfume in the morning :-) Woods or flowers can not be found in WHITE FLOWERS, but good quality leaves and fern is there. It will not attack others' olfactory, and I would reommend it for daily usage, business trips and negotiations. I risk to say, that it is more attractive on men, but I can not be sure without experience, however it is not sensual at all. It keeps distance, so to say something extreme, it is a perfect choice for the occasion, when you break up with your partner.

For such an expensive perfume house, this smells shockingly like the perfume I wore in high school, which came from Aeropostale. (For the uninitiated, that’s a cheap mall clothing brand that was very popular in the early 2000’s.) The scent isn’t offensive, but it’s not especially exciting either. I wouldn’t be able to pick this out from a lineup of other white floral fragrances.

Although the paper form had made me skeptical, I had to try a sample of the white fire - once I was hooked, I was captivated by Angelliese's fine commentary. Accordingly, my expectations were rather indifferent before the first test. Right after application, I am hit by a presumably aldehyde-induced prickling, which might remind me of a proper portion of icy, fresh air. Alpine or Dolomite air, or ice for that matter, is also fine, see marketing chatter. However, I hardly believe that my nose, when inhaling cold air, distinctly perceives the oxygen among all other atmospheric components, let alone precisely records the specific aggressiveness of this essential yet life-threatening cellular poison. Still, it's a fun and apparently rather rare pyramid idea. The head, as we know, is always sniffing at the forefront. The thing about oxygen and ice reminds me of a highlight of university life in Kiel: the annual Christmas lecture of the chemists; a tradition that is similarly upheld at other universities. Spectators from all fields always gathered in droves. One of these spectacles had "Liquid Air" as its theme, and the lecturers played all sorts of pranks, for example with umbrellas that broke through a liquid oxygen rain or liquid carbon dioxide-frozen rubber boots that shattered with a hammer strike. A particularly lasting impression in many ways was made by frozen and accidentally shattered mercury, which lay on the floor and thawed again, partly evaporating undisturbed because - certainly unintentionally - not all of the scattered drops had been bound by pouring sulfur over them. I learned that day that the stuff evaporates like water. Probably, the demonstrators and the audience in the front rows all got their share. Sustainable indeed. Relaxed people, those chemists. Such dangerously exciting things never happened in my accounting lectures; boredom usually doesn't cause immediate health impairments. The impression of "let's believe it's oxygen" quickly faded, though. Jasmine takes the stage. It is only slightly soapy and far from that enchanting fullness that I like in Jasmin de Nuit. Glassy, clear, and pure it indeed is, thus living up to the name and concept, although not to my preferences. During the third hour, an unmistakably synthetic note (Hedione?) emerges, which cannot be completely hidden by the jasmine. However, soon (still during the third hour) it is creamed over by the musk. From the fourth hour on, this becomes the central component, naturally kept white itself. While it complements the jasmine well, unfortunately, it is once again less to my liking. It could be a test recommendation for our musk ladies! Within the seventh hour, the scent completely retreats to the skin - the sillage was never lush anyway - and lasts there for about another two to three hours as a lightly blymerant musk skin scent. Even in further tests, I could hardly recognize more than a subtly noble jasmine-musk mélange in the first three hours and a noble-subtle musk-jasmine mélange in the last three hours after the admittedly quite furious start. What a pity. I found the commentary better.

Yes, but surely there is an oxygen accord, an ice accord too, Augusta snorts, I can smell it in this top note. The nostrils open, a deep breath. This opening is cloaked in green and glue, or solvents if you will, yes that sounds dreadful, but it is really decisively different and smells exceptionally good! A brief shallow breath is followed by a deep inhale. This is not aromatherapy, rather an aroma experiment, although there is nothing wrong with breathing exercises. The transition into a somewhat treacherous jasmine is perfectly veiled by this familiar synthetic and pleasantly sharp almost sweetness with a green tinge. And with plenty of air, from the very beginning. The scent is airy, not ethereal, neither fantasy nor close to nature. Rather cold and hot from the fire in the snow. Admittedly, it fits. One can also set the image aside and simply find the scent white, green, slightly resinous, and only then floral. The top note is practically upside down and is as permeable as possible. This is why AugustA considers this scent to be one of the most exciting in her small collection. The effect is exhilarating in the sense of awakening, sparking curiosity for more and for something different. The different here is the jasmine. It shines and blazes in white, white white. Not indolic, not fleshy. But hot and cool at the same time. Accompanied by a dry and a resinous wood note. Honestly - I know nothing comparable. This wonderful peculiarity with flashlight feeling in the snow under intense sun glitter remains for a while, but recedes into the background in favor of this gentle and light-footed, almost weightless jasmine-wood note that lingers. Always haunting back and forth on the skin and in perception. Flickering light, hot and cold at the same time. Fascinating. Intellectually appealing and heartwarming exciting at the same time. With the first breath, landed on an ice planet, with constantly glaring sun and this strange foreignness that feels so familiar.

It is absolutely unique. At first acquaintance, it didn't make a special impression on me, seemed very fleeting and not strong enough. A very delicate and natural scent. A truly deceptive impression. If you don't hold back when applying, it is wonderful. For a long time, for me, one of the most beautiful scents for the warmer season. A jasmine flower in a crystal glass full of ice water. Lasts until the evening.

Here we come to another fragrance from the line where Terenzi aims to capture the symbolism of fire. As always, fire is somehow sacred to the Terenzis, and they hold the belief that fire is omnipresent and possesses great symbolic power.

Actually, I don’t like aquatic scents. And when the nice saleswoman sprayed this fragrance “with aquatic notes” on the test strip, I only smelled it because nothing else appealed to me that day. And I slowly felt sorry for her. “It’s just been released!” This sentence is something I despise from perfume saleswomen.

do not come together, cannot be bound, are not related, sunk in sparks I stand in flames and have burned in water" Aquatic scents have a hard time. They quickly slip into the cheap. Soapy-creamy is the new freshness. White Fire is primarily fresh, not just clean. The main protagonist Jasmine burns in the water and makes my head spin.

The appearance, the fragrance notes, the price - all of that conveyed class, possibly even something extraordinary. I thought so. So I ordered samples from the Terenzi Parfum series and was quite fidgety when they finally arrived. I start with "White Fire". The top note is already quite faintly perceptible, a bit of green, a few aquatic notes, a certain sweetness.

Come to the dark side of the force, mu ha ha ha… oh! Wait! What a mess… this scent is called Dark Light and not Dark Side… mess mess mess, all my concept for this comment is gone, great… Well then… first of all, a warm welcome to my latest comment, which I will have to improvise today. It’s about Prada Olfactories - Dark Light, which I mistakenly read as Dark Side and thought I could bombard you with many Star Wars stories again. I was really looking forward to it! *sigh* Alright, then Dark Light it is. Dark light… whatever that is supposed to mean. The only thing that comes to mind is black light, which you’d rather not go into the bedrooms of perpetual singles like me, unless you want to discover the many suspicious stains on the floor, walls, and even ceiling… hrrmmm…. :D According to the description, the scent is supposed to inspire oriental fantasies (it was clear that one would think of belly dancers now… :D), especially with its resins and warm-soft notes like vanilla. All of that sounds like a rather pleasantly soft and gentle scent, so I could talk about cats again, right? Hopefully, that will bring back all those who were scared off by my Star Wars mention! Although I will probably only mention the cat once AFTER the scent description, he he he :DD Alright, now onto the scent! The scent: The scent starts immediately with a rather warm and soft combination of vanilla, amber, and resins, especially myrrh. Basically, the scent stays like described for a while. I would say that you can smell the angelica a bit later on, but without the listing in the scent notes here, I wouldn’t necessarily come up with that, although maybe that’s just me, since angelica is a note that is recognizable but doesn’t appear in many fragrances, and botany laymen like me could quickly forget its scent! The angelica definitely becomes much stronger later on, making this floral note come across as a bit heavier. Otherwise, it remains gentle and warm as before. And basically, that’s it, I think, since even in the base, the scent mostly smells like a nice mix of vanilla and myrrh. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is just okay, but for a scent with vanilla and resins, I find the sillage rather weak. Which is a bit of a shame, since such scents are usually worn more in autumn and winter, where the projection can be stronger. Well, if necessary, you just spray it on again. The longevity is good, though; you can still smell the scent (weakly) on the skin after over eight hours. The bottle: The bottle is rectangular with beveled edges and has a dark blue tint. The label is gold-shiny (or was it metallic instead of a gilded sticker? I can’t remember, I haven’t held the bottles of these scents in my hands for a while) and shows the name and brand. The cylindrical cap is gilded and wrapped in leather, which looks elegant. A beautiful bottle. Conclusion: Oh yes, this scent here has turned out very nicely. It is really warm and soft, even cozy and powdery. All these notes with vanilla and resins feel very gentle, beautiful, and even soothingly peaceful. It’s almost like on a cold winter night, where the icy wind outside would cut into your face, but you are safe inside, where it is warm and cozy. You look out the window into the dark, deserted night and are glad to be inside, where the heating or fireplace keeps the room warm. A warm blanket, which you usually throw over your shoulders, lies on the bed and has been claimed by the cat, who is just waiting for you to lie back down so you can cuddle. Yes, the scent creates a pleasant feeling, even though I wouldn’t necessarily describe it as oriental. Although I must admit that I think more of roses, oud, and spices when it comes to oriental scents, and therefore don’t associate much oriental with this one. But that doesn’t really matter, because what’s important is how the scent smells, and this one simply smells very nice. Due to its gentle and warm aura, it is for me an autumn and winter scent that could be used both alone and for nice evenings. It is definitely worth a test. I just think that for a winter scent, it could have a slightly higher sillage. But well, sometimes you can’t have it all. Nevertheless, as I said, it is definitely worth testing! And that’s it, thank you for reading! I wish you all a lovely evening, do something nice (like watching Star Wars :DDD) and see you next time :)

I wouldn’t have guessed a single note of this just by smelling. Pineapple? Orange? Flowers? Are you kidding me? This cannot be true. It’s definitely a synergy – a picture you cannot pick apart to basic colors. I perceive it as a unisex summery fragrance, it has something about it that smells like salty sea breeze with a touch of iodine and dry towels bleached in the sun, with tiny pieces of seaweed stuck in the pile. It communicates relaxed feeling and invites you to listen to your body: enjoy smells, sounds, and physical sensations while being lazy like a cat on a window sill. At the same time, it has a fresh and invigorating side. Yes, this is a beach. Apparently, “Gumin” is a diminutive from Guglielmo – the name of the house’s founding father to whom the scent is dedicated, but maybe also a word play on “gamine,” so it’s either a calm and caring masculinity or cheeky and confident femininity – take your pick. Yet I like to think that it’s a name of some mythical youth who lives in the cave by the sea, dives for pearls, and collects seashells.

Gumin is difficult to place in a single olfactory group. There's an interesting contrast of notes that transition from very bright to woodsy. The ozonic tones and vivid florals play the peacemaker between the fruits & citruses versus the sandalwood-agarwood accord used. I even find it to be aquatic in some ways with a whisper of Aventus's worshipped pineapple. It's a great balance and ideal for daywear. This could potentially be a great summer fragrance. While a niche offering, it is quite safe. In Korean, "Gumin" translates sexy or cool. I am unsure whether or not Gumin was used in this context, but it fits that description.

Its opening is made up of an absolutely delicious fruit explosion. A pineapple reinforced by citrus fruits are the culprits of this first phase. As the first original point, after a few minutes the aldehydes give a very funny twist to this first phase. During the heart, some floral tones are very subtly perceived, but nothing dominant or easily recognizable. Musk and sandalwood are the two predominant ingredients at the base of the creation, although denser and smokier woods are also perceived.

Gumìn literally knocked me off my feet. I had to wait a long time before I could finally purchase a bottle of Gumìn at a reasonable price. The packaging is, of course, a bit too large again, which can lead to a real space problem for someone with a passion for Tiziana Terenzi perfumes. Gumìn is truly like an explosion of fruits, but it must be clearly distinguished from other fruit bombs like Kirké or Erba Pura. Gumìn is not very sweet and therefore manages to be perfectly unisex; the sparing use of musk will please some as well. Gumìn really smells like pineapple, orange, bergamot, and mandarin in the top note. The heart note with the floral notes is only very faintly perceptible to me and forms a kind of soft floral frame around Gumìn. The base note, which slowly emerges after 2-3 hours, brings woody and spicy notes. Here I smell oud, sandalwood, birch, and a bit of amber. The fruity top note, however, remains constantly present and manages to convince throughout its entire duration. It is truly one of the few top notes that manages to remain almost unchanged throughout its entire development. I also really like that Gumìn bears similarities to the incredibly beautiful and pure DNA of Creed Silver Mountain Water, but Gumìn executes this note better and more creatively. However, I don't really see a similarity to Greenley. Gumìn simply lacks the apple note combined with synthetics. The longevity is absolutely above average for a fresh scent. I was able to perceive Gumìn for a good 8 hours. The sillage is noticeable at just under an arm's length but becomes increasingly quieter and closer to the skin after about 5-6 hours. I really find Gumìn to be the best blind buy in a long time, and for me as a Silver Mountain Water lover, Gumìn truly has signature scent potential.

Honestly, I don't even know where to start with this fragrance. I traded for it blind at the souk, without knowing what was coming my way. It hit me like a bomb and immediately blew me away. What an incredibly awesome scent! You get a great bottle in high-quality packaging. The bottle is simple, stylish, and feels premium. Right upon spraying, it became clear to me that this is a real fruit bomb. However, one must clearly differentiate here. It is by no means like Kirkè Extrait de Parfum or "Erba Pura | XerJoff". This fruity note is clearly dominated by an orange that smells like fresh and delicious orange juice mixed with a bit of sparkling water. There isn't much development until the base note comes forward, but a hint of something woody and slightly spicy is added. The top note remains almost unchanged and thus accompanies you throughout. The fruity notes are also by no means overdone and never drift into the synthetic. I actually can't pick out the floral notes mentioned in the heart note at all. They simply get overshadowed by the prominent top note. The scent is not overpowering, but people around you will notice it, partly because Gumìn is just different (better) than many of the well-known summer fragrances. Gumìn is one of my absolute favorites, and I am super glad I got it blind. It is elegant, spreads good vibes, but above all, it is different.

A wonderful fresh fruity orange juice scent. That's how simply it can be described! Why lengthy descriptions? Gumin is wonderfully juicy and elegant. I find it one of the best from this house. Longevity is 3 hours, then there's nothing left to smell for me. null of the many ingredients come through for me, just orange from start to finish, but well done and absolutely likable.

The opening starts quite strong and very fruity with orange and pineapple, citrus fruits. As the fragrance develops, it becomes a bit woodier, but the DNA remains consistently the same. It feels very high-quality and classy with its fruity freshness. I would categorize the perfume as suitable for any occasion and anywhere.
After I was able to acquire a Dionisio from the Anniversari edition and was quite convinced, I had to get the next Terenzi from this line.

With "Gumìn | Tiziana Terenzi," I am dealing with a fragrance on Parfumo that is mostly well-received but unfortunately does not evoke much in me. The scent is fine, no question about it, but in the end, I think to myself: Is that it? Nope, the fragrance is okay but not a "game changer." At least it lasts about 10 hours on my skin with a solid sillage.

Recently, the Gumin has moved in with me. Filled with curiosity and inspired by the reviews here on Parfumo, I was eager to see what this scent had in store for me. The first spray on the skin reveals a scent of freshly cut lemon.

This smells like clean (unused) baby diaper to me. I don't know what it is about the Prada Candy line, but they are so hit-or-miss... Candy and Candy Kiss smell delectable but L'Eau and Sugar Pop smell sooooo dusty, powdery, and not at all what other commenters here have described. I do get some of the 'citruses' and 'floral notes' but not in a remarkable or exciting way. Just a freshly-opened pack of Huggies. Glad I got a mini of this before tracking down a big bottle.

This fragrance is delicate, sweet in a floral way, inoffensive/ work-church safe, with a soft to moderate projection (depending on application and climate). I find the scent linear which isn't a bad thing as this fragrance is lovely from the very beginning. She does last longer on hair and textiles, much longer than on skin (in my experience). I find this primarily a fresh and citrusy white floral, delicate and refreshing but with a refined fruity sweetness from the peach and apple (in that order). I get little to no caramel or vanilla other than as perhaps afterthoughts or subliminal suggestions here but have no complaints in that regard because I love the fragrance. I think there's perhaps *just* enough of a touch of caramel and similar touch of vanilla to bolster the floral sweetness as basenotes do rather than stand in center stage as the main accord; this baby's all about the fruit and flowers. Performance: questionable/ mysterious to me. Hours after application when I can't smell it, my husband can. So I'd have to give her at least a moderate rating there. Fragrance: I love it. 9/10 Value: Fair, I have no complaints about present price-points

I am repeatedly drawn to the Candies - on one hand because of the beautiful name, as my first poodle had it too - and then of course because I like sweet things. I like the original Candy - but it is too fleeting for me. I got the Floral version because it has more substance due to the floral note. What will it be like with Sugar Pop? The name suggests a mix of lollipop and popcorn - and I am eagerly waiting for it. I wait - and I am still waiting. Nothing deliciously sweet pops up. My sweet tooth remains unsatisfied. A greenish scent wafts towards me, underlaid with delicate peach. An apple note pleasantly joins in, but then the scent surprisingly turns bitter. I do not like this turn. Sugar Pop is unsuitable for sweet tooth lovers, and the finish is also disharmonious. However, the longevity is commendable - but not enjoyable. I would rather stick with Candy Florale.

Ah yes… a new year, a new Candy flanker. So far, so good… *sigh* As you know, I've been struggling for ages to test the Candy scents because they are not only women's fragrances and therefore are located in the women's section, but they are also filled in brightly colored, beautiful bottles that invite all the women nearby to try them just by their appearance! But 2018 was supposed to be THE year when I finally had to be braver. No more fear of testing women's fragrances in public. No more fear of being observed while doing so. No more fear of insulting you silly perfumes… oops, that last part probably shouldn't have been said out loud… oh well, I'm not afraid of you… unless you want to hit me!!! :D Anyway, I went to the shelf with the Candy scents as usual. This time braver than ever! By the way, the shelves with the Prada fragrances are a nice sight, as there are now quite a few flankers standing around there. Although some might say that there are already too many flankers in this fragrance line, I think they are all great! So I grab the latest bottle and want to spray it on myself… As I said, 2018, I want to be braver, blah blah blah. Then, of course, it happens. I realize that I am actually standing in front of the colorful Prada women's fragrances. And at that exact moment, the following things happen: My mind tells me: Come on, just test it! Nothing will happen! My gut feeling tells me: Don’t take the bottle in your hand, but rather take your legs and run away as fast as you can! My heart tells me: … my heart isn’t saying anything at all, it has long since stopped beating out of sheer fear,…! Suddenly… while I’m stuck in my thoughts and wondering how I could best spray it on unnoticed… I hear a voice. A real, female voice: “Hello, you’ve been standing here for ages! Can I help you?” I jump. It’s a saleswoman! She’s smiling at me! “Uh, I… *sweating* I just want to see how the new Candy smells, because I really like the line! I’ve tried them all and I love them all!” OH MY GOD, I’m such an IDIOT!!! Why did I have to say at the end of the sentence that I would LOVE all these fragrances? What one says out of nervousness... Because I swear to you, the saleswoman’s face lit up a bit more after that. At that exact moment, combined with the last part of my statement, it didn’t sound like I was looking for a scent for a girlfriend/mother or anyone else, but for MYSELF!! I try to salvage what can be salvaged and stammer something like: “Yeah, yeah… you ladies have so many more beautiful fragrances than we men do!” Her response: “Yes, that’s true. There is indeed a larger selection for women. That’s why I know quite a few men who regularly come here to buy women’s fragrances for themselves!” … “FOR THEMSELVES!!!”, she said! Aaaaaaaargh,… why did she have to say THAT? What does she think of me now???? She must think that I actually want to smell like the Candies myself. So sweet and sexy… and that I generally use such women’s fragrances… aaaaaaaarrrrrggghgghghghghghgh!!!!!!!! Of course, she immediately asked if she should spray the scent on me, and you can guess what I, the fool, replied…: “Yes,… VERY VERY MUCH!!!” … *sigh* Believe me,… I will probably always struggle with testing Candy scents. ALWAYS! So I almost hope that this is the last Candy flanker… but only almost… *sigh* The scent: First of all, the scent seems really light to me, as I can hardly perceive anything properly. Only gradually do I smell light, fresh citrus notes, after which the scent becomes fruity with the peaches. It takes a while to recognize the Candy DNA, as the scent is less sweet than the other fragrances. Overall, it hardly has anything to do with the cotton candy-like sweetness anymore. This makes the scent feel more relaxed and summery. In the base, however, there is (temporarily) something that I unfortunately don’t like very much, and this is also the reason why I don’t rate the scent as highly as I usually do. Because I now smell a somewhat stuffy, floral note that reminds me a bit of ylang-ylang. I generally don’t like ylang-ylang very much, and I think that this makes the scent a bit stuffy and sticky, losing too much of its sweetness and, above all, even appearing a bit more mature. This also slightly diminishes the freshness of the scent. Later in the base, the stuffy floral note becomes weaker again, although it remains floral and slightly sweet, with the sweetness now coming from a somewhat lightly done vanilla, which smells quite pleasant, also due to the powdery creamy notes. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is initially relatively weak, but from the base, the scent becomes noticeably heavier and is then also better perceivable, leaving a small scent cloud behind later on. The longevity is okay, six to seven hours are possible. The bottle: The bottle is, of course, beautifully designed again. It is cylindrical with a yellow base and pink fragrance liquid. At the end of the bottle, you can see a white band with golden edges, featuring that well-known Prada faux leather pattern, and the golden Prada logo is visible on it. The spray head is half oval or slightly dome-shaped and is gilded, with the dome being pastel blue. This bottle is also a success. Hmm… so… I have to say that I don’t like the new Candy as much as the previous ones, but it has still turned out quite nice. However, this is not because the scent is significantly less sweet, but much more due to the stuffy floral base, which is absolutely not my thing, as I don’t like this ylang-ylang-like scent very much, even if you should smell it more up close than in the rising scent cloud. But this becomes weaker in the later base, so it’s not so bad for me now and might even appeal to you ladies, and you might find a nice summer scent with it. … Oh dear, you know, I usually spray fragrances on myself in a store. Occasionally, I get sprayed by a saleswoman. Normally, I just smile and say “Thank you” or something like that… but after spraying, she of course said something else to me… and it was the following: “So, now go for a 30-minute to one-hour walk and let the scent develop on YOUR skin to see how it smells on YOU, because scents smell a little different on everyone!” That’s it! End! After THIS sentence, it was absolutely clear that she assumed I was trying the scent for myself and was now planning to let the scent work on my skin to decide whether I would BUY THE SCENT FOR MYSELF!!… I will definitely NEVER GO BACK to that store *sigh* … Why does this always happen to me?? :((

WOW Dionisio is an incredible fragrance. It is cozy, smells super sexy but not invasive. the ambergris is of very high quality and makes smelling it an experience. It is one of the best pieces in my collection, for me it is Tiziana's best fragrance. The price is high but it is worth it. I can't stop sticking my nose in the bottle cap every day.

On that day, a quiet excitement spread within her. It was already afternoon, time seemed to fly by. She put on her coat to arrive on time for her first date. Hastily, she closed the door behind her and happily galloped down the stairs. On her way to the little patisserie in the old town, she walked through several small streets and alleys. Round cobblestones and ancient walls created a cozy atmosphere. The air was already cool, and the colorful leaves of the trees danced dreamily with the wind. There it was, the little patisserie. She opened the door, and a warm, soft scent of gentle vanilla and caramel notes greeted her. In the display, there were very appetizing, these little delicious cakes and pastries decorated. That could only be found here. It was rumored that the recipes of the little patisserie had a magical "something" that no one knew. But everyone who tasted it was enchanted. She took a quick glance and sat down, as always, in the corner by the large window. And as always, she noticed the scent of the old wood of the paneling, the counter, and the wooden floor. That blended finely with the nuances of vanilla and caramel. The door opened, and the little bell above the door frame jingled. There he was now. Their eyes met. A smile. An intimate hug. And suddenly there was more than just the scent of the little patisserie. A delicate temptation spread and enveloped her heart with warmth. Dionisio A big thank you to Garcon.

Dionisio and I encountered each other very intensely and completely unexpectedly. A few months ago, I met an old friend; we hadn't seen each other in a long time and arranged to have dinner. I was looking forward to seeing him, had so much new to share, and was curious about how he had been doing lately.. When I got into his car, I experienced one of the most unforgettable moments of my olfactory senses! I perceived the most irresistible, hypnotizing, addictive scent.. Immediately, amber greeted me, a concentrated dose, accompanied by sweet vanilla and a light oud note. And there was something else! Something that made this scent fascinating and absolutely seductive for me, but I couldn't figure it out (pheromones?). I was helplessly surrendered to this fragrance, enchanted with all my senses, unable to focus on the old friend I hadn't seen in so long. I could only think of this scent, which stole all my senses second by second! “What is this fragrance?” - I asked him first, without any greeting or inquiry about his well-being, after we hadn't seen each other for what felt like an eternity.. He had the bottle strangely in the car, so I could test Dionisio on my skin and knew clearly: This is MY FRAGRANCE! A few weeks later, I was able to call Dionisio my own, and it still fascinates me! I wear the scent at least twice a week and often have to persuade myself not to wear it so often and to try something else. I receive incredible positive feedback from my surroundings every time and would even claim that this is the fragrance I could wear every day without needing a change! I love Dionisio for being incredibly sexy and alluring. For giving you a powerful dose of amber (I’m a big amber fan) and harmonizing wonderfully with vanilla and musk. The scent has an incredibly beautiful and exciting progression; at some point, the oud comes into play and gives the fragrance an even more magical effect than it already has. Moreover, I love Dionisio for its incredibly great performance! Even after 12 hours on my skin, I receive compliments for Dionisio and can still perceive it very well (not skin-close)! Even the next day, everything on me smells of this fragrance! And that’s something a scent has to achieve.. Dionisio is definitely my BEST discovery of the year, turns my head every time, and captured my heart from the very first moment.

After I set a new compliment record with a fragrance last weekend, I have to write a little review about this scent. I wear fragrances primarily not to receive compliments. However, Dionisio managed to achieve a personal best this weekend. I was approached about my scent the entire weekend, non-stop, exclusively by women, from young to old. On the flight to Madrid, every flight attendant stopped next to me and asked what fragrance I was wearing, saying the whole plane smelled so pleasant (I had sprayed 3-4 times in the morning). There’s something about this fragrance that resonates very well with the opposite sex. Is it the pheromones? I don’t know. I have never been approached about my perfume so many times in such a short period; it continued just the same during dinner and at the club. Incredible. Now to the fragrance: Dionisio doesn’t reinvent the wheel with its notes. However, Tiziana Terenzi has managed to combine these notes so elegantly and seductively that an absolutely unique fragrance has emerged. The base throughout the fragrance journey is amber, with musk playing only a minor role for me. I wouldn’t label the opening as an absolute crowd-pleaser, as it starts slightly sour for me on some days; definitely not a scent you quickly spray on and rush out the door. The sour note is only temporary and develops quickly. In the heart note, a beautiful vanilla joins in, acting as a sweet companion but not being too dominant in focus. The jasmine and lily of the valley give the fragrance a slightly floral touch without becoming too feminine. In the base note, the fragrance becomes woodier and more pronounced with the oud. Here’s a little layering tip: definitely layer the scent with Nasamatto Duro; the mix of the pronounced and masculine woods from Duro with the ambered musk vanilla and sweetness from Dionisio is simply dreamy. Dionisio always envelops you in a warm and recurring cloud of scent and lets you dream. It is always present but not intrusive, a dream of a fragrance. The sillage and longevity are extreme; I can promise you will be noticed. Especially as a man, the fragrance seems to have magical effects on women. The combination with Duro probably ranks among my absolute favorite fragrances of all time, but even on its own, Dionisio is an absolute experience. Seduction par excellence

After a little more than half a year with this wonderful fragrance, I feel the urge to write another comment on this masterpiece. The opening of the scent is brutal - I stand by that.
