However, my nose has become a bit more delicate, and I also notice the musk. Nevertheless, I still smell a bit of vanilla in the opening. Musk is by no means a core component; it contributes more to the overall picture in the background. Most people will not perceive the musk separately. I continue to wonder how one can create such a brutal and harsh entry from amber and vanilla - but so be it. The first hours are spent with amber and vanilla. I still do not smell jasmine and lily of the valley. Amber and vanilla actually suggest a heartwarming and gentle creation. It is warming, even against a snowstorm in the depths of winter. However, this combination can only be so warming because it is not gentle at all and has many edges and corners. Amber and vanilla fight for dominance in the perfume with elbow tactics. The competition ends in an incredible potency of both fragrance notes, which provides a breathtaking and harsh warmth. Similar to a campfire, whose heat can sometimes be difficult to control. But that does not make the scent unpleasant; on the contrary. While I always associate MFK's Grand Soir with sofa-fireplace vibes, here I have more of an après-ski campfire feel. That can also be very nice. Fragrances that I like have always had a relatively linear scent progression. Therefore, I was initially a bit surprised by the promotion of oud in the fragrance by my niche perfumery, as I definitely could not perceive the oud there. But it turned out that at Tiziana Terenzi, base notes are indeed base notes. After a few hours - I would estimate around 6-8 - amber and vanilla become a bit tired of their competition. They are clearly present but have agreed to go into part-time and give the freed-up space to the oud. This makes the scent significantly softer and rounder. Here, I like it best, even though the amber-vanilla opening is also very nice. Conclusion: This fragrance provides campfire heat instead of winter warmth on winter days and a feeling of cozy exceptionalism on all evenings of the year. Yes, I know, it sounds strange. But I think you know what I mean. Cheers!
Dionisio is both angel and devil. The scent starts off powerful; for the first 5-10 minutes, I feel like I'm being pushed against a wall, with no way to throw out a lifeline.

For about a year now, I have been actively engaged on this wonderful site, which has introduced me to such a marvelous world. I long pondered which fragrance would be the subject of my first review. Until this moment, something always held me back from choosing a scent. Until today, when the sample of Dionisio arrived. At first, I was anything but impressed by it.

Dionisio, a variant of the name Dionysios which means "under the protection of a god". Terenzi has chosen a rather beautiful name here to market a truly opulent fragrance. The presentation in the form of the packaging, including lighting and marketing of the scent, is indeed opulent, not least because of the price.

One of the best vanilla-centric perfumes I have ever smelled. After Guerlain's Spiriteuse Double Vanille, it's my favorite! Unfortunately, it wasn't love at first sight. It has a rather unique opening that takes some getting used to. But once you get past that, a creamy deep vanilla emerges, supported by oud. The sillage is above average and the scent lasts forever.

Dionisio is both angel and devil. The scent starts off powerful; for the first 5-10 minutes, I feel like I'm being pushed against a wall, with no way to throw out a lifeline. Amber and musk are clearly and distinctly noticeable, and as the fragrance stabilizes, you want to lie down on a blanket spread out in front of a fireplace with a glass of red wine and a partner.

I live in London and went down to Harrods to try perfumes and oh boy! Eclix is absolutely divine. I love iris and its very long lasting. I feel enveloped in gorgeous soft woollen material and can't get enough of it. I have ordered this perfume from amazon uk from company called 'leslilasperfumes' with awesome prices. I bought for £138 and it retails for £250. That's a bargain!

This is another perfume (the other being ~Ibitira~ by Xerjoff) that is based primarily, to my perception anyway, on a synergy of musk & orris. These two elementary perfumery substances seem to my mind to exist specifically to be put together. If you were to force me to name a single accord of which I could have no perfume other than for evermore, it would be that one. I remember at one of the apothecarial houses I am wont to visit, I was looking through perfumes of more standard price-brackett. I had been particularly successful in that I had found a couple of outstanders value-for-minlet-wise. I began to think "I don't know why I bother with high-end 'fumes". On the way out, beginning to translate my just-had schooling into a plan for an acquisition, I passed the Tiziana Terenzi stall. I thought "ah! there's Eclix - I sampled that briefly once before, & seem to remember liking it: let's have another try!". I did indeed so, and ... "now I remember why I ^do^ sometimes bother with these high-end 'fumes!" Weird thing is, if I were to name a figure that is the one that instantly comes to mind when I intraspire of either of these 'fumes, it is ... rubber party balloons!! But this only goes-to-show the weirdness of colaterallity of aromata. Some for instance say the smell of oud is like that of burnt rubber. It brings into question what precisely it is one means when one says something smells °like° something else. It is a very deep question; and this is not the place for uttermost searching-out of it: but I will venture this much - that it is ^not^ like, say, two points on a plain being literally ^close^ to each other. Nay! it is very different fræ that! This one is however different fræ ~Ibitira~ in that being heavy it is heavy. It's heavy in the sense that it ^feels^ wearing it like one has got a ^heavy^ thing on, like a heavy gold chain, or something. Ibitira is certainly not lacking in substance; but it kind-of feels as though one is not ^bearing^ the weight of it: its kind-of like the heavy thick door of a bank-vault on exquisitely engineered & thoroughly-oiled hinges.

Let’s go dreaming ... pause time ... find peace ... arrive. *Traumsequenz* or a bit of magic in a bottle ;) The magic formula for your own life you have to think up yourself, as only you inhabit your palace of dreams. -Irina Rauthmann- About the fragrance: Eclix starts with powdery iris interwoven with citrus notes plus velvety vanilla. A touch of almond is added as well. Violets join in, and petitgrain contributes green tones. I perceive Eclix as a cool scent for a long time, which only gains warmth in the base. The violets are carried into the base by orris root and woods, and a delicate hint of musk rounds it all off. Amber adds a resinous undertone to the fragrance and darkens it together with the woods. It smells enchanting from the wrist :) For a Terenzi, Eclix is unusually quiet ... but that doesn’t bother me ... it is simply beautiful. It has a bit of vintage charm ... but it’s not old-fashioned! The longevity is just under 8 hours, and the sillage is moderate. A delicate fragrance aura envelops me. I would say Eclix can be worn all year round ... although I would exclude hot summer days. The bottle is beautiful and wow ... quite hefty :) Unisex? ... no ... this one is for us girls ;) Conclusion: There’s magic in the bottle! Captivating mix of violets, orris root & woods. Unusually quiet for a Terenzi - beautiful! *Traumsequenz* Psssst ... girls, you have to test this ... honestly ;)

It opens with an overdose of sickly sweet Rose and Leather and earthy Patchouli. Then dries down into a smoky harsh fuzzy wood and tobacco base. It's too sweet and too skanky. Reminds me of Guerlain Ideal EDP which is also an assault on the senses with it's sickening concentration of sweetness. My worst nightmare. Everything I hate about fragrance is in this mess.

For those who still believe that the rose can only smell feminine or is not "masculine" wearable for men, I recommend the surprise upon the first spray - no - the surprise is even certain! A powerful wave of dark rose tobacco. Initially herbaceous and cool, then leather-warm. And even though I chose the word "powerful," it is meant to describe the strength of the fragrance. I do not mean to say that the scent is too strong or even intrusive! Rarely have I experienced a fragrance that feels so skillfully unisex for both genders. However, a bit of self-confidence is still needed. It doesn't matter whether you have something in your blouse or your pants. In the former case, due to the dark strength of the scent. In the latter case, because the rose (which, although here extremely unflowery, comes across as rough and sexy) will still likely be found more prominently in women's fragrances... Long was the attempt to describe the scent or to visualize it, briefly summarized towards the end: If rose can manage to appear masculine in some fragrances, then "Miracle of the Rose" definitely counts among them. A refined, expressive, and character-strong exceptional fragrance. In my nose, it is indeed more extroverted and confidently masculine than feminine; although it is very well wearable for both.

Maremma is a very nice scent. It is a sandalwood & patchouli creamy fragance with loads of cocoa and a sweet flowery vibe. It is true that is very similar to black orchid by Tom Ford. If you smell them together there are some differences. Maremma smells more intense and overall more natural while black orchid is a bit more medicinal and plástic. In adition maremma has a better performance and lasts more time on skin projecting in a low/moderate level for 3-4 hours while black orchid projects high the first hour and then fades off quickly. However if a smell them separatly un different days i cant say which perfume is...i have tried It with my brother telling him use the two different days and i would say which one are you wearing...and not...i couldnt! I must say that i usted to LOVE black orchid because years before had a gorgeous performance. Now nevertheless It has changed and It has Lost all his powerful so maremma is a good option for those Who miss the old black orchid... Better for night time with fresh weather. Unisex! Scent: 9 Longevity: 9 Sillage: 8 Quality/price: 5 Versatility: 6 Originality: 6 Global: 9

I included Maremma in my Tiziana Terenzi sample order because it is supposed to be similar to highly touted Black Orchid. I have never sampled Black Orchid and figured on testing Terenzi's version while going through others from this house. Well, assuming Maremma does smell close to Black Orchid, I'm never coming close to it. In short, Maremma is a sweet, floral, plastic, synthetic mess. It's only redeeming factor is that as it dried down, it did mellow out a bit although it still remained awful. I can't see any man or woman wearing this. It is just SO bad. Longevity was good while projection was more moderate. The only thing worse than Maremma's scent is the fact that its longevity was good and I had to put up with it for so long.

With this fragrance, we have arrived in Tuscany, specifically in the hilly Maremma Valley, where this perfume attempts to exude the essence of this place. The scent promises fruity and floral notes with a woody base, all of which, according to the description, has "incredible" longevity. We shall see…. The scent: The fragrance starts off fruity-fresh and initially reminds me completely of grape sugar; shortly after, blackcurrant joins in. I believe there is also some Ylang-Ylang, which provides a light floral note in the background. Additionally, the scent is very powdery from the start. Perhaps this is due to the iris. From the heart note onward, a gradually stronger oud appears, which, in my opinion, does not quite fit the soft-sweet fragrance direction, as the iris makes the scent powdery, but the oud makes it seem a bit sharper. However, the fragrance remains floral. In the base, it becomes woodier. Fortunately, the oud does not become too strong and even recedes a bit, allowing the scent to remain powdery and pleasant (of course, the fragrance is still pleasant for anyone who likes oud). Patchouli and amber are hardly noticeable; cocoa is initially very faint, only detectable if you put your nose close to the sprayed area. Otherwise, from the base onward, you only perceive a floral-powdery scent. Only after two hours and even longer does the base become truly wonderful, with a powdery chocolate-cocoa note that smells delightful, though unfortunately it starts to weaken in sillage at that point. Nevertheless, it is an excellent fragrance. Longevity and sillage: The stated incredible longevity is okay, not really incredible, but it lasts on the skin for 8-10 hours and can still be faintly detected the next morning with generous spraying, although then it only smells like "something sweet" on the skin. The sillage is okay. I would say above average. From the heart note onward, it even becomes a bit stronger and will thus be noticeable to others. The bottle: Somehow, it seems there are only round and rectangular bottles here. We have another rectangular one, which, as I always write, somewhat resembles the cubic bottles from YSL. This one is black and has a thin wooden plate as a label, on which the name is engraved. The cap is appropriately rectangular, also black, and sits on a golden neck. All in all, very well done. Ah, Maremma is really well made. As already mentioned in the statements, the beginning indeed reminds one of sweet and delicious grape sugar. Since the fragrance is powdery from the start, many will enjoy it; however, I find the oud note somewhat unnecessary, but fortunately, it quickly fades. The base should not confuse, as it initially smells floral-powdery for some time before the lovely cocoa notes come through and make the fragrance more delicious. Whether this fragrance can truly exude the essence of the Maremma region, I cannot say, but it has become a lovely scent that is great for going out and can be worn in autumn/winter. Those who wish can also use it at home due to its soft and powdery notes, allowing one to be surrounded by a pleasant and fragrant cloud for a while. I would definitely recommend giving it a test.

If a fragrance settles on my skin for 24 hours, and the first thing that hits my nose in the morning is the scent from the day before, then that’s definitely worth a review. One thing in advance, my attempts to navigate the fragrance pyramid have miserably failed. Maremma has too much power, and after two full sprays, I feel completely overwhelmed. This stuff packs a serious punch. And that punch lasts a long time. The opening on my skin is like a blend of fresh, fruity, spicy, and at the same time sweet, although the freshness fades (too) quickly, but maybe that’s intentional. After that, as I said, I can’t find myself in the fragrance pyramid; Maremma simply remains incredibly full. I feel like I’ve layered Tom Ford's Oud Wood and Lost Cherry with Kilian's Intoxicated. Whether this massive mixture is appealing or not, the scent is definitely impressive and remains so. What I completely miss in the pyramid, and what I increasingly perceive over time, are vanillic undertones. However, arranged quite differently than one would expect from typical vanilla scents like Vanille Fatale or Tobacco Vanille. This blend of woody notes with the sweetness of honey and (I stand by this) vanilla likely brings that heaviness, and the scent gradually envelops its wearer (m/f/d) in a pre-X-mas mood. Heavily suitable for Christmas market vibes. As I said, I have rarely smelled a perfume that I find so difficult to describe. Also because there are always new facets to discover over many hours. And for that reason alone, a test recommendation. Longevity is massive, overnight is no problem. Sillage is dangerous, because first, it’s strong, and second, it might cloud the senses of the office neighbor. The bottle is a statement; this is not for the faint-hearted, but for someone who knows what they want. When: in the evening and in winter. Who: I see the ladies among us finding it appealing; for the gentlemen, pffff, I’m not so sure. Definitely not mass-produced, in my view, a special fragrance for special people.

I have had the fragrance for a bit longer now and I must say it is not bad! Especially considering I got it for under €90 back then. :D Regarding the scent itself (8.65 out of 10): Maremma is a sweet-fruity fragrance that also includes various floral, earthy, and woody components. I actually perceive a slight animalic note as well! Right upon spraying, the fruity and floral notes come forward. In the heart note, among others, lotus, oud, orris root, and honey join in. The fragrance retains its floral and powdery character, but it develops a woody-leathery + animalic aspect over time. This is probably due to the combinations of oud, lotus, and honey. Overall, it is still not completely animalic. In the drydown, it remains relatively linear like the heart note, but thanks to the base, it changes slightly. The patchouli harmonizes with sandalwood, cocoa, and amber, giving it a certain creamy and earthy scent progression. Not listed, but I also perceive a minimal lavender in the drydown. Longevity: 9 out of 10 Strong and intense due to the high fragrance oil content (Extrait de Parfum). [PS: My spray routine varies depending on the fragrance, but here a maximum of 4 sprays] Sillage: 8 out of 10 Very strong in the first 1.5 hours but becomes a bit closer to the skin after 7.5 hours while still projecting solidly. Final Rating: ~8.5 out of 10 A very solid fragrance if you can get it for under €150. I personally find it perfect UNISEX; not too feminine or masculine, but it tends to be more geared towards women here. If you like patchouli fragrances, you will most likely love this one. However, in my opinion, you should test every T. Terenzi beforehand and not order blindly. Except, of course, for Kirké :). Fans of Tom Ford Black Orchid can almost order this blindly; for me personally, it just smells a bit different, more luxurious, and less overpowering than TF Black Orchid (EDP).

... I have arranged to go on a picnic with friends. In my basket, I have fruits, baguette, and honey. Before I reach the park, I have to pass through an underpass. What stinks here? Luckily, it’s not long, and I arrive in the park. The scent of flowers and woods wafts into my nose. As planned, we meet in a small clearing.

Actually, I don't really like this - but currently, there's no other way. When you get the chance to sniff this relatively new and exclusive fragrance from the Prada Olfactories series, I want to preserve these impressions for other perfume lovers in the form of a comment. Unfortunately, I received neither samples nor a decant for extensive testing, but had to make do with a spritz on my arm to make the best of it. At least it's better than nothing! Now, let's get to the essentials: Soleil au Zénith is a fine, high-quality almost-gourmand that initially finds its way into the synapses a bit fruity, but at the same time also velvety-creamy. Accompanied by a rather linear progression, spicy notes like nutmeg and cinnamon emerge with a shy peach that timidly casts its shadow and takes its welcome place. Peach often quickly raises suspicions of not being of natural origin. Here, the fruit integrates unobtrusively as a small counterpoint in the composition. Ylang-Ylang contributes significantly to the floral-sweet orientation, making Soleil au Zénith overall more delicious, but not necessarily more gourmand. As I write these lines, I perceive the last molecules of this successful fragrance on my arm and must come to an end. The longevity is, of course, longer than the sun can stay at its zenith - and the projection is more than okay. Despite the name, one should not assume it's a summer fragrance, although it would still be quite wearable then. It should also be noted that given the absolutely high purchase price (I believe I heard something over €200 in the shop), the bottle could be designed to be a bit more stylish and noble. While it is nice to look at and hold, it reminds me enormously of Davidoff's Agar Blend. Otherwise, there's nothing to complain about.

When Peter Steele said "Her perfume smells like burning leaves" in Black no.1, THIS is the perfume he was talking about, this is dark, depressing, mysterious, foresty, this perfume embodies the essence of serenity and I am in love with it. To explain the scent, to me it opens up smelling like foresty pine, grass, soil, wet wood, and incense, drying down into a dark, almost burnt, smoke, incense, patchouli, and wood combination, with the slightest kiss of rose, I feel like unexperienced noses would not enjoy this, but that's not my problem, I would TOTALLY wear this, comfortably, it smells absolutely incredible.

Testing this today. The pine at the top is nothing as the one in Fille en Aiguilles, which is what I had hoped for. It smells artificial, like pine scented toilet cleaner, car perfume etc. That goes away quickly and I get a strong note of jammy, sirupy, cloying rose, because my skin always amplifies the rose notes. There’s a bit of incense and some screechy patchouli at the back. The drydown is woody with mild amber, but it just feels like it’s not well blended and smells dated. Had some friends smell this on me and they all agreed it smells like our grandmas in the 80s. Mind you, they all used cheap rose perfumes back then. A hard pass from me

It was a blind buy when I was looking for a substitute of my decade`s favourite Sisley. I don't know any more what pushed me to purchase it, but I fell in love immediately. It is pine, it is cedar, it is wood, it was a love from the first sniff. Clean and crystal fragrance, not too colony, not too male, great unixes, making you feel easy, casual and comfortable. Prominent Patchouli and Earthy notes, I just unexpectedly found them so great and wonderful. That direction was totally new for me and I felt exited to dive into unknown! It was a promising start, but sorry to say too short love story. Ecstasy didn't like me, after a couple of hours it turned into a smell of sunflower oil, which was so strong that I even felt being physically greasy und unwashed. Several years passed since then and I still keep a bottle, hoping my skin will change and Ecstasy will love my back. Please, please, I will be your loyal and devoted wearer.

Unfortunately, I was not impressed by this fragrance. When something is trying to portray a niche perfumery and often expensive story, I expect more. I want to see that artisanal quality, and the ingredients cannot be on the cheaper side. In case when a fragrance is made from a familiar and well-known composition, we, the fragrance enthusiasts want something that will shake that genre and sweep us from our feet. TOP NOTES The fragrance opens up with honeyed pine needles and aromatic spruce with gentle undertones of jammy rose. The combination of pine needles and spruce gives a foresty and resinous type of smell without going too much into the Christmas tree and holiday vibes which thanks to pebble accords gives it more of a watery impression. Overall, I found that the rose used here is somewhat flat and recognizable from many other scents I have tried in the past, and smells soapy. HEART NOTES The change in the heart notes is quite obvious and a nice change of pace. The greens turn into a flowery and earthy smell thanks to the woody patchouli and lingering violet. The rose is still prominent here, but softer due to the sweet smokiness from incense which becomes stronger, and the church smell starts to top above the other notes and accords. BASE NOTES By the time Ecstasy dries down, the soapy base gives it a nostalgic smell of realistic nature which is beautiful, but unfortunately uninspiring. The semi-wet woods thrown into the campfire, somehow slightly burning is what the left of the fragrance when it reaches the full dry down, and all the other notes had left their presence. *Check out my Parfumo profile to find out how can you read full reviews on my website.*

I have been coveting this for a very long time. Smells like dark forest and an underbrush of ripe berries. Reminds me very much of Bois de Paradis, which I regretfully sold or swapped some time ago. But I think this has less sweetness to it. It's a beautiful, quality fragrance that does not smell like chemicals.

Whatever artist names one of his works "Ecstasy" is not quite right in the head. No one can actually be that ridiculous. It really only fits in the category of "sex support." One could leave it at that, but fortunately, the results of artists are often better than their sense of naming.

Ecstasy is another fragrance from Terenzi's fiery line, where they symbolically incorporate the power of fire into their perfumes. So far, this scent is my favorite from this collection. Let's move on to the scent description: The fragrance: The scent is fresh-green with a wonderful pine note. A very light, oud-like scent accompanies it, but it fades away quickly.

Even though I like dark, earthy, and even musty scent notes, the perfumer has obviously slipped up with the patchouli here. The extraordinary opening initially thrilled me, as the scent begins dark and resinous-green, which definitely meets my expectations, but a pinch of patchouli would have sufficed in the base to round off the dark, mysterious aspect of Ecstasy.

When the Schildbürger emigrated to Holland, they founded a town called Den Bosch. The public prosecutor's office of this town was bored in 2019; no one wanted to build town halls without windows anymore, and before they brought out the mouse dog to burn the whole town down, they came up with the glorious idea to develop an artificial scent against ecstasy labs.

Night is slowly falling over the pine forest. The wind calms down. Softly, very softly, fine mist rises from the damp earth. And quite subtly, they seem to take shape. Bodies? With heads, arms, shoulders, and legs? Translucent and looming. They seem to appear everywhere among the tree trunks and underbrush. First individually, then in small groups.

tested at the Printemps de Bellecour store in Lyon last Saturday, I was eager to see what the other Pradas could offer, being a fan of night cargo. Well after smelling this one, I can clearly say that Prada is not reinventing the wheel and offering a basic perfume. the notes are also basic, we are on a perfume that resembles milly la foret, bergamot 22 or even neroli portofino. we have the impression that Prada did not try to stand out with this fragrance, that the brand just wanted to say look at me too I have a neroli. the only advantage that this perfume has with the others mentioned is the staying power which surprised me for about 5 to 7 hours when the neroli portofino scam no longer smells anything after 1h30. so if you had to choose a neroli that lasts I recommend this one. In my opinion it does not equal the best neroli which has unfortunately been discontinued by Prada infusion d'homme.

In general, I'm not a big fan of green heavy fragrances, mainly because they remind me of the smell of my hands after a garden weeding session. XIX March isn't that. It's green but in a creamy or fluffy sort of way. A quite pleasant green scent that would work well in summer. Unfortunately, the performance of XIX March really sucks. Barely 4 hours until it becomes a skin scent - that is - put your nose to your skin to even detect it. Projection is just as soft.

XIX MARCH was the first Tiziana Terenzi fragrance what I tried. Longevity and sillage are on satisfactory level, but I am puzzled with the perfume itself. It is mild, creamy and green at the same time, but without any characteristics. It does not irritate me, but I also do not remember after one day, what was it like, even though the components are high quality.

I have steadfastly stood planted in a no rules for fragrances stance where seasons are concerned. Perhaps that was due to just wanting to please the whimsy of my nose when I’m just jonesin for something like Laudano Nero on a summer eve. I’ve found this stance has led me to go far too long with experiencing some fragrances while others get all of my nose’s attention. I’ve been trying to change that by paying closer attention to what I’ve worn using the tracker while cross referencing how votes have classified frags where seasons are concerned. One such fragrance that I hadn’t smelled in… well, honestly, I don’t know how long… was XIX March. I visited Italy with family some 30 or so years ago and have long had a special place in my heart for all things related to Italy. One of those Americans with a romantic view of Roma, and the Umbian and Tuscan regions, who often dreams about expatriating. Due to my romantic remembrance of Italy, my nose has taken a particular liking of several Italian houses, Tiziana Terenzi being one of them. I particularly love the stories of inspiration that led to Paolo’s creations I’ve been joyed to have in my collection. This one surprised me. I absolutely was shocked by how much I loved it at first sniff today. Then again, I wasn’t surprised, after all this is one of Paolo’s magical elixirs. At first spray, I get a blast of green mint mixed with orange juiciness. This mix shocked my nose wonderfully so. I don’t know that I’ve smelled an opening quite like it. Not long after, as the heart notes come to play, that minty citrus gets a spicy zesty kick from the cinnamon and clove before it oddly, to my nose starts to get a bit of a classy shave foam scent. I’m guessing the lavender and Jasmine somehow take it down that road that took me by surprise. As the heart makes its way to the base, the woodiness of the cedar, sandalwood, and Vetiver come out giving it a woody footing as the Rosemary and nutmeg support the green spiciness mixing sight the woods in the base. I’m really pleased with this one and I’m glad I’ve ventured down this road to be sure I’m giving love to all my frags and categorizing them more to be sure I do just that, and don’t find myself wondering if it’s been 6 months, a year, or longer since I last wore a particular fragrance. For those who are concerned with whether something garners compliments, this one just might get you some olfactive love from others. I must admit I’m usually more drawn to fragrances I find fit the “that’s interesting” bill rather than the crowd pleasers. When I think of my TT frags, I tend to think along those lines, and not what I’d anticipate getting complemented for by passers by. This evening I wore this to class and a female classmate I estimate to be nearly 25 years my junior asked me what I was wearing and said “it smells like a really classy aftershave.” I’m guessing she was getting some of the same shave-related vibes I got when I began to think “classy shave foam.” Really lovely masculine feeling - to my nose - fresh spicy woody citrus frag for spring. Round of applause for Paolo from me!

The Terenzi family is primarily known for room fragrances and candles, which they produce under their own name, but also for other brands, near Rimini in Italy. Currently, six fragrances are also offered as Extrait de Parfum (30%), all well-crafted, some of them opulent with a broad fragrance pyramid, others delicate and fresh, like the one discussed here, "XIX March". "XIX March" is one of the more interesting fragrances in the line for me - and that’s because of the mint. I have been searching for a perfume with mint for a while (Menthe Fraîche by Heeley appeals to me, for example, but it is far too fleeting; Cartier's Roadster I find ordinary and quite dreadful). Mint seems to be a challenging note, as it quickly drifts towards chewing gum or toothpaste. I have the impression that mint requires a lot of finesse. "XIX March" starts off very green, with the mint at the center of my perception - probably also because it is such a characteristic note. The nice thing about it: the mint is finely integrated here, appearing as part of a silky-light overall composition, not intrusive or cheap. Overall: "XIX March" is very unobtrusive. This may be a disadvantage for some or at times. The name of the fragrance refers to a festival celebrated on the night of March 19, Focarina di San Giuseppe: fires are lit to welcome spring. I only recognize this to a limited extent: "XIX March" becomes woodier, balsamic over time, flattens out a bit, but nothing here burns, glows, or smokes. I smell spring-like, young flowers, fresh, bright green, and - as the last greeting of winter - the cool air of mint. "XIX March" remains very close to the body; one should not expect anything misleading from the "Extrait de Parfum". The longevity is good. Definitely worth a test as a summer fragrance!

XIX March was a Tiziana Terenzi perfume that had been on my wish list for a long time. The notes sounded truly fascinating, but ultimately it took me a whole 6 months to decide to order XIX March blind. Today my bottle arrived and of course I tested the scent extensively. XIX March is a really complex fragrance. The top note starts fresh and green. The notes here are a fresh orange, framed by a note of leaves right after a heavy rainfall, along with a mint note and an extraordinary nettle note. This nettle note is clearly what makes XIX March so unique. The heart and base notes are woody and slightly sweet. I can detect sandalwood, cedarwood, cinnamon, clove, nutmeg, and rosemary. However, I cannot smell vetiver or a floral jasmine note. The longevity is solid at about 7 hours with a moderate sillage of just under an arm's length and after about 4-5 hours it becomes close to the skin. The price is definitely a very good argument for XIX March. Being able to buy a perfume of this quality for a price of 65-90€ is truly an exception and makes XIX March a perfect scent for everyday wear and the office.

Many here try to approach this fragrance through the seasons. I find that exactly right and agree: XixMarch is something special. The combination of sweet, warm cinnamon and cool, green mint creates a very rare state of suspension. Connected by the full orange and garnished with touches of floral aromas, something so balanced emerges that carries many contrasts within it.

XIX March feels like a balancing act, like a rather cleverly crafted scent. It starts with a spicy orange, which at first seems familiar and less exciting, but is pleasant. Soon, however, a very green mint note joins in, compelling me to keep sniffing my arm.

XIX March is the first extrait from the Terenzis and thus also the first fragrance of the "Fire" collection. I personally think it’s great that they try to bring certain traditions and feelings closer to perfume lovers with various themes or collections. Even if the scents may not always be extraordinary, they still smell good.

Naming a fragrance after a mere date? "XIX March" by Tiziana Terenzi has done just that - but why? I didn't think much when I bought XIX March for the slowly approaching spring, but soon I found myself wondering what might have happened on that particular day, and so I began to search for it online. The coronation of the last emperor in the Holy Roman Empire on March 19, 1452?

Dry earthy Labdanum and leathery Saffron and Suede. It has a nice sweetness from the Jasmine. But as it dries it becomes a little bitter and unpalatable as the suede note dominates. Its extremely dry, powdery and resinous. it's smoothly blended. Just the notes are a bit heavy and skanky for me in the dry down. It's a shame as the opening is nice with the Saffron, Cardamom and Jasmine blend.

And the child surely wants a grape sugar candy! Mrs. Miehlke's heavily made-up face between her reddish hair suddenly begins to enlarge rapidly as she leans over the high counter of the old pharmacy towards me in her white apron. Her gnarled features twist into a smile, her bony hand fiddles with the tin can, and Mother's elbow nudges my shoulder. How do you say? Thank you! Instantly, I disappear along with my checkered sweater vest and corduroy pants into the old tin can. I dance in soft veils of powdery grape sugar, more lemon than orange, without the color of the packaging, you can never really say, as it shines and sparkles like in Grandma's snow globe, I glide on a small sled through the creaking artificial snow, dressed in Mama's brown suede jacket, warming myself in its subtle scent. I feel like I've been here for hours, in the can or in the old pharmacy. From the hall of forgotten moments, Mother and Mrs. Miehlke bleat like the adults in Charlie Brown, trumpeting and clucking in front of the beautiful wooden drawers with brass handles. Only in years will I come to appreciate their beauty, but their scent blends warmer and darker into the powdery snowstorm. Whenever I tug at Mother's suede jacket during these hours, I also catch a whiff of her fragrance in my tin can, whose dispersing magic is gradually fading, powdery, woody, slightly resinous, and just a bit leathery.

Al Contrario is mostly a yeasty, woody gourmand. Honestly reminds me of something that Kerosene has done, though can't put my finger on what . . . ? Maybe Sweetly Known? Anyway, it's pleasant, though pretty linear and as such ultimately boring. Some earthy nutty facets, a bit of dusty cacao. Lots of vanilla/benzoin and overdose of synthetic powdery sandalwood. The most interesting aspect is this faint, weird, musky human-skin, rubbery-yeasty accord. You're going to smell sweet, woody, and a bit animalic. Not bad, but nothing to write home about.

At first, I tested the fragrance on my wrist and thought it had power. Then, at the next opportunity (in the coming days), I applied 2 sprays to my neck. In my opinion, the scent actually becomes even stronger and with 2 sprays, it was really overpowering (not just for others). The extreme sticky sweet cloud of fragrance went straight to my head. I thought to myself, I can never do this to myself or others again. It smells incredibly intense and good, but one becomes very quickly saturated. After that, I almost wanted to give it away right away. However, I experimented a bit more. I actually only give myself one spray and I do it in such a way that not 100% of it lands on my skin. So from a certain distance. Then it is simply wonderful. You smell so delicious, you receive an incredible number of compliments, and it doesn't overwhelm anyone anymore; it is still very noticeable and by no means inconspicuous. If you know how to handle this extrait, it is wonderful. By now, I love it, especially during the autumn and winter season. You smell like roasted almonds, a bit of cotton candy, and a stall full of chocolatey sweets. In short, like a Christmas market but without any alcoholic note or anything from mulled wine.

Well, this seems to fall into the category of gourmand fragrances that I just can't handle. If they are refined? Sure. If they are complex? Show them to me. If they strike the right balance between sweet, spicy, and elegant? Bring it on. But Tiziana Terenzi hits you with such sugary force here that my saturation curve reaches its peak in less than 10 minutes. Malt as the opening aroma, quite authentically captured, reminiscent of a well (very well!) sweetened Caro coffee that I used to enjoy drinking with my grandpa as a child. But even back then, it had far less sugar added than what is used here. Vanilla, hazelnut, sugar cane... just reading the ingredients above slightly repulses me because I discover absolutely nothing in this fragrance that provides a bit of counterbalance, a little glucose compensation. The syrupiest of them all - I am reminded of the flavor syrups at the big mermaid coffee roasters, with which so many people completely ruin their wonderfully roasted coffee beans (that have at least flown halfway around the world for their consumption) and still grin happily. No, "Al Contrario" does not work for me at all. Gourmand can be so artful, but here everything sinks into a sticky, viscous, headache-inducing sweetness of the most cloying, sticky, and also one-dimensional kind.

Thanks to the dear AnimeFreak, I had the opportunity to get two Tiziana Terenzi fragrances at a very fair price in the Souk, and alongside the Rose Gold Oudh, Al Contrario was also included. Due to the partly very negative comments here, I was initially quite skeptical, but I thought to myself, as someone who prefers sweet fragrances, this sounds like it could be to my taste. After the package arrived from Austria remarkably quickly and I eagerly and excitedly held the two bottles in my hands, it took hardly a minute before I had the first spray of Contrario on my arm. The fragrance starts with a brutal malt note that I neither expected nor had perceived in a perfume before. Slightly bitter, somewhat fermented and spicy. Very interesting, but I can understand why some might flinch. After this malty, bitter scent faded relatively quickly, the intense sweetness that is often criticized here makes its first appearance. A truly almost sticky, burnt, and intense sweetness.. I liked it right away, and my first association was crocant. The crocant that I must have on my Pinocchio children's cup at every ice cream parlor. Caramel-like, nutty, sugary. The image of the ice cream parlor was further enhanced by the slight coffee scent that slowly developed from the bitter malt. As mentioned below, nuances of sweetened macchiato or milk coffee keep appearing. After about 30 minutes, the development of the fragrance is mostly complete, leaving a very pleasant scent of roasted nuts, crocant, children's malt beer, and sweetened coffee. I can understand that this fragrance may not appeal to everyone, especially since the constantly present sweetness makes it something only for sweet-toothed individuals. For me personally, it is a quite interesting, pleasant, and somehow special gourmand that I would love to wear on a date, during a winter walk, or at the Christmas market. The bottle is very high-quality and sprays very finely and cleanly. The longevity is, of course, due to the heavy sweetness, above average, and on my skin, I could still perceive the fragrance very prominently after 10 hours. The sillage is rather close to the body but also has strong performance. After 8 hours, I still had a light coffee-nut cloud trailing behind me. I would recommend this fragrance to any fan of sweet gourmands with a certain something. Treat yourself to a few calories on your skin and transform into a children's ice cream cup that doesn't take everything too seriously.

I tested this Al Contrario a few years ago, and now it is in my collection. I found this Al Contrario a bit overpriced, especially since it is the only fragrance in the Black line that comes in 50ml. The other fragrances in the line come in 100ml for the same price. However, this Al Contrario is still one of the better-selling scents from this Black Collection. 50ml should be more than enough here since it is not a daily wear at all. I tested it a few years ago via a small sample, which I revisited every few months or years. It’s a challenging scent that is hard to categorize and doesn’t fit every occasion. However, if you are looking for something unique, you are in the right place. Of course, you should be able to handle and wear gourmand notes. I find the current MSRP of €200 excessive. Even before inflation, €170 was already a bit overpriced for me, especially for 50ml. If you can get it for around €100, that’s already reasonable. Al Contrario seems to be the translation of “the other way around.” Fitting for the bottle: Unlike the other 100ml fragrances in this line, you get a 50ml scent with a huge cap and a small bottle. The label is also on the cap. Original. Out of habit, you might want to spray with the cap. This sweet-gourmand fragrance goes all out. It shouldn’t be blindly bought. If you are looking for a different gourmand that stands out from the usual sweets, you are generally on the right track here: Cozy notes like malt, hazelnut, cocoa, and a bit of sugar are very present. A very warm aura that stands out. Especially the malt opening is extremely unique. Malt is very rare, and this one scores points for its uniqueness. It may not appeal to everyone. This pleasant cocoa note fits perfectly with it. The vanilla in the pyramid is not present, but you get a lot of sweetness throughout, more of a tonka sweetness with some sugary notes. The hazelnut also comes in early and gives off a slight Hanuta vibe. Extremely pleasant without getting lost in the crowd. The base is quite nice with woody-balsamic notes plus this hazelnut-tonka sweetness. Overall, very rounded and pleasing. Performance is criticized in some statements. For me, it lasts quite a long time, and this scent easily reaches double digits with initially strong sillage. With Terenzi, you only get extraits, which you can definitely notice. This one does justice to a gourmand and should be worn more in leisure time and in the evening. Overall, a very pleasing and also unique gourmand, especially due to the malt. Specifically, this malt-cocoa top note should be tested, as it is very present for 3-4 hours. The further development is more pleasing and conventional, but not boring. A great gourmand for both ladies and gentlemen.
Upon spraying, a lot of yeast-fermented malt emerges, which hovers over the entire scent progression more or less.

I searched for a sample for my hazelnut fragrance, sprayed it on my skin once, and experienced that moment of magic - it was immediately clear that this is "my" scent. Ah, I love that feeling! I could hardly wait for the development before buying a bottle. For me, it is dark and bitter, but definitely sweet, not bitter.

The scent opens very pleasantly with sugar cane. Hazelnut and vanilla then emerge later. However, I cannot understand the comparison to the smell of Nutella at all. Those looking for Nutella will not find it in this fragrance, in my opinion. Nevertheless, I really like this scent, especially because of the interplay between sugar cane and hazelnut. Recommended for purchase.

This is like a creamy, sweet, Honey Custard from the Ylang-Ylang. With a rich thick White Floral centre from the Jasmine on a base of sugar sweet Vanilla. There are also little nuances from the Frangipani that are fuzzy and Peach like. Also reminds me of Gardenia with its dense heady sweet White and Yellow Florals that are creamy and silky smooth. Also has a tickle of fresh green spice maybe from the Ylang-Ylang that that give this a unique sparkle and is lovely when you catch a waft of it when it occasionally surfaces.

Now that I know that some Prada fragrances from the Olfactories collection have a connection to well-known or lesser-known songs - just think of Purple Rain, Tainted Love, or Marienbad - this fragrance is likely dedicated to the song of the same name from the early 60s by the Motown R'n'B singing group Martha Reeves & The Vandellas. It's not really my style, but okay - this is about the scent. And it is simply fabulous, if not even exorbitant. I rave so much about it because it is an absolutely floral-heavy perfume, which I usually struggle with, but here I am positively well served. The flowers - and I can at least recognize jasmine, ylang-ylang, and the night-blooming cactus - come across as lushly sweet, but to my taste, they are excellent. In between, a few spritzes of lemon have been cleverly smuggled in along with a light, naturally appearing vanilla. The whole thing feels relatively exotic and creamy, yet still masculine enough that I could wear it without any issues. That really means something, even though I think that women could probably relate to this heat wave more, without me having to think of menopause or something like that. In winter, but also on warm to sultry summer nights, Heat Wave could best showcase its potential. Longevity and projection are certainly rich and will draw enough attention according to the scent. I like it anyway and wouldn't have thought that I would find such a strongly narcotic floral scent so likable. On the other hand, I must attest that Daniela Andrier has done a solid job as usual. She probably has enough creative freedom with the Olfactories series from Prada and can wonderfully apply her own signature. My compliments!

Another Olfactories to fall in love with. The opening has quite an animalistic note. From my fragrance experience, this should be attributed to Ylang-Ylang. Whether it blooms at night, I have no idea. The opening is also quite lush. However, what emerges after a very short time is pure summer-sun joy, creamy, and it makes my winter blues heart shine. Other flowers are also playing a role, probably honeysuckle, or those bushes by the roadside that bloom at the end of June and whose scent fills the evening air, heralding warm nights. But by now, in terms of sillage, everything is in an average range, so I have no fear of potential headaches. In any case, I am quickly in a good mood and full of anticipation for summer.

I fell so in love with the comments here that I ordered a bottle blindly! Who wouldn’t want to appear feminine and attractive!? Unfortunately, the scent develops into a powdery lilac cloud on me! And I must say that I’m not a big fan of lilac! I also read that Afrodite reacts a lot to skin chemistry, so one should pay attention to a "balanced" diet due to the pH value... so that the pheromones can unleash their magic... the "OUT" came when my husband said that this scent smells like "Rosamunde Pilcher" :))) and of course I had to laugh and question this. He said "for more mature ladies." Yes, maybe you really need a certain maturity for this scent, and it’s like with orchids: with some, they thrive beautifully, and with others, they wilt!

Just like the second comment from my collection project, I would like to dedicate this to Afrodite - a fragrance that leaves me rather perplexed. For me, it is simply a dreamy veil of scent that I find absolutely heavenly, yet I find it incredibly difficult to put into words. I do not perceive the individual components separately - and I can say little about its development... The fragrance is definitely a perfume, and yet it merges so seamlessly with the skin that I could think I smell like this myself. My impression constantly swings back and forth. I spray the fragrance on and feel clean, fresh, and divine all at once. A fine powdery veil with a delicate lilac, which is noticeable but not "in your face," as I have experienced more often. It starts almost unisex-herb, cool - perhaps due to the lily of the valley, which I personally do not clearly detect, or the white peach, the white currants, for which the same applies? Almost unisex? Because I categorize lilac as more feminine. Additionally creamy-powdery - not too "heavy" and not too dry. Transparent but still present. Over time, the sweetness increases, yet I do not perceive the fragrance as sweet at any time. "Perfume-like" comes to mind - but only to the extent that I know it is not my own skin scent. Unfortunately, I cannot concretely describe "perfume-like" either. I perceived perfumes similarly as a child with my mother - perhaps amber? Or does the lily of the valley indeed give a certain perfumed sweetness? My mother loves lily of the valley, but she never had a signature scent that I can reference. Or is the peach perhaps becoming riper and sweeter here? Possibly also the tuberose... All ingredients that I like in perfume, but here I do not detect - only this incredibly divine mélange. I love to sniff at myself. Is it perhaps due to the listed pheromones??? Or do I simply enjoy the mix? While I do not find the fragrance sexy, I also do not think it is unsexy. I would gladly smell like this myself. The only scent notes I can clearly identify are the lilac in a creamy-powdery musk bed. Initially, there is this unsweet component that I have already speculated about above. Later, there is a transition to a perfumed sweetness, which, alongside the aforementioned suspects, may also be triggered by the vanilla pod. I perceive the fragrance only as a harmonious mélange, from which none of the scent notes stands out for me, which is why I find the description so difficult. Afrodite is infinitely delicate and transparent, so that "she" can pass as a skin scent, a delicious (but by no means gourmand) veil. Nevertheless, it is a perfume and, despite all its softness and skin closeness, surprisingly long-lasting - still noticeable on the nightgown the next morning. As for its development, I perceive only a shift in focus from unsweet, almost herbaceous (or better: cool) to perfume-like-sweet (or warm) and the fact that the fragrance almost merges with the skin. Wearable year-round for any occasion. For me, a so-called "Dumb Reach," as it never seems inappropriate in my opinion. It surrounds me with a divine aura. Under a fragrance named "Afrodite," I would have imagined something stronger and more erotic. Perhaps an oriental bomb? On the other hand, I have used words like "heavenly" or "divine" throughout this comment. I find it delicate yet enduring and feel comfortable with it. This lovely aura described earlier may evoke the goddess in each of us - initially cooler, then becoming warmer, but always delicate and soft (at its core?). It suits young and old, blonde and brown, in short: all women (of course depending on individual preferences). To my own surprise, after many shared moments, I actually perceive it as a tribute to femininity - not least because it is so hard to grasp despite all the warmth it conveys :)

You have to be a bit crazy to add a comment to a perfect one like the one from Sweetsmell75. Or a bit arrogant. Or maybe you just can't help it; you want this perfume to get the attention it deserves. And that's how I feel. I have a question right from the start: When you think of "Aphrodite," or her Roman counterpart, Venus: What image comes to mind? Is it one by Sandro Botticelli, showing the goddess standing naked on a shell, with her hair in the wind? I bet it is. But if not, then bring that image to mind, Google it if necessary, so you know what I'm talking about. I need it for this scent. I believe that "The Birth of Venus" has endured for over 500 years, has been referenced countless times from Warhol to advertisements for women's razors, and is so easily retrievable from our memory because Botticelli managed to create an archetype, the image of a goddess, or rather: the divine in the feminine, so that we understand it with our souls before our minds can, and even beyond that. And I have a feeling that 532 years later, Paolo Terenzi may have achieved just that again: with a perfume. With quotes and allusions in the choice of components and a masterfully crafted progression, he paints the image anew, olfactorily, into our senses and our souls. The very first impression when spraying the fragrance belongs to pink pepper, which creates a diffuse excitement, an uneasy anticipation, as if something were in the air, before it is almost immediately overwhelmed by white lilac, which, more complex and less innocent than its violet siblings, wildly washes over me, then is bound by the delicate, sensual, almost luminous sweetness of white peach. Do you still remember Botticelli's image? The rushing winds, the foaming spray, and in the midst of this tumult, the foam-born Venus, radiant and sweet? That's exactly how this smells. Vanilla outlines softly, white currant ensures that the fragrance, despite all its sweetness, does not become cloying, and preserves it, just like the iris later does, right at the threshold of the perceptible, from sliding into the trivial. Over time, the fruity peach note becomes more subdued, while the lilac remains in my perception for many hours. The scent now becomes more floral; lily of the valley exudes cool beauty, again bound by the sweet-creamy tuberose, which this time does not want to show off but only wants to be tender: the heart of the perfume belongs to the goddess. Like her, the fragrance in this phase is absorbed in itself, completely self-contained, not aware of the attention it attracts, or let’s say: not interested in it. It surrounds its wearer with an aura that radiates, a beauty that is neither young nor mature, but timeless, eternal. Terenzi is wise enough not to succumb to the obvious temptation of tonka bean, sublime vanilla, or something similar in his base, which would have made the scent too agreeable. And it's true, I don't know what ebony smells like. But I imagine that, alongside the patchouli, which I accept as given because I can't really pick it out, it provides what I would call "grounding," even if that is an inappropriate term for a goddess. Perhaps also for something mystical. Sandalwood and white musk lend a playful, unobtrusive warmth, amber a physical sensuality. And then there are the pheromones: whether this scent needs them, I can't say. But when you smell it and are enchanted and have to smile, then that might have something to do with them. Sweetsmell75 is right, very right indeed, when she says that the drydown is special: it stays close to my skin for hours like the wonderful memory of something that was perfect. I believe that when Botticelli painted his Venus, he loved women: so much that he wanted to honor them. And Terenzi does the same. He gives me, when I wear the scent of Aphrodite, a radiance, an aura that makes me feel connected to a goddess - and to every single other woman. Addendum: My special thanks go to Sweetsmell75, who, without knowing it, inspired me through her comment to this happy blind purchase, and to Covex, who encouraged me to trust her judgment blindly.

Aphrodite is, according to Greek mythology, the goddess of love, beauty, and sensual desire. One has certain expectations of how a fragrance named after the goddess of love should smell ;) Cool Sheets_Naked Skin ... sensual ... sexy ... extremely feminine! Well done, Mr. Terenzi ... the fragrance is worthy of a goddess! ;) About the fragrance: Aphrodite starts with a delicate peach note and lilac. Blackcurrant is subtly detectable with hints of vanilla in between. Fruity-floral-lightly sweet with peppery sprinkles. It smells very fine. As it develops, it becomes powdery through the iris with a floral background noise. Tuberose, neroli, and co ... I can't really filter it out (no heavy hitters!) :) Pure harmony! With fluffy-cool musk and earthy patchouli, it transitions into the base. Woody-creamy tones and warm-spicy amber are also part of the composition. Pheromones ... you can't really smell them, that happens in the mind ... but one might think there's something there ;) The drydown is simply sensual-sexy-feminine-beautiful ... I am so thrilled! *Woody Musk_Sensual Base* Aphrodite reminds me of Panthea (just without smoke and herbs), but also a bit of White by Puredistance. This Terenzi lies somewhere in between. Not loud, not harsh or heavy ... just wonderfully sensual smelling ;) Unisex? I think we ladies should keep this one for ourselves! Men, believe me ... you will love this on us! Aphrodite can be worn by women all year round. A true all-rounder! The longevity is around 8 hours plus ... the sillage is rather subtle. An intimate skin scent would fit ... have I already mentioned that the base is very special? ;) The bottle is beautiful and high-quality. Conclusion: Cool Sheets_Naked Skin What do pheromones smell like? *sexy* Panthea without smoke & herbs. Flowers fade over time. Woody Musk_Sensual Base! Psssst .... Aphrodite awakens the goddess in us ;) .... so girls ... give it a try! I can't wait for the fragrance to be on our shelves *impatiently_am*

Take that powdery, cosmetic scent you’ve smelled a hundred times, now mix it with a caramelized raspberry, and there you go — Pink Flamingos. Zero cherry on my skin, despite what they promised. But honestly? It still smells expensive. It’s refined yet playful, cheeky and intriguing. Like wearing a couture bag with sneakers.

From the top it has a light Lime and Citrus opening with a sharp, tart Raspberry, and Cherry accord. It has a strong fruity concentration with lighter florals like Violet and Rose that shine more in the drying stage. It has a synthetic edge to it which grates on me a little bit. It may be the over sharpness of Raspberry with the synthesized Hedione and Iso E Super that give it a slight hair spray texture, consistency and overly bitter lift like an aerosol. It does have a slight powdery texture but is overpowered by the hair spray smell. It is well blended. But is too unnatural smelling for me. It also reminds me of cheap cherryade or fruit squash.

After a tiring day, I come home and first take a bath. My thoughts are still swirling around the events of the day. I slowly relax in the warm water. Later, I apply Lince. Hhmm, what a wonderful scent, it gives me calm and security. Like a cozy blanket, it wraps me up. The similarity to Hypnotic Poison Eau de Parfum is definitely present. But Lince is much finer and more subtly woven. The star anise is zesty, and I also think I can perceive the absinthe, but none of the fragrance notes takes center stage. H/S is moderate and will not disturb anyone.

In search of a creamy, feminine scent, I came across Lince. I was already familiar with "Casamorati - Dama Bianca (Eau de Parfum) | XerJoff," but it didn't quite convince me; a nice scent, but for me, it's too sweet-sour. In the drydown, I like this "lilac-vanilla," but before that, this sticky powderiness annoys me (I know, powdery and sticky seems like a contradiction, but I really perceive a sour orange juice every time, as if it's been poured over powdered sugar until a mush forms. But enough about that scent.) Lince initially goes more in the direction I hoped for! In the first test: a castle full of valuable dresses; in the opening, I detect charming vintage vibes, an interesting absinthe & anise. The fragrance radiates romantic sensuality, I perceive soft creamy orange blossoms without it becoming fruity, and the absinthe note remains, as does a floral creaminess. The iris adds a bit of powderiness, while the fig seems to make the scent sweetly smooth, causing the fragrance to shift between powder & cream. A beautiful woman who does not sit in a tower like Rapunzel waiting for a prince to rescue her; instead, she is a confident, sensual woman who knows what she wants and develops strategies to get the best for herself. The vanilla, which comes in much later, is sweet, but more like vanilla blossom than gourmand, as the floral notes continue to dominate. In the next test, the scent comes across to me mainly as white-floral-creamy, and I don't perceive the distinctive absinthe note as strongly this time. For me, Lince is only conditionally vanilla; to my nose, it’s predominantly flowers and white body cream. Nothing special, I suddenly think, a bit 90's-like, nothing I absolutely need to buy. What a shame, the first test promised me more.

What a scent! So delicate and fluffy, it envelops you like a cloud. Lince is not a powerhouse like the other Terenzi fragrances I own, but it is no less intense and substantial. It’s probably due to the vanilla - it gives the fragrance a delicate note, but doesn’t let it dissipate easily. Overall, Lince is a vanilla scent, no ifs or buts! However, it’s not a "baking aroma" and also not too sweet, but dry and powdery. At first, I even smell a slightly bitter note (definitely due to citrus fruits), but thankfully no anise! There is a slight spiciness, but whether I should attribute it to anise - no idea, my nose is too inexperienced for that... And then the flowers come - an opulent bouquet of white flowers with powdery iris in the center. After that, the scent doesn’t change significantly, becoming a bit spicier... I agree with my predecessors, a very feminine scent - delicate, slightly seductive, in my view - very successful.

discovered in 2022 during a blind purchase to give as a gift to Madame. it is her favorite perfume to this day. elegant, refined, powdery and musky. I had never smelled anything like it until then in classic perfumery. the hold is impressive for almost 24 hours. if it had been classified as a women's fragrance and not unisex, I would have increased the note to 9. it is rather a feminine perfume for those over 30 to put on in autumn and winter. for those who wish to stand out with their trail and their smell. Hope this review was helpful to you.

I decided to switch over to Scentbox from Scentbird and this was the first fragrance I've tried from Scentbox and I feel very sophisticated in it. It starts with an absolute patchouli bomb that mellows in a few minutes to reveal a nice, tangy citrus. I picked because I love magnolia and you do have to look for those notes in this but it is there. This is very patchouli heavy but it's very refined.

Very cool women's perfume, I like its combination of powder and citrus, suitable, as I think, for any time of the year It smells like fresh baked goods to a lot of people, but not to me. I think it's suitable for any time of the year. As a minus I can mention its price, although it deserves it. My personal rating is 9.5/10

Do you remember Fuchur, the white, pearlescent lucky dragon from Michael Ende's "The Neverending Story"? I immediately thought of him when I first applied "Draco"... Light, bright, shimmering, shifting is this fragrance, which starts with an abundance of citrus notes that radiate nothing harsh or fresh, but gently prepare the stage for peach and jasmine. Like a warm summer breeze, I am enveloped by the initially strong sillage of this expertly crafted perfume. I can't filter out patchouli and cedar, but these components are likely necessary to prevent the fragrance from drifting into sweetness or becoming syrupy. Over the next few hours, a flattering development occurs into wonderfully creamy nuances, eventually releasing the juicy pear aromas. This scent is a women's perfume through and through! Understatement, cleanliness, freshness, and neatness would be my attributes for "Draco"! The sillage is strong in the first hour, but becomes more subtle while remaining noticeable for a long time. The longevity is excellent at 8-10 hours. Now about the bottle: I would have liked to ask Mrs. Terenzi to pay attention not only to the design in the future but also to test the usability. The bottle is quite unwieldy and covered with a tactilely unpleasant rubber coating; the extremely heavy metal cap sits precariously on top, and I can already envision some bathroom ceramics shattering if this thing falls... But those are just superficial details! Conclusion: Definitely test it, you girls among women who are looking for a very special, brightly shining summer fragrance! EDIT Hamburg... 10 AM... the scent lasts... ...of course, I mean 10 AM the next day!!! I have never experienced such incredible longevity, against all showering, hand washing, and moisturizing. Last night, this ever-present, gently fruity-pear aura annoyed me so much that I simply doused myself with "Poivre Piquant". Now the perfume lasts at most 4-5 hours, and the later the evening, the more Draco re-emerged! I neither want to retract my previous review nor the comment, as it is my true impression... Hereby, I only revoke my personal taste! I had forgotten that as children we collected tons of pears in the garden in autumn, which were then canned in jars. There was always a huge supply of them in the cellar, and in winter, we had pear compote for dessert. And pear compote and pear compote... (How enviously one looked at Libby’s fruit cocktail!) So, since that time, I simply haven't eaten pears anymore because I don't even like the smell... I had completely forgotten all of this, and during the first skin test, I didn't give the fragrance enough time... What a pity! My most expensive mistake!

The Hesperides are nymphs who guard a garden where a wondrous tree with golden apples stands. The tree was a wedding gift from Gaia to Hera and Zeus. Its fruits grant the gods eternal youth. Ladon is a multi-headed dragon who, at Hera's command, assists the Hesperides in guarding the wondrous tree. Heracles was to obtain these apples as the 11th of his 12 labors. As is common in myths, there are several versions, but in each, he manages to defeat or outsmart Ladon. For example, Heracles is said to have asked the Titan Atlas for help. As the father of the Hesperides, he would have had an easy time obtaining the apples. However, through various means, the fruits eventually returned to their rightful place, and Ladon was placed in the sky out of gratitude for his services. Draco is the scent from the Luna line that has not made it easy for me to put into words, as it behaves very fleetingly and quietly on me. There is the smell of freshly grated citrus peels that transforms into very tame floral notes. A fresh morning breeze in the garden of senses while the nymphs dance around the flowers with song. Towards the end, there are sweet tones of the alluring fruits that must have so intoxicated the dragon that he hardly put up a fight. I do like the scent as such. However, it may well be that it does not have the opportunity to fully unfold on me. My parallel test with the paper only allows me a longer perception but does not reveal any significant change in the scent. Draco remains simply quiet, tame, and fleeting for me. I find it somewhat unfortunate that I might have even liked it better than Andromeda. But perhaps others have the chance to engage in a longer battle with the dragon before he surrenders.

It's only New Year's and spring (or warmer weather in general) is still a ways off, but I'm going to test this fragrance here that is more suitable for warmer days. This one was included in the Terenzi sample package that is currently circulating and has landed with me, so I tested it right away. Thus, this fragrance is the first one I am testing from the "Moon" collection.

Draco is a very beautiful fragrance that has positively convinced me. It sounds expensive from start to finish. After reading some not particularly positive comments on certain forums, I initially became afraid of "overdosing" and therefore only sprayed once. And I must say: longevity and sillage are very good!

Interestingly, the reviewer before me had the same association with the white lucky dragon :) Fuchur was a hero of my childhood... my cuddly, beautiful snuggle dragon. In my childish daydreams, I often flew alongside Atreju on the back of this friendly, child-loving dragon.

I have been a total Tiziana fan for a week now… I alternate between my test Souks Draco and Cassiopea and I don't even know which one suits me better. I was worried about Draco having too much musk, too much sweetness, but none of that turned out to be true. I find Draco to be suitable for everyday wear on my skin without being the least bit ordinary.

A somewhat different fresh scent. Very floral but at the same time with a slight fruity note Great for ushering in spring or summer Longevity and sillage are average Very, very soft, powdery, and pleasant Unisex Price-performance ratio is, in my opinion, appropriate Personally, I find it better than the flagship Kirke

The opening of this is heavenly. It has a fresh punch of Orange, Honey and a tickle of Eucalyptus and Mint that melds together creating an old fashioned, luxurious blend that has little nuances and Complexity. The newer Prada Rose is more powdery and simple but still absolutely gorgeous where as this is more fresh, bright and Green with the Tea and Mint. It has the same double Rose heart. This is sweeter with the honey accord. I prefer the pungent effervescent opening of this but the powdery delicate soapy soft dry down of the 2017 version. Both probably the most gorgeous scents I've ever smelt along with Fleur D'Oranger.

"Infusion de Menthe" could have been an appropriate name for this scent, and it could have been marketed unisex as well. But, from the beginning: To my knowledge, "Infusion de Rose" is only available in Prada boutiques, but I was lucky enough to trade with a dear Parfumo friend and came into a generous decant. Thanks! The scent opens with a fresh, slightly sweet rose. There are delicate flowers, no "Wham, here I am" flower. More like in "Clair Matin" and yet different. For a more sophisticated explanation we need to ask our "Original Rosenliesl" member. A more orange than yellow citric splash is also among the fruity notes. Little by little the mint comes in, spreads out more and more, and gone is the rose. Again and again, the flowers are trying to battle but don't have much of a chance and then give up. Only a touch remains. It was at that point when I thought that the name does not fit 100% the scent. And, it was then that I had the impression that the fragrance is quite suitable for men, too. There is no further development. The longevity is quite decent for such a fresh scent, with 4 hours. In my closet "Infusion de Rose" gets a place next to "Pamplemousse Rose" by Hermes. I think that those two get along quite well.

I love the scent of roses and I'm a sucker for anything that smells like the traditional rose. Prada Infusion de Rose, in terms of comparison, is much fresher than my staple rose fragrances which I'm used to. This fragrance is better suited to the warmer weather. The opening was quite beautiful. A sheer, Spring-like pink rose with mandarin orange and a touch of mint. It was perfectly refreshing in all its glory. Pretty and feminine as well. I actually wished this fragrance stayed that way, however the heart, while not a complete disaster, introduced some notes that I personally think don't work too well with rose. I found the holly and honey notes a bit too much when blended with the sweet, delicate rose accord. It actually turned the scent a little bitter on my skin. I'm pleased Prada took a risk, but I'm disappointed that they couldn't make it work. The bottle is a work of art in itself, yet the fragrance left much to be desired. The drydown is mostly strong minty tea and soaped-up roses. I'm not too impressed with this strange blend. I had such high expectations I'm afraid. The lasting power was poor, which is a sad effort from Prada who usually produces quality scents that linger for hours. It's difficult to find a clever mainstream rose-based scent, so in times like these, I still rely upon my niche loves, particularly Annick Goutal's rose fragrances.

I always look forward to testing a Prada fragrance (oh,… this is once again the last one for now due to lack of samples…). I find Prada fragrances really well made and, as I often mention here, they belong to the scents that are well crafted despite the synthetics. But I must also admit that I am somewhat envious of the ladies. Sure, we guys have d’Homme and Amber pour Homme, two great fragrances, but you ladies… you have so many infusions to choose from! Aaargh, luckily some of the newer Prada fragrances are unisex,… and I MUST get samples of these scents. But I digress. Here comes Infusion de Rose, a lovely fragrance,… once again for ladies… of course… The scent: The scent starts off quite fresh (but not citrusy) and clean. Before you can even distinguish the individual notes, you smell the typical, slightly soapy and fabric softener-like Prada DNA. In the top note, there is a light, but very fleeting mandarin, along with the sweet, but also slightly off-putting beeswax. However, the roses and mint are the most prominent. While the roses give off a beautiful, floral-sweet scent, the mint adds a certain freshness and blends well with the rest of the fragrance. Of course, there is a certain synthetic quality, but it is well done. For the most part, the scent smells of roses and rose fabric softener with a hint of mint. And of course,… the powdery aspect cannot be missing here, although the scent is not as powdery as, for example, in the d’Iris infusions. The longevity and sillage: I saw it coming that this fragrance would not have great longevity. Even though I thought the beeswax could save the day, it unfortunately turned out to be a bit too weak, so the scent lasts only about five to six hours. The sillage is also more average and will not leave a significant scent trail behind, but the fragrance still rises well to the nose of the wearer. The bottle: The bottle is rectangular with slightly rounded corners. It is transparent, allowing you to see the pink perfume liquid. On the front, the metallic Prada plaque is attached. On the side, there is a label that shows the same pattern as the packaging and lists the fragrance ingredients. All in all, as always, a beautiful bottle. Hmm, it must look great to have some of these infusion fragrances on the shelf. *sigh* Infusion de Rose is also a very successful Prada fragrance that can captivate from the very beginning, as long as you don’t belong to the group of people who protest with posters against synthetic and/or “soapy”-smelling fragrances (but if you do belong to those people, then you’re just missing out on a lovely scent). I mean sure, I’m not particularly fond of synthetic fragrances either, but as mentioned at the beginning, Prada does a pretty good job here, as in all the infusions. Moreover, the synthetics are much less noticeable here, so it could even be tested by the aforementioned protesters, as the scent has become a lovely rose/mint fragrance. It is an all-rounder that can be worn in any season, although it probably won’t be perceived at all outdoors in the cold during autumn and winter. Those who want to use it outside should rather apply it in spring and summer. I would definitely recommend Infusion de Rose. I liked it, and I would love to smell it on a lady!

Generously, I received a surprise sample of this fragrance from a former user. Golden light and angelic choirs were the first words that came to mind when he asked me about my first impression. When I wear Borea, I feel as if I am immersed in golden light. A comforting warmth flows through my body. At first, this scent is sweet, fruity, and brightens my mood even on a dreary day. In the drydown, a very warm, sensual warmth develops. Sandalwood, vanilla, and musk create a wonderful symbiosis, and now and then, the scent of peach wafts around me. In short: Borea simply smells heavenly, and I no longer want to be without this fragrance.

Franca and Tonino have a garden in the lagoon. Of course, they also have a house, but that is completely irrelevant: What can you do in a house other than cook and sleep? In a garden, however, ah, in a garden, that’s where you truly live! Only about how this garden should be, there is disagreement: Tonino, who hails from the fertile plains of Apulia, has very clear ideas: In a garden, you grow fruit, basta. What else? Franca, on the other hand, the Venetian with milk-white skin and Titian-red hair, can only shake her head at such simplicity: A garden must be a sea of flowers, a frenzy of colors and scents. And if it’s not that, ha, then it’s just a maledetto vegetable patch, per amor‘ di dio! The battle for the garden has been fought with the utmost passion for decades, resulting in incredible rose bushes standing between slender, tall peach trees and those with cherries, plums, and pomegranates, irises, freesias, and all imaginable varieties of white flowers.
