The veranda is overgrown with jasmine and climbing roses, bougainvilleas climb along the house wall, and beside it stands a tall pine tree that gently creaks in the wind, providing us with the shade we need in the heat of the lagoon. I sit on the veranda, the sun is just setting, painting red-golden circles on the house wall and on my face. Tonino has impressed me with his expert dissection of a coconut; my fingers still faintly smell of its firm flesh. Now he comes back from one of his beloved trees to the table, with two or three peaches in hand. “Guarda queste!”, he calls out, “Look at these! Can you smell the fragrance! Ah, like roses and raspberries and like the skin of a girl!” He winks. Peaches, he explains, must be eaten while they are still warmed by the sun. And that simply doesn’t work, he emphatically states, if you take them from a supermercato’s refrigerated shelf, ecco! The last sentence is, of course, directed at Franca, who comes onto the veranda with a tray full of almond sweets and unloads it in front of me. I am just cutting the peach, pink at the edges, white inside, sun-warmed, fragrant, and incredibly delicious. Franca rolls her eyes: “Madonnina mia, Tonino! Don’t you see that you’re boring her! She’s a woman, don’t you understand that, you Apulian donkey driver? A woman, Tonino! She loves beautiful things! Did you notice the roses, Cara, do you like them, yes? I’ll make you a bouquet of them later, you can take it home, the whole room will smell, you’ll see!” Of course, I noticed the roses. They compete with the jasmine in their fragrance. And with the almond cookies and the peach and the coconut. I nibble on the sweets and listen to Tonino’s fiery retorts. From time to time, he calls upon the assistance of the Virgin Mary; when he moves, he exudes a very delicate, subtle musk scent: a discreet hint that Franca is a happy woman. The wind gently blows from the sea, wafting clouds of jasmine fragrance over to me. The pine tree creaks softly, and the crickets make a hell of a noise. I close my eyes and think: if paradise were to be any different, I would much rather be with Franco and Tonino. And I silently pray that this moment does not pass. But that’s exactly what it did. Twenty years lie between Franca, Tonino, the garden in the lagoon, and me. Sometimes I think of them and where life is taking us. And then a perfume package arrives at my home. Black and gold, Borea is written on it. I spray some on my wrist, close my eyes, and inhale the fragrance: A wave of sandalwood crashes in, recedes, and behind it: A peach warmed by the sun, a hint of coconut. The lovely sweetness of almond. And right after that: A wild frenzy of jasmine and roses and all kinds of flowers, powerful, warm, and I am back in the garden in the lagoon, listening to the two of them comfortably argue, nibbling on almond sweets, enjoying the hint of musk. It is summer, and I am back in paradise, and I get to stay. They say that the scent was created by Paolo Terenzi. But that is, of course, nonsense. It comes, I am sure of it, directly from Franca and Tonino.

Don't be fooled - despite being a shimmer mist, this is actually really lovely; plus it's a truly-new scent from VS (I haven't tried anything else similar from them). While this starts out with a brief coconut nectar opening, it quickly moves into the bulk of the fragrance: a Tahitian vanilla "fresh laundry" blend. The note breakdown for me is: OPENING: [70% coconut nectar] much more present in the beginning, this is slightly indolic and sweet; a nectar-like take on traditional coconut (I picture honeysuckle combined with creamy coconut) [30% Tahitian vanilla] more subtle at this point, see below for more detail DRY-DOWN (after 10-15 minutes): [10% coconut nectar] faint background player to me at this point, only noticeable if focusing hard [50% Tahitian vanilla] an almost "fruity"-like tropical-feeling vanilla, with a "vanilla yogurt" type of quality to it [40% "fresh laundry"] I believe this is the "sea breeze" note mentioned; it does feel like laundry that was line-dried by the ocean - a quiet hint of salty sea breeze, but mostly feels like a solar cotton/fresh linens that are "neutral" (not overly sweet, floral, musky, etc.) OVERALL: A fresh, clean, tropical vanilla choice for summer! WEARING: - Smells the same on my skin as it does on paper - Mild projection: not a "beast" performer, but a bit softer; perfect for the office or sensitive noses - Decent sillage: was nice to catch wafts of myself when moving my arms - Good longevity (for a mist): up to 4 hours for stronger wear, then much weaker after SIMILAR BLENDS: If you've smelled any of these, I'd say it smells like a combination of: Fresh Vanilla Blossoms (the "fresh vanilla" part) Beachfront Blanket (the "solar linens" component) Coconut (2024) (the warm coconut), and Sea Island Shore (the sea-infused fresh laundry/linens) So if you like any of the above, you might also enjoy Coconut Sol Shimmer ! A NOTE ABOUT THE SHIMMER: There are a variety of shimmer/glitter mists out there, and Coconut Sol Shimmer is definitely more of a "shimmer" rather than a "glitter" mist. Meaning it's a "fine" or small-piece shimmer, rather than chunky or larger pieces of glitter. The amount of shimmer was also small on my skin, in comparison to the concentration/amount you see when looking at the bottle. After I applied it on my skin, the shimmer was present but not particularly noticeable. It also didn't rub off to other objects/clothing/etc. - but it might be that I wasn't particularly heavy-handed in application, and I also waited for it to dry (especially because this is more "runny"/prone to dripping than the non-shimmer mists) before having any contact with other fabrics/things.

Creamy white florals with a soapy, Aldehydic texture and freshness. Magnolia, Orange Blossom and Patchouli are most prominent to me with a golden sweet amber accord that melds everything together. Very unique, smooth and natural smelling.

Yesterday I wrote a review for Purple Rain by Olfactories, and today I'm focusing on Nue au Soleil, as the two are practically siblings. Just as Purple Rain bears a strong resemblance to Infusion d´Iris, Nue au Soleil relates to Infusion de Fleur d´Orange by Prada. However, I find Nue au Soleil to be significantly softer, rounder, and more harmonious (well, somehow the considerably higher price has to be justified ;-)). While Infusion de Fleur d´Orange starts off a bit scratchy and generally has a greener and harsher vibe, Nue au Soleil is soft, gentle, delicate, and harmonious from the very beginning. Perhaps it's the musk, which is absent in Infusion de Fleur d´Orange, that makes me perceive Nue au Soleil as so tender and cuddly soft. There are no harsh notes here, and the scent remains linear until it fades. As soon as I get a whiff of Nue au Soleil, I feel transported to summer, envision a beach with white sand before me, and experience lightness and happiness. This may sound cheesy, but somehow this fragrance truly brings joy. I can't help but smile just thinking about it. It's now on my wish list!

I wanted to try Tiziana Terenzi perfumes for some time, but managed to get ahold of a sample only recently. To be honest, mostly because a lot of the descriptions didn't sound very encouraging to my tastes. But Moro di Venezia came with a lot of promise and I'm glad to say that it indeed delivered. The scent opens up with sparkly fruity goodness, gets a bit powdery and cloyingly floral sweet on the drydown, without losing the fresh fruity aspect. I absolutely adore summery fragrances and this indeed one of the best summer smells I've ever tried. Fruits and berries ripened with sunshine, jovial flowers blooming all throughout - it all feels like a summer fairy tale. The scent is so perfect it doesn't feel realistic, more like a description from a book or a nostalgic memory. The staying power is not the best, but this one doesn't have to be really strong. It sort of matches the description of a fleeting Mediterranean season. I'm not sure whether it's a keeper for me, but I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a fruity fresh summer scent. It's a really well done scent, a whole experience is something one must try for themselves.

I bought this Tiziana Terenzi blind as well, through a good deal in the Souk, and I was willing to take the risk. The notes sounded very interesting to me, actually worth a test, if it weren't for the usual problem with some Terenzis. There are simply no offers for decants in the Souk on Parfumo. Moro di Venezia arrived at my place in the middle of last week, and now I have tested the fragrance 3 times and think it's time for a review. I want to address the question right away whether the fragrance is more for women. I believe the fragrance is truly unisex with a slight tendency towards the feminine. Personally, this doesn't bother me. But men who do not like flowers and fruits should better stay away from Moro di Venezia, as this would lead to disappointment. Moro di Venezia is a floral fruit bomb. I can really smell the listed fruit notes: grapefruit, pineapple, bergamot, and blackcurrant form the fruity component throughout. The floral component is also recognizable as stated: violet, lily of the valley, jasmine, with the violet being particularly noticeable to me. The whole thing is rounded off by a gentle vanilla note, which adds a bit of sweetness. I don't really recognize the woody notes. In my opinion, they are more present as a fixative for the other notes and increase longevity. Moro di Venezia will definitely please fans of: Tom Ford Soleil Neige, This is not a Blue Bottle 1.2, Accento, and Accento Overdose.

The past months have been a challenge for all those who do not indulge in winter. The temperatures have become milder, and the sun is gradually claiming more and more time in the daily routine. On a cold night, where temperatures regularly drop to freezing, gentle morning hours follow with softly muted light. The rising temperatures envelop the meadow in front of your house in delicate mist. Morning dew has collected on the blades of grass, and the lily of the valley blooms gently across the entire meadow. They defy the cool conditions of the night and carry their scent softly through the streets. The increasing hours of sunshine result in a boost of vitamin D. This, in turn, has a direct impact on your immune system and your mood. You feel happier, more active, and more content. The season is perfect for permanently brightening your mood. So it makes sense to close your eyes with the help of thoughts and a little spritz of Moro Di Venezia: - A delicate mist from the spray head envelops you, and you close your eyes. Zesty fruits are present. The grapefruit from the street vendor in the small alley in Venice competes equally with the pineapple and blackcurrant. At that moment, the hustle and bustle of the busy alley fades away, and you find your way back to the beautiful meadow with lily of the valley that you gaze at when you stand on your balcony. The sun caresses your face, and you can't help but grin. You feel refreshed and clean, and you lie down on your freshly made apartment bed. The balcony is open, and the curtains are carried into the room by the wind. Nothing can upset or stress you today, and if it does - you close your eyes and dive into the hectic yet peaceful world of Moro Di Venezia. - And here we arrive at the fragrance that has accompanied me through the last months and is now finally able to showcase its full potential. I love the fruity opening, the drydown that comes across soft and clean, and the lily of the valley that keeps making its presence known. The longevity is very good for a fragrance in the fresh, fruity category on my skin. I perceive it for 8-9 hours. On clothing, it lasts noticeably longer. The bottle is beautiful. At least it suits my taste. Black and gold, lovely embellishments on the cap and neck of the bottle. Everything feels very high-quality and elegant.

This fragrance was recommended to me at my favorite perfume shop, and I was head over heels in love after the first application. Yes, a man must like this floral scent, but then it is a prophecy for the nose and its senses. A little tip: there is a mutual fragrance twin for me, equally pricey and therefore not a budget option, but I have both perfumes and they smell really, really similar, and I even like the combination when I mix them in a travel atomizer in a ratio of 2/1. I’m talking about the fragrance Xerjoff Apolonia. The Apolonia has a single scent nuance that I can distinctly recognize as a difference, and that makes the blend more rounded. So, the fragrance is insane, and anyone who likes this scent direction, whether man or woman, will love this caressing fragrance. It always reminds me of my former teacher, who wore a scent that was clean, floral, and at the same time carried the sweetness and aroma of fruit, with a very light woody background. The fragrance lasts quite long and intensely, but by no means is it loud or intrusive, and I love smelling it on my own skin and always sniff at my wrist. It also screams love and sexuality in the form of, let’s cuddle and enjoy closeness. A great fragrance that, by the way, can occasionally be bought for significantly less than 300 euros, and then one should seize the opportunity. You can’t go wrong with this wonderful scent.

At first, it’s super pleasantly fruity, and then flowers join in as it develops. It rounds off perfectly and smells really great. But after about 45 minutes, the scent literally takes a turn. It starts to smell more like stale flower water, how unpleasant! I don’t like that! Sillage was good up to that point, but I can’t comment on longevity - I had to wash it off.

My first perfume from the brand TT. I didn't want to test the classic like Birch at first since I own Erbe Pura and according to the forum, these two have a lot of overlaps. So I ordered a sample of the Sent. Three sprays later and I smell blackcurrant everywhere. Wonderfully crafted. It is sparkling, fresh, and of course, the blackcurrant is strongly in the spotlight.

During my last visit to my favorite perfume shop, I was once again impressed by the dedication and love for her profession shown by the saleswoman. Her ability to find the right scents for me led me away from my original plan to test the Xerjoff fragrances.

Prada’s Highline series does not hold back. Many high-quality fragrances and of course a musk offshoot among them. There is a connection to Armani’s Musc Shamal, although more in the base. I discover at Prada: Peach, earth, moon dust, powder, white soap, rose, textile cleaner, vanilla ice cream, super glue, Hansaplast bandage, gray woods, benzoin mist. For me, it’s more asexual than unisex. It has a positive presence, yet it’s not even very loud! Worth €250? Maybe. Better than the secondborn Musc Shamal by Armani? A subtle yes! The musk family remains the musk family, and both are lovable, albeit from different parents. Armani has more of a dentist atmosphere and cooler chemistry. Update: Fragrance purchased (-30%, oh you unholy Black Weekend). It is warmer and more pleasant than the Musc Shamal. Not as soapy and metallic. In short, the dear older brother. But maybe just adopted after all. Who knows for sure? They can live well side by side on my arms. Amen.

Due to the super exciting fragrance pyramid and my not-so-stable mental state, I bought Velorum blind. Admittedly, for the bargain price, it would have been almost a crime not to buy it. Fortunately, my nerves were not strained by an unnecessarily long delivery time, and I was able to hold my treasure in my hands after a few days. Bottle: The bottle gives a high-quality and solid impression. The golden embellishments are well-crafted and complement the elegant appearance. Scent: Naturally, with a fragrance in this price range, the expectations are particularly high. For me, Velorum starts as a sensual fruit cocktail that gains more sweetness as it develops. Furthermore, bright woods, amber, and musk are clearly perceptible, but in a very pleasant measure. The individual components are, in my opinion, extremely well balanced; you don’t feel overwhelmed by anything. For me, Velorum represents elegance, with a mysterious sexy note. I could perceive Velorum on my skin for about 8-10 hours; even after showering, a hint of it could still be sensed. With Velorum, you definitely attract a lot of attention, compliments are practically guaranteed. Conclusion: Velorum has shaken my world, one of the most beautiful fragrances I can call my own. For me, it is an absolute dream scent, at a very indecent price.

There are many scents that practically scream for more. They are perceived and transport you into the world of fragrance dreams. I would like to particularly highlight "Velorum," even though the price is very high. Every drop is precious to me; it allows me to dream and fulfills me. I enter the room and blossom, and I hear this rapture. Oh noble scent, you have a high purpose; you give me warmth in my heart. I love the sharpness of the spices and your fruity beauty. The cinnamon and almond take me by the hand and guide me through the room. Every embrace from you is a revelation. You gift me the most beautiful rose and stay with me for eternity. Thank you for this feeling.

I find the scent perfect for the days when it’s not too warm, but also not so cold that you can wear the right beasts. The perfume opens very fruity. Over time, the typical Terenzi sweetness comes to the forefront and the fruity aroma takes a backseat. Too sweet for hot days, and on really cold days it gets lost. But on autumn days, when it’s pleasantly warm and only occasionally a cool breeze blows, Velorum is an absolute dream and worth every cent. Everyone has to decide for themselves if it’s worth that much money.

"Intense!!" is indeed the first thing you think after the first whiff of this rich Prada in its classy bottle reaches your nose: WOW! On me it's all sultry, sexy, creamy patchouli with a citric edge (NOT a hippy patchouli, but rather a smooth and *posh* type of patchouli) mimosa and vanilla in a balance struggle with the labdanum, and a rose note that peeps its head in now and again to say "Hi!". It's a beauty for everyone that likes sexy, mysterious and balmy scents that smell rich and expensive. It's a stubborn, mysterious and heavy scent that makes it a must love perfume so it is not for everyone, a definite 'MUST sniff before buy' scent! I can smell a likeness to Strip by Agent Provocateur - but to me, Prada is deeper and more 'demanding' on the wearer. This one needs a woman (or man) that isn't afraid to be noticed, since it is a loud, intense and Diva like fragrance I would recommend this one for evening, date-nights and any special occasion that you want to make an 'Intense' statement. ::NB:: The atomizer on the bottle is been known to leak! On the first bottle I had, the atomiser bulb did not leak, but on the second one it did. Badly! To preserve the gorgeous (and pricey!) potion I solved that by pouring it in a CLEAN! perfume decanted. Pity, since the bottle is very classy. I have complained about this (as I am sure many others have) and wonder if Prada will fix this issue before I run out of potion and start craving a new bottle. Silage is: "I will knock your socks AND shoes off!" -- Longevity is: "I will keep you barefoot for a good 7+ hours".

Prada - a label that can evoke the "want" feeling in many people. Whether it's clothing, bags, accessories, or fragrances, each piece awakens desires. Thus, Prada undoubtedly plays in the league of Gucci, Chanel, and Louis Vuitton. The driving force behind it all is the visionary Miuccia Prada; no season goes by without eye-catching new patterns, shapes, color combinations, and materials. Without her, Prada probably wouldn't have managed to stay in the top league for so long. And when even Anna Wintour (editor-in-chief of US Vogue and universally recognized and undisputed fashion authority) publicly admits that Prada is her favorite label, it speaks volumes and brings invaluable publicity and PR. Prada only decided to launch perfumes relatively late. It goes without saying that this decision was the right one and is presumably profitable. My "problem" with Prada fragrances has always been mainly that they were too light and fleeting for me (the Infusion series as well as Amber pour Homme). However, I have come to appreciate "Infusion d'Iris" very much, and "Amber pour Homme Intense" is one of my personal favorites, as it truly is an "Intense" and not just carries the name addition. Yet somehow, the scent that was missing was THE fragrance, a statement scent, unmistakable, radiant, and sophisticated. Characteristics that Prada likes to flaunt. And then came "Prada Intense." Now somewhat aged, at the time, to my knowledge, not really noticed and nowadays only difficult to obtain. Since "Prada Amber" and "Prada L'Eau Ambrée" did not really meet my expectations, my last attempt should be "Prada Intense." OK, when the bottle arrived and I tested the scent for the first time, I was really skeptical. Because I expected, uncharacteristically for Prada, an extremely powerful, expansive, and overwhelming "women's fragrance." Far from it. Powerful? Yes! Expansive? Yes! Overwhelming? No! The top notes are fresh, unsweetened, and unfruity, and are actually flattened on the spot by the heart notes (patchouli, Peru balsam, and rose), with the rose playing a rather subordinate role. Patchouli and Peru balsam, on the other hand, are unmistakably dominant. Not whispering and sweet, but almost cool and harsh. A real surprise - at least for me. And then the base comes into play. Initially very gentle, it increasingly asserts itself against the overpowering heart notes. After a relatively short struggle, it gains the upper hand - incredibly soft, powdery, and noble. And this lasts for hours. All base notes seem to merge with the skin, digging deep into every pore, only to be gradually released again. "Prada Intense" is undoubtedly not a wallflower, but it comes across gracefully, mature, and sophisticated, so it never becomes clumsy, cheap, or vulgar. I would call it self-confident. Since the scent (for me) never slips into the floral, it can also be worn by men. However, one must absolutely and unconditionally like patchouli, vanilla, and all the other "softeners." The longevity is immense, the projection could lead to irritation in the environment (so restraint is advisable), and the bottle with the Prada typical balloon atomizer is absolute luxury. For me, "Prada Intense" is a Haute Couture fragrance that I will wear (contrary to my usual habits) situationally, thoughtfully, and very selectively. In my opinion, this fragrance requires a certain setting, a festive occasion, cultural events, and the like. However, this certainly does not exclude the possibility that it might just catch me off guard one day ;-)

...is just the sight of the bottle with its toxic green contents and the noble spray nozzle, I feel like a true lady when I sit at my dresser, look in the mirror, and spray this exquisite patchouli scent on me. Those who do not like patchouli should not acquire this fragrance. It is not a sweet fruity opening, although it is introduced by citrus fruits, which are immediately overtaken by the warm notes. I cannot detect mimosa; I do not know that note well enough, but patchouli, rose, and the vanillic Peru balsam, which also has a scratchy and slightly bitter scent, immediately take the lead. The honey-like labdanum resin, sandalwood, tonka bean, and vanilla make it very warm and powdery fine, the long-lasting base is absolutely fantastic. The musk is missing in the classic amber; I think I can tell whether another woman is wearing the amber or the intense version. The intense version is also less floral in the heart note; here, patchouli and the Peru balsam definitely take the part. I honestly do not understand why so few have it. This is a very noble, subtle, aphrodisiac scent for ladies, a balsamic aromatic fragrance par excellence. To all Prada Amber fans. Get it for yourselves:-)...but it seems to be only available abroad now! Postscript: by replacing the screw cap with the spray nozzle, slight flakes seem to have formed in the bottle. So it seems that bottles with spray nozzles are not 100% airtight. However, Prada seems to be more airtight than Dior with Midnight Poison Elixir, because if you turn the Dior bottle upside down, it immediately leaks. Prada does not, but I would not recommend transporting it in a handbag; I have never considered it myself. Nevertheless, I prefer a normal spray bottle. Furthermore, it seems that the contents evaporate from time to time and the liquid reduces. I have now closed the cap again and removed the spray nozzle. Otherwise, the bottle would probably be empty in the box soon without me having used it. A spray nozzle is only good if you use it constantly. For long-term storage, it is probably less suitable. What a pity.

After experiencing L'Eau Ambrée, I soon found myself feeling quite differently after a promising start. The amber note, which initially held back and behaved as if it were outside the gate, did not politely knock later on, but rather burst into my nose with a huge bang. The result was nausea and dizziness, and I needed something to scrub it off quickly! Despite everything, I could never forget the pleasant aspects of the fragrance, nor that I actually really enjoy having amber in my perfumes, as it comes across so beautifully sensual and cozy. If there’s too much of a good thing, I tip over and my love for this fragrance note fades. Now, since I really liked the fragrance pyramid otherwise, I took a look at the siblings of this Eau Ambrée. I was particularly taken with the Eau de Parfum Intense, whose composition reads wonderfully and goes down like oil. Thanks to a bargain purchase, I finally got my hands on the jewel. The start is clearly in orange "colors," and with bergamot and oranges, this happens in the truest sense of the word. The mimosa and patchouli knock on my door only timidly and supportively after a few moments, and a wonderfully balsamic note takes over from here. The rose is hardly perceptible here; it holds back a lot, and if it weren't mentioned in the list, I wouldn't miss it at all. It is really hardly present. After about ten wonderfully fragrant minutes of feeling good and winding down with this scent, a strong wood note sets in for me. I have never been able to perceive wood like this in a fragrance. I really feel as if I am fenced in by it and sitting right in the middle to test this perfume. It reminds me of the moment when you enter a church and immediately perceive the intense scent of the wood from the pews. I always find myself inhaling and enjoying it, and somehow this wood smell completely calms me. I always have a very cozy feeling then. In Prada Eau de Parfum Intense, this wood note remains dominant until the end and gives off a warm, sensual, and cozy warmth with the vanilla. Thus, I see the fragrance more for cooler temperatures, as it would otherwise come across as too heavy, and especially the individual notes would choke each other. The longevity is indeed fantastic, and the sillage is decent. One should not overdo it here. Too much of it also clouds the experience of gradually exploring and enjoying the different fine notes. All in all, a perfume to feel well-groomed, elegant, and feminine, to wrap oneself in sensuality, and to defy the wet and gray of autumn and winter. Fans of the "Shalimars" should also find something here if they are looking for something without their usually dominant jasmine note but want to linger on their noble vanilla. Prada L'Eau de Parfum Intense: a pure "Boisé de Sensualité"! PS: The image is misleading: the bottle is in a cardboard case. Without it, it actually looks like the Prada Amber, only the liquid is a bit greener.

As some know, a great love was born in Munich... for meatballs. The transport to Liechtenstein (it didn’t make it to Switzerland because of my male companion) only succeeded through being tucked into my Prada bag and a glance into the meatball cave every 15 minutes. As long as nothing leaks out, nothing gets smeared, right? In hindsight, I found it quite amusing that I was transporting dead animals in dead animals, but that’s just a side note. The brand Prada has thus been associated with meatballs since last weekend, and I like both very much! Due to current events (to all Swiss: 50.- (instead of 110.-) for 50ml at IMPO), I have to share my thoughts on this fragrance ;-). "Prada Intense" is, as Confusion already said, a real patchouli bomb and reminds me strongly of my "Midnight Poison Elixir". I find the opening quite similar, very spicy, it really hits you. Compared to Dior, however, Prada is overall a bit shyer and fresher, not quite so "overbearing". Nevertheless, it is a very mature scent, not for a femme-enfant! If Midnight Poison is perhaps a bit too heavy for you, you will find with this Prada a slimmer, more subtle version that is just as beautiful! I also agree with Confusion regarding the wearing recommendation: Please apply sparingly and especially wear and enjoy it in the evening! By the way: The bottle is actually transparent and the lovely liquid is a subtle poison green. I find it strange that only 2 users are listed here, as it is actually too good to be ignored. Therefore, my personal call to all Prada lovers: Let yourself be bombarded with "Prada Intense" during your next perfume store visit!!

…Smelled like this. Noble, gold, luxury. Sun. Fruit. Heat. Phew. I took a blind leap and did not regret it. The scent is on one hand very velvety, warm, and elegant. On the other hand, luxurious, heavy, and intrusive. Not sweet, it is finely bitter with a sweet component. The bergamot and peach are especially present at the beginning in the top note. Afterwards, I smell the warm woods, the very fine caramel, and the sand. The blend is simply extraordinary! An absolute fragrance for a noble, strong, luxurious woman! But not one who walks around with brand designers, plastic nails, and lots of makeup, but for one who radiates luxury and wealth solely through her presence, her aura, her voice. Bet this fragrance makes you wanna dance…

I discovered Tabit rather by chance in a perfume store. For me, it was a real surprise at first sniff because I initially thought I was smelling a €400 version of my hand soap. However, this was only the case in the opening, and I found the scent to be quite soft and very pleasant afterwards. The quality and the scent itself are simply amazing, and it is ideal for a warm summer day. Although it is somewhat reserved in terms of sillage, the reactions (especially from the female side) are always positive.

TABIT, a beautiful summer fragrance. I am immediately in the sun and warmed fruitily and softly. Not as enchanting as Kirke, lighter but similarly fruity, a Terenzi scent of course. Nevertheless, it stands on its own and is for me the alternative in summer. The bottle is very high-quality and elegant. Thus, spraying it becomes a visual experience as well.

Tabit is another blind buy for me. Of course, it’s not exactly sensible to buy such fragrances blindly, but you surely know how it is when the passion for scents is greater than reason or rational thinking. Tabit is mostly purchased by women, if I take a look at the category “I have.” I can ease your fears right away. Tabit also suits a man; of course, “man” has to be okay with the floral fruity notes, but anyone who can handle this need not fear that Tabit is not for him. Tabit is truly a fruit bomb. There is a lot of peach to smell here. The peach is the dominant fruit note. The bergamot gives it a fresh twist, which also makes Tabit unisex. The coconut is really very subtle; you need not worry about smelling like a Piña Colada. The flowers make Tabit harmonious and soft. Unfortunately, I cannot identify what kind of flowers are present here. However, the base changes Tabit significantly. Wood, vanilla, musk, and amber push the fruity and floral notes aside, leaving Tabit to finish woody, sweet, and fruity. The packaging is definitely a highlight here. Unfortunately, I don’t really know what to do with all these huge packages, because besides taking up a lot of space and looking good, the packages serve no other purpose. The price is, of course, a very controversial topic. I can tell you right away that I would definitely not pay the MSRP, as it is outrageous, but I will still orient my price evaluation around the MSRP, because that is what I will have to pay if I want to purchase the fragrance from an official retailer. Another point of criticism is clearly the bottle, which seems to be a magnet for fingerprints. I can tell you that these fingerprints on the bottle drive me crazy, even more than with other Tiziana Terenzi perfumes, because with Tabit, the cap is also gold. The longevity is definitely very good; I can perceive Tabit without any problems for over 10 hours. The sillage is clearly more than an arm's length with generous dosing and only becomes close to the skin after just over 7 hours. Tabit is truly like a vacation in a bottle and transports me to distant beaches, which is especially wonderful in these times and can put a smile on my face.

I purchased Infusion d’Iris Cedre and received a box of Prada Infusion de Cedre instead. After being confused, I contacted Prada directly. There was some initial confusion on their end too, but after some time, I was informed Infusion d’Iris Cedre was renamed to this. I was told the formulas are the same so I’m not sure what accounts for this version being slightly lower rated. This perfume does open with a nice helping of doughy Iris (the same found in her sister, Infusion d’Iris) but I was sad to see it soon fade by the midpoint. As an iris lover, I never want to see it go. The cedar here does lend the perfume to take on a slight “baby wipe” scent at the mid but it mostly settles by dry down. Iris does make a return at dry down. That is not to say this perfume is poor. It’s not. It’s a soft, powdery (at mid through base), clean, pleasant scent. Compared to other iris-cedar perfumes, this one isn’t as well done as I’ve smelled but for a simple, clean, uncomplicated perfume it does its job.

Had I not known that the most famous of Prada's infusions features the iris, I still would have felt that this Infusion de Cèdre was somehow searching for a missing part of its soul. I haven't had the pleasure of sampling Infusion d'Iris (2007) Eau de Parfum , and I have to assume that Infusion d'Iris Cèdre is the same as this. Can anyone let me know, please? Because I see bottles of all three marketed in various corners of the web as three distinct fragrances. Back to Infusion de Cèdre , it's a nice, intimate, powdery fresh scent that seems a bit masculine to me, a perfectly acceptable scent for the office. It has that freshly washed, dried in the sun white shirt smell. But, for me, it's missing something that would make it amazing and make me fall in love with it. And I have to assume that that something is the iris. Because without it, it's a good, but not particularly amazing perfume that I just have to have. So now, I have to find out what Infusion d'Iris (2007) Eau de Parfum is like. As a lover of the iris, my nose demands it.

.. or also "The Great Prada Iris Test". Here you have to be careful like Schmitz' cat! Three fragrances, almost identical names, very similar scent pyramids - spoiler: I think they're all three great - but there are small, fine differences that I want to break down here. Testing conditions: all three fragrances applied on the arm as simultaneously as possible It should be mentioned right away that Infusion de Cèdre is considered the successor to the unfortunately discontinued Infusion d'Iris Cèdre . Why they left out the iris in the scent pyramid, who knows, maybe they wanted to market the fragrance as "more masculine"? But it’s there! On my skin, it even appears right from the start and amusingly more powdery than in the fragrance that has it in the name. This leads to the local comparison tool showing 'only' 44% similarity, nonsense... Infusion de Cèdre comes across to me differently than listed here: dry, name-giving cedar with powdery iris, then becoming balsamically warmer with a bitter dried mandarin peel. Unisex. Well-groomed. Somewhat distant/tough. Extremely suitable for business. Quit playing games (with my heart)! In comparison, Infusion d'Iris Cèdre has less mandarin, is a bit more mineral, with a few bright neroli sprinkles; I envision bright white lab coats (alternatively starched shirt collars) and stainless steel surfaces. Target audience identical. There really isn’t much between the two; I would say 90% identical, and then personal preference decides which one you might prefer. You definitely don’t need both. The third in the group, and in direct comparison more feminine, is Infusion d'Iris (2015) Eau de Parfum (Be careful! Most people today are likely testing the 2015 version and not the original 2007 one..). Actually, only the weighting of the fragrance notes has been shifted in favor of the iris, and a bit of musk has been added, but that’s enough for me not to see it as suitable for men anymore. Important in all three cases: powdery iris, not lipstick iris! And all the included fruits are unsweet, more dried/bitter than juicy-fruity. The longevity is also business-suitable for me, maybe just a discreet touch-up during lunch break. But you won’t suffocate colleagues or leave a scent trail down the hallway (never say never, but you’d have to bathe in it for that). Usable all year round except in the absolute high summer.

The Infusion line from Prada has produced some quite appealing fragrances that initially seem monothematic but then turn out to be a bit more complex. Fortunately, "de Cèdre" is not just composed of cedarwood notes, but has some additional elements, here indicated with mandarin, benzoin, and incense. So far, so good; however, these ingredients are hardly discernible. In contrast, a trace that reminds me of Amber pour Homme Eau de Toilette with its slightly dry powderiness is much more noticeable. The source of these vibes is completely left open by the fragrance pyramid and remains a mystery. This is actually further proof that one should not overestimate these pyramids. At least the cedarwood fades relatively quickly, and what remains is for me very intensely oriented towards the soothing pleasant "Amber pour Homme (Eau de Toilette) | Prada." Sure, that's not necessarily the worst thing that can happen to a fragrance, but it does feel somewhat irritating when you were primarily expecting cedar. Therefore: Infusion de Cèdre is a rather unexciting Eau de Parfum that plays the cedarwood card from the top note and then switches to "Amber pour Homme (Eau de Toilette) | Prada," which makes the creation more interesting, but for those who prefer a cozy powdery scent without much sweetness, it's better to go directly for the original.

Today I finally tried my sample of Tyl for the first time. Upon spraying, the top note of lavender immediately comes forward; I couldn't detect any lemon. The scent is so soft-powdery, simultaneously creamy and gentle. It floats above me like a silk cloth. In the heart note, jasmine clearly dominates in my perception, with a slight hint of rose detectable. If innocence had a scent, it would be this one... It is so incredibly subtle and unobtrusive that it almost annoys me a bit. For this incredible price, I expect a bit more development - though this happens differently for everyone. Maybe we just don't match well... In the base note, vanilla unfolds very distinctly and incredibly pleasantly, flattering. I perceive musk very subtly. All in all, it is literally a fairy-tale scent that is very, very seductive, yet innocent at the same time and very, very feminine. However, I would not buy it at this price under any circumstances.

Let's not beat around the bush: the fun is expensive. I had the scent as a sample. Originally, I wanted to wear a different fragrance for my wedding, but I simply fell in love with Tyl and chose it. However, I will now try to describe the scent as objectively as possible. The scent: With the top notes of lavender and lemon, the opening is just 0815: fresh, making you think, "well, not very promising." It takes an eternity for the rose to finally come out. This is not about a cheap synthetic rose. No, it is very natural, soft, delicate, modern, hand in hand with amber and jasmine, which are definitely not overpowering. Vanilla and ebony dance together with musk, and this is not a turbulent musk, but as soft as that of Narciso Rodriguez in white musc (for comparison). So it is fresh, clean, powdery, floral, but what makes it special? The oxygen note, it rounds everything off and makes it unique. Longevity: It lasts and lasts and lasts. Even after showering, it remains. It doesn't go anywhere, it's there for days. The chemistry with the skin varies from person to person, so you have to test it on your own skin. On clothing, it lasted all day and left no stains on my white dress. Sillage: It holds well, but it is not an opulent scent; you can only smell it closely after a few hours, but it is still present. It is definitely room-filling, as I have received endless compliments from people about the scent indoors. Outdoors, you can forget it, no one smells you, except those who hug you (if you like skin contact, this is for you XD). A big paradox, but this saying describes it perfectly: "money talks, wealth whispers." One person who hates fragrance (yes, such beings exist) told me, "It smells so pleasant, so different, I've never smelled anything like it." Lovely. I can't evaluate the bottle since I don't own it and will probably only buy it when I've made enough money so that spending 800€ on a perfume doesn't hurt anymore. But let's be honest, if I buy a perfume for 800€, everyone has to smell me lol. I don't want a mediocre sillage that can only be smelled in an enclosed space. Also, another thing, it is more for women; I am the type who likes to wear unisex scents, it doesn't matter, as long as I smell good and it should be the same for everyone, but this is absolute femininity, you smell like a delicate doll. I can completely understand why men don't like it on themselves, but try it on a woman... I love it, and you don't choose who you fall in love with.

I am new to Parfumo and trying my hand at my first review: A very unusual scent (for me): a fresh, creamy, and sweet vanilla, very delicate and rather feminine. I find it very suitable for spring when everything is blooming. In the opening, citrus fruits and ozone are noticeable, followed by lavender and amber coming to the forefront. All notes are very well balanced. Vanilla and woody notes linger in the base. This is love at second sniff.

For those who honor Prada La Femme, the spring edition is also worth a test ;) Because alongside frangipani, floral components as well as mandarin can be discovered, giving the fragrance a fresh-fruity character. While the base is very similar to the original: elegant cleanliness, white dress, freshly showered, smelling expensive. Floral soap in the porcelain bowl. Like Prada La Femme, this one is also suitable as an everyday/outgoing scent. The top and heart notes have been expanded scent-wise (see above). Season: Spring-Summer. However, rather at 23 than 30 degrees. Even Water Splash, although the name might not suggest it, smells very elegant, well-groomed, and simply beautiful. A few years ago, when I smelled Prada La Femme, I was blown away. This is not a perfume, I thought, this is a lifestyle that radiates nothing but luxury and quality without even trying. Prada La Femme speaks for itself. I think of a young lady who is elegantly dressed without appearing forced. Never arrogant, just naturally self-confident. Intellectually, she is as attractive as her appearance. One might think she wears no fragrance; she is the fragrance itself because it simply fits, because the scent lies on the skin like silk. In "Water Splash," this DNA is also present, but to return to the image of the lady, it feels as if she is walking through her large castle garden, between magnolias and frangipani, the water of a fountain splashing in the background, and the midday sun bouncing off the glass roof of the white pavilion. Was that too far-fetched? Well, it’s just that Prada La Femme and this variant fascinate me so much because they don’t smell like a perfume but like the natural scent veil of the wearer herself. Do you know that feeling?

Hey fragrance enthusiasts, we all have little time, so I’ll keep it short and concise this time! I can’t remember exactly how it happened, but the scent came to me, like the child to the virgin. From the first breath, I liked this dry, fruity, leathery aura. But it always felt too harsh and rough for me, especially for 250,-! However, as I progressed step by step on my perfume journey, I realized what quality this fragrance holds: 1. The bottle is incredibly high-quality and stylishly crafted. 2. The scent lasts "only" about 8 hours on the skin, but those hours pack a punch in terms of sillage! 3. Finally, I discover a fragrance where I can truly sniff out all the notes (except "forest")! Dry leather, delicious cocoa, fruity fig, and other dried fruits! 4. The scent is equally good from top to base, and I find that wonderful. It smells exactly the same after 8 hours as it did at the beginning; it doesn’t develop into an Ambroxan, vanilla, shower gel, or wood chaos. 5. It’s wearable all year round. Whether in warmth (that’s when the fruits come out) or in cold (that’s when the leather and cocoa come to the fore). In short: For me, truly a masterpiece. When my last decant is used up, the bottle will come to me! It’s a shame that the fragrance gets almost no attention... or maybe that’s a good thing? Thanks for reading! Love you all Moritz

Recently, I wrote a rather euphoric comment about Soul Of The Forest. I mention this right at the beginning because there is at least a recognizable similarity between these two scents. Moonlight Shadow starts off woody and remains woody throughout its entire scent journey. This base note varies depending on the 'companions' in the fragrance pyramid, but I would definitely describe the scent as woody-sweet-bitter. Moonlight Shadow initially presents itself as fruity-spicy upon spraying. Not gourmand or overly sweet when I say fruity. Rather creamy and bittersweet - like a ripe peach. The fig also comes through quite dominantly from the start. Slightly bitter and very spicy for a fig scent (perhaps also due to the connection with cumin, which I personally don’t perceive as strongly as I had feared). On my skin, the scent has from the beginning the already mentioned forest aroma, which probably comes from the cedarwood and suits the fragrance excellently. The opening smells almost a little mystical. After a few minutes, the cocoa becomes noticeably present yet not too prominent. The cocoa really deserves mention here, as it does not smell sweet, nor chocolatey. The cocoa unfolds a background aroma that is already patchouli-esque. And I mean really good, non-musty, and by no means hippie-like patchouli. So dry and serious, like (to make another comparison) in Patchouli Absolu, which has been my signature scent for years. You can already tell that Moonlight Shadow is a rather dark, spicy, and enveloping fragrance. It is also unplayful and serious, which I mean in a very positive way. Unexcited might also be a very fitting word. And strangely erotic. The previously mentioned mystical touch is maintained throughout the scent's development and almost takes on meditative qualities when the cedarwood, which has been perceptible all along, comes to the forefront. And it smells incredibly good and surprisingly authentic regarding the "forest image." Once the scent has settled after about (for me) 20-30 minutes, something in it reminds me of Au Thé Rouge. There is some herbal tea-like note that keeps bringing this association back... But also this comparison (like the previous ones) is not meant to say that Moonlight Shadow "smells like..." but rather to convey an image of the type of fragrance. Oh, I can't detect leather at any point, but I don't miss it at all. Ultimately, I find it difficult to summarize everything into a kind of conclusion. Moonlight Shadow is a dark, spicy-bitter scent with a distinctly noticeable forest theme. Great fig note and dark brown patch-cocoa elevate it significantly. It indeed appears noble and yet, due to its almost meditative character, also relaxed. And somehow quite sexy.

I had couple of samples before ordering this rocket, but today I recieved the big boy full bottle This vanilla is to die for, this is a very spicy very warm very sweet/ambery addictive smell. I do get simularities with nishane Ani but Ani is less refined and much boring in my opinion, ani would be good for daily use while hale bopp for a night out because this rocket really stands out. Performance is on the roof, is very potent especially the first hour, it’s an extrait de parfum so you wouldn’t expect it to project as much but this one does trust me. It is a little bit pricy tho but if alexandria 2 can cost 500€ then spending 350€ on this is like getting it for free this stuff is really good, its bold its rich it’s powerful,potent,sweet,warm, night out or a date would suite this the best. It’s very sweet spicy and ambery but it’s also very refreshing because of that lemon on the top. Overal rating: Smell 9/10 Longevity 9/10 Projection 8/10 Versatille 8/10

Hale Bopp is a comet that we probably won’t see again on Earth until 4419. My grandma used to say, if I’m still alive then. Surely none of us will be, and this Hale Bopp will likely be forgotten by then. There was also a cult - they called themselves Heavens Gate. The followers believed there was a spaceship behind Hale Bopp. They committed suicide, hoping to be picked up by the spaceship and reach a higher level of consciousness. Some men were even castrated to live particularly ascetically. I’m not really into astronomy and astrology - gastronomy is more my thing. But when I read Tiziana Terenzi, that changes abruptly. I’ve decided to test all the fragrances from the Terenzi universe. In my mind, this scent feels like a dense fog and is also a bit harsh due to the lemon. But this comet becomes smoother and softer. I like the mix of rose, vanilla, and patchouli. A bit of cinnamon and nutmeg rounds it all off. I don’t smell sage at all. It somewhat reminds me of Coromandel because I also perceive it as slightly powdery. I’m not a big fan of labdanum. If the note comes through too strongly, I don’t like it. With some fragrances, I can overlook that or accept it, but not here.

tested at the spring store in Lyon Bellecour. I had the pleasure of discovering some references from the Prada private collection. The bottle from the oriental collection is really beautiful, elegant and refined. It makes you want to try it. the pchit then the disillusionment, I was disillusioned because it looks a lot like memo shams or shl mortal skin. this perfume smells of heat and dryness, I had the impression of being in the desert and looking for an oasis, littering a rocky ground with dead snake skins. the name was therefore well found, the perfume corresponds to it. It's one of the rare ones that I find can be worn in any season, with a preference for winter to seek the heat of the desert. a rather masculine perfume and for those over 35. This is not my style of perfume, otherwise I would have kept my mortal skin. So this perfume will not be added to my collection, I advise you to test it before purchasing because it is special.

Porpora opens with a mild raspberry tinged thin, slightly airy rose underpinned with moderate clove spice and animalic musk support before transitioning to its heart. As the composition enters its early heart the thin, airy rose turns piercing green as it adds a clove-laced incense facet, shedding most of its raspberry accompaniment with slightly earthy patchouli joining as co-star with the musk remaining in support. During the late dry-down the composition remains highly linear, as the rose and patchouli gradually recede, leaving the remnants of the musk and piercing clove-laced incense combining with amber from the base through the finish. Projection is good and longevity outstanding at over 20 hours on skin. Looking at the ingredients list, many have compared Porpora by Paolo Terenzi to my favorite perfume, Portrait of a Lady by the great Dominique Ropion, finding it an excellent alternative for far less money... Money aside, it was with great interest that I secured a sizable spray sample to see if I agreed. To save those that want an immediate verdict from reading further, the answer is "not even close." Porpora opens immediately with a *faint* similarity to Portrait of a Lady with its rose and raspberry tandem, but the ingredients and implementation are completely different. In Porpora, the rose is thin, slightly synthetic smelling and the raspberry very subtle, with an odd smelling musky undertone that is rather off-putting. By contrast, in the original formula of Portrait of a Lady the rose is jammy, huge, natural smelling and the raspberry much thicker and more intense, with patchouli already playing a key role in the development. In the middle of Porpora, the synthetic thin rose joins modest earthy patchouli with the odd animalic musk remaining, but now adding a sharp-pitched, whiny green tinge from poorly implemented clove and incense. Portrait of a Lady keeps perfect balance of the jammy rose and patchouli, with ambroxan from the base by contrast. The late dry-down of Porpora is very linear and that high-pitched green tinge to the remnants of the rose with the odd musk remains through the finish, only adding in slightly sweet amber to the mix that doesn't improve things. Portrait of a Lady, by contrast, also remains linear, but in its case the perfect balance of rose, patchouli and ambroxan remains through the finish. Both perfumes have unbelievable longevity at nearly a full 24 hour day, but Porpora is much less vociferous. The bottom line is the $170 per 100ml bottle at discounters Porpora may have an ingredient list similar to Ropion's greatest masterpiece Portrait of a Lady, but passing similarities are all that overlap, and the "average" 2.5 stars out of 5 rated Porpora comes up *way* short both by comparison, and unimpressive when judged independently, mustering a neutral recommendation by itself, and a *huge* avoid if being considered as an alternative to Portrait of a Lady at any price.

I recently received Porpora as a sample, and of course, I had to test this fragrance immediately. First, I must say that I am not a big fan of roses, but that was not the issue here, nor was it what bothered me. To me, Porpora is floral, fruity, and spicy. However, this combination poses a problem for me, as it makes the entire fragrance feel inconsistent. Porpora definitely has rose as the main note, but unfortunately, the raspberry with its fruitiness pulls everything in a terribly unbalanced direction. On top of that, there is the sweetness of cinnamon, which clashes horribly with the clove and patchouli. The slight notes of incense and myrrh round everything off inappropriately. Normally, I am a fan of Tiziana Terenzi, but this fragrance is clearly a failure for me. The notes suffocate each other and clash, and they simply do not harmonize with one another. The longevity is really very good; I could smell the fragrance on me for over 12 hours. The sillage was perceptible for almost 8 hours at arm's length before Porpora quickly became close to the skin after 10 hours.

I am not sure I would call this floral-spicy, to me it is more of a chypre - a crisp, tart and wine-like rose-honey-patchouli chypre. I find it similar to Cardin Rose, but muskier, a little drier (more oakmoss), and even more elegant. Makes me think of an early autumn morning, with smells in the cool, fresh air of sweet-sour fruit lying on the wet ground. I almost loved it. The patchouli was balancing between just right and just too much, although it should be said that I normally don't like patchouli and am very sensitive about it. But what made me decide not to buy a full bottle, was the musk, which unfortunately got very, very soapy on me as the scent developed. Soapy musk is not my favourite either. Too bad, as it is a lovely and very elegant perfume and I would have loved to be able to wear it.

The house of Prada was founded in 1913 by Mario and Martino Prada in Milan and initially produced fine leather goods, bags, and travel accessories under the name "Fratelli Prada," which were sold in a shop in the elegant "Galleria Vittorio Emmanuele II." In 1978, Mario's granddaughter, Miuccia Prada, took over the company with her two siblings and gradually transformed it into a fashion house. Revolutionary were the first bags made from black parachute nylon, which are still produced today. At the end of the 1980s, the first Prada fragrance was launched by Orlane. A typical and widespread fragrance genre of that time was employed: floral chypre with fruity and woody-warm accords. The scent is comparable to Paloma Picasso's "Mon Parfum" or "L'Arte di Gucci," although the Prada fragrance comes across as a bit darker than the two mentioned. The fresh-green-floral top note quickly gives way to a sultry, slightly oily rose-jasmine heart, which gains real punch from the honey. The woody-earthy base is dominated by moss, patchouli, and benzoin, giving the fragrance an almost oriental depth. In Germany, it was very rarely available at the time, but you can occasionally still find it online at moderate prices. In Italy, I recently saw the complete range in a small private perfumery, from extrait to various EDT sizes to the bath line, everything was still available :-) It's a shame that this wonderful fragrance was discontinued; it absolutely deserves a revival without reformulation. The packaging and bottle impress with their simplicity and still fit into the Prada cosmos today. Although produced as a women's fragrance, it is also quite suitable for men, more for the evening and on cooler days.

Prada has really outdone themselves with this beautiful, ambery oriental. It has me wondering why mainstream brands always seem to knock me dead with their exclusive, hard-to-find releases. Prada Opoponax No.8 is quite sensual, warm and elegant. It opens with rich, resinous and slightly buttery opoponax and galbanum, with a subtle, citrusy hint of bergamot, which surprisingly works. As it dries on the skin, Opoponax No.8 turns quite powdery, yet it maintains it's delicious spiciness, and golden syrup type accord throughout. The musk also kicks in quite early in the composition, adding an animalistic touch, that smells oddly clean at the same time. The resins in this fragrance can be quite sweet, making it very feminine and sexy. In order to believe that this fragrance could work equally as well on men, I think I'd have to try it and see. The way I view Prada Opoponax No.8 is with great admiration. I think it's a total man magnet. Unfortunately the only downer is the lasting strength which is surprisingly weak. I have worn this fragrance twice in the last few days, one time on a rainy day where it struggled to last a few hours, and again today, where I perhaps only enjoyed it for the duration of the morning but desperately needed a touch up come the afternoon. Regardless of poor longevity, tossing it aside, Prada Opoponax No.8 is one of the most sensual and alluring orientals I've stumbled across in quite some time. If I ever have enough luck to find a bottle of this in my travels, I will be quick to purchase.

This fragrance is a true revelation for those who enjoy resinous, balsamic, and spicy scents, and who do not shy away from a slight earthy note. But beware, the fragrance also develops a quite strong, earthy note that almost resembles a smoky patchouli; those who do not like such scents should better steer clear of it. Opopanax in concentrated form is quite special and lasts incredibly long. Here, paired with a profound amber, the fragrance is more suited for cooler days and is certainly not an everyday scent. It can be worn by both ladies and gentlemen alike. Like the other fragrances from Prada's Exclusive Series, it is available only in a 30 ml splash bottle as an extrait.

This odor was a gift from my girlfriend. Casanova opens with a flowery powdered scent. There is also a slightly sharp smell of fig leaves at the opening. But this sharpness does not bother you, because it is powdery touch dominates the smell. From opening to finish, the orchid note dominates this smell. This powdered orchid smell is accompanied by the smell of jasmine. The smell of Bergamot is very shy. After a certain time, a woody and slightly aromatic smell is added to this powdered flower smell. With this effect, casanova becomes more of an unisex smell than a feminine one. Hours later casanova turns into a woody, powdered, soft, slightly elegant and floral fragrance. İts character is now clear. It's a beautiful unisex. It is a genderless playboy. Tricks and achieves the person it wants with soft touches. The most obvious aspect of Casanova is that it is flowery (especially orchid), a little woody and powdery. Especially suitable for autumn and winter seasons. It lasts more than 15 hours on my skin.

This is one of the best fragrances i have tried it is spicy, woody, herbalm, (i dont think its as flowar as parfumo says) but so well mixed and blended it smells awesome it reminds me of dior homme sport but withouth the citrus. great for all year around elegant and easy to wear withouth beeing too boring. Defintly one of my favorite frgarances i have tried. Longevity is good, sillage is average. Elegant and serious while beeing easy to wear. Perfecten, even price is ok for 100ml.

Well, he is already uuuuur old, the good man! An Italian writer from Venice. Imprisoned for godlessness, escaped, and became famous. Not least because of his extravagant memoirs filled with frivolous, erotic adventures. But why did Paolo Terenzi give this fragrance the name Casanova? Admittedly, it is a very pleasant, cuddly, and spicy scent. Not dusty spicy or too masculine. But a "woman magnet" for sure. I mentioned in my statement that it bears a strong resemblance to "Geste." And Geste, on the other hand, is more of a "man magnet." So it’s no wonder that Casanova is unisex. The top note is the "Geste" part. Orchid and powder convey something noble, soft, and attractive. A feeling of security with a smile on your face when you snuggle up to someone. But how do orchids smell? In the hardware store or at the gardener around the corner, they always look so elegant, but they don't smell. However, there are orchids that do smell. Many different varieties. Here it could be the Phalaenopsis Lea Maria Salazar 'Joy.' It has a Nivea-like, slightly sweet scent. And this gives me that feel-good sensation with Casanova, without coming off as too "clean." It becomes slightly sweetened by cardamom, vanilla, and amber. I can't filter out tonka bean. After a short while, the beautiful, cuddly scent remains, but it becomes spicier. The woods like cedarwood, guaiac wood, and also oak moss now envelop the top notes. Myrrh is said to smell resinous, but I don't perceive that here at all. Myrrh could have not been listed. It wouldn’t have been noticed. And then a splash of freshness from vetiver. Woody, herbal, and exotic - not everyone's or every woman's cup of tea. But it fits perfectly. I can't say it any other way. But it is truly a magnet for attraction between women and men. And who doesn't like that feel-good sensation, the cuddle factor... now and then?

It's a pity that there are no comments on this fragrance yet. I have it on my left arm, Ecstasy by Terenzi on my right, and I feel that I am not quite doing justice to this wonderful scent with this somewhat divided attention. But if I don't test two fragrances at a time, it will take forever before I can send the sample package on. With a fragrance named Casanova, and one that includes oak moss, I would have expected something more classic and distinctly masculine. However, as it turns out, it fits quite well into the "aphrodisiac" series. Casanova starts fresh and lively, with citrus notes immediately accompanied by a distinct floral note and something pleasantly powdery-creamy. It smells seductive, but rather like a slightly feminine, refined grooming scent. After a short time, the floral notes become less intense, and it becomes difficult to describe Casanova in terms of fragrance notes. It now appears primarily clean, creamy, yet still sexy. It is quite close to the skin, but that works. Casanova could perhaps be compared to L'Eau d'Hiver or Helmut Lang - Eau de Cologne. A fragrance whose sexiness lies in restraint and tenderness. Your own skin smells incredibly well-groomed and takes on some of that aesthetic that freshly showered skin has, which is particularly attractive. Now and then, a glue-like, synthetic note joins in; this may be an interesting contrast, smelling intentional and not cheap - but I find it somewhat disturbing in combination with the floral notes. Beautiful for a man and especially for women.

Ah yes, Casanova. A term that many a man may have dreamed of being. Well, with this fragrance, it might just be possible. But only maybe. Most likely, the ladies will prefer to wear the scent themselves rather than smelling it on someone else, as it has a beautifully feminine quality and with its delicate, floral-powdery notes, it will certainly appeal to every woman. The scent: The fragrance opens fresh-floral with bergamot, a slightly bitter orchid, and sweetish jasmine. They convey a spring-like impression, complemented by powdery notes that make the scent immediately soft and gentle. The beginning feels more like a women's fragrance. In the heart note, there is a hint of pink pepper; perhaps the bitter notes from the beginning came more from the pepper, I'm not sure. The scent develops slight leathery notes with a touch of vanilla, all enveloped in a light cloud of myrrh. Only in the base does the fragrance become somewhat woody. Additional slightly sweet notes like amber and especially musk come into play. However, most of the fragrance notes are really so light that they are hard to distinguish from one another and simply create a large whole, something pleasantly fragrant, with a feeling of cleanliness. The longevity and sillage: I wonder how the ratings come about here, as the scent is light and not particularly strong; after less than six hours, there is nothing left of this fragrance on the skin. Well, that was the case for me. The sillage is, as mentioned, not particularly strong, so it is at best below average and soon becomes more of a skin scent. The bottle: The bottle is cylindrical, gilded, and looks elegant. The cap is also cylindrical and black. On the bottle, there is a narrow label with the name of the fragrance written in golden letters. Everything is very well done. From the very first note, this fragrance will mainly appeal to the ladies. Beautiful floral and soft powdery notes smell delicate and fragrant, conveying a pleasant feeling as well as a sense of cleanliness (but not in the form of fresh laundry). Although the fragrance is intended for spring and summer, due to its low sillage, it will be more of a feel-good scent for oneself rather than something to wear when going out, for example. This makes it practically usable at home in any season. The fragrance is unisex, but as mentioned, it leans a bit more towards women's fragrances. I am sure it will be well-liked by many, so I would definitely recommend giving it a try. The question is whether the high price is worth it, as there are many similarly scented fragrances available that cost significantly less.

This is how the young lady smells, who is stylish yet timelessly dressed and strolling through the streets of Paris. That was indeed my first impression after the drydown. The opening truly disappointed me at first. A very alcoholic (almost nail polish remover flair) and biting scent shot straight to my head and caused a brief headache. I was all the more surprised when this harsh fragrance quickly faded and the scent became really soft. Lightly fruity, powdery, green, and at the same time floral in the most exquisite form. If I were to smell this fragrance on a lady, I would have regretted not asking what scent it was! Overall, the fragrance simply gives me a certain warmth. This scent is just very pleasant to have around. The fragrance is by no means a beast in projection, as it is really very soft, yet this is exactly what makes the scent so special, as it arrives very quietly, almost stealthily, and when the fragrance glides into the nose, the present moment is forgotten effortlessly.

In sampling both Apple Brandy and Angels Share at the same time with my wife, the warm, cinnamon, boozy, and sweet notes in Angels Share kept tricking us into thinking we were smelling Apple Brandy. It just seemed to fit better with the name. Regardless, this is the better option of the two. It really has a high-end, boozy, apple pie scent. On my skin, this projects and lasts a long time. It's very loud even with 1 or 2 sprays, lasting all day.

What can't be said about this mesmerizing perfume? A perfume that is a masterpiece. Pure unisex. A perfect perfume for dates. Every time I wear it on dates, the woman asks me what perfume I wore. In my opinion, this perfume is the best from Kilian and of course even better than the new version Angels' Share Paradis which is too sweet in my opinion. It's difficult, if not impossible, to beat the original version. Plus, it's an amazing presentation of a glass of whiskey. It's definitely worth it. 9.5/10.

Originally written over a one year ago. First I decided not to buy this because of the hype and I noticed that so many have this, but it’s just so delicious. I would like to have rare things but like with many perfumes I have to admit that it’s not so bad if there is few thousands of other happy owners. This juice is like a Christmas time in the bottle. It’s delicious fresh cinnamon vanilla apple pie and a cognac in the nice crystal class on the table and you walk in the room and get those notes mixed together. This is an amber vanilla fragrance, I would say boozy gourmand and I like the level of sweetness here even if overly sweet scents are not my favourite category. Vanilla is not popping out here, it's so smoothly blended. Cognac note and cinnamon keeps the sweetness from vanilla, Praline and Tonka bean in the balance while cinnamon gives warm spicy effect to this. The base is utterly soft, velvety sandalwood with a hint of vanilla with some nuttiness. I don’t get any powdery vibes here. Despite how I describe the perfume this is elegant and interesting blend and I think this is really wearable during the autumn and the winter time, day and night. This is really addictive, intoxicating scent and I just want to smell it more and more. I'm very sensitive to synthetic aromas but I don't find any here. Even if there was, they are made very well. The bottle is really beautiful as well giving a crystal glass feeling when you hold this. As this is popular there is clones and dupes a lot of this. I haven’t tested not even one and actually I’m not interested to test any - I always prefer the original and authentic of everything. There is many similar perfumes in the world for sure (I don’t mean this one, like overall) but this one is really copied. If you feel that "Angels' Share | Kilian" is too potent, thick and sticky sweet I recommend you to sample 31 Tonka Bodykon which is like a sophisticated feminine version of this one. All the notes are like diluted there, it's very sensual and cocooning. It's not similar or same at all but it has many similar notes and you will get the similar feeling. I'm aware as well that many perfume connoisseurs don’t respect Kilian as a perfume house but I have found there anyway unique and adorable scents and blends of notes which I haven’t found anywhere else. This scent is totally unisex. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

Angels share gets its name from the evaporation of alcohol in the cognac barrel. (And that’s as much as I know) Initial spray: Absolutely. Fantastic. It’s beautiful, it has a very intriguing, fruity, apple rum scent. It behaves very calm while also looking at you in calamity, sharpening a blade and getting ready to slice your nostril hairs. 2-3 hours in: It’s not exactly what I would wear to anyplace. It’s a fresher scent, while having very sweet, almost sharp skin projection. It reminds me of extremely sharp sugar crystals, that have formed around the rim of a whiskey glass, with an apple slice in the middle of the glass. It’s like taking a sip of apple whiskey, and getting cut from the sugar crystals on the rim. It reminds me of a very rich soccer mom, that might’ve taken a few swigs from the grey goose prior to her sons soccer game. 6-8 hours in: It has died down, while also staring at you with the intent to kill. Still very sharp, almost like nails on a chalkboard. I can hear the crunching of the sugar crystals when I smell it. It’s not a soft ice-cream, but more of a harsh rock candy. I wish the initial rum scent would stay longer, I almost feel like the rum scent makes it calm down a little. The sandalwood becomes extremely harsh, and I almost want to wash it off immediately, but for some reason I just keep smelling it. To the packaging: I’m a stickler for packaging. If I’m paying big money for a fragrance, then I expect high quality packaging. I think Estée Lauder murdered the packaging on purpose, as their goal was to maximize the profits of the fragrance. I wish the plastic top was glass. I wish the sprayer was slightly more sturdy. It wobbles around when you spray it, and I really hate that. Again, I’m a major stickler for packaging so take my words with a grain of salt on that front. Final thoughts: It’s really good for the first 2 hours of an event. It quickly dies down after that to something I kind’ve hate and love at the same time. I wish it wasn’t so sharp, and I want more smoothness to it. It leaves so much on the table, and this could be an absolute KILLER fragrance. I just want the ice-cream smoothness, instead I get this sharp crystallized apple sandalwood on the dry down.

Angels share is the holy grail of apple pie scents. When you mention a perfume that smells like apple pie you already know someone will ask if its similar to angels share. Angels share is a boozy, spicy apple scent which is one of the most perfect scents for winter and colder weather. It lasts a good 8-10 hours on my skin which is really good.

I love apple pie. Warm apple pie with a sprinkle of cinnamon, lots of sugar, some rum raisins. Who’d have thought a perfumer put that all in a blender and made a perfume out of it? Needless to say as an applepie lover I absolutely love this fragrance as well. It’s just that it’s just so… I don’t know, specifically for the holidays.

This is one of the few fragrances that have left me speechless in my olfactory journey. I perceive many things, liqueurs, praline… Angel's Share is not as sweet as some mentioned below, from the previous descriptions I imagined it was going to be a toffee type scent but nothing to see. Real unisex for sure, a solid 10 out of 10.
When I first sprayed it, there was this boozy warm apple pie that lasted about a second. Afterwards, the cognac immediately took the spotlight and came on strong, really strong.

After buying and returning a fake from eBay, I decided to bite the bullet and a buy 1.7 oz bottle of Angel’s Share directly from Bloomingdales. This is a gourmand like no other! As the notes listed on various perfume websites are getting increasingly unreliable, I am relying on my nose and the perfumer’s notes to discuss the accords.

It's a pity that no one has written much about this fragrance yet... But well, I'll do it then;) I must admit I wouldn't have discovered this special scent without dear Flickchen. Thanks again for that in case you read this:) Anyway... A year ago, I didn't even know that lipstick scents existed; well, how should one come to that, I wonder now. You know there are floral, gourmand, fruity, and woody scents, but lipstick or rather cosmetic scents were new to me personally! Now I know why I love perfume:D Because it never gets boring!:D My grandfather also bought me Prada Rossetto as he wanted to test this scent just like I did. Yes, I know one should rather test such a fragrance beforehand instead of making a blind purchase... To be honest, I don't know any perfumery that sells or carries this scent, which I think is a pity because there would definitely be many people interested in such an extraordinary fragrance... Or??? My package arrived after a good 3 weeks... At least the wait was worth it. I do have one question for the lovely ladies;)) Do you ever smell your lipstick or powder while doing your makeup??? I always love to smell my lipsticks or glosses:D I find it so interesting that every cosmetic brand has its own lipstick scent/smell ... Especially the Lancome/Yves Rocher lipsticks I find smell perfumed but still smell amazing:D Now you probably want to know how Prada Rossetto smells?:) I can already tell you, anyone who loves lipsticks but also adores them should definitely get this scent;)) When opening the package, I could already smell the scent of the lipstick... At first, I was afraid that the bottle had been damaged or something had leaked, but luckily that wasn't the case... I was lucky. My grandfather was also curious, so I dabbed a bit on my wrist (The bottle doesn't have a spray head; you have to dab it or transfer it to another bottle if you want to spray it.) What I must say is that it is not an extremely strong scent (Also here depending on the number of dabs) At first, you can clearly smell the raspberry, not sour or synthetic, more like a light mix of sweet but also fresh. The raspberry note fades after 10 minutes, which I don't find too bad; then comes the hoped-for note: The lipstick note;)) It smells very much like an expensive, vintage but also somehow juicy and creamy lipstick. I assume that the creamy note comes from the rose note, as it gives everything a slight perfumed but also luxurious touch;) I think I can occasionally smell a light iris note that gives it this powdery cosmetic/makeup note. Prada Rossetto is subtly sweet, but the sweet note makes the scent development harmoniously and elegantly fade out. My grandfather thinks this scent would perfectly match a rosewood lipstick shade but also a white oversized shirt, paired with blue jeans and sneakers. He also thinks this scent is more suitable for special occasions or for a date.
