Personally, I find this scent very romantic:) For everyday wear, however, he thinks this scent is way too special, and I agree with him. Sillage is okay, on clothing 5 hours, on skin rather 3 hours.

I love vanilla, and this has a strong vanilla note. However, it also has a putrid stale-bubblegum note on me that comes pretty close to making me retch. I hoped it would pass but, after an hour of trying to breathe through my mouth (how sophisticated I looked!), I gave up, scrubbed my arm, and sprayed some Sula Vanilla Blossom on top of it to cancel out the residual smell. I try to give perfumes at least 2 tries, but this was one of my once-and-out ones. (072209)

By Kilian LOVE is a ridiculously sweet perfume. Had I tested this one blind, I'm sure that I would have guessed that it was launched by the house of Britney Spears. But no, it's a hoity-toity niche perfume which costs ten times the price of any celebrity scent. The aesthetic of this composition is reminiscent of the house of Laurence Dumont, specifically the Senteurs Gourmandes collection (which, by the way, also cost a small fraction of this). Very, very sweet. Did I mention that this is sweet? Spun sugar flavored with vanilla is really the take away to my nose. I cannot really recommend this perfume because, although it does smell natural, from start to finish, it seems too much like a dessert which could very well induce a diabetic coma. I simply cannot think of any good reason for buying LOVE given the panoply of similar fragrances, often associated with celebrities' names, available today. For those who crave this level of sweetness in a natural-smelling perfume, I highly recommend that you investigate the house of Laurence Dumont.

When the cold weather rolls in, I have an irresistible urge to wear sweet and cozy scents. Love by Kilian is super sweet and could be rightfully called a sugar bomb filled with marshmallows, vanilla and all things sweet. It is fluffy, delicious, and a bit over the top. It reminds me of an enormous, over-decorated wedding cake with creamy frosting and cute cherubs. There are flowers in this frosted, sugared bouquet but they are so much covered in sweetness that I barely can smell them. However, what I really like about this perfume is how smooth, creamy, and natural smelling it is. I own many overly sweet perfumes including tons of celebrity ones. The main difference between those one and Love by Kilian is the quality. I find that synthetic loudness of many celebrity scents are getting on my nerves, so though I do love perfumes with super sweet personality, I cannot bear to wear most of them. Love by Kilian is a different story. I love wearing it and it lasts for at least 10 hours on me. Is it worth a hefty price tag? Still not sure. I would have liked to see more complexity in the dry down phase of this scent, something that would make it more dimensional and exciting instead of just a straightforward marshmallow vanilla. But it is still a lovely fragrance to wear and my rating is based on its comparison to other fragrances in this category. Overall score is 7.5/10.

How could you be shy while wearing this fragrance? One does not have to be a dog to track you down along the threads of this scent... Neroli as top note? That would be a so-called „shy, tentative kiss given by fresh lips” – as it is written on the page of one seller. Pure and poor theory. Do not bother with neroli, do not waste even a slight thought for it. It can not do anything against the flood of jasmine and vanille, so freshness is absolutely not present here. The perfume is strong, stable, forms a wall around you, a wall of self-esteem and a bit violent kind of flirt. LOVE is indiscreet and tactless. Completely feminine. Upon the waves of sweetness there is a weird, floating odor, most probably iris and vanille made an alliance against sobriety. The weirdness is the same kind as in VANILLE ABSOLUMENT, but executed in much higher quality. The base: less jasmine, stable vanille. Musk is trying to push the fragrance towards demureness. Sorry, dear Musk, maybe another time, LOVE and love does not need too much rationality. - Age: does not matter, just be enough brave to wear. - Gender: woman! - Season: summer. Such a strong and sweet perfume together with those who contain oud, are meant for heat. - Warning: the liquid has an intensive red color, that can leave stains on your clothes, so portion it only on skin.

This perfume lasts forever, it is not shy to stick around for however long it likes. I tried it once because my mother was very eager to share in my perfume interest, it ended up lasting more than 12 hours on my skin and was still very fragrant when I went to sleep. Granted, I was just chatting with my brother online. Still, how long does a fragrance need to last? I recommend this for anyone who loves really sweet marshmallows and hates when a scent doesn’t last. I personally don’t like it, but I respect the longevity. I can understand why people like it, but I leave it to the ones who adore this to show it proper love. I will turn to more refreshing white florals and gourmands.

I've been pining for a bottle of Love Don't Be Shy for ages, and this year I finally got one for my birthday from my husband. Can't imagine a better gift. Smelling it is like laying in a sea of orange blossoms and slowly sinking into a thick creamy caramel.

...because I hate it. I hate hate hate it. One spray is so strong that it gives me a headache. I might as well have broken into a Krispy Kreme and bathed myself in their doughnut glaze. In warmer weather, it's unbearable.

Undoubtedly the symbol of femininity and sublime happiness, with an aroma that instantly brings a smile on your face, Love by Kilian is an opulent and sophisticated fragrance, a lush floral created around the orange blossom, one of the most courted ingredients in modern perfumery. .

this is wayyyy more floral than people let on. Yes it is definitely sweet, a marshmallow fluffy type of sweetness for sure but all that is enveloped in extremely heady florals with the jasmine and honeysuckle being the most prominent.

So, let the journey of trying my first Kilian perfume begin. Not only that, but I have twenty plus samples to go through! I honestly just pulled a fragrance out and got the one I have heard most about. Love Don't be Shy...

The best fruity-floral fragrance I have. It could be argued it leans feminine, but on my skin it becomes delightful and biteable. The mix of peach and blackcurrant, enhanced by flowers and rounded up by some punch of vetiver and patchouli, along with the creaminess of the sandalwood make this a masterpiece. Performance is fantastic, and so it's the projection and the overall presentation. It's not spoken about enough. I don't feel the ambergris, tho, so maybe it's there just as you put salt in a recipe.

I can firmly say that this is my discovery of the summer. A tremendously rich perfume that has given me many compliments. It is a perfume that comes out with a delicious pungent grapefruit that in a few minutes will be calmed by a delicious peach and black currant. Amber, flowers and a background of sandalwood and vetiver make it a complex perfume, super easy and really delicious. The drying is a true delight and I would say that I cannot not like this. Brutal projection for the first 3 hours and then it is perceived at less than a meter for another 5. A 10/10 perfume for Paolo and Tiziana on this occasion.

Tuttle starts with a bright and zesty citrus note that reminds me of the ginger note in Vibrato. The grapefruit brings a lot of life to the fragrance. In the middle, it becomes a bit softer thanks to the peach and takes on an amber and woody character. The drydown is a good mix of everything that lasts a very long time. I receive a lot of compliments for this scent. It is also strong and refreshing at the same time for my nose! The fragrance gives me absolute Saint Tropez vibes. A long night filled with pure citrus freshness.

Lovely but with an attitude. Balmy fruity floral with a certain je ne sais quoi! I think it's the red pepper and the tolu balm that elevate this from the million fruity florals out there and give it a perfect ooomph. It feels exotic but not Hawaiian white-florals-and-coconut style tropical. The flowers feel orange in colour, the fruit feels Mediterranean and the whole attitude resembles Southern Spain. A beautiful day basking under the sun, visiting the gardens of old castles, sipping fruit cocktails and at night watching a raven-haired woman dance flamenco in a red dress, accompanied by Gypsy guitars. I got a bit carried away, but this is truly a scent that makes your mind wander! Perfect for day or night, never too heavy (ok don't use it during a heatwave), outstanding longevity and silage. An all-around winner!

I can clearly smell jasmine here. So where are you hiding? Neroli is also noticeable, but it's not summer neroli. More like spring/autumn. Overall, you are very floral, dear lady. Orange blossom is not exactly subtle... Has nothing to do with La Femme. Somehow you also remind me of lipstick, women's perfume, large handbags. I don't feel addressed by this fragrance, even though it is well made, but I just wished for more soapy freshness. Too floral for me, reminds me a bit of Jasmine Rouge by TF mixed with No5 by Chanel and a big dose of orange blossom. I’ll stick with La Femme. But definitely not a bad choice for the evening!

Atlantide is a very expressive fragrance for summer that certainly won't appeal to everyone. It embodies an exclusive beach club by the sandy shore. With a cocktail in hand, gazing at the sunset on the horizon while enjoying the cool sea breeze. In other words, it's a more exclusive summer vacation in a bottle. Clean, floral, and elegant. However, I have already experienced that due to its very pronounced tuberose, it can be somewhat overwhelming in strong heat. Therefore, in my opinion, it is only suitable for the cooler evenings. Conclusion: An exclusive summer fragrance with impressive character, but one that can easily be done without.

Orza and Telea both appealed to me greatly. Each had its own uniqueness and ranks among the best fruity fragrances for me. Unfortunately, this collection is far too expensive. However, after the two fragrances mentioned above, I wanted to test them all. I was quite biased due to the fragrance pyramid. Tuberose is not my favorite note, and here it is impossible to overlook it. I can say upfront that Atlantide is far too dominated by this tuberose for my taste. It is very heavy in the fragrance, somewhat numbing to the other notes, and overall not very well balanced. The listed top notes come through quite well in the first few minutes and are recognizable, presenting themselves as a fresh-creamy note with a bright and soft rose. Beautiful in itself, but everything is overshadowed by the tuberose. The passion fruit remains somewhat detectable for a bit longer, but really only subtly behind the tuberose. It's like a squeezed passion fruit, with a few drops of it trickling into a huge field of tuberose. In between, I can smell a few red berries and some orange blossom, but these too are overshadowed by the tuberose. At times, I also catch a whiff of a kind of floral-green note. I don't know where it comes from, but it comes through briefly. Somehow the fragrance also has a youthful quality; these loud, bright, and floral notes remind me of that. On the other hand, this creamy-floral aspect reminds me of a woman in a white dress, which seems quite grown-up. After several hours in the drydown, a familiar Terenzi base of amber, musk, and benzoin emerges. Quite nice, they know how to do this, but it appears a bit too late here. The performance, however, is on par with the other fragrances in the line; Atlantide lasts all day. The sillage is noticeable for 5 hours. The white-gold bottle matches the fragrance very well, but I cannot understand the naming. I share the same opinion as the Ischgelroi before me in his review. I was expecting a strong aquatic, salty, or algae-rich scent here. The overall presentation feels a bit excessive to me. Unpacking it is a one-time fun experience as you struggle through this pompous packaging, but afterwards, this huge block just sits around. I find the design of the bottle quite beautiful; it’s something you haven't seen before. Visually and color-wise, the bottle also fits ideally with the content. But I find the quality of the bottle to be good, yes, but nothing more. The spray head, like with the other Terenzi fragrances, is not very nice; they could really improve that. Very little comes out with each spray. The cap does not sit 100% securely on the bottle, so you cannot lift it by the cap. Overall, Atlantide is too bright, loud, and floral-fruity-creamy for me. Initially, it was accompanied by a pleasant freshness, which was only recognizable for a few minutes, very unfortunate. Unfortunately, I can't do much with the tuberose. However, for those who like tuberose and do not perceive it as so overwhelming here, they might find a very beautiful floral fragrance in Atlantide.

I received Atlantide as a sample today. The price and the entire design made me so curious about the scent that I absolutely wanted to test it. A retail price of €650 is certainly a statement. Accordingly, Atlantide must really smell very luxurious. Atlantide opens with an explosion of tuberose followed by the typical Tiziana Terenzi passion fruit. These are the two main players of Atlantide. After a little over an hour, a few berries make their way through the passion fruit and tuberose, pulling Atlantide towards the fruity side. From all the other floral notes, I can only identify an orange blossom. The base naturally contains a hefty dose of musk and a bit of amber, with these notes primarily used to fix the more volatile notes. Now we come to the question that probably interests all readers the most: is Atlantide worth the price? I can clearly say no; even though the entire design is insane and Tiziana Terenzi was able to fully unleash their creativity here, the content is definitely very good but not worth €650, at most €300. Here, you are certainly paying over 50% just for the design and exclusivity. Of course, in the end, everyone has to decide for themselves whether they are willing to do this. Personally, I am not, but for a price under €350, I would actually consider a purchase. Honestly, I don't understand the name Atlantide at all. The Atlantic is rather wild, stormy, and has a typical smell of the sea. However, Atlantide smells more like a trip to the Caribbean or a vacation on a tropical beach. I find Atlantide only slightly similar to Tom Ford's Soleil Blanc. Atlantide is definitely an independent and very good fragrance. The longevity is over 10 hours. The top note practically clings to the skin. The sillage is also very strong for 5-6 hours, after which it begins to fade and become more intimate.

A spectacular Gourmand perfume. The combination of coffee with rum is perfect. Gives a luxurious and caressing feeling. I recommend wearing this perfume in the evening and cold nights. What is certain is that this perfume will attract the attention of your dates ;) In terms of performance, the longevity of this perfume is average and the sillage is not exciting either and it stays mostly close to the skin. 8/10.

A lot of times when I have come across a gourmand, I find myself thinking it’s too sweet, or too cloying or generally just too much. But when I first tried Black Phantom, I knew I had to get a full bottle, no matter the cost. This is how a gourmand should be in my opinion. Filled with dark chocolate, rum, caramel, coffee and sugar cane… This stuff is mouthwatering. Black Phantom takes a dark and mysterious, yet incredibly addictive take on a gourmand fragrance. People get curious whenever I wear this, as if they haven’t smelled something like this before. That’s what I really enjoy about Black Phantom. Even though it’s a fantastic gourmand, it still manages to stand out from the rest. It’s still the best gourmand I have ever laid my nose on hands down. I could not ask for more. It’s really yummy, unique, addictive and very luxurious. It also gives off a vibe of some sort of chocolaty/caramel deliciousness, served at a restaurant that’s really expensive. I found very few people who dislike this fragrance. If you like gourmands in general, this is almost a blind buy, and I’m the type of guy that HATES blind buys! Says a lot really. If you like your gourmand not too sweet, but still addictive and refined, this is a must try. I only go for 2 sprays, 3 max on this one… Longevity is amazing (8-10 hours) and it projects really well. Sillage is mesmerizing and you will evoke a great curiosity around you, from the lucky ones, who get the pleasure to catch sudden whiffs of you. I’m gonna end all this by letting you in on a secret… And tell you how much I love this perfume. It may sound really corny… But the very first time I got a full bottle of this, I had a sudden urge to rip off the atomizer, and drink all the damn liquid. Yes, it’s that delicious! What an absolute wonderful release from Kilian, they really set new standards for gourmands with this one.

Disclaimer: this is my opinion, based on my personal experience, and on my maybe broken sense of smell, and you may not agree with it. So: If you want coffee - try Coffee Addict or Little Song. If you want chocolate - try Wicked Good. If you want rum - try Side Effect or Bvlgari Man In Black. You cannot find much of these notes in a recently produced Black Phantoms. (even though chocolate is not even a note in the composition) Maybe your older batches / pre-reformulation bottles are juggernaughts, but nowadays, you can only get a bottle that gives you a faint soft smell in the dry-down, reminiscent of sweet sandalwood, maybe. I've tried several bottles, in 3 diff. shops + my own bottle. It's not masculine, not even a fragrance, just a soft, pleasant smell of something. I also think that Mr. Kilian Hennessy never smelled the sweet, full-bodied dark rums of Cuba and surrounding islands, only maybe French or other sour, unpleasant, tangy rums. At least, his cognacs are much sweeter than his rums. Which is a shame. This could have been a top top scent. And the price is like 5x more than it is worth in my book.

This review is based on a 7.5ml vial from a discovery set for The Woody Cellars collection. This is more than a discovery set as 7.5 ml is a lot of perfume. As this translates 15-20 uses, this should last for a while. This is a creation of Sidonie Lancesseur, who has designed many of Kilian’s flagship perfumes. The full name of this perfume is Black Phantom - Memento Mori. Memento Mori translates roughly into ‘Remember you will die”. The whole things smells of kitschy marketing. Is the perfumer suggesting that that the bitter almond (cyanide) reminds us of death and murder? Anyway, in case you missed the connection to death, the full bottle is also available in a lockable coffret with a black skull attached to it. Not surprisingly, Black Phantom does not evoke death to me. Can any perfume evoke something as profound as death, unless you are an angst-ridden teenager? The opening notes are coffee and cyanide (essentially the bitter almond accord), but embellished with a set of lovely ancillary notes. I can smell vetiver, but the other listed notes - cane sugar and sandalwood - are lost in the pungent backdrop. There is also a hint of some sort of alcohol, which the perfumer lists as Caribbean rum. It could be, but I would have also believed cognac or absinthe. The combination of this mysterious spirit, coffee, vetiver and cyanide makes this perfume appear medicinal, the exact opposite of death. These notes are the heart notes and they eventually turn into the base notes. I don’t find a clear olfactory pyramid in Black Phantom. But I find that it becomes a bit more woody and sweet in the end, when the coffee and almond goes down. The performance on my skin is very good, though not monstrous. It lasted for 6-8 hours on my skin, and longer on my clothes. The sweet woody dry down survives for almost the entire day. The sillage is very good at a few feet as long as the heart notes are alive. I wonder what this bitter almond-coffee perfume tells the world when you walk by. If you are in search of a lovely sweet coffee cyanide perfume with liquor notes, this is a great option. The only time you contemplate mortality is when you see the listed price of $295 for 50 ml. If you think that you can’t take all that wealth with you when you die, please feel free to spent it on Black Phantom. I would buy it around $150 for 50 ml. Be very aware of the hype surrounding this perfume when you test it. If its name was Lattafa Coffee Oasis, would you still buy it?

Black Phantom, gotta love that name. It’s dark, eerie. Just like a coffee that’s poisoned. And that’s what it smells like. Coffee with some sweetness but also some high-pitched, medicinal, piercing woodsmell. It’s a wonderful thing really, I can imagine that wearing this while dressed up in a nice suit you’ll gain quite some respect. I myself don’t dress up very often so it’s not really my thing. I based this review on a discovery set, which had some great samples. This was certainly one of them.

Black Phantom is a blast of booze and nuttiness, immediately establishing itself as a dense and decadent gourmand. I feel almond is oddly underrepresented in the voting for the note breakdown. It dominates on my skin. Easily comprising 90% of the fragrance.

When I first tried it I wasn't such a big fan,it was unique for me but I wasn't really into it.After like 5 or 6 hours I smelled it again and again and again,I simply could not stop smelling it.After that I bought a 5 ml sample from one of my friends and wore it the same night.I got so many compliments that I knew I had to buy it.
Sampled this for the purpose of cosy nights in as I was getting bored of D&G The One EDP which became my dumb reach for the job.

All you can hear left and right about this one .. price price and.. did I say price ? But it's really worth it guys. Quality, class and elegance. Luxurious ? Of course. Sugary sweet but very unique. Not your typical sweet. Very refined and quite complex. Dark, mysterious, opulent. A 10/10 for me, real stunner. You want to turn heads ? Save some bucks for this one.

Thanks to my friend's kindness, I got to know a scent that I would probably (because of the scent notes) I would never try. So ... tried and? Maybe I'll start with the pluses: veeeeery durable and veeeeery designing. In my opinion, thats all. These are now cons, which for some will probably be pluses: the scent of cotton candy, caramel, fudge and almonds.

Leo opens with a bright, creamy-sweet kumquat/orange - after a few moments the brightness and sharpness of these notes is replaced with a soft, woody floral base. Quite feminine, it smells like a high-end hand lotion, slightly powdery with musk and tonka coming through. Performance is pretty good for this type of fragrance, usually they stick to skin. But the scent itself is a bit lacking in my opinion, too generic and tame.

l e o. he does not enter. he sneaks. like a lion, with a silky gaze, born from warm twilight. no roaring, just the whisper of mandarin peel from Sicily's golden glow, bergamot a hint of courage, and orange, dancing on the tongue like desire. kumquat kisses the air with nimble zest, a promise on the skin. playful, teasing, never grasping. he purrs into the depths. there, where magnolia blooms, Italian soft, a dream of ivory and sweet, blossoming longing. Bulgarian rose opens delicately, like lips before the kiss, that does not ask, only takes. jasmine sambac. India's breath of night, a drop of heat on bare soul. leo. he is no trace, he is an imprint. a tremor on the skin. a glance in your direction, and you go. not away, but in. there, where scent becomes desire, and desire loses itself in you.

After a long time, here’s a review of a Terenzi fragrance, as I recently purchased one after several months of abstinence from this brand: Leo from the wonderful Luna collection. I already own Cassiopea and Orion from this collection. Price-wise, the MSRP is quite expensive, but most can be found for 50% less. Regularly, these are a hefty €285, but as mentioned, most can be bought for around €140. It’s worth it if you appreciate the signature of Terenzi fragrances. With a score of 7.3, Leo is rated quite poorly for niche standards. The rating doesn’t sound too bad, but for niche standards, it’s a bit of a penalty. Many Terenzi fragrances are positioned in this range, so I would say: Make up your own mind. Many here don’t like this style or have a dislike for the brand. Personally, I find this brand very catchy, modern, and of good quality. For the modern casual style, I think this brand is top-notch. The bottles of this brand are great, especially due to the oversized cap. Only the sticker looks a bit cheap, which could have made this brand appear more beautiful. The cap with the constellation is quite impressive in the Luna collection. This Leo represents the zodiac sign Leo. Now to the most important part: The scent. Under inspiration, "Musk Therapy | Initio" is right at the forefront. Even though these two fragrances have some parallels, this one is not so close in DNA. The commonalities are clearly the creamy-light fluffy musk notes, the quark-like mandarin, and the clean flowers. In terms of style, it’s similar, but in terms of DNA, it slightly reminds me of "Decas | XerJoff". The Luna collection is overall white in color, and this color fits perfectly here. A clean and well-groomed scent that can be wonderfully worn in spring and summer. The start features a wonderful fruity-sweet-quarky mandarin paired with other citrus notes. The mandarin is very present in the opening and delights with this great quarky-creamy clean DNA. Some floral notes follow, but these floral elements never become too feminine or overpowering. It remains a clean-bright scent with this fluffy-bright musk and a hint of exoticism. There’s also a slight bubblegum vibe present, but never too overpowering or cheap. With this citrus freshness in the background, it’s a great DNA that never becomes too heavy or overwhelming. In the base, there’s some benzoin, which is nicely rounded and slightly balsamic. Along with some wood, tonka sweetness, and of course, well-groomed light musk that is present throughout the entire duration. For me, it’s an absolutely wonderful scent that, in my opinion, is suitable for all occasions due to its clean aura. Performance is quite good, especially for this type of fragrance. You get a fresh clean scent that lasts a minimum of 8 hours with initially really good sillage. It’s worth it if you want to perform fresh and clean in everyday life. Overall, a great scent for both ladies and gentlemen who enjoy this "white" well-groomed freshness. This slightly exotic DNA will surely appeal to most people, especially since such fragrances are rarely represented in the mainstream.

At the beginning, I must mention that I come from the countryside! And I mean real countryside. With everything that goes along with it! The cows are next door, and you not only know all the people by name but also the cows! Something like that. In any case, we don't have a perfumery here. Not even a drugstore! Therefore, visits to the perfumery are not only rare for me but also something really special! I received a 20% code for all brands at the perfumery P..... (I'm not sure if I can mention that here) by mail. They had VIP Days. My sister lives in Dortmund, and I casually suggested that I visit her with Mom. So, armed with my voucher and full of excitement, I headed to the perfumery. I started to tremble because I saw that there was now a huge corner with niche fragrances! Byredo, Terenzi, Xerjoff, Initio, so many new brands. I turned bright red and was actually overwhelmed right away. A really very, very friendly and knowledgeable saleswoman was by my side. She quickly noticed that I already knew quite a bit and was totally open and interested in scents! She took her time with me. After a while, we arrived at Terenzi. She said, "So! I think I can gauge you a bit! May I just spray something on you that will accompany you for the rest of the day?!" Of course, bring it on. I thought the woman was great. Honestly. I would have loved to have a coffee with her right away. She sprayed Leo by Terenzi on me! By the way, she mentioned that it was her favorite scent for going out! Inhale, pause for a moment. I got huge eyes! What is this?!! I had actually never smelled anything like it. I could sense citrus notes, but I wasn't sure. The lady said, "It's great, isn't it?! I knew you would like it!" She was right. I found it amazing! Extraordinary. Fairly speaking, I must say that the opening was intense. A bit biting and just strong. The typical Terenzi synthetics, you either love them or you hate them. Shortly after, the magic of this fragrance unfolded: Creamy, powdery citrus notes. Soooo beautifully blended. Polished, elegant, confident. Striking!! I was looking forward to testing it further throughout the day. By the way, I bought Animalique . Oh man, I was so happy about the purchase that I almost cried. But then this: Mom and my sister were waiting for me in a department store. Proudly, I walked over and presented my bag. Mom squinted her eyes, even needed a tissue. "My God!! What is that?!!? You didn't actually buy that, did you?!" And my sister started sneezing. Hatschi, Hatschi. "Wow Anna, that really doesn't work at all!! Did you really buy that?" - they smelled Leo in the air! I said that I bought another one. Both were very happy about that. At first, I found it amusing, but in the restaurant, Mom asked me to please sit a bit further away because she couldn't breathe because of the scent. She was unfortunately serious. Accordingly, the drive back home was quite tense! An hour and a half of complaining about my beloved Leo . A few days later, I got a decant. The scent wouldn't leave my mind! I sprayed it on again. Terenzi synthetics, authentic, soft citrus. Powder. Powdery musk, powder fluff. An adult cloud full of energy and confidence. I loved it. It drew me in! Mom doesn't need to know about this!

I was interested in this scent. There are some reasons: 1. to compare with Strawberries & Champagne 2. design Both of two body mists have similar notes but they're literally different! If Strawberries & Champagne smells like fragolino with wild strawberry and green notes for spring, Bubbles & Berries smells like strawberry lemonade. My biggest mistake is wearing the second one during hot summer days. It smells like rotten strawberries! But if you wear it during cold days, it will smell sooooooo gooooood

One of the few I was really disappointed with; First of all, I acknowledge the insane and incredibly cute design (which was my first reason of buying this) (don't judge me I'm just a girl with spending problems for cute things). I think this perfume is not as good to the point of being memorable. Like the girl under me said, this is literally so similar to Champagne Toast Fragrance Mist and so, nothing really unique and very dull. The perfume itself is supposed to be a "strawberry" and "champagne" mix but therefore gives a very poor strawberry note and more fizzy drink than fruity/drink . It's indeed bright however synthetic /screechy, yes it's discontinued, but Bath&BodyWorks did it better to be honest.

Intoxicated is my all time favorite scent from Kilian and im really shocked that i havent bought a full bottle! Intoxicated is a smooth almost soapy coffee scent iin the opening. In the drydown the cardamom and vanilla smoothens the scent out and takes it too a whole better level! longevity is really good for being kilian as i get 8-10 hours with it on my skin but it does get a little light after the 4th hour. Beautiful scent that everyone should try!

I get here the cardamon giving shape to Mocha, in the same vibe the ginger giving shape to Tobacco in Tobacco Vanille. They are not comparable scents, of course. It's instead how these darker (Mocha and Tobacco) notes play with fresher (Cardamon and Ginger). The first spray is mesmerizing. So delicious. Smells sophisticated, bright, fresh sweet. I don't get a lot of cinnamon here, which may indicate a good blending with something else (the Caramel?). I have a selection of fragrances I put on my Hall of Fame, and this one almost made its way to it if it wasn't for the linearity. After 4 hours, almost 5, the scent is more or less the same. The same cardamon, the same Mocha, only slightly subdued and with a tiny hint of powdery. The linearity of the fragrance makes it a bit tiring and monotonous. Not necessarily a problem, but it steals a lot of its good grades. Occasion: I would mostly pick it for a night out, evening, and gatherings leaning towards special occasions. Not your next office, day-to-day fragrance. But an excellent addition to the collection.

The opening is a freshly brewed and aromatic coffee. This note is perfectly complemented by cardamom, which adds a spicy touch. The fragrance remains fairly linear throughout, with a longevity of about 8+ hours and a very strong sillage during the first 2 hours. Unfortunately, the newer batches no longer have the same longevity as the 2019 one I own. Nevertheless, I recommend this fragrance to those who enjoy coffee notes in perfumery.

You really, REALLY have to love cardamom to love this fragrance. Sometimes I cook with cardamom, sometimes I brew with cardamom and what I've learned with that is that you have to be really careful with this powerful spice or it will ruin whatever you were working on. I've got the impression that the perfumer of Intoxicated didn't get the memo and threw in all cardamom they had. Which is a lot. Anyway. It may not look like it but I'm no cardamom hater. It's just way too strong for me and I really loathe it in this fragrance. Looking at the notes there should be a hint of coffee and some sweetness but I don't get that at all. Maybe my nose is just oversensitive for this spice but it gets a nope from me.

I have the Oil Perfumery version. I get coffee + aldehydes and citrus off the top (bergamot) which is such a fun mix of contrasting scents it confuses my nose in the best way. I can’t pick out the tobacco (some say smoke) or balsam fir for the mocha and the florals, but I assume they just all blend seamlessly. This has quite a soapy dry-down, so I don’t categorize it as a gourmand. Fresh for Spring, but cozy for winter. Great year-round to my sensibilities.

I have been introduced to Kilian by a friend who worked in a perfume shop in Switzerland, Basel. She said the scent would work great on my skin. I then tried it out! I enjoyed it a lot, its a very sultry, sweet scent. I do feel like the name is deserved. I wished it would stay longer on my skin. The performance is okay, but I definitely expected more for this price.

Spicy cardamom coffee that I just can´t stop sniffing. There´s a lot of aldehydic soapiness that I didn´t like at first but I´ve grown to love it. The dry down is where it really settles into the soapy cardamom. I´ve never smelled anything like this for sure. Worth a try if you like coffee and aren´t afraid of aldehydes. Not a safe blind buy.

By Kilians intoxicating curation is a scent of curiosity as well as nobility. TodayI give you guys my impression of what a 10/10 coffee fragrance has to offer with Kilian's "cellar" collection Intoxicated. Purely Sublime!!! This is a scent that needs to be savored and shared. Far from clinging in the kitchen or the obscure background conversations, this your cup!

Who knew wearing spiced coffee could be so sexy? “Intoxicated” is the right adjective to describe this fragrance, especially if you love gourmands as much as I do. Addict would have been a great title, but Dior got the jump on that one. Kilian executes yet another perfect gourmand without being dependent on vanilla.

It feels like Intoxicated belong to a bygone era of exceptional creativity from Killian, though such a period might be an illusion in our minds. For me, Intoxicated, Angels Share and Black Phantom are an unparalleled trinity of gourmand perfumes that carries this brand forward still. This review was written initially for a 7.

I decided I really wanted this for my birthday. The scent is really really natural, very nice. Puts me in mind of Bellodgia, though its not sweet at all. On me I get carnation, clove (its way tamped down), and an amazing buttery and slightly dirty iris. After a while it shifts and the clove and rose come into play. there is a slight powder to this, but its amazingly pleasant and does not ruin the composition at all. My partner says it smells distinct, like Lagerfeld Classic type powderiness. Everything smells so natural though, no one note is too overpowering. I'd be interested to know the type of musk used here because it smells great. Likely its synthetic but thankfully its not so harsh that it would tear my nose to pieces. Longevity is high, sillage is moderate to soft... it wears close to the skin after 4 hours but its totally still there. I don't find it to be too linear at all. It changes quite a bit through the drydown. This one changes much more on me than No4, which I like but is quite linear on me. From my understanding the exclusives were made to be worn with each other. I haven't tried that yet. I can see this being worn 3 months of the year, it may be a bit much for summer. Worth testing out if you can, especially for those who enjoy carnation. Pricewise, its a bit expensive but its also an extrait and a darn good one. Absolutely unisex.

Swoon. The initial blast of this is just unbelievably good. Back to Black is a heavenly spicy/smokey gourmand fragrance in the vein of Tom Ford's Tobacco Vanille and Serge Lutens Fumerie Turque, a genre I admit to loving. Of the three, Back to Black is most definitely my favorite. I also find Back to Black to be the most feminine of the group (although certainly still unisex). The top notes are particulary delicious. Although I don't see any flowers listed, I get a bit of a floral feel here (maybe the bergamot?) along with jammy fruits, honey and spices. It truly smells good enough to eat. Supporting the delectable top notes are the classic oriental perfume ingredients of amber and vanilla. Bitter almond provides a nice twist on this classic formula, adding a subtle powdery sweet note. Patchouli makes an appearance as well, and when combined with the fruits, adds an element reminiscent of modern fruity chypres such as Badgley Mishka. Back to Black pretty much takes the best aspects from several perfumes I admire and rolls them into one fabulous, well-blended fragrance. Since this is frequently compared to Tobacco Vanille, and having a decant of Tobacco Vanille, I thought it might be interesting to compare them side by side. At first spray, I find Back to Black to be more honeyed fruit and amber and Tobacco Vanille more of a boozy vanilla. Both have that smokey element, but Tobacco Vanille is more in your face about it. Tobacco Vanille is also more blatantly spicy and stronger in general. Back to Black just feels softer and more nuanced. I also find Back to Black to have more layers of development (as I've descibed above) than Tobacco Vanille. Tobacco Vanille is pretty much just what it says it is, a smoky vanilla, and the aroma of Tobacco Vanille remains very stable throughout the life of the scent. On the plus side for Tobacco Vanilla, it's sillage and longevity are superior to Back to Black. If you're looking for bang for your buck (ok, lots of bucks), Tobacco Vanille wins hands down. Unfortunately, I do not have any left of my sample of Fumerie Turque, so I can't compare that directly to Back to Black. I'm fairly certain, though, that I would find Fumerie Turque smokier and more leathery than Back to Black. No doubt, because of that, I view Fumerie Turque as more masculine than both Tobacco Vanille and certainly Back to Black. It would probably be my first choice for a man. For me, Back to Black is the ultimate spicy gourmand and destined to become one of my very favorite perfumes

By the drydown, By Kilian BACK TO BLACK seems closer to Jesus del Pozo IN BLACK than it does to Tom Ford TOBACCO VANILLE (to which some people are comparing it). Well, except that the ingredients used in this composition are of significantly higher quality than those used in IN BLACK... Initially the tobacco and honey notes see very dominant, but the saffron is also conspiring with the olibanum and woods to produce an odd rubbery myrrh-like facet. This aspect becomes more pronounced as the perfume dries down, and eventually reaches the point of reminding me of IN BLACK. I realize that this may smack of heresy, given that Jesus del Pozo is something of a low-brow juice factory, while By Kilian is one of the hoitiest and toitiest of niche houses. However, it's important to bear in mind that Jesus del Pozo does enlist the services of good perfumers: Christine Nagel designed IN BLACK, and had she been afforded a "sky is the limit" ingredients budget, her creation would have been every bit as good as this one by Calice Becker.

~ I have always admired a fellow gentleman who smokes a pipe especially one with the sillage of sophisticated cherry tobacco aroma in the air. As a nonsmoker my initial impression of BtB allows me to share that very same mental image in my mind and in reality on my wrist. I easily evoke myself in a high back chair in my own private library with it's well polished shelves and classic leather bound books. This is a fresh out of the pouch opening dab of raspberry and saffron followed by a long lasting perfectly sweet honey and smooth tobacco that I puff on for many enjoyable hours as I read chapters from Dickens or Hemingway. I find this more of a comfort scent than an aphrodisiac perhaps a seduction scent for the mind only? If this is genuinely inspired by or a tribute to the late Amy Winehouse song "Back to Black" then it is very fittingly so. "....And life is like a pipe. And I'm a tiny penny rolling up the walls inside" Kind Regards, Plat ~

Speaking as someone who has been working with perfumery aromachemicals and natural extractives for the better part of 15 years, it is hard for me to see this for anything other than its constituents and the fact that it is a pretty average fragrance when you really break it down to them. It's also one of my favorite mainstream creations of all time, and that's coming from a guy who doesn't have a 1000 bottle shrine, or who seeks out the new hyped banger. When this came out, it really set a trend for "niche" (I hate this term) perfume, and I can confidently say this has been an inspiration for so many perfumers who came later. It's sweet, it's spicy, it's woody, it's honey and booze and fruity and brooding, with a friendly, sexy "come hither" pull. It's a whiskey cocktail. It's a leather chaise that has seen the unthinkable. It's the storage room of a Northwestern farmhouse rife with fruits of the fall harvest. It's a clever creation. I am reminded a bit of oak, tobacco, tea, peaches, and something I've never been able to totally isolate. While I know most of its secrets and it doesn't wow me like it once did almost 15 years ago, it's still one of my most frequently worn fragrances, and I have to bow down in appreciation and admiration, for, in my opinion, one of the most important trendsetters of the 2010s perfume scene. You should try this at least once if you haven't. A sort of historical study piece.

Absolutely incredible fragrance! If only the longevity matched this wonderful scent. I adore this slightly fruity, slighty sweet tobacco scent, which I received in a Kilian sample pack. It's a dark fragrance which is perfect for evenings and fall wear. Definitely NOT in the mold of mass market fragrances or in the mold of modern rose (of which Kilian's Dangerous Liaisons is one that I love & own). Even with longevity that falls short of its price tag, Back to Black just shot to the top of my full-bottle wishlist, and maybe Santa will get it for me this year. Until then, I am wearing JDP's In Black which a cherry-tobacco fragrance that is similar to Back in Black. Although the JDP is not as good as the Kilian, it's only about 1/10 of the price of the Kilian on a per ml basis. For now, JDP will do ... at least until Santa comes. :)

Highly addictive I kept applying a bit on my wrist .. just to smell it!! ...stealing private "scentual" moments to myself .. while riding the bus...! To breakdown and pin point all of this fragrance's complicated notes belittles it somehow.... but this is my impression... fruity at first ... Raspberries ..a touch of honeydew melon...

I first was able to test a vial of Back to Black, and despite the little dabs I was able to get, it went straight to the top of my want list. A year or so later, and I'm happy with my purchase! On a quick side note, I love the fact that you can buy a sturdy purse spray, and then use any Kilian refills you want in it.

I confess this is an unusual fragrance. The notes of the scent are so mixed and crowded,like an ''ashura dessert''. This is a fragrance I classified as extremely sweet-spicy masculine. I don't think it is unisex. Although it contains a dominant honey fragrance, I don't think it is feminine.

Very nice fragrance that opens with a hint of chocolate. From the brief chocolate opening, it quickly transitions to a very natural smelling tobacco and honey combo that is quite nice and is on par with the also excellent Tobacco Vanille from Tom Ford.

?nitial spray; I get raspberry and tobacco honey mix.For me this is not feminine at all and sensually very effective.At a certain point it really deserves the l'aphrodisiac name.After a while there is powdery smell in a good way.it is not as heavy as tobacco vanille and more appropriate even for daily use.

On my own initiative, I probably would never have been interested in this fragrance, and so I must first thank the forum and the inspiring contacts that arise from it, which sometimes manifest in unexpected sample additions in mailings - in this case, my thanks specifically go to Mightynaf. At first glance, I would have overlooked this extrait and dismissed it as at best harmless, fresh-floral with a woody-leathery, seemingly vetiver-containing base. Nevertheless, probably nothing special, and for my taste, perhaps a bit too polished and not quite aligned with my preferences. I become curious, however, after the sample has unexpectedly come my way, when I look at the classifications here in the forum: comparisons to “Irish Leather” are repeatedly drawn, which I like very much. My curiosity is piqued. The comparison is not entirely unfounded: the similarity is indeed present due to the juniper in combination with leather and crystallizes quickly after the bergamot fades. But “Kaff” is distinctly brighter, fresher, and thus also more appealing and less edgy. In the online presentation, the house Terenzi boasts that the fragrance shines as brightly as the star after which it is named. This luminosity must therefore lie at 2.27, since according to my research, the namesake must be β-Cassiopeiae (alias Caph). However, does the fragrance live up to this high claim? The name puzzle is thus at least solved, but the still somewhat puzzling, because also unusual in Italian, spelling remains. The information regarding the name reference is already exhausted, and the rest of the promotional text is more of an emphasis on the special luxury that the fragrance represents rather than being helpful for classification. Nevertheless, it can be said that the Terenzis apparently have a special affinity for astronomy (or probably rather astrology). “Kaff” is part of a “Lunar-Stars collection” - seemingly all named after celestial bodies - and the cap of the bottle is adorned with the phases of the moon and the zodiac signs. Such things are certainly sales-promoting. Be that as it may: perhaps the comparison with the French Irishman is also not entirely fair. If it’s not a fragrance from another star, “Kaff” is certainly more than a Memo light with a somewhat brighter disposition. It soon develops a remarkable spiciness, which begins with a peppery tingle in the top note and is primarily carried by the juniper as it progresses. Yet alongside this, floral notes provide a floral-powdery counterbalance, and a rather nice, unsweetened citrus note makes the fragrance really appear quite lively and fresh for a while, which is a joy. It could, yes it could almost win me over if this first impression lasted longer and if there weren’t soon a somehow disturbing, very synthetic-seeming component that is likely meant to represent the woods in the base, but comes across as if it were largely built on Iso-E-Super. A disappointing turn. This aspect then remains present over a considerable period, increasingly overshadowing the interesting impressions of the beginning and is unfortunately also what ultimately remains as the overall impression. Now I understand the occasional slurs against Tiziana Terenzi as a fashionable fragrance house for the nouveau riche. It’s a shame really; it started quite promisingly. If I’m looking for a star fragrance, I might take a look at “B-612” by Nishane. I generally get along better with the little prince than with horoscopes.

The Kaff Extrait de Parfum impressed me greatly, especially since the scent progression offers enormous variety. The longevity on my skin is incredible at around 24 hours, and the sillage is also convincing. The top note starts fresh and citrusy with bergamot. It also has a green, spicy, and herbal scent of juniper berries, ginger, wormwood, and pepper. The heart note then becomes somewhat sweet-floral, with notes of iris, violet, and magnolia. Over time, a distinct leatheriness emerges. In the background, there is also a powdery nuance. The base offers a sweet-woody combination consisting of tonka beans, sandalwood, bourbon vanilla, and cedarwood. For a brief moment, there were even certain vibes that made me think of "Elysium pour Homme (Parfum) | Roja Parfums." I thank Will for the sample.

Whatever one may think of Terenzi's Kaff - the popular perfume is certainly high quality and one of the better Tiziana creations. Kaff is grassy-herbaceous, floral, spicy, and woody. So it has a DNA that is packed with all sorts of olfactory beauties, a scent that somehow always seems to be in motion. The iris, I have the impression, is such a beautiful Xerjoff- "17/17 - Irisss | XerJoff"-iris, thus possessing a very attractive floral note…. I do not detect the leather here, unlike many others, nor the tonka bean, neither in the drydown. What the detectable or (for me) undetectable ingredients indicate, however, is the undeniable complexity of Kaff. It can be used in many areas and actually excludes nothing; it is also suitable for both genders. For me, the scent impression changes, which is mainly due to the herbaceousness: sometimes too much, sometimes completely within bounds. Therefore, this change influences the usability of the perfume for me. Nevertheless: All those who enjoy something more herbaceous and also highly complex scent nuances will be well served with Terenzi's Kaff!

Kaff smells like a 5-star hotel where nothing is lacking... Here you get an incredibly elegant iris-pepper note. This slightly reminds one of Aventus, but without the smoky part, which takes away the extreme masculine quality of the scent, making it simply smell luxurious. But please don't think that this fragrance is an Aventus clone, because it is by no means that. It is much more a refined version of it, which can be worn not only by men. Sure, Aventus can also be worn by women, but due to the smoky pineapple, it tends to be more masculine. However, after a short wait, leather pairs with this iris-pepper accord. But not a stinky opulent leather, rather a soft, balanced luxury leather that is not particularly aggressive. Additionally, I think I can also slightly perceive the magnolia that complements the scent. In summary, I can say that Kaff smells extremely elegant and luxurious and is well-received by a variety of people. Furthermore, the fragrance is extremely versatile, as I find it suitable for almost any occasion. Moreover, the scent has a quite good longevity (about 10 hours noticeable). But since it has some parallels to Aventus for me, one should think carefully about whether to invest so much money in it. Because €390 is quite a hefty price, but you do get quality for it (which should be normal at such a high price). And not to forget, the bottle. It is truly a work of art. The bottle features an extremely beautiful golden color and a heavy, beautifully decorated cap, as one is accustomed to from Tiziana Terenzi.

Overall, I would describe this scent as quite masculine, yet very elegant. What I mostly get from this on my skin is a very woody, slightly sweet, and rich "dampness". In the opening of the scent, there is actually a really nice and subtle rum note that provides a classy "booziness". The dampness comes from patchouli, which can often lend an earthy/dirty accord that can be off-putting, but it's done very well here...a purely complimentary element, and stands out just enough. The "dried fruit" accord is a stand-out one, and I truly love it. It certainly adds to the olfactive identity of STH. As the scent dries, you lose the booziness and fruitiness, and you're left with a warm, dry yet damp, and slightly vanillic woody patchouli. Potency: I only used one good spray from the sample vial, so this may be different compared to a full spray from an actual bottle. It is subtle but definitely present, even after a few hours. This is surely in the fragrance's favor. This combination of ingredients can often create something a bit cloying if it's too potent. Its lightness is a strong suit. However, it should last on the skin an entire day of activity. Occasions: in my opinion, this is a very good scent for the cooler seasons, when you're dressed nicely. This would suit an upscale event perfectly, whether tuxedo or suit/tie. However, I wouldn't consider this a casual-wear fragrance. For one, it's scent profile seems simply too elegant. But more importantly, the price of a bottle of this stuff will make it not so ideal to have to replace if worn too often. Value: as far as I know, a full bottle only comes in a 50ml size, and I've seen prices as low as $260 and as high as $500+. It's no cheapie. You're supposedly paying for the quality of the ingredients and the presentation of the bottle and optional coffret (which looks great). I might consider the value much better if they offered the fragrance in at least a 100ml size for that price. But hey. Spend it if you got it (and if you love it!) Parfums Vintage has an interesting alternative to STH, which I have reviewed on my YouTube channel. I'll post the review here.

Boozy alright. More like cheap & sweet liquor, or a medicated cough syrup. I suspect the "rum" and sweet patch. At least at the opening doesn't last! The cedar doesn't sit well with me. After an hour or so, it settles into a nice - albeit slightly sweet - skin scent. Maybe even an anti-perfume. I'd pass this by at $20. For $200, I just think what-the ?

The combination of rum, nutmeg, amber and woods in By Kilian STRAIGHT TO HEAVEN conjures up memories in my mind of Bond no 9 HARRODS AMBER, which appears to share all of those notes in significant concentration--except that the rum is not specified as such, so it could be some other form of spirits. Anyway, as a lover of nutmeg in oriental woody perfumes, despite the fact that it's supposed to be a characteristically masculine note, I find STRAIGHT TO HEAVEN quite likeable. Not sure that wearing this fragrance transports me directly to or even in the general neighborhood of heaven. It's nice, but I do not think that it is all that new, and it's certainly not transcendent. I would call this a very safe choice for guys and a somewhat more daring one for gals. I suspect that this sort of composition can be had for significantly less than niche prices, but I do think that STRAIGHT TO HEAVEN is worth sniffing if you like nutmeg and spirits. Why in the world is this subtitled "White Crystal"???

I am a big sucker for the earthy patchouli and this is no exception. A bit in line with Creed Aventus and Nishane Hacivat, Straight To Heaven will bring you the goodness. Sometimes there’s a sweet and spicy whiff coming through. A bit vanillic, even a bit fruity. Great for the cold days. It’s a way toned down perfume though. I sprayed on like 6 or 7 sprays today and still I find it very much a skin scent. So beware you’ll run out pretty quickly. And at the price they’re asking you’d better think twice before buying it.

We all know that anyone can wear anything, that there is no seasonality, that gender and class and age are labels, marketing ploys, social constructs and all that jazz. Yet there are times when you bring a fragrance to your nose for the first time and the picture it paints is so vivid that the associations are very hard to deny.

This is a Masculine version of Queen Latiffah' Queen add in the tabacco Rum And Endear Over 2 Hours of Grandpa's Rants when he was in the war or how like was like Without T.V Computers Cellphones Videogames Things we take For Granted.

Unisex (leaning male) Fragrance story: “Smoldering with addictive sensuality, a burning splash of rich dark rum defines the opening, its sweet gourmand chord is softened by creamy vanilla and dried fruit. Spicy patchouli pairs with the fresh, woodsy scent of cedarwood to finish, finding animalic harmony at long last.

My second by Kilian review on this site. Straight to Heaven is probably my favorite by Killian scent that I own but not the best that I've smelled. I do wear it fairly often, mainly in the fall. Something about the leaves falling and the fields near where I live, it just fits. I do have some memories with this one and I look forward to diving into this with you.

This review is based on a 7.5ml vial from a discovery set for The Woody Cellars collection. This 7.5 ml of Straight to Heaven is all that I would ever need in my life. Contrary to the glowing reviews and hype, I do not find Straight to Heaven even in the same area code as heaven. The opening notes of Straight to Heaven is a woody note embellished by patchouli.

Bianco Puro ain‘t a white fragrance at all. It starts with a smell full of spices, a decent amount of oud will develop after few moments. The scent develops alot. It is not that far off to say that the fragrance will be a whole diffrent one after few hours. I personally like the scent a lot. It is a fruity, sweet, but not to sweet, spicy, woody oudy scent. I would not recommend to purchase it for the €315 but ever yprice around €200 would be a buy for me!

Today is the day for this Terenzi to receive its first review. I am truly surprised that this Terenzi has not yet received a review, it can't be due to the price since there are sharings, but even the price is a bargain compared to most Rojas or other niche brands. Now to the fragrance itself: Bianco Puro opens surprisingly oriental, which really astonished me, especially since I can't identify any individual notes here. After about 5 minutes, the fresh notes take over, revealing a lovely fresh, slightly sweet mandarin, while bergamot and lemon remain very quiet in the background. The mango is very noticeable, giving Bianco Puro its own unique twist. The sweetness mainly comes from the vanilla and caramel notes. After about 4-5 hours, Bianco Puro begins to transition into the base note, where slightly woody notes, particularly sandalwood, come into play. Oud, myrrh, and patchouli add a bit more depth here. Is Bianco Puro a summer fragrance? I would say yes, but at very warm temperatures, it should be dosed very carefully, as Bianco Puro is sweet, creamy, and fruity. Some shops have listed Bianco Puro as a women's fragrance. I cannot agree with that at all, especially since Tiziana Terenzi himself labels his fragrances as unisex, including Bianco Puro. With the previously mentioned depth and the woody notes, Bianco Puro absolutely manages to be unisex. Here, a man really has no reason to fear it could be a women's fragrance. The price is not exactly cheap for a Terenzi, especially since there are other Terenzis from the Luna Collection like Orion available for around €100. But I think Bianco Puro is truly worth the €280, and with a voucher, it can become a bit cheaper. Luckily, I had a voucher. For those who are afraid of a hairspray note, as some might perceive in Kirké, I can give the all-clear for Bianco Puro. This note is not present here.

I wonder how this fragrance got its name... Bianco is, for me, clean, sweet, spring, fruit, sun, and so on. Bianco Pura and you get Oud, but really-not light and deep. On top of that, there’s a light fresh citrus, which is a perfect contrast that makes the fragrance totally interesting. As it develops, however, the citrus fades and the Oud comes more to the forefront. Overall, I perceive the fragrance as dark. I simply expected something different and then got something that I don’t really like. It’s not my thing.

I need to elaborate a bit: after shopping, I went to pick up the package with the fragrances. As soon as I got home, I sprayed all 3 fragrances on myself since it was a blind buy. (They were 3 Tiziana Terenzi fragrances) I put away the shopping and had to drop everything right then to IMMEDIATELY write a review for Bianco Puro. OMG…who would have thought. Sure, the fragrance pyramid would indicate it, but because of the name, I was somehow focused on a clean, fresh scent. What did I have instead on my arm? A mega awesome spicy creamy feminine scent. I can faintly detect caramel. Unfortunately, nothing from fruits, but I am still satisfied. A really beautiful spicy woody scent that smells creamy and is not harsh. Oh yes…something different from what I usually have (well, that’s not entirely true, but I don’t have one like this yet). I was really afraid to buy it blind since there are quite a few reviews that don’t speak well of it. The fragrance matches my taste, and I’m glad I decided on it. Slowly, I can’t hide from all the new Terenzis that I have a new fragrance anymore. I’m very happy to have found a “brand” that hasn’t disappointed me yet and that I like sooooo many fragrances from so far. I should really go visit them in Italy..hihi.

Another review from the Luna collection by Tiziana Terenzi. A fragrance that I ordered together with Leo . The prices on some sites are really very good when you look at the (overpriced) RRP. But as it often is with scents that are more under the radar: These are often available for 50% less, or even more like this Bianco Puro. The less hyped and unpopular fragrances in the perfume community can sometimes be found at great prices, so one should make their own judgment about each fragrance. This one hovers around 7 here and gets little attention. For niche standards, that's already low. Specifically, the less hyped fragrances from this brand should be checked out, as you can really score a good deal. I don't understand why this fragrance isn't more popular. It doesn't smell cheap and has its own recognizability. But it isn't as white as the bottle and the name Bianco suggest. No fragrances are listed under inspiration, but personally, this scent slightly reminds me of M7 (2011) : Not too heavy, a slightly medicinal touch, oud, fruity notes, fine spice with myrrh, clean wood. This combo definitely has style. This direction is tricky, as this fragrance has many facets. Thus, it can't be clearly categorized by occasion or fragrance type. The fragrance comes in the typical Luna box. A nice box that looks pretty and does justice to the niche. However, there are definitely higher quality options. The bottles are also quite pretty and feel good in the hand. However, the labels with the fragrance name do seem a bit cheap. But overall, a solid presentation. As mentioned, it's hard to categorize the scent. It's not really fresh, even though this citrus-fruity top note subtly provides a light fresh breeze in the background. The sweet-spicy notes from the heart and base notes come in quite early. A slightly medicinal-fruity vibe also comes through, similar to M7 Oud Absolu. However, this DNA is a bit brighter due to creamy-sweet notes. Saffron and a light clove note come through early in the progression. The mango note is not clearly recognizable, but there is a fruity note with sweetened caramel-vanilla. Not too sweet-sticky, but overall a pleasant sweet-spicy DNA with a clean touch. In the base, this fragrance then becomes gently woody-spicy with this wonderful sandalwood-musk. Creamy-clean bright musk with a refined sandal note. The myrrh-oud blend is also present and adds a wonderful spice without being too oriental. Overall, a great creation that is quite unique and a fantastic choice if you want to wear something special. The creation feels well-groomed and clean, even though this is not a typically white fragrance. Performance is quite good. This fragrance lasts around 10 hours with good sillage in the first 3-4 hours, and even afterwards, it remains perceptible close to the skin. Thus, it can be easily integrated into everyday life if you can handle this DNA for daily use. Overall, too specific for a blind buy. However, those who roughly like this DNA from M7 can test or buy this one well. A wonderful sweet-spicy fragrance with a clean background.

Euphoria...Excitement...Relaxation Bianco Puro feels like the path to the mountain peak. Beginning of the Journey Filled with anticipation and euphoria, the journey begins. Bianco Puro opens fresh, with a hint of spice in the background. It reminds me a bit of Soleil Blanc, but with more spice, which gives it its own unique character.

It all says it in the title and I'll explain, Love: Amazing scent, suitable for all seasons, very versatile, day and night. Disappointment: Poor performance, average longevity, SILLAGE is almost non-existent and most of the time the perfume stays close to the skin. I have a bottle and I'm debating whether to sell it or keep it anyway... What do you recommend for me? Update 12.3.25: I sold the perfume after I felt that its performance did not satisfy me. 7/10.

Fruity fresh opening with a spicy peppery undertone and a blast of cardamom in the top - extremely refreshing while being dark and unique at the same time As this is part of the liquors collection, this is also based on an alcoholic beverage: rum and it is noticable! Not overly alcoholic but more in the note of a dark wooden barell that had the boozy juice inside. Also I get a hint of smoke. Super masculine, very dark and spicy This scents is way less sweet than angels share. It has a woody vanilla with a very subtle sweetness - but this is not a sweet scent by any means To me, this is the perfect bad boy scent. Boozy, peppery, a hint smokey and woody. Unapologetic and powerful Definitely not a blind buy - get your nose on it before buying. Performance is great - the freshness fades after the opening and then the boozy dark vibe stays for quite a long time

This is an well crafted fragrance that i consider one of the best made by the brand. The rum combined with the vanilla and pineapple gives this sweet,fresh boozy feeling to it. The scent really grows on you the longer you wear it. The price for this is an little overpriced in my opinion but if you have the money for it this is definiently something you need to have in your collection if you like sweet fruity scents.

It's 20°C out here, the wind is picking up a bit. The sky is clear, sun is out, but there's no doubt fall is peaking around the corner. I'm starting to leave behind my warm weather fragrances for the colder one and I felt like trying a sampler in my collection which is how and why I stumbled upon this one that I had forgotten about. I'm starting to think the Kilian brand is not for me. It's ironic to see that I, who's a Straight Edge (I do not drink, smoke, take drugs) person, have a skin chemistry that absolutely loves alcoholic beverage notes. When I first sprayed it on, I got maybe a second of fresh, fruity notes, but then everything changed. The rum came barreling through the door, overwhelming everything else, like someone who refuses to surrender the spotlight. Since I don't drink, I must say I was quite indifferent to it. Then, after about 15 minutes, there's the cardamom that came out, looking for a fight. Both notes vyed for attention on my skin, although I have to admit the perfume is well-blended. At that moment, I could detect a sort of spicy warmth that's a great fit for autumn. I don't know if its because of the strength of the cardamom, but I could almost compare the overall scent to a fall candle (albeit not a cheap one). After about an hour there's a woody base that starts to shine through with a subtle synthetic sheen to it. It fades admirably well into something that's still warm, but also soft and comforting. All in all it's probably a good perfume for those who love the Kilian DNA, but since I don't drink, this perfume is overall a miss for me. A great fit for fall nonetheless!

Another one from the Liquors by Kilian that is going to make it into all top-whatever-lists on youtube afer last year's Angels' Share. The perfume is super likable. The fruity part is not too sweet, the woody not too tart. Together they are delicious, right in the middle of the balance between too straightforward catering to the tastes of the masses and the Kilian-esque elegance. Not super original, but super cozy and pleasant and probably going to be a success commercially.

Now please, don't tell anyone, but I ordered a sample set from Skins because the money didn't stretch for a full bottle of Sweetly Known or Lamar. After I placed the order, a sneaky mail came in that a retailer had 20 percent off an already discounted perfume. That perfume was Apple Brandy.

Unisex (Originally written on 25th of February) This delicious slightly boozy perfume was the one which I was testing a long time ago and I didn’t like it at all. It was offensive yet interesting but I didn’t know that some day I would love it a lot and own the bottle. So if you didn’t like it back in the days maybe you should test it again!

This was not the gourmand I was expecting and that is a good thing. Its the smell of autumn without the gourmand that usually comes with autumn scents. I would even argue that it can be used for summer and spring with how versatile it is. Its a juicy and fresh opening with a oak and spice middle with hints of boozy sweetness that lasts all day. Its addictive.

I think Apple Brandy stand out the most in Liquor collection. Tons of review and youtuber 99 percent usually talk about Angel's Share but don't overlook Apple Brandy it's very sexy and boozy At first for me i get the boozy with the apple syrup( even though it's the pineapple note) have to give big applause for perfumer.

Such a dreamy well-blended boozy apple! It’s not too sweet and I don’t find the alcohol to be too sharp or jarring, (which is my experience with Angels Share). It’s cozy and sophisticated, yet refreshing at the same time, probably thanks to the Cardamom and Bergamot, and unique to what I’ve tried. I don’t get any pineapple, and I’m surprised to see it listed here.

There is a kilometers long sand beach on southern Adriatic coast where I spent my summer vacations as a kid visiting my italian Nona (the other nona was by contrast - Austrian). This scent is exactly how I associate the smell of scorched mediterranean shrubs and soft, emulsified, salty evening air as waves grind rough rocks into sand. Terenzi parfumes are created here, literary 10 walking minutes from this beach and I totally get it! This unique vibe is unmistakenly endemic, I cant imagine finding it anywhere else. Tiziana says Sicilly, sure, but it may be anywhere along olive-tree belt. Like with other profumieri who share similar DNA (Pazzaglia, Bianchi, Martinelli), dominantly soapy/powdery notes dance around citruses, salt and myrth in such a sofisticated and refined way making it simply beatiful. It is mellow but not feminine. Akragas does not scream, it does not impose itself, just softly envelopes itself around you in a nonchalant, I-Dont-Give-A-Foque kinda way. Sì, questa è la sensibilità italiana in una bottiglia, assolutamente! Super cool. The scent a Sigma would wear.

Akragas, the Valley of the Temples. Today only ruins, once a flourishing city in Sicily. One can only imagine how it must have smelled there once. Sea, salt, herbs, and limestone. In my opinion, these notes are also reflected in the fragrance of Tiziana Terenzi. It opens fresh, a bit eucalyptus-like with a slight citrus that leans more towards the delicately sweet, all enveloped in a salty mineral cloak. As it develops, Akragas increasingly transforms into a warm-soapy scent with great longevity and a very decent sillage. All in all, a successful composition that truly lives up to its name.

Summer is over and this one is likely to be rather uninteresting for the next few months. It was released quite late, but anyone looking for an aquatic spring/summer scent for next year can give this a try. Especially if you like this style à la Acqua di Sale, this is a great option. I love this salty-seaweed DNA with beautiful myrtle. For me, this fragrance is less appealing as I already own two of this kind: Acqua di Sale & "Sandflowers | Montale." Salina & Salaria are also two great alternatives. Salaria was also created by Paolo, and I believe this brand belongs to the Terenzis as well. Here again for Tiziana with a bit more budget, which you can also smell. Akragas is, I believe, an ancient Greek site in Sicily. In terms of price, this line from Tiziana Terenzi is one of the more affordable ones, usually with a retail price of 190 euros. However, some of these can be found with a 30-50% discount if you look carefully and have a bit of patience. Like these typical saltwater aquatics à la Acqua di Sale, this one also has the classic notes of myrtle, seaweed, and salt. I love this combo as it simply evokes those authentic saltwater vacation vibes and fits perfectly with sunny hot days. A serious and mature appearance. What distinguishes this Akragas from Profumum Roma? It is clearly much more complex and more fragrance notes are perceivable. While the AdS is rather monotonous, this Akragas develops with many spicy notes. It comes quite close to "Salaria | Giardino Benessere," although I find this one much more harmonious as it really develops beautifully in the heart note. Geranium doesn’t say anything to me, but the heart note has great vibes with pleasant spice, nice wood, and soft-sensual notes. Patchouli also develops over time. The base and the dry down are already very pleasant and sensual. I don’t really perceive benzoin & vanilla, but the base rounds off this fragrance very well. Performance is traditionally good for a Terenzi, but by far not as good as Profumum Roma. Sillage is pleasant and longevity should be around 7+ hours. The scent is clearly unisex and shines best in late spring and summer. Due to the strong spiciness, this one theoretically wouldn’t be wrong in autumn either. For me, it’s an absolutely good fragrance, even though this style isn’t really new. If Acqua di Sale is too monotonous for you, you should give this one a chance. Those who don’t like this salty-seaweed style probably won’t really enjoy this either. I love such unique freshies.

The fragrance, which can either be a compliment magnet or the reason for a ban from the local shopping mall, has received a big sister - or as I actually find it more fitting: a mother. The fact is: No one can match Tiziana Terenzi when it comes to packaging. The quality of the bottle itself has also been significantly improved; it is much heavier and closes beautifully this time. But how does the fragrance smell now? I think I can best illustrate this with a little metaphor: Imagine Kirkè is a lively teenager who is totally curious and adventurous and knows how to make a splash. Kirkè wants to leave an impression, no matter what kind - as long as one remains memorable. If I had to describe it in colors, I would say: Kirkè is neon colors. Kirkè overdose, on the other hand, is Kirkè's mother, who has gone through all those times and carries them within, but has now grown into a mature, radiant, mysterious, elegant adult. I would say: Kirkè overdose is pastel colors. The two definitely have some similarities, but each also has its own signature. The first thing I noticed is that Kirkè Overdose has much less fruit cocktail DNA and carries significantly less synthetic elements. Accordingly, it is less shrill and piercing and somehow rounder and perhaps more pleasant for some noses. We also have a bit more floral notes here with a delicate, understated rose note, which is listed instead of the pear in the opening, making it somehow a bit deeper (and possibly even more unisex). The fragrance also has a slightly resinous or lipstick-like quality. Additionally, I must say: I didn’t really know how this sand note in the original smelled - now I know: in my opinion, it is a bit stronger here and makes the fragrance a little drier. In the drydown, Kirkè Overdose then moves further and further away from the typical Kirkè DNA and leaves behind a slightly floral, dry but beautiful musk with sandalwood on the skin. Overall, I feel that Kirkè Overdose hugs the skin a bit more and "connects" with the person wearing it rather than laying like a mask on the person. It simply feels a good deal more mature and "natural". In this respect, Kirkè overdose is not necessarily an overdose of the original Kirkè DNA for me, but rather an overdose of luxury, elegance, style, and finesse. Ultimately, both carry the Kirkè DNA within them, but in my opinion, they are different enough to own both or at least take a look at them. And especially those for whom Kirkè is not quite right should perhaps still dare to try Kirkè Overdose, as it is simply a bit more "digestible" and doesn’t shout at you, but rather whispers in your ear. Personally, I was and still am a big fan of the fruit-musk DNA in Kirkè, not least because it was my signature scent for a long time, associated with many memories and emotions. Accordingly, it simply holds a special place in my heart.

When I first heard about Kirke Overdose, I didn't think I would like it so much, as the Kirkè Extrait de Parfum is my absolute nightmare fragrance. The fruitiness is much more pleasant, and the creamy, slightly sweet-woody base comes through beautifully. The Kirkè Extrait de Parfum is very loud compared to the Overdose, which is much more elegant and wearable. Overall, a very nice, more mature scent that can be worn well without getting a headache like with the Kirkè Extrait de Parfum .

I would say yes. Even though the scent is truly not an innovation. The name "Kirke Overdose" is fitting on one hand, as it also carries the word "Kirke." Thus, the Kirkè Overdose implies that it is based on the well-known "Kirkè (Extrait de Parfum) | Tiziana Terenzi," and that is unmistakably the case.
