The fruit basket is still there, albeit a bit tamer and more beautifully and appealingly composed. On the other hand, the word "Overdose" suggests to me an even stronger Kirke. That, however, is absolutely not the case. The current batches of Kirkè Extrait de Parfum are already not as strong performers as they were a few years ago; the Kirkè Overdose is even tamer in comparison. Pleasant, not quite so screechy, not quite so taxing on the nose and without hairspray associations; but also with less power. For me, Kirkè Extrait de Parfum and Kirkè Overdose are to each other roughly like Erba Pura and "Erba Pura Magica | Sospiro." Each is based on the other, unmistakably related scents with their own, sometimes better nuances and therefore rightly independent. Whether it is really necessary, everyone can decide for themselves.

My first impression is and remains positive. I own Kirkè Extrait de Parfum and Kirkè Overdose ...so I was able to compare them directly. I noticed that the Overdose comes across as a bit "deeper," which is probably due to the rose that seems to have taken the place of the pear. While Kirkè Extrait de Parfum is quite linear, Kirkè Overdose transforms into a completely different scent in my opinion - at least on my skin. In the top notes, they are very similar, while in the heart notes, they take their own directions. In "Kirkè Overdose | Tiziana Terenzi," the rose fades into the background, leaving a slightly fruity musk behind. Who is this fragrance for? Even more masculine, due to the rose (yes, due to the rose!). Thus, it is more for men - even though it is a purely unisex fragrance. You just have to be okay with the progression. Therefore, it's best to test it yourself and decide. The packaging is on another level. It takes up a lot of space and comes in the typical Terenzi box with an LED lamp, as known from the brand's special fragrances. The packaging is wrapped in black velvet and feels nice to the touch. The bottle itself is the most beautiful that TT has ever made. It's worth testing. Great scent.

Well, i don't know exactly how a narcissus flower smell or should smell, but if it's something closer to it i'll fall in love with it. Prada Narciso seems like an essence of a summer afternoon bottled. It's an air dominated by a smell which is sweet as the orange flower but has something spicy, waxy, and slightly animalic. It's very sensual and clean at the same time, a beautiful perfume. 16/03/2015 Update: Almost an year after i wore it and wrote a short review about it, today i can be certain that this creation in the prada exclusive line is not exactly an Narciso soliflore. Indeed, the fragrance seems more to use its smell in an abstract way and i suspect is there is narcisse absolute in this creation it's volume is low due to european resctrictions on its use, the price of the absolute and supply variabilities of this flower. Besides that, i still think that its smell captures very well a blissful summer aroma, since it uses in a quite abundant way a flower that gives me this impression, the orange flower. It's an interesting choice, considering that Narciso has aromachemicals in common not with the orange flower but with the jasmine. This way, i believe that the orange flower here is used to compose the white floral part of the idea, extending the honey nuances with the waxy side of beeswax. The opening tries to convey the fresher aspect of the absolute combining the citrus and slightly bitter bergamot aroma with the citrus floral nuances of the orange flower. When it gets into the base, the fragrance goes into a musky, velvelty impression, with a bit of woody vetiver aroma and an olibanum giving a discreet minty incense fresh aroma. It's a beautiful and lavish recriation of the Narcisse dynamics of evolution, but still it could have been extended in some points (spicy touches and a greener tone on the aroma, for instance) to give a a greater resemblance with the flower.

Cringe of the full name aside, I love this perfume. It's both cozy and refreshing. At first spray, you can pick up on all of the notes: the freshness of the green tea, the sweetness of the marshmallow. But, without being overpowering, the strongest of the three is the ginger—it's citrusy and fizzy with a bit of warm spice. Overall, lovely and smells like a warm tea latte. After about two hours, the green tea begins to fade for me, leaving behind the ginger and marshmallow for the remainder of the wear. This lasted for about 7 hours on me and the sillage was moderate. This perfume strongly reminds me of Commodity's Milk (expressive) with the marshmallow and its creamy, almost lactonic, quality; as well as Being Frenshe's Moon Milk—also creamy and sweet with warm spice.

It might go without saying that this perfume holds a very special place in my heart. Originally what attracted me to this fragrance was the name. It sounded very kitschy, a little funny, and inspired me enough to give it a try. Upon first sniff it was a very pleasant ginger tea with a fluffy quality to it. As it dried down on my skin it began to transform into a "quiet" marshmallow perfume, subtly sweet, and the greenness balances out the sugariness overall. Creamy marshmallow, warm ginger, and fresh green tea in an incredible combination. Initially testing this out I would say it lasted a good 5 - 6 hours on my skin in warm weather. This is the type of fragrance that likes to stick to your skin in a small scent bubble. For Christmas, I was gifted this perfume from my mom and I was overjoyed to receive it. It took a month of deliberation if this was the fragrance I wanted to use for my wedding day and I avoided using it at all until it was time. Ultimately the deciding factor came down simply to the name; it was ironic enough for me to decide this was the one to use. I have no regrets about it. When January rolled around and it was time to use it for my wedding, it felt like the perfect and "right" choice, much like finding the wedding dress made for you. Now that I've moved into colder weather I've noticed some differences in performance as well as the way it smells. The longevity increased, giving me around 6 - 7 hours of wear time, and I've noticed the projection has improved too. In the chilly months, I feel like the sweetness in this fragrance is much more apparent. It's in the same vein of being light enough and not cloying, although the marshmallow goodness stands out amongst the other notes on my skin. Sweet, warm, like a fluffy hug, perfect for all seasons and all occasions, even your most special ones.

Why did I buy this? I got caught up in the hype, sadly. I did get a sample first, and enjoyed it. My full bottle, even thought I've let it sit for a few months, is nothing special. It's pleasant and inoffensive, but I can't detect the much-hyped marshmallow scent. It just smells lightly sweet, with a faint whisper of green tea. It's pricey, and I should have spent my money on something more unique and exciting. Princess isn't bad, but it's nothing special either. Maybe I'll use it as a bedtime scent.

Unmistakably marshmallow, this is a sweet, creamy gourmand with lovely cozy vibes. I love that the marshmallow note is so immediately identifiable throughout the life of the scent and doesn't pull vanilla; it's a fun and more interesting twist on what could have easily been a cloying and obvious dessert gourmand. The green tea is buried under a thick layer of marshmallow fluff at first, but as the strongly saccharine open calms down a little, the sweet earthiness of matcha comes through and tempers all the sugar a little, with a hint of ginger spice. The overall vibe here is sitting by a warm fire under a cuddly blanket and sipping a hot cup of tea with marshmallows (ignoring, of course, that marshmallows are not normally a tea thing!) It's candy-sweet and snuggles nicely into the skin, with its silage on the softer side of average, and would be a lovely scent for the holidays or the early, still-cold days of spring.

Forget the cheesy name, this is a beautiful fragrance! I would almost not have tried because the marketing for this line is so cringey, now I'm glad I overcame my prejudice and found something I love and wear often. This is relatively simple and linear, but gorgeous and unique. Princess is a very sweet gourmand, a fluffy cloud of vanilla and marshmallows. I think the sweetness is very smooth here. The green tea really shines on my skin and lends freshness to the composition, it contrasts so nicely with the sweetness. I can smell lemon, ginger and jasmine too, but only as very slight accents. The overall effect is an olfactory equivalent to a matcha latte with vanilla whipped cream or those green tea cheesecake drinks. Princess can easily be worn in the daytime as it's soft and fluffy and not loud or especially sexy, but it has a nice creamy texture and doesn't come across as thin or weak. I saw many people online compare this to other sweet fragrances, but I don't think Princess is that close to any of them. Especially not to Pink Sugar, I actually think these two are on the opposite ends of the feminine gourmand spectrum.

What a gorgeous fragrance. This is an instant love for me. Absolutely beautiful. I get the marshmallow and matcha. I just wish this scent was much stronger. My bottle will be used up so fast, because I can’t get enough of this. It leaves such a beautiful scent bubble around you. This is one I’ll repurchase over and over. I love that the bottles are refillable as well.

I bought a Kilian sampler set that included Angels' Share because I loved that but wasn't ready to pull the trigger on it quite yet. This was in the set and I was expecting to love it because of how much I loved No Prince Required Eau de Parfum , and I definitely wasn't let down.

This scent reminds me of staying in at night and wearing a matching pajama set. It's quite feminine and put together but in a cozy way. A really lovely marshmallowy, matcha latte scent. Suuuuper sweet but I think the matcha makes it a bit more interesting and earthy so I enjoy it even though gourmands aren't always my style.

The notes on this are right up my alley, so I was really excited for this one. People tell me every time I wear marshmallow scents that they are made for me and I should never wear anything else. But man, this one instantly smelled like baby wipes on me. Just a really generic powdery scent.

I absolutely love this line: I Don't need a prince by my side to be a princess. Its a reminder of inner strength and independence, and it really resonated with me! My friend gifted it to me, and now I can't stop buying everything kilian...its empowering and inspiring!!! Highly Recommend!

discovered following a blind purchase, it was a gift to my wife for the holidays. given the success of this brand with already telea and draco very appreciated by madam I thought once again to have found the perfect gift. then the bottle is magnificent but then the smell is very special it is really very green perhaps because of the rosemary we also smell blood orange and grapefruit, but there is a smell that is a bit old lady in addition the sillage is strong and heady. the sumptuous bottle justifies part of the price but the perfume does not. I advise you not to buy it blind. It is clearly a feminine perfume and for a fairly mature lady, I would say at least 50 years old. I hope this review has been useful to you.

Kilian’s Smoking Hot, crafted by Mathieu Nardin, is a quirky and intriguing take on a smoking apple accord. It's often described as an "apple hookah" fragrance, blending a tarty, almost cidery apple sweetness with a dry, slightly smoky warmth. Licorice and (a very wearable) tobacco give it further personality. The result is a unique balanced sweetness, which is not cloying, making it neutral in terms of gender wearability. Performance is good as you would expect given Smoking Hot's main notes. It lasts around 8-10 hours on skin while maintaining solid projection within arm’s length throughout. On clothes, it lingers for a full 24 hours, ensuring its presence well into the next day. I first discovered Smoking Hot through Lattafa Mashrabya, a well-executed clone that, while enjoyable, suffers from the usual issues of synthetics and a more indistinguishable note structure. However, after experiencing the original, I found it compelling enough to purchase a full bottle, something no other Kilian fragrance had convinced me to do before... If you're looking for a bold, smoky apple scent with an addictive, almost dry sweetness, Smoking Hot is a fantastic option for colder months. It is a solid 8, if you need a numerical score. Given the price, sample first or try Mashrabya.

I do not own this fragrance, I have tested it in store. So now that we have gotten that out of the way, lemme tell you that this IS SO SEXY. I don't know how they managed to perfect a hookah fantasy note, but they did, and they made a blend so sexy, that I am crying right now, because I know I cannot afford a bottle. But let's start with the opening, it's very sweet, sharp, headache-inducing, hookah tobacco. But fear not, after 30 minutes I started picking on the hookah smoke. I still have it on my hand, I love how this one smells. After 30 minutes, it turns into a very sweet, syrupy, hookah smoke. I showed this to a girl, she said it's too sweet. So, if you are not a fan of sweet scents, sample this one before you buy a bottle. But either way, I love this. It's very unique. Though, be prepared to smell like a hookah when you wear this!

I don't usually blind-buy fragrances, mainly because I dislike landing in situations like the one I think I am in with Smoking Hot . After my first wear, I'd say that I like the scent but I don't love it. Take your current wish list and look exactly in the middle - those are scents that you like (and may eventually buy), but don't need. That's where Smoking Hot would be on my list. The wearing experience offers some layers. Upon first spray, I guess the surprising part is that there is zero smokiness, incense etc. I mainly get fruity & a little bit bitter/sweet. Shortly after, the sweetness starts to accumulate & the fruity/bitter accords turn into a clearer apple note. The scent begins to mimic a winterized version of Apple Brandy on the Rocks . Thereafter, it's the dry & warm spicy tobacco notes that star with the apple for the next 2 hours. The key comparison here is to think of Smoking Hot as the apple-tobacco equivalent to how fragrances like Herod , Manhattan Eau de Parfum , and Boundless use their cherry-tobacco tonality. You could even think of the latest Kilian as a blend of (1) an amped-up Apple Brandy, and (2) a milder Herod. Worthy of note is that this scent doesn't actually offer me any resemblance of "Angels' Share | Kilian". I think as a whole it's blended well. I think it offers some unique edges, as it isn't just another play in the Herod ballpark nor in the Manhattan/Boundless ballpark. I think in the air it's really nice - it's approaching niche-smelling niche much the same way like a Russian Tea, or an Aquila Absolute in that it combines accords in non-standard fashion. But simultaneously, I don't think it's that innovative. And post-Estee Kilian as a whole isn't putting out anything that has me in a chokehold, much like how Maison Francis Kurkdjian is riding on the coattails of BR540 & Grand Soir. Fall-winter fragrances are the only thing Kilian is objectively great at, but just like MFK, I wonder how much of my sentiment is just nostalgia and the brand living off their household names. There's no doubt that I need more time with it. But I will start (in my opinion) conservatively and rate it an 8/10. It's a like, not a love. While the performance is subject to change, I'd say I get moderate-to-strong sillage for a couple hours. Longevity is on the lower end of good; my 7/10 ranking is 7 to 8 hours but I did feel like the scent does actually die off far before 7 hours with shred ounces of the warm spicy & tobacco accords remaining for upwards of 10 hours.

…so, I got this and Mashrabya to compare… It’s a little bit both ways. Kilian is by far superior in QUALITY. From the first minute to the very end (over 12 hours), the quality of ingredients is absolutely apparent. The smoky intro into the mid, then into the dry down. All of it. Superior in quality. Mashrabya doesn’t even come close in the opening, and where they are similar (very similar) is in the mid. The difference is not only in the quality, but the depth. The darkness. Smoking Hot gives a very visual picture. A dark whiskey/scotch color comes to mind when sniffing it. A spiciness that you can feel. The actual spices. While Mashrabya gives the “same feel” it’s much more sweet, and it’s louder. I would compare it to a cherry sweetness in Mashrabya, while Smoking Hot is a collaboration. A resinous mixture of booze and spice. Mashrabya feels more feminine to me. A louder, more feminine, cherry stick is how I would describe it. Anyone who has smelled Smoking Hot WILL know that you are wearing a dupe. It is VERY close, but the quality difference IS HUGE. As you progress further, smoking hot continues to evolve more smokiness, and projects well to the very end. I would say it projects a good 3-5ft radius on 5 sprays, and leaves a nice lingering sillage trail. Again it lasts an easy 12+ hours. Now while the mid of Smoking Hot is similar to the majority of Mashrabya, when it drys down to skin they get a tad closer, but the ingredients still tell the tale. A much darker, spicier, smoky resin is the vibe from Smoking Hot, while a brighter, rounder syrup is what I get from Mashrabya. It’s about what you want from your fragrance. No more, no less. It’s like buying the real handbag or a fake. It’s there. The enthusiast WILL immediately know. The average Joe won’t. It was a fun comparison, but Kilian won in a blowout.

It smells a lot like Tobacolor , but… better! Dior’s take on tobacco feels bitter and overpowering to me, which I really dislike. Here, the tobacco is still prominent but perfectly balanced with the sweetness. The cinnamon adds a lovely spicy touch, the vanilla is soft and plush, and most importantly, there’s zero bitterness. In the opening, it’s intensely gourmand, but as it settles, the tobacco steps in, giving the fragrance a whole new dimension. In short, I really like it!

What can i say about this one. All i smell is a licorice real strong licorice. It starts very sweet like “angels share” But dark sweet as dark as a tobacco smell, like you did smoke a cigar and you did spray a very sweet perfume. Anyway not bad at all. Good silage and longevity A good Men Men perfume.

In a bit of a deviation from my other reviews, this piece is based on a first impression. A lot of the time in the fragrance space, expectations ≠ reality. What you think you might get can end up being far from what it actually is. Same with food, same with cars, same with… well, everything really. And that is to say: this is NOT blind-buy safe.

What happened to Kilian? They released so many good fragrances in the past. This one is a big NO for me. It has synthetic vibe with accord of rotten apple. I tried it like a 5 times in different temperatures - every time this "rotten" vibe destroyed everything! Smells like a dirty narghile, sorry not sorry!

The fragrance begins with a creamy, realistic, high-quality apple/cinnamon shisha scent. Then the fragrance develops with the entry of vanilla mixed with orcanox. The best types of vanilla (bourbon) were used. At the same time, tobacco begins to form the heart of the fragrance with the shisha/vanilla mixture.

At night, darkness envelops every gesture, leading the soul along paths of perdition and unstoppable temptations. Every prohibition dissolves in darkness, giving life to a kingdom where everything is allowed and silence becomes an accomplice to our daring adventures.

I'm so amazed that I love this one! I never like the Love Spell flankers. It's super whipped, light, and airy. The best explanation I can give that I haven’t seen anyone else say is that the initial “kick” of the core fragrance is not there. Instead you get a whipped cream scent with a “twist.” Example - fluffy, lactonic whipped cream with a Love Spell kiss, etc. null of the screechiness of the OG Love Spell at all.

…I don’t get the Carlisle comparison though. Not at all. Red Tobacco? I don’t get that either. Arrakis is a nice, smooth, sweet tonkabacco scent. Very high quality ingredients. Every little bit of it. It takes you on a journey. The opening gives a peek of what’s coming, a little tease of the tobacco, but a light, breezy opening quickly starts to thicken up and become darker and darker as every minute passes. After the windy feeling opening subsides and you go into the mid, you feel the woody tobacco become more and more present. It’s not that moist, dark pipe tobacco feel of Carlisle or Red Tobacco though. It’s a drier, woodier feeling. As the hours pass, the tonka bean and Oud moisten it up a bit, and add a darker depth, but it definitely has its own fingerprint. There’s no syrupy feel to the sweetness. It’s more of a dry, woody elegance. Performance is FANTASTIC. Projection of a 3-5ft radius, with a slow, lingering Sillage trail that lasts 12+ hours. I am happy I found this because it’s not a common scent where I am. Very happy with this buy.

Tiziana Terenzi has an impressive pace when it comes to introducing new fragrances across various lines and price categories. Despite the large number of scents, the quality does not seem to suffer, at least with the fragrances I’ve had the chance to experience. Of course, not everything is to my taste, but the quality is right. With "Draconis" and "Arrakis," two fragrances from the crisp and expensive Luna Gold Collection are now included. Both are stars from the constellation of the dragon, with Arrakis also being the fictional desert planet from the Dune cycles for cinema lovers. However, the Terenzis do not refer to the latter. Now to the scent: It opens with a citrus-medical cloud, where the citrus fruits are not individually identifiable. Not very lemony, but also not extremely bitter. So, well blended. I think bergamot plays the main role, supported by the rest. Alongside the citrus fruits, a saffron-oud combination takes on the second main role of the top note, leaning more towards the medicinal type of oud. Even though oud is not listed in the top notes, I can definitely sense it. For the untrained nose, this might be a bit harsh, but niche perfume enthusiasts will enjoy it. The top note recedes, and the heart quickly comes in with a hefty amount of marzipan. Not exactly subtle, but very delicious. The sweetness is fortunately not too sticky, but rather good quality marzipan. This quality marzipan is supported by remnants of the fruits from the top note, along with slightly bitter undertones that I attribute to the also rather supporting woods. This marzipan heart lasts quite a long time, around 2-3 hours, and forms an important pillar for the feel-good aspect of the fragrance. Apparently, the supposedly only present tonka bean in the heart note has sneaked forward a bit earlier and quite noticeably, creating a really beautiful marzipan combination with the resinous woods. Now one could be satisfied with this situation, as it lasts quite a while for me. In my mind, the fragrance was already mentally categorized when it surprises me with what I find to be a rather late base note. This then also comes unusually suddenly, as base notes usually tend to creep in slowly. The marzipan recedes - though not entirely - and gives way to leather and tobacco. The tobacco should have already shown itself in the heart, but I find it comes rather late. For me, leather also comes into play, even though it is not listed in the notes. Thus, the heart forms a very warm and slightly sweet fragrance combination dominated by tobacco and leather, which is a nice continuation of the also pleasant but somewhat louder heart marzipan. Amber certainly plays a diligent supporting role as well. A very beautiful fragrance that has surprised me a bit with its development towards the end. Up to the heart, it is somewhat louder and (non-sticky) sweeter, which might appeal a bit more to the ladies. The base note is almost a bit masculine with the leathery tobacco. Even though I have mentioned marzipan several times, the fragrance is not squeaky-sweet but truly good marzipan. Marzipan fans will know what I’m talking about. However, this fragrance should only be used by those who have no issue with tonka. Without tonka, there would be no quality marzipan here, and the diligent tonka bean also takes care of the residual sweetness in the base. Oud in its slightly medicinal variant is also present here, but for me, aside from the initial top note clouds, it plays a rather subdued supporting role and is not in the foreground. So, no panic for those who do not like oud. For me, a candidate for purchase as a great feel-good fragrance, modestly dosed in the base, possibly even suitable for work. The notes come across somewhat differently in timing than indicated in the pyramid, but as they come, they work wonderfully.

Tiziana Terenzi Libra is a very beautiful scent for both men and women. The opening starts with a lovely rose note and a hint of fresh lemon. After 20 minutes, the Madagascan vanilla blossom comes in, rounded off by amber and musk. The patchouli gives the complete fragrance a pleasant note at the end. H/S 8.5/10

After having this scent in my collection for a while I have to pay tribute to it and write a comment. Lavender + Vanilla but neither Jicky not Pour un Homme. How is that? You can find the recipe of this dream-scent at http://www.bykilian.com/en/les_fragrances/a_taste_of_heaven/ What you see are mainly high-quality naturals, amber seems to be the only component that is synthetic. And they make us pay for it (although lavender is not particularly expensive, it must be the real vanilla and tonka) - but the travel refils are affordable. I've just sprayed some on my arm - in summer (original written in august) the sweet vanilla notes are a bit more prominent, I think. The scent seems quite linear for quite some time. The vanilla is present from the beginning, the lavender is very long lasting. The transitions between the different stages are veeery smooth. I suppose that this is due to the high concentration of perfume oils and the technically very good composition. The longevity of the scent is very good and the sillage very noticeable but not too overpowering. In this scent Kilian uses costus oil as a fixator. Together with Barrême lavender this ingredient seems responsible for the slight animalic touch of this scent. The Barrême seems to dominate the other lavender oils although it doesn't have the highest percentage (I own some decants of different lavender oils, and I clearly smell the Barrême in this one). Animalistic and sexy - yeah. But very different from Jicky, which has a good dose of civet and herbes provencales. Actually I don't think that it ressembles Jicky that much at all. In taste of heaven the lavender note is more dominant and more long-lasting, while the drydown of Jicky is more carnal and muskier. To be honest, I have no clue what absinth smells like, but I don't think that it contains that much even though this perfume owes its name to this component. Luca Turin calls A taste of heaven a "refined version of Pour un Homme" (more refined but one star less than the Caron). I don't agree with him in this point for one simple reason. I love taste of heaven but can't stand Pour un Homme. To my nose Pour un Homme is pure synthetic and not well composed. It does have a civet note (I think) that strongly reminds me of bad breath. Taste of heaven is a unisex scent. Due to its classic fougère structure it leans a bit towards the masculine side. But the vanilla sweetness makes it very wearable for women. Despite its classic character I wouldn't consider it dated at all. Due to its intensity it is more of a special occasion scent and not an everyday-to-work-scent. Especially in summer I wouldn't wear it to the office. Actually I don't have many opportunities to wear it. I think it would be very suitable for formal occasions (suit+tie / coat and skirt), for theater, opera, work dinner amongst others - as long as it may be less subtle than Pour Monsieur. Don't misunderstand - it is not a terribly loud fragrance, but it does have presence and you will get noticed. Simply beautiful, classy, perfectly balanced. Addition: Later it starts developing a herbal, slightly bitter note. Especially when you stick your nose close to the skin. Might be the absinth.

By Kilian A TASTE OF HEAVEN initially smells quite green to my nose, and I immediately caught the absinthe note, familiar to me from a recent wearing of Tokyo Milk Dark ARSENIC, which boasts a very powerful dose of absinthe (albeit combined there with salt--a very eccentric and unique composition, it seems to me). After a couple of minutes, the lavender and vanilla really crescendo and take over for a while. However, I still detect the absinthe in the background. Eventually, as this perfume dries down, the absinthe reasserts itself. I really have the sense that the absinthe is woven into the lavender-vanilla complex, making it less sweet and less brash. All in all a nice journey! I compared A TASTE OF HEAVEN with Caron POUR UN HOMME, and I have to say that I like the By Kilian much more. First, the absinthe adds real interest to a combination which is not really beloved to me: lavender and vanilla. But the lavender in the Caron creation is also quite a bit more harsh to my nose. All in all, I would recommend A TASTE OF HEAVEN both for the absinthe facet and for the smooth-wearing lavender.

This does not deserve the 7.6 rating. A Taste of Heaven is a lovely lavender barbershop fragrance with a warm rich vanilla and amber undertone. The absinthe gives this fragrance just enough green and herbal vibe to make it different from other fougeres. I will be the first to say that I’m not a fan of barbershop fougeres. I tend to gravitate towards sexy evening scents and not into gentlemanly type office scents. I have the private blend Beau de Jour by Tom Ford and Masculin Pluriel by Maison Francis but never reach for them. This on the other hand is smooth & sexy. It’s warm, inviting and welcoming. I can see myself wearing this to dinner/evening out. Also, A Taste of Heaven does not have performance issues like some of the other Kilian offerings. This is really sticking to my skin nicely and I don’t have to find the scent. The sillage is really above moderate. Many say this is similar to Pour Un Homme de Caron. I’ve never smelled it and to be honest probably never will since I have this. I recommend giving this discontinued gem a try because it is an excellent choice from the house of Kilian.

As far as I am concerned, this should be renamed "A Taste of Hell". It could be I just don't care much for lavender fragrances, but all I can say is I find this completely unwearable and sickeningly floral. Bad smelling and relatively high priced equals an easy thumbs down from me for this 1 star out of 5 abomination.

Usually I put on a lavender dominated scent when I suspect I will have troubble getting some sleep. And then I turn to basic lavender with not so much else going on. More complex kind of lavender fragrances seem to not work as well as sleeping pills and I have, until I tried A taste of Heaven, not found any other lavender I fancy to wear during daytime. To me lavender usually is something either sleepy/relaxing or something clean, starched and somewhat old fashioned. By Kilians A taste of Heaven is an outstanding exception. This is a "dirty" (but, not as dirty as poor old Jicky!) sensual and also, almost melancholic lavender to me... There is something dusky, something gloomy, yet very soothing about it. The lavender is very prominent, but kind of muted, mellowed down and I do belive it can be that absinthe... making it more aromatic, with an almost haylike note and something that to me also smells close to buttery (in best possible way, there isn´t anything oily or fatty about it). The opening is addictive. Maybe that´s also absinthe related? Even though I really, really like the whole scent, the opening and heart is what makes it so outstanding to me. The drydown is powdery, slightly sweet and well rounded but also add a little more "masculinity" to the fragrance, which I don´t mind, but not like as much as the rest though. But, on the other hand, A taste of Heaven also works just great on my husband. Prett much a must try if you have the slightest interest for lavender or looking for a little more modern take on this classic perfume ingredience. Longlasting, utterly well made, smoth, sensual and luxurious.

Heaven ... so many things to so many different people. My idea of 'heaven' is drowning in a vat of my favorite fragrance :) (amongst other things) ... but I'm pretty sure that vat won't be containing this by Killian offering. Far from not being a good fragrance, A Taste of Heaven is actually a very lively take on the somewhat dated combination of Vanilla and Lavender.

Lots and lots of lavender in the beginning. Although lavender blooms in the summer, I find this to be a cold smell. There is something reminiscent of a forest in winter about this scent. I pick up a balsamy aroma that makes me think of very fresh winter air.

Ladies don't be afraid to try this, I feel it's unisex, very wearable for a confident woman. On first spray I get the Lavender note mixed with wormwood and bergamot, I actually find this phase quite relaxing and calming.

A strange scent. At first, a fleeting hint of citrus fruit - gone in an instant. Orange blossom? No, far too sour for that. Next come lavender and patchouli. The lavender is not sweet at all, almost bitter, and bites at my nose. Unfortunately, it also involuntarily reminds me of old skin after just a few minutes, which is not an isolated incident in my lavender experiments.

Everything has been written about this fragrance, but because it has touched me so much, I must also share a few sentences from my notes about it. The opening is powerful and three thoughts race through my mind: Finally, I am smelling a Fougère fragrance again, Roger & Gallet soap, what was that bath additive in childhood?

I tried it for the first time in Italy at Zhor Perfumes and it has never stopped being part of my life. . The best Oud and Rose combination very balanced! Such a gorgeous rose scent and the oud in it is so beautiful. The rose opens with a freshness and dries down to sweet and spicy notes. Although the oud is not loud, it serves as an anchor to the rose and other notes. It's so smooth and really rounds out the fragrance. Better wear in fall and winter. For secure try a sample first! For special moments not for everyday life!

The first impression of Mirach can initially be very off-putting for many. I smell a mix of medicine, mothballs, and citronella candles with a fruity rose water. However, once the initial shock fades, the rose becomes softer and softer. The oud comes through stronger, and a cozy, warm vanilla envelops the fragrance. A warm, rosy creaminess sets in. Initially very feminine, Mirach becomes increasingly masculine, and after 30 minutes of "enduring," a very beautiful, rounded rose-vanilla-oud scent emerges that can be worn by both men and women. Due to the certain heaviness of the fragrance, I would only wear it cautiously in everyday life and also use it for special occasions because of the price.

Mirach was once again a "blind swap" .... I opened the package with great anticipation, opened the beautiful golden box, and lifted out the stunning and heavy golden bottle. A truly beautiful bottle! Nose close... but I haven't smelled anything yet... it has to go on the skin ;-) I was very curious about this fragrance because the SAND intrigued me :-D Mirach starts on my skin fresh-spicy with a lot of neroli... fine saffron and spicy nutmeg... In the background, a shy but juicy red rose appears - very noble and somehow "crisp"... The opening seems a bit off-putting to me and slightly reminds me of those lemon candles you light in the summer to keep mosquitoes away... strange association, I know... Fortunately, the citrusy top note doesn't last too long... Slowly, warm oud and something "dull" creeps in... it almost feels muffled.... is that due to the mentioned sand? What does sand smell like exactly? Yes, somehow warm, "dull" and muffled, that's hard to define... but this slightly unfamiliar note is really beautiful.... Gradually, the oud becomes a bit stronger and the neroli pulls back slightly, which also chases away the "anti-mosquito thought" ;-) And from that moment on, Mirach starts to please me.... This happens on my skin about 30 min. after spraying it on.... What follows is a beautiful scent of the finest sandalwood, gentle spice, subtle resin, a generous portion of oud, and a very restrained rose that occasionally breaks through - all together with a "dull" and muffled finish.... I don't find Mirach sweet at all, as it has been described here in parts... It is not a "classic" oud-rose fragrance, no, Mirach is a bit more special... finely balanced ingredients with an emphasis on high-quality oud.... Mirach is not a mirage.... No, you get what you read... Sillage and longevity are TOP - really, you only need 1-2 sprays and it lasts ;-) For me, Mirach is absolutely unisex and wearable in any season... well done Paolo Terenzi :)

Back in late February (of 2025), I blind-bought Kilian's Angels' Share Paradis , a highly anticipated flanker of the brand's hero franchise Angels' Share Eau de Parfum . While the gap in ratings between the EDP and Paradis is insignificant for the Parfumo community, in the real world Paradis was a significant let-down that couldn't even get buzz after the brand invited two dozen influencers to the opening of their Milan boutique in late March and gave them all both bottles. And unfortunately, I feel like the end result won't be that different for Angels' Share on the Rocks as the EDP continues to rule the roost. The latest Angels' Share on the Rocks opens as a contrast between the signature DNA of the EDP (the sweet-spicy-boozy scent) and a very prominent citrusy-fruity contrast, primarily smelling like gourmand lemon. This specific lemon is the one that I recognize from Amouage's Outlands . That is to say the scent opens sweet-spicy-citrusy-gourmand. There is a very noteworthy lack of intensity in the spiciness, likely from a serious downsizing of the cinnamon note. This feels like a key discrepancy between the EDP and the OTR version. The aforementioned lemon note carries into the dry-down for a few hours I'd say, but the scent ultimately lands at the doorstep of the EDP version, just with a significantly lighter feel with noticeably weaker performance. When I compare my experience with Angels' Share on the Rocks in the 3 wears I've had with the listed notes, I'd say the primary notes here are the lemon and cognac with moderate ambers and mild cinnamon. For me, the listed aldehydes and the ice accord are hard to notice, but the oak is more evident when you go looking for it on the skin as the scent trends towards it into the latter stages of the dry-down. Unlike with the Paradis version, the weaknesses of Angels' Share on the Rocks aren't necessarily related to blending. A key negative of the OTR version is the performance: the EDP and Paradis both have strong openings into more moderate dry-downs while the OTR version opens below moderate and ends fairly weak. In some ways, it does feel like that was the goal as lightening the structure enabled the brand to sell a summer-wearable version of Angels' Share Eau de Parfum , much like Nishane did 2 years ago with Ani X . Relative to the original Angels' Share Eau de Parfum , the OTR version doesn't feature a single advantage outside of the aforementioned summer utility. With Paradis, albeit the final product lacked quality in the dry-down, the vision/idea was worth something. With Angels' Share on the Rocks , the idea is lazy and the execution doesn't have enough nuance to justify owning this version. Originally rated as a 7.5 before revising down to a 6.5 and now, in this November revisit back up to a 7.0, this version is average-to-good as a product, but largely off the back of the EDP's success. If you're interested in a summer wearable version of the EDP, give it a try. Otherwise, steer clear.

When I first sprayed this on my wrist I was stunned at how well it captured the scent of cognac on the rocks. Zingy citruses, spicy facets, and a beautiful realistic brandy. Unfortunately, about an hour or so later, it was all gone and I was left with Angels' Share Eau de Parfum -lite as the drydown. There's probably some chemical reason for it (or maybe a financial one) but for whatever reason, the richness of the original just isn't there. If the stunning opening could be somehow combined with the actual Angels' Share drydown, this would be a 10/10 for me.

Angel Share On The Rocks. Let me start off by saying don’t listen to the web. I’m a huge fan of the Angel Share DNA. When i heard of a fresher version coming out I was pumped to say the least. Then the internet started talking, people saying it’s a cash grab, it no diff then the OG, it’s redundant, it’s garbage ect. This is my thoughts on it. I tested all three flankers on my skin at the same time. On the rocks, the OG , and pardis. They all split and go separate ways imho but I can understand if you not the hugest fan of the dna they could be redundant but not to me or my nose. nnOG projects a lot and has the heavy Cinnamin sweetness and cognac. nnParadis has the fruits from the raspberry and it is beast mode just like the OG and lasts and projects but not as much of the cinimonn and heavy syrupy sweetness it’s the wife’s fave but not mine. After the dry down the raspberry starts to soften up and goes into the background. It Dosent disappear but it not as prodomint as the first hour or 2. nnThe on the rocks is amazing becuase of the versatility. I think it could be worn in the summer cuz the sweetness and nCinnamon is toned way down. Just don’t over spray. It freshens it up ALOT With the added orange, lemon and grapefruit notes. At first the opening is very fresh and pleasant to the nose with that OG DNA in the background but not hesvy at all. But you know it’s an angel share DNA. To my nose i can still pick up on the citrus hours later and the freshness stays around It won’t project like the other two but it’s not soposed to. It’s still Is leaving a nice big scent bubble around me. It’s going on 6 hours and it’s still really strong. I’m very pleased with it, if You give it a shot wear It and see how it develops for you after a few hours before you make a decision. But if you love the OG DNA I think you would like this one too, with the ability to wear it more often and easier. nnIt’s. Win for me.

Boozy scents are generally related to cold seasons, and Kilian is really courageous to try for the hot climates because she has a really solid, famous background: Original Angel's Share. The opening has refreshing citrusy notes but not as clear and intense as Renaissance from Xerjoff. Then the slightly boozy cinnamon has visited my nose and brain. Then the scent says goodbye with tonka and woody notes... if you live in a hot climate dominated city as I do and like spicy-warm fragrances, then I recommend a try to this.

I try the new flanker of Angel share and I was surprised that is similar with less known state of mind secret of succes, so from my side nothing new in this formula . On my skin it stayed like 3 hrs so again same problem with performance , and it is incredible that same DNA on previous mentioned perfume last at least 5-6 hrs. So another well announced release without bringing something new in smell and also in improving perfomances .

Almost a year ago, an employee at Killian told me about the rumors surrounding this fragrance. I was curious for months... Now I could test it and I have to say: On my skin, turbo crap! First impressively fresh with wow factor. After 30 minutes, the normal Angels Share comes in with a teenage identity crisis.

This morning I woke up and immediately felt that strange mix of restlessness and anticipation. The city outside was still quiet, only the distant honking of a bus and the chirping of birds filled the streets. I didn’t know exactly why, but something told me that today would be a special day.

With an Old Fashioned in hand, Kilian follows the headlines at the end of 2024: While Dior boosts sales with its successful extraits, Kilian's latest fragrance leaves many indifferent - just like the Lattafa kitchens.

When I heard about a summer flanker of my favorite scent, I had been on the lookout for that one summer fragrance for so long, and it was hyped like never before for an upcoming release. After the first spray right after the arrival of my sample, this hype initially transformed into boundless joy, because I have rarely had such a beautiful scent under my nose.
Can someone tell me what ice, meaning frozen water, smells like? Or how to create a cooling effect without it actually being cold? In any case, this has worked here!

I have been hesitant to write this review, because I love the house of Kilian despite the Lauder takeover. No matter how many times I have tried this fragrance, no matter the temperature, the result is the same. Initially Old Fashioned smells great, but the performance is almost embarrassing. It struggles to hold on to that first impression that draws you in and doesn't evolve well, which was mournfully disappointing. Something is severely lacking from this composition. Whiskey perhaps? Kilian's Old Fashioned sits in the shadows of Apple Brandy. A failed release, that had great potential in my opinion, but hopeful for Angels Share Paradis.

Yes, it's similar to Single Malt London, but it's differences can still be celebrated. I was a fan of SML, and I'm a fan of OF. It starts out similar with a strong, boozy Scotch whiskey, but with out all the strong plum sweetness we got with SML. I appreciate this change making it less sweet and more bitter like your typical old fashioned. I get a slightly sweet licorice with a basalmic floral, mixed with an amber-like wheat. It dries down to a confident cedar that's had a few drinks, mimicking the aroma of an aging barrel. Average performance, but an overall win in my book.

It was the running rumor for weeks (if not months) prior to the launch of Old Fashioned that the fragrance was a re-release of the well-regarded but now discontinued Single Malt London . While I am here to stamp those rumors as being true, I am also here to stamp that the re-release is unable to match the highs of the past. The funny part about when you first put on Single Malt London is that the scent doesn't instantly waft and the same thing happens here with Old Fashioned , but once the scent hits your nose, it is undebatable that the scent tries to reimagine Single Malt London . The structure retains the sweet-spicy DNA in the opening, but it is missing the sensational plum compote opening of Single Malt London as the fruitiness isn't that evident, instead smelling a bit closer to apple (if there's any fruitiness to begin with). The base and the evolution differ substantially. The original Single Malt London is built upon medicinal ambers with mild woody nuances. Contrast that to Old Fashioned which is mainly built on a dry woody and boozy smell with the woodiness offering a very realistic oak barrel type of smell. The aforementioned ambers never appear with Old Fashioned and as such, the overlap in not identical. The structures of both feature warm spiciness as a leading accord, but Single Malt London has more fruitiness both in the open and throughout the wearing cycle. This review was originally written on the 30th of August 2024 when Old Fashioned just came out. I subsequently sold my bottle for a strong price, meaning I didn't lose $ even after buying it for full retail (since Kilian adds travel sizes to their orders). In the summer of 2025, I managed to acquire full bottles of both Apple Brandy New York and Single Malt London . As of the 23rd of August 2025 when I am writing this revision, Single Malt remains the superior product, but I feel like the dry-down of Old Fashioned actually smells more like Apple Brandy New York which has a similar woody-boozy dry-down. For those who haven't experienced Single Malt, I'd say Old Fashioned will only get you in the ballpark of the original product and for anybody seeking the superior product, this is unfortunately not that. nulltheless, it smells significantly different to Kilian's current catalogue and is worth a look, esp. with product occasionally trading for 50% of retail.

With the name "Old Fashioned," I might have expected a fougère or vetiver, but certainly not such a sweet, luscious gourmand... But I probably just completely forgot about the famous cocktail of the same name, which is much closer to the essence. As a whiskey fan, I should give that a try again... Kilian's "Old Fashioned" is definitely a juicy powerhouse. Especially the top note is a little grenade, boozy and bombastic. Whiskey, cake vibes, heavy yeast, dessert nails with heads. And burst buttons. Kilian doesn't hold back. It's catchy, it's aggressive, in your face, it might even overwhelm and scare some people. Sugary, textural, imaginative. A cinematic experience at full steam. Between chocolate factory and whiskey barrel, between cocktail bar and leather case, between pirate prose and pony farm. Hay, no shyness. Beefy, brutal, one has to be careful that no one thinks you have a hangover. The sweetest and most luxurious hangover of all time. Viscous and completely niche. Even more drastic and steamy than 99% of the Tom Ford lineup. Truly a balsamic bombshell. Crème brûlée champion. Bottle: big, thick, chic Sillage: very pronounced Longevity: 10 hours and up Conclusion: a knockout aperitif and dessert of the most gourmand kind. Between whiskey, cake, top hat, and aftershave. Not old-fashioned at all.

I would claim that fate led me to "Old Fashioned | Kilian." My last name is "Smiljic," and it was two weeks ago that I researched my name and came across the explanation that in the Yugoslav language, immortelle is translated as "smilje," and apparently, the people who processed these plants as herbal traders were given the nickname "Smiljani," which ultimately led to my last name. Also, two weeks ago, I wanted to order a gift for my sister from Kilian Paris, and the choice fell on "Angels' Share | Kilian." Since I could choose two samples, I was quite surprised when Old Fashioned was suggested to me purely by chance, featuring the ingredient immortelle. "Old fashioned" somehow fits me too, as I would describe myself as a man of the old school. For those who need proof, I am 31 years old, it is the year 2024, and I still do not have online banking; instead, I walk to the bank every month to manually obtain bank statements and make transfers. I expected a scent that smells like my grandparents' apartment. The old man smell of my grandfather has been etched in my brain to this day, when he came back from carp fishing and heartily grabbed my cheeks with his slippery fish hands, giving me a grandfatherly kiss as a greeting. Fortunately, the scent differs from this experience, but still a bit differently than expected. As part of "The Liquors" fragrance line, the start is nearly perfect. An authentically strong whiskey note hits my nose so hard that I would advise anyone against spraying this scent just before a police traffic stop. But as much as I enjoy this initial alcohol charge as an eternal non-drinker, the further development is rather sobering. The whiskey doesn’t linger long, and the scent moves in a creamy/floral direction, which I can't find much to appreciate. Somewhat unspectacular and boring. Given the whiskey note, it doesn't surprise me that 67 percent of the 106 users on Parfumo are male, but at least the creamy/floral part definitely has unisex potential. Regarding performance, the scent also leans more towards the word "old" and doesn't show much endurance. I could perceive four sprays on my neck for four hours. The bottle is a dream and fits perfectly for a scent from "The Liquors" line. I wouldn't be surprised if someone wanted to take a hearty sip from the bottle. Probably the biggest criticism would be the price. 245 euros for 50ml. You have to let that sink in like good whiskey. The bottle may justify this price, but all other aspects of the scent definitely do not. The scent makes me understand why, despite my name's meaning, I did not become a herbalist or plant trader. I hope that my second sample in the form of "Angels' Share | Kilian" can excite me more.

It's Sunday, a quiet afternoon in Ginza, Tokyo. Old gentlemen are playing cards in a dusty whiskey lounge. The sun shines through darkened windows, bathing the room in red light. I'm trying to stay awake with coffee, but even that isn't helping. How about something new? Among all the expensive whiskey bottles, I discover something unusual... Choya plum wine?

Old Fashioned is a fragrance that tells completely different stories on paper and skin. Sprayed on paper, the scent initially conveys a strong alcoholic impression, reminiscent of the morning after a lively house party when one is clearing away half-full drink cups.

Old Fashioned by Kilian is a fragrance that impresses with its surprising scent development and depth, serving as a unique homage to the classic whisky cocktail. The scent arrived as a sample from an online order, and I didn't expect much since I generally don't like fragrances with alcoholic notes. However, I was pleasantly surprised.

During a weekend trip to Lyon, we inevitably made a detour to the Galeries Lafayette. Old Fashioned had only been on the market for a few weeks at that time, so it was impossible to overlook its presentation in the perfume department. I had already been made aware of the fragrance through social media, so I took a test strip and sprayed it on.

At first, it smelled just as I had hoped - a strong initial whisky/cognac note. Then it becomes - for me - too woody too quickly, and the wheat becomes very prominent. I also perceive the already frequently described plum note. Overall, it's a nice scent, unisex & elegant, but nothing that stands out enormously and unfortunately also lacks good longevity.

Summer is over, yet I still have a review for a fragrance that best suits the warm season: Cabiria from the Anniversari line. A line that is extremely expensive and comes in a hefty packaging. A large box, when opened, shines an LED on the golden part of the lid. It already seems very decadent, even if it probably isn't that costly to produce. From this line, I also own the "Burdèl | Tiziana Terenzi," which leans towards Alexandria II. Here, this fragrance is indicated as similar to "Kirkè (Extrait de Parfum) | Tiziana Terenzi." These fragrances are quite distant but go in a similarly fruity-floral direction, though they don't remind me of this bestseller from the same house in terms of DNA. Price-wise, it must be said that the RRP is somewhat cheeky, like many niche fragrances. Currently, 100ml has an RRP of €415. No way, in my opinion, this price is totally inflated and is possibly worth more like half that. Fortunately, it should be noted that the internet prices for Terenzi fragrances are usually between 50 and 70% below the RRP, which often reflects the real value of the fragrances quite well. Cabiria is a fresh-fruity fragrance, where floral notes also unfold after some time, along with the usual musk base. What I particularly like about this fragrance is the wonderful cheerful fruity top note, which lasts a long time. Juicy summer fruit, especially melon, with a fantastic authentic apple note. There’s also a slightly grassy green freshness that simply lifts the mood and fits best with radiant sunshine. Pear and blackcurrant are somewhat overshadowed but may play a part in this wonderful fruity top note. After about an hour, floral notes come into play. Fresh rose & jasmine create a lovely pleasant fresh-floral heart note that beautifully complements the fruity notes. Some heavier heliotrope notes also come in, but they harmonize well with this rather summery creation. The base consists of clean musk, vanilla, and soft woods. You have to be okay with the musk base, which leans towards Kirke and Erba Pura. Here, however, it’s not as overpowering due to the gentle vanilla and sensual wood notes. Overall, it is beautifully soft without having a weak sillage. Performance is, as usual, very Terenzi-like. For this price, you get quite a lot if performance means a lot to you. Specifically, the fruity-floral part is very strong, and the longevity should easily surpass the 10-hour mark. Overall, a great unisex fragrance with this typical Terenzi signature. Due to the floral notes, it may be too feminine for some, but anyone interested in fruity-floral can wear this if it suits their type. Versatile in terms of occasion due to the relatively fresh DNA. Also wearable year-round, thanks to the heavier notes in the base. All in all, a great alternative to fragrances like Kirke. Those who roughly like this style could find an alternative here. I think the melon opening is fantastic, and the further development is pure Italian joy of life. Worth it, especially at the price between €150-170.

Looking at the fragrance notes, I didn't really expect anything extremely new. Since I have already smelled many fruity fragrances, many from the same house, Cabiria didn't really appeal to me. The fragrance Cabiria starts with the fruity Terenzi DNA, except for a few fragrance notes. However, quite early on, Cabiria does differ from many other fruity fragrances. In the top notes, I can most strongly detect blackcurrant, apple, grassy notes, and a bit of pear. Mint and melon get a bit lost for me. The grassy notes give the fragrance a rather unique direction. Then, in the course, floral notes emerge, with jasmine being the most prominent. Generally, all the floral notes are quite rounded; none stands out, and even the rose remains very subtle and does not dominate. They are not overly bright and strongly floral. In the drydown, there are some woody notes that are very soft and hardly noticeable, as well as vanilla and musk. Overall, Cabiria is a very fruity fragrance with a slightly woody drydown and sweet notes throughout. The green notes from the grass make a huge difference compared to other fruity fragrances. Combined with the blackcurrant, it fits very well, giving the fragrance a fresh quality. It is worth highlighting that Cabiria has really good quality for a fruity fragrance. I have no associations with hairspray here. Also, there is not much synthetic quality; compared to Kirke, for example, I find Cabiria to be significantly better in quality. Also, in comparison with Kirke, which I personally find way too sweet, I would wear Cabiria myself. This fragrance is more unisex to my nose. Due to the green notes, this fragrance is versatile, as this sweetness gets a counterbalance, preventing the fragrance from becoming endlessly sweet. Many of these fragrances that remind me of fruit cocktails are often scents I prefer for vacation. However, because of these green notes, I wouldn't categorize Cabiria there; rather, they make it a fruity fragrance that can also be worn quite well in everyday life. Cabiria stands in the shadow of other fruity fragrances for me; it is not marketed as intensely. When I think of fruity fragrances, many other scents come to mind. I really like it, but I probably wouldn't have tested it if it hadn't been given to me at a souk. Most people will likely not test it. Unfortunately, it is also a bit more expensive compared to the well-known fruity scent from the house, Kirke. Longevity and sillage The longevity is extremely good. This perfume lasts all day without any problems. The sillage, however, is not too extreme, but it is very noticeable. Conclusion I really liked Cabiria. A slightly different fruity fragrance with great quality. Unfortunately, it is also a bit more expensive, but compared to the Sea Star collection from Terenzi, it is a fruity fragrance with a more affordable price and a somewhat unique DNA. It belongs to the newer fragrances and may gain a bit more attention in the future.

Cabiria has been in my collection since yesterday. It was once again a typical blind buy for me. The price was simply too good to resist. I can immediately reassure all the haters of Kirkè, for me, Cabiria is much less sweet and does not have the hairspray note that many always fear. Of course, the typical fruity and sweet Tiziana Terenzi DNA cannot be completely absent here, but it has been used very gently and cautiously. I can identify the following notes in Cabiria: A green grass note, where I would rather describe it as the scent of grass on a slightly cooler summer morning where there is still a bit of dew on the blades of grass and the sun is slowly starting to warm the ground. An apple note can also be recognized, although it reminds me more of apple blossoms, which could certainly be influenced by the other notes of Cabiria for me. I cannot perceive a melon at all. The mint is very faint, where I rather smell a slightly sweeter spearmint. The blackcurrant note is very prominent for me. I also liked it very much in Bleecker Street . The heart note is rather floral fruity and represents a change from the top note. This pulls Cabiria in another direction after about an hour. I can recognize all the floral notes, with jasmine dominating here, followed by rose and the rather weak heliotrope. Fortunately, I could not detect amber. The base note does not really reveal itself to me. I can only recognize vanilla and musk here. The woody notes are completely absent. For me, the floral aspect remains present in the base note, combined with the fruity top note. I must also say that Cabiria is quite similar to Moro di Venezia , although Cabiria is significantly less floral and truly perfect unisex. Actually, you don’t necessarily need both perfumes, although I find Cabiria a bit more suitable for a man and truly see it as a 50/50 unisex scent. The longevity leaves nothing to be desired; even after 10 hours, I could still faintly smell Cabiria. The sillage is a bit over an arm's length for 2-3 hours and then gradually returns to a sillage under an arm's length. Cabiria was only close to my skin after about 8 hours. The MSRP is, of course, set too high again, but with a 50% discount, the price is in a reasonable range. For me, Cabiria is another very successful creation, even though I would have appreciated a bit more uniqueness.

Roses on Ice is weird and unique aquatic fresh scent which is like Gin Tonic made of Hendricks Gin with Cucumbers and rose water in it. It sounds weird but it’s very beautiful and addictive, interesting as well which is not the right word to describe the most of the fresh and aquatic scents. Roses On Ice doesn’t smell clearly alcohol and if you know the difference between normal, original GT and Hendricks with cucumbers you get the idea of this scent (It’s my favorite drink btw). You just have to add rose water made of baby pink petals. The base of this scent is clean white musky and the texture of the scent gets a bit thicker in the drydown thanks to Sandalwood. Anyway, it’s not creamy in any kind of way. Thank you for reading and I hope you liked my compact review. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more

My husband surprised me with a bottle a few weeks ago and I was taken aback by the strong cucumber scent. It’s so fresh and invigorating, at first I thought it was for a man. He smells roses, but I can’t smell any rose whatsoever. I don’t know what’s wrong with my nose, because all I can smell is glorious cucumber and gin. I love wearing this perfume day or night. It’s a happy, lighthearted scent that I think might take some time for some people to appreciate. It’s absolutely nothing like Angels’ Share! That’s like comparing apples to oranges. The only thing in common is the maker, the beautiful glass bottle, and that they’re both beautiful perfumes. And this perfume doesn’t project too far, so I would consider this only a skin scent. It lasts 4 to 5 hours (at least in the winter). I’ll revise this review once worn in the heat.

I have spent like a year spraying this fragrance everytime I go to the store, but I finally pulled the trigger. I see it's apparently not for everyone based on the comments but I find this to be a great spring/summer scent. The cucumber and juniper berry gives me distinct gin and tonic, but the cucumber also evokes nostalgia for my middle school years when I doused myself in B&BW Cucumber Melon body spray and lotion. Though the cucumber note here lasts around for the full duration of wear, I find the juniper berries give way to a sort of unique rose. The rose gives me the feeling of poutperie or dried rose petals floating in a bowl of water. There's something simultaneously diffuse, blurry and watery about this rose. It is not a crisp rose but neither is it heavy. Some may call it musty, but I wouldn't go that far. Performance is average. About 5 hours on skin, a little longer on clothes but not much. Also worth noting I adore the packaging. That bottle, the green juice...I love everything about it. For me, Roses on Ice is a real winner and a lovely, refreshing spring/summer freshie.

What a blast of green freshness in the top! Zesty lemon lime, with a hint of cucumber and a green rose in the far background. Similar to the rose used in something like ToyBoy but waaaay softer and way lighter. Despite the name, rose is not prominent at all Soon a bitter herbal alcoholic note becomes present - I believe that's the note of Gin, an alcoholic beverage made of juniper berries. This explains the green foresty vibe it gets after some time As with Apple brandy, I don't get alcoholic notes. This is even less boozy To put it into a picture: A couple of roses inside a dark forest in a cold winter night - cold, herbal and just every so slightly floral. Beautifully executed. Performance is average - kind of expected for this kind of scent profile. Definitely a summery scent for warm and hot weather. This DNA is usually on the quieter side of things. I would have hoped for a bit stronger sillage, especially in the beginning

Roses on Ice kicks off with a semi-aquatic profile of crisp cucumber and a bright lime note. It is indeed quite a cold feeling, juicy, with a spicy finish thanks to that cucumber. It is a heavy weighting to that note early on, so be prepared. Beyond that, juniper and rose start to come up from the heart early on, and will only grow in strength as we move forward. Very much a gin-like aroma with tonic carbonation, super boozy in its presentation. After some time, the cucumber note will fade. Juniper and rose take the top, with a growing strength of sandalwood and a general muskiness. Roses on Ice isn’t all that complex. In the end, I get a generally chilled scent with a heavier weighting towards the juniper, musk, and the lingering rose. It really is exactly how it is described by Kilian. So, if you can imagine that impression in your mind, you have a close idea of what this perfume is all about.

I love this perfume a lot. It's refreshing and its sillage is just perfect. A little on the strong side if you want to wear it to a closed space such as the office or a coffee shop, but the scent is very safe and unlikely to offend any noses, so I'd say go for it. While I'd regard it as a safe scent, I'd also say it's not your typical scent.

I got samples of this and Angels’ Share from my Kilian ambassador right after attending the launching webinar. I fell in love with AS immediately but not the Roses on Ice. It starts out quite refreshing without the strong citrus that I usually dislike so I thought I would love it but oh no...I can’t stand the strong cucumber note.

Sampling the other offering from the new By Kilian liquors duo, Roses on Ice, which is based on a gin note, with fragrant notes of cucumber, rose juniper, and sandalwood per the Kilian website, and additional notes of lime, sandalwood, and musk per other sources.

This is a weird scent. The first thing I thought of when sampling it in the boutique was The Body Shop's Cucucmber shower gel my daughter used to get years ago. Considering it's price I don't want to be smelling like a cucumber, nor like a washed teenager... In the opening it is all about the watery cucumbers.

“Roses On Ice” perfectly captures its theme. “Cucumber On Ice” would have been even more fitting, but it just doesn’t sound as cool. However, this doesn’t change the class of this olfactory luxury cocktail, even if cucumber is certainly not as romantic and sexy as the rose… or, if you think about it in a precise and slightly naughty way, maybe it is…?

Is the perfume simple? Yes, but that's not a negative thing, it just means it's a common one. It is aquatic with aromatic, brackish, ozonic and functional characteristics. The opening reminds common deodorants as if it were the smell of things that we feel in our day to day. The perfume is initially a somewhat spicy mix, with the presence of coriander and cardamom. The transition to drying gradually incorporates rhubarb with lily of the valley and a slightly spongy oak moss. Added to this is a good dose of ambroxan, which is popular with the general public. Drying has an herbal aromatic freshness that reminds me of Cipresso di Toscana. In my opinion the fragrance is a very trivial aromatic with a smell that reminds me of deodorants and washing powder. It's not exactly an unpleasant aroma, but with this proposal there are many perfumes that do the trick at a much lower cost. If you ask me what perfume it looks like I would say it resembles: Legend and Percival. Due to its more relaxed vibe, I think it is a fragrance for hot climates (spring/summer). I find it ideal to be used in everyday life with casual clothes. The fixation on my skin lasts around 8 hours and the projection is average. The scent is light, soft, fresh, luminous, masculine, casual, youthful and ordinary.

Scentrack: Richard Cheese – Gin and Juice Good vodka is odorless and devoid of any taste, thus in my opinion, creating a vodka-based fragrance is a challenging task. One has to recreate the essence of this East European drink without obvious ethanol smell that consumers rate as cheap. It seems, the perfumer solved this problem by introducing some spicy and herbal element to the composition. Vodka on the Rocks opens with the pale whiteness of aldehydes accompanied by some pepper, strong coriander and herbal cardamom. The initial blast tenders gradually to washed flowers accord, delicate by design yet strong in performance. This fresh, futuristic bouquet is paired to very nice rhubarb note. All the interplay notes morphs to gray base of Ambroxan and something similar to white musk, which gradually lose their intensity. Does Vodka on the Rocks remind me of real vodka? Yes, but just on one brand. Polish vodka Žubrowka, infused with bison grass, and very distinct herbal qualities, which was prohibited by the FDA until 2010 due to its coumarin content. Additionally, the herbal aspects of this composition reminds of several G&T-inspired fragrances. The performance of the composition is average (5-7 hours) with moderate sillage. In conclusion, Vodka on the Rocks, is a solid recreation of vodka atmosphere. However, it lacks distinctiveness of the other By Kilian offerings. Personally, it is not my cup of tea, but one who wishes to wear a fresh herbal/alcohol combo could appreciate this fragrance even more. Still, the main question remains - is it proper to drink vodka with ice?

I was actually excited when this scent was announced. The theme was intriguing (Vodka on the Rocks). I saw the interview Mr. Hennessy did about this scent and he said he was trying to achieve the feeling of vodka (which has no scent) being chilled by ice. Sounds great so far right? How was he going to achieve this feat? The idea was to use "cooling" spices (cardamom being a big player in this one) to create that illusion for your olfactive senses. I was on board totally. Wound up blind buying this one actually as a result. Time to find out if the "blind buy" roulette came back to bite me in the end. The Smell: You look at the note breakdown after watching that interview and you're expecting magic right? true to his word, cardamom was the major player in this one and, if you close your eyes while smelling it, you can trick yourself into seeing the illusion of a "cooling effect." We have "the rocks" part of the title covered. The thing is this fragrance gave me another smell. One that isn't on the note breakdown but probably would have been more effective at achieving that cooling effect - eucalyptus. Every time I smell this scent now, I cannot get that smell out of my head even though I know it's the illusion created by the spices. The florals are there to help tone the spices down a bit and smooth the fragrance out but when I sniff it as I write this, it actually stings the nose a bit. Instead of providing an artistic, fun illusion, it's straight up assault on my olfactory nerve. Coriander, I suspect, is the guilty party here. It's sad because I was expecting the magic but I feel like the "illusion" was ultimately dispersed and left in its place was disappointment. It's also very linear and doesn't change much. Rating: 5/10 Projection: Not the best, not the worst. The first 3 hours of wearing it, it was fairly decent. After that, it's a skin scent. I own two other by Kilian scents and neither one of them are projection beasts but they linger for a very long time. This one lingers but I feel like it just disappears after 6-8 hours. Might be my skin but it even left my clothing around the same time as well. Kilian even says most of his scents are meant to draw people closer and I agree that this should be the goal. You just better hope it happens within that 3-5 hour mark. Rating: 6/10 Price: On luckyscent (where I get most of my niche stuff), it's $240 USD for 50 mL ($4.80 per mL). Not terrible but the price tag doesn't match what you ultimately pay for when you get this fragrance. Rating: 4/10 Versatility: I can see how this can work in a variety of scenarios. Dates, special occasions, or just going to have a good time are all viable options here. The problem for me was that it was very cloying in warm weather. The spices felt like they were dialed up and I was in a rush to scrub it off of me. Cooler weather was where this really shined for me. I've worn it to work and class and it was not ideal. Not saying it doesn't work but it's not the best scenario for me. Rating: 8/10 Final Rating: 5.8/10. When I look back at my original review on this, I was a bit more generous on the scent because I held out hope that there was something I was missing. There had to be a mistake with my nose or something. The more I wore it, the more rigid my belief was that this fragrance is just simple and missed the mark on what it tried to achieve in my opinion. Interesting concept but the execution was lacking something. Definitely worth a sample but I can't say that I'd buy it again. I'm a fan of several by Kilian scents and I have a ton of samples from them. I've learned my lesson on blind buying and will test those samples 'til the last drop. Cheers.

It opens with an enormous blast of ambroxan and aldehydes, sharp and bold, immediately followed by the unmistakable tang of alcohol. As it settles, it dries down to a warm, spicy, and woody base, with a skin-like effect that feels incredibly intimate. The scent is super peppery, with a strong coriander presence that adds an extra layer of spice. This fragrance is undeniably masculine, exuding that quintessential "men's cologne" vibe. It's perfect for a casual, everyday wear. However, it's just not my thing. Not my cup of tea... I mean... not my cup of vodka!

Kilian is a brand for me with some decent to good fragrances, a whole lot of below-average to flopped scents, and so far, the big highlights have eluded me. Nevertheless, I have been following the "Alcohol Series" with interest. Not necessarily from the perspective of a "later consumer," but rather from the technical side, meaning, how well/authentic have they executed it!? With Single Malt, that has turned out quite well. With Vodka on the Rocks, the comparison is much harder, as I don't have any vodka at home and I can't even remember the last time I actually drank vodka... despite the martial advertising... it never appealed to me... except back in the day as a regular club-goer with Vodka-Bull... which, in hindsight, was actually a perverse mix... based on the advertising, I now know why I don't have a pure soul;-)! As for the scent, yes, it starts off alcoholically clear, slightly medicinally sharp-stinging and bitter in character. Interesting, but anything but a nose-pleaser. More of a smell than a perfume, an overdose of Ambroxan and a few lab flowers enhance the impression of sterility and harsh synthetics. Whether that's the case, I don't know, but the scent feels that way. As it develops, the fragrance continues to flatten out, taking on a typical men's shower gel spice mix, but without the obligatory "marine" touch. It somehow feels like low-budget mainstream à la Ralph Lauren, Calvin Klein, Paco Rabanne, or Boss... not really bad, but for over €200, it's downright cheeky. During the scent's progression, Vodka on the Rocks repeatedly reminded me strongly of Fierce by A&F and Sauvage by Dior, so not exactly the most pleasant nose-pleasers either. The very last remnants of the scent quickly disappear, leaving the entire field to Ambrox01, which smells of artificial freshness with a slight woody note... that's it! Conclusion: Although I am a marketing victim (everything has to look nice first, then be practical), the bottles are still the most beautiful in the perfume world for me, I won't fall for this deceptive packaging, even if this trick of "great exterior, little content" is found in many areas of life and often "works" there. For €30-40, I wouldn't say anything, but as it stands, I am very annoyed by the fuss with so little fragrance. The longevity is good at 6-7 hours, the sillage is decent and still office-appropriate. The scent can be worn year-round and is for me 70:30 masculine.

Well, the question of which vodka it is now is hard to answer. It is not a clear little water like "Belvedere" or "Grey Goose," nor is it a floral fruity one like "Karneval" or "Ciroc." One thing is clear, it is pure, noble, and tells a story. So it is not a cheap vodka, and that would be outrageous given the price.

Today something very unusual from me. I am writing a comment even though this fragrance is not yet in my possession. I had the opportunity to test it yesterday during a visit, and it left a lasting impression. The opening is strong, dominant, and possessive. Almost a bit too much of a good thing.
