Season: More suitable for colder days, but also wearable on cooler summer nights Age: Not necessarily for teenagers, but suitable for both younger and older wearers Occasion: Despite the unisex declaration, for me it is more of a men’s fragrance.
That 'having too much of a good thing can be wonderful' was already known by Mae West. On the other hand, 'too many cooks spoil the broth,' as the saying goes.

"Cruel Intentions" is not a revolution, but rather an extremely fine evolution, as the saying goes. A very good foundation already exists in this regard. This is more or less intentionally represented by Yves Saint Laurent's "M7" and its sexy, sensual refinement.

First of all, a "Hello" to the community and a little anecdote. I jumped right into my first scent comments, starting with my rating, under the vague assumption that I was moving in the veil of anonymity.

Woodiness is not an accord that I experience with this perfume at all. This is very white and yellow florals and soapy with a touch of sweetness on me, like a bar of soap. I find this pretty dense and mature actually like a grandma version of Valaya almost. The performance is good! Lasts on skin and clothes for quite some time and remains this heavy clean floral scent.

Notes: Bergamot, Cinnamon, Anise, Honey, Vanilla, and Patchouli Perfumer: Pascal Gaurin Gold Knight opens with Bergamot and Cinnamon, I also get an menthol vibe in the opening which goes away quickly. The major of this fragrance "Honey" comes oozing in and takes over the other notes combined with Anise and Vanilla, these 2 notes amp up the sweetness even more. Finally Patchouli in the drydown, the notes of Patchouli is toned down and blended perfectly along with Honey, you are still able to detect the earthy nuances of Patchouli and this controls the sweetness of this fragrance, if that makes sense ????. Overall a sexy and seductive scent which will stay with you throughout the day.

Rich, delectable honey slathered over vanilla beans and sprinkled sparsely with anise. No matter how deep we get into this composition, the focal point will always be honey but it evolves beautifully. All of the animalic facets that honey often provides are vacant here, but in its place is a somewhat herbaceous sweetness that comes off very natural. Most reviewers have not acknowledged the bergamot. While it is not a key note here, it does play an important role when it comes to contrast. The bergamot is a dim light that gradually brightens the longer it wears. There is also a not so obvious patchouli that whispers in the background. I will not speak of redundancies between Gold Knight and Back To Black, because while they both involve honey they are not at all the same fragrance. Back To Black is the dark knight with an unapologetic presence. Gold Knight is kinder, brighter and softer to my nose. Brothers, with much in common but enough differences that they stand apart. The Cain & Abel of the fragrance world. Gold Knight (Abel) is sadly discontinued, while Back To Black is still available at specific retailers.

The movements to Gold Knight could be described like a tempo instruction for a piano player – honey, honey, patch, anise, honey, patch, patch, hay! The strands of the music seem very separate at first - there is a brief moment at the start when all you smell is a whipped honey product, pale and moussey, and the next all you can smell is the pungent mustiness of a patchouli so earthy you suspect it comes decked out with a full 1970s bush. The minty anise flips the switch here, drawing out the booze and the rich, immortelle-like grassiness of the patch, and roughing up the honey with its weird medicinal edge. I am not sure about the anise, to be honest, at least not at first. It almost smells too spicy, like those really strong varieties of mint or basil that taste like Scandinavian licorice. There is also a strong aftershavey undertone to it for the first hour, which puts me off. But eventually it mellows out into an aromatic, anisic whole – a grassy patchouli, with hints of dark chocolate, smelling for all we know like tobacco. For a honey-themed fragrance from the same brand that did Back to Black, I am surprised (and encouraged) by the absence of baby powder and cheap sweets. The honey remains strongly present throughout, but there’s not a hint of either syrup or dried saliva; it is a rich but light and true take on the note. That anise is key to everything. It makes everything smell like the aromatic undergrowth along a meadow, half-green, half-burnt gold. Gold Knight is an aromatic, quite dark or roughened patchouli, against which the ‘ochre’ notes of hay, honey, and minty herbs flicker like sudden shafts of sunlight. It is quite a simple, monolithic smell until you put your nose directly up against your skin and you smell a golden liqueur, like a shot of mead.

So far only one comment, very different statements... Rating is quite okay but not super good.... What should one do with that? Nothing at all. Just look (or better said, not remind oneself) and try the scent. After 3 days of training, I had to briefly visit the local perfume flagship in the pretty sleepy but very expensive shop-filled Baden-Baden at least at the end. Without a specific goal, just to look and smell. I actually wanted to sniff "Straight To Heaven Extreme," but it wasn't available. So Gold Knight ended up on the strip. Quite sweet, not really my target... "That will become a bit less sweet soon." Strip set aside, sniffed something else. Picked up the strip again. Hmm, interesting. Must go on the skin. Said and done, waited a bit, bought on 1/2 risk, as it was still quite sweet. After some time, I was pleased with my good purchase, as I really like it. Yes, it starts sweet. Honey? Yes, maybe, could also be beeswax, but that is related. The vanilla blends with it and doesn't stand out alone. In the background, however, there is more, and that gets exciting. The anise note or as written here a few times, licorice, is indeed noticeable, but subtle and also integrated. After a while, the prominent sweetness fades and the sillage decreases significantly. I even find it rather subtle for a relatively sweet scent. But what is most interesting to me is the overall impression of the fragrance that reveals itself after about 30 minutes. A very non-aggressive and non-sticky sweetness, for me more beeswax than honey, lies on a soft but quite dry bed. Patchouli is probably responsible for that, but I am uncertain about the classification of the base. I think I smell a bit of tobacco and even thought of very fine leather (not the usually rather strong direction of the well-known leather scents). The brain clearly points to the role of patchouli, but the heart says it is something else. Sometimes it smells like soft wood, then tobacco (flower), and sometimes fine leather. Maybe the anise/licorice part also plays a role in the whole that one doesn't directly notice? In any case, everything works very harmoniously, softly, and pleasantly. This harmonious and not entirely easy-to-classify overall impression lasts quite long, about 6 hours. Then mainly the beeswax takes over, and the scent loses some complexity. For me, Gold Knight is a positive surprise. The sweetness appears very universally acceptable to me and is wonderfully embedded in the base. A sweet scent that I will definitely wear to work because it is noticeable but doesn't fill the room. And probably won't clash either. I felt somewhat reminded of "Field Notes From Paris," which I also like. There, beeswax, tonka, and tobacco play the main roles on patchouli, but it somehow feels completely different despite the relationship.

Great, very warm and cozy scent that has everything a distinctive fragrance needs. It has that special something that piques curiosity and makes you want to sniff it a second and third time, because it feels familiar yet is newly combined and not immediately recognizable or overpowering. For me, it's a scent that fits nicely with a man in cool jeans, a casual shirt, and a knitted scarf, paired with rugged boots. A man with whom you want to spend the evening in a cozy cabin by the fire, enjoying hot chocolate or tea, and a delicious heavy red wine. However, I also see it on a suit-wearing man, as it has an elegant quality and a fragrance can also be contrasting/create tension. For me, it's a great scent also for confident women. The honey and vanilla emphasize the feminine side while simultaneously having something powerful and cheerful from the bergamot.

The 2nd Act of the Kilian scent journey takes me into the kingdom of the golden knights. I received 20ml of this noble brew and could hardly wait to test it. GK is rather one of the lesser-known and underestimated fragrances in the Kilian line. It is more of a warm, soft scent and the complete opposite of Intoxicated.

Long Story short I love the scent, but the price...... I was able to smell it for the first time today and what can I say....Love at first sniff. I smelled it and I wanted it. Then I remembered, however, that it is not a designer fragrance from Versace, which is well made and reasonably priced. It smells super luxurious and high-quality.

In 2019, a Kilian Sample Set accompanied me through the initial discoveries of the niche world. One of the samples was "Gold Knight | Kilian," which was less accessible to me at the time than some other fragrances that snuck directly into my heart. This was mainly due to one note, the anise.

As a very big fan and lover of the Terenzi brand, whose floral, partly synthetic, and often playful DNA I greatly appreciate, I must state here and for the Ilba: This is nothing at all! From the very first minute, I was accompanied by two thoughts, namely "you know this scent" and "this doesn't smell really good." Now the big pondering began, because it is, at least for my nose, a fragrance that I have perceived multiple times before. But I couldn't recall where and when. For days I pondered and waited with my review, and BAM: The moment of inspiration struck me. When I, as so often after eating chicken, used the included fresh towel, Ilba immediately came to mind. You surely know these fresh towels for hands, and yes, there are countless variations of them, with lemon and so on, but also this seemingly fresh, floral touch. I am happy to stand by this opinion alone, but a comparison on my skin, which I conducted two days later, confirmed my assumption. Sure, Ilba smells a bit finer, it doesn't have that "disinfecting" note in the background and is also a bit more full-bodied, but the base matches for me. From my perspective, Terenzi fails here to implement the otherwise so attractive floral structure of many fragrances from this brand. The clearly noticeable fruity notes do Ilba no favors at all and rob it of a pleasant form of freshness, which I usually like. Towards the middle of the fragrance, one can detect a slightly sour note in the background; otherwise, the fragrance remains fruity, floral, and somehow synthetically fresh as a whole. This is all supported by a sweet base, which only makes everything worse. For a fruity fragrance, it still smells quite clean, probably due to musk and oxygen!? But for me, it is unpleasantly clean, synthetically clean, which brings us back to those fresh towels for hands. I find no access to this fragrance at all... Lavender and juniper would have done the fragrance good, but these can only be found in the fragrance pyramid. I would have also wished for a slightly spicier/woodier base. From my point of view, this fragrance is a failure. This fruity-sweet demeanor, I simply cannot warm up to. If anything, it requires a bit of refinement, which I completely miss here. I tend to find it rather feminine; projection and longevity are solid but not annoying.

This is my Roja Parfums Elysium Review. My Elysium Pour Homme by Roja Parfums Fragrance Review. This was an unexpected delight of a fragrance from Roja Parfums. Not typically the style of fragrance I would expect from this luxury niche brand, Roja Parfum but it really works. What we have here with Roja Parfums Elysium Pour Homme Parfum Cologne is a crowd pleaser and a compliment getter. This is an ultra classy, masculine fragrance and very easy to wear but still very complex with lots of great notes. It's a very modern fougere. Please watch my review for more info about Elysium Pour Homme Parfum Cologne.

True, the durability of this perfume is not very impressive, but the smell is simply amazing. When I wear it I literally imagine I'm a Greek god. He is so impressive, but as I said at the beginning, it sucks that his performance is not better. At the same time, in my opinion, it is a must in every collection And undoubtedly the best version of Elysium perfumes. Elysium pour Homme Parfum Elysium Eau Intense 8/10.

This is pretty much the definition of a perfect everyday wear for me. The one you use for everything and anything, resting assured it will work wonders. This could be just another blue fragrance in this current “blue craze”, but it’s not. The vetiver plays a major role here for me, and I’m glad it does! What a great vetiver it is! The way the florals dance with the citrus while it develops, even hinting sometimes at a slight smoky/leathery nuance is just fantastic. Mass pleasing and easy to wear? For sure! Boring? No. Not to me. And I don’t just say this. The first time I sampled this in Budapest at freezing point temperatures, I couldn’t stop smelling my wrist. Now tried and tested in all seasons and occasions, with a full bottle in hands, I can happily say it was my most used fragrance in 2022, and one of the most special (Wore it even to the Wedding of a loved one) Bottled Class and Versatility.

Elysium has been plastered all over the YT fragrance community for a while now. I finally decided to order a sample/decant and see what all the hype was about. I'm not a scent guru but I tend to give fragrances a few wearings just to see if I truly like them or if there any good, so I did the same with this. Smell: A fresh and clean but slightly fruity scent. Conclusion: If you hid the bottle behind your back then held out your wrist and said “Smell this” I would reply to you and say “Is this a new Bath and Body Works scent..?” Elysium may be great to others but to me, this is nothing special. If you are looking for something simple, easy to wear, and non-offensive then this is for you. Honestly, it's very linear & the price is not justified for the scent that you get, overhyped. Pay half the price and get a clone of this fragrance instead. (P.s. I didn't know people actually get offended by someone's opinion about some juice in a bottle called a fragrance.)

First and foremost, this smell is incredible. The opening of Elysium is one of the nicest I've ever smelled, and overall, it's the most complex fragrance I've ever smelled. There are various phases to the dry down, and each one grows more seductive as it progresses. Do you want compliments? Then I recommend wearing it almost anywhere and you will get them. This is a well-balanced fresh/green aroma that is appropriate for any occasion. People WANT to be around this scent, and when they complement you, it's not simply because they smell your cologne; they complement you because this cologne is sophisticated and smells amazing. Grab a sample and you'll see why some believe it's superior to the king of niche scents.

I have waited for years to acquire a full bottle of this perfume due to its popularity within the fragrance community. Additionally, I tend to steer clear of perfumes hyped up like this one. At its core, this is a fundamental designer composition with higher-quality materials within, yet its performance is underwhelming for this category of perfume.

Complex, expensive spring, summer fragrance. Not similar to Aventus but much better as a scent. Currently one of the best citrus fragrance on the market. Lacks of performance and has sillage issue. Like nishe version of Bleu de Chanel. nulltheless, scent is so gergous and must try this rich juice for sure!

For the price of Bleu De Chanel parfum you get cucumber water and the safest most plain vetiver you've smelled throughout most designers, in the drydown. All the cost with nothing remarkable to show. That's basically the entire fragrance. Considering the massive amount of ingredients Roja claims to use, you think there would be more complexity involved.

I own quite a few fragrances and tried even more, both niche and designer. This one is different in so many ways. It gives me goosebumps each time I put it on...absolutely gorgeous vibe, very fresh and complex. Not your linear "Torino 21" kind of smell as it changes quite a bit over time which I like very much.

Beautiful fragrance that garners lots of comments. Fresh, sharp, but settles down to a very inviting scent. Unfortunately the price is beyond most people’s budget, in which case Dua supernova is a very solid substitute. Ideal for summer months, but also doubles as a very classy fragrance all year round.

Not a bad scent to be sure, but not impressive either. The scent on my skin is extremely subtle and does not change much. I pretty much get the smell of an Orange Cream Popsicle throughout, and I never liked those much. Longevity was well below average on my skin. I give this walking creamsicle a 2.5 star out of 5 rating. Not recommended.

Give me anything that is Neroli or Orange Blossom dominant and I usually am in high spirits. This is no exception. There is something about these notes that is so joyful and energising. Take a long and slow sniff and … ahhhh. It’s a known fact through many clinical trials that jasmine has an effect on the brain that is as strong, if not stronger than antidepressant medication. It really would not surprise me if Neroli does the same. After all, our emotions are based on chemical interactions within the brain, so it boils down to logic that different smells, will prompt a variety of physical stimuli in the grey matter. Sweet Redemption has an almost gourmand personality. It is a very well rounded and comfortable fragrance to wear. A cosy perfume with an acidulated edge. Projection is medium and so is its longevity. A really lovely creation by Mr Kilian … the price, however makes me reluctant to invest because there are plenty of other delicious and far more affordable offerings on the market that are way too similar to warrant the expenditure.

I immediately smelled the orange flower in the opening, but it mellowed out fairly quickly when the benzoin, incense and vanilla notes totally took over, and laid in a murky thick puddle. My final impression of Sweet Redemption is that it's a sweet menthol-root beer concoction. Yup. Very odd, this one's just not working on my skin. I gladly shared my sample with someone who loves it. Can't win'em all right?

I'm just tuning into the house of By Kilian now, at the supposed end of the L’Oeuvre Noire series, with Sweet Redemption. I had heard a lot about this house being on the strong side, and seeing that I like bold and somewhat outrageous smelling fragrances, I find that this house, and this fragrance in particular, suit my personal tastes. Sweet Redemption is either a love it or hate it. I personally adore it, however I have had many repeated wearings, over which time the scent has grown on me. It opens with a deliciously zesty and juicy mandarin orange, slightly sweet but also very natural. Once settled, Sweet Redemption has a somewhat medicinal accord, slightly antiseptic but strangely likable. The scent becomes darker and richer as the fragrance progresses. My nose seems to detect a hint of creamy benzoin, chocolate, vanilla icecream and smoky myrrh. Honestly, it is a bit of a gourmand experience, especially with all the vanillary and orangey sweetness. The base is quite sexy, with the myrrh, incense and opoponax creating something quite animalistic and gritty. I've been game enough to wear this to quite a few social gatherings, where men in particular have gone bananas over the drydown of this fragrance on my skin. It is unisex after all, and although sweet, I wouldn't call Sweet Redemption entirely feminine. This fragrance clings to fabric so well, that I can smell it on my coats and jumpers for days. The longevity is of course, very impressive, as is the sillage, which could knock someone out if applied too heavily. All in all, I'm impressed.

One of my favorite Orange Blossoms. This is a honeyed and sweet orange blossom. Very edible. The orange blossom and opoponax are the dominant notes in the opening but I get a hint of incense and vanilla too. The heart is more benzoin than opoponax and I loose the incense but the oranges blossom is still dominant. The incense comes back in the drydown and becomes the dominant note with the orange blossom. There's also a hint of vanilla and myrhh. this is the least sweet stage of the scent which is good because by the time you get to the drydown you need a break from the sweetness. Or at least I do. The longevity is great, about 11 hours. I catch snatches of it up to a day later though. The sillage is huge (BOOM), so use a light hand or you'll suffocate. May 31 2014 ROUND TWO: This is my second review of this scent. My first review was written in the hot and humid summer of Florida. This review was written in the cooler and drier winter. For the first time ever I got the root beer note others have mentioned. It surprised me. Besides the root beer note it opens with a Honeyed Orange Blossom full of Opoponax and Vanilla (which probably adds to the root beer). There is a menthol/ medicinal quality here, sitting behind the Orange Blossom, that reminds me of fresh, crushed orange leaves. Could it be from the Myrrh? Orange leaf isn't listed but I swear it's in there. The opening also has a hint of incense in the background. It's a very sweet opening. Not candy sweet but that sweet scent you know will taste bitter, like vanilla extract. It's a really interesting dynamic. As it warms up, the Orange Blossoms comes forward more and the root beer edge lessens. It's also a little more dessert sweet than vanilla extract-like bitter sweet (for lack of a better way to explain it). It's a lovely change and very different from the opening. There is also more... Orange... pulp? I don't know what it is, but it has a nice Zing and I am still getting a hint of that menthol/ medicinal quality that I think of as fresh crushed orange leaves. The Zing and the medicinal really balance out the dessert sweetness. It's truly lovely. The dry down is still mostly Incense with Vanilla and a hint of Myrrh. The Vanilla isn't very sweet and it is a nice break from the sweetness of the other two stages. It's warm and comforting. I'm not sure which is my favorite stage but the dry down is very beautiful. It's actually that menthol / medicinal edge, that I perceive as crushed orange leaves, that really makes this a work of art. The composition walks the line between overly sweet and overly medicinal like a tightrope walker who's perfected their skills and can run across the tightrope, blindfolded with no net. It's mastery of an art and beautiful to experience. How this composition wears is greatly impacted by the temperature and humidity (at least for me it is). More so than any other scent I've worn (except maybe Seville). The longevity is amazing and lasts forever. The Silage is NUCLEAR and you will kill people if you are not careful and use a light hand. Dec 29 2015

By Kilian SWEET REDEMPTION seems like a very simple perfume to me. I smell orange blossom, I smell benzoin, and I smell vanilla--and that's about it. Each of these components seems very clear and identifiable, what is rare in composed perfumes. The overall effect to my nose is that of cooked-sugar glazed orange blossoms.

Tested vintage travel set in August when it’s at its most humid and hottest in Texas. Sweet Redemption opens with the same orange blossom from LDBS, here it’s more green and instead of a powdery, marshmallow texture, the orange blossom is dense and syrupy.

This really smells like Memo Sintra in my opinion, especially with that bitter orange blossom opening. On my skin they are nearly identical, but I prefer Sintra more. The performance is OK, about 4 hours but really, for the price, I expect more. Dries down to a Love Don’t be Shy genre. A bit redundant if you own Love, Sintra and other perfumes in this family.

So, when I read through my old comments, we find Escada Magnetism Cherry Coke, and in Invasion Barbare we find Thomas Henry's "Spicy Ginger Ale," and with Pure Malt the master brewer sodas from Eichbaum (I hope this isn't misunderstood as advertising for beverages). With Sweet Redemption, I have now found a comparison to Root Beer.
The theme of orange blossom has me a bit captivated at the moment, and I went on a search. The comments about "süße Erlösung" read really well, and I became very curious.

First of all, I would like to say that this is my personal impression. I am writing this here just to provide others with possibly helpful information. I can understand differing opinions well. Testing it yourself is usually the best. This is a blind buy that I honestly made based on the fragrance notes when I saw the scent on sale. I enjoy citrus top notes, Neroli and Bergamot paired with pepper notes. When I then saw the base notes of Amber, Musk, and Patchouli, I found it worth a closer look. Sometimes you pay for your education. But you can also learn something. What I don't like: The scent literally explodes upon spraying with immense force and variety. Sounds good at first, you might think. However, there is something that is not well balanced for my nose. I perceive a sharp, smoky burning note that I really dislike. Unfortunately, I can't exactly identify what it is. My suspicion is that something between the combination of Vetiver, Frankincense, the pepper notes, Juniper, and Geranium clashes for me. The biting burning note lasts for the first 1-2 hours on me. During that time, I would give the scent a 1 to 2 out of 10. Interestingly, my wife does not perceive this strongly piercing smell. She finds the scent "Okay. It could be better, it could be worse." What I like: - After I "survive" the first 2 hours, it really starts to roll. The pepper caresses the Juniper, which somehow rings in the nose first subtly and then increasingly clearly. - Amber, Musk, and Patchouli are then well blended and feel very exquisite. - The performance is simply outstanding. Almost too intense, and one should be careful to use this scent in moderation. The scent strip, on which I first sprayed it, still smelled throughout the entire room after 24 hours. And that was after just one spritz. - After a longer time, I really enjoy the scent and would rate it an 8.5/10. Conclusion and recommendation? I would not recommend this scent to most people. It is simply too specific. Not for beginners. However, if people are looking for a versatile scent with exceptional performance, they might find a gem here. For me, however, it is not a scent for going out, as it could offend some people. It is more of a scent for when you want to enjoy what a fragrance can do and perceive it as a personal experience. Maybe read a good book and let your thoughts drift. I am completely torn back and forth with this scent. The beginning is really tough and unpleasant for me personally. But after some time, the scent develops so well that I am overwhelmed with a simple "rating" of the fragrance. Overall, I have therefore landed at a "middle rating"... which means I can't really do justice to the scent in either the "good" or "bad" category. It is just like the scent: complex.

Draconis is another blind buy that I took a bold risk on. Fortunately, I was not disappointed here either. The reason for my purchase was clear: I really like Comme des Garçons Black Pepper. Draconis was supposed to be the next step for me. I want to immediately contradict the statement that Draconis is an ordinary fragrance. Draconis deserves to be tested more often because it is a scent with many facets. Draconis opens with a powerful burst of fresh notes, particularly strong grapefruit and lemon. Following this is the fascinating part of Draconis, which completely captivated me. The fresh notes blend with the pepper and the wonderful incense note, creating a whole new scent profile for me. I can perceive this fantastic DNA for a full 7 hours, after which the incense becomes stronger and vetiver and patchouli join in. These notes allow Draconis to linger for over 3 hours. The longevity of 10 hours is truly perfect, and the sillage is also strong for about 5-6 hours; after that, it retreats to within an arm's length and lets the scent fade close to the skin. The MSRP is, of course, too high, and I wouldn't buy Draconis at that price. I also find myself wondering again what the buyer is supposed to do with the huge packaging, as it simply takes up so much space. The combination of spices and fresh notes along with smoke is perfectly executed here and also unique.

A walk through an enchanted garden,a story about fauns and bewitched forest beings.A complex masterpiece created to transport the wearer through a summer night dream,through a flora and fauna marriage,through trees covered in moss and orange blossoms.A fresh floral fragrance designed to look and smell just like a Shakespeare poem,a fairytale with no beginning and no end,A Midsummer Dream aims to uncover the unique mythical universe of Master Roja Dove.

Roja Midsummer Dream is the olfactory equivalent of the urge to disappear into a haunted glade and become local folklore or of how your body isn’t a temple, it’s the moss-encrusted altar where primitive rituals once unfolded. But we are a soft, suburban people, and I think this sense of longing is tempered with the fog of nostalgia for something we’ve never possessed –and quite frankly, might not be equipped to handle. So sure, be the cryptids or feral forest witch you wish to see in the world or become one with your inner family of raccoons, but also remember that you don’t actually like the cold very much, and getting your hands dirty isn’t your idea of a good time, and a dark moonless night where the only sound is that of your own frantic breath, and the invisible scurrying of nocturnal creatures would be better spent dreaming indoors under a downy granny quilt. Roja Midsummer Dream is the best of all these worlds– a gentle elven chypre, an ancient amber that hums like skin warmed by forgotten fires, the faint rust of autumnal spice, and the phantom sting of bitter grapefruit in the golden memory of sun-dappled woods. It's like a gentle ghost story of arboreal elegance told under the soft glow of glittering fairy lights, except, unfortunately, the ambient lighting costs four hundred bucks, and the only ghosts you might encounter are the missing funds in your bank account. All this existential exploration, this whispered communion with the primal self, sounds delightful, but I’m afraid I prefer my delights slightly less expensive. These enchantments are best enjoyed in my dreams, where perhaps money grows on moss-covered trees.

When I moved to Japan some time ago, I learned through research that wearing strong perfumes could be considered disrespectful in certain settings. To adapt, I chose two fragrances for my 6 months journey Creed Aventus and this one. There isn’t a more evocative, happy, and nostalgic fragrance that takes me back to some of my best memories: a summer in Tokyo. It’s like a magic potion. The top notes open with zesty citrus and the bright resinous touch of elemi, giving it a sparkling, spicy uplifting feel. Then, the heart brings in soft florals, orris, with an earthy edge grounded and elegant, like the gardens of Japan. Finally, the base notes of warm, powdery woods and musk wrap you up in a velvety embrace that lingers beautifully. It’s an earthy, powdery masterpiece, a true Midsummer dream. Shakespeare said it best The course of true love never did run smooth but this fragrance might just be the exception. And if you’re after compliments, this one’s a « panty dropper ».

This one is certainly unique and special, although not quite right for me. It opens with an extremely bright and clear resinous floral citrus that's not sour or juicy at all. Imagine Elysium Eau Intense, except its a Spring edition. It behaves more like a breath of fresh Spring air than your typical citrus juice fragrance. I enjoyed wearing this phase as it felt very uplifting, magical, and calming. As the mid approaches quickly, it takes on a vintage mossy floral soap quality. Perhaps its the oakmoss note, which I would associate with vintage women's perfume mixed with the bitter white florals that remind me of soap. Unfortunately, this phase of the fragrance smells completely wrong on me. I simply have no desire to smell like great-grandma's soap. As it continues to dry down, it becomes more of a clean and earthy vetiver with bitter soapy undertones. While I can appreciate the quality and creativity of this fragrance, I don't enjoy wearing soapy fragrances or vintage feeling fragrances.

I would venture to guess about a year ago, I’d stumbled upon this Roja on a YouTube video. At that time, with the price of Rojas, I paid it no mind, aside from wondering if it had anything to do with A Midsummer Nights Dream. I recall wondering that and immediately being transported back to my youth of high school. Given we read this amid several Shakespeare works, but that having been about 30 years ago, I didn’t recall the work itself, though recall how I felt around that time. Somewhat recently, I found a “unicorn” fragrance in Royal Crown’s Sultan… so much so, I regretted buying a 50 ml, rather than 100 ml. I decided to buy another 50 ml and while that sat in my online cart for a couple days, I again stumbled upon this fragrance on YouTube. I immediately had that reminiscent feeling again and had to learn more. The feeling that memory gave me was one of warmth, love, feeling the invigorating feeling of being in a forest. In those younger days I was in love with the idea of being in love and spent a lot of time hiking through local forests, so it very well could be that I’d had very loosely connected memories to that time frame rather than the work itself. After pondering the price at roughly 180 usd for the 100 ml for a couple days I decided to make the purchase. I must admit as the last 4 or so days passed by, having not tested A Midsummer Dream prior, I was a tad worried and began thinking “what if I finally get a fragrance delivered and I just don’t like it… and it’s one I paid nearly 200 bucks for?” Well it arrived yesterday, and those apprehensive fears were absolutely not realized. I have found my second unicorn fragrance. My immediate thoughts upon spraying this was “wow, this smells exactly how I feel while trying to recall the play, and only being able to recall how I felt, generally, around that time - the warmth, the peace, calm, and invigorating feeling of being in the forest, and smells like the most well blended love ever!” I additionally thought “what the heck am I going to do with all my fragrances now?” - if I am to be honest, wearing this for several hours yesterday, and again today, makes me feel as though I don’t even want to bother with most of the 325 or so fragrances in my collection. I typically am not much of a fan of fragrances that are on the greener side of the spectrum. I would consider this to be quite green. However, this is absolutely magical and is an absolute masterpiece and within the top 10 or so fragrances I’ve ever smelled. There have been times where I’ve seen and experienced fragrances that have a massive list of notes and while I’ve come across very few fragrances I didn’t like, more times than not, when there are too many notes, the blends can tend to be messy, lackluster, too heavy or not heavy enough on one or several notes. Now I see… or smell… or both when taking into account the lovely bottle - why it is that some praise Roja Dove. This is a magic potion I wish I could swim in. I want to smell like this, I want every scent to smell like this. This is that magical in my opinion. I can’t stop smelling my arms, it is simply the most amazing fragrance and between this and a couple other new purchases, picking fragrances such that I put them all to use is going to be extraordinarily difficult because I’m going to want to wear this every darn day. Bravo, Roja, bravo!

A midsummer dream is a calm fresh citrus/vetiver fragrance with a spicy touch of cardamom. Absolutely stunning, i want to wear this everday, but please don’t tell the rest of my collection! Great performance without getting to much or cloying. And do we need to mention the bottle? I don’t think so. 10/10

The first few seconds are marvelous and set the stage for a wonderful act! I smell moss, greenery, sweet citrus, which gives the impression of softly glowing light. So magical, evocative and fitting of its name. No flowers though, so don't be expecting a blooming garden. It's just a lawn. It's also powdery.

Rarely have I encountered a fragrance more evocative than this one. First, the name: A Midsummer Dream. An obvious nod to the Bard, the scent suggests something both herbaceous and radiant—perfectly embodying a dream: fleeting, shifting, and unpredictable. Or perhaps it’s a forest, where you stand alone at the edge on an autumn evening.

Linen, sun, sea and high temperatures means only one thing. Vacation and all the way summer vibes with my magical fragrance from Roja. Zesty grapefruit in the opening with cardamom and pink pepper later turns into sophisticated and seductive scent with oakmoss, vanilla, benzoin, vetiver, cedarwood and carrot seed as the most recognizable notes.

A Midsummer Dream (AMD) may be a little generic for a Roja scent but is beautiful nonetheless. It sparkles like many of his other scents and mixes elements of freshness with warmth with the citruses, spices, and resins.

STH Extreme has the scent of a masterpiece but the performance of a piece of crap. I own both the original STH with the black cap and STH Extreme. Both have extremely poor performance issues. STH Extreme turns into a skin scent within two hours and then completely vanishes. Talk about gut wrenching…and to add insult to injury, it’s discontinued so over-spraying is completely out the question. Maybe I’m wearing it during the wrong seasons, but I can’t help that because where I live, it’s usually hot eight months out of twelve. If you love boozy woody fragrances that will ghost you after a couple hours, I would recommend STH Extreme. Lol

It just clicked with me. This is my favorite niche perfume of all time. Final answer. If you have smelt the original STH, it still retains that DNA and amps up the booziness (rum note) and tad bit of sweetness (vanilla). Unfortunately, this has been discontinued but there are some rumors that Kilian may re-release this.

I discovered this perfume in Printemps Boulevard Haussmann Paris today. I knew I was going to go for a powerful masculine scent. but this one is really too powerful sickening heady intoxicating. all you can smell is alcohol, rum and maybe a little vanilla, I really find it sickening. and on top of that it costs 200€? it's actually a joke.surrated . I advise you not to make a blind purchase with this reference

This is one of my favorite evening scents. Everytime i spray it i enjoy the scent so much. It's mysterious and a pefect composition of notes. Not to much vanilla. It's in balance with the dried fruits, the cedar wood and the rum. It is stronger than the original STH but very similar to each other. In particular the rum and vanilla is a little amped up. Maybe my next bottle will be the original again. Because it's in the base the same scent and much easier to get at a much lower price. But i treasure the extreme version as long as i can :)

Straight to Heaven is my fragrance of the year 2020, and to draw something positive from this absolutely modest year, I want to honor this little masterpiece by Kilian with this comment. "At the end of these lonely, liquor-soaked long nights, not much remains. Mostly just memories in the form of melancholic love texts. Love? Annoying. Now that the joys are gone, only the affection for silent scratching on vinyl remains, my heart tightens, give me the damn Orfiril. After the chaos somewhere between alcohol and tobacco smoke, we are still awake, yet outside the lights go out. Everything dark, so infinitely quiet. We alone stay awake, in this sleeping world. When I close my eyes, I smell warm skin, the rum, hear your breath and think of the patter of rain on the tarp back then in the tent. 2 souls, together, yet lonely. Distorted by society, On the run from ourselves and what we have ultimately become, already in childhood: problem child. Depressions are strange, it's as if no one notices the lack of air, the pressure on the chest comes back again and again, I think of the puddles on the kitchen table and your vanilla-scented candles. The freezer full of frozen fruit gnomes. And now......reading by candlelight. Silence in my room and the next room, I pretend I don’t miss you, I turn the page, the pages rustle and outside the rain gets worse." Straight to Heaven Extreme is not a complex scent, not demanding, not.....extravagant. At least not in my nose. Rum + vanilla very prominent and strong, behind it almost barely perceptible patchouli, nutmeg, and a bit of wood. Despite everything, the scent fascinates me so incredibly, the ingredients harmonize perfectly and shine. It is boozy, clear, but somehow there is more. As one can gather from my little text, I associate this rum aroma with an extremely beautiful time. Chaotic, loud, young, and foolish. But truly happy. When I wear Straight to Heaven, I become melancholic, yes almost on the brink of depression when reflecting on what has been lost. Beautiful pain. The scent does something to me. And yet I never really feel uncomfortable. Soft warm melancholy in the promising black bottle. Gentle vanilla pods in sweet rum, this connection, this alcoholic must be liked, but if you do, you get a lot for your money here. Bottle: As always high quality and a smooth 10 Sillage: Not room-filling, but still radiates well, especially in the first 2-3 hours Scent: Perfect gentle rum, it really can’t get better Longevity: Lasts significantly better than the Straight to Heaven White Crystal For all fragrance alcoholics, bar-goers, drunks, Charles Bukowski mixes, decent gentlemen, and perhaps also for the average Joe with a flask in his pocket, this is definitely the ultimate. Love

Welcome to the Caribbean. My name is Rum, Rum Absolute. I am the helmsman of my captain Jack. Our other friend on the sloop is Vanilla. The three of us get along great from start to finish and will never be separated. But since our captain got a bit too drunk on a deserted island, we unfortunately can’t find him anymore.

Performance is basically zero. Scent is ok, nothing to rave for. To be fair, it's a good skin scent but pricepoint, hard to justify. Kilian is my fave house but I won't recommend this to anyone. If you're not a hardcore fan, this is a hard pass. Get something else. A lot of options if you need a citrus and fresh scent in your wardrobe.

Subjective: A Classic “men’s” profile executed at a high quality. The citrus is well-balanced and elegant, with enough depth to keep you engaged. The fragrance dries to a clean, soapy base on my skin. Is this the ultimate no-fuss “clean boy” scent? There is nothing wrong with a basic crowd-pleasing profile executed at a high level. It’s not an incredibly complex scent that evolves over time, but its likability, combined with its quality, makes it special. Opening: Elegant classic opening. The balance between the citrus and herbal notes is masterful, soapy in a good way, like a classic pine bergamot hand soap. Development: After a couple of hours, the citrus and herbal notes fade, and a soft, creamy, clean scent lingers on the skin. A bit piney and still fresh, but nicely rounded and almost translucent. A nice, softer alternative to those who don't enjoy amber or woody drydowns. Performance: It performs more like an eau de toilette than an eau de parfum. But to me, that’s ok, it fits with the target audience and use case for this kind of fragrance. I’m not sure I would want to smell like classic men’s pine soap for 8+ hours.

So far best citrus piney scent, but to me this is eather game changing, eather a particular personal hit? Because I don't like the pine note in most fragrances, own a few as well, not my jam. So I guess the way byKilian handles this part of the spectrum? The fresh, the citrus, the blue? Yes supremely classy.nnVery much fresh, also get a similarity to Moonlight in Heaven after the opening. Three to four hours performer, will definitely try out a few overspray sessions to see how it goes since, I've heard it's not natural oils, do not get the synthetic feel on this, at all.nnDon't trust, sample it for yourself, no, it's doesn't smell like a cheap shower gel, the opening isn't bug spray, doesn't smell like laundry detergent.nnGet a joyful standing at the heaven gates type opening, after less than half hour settles into sheer elegant freshness. It's a full treat for those few hours, like it gets you and gets you. Maybe citruses work well with my pH, at the moment, idk, but it's a party right now.

The opening is fresh and uplifting with some gentle sweetness coming from the mandarin. The main notes are mandarin and rosemary. There's some woodiness in the background, but overall, I find this scent to be transparent and light. It's not a particularly complex fragrance, but it's easy to wear and perfect for the warmer months. While it leans slightly mature, I think anyone could pull this off. Shahbaz_2009 already summed up the scent really well, so read their review below mine for more in-depth analysis.

“Kologne” is an ice-cold citrus cologne that could hardly be more modern, minimalist, and yet complete. This is exactly the kind of perfume Kilian will wear on the hottest days of the year. Personal, intimate, and by conviction. Cooldown witness. It is always difficult to compare such a straightforward, slightly green ice cube accord of the luxury class with complex masterpieces of perfume history. And yet “Kologne” deserves nearly a top rating for me. It simply works. Round, clear, ice-cold. Sparkling and hissing. Rosemary spreads its radiant color. Mint adds even more flavor and is just the right kind of green behind the ears. A cocktail for princes. Softer towards the end. Lasts longer than one might think. A scent at the peak of its genre. “Dior Homme Cologne” from the fridge calls. A masterpiece of its kind. Just the right sweetness, just the right bitterness, just the right revitalizing. A la bonne heure! Bottle: high-quality and expensive Sillage: lemon splash understatement Longevity: 6 hours of air conditioning for the handbag Conclusion: Kilian Summer Deluxe - the most exquisite scent for a white shirt!

This is the perfume that made me fall in love with the world of perfumery. This is the second niche perfume I bought at the beginning of my journey and it was after I was in the store and the price deterred me so I put a few squeezes of this magical perfume on a scent paper and for a whole week, from Saturday to the Saturday that followed, I smelled this scent and I simply fell in love with the perfume and went to buy it, despite the price tag. If there's a reason I'm waiting for winter, it's this perfume. It is so elegant, sexy, attractive and high quality that I long to wear it. I wore it on one date I had and the woman the next morning told me that all my scent was on her hair and she just fell in love with this scent. For me, 10/10 without question.

I'd say that this to me is much more a Rose Aoud than a properly Amber Aoud. It doesn't have the thick, vanillic and incense aura that you would expect from a classic Amber approach, and it also doesn't have the woody, light, sometimes plastic modern aura that you get from woody ambery bases. Leaving this aside, this is a good, silky and rich aoud and rose orchestration, surrounded by a velvet suedish touch which lingers discretly on skin. Altough the fragrance seems to be more complex, it relies basically around these three facets, creating an harmony which is very pleasant to be noticed all day. It has a great longevity, a small sample lasted all day on me, and while i see a lot of quality on here, it seems to me very safe, something made for the one which is willing to pay for quality and wants and oud rose orchestration which softens the rough aspects of this noble wood. It's at least worth a sample.

Delightful and unique way in perfumery to start a dificult and astringent chord of oud, ambergris and rose. Like no perfume that I could test. Then begin to shine the saffron and soft ambered texture. Starts very promising, but then the initial strenght goes down and ruins, in my opinion, a perfect smell; an "unstable-stabilized" perfection of oud. Perfume turns into an ambered soft common base mixed with saffron that we all have seen before, and we can get of many other perfumes in a cheaper range of prices. I can see clear references to Red Aoud of montale. Worth the price? Sample yes. Full Bottle.. I don´t think so..

A kind gentleman at bergdorff in nyc was kind enough to make me a 2ml sample of amber aoud to take home with me. I was beyond excited to try it out and see what all the fuss was about and what an $800 bottle of fragrance smells like Powdery rose bomb with some ambergris and benzoins, thats all i get. No oud, no woodiness, no animalic notes….just rose, rose and more rose. Don’t get me wrong, it smells nice, but having “oud” in the name is so misleading, if there is any in here, it’s at such low trace amounts it’s undetectable to my nose. Also, very feminine leaning in my opinion. If you want a REAL rose oud fragrance for men, just get ombre nomade, its half the price and double fragrance this could ever hope to be.

I haven't written a separate in-depth review of Amber Aoud yet but here are a comparison of differences with Aoud. You find my in-depth review of Aoud. The rating is same for both. DIFFERENCES BETWEEN AOUD AND AMBER AOUD Both unisex with eternal longevity, huge sillage and projection. I wanted to write about these Roja Dove’s two perfumes since there seems to be people who would like to know the difference of these two and if another one is redundant if you already have the other. You can check the differences from the notes of course but that doesn’t tell always how those similarities or/and differences appears. So here is my opinion. As I love Roja so much I have both: Aoud in 30ml and 100ml and Amber Aoud Crystal in 100ml. I like to have both and for me I feel that I need to have both. The difference is not so big for most of the people but it’s very noticeable for trained nose, rosewood lovers and Roja fans. Differences are: - Amber Aoud is slightly more sweet because of Fig in the opening and Benzoin in the base. - In the same time it’s warmer because of Ambergris and Benzoin in the base. (Ambergris is as well in Aoud but it’s not the main note.) - Aoud is more fresh and rosy. It’s more traditional Rose Oud scent. - Even if there is Saffron in both, Aoud is more earthy since there is less the main notes in overall so Saffron is easier to detect. - I would say that Aoud is not so complex than Amber Aoud. In Aoud it’s really easy to smell Rose, Saffron and Oud separately while in Amber Aoud its 5 different main base notes are really well blended. - Aoud is the first one of those three (Aoud, Musk Aoud, Amber Aoud) which Roja launched so it is like the most simple one. - Amber oud has a smoky feeling in it, it varies a lot between different batches though. If you want a real Rose Oud scent go for Aoud, if you are not a huge fan of traditional Rose Ouds, you can love Amber Aoud. MY OPINION: If you like AOUD, you will like Amber Aoud as well but not automatically in the other way. I hope this will help some people to choose between these two chic, captivating and mesmerizing perfumes. Musk Aoud is by the way totally different and unfortunately it’s discontinued due to the regulations of certain natural ingredients. I’m happy to own it as 30ml og and 100ml crystal. These both perfumes are suitable in the same kind of occasions, they share the same kind of feeling and character despite of the differences. They are attractive, seductice, rich, complex, mesmerising, utterly luxurious and absolutely in among of the best scents ever. The juice of the original perfumes is very dark and it stains clothes permanently so Crystal versions of those scents are very practical. I love to wear these scents during a summertime and with white clothes so clear juice is great with them. The scent itself is identical with the dark, original juice, only the colour has been removed.Both perfumes are unisex. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes

Roja amber aoud is probably my favorite from the brand. The beautiful blend of amber, rose and a blend of citruses just makes the perfume stunning. I could never really justify trhe insane price for this but if you get a bottle for a good deal it would for sure be worth it. Will maybe upgrade to a full bottle from my sample in the near future!

I have to admit, there's rarely a fragrance that I would rate a perfect 10/10. My collection has approximately 120 fragrances and I've tested probably about 500 more. From all of those fragrances there's probably a hand full that I would give a perfect rating. And Amber Aoud by Roja is one of them although it's not perfect. Amber Aoud is part of Roja Aoud collection.

Roja Dove Parfums Amber Aoud Parfum   Top Notes:  Lemon, Bergamot, Lime Heart Notes:  Rose de Mai, Jasmin de Grasse, Ylang Ylang, Fig Base Notes:  Cinnamon, Saffron, Patchouli, Oakmoss, Sandalwood, Aoud, Benzoin, Orris, Birch, Ambergris, Musk  Roja Dove Amber Aoud Parfum opens up with a bright blast of bright combination consisting of juicy fig and jammy rose.

I love aoud and amber and to have a combination which is smooth is just divine. The aoud is quite soft and the amber is not like Tom Ford medicinal amber absolute. Amber aoud has excellent silage and longevity 18 hours and going. Another fab creation from 'professor of perfumery'!

One of the quintessential rose-ouds every fraghead needs to try. I actually think this is a particularly Arab/Middle-Eastern take on this DNA, despite the fact that it was made by a British perfumer. There is this honeyed rosewater-y aspect in Amber Aoud that is also apparent in certain ambery mukhallats, at least the few I've tried.

According to Google, the fragrance is dedicated to a yacht design from 1929. This design is said to have sustainably influenced yachting. Whether Terenzi will celebrate the same successes with this fragrance, I doubt. To get to the point: This is truly a great perfume! In the top notes, I get the citrus notes - the fragrance feels very fresh and masculine to me, but not annoyingly overpowering. Lemon, rosewood, and just a tiny bit of eucalyptus come through. Then the fragrance becomes a bit softer, and the strong masculinity tones down slightly. It develops into a fresh-woody scent without feeling cool. I also pick up a slight spiciness, but I can't quite place it. In the dry down, the freshness recedes into the background, and the woods come to the forefront. Overall, the fragrance feels very high-quality. With the story behind the fragrance, I find it easier to categorize this scent. And yes, this is how I imagine the scent of a very well-groomed, wealthy man in white linen pants and a striped shirt. A bit cheeky, but down to earth. He has bright white teeth and loves to smile at everyone, but is never intrusive. Since my husband and I unfortunately do not own a yacht, I associate the fragrance more with a lovely walk with my beloved at the marina. The dorade is great, but it doesn't change the world. It remains what it is: a citrus-woody, maritime scent with a very gentle spiciness. I am sure there are brave ladies out there who would rock this fragrance as well. Personally, however, it is much too masculine for me.

Earlier today, PBFriend mentioned in a review that there are some houses she just "doesn't get". In my case, the big fat question mark is nearly always hovering above the house of Kilian, or is it "By Kilian"--not sure whether they finally realized that the preposition was a silly idea and have omitted it permanently from the name, or only from the sample set folio of the "In the Garden of Good and Evil" collection. Perhaps they were testing the waters: all other things kept the same (type of rhetoric, etc.) do consumers buy more perfumes from houses whose names are not preceded by prepositions? Honestly, I sometimes wonder, believe it or not, whether (by) Kilian might be an elaborate marketing experiment being conducted by the gurus at LVMH. Perhaps you think that I jest. My first issue with this house is the radical chasm spanning their hyperbolic pseudo-erotic texts and symbolism and the incredibly genteel and polite quality of their compositions. FORBIDDEN GAMES offers yet another example of what I'm talking about. Here is the marketing text for this perfume: ... "When going beyond the boundaries has never been so exciting and dangerously attractive." ... Let's see: what boundaries would those be? I ask because, to my nose, this perfume smells an awful lot like Nelly APPLE BOTTOMS: a sweet apple blossom in a clean resinous musky base with a few embellishments thrown in, but overall a high-quality fruity-floral fragrance. So naturally my first reaction upon donning FORBIDDEN GAMES was: what is supposed to be "forbidden" here? According to a well-known folk adage, "an apple a day keeps the doctor away." So apples are healthy. Why would they be forbidden? The only sense which I have been able to make of this involves a possible biblical allusion to the Garden of Eden, and the temptation to bite into the apple which led to--or was it constitutive of?--The Fall. That is a coherent interpretation, to be sure, but I still find that the quality of this fruity-floral fragrance is so innocent and juvenile that it is very difficult to associate it with any form of vice, least of all those of the "adult" kind. In fact, it's not even possible to commit the sin of gluttony in the case of apples, because they contain so much water and fiber, that it's not humanly possible to exceed one's RDA of calories through overindulging. Am I giving (by) Kilian too much credit here? Perhaps. This is an apple blossom perfume, and I believe that in a blind side-by-side test with Nelly APPLE BOTTOMS there are few people who would be able to pick out the haute niche from the mainstream offering. The quality seems very similar to me. I did not want to rush to judgment on this matter, so after donning FORBIDDEN GAMES this morning, I decided to dig out my small bottle of APPLE BOTTOMS. I haven't worn that perfume since I reviewed it, so it took about ten minutes to find, but once I did, I confirmed my initial impression that the two compositions are very similar. Perhaps this should be viewed as a compliment to APPLE BOTTOMS rather than an insult to FORBIDDEN GAMES? Which brings me to another gripe. "Jeux Interdits" [Forbidden Games] is the name of a justly celebrated film directed by René Clément in 1952. I realize that words belong to everyone, but come on, Kilian: why choose the title of an incredibly famous anti-war film? What does it have to do with a fruity-floral frag? I don't want to blame Kilian himself for this conceptual mess, my best guess is that we have LVMH to thank, yet again.

Firstly I do love Kilian creations so far, this is also a love. Imagine warm lightly stewed apricots, plums & granny smith apples topped with whipped cream and a dash of vanilla! This is it, gourmand lovers would delight in this. Its sweet, very creamy, syrupy ..almost jammy, however its slightly fresh too, must be that apple note. It stays relatively linear, though at times, like waves the apple note will come up, then down again. I want full bottle now! Yes it does smell familiar, and this type of formula has been done before, but I would still prefer this over a cheaper type fragrance, but thats me. If you dislike fruity floral gourmands, maybe best to stay away.

Forbidden games opens with a plum-laced peach that can easily be confused with a tropical coconut and banana vibe. The overall opening accord is very reminiscent of many of the low-end tropical suntan oils you smell at drugstores. A somewhat sharp artificial apple note joins the party in the early heart, joining the peach as the plum recedes. After the opening and early heart, the scent turns quickly into a skin scent consisting of the remnants of the peach now mixed with a very subtle artificial smelling rose undertone floating on a very quiet and just slightly sweet mundane vanilla base. Projection is poor (with the exception of the open) and longevity is average. Forbidden Games is definitely a disappointment. It smells good, but the smell is really so similar to Banana Boat Suntan Lotion that one just feels cheated with this composition by Becker who is capable of so much more. The dry-down is no better, as the vanilla used here is so generic and subtle it just comes off as a cheap cop-out that you might expect from a scent selling for 1/10th the price of this one at $245 for 50ml. While the fabulous container housing the juice is worthy of a scent with that price tag, its contents should be sold in the same drugstore as the suntan lotion it has cloned. One of the worst releases from By Kilian, Forbidden Games earns a disappointingly average 2.5 stars out of 5 outright, merits a value score of 1.

I stayed away from many Kilian fragrances because they seem to have low ratings here. The notes for Forbidden Games look lovely and I like Calice Beckers work so I blind bought an older bottle. OMG! I didn’t expect to love it this much. The opening is sweet, realistic ripe peaches with vanilla. Honey dripping from the yellow and red tinged flesh. The rose, jasmine and freesia are in the background but they never take over and they keep everything clean, balanced and sophisticated. The siliage is above average and I’ll comment about longevity later as it’s only been 2 hours. I’m in a divine scent bubble. This is very sexy to me. It’s been a total of 6 hours, it’s sitting closer to the skin but I still smell it when I love around. The dry down is more floral but the peach is ever present and it’s still creamy. Not creamy in a lactonic way, smooth, silken. It reminds me a lot of Chanel Allure EDP but here the fruits are riper, the base more vanillic and less polished more vamp. I don’t get potpourri, I don’t get generic, I don’t get boring. Don’t go off the reviews and try it yourself

The Saks online shop sums up this perfume with one great descriptor: potpourri. This is a mix of apples, peaches, plums, and a sprinkle of cinnamon. It works great if it were a candle or a room freshener; but I do not feel like it was meant on my skin. For a fruity perfume, the longevity is great--about 7-8 hours. But I don't want to smell like a tart warmer.

Another landmine this week, a mild disappointment, a real hit-and-miss, so to speak. A lovely, sparkling fruity opening; a harmonious and pleasant fruity-floral salad, very refined and easy on the nose. The apple and peach come forward quickly; yes – as if there’s some lychee in there too.

For the inexperienced: Stevia is a South American plant that has been used for sweetening by indigenous peoples for thousands of years. Its sweetness is hundreds of times stronger than that of sugar. In the meantime, you can buy both the plant and Stevia in powder and tab form to sweeten coffee, etc. here.

Forbidden Games opens with a fresh, lush fruit cocktail that gradually becomes warmer, until a note of peach compote remains. At first, I was a bit puzzled, is that all? Such an expensive fragrance, with a grand opening, and then there's peach compote? After three-quarters of an hour, relief washed over me as roses appeared, taking center stage, opulent.

Forbidden Games starts like a fruit basket covered with flowers. The scent profile is completely generic and lacks identity. If I were presented with a range of fruity-floral-fresh mainstream perfumes of today, I certainly couldn't pick out Forbidden Games.

a wonderful, honey-soaked peach, with great longevity. forbidden games is a fragrance that awakens the youthful lightness in me. for me, the scent is definitely the color yellow: cheerful, summery, a bit creamy & definitely not sensual enough for forbidden games. a great scent for summer that I enjoy having around.

An amazing perfume, both its opening and its drying are amazing. It's so luxurious that every time I wear it, I imagine I'm on a luxury yacht. Suitable for summer and spring mainly, I really like it. Interesting notes of grass, lime , Blackcurrant, champaca flower and coconut take this perfume to very special places. And his presentation is so amazing! Of course this is a renewal of the old perfume Oligarch Eau de Parfum . Definitely worth the price tag. 8.5/10.

How can you call something luxury overpriced? It means you are not interested in the product. Roja as we know is a high brand, like any other luxury brand, so the word overpriced makes no sense. The big problem with reviews is not being focused in the context of a product. Finally I can say that as an owner of hundreds of perfumes, from the most indie to the most luxury, this is an exceptional work, perfectly balanced (not like those horrible clones) by a nose who has worked a lifetime for quality and to achieve almost perfection in his works. Simple does not mean banal or overpriced, on the contrary, well-made simplicity is the most difficult thing to do, but objectively, all Roja works can boast of their ethereal beauty Ps. this doesn't even remotely resemble Hermes (respect the work) but not in 1000 years

It's official. I'm a bonafide member of the "I hate the 'aqua/marine' designation that's associated with a generic 'blue' accord in men's perfumes" club. It's a MARKETING PLOY! Literally a scheme cooked up by corporate advertising suits in NYC after running focus groups on a bunch of impressionable dullards. And judging by the reviews here on Parfumo, fragrance enthusiasts appear to be no less resilient to being afflicted by this virulent PSYOP. After all, young men are eager and willing to open their wallets for the "upscale" experience of wearing a brand like Roja! NO, this fragrance does NOT remind you of relaxing and sipping cocktails on a boat in the Mediterranean. That is a false association that was seeded in your brain, and subsequently watered, fed, and mimetically nurtured in your subconscious through your overindulgence in online perfume media run by shysters. Do you know what being on a boat in Italy actually smells like? Brackish salt brine, iodine-heavy kelp, crustaceans + mollusks, a hint of olive trees, a whiff of herbal aperitif from the Campari you spilled on your shirt earlier that day, and a vaguely fecal/humanoid-musk note that varies in intensity depending upon how near you are to a major urban area. This doesn't smell like that. At all. Is Isola Blu a mass-appealing, citrus-forward, 'blue' scent? Absolutely. If that's what you're into, fantastic -- go forth and wear young man! But don't pretend that this somehow "captures the essence of an aquatic lifestyle" (*I just experienced pure physical revolt and cringe by typing that*). But remember, the market for synthetic 'blue' fragrances is completely saturated, and there are perhaps hundreds of options available to you as a consumer. If you feel inclined to drop $500 MSRP for 50mL of Isola Blu, more power to you, but you could also just get the sufficiently similar Blue Talisman by Ex Nihilo at half the price. Meanwhile, if you want something that's been thoughtfully composed, is uniquely refreshing, and does a fine job of capturing the aroma of coastal myrtle trees and salty, kelp-laden bodies of water -- go try Acqua di Sale by Profumum Roma and thank me later.

Oligarch is a fragrance for a true oligarch, who spends summer vacations on his yacht in the most enchanting locations overlooking the Mediterranean Sea. Fresh, citrusy, crisp and aromatic. As in all Roja creations, it is difficult to separate the various notes that compose them, but I can say that juniper, citrus and pink pepper are well perceived. The woody structure holds all the volatile components very well, providing truly remarkable longevity for the type of fragrance. Despite not being a lover of the genre, I must say that I like it very much: it is fresh, clean, but at the same time has depth. 14 Swarovski cap, engravings and gold plate. PPS: Oligarch was discontinued due to the war between Russia and Ukraine and was put back on the market under the name of "Isola Blu"... But the original it's only one.

I read the reviews both good and bad. I tend to trust reviewers who are fans of this dna that's similar to TDH edt. The opening I can understand the negative mosquito repellant statement. I can see that, but I look past it and really appreciate the note structure and development of this fragrance. It's more than just a simple fragrance statement. It's what alot of positive reviewers say that "It smells luxurious." It does and smells blended to perfection. The vanilla and coconut notes really round it out nice! It's just a tiny sweet around the edges. Also i dont see vetiver in the note breakdown, but there has to be vetiver in the fragrance somewhere. I smell a high quality vetiver in this in my opinion. My third fragrance from the house of Roja. Roja fragrances are of high quality on both the fragrance ingredients and bottle presentation. This is just off my first spray on my hand and it's a happy yes for me!

I tend to like smooth, mellow, velvety fresh scents - ones where the sharp, spiky citrus highs get toned down and mellowed out. Isola Blu is NOT that kind of fragrance. As always with Roja fragrances, almost the entirety of the list of 50,000 notes is utterly indistinguishable to my nose. Is there birch in there? Grass? Maté?
This fragrance is absolutely one of my favorites. It’s fresh, masculine, classy, and an excellent year-round fragrance. However, I believe its true beauty shines through in the summertime.

Opens with an herbaceous zest and refreshing green apple. There are woody, mossy notes lingering in the background with emphasis on pepper, birch and cedar. This is the 3rd fragrance in Roja's line that reminds me of Terre d'Hermès, but this one is closest to that scent profile. If there were ever a Terre d'Hermès Aqua, it would certainly be this.
On my personal opinion this is the most beautiful summer fresh fragrance, j have tested a lot and this is my favorite Is simply gorgeous , elegant and really complex and absolutely not boring .

Thia is my number one Tiziana Terenzi fragrance. What I love most is how it evolves on the skin—it genuinely gets better and more captivating the longer I wear it. The opening is bold and confident. You get a prominent blast of Laotian Oud right at the front, with that perfect, subtle animalic touch that I absolutely adore. But don't let the strong start fool you. Little by little, it softens into something incredibly rich and wearable. The true magic happens in the dry-down: a beautiful, creamy, almost lactic texture emerges, blending perfectly with deep coffee and subtle caramel sweetness. This is where the surprise is: to my nose, this is a luxurious, high-quality oud take on Kilian's Black Phantom. It shares that decadent gourmand DNA but adds a mysterious depth and a silky, creamy texture that Black Phantom doesn't quite have. It's truly wonderful and mysterious. It's built a real tolerance—I'm finding myself reaching for it constantly, it's that addictive. Longevity is fantastic, lasting hours without being aggressively loud. You simply must try this one.

I have this in the lotion. Lol I just left a bad review on another scent for being “bathroomy” but this one is more like a luxurious bathroom candle scent. It pairs decently with Juicy Couture Oui and just smells fresh and like a typical “watery” scent to me. However it does NOT smell like citrus at ALL. And I don’t think I can detect any passionfruit either. I agree that it smells far more coconutty and floral. It is fairly sweet. I bought it on clearance during the SAS so it was a great value!

To be honest, I can't get enough of Love don't be shy! It's just addictive and above all, I find Love is pure sensuality in a bottle!*.* Of course, I also knew that there is an Extreme version of this beautiful fragrance:))) Since the original has captivated me and also seduced me, I thought that I probably wouldn't be able to get enough of the Extreme either, meaning I would (probably) wear it day and night:D So, I got a decant of Love Extreme to compare it with the original Love. I have also repeatedly heard that the Extreme should actually smell 1:1 like the original Love... And I disagree! Sure, it has the same fragrance DNA as the original, but I will now describe and compare it as best as I can with the original. The scent... - Love Extreme: Starts with a citrusy bitter note that unfortunately lingers on my skin for far too long for my taste... It's not bad, but bitter citrus notes that are also very cold don't really appeal to me. - Love: Immediately starts with this heavenly marshmallow note blended with the finest and most exquisite orange blossom note. And that's exactly what I love about Love; it's so beautiful from the first spray to the end of the scent development and above all, so perfectly rounded! - Love Extreme: I can still clearly smell this bitter citrus note, but after 15 minutes, a cold yet very powdery rose note joins in with a very delicate marshmallow note that unfolds very slowly minute by minute and merges with the scent development. I'm slowly warming up to the scent development. - Love: The marshmallow note still sets the tone but merges so well with a very noble, almost velvety, and warm rose note. The rose note in the original Love is velvety and very noble! Sweet, of course, but not synthetic, rather seductive and extremely feminine, in my opinion. But I must say, now that I'm smelling it again on my wrist, the marshmallow note is sooo fine, creamy, and sooo warm at the same time*.* - Love Extreme: Now the hoped-for orange blossom note is slowly coming through with a delicious overdose of marshmallow cream... The bitter note is very slowly bidding farewell from my skin, which honestly pleases me! What comes next is a very powdery and fresh rose note that brings a playful touch:)) Definitely very nice for the warm season and something different:)) - Love: For some time now, I can occasionally smell a tuberose note that, in my opinion, gives the scent development a very sensual and mature note, making it seem even more noble and feminine! :) The marshmallow note and the velvety rose note still make me dream, and I simply enjoy every time I spray it, the entire scent development!:)) It just makes me happy and lets me shine anew every time. Because what could be more beautiful than a fragrance that makes us happy and also gives us a good feeling?!:)) For me, such a thing is always a very valuable gift :) - Love Extreme: Becomes warmer and more pleasant as well as more sensual through the orange blossom and marshmallow note. The H+S is only more intense for an hour than the original. In my opinion, both are WONDERFUL, but I prefer the original much more. The Extreme can also be perfectly worn on warmer days due to the citrus notes that like to set the tone here;)) For me, both last all day on clothing but only 6-7 hours on the skin. What do YOU think?:))

My great love I had no idea about Kilian fragrances. My best friend and I were out shopping and she sprayed it on a tester. I was immediately positively surprised by this heavenly sweet fragrance cloud, which I could even strongly perceive through my mask. I smelled it and thought the whole time “HOW DELICIOUS.” I had truly never smelled anything like it before. Sprayed on the skin, it was initially a bit citrusy. I didn’t really like that at all! But after a few minutes, that sweetness was back in full force. It accompanied me all day without becoming overpowering. Of course, this is a “Hello, here I am fragrance,” but it still comes across as so sexy, playful, and seductive. My nose was glued to my wrist the whole time. I couldn’t get enough of this sugary sweet, floral scent! It completely captivated me 100%. I never would have thought that I could fall so much in love with a fragrance! The price is, of course, quite steep. Nevertheless, this fragrance is worth every penny. Just a few days ago, I said, “I would never spend so much money on a fragrance.” Well, you can guess how this story ends.

Finally, I have luck with a test. I’m sitting here and feeling so happy, just like one can only feel when one is an absolute fragrance freak and has just found the holy grail... For 99%, I’ve had bad luck with my samples lately, because I admit I am very, very critical when it comes to scents. If a note bothers me, the fragrance has failed for me... So I feared it would be the same with this scent... There was always something. Too penetrating, one note dominated too much, too masculine, too piercing, and so on... Those who seek will find, as they say :-). This fragrance catapulted me straight to heaven... Wow, what a dream scent... I am smitten.. Finally, a feminine floral fragrance without piercing annoying notes that somehow come across as deliberately different.. A perfect blend of orange blossom and Bulgarian rose and an extraordinarily gentle and soft neroli. Gentle, soft, and super feminine is this fragrance.. It doesn’t get more feminine than this.. Not a single note is piercing or pushes past the other notes, nothing is annoying and no note is penetrating. Everything is in 100% perfect harmony.. The note of marshmallows is simply so perfectly blended with the other notes that the fragrance doesn’t become a gourmand, but rather the most beautiful floral scent with a little sweet marshmallow on top, which I have tested for years..

Love, don't be shy...be EXTREME...simply extremely delicious and perfect. This scent is so damn amazing, this powdery, sugar-dusted rose. I wouldn't say this fragrance is typically floral. It's more of a sugary candied rose, with minimal freshness, almost slightly citrusy, faintly resonating. For me, the comparison to a rose sculpted from sugar is the most fitting. Delicate and overwhelming at the same time. And like any delicious sugary treat, this fragrance is extremely addictive. The longevity is great, the sillage in the freshly sprayed phase is very strong, then the scent becomes almost skin-close, yet always slightly perceptible. I never thought I would love a rose scent this much, but Kilian has done it. Compared to the OG "Love Don't Be Shy (Perfume) | Kilian," I find the Extreme version significantly denser and rounder, more powerful and not as sticky.
