In my opinion, you can wear this fragrance all year round, but for me, it is just perfect right now in spring.

Kilian....a house that is repeatedly associated here in the forum with words like "noble, expensive, Rihanna's signature, etc." Thanks to a dear perfume friend, a sample has landed with me. Recently, I thought "Marshmallow, that's just your thing, you can almost order it blindly." I generally like sweet gourmand fragrances, but with Love don’t be shy, I was catapulted into another level of marshmallow. The scent starts off a bit bitter, almost so bitter that I doubted whether it was going in a direction I desired. I unfortunately don’t know what Neroli smells like...maybe it’s this note that doesn’t sit well with me at first. This bitterness, yes almost bitterness, lingers for a while and is only slightly softened by the orange blossom. After an hour, I was almost at the point of saying "No, this isn’t going to work between us....please delight others who are more inclined" and then suddenly it’s there....marshmallow. Sweet and delicious, yet with a depth and wickedness. Not candy store sweet but "Hey, come here, let yourself be seduced. I’ll turn your head and you’ll think of me forever." Only the rose can somewhat tame the smoky marshmallow note, and it does this very well. It reminds me of that powder that envelops marshmallows. H/S I would describe as above average. Unfortunately, I can’t say anything about the bottle and packaging, as it is a sample. The scent is truly beautiful, exciting, and multifaceted, and certainly rightly positioned in the upper price segment.
… you don’t need to be shy. This rosy, floral fragrance, which initially lays over the sweet marshmallow and delicately envelops it, is simply beautiful to my nose.

After I got a sample of the regular version, I obviously had to test this more intense variant as well. So off to the Kö! With the first spray, I found it extremely floral, not at all what I usually prefer, but after a short waiting period, the typical love feeling was there. I actually think it’s successful as an Extreme version.

This is a beautiful fragrance. I actually prefer it to the original. The rose gives this perfume a very nice balance of sweet and floral. It also lasts much longer than the original version. Is it extreme? The lasting power makes it extreme, but the scent is more of a flanker than an intense version of Love, Don't Be Shy. I absolutely love it.

The scent is immediately appealing when first sprayed - sweet but delicate, really wonderful. The problem is that the fragrance is not really special. There are scents you want to smell constantly because they are simply incredible, but unfortunately this one fades at some point, as you end up smelling it too often.

The perfect elegant versatile modern All day man fragrance, perfect blended beautiful modern fragrance whit a touch of old money , love this fragrance , simply perfect and all occasion the right decision to wear elysium Perfect in the summer days versatile too in a sunny day in spring saison Sillage and durability are not a bomb but 5/6 are really top for a summer fresh fragrance

This is a beautiful fragrance. I'm a big fan of Roja Dove but have issues with pricing and Longevity of many of his fragrances. I don't think Mr Dove smelt Aventus and decided oh I can make that better and more potent. This is his unique creation and boy is it good. Finally a fresh citrus scent that lasts. But it's so much more and quite complex. It's very smooth but has good projection. I find I'm smelling myself constantly and have a very luxurious cloud around my body. It's woody and slightly dusty with very amazing natural citrus notes. I'm early on into smelling this fragrance but it does change over the 2 hours I have been wearing it. It's a sexy, warm weather fragrance which is perfect summers night out on a Mediterranean island. So good.

This truly blows the cologne out of the water! It's overall just so much smoother and has a more prominent sweet vetiver note in the drydown that is incredibly addictive. The night time version of Elysium with the cologne being much more of a daytime casual scent. 10/10!

There are some fragrances you come across and they are just miles beyond anything else you've smelled. Only a few things come to mind when I think of things I've smelled and just been blown away: Blue Sapphire Supercharged Neroli Portofino Forte "Hermessence Ambre Narguilé | Hermès" Baccarat Rouge 540 Extrait de Parfum Reflection 45 Well Elysium pour Homme Parfum belongs with the others in that group. This one is 99% identical scent wise to "Elysium Parfum Cologne (Eau de Parfum) | Roja Parfums". At discounters I can regularly find the PC version for $180 and the extrait version for $250. Go with this version and not the PC. I've tried layering the PC version with this version and it doesn't seem to make any difference, so it seems like a complete waste to own "Elysium Parfum Cologne (Eau de Parfum) | Roja Parfums" let alone both... Do yourself a favor buy this version, It's better in every possible way...albeit, not much.

Amazing versatile Fragrance. Much stronger and deeper than the Parfum Cologne version and 2.5x times the performance (I use 4 sprays of the Extrait and get 12 hours, while 12 sprays of Cologne get me around 4.5-5 hours, so I end up applying again after 4 hours, for a total of about 20-24 sprays with Cologne version). That makes the price difference much more bearable. This fragrance can be classified in the same genre as Aventus, Blue de Chanel, etc, but it doesn't smell like any of them. You can tell right away, the ingredients used are of the highest quality and that nothin in the market really smells like this. So the uniqueness is very high, even in this so popular genre of fragrances. it doesn't have to be daring or animalistic to be a great fragrance and this proves it. It starts with a fresh burst of citrus (I pick up a lot of grapefruit, some tart lemon and bergamot), which then transition to a beautiful vetiver dominated mid, which is then sustained by the backbone of vanilla, ambergris and some wood notes. Signature fragrance worthy for someone that is not looking to own 100 frags, if you have the means to use this as a daily wear. Cheers

The citrus and fruity musk opening does remind me of Aventus a little, I guess. However, I do not really see this as Aventus-like fragrance and warn you, blind buyers: don't! Don't assume this is just an Aventus clone, it is not!!! After Aventus like opening, the fragrance goes into traditional fougere territory and pretty much stays there.

After loving the new Oceania Parfum , I decided to revisit Elysium Parfum, having only ever tried it previously on strip in a store. I thought then that it was very "basic" since I was excited about trying new scent profiles back then and was essentially a fragrance edgelord.

It pains me to say that this is just not that special. Beyond my ego telling me how cool this tiny $500 bottle is, there isn't much there. The opening is great and smells like bubblegum and grapefruit, then it gets boring- woody/musky/galbanum. It settles into the skin quickly and becomes incredibly flat.

The Elysium Pour Homme Parfum is a masterful fragrance crafted by the renowned perfumer Roja Dove. The bottle stands out with a luxurious design, blending a brilliant gold finish with black crystal accents, reflecting the high quality and uniqueness of the scent.

Opens with lots of apple, though its acidity is tamed with some gentle smoky darkness. The perfume progresses very linearly; I hardly notice any changes as the scent gradually fades from my skin over the course of about 8 hours.

This perfume could have been called Incense Rose and it would be more realistic, the oud of this perfume is so light that it is almost not felt, it is, but in a very vaporous and ephemeral way. The beginning is one of the most beautiful parts of this perfume and the one that lasts the least, a sigh, but it leaves you ecstatic with vaporous and balsamic spices asking for more. Next, a splendid smoky rose opens up, truly beautiful, on a woody, balsamic, warm and spicy background. From here the rose and incense agreement remains until the end, I only conceive small changes of nuances, which are caused by the evolution of the notes that make up the background, sometimes they stand out some more than others, and thus make up an aroma very dynamic, despite always smelling of smoky rose. Of moderate high duration, with a performance of about 7 or 8 hours, and moderate wake from the start, although somewhat more noticeable in the first hour. Perfume from cold or temperate climates and to wear it at night preferably. As for recommending it, this time I would say that it is not a perfume for all noses, so better to try it before purchase. The perfume is of quality, but I think it is a scent that is already very exploited.

Incense Oud is a truly fabulous incense scent. The natural smelling incense accord that immediately hits you with the top notes mixed with hints of rose and citrus, hanging around through the heart notes is out of this world incredible, and the best I have smelled to date, eclipsing even the great Avignon. I guess I would describe it as similar to Avignon, but smoother and just overall more refined and somewhat more subtle. Incense Oud is the much more wearable and versatile scent of the two by far, IMO. In the base notes, I get some Oud mixed in with the sandalwood and musk dominant base (even though it is not listed in the official notes). That gets me to the primary concern I have with Incense Oud... There really is not that much Oud in it to my nose. At $395 for a 50ml bottle, that is a relatively high price to pay for what amounts to even a reference incense scent, when other excellent ones are available for a fraction of the price like the aforementioned Avignon as well as others. That said, if you are looking for the best incense scent you can find regardless of price (and don't mind that the scents name is a tad off), then I have not found as good as Incense Oud and would have to recommend it, awarding it a strong 4.5 star out of 5 rating.

I've had a sample of this banging around in my sample box for some time now. I haven't had much of a chance to truly try it, but with a bit of free time available today I found it and whacked the entire sample bottle to my left arm. It's beautiful. It's pure Frankincense on me ... very little else and quite linear. I'm a bit of an Oud nut and I don't get very much of it here. I had a very strict Catholic upbringing (yep, parochial school et al ... it's taken years of therapy to get over LET'S NOT GO THERE!!!) and without much say in the matter became an altar boy at around the age of 10. It was my duty to carry the censer (the incense burner) and I would dutifully swing it about (like a fabulous gold Judith Leiber handbag!!) until I was fairly obscured by nimbus like clouds of fragrant smoke :o). Incense Oud smells EXACTLY like the little gold box of resinous crystals that housed the incense we used! Is Kilian Hennesey's Incense Oud worth it's (IMO) exhorbitant price? Not really ... as lovely as it is. I think the sublimely gorgeous Mr. Hennesey would do well to market his fragrances in less costly packaging. I read somewhere that a 50ml bottle at GBP 140 is refillable at GBP 60. That's QUITE a difference for a pretty bottle! Nevertheless ... one cannot take away the fact that this is a REALLY beautiful fragrance ... I'd have it if I could justify the price!

Wonderful smell .... a mixture of oud, herbs, sandalwood, pepper (wish it was black - it would have been more masculine), patchouli and rose. could be more incense smells - at least for me. It develops beautifully and holds for a very long time. addictive beast ... and it's very - every now and then it's nice to smell the sprayed spots ;-) As a male and a collector of dark fragrances ... incense, agaric (oud), vativer, woody and not sweet - I recommend this fragrance, but probably more for women. The fragrance is really beautiful, unique and addictive. Price .... um ... expensive and too expensive in my opinion. So to sum up - there are ahs and ohs (PROS), but also some (MINUSES): the price, more feminine (rose and pink pepper), there could have been more incense. This is of course in my opinion. Personally, I RECOMMEND ... and the cons can be treated as ... he "nitpicks" ;-)

Ah the good old Kilian. Spend your hard earned money on a good smelling But very generic scent, which unfortunatelly does not perform as it should for the Price. The bottle is beautiful like all Kilian bottles, But the scent itself again, just like all kilian scents, does not perform the best. try before buying. Otherwise you would need to respray often.

Gabriel Fauré composed the Requiem op.48 between the deaths of his two parents. One of the most beautiful musical works I have ever heard. Liturgically speaking, a Requiem is the holy mass for the deceased. Thank you R., for enriching me immensely here; this fragrance fits exceptionally well with it.

.... is nagging again. But really, and the lovers of this fragrance can gladly tar and feather me (that would reflect the scent perfectly). Before I really get started, here are a few facts about Oud: Agarwood has a very wide range of scents, from balsamic-sweet to spicy-bitter and woody-animalic.

I do think that this fragrance contains Oud. Somehow, Oud smells different in almost every Oud scent - yet my brain switches to a mode that says "ahhhh Oud," even though I can't always articulate that olfactory impression in words. It's more like a bed into which the entire fragrance has been laid.

Most of the time, after testing a week full of mediocrity or even truly terrible fragrances (the latter being somewhat more entertaining^^), suddenly and unexpectedly, a perfume comes along that truly blows you away, enchants you, and brings back your faith, passion, and sense of happiness.

.. then I would be thrilled. There are fragrances that develop the penetrating smell of cleaning gasoline on me in the top note. Incence Oud unfortunately does too! I suspect this comes from the grapefruit combined with pepper or cardamom. As already mentioned, IO starts with a piercing gasoline smell on my skin and I resist the urge to wash the scent off immediately.

Forget the notes. If you get wrapped up in that endless list of notes on this fragrance, you'll miss the forest for the trees. Yes, it's got citrus; yes, it's got florals; yes, it's got some musk. But focusing your attention on any one of those elements means you risk trying to put this fragrance into a box in which, once you wear it, it stubbornly refuses to stay. This is a masterful, sensational blend that envelopes you in a breezy, almost gauzy veil of soft and delicate aromas that also lingers and projects far beyond what you'd expect for something so bright. It's transportive, evocative, and even intoxicating. I can't overstate how SOFT the aroma itself is. I don't mean "soft" performance: I mean that there's something so sophisticated and elegant, something round and gentle, about the way this fragrance approaches you. But once it draws you in, it refuses to leave you. It stays with me for hours and hours - easily one of the best-performing fresh scents in my collection. I know the name seems to point toward water, and there is something somehow watery about this - but for me, this evokes air. "Oceania" also refers to a region, and this fragrance does put me in mind of a warm, heady floral breeze in some idyllic tropical seaside. This was such a surprise. On the page, it doesn't necessarily read like something I'd love. But on skin, I just can't get enough of this stuff. Easily a top 5 fragrance for me, and makes a serious case for itself as my absolute favorite.

Oceania has a super citrus, refreshing, and slightly sweet opening, not that sharp biting citrus. Delicious exit! Lavender is already present, bringing that slightly powdery aspect of cleanliness. This lavender, together with the green and fresh spices, place the fragrance in a very pleasant aromatic zone of freshness. In the center is a luxurious bouquet of flowers in which Roja Dove gives her demanding personal touch, raising the level of perfume to levels of sophistication that few brands can reach. Everything distributed with great balance, care and without weight and intensity, keeping the composition in a safe and pleasant field always. Easy to please the user and close people. It has a satisfactory average performance for this classification of perfumes. Oceania is to shine on days of intense heat! The duet of iris with violet with a powdery nuance, fragrant, without makeup vibration that, intertwining with musk, reinforces the feeling of being clean and fragrant all the time. Towards deeper oceans with mossy greenish woods, and I feel the juniper also bringing only depth to the composition. It has an ambery accord of vanilla with benzoin that accompanies the fragrance throughout its evolution. But the protagonists of this creation are bright citrus, florals with emphasis on lavender, iris intertwined with moss and a clean musky. Oceania is a simple fougére with exquisite ingredients. I didn't get any aquatic/oceanic or blue vibes, but rather a lot of citrus, aromatic, floral and herbal green. And yet it's very good!

This is such a lovely scent. It’s so light, soft, airy, but very much present. It’s watery without ever being aquatic or salty. The citrus and herbal touches at the top are super vibrant, efervescent, energising, natural feeling. Really opens up your eyes. Then the way it transitions to an airy yet powdery Violet, slightly carnal jasmin and soft enveloping iris is heartwarmingly beautiful. The base is soft, musky, melds with the skin. But never stops projecting its airy, watery, fresh presence. At first glance a very simple and straightforward scent, that surprises you with its complexity and behaviour as you wear it. Climbed to the top of my favourites for warm days and, mind you, rainy days as well! I find the floral and violet nuance of this, amazing for rainy days.

This is one where the original is worth the price of admission. I've tried some clones of this one, and they all fail to capture the breezy airiness of the citrus. There's an ethereal quality to it. When it wafts, you're reminded of scents that are ancillary to a beach vacation. It's wonderful that this is accompanied without traditional aquatic notes, yet it feels aquatic. The citruses are some of the brightest out there. It serves a similar evocative purpose to Erolfa, although it is not quite as effervescent, and the scents themselves are not similar.

Very nice, quality scent, it has the DNA typical of Roja perfumes, it looks a little like Elysium, but I think it's just because of the DNA. It starts with a strong citrus scent, which first becomes floral, then becomes fruity. It's a unisex scent, but the drydown is more masculine. Its longevity is okay, compared to a summer scent, 8-10 hours on my skin.
This opens with bright, tart citrus which smells like Pixy Stix candy (I leave it up to you to discover the candy for yourself), and dries down to smell exactly like liquid fabric softener.

The Oceania combines an aromatic woody composition with a distinctive artistic touch. The bottle features a luxurious design that reflects high quality, adorned with a cap featuring shiny blue stones that evoke the color of the sea, complemented by a golden frame that enhances its elegance.

here you can find a versatile perfume for all seasons. trust me. opens with soft but bright lemon, never too much. many citrus fruits are mixed together with it to make it perfectly balanced. lavender and a few flowers in the centre, give the right creaminess. in accompaniment in the finale we can hear oakmoss and woods. how perfect everything is!

The title says it all. This is a very simple scent compared to Roja's other creations but regardless of that, it's a tart citrus bomb that does last a good while. It's great near the water as the citrus cuts through the heat. It's not worth retail price but if you can get it cheaper it's a good summer fragrance for any occasion maybe except office.

How can i describe this? I feel like i am so little in front of such a classy perfection. You know when you go to a 5 star michelin restaurant? You can complain about the price but you know you’re gonna get the most professional and high quality food you’ll ever eat. Niche perfumery at its highest peak. Classy, smart, refined, royal. Please Roja, make a discount…

My first impression: “What am I smelling? Wow, this is quite atypical for Terenzi!” At first, it's a bit absurd, hehe. Very unusual, green, and creamy. After just 10 minutes, a very elegant, green cream develops, which is beautiful in the air but still somewhat strange/very special when smelled directly on the skin. At this point, I’m really looking forward to the drydown! What remains is a coconut cream with a hint of mandarin and green tea, underlined by the sweetness of vanilla. Absolutely intriguing!

It actually didn't take me all that long to place from where I knew this scent--alas, PLAYING WITH THE DEVIL is familiar because it smells exactly like the "Pink Medicine" you had as a kid. A pink bubble-gum looking medicine with a cooling note is what you find in this fragrance. To be clear, I'm not suggesting that it smells like bubble gum. No, it's the "pink medicine." Please don't kill this messenger! It's true!

... So perhaps this is what the name is all about because this stuff is so potent, so linear, so there, in your face, your nose, everywhere that it takes a special kind of fragrance enthusiast to handle it. Not me sadly. It smells expensive in a trashy, generic and predictable way. Funny, because I like stinkers. Give me heady Orientals, lush Florals, and savage Animalics, and this girl is happy. El cheapo note as per usual is Lychee. Love the fruit. Delicious, succulent, with a scent to die for. Unfortunately, every time it's used in compositions, it produces an overpowering sickening artificial edge. Ditto here. Add peach, black currant, and pimento to the mix and you end up with a headache inducing compote that ultimately makes me feel nauseous. Devil indeed for this fits well with my idea of hell.

one of the most underrated kilian perfumes ever. sweet spicy peach peach with woods. it has a small resemblance to something that would be in a cellar. not feminine at all, even if it is a peach scent. will always have a special place in my heart. In the beginning I thought that its just a plain fruity scent without any depth, but after experimenting a bit with it I was quite impressed!

The Kilian Club clearly hasn't forgotten me, as today yet another envelope from France landed in my mailbox. The play with the devil is not so far-fetched, as the scent truly surprises me, is enticing, and cheeky in an elegant way. To put it succinctly, I would describe Playing with the Devil as fruity-powdery, and this is a combination that is completely new to me and my nose. The opening is already strong and herb-fruity. Here, I notice the blood orange and sun-ripened, fully fruity blackcurrants with their tart aroma. I cannot detect lychee and white peach; they completely fade away for me. However, this does not come across as vitamin-rich and healthy, but rather fully ripe and powerful. Now, one expects a top note to often serve as a hook and then retreat in favor of the heart note. However, with Playing with the Devil, this is not the case for me, as the opening stubbornly persists and is only supported by the spicy-floral heart note. It does not take the lead in this fragrance, as we are usually accustomed to. On the contrary, here the top note and base unite, presenting a soft, woody powderiness against the tart fruitiness, thus creating an interesting tension. Playing with the Devil is a cheerful, positive scent, but without the sometimes silly girlishness that fruity-floral perfumes often display. Additionally, I detect a certain wink, which results from the unusual harmony of the top and base notes. There is no trace of banality, even if the pyramid might suggest otherwise. The sillage and longevity are appropriate to the expressive character of the fragrance, and I thoroughly enjoyed getting to know this unusual scent.

So. This is it then. You sell your soul. You're a bit uneasy, but you really want it. You know exactly that you are the right person for this leadership position. And for everything it brings: the respect from friends and enemies, the money that will finally satisfy your wife and mother-in-law, and the company car to escape from them. And of course, the lovely blonde secretary with the insane - um... arguments. You've already worked your butt off for this position. Spent days and nights in the office, ruined your nerves and health. And now you've been passed over again! For that young show-off who has no clue about the subject but always knows how to butter up the higher-ups. This can't go on. You'll show them! You have a little secret. A direct line to the dark powers, so to speak. You've freed the old book from the dust of the last centuries and prepared the ceremony. Brewed the potion, painted the mysterious signs on the floor, and recited the old incantation. And you can feel it, it's about to happen, it's going to bubble and hiss, then the room will fill with pitch-black smoke, and then HE will stand before you, in the flesh. Now... Now... NOW it will... ---pffffttt. No bubbling and hissing. No smoke. Just a small lukewarm cloud of steam. And in the middle, a little wrinkled man. With a fruit basket in his hand. Yes, he IS the devil. No, not the accountant from the second floor. No, really not the accountant. The smoke? Yes, we got rid of that. It gave too many people headaches. We don't want that. The fruit basket looks much friendlier. You look at him in disbelief. And then at the book. Did you forget something? No - all there: allspice, pepper, patchouli, sandalwood, cedar, benzoin - everything. And if you concentrate, you can still perceive the scent. Maybe you should have taken more of it? Much more? The homeopathic dose had already surprised you. There's probably more patchouli in every women's fragrance from the 80s. And tonka, vanilla, and flowers? It was in the recipe, so you just poured it in. Together with the fruity scent emanating from the fruit basket, it now creates more of a cozy, feel-good atmosphere than a foreboding of hell. And you really are not...? NO. NOT the accountant. Why does everyone always think of accountants??? But never mind, let's get to the point. Your soul? No, I can't use that. It's not worth anything these days, such a soul... Well, I want money, what did you think? 195 euros... No, you won't get that position for that... No, not the secretary either. Really not. We've reoriented: potions are out, we now offer fragrances. Here - the ones in the white bottles are my favorites - sooo nice! And this one - a really aesthetic combination of blood orange and lychee, underlined by peach, and with a gentle transition to a floral-vanilla base. With a splash of stronger ingredients, so it doesn't get too boring. But really just enough that it doesn't even annoy the finest nose. It instantly lifts your spirits, and with good spirits, everything is much easier. It would make a lovely gift for your wife! No? Well, okay, but think about it again. Maybe you could impress the secretary with it...? See you soon, I'll leave you my business card here ;-)

Hello! I'm feeling like Turandot, as I too had my mailbox once again filled to the brim with Kilian samples today. :) However, when it comes to analysis, I'm not like Turandot; two noses, two thoughts: First of all, what a pity! It's a shame that the fine (untitled) bitterness of the blood orange jam fades away so quickly.

Ned Flanders, whom I hope you all know, as he is one of the most famous Simpsons characters ever, is a very devout person. The fact that he is the devil in a Halloween episode and gives Homer Simpson a donut that he must "only" pay for with his soul is all the more amusing.

PwtD starts off very fruity like a sparkling fruit cocktail. You can smell the combination of fresh berries and blood orange-peach omnipresent. These core components accompany the fragrance throughout its entire duration and give the scent its zesty fruity character. After about two hours, floral notes blend into the fragrance.

“Playing with the Devil” is an intriguing name that suggests a lot. The fragrance opens with strong peach and lychee, which personally reminds me a lot of peach-flavored thirst quencher, evoking a nostalgic feeling. The peach feels ripe, and the lychee appears intermittently. As it develops, floral notes emerge, with the rose being particularly dominant.

Playing with the Devil is like a dance between innocence and seduction. Behind a sweet smile and captivating eyes lies something mysterious, almost dangerous - just like in this fragrance. Zesty blood orange and dark blackcurrant open the game bright, fruity, enticing.

So, I was hearing a lot of hype around this perfume how people thought it was just amazing. So I had high expectations on it from the beginning. Decided to blind-buy a bottle and hope for the best. It came, I opened, I sprayed. I did not really know what to say after that. It was good for sure, but it was just nothing special, it felt a bit boring and not at all what I expected. If it would have cost 150$ I would be okey with it, but at the price-tag it has, it’s just not good enough.

Many a fraghead shy away from citrusy perfumes. I think it’s an unwritten rule in the sub-culture (I’m more than pleased to be a part of, however finicky). Most would scoff at this one as well. I, however, enjoy it very much given the practical opportunity: warmer weather. Do you know the famous and popular Bvlgari Tygar? 3 notes: Grapefruit, ginger, and ambroxan. Actually quite nice. Constructed by the legendary Jacques Cavallier. Tygar is hidden here, as in a bush, behind leafy mint and spiced rum. Less BR540 airy, as Tygar is, relying on that ambroxan for that near invisible push that others enjoy and you will rarely experience after the initial sprays. This is more standard fare in such regards. You will enjoy it throughout. It is long lasting for its genre, very pleasant, and never boring. I have to give kudos here. Some say it’s like a mojito. I can’t disagree. It’s much more bright and citrusy than the other mojito experience you might find in Guerlain’s Homme, which is about 1/10th the price, btw, and far more floral than citrus in comparison. Liken to colors and textures, Burlington is bright, sparkling gold-hued yellow while GH is velvety bright pink. Both are great in their own right! I get FAR more mint in Burlington, and as much of a fan of Guerlain as I am I must admit the Roja smells much more luxurious (as usual, and why I am such a fan). There’s much more going on here than I give justice to. In the end, if you know Tygar and like the idea of that with an addition of potent mint supported by rum then you won’t go wrong here. There is certainly a Tygar hiding inside Burlington 1819.

If you're ever chewing Juicy Fruit, or are around someone who has a fresh piece in, the scent of it is so strong at first, and it's wonderful. Burlington 1819 smells so much like that. This is Juicy Fruit chewing gum with more depth. I was not expecting that from this, based on the name of this but I have to admit I am in love with this one. This one has really great performance, as most things from Roja do (except Oceania.....) and a really strong projection which is nice for a fruit heavy scent. I think this one would be magical on any gender, any setting. My only real negative here is that this is super linear...and with strong performance you're getting that same smell for a long time. After a few hours it's almost too sweet, too overpowering. I'm just not sure on this one, as much as I absolutely loved this one at first...after a few hours I'm almost wishing it would go away.

I have to mention straight away that I’m not a fan of citrus based perfumes. I don’t like those on my skin and I don’t like to smell those on anyone. I find those boring, extremely uncharming and all of those has been done a million times. Roja Parfums Burlington 1819 IS THE ONE AND ONLY citrus scent which I love and even like. Burlington opens up with an amazingly natural smell of fresh Grapefruit and Lime with a hint of Mint and it never gets synthetic. That smell of citruses is so realistic, so bright, uplifting and delightfully different than those million others and it lasts long time. I can even say that citruses are delicious here. In Burlington all used different citruses are blending with a delicated smokiness and beautiful mossy woody base. Tobacco is not dirty nor too dry but it's easily noticeable. I like how the fresh nature of the fragrance, thanks to both citrus and spices, is combined with warm notes like Vanilla and Benzoin which is a note reminiscent of it. Those together with Labdanum and woody notes create a more interesting fragrance with depth, power and numerous unique tones. On my skin this scent is more simple, let's say more feminine as well, and as I test all of my scents nowadays on my husband’s skin as well I can say that the performance on his skin is deeper, darker and stronger and a bit more interesting than on my skin. What seems to be hidden on my skin is Ginger and Rum and overall the beautiful complex drydown with dark nuances is somewhat lighter on my skin - amazing anyway. Airy Saffron is barely detectable. I enjoy this scent a lot in both kind of ways how it performs but I have to admit that if it’s admirable on my skin, it’s totally unique experience on warmer skin. Most of citrus dominated scents try to imitate Lemon or Citron (in the bad way) and I think it’s lack of imagination since there is many different citrus to use - most common ones being Bergamot, Sweet Orange, Orange Bigarade (Bitter Orange), Mandarin, Clementine, Yuzu, Lime, Lemon, Citron, Verbena and Grapefruit. Roja has chosen the best ones imo into this scent while Yuzu being my favorite as a note in perfumes from other olfactive families. If you love citrus scents this is something which you really need in your collection. Any other citrus is not comparable with this one. This is just simply AMAZING, so special. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

Now, this thing is highly addictive! To be completely honest, this one just blew me away! I am a big fan of orientals but I wanted a fragrance which I could wear through the whole year, especially during the summer but with oriental facets..and that's exactly what Burlington 1819 is! Lively start with sparkling lime and grapefruit as the first notes you get. Followed by uplifting mint, ginger, oakmoss and cashmere woods..then everything suddenly go quiet..like calm before the perfect storm..then you smell a beautiful blend of aformentioned notes with fresh tobacco dipped in finest rum. Benzoin, labdanum cumin and cedarwood are also prominent in the dry-down, giving this creation a truly unique feel. This fragrance is ideal for well groomed Gentleman or rugged but stylish one too. Polivalent fragrance with many layers! Hands down, one of my favorite dry-downs ever! longevity on my skin is good 8 hours and sillage is moderate but veeeery pleasing! I will be wearing this one a lot!

The fragrance opens with bright notes of grapefruit and lime, to which is added a very fresh note of mint. A heart of golden rum, ginger and refined spices create a fantastic contrast between past and present. Notes of Amber, precious woods and tobacco mix with soft notes of vanilla and patchouli to create a woody base that gives structure to this masterpiece.

Burlington 1819 is a perfume that was created to celebrate the five-year existence of Roja's leading perfumery in the famous place and home of many luxury brands, Burlington Arcade, which was built 200+ years ago, in 1819 to be exact.

Burlington 1819 is a pretty simple, elegant, easy wearing citrus that doesn't bring much to the table. If money isn't much of a problem and you have fallen for the, potentially, false pretense of Roja "luxury" then sure, it is a fine spring summer frag, but I think the brand offers better elsewhere.

what can we say that hasn't been said about Roja? here it touches simplicity in a harmonious, decisive, satisfying way at every moment. few manage to create things so simple but at the same time so complex. it is one of the few brands where I really feel the three-dimensionality of the ingredients. pure mastery in this man.

At the beginning it might smell citrousy and minty, but once your nose get used to it and when it settles, it changes absolutely. The better way for me to describe it is to take baccarat rouge, remove its sweetness and add tomato leaf. Smells reaaaaally expensive, sophisticated, elegant and very very complex, while staying really likeable from people.

Can't Stop Loving you is quite shy compared to her predecessor, "Love, Don't Be Shy". She is quite literally the meek sister of the praised Riahnna favorite. This composition is "Love" without the warm sultry notes and heady florals. CSLY is a luminous floral centered around orange blossom, very fitting for Spring and Summer. What we have here is a day & night situation. I'm always excited for olibanum, but could only detect whispers of oakmoss in the later phases. I suppose it wouldn't be a true white floral otherwise. Kilian always comes with great expectations, but I am greatly underwhelmed by this release. A safe quality choice however, for entry level or someone seeking simplicity. Perhaps the subtitle should be, "Love Be Shy".

Cant stop loving you is a great addition to the Love line of Kilian Fragrances and has its distinct place among its siblings. It trades the marshmallow of Love Dont be Shy for honey and a heavier dose of Orange Blossom. This creates in my view a fresher and more universal fragrance, wearable in most occasions / seasons except for winter. It almost feels like Love Dont be Shy and Woman in Gold, also by Kilian, were merged and the combination of the two brought about this fragrance. Longevity is average for me, definitely lesser than the two mentioned before, though this is less of an issue, since it's more appropriate to wear in the hotter seasons. Overall I am happy with this purchase, as it's an easier dumb reach than love dont be shy or woman in gold, but I was secretly hoping for something with more punch. I will not be getting rid of this from the collection, maybe only if I can get my nose on Love dont be Shy Eau Fresh.

Starts out slightly sweet and pretty floral from the honey and orange blossom. The honey and jasmine take up the early and middle stages of the wear. Then, finally, the earthier moss and resinous incense notes emerge along with the vanilla. Overall, it's nice. This reminded me of honeysuckle until the paradisone kicked in and turned my nose (I do not like jasmine notes). Won't be wearing my sample again or buying a full bottle due to the jasmine, but it's not horrible.

The fragrance is pleasant, but it does have more spice than sweetness. There is a hint of sweet, but it’s subtle. This is heavy to the floral notes followed by spicy notes as it drives down. Overall, it’s not unpleasant, but I don’t feel like it is something I would gravitate to the longevity lasted all day on me and the village was good without being too overpowering. I would give this a six out of 10 for a rating.

the scent is sweet but in an elegant way; not candy-like, more of a warm honey-vanilla with a hint of wood. It has something soft and cozy about it, perfect for cooler days. There’s a touch of BR540 in it, but it’s gentler. On me, the longevity is very good and the projection is balanced — noticeable but not overpowering. The fragrance has class and a unique warmth.

I was very curious about this fragrance and now the time has finally come, a strong spray of the new Kilian scent lands on my wrist: Bam - a hefty dose of sweet orange blossom hits me right away and my first thought is, wow, as if someone mixed Love don’t be shy with Sweet Redemption.

My favorite piece of furniture in my parents' living room was a high-gloss polished music chest. Even as a little kid, I understood that the "La La" came from there. When I got a bit older, I could operate it by myself. I listened to a lot of classical music, but also the songs that were hits in my parents' youth. Ray Charles' I can't stop loving you was also among them.

A sunny afternoon in L.A.: well-to-do ladies over 30 stroll along the designer shops of Rodeo Drive. Expensive sunglasses, spring blouses, and pencil skirts, bags dangling from their wrists, ridiculously expensive cars parked on the side of the road, the sidewalks impeccably clean. Overall, I remember Rodeo Drive as more extravagant than 5th Avenue in New York.

Mature grace enters the room confidently knows what you need. Strong, self-sufficient, no longer playful yet playfully enticing Summer meadow evening warm and wine-drunk embraces you and us. Laughter, clear and full in the moment of happiness. You invite.

In golden drops of sweet splendor, honey merges, sweet power. The orange blossoms gently fade, in tender love, sweet pleading… Their scent unites, a love play, like sweet dreams, soft and still. The bees dance, humming, joyful, a love song in the flower choir. Honey kisses sweet as summer days, with orange blossoms, sweet tale.

This scent isn't for the really young people/demographic.... The ideal age for this fragrance is 30+ & up.... . When you smell this fragrance off the bottle/atomizer, to me & a coupple people have agreed, it smells like a mixed drink. Particularly, a jack & coke..... It has this beautiful boozy note that says it's in the base but you can smell it clearly in the fragrance as soon as you spray it. . When I spray in on my skin, I get a little bit more benzoin & floral notes, along with the touch of cognac along with the tobacco. This scent is fun & very pleasant for the crowd as well. I received multiple compliments the first & 2nd time I've worn this.... . I'd wear this mostly in spring & fall, those nights you are in a bar/club or even at a bon fire/party/house party/get together. This scent will have women & men both telling you how much they like it. It's worth the buy, the presentation is very well done & the bottle is very nice/classy! Easy Blind buy for me, but if you dnt like seductively, boozy fragrances, you won't like it. But I LOVE IT!

Currently I found out, this fragrance is named "Creation-E" (different to Europe) in the United States. Nevertheless, doesn´t matter if Enigma pour Homme or Creation-E, this is the most brilliant and perfect fragrance, I ever had. Its outbalanced, smooth body derives from rich and luxurious ingredients. Though in my German review I included a riddle for the audience, here I will keep it short and simple: The overwhelming, sweet and oriental touch of the whole experience is due to the fine cognac and vanilla notes, which can be smelled from the beginning to the very end. It is like to open Cognac and Tom Fords Tobacco Vanille and smell both simultaneously. Ok, a little bit more is included in this one. The first impression by spraying it to the skin offer crisp and dazzling citrus notes and a bit like an open bottle of fresh and icy-cold cherry coke or cream soda, though not too sweet it would stick on you. This could be the mix of Bergamot, Neroli and Heliotrope. Together with Jasmine the impression turns into something creamy, like almonds. Hard to describe the balance between fresh and creamy notes on the top, but which lead the path to the golden heart. The heart reveals quickly and offers the appetizer, spiced vanilla cream with cardamom and ginger, before the basenote invites to enjoy a cigar with sweet, greasy tobacco and first-class cognac in a gentlemen´s room. Overall, this fragrance lasts for more than 12 hours by a very small amount of it applied to the skin. The Sillage is a beast and you´ll get tons of compliments for it. Due to the horrifying price, this is the slightest Roja Dove should offer to his clients with this creation. By the way, this is the only Roja Dove Perfume I´d buy again. Unfortunately I don´t know, how the extrait is like, this review is about the Eau de Parfum.

I finally got a decant of it after I bought a full bottle of the Parfum Cologne version since many people said it is a better version of Parfum Cologne and I love the Parfum Cologne so much. Ok, I really love both versions but I would say it’s kinda redundant to get both in FB. They smell exactly the same to my nose except the Parfum Cologne has much longer lasting of the frizzy opening while the Pour Homme Parfum version dries down to heart and base much quicker. Parfum Cologne last about 7-8 hours on my skin with bigger projection while the Parfum version the frizziness fades quickly then dries down to the boozy and woody that stay closer to the skin but last 10+ hours on my skin. Honestly my nose can’t detect the difference of their quality because they are both divine. Depends on what you’re looking for. If you looking for a longer lasting and don’t want big projection, go with the Parfum version but if you live in a warm climate (I’m living in Los Angeles where mostly very warm in a year), I think the Cologne version is more suitable. The longer frizziness provides a fresher take of it. I will still get a full bottle of it when I finish my decant of it because it is nice to add it to my collection but I just don’t know when I’m gonna finish the decant as the weather in LA starting to get warm already and I’ve been reaching to the Cologne more often.

Enigma Pour Homme Parfum from English House Perfumery of Niche Haute Luxury Roja Parfums is a Oriental Amber Spicy Alcoholic Tabacado Woody Men's perfume. It was launched in 2013 and the perfumer who signs this fragrance is Roja Dove. With a lot of delay I finally managed to bring this iconic creation by Roja Dove to the collection. Enigma alongside Amber Aoud are the House's biggest bestsellers. Enigma Parfum unfolds on my skin to my sense of smell with a brief opening of fresh green bergamot and a white masculine floral bouquet, light and sprinkled with the very rich ambergris, of very high quality, a striking characteristic of the brand. This initial part merges with tobacco and vanilla, this classic duet is dominant in the fragrance. Which, adding to a well-spiced and spicy accord, carries a bittersweet almost sour facet... and it still has the alcoholic aspect of the perfume with the famous Enigma brandy bringing a tasty warmth to the composition. The patchlouli here brings its woody side and the benzoin reinforces the ambery character of the perfume. As for the "controversial" Cola soda accord that some feel others don't, well I've been addicted to Coca-Cola since I was a child and drink it every day [I love it]; and when I met the old version discontinued in EDP years ago, I remember that I didn't notice this similarity, today paying more attention and maybe even suggesting I can get some Coca-Cola vibe. Enigma Pour Homme Parfum is a perfume: Ambré Delicious, Rich Sophisticated, Mild Fresh, and at the same time Spicy Hot, and also Dry Powdery. And even with these alleged antagonisms; this fragrance delivers a lot of Virility with Sensuality and a lot of Elegance. Roja's Masterpiece and with a Great Performance!

Roja Enigma PPH is a sophisticated fragrance for the modern day gentleman and made with high-quality ingredients. The opening is bright, fresh and fizzy, and shortly thereafter, ginger, cardamom and black pepper provide some spiciness. But the best part of this scent profile is the heart and base where the boozy cognac, smooth tobacco, and sweet vanilla combine exquisitely to form an instant classic. Warmth from benzoin adds depth to the fragrance. In general, Roja is a house I do not gravitate towards (can’t get along with the house DNA), but Enigma PPH is an exception to the rule because I thoroughly enjoy the scent profile.

Rich shades of vanilla, warm Cola-Cognac, and creamy sandalwood come together in this exquisite blend by @rojaparfums. I wouldn't consider it too playful, but it is surely seductive and appealing, I can't imagine someone disliking it. It’s a fragrance has depth and sophistication, revealing new layers as it unfolds on the skin.

This is a release from 2013 by ROJA DOVE in pure perfume concentration, there is also a parfum cologne version which I do not have but smells similar. If you are wondering which is it in EU called Enigma and in the US Creation E, is due to some copyright issues.

What a beauty. An enigmatic fragrance: you smell it, and you wonder: "Wow! What is this fragrance? Where does it come from?" Crisp, boozy, warm spicy. Citrus in the opening, Roja-style, gives a pleasant crispness and brightness.

Enigma smells like a luxurious cola, with a fizziness up top that I presume is some kind of aldehyde. This is what I put on if I want to feel classy while having presence. After two hours the fizziness disappears, making the cola feel flat. What remains is a sweet, warm, boozy tobacco amber that keeps you cozy throughout the day.

Mannn this stuff has always blew my mind... Opened a second bottle today and god damn, Every time I smell this fragrance I am stuck with alacrity . The Boozy note is just tooo good. To my nose its a best cognac scent ever made... I generally sift through all the fragrance daily to choose the best SOTD, but for this fragrance,I need not give second thought...

Sidonie Lancesseur, the perfumer behind Kilian's Apple Brandy is also the nose responsible for many other wonderfully boozy scents such as Straight to Heaven, Single Malt or Frapin's 1270. To say she has mastered the alcoholic genre would be an understatement. Here Madame Lancesseur has created yet another quintessential masculine Kilian fragrance: boozy but classy, sober yet playful, elegant and mischievous at the same time like a James Bond in party mode. In that sense the scent shares more similarities with the sweet Single Malt than the drier Straight to Heaven, although if the former featured whiskey and the latter rum, in Apple Brandy the protagonist drink is a more laid-back calvados or distilled cider liquor. The sharp, tannin-filled opening is followed by the deep aroma of old oak barrels and smoke, and the balance of this simple and effective combo shifts as the scent dries down, from a rather fruity and very alcoholic opening to a much woodier, comforting and subdued final phase. Performance is discreet throughout but acceptable, perhaps a necessity for a subtle scent that invites a few chosen ones to come closer if they want great things to happen. All in all another beautiful creation worth celebrating with the right company and a drink or two.

Before Kilian released Old Fashioned , the decently executed product adjacent to the discontinued London exclusive Single Malt London , Kilian had already been selling Apple Brandy on the Rocks (AB OTR) for years. Similarly to Old Fashioned, AB OTR came as a worldwide alternative to Kilian's New York exclusive Apple Brandy New York , yet in a way, I'm not sure there even was sufficient demand to remaster this. These are some of my thoughts on my first wear of a recent 50ml full display blind-buy. With 4 sprays on my left hand, Apple Brandy New York opens sweet-fruity-boozy. Within milliseconds you can spot the resemblance to Apple Brandy on the Rocks as it has that exact same sweet-crisp Apfelschorle type smell. AB NY's top smells spicier and boozier than the fruity-fresh ambroxan-driven profile of the On The Rocks version. However, it is in the transition where the differences between the 2 products really begin to distance themselves. Very much like the dry-down of Single Malt London , there is a present amber tonality incorporated into Apple Brandy New York as it features the same style of medicinal-smelling labdanum, albeit in lower quantities than with Single Malt. The key aspect of AB NY's dry-down, however, is the dominating presence of woodiness. I would dare to say that the woodiness featured here is even more prevalent than in the re-released version of Single Malt, i.e. Old Fashioned , as you get a hefty dose of oak with a moderate amount of cedar and a mild accompanying feel of booziness. Ultimately, that's where Apple Brandy New York ends up at: in this very woody dry-down with moderate medicinal ambers and that bitter-boozy touch. The re-released version, i.e. Apple Brandy on the Rocks , retains the opening of the original version and takes the scent in a fresh-fruity direction with zero ambers and mild-to-moderate woodiness, losing out on performance (which isn't great to begin with) in the process. I'd rate the performance here to be subpar much like with many of the other scents mentioned in this review: I'd give it around 6 hours of longevity on soft sillage. As a somewhat unexpected takeaway from this review; I would dare to say that Old Fashioned , the relaunch of Single Malt London , actually smells more like Apple Brandy New York than it does like Single Malt as the wood-dominant base tones and the bitter-boozy touches offer strong overlap between the two, esp. on-skin. Unfortunately, even with that overlap, AB NY has fewer nuances in its execution, making it inferior to Old Fashioned and miles off the highs of Single Malt. I would conclude by saying that this is discontinued for a good reason.

1/3 ml is enough... to blow me away! No matter how often I have criticized Kilian as an expensive copycat (mostly rightly so!) - Apple Brandy, the New York exclusive, is top-class scent cinema, unique enough & one of the best boozy alcohol fragrances you can buy for money! There are 2 main buyer groups that will find Apple Brandy brilliant: wood fetishists & scent alcoholics who love rum, brandy & whiskey in fragrances. If you find yourself in the intersection of both groups, I believe it will be over for you faster than you can say overdraft. Vodka on the Rocks from Moscow will have a hard time topping this - but it certainly deserves a chance. However, getting a sample of that is currently almost impossible. Apple Brandy is fascinating, delicious, alcoholic, party-ready, luxurious, thick. Especially the top note is typically Kilian and hits everything out of the park that you can imagine. I love it so exaggerated, but the last time I got hit with something like this was from the doctor at my birth. And of course with Tobacco Vanille. The bigger question than a striking, attention-grabbing top note is the further development. Does a generic, boring second half of the fragrance come, which is just as typically Kilian as the head full of apples floating in brandy oak barrels? Not quite. Of course, it does mellow out, and that's why it doesn't reach the top rating, but I also like the cedar-like final act and the alcohol-soaked base mood. Bottle: you also pay for this chic presentation! Sillage: a going-out fragrance for bars & chic clubs. Longevity: the woody base lasts up to 12 hours on my skin. Conclusion: when I visit the city that never sleeps & my account is still full, I probably won't be able to resist this high-proof, expensive souvenir. At this level, only Pure Malt can evoke a similar fascination & euphoria in me.

Do you know that feeling? Sometimes, when you test a perfume, it smells so strongly of alcohol that you have to wrinkle your nose before the scent becomes pleasant. Other times, however, the fragrance smells rather deliciously of alcohol, and you would rather just down it right away. Well, with Apple Brandy, we have an alcoholic note that smells pleasant and seems quite tasty, … although it’s probably best not to drink it… But you can definitely apply it. Because, as I said, it smells quite good. Here’s my scent impression: The scent: It starts woody and sweet. You can quickly perceive the alcohol, which has turned out really well and should appeal to anyone who likes alcoholic fragrance notes. Additionally, you can also smell a bit of tobacco. The wood notes come through very well, but I can't say if it's the oak barrel. Shortly after, the fruity notes (apples) become a bit stronger, and the scent also becomes sweeter, probably due to the labdanum and ambroxan. I can also detect the vanilla quite early, which makes the scent softer and gentler. In the base, the scent is mainly woody and fruity with the sweet accents from the heart note. I also perceive the light tobacco note again. The longevity and sillage: The longevity is quite okay; the scent lingers on the skin for at least eight to ten hours. The fragrance projects fairly strongly and remains at this level for one or two hours before it slightly weakens, but is still quite noticeable. The bottle: The rectangular bottle is black and has thick glass edges. On the sides, there are elegantly shaped, circular patterns (or they would be circular if the bottle were larger). On the front, there is a metal plaque with the name and brand of the fragrance, written in a beautiful script, which makes the whole bottle look even more elegant. The black cylindrical cap features the Kilian logo on the top. Apple Brandy is a fragrance that smells of alcoholic notes, but you shouldn't imagine it as trailing a scent cloud behind you because you've looked too deeply into your glass. No, it is a pleasantly fruity and woody scented fragrance that reminds one of an alcoholic drink. I wouldn’t necessarily call this a daily scent, and it’s not particularly suitable for the office either. But as an evening fragrance, it is quite wonderful, whether you’re going out to celebrate or sitting in a bar, although in the latter case, the scent might get lost among all the other alcoholic notes :D As for the season, I would recommend autumn and winter, as Apple Brandy doesn’t quite fit the warmer season. But on colder (and wetter) days, it fits perfectly and warms you up, just like a sip of rum or something similar warms the body on frosty days (okay, I hope you all know that’s not really true, but it’s a widely held misconception!). Anyway, feel free to test it out. Anyone who doesn’t like alcohol should steer clear of this fragrance, but everyone else should give it a try. I personally think the scent is great!

Well, thanks to the current crisis and the resulting free time, I finally decided to write my first comment on a fragrance. My nose is not very experienced, but with this scent, which I find quite one-dimensional, I dare to express an opinion. First of all: The house of Kilian quickly won me over; a certain class and elegance is conveyed not only by the name Hennessy but also by the overall presentation and packaging. Beautiful boxes, custom-made cases lined with velvet, complete with locks, and flacons that feel very high-quality. All in all, very nice. If you combine this with my preference for boozy scents, you can imagine that I feel quite at home when it comes to "sniffing" the fragrances this house has to offer. After Single Malt, Intoxicated, Black Phantom, and Back to Black, I was in the mood for something new: Enter Apple Brandy! The name is, as expected, programmatic. However, the first whiff brought back memories that absolutely do not fit the image of the "premium brand" that Kilian wants to create. I grew up as a village kid, and there isn't much to do in the village besides frolicking in nature and driving the neighbors crazy when you kick a ball against a wall on the playground with half a dozen other kids during the midday quiet hours. By the time I hit my teenage years, there were then shooting festivals, village discos, and... exactly, alcohol. Sometimes mixed up, sometimes too much, but always somehow present: Korn, Berentzen, or Obstler. Imagine a tent combined with Schlager hits, Wolfgang Petry, stuffy air, smoke, pretty girls, and blurred vision, all topped off with the scent of schnapps wafting from almost every face. Apple Brandy brings back exactly this feeling for me and even more. Upon the first spray, I am overwhelmed by this alcoholic note, while a light apple note gently wafts in the background. Yes, hello and straight to the head with the stuff. Just before closing time, we grabbed a bottle of Sour Apple from Edeka before heading out to party, and it has to be finished before we can go into the tent. So down it goes quickly, intense and short. The bottle is empty, but the scent lingers. Waiting at the bus stop, warm air, and the guys around. The scent of the drink surrounds us like a cloud while we huddle in the small wooden hut. You feel grown-up, masculine, intoxicated, and ready for more. One pulls out a small bag, tobacco he swiped from his father's pack, and some rolling papers. Cool as we are, we try to roll our own cigarettes, more poorly than well, with tobacco landing everywhere and the scent mixing lightly in the air. Before we light the first one, a group of girls squeezes in with us. It smells slightly of vanilla, pleasant. The scent remains something beautiful for me. Many describe it as gentleman-like, mature, perhaps even distinguished. I can completely understand and see why someone would describe this scent that way, as it is a Kilian, boozy and impressive, but also not much more. Schnapps, to be precise, apple schnapps, and I personally associate this with village festivals and unrestrained joy. Sure, Kilian is too refined for this level, and of course, you don't smell like a drunken teenager with a bottle of Obstler in hand when wearing this perfume, but rather something "elevated." However, compared to whiskey or cognac, I believe that brandy simply does not have that gentleman club/bar flair that so many want to perceive as upscale. Sillage and longevity are completely within the range. With a performance (on my skin) of about 9 hours and a sillage that is noticeable enough not to be intrusive, you can wear it like that. Maybe not exactly to work. It will surely be great in the cold season, but I can also imagine it on a balmy summer evening in nature. All scent alcoholics will definitely enjoy this thing. Whether the ladies will like it, I would rather doubt, but scent perception is always quite subjective and dependent on the person.

Apple Brandy New York Like two sides of a coin. Young, fresh, energetic. Mature, elegant, eloquent. Jogging pants, oversized sweater, sneakers. Suit pants, turtleneck, loafers. Developments from young to old. Sparkling apples in abundance, energetic, warm, and cooling at the same time. Wooden barrels as far as the eye can see. Burnt out, alcoholic residues.

It is one of my favorites from Kilian, alongside Intoxicated. A very warm, spicy, slightly alcoholic note with the beautiful, roasted apple tone like fresh out of the oven. It lasts a long time and evokes a desire for autumn/winter vibes. When the sample is empty, a beautiful bottle will join my collection.

A fantasy journey for the Advent atmosphere - is easily achieved with this perfume. A few sprays, close my eyes, and I find myself at a Christmas market. The hot apple cider (or "Glühmost" for those not from Austria) steams from the cup I hold in my hand.

Apple Brandy starts like an olfactory aroma explosion of an alcoholic Berentzen schnapps in the flavor direction of "Sour Apple." However, this rather intense scent journey only lasts about 3 minutes. Afterwards, the top note shifts into a slightly alcoholic but still well-balanced fragrance profile with a wonderfully harmonized underpinning of smoky and woody accords.

There is a lot to say about this legendary perfume. It is definitely not for everyone, you definitely can't wear it too much. You have to adapt yourself and your outfit to this perfume, choose the place you wear it to with tweezers. But definitely, a celebration of royal and 'dirty' Chypre. Suitable for cold days. A really high-quality perfume, compared to the Chypré Extraordinaire I personally like the chypre Extraordinaire more but I have both. Another perfume that really reminds me of Diaghilev is this perfume Freefall - Etruscan Water . 8/10.

*This is a review of the Parfum version of Diaghilev. Diaghilev opens with an amazing orange-laced luscious rose floral accord with a very slight dirty cumin-like undertone. As the fragrance enters the early heart phase the very full rose remains, now joined by relatively indolic jasmine and slightly powdery iris supporting florals with a minuscule measure of early patchouli driven sweetness before hints of leather and sharp vetiver quash it. The vetiver grows in intensity throughout the dry-down until by the end of the heart phase it is a solid co-star to the rose. During the late dry-down the rose finally dissipates, leaving the sharp vetiver and supporting leather to take control, with a surprising quantity of slightly powdery oakmoss underpinning the base accord. Projection is outstanding, as is longevity at nearly 15 hours on skin. Let's get this out of the way straight off, Diaghilev is an amazing composition that conjures up visions of deep animalic's like Onda Extrait by Vero Profumo early, then leather-laced vetiver from the base of Puredistance M (another great Roja Dove composition), while infusing the composition with a similar captivating rose to the one used in Lalfeorosa by O'driu. Successfully channeling aspects of those three greats, Diaghilev is as close to a "sure thing" for lovers of those masterpieces as you will find. The bottom line is the approximately $1000 per 100ml Diaghilev in its parfum concentration is a masterpiece through and through, earning a corresponding 4.5+ stars out of 5 and an extremely strong recommendation. The near $10 per ml cost is quite dear, but compositions of this quality are extremely rare, meriting one to at least try to get their nose on a sample to witness near-perfection in a true modern day chypre composition that keeps close ties to the classics.

Is quite interesting that the differences between the original Dighilev composition and the relaunched parfum strenght are, somehow, the same differences between Mitsouko and what is known to have inspired Mitsouko, the legendary Coty Chypre. The Original Diaghilev is more muscular, dry, almost masculine, putting much more emphasis on the moss and on driest citrus and flower aromas. The Parfum, however, is like a classic Mitsouko with a nod to current chypres (it comes to my mind, besides the Amouage one listed on the similarities, Gucci Rush too). It fills the driest sections of the first version with soft peachy tones and sensual flowers that blooms on different moments on skin. The spices also seem to be more intense and dirty, but the scent itself isn't dirty. It's complex, abstract, very sensual but in a refined way. It's not a kind of fragrance that is on trend anymore, but i guess that there is always space for some high quality chypre (too bad that it's so expensive!).

Just as the title suggests, this fragrance is not for beta males. If this is you, stop reading and go pick up Daisy Eau de Toilette or something along those lines. If you get smacked, punked and disrespected on the daily, again, not for you. If you constantly get your cookies taken..... not for you. If when you speak, people stop and listen attentively, you're in the right place! Diaghilev Parfum is, in my opinion, the quintessential fragrance for the alpha male, the leader, the "by any means necessary" type of guy. A timeless, dominating chypre that screams "I'm in charge and everybody knows it." Only to be worn with a suit and tie, Magnanni on your feet and nothing less than a Mercedes-Benz. I love this fragrance!

Diaghilev by Roja Parfums is the ultimate Chypre, a true masterpiece in the world of fragrances. It’s one of those scents that feels impossible to fully describe because of its extraordinary complexity and unmatched quality. For me, it even eclipses the legendary Mitsouko by Guerlain—an homage that feels as bold as it is well-deserved. From the moment it opens, Diaghilev presents a beautifully orchestrated blend of freshness and animalic undertones. These notes stay gracefully in the background, perfectly complementing the lush, peachy heart of the fragrance. The result? A luxurious, finely tuned composition that radiates sophistication, taste, and elegance. It’s not just a perfume; it’s a work of art meant for those who see fragrance as something more than just a pleasant aroma. As for performance, Diaghilev doesn’t just deliver, it dominates. With incredible longevity and a sillage that makes a statement, this is a scent for anyone looking to leave a lasting impression. For lovers of fine perfumery, it’s a must-experience creation that embodies the essence of true luxury and craftsmanship.

Roya Diaghilev, a real theatrical perfume. It is made up of 33 raw materials. A cypre, floral, spicy perfume. Of extreme elegance and excellent persistence. This perfume is art. The ingredients are of excellent quality. It can fit for both men and women. If you want to be remembered on an important evening, this is the perfume you should wear.

I have some scents - like a pair- which are perfect to wear for couples. This is the first pair. The best classical timeless Chypres inspired by vintage Mitsouko! If you want to buy a totally new bottle and the budget is not limited I highly recommend to try these ones before buying a new version of Mitsouko or Rochas Femme.

Sergej Diaghilev, famous Russian theater impresario of the 20th century. Like a play captures and engages you at the highest level, this fragrance is like a journey into the early 1900s into Sergei's life. Thirty-three notes, thirty-three raw materials of the highest quality are masterfully dosed and combined by maestro Roja Dove into a First La Scala fragrance.

From a perfume so costly it can serve as mortgage collateral, one should expect some fireworks. In terms of craftsmanship it is fair to say that yes this is about as good as it gets. Bourgeois, decadent and pompous. Just as it should be in this genre. Despite the bombastics, something is holding me back from fully indulging in this.

I just love, love, love this scent. I have the parfum extrait and also the original EDP which is just breathtaking. I bagged the limited edition EDP bottle on ebay which came with a wooden cork and the atomiser. Wow! the cork alone perfumed my wardrobe for weeks on end. Another masterpiece from the 'professor of perfumery'.

I need to start saying that it's not my favourite Tiziana and the price that you find It is critical, said that, it's probably one of the best Tiziana notes quality, It easy at an Amouage level. It's an oregano, myrrh and the Tiziana amber gris combination, comforting, a green amber spicy, not crazy complex but true niche quality, I think that even though I like It, I'm underrating It because I like more weird fragrances but probably to people who loves amber fragrances this is one of the best in the game, wise price would be 200€ max per 100ml. Performance over the average.

Absolutely stunning. It's very similar to Ambre Sultan, but richer, warmer and more opulent. Quality, sillage and longevity are excellent. Very hard to get hold of outside of the UK so if anyone has one to sell please message me (I'm in Australia)!

Enigma Cologne starts with a very pronounced bergamot. Then we started to feel a delicious Cognac that reminds me of a Dutch liquor called Advokaat. It has a certain Coca-Cola vibe, as many people have already mentioned. But after a few hours is when the perfume pleases me the most, with an addictive drydown and a perfect sillage to my nose. Longevity is quite good and the sillage is better than I expected.

What is the intention of this perfume? We have here the typical chord that pretends to be sexy mixing ingredients like vainilla, alcohol and tobacco. A completely night out kind of fragrance. Before testing I was expecting something sexy but in a luxury way, maybe the sexier perfume in this range of notes (Herod, Tobacco vanille, Back to black, chergui, etc..). But I found something different, we have those notes, but the intention of this perfume is not sexy. After a dared and shocking start, the perfume quickly turns into a totally different texture that what I´ve seen in another range of perfumes.. like.. Blue amber - Montale, Amber Oud - by kilian, Ambre precieux, etc. This has clearly another intention. Something like ambered vanille but not in a sexy way if not in a powdery, comfortable, friendly and warm adorned vanille. This is not what I was waiting for, but being what it is, we have a masterfully well blended powdery and relaxing perfume, that uses ingredients to grab attention but in a safe way, on a secondary level to complement the main idea. Personally, I'd rather have this two intentions (seduction/endearing) separately in different perfumes.

An intoxicating foray of black pepper and Lime collided intensely yet stunningly with freshly chopped ginger and cognac straight from its oak cask. Exquisitely underpinned by a bouquet of animalistic Jasmine massaged in benzoin and barrel aged tobacco. A Boozy, classy delicate dance on the promenade; cigar smoke fills the air while the spill of spirits become more distinguished with each temptress that passes by.

you know how we all wish we can go around and smell like our favorite bottle of soda? and you figure to yourself "hey let me just pour this old bottle of grape fanta over myself and see what kind of compliments I can pull"? and so you did? and you remember what happened right? you felt like shit cuz you were so sticky from the massive amount of sugar in the soda; insects would not leave you alone all day; and the dread you felt knowing you have to take those classes to get custody of your kids back? yeah you remember, because I remember that day: boy were you an embarrassment. well what if I told you there is finally a way for you to smell like carbonated, medicinal goodness, all without child services knocking on your door? and guess what; it's only 200 times the cost of that one bottle of soda! judging by that look on your face I'd say you're curious and I am here to tell you that God damn it where there is a will there is a way. Roja creation e pour homme parfum cologne (I think I got the name right, I really wish Roja would find a better way to name these fucking things) is a resinous, Ambery a slightly medicinal fragrance that has a very unique fizz like quality about it when sprayed on skin, that when combined with the fragrance itself gives off its trademark Coca-Cola vibe. I am one that enjoys wearing fragrances that I find to smell good, but I also enjoy fragrances as art especially when there's a theme and a vision behind it ( shout outs to T-Rex and Rhino ) even if I wouldn't necessarily wear it. fragrance like this normally wouldn't be up my alley, but there's just a slight nostalgic touch and a calm medicinal factor to it that isn't off putting to my nose, as I'm not the biggest fan of medicinal fragrances. performance on me is okay I get 6 hours usually; eight in a really controlled environment, fragrance isn't what I would call a projection beast but with this scent profile you don't necessarily want it to or else you would be kind of offensive. it's safe to say maybe elbows length projection? this is the scent that due to the Amber and the residence qualities would you know be better suited for the fall but it's not quite so heavy that it could withstand the punishment of the winter so it might be strictly fall/Cool spring nights. presentation as with all Roja is immaculate even though this is a flanker of the more expensive parfum version, and the price (390) reflects that. luckily our friends over at olfactory, venba fragrances, and some Sellers and Facebook groups have this for well on the market value, as I seen it as low as 179. I keep forgetting to give my fragrance review scores so I will leave you with this; it's a nice unique fragrance that you probably don't already have in your sent profile especially if you're a beginner but please sample this or walk into a local Neiman Marcus or saks and try before you buy because this certainly isn't for everyone.

I haven't tried that many of Roja Dove's creations, but Enigma Parfum Cologne smells spectacular. It opens up with a very fizzy, yet a bit boozy bergamot (an awesome opening, tbh). Then, the florals start to come in the mids. I can't quite describe what kind of florals, but it is there and I can feel it. Lastly, the drydown. Good lord, the drydown of Enigma Parfum Cologne is just beautiful. The cognac, tobacco, vanilla, and benzoin here are blended wonderfully. I do get the boozy-vanilla-coke with a touch of cherry in the drydown, which is great. It is one of those fragrances that really have noticeable differences between each layer of the pyramid (top, mid, and base notes). It lasts for a very long time, with a very good projection. The whiffs I get from the sillage when I'm wearing this one is just awesome, even when I only use two or three sprays. It is beautifully blended, performs greatly, and I'd even wear it on a summer night (or even a summer day, as long as I go easy on the sprays). I don't know if I'm pushing it too far, but it is that amazing to me. You'll definitely get those compliments that you want and deserve. Something I'd love to tell you though: - It does not smell like Herod, like what some people have said. - It is so underrated. - I think it is the best out of every Roja's Parfum Cologne collection, Elysium is my second place. My rating: - Scent: 10/10 (probably my first ever 10/10 fragrance in terms of scent) - Longevity: 9.6/10 - Projection and Sillage: 8.8/10 - Versatility: 8/10 - Value: 8.5/10 (well, even though it's quite expensive, it's worth the money for me). - Uniqueness and Complexity: 9.5/10 (it is more complex than it is unique) - Overall: 9.1/10
…but it is very good, indeed. I can understand the “Vanilla Coke” vibes, but it also smells very similar to a lot of the sweet scents that are out there already.

Nice scent but nothing special for me. Very genéric. Honestly i am dad and a bit dissapointed with this brand. This is the third roja perfume that i try and the third rhumbs down... Os It bad? Not at all...but It is not special o better than Manu other perfumes so i cant understand why the price tag. I think this is one of the most overrated brands un the market right now.
This was one of the fragrances that really piqued my interest when i was starting to discover niche perfumery.
I would like to start with the fact that this perfume did not had the "wow" factor for me, like years ago the "Guerlain Homme" did. I gave it a wear and said, meh .. not for me.

Be aware, this is not a linear cola scent from opening to drydown. I was really hyped for this release by Kilian. I wanted a cola scent anyways. The instant lime-cola opening blew me away. Unfortunatly yes, it do fades quickly but for me the cola note is still there but way-way in the back supporting the cedar, the nutmeg and the cinnamon making them sweeter. The drydown hours after fades into this sweet fresh vanilla coca cola with cinnamon and i love it.
