Not heavy on the nose, not overly sweet, and not generic or too linear but as i said, I wouldn't use it as a daily personally it could tho. Suited for both cold and warm weather. The performance is average tho, solid 6-7 ish hours. It's worth the money if you know what you're getting. Very unisex imo. Definitely test and/or sample before buying.

First wearing of By Kilian Bad Boys Are No Good But Good Boys Are No Fun (from the My Kind of Love collection), a travel size of which I bought due to its reported cola smell, and certainly there is somewhat of an attempt to recreate the sort of fresh caramel citrus fizz that usually amounts to a cola smell, but this mostly smells like mixed citrus/woody designer-ish mix with hints of sweetness, and not a lot there overall. I’ve not tried much of the My Kind of Love collection so I do not have a working sense of its quality or focus, but I’m a little disappointed in this specific offering, given that it doesn’t smell much like cola nor is that lovable of a generic, designer perfume, either. I’m not exactly sure what the perfumer was going for in this creation. It’s not bad, but it’s not especially good, either. Fortunately, it performs decently, though. It doesn’t appear to be for sale through normal retail means anymore (it was released in 2018) so I assume it’s been discontinued. 5 out of 10

I'm still on the hunt for the perfect cola scent, so I blind-purchased a 10ml travel spray of BTBU. Thank goodness I bought this travel spray, I couldn't be more disappointed. I already had Mancera Tonka Cola and Roja Enigma, the first one had a very realistic cola smell, but it was too sweet and cloying. The second one had a delicious cola opening, but the drydown is all vanilla and amber, which I don't like. So let's move on to BTBU: it smells like a cheap and fresh men's deodorant, like Axe/Lynx with a nice hint of cola. But it's just a hint that doesn't last long. About 30-45 minutes the cola disappears and the only thing you smell is the deodorant. (Un)fortunately this smell lasts much longer than the coke smell. It has good longevity, but who wants to smell like that?

Put it on and immediately scrubbed it off so really cant comment on longevity etc. This is another one that smells repulsive to my nose, I know its a me problem and I'm yet to find out the note that is the source of the upsetting smell lol but a few other perfumes do this to my nose and they all smell the same! (like a dirty dishwasher with rotting water and bad breath) but don't really share a similar profile or perfumer etc. No cola, no lime, nothing but rancid water. The other ones that I get this specific smell from is Commodity Wool and Magnolia, Ghost in the Shell and Shes an Anomaly by ELdO My skin chemistry is a pain in the ass

Kilian’s Born to be unforgettable. Somthing completely different than most fragrances out there. This is a very fresh take on some coca cola with lime, cinnamon, vanilla and it drys down to a nice cedar base. It’s not a gourmand by any means if anything it’s very fresh with some woody sweetness to it. It’s in the same realm as Tonka cola but not as strong and a lot fresher. Somthing different but I really enjoy it. And I think it’s versitile enough to worm year round with the freshness. Since it’s not too heavy on the sweetness but just enough. If you get a chance check it out

Really woody and spicy upfront, lots of cedar, nutmeg, and cinnamon. I’m getting black pepper also. It settles down into more of a lime-heavy cola scent after about 10 minutes. Got to say at this point it reminds me really strongly of a Yankee Candle I used to have; Vanilla Lime, not that I’m picking up on a lot of vanilla in the actual scent itself.

Bad Boys by Kilian... So far, it has been poorly received and rated quite badly like almost all from the "affordable" hypersexualized line. In my opinion, however, this is truly unjust. Most fragrances from this category are very youthful, which shouldn't necessarily be a bad thing. They are fruity, sweet, bold, and unique.

And that's why I want to maintain my consistently bad style! ;P No one: "This perfume clearly appeals to your low human needs and drives." Me: "Okay, I'll take 2 of those, please!" :D Seriously, I totally understand that the marketing and image choice of this fragrance line from "Kilian" offers a perfect springboard for cynical comments and viewpoints.

This purchase was a pure blind buy. Not so bad, I would say. It was on sale at the airport in Cologne for a mere 29,- bucks. Every perfume lover would jump at such a brand for this price. Once home, unpacked, admired the bottle, and immediately sprayed two spritzes on my hand. First thought: I know this cola?! I’m a "Hamburg boy" and for me, Fritz-Cola is the one true cola.

I received this fragrance as a gift and immediately thought: "Yes, Kilian!" After the first application, I was very fascinated by how a perfume can actually smell so strongly of cola... I don't even think cola smells more like cola than the opening of this perfume! My thought: "Is this my thing?" ...after wearing it longer, the answer was "Yes"!

Let's get it out of the way right off the bat: this is my favorite fragrance. Full stop. Out of the mountain of fragrances I've smelled or sampled at this point, Manhattan is the one that feels most like a perfumer rummaged around in my brain and came out with this scent. To my nose, it's a gorgeously blended tapestry of most of my favorite notes that creates a warm, intoxicating mélange. My brain won't let me have a single signature, but this one would certainly be on the cold-weather shortlist. Of course, in typical Roja fashion, this fragrance lists about fifty thousand notes, of which I can notably detect maybe five or six. But setting the notes aside, as an EXPERIENCE this sings. Another reviewer, Tiago, used the word "sparkly" to describe the fragrance, and that's what the opening is to me: a surprisingly light and sparkly pop of citrus and lavender, something just a bit boozy, and a warm, toasty...coconut?! What's that doing in here?? Not the note you'd expect, but wow it works: enveloping the effervescent opening minutes in a lightly sweet, warmly roasted base. As the opening fades, you sink into a world of warm baking spices, vanilla, sandalwood, and a quite lush tobacco. It's much more graceful than those notes might make you expect, though. I wouldn't call this fragrance LIGHT, but Manhattan has a much airier, loftier presence than something like Tobacco Vanille, which has similar notes but in my experience sits much darker, heavier, and closer to the skin than Manhattan does. I get excellent longevity and presence from this, but of course your mileage/bottle/batch may vary. I know the Roja bottles are love-em-or-hate-em, but they don't bother me. The only place I can knock real points off here is for price: the value proposition in any Roja is gonna be for you to decide for yourself, but even for the already-inflated world of fragrance costs in general, Roja's prices can make your eyes water.

“At night the buildings shimmer vertically, against the dark sky. In the morning the sun rises over Manhattan illuminating the city that never sleeps." This beautiful bottle really shimmers against the darkness. There is a lot of notes in this perfume and a lot of going on like in New Your city. Happily I still don’t get a hectic or chaotic vibe from this scent - it’s rather calming and relaxing by forgetting all that traffic and hurry and I’m thinking myself watching all that up in the sky in my own peace. That never sleeping Manhattan with a millions of people is under my eyes and I concentrate on my own business. Manhattan is captivating and uplifting scent with ingeniously blended juice and the main notes Heliotrope, Coconut, Patchouli, Tobacco, Cedarwood and Vanilla open up brightly together with aromatic Lavender and other floral notes. In my skin this doesn’t change so much during a couple of hours. You don’t have to be worried about overspraying this since after the opening it settles down to a beautiful skin scent, not too weak but just perfect for wearing at the office. I can get easily a little bit sweet Vanilla and Coconut while Patchouli is giving the fresh, earthy take on it, other spices are tuning the sweetness down with Oakmoss, and tobacco gives a unique polished touch to this juice. It’s really sophisticated so you shouldn’t be worried about that note if you are not into that note. It’s not dirty nor literally smoky. Coconut here is beautiful as well, not at all cloying or sun lotion type - what else you can get from Roja Dove than divine, luxurious vibe in notes. Overall this perfume is posh, modern masterpiece from Roja Dove! Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes

Upon first spraying Manhattan, I was immediately reminded of the spicy sweet tobacco of Tobacco Vanille Eau de Parfum but quickly other notes entered that set it apart: a subtle coconut note and some powdery florals (heliotrope?). Resinous-woody amber supports it in the base, with the smooth tobacco note lingering throughout. I mostly perceive the drydown as a benzoin-cedarwood combo along with a bit of powdery vanilla. I think I still prefer Enigma pour Homme Parfum as Roja's best tobacco fragrance, but Manhattan really is very good. Not as dense and sweet as some other tobacco perfumes in this genre, but still with woody depth in the base. I don't think it's going to make the cut for a full bottle for me, but it's knocking on the door.

Search for a good tobacco-centered perfume and you’ll eventually end up with Manhattan on your list. And with good reason; it’s got probably the finest, most realistic vanilla-tobacco out there. Tobacco is not the only star of the show though, and the blend makes it a tough one for me to judge. I respect the smell; sometimes, when I get a whiff of it, I’m like… “yeah this is good!” But there’s something in there which I perceive as a frivolous fruity note. That doesn’t feel right to me. At least… it distracts from the serious character that the beautiful tobacco-vanilla notes demand. You could wear a beautiful suit with a quirky handkerchief, but in my opinion the quirky got a bit zany in this case. Sillage I found hard to measure. I wore this a couple of times. From just a few sprays to a full 8 spray wear. I was able to really smell it myself in all cases but asking for feedback left me with no useful input. I’d say it’s okay, but can be easily be overthrown by others around you wearing perfume. I enjoyed it at least 8 hours on myself. The bottle I found strikingly beautiful, with its art deco gold plate, its shiny stone-layered cap. Is it worthy of the money? Let’s thrown in a truism: Only if you really, really love that smell and have money to spare. Which I don’t.

This fragrance is an masterpiece. I was browsing through notino and found that this was on sale and instantly bought it. First of all the packaging and bottle is top notch. You really get that luxurious feeling to it. The parfume itself is really well blended with the vanilla really seeping through the whole fragrance. At first you get that really fresh feeling to it with whiffs of vanilla and lavender. While letting it sit for an couple of minutes you go through an well crafted work of art. The smell seeps through the room and you get this cozy, pleasant feeling. Overall this is an really well crafted fragrance that you should atleast have smelled once in your lifetime.

Manhattan by ROJA Parfums What a stunner this is! And I’m not just talking about the presentation which is just beautiful. This seems to have been tailor made for me. In one word: Boujee And I mean it. It manages to be both warm, spicy, rich, enveloping, opulent… …AND bright, sparkly, aromatic, energetic, classy, elegant.

I just received the fragrance this morning and after giving it a full wearing I can confirm that this is going to be my go-to-scent for the upcoming winter months. The scent starts with a sparkling mix of citrus, aromatic notes and tobacco. Although not being redundant the opening gives me a similar feeling like wearing the Enigma (Creation E) Parfum Cologne.

Opening is very safe, like, something a designer would make? The way the vanilla and lavender is used here is very common with a tinge of basil and bergamot. But the SPICES quickly come in.. lots of cinnamon and cloves with a very wearable tobacco and the florals here a become a backbone for this fragrance balancing everything out.

I was really impressed: it opens with a very realistic hint of tobacco, cloves and cinnamon. Realistic and definite notes; then this luminous coconut declares itself with a creamy vanilla that is green at times and then settles on an almost poudre but not annoying sensation of lavender. It's all perfectly balanced, no blatantly synthetic hints ever emerge.

Reminds me of Xerjoff 's Naxos creamy notes. The initial spray is outstanding and with effervescent hints and the dry down is warm, creamy and inviting. This should be a great fall and winter perfume. I would say this leans more masculine. This is so nice. Overall, I'm very pleased with this blind buy Roja creation.

What hasn't been said about this wonderful Gormond perfume? It's either you like it or you don't and I hope you're on the side that likes! Perfect gourmand and oud perfume. Anyone who wears it imagines that they are in a pastry shop in Paris. Sweet notes of Patisserie, Oud, Artemisia, Cistus and more... Average performance. A little bit reminds me of "Parfum de la Nuit 3 | Roja Parfums" plus the sweet and oud notes. 8.5/10.

For those of you who aren't aware, Sweetie Aoud has been repackaged and revised along with many other Roja fragrances. Sweetie Aoud previously had a cursive font on its gold plating and came in a white box with the traditional satin padding inside. Now the bottle has standard font (CAPS) and comes in a black box that I will just say does not travel well when shipped. I almost never enjoy reformulations, but this most recent era of Sweetie Aoud is actually an improvement. I liked the original formula and it was a strong like, but it just lacked performance and did not wear like a Parfum should. Otherwise it was a great fragrance. It is now fuller and dances on the skin beautifully, with added projection. How is it different? Sweetie Aoud (cursive font) contained oud, but was really more about olibanum (frankincense) and didn't allow the oud to really shine. I also found that I needed to wait before I could really enjoy the fragrance. Sweetie Aoud (standard font) is more true to its title, while still conserving that patisserie shop vibe. The updated fragrance speaks to oud more than it did prior. It seems to outlast the rewritten formula and much more enjoyable in my opinion. Stunning, addictive and luxurious.

OMG!!! The most unique gourmand fragrance I ever smelled. I just finished the whole 2ml sample within few days and I just miss it so much that I have to get a full bottle immediately, which I already did and it should be on its way. I’ve heard many good things about it for a long time and I was willing to blind buy it if I can find a discounted one from reputable sellers because I just love gourmand so much but I just never could find one. I finally got a sample to find out if I really love it and if it worth the high price tag. I ended up gave up on waiting for a discount bottle and just went to get one from their official website because I just love it this much. At the first spray, the strong buttery opening was a little overwhelming but after couple minutes the buttery note would tone down a lot and then it starts to smell very much like French patisserie. Particularly a croissant. It’s not the cloying sugary sweet though, which I appreciate. I love gourmand sweet but I don’t like sugary cloying sweet. The sweetness is just right. Also once the buttery accord tones down, I actually love its perfect amount of the buttery and that compliment the whole vibe of it. Interestingly, I can smells the Oud in the dry down but still maintain the gourmand pastry vibe. Not animalic or barnyard at all. This is surely a masterpiece. Performance wise, it stays closer to my skin but not an intimate skin scent at the same time. I would say it projects about 2 feet from skin until 6-7 hours mark then start fading to a skin scent. It has amazing longevity though. It lasts 12+ on my perfume eating skin. My skin tends not to grip perfumes very well (at least 2 hours less than other people). I know it’s very expensive but I do think it worth the price; the uniqueness of the fragrance, the quality ingredients you can smell from it, the performance and the bottle are all at the top notch. Especially I personally just love this scent.

Unisex I had a difficult relationship with this special unique so called “gourmand” for long time. I loved it from the beginning, that was sure but I needed to get to know her better. I’m just not so big fan of gourmands - I like many and love some a lot but I don’t want to smell myself like many of those. There is just few gourmands which deserves the place in my collection and Sweetie Aoud is one of those. Sweetie Aoud is not so obvious gourmand since the gourmand note is “patisserie accord” which is not any concrete food. That’s why I love it a lot. It’s rather a feeling and a smell which is a whiff of a French or Italian cafe full of delicious pastries made mainly from butter dough. The smell is a littlle bit sweet and soft buttery but the genious blend gives in the same time such a fresh vibes which I find extremely interesting. There is a really herbal fresh opening with Bergamot and Artemisia and quickly after that follows Patisserie Accord which is the strongest during the first 30 minutes. It’s so realistic that you can just close your eyes and you can imagine yourself in front of that glass in patisserie choosing something delicious to eat with your Latte. Rose is only supportive note here and Cistus is barely detectable but those tunes down the sweetness. After this starts the main show! Next the basenotes take over your senses and the buttery note melts beautifully together with spicy, aromatic and earthy notes, Frankincense and Aoud being the prominent ones. Like all Rojas this juice is so well blended that it’s very difficult to separate notes but that makes even the gourmand perfume luxurious, polished and charming. This is simply a stunning perfume for wintertime! Edit: actually love it a bit more in warm weather. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes

Sweetie Aoud from the British House of Niche Perfumery Haute Luxury Roja London is an oriental gourmand woody floral aromatic spicy balsamic perfume. It was launched in 2015; the perfumer who signs this fragrance is Roja Dove. At the top, Bergamot mixes with Davana to create a fresh leaf with a note of Rose, adding more freshness to the heart of this fragrance, slightly sweetened by a DELICIOUS 'Patisserie Accord'. Which is soon warmed by an incredible accord of Noble Woods intertwined with the very present in this composition, the 'Oud safe and clean, characteristic of Roja Dove, and Incense, which bring a slightly smoky facet. And where an exotic balsamic spicy accord of Gurjan Balsam, Cipriol and Patchouli are further tempered by Cumin and Cardamom, set on a base of Incensed Leather and Resins. One of the best gourmand perfumes in history! Sweetie Aoud is a beautiful and TASTY gourmand centered on 'Oud, Precious Woods, Incense and a Sweetness just right, it gives me the feeling of sweet bread or shortbread freshly taken out of the oven, a masterpiece of the master Roja Dove; and with Great Performance!

Sweetie Aoud is a gourmand Aoud fragrance that reminds me, as a child of the Bodensee region, of the city of Zurich. But how can a May rose-incense-Aoud fragrance with a deliciously warm gourmand note remind one of Zurich? Well, it is the elegant, warm, and relaxed restraint that Sweetie Aoud displays, combined with a wonderful Luxemburgerli note.

There are fragrance notes that you love, there are fragrance notes that you hate, and then there are those in between that you can tolerate in some combinations but find abhorrent in others. And exactly in this last category falls Oud for me.

My predecessors have already said everything about this wonderful scent and described it so well that I initially didn't want to write a comment on it, but I have now decided to share how the fragrance affects me, what it evokes in me, and why you should definitely try it :) I tested it quite a while ago and was already very taken with it.

It was one of those evenings when I had no plan about where to go, but the restless feeling inside me urged me outside. The rain had washed the streets to a shine, the air was cool, filled with smoke from the kiosks, and somewhere there was the smell of freshly baked bread. I stood in front of the shelf, looked at my bottles, and knew: today I needed something different.

There is probably no fragrance that I consider buying as often as this one. The patisserie accord truly delivers on its promise! A heavenly scent that inevitably makes your mouth water. And this is combined with noble other components that together create a high-quality and unique perfume.

It certainly has a very interesting twist/evolution. In the first few minutes, I thought: definitely a purely masculine scent, although I find this categorization ridiculous. For me, it has a slightly synthetic soapy opening, almost ethereal, grapefruit/vetiver etc., and the cardamom is really strong here; some perceive this as (sweat note) which I don’t understand.. I actually find it very successful in the Chypre shot. OK, but let’s move on to this uh, hybrid creature from Tiziana Terenzi. Now it gets really spicy; somehow the sample completely slipped through my fingers...too much testing...haha, and you really get the feeling here as if you’ve rubbed leaves that release certain essential oils between your fingers. Or cut open a grapefruit and didn’t dry your hands. This might be a bit "tear-inducing" for gourmands. In the sense of being too bitter, spicy. Ylang ylang is completely drowned out, which is better for me...In the dry down, a hint of rose can be detected. CONCLUSION! Interesting for fans of green, spicy scents, slightly smoky. The stars here are vetiver, citrus, and cardamom. I see it more as a perfume for sultry hot weather. Cooling effect. A fragrance that I personally don’t like on myself, but find quite interesting on others.

Although the notes announced are very different from those of Creed Aventus or Mancera Cédrat Boisé, there is a great similarity between Loewe Esencia and these two fragrances. Opens with citrus, which lasts the entire life of the scent and joins the sandalwood. This perfume does not have the smoke of certain batches of Aventus. The nuance here is the slight green note that appears and makes the perfume very pleasant. It is a very good perfume, which I prefer to the last batches of Aventus and which has a similar performance. For the price, I definitely choose Loewe Esencia.

From what appears on the fragrance sheet or the Loewe website, to what it smells like in reality, there is an abyss. No lavender, no moss, no sandalwood, or vetiver. Perhaps there is something of the latter two over there at the bottom, putting a dash of ingenuity .. Yes, it may have a dash of incense, also on this base, but very diluted and insignificant. We are facing another "gross" clone of "Aventus", of which both proliferate today. It opens with the typical explosion of synthetic Bergamot, nuanced to subtract some acidity with some strange ambroxan-like molecule and some wood / vetiver in the background, as a base. Compared to the "current Aventus", well, but it totally lacks the nuances of rose, green apple or vanilla that could be found in jars of years ago. I see it far below, both in quality and in distinction, or creativity, of releases such as "Loewe 7" or its "Anonymous" flanker. With much less elaboration and nuances than these, apart from that we are talking about a copy of other perfumes that have been in the market for some time. As for the performance, here I think it is going well. It is powerful, especially at the start. Gaudy. I think that much more than the "Aventus" itself and even the unbearable (for my taste) "Club de Nuit Intense", which is the one that has reminded me the most, for that squeaky look. In the cardboard, although it has lost strength, I still smell it 24 hours later. With no intention of offending, this type of perfume reminds me a little of the typical "redneck" with money (or that it pretends to appear), which seeks to attract attention and be recognized by everyone and arrives with its car full of spoilers tacky, making a ridiculous noise with the engine, while destroying the gearshift absurdly, with the purpose of attracting more attention. Obviously, I do not say that everyone who dazzles this perfume has to be like that, much less. It is a mere personal association.

As is repeated ad nauseam and everyone knows, Loewe Esencia is an Aventus Inspiration, and that is why we came to have it. Personally, I am interested in having a quality perfume with the Aventus gene without having to spend 400 dollars. It's just what Esencia offers, with its nuances, but come on, who in the world is going to think "it doesn't have as much pineapple or smokiness as Creeds." They are broadly similar and thats it. It has no declared citrus fruits, curious that I feel it quite citrusy at the beginning of its evolution, leaving after the prominence to lavender and vetiver. It always seemed to me that there is a point of contact between Aventus and Terre d Hermes and I think that in Esencia that contact is greater, due to a vetiver that is the protagonist. It is a fresh, versatile composition, for daily use and on all occasions. The bottle I have has a discreet performance, but superior to Creed's current batches. It is a classic profile that every perfumery lover falls into, and falling into Esencia seems to me to be an excellent option.

Loewe has done a great job here. Available in 150ml! I use this in summertime and like to overspray myself. Funny how friends always say that i’m on Creed Aventus lol. Where Creed had his period now its time to move on. If you ever visit Tenerife…buy it there at a cheap price, you wont regret it and you will be noticed!!

Another Aventus clone, and a cheap one at that. The lavender and basil are nice, but there`s a synthetic sweetness that you could read as pineapple, if you`re willing to keep an open-mind or practice suspension of disbelief. Unfortunately, I couldn`t do either. There`s lots of good stuff in there, notes I generally love, but that chemical screech is heard and felt in unison with all that fragrant goodness, ruining it completely for me. If you love this thing, good news is that it lasts and projects like crazy. Uber macho and annoying, like a cocky jock flexing his muscles in your face while that Right Said Fred "I`m too sexy" track is blaring at max volume without a trace of self-irony.

I received a miniature sample of this perfume, and as a long-time fan of fragrances similar to Aventus from 2016 or earlier, I was excited to try it. This perfume definitely scratches that itch, as it smells very similar to the opening of the original Aventus.

I like this one way more than the Elixir. While Elixir's main accord is vague woody masculinity, this one is mossy and earthy, almost excessively so. Unfortunately, it doesn't strike me as a wild kind of earthiness. It smells so... docile? Domesticated even.

Yes, it was the bottle that somehow caught my attention. The new Esencia from Selfridges. Black bottle. Hand-painted ash wood cap. I wore the "old" Esencia EdT quite often during my first summer at Parfumo. Then somehow too rarely. This caused the scent to fade into the past and then out of my collection. It was green. A bit edgy.

Legendary DNA, I have found my version. If I had smelled this fragrance 10-15 years ago without any idea, I am sure it would have come close to being my signature scent. It doesn't reach those heights today, but I am glad to have it. First of all, my view on the DNA and the forms I know. Afterwards, I will go into more detail about Esencia Eau de Parfum .

Hello everyone. I am Tamas and not German. I hope you understand everything. This perfume drives me crazy. Simply a miracle. I have tried it several times and even bathed afterwards… the scent just won't go away… unbelievable. I have about 100 different perfumes. But this one, like this… simply leaves me speechless. First very citrusy. Then very-very masculine.

I had the chance to test Apex on skin at the Burlington Arcade shop in London, and let me tell you - I totally see the comparison to Sauvage Elixir, especially during the dry down. Apex is like the refined, sophisticated older brother in this scenario. While Sauvage has its charm, Apex feels even more polished and expertly blended. Apex was created by master perfumer Roja Dove and launched in 2022 as part of his luxury fragrance line. With its animalic, woody, and spicy notes, it’s designed to channel confidence and power, hence the name "Apex." And yes, it delivers on that premise. For the first two hours, the projection is what I’d call beast mode and I don’t throw that term around lightly. If you want to turn heads, this is a good option. This also means that if the weather is hot, anything beyond 1-2 sprays, will probably cause an extinction event. Now, here’s my dilemma. I’m almost finished with my Sauvage Elixir bottle, and while I’m likely to purchase Apex next, the similarity between the two makes it feel a bit redundant. But if you don’t already own Sauvage Elixir and you’re willing to pay a (significant) premium, Apex is hands down the winner. It’s like Sauvage, but after a fancy upgrade.

When I was 10 or 11 my mother took me and my brothers to Dawlish to a caravan park. We went to a entertainment night, where the headline act was Cannon & Ball (sorry non-UK-Gen X and younger UK readers…go on YouTube they were huge in the UK in the 80’s) any way they were very well known acts on that show and the Headliners came on and it was comedy and etc and then it closed out with a song. Bobby Balll came back on stage and started to 'rap' (it was the late 80s) and Tommy Cannon came out and said " Woah woah woha what yer doin? Kids nowadays don't want the rapping, they want the Durty Dancin" (again it was the late 80s and the film had just come out) and they proceeded to sing ' 'I've had the time of my life'. Now you might not know what this has got to do with this fragrance, but if as I suspected this is an attempt to appeal to a younger demographic by Roja Dove and not the dowagers, aged moneyed spinsters and tacky nouveau riche; then sheesh! In this there is a very similar signature of early to mid 80s powerhouse fragrances , in the opening I could not stand a very prominent citrus, I don't know if it was the pineapple or the lemon, but it did not sit well with me; and this being a Roja it could've been both and other citrus notes as well. I really could not wait for that to disappear. If that had stuck around I would be writing something completely different. I am surprised how much I like this, its much better than the criticism suggests, and I'm not really a Roja Dove fan (although I do like and respect what he's doing insomuch of recreating a classic style of fragrance) I can see he was trying for a 'younger' demographic but like Cannon & Ball missed the target. Not a bad shot though.

This is a truly extraordinary scent. At the beginning for a few moments, it is fresh, and flawless. And then comes the heart of...lightness. It is like wandering through spring forest or herb garden places next to the woods. The opening crisp is due to citrus and pineapple. The real story told by the bottle bases on the outstanding mix of labdanum, juniper berries, incense, tobacco, woods, lether. And yes, patchouli - so gentle, yet significant, in the set. I love Apex Eau de Parfum from the first sniff.

I was able to test Apex in peace today. To be honest, I was somewhat torn; the various statements left a rather negative impression of Apex. A Roja with a bad rating is indeed something rare and unusual. Before this review, I thought about what might be the reasons for the somewhat poor ratings and whether I might be too optimistic in my review. After much consideration, I am confident that my assessment is not overly optimistic. In my opinion, there are several aspects that may have contributed to the rather low average rating. 1. Some users probably only know Roja's Colognes and may not be able to appreciate those from Roja that are different. 2. Most associate Roja with Elysium Cologne and Enigma Cologne, which clearly have a more modern DNA; anyone hoping for something comparable with Apex has, of course, been completely disappointed. 3. Apex is more comparable to lesser-known Rojas like "Danger pour Homme (Parfum) | Roja Parfums," "Scandal pour Homme (Parfum) | Roja Parfums," and "Goodman's | Roja Parfums." The result here is that the buyer or tester receives a very classic DNA in the Fougère style with slight Chypre undertones. Some may have created a different expectation in their minds due to the advertising. 4. The DNA is clearly classic and not modern. Now to Apex itself. Apex is a very beautiful and modern Fougère with a few modern additives or enhancements. I see in Apex a familiar DNA that has been adjusted and altered. The DNA consists of the Rojas mentioned in point 3. Particularly in the later stages, Apex has some interesting components. There is a slight Enigma DNA through the rum and tobacco. Another interesting novelty is the pineapple note. For me, Apex is a very good extension of the Cologne portfolio. I do not see any resemblance to "Aventus (Eau de Parfum) | Creed," "Bleu de Chanel (Eau de Parfum) | Chanel," "Percival | Parfums de Marly," or even Aqva Amara Eau de Toilette in the slightest. Please test again, because this association is simply not correct. I had 4 people test and compare Apex, and no one had these associations. I do agree more with the comparison to "Eau Sauvage (Eau de Toilette) | Dior," as this fragrance is a classic Fougère scent. However, Apex is more modern and creative, especially due to the pineapple and the rum and tobacco twist. I also cannot understand why some always see this scent as only for old men. I am also significantly under 30 and see Apex as a modern fragrance for today's gentleman. No, Apex is not a pantydropper; anyone hoping for such a thing from Roja unfortunately does not understand the Roja brand and its typical clientele. Unfortunately, some also seem to make no effort to explore the fragrance, because Apex is complex and profound; in my opinion, Apex is even the most profound of the Cologne series. The longevity for me is very good. I was able to perceive Apex for 9 hours. The sillage is relatively strong for 3 hours and is even minimally detectable beyond an arm's length. After that, Apex becomes quieter and is close to the skin after about 7-8 hours. I just looked at the list of similar fragrances, and I do not see Sauvage Elixir even remotely similar, because Sauvage is much sweeter and contains more lavender as well as some Ambroxan.

So here it is, the new fragrance from Roja Parfums. As is customary with this house, the expectations for the scent, its longevity and quality, as well as the design of the bottle, seem almost immeasurably high. Such expectations can only lead to disappointment, especially since the bar has been set very high by the manufacturer itself due to its boastful marketing and ultimately the price tag. I must admit that I am a fan of Roja fragrances. Not because of the bottle design (too much bling bling), not because of the marketing (“the FINEST fragrances of the world”) or the innovative power of the scents. No, it is actually the ingredients that radiate a truly high level of naturalness that convince me here. Nothing scratches, nothing clashes, and there is no gym-filling sledgehammer synthetic (a shout-out to Mancera and Montale) with longevity beyond the 24-hour mark. These are simply fragrances that come with a high feel-good factor for me, which I enjoy wearing without having to envelop those around me. Many comparisons have been drawn here, with Chanel Antaeus, Roja Scandal and Danger, Nishane Hacivat, and even Dior Sauvage Elixir. Except for perhaps a tiny bit of the latter, I really cannot relate to any of these comparisons. However, I have only smelled Sauvage Elixir once, so I could be wrong here, as I do not have a good scent memory. It is also rumored that Apex smells like a mix of “x and y.” Well, I have never mixed two of my perfumes together, but I claim that the mixture will yield something different than the sum of its individual parts. As usual, Roja provides us with a whole list of notes. (Marketing) notes or accords are not the same as ingredients, but rather consist of multiple components. Therefore, I do not know how a person should perceive all these individual notes side by side. Nevertheless, for me, two of the notes are quite present throughout the entire scent journey, namely cypress and oakmoss. I guess that is why many testers immediately trigger the red “grandpa alert” lamp. Oops, a fragrance not exclusively for teens and twenty-somethings, but for OLDER people, how dare Roja?? However, I would disagree here as well. Yes, the fragrance is not for teenagers and students. They should not really be buying a perfume for 300+€, right? I would say the fragrance is excellent for people from the “young professional” age, all the way up to retirement. It is indeed an ideal office scent. Yes, many fragrances with a chypre structure and oakmoss in the base can sometimes come across as a bit old-fashioned. A rather dominant cypress can also make a fragrance seem a bit dull and musty. However, this is not the case with Roja Apex. Rather, this fragrance manages to complement the more classically green components with an incredibly sparkling, almost soda-like freshness. And the result is pleasing! It’s a kind of Tom Ford Italian Cypress with an added freshness kick. By “soda,” I do not mean Ahoi-Brause. More like the feeling when you hold your nose over the surface of a freshly prepared lemon-grapefruit lemonade, with the volatile citrus components rising into your nose along with the fizz of the carbonation. This freshness in Apex, however, does not feel forced but is excellently woven into the green base. Furthermore, this fresh component surprisingly lasts almost as long as the base. It only recedes towards the end of the scent journey, after about 8 hours. My conclusion for this fragrance is therefore positive. Has Roja reinvented the wheel? No. Has he ever done that? No. Has Roja managed again to create an improved version of a fragrance that I already like very much (Tom Ford Italian Cypress)? Absolutely, yes! Longevity: 10h+ Significant projection: 4h+

New Roja, impressive presence, stylish bottle, appealing pyramid. null of this directly speaks against the fragrance, but it can certainly lead it to face a few walls of expectation and doors of prejudice. 2022 - It's almost time to look back on this year. Do I want to? When it comes to Apex Eau de Parfum - yes! What actually gives us the strength to face challenges? My second fougere from the house of Roja was quickly found during the discovery of the genre. After "Reckless pour Homme (Parfum) | Roja Parfums," it could only be "Apex | Roja Parfums," which, with its strikingly sporty appearance, is vying for the favor of the younger generation.

La Nuit de l'Homme is very woodsy. You have been warned. Woodsy yet clean, this fragrance does have that undeniable classic charm to woo the ladies. I preferred this particular release over the original L'Homme, due to its darker nature. I like my men to smell mysterious, and this fragrance captures that essence well. La Nuit de l'Homme may be simplistic, but its basic composition works well. Opening with peppery woods and a boozy rum-like note, this fragrance screams masculinity. A touch of soapiness appears a few seconds into the heart which hints that its wearer, although dangerous, is classy and cool. Does this fragrance evoke a feeling of a night out on the town? I would say yes, however I'd also encourage those to wear it casually during Winter as well.

La nuit de who? This is la nuit de le 12 years old sipping a Diet Coke and smoking puff cigarettes. A disappointing, juvenile and cheap lavender-cardamom-woody-tobacco “club scent” smelling like YSL L’Homme layered with Declaration, Lanvin Avantgarde and/or Armani Code, inexplicably relating “night” with a bright, sweetish, teenish vibe. Lasting like a fart - which is good, though: the barely-perceivable drydown is almost enjoyable. If “ladies love this” then either I don’t understand a thing about women or we agree to disagree on the concept of “ladies”. Meh! 5/10

La nuit de l'Homme is a scent that is frequently evoked when guys search for a womanizer / pantydropper / clubbing scent. On youtube you see lots of positive reviews, women are said to go crazy when smelling this stuff. After I got a sample vial of this scent today I sprayed it on my arm about an hour ago (edit: this was in september 2011). So, I'd like to tell you what I think of it. Maybe you guys are interested in a lady's opinion - though I have to admit that my taste is sure not representative. The first thing that came to my mind after spraying was that it was very sweet and quite ordinary. Not bad, but not special at all. Though I really like wearing guys' scents I would never wear this one. Despite of its sweetness it screams masculinity. Well, from a neutral point of view it probably doesn't but it has some notes and accords that everyone knows from men's deodorants and cheap after-shafe. Maybe the minty note (not in the pyramid) and some sort of synthetic lavender are responsible for this. Unfortunately I don't get the cardamom. This description may sound very bad - but actually it is not. Following this poor start the scent develops and gets slightly sweeter. It starts smelling really nice and attractive. Not so special, but very pleasant. It probably works fine for clubbing when the target group consists of younger girls who are probably not experienced perfumistas. A very complex scent would probably tend to overcharge. This is a pleasant one, you just can't go wrong with ist. It is definitely better than no scent at all (that's not always the case in my opinion). It does have presence, but it is not intrusive. Could become a best-seller like Boss Bottled. I would like to smell it on a man although talking about sweet frags I would personally prefer something more classy like a Guerlain (l'instant extrême for example).

What can you possibly say about a fragrance that has been "Over Hyped" from every angle? The one testimony to it's greatness is despite the myriads of reviews and recommendations it hasn't become a victim of it's own success.

An interesting thing you should know is that the name 7 comes from the seven ingredients of which it is exclusively composed. This fashionable fragrance is marked by higher pepper, incense, flowery notes, and vetiver, forming a modern, sophisticated, and divine scent. It is a truly masculine scent, and 7 Men is as complex as his scent, traditional yet rebellious and brave. Each specially selected ingredient represents the seven values that the 7 men should have: passion, pride, bravery and force, solitude and spirituality, art and tradition, life and death, human and divine. I would dare to say L7 does not conform to the other design fragrances' ways. I came across it by chance since I was looking for a bottle of SOLO and the clerk kindly asked about trying this instead... I imagine I got blessed that day, and here you are, what I got. L7 is supposed to be aromatic, woody, and floral, and it opens the same as a clove and pepper bomb, but nothing to do with Marc Jacobs Bang or Viktor & Rolf Spicebomb... The mouillette (paper strips) smells like an ever-new packet of cigars, with that distinctive smell of raisin. Don't get me wrong. I am referring to the fresh tobacco aroma and not the irritating hash. Yeah, I am a non-smoker, man, but I smell raisins when I sniff a packet of cigarettes, and I like how fresh cigs smell. To me, it's quite a beautiful smell. I didn't get too many apple notes; perhaps the spicy notes are too strong for my nostril and cover it. Even though there is no mention of the clove buds, I surmise that aroma comes from the pepper leaves. Pay attention that the excessive clove note you get is intense in the first couple of hours. Then, I got a bit of graceful rose and beautiful fresh incense and vetiver that started playing the game, together with the cedarwood and a sort of mild musk (not wild, forget about YSL Kouros or Narciso Rodriguez for Him, this is a gentle musk!). That blend makes L7 so damn masculine and modern. In my opinion, the dry down reminds me of something about Cacharel pour L'Homme Eau de Toilette , maybe the use of the very same vetiver and musk ingredients. But I don't mind; CpH used to be my signature fragrance when I was 20! Oh man, it is so powerfully spicy, though not too harsh, far away from the oriental and bittersweet fragrances I am used to, yet so damn gorgeous. L7 is lovely to wear, just suitable for cooler and colder seasons. Since I bought it last fall, I have no clue how it might work during warmer seasons. Well, I would recommend it for spring, fall, and wintertime. Still, I would refrain from wearing it during summer due to the excessive clove note. It's suitable for leisure time, maybe day and evening are the correct times to wear it. It's a modern and stylish scent, not overpowering so that you can go safe with it. What I like most is its unpopularity in Italy, meaning that when I wear it, I smell good, distinctive, and not similar to anyone else around me. I hate feeling like 'most men' when I wear one scent. Of course, there's no reason why you can't wear this fragrance for work since it smells clean, crisp, and fresh and stay close to you. My two cents: L7 is an extraordinary fragrance. Initially, you will detect an overdose of cloves. But after a while, it reveals a lovely and robust incense, which combines perfectly with the cedarwood and vetiver to create a beautiful, exquisite, and very masculine cologne. Although you will get the fresh feel throughout the fragrance's life from intense to moderate, L7 is an energetic melange and very rich in flavors, perhaps almost too influential for the typical nose to appreciate. But if you want aromatic herbs and spices, look no further since no one is better than this jewel. I am writing this review right after dinner, and I can still smell it out of my chest. That means it is a long-lasting fragrance with a moderate sillage. For all the above reasons, I would rate it 8/10. -Elysium

Many a reviews (video and written) rave about the depth and scent character of Oligarch. Rich, opulent, luxurious, multi-faceted, alpha. I would agree with all these adjectives except for perhaps the alpha one. Here is my rather simple take on Oligarch. Top: Our billionaire wakes, as they do, in the early afternoon on vacation on a tropical island surrounded by fruits a plenty. Lounging in a private villa, he indulges in an invigorating citrusy drink enriched with the lingering smell of tropical fruits and flowers that is carried by the non-salty breeze. He observes his surroundings and thanks his good fortunes. What a great way to start the day. Mid: Mid-afternoon, his palate tingling with citruses, our protagonist leaves the villa to wander along the boundaries of this island. Venturing away with his significant other towards the beach surrounded by broad leaf trees. An air of sweet coconut mixed with champaca greet his nostril and as he turns to his significant other, he is greeted further more by the delicate scent of the white florals she has tucked around her ear. Ahh this is bliss. It wouldn't smell this good if it was any other time but summer, thats for sure. Base: Early evening, the sun is due to set soon. Perhaps tired of terra firma and in need of a little relief from the sun, our Oligarch and the significant other plunge into the water for a short swim towards their exuberant yacht, decked out with the finest of cedar and juniper floors. Once there, the lingering heat gently evaporates their watery footsteps and along with it, the soft woody aroma of the mixed woods pervades the air. Gone is the citrus cocktail of the morning, the breeze still carries the tropical air from the afternoon but with a faint coolness to it. Day will be ending soon. A cool matè drink awaits on the top floor. The sun is setting, the silent waves ripple against the hull. Cedar, juniper and matè mingle in the cooling air. If only these moments lasted longer. Who needs a fragrance when life smells this good? To be an Oligarch...EDP.

For me this is easily a signature scent that can be worn anywhere. The mixture between the citruses and smokiness reminds of the same feel I had when I smelled the "real" Aventus back in the day - which was that this is how a man should smell. Do not buy Parfum version. If you can get it, EdP is the king.

Oligarch reminds me Terre Hermès, but much more better, richer, deeper, more projection and longevity. If you chose between Terre Hermès and Oligarch, then only Oligarch. Really, this is best version of Terre. This parfum created for successful Russian billionaires, kinda Abramovich

One things we gotta give Mr. Roja credit for is his masterful blending and re-interpretations of mainstream classics. This is supposed to be a sublimation of TDH, and I'd say "I see what you mean, but nope". Don't get me wrong, TDH is a fantastic perfume, but this one is a whole new level: layer after layer of polished complexity. Another thing Roja does, and does very well, is to "hide" notes. His blending of too many notes prevent you from isolating them, and evokes sensations. The more easily detectable are the citruses, a very high quality trio of lemon, bergamot and lime. The drydown is a soft amalgamation, sweetness from anise and apple, creaminess from coconut, and then all the rest of diverse notes that, on paper, wouldn't work, but here they do, creating a masterful and inspiring result. No one's gonna be blown away by how different or unique this scent is, but it's an absolute delight. What a Russian oligarch would wear during his Summer in Nice, linen beige suit and all.

If you've never smelled Y EDP and are wondering what it smells like, know that Y is nothing more than another warrior in the battle of the blues, featuring Versace pour Homme Dylan Blue Eau de Toilette , Bleu de Chanel Eau de Toilette and Sauvage Eau de Toilette . Luckily, it does not smell like many other recent blue fragrances, which is a good thing, thanks to its fruity and greenish, slightly creamy and fresh, spicy trait. Y EDP is a sweet fragrance with the apple up top and the tonka, but there's a lot more going on. With light and dark fougère facets, Y EDP blends woody and aromatic accords and reveals itself with a crunchy green apple and ginger with subtle citrus hints. An opening that immediately catches my attention with its creaminess. The apple note, in particular, stands out and gives it a juicy and slightly sweet bite. The head phase is perhaps all too sweet, creepy and loud for me, even though I say it as someone who likes nothing too sweet. I think the sage distorts the apple note a bit. The spicy ginger is also noticeable, and I feel it invigorates the opening so well with the soft creamy bergamot. The citrus peel essence vanishes in a short time, leaving more room for spicy ginger and slightly synthetic apple. Compared to Y EDT, EDP appears less incisive on bergamot and more decisive on apple. When Y approaches the centre, I get a kind of aromatic fresh sage, now amplified. At first, it works in tandem with the ginger top note before overcoming it. Delicious resinous juniper berries and a hint of geranium pop in. The heady punch from velvety sage isn't too herbal here. A certain dustiness emerges, which slightly reduces the synthetic leading edge. I don't know if it's my skin, but I feel hints of something metallic, perhaps because of the amber and sage molecule. Sage and juniper bring virility in contrast with the elegance of geranium and lavender, two floral notes in the heart with herbaceous facets. Although it is not mentioned, the violet leaf is apparent. Dry down sets it apart from EDT because it has more heart and soul overall, is more refined, and is a little more grown-up. It exudes sweet, warm and resinous woody accords. Cedar and vetiver sitting on the bottom look more exciting and dynamic to my nose. I get a nice amber wood, a large dose, mixed with a bit of tonka, which gives it warmth and a semisweet. There is just a hint of tonka that releases vanilla undertones and softens its edges without overpowering the other notes. I am happy to catch the light traces of a delicious incense, strengthened by the audacity of smoked vetiver for intensity. Amber and tonka bean give Y EDP a soft warmth, which adds depth and durability to the composition but does not kill its touch of freshness. As I'm testing it in the middle of January, the freezing winter weather emphasizes resinous, contemplative olibanum and amber wood. I love amber wood, which is less salty and mushy than ambroxan, and it embodies the feeling of walking in a forest with a natural, musky, and woody smell. Y has that out-of-shower vibe, and it's pretty sweet, and I wouldn't wear it for tropical climates as it could be rather sentimental. Discreet for the rest of the year, it fully satisfies the intermediate seasons of autumn and spring and may surprise you on a cool evening during the summer. Besides, many people say it pierces through the cold weather of the winter months. The sillage is acceptable, the longevity is good enough for what it's worth. It sticks well to clothes, so beware of over application. However, it is not faint, and people will surely notice it. Overall, do I like Y EDP? Yup! Will I buy it? Maybe not. I think I have a lot of colonies with that vibe, and I don't need another brick in the wall. However I would appreciate it if I had to receive it as a gift, it is a great perfume. I base the review on a decant I have owned since March 2021. -Elysium

Y EdP remains the most popular and highest rated among the five releases in the Y series. While Y EdT has been harshly criticised for being too mainstream and unoriginal (especially when compared to its two illustrious older siblings, L'Homme and La Nuit De L'Homme), I think the praise and hype heaped upon Y EdP are equally undeserved. I received a sample with my order of Bleu Electrique and was I underwhelmed. I purchased Y EdT when it was released in 2017 because I enjoyed its fruity and airy nature. With the EdP, the lightness of the EdT is gone with the removal of aldehydes, and the sweetness is amplified with the addition of juniper berries, tonka bean and amber wood. The result is fresh sweetness combined with warm sweetness to produce an overall dense sweetness, which I find rather unpleasant. They succeeded in making a more intense and sweeter version of the EdT but it is still to me very one-dimensional. Y EdP could have been better if it was more oriental or woody or aromatic or citrusy or even floral, rather than simply relying on an overabundance of sweet notes. For the warmer weather or daytime or to wear to work or the gym, I think Y EdT is the more versatile and inoffensive option. For the cooler weather or evenings or to wear on dates, choose Bleu Electrique instead of this; Bleu Electrique is much more refined and appealing, and costs less than Y EdP.

I can’t stand this fragrance. I blind bought it because it was on everyone’s list of one of the best designers out there. I wore it one time and found it so headache inducing that I sold it shortly after. The opening apple bomb is so sickly sweet and loud that I don’t know how anyone considers this a good hot weather scent. The dry down was shockingly feminine. After the obnoxious apple finally goes away, you are left with something that is very generic perfume smelling. No offense to anyone that enjoys this. I’m happy for you. It’s just not for me.

This scent is nothing short of spectacular. . This is dior savauge without all the people wearing it, & still crushes with the ladies.... . When you first spray it on, u get citrus, the Bergamot & ginger with a sweet touch of green apple in the background of it. It always get compliments! Women love that citrus. . This is a very easy-to-use versatile scent, it can be worn day or night. I wouldn't suggest wearing it to workout because how pungent it can be. But daily wear, leisure, night out, kickin it with the lady inside, this scent works! . I've been told it can be a little overpowering if u spray on a lot & im a classic OVER SPRAYER but I dnt care because the dry down is so damn good & still projects very well. Fellas, stop wasting time & get ya nose on this scent, you won't regret it!

I bought Y EDP in the summer of 2022, and made a statement on Parfumo recently, noting that the fragrance is divisive, and people will love it or hate it. I want to expand on that statement with a full review. ---- The opening combines herbal notes (mainly ginger and sage) mixed with a scent reminiscent of a sour apple candy that leans youthful.

To simplify it.. A great scent. Smells very nice. Since the first time I have smelled it, it just had something apart. Yeah, I know & I get that common fresh and your everyday scent. But guys, let's be honest..It's not quite your everyday scent. Yes, it's fresh, fruity and a bit sweet but in its own way. A great creation.

I liked this when I first purchased it. Then as time went on either I became more used to it or the sweet smells of the fragrance became stronger. When I smell this now it still evokes happy emotions of when I first wore ot, however now if I smell it for more than an 20 minutes it smells horrible. I think the apple or something is too sweet.

Oh, where do I even begin with Y Eau de Parfum? It is simply an incredible fragrance that exudes sophistication and class from the very first spritz. The blend of bergamot, ginger, and lemon in the opening notes immediately captures your attention, and the freshness of the scent lingers on your skin for hours.

This is such a fresh intoxicating smell. You can wear this day, night, casual, dates, and year round. I have received multiple compliments while wearing this. I started off buying a couple of decants and decided pretty much right away it’s bottle worthy and ordered a full bottle. It has good performance and longevity.

*This is a review of the original formula/vintage Loewe pour Homme. Loewe pour Homme opens with a blast of basil herb-laced aromatic lavender with hints of oakmoss rising from the base. As the composition moves to the early heart the mossy green oakmoss, aromatic lavender and herbal basil remain, now joined by sharp woody vetiver with accents of supporting lime-like tarragon and natural smelling mint leaf. During the late dry-down traces of the green oakmoss and vetiver remain, as relatively dry powdery resinous amber adds a touch of warmth. Projection is good and longevity excellent at 10-12 hours on skin. In its original formula Loewe pour Homme is quite the impressive one. It is a bit rough and ready at the open with its aromatic lavender and basil going all-out but that's just fine by me. As the mossy green oakmoss joined the party shortly after it became clear this composition is a winner and will not smell similar in its current form due to IFRA restrictions on the ingredient. The vetiver is just as important to the success of the composition as the lavender and oakmoss, as all three keep its aromatic fougere nature well-intact until reaching the late dry-down as powdery amber smooths the composition late. I have smelled better examples of vintage aromatic fougeres, but this is an excellent one for sure. The bottom line is while Loewe pour Homme (vintage) may lack the polish of some other vintage aromatic fougere peers, it definitely does not lack character and smells great, earning an "excellent" 4 stars out of 5 and a strong recommendation at the average eBay aftermarket price of under $24 a 30ml vintage bottle.

We are greeted by geranium, clary sage, rosemary, petitgrain, and also bitter orange. Sandalwood, vetiver, and moss come alive in the dry-down. To my nose the citrus is not strong enough to warrant comparisons with popular citrus bombs. Loewe PH is sadly overlooked, maybe because of its typical structure: spicy-herbal-citrus opening and woody base. Maybe it wasn't ground-breaking in 1974, but I appreciate its ability to be inoffensive while retaining its unabashed masculinity. You could easily rock this at the office today instead of resorting to something fresher and less masculine. Projection is moderate but longevity is good. I hear this 2010s formulation is less floral and less mossy than the vintage. It's well worth a sniff, but I can't attest to the juice in the newer tall bottles. Masculinity Level: Gordon Gekko delivering the "Greed is Good" speech.

Oh wow what a horrid opening. This thing will clear your sinuses for sure. Like getting sprayed in the face with lemon cleaner, drinking a shot of vodka, and eating a handful of basil all at once. After that assault on the senses, it just morphs into a tame fougere. Trouble is, there’s way better fougeres which cost way less and have much better openings. Pass.

Yes it is Spanish luxury niche quality company, and niche smell, sour citrusy blend, very elegant exellent quality spring-summer,this opens whith beautiful citrusy and lavender,(like azzaro p.h.but with added spises. the citrus stays From start to finish!!!!!is very masculine (oakmoss) yet elegant fresh citrusy smell.high quality realy special fragrance, Extremely long lasting,10hours.The projection is Medium(Ideal for the office) but !!very long.Even after 5 hours it still goes lightly feel 25cm From the skin,But you can feel it on your skin even after 8 hours skin scent Of course. For men 30+ Man in suit,Lawyer,Boss,Company manager,It evokes a feeling of luxury, By the way That lemon is beautifuuuuul.

I have days where I wake up craving a lemon in my life. And in those cases, a perfume like Loewe pour Homme is perfect. It follows a path already trodden by other more famous works, such as Eau Sauvage by Dior, but with some differentials of its own. At first it's just lemons... very potent and astringent. After a few seconds, the moss enters the scene, never to leave. As soon as this initial phase of lemon subsides a little, you can feel an accord of herbs, especially basil and lavender, such well-matched notes that are only perceptible together. Next, a bitter bergamot, which gains a floral touch from geranium. It gets more and more bitter, with the entry of vetiver and patchouli, but softened by musk, under a slightly amber base. The result is a unique old school elegance, with very good longevity, around 7 hours, and very good initial projection, which later, despite losing a little of its initial strength, does not leave anything to be desired. And the combination of notes, especially the moss, makes it very flexible, for any climate, from intense heat to autumn coolness.

It´s hard to find words to define the excellent quality of this fragrance. Outdated? No! Not at all. This fragrance reflects the excellence of Loewe House. As mentioned on the package it's "full of memories". I remember using this perfume, in my 20's on those early days of the 90s.

Special occasions or simply a perfectly groomed everyday appearance require special fragrances. Loewe pour Homme (formerly para hombre) has been a cornerstone of the aromatic citrus men’s genre since 1978. An outstanding scent! Over a basil-lavender backbone, rooted in a soft base of amber moss, rises a beautiful vintage lemon top.

There are days when I really don’t feel like ambiguity, unisex, or - to use a modern term - ‘gender-bending’. On those days, I want to smell like a man, straightforward, unpretentious, and simply: clear. To scent like a man. Not to smell and certainly not to stink, no: to scent!

Sure, this Loewe leans more towards a "classic" scent and will probably be predominantly worn by those over 30. But just as you might encounter an enthusiastic 20-year-old at a classical concert, the same should apply to this Spaniard, whose acquaintance I would like to recommend explicitly to younger people, despite the target group of the diagram.

This is how a well-known Frisian brewery advertised its product in the 90s - very successfully, many still remember the slogan - A distinctive male voice delivers the aforementioned statements from off-screen, while a no less distinctive man roams solitary coastal landscapes. At the end of the nearly thirty-second spot, he falls back into the dunes. No other beer. Angular.

As someone who really loves Roja's Elysium perfume, I bought it when it came out on a blind buy, hoping that this perfume would be better. In retrospect, it turned out that this perfume doesn't perform any better than the good, regular Elysium, and in terms of smell, it's also less good in my opinion, of course. After a month of in-depth testing, I decided that it was unnecessary to keep both in my collection and sold the intensive version. 6.5/10.

I heard everybody saying it has nothing to do with elysium. I disagree. Upon first spray you can immediatly recognize the elysium adn but with rhubarb which quickly fades into a wonderful grapefruit note, and some fruity nuances amped up. After 20 minutes becomes a bit more floral, but it always keeps the elysium core. I can definitely tell that it’s an Elysium flanker, not a stand alone one. I think this is lovely, probably superflous if you already own Elysium, but if i had to buy a bottle i wouldn’t know which one of the 2, cause they’re similar but with its own nuances. In any case, gorgeous, as expected, with very great performance as the Parfum Cologne.

Roja Dove Elysium Intense is a soft and deep aromatic fougere. Although it has a classic fougere structure, it smells quite modern/different to me. It's a well blended complex perfume where I find it difficult to isolate notes. Overall it is a green, clean, musky, floral, woody and leathery scent with a tart rhubarb note that makes it quite different and not off-putting to me. It has a decent longevity compared to Elysium, 6-8 hours depending on the amount applied, but far from "intense" IMHO. Yes, it's overpriced, but it's pleasant and distinctive.

Elysium eau intense starts with a big explosion of a soapy detergent smell. First i thought it was the bergamot, but it is actually white musk. Very synthetic and very strong. It is there to stay as long as the fragrance lives on! It burned my nose, wet my eyes. You get some hints of floral, aromatic and woody accords but none of them will triumph over the white musk. You see a complex notes pyramid but you barely get ghosts of the notes. Rhubarb tries to make itself shown but that detergent smell blocks it. I can dig a nice juniper accord but it is covered by that musk note. This has been the worst experience of my infatuation with fragrances for the last 25 years.

I did not like Elysium Eau Intense upon first testing. The problem, for me, was the rhubarb note. I love a well-done rhubarb note in fragrances but the challenge has been to find one that is sufficiently masculine-leaning to suit my taste. Up to that point, my benchmark rhubarb note was found in Bois 1920's Oltremare (and to a lesser extent, the rhubarb note found in Jovoy's 21 Conduit St). In Oltremare, the rhubarb note is fresh, crispy, and crackling. While the rhubarb note in EEI is definitely masculine - and as fresh as the rhubarb note in Oltremare - it lacked the crispness that I had come to associate with how that note is supposed to be done. The rhubarb note in EEI is soft and even, to certain extent, gelatinous. I could not overcome this bias for the first few testings, but there was, at the same time, something about the scent that kept me coming back. I am glad I did not give up on this delightful fragrance. Not only have I discovered a new approach to rhubarb, I could appreciate EEI for what it is: a unique, well-constructed, and polished warm-weather aromatic with an amazing rhubarb note! I fully intend on purchasing a full bottle in the near future.

The 3rd & final chance, as can be read from the title, because the previous two Elysiums have never managed to convince me after numerous tests so far. One might ask: Why do I keep putting myself through this? Why have I tested 32 Rojas, even though most of them couldn't convince me in the slightest?

I had already made my peace. With Roja Dove. The fragrances accompanied me on this scent journey, I even had the Elysium Cologne in my collection once, and I have tested almost all the others. But by now, they don't quite captivate me anymore. Don't get me wrong, there are wonderful compositions among them, but they mostly don't quite fit me, my preferences.

Roja takes us on an olfactory journey that is as exciting and captivating as a drive in a convertible along the windy coastal roads. This fragrance, a dynamic reinterpretation of the older Elysium, envelops us in the top-down freedom of the warmer seasons and lets us feel the pure joy of endless expanses.

Hello everyone, today I want to share relatively few and honest words with you about the Elysium Eau Intense ... Roja is one of the houses that has accompanied me for a very long time, but from a safe distance. Why? On the one hand, the somewhat absurd price of certain products (the perfumes) is well...

Hello everyone, So I have all 3 perfumes from the Elysium line, I am a fan of the Ely family…. and unfortunately, the Intense version is the worst of all, this is of course just my subjective opinion but it feels like the components have become less qualitative, which is probably why the prices are so cheap in quotation marks of course :) cheap.

In the journey of Perfumes, you might some times fill in traps, and one of those traps is you Mr. Bleu. No body can deny that it is a nice smell. But >>> Is it unique!!? Nope Is it powerful!!? Nope Is it a paradigm shift in perfume world!!? Definitely not Will, for my opinion its just another overhyped perfume i just fill in its trap, and its another boring flanker from the iconic perfume la nuit de l'homme>>>

This one is slightly fresher than the typical La Nuit de L'homme with better performance. I love how they substitute the vetiver and tonka bean notes of the Original LNDH with lavender and geranium on LNDH Bleu Électrique. Can be worn all year and most occasions, just be mindful in the high heat. A fantastic opening with a soft sexy dry-down. Very sensual scent, One of my all time favorites.

La nuit bleu electrique is the closest scent to the vintage version of the la nuit. La nuit EDT’s current formulation still smells heavenly, but it’s performance is such a disappointment. La nuit bleu electrique smells heavenly and it has acceptable performance. Fragrance opens with bergamot, cardamom and ginger. Opening of bleu electrique is a blue interpretation of og la nuit, more versatile and fresh. In the middle notes we see geranium that adds a floral depth and classic strong lavender of the la nuit line. In the base, cedar and vetiver adds a earthy, woody smell to the fragrance. The fragrance is pretty much more floral and powdery version of the Og la nuit. It’s a sweet scent and it was synthetic before maceration, but after maceration the synthetic smell is gone. I own about 50 fragrance including 6 niche ones (Green Irish Tweed, Oajan, Naxos, Layton Exclusif, Greenley and Torino 21) but this fragrance is my favorite one, I lost my virginity with this fragrance.This is all I should say about the smell. Suitable for Winter, Fall and Spring full-time, I also use this in summer but it might be over-sweet/cloying in extreme heat (+35 Celcius). Performance is above average. I get about 6-7 hours of longevity in summer and 8+ hours of longevity in winter. Projection is much better in high heat, but still enough for cold weather. It has a limited availability since it’s discontinued, I manage to find one from a prestigious store in Turkey, a 100ml bottle was about 73 Dollars in discount. Imo totally worth it, I regret that I didn’t buy a second bottle. If you would want a more versatile and better performing La nuit, would %100 recommend.

YSL did it .They fixed LNDH in its tragic 2021 state and transformed it into a powerful , mass appealing and sexy Fragrance . Dont get me wrong they did not reinvent the wheel nor did they make something groundbreaking that will change the shift of the fragrance world ,but they finally did something right. They created a fragrance that is meant to appeal to the masses and it actually does .Judging by the past mens releases of 2021 and 2020 it went downhill for the Y and L'homme line ,with one weak release after the other. But once again ,we're here LNDH Bleu Elecrtique is here and all that is past news. The fragrance kicks off with a spicy-fresh opening with the ginger not being that present in my nose but subtle yet existant.The bergamot and cardamom as well the cedarwood dominate the first note grabbing your attention by the instant. As it sets down the lavender geranium and vetiver show up as it dries down and turns into a more intimate scent in the matter of 3-4 Hours ,where I think its scent peaks. Copliments fly in with this fragrance ,its pretty much a case of the "you cant go wrong with this one" ,it is inoffensive ,it is pleasant and certainly not difficult to pull off. Some may find it boring ,I personally dont,I find it more interesting than your average blue line .Longevity is basically all day long especially on clothes ,silage on the other hand is not as strong ,with a 1-1.5 half foot projection at its peak.Finally, I really liked the bottle even when eau electrique came out ,turns out this time I like the fragrance too.

Among the perfumes I have, this one, along with Guerlain's L’Homme Ideal EDP, gives me the greatest sense of happiness and calm (and I don't have any olfactory memories associated with these two fragrances). For a few months, this YSL was hard to find in Europe (mine came from the Czech Republic), but I finally managed to buy it. Even though I paid more than usual compared to a few months ago (I bought a 60 ml bottle for €62 in September 2023), the purchase was fully satisfying. It belongs to the YSL L’Homme “family” but has some special characteristics. The opening is fantastic, and the dry down is as well. It is not a great projector and doesn't last long on my skin (about 6 hours on a good day), but it is one of those scents that are truly worth trying at least once in a lifetime. Suitable for any season of the year, this is the scent profile I would like to find more often among the blue fragrances that proliferate out there. I don't like most of them (neither Sauvage, nor Bleu de Chanel, nor MYSLF or Luna Rossa Ocean, among others), but this perfume is quite different from the ones I mentioned. A must-have!

Wow. This is like the original only fresher. And longer lasting. Fantastic scent. Powerful opening and soft dry down. Very spicy and fresh. Lovely blue bottle. You won’t be disappointed if you like the original. You will love this more

This Flanker is going to fight! This fragrance has recently come out and very good feelings were already coming from those who had tried it. After trying it, I can say that he has conquered me. Is it novel and original?

This fragrance is like a midnight stroll under a clear sky full of stars. It's mysterious and a bit spicy, but not too overpowering. It has a fresh and clean feeling that's perfect for a special night out. It's not too strong, so you won't overwhelm anyone, but it definitely leaves a pleasant impression. The bottle looks elegant on the shelf too.

It smells very good, and reminds a lot of the original LNDL. I guess from a marketing perspective it doesn't make much sense to market a perfume so close to the original, and is probably the reason its gone already. I did get a quite good longevity, and a nice silage with this one, which I dont get with the original, at least not in the same way.

This flanker of LNDH have same bottle style, same packaging, same recognizable DNA from the origin LNDH. An electric blue liquid inside the bottle very similar to a dilution of Methylene Blue. With the application you detect bergamot, ginger and creamy cardamom. A sweet and spicy scent.

The opening it's not very good, but after that, with the drydown, get better, a lot better. It's a old school smell but i think that is acceptable. PROS: - Last a lot and projects well - Not popular - A old school with nice drydown. - A quality fragrance - Elegant CONS: - Someone can think that is grandpa smell - Can be offensive if over apply It's a nice acquisition for a collector or for someone what looking for a good alternative to the formal - old school scents out there. If it's your case, try it. Regards.

I discovered this fantastic fougere a few months ago thanks to Scents of South Jersey on YouTube. For fans of old-school green fragrances like myself, Esencia is a dumb reach, especially in Spring. The pine tree needles note in this one is just outstanding throughout. It is often compared to Polo Green, Paco Rabanne Pour Homme, and Jaguar For Men, but its dry-down is much more subtle with just the right amount of oakmoss, no soapiness, and dare I say, it's just classier overall. Masculinity Level: Tom Berenger in Sniper, spending weeks in the forest getting his job done without ever actually getting dirty.

A fantastic '80s scent that transports you to a men's barbershop. Sharp scissors, razor, pomade. I sit in the chair and look in the mirror and sense the smells around me. And beside me, to my right and to my left, other gentlemen with sharp razors running down their faces, their eyes closed, sensing one scent as I do. Esencia pour Homme. Great !

Born in the 80's, but its soul lives in the 70's! Huge powerful frag that is awesome if you dig Polo Green, Quorum or other chypre/leather/fougere cousins from the era. A massive, in your face, rainbow of green wet forest, smoke, and leather. Extremely masculine and present with a projection sillage that may redefine "vapor trail". Put on your flannel, find an axe and splash away! 4 stars

Esencia starts off very fresh and extremely pleasant with a blast of aromatics and lavender. Then it turns very green (maybe a strong pine, perhaps?) and that is where it loses the thumbs up from me. The green notes are somewhat harsh and in your face at first, making me take pause and reconsider my initial positive impression... then they settle down and become pleasant.
