Bottom line is if you like green scents you will most likely enjoy Esencia. I can appreciate a lot of the positives that others have mentioned and concur with many of them... I just keep coming back to the initial pine overkill in the early heart notes before it calms down that prevents me from strongly recommending it. It is an above average green powerhouse, just not quite there. 3 out of 5 stars.
One of those 'boy toys' whose appeal (at least in my memory) is completely lost on girls of the same age is car quartets.

Today I finally had the chance to try Esencia by Loewe. I have wanted to test this classic from the brand for a long time. Loewe is known worldwide for its finest leather goods and classic fashion. It is mentioned in the same breath as Hermes. The company was founded in 1846. In that year, two royal weddings were to take place in Madrid.

Today I found myself wandering around car dealerships again, because I love shiny bodies and well-engineered engines. Time and again, I am drawn to the "star," even if my friends find it a bit stuffy, but these cars have always stood faithfully by my side. Solid with a touch of conservatism.

Essencia is one of the more inventive men's perfumes from Loewe. Which doesn't automatically mean it's good. The presentation and impression of this fragrance is dark green. Behind the citrusy top, which is tinted green with tarragon, there is indeed quite a bit of interesting stuff.

Somewhere I read that a man should not only father a child, build a house, and plant a tree in his life, but also have embraced the latter at least once. I imagine that embracing a tree would be somewhat unfulfilling on a tactile level. However, on an olfactory level, I was already tempted.

ROJA PARFUMS Aoud (2010) Parfum Unisex Sensual Inviting Sophisticated Mellow Very versatile Rather fresh than sweet High end quality One of the best rose ouds in my opinion! This was one of my first niche perfumes when starting my journey and the first rose oud in my collection. I still remember the feeling when smelling this one for first time. It’s still astonishingly A M A Z I N G Like all Roja Doves this scent has a lot of different notes and it’s impossible to separate those all. Three of them are anyway dominant in Aoud: Rose de Mai, Saffron and Oud. Oud is not skanky or animalic in this at all. It’s very restrained. After this settles down it’s getting more soft because of vanilla, nutmeg, cedarwood and sandalwood in the base but it’s strong anyway. Vanilla is like in most of Rojas: it’s impossible to detect. It gets mystical vibe and certain character from musk, leather and ambergris but all of them are blended perfectly and not at all bringing that sexual and erotic slightly animalistic vibe like in Musk Aoud. Longevity is eternal. From their website Top Notes: Lemon, Bergamot, Verbena Heart Notes: Geranium, Rose de Mai*, Jasmin de Grasse, Ylang Ylang Base Notes: Rhubarb, Cinnamon, Nutmeg, Saffron*, Patchouli, Cedarwood, Casmir Wood, Sandalwood, Aoud*, Vanilla, Leather, Ambergris, Musk * KEY INGREDIENTS That travel size is Aoud Absolue Precieux (discontinued). It’s a little bit more refined than original Aoud and the oil concentration is higher. Just a note: juice is really dark and it stains light clothes. Available in Crystal which is the same perfume without a color. DIFFERENCES BETWEEN AOUD AND Amber Aoud Parfum Both unisex with eternal longevity, huge sillage and projection. (The rating matches for both) I wanted to write about these Roja Dove’s two perfumes since there seems to be people who would like to know the difference of these two and if another one is redundant if you already have the other. You can check the differences from the notes of course but that doesn’t tell always how those similarities or/and differences appears. So here is my opinion. As I love Roja so much I have both: Aoud in 30ml and 100ml and Amber Aoud Crystal in 100ml. I like to have both and for me I feel that I need to have both. The difference is not so big for most of the people but it’s very noticeable for trained nose, rosewood lovers and Roja fans. Differences are: - Amber Aoud is slightly more sweet because of Fig in the opening and Benzoin in the base. - In the same time it’s warmer because of Ambergris and Benzoin in the base. (Ambergris is as well in Aoud but it’s not the main note.) - Aoud is more fresh and rosy. It’s more traditional Rose Oud scent. - Even if there is Saffron in both, Aoud is more earthy since there is less the main notes in overall so Saffron is easier to detect. - I would say that Aoud is not so complex than Amber Aoud. In Aoud it’s really easy to smell Rose, Saffron and Oud separately while in Amber Aoud its 5 different main base notes are really well blended. - Aoud is the first one of those three (Aoud, Musk Aoud, Amber Aoud) which Roja launched so it is like the most simple one. - Amber oud has a smoky feeling in it, it varies a lot between different batches though. If you want a real Rose Oud scent go for Aoud, if you are not a huge fan of traditional Rose Ouds, you can love Amber Aoud. MY OPINION: If you like AOUD, you will like Amber Aoud as well but not automatically in the other way. I hope this will help some people to choose between these two chic, captivating and mesmerizing perfumes. Musk Aoud is by the way totally different and unfortunately it’s discontinued due to the regulations of certain natural ingredients. I’m happy to own it as 30ml og and 100ml crystal. These both perfumes are suitable in the same kind of occasions, they share the same kind of feeling and character despite of the differences. They are attractive, seductice, rich, complex, mesmerising, utterly luxurious and absolutely in among of the best scents ever. The juice of the original perfumes is very dark and it stains clothes permanently so Crystal versions of those scents are very practical. I love to wear these scents during a summertime and with white clothes so clear juice is great with them. The scent itself is identical with the dark, original juice, only the colour has been removed.Both perfumes are unisex. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes

After reviewing Amber Aoud and Musk Aoud, here's my final review of the trio from Rojas Aoud collection. This time, it's about the one that started it all in 2011: Aoud. I have to say that Aoud is the only one of the trio of which I haven't tested the crystal version as well. Aoud can be considered a classical Rose-Oud-Saffron combination with the other notes from the breakdown supporting the blend but never becoming dominant. Aoud is a very authentic middle eastern smelling fragrance which not taken for granted at all considering it's released by a European brand. I've travelled a few times to the Middle East and can confirm that you are getting the real middle eastern smell with this fragrance. That means that the fragrance takes no compromises to appeal to costumers from the Western world. Either you like it or you don't. Aoud has some minor animalic facets. It's a smoothly blended mixture of opulent rose, dark and slightly smoky woods and spices. The opening is quite strong but after 1-2 hours, the dry down is more appealing to most people. Actually, the dry down is similar to the ones of Amber Aoud and Musk Aoud. Nowadays, Rose-Oud combinations are offered by many brands, so what makes Aoud stand out from the rest and worth 720€/100ml? Aoud was released in 2011 so it can be considered one of the first Rose-Oud fragrances on the western market. In addition, as I said it's very authentic. The packaging and presentation is very luxurious and Roja has high standards when it comes to quality of ingredients. But if that's enough to justify the price tag anyone has to decide for themselves. Considering performance, I had slightly higher expectations. Same as Amber Aoud and Musk Aoud, the fragrance last on my skin for about 8 hours with about 3 hours detectable sillage from my side. That's not bad but also not great either for this type of scent and also considering the price tag. However there are a few things I have to mention: I only tested the fragrance in colder climates. It would be interesting to see how it performs in the Middle East. Also, it's the only one from the collection that I currently don't own a full bottle. Spraying from a sample might be considerably less juice than spraying from the bottle. I can also not rule out that I'm just going to become olfactory fatigue after 3 hours because especially in the first hour Aoud is the strongest projecting of the trio to my nose. Let me finish the review with possible occasions where the fragrance is most suitable. The fragrance is of such high quality that I wouldn't waste it on anything except special occasions like birthdays, family gatherings or high class/black tie events, simply situations where it really matters. Of course, depending on your finances, this fragrance would be a great signature scent as well but a pretty costly one. When it comes to Oud our western conception is often that it's only going to work in colder climates. I happen to find the opposite. In the Middle East temperatures rarely go below 15°C through the year and in summer it's about 45°C. They still wear their oud scents so why we in the west shouldn't as well?

Roja Dove Aoud Review Aoud initially opens with fantastically bright notes of Lemon, Geranium, Jasmine and Ylang-Ylang however quickly develops more depth and complexity as the Oud, May Rose (the signature rose that Roja Dove uses in his Aoud creations), Saffron and Ambergris become more prominent. These notes blend together so beautifully. The opening feels Plasticky and screeching a bit after few minutes it fades away.   The dry down bears a noticeable similarity to Amber Aoud as the Rose, Saffron & Ambergris is the same. However as it lacks the fig and the resulting scent is much less sweet and instead more dry and woody compared to Amber Aoud. The warm spices of cinnamon and nutmeg are also slightly noticeable (the nutmeg is such a nice touch), however the rest of the notes are so well blended you would struggle to pick them out as we all know Roja Dove does his best work, creating a fragrance that is classical, timeless, complex yet modern & he always take pride in himself to use very high quality taw materials he even uses fractional distillation technique in making his pitch black dark, thick, staining fragrance liquid to make it as clear as tap water so that it won’t stain light colored clothes Of the 2 Aouds i have (Amber Aoud & Aoud) Amber Aoud to me have the best performance. Aoud is the dryer Amber Aoud is the sweetest & of the 3 Aoud is the most masculine (although as a Middle Eastern we don’t buy this Masculine/ Feminine thing unless is too feminine like for example Viva La Juicy or Tresor) I've read reviews of those that say his fragrances are just copycats of others before them ( Danger is a copy of Heritage, Fetish is a copy of Moschino PH blah, blah, blah) and I'm not buying that at all too, this how the fragrance industry works right now unfortunately after IFF banned so many raw materials and because of that many fragrances have been reformulated, now everyone is copying the other + look at those blue fragrances for example they all smell the same and i’m not a Roja fanboy not at all I’m not a fan of nobody, i just like some of his creations just like anybody else, who doesn’t like Diaghilev for example or Amber Aoud weather it’s Parfum or Absolue Precieux concentration. To me this is much more regal and refined than many Rose-Oud perfumes, a one of a kind fragrance and a true modern masterpiece. But to me Amber Aoud will always top it.

If anyone is looking for smooth non-barnyard aoud, then this is the one to go for. I love aoud, but this is my favourite so far. It has become quite a norm for niche houses to launch aoud perfumes, but hands down, no one has done it better than Roja Dove. This is a winter warmer and for formal occasions.

Aoud is actually so stunning, compared to Amber Aoud, this one is underrated. With that being said, I understand why, this is more traditional and Amber Aoud is sweeter. This is very dense, oily, almost inky oud/rose. There’s a bunch of salty ambergris here and the saffron gives a nice and smooth sweetness, it’s actually hard to imagine what this smells like just by description, one simply has to try it. Aoud will be my winter daily from now on :)) By the way, you can definitely wear this all year round

With Roja Dove, one would generally expect his creations to come across as radiant, substantial, and of the highest elegance. So far, none of his fragrances have disappointed me, even though the price range is notoriously beyond good and evil. Although the topic of Oud no longer really draws one in, it is still exciting to see what the master of exclusivity has made of it.

The first time I wore Aoud, the scent was heavy in the air, a blend of deep, dark warmth and mysterious elegance. As soon as I sprayed it on my wrists, it felt like I was stepping into an old, velvety palace in Marrakech; the woody notes of oud merged with the sensual rose and a hint of saffron into something that was both majestic and seductive.

It all started with my desire to be inspired by a fragrance once again. That doesn’t happen very often, and I mean real enthusiasm, like OH MY GOD! What is this? Smell, rejoice, dream.... I made my way to Düsseldorf to browse through the perfumeries, among other things.

As a newcomer to perfumes, I gladly accept being labeled a philistine who does not appreciate the artistic craft of Roja fragrances. Yes, exactly, plural. Because somehow I just can't warm up to them, or maybe not yet?! At first, I was willing to force myself to find certain highly rated Roja scents just as good.

A monstrance is an elaborately designed device for the ceremonial presentation of, for example, relics. Aoud is in a way a similar monstrance and serves, in my opinion, solely to showcase an idealized rose. I have rarely experienced a fragrance that so intensely brings a single ingredient to the forefront. The rose is staged here in an almost otherworldly manner.

"Black Opium" - a new scent by YSL? It would be better to openly declare on the package that it's a product by L'Oreal. The marketing people have tried very hard to make the most of a legend, but the result is a flanker which smells like a cross of "La Vie est belle", "Flowerbomb" and "Si" with a touch of coffee. Mediocrity, here you come. The bottle is from cheap-looking plastic and doesn't impress me much. Staying-power is good, but that's the only positive thing I have to say about this kind of horror from France. A loud, coarse and chemical scent capable of turning me into a perfume-hater.

i can never slander black opium. even though my tastes have expanded and i do not wear it daily, nor do i wear it often, when i need to smell sexy it is always there. this is a popular fragrance for a reason with a gorgeous drydown that really lingers on the skin. i recently oversprayed a little (for me anyway) and received one of my first fragrance compliments in a long time while wearing black opium, which continues this bottle's run as my most complimented scent. it's one of the first true crowd pleaser designer frags of the modern era, and for me, it will never overstay its welcome. on a separate note i do not enjoy any of the flankers, especially not the milquetoast "marshmallow" black opium glitter and my dislike of cherry continues with black opium over red. broadly with designer fragrance i am getting tired of brands attaching themselves to one line and releasing flankers like there's no tomorrow, even when the original DNA is completely absent or altered enough that it feels like photoshopping a family member into the picture. it's extremely hard to maintain original DNA and branding when you're stretching and modifying the fragrance's image and notes every two weeks to make more and more money, and as time goes on i fear brands will not innovate and produce more modern classics like black opium under unique branding, and will instead shove millions of dollars into making the next Donna BIR flanker that really should have been its own fragrance. one can complain about black opium but at least, for a long time, it was a stand-alone titan.

Smells like being drunk as fuck in New York City, stealing drags off of someone's off-brand menthol 100 and reading tarot cards at the bar. Little whiffs of it clung to the collar of my coat and followed me and my hangover around all the next day- little bursts of sweetness fading in and out, still-frames from a night that I couldn't quite remember all the way. A sexy, trashy, sugarbomb covered in glitter and mascara smears- I literally don't know what this smells like when it's not mixed with an ambient miasma of cigarette smoke, but if you wanna be the hottest girl loitering outside the door to the dive bar, there you go.

Only the name and bottle design reminded of glorious Opium brand, everything else is different. This is just another contemporary uber sweet Manifesto clone. Inspiration as usual was find in legendary Angel. Some mocca, lots of glucose and patchouli, fair amount of vanilla and voila... Black Opium is served. Not bad but already done and stereotypical. Rating: 5/10

I've always been of the opinion that Black Opium (and the whole Black Opium line) is a classic for a reason. It's sexy while remaining accessible and approachable. You want to dip your toes into the dark side? Start here. Maybe it's a bit overplayed, or maybe it's just widely beloved. Maybe both are true. I don't own a bottle currently, after falling in love with Illicit Green and it being sadly discontinued, but I still enjoy playing around with the different dupes as well as other fragrances that draw on similar Black Opium DNA. It's hard to go wrong with coffee, vanilla, and jasmine! And patchouli, of course. They could never make me hate you.

I'm so glad I got a sample of this before purchasing a full size! I hate this fragrance. It was so strong and overpowering that one spray filled the room, and I hate to air out the bedroom. If you have migraines that can be triggered my certain scents, I highly recommend trying this one first! I did not, and I regret it.

I have mixed (but mostly positive) feelings about Black Opium. The pear, vanilla, and white floral notes are weighed down heavily by the patchouli and the woodiness; the result is a very heady sweet suffocating scent. Yet I enjoy it; it makes you feel like a messy glamorous hot girl in 2014 who listens to Lana Del Rey and uses the Valencia filter on Instagram.

Clearly has been overhyped by social media, but still one of the better designer fragrance I've smelled recently. Very sweet, fresh and uplifting floral orange blossom blast (thankfully, it doesn't have that marshmallow vibe) paired with a small kick of spiciness. Starts settling into a coffee scent.

Black Opium by Yves Saint Laurent has become a classic, and while it's so popular that it might not seem unique anymore, I honestly still like it. Its sweet notes of coffee mixed with vanilla and jasmine create a rich and captivating scent, perfect for evening outings.

Perfectly balanced, signature worthy scent. It tangentially flirts with blue scents, but there's much more: there's incense, there's fruitiness, there's spices. I wouldn't call it a fresh scent, but a versatile one. I cannot think of a perfume that would fit the 4 seasons better. I think it's one of the most underrated fragrances out there.

I absolutely cannot understand the negative reviews! I got to know this scent a few weeks ago at a concert. I was standing in line for entry when I kept catching a whiff of an unfamiliar fragrance. I thought to myself: it must be the guy behind me who smells so good. So I simply asked him if he was wearing a perfume. He replied in English that he only understands English and Spanish and had traveled from Spain for the concert. So I asked him again in English, and he told me the name of the fragrance. After the concert, I ordered this scent blindly and I don't regret it at all! Upon spraying, it is quite synthetic. It feels cool and metallic. I can recognize blackcurrant. It has a bit of a shower gel vibe! But after a few minutes, a spiciness comes to the forefront, and the synthetic smell pleasantly rounds it off in the background. At the same time, this spiciness alternates with a woody scent. It's as if you were mixing pepper with incense, but both do not blend into one scent but rather alternate every few breaths. This is something that absolutely blows me away and is somehow also new for the German nose. This is why it is a perfect mix of designer and niche fragrance for me. The synthetics: designer, the unique spicy/woody: niche. Longevity is about 6-7 hours, and I find it not too close to the skin. My surroundings can definitely catch the scent. Great all-rounder for everyday use or for special occasions! The scent has completely convinced me and stands out massively from the German fragrance trends (which I now find nauseating) like Ombre Nomade, arabians Tonka, and all the other overwhelming stuff! Price/performance is also great.

I like freshies. I like "blue" scents. So the 7 Cobalt quickly came onto my radar, but after a sobering test on my arm, it didn't stay there long and disappeared. After I recently gave the Esencia Eau de Parfum a new chance and found it much better on my neck and in the air than just on my arm, I had to try the 7 Cobalt as well, and I was richly rewarded. I must say about this fragrance: Test it on your neck or don't test it at all. How I perceive a so-called "Full Wear" on my neck, I will now write here. (4 sprays in the neck area) The scent starts with a very refreshing and juicy blackcurrant and a refreshing blue trail; yes: a fruity shower gel aura spreads in the air. But the opening "disappears" quite quickly, and the drydown sets in very, very fast in my perception. And in the drydown, this fragrance is very unusual because I feel that at no point from the drydown do I perceive a mixture of several scents, but the different notes of 7 Cobalt come back like actors on stage, hold short monologues, and make way for their colleagues. The speaking parts are divided as follows: Sage and incense take the stage the most and hold the most energetic monologues. Pepper and vetiver have fewer speaking parts. Clove and tonka, on the other hand, are even less present, with the clove speaking very, very quietly. Fortunately. What surprises me: I often see the juniper berry on stage. However, it is not listed. Could it be? Is it the combination of blackcurrant, vetiver, and clove that makes me think of juniper berry? Be that as it may: The fragrance has something fresh, something dry, and through sage and incense a depth that, in terms of construction, reminds me of the legendary and beautiful "Acqua di Giò Profumo (Parfum) | Giorgio Armani," as there, too, the freshness is embedded in a deep and austere scenery of rosemary, sage, and incense. I don't want to say that 7 Cobalt resembles Acqua di Giò Profumo Parfum ; caution: I am talking about the "function" or construction. In fact, 7 Cobalt reminds me more of masculin Pluriel - less sharp, less pronounced, brighter and airier, and indeed bluer. This fragrance is not listed at all under "Similar." I can understand the similarity to Silver Mountain Water and "Bleu de Chanel (Eau de Parfum) | Chanel." Partially also to "Percival | Parfums de Marly," which was far too blue and far too "shower gel" for me. The alleged similarity to Antaeus Eau de Toilette must be more of a joke. Despite the incense, I see no closeness to my beloved "Dior Homme Sport (2021) | Dior." And I want to make the next point based on that: 7 Cobalt does not radiate as much as, for example, Dior Homme Sport (2021) ; it is significantly more reserved. However, I smell at least 4 hours of subtle scent clouds that I perceive as being between shower gel and interesting, mysterious accords of incense, sage, and pepper. Additionally, I must say that for me, one of the most beautiful and interesting variations of vetiver belongs here. After 4-5 hours, the fragrance becomes very close to the skin; I don't smell it myself anymore, but others (not strangers!) do upon inquiry. For me, the longevity is absolutely secondary or even uninteresting. For fragrances that I like, I find an application. As someone who showers multiple times a day, exercises, and has a fragmented workday, it's not a problem. And even if a fragrance is only perceivable to me for 2 hours, I enjoy it for those 2 hours and look forward to applying a new scent after my shower in a few hours. But this fragrance does last through a workday (7-8 hours), with the first half perceptible to the wearer and the second half only to others. And part of the religious mystery is also believing in what you cannot see. I believe, no, I know that the fragrance is there, even if I can no longer perceive it after 4-5 hours. That would be mystery number 3. Mystery number 1 arises from the sacral-sounding notes like sage and incense that frame the freshness. Mystery number 2 arises, as mentioned, from the fact that the notes are sometimes more, sometimes less perceivable, coming and going without one knowing when and why certain notes come back to my nose with varying intensity. The wearer must accept this. In this lies the beauty of this sillage: a variety of beautiful accords spread over several hours. I find the bottle beautiful. The wooden cap also fits wonderfully with this bottle color (dark turquoise with a metallic look?) Loewe, we are learning to love each other. I now have the Esencia Eau de Parfum in a 15ml travel bottle and this one in 100 ml. I also find the 001 Man Eau de Parfum interesting, as well as those with air and water labels on the bottles. But for now, this is good. I am happy with this access.

7 Cobalt is described here as a very masculine business scent, for which it could almost serve as a reference. Although the fragrance does not suit my taste (the dominant synthetic-mineral notes are to blame), it is really well made and comes across as extremely professional. The top note features a dry, bitter blackcurrant and herbaceous, sour sage. This gives the fragrance a fresh quality and radiates a certain strict coldness that becomes characteristic. Fruity pink pepper combined with subtle vetiver adds a pleasant spiciness. The scent is underscored by tame incense, which integrates beautifully and unobtrusively. Up to this point, the fragrance is pleasing and shower gel-like. However, I am still bothered by the typical citrus synthetic note. Following this, a cool-metallic graphite note emerges, which is elevated by a subtle clove spiciness. Everything feels well thought out and well executed. Personally, I miss some beautiful notes, although a certain harmony is indeed created. The metallic-cold scent is a bit overwhelming for me. However, I do see 7 Cobalt as a perfect business fragrance.

During my stay in Spain, I wanted to treat myself to a small, fragrant souvenir, so just before my departure, I found myself in a perfume shop. The saleswoman, charming and attentive, offered me to try Loewe 7 Cobalt after I told her about the scents I usually like. I was initially skeptical due to the rather cheap-looking bottle, but as soon as she sprayed the fragrance on me, I was immediately captivated. Upon spraying, the scent is quite cool and smells of blackcurrant (even though I don't really like it, I find it quite pleasant in this perfume). Many would label the scent as a "boring shower gel scent," but in my opinion, it is simply more than that, as it has an extraordinary H/S for such a fragrance, and the interplay with the incense harmonizes well after a few minutes. I can recommend this perfume to every Freshie lover to at least try it once. Another big plus point is that it seems to be a real insider tip, as the scent is practically under the radar. Even on YouTube, you won't find any German videos about it. This makes it all the more special in my eyes. If you're looking for something unique, you’ve come to the right place.

A lot happening at 7 Cobalt! Here are my brief impressions from the second test on skin & test strips (but perhaps without guarantee, as I'm slightly under the weather & I'm not sure how much I can trust my nose right now): At the beginning, the fragrance launches right away with a short citrus moment and is very, and above all, spicy!

I had the opportunity to get to know 7 Cobalt because shortly after the fragrance was released, I bought a perfume from a Spanish perfume retailer and received a few samples with it. One of these samples immediately appealed to me, and I knew I would have to buy this perfume sooner or later.

I bought the perfume blind here on Parfumo, but unfortunately I was a bit disappointed. The scent does not smell "fresh" and "green" to me as described, but rather has an old-fashioned quality, as if one were in a church during a funeral, but unfortunately the minister burned way too much incense and additionally a tonka bean slipped in.

Ok this one is kind of weird. In a good way though. What other reviewers stated so far is correct: A hyper masculine fresh opening. Very very blue and like a super simple shower gel...only soon after the opening you realize the actual complexity: A lot of different aromatics and the actual star of the show: incense.

This fragrance reminds me of something, but I don't know what. Sometimes I have the impression that there is blackcurrant DNA from YSL Opium homme. But I don't know if that's true or if it's just longing. Cobalt has a very aromatic, thick mousse of blackcurrants with a lot of woody, dry vetiver and fresh sage.

This is an extremely well-constructed oud blend - not too heavy, not too light. I'm not a huge oud person but this is the best oud blend I've tried. The more I wear this the better it gets. It's put together perfectly I think. But 600 bucks for 50ml? Probably not gonna happen.

This is the best from roja parfum imo its start with a creamy oud taif rose smooth but last and project imagine yourself in a big party in thge middles east where all women are in bikini on the side of the beach and your the baller! in lamborgini or rold royce this is what you whant to smell like!

"Smoky frankincense and hot pink pepper make up the backdrop of a modern and vibrant metropolis. Escaping the heat of the city, you take to the skies to attend a luxurious rooftop party. A fresh note of rose brings a breath of fresh air – a relief from the street mist. With the lights of downtown Dubai twinkling against the arabesque sky, a cloud of smoky cipriol and sugary blackcurrant releases the scent of hookah(narguilé) into the night. This is an energetic Oud scent, created to reflect the rhythm of the UAE." (Roja Dove) United Arab Emirates from the British House of Haute Luxury Niche Perfumery Roja London is part of the 'Gulf Collection', it is an Oriental Oud Rose Woody Spicy Incensed Unisex perfume. This fragrance was launched in 2017 and the nose behind this creation is Roja Dove. The UAE, home to the gleaming metropolis of Dubai, is a place where modern sensibility meets the heritage of a long tradition, which comes to life in this fragrance. The elegance of the rose, combined with the ancestral ingredients of 'oud and incense, form the tripod of this composition and pay homage to traditional Middle Eastern perfumery with a contemporary twist. As always, the quality and naturalness of the notes and chords are impressive! The fragrance opens with a shimmering burst with an expressive duet of mugwort and bergamot. Herbaceous mugwort adds a subtle green freshness, with a slight almost medicinal bitterness, which contrasts beautifully with the vibrant citrus of bergamot, creating an intriguing introduction. The rose of Taif reaches the heart of the fragrance with its sharp and fresh citrus characteristic, intertwining with the effervescent acidity of blackcurrant, effectively enhancing the sweetness of its petals. The clove imparts an aromatic warmth, balanced by the delicate masculine florality of the geranium and the sweet fruitiness of the ylang. A rich accord formed by resinous leathery labdanum merges with the intoxicating sweetness of jasmine, creating a complex and seductive floral heart unfolding in a warm and spicy embrace. On its way to the base the fragrance provides a slightly smoky, dark, deep woody and enveloping touch of the usual comfortable 'oud of Roja Dove. A powerful earthy accord is built on the resinous depths of the cipriol, whose smoky facets are enhanced by the woody and mossy notes. The sweet warmth of benzoin and frankincense creates a fine sacred and mystical aura, while the spice of cumin and pink pepper adds a spicy warmth and a surprising yet harmonious spice to this creation. A sensual nuance of musk completes the fragrance, leaving a lingering warm trail that is luxurious and enchanting. The overall effect is a mesmerizing dance between light and shadow; from spices, flowers, woods and resins. It performs very well!

Beautifully balanced rose-oud fragrance. Whenever I wear it, I feel so powerful. UAE is complex and highly nuanced fragrance with Taif Rose being its beating heart. Its opulent without being excessively grandiose - in other words - extremely mesmerizing! The oud in here isn't animalic nor funky at all, so nothing to be scared of. I run this one on special occasions, however, I do see this one could easily be all-year fragrance. Longevity 10h+ Projection - strong in the first 3h.

United Arab Emirates is a spicy woody-resinous-smoky oriental fragrance from 1001 Nights. Fairy-tale olfactory perfection. Euphoric, powerful, warm, soft, deep, and characterful. The United Arab Emirates are the source of inspiration for this wonderful scent by Roja Dove. United Arab Emirates is an ode in aesthetic Aoud, stunningly beautiful rose, and warm resin to this Arab federation. Since its founding in the early 1970s, the United Arab Emirates has grown into a confident nation. United Arab Emirates by Roja is infused with this powerful self-confidence. Yes, United Arab Emirates even has something euphoric about it that makes you want to dance after applying the fragrance. United Arab Emirates is a modern olfactory homage to the love of the UAE population for the scent note Aoud and other notes of Arab fragrance culture. Aoud has a long tradition in the United Arab Emirates. For several thousand years, Aoud has been used for incense. Even today, pieces of agarwood can be purchased in markets. For centuries, special incense vessels have been used in the East to perfume spaces, clothing, and oneself. Unlike the breathtakingly beautiful AJ Arabia VII, United Arab Emirates is not a consistently uncompromising Arab Aoud fragrance. Roja Dove looks at Abu Dhabi and Dubai through a European lens. United Arab Emirates is not characterized by the ornamentless opulence and purism of Arab perfumery through the minimalist use of a few traditional fragrance materials, as is the case with AJ Arabia VII. United Arab Emirates is therefore not an Arabic desert scent; it is rather the fragrance of cosmopolitan Dubai or Abu Dhabi. It evokes associations of well-measured warmth, well-groomed, stylish opulence, cosmopolitan luxury, and zest for life. Unlike traditionally Arabic fragrances (AJ Arabia, Al Kimiya), United Arab Emirates is not a linear scent with a few fragrance notes, but rather an exceedingly multifaceted and densely woven fragrance. United Arab Emirates is not a heavy, overloaded, oriental cliché fragrance; rather, despite its strength, it is imbued with the density of a delicate veil. A noble density of precious material that makes the fragrance seem to float dreamily over the cosmopolitan Emirates in 1001 Nights. United Arab Emirates is richer, more opulent, and denser than the other Aoud fragrances from Roja. I also find United Arab Emirates to be more versatile, Arabic, and - despite all its perfection - less self-absorbed in its own aesthetics than the other Roja Aouds. The Aoud note itself, however, is less prominent. Despite its orientation towards Arabic fragrance culture, United Arab Emirates remains a fragrance that is well-worn for European noses. Furthermore, United Arab Emirates is hardly more expensive than the men's fragrances from Roja. After spraying, a note reminiscent of freshly pumped gasoline is noticeable for a short time. By no means sharp, chemical, or unpleasant. It is much more the enticing scent that lingers in the air when you stand at a distance from a gas station in the summer heat of southern France, and a warm breeze carries a hint of the smell of heavily diluted, somewhat ethereal gasoline, mixed with the warm Mediterranean summer air, into your nose. The gasoline note quickly disappears. And the scent of a wonderfully, wonderfully, beautiful rose unfolds. I would go so far as to say that it is the most beautiful rose I have ever smelled in a perfume. Deep, profound, majestic, sublime, radiating in dark red, yes, even radiantly so, with breathtaking, legendary beauty. The rose appears in a way that is three-dimensional, as if one were standing in a surreal, magnificent, fairy-tale rose garden in 1001 Nights. At the beginning of the heart note, a light summer breeze of fresh berries joins the rose. However, this oriental berry note gradually recedes into the background over time. Green-floral facets accompany the rose for a bit longer, initially green, gradually taking on a citrus-fresh character. A latent smokiness quickly develops, which remains with the fragrance until the base. Black, desert-dry incense. Not dense smoke, but rather a fine mist, loose incense clouds. This underlying smokiness enhances the dark brown, distinctly noble spiciness that now becomes noticeable (clove and a bit of lively pepper). And then the Aoud enters the stage. The underlying incense makes the Aoud appear somewhat smoky. The Aoud component itself most closely resembles the Aoud component in Roja's Amber Aoud, especially at the beginning. Thus, the Aoud note in United Arab Emirates is rather of the gentler kind. It has the color of dark brown precious tropical wood, smells dark-woody, minimally ethereal, and in consistency, it moves towards Aoud oil as the fragrance progresses. The Aoud used has something very velvety, almost embracing in its nature. The Aoud is neither musty, animalistic, fecal, nor bestial. There are no associations of cow stalls or manure. Only a subtle note of cumin playfully teases out a slightly corporeal note from the Aoud. These undertones of incense and cumin take away any boredom from the exceedingly aesthetic Aoud, which can indeed set in after a while with Amber Aoud by Roja. A discreet benzoin note, warm, dry-resinous, with hints of vanilla in the further fragrance progression, gives United Arab Emirates a characteristically oriental-sweet touch. Cotton-soft, summer-warm musk and amber-colored resinous notes increasingly lend United Arab Emirates a sensually velvety and warm softness. Occasionally, a citrus facet flashes, which slightly enhances the green note in the background. As the fragrance progresses, United Arab Emirates becomes more beautiful and more aoud-like. While Aoud is an important note among several at the beginning of the fragrance progression, it gradually emerges more and more. This makes United Arab Emirates rounder and woodier with a very slight bitter note. The warm sweet-woody and sweet-resinous notes provide a counterbalance. This is due, in addition to the already mentioned benzoin and other warm, more dry than sticky resin notes, to guaiac wood. Sweet, balsamic, aromatic, with a slightly smoky undertone. United Arab Emirates is less smooth, less emphasized aesthetically, and velvety than Amber Aoud by Roja. Instead, it is clearly more Arabic and characterful. United Arab Emirates is for me THE perfume of cosmopolitan Dubai or Abu Dhabi. The perfume exudes the confident, oriental, modern, euphoric spirit of Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Stunningly beautiful, in olfactory perfection, euphoric - that makes you want to dance.

With Cravache's excellent commentary, everything has already been perfectly said about this noble Arabic fragrance, which once again shows what elixirs this wizard, Roja Dove, is capable of brewing. So I would like to add my impressions of wearing this olfactory powerhouse, which steals the senses of its wearer and the surroundings, and therefore should be used with caution.

A few days ago, I briefly "tested" the UAE and found that it deserves a proper test. So today is the day of truth. This morning, I applied 4 sprays generously ;) I was a bit taken aback at first, but this fragrance creation is worth a little cough... On the tram... no noticeable reactions. ............ Arrived at the office "Wow, you smell strong today" mhm.

Niche fragrances, scent pyramids, top, heart, and base notes are uncharted territory for me. Also, 'olfactory' had not yet been stored in my vocabulary and had to be chased down through the search engine first. Thus, it is undeniable that I am an absolute amateur in this field. By the way, my signature scent is Oud Wood by TF.

What is this? I spray UAE on myself and what do I think I smell? SAFFRON! That can't be right, at least it's not listed in the fragrance pyramid. This note ruins many scents for me, especially many ouds. Am I mistaken? Is there another culprit?

I remember the first time I fell in love with this perfume. It happened unexpectedly, in the duty-free shop at the Barcelona airport. I sniffed it once—carelessly, perhaps—but something about it stuck with me. I didn’t buy it then, and I’ve regretted that moment ever since. Onboard the plane, I couldn’t stop smelling the back of my hand. The more I inhaled, the more I fell for it. It was already too late. Let me introduce you to this olfactory marvel: SOLO by Loewe—an original bouquet as intricate and wild as one of Antoni Gaudí’s masterpieces. For me, it’s a dry, sweet-oriental woody-spicy fragrance—complex and full of contrasts, like sunlight filtering through colored glass. It opens with a zesty explosion of citrus: lemon, mandarin, and bergamot, both juice and peel—bright and sparkling. But it’s not a sharp citrus. It’s round and full, like the memory of fruit on warm skin. The opening reminds me a bit of John Varvatos Artisan, but then... something else arrives. Something strange and wonderful. I think it’s guava. I don’t know if I’ve ever truly smelled fresh guava—but if a Hawaiian sunset had a scent, this might be it. It’s sweet, floral, exotic, but never falls into the usual coconut-pineapple cliché. Instead, it’s aromatic and slightly heady, like a breeze carrying the scent of blooming fruit trees from some distant grove. I’ve read guava is hard to describe—and that makes sense. It smells like a warning wrapped in a lullaby. All I know is, it makes me feel far away, somewhere softer than here. Then comes the green twist—rosemary and thyme, subtle but persistent. They don’t shout; they hover—light, elusive—like something you catch in passing. Soon after, the base begins to stir. Warm notes of cashmere wood, patchouli, and cistus rise from the skin—resinous, rich, and beautifully blended. It’s unusual to feel these deeper notes surfacing so soon, almost bypassing the heart altogether. And yet, here they are, guiding you gently forward. The heart reveals more layers: pink pepper in generous doses, spiced with a hint of cinnamon and caraway. A second breath of citrus—likely tangerine—flickers back in, reminding you the brightness never truly left. Aldehydes, too—but not the sterile, aquatic kind. These are like crisp air through an open window. And amid it all, the dry, bright trace of crushed pink peppercorns lingers—one of my favorite aromas in perfumery. After about an hour, it all settles into a warm, dry woody accord—amber, soft musk, oakmoss, and vanilla. It wraps itself around you and stays for hours, gentle on both skin and fabric. Despite the presence of vanilla and musk, the scent never turns powdery. It remains clean, earthy, refined. There’s lavender. Guava. Cinnamon. Mint. A kaleidoscope of notes that might sound familiar in theory, but in practice, feels utterly new. Nothing here is quite what you expect—and that’s precisely the magic. This fragrance stunned me. Its complexity is rare. SOLO is extraordinary, and I can’t think of anything else that smells like it—except perhaps its own elusive flankers. The bottle is as elegant as the scent itself: clean design with bronze metal detailing, orange-brown juice inside hinting at sun-drenched citrus and glowing spices. It wears best in warmer months—late spring, summer, early autumn—when its bright, airy depth feels most at home. On my skin, both longevity and sillage are above average. I’ve worn this scent many times since that first encounter, and it never fails to move me. It deserves a solid 9/10. I’m glad it’s not worn by many—it makes it feel like a secret. A scent that doesn’t shout, but sings to the soul. It makes me feel like I’m someone worth reflecting on. Like an artist. Like a thinker. Like someone momentarily lifted out of the noise and into their own clarity. And how fitting, then, that it’s called SOLO—because this is a fragrance that understands solitude, and somehow elevates it. I’ve owned my bottle since that unforgettable brush with fate in Barcelona, April 2017. And every time I wear it, it brings me right back to that moment—wistful, alive, and surrounded by light. — Elysium

This fragrance opens beautifully with citrus and a tropical fruit and lavender. Especially, the citrus effect is more dominant and the fruity effect is pleasant. Also at the opening, lavender has a floral touch. The dominant citrus effect and slightly fruity effect at opening continues until the fragrance loses its effect. After a while, beautiful fresh and mild spices accompany this fragrance. A very mild mint scent over time adds a fresher air to this perfume. Sometimes I can smell the rosemary and cinnamon notes lightly. Then, when a light green and woody effect is added to this fragrance, the dominant citrus and fresh fruit make the character of this scent. It's such a good and aromatic mix. A classic and beautiful fragrance for men. This perfume was a gift from my darling. A nice gift.. I think it is a more suitable fragrance especially for spring, summer and warm weather. It lasts more than 15+ hours on my skin.

As I wore this through the day my mind kept going back to thoughts of Hermes' Terre, the original. Dirty, spicy and sweeter though tangerine instead of orange-add guava and no inert mineral note. I had no hesitation in wearing this though like Hermes'TdH it seems to lean more towards the older gentleman. Loewes, a Spanish company, has kept me happy with all their scents that I own so far.

Solo is a good fragrance and a safe buy. Nothing extraordinary, but a nice fruity blend for everyday/all-year-around. Smells good and not offensive. Fruity and fresh. Lots of lavender with guava and tangerine. Actually smells very synthetic. Projection, sillage and lasting power are medium. Updated December 2013

It seems that the little lion doesn't have too many friends. He is criticized for being too tame, too mass-appealing, and too polished, a bit weak on the chest especially, and certainly not independent, quirky like the head that promotes him. Disappointment resonates from this judgment, disillusionment, and one or two lost illusions. And none of that is wrong - actually. And also not right - actually. Because he can do a bit more than what people expect of him, what they attribute to him, he does on my women's skin. In the almost two weeks during which he was "the one and only," during which he shared table and bed, day and night, train and car with me, the little lion, I got to know him in his many facets, which revealed themselves one after the other - some on the same day, some only the next, the day after, or even later. They all led me to Spain - the Spain I encountered on my travels to Andalusia and the Costa Blanca. My first encounter with the little lion took place on a warm day - the sun warmed my bare skin, bringing summer early at the end of March. Blue sky, no clouds, the garden full of yellow and green. "Solo" opened with gentle white, with bright green, with plenty of neroli and soft bergamot - a cologne like so many that are loved passionately in Spain, which stand in half-liter bottles in almost every shop at a price one can hardly believe, considering what the nose later tells. Nothing stings, nothing scratches - no Domestos, no toilet cleaner. Light, fresh, fine - perhaps the only thing that helps at 40 degrees in the shade. So he remained, the little lion, the whole long day - whatever else the pyramid said: Nothing was true. Not on that first day. In the following days, which were cooler, rainier, rougher, I was surrounded by the salty sea air of the White Coast, climbed from orange and lemon groves up into the ethereal coolness of the conifers and the rocks high up on the Montgó, in the Sierra Nevada, sat in some bar in a side street of Granada back to back with a stranger who wore Parera's "Varon Dandy," smelled the scent of woods and spices, the clean skin and the sherry in front of him on the table. I stood in the cool walls of the Alhambra, the remnants of sacred smoke in my nose, mixed with the water of the outdoor pools. He is not a loud scent, Loewe's "Solo," never, in any of its quirky facets. You notice him, you notice me with him, turn your head when you are close to me, mostly wordlessly, with a smile. Only once, just once, was I asked: "What do you smell like?" By a boy, a little one, nine years old, whom I had known since his birth, who had never asked in all that time. "What do you smell like?" "A perfume. Is it good?" He nodded, smiled, a bit shy almost: "It's good. I like how you smell." And for the rest of the time, he sat a little closer. The little lion had a new friend.

The eccentricity of the advertising posters depicted above does not match the fragrance. That’s for sure. One expects something punky, slightly quirky, at least unconventional. Fairly speaking, one must then note that the bottle reflects quite accurately what "Solo Loewe" contains. A fragrance that falls into the "Okay" category. No more, no less.

That's me never ever! This was my first thought that immediately manifested in my mind after spraying it (and then clumsily dropping it). The top note is very fruity and the lavender adds a bit of sweetness here. The heart note then presents itself somewhat soapy with a hefty spice potpourri. That wouldn't actually be bad if the mint had been left out.

Somehow, I’m currently on a roll with beautiful scents that have very weak longevity and sillage. Unfortunately, Solo Eau de Toilette is also one of those fragrances. I don’t quite understand why this one has been rated so poorly. Or was the disappointment over the poor performance the overriding factor?

I first encountered Solo Loewe in 2006 at the renowned perfumery Kobberger, when it still had its doors open on Frankfurt's Zeil. I was looking for a new fragrance for myself and was ready to spend some time testing. I made it clear to the saleswoman that I was searching for a characterful, leathery yet fresh scent suitable for everyday use.

"...or stay single!" If your girlfriend says this to you, I fully understand her words. Because as a guy, you probably chose the wrong scent... "Solo Loewe". After the wonderful "7 de Loewe" joined my collection the day before yesterday, I received a few samples of Solo. And unfortunately, it cannot hold a candle to the beautifully designed blue bottle...

Libre EDP it's a quite soapy, clean, fresh, florally scent. I like the dry down way more than the opening as it can be too citrusy and sharp at times. The lavender can be a bit overwhelming as well and it sort of gives the fragrance a certain "masculine" edge that might be exacerbated in certain skin chemistries and might not be everyone's taste because of it, however I personally love that androgynous edge and find it quite exquisite and unique. The dry down is delicate and pleasant, the vanilla blends beautifully with the white florals and the amber in such a classy and timeless way! I wear it year round as I find this one a very versatile atemporal scent. Longevity and projection are not great though...I'm not too sure if it's because I bought a 2019 batch or what, but it doesn't last at all on me and people don't seem to really smell it after around 2-3 hours, I can't even smell it that much after that time on my own skin either which I find odd since all the samples I had before performed better than my actual bottle, but like I said, it could be because it's an "older" batch. Overall I really like it when I want something quick and versatile to wear that works with pretty much any weather and any occasion and makes me feel quite well put together!

OG Libre and Libre Intense are STRONG, you don’t need much, but they are lovely. Very similar to each other, the OG is fresher and fruiter and i get more of the lavender than in the intense. I get lavender, vanilla, florals and musk and the mandarin orange is mostly just in the opening. Really love them.

Really hated it on me, it smelled dated and funky. I enjoyed the lavender start and was waiting to be taken onto an interesting ride but on my skin it went completely sour. Love the bottle and on the right person I can imagine this smelling nice but to me it was not worth the price and there are way better alternatives out there.

Tried this every which way, in different seasons, and this is a definite NO! Yup, with an exclamation mark. I get a beautiful bouquet of white flowers buried deep, like 6 feet under a thick layer of radioactive aspartame sweetener. Mortuary flowers hiding a rotting corpse, and no amount of vanilla or musk could keep your imagination from wondering what the whitish, decaying flesh that`s dripping into a puddle at the bottom of the coffin would smell like. Apologies to anyone who loves this, but this is what Libre evokes for me.

Very strong sillage – it consistently choked out the whole room for the first few hours. The flavor profile was all over the place. Vaguely citrusy, super sweet, aggressively jasminey, warm and kind of powdery underneath... And somehow none of those notes mixed together in a cohesive way. I sprayed it once and felt like I was sitting in a poorly ventilated room with three people with very different perfume tastes (and the same overspraying problem). The smells were constantly clashing and trying to overpower each other, giving me a headache. At first I thought that maybe it would mellow out into something interesting if given a little time? Nope. The composition never came together. Crowded. Loud. Overwhelming. Neroli and orange disappeared first – in about an hour. Jasmine left the room another ~1,5 hours later. I was left alone with the base notes, which at that point settled closer to my skin – still very sweet, with an unpleasant prickly undertone that I couldn't quite put my finger on. In ~2 hours the base became nice and mellow, and in another ~3 it was gone. I was finally home alone. It somehow managed to drain my social battery without ever making me speak to anyone, lol. And I don't even have the energy to be annoyed about it tbh – I'm just glad the party's over now.

Nothing new, just a rendition of a perfume very popular during the 90s - and that's the vibe more mature people can get from it. This could actually be a dupe of Dolce & Gabbana - BY (try to believe!). Same soapish, bitter and cold notes - like in a lavender soap bar. Very boring and unpleasant, and surely distinctive because of that.

I really don't like saying this, but i kind of dont get the hype? i feel like something is missing. It's a floral lavender, but i think it's non-offensive. It does have that "perfumey" smell if that makes sense, like it's not a natural smell.

Libre was love at first sniff for me, which happens a lot...I can't lie about that, however the major difference is that this has become a long-term love. My husband complimented me on this fragrance the first time I tested this, which never happens...so I know if I love a scent and he loves a scent, it's "go time".
I'm not fan of powerful and heavy perfumes, so YSL Libre didn't work for me, unfortunately. The smell of overbearing florals and chemical s gave me a headache.

This is a masterpiece that takes them to the best places at night. When you wear it you feel like you are present, that everyone notices you. The first time I wore it was when I went out to a wine bar and a lady sitting at the bar just came up to me and told me I smelled good and from there we kept talking. The super masculine version of the perfume Sweetie Aoud just without the DNA of Patisserie Accord and with a few other small changes. I tell you again - this is a masterpiece. 9.5/10.

The best of the 3 PDLN's, expensive stuff but I was lucky to get mine for half the price. Luxurious scent and makes you feel good for sure, its not for everyone, especially with the price. It Reminds me abit of a cheaper Roja Dove scent in Sweetie Aoud, but this is more luxurious.

Before a full depth reviews: PARFUM de la NUIT 1 Very sensual and seductive, not the easiest one of these three. There are light leathery tones and an animalic touch in this -very sophisticated though- with soft Vanilla. This is definitely my favorite and it performs best on my skin of these three. Absolutely stunning and sexy, a tad naughty scent. PARFUM de la NUIT 2 Three notes - Rum, Cocoa and Vanilla - together with balsamic notes creates a pleasant a little bit sweet, not exactly but Coca Cola kind of scent which is chic. This is the most versatile of these three because of the missing animalic nuance (in 1) and leather (in 3) and this is the most unisex one. You have to like boozy note tho. Anyway on my skin something bothers me sometimes. PARFUM de la NUIT 3 Rose, Labdanum, Leather and earthy Saffron create the soul for this blend. This is not at all a rosy scent though, it’s only a supportive note. This is the driest one of these with woody, balsamic warmth of Amyris. Not at all sweet. This is the best on men imo. Leather is very attractive here. PDLN1 is my favorite even if now while wearing them all I want to have them all. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

So how does a businessman smell, you ask? Exactly This scent is so suitable for a night out at a fancy restaurant when you arrive in your expensive car and all eyes are on you. A perfume that only insiders will understand its greatness. Do you know Sweetie Aoud ? So Roja took the same DNA of the perfume and simply released the Patisserie Accord. A perfume that opens with bergamot and Artemisia and after it balances on the skin you feel the power and uniqueness of this perfume Amyris Frankincense Cumin comes with an unforgettable performance and simply gives a wonderful feeling of a serious businessman! for me : 9.5/10

This is not even a fragrance, this should be marketed as: the second skin. It feels like a second skin, which radiates this otherwordly aura of it, it is truly magical. . I just cannot get enough of it. That smooth leather mixed with the beautifully done cardamom and amber. The fragrance is light But still dense. I rememver Roja saying that one of his favorite comments about himself was when someone told him, that he is the pornographer of perfumery, and true, Pdln3 is really fragrance porn.

Getting directly to the point: to my nose, PDLN3 is a remarkable achievement in perfumery. It's exactly what I've been looking for in an upscale, 'special occasions only' fragrance. SCENT: A dreamy, resplendent rose and frankincense combination almost too extraordinary to be accurately described.

Roja Parfum de la Nuit 3 strikes me as a warm, amber-balsamic fragrance with a smooth, sweet floral-honey layer. I don’t read it as a rose-driven perfume. Instead, I get honeyed softness over resin, woody, spicy character with an ash note that adds depth without weighing it down. It feels elegant, polished, and quietly sensual rather than flashy.

Uncommented Fragrances No. 107 To get straight to the point: Roja's Parfums de la Nuit have an extravagant price-performance ratio. The three fragrances are said to cost around 1,200.00 euros (for 100 ml of pure perfume, for Extrait?

Hello everyone, today I would like to say something about "Parfum de la Nuit 3 | Roja Parfums" and address quite precisely what I wrote above. I have known the entire range for quite a few years now, and ultimately I liked each one in its own way (some quite a lot).

This fragrance is a masterpiece of seduction: An incredibly sensual and dry leather chypre, exotically enlivened by a fascinating spice, dominated by cumin and saffron. The warm base of resins and woods makes it a profound, elegant companion for the night. A luxurious, unforgettable statement.

Solo Cedro opens very blandly with a slightly sweetened vague aromatic woodiness. I usually refer to this style of bland modern department store designer perfumery as "amberwood," but it turns out Solo Cedro actually lists the aromachemical "amberwood" as a note so I'll refrain from calling it that as it might get confusing. But regardless, it smells like a very bland blue fragrance in the opening. It gets a bit woodier in the heart of the fragrance, with the cedar and guaiac shining through a bit, but the synthetic notes cling on and don't really allow anything really interesting to happen. The drydown is remarkably similar to Versace Man Eau Fraîche Eau de Toilette or Bergamote 22 Eau de Parfum (possibly cedar/petitgrain/amber combo) which is nice, but I would definitely take the Versace's opening to this one. So it's just a worse version of a scent that came out 10 years before it, and costs way less on discounters? Not a great place to be. Pass.

Duller than the dullest woody scent on Earth, but I’ll admit it: it’s nice to wear. And compared to other mid-range cedar-based scent like the horrid Chopard Noble Cedar and the likes, it’s easily better than many of them. It’s flatly artificial to the bone but it feels smooth, fresh (a refined, slightly powdery kind of orange-infused freshness, thanks to neroli), slightly sweet-fruity, with a classy touch of balmy herbal mint and something like tea. And cedar, of course. It reminds me a bit of Dunhill Icon with less complexity and more crisp wood. And obviously it’s in the same league of Terre d’Hermès and countless of other woody-fresh scents, but the presence of neroli, of a powdery-minty axe and of cedar more than vetiver makes it slightly (really slightly) different from many of them. Say, drier and warmer and the same time. Simple and unpretentious, completely uninteresting from a “fragrance fan” point of view, but quite pleasant to wear. Clean, cleverly composed and showing a really nice balance of tones – from warm to tart. Easily (and nothing more than) a safe and surely successful Christmas gift for dads, brothers and colleagues ready to dismiss their Axe fragrances. 6/10

I recall trying this fragrance at a store about 3 years ago, before the quarantine and I really enjoyed it, perhaps not enough to purchase at full retail but it did left a good impression. 3 years later I recalled it and somehow a needed to have it and I wouldn't stop at anything to get it but it seems to be either discontinued or just hard to get anyhow, I got it from a discounter (not too discounted) and what happened after these years? Well it's just as good. It's all about the cedar here as you can expect (Cedro is spanish for Cedar) and it's done right. It's not a ground breaking fragrance by any means or a sexy bomb but it's a solid elegant fragrance that's great for office wear or night out, cooler afternoons and formal events. Performance here is solid so all good with this scent, very glad I purchased it.

An absolute delight is what it is. Airy and fresh with a sweet cedar undertone, like taking refuge from the scorching summer sun under a canopy of an old coniferous tree. Almost milky with just a touch of spice, like picking out and eating the yet unripe grains off a feral wheat plant you found in the fields as a child. A very gentle woody smell that's hard to overdo or go wrong with. It's delicate, it's elegant... It's just sublime. I can't help but adore it.
The opening is an average citrus-blue scent, like so many others that came before and will surely come after to please the masses.

Tested together with my husband, I am thrilled. A dreamy, woody scent. It lasts a long time and the sillage is not bad either. His jacket still smells of it and I keep taking a sniff in between. I wanted to gift it to my husband for his birthday. However, I suspect that he will acquire it himself next week.

Tested yesterday. Consultant No. 1: "Do you know this Loewe?" (emphasized like "the lion"). Consultant No. 2: "Well, then you should definitely try this Loewe." (emphasized like Loo-äwe). Consultant No. 3: "And...? How do you like the Loewe?" (emphasized like Jogi Löw). In short: I do not recognize any of the fragrance components listed above.

..... it bites! Really. Scratchy sharp and full of synthetics. BUT: A scent like I have never known before. And I can and must say that I find it good that the spoiled buyer (that’s how I’d like to call myself) is finally offered something new in fragrances. Even if it is bursting with artificiality. If it smells good, all the better. But what does good smell mean?

Two associations are immediately triggered by Cedro upon spraying: An aquatic freshness hits you, which comes across as very mainstream and inevitably evokes memories of typical blue, inexpensive shower gels like Duschdas or Fa. Initially only in the background, then dominating, a pleasant woody note joins in, which is dry and has a slight sharpness.

I am the lucky owner of this beauty and unfortunately before getting my perfume I have read a few "reviews" about it on Fragrantica or Parfumo .. of course they are mainly unfavorable. And we humans tend to be very easy to influence with visuals or text, therefore my expectations were low .. I was waiting to dislike it. Then when I got it, with the typical luxurious YSL La Vestiarie presentation, the 125ml version .. I opened it, it was already potent without spraying and two sprays on each shoulder and one on the wrist to see what will it be .. This starts very smoky and spicy in the same time, the pepper does a great job and the elemi with its resinous character makes it very mysterious, oriental like. Then you are hit with the saffron, but not in big quantity .. and a big heart of frankincense, almost reminding me of the Dhofar one from Amouage, very very high quality smelling. And in a few minutes, the awesomeness comes to life .. a vanilla to die for, in the company of the strong smoke and the nicest frankincense you can smell in a non Amouage/OmanLuxury. Projects like a maniac for 4 hours or more .. then up to 8 hours stays like a skin scent, but so addictive .. so far this is the first scent which made sniff my arms over and over again. I know Dominic Ropion created Vanagloria too, which is regarded as one of the nicest vanilla out there .. and I do not know the Laboratorio Olfativo creation but if they smell similar like someone said, why is that bad? Ropion created Promise for Malle and Oud Aquilaria for OmanLuxury which are 1 to 1 .. how is this not good, I would ask? YSL made a good job here, the scent is awesome .. and has nothing to do with the name.

Babycat, also known as Copycat, is an exact copy clone of Vanagloria by Laboratorio Olfattivo. Created by the same perfumer (Dominique Ropion) who seems like he used the same formula to gain double money. Since laboratorio olfattivo is true underground niche and youtubers hardly get at that, ysl is easier to hype. I’ll stick with vanagloria. Both are caramelized incense. Same juice in 2 different bottles. I really can’t understand why nobody knows about Vanagloria and Babycat is out of stock :-) Ropion is laughing at that i’m sure. Similarities: Rosendo Mateu 5: 75% Vanagloria: 101% (altough i wouldn’t say similarity, is actually the same juice in 2 different bottles).

Such a bizarre name for a fragrance. I anticipate the squinty eyed stare when people compliment and curiously ask what I'm wearing. I find myself pridefully stating "Yves Saint Laurent", just before mumbling "Babycat" with slight embarrassment. "As in kitty cat?" Yeah, sure. Truthfully, I bare no guilt when wearing this fragrance as I genuinely enjoy it. Is it worth the hype? Yes, of course! It was created by Dominique Ropion! However, it is not worth paying the ridiculous upcharge for the sake of saying you have it. I was lucky enough to have a friend grab me a bottle from Harrod's in London. Babycat is a fragrance for both vanilla and frankincense lovers. While it evolves beautifully, I favor the dry down. The final phase of this fragrance is where the frankincense note is most prominent. This fragrance opens with sueded vanilla and pepper, although it doesn't come off peppery by any means; at least not to me. Soft, yet deep and lingering. This cat has good longevity and clings to me without a problem; and I should add I don't have the most hydrated skin. Babycat is not close enough to Caftan to be deemed a substitute, but it is in the family. While I have very little desire to wear this fragrance right now, I see myself reaching for this often the moment September is upon us.

Okay this perfume has me in a chokehold. This is a perfume that shines as it wears on your skin. Seriously, the dry down is absolutely gorgeous. I am a big fan a dark resinous scents. The opening is a powerhouse of resin and smoke. So you have to like that style of churchy incense and smokey vibes. But as this drys down on the skin the vanilla and suede are absolutely essential to making the resin feel cozy and soft. It’s a dream, and for those who love it know it’s a lifer. If I had to only pick 5 perfumes this would 100% be one of them. I just wish YSL would make this more available.

I'm a big fan of Rosendo Mateu 5, which Babycat is always compared to. Vanilla is my favorite note, I like the animal print this was inspired by and I obviously adore baby cats (who doesn't?). So I was already sure that I wouldn't hate this before I even tried it, and it really is quite a lovely fragrance. It has the same blend of sweetness, muskiness and sharp saffron that RM 5 has, so this is not a simple vanilla scent. I wouldn't say the two are twins though. Babycat starts out quite spa-like and even herbal. I have no idea where this is coming from, nothing in the notes list indicates a herbal scent, but I got it every time I sampled this. This is something I don't get in RM 5 and can honestly do without. The next difference I notice is that the vanilla in here is warmer and more buttery, which I love. It's mixed with a cool, almost soapy frankincense note. Together they feel soothing and cozy, but the saffron and pepper keep everything lively. This is a scent of contrasts that come together in harmony. There is something smokey about this, too, but if you want an even smokier version of this scent profile, you also need to try Queen of the Night by The Merchant of Venice. There is one thing that I love in 5 and don't get in Babycat (or Queen of the Night), and that's the heavy dose of floral creaminess. It just takes the scent to a whole new level. I would say that these are different enough to own both, but I know that I would always reach for 5 if I had to chose. So I don't need Babycat in my life. My bank account surely feels relieved.

I am surprised! Yep! I bought into the hype and ordered a sample. I don’t know what it was but my birthday passed and though I had got some very thoughtful presents from my Wife and daughter, I wanted to spoil myself with a fragrance purchase. I had a list of contenders. This was on the list; along with six others. That list now, just those six others.

The weather is changing; the sun is out longer; it is getting warmer and the flowers are blooming—Spring has finally arrived! This is the effect NuWa has on me, and it is absolutely beautiful. The opening sparkles, like many Rojas do, but this one feels a little different—it's more fragrant and actually smells like a vibrant and ultra-fresh rose garden with other flowers here and there. In the opening, you're blasted with a load of photo-realistic florals with a tinge of greenness and sweetness which last throughout the wearing experience. In the mid, the florals remain, but a nice spiciness emerges—giving NuWa a spicy/oriental edge. In the base, the vanilla and sandalwood shine and lend a rich creaminess while remaining a tad spicy; the florals and freshness move into the background; by this point, NuWa has become a full-on floriental. She is gorgeous throughout the entire wearing experience. Longevity is good and occasions lean more formal; NuWa can be worn casually, however, as she has a freshness to her because of the florals; you'll just smell elegant. Seasons, spring days and summer nights, or anytime you need a pick me up. Unisex leans, leans more feminine IMO. Performance is excellent and projection is decent. The only downside is the big price tag, but that's Roja I guess. The bottle also looks amazing on display. I don't hear this one talked about in Fragcom much, but I think that's a good thing—it's our little secret!

A 1982 song sung by the Russian pop icon Alla Pugacheva with her distinctive smoky voice, one of my favorite songs from childhood... Those from the former Eastern Bloc countries might remember it or one of its translated versions - a beautifully tragic story of a poor artist who sold all his possessions (a small house and his paintings) to buy flowers for the love of his life, an actress. One morning, when she looked out of her window and saw a sea of scarlet roses, she delighted the unfortunate admirer with a brief meeting and left the city forever. The bankrupt artist was left with the memory of a million scarlet roses... Back then, as now, only a part of the large fan base in Eastern Europe and Asia knew that the deeply moving song was a retelling of a true story. It is dedicated to Niko Pirosmani, a poor Georgian painter whose works gained recognition only after his death. During his lifetime, he became known for a single crazy act when he sold all his possessions and bought enough red roses for a touring French actress to cover the entire town square in front of her hotel room window, plunging himself into ruin. So, why do I associate Nüwa with some old song? It’s the rose interpreted in Nüwa... One among many... But one that you have searched for your whole life and now found. And a whole sea of it! The feeling of having arrived... That must be how overwhelming the sight of a million roses is. Here we have a rose of incredible beauty, so much so that I immediately compared it jealously to my favorite rose in Noir de Noir. There are clear differences, such as color association - I see the NdN rose as black-red, while this one in Nüwa is blood-red, or scarlet, if you will. And while I love the NdN rose for its dark, mystical framing, Nüwa relies on the natural beauty of this royal flower. In NdN, the overall composition of notes is a masterpiece. In Nüwa, the masterpiece is the rose itself. The other notes reach my nose only as extras, while the rose makes a clear statement - here I am, kneel down and admire me! From the very first minute, it is present with full force, initially accompanied by a subtle bitterness of grapefruit and a pinch of pepper in the top notes, which give the rose a fresh spiciness. Shortly thereafter, the rose takes on a soapy touch on my skin - I blame the orange blossom for that. Since I personally find the soapy aspect in perfumes less appealing, I see this phase of Nüwa as a tiny little downside that slightly hinders me from enjoying the full purity of the rose. Jasmine does not make an appearance throughout the entire fragrance journey. Slowly, the clove along with cumin comes through, and the soapy aspect disappears. The scent becomes a bit warmer. Cumin has never bothered me, probably because I have never found it to be grossly sweaty. And the scent becomes most beautiful for me in its infinitely long base phase, when the sweetness of vanilla and the creamy sandalwood mix in, and the rose gradually glides into a transparent powderiness. I won’t pretend to know how Peru balsam smells, so this note remains unrecognized by me. But I could have sworn that at least some patchouli leaves are swimming in this sea of roses, which I perceive as little drops along with all the other mentioned complementary notes. They are all not decisive for the scent, but they make it livelier and more interesting. If we set aside the price question (I had to gulp), and focus only on the scent aspect, the following emerges: the rose connoisseurs and lovers among us (I remain modest and count myself among the latter of the two :)) will enjoy drifting for a long time in a sea of millions of red roses. In my case, for about 10 hours, until I am washed ashore to the reality.

Nüwa is a Chinese goddess? And even the creator of mankind? OK - learned something new. What you also realize with this perfume is how a well-crafted scent can develop masterfully. After the first spray, I assumed that Nüwa would move relatively linearly like any other rose scent. Quite rich in rose, with all sorts of sweet embellishments around it, but nothing more. A few moments later, I had the strong impression that Nüwa was heading steeply towards Gold Man by Amouage. This means a slightly metallic-cool sharpness from bergamot with the soaked complexity of floral notes, especially the May rose (the dog rose in Gold Man), just without the frankincense. A little later, the rose blooms even more intensely again, and one might think that Nüwa, as initially thought, would find its conclusion with this theme. Nice, nice, but then one wonders why the perfume scores so many points in the ratings, especially when Roja Dove sets such high standards and critically questions his creations. The answer comes with great strides when you wait a little longer and give the drydown time for a glorious appearance. What then reveals itself is a lesson in development and twist, as Nüwa transforms into a fabulous orange blossom dream with balsamic-vanilla cushions of rest. It feels absolutely harmonious and heavenly. And all of this is absolutely pure, high-quality, and without any kind of disturbances or resistances. Yes - the stuff is expensive, but the wearer and their surroundings get a lot out of it. No - it won't end up on my wish list. And despite the seemingly lack of innovation in the respective facets, it shows at a very high level what can be achieved with a natural scent.
