Initial explosion of bitter citrus and slightly smoky cardamom (and what felt like a hint of cumin?) dissipated from my body in under ~20 minutes. A cozy, warm and well rounded composition of sandalwood, sweet cedar and several other notes I haven't heard before waited underneath. I spent the first ~3 hours in a gentle powdery cloud. I was worried it would give me a headache, but the woody sweetness was mellow and subdued, so I never felt unwell (unless you count "lazy" and "sleepy" as an affliction). Once I got out of the woods, a field of violets softly swaying on the wind awaited me. I have confirmed with my partner that somewhere at this point it stopped projecting and settled close to my skin. In another ~2 hours the violets also faded away and left just the soft fluffy base (which took another ~3 hours to dry out). It made me feel so safe and warm I just wanted to lay in bed the whole day instead of doing any work, lol. This should be great for a lazy weekend during colder parts of the year, as it envelops the wearer like a soft fur blanket; but when I want to take it out in warm weather I spray it on my clothes instead — they can't bring out the warmth underneath, but trap the upper notes pretty well, so I end up smelling like an adorable fresh cardamom pastry ٩(ˊᗜˋ*)و

Loewe 001 Man is a more interesting perfume than it may seem at first, multifaceted in its combination of what has dominated the commercial and niche perfumery. At first I had the impression that its dynamics would revolve around exotic woods, amber and with an aromatic bitter absinthe, something that briefly reminded me of Amouage Memoir Man. However, this is just one facet of 001 Man, which balances between citrus and clean touches, a note of earthy and slightly powdery iris (which some relate to Dior Homme), a dry woody scent of sandalwood and creamy vanilla and musk tones at the base. It is a complex perfume, one that deceives with a false sense of delicacy in an aroma that lasts nicely on the skin. It has notes sufficiently unisex to be shared, fitting with what the proposal says.

At first, it's cardamom. It's like ginger. It starts with a food scent. After a while, it becomes a bit vanillic. I think it's violet. It reminded me a bit of Flower by Kenzo. It's like a mild spicy woody scent. I'm glad there's no lavender in this. If this note didn't have ambrette and violet, it would be a pretty typical men's fragrance. I have ambrette seed essential oil, and this sweet vegetable musk and violet fill in the gaps of the masculine spicy woody "thorns" and make it mellow. And the only thing that has a clear cardamom effect is that it smells like spicy fried chicken, and it has a "food" feel. (But it's by no means gourmand) I've tried this a total of five times. That's because I've tried almost all of Givenchy's Gentleman series (both the derived flankers and the original), but I was completely disappointed. I just barely liked the original last note. Yes, designer fragrance notes. This has about half the designer fragrance notes. Someone wrote in a review that it's somewhere between niche and designer. If I had improved Loewe for me, I probably would have lost fans, so this is probably the right choice, but reading the reviews, I feel that Loewe tends to have stronger top notes overall. I also agree with the opinion that the musk is strong. I saw an opinion that the drydown is similar to Rochas Man, which I don't like, but because the cosmetic notes are toned down, I found it much easier to wear than Rochas Man. However, I preferred to put it on my clothes rather than on my skin. I think it's too loud when I put it on my skin. To reduce the volume, it's better to put it on your clothes rather than on your skin. As an aside, I put this on the front of my clothes and ate a hamburger (chili sauce fried chicken), which I rarely eat, but it didn't interfere with my meal. I guess that in Europe and America（And countries that love spices on a daily basis... in Asia? Maybe all countries other than Japan?), people probably eat these spices on a daily basis, so the spicy scent doesn't bother them. I guess the scent of spices stands out when it comes to Japanese food. I think it's a casual fragrance for people who feel the somewhat "formal" feel of Givenchy and Dior fragrances is too much. As the bottle says, it's colorless and transparent, and not a very flashy scent. (Except for cardamom) Recommended for cardamom fans. I think I'll use up the sample.

To get straight to the point: Loewe 001 Man is not a bad perfume. It is velvety, cozy, and warms like mulled wine in the late hours. It fits perfectly into the cold season. The fact that there is apparently no iris in it is surprising. Because: The scent is indeed powdery and a bit "papery," but this aspect is not as prominent as in other representatives of this fragrance direction. It starts off with a salted cardamom sweetness that is quite pronounced. L001M seems, at first glance, to want to take new paths, but at the end of the day, it only treads well-worn trails: Dior Homme (with its variants, although the EdT is probably the most suitable for comparison), Carthusia 1681 (Paper), or - to mention a newer representative - L'Homme by Prada (with a subtle freshness kick, but otherwise conventional) are glaring references. In any case, L001M is not thematically new. No contrast, no twist. This is almost a bit surprising: Sure, Loewe is not an experimental hidden gem, but they have released an extremely noteworthy incense variant with the blue 7 Loewe: Modern, slim, wiry, a bit overly apple-like and completely unassuming in any sacred proximity. And otherwise, the fragrances from this label, which seems to navigate the no man's land between "niche" and mainstream, are worth a test. Compared to 7 Loewe, Loewe 001 Man at best comes off like the nice son-in-law from next door ... The idea that a woody drift is to be initiated with cedar and cypress as well as sandalwood can hardly be taken seriously. L001M clearly remains in its slightly boring and somewhat sedating sweetness, especially at the beginning. Fortunately, this sweetness does not become too sticky as the scent develops, and the merely hinted woodiness is not scratchy (like in Bleu de Chanel, for example) - this makes L001M wearable and pleasing. The base of the fragrance reads complicated and suggests a touch of uncleanliness. Whether this is a self-fulfilling prophecy remains open ... The formal quality of L001M is impeccable. Projection and longevity do their solid job like the old diesel engine in U96. The bottle is very attractive and appears classically elegant. Conclusion: L001M is indeed a new wine, but in old hoses. It’s something you can drink once in a while.

When this came out, and after watching some yt impressions, i thought it would be something "big". Since 2015, with Sauvage, we didnt had anything that popular in the mainstream audience and this is the first new YSL masculine line since 2017's Y EDT. When i smelled it, i immediately liked it and understood the controversial opinions. It has all the ingredients for The success. 1⁰ it was, right away, very controversial on out community and yet, very popular in the mainstream world 2⁰ the smell is very appealing and "familiar" 3⁰ its very loud and longlasting Sauvage was all of these. I remember seeing a lot of hate for Sauvage and now, it's a classic and a best seller. The same is happening with MYSLF. Its in every online shop's top 10 or 20 best selling fragrances for men. And its going popular for a reason. Its unique in a way, but yet familiar, and will give compliments. Opens up with bergamot, Orange Blossom and Ambroxan. The Bergamot-Ambroxan is reminiscent of other masculine scents (hello again, Sauvage) but it smells somewhat new. The Orange Blossom turns this one into a completely different scent. Usually, an orange blossom scent is super fresh and short living. More of a cologne type of style. Fleur Du Mâle was a different take on the ingredient but it was more focused on a barbershop scent with a big dose of camomile too. Here, you get a strong sweet, floral, woody scent. It has some similarities with YSL Libre but more Woody. Patchouli is there and it helps beeing masculine. It can give noseblind like Sauvage does, specially if you overspray it, since it's very strong and it has that "synthetic" quality that many people dislike. When people say they cant smell it, it's nose blind. It happens with me sometimes The scent is controversial because it's an ambroxan bomb and ambroxan works different on every nose. Some hate the smell, some get noseblind and say it does not perform, and others enjoy it, like myself (in small doses). I find it somewhat unique and i think it will define a new genre of florals for men. Like Sauvage, 1Million, Invictus or Le Mâle clones, i think we will see many MYSLF clones for the next years to come. Saying that, i dont think this is the best new thing or masterpiece, but its disruptive in a way, and i like that. It has personality, liking it or not. 3/5

YSL's MYSLF didn't find its way onto my "To Test" list, as I didn't find the notes breakdown interesting or eye-catchy in anyway. Nevertheless, I got my hands onto a sample. And for the most part, I was right. It opens pretty synthetic, thing I did not expect. But after a minute or two, that initial synthetic blast turns into a simple, citrusy bergamot. It is aided by the orange blossom which gives Myslf a floral edge. If anything, it smells very similar to clean laundry or a high quality soap. And it keeps that pleasing, clean profile across the whole wearing. As it settles down, the ambrofix and woody notes come into play too, just to give a bit more depth. I don't get much patchouli; maybe just a hint of its muskiness in the back. But these do not overpower the clean laundry-like scent. All-in-all, it's nothing to be impressed by. It's your average smell-good, designer scent which adds nothing new to the catalog. Sure, it's a pleasant scent, but if uniqueness is what you're after, then there's none to be offered here. In terms of longevity, Myslf really impressed me. I didn't expect anything more than 6 or so hours. And yet here I am, over 10 hours since I sprayed it on me and I can still just ever so slightly catch a glimpse of it. That doesn't translate to good projection too, however. Although for the first hour or two, I had a solid two feet of projection, it then abruptly closed in to my skin; still noticeable, but definitely not beast mode. Still, I'm more than pleased with the longevity, and I'd say that you don't need any more than 5-7 sprays of MYSLF. For occasions, jeez, I mean you can literally wear this anywhere. School, work, going out, events... It's a great leisure, everyday, signature fragrance that won't offend anyone. Sure, maybe it's not the best choice for partying or dressed up events, where you want to stick out and smell different. But if you just want to smell clean, out-of-the-shower-like, then you might have a winner here. But I still can't ignore the fact that it is nothing special. It's not a scent profile that's worth phoning home about, nor one that will have you stick out from the crowd. It's basic, boring, and a little flat, but nonetheless pleasing. It's somewhat linear too, and the quality is not elite-level. It's not a beast-mode projector, but it's got some good longevity (at least on my skin). Although I think it is a bit overpriced (though in the end, you're paying for the brand), if you only want to smell good, clean and simple, Myslf does a good job at that. It's not trying to stand out or to enter uncharted territories; it's just trying to be as serviceable as possible to as many people as possible. Overall Rating: 6.2/10

For me, the value of art has a lot to do with the reason it was created. Why does a perfumer create a fragrance (other than, of course, being commissioned/paid to do so)? As an artist myself, I think that art is mainly communication - the transfer of a feeling, memory, emotion from one human being to another. If you give a perfumer full freedom, they would create something special to themselves; a feeling they have had or an association they have made with a memory, and when you wear it, you get a glimpse of their emotional state. But when the creative direction is controlled by a bureaucracy, focus groups, and businesspeople, well, this is what you get. So why then was YSL MYSLF created? For the same reason that Apple releases a new iPhone every year, regardless of whether there are any new features. It wasn't because anyone had something to say, some emotion or feeling to communicate to an audience. It wasn't because they wanted to create anything new or exciting, or challenge the status quo. It was to fool people into thinking that somehow because of the new packaging or advertising, that this is something different than already exists on every department store shelf in the world. "Go buy our new fragrance simply because it is new." The most ironic thing is the name, which is actually quite reflective of modern attitudes toward individuality. As if this scent could ever make you embrace any sort of individuality; it places you firmly into a box of "soapy aromatic amber" like so many others before it. But isn't it appropriate? People today only know how to express their individuality by joining a enormous collective: whether it is by listening to a certain podcast which millions of others listen to, supporting a candidate millions of other support, or believing in a cause the vast majority of people around them also believe in. The marketing for MYSLF advertises it as sort of a "skin but better" scent, saying, "a fragrance that seamlessly fuses with your skin, revealing a distinct signature for each individual." But it fails in that spectacularly. It is squarely an ambroxan-fueled aromatic amber with some soapy neroli thrown in - a far cry from subtle musky "skin but better" scents. Why did we need this fragrance? What does it do that other fragrances, even in YSL's own line, don't do? Does it serve any purpose other than being the "new" thing on the shelf for department store salespeople to push?

Packaging: At the department store you’ll very quickly notice the similarity of Ysl “Myslf” and its bigger sister “Libre” by the same brand. The packaging is almost identical, but whereas Libre comes with golden writing, Myslf comes with the same black and white wrapping, but with black letters. Whether or not this similarity in wrapping is supposed to trigger associations to the Libre line or not are unknown, but at first glance “Myslf” could be (mis…?)- interpreted as a flanker to the Libre line. The bottle: The bottle reeks of quality to me. It’s minimalistic and classy at the same time. The Esthetics of the tall, sleek and black glass bottle is superb, and would fit in nicely in almost every bedroom or bathroom across the modern world. It’s just elegant and modern looking. As for the associations made by its appearance I tend to read it as both masculine and feminine at once. It kinda looks both like a black monolith as well as a black eyeliner at once. And as such it paints the picture of the scent within. The scent: This perfume opens up with a combination of a rather strong bergamot accord alongside the main actor, the orange blossom. Ten minutes into the experience the scent begins to changes to my nose, and the bergamot slowly start to faint into the background a bit while the orange blossom gets more dominant for every minute. Through the next 3-5 hours you’ll enjoy a very noticeable orange blossom note that comes of increasingly powdery and creamy as time goes by. Towards the end of the fragrance life you’ll experience the base notes with its obvious ambrofix and patchouli notes. At this point the perfume has turned into somewhat of a skin scent to me. The name of the fragrance and its ambitions: Myslf - aka Male-ysl-Female. As for the scent profile and Ysl’s ultimate goal to achieve a somewhat androgynous perfume for men, I’ll very much compliment their work and efforts. To me and my nose id stray clear of the term androgynous in my evaluation of the scent. There’s nothing tomboy-y over this perfume nor is there anything super masculine or girly girly. To me this is a refined piece of art that catches the shades of femininity that rests inside every man. I write “every man” as we all posses both masculine attributes as well as feminine ones. To me this fragrance pay tribute to men’s feminine sides in a great way. To me I find this fragrance feminine, but done so in an ambiguous way. Which is why it’s best describes as “a feminine cologne for men”. It’s soft and tender, but nothing inherently female nonetheless. Idk, it’s just soft, warm and inviting I suppose. I’ll say that this perfume helps widening the scope for male perfumery and it gives us men something that can reflect our complexity in a better way than before its launch. It fills some of the gap that has been missing for decades in male perfumes. I’d argue that it’s not something to fret about for those who prefer more classically masculine scents as they complement each other in a perfume wardrobe as I see it. In the same way as heavy ambers, leathers and spice goes for winter and citric scents shine in the summer this one adds to all of this by offering a great floral year round. Sillage: Ysl Myslf has a great sillage in my experience. It’s very noticeable as far as two-three meters away, and you will be complimented on this by a lot of women. They love it! Longevity: 6-8 hours, but heavy projection for approximately around 3-4 hours. Versatility: Pretty much every occation and season but funerals. A real crowd pleaser and non offending. Safe blind buy? Yes, but only if you appreciate a feminine touch in your perfume. To me it’s delicate and tender, but then again taste varies. Value for money: Good.

… so that means people are going to LOVE it in 9 months . All kidding aside, my wife thinks it smells great, and a lot of women I come in contact with say the same thing. They really like it. Personally, when I first sprayed it, I was worried that it was leaning too feminine. The orange blossom makes itself present , and you WILL feel the flowery vibe it gives. It also seems that it’s a light, low projection/low sillage scent, but as I walked around, I kept getting “phantom wafts” of it; it’s easy to go nose blind to it, but it isn’t as bad as you think. Also, when I went outside into higher temps, it got MUCH louder. My initial thoughts were a dislike, but I got more and more addicted to it as time passed. I couldn’t stop smelling my wrist. I went home without buying it, and woke up to still smell the SINGLE SPRAY on my wrist. I immediately went back and bought a bottle. Projection is difficult, as I said above I was nose blind, but sillage IS there, as is the longevity. Not for everyone, but it’s hated more than it deserves to be.

Great scent from opening thru the mid and the dry down EXCEPT. There is a funky smell in the dry down that’s in both Myslf Edp and MOR prominent in the Parfum. And I could not for the life of me figure out why women like this on men. To me it’s a barely noticeable but it’s there.

Delightful is first word that comes to mind when I think of MYSLF EDP. Bright and zesty bergamot with patchouli and ambrofix base. I love wearing this in hot weather and it seems extremely well suited for office and professional settings as it is for a nice outdoor brunch or picnic.

Wow! This fragrance is extraordinary I’ll keep this as brief as I can as I do not want to make out that I have some very heavy opinions about this fragrance. It just reminded me of something very common about these mass appealing fragrances.

Myslf perfume offers a moderate projection and sillage during its initial hour, accompanied by a longevity of around 5 hours. Upon the first spray, I found it to be reminiscent of both Armani Code Perfume and YSL's Libre EDP for women fragrances.

It’s a minimalist scent but done so well. The opening is uplifting, vibrant and just puts me in a “scent mood” immediately. Never imagined I would love orange blossom so much, and the bergamot opening with it just makes this sing. So fresh, and intoxicating. The long dry down with the patchouli is beautiful, and I’ve had compliments on it after 4-5 hours of wear.

This is how a man should smell. Undoubtedly a high-quality perfume with the most impressive performance!!! I wore the perfume at my friend's wedding and on the dance floor the bride herself complimented me on the perfume while dancing! The next morning I still woke up with this smell, I didn't want it to end. A scent of leather that combines with lemon and fig, jasmine and neroli. This is a winter perfume and not suitable for every situation and you really need yourself to perfume with the clothes. 9.5/10 easy.

if you are looking for chypre, land here. this is exceptional. you can find leather sides, smoky sides, driftwood and something of flowers. citrus opening, of considerable duration. You will notice a lot of changes in Fetish. amber base, smoky of vetiver, and spicy of pepper with the freshness of cardamom. the quality is excellent as is its durability and projection Beautiful

Fetish pour Homme (Parfum) opens with a dash of brief bergamot and lime slightly tart citrus before quickly transitioning to its heart. As the composition enters its early heart an emerging cardamom spiced slightly smoky, woody incense-like accord takes command with hints of ginger joining the remaining lime citrus in support. As the composition slowly moves further into its heart, the woody incense gradually recedes as vetiver spiked leather slowly takes over as star. During the late dry-down the vetiver spiked leather remains, now joined by slightly powdery vanilla and oakmoss in the base through the finish. Projection is excellent and longevity outstanding at over 15 hours on skin. Fetish pour Homme (Parfum) is frequently compared by many to Puredistance M. The vetiver and leather found in the late heart section certainly does have some major similarities to M, coupled with the two additionally sharing a similar spicy structure. That said, those calling Fetish pour Homme (Parfum) pretty much the same composition as M do both a disservice. The key difference (though far from the only one) is Fetish pour Homme (Parfum) features a very strong woody radiant incense-like accord that really is the focal part of the composition for a good portion of its development. So strong was the woody incense in the heart that I really would classify Fetish pour Homme (Parfum) more as a woody composition than the leather most focus on. While M is a more pure spiced vetiver leather play, Fetish pour Homme (Parfum) has a lot more going on as it transitions from citrus to woods to leather to slightly powdery vanilla with each transition seamless. As with the other Roja Dove compositions I have sampled so far, ingredient quality is superb. Also, just like the other Roja Dove compositions the selling price is anything *but* superb. That said, in the case of Fetish pour Homme (Parfum) the quality of the materials and the outstanding end result of the perfumer's skilled execution makes me want to forget about the relatively high cost per bottle and just "bite the bullet" and acquire some of this stuff because it gets pretty addictive, fast. The bottom line is the $480 per 50ml bottle Fetish pour Homme (Parfum) is much more than a duplicate of the great Puredistance M, both proving near equally worthy of owning, earning it an "outstanding" 4 to 4.5 stars out of 5 and a strong buy recommendation if one can afford its admittedly lofty price.

"For Men not for Boys" is taken from a quote from Roja himself A spicy leather perfume with crazy Sillage! This perfume opens with lemon, bergamot and fig which balances the perfume very well After a while the leather becomes more dominant with a combination of cardamom This perfume is great for evening outings and not for closed places For me 9.0 /10

Fetish, succumb to desire. Yes, the desire to be enveloped in a sensual and provocative scented aura. Leather, castoreum and much, much more. The opening, Roja-style, is always a treat for the nose with citrus that I have never perceived as realistic and of such quality. After the fizz at the start, the leathery notes that are the stars in this fragrance begin to emerge. Around them revolve spices (cardamom and black pepper first and foremost), earthy, dry notes of vetiver and patchouli, and a delicious oakmoss. A dynamic, characterful fragrance that in the drydown, however, softens quite a bit, cuddling you almost 12 hours after the first spray.
I’ve recently tried the cologne version of elysium and was disappointed. I smelt some nice fruity cola style scent but found it to be very weak, or I was just unable to smell it.

Leather, leather, sweat, leather! This scent surrounds you with a cloud of leather, sweat and animalic spirit! Its enourmous impact on your dates, friends or job is unpredictable! This fragrance is just different. It‘s sillage grabs everyones attention and secures you a save place in everyone mind! It‘s one oft Rojas strongest scent!

The second word after `Diaghilev` that pops into my mind thinking of Roja Dove is definitely, Fetish. I consider it one of is best creation out there, a fierce perspective on leather, just pure Testosterone in a bottle. It starts with a fresh lime/bergamot and turns few seconds later into a very powerful, slightly bitter, musky animalic leather.

Once again I am under the spell of Roja Doves' gorgeous perfume collection. I am captivated, bewitched, enslaved by the glorious splendour each of his fragrances exude. Until now I had the chance to try the following Roja Parfums: Amber Aoud, Aoud, Scandal pour Homme and now Fetish pour Homme.

Fetish Pour Homme from the British Perfumery House Haute Luxury Roja London is a Cyprus Leather Citrus Animalic Spicy Amber Smoky Fragrance for Men; it was launched in 2012 and the perfumer who signs this fragrance is Roja Dove. Unfortunately, this masterpiece has been discontinued. Best roja I've ever put my nose on. My favorite in the house!

"Anónimo" is a formal and elegant fragrance, a leathery, earthy incense with a wonderful sweet spot. The start is a fresh incense, balsamic and slightly fruity, which then, quickly, smokes and begins to emerge in the background, a leather with a sweet resinous dot, and a dry, earthy vetiver, with a woody, precious air. There is no more evolution, or lack that does, being at all times a very distinguished, gentle and masculine incense, which I liked very much. The duration of the perfume is good, in my skin was about 7 hours or so, with a moderate projection, which is not bad, if it had been greater, I think it would subtract that touch of distinction that has, performance at your point, no more no less. Perfume of cool or temperate climates and to dress it, indifferently, both day and night, but not in any way, it is a scent that implicitly carries elegance and begs for a chord dress, dress shirt is your essential complement. Highly recommended for all those users who love this note, and recommended, at least your test, for all those who seek a different and elegant perfume.

The best way to quickly describe it would be a "fresh incense". At the same time it's clean, green, and leathery. Great stuff from Quentin Bisch. Anonimo is a very contemporary and at the same time different scent, as it is miles from the sugary sweet designer releases trending these years. In a blind test, I would most likely guess this to be a new offering from CdG. It's dry but aromatic, and the main notes are vetiver, incense, pink pepper, leather (that actually comes across as suede to me), benzoin and labdanum on a backbone of subtle clove. Very well balanced and dries down to something that is somehow slightly "floral". Even if incense is probably not so easily digested by newbies, I could imagine this one as being acceptable by the less experienced perfume user, as the incense is somehow muted and blends very well with the other notes. The overall feel is laid back but without getting overly casual. It doesn't evolve too much after the first half hour, but stays rather linear. An excellent perfume very well suited for slightly colder seasons like autumn. Great bottle as well!

Not at all what I expected from this composition. Don't get me wrong, if I concentrate on untangling them – I can smell each of the notes. The faint sweetness of frankincense, the prickly pepper, the earthy vetiver and smoky leather... I just half-expected and half-feared that they would all mix together and make me smell like a sexy little church. And yet I sprayed it and found myself in the midst of a coniferous forest, breathing in its cold autumnal air. Fresh, invigorating, with a hint of smoke and bitter pine tar. Lasted an eternity and then some. I still caught faint whiffs of it on my skin 24 hours and a shower later. Other people were able to smell it an outstretched hand away from me for the first few hours, but it settled closer to the skin as time went on. I tested it on my partner as well and achieved a slightly warmer and sweeter, but otherwise identical result. A very clean, minimalistic and versatile scent. So simple, and yet by the end of the day I became absolutely enthralled by it. 10/10 blind buy, worth every penny.

Anonimo opens up with a blast of alcohol and synthetic woody molecules à la Quorum Silver. The alcohol fades pretty quickly, but the synthetic woodies remain throughout the life of the fragrance. Not a strike against it by any means, but just pointing it out. The minor unpleasantness of the immediate opening aside, this is a very nice incense fragrance. It immediately called to mind two fragrances which other reviewers have already mentioned: Amouage Jubilation XXV and Fille en Aiguilles. Anonimo smells rather berry laden, despite containing no berries. The pink pepper is very, very tart and fruity in this fragrance, and it remains throughout the drydown. It strikes me as a less opulent, more wearable Jubilation, or Fille en Aiguilles bereft of pine and fir. Many reviewers have remarked that this is dark, rugged, and mature. On the contrary, I find it to be fresh, somewhat pretty, and definitely not only suitable for mature wearers. The freshness also makes this a fragrance I could see being worn year round, except for the hottest days of the summer. There is some darkness here, to be sure: the base chords of labdanum, synthetic woods, dusty leather, vetiver, and benzoin rough it up a little bit. Overall, though, this is not the super smoky, dark, powerhouse masculine fragrance I was expecting. I think the comparison to Bottega Veneta Pour Homme/Pour Homme Extreme is apt. Although they don't really smell alike, they share a similar vibe and aesthetic. Clean, somewhat fresh, masculine, but not brash or rude. I find them both to be very pleasant fragrances that most everyone will enjoy. Despite the fact that incense is not exactly the most mass appealing note, I can't see most people outright disliking this, unless they have a particular distaste for incense. Performance on my skin so far is not great. I think my bottle needs to go through some maceration. I haven't checked the batch code, and have no idea about reformulations, but this wears pretty light on me. Around 5 hours of longevity, an hour of projection, low sillage. I have to bury my face in my arm to smell anything other than that Quorum Silver woody molecule after a while. But it could very well change with time; I'll update my review in a few months after it's had time to sit. I'd also like to point out that the bottle is simply ridiculous. A tragicomedy of a container. The spraying mechanism sticks upon every spray. In theory, you just have to push it down again to get it to release. In practice, pushing it down again causes it to lock up even more and release feeble little puffs, like an octogenarian leaking urine in the Arby's men's room. But hey, what matters is the juice inside, right? My review seems pretty negative. Maybe I'm just in a cynical mood today. Overall, I do like Anonimo quite a bit, and will be wearing it often. It's a nice, easy to wear incense; in that category, I'd compare it favorably to something like Zadig & Voltaire's This is Him! Check it out, if you can find it. 7.5/10 EDIT: After letting it macerate for about a month, the performance has increased exponentially.

This has been one of my favorites for years. I love the incense notes, they last for a good while and remain in the background throughout each use. Then comes the subtle leather, which is also great. I have been praised many times. Performancewise I'm able to smell this on my skin after many hours. Unfortunately they told me today that it is going to be discontinued. It's a shame when they do this.

This lion doesn't roar, it... swims? I detect a slightly maritime, bathhouse-like freshness in the opening, possibly even a hint of vetiver-salt. This quickly settles down, making way for the protagonist of the initial part - the pink pepper. It shows aroma, a certain sharpness, and a hint of smoky capability all at once.

Since my dear friend is a Leo and has a penchant for good scents, I am looking for a fragrance from the company Loewe to be somewhat original. So far, nothing from the line has convinced me - 7 natural even turned out to be the much-quoted "evil 7" for me. Fragrances that I give as gifts must also appeal to me - and primarily suit the character of the recipient.

When I recently took a closer look at my "Anónimo" sample, I noticed a DNA that was quite familiar to me. Bright, fluffy, synthetic, and almost lightly ethereal ... similar to Ganymede Eau de Parfum and "Bois Impérial | Essential Parfums". Both are known to have been created by Quentin Bisch ... and who appears here as one of the three perfumers?

Waxy, but sharp. Spicy, yet pure. Dry as ash, can’t resin be? Gray, stoic, cold. Wise, but not old. Skin as space carries gray, in sandalwood glue construction. Aleppo soap clean, could it be laurel oil? Movement in stillness. Silence as language. Meditative, contemplative. Temple of craftsmanship. Ritual passage to the manufactory.

From what I've heard and observed, L'Homme has many female fans. I'm a definite fan, L'Homme makes a lovely, refreshingly spicy scent, with all the allure and appeal that makes it decidingly popular. Woodsy, spicy and crisp sums up the whole composition in three simple words. This fragrance seems to suit any man of any age, regardless of the occasion or personality. Versatile enough to be worn casually, classically or to a strict suit and tie event. The delicious spiciness was what immediately intrigued me when I first smelt L'Homme. I was not surprised when the sales assistant piped in with such praise with how popular this fragrance is as a present for lovers, family and friends. I can distinguish an odd, tasty orange note, that seems to be neither the lemon nor the bergamot. Personally, this is what I feel makes this fragrance so amazing. I could smell this fragrance forever, just cuddle up to its wearer and relish in its woodsiness and deliciousness. Some mention an aquatic type quality, and I slightly agree, even though it's not so noticeable that it drives the scent. I'm not so certain as to what makes this fragrance so sexy, but there is no contention as to its obvious sexual appeal. The sillage and lasting power is excellent, lasting for what seems like forever and a day. There is absolutely nothing else to say. I highly recommend.

Scentrack The Killers – When You Were Young L’Homme is an easy, likeable fragrance. It is clean, positive, light and inoffensive. L’Homme is a compliment getter from the opposite sex. It opens with bright citruses, peppery ginger and to my nose unidentified spices. To me L’Homme has some chamomile tea soft vibe. On my skin cedar becomes very soon the main player. Very pale vetiver note lays beneath a clean cedar and musk. Tonka bean gives just a touch of sweetness, but I have to admit I couldn’t recognize it without a help of Fragrantica’s note breakdown. The whole composition is extremely well balanced and tweaked. A lot of work is spent to make so approachable. Some may say is too simple and boring, but I consider L’Homme as a great example of a mainstream blockbuster and financial success. Rating: 6/10 More on Scentimentalwords

I can't stand this stuff. It is so generic, artificial and strong that I immediately want to get it off my skin. I get a faux citrus mixed with tonka beans and artificial ginger as a supporting note. It all comes together poorly and unwearable for me, at least. Ropion is extraordinarily talented, but this scent is not worthy of his name. I know L'Homme has a great reputation with the ladies, but I don't know what they see in it. Disgusting! On the positive side (I suppose), it has relatively good projection and unlike many other reviewers, longevity is at least average on my skin. Believe me when I say I wish that were not the case. Two tremendous thumbs down on this one. 1.5 stars out of 5.

I can’t say I hate this, but this is surely the duller and blander YSL fragrance for men I’ve ever tried, together with the other couple of flankers they made out of this. It isn’t bad, the quality seems to me mildly good, and if you’re looking for a safe unpretentious gift for a non-fan of fragrances to wear all day long, all year round, this would be a nice choice with a decent price for the value. It’s a fresh, unobtrusive ginger-citrus-woody fragrance playing some aromatic fougère chords but with a decided “younger” vibe, focusing on sweet woods and spices (Envy for Men), and fresh-aromatic notes, with a conventional note of soft violet. Mellow and polished, sweet and boringly fresh, kind of “young” and if I got the term correctly, kind of “bro” too – the smoky-fruity sweetness, the extreme linearity, the overall dullness (but maybe bros need bombs? This isn’t, just in case). Miles away from what once was a mature and classy brand delivering delightful fragrances like M7 or Rive Gauche, they seem now more aimed at 20-something in need of boosting their sex agendas. Not bad as I said, but nothing really special. 6/10

L'homme is a great option for office and summer days. Actually it goes well on every occasion. I like its ginger note combined with the sweetness of tonka bean in the base. Do not expect something extraordinary, but just a good scent for every day. Sillage, projection and lasting power are below average. Updated January 2014

Have you ever tried to find perfection in a fragrance ? Maybe you have, or maybe you haven't. I certainly have tried this and it's not that easy, trust me. But this is one of the few fragrances that in my eyes represents what I call perfection. Freshly smooth, a bit spicy, a bit green, a bit citrusy, a bit floral, a bit woody and so easy to love.

An old-school contemporary, we might say. Aristocratic aroma whose bottle is very reminiscent of what it craves: disengagement. The cylindrical and hexagonal (on the lid) demonstrate that L'Homme is a perfume of contrasts: the freshness of the sweetened bergamot and strengthened by cedar. Vetiver is light, without the grass-pulled scent of so many other brands.

I think this is a great fragrance. It's incredibly versatile (in warmer weather). It's fresh, but alluring. Like sweet, wet driftwood. This could work for both a date night in a dimly lit restaurant, or a day at the beach, or at the office and everything in between. Although there may be better options for either dedicated scenario, it's hard to go wrong with this one.

YSL's L'Homme begins as the classy, gentlemanly scent, but after announcing its presence, it quits the scene. Its projection on me is usually short, but when it does last, it's barely there. It's like someone showed up with a bang, sat down, and melted into the furniture. It begins with a vibrant pear smell, and then hits an aromatic sandalwood sort of smell.
it have a very fresh and nice opening note of ginger and lemon and suitable for spring season but unfortunately sillage is very soft and longevity is very weak ....

As I’m trying to explore more on Roja Dove creations after I fell in love with the Engima (Creation E) Parfum Cologne version and bought a full bottle of it, I struggled which pour homme I should get. Yes, I prefer the pour homme over the pour femme version because I love unisex or men’s fragrances. I struggled between Engima Pour Homme, Fetish Pour Homme or Reckless Pour Homme. Finally I decided on the Reckless after reading about its notes composition. Since I already own Engima Parfum Cologne so I shouldn’t get one that has a similar scent (at least not as my first Parfum concentration of Roja and try something new first), and lots of reviews said Fetish is way too masculine so I went with Reckless. It is my first chypre fragrance that I own since I thought chypre usually smell more classic and mature while I love scents that are more modern. Lucky this doesn’t disappoint me. The opening does smell very chypre and classic but the dry down is phenomenal. It is still chypre but very cozy. The floral mid notes in this is not prominent at all. Instead, the base notes peak thru and take the main role after since the 1-2 hours dry down of the top notes. The base notes definite overpowering the mid notes especially the cinnamon, black pepper and cardamom, which I love it even better. That makes it more modern and cozy. The only downside of this is the performance. It lasts very long about 10+ hours but doesn’t project very well, about 1-2 feet and stay closer to skin quickly in about 2-3 hours. I know Parfum concentration usually don’t have strong projection and I expected it but still a little lower than my expectations since I found the Engima Parfum Cologne has better performance (both longevity and projection). But I do find that the Reckless Pour Homme has divine quality (even better than the Parfum Cologne) while I thought the Engima Parfum Cologne already has top notch quality. Still became one of my favorites because it is the only chypre and so different in my collection. Definitely 9.5/10

Reckless is somewhat a real treat for the confident suit wearing But daring man, it has great performance on me and even though they remind of one another, Reckless is better than X by Clive C. Reckless has the cinnamon Toned Down a bit which suits me just fine. Amazing stuff

Reckless - daring. Well, daring is certainly the price of the Roja fragrance. Several hundred euros for 50ml. However, I do not find Reckless olfactorily daring. Rather, Reckless is a scent whose nuances excite the tones in between. Despite this somewhat inadequate name, Reckless is undoubtedly a typical Roja: quality and sophistication are unmistakable. Whoever the perfumer may be (Roja Dove is a marketing guy), he masters his craft. Rojas Reckless conveys warmth, self-confidence, elegance. As a rather classic and genuine Chypre fragrance, Reckless is timeless. Reckless emphasizes the seniority of the wearer without making him appear undynamic. Reckless exudes, like a well-tailored suit, a masculinely strong aura, aromatic, yet not harsh or edgy. Rather, it is sensually subtle. If Reckless pour Homme were a man, women would undoubtedly be at his feet (damn, why isn’t Roja Dove my father and why am I not named Reckless). Reckless opens fresh and zesty. The top note is dominated by citrus notes, lavender, and a strong bay leaf note. As a fairly classic Chypre fragrance, rose and jasmine form the main elements of the floral-warm, spicy-green heart note. Moving towards the base, also typically Chypre, woody-warm notes define the harmonious scent profile. Vetiver, oakmoss, cardamom. Combined with slightly powdery undertones and a hint of pepper. Reckless is a Chypre for men. And thoroughly so. Not herbal, not sweet. In a beautiful way, it goes against the zeitgeist, relying olfactorily on timeless values. Sensually masculine, even with a hint of eroticism. Reckless is enveloping, yet in a pleasantly unobtrusive way. For those who find Fetish pour Homme by Roja too lustful and obvious, Reckless is recommended.

There are fragrances that you spray on, or that are sprayed on you. And after two hours, you forget about them. And then there are those that you constantly sniff - because you want/need to sniff them. This happened recently in the perfumery I trust. My consultant gave me a little spritz on my right hand. Already on the way to the airport, I caught myself constantly bringing my hand to my nose or vice versa. Even on the plane, there was a persistent urge to inhale the scent. It was already clear: I had to get this thing, and ASAP! So, at the next opportunity, I made an impulse purchase. Whether the price point is justified, we can leave that aside. For what’s in the bottle, probably not. But scent and exclusivity do come at a price. And the likelihood that the colleague at the desk next to you is wearing the same fragrance is extremely low. The scent itself is hard for me to describe because it simply doesn’t fit into any category. It has edges and corners and is difficult to classify. Somewhere between alpha male, provocation, leather, wood, and animalistic. Striking. Dominant. And yet finely crafted. Who does this scent suit? Not for softeners, but, as mentioned above, the wearer should also have edges and corners. Types, with clear opinions. And self-confidence. Because it can happen that the gazes of others, especially in crowds, linger on you. Questioning looks. What smells so special here? Is it that guy? What kind of scent is that? A very special one indeed. When do you wear it? In the office, hmmm, it needs to be used thoughtfully, as it makes quite a statement. Certainly never in job interviews, as it is too dominant and provocative. Dinner: absolutely. Club: even better. Leisure: why not; perfect for a city stroll with an espresso. Overall: A hammer scent that will be too much and too expensive for many. Something very special that Roja has created. Full marks for the scent! Addendum Most of us will know those situations where everything that was once new loses its charm over time. New car. New clothes. New relationship. New furniture. New tech gadget. New perfume. With Reckless, the exact opposite is happening for me. Adorning my bathroom for half a year, I enjoy it even more than at the beginning. Not only the bottle, which is known to look simply stunning. But also the scent, which still completely convinces me. If I could, I would raise the score from 10 to 12. For a signature scent, it’s too exclusive, too expensive, and also too valuable. But for a convincing appearance, it’s priceless.

Always, always one is perfectly dressed, with a scent from Roja Parfums pour Homme. This one is the "weakest" in the men's department; I have now tested 5 out of 8 Rojas. Overall, they are all so elegantly composed that one could never even think that the fragrance one just sprayed on would not suit them well, or that one would not be excellently dressed in terms of scent. Rojas men's fragrances all radiate warmth, self-confidence, and understatement, never arrogance or alpha-male attitudes, and that is a fine line with such intense compositions. Here, it is truly the most restrained, the finest. This scent fits extraordinarily well with Arthur "Boy" Capel, one of Coco Chanel's lovers. Boy was always excellently dressed, a polo player, a gentleman. This connection of muse and genius manifested itself in creative creativity: His style significantly inspired her in her early years to the famous Chanel look. The opening of Reckless pour Homme is very intensely lemony and spicy; one would also think of bay leaves, even without knowing the fragrance pyramid. Aromatic-green could be a fitting description. The heart note, which is supposed to include jasmine and rose, reveals itself maximally as a delicate rose, fortunately not overly floral, with jasmine holding back completely. Instead, the actual players quickly dominate: oakmoss, spices, woods, especially sandalwood and vetiver - vetiver is skillfully embedded here, without appearing bitter or harsh, rather warm, herbaceous-aromatic, herbal-soapy. All notes that harmonize beautifully together, reminiscent of top-quality soaps with sandalwood, lavender, shaving soap as well, and noble aftershaves without a cumbersome touch. Especially the base note is typically determined-masculine, without appearing exaggerated. For hours, this green-herbaceous, powdery-soft yet also tobacco-like note lingers with a restrained sweetness and the aroma of spices. This fragrance completely lacks the "archaic-sexual" aspect, but that doesn't always have to be the case, as it is attractive in its own right. A very typical representative of gentlemen's fragrances, not a showstopper. The longevity is typically above average for Roja, and with 2-3 sprays, one wonderfully gets through the day, although the sillage here is not the strongest compared to other scents from the line. Overall, this fragrance is elegant, classic, and the word "classic" has several meanings: Its original meaning is 'first-rate', perfect. This scent is also timelessly valid, always appropriate, never too much or too little. So if one is looking for a not-so-daring perfume, as the name might suggest, and is willing to invest more, they will be well placed here. This could be the one for everything.

...or even bold is Reckless for me... if we stick to the literal translation. I’ve slowly gone through almost all the men’s Rojas, and somehow none of them really stick... none remain stubbornly in memory. They are all very finely and valuably made... exuding something noble and a nice depth.

I have been asked multiple times to comment on the Roja fragrances, repeatedly questioned why I hesitate to test them. I don't really have an answer to that. A significant factor is certainly the price, which I find too high and am not truly willing to pay for a fragrance, no matter how amazing it is. But I've said that about many € pain thresholds in my perfume life.

With "Reckless pour Homme (Parfum) | Roja Parfums," I dared to approach a fougere scent again after a long time. Not just any fougere, but one from Roja, whose namesake brand stands for classic fragrances like no other.

Reckless is neither a freshie, nor a fougere, not a barbershop scent - and somehow it is all of that in one! It starts off very spicy-green, fresh, and woody, exuding an old-school note that is hard to find elsewhere. Reckless stands out; it is not a quiet fragrance, actually uncharacteristic for Roja!

It is a sunny, not too warm spring day. The classic wet shave is perfect, a few generous sprays of Reckless before I put on my tweed suit and drive my Aston Martin from my country estate into the city… Well, I don’t even own a damn tweed suit, let alone an Aston or a country estate. But that’s exactly the association Reckless evokes in me. One of a stylish gentleman.

Paula's Ibiza is not your tropical, vacation getaway beach scent. It's more of the funkier, oceanic part of the beach, where you'd find dead jellyfish, algae, sea foam... I'm amazed that driftwood is captured so well, too. For an eau de toilette, this has some muscle. I easily smell it the next day on skin, confirmed by a friend who tested my sample (kindly given to me by Ihwayne). Great longevity and projection, I am definitely impressed for an EdT. The bottle looks fun, too; different from most, anyway. And although I do love beach scents, I'm on the fence about a full bottle (currently leaning towards yes) and will continue to test.

This fragrance is exactly what I was hoping it would be while reading and watching some of the reviews. I agree with a fellow reviewer Naipe that it's all about balance here and Núria Cruelles Borrull who composed Paula’s Ibiza got it so right. It's green, tropical (due to use of flowers such as frangipani and narcissus) and aquatic but not like a typical aquatic scent. Coconut note is more like coconut water and combined with bourbon vanilla create an aura of a luxurious body lotion. Flowers are kept in check by galbanum which I think is why this scent doesn’t smell like a sweet sun screen. Paula’s Ibiza is a perfect combination of green, flowery, woody and creamy notes. The impression I get is like being in a tropical place surrounded by sea water, filled with flowers and woods after the rain (great combo of driftwood and ambergris). Very laidback and classy and the same time. I have worn it in the heat and it worked perfectly. Its longevity for eau de toilette is almost unrivalled and projection at least moderate but never too much. I have to confess that I ignored Paula’s Ibiza at first because of… the bottle. Now that I have discovered the scent and worn it I have to say that the colours make sense. One of my top summer fragrances, easily.

I won’t lie to you and say that Ibiza is an easy sunscreen-type scent that is easily likable because it isn’t. It requires a mature nose to appreciate all of its nuances, and even after three months, I find myself wondering whether I like it or not. Regardless, this fragrance is nothing short of a masterpiece—a fragrance that finally doesn’t smell like the typical beachy and boring scents on the market. TOP NOTES It opens up with the juiciest mandarin orange, combined with hints of coconut and that unapologetic galbanum present from the start until the fragrance fades away from the skin. The effect is a rubbery smell that I can guarantee you either haven’t smelled yet or you rarely see in other releases. The issue for me is that galbanum comes off as bitter and smells like immortelle and old-school patchouli, which is also in the base here. HEART NOTES The heart adds marine and floral touches to the composition, getting more complex but never stronger than galbanum. Each time I wear Ibiza, I’m never reminded of a sunny beach but rather a stormy day and a cold rain about to fall on hot sand. Driftwood adds woodiness, and ambergris comes sooner than expected to provide a salty touch. BASE NOTES It will take some time to detect the base notes perfectly, which are vanilla, ambergris, and patchouli trifecta. With its earthy nuances, patchouli is also unapologetic like galbanum, while vanilla and ambergris balance the composition. Besides the fading of mandarin orange, coconut, and florals from the heart, the scent is more or less what you got from the first spray until it dries down. OVERALL I know that we are constantly complaining about how most of the scents these days are copies of a copy, and this is your chance to see what creativity is in this over-saturated genre. If we don’t start supporting brands willing to take creative risks, scents like these will become rarer by the year. Regardless of their price point, the “best” beach scents on the market cannot hold a candle to this masterpiece, which can be purchased for less than a hundred bucks. Read the full review at scentgrail.com

Challenging, it's not what it seems to me. Those bright colors do not represent it exactly, but be careful, this does not a negative interpretation, on the contrary, I love Paula's Ibiza. Far aquatic to my taste, green and wood notes predominate, and the big surprise is that its composition creates an accord that reminds me a lot of the fig leaf that feels great. I perceive it to be so green and woody that I think it feels better in autumn and spring than in summer, I am going to enjoy using it almost all year round. Its performance is more than satisfactory for the type of aroma, and it can be perceived at skin level after 8 hours. It's one of those love/hate fragrances, I'm on love team . The perceived quality is high, the creation is delicate, and its uniqueness is charming.

Light scent. A light persistence, but pleasant, even if I would have expected more. Strong tropical hints of coconut that accompany throughout the duration of the perfume. Mandarin can be heard in the distance. There are other green/floral notes that give a feeling of freshness. The scent closes with sweet notes of vanilla, slightly amber. Perfume, in my opinion, summery. To be used on any occasion, perhaps before lying on the deck chair on the beach .

This fragance is completely green, I don’t detect any sweetness (and maybe it could use just a tiny touch of it), but it’s not a bitter green either. It’s strange, yet beautiful. It has originality, it has good vibes, it has summer in its soul… That said, it could become overwhelming in very high temperatures

If this is how people see me, I'm satisfied with my image. It's so fresh and green, but unique. Smells like a day at the tropical seaside city, but without the stereotypical sweet fruits. Like walking around in the early morning, drinking a truly refreshing drink, surrounded with lush greenery that has been washed by a thunderstorm.

A different aquatic fragrance, everything revolves around water, coconut water, driftwood, amber gray, it is fresh but without being light, it has a lot of presence which makes it quite versatile in temperate and cold climates. It is unisex with a good performance.

This fragrance transports you to a beach in Spain. When I spray this, I get the coconut water, I get tye freshness from the frangipani and orange though it doesn't smell particularly fruity or floral. It's green, it's a bit sweet, it makes you feel like you're lounging by the beach with a fruity drink in your hand, your skin a bit salty.

Uncommented Fragrance No. 151 I first set foot on Ibiza in the early 70s as a child, and I am still grateful to my mother for being so inspired by the hippie lifestyle, which was barely noticeable in our everyday life apart from a few flared trousers and white blouses, that it had to be a vacation on the white island around '72. That was formative.

I was on the fence trying this one, mostly due to the hype surrounding it. Finally gave in and sampled it in a local store here in Copenhagen. It was not love at first sniff at all, we had to find our compromises and accept each others differences. After a few wearings I started to understand this wonderful scent better. It is not loud by any means, in fact it´s more of a silent statement. It leans slightly masculine and is a fragrance for the confident and more mature man, it represent everything I aspire and therefore it has become a somewhat signature scent for me. It makes me strive towards the man I wish to be, it reminds me that class and style is not being as loud as possible, it is completely it´s own and doesn´t compromise with that. Stunning fragrance.

YSL Tuxedo is the one fragrance that does everything for me. It is hard for me to classify this bright, uplifting and sensual scent. I can wear this to my workplace, to nights out with friends and just for heck of constantly sniffing myself constantly. It surely is a head turner; no fragrance in my collection garners so many compliments than YSL's Tuxedo. It is pleasant and stunning to the very core of the words. The rose is subtle and majestically executed in a spicy manner such that it often feels that the rose is only but a figment of imagination. One of the best smelling scents in my collection and that I am wearing the most this fall and winter. The fragrance exudes class and style. In short, Tuxedo is the fragrance that everyone needs but not what they deserve right now

The Viennese waltz is a rotating dance in which dancers continuously turn to the leader's right (natural) or to the left of the leader (reverse), interspersed with non-rotating change steps to switch from the direction of rotation. If I close my eyes and bring my nose closer to the point of the wrist covered with YSL Tuxedo, I can see the graceful violet and the resolute ambergris dancing Johann Strauss II's Blue Danube waltz. He dressed in a tuxedo as dark as patchouli, she in a fluttering vanilla-coloured chiffon dress. Although classified as a spicy chypre, I don't really recognize that kind of family. This is all about caramelized amber patchouli infused with light, juicy floral touches and soft spice. Also, the official description was misleading to me, as you will read later. This is what they say "L'eau de parfum Tuxedo contains the opaque texture of patchouli illuminated by the dark brightness of the spices." Indeed, when I smelled this perfume for the first time, something familiar came to my mind, but at that moment, I couldn't touch it; then, after wearing it, my memory took me back to a perfume I used in the past. This perfume is very reminiscent of Gucci II, especially the atmosphere of tea and violet leaves. Initially, I am greeted by an alcoholic and leathery accord, more or less similar to boozy craft cocktails and suede. I don't get any citrus flavour from bergamot; instead, a handful of sour coriander and berries pops up. While these are all perfectly blended, I pick up a burst of wet violet leaf in the opening. I feel the sweetness, the hint of smooth patchouli, and I also sense the coumarin to give it an extra dimension. The violet and patchouli hang in the middle and finish, and the heart almost feels like a gourmand, but the rose and lily of the valley seem to keep it on edge. The intermediate stage is captivating; I can't get my nose out of my hands. The finish is woody and sweet, with a significant warm and toasted caramelized vanilla flavour, but it is also sensual, dark, and smooth, a type of romantic scent. If vanilla is delicious, like a crème brûlée, ambroxan and pepper give it a powdery amber cocoa sensation. Unfortunately, I'm one of those who get little patchouli—just a breath, but nothing more. I mean, it's not the signature I get from Chanel Coco Mademoiselle or Zino Davidoff, for example. In Tuxedo, it is not one of the critical elements, but only a complementary, clean, lightened part. It smells like dusty wood, softened and made slightly delicate. Tuxedo is a slightly sweet, alcoholic, smoky fragrance with a creamy vanilla base. Very well blended. Just a beautiful perfume that smells like elements of a luxury cocktail party. The most dominant notes are leathery vanilla, salty and creamy ambergris, and green violet leaves. I even got a hint of smoke that sang out, a sort of fluid and shiny incense, bringing a slight sharpness to the warmth. YSL Tuxedo is just light and pleasant enough to be an everyday perfume and a memorable evening-outs for Fall and Winter months. The scent is so pleasing and not overwhelming. Longevity is not an issue, but projection might be better; I only get a couple of hours before it turns into a skin scent. This review is based upon a decant I own since February 2021. -Elysium

The tuxedo, a cloth considered exclusively masculine, was cleared and worn by a woman on the catwalk in the late 1960s and by Yves Saint Laurent himself. His choice triggered many negative comments, but later the women's tuxedo would conquer catwalks all over the world. A fragrance that in my opinion combines feminine notes with deep and masculine ones, creating something unisex, sensual and decisive at the same time. For me more suitable for cooler seasons.

YSL Tuxedo fragrance is just amazing! It's classy, sophisticated, and elegant. The quality is top notch, like a niche product. It has this cool and warm vibe that I love. Everyone always compliments me when I wear it, the patchouli, the spices, the vanilla oh man, it's so good! I absolutely love this scent, and it's definitely signature worthy for any classy man. A bit on the pricey side but what the hell? YOLO!

Damn … That's SO good! Complex and VERY impressive. Think POWDER, PACHOULI and VANILLA mainly, with a touch of wood and spice. The citrus and pepper are discernible. Later in the evening it was smoother and maybe a bit sweeter than earlier with the vanilla. 4+2 Versatility but could be wasted on certain occasions - meaning, it is special. It's THAT GOOD!

A classy, elegant fragrance that it warm but not overly sweet. The idea of associating fragrance with a comparable item of clothing is very useful and fitting. Certainly not everyone’s cup of tea, but it will get attention and most people upon smelling it with gravitate towards it I think. Rather expensive, but a unique creation.

Elegant, sophisticated and appealing fragrance with class. This perfume has two faces: Tuxedo is cooler due to the moist and cold patchouli, but at the same time it is warm due to the creamy and sweet vanilla and amber. An amazing combination. This is one of those fragrances that is completely unique. You can wear it all year everywhere, except hot summer days.

Opening is slightly harsh, but 30-45 minutes in, Tuxedo settles into a truly magnificent fragrance. smooth and woody, slightly spicy, with traces of florals to even everything out into a light vanilla-patchouli masterpiece. Sexy? I don’t know, but, it makes me feel more confident.

A wonderful diversion from the designer norm of winter fragrances. The contrasting pair of sweet vanilla and salty ambergris is really enjoyable, and the pairing of rose and patchouli is the cherry on top. It can be dressed down and worn daily as well as it can be dressed up for formal occasions. Not too sweet or youthful for business, not to tame or mature for leisure.

I don't headline this in a negative way at all. I love the way this smells. It's a scent for you alone as it does not project at all. Although if you have someone lying on your chest they would enjoy it. I understand why some people say they get nose blind. It is subtle and one minute you smell it the next you don't. It's not mind blowing but you can tell its smooth and well compiled. The big problem is, just like oud wood from TF it just doesn't last and yet again the price just does not rectify the performance. I can't afford to keep spraying this over and over again. I'm very sure other perfume houses could make the same thing but make it last. Out of all the RD creations Amber Aoud is still the only one that has great projection, sillage and longevity. It's such a shame ?

The Biblical history of King David was on this wise - before he was anointed king over israel the young man David stepped up to take on Goliath when nobody else would. And when David was brought to King Saul, before battle, King Saul fit him with his own suit of armor. Young David found that the armor was ill-fitting, and rejected it. David found that the armor wasn't fitting for him, but it's the complete opposite for me with Musk Aoud as far as wearing fragrance. Musk Aoud is so... "me" The slot for my second all-time favorite fragrance would be a difficult pick between Roja Parfums Musk Aoud, and Creed Windsor

I love aoud and add musk to it, wow, simply gorgeous combo. This is a bit skanky at first, but then the dry down is absolutely wonderful. I would wear this during winter or fall and on special occasions. Love it.

I already wrote a review on Amber Aoud and since I also own a bottle of this fragrance I want to report my experience. Unlike Amber Aoud, this time I own the crystal parfum version but also tested the normal one. First things first, to my nose the crystal version smells exactly the same as the normal parfum version. If someone tests both versions side by side and notices any differences, it's more likely due to different stages of maturation than due to the scent itself. Also the performance is the same but I'll get to this later. Musk Aoud was released in 2013 being the last part of a trio. Aoud came first in 2011, followed by Amber Aoud in 2012. Whereas you could consider Aoud the classical Rose-Oud-Saffron combination, Amber Aoud was sweeter and more mass-appealing because it softened rough edges occurring in the original Aoud. Musk Aoud took a very different approach by adding a natural musk note coming from Ambrette seeds rather than an animal. Due to the musk note as well as nutmeg, oud and jasmine the fragrance is definitely more animalic than the other two of the trio. Especially in the opening (first 5 mins), the fragrance might be too animalic for some noses. However, interestingly the fragrance is not stinky at all, especially after the first 5 mins are gone. I even find the original Aoud more stinky than Musk Aoud, although I wouldn’t call Aoud stinky as well. I guess it's the rose and leather note getting more prominent and contributing to keeping the fragrance in balance. To really appreciate the fragrance you have to get through the opening minutes and afterwards the smell is one of the most sexiest, intoxicating and just somewhat interesting one could imagine. All in all, the scent drys down to a base more similar to Amber Aoud. I slightly prefer Amber Aoud but only by centimeters or inches. It is no secret that Roja uses very fine materials and luxury packaging resulting in luxury prices (720€/100ml) and this one is no different. Considering performance, as I said, there's no difference between the crystal and the normal parfum. The scent lingers for around 3 hours, not shouting but also not close. Afterwards it gets closer to the skin and stays there until the 8 hour mark. Honestly, I expected and hoped for a little better performance from a fragrance of this category and price tag, but maybe it's just my skin or the fragrance has to maturate a little more.

Musk Aoud is one of my favorite Rojas from Aoud Collection and it has a very special place in my heart since it was my first scent from Roja Parfums. I bought it blindly and its enchantment has never faded. The color of this crystal cap is the most gorgeous of all! I think that this scent is totally underrated but I understand that it's not so easy to wear for many. I can’t get enough of this deep and complex scent. It's so sexy, sensual, erotic and mysterious. It's slightly animalic woody musky juice which is blended into perfection like all perfumes from Roja. You have to like oud and musk but it is not so challenging which you could think. The aroma of the scent is Roja's sophisticated and classy style without any roughness or pungent and brash nuances. Musk and Oud are not edgy here but noticeable ones and appropriately naughty but so pleasant in the same time. This will grow on you easily. Flowers play a supporting role in this fragrance rather than bringing a really floral aspect to it. After this settles down it turns so soft, a little bit powdery and a little bit sweet. It’s like the sexy smell of the skin! Vanilla, Nutmeg, Ambrette and Tonka they each bring their own "neutral" and natural sweetness to the fragrance, without being in any way comparable to sugary sweetness. The spiciness is really soft, and it doesn't remind of any food because the traditional oriental spices are missing. One note which can be challenging for me is leather but I never have that problem with Roja's style to do it. Everything in this is so polished. This is totally unisex since it doesn’t have so obvious “man” or “woman” characteristics. There is a little difference in the opening between dark and crystal juice but after 10 minutes those are totally same. The difference can be as well because of the age of the bottles. The longevity is eternal. I simply love this, I can't praise it enough and I need to add a big bottle of dark one as well. So sad that this is discontinued. Again one Roja's scent which doesn't have any similar competitor in the market. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

Musk Aoud is a warm musky scent. Very soft, gentle and rounded. Musk is the main player here. Warm, cozy, silky, almost powdery. Very soft with just a touch of animalic aspect. Nothing overpowering, not at all. The animalic facet is bearly detectable, shy and quiet. But it adds depth and warmth to the scent. Oud is at the base, together with other woody notes and leather.

Is that true? I would claim that right off the bat. Although I must quickly qualify that I am not exactly a great Oud expert. There are far more qualified perfumers out there. This is just my little completely subjective assessment. In this case, our Musk Aoud cannot completely hide its stable origins.

Musk Aoud completes my Roja Aoud collection as a milder representative of this line. While United Arab Emirates is a striking representative with a distinctly oriental character, Musk is rather the more socially acceptable version for European noses. The overture typically features a slightly citrus note of bergamot and lemon, which, however, becomes unnoticeable in no time.

Musk Aoud - this could have been so beautiful. I had hoped that with a Roja Aoud, one would understand a reference to real, black musk under Musk and try to combine dark-sweet-balsamic with slightly animalistic accents and a beautiful oud note. Instead, what we have here is more like everything you could find in synthetic hairspray musk. Real oud?

Here it is, my first review and then straight to a blockbuster and classic - Musk Aoud. Since there are already several reviews of the DNA by much more experienced perfumers, I want to focus on my encounter with the brand and will later discuss the fragrance. For a long time, I have been interested in Roja, but always from a distance.

I have to admit, when I first bought this I was a bit disappointed that it wasn’t as sugary sweet as I had expected and that I couldn’t discern any cotton candy note. It smelt nice but was just that. Nice. And nothing more. I revisited my bottle after a few months and I’m not sure if my bottle has had time to develop or my tastes have simply changed over the seasons but White Magnolia has won me over. It’s a gorgeous floral cotton candy scent that is so beautifully blended together. It’s sweet and sophisticated without being juvenile or cloying. I’m glad I held onto my bottle.

I discovered this while living in Spain, and it is my favorite from the Loewe collection. The yuzu note is a sweeter citrus than orange, lemon, or bergamot, and adds to its uniqueness. The cotton candy note is subtle enough that it doesn't come across as too juvenile or cheap, but adds a quality which makes people want to lean in. The vanilla works well with the cotton candy but is't overwhelming. Magnolia is one of my favorite floral scents and blends well with the other notes. I have been complimented while wearing this by my grandmother as well as friends, and it is definitely buildable strength. I like spraying in my hair as well. I would describe it as a sweet floral that works for all ages, not too young but not too mature at all. Reminds me of Madrid and carefree times :)

When I hear "White Magnolia" I think of a pure, fresh floral, but this is very gourmand on my skin and smells more pink than white. Actually, the titular magnolia is the least prominent note to me. It's not non-existant, this scent definitely has a floral aspect, too, but if you want to smell like a blooming magnolia tree, maybe look elsewhere. The whole base, front and center of this fragrance is the combination of sweet vanilla and cotton candy. It's not the burnt, cloying kind of cotton candy though, together with the other notes it comes across as creamy, smooth caramel. It reminds me of Werther's Caramelts, if you know these. The overall scents still retains the funfair atmosphere, so it makes sense that they listed cotton candy instead of caramel. The next important note is yuzu. It breaks up the sweetness with a realistic bitter and acidic note, much more than other citruses like lemon or pink grapefruit would. And the magnolia? Well, it adds a clean, creamy backdrop that makes clear that this is a spring and summer fragrance. It's a simple, but surprising and effective blend of notes. Sweet and playful with a fresh twist. A spring floral for cotton candy girlies, a funfair gourmand for fresh floral ladies. Of course, everyone else who enjoys sweet perfume is welcome, too, regardless of gender.

Do you know the famous quote by Albert Camus: “In the midst of winter, I finally learned that within me there lay an invincible summer”? I think of these words almost every time I wear White Magnolia by Loewe. Only here, it’s not an invincible summer that I feel within me, but an invincible spring full of floral scents, blue skies, and gentle breezes. Magnolia and cotton candy are distinctly noticeable, yet very fine and airy, not a bit gooey or sticky. A feather-light, powdery sweetness wraps around me like a scarf made of air, holding me tightly in its embrace. I wore White Magnolia on one of the darkest days of my life and felt, in a magical way, calmed and comforted by it. As if the fragrance wanted to whisper to me, “Don’t be afraid. I am with you. Life will be beautiful again.” That was the invincible spring that granted me an inner strength I never thought I possessed. After that, I couldn’t help but buy a bottle. I owed it to the fragrance in a way. I have not regretted it to this day.

For me, as a passionate collector of all scents leaning towards sweet, with a very high pain threshold for "that's too sweet," there has always been a problem: summer! That's when my beloved fragrances and I don't really get along. And I'm always on the lookout for a pretty floral scent that doesn't overwhelm me. Nothing fruity and nothing green should spoil my mood here. As always, when you want it just so, the search was difficult. But those who seek will find, and so I ended up with Aura White Magnolia. The beginning was already very promising with a lot of flowers. I specifically mention flowers here because I have no clue how magnolias smell. The cotton candy mentioned in the scent progression makes it sweetly lovely, but one shouldn't expect a sugar club. After half an hour, vanilla wants to join in, and by now, the scent becomes a little dream. It feels like being nestled in a cocoon of soft flowers that lift your spirits, and the day becomes beautiful at this point. It should also be mentioned that I have no idea what a yuzu fruit smells or tastes like. I can't smell any fruit at the end of the scent either. Perhaps finer noses than mine have more success here. Conclusion: I wanted a beautiful floral scent and only flower. I definitely got that here 100%. If one doesn't mind the rather linear scent progression too much, Aura White Magnolia is the perfect choice. Furthermore, the longevity of about 6 - 8 hours is absolutely sufficient for my needs. In spring or summer, I can truly recommend this scent dream to anyone. Here is the flower garden in a bottle, waiting to be discovered.

The notes initially suggest a cloyingly sweet and girlish sugary scent, or rather, one might fear that… However, it is nothing like Oriana by PdM or Love, don’t be shy by Kilian… but rather an almost elegant vanilla with a touch of sweetness, made extraordinary by the note of magnolia, which also somehow adds a sense of coziness.

Magnolias in spring are always a very special sight. The huge purple-white flowers that hold a gentle pink shimmer in the center. They quickly fade away, but the short time is worth it. The magnolia in Aura White Magnolia is not a quick bloomer; in fact, it is quite long-lasting, contrary to the floral dream that often fades so soon.
