Does that exist? Indeed, yes. Aura White Magnolia starts off very floral and fresh. You are not overwhelmed by the cotton candy, which makes the fragrance suitable for warmer days. After a few minutes, you can smell the vanilla cotton candy, which gives the scent a very feminine touch, but it never becomes something sticky.

“When I was a child, I talked like a child, I thought like a child, I reasoned like a child. When I became a man, I put the ways of childhood behind me.” 1 Corinthians 13:11 "Eww, you smell exactly like your father!"-she said. During my teenage years I never knew why my mother always said Kouros was one of her favorite fragrances ever. It seemed like everytime I tried to get myself to understand that I end up on the cold dark road (that pissy road to be exact, you know, the one next to the main highway). It seemed like I was tapdancing in the dark..for a long time. I remember I couldn't stop thinking about the fragrance for some reason..so periodicaly I kept coming back to it, to smell it again and again, hoping I could experience the exact feeling my mother had when she smelled Kouros (the best men's fragrance ever-her words) for the first time-but still no luck! After that, my interest started growing more and more each day because I couldn't understand that fragrance from the inside out like I used to understand other fragrances..and why was my mother so obsessed with it..this was a big enigma for me, and since I always loved mysteries, I kept pushing forward, I had to. After 15 years..as soon as I got my first few greys on my beard I thought maybe now is the time, right?! Still the same effect! Weird. All untill.. ..one year ago I saw Kouros standing on some dusty shelve in an old perfumery in Switzerland. It looked kinda lost, lonely..something spoke to me in that moment and I went and sprayed it directly on my skin. Sensation I was anticipating for more than 15 years was there! From the opening untill the most beautiful, manliest, perfect, addictive drydown ever! Yes! It was worth of wait for so long! Now I understand how my mother felt when she experienced it for the first time! I was so happy and thrilled, so I came home and started telling whole story to my girl. After my half-hour monologue she just said "Eww you smell exactly like your father!" (I sat there for a brief moment in silence and then it hit me) - "Yes I finally do"-and I smiled.

I’ve worn Kouros on and (mostly) off since its release. I’ve never found it skanky or off-putting in the least. Categorically, I find it a musky, spicy-floral fougère. I’ll admit the musks give it a bit of a mammalian undertone, but the clove, botany’s super antimicrobial, more than holds the unwashed at bay. I tend to find the musks that others find raunchy, dirty or displeasing merely skin-sweet and appealing. I find Muscs Koublai Khan adorable and actually a bit quaint. So here’s my scorecard on the judgments leveled on Kouros: Musky? —Yes. Sweet like the skin at the nape of someone’s neck. Clovelike? —Yes, cool to the touch. Indolic? — Yes. Orange blossom. Urinous? — No. Skin, not piss. Poopy? — No. Simply, no. Powerhouse? Compared to an eau de cologne for instance, yes. Otherwise, if worn at a moderate dose, it works like a fragrance. (You know, you’re supposed to smell it.) All I knew on my own skin before Kouros was the original Chanel’s Antaeus. It was dark and brooding and had huge projection and sillage. I wasn’t sparing in applying Antaeus and while it left a wake a mile wide, I believe it often actually preceded me into a room as well. By comparison, Kouros was a sweet pussycat.

I'm relatively young to wear such classics because I was born in a magnificent year 1989, which in my country (Poland) is known as the year of change because exactly on 4th of June 1989 it was announced that the communism was done for. I spoke to my father about perfume habits in the communism era and he said that most of the men wore a couple of types of colognes that were widely available and most of them had a classic smell. Those who could afford designer fragrances needed to visit a shop called Pewex where they could buy Guerlain's Habit Rouge, YSL's Pour Homme, Polo etc. My dad was lucky enough and for his 18th birthday he was gifted YSL's Pour Homme, a fragrance that was already a couple of years on the market and was pretty popular. He used it very occasionally because it was a really expensive cologne back in that day in Poland. He got interested in fragrances though so he started to save money for another bottle. When he saved enough he visited Pewex and after he assured the vendor he could really afford a bottle of a western fragrance (yeah, he needed to show the money lol) he was offered to sample Kouros. By the way it was not that easy to sample back in that era and the owner shared his own private bottle. Crazy huh? He doesn't remember exactly when that happened but for sure it was the first edition of Kouros, manufactured by Charles de Ritz. He instantly loved the smell, said it was the most complex fragrance he has ever smelled. Immediately he asked for a bottle but when realized the price point, he resigned and went for...Drakkar Noir. Yeah, Kouros was damn expensive. It was one of the most expensive fragrances on the market. When it launched it was considered what nowadays we call "metrosexual" (lol, how things changed). It was supposedly a favorite fragrance of the French LGBT community (well, it seems that gay people always had that impeccable taste for fashion and fragrance, nothing has changed here). Enough nostalgia, I will now tell you how my story with Kouros begun. I kept hearing about Kouros all the time because I'm a member of a large perfume community. Memes, jokes, "hehe a date? you should pick Kouros buddy" etc. I've never tried it before, it was not available in Sephora or Douglas and I didn't feel like buying a decant so I just forgot about it. I was in Greece a couple of years ago and I noticed a restaurant called Kouros and getting my memory refreshed, I just entered a large perfume shop in that town. And they had it, even exposed. The clerk said he personally liked it and that it's one of the few fragrances that had a Greek name. I thought it was awful, chemical, urinal cake smell and asked the clerk if I could wash my hands. He laughed and said it is a common reaction among young people and said that I will enjoy in a couple of years. A couple of years later when I was past my 30 already, I noticed a guy on a facebook group was selling a decant of the vintage juice from 1992. So I grabbed it because I was curios how the old version smelled, knowing that vintage perfume was better before IFRA messed up the perfume world. Aaaand that Greek clerk was damn right, I just needed some time and a vintage to appreciate it. Animalic, deep, musky, slightly powdery smell conquered my heart and I just got crazy, started to ask people about decants, scrolling groups etc. I managed to find a rare bottle of Eau de Sport and blind buying it for a fair price (now they are crazy), got another decant, then got a 50 ml bottle of Parfum Corp version, 50 ml after shave from Charles de Ritz era (yay!), then time came for 100 ml of Gucci version, had a Sanofi bottle but sold it, and finally I found the holy grail. 100 ml of Charles de Ritz from 1984 + a decant of 1981 premiere edition. I felt like a junkie hoarding my favorite drug. Funny thing is that I paid 100 euros for that and I actually asked the vendor if he was aware what he was selling. It turned out that he was Kouros's fanboy and had a lot of bottles so he decided to share it in the name of love. So how different they are? Charles de Ritz - my favorite of all, is the most complex one, the most musky one. At least my bottle is not that animalic, I smell less civet, the amber here is also gorgeous. The opening is a real musk bomb and it is just slightly dirty. It is also the most powdery of all and feels really classy, old school. It has a veeery good longevity while the projection is not huge, but it is ok, I wouldn't like this type of fragrance to suffocate people. The AS version is of course less potent that the EDT and it fades quicker but it is exactly the same as the EDT, high quality stuff. I wear a beard so I can't use it on my whole face. When I shave my neck then sometimes I use if I'm planning to use the EDT. It doesn't irritate my skin and amps up the EDT. Parfum Corp - it was the first vintage that made me fall in love with Kouros. This one (at least my bottle) is more animalic and the civet is easy to distinguish. It is more skanky than the Charles de Ritz and less powdery. However, after and hour or two it smells almost exactly the same as the first edition. It has the same performance. Best price/quality ratio in the Kouros world. If you see it on ebay or local marketplaces, just buy it it is worth it. Sanofi - I had it, sold the bottle because I felt it was redundant in my collection and I made another Kouros aficionado happy. It is more potent than Parfum Corp but less deep than the predecesors. It is heavy on the dirty musk, definitely more aldehydic than the rest. Performance is superb, easily 24h on clothes. It smells fantastic when you spray 2-3 times on your chest and wear a linen summer shirt. It won't offend people and you will smell whafts every now and then. Gucci - It is basically same as Sanofi, even better because even more potent. That one is the strongest Kouros in my possession. 2-3 sprays maximum, even one spray in summer months will be enough. This is basically a high quality slightly dirty musk scent. L'oreal - I don't own it but current batch seems to be more aldehydic and citrussy in comparison. It doesn't have that skanky nature, which makes it more wearable for people that don't like animalic perfume. The longevity is decent but the sillage seems to be weaker. I also own Eau de Sport so just a quick note - it is basically like a Parfum Corp edition but with less animalic features. The musk is there but is less potent and cleaner. It is good but not worth the price. --- I think that Kouros pushes people off because they smell it close to the skin. The whole beauty of this fragrance is that it needs some body heat to show its true nature. Hence, I strongly believe that is a summer scent. People tend to avoid it in the summer because they worry about scaring people off. Grab even the most recent batch, spray under your shirt when it is hot outside and see for yourself. For me it is a masterpiece and an icon. I hope it will never get discontinued.

My final bottle of vintage Kouros arrived last summer. Its a 1.6 oz splash. The price was worth it. The splash is the best way to control its power. The aldehydes are hushed. Just a drop is all it takes. This box came from the 1980s with the silver foil. The bottle reminds me of solid marble. It feels so clean and powerful in my hands. It is still radiant and warm. Now the magic begins... I am forever 20, young and in style. Its 1984 every sniff I take! "When Doves Cry" was new on the radio, Ghostbusters in theaters, my hair was ratted high with mousse, long trenchcoats and elf boots were in style. I was a freshman in college. The world seemed so easy to conquer. Kouros was carefully tucked in my bookbag and worn liberally. I was the only man on campus to sport this fragrance. It helped boost my self esteem as everyone focused attention on me as I entered a classroom. YSL had created "me" with this classic bottle of luxury. Sure, others would follow-Paco Rabanne PH, Drakkar Noir, Lagerfeld and even CK Calvin. Yes, the perfume revolution began with Kouros. I found that I could control crowds without saying a word! Yes, it was like a chapter from "Perfume" by Suskind! That was the power of the "powerhouse". Ladies had Poison, Opium and Knowing to use. I never paid attention to the notes. It was this "magical potion" that just worked, honestly! Kouros had this subjugating effect on those around me. It made me feel sexy and magnetizing. I remained single, celibate and the center of attention throughout the 80s. The 90s is another story... Kouros put the "come hither" on anyone I desired. It would accompany me for the rest of my life, through today. Pure Alpha Male... Now, this 3rd and final bottle of my lifetime is in my hands. I hope to have it used up before I die, because it is too good to take to the grave! Its unfortunate that future generations will not get to feel its power. Yes, I am happy the "despot formula" is on the shelves. I will never own a bottle. For those of you that developed an aversion to Kouros, you have my sympathy. May you never forget however, that once upon a time the was a mighty fashion house called YSL that made a holy water named Kouros that granted men the power of gods !!!

Right at the start of my fragrance collecting, I encountered Kouros. It appeared mysteriously on the shelves of my local Kmart, a variety store that generally, in Australia, carries nothing more fancy than Axe (Lynx) or Blue Stratos. The store apparently had a failed venture into fragrances and I definitely benefitted from it. Two 50ml bottles cost me $14.40 in total and I bought the bottles unsniffed. When I got home I opened up one box and sprayed, whoa, I was sold straight away. For me the brilliance of this polarising fragrance is how close it comes to being utterly repulsive, but holds enough back to be magnificent. The sweetness, aromatic notes and civet are balanced so well that I cannot imagine a more perfect blend. The recent reformulation really strips the power away from Kouros and tones down the animalistic aspect big time. I find it hard to identify individual notes in Kouros, but a honeyed, animalistic spicy fragrance is how I would describe it. The sillage and longevity are colossal, at least with the previous formulation, the current one is still, however, good but nowhere near the older. My wife can barely stand this fragrance (the same with Lapidus pour Homme), but other women I know absolutely love it. As this is my first review on Parfumo, I thought I would start with what I consider to be THE masterpiece of male perfumery.
An iconic fragrance and a refference in the scent world, which I used to dislike when I was în college (when a lot of foreign students wore it way too loud making it unbearable for the rest of us).

This review is based upon my new (not vintage) bottle purchased in 2023. Initial spray is kinda harsh with punches in the nose that change - yeah, the urinal cakes, grandma's floral perfume, a wiff of WD-40, a carnation - very interesting experience with the opening.

Nothing can prepare you adequately for the moment when you first experience Kouros. I tried it for the first time after reading oodles about it and smelling hundreds of other fragrances, many of which were strong, vintage fragrances, and I thought Kouros (or any other fragrance for that matter) could not wow me at that point. I was wrong.

For a perfume that's supposed to be bold and challenging, Kouros is surprisingly fresh and evocative. It's a bit pissy and sweaty, but when you combine bodily fluids with soapy florals reminiscent of clean bedsheets, the scent suddenly becomes deeply sexual. Bottles with silver shoulders from 2000-2008 are the sweet spot.

Launched in 1981, Kouros has been one of the most famous love it or hate it fragrances of our time. My 1st purchase was around 1990. I wish i still had that bottle for sentimental reasons and of course for vintage purposes. I own 3 bottles from different time periods. 1986 2003 2019. The scent is similar and boy is it powerful. This stuff just lasts.

I was expecting a richer take on the esencia edp, which is already great on its own and has very good performance (actually i don’t understand why an elixir needed?). The first seconds are very similar, but after some minutes the smell turns into a very bad chemical and synthetic smell, a very very cheap scent that reminds of very low budget clothes shop. It is also nausea inducing because of its density, it’s like a nauseating very low lever designer fragrance on stereoids. And it’s more expensive than a lot of very high quality niche perfumes. It’s around 230€ for a 100ml bottle. I wouldn’t wear this even if it was for free, it smells really really annoying, basic, cheap, disturbing, gives me headache.

It opened up pretty nicely on my skin. A woody comfy male fragrance. It was pretty delicious and I was enjoying myself for about 40 minutes. Then my partner came home and wanted to try it as well. And on him? An immediate overload of something vaguely citrusy and super aggressive for no good reason. My partner loved it, I couldn't stand it. But it enveloped our whole apartment, so I didn't really have a choice in the matter. The initial explosion took more than 30 minutes to settle, and ~4 hours to become soft enough to smell pleasant to me. Once the it mellowed out on his skin, it actually became pretty cute, almost like a zesty panettone. It pretty much disappeared from me by then, and whatever hints still remained would easily get choked out any time my partner walked past me. It also clung to his clothing and stayed strong there for more than ~9 hours. And on a clean sweater straight from the wash too... Ugh. I was desperate to love it, but alas.

when i try this perfume i fell in love it smells like aventus but little be dark more strong it last all day with good sillage and projection it cost a little be expensive here in spain 160euros ,you can´t go wrong with this perfume for the price you can get the best version of aventus gracias loewe

How chance plays in life sometimes!? In a perfumery in Lanzarote, I was actually looking for scents for my dear wife - and was well advised by a very friendly, knowledgeable young lady. But what on earth made her spray a scent on my arm without asking, which immediately captivated me completely? “Ahh, this is the one,” I stammered - but she said: “no, this One is for You”! Not only did all the scents I had previously tested for my wife suddenly seem banal, even downright ridiculous: I had never smelled something so good, dense, and harmonious in my life! Now, I must say, I am a fan of bold perfumes, patchouli, vetiver, wood, pepper, and so on! - I love Encre Noir, the old Givenchy Gentleman, and the new Dior Homme Sport, not to mention the now hard-to-find (unless grandpa has passed away and the grandchildren know the value of this drug on eBay) Rochas Macassar… and yesterday I found the souls of all these treasures united and preserved in this one scent: Esencia Elixir by Loewe. Loewe is indeed an elegant, old company that always uses good ingredients - at least the vintage versions of their “pour homme” scent are also brilliant! But this one, it is hard to find words! This is a powerful, yes, overwhelmingly powerful elixir that, however, does not penetrate in any way or even (like another, the Elixir for stinkers) stink. Here, one simply finds the sublimity and the fullness! It wears like an ermine of smoke and deep green! For me, it is the absolute EXIT - perfume - one would actually never need anything else, because it seems unimaginable to me that it could ever become boring to perceive this scent on oneself and to bring joy to other people with it. All the other perfumes are not bad, they can still serve for variety, like drinking grain and caraway during the week, only to enjoy the 16-year-old noble single malt whisky on the high holiday. Green then, foggy forests, fairy forests, mossy witch grounds, November and June at once - Norse, trolls, and elves! Even the next day, after a thorough shower, you smell this scent on your skin and on your shirt - but without any intrusiveness, just as the trace of something higher, yes almost sacred. I look forward to every day that I will walk with this scent and stride in splendor and glory in my ermine of rainforest smoke. PS Please forgive my childlike enthusiasm, I am actually a very sober person. But this here…

I have spent several years looking for a more affordable fragrance that resembles or is similar to Creed Aventus. How much time has passed, from Insurrection P2, La Martina TDF, to Armaf's CDNIM versions that have created their own hype. Anyone who knows these fragrances will understand how good some of them are. Compliment Kings are among them.

Currently, there are 3 other reviews and two significant statements about Esencia Elixir alongside mine, but so far no complete review. Now I have the privilege of writing the first review for this little fragrance. As a fan of the Esencia edP, it was already exciting to learn that there is now an Elixir of this wonderful scent.

Young people are often said to be green behind the ears. An expression likely derived from immature vegetables, which often have green spots as well. However, for those who have left any immaturity behind and still want to enjoy being green behind the ears, they can easily apply Esencia Elixir .

For me, this is the perfect manager fragrance for the office. Elegant, self-assured, and yet extraordinary. It has this clear, masculine presence without being intrusive - just the right balance between authority and a sense of style. Many compare it to Creed Aventus, and yes - that noble, fresh note is definitely there.

The slightly more mature, lightly smoky and spicy elegant version of Esencia! Compared to the EDP, this Elixir version is tuned a bit darker but still fresh. The regular EDP is a bit sportier. Both are top fragrances. Those who prefer a smokier and more elegant scent, like with older Aventus batches, will surely not be disappointed here.

This fragrance gives designer fragrances a good reputation. It has a combination of all of my favorite accords: White florals, vanilla, sweet, aromatic, ambery, etc. Strong on the lavender (so if you don’t like lavender, skip this one!!), but not overbearing because the vanilla is turned up on this one compared to the OG Libre. I would place it in the same genre as Mon Guerlain because of the combo of lavender / vanilla / aromatics; but Libre Intense definitely has more of a seductive edge to it. I not only adore the way it smells, but also, the way it makes me feel! It’s sexy, sophisticated, powerful, and enticing. This one is an obvious crowd pleaser, but I think the entire Libre line is. They’re not only beautiful in their composition, but the performance on each of them is spectacular. This lasts FOREVER on clothes (literally this stuck to my sweater dress for A MONTH until I got a chance to wash it) and has a strong sillage / projection. You don’t need to overspray this one at all and people around will most definitely notice you wearing this. What I also love about this fragrance is how well it wears on its own AND how well it layers with other scents. Because it has such a diverse accords list, it layers well with other white florals, vanillas, aromatics, citruses, ambers, and spicys. I can’t say that about many of my other fragrances. Libre Intense is also very versatile in when / where you can wear it. You can wear it in the dead cold of winter, and also in the heat of summer. Day or night, work or out to party, you name it! While I did declutter this, I plan on adding it back into my collection at some point. I just need to focus on reducing my collection badly as I’ve been overwhelmed with the amount that I have.

This has the same vibe as Lucy Liu in Charlie's Angels where she's wearing the leather outfit and carrying a riding crop. Is she going to f*ck you? Stab you? No one knows. This is big like an 80's powersuit. This reminds me so much of the 80's because it's just so confident and bold. Feminine but also a little masculine. It's sweet and enticing but in the way a Venus Flytrap is enticing to insects. Maneater would have been a more appropriate name.

It's marketed as a bold scent for an independent woman, and the fragrance itself definitely embodies a pantsuit type energy. Although I don't envision myself as a alpha female girl capitalist, if there is ever a time where I become one of those Chinese influencers that pay $75 to join a WeChat group for "wealthy socialites," maybe I might put this on while posing with a rented Lamborghini to really sell the possibility that I could be on the Forbes 30 Under 30 list.

It is clearly a flanker of Libre, it has the same essence, but this one is much more gourmand and predictable. What I like about the original libre is that it doesn't look like those commercial aromas that you smell everywhere, however this one is a little closer to that, it's more people pleaser. Lavender is super present but by changing the musky and woody base notes for tonka bean and vetiver where vanilla stands out, the seal is more reminiscent of a mass fragrance. In any case, that does not make it any less rich and enjoyable. The only thing that doesn't convince me is that although this flanker is the intense one, it lasts much less than the original, which is a bomb in duration. I've had it on my skin for 5 hours and it already feels very flush, when Libre lasts 12 hours or more, and even after bathing it feels. It seems to me an interesting version that I would buy and enjoy, but if I have to choose one, I'll stick with the original Libre.

I often like the Intense flankers of perfumes better than the pillar, and Libre is no exception. Actually I'm not the biggest fan of the original version, it just veers too much into fabric softener territory for me. Libre Intense still smells like Libre, but richer, warmer and more feminine. All fragrances in this line have a bright, clean aura, but the Intense version also has warmth and depth. The vanilla, tonka and amber are beautifully done and really ground the laundry-fresh orange blossom and citrus note. And the best part is that the lavender is not only stronger, but also comes across as more natural and aromatic than it does in the original. This is really balanced, even in the final drydown it still has some of the fresh, herbal-floral Libre DNA and doesn't turn into a run-of-the-mill vanilla. Let me describe it this way: When I smell Libre, I think of a woman who prefers clean lines and no frills, minimal make-up and jewelry, sleek hair and so on. Libre Intense is the same woman, but with bold lipstick and big, geometrical golden earrings. Which is closer to my personal style, so it's no surprise I like this better. It's just so pretty, and the "Intense" label is no joke. I was torn between buying Libre Intense or Libre Le Parfum for a long time and sampled them often. Theyr'e quite close to each other, but I'd describe the differences like this: Le Parfum is even creamier, sweeter and more feminine than Intense, but it's also brighter and lighter on the lavender. It's really beautiful, too. I'd say Libre Intense is more exciting, Le Parfum is more comforting. In the end I bought the latter, it's a tiny bit more fitting to my personal taste.

OG Libre and Libre Intense are STRONG, you don’t need much, but they are lovely. Very similar to each other, the intense version is a bit more powdery and sweeter with a lot of vanilla in the drydown, and more suitable for colder weather. I get lavender, vanilla, florals and musk and the citrus is mostly just in the opening.

Smelled and wore this perfume for the first time today. At first, I didn't know how to feel about it because the opening smelled like laundry detergent. Far from that thick, headache-inducing perfume that people were talking about.

libre intense smells similar except that they've added vanilla, & i personally think the lavender + vanilla is a bit too overwhelming for me. og libre is heavy on the lavender, which makes it more fresh, so i prefer this one.

On the initial spray, it's quite soapy to my nose. A strong lavender with orange blossom and jasmine, juicy mandarin and bergamot sitting on top. It's settles down within a couple of minutes into a pleasant creamy tonka/vanilla base, with a somewhat underlying boozy vibe. I will also say at this point, this is a powerhouse! And i've only sprayed once.

I actually like Libre EDP better than the Libre intense version. This one is warmer, spicier and just overall stronger. It’s not bad. I just don’t like it as much. The sillage is kind of strong and travels a bit, and the longevity is several hours. Overall I would say it’s an alright fragrance. I don’t mind it.

Not much to say about this, except for the fact that the “extrait” name (and the price) may be somehow misleading. Vetiver Extrait smells great, but well... simply put, it’s no different from any good vetiver scent. It’s a really simple, smooth, light straightforward vetiver, classy and cozy, not particularly powerful (actually, not at all) or rich, just diligently bearing most of the usual nuances of most vetiver scents – it feels initially zesty, peppery and crisp, slowly becoming smokier, rootier, still keeping vetiver’s traditional subtle feel of “oily grassiness”, subtly paired with a rather conventional base accord of powdery-dusty notes. It’s all good, really. It wears extremely well, it feels refined and laid-back, carefully mannered enough to avoid any “raw” earthy effect – on the contrary it feels rather polished, bright and distinguished. It conveys an extremely enjoyable albeit slightly pedantic sense of calm, class, confidence and sophisticated weightlessness. If compared to dirtier or richer vetiver scents, this is quite on the opposite spectrum – it feels very clean, almost ethereal. Even a tad too much, as it soon feels quite – if not, completely – unexciting, and almost kind of mute (I suspect there’s some generic “woody smoothener” used here – some very generic plushy woody base). The longevity is a bit weak, but that’s the price to pay for higher concentrations of natural materials. So all in all, it’s unquestionably nice. But really only that. For £ 275. Not grounbreaking, not heart-melting, not mind-blowing – just an impeccable everyday vetiver fragrance for office time. Ready to let your rock and rule the printers’ room and the vending machines’ corner. Just as any other good vetiver scent. It can be fantastic for you if you like vetiver, but in no way it can be worthy that price and that pomposity (and come on... for that price, some crap cardboard box? I want my box to be lined in Elton John’s skin!). It does no more and no less than any simple, solid vetiver fragrance (there’s so many of them I can’t even think of a couple of specific names to mention – Guerlain? Carven? Ford’s Grey Vetiver? Heeley? Anyone, really), and I think there is really no standout features that would explain why one should prefer this over others. Clearly, the value lies in the “status symbol” allure of the brand and the presentation. And that has nothing to do with fragrances, so... Anyway if you’re really wealthy and you really like vetiver then go for it, otherwise I see really no need to break the bank for this. 6,5-7/10

Vetiver Extrait opens with a nose tingling mix of effervescent lemon and bergamot before quickly moving to its heart. As the composition reaches its early heart the lemon remains, sans bergamot and effervescence as it joins clean citric, grassy green, slightly woody vetiver infused by bitter-green resinous galbanum and slightly sharp cedarwood, with a relatively subtle wet concrete-like undertone. During the late dry-down the composition loses the wet-concrete-like undertone, with the clean vetiver remaining, supported by slightly powdery oakmoss in the base through the finish. Projection is excellent and longevity outstanding at around 20 hours on skin. Roja Dove's Vetiver Extrait is not the usual vetiver presentation I go for. I love my vetivers rough, aggressive and smoky, and Roja's Vetiver is none of those. One might think that I disliked the composition as a result, but that would be quite far from the truth. To the contrary, while this presentation of vetiver is more of the grassy, clean variety, it uses extremely high quality raw materials throughout. Another distinguishing aspect of the composition is its very appealing use of natural smelling lemon through most of the composition's development. If there was an aspect that required a bit of getting used to, it would have to be the concrete-like undertone that hangs around through the entire mid-section, but while the accord is a bit unsettling when sniffed up close, when experienced in the composition's generous sillage it melds rather nicely with the lemon infused vetiver, giving the composition a distinguishing facet while still smelling extremely pleasant. "Pleasant smelling" is probably the best descriptor of the end result, come to think of it. This is the kind of vetiver composition that even folks disliking many others may still enjoy wearing due to its highly refined clean nature. While I maintain there are a lot of great vetiver options far below the composition's relatively stratospheric price point per ml, if one can afford Roja Dove's Vetiver Extrait, it is hard to say it is a poor investment, especially if you enjoy your vetivers of the clean, polished variety. The bottom line is the $395 per 50ml bottle Vetiver Extrait is quite the bank account buster, but Dove delivers the goods with top-notch raw materials and superb execution earning it an "excellent" 4 star out of 5 rating and a solid recommendation. I don't know if I can personally afford the price to purchase a bottle, but I certainly envy those that can and do.

Vetiver Pour Homme Parfum from the British House of Haute Luxury Niche Perfumery Roja London is a Cyprus Citrus Spicy Woody Earthy Green Men's perfume. It was launched in 2012, and the nose behind this fragrance is Roja Dove. Choosing Vetiver as the central component of the fragrance means capturing the essence of this versatile ingredient, known for its unique multifaceted combination: earthy, woody and slightly smoky. Vetiver is celebrated for its depth, longevity, versatility, and masculinity. It reminded me a little of Grey Vetiver(TF), with more quality, more refined, exquisite, luxurious. Vetiver Pour Homme, a warm, dry, fresh and spicy fragrance... all this at the same time; unfolding around the earthy green, dry woody, subtly smoky and voluptuous aromas of vetiver, refreshed by a sharp citrus green accord. At the opening, the vitality of bergamot, with the power of lemon amplified by the cutting citrus green litsea with another clean floral citrus touch of petitgrain, is further tempered by a spicy pepper mixture. A discreet bouquet of rose and jasmine bring a refined refinement to the fragrance. These floral elements soften the sharp citrus green sting of the top. The base is marked by spicy spices, woody and mossy notes, which give depth and a mystery to the fragrance. With pepper, nutmeg and cumin, and an original celery seed and galbanum note add a spicy freshness to the warm, smoky central theme developed around vetiver. This set rests on a pleasant base of guaiac wood and more Green Aromas: needles and cedar wood that are intertwined with the dry aromas of oakmoss and a leathery resinous touch of labdanum, which perfectly complement this perfume, a sophisticated blend, a chypre par excellence. Delicious Perfume For Hot Days!

Ahh Roja's Vetiver Pour Homme Parfum... First, the price... Yes of course it is expensive, this is Roja. If you want a legit bottle as well as a good price, go to Jomashop and get it for $214.99. That is the price I paid, obviously if you pay retail you are going to feel scammed. This is a beautifully constructed and blended parfum. I see a lot of people on here complaining about this being average as far as silage/projection and just the overall profile. This fragrance is very heavy on the raw materials so of course it is not going to project very well, with raw materials like sandalwood and rose absolute you're just not going to get "insane" projection/silage. If you want something like that please look into Dior Sauvage or some Versace cologne, they go very heavy on the aroma chemicals. So, with that being said let's talk about this fragrance... At the top I'm getting a really nice litsea cubeba with slight bergamot which gives it that Roja sparkle. This litsea cubeba lasts about 2 hours and carries really nice into the hearts notes where you will find massive amounts of lily-of-the-valley florals which smell of complete elegance and intrinsically blend with the soon to come vetiver. Heart notes last about another 1.5ish hours until we get the base note dry down. The base is where this fragrance really makes its mark (Wait about 3.5-4 hours) ... transitioning from the heart of florals blooms a light, airy and clean vetiver. This vetiver is draped in loads of dry woods and leather like ingredients. This may be why some complain because the vetiver is so delicately added and wrapped in many different notes. I get an almost aquatic like vetiver which to me smells absolutely brilliant. This fragrance has ruined other "fresh" fragrances from other brands just because of how greatly constructed it is so, beware lol. So, is this an amazing fragrance? 100% this is peak perfumery. Are you going to fill a room with everyone's head turning and people bowing before you? No, but I have a feeling the man that wants this fragrance would in no way want to do that.

I recently blind bought it,so it was a first impression let me tell you that it DOES NOT worth the price tag.The first 2-3minutes it was like a better version imagination ,it was like a soapy smell(better than imagination then a citrusy smell continues. 30minutes later the earthy vetiver starts to shine first i liked it but the second wear was no for me. I barely smell the flowers after 2-3hours the only thing i can smell is the earthy vetiver that is still goin strong overall I wouldn't consider buying it for this high price and I barely think I would buy it for even half the price.Just go with a designer vetiver scent.

Uncommented Fragrances No. 45 One thing must be said upfront: I have developed an ambivalent relationship with the fragrances of Roja Dove. At first, like with many niche brands, I was disappointed with the price-performance ratio of many Roja scents.

With some fragrances, it is almost forbidden to ask about the notes, and Roja Dove's current Vetiver is one of them. Litsea Cubeba, rose, and guaiac wood are unimportant, as they confuse more than they could explain. In recent years, the market has certainly not been lacking in new Vetiver releases. Yet hardly a fragrance exists without a significant caveat.

What have I not tested in Vetiver fragrances, the dark ones, the creaky ones, the dull ones, the bright ones, the mild ones, the soft ones, the affordable ones, the sinfully expensive ones, the nutty ones, the creamy ones... no matter.. I never really warmed up to them..

My first encounter with a classic sweet grass scent is thanks to the Vetiver Eau de Toilette by Guerlain. That was quite a few years ago, and at the time, I found it simply too woody and thus unsuitable for me.

Vetiver pour Homme is, for me, the most elegant vetiver fragrance currently available on the market. Modern, medium green, fresh, warm, and spicy. The English lord among vetiver scents. Like an elegant, green, finely woven wool sweater, made of the finest merino wool. However, I would like to somewhat qualify this judgment right away.

While I agree that Cinema is a lovely, elegant and inoffensive scent, I have experienced what many other reviewers have casually mentioned; it reminds me of something I've smelt before. I don't mean that in a bad way, and I certainly wouldn't be put off this fragrance because of it. After racking my brain for a few hours I haven't pin-pointed exactly what it smells like however I think it's a little similar to Organza by Givenchy, Poeme by Lancome and Donna Karan's Gold. In regards to the scent, I find it to be very classy and cosy. It has all the glitz-and-glamour to be worn to special occasions and the comforting vanilla in the drydown that makes for a wonderful casual, 'hanging around the house' type scent. Cinema fits the oriental category perfectly, with rich ambery and musky notes surrounded by sweet, honey-like florals and thick vanilla. The woman that wears this fragrance, in my mind, is mature and confident. It also has a soft, powdery-like quality which I really admire. Cinema certainly wasn't as strong as I expected it to be. For some strange reason I expected a loud and brash floral explosion. While the sillage is quite average, the lasting power is not. Cinema lasts considerably well, at least 9 hours so far. A somewhat creamy and rich oriental, that I do whole-heartedly recommend.

I am so glad I got to sample this before (blind) buying. I had high hopes for this one, but it left me feeling disappointed. Right after application I thought that this was nothing new, just another generic (synthetic) vanilla based wannabe classic perfume. Been there done that, seen this smelled that. I didn't find it very pleasant, quite cloying and annoying at times. Many people rave about the vanilla notes in Cinema, personally I didn't get any sweetness. I guess it's all about chemistry, but on me the citrus notes linger for ever and I dislike citrus. I want a perfume to make me feel good, and go "aaaaahhh" when I smell it. You know that feeling of wanting to sniff so hard that you want to absorb every single molecule, and you can never get enough? Well, with Cinema I could only take very short sniffs, had to pull my arm away from my nose after a fraction of a second because it makes me feel irritated every time I smell my wrist. Pass.

When the nights grow long and cold, I always look for a nice scent to lighten up my mood. Cinema is one of those scents. It smells gorgeous mixed with the cold air when its honeyed floral notes are balanced by the chilly weather outside. Cinema is smooth and comforting but it is not a scent that I just want to cuddle with while reading a nice book on a stormy night. It is great for a night out when I need something more sophisticated than just a straight up vanilla gourmand. Cinema is very attractive and elegant scent. She is not an eccentric diva but a woman who is classy, considerate and warm. The composition is largely based on the sweet honeyed notes and vanilla but I also like how it brings the sensual beauty of jasmine in the mix. After the quick fresh spring flowers opening, the scent transforms into this beautiful sweet floral scent which stays linear but quite lovely surrounding me with its smooth golden wrap. Nothing is out of place here. It is like a nice, well-made evening gown, which looks classy and beautiful without revealing too much. As the scent transforms into a dry down stage, it continues to be smooth and sweet while vanilla, benzoin and amber take over. The scent lasts for at least 7 hours and has decent projection. Few sprays last all day. My overall score is 8.5/10. This scent is pure luxury. If gold had a scent, I think it would smell like Cinema. I recommend it if you are looking for a nice, smooth vanilla oriental scent. It is not there to shock you but it is reliable, elegant and easy to wear.

I'm pleased that at least this perfume has the substance to divide opinions somewhat -- to my nose, Cinéma is very much a nice auntie kind of perfume. Definitely classy, always pleasant and well-mannered, never too much or too little. I detect a gourmand aspect, too, but whatever citric there is about it is so fleeting I couldn't pinpoint it. The comparison to the glamour of movies stars of old is very apt. Beyond the obvious big names, those beautiful women came and went (as they still do) as soon as any sign of age crept in, always replaced by a younger version of themselves, never unique or remembered. That is what the glamour of the cinema is built upon, that neverending re/cycling of looks and maybe talent, and that is what I'm reminded of when I sniff Cinéma: the fifty flavours of vanilla pudding, varied just so those who consume their image won't get bored too easily but staying the same in their essence so the punters will keep coming back for more. It's a well-made floral, oriental vanilla, and so generic it will probably remind you of loads of things you have smelled before. If Shalimar is too gutsy (or alternately old-lady) for you, Cinéma is a worthy contender for the favoured comfort/luxury scent. If you like that sort of thing, you will love Cinéma, an it certainly has its strengths; if not, keep looking.

A very classy and rich perfume. Floriental Vanilla to my nose out of the bottle and that is the characteristic it reveals on my skin as well. A pretty floral concoction highlighted by a most exquisite creamy vanilla. If you have the money for it, don't hesitate to add this gem to your collection.

Beautiful, but so fleeting. I douse the heck out of her, and two hours later she is barely there. She is almost too discreet for me to be considered as an evening frag. So I will enjoy her more in the daytime, and carry the bottle with me to reapply every two hours.
With one purchase of Y.S.

Just read the book of Nadja Spiegelmann, another halfway interesting book about neurotic families and the only passage that stuck to my mind so far is when she talks about her English teacher claiming that "nice" is not a compliment and the word should be abolished all together...

I have come to know that the difference between an Eau de Parfum and an Eau de Toilette can be everything between nonexistent and a totally different fragrance. J’Adore edt was so faint and short lived I let it go, but I kept the edp due to its interesting unisex vibe.

Oh this one is perfection in a bottle ! Powdery vanilla, clementine, almond and jasmine... So beautiful ! Cinéma is lovely yet very chic, chic yet sexy, sexy yet ingenuous... It's indeed a film, an epic, a novel... Very underrated, it has unfortunately become difficult to find online... When I see a bottle, I have to stock up! :p

In a world where rose/oud combos are as common as ketchup, there's one brand thatft packages it up the fanciest. Roja Parfums Taif Aoud. Fancy ketchup. It would be a travesty if I left a review at that, so all jokes aside i'll say this is actually a good quality departure from sweetened-up westernized oud fragrances. Taif Aoud opens with a burst of aldehydes. I do share in the sentiment of reviewer Gabri031982, wishing that that opening would last a bit longer. The fragrance transitions to a heart of Taif rose of exceptional quality, and oud. There is something a bit sharp about about it but it wasn't enough to make me feel like i'm being stabbed in the nose and make it bleed As the fragrance continues drying down into the latter stages, the cassis becomes more and more amplified, giving Taif Aoud an animalic edge quite similar to the one which civet was responsible for in Roja Parfums UAE Spirit Of The Union (original formula multi-colored cap bottle), but with a greenness to it. Taif Aoud was at no point sweetened up and seems like one which would appeal more to a middle eastern audience, although anyone can enjoy it whether it be an acquired taste or naturally appeals to your palette. I fall into the former category and from time to time still struggle sometimes with that animalic side of things. Taif Aoud is perfectly suitable for both men and women, terrific for the brisk months of fall. I wouldn't describe it as 'thick' or 'warm,' found it a bit on the lighter side and slightly airy, so i'm not sure if it's adequate for cutting through the piercingly frigid temperatures of mid winter. I can certainly put it to the test if i live to see another winter

Unisex Characteristic for Taif Rose are intense but soft, powdery and even honeyed notes yet honey is not noticeable in this perfume. Taif Aoud opens up with sparkling Aldehydes together with that captivating, sensual and mesmerizing Rose and that makes it feel like the fresh mountain air, the fresh wind from the mountains which fills your senses. That fresh and earthy vibe is toned up with Patchouli and Frankincense which is really intoxicating here together with non animalic pleasant, round and elegant oud. Taif Aoud is very versatile since it’s not offending people. The blend is not so strong, it’s not the Oud which screams and shout it’s existence but in the same time it’s noticeable. The longevity and projection is not like a typical oud perfume which makes this great for the spring and a summertime like as well for the people who are not so big fan of the bold and brash oud scents. This parfume is all about roses and oud so on the other hand it’s leaning on feminine side but on the other hand there is certain masculine vibe. Even if Labdanum doesn’t come out in leathery way it certainly brings depth to this. For those who are not familiar with Roja Parfums’ compositions I want to mention the following of the notes here: -Bergamot in the opening is barely noticeable. -From the middle notes the main note is Rose and it is what you get. Even another main note in the middle, Cassis, is really tame. -You don’t find here strong Patchouli neither Labdanum as a clear leather note. Vanilla and Musk as well are well blended and not noticeable in a traditional way. Taif Aoud is magnificent and addictive scent. I love it! Top Notes: Aldehydes*, Bergamot Middle Notes: Geranium, Rose*, Jasmin de Grasse, Ylang Ylang, Clove Buds, Cassis* Base Notes: Patchouli, Aoud*, Benzoin, Vanilla, Frankincense*, Labdanum, Musk * being main notes I will edit this review later since this was first written on IG where the space is very limited. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes

This scent has taken my sophisticated evening selection by storm. Weddings, dinner parties and holiday banquet are prime wearing situations for taif aoud. I’d. Recommend this fragrance to any gentlemen that is looking to make an impression on his significant other or steal the night away with a brides maid.

Roja Taif Aoud is a luxurious fragrance that blends the deep floral sweetness of Taif rose with the rich, earthy tones of aoud. Spicy notes like saffron and warm base notes of patchouli and amber add depth, creating an opulent and sophisticated scent. Its impressive longevity and strong sillage make it ideal for special occasions, capturing the elegance of Middle Eastern perfumery with a modern touch.

Uncommented Fragrances No. 96 That I would write another comment on a rose-oud fragrance, even though I complain at every opportunity about this now overly trodden path in (niche) perfumery... After I managed to get a small decant of this highly praised and apparently extremely rare fragrance (only available at the royal British supplier Fortnum & Mason, see above), but there was no comment available so far, I will attempt a hopefully not too subjective consideration and the question of whether a purchase could be worthwhile. Let’s set aside the aforementioned fact that the rose-oud combination is encountered with almost all niche brands and has increasingly made its way into the mass market. Which manufacturer that takes itself seriously hasn’t tried this highly sought-after composition? Let’s also set aside the fact that Roja fragrances are positioned in a price segment that some see as a mark of quality, while others consider it evidence of unappetizingly decadent pricing. Yet, Taif Aoud, despite its exclusivity regarding availability, is not even an exceptionally expensive Roja. The royal supplier asks for 395 British pounds for a 50 ml bottle. There are already more expensive bottles on Roja Dove's homepage. This observation is not to be understood in terms of unreflective snobbery or political sarcasm. I simply state it as it is. Nevertheless, one should expect the highest quality for this price. Do you get that? Is this great? Beauty lies - as so often - in the eye (and nose) of the beholder. What I can say about it: I like the fragrance, and this is despite the fact that I can hardly tolerate compositions of rose and oud anymore, as they dominated the niche segment, to put it bluntly, until a few years ago. However, here the balance, in my opinion, is well achieved, as the fragrance comes across neither too Arabic-oriental nor too baroque or overly cloying. Rose and oud are in a balanced harmony that creates a beautiful bridge between East and West. Amidst all the floral intoxication that this fragrance exudes, a very clear green, hardly powdery rose dominates for me, whose sweetness initially blooms rather naturally than oppressively. The oud is always noticeable without being intrusive. At the outset, it seems a bit medicinal (almost synthetic) to me, but this impression fades over time, and then it remains pleasantly harmoniously present without dominating. Having been alerted by Kankuro's statement, I would say that this fragrance contains noticeable aldehydes, without overlaying the characteristic fruit-like floral scent of most aldehydes (as known from classic women's fragrances) over the rose-oud combination. The effect is rather different: the fragrance has something very feminine, classic, without appearing dusty, and is ultimately more suited for women. As a man, I would like to use it at home, but wouldn’t want to wear it out. All in all, however, it remains with a clear focus on rose and oud, admittedly in great harmony, but without providing exciting surprises. There isn’t much happening in the further development of the fragrance either. The scent clings well, has a sensibly proportioned aura without filling the space, but becomes increasingly heavier, oilier, denser in the drydown. One might like that, but it also leads to an even stronger concentration on this oriental rose, which then appears quite sweet in the lingering base. All other ingredients can be imagined, but, as is often the case with the very complex Roja fragrances (which repeatedly remind one of 80s creations), are hardly discernible. Anyone who can differentiate more has my full respect. Whether one would want to deduct points from the fragrance because it offers no more than what is described above for the price also depends on the perspective of the observer. I personally evaluated it without regard to the price. However, anyone who wants to consider this for understandable reasons may need to reduce the rating a bit.

I saw him. I mentally circled around him, unsure of what to do. Good-looking, yes of course! But not a pretty boy! And looks aren’t everything, inner values and all that… And what if I make a little contact first? Just a glance? Friendly, but disinterested? Oh no. What if I embarrass myself? What if he looks away immediately? He might even laugh!

This week I tested Roja Taif Aoud in peace. Taif Aoud was one of those Rojas that particularly piqued my interest. This is partly because I didn't like Aoud very much, as the DNA has unfortunately been used almost inflationarily by other brands, and somehow the spark never ignited for me with the rose and oud DNA.

Hello everyone, In the last few years, I have really come across a lot of fragrances that play with rose - oud, and easily 90% of them are quite similar in that regard. And yes, this one is also among them, but certain things are said/spread that, in my opinion, only partially or not at all correspond to the truth! Which ones?

The Black Week and shopping addiction led me to a blind buy of my first Roja fragrance, Taif Aoud. Why this one in particular? To be honest, the bottle caught my eye, I saw the fragrance notes and even though I already own a rose oud fragrance - "Les Sables Roses | Louis Vuitton," I still wanted to have it.

Plush citrus musk. The musk is pillowy, downy, almost lactonic. It’s livened by pulpy tangerine, with sandalwood seeds. All this is married by a flutter of jasmine stars. It’s a smooth, slumbery caress of a scent. An ASMR croon that everything is going to be okay. I like it far better on my skin (leans tangy) than on fabric (leans lotion-y). Byredo has a body lotion called Le Chemin (that you can only waft at select “Luxury Collection” hotels), which is also a woody-citrus-cream. I was disappointed to find there is no Le Chemin perfume, but 001 Woman is my closest match yet. The most luxurious week of my life was a weeklong business trip where I roosted at the Josun Palace in Seoul. And I practically marinated in that butter. And, dear reader, some of that Luxury Collection lotion may have found itself siphoned into a few $1 travel containers... Mental Snapshot: A solitary wellness retreat, to a cottage of your choosing. Everything closes by three, but you want for nothing. The grocer at the sun-bleached bodega sees that you get at least two of her homemade sourdough loaves a day. You lay in a wildflower patch, curling snug beneath a marshmallowy duvet, and watch creatures shift in the clouds. You reunite with all your childhood imaginary friends. tl;dr: asmr tangerine

Loewe 001 Woman, as well as its male pair, tricks in the first few minutes or when feeling quickly on blotter or spray. Like its male counterpart, it interprets 2 olfactory tendencies that have proven strong - those of gourmands and white narcotic florals. So feeling quickly passes the impression of another super sweet floral to the La Vie Est Belle style of being. However, sprayed on the skin the sweet and sugary impression is very moderate and gives space to a shimmering citrus tone that makes a good link with the male version. The heart shows to be more floral and presents a delicate, fresh and slightly green jasmine, something half springy in its aroma. The musk and wood base of the masculine is reinterpreted to give a more gourmand connotation, with an accord of sandalwood nutty and vanilla nuances, something that softens the drier edges of the woody idea present in Loewe 001 Man. Like its pair, is delicate yet durable in its aroma and despite the gourmand connations is a scent that can be used on warmer days. The floral aspect may make it more daring for the male audience, but nothing that can not be shared or even mixed with the Loewe 001 Man to give a special and different touch.

Musky, creamy, milky, with a gentle sour twist from the sandalwood and a faint coarseness from the pepper. Mellow sillage – I can feel it when I move my arms, but it's pretty airy and soft, and never strays far from me. Maybe half an arm's length? My partner had to come up to me directly to notice that I applied something. But that also may be because I'm testing it from a dabber miniature (the miniatures are super cute by the way, 10/10, I wish I could own every Loewe perfume in a teeny tiny 7ml bottle) instead of spraying like I would usually do with my testers. It also may be the reason why I don't feel much citrus or jasmine in it? On me – it's all about musk and milk. When I concentrate on it, I can easily imagine the "linen" note listed in the pyramid – slightly coarse, yet soft and airy. But when I enjoy the scent without looking at any accompanying data, to be honest, all I can think of is Actimel. The probiotic yogurt, unflavored one. Its soft subdued sweetness, gentle and playful sourness... The smooth milky taste paired with a peculiar consistency – sleek and uniform, yet somehow delightfully textured, like the feeling of your bare feet sinking into very fine grains of sand (ㅅ´ ˘ `) Takes ~2 hours to completely settle on skin. Softens. Fuzzy musk with a light milky sweetness. In another ~2 hours dries down to the base. Creamy musk, same kind as in 001 Man Eau de Parfum . For ~2 more hours it lingers, then completely fades away. I don't know what else to tell you. It smells like Loewe's white musk and unflavored Actimel. Is it fair to slap a "gourmand" label on it at this point? Also, how do I stop myself from wearing it every day? It's super adorable (*´▽`*)

I don't know if my skin reacts differently (but I believe that every skin reacts a bit differently to various fragrance components). However, I find Loewe 001 Women to be wonderfully soft and woody after multiple tests... I don't perceive any mandarin in the top notes, let alone pink pepper. And that's just fine. After a while, a deep, slightly sweet scent emerges that lasts a long time. As for the linen accord, I don't know how it's supposed to smell. The fragrance gradually becomes softer and lasts about four hours with a small sillage before it slowly becomes very close to the skin. All in all, for me, it's a scent that makes me feel very comfortable during the day.

So my dears... with an order, a sample of this fragrance was included for my better half, for the lady and the gentleman. Basically a gender set :-) One thing should be said right away...both fragrances fit! Dave currently has it in his collection, what a coincidence I thought. So yesterday I did the first test. I looked for a free spot ;-) on my still fragrant skin, also on Mrs. Smith. So I sprayed 001 for him and her and tested it. Not bad was our first impression. But other fragrances were also present. One couldn't form a judgment like that. So today I conducted the ultimate test...and found it good...but... the woman has a small range, you have to reapply often, but it smells delicious and is also suitable for everyday use! The man is also a very good fragrance, has a greater range, so it lasts longer. He is also absolutely suitable for everyday use. Now we are already at the topic, because Loewe has composed a fragrance here that is supposed to please and it does. A fragrance without many edges and corners, a fragrance that could also be sold at Douglas, without any problems. Sometimes when I smell on my wrist, I think of Armani's Eau de Nuit, although I wouldn't see it as a twin, because 001 has several facets compared to EdN. 001 is a warm and rounded fragrance. Round...clear...without edges and corners ;-) In this case, the roundness is not only warm but also very soft, yet still masculine. But completely suitable for every day. You definitely can't go wrong with this, no one will wrinkle their nose like they might with some niche fragrances. With both 001s, you can spray until the doctor comes, you can go out into life, right among all the people who might otherwise look at you strangely. So it fits every business appointment, which a Black Afghano certainly does not. I didn't mention the BA without reason, because at the end of the fragrance development, a bit of the BA appears in its most harmless form. The woodiness comes to the surface, very gently, tolerable for everyone. Of course, you need imagination to realize that. The women's fragrance is softly alluring, feminine. Mrs. Smith associates it with Cleopatra and then it becomes exotic, sometimes almost coconut-like. Conclusion: The fragrance development of both fits the pyramid. Both are fragrances that fit into any collection. Both are fragrances with which you can't go wrong at all. The price is also right. So if you are looking for a fragrance for a "Douglas buyer," but still want to give them a niche fragrance, you hit the jackpot here. Let it smell and happy holidays wishes Mrs. and Mr. Smith

The scent came to me as a travel spray in a beauty advent calendar. The smell is fresh, clean musk, fresh laundry, feminine but not sweet. Similar to For Her Pure Musc Eau de Parfum , however, the longevity and sillage are a notch better… Why is a purchase out of the question?

All the incessant bleating about this not being anywhere near the original etc, etc are annoying! I snapped this up when brought in by an independent fragrance vendor (it won't be released where I live for months yet ... if at all) and all I can say is " Welcome back M7!!". Oud Absolu is every bit as fabulous as the original M7 was ... perhaps a little more refined and not so 'in your face' ... but it's evolvement has left it pretty much unscathed. Streets better than the reformulation of the clear bottle (I only ever had one bottle of the original) ... let's just hope that this time, it gains the following it deserves. Look no further if you hanker after the original ... Oud Absolu stands it's ground firmly in the face of adversity!!

I had the first M7 (2002) Eau de Toilette original, the scandalous one with the solid dark brown bottle, and for me, it was love at first sight. If I think of it, I can recall its smell in my mind. Then all traces disappeared. It seemed abandoned, but no, they relaunched it with new packaging. I have one of the last batches, the one with the clear glass, and I'm unsure if it smells like the one covered in black. Wow... After the first spray, I take a while to recognise M7 in this potion. I miss that familiar accord of citrus and velvety sweet resins in the opening that characterised the OG. Instead, an explosion of herbaceous, medicinal, and syrupy undertones comes to my face. The scent of hay, and dry grass, with dusty and mineral undertones. Though it mentions at least three different citrus fruits, I need help distinguishing them clearly. A caramelised citrus peel may fill the air. To a certain extent, I get a thick and alcoholic aroma, which is still pleasant, unique, and interesting; indeed, it is very pleasant. However, it deviates from the original M7. If the citrus accord is tamed, the smoky of an incense-like oud in the background is already evident. After a few minutes, the initial outburst subsides, and something darker, more aromatic, and thicker oozes from my warm skin. There is a lot of fragrant rosemary with a strong balsamic but not too mentholated component, which blends with oud wood and patchouli leaves, the latter with chocolate vibes. M7 was, and still is, a clash of Western and Eastern cultures, where classic woody and spicy aromas meet mysterious oud. We are not dealing with a true oriental oud with faecal or barnyard edges, but rather a cleaned and purified fluid that adds darkness and depth with elegance. M7 Oud Absolu is one of the best oud fragrances among designer ouds and could be the first step to familiarising yourself with the oud note. You get used to it quickly, and then it creates a sort of addiction. The fragrance becomes incredibly balsamic, sweet, and sour in the middle stage. When the dry-down comes, all the waxy and resinous components take over. The leathery and powdery aromas of cistus and myrrh's sweetish and creamy ones dominate the base notes composed of moss, a salty ambergris-like amber, and a slightly earthy vetiver. And it is in this phase that I recognise many notes reminiscent of the first M7. They are sweetish, powdery, woody, amber accords, with that malice given by the touch of smoky oud wood. Let me insist that the M7 Oud Absolu takes the oud to a level that doesn't flaunt the sometimes cranky putrescent character but alters it with an understated mix of sweetness and mystery. A touch of smokiness appears in the final stage also. Hence, M7 Oud Absolu is amber, woody, slightly earthy, and somewhat dirty. Not linear; it changes quite a bit from top to bottom. Compared with the OM, it does not have an impressive performance on my skin. It is a fall and winter cologne, better for late evenings and nights. Indeed is a great frag, even in its reformed state. I'm basing my opinion and review on a bottle I've owned since January 2019 (BC 62PN01L, 2017-11). -Elysium

Only ever tried this iteration of M7 so i have no refernce re original. This is one of the best smelling oud-dominant designers on the market. I especially love how the citrus-sweetish, chinotto opening develops into a patchouli/oud cooling middle. The trick is that it opens warm and develops to almost a cool minty patch within the first hour. This i think makes it not just a cold weather scent, but wearable in most spring weather. Eventually it transitions to a lovely syrupy, myrhh and oud combination. It is a beautifully composed scent given the minimal accords used. The one let down on my skin, is that i am luck to get 6 hours maximum longevity. Thus sits close to skin from the outset, and i find myself craving to get wafts of it as the day progresses. At this point, i'll keep it in my collection because it lasts long enough for evening wear, and reasonably priced enough that i am not going to be stingy with sprays.

I went out of my way to order this considering it could be 6 to 8 months before it's arrival here in the USA, as we saw with La Nuit de L'Homme Le Parfum. I was hopeful that Oud Absolu would be a deeper interpretation of M7. Instead, I found it to be a reformulation in a classier bottle. If you missed out on M7 when it was widely available, this will suffice. Does it have that sillage, projection and longevity it's ancestor had? No, but still a nice fragrance. Think of M7 restrained, harnessed and tamed. Is it necessary to chase after Oud Absolu if you've already obtained the M7 original? No. Unless you're a serious bottle collector. I'll conclude this by saying, I believe the M7 original deserves the title and packaging of La Collection Oud Absolu.

Wonderful designer fragrance. It's in the same level or even better than other oud fragrances that are "niche". But i have to say actually this is not a main oud based fragrance. It's a well composed one that plays with patchouli, incense and oud, and also this has a nice resinous smell when dries down. Sometimes i smell a cherry syrup that's not comfortable to my nose. Sillage, lasting power and projection are medium-high.

During the years old M7 had to regulate his diet to maintain the line and lower the calorie intake. This new M7 is thinner, but keeps the old vibe. Compressed, like the CD quality of sound is compressed in mp3 format. Oud Absolu opens with mandarin, and even some rosemary of the original. Patchouli and oud give some robustness.

Stunning Fragrance ! Elegant, Classy, Sophisticated , Modern , Complex and Unique. In my opinion, A MASTERPIECE with High Quality Similar to Niche Perfume that has well-blended composition and Lovely balance between Patchouli , Myrrh and Labdanum. I love The Myrrh note in this Scent.

Perfume versed in the oud, spectacular, I love it, and if its performance were greater, it would be a perfume of 10. The beginning is an explosion of forceful oud, leaves no respite with its effluviums of powerful, medicated and dirty wood.

I had very high hopes for this fragrance because of all the praise the original M7 was getting in online fragrance reviews so i blind bought it since I love the sweet resinous amber and oud style of fragrances.

As soon as you spray this on you get this sweet floral smell. The scent changes alot during the initial spray because it becomes an mess of sweetness and floral which is rather good. The musk and cashmere starts seeping through the floral rather fast and you get this musky, cashmery smell with hints of oud. The cotton candy which was rather an interesting note to combine with oud has yet to arrive. After a little while the sweetness has finally come back and blends beautifully with the oud making this a rather woody sweet scent at the moment. The woodiness starts to disappear and the sweetness combined with the oud stays. Overall this fragrance really takes you on a fieldtrip. From a newly blossomed garden in the spring to a walk through the forest. An easy 9.2/10 smell wise.

There is only three scents in Gulf Collection which is not discontinued and this is one of those. Qatar smells rich, expensive and gasoline like blend with the key ingredients: Peach, Pear, Candyfloss, Casmir Wood, Aoud, Saffron, Labdanum, Musk. I get leathery vibes as well from Labdanum. This is like driving a luxury car with a finest leather seats and a huge tank of gasoline and the next day you have to fill the tank again. I really don't know from where I get that gasoline vibe and I get the same from Sultanate of Oman but it's a pleasant one, somewhat abstract feeling. From the key notes you can get wrong kind of vibe of this juice because this is not so sweet imo and this is rather a dark and mysterious - and very complex. Oud as a note is very unique as well bringing a depth to the fruits. All those ingredients anyway has an important role here and without flowers in the heart notes this would be boring I think. I have to mention Cotton Candy since I like the idea a lot, it brings a distinct and intoxicating character to the juice and with that note is nice to add the sweet accord in the next level if wanted. In the dry down this amazing V12 sport wild beast turns a little bit more tame version but the smell itself doesn’t change so much. And it lasts and lasts. Like all Rojas this is so well blended that it’s really hard to separate all the notes. I love this scent a lot and it’s definitely a backup bottle worthy for me like FM The Perfume as well. And if I spray once Love Don't Be Shy Perfume sugar overload on top I’m in the heaven! I have written of layering pairs with Qatar. I will write a blog of it. This beautiful scent, absolutely unisex but sweet. It creates amazing bubble around you. Honestly I would need another bottle since I'm afraid to wear this as much as I wanted to. Top:  Citrus Notes Middle: Rose de Mai, Jasmin de Grasse, Violet, Pear*, Peach* Base:  Clove, Saffron*, Patchouli, Cedarwood, Casmir Wood*, Sandalwood, Aoud*, Candyfloss Accord*, Benzoin, Vanilla, Orris Sur Cèdre, Orris, Styrax, Birch, Labdanum*, Ambergris, Musk* *key ingredients This perfume you have to experience yourself but sample it first!
