Suitable for every season and every occasion but performance is weather -dependant. Performs CRAZY in spring and fall, 12 hours with 4-5 sprays on my skin with quite impressive projection. Longevity is worse in winter and summer but still good. Price is the only reason for me, 110 dollars for 60 ml (in my country) is a HARD pass, even though I really enjoy the scent. If you can find it for a nice price, don’t miss a bottle.

Smooth lavender, synthetic apple, and sweet tonka beans. Smells like fresh laundry sanitiser. All season, signature scent worthy. More mature and dressed up than EDP. I personally rock this as a gym scent with an all black fit in winter. There's a nice dose of sweetness in here, and it makes for a good fresh, sweet scent for colder weather, as for hotter days though the sweetness can easily become too cloying. Performance is decent. I get around 5hrs of projection with 6 sprays. Quite easy to get nose blind to due to the aldehyde dominant dna so I suggest avoid spraying the front of your neck or chest. Sillage is a weird one, the projection is quite good but the fragrance is so aromatic and airy its hard to pick up on especially outside, but its also potent enough where you don't want to overspray indoors.

So I bought it IMMEDIATELY. I absolutely LOVE the EDP version, so it was a “no brainer” for me. I grabbed it online, and picked it up, curbside. Now the scent itself? Scent wise, I think it’s great. The apple-esque opening of the EDP on steroids. Very sweet, and full of dark depth. I feel a similarity to the Eros EDP in the mid notes... just erase the minty notes that Eros has, and that’s what’s there. Projection though, is VERY close to skin. This is very disappointing, considering we’re living in a time where wearing masks is mandatory. No one is going to pick this up wearing a mask. Sillage is affected by this as well. This doesn’t say that this doesn’t have longevity, as it lasts on the skin; the problem is, is that it’s ONLY on the skin living... and for $150, you’d expect more. So yes, I think the scent is great, but would I recommend it to anyone? No, I would say grab a bigger bottle of the EDP... Hell, I think I AM going to, before it’s reformulated.

As a fan of YSL Y EDP ,the apple dominating synthetic release of 2018 had me excited for a parfum release with my hopes high waiting for a stronger and darker scent (especially when i saw the black bottle my expectations were really high).When the time came to smell this thing I was shocked ,I was hoping that what I smelled was a mistake ,but no it was really true. A shower gel ,basic ,run off the mill concotion that was mediocre from the time it was sprayed till the time it faded .It actually has 0 character I can recall at least 10 shower gels that smell just like it .Hell, it even has less character than the edp which i thought was pretty much impossible.There is no way to describe this scent because there is nothing to actually say ,apple is still there,sage is still there its just just more generic. Longevity is great i guess it lasted for like 8 hours on my neck i could still smell it ,but no one around me could ,unless they came close to my neck.Thats all I have to say YSL Y Le Parfum most dissapointing release of 2021.

You get a deeper, smoother, and more refined and gentlemanly scent than the Y EDP. You get that fresh sweet apple vibe that comes across as fresher, more mature and an elegant take on the Y DNA. Then dries down to dries down to a warm and sweet vibe that doesn't project as loud as the EDP but still get a nice scent bubble around you. Lovely fragrance.

I've gone on such a journey with this old bottle of Y Le Parfum. Let's start with the fact that I got it by mistake: they literally handed me the wrong box at Sephora when I was really into Y EDP and I just rolled with it. (Don't do this, by the way.) Since then, I've mulled over exactly what this thing is. Is it a green apple-aldehyde fresh scent?

YSL Y Le Parfum is an absolute banger! It exudes a strong and assertive masculinity, while also maintaining a refreshing and invigorating aura. The synthetic elements, far from being a drawback, actually contribute to its unique appeal. The combination of apple, grapefruit, and lavender creates an irresistibly pleasing and revitalizing scent.

Strong sense of freshness with rapid opening that calms down after a while and becomes more sweet without loosing its' clean character. Seems very strong at the beginning but unfortunately the silage is not as much as it promises in the opening neither the longevity.

I thought that being that it's a parfum it will perform, boy was I wrong!!! It lasted on me for about 4-5 hours, even on clothes. I smell the apple, ginger, lavender, patchouli, and hint of cedarwood. The EDP was a way better performer, lasting at least 7 hours on me. Yes, the Le Parfum is a more mature fragrance, but I'll stick to the EDP and wear it independently.

The cremiest, sweetest and most feminine of the Libre line. I wasn't all that impressed by the original, it was too much of a clean, laundry-fresh scent for me, but Le Parfum and Intense are beautiful perfumes. Not a big surprise for me, as I generally tend to enjoy the night-timey, wintery flankers of designer fragrances more than the pillars (but of course there are exceptions to the rule!). This is still unmistakably a Libre flanker. The signature accord of orange blossom, bright vanilla and lavender is still there. The lavender is more clearly defined and shows a little bit more of its herbal facet than in the original, but less than in the Intense version. The vanilla is stronger and warmer, and while I don't smell a lot of honey here, I think the honey note plays a crucial role in warming up the base. It makes the scent sweeter, deeper and not as sterile as the original can be. The saffron and ginger are very subtle, so this is not a spicy scent. I think I can smell a bit of ginger, it adds a hint of bracing freshness to balance the sweeter notes, but I honestly wouldn't have thought of ginger if I never saw the notes list. I get beautiful wafts from this, they almost smell better than the scent directly on the skin. The longevity is good, too. For a long time I was craving to have a Libre flanker, but couldn't decide between Intense and Le Parfum. It doesn't help that they're quite similar to each other. After testing them again and again, I finally went for this beauty, I just found it a bit more fitting for myself. I think I'll wear this on many occasions around the year, except of course in the heights of summer.

This version is Libre is closest to the Intense version, but with a noticeable kick of spice and citrus, and with the thick drizzle of honey on top. It’s SO delicious and it’s easy to see why this gets all of the amazing reviews that it has. From first smell, this and the intense smell almost exactly the same, and I actually almost dismissed this one because of that. But, I gave this one a proper wear and then learned that the Le Parfum and the Intense are not that similar at all in the dry down. Libre Le Parfum is a heavy hitter fragrance that is most suitably worn in the fall and winter, and can be worn on spring evenings when it’s still a bit chill at night. This one does not require over spraying (really, none of the Libre line does, but this one especially), and can easily fill a room. This is a head turner and show stopper, and definitely gives man eating vibes. It’s super sexy, so be aware of when you are wearing this out. The sillage / projection is loud and the longevity is great and long lasting. As Libre Intense is my favorite out of the Libre line (and of my favorites in general), this Le Parfum is probably my favorite after the intense. Warm spicy accords are up there with my favorite accords in perfumes, and I’m quickly learning that I love saffron and ginger in my fragrances. YSL did a great job with this flanker. I did however declutter my bottle because I found it was a bit too sweet for my liking. Still an amazing scent though!

From the first blast this is an elegant and very pleasing lavender vanilla aroma. It's very strong at first, but mellows out nicely. The impression it gives is luxurious and upper-class. I can definitely see why people say this is the fragrance for a woman in the board room. It will likely not offend anyone at the office and will make you smell like you deserve that six-figure salary! Sillage and Longevity are also great, so you get your money's worth. That said, there is something generic in the "DNA" of this fragrance. It smells like a lot of the mass produced crowd-pleaser fragrances that you'd find at the Macy's counter. It doesn't stand out as anything creative or groundbreaking, but most people just want to smell amazing, not necessarily original. This is a safe blind buy.

Libre Le Parfum by Yves Saint Laurent is the latest flanker (2022) of the well known Libre line. This perfume is bright in the opening, with a floral heart and a delicate lavender, that is barely there, drawn into sweet vanilla and tonka touches. If you are interested into hearing more details about this perfume, please watch my review on Youtube.

The opening notes immediately tingled on my skin announcing the presence of ginger and saffron. The floral note still dominating the scent but this time around layered with syrupy honey. I much prefer this version over Libre Eau de Parfum . While it still feels floral and sweet, it doesn't feel overdone. However, the scent can become quite 'full' almost cloying at one degree if you are not careful with the number of sprays. It also weirdly smells delicious, thanks to the honey note that gives it a slight gourmand touch. I can definitely see myself spraying this on. true, it still leans slightly toward feminine side but it can dubiously transform itself into unisex territory, at least to the untrained nose. The sillage performs well on my skin and the longevity is impressive. I’m genuinely surprised by how well it blends with my skin chemistry. This version steps into more mature territory, freeing itself from the prominent floral chains that held the previous version to an obviously feminine-leaning scent. This time around, it finally walks the lines between masculine and feminine. I wish YSL would dare to fully live up to its name by officially liberating this scent as a unisex fragrance rather than boxing it into a specific gender.

I need to go back and test this again because I tested it on skin after several fragrances. I was admittedly a bit fatigued. Of everything sprayed on my skin, this was the scent that had the strongest sillage. The sillage is superb but there isn't much when you smell it in place. I was hoping for a nice vanilla to appear but all I could smell was lavender.

Just like Gucci's Mémoire d’une Odeur, Libre is so eye catching that I have given both perfumes more chances than I should. I would love to have the two in my collection just because of how they look, but I haven't. I think myself more sensible than that. Last week I was at a YSL-Prada-Armani event and it was announced that Libre has now been decorated with saffron.

The gingery bergamot and mandarin is what immediately bursts forth upon spraying, and a lovely waft of soapy orange blossom and lavender. For some reason I don't percieve the honey note very strongly at all. The lavender seems to be notably less strong in this version that the intense version, which for me is a good thing.

After reading enough praise of the fragrance online, I had to try it for myself in the perfumery. Said - done. Only I had already tested my way through what felt like 20 fragrances that day and both wrists were already occupied. So all that was left was to test it on a test strip.

The new Libre is a poem. Honest, beautiful. Rich, dark, full, sweet, floral, captivating, sensual... I could go on like this forever. But one thing it is also: quickly rather quiet. And that is exactly what ruins our perfect love story.

Yes, the price is outrageous - $3,500. Yes, the whole idea is overblown - actual gold flecks, I'm told at the counter. Whether in the bottle or the actual liquid, I didn't get. I wasn't paying attention. My nose had taken over my brain. Today, clearing my desk, I came on the scented paper in its envelope and had to write a review because I'm once again concluding this is the best thing I've ever smelled. By genre it is both a proper chyre (bergamot, labdanum, oakmoss) and a near-proper oriental (bergamot, jasmine, amber, vanilla), missing musk. The chypre element is deepened by addition of the faux oakmoss note now in vogue because of EU regulations (patchouli/vetiver). I mixed both the pure chypre accord and the faux one during my on-going Learning Chypre sniff fest to experience them and what's here is authentic. The spice in Roja is delicious, the cedar entrancing, the florals an olfactory garden of sophistication. It's as if Roja Dove decided to take the best in perfumery and push them beyond magnificence. For 10 years this was Roja Dove's personal perfume. It wasn't on sale. Now you could still say it isn't really on sale. There was only one bottle at Neiman Marcus when I went there a day in advance of his visit. You have to order it online at his site or go to Harrod's in London and there's no guarantee it will be in stock, I hear. Roja perfume (which at the counter they called Haute Luxe) is the best of the best I've smelled in my two years as a perfumista. Wear it and be assured only a handful on the planet will smell as good as you. I didn't love love his other fragrances. Innuendo is my favorite of the women's line. Diaghilev is wonderful among the men's. But as soon as I get an extra $3,500 I don't need for anything else, I'm getting on a plane, flying to London, getting in one of those Hackney cabs and driving straight to Harrod's. They called him Professeur de Parfum during the years he worked at Guerlain. With Haute Luxe, Roja Dove proves he deserves that title. 4/19/16 The 7.5 ml Discovery Atomiser I ordered on the website arrived today and fully justified the price with its great beauty--notes of far greater quality and depth, a composition far more brilliant than any of the hundreds I own. Only two or three stellar vintages (Shalimar extrait, for one) are even close to the same league.

100/10 and every other word is unnecessary. This is a perfume that only after wearing it, you realize how much it justifies its crazy price. To smell on the hand or on a sniffing sheet - does not give anything. Wear it and only then will you know what quality is. A luxury perfume that can match any luxury event you have. I keep my bottle in the safe. true, the price is crazy, but that only makes this perfume unique. For me it's 100/10.

I went down to Harrods Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie and i tried this one. Was totally blown away by this out of world parfum. Yes, the price is very hefty, but the sheer quality of the parfum justifies the price to me personally, someone else may think otherwise. This parfum reminds me of the movie 'Perfume The Story of a Murderer', underrated classic must watch film.

I put my nose to this perfume for the first time in Dubai and I want to say that I have never smelled anything like it. My friend and I wore it to a luxury bar and restaurant for the first time and the experience we had with the scent will never be forgotten! After this experience we simply bought a bottle and to this day we are wholeheartedly in love despite the high price. true, the price is very high for this perfume but to try it you have to wear it and really feel how high quality it is! I can really understand why ROJA DOVE chose this scent for him! For those who find the price too high for the perfume and cannot afford to buy it, the RDHP15 can be enough! For me 1010 THE BEST !

I bought a little 3ml sample that I’ve been wearing around to get my thoughts. It’s a bit of a hard scent to wrap my head around because I’ve never smelled anything like it. It’s quality is apparent the moment you catch a wiff, the material’s chosen are of the highest quality and the blending is superb. The scent, to summarize it, is very mossy, spicy, slightly sweet, salty, slightly floral and very old school. This is not for a man under the age of for 40-45…it does not smell youthful or playful in the slightest bit. This is for someone successful, sophisticated, well put together and confident. This definitely isn’t for women either, it’s too masculine. It’s a beautiful scent, i enjoy wearing it, but i feel as though it’s wearing me…I don’t feel “comfortable” smelling like this in public. I’m only 28 and I’m not doing the fragrance any justice. The longevity is nearly eternal but somehow doesn’t overwhelm which is interesting. The sillage and projection is always kept in check. No one i asked said it smelled good, everyone said it smelled “weird” or like an “old man” or like “an old lady”. Is it worth $3500 usd for a bottle? No…but if you have a lot of money to burn, why the hell not. This is THE endgame fragrance, there is nothing more opulent or outrageous out there.

Where do I even begin with this one… Probably the most regal smelling scent there is, and will ever be for a long time onwards. This perfume to me, felt like I reached full perfume climax when I got it. It’s undeniably french perfumery at its best.
I had a chanche to test this in Dubai Mall. I is poudre with lavendel and some eastern ingredients. The quality of the ingredients is really good. Not bad at all, but definetaly overpriced.

100 ml / converted to €2900. Malicious tongues claim that Roger Dove has lost his mind when it comes to his pricing policy, and with this, he is likely propelling himself even further into an abstract dualism of supposed genius and (well) madness. With Enigma pour Homme, he created a bespoke fragrance for me, I can truly say that.

I recently stood in front of a Roja stand. I'm not really a Roja fan, but I have to admit that it was quite impressive to be in front of all those luxury fragrances. By the way, I was with a nice perfume enthusiast who had dragged me to the Roja scents because she really wanted to try a few.

Almost €3,000 for 100 ml of perfume? That’s no longer just a statement, but an absolute challenge, if not pure provocation. For many, it may be a monthly salary, for some inhabitants of the world a yearly income, and for a select few, just a quick reach into their wallet or some pocket money.

7 Natural is a great smooth citrus which is also slightly ozonic/aquatic. At first it seems like a straight up summer scent, but it actually goes well for most seasons, probably due to the incense and woody vetiver that shines through after the opening. Excellent longevity and moderate projection - what's not to like?

Since I greatly appreciate the Loewe women's fragrances, I reached for Loewe 7 Natural as well. My dear friend is a Loewe native, and what could be more fitting than to dedicate a fragrance of the same brand to him. The addition of "natural" makes me think of a light, natural scent that would also suit my nature-loving Mani well. But that is an understatement. The pepper strikes harshly, completely overshadowing the yuzu. Fortunately, neroli counters the pepper with some coolness - a tough battle in which the pepper prevails. The incense gives the brash pepper a good smack, causing it to retreat to the corner, counting itself out. The smoky cedar can now shine, with slightly sweet, grassy vetiver in tow. I breathe a sigh of relief - but the sturdy pepper has regained its composure and rises again, albeit a bit battered, back into the ring. A combative, dynamic scent - without being sporty. This uncomfortable fragrance does not suit my balanced friend, who loves tranquility. Much more fitting for fiery spirits with a contrarian streak. The description on the cover "Human and Divine" is also contradictory, and the "Divine" part is quite exaggerated. A controversial scent that I cannot warm up to, and one that I cannot imagine on my dear Mani.

After I recently tested the extraordinary 7 de Loewe, which was only comparable to Cacharel's Pour L'Homme, it was a perfect coincidence to receive a small sample of the "Natural" version from a nice Parfumo member. Finally, a different flanker name, no Light, Sport, or Intense. However, I can't fully believe the fairy tale of natural perfume. But that doesn't matter much, as there are hardly any purely natural perfumes these days. What’s important is the scent itself: and it is a fresher, more wearable version of the original. Almost everything I wrote about the original applies here in a diluted form, just much brighter and with a fresher undertone. If the original was too heavy and different, this offers a softened variant. Still, there are huge parallels, and it can hardly disguise its father. For 7 Natural is also quite far from the mainstream track - through resinous, piercing incense and a pine tree feeling. Only here, it is diluted and made juicier with the trendy fruit yuzu, a bit of pepper, and orange. It is still above average in dryness, though. Definitely a scent for eccentrics and gentlemen who swim against the tide and are a bit different. This number 7 is just a bit more cultivated and less stubborn than its angular ancestor. And also a bit more boring. Bottle: like the original, just lighter. Quite nice. Sillage: lighter, brighter, softer than the original and now more variable. Longevity: beautiful 7 hours show no summery light shortenings! Still not a top scent, and for incense fans, it’s hardly worth mentioning if you know the original - but objectively speaking, it is the slightly better, prettier scent for me, without completely denying its angular, futuristic incense core!

An interesting concept: "Loewe 7 Natural" contains exactly seven ingredients, of which six are of natural origin and only one synthetic (musk) had to be used. This aligns perfectly with my constant mantra that everything begins with the best possible components, ingredients, molecules; if you skimp here, you can orchestrate and combine as well as you like later on, "garbage in garbage out" applies nowhere as much as in the art of perfumery. So how does this Loewe product, which prominently features natural ingredients, perform? While the opening with bitter orange and yuzu is still quite one-dimensional (I almost would have said "artificial"...), screaming very citrusy-bitter, bright yellow, and very sour so that everyone really understands "fresh!!!", this initial impact quickly fades and then becomes briefly really pleasantly bright citrusy and light, but still with substance and body. This impression is beautifully enhanced as soon as the pink pepper joins in combination with a resinous-green frankincense; interestingly, I perceive these two together almost as clove plus nutmeg, they have such a spicy-green character, but that is also quite spicy-pleasant. The cedar note early on leads into the transition to the base, which then rounds off warm with musk and vetiver and lasts quite a long time. So does the "Natural" concept work? This has certainly not become a breathtakingly large, surprisingly impressive fragrance, but although it appears a bit watery or "diluted," this version shows itself to be, in my opinion, far better and vastly superior compared to the "normal" Loewe 7. The top note is much more natural, pleasant, and rounded after the initial attack, especially the heart note is significantly better, more harmonious, and "real." For a fresh, light, yet rounded summer fragrance with substance, "Loewe 7 Natural" is definitely a contender!

What a beautiful gem of a fragrance for men! Stunning! This was one of the first Eau de Parfum marketed fragrances for men back in 1995, and in no way does it smell dated now! It's sensual, sweet and exotic. This perfume has no sharp edges, completely smooth and sensual throughout. The fragrance itself opens up with zingy aromatic star anise and rich blackcurrant. It's completely beautiful. Followed by galanga and sichuan pepper, and drying down to beautiful tolu balsam and a deep, creamy, rich bourbon vanilla. Utterly intoxicating. Smooth and sensual, this is one of the best designer perfumes ever made for a man. You have everything you could want in a niche (e.g. a Serge Lutens oriental) from a well-known designer house. This is the YSL of the past, the one we all miss! You can still get this one as (thank God) it's still in production! I hope it stays that way. Easily one of the best and most luxurious for men out there.

As the name Opium suggests, this scent has something alluring and addictive in it. For an oldskool lover like me, it can cause an euphoric state of mind what I've never felt like before. If you had a chance to grab a vintage EDP bottle, do not hesitate to buy it. This was made in an era of perfume history which will never come back again. This 2006 bottle is truly a gem in my collection.

One of my favourite perfumes ever! The opening mixing the blackcurrant and the anise, and the heart with vanilla and amber are fabulous!! The longevity is not specially good. It is not bad but It is not already the beast that one day was. I think that the edp today id like the edt before but the smell is very nice and still today different and original. What is true is that for me It is not a perfume for everyday. Only for specisl occasion. I dont like It very much for nightout because i feel as i feel that the smell dissapear un contaminated ambientes, but is very good to go to some events overall at wvening- night. It is sweet but very spicy and a bit fresh. Almost unisex but more in the masculine side.

This masterwork, sadly not available anymore, will forever be among the very best cool-weather evening scents I've ever smelled. Blackcurrant is the star of the show, particularly in the opening. This is a dense fruity-spicy top in the fragrance. While it is a classic masculine scent, I feel like it could be almost a unisex option. There's no aggression in the spices, though the star anise really warms and sparkles in the development. As it dries down, the tolu balsam amber and vanilla develop more. Once it's been on your skin for a couple hours you really notice the difference between it and EDT. While the EDT fizzles out relatively quickly, the EDP doesn't back down. I couldn't call it monstrous performance but the EDP gives me at least 4 hours of strong projection, and another 4-6 hours of mild projection. This fragrance isn't the easiest to pull off in all settings, it's not one I want as an office/school fragrance. And even in more intimate circumstances, you need some confidence to wear the strong blackcurrant note and spices this brings. But this is a Mount Rushmore fragrance for me on date nights and special occasions. I count myself lucky to have a half full bottle and a sealed second bottle, they will be treasured.

Take the EDT and imagine it thicker and more concentrated (of course, you'll say, this is an EDP...). Unlike almost all other EDPs, Opium Homme keeps the pyramid of the EDT version almost intact, "simply" increasing the concentration. The result is a scent that's practically the same, but with more strength and more emphasis on the vanilla note (which is still a 1990s vanilla, so nothing modern or cloying gourmand). Compared to the EDT, it's certainly less versatile and perhaps not suitable for daytime use, but certainly fabulous for winter evenings. It's much more enveloping than the EDT version, more "cozy" as the English-speakers would say, and tends to be much warmer and spicier. It still maintains that very special contrast between balsamic/fresh/fruity and warm/spicy notes that I love so much and that made me fall in love with the lighter version. Well...

The EdT is more famous and successful, but this EdP is the real gold. Anyone buying Opium should search more carefully, because those who compare too late might end up cursing. The search is worth it, the EdP is the true hit, in contrast, the EdT feels like a car with only half a tank.

I have known Opium pour Homme since its release in 1995. I first caught a whiff from a friend and was thrilled. It must have only been a few days since it hit the shelves, and my friend was always the first to know about new releases. I was also allowed to try it, and he generously sprayed the fragrance on me.

Basically, I could largely compile this review from excerpts of my discussion of Guerlain's "L'Instant pour homme" (Eau de Toilette). Not that the Eau de Parfum of "Opium pour homme" is a fragrance twin; that's certainly not the case!

Once upon a time, there was an athlete - a soccer goalkeeper, to be precise. With Werder Bremen, he won the DFB-Pokal, and he participated in a World Cup and a European Championship with the German national team.

"That my pains had vanished became a trifle in my eyes;... here was the secret of happiness suddenly discovered, which philosophers had debated for so many centuries; happiness could now be bought for a penny and carried in one's waistcoat pocket, portable ecstasies could be obtained in half-liter bottles, and peace of mind could be sent by post." ..

The first time my friend let me smell this perfume, I put one spray of it on my hand and my reaction was: wow, this is the smell of heaven! It is difficult to analyze and understand the beauty of this perfume just from one spray on the hand... After a few months I wore this perfume and only then realized that I had to purchase it as soon as possible and that's what I did. luxury luxury luxury I can say that it is quite reminiscent of #Roja Haute Luxe for those who want to enjoy themselves for much less money. 9/10.

Aldehydic powdery ,with iridescent purple nuances of irises and violets,spices and sweet aromatic accords of benzoin and peru balsam,Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie 15th Anniversary embodies the luxury and the glam that the world renowned Roja Dove Salon de Parfums represents. A burst of luminous citrus notes introduces RDHP15 ,sparkly glittery aldehydes mingling with Roja' s favourite floral bouquet of irises,jasmines and lillies of the valley,accords of smooth suede,balsamic resins and spices embracing this gorgeous blend.Sensual musk,aromatic sweet tonka ,vanilla and precious woods seal the scent,resulting a wonderful,opulent and rich composition,just as Maitre Parfumeur Roja Dove has taught us. Feminine leaning to unisex,various elements in the fragrance making it a great choice for men too,RDHP15 is an absolute delight,a full bodied,warm powdery perfume with a strong and powerful personality.

This is the first scent I was exposed to from ROJA super fragrances! And this perfume simply took me to a place of angels, heaven! Luxury in a bottle of simply wonderful perfume! It opens with grapefruit, lemon, orange, aldehydes, and then it continues to be a scent I haven't smelled before! A perfume for connoisseurs! 9/10

A little bit updated Once again, First I do a simple approach to a very complex beautiful scent. So the most describing words which comes straight away in my mind: Powdery Fluffy Violets Mossy Vanilla Woody Top:  Aldehydes*, Lemon, Bergamot, Grapefruit, Mandarin, Orange Heart:  Lily of the Valley, Geranium, Jasmine, Cistus, Heliotrope*, Violet*, Peach*, Red Champaca  * Base:  Coriander, Ginger, Pepper, Moss Notes*, Patchouli*, Vetiver, Casmir Wood, Amyris, Sandalwood, Benzoin*, Vanilla*, Tonka Bean, Peru Balsam*, Orris*, Frankincense, Labdanum*, Ambrarome Absolute,  Civet*, Musk* * Dominant imo but all blended absolutely perfectly in Roja's style so nothing pop out. Most of Rojas are very versatile for me and it’s really difficult to find an occasion where I definitely couldn’t wear them but RDHP15 is one of the most glamorous, glorious, solemn and impressive for sure. There is a certain kind of sophistication in it but in the same time it’s enormous, regal scent. It’s charming, luxurious and glamorous, it reminds me of lavish velvet dresses from the Baroque era. Still there is some coziness in it, especially in the dry down. RDHP15 opens up with a little bit sharp sparkling aldehydes but quickly settles down into surprisingly warm scent and surprisingly since Violets and Iris are very present but not in a cold way at all - and still - the color of the metal plate and cap describes perfectly this scent. Sweetness of Peach and warmth of Champaca works together with amazing base creating that heavenly fluffy and powdery feeling which is palpable. Balsamic and ambery notes add not only the deepness but the warmth as well whereas Civet and Musk bring the sensuality to the scent. Special mention for the incredibly skillfully crafted mossy note which is present throughout the entire life cycle of the scent. This perfume gets clearly deeper and somewhat even more polished when time goes by. The longevity is easily 12 hours and it projects a lot. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

"I just looked at the pyramid; I'm feeling dizzy." This is how Gelis comments on my statement. That's understandable; the pyramid is just as rich as it is noble. In this, the Roja fragrance creations remind me of those by Annette Neuffer; she too draws from the abundance of her many fragrance notes. And yet "Roja Dove Haute-Parfumerie" once again shows that not a single one of the precious ingredients is superfluous. Each fragrance note harmoniously blends with the others, creating an exceedingly captivating composition from the first beat to the finale. Surprisingly, this time not with a grand orchestra: this Roja fragrance clearly walks in the footsteps of Romanticism! It is no coincidence that I referenced the "Loreley Song" in the title. It evokes words from Heinrich Heine, Clemens von Brentano, as well as melodies from Franz Schubert, Robert and Clara Schumann, and many others from this era. All were in search of the "Blue Flower of Romanticism"! (Years ago, I saw a blue, floating blossom on a long stem in the Victoria-Regia House of our Botanical Garden. It stood in a corner of the water basin, and a hand-labeled sign revealed its name: "Blue Flower of Romanticism"! Let us believe it - it would be too beautiful!) After an aldehyde-rich fragrance explosion from the many fruity-fresh and colorful fruits of the Hesperides - what a collection here - this fragrance creation leads us back to the flower fields of Grasse. Why wander to exotic lands? Not without, of course, picking the almost typical juicy ripe peaches with their velvety skin along the way. Not only the cheerful, tireless lily of the valley, but also the white and aromatic jasmine with its golden-yellow faces, has been invited again. The dark violet beauty of the vanilla-scented heliotrope and the cheeky violet may also join this fragrance composition. A bit more robust, darker, this summery bouquet is enhanced by the addition of the always slightly crumpled cistus spice and the strongly aromatic rose geranium. Through these two, this rather delicate bouquet gains additional depth. For the truly powerful-sounding fragrance finale, nothing was spared: spices like coriander, pepper, and fiery ginger meet rich, moist, mossy tones. This fragrance sequence corresponds excellently with the two earthy companions: patchouli and vetiver remind us of the fertility of the soil on which everything grows and thrives. Exotic woods and oils must not be missing here either. They alternate with the spicy-smoky resins like benzoin, frankincense, and labdanum, whose scent veil envelops everything that has come before. These slightly stronger fragrance notes are softened by the sensual warmth and creamy sweetness of vanilla and tonka bean; even tolu balsam has a wonderful influence on the fragrance progression. Finally, iris and musk wrap the entire artwork in a generously soft, powdery blanket. On this, the not entirely clean, slightly musty civet cat curls up and provides a certain animalic touch in the end. In all the romance: a little erotic thrill must be there! Too tame would be boring! At "Roja Dove Haute-Parfumerie," the many different fragrance tones are skillfully tuned to a magnificent symphony of Romanticism! In the harmoniously escalating flow of fragrance - from radiant fruity citrus freshness to the animalic of big cats - all strings are resonantly played, forming an extraordinary fragrance ensemble. Surprisingly soft for a Roja composition and yet marked with the familiar signature. Long-lasting fragrance luxury is offered here again and invites enjoyment! I am allowed to embark on this enchanting fragrance and sound journey through the filling of Azura. I thank you and savor every fragrant moment to the fullest! Who doesn't like to float on the wings of romance?

Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie has been a Roja that has interested me for a while. Chypré Extraordinaire, Fetish pour Homme, and Diaghilev were either too expensive, too heavy, or too old-fashioned for me, but Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie addresses these issues and is therefore very interesting to me.

First, I must admit that I have not been a big fan of Roja's fresh-floral fragrances like A Midsummer Dream until now. Usually, it was due to certain base notes like elemi resin or fir balsam that led the fragrance in an undesirable direction after a while.

Hello everyone, I would like to share a few words about "Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie | Roja Parfums". It had been on my list of fragrances that I absolutely wanted to test for a while, but samples were relatively rare and NEW it was "a bit" too expensive for me, and why do I need 100ml ... - my THINKING on that.

Roja is one of the most well-known niche brands and correspondingly expensive. Roja Dove was released to celebrate the 15th anniversary of the brand four years ago and was designed by Roja Dove himself. The fragrance contains 32 notes and belongs to the woody, oriental, and amber fragrance family.

To me, Aire Sutileza reminds me of the scent you'd want to smell like at the gym. Fresh, not too aldehydic, but clean. For me it is unisex but leans slightly masculine. I really enjoy this scent, but I don't think it would be a daily wear for me. I like it for the gym or for work, wherever you'd like to smell clean & polite, but not necessarily an attention-grabber from across the room.

This was a complete surprise. I was browsing the perfume isle and was about to give up after not liking anything I smelled when I found this beauty. It's currently my favorite. It's fresh and light and happy. I feel like wearing it all the time, no matter the occasion. It's taken me out of my perfume slump, after 2 long years of not linking anything new. I've also gotten a lot of compliments from friends and family when I'm wearing it.

Here’s a fragrance that, in my eyes, flies well under the radar: the Sutileza flanker from the Aire line by the Spanish fashion brand Loewe. Translated, this title means delicate air. You also get a scent here that is very airy and conveys that typical Spanish joie de vivre well, like most of this brand. Overall, this brand is very underrated, as you can see here: under 100 reviews and not many reactions to this fragrance. But that’s not always a bad thing, as it means you can enjoy a scent more for yourself rather than some hyped fragrances. I ordered several Loewe samples, and this one immediately caught my attention and stood out. This fragrance simply has something about it that I really like. It’s probably the lightness with this mix of fruits, flowers, freshness, and a bit of sweetness. If you want a pleasant, easy-to-wear scent with a compliment guarantee: this one. Don’t let the 7.2 scare you off, especially since not many have rated it. In terms of price, the Loewe brand is really good, especially when you order it online from the usual shops. Even though this is a designer brand, these fragrances are quite niche with a slightly elevated price. The charm of this brand also has a somewhat niche quality. I bought 100ml for under €90, which is absolutely worth it if you like those cheerful summer scents that bring a smile to your lips. The packaging is cool but also simple. A great large box in which the bottle sits securely. The bottles are usually uniform and have the standard labels and caps. Here in a lovely shade of green. The sprayer is very soft and nice. Even though this was launched as a women’s fragrance, it is also quite wearable for men. Provided that one can handle flowers well. Here you get a great mix of fruit, freshness, and flowers in the first hours. The fruity notes remind me slightly of Pacific Chill, without being a fragrance twin. The fruity notes are very lively and cheerful. You get pear, which isn’t too synthetic like many others with this note. Along with creamy-citrusy juicy mandarin and herb-sparkling blackcurrant. Flowers also come in early with lily of the valley and jasmine. Very summery-fresh flowers that are uncomplicated and accompany the fruits very well. The best part of this fragrance, in my opinion, is this fruity-sparkling vibe that will 100% bring many compliments. In the base, creamy-sweet musk comes in with a bit of pleasing and uncomplicated vetiver. Well-groomed sandalwood also comes through in the base. Everything is really very rounded and, in my opinion, there are no disruptive factors. The scent is predestined for summer days with plenty of sunny hours. It could also do well in spring and autumn. Performance is in the medium range, so I can absolutely recommend this for casual wear. In leisure, at work, or just for that quick mood boost. Longevity should be around 6 hours. The fruity-floral top and heart notes radiate well too. Overall, a great fragrance that could definitely be considered an insider tip. I love this carefree floral-fruity DNA with those Spanish holiday vibes. It’s worth at least a test.

…this fragrance! It is the scent that brings me the most compliments. Everyone really likes it. A fragrance that is so fresh and at the same time floral, suitable for any occasion (except the club), unobtrusive yet soothing. It feels like a hug from a freshly showered person who has a big place in their heart. Everyone should try this fragrance at least once - let yourself be surprised!

I actually discovered the fragrance on my vacation in Spain - and it fit perfectly. It feels like walking along beautifully fragrant blooming trees that give off a certain fruity freshness. You can clearly notice the mandarin and pear at the beginning. As the scent settles, jasmine comes through. I really like the composition, and for me, it’s a very special summer fragrance.

Amara is in her early thirties, calm yet confident, and surrounded by a shimmering elegance. Her style is clear, understated, and timeless - old money - flawless skin, a simple white shirt, golden hoops, and the subtle shine of well-groomed hair. A fitting example of the clean girl aesthetic. Naturalness with sophistication.

I did not like the original BO at all, found it screechy and basic and got rid of it fast. Le Parfum is the only BO flanker so far that I can see myself wearing. The notes are much smoother and gourmand without being overwhelmingly sweet. Tested at Ulta and was pleasantly surprised. On the blotter paper, it had outstanding longevity and made my purse smell soooo good! So, I got tempted and went ahead and got myself a used bottle to see if I could tolerate it on my skin. It's very nice, I actually crave it in the morning with my coffee, it’s such a delicious way to start a day! I think it's too heavy for office wear, especially in the summer, but I work from home and sit under the air conditioner, so it works for me!

In this take of Black Opium, there is a heavier delivery of vanilla and coffee with a touch of spice. So, there is actually less focus on the white floral aspect. This is the true sequel to "Black Opium", as it relates directly note-wise. Think of all the other flankers as fun franchises. Black Opium Le Parfum is deeper, yet softer. This often happens with "Parfum" or pure perfume concentrations. Parfum or Extraits don't always equal more projection, but will linger on the skin longer in most cases. I did find this to be a tad bit fleeting for a Parfum, but wonderful otherwise. I will be revisiting this concentration again to confirm. Despite this factor, it is still my favorite interpretation of Black Opium. I would put this in the class of Good Girl Supreme, which has a prominent coffee note as well. Le Parfum is darker and much more gourmand, but leans on the patchouli to give it depth and some sophistication. Now that Black Opium and Libre have reached their max concentrations, I am curious to know what YSL/L'Oréal Luxe does next.

The opening of Le Parfum is already sweet, with the vanilla being very present at the start. It does have a ‘quartet’ of vanilla notes, so, that’s understandable. But, early on I get a good deal of cinnamon in the mix. Much lighter on the green mandarin here versus Illicit Green, and even not too much of a pear influence. With that cinnamon, the vanilla, coffee, and general warmth this does have a coffee drink sort of vibe and not just beans. With that, the coffee note is diluted and isn’t as strong overall. To me, this is much smoother and less messy than the original Black Opium EDP. I’ve also seen Le Parfum get compared to Vanilla 28 by Kayali. Not really the same. That’s more linear, thinner, and has that brown sugar note which sets it apart from this. Plus, it lacks the same level of spice that is present with the cinnamon. That spice, will relent as we move along. The usual jasmine and orange flower floral heart will begin to emerge, but never fully overtake anything. It’s still a warm/sweet/spicy blend of the vanilla and coffee notes. Just, with a light blend of floral notes.

As much as I do not like the black opium series as much this one has a rather delicious evolution I must say. Tested by chance today (being a fan of olivier cresp I always test) I headed to this bottle that I did not know, exit the glitter, hello black bottle. First a direct sniff near the atomizer, hold it looks not bad, hop the mouillette, pschitt pschitt ... Hmm. Let's not see Mazal, one. Vanilla rather dark, hold, orange blossom .. Rather classic oh no wait it's spicy... cinnamon. Ok so in mind we are good I confirm. Then I say to myself go we test on skin (1 pschitt this time not crazy we never know) the start is identical then it arises the vanilla remains present but is adorned with coffee a little dry (patchouli?) It's sweet but not sickening, To my astonishment I did not smell this jasmine that usually bothers me so much. In short, a beautiful perfect that married my skin with a black softness. It s a win for me

Ok, if you’re not a fan of the original Black Opium then you NEED to try this. I don’t mind Black Opium applied sparingly for going out, but it’s borderline too sickly sweet for me and too many sprays actually makes me feel nauseated. This flanker is a lot more focused on the vanilla and feels a lot cozier and intimate. If the original is coffee, this is a latte with lots of cream! It’s not as overwhelmingly sweet as the original. I heard a reviewer describe this as a “politer” version of Black Opium and I agree with that. This smells like a delicious vanilla baked good on me. It also feels more appropriate for daytime. Perfect for a cold winter day.

... but that's exactly what I smell. Yummy almond cookies. A little citrus in the opening, with a sprinkle of cinnamon. This doesn't hang around for long, but ushers in a nice creamy cappuccino feel. It is SO rich in the heart notes. This is decadent in the most delicious way. Miles above the original Black Opium... Which I never cared for.

I think my nose is very sensitive to tonka in fragrances, and there is plenty in this Black Opium flanker. It is a little tobacco-y, a little smoky, and a little sweet. This isn't bake shop vanilla, but rather the raw stuff that still smells like it comes from nature.

The vanilla bomb of the Black Opium world. I get some pear in the opening, which is really pleasing, but then it’s vanilla all the way against a background of white flowers (primarily jasmine, to my nose) and coffee. It’s smooth, creamy, and delicious. I’d also say it’s quite a heady vanilla, thanks to the florals.

But I can't with this one, sadly. Yeah, it has vanilla, but it's boozy. It's not hyperfeminine. Cinnamon and pear in the opening make it quite pleasant, I'll be honest. I was expecting something very bad (as I'm biased against my mother's perfumes) but this one is a hit. I'm surprised.

Someone once said about Vivaldi: "He didn't compose 600 songs, but one song 600 times." In comparison to Vivaldi, I think that's far too sharp-tongued. He simply has a distinctive, marked style, but other composers have that too. Mozart is also relatively easy to recognize, but no one would dare to speak like that about Mozart.

Do we need yet another fragrance with tropical notes and sunscreen vibes? Yes, absolutely yes!! because we want to think about summer sea and freedom. if done with the right criteria can we say “Yupppie”! What is the right criteria for me? it's not a sugar explosion, it's not unbalanced, it's not gourmand, it's not powdery or a fluffy coconut donuts. It has a beautiful green opening that opens into a tropical floral heart made creamy by coconut. Yeap that’s all? Yes but what a beautiful sensation on your skin!! It looks a bit like TF's Soleil Blanc but in a slightly wilder way. More feminine than masculine Duration good projection lower due most Killian fragrances.

What to say? An amazing summer feeling will envelop you as soon as you will spray this wonder new fragrance from Kilian. The coconut note is absolutely predominant and it makes you feel on a tropical island. The tiare flowers and the vanilla give the fragrance that special summer vibes that you would appreciate in the months to come. The longevity is very good and few pumps will accompany you for an entire day.

Sunkissed goddess is essentially Eau de Soleil Blanc by Tom Ford on steroids. The coconut note is dominant, but undercut by a floral backbone and zesty opening. As a fan of the original Soleil Blanc and being disappointed by the fresher Eau de soleil blanc release, this has scratched that itch for me that I was missing, as the performance is beyond good for a summer fragrance. Highly recommend if you are looking for a fresh coconut - suntan lotion fragrance.

A release that was eagerly anticipated. Is it the scent of a goddess, kissed by the sun? Maybe. But perhaps it is just a promise, fleeting like a kiss blown into the air with hopes for more... The fragrance is tropical. Top and heart notes are easily perceptible. Sweet, floral, and with coconut.... Summer, sun, white sandy beach. Where would I wear it? In a luxury resort in the Maldives or during a vacation in the South Seas. After a day of sunbathing at the Waldorf Astoria Maldives, slathered in the finest sunscreen, I rinse off the wellness day, using the Frangipani shower oil and coconut shampoo from the luxury resort. I apply aftersun lotion to my body, the scent is delicate. I pin up my still damp hair with a clip and choose a long white dress for dinner on the beach. I apply SUNKISSED GODDESS, the fragrance fits so well with this fantastic vacation in the Maldives.... Conclusion: A well-made summer scent, fine and luxurious. Made for postcard-worthy vacations in life. However, I miss the special something that makes the scent a "wow" for me. Also, the price is too high for a nice summer fragrance. In everyday life, I lack the opportunity to wear it, as I am not lying on a dream beach every day and showering under a rainforest shower ;-). For anyone who wants to beam themselves into such a moment, or wants to have a paradise summer 365 days a year: A test is worth it! EDIT 02/2025: A small decant accompanied me to Maui, Hawaii. Now when I sniff it, it smells of sun, Kaanapali Beach, and a beautiful time! A leftover bottle had to come home - in memory of my wonderful trip!

What can I say, another fragrance that has blown me away. It starts fresh, exotic, and gains more sweetness from the vanilla as it develops. The woodiness becomes a bit more noticeable towards the end. A beautiful creamy yet lightly fresh summer scent. It really reminds me of a holiday by the sea. You get lovely sunscreen vibes.

Sunkissed Goddess convinces for various reasons. What makes this fragrance particularly special, in my opinion, is that despite its floral facets and a certain sweetness, it fits perfectly for summer. Nevertheless, this scent actually has a slightly fresh flair to it. This composition is extremely well done. I imagine a summer day at the outdoor pool.

Thanks to a perfume sample, I was able to try this scent, and I must say that it unfortunately doesn't blow me away. It's not bad. But "not bad" is unfortunately not "good." The fragrance smells like a softer, better-balanced version of Yves Rocher - Vague d'été Monoï or Guerlain - Terracotta.

Today the fragrance sample I got from a very nice perfumer has arrived. I was so curious because I really like coconut. The scent met my expectations regarding coconut. However, I have come to the conclusion that there are fragrances from other brands that smell similar and don't strain the wallet as much. I recommend testing it first.

I got a decant. In the opening, there’s citrus + soap, which disappear after 2-3 minutes. Then it becomes slightly sweet, a bit of coconut comes out, but it doesn’t last long. Gradually, the scent develops towards Terracotta Le Parfum by Guerlain, but fresher and soapier. Most of the time, I smell Tiare flowers, which I don’t like at all.

... that's how I feel when I wear Sunkissed Goddess . For a long time, I have been searching for just such a summer fragrance. A scent that has everything I need in summer. A fragrance for every occasion, for all events. I have many beautiful summer scents that I enjoy wearing, but not for every occasion.

The parfum version of MYSLF takes some cues from the original, but introduces a sort of "dirtiness" to the white floral accord that reminds me of Reflection Man or Guilty Elixir de Parfum pour Homme . It improves the overall effect, but for me, there's no reason not to just get one of those two, where the white florals are more pronounced and the effect is bolder. MYSLF "Le" Parfum doesn't really know what it is. A male-oriented white floral statement-maker? A bland and boring Amberwood™? It splits the difference without being very good at either. Still better than the uninspired utter tedium that is Myslf .

Smells like a blue version of one million to my nose, can wear any time and it's classy with a YSL french touch. I've seen some people say they smell cinnamon and others say absolutely not, but i also get cinnamon. Feels like a great mix of cinnamon/orange blossom/amber wood. I've been using it as a signature fragrance since i got it and it gets alot of positive attention. I used to own BDC Parfum and Y EDP and they're good and got similar attention but this beats them in that department. To me it also just smells better than any other blue fragrance at the moment. I'm comparing MYSLF to these fragrances because it has a very nice clean "shower gel" vibe to it, which i desire in an everyday fragrance. Tested both this and the EDP version before buying and the Le parfum is deeper and lasts longer. I think the EDP would only be better in very hot sunny days. Snobs on the internet that want to smell like ink and cumin won't like it, but if you just want to smell good i highly recommend you try it.

Great scent from opening thru the mid and the dry down EXCEPT. There is a funky smell in the dry down that’s in both Myslf Edp and MOR prominent in the Parfum. And I could not for the life of me figure out why women like this on men. To me it’s a barely noticeable but it’s there. Then one Saturday after a brisk walk with no deodorant or cologne on, I smell the same scent on me. This is crazy the smell from both myslf esp and parfum is a mildly sweaty man after a workout. This explains why I have women complement me more during the dry down. Don’t get me wrong, it’s not a crazy bad smell just a mild sweaty musky scent mixed in. I still think it’s a banger tho and it pairs well with other scents and that sweaty smell always comes through.

Is it downright bad? No. Is it good? Not quite. It just has no personality, nothing that makes you want to wear it. I find it soulless, with a dull opening made by orange flowers and pepper that is barely bettered by the base notes of amber. A totally forgettable fragrance that, on top of that, lasts for a quite short time with very little projection and sillage. It smells like a Jean Paul Gaultier that did not make it.

I am wearing a perfume oil version of this and I can get the orange blossom, a small dose of black pepper, jasmine (I think there must be, I think... with some cheeky musk), vanilla with a touch of amber and patchouli. The orange blossom here is heavy with a dash of jasmine and if I am not entirely wrong, I kinda get a Dior Pure Poison vibe to my nose. I have tasted Pure Poison before giving it out and loved it, so I am so glad that YSL is bringing back the memories. I love it myself. It's not super unique but it's a great scent to try out. You will get the laundry vibes for a bit in the opening which is attributed to the Orange blossom and jasmine. I don't know what the EDP smells like but I heard that owning both feels rather redundant so I think I will just stick with this bad boy. Also, I do think that this is versatile and can be perfectly be worn all seasons.

Been testing this one for some days now, and all I can say is that is just alright, smells good, doesnt smell cheap, but surely you've smelled something like this at least once. It opens with this white floral smell, that can remind you of some clean sheets or towels, that shortly after turns into a sweeter, richer aroma.

This is easily my new favorite. So many men’s fragrances are just too harsh or straight to smell like shower gel. If that’s your thing, so be it. However, for me this is a new masculine, one that is sophisticated and robust.

I prefer this to the original, as the scent profile is more suitable for special occasions. It is unique and not generic, but somehow I still find it boring to wear. I get why the brand created this though, it's massappealing and has some class at the same time, so I guess a lot of "one perfume guys" owns this.

Le Parfum is definitely better than its predecessor released last year, which, to put it mildly, was embarrassingly weak and I'm not surprised that it was met with such a wave of criticism. The new YSL perfumes have primarily got rid of the vulgarly artificial shampoo note known from the classic edition.

Pleasing everyone and being versatile is what this fragrance carries as its flag. It is a recognizable and clean smell. To me it reminds me of certain hair conditioners. Sweet, flowery and soapy to my taste. Quite fresh and clean.

ISOLA SOL Roja Dove 2024 People have seemed to have stereotypical expectations of this fragrance, which led to disappointed reactions. However, by taking a closer look at the notes and taking into account where the flowers in question grow and Roja's style of making fragrances, the description of the fragrance is not misleading. Tropical doesn't always mean splashy edible fruits (lastly in Roja’s perfumes) - here it means flowers, Ylang-Ylang and Jasmine, the both of them are growing in tropical regions. Roja’s style has always been classy and this scents fits into that style. Then we move on to the fruits. Fruity notes are in the opening and I know that many was expecting to detect them clearly from the scent but those you can’t find in that way. Roja’s perfumes are always complex and rarely you can separate individual notes. He uses a lot especially Peach, you can see that note in several perfumes. But can you smell it always clearly? Mostly yes, if it’s one of the middle notes but now all the fruits are in the opening. Honestly I was still expecting more than a subtle hint of Apricot and Peach as well and I really don’t know why. And to the third important point: the name of the perfume is Isola Sol but have you seen somewhere a mention of solar notes? I even saw someone complaining that the scent is not solar. Or what defines the word beachy? “Marine” is an accord but beachy is not, it's a term which people can imagine in very many different kind of ways. There is an idea behind the pair Isola Blue and Isola Sol. First one is the scene on the sea: fresh air on the yacht, refreshing Coconut cocktail and water with citruses in the glass (I don’t concentrate on that now more), and the latter one Isola Sol is the scene on the beach. Bright beautiful Jasmine scent on a sunkissed skin after the swim in the crystal clear salty water. Coconut - which here reminds me immediately of the sun - is lingering around mellow Jasmine and restrained Ylang-Ylang while Neroli brings freshness maintaining the concoction from turning sweet or creamy one. Jasmine is very natural and I love so much that there is not Tuberose at all. In this fragrance, the middle notes tell the most essential part of it. This lasts 6-7 hours an the longer it’s on the skin the softer it becomes. This is not so complex than perfumes in Roja’s other lines but it’s in the same level with those in Women’s Collection. It’s the quality which you pay for. Top Notes: Lemon*, Bergamot*, Mandarin, Petitgrain, Apricot*, Peach* Heart Notes: Neroli, Jasmine Sambac*, Ylang Ylang*, Coconut* Base Notes: Pink Pepper, Cedar Wood, Sandal Wood*, Amyris Wood*, Salty Accord*, Musks, Ambroxan *Key notes Thank you for reading, I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

neither the price nor the brand nor the users nor what is supposed to be special about it. I don't know who wants to adorn themselves with this brand in wealth... The whole brand seems to me more like appearance than reality. The notes do not indicate a masculine fragrance at any moment; the notes say white flowers with a lot of fruit. Nothing more, nothing less. And that's exactly what you get. It's interesting that men are more attracted to this brand; I hardly see a collection of women who own Roja. It must be due to the price. The souk is flooded with offers, mainly from men, what was the hope, guys? What it definitely is: rather feminine, reminds me in the first 10 minutes of fragrances from the 90s, opulent, striking, and extravagant. It somehow becomes slightly creamy and well-groomed. There are other ways to smell creamy and well-groomed. This is way too little for a new release from 2024. Is it pure perfume or Eau de Parfum or can it go? Hmm.. at that price, I expect a triple extrait! Something comparable exists with The Only One Eau de Parfum Intense Sorry for the harsh criticism, it doesn't happen often but this time it had to be said. PS: for me, there is no fragrance that would ever justify such a price.

On March 15, 2024, the fragrance could finally be ordered from Roja. The order went out the same day, as I am a big fan of "Isola Blu (Parfum) / Oligarch (Parfum) | Roja Parfums." I must admit that I had envisioned this wonderful summer scent differently. But as I have read here, expecting a hybrid of Pacific Chill and Virgin Island Water would absolutely not fit Roja Dove! However, we also do not get a classic Chypre here. I can certainly understand why the fragrance polarizes. It is simply not a typical Roja and also not a typically fresh, citrusy summer scent. However, I do welcome that Roja Dove is taking a different approach here. After all, he has created enough Chypre masterpieces! Here, you get a floral, creamy-powdery, slightly fruity summer scent. For some, the fragrance may not be extraordinary enough. But I believe that Roja has created a "sunscreen vibe" scent in great quality. In the opening, you get a fresh citrus note, but not as "sharp" as in most summer fragrances. The floral notes are also immediately present and remain dominant throughout the entire fragrance development. The apricot, along with the coconut, adds a very light sweetness to the whole. For me, these two fragrance notes are beautifully intertwined and not "overly present." The citrus notes fade into the background relatively quickly. Light aquatic notes and a gentle base of musk and woods round off the fragrance. The entire creation comes across as very elegant, soft, and clean. From the description, one can already see that the fragrance leans more towards the feminine side. The scent definitely needs the right wearer. I think the fragrance is quite pleasing and certainly wearable as a signature scent, but it is not a blind buy. It definitely fits better with a slightly dressier outfit, like a white summer dress or a white polo. The longevity and sillage are really good for this type of fragrance! Also, the scent is just right for its character. So, it’s not "beast mode," but rather elegantly understated. You will be noticed, and it lasts a good 8 hours on me. Lastly, a few words about the presentation. For me, the packaging of the fragrance fits perfectly. Watching the sunrise over the sea from an island. Capturing the first warming rays of the day, feet in the sand, while the waves gently awaken the senses. The "packaging" is reminiscent of the design of Isola Blu Parfum and is really very beautiful. The only connection I see between the two fragrances is the coconut note, which is subtly incorporated in both. Undoubtedly, they are both summer scents. The bottle and sprayer are typically Roja in the 50ml design and are a solid 10 for me. I had Isola Sol and Isola Blu Parfum standing next to each other, and it was simply beautiful. Almost as if Isola Blu Parfum got a "sister." Don’t get me wrong, the fragrance is great, certainly wearable by a man, but personally, I prefer to smell it on a woman. Feel free to test it and make your own judgment! Sunny regards, Micha

After Isola Blu Parfum , I was curious about this one. And what can I say, it’s a good fragrance. I see it more suited for women, as the scent screams very loudly of jasmine! The fruity top notes are only briefly noticeable and subtle. Many here are surely familiar with fragrances that smell like sunscreen, body lotion, or ice cream - this is one of those. A soft, white creamy scent. It doesn’t reinvent the wheel, but does it have to? I am a big Roja fan but I never defend him blindly. He has many fragrances that don’t appeal to me. Yet here we have yet another good example for our community and their expectations. Roja releases a rather linear and simple scent like this, and many say “he’s running out of ideas,” or “omg ambroxan, that’s not acceptable at this price point,” “the scent is bad” - just to name a few. And yes, the price is too high for me as well. But often these are the same people who rate a similar scent from other brands with an 8 or higher. A double-edged sword… But the fragrance remains solid nonetheless, and even a Roja or a Marly can be simple. Without notes of barn or leather. In my opinion, many too often let the price influence their pure scent evaluation, but that’s what the different categories are for ;) I find that this scent smells very similar to Surfing Puerto Escondido . That one also does well - maybe the price-to-quality ratio is better there, or you simply expect less from the outset. People should not forget what luxury is or which brands count as such (want to ;)). Now back to the fragrance: For anyone looking for a creamy jasmine scent with subtle fruitiness and noticeable aquatic nuances, this should be a good find. I would wear it myself, but I prefer to smell it on my girlfriend. The longevity was more than good for both of us, it was clearly noticeable for about 8 hours. The new bottles and the simplified design at Roja are not my thing. Nice to look at, but that’s all. Test it and form your own opinion - many here should do that more often ;)

Hello everyone, At this point, I just want to say that everything I share are personal impressions and thoughts...! The scent is good and will have some fans, and I think that's great, but... FOR ME, something is missing... something special. Why? When I have a fragrance (or smell one) and we are TALKING about a real premium provider in the high-end sector, I also have a "subtle" expectation. In the sense that, for example, I am looking for something "niche" like the Musk Aoud or something absolutely AMAZING like, for example, the Diaghilev Parfum or the Amber Aoud Absolue Précieux . And what do I get.... = sunscreen in a slightly floral, fruity, and naturally creamy scent. The fragrance is good, it doesn't blow me away, but it's what I expect at a minimum. I do NOT find it disturbing, bad, or anything negative..., it just doesn't grab me. And in my opinion, the biggest drawback is its price! Because for me, it is nothing more than the most expensive spray sunscreen I know, and I would never spend the price it costs. In that sense, I cannot make a recommendation here, just a REQUEST, please test it and do not buy it blindly. And now, have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______

I was very excited about this release from Roja, I was hoping for my summer 2024 fragrance. It is indeed a summer scent, but different from what I had imagined. The apricot and peach dominate the fragrance very strongly, making it smell mainly sweet and quite a bit less fresh. On 30-degree summer days, I think it would definitely be too sweet for me.

So....I initially read about the fragrance in a perfume group and thought to myself: I MUST HAVE THIS!!! So I ordered a decant and it was disappointing... A love only on the second sniff. I wanted to sell the fragrance and sprayed it on myself one more time and lo and behold.... I was thrilled. But why not the first time??? Who knows?!?!

Isola Sol reminded me right from the start of a familiar scent. It is the Soleil Blanc by Tom Ford. However, Isola Sol feels generally more finely tuned, somewhat more natural and rounded. Nevertheless, I have never been a big fan of Soleil Blanc, just as I am not of Isola Sol now.

So this scent is a luxury summer fragrance in a bottle. A lot of white flowers and Tiare!!! Initially citrusy and then becoming creamier. It is not that fresh summer scent, but rather leaning towards the creamy, slightly sultry direction. More on the feminine side, but still wearable by anyone. I will wear this fragrance all summer long.

Isola Sol what is interesting about this summer scent is the fruity, slightly herbal start. I had suspected that this golden sun island would kick off directly with coconut, Tiare, and solar notes, as that is part of a decadent beach holiday, but no... for my taste, it's quite fruity and herbal. Rioja is definitely not the bounty island.

Kilian BEYOND LOVE is touted by some as the best tuberose soliflore around, but I myself detect a significant jasmine note, in addition to a touch of coconut and a dash of dirtiness (apparently imparted by synthetic ambergris?). Although this composition is a bit thick, it is nothing next to Serge Lutens DATURA NOIR, which offers hefty doses of both tuberose and coconut and ends up rather clunky (and unwearable by me) as a result. I do not recall having sniffed another quasi-tuberose soliflore before, but maybe that's because there are so many much better and more complex tuberose-centric perfumes around. Perfumers probably figure: what's the point? Versace BLONDE is darker and dirtier, Robert Piguet FRACAS is brighter, juicier and more vibrant, while CARNAL FLOWER is vegetal and green. Next to such masterful tuberose perfumes, BEYOND LOVE seems somewhat opaque, linear, and unidimensional to me. Wearable, yes, but not compelling to my nose.

I'm a tuberose girl so for me this is pretty glorious. If you hate tuberose, you're not going to like this because its tuberose all day, all the time. I find it sweeter and warmer than Carnal Flower, and less formal than Fracas. The coconut helps to give it a more tropical edge and the green notes keeps it from being pure tuberose syrup. Sillage can be a bit out there...especially if you over spray, and the florals get bigger as they heat up to your skin. Being so strong 1-2 sprays is plenty. Longevity is good, for me its 9 hours. I like to use this to layer with other perfumes (half sprays only!!) This is one of those perfumes thats a tuberose lovers paradise.

This is probably the closest fragrance to the real flower , a lush and romantic tuberose on a sweet musky bed. It starts with a green vibe and has a lot of radiance but later on, as evolves on the skin, this tuberose shows also its dark side common for all tuberose scents starting to play the Diva. Beyond Love it a a modern interpretation of this flower note , away from Fracas and it’s quite easy to wear if you love this note otherwise if you want to start exploring tuberose scents is much safer to start with Do Son.

I feel once again compelled to defend the dreamy Beyond Love...:)= Such a beautiful creamy, silky-green Tuberose! It reminded me a lot of Carnal Flower or Do Son...maybe even a kind of mix of the two.. Although Beyond Love does have something uniquely special: the deep, animalistic amber note!! For my nose, BL is truly one of the best so-called Tuberose soliflores available on the market. Together with the two mentioned above and Nuit de Tubereuse by L'Artisan. BL also smells wonderfully natural, thankfully I can't detect any chemical cocktail like Fracas.. The Tuberose in BL feels buttery-creamy and initially very fresh-green. As the fragrance develops, the coconut gives its best...really a dreamy complement to the green-meaty Tuberose here! In this Tuberose scent, I can really smell coconut very distinctly. And yes, the Tuberose, together with amber, remains...well-preserved until the end; on me, the scent lasts about 5 to 6 hours on the skin, which is really long for me:)! BL even reminded me of another masterpiece by Calice Becker, albeit only fleetingly in the top note: Beyond Paradise...maybe because of the jasmine-amber-gardenia combo...simply intoxicating! Tuberose scents often polarize opinions/noses just like BL. For me, it has even become more: "Adoration" indeed... Thank you, Calice..

Boy oh boy, I was excited about the black Armada..the bottles are so grand and elegant...then this morning the first hit in the engine room with Love and Tears. By now, after Beyond Love, the Armada has a massive list to port..especially since I didn't find Back to Black that great either..but in hindsight, it is a true gem compared to this! Beyond Love hits you immediately with a jab - similar to Klitschko on Saturday - with a piercing apple-pear note combined with a very green floral note that seems to be steeped in alcohol..I briefly thought, well, I know this from Borsari Assenzio...but after 2 minutes that impression is gone, Borsari is too valuable and natural against this chemical club. So the tuberose will probably not be chosen as my flower of the year...it simply shapes the perfume very femininely..but the versions from Monsieur Lutens are simply dreamy in comparison. This is just shy of disgusting here...the saving musk I can only recognize lukewarm in the background..it has already hidden itself..beyond good taste, probably. I can't detect any coconut either...maybe dear Calice should ask Mr. Creed again how a beautiful coconut note is done. So with the next hit, this Armada is going down for me...as I am already pondering a bit about what the good, great reputation of this house is based on!!!

A reserved tuberose is actually a contradiction in itself. Tuberoses are usually loud, screaming, and overwhelming. In all the fragrances where I have perceived tuberoses, they have pushed themselves to the forefront as a central theme. I’m fine with that; I love tuberoses.

...what could there possibly be? Is it nothing? Absolute emptiness? Or even hell? After all, we all live through love. How can a place smell good that is outside, or rather beyond love - at least if we are to believe the name? Well, in Kilian's imagination, one enters this place through a green, herb-covered archway.

Oh, what a brew. I'm sorry, but has niche fragrance recently come to mean "Can only be smelled by 1% of people without fainting"? I had high hopes that the third niche fragrance from my sample pack would blow me away. In a way, it did, but unfortunately in a "knock you off your feet" kind of way. Upon spraying, BAM, full-on green notes hit you! Where's the amber?

Intense, intense, that's all I can say. Tuberose of the bad kind. What I mean is that the tuberose kicks in strongly, along with a medicinal herbal scent and artificial coconut. As far as I know, Kilian's fragrances are quite expensive. They should be. At least for this one, I wouldn't want to spend a cent.

Beyond Love A brief explanation on the side: I love flowers, especially tuberoses and jasmine; jasmine is one of my favorite flowers. I have 5 varieties of jasmine in my garden, including night-blooming jasmine, my favorite floral scent.

Launched this year just in time for X-MAS shoppers (I'm thinking of men who rely on an established brand-name and who know that "Opium" would do for their mother but not for their girlfriend), "Manifesto L'Elixir" is even more opulent than the regular "Manifesto". "L'Elixir" has got strong notes of jasmine and tuberose and a very sweet vanilla-pudding base teamed with loads of ambroxan. This "new" formula is all about creating more impact with even less ideas than last year. Picture someone who wears giant jewels, power red and bubblegum pink and adores anything with too much shimmer and gloss. At work, she is neither the team player nor the boss lady, but the office party girl. Probably a modern heroine of capitalism. "Manifesto L'Elixir" tries very hard to come across as glamorous and grown-up, but my appetite for original fragrances is not in the least satisfied.

I love vanilla fragrances. Hypnotic Poison, Addict, Sensous Noir… to dive into a wonderful, strong vanilla note is heaven to me. To sniff your sweater and sense the sweetness. That makes me happy. Sometimes the vanilla note is the only note remaining after many hours. Sometimes it is still strong. Manifesto l’Elixir is that kind of fragrance Manifesto l’Elixir is one of the best vanilla scents there is, in my honest opinion.. The note is there from the beginning to the end. The lovely citric notes start the scent and after a minute the vanilla bounces on the walls. The flowers are there but they only support the vanilla note. After a while the cashmere note melts into the scent. Just delicious. I have worn this for a day, gone to bed, woken up and the vanilla was still there. The bottle is a beautiful purple with golden details. Shaped like an hourglass figure you get the impression that this is a seductive scent fit for a visit at the nightclub. And it is. It looks amazing when the sunlight shines through the dense purple colour. 92/365

Manifesto L'Elixir is one the few modern-mainstream perfumes that has a unique and distinct DNA.
