It is a high quality vanilla creation, my main summery night time choice, extremely feminine, sensually and playful perfume that never fails giving me lots of compliments from men & women. I will enjoy it till last drop but I will propably not repurchase it, although it has the potential of a signature perfume. Bravo to YSL house!

For a good half year, the Eau de Parfum intense has been in my collection and has already been put to good use. However, it didn't lead me to comment on it quickly, as it is one of my absolute favorites and is more multifaceted than I initially thought and felt. Often, I feel fear and discomfort at not finding the right words to describe all sensory impressions as precisely and helpfully as possible. It borders on reverence; luckily, we are all subject to the same addiction and know the problem of not being able to "honor" one of our favorite fragrances enough and to appreciate its uniqueness. It was one of those unforgettable back-and-forth moments during the first sniff. This was during the pre-Christmas season, tossing money around in the city, with this scent in the back of my mind. The bottle immediately convinced me, as did the fragrance pyramid and the scent classification. The elixir seems to have quite a bit going for it. By the way, this is the first flanker of Manifesto. Unfortunately, I don't know that one yet; I don't see it as a disadvantage, as it allows me to approach the flanker as a completely independent fragrance. So I quickly visited the next perfumery and sprayed it on...Ooooaaaahhhh, what is that? A juicy, fresh mandarin greets me in a flash and is promptly washed away by a soft, creamy, powdery, opulent floral, oriental, gently spicy wave of vanilla. With wide-open eyes, I stand there, lingering with my nose on my wrist and probably looking like a paralyzed rabbit, but I don't care. Somehow, this feels familiar, the milky, gentle, and creamy accord. I experienced a similar blend of white flowers on the finest sandalwood with Dangereuse from Sentifique. The fragrance pyramids hardly resemble each other, yet both can boast their delicate, feminine melt. So delicious, so intoxicating and subtly narcotic, definitely distant relatives, those two man-eater fragrances. It was the latent similarity that forced the wicked want-it impulse upon me. Since then, the fragrance has been used quite often and continues to impress and delight me with its many passionate facets. As already mentioned, the short, fresh, orange-fruity opening. A cheeky contradiction in itself, as it is followed by a voluminous sea of flowers, crowned by an intense, simultaneously confusing transparent, woody vanilla. A feast for the senses, an adult, sensual, and demanding gourmand with oriental accents. Although it is quite a punch, it retains an airy lightness. Similar to a creamy calorie bomb that melts so outrageously tender and smooth on the tongue as if it were nothing. This unusual aspect makes the fragrance still wearable even in warm, humid temperatures. I like it very much and it continues to amaze me anew. The characterful heart note lingers very long on my skin and has quite a hefty sillage. The woody and spicy accents ensure that the strong vanilla note does not drift into the trivial and that the floral notes do not dance too rebelliously. The fragrance comes across as radiant and self-assured, feminine nobility and sophistication, passion, eroticism, and obstinacy, paired with oriental, spicy warmth without being strict. Along with a mischievous wink and a provocative but never cheap hip sway. My personal essence of the fragrance. The base lures with gentle, quiet, powdery, minimally spicy vanilla. The fragrance shifts down a few gears but remains ever-present. If somewhat more subdued. A woody, slightly smoky echo gives the base an exciting, dark twist. A fragrance that always suits me, never feels overloaded or trashy with appropriate dosing. However, it is best suited for evenings or going out. A true magnet for compliments, sneaking in with this scent is nearly impossible. When it comes to head-turning factor, it can easily measure up to Classique, Alien, and Code femme. It brings a hefty sillage and longevity and clearly has the potential to be a signature scent. Definitely a candidate that must always be in my collection. Due to its intensity, transparency, and richness of facets. I am curious how many bottles will fall victim to me and whether there is any other fragrance that will dethrone the elixir.

In this review, I will skip the backstory. Just like you. You skip any small talk and get straight to the point. Anyone who dabs you on their skin immediately feels your rich, warm, dense, and sensual vanilla kiss. For just a moment, bergamot and mandarin make a little bow together. One might almost think it's just to protect your victim because you immediately go all in. There’s no escape - your full-bodied, embracing nature completely captures one. Dense, opulent vanilla threads entwine me and won’t let go. If the name Addict hadn’t already been taken, it would surely belong to you. Captivated by you, I follow your further magic on my skin. Although I can feel you with every fiber, I still find it hard to put you into words. The rich violet of your bottle reflects you perfectly - you are for me Purple Vanilla Rain. I once danced in you and have not been able to forget you since. You wear your golden cap proudly like a crown, and rightly so. In the drydown, you envelop me like a protective cocoon. Only then does one recognize your gentle nature. To then say goodbye to you, melting softly after many hours - almost like a raindrop that evaporates before my eyes on my skin due to the warmth of the sun. You are wild, exciting, dark, heavy, sensual, and simply beautiful. What a pity that your creators have taken you off the market... Scent: Just as described, dense, opulent, sensual, dark, and warm vanilla magic. Sillage: Oh yes - it has that. One or two sprays are enough. Longevity: Very good - worthy of YSL. Bottle: Beautiful feminine purple dream. Price: It used to be reasonable... currently, I’d rather not talk about it.

I gifted this fragrance to my girlfriend just before Christmas as a little surprise for passing an exam. We had tested various scents, and this one was among our favorites. However, we could not have anticipated just how incredibly good it is. When she first tested it on her skin, it blew us both away.

I was initially skeptical because I find "line extensions" quite uninspired, but Manifesto L'Elixier convinced me right away. It is much rounder and more balanced than the original Manifesto. Soft and cuddly, but not boring.

..., still quite early, everyone in the house is still sleeping, even the dogs don't want to go outside. No wonder, it's gray, wet, the black ice from yesterday has thawed overnight, one doesn't want to look out the window. My olfactory perception is still unclouded, I haven't even had a coffee yet. I love this morning tranquility when I seem to be alone in the world.

I own the first Manifesto as a sample; I wore the fragrance a few times in winter and found it quite okay. However, it didn’t blow me away. It was some kind of mix between sweet and spicy, which sometimes became a bit scratchy. That’s why I approached the new one with a corresponding expectation, and what can I say, it really surprised me positively!

We look deeply into each other's eyes. Two half-full red wine glasses sit on the table. Black and purple candles flicker. In the background, soft rock plays. "I like looking into your eyes," he says. Then he brushes a strand of hair from my face and carefully tucks it behind my ear. I grin at him stupidly. My hands cradle his head. I feel like a teenager. He is so gentle.

I am a little shocked to discover that some find Love and Tears simple and forgettable. I do not agree. In fact, I've enjoyed this fragrance so much that I've worn it three days in a row. Love and Tears has renewed my adoration for jasmine. Jasmine can sometimes be hard to love, especially if it smells synthetic or soapy. The jasmine accord in Love and Tears is creamy and lush, made slightly crisp with citrusy, green bergamot. It wears beautifully on warm days, however it could also be appropriate for night-time, or even mild Winter weather. Love and Tears seems like the perfect name for this white floral beauty. It is both romantic and melancholy. I'd be really interested to see how this wears on a man, seeing that it is marketed as unisex. It smells very feminine and floral to my nose. I feel very comfortable wearing Love and Tears, and that may be due to the rather intimate sillage. It's quite a tender and elegant scent, that really brings out the softer side in everyone. It reminds me of the character of Anne Catherick from the novel, The Woman in White by Wilkie Collins. It has that very classic, 'damsel in distress' feel to it. In some ways Love and Tears is a soliflore, a jasmine one at that. I would encourage everyone and anyone to try it, even if jasmine scents aren't really your thing. I consider it one of the best jasmine fragrances around. It's refreshing to say the least. I can't say that I find it particularly indolic though. The longevity was excellent on my skin, lasting a good eight hours, or sometimes longer. The sillage, like I mentioned previously, is soft but not weak. Love and Tears is not particularly innovative, but it definitely is pretty. Signature worthy too.

Jasmine soliflores sometimes really speak to me. Molinard JASMIN and Montale JASMIN FULL are two examples which fill me with joy upon application and make me forget all about my obsession with roses. Other jasmine soliflores leave me, if not cold, at least capable of walking away. They are too dry or too austere or simply too simple to draw me in. By Kilian LOVE AND TEARS falls into this category. There is nothing wrong with LOVE AND TEARS. It is a jasmine soliflore on the dry side (closer to Keiko Mecheri's than to the lush varieties mentioned above), and perhaps that is why I cannot get that excited about it. This is not a green jasmine, nor is it sticky and sweet, and it even smells quite natural, but it is on the dry side, and I prefer my jasmine soliflores to be lush and, well, overwhelming, so this one is not for me. I would probably wear LOVE AND TEARS now and then, if I happened to have a bottle lying around, but honestly I believe that I would still reach first for the Molinard JASMIN in my collection to satisfy my thirst for this flower, and among the many haute niche jasmine perfumes on offer, Montale JASMIN FULL (also better than this) is already on my wish list.

A melodramatic name (how catchy! Good marketing strategy!)for a very conventional flowery, light bouquet dominated by jasmine. There are no deep roots to this fragrance, I would not compare it to any of the great classics, "Love and Tears" is too shallow. It reminds me of "Jasmine" by Keiko Mecheri or "Jasmin 17" by Le Labo. All these are expensive niche creations which are - in my humble opinion - not worth their money, since they are boring takes on a very old, hackneyed theme done much better so many times before.

Thank you Ergoproxy for the sample. Love and Tears gives me neither love nor tears. I have nothing against lily of the valley when they stay nicely in the background in fragrances. But Love and Tears was for me almost to the base a "Attack of the Killer Lily of the Valley." Maybe I'm also scent-damaged when it comes to lily of the valley, because my neighbor has a field of them under her fir trees, I don't know how many square meters. And when you talk over the garden fence there at the beginning of May, you end up in a coma after 10 minutes. My daughter, who was sniffing along during the testing today, could hardly contain her excitement, while I tried to shoo the lily of the valley off my arm to smell the other ingredients, because the oak moss was already growing lichens on my arm. When the lily of the valley finally released me from their grip (may the flower god bless them), I could still catch a hint of jasmine and lavender. Love and Tears is definitely a wonderful fragrance for all scent lovers who need intense flowers. My daughter is also thrilled. But I have never been the floral scent aunt (with a few exceptions) and especially not when a fragrance comes off so sweet. Too sweet, too much lily of the valley. Fine for others!

Immediately upon spraying, I am greeted by a jasmine scent that is so real, it feels as if I am standing in Spain, right in the middle of a huge, fully bloomed jasmine bush. I am overwhelmed. It is very floral and very fresh. But then this extremely bold lily of the valley comes in, which is actually a delicate, small, white flower that in reality has a very soft green-floral scent, but after a while causes headaches. The most beautiful lily of the valley still smells best directly in the forest under the trees, when the various scents of the forest mix together and the lily of the valley is just one part of the whole. In Love and Tears, however, it is the protagonist, the queen of the event. She sets the direction, and all the others just fall in line without protest. Whether bergamot, lavender, daffodil, orange blossom, ylang-ylang, labdanum, or even the jasmine, which has now spread its wings, the flowers simply do not dare to stand up to the lily of the valley and assert themselves. And so it remains, even though the woods and resins make the scent a little darker and not quite so piercing, and the oak moss tries to give it that certain forest note. No regular lilies of the valley have been used here, but rather oversized lilies of the valley with an intense fragrance. If you hold the sprayed area far enough away, it actually smells quite pleasant - just like lily of the valley - but the closer I get to my wrist, the more unpleasant it becomes. Therefore: pleasant for the environment, but quite unpleasant for the wearer of the fragrance.

I had a terrible image of Love and Tears. An overdosed jasmine that reminds you of mom and causes headaches? No. I am once again very positively surprised, as the jasmine is interpreted in a very unique, beautiful, and exciting way. At first, the familiar jasmine scent hits you - strong and soapy. But soon after, other notes mix in that make this fragrance cheerful and fresh.

A few weeks ago, I received this fragrance shortly after its market launch as a sample. Now I finally have the inspiration to dedicate myself to the scent. I have been wearing the fragrance for two hours now and smell like a jasmine bush that has been chemically enhanced. However, with air freshener and not à la Serge Lutens with benzoin and musk.

Yes, "Shout" would be the right motto for this fragrance... or better yet, "cry"! Thanks to the sample promotion from Hasi and Ms. Piggy, I got to experience the "pleasure" of 5 Kilian samples... the anticipation was very high even though Back to Black didn't excite me that much.

In Switzerland, horrific crimes are occurring that leave even the investigators puzzled. Young women are mysteriously disappearing there. There is no trace of the kidnapper or his victims. No one knows their whereabouts. The parents and friends of the victims are desperate; everyone has alibis, and none of the questioned individuals are considered suspects.

Beautiful jasmine soliflore scent, like a soft silk or chiffon dress. I can very well imagine this perfume as a wedding fragrance. If you interpret it this way, even the name fits: Love and Joy's Tears of Emotion. Those who do not like jasmine will not be able to appreciate this scent either. Floral, soft - wonderfully feminine.

What a pleasant surprise this flanker of Black Opium has been to me! To preface, I’m an avid cherry hater (only because it usually smells very medicinal to/on me) and I don’t love coffee notes in my fragrance. BO is a fragrance that I’ve always found to be too sweet, cloying, and kind of annoying. So when I heard this flanker was coming out, I totally disregarded it. However, I got a surprise sample of it and immediately fell in love after just one wear. This Over Red flanker has done something for me that none of the other flankers have and I’m pretty excited about it. The BO DNA is there at about 95%, but the added cherry just fits perfectly in with the vanilla-coffee-white floral staple that BO is. The “green” flanker felt a bit weird (wasn’t a fan of fig mixed with those notes), the Le Parfum was cute but just had more vanilla, but this one has uncovered a new appreciation for cherry notes for me. The cherry isn’t overpowering, but it’s not the most prominent note in the composition either. It sits perfectly atop the OG DNA and provides a gentle syrupy bite to an already sweet scent. I also feel like it helps to darken the coffee note a bit without making it louder and does give the scent a “red” aura. It’s so sexy, delicious, and fun, but also very wearable and kind of “grown-up” feeling. Performance-wise, it’s comparable to all the other BOs, so moderate to good longevity with a fairly good projection. I think it’s best for cool weather wear, but the pop of cherry gives it a cheekiness that could make it appropriate for spring and summer nights as well. To me, this is the best and most well thought out Black Opium flanker, and I’m happy to have given it a chance.

dark, sticky and not at all cloying like other cherry fragrances. the coffee is prominent but not overpowering. this is not a coffee fragrance. the sweet, creamy cherry is the star of the show. completely gorgeous and the only good Opium flanker. if you could own only one cherry fragrance, let it be this one.

Opium Over Red is a lovely, inviting and unique scent. I don’t think I’ve ever smelt anything quite like this. I get the mandarin in the beginning which I didn’t enjoy but it does disappear. I don’t smell any coffee, tea or jasmine at all, at least that I can identify, This to me is like a creamy vanilla pudding that has a little strawberry and cherry puree mixed through it, with some powdery, pink marshmallows sprinkled on top. In fact I think a more accurate description of this scent would be if you were to take a bag of Barrett “Flumps” (the pink and white twisty marshmallows) burst it open and stick your head in it. To me that’s near enough this exact smell. The scent bubble this creates is very comforting and relaxing, like a big fluffy cloud. This could easily be worn all year round in cool temperatures. While I enjoy the scent, I just can’t wear it as it’s just too much for me. I like powdery scents but this is powder overload and a little nauseating sadly. I chose Simona Andreoli’s Vicebomb over this which is similar but a much easier wear, for me anyway.

This marks my debut into the Black Opium collection, having previously only delved into the classical Opium by YSL. The allure of the Black Opium Over Red caught my attention, prompting a blind buy driven by its promise of a cherry-centric fragrance without the common tonka beans or almond notes. And girl, am I delighted with my decision! The fragrance opens with an intense burst, asserting its identity as a bold cherry-infused perfume. Picture cherries enveloped in cream with a subtle smoky undertone – it's a unique olfactory experience. While distinct from Tom Ford's Lost Cherry, it shares a certain intriguing similarity. I've noticed parallels with cherry scents from Banana Republic and Kayali too. What sets Black Opium Over Red apart is the inclusion of black tea and coffee notes, adding a zesty and bitter edge that I find quite appealing. The result is a concoction that exudes sophistication and uniqueness. It's a fragrance that commands attention and makes a statement. If you enjoy cherry-centric perfumes with a twist, this could be your next go-to. I encourage you to try it and share your thoughts in the comments. I'm eager to hear fellow fragrance enthusiasts' reviews and experiences with this captivating addition to the Black Opium line. Cheers to exploring new olfactory horizons!

As a big Black Opium fan and apologist, I have tried all the flankers. And I have to admit that some of them are pretty uncreative and way too close to the original. But this is a good one! Recognizably Black Opium, but with enough differences to justify owning both. It's basically the sweetened coffee from the original with a richer vanilla base that makes it similar to the Le Parfum flanker (which is also great). Besides that, there is a generous dose of juicy cherry and jasmine. While the original has a more general floral accord, this one has a more defined jasmine note that comes across as sweet, creamy and even a bit bubblegum-ish. It lends a new textural aspect to the scent, which in my opinion is just as important as the addition of cherry. This is a playful scent that would be perfect for evening and nighttime wear. It's very sweet and girly, but smoother and more rounded than the original EDP. Maybe because the cool pear note is missing and got replaced by warmer, creamier notes. It's also a great take on cherry for gourmand lovers who are tired of the myriads of Lost Cherry clones. In my opinion the whole is more than the sum of its parts here. One could think that Over Red is just Black Opium or Blacl Opium Le Parfum with a little cherry on top and the same effect could be achieved with layering, but I don't think you'd get the same result. I actually tried it with a sample of Le Parfum and Lost Cherry, and while also very nice, it's different. I might add this to my collection.

Yeah, this was really good. I usually can't wear designer fragrances.Because they give me unbearable headaches. That's just how I am. I liked the original Opium the best so far. That strong spice scent.But I don't think it suits me very well, and it's quite annoying to wear a scent like this in Japan, so there are limited occasions to use it.

The latest flanker in the black opium li r keeps the dna of the original and it is less sweet and fruitier. The cherry is pretty nice in the opening and the fruitiness lingers around. Unfortunately on my skin the licorice is prominent and the rest of the composition dies down in comparison.

opens with a sweet vanilla and candied maraschino cherry, backed up by its signature coffee, carries an almond nuttiness and some florals. has hints of a dark chocolate deep within the base. the cherry quickly steps aside to let every other note through, resulting in something close to the black opium classic with a kiss of cherry

If you're a fan of the original Black Opium, the Over Red version is a fabulous twist to a favourite. Addictive and comforting, the vanilla and coffee sparkles with a dark chocolate cherry warmth. I expected a juicier and fresher cherry profile but since buying and wearing this perfume, I'm absolutely loving the slightly darker and mysterious scent of the cherry instead.

As a cherry lover, this perfume from the Black Opium series surprised me. At first, I was pleasantly surprised because I could smell a beautiful cherry note. However, after literally 2 minutes, just a hint of it remained... All I could smell was floral coffee. Though I love this combination, I'm quite sad that the cherry note doesn't last that long. Still, it's a nice scent.

For some reason, the PC flanker isn't available to review here (hopefully that changes at some point) so I'm leaving my thoughts on it on this thread for the OG. I have yet to smell the Parfum/EDP of Scandal, but if it's anything even close to the PC flanker, it would be an absolute love for me. The Parfum Cologne is about as close to a "signature scent" that I've come across since first smelling Terre D'hermes Pure Parfum. I love any frag that could be labeled as "no nonsense", "old man" or "vintage" and even though Scandal has newer aged aspects to it, it very much comes off that way to me.

I love this. I normally wear this on a summers day. Perhaps its the Cashmeran , but I really smell a soft leather. Perhaps its just me lol. I prefer this version to the new one in the blue bottle. I haven't tried the Parfum version but certainly will. I will say though, this reminds me of Costume National Homme. Both very spicy, slightly sweet and long lasting. Scandal is lovely but I don't get why its called Scandal? Its too safe for that.

Hello everyone, I'm back again. After my first comment was received so positively, I’m trying my hand at another one today. Again, I must say: I am still quite new to this hobby and my nose is certainly not as trained as some of yours here. Please forgive me if I don’t describe everything in minute detail. This time I’m trying a fragrance from the house of Roja, and I would like to thank Cedar for sending me the sample :) Right off the bat: I completely understand the association with Eau Sauvage, as my father wore it for a time and it smells exactly like I do today. Now, Eau Sauvage is from the 60s, and the scent of Scandal PC immediately transports me back to an old barbershop from that era. I’m sitting in the barber's chair, freshly shaved, and the barber is applying aftershave to my face. But enough of the imagery, let’s get to how the fragrance smells to me: The opening is very powerful and herbal for me. I suspect this comes from the Petitgrain. Additionally, lavender tickles my nose, which remains present throughout the scent's development. I can’t detect the other ingredients in the top note, as the lavender blocks everything else, which I find a bit disappointing since I’m usually a big fan of basil and bergamot. The herbal opening fades quite quickly for me, leaving behind lavender, which is now lightly accompanied by jasmine and perhaps a hint of violet. From the rather richly composed base notes, I can still smell the cardamom and perhaps the clove; unfortunately, the other notes are not perceptible to me. However, the lavender is still slightly detectable and hasn’t completely disappeared. Now let’s get to my biggest criticism of this fragrance: namely, the longevity and especially the sillage. After I applied the fragrance this morning, I asked my girlfriend what she thought of the perfume I was trying out today. Her reaction was a rather confused look and the question, "You’re wearing a perfume? I can’t smell it at all." Now, I tend to be more of a subtle wearer when it comes to perfumes, but in many other tests, the scent could at least be perceived. Here, I had to hold my arm directly under her nose for her to smell anything at all. Her reaction wasn’t much better when she said, "You smell like an old man." And while I find the scent itself okay, I think she hit the nail on the head with that comment. Throughout the entire duration of the fragrance, I keep thinking, "I’ve smelled this before, nothing new here." The longevity is also nothing special; after a good 6 hours of wear on a rather cool day, the scent is only detectable if I hold my arm up to my nose. Anyone can wear this fragrance if they wish, but I see it more suited for an older gentleman in a suit at a dinner or attending a play. For me, it’s too classic, too boring, so it will remain just a test. Conclusion: Not a special or novel fragrance, but very classic. You feel transported back to the past upon application, but the impression lasts only briefly before the scent fades away. For the price, I think one should definitely expect more. So, there’s only one thing left, as I already wrote in the title: An expensive whiff of the past.

When I tried the perfume version at Mr. Wuchsa's, I was completely overwhelmed. A great, rich fougère with balsamic undertones. Classic, but without being old-fashioned or musty. The purchasing decision was made immediately after the first sniff, and I regularly repurchase the perfume. But what was Mr. Roger Bird thinking when he released the PC version? The scent is in no way comparable to the perfume, except for the basic DNA. I can no longer recognize the "potentiation" to the PC concentration, which RD states is around 18%. The PC offers almost disastrous performance and feels significantly weaker and more watery compared to, for example, Enigma PC. In this version, the scent resembles a somewhat better formulated Eau Sauvage rather than the original Scandal perfume. I sprayed 2 ml of it, as recommended by Dove, on the lower side of my neck and collar, along with a good dose on my jacket. My hair was then treated with an additional 3 sprays. All in all, a rather high dose. I wanted to be well-scented for an entire evening at the casino. The first 30 minutes were dreamy. Great sillage, balsamic like the perfume, and absolutely no reason for complaint. Upon arriving at the casino, I waited for my friends at the bar, and about 90 minutes had passed since application. I was sweating when my best friend was the first to say: "Oh! No perfume today! We don't know you like this!" ... Laughter! Of course, I immediately asked my friend to smell me to convince him of his mistake. "Ah ok, now! Today it's just aftershave..." I was appalled. Not only did I experience only a hint of Eau Sauvage, but the fact that I was olfactorily naked that evening has since shaped my impression of this scent. Reapplying hourly works for the scent. If you don't have a bottle with you, the magic fades after 60-90 minutes. I hold Roja in high regard regarding his expertise. Therefore, I seriously wonder if he does this on purpose. Just to force the customer to apply more. I don't know. The scent is okay, but Eau Sauvage also works in this category, and H+S are not weak but simply nonexistent. Therefore, I see absolutely no reason to buy this work again. Unless Roja finally realizes that improvements need to be made regarding performance. He can do it. The question is whether he wants to. I recommend the perfume. The PC, however, is not worth discussing. I'm sorry.

... is not always easy. Why interpret a painting when its aesthetics delight? Why dissect a symphony when it moves from the ear to the heart? Why break down a perfume into its 25 notes when it makes you dream? A dream of a walk over moss and underbrush, across a meadow of lily of the valley and lavender, past lemon trees. In the bag: spices from the Orient. This scent is a potpourri of natural ingredients, refined with a touch of synthetics. Because as Mr. Dove once beautifully said? The cotton shirt only becomes really comfortable with 1% elastane. I like the comparison, because this perfume is the ideal mix of both worlds. I don't perceive the cashmeran, but it surely serves its purpose. It is supposed to smell woody-sweet. Yes, it’s definitely there. But more as a booster. Great thing anyway, but worth the price? That has already been discussed elsewhere. Many do not want to afford these perfumes. But art remains art, and I gladly pay the artist for that. When I see the Diors in my friends' bathrooms, I think to myself: All nice. But luckily I have Roja... The perfumes (extraits) were the expensive beginning, but the slightly lighter EdPs from this house are affordable. Perhaps the EdPs perform better here for that reason. Prejudices against excessively high luxury prices do have an influence. Personally, the golden cap is enough for me; I don’t need the black one. Sauvage, Eau Sauvage, Moustache... many comparisons have been drawn here with other fougères, with aromatic fougères and other fougères... but no matter what this is here... For me, it is a real perfume. Real art.

The Roja Scandal is for me an absolute men's fragrance, just as it should be. Very noble, fine, unobtrusive, delicate, and full of memories of the past. I would describe it as a classic barbershop, shaving soap, shower gel, or even a fougère scent. The first time, I really smell mint. It starts fresh, very slightly bitter and pleasant.

Alright. I gave this a couple of wearings. Before I review it I have a few remarks, If this is the Arabian Nights finale, then well done. Bravo. Kilian has managed to seal an excellent series with a perfume that captures every shining aspect of each perfume from the line. Which brings me to my next point. The name is a misnomer. But this time it's a good thing. Meaning there is musk but it's not a musk dominant perfume. Rose Oud is rose and oud dominant, Pure Oud is oud dominant, Amber Oud is amber am oud dominant Musk Oud is the alpha of the series. It's comprised of the star accord from each perfume. It's got the incense from Incense Oud, the soft boozy rose from Rose Oud, the stellar quality oud in Pure Oud and the cardamom from Extreme Oud. Add an oily delicious musk and you have Musk Oud. If you were to only have one from the Arabian Series, this would be it. You should get this, then get the other flavors that appeal to you (amber / Amber Oud, Rose / Rose Oud, leather / Black Oud etc etc). This not only represents the complexity and quality that stands behind the Arabian Series (I'd have liked to say the Kilian line, but the generic waste that's seen spewing lately forbids it) but it is the most representative of all. This is akin to 34 Saint Germain Boulevard, the flagship creation. Muscle flexing if you will. Like a chameloen constantly changing pigmentation of smell. One minute it's an aromatic coriander , crisp cypress, the next it's cardamom ansd cypress. Then it's rose oud, then a boozy incense. Allllll of the above sitting on musk. The musk isn't pronounced at all. Neither is the rose. Nothing blatantly stands out. The epitome of complexity. An ever changing complexity. Notes and accords ricocheting back and fourth but in utter harmoy. A complex chameleon of a scent. If this is the Arabian Nights finale, then this is the expected climatic ending bringing together the best of all of the series.

Musk Oud opens with just a twist of fresh lemon juice before hints of the Oud in the base peek through. As the fragrance enters the early heart, the lemon disappears, now replaced by a mildly spiced soft airy rose that takes on the starring role with the now slightly more assertive Oud in support as radiant, almost honeyed incense and relatively sanitized patchouli are also detectable. During the late dry-down the slightly rubbery Oud and rose both remain though largely diminished, as relatively clean Musk from the base emerges and takes over the starring role while lacking most of the animalic facets one might expect. Projection is below average and longevity is average at 7-8 hours on skin. Musk Oud was not really the fragrance I expected based on its name. I thought musk and Oud would play co-stars throughout, but instead I got more rose and incense than musk until the last two hours or so of development. In fact, the Oud note that is certainly there (though quite possibly derived from a high quality synthetic) never really plays the star throughout, ceding the role primarily to the rose which is much more prominent in the key heart phase. The fragrance always stays relatively light, surprisingly clean to a large degree and rather easy to wear at all times. I like Musk Oud quite a bit but while I have not worn one of its sister scents, Rose Oud in quite a while I get a feeling Musk Oud smells similar during the heart phase, probably due to both having a similar smelling rose. The bottom line is the relatively expensive Musk Oud at $395 a 50ml bottle is a worthy addition to close out the By Kilian's Arabian Series, but it errs to a degree in its over-familiarity and by focusing too much on rose and not enough on its two supposed co-stars, earning a "very good" to "excellent" rating of 3.5 to 4 stars out of 5.

Kilian makes a lot of mediocre perfumes, but this absolutely is not one of them! (wtf is the point of sacred wood. god that perfume is so bland it makes me mad). Aaanyway.. Musk oud is an extremely unique take on the popular rose/musk/oud combo - I promise this isn't like anything you've smelled. Suffers from having a weird opening - hence the pretty meh reviews on parfumo (most people rate perfumes from a 20 sec paper test. smh.) It's outwardly super clean and professional, but there's a dark undertone of skankiness which makes this anything but your generic office perfume. Perfect for the office and for date night. It's heavily incensed but it's surprisingly fresh and airy from the green spices and dry citrus The patchouli is perfect here. This perfume has substantial 'weight' behind it already so the chouli isn't at all overpowering, but it lends a slightly dirty and spiced note that's just perfect. I don't get a lot of the rum here, but it's quite a heady perfume. I regularly get dizzy from wearing this because I try to suck as much of the juice up my enlarged nostrils as I can get. The notes all blend into a silky smooth sensual piece so it's hard to distinguish them from one another until you've worn it a few times. Intoxicating. It's very gently animalic which suggests that the wearer smells good, rather than them simply wearing a nice perfume. Lovely sensual and natural touch. To me Musk Oud feels like the much more handsome naughty uncle of Les Sables Roses from LV. Another Morillas Masterpiece. I love this stuff so much - one of my favourites of all time. 10/10

Longevity of 7.5, sillage of 7.1? What! There's no way in hell Musk Oud hasn't been reformulated *heavily* at some point. I've got an older refill bottle (doesn't have a batch code, so don't know the year) and this stuff projects and lasts like there is no tomorrow! Mind you, my daily drivers include names like Ombre Nomade, Terroni, Oud Satin Mood, and alike, and Musk Oud stands its ground even next to those nuclear bombs. In terms of the scent profile, Musk Oud is very clean, metallic, and polished. Has a gasoline-like undertone. No skank in here at all - yet this is undoubtedly an oud fragrance. While dark and mysterious, Musk Oud also has airy qualities to it and is totally wearable during the daytime. All in all, a very unique creation, not your typical rose-oud scent.

I discovered this perfume at Printemps Boulevard Haussmann in Paris. it is a more feminine perfume, even if I can be considered unisex. we clearly feel a mixture of musk and rose very similar to randal de al rehab at 2 euros. but nevertheless more accessible in price to pay since it is a 50ml bottle. it is more expensive at the price per litre. it remains a good compromise to have a luxury perfume that is difficult to access cheaper than louis vuitton. for those who are looking for the same accessible there is the brand al rehab.
Recently, while I was in Milan at an upscale department store inspecting the wonderful perfumery, I stumbled upon a Kilian stand for the first time in my life.

To get straight to the point; nothing has actually gotten lost here. I consciously bought Musk Oud. And I would have never thought it possible, because until now I couldn't stand any fragrance with Oud. Musk Oud is the reason why I no longer categorically exclude Oud fragrances. I first smelled it in the perfumery.

First of all, I should note that rose-oud fragrances generally bore me. I have never really been able to enjoy them; it’s probably just not my direction. Rose scents are always classic and beautiful in themselves, but oud often makes them quite unbearable for me.

It was an absolute spontaneous test (definitely better than a spontaneous purchase ;)): Parfumo meeting, right hand back still free after 4 hours of continuous testing, no desired test candidate in mind or at hand. Just trying Musk Oud - the combination of these two absolute opposites sounded simply tempting and worth testing.

... was my first thought when Musk Oud hit my nose. One was used to the strangest fragrance creations from Mr. Hennessy, yet all were beautiful and harmonious. Unfortunately, the attempt to create a well-rounded perfume with Musk Oud fell short. One would actually think that the combination of oud and musk would have a wonderfully imposing effect.

I bought a sample of this after looking at the notes and thinking it sounded interesting. The opening is a rather vibrant and sharp green - I like this, I think to myself. Then after maybe 2 minutes it's all about very loud vanilla and tonka. Reminds me of a very sweet vanilla flavored marshmallow. Soon enough after that, the powder kicks in and now it's a powdery vanilla flavored marshmallow scent. This smell makes me feel a little sick actually. Naturally, it has tremendous lasting power and is hard to wash off. What is YSL thinking here? Definitely not full bottle worthy for me.... heck I won't even finish these samples!

After buying this, I opened it up on the spot and sprayed it twice on myself. And holy cow! It smelled like my dad’s tomato plants! Green, green, green! I was alarmed. About 5-10 minutes later, I kept smelling this wonderful citrusy-powdery scent. I thought it was coming from someone shopping nearby, but nope. It was me! That biting green note had completely disappeared and had become so beautiful. There’s really no way to say it other than that I love it, despite its hideous and unfortunate name, which reminds me of communism. The green note is very sharp initially, and for that reason I was afraid to wear it to church the day after I bought it. Today I sprayed myself 4 times (back of neck/hair, front of neck, and once on each arm) to see what would happen. The green note goes away within five minutes. As it recedes, that bergamot comes forward in all of its citrusy glory, but it is tempered a bit by a sweet hit of something…maybe the currant bud? No idea because I don’t know what currant bud smells like. Slowly, the florals arrive, but they’re subtly sweet and gentle. The vanilla and tonka bean really hit hard, but not in a bad way. I would say the tonka is a bit stronger than the vanilla, but together they form a powdery and somewhat sweet powerhouse of olfactory delightfulness. I cannot pick out the sandalwood or the cedar notes on me at all. This perfume reminds me of Ellen Tracy Bronze, which is also “citrusy-creamy-powdery.” There’s a strong Johnson & Johnson baby shampoo vibe here, too. Not bad for a $12 clearance blind buy at Kohl's.

Manifesto is a lovely and radiant scent. Black currant gives it a sharp and juicy quality, which seems to cool what would otherwise be a warm & woody vanilla/tonka combo. The green notes and jasmine provide a light freshness, and there's an almost glimmering or sparkling element (which is completely appropriate given the bottle design). The drydown transitions from juicy to powdery. After a while it matures quite a bit, and lends a 'come-hither' quality (but in a classy way).

I smelled this perfume at a Zurich department store. The sales clerk kept saying: yes its sexy, a sexy fragrance. "Sexy" was not the word I would have used to describe it. I didn't care for the flat face-powder smell. But I'd be interested to hear what others think.

These 3 musketeers are the most coming to your nose. This scent reminds me luxury face creams. Maybe ysl skin care if they produce a face cream, they can give Manifesto's smell to it. Bergamot starting mini fresh. Then the tonka bean and vanilla are dominating the scent. Mysterious, creamy because its smells like cream :) hhh, sweet but not overly sugary. Especially night outs or dinners good choice. I bet in past its longevity better, today its fine but not the beast mode. You are waiting more longevity, I confess. Age= bit mature but timeless. I confess again I think its name is shadowing by Black Opium edp. I prefer Manifesto 4 times over than Black Opium edp.

YSL Manifesto is a cozy, warm vanilla that wraps you in a warm hug yet doesn’t overpower. I don’t get nose-blind to it, it keeps on pleasing me throughout the day. If you like Dior Addict, Guerlain’s Angelique Noire, Lancôme Hypnose and other green vanillas, you will probably also enjoy Manifesto.

It started very promising and I loved it but the the sandalwood took over. It´s not the first time. It buried all the promising notes. It´s just something with sandalwood that ruins it for me in several fragrances that I i have tested. I will try it again.

Thanks to a lovely perfume, the scent has moved in with me... now three of the Manifestos have really made it into my collection. Eclat is for the warm days of the year - L'Elixir is good to wear in autumn. I just need Le Parfum from this line. I'll keep this one in mind for testing in winter ;) This Manifesto is perfect for the transition of the seasons.

It's the year 2012. Probably late summer. The just-16-year-old Pauline is in the perfume shop with her mother. She's really only interested in makeup - and excessively so. Until now, she has only had some drugstore scent, which she doesn't like at all. She doesn't particularly care for her mother's fragrances either; they all smell so citrusy, like a bathroom.

My new statement maker for higher class occasions! A modern interpretation of a classical structure - The Chypre. In my opinion a more polished version of the original APEX EDP. Even though they share the same notes, this Parfum shows more facets and seems to have more time to develop each stage of its very complex composition. It opens up fruity and efervescent with a melange of bright citrus and an almost ripe pineapple accord. I get some smoky pops from incense, woods and a leather accord. There’s a floral undertone from jasmine too, mind you! A lot of greens as well - this being a green dominant scent: I get a lot of fir and pine-like qualities with hints of Anise and Juniper, which at times from the cap, reminds me of a half gin - half Absinthe concoction. It does have a super rich base, almost sweet but not quite. This one goes more on a boozy, resinous, leathery and slightly bitter/smoky direction. With the Labdanum being very apparent to me. This is a bold, loud but very classy and modern interpretation of a Chypre composition. A head turner in a tuxedo!

Apex Parfum seems to be Apex Eau de Parfum , which smelled identical to Polo Eau de Toilette to me, with a synthetic-sweet maltol-ish note added. The effect is alright, giving a sharp sweet edge to what is a masculine oakmoss bomb. The Sauvage Elixir comparison I'm baffled by, as Apex Parfum doesn't contain any of the spices that are very prominent in the Dior: nutmeg, cinnamon, and cardamom. Also Sauvage Elixir is built on a fougere base while Apex is a chypre: bergamot, cistus, and oakmoss along with other animalics and resins, while Sauvage Elixir has the unmistakable lavender/oakmoss combination. I see more parallels with Absolu Aventus , though Apex Parfum is much less fruity. I like both about the same, enough to enjoy wearing them but no desire for a full bottle, partly because of the price point of each. Longevity is decent, but projection really suffers, probably due to the high concentration. I wish there were a middle ground between the EDP and Parfum concentration, something that didn't rely heavily on the synthetic ambery aromachems to acheive high concentration, but also more unique than Apex EDP.

Somehow this perfume wasn’t a banger for a lot of people. I could understand it has vibes of some perfumes and they smell a like. Yet again this is a perfume on another level if you ask me. The cinnamon is done very well. It’s manly it’s fresh it’s strong and it will get you compliments. To be honest it’s one of the better office scents. It is quite expensive but yet again which Roja isn’t?

Roja Apex is a refined green-woody fragrance that feels confident, modern, and deeply connected to nature. It opens with a fresh yet slightly resinous greenness that never turns sharp, gradually evolving into a smooth woody core with an elegant masculine presence. Projection is moderate but noticeable in the first hours, creating a confident aura rather than loud sillage. Longevity is excellent, easily lasting 8–10 hours on skin, with a refined dry-down that stays close yet persistent. Apex feels polished, versatile, and quietly powerful, ideal for those who value sophistication over excess.

My review of the firstborn Apex Eau de Parfum was 8 months ago. In the meantime, no one has dared or felt motivated to write a report for the latecomer Apex Parfum . Both are reason enough for me to finally share my thoughts on the perfume variant of this great scent. As I mentioned in my report on the Eau de Parfum, I came across the 10ml travel spray through ROJA Gifting. Since I also had samples of the perfume, I have only just now gotten around to opening the travel spray. This also means that I would like to take a moment to say a few words about the perfume. - The packaging and the feel are absolutely high-quality, as is typical for Roja. Even the travel spray feels premium, and the sprayer works flawlessly. The APEX theme is reflected on the small sliding box. Of course, due to space constraints, the power animal card is missing here. (I mentioned this in the Apex Eau de Parfum review). According to photos from other users, however, a card is included with the full bottle. - I must confess: I am now a bit sober when it comes to classifying ROJA's perfume concentrations. Often, when comparing, you read words like "more faceted," "more complex," "deeper," and "more mature." I have now been able to compare several ROJA siblings and perhaps belong to the few representatives who do not see the added value in the perfume. And with that, I might already be giving away the conclusion of this review. - The scent (in comparison): Where Apex Eau de Parfum starts with an incredibly interesting mix of mandarin-rich citrus, freshness, and a pronounced pineapple, the freshness and pineapple in Apex Parfum remain more in the background. In direct comparison, I feel that it starts off a bit darker, spicier, and perhaps with a hint more incense. After a short while, the two come closer together, yet both remain true to their start. What I perceive means that the firstborn consistently tries to come across as a little more modern and appealing. Those familiar with the Gatekeeper comparison from the Apex Eau de Parfum reports know that perhaps this is exactly where APEX's strength lies. The goal is to create a balance between classic and modern - and in my view, the competitor does this better in its larger bottle. Regarding longevity, I also see no significant strengths in the perfume. - For whom is Apex Parfum suitable? Roja clearly attributes APEX to the masculine gender. This is indisputable for me. While younger audiences may dare to try "Apex (Eau de Parfum) | Roja Parfums," I would really suggest starting with the perfume in your 30s. But honestly, regardless, if asked, I would always recommend the older brother. With that, you get more content for less money. Collectors and those financially unburdened will certainly find their happiness here as well. I am left with the good feeling of having spent way too much money on a great scent, but at the same time having saved even more money by not choosing the full bottle of Apex Parfum . In this sense - choose wisely! ;-)

Hello everyone, today I would like to say a few words about Apex Parfum . Right off the bat, most Rojas (not feminine) always have an adult and mature touch, and they have nothing in common with youthful easy-to-wear fragrances (like e.g. D&G, CHANEL, DIOR) I think you know what I mean.

I had a sample of the Apex perfume lying around for quite some time. Recently, I finally got around to bringing it out and testing it. At the beginning, I get a distinctly citrus-fresh opening. However, it is worth noting that this is immediately enveloped by a pleasing incense. I also had the impression of perceiving some pepper, but I must have been mistaken.

I never read the other reviews before writing my own, so I am not subconsciously influenced. This time, I had no expectations for this fragrance, so I occasionally read a few texts. For me, this scent is nothing special; it is a fragrance direction that I personally cannot relate to. I mean, I can't even assign it to a family relationship.

In the City of Sin opens with just a faint whiff of bergamot and pink pepper before a very nice cardamom, almost cumin-like undertone grows over time to dirty things up just a tad. The cardamom remains into the early heart, now joined by a relatively sharp apricot and plum fruity tandem with a rose undertone. As the cardamom recedes, it is replaced by a very nice incense note that remains through the dry-down. Cedar wood from the base dominates and bleeds into the lower heart notes combining with the incense and fruity rose accord that still remains, while a subtle patchouli note adds just the slightest amount of dirtiness to the dry-down. Projection and longevity are both excellent. In the City of Sin does a fine job of combining slightly dirty notes with a more traditional fruity rose and incense accord with a woody base. The fragrance smells very nice from start to finish, and the dirty notes never become overpowering or call undue attention to themselves, instead providing great balance to the composition on the whole. The scent leans a bit to the feminine side of unisex and I personally would prefer smelling it on a lady, but it really can be worn well by anyone. In the end, I would say the composition is not ground-breaking and it is rather expensive in relative terms, but In the City of Sin certainly is well-done and smells quite pleasant earning a "very good" 3.5 stars out of 5.

Is By Kilian IN THE CITY OF SIN a reissue of LIAISONS DANGEREUSES? I ask because it has precisely the same (eccentric) effect upon me. I smell hyacinth very strongly in the opening, after which the perfume becomes more of an unsweetened fruity chypre. Where is the sin in this, for heaven's sake? I may be in the minority, but I never really connect the By Kilian market hype with their perfumes. In this case, the tag line is: "The temptation which leads to carnal desire." Huh. I have yet to detect a single animalic note in the entire By Kilian line-up, so either I'm anosmic to their erotic inducements, or we simply have wildly divergent views on what the word 'racy' is supposed to mean. Honestly, the snakes and all of the clumsy pseudo-erotic writing does nothing to make this composition anything more to me than a reissue of LIAISONS DANGEREUSES, as tame as plum pudding--but much less sweet. In the end, I am forced to conclude: I just don't get it. At all.

The second of my three Good & Evil candidates, which already resonated better with me, is In the city of Sin - in the city of sin, that is! Poor Kilian Hennessy, he has probably never been to a city of sin or what kind of sin did he think of with this fragrance?? Did someone take the fabric napkin or pick a flower from the terrace border? In the city of Sin is a nice, light, summery floral scent - I think of faintly scented pink roses on a bed of hay. At first sprightly fresh, later a little warmer and cozier, but still a light, fluffy floral fragrance. Sin??? Too weak and too light! Sin??? Too flowery and softly harmless! Sin??? Not what I would think of when considering sin! In the city of Sin is nice, but not nice enough for the price. There are already various other candidates on the market that are significantly - significantly - cheaper to acquire, even if not in such a beautiful bottle. The longevity leaves much to be desired here and the sillage is not worth mentioning. It's a pity, but there have been much better offerings from Kilian - I can only think of A taste of Heaven. But ultimately, names are just noise and smoke. If this fragrance showed more character, more body, more facets, more depth, and if it had better sillage and longevity, it would have been my top choice among the three. As it stands, it remains my second choice.

I cannot associate this fragrance with Sin City, the hard-hitting blockbuster from 2005, nor with other dens of iniquity that might come to mind with that name. It strikes me as rather retro. Therefore, I draw certain parallels to the great Hildegard Knef. Younger people might know her from a collaboration with Extrabreit; otherwise, she has stood out in recent years for her fabulous eyelashes and that certain glamour that characterized many divas in the post-war years and which has almost been lost now. In the City of Sin expresses this old school glamour. It feels familiar to me, yet I cannot say where it’s from. It comes across as very feminine, very cool-erotic, and extremely wearable. Almost too tame and unremarkable for a Kilian. The prelude is fresh-spicy with a lot of cardamom. Then violins come in... or rather a creamy-floral mélange. "Let it rain red roses for me!" - sweet, velvety, fruity delight. There’s no trace of patchouli or other irritatingly dominant notes; they are only there to give the fragrance an aura of timelessness. I perceive the drydown as rather soapy-clean. Very surprising and different from what I expected!

One has to give it to by Killian. The names are sensationally good. They spark curiosity and a desire to test. In the City of Sin is the first by Killian that I am consciously testing and examining closely. I have smelled one or two before, but always rather casually. A big thank you at this point to Laurel, who was kind enough to provide me with this sample. Now to the scent itself. What does a sinful city smell like? Dirty, sweaty, animalistic... A glance at the fragrance notes quickly makes it clear that such expectations are not to be found here, but rather a gourmand. I also like that very much, so let’s apply it to the skin. The first impression that the scent makes immediately after spraying is fruity. However, the fruity notes are very muted, as if covered by a thick, heavy layer of powder. With intense sniffing, I can even slightly detect the apricot and plum, although the latter doesn’t really come across as caramelized. The fruity notes also fade quite quickly to make way for powdery-sensual notes. The scent has something floral, but it reminds me more of a dried flower potpourri than a fresh bouquet. I can't pinpoint specific ingredients, but in general, I find it a bit difficult to grasp this fragrance. In any case, I perceive it at this stage as quite classic. The plum occasionally comes through, but it is not a fresh, juicy plum that would add a fruity freshness to the scent, but rather a dried plum that blends well into the floral powderiness. In the base note, the fragrance still has that slightly soapy, distinctly floral composition, which remains somewhat detectable on the skin for a reasonably long time without being particularly strong or prominent, and without any special notes standing out intensely. All in all, the fragrance has developed quite differently than I would have expected from the name or the ingredients. Instead of the gourmand notes, the flowers are clearly in the foreground here, although I think that in this city, there are other blossoms living here besides just roses. I find the longevity and sillage to be mediocre to okay; I wouldn’t buy the fragrance now, but it was, as always, interesting to test something new, and I am very curious about the other fragrances from the brand thanks to the great names. Even though the sinful city turned out to be more of a brave living room potpourri, a bite of heaven can still taste delicious, or a dangerous affair can awaken certain desires. I remain curious and open-minded.

Sometime ago I tried some Opium from a big 4 oz bottle and it was a m a z i n g !! I saw an endless paradise. I felt real warm carnation waves... My hair bathed in moonlight coconut. My heart beat sandalwood hard. and...the next day...paradise still being there with some amber on my chest... I tried Opium in a perfume store. Oh my why..... It was strong, bitter and so...chemical...... I forgot to tell you my Opium is about 24 years old. why they killed this jewel...Oh why Oh why do you destroy such a gems like this one... The answer my friend is blowing in the wind..!

-It is a scent of contradictions, like the ancient incense of vespers and the fleeting musk of an one night stand. -In small doses, Opium is not incompatible with dining, clubbing or romance. Used excessively it will ward off flies, humans and evil spirits. -A spectacular incense of monstrous proportions. -The smell of Marco Polo's clothes as well as come back at Venice from his journey along the silk route. -I particularly love to apply a single, small squirt before bed. The smell is just heavenly. And all night I dream of the hanging gardens of Babylon... -I know why this perfume is called Opium. It is totally addictive... -Good lord, this is chemical warfare of the highest concentration! -God, Opium... what are you doing to me? -Is it possible not to be consumed by its beauty? -This is a sin. It must be.And the name, God that name! The whole thing is criminal. -The Opium is the most glamorous and dangerous girl ever appeared from Paris, seducing one feeble admirer after the other as she moves along. -Holy mother of god, this is amazing!!!It is just to die for... -OPIUM feels more like an impressionist painting about life and love on the ancient Silk Road. Truly you can't appreciate what an oriental fragrance really is until you've smelled this masterpiece. -Oh god, I literally felt like this perfume had a death grip on my throat. -Even after 32 years on the market, this scent still screams "OBEY ME." -I like it because it doesn't try to be likeable. It's just there. -I do believe that this perfume wears you... -While I do not wear it regularly, when I do, I intoxicate.Seduction in a bottle... -This is what I imagine the spice from Dune smells like... -It caused such a stirring in my loins that I'd track and hunt a woman wearing this down forever. BRILLIANT! -Treat yourself to the parfum. There is nothing in the world like it. -Opium is intoxicating and heady stuff. Something no wicked, decadent girl should be without. -It is my default fragrance. The one I want to be remembered for. The one I want to be buried in. -When it comes down to Opium, I'd have to say I'm a total sucker for it. -Dear God!!!What on earth is this???How could you ever create such a temptation??? -Opium is timeless and magical, and it is still THE Oriental. -Proof that there is a heaven. -I admit it, I'm hooked. I always heard that opium was highly addictive... -This stuff should be illegal... -It doesn't offer any favors, you don't have to just like it, you have to love it and if it loves you back, it will be a best friend for ever ... -It’s a bit of a creepy feeling, like meeting one of your old boyfriends, or someone’s walking over your grave... -Opium is the most magnificent antidote to the waves of pubescent pop princess, foody/deodorant-style, mass-made scents that rule young fragrance buyers as the 20th century closed and the 21st century begins. -I thought I bought a scent,I got Lilith in a bottle... Do I need to say more?

Having avoided Opium all my life because it sounded just too gauche, I finally sniffed it the other day and was sunk. Opium is a quite fabulous oriental in the style of Panthère and other greats of the genre, except as its name implies, this one was truly born in the east. I'm sure if you added a wonderful incense perfume like Jovoy's Liturgie des Heures or Naomi Goodsir's Bois d'Ascèse, to any classic floral oriental, you'd get something close to this. Think Panthère with lots more frankincense, as well as myrrh and opoponax. The result is far more than I'd guessed, a hypnotic fragrance that could have perfumed emissaries traveling China's old silk road, something Marco Polo might have smelled at Kublai Khan's court, only to be disbelieved in Europe when he told of the marvels he'd found. Projection and longevity are great and I expect sillage is, too. When you tire of smelling like a potentate (Bal à Versailles) or growling like a panther, wear Opium and smell like China's only female dynastic ruler, Empress Wu Zetian.

Oh, how I love spicy orientals from back in the day! Back then perfumers knew what they were doing. They knew how to create a sensual fragrance that would last decades. They understood the art of perfumery. Opium is one of those breath-taking scents. A seductive blend of spices, smokey incense and floral notes inter-mixed with subtle fruits. A scent that requires an acquired taste for sure, but one that you can hardly push aside. The woman that wears Opium is very stylish and as some might agree, exotic. There's an element to Opium that is rather dirty and shocking, like the scent of a heavy smoker or the scent that lingers in the air after a night of passion. While some will find Opium repulsive, others will love its blatantly sexual appeal. For an EDT, Opium lasts and lasts, so I assume that both the pure parfum and EDP could possibly last on the skin for days, (that is if you didn't shower). I highly recommend.

Opium is one of the hardest scents to review. Because I love it so much, I seem to fall short in words to express my love. Nevertheless I will have a go. I have tried several reformulations, but my love is for the original version. The current formulation is so weak compared to the original and so completely different. I have 2 versions of the EdT: the 1st bottle is somewhere from the late 70's until the first years of the 80's and the 2nd bottle is from 1994. There is already a huge difference between those 2, but the '94 version is also very nice. My review will be for the original formulation though. Just sprayed it's overwhelmingly strong. I only need a tiny bit. I can directly smell the incense combined with a somewhat soapy (makes me wonder if there is ambergris in the original composition) and spicy cloves. It takes a few minutes to settle into a delicious, warm, sweet, spicy, mysterious and oriental brew of the gods. And it last for more than 10 hours on my skin. After I finished my 30 ml bottle, I will probably not be able to find a new one. On the other side, seen the strength it will take quite a while. I will defintely cherish my treasure.

Oh boy where do I begin with this?! First off the vintage version is far superior to the modern version. Truly decadent scent wrapped in oriental warmth and mystery. If you love strong oriental/ spicy scents you will love this! Why did they have to reformulate this master piece? If I spray just one spray I can still smell it the day after on my coat it's that strong.

People talk of Giorgio and how it created a sensory overload but Opium was right up there in its distinct aroma and how women over-sprayed it. Now, the prices for a vintage bottle are ridiculous. Did I notice the ice had melted around the box? I already have EDT, EDP and several flankers that I carefully guard on my top shelf. What could this concentration have that the others do not?

There is something ancient about this fragrance: it is the oakmoss that speaks, with its deep, earthy, almost austere timbre. It does not have the woody dryness of vetiver, nor the herbaceous freshness it tames, but a gravitas that anchors the skin to the earth. Powerful, uncompromising, this fragrance is robust and built on a balance that does not bend to fashion, an olfactory architecture. It is the scent of those who carry the weight of their history, of those who are not afraid to leave a mark. Perhaps it is not for everyone, and perhaps that is precisely why it is so fascinating.

I wish everyone could have the opportunity to hear the works created by the master Roja

Deep in the Allgäu Alps lies a crystal-clear mountain lake. The last rays of the setting sun gleam cheerfully between the mountain peaks, bathing the magically greenish shimmering lake in a mysterious light. Up here, where fox and hare say goodnight to each other, nature remains untouched and the problems of everyday life are far away… In the sky, the glowing moon begins to take its place, and the transition between day and night seems seamless. The cosmic balance, perfectly calibrated and undisturbed, allows countless lights of shooting stars to fall deep into the mirror-like lake. The scent of earthy grasses rises sharply, mingling with the smoky soft mists swirling on the surface, to unite with the aseptic woody tones of the deep lake. Pulsing and unstoppable, in the rhythm of the night, the origin of all life returns to the source. ** Roja has once again managed to captivate me. Incredible, as I am by no means a compulsive vetiver fan, yet this one compels me even more and truly leaves me in awe. There are so many interpretations of vetiver available and executed, but none have resonated with me as much as this one does. An authentic and extremely successful Cologne opening makes the scent initially feel very refreshing. The oil of Litsea Cubeba belongs to the laurel family and certainly shapes the beginning with its lemongrass-like note. By the way, I find Cologne to be relatively so, as the scent appears very enduring in its development and longevity. But it is also a parfum Cologne…whatever these designations may exactly mean. What excites me about this Roja is the delicate execution of the theme. From the very beginning and throughout, there is a beautiful aseptic, slightly sterile undertone. From this undertone springs the melody, in the form of a mild, earthy, slightly smoky vetiver. Not sharp and edgy, but extremely clean and harmoniously integrated, a fantastic and complex scent scheme emerges. You can almost witness how the vetiver gradually reveals itself, carried by the aseptic base tone. Accompanied by the very fine woody component typical of vetiver scents, I believe there are no wishes left unfulfilled. The wearability and longevity are versatile and commendable. I think, for most people, it is perceived as pleasantly fragrant, and the Roja vetiver can be excellently enjoyed in the sunny months. In conclusion, while the rather high price remains a drawback, the quality clearly speaks for itself in this case.

I hesitantly grabbed this one off of FragranceNet as it gets a lot of hate. I like the edt LNDL, but don’t think it lasts long enough (as does the rest of civilization). I saw the 50/50 love/hate propaganda that surrounds it, and decided to give it a shot, as I can’t find it anywhere that I can test it out in person. When I gave it the first blast, I was pleasantly surprised. I get a very nice, very spicy feel in the opening. Not the same as, but similar to the Spicebomb Infrared, or maybe even Fahrenheit (remember that I’m saying “maybe” or “kind of” in the comparisons). It opens with this spiciness, and slowly creeps into a sweeter feeling version of the edt. Not bad at all. I enjoy it a lot. Performance is great on my skin as well. The projection bubble is a tight 2-3ft radius, but the sillage lingers just long enough, and longevity, although close, is a solid 8hours. So if you can find it to test, by all means give it a shot. If you’re thinking of a blind buy, you better really enjoy the edt, and remember that the opening has a very red feeling, chili pepper-esque spiciness to the opening. After all, the community either loves it or loathes it.

There are very few fragrances that are as daring and have an opening as bombastic as this. As an intermediate level fragrance collector, I own, have owned and smelled an obscene amount of fragrances and it is very rarely that I am caught off-guard by a fragrance, especially one of designer sensibilities. Any fragrance connoisseur knows the original La Nuit - this flanker is a bold and daring departure from that legendary DNA to darker and more adventurous territory and let us unpack it very briefly: This is a dense and enveloping fragrance loaded to the rafters with cardamom, leather and Tonka to create an aura of fire around any so daring as to wear the scent. The opening is loud, sweet and truly dense on first application. It quickly becomes apparent that this scent is something of a monster and addresses the very well documented performance issues of the OG La Nuit while striking harmony between the core elements of the original and evolving the scent with the inclusion of the leather and Tonka. This EDP does come across more masculine and is a dangerous item to have in one’s arsenal on colder days and those evening excursions. From the onset, all of the new accords are on full display and they gradually make their way to the front as the freshness at top subsides. After which, the leather and Tonka become the most prominent and these are accompanied by a slight powdery texture, while the famed cardamom retreats to a supporting background role on this iteration as opposed to being the protagonist like on the original. The scent opens warm, rich, sweet and very sensual with a quick bite from the grapefruit, which quickly retreats, with a dash of powdery dustiness from the lavender herein. This phase of the fragrance is very short-lived, which makes this version come across as less fresh, at least, when compared with the original. Once the stars of the show, the leather and the Tonka, take center stage, the fragrance becomes smoother and even more elegant with the emergence of the sandalwood which polishes the scent slightly while mixing in a slight woody element. When comparing the two, the EDT is more attention grabbing and may be favored more by the general public but I favor this EDP a bit more as it feels more creative and a step away from some of the traditional leanings of mainstream fragrances, making it slightly more unique while still keeping some of the designer mass-appeal. Naturally, this will be a cold weather and night-time scent as I suspect it may grow slightly cloying in high-heat situations. As earlier indicated, the fragrance does perform very well – Lasting cleanly through entire work days with a few feet of projection around the first two hours of application and gradually growing closer and eventually resting as a skin scent which you won’t have to work very hard to locate at the end of your day. Overall, here is my rating: Scent: 8/10 Pricing: 7/10 Versatility: 7/10 Longevity: 8/10 Projection: 8/10

Hello dear community, I have now been regularly wearing the EdP version of the much-loved La Nuit series for several months and would like to share my experience and opinion with you. When I started to delve deeper into this hobby at the beginning of the year, I, like most people, stumbled upon the La Nuit series. In particular, I wanted to try the highly praised original version of the EDT. It was hyped by well-known YouTubers, which made me curious. So, I went to a large department store and immediately looked for the YSL shelves... After finding all the La Nuits, I grabbed the EdT and sprayed it on my wrist... First thought: “Phew, this is kind of musty and not for me at all...” [...] “Never mind, it’s just the top note, wait a bit...,” I thought. (It is said that the older batches cannot be compared to the new ones; I cannot confirm or comment on this, as I have never smelled the old batches...). A few bottles later, I noticed another bottle, red-black, same bottle style, same lettering, but Eau de Parfum... “Oh, the same as EdP? I have to test this right away!” I thought. I immediately took the bottle in hand and sprayed it on my other wrist “Wow, this is intense! And damn sexy!” [...] Yes, with the EdP, I immediately had that wow effect that the EdT didn’t give me... So the first impression was amazing! To test the longevity, sillage, and development of the EdP, I sprayed myself with 4-5 sprays and spent some time outside... About 3 hours later, when I got home, I greeted my partner and her comment was: “What do you have on this time? It smells and practically calls for sex... xD [...]. Well, the scent had already blown me away from the start, but this compliment finally convinced me to make a purchase. So I searched online for a good price and found one. Thus, I ordered the large 100ml bottle... A few days later, I went to a restaurant for a team dinner with my colleagues... When I hugged the female colleagues to greet them, one said with a wink: “Mmm, so who are you trying to pick up today? You smell very attractive.” [...] After a few weeks of wearing it, I noticed that it doesn’t necessarily project a huge scent cloud, meaning the sillage is rather mediocre. But the longevity is all the better; on my skin, it lasts a strong 8-9 hours! I even sprayed it on my wrist again last night before going to bed and could still perceive it well after waking up. The scent opens refreshingly and spicy, the grapefruit stands out right from the opening and instantly lifts your mood. The cardamom stays a bit subdued but still gives it the exotic spice for a masculine touch. After a while, I perceive the lavender; although it doesn’t belong to my favorite notes (at least so far), it adds a pleasant - and fitting to the grapefruit - additional freshness to the scent. As it develops, it becomes fruity or honey-sweet (that’s how I perceive it); it could and should be the absolute... In the dry-down, the sandalwood brings this sensually warm, oriental flair that I really like. The patchouli and vetiver also make the scent earthy and woody-herbaceous, which contributes to its long-lasting nature. Overall, this EdP has a very dynamic development, which I really enjoy. I also let a few buddies smell the scent... The consensus among them: “This is a scent for one-night stands...” :D [...] Conclusion: As mentioned above, this scent does not have what you would call monster sillage; you have to get close to smell it. But on the skin, it is all the more intense. And I think that’s intentional. I didn’t even care about the EDT anymore, as the EdP convinced me so much. This is truly a very attractive, sensual, and erotic scent that, despite a minimal synthetic quality, is very seductive to women... Regarding the seasons, I think you can wear it in every season except high summer (it would be way too strong for me then). But rather in the evening; I see it less during the day... You should give it a chance, as I think it really smells incredibly sexy, sexy, and once again sexy! [...]. And I thank everyone as always for reading and wish you all the best! Best regards
