Addendum 08/2023: Today's scent unfortunately has little in common with the one from back then (in my opinion). It has been diluted and made more mass-appealing. I can hardly detect the animalic notes anymore. Also, the longevity has unfortunately become poor. I wouldn't pay 1,200 EUR for it. Original review: Scent - oranges soaked in erotic rum and resins “...and kiss you. Deeply. The night burns brightly.” PDLN 2 - a complex composition that represents a warm embrace of two lovers. The light is slowly dimmed. The closeness increases. I feel your breath. There is playfulness. Seduction. People are not people without the deep breath of love. From the moment I applied it, I was immediately captivated by PDLN 2: opulent and soft. Fruity and resinous. Oriental and spicy. And a lot of rum. The dominant notes for my nose are orange and rum. The oranges smell very natural and not synthetic at all. From the very beginning, you can tell that this is a true luxury product. Resins join the two main players, as well as cocoa, which does not come across as gourmand-sweet, warm woods, and leathery labdanum. From start to finish, the scent does not develop as strongly as one might expect from many other Roja perfumes. With most of his fragrances, you can sense how the ingredients flow from top to bottom like an hourglass. But not here. New nuances occasionally pop up, the fruity notes fade after a few hours, and the resins and woods dominate. The scent develops very slowly on my skin and almost merges with it. The base remains present on my skin for a long time and wafts around my nose throughout the day. “Oh, I love looking into your eyes. I love feeling your skin on mine.” Timing - I would wear it in the colder and warmer months in the evening, but also during the day - because I love it so much. It evokes deep emotions in me. And that is exactly what perfume should do! Sillage - I was noticed, I received many compliments. The sillage is initially very strong and only settles after a few hours. The scent is always well perceivable by the wearer, even when they think the sillage doesn't seem that strong anymore. In my opinion, this fragrance can fill rooms well. Yet, as is typical for Roja: the scent is always present, but never overpowering. And so it is in real life: even if we don't always perceive desire, it regularly overwhelms us, and we succumb to temptation. “I feel this tingling in my stomach. This love - I am in seventh heaven.” Longevity - 24+ hours Gender - Unisex

The fragrance pyramid reads really interesting and very fitting for the cold season. Orange, rum, chocolate, it immediately makes me think of a heated room where grog, warm cocoa, and cake specialties are served. Cozy in beautiful armchairs, outside it is bitterly cold and snowing, nice music is playing, and one can truly relax. These thoughts really go through my mind with this scent. It starts with an orange, a bit bitter, sour. However, over time it becomes softer and sweeter. The rum note mixes in and takes some of the sweetness away. Wood is also strongly present here, giving the scent a slightly smoky quality. Now the fragrance seems masculine and very mature to me. But also very noble. It remains somewhat sour throughout, perhaps this is also due to the lemon. However, there is another turn, which is likely due to the vanilla, cocoa, and tonka bean. It becomes sweeter again and more unisex. The cocoa is dark and more bitter than sweet. The vanilla and tonka create for me a fine milk chocolate that blends wonderfully with the rum, the orange/lemon. A beautiful hint of adult sweetness remains. The somewhat difficult struggle through the sourness is therefore rewarded! For me, a rather understated Roja, not too wild, rather simple and not too loud but still has fabulous longevity and strong sillage! Despite the sour characteristic, I have grown to love it and enjoy wearing it at home on cold days as well.

Hello everyone, Today I would like to talk about a very special fragrance, Parfum de la Nuit 2 . Foreword: I recently treated myself to this one, partly because it was used (more on that later) and primarily because I wanted an "old" batch; I have one from 2020! Why an old one? The topic of batches is a very tedious and serious one - but why exactly? Companies like Roja, Xerjoff, MFK, CC, and others have had to adjust their entire lineup from 21 to 22 (IFRA regulations), and for some, the differences from before to after were less severe, while for others, they were really noticeable, even to the point of being quite disappointing. And here at Roja, I find them to be softer, more pleasing, with fewer rough edges, and the performance is not what it used to be... a good example is my Diaghilev Parfum , which used to last almost 17 to 20 hours, while the new one lasts just about 10 hours and is significantly softer... Many also say, yes, but what if the fragrance runs out with an old batch... To that, I always say this: I have xx fragrances and some ML or liters of fragrances. If it happens, it happens; then I can get something new.... How does it smell: It is warm, woody, slightly sweet, slightly smoky, and VERY alcoholic! And that is sooo great! Why? There are more specific directions like this. Certain directions that you don't wear every day. Those directions never lose their charm and magic, and this is the same here! I love these smoky - slightly alcoholic and subtly sweet fragrances, like Herod , Vanille Havane Eau de Parfum , and also Triumph of Bacchus Extrait de Parfum + Carlisle , so you know what VIBE I mean = the rough direction. And the Parfum de la Nuit 2 focuses noticeably on the alcoholic aspect. It might even resemble Enigma pour Homme Parfum , which is DEFINITELY mine - mine is from 2015 (!) and the Enigma pour Homme Parfum has that cola note = the Parfum de la Nuit 2 does not; it plays with COGNAC, and not just fleetingly as is often the case, but for a very long time, and certain notes and developments harmonize beautifully over time! In the boozy direction, in a sophisticated (wealthy - silly word, I know) gentleman style, it is my reference. How does it come across and when would I recommend it? All year round, but only in the evenings! At parties, in bars, cocktail evenings, dining out, and on dates. How does it come across - absolutely great. (For the right character (also visually), a 15 out of 10 = safe) If you want exactly that + are looking for it... = here! (I have mine, and it has come to stay!) However, it has one big problem, and that is its price. One doesn't need to sugarcoat it or anything.... it is a fact that it is astronomical and less justified, etc. I would love to recommend it, and very much so, but not at that price, but do give it a try! And now, have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______ (Now the same as almost always - because it applies!) Now to the topic of luxury: As you can see in part in my profile, I have really smelled many fragrances, and there are fragrances where you can smell a certain (sometimes) strong synthetic quality, and you quickly realize that some fragrance houses focus more on quantity than quality, while there are others where you can tell "oh come on, let's put in more + better ingredients," and you can smell that at the end of the day. A brief note on packaging, bottle, sprayer: I’ll keep it short: I give a 10 out of 10 in every category, and I know very well that tastes are very different. So if someone honestly rates this with a 7 or less... - PHEW. Beautiful and very high-quality cap, nice timeless bottle design, etc.... so I find it very hard to rate it differently, and I say this not because I like or dislike a brand! Now a quick note on my opinion: I am not sponsored, influenced by anyone, receiving money, or anything else. I approach the topic of perfume as I am, honestly; everything else is not my style. My true personal opinion is very VALUABLE to me, and I hope perhaps ;) that this is noticeable. If I don't like something, such as packaging, bottle, sprayer, or H/S, I will communicate that too!

I don’t have the greatest knowledge and I haven’t been in the perfume scene for long, so I’ll describe it for people at my level: - if you want to read a more detailed professional version, check out my bro sirbennyone I got a small sample of the fragrance and I have to say one thing upfront - this scent is a mf.

In the range of "Parfums de la Nuit" fragrances by Roja, I was particularly intrigued at first glance by "Parfum de la Nuit 2 | Roja Parfums," which sounded appealing due to its often-mentioned association with whisky or general alcohol notes. The fragrance pyramid also immediately caught my attention, as rum and labdanum were listed.
Very flowery scent. waterlily and magnolia are the dominant notes. The drydown is flowery and a bit powdery even. Some may say a slight aquatic perhaps. Not my kind of scent

Water Calligraphy is a nicely presented and skilfully composed floral aquatic. I'm not a huge fan of aquatic scents, but whenever I get the chance to smell an aquatic of this calibre, using quality ingredients, I can understand why people love them. It is best enjoyed during the heat of the day. This fragrance is predominantly focused on water lily and sweet, dewy jasmine. It smells rather pretty on the skin, and even the tart opening of grapefruit goes down a treat. It is definitely a fragrance that has the ability to grow on you. In terms of creativity, I feel it somewhat lacking. Many comparisons can be drawn from the very popular Issey Miyake L'eau d'Issey, which is a staple in almost every aquatic lover's wardrobe. I find its somewhat generic approach disheartening. I hoped to discover a new and exciting take on an aquatic that hadn't been done to death. I wish that the vetiver accord in the drydown was stronger, and more earthy. In this composition it presents itself as salty and woodsy, which is certainly pleasant but nowhere near as striking as it should be. Overall, Water Calligraphy is fresh, crisp and summery with a slight oceanic twist. It seems to be more of a hit with men than it is with women. Many have agreed that the scent is well-constructed, however the price does pose a slight concern. Is it really worth the big bucks? In terms of aquatics, Water Calligraphy is easily one of the nicest. It's a slightly different path for By Kilian, but I'm rather liking the risks they're willing to take for their consumers. I won't be buying a full bottle, but that's not to say that I didn't thoroughly enjoy it.

So far, I had a very specific image of Kilian in my mind: powerful, extravagant, and sometimes quite oriental luxury fragrances. This has changed with Water Calligraphy. I had to test it long-term twice to believe it. All the notes I hoped to find in WC (hahaha - you get it..) because I like them, e.g. jasmine, cardamom, do not reveal themselves to me or not noticeably. From beginning to end, I practically only smell water lily, oceanic, slightly sweet, slightly green, but too dominant for me. A slight grapefruit peel note that occasionally appears makes the scent appealing to me, but I am still puzzled, as overall it feels very familiar and also very un-Kilian. Is this supposed to be a summer fragrance? Is this a fresh Kilian, in contrast to the otherwise heavy ones? I am one big question mark.

It seems that Kilian wants to conquer a new customer segment, or why else would they have oriented themselves olfactorily towards the currently prevailing mainstream taste with these two new releases? Water Calligraphy also feels immediately familiar to me! Such shallow scent trails have been wafting through all the department stores in Hamburg on warm days for quite some time. In contrast to Bamboo Harmony, this Kilian has a bit more assertiveness and fills the space somewhat better. I can't discern a great scent progression. The fragrance remains constant with its floral-watery and pseudo-Asian fresh accord. Even though there is an effort here to spread the magic of Asia with a shallow, light floral scent, it doesn't even come close to succeeding. A Japanese brand did it better years ago. Kenzo's Parfum d'Été goes olfactorily in a similar direction, but with much more finesse and, above all, statement.

At first, I thought it was due to my stubborn cold that I perceived Water Calligraphy as just a fleeting scent. But even now, days later, when I am relatively recovered, the fragrance still comes across as quite minimalist. The supposed grapefruit peel is almost nonexistent. Instead, jasmine and cherry blossom are much more apparent to me. OK, there's a hint of cardamom and the faintest touch of magnolia also joining the mix. The rest fades away somewhere between imagination and mere fantasy. So, what remains for me is rather a blurred image of a fine, yet somewhat reserved fragrance with floral notes and a slight creaminess. I could also say that "WC" reminds me of a subtly perfumed night cream for older ladies. No, this Water Calligraphy is certainly not a work of art - but it's also not a poorly mixed generic water. However, I expect something more interesting and fascinating from Kilian. This one feels too tame, too timid, and interchangeable for me.

This is quite an outstanding Kilian ... going down! Because I believe I have never smelled anything more trivial from this hyper-expensive brand. Definitely not worth a long, creative comment. The entire Asian Tales collection is a flop for me, even though Bamboo Harmony was somewhat better.

The opening is an enjoyable blast of tart berry juice and sparkling synthetics. As it dries down it remains very fruity and sparkly with a fresh peony note and the suggestion of some low key white florals, cottony musk and just the tiniest smidgeon of clean patchouli. The overall effect is fresh-fruity, bright, optimistic, and frankly effervescent. It is not as sweet as you would think based on the notes. Those who have likened it to champagne are right on the money IMO. To those who are wary of trying something with a calone note, have no fear. Calone is used judiciously and to great effect here as an accent to the fruitiness. There is not cucumber/melon here, no 90's aquatic vibe. I suspect that the calone in tandem with some soft aldehydes are responsible for the sparkly effervescent quality. Final verdict: Fun and easy to wear, perfect for someone who wants a fruitier and less patchouli forward option than Miss Dior (2012) or Coco Mad. Way, way, less sweet than LVEB and Flowerbomb and with a much less woody base note than either of them. Casual and flirty.

A juicy strawberry with a patchouli backbone rounds out the opening. There is a tanginess that almost calls to mind cheesecake or shortcake. The delicious opening lasts about 30 minutes or so, by far the most exciting stage of this fragrance. As time goes on, the berry calms down and blends into a familiar sweetened patchouli heart. Somewhat more generic but still highly enjoyable. Unfortunately, it all fizzles out into something that smells like a Victorias secret spray after about 2 hours. Sweet, berry, musky, sits very close to the skin. Similar to the dry down of Parisienne, but far weaker. Disappointing. I like this fragrance and I see comparisons to Miss Dior Cherie and maybe even the 2012 Miss Dior.. In the opening. The dry down just isn't it. If you have the cash to lay down to respray this supposed EDP every 2 hours, it's worth it! If not, go ahead and give this one a pass.

I had bought a bottle in 2016 when it first came out. Now, I tested the most recent batch at a Sephora and it’s definitely been reformulated. It used to be a muskier, more refined perfume, patchouli-dominant and still with a youthful aspect. But now, all I can smell are pink fruits like raspberry and strawberry.

This is very, very fruity. It reminds me of a liquid soap and hand lotion from a Bath and Body Works type store—in my case, it was a Fruits and Passion soap/lotion set I got for Christmas once...I think it was called Cranberry Love. It’s an okay fruit scent, especially for inexpensive hand soap and lotion, but I’m kind of surprised to be reminded of it by a high end perfume from YSL. There is an echo in here that reminds me of Calvin Klein’s Escape, which I find quite pleasant. Not sure what it is though. Probably the orange, oak moss, jasmine, musk and cedar, which the two have in common. Also, I always detected a calone note in Escape, even though it’s not listed. However, Mon Paris is just too fruity for me to wear easily. The berries are overpowering despite my caution in applying. I’d say I put on half a spray, and it is a beast.

This fragrance doesn't seem to get anything right. The scent starts with a sickly sweet berries note, its generic and you cannot discern any individual fruit or citrus in it. It needed the citrus too, for complexity and toning down the sweetness but I could not find it. It quickly moves into a dense white floral. Its just generic white floral and it makes the perfume feel even heavier than the opening notes did. The middle notes do not last long either. The scent then quickly disappears altogether. I caught a tiny bit of citrus in the dry down but that was it. No earthiness, musk, woodiness, or anything. This scent lasted maybe a hour and half on my skin and the projection was only noticeable for the first 30 minutes. The 10mL is $33 but that is even too much for this fragrance if you ask me.

What was once my signature fragrance has been altered to a shell of itself. I believe changes have been made to this fragrance. My original bottle was 30 ml EDP, purchased sometime around launch (maybe 2017). I wore it almost daily until around autumn of 2019.

when I tested it, and a cloud of fruity-flowery notes involved me . In particular I smelled the raspberry notes and I found them very gourmand , maybe a little girly, but pleasant. The heart and base notes arrived later and on my skin remained a good mix , well balanced.

Mon Paris was the perfume that started my addiction with perfumes. From the opening till the dry down, the berries dominate in this fragrance. The opening is juicy and very sweet but also a bit tart. As it dries down, it becomes less sweet on my skin and the floral and patchouli notes starts to appear a bit more.

Reminds me of strawberry champagne. Sparkly floral strawberry. It is light and airy at the top and dries to a warmer, somewhat decadent floral. It is not a fragrance I would repurchase as I think I have matured out of it. It is nothing special and maybe I've had it for too long but it smells like something I could get at Bath & Body Works.

I love strawberries and I love sweet things (but not overly sweet fragrances) and this is just it! It's a very tender and close to the skin fragrance. When recently sprayed, it's all berries and citrus, just like a nice, refreshing strawberry lemonade.

A perfume that is definitely not for everyone. It is less wearable than the other two in the PDLN series, but those who do like this scent - will enjoy it very much. A male perfume, for a winter night. You should dress accordingly when wearing this perfume. I'm definitely waiting for cold nights to wear it 9/10.

This perfume is so sophisticated that only those who delve into its scent understand how special it is! A scent so masculine and so sensual. A perfume that throws you into Peaky Blinders suit hat with whiskey in hand and a cigarette. As soon as you spray it you get a strong power of Cistus and Labdanum throughout! With touches of clove that wraps up this whole special scent. A scent for people who radiate presence and power for me 9/10

Before a full depth reviews: PARFUM de la NUIT 1 Very sensual and seductive, not the easiest one of these three. There are light leathery tones and an animalic touch in this -very sophisticated though- with soft Vanilla. This is definitely my favorite and it performs best on my skin of these three. Absolutely stunning and sexy, a tad naughty, resinous scent. PDLN1 is my favorite even if now while wearing them all I want to have them all. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. Roja Dove was referred to as the pornographer of perfumery by a journalist a few years ago. It is quite telling to conclude from Roja's clothing style, which is indeed rather pornographic, whether he likes this designation. Because Roja Dove was thrilled by this label and immediately got to work. The result: the "Parfums de la Nuit" series. Three perfumes with distinctly risqué backgrounds: olfactory bed bunnies. Three playmates that are different in their essence. The scents of the Parfums de la Nuit series stage our very own basic human needs: three odes to bed-related amorous activities. Roja writes: “Desire calls when darkness falls.” The darkness evokes the pleasures and desires that slumber within us during the day. Sexually charged fragrances, not romantics like Roja's Profumi D’Amore scents (Amore Mio, Ti Amo, Un Amore Eterno). Number 1 is dedicated to the big cat. Hunt the flesh, kill the flesh, eat the flesh. To get straight to the point: delicate souls may not want to read this comment and should click the red report flag below immediately. Because Roja does not compose here for the faint of heart. The big cat lurks before warm, leathery, soft beaver musk in the background; I wouldn't want to rule out a drop of civet either. This underlying beaver musk vibe runs through the entire scent. Number 1 is most closely related to Enslaved (Clove, Labdanum) and somewhat more distantly related to Fetish pour Homme, which is overall more overtly lustful, leathery, and oriental in its spiciness. Parfum de la Nuit Number 1 is very sensual, sexually charged, very warm, leathery, spicy, and resinous-sweet. Number 1 starts with a bergamot flash that lasts only a moment. Bam, then the little dress is gone. The big cat is not interested in an extensive foreplay or pseudo-original corset creations. Then, typical Roja labdanum spreads out. Leathery-bright, warm like the lower back, erotic, animalistic. A scent as if you were pulling the string of the big cat with your nose, a hint of nothing, while sniffing at her excited skin. After a few minutes, a lust-fluttering clove unfolds. Reminiscent of the scent of excited genitals. Freshly showered genitals, as Charlotte Roche would complain. Powerful, spicy-aromatic, warm, not dirty, sweet-powdery, very erotic, sexual. A hint of slightly bitter saffron teases it out further. After about half an hour of big cat cuddling, the wild kitten pulls back a bit for a moment. First, balsam gives a warm softness, with just a touch of vetiver emphasizing the green facet of the balsamic scent impression. Soon, bright, sweet to aromatic light woods become noticeable. A little less dirty and smoky patchouli adds depth to the scent of the night. And after 1-2 hours, suddenly full vanilla is present. Full like lips. Red lustful lips. Warmly radiant, powdery and sweet. The labdanum comes back stronger to the forefront, slightly more leathery than before. Towards the base, more and more golden resin joins in. I mainly smell styrax and benzoin. Warm, almost hot, somewhere between honey-like and ambery, lustful, sweet, and very, very sensual. A scent as if you were sensually and intimately massaging warm skin. Naked, hot bodies, intimate, lustful. You don't know whether you are already taking off or still lying there trembling. Does Parfum de la Nuit Number 1 smell pornographic now? The background of the scent is warm, leathery, soft beaver musk. At the beginning, bam, the little dress of the big cat is already gone. The big cat is not interested in foreplay. The wild kitten initially presents itself demanding, wild, purposeful, focused on the lower back, provocative. Then it takes a short pause, cooling down a bit with bright wood, balsam, and vetiver. The scent changes its character. Patchouli gives it a nocturnal depth; the wild kitten is no longer arbitrary in its lower back animalistic passions and desires; it is now directed towards a specific person. Number 1 now smells of love - like the bed linen. Of couple love. Towards the base, Number 1 becomes very sensual, very warm, sweet-resinous. Caressing, massaging, building up, overflowing, melting, floating in heaven. Parfum de la Nuit Number 1 shows the typical behavior of an extrait. It lasts easily more than 12 hours on the skin. The wearer feels enveloped in an erotic aura, perceiving the scent as seemingly close to the skin. However, when you leave the room and re-enter, you perceive Number 1 as present in the room.

Hello, hello, hallo! :D Today I will describe the fragrance “Parfum de la Nuit 1,” a scent from the “Parfum de la Nuit” line, of which there are three. These fragrances are meant to bring forth the inner desires, lust, cravings, and longings that slumber deep within all of us and rarely surface during the day. But when night falls… then… BATMAN appears!!! Mu ha ha ha ha!!! *sigh* Of course, this is typical. If I write “Batman,” I’m considered a nerd. If I mention something about the dark side of the Force (because of the darkness of the night), I’m seen as a freak. But if I had written that we all become lust-driven beings at night, I would once again be labeled as perverse, someone who only thinks about dirty things and desperately needs a girlfriend. That’s what you think of me, right?? Okay, okay, I may not have a girlfriend, but I don’t think ONLY about dirty things… every two minutes I think about Star Wars and every three minutes about cats… which would mean that I don’t think about dirty things every minute, but at least only every three minutes or so!! Hm… Well, fine, I guess I am a little perverse and freakish… it fits the cliché quite well, doesn’t it? *sigh* Aargh… :D Anyway, Roja Dove, the perfumer of all these fragrances, also likes the title that some have given him: He is said to be the Pornographer of scents… so who’s perverse now, huh?? The Fragrance: So, in the top note, we have bergamot. I don’t smell it at all. Instead, the fragrance starts off slightly floral, but with a dry-spicy scent. It’s like flowers in Mediterranean places that grow in large fields during the summer and are roasted by the blazing sun. This is both a beautiful sight and gives you the feeling of truly being on vacation when you stroll through such fields. And since it also has a resinous scent, I can smell the cistus, which has a slightly resinous fragrance and primarily grows in dry areas in Mediterranean places like the Mediterranean region. To this dry resinous scent (where the dryness is softened by the resinous quality, making it smell a bit gentler later on), additional notes like saffron and clove fit perfectly, although the cloves are a bit harder to detect. Even though the fragrance remains slightly dry later on and the cistus is still noticeable, it becomes softer overall due to the resinous and other gentle notes like balsamic scents and powdery notes like vanilla and tonka bean. It does acquire a slight sweetness, but I wouldn’t really describe the fragrance as sweet. It is very beautiful and definitely worth trying out. Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is quite good. In fact, it’s really good. You are enveloped in a larger scent cloud, which may seem smaller to you because it comes off a bit dry at times. Others will certainly be able to perceive the fragrance well on you. The longevity is also really good, as the fragrance lasted more than twelve hours on me. The Bottle: The bottle is, as always, extremely high quality. It is partly handcrafted, as the black gemstones in the gilded cap seem to be set by hand, just like the golden label, which is always supposed to be applied by hand. The bottle itself is rectangular and filled with an amber-colored fragrance liquid. It is solid and therefore a bit more difficult to handle with the larger bottles. But it is still beautiful and, above all, extremely high quality, which enhances the feeling of actually holding a luxury product. Yep, the bottle is (once again) very successful. So, somehow the name of the fragrance confuses me. Because the scent smells quite “bright” to me, as described, like I’m walking during the day on vacation in beautiful places and smelling the scent of dry-resinous and sun-roasted flowers. It’s a lovely fragrance, one that makes you happier or brings you good mood. It may not be fresh, but it’s also not really heavy. It feels as if it would bring back summer when you wear the fragrance in autumn or winter, although I think it’s also quite suitable for spring. After a passionate night full of fire and desire, it certainly doesn’t smell like that to me… however, as I mentioned at the beginning, I currently don’t have a girlfriend, so what do I know about passionate fragrances! :D So please be forgiving if I’m totally off and for you the fragrance is the total “porn fragrance,” perhaps just as Mr. Roja Dove envisioned it :D It’s definitely worth testing, especially for those who love the Mediterranean and everything that comes with it, including its fragrances! That’s it! Have a nice evening, a good start to the week, and see you then :)

Three weeks after acquiring this perfume, the act of purchasing it at such an exorbitant price was already an incredible feat that only a true perfume junkie could manage. I now dare to share my impressions in a comment. Cravache's top-notch comment describes this lustful scent very precisely, and none of it is exaggerated!!

Some time ago, I had the pleasure of testing "Le Lion de Chanel | Chanel," a fragrance that offered a fascinating scent through a complex construct of notes centered around the main ingredient, labdanum. Intense, yet finely balanced and very long-lasting. Overall, a lovely experience.

What a fantastic scent! The metaphor with the big cat describes the perfume excellently. The fragrance doesn't waste any time and immediately offers what it promises: an erotic, seductive aura. The top note is hardly noticeable, and the cistus is also more in the background.

A relatively positive recommendation on Pure Oud from me. It has a rubbery, slightly medicinal Gaiac heart mixed with real Oud that I find intriguing and is keeping me interested in smelling it throughout its development. Amber, and maybe a hint of musk join the Oud to form the base of the scent. I have to give By Kilian some points for using real oud in its composition, and keeping to the scent's name in spirit. Projection is above average here, but longevity is only average. This is not the easiest scent to wear, but still nice on the whole. I would say 3.5/5. If this more straight Presentation of oud scent is too much for you, then the other By Kilian Arabian Nights oud scents may be more appealing to you... Rose Oud for a Rose dominant oud, and Incense Oud for a reference incense scent that may not contain much or even any real oud, but smells incredible nonetheless.

Pure Oud is the racehorse of the Western oud-based fragrances; all sinew and nerve, and not an inch of fat to spare. Kilian could have easily named this Oud Noir or Dark Oud, because Pure Oud really does convey the inky, matte darkness of a moonless night sky. It smells like a black leather jacket tinctured into a pool of black tar and then vaporized into a mist of gasoline. Pure Oud draws a line around itself and stays within it. Real oud oil has a smell that spills messily out over every line you've drawn for yourself; the brazenly-named Pure Oud (it is purely synthetic) is self-contained. But they do share a common denominator - both smell other-worldly and somewhat stark. For me, it is the Western-based oud fragrance that comes closest to mimicking the smell of real oud oil. Not a sour, fermented-smelling Hindi or Assam oud oil, but one of those aged, dry oud oils where you can pick out hints of leather, dried fruit, melting plastic lunch boxes, and smoke. Caveat: Pure Oud is a minimalist take on a maximalist smell, i.e., it does not approach the complexity or range of aromas of real oud oil. Nothing this obviously synthetic can come close to copying something so rudely natural. But the experience of using oud oils and attars is not interchangeable with or comparable to using traditional fragrance; one is a quiet, more private experience geared toward internal contemplation; the other is a projection of oneself to the wider world. We shouldn't keep holding up one against the other in a race for authenticity. Prefer instead that benchmark of Guy Robert's: Does it smell good? And yes, Pure Oud does smell good  very good indeed. I find Pure Oud to be very quiet, but long-lasting. Sometimes, to turn up the volume a bit, I re-spray during the day, twice, or even three times. This way, it builds up on the skin in layers of translucent ink - leather upon rubber upon gasoline, until it finally pushes off the skin in a sulky swirl of woodsmoke.

Notes: Saffron, Copaiva Balsam, Oud, Amber, Cypriol, Guaiac Wood and Labdanum Perfumer: Calice Becker I love Oud and really enjoying Pure Oud by Kilian. Yes, the Oud here is on the synthetic side. This is a pretty linear scent, Smokey, a bit Spicy oudy woody fragrance.

Gasoline, used oil, nitro thinner, burnt rubber, acetone, burnt wood … no, my nose can't take it anymore. That's enough! Is this perfumer's art or the result of a chemical accident? I recognize this scent mixture. Lolita's comment reminded me of it again. I know this from the time when I worked in a steel mill - at a rolling mill for rail profiles. When "building" or repairing rolls, we were up to our elbows in a sludge of old oil, bearing grease, and tar pitch. Afterward, we scrubbed our skin in the washroom with harsh hand cleaner and soap to get rid of the dirt and, above all, the smell. The work uniforms went into the washing machine for two cycles. After the first cycle, they looked clean but still smelled of oil and solvents. Do I want to smell like I just had a grueling shift in the rolling mill? No, why would I. Pure Oud is sold in the "Arabian Nights" line. I don't smell any Arabian nights here. I have to say, the theme misses the mark. "Steelworkers night shift" would have been more fitting.

Hats off, Mme. Becker! An Aoud fragrance that even I like, although I am not a big fan of this often overpowering material. Generally, in my opinion, it tends to trumpet with a high falsetto voice over the orchestra, in a penetrance that I find rarely bearable. But there are exceptions: 'Black Aoud' by Montale is one such exception - a beautiful, almost intoxicating blend of rose, geranium, and Aoud, or 'Fetish' by Neil Morris - a fragrance that emphasizes the rubbery and leathery facets of Aoud, while simultaneously charging its medical coldness and stiffness with a good dose of erotic vibes. And Pure Oud by Kilian is also an exception, and what an exception it is! Gone is the falsetto voice, replaced by a deep, organ-like bass - what a relief! And the often-criticized haughty, medical tone: also gone - another relief! No more aseptic-arrogant chief physician with a piercing falsetto voice, instead, an oil-stained auto mechanic, wafted by the fumes of whole stacks of tires and canisters full of lubricants. This fragrance has something irresistibly distinctly masculine about it - I like that. However, it does not gain its masculinity through the popular enrichment of aromatic fougères in the 70s and early 80s with an excess of animal secretions, which gave so many fragrances of that time either a sweat or urine note, or even a mix of both. No, Pure Oud avoids that unpleasantness. The mechanic has showered after getting up and then put on fresh underwear. His distinctly masculine scent is solely derived from his environment soaked in oil and turpentine. One searches in vain for flowers, as well as fruity and spicy notes: they simply do not exist, not even hidden (aside from a hint of saffron, but saffron doesn’t really smell 'spicy', at least not in the classical sense, but rather bitter-woody). But resins, and plenty of them: labdanum, myrrh, and amber - all without sweet embellishments - and oily balsams. However, not those that maintain the suppleness of human skin, but rather those that weatherproof untreated wood. And as much as this fragrance smells of a workshop, it would suit a well-groomed man of mature age, wearing a well-fitted suit and perhaps holding a smoky whisky in his hand, a man like Sean Connery, fantastically. This fragrance could also unfold wonderfully on a woman who wants to emphasize her masculine facets - the contrast makes it! But, as mentioned: Pure Oud is absolutely not sweet (yet warm and sensual), does without a floral bouquet, and is hardly surpassable in its oily and heavy earthiness. It is an assault on our sense of smell, an assault from an unexpected side: grounded and unpretentious, upright, honest, and humorous, in contrast to all that over-refined, cerebral, and artificial. This fragrance is real, it is truly 'pure' - and that makes it so irresistible, at least for me! Thanks to Maharanih for the sample! It is quite possible that Pure Oud will be the first Kilian fragrance in my collection (despite the outrageous price...).

So, this is supposed to be "Pure Oud." However, the fragrance pyramid already contradicts this name. I have no doubt that there is somehow Oud in it; you can certainly sense it - so much for the name of this scent. And what is it supposed to cost? 295 € for 50 ml - Aha! Pure Oud is very far from the classic Arabic Oud perfumes.

I first encountered Pure Oud by Kilian at the beginning of my perfume journey. Oud has fascinated me from the start, as for many, everything began with Tom Ford Oud Wood, due to numerous appearances of the fragrance in interviews and YouTube blogs.

If you're not an oud fanatic, and even tend to be slightly averse, the name is almost more off-putting than the price. But then you think, oh, it can't be that bad, By Kilian won't go too far. Right and wrong.

What is it about this Oud hype in so many niche fragrances? In Arabic perfumes, this scent component has long been common, but I get the impression that Western markets are now oversaturated with Oud niche fragrances. I have hardly tested any Oud scents so far because I didn't feel any interest based on the idea of an aromatic incense wood.

We know Yves Saint Laurent in the world of perfumery for several masterpieces. When I approached the world of fragrances as a teenager, the trending perfumes of this brand were Opium (1977) Parfum , Paris Eau de Toilette , Kouros Eau de Toilette and Jazz (1988) Eau de Toilette . The first three were rare, super-powerful animals, while the last was already something more tamed and commercial. Many other fragrances came out on the market long before these, but the ones I mentioned were around at the time. Then came the unexpected, polarizing and disruptive "M7 (Eau de Toilette) | Yves Saint Laurent", followed by a plethora of L'Homme Eau de Toilette and La Nuit de L'Homme Eau de Toilette with their flankers. And so did Black Opium Eau de Parfum . Two new fragrances have recently arrived on the shelves, namely the feminine Libre Eau de Parfum and the masculine Y. As I've tried and reviewed some of the Y flankers, I thought it was time to look at the original, a free sample I received a while ago. A few good things have been said about EDT, but it was generic and forgettable. I like it now that I've had the chance to try it for myself. You may wonder what it is, so here's my take on it. Firstly, I would classify it as a fresh, aromatic, modern fougére and semi-aquatic perfume with light woody notes. Y EDT opens with an energizing freshness from sparkling aldehydes and soapy citrus fruits, which give a luminous, joyful, and floral sensation. The aldehydes are distinct and give Y a solar arrangement, which is very refreshing and effervescent, like sparkling flavoured water. I feel powdery shades coming from the violet leaves, slightly watery and dusty. I let the booze vanish, and a creamy lemon comes to the fore along with the aromatic sage, which brings a herbaceous tone right from the start. Thanks to the blend of citrus, herbs and a warm, musky undertone that is clear from the first spritz, I get an atmosphere that belongs to the fougére family. Something immediately familiar to me reminds me of several famous men's fragrances out there, some edges in common with "Defy | Calvin Klein". Y is a relatively straightforward scent, which doesn't undergo much development, and the next chord that hits my nose is a violet leaf with a hint of ginger that adds some spiciness. The violet leaf is very prominent, providing its familiar powdery aroma. The heart, formed mainly of green geranium and herbaceous sage, gives a touch to the aromatic and dry fragrance. In short, bitter puffs arise from the sage leaf. My nose is sensitive enough to sense this bitterness inherent in clary sage. If you know the aqueous accord, you too will capture the watery and dusty atmosphere of the violet leaf. The base moves into a more decadent and more seductive territory, resting on soft notes of not too heavy but dry wood and a sort of dense amber. There is some cedarwood in there, a touch of balsamic fir and marine ambergris warming it. A powerful woody and balsamic base contrast with the sparkling freshness of the beginning. The balsamic tones stand out. I can feel them clearly if I bring my wrist to my nose. Deep, earthy, animal-like. Although Y has many other notes, it is the aromatic and salty ones that shine and dominate. Not bad, especially if you like amber types of fragrances rich in sage and violet. It retains its freshness on the bottom with a sweet and airy character and a solid woody base with a sprinkle of sage. Head, heart and tail come together in a clean, easy-to-wear fragrance suitable for various casual and professional environments. Y feels lighter and brighter than other fragrances that other people often compare. My final word, I think Y EDT is a pleasant scent, so it's fun and non-polarizing. It is a rather versatile fragrance, but I would prefer to wear it during the day rather than at night, in the warm seasons, a good perfume suitable for the office because it is harmless. THIS WOULD BE A CONTENDER when I need to reach for a scent that smells good but subtly gives me a sense of cleanliness. The projection is average to good. I feel it, and those around me should get too. It smells like a fresh shower. It is very refreshing, with a hint of woodiness and musk. As for the projection, I'd say it's pretty moderate; Y EDT's sillage isn't enormous, and longevity is good, but not insane, on my skin. Makes it perfect for spring or summer, or an all-rounder if you're looking for a scent for the day but would look great in warm weather. Since it is so light, it is very versatile. You can wear it in just about any setting, from going to school, college or university, to work in the office or out for lunch. I base the review on a decant I have owned since January 2022. -Elysium

Perhaps This scent is called Y simply because Y was the initial of the name of the great couturier Yves Saint Laurent, but this letter hides a whole world of ancient symbols : it's the choice between two ways, it's the magic stick, it's the second coordinate in the cartesian system, it's the masculine strength, it's the ambiguity and so on. This scent is almost magic: I tested directly on my feminine skin for the first time just today and I fell in love with it. The moment I sprayed it I immediately smelled a very particular scent of "old lipsticks", something powdery-aromatic which becomes warm after a few minutes without being too "masculine" and heavy. Aldehydes and frankincense are very noticeable maybe covering a little the citrusy notes and the ginger, but what I love is the balsamic touch and the ambergris at the base. In the edt version, this scent has a discrete sillage, quite soft and gentle, perfect for a woman too. The simple and almost minimal bottle is refined and classy, just like the man who could wear this scent. In this concentration it could be worn in the mid season and by day, at the office too for its particular discretion and its sense of "clean".

My first impression upon smelling Y, is of just how incredibly fresh this fragrance is. Very cool, crisp, airy, and quite clean. I like it. The bergamot is light, but adds a great citrus juiciness to the center. The aldehydes are distinct and give Y a bright and sunny disposition. Add to that, an ambergris note which isn’t too heavy but plays off of the other ingredients, much as it does in Creed fragrances. The opening is delightful. The next layer to hit my nose, is a bit of violet leaf and ginger. The ginger brings forth a light spice and the violet leaf isn’t super prominent, but does provide its familiar aroma. Y is actually a pretty straightforward scent that doesn’t undergo too much development.

I recently ran out of this fragrance and I am looking to buy a new one. This is a very good scent for daily use and it's hard not to love. It is a mainly fresh and little bit spicy fragrance. Whether you're going to school, the office or the gym it is an easy reach and will leave you satisfied every time. I would definitely recommend this to anyone especially someone looking to get into fragrances or someone who just wants something simple to smell good.

In the interview for his first internship, he mentioned that as a little boy he always wanted to be the bank in Monopoly - and how he then won the stock market game of his local savings bank in the U12 category with a self-developed system. After the McKinsey summer camp, he was immediately taken into the Young Talents program, and of course, he is also a scholarship holder of the Study Foundation. He uses two of his vacation days to hang up nesting boxes for owls - he doesn't really care about the owls, but: 'I haven't had any charity on my CV this quarter.' He actually means it that way. In his first job, he quickly realized that unfortunately not all juniors can be promoted at the same time - and that it’s really not worth staying late on Wednesdays because the boss always has to leave right on time and therefore doesn’t see it anyway. Long before the company car eligibility is even within reach, he has the configuration ready in the drawer - smallest engine, but with a Bose sound system and of course not the uncool stock rims - and he still finds the 'Your poverty disgusts me' sticker somewhat amusing. He has never greeted the cleaning lady, who always vacuums loudly when he wants to make personal calls. He has an eye for what the bosses wear - those who have something to say - the controlling team leader with the silver gaze, who comes in summer in a bus driver shirt, is totally irrelevant to him. But since the drinks for Saturday Tinder dates don’t pay for themselves, the Corneliani suits and John Lobb shoes are unfortunately still not really within reach. He did treat himself to a nice little fragrance recently, one that suits him: top performer, tough, present, and in the office supply and copy room, 'where getting things done is actually really too expensive for him,' as he recently said somewhat jokingly, still lingering for hours. Conclusion: Yves Saint Laurent's Y - pronounced as a Frenchman would say 'I-grec', according to the French pronunciation of the letter Y - is a perfume for and like Jan-Hendrik (who could just as well be named Lars-Friedrich or Carl-Philipp, but double names - the first one syllabic, the second two syllables - are surprisingly common. And if anyone with one of the aforementioned names is reading this: You are of course not meant!). Ambitious. Hotshot. On the surface, quite performative. Almost no creative input, but thick-skinned. Pushy regarding visibility, but ultimately nothing original to offer. And not really likable.

For my birthday, I decided to spoil myself. Like, really spoil. Probably, even some fragrance lovers like myself could call me crazy. I spent more than €200 on 7,5 ml Roja Amber Aoud Absolue Preciéux. Worth every cent, though. Honestly, this is one of the most beautiful, mature, and refined scents ever. At least, from what I smelled, of course. I don't mean to overhype it, but I have to say that it is hard to think that such a great fragrance exists at all. This is rose and oud perfume, with a juicy fig and the deepest, most sensual, and powerful amber. Wearing this perfume is a fragrant journey. Opens with a blast of citruses and then gets darker. One after another, layers unfold. Softly sweetened fig flirts with rose de Mai, and you can feel the spicy warmness of amber coming out and the reserved touch of aoud. If you compare it to the EDP, the scent itself is very similar. However, the wearing experience is something else because it is in a very concentrated form. When spraying this one, it feels as if I am wrapping myself in some sort of luxurious cashmere. It is so soft and gentle, lends on the skin smoothly, and wearing this, feels almost like a royal ritual. And the performance – well, it is way stronger than the EDP. But it is not about the performance; it is about the feeling it gives.

The acquisition of an unsprayed 7.5ml atomizer of Amber Aoud Absolue Precieux (Aoud AP) presents a classic collector's dilemma: is this a sacred display piece or an intense experience meant to be worn? The decision to test it reveals that Aoud AP truly lives up to its name, delivering an even richer, deeper, and more concentrated interpretation of the already iconic Amber Aoud. Scent Analysis: Sweetness, Spirituality, and the Cool Twist The Opening – Holy Sweetness: The initial spray is marked by a sudden rush of extreme, almost overwhelming sweetness (significantly amplified compared to the standard Amber Aoud). This intensity, combined with deep oriental resins and spice (Saffron, Cinnamon), immediately evokes associations with sacred shrines, mosques, and incense for those familiar with the cultural smells of the Orient. It is a luxurious spiritual sweetness, a profile often mirrored in potent creations like Aaron Terence Hughes’ Onyx Extreme. The Creamy, Nostalgic Accord: The fragrance quickly settles into a distinctive creamy texture. It possesses a nostalgic quality, with some finding it reminiscent of a high-end, luxurious hand or face cream from decades past. This creamy-floral (Fig, Rose, Ylang-Ylang) note is crucial, acting as a rich, comforting buffer to the potent sweetness and Aoud. Aoud, Chocolate & Honey: The heart features an Aoud note that is not aggressive but is instead enveloped in a deep, gourmand sweetness that suggests a combined accord of chocolate and honey. This scent is a masterclass in tension and balance, pushing the olfactory threshold for sweetness without crossing into cloying territory, thanks to the grounding Ambergris and the contrasting brightness. The "Cool Cassis" Drydown – The Signature Surprise The Drydown delivers a fascinating and unexpected development: beyond the warm, opulent Amber base, a sharp, cool freshness emerges in the later stages. This cooling effect is highly specific, vividly recalling the aromatic, lightly fruity menthol of an Airwaves Cool Cassis chewing gum. This contrast—warm, sweet, resinous Aoud versus the fresh, cool, "cassis" edge—is what elevates the Aoud AP, preventing it from remaining purely a traditional "shrine-style" oriental and lending it a unique, addictive quality that compels one to smell it (but only briefly, to avoid the saturation effect). Performance and Wearability Sillage and Longevity: Performance is, as expected from an Absolue Precieux, immense. Sillage is powerful for the first 2-3 hours, and longevity is outstanding, particularly on clothing. Wear Occasion: Due to its density and imposing character, Aoud AP is best reserved for closed, large environments (banquet halls, theaters, high-end restaurants) where its majestic sillage can project without overpowering. Unisex Appeal: While the scent garners significant positive attention, particularly from women, its rich and creamy depth confirms its classification as a powerful and perfectly Unisex statement fragrance. In Summary: Amber Aoud Absolue Precieux is the epitome of creamy, spiritual, and sweet opulence, punctuated by an unexpected cooling lift. It ultimately wears like a royal, sweet-fresh Aoud hit—the feeling of applying a deeply luxurious, subtly cooling hand cream before bed in the winter.

In this post, I would like to make a comparison of Amber Aoud Absolue Précieux (Extrait) - Amber Aoud Crystal (Parfum) - and the Amber Aoud dark version (Parfum). One might often wonder what the difference is and which one to ultimately choose :-) At least, I felt that way at the beginning... After some extensive research, many conversations with connoisseurs, and numerous tests, I would like to share one thing upfront and elaborate a bit: The Crystal version is absolutely not inferior to the dark version in any way! Both are parfum versions! The Crystal version is neither weaker nor less long-lasting! The Crystal version differs from the darker version solely in terms of color! The color pigments have been removed through elaborate processes - without affecting the scent! The reason for creating a clear fragrance is - who can guess it.... indeed the stains on clothing! Aoud is dark by nature - and the older and more mature the Aoud is, the darker and more intense it becomes. Since Roja only uses the highest quality raw materials, the Aoud used in the fragrances is also quite dark and leaves stains on light clothing! Aoud fragrances are highly valued in Arab countries, much more than in Europe. Both women and men wear Aoud. Since women in Arab countries predominantly wear black or dark clothing, the dark version of Amber Aoud is very popular and widely spread there. Men mostly wear light or white clothing. Thus, the desire for the beautiful Amber Aoud - without leaving stains - reached Roja - leading to the development of a process to crystallize only the dark pigments from the dark luxury water - without compromising the quality of the fragrance! And tadaaaa --> This is Amber Aoud Crystal! To truly convince myself of this theory, I, of course, conducted a 1:1 "practical" test :-)) On the left is the Crystal version and on the right is the dark version of Amber Aoud: A small spritz of each is enough, and I am in seventh heaven..... *swoon*..... But now back to the test: A sweet, slightly resinous Aoud note with strong amber tones sets the tone... Delicate citrus sprinkles leave a subtle freshness... the lime is truly detectable, fantastic.... Soft flowers (mainly rose?) blend in, everything so finely tuned.... grandiose..... Creamy sandalwood provides that fantastic woody softness that I love.... Spices follow... saffron complements the ever-present oud so incredibly well.... everything just fits.... Later on, an earthy-musty note flashes up... it must be patchouli and oak moss... The scent becomes increasingly complex and multifaceted, truly high perfumery...! During the test, I repeatedly compared my left arm (Crystal) and my right arm (dark version) and I could not detect any difference whatsoever...! So here is my confirmation: the Crystal and the Dark version of Amber Aoud really only differ in color, period. Of course, everyone is free to express their opinion on this, and I am really curious if you see it the same way, dear fragrance friends :-) Well then, the comparison with Amber Aoud Absolue Précieux follows. I tested the Crystal (Parfum) version on my left arm and the Absolue Précieux (Extrait) on my right arm: To avoid explaining the entire progression again, I will now only describe the difference from Absolue Précieux to the previously mentioned fragrance progression of the Parfum version :) The Absolue Précieux starts with a more intense blast of Aoud, powerful and even more robust than the Parfum version.... The oud strikes me as not only worlds more intense but also somewhat more animalistic, stronger, and captivating.... the gentle "pig note" from the parfum, just stronger - not musty-stable, but just stronger (quite a bit stronger).... The concentration of oils in the Absolue Précieux is said to be between 60-65%... According to a reliable source, it is the highest concentration that is still "sprayable"..... In the parfum, the concentration is already between 40-45% - so already quite substantial! In terms of the scent itself, the progression of the Absolue Précieux is indeed very similar to that of the Parfum version.... Individual notes are simply a bit more pronounced..... The Aoud is incredibly beautiful, strong, but stunning.... it seems to caramelize over time, merging with amber... sweet.... animalistic.... powerful..... I perceive the flowers in the Absolue Précieux as slightly less pronounced than in the Parfum version, but the resinous and earthy notes come out a bit more... You can also see a difference on the arm... The parfum leaves a delicate film and then dissipates within about 15-20 minutes... Absolue Précieux leaves a good and slightly oily film, which remains visible on the skin for a bit longer... While the parfum spends a good 8 hours with me, Absolue Précieux has a much longer lasting presence...! I can still perceive Absolue Précieux well the next morning - even though there was a good shower in between... Even if it is more intimate, you can still recognize Absolue Précieux very well.... That is truly grandiose! I would give the parfum an overall rating of 9.5 Absolue Précieux gets a straight 10 from me - it must be love! I hope that my post has helped those who have asked the same questions as I did and I look forward to other insights and opinions :-) Fragrant greetings

…please don’t be too critical, as this is my first review here and it shouldn’t be my last. But I am trying to review the ultimate variation of my signature scent; and believe me: it’s not easy. And then the drydown, which invites me to dream again and again and accompanies me throughout the day. To begin with: I have both the perfume, the Crystal Perfume, and the Absolue Précieux. For me, the perfume and the Crystal are absolutely on par, and the legendary "rubber note" that is supposed to be in the Crystal is something I do not perceive. Perhaps a year ago I would have been a complete Roja disciple who would have accepted anything, but even without my rojarote glasses, I still see no difference. In stark contrast to the Absolue Précieux. For me, it was a (very expensive) blind buy that I have not regretted to this day. The powerful and intense fragrance explosion right upon application is indescribable. I simply lack the words in all the languages I speak. It is just wonderful. A delight for the senses. There’s no other way to describe it. I am the type of perfume lover who often needs 10+x sprays for bliss, but here I have found my master. Two sprays on the neck and you are ready for the day. And the evening. And whatever else may come. This rosy, oudy, and floral masterpiece enchants me every time I get to wear it. And this has nothing to do with being over 50; it is simply a masterpiece that is unparalleled. With every movement, you have this wonderful scent in your nose - and let’s be honest: we wear our fragrances only for ourselves, that’s clear; but a compliment - and you are sure to get one with this perfume - is of course good for every perfume lover’s soul. So, for those who have the necessary pocket money, and who really want to ascend to heaven, you should at least test this fragrance, as it is, in my opinion, the best there is. Period.

Although I have been part of this wonderful community for a while, I have enjoyed the development of perfumes and fragrance enthusiasts from the background. With this exceptionally well-composed scent, one makes a presence. The very strong sillage makes one immediately noticeable. However, this presence is not tainted by feelings of inferiority. This fragrance has nothing to prove. It is simply so majestic that one can only bow down. The scent opens with a symphony of lightly citrus-spicy accord, accompanied by an Oud-Amber-Patchouli composition, along with floral components. ...can pack it in. With AAAP, you choose a statement. However, never any form of understatement. This fragrance polarizes. You need quite a bit of experience in the world of perfume to give this scent the love it deserves. It impresses with an absolutely solid composition.

That I come across fragrances that are actually labeled as "women's scents" is relatively rare. This usually only happens when my wife treats herself to a new bottle that I haven't encountered yet, and I want to share my thoughts on it. As part of my re-testing of Kilian fragrances, I wanted to try a few perfumes that I didn't know yet. Of course, Good Girl Gone Bad Perfume already existed in its normal version when I started in 2019, but when comparing the scent notes and comments, I preferred the Extreme variant, so I ordered a sample of that as well. Good Girl Gone Bad Extreme is, for me, a scent that is "on the edge." It teeters on the brink of a women's fragrance towards a unisex scent. I perceive it as a wearable floral dream that a man can also enjoy. Unlike "Love Don't Be Shy (Perfume) | Kilian," the sweetness does not come from a reinterpretation of a gourmand as Kilian Hennessey intended, but rather from a - for me - stylish combination of gentle chocolate and osmanthus. The latter note also contributes to a chocolatey fruitiness reminiscent of a ripe peach. This not only harmonizes exceptionally well but also keeps it firmly in the unisex realm. Of course, one cannot deny the feminine side of it, as it contains many flowers and blossoms, but they are presented in a way that is quite bearable. For example, I can only faintly detect the indicated rose in the deep background. The note is so beautifully hidden that I like to hold my nose to the sprayed area. In the foreground, one can perceive a delicate jasmine note that appears quite powdery and has a minimal-animalistic touch, similar to Love, Don’t be Shy. Additionally, there’s the blooming orange blossom, which I have never heard more beautifully than in the Kilian creations. Here it is orangey-fresh and is perfectly embraced by the chocolate-osmanthus combination. The experience is a true dream of blossoms and embellishments. This orange and peach complement each other so well that it smells like a sweet exotic orange. The flesh of the peach surrounded by orange segments. Alongside the light blossoms of jasmine, which add a powdery-creamy undertone. The citrusy peaks of orange occasionally flash when you get closer to the sprayed area. Sexy, alluring, elegant, and sweet. I could bathe in it. Here, I feel a strong urge to buy as a man. Rarely have I experienced such a well-balanced construction of a fragrance lately, where the notes in the foreground create an incomparable experience. So I not only enjoy the scent, but I also love to smell it. I think I need a bottle….

Hello dear noses, today straight from the strawberry field about a scent that has the -for me- best illusionistic strawberry I have ever smelled in a perfume, as it is not listed in the fragrance pyramid and probably isn't included at all. Strange, right!? Thanks to @FrauMieze for this temptation, um, decant ;) Now I will try to describe this fragrance experience to you. Once Pfft Good Girl Gone Bad Extreme on my forearm please and here we go... Top: In the opening, I smell a wonderful juicy, fruity strawberry. It must be one of the roses that my nose has never smelled before and therefore associates with strawberry. The top note is wonderfully invitingly sweet. For me, it's not unpleasantly sweet, as I don't like that. No, it -the fragrance- envelops me in a soft, deep pink-red cloud of, excuse me, strawberries. Alberto Morillas will probably be tearing his hair out when he reads this. Nevertheless, I thank Mr. Morillas' nose for this truly enchanting fragrance experience. Heart: After a few minutes, the fragrance gently glides into the heart and I perceive more sweet flowers. I can't really differentiate them with my untrained nose, as the notes transition seamlessly into one another. Only rose and jasmine are what I perceive now. It still smells wonderfully of the imaginary strawberry from the opening. I can still smell it many hours after spraying. Base, the soul of the fragrance: The base, the soul of the fragrance, is cheerful, warm, heartfelt, cuddly, and somehow seductive. This fragrance invites you to see the world through rose-colored glasses. It brings a smile to my lips. I don't perceive any "badness" in this scent. Or is it perhaps this clever rose, disguised as a strawberry, that has quietly sneaked into my fragrance heart and made me addicted to this scent? Conclusion: Good Girl Gone Bad Extreme is a fragrance whose fragrance pyramid is probably not yet fully deciphered -for me-. A fragrance that gives you a good feeling when wearing it. Its longevity on fabric is enormous, on the skin, depending on the outside temperature, between 4-8 hours, unfortunately almost skin close. But still a fragrance that even my husband dives into the sillage to sniff what smells so lovely. Thus, it is a rather close-to-body sillage, as it is more perceived by people who are (very) close to you, in the truest sense of the word. Perhaps a hidden love spell? A sweet fragrance that gives you what you need right now. For me, it’s probably strawberries and a few cuddles ;D What is it for you? Perhaps the chocolate from the pyramid? Thank you for reading, dear noses. I look forward to your impressions of the fragrance in the comments. Wonderful fragrant greetings Your Miss Chippie

I saw the title of the perfume and thought it would be a spicy scent. Possibly with an oriental note. Smoky. That's certainly my idea of a “Good Girls Gone Bad.” Therefore, I wasn't interested in this fragrance at all and left it aside. When I was out shopping with my best friend last week, we still wanted to “take a quick sniff.” What can I say? This scent is fantastic! Sweet, floral, creamy. The composition is wonderfully done! It is definitely a “wow” fragrance without being intrusive or sharp. You also won’t get a headache. This fragrance is not your average scent, so I would advise against a blind purchase. The longevity is also great. Anyone who has the opportunity to test this little gem should definitely take advantage of it :-)

I have already written a statement about this fragrance, but since it turned out so poorly, I would like to elaborate on why this scent just doesn't work for me at all. Many love this fragrance and it is quite well-received here, but it scores poorly with me.. I have long since stopped studying too many notes to get an objective and unadulterated first impression when I test a sample.. Most of the time I can pick out the individual notes quite well, but here I was more than wrong.. So how does Good Girl Gone Bad Extreme smell to me: Honestly, I smell very little in the first seconds, a beast is something different, but then some notes emerge that I would describe as fallen fruit or very overripe fruit.. Some very overwhelming note that almost triggers a kind of nausea in me and makes me want to wash the scent off immediately.. A certain aversion rises within me, just like the aversion I have for PDM Cassili.. Fallen fruit just before fermentation begins.. Surprise, surprise, there is actually no fruit in this fragrance according to the fragrance pyramid… Hmmm… In any case, a synthetic blend for me of some floral notes that I would describe with a very good imagination as super synthetic overwhelming tuberose. Surprise, surprise, according to the pyramid, there is also no tuberose contained.. Therefore, I limit myself to a synthetic and overwhelming scent, with many notes that are not definable for me, which are obviously floral even though my nose smells overripe berries and fruit.. Soulless and synthetic.. I don't see a picture in front of me and I have no idea who could wear this fragrance. It seems very girly to me, I personally don't see it on a woman over 30.. But of course, it's all a matter of taste.. It's just not for me..

With Good Girl Gone Bad Extreme, Kilian Hennessy explores the darker, more intense side of one of his most iconic creations. He takes the essence of the original, the elegance and sensuality of white flowers, and allows it to blossom in a new dimension: richer, warmer, and bolder. A delicate sweetness envelops the floral structure, like a silky veil of toffee and milk.

Similar to La Nuit, L'Homme Parfum Intense is a subtle, yet luxurious creation from the masterful house of YSL. Bright and warm at the top, soft and luxurious in the heart, and a beautifully seductive drydown. It doesn't scream "smell me!", but that's certainly no crime. It's a beautiful, sensual frag that delivers on quality, complexity, and balance. Perfect for evenings out, intimate encounters, and when your S.O. wants to get 'real close!' She/he won't be able to stay away from you. Longevity is better than average, about 5-7 hours, and sillage is moderate. But again, a beautiful fragrance doesn't have to be 'in your face'. Comparisons to 1 Million aren't accurate IMO- Paco is much louder. But it has a sweetness to it that is divine. I love this frag, and better yet my girl loves it! Two BIG thumbs up from me!

After a long time, I decided to buy myself a new perfume. I get into the shop where the fragrance department is not much bigger than my living room. There were 5 shop employees & I described to them accurately what I like from perfumes & expect from them. A fresh, fruity scent and all other 'stuff', which you can read on the page devoted to me on this website. I was also very explicit in my statement, that my signature scent was LONG AGO (10 years +) 'Magnetism' from ESCADA for men, but those sellers didn't have the slightest clue what I was talking about. But NO! I was there for more than one hour, tested around a dozen perfumes, but not a SINGLE one was remotely related to what I was asking for. As I already wanted to go home, the only male employee persuaded me to try on my skin (which was still 'reserved' for the right scent) EDT 'Valentino Uomo Born in Roma Yellow Dream'. Believe it or not, because I'm not exaggerating, I was already a bit dazed & felt slightly nauseous from trying out so many scents, but still he had chosen the best fragrance of the day based on my description of what I like. I chose to follow his advice and I must say that in spite of being (only) an EDT, this fragrance has a very strong scent. (YES, I DO know that many other factors are at play here!). In spite of the fact that this 'Yellow Dream' smelled quite pleasant, it wasn't quite what I was searching for. If I were a more impulsive person (also read younger :) & my wallet would be thicker, I'd buy this fragrance instantly. Yet I chose to come back tomorrow and see how the scent will develop and IF this was really the fragrance I was looking for. On the first glance everything seemed alright: The scent was the closest match to that I was looking for and it was in my price range (even BELOW). And yet as the popular saying from Aristotle goes: 'The whole is greater than the sum of its parts.' , could be applied here perfectly. I said to myself: 'Enough! You don't always get EXACTLY what you're looking for!' But after having enough of everything, I was prepared to pay and leave with a thinner wallet. I really don't know what STOPPED ME from making the purchase almost at the time, when I wanted to take the wallet out of my pocket. I decided to come back tomorrow or in the following days - the stock of the perfume was plentiful, so there was practically no chance that people would buy all of them - think about everything a bit more and enjoy (or not ?!) how the scent, according to the 'pyramid' and the info on the net, will develop. In next hours at home I was rather disappointed, because obviously the perfume had reached it base notes rather quickly and didn't change anymore (though it smelled nice - not fabulous, where you can say 'WOW!', it was nevertheless a pleasant experience to put my nose in the vicinity of my arm, where I originally applied 'my' fragrance. Next day in the morning, when I woke up (17 to 18 hours later), the scent was still there. Of course much milder, but if you put your nose not more than 1 inch or 2,5 cm away from the original 'spraying point', you could perceive the milder but the SAME scent as yesterday & it went away only through my morning wash routine with a touch of a liquid soap. Although the next day the shop was open to 9PM in the evening, I had ABSOLUTELY no more impulsive desire to spend quite a lot of money for something that is OK, but nevertheless misses something, that I can't define with words, but after the FIRST spray on your skin I could say without any hesitation: "That's it!" (& you also go with almost no regret OVER your predefined budget). And so my story with the first perfume (which I even wasn't supposed to review :) ended. Around 2 or even 3 weeks went by & I have completely forgotten my negative experience in the perfume shop and decided on the weekend the 30th October - it was Saturday, to give it another try. It was a spontaneous visit, without ANY expectations, maybe more to just get acquainted with new fragrances. I brought to shop a small paper notebook, to write down my experiences with individual perfumes, so that I could later check on the net (in my country we have ONLY one online shop devoted EXCLUSIVELY to beauty products and original (VERIFIED!), newest perfumes - and most importantly, they sell them for a minimum of 30% lower price as in the 'physical' shop and sometimes the difference can be even bigger), what of interest I found. But a surprise was waiting for me. After 20 or 30 seconds a female employee stepped to me (I didn't ask for any help) and nicely offered me her help by asking me what I was looking for. I wrote above why I was there, so I must have looked somewhat uninterested and told her what I was looking for very fast & left out my Escada experience. Everything lasted maybe even not a whole minute - a total opposite to my first time. But she remained her composure, was calm and smiling (NOT 'artificially'). And there I was: There were only 2 bottles of "YSL L'Homme L'Intense" 60 ml left & I didn't even check the price (fortunately or maybe it was meant to be, that it checked out perfectly) & in the tester was only a small amount left (15%?). I really don't know why I offered my hand to spray the perfume on it (usually I reserve this to the last, best 'candidate' and other scents that come first are tested on paper test strips). I really don't know how to start with the description of the scent. It is strong, yet discreet & not too heavy and doesn't go into the nose 'forcefully'. There's something mysterious about it & I fell in love INSTANTLY & I was mesmerized. Even if you don't find it special, there's a big chance that you won't describe it by using negative adjectives. Without ANY thinking I bought it & I don't regret it a bit. At least on my skin, EVERYTHING: sillage, longevity & projection are quite above average. As I got home, I tried it out, by putting 1 spray behind one ear, the 2nd one behind my other, the 3rd & 4th on my collars of the shirt and the last 5th spray was left for the back of my neck. PROJECTION: As my mother came home and was still more than 1 meter away, she INSTANTLY asked me, what smells so nice? But whatever she tried, she couldn't accurately define the smell. She went past me & I felt that a pair of eyes was looking at me, but as soon as I turned to her, she acted as she was doing her usual errands. I'd say, this is a good measure of SILLAGE, because in 3 days this happened twice to me (my mother & a female colleague of mine). Back to my mother: On the day I bought the perfume, I couldn't get enough hugs from her & she said the reason is that I smell so good, but not too 'intrusive', because she couldn't get enough of her nose on my head. :) Let's go to LONGEVITY: I don't have to write a lot here. On the day I bought the perfume I was quite tired & have fallen asleep in the shirt I had on in the shop & at home. I know, a bad habit, but this was an exception. Yet in this case it helped me, because the collars smelled excellent (the shirt had to be washed because of the scent) & only AFTER a LONG shower the scent of the fragrance disappeared. Only 2 comments more, before I run out of space: In this instance (or is it my skin?): 'LESS is really MORE.' And IMHO, this is a fragrance that may seem too casual or dull to you, but there is a GREAT chance, that whatever the END impression, it'll be in worst case NEUTRAL, but not BAD.

This smells very lovely. Overall, but it still doesn't last. So carry a travel atomizer to fix the issue. Short but sweet... I used six sprays...both wrist, back & front of my neck, chest, and front of my shirt. Will I buy this again?...Yes(If I can find it). What's the strength of this? EDP. Can you use it as a unisex scent? No. Am I willing to trade this fragrance? No. Should You Skip It, Sample It First or Blind Buy It? I say Sample it first. Is it the old, new formulation? New. What's its availability; in production, limited edition or discontinued? In production. SKU Number: 3365440328303 Batch Number: ? (Production Date: 2017) Age: 25+ From: Girlfriend x-mas gift Size: 100 ML Scent: 5/5 (Nice). Value: 5/5 (Gift). Sillage: 2/5 (Two feet). Longevity: 2/5 (Four hours Tops). Creativity: 5/5 (Nothing groundbreaking). Projection: 2/5 (One hour). Versatility: 5/5 (Anytime & anywhere). Compliments: 5/5 (Nice). Until next time, I'll catch you on the flipside.

There is a lot of mixed reviews on this, but it is a unique scent to me. I’m not an average collector I’ve been doing this since the mid 90’s. This has a nice transformation starts off spicy and then the orange and violet kick in which freshen it up a bit. The dry down is woody with touch of leather, just a little leather, but the sweetness from the orange and some of the spice sticks around, I do not find this overly sweet, and the performance is very respectable I get a good days wear out of this, and it is not to loud, so you can wear this to the office or church. I also get complements when I wear this. Blind buy? I always recommend a try before you buy. But this one is disappearing so if you find it for a reasonable price on line grab it!

I scored 100ml of this for $60 on Macy’s online… an absolute STEAL! This one is more appealing to the people who like the somewhat sweet feeling “well dressed” feeling scents. One for a nice dinner with that special someone, or a formal drink with some business associates after a successful long workday. It’s that kind of scent. I get a sweetness with the suede notes that make this one shine bright. I also get great performance out of this one; a solid projection bubble that reaches a good 3ft radius, performing well for the entire 8hour duration, as it leaves a solid sillage trail that points in your direction. If you dont mind a touch of sweeter feeling playfulness in you formal wardrobe, give this one a look. It’s perfect in that sense.

Tried it and replaced it the next day! Its not that bad but this scent is too far from the original and successful l'homme as people may think!!
