Although its a parfum, i found the performance is so far and maybe worse that some EDT there in market specially sillage. Its a try to copy one million intense but far worse, i find it over sweet too for a man.

Warm, sweet and spicy fragrance with good performance, it really is a shame that YSL are replacing this with the L'Homme Parfum Intense. I don't know what these go for on discounters anymore, since my bottle was purchased a long time ago, but I'm sure the prices will be going up. Great fall fragrance, in my opinion.

A fragrance that is not talked about much and in my opinion has to do with its discreet projection. But on the other hand we find a fragrance that can work very well to seduce. Its aroma is very well balanced, it is very warm, elegant and mysterious. Despite having intense notes, it is very wearable and not heavy at all.

Very classic, warm, masculine scent. Reminds me of Dean Winchester (from the show Supernatural). Strong without choking you out, decent if a little lacking longevity - lasts longer on clothes than on skin. The amber is cozy and sensual without being cloying - it's almost a clean, fresh amber, if that's even a thing. I like to wear this when I'm feeling more masculine.

No, this will not be a negative review! I like the scent too much for that. The beautiful fragrance L´Homme L´Intense by Yves Saint Laurent moved in with me about 3 years ago. I was on a short trip to southern Sweden and visited a friend in Helsingborg, a nice town located right by the Öresund.

It's about a rose with sweet raspberries and peaches. Flowers and violets also appear. The scent is powdery and very delicate. The power is unfortunately low, it's a beautiful feminine fragrance but too expensive for the power it gives. If it were stronger, it would be a pleasant fragrance. The perfume becomes a skin perfume after 2 hours. It is very soft. It is a bed perfume, a pure woman's perfume, not a perfume that is meant to be worn to the office.

A super delicate, floral perfume, sweetened by raspberry and peach, but you hardly feel the fruity side, rather the pleasant and very subtle hint of white flowers combined with cashmere, which gives the scent great comfort. It is a super second-skin perfume and could disappoint those who enjoy fixation and projection, as it comes with a very high price tag, because it is simply a wonderful subtle perfume that leaves you wanting more! It manages to be daytime appropriate, easy to decipher, but it reminded me of no other perfume, neither imported nor domestic or niche. Although it looks beautiful and is more of the same, it doesn’t feel like another. For lovers of well-made, feminine, floral-sweet, and skin-close perfumes who have some money to spare, it is worth the investment!

I have one or two Roja fragrances, but I tend to be rather distant when it comes to Roja. Too expensive, and some simply lack longevity, or there are comparable options on the market that are significantly cheaper. Furthermore, I find Roja as a person rather opaque, cold. What he was thinking with this creation, I do not know. Maybe he had a weak moment, perhaps he was in love... newly in love, maybe his muse left him or he has a new... significantly younger muse. Maybe, maybe... This fragrance is not bad. But it’s not a standout either. This fruity-sweet direction is already very common in the fragrance market. Raspberry, rose, a bit of oud and white flowers, musk, and perhaps to round it off a touch of vanilla. Unfortunately, I don’t smell any cinnamon at all. An example would be "Delina". But even Delina has more character and especially more longevity. This is my perception that I am describing here, and I believe this fragrance is not worth the money. For some, this may be incomprehensible, but I was simply disappointed. I love roses, raspberries, and I enjoy it when it’s refreshing. But it should go a bit deeper. If I want a fleeting "companion," I would rather reach for something in the notorious mainstream area, and take a fragrance that every second woman already wears. And even there, there are fragrances that have significantly more longevity. Elixier is wearable - no question about it. Sourly fruity and a bit sweet. The bottle is elegant, and the name Roja on it certainly makes an impression. But somehow, I think Roja had a weak moment with Elixier (in my opinion).

Perfume can be a trigger; for old memories, unconscious associations with people, landscapes, events. Perfume can also be a wish, hopeful, for freedom, for love, for companionship. As we perfume addicts know, the sense of smell is largely developed at birth and plays an immense role in all areas of life, of subjective significance. This fragrance, often criticized for understandable reasons, is for me the touch of lightness and joy of life. While "Cosmos Flowers" evokes something similar in me, the strong patchouli gives this one a distinctly different depth. Elixir Essence de Parfum remains light, one might think, without depth. Elixir starts off zesty, fruity, raspberry-like. I love raspberries. In my perception, the raspberry is there from the very beginning with full presence. Citrusy fresh through bergamot. As different roses come into play, the plump juicy peach gradually joins the flowers. So, for several hours, it is a skillful mix of fruits and flowers. Very powdery. In the heart note, the fragrance, still powdery, begins to gain creaminess. I don’t see tonka bean in the list of notes, but the base becomes gently vanillic with a pleasant nutty note and slight woodiness. It seems that the fragrance disappears after a few hours. But on my skin, this creamy base lingers very closely for many hours. Without drifting into the old-fashioned, without sharp undertones, without becoming bitter. Roja Dove, or his secret wizard, is an artist in his field. This perfume, or rather Essence de Parfum, truly stands out in its properties. And yet I assert that the DNA of Roja Dove is recognizable here. The comparison to a cheap drugstore scent may hold true, but for me, the difference is, and this is my personal perception, that I do not get headaches from Elixir. With many mainstream fragrances, I have tested and owned several, this was the case. Or there was always some note that spoiled the fragrance for me. Ultimately, it doesn’t matter. It is the overall mixture that feels just right for me and my current state of mind. So many years I have been with Parfumo, so many fragrances I have come to know and love, in so many corners of my life, perfume has catapulted or accompanied me back...into beautiful times, when I think of "Bombay Bling!", into dirty hard times, when I think of "Trayee" or "Shalimar", into free, autonomous times, when I think of "Black XS for Her", into secure times, when I think of "Danger"... And now, the lightness of being.

I discovered an original black 1.6oz EDT box circa 1983 on e-bay. It is quite different from the familiar formula on todays market. This was truely the biggest and best rose perfume ever made. In its time, I only detected it from afar. Indeed by 1985, it was everywhere. The traffic jam of perfume from that era shall never be forgotten or matched. Paris however was different. Its pays tribute to Apres l'Ondee and was like Nahema containing a profusion of rose damascenones so boldly. This is YSL running along side Guerlain equally. It is Sophia Grojsman's magnum opus. It is the definitive French rose perfume. Its production cost had to be astronomical at the time and it gradually weakend to the current formula. This original bottle relys little on the supporting cast of violet and mimosa. The rose dominates the composition for hours and then the natural, rich sandalwood and oakmoss hold it up even further. They are no longer in the pink box. This isnt sexy like Opium, bold like Rive Gauche or mysterious like Y. As great as they are, Paris explores love. This is the gentle, blushing, innocent love that happens once in a lifetime. One drop on your pulse is profound. It gets under your skin and into your heart. Its mood enhancing and hypnotic. I can almost taste the rose. Paris is a timeless 20th century giant that was really only around for about 5 year in its pure strength. No wonder it was on display in the Louvre! It was a work of art. Often imitated, even by YSL itself, but never as great as those original bottles. Time is passing-get a bottle today before its too late!

One of the few perfumes that is 80’s in style, size and exuberance but can still be worn today without irony. It’s a cartoon-like rose with candied violet. A bit shrieky up top, but fortunately by the heartnotes the rose grows citric and astringent, lending a sweet/tart quality to the accord. Paris has a crystalline quality similar to Guerlain’s Nahema, but is far less dense and juicy than Nahema. Paris gains a woody, musky quality in drydown, but remains true to the artifice and exaggeration of its era and is proudly an 80’s Huge Floral.

I am a passionate rose lover and as many fellow rose lovers for a very long time now I am searching for the perfect rose.. And I think my quest is so difficult because I smelled YSL Paris first of all. This is the classic rose smell, I don't know any other rose which smells so classy, elegant and natural, nothing else I have ever smelt in the rose category, even the pure rose oils manages to give me the rose smell i adore like Paris. Any rose lover should own this, it couldnt disappoint anyone!

This is one loud rose fragrance that I do enjoy greatly. As a child I always preferred the scent of the Black Madonna rose to any other rose in my Mother's garden. It had such a rich, distinctive smell that has been so well emulated through Paris. This fragrance opens with rich, (and in some ways harsh) rose, gernanium, green notes and what seems to be aldehydes. There is a definite soapy/powdery quality throughout the composition which I find rather alluring. Just looking at the adverts, I can't say that Paris is particularly sexy or seductive. I'd say forget the sexual aspect and focus on the romantic and classic feel of the scent. This is romantic, candle-lit dinners in a restaurant with a view of the Eiffel Tower, not a clothes-tearing, extremely urgent romp, beneath red satin sheets in a sleazy motel. I also find this scent to be quite fresh, almost something that I could imagine wearing during the heat of Summer, despite the scent being quite strong. For me, Paris sparkles with vitality and commands attention. The lasting strength is absolutely amazing. Even showering doesn't completely rid oneself of this potent fragrance. To some this will seem out-dated, far too strong and 'nightmarish', however I do have hope that some will appreciate this fragrance like I have.

Yves Saint Laurent PARIS is a *very* floral fragrance--a huge flower garden dominated by roses of all colors and sizes. It's all a bit overwhelming: I feel as though I'm wearing a huge corsage. Or maybe twelve. The flowers do smell nice and fresh and as genuine as they would be at a rose competition--perhaps at a state fair--but I feel uncomfortable in this scent. It's really not me. And I must say that it does not cohere in any way with my concept of Paris. PARIS seems more along the lines of what Monica Lewinsky may have worn to go with her blue dress. Yes, as others have said: big hair, shoulder pads... Hmmm...earlier images, too, of Joan Crawford in MILDRED PIERCE keep popping up in my mind, along with one of my favorite movie lines of all time: "No wire hangers!!!!" Perhaps a better name for this fragrance would have been DALLAS.

A classic beauty that is very appropriately named after the city of love: Paris. And filled to the brim with the flower of love: Rose. A spring walk through the "Parc de la Roseraie" in Paris. Roses everywhere and a hint of violet, lily and wood notes carried on a warm breeze.

A dreamy, powder-puff of a rose perfume. A chypre-like rose, with lots of soft violets, sweet mimosa, and powdery iris. Very pretty, and very romantic. In my mind's eye I can envision a beautiful peaches and cream Gibson girl in the 1890s wearing something like this. It definitely has a vintage feel. So, if you love vintages as much as I do, you may enjoy this.
A Tale of the Parisian Sisters Y.S.

In 1983 I was 12 years old (did I just give my age away so easily?!!) I did not have proper perfumes, just deodorants, primarily Date and Limara. But I really wanted a perfume. In a beautiful bottle. Just like my mum. I had wished for one for Christmas. Told my mum I reallyreallyreally could not live without.

Paris – YSL Digging around in my perfume cupboard I came across a 7.5 ml miniature of Paris Eau de Toilette from the early 1980's. I have about 1/4 left. The strength of this EDT is nothing short of phenomenal; no wonder after all this time I still have a 1/4 bottle remaining - it really does only need a little dab and lasts 12 hours plus.

These two perfumes share a similar style. • Voulez-vous coucher avec Moi (2015) • Danger Parfum (2012) CREAMY, RICH WHITE FLORALS WITH VANILLA, SANDALWOOD AND YLANG-YLANG That previous combination is truly amazing. Of the two, VVCAM is the stronger, fuller and somehow fatally seductive, as it has Tuberose, Orange Blossom, Neroli and Gardenia in it. Danger is noticeably more refined, innocent, powdery and softer with Jasmine and Gardenia. In Dander, there is that subtle, elegant, tender Roja’s style sweetness from Peach and vanilla whereas the sweetness in VVCAM comes from Tuberose, Ylang-Ylang and Vanilla, being more intense and deeper, like the aroma of white flowers themselves. Both are intoxicating in their own way. New Look 1947 is quite close to VVCAM as well, the biggest difference is in the opening and in overall VVCAM is more sour and creamier with stronger Ylang Ylang note while New Look 1947 stays somewhat earthier. New Look 1947 lasts longer and projects more. I will write an in depth review of all later. Thank you for reading, I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more

I thought I'd write this up as people might be wondering if this can replace the Samsara extrait. Crazy priced as this is, the extrait is not cheap either. TLDR: no, this closer to modern Samsara EDP rather than the extrait. The opening markedly different from the extrait (I have early 2000s version) - the Samsara has a mix of citruses with prominent lemon, and something else, very sour (not sure if the top notes in my bottle went south tho - the EDP doesn't have anything sour in it, the lemony citruses + something fruity like a peach or the like). Danger has sweeter citruses, I'd say mandarin and lemon are very prominent. Samsara extrait is very woody, creamy, powdery and vanillic. There are aldehydes as well. It has a slight vintage vibe (likely from the aldehydes and carnation), but it manages to avoid smelling old-fashioned. Danger is a simpler scent, smells like powdery jasmine-rose vanilla (aka the Guerlinade type of thing). There is less woodiness comparing to the extrait (although I can tell the base does have something woody synthetic in it, but not a lot), and less creaminess. I think it's closer to the modern Samsara EDP rather than the extrait, as the modern EDP is also simpler than the extrait, and less woody and creamy. All three scents are not long lasting, Samsara EDP being the most fleeting (3 hours on me), Danger in the middle (4 hours on me) and then the extrait (5 hours on me). The deep dry down is different for the three: the extrait is actually powdery, vanillic and musky (in a cat litter sort of way, but it doesn't smell bad on me, there aren't many of those musks in there); Danger displays some smoked wood (similar to maybe synthetic vetyver); Samsara EDP is very powdery. Considering the price difference, I'd go with Samsara EDP instead of this (unless you want not so much the scent as the luxury bells and whistles), or would procure the vintage Samsara extrait as it is more interesting and complex and lasts longer. Final note: I had a discovery set with 51, Elixir, Amber Aoud, Sweetie Aoud, Gardenia, Enigma and this one. This one is the best of the bunch - because it smells like a Guerlain lol

I first sprayed Danger at Harrods in London! Surrounded by absolute luxury, I was extremely excited! The scent has something special, something Oriental! I was also thrilled by all the beautiful things around me and took it home!! It is a lovely fragrance, very elegant and unique. The bottle is super beautiful. Now I am back home, winter is over. What remains is a whole bottle of a fragrance that costs almost 400 euros!!! - and no, it is not worth that! So far, no one (my own husband first and foremost) has found me particularly erotic with it... (That’s how it is described) It doesn’t really match that description. Conclusion: certainly elegant, certainly beautiful, like a classic great perfume!! But not worth the price! I acquired an emotion for a certain moment. Nothing more, nothing less.

For days, my thoughts have been circling around Danger... and how I might describe it. I just can't find an image for it. My first encounter with Danger was at Douglas on the Kö during our Parfumo meeting; it only got a tiny test spot on my upper arm, the rest of my arm was already a sea of scents. No way to perceive it. During the second test, it had one arm to itself... phew, I thought, what a bomb, only animalistic notes reached me. Not my thing. Somehow, a little sting remained that wouldn't let my curiosity rest. So I got myself a sample. It took a whole three tests until it exploded. Quietly exploded. Although Danger comes across loudly like a decked-out diva in a garish costume, it is indeed a serious lady. A full-bodied woman. Danger starts like a firework, where the sparks are flying. A lump of honey, mixed with flowers, fresh citrus splashes that provide relief. Very heavy, pleasantly sweet. For me, a bit animalistic. With a strong sillage. Right now, I am only testing the Eau de Parfum. I am curious about the parfum. The strong beginning gives way to a little calm after more than an hour. Here, lovely flowers make their appearance. The scent becomes beautifully powdery. A slight soapy quality comes in. I don't pick out the peach, but the roses are present in a very subtle form. Rose honey. Is it the jasmine? There is a scent note, and it’s not the citrus notes!, that makes the fragrance a bit invigorating, consistently, very minimally sharp. I would almost say it’s pepper. But I will probably be laughed at for that.... Thus, the scent lingers for many hours. Very intense, but without being too heavy. Danger could be a cousin of Coco. But Coco remains heavy. Danger accompanies me throughout the day without needing to reapply. Like a warm, soft scarf, without constricting me. There are hardly any fragrances that I find erotic. I find Danger highly erotic. Sensual. Elegant. I would be burning with curiosity to know how men perceive this scent. I perceive Danger as a very complex fragrance, even though I lack the words to justify it. Mature. And what I love most about this perfume is the end. To me, the base smells like warm skin, lightly brushed with honey. Definitely more warm skin than honey. That’s why Danger is a skin scent for me. Different from L’Eau D’Hiver, which is fresh and brings me to the sea. The end is closeness, physicality, and security. Still mature. And that lasts for hours... how wonderfully good... This perfume stimulates my imagination. Due to my years-long Guerlain trauma (which I have now overcome ;)), I unfortunately cannot draw parallels to the fragrance twin mentioned here. Danger, not a pretty name for this scent, not a pretty sound. But there is certainly some truth to the meaning.

Hyenas - cunning, quick, angular, mysterious, and for some, downright malicious. - Yet they reflect something entirely their own. Something that slyly drives fear and rigidity into the body. Respect is paid to them. Whether one wants it or not. There are several myths about hyenas. I've heard a lot over the years while traveling in Africa. In some parts, the hyena is an animal that one approaches with caution and respect, while in other areas it is despised and people have a terrible fear of them. It was said that witches rode hyenas, sang loudly and laughed to poison people, especially children.. With their song and a truly dull voice that teaches one to fear. Penetrating the memory of people, clinging like a grotesque tick and taking over the whole body. The hyena is indeed a powerful animal. No question. King of the beasts? The lion? African culture also remains silent about the hyena. No known mammal looks as grim and evil as this one. No facial features that show any sensitivity. Even the Black Man would laugh in his fist. And then there is a very fine aspect and side to hyenas. In some cultures, it is said that the hyena represents rebirth and according to myths, it is the animal that brought the sun to the earth. In its barren, yet shimmering fur. It is also an animal that brings the cycle of life to total decline or end. For hyenas are scavengers and eat what others leave behind. And then she came. Out of the blue. Dignified, well-dressed, with a stern look and a handshake like that of a street worker. I was immediately fixated on her. Her eyes seemed cunning, as they twisted between a part of evil and then again of good. The blue sank partially into green and vice versa. I had never looked into such eyes in my life. The black hair framed her face, clinging to a body that had a rather impressive stature. Her lips pointed like a snitch, her body straight as a pencil.. She seemed uptight and truly evil. No looseness. Nothing. Not even a little. This appearance of a woman breathes fear into one’s body. A fear that has something positive about it. When you feel it, you realize you are truly alive. Feeling the threat at your neck. My insides tremble with adrenaline. But then she opened her mouth. The body relaxed, the lips curled into a smile, the eyes widened into beautiful round eyes, the blue seemed to pull the sea into her. Life breathed into her at that moment. How one can be mistaken by the eye. Hardly seeing someone, one judges. But if you engage with the person and talk to her, a completely different wind begins to blow. Dates followed and we exchanged a lot. She liked my urge. The urge to always have perfumes around me. So we spontaneously set off on a short trip. I absolutely wanted to buy her a perfume and spent days racking my brain about what I wanted to gift her. It had to be something entirely unique, something that couldn't possibly come from this world.. Above all, there should be a mystery resonating in the perfume.. I also wanted something threatening in it, all combined with a juicy, extremely lovely guy. I just wondered where I would find that? Then chance came to my aid and I encountered Roja. I tested a few scents and came to Danger. I didn’t know the name beforehand, only had numbers and a list. I smelled it and the scent immediately sucked me in like a black hole in the sea. My body sank into the black nothingness and seemed to simply swallow me. Away from this world, straight into the other. There is something treacherous and threatening in the scent. It’s addictive! Danger starts extremely strong, threatening, and one feels dazed. A fine hint of citrus allows for some looseness, but this is all suppressed by the bergamot. It is sweet, almost overwhelmingly sweet. The flowers weave through the perfume and take everything with them. The jasmine is very strong and presents itself here like the Grand Madame. Then it quiets down, the sweetness fades a bit. The powderiness rises. Gently it clings to my skin. It really fluffs up. My nose is pleasantly tickled. I have to shake myself briefly. First such depth and heaviness, and then this soothing feeling of softness. Gently I place my nose back on my skin. My daze has still not faded. For the roses feel evil and solidify with their thorns on the body. A truly dirty perfume, I thought. I can hardly smell anything animalistic, try as I might. The musk is subtle, and that’s a good thing. Otherwise, everything would overwhelm me. A beautiful musk scent that makes everything seem gentle and fine, even if there is a lot of threatening in the perfume. Fine wood spreads out and pulls the perfume back into the depths. A beautiful depth that carries pure excellence within it. I love black, and this is an extremely dark scent that also allows rays of sunshine. Light that illuminates the black souls. The hyena brought the sun into the world .. Mhm.. Farewell powder, you were almost swallowed. Danger came after the pull into the black nothingness, with large threatening steps, settled in one, and then slowly departed. With small steps. I had a hyena in front of me. Why, I don’t know. It just came like that. This face. These movements that the hyena makes. I told her about it. She grinned and then we both had to laugh. "You compare me to a hyena?" She looked at me in amazement and tilted her head back. Then she began to laugh mockingly. This turned into genuine joyful laughter. "Hyenas are mysterious, angular but also elegant. That makes them quite unique personalities!" The comparison was only vague. I only associated her with that. Her appearance. Our first encounter.. Oh yes, that made it. A personality that connects fear and life. When I then learned the name of the perfume, I had to pause. Someone had really thought about it. She applied the scent, stretched, and she too seemed to fall into the pull .. My nose jumped with joy. * Nothing is more threatening than that which simultaneously breathes enlightenment and fear into one. Love.

Here it is again! I had taken this comment off the net this morning! There was some need for clarification, and I did not want to clear this up "on the back" of a perfume comment. With the brand Roja, opinions often diverge, and sometimes the waves run high.

Danger is a fragrance for the female version of a Tommy Shelby. She enters the room, appears cool, and yet everyone turns to look at her. Perhaps also for Persephone from the Matrix. This scent certainly has a lot of presence like Monica Bellucci and is quite exciting. It strikes me as mature, confident, sexy, dark, and mysterious. A fragrance that is not easily forgotten.

In anticipation of Kilian's upcoming launch Old Fashioned , I opted to get myself 10ml of the now discontinued Single Malt London . Due to this fragrance being nearly impossible to find and most influencers being mere opportunists, I have seen the few people who already have Old Fashioned compare it to "Angels' Share | Kilian". We can set the record straight: if Old Fashioned is actually inspired by Single Malt then it smells nothing like "Angels' Share | Kilian". Single Malt London features the best open I have smelled since Royal Crown's 2023 release Aeternum as the listed plum note resembles roasted plum compote with slight boozy nuances. The surprising twist with Single Malt is that when smelled up-close, the fragrance features prominent medicinal ambers and mild oud/woodiness. The medicinal amber tones mentioned are very similar to the style of fragrance you get from Carner Barcelona with scents like Megalium . The base tones provide good lift for a fragrance that mainly smells sweet-fruity-spicy with oriental-woody-animalic being the accords on which the scent is built upon. The previously described complexity remains for more than half of the wearing experience until the scent eventually settles into a faint combination of fruity & warm spicy, feeling more like a distant relative of the Tobacolor family of fragrances (incl. Kilian's 2023 release Smoking Hot ). Within the community of owners that Single Malt London has, performance has been criticized and I think there is space for that criticism. The scent opens strong and remains so for around 45 minutes before sillage dies down to just above intimate with people being able to smell you walking by. For me, the scent lasts on skin for around 7-8 hours, somewhat similar to the longevity of Smoking Hot . Another obvious issue here is the pricing - this is a discontinued fragrance that in BNIB form (brand new in bottle) is now trading around €500/50ml. That places Single Malt London in competition with premium/luxury product like Clive Christian's Jump Up and Kiss Me Hedonistic (€550/50ml) which brings more depth and better quality. Now all one can do is wait and see whether Old Fashioned can live up to the standard set by Single Malt London . Regardless of whether it actually does, Single Malt will be remembered as yet another successful release in Kilian's fall/winter catalogue which already features nearly a dozen of them.

There are no sharp edges by the old watering hole, only the gentle touch of a million fingers pouring as many drinks, sliding beveled glasses down the bar, helping tired bodies rest against the smooth lacquered wood with slow gestures repeated over the decades. In this dark, musty environment every piece of furniture has soaked the scent of countless whiskeys and now greets customers like a familiar hug after a long day of work. Tonight though the speakeasy seems unusually loud, with more than the customary mumbled conversations and clinking tumblers. There are fresh new faces in a corner, an unexpected group of young visitors seeking refuge from the cold and rain outside. No-one at the bar pays much atention to their cheering and laughing but soon the room is filled with something that cuts through the old single malt: there is warm vanilla cake, candied fruit and spicy cinnamon, a powerful aroma that brings memories of family celebrations at home, wherever that may be. As the party songs get going some customers finish their drinks off, grab their coats and head back to their loved ones early for once. Others try their best to ignore the happy mood and sweet scent in the air, and remain focused on the swirling bourbons under their noses; probably nowhere else to go or no better place to be on a cold lonely night.

Scentrack The Last Shadow Puppets – My Mistakes Were Made For You Single Malt opens with a strong plum note which reminds me of plum compote or plum brandy. The Tolu balsam is definitely partly responsible for this extremely fruity opening. Beneath this plum note there is a darker grainy wheat note, sticky resinous and smoky notes. As composition progresses dark vanilla, moist tobacco and oak/cedar wood maturation notes are more pronounced. The composition is very compact and linear, but never overpowering. Single Malt is not a reinterpretation of peaty Islay whiskies. It does not possess the medicinal peaty kick of Islay single malts, as smelt in Profumum Roma Fumidus. Single Malt reminds me more of Johnnie Walker Black blended whisky with an extremely balanced composition of fruity Speyside malts, touch of smoke and strong vanilla finish of ex-bourbon cask maturation. Rating: 9/10 More on Scentimentalwords

A warm, resinous woodsy fragrance with gloomy sweetness presenting both golden ratio beauty and beasty masculine aggressiveness, as presented in ad picture with hairy naked guy. YSL has done a perfect plan to change the path of perfumery as Chanel had done with No5. Releasing the first oud-dominant fragrance from a designer brand - no matter how pioneer in fashion - was jaw-dropping. M7 is the world's first serious take on oud that opened the gates of heaven to westerns… M7 is a solid linear fragrance that doesn't promises for anything. It's a long rocky moan of guitar in Guns n' Roses stage. An open-shirted modern virile masculinity that before this, used to be identified by hairy cocks of aromatic fougères that lack one thing M7 presents: oriental mystery. It maintains a close kinship with medicinal materials and cough syrup, which M7 has always been notorious for. Some people were afraid of this medicinal aspect of oud (I clearly remember the debated on the very page you're reading now), whom I'm afraid to be still on the same idea while there are oud oud oud everywhere! So pity that badass Tom Ford has ceased the line and the house replaced it with new edition. M7 was and still is an unequivocal masterpiece. 9.5/10

Tom Ford was known for a lot of things... he was the man who turned around the fortunes of Gucci from almost bankrupt to such a degree that they were able to buy YSL. He always took risks and they paid off, they were always daring and innovative. A master of design. M7 was (and in some cases still is) a fragrance unlike any other. It was the first time the note of oud was introduced in mainstream perfumery. There was nothing like it at the time of release. Innovative and daring (just like the YSL of the past). This fragrance is strong yet soft, powerful yet quiet. Very masculine but with a hint of femininity. It's also very well made. Beautiful, elegant stuff. M7 opens up with a slightly herbal and aromatic accord of rosemary with fresh bergamot & mandarin. What starts to come through very soon though... is the oud. Oud, or Agarwood, is the sap from an infected tropical tree. It can smell medicinal, it can smell sweet, animalic, and can often be cloying. Here that isn't the case. In M7 the oud is perfectly balanced with the other notes, the amber and the musk. There is also an earthy vetiver note which stops this from being overtly sweet, and the drydown is a smooth, powdery amber & musk combination. Extremely pleasing and nice. My bottle is a reformulation from 2009, but not the "re-orchestrated" version released recently by Yves Saint-Laurent called M7 Oud Absolu. I haven't smelled that but I'm told it keeps some of the character of the original. Personally, I think this is a wonderful gem of a fragrance, but I think that this has since been explored more by the countless oud variations that flooded the market in recent years. I have a hard time recommending this purely as an oud fragrance, and if you want oud, there are better examples out there. But for what it is, it's a masterpiece in my opinion. But for everyone else, feel free to check out the new version or any "stronger" oud blends out there... because I'm keeping this one for sure!

This masterpiece is so difficult to review, I always find it difficult to explain that I particularly like them also because it is like dissecting my intimacy, it becomes a very personal thing and honestly I don't know where to start, but let's start with a similarity. Compared to modern perfumery, M7 is an orange spot in a sea of gray. It is certainly one of the most beautiful, original and fascinating perfumes I have ever smelled. I went in search of M7 when the hype wasn't as high as it is now, as soon as I smelled it, I immediately felt that it had something different than all the other perfumes. Today it has become almost impossible to find, and deserves all the hype surrounding it. To understand the essence in all its completeness it seems only right to start from the birth of this perfume. In 2002, Tom Ford, creative director of Yves Santi Laurent deals with the marketing of the seventh fragrance of the group, for this reason it is called M7, and he succeeds very well, the bottle, the mysterious amber parallelepiped is more striking than the nude used as a testimonial, a trusted creation. in Morillas and Cavalier, not two common noses. The thing that makes this perfume special is the introduction of real agarwood, never used before by Western homes. Today there are an infinite number of perfumes containing oud, but with the difference that in M7 the oud is real and not synthetic, and also blends perfectly with the ingredients, it does not want to be a perfume made mainly of oud and more. The opening of M7 is nothing short of overwhelming, aggressive, it is a paw of a tiger, medicinal, pungent spicy, dried herbs, mandarin rosemary and Haitian vetiver which then blend perfectly with amber, the round and woody oud, but not chewy as we are used to in modern perfumes. The perfume with the passage of time becomes sweeter, amber, dark, it lies gently on the skin remaining slightly powdery, deep, soft, modern despite being a 20-year-old perfume, it stimulates the senses, very versatile, and above all, elegant, masculine, oriental, absolutely three-dimensional, dense and damn sexy and long-lasting. And there is another reason why they like M7 so much, by now I was tired of perfumes, I had boxes full of the usual cheap perfumes that now appear like mushrooms on the shelves of perfumeries, M7 was my key to perfumes vintage / discontinued, it made me understand you can find emotions in the bottle even in old perfumes, finding old gems has given me a lot of satisfactions that not even the best niche could give me. I knew this review was going to be long and I'm sorry if I bored you. I close with a banality but it is the harsh truth, they will never make perfumes like this again. Rated 10/10

This rare 2002 bird displays quite a strange cargo yet it defines color Sinopia, shade of red and brown. Named after the Turkish city it is a reddish-brown ochre-like earth color pigment, also used in traditional oil painting, in fresco or in secco. Sinopia was written in the 15th century in Florence, Italy and described as full of honeyed ambrosia yet lean and dry in character. It projects up well. For the more it is worked up, the finer it becomes. It is good for use in dry autumnal weather. Fresh even to start with, it quickly transforms to calm, serious and mature tune. Phenomenal use of medicinal agar as the side effect, with also prominent orange on top and myrrh and labdanum at its base. Intensely masculine, elegant and sensual. You will need to lit the fireplace, source hand rolled cigars Made in Cuba, and splash for a few bottles of an extra old cognac. Thanks to Morillas & Cavallier.

This is a very active fragrance, as if to say the notes have ADHD... or simply get along very well. When they calm, there's a Black Orchid vibe. In the sense that the two come off warm, spicy, balmy and almost obnoxious. When I think of Black Orchid, a clean shave and a suit comes to mind. When I think of M7... stubble, a blazer and jeans immediately surfaces to mind. M7 is far more rugged with a masculine feel. Smoked oud and vetiver, laced with dry spices and amber. Rough yet smooth, if that makes any sense at all. Discontinued? What the hell for? You ever wonder why the best ones get voted off? This industry is rigged like reality TV.
The original formula is a beautifully intoxicating fragrance that spells Man with a capital M.

I'm curious about many discontinued fragrances, the reason being, I want to know why they were removed from the market. Seeing the amount of rave reviews M7 had been given, its discontinuation was quite unclear to me. The moment I applied M7 to my skin, I was not repulsed, however I detected a straight-up cherry flavoured cough syrup note.

Some things happen without a valid reason, or we don’t know how to explain. Therefore, I cannot explain how two master perfumers, namely Alberto Morillas and Jacques Cavallier, beneath the direction of Tom Ford, could have created such an outrageous, dangerous, and gorgeous masterpiece, and then the house of YSL discontinued it.
Again another long one, with metaphors, similes and analogies.

This review is for the second formulation that comes in the bottle where half of it is transparent. Testing the first presentation of agarwood that was to introduce quite a trend over the coming years is still a joy. And what a pleasure not having to bother with the oh-so-boring oud/rose combo as well.

To simplify it, A Goodnight Kiss is a classic style powdery floral aldehyde. But nothing about this fragrance can be simple, not for me at least. For starters, the way I came about owning it may make me a bit biased and emotional. Second, I know this was a fragrance made to recreate the scent of Roja's mother as she kissed him goodnight, and she is resting in peace. So, there is nothing simple about it. But it does smell exactly like a woman, a prim motherly lady, and how she would smell in close proximity. Her floral perfume, her powder, her lipstick and the natural human smell of musk we all get toward the end of the day. This is the smell of a goodnight kiss. A sweet kiss, a loving kiss, a gentle kiss. The meaningful kind. It is the smell of love. The iris is gentle and glorious, the powder is a very realistic rice powder scent. If you have ever worn rice powder, it's unmistakable. There is prominent ambergris that gives it warmth, it's never too floral, there is a human musky quality to it. Everything about this fragrance is human. So, it makes it a bit emotional to wear it. For me at least. It is elegant, it's understated, it's classic and it's very refined. It's comforting and I feel a range of emotions wearing it. A Goodnight Kiss is a captivating fragrance. And it smells like powder, it smells like flowers, it smells like soft leather, it smells like musk....and it smells like love, nostalgia and beauty. It smells like a gift. And it smells like a memory. And I feel like a princess wearing it. And there is no price on those things.

A Goodnights kiss tells a beautiful story about Rojas early life, its a beautiful powdery, floral Chypre which I adore to wear even as a Man. Roja says this fragrance interprets feminine love which I totally agree upon! A Goodnights Kiss is a collectors item, For those who can admire the story behind the fragrance, Not just the regular individual who just wants to smell good considering the hefty price.

"Only kisses taste better!" was once an advertising slogan. Hearts and co. are always a safe bet when it comes to selling. Put a heart on it, and people are happy. Now this gentleman Dove calls the perfume Good Night - Kiss. And says it comes from mommy, so to speak. Hm. That doesn’t really have anything to do with eroticism. What should one make of that? I briefly racked my brain but couldn’t remember for the life of me how mom smelled when putting me to bed. Well, she didn’t go out afterward, so she must have smelled the same as always. Besides, I never wanted to go to bed, kisses or no kisses. Out of pure curiosity, I wondered how things looked, or rather smelled, at Doves? So here: Like perfume! (I should have figured that out.) I spent quite a while with the Goodnight Kiss, first out of curiosity, and then it just became unavoidable. At first, there was almost a daunting elegance. The fine lady with the aldehydes is here, nose up, frigate alarm. To the side, the LADIES' fragrance. Pretty, not suitable for me. Not at all. At some point, I dug it out again. The same thing in green. But the nose had become curious now, wondering why it should sniff again and nodded to itself. Do it again, it’s not so bad, I think! In the meantime, I had sniffed various things nicely, powder for example. The aldehydes now also come by more often without the made-up widow's wreath, of which I want to be a member someday. (Note to self: Don’t forget to get married!) At some point, I found myself unusually awake, sniffing around in my white little bed. And I had a mental flash! THAT must be what makes the Goodnight Kiss! THAT, what I smelled. Soft, warm, white, elegant, cool, and delicately spicy fluffiness. (A gentle waft, even though waft is a silly word. What fog banks do when they’re not rising. Noble fog banks!) After various sniffing sessions, I actually managed to wear this perfume during the day. Wow! I smell in broad daylight like I probably look at night. Definitely. And a bit of grandiloquently formulated coziness is probably in there too. One must never forget: Good night! That’s what it was called. And no arguments! And exactly this slightly aloof-seeming strictness fascinates me. And distinguishes the Goodnight Kiss from little Oscar. For me. ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥ ♥

The scent has a story that precedes it. I am already influenced before I even smell it and immediately think of the following song. https://youtu.be/AEQlU3eDcVk Leo and Luna. When I listen to the gentle, soothing character of the song, it can be perfectly transferred to the scent. Roja Dove, I have never really engaged with him as a person. One thing is certain for me, he must be older. My mom smelled different when going out. She smelled of Armani She and leather. Only when at home did she smell of Nivea. Therefore, the click of the can lid on the sink and the scent of the cream are irrevocably associated with my mother. And indeed Armani She with leather. And although a certain memory arises, Roja's mom must belong to an older generation. I spray and smell a lot of aldehydes & powder. But also soap. It is intercepted by the powder and doesn’t directly foam in my mouth, but undoubtedly Roja's mom must have scrubbed herself well with her best soap beforehand, the pure soap stayed in the cupboard because of the occasion. Flowers join in and suddenly I feel like I have an old classic in my nose. The scent feels very Guerlain-like to me, but to be a Guerlain, it is too soapy and does not drift into that deep, slightly animalistic spiciness. The flowers that would allow this, especially clove and orange blossom, are present, yet they always remain just out of reach. Trapped under powder soap. Only hinted at. Kissed. And so the scent wafts around me. A little excited yet calming, the scent, which initially came across as unusually loud for Roja, becomes quieter, more delicate, and calmer. And it reminds me more and more of the aforementioned blue can. The soapiness decreases or I get used to it, and the scent develops a creamy powderiness. It seems as if mom has left, and only a trace of her scent lingers in the air, the taste of the scent kiss still on my lips. I taste this goodnight kiss. Indeed. Literally. I do not want to deny it. The scent is a dream. Its character is gentle, its notes balanced and calming, its song loving. For a fraction of the price, I would find dreamy words. The theme hit. What keeps me so sober is the knowledge of its price. As much as I know that Roja scents are not created for my wallet, the open question remains whether the scent justifies the price. What do you pay for? A good scent? Roja's memory? This wonderful love letter to his mom? To smell this goodnight kiss was my greatest desire. A dear perfumer made this possible for me. Without asking anything in return. For that, I thank you, in the spirit of the scent with a curtsy. :)

…….he had already gone to bed, almost sleepy he still hears her quietly entering his bedroom. The small nightlight on the console is still on and he sees how her long dark hair is artfully pinned up. Her face is made up in such a way that it appears very sophisticatedly unmade up. She looks at him. As earrings, she has put on her favorite chandelier, which shimmers in competition with her lipstick. She is dressed in her evening gown made of a light silk fabric, a satin that is embroidered all over with creamy white flowers. She approaches, her chandeliers sparkling as she steps to the foot of his bed. With her gloved hands, she lifts the end of his sheet. He sees that her evening gown is open in the front… she continuously looks calmly into his eyes…. as she slowly pulls the sheet closer to herself, then bends down slowly, her lips almost touching the fabric… _________________________________________________________________________________________________________ A sea of moist, powdery scented white flowers overwhelms me right from the first spray. At first, I am shocked by this abundance, as the aldehydic accord greatly enhances this impression and also adds something dirty that I sense among all the flowers…. But wait, it can't be the aldehyde, such a thing doesn't come from aldehydes. It seems to originate from the base. ….. aaah... it’s an iris root. A strong, carrot-hued iris is anchored deep down there, one that likely holds all the base notes and the rest together. The carrot-like scent is not just simple little carrots, but much more the stems and the fresh green herb of a bunch of market carrots, still clinging to some earth. I find this extremely refined. It grounds the fresh flowers, gives them corporeality and takes away the often mentioned madam-like and cloying touch. After about 2 hours, the perfume is much softer and I sniff how the violet has teamed up with the iris, the perfume becoming creamier and rounder, with my beloved May rose quietly shining through in the sea of flowers. The character of the perfume behaves in its floral obsession during the further drydown. It remains flower-soft, in a powdery iris gentle manner and creamy fine softly. A Goodnight Kiss is a strong, a fantastic modern floral cream scent. It does not disappoint me at any point and there is nothing I can criticize. In everyday life, I recommend dosing the perfume carefully, it is an exceedingly seductive scent. Now in winter, I was outside with it, the cold air is a catalyst, the sea of flowers constantly announces love. Now to the price. We tend to wear high-priced perfumes only on special occasions, which I think is wrong. Perfume lovers wear their treasures wherever and whenever they want. This scent is exorbitantly expensive and one might try to generate a flaw from this circumstance. Be that as it may, my dear readers, I must say the perfume is of course ridiculously expensive and I throw in the towel. But, smell for yourselves……

You left me, and yet you are still with me: a few drops of Roja's "A Goodnight Kiss" connect us for the time before falling asleep, the time of dreams. No sadness, just tender memories and gratitude for our time together are captured within it.
This perfume smells to me as an average 10 in a dozen perfume I have smellt before. Nothing special for such a rediculus price

On me, this might as well be a simple orange blossom cologne. Perfectly pleasant, but the kind of thing you can pick up for $10 US a bottle, not $200 US! Some lines just don’t work for some people. This is the sixth By Kilian I’ve tried and thought, “Why bother?," so I guess it's not the brand for me.

By Kilian PRELUDE TO LOVE is a very straightforward citrus-floral cologne. It reminds me very much of two other fragrances familiar to me (and probably lots of others in existence...): Bond no 9 EAU DE NEW YORK and Banana Republic W. I am sure that the latter comparison will be viewed as heresy by some, but before you balk, I defy you to try these three creations in a side-by-side trial and *then* try to deny that they are olfactory neighbors! PRELUDE TO LOVE is less green and sharp than Bond no 9 EAU DE NEW YORK, and for that reason some may prefer the By Kilian composition, as it is definitely less bracing. In the summer, I love EAU DE NEW YORK; in the winter, not so much. At the other end of the price spectrum, Banana Republic W compares favorably to PRELUDE TO LOVE, as well. W is less floral, and less declarative. To some people, that would make it more desirable as it is entirely inoffensive. However, I should say that from reading other reviews, it appears that some wearers' skin does not mix well with W, so those people probably would do better with the By Kilian. For those who are compatible with W, it's a fantastic bargain compared to either of these niche analogues of the same type. Do I like PRELUDE TO LOVE? Yes, of course. But I do not need a bottle, as I already own bottles of both EAU DE NEW YORK and W. A third bottle of such a similar composition would be more than redundant, and I do not believe that this creation is original. I'm not saying that Calice Becker copied anyone, but this is a good idea which others have had before--and have executed very well.

Since the scent is quite simple, I’ll use a bullet-point comment today: Dominant notes: (Klo-stone) citrus, musk, orange blossom, iris Fun facts: my first encounter with the Love Trilogy Occasions: upscale leisure events Gender: clearly more feminine Associations: the cleanest women's restroom in the world Seasons: spring and summer Familiarity: clearly and justifiably in the shadow of other Kilians Popularity: has fans, but it’s limited Criticism: very simple, slightly synthetic, and a strange musk-citrus combo Buy, Try or Pass?: pass for me and most Worth the price: oh no, no, no Bottle: beautiful silk coffin Sillage: delicate like a midsummer night's dream Longevity: 4-5 hours is poor Conclusion: one of the weaker Kilians and definitely not a turn-on for me...

Before I delve into the fragrance, I would like to express my heartfelt thanks to Seymour. He has introduced me to some of the most beautiful scents with entire sample collections, such as Les Parfums de Rosine. He has also brought me closer to Histoires de Parfums and Les Divines. His latest sample gift arrived just on Christmas Eve: a whole sample set of the now-famous Hennessy scion Kilian Hennessy. Dear Seymour, I thank you especially for this wonderful olfactory experience. The scents of a cognac cellar are certainly particularly enticing, and it is no surprise that Kilian Hennessy felt inspired to develop perfumes that meet his very special demands and expectations. Prelude to Love is an iris scent and truly reminds me a lot of the iris fragrance "Impossible Iris" by Ramón Monegal that I recently tested. The similarity between these two is astonishing. Prelude to Love starts with a juicy, orange-sweet citrus accord that lingers for quite a while. After about 20 minutes, you can already perceive the iris, still in conjunction with the top note. As the citrus accord weakens over time, the iris becomes more stable, and only the iris. I cannot perceive any other notes, neither neroli, nor pepper, no bergamot, no ginger, no orange blossom. Just a gentle, dry, slightly powdery iris, accompanied by the ever-fading orange note. Once this orange accord has completely evaporated, the iris calms down, becomes darker and a little softer, but remains powdery. Those expecting a fragrance progression here will be disappointed. Prelude to Love is a summer-fresh, powdery iris scent with a light, sweet, and very juicy citrus note, perfectly suitable for spring and summer, but also quite wearable in autumn and winter. Kilian describes this fragrance as the invitation. By name, the invitation to a love foreplay, the prelude to love. However, I do not see it that way. I cannot find any erotic traits in this scent, as there is absolutely no musk to be perceived, except for a gentle sweetness in the darker base. However, I must say that I do like this iris. It is less powdery than I usually know from iris scents and very pleasant for all occasions with this beautiful, juicy-sweet orange note. The sillage is very soft and close to the body, but the longevity is quite good. The latter applies to all Kilian fragrances, which hold up quite well. However, the sillage can vary significantly, which I can certainly demonstrate in further comments. For iris lovers, this fragrance might be too gentle, too fine, too quiet. For me, it is perfect, yet not a purchase scent. I fear it is not worth that high price to me, even though I really like it.

This is my second Kilian, but the hit rate is already significantly better than, for example, the Nouveau-Riche trash like Bond or the self-representations of Serge Lutens at a similarly exposed price level. Shortly after the citrusy start, you can already sense that it won't be too sweet. Okay, I'm in the right place.

Within the subcategory of the L'œuvre noire collection, there are three fragrances that deal with the theme of love and its prohibitions. While the other two fragrances, Love and Beyond Love, come across as quite sweet and therefore did not pique my interest, Prelude To Love is a flanker, as Kankuro has already mentioned.

There are fragrances that are energy boosters. Life elixirs. Scents that are associated with positive memories. First love, deep friendships, graduation, beautiful vacations, marriage, becoming parents, deep love. Things that one fondly remembers, that, as soon as they come to mind, bring a smile to your face.

or also: the mist must go! Fresh, clear, clean? What, please??? Uhhhm.. so more artificial lemon at the beginning is not possible, right? First, I am overwhelmed by chemical substances that smell like spirit, gasoline, or cleaning products. Terrible, just awful.

... these are, in my opinion, the most fitting words for this fragrance. It feels very clear, fresh, and summery. And it manages to be citrusy without being generic. The whole composition is truly extremely balanced, none of the notes are overdone. And I say this as someone who is not a big fan of citrus notes.

Fougeres rarely get my love  blame the countless synthetic clones occupying the 'men's' shelves in perfume shops. The genre seems to have been Xeroxed to an indistinguishable sludge. However, quality and craft will out. This doesn't start too promisingly: with a blast of aromatics ranging from mint toothpaste to pine room freshener. But soon we're into the heart notes (the best stage of this perfume) where everything turns more natural, the woods amplify, there's warmth but characteristic freshness too  one of those fairytale transformations where the figure in a painting or in a mirror slowly comes to life. Chest hairs sprout, one by one. One gets the impression of incredible detail without overbearing richness, so pleasing and stimulating. The drydown is a bit talced over, but the gaiac base keeps things beautifully rounded, sweet but still woodsy, the depth is not lost. This is handsome in a square-jawed kind of way but wears a check shirt and is basically unadventurous. Worth a fling just for the bone structure but don't expect the earth to move.

I had been on the lookout for this one for some months when I finally managed to salvage a bottle. Yes, RG being discontinued did give me a FOMO reaction. This time around I’m happy I stayed persistent in my search. The evening I got the bottle I spent sniffing my wrist, time and again, not being quite able to believe a fragrance can smell so good. Creamy, aromatic, smooth yet clean. The initial blast is one of airy and slightly piercing rosemary that quickly subsides. At this point, the scent is somewhat green and bright. Interestingly, I catch the oakmoss at this stage rather than in the dry down. It’s present on the fringe rather than as a stand-out element. The aniseed kicks in, followed by lavender and a cool/slightly metallic geranium. I believe it is the patchouli and guaiac wood combo that’s responsible for the backdrop against which the above notes play out against. This gives RG a multidimensional feel. A very 3-D scent. While there are fragrances similar to this, none of them do the smooth and clean shaving cream thing just quite like RG. Azzaro is more ’grandpa’ whilst TF BdJ is overkill on the lavender and patchouli, making it over the top aromatic. I like the mint note in the latter mentioned, though. Point being, I find RG unique enough that I can fully vouch for all the praise. Yes, it is that damn good!

It opens with some geranium, cloves, and mostly a very creamy anisic lavender. There's a substantial fresh shaving foam vibe that is sustained throughout, and a tiny bit of powderiness. That description might make this version of Rive Gauche sound run of the mill for American barbershop style fragrances, but what sets it apart is the sheer quality of the ingredients used and how well they are blended. When it comes to refined shaving foam, this one is hard to beat. If you're seeking to replace a vintage tin can bottle you should know that it’s substantially stronger and the gaiac wood note is almost completely absent in the reform. Projection is low; this reformulation is very subtle - nothing about it is in your face. For my tastes, overspraying this one is a necessity. On the other hand, longevity is outstanding. Masculinity Level: Paul Newman playing an aging lawyer in The Verdict.

Pretty much the same as the tin can, maybe the tin can is a little stronger and longer lasting, but if you are not a perfumer you really can't smell the difference. Price is very similar as the tin can so if you need to choose the tin can is a better choice, mainly because it's the original version and very rare. The same goes for this version, the greatest fougere/barbershop fragrance of all time. Masterpiece 10/10!

Eight years after the launch of 'Rive Gauche pour Homme', one of the most successful aromatic Fougères came to an end, a belated successor to the legendary 'Azzaro pour Homme'. Perhaps they should have waited a few more years, as aromatic Fougères seem to be coming back into fashion today. However, at the beginning of the new millennium, a new representative of this dusty genre was not going to win any accolades. Sure, 'Azzaro p.H.' was still around. Its success was so immense at the time that there were apparently still enough wearers contributing to its existence. But the reevaluation of this fragrance as one of the most important and influential creations, one of the best men's fragrances ever, was still pending back then, although it happened a few years later. RGpH was thus quite alone in the field and was completely overwhelmed by the role of being the flagship for a revival of the aging genre of aromatic Fougères. To make matters worse, IFRA also targeted an integral component of almost every Fougère (and especially every Chypre), oakmoss. RGpH was full of it, although not as much as Azzaro's scent - the use of oakmoss was already limited at that time - but the green-bitter tone, alongside the lavender-coumarin accord and the aromatic nuances, defined the character of the fragrance. Fortunately, the responsible parties at YSL did not give up without a fight and gave the fragrance a second chance. Quite revised, it became part of the Hèritage collection alongside other slow-sellers like 'M7', 'Jazz', and the classic 'Pour Homme'. The fact that RGpH was not hastily reformulated, that they made an effort to create a changed but still good fragrance - this honors YSL. And the new version is indeed good: woody, creamy, with the so typical soapy hints of aromatic Fougères, with plenty of civilized patchouli and well-balanced aromatic accents, foremost star anise and rosemary - all infused with a hint of fresh-floral geranium. Very nice, very finely balanced and blended. Compared to its predecessor, the entire fragrance experience feels much more civilized, more restrained. Not that the original was chaotic, no, but it was more contrasting and therefore more exciting. Similar to how the first 'Bel Ami' was more dissonant and thus more thrilling than all its later, smoothed-out successors. But be that as it may. The new RGpH is primarily woodier than its predecessor - the guaiac wood is now noticeably more central. The fragrance is still long-lasting and has a certain presence. Fears that the new owner L’Oréal might not handle YSL's legacy with care have fortunately not materialized, at least concerning the Hèritage collection. But somehow it is a shame that such a beautiful and characterful fragrance can no longer stand on its own and has to share the bottle with three others - the old cylindrical metal bottle was simply fantastic! Still: a wonderful Fougère fragrance!

Rive Gauche refers, according to Wikipedia, to the urban area of Paris located south of the Seine. Let me elaborate a bit. I have a fondness for classic fragrances that shouldn't remind one of a retirement home. Well-known retirement home scents would include Monsieur de Givenchy, Chanel pour Monsieur EdT, or Lauder for Men Cologne.

I have now been registered here for several months, during which my account balance has decreased, but my collection has grown just as much - I just haven't gotten around to actively writing yet. I think it's time to change that, and Rive Gauche is the fragrance that gives me the occasion to do so.

Over the past year, I have used a bottle of the "old" Rive Gauche pour Homme. I loved it but thought: That's enough, now I want something different, because the scent is now history. So far, so shortsighted, because I didn't yet know that I would have to rethink my attitude towards reformulations.

Dear Yves. Until your death, you released olfactory real hits. The "Jazz" that I love so much, your classic "Pour homme", the Opium for men, the universally controversial love-hate "Kouros", the beginning of the oud hype "M7", and this one here. The "Pour homme Variation" of your best-selling women's perfume. Rive Gauche. And since then?

With the (presumably reformulated) "Rive Gauche," one can hardly go wrong when searching for a green-masculine-spicy men's fragrance that doesn't overwhelm you with its spicy nuances right away. The scent fits well with its pleasantly unobtrusive masculinity for going out, without immediately hitting the other person with an aromatic punch.

You know that when you smell something, something comes to your mind? This something is a crown - a crown on your head. This perfume is so luxurious, a scent of violet, rose of May with leather. A male perfume. Good performance but don't expect all day performance. Expensive but in my opinion worth every pound. For me it's 9.5/10.

The first time I smelled this perfume was in Dubai After being very intrigued by it, the moment I smelled it I felt like I had entered the British royal family. It felt like I was smelling King Charles' perfume Chypre leather perfume but not just any leather, Russian leather! Russian leather with violet, May rose and iris which makes it the most royal! For me 9.0/10

This is my Roja Parfums Great Britain Fragrance Review. Roja Parfums Great Britain is an out of this world leather, chypre fragrance. Very sexy, very dry but very smooth with light sexy animalic touches. This is an absolutely stunning concoction. I highly recommend this out of this world leather fragrance. But it's certainly very very pricey. $1750 suggested retail for Great Britain. Either way, please make sure you get your nose on this one as it’s a must, must try for sure. This is of course created by Roja Dove. If you feel like finding out more about Great Britain please watch my review on YouTube. Thank you.

An exquisitely sophisticated fragrance, one I returned to after exploring many others from the same genre. With time and a bit of maturation , I’ve come to appreciate it even more. Now, a year later, I can say that it’s the finest Cuir de Russie I’ve encountered. It shares a kinship with Chanel’s Cuir de Russie, but this rendition has its own distinct charm. The violet and orris lend a soft elegance, while the leather leans suede, supple rather than stark. The animalic notes are present yet refined, and the aldehydes add a beautiful vintage glow. In short a stunning composition. Easily one of Roja’s best, right up there with Diaghilev, Fetish, and Musk Aoud Absolue.

Perfectly blended composition of leather and violet. These notes are not overpowering but dominate the whole composition. One of my favorites from the Roja Perfumes brand. Worthy of attention, but the price leaves much to be desired. The parameters could be better for such a price, but the quality of the ingredients is high - as is the case with Roja

I quickly deleted my last comment about "Opera" by Xerjoff; hence it is announced in vain. The very first response was hurtful and showed how little appreciation this "opus" would receive. As is well known, the opening is decisive, and unfortunately, this trend continues! Who likes to see something that has been carefully and lovingly composed go down the drain?

Hello everyone, This evening I would like to talk about Great Britain . I have known it for quite some time X (here we are talking about almost 7 years), but I never believed that I would actually own it, and this brings me directly to the one (!) but significant downside, which is its price...

Great Britain is a Roja that really appealed to me with its scent notes. My hope was to experience a wonderful woody, spicy, and slightly leathery unisex fragrance. This has certainly been achieved, if it weren't for a major catch. Great Britain simply smells like Dior Fahrenheit to me.

I wear the fragrance regularly in my daily life and have truly come to love it. Those who have only tested this scent briefly can hardly grasp how many facets it can show depending on the external and body temperature, in my opinion.

"I skillfully avoided 'Great Britain | Roja Parfums,' partly because of the price tag, and partly because few fragrances have truly satisfied me over the long term. Don’t get me wrong, the scents have a high level of refinement, but this classic style just doesn’t resonate with me.

This is a truly lovely tea scent! I bought this perfume a few months ago. I really love the pure black tea and jasmine tea scent. I love it! When I first put it on, it had a flat tea scent, but after a few minutes, it became a jasmine tea and floral scent. So I bought the previous version of Imperial Tea, and I liked that too. However, neither of them lasted very long.

From many scents that Calice Becker has created, a delicate tea aroma has wafted forth. I once read in an interview that Calice Becker is of Russian descent and grew up "next to a samovar." And now I wanted to smell the tea of all teas from the tea specialist. So off to Tanagra in Nice. I had probably underestimated that even there, where wealthy Russian women throw their money on the counter, not every day does a Kilian get sold. Accordingly, the consultation was quite engaging. After at least 30 minutes, I left with a buzzing head, trailing a cloud of "Liaisons dangereuses" behind me and with a sample of Imperial Tea in my bag, heading home. No, I would not buy Imperial Tea; it smelled like an oversteeped, swollen teabag into which a madman had dumped tons of jasmine flowers. At home, I sprayed it on again - and suddenly I had changed my mind. Hmm, tea. Tea. Tea. Somehow still elegant. Chic, somewhat noble. In my mind's eye, a few foot-stumbling, tripping maidens appeared, offering the "Lord of 10,000 Years" in the Forbidden City a delicate porcelain bowl. With tea in it that smells just like this. I wanted to smell like that too. Rarely, but somehow now and then. The fateful desire-to-have reflex had kicked in. And now I felt like those women who always end up with the wrong man. Reason speaks, but one does not follow it, even though one knows exactly: He is not great, he is taking advantage of me, he is completely unnecessary, I don't even really like him, I certainly don't need him. I still want him. What can I say: I bought it. Since I didn't want to subject myself again to the tirades of the saleswoman and endure her embarrassing expressions of gratitude ("Ah, Madame, you have exquisite taste" and mentally adding: "No, I don't, I rather have a screw loose for spending 200 euros on this swamp brew"), I ordered Imperial Tea online. Horrible... I know. I threw the stupid little box, lined with red polyester silk inside along with the cheap key, all trinkets made in China, into the trash. The bottle, on the other hand, is brilliant, beautiful. The perfume too. At least now and then. It doesn't last long, smells like a swampy teabag, doesn't change - and is completely unnecessary. But I like that it adorns my collection. And it's easier to care for than the wrong guy.

I must admit that I don't know many Kilian fragrances yet. The few that I have sniffed in perfumeries don't count, as sometimes you just catch a whiff of many scents, especially when your arms (and legs?) are already sprayed with fragrances. As a brand, Kilian has caught my attention mainly through the excellent scent Apple Brandy, which I found quite amazing. Now I'm testing Imperial Tea on the recommendation of a friend, as she knows exactly that I love tea! You know that too, and so it’s no surprise that sooner or later a comment from me about this fragrance would appear… of course with a nice cup of tea that I'm sipping while writing this. I'm also munching on some tea chocolate that I got from another fragrance enthusiast here… um… I meant fragrance fanatic :D (… keep it up, DonJuanDeCat… one day you will have all the perfumes here against you… :D) The scent: The scent starts off floral for me, even though I can't identify it immediately. It even smells a bit stuffy to me. At first, it also seems a bit smoky, but that fades quickly. Only after a few minutes do the stuffy notes weaken a bit, allowing you to distinctly smell a jasmine tea. And basically, that’s it, as the scent doesn’t develop further and remains the same until the end, with the stuffiness gradually diminishing, but the fragrance still comes across as quite floral. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is okay at first, but then falls to the level of most tea fragrances, making it somewhat weak and only detectable up close. The longevity is a bit better, as the scent can still be smelled on the skin quite consistently after about four to five hours. It only fades after seven to eight hours. The bottle: The bottle is rectangular, black, and has thick glass edges. On the sides of the bottle, you can see (cut-off) circular patterns that seem somewhat mysterious. On the front, there is a silver/metallic label with the name on it. The cap is cylindrical and black. All in all, a beautiful and high-quality bottle. Imperial Tea… yes yes, alright, you probably expected that I had to think a little about Star Wars because of the word Imperial, you know, the Empire and all, wanting to eternally suppress and destroy the rebels, only to be defeated in the end, with a new threat rising from its remnants, led among others by a bland milk-faced character named Kylo Ren… argh… But fine, I won’t dwell on that *sigh* Although it is a funny thought to wonder how Darth Vader could drink tea through the mask (probably about as Lord Helmet does in Spaceballs… :D). Well,… despite all my love for tea fragrances, I have to say that this scent disappointed me a bit. For me, it just turned out to be floral, but maybe I just don’t like the scent of jasmine tea. Aside from that, the fragrance is quite simple, especially given the price, almost trivial, and is therefore really only recommended for jasmine tea lovers, especially for warmer days.

Mr. Kilian thinks he is the new Tom Ford. His perfumes are mostly beautiful knock-offs and brazenly overpriced copies of successful classics or hidden gems. Taste of Heaven like Pour un Homme, Cruel Intentions like M7, Sweet Redemption like Fleur de Male, Sacred Wood like Wonderwood, and the new Imperial Tea like a feminine, weaker Gucci PHII.... This could be how an extremely hostile and critical review of the new by Kilian fragrance might begin. But I'm not like that and am happy to have received samples of Sacred Wood and Imperial Tea as gifts. Besides, there are indeed really good perfumes and aspects of By Kilian. Unfortunately, Imperial Tea does not belong to that category for me and is qualitatively further away from Back to Black than an R8 is from a Papa Mobil. Imperial Tea is really very unremarkable and only for jasmine and tea fans. But to be honest, I find both Bulgari and Gucci PHII better. Even if you disregard the price. IT is a bit smoky and minimally fruity, maybe forest berry tea... but the rest is pure tea and white flowers. But very natural and calming, if the jasmine wouldn't drive me up the wall. Luckily, Sacred Wood is much better, even if it is again a copy. I hope to test Apple Brandy and especially Vodka on the Rocks someday, without déjà vu or other bitter aftertastes. Bottle: all the same from by Kilian... equally dreamy! Sillage: this tea simmers quietly. Longevity: 6 pale hours. High quality but boring and once again more or less well copied. That's not enough for me, and the jasmine is annoying again... even if it is served here as tea.

Better then La Nuit L’Homme It smells like La Nuit L’Homme, but it has in 3-4 times more longevity and Sillage. Longevity 12 hours minimum Sillage 2-3 meters If you want best version of La Nuit L’Homme, then buy this.

Assuming that the 'frozen cocktail accord' listed on another site means Gin & Tonic with ice and lemon, its fair to say this juice lives up to its fanciful note description. The structure tries to balance coldness with an underlying dose of syrup, which becomes more apparent as the Gin & Tonic - and cardamom - wears off. Done in the regulation smoothly synthetic manner, Frozen Cologne arrives perky and sociable and seems designed to not offend anyone - unless they have a dislike of gungy sweet drydowns. For the G&T effect to work at all, which is the the sole reason for this flanker, I think it needs to be worn on clothes as it doesn't project from my skin. There is little to recommend here, the G&T accord being fragile and the drydown banal, but overall I wouldn't call it bad, just gimmicky.

Given how much I enjoy the original as well as Bleu Électrique, when I saw this for sale on eBay I couldn’t resist. Despite the significant price gouging I incurred, I’m happy with my purchase. Hindsight is 20/20 and I must say that the hype behind this one is well warranted, La Nuit de L’homme Frozen is far superior to the other flankers in the line.

This has been sitting on my wishlist for a while, I was sure I'd never get this in my collection since it's been long discontinued. I read extensively about it, how it was a fresh take on the grand La Nuit de l'Homme. All reviews are positive mentioning the fresh notes, the tender sweetness, the delightfulness so my expectations were very high. I was lucky enough to find a 100ml brand new Frozen Cologne with 30% off (if they only knew they could've sold this over ebay for 3x the price) so I didn't even think twice before purchasing and yeah, I wasn't ready for it. I've read that Geranium is the main note and key player here and I don't recall any of my fragrances having any prominent Geranium notes so this was already uncharted territory for me. The fragrance opens with a nice citrus blast with some sweeter notes, they got that right however this lasts 10 to 15 mins before all the fresh and 'frozen' notes disappear. After that it's La Nuit de l'Homme Cologne (nothing frozen about it). Then there's the Geranium, Pepper and Cashmere Wood present and I guess the tonka in the back (in account for the creamy and sweet feel). On the first wear I didn't like it but didn't hate it, on second wear it grew on me. I still haven't decided if it Love or Like, I certainly don't Hate it but it'll take a couple of wears to get there. The 'frozen' name is misleading and I'm not sure this is a day wear for Spring and Summer, to me this is an evening/night wear for Spring and Autumn. Longevity is very good for an Eau de Cologne.

La Nuit is not only the biggest number from YSL. Not only the best perfume of this brand by far (imo). And not just an even better, sexier version of the already good everyday original L’Homme. La Nuit de L’Homme has also gained recognition and immense popularity in the absolute mainstream market among the masses. And rightly so. The fact that it is not yet in my collection is a small shame, as I like the original so much. I haven't tested the perfume version yet, but since the EdT is supposed to be better anyway, I don't think that will happen. However, I just had to test the Frozen version.
