The bottle is one of the greatest eye-catchers ever, topping the already beautiful and heavy original with its ice look. My aversion to unnecessary extreme, fresh, or intense versions that only create confusion easily disappears here. Even though I could never really shake the question of sense and justification throughout the entire testing period, the Frozen Cologne performs well to very well for me. The La Nuit DANN is skillfully altered and complemented by a citrus note that builds a clever blend of icy cold breath and warm tension. Very nice. Not necessarily needed, as La Nuit is quite perfect. But for those who prefer it a bit cooler and more varied, they can certainly make the comparison. Although Frozen is still a bit too heavy for summer, there is this accompanying citrus note that takes away some of the excitement of the original and adds a coolness and a bit of humor. If there are updates, then let them be like this. Even though you can hardly go wrong with this DANN. With Brangelina, it’s hard to imagine a child not looking good ;-) But whether they need so many children is another question parallel to the perfume world! The scent is not quite as sweet as La Nuit, but still smells seductive and a bit like chocolate and a vanilla praline with a citrus cocktail. Very great mix, I can only emphasize again and again, this offshoot is no flop, on the contrary. The light hint of pepper paired with fruits, here more citrus than apple in the original, gives it the finishing touch. The bottle is, as mentioned, top class, the sillage is weaker than the original, but still a bit too wild for summer in my opinion. But you can try it out in a well-dosed manner. The longevity is also slightly lower than the high bar, clocking in at 7-8 hours. Not perfect, as it doesn't surpass the original. But that was already clear beforehand. And otherwise, thumbs up!

I was lucky enough to find a new 60ml stock bottle today and took it home blindly. I never liked this direction of fresh fragrances. I didn't like the YSL men's line either. Everyone wears it, it smells too much like mainstream. So it was doubly hard for my new YSL. However, I was completely surprised and instantly convinced!

Now a comment on a flanker from the endless L'Homme series. Sometimes it's really hard to judge whether you actually need a flanker of a fragrance classic. The number of flankers hitting the market is truly enormous. Usually, it's just about making quick money. Nice gimmicks are sold for a high price. Especially with brands like Yves Saint Laurent and the like.

Yesterday, I gave the latest iteration of a rather poor "flanker" from a French fragrance its (only) chance. And what can I say: Reconstructing the experience the next day is as difficult as remembering the faces of strangers from last night. First, a few cheerful, youthful berry accents wafted up.

About the scent: Great opening with citrus accord and pepper, a fresh, cool aura surrounds you. Perfect for warmer days. Quickly balanced by the woods and the fantastic La Nuit DNA. Certainly not the strongest connection to the classic DNA, but for me, the best fragrance flanker from YSL.

What a shame that this flanker is no longer produced! I recently had the luck to snag an unopened flanker at an affordable price. It was a blind buy that was worth it. Frozen Cologne has the beloved La Nuit De L'homme DNA with a wonderful fruity note - especially the mandarin comes through strongly. For me, this scent is also perfect for warmer days.

I'll get to the title later. Yesterday, I went out with two other perfume enthusiasts in Munich. We had a lot of fun and were able to exchange ideas well... "You absolutely have to try the new one from Roja." Alright. Although I must say, without wanting to stir up any trouble, I was a bit disappointed with Roja. Firstly, none of the previous ones lasted on my skin, and secondly, they simply didn't develop the magic and pull that would have made me willing to invest in a bottle. Well, that changed yesterday. In the small Theatiner perfumery, it stood fresh and innocent before me, and boom, two sprays on my arm. I love amber. I love chocolate. I like dark, heavy, warm, soft scents. All of that is amber. It doesn't have a significant development to speak of. It is warm, rounded amber with the finest chocolate, or should I say: cocoa. I can smell that very clearly. And to balance it out, there's a hint of tangy oranges. I can still perceive something woody, the vanilla is noticeable but not strong. I am thoroughly impressed. This is not a spectacular, loud scent. But very unique. Soft, skin-like, ambered, chocolaty. Delicious. In the forum, someone was looking for comforting scents. This would be my comfort scent. Truly. A perfect soul soother!

what happens when you test an amber that costs 275 British pounds for 50ml? Either you assume it must be something grandiose, or you are critical and have grand expectations. For me, it’s probably more about the high expectations, which makes it difficult for the fragrance to score points. For this price, I expect a clear unique selling proposition and a quality impression that seems unattainable in lower price ranges. "Amber" starts off a bit uncomfortably for me. Herbal lavender and geranium open the fragrance together with plenty of bergamot and orange. Very herbal-floral-fresh, which directly meets the amber. I find the combination a bit disturbing; especially the herbal and floral notes take away some of the warmth that Althea mentioned, and come across as a bit rough. Fortunately, this impression gradually fades, and a decent dose of patchouli smooths everything out. Patchouli? Yes! The amber seems almost to have disappeared. In the opening and in the transition to the heart note, I smelled a chocolaty amber that was great but lost some appeal due to those herbal notes. Now amber becomes a patchouli scent for me. Amber, sandalwood, vanilla... that seems to be present only to soften the patchouli. Now the fragrance smells to me like a particularly cuddly "Psychedelique," with a touch of vanilla and amber. A beautiful fragrance, a soft, rounded, well-composed scent. Not an amber for me; but should I praise or criticize that? I find it nice when an amber doesn’t develop like thousands of other amber fragrances. However, when an amber smells more like patchouli and hardly like amber, I question whether the goal has been achieved. Roja has not created a century-defining fragrance for me here, nothing that breaks boundaries or leaves me speechless. It’s a lovely scent for people with well-filled wallets. However, there are so many cheaper, beautiful fragrances in the realm of amber and patchouli that, in my opinion, the Roja does not represent a must-have. Certainly the Bugatti of any collection, but olfactorily I see it as interchangeable. The extrait, however, shines with a decent sillage and a longevity that easily lasts intensely into the next day. That’s already a bit too much for me. I’m a bit uncertain about the rating. There are fragrances that I like less but still received 80%. I found them particularly interesting; there were other motivations. I find the Roja nice, the patchouli annoys me, I wanted an amber scent, not a patchouli. "Amber" is, however, detached from price and other factors, rounded and beautiful, even if not outstanding and somewhat "missed." Just for the scent impression, it certainly deserves 80%, but there are simply points like the outrageously inflated price and considering that the disturbing notes in the opening and the almost pure patchouli base that bring a deduction for me.

My dear Mr. Roja Dove, or something like that, I can still understand that you want to ride the Oud wave, but that this dreamy amber fragrance had to make way for it is simply unacceptable. I truly wish you would/could read this and would immediately bring it back into your collection. There, that needed to be said. I, who actually don't like lavender at all, and chocolate scents either, find this combination of lavender and cocoa in the opening genius. Cocoa softens the lavender, and the lavender gives the cocoa something fresh and takes away its bitterness, because it's not sweet cocoa. And then this wonderful amber base mixes in. Simply a dream. Everything else is just embellishment, rounding it off. I am thrilled with this amber fragrance and can only repeat: "Please bring it back to us!" Especially for us girls. The amber-oud cannot compare at all.

Ah Roja, you and your high-priced fragrances. In selling, you are a king, but promoting the uniqueness of your scents doesn’t always succeed (excellently). Yes, it is easy to claim, although not easy to analyze, what should qualitatively set your fragrances apart from others. You come across as too coy and pretentious, which doesn’t exactly benefit your commercial intentions. Anyway, much of it seems…well…somewhat strange, if one sets aside your sometimes outrageously exaggerated self-presentation, which you try to completely *ignore*. Your affluent clientele may not care, and they should, in case of doubt. A rascal thinks ill of it. You certainly cannot be denied sophistication, nor a shrewd eye for quality - even your biggest critics have noticed that. And yes, with Amber, you have truly achieved a great success, far removed from your mostly overpriced average goods. Here you present us with a wonderfully balanced gourmand, though the name alone may cause some confusion. But more on that elsewhere. Amber initially opens with a cocoa note that is clearly in the foreground, which, to give you a heads-up, could hardly be more finely resolved. At least nothing of comparable quality has been presented to me so far. A characteristic aroma consisting of malty, slightly caramel-like nuances, refined with a not overly sweet vanilla: Wonderful! The base is indeed lovely, but it initially gains a darker character through the lavender and, in the later development of the scent, thanks to the spicy resins, particularly the increasingly prominent patchouli, which certainly benefits the sillage and likely sways the last skeptics who had feared an overly heavy base from the start. No, nothing detonates in the candy store of your trust here! Surrounded by a light sandalwood note, after 4-5 hours, the labdanum along with the benzoin unfolds, giving the gourmand direction an oriental twist. For some, this phase could certainly have been a tad more voluminous to do justice to the name that Roja has given his extrait. In the drydown, the resins then take over. The benzoin sets the course and is pleasing: very creamy, warm, and sensitive - as snug as a second skin. A dream. As part of the Heritage Collection (again) available, Amber is definitely worth a look and for lovers of cocoa-like fragrance compositions, an absolute recommendation to buy. I love it!!! The sillage is particularly excellent in the (no longer available) extrait version. Just 1-2 sprays are enough; anything beyond that: no guarantee. Longevity? Also extraordinarily: It fades - depending on moisture and warmth - only after 10-14 hours on my skin. A masterpiece by Mr. Roja Dove.

You can say something like that in the headline, right? At least it is true!;) The tragedy about the box....., the fragrance is no longer available. Typical Roja, of course, exorbitantly priced and since the scent is no longer produced, it gets even worse. But what a stroke of genius, warm, spicy, gourmand, always caressing..., I just fell in love, uh, I mean, I’m smitten! How cheeky, how beautiful you are?!! I don’t even want to break down the individual components, this masterpiece is too brilliantly complex. I feel a bit like "Gollum" right now..., my precious!!! And even if one looked like that, this fragrance would make everything worthwhile. Mr. Roja, thank you very much for this masterpiece and at the same time a curse..., but the best go first.
The more I wander around in the "Roja fragrance world," the clearer it becomes to me: the top and heart notes of most creations are rooted in Provence.

Imagine giving three among the nicest masculines by Lutens - Fumerie Turque, Borneo 1834 and Chergui – to your 8 years old nephew asking him to make a Frankenstein hybrid out of them. This is Light my fire. It has them all: hay, tobacco, honey, vanilla, a lot of patchouli, the zesty-salty touch of vetiver. It’s nice, pleasant, warm and sophisticated. And costs almost like the three Lutens together. With a quite remarkable – negative – difference as regards of quality, as it quickly becomes a saggy, unsubstantial, plain blend mostly centered on patchouli and vetiver which just an earthy sweet-smoky feel, and an annoying synthetic aftertaste. On the drydown it also recalls Jovoy’s Private Label a bit, mostly for the same way vetiver is treated here – that same dark “inky” and oily kind of note with hay-earthy nuances. That’s it, uncreativity at its best lasting like a fart. Meh... 5,5-6/10

For several years now, our family has been making a specific tour on one of the weekends following May 17th: We head out early in the morning to Eckernförde. There, we have breakfast in a café by the harbor before visiting the “Bonbonkocherei Hermann Hinrichs” and strolling along the pedestrian zone. At some point, we drive around the Eckernförder Bay to the burial forest “Küstenfrieden,” where my mother, who passed away in 2011, and my father's second partner rest. A beautiful little spot right by the steep coast. Most of the time, I bring two branches of blooming lilacs. Then we take the back road to Kiel. Sometimes it’s already warm enough to linger for an hour at one of the small beaches on the Danish Wohld. Upon arriving in Kiel, we stop at the northern end of Knooper Weg and have a scoop of ice cream from “Eis-Paradies.” One scoop is enough; the tiny shop has been locally famous for decades for a delightful combination of quality and quantity. Afterwards, we either drive home, trusting in temporary saturation for the short hour, or if hunger strikes too hard, we make a detour to Metzstraße to Garips Imbiss for a döner on the way to the highway. How now? Yes, now! Threefold: 1. Of course, we have the ice cream first. We’re not going back and forth. 2. The internet only partially tells the story of this culinary gem. In truth, it goes back at least to my student days. I know this because 3. my wife and I had our first shared apartment just around the corner. During our last visit, we were sitting on the small terrace in front of the restaurant with pastries in hand when another family with somewhat younger children showed up. What we heard proved that we were not the only ones who had come out of nostalgia. Dear Farih Garip! You haven’t been there for ages, but you and your successors may forgive me for starting with your snack bar here, even though I never had any reason for a complaint like the one mentioned below. Your “With everything? And with plenty of spice again?” is still ringing in my ears in the best memory. So. To the scent: A gasoline-biting botanical note is quickly followed by a massive dose of hot, sweaty cumin. It smells like slyly spiced döner meat, the age of which - or a break in the cold chain - should not be revealed. Of course, the olfactory evidence still wafts out of every pore of the dead meat. At least the operators have put in above-average effort into the originality of the salad. Probably a smokescreen that - see above - is also meant to distract from the real problem. Only after a good half hour does more floral emerge, and the salad impression fades. Additionally, a trace of caramel-cream-vanilla artificial sweetness appears. Well, occasionally questionable desserts linger in the refrigerators. I even kept my hands off such things at Farih… The undeniably musty-sour-sweaty spice scent, the budding fresh botanicals, and the prickly-synthetic sweetness mix, in my opinion, extremely unhappily. It may be originally conceived, but the originality in this case seems somewhat forced, as if drawn up on a drafting board and merely meeting theoretical claims. As time goes on, I find the scent to be very static for a long time. Even around noon, the same description could fundamentally apply, although the focus has steadily shifted towards spice and continues to shift. In the afternoon, a new phase begins as various aromas from the sweet corner increasingly frolic beneath the sweaty-musty layer. Wish upon a star - the descriptions are quite plausible: honey, baking aroma-bitter almond, hay-tonka-coumarin sweetness. They all seem to be united by a girlishly-nervous-giggly-clean musk cream to a mannered, charming overkill. A few herb-woody aspects and a stubborn remnant of sticky sweatiness stand on the losing side. At the very end, it is already evening, I imagine a diffuse animalistic hint (one that goes beyond dead animal on a spit, I think). Perhaps a pinch of castoreum? Stinky labdanum? But that may be nonsense; basically, I’ve already tuned out and am glad that this aftertaste is happening very close-up. Conclusion: Strange and annoyingly unbalanced. I thank Ergoproxy for the sample.

And indeed one with lots of marzipan and almonds (and presumably candles that want to be lit, considering the name of the fragrance). So delicious starts "Light my Fire," the latest work from Kilian alongside two others from the newest collection "Addictive State of Mind." Along with the marzipan and almonds, more and more fine tobacco joins in, immediately bringing back memories of "Tonka Imperiale." However, I won't dig out my Guerlain sample for a direct comparison; the similarity should be recognized as it is. And the associations continue: yes, clearly "Dolce Acqua" by Profumum Roma or "Heliotrope" by Etro. It's not quite Christmas yet, but with Kilian, it already smells like it. A delicious mix of the mentioned fragrances and certainly a good splash of Tom Ford's "Tobacco Vanille," and there you have the good Kilian dough. Everything is very sweet, very high-quality, elegant, still quite unisex (the tobacco is herbal!), and it just makes my mouth water, bite marks included. And the more you chew through to the cake base, i.e., the closer you get to the fragrance's foundation, the stronger a spicy-animalic note suddenly emerges, which I would have guessed to be clove, cinnamon, and musk, but it’s probably cumin here. So, the good Kilian must have poured in half a bottle of "Musc Ravageur" to avoid creating just another trivial sweet scent. From here on, it definitely becomes unisex, if not slightly masculine. Thus, "Light my Fire" is a complex fragrance in its development. And that's exactly why I love niche fragrances; "L'Homme Ideal," for example, smells embarrassingly bad and inferior in comparison. Do you need "Light my Fire"? Only if you don't already have enough other similar sweet treats. But even then, it's worth taking a sniff; Kilian skillfully quotes, summarizes what belongs together, and delivers an overall fantastic, slightly different delight for the senses. Applause!

Light my Fire starts intensely and darkly with omnipresent accords of tobacco and leather. After the drydown, Light my Fire quickly becomes calmer, and a sweet woodiness mixes into the fragrance profile in a very minimalist way. However, the sweetness is only to be seen as a subtle accent and not as an independent fragrance component. The mixture of dark tobacco and the wood accord creates a very rounded and cuddly scent profile. After about 2 hours, a warm smoky note blends into this texture, but the fragrance also continues to retreat further onto the skin. Overall, Light my Fire is a truly finely tuned warm, dark, and distinctly masculine fragrance. The scent texture is wonderfully dense and envelops the wearer like a fine elegant veil. Unfortunately, the sillage is really minimalistic after about 1 hour, allowing the fragrance to be perceived only very closely and withdrawn. Longevity is also a problem, as after about 4-5 hours, the olfactory delight is already over. It's a pity because the fragrance profile itself is truly elegant and exudes a noble quality; unfortunately, this does not help a fragrance that remains shyly in the background and is barely noticed. Sillage: weak Longevity: 5h Projection ___- ( ) More by Kilian fragrances on my blog: http://www.parfumo.de/Benutzer/RisingScent/Blog/Eintrag/1_by_Kilian_Eine_bersicht

Normally, I really like many of the "by Kilian" fragrances I've tested. But with this one, I'm not quite sure if I should like it or not. "Light my fire" is a bold blend of gourmand scents, flowers, and dry, slightly "burnt" wood notes. And dried hay. The sweeter fragrance notes come into play at the beginning of the scent evolution, vaguely reminding me of a certain "Lutens". As it develops, flowers mix with a slightly bitter almond aroma, similar to "Armanac" (I don't know the correct spelling), an almond liqueur. Then "Light my Fire" gets to the point, living up to its name: A dust-dry, sawdust-evoking wood aroma that settles on the nose like powder. Almost tangibly physical. It has a slight "burnt" quality to it. Not burnt like charred, more like sawdust exposed to the summer sun. The scent is quite interesting because I haven't smelled anything like it before. But I believe that if I were to smell "Light my Fire" on myself for an extended period, I might grow weary of it. Apologies to everyone who likes this "Kilian": This is my very personal impression and has NOTHING to do with the QUALITY of the perfume.

Briefly, YSL La Nuit de l'Homme meets Fahrenheit Absolute. Unfortunately not resulting with synergistic effect, because the best features of both perfumes are hidden in this l'Intense. Lavender, cardamom and iris paired with sweet darker notes of tonka and vanilla, but this alcoholic sweetness lacks refinement. Seems this perfume's target groups are more mature 1 Million lovers. Le Parfum version in my opinion is more successful attempt to make La Nuit darker. L'Intense is nothing groundbreaking, and just an average release. Rating:6/10

This is truly wretched. If you want to create a mental picture of how this smells, imagine the following: a gossipy, oversocialized teenage girl sits in the driver's seat of her father's car, waiting for her homosexual male friend to return with the artificial vanilla drinks they just ordered from Starbucks. She sits there, quietly and nonchalantly applying cheap plasticy makeup in the mirror when he bounds up to her window, frightening her in the process. She yelps and drops the compact on her thighs, splattering the ionone-laden powder all over the seat and center console. "Oh my god, I'm sooo sorry!" he says and leans in the window to brush her off, spilling the corn syrup sweetened drinks inside the car in the process. "My dad is going to f*c&#^g kill me, Ja'relle. We need to clean this up now!" They pop the trunk and discover a three pack of Lysol linen-scented disinfectant wipes and an unused cannister of Febreeze. They hastily scrub at the saccharine, powdery mess now permanently imbued in the carpets with a duo of America's most disgustingly and synthetically scented consumer cleaning products. "We need to get some of those little blue tree air fresheners to cover up the smell" she remarks. He agrees and they quickly head to the nearest gas station. With a blue "New Car Scent" tree freshly hung from the rear view mirror, they head home and park the car in the garage. In uncharacteristically quiet fashion, they slink away to their friend's house down the street, unnoticed. Four hours later, her father walks into the garage so that he can grab the cleaning products that he had purchased but forgotten to remove the night prior. He pops the trunk. Not there. But wait.. what's that? He lifts his nose into the air, catching the faintest aroma of the tragedies that unfolded on his upholstery mere hours ago. He squints and sniffs a few times more, realizing that the scent is coming from inside the car. He stands up, closes the trunk door, and heads to the driver's side door. He hesistates for a second or two, and then slowly opens the door. Immediately, his eyes and nostrils are greeted by the heinous chemical abortion wrecked upon his automobile in full, synthetic, gory detail. He closes the door, and then his eyes. "I'm going to f*c&#^g kill her" he mutters under his breath.

This perfume is a good example why I never listen to people's *opinions* on scents - or anything really. When it launched, it got no good rep and I don't even know why. When I first tested it - it became an instant certified classic to me. I can't explain how special this scent is. I ain't no expert on notes but I can pick up the iris strongly - I know that note from other iris fragrances I own, and overall it shares the "feelin of the OG La Nuit while being different in a very good way. I can appreciate something that smells this damn good. If it's cooler and it's dark out, often will reach this one. Even better when around a young lady. And how come there are complaints about performance? It radiates on me, and I been told by people around. This one is discontinued and I am sure cause I don't see it on the shelves anymore. So I rushed to grab a bottle, and I am damn glad I did. You should pick one up while You can, You will thank Me later.

I have used about 23 bottles of La Nuit De L'homme in my life, about 9 bottles of L'homme. I know the FRAGRANCE DNA In and Out. This perfume La Nuit Intense is awesome - period. The only dangerous thing is that it is even SOFTER than the already unisex/feminine La Nuit De L'homme, and that has also been the reaction from women to this perfume so far. Either they find it too soft or the IRIS turns them off (it's the same with Dior Homme/Intense); when you smell an iris fragrance too closely to the test strip, you get a relatively unpleasant earthy/carrot scent from it. The dry down after 6-7 hours is indeed "fuller/richer" than the La Nuit EDT, La Nuit EDT is "sheer," the Intense is "packed," even though the longevity isn't bad - it remains a very, very gentle scent. I love the new Intense (but that was obvious). However, women currently prefer the EDT more! My first impressions video on the fragrance is here: https://youtu.be/PhCawswxZgk

I already wrote something about this flanker of La Nuit de L'Homme almost a year ago. Back then, I was slightly disappointed. The reason for that was that I tested two fragrances simultaneously. Just before Christmas, I wanted to try two sweet scents for the cold winter season. On one hand, I tested this one, and on the other, the Armani Code Profumo. My judgment was clear. The Code Profumo won by miles. Also with this beast mode performance. Actually, it was an unfair duel, as this one is really not bad, even though it quickly fades after a while. Perhaps the anticipation and expectations were simply too high. In the meantime, this flanker is even in my possession. For just under 70 euros, you can get 100ml. Not cheap, but for Yves Saint Laurent, it's reasonable. The bottle is really very, very pretty. The usual L'Homme bottle, but the gradient is really lovely, and this color combination fits perfectly with the sweet wintery La Nuit. Regarding the scent: At the beginning, there is a strong iris dominance, similar to Dior Homme. A carroty and earthy iris, slightly powdery. This dominance of iris lasts about 1 hour and then fades slightly. A clear La Nuit DNA follows. However, it is noticeably cozier and more wintry. This is of course due to the tonka bean and vanilla. Like in so many winter fragrances, two great notes that provide a high cuddle factor. Here, it is also very elegantly executed. The DNA is clearly recognizable. A nice and sweet companion for the colder season. This creation is not very masculine, but masculine types can wear such fragrances well, and women might like this one. Similar to Dior Homme, it is more of a sensual evening and night scent. After the powdery opening, it is an elegant sweet fragrance. Perfect for cold days. One should not overestimate the iris here, as it is really almost exclusively in the top note. I cannot confirm the name of the flanker L'Intense. In terms of performance, La Nuit de L'Homme is significantly better. At least the old batches, as it has been reformulated. I had hoped for more performance with the L'Intense addition. The longevity is not bad at about 6-7 hours, but especially for sweet winter fragrances, there is definitely more potential. Moreover, it really only has a significant sillage for the first 3-4 hours. Since it is not a work fragrance anyway, it is not a hindrance. Overall, a great flanker that you don't necessarily have to own. Especially regarding performance, there are better winter fragrances. I like the sweet intense version of L'Homme much better. For me, it is a great alternative for colder evenings. Addendum: After wearing it several times and having it for a few months, I must elevate it again. It is a fragrance that I like even more after wearing it multiple times. Worn often in the evening, I felt very comfortable. The beautiful, very carroty, powdery iris simply comes across very stylishly in combination with vanilla, tonka, and patchouli. A great sweet-powdery combo that is quite special. Plus, the La Nuit DNA. Wonderful!

The "L'Homme" line from YSL is probably one of the most extensive sequels in the perfume sector. While I still quite like the regular version, the fresher variants are particularly too trivial for me, and the nighttime stories are a bit too flatly sweet.

Every few months, a new L'Homme flanker from YSL comes out, you can set your watch by it. The success seems to continue despite mediocre reviews. Soon, not only the football team will be filled, but also the substitute bench. An annoying success story. But success justifies itself & doesn’t diminish my anticipation for the new La Nuit L'Intense. Okay, a little...

After extensively testing the La Nuit de L'homme series by Yves Saint Laurent with the (presumably?) last flanker, Eau Electrique, I am very convinced that this one could be the best variant for the future. This is partly because two very successful components have been combined here to create an unbeatable fragrance. Now, YSL has only partially succeeded in this.

I already own La Nuit de L‘ Homme le Parfum, which I enjoy wearing because it is a cozy scent, not too loud, but still elegant. The Intense, on the other hand, starts with a more dominant iris note that is much harsher, which initially irritated me a bit, but now I really like it. After about 1 1/2 hours, the iris becomes weaker, but remains pleasantly present.

You were beautiful. You are beautiful. You will always be. La Nuit de L'Homme with glowing iris at its heart. Started as a sidekick, you just weren't fresh and spicy enough to step into the vintage La Nuit de L’Homme’s footsteps.

Roja Dove is much debated on fragrance boards lately. From high praise and euphoria to disappointment, every kind of opinion can be found. And not only on fragrance boards you can find discussions about Roja Parfums. Various fragrance groups, as well as many Facebook are enchanted by Monsieur Doves' creations. This makes one thing very clear: The Maître and his creations are highly polarizing. No wonder, since the prices of the products are far higher than comparable manufacturers, such as Amouage, Maison Francis Kurkdjian, by Kilian or Bond No. 9. There even have been claims that the high prices are only a tool to attrac a certain kind of clientele. Let's be honest: Every perfume maker needs to make money in order to continue existing. Each product has a target audience, which doesn't mean other buyers are not welcome. Also, whether I belong to the target group of a brand or not, I do not care about such things. But let's talk about the scent, Scandal Pour Homme. Currently it's the only Fougère fragrance in the men's line of Roja Parfums. To be honest, I did not expect too much from Scandal pour Homme, as I have never been a great fan of Fougère fragrances. Scandal though, taught me to be patient and try to let a fragrance uncover all of it's secrets, before judging it based on the olfactive family it belongs to. Scandal pour Homme is a kind of scent I can not classify easily. Why is that? Well, the opening feels like it has a little bit of everything. Shy citrus notes, who sneak around. They disappear as quickly as they appeared, leaving a pleasant blend of mild herbaceous and lush green fragrant impressions. Also, there is a subtle kind of fruitiness, which is by no means edible or sweet. So this is a fougère? I am not sure about it, and really, it does not matter. One thing is certain: Scandal pour Homme does not smell even a tiny bit like contemporary mens fragrances. It rather reminds me of a scent from another time. This is by no means negative, as it's a pleasure to find such a classic smelling scent that was launched only three years ago. The first stage of the scent, which still smells moist and pleasently green, only starts to change after about 25 minutes. A delicate floralcy emerges from the depths of the composition. The heart note is still green, but I clearly notice some white florals, like jasmine and lily-of-the-valley. In addition to the floral elegance, the first signs of the base notes start to emerge. Especially the moss is already present. Together with the flowers, the overall impression is a bit sweetish and definitely forest like. Those who know my preferences in fragrances might know that I appreciate neither green nor forest like fragrances. Scandal pour Homme is one of the very few exceptions. Why? For me, the rather unpleasant flavors were used subtly in the composition of Scandal pour Homme. They all work together perfectly and create a beautiful and lively harmony. Mr. Dove has created a perfume that truly deserves the title "Parfum". Unlike fragrance creations that try to imitate the smell of a certain object or a certain note, or are highly Gourmand and remind of delicious delicacies, there are those scents that unmistakeably smell like perfume, or like some people would say: Perfumey. And this is what I've experienced in all Roja creations I have tried so far. No wonder that Mr. Dove prefers these classic accords, he worked for 20 years at Guerlain. Everyone who knows Guerlain will understand why. If you look at the base notes of Scandal pour Homme, you will notice a big variety of notes listed. Frankly, I can not make out a single one. This happens a lot to me with complex creations, the big amount of single notes tend to create a whole new olfactive impression. It's delicate, still refined and green with plenty of moss. A delicate sweetness sneaks around, surrounded by an elegant woodiness. Scandal pour Homme ends like it has begun: Difficult to classify, interesting and "très élégant". Chapeau, Maître Dove! You created a fougère fragrance which appeals even to me, a lover of oriental and gourmand fragrances. This rarely ever happens, and I am happy I had the chance to sample Scandal pour Homme. This fragrance test made me realize once more: Fragrances need time to unfold all their aromas and nuances. Scandal pour Homme, even if there is nothing scandalous about this perfume, is the manifestation of elegance and class. For me it was love at second sight. Roja Parfums is a line every perfume lover should eventually try. Give them time, and they will reveal their true nature to you, these fragrances are alive and full of beauty!

Scandal pour Homme (Parfum) opens with a brief blast of grassy green tarragon tinged bergamot citrus with hints of aromatic lavender before quickly moving to its heart. As the composition enters its early heart the aromatic lavender remains, now somewhat stronger in its intensity, joined by a gentle nutmeg spiced jasmine-like lily-of-the-valley led white floral accord slightly sweetened by tonka bean. Moving further through its heart, the lavender and white florals join a vague blonde woody accord that takes on a co-starring role. During the late dry-down the composition turns distinctly green as oakmoss' mossy green facet is featured initially, later turning powdery as leathery labdanum and slightly sharp cedarwood join in through the finish. Projection is very good and longevity excellent at about 12 hours on skin. Scandal pour Homme (Parfum) is one of those compositions that is difficult to dislike but you feel doesn't really take a lot of risk either. While not taking risks, only smelling "pleasant" is far from a fatal flaw in a composition, it does seem somewhat beneath a composition from a house with Roja Dove's reputation. Also somewhat beneath the house's reputation is the tiresome synthetic cashmeran-derived blonde woody accord used in the latter heart section. In all fairness, the cashmeran is quite deftly controlled, far from an easy feat, but its use seems somewhat unnecessary. Probably the best part of the composition's development is the late dry-down when the cashmeran vacates and the oakmoss and labdanum base notes really get to shine. At the end of the day the whole thing just does not distinguish itself from so many other compositions on the market that are possibly less exclusive but no less appealing. The bottom line is the $480 per 50ml bottle Scandal pour Homme (Parfum) is easy to like, but the composition is a bit of a let-down, not distinguishing itself from many others in the genre earning an "above average" 2.5 to 3 stars out of 5 rating and a neutral recommendation with a slight positive bias setting price aside. When price is taken into account, this offering is quite scandalous indeed!

ROJA scandal is a freshie I enjoy quite a lot. While its not exactly my favourite fresh fragrances, it gives you what you want. It starts off with this citrusy, aromatic, green blast of freshly cut grass and spearmint with a light drizzle of bergamot. Afterwards it fades down to a floral woody fragrance that sits just on the skin, yet very refreshing to catch a whiff throughout the day. Despite the very well done scent profile and ROJA's usual exceptional quality, this fragrance only really lasts about 3 hours in optimal conditions which I find very strange as you can tell the quality is there. Regardless if this lasted longer it would be a personal favourite.

Scandal pour Homme was a blind buy for me. The reason for this was as follows: I had been looking for a high-quality Fougère with good performance for quite some time. Unfortunately, I had already tested several Fougères that were often more suited for older gentlemen, had a somewhat scratchy quality, and had miserable longevity. In the end, I stuck with Acqua di Parma and the Colonias, but the somewhat weak performance and the occasional lack of depth never completely satisfied me. Sure, the Colonias are great because their price makes them very attractive, and such quality at this price is also rare, but there was always a little something missing. Scandal pour Homme really manages to fill this gap for me. It is a fresh, classic Fougère as it should be. The top note consists of all sorts of citrus fruits and, of course, lavender and tarragon. There’s nothing special here. However, this changes in the heart note. Here, something scratchy often comes to the forefront, or a much too dominant lavender and tarragon combination that reminds one of typical scents from grandparents. Scandal pour Homme cleverly avoids this problem and instead opts for soft florals that prevent the previously described issue. Unfortunately, I can’t quite pinpoint which flowers they are, I can only slightly detect the violet. In the heart note, Scandal pour Homme is again a typical Fougère that is very complex. I simply cannot recognize even half of the notes. I can identify moss, vetiver, woods, clove, patchouli, and labdanum, but nothing more. The longevity is good; it could have been a bit more, but 8-9 hours is absolutely fine, though not very good. The sillage is typically restrained for Roja; it’s not a Xerjoff or Tiziana Terenzi scent, which doesn’t bother me, but it should perhaps be considered before purchasing. I find Scandal pour Homme is perceptible at arm's length for 6-7 hours before the scent becomes intimate. Scandal pour Homme is more of an understatement, so it’s not suitable for going out to a club or anything like that. Scandal pour Homme is perfect for everyday wear and any weather, except perhaps over 35 degrees. The biggest downside, of course, is the price. It is simply inflated, and it is advisable to look for offers because the MSRP is far too high, in my opinion, but at least it’s not completely outrageous like some other Rojas. I can only partially understand the very negative reviews; sure, Scandal pour Homme doesn’t reinvent the wheel, but what this fragrance aims to be, it fulfills perfectly. Scandal pour Homme is not extremely exciting but simply classic and perfect. I often think the expectations for Roja fragrances are too high, but I can certainly understand that one might be disappointed or expected something more unique. I also don’t like some Rojas at all, for example, Diaghilev, but Scandal pour Homme is a scent that is even easier to like than, for example, Diaghilev, especially for younger people.

Even though not all Roja fragrances were must-haves for me, I recognized even in the mediocre to good examples that they left little to be desired in terms of complexity & finesse, often overwhelming the nose & hardly decipherable during a test. Scandal PH is also extremely versatile & hard to describe - but for me, it is not nice at all, completely against my taste. The first from the brand that does not work on my skin... no scandal, not every shot can be a hit ;) On my skin, Scandal PH is also citrusy, classic & green - but above all, extremely floral & old-fashioned. It is never well-received to say, "this smells like old gentlemen" - but at times, it unfortunately smells exactly like that. An unpleasant mix of flowers (dusty lily of the valley, jasmine, lavender) & animalistic-green nasty creatures (basil, moss, tarragon, sweat). It reminds me a bit of ancestors like Grey Flannel or Hermes Eau de Narcisse Bleu. A true narcissist, who, however, is far behind his third spring & downright stinks. Of course, this is not just old-fashioned & aged, one can also recognize a certain style, a once-believed-lost, gray-streaked, extremely well-mannered & well-to-do world that one thought was forgotten. That does impress me, but it doesn't change the fact that I don't like the scent. These are flowers for men that I don't need at all. I will lay a noble cloak of silence over the price, from the attic, full of moths, mildew, dust & dryness. Among the five men's fragrances in the line, this one is by far my least favorite. Bottle: a crown as a bottle Sillage: fortunately, I only have the small dab sample - I don't want to experience this after 4 sprays. Longevity: a stinker for 9 hours. Conclusion: the first Roja that I like almost not at all... it even gives me the shivers at times!

A sunny morning in Mayfair, City of Westminster, in the midst of the Autumn of Terror. He coolly skims through the newspaper, in Whitechapel, a "stone's throw" away, something scandalous has been discovered again. No Reflection, just a slight sense of satisfaction that is quickly replaced by the urge to move on. But, first things first: The gentleman needs a bespoke suit.

What is the snob effect? The snob effect refers to abnormal behavior in the market regarding supply and demand in microeconomics. The rule is: when the price drops, demand increases and supply decreases. When the price rises, the opposite occurs. With the snob effect, demand increases with the price. I can't explain Scandal and its popularity any other way.

A dear perfume friend sent me some Roja samples, which is of course an exciting endeavor with such a perfume house. Already, Fetish pour Homme overwhelmed me with its quality, and it’s hard for me to approach a test without any preconceived notions. Today, I sprayed Scandal pour Homme on and was clearly reminded of an earlier fragrance experience. Could it be Le Male?

THE BEST LIMITED BODYMIST EVER!!!! I fell in love with this scent: fruity, alcoholic, sexy. I don't regret buying this as a present for my 19th birthday. Design is rich and pink. My little brother says that it smells like Pina Colada and my friends gave me compliments If I had to choose which fragrance would be a brand constant, I would choose this one

The top note is a cinnamon spiciness wrapped in a dry dark chocolate powder. It looks like I'm wearing a marge chocolate powder dress. Cinnamon keeps the spiciness at a wearable level without being too strong. The chocolate is not too sweet and has no moisture. The progress of the scent brings the spiciness and the spiciness of the chocolate as it is. The scent is a bit like vanilla hot chocolate. It's a unique and easy-to-digest perfume that creates an alluring vibe. It goes well with thick makeup, and it's a great perfume to spray daily.

Today I have a craving for chocolate. And I don’t mean the kind that immediately turns into love handles.... No, I mean the chocolate that gently hugs my skin and deliciously lulls me to sleep. So I spray on the delicious diet chocolate and, who would have thought, you can smell a deep, subtly sweet chocolate. A dream, a guilt-free indulgence. In the background, I catch a whiff of cinnamon. The whole fragrance experience is lightly underscored by a lemony note and subtly dusted with floral hints. Thus, the scent is not to be confused with melted chocolate poured over the body. For me, it’s a beautiful winter gourmand that can be worn not just as a dessert. Update: after wearing it several times, it gives me a headache and becomes too heavy for me. What a shame.

chocolate..... chocolate that melts on warm skin,... losing your mind.... a delicate jasmine note gently intertwined with bergamot makes the chocolatey scent tender, skin-like. the scent brain signals: this is what tenderness smells like! not heavy at all, delicious, transparent, blissful... a small, satisfied chuckle rises from the belly and with a blissful sigh, you float directly into ..... yes, where actually? ....... oh never mind, just keep floating!!!!

It seems to me that patchouli has become increasingly popular in fragrances these days, even though there are still many people that dislike its scent. Elle is very much dominated by the patchouli. There are many similarities between this fragrance and Dior's Midnight Poison, which reviewers before me have already noted. This is patchouli in a dark, earthy and somewhat spicy sense. Not particularly feminine yet not unpleasant either. Delicate just isn't the right word here, Elle is actually quite strong and in some ways sharp. In the top notes, the lemon, litchi and peony are rich and bold rather than being sweet and flirtatious as they are in most scents. The patchouli and vetiver tend to discourage the entire composition from becoming too sweet, too fruity or too flowery. The red berries seem to be the only competition with the patchouli in the heart, which tends to create an almost boozy-type smell. Elle definitely has character in an alluring and powerful sense. This fragrance is not for a meek and mild woman. Elle is a demanding, attention-seeking, modernistic femme fatale. Elle is in some ways too loud and dark for my tastes, even though I do enjoy patchouli in heavy doses. This fragrance does not suit my own personality, and even though it did agree with my chemistry, I couldn't feel comfortable wearing it.

In my search for an introductory patchouli fragrance, I've come across this beauty thanks to the great suggestions from the forums. At first application there's a lot of pink pepper, patchouli, and a little bit of red berries. In about 15 mins, comes the heart phase. Cedar lovers - Definitely go for this one! I smell a LOT of cedar and I mean a LOT of cedar! Whew! It's like the smell of a cedar closet. It's not bad but I think this is where a lot of people say they smell toothpaste or something medicinal. It can take that direction as well. So I can see what they're talking about. The dry down is my absolute favorite part... Sweet powdery patchouli with berries. YUMMY - but - I have to wait at least an hour to get there. I've tried this scent on a tester strip a while ago and remember not favoring it much. THIS is why I didn't. Because on a tester strip, I got stuck in the pepper, cedar, patchouli phase. Not bad but not my thing. It's not as feminine as I'd like my perfumes to be for at least half of its stay on my skin. Unfortunately, I cannot wait that long for an olfactory pleasure. It's a pass for me.

Elle reflects the chicness of modern Womanhood confident yet refined this scent is the new Era of the powerhouse scents of the 80's a scent just screams HERE I AM JUST LOOK AT ME! commands your attention with just one spray. Open zesty with Almalfi Lemon with a crisp and bitter texture in a minute it dries a bit softer with Petals of peonies with it's semi sweet airy scent floating in the notes, Sweet and succulent Litchi plump ripe with the purest transformation to dark pink to bright Red dries sweetly finishes the top Layer with intoxicating nuances. Delicate and spicy pink pepper opens the second layer turns the scent with a bit of dryness that adds to the intensity Jasmine is very easy to detect in This scent and give off an greenish herbal smell. The drydown or the bottom layer fades and the only note i can pick up is the diluted silage of Patchouli, and deep almost elusive patches of musk that finishes this Scent. What i also think why this scent is sexy the reason for this is the shape and the color of the flacon Clean slender lines reminiscent of the perfectly built and well groomed businesswoman domineering and Sexual who put men in their place and also the color the sexiest of all flacon colors conjours bright neon signs of a nocturnal city, adds to the futuristic minimalistic style of Today.

The beginning of Elle is something else. There is a combination of spicy and fresh/fruity that is totally unique. I have not smelled anything like it. I really enjoy the first 15-30 minutes. Then it turns into a delicate but very anonymous scent. The uniqueness disappears and I feel an urge to spray again. Therefore I do not wear it very often. The bottle is like a monument. A beautiful one of its kind. The colour is refreshing and the golden details mix so well with it. So even if I is not one of my favourite YSLs I tend to like it anyway. 200/365

Elle is misnamed. It's a dry woody floral that hardly falls on the feminine side, and that's only due to a watery-pink note of lychee and some red fruits. Everything else; the scratchy pink pepper, the lemon, the gritty indoles of sambac, papery flowers, what Luca Turin calls the Feu d'Issey bread-milk note, the patchouli and dark woods, all of them are not Feminine. The only other feminine note is a sweet powdery-woody in the base. This isn't a criticism of the profile, just the name the marketers gave to it. It actually works quite well, just not under the name She. 'He' might have been less incongruous, but either way, with it's inherent weirdness, this was always going to be an outlier, a non-conformist luking in it's square-cut androgenous bottle. Elle, this gritty 'feminine' with a hipster beard, should have a metrosexual twin called Lui; with lavender and not lychee, and keeping the papery florals, but swopping out the dark woods for a plush oriental base. This suitably mixed up affair would be packaged in a bulbous curvy bottle in pink and grey. These two could have been the first Mix & Match pair, to be layered as you feel. Like Alan Turing, Elle is a Code Breaker; unconventional, an outsider with a different point of view. But is it a good perfume? I'm not sure. As a feminine, it's adventurous, but the form - as well as the theme - is rather crude, and this would normally point to a masculine. When seen from this perspective though, Elle seems to function rather better, and guys, it could be worth checking out. Just don't let the name put you off, because after all, gender in perfume is just as arbitrary as it is conventional.

After Tom Ford and before L'Oreal came Elle. Like its magenta bottle, its contents match the color. This patcholi is chemically altered beyond its usual limit. Elle is very likeable. This should have been the YSL best seller for the 21st century. Vetiver is suggested. Oakmoss? Possibly. Otherwise, it's a modern fruity chypre.

For about 8 or 10 years, this was my signature scent. I was crushed when production discontinued. Sadly the formula doesn't hold up very long, so old stock from the secondary market is out of the question. I tried and failed to find a bottle still in good condition.

~ Inspiration ~ When I recently got to know YSL's "Manifesto" (and was impressed by it), I wanted to test other perfumes from this brand as well. I got a sample of "Elle." ~ Bottle ~ This vibrant pink with gold is amazing! Why have I never seen this bottle before? The shape also reminds me of a high-quality lipstick.

and quite a bit, actually getting better all the time. The first time I stumbled upon Elle in the forum, I was looking for a replacement for Midnight Poison. However, the thought of it was quickly overshadowed by another fragrance (Vengeance Extreme). A few months later, while shopping at the local Müller, I noticed this striking pink bottle with the golden plaque.

For me, it is the scent of a successful, independent woman strolling through the streets of Paris with a coffee in one hand, a croissant in the other, and a Chanel bag on her shoulder. I discovered it 13 years ago. It is my perfume-self. How many experiences have I had with this scent. So many memories! As they say, the smell of an association, so it is for me.

First sniff left me speechless, I ordered a couple of discovery atomizers from Roja Parfums and this one I just picked at random, turned out for me personally one of my top fragrances in my collection to date, so much so I purchased the 100ml Parfum bottle. Beautifully blended, a masterpiece from mr Roja. Opens up warm and fruity and just gets creamy warmer and warmer. All year round fragrance but on the hottest days in summer just a light spray or two. 3 to 4 sprays is enough for a scent bubble about 8 to 10 hours on skin, on clothes about 2 weeks. As this is a very expensive bottle to buy blindly, would suggest the discovery atomizer first to really dive into this fragrance. Is available in 50ml and 100ml the Parfum concentration, 100ml being the better deal price per ml. Also exists in eau de parfum concentration and as of now also in the essence collection. * I tested and own the Parfum concentration

Roja 51 is an absolute feel-good fragrance for me. I can wear it for any occasion and in any season, and I always feel perfectly comfortable. I associate this scent with a beautiful and well-groomed woman. Very powdery and creamy but also floral and a bit fruity. The major downside of this fragrance for me is its longevity and sillage, and thus the price-performance ratio. I expected more in that regard. What a pity..

I have already rated the significantly cheaper 51 Essense, although the price for that one is quite high as well. The Essense had a nearly catastrophic longevity and almost no sillage for me.. The scent is actually beautiful and very feminine, just the typical Roja floral bouquet, which is why I spent 28 euros on a 3 ML tester for the Eau de Parfum, hoping that for the astronomical price there would be a significantly better longevity and a bit of sillage.. What a joke. I am shocked.. A super skin-close scent that actually has even less performance than the Essense.. I have to hold my nose very close to my skin right after spraying to even smell this fragrance.. Absolutely zero sillage.. Longevity with very good imagination 1 hour.. Not acceptable for the very high price. I asked my husband if he could smell the fragrance, he was sitting next to me on the sofa and he said he couldn’t smell it at all, only very faintly when he smells directly on my skin.. Honestly, I feel so cheated. I could have flushed the money down the toilet.. what are you paying for with this fragrance? The bottle?? Addendum. My letter from Essenza Nobile actually states that it is the Extrait de Parfum. It should be even more concentrated than the EDP.. I am shocked..

I have sniffed nine fragrances from Roja, of which I owned two bottles. null of them really blew me away. The longevity was not exorbitant either. By chance, I discover “51”. I spritz it on the back of my hand with enthusiasm and forget about it. I meet my friend for “Goldwürstchen”. Those are Vienna sausages at KADEWE. At that price, they deserve that name )). I am sent into a coma. Absolutely heavenly. I am in a foggy cloud when I catch a whiff of my wrist. Phew, I smell a very strong ylang-ylang-vanilla note with a hint of red berries, white flowers, and spices. The ylang-ylang note is very pronounced on my skin. A lovely creamy scent. 51 is very long-lasting. I find the fragrance very powerful. I still catch a strong whiff of it the next morning on my laundry, very encompassing.

Previous Y flankers have been alter egos of the original EDT, but Y EDP Intense seems to be an amplified revision of that release. Only greener, louder and matured. It's intense if compared to the original fragrance. I'm not able to grasp any sage like the Eau de Parfum (2nd release). The prominent notes appear to be bergamot, juniper and cedar. If you wait patiently, patchouli fades in gradually. In this moment, the fragrance feels complete. Ultimately Y EDP Intense is clean, safe and familiar.

… but that doesn’t mean it’s terrible. You can definitely tell it’s in the Y family. It’s not even close to being “intense”, but honestly that’s the biggest flaw I see in this one. Yes, you heard me right. The biggest flaw in this one is that they call it “intense”, when it’s not as strong as its older brother, the EDP. I like it though. Is it worth $160? Not if you have any of its relatives. If you don’t have ANY of the predecessors, or you're an absolute fraghead who loves YSL, then grab it. This one is like they made the EDP without the sweetness. Performance is about the same as the new EDT. 2-3ft bubble with a decent sillage trail that lingers well. Longevity is 6 hours on 5 sprays. So/so release, but it still smells good. It’s just a variant of the line.

So I got Y Le Parfum three months ago and now got to my collection EDP Intense. Let me say this, people sub 30 that love Y EDP are going to hate Y EDP Intense. Y EDP Intense it's thought for a different market. A more aged market. I almost stopped using EDP over the years (got it in 2019). With Le Parfum, I started using the line again as the sweetness was toned down and it isn't a "In your face" perfume, and now I'm loving even more this EDP Intense. I like how EDP smells but, for me, it's just the perfume the kids going to a party use. most likely EDP will go to the gifting list to my younger brother. If you are over 30 and haven't smelled Y EDP Intense, I would recommend you to not take the critics on the perfume. Go try it. most likely you'll be surprised!

There are some fragrances that have an offputting note to some people. I know I'm in the minority here, but that's just my experience. This fragrance has quite a strong resinous note that doesn't bode well with me. It's like olibanum or elemi but much worse (I'm not opposed to the aforementioned). I'm getting a headache from this fragrance because of it. Without that note it would be fine, but nothing ground breaking. It's like a slightly sweet woody aromatic. I actually quite like the woody and aromatic notes, but this one resin note I just cannot get past. Too bad.

Y EDP Intense is a much more mellow and mature take on the Y Formula. Personally not a huge fan of this one. The opening almost reeks of Iris and powdery notes (could be the Lavender). Once you get past the opening, about 30 minutes into the fragrance, it really starts to improve, with the juniper berries and woodiness really starting to flaunt themself, however even then, I would expect it to project 3-4x more with a moniker like Intense being added to the already strong EDP. This probably would've been better off being the "Elixer" flanker, as it's much more mature and toned down than the typical Y cologne in the line up. I'm surprised that so many call this the definitive fragrance in the Y lineup as this doesn't even compare to my bottle of Le Parfum unfortunately. It's not bad, but leaves a lot to be desired.

A very different Y-perfume. This does not remind me much of Y EDP. This is like a niche version. Much darker and a lot of wood. This is a woody fresh scent. Very mature and masculin. Not for "young" guys. Definitely a + 30 years old perfume. I wear it in my 20'ies and I try to act older. Very unique compared to the others. Perfect suit fragrance.
First of all, I want to say that I am an absolute newcomer to the perfume community and I am also just a teenager myself.

My review is based on a miniature sample that came with an order. Overall, I find the scent to be much better than most reviews from the Parfumo community would suggest. The top note is vibrant and smells delicious and citrusy. The aroma of bergamot is simply beautiful here. In the background, I can still detect juniper berries and a hint of ginger.

I had been very interested in the popular Y Eau de Parfum for a while, but I initially held back due to budget reasons. When I heard about the new Y EdP Intense, my attention shifted to this one. I ordered a sample and can now provide more details.

The fragrance is advertised by Yves Saint Laurent as follows: "ESPECIALLY COOL, EXTRA-SENSUAL FRAGRANCE FOR EVEN MORE INTENSITY. THE NEW SCENT OF SELF-FULFILLMENT." And at the latest, when a fragrance is marketed by the manufacturer as particularly cool, you should be a little suspicious, after all, I am no longer a primary school child who can be impressed by such words.

People are reacting to this as if it's a huge departure from Elysium pour Homme Eau de Parfum or Elysium pour Homme Parfum , as if those were revolutionary fragrances and Noir is strictly derivative. All of the Elysiums are basic blue fragrances chock full of ambroxan (just because it's called "ambergris" in the notes doesn't make it any more natural). Elysium Parfum is an improvement upon the blue genre but I wouldn't say it's worth the money. Elysium PC and Elysium Eau Intense are both on par with the higher end blue designer frags, i.e. 7 Cobalt or Bleu de Chanel Eau de Parfum . With all this I'm trying to say that if you rated Elysium PC a 9 and you're rating this a 2, you might have on your rose-tinted glasses. I get that people are tired of this genre, and believe me, I am too, but it still annoys me that this is rated lower than Isola Verde . Elysium Noir may be basic, but it's at least well-composed. It is not the worst Roja release of this year. I guess my rating is only going to further lower it. Anyways, let me describe the actual fragrance. It's a slightly ambery shower gel in the vein of Y Eau de Parfum but there is some depth here unlike some other releases in this genre this year (*cough* Valero *cough*). I get a kind of Megamare -ish dry spiciness somewhere in there, almost hinting at cumin, but there is no blackberry note which would have been a welcome addition. So, a very boring idea but not executed horribly. Longevity is acceptable while sillage is quiet. I'd say it's a good office/gym scent but there are probably better options for 1/3 the price.

Occasionally, bad fragrances are just that: bad. More often than not, there's a bit more to the story. You see, perfumery is a credentials business, yet in most cases, it doesn't even matter if you actually have them, you just need the public to be under the impression that you do. This is the story that followed Roja Dove for years (if not decades): the idea that he was just a marketing pleb from Guerlain, yet ultimately, it doesn't even matter if Dove himself is the perfumer or not since Roja Parfums as a brand boasts an elite catalogue of market-leading products within various different genres. The product spoke (and still does) for itself with Dove receiving positive reputational windfalls. With Dove looking to sail off into the sunset, the brand was given a difficult task: to find someone who can tell the story just as well as Dove, regardless of whether they had a helping hand or not. And so they turned to French flavors house Argeville where we find waterboy Antoine Cotton. After releasing a couple flops earlier in 2025, Elysium Noir will likely end up being the final creation for Cotton with the brand looking to pivot to a different creative nose in 2026. And on behalf of the fans of British luxury niche house Roja Parfums, I say good riddance. You see, Cotton didn't have any verifiable credentials as a perfumer to begin with. When Omani brand Amouage opted to bring in Alexis Grugeon back in 2023, he already had more than a dozen designer products under his name, some more generic than others. Maybe that lack of experience is in-part to blame for Cotton's complete ineptitude. The original Elysium pour Homme Parfum is certainly among the top 5 well-regarded citrus-aromatic fragrance in the niche market today (I'd argue it's number 1, but that's a different story for a different day). This 50ml PPH version already had 2 flankers prior to the release of Elysium Noir and both of those fragrances stayed sufficiently close to original, yet for some reason, Cotton thought that was not the right lane. Execution wise, Elysium Noir is the Roja that smells the least like Roja and that's largely because the scent basically smells like a designer fragrance. Elysium Noir opens in the fresh, macho masculine shower gel genre. There's essentially *zero* of Elysium's citrusy DNA shown with Noir's scent profile being dominated by ambroxan and lavender/geranium in the top. On-skin there is a prominent smell of musk and there are some touches of soapy white florals. As the scent develops, that same musk is opposed by what I assume are juniper berry and cypress in the heart/base. Performance is objectively light, I'm rating sillage 3/10 with implied longevity around 5 hours, likely biased downwards. Some might think the heart of this review is the build-up to the product coverage, but alas, it is not. You see, on the German version of Parfumo there is the aptly titled review (and I'm quoting verbatim): "5.1 is bullshit". The reviewer is referring to the average rating this fragrance held at the time of review which has since trended upwards to 5.4/10 (n=148) as of the 3rd of November 2025. As a niche hobbyist, I find that take amusing, because 5.4 is effectively a compliment for the generic product launched by the brand with Cotton at the helm. With review after review comparing Elysium Noir to generic designer products like Y Eau de Parfum , Versace pour Homme Dylan Blue Eau de Toilette and Invictus Eau de Toilette , it shouldn't be a surprise why fans of Roja don't want to be quoted €350/100ml to smell like the basic bro who thinks the aforementioned designers are worthy of their inflated ratings & coverage. There's a reason why they say the best ability is availability: a reduction in choice leads people to feel more fulfilled with their decisions. And given the type of choice I both have myself and have explored, it goes without saying that Elysium Noir is a slap in the face of Roja's fans. Antoine Cotton, you are FIRED effective immediately.

Synthetic and designer have never been a pair of words in my mind while smelling a Roja scent but they’re the only two that come to mind when I smell Elysium Noir. Smells like Y edp, green and dark body wash. Simple, linear, synthetically fresh; it’s unexciting as a whole. This bottle doesn’t deserve to wear the Elysium name.

I am not a big fragrance connoisseur nor am I good at smelling and describing scents and their individual ingredients. But I find the rating does not correspond to the fragrance. I understand why people are pissed off, “Oh, a new Roja” “Oh, another Elysium” expectations might be high and yes, the scent is not new and it wasn't really needed, and yes, the price is also ridiculous for the fragrance, but all of that does not make it a bad scent. I would actually describe it as a spicier version of Y by YSL and Invictus. For me, this one, in contrast to most reviews, is less synthetic and more wearable than Y and Invictus. That is the point that makes the fragrance good for me, I like both of the aforementioned scents, but personally find them so penetrating and unbearable due to the synthetics that this one unites the actually not so bad scent of the two into a wearable fragrance. Furthermore, the Roja has a smoky/leathery touch. If I were to receive it as a gift, I would be happy and would wear the fragrance. It is a scent that can be worn anytime and anywhere. Yes, it is not an innovation and it is also not what I expected, but a 5.1 is just bullshit in my opinion. Addendum: it has absolutely nothing to do with the “Elysium” line. No citrus, no freshness that one knows from the predecessors.

We usually expect that new releases will surpass what already exists. I find this expectation to be general and for everyone. A new fragrance must be louder, last longer, attract attention, and preferably be given as a gift. Only then is it considered good and accepted. Contrary to the impressions of many previous speakers, I find this release to be very successful. My nose and I are in agreement. The Noir smells great. The experience of the first encounter can be well compared to "Castley | Parfums de Marly." A certain synthetic quality somehow belongs to it these days. Whether that is bad or good is for each nose to decide. Personally, I like it. Also because I really enjoy molecule fragrances, and they wouldn't exist without synthetics. I would probably have chosen a different name. "Noir" doesn't really fit for me. To me, it is a fragrance that works very well during the day. In general, I would have dedicated a completely unique name to the scent. Starting off sparkling fresh and slightly fruity, it quickly transforms into a fresh, soft, spicy, slightly "warm" clean man scent. Bright and clear, in no way "Noir." The cypress gives it a minimal green touch, the leather note is very light and reminiscent of soft suede. Patchouli stays in the background. I smell a very fine rose-ambroxan accord. Every nose perceives differently, and that's a good thing. I really like the Noir, especially because it is understated and feels rather quiet. Nevertheless, I find the sillage to be quite strong, at least in waves. For a fresh fragrance, I consider the longevity to be very acceptable. Elysium is and remains a reference in the world of niche fragrances, quality for which one is happy to spend a few extra euros. It is exactly this quality that I also smell in the Noir, albeit differently, but certainly not worse.

TL;DR: Elysium Noir is a deeply disappointing, synthetic fragrance that reminds one of cheap aftershaves and quickly loses its sillage. First, the few positive points: Elysium Noir is indeed a "dark" and masculine scent that would suit the broad, uninformed masses.

I already like the original spherical bottles from Kilian - and the subtitles that immediately lead into a special mood. So when I think of Fun Things always happen after sunset, I remember my time as a night owl, when I used to roam the streets with my girls until the early hours. There was always something promising in the air - we wanted to experience something - to see and be seen. Sometimes casually testing our own "market value." We enjoyed being flirted with - because those are vitamins. Some light flirty conversations arose - and floated on - like a shimmering soap bubble. But we were also content with ourselves and drove Birte's old VW bus to the Ruhr meadows, opened the wide sliding door, looked at the Ruhr where the moon was reflecting - and let the wine bottle circulate. A fresh scent of grass and currants surrounded us, and the rose bushes by the shore pampered us with pure nature. Fruity aromas flowed from the gardens, and we flirted with nature - which was no less beautiful than wandering around in clubs. From the car radio came: Because the night belongs to Lovers - and we felt addressed even without male company. So we sat until sunrise - talking and being silent - and missed nothing.

It’s strongly autumnal and the rain from the last two nights clearly showed with its plop-plop-plop against the windowpanes that we should prepare for the upcoming - hopefully fragrant - seasonal cave life. And yet, this Kilian scent that I tested in the last few days remains vividly in my memory. It shouts loudly: Hello, summer!!! A summery warm day gently transitions into evening: Bare feet rejoice in the light moisture of the freshly mowed, recently watered lawn. Its scent promises: pure evening coolness! A gentle breeze rises and plays with the many layers of the light summer party dress, while the gaze sweeps over the expanse of the garden areas: the promising beginning of a summer night! On the terrace in the background, the suave pianist tinkers away, while the members of the combo start singing a Cole Porter song: pure daydreaming! The ice cubes in the shaker clink softly; the bartender smiles mischievously! The tart blackcurrant aroma sparkles in the glass and tingles like a refreshing Kir Royal in the nose: pure promise! A hint of fully bloomed roses and the vibrant scent of a summer night wafts from the gardens: Isn't it romantic? A quiet eroticism lingers in the twilight; the scent of this evening subtly tempts one towards recklessness! All of this is told to me by a few spritzes of "Fun things happen after Sunset"; not long-lasting, not particularly spirited or substantial: just the fragrant impression of a nocturnal summer flirt! Fruity, fragrant, sparkling - a little Flirtation: born from a summer night! (And: since "funny things happen," it could even be that a somewhat plump, brightly pink unicorn with a dark purple mane and tail, exceptionally long slender legs in beautiful nude-colored high heels comes hopping out of the bushes and dances through the summer scene. My Facebook friends surely know which unicorn video I mean!) So it is: Funny things happen - thanks to Kilian!

I love this perfume. I’ve tried all the versions in the line-up and this is hands-down my favourite version of Libre. It’s soft, smooth, clean, and the most staunchly unisex version to my nose (even though perfume is for everybody). The addition to aldehydes in the opening makes it more interesting—fatty, soapy, fresh and clean. Coupled with the lavender, the aldehydes play very nicely to the Libre DNA. It really sets it apart from the rest of the line right away. You very quickly get the signature Libre jasmine-orange blossom and it’s as beautiful as ever, but made even better by the addition of ambergris. The way the ambergris blends with the orange blossom and jasmine is seamless and produces a smooth, augmented white floral scent that’s just lightly sweet enough to be incredibly pleasant and addicting. It’s the part of wearing this perfume that I always look forward to most. I find this such an interesting change to the OG Libre that we all know. This is less brash and sits closer to the skin, but still has a presence.

Libre, Yves Saint Laurent's cash cow. I'm not against flankers per se. There may be gems in between. But in my eyes, Yves Saint Laurent is the king of the boring and uninteresting flankers. This fragrance is little different from the original edp. However, it is closer to the skin and lacks the sparkle of the edp. Lifespan; less than the edp. And then looking at the price of this perfume. It costs €230 here in the Netherlands. For this amount, or less, you have so many better (niche) scents. For me, Yves Saint Laurent has now definitively disqualified itself from the perfume market.

This has the most peculiar beginning. Let me say: I love lavender! Lavender has a calming effect on me, and from time to time I spray my pillow with a Lavender spray from The Body Shop, because it has a great effect on my sleep. Therefore I was thrilled when I saw the notes in Libre L'Absolu Platine: White Lavender, Provencal Lavender and French Lavender - all at once. My expectations were pretty high at first spray. But Alas! What hit my nose was a chemical, synthetic smell with absolutely no similarity with lavender. Unfortunaly, this smell disturbs the whole picture and I become annoyed when wearing. It disappears after two hours and becomes more sweet due to the Bourbon Vanilla, which ends up saving the scent from total failure, but I do not want to wait for it. This leaves my forever collection. Year 2, 34/365

Tried this on my skin. I liked the opening and the sillage in the beginning when biking home on a sunny, but fresh, windy day. I like the drydown less though. I find it a bit boring and linear. I don't get any lavender the way I know the real flower by the way. Don't get any of the listed notes either. Just something abstract. Not unpleasant, maybe even pleasant, but for a perfume, that is not enough for me. I also get something very synthetic, almost juvenile. Wouldn't call is masculine, nor feminine, nor unisex actually. Maybe no gender-profile at all? That I don't mind, but the scent just doesn't thrill me.

To me this smells abit like YSL Myslf Le Parfum but then as it develops you get something akin to the plum and heliotrope found in Narciso Rodriguez Musc Noir. I think it's because Narciso Rodriguez Musc Noir and this both share a heliotrope note I think. Perfectly unisex in my opinion. I will get this scent as a gent. Just that I adore my YSL. When it's finished though I am coming for this.

I'm a fan!! Definitely not the sister of the Libre line, more like a third cousin. What I particularly appreciate about this fragrance: it radiates really well, but not too much. It lasts a long time. Even though I love spicy, sweeter scents, which are popping up everywhere, this one is not that, it brings variety (signature potential).

I am glad I got this fragrance before I saw the comments and ratings here. The negative reviews would have otherwise deterred me from testing the scent. I find it absolutely lovely, not too intrusive, slightly fresh, and develops softly with a pleasantly fine, creamy sweetness. It’s among my TOPs In my opinion, unisex Average longevity

Don't listen to the fake news down there ^^. The scent has something endearing about it and is right on the threshold between aloof and ingratiating. Timeless, genderless... A comforting embrace every time I slip into my coat, scented with it. Soft, velvety, cozy, angel wings... Moderate and transparent sweetness along with grounding lavender calms me.

I was so curious after seeing the fragrance pyramid. I do love lavender ... the real kind, from my garden. And I have 4 different varieties including the white lavender. So I was very eager for our test today from a newspaper supplement for my sweetheart & me.

... I also stroll through the women's section in my trusted perfume shop and see this fragrance here. I spray it on a strip and find it interesting.
