So I try it on my skin and am immediately thrilled. But wait, not so fast. I was about to reach for the bottle. But let's wait and see how it develops, and what can I say, I am still excited.

Madison Pour Homme conveys elegance, class and masculinity. This fragrance was created exclusively for Madison Perfumery of Romania where they offer anything from luxury perfume, beauty products, fine jewelry to specialty coffee. As many have mentioned, Madison Pour Homme is similar to A Midsummer Dream, but with some minor differences. For some, these differences are a critical deciding factor. Like A Midsummer Dream, the notes that immediately call out to me are grapefruit, elemi, vetiver and Roja's signature oakmoss. Although the note pyramids are almost identical, I find myself more partial to Madison despite the subtle nuance. There is more complexity and depth in comparison. I also enjoy that the vanilla is more identifiable here. While this is a rather unique scent profile, there is a Terre d'Hermès vibe; only smoother and much more powdery. Terre d'Hermès leans heavier on the pepper and vetiver, which is not a terrible thing. It's simply a different vibe. Terre d'Hermès is one of those fragrances that I envy others for wearing well, because I do not. Madison has its own personality, but certainly checks all the same boxes for me.

Roja Madison is one of those fragrances that really took an eternity to finally land in my collection; before, I guarded my small decant of Madison like the apple of my eye. Some of you may have read my negative review of "A Midsummer Dream | Roja Parfums," which I didn’t really like, but this fragrance always had something interesting about it, which is why I still own a bottle despite the negative review. With Midsummer Dream, I have a love-hate relationship; sometimes it feels like insect repellent, and a day later, I love the scent again. That’s also the reason why I haven’t changed my review yet. I actually had no high expectations for Madison either, but here I was truly proven wrong. I always feared that Madison would end up like Midsummer Dream. Now, I want to get to the most important part of this review: the scent itself. I really focus on my personal reasons and differences as to why I like Madison so much. Madison feels fuller and more voluminous; my impression is that there is a stronger presence of the scent, not in terms of sillage. I see the reason for this in the stronger use of cocoa, oakmoss, patchouli, and guaiac wood, which darkens Madison significantly, and I think this completely prevents the association with insect repellent for me. Another difference is the spicier top note, which is due to the bay leaf note. For me, Madison is clearly the better creation than Midsummer Dream, but conversely, I have to agree with anyone who says the fragrances are very similar and that it’s somewhat pointless to own both. However, in the end, it was the subtle differences that led me to buy a bottle. I really like the floral and spicy aspect of Madison, and somehow this combination is somewhat addictive for me, which is why I can hardly help but cautiously sniff the sprayer of my bottle even on days when I’m not wearing Madison. Unfortunately, the price of Madison is really too high to recommend a purchase, especially considering the very similar and cheaper Midsummer Dream. I can only recommend the purchase if the points I mentioned about Midsummer Dream bother you and you are truly willing to pay much more. Madison is truly one of my absolute favorite fragrances, and I really enjoy this masterpiece every single day. The longevity is really a good bit better than that of Midsummer Dream. I could perceive Madison for about 2-3 hours longer than Midsummer Dream. However, more than 9 hours is also not achievable with Madison. The longevity definitely leaves nothing to be desired for me. The sillage is typically Roja, rather understated, but stronger than with Midsummer Dream; for 3-4 hours, Madison is perceivable at arm's length, after which the sillage slowly decreases to become skin-close after 7-8 hours.

Some time ago, I wrote a comment on Creed's "Spice and Wood" titled "Father and Son." I feel, then as now, that SaW is a cross-generational signature scent that has everything it takes to shine in any time and on any wearer. This feeling returned to me while wearing "Madison pour Homme." It is difficult to capture this special experience in the few characters of a statement, so I remained rather analytical and minimally euphoric, emotionally. ;) First, I would like to mention that, in my opinion, the optimal projection distance is "from 5cm" above the skin. Since the sillage is more than convincing, I can perceive the scent very well at any time without having to imitate a little truffle pig on my arm. Madison starts with a brief burst of pepper and citrus, which is already beautiful in itself. The pepper then cuddles back into the background, leaving the citrus notes to take center stage for the first good two hours. These are mature and very, very pleasant. Not fleetingly transparent, but THERE. This Roja has a certain calmness that always resonates with me, just like Spice and Wood. Really wonderful. Subsequently, spicy-floral accords emerge, but they continue to appear fresh and with a masculine twist due to the fading citrus notes. Here, a certain spicy creaminess comes into play, which skillfully fixes this fragrance world for the next hours and indulges both me and those around me. Reluctantly, more and more woody and "delicious" accords set in as the hours go by. The cocoa is carried by the iris, and together they create a fragrance marriage that radiates harmony. We are talking about well-measured iris here. Therefore, it is not a foe for me, but proof that in the right combination, there are endless possibilities and potential. The vanilla and wood that also resonate have always worked well in the niche, but here they also act as background singers and team players. I do not know "A Midsummer Dream." I haven't had the opportunity yet. I became aware of the fragrance through the wonderful comment of dear Parfuma "Pepper81." Whether it is really "only" 50 bottles or more? Whether the usual lament about price and proportionality is not redundant? All of that is actually completely irrelevant to me. :) Madison pour Homme is a truly successful Roja that wonderfully crowns the anniversary of the Madison Parfumerie in Bucharest and has gifted us all with a fabulous scent. I can only recommend contacting the lovely team there via email and getting to know this fragrance in one way or another. It has signature character and should be permanently included in the range. So that it can indeed send generations from Father to Son into the day with a smile. (PS: The scent definitely also has potential for women who do not like sweet fragrances.)

Actually, I’m quite annoyed and have been debating whether I should write a comment about this fragrance. But I just can’t help it, so here we go. Well, this liquid gold is limited to 50 bottles, which is what annoys me a bit. Why is that? I had feared that if I ever got a whiff of this, I might fall in love, and it’s not the first time with Roja. It’s expensive anyway, reportedly around €480 for 50 ml. But I could overlook that if I really, really liked a fragrance; I’m willing to spend for a good piece of luxury! Unfortunately, I will probably never own a bottle, as I don’t plan to travel to Bucharest anytime soon. My mini sample has unfortunately come to an end; I was able to test it a few times and today again for this comment, which hurts. But I did manage to snag a few ml, which I will have to ration very, very carefully! Well, enough about that, let’s get to the essence, the scent... It has already been mentioned several times that this one resembles A Midsummer Dream, and yes, that’s my impression too, and it’s truly a wonderful fragrance! However, in my opinion, this one takes it up a notch. It starts like picked citrus fruits sprinkled with slightly bitter/spicy spices. Served on a wooden platter, everything feels quite masculine but very sexy. This lasts for a while, which I find very pleasant, but then it gradually becomes a bit darker yet softer at the same time. The vanilla/cocoa combo might be to blame for that; wow, it’s fantastic! The fragrance never loses its masculine spiciness, strong, dark, and confident. But the longer it stays on the skin, the softer side comes to the fore, and that is really damn sexy and simply genius! And so it has happened again, I am in love with another Roja... To everyone who gets the chance to test it, congratulations! I can only wish you not to fall for it; most will probably have no chance ;) Also wearable for women if you like it spicy/masculine! Longevity and sillage are typically very good for Roja; I can easily get through the day, and the surroundings definitely notice it well.

I applied Love Don’t Be Shy Eau Fraîche on one of those mornings when everything feels too bright and too fast, and it was like a little counterpoint: a splash that first felt like fresh dew on the skin with neroli and petitgrain, then gently embraced by orange blossom. In the heart, something floral and light opened up: peony, jasmine, a hint of rose, along with the familiar marshmallow, but detoxified, as if the sweetness had been dissolved in sunlight. It didn’t last all day, but faded like a beautiful thought that lingers. For me, it is not an opulent perfume, but a small, intimate happiness, a scent that feels as if it has been chosen just for oneself.

Love Don't Be Shy Eau Fraîche starts with a decent amount of neroli, which to be honest is not my taste, but it does mellow out. Delicate rose petals float on fluffy marshmallows riding on clouds of musk. Yes, you have to like it; I find the consistency a bit oily due to the petit grain. Petit grain is an oily extract obtained from the branches and green leaves of the orange blossom. Personally, I would wear this creamy, subtly fresh candidate more in spring. In summer, it's too heavy for me. I perceive the rose very faintly. That would be too much of a good thing.

Parisienne is yet another quintessential rose fragrance on the market today. Unlike the original Paris by YSL, Parisienne is a much softer, more watery rose scent, excellent for wear in the warmer months. The red berries and blackberry in the top notes, really adds a lovely fruity touch to the already dominant rose note. It gives this fragrance a subtle tart-like finish. Parisienne is a modern take on a very popular scent; rose. In my opinion it is very chic and stylish. Kate Moss actually represents this fragrance well. I was a little surprised that this was in EDP concentration. The way it rested lightly upon my skin with such little sillage strength, made me swear it was an EDT. Like I previously mentioned, this is a very refreshing, watered-down rose scent with a slight greeness about it that makes for a very Summery and inoffensive fragrance. Casual yet classy, Parisienne will impress you with its simplicity rather than its uniqueness.

YSL PARISIENNE opens with a blast of sweet pinkness common to several of the other currently available mainstream designer pink fruity floral fragrances. The red fruits are far more dominant than the rose in this composition, making this a quite different perfume from the rose bomb PARIS. This is obviously geared toward young consumers for whom PARIS smells too much like their mother. The sweetness level of this eau de parfum is quite high, so I would not recommend this as a rose fragrance. The flowers seem pretty abstract as they say, but the overall composition smells friendly and sweet and nice, conveying the image of the high school homecoming queen whose signature scent this may be. Nothing offensive, nothing contentious, just a nice, sweet ordinary scent. I do not think that PARISIENNE smells overly synthetic, nor is it very complex. But it is basically interchangeable with any of the similar fragrances on the market today, including FERRE ROSE, among others. If you like this sort of thing, just look for the pink, as they have been color coded, it seems.

It opens with a handful of fresh red berries. Then comes the powdery rose blended with vinyl. The vinyl can be easily detected on me, and it's an interesting twist. I totally get the plastic makeup bag comparison. The red berries are still detectable, and add a hint of tartness to refresh the rose. However, I can barely smell the woody base. And the fragrance doesn't evolve much after then. The sillage is moderate and the longevity is around 8h on me. Parisienne is chic and casual, an effortless elegance. However, I doubt if the vinyl note smells good to everyone. I suggest testing prior to blind buy. Originally written in 2013

For those debating on whether or not to make the plunge for Parisienne, I think that it is important to consider that it has a tendency to vanish in cold weather. I first got this fragrance in the summer and thought that the fragrance had acceptable longevity: I would get whiffs of it 5-6 hours into my workday. In the winter, it pales in comparison to other sillage bombs in my closet and I find it's completely gone before I even have the chance to smell it. The bottle is beautiful and well made. The cap is heavy and the bottle ergonomically fits into your hand. The scent is also quite pretty... it's comparable to other juicy rose/berry fragrances out there (like VC&A's Feerie, for instance) at a similar price range. I cannot smell the plastic notes although I've been assured by many that the plastic-feel is there. I think it's a versatile fragrance and a would make for a good present but I found that I tired of it quicky: something that rarely happens for a fragrance I initially love. To the seasoned perfumista it will probably be boring, but it held quite a wow-factor for me when I was new to perfumes.

In the English original quote: 'Nothing tastes as good as being skinny feels' - this is perhaps the most famous (and controversial) statement by Kate Moss, the face of Yves Saint Laurent's Parisienne - one that got her into quite a bit of trouble back then. However, trouble has always been part of the success of her brand. Why the house of Yves Saint Laurent chose 'La Moss', a self-proclaimed non-Parisian (she hails from the South London district of Croydon), as the face of Parisienne seems surprisingly obvious - after all, there is no shortage of prominent, pretty Parisians or at least French women. And yet, this seemingly misguided choice turned out to be a success - after the Daily Mirror published a photo of Kate Moss using cocaine in 2005 and her career seemed on the verge of a sudden end, she experienced an unexpected renaissance in the late 2000s. The campaign for Parisienne and thus the renewal of a traditional house's commitment to the Kate Moss brand played no small part in that. More than any other model, Kate Moss embodies nonconformity and even now - beyond forty - a certain rebelliousness. And unlike Paris, Yves Saint Laurent's whimsical, ladylike first homage to the city on the Seine, Parisienne feels younger, appearing more unconventional. The note 'Vinyl' may seem unusual, but there is nothing that reminds one of vinyl amidst the typical girlish triad of berry, flower, and patchouli/wood. And yet it has a coolness that smells more like Jaurès than Passy, more like a street market than Faubourg Saint-Honoré - perhaps it is vinyl after all? With the top note, it dissipates, and a floral sweetness follows that is not tumultuous yet not trivial - almost classic, but not conservative. Conclusion: a surprising hybrid of classic French and youthful. Well done and even better marketed - a bit like the great and eternally cool Kate. By the way, it is not 'skinny'.

Recently-- the following scenario at a friend's place: Three fragrance noodles in front of a groaning bathroom shelf. The fragrance noodle that belongs to the bathroom shelf is ranting in rage about unforgivable mispurchases and unbelievably idiotic fragrance gifts.

Today I felt like it again. :) It's funny, sometimes I can't smell 'Parisienne', and on other days - especially when it's spring-like outside - it really draws me in. I started my journey with 'Parisienne' about 3 years ago, when I fell into the sniffing and spraying craze. ;) My boyfriend gifted it to me for Christmas.

Yves, I hope you can't smell this fragrance, wherever you are, because you would be disappointed by your house. My first thought, the roses lie just like the patron of this brand in the cemetery. Withered, harsh, a bit of formaldehyde and the last embalming. No, this is not a true Saint Laurent, there is nothing sacred, nothing glorious.

When I first caught a whiff of a Yves Saint Laurent fragrance, I had just turned eighteen - and was actually still too young for "Paris," which nonetheless became my almost constant companion while my peers were still wearing "My Melody," "Janine D." or even the other Yves (Rocher).

Some saleswomen just have it in their blood, a good intuition, skill, clairvoyance, or whatever you want to call it: Parisienne was the first recommendation from a counter lady when I was once again on the hunt in the flacon jungle.

I don't think Parfumo has the formulation of Enigma I am reviewing (2023 edition). I've been working my way through the Roja women's sample pack and I have to say this is so far my least favorite. It smells like overly floral, synthetic hairspray. Too fake and overwhelming. Probably the Orris. I can be picky with orris. Save your money and go buy some aqua net or something.

I had the pleasure to try a sample of Enigma and I have been positively impressed by this fragrance. It's fresh at the beginning, the note of bergamot makes its magic in the first minutes. It then gets softer and warmer in the dry down phase and on my skin I can clearly identify the rose and sandalwood notes. It's an elegant composition with this subtle contradiction between the freshness of the bergamot and the warmth of the sandalwood. I would also say that this is a fragrance that would mostly suit mature women.

When I first got Enigma, I was slightly disappointed. It somehow reminded me of a scent my aunt used to wear years ago. But the more I wore this perfume, the more I fell in love with it. It is slightly powdery on my skin (not overly powdery as other reviewers often describe), with a prominent note of peach. It seems simple at first, but the longer I wear it, the more nuances and layers I notice. At first, I did not detect a prominent musk note, but now it peeks through sometimes. It is a sweet perfume, but not overly sweet. It gives a candy-like feeling, a very yummy sweetness, but not gourmand. It has a signature Roja's powderiness, and now I notice the saltiness of ambegris, which is not overpowering, but adds depth and something special to this perfume. I think this is the most elegant fragrance I have in my collection. The longevity is good, but it is not an overly loud perfume (which is my preference). This is one of those rare perfumes for which my love grows with time rather than diminishing.

In addition to the pompous Enslaved, I also tested Enigma on my first, personal "Roja Dove Day," in the perfume version. Unfortunately not Pour Homme, but now I am approaching this high-end brand through the women's line... And the men's counterparts or their tests will probably not take too long to appear now that the first step has been taken. Is it THE peach scent at all? That was actually the crucial question from the beginning. And although there are certainly a few other effects and facets to discover in the fragrance, an astonishingly large amount is happening in the peach realm. Particularly shocking and somewhat dull for a scent that lives quite briefly on my skin anyway. Not to mention the inflated price. Overall, I expected much more, and I am somewhat back on solid ground. Enslaved was significantly more spectacular, more aligned with its price. You simply expect fireworks in this weight class. This is more of a quiet, unfortunately rather one-dimensional sparkle. Since the top note on my skin is not noteworthy to non-existent, the fragrance goes directly to its rosy-soapy, extremely high-quality peach. Definitely a contender for the throne of the best & most exquisite peach fragrances. Often, due to the cheap Asian peach iced tea from my youth, I do not associate this fruit with luxury and nobility - here my opinion changes dramatically, and the fruit reveals itself in its purest, finest, most noble light. With the many floral elements alongside the rose (like ylang-ylang or especially jasmine), the fragrance in its first half comes across as extremely feminine, but somehow also humorless and strict. There is little playfulness here, and I would have preferred the neroli or heliotrope to be stronger. The second half of the fragrance then becomes even quieter and earthier, but fortunately distances itself from the uprising of luxury flowers. Here, patchouli, vanilla, and green-earthy tones slowly come to the forefront - much to my pleasure. Bottle: do I really have to write 1+ for every Roja now? ;) Sillage: a delicate little plant that wants to scream loudly but cannot. Longevity: only 4-6 hours - for a perfume. For €450. Quite shocking. Conclusion: completely different from Enslaved, an example that Roja Dove can also be delicate and calm, and for a short time the perfect peach fragrance... but that is still far from enough to earn a good or very good rating against the many negatives on my list!

My first Roja fragrance. As so often, I come to enjoy this scent thanks to a dear perfumer. Roja may be generally well-known, but due to the exorbitant prices, these fragrances have hardly received any attention from me personally, even though I was curious to see if they smell as good as they cost (somewhat, at least). Now I even have a few Roja samples with me and can hardly wait to apply these precious drops to my skin. Oh no… the samples are in a small tube. Now just don’t spill anything when opening… :D The scent: So,… at first, I smell something completely different from the listed notes in the fragrance pyramid. Because I smell gentle, sweet honey! And it’s the very pleasant kind of honey, not the slightly sharp-spicy variant like in an Angel fragrance or something (which is not to say that Angels are bad, but some of them are quite an acquired taste). You can smell the bergamot afterwards as well, but it comes across more like a tea, which makes the scent even better. Quickly, a fruity-fresh peach joins in, which fits well with the beautiful scent. The heart note is generally floral-sweet, but I find it difficult to distinguish the notes from one another here, as they smell more like a unit. The base is a bit easier to decipher, which is also due to the fact that the base notes smell more familiar to me than the floral scents of the heart note. You can definitely smell the vanilla, which beautifully complements the fruity peach and appears nicely powdery together with the iris. The sweet notes seem a bit darker; by that, I mean that the sweet notes no longer come across as floral-sweet, but rather come from the amber and musk, with the musk being slightly more noticeable than the amber. However, there is still a hint of gentle honey present in the later base. The woody notes, however, cannot be discerned. Overall, a very beautiful, sweetly gentle scent with light floral notes. The sillage and longevity: The projection is above average; it could have been better, but it’s still enough to be perceived from not too far away. The longevity is also okay; you can enjoy the scent for six to seven hours. The bottle: Unfortunately, I only know the bottle from pictures, but I must say it looks quite high-quality. Well, it IS very high-quality, as each bottle is handcrafted and the golden decorative elements are made of real gold. It is rectangular with a thicker glass bottom. Aside from the golden shimmering label, the sides of the bottle also say Roja Parfums (here, however, printed directly on the bottle). The neck is gilded, and the name is embossed there as well. The cap is rectangular and also gilded. Additionally, it is adorned with Swarovski crystals, which makes everything appear even more elegant and high-quality (and expensive). A very beautiful bottle. First of all: Yes, I managed to open the sample tube without spilling the fragrance, although the cap did fall from my hand, and I probably wasted 0.1 mL, noooo!!! :DD Okay, one can actually argue about the Roja prices, as cheaper fragrances can also smell very good and have high quality. But the scent is just as I imagined it. Very pleasant (though that always depends on taste) with above-average sillage, it also conveys a feeling of high quality, as you can’t smell any trace of synthetic notes (which doesn’t have to be bad) and the scent simply doesn’t come across as cheap. But as I said, other, much cheaper fragrances can easily achieve that, and this Roja is not extraordinarily different (but it smells great, and that’s what matters!), so the price will likely remain controversial forever. But in terms of scent, it initially feels almost like an all-rounder, but over time it does become a bit heavier, so I find spring and autumn to be the best times to wear it. It is suitable for many occasions, even for going out, although it seems too precious for everyday use. If you see the scent somewhere in a store, I would recommend giving it a test. It smells really good and should especially please those who like honey.

Enigma - it reminds me of the cipher machine, which was thankfully cracked by the clever English, possibly preventing further suffering in the world. Thanks a lot! Or the poetic music project by Michael Cretu, which provided me with relaxing breaks. Or according to Wiki - Enigma - Greek for the riddle.

My first Roja. I have to admit I was a bit excited to test it. At first, the bergamot knocks shyly and timidly at the door, only to be shoved aside in the next second by the peach, which boldly pushes its way into the top note in addition to the heart note and loudly claims its place there.

A seaside facet of Loewe's Solo collection. Gorgeous never-ending neroli on a salty mineralic backdrop, like a fading memory of the humid summer air at the salt flats. Once the initial peppery citrus cloud dissipated in the first hour, it settled close to the skin and stayed there, unchanging, for ~7 hours more. I tried it on both myself and my partner. My partner's skin brought out mastic, amber and hints of frankincense after the first hour of wear; on me it was mostly just the salty airy neroli until the very end. Both versions smelled delicious in their own right though, so I'm not complaining. It's like an idealized version of your skin smell after a day out near the seashore :) Great for daily wear during warm half of the year, though (like any other perfume) I would use it with caution during the hottest most humid parts of the summer.

Oh, and here is a precious nectar! I am speechless for this delicious hidden gem... A rather beautiful though common opening could mislead you, but be patient and wait, and behold the curtain opens and here is Néroli letting the protagonists of this masterpiece dance be incense and white flowers. You will not forget them easily. And they will never leave you. And for hours they will come back to visit you with a lucid vivacity that I have rarely encountered. And never forgotten. Hopelessly in love! I think it's wrong to position it as a masculine fragrance, I'd say unisex and perhaps even more feminine, women try it, it's really sensual... Nuclear duration and discreet projection, I'd say a perfect combination. A masterpiece on my skin.

Belle d'Opium has traded the spices in the original Opium, for pepper instead. If pepper is not your thing, I'd skip this fragrance entirely. I was so angered by Opium's repackaging and reformulation, that I'd put off testing the flanker Belle d'Opium for a long time so that my anger wouldn't hinder my review of it. I have long since cooled off and have given Belle d'Opium a fair chance to prove itself. Shortly after smelling Belle d'Opium for the first time, I commented on how musky and peppery the scent was. Pink pepper seems to be the starring note in this composition, followed by musky sandalwood and slightly soapy lily. The composition is not all that predictable, as it has some elements of complexity, however it is much softer than what I expected. Opium is such a sillage monster than one could be forgiven in believing that a flanker would be just as loud. The scent is not strictly feminine, I actually think it would wear just as well on a man's skin. The pepper gives it that slightly masculine kick. In all honesty, Belle d'Opium isn't really my cup of tea. It smells a little sharp to me, perhaps even a little fruity at times, even though fruits aren't listed in the scent pyramid. I absolutely adore the bottle and packaging, easily admitting that it's one of the nicest designs I've seen in the last few years. It's a shame that the scent didn't grab my attention the same way that the bottle did. I wasn't so convinced by the almost non-existent white florals smothered by rich pink pepper accords. Belle d'Opium lasts for a relatively long time on the skin, however it's not too persistent. I personally find this fragrance to be lacking in some aspects, that I haven't quite managed to figure out. I'm left feeling a little underwhelmed.

A couple of years ago, good old OPIUM was reformulated (which I perceived as a tragedy in itself then, while meanwhile I have managed to come to terms with the reformulation), but the 2010's Opium-flanker, Belle d'Opium, struck me as a very uninventive attempt at producing yet another "floriental" in the style of Lauder's "Sensuous" from 2008 (not a favourite of mine either). "Belle" uses loads of white pepper and mandarine in the top-notes and then morphes into a very powerful flowery gardenia-ladden fragrance on a strong bed of synthetic sandalwood (the key-word is synthetic). I don't even like the bottle it comes in (which is not a piece of art either, btw). "Belle" was a major disappointment, even worse than "Parisienne". When will YSL stop producing trashy flankers which only damage the image of the house?

To some, this is quite synthetic. I personally like the start with the very dominant peach and mandarin. The drawback is that it disappears very soon and left is a rather anonymous scent that does not have anything unique to offer. That is not what I am used to by the power house, YSL. The bottle, however, is really beautiful. The detail with the red tube which can be seen through the bottle is so nice. The colour of the bottle is outstanding. Is it enough to get the perfume, that the bottle is gorgeous. Hmmm… you decide. 236/365

We met when things were not easy for both of us. We had both just separated from our husbands, and we were now single mothers. You with a teenage daughter, I with a toddler. You were always so positive, so powerful, and always full of humor. How many times did we talk for hours until the phone battery was dead? I received many good pieces of advice from you, and now and then you also set me straight. Never malicious, but always honest. And I often did the same for you; a good friendship can endure that. You accompanied me through tough times, when I was at my lowest, had to apply for Hartz IV, you always stood by me, and I was there for you when you had to vacate your apartment due to the landlord's personal needs. We spent New Year's Eve 2012/13 together. Four days at your place in Lower Bavaria, along with your now-adult daughter. Those are some of my fondest memories. At that time, I had organized a decant of your favorite perfume "Belle d' Opium" from the souk, you were so happy about it and applied it right away. That scent suited you so well. You were a beautiful woman with dark hair and almost black eyes, the slightly oriental fragrance note emphasized your aura. In 2016, you married again; of course, I was there with my then-fiancé and my son, I gave you a wedding candle and was allowed to read prayers in the church. At my wedding in 2017, you were my maid of honor. I never would have believed that I would see you for the last time then. But fate struck cruelly. In December 2018, your beloved husband died unexpectedly from a brain hemorrhage after just 2.5 years of marriage; he didn't even reach 60. Again, I was there for you, unfortunately only from a distance, as we are over 200 km apart. And yet, one can maintain a friendship even over such a distance. The next blow was already looming, but unfortunately, it was not initially recognized by the doctors. Since November 2018, you had been treated for a supposed stomach ulcer. This stomach ulcer turned out to be a tumor on the pancreas at the beginning of 2019. When you told me about it back then, it knocked the wind out of me. But you had so much hope, you were determined to get well again. You nearly halved your weight due to chemotherapy. You had to endure a lot of pain. The last I heard from you was in February. You sent me photos because you had been to the hairdresser and bought yourself a new dress. That photo radiated so much joy of life, humor, and fighting spirit. On Easter Sunday, I unknowingly sent you an Easter greeting. A few hours later came the response that changed my life forever. Your daughter replied to me, informing me that you had passed away peacefully and without pain on Good Friday. At just 50 years old. Damn cancer!!! Now I can't even say goodbye to you; due to the Corona situation, you will be buried in the closest family circle. The memory will now accompany me. Of a truly wonderful person. Thank you for everything.

The name might mislead you, and it doesn't really matter anyway, as the fragrance hasn't been available for a long time; in any case, it has little to do with Opium. I had bid on this several months ago for a good amount of money because I remembered that this was an evening caresser soft wonderful warm sweet scent for me back then.

Hello sniffers, welcome to a new review from me, this time about Yves Saint Laurent's Belle d‘Opium, which unfortunately is no longer produced. Some are sad about this, while others probably don't care much, as not all ladies like the Opium fragrances. For whatever reason… some of the fragrances smell really nice. Even delicious, even you more mature ladies! HOLD ON!

I love my Opium - but in summer it feels too heavy for me. So I set my sights on Belle d`Opium. I took a friend along for advice, but she scrunched her nose at the first spray. Not me, though. I immediately liked the combination of mandarin and white pepper. Spicy - fruity. Beautiful. Then there's the smoky woody development of incense and sandalwood. Tres francais!
sometimes a glance is enough, sometimes a gesture is enough, a word, a look, a moment.

I bought Belle d`Opium three and a half years ago in a perfumery during the post-Christmas sale after a short test. I had loved the "mother" Opium since my teenage days, and I didn't know this one yet. The bottle is violet, a color I really like, and the packaging is also very pretty with the peacock feather.

Roja also calls O "Ode to Joy." And O is an olfactory joy. Oriental-warm, rich, opulent, self-assured, and powerful. O starts floral-fresh, quickly becoming very warm and spicy with woody, resinous, and slightly animalistic facets. Even though O is imbued with a Roja-typical perfectly composed symphony of fragrance notes, O is different from most Rojas - not floating in the heavens, but rather firmly rooted on the noble pavement of Zurich's Bahnhofstrasse. O is a dense, heavy fragrance, almost formal at the beginning. O starts off almost harsh, but loosens up as the scent develops. Most closely related within the Roja family, O resembles Musk Aoud (my favorite Roja oud, as it is the least pleasing) and Fetish p.H., although with less lustful loins than the latter. Roja Dove primarily dedicates O to Munich and Zurich (and a bit to Berlin as well). It is no coincidence that Roja Dove dedicates O to Zurich. The Swiss spend the most money on perfumes per capita worldwide, by far. And not the Arabs. Roja Dove writes: "I have always loved the opera. On all my travels, I try to visit the local opera house. During my first visit to Switzerland, I was therefore delighted when a friend invited me to the Zurich Opera House - a truly majestic building that was built in 1834. Every element of the house is so lovingly preserved and maintained that it almost seems as if it just opened yesterday. The roof is adorned with angels - a sight I will never forget." The Zurich Opera House was built in the Viennese grandeur style and opened on Lake Zurich in 1891 (not 1834). And indeed, like winged guardians, some meter-high angels watch over the building and the adjacent Sechseläutenplatz. One of the magnificent angels holds an O-shaped laurel wreath in its hands. Furthermore, the name of the perfume, O, is a cheerful reference to the name of the Zurich perfumery that exclusively distributes the scent in Switzerland (besides O-berpollinger in Munich): O-sswald. The Osswald perfumery, this unique jewel on Zurich's Bahnhofstrasse, is not only considered one of the oldest niche perfumeries in the world. It is also regarded as the most interesting and best-stocked in Europe. Only Harrods might offer a bit more in terms of flacons, although Osswald, very Swiss, leads in terms of friendliness, flair, modesty, and expertise. Even though Roja speculates in the booklet included with the flacon whether the people of Munich and Zurich are as enamored with angels as he is, I can affirm this for the Catholic wheat beer drinkers, but angels fit Zurich about as well as the Bremen Town Musicians fit Hamburg. Zurich is the city of Zwingli, where angels are suspect. When one thinks of Zurich, one usually thinks of banks, watches, the wonderfully rustic cheese shop at Münsterhof - and perhaps even Zwingli. But not of angels. Despite this wealth in Zurich, it is a very relaxed and friendly place. Modest, down-to-earth, industrious, cosmopolitan. After testing around 3500 perfumes, I am both demanding and skeptical. Can a fragrance in which oud, leather, and rose notes play the leading role still excite me? To cut to the chase: Yes, Roja Dove succeeds. I am enchanted. Not only by the nightly sight of the opera house, which reflects in the Zurich lake at dusk, but also by Roja's powerful perfume. Roja Dove himself is not a perfumer, but a marketing person. He is somewhat the Djagilev of perfumery. Whether he himself has a creative nose behind it or if it is one of his employees ultimately does not matter, just like with the mediocre dancer Djagilev. The aesthetic, artistic product counts. And that is breathtakingly beautiful and moving here as well. O starts floral-fresh with a fresh rose geranium and a bouquet of bright blooming May roses. The rose geranium is light to medium red, fresh, slightly sweet. A bit of zesty bergamot underscores the floral morning freshness of the geranium. Quickly, the May rose joins in. The May rose smells full, sweet, intoxicating, warm, and has a faint note of nectar. The scent of the May rose reminds one of the first warm rays of sunshine. Almost simultaneously, medium-dark, dense oud can be smelled, hardly animalistic, as well as medium-dark, firm leather. The noble woody oud and the leather could almost belong to the consulting room of an old Zurich private bank with their almost formal strictness. Soon, angel-white flowers and blossoms join in. Full-bosomed, enchanting, kissed by a bit of nectar. A bright, very beautiful note of a slender birch provides a certain counterbalance to the heavy oud and the firm leather. Unlike most Roja fragrances, which can be clearly divided into four fragrance notes (a short top note, a not very long-lasting heart note, base note, and an almost eternally lasting deep base note), O shows relatively little development. Over time, a background fruity-fresh raspberry note takes away some of the formality, which for a brief moment immediately after spraying almost radiates Zwinglian strictness. Yet the powerful, self-assured character, rooted in the Zurich Bsetzistein pavement, remains. Gradually, O becomes somewhat warm-resinous and sandalwood-creamy. A pinch of pepper, however, emphasizes the oriental, spicy-warm character of O. A warm, slightly softer, yet with an animalistic hickey marked opulent-oriental base of woody oud, warm leather, warm resin, and weasel-skin-animalistic labdanum brings O to a close. O is another masterpiece by Roja Dove. A perfectly composed symphony of fragrance notes. From the first fragrance note to the last note of the deep base. Nothing frays, no fragrance note is diluted - as in so many Arabic fragrances (I think of Black Prestigium by Mancera, for example). O is by no means a classic, often-smelled rose-oud-leather fragrance. Despite this outstanding quality, the perfectly orchestrated harmony of the fragrance notes, and the opulence of the perfume that makes it almost grow into the third dimension, O is not a perfume just for special moments. Certainly, the price is not modest at first glance. 50ml of perfume - O is an Extrait - costs 555 francs (regular customers naturally receive a discount in the double-digit percentage range). However, 30ml of Mitsouko Extrait costs around 360 francs. Compared to the same concentration, Roja Dove is not more expensive than a mainstream Extrait from Guerlain. 1 to 2 sprays of the Roja fragrance are sufficient for a noticeable perfuming for a workday - including one or two overtime hours. O by Roja Dove is stunningly beautiful, composed in olfactory perfection. Self-assured, warming, harmonious - like the temperament of the Swiss. O, that is a day in the cosmopolitan, industrious Zurich. Zurich, the island of bliss - if one is to believe the German mainstream media.

....I smell a refreshing and delicately sweet, yet very synthetic raspberry in the opening... I generally don't like "fruit baskets," so I'm not particularly taken with the opening of this exclusive Roja... It smells very much like artificial raspberry soda powder to me... (Who really likes raspberry in a fragrance? - for me, it's an absolute no-go - Sorry to all the lovers, I don't mean to step on anyone's toes, fragrance is a matter of taste ;-) Violets, geranium, and May rose show up equally... A delicate citrus note also mixes in, making the opening appear fresh-fruity and softly floral.... A hint of leather and saffron blends in and pushes the raspberry a bit into the background.... Gentle wood sprinkles, resinous wafts, and leather nuances are in the foreground, and the raspberry has now retreated significantly, only occasionally whispering through... From there, I find the fragrance somewhat better... I like the resinous tones that surround the soft leather notes together with earthy patchouli... My initial disappointment over the raspberry-soda-like opening fades a bit, allowing me to perceive the fragrance as somewhat more pleasant now... Only the question arises whether I want a fragrance in my collection where I really don't like the opening at all.... Hmmmm....No, I actually don't want that... Just unfortunate that "O The Exclusive Parfum" was a blind buy.... ....But where are the horses? The stable? And the piglets? In some statements, it can be inferred that the -O- comes off very pig-like, stable-like, and animalistic... For me: No horses, no stable, no piglets... I would have actually liked that, but far and wide there is nothing for me... Either I've become somewhat desensitized as an oud fan, or there are no horses... Maybe the raspberry just comes out too strong for me and I only smell that... The perception of fragrance is also totally different, so I would say everyone is right :-)

Criticizing a Roja Dove is almost like sacrilege, but this fragrance simply invites it. Today, 23.07.2020, it is rated 8.4 / 10 points and will surely find its followers. So, a warning in advance: Whether the 8.4 is justified or not is a matter of taste. The value should be seen purely statistically: few people can afford an RD or even step into a niche perfumery. Among niche-goers, not everyone has access to Roja Dove, and even then, the number of people who can actually smell the O is smaller. And from those ... well, you see where I'm going with this. Count von Count sends his regards! For the average person and the enthusiast's nose, it is already "special." Looking at the pyramid, it sounds really promising: beautiful noble woods, wonderfully introduced by floral and fruity notes. What reads great in theory is practically more like the job description at Farmer Wants a Wife. Imagine a large barn, enter the honorable vault, and enjoy pure nature. Roja has good hands, so you can't quite tell if it's more cow or horse or perhaps more piglet. That's how it smells ... well, it smells like that for about the first 2-3 hours, which is already longer than an episode. Therefore, you really can't complain about the performance. At some point in the evening, everything calms down, and the wood-spice mixture increasingly transforms into a wood-spice blend. But, but ... there are berries and orange, and look ...!?! Yes, they are there too. And they are in my bathroom when I wash this stuff off with soap and then try to freshen the room olfactorily with those synthetic air fresheners. So that's how far we've come: Synthetic versus Roja Dove's O! And yes, I know that oud is not everyone's cup of tea. However, there are also oud fragrances that, in my opinion, are much more wearable and, above all, offer a minimum level of decency and non-violence, especially towards Europeans. I would not count O in this category. Why a fragrance gets 8.4 / 10 while others - admittedly not so artfully designed fragrances - are heavily penalized is not entirely clear to me. However, it itches my moral sense of justice so much that I feel statistically compelled to give the fragrance a very low number. And why O at all? S for Stall or B for Barn would be more appropriate. But well, Oh dear could also fit. Maybe a flanker in 2021 named P. Yuck ... Addendum: I’ll blame the fragrance for not realizing it right away. But of course: O for Oberpollinger - it is supposedly an exclusive fragrance for the perfume paradise in Munich. I wonder which marketing expert just chose such a fragrance as a representative for the luxury department store.

I tested O - The Exclusive Parfum yesterday and today and was really extremely torn about how to rate this fragrance. O - The Exclusive Parfum is one of the most multifaceted perfumes I have tested so far. Unfortunately, I have to admit that the price is almost justified. O - The Exclusive Parfum starts with a very strong cow barn smelling Oud note. This Oud note dominates the first 5 minutes of O - The Exclusive Parfum, without allowing other notes to take the lead. In those 5 minutes, I would have said it was just another Oud fragrance with a crazy price that smells like a farm. After 5 minutes, the Oud suddenly retreats and gives way to the raspberry. This raspberry is accompanied by rose, jasmine, and bergamot. These notes allow O - The Exclusive Parfum to take on a fresh, fruity, and floral direction, while still maintaining a present Oud note, but without any barn associations. After 3-4 hours, the Oud completely disappears and makes way for an excursion into the Chypre genre combined with leather. I would now say that we have a fruity, fresh leather scent with Chypre undertones. The raspberry continues to play an omnipresent role and accompanies O - The Exclusive Parfum permanently. As it fades after about 10 hours, a bit of vanilla is added, preventing a strong musk note from coming through, which often makes fragrances unharmonious during the fade. O - The Exclusive Parfum fades out fruity, sweet, and fresh with a very gently dosed vanilla note. However, I still need to express something: I simply do not understand how Roja Dove came to the statement that O - The Exclusive Parfum has a connection to the classic German perfume culture, particularly highlighting the "classic Eau de Cologne." I think the comparison applies to 4711. Unfortunately, I see absolutely no similarity between O - The Exclusive Parfum and a Cologne, even less so to 4711. While O - The Exclusive Parfum is somewhat fresh, it is by no means comparable to an Eau de Cologne, as it also lacks the strong neroli note. I would have never seen any similarity to an Eau de Cologne, let alone to 4711. The longevity is really very good and leaves no wishes unfulfilled with 10-11 hours. The sillage is clearly above an arm's length for 6-7 hours and thus unusually loud for a Roja. O - The Exclusive Parfum only becomes skin-close after 9 hours. I really enjoy experiencing a stronger Roja. O - The Exclusive Parfum is extremely fascinating to me because this permanent shift between the different fragrance directions is truly unique and has been perfectly executed, especially the transition from cow barn to a fresh fruity scent with Chypre nuances. This change of facets with its perfect execution is already worth 10 points on its own.

After so many tests in the realm of Roja fragrances, one could even speak of a scent journey. An English scent journey through the oriental thoughts and inspirations of a man who was shown the French art of perfumery and intertwined it with a lot of the Middle East. In doing so, the advantages of a past fragrance art were also renewed. Rarely do you find houses that truly showcase the complete spectrum of different fragrance directions. Since I particularly enjoyed the oriental-tinged fragrances, I had to try #otheexclusiv as well. This will likely be my last Roja review in the short to medium term, as I currently had everything from the house in my nose that interested me. Oh, as was already readable in the statements, it seemed to be quite similar to my favorite "Fruity Aoud | Roja Parfums." I was certainly curious about how the fruits and the Aoud would present themselves here, but I hoped to sniff out a similar fragrance distinguished by a differentiated consideration and treatment of the fruits. O is very close to Fruity Aoud, not the same creation, nor the same fascination, but surprisingly close. The decisive difference is simply which fruits were used and the intensity of the Aoud. While Fruity presents a whole fruit bouquet, O only has raspberry. It shares the same tone of fermented, slightly sour notes, which makes both fragrances true experiences. The difference becomes more noticeable with Aoud. Fruity was characterized, in addition to the fermented fruit, by a cuddly wood component that was not very dark and partly created the impression of sandalwood. O, on the other hand, brings out the steam hammer and presents itself darker, slightly leathery-animalistic with more inclination towards cedarwood. This could be perceived negatively by some, as the combination of this sour raspberry and the quality of the Aoud allows the animalistic touch of the leather component to bloom and appear stronger. Here, a hint of #leatheroud resonates in a significantly muted form. In this case, it is much more pleasant for me that the fruit makes the whole thing sweeter and more bearable. The notes are also present from the very beginning and show themselves on the skin for quite a while. I find this very pleasant and not as bad as some others report here. Only after a while do both the animalic and the sour note recede, leaving only a lightly sweetened raspberry and a dark wood component behind. In this regard, I am somewhat disappointed, as the wood lands very generically in the nose and no longer feels so "special." I missed something that would give the whole thing a finishing touch. What is not lacking is strong longevity and sillage. Both are at a high level like most oriental Rojas. Nine hours are the minimum here, sometimes even longer. In the first three hours, the fragrance radiates quite well. Here, the sour component mainly lingers in the air, which is surprisingly refreshing in warmer temperatures. A truly beautiful and wonderful fragrance that wins my heart in the first hours. Unfortunately, the late drydown is a bit boring due to this unspectacular and interchangeable wood note. But you can't always get everything you wish for. Thus, Fruity Aoud remains my unmatched number 1.

I sadly recognized an old and well known odor in AIRE. My grandfather was a drunkard, and he used every day a very old-fashioned face-wash. He also smoked a lot. AIRE is exactly the same. A strong, alcoholic smoke on an old drunkard. My heart is heavy. Please tell me, that there was something wrong with my sample. There is summer, maybe it turned sour. Flowery, citrus, green categories... I did not smell anything like this.
Crisp and lemony, Aire Loewe is good for the warm months. I miss the oakmoss it had in previous formulations, however. Nice, sleek bottle

Leather dominates, it screams so loud, animalistic, wild... unfamiliar. Saffron fights for power, but leather watches over everything. The rose whispers, barely heard, amber flickers, but leather disturbs. Lavender struggles, but remains quite small, vanilla is more show than substance. Sandalwood floats in the base, light as a feather. In the end, what lasts forever... is the leather. Pisces is not a delicate leather scent, but a leather tsunami that rolls over all other fragrance notes and buries them for a long time. Unfortunately, I can hardly perceive anything other than stable leather; with a lot of imagination, the rose and sandalwood eventually come through. Unfortunately, not for me, but... fans of strong, dark leather fragrances and wild animalism should definitely give it a try.

Full of anticipation, I wanted to test my first fragrance from Tiziana Terenzi. It was supposed to be Pisces, as I was born under the sign of Pisces myself. Based on the fragrance pyramid, I imagined an exciting, multi-layered, and wonderful scent! In short: I have never been so disappointed. During the first test on a paper strip, I didn't find it that bad. There was just way too much leather, so I could hardly perceive the other notes. During the second test, on my skin, I was frankly hit hard. No matter how hard I tried, I could really only pick out two of the listed notes: an old rancid leather bag and a nasty, piercing lemon cleaner. This must have leaked in the leather bag, so that the bag was first stored in the musty, slightly moldy basement before it eventually ends up in the trash. Where the nasty smell doesn't bother anyone. Really, I'm sorry, but I don't understand this fragrance! Nothing about it is even remotely pleasant to my nose. Nothing. You just want to wash this perfume off and get rid of it. However, thanks to its fairly good longevity and sillage, you have to deal with it for quite a while. No, unfortunately, this won't work.

While preparing for a future sniff-fest, I decided to search the perfume database on classic chypre notes to make sure I hadn't missed any chypre fragrances among my FBs and samples. According to everybody, those notes are: citrus (usually bergamot), cistus labdanum, oakmoss and musk. What a surprise to discover that of the forty-seven I've gathered, only Enslaved has all the chypre notes. Not Chypre Rouge or Chypre Palatin, not even my adored vintage Chypre de Coty and Mitsuouko. Chypre de Coty has civet instead of musk. Mitsuouko has ambergris and per the notes pyramid, it has no labdanum. Can that be right? Time to investigate. Sniffing cistus labdanum from my perfumery notes kit. Now smelling Misuoko. Wow, I don't think it's there. Checking Fragrantica. Nope, Mitsuoko has no labdanum. Do classic chypres deviate from the classic definition or is Enslaved the only true chypre I have? Personally I'd classify Enslaved as a Chypre/Oriental, missing only a classic oriental's amber, but labdanum stands in nicely for that. Wait, I think I read that many ambers used in perfumes are really a combination of labdanum and vanilla? Okay, then check. It has amber. Enslaved certainly smells like both genres, has a chypre's dry haunting allure, an oriental's exuberant luxury -- both muted in this case, yet the result is satisfying. I suppose Enslaved is especially good for non-extremists who want to smell terrific without knocking others over with their scent. In the years I have left to smell things, I seek the glorious reek. Give me the original Mitsuoko, give me Bal à Versailles. I pursued them both with breathless passion, not caring one whit what they cost. When I looked up Enslaved, I decided it was too expensive. Or maybe it's just very British, like its designer, Roja Dove. One day when I'm finished buying everything else I think I'll adore, I might consider owning the beautifully reserved Enslaved, my (apparently) only true chypre. p.s. Now I see it's musk that's eliminating so many from my chypre database search. When I search on the basic accord of bergamot-labdanum-oakmoss, a few more perfumes show up. Still, many chypre fragrances don't contain all of those three, Mitsuoko being a prime example.

Roja Dove really seems to apply his curator habilities also in his collection, in a kind of an attempt to preserve classics that may be destroyed with reformulations or may not exist anymore with discontinuations. I don't know if the current Habanita Parfum is still good, but Enslaved in parfum concentration really reminds Habanita. It has the dry, spicy tobacco accord, with honey nuances, with a drydown that is good woody vetiver. Between there seems to be something like heliotrope or tonka that gives the fragrance a slightly almond aura. It's quality stuff, expensive indeed and maybe it lacks the originality factor, but not the deepness and personality as said before.

I wanted to bind you, yet I knew that prisoners do not love their guard. So I loosened the bonds, and now I feel how good it is when there are no chains chafing at love. -Kristiane Allert-Wybranietz - My statement back then was ... wish list ... one can still dream :) And it won't let me go... I cannot escape this Roja. Just as I believe in true love, I know that Enslaved will someday be a part of me. Not today and not tomorrow and perhaps not even next year ... but this love for the fragrance will be eternal. A heartfelt thank you to dear Parfuma who treated me to a sample of this beautiful scent and included it in a fragrance package. I was thrilled and still am :) About the scent: Enslaved opens with a radiant bergamot, creamy, almost spicy. It smells harmonious and not at all piercing. Why was I so surprised? I had imagined a vintage appearance that did not come, and that is a good thing. The flowers blend beautifully into this almost fruity scent progression, and I can distinctly smell the clove (a lovely clove, mind you!). Here too, everything is wonderfully harmonious, and everything together forms an excellent unity. Spicy-floral-oriental and dusted with the finest powder, I now perceive Enslaved. I can't really dissect the base ... amber and balsamic notes with a hint of vanilla and patchouli give the fragrance depth and warmth. A fine touch of musk is also part of the mix. For me, Enslaved is a spicy-ambered oriental in the base. The drydown is divine and captivating. A sensually warm scent. The longevity is about 10 hours. A beautiful fragrance aura surrounds the wearer. Enslaved is not overpowering but very present. The bottle is beautiful. This wonderful scent is wearable for many occasions. Enslaved is not tied to seasons, and my personal feeling: It fits just as well with jeans as it does with an evening gown. With tattooed Sweetsmell just as much as with an elegant lady ;) A very high-quality fragrance ... Well done Mr. Dove! Conclusion: Oriental-spicy dream. Wish list ... one can still dream :) I am "enslaved" ... and there is no escape. A great love for this fragrance on my part, and even though this beautiful dream is indeed very expensive and my surroundings (all non-perfumistas) do not understand it ... I believe you understand me ;) Testing recommendation! P.S.: Later found out that my sample was the EdP!

Roja Dove has gained many fans in recent years with his, as he claims, world's most expensive perfumes. Regardless of the opinions: overpriced, somehow nouveau riche clunky, often simply adopting ideas & trying to perfect them (e.g. from Guerlain), a somewhat confusing release policy (EdP, perfumes, extraits, Pour Homme...) - but the style & the money/price have once again sparked a small hype. Partly justified, partly shaking one's head. I was also deeply impressed when I saw the bottles live for the first time. And this awe lasted/lasts a long time - usually, bergamot, vetiver, danger, amber aoud, and co. are just sprayed briefly on test strips and then I move on. But today was Roja Dove day and my two samples at home had to be put to the test. Enslaved is a monster of a fragrance. A constant pendulum between glamour & porn, diva & whore, royal palace & swinger club. Sometimes it’s just too much of a good thing for me, sometimes it’s close to the perfect evening scent for women. A rather skillful dance on the soapy razor's edge. And as sexually charged as the fragrance sometimes struts, this edge is not really at the face, but rather in more southern regions. Actually, for men, it’s close to unbearable and perfect for today’s Sophia Lorens - but one should never say never, perhaps a young demigod will find this dominant perfume suits him. Ultimately, the deciding factor for me that Enslaved belongs to the absolute top perfumes and would never have received less than 80% was the base. Vanilla meets oak moss on heavenly paths. This is also rather unisex and the undisputed, albeit simple, but delicious green-yellow highlight of the fragrance. Before that, there is much to discover, but they are rather hard blows and whip lashes of rose, iris, ylang-ylang, bergamot, and amber, which I admire, but personally find a bit too harsh and tempestuous. A fragrance only for going out, sometimes even too strong for that. It gets full marks in all statistical values - that’s rare, but here it’s not exaggerated! There is a great similarity to Habanita. Bottle: the sheikh in the Taj Mahal could not have more beautiful bottles. Sillage: Enslaved behaves not at all submissively, really makes a statement in the room & goes all out. Longevity: still well distributed in the room even after 12 hours. Conclusion: a classic diva in new, unaffordable designer dresses, sparkling in competition with the stars and the great perfume classics! *Tested was the EdP

I have wanted to write a comment about Enslaved for a long time, as it has absolutely blown me away this year, alongside Shem el Nessim, and has helped reduce my oud obsession and simply enjoy fragrances more diversely. But I was lazy about writing, though I think the world still needs to learn a few aspects about this masterpiece. :) It is true love, not a fleeting infatuation that usually comes and goes. What my predecessors have written is correct; Enslaved is powerful and deep, yes, perhaps even diva-like. But it is never loud or intrusive. Personally, I can wear such scents in any situation and with any wardrobe. This may be due to my fundamental belief that one should not hold back, that one does not have to adapt to anything, and that the things one owns are there to be used and enjoyed at will. Now to the scent, or rather the opening, which is the most beautiful of all and very difficult to describe. In fact, it is a radiance that is most prominent in the top notes. I suspect it is the bergamot, but a creamy bergamot. And this radiance runs through the fragrance, although it diminishes over time as more notes come into play and the scent becomes increasingly powdery. This brings us directly to the comparison with Habanita. One cannot deny a similarity, but it only appears from the heart note, and even then, Habanita simply cannot keep up. Habanita lacks the radiance, the bright liveliness, the versatility. I have now gone through several samples, both of the EdP and the Extrait, and the Extrait clearly wins for me. Because the best part of Enslaved for me is the opening, and it is so much more intense and longer-lasting in the Extrait. A long-term love that will accompany me for a long time and at a high cost.

Yes yes yes... this fragrance is one of my private favorites. It enchanted me from the very first moment, enslaved me, captured me. This oriental seducer is, like all Roja Dove perfumes, strongly influenced by classic opulent fragrance models, so it’s for scent adventurers with a taste for expensive elixirs.

Women’s fragrances don’t have it easy with me. There are few that I truly love. Shalimar, for example, which I immediately embraced. Some I appreciate very much for their quality, for their wonderful composition; however, I wouldn’t necessarily want to wear them. Enslaved falls into this category for me; just like the Grossmith fragrances I have tested so far.

Sweet, humid, and very lovable. I was worried I'd hate it based on my prior experience with Solo Ella Eau de Parfum , but they ended up being nothing alike. Huh! I have to preface this with the fact that I never smelled fresh passionfruit (and found dragon fruit to have a very mellow and whimsical flavor profile that, imo, doesn't translate well into perfumery), so I can't judge if it smells like either of the fruits that it lists. But it is adorable! There are two visible layers to it. The airy outer cloud cloaks the whole room in a thin mist of sweet peony-flavored cotton candy. Playful and pink. It slowly fades out over the first ~2 hours. The thicker inner cloud is fruity and wet, with a tangy tropical twist and a gourmand praline backdrop. Well, that and sandalwood. Sandalwood is there and it's, well, itself. I don't love it, but I admit that it fits the composition well. The playful tartness is my favorite aspect of it. It's like a sweet and sour metaphorical cherry on top of a delicious tropical cake ٩(ˊᗜˋ*)و Cutesy, girly, youthful. Not something I'm interested in wearing myself, but imagining it on someone else makes me happy. Feels like something straight out of a "main character's childhood friend from the time he visited a tropical island" fantasy. The lulling sound of ocean waves crashing onto the shore, lively chirping of insects, distant noise of the city – and the way all of that fades away when you see her tan skin illuminated by the setting sun. A sight that goes straight into the "core memories" pile in your brain. Honestly, if someone told me that this was Paula's Ibiza Cosmic , I would easily have believed them. It may be less traditionally unisex, but it's unique, works great with its sandalwood backdrop, and fits the tropical vacation vibe much better. Also, for what it's worth, I tested it on my partner (noticed no major differences in either flavor or longevity), and thought that it fit him wonderfully. Once peony and cotton candy disappear after the first ~2 hours, everything else settles on skin. Fruits linger, but become sweeter. As if they ripen on your skin. Praline slowly dissipates, sandalwood becomes more prominent. In another ~2 hours fruits start fading away as well. Around ~6 hours in all that's left is sandalwood, ambers and a faintly gourmand aftertaste. Sandalwood dominates for another hour, then dissipates. Feeling that there's nothing else interesting this perfume will be able to say, I go take a shower. In a good mood. Content.

A summer freshie that gets better as it dries down. I find that interesting, because many perfumes in this category start out nice and dry down to a nondescript thin base, but here it's the other way round. The opening is fruity, but in a kind of artificial way. Even though there are no citruses listed, I smell something like mandarin and grapefruit besides the tart passion fruit. And it smells like the whole citrus fruit with the zest and the piths, sweet and also a little bitter. It gives me poolside vibes, but comes across a tad harsh. After a while the sweetness of cotton candy and vanilla changes the scent. It feels warmer, rounder and more natural after a couple of hours. Still very fruity and fresh, but more cocktail-like and very inviting. The subtle peony adds a nice touch of clean floralcy. I tried the original Solo Ella EDP a few years ago, and from what I remember, I don't find them too similar. The EDP was more peachy and floral, not as zesty as the EDT. I also tried really hard to detect the similarity to Baccarat Rouge 540 that some get from this, but I don't even smell the tiniest hint of it.

Solo Ella Eau de Toilette is for me a true good mood fragrance. Cheerful, carefree, summer. About the scent: Sweet - for my taste and my usual fragrance preferences, even very sweet. But not too heavy, not overwhelming, and not unpleasantly sweet for me (even chocolates and cotton candy can't throw me off).  Otherwise (slightly synthetic) fresh fruity with subtle peony and delicate vanilla, along with warm wood. All in all, just as @Parfümlein described it very aptly in the second part of her review: “Diffuse fruits in warm sun, round sweetness, indefinable beauty.”

Amore Mio reminds me Reflection man and Prada L’Homme Good projection and Longevity More for women, then for men like Reflection man. Prada L’Homme is unisex, I think. I have them all, and you can’t detect difference

… when hearts are beating …“ Another old song that now rests in the drawer labeled “long forgotten.” What a shame! But to stay on topic: isn’t it wonderful to be in love, to feel that multitude of colorful butterflies fluttering in your stomach? The heart beats too fast, the skin is softly flushed with a rosy hue, the eyes shine more beautifully than the most precious gemstones! To immortalize these exciting, all-consuming feelings in a fragrance is surely the goal of every perfumer. Whether it is achieved is decided by the lovers of these scents, who love to surround themselves with them. “Amore Mio,” this enchanting fragrance creation of love and lovers, was actually built in the well-known Roja manner: first the freshness of the hesperides, then romantic seduction in the grand floral garden à la Grasse, and finally the magic of spices and woods, warm, spicy, and balsamic. As simple as that sounds (almost a bit boring: this predictable repetition of the structure), each individual fragrance composition unfolds surprisingly! At the outset, we traverse a grove of hesperides, whose composition changes from scent to scent. One wanders among citrus trees, in the shade of the dark green lacquered leaves that rustle softly and perform changing light plays. The aromas of the sun-warmed wood of the trunks and foliage awaken the senses quietly and playfully. Sometimes, I wouldn’t be surprised if Apollo stepped out from a nearby thicket and calmly selected the “golden apple of the hesperides” among the ripe, gleaming fruits in the dark foliage to later present it to Aphrodite. With “Amore Mio,” this is not the case: the fragrance weave of bergamot and mandarin is simple, clear, and fruity-fresh. Young and almost innocently buoyant, this fragrance begins before it enters the summery, endlessly delightful floral garden with all its beauties: just the sight is splendor and joy, not to mention the fragrance development on the skin! Colorful, lavishly fragrant flowers everywhere, visited by thick bumblebees, lively buzzing insects, and many butterflies. Some linger there in the sun, seemingly enjoying the intense fragrance diversity that surrounds them. This fragrance impression spreads richer and richer on my skin over time. Of course, the Grasse rose is also present, also known as the May rose: a particularly special type of fragrant rose that is being cultivated again for the perfume industry after years of being forgotten and now bears rich blooms. It appears accompanied by white flowers: sensual, slightly animalistic jasmine aromas, heart-warming orange blossoms with a delicate scent, and balsamic neroli gifts unite with the abundance of fragrant roses. This bouquet is loosely arranged and tied with ylang-ylang vines adorned with flowers before stronger fragrance notes of the existing splendor adapt: Cistus with its small pink flowers, which always appear a bit crumpled, releases its spicy, very unique aroma, generously sharing wood and leaf green. The previously softly flowing fragrance progression becomes somewhat more robust due to them, containing small thorns and barbs here and there; thus, the floral splendor already appears stronger before violet fragrance notes of violet and heliotrope mix in heavily and intensely: the previous liveliness and carefree cheerfulness become more sensual, corporeal, and mature. “Amore Mio” loses a bit of its fragrance innocence. In return, warming, stimulating spices like ginger, pepper, and other exotics now take the fragrance scepter: they accompany all the floral notes before woody, aromatic, and balsamic additions, which appear in a variety of fragrance notes and refined dosages, lead to a magical fragrance finale. Who names all the ingredients woven in here; that would be tedious, boring, and also unnecessary: after all, there is the fragrance pyramid for that. Here and there, however, aromatic-sensual sandalwood and moist, earthy patchouli peek out from the fragrance weave; warm, erotic vanilla accompanied by tonka bean appears and is supported by a good splash of dark rum before the proud and elegant iris generously swings its powder puff in conclusion. Together with the slightly animalistic musk, it weaves a powdery-soft fragrance net with smoky-glittering amber inclusions that it lovingly spreads over this entire creation with all its secrets and beauties. Sillage and longevity are no longer an issue with Roja fragrances: both are truly exceptional: if you like it, you like it! Thus, “Amore Mio” also envelops richly and durably; this fragrance being accompanies through many romantic hours, regardless of what time of day they take place: this fragrance is time-neutral! With “Amore Mio,” the fragrance trilogy “Profumi d’Amore” begins, in which the individual phases of love are described in scent. After the romance of “Amore Mio,” “Ti Amo” is a declaration of love in fragrance form, and “Un Amore Eterno” stands for love in eternity. I really like this opening of the collection with its rich fragrance romance of awakening love. Softly and tenderly, instead of rushing forward, this composition presents itself: beat by beat - note by note: it wants to be carefully cherished, this still shy young love, it must not be startled! How this trilogy develops, what the other two fragrances tell, I may not be able to witness; but to be a witness to this phase of a fragrant fresh love has already been worthwhile. Imaginary colorful fragrance butterflies, eternal companions of the lovers, flutter around me; I am enveloped in a rich variety of flowers and aromas. A charming fragrance romance that awakens memories, I got to know thanks to Gelis. It is lovely, this first time of love, and in “Amore Mio” it has found a fitting fragrance.

Amore Mio ... ah ... just the name of the fragrance makes my heart melt. How much I was looking forward to this Roja. Thanks to a dear perfumer, I was able to test the first fragrance from the Roja love trilogy ... heartfelt thanks again for that :) The opening immediately ignited a fire within me and the hearts in my eyes grew ... by the end of the test, it was clear to me ... Amore Mio and I ... let's just leave it at that ;) Of course, one doesn't give up so easily, and the remaining sample was tested from time to time ... but my judgment remains ... Amore Mio doesn't soften me :) About the fragrance: Bright and clear, mandarin and bergamot shine in competition. Neroli, orange blossom, delicate violet, and powdery heliotrope join the fragrance progression. It smells soft and powdery from the wrist. Slowly, rose and jasmine come into play, and Amore Mio gradually shifts into a different mood. Deeper, spicier with an animalistic note that I don't quite enjoy here. With cocoa, woody notes, and powdery iris, it heads into the base. A slightly creaky note occasionally flashes through the gently powdery cocoa-iris note. I think this comes from the patchouli plus various other notes that I can't really detect in the fragrance progression. The base itself is really beautiful ... vanilla and tonka bean give the fragrance a slight sweetness, which harmonizes very well with cocoa and iris. If it weren't for the cumin, which I find most off-putting about Amore Mio ... it unfortunately develops a sweaty quality on me. Even a Roja cumin doesn't make an exception here :( Fortunately, this doesn't last forever, and Amore Mio gradually becomes more agreeable with its sweet smell :) A floral-powdery-creamy fragrance with sweet tones and this beautiful cocoa-iris note that stays with me until the end. The longevity is around 9 hours plus ... Amore Mio is not too loud, and I find the scent aura pleasant. This unobtrusive fragrance won't disturb and is thus suitable for many occasions. A fragrance for autumn/winter and I also count the first days of spring among them. Unisex? Yes The bottle... elegant and beautiful ... typical for Roja. Conclusion: Between "Hearts in the Eyes" and "I Don't Like It After All" - floral-powdery-animalistic ... it crackles and creaks - repulsive yet captivating! I whisper a test recommendation to the Roja fans. Not a candidate for my perfume shelf. Luckily ;)

Roja, a niche brand that unfortunately keeps adding more fragrances to its lineup, is becoming increasingly overwhelming, and with the prices, one wonders if it really has to be this way. But no matter, there are always beautiful surprises from the house of Roja, and for me, Amore Mio is one of them! From this trio collection, it is clearly the most beautiful! After multiple tests, I am sure I would love to wear this more often. The fragrance starts beautifully soft, creamy, and not too overpowering as one might suspect when reading the pyramid. For me, it is from the very beginning a clean floral garden with a very pleasant orange blossom. I can't pinpoint neroli directly; it blends in perfectly without evoking any 4711 memories. The longer the fragrance lingers on the skin, the sweeter it becomes, but not in an annoying, sticky, or cloying way; rather, it is a mature sweetness. It could really remind one of cocoa, a cocoa with a splash of milk and a small pinch of cinnamon, not too dark and bitter. The scent settles on the skin like a very luxurious powder-milk-cream and allows the wearer to indulge in a story full of love. Amore Mio does not overwhelm its surroundings with a killer sillage but approaches it more gently and lovingly; for that, its longevity is stunning and accompanies me for half a day. A truly wonderful fragrance that rightly deserves its name - My love grows stronger with each wear :)

Today we stood in front of the locked practice of our dear doctor. "What now?" says the Ruhri. So off to the city for a substitute, navigating through the overcrowded parking garages, battling through the crowd.
