In the substitute practice, one is greeted with a distinctly rude reception and often has to apologize for their disruptive presence. Fortunately, my "fragrance oasis" is just around the corner, and a visit was now due. The friendly owner hands me a bottle, which I gratefully sample. Loewe Aura EdP. What a welcome, soothing effect! Gently, bergamot and pink pepper caress my heated cheeks, and the violet leaf adds a mild bitterness. I slowly return to the present. The iris is soft and powdery, and the narcissus has an uplifting effect. The raspberry comforts with subtle sweetness, and the leather wraps around me warmly and nobly. The scent is like the embrace of a strong friend who protects and preserves you. Despite its presence, it is sensitive and almost transparent, justifying its name "Aura." For me, it is pure nerve balm. I received a sample for a "quick charge" of my battery, but a large bottle will follow,

I first wore this fragrance in Barcelona. I was aimlessly wandering around a department store and sprayed this scent on my wrist rather thoughtlessly. It ended up with me walking around this beautiful city, sniffing my wrist half the time. This fragrance developed so wonderfully on my skin! The relatively sweet-floral top note gradually became a bit woodier and even slightly spicy. Yet it always remained softer and warmer. With this fragrance, I associate incredible warmth and very soft, flowing movements; at the same time, the scent is oriental-spicy and therefore anything but those 0815 fabric softener perfumes that say nothing about their wearer. The woman who wears Aura is gentle yet proud, elegant and striking. She envelops you, caresses your head, without you ever feeling like you can fully grasp her essence. That is Aura for me. I have since purchased the fragrance and I'm in love just like on the first day :)

This is a pretty and very feminine scent but nothing about it sticks out as particularly special to me (excluding the absolutely beautiful bottle). I really appreciate how fresh and joyful the peony is in Elysium Pour Femme and I enjoy that note quite a bit here. However, there is something about Elysium Pour Femme that feels akin to hairspray. Nice scent that I can't imagine anyone being offended by, but I think you can find other similar scents that are similar for better price. Of the Roja Women's sample pack this sits somewhere in the middle for me. Not my favorite but also not a dislike. It's just sort of fine.

Elysium Pour Femme is … okay. It is exactly what people say: A bright, fruity-floral scent (but with a powdery base) that tends to lean in a shampoo-like direction. It is pleasant and unobtrusive, but surprisingly basic for a Roja fragrance. An aldehydic-sharp freshness that is nice enough, but not particularly memorable. I’m glad I didn’t blind buy a whole bottle. The 2 ml sample was the right decision - a few wears confirmed to me that Elysium Pour Femme is perfectly fine, but nothing special or something I would prefer over other fragrances in my collection. The long longevity and the charming bottle are positive aspects.

it smelled on a hot summer day in my grandmother's garden. This fragrance opens with fruits that harmonize very well together. Then a multitude of different flowers joins in. My grandmother had a large garden with fruit trees and bushes, as well as many flower beds, hence the comparison. The base makes me think of sitting with a vanilla ice cream in hand on one of her old wooden garden chairs. This fragrance certainly hasn't reinvented the wheel, but it is a truly lovely companion in summer.

As has been read in many statements, the expectation was high, and the fall therefore deep. It is not a bad scent in my nose. It starts fruity, slightly citrusy/sparkling, accompanied by a lot of floral notes, and ends sweetish/slightly woody. It is rather light, bright, without much depth. If one were to be unkind, one could label it as "watery." On my skin, it has a somewhat melony quality. A fruity scent that works for me, a light all-rounder, but also nothing new, nothing special, and therefore unfortunately not worth the price for me.

If Paula's Ibiza represents a day at the beach, Eclectic is later that day when you're partying at a bonfire or drunk at a bar after spending all day in the sun. Eclectic is a great name for this because it has a bit of everything - it's sweet and creamy, it's a bit woody, it's spicy. At times it feels sharp or I'm not quite sure if I like it and then I find myself sniffing where I sprayed it on my arm. I think this is such a great vacation scent.

What can I say, "Eclectic" is a very fitting name for it. A vibrant orange initial cloud. Heavy florals underneath. A subdued sweet backdrop – creamy, coconutty, almost gourmand... and that's just a start. In about ~20 minutes prickly pepper becomes visible, and with it – sandalwood, adding a layer of fresh sharp woodiness to an already oversaturated mix. Another ~10 minutes and the initial cloud fizzles out. "Eclectic" settles close to the skin and adds one more layer – warm esoteric resins. It's kind of a mess, but a very well calculated one. It's a lot, but never too much. It's not screechy. A bit weird, maybe, but in an enticing tourist-friendly way. A very sensible rendition of a long dead hippie aesthetic, perfectly blended and packaged to be a hit tourist attraction. Like a fun memory of getting scammed at an esoteric shop during your tropical vacation. About an hour into the experience fruity and floral notes start fizzling out. Sandalwood takes centerstage. A pleasant musky woodiness, creamy vanilla and a prominent yet vague tropical aftertaste. Over the next few hours the tropical twinge softens and disappears. Each time you notice it – it's like a bittersweet fading memory. After about ~5 hours since the first spray a faint sandalwood aftertaste is the only thing left, but it easily lasts into the night. I tested it on both myself and my partner. On my body jasmine was more prominent, on him – ylang ylang; but I haven't noticed any other tangible difference between our experiences. Credit where it's due – it's a very thought through and well-blended composition. It has a particular vision and executes it masterfully. I guess I'm just not the target audience for it.

For the sake of completeness, I obviously have to review this Eclectic from the Paula's Ibiza line. I initially reviewed the original Paula's Ibiza since it is in my collection. I reviewed the latest flanker Paula's Ibiza Cosmic last week. Now here is the second release of this line, which fits perfectly with the current time, just like all the very summery releases from this Spanish brand. Generally, most fragrances from this brand are very fresh, uncomplicated, and simply suitable for the brand's location. The Paula's Ibiza line is a bit more casual and has a slight beach feeling, making them quite suitable for summer leisure. Which one do I like best from this line? Tough question, as they all have their charm. The original is greenish with a great exotic coconut water note, the Cosmic is fruity and roughly in the direction of Erba Pura, and this one is beautifully creamy-floral with a slight sunscreen vibe and also light tropical vibes. A great flanker, available in 50 and 100ml like all from this brand. In my opinion, this is the most feminine scent in the line, but it is not unwearable for men (if it matches their style). The colorful packaging of this fragrance is quite cool and fits perfectly with this scent and this bottle. This line stands out a bit, as the bottle design of this brand is usually uniform. However, it fits this casual summer style. The pyramid captures this scent quite well, and since this fragrance is rather linear, the omission of the top, heart, and base note classification works well. Primarily, the Eclectic is a floral-creamy fragrance that is still very summery. This is particularly due to the creamy-exotic mix of ylang-ylang, coconut, and sandalwood. It harmonizes well, and I am a fan of it. Additionally, there is a fresh-fruity mandarin with a floral combination of orange blossom and jasmine. This floral combination smells summery-fresh and not too cloying. Thus, this creation is also wearable at temperatures above 30 degrees. The vanilla sweetens this fragrance very well and makes it perfect for those who cannot do without sweetness in the high summer. The rest is made up of creamy-clean musk and a great mix of spicy pepper and incense. These notes do not come through strongly but round off this "base" nicely and give the finish a bit more elegance and depth. I don't really find any true scent twins here. Quite unique, even though there are already some alternatives with this floral-creamy DNA. It feels well-groomed, and I see it best suited for summer leisure or in the evening. However, it can also work well in everyday life. The performance is quite good, and it could last around 8 hours with a few hours of good sillage. Everything is in a pleasant range, making it versatile. Overall, a great floral-creamy fragrance that one could buy quite well in the month of July and also use. Recommendation goes out, especially to the ladies.

On vacation, the biggest highlight for me is usually going into a perfume shop and searching for a scent that captures the essence of the place for me, so that it can still envelop me and bring me back home. So here I am for the first time in Mallorca, far from Ballermann and the big city, in a small tourist village where I happened to spot a little perfume shop from the hotel balcony. The selection was of course a bit meager, but at least I was able to test a whole range of different Loewe fragrances. Just as the island itself has become a story for me, one that cannot be told without one or two "actually" and "but," so it was with "Paula's Ibiza Eclectic | Loewe." Actually, I don't like citrus scents. And the bottle is a bit too colorful and flashy for me. And actually, I had not planned for an Eau de Toilette, but something with more longevity - yet I let myself be drawn into this little flirt, enchanted by a soft, warm mandarin scent, nestled in sensual white flowers and a truly gentle coconut note. It doesn't smell like sunscreen; on the contrary: it smells not freshly washed, but lived-in and warm in the best possible way. After a sun-kissed day at the beach, fresh fruit at lunchtime, and the waning heat of the early evening hours. For being "just" an EdT, the performance is actually quite decent, although I would say that after about four hours, it would indeed be time to reapply.

Got this one for a bargain and I am yet to wear it in high heat, but I am so excited for when I do. This is a mossy and bitter citrus grapefruit scent, not sweet or zingy. I don't really get fruity or woody notes, even in the drydown, but I do like this a lot. Longevity is okay, but it's fairly inoffensive so you can go on the heavier side of spraying. Definitely unique.

I'm surprised to see this fragrance rated as mediocre as it is. As one who doesn't go in for aquatic scents very often, this one really surprised me and has become a hot weather favorite. At its core you won't find anything that breaks the mold. There have been oodles of designer aquatic fragrances over the last two decades. What I enjoy most about this fragrance is a really juicy, mouthwatering bouquet of citruses and other fruits particularly in the opening. Loewe pushed all their chips in on a lovely, lively blend of tropical goodness here. The pineapple and black current lend a tangy complex fruitiness. It never goes really sweet, but the black currant and tangerine have a hard candy quality. The drydown introduces some marine minerality to the fragrance, and it settles close to the skin. The sandalwood and musk are not the stars of the show, but they do smooth the fragrance out a little and this never becomes harsh. I don't mean to mislead by comparing this to Aventus. There are none of the smoky tar and leather darkness that the Creed flagship has in its drydown. But as far as the opening goes, that bright fruity zing may be reminiscent of the livelier qualities that Aventus has.

Indeed, this masculine fragrance starts off citrus-sweet-aquatic. The fruit components primarily contribute their acidity. I don't find it very fruity at all after spraying. Right from the opening, there is a woody spiciness that intensifies over time, at times almost creamy/balsamic, but then settles between sweet-aquatic-woody base notes and lingers in this stage. Conclusion: It is indeed a fresh scent. However, one should not expect pure "refreshment" here. It is more of a warming freshness. This becomes clearer the closer you sniff it. It doesn’t aim to be too sporty either. More casual. Those who take this into account will receive an uncomplicated fragrance for the office and everyday life with average sillage & longevity. Given the existing spiciness, I would only recommend it to a younger clientele with reservations. In any case, test it beforehand. All in all, a wearable average fragrance that neither stands out negatively nor positively and thus has to share its place in this fragrance category with many other competitors.

Agua de Loewe is boring. As expected, there's a nice bergamot-grapefruit freshness in the top notes, resting on an unremarkable, slightly woody base. The fruity heart notes are not particularly noticeable. This is so ordinary, just the modern standard of fresh men's fragrance with not the slightest hint of uniqueness. Moreover, the scent is scratchy. And at 64 euros, it's not even a bargain. At Douglas, there are 4 - 5 similar, cheaper fragrances.

Here, the floral All-Star selection meets a creamy peach note that doesn't take center stage but resonates clearly. The fragrance starts soft and friendly, with a creamy sweetness that immediately brings to mind peaches in cream - those who enjoy peaches + cream on waffles or cake bases know what I mean. The floral components - rose and a bit of jasmine as well as magnolia - come across clearly, but never piercing. The oud? Very subtle. Not loud, rather a reserved shadow in the background. It brings a slightly smoky-woody structure, providing grounding, yet always remains within limits. Those who associate oud with heavy, medicinal-resinous notes will be disappointed. Nothing feels forced or overly thick. Especially in the warmer season, this fragrance can work well - not as a pure freshness kick, but rather as a gentle, floral-fruity accompaniment. Overall, a pleasant blend with depth.

I must say that I really like "Enigma Aoud (Parfum) | Roja Parfums," even though I see it more on a woman. The longevity is quite impressive at 10 to 12 hours, but I find the sillage to be rather mediocre - I expect much more in this price segment. The top note starts off fruity-sweet with peach and a bit of pear compote. Aldehydes underline this impression and immediately create a decent floral quality. In the heart note, there is a sea of flowers consisting of jasmine blossoms, ylang-ylang, iris, rose water, and violets. There is also a significant creaminess present. The base remains floral with a sweet aura and a certain powderiness. Here, I recognize bourbon vanilla, benzoin, and a bit of musk. Additionally, there is a subtle, woody oriental vibe thanks to sandalwood and barely noticeable oud. The fact is that Enigma Aoud Parfum is a beautifully crafted fragrance. I thank Will for the sample.

Enigma Aoud Parfum , what a fascinating name! What olfactory splendor might be hidden behind it? Surprisingly, I found not a single review on Parfumo. This puzzled me and made me curious, so I decided to ask Google for advice. There, I immediately stumbled upon three mysteries: Mystery No. 1: Only four videos about this fragrance. Mystery No. 2: Are those really aldehydes? Mystery No. 3: Often referred to as Enigma Aoud Pour Femme - yet I thought this fragrance was unisex. The listed formula also seemed to differ from the one I was familiar with. Enigma Aoud remains a mystery. As a result, I contacted Roja Parfums, and the response was enlightening: Enigma Aoud is definitely unisex, and there have been no changes to the formula. One mystery was thus solved. Nevertheless, on Parfumo, the community is divided on whether the fragrance is more suitable for women (ratio 2:1 compared to men). However, some emphasized that this fragrance is indeed unisex. In summary: Few internet videos or reviews, and the little information available is often incorrect. So I decided to test the fragrance myself. After a few days of waiting, the sample finally arrived, and I could hardly wait to test it. So I grabbed a test strip and sprayed it on. The opening is breathtaking - bergamot and aldehydes(?)! I was already familiar with aldehydes from N°5 Parfum , but these smell completely different; I detect artemisia but not quite as spicy. The scent is voluminous, rather fruity-sweet and slightly alcoholic, reminding me of fermented plum. This mystery I probably won't unravel. The oud from the base also announces itself with a slight smoky-spicy note. After the opening, the fragrance becomes more seductive, ylang-ylang makes an appearance, accompanied by peach and the slightly cucumber-like jasmine. In between, may rose and geranium appear like through a curtain, only to disappear again; similar to a jewel that shows its facets depending on the light. The oud in the base, which I had already perceived as slightly smoky-spicy in the top note, re-emerges, this time more leathery, but it is a bright oud, accompanied by sandalwood and vanilla. The fragrance becomes more powdery. Iris and labdanum rounded off the overall picture. This fragrance is incredibly complex. One is tempted to keep smelling it to explore it and discover new nuances. Yet it is never fully revealed, and that is a good thing. It remains a mystery. The longevity and sillage are extraordinary. The fragrance lasts easily over 10 hours on me. My friend recently said: "Don't move so much!" because he thought I would otherwise constantly exude this incredible scent. Another friend, who had also researched the fragrance, asked: "Why does it say everywhere that it's for women? It's way too smoky/spicy for a woman." That probably says it all on this topic. In conclusion, I can state: This fragrance deserves far more than just a review. It is as multifaceted and mysterious as its name suggests.

I actually hadn't planned to publish a review today. When I mentioned Solo Esencial full of praise in the Parfumo Ticker about 4 hours ago, I had no idea that the scent would fade so quickly. The fact is that the fragrance becomes very close to the skin after 2-3 hours, and after a maximum of 5 hours, I can't perceive anything at all. Am I scent-blind today? Well, this morning I still reviewed Samba and I can still smell it. This afternoon, I assessed Samba Nova Femme and the scent is still there. And in the afternoon, a miniature of my beloved Woman No. 1 arrived - logically, that can still be smelled as well. All were applied beforehand. So I wouldn't attribute any scent blindness to myself. After all, the sillage was still quite good at the beginning. However, in the end, that's still too little, even though I really like the scent... The top note starts fruity, green, floral, and herbal. Here I recognize tangerine, lavender, mint, rosemary, mate tea, and limes. The heart note offers a certain creaminess and oranges - I immediately think of Solero ice cream. The base provides sweet, creamy, and vanillic nuances, reminding me of almond milk and tonka beans. In the end, somehow disappointment prevails. I definitely can't see a comparison to Armani Code (2004) Eau de Toilette - no idea who listed this similarity here.

To answer the question right away: In this case, yes! Of course, the origin of the original Solo cannot be denied here, but fortunately, it is only very rudimentary. Nevertheless, it is an independent representative in the now 8-member family of Solos. While the first 4 flankers were more at the drugstore level (with the exception of Solo E.d.C. Extrème), I found myself enjoying the Pop version at the latest, which stood out from the crowd with its beautiful, unusually dominant lavender accord; unfortunately, it seems to have been discontinued, well then... The second revelation for me was Solo Sport, with its opulent mandarin-heavy synthetic charm, and now I have another nose-pleaser in Solo Loewe Esencial. The fragrance starts fresh-fruity, with the tangerine dominating for me, while lime, mate, and mint add a bit of summer cocktail attitude. These notes last quite a while, and only after a good hour does the warm-spicy heart of the fragrance begin to kick in. Rosemary, thyme, and lavender give S.L.E. a Mediterranean touch and create a bridge towards the brilliantly crafted Esencia for me. However, they are softer and less herbal compared to this. The further development is initiated by the spice accords of cardamom and nutmeg, which blend pleasantly with incense, tonka, patchouli, and guaiac wood into a subtly spicy-earthy base. For me, there is also a slight nod to Loewe 001 Man here, although S.L.E. is lighter and more restrained in comparison. Conclusion: A successful all-round fragrance that does not offend, wearable for many occasions (except at temperatures >35°C) Certainly not a milestone, but still, in my opinion, one of the Solis from Loewe that definitely has its right to exist. The longevity for me is around 6-7 hours, and the sillage is rather subtle. Opinions are somewhat divided on the bottle; if the cap were not a simple, completely open wire cube, but perhaps adorned with transparent plastic on the front sides, it would a) be easier to handle and b) look more substantial.

A simply wonderful scent of suede with a deep and luxurious raspberry! Imagine yourself wearing a leather jacket riding a horse in the Wild West with the most luxurious feeling! I think this is a perfume for connoisseurs only. If you are a big fan of Roja Dove and his works, you need it in your collection For me : 9/10

In my opinion, one of the most masculine perfumes there is. A perfume that you have to dress for and adapt yourself to. A suede and raspberry perfume from the best in the category. Its performance is impressive. I can say that it is a winter perfume and is also suitable for autumn, suitable for evening outings, a black leather jacket and then it's yours. 9/10.

A few weeks ago, I discovered a sample of H - The Exclusive Black Tier and was immediately intrigued. It is often compared to "Ombre Nomade | Louis Vuitton," with leather and raspberry taking center stage. While I am no longer as drawn to "Ombre Nomade | Louis Vuitton," the DNA of this fragrance continues to fascinate me. When the sample arrived, I naturally sprayed the fragrance right away. Two sprays as always, and then I enjoy the opening in all its glory. I was surprised: “H” really starts off very dark, and you can clearly perceive the leathery, almost dirty component. At first, the fragrance can seem a bit overwhelming, but that is precisely what gives it a certain magic. Now to the heart of the fragrance: As it develops, “H” becomes very creamy and soft. The raspberry comes to the forefront and harmonizes wonderfully with the vanilla. Although I describe the fragrance components, it is very difficult to clearly identify them individually. Overall, the progression is very well balanced. With Roja, I always find it hard to clearly identify individual notes, as they are always very well crafted and harmonious. The drydown is simply excellent and hardly recognizable when you have the harsh, dark beginning in mind. That is exactly what makes this fragrance so incredibly beautiful. You really embark on a scent journey and discover different facets. Hence the metaphor of the knight with two sides: a dark, hard “outer shell,” yet still with a soft core. I understand the parallel to "Ombre Nomade | Louis Vuitton," but I do not find it justified to equate both fragrances. This fragrance stands out due to its outstanding quality and is clearly rounder and more versatile. I also know fragrances like "London | Widian / AJ Arabia" and "Sillage | Kinetic Perfumes," but I do not think they can hold a candle to "H - The Exclusive Black Tier | Roja Parfums." I have long searched for a fragrance that covers this area, and I am happy to have found it. It is indeed what I once hoped for from "Ombre Nomade | Louis Vuitton." I do not want to delve further into the pricing issue, as I find Roja generally overpriced. I can only recommend smelling this fragrance at least once and giving it the time to fully unfold. Enjoy the scent journey. :)

As I have proven to be a fan of darker and more oriental scents, this is evident in my various blogs. Since I am also actively adjusting the space in my collection that covers the dark-woody, and partly leathery aspect, testing H - The Exclusive Black Tier is not too far-fetched. Ombre Nomade still has to earn its place. Black Tier is one of the darkest from the house of Roja and skillfully rides the wave of dark woods, leather, and a fruity component. It is hardly surprising that such a scent must also come from the house of Roja, combined with the brand's typical influences. At first, I must admit I was a bit disappointed, as my internal expectations were perhaps set too high and I might have been expecting something different. Ultimately, it does convince me, but I only realized this after extensive testing. So, it was love at third sight. One can already note that the scent appears significantly drier and darker, almost dusty, when in direct contact with the nose. However, once it unfolds in the air and the sillage, the scent becomes much more accessible, brighter, and above all, fruitier. Especially with the currently warm temperatures, the combination of saffron and raspberry blossoms. It is therefore difficult to describe the scent, but since it is meant to be worn in the throat area, I will limit myself to the impressions I could gather here. At the beginning, at least for me, no bergamot from the top note is perceptible. It aligns itself within a construct of flowers and dark notes and does not exhibit the sprightliness one would normally expect from the note. The floral notes of May rose and jasmine, which Roja repeatedly uses in its fragrances, do not radiate too much to correspond to the impression of a floral scent. The rose appears very muted, more as a support, while the jasmine is much more prominent in the nose. Additionally, there is a prominent dark woodiness that corresponds to the typical scent of a western oud. Initially quite hard-woody, it becomes softer later. The pepper also plays a certain role and tries to arrogantly push itself to the forefront, which one notices as soon as one presses the nose against the sprayed area. The jasmine flower also contributes to the impression of dryness, shielding any sweetness and fruitiness. During the first test, when I sniffed my arm more often, I was left breathless a few times, as the combination acts like a vacuum and sucks in any peaks. A certain powderiness also plays a role here to underpin the impression of dusty wood. In the sillage, the fruity notes gradually come through, so that one perceives a delicate and very fruity raspberry, which was only noticeable in a similar form in Oro 1920 . The fruit tickles the nose and invites one to dream, as it acts like a bait that pulls one into the depth and darkness of the scent. The typical leatheriness of this category comes through and wraps its arms around the fine fruit to form a perfect harmony. This lasts well for an hour until the next notes join in. Subsequently, especially benzoin, amber, and musk become more present, as it becomes sweeter, a bit resinous, and significantly warmer. A beautiful progression that comes across as varied and hardly lingers in silence. It is like an escape from the dark depths. They never stand still, the most diverse abysses fly by, each with different circumstances. The performance has not let me down either. Sure, it cannot compete with the pure power of an Ombre Nomade, which I do not consider a personal reference, as the DNA is more important to me than the performance. Nevertheless, it manages to last over nine hours on my skin, delighting me, while in the first two to three hours, my mood is also uplifted by the pleasant sillage. Overall, a great scent that I actually prefer in terms of DNA compared to the Louis Vuitton and is on par with the Oro 1920. One certainly has to fight through the dryness at the beginning, but this is rewarded with a varied and deep scent progression.

I am one of the lucky ones who knows someone who knows someone. Thus, I was able to buy the Kuma at an extremely interesting price. Anyone can take a look at the bottle; I won’t go into that. One thing maybe: the craftsmanship is more than sufficient ;) Now to the scent. My first fragrance of this kind. The fruit salad at the beginning, with its very subtle creaminess, is simply phenomenal. The citrus fruits naturally set the tone. Just barely behind them, the rest falls into line. It seems as if the fruits, each on their own, are competing for the favor of the nose. Sounds like chaos and confusion. But it is not. Everything harmonizes absolutely excellently with each other. The passion fruit is definitely noticeable on my skin the whole time. Excellent! The sweetness of the raspberry and the peach rounds it off very well at the beginning. After a few minutes, a bit more creaminess comes through due to the vanilla. The scent now reminds me a little of an ice cream from my childhood. Sandalwood and musk join in. Soft, noble… truly dreamy. The scent does come off as sweet, but aren’t fruits always a bit sweet? A light, relaxed sweetness, with a wonderful creaminess that carries the sweetness on its white velvet gloves. The fruit basket never gets lost in the scent and flatters the nose the entire time. Wonderful. 10/10 summer fragrance, and you definitely smell unique. My association would be the following: Vacation, palm trees, hotel motto that evening: white night. Dress code, of course, white clothing. After dinner, you gather for a nightcap at the beach bar. You are wearing a white shirt (of course, the first 3 or 4 buttons are open), beige linen pants, and white slip-ons. Around you, this scent. On the other side sits the unknown beauty in a white dress. Her brown curls shimmer in the red sun, which is gradually setting behind her. The rest is open to interpretation. If someone finds the scent a bit too unisex, it layers very well with Aventus. I use the 2013 batch for that, which is still a bit smokier than today’s versions. The pineapple plus this woody smokiness fits excellently with the Kuma. Unfortunately, I’m not a full professional when it comes to reviews, but I hope I could provide a little insight here. Take care. Chris

"We don't make mistakes. We just have happy accidents." This is how the famous television painter Bob Ross expressed it. I call it - my marketing professor may mildly punish me for the assimilation of this term - a variant of serendipity. Background: A year ago, maybe a bit more, a perfume order from the vastness of the internet came with a free sample of Loewe 001 Man. I was thrilled. And puzzled at the same time. Because as much as I liked the scent, I found it hard to categorize. Not by occasion. Not by time of day. Not by season. And - my marketing professor would agree - if you don’t know what you need something for, then … you just don’t buy it. Well then. Some of those mysterious cerebral twists recently conjured up the memory of this perfume from the … um … sleeve. I could no longer find my free tester anywhere, but presumably, the remaining content would have already diffused into the atmosphere of the bathroom's microclimate anyway. So: into the shopping cart with Loewe 001 Man! A quasi-blind buy. Actually even: the most uncertain purchase (my German teacher may mildly punish me) since the mathematical sets "History of Perfumes" and "Zacharias' Presence on the Planet" are equal parts. And what do I say? This perfume is simply … amazing. When I spray it on, I am enveloped by pepper, lime, and sweet wood. And while the other brands out there become increasingly leathery, powdery, and often even musty the longer you wear them, Loewe 001 becomes more pleasant with every minute of wear. It is a feel-good scent. I smell it, and I feel good in my skin. Loewe excellently manages to balance citrus freshness, herbal woodiness, and a touch of sweetness. This makes this scent a true all-rounder. It suits a workday in the office just as well as an informal evening event, like a casual cocktail party. As a season, I associate Loewe 001 Man more with the warmer half of the terrestrial elliptical orbit of our stellar photon pump - but even if you wear this scent in a snowstorm, you can hardly go wrong. Loewe 001 in winter is at most a happy accident. Bob Ross may mildly punish me.

There is a fruit “note” in this scent that makes it a bit sweet. All the rest i cant find words to describe. This is a masterpiece! The only scent that leaves me speechless. Like other Roja’s Gulf collection you get beside the fruity note also Oud wich is so sensual and calm...again speechless. Next to Kuwait from the collection Is this one of my favorites. Groundbreaking & lots of compliments. Again it’s very hard to describe this scent. 11/10 for sure!!!!

Today I am focusing on the fourth fragrance from Roja’s Gulf Collection, which I have had the chance to test multiple times after "Qatar | Roja Parfums," "United Arab Emirates | Roja Parfums," and "Sultanate of Oman | Roja Parfums." Although I find the concept of the Gulf Collection to be quite opportunistic (aka how can I make a good impression in the Emirates?), I think fragrances like "United Arab Emirates | Roja Parfums" are truly top-notch. In my opinion, the construction of the Gulf Collection fragrances follows a relatively simple concept. The base is quite similar across all fragrances: Oud, patchouli, something woody (cashmere wood or cedar wood), saffron, labdanum or frankincense, clove or cumin, leather. The heart notes vary primarily. The citrus top notes often serve merely as an accompaniment. Now, let’s talk about "Kingdom of Saudi Arabia | Roja Parfums." This fragrance attempts to marry fruity heart notes with woody-oudy base notes. Why not? The combination of raspberry with oud-leather in the base has become mainstream and often yields very good results, and plum with oud-leather also works well. So overall, a very solid foundation for a fragrance. About the fragrance: In the opening, the fruit cocktail emerges as expected, supported by a hint of citrus. Immediately, the banana hits my nose. Some unpleasant synthetic notes overshadow the slightly floral fruitiness. The result is quite an olfactory jumble. As the base notes no longer want to remain uninvolved, they now intervene. The green violet acts as the mediator. The transition from fruitiness to a slightly spicy green heart is beautiful. Subsequently, the spicy-balsamic character of the fragrance becomes a bit stronger. This is accompanied by mild oud (medicinal, not animalic) and a hint of cocoa. The sweetness of the fruits is made even more enduring with sandalwood, vanilla, and an additional sweet note that I cannot quite identify. After about 3-4 hours, a slightly fruity balsamic woody oud scent remains. Overall, the fragrance becomes increasingly attractive to me as it develops. I am not particularly fond of the opening. The synthetic notes (especially the banana) bother me quite a bit and somewhat diminish the value of the fragrance. However, the fragrance then transforms into a wonderfully balanced oriental and possesses very good longevity of 10 hours+. Therefore, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is, for me, a very successful fragrance overall, and I find it unfortunate that it is no longer produced. However, the pricing is a significant downside for me. In my opinion, there are too many inexpensive synthetic fragrance materials used to justify such a high price.

I have a kind of love-hate relationship with the house of Roja Dove. I am a fan of Roja's marketing and the special focus on elegance and quality. I also enjoy many of his compositions. However, I have two small issues with the Aoud perfumes from the house: First, they are clearly "overengineered" for me, with a few too many components. In brevity lies the spice, and I like to know what I am smelling. I do not like constructs that are hardly comprehensible in their complexity. Additionally, I really appreciate perfumes that are intense, preferably with edges and facets. In short: a clear (preferably innovative) concept and room-filling sillage. Roja's Aoud compositions correspond to this only semi-well. The scents are unparalleled in complexity - and they are supposed to be! This makes it difficult for me to discern the ingredients. I undoubtedly recognize a blackcurrant, a hint of apple, and some oud. In the entrance, there’s even a bit of lime. But: all of this together feels like it makes up not even 40% of the character of the fragrance. A multitude of other notes comes into play that I cannot distinctly unravel. Yet I want to, because I feel that these notes are clearly co-responsible for the DNA of the scent. For me, this is where the difference lies compared to fragrances like XerJoff's Alexandria II. They are also more complex than just oud-rose-lavender. But the scent is defined by these three ingredients. And that is the difference to Roja's oud creations, which are not solely determined by the components that are just barely detectable; much remains diffuse. Diffuse not in effect, but already in cause. And I find that a pity. Almost equally disappointing is that Roja's Aoud creations are so soft and rounded. This is undoubtedly also what Roja intended. But it does not fit for me with the animalistic-mysterious character of real oud, which I so enjoy. Additionally, I have a problem with the longevity and sillage of Roja's oud creations. I do not know why and I am aware of the many contrary experiences. But I have to almost drown my forearm in Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to still perceive anything after 10 minutes. I do not only have this problem with Kingdom of Saudi Arabia but also with less complex Aoud scents like Amber Aoud. In contrast, for the same effect, I need just a spritz, or even less, of Creed's Royal Oud or MFK's Baccarat Rouge Extrait. I cannot figure it out, but it bothers me. Interestingly, I do not have this problem with the scents from Roja's Parfum Cologne series. There, the longevity and sillage are just to my taste - contrary to the many local reviews. Conclusion: For the reasons mentioned above, I unfortunately cannot warm up to Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. It is a beautifully rounded fragrance that loses its charm for me in its over-complexity. But it is exactly what Roja Dove wanted to deliver. So do not hesitate to try it if you are intrigued by what bothers me. :) Cheers!

KSA opens with a broadside: After a handful of dung (I lack the expertise for the origin), a decent load of fruit follows. I believe I can recognize raspberry and plum. At this point, I allow myself a small note due to the frequently encountered outcries: If you can't stand cow or other stable scents, you're probably venturing into the wrong territory with oud fragrances, right? In any case, the dung throw - from whatever animal it may be - is of tolerably short duration, and the strong fruit accord fades quite quickly. After that, the scent settles into something for which I had to engage my olfactory memory (if it exists) for a while: For me, it's a kind of mix between Fruity Aoud and Un Amore Eterno, of which I especially love the latter. Perhaps after all these years, the master is losing a bit of originality - die-hard fans may forgive me the blasphemy. After a few hours, this fruity-amore harmony gives way to a slightly spicy, unobtrusive chocolate-vanilla sweetness, which is still pleasantly detectable to me even after nine hours. Now a rarity from the Gulf collection, KSA is so far my favorite from this line.

Personal: 7/10 - It's fine. I respect the quality, and I enjoy the clementine note, but it's too herbal. Mass appeal: 7/10 - Classic citrus and herbs can feel elegant, but it may be a bit divisive due to its green, herbal nature. Performance: 7/10 - Fair longevity for something reasonably fresh. Value: 3/10 - For the price, Roja makes it a tough sell when similar fruity DNAs exist. Uniqueness: 6/10 - Polished take on a citrus-green fragrance. Vivid citruses. Not revolutionary. SCORE: 60/100 Full bottle buy? NO, not at Roja's price point. Blind buy? NO, the herbal bitterness I get may not be appealing. And the price is prohibitive. Recommend? YES, but only if you love super vivid citruses and don't mind herbal/green accords. Date night? NO, it feels more sharp and herbal than romantic. Office safe? YES, it's professional and refined but I wouldn't enjoy sitting next to it at a meeting. Pros: It's a high quality, vivid citrus with Roja's expert blending. Elegant. Cons: Extremely expensive, feels dated despite being new, herbal bitterness isn't for me. Isola Verde feels like a solid, citrus fragrance. The more complex and WAY wealthier cousin to Sicily that people like less. This fragrance isn't bad, but it's extremely forgettable in the world of niche perfumery. The DNA is solid, and I think the citruses keep it interesting, but I wouldn't buy it, or even wear it frequently. Mediterranean, chic, clean, citrus that's enjoyable to smell. Occasionally. *Review #47 in my fragrance journey - this fragrance I own as a decant*

I put on two 2025 Rojas today: Oceania Parfum as my SOTD and Isola Verde as my SOTN, and my experience with each cannot be more different. Isola Verde is chock full of headache inducing aromachemicals, and any individual notes are completely lost in a musky haze. Vaguely sweet, creamy, green, floral? I don't really get any fruity notes strangely enough, even though that is the highest rated accord. Fruity notes would have some sharpness or sourness to them, there is nothing like that here. Just a wave of smooth sweetness that doesn't really go anywhere. Quality here is piss poor, with the composition/blending as well as with the individual materials. I couldn't even tell you what they were thinking selling this for $500. $100 would be too much for this scent. I suppose it lasts long, I guess they're charging you for the extended headache package. Probably the worst dollar-for-dollar scent in 2025, and with Kurky released this year, that's saying something.

I feel like there's a much bigger story around Isola Verde that isn't tied with the product itself. With Roja Dove officially out of the game (assuming you think he was the perfumer behind the brand's catalogue), the brand took a daring step forward by appointing Antoine Cotton, a perfumer with less than 3 years of full-time experience at Argeville, a French ingredients/flavors company. Cotton now has credits for 2 products, both released under the guise of the British brand, yet the start has been anything but smooth. Isola Verde is the 3rd product to be launched in the collection, coming off the success of Isola Blu Parfum and the underwhelm of Isola Sol . Interestingly, Isola Verde slots into the lineup with no overlap from either of the other two. Without looking at the listed notes or accords, the scent opens fresh-fruity and lightly synthetic. There is a very prominent tropical fruity feel that reminds me of mango, a genre that has had various hot launches in the past 3 years. However, I don't see strong overlap with any of those launches: Verde isn't as sweet as God of Fire as the freshness is more prominent, reminding me more of how Mind Games structured Blockade . On the other hand, there is a very interesting green feeling in the top that makes me think of nettles, giving it an aromatic mint-like feel, so in ways I can also compare this one-two to Unique'e Luxury's Mangonifiscent . Unfortunately there is a very prominent flaw with this product from start to finish and I'm not even talking about the performance or the price - I'm talking about the blending. Even after looking at the scent pyramid, I struggle to allocate the cause of the issue. Both in the top and in the dry-down, there is a very poorly incorporated musk somewhere in here. I am assuming the floral parts don't sit well with the ambroxan. Overall, I feel like the aromatic nettle-like parts are driven by the patchouli and the floral tones are fairly mild throughout. The scent's core DNA is tropical fruity & fresh, with green-woody-floral having their moments throughout the wearing experience (greener in the open, woody-floral base DNA in the dry-down). Performance is light with soft sillage and what appears to be longevity in the 4 hour area. The pricing is predictably offensive and even at grey market prices (assume 50% of RRP, so €230/50ml) this isn't a recommendable purchase. What I can't get over is the recent brand direction. Every release from Roja after 2023's Elysium Eau Intense has not only underdelivered, but has also completely missed the mark of what Roja as a brand used to be about. Even before Antoine Cotton took over, we were getting products like Aoud Extraordinaire which is a poor interpretation of a fruity musk. The brand has tried to hide behind products in the more premium price-point, sometimes with limited availability, with scents like Lost in Paris and Tea at BG , but even these are a distant memory of Roja's true top products. Fans are now stuck hoping Cotton can restore the brand's image, yet so far in, he is 0-for-2.

I have tested Roja Isola Verde several times and I must say, I am very positive about it. The perfume offers a strong opening with melon, mandarin, and guava dominating at first. After a while, a hint of musk can also be detected. In short, this is a beautiful fruity yet fresh scent that is really great for summer. On my skin, the perfume lasts about 7-8 hours, which is perfectly fine for a summer scent. In terms of price, Isola Verde is a bit expensive as it is priced at €465 for 50ml. Nevertheless, I truly believe that the purchase was worth it. I really don’t understand the hate, as it is simply perfect for summer, offering exactly what I envision in a summer perfume.

Loewe is one of those brands that tends to get lost in the perfume market. And if you look at the reviews of the original Solo, it’s probably for good reason. Now, "Aus Liebe zum Duft" sent me a sample of Solo Platinum, and I must say, reading the scent notes made me eager to test it. Even though I usually prefer to test flankers only after I know the originals for better comparison (that's why I've been postponing the Givenchy Play Intense test for weeks!) Leather, benzoin, pepper, tea - that sounds like my taste, and maybe there’s a surprise in store. But no, the fragrance has some good aspects that oscillate somewhere between ordinary mainstream and a hint of leather luxury, yet there are a few notes that make me furrow my brow and wrinkle my nose. Animalic sweat or urine notes appear in some absolute classics (I’m just saying Kouros or A*Men) and often serve their erotic purpose. When I take a short breath of Solo Platinum, it smells quite nice with soft leather on which a bit of tea has been sprinkled. But when I take a deep inhale, this intimate note comes through that you sometimes recognize from women. Not pleasant at all, and I’m not sure if it’s sexy or serves its purpose. I have serious doubts about that. And I have no idea which unknown ingredient in me evokes this silly association - maybe the Siamese benzoin. But then it should smell different from the typical Le Male benzoin. It’s all interesting, and the environment usually doesn’t take such a deep breath close to the skin. But still, there are far better leather fragrances, and the scent doesn’t live up to what I had hoped for with some of my favorite ingredients! The bottle is nice, even if Loewe is a bit heavy-handed with the name. The sillage is fine, and the fragrance pairs well with a modern leather jacket. Longevity is good at 8 hours, already meeting a decent quality standard. On one hand, it’s totally ordinary and standard everywhere, but then there’s a strange, animalic wannabe-sexy note lurking in the background!

It is going to be a struggle for me to say anything about the fragrance itself, because Aoud Extraordinaire serves as an insult to the intelligence of niche fragrance hobbyists all around the world. Strap in, this is going to be a slaughter. Before even spraying the fragrance, the price tag of €720/100ml sets the expectation high, yet when putting it on, you are met with off-the-charts levels of disappointment. Aoud Extraordinaire opens as a very generic fruity fragrance with a creamy-sweet structure and some floral nuances. Essentially, the scent is adjacent to the fruitchouli profile traditionally worn by women and does not have any separable edge in the air over fragrances that can be found for as little as €20-30. Relative to these cheapies, the Roja will obviously outshine them for blend quality, given the lack of synthetic edges, but that clearly is not enough to warrant purchasing this product. There is no significant evolution as the scent dries either: the fruits eventually are equaled by various floral notes with vanilla, musk and white florals making up the ultimate base structure. Like many other products in the line, the oud qualities here are not well pronounced and the scent has zero oriental/woody feel for several hours. Accords: fruity-creamy-sweet-floral But most of all, what Aoud Extraordinaire showcases is that their feminine fragrances within the Aoud line need influencers pushing it over social media. Much like Enigma Aoud Parfum , this fragrance was sent out in PR as it was predictable it would be a flop. Now those same people are not only trying to upsell us on this dead average product, but also on fruity-floral fragrances being unisex - when has this category ever been viewed as something to be sold to male consumers? That makes it impossible to take Roja's marketing outlet seriously, because the concept of integrity is completely lost on these dishonest parties. Ultimately, we have a product that, albeit not synthetic, still suffers from numerous amounts of products: generic profile, no blend upside, very high price point, mediocre performance (intimate-to-arms length sillage + 5-6 hour longevity), being pushed by people who'd never buy it etc. But perhaps the most puzzling part is why would the brand even put this out? Roja appears to be trying to target female consumers with a majority of their releases in 2024 (Elysium pour Femme in 2 concentrations, Isola Sol , Aoud Extraordinaire and maybe even Lost in Paris ), yet nothing is sticking. Creed is trying to diversify their portfolio in the same way, but brands should never forget the hand that feeds them - when the core of the catalogue is driven by scents targeting the men's market, there's only so much to be achieved with a pivot like this and if you do pivot, it needs to be a home-run, not a three-and-out like the one Roja has here.

This fragrance has received very mixed reviews, and some of the reasons I completely understand, some I don't. Of Roja's latest releases, Isola Sol (you can find my review) and this one are the ones that have caused a lot of emotional turmoil. I think the biggest reason in both cases is the name, although personally, the name Isola Sol fits the scent quite well (more on that in the review of that particular scent). Aoud Extraordinaire , on the other hand, as a name, gives a completely different picture of what the fragrance contains and if you are very inexperienced with Roja's fragrances, then I understand the disappointment. However, if you consider the other fragrances in the Aoud collection, then Aoud as a word in Roja's fragrances has never meant a heavy, challenging Oud, so why would it here? Take Enigma Aoud Parfum for example, which is one of the most beautiful and elegant clear fruity fragrances: the amount of Oud in it is also minimal, but just right to bring the necessary depth to both the peachy scent and the peachy soft powdery character. I think the bigger issue is the word "Extraordinaire" since for many of us Chypré Extraordinaire is the best Chypre in that style, in that category ( Diaghilev Parfum , Femme (1989) Eau de Toilette , Mitsouko Extrait , Jubilation 25 Woman Eau de Parfum etc.) and the combination of those two words "Aoud" and "Extraordinaire" made many of us think and imagine some very special Oud scent, possibly distinctly oriental, and it led to huge disappointments and emotions because it wasn't. Aoud Extraordinaire opens up with an intense cocktail of fruits, with only Pineapple clearly standing out first. It also blends in very quickly with the others. As the fragrance develops, the clear fruity aroma fades slightly and the huge floral bouquet typical of Roja takes the stage. The heady scent of the flowers remains under the fruity veil for an hour, yet creating an elegant and adult style to the scent from the beginning. When you add to this a complex base, where depth and a subtle darkness as well as softness and sweetness come from many notes, it is very difficult to find a similar concoction (or even close) in existing fruity fragrances. I am happy to get suggestions, because fruity fragrances have been difficult for me precisely because they are either too youthful, too clearly juicy fruity, too simple and/or shockingly synthetic. Most often, fruity fragrances combine all of the things I mentioned. If there is something comparable, it is unlikely to be at the cheapest end of the spectrum, and I personally don't need it, because quality rarely comes cheap. If this fragrance were a simple fruity scent, if it only had the top notes with some musky base, then it would be generic. However, this fragrance is much more than that. There are no three dramatically clear phases in the fragrance, but there is usually nothing more in Roja's fragrances, but all the scents are skillfully, elegantly and ingeniously mixed. However, those phases are always distinguishable. If you are familiar with Roja, Aoud in the name or Oud in the ingredients does not necessarily make the fragrance an Oriental, so I will mention it now so that this does not cause disappointment or misunderstanding. Don't expect overly sweet or clear Cotton Candy or Caramel either since they don't perform in that kind of way. Caramel for example is not like in Lost in Paris . As the fragrance progresses to the 1.5 hour mark, the abundance of fruit fades into the background, while still maintaining the irresistible tropical undertone like the vibrant and luminous vibe as well that fruits give to this style of fragrance. The scent is also extremely unisex, thanks to the deep, intense and Ambery base, and it is not too sweet at all, thanks to the floral heart. On my husband's skin, the leather and Vetiver come through more than on mine, which partly changes the experience of the scent. The texture is extremely thick but I don't find it creamy. Fruity scents can also easily be made too strong, making simple scents tawdry and somehow girly, while such a dense and rich scent like this would feel suffocating, even though the quality is the best. Although at first I myself thought that the scent should project more, this way it is more versatile, especially for the work environment. Personally, I love this luxurious, golden, energetic scent and especially the phase it develops into after an hour, which lasts 6-7 hours. On clothes, the scent lasts forever. Fruits are always welcome in my fragrances, as long as they are not clearly edible or drinkable and are part of a more complex blend like they are here. This is definitely not that typical feminine fruity scent and if you are sampling this one, please give it at least a couple of full wears. The magic really happens when the aroma of all those fruits fades. First, this didn't made that kind of wow effect like for example Turandot Parfum , Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2019) , Chypré Extraordinaire or some others did but there is not this kind of scent in Roja's catalog so after the initial astonishment I started to like it a lot and I found there some kind of vintage style complexity that you find in 80s floral fragrances. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

Hello everyone, when I heard a few weeks ago that the fragrance was supposed to come out soon, my anticipation was really huge! A friend of mine immediately bought a bottle (Roja lover for over 10 years) and I received a larger sample for testing. My expectations - Preface: I am a fan of certain fragrances from the brand, although many of them have their origins in the past and my batches are usually a bit older.... (different topic), but when I read the name "Aoud Extraordinaire | Roja Parfums," my excitement was great. Why? On one hand, I am a big fan of the old (!) and classic Aoud and the old (!) "Chypré Extraordinaire | Roja Parfums." And I hoped that they would combine the best of both worlds... Result + Test! My anticipation and my wish, as well as my expectation, lasted until the test, and already with the first spray, I was shocked..., but let's leave it for xx minutes and hours and repeat this process x times to rule out certain sources of error and form a certain opinion.... So, many Rojas start quite similarly, and this is certainly nothing new in that regard; it is also KNOWN, in the sense of citrusy, fruity, and floral, and it does that. So far so good, however, in my opinion, there is already a disturbing component, and it is the "artificial" and really noticeable, somewhat unpleasant sweetness... .There will likely be some people who like exactly that, but it is not for me, and I honestly find this phase unpleasant. After that, we have the floral heart note, and it is, for me, the best phase (by far) of the fragrance. Floral, clean, and the slightly fluffy musk from the base is already coming through. It is nothing new from the brand, but something tried and tested + good... Now to the heart note, and here .... well, some things were done wrong / implemented incorrectly, and the name does NOT fit the fragrance - let me explain! When I think of Roja Aoud, I think of rose and oud, and when I think of Extraordinaire, we quickly get to flowers, chypre with a certain twist, and when we combine both, a picture emerges x...., right? And what do we get? An Aoud without Oud - I really don't perceive any woods. I'm not even saying that there aren't any (in the structure or background, certainly), but they never come through noticeably, and I find that really disappointing. And the worse thing, in my opinion, is this constant and sometimes inappropriate and almost annoying sweetness, which I find unsuitable and unpleasant! And when I combine all this and look at it and evaluate it, then... - way too expensive - name pure marketing - expected much more (+ wished) H/S: Good, nothing more. Unisex? I would say it leans more towards feminine! When + where: I find this very difficult, as the noticeable sweetness can quickly become annoying... I do NOT see it in a classic office setting. More like outside while shopping from the end of September to April! Recommend? PLEASE test it and then decide! And now have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______ (Now the same as almost always - because it applies!) Now to the topic of luxury: As you can see in part from my profile, I have really smelled many fragrances, and there are fragrances where you can smell a certain (sometimes) strong synthetic quality, and you quickly realize that some fragrance houses focus more on quantity than quality, and there are some where you can tell, "oh come on, let's put in more + better stuff," and you can smell that at the end of the day. A brief word on the topic of packaging, bottle, sprayer: I'll keep it short; I give a 10 out of 10 in every category, and I know very well that tastes are very different. So anyone who honestly rates this with a 7 or less... - PHEW. Beautiful and very high-quality cap, nice timeless bottle design, etc.... so I find it very hard to rate it differently, and I say this not because I like or dislike a brand! Now a short note on my opinion: I am not sponsored, influenced by anyone, receiving money or anything else. I approach the topic of perfume as I am, being honest; everything else is not my style. My true personal opinion is very VALUABLE to me, and I hope maybe ;) that this is noticeable. If I don't like something, like packaging, bottle, sprayer, or H/S, I will communicate that too!

Hello dear community, Starting with such a wonderful fragrance is always a good question. Especially with Roja, this is particularly difficult, as we are presented with a masterpiece of fragrance art 95% of the time, which is also very complex! Typical for Roja, the opening is again rocket-like. The opening is fruity, floral, and has a subtle sweetness that I find very pleasant. Clearly standing out are the main players, which for my nose are unmistakably: pineapple, peach, bergamot, and plum. After the first 15-20 minutes, the floral notes join in a very pleasant and not overly feminine way. I particularly like the combination of lily of the valley, orange blossom, and jasmine. The rose, on the other hand, I perceive only lightly and in the background, which I really like, because we already know enough about a prominent rose from Roja! (in my opinion) A pleasant touch of leather, vanilla, woods, and very delicate oud also joins in and completes the picture. Musk, amber, and vetiver can only be faintly sensed later in the drydown, which I actually find quite pleasant. A fruity, floral touch remains throughout, which is neither too feminine nor too sweet or too sour, but is very balanced and authentic to my nose. Of course, the classic Roja DNA remains a prominent part of this fragrance composition... Who would expect otherwise? ;)) Later in the drydown, the fragrance gradually becomes woodier, deeper, and less fruity. The floral notes, however, persist until the "bitter" end. All in all, once again a very successful Roja fragrance! It is truly special, striking, and as the name promises: Extraordinaire! I see little similarity to, for example, City of Stars or "Dubai - Ajyal | Nabeel." If anything, more to "Dubai - Ajyal | Nabeel," although these two fragrances mentioned above can only be compared quite imprecisely, as the direction differs quite significantly. Longevity and sillage are, as with most Roja fragrances, very good! On my skin, the fragrance lasts around 8-10 hours with about four sprays, and the projection is also very good! The price, however, remains a topic... It is basically the same as always; everyone has to know whether it is worth the money to them and whether they find the price justified. In my opinion, the price here is quite inflated, typical for Roja. Yes, you get a beautiful, elegant, unique, and complex work of art, but I believe a few euros less would be appropriate. Currently, we are looking at a price of €720.00 for 100ml. For Roja standards, not the absolute pinnacle, yet still a proud sum that one must be able to afford/want. All in all, I can say that yet again a wonderful fragrance is on the market that should please every Roja lover and will certainly find its way into many collections in the future. It is worth testing, whether you are a Roja fan or not! Therefore, I can only say, as always, enjoy the test and……… Thank you for your attention and stay decent ;)

It seems Roja wanted to follow the mainstream and now present his vision of a fruity scent. After testing it for a few days, I already have my first impression. I’m happy to share it with you :) At the start, there are many tropical fruits with a recognizable apple note. But I don’t want to eat these fruits; they smell a bit synthetic to my nose.

Aoud Extraordinaire is a fragrance that somehow leaves me with a few question marks. Somehow, the scent has beautiful facets, but it also has some really unpleasant sides. As is typical for Roja, we definitely get lovely citrus-fruity and floral notes. However, there is a perceived synthetic quality in here that I find quite strange and not at all typical for Roja.

In the opening, it reminds me of MFK Kurky, but with even more sweet, synthetic, and tropical fruits. Super sweet and cotton candy/Tropifrutti vibes, but in the drydown, it becomes beautifully creamy, and the sweet as well as tropical accords become more subtle and rounded. The first 30 minutes: flop, but after that: top.

As soon as this beautiful fragrance is sprayed, one perceives a pleasant but extraordinary fruitiness, primarily peach, pineapple, and pear. However, once this scent reaches the drydown, everyone I have shown this fragrance to experiences the WOW factor. A sweet, creamy, rich - yet still fruity scent emerges, which will delight any fruit fan.

I like it much more then the original. It is not so sickening sweet, not so in your face. QQQ was my formal wear go to scent, I will now switch to Pasion! Longevity is fine on my skin, sillage is fine for being in a crowed or work. You can always spray it on cloths or a scarf if you want it to last longer. Or moisturize before applying. It develops in more stages then the QQQ original, it is not as "flat". Must try in my eyes :)

I was really excited to try the new version of Loewes-Quizás, Quizás, Quizás and i must say i'm a bit disappointed. The scent is not bad at all but i thought it would be better. The opening is really really fresh and Citrus like, i smell a lot of Bergamot and alcohol. When this fades away i also get some Flowers like Fressia and Magnolia it turns into a soft and pretty scent it's a bit spicy/woody too. But this scent is not really overwhelmingly or powerful. It last not such a long time. I prefer the Original Quizás, Quizás, Quizás.

Yesterday, my perfume sales associate handed me a sample of Quizas Pasion, asking me to listen to the song Quizas, Quizas, Quizas on YouTube while spraying the fragrance. I like this idea of drawing attention to the right music with fragrances, as I also enjoy associating aromas with melodies. Recently, I was kindly given a classical CD with a perfume purchase. That should become a trend. Of course, I followed Ms. P's advice - and listened to a soulful rumba. A dance that comes from the hips, with a touch of eroticism. I would also like to gently "sway" with a smart dance partner to this fragrance. The bergamot is fresh, but the red berries provide an interesting tart counterpoint. Freesia and magnolia are bright floral notes, but are softly muted by smoky cashmere wood. Amber and vetiver represent the smoothness of the fragrant dance. Quizas is an alluring "Maybe" - the word that adds spice to a flirt. And I also feel skillfully "flirted with" by the fragrance. An aroma, more intense than the most erotic caresses - proclaims the cover. I will fire up YouTube again, and with this scent, dare to dance with my husband. Let's see what happens. The magic word is "Maybe".

The original from Quizás, Quizás, Quizás is well-known to me - at least as an EdT - because I once owned a 50ml bottle of it. However, I used the fragrance quite rarely; somehow it didn’t quite fit me. It was too harsh and too "masculine" to be my scent. Quizás, Quizás, Quizás Pasión is the daughter and shows corresponding facets. In the opening, the berry fruits dominate, and it truly smells just like a good champagne with cassis - a Kir Royal! Very juicy, berry-like, fresh, and natural. A real appetizer that makes your mouth water. Despite the flowers, it doesn’t become cloyingly floral in the heart note. The flowers cleverly blend with the berries, giving the fragrance a very nice and very wearable accord. Lively, youthful, passionate, and sparkling. Quite early on, an animalistic note emerges and "moves" the fragrance in the background. I would have guessed musk, although amber is mentioned here in the pyramid. Interestingly, the animalistic aspect disappears in the base; on the contrary, it is quite dry, only very faintly sweet, and shows a slightly green bitterness, underlined by fruity berry notes. Cashmere wood seems to be used rather sparingly here, as the base does show a certain woody note, reminiscent of sandalwood, but lacks the cloying sweetness of cashmere wood. Quizás, Quizás, Quizás Pasión is comparable to Flowerbomb EdT but significantly less sweet and clearly fruitier than that. Euphoria and Forbidden Euphoria also go in this direction. Nevertheless, Quizás, Quizás, Quizás Pasión has something unique, more natural, happier, and less sweet-sticky than its two competitors. A very refreshing and lively everyday scent that is wearable for young people of any gender.

H - The Exclusive Parfum pour Homme I bought blindly in the hope of finding a better and more noble Tom Ford Plum Japonais, as that has unfortunately been discontinued. Unfortunately, this also applies to H - The Exclusive Parfum pour Homme, but at least this one is still available. Roja fragrances generally don't have it easy with me, as some may know. The price always triggers facial paralysis for me. This is no different with H - The Exclusive Parfum pour Homme, but here I could somehow justify the expenditure for my inner self. H - The Exclusive Parfum pour Homme is a delicately fruity, fresh, and oriental scent. I couldn't really detect the freshness of the top note, but that didn't bother me much here. H - The Exclusive Parfum pour Homme starts off with the plum, which is gently accompanied by oud. For me, oud and plum are the main players here. The other notes in the base note rather soften the oud and create a gentle framework around the whole thing. I can perceive woods, patchouli, amber, and sandalwood, but I couldn't identify the vetiver and the pepper note. The longevity is in a good range with 9-10 hours; it could have been a bit more. However, I find the sillage rather disappointing. Here, the sillage is more like an arm's length away and after about 6 hours, it's already very close to the skin. I really expected more in this case. I only accept this because the scent has absolutely blown me away; otherwise, it would have already ended up in the souk for that reason.

Yesterday, I went to the opera Carmen by Bizet. Great production and cast, and for me, a welcome occasion to wear H - The Exclusive Parfum pH. One could certainly have chosen another fragrance, but I assumed it might fit. And yes, it fit. I could hardly perceive the top note. While the citrusy start is noticeable, the plum kicks in very early, and the citrus notes and sweet, juicy ripe plum wrestle for a while. During this phase, I was uncertain; it didn't smell really good at first. But then the plum takes over. It doesn’t remind me of plum jam, as that includes spices that the Exclusive Parfum does not contain. It's more like the plum compote made from real plums that I loved eating at my grandmother's house as a child, and the most delicious part was slurping the juice from the polished glass bowls. Rockrose and plum engage in a wonderful interplay. And this with a lot of power and emphasis. As the romantic entanglements of Carmen and the until then exemplary and duty-bound soldier Don José tightened, woody notes, a slightly leathery oud, and piercing vetiver burst into the plum-rockrose harmony. Similar to the proud torero Escamillo, who, with his appearance, quickly brought an end to the love happiness of the two protagonists. And it may sound overly sentimental, but now the fragrance really turns up, just like the plot. Plum, rockrose, oud, and at times warmer and at times sharper notes from wood and vetiver vie for attention. That’s exactly what I love about complex fragrances; a slight movement of the body, and a different note comes forward, only to be replaced by another fragrance note in the next moment. But the fruity plum always returns, providing a harmonious balance. Hardly anyone in my row at the opera, including two rows in front and behind me, could have perceived Carmen as a Bohemia working in a cigarette factory after this evening (or can one still say gypsy in relation to an opera?). After this evening, the culture enthusiasts were surely convinced they had met Carmen as a picker in the love tangle on an Andalusian plum plantation. This Exclusive Parfum has many elements that excite me. It remains on my wish list, and I will probably always associate this fragrance with the opera. And thanks to its strong sillage, probably not just me.

Like the Atlas, but worse: you take away that incense-like background note, that mischievousness of the neroli and orange blossom, and that thunderous opening note with the mandarin, creating a soapy scent that lasts for five hours at most. One gave you a spring scent, this one, well, something you already know.

This scent is unbelievable. Though Loewe's are generally a fantastic-smelling fragrances, this perfume is something beyond 'good and evil'. Well... we all are different and someone may even like it, but I strongly believe that there is a good portion of people that would be simply left without ability to speak (and inhale) for a time. You know when there is a scorching day, the sun is burning the skin, and you are amid the crowd that burns something resinous and spicy, so that you are balancing between wanting to throw up or passing out due to lack of oxygen? The Vulcan can help you to embrace the feeling! Maybe the first few seconds are OK, but then something really terrible happens to my nose and lungs... MAYBE, you'd like it as an individual. YET, I'm sure it is not a crowd-pleaser. Careful!

Absolutely intoxicating. Smells like an evening out in the steppes after a wildfire burns a part of them out. It's warm, it's just a little humid now that the scorching sun is finally setting down, there's but a hint of bitter smoke in the air. Orange blossom is very intense compared to the other notes, but it's not sweet at all. At least not on me or my partner. It's sharp, fresh, and contrasts beautifully with its thick herbal backdrop. The scent can be overpowering in the beginning, especially if you apply it too liberally. The initial cloud has a very realistic bitter and almost smoky quality – pretty much identical to the smell of burnt grasses after a wildfire. I understand why it might not be everyone's cup of tea, but I find it mesmerizing. 10/10. I usually do 1 spray, which mellows out and plateaus in about 30 minutes and stays consistently delightful for the next ~4 hours. Takes a relatively warm season (or a cozy indoor setting) to shine though. Cold winter weather neutralizes most of the herbs and cheapens the citrus notes. Should be perfect for the warm parts of spring and autumn; but will work great in the summer too, if applied in moderation.

What a shame that this amazing perfume was discontinued! The scent opens with lemon, May rose and almonds A perfume for women but it is truly unisex! The scent has nuances of " Amber Aoud" our just with the addition of almonds I really love this scent, so elegant and so sensual at the same time For me : 8 /10

My opinion is that this perfume is better than the roja aoud and roja amber aoud. It has a nice, not strong flowery touch to it which makes it soft and classy. It don´t always need to be a nuclear perfume to make it a great scent.

For days the sky was gray, the air damp and cold, transitioning from November to December. Light was missing, the gray blanket hung heavily over the city. People hurried along, bent and introspective. Then, one morning, the sky was suddenly bright, covered with a fluffy white layer through which a winter sun cast its soft and blurred milky light. I stood there in awe, gazing at this shimmering spectacle, unable to take my eyes off this sky; it was as if a fairy had waved her magic wand, and you could still see the silver sparkles that had escaped. The sky was covered as if with gauze or the finest silk, through which the milk of winter light scattered. The noise around me suddenly fell silent, and in the middle of the city, I felt as if I were in a fairy tale, believing I could hear delicate, soft sounds from afar; for a moment, everything stood still. There are moments that are so surprising in their beauty that one is momentarily catapulted out of space and time. That’s how I felt when I experienced this fragrance for the first time. This shimmering light, this finesse, delicacy, and yet strength, the coolness resting on a warm layer. I don’t even want to dissect the scent, although I perceive the citrus notes, the wonderful flowers that are so light and fluttery, hardly sweet perhaps due to the iris, yet held on this warm bed of the finest oud, sandalwood, musk, powder, and amber. The colors for me are bright violet, pink, silver, white, and cream, and as a base, all shades of violet, gold, and blue. The music that represents the mood for me is Grieg’s Peer Gynt Suite No. 1. I had a friend try the fragrance; she was so surprised, an Aaah escaped her as she took her nose from her hand, she was enchanted. I can only express my admiration for this masterpiece, and I am grateful to experience it.

In a blind swap, I managed to get a new bottle of Ahlam... I had never smelled Ahlam before, but somehow I had the feeling that I might like it based on the ingredients.... Do you know that feeling when curiosity is greater than reason? Well, the swap was already finalized, and after what felt like an eternity of waiting, it finally arrived... Ahlam - still in its plastic wrap - shone at me... My fingers were tingling... that wonderful feeling when you can finally take a bottle out of the wrap and packaging.... I love that ;-) Thoughts were racing: "What if I don't like it...." ---- "A blind swap with Roja fragrances can really go wrong or cost a lot...." ---- "And what if it stinks..." --- "Aah, careful with the plastic..." --- "It has rhubarb in it, I don't even like that" --- "You probably didn't look at the fragrance pyramid closely enough, did you" --- "What if it's really as sweet as someone said here...." --- "Ahlam, what does that actually mean" --- "Floral-sweet - not necessarily my type" --- "Open the box: ooooh it shines so beautifully" ..... Taken out of the beautiful golden packaging, from the velvet bed, a sweet and high-quality bottle - just like Roja... Then the big moment: took off the pretty stone cap and sprayed a little on my wrist.....
