Thoughts racing again: "There's lemon, I can recognize flowers: Ylang-Ylang and jasmine are very clear" --- "fresh and floral..." --- oh, marzipan or almond is super clear: not sticky or gooey - more fluffy and sweet... --- "Oud comes in, not stinky oud..." --- "wow, how beautiful..." --- "oh, it really is beautiful..." --- Yes, the blind swap was a good choice..." --- "mmmmh, there's a bit of powdery fluff coming..." --- "that could be sandalwood, creamy-woody-noble..." --- "Damn, there are only 30ml in the bottle..." --- "Is there a bigger size...." --- "www.Roja.com - Search: Ahlam...." --- "ooh, 100ml - - - - 295.- £..." --- "Damn..." --- "Salary just came in yesterday...." --- "Shopping cart - add...." --- "Ahww should I or shouldn't I...." --- "Order finger twitches" --- "Don't you want to use the 30ml first..." --- "Confirm..." --- "I wonder how long delivery will take..." Yes, who among you doesn't know that...? Sometimes addiction overtakes reason, pushes it aside, and races to the finish line.... I really like Ahlam, even though it is a rather sweet oriental :-) The bottle with the pretty stone cap, as always with Roja: top-notch Longevity: in the upper range Sillage: right after spraying: suuuper, but after about 15-20 minutes it diminishes a bit and Ahlam pulls back somewhat. Compared to other Rojas, it is rather "subtle" Addiction has won, and I am happy ;-)

I am a little bit obsessed with this fragrance. I love it more and more with each wear. I crave it and want to be drowsed in it all the time. It is soft but long-lasting on me. It is delicate, elegant, and sweet, but not overly so. It is incredibly smooth. It is powdery, floral, with a beautiful woody base. This comes from a person who does not like woody scents. It bewitches me. I adore catching whiffs of it throughout the day. At first, when I received 51, I was quite indifferent to it, and then the magic happened. I adore it now!

I had ordered the Discovery Set from Roja, which included 51 Essence de Parfum as a manufacturer sample. I liked the scent, but H+S was very low. By chance, I then saw that a Souk partner was offering a sharing for 51 Parfum at a great price (compared to the original). At that time, Roja had reduced the price of 51 Parfum by 50%, and the Souk partner seized the opportunity. I ordered a decant from that and must say: I am appalled! The scent is just as heavenly as in 51 Essence de Parfum : in the top and heart, a lovely blend of bergamot, jasmine, lily of the valley, May rose, and tuberose. I perceive a minimal amount of raspberry, gardenia, and orange blossom. Later, a bit of sweet vanilla, sandalwood, and minimal patchouli come in. The iris and violets make the scent slightly powdery (I don't find it creamy). Anise and clove only waft through the scent with a hint. So everything is very nice for my nose. But: The longevity and sillage seem even lower than with the "Essence," which is not an essence of pure perfume, but of Eau de Parfum and should therefore contain less perfume concentration. Considering the original price that Roja charges for "51 (Parfum) | Roja Parfums," namely over 700 euros, this is simply an outrage! I cannot recommend this perfume!

With the first spray, I perceive a sweetness, specifically a sweetness that comes from sugar water, not an overpowering heavy sweetness, rather a very subtle sweetness spiced with bergamot and possibly even a hint of anise. This scent perception reminds me of something from long ago, perhaps some candies on the shelf of a forgotten, no longer existing corner shop, where the scents of laundry detergent, soap, cleaning products, shoe polish, sticky-sweet treats, vegetables, old iron, etc. mix in one room. This little cloud of fragrance is so beautiful, I sniff and sniff and don’t want to stop, unfortunately, I cannot hold onto it. It transforms and becomes somewhat creamy, lightly dry-powdery-creamy, powdery is rather cautiously expressed. The heart note is a play of flowers, with a veil of orange blossoms hovering above, ensuring that the individual floral scents do not explode or take a solo journey through the heart note; however, the lily occasionally finds a loophole and peeks out like a mole, throwing up sand hills that transition into benzoin and vanilla before diving back down. A gourmand touch, sometimes gentle, sometimes more pronounced, is present. The lily stands out to me the most, reminding me very much of Baiser Vole; I also recognize tuberose, but not piercing, rather gentle and soft, a beautifully tamed tuberose, the interplay of tuberose, sandalwood, and benzoin, similar to Queens/Bond No.9. The base has something of Grand Soir, but not as unsweet; and genes of Amber Star, but not as deep and intense as in Amber Star, rather delicate and reserved, flat vanilla and benzoin, quiet, subtle, shy, and raspberry floats along. I tested it last night. I then fell asleep on the couch, and when I woke up after about 3 hours around 11 PM, I couldn't get my nose away from my forearm. Amber Star genes with raspberry pudding, very gentle and mild. This morning, I immediately put my nose back to my arm, but there was nothing left, nada. I have often tested it in the evening, overnight. Many were still clearly perceptible in the morning, Grand Soir, cologne pour le soir as an example, and Absolue pour le soir, which you can't get rid of at all. But 51 Parfum had disappeared, what a pity! It becomes increasingly weak on the skin, but it is still recognizable in my scarf. A very beautiful, dreamy scent, unfortunately quite short-lived, a poor testament for an expensive Roja. I will still praise, honor, cherish, and care for it.

If I had to crank out dozens of new body mists every year, then maybe I would have a few duds too. Pink Macaron is so odd and cheap and smells like plastic. It also instantly evaporates from my skin. I would recommend this for a gym bag, but I have so many better mists for that purpose. I WILL say that there is an every so slight coconut hint that reminds me of a macaron. If that was intentional, then that's pretty cool. Otherwise, I wouldn't get this one blind.

If you, like me, grew up in a more "rural" environment, at some point you start to question whether you want to stay there or not. I can clearly remember that I always enjoyed my stays with my aunt in Berlin immensely. The differences between my East Westphalian hometown and the ever-bustling metropolis couldn't have been greater. Therefore, it became clear to me relatively early on that I am probably more of a city person with a distinct tendency towards big cities. So it’s no surprise that I am a big fan of city trips. I always find it exciting to gain very different impressions and meet regionally diverse people, and even get to know some of them. And when the company Loewe also launches fragrances titled "A Walk through Madrid," I am inherently interested. Due to my more than positive experience with "Un Paseo por Madrid - El cielo sobre la Plaza de Oriente," my curiosity was piqued by "Un Paseo por Madrid - Un balcón sobre el Paseo del Prado." Since saffron, amber, and iris have long been fragrant temptations for me (and recently oud has also been allowed to join in), I was very curious to see how this Loewe fragrance would turn out. To get straight to the point: The city tour through Madrid from Plaza de Oriente to the world-famous Prado Museum should not end in a dead end. From the very first moment, the included oud is present. However, it does not have any medically piercing and/or intensely oriental characteristics, for which I am very grateful. Instead, it initially appears cool and somewhat androgynous. The iris, too, reminds me a bit of the "Hiris" iris from Hermès at this stage. But both the oud and the iris gain warmth and depth as the fragrance develops, although this Loewe fragrance does not become a cuddly scent. I can distinctly smell the fine saffron; the rose appears to me only as a softly scented shadow of itself (for which I am grateful, as I am not currently fond of roses in fragrances). Ylang-ylang gently lays beneath the iris and oud, softening their initial coolness in a pleasant way. Overall, the transitions in this fragrance are very fluid. Oud and iris are permanently present for me, while all other components come and go in varying degrees. I quite like this, as it keeps the fragrance in motion, making it feel dynamic rather than static. The amber contributes a pleasant warmth but does not overshadow the two main protagonists. More and more, the musk begins to assert itself. Bright and unsoapy, it rushes forward - and from this point on, this fragrance reminds me of "Amber Aoud" by Roja Parfums. While "Amber Aoud" is, in my view, an absolute "fragrance club" (and I mean that positively; I love the scent), the Spanish counterpart comes across a bit quieter and more subtle. Both fragrances ultimately lead me to a base of the finest oud, amber, and musk. Incredibly successful, infinitely noble, infinitely elegant and sophisticated. Despite the similarity, "Un Paseo por Madrid - Un balcón sobre el Paseo del Prado" is its own distinct fragrance with a lot of depth and character. It has (with normal dosage) no overpowering sillage, but is still naturally perceptible, making it suitable even for the office (which I wouldn’t consider a suitable setting for "Amber Aoud"). And it is a loyal companion, clinging to me for an incredible 12 - 16 hours, a "tough beast" that even withstands showers and hand cream applications almost unscathed. In this sense, I would describe it as rather introverted, whereas the Roja fragrance is the exact opposite and comes across as more boisterous. But boisterous with style. All in all, "Un Paseo por Madrid - Un balcón sobre el Paseo del Prado" completely convinced me, as it is simply a very finely composed fragrance that exhibits a certain understated quality, making it appear mature and superior. To all those for whom Roja's "Amber Aoud" is a bit too much, you should definitely test this Loewe. Also, in terms of price, the Loewe at €165 for 100ml is significantly below the Roja fragrance. In my rating, I wavered for a long time between 90% and 100%, but then, true to the motto "In doubt for the accused," I decided on the full score because it simply convinced me. OK, it would deserve a point deduction for the painfully long name, but the fragrance can’t really be blamed for that ;-)

I love love love perfumes with oud. It has now become a frenzy amongst perfumers to use oud in literally most of their perfumes. Alshain starts off with beautiful note and ends with gorgeous dry down that lasts well into next day. I live in London hence I was able to get it from Harrods where this perfume is exclusive to Harrods only, but I am sure one can get directly from Terenzi in Italy or even from Harrods as they offer international shipping. Any oud lovers out there, this is a must if you can get your hands on it.

…today, you smell like shampoo. Right off the bat: I have never smelled anything like this before! As already hinted in the title, there are countless fragrances that smell like shower gel, and most of them are solid representatives of their kind. However, here Terenzi takes a, at least for me, new approach. And even if it’s only a slightly shorter path to reach for shampoo instead of shower gel, the olfactory distance could hardly be greater! For instead of solid and "just-no-experiments," we transition here to a rapidly changing fragrance experience. At the beginning, there’s a gummy sweet-freshness. As indicated in the fragrance pyramid, the fresh notes of the top note. And even though the base from the fragrance pyramid suggests a floral bouquet, it reminds me more of a fruit basket! In the drydown, finally, the already mentioned shampoo vibes! An effect that musk often evokes. The oud provides the scalp note under the shampoo. And even though it becomes slightly animalistic because of this, it still remains fresh-fruity-lightly sweet-shampoo-like. Perhaps that’s also why it’s a rather feminine scent. I will still keep it for now; as the fragrance DNA is absolute new territory for my nose.

That's what my husband called it when he smelled it. To be precise he said, "Phew! Old lady, almost dead--inches from the grave!" Impolite, if you ask me, but accurate nonetheless. Naturally, I forgive the designer who made Haute Luxe (aka Roja), unsurpassed to date in my personal experience of perfume.

I am not keen on this version of gardenia. Its nothing spectacular, just like any other white floral scent. It is extremely difficult to imitate the real gardenia scent from nature. Sadly Roja has failed in this version. To me, personally i don't think any gardenia perfume out there can beat vintage Tuvache Jungle Gardenia. Second best would be vintage quadruple gardenia by Richard Hudnut, followed by vintage gardenia by Lucien Lelong, then again vintage gardenia by Houbigant and lastly velvet gardenia by Tom Ford. I am a big fan of Roja Dove but this one definitely failed to impress my senses. Sorry Roja!

This one seems to suffer on my skin from the same problem of another in this extrait line, lilac. Both start with intense aromas and go to discreet scents very soon. This is more a jasmine and tuberose composition, it lacks the odd notes in gardenia reproductions. It smells fruity, sirupy and rich at first, then it gets a little bit tart with a rose apparation that last some minutes. Then it ends in a very close to skin musky and woody base, which is a disappointment in such an expensive and exquisite fragrance. Honestly, it's the roja dove that i liked the least so far.

…… and I could say: Phew, the scent leaves me completely indifferent and awakens no desires. But no, my madness of purchasing a sample for 24 euros (!) will not be forgiven so easily. The opening is overwhelming: It smells floral, spicy, citrusy, bitter, and sweet all at once. WOW!! It clears my nose all the way to the farthest corner of my sense organ. After a short time, “Gardenia” becomes increasingly floral and lush. How does the fragrance manage to be lush but not cloying, overwhelming but not intrusive, filling the room but not suffocating? I can’t identify any individual components apart from something resinous-herbaceous and something spicy (clove? cinnamon? star anise?). It is a perfect floral wonder! It may sound silly, but “Gardenia” is not white for me; it is orange-amber and radiant. And yes, it is a perfectly formed, fully bloomed gardenia at the peak of its beauty and fragrance! So, what do I do now? Unfortunately, I didn’t know that Rojas are so incredibly expensive! This morning, I already scrutinized my collection with a stern look and mentally calculated the financing of various perfumes for the distant future. Let’s see, maybe I’ll get lucky and by then my taste in fragrances will completely change. In the meantime, I have decided to save the sample until my husband’s upcoming milestone birthday, where “Gardenia” will get the grand appearance it deserves!

The lake lies still as I stroll through the still morning-wet grass with bare feet. The dew clings to my skin and makes me smile briefly again and again. The slowly rising sun finds its strength, yet it is still cool. Distantly, birds sing. They greet the new day. The scent of bright flowers rises to my nose and mingles with the feeling of untouched beauty. I sit down in the grass and become one with the awakening world. Gardenia Extrait starts, like almost every Roja, with a roar of accords. However, these calm down very quickly and open up a citrus-green soundscape that increasingly merges with the skin over time. The underlying green bitterness of the opening quickly makes way and gives space to white, calm floral accords. It is simultaneously a feeling of tranquility and skillfully staged clarity. Almost purity. The green remains in the background as the fragrance develops, and Gardenia creates the impression of sitting in a meadow full of blooming scented flowers. It never overwhelms. It is not a Flowerbomb. It feels extremely natural and allows me to experience a sunrise over the meadow with every wear. My happy place. Where the sun gently kisses the blossoms and, with its warmth, sends the world into a beautiful day.

Escaping the darkness of the prince, whom she has once again banished into angry solitude with her tale for a night, Scheherazade hurries out into the palace garden. The rays of the morning sun kiss the first blossoms awake in the magnificent garden.

The punchline: Expensive scent for the older lady Rhetorical question: Why was this fragrance discontinued? Answer: Well, Gardenia… that’s how it smells, a bouquet of many different flowers and also branches. This old/rich scent flatters me less. A bit too creamy for my taste. It reminds me of my grandmother. Of old days in spring.

The scent truly elicited a wow from me, and that happened twice. The first time was when I opened the sample vial. A truly wonderful fragrance for me, with above-average longevity. After the opening, which predominantly reminds me of fresh bergamot, the floral notes of the heart slowly come to the forefront. I can't really notice much of peach and coconut. However, I also lack the experience to identify individual components specifically. After the transition to the base, which for me consists largely of wood and a pleasant sweetness with a hint of musk and vanilla, the scent remains well perceivable for a period of 12-14 hours. The fragrance notes are harmoniously coordinated with each other, creating a wonderfully soft, relaxing scent composition. I would prefer to categorize the scent as a women's perfume. However, it is also wearable for men. I certainly have no problem wearing it. I can't say anything about the bottle, as I unfortunately only have a test vial. The second wow came when calculating the 100ml comparison price. Even considering that it is pure perfume oil and you really only need a dab to smell good for 12 hours, the price of the 15ml bottle is the reason why it probably won't be sitting on my shelf.

Taking a walk through the mall, I went to the perfume shop and asked the clerk if there was anything new, and she kindly told me that Loewe 7 Silver had just arrived. I have been testing it during the afternoon and I must say that I like it, it is not something exceptional or new, but I like it. Loewe 7 Silver is a greener incense, spicy and metallic than its predecessors, it is fresh and herbaceous, but with a metallic nuance of very sharp incense, which I liked. Here the spices feel more natural and raw, not so clear, but very fresh, and the incense of their predecessors is, but this time something more crystalline and herbaceous, which I liked a lot. In performance it is not a pump, but it maintains a good hours in skin with a moderate projection pulling down. The price has seemed a little high for what it is, but well, as it is a novelty, it will go down, and since I have not loved it to buy it now, I will wait to catch a good offer, if I find it, and if not, well, nothing happens either.

This one is pretty amazing. The most dominant notes which my nose picks are roses and leather with some kind of pencil wood in the background. I really love it. This is what Noir de Noir should have been, and not the cloying overbearing linear fragrance that it is. This has a beautiful rose fragrance with a subdued patchouli and a little leather note in the dry down. Wonderful stuff. Scent: 9.5/10 Longevity: 8/10 Projection: 8/10

51 start with the Oud, and maybe it can be hard for begginers. But this is a masterpiece in the drydown. The rose with the oud is magic. I love it. I only hace 20ml but for sure I will buy more in the future.

Uncommented Fragrances No. 97 Another Roja: yet another new fragrance from Roja Dove and once again a comment from me about it. However, No. 51 is not all that new, as it has already existed as an Eau de Parfum. And now, therefore, as a perfume in the stricter sense. An in-house trend that can be observed with many Roja fragrances: the concentration is raised, from Eau de Parfum to perfume, for whatever reason this is deemed necessary for these strong, clingy scents. It certainly brings in more money, as long as the followers are willing to pay. I too was tempted to order a mini bottle in England, which promptly arrived within three days. At least that’s already good service. Since I do not know the Eau de Parfum in this case and the (old) fragrance seems to be quite rare, I have to rely on what I can perceive from No. 51 (perfume). So much for now: I don’t find it to be overly animalistic, as partially described in the EdP. I also cannot perceive a noticeable rose-oud-saffron combination. Was the fragrance reformulated more distinctly than with Fetish, Enigma, Danger, Reckless, Scandal, Vetiver, etc., and not just concentrated and intensified? I cannot judge this and must leave this comparison to connoisseurs of the old material (No. 51 EdP). However, there are also clear parallels: Like all Rojas, the fragrance initially seems somewhat overloaded and more than in all other fragrances of this brand, the ingredients blend so harmoniously that at first, a sense of boredom almost arises. Fortunately, this changes in the base note, as more and more ingredients can be differentiated because the similarly opulent top and/or heart note (I cannot discern a difference) has faded away. After the brighter tones have departed (especially bergamot is recognizable, less lavender or other light, citrus tones) and after the floral notes, which were only dabbed, increasingly sink into the drydown, the fragrance becomes a beautiful leather chypre (which is quite rare today), becomes spicy, subtly oriental (oud is not very present, but rather subtle by today’s standards) and unfolds a bouquet of spices that never appears overloaded or peppery bitter, but rather radiates warmth. That is certainly successful. Everything then ends with woody and aromatic notes, which ultimately give the fragrance a more masculine touch. However, it is also wearable by women at any time. And now the obligatory question that arises (for me) with all Rojas, which are indeed priced ambitiously, even if one might be willing to pay more for a Guerlain perfume (same concentration): Is this an outstandingly good and beautiful fragrance? YES and NO: I waver between 8.5 and 9.0, because the fragrance takes quite a long time to unfold in a way that seems completely successful to me. This is not a plea for synthetic blends, whose top note is identical to the base note and which only want to be purchased based on first impressions. However, it is the desire for a top note that at least captivates me similarly to the further development (think of many great classics of perfume history - including those from Guerlain - up until the end of the 1980s, which Roja apparently strongly orients itself towards in all respects). NO also because the fragrance, precisely because of this orientation towards older traditions, has little originality to offer. But it does have one thing: charm and British understatement. This is not a snob (as one might expect from such an expensive fragrance); No. 51 is rather distinguished - and that is perhaps the greatest compliment one can give (to a fragrance) for Anglophiles. So probably rather YES, to finally answer my question above.

I started exploring the fragrances from the house of Roja over a year ago - hooked by the ranking list and many reviews from competent perfume enthusiasts, I extensively engaged with Enigma, Reckless, Danger, H-pH, Elysium (all in the pour Homme variant) & some unisex staples like Midsummer Dream, Ti Amo, Amber Aoud, and a few other Rojas, and I even managed to snag a few at a bargain from eBay... Interestingly, I haven't commented on any Roja so far, probably because there are already countless competent reviews and comments on most Rojas, and I didn't want to add my two cents to the mix :-) However, the 51 pH has hardly any comments, so I’ll jump in here and try my hand at a new comment on it :-) Roja is simply outrageously expensive, and even €150 to €200 less per bottle would still be a hefty price, but it seems that exclusivity is generated through a perverted pricing policy - so be it, everyone should decide for themselves what a perfume is worth to them or how much money they are willing to spend on a scent... My latest find is the Roja 51 pH in the parfum variant; I “blind bought” it after hearing and reading a lot of good things about it & the fragrance pyramid appealed to me greatly... I eagerly awaited the package, and when it finally arrived, I could hardly wait and had to start a test immediately. In its newer versions, Roja celebrates the themes of luxury & exclusivity, so both the packaging and even more so the handmade bottles with their very noble and elaborately designed labels and closures are a real feast for the eyes and make me a little bit happy every time I apply the perfumes from the bottle - it truly is a celebration for me each time, which I curiously practice less often with other perfumes - the outer packaging of the perfume has a significant effect on me and is, in my eyes, part of a really successful overall package - emotions are not only triggered by the scent itself but even beforehand when the wearer unpacks and applies the perfume - for me, it is always a special moment that I look forward to again and again :-) I first experienced this effect when I received and unpacked the Black Cube from Molvizar the year before last, especially since Molvizar, with its elegant wooden box, the hand-signed and numbered card, and the platinum glitter in the perfume itself, also radiates a lot of luxury - back then, I was completely captivated by it and enjoyed this wonderful presentation for a long time - and even today, I still really like this type of packaging - it is a truly harmonious overall package, and the same goes for the Rojas - some call it decadence, I call it magic ;-) How does the 51 pH come across to me? I also don’t know the EdP, so I can’t derive any direct comparisons here; at first, I perceive a very distinct oud note, which I have not experienced in this intensity with the Rojas so far. Accompanying this is a very pleasant leather timbre; unlike Yatagan, I do perceive a top and subsequent heart note, which settles on my skin after about 1.5 hours. Various spices join in, which I can hardly distinguish, so tightly are they woven together; the perfume becomes noticeably warmer and radiates more, the sillage develops only over time - for me, there are clear parallels in the heart note to Roja's Enigma pH, at least the scent accord feels that way for a while, without, however, containing an overly strong cognac note - it remains very dense, spicy, refined, and very, very noble - after another 4 hours, the 51 approaches the base, which comes across as woody aromatic and quite masculine - although it is no longer considered “politically correct” these days to categorize perfumes by gender, I perceive Roja 51 pH as a pure men's fragrance and can hardly imagine it on a woman (by the way: just as little can I imagine the unisex scent “Ti Amo” on a man...) The perfume has a very long-lasting presence and is still very noticeable after 15 hours - a blessing, as some Roja perfumes last far less on my skin than the EdP variants; however, this one really clings remarkably well and truly has wingman qualities (thanks to Maggy4u for this term, which fits this perfume perfectly :-) ) For me, the Roja 51 pH is a direct brother to Enigma, but without its cognac intensity; I feel very comfortable with this scent and wear it both in a suit at work and for more upscale occasions like opera, theater, or similar - it is not a perfume for every day but rather to set special accents with a truly special perfume when worn consciously - worn too often, the 51 pH could certainly start to annoy over time, so I only wear it sporadically in the office and for the aforementioned occasions - contrary to Maggy4u's perception, I do not find the 51 to be a playful boy - but rather a distinguished and serious scent with elegance and spirit, quite mature and noble - in my opinion, more suited for men aged 35+, not for twentysomethings or boys ;-) - since for me, one spray on the chest and neck is quite enough to be well-scented all day long, the 50 ml version will surely outlast me, so my grandchildren - if they can wait until they are 35+ - will still have some of it left ;-) Is the Roja 51 pH worth its money?!? Well, certainly not at the original price of €450, but I can definitely agree with a price according to my above calculation formula, as it is surely worth that. The bottle will last me at least 175 years in quantity ;-)

For a long time, I searched for him, "observed" him, and "sneaked" around him, the 51 Pour Homme.... But why exactly the 51 PH? I can't say for sure... I really like many creations by Roja Dove, and some of his masterpieces enrich my collection, for which I am very happy and grateful... For me, many fragrances by Roja Dove are simply art - PERIOD. But back to my strange "obsession" with 51 PH: I kept looking at the fragrance notes and imagining how it might actually smell... Thanks to Parfumo, I also got some impressions through the comments and statements of the community, but the perception of scent is always very different and personal.... Do you know that feeling? You have this fragrance constantly in your head and wonder what it might be like, and you just want to have it, even if you don't really know how it actually smells and whether you will like it... (You could also call that addiction, but let's just leave it at that ;-P For months, I "stalked" around the fragrance, considering whether to order the Heritage version directly from Roja Dove or to wait and see if a bottle would appear in the souk.... After weeks and months of keeping an eye out and pondering, I finally decided to order the 51 PH Heritage directly from Roja Dove... (According to the fragrance pyramid, the 51 PH perfume version from 2017 and the Heritage version have the same structure - has anyone tested both? What differences are there?) The ordering finger was quick, and bam - it was done! A feeling of joy overcame me, and of course, I wondered: "What if I don't like it at all?" Not that this was my first blind buy, but because I had thought about the fragrance for so long and imagined it, I was even more curious... Well, the excitement was there, and I could hardly wait to finally have 51 PH Heritage in my mailbox.... When 51 PH Heritage actually arrived after 10 days and I took it out of its packaging, I was super happy and, of course, full of anticipation... One-two-three, eyes closed and sprayed once: 51 PHH opens with zesty citrus notes, accompanied by a subtly sweet lavender, not herbal or grandma-like.... rather something "fresh-soapy"... - A flight of the senses... the scent feels bright, fresh, and open in the opening.... Immediately after that, gentle floral tones follow - surrounded by delicate spices and a hint of sweetness.... I can clearly recognize ambrette, vanilla, as well as benzoin and a touch of oud.... - The scent becomes a bit "darker" here... It starts bright and fresh, then gradually becomes darker and more mystical - very exciting.... Later, resinous-earthy tones, fine woods, and a touch of leather come into play... - The scent drifts a bit more, becoming a little darker and earthier... For me, the 51 PH Heritage is like an "out-flight": ...you start fresh, take off, float over mountains and valleys, high up.... then it goes a bit lower, past flowery meadows, through deep forests, the earth swirls up, you enter a dark cave, it smells earthy dark, mystical, and enchanted... out of the cave again, it's evening, the flight slows down a bit here, everything happens very slowly now, you no longer float, you walk now... slowly forward - from a distance, you see a paddock with horses - the leather saddles ready .... - you recognize it, but it is far away... you lie down on the ground and let your thoughts sink, looking up at the sky, the sparkling stars, until the out-flight ends here.... A quite complex fragrance with so many facets!

After I gave my heart to the EDP, I couldn't help but pay my respects to the perfume as well. Thanks to this wonderful community, we were able to realize a sharing that is by no means a given considering the price range of the 50ml bottles from Roja. It is the passion that unites us. A thousand thanks.

Rose-Oud with everything and more, and too much of it, and then some more - FULL BLAST. For me, it's unbearable. This is how I used to imagine Jubilation XXV by Amouage, only that XXV surprisingly turned out to be really beautiful, easy to wear casually, and "very pleasant". 51 is really like an olfactory gladiatorial fight for me, where in the end, there are only losers.

This Roja has been described here a few times already. Some have torn it apart, while others have praised it highly. But no description quite fits my impression. So here is my take. Years ago, I bought the fragrance blindly, just like my predecessor. I was so taken with some of Roja's scents that I couldn't resist an offer for almost half the price.

imagine a fragrant drop of oil that gently adheres to the skin, then melts into it, creamy and transparent..... this attar is like that after a few minutes: like a fragrant skin: familiar and precious, very close and soft, lasting and penetrating. the wood notes dance with flowers and passion fruit on a softly vanilla base. everything stays close together, mild, warm, velvety, like a chord from which individual overtones quietly and alternately emerge. none is prominent, none alters the harmony.... calm sets in and peace of mind.... this is not a scent that you wear-- this is a scent that you submit to with a smile.

I find this to be a bit more of a fruitier take on the Paula's Ibiza line. Definitely my favorite of the three since I love mango, and I find it to be quite prominent in this one. Sure, it could be a bit more longlasting, but for me this is never a problem anymore since I always carry a refillable decant with me. This one is summer in a bottle, light and airy, perfect for when you don't want to choke someone. Office-friendly and definitely unisex.

Initial cloud smells like synthetic apple flavoring. Fruity in a chalky candy way. Unpleasant. Once that settles down, coconut opens up and gives the composition a creamier flavor profile – more tropical, sure, but in a vague "tropical vacation flavored shower gel" way. No mango. Where's my mango? I was promised mango's best. Where is it? I can feel it clearly on a paper strip, but on my skin – nothing. Just that vague and cheap fruitiness :( Strong sillage – the whole street will smell it together with you. Great if you like it, really annoying if you do not – because while it does get softer with time, it never really becomes a skin scent. It will continue making its presence known until the bitter end. Oh, and speaking of bitter end! It lasts forever. Fruits fizzle away in about ~2 hours, but the creamy woods below latch onto you and never let go. They're quite pleasant at first, even if a bit too strong for me – sharp, prickly. But in another ~2 hours something in the composition starts going sour. Like it's curdling on your skin. And then – good luck getting it out! I showered – it didn't help. I went to sleep ~5 hours later – it didn't help. I woke up the next day, about ~20 hours since I first sprayed it – and it was still there. Both on my clothes and on my body. That would've been too much even if I loved the smell. But I've come to despise it. When I tested the same perfume later on my partner, his skin brought out a very reasonable composition of sandalwood and cream and a just a wee bit of unripe mango on the sidelines. The fruits were fleeting and never took centerstage; and while the overall scent did become more sour as time went on, it never spoiled. Kinda boring and one-dimensional, but still a great result compared to my experience. Who knows, perhaps this thing just has something against my skin in particular. But either way, it was a huge let down. Hard to believe that this came from the same perfumer as my beloved Solo Vulcan :(

This is so underrated I want to scream it from the rooftops! I was on the hunt for a summer tropical scent and I fell in love with this and the next one and had to get them both. It’s creamy from the sandalwood and coconut, but not lactonic. It’s sweet and fruity, but not juvenile or too feminine. It’s comforting and woody so it’s nice in cool weather, but also tropical and the fruitiness shines in warm weather. And I can’t sing its praises enough in sillage and longevity, it lasts all day on skin, days on clothes, and I can smell it on myself all day. It’s so, so lovely, my favorite discovery of the year. Sillage 9/10, Longevity 10/10

I adore Cosmic. It's an ambery woody scent with just enough fruit and coconut to make it feel like vacation but it's not overly sweet. You get more of the creaminess of coconut rather than a sunscreen coconut type scent. It's really unique and I haven't worn anything else like it. It lasts forever - if you spray it on your clothes, it'll still be there the next time you wear it. Loewe is my favorite fragrance house and this is one of my favorites.

Loewe is a totally underrated brand for me, as this brand is not really widespread. Even though the brand doesn't suggest it, it comes from Spain and has quite a large assortment with many flankers. This fashion brand is distributed by LVMH, even though it is relatively unknown in Germany. Thus, this brand can be categorized into the designer category, even if many creations are quite niche and also somewhat elevated in price. Nevertheless, the perfumes are quite affordable in terms of price and have great quality with fairly serious creations. I find the Paula's Ibiza line wonderful, as it is quite summery and represents this joyful island well. The original Paula's Ibiza is in my collection, and this Cosmic is the second flanker after Paula's Ibiza Eclectic . The line has a carefree vibe and some light tropical vibes. The original is distinctly greener with coconut water, while this one leans slightly towards Erba Pura with its fruit cocktail. I have tested this scent several times with a sample. The samples are really cool with this great design. The cardboard indicates the notes of apple, sandalwood, and vanilla. Apple is not listed here but is quite noticeable. The actual bottle and packaging are also impressive, just like all the lines from this brand. Roughly, this scent can be categorized in the sweet-fruity section. With such exotic fruit cocktails, the Erba Pura DNA immediately comes to mind. Very roughly, they go in the same direction, but it is independent. This fruity DNA is by no means as penetrating, and this musk base is not present here. The opening impresses with an exotic fruit cocktail of pear and mango. Apple is also present, coming across as rather green. A wonderful cheerful mix that fits well with this party island. There is also a slight coconut note, but it does not play a main role. This coconut is slightly creamy and harmonizes with the fruit and sweetness. After 1-2 hours, a wonderful cistus appears, accompanied by warm notes like amber and a slightly resinous spiciness. Woody notes perfectly round off this rather linear scent progression, especially a creamy sandalwood note. The creation is already very rounded, modern, and completely unisex. Performance is in a solid range. This scent definitely lasts 8 hours with a great pleasant sillage over a long period. Well suited for leisure and also for everyday wear, as it is quite uncomplicated. Overall, a great scent that is not completely mind-blowing. Sweet-fruity cocktails are often nothing really new, but they feel good and are almost always wearable. A great flanker from a wonderful line.

Cosmic starts subtly fruity, it is truly a pleasant fruitiness that cannot be compared to a sticky sweet fruit cocktail scent. Rather, it is really subtly aromatic yet still noticeable. After a few minutes in the drydown, the creaminess unfolds through the sandalwood and vanilla - in combination with the fruits, it creates a really great combination.

In the aftermath of publishing my 2024 rankings, Lost in Paris was the #1 scent on my sampling target list going into 2025. Driven by the huge retail price tag and the almost strictly (albeit limited) positive coverage, the expectations were firmly placed at the highest of highs, yet Lost in Paris also features significant lows. One could argue that it is the scent's opening that makes the sale here as Lost in Paris opens as a high-quality gourmand fragrance with a very realistic sweetened/bakery style orange smell. I have seen various people compare this to the patisserie smell that Sweetie Aoud has, but I am more-so reminded of Creme Savers or products like it, i.e. the swirl candy that is half white, half orange. As I don't partake in alcohol consumption, the listed curaçao is hard for me to find and I would argue that the scent never features a boozy feel throughout the evolution. The first negative of the scent comes when I smell it on-skin. The scent lists "mandarin orange" in the top which I suspect is the reason why the scent has some window cleaner feel to it. This particular orange note is something that I already have history with as Italian premium brand Royal Crown also used it in Celebration . Ultimately, I feel like this note gives way and isn't there 30 minutes into the drydown. Accords: sweet-creamy-citrusy-gourmand-spicy Subsequently heading into the aforementioned drydown, butter appears to be the primary note on which the base is structured. On-skin, the scent has a sweet-creamy-spicy structure that is not too far from THOO's signature DNA with scents like Wonderly or even scents like Spice D'Arno . This is primarily due to the opening gourmand highlights not being as relevant in the drydown, making for a very average drydown with Roja's blend quality being the only thing carrying it forward. Performance of the scent is fairly moderate throughout (average projection within a couple meters) and while I don't think there is a scent like it in the niche market today (perhaps the closest ideas would be between Panettone and Sweetie Aoud ), I do believe that the retail price tag of €1,195/100ml should justify more than just uniqueness. As much as the artistry is towards the 99th percentile of the modern niche market, Roja's history of elite blending is not visible with Lost in Paris and that is a significant shortfall of the scent. To further comment on the pricing, the scent was originally listed at Harrods with a price tag of €995 (£850) and while the brand has offered me the chance to honor that price, them not changing it is still a red flag. While my current collection peaks at the €600/100ml price tier, I was (and remain) extremely open to entering the tier above it to make for a more distinguished collection. However, that entry point won't be here as I ultimately feel like the product doesn't align with the expectations. There are very few premium products in the market today that can successfully retain the opening highs into the drydown and to me, Lost in Paris is not one of those fragrances.

I was really looking forward to smelling such a clear gourmand scent from Roja and I knew right away that I would love it. The fact that it had been criticized was just a sure sign of the sophistication that the scent represents - I personally don’t like overwhelmingly strong one-dimensional edible scents, it has to be done with style. The woody bed with indulgent, gentle spices and thick, cuddly Vanilla accompanied by sensual Musk and Ambergris is covered with Caramelized citruses and elegantly delicious different kind of gourmand facets. Sweet and salty nuances are dancing fluidly, seamlessly, addictively. The creamy, dreamy, buttery, silky smooth texture is incredibly attractive and elegant yet I can’t help but think about the smell of various freshly baked pastries floating in the air. The scent has a golden, bright, luminous and vibrant aura. Simplified, this scent is a creamy, buttery toffee with a hint of mandarin wrapped in a cashmere blanket, but the scent is adult-like and dignified with a subdued performance that is not at all too weak and lasts a long time. What comes to the fruits: I love them in fragrances, but I’m so glad that nothing but different kind of Oranges have been put into this fragrance. That makes this unique. They are so amazingly well made and this scent has the best citrus aroma along with Burlington 1819 . I haven’t come across a similar gourmand scent that exudes luxury and opulence. That’s why I’m completely in love with Lost in Paris. This is Gourmand Extraordinaire. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

Lost in Paris is supposed to represent a streetside crepe stand according to Roja's blurb on his website, and it does this very well. A buttery thin pancake drizzled with caramel and Grand Marnier. The opening threw me off a little bit, it smelled weirdly sweaty or cheesy, but this faded very quickly (within like 10 seconds). I'm not sure why "Grand Marnier" wasn't included in the actual note pyramid because it is described as smelling like it on the Roja website. It gives a very good impression of that sweet orange liqueur, and makes more sense theming-wise, as a French drink, rather than curaçao, which is Carribean. EDIT: Never mind, the official website lists Grand Marnier. Not sure why Parfumo is listing it as curaçao, as they are different drinks, with wildly different connotations in terms of fragrance. The buttery notes then appear, and really give the impression of walking into a bakery in Paris. Bready and decadent, along with the vanillic caramel making it smell like French pastries. There is definitely a floral component that is missing from the note pyramid, albeit slight, but it really rounds out the creation. The drydown is sweet, woody, and musky. The citrus opening, sweet and smooth mid, and woody drydown really remind me of Symphonium . Although not a 1-to-1, they have the same vibe, and I feel like if you are searching for the "perfect" form of Symphonium, you might be really happy with Lost in Paris since it feels more natural, richer, and longer lasting. For me, I still prefer Symphonium because I actually like the simplicity of it. Lost in Paris goes a bit too far with the decadence.

I’ve been sampling out of a 10mL for a week and a half now, with a bottle on the way. Here are my initial thoughts: Roja has released a few fragrances on the sweeter side in the past few months with Aoud Extraordinaire, Chou Chou, and now Lost in Paris. Both Aoud Extraordinaire and Chou Chou were lackluster releases, for me. I was intrigued when Lost and Paris was released and I saw the notes. 7 of the notes in the composition are in my top 10 favorite notes. Now to the scent. I enjoy the scent, but it doesn’t put me in the mindset in the way Roja was marketing this fragrance. I’ve never been to Paris, and never had a crepe so I can’t make a correlation there. The opening is spot on with the listed top notes though. A blast of orange hits you in the face right away. It’s more of a bitter orange than a mélange of sweet and juicy oranges. Very quickly (A couple seconds), a rum note comes through adding extraordinary warmth to the bright citrus, making it such a pleasant contrast and a very nice smell. This only lasts for 5 minutes unfortunately, and I would’ve been content if this was the linear scent through the life of the fragrance. As this dries down, an overly sweet burnt sugar and caramel note comes through. Think of the scent of crème brûlée. I do really enjoy the butter accord as it adds a creamy, almost milky facet to the mid. If the butter accord wasn’t there to smooth this composition out, this would’ve been a mess in my opinion. It sure is a gourmand lovers dream at this point. Now to my least favorite part of the scent. A lovely vanilla and many spices come through, making this scent come together to feel like a fuzzy, warm blanket hugging your body. Why the overdose of clove though?! The clove turns me off and is almost headache inducing at times, if I’m not fully prepared for it. It’s super heavy and is a large part of the projection, unfortunately. On to performance. Hands down a beast of a performer and probably top 5 in my collection based on the collective longevity and projection. Every time I wore this, I could only bear two sprays as this projected heavily for 8 hours. The life of the fragrance went on for 18 hours, and both my wife and I noticed it 14 hours later when we woke up the next day. Be prepared for a beast! Overall, I think this is a nice fragrance and is much better than Roja’s other two latest creations. However, I long for a better dry-down only because the clove can be overbearing and take over the whole dry-down. Unfortunately for us guys out there that don’t enjoy feminine scents, this does turn to the feminine side after a couple hours on skin but many will consider this unisex. The opening is WOW, the mid is good, and the dry-down is MEH. The performance is beast mode and will contend for one of my strongest fragrances. The moral of the story is, this should be called “Lost in Christmas” as this conjures festive moments and reminds you of the warmth and love of the holiday season. PS: This is no where near worth its retail price, nor does it belong in the prestige/purple cap collection. Thank you for reading!

quite an interesting gourmand. i dont know what curacao is, but I am smelling something mysterious in the opening, like a poisonous sweet drink. I'm definitely getting the bitter citruses combined with the rum which smells very unusual. under it lies a STRONG buttery caramel. imagine pouring a rum & coke with blood orange on top of your melted caramel butter mixture. if you wanna smell something you haven't smelled before, id say go look for this scent. decant gifted to me by a generous friend :)

With great anticipation, I ordered this perfume, as it was described by many as a seductive, complex scent that is bound to attract compliments. However, when I applied it, I was surprised from the very first second - and not necessarily in a positive way.

The new Roja fragrances are really having a tough time at the moment. Especially with the prices, it's almost clear that people are particularly critical. Understandable, I mean, we're talking about over 1000 euros for a perfume.

A bit atypical for Roja, this fragrance actually allows one to perceive almost all the listed components of the fragrance pyramid. Gourmands are somewhat atypical in the Roja Dove house anyway, where everything is often blended into a whimsical ethereal medley.

When Roja releases a new fragrance from the Prestige Collection, I naturally have to test it. However, as is known about him, one must first get to know and understand this scent. The fragrance opens with an alcoholic composition of Blue Curaçao and a fine fruity mandarin paired with blood orange.

I think, at this price, the expectations of anyone who smells it are more than high, and rightly so. When you look at the fragrance pyramid, it either makes you hungry or makes you feel sick. Butter, caramel, vanilla, brown sugar, etc.... Enough teasing, now show me the damn fragrance.

Opens in a mouthwatering explosion which I can only describe as accidentally dropping a full package of ground up mulled wine spices and getting the cloud of spice dust all over yourself. Cloves, star anise, the whole shebang. Aggressive, but very earthy and immediately relaxing. Once the initial powderiness subsided a little, fresh undertones started peeking through and blended together on me into an adorable artisanal cola smell. My partner got even luckier, his warmer skin smelled like a spicy apple cider. Absolutely delicious! I can't help but adore its whimsical almost sparkly quality. The only downside for me is the super strong and aggressive trail. I did one spray and it immediately enveloped the whole apartment. Which is great if you love it, but going outside like this feels super inconsiderate to other people. Especially if you're going to sit in enclosed spaces. I don't wanna be the person whose entrance immediately chokes out the whole bar :( And it's not the kind of short-lived sillage you can easily wait out. It took ~3 hours to mellow out on me, and about ~4 for my partner. It also sticks exceptionally well to clothing. ~7 hours into the experience there was just an intimate spicy aftertaste on my skin. But I could still feel most of the notes within arm's length of my partner's shirt until he threw it in the wash the next day. A lovely and fun experience, but one that I need to schedule my whole day around to feel comfortable wearing outside of the house. And I'm very lucky to have enjoyed it! With how long-lasting and all-encompassing that sillage was — this very well could have ended up in a gigantic headache.

For some, the number 7 may just be a number like any other, but in many regions, it is said to carry deep symbolism. The 7 is a lucky number that is considered a symbol of perfection and enlightenment in numerous cultures. This number is also frequently used in a religious context. Examples from Christianity include the seven days of creation, the seven virtues, or the seven deadly sins. Perhaps currently interesting is Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, although the reinterpretation of the classic is being heavily criticized. Whether the criticism of the interpretation 7 Elixir is similarly negative will be clarified later in this review. Loewe was a brand I was completely unfamiliar with. Recently, I was sitting with my sister, staring at a framed picture of the Loewe brand. I casually asked, "Sister, what is Loewe?" She replied that it is a designer brand from Spain. This aligns with my research and the company's beginnings with leather goods, followed by women's fashion, and ultimately the launch of the first perfume in 1972. 7 Eau de Toilette was the only fragrance I had ever come across before, but I paid little attention to it since I didn't know the manufacturer. However, as luck would have it, a sample of 7 Elixir landed on my neck, and my first impression is quite positive. What sounded promising was the short ingredient list. Less is more, I firmly believe that when it comes to ingredient lists in the perfume world. The sample packaging listed only three ingredients: red peppercorn, incense absolute, and red apple. Somewhat strange because I find no mention of an apple note anywhere else, and instead, chili, lemon, and patchouli are listed online. But it doesn't matter what is written where; the fact is: The opening and the following two hours are the best part of the fragrance. A freshness spreads that is spiced up by the pink pepper and hints at a touch of floral/fruity notes in the background. Immediately, I see a young office guy in a suit and tie in front of me. My spontaneous first thought is, very clean. As time goes on, labdanum and patchouli push more to the forefront, and the spiciness gradually fades. I am a bit surprised that 25 percent of the 12 owners on Parfumo are female. In terms of performance, the title of the fragrance could easily use a higher number because this scent has fire! I don't know if chili contributes to longevity, but with four sprays on my neck, I could perceive it for over eight hours. That definitely deserves more than 7 points in the rating. The bottle is not unattractive but is nonetheless unremarkable and simple. From the color of the bottle, I would have expected a maritime scent, but I was successfully played a trick. From the first impression, one might think that Loewe is a niche house. However, since my sister clarified that it is a designer brand, I was curious about the pricing. 50 ml can be found online for 89 euros. With a successful fragrance DNA and top performance, that is a very fair price. The Loewe brand claims to create fragrances inspired by nature, and at least with my first scent from the house, I would call this endeavor completely successful. Although only 22 reviews have been submitted, I cannot understand the poor average rating of 6.6. A spicy-fresh all-rounder that can especially showcase its strengths in everyday life and at the office.

One of the users included a sample of this perfume with a purchase from his souk, thank you for that;) I had never heard the name Loewe before, and since I was curious, I applied it without thinking twice… It smells strong, strongly of chili; at least that's the scent I perceive the most. For the nose, it feels like what the eyes feel when you've had chili on your hands and then rubbed them… slightly irritating/burning smell in my opinion. I also perceive a hint of lemon beneath the chili; all in all, I would describe this scent as somewhat devilish due to its sharp aroma. If this fragrance weren't so incredibly strong, I could see it on a well-groomed man, a suit wearer, expensive watch, important job! I wouldn't buy it for myself after the trial, but on a given occasion, I will definitely use the tester;)

This is a very hard composition to describe so I’ll try my best. Turandot is like a painting of two stage of love. It starts off very bright, exciting and vibrant and then transforms into something opposite - calming and indulgent - like thunder strikes filling the sky, spectacular and captivating… and settles down to a sleeping sea. The scent announces its presence with a theatrical entrée with an unusual green tea-like aroma with fresh and zesty citruses with a sunny day-like Aldehydes. There’s also some sweetly gluey, herbal and tea-like floral note that is quite noticeable, which is Immortelle. As the brightness settles a bit, the orchestra of bouquets of flowers bloom up and concours the whole composition. The conductor of this orchestra is a powdery, almondy and delicate sweet spicy floral sensation composed by Paulownia flower and Heliotrope. In the first round sits gloriously voluptuous Rose de Mai along with tropical fruity facets of Ylang and Peach. A bit of sourness from Black Currant whispering like a dreamy string instrument. The composition changes quite remarkably as the base rises up. The prominent powdery facets remain but the quality of it changes giving off a warm and almost skin like feel. The buttery Orris merges the core making it more earthy with a clean “purple” undertone. Orris Sur Cedre steps forward and took the lead. Under this powdery woodsy combination lay fresh soily, earthy and mossy base. The ambery warmth radiates from sweet Benzoin with an intimate feel of Labdanum. There’s a little touch of tannin of Coffee but it’s very soft and in the back seat of the orchestra. Turandot is somehow familiar. It has similarities with his other creations but just by the parts here and there. The powderiness reminds me of RDHP15. On the other hand the peachy and warming Ambrée sensation takes me to Britannia. The floral Chypre base makes me think of Chypre Extraordinaire. What really makes Turandot stand out as its own direction is a prominent note of Orris Sur Cedre.

Created to celebrate the 10th Anniversary of The Royal Opera House Muscat in 2022 I have been wearing Turandot now for many days just to find the words how to describe it. Chypre is what Dove does definitely best and Chypre Floral Turandot is definitely no exception. Turandot is a passionate perfume full of emotions and very rich in flowers and some fruits. It opens up with uplifting aldehydes and citrus which is barely detectable and straight away you will be surrounded by a huge cloud of flowers (Rose de Mai and Magnolia being dominant in the middle, Iris on the base) and somewhat delicious touch of Blackcurrant and Peach. null of the notes are straight out on a tray, but have been shredded into a million pieces and blended towards perfection. This puzzle, where is the picture of the intact tray with flowers and fruits, is completely impossible to put together ever again. It’s like a beautiful compact powder which has dropped on the floor. Turandot is an evocative, mellow and dense blend, it’s delightfully brash compared to any other floral blend of Roja. It’s very sumptuous. Even if there is Princess Flower as a one note and Turandot was the imperious Princess in China based on a vivid fantasy I would say that Lakmé would be a scent of a princess and Turandot would be a scent of a queen. This fragrance is unashamed and bold, not shy and snooty. The base of Turandot is warm and woody and there is slightly earthy and mossy undertones with a depth from Labdanum. The presentation of Turandot is phenomenal like is the presentation of the previous perfume - amazing and delicate Lakmé - made for The Royal Opera House Muscat in Oman in 2019. I will edit this review soon since this was first written on IG where the space is very limited. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

Anniversaries should be celebrated accordingly, including the tenth anniversary of the opening of the Royal Opera House Muscat in Oman. Not only was there a festive performance of Giacomo Puccini's "Turandot"; the house of Roja Dove was also commissioned to crown this occasion with an appropriate fragrance creation. Now, commissioned works at Roja Parfums are never the worst: I think of the creations I know, "Bergdorf Femme," for which I still owe my contribution, and "l’Oscar," which reflects the glamour of a very special hotel in London. Since I sympathize with the brand (even if I mention what I don't like), it is of course no surprise that I also view "Turandot" positively. Why Puccini's last opera was chosen for this gala is not entirely clear to me. After all, it is this work, with its final act of the libretto, that Puccini struggled with and could not complete before he died. A festive performance that ends with a marriage vow between two powerful figures, where one immediately wonders after the curtain falls: "And that's supposed to go well?" But perhaps the numerous choral scenes that fill the stage and the widely known "Nessun dorma" since the 1990 World Cup in Rome played a role in this choice. I do not know; however, I do not have to understand it! What I do know for sure: Roja's "Turandot" fascinates me, just like so many of these fragrances before. Just as the unknown prince Kalaf in the opera conquers (or should we rather say "outsmarts"?) the proud princess Turandot, this fragrance creation conquers me. It also follows the familiar structure of Roja fragrances: should I call it "Rojanade" in reference to Guerlain's "Guerlainade"? For I find Hesperides in the top note, May roses, jasmine, and iris, as well as some sun-ripened fruits on a mossy base with rich earthy patchouli addition in every one of the fragrances I know from this house. Around this fragrant trellis are the special scent notes that then define the personality of a composition. Except for this "Rojanade," no fragrance creation resembles the other; each is special in its own way. And so is "Turandot." Right from the start, the Hesperides aromas (lemon, bergamot, petitgrain) are perked up by aldehydes: After all, the foyer and staircase of an opera house are particularly glamorous and enhance the anticipation of what awaits us after the curtain rises with the multitude of voices, the magnificent gala wardrobes, and fragrances. In "Turandot," Roja's very personal fragrance garden in Grasse (as I call it) was also raided: Bouquets of May roses, richly blooming jasmine branches, and warm-vanilla-scented heliotropes were loosely tied and arranged with long slender flower vines of ylang-ylang, adorned with delicate orange blossoms and noble magnolia flowers. The blue flowers of the bluebell tree complete these arrangements and their exotic aura in scent and color. Next to them are large beautifully crafted bowls with ripe peaches, whose velvety skin invites you to bite, and bundles of black currants. Surprisingly, these were arranged on a bed of immortelles; unusual, but herbaceous and therefore well-suited to the fruity-strong aroma of the dark berry fruits. Here we encounter the familiar contrasts again - peach-sweet and berry-bitter! Refined is Mr. Roja Dove - hats off! Enticing, inviting moss cushions open the spicy-woody base, which receives a special note from aromatic coffee and powdery iris. Patchouli in golden brown, cedar, and cashmere wood were to be expected alongside resinous, smoky benzoin and labdanum: but coffee and iris? It is always exciting to see what scent results emerge at the end of a collection of flowers, fruits, woods, and resins when they are skillfully arranged. Nothing seems random; everything fits perfectly together and could not be any other way. Roja Dove shakes the kaleidoscope of fragrance notes with seemingly effortless ease, and out falls a new, very special creation: each a luxury creation, none resembling the other, and all transporting you to opulent, extravagant, and sometimes decadent scent interworlds. Admittedly: You have to like them; otherwise, you will be overwhelmed by the richness of the sillage and the enormous longevity. A preference for a luxurious ambiance is also necessary: sober, straightforward characters often get lost in many Roja fragrance works. After all, they are not the "Bauhaus" of fragrance architecture. I indulge in them, and so in "Turandot." This creation is indeed worthy of an anniversary and the corresponding gala performance. You often find glamour and exoticism in Oman and at these official occasions; why should the fragrance commissioned for this occasion come timid and mouse-gray? They complement each other, and so "Turandot" has also captivated me in the spell of this fragrance euphoria. If I drown in it, then I drown in it! The eighth hundred of my fragrance contributions is hereby concluded. It should be another extraordinary fragrance that crowns my very personal anniversary. "Turandot" fits this occasion perfectly! How it will continue, I do not yet know: but it will continue! So many beauties in fragrance are waiting to tell me their story; the stock for new "nose food" is still well filled. Let's see: I am certainly curious and now apply a few more spritzes of "Turandot"! And, dear ones: thank you for reading and your patience!

Roja Turandot has been in my collection for almost 2 weeks now, and I have really been looking forward to this fragrance because the EDP is very hard to come by, and when Roja Dove announced that Turandot would be released as a parfum version, it was clear that I had to have this scent. My excitement was immense when I finally held the package with Turandot inside in my hands. With a price of almost €700 including customs, the expectations were, of course, very high. At this point, I must contradict some statements after wearing it several times. I do not smell Diaghilev Parfum or Chypré Extraordinaire here. The only similarities I can point out are with Lakmé Parfum and "Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie | Roja Parfums." Haute has a similar peach and chypre combination, and the creamy component resembles that of Lakmé. I must also disagree with the comparison to "Semi-Bespoke 4 | Roja Parfums," which is much fruitier and sweeter and feels more feminine to me. Unspoken, on the other hand, is spicier and different. Now let’s talk about the scent itself: Turandot opens with a Roja-typical aldehyde note, accompanied by citrus fruits and petitgrain. Of course, some might claim that Roja uses similar concepts. This is true, but Roja Dove simply excels at this type of fragrance. I really like this concept. The heart note is, for me, the best part and what makes Turandot unique. Here, the blackcurrant particularly stands out. I would even say that the other notes are arranged around the blackcurrant. The peach gives it a fruity twist. I find the contrast between peach and blackcurrant fascinating. The blackcurrant has a slightly bitter and rather tart fruity scent, while the peach is sweet and fruity. Here, it can truly be said that opposites attract. This fruity ensemble is accompanied by a gentle rose. Heliotrope gives Turandot a sweet, creamy twist. To me, heliotrope has a scent comparable to vanilla. Jasmine is also recognizable. Jasmine always has something unique and fascinating for me. Jasmine gives Turandot a honeyed, floral, and sweet touch. I also don’t think, as is often claimed, that jasmine makes fragrances feel girlish. Ylang ylang remains more in the background, which may also be due to the similar attributes it shares with jasmine. Immortelle adds a slightly spicy touch, but fortunately, there are no associations with curry, as happened with "I-I Terralba | Masque." The base note, in my opinion, only comes through very faintly, which is rare. There are few fragrances that can hold the heart note for so long. From the base note, only a bit of moss, labdanum, patchouli, and to maintain the sweetness and creaminess, iris and benzoin come through. The longevity for me is in the good range of 9-10 hours and leaves nothing to be desired. The sillage is only over an arm's length at first. Turandot becomes quieter after about 5 hours before the scent becomes intimate after 7-8 hours. Now I would like to address the name of this creation and whether I find it fitting: Yes, I find the name fitting for this fragrance. The scent undergoes a very strong transformation, just like the character Turandot in Giacomo Puccini's opera. For me, the fragrance opens with the aldehyde note feeling somewhat aloof and cold, just as the princess Turandot does. Only over time does the princess thaw and develop, which I also see in the fragrance Turandot, which becomes sweet, fruity, creamy, and intimate in the heart note and possesses something familiar; it’s as if the fragrance shows its vulnerable side. For me, the fragrance shows a progression from the icy, aloof to the vulnerable, which remains until the end. It’s as if a barrier breaks between the top note and the base note. I think Roja Dove had a similar idea in mind during the creation, as this vulnerability is also described on the website in relation to Turandot. I can really imagine this scent very well on Princess Turandot. Here, Roja has truly captured his muse perfectly in the form of a fragrance.

You are lost, divine beauty! Life, father, is here. Turandot!........her fragrance fills the night. My thoughts are not quite so flowery, but I found the production of Turandot at the Vienna Opera in 2023 modern and understandable for people. For me, it was previously more of a screeching of men and women in ancient costumes, made up and powdered. Dear opera lovers, forgive my philistinism ;) The reason I enjoyed it so much was simply the Turandot, who did not screech but sang in higher registers. I thoroughly enjoyed those two and a half hours. Turandot by Roja Dove starts off sparkling with aldehydes. But right after the start, a beautiful rose joins in, and after a few more minutes, you can smell this wonderful peach that accompanies you all the way to the base. The blackcurrant provides a contrast to the sweet peach. I can't really pick out other flowers. Only the iris, which adds a powdery note, and heliotrope, which gives a very light almond note. Only in the base, as I perceive it, does the fragrance become more masculine: I now notice patchouli, coffee, cedar, and moss. That’s why I find it so exciting that so many men have this fragrance in their collection, because I perceive it as wonderfully feminine in the first hours. The fragrance starts with the aldehydes and the rose in a somewhat cold manner. The peach doesn't soften or sweeten the fragrance either. At first, I feel like an ice princess with it. Only towards the end, when it transitions from the heart to the base, does the fragrance become warmer and also more masculine. As if Calaf has transformed the cool Turandot. I love Roja Dove's stories; they are usually long and detailed. Turandot's story was not as expansive for me as others of his, but I believe it could become one of my favorite fragrance stories.

A fragrance inspired by the opera of the same name. As with most scents from Roja Dove, I find it difficult to interpret this one precisely, as the notes are so immensely intertwined. I will do my best. Overall, the fragrance smells very powdery and soft. Secondarily, I would say floral and fruity, but the powdery notes clearly dominate here.

I like Loewe fashion, but so far their fragrances are a total miss for me. Didn`t think I`d meet an aquatic scent that I could hate so much, but guess they gone and proved me wrong. I`m really curious which note is exactly responsible for the creepy sensation of chilled, sweet, wet drool that takes over on my skin. Aside from the pear, I seem to agree and even like most of the other components of that pyramid, so maybe it`s the calone? If I were to describe Aire Anthesis , I`d say it`s the beautiful peony in Pivoine Flora Eau de Parfum drowning in detergent powder and calones. I find it excruciatingly nauseating.

Initial cloud mostly consists of pear, but also has a broader fruity quality. Not the sweet kind – very fresh, almost unripe. Rhubarb is lovely, I wish it wasn't stuck on the sidelines. Sillage is moderate at first, but disappears completely in about ~1,5 hours. Fruitiness doesn't last long. In about ~20 minutes my skin became a crystal flower vase on the windowsill. Full of clean water, reflecting spots of sunlight; and of freshly cut flowers. Beautiful. But tell me, can a vase possibly know what kind of flowers are put in it, given that all it can feel is their freshly cut stalks? Well, neither could I. The scent was undeniably floral, but I felt like I was sniffing the flowers by the wrong end. It lasted on me for about ~6 hours in total, and past the initial fruity stage I was stuck smelling the flower stalks. Green, watery, rather funny in retrospect. I tested it later on my partner, and on him it didn't work at all. The florals opened up too aggressively on his skin, forming a "recently deep-cleaned public toilet" composition. Ah well, the more you know. The overall experience was... unique. But while it was both fun and pleasant while it lasted, this is not my kind of scent. It's pretty and feminine, and could be mesmerizing on a right woman, but I'm not that woman.

Imagine putting a crisp pear through the laundry. (Figuratively speaking). My favourite of the Aire suite. A fresh, greenish fruitquatic, without feeling sugary or soapy. It’s like describing a cucumber without ever saying the word or sampling its extract. Not that it smells like cucumber, just that Antithesis's olfactory charades pack the exact same ~vibe~. The only notes I could put my finger on were the pear and muguet, which blend into a succulent dew drop. I clocked its performance at around five hours on bare skin – pretty decent considering the clarity of its freshness. Mental Snapshot: Stock photo dew drops on a juicy pear. Stand in the produce aisle and bathe in the lettuce misters. Lay in the grass and allow yourself to be beaded in the sweet honeydew of a thousand benevolent aphids. tl;dr: Moisturized. Happy. In My Lane. Focused. Flourishing.

If you love the OG Oceania but hated the longevity, this is the solution. It keeps to the same scent, but slightly more citrusy in the opening and more depth in the dry down. This is such a beautiful scent and you can find this on discounters for $220. 100% worth it imo. Truly endgame worthy, honestly thinking of getting another bottle because I know I will run through the one I have.

In my experience in the fragrance community, I've found that there are (at least) two types of fragrance enthusiast: the adventuresome ones who want to smell utterly unique, and the people searching for "the one." "The one" doesn't have to be especially unique, artsy, weird, or challenging in any way, just be the best version of that person's favorite DNA or fragrance family. It took me a while, since I am mostly in the first camp, to realize that is why people go head over heels for scents like Imagination or Aventus when to me they are not really innovative or that creative. But I think I'm coming around to the views of the second camp. Not everything needs to be artsy and challenging. Sometimes the best version of a "common" scent profile is simply a great fragrance. And so we come to Oceania Parfum. Unfortunately I only tried the EDP once long ago, and only on strip, so I'm not going to do a compare/contrast. It could be that Oceania Eau de Parfum is completely identical and this is a redundant release, I wouldn't be able to tell you. But what a great scent this is. It starts a little rough, with a green sort of soapy accord dominating, the "old-school" lavender/bergamot combo, but this is definitely not just a "gentleman" scent that smells like grandpa's soap. More like a modern wet-shaving experience. The aquatic/ozonic notes then come in, which are not really listed in the note pyramid, and are grounded by masculine florals (I get mostly the geranium). At this stage it smells like a more natural version of a blue shower-gel type fragrance, but the best is yet to come. The drydown is absolutely gorgeous. A slightly smoked vetiver/oakmoss base with amber and musk, and I can swear I get some tobacco even though it is not listed. It's just effortlessly masculine and ultra high class. This is not your average "blue" scent. And yet, it's still a blue scent. A couple of years ago, I would have dismissed this as "just another." It might not be "the one" for me since I'm more of a collector than a seeker; but for someone searching for "the one," who's signature scent is currently Sedley or Silver Mountain Water , Oceania Parfum could very well be it.

First of all, my bottle is square and elongated with a dark orange glass, like the Loewe Solo. So not like depicted here on Parfumo. The scent Solo Mercurio opens quite spicy, slightly fresh with a decent splash of orange-colored, citrus-like synthetic notes. Mandarin and orange blossom accompanied by various spices. There's quite a lot happening at the beginning, which might not appeal to everyone. Then a spicy-herbaceous lavender note comes in, which I wouldn't describe as clean and pure, as one is more accustomed to with lavender. The spiciness remains throughout the entire progression, with cardamom setting the tone, while the ambered geranium presents a playfully sweet-floral image. The listed licorice can also be detected, in my perception. Somehow also sticky. In the drydown, slightly sweet and woody nuances come into play - honey and tobacco provide a nice presence. Here I find the scent truly most pleasant, as the top and heart notes are somewhat overloaded. Sillage is quite strong at the beginning but then fades relatively quickly. Longevity is average, not outstanding but also not bad.
