The scent development is not spectacular and rather linear until the drydown, which then transitions into a woody-sweet profile, leaving the spiciness behind. In my opinion, a somewhat playful men's fragrance for leisure activities. Its aromatic-spicy character fits perfectly into spring, as well as into the orange autumn and the golden late summer days.

This fragrance is simply beautiful, even though the performance could be better. It is soft and powdery, elegant and refined. This composition is gentle and transparent, the components are very well balanced, nothing irritates and nothing stands out. It tells the story of fruity May rose with a warm woody kick. The rose is also a bit fresh but without green notes. The other flowers in this bouquet are also really beautiful. Over time, this fine bouquet becomes slightly warm and herbaceous, and you can smell the vanilla. Enigma is suitable for wearing all year round and could also be a signature scent. It is totally feminine and of very high quality.

You are the woman I want to be. A vision of my future that began with the first hint of your essence. You smell like the women I admired as a child: strong, confident, beautiful, independent women who enjoy life and are at peace with themselves. Satisfied and lovely beings who exude the scent of harmony and sensuality. You smell like my future life, my complete being - how wonderful that we have met! You start classically beautiful, enveloping and calming me with your captivating fullness. You are immediately present, yet never overwhelming. You become finer and fresher, almost ethereally light. It is worth waiting for this moment. You end with a comforting satisfaction, delicate moments full of sensuality and love. Your fruity note is mature, pure, never too sweet or immature. Your bitter notes are sublime and harmonious. They radiate strength and underscore the femininity of your wearer. Your warm and sweet notes bring tranquility, serenity, and happiness. I will wear you often, you belong to me now and I to you. When I found you, I first realized that I had been searching for you.

Enigma. Just the name alone... nose wrinkled and curiosity piqued. Souk? A poor little problem is there in the foreign offerings. Additionally: With samples, I don't even bother if my interest goes beyond mere curiosity; they run out faster than I can think "Aha." And then you're left standing there again. So I cobbled together a Souk request at some point and forgot about it. And yet one day I received pink mail! A private message about it. A very attentive young lady had read my woes and mentioned she had a little bit, not much, but enough for testing, she wrote. Thank you, I said, and now let’s get to the point. Enigma. Enigma - according to Mr. Dove "MYSTERIOUS & COMPELLING". Aha. First of all: true. Mysterious in the sense that I could never imagine that anything with peach (especially written in large or bold letters) could appeal to me. Except for peaches themselves, very occasionally. (That's why I hadn't made any serious efforts to obtain it here.) And yet! Apparently, one just needs to know how to administer it to me. With soap, it works! Then a harmless, almost universally appealing peach (oh, sooo sweet, but no) turns into an elegant little fragrance. And this little treacherous fruit has indeed been washed so thoroughly that it is impossible for me to resist for long. The soapy peach doesn't develop much on me; it rather focuses on consistently impressing. A gentle sloth that knows what it can do. Every time I wear Enigma, I think to myself, I would really like to sit next to me. Not intrusive (although one should be a bit careful; as fluffy as one thinks, it’s not; I suspect it has a hefty presence), not too soapy, not too fruity, not a touch too much. I have no idea, but I would say: Perfect solution in terms of peach. Longevity? You shook me all night long. (By the way, its extreme endurance in my sweater caused that, ... let's leave that aside.) Enigma has remained a little riddle for me, but that’s okay.

Whether I love SOLO Absoluto or not, I’m here to give you my honest, detailed thoughts. And honestly—this is another spectacular fragrance from Loewe. It’s not an intensified version of the traditional Solo Eau de Toilette ; instead, it takes an entirely different path. The most notable difference? The guava note, so central to the original’s charm, is absent. In its place, a beautifully soothing orchid emerges, and that swap alone gives SOLO Absoluto its own personality—soft, warm, and distinctly comforting. Marketed as a sweet-oriental, woody, spicy, and slightly powdery fragrance, SOLO Absoluto includes notes like lavender, neroli, orchid, sandalwood, frankincense, bergamot, tangerine, wormwood, basil, tonka bean, amber, and musk. On my skin, only a handful of these stand out clearly—but the evolution is where the magic happens. It’s sweeter and deeper than the original SOLO, with a similar vibe after the top notes fade. Yet its development is quite different—more floral, a touch darker, and rich with velvety complexity. The orchid note is especially well-applied: delicate, present from the opening, and lingering gracefully throughout the heart. I have to say—the first few minutes after spraying offer one of the most beautiful aromas I’ve ever experienced in a fragrance. It’s immediately captivating. What follows is an elegant, slightly unusual blend: the sweetness of orchid, the resinous woods, and a gorgeous smoky trail of incense. Together, they create something genuinely soothing—like sipping a warm cup of Honey Orchid tea (Mi Lan Xiang), descended from old Phoenix Shui Xian trees with that rare, honeyed depth. Frankincense and tonka bean stay present from the opening through the dry-down—not overpowering, but just enough to create balance. They never feel cloying or overdone. Instead, they provide structure, grounding the orchid’s sweetness with smooth warmth. Interestingly, the musk, sandalwood, and other woody notes don’t emerge until hours later. Loewe seems to use a secret formula—the notes don’t unfold in typical order. Instead, they reappear unpredictably, like scent memories coming back in waves. It’s strange, but oddly appealing. The progression feels almost circular—revolving, not linear—and it keeps me engaged each time I wear it. This is a fragrance made for cool weather—perfect for fall, winter, and the early days of spring. It performs beautifully on my skin, with impressive longevity and above-average sillage. Smooth, intimate, and hypnotic. And let’s not forget the bottle: golden juice housed in clear glass with metallic gold accents—a luxurious vessel for a luxurious scent. — Elysium

But because it's (almost) Great. A striking Tangerine-Orchid-Incense, oriental. Rare is the orchid in men's "designer" class fragrances. This particular rarity is simultaneously Musky (in it's orchid), Arid (in it's incense), and Muted (in it's tangerine rind) : As opulent as it's concept may imply, "SOLO Absoluto" possesses a tonal balance that boasts very little contrast. Resulting in a lack of dynamism. Without any acidic brightness pass the opening, it very quickly became ashy, life-less, and claustrophobic. Like a beautiful gilded and bejeweled sarcophagus. Grand, but somber. Warm... alas, aloof. This is very much a Niche type work of... "art": Exquisite to admire on a blotter, but not necessarily as wearable, IMO. (Save for maybe with a poker face, for an upper-hand in business negotiations, LOL). Stunning bottle design and execution, to boot. Rather a disappointment. *Sighhhhh...*

This is a good release from Loewe. Lots of tonka with a small amount of incense and musky orchid note. Thats suitable for all year. Medium projection, sillage and lasting power. Definetely a must try. Updated September 2014

Let's get this out of the way first: Apex Eau Intense smells nothing like Apex Eau de Parfum . Apparently according to the Roja website they're calling it a chypre, but it is missing two out of the three components of a chypre in the note pyramid, labdanum and oakmoss, and I don't smell them either. So not a chypre, no resemblance to Apex. Apex Eau Intense is a light green fruity woody scent that reminds me a bit of the "Aqua" series by MFK, although the musk in the base is not as prominent as most of the ones in that collection. Slightly fruity sweet opening with lots of citrus, and stays fresh throughout its lifetime, supported by ambroxan and woody notes in the base. It's like a heightened, more well-defined version of a designer freshie. What it's trying to do is similar to the LV freshies—mainstream, but better than department store fragrances. And that begs the question, why is this shit on (Parfumo rating is not bad at 7.6 but Fragrantica has it sitting at 3.5, equivalent to 7.0 in Parfumo terms) while fragrances like Afternoon Swim , Pacific Chill , and L'Immensité are almost universally praised? I enjoy Apex Eau Intense much more and the quality, idea, and even pricing are very much similar. My only answer is that the expectations are different; Roja fragrances are held to a higher standard. Or perhaps it's the decrying of niche houses going "mainstream" even though Roja has always made quite mass-pleasing fragrances like Elysium pour Homme Parfum and Oceania Eau de Parfum , which are also very much liked by the community.

Apex Eau Intense is Roja's second Eau Intense flanker, following Elysium Eau Intense in 2023. With Elysium Eau Intense, the scent came after the Parfum Cologne and Parfum concentrations with the scent ultimately smelling like a twist on "Elysium Parfum Cologne (Eau de Parfum) | Roja Parfums" as it introduced a prominent rhubarb note. However, with this Apex flanker, it was always going to be a hard sell as the two products inspiring the flanker are fougère fragrances and a fresh fougère would still be a fougère... or would it? After putting on Apex Eau Intense , the very first thing that I wrote down is that it doesn't smell like the original Apex Eau de Parfum . The flanker opens citrus-aromatic with light tea feel which made me think it was closer to scents like Aqua Media Cologne Forte and Wūlóng Chá Extrait de Parfum . The performance felt pretty poor off the rip and the scent doesn't have much special about it up-close either where it initially smells like a pretty standard citrus-aromatic with a prominent lemon note. Some nuances of barbershop are featured due to the woody-musky base, making me think of scents like "Casamorati - Mefisto | XerJoff". I feel like once we get out of the initial moments, we get to see some nuances that can be associated with Apex, but in a completely different way. In the base, the two notes that I can pick up on the most are the grass and the driftwood, with the driftwood specifically reminding me of the composition of Clive Christian's Crab Apple Blossom . Ultimately, the scent is very much a woody citrus-aromatic, but the green touches are noteworthy in the base. The overall package being proposed here is underwhelming. Performance does indeed end up at poor and it never really had much lift to begin with. I would place the longevity at around 4 hours with the sillage being intimate. The scent retails at €335/100ml, but the product itself shouldn't be anywhere near that price point. To summarize, there's nothing here that's even mildly reminiscent of the Apex Eau de Parfum DNA outside of the name. Apex Eau Intense slots in next to Roja's Parfum Cologne line where they sell various watered-down (and generic) products for nearly the same price.

So in the 8°C wet outdoor drizzles though: quick minute fun creamy citrus diffuses into dry bitter Lime zest, builds Cardamom, Patchouli, Pepper accord main presence. No Mint in the cold, subtle Sage, overal woody, slight spicy and dry. To me this is an edible, dry bitter greens. Great Eau de Cologne, on first couple of tries seamns to be not an oversprayer, get's kinda powdery on plus 5 puffs, don't recognize no similar general Roja notes.

Apex Eau Intense starts with a real explosion of mint, which soon either loses intensity significantly or overwhelms my sense of smell to the point that I can no longer perceive it in its entirety. Similar to @Montross, I also perceive a fruity melon alongside it, evoking a longing for summer and memories of stifling, sultry days at the outdoor pool. Looking at the fragrance pyramid, this opening is a bit confusing, as it presents a completely different scent impression than I would have expected. And while the opening fades away, a hint of "Oceania | Roja Parfums" briefly envelops a powdery violet leaf that has been present from the start, as if to remind us that at Roja, one does not want to entirely forget oneself and wishes to integrate the self-referential charm of the brand into the new, seemingly modern identity. But before one can fully grasp this scent impression, it has already vanished. Instead of taking us to the beach, Apex Eau Intense takes us to a meadow, to days by the lake, the feeling of grass on wet skin, and the smell of earth. The base becomes warmer, without being warm, earthy and green. Here in the heart, the scent impression aligns again with the expectations raised by the fragrance pyramid. The fruitiness is still present in the background, but has lost some sweetness, and with a bit of imagination, one might actually see the listed mandarin in it from a distance. Similar to the already mentioned "Oceania | Roja Parfums," the powdery aspects of the fragrance here transform into a creamy consistency. Perhaps the same sandalwood accord can indeed be found behind the green medley. This could all be quite nice, even if it does not cover my primary preferences, if it weren't for a synthetic wood note that runs through the fragrance, which, in combination with the violet leaf, may not be unpleasant to everyone, but makes this scent less appealing to me. So what is the conclusion regarding the official debut of the brand's new perfumer? Overall, one must say that Roja has successfully implemented its goal of giving the brand a modern identity. Apex Eau Intense has little in common with the classics of the house and fits well into newer releases like Isola Sol or "Elysium pour Femme (Parfum) | Roja Parfums." Cynics might claim that Roja has taken on a touch of insignificance and has not done itself any favors by shifting from its vintage-inspired fragrances to a designer flair. But it would also be wrong to objectively call Apex Eau Intense a bad fragrance. It will surely find its admirers, but it will not find a place in my collection.

Normally, I am not a fan of fresh scents, whether "blue," "green," or pale purple. Just for reference, my preferred selection ranges between YSL Cuir, ATH Onyx, Satin Mood, and when I need something more subtle, a TF Noir. However, I have always made an exception for Apex. Both the EDP and the perfume give off great old school vibes without feeling dusty, being more fresh-spicy than an ambroxan bomb, and in my opinion, a good alternative for the office and "normal" social settings. The perfume presents the wonderful DNA a bit stronger and smokier, hence my favorite. Now here comes the eau intense... and suddenly you have a lighter DNA of its predecessor, mixed with fruity minty shower gel vibes... Of course, one turns up their nose at that. I’d rather just take the EDP, especially since the price difference isn’t much. And yet - you find yourself repeatedly digging it out and applying it. Especially when you want to avoid being too powerful (negatively) with the h/s bombs and the smoky clouds that are more reserved for true fragrance enthusiasts. To be fair, the eau intense is a lovely scent after all. It is just a variant of Apex, a homage if you will. But for a true fragrance lover, a "nice" scent just isn’t enough. H/s are satisfactory for everyday use; you notice it time and again, and by the evening of a long workday, there’s still a light veil left. In conclusion, as a self-reflective person, I must point out that my OA favorites are almost full, while my eau intense is half empty. Even the Apex perfume looks enviously at the youngling. Why? Well, we fragrance lovers are just not the masses. And in everyday life, you find yourself in situations where you don’t want to overwhelm others or waste a valuable treasure inappropriately. So, you do need the "nice" scent and not the glorious 11/10. All in all - beautiful scent DNA, for all who liked Apex and are looking for a change, as well as those who want to evolve from freshies, with satisfactory h/s. We don’t need to talk about price, but how many of us perfume lovers are REALLY price-sensitive? We have the wrong hobby for that. I like it, and it works for me as it should. Everyone needs an everyday hero, even we self-proclaimed scent connoisseurs!

This is my first review. A little about me, I own between 75-100 perfumes of various directions and my two favorite perfumes are the wulong cha nishane and indeed the layton exclusive. I have never been captivated by a truly green scent and have not owned one before. About the brand: I usually associate the house of Roja with a wonderful complex fragrance.

I love green, fresh scents, which is why this is the perfect fragrance for me. I am new to the "niche game" and my nose is not very trained yet, so my descriptions might not be very clear - I will do my best. The scent really starts with a fresh kick to the face - in the best way.

The first time I tried Gala - I think it was a sample that a kind person sent to me, many years ago - I was completely floored. A wonderful, huge blast of soft aldehydes, sweet, very realistic jasmine, creamy sandalwood and loads and loads of dark, animalic castoreum... I had never smelled anything like it. It was like a huge piece of beautiful cloth, a blanket, a cape, a shawl, I am not sure exactly what, it was soft and heavy at the same time, it was dark velvet and airy lace, and I just wanted to wrap myself in it and breath in the beautiful scent forever. I knew I had to have it, and ordered a bottle immediately. Strangely enough, I hardly ever wore it. I suppose I found it a little difficult to wear in public, I was worried that its heavy animalic trail would scare people away. Vintage perfumes sometimes have that effect on those who are not used to them. I love animalic perfumes myself, but yes, I admit that with some of them, people might sometimes wonder if perhaps you didn't wash for a while. So Gala stayed in my closet, unused for years. I tested it again recently, and found that I am not as enchanted by it as I was all those years ago. I feel that the castoreum floats on top like a much too heavy lid, it doesn't blend in with the rest in the way that I remember, and I keep wishing for it to go away. It makes me a bit sad, because when you remember something as being very beautiful, you want it to stay that way. But maybe it's just me - getting older, no longer able to carry that gorgeous velvet-lacy cape with the natural grace that it requires. Gala will remain with me as a bitter-sweet memory in a beautiful bottle.

For a long time, I had been searching for an evening and night fragrance that would provide a counterpoint to my green-dominated collection. That it would ultimately be a floral-animalic-balsamic scent with a smoky amber note, and moreover from the creative kitchen of a Spanish perfume house known primarily for its fresh, lightly floral, and herbal women's creations, did surprise me. If Gala were a piece of clothing, it would be a fitted dress with a seductive back neckline - meaning it is an overtly elegant, balsamic-floral, and yet not sweet fragrance, whose subtle animalic component adds a touch of sexiness and wonderfully rounds off the opulent scent. Gala starts off zesty with citrus fruits, green notes, and aldehydes, while the unsweetened flowers of the heart note, especially the clove, lend elegance to Gala and make the fragrance shine. After about an hour, the civet and beaver make a brief appearance. However, both little creatures behave very decorously and add spice, warmth, and depth to Gala alongside patchouli, sandalwood, resins, and amber, as well as a hint of eroticism. In the green-woody, ambered base, spices mix in that are not listed in the pyramid, which I attribute to a consistently noticeable clove. Gala is a floriental that definitely shows presence, radiance, and a strong sillage, yet it is not a loud fragrance and certainly not a blockbuster. Nevertheless, in my opinion, it is not a scent for days with early summer and midsummer temperatures. It simply develops much more beautifully on cooler days. Especially women whose perfume socialization took place in the 80s and before will love Gala or at least appreciate it. Younger women may find it too intense, strong, and too much a child of the early 90s.

The large double door opens and I walk through the wide entrance to the crystal-lit hall. My gown is made of dark violet silk taffeta, and the train, adorned with gold embellishments, sways with each step. A blossomed rose, also in dark violet, is nestled in my elegantly styled hair. My cavalier approaches and offers me his arm. We stride to the center of the hall, and at the moment the light from the oversized crystal chandelier captures us, the orchestra begins to play a waltz. Lightheartedly, we take off and dance across the expansive ballroom floor. The opening is floral-green and immediately captures full attention. We spin faster, following the rhythmic melodies. The rich bouquet leaves no room for contingencies, demanding its tribute right away. The orchestra plays with full passion. Then, after what feels like an eternity, the moment arrives when the heart of Gala opens, and pure nobility is in the air! The strong rhythms fade, and the tempo adjusts. We join the other dancers and glide elegantly, almost weightlessly. Now everything seems to blur-the sparkling light, the dancing couples, the intoxicating colors of the elegant evening gowns, and this enchanting scent of the grand, opulent floral arrangements around us. Wonderfully finely woven floral accords come together. Not as soft and delicate as silk, but rather like a noble silk taffeta, slightly strengthened yet so wonderful to see and touch. A radiant floral cream, like a symphony, smooths the surface. I spin and spin and spin, dancing through the night of grand fairy tales and float away until the spicy amber base note accompanies me home on a velvet green carpet late at night. I can still vaguely perceive the scent of my rose in my hair the next morning.... ~ A celebration like one out of a storybook, a grand entrance in a magnificent gown on a very special evening-Gala is a must! ~ Conclusion: I count Gala by Loewe among the fragrances that should not be worn "just like that," but rather deserve a truly grand entrance. My first thought when I encountered Gala was of a ball, a gala-a major event-where such a magnificent scent cannot be missed. And indeed, Gala is a magnificent fragrance! Just the bottle alone exudes opulence and splendor. In satin-finished dark violet glass, it presents itself beautifully with a golden, embellished collar at the base, and fittingly, it has a matching lid, also adorned with a collar of decorated gold. The overall appearance reminds me a bit of a lady with a hat (...in a gown with a wide crinoline and a delicate waist). Nevertheless, this appearance benefits the fragrance, as this beautiful fullness is reflected in the scent itself. Some ladies may feel overwhelmed by the endless top note and flee in fright. Strong (olfactory) nerves are required here. Some perfumers would describe this opening as "boom." Even as it unfolds, Gala shows no weakness; it remains opulent and grand. This is not a terrifying blast that robs the dear surroundings of breath, but rather a strong, well-composed fragrance with expression! Therefore, it should not be worn in everyday situations and certainly not during meals. This scent demands its own personal show and will undoubtedly be the grande diva among the other "fragrances" at many festivities. A grand spectacle, as Chanel described, a big entrance-for a grand evening.... or should I write: for the grand night! ~ And now let’s pop the corks: So glad you exist, Gala! You are the reason to celebrate big once again! Thanks to "DeKant" for this wonderful gift!

First, I must quickly clarify that I am not a fan of German pop music, nor of Cindy + Bert (does anyone here know them?). Unfortunately, my ex-mother-in-law was a big fan, and especially enjoyed playing this song during visits. If she hadn't served such delightful Alsatian dishes, I would have stayed away. So I just tuned out. Even after the divorce, we had a good relationship, which is apparently quite rare, but she was a wonderful person. Last year, she sadly passed away, and my children and I miss her very much, and now I even miss the Flammkuchen with Cindy + Bert. When I used Gala this morning, the song and the whole sad story came back to me. I got to know Gala by Loewe in Fuengirola near Malaga when I was on a mini-vacation there with a friend, as I often did in the mid/late 90s. We were both born on the same day, only she was about 20 years older and had more money. But the remarkable thing about our friendship was - we both collected bottles back then and had the same taste. This even led to occasional little competitions, but we always handled them fairly and maturely. When it came to fragrances, however, our tastes completely diverged!! Everything I loved back then, she found unbearable, and vice versa. I loved Fendi Asja, which gave her a headache. She often wore Eau de Soir, which I found unpleasant. We strolled past a perfumery that had Gala on display. "Great bottle," we said in unison, and went inside. Since she had the lead this time, she asked if the large factice was for sale. The saleswoman consulted in Spanish with another person, then called someone, and then came to the conclusion: Yes, the factice is for sale, but only with the others standing there, and it costs 15,000 pesetas. My friend had no interest in the 2 small factices and wanted to negotiate the price down, but no luck. She bought the "set" anyway; otherwise, I would have done it, and she gave me the two supposed small factices. Upon closer inspection, however, it turned out that one of them was a tester. I sprayed the fragrance. Ka-Boom. A soccer ball-sized orange jumped at me without warning. Whether something is mentioned in the pyramid or not, I don't care at all, because the top note is orange in syrup with Grand Marnier. My friend gasped and said, "It's awful, don't you think?" I did not think so. The heart note is so beautifully creamy-balsamic-floral that I wore the fragrance on many occasions thereafter, even though it was actually too heavy for warm weather, especially under the southern sun. The base is amber, green-woody, animalic, and veeeery spicy. Super long-lasting, the sillage is a big show. An unusual Spanish fragrance. Hombre, hombre, hombre! It always brings to mind an image of the Alhambra for me, as this Spaniard is more of an oriental, as if the Moors had a hand in it. For me, full of memories, and even without these, it would be my favorite Spaniard.

“Lakmé” - a new Roja fragrance for my curious nose; of course, I had to test it right away. And once again, it is a commission for the Royal Opera House Muscat in Oman, for which Roja Dove transformed the music from a classical opera into scent. This time it was Léo Delibes’ “Lakmé”; who doesn’t immediately hear the floating sound of the “Flower Duet”? The idea of filling the entire audience area with this fragrance at the beginning of this enchanting piece of music, so that rose and iris aromas accompany these tones, is already fascinating. “Sous le dôme épais Où le blanc jasmin À la rose s’assemble Sur la riev en fleurs.” Not exactly matching the text, but I don’t want to be too precise. Whose idea was this? Was it once again “the master” himself? (However, there’s also the question of how this Roja fragrance experience matched the scent garments of the audience: This idea confuses me a bit. Or was the audience asked to appear “sans parfum” or “fragrance free” to avoid a scent chaos?) It is said to have been the Eau de Parfum concentration that accompanied this “earworm” from Delibes in floral splendor. This is in the small spray bottle left to me: So off to Oman to the opera! First, I have to get my bearings: Since I am used to perfumes or extraits with Roja fragrances, this concentration seems a bit light at first! But when I think of the music, of the floating tones of the “Flower Duet,” I realize: Everything is as it should be! Too much of this fragrance would overwhelm that enchanting, floating sound. It is a true Roja composition, as genuine as the already mentioned duet bears the signature of Léo Delibes. It deviates slightly in the heart note from the expected “Roja-nade” (or whatever we want to call the Guerlinade-like scent structure); the iris is successfully shifted to the base and contributes to a special fragrance experience from there; jasmine is completely absent this time. But first, Hesperid notes shine in the usual accompaniment of aldehydes: A citrus-fresh fireworks greets, awakens interest, and already makes one smile for the first time. These fragrance notes envelop and prepare for a rather astonishing heart of scent. But I miss the iris and jasmine mentioned in the context here! So the white-flowered power comes solely from the small, brave lily of the valley: sweet and herbaceous at the same time, intensely fragrant and always slightly on the verge of becoming “stinky.” This is what the little bell has in common with its partner jasmine: When they become truly ripe, the resulting scent drives many noses away: Both run the risk of becoming “little stinkers”! Well, I love them in this state - but that’s just a side note. Lily of the valley does not disappoint, rather hums than sings loudly, but clearly shows presence and harmonizes exceptionally well with the noble nuances of the fine roses, and thus the ripe, velvety sweet and juicy peaches find themselves in the best floral company! A resinous-woody base spreads out; now the master swims again in familiar fragrant waters. The mixture is exquisite, consisting of the usual suspects: Labdanum and benzoin, frankincense and amber stand alongside musk, providing aromatic smoky impressions, the animalic quality of sandalwood unites, as often, with the rich, warm sensuality of vanilla, but is still - don’t forget: We are in the Orient! - topped with ripe, dark oud! While oud is not entirely unexpected in the base composition of a Roja gem, the proud iris as a powdery finishing note surprises now (as already mentioned)! The transition from the previous floral, woody-resinous fragrance creation to the rich powder scent is successful! “Lakmé” is an interesting fragrance composition, and the recurring “Flower Duet” in the background further emphasizes this effect. But the two of us will not meet again in the future; experiencing a fragrant performance was impressive, but it does not leave the impression I am used to. Is it just the concentration; is the Eau de Parfum too light for me? Perhaps I also need to learn to understand that the floating lightness of Delibes’ “Flower Duet” is also reflected in this Roja fragrance composition and that is why I miss the usual opulent depth.

Lakmé, the name sounds like creamy full milk chocolate from Hachez, melting on the tongue. I was lucky enough to receive a sample from a charming Parfumo. I don't exactly know how aldehydes smell, but the first minutes are extremely harsh for me; I can't place the scent, maybe a faint plastic smell. Now a very smooth, bright, white, uplifting floral scent unfolds. It floats above me, completely fresh. Then I see a juicy orange-yellow peach in a round peach glass filled with sparkling Prosecco. In front of it stands a bouquet of lily of the valley. After about an hour, a fragrance euphoria unfolds that is indescribable. Wonderfully creamy, cuddly, rich, complex, and full of volume. The warm combination envelops me, and I smell sandalwood, vanilla, and musk perfectly blended. I am wearing it now in early summer, and it fits perfectly. Every day for a week, and it becomes more expressive; I would say it's unisex. Lakmè absolutely must have!!!

in the land of elves, fairies, and unicorns, one does not breathe mundane air... no, Roja's fairy dust gently lies over the softly blurred hills and valleys... everything sounds soft, melodic, and fine... everything blooms wonderfully in pastel tones... a light cloud of smoke rises in the distance... everything in harmonious perfection... Roja enters another world and lets us partake in it... only the label is irritating... silver-gray speckles in fluffy pink would be more fitting... the elixir bottle would be the first choice here... thank you, Dove, for this journey... the fragrance starts lightly fruity floral... develops more and more into a softly floral sweetness with a hint of vanilla... incense barely noticeable... rather supports to avoid slipping into the kitschy...

Since I own the 7 Eau de Toilette and the 7 Anonimo, both of which have a very distinctive incense scent, I decided to try the 7 Sport. The first thing that came to mind was the scent of Aramis Life my Summer. They definitely have a similar smell. The 7 Sport has nothing in common with the 7 edt and 7 Anonimo. This one really smells fresh, green, and citrusy delicious. Anyone who liked Life my Summer will love this one. The 7 Sport is a bit rounder; I assume this is due to the amber and incense. The bottle is okay. The longevity is very good, easily 8 hours, so don't overdo it with the spraying. The 7 Sport definitely has, despite the freshness, a special depth/warmth at the end. In my opinion, this comes from the neroli, amber, and incense. Tomato leaf and yuzu are always subtly in the background, unobtrusively accompanying the fragrance experience. It definitely smells unique and does not need to hide from the other fresh scents from other manufacturers. On the contrary, this one stands out, as I personally don't know of any other fragrance twin like it, except for the mentioned Aramis Life my Summer.

One might chuckle at the old GDR television format that stubbornly occupied a very good time slot for decades, where various school teams competed in sports contests to crown their champion every two years, with a trophy (sic) from the National Olympic Committee of the GDR awaiting them. It reflects very well my thoughts that I experienced while wearing 7 Loewe Sport - fragrances in competition, and then one at the center that even carries "Sport" in its name. One might think that the fragrance could be aiming to shake up the field of fresh-spicy mainstream scents a bit. For me, it works quite well... To stick with the television format, there are several competitors with which 7 Loewe Sport, the entry from Spain, can and wants to compete. For Italy, we have: Armani's classic Acqua di Gio, Bvlgari's Aqva Amara, Cerruti Image Fresh Energy, Aqua Nautilus, and Aqua di Roma; for the USA, Perry Ellis 360 Degrees Red for men, as well as Clinique Happy for men (CK One unfortunately does not qualify); for Japan, Eau d'Issey pour homme. For me, 7 Loewe Sport holds its own well against the mentioned candidates, and I would consider it my winner in this shootout. It starts very herbaceous-citrusy, almost a bit piercing and penetrating. The yuzu note is clearly recognizable, and there are indeed associations with Eau d'Issey. Similarly penetrating, wiry-citrusy is Fresh Energy, which conveys everything a bit scratchy and metallic. The citrus note is significantly more herbaceous in both than in Clinique Happy for Men and Acqua di Gio, where the mandarin offers a somewhat softer, wellness-like introduction. Acqua di Gio seems a bit paler after all these years compared to the original version, which I really liked when I first smelled it in the mid-90s; by now, it has been smelled very, very often, so it feels somewhat worn out to me, parallel to the increasing dilution through reformulation. Perry Ellis presents this even more penetratingly, piercingly, and somewhat more synthetically, while Aqua Nautilus in its current version is a bit darker and spicier. The last three bring a distinctly fruity note that feels a bit more playful and approachable, which is not the case with Loewe and Fresh Energy. What I like about Loewe are the somewhat "cooler" facets introduced by mint and tomato leaf, providing a pleasantly cooling effect. As it develops, Loewe remains relatively straightforward, becoming a bit woodier and radiating a clear, but not soapy, cleanliness through the notes of incense and musk, which also adds a somewhat warmer, soft pulsating quality in hot temperatures. Slightly woody elements can also be perceived, as mentioned. However, it does not have the somewhat pressing central woodiness of Eau d'Issey pH, which I could never really warm up to despite longer wear. For me, it rather evoked associations with utility wood cuts in a sawmill, which is one reason why I never fully liked the fragrance, and also, when I smelled it on someone else, it underscored my reservations. Additionally, there is perhaps the somewhat unfair and subjective accusation that Eau d'Issey, on the one hand, was intentionally edgy, yet also unisex, and thus always seemed a bit "expert" to me, in relation to the range of well-available men's fragrances at the time, just as a current bestseller might be unfairly labeled as a "teacher's scent" out of envy. The drydown of Loewe remains a radiant, clean, yet also somewhat warm, steamy impression that stays very linear, while fortunately avoiding cucumber-like, melon-like elements, as found in Aqva Amara, Acqua di Roma, or Sel de Marin, which I unfortunately do not like much due to their stylistic proximity to sporty women's fragrances of the 90s, such as New West for Her, Sunflowers, or Polo Sport Woman. I appreciate the cooling freshness, which, in greater heat, is once again intercepted by the pulsation of musk and incense, making the fragrance very suitable for hot days or sporty activities. I cannot deny a certain synthetic quality; Iso E-Super might well be at play here, as is the case with Escentric 01 and Theorema Uomo; in my opinion, it serves a good purpose. White T-shirt, very hot day, and 7 Loewe Sport, that fits me very well. For me, the fragrance, despite many parallels to well-known classics, is a nice addition in the direction of herb-clean freshness. The bottle is heavy, feels good in the hand, and is somewhat quirky with the integrated, almost deodorant-spray-like nozzle, but it allows for good dosing and creates a rather cylindrical spray area. Whether the special edition with the blue stripes that I have here offers any added value, I will leave open. All in all, a successful all-rounder for hot days, especially when one is done with Acqua di Gio and Eau d'Issey pH. An honor from the NOK of the GDR is, however, not to be expected anymore. At this point, many thanks again to InGENIEur for the swap.

Today I tried Loewe 7 Sport - and thought: This is not for couch potatoes! I spontaneously recalled my first encounter with my friend Paul - a true Spaniard. We sat in icy, oppressive silence during a job center workshop in a classroom, straining our ears over solving some math problems, tricky ones, as this gathering was only for drop-out students. No one knew anyone - tense atmosphere. As I sighed and set aside my scribbles, you could still hear a pin drop. Suddenly, an attractive young man with black hair turned to me, smiled at me warmly, and called out across the aisle: What are you up to? I want to chat! Wonderful! We chatted lively with each other, and the other delinquents also woke up from their shock paralysis. My Paul had broken the ice, and we were like two peas in a pod until the end of the workshop. Neither of us could sit still, and we received many reprimands for chatting. And 7 Sport is also a lively "icebreaker". Mandarin and Yuzu are cheerful and invigorating - the mint, on the other hand, is cool and thoughtful. The tomato leaf appears green and original, and the neroli enhances concentration. Soft warmth spreads through amber, and the incense is attractively masculine. A fragrance with temperament and depth. Tailor-made for my Paul, as he could be both charmingly funny and profound - but also great at losing his temper. I recently heard with joy that he has made a steep career. Ole Paul!

So, I’ll write a comment too :-) Just been on vacation and got this fragrance, I think it’s a great summer scent that starts off very fresh, at least on my skin! The scent develops only after a good hour and I can definitely smell the incense. The fragrance lasts a good 5-6 hours, which I personally find sufficient for a summer scent!

If I had only three words to describe Rive Gauche Pour Homme, I'd say "woody marine aromatic." Now as for the rest of this review, I'll trace the etymology of each of these words back to -- just kidding. This scent combines a faintly sugary pine with an aromatic water-wind freshness for a few feet projection. It's fresh without being soapy and masculine without veering into machismo territory. It evokes a sense of gentlemanly class without being stuffy, arrogant, or overly mature. Interestingly, it lends class to whatever you’re wearing, instead of forcing you to wear something specific. Rest easy; you won't feel unworthy in your workout clothes. I can see why this fragrance appeals to men, and why men wearing this would appeal to women. Words like "class" and "quality" come to mind, both in describing the notes and their effect. Occasionally, it takes a swerve like a distracted driver into a urinary/stale smell that lasts a minute or so. That's the only negative here. Even the duration pleases, clocking in at eleven hours. Rive Gauche Pour Homme provides an inexpensive and satisfying way to smell like a gentleman and obtain a self-esteem boost. It's been discontinued, so grab it while you can! Recommended.

Rive Gauche for Men is a timeless masterpiece that deserves widespread availability. I'd love some of the younger men in my life to have the opportunity to experience something so extravagant and earthy as this. Rich and herbaceous, Rive Gauche for Men is understandably an acquired taste. However that's not to say that this fragrance is in any way offensive or loud. I would actually say this fragrance is quite clean and refreshing despite its earthiness. The scent leaves me slightly perplexed at times with its clean, shaving cream accord counteracting with a somewhat dirty/earthy patchouli, clove and vetiver blend. Essentially, Rive Gauche for Men jumps to and fro between gentleman cleanliness and raw, masculine filthiness. This is what makes this fragrance so intriguing. As a woman, I wouldn't dare wear Rive Gauche for Men, that is unless I chose to get in touch with the barbarian behind the reserved exterior. On a man's skin, this fragrance exudes elegance and old-fashioned charm, like a slick man in a tuxedo puffing ever so gently on a cigar. Rive Gauche for Men perfectly compliments the feminine version of this fragrance, which bears the same name. They both share a classic powderiness that when worn on the skin can create a dense and rich feeling. In my opinion, Rive Gauche has not reached its use by date, even though I will admit that it has the tendency to appeal to much older men. The sillage is moderate but thankfully not too strong and I'm happy to say that the scent lasts and lasts.

Brilliant. Awesome. The epitome of contemporary men's perfumes. Truly masculine, this is a masterpiece. One of the best releases of all time. Anise, lavender and rosemary are the most pronounced notes to my nose. A modern aromatic fougere without losing tradition. It has a barber shop smell, which is wonderful for me. Classic and modern, serves for the whole year and at any time and station. If you like Azzaro, Chanel Platinum Egoiste, you'll love Rive Gauche. Sillage, staying power and projection are good. Versions 1) Original tin can version - has written "Yves Saint Laurent Parfums" on the packaging - the first version, more charged in anise and oak moss. 2) Reformulated tin can version - has written only "Yves Saint Laurent" on the package - more herbal, with rosemary notes and more pronounced patchouli. 3) La Collection version - latest version, glass - lighter version and cooler with less moss and less anise. 4) Rive Gauche Light - far more diluted and fresher version, with a pronounced mint note in his opening - shorter duration. 5) Rive Gauche Intense - more rounded version of the original, longer duration - more evident patchouli note. Updated December 2014

When I was first contemplating which fragrance I wanted to buy for myself, it was between this and YSL Opium for Men. I couldn't decide which one to get between the two. I ended up getting them both! I wore the Opium a few times and while I did like the scent, I found it to be too strong and overpowering to my nose. I ended up giving my bottle away. I finally got around to wearing Rive Gauche. Right away I liked it. Not too strong, perfectly blended, smooth and soothing. The lavender and soft spices in this are so beautiful! One of the best men's colognes I've smelled in awhile. It's unique and different with a personality all its own. I can see myself reaching for this quite often. Smells clean and masculine without being too over-the-top macho. Perfect for any occasion. Every man should have this in their collection.

Rive Gauche pour Homme is a thick, heavy aromatic fougère. Its aromatic notes are balanced, but aren’t key players. They are the Greek chorus to the lavender and coumarin that define RGpH. Clove focuses our attention on the coumarin, and rosemary and geranium steer us to the lavender. RGpH reminds me of what I love about the fougère. Because the interaction of lavender and coumarin plays out mostly as contrast rather than agreement, the greater the counterpoint, the better the fougère. The aromatics merely keep our attention on the lavender and coumarin and their combined raspiness. If the accord is stark, the transitions are not. It moves easily from an enveloping church organ blast of a perfume to a brisk barbershop slap to a husky whisper. There is nothing superfluous. The fragrance emerges from the fundamental duality of its defining elements. RGpH is not pretty, it’s handsome. By historic fragrance norms, it is so classically masculine that I can’t help but feel like I’m in man-drag when I wear it. By the same reasoning, it’d be loads of fun on a femme woman.

Un parfum doit avant tout sentir bon. (A perfume must above all smell good.) ~Guy Robert~ And that's exactly what Rive Gauche pour Homme does! A "modern fougere". IMO, everyone should have RGpH in their collection. It's not my #1 favorite but it's a solid, clean smelling, non-offensive performer that's perfect for when you just want to smell good.

If you're facing this perfume for the first time, your facial impression when you realize that Rive Gauche is a 2003 production would be hilarious! I had the same face once! This is quite interesting and very daring to flashback to aromatic fougères while their era is demographically ceased. Rive Gauche is the last standing powerhouse this around.

Like Turin wrote in his guide, “it took guts to come out with an aromatic fougère in 2003”: it did, indeed, as Rive Gauche pour Homme is truly a jump into the Seventies. Not a “rewritten tribute”, but a veritable, extremely elegant and pleasantly pedantic aromatic fougère exactly as they made (plenty of) them thirty years ago.
Please enjoy my video review of Rive Gauche Pour Homme. Classy, luxurious shaving-cream scent dominated by star anise, lavender on a classic fougere base.

Scentrack: The Bastardz - Love Dance Unbelievably good retro-avant-garde (oxymoron) shaving cream fragrance. Like some old time residues in the air, perfectly made for rainy urban landscapes. A fantastic blend of star anise, Mediterranean bouquet of rosemary and lavender on the darker base of patchouli and vetiver. Classy, sophisticated and reliable.

If you are not wearing a suit, you have no reason to wear this perfume. This perfume is so elegant, so luxurious. The scent opens with notes of bergamot and mandarin orange. After it settles on the skin for a bit, the vetiver arrives, which you can feel throughout the scent with a combination of coriander and cardamom. A perfume that is suitable for evening and special occasions, especially with a suit! Or any other elegant outfit ! For me : 8.5/10

This one will fool you. Upon initial spray and opening, the vibe is that of a very well done traditional citrus aromatic fougere - in the vein of eau sauvage, scandal, etc. The opening was a bit disappointing, if I'm honest. It smells great, very high quality and complex blend to be sure, but I just didn't need another trad citrus aromatic fougere..... BUT, it changes quickly on skin. The citruses are there, sure, but the fragrance becomes a rich, elegant, regal, woody, even modern mens fragrance. I've heard this described as smelling like money, and I get it. It does smell very refined, very expensive, but not terribly stodgy. It has modern aspects - I smell a bit of Apex, a touch of sauvage elixir in this. Not so much the spice, but the clean hardwoods and green notes at the base give an echo of that profile, but they're not redundant due to the citruses and florals lending a smooth, fresh, elegant layer that doesn't exist in Apex/Sauvage Elixir. The overall vibe is a bit different from those, and the brutal masculinity that hammers the nose in Apex is softened and lightened, freshened and cleaned here. But, it's still there lurking around the corner - making no apologies. Overall, this fragrance grew on my quickly and strongly. Don't let the first 20 minutes fool you, it's going to get better and get different. Not for young men per se, unless you want to smell completely mature and confident. This can clown you if you aren't confident with it. Projection is on the strong side of moderate. Longevity is 8 hours, easy. Scent on this gets better and better as it develops. 8.75/10 Overall a traditional, but modern tinged mature mens fragrance, for mild temps.

Goodman's is truly an exceptionally good men's fragrance in the Chypre or Fougere category and currently for me the reference in this category. I'm not too strict about the differences between Chypre and Fougere :-) The scent progression has already been nicely described here... it starts off a bit citrusy/fruity, then a few flowers come in (but very subtle) and the drydown goes towards wood, green, and spicy. Conclusion: A very nice men's fragrance that has so far outperformed all comparable scents in this category that I have tested, such as Viking, Diaghilev, etc.

After this insatiable hunting fever and collecting passion has led me into the territory of Roja, of course, the filling for Bergdorf-Goodman was at the top of the list for my upcoming stay in New York, as I was also looking for a good perfume for spring/summer. So, I checked into the hotel, took a fresh shower, and off to Bergdorf-Goodman! Already upon entering the fragrance department in the men's store, one feels quite dizzy as a "parfumo," and the rational part of the brain starts to shut down.... All these exquisite brands like Roja, Clive Christian, Amouage, Kilian, Maison Francis Kurkdjian, Tom Ford, etc., all gathered in a few square meters, nice sales staff as usual, my ratio in the back of my mind warns that this can only end badly... After a brief moment to catch my breath, I focus on Goodman's and let the lovely Sam, who works for Roja, apply it to my wrist. In classic Chypre manner, fine citrus/orange scents rise to the nose, quickly complemented by beautiful floral notes. Later, the overall picture darkens, subtle "incensed" wood, fine spice with a touch of vetiver rounds off the perfume. A noble reinterpretation of the classic Chypre scent by RD, which perfectly reflects the noble Bergdorf-Goodman image. With this fragrance and the corresponding outfit from BG, one is perfectly equipped for a visit to an exclusive Upper East Side club and to indulge in an exquisite whisky. An elegant scent that can be worn all year round and suits both a business dress and a casual chic look. PS: Even over 6 hours later, the scent was still perceptible in the surroundings and still noticeable on the skin after more than 10 hours.

Feminine fragrance right from the start; very fruity & rosy for the first hour; then the miracle happens...it turns into a musky sweet comforting never ending dry down which is truly delicious and unisex.

I think of the day I saw you for the first time. I think of the first time we got closer. I think of the uncertainty of asking if we should go out. I think of the restaurant I invited you to. I think of the first touch. I think of your lips when you said - I love you! -. I think of the first tender kiss. I think of the way home with you holding my hand. I think of the first night and the first morning. I think of many happy hours with you. I think you are what I have been looking for. I think of your - Yes, I do! -. I think I can’t be without you anymore. I think I am afraid of losing you one day. I think I would break from that. I only think of you. And now I think I carry these thoughts on my skin. I have so much of you in my heart. - John Keats - I thought it was impossible to create such beautiful thoughts from iris, rose, bergamot, musk, and vanilla. I think I was very wrong!

To my surprise, I enjoyed Candy Aoud more than Fruity Aoud. Candy is not as smoothly blended but it is more interesting to my nose! It is so effervescent and the candy feeling really shines through, like a sweet hard candy with oud underneath, this one was also more fresher. Fizzy apple, pear, green and fruity rhubarb, light leather (more leather in Fruity Aoud), woody oud (not too animalic). I could unfortunately see myself buying this overpriced scent haha. I just love it, unique and lovely.

Roja is definitely one of my favorite houses, but I'm not thrilled with their new direction, and certainly not with the fact that Roger isn't the nose behind the scents anymore. I probably won't buy many of the new releases from the house, as the scents are simpler, more synthetic, and lack Roja's signature style. The older releases, however, have many that are on my wishlist. Even though I'm a known blind buyer, for the most part I've wanted to test them out to see if they're worth buying and I've been wearing this for a dozen times for now and I still don't know weather I will buy it or not. Tutti Frutti is a collection that many people covet and at the same time there has been a lot of wondering why the two fragrances in the collection, Candy Aoud and Fruity Aoud , were discontinued. Maybe they thought there were too many similar scents, because those two and Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (I will write a review soon) have a lot of the same elements. I kind of understand why Sweetie Aoud was left out, it is clearly a very unique scent and completely different from the others. On the other hand, it was unfortunately decided to abandon elegant animalic nuances, which were considered difficult but so addictive. Unlike Sweetie Aoud , Candy Aoud opens with a slightly animalic, albeit very refined, Oud. The fruity notes are extremely well done and none of them are cloying or synthetic in any negative way, despite the fact that they really do remind me of very delicious fruit candies. So the fruits are not juicy and completely realistic, but they remind me of both a colorful basket full of fruit and a kip full of gummy bears. Still, I get a clear hint of banana and pear, especially. The feeling is just as unreal as the smell of a croissant in Sweetie Aoud - it doesn't smell clearly edible either, but rather like the scent and the vibe that wafts through a bakery, and that's what makes the scent so great. The sweetness is also nicely executed without being sugary sticky, but rather gentle and pleasantly natural. The note list is long for the type of scent it is. It's not as complex as I'm used to and the scent doesn't have as clear distinct phases as Roger's scents usually do. I'm actually surprised and disappointed with the scent after all the hype. Don't get me wrong, it's an excellent scent, and I don't know of anything like it, but something is missing. If some of my favorite notes - Labdanum, Iris, Leather, Ambergris, Frankincense, Oud, Musk and Oakmoss - performed stronger and brought more character to the scent, I would be completely enchanted. Now the scent is too easy in all its softness, roundness and lightness. The slightly dirty Oud from the beginning unfortunately disappears and it brought an interesting contrast to the scent. On the other hand, a darker and more serious version of the scent is Kingdom of Saudi Arabia , although Fruity Aoud is apparently more similar to it. Unfortunately, I haven't tried it yet. Despite Candy Aoud's simplicity, the scent will remain in history for a reason. It is a masterpiece of many different and different types of fragrance notes, balancing everything so well together that it is difficult to distinguish the notes separately. It combines unrealistic deliciousness, edibility, even imaginary colors and connects them to notes that are perceived as dirty. The end result is infinitely harmonious, sensual and elegant, and at the same time playful and natural. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

Candy Aoud stylistically completely stands out from the Roja fragrances I have tested so far. These have been more classic or elegant, stylish. I perceive Candy Aoud differently, but that doesn’t make it bad. It strikes me more like something from Mancera or Montale. As my predecessors have already mentioned, the opening is distinctly animalistic. That was my first surprise, as I have not encountered a Roja Oud that dares to do this. More and more candy-like fruity notes then join in, which come across as quite kitschy. Especially at the beginning, the combination of crashing Oud and candy fruit is truly attention-grabbing, but in a somewhat exaggerated, contrasting way. It simply seems at first that two very opposing fragrance notes come together, without being olfactorily harmoniously connected. As it progresses, the Oud kick diminishes and it remains a fluffy musk fruit dwarf with only a tiny Oud undertone. This is relatively unspectacular, but it smells really good. And here lies the difference to many Mancera/Montale: these often fade over time. The Roja, however, becomes increasingly harmonious and shows that it is of high quality. Candy Aoud is not my thing, but it convinces me because it has character and seems well made. Because it apparently does not only aim to please the well-paying clientele, but is actually a fragrance that could fit Roja Dove.

...would not do justice to Roja's “Tutti Frutti” fragrance Candy Aoud. For Candy Aoud is a squeaky original, flirtatious combination of provocative Aoud, warm skin, and ripe fruits that one nibbles from this warm skin. Roja Dove has launched three unusually playful Aoud fragrances under the name “Tutti Frutti.” When thinking of Tutti Frutti, one inevitably recalls Hugo Egon Balder's TV show “Tutti Frutti” from the early 90s. Two contestants could earn points in guessing game rounds, which were invested in clothing items to be stripped off by strippers. If a contestant managed to undress a stripper, he received the country point assigned to that stripper. Particularly popular with the private TV audience was the ballet Cin Cin. Erotic models took on smaller roles in the quiz rounds, presenting themselves scantily clad. Each model represented a specific fruit (or color). The game rules were so confusing that no one really understood them (not even the host), so most critiques that went beyond a Jeremy-honest “Wow, cool!” or the Schwarzersche Maledictum “Man!” could be summarized with “At least a few tits seen!” Candy Aoud plays carefree and is at least as unconventional as Roja Dove's clothing style with contrasts. A suited man with a black bowler hat on his head, joyfully spinning on the horse of a carousel with a giant pink lollipop in one hand and a leather briefcase in the other. Candy Aoud is a prancing flirtation of entirely contrasting notes. Slightly animalistic piglet Aoud dances around the cheeky striptease fruit, sweetly warm and fruity notes on little clouds of incense, metallic cool iris on bare skin. Candy Aoud is squeaky pink - at least the Swarovski stones on the bottle cap and the labeling. Otherwise, the name and the bottle deceive. While the Aoud used is a little bare-breasted piglet (at least at the beginning, as the Aoud striptease unfolds in reverse chronological order), Candy Aoud is neither girlish nor pink. It does not smell like SpongeBob's marshmallows, colorful street parade lollipops, or synthetic Escada cotton candy on a girl's balcony. Although the individual fruits are recognizable and identifiable, Candy Aoud does not remind one of anything edible. Unlike Sweetie Aoud, I do not perceive Candy Aoud as an actual gourmand fragrance. Candy Aoud starts with a freshness kick from voluptuous bergamot, which lasts only a few seconds, similar to Sweetie Aoud. At the same time, Aoud and ripe fruits storm the stage. Red, fruitily ripe apples, sliced, and some sparkling sweet-sour berries initially dance on the Aoud floor. After a while, two or three freshly peeled bananas join in the background. Not the EU-standard supermarket bananas, but the sweet, flavor-intensive mini bananas that grow in the north of Gran Canaria. In the background, some generally fresh, slightly sugary, and creamy breakfast buffet fruit salad notes can also be discerned. The fruit notes are rounded off by a pastel-soft note of May rose - the only note in the fragrance that is pink like a box of chocolates. The May rose smells lovely, sweet, and warm with a slight touch towards candies. While the Aoud note in Sweetie Aoud and Fruity Aoud is rather ethereal-tame and marked by British restraint - serving more for refinement - the one in Candy Aoud initially proves to be strong, almost hefty. It is most comparable to the Aoud component of Kilian's Pure Oud, albeit more potent. It is a very dark woody, almost oily-dense Aoud note, perhaps a bit woody-resinous at the beginning, with an animalistic undertone. Pigsty 250 meters against the wind, not really fecal, but charmingly animalistic. Pig sex, bathing in the beauty of the animal. I suspect that warm, dark patchouli and dark nagarmotha oil with a note of smoky leather are responsible for this character of the Aoud. Candy Aoud is both an Arabic and a European fragrance. Typically, when thinking of XerJoff, AJ Arabia, etc., animalistic Aoud forms the connection to Arabic fragrance culture, while the other fruity, berry, or floral components connect to European perfumery. Interestingly, this is reversed here. The Aoud leans towards moderate European Kilian Aoud, while the fruity and floral aspects of Candy Aoud remind one of fruity accords used in Arabic fragrance oils (e.g., Hind al Oud). As the fragrance develops, the animalistic undertones almost completely recede, as does the slightly resinous quality of the Aoud. The dark woody, dense character, however, remains well into the base. The Aoud note is not the dominant note, but unlike in Sweetie Aoud and Fruity Aoud, it slightly overshadows all other notes, at least into the base. Over time, the sweet-fruity impression transforms towards warm-sweet-balsamic-green. A fruity, pixelated green note becomes noticeable. Rhubarb is noted in the pyramid. Well, this green note does not smell like self-satisfied rhubarb; it is sunnier in spirit, sweeter in nature, warmer at heart than an unconsidered bite into a ripe red rhubarb stalk. An aromatic-sweet cardamom note adds oriental warmth, while a yellow, sweet-fruity floral note with slightly bitter undertones provides a counterbalance and some dry, climate-conditioning incense clouds rise from the depths. Gradually, warm, distinctly praline-creamy-woody and sweet, candy-filling-balsamic green notes cover the last summery fruits. An exciting counterbalance is formed by a cool and distinguished powdery iris note, like flashing metal. The dry incense emphasizes the cooling aspects of the fragrance. In the background, the scent of warm bare skin slowly becomes noticeable. Candy Aoud concludes in this contrast to the cool iris with a hint of loins-skin-animalistic labdanum, a bit of freshly tanned dark corset leather, and a musky-soft, carnival-warm, seductively sweet amber note. Candy Aoud plays with the Swarovski crystal sparkle of contrasts. Even though the fragrance pyramid reads like a wild boar ride through the animalistic-gourmand fragrance universe, there are no strenuous or overly intentional contrasts (or even breaks in the fragrance). Candy Aoud is exciting and unusual from start to dry down, the contrasting notes are artfully intertwined. Candy Aoud is prancing flirtation. While Sweetie Aoud is a rather everyday, spring-like good-mood fragrance to be worn year-round, Candy Aoud is worn ioci causa - all the more convincingly. Candy Aoud is not worn out of an indeterminate mood, but consciously. For Candy Aoud has confident edges and corners. Candy Aoud is a fragrance for the days when one devours a box of pink Luxemburgerli for lunch, orders a giant cup of children's ice cream at the ice cream parlor, sucks on a lollipop during a meeting, drinks raspberry lemonade at a business lunch, and dresses as Roja Dove tends to do.

This brand is not available in my country, so a dear friend of mine kindly sent me a decant. First things first, it is Winter where I am at present, so it's probably not the best time of the year to be testing something so Summery and fresh like A Mi Aire. However I get the gist; the general idea. The opening was a little too sharp and aquatic for my liking and it took a long time to settle on my skin. For the first few minutes I regretted spritzing this on, however as it began to settle, I was quite intrigued by the fresh and zesty bergamot note which was more than pleasing to my nose. It went from being a scrubber to a unique floral aquatic that I didn't mind wearing in the least. It somewhat resembled 212 by Carolina Herrera, a guilty pleasure of mine that I enjoy wearing in the midst of Summer. The jasmine accord in the heart is so very pretty and transparent. I'm rather shocked by how natural and true to life these notes are. The bergamot and jasmine come together so beautifully, and smell like they would if they were placed right in front of you. It's at this point that A Mi Aire reminds me of yet another Summer staple of mine, L'eau par Kenzo. This fragrance really captures a picturesque ocean view, especially with its intense blue coloured liquid. I feel refreshed just smelling this from the bottle. I really applaud the citrus accords being so well presented in this fragrance, along with the gorgeous hinoki wood and musky base. The longevity is good on my skin, as is the sillage which can be rather strong at first. I recommend.

For days I have been trying to sniff out any possible different facets of the scent to give a fair assessment. I am certainly curious. However, my nose really doesn't manage to enjoy a greater scent development. So, straight to the point: If you like strong citrus notes, you are well served here. A Mi Aire starts with a pronounced bergamot note, while the mandarin remains slightly shy in the background. Soon, jasmine joins in - this results in a slightly sweet-citrusy scent. Period. I can't smell much more, even over a longer period. This jasmine-bergamot mixture reminds me of an inexpensive men's Eau de Cologne, no more and no less. A Mi Aire is categorized as fresh-fruity-floral, and the fragrance pyramid promised something exciting. Especially the prospect of hinoki and cedar combined with musk made my heart race. With a lot of imagination, I could say that something woody and needle-like is recognizable in the further development. However, this permanent citrus note is so strong that it dominates the entire scent progression and completely overshadows any potentially present other components. Therefore, this scent does not seem modern to me, as the manufacturer's marketing language claims. Somehow, I have often smelled something like this in the 70s. I assess the longevity as mediocre, and the sillage as well. You won't stand out with this scent - it is certainly suitable for everyday wear. Thanks to Hasi for the sample.

In 2006, the original L'Homme by Yves Saint Laurent was launched and is certainly one of the bestsellers from the brand, alongside La Nuit de l'Homme. Whether it has been reformulated or not, I cannot determine, but a very good friend of mine has been wearing it for years, and I can always recognize the scent. It is understated, yet very pleasant and still has a distinctive character. Over the years, YSL has excelled in an almost absurd extent of flankers for both of the aforementioned fragrances. They have really gone overboard with this. So after the Le Parfum for La Nuit de l'Homme, there is now also a Le Parfum for the classic L'Homme. Around 2010, I had La Nuit EdT and EdP in my collection and must say that at that time, they were the best and most complex fragrances in my collection. Of course, I was just starting out, only had Boss Bottled Night and a few cheapies in my collection, but these two fragrances were heavenly for me. YSL was the pinnacle for me. In the meantime, I must regretfully note that YSL no longer matches my taste. Perhaps it is because I am gradually outgrowing their target audience, but it still disappoints me. Just like this flanker here, which further underscores my claim. The first spray of this flanker starts with what is referred to as ozone, which for me simply embodies the classic freshness of an aquatic. However, L'Homme Le Parfum is definitely not an aquatic. It leans more towards fragrances like Y from the same house or Acqua di Giò Absolu by Armani and is thus one of the many developments of the infamous Invictus by Paco Rabanne. I am aware that this fragrance DNA is currently quite popular, but it does not suit my taste. The top note is overall a bit overwhelming. Upon first sniff, I even got a slight headache. It starts off very fresh and yet has an overwhelming sweetness. I can detect cardamom (here in a rather sweet form), but the lemon disappears in the blink of an eye. This sweet-fresh mix quickly drifts into geranium, which more or less constitutes the centerpiece of this fragrance. The geranium here has no spiciness that can sometimes be detected, but rather leans towards the rosy direction. This blends with the sweet-fresh scent mix that continues to persist and gives it an additional floral character. The sillage is already somewhat fading here. Towards the end, everything becomes quite unremarkable, as the fragrance becomes a bit woodier and thus fades into a woody-fresh mix with a hint of sweetness. The longevity is quite okay, but I find the sillage really very weak. The fragrance is probably a crowd-pleaser, but I see it more suited for leisure time in a sunny park (I need to get out of this house) rather than at work. I rate the recognizability on a scale from 0 to 10 as 0, as I couldn't distinguish it from other freshies, like the ones I mentioned above. I find this particularly disappointing, as back around 2010, the La Nuit fragrances were especially marked by their recognizability. The regular L'Homme that my buddy wears, by the way, is too. This is probably the perfect gift for your young nephew, whose interests and preferences you know nothing about and who will surely appreciate it. For the perfume enthusiasts who have already experienced several fragrances, this scent will either be a disappointment or simply forgotten. To put it in the words of the poetess Ariana Grande: Thank U, Next.

When I try fragrances, I always think about how each scent would affect my loved ones. At the moment, I am sampling men’s fragrances, and with this YSL, I have my best friend Thomas in mind. The lightness of Le Parfum would suit his elegant nonchalance. The lemon tickles a bit in the nose - hello fizz, but my friend has a sense of humor. Overall, the scent has a playful wink - and doesn’t take itself too seriously. The flowers are buoyant - and the woods soft and pliable. Charming. I see myself sitting with my charmer over wine and cigarettes in the warm evening air at a street café - we flirt with each other - and have been doing so for 30 years, with growing enthusiasm. We exchange compliments - but also secrets. Thomas, my secret-sharer - and also scent accomplice - because we can also philosophize about fragrances for hours. What would he say about YSL Le Parfum? Not an extravagant scent - but definitely in a positive mood. Just right for the scene in the trattoria. Just right for our relationship, which has never lost its lightness. Thomas, my traveler - who always called me faithfully from every corner of the world. And the scent also says - travel... Now he has embarked on a long journey - and left this earthly realm. But I won’t let that stop me from continuing to choose fragrances for him, and imagining or remembering different situations with him. The persistence of memory indeed - like the eponymous painting by Dali. Music: Goodbye my almost Lover by Fine Frenzy

Performance: Fragrances from the L'Homme line are not exactly known for their long-lasting power. However, nothing can be said regarding the price/performance ratio. The projection is good, just like the longevity. One should not expect miracles, of course. Nevertheless, there is nothing to complain about. Who can wear the scent? A great men's perfume for young and old. You can't go wrong with this fragrance. This scent is so balanced that you won't stand out for its uniqueness, but you will still be pleasantly perceived by those around you. Certainly also a very good fragrance for people who do not own many perfumes. However, it is also suitable for those who have many niche fragrances and occasionally seek variety. Where can you wear the scent? I can't think of any moment that would be inappropriate for this perfume. Personally, I even tend to wear this fragrance while working from home, as I simply enjoy the scent. It doesn't get boring and doesn't cause any headaches. With three sprays, you're set for half the day. My opinion: I use this perfume as a balance for the niche fragrances that I also like to wear in everyday life. It is certainly not a scent that makes statements, but sometimes you just want to smell good without wanting to say anything. I can definitely recommend this perfume to anyone who doesn't want to spend much money on a solid everyday scent. In my opinion, you don't even need to test it beforehand.

I received the predecessor of this perfume a long time ago as a young, 16-year-old growing man. Since then, I must admit, I have been a fan. I was excited from the very beginning and even bought this bottle not too long ago. I admittedly don’t wear it much these days, unless I feel a bit nostalgic, but I still like it. Even though opinions are divided here, I stand by one of my first real fragrances. Maybe it’s also a bit of nostalgia. Very fresh, a bit woody, and generally charming. I can’t quite understand the harsh opinions here, but some share my view and have a positive association with this scent. :) I must confess, I find it a bit too expensive for what it is. However, I quite like the bottle. Very long-lasting scent, which you can enjoy all day long. As a gift, as you can tell, it is certainly well-suited! :)

I gave a good rating for the price-performance ratio, despite my poor rating for the scent itself. Those who like this fragrance and enjoy wearing it will get a lot out of it, not needing to apply much and not having to worry about feeling "naked" after a few hours. Personally, I find the scent very aggressive and sense a significant danger in that fellow citizens might overdo it and then head into the packed subway or anywhere else where there are many people in close quarters. You then smell nothing more than an all-covering, testosterone-loaded, penetrating bomb, a faceless medley, as one unfortunately constantly gets shoved under their nose in public. That said: I mistakenly grabbed the wrong labeled samples and have this scent in my collection. If anyone wants it, feel free to reach out, my souk is not yet activated.

The citrus and ozone notes are very noticeable in the top note. The synthetic scent is quite strong. Personally, it's too strong for me. Over time, it diminishes more and more. In the base note, the Ambroxan is prominent. The longevity is decent. A fresh summer fragrance that is perfect for dates on warm summer days. Especially in the evening, if you ask me.

In the product description of this fragrance, it says; Yves Saint Laurent L'Homme Le Parfum embodies the modern gentleman and promises masculine allure with uniquely combined fragrance notes. The zesty opening blends with exotic flowers, refined with bitter basil. Woody aromatic accords allow the scent to fade perfectly and ensure long-lasting wear.

Apparently discontinued a few years ago, Risqué pour Homme is in my opinion an underrated fragrance from Mr. Roja Dove. I would even take the risk to say that it lies between his best creations. The perfume represents an homage to the Pelargonium graveolens who plays the central role in the fragrance´s developement. After a clean, beautiful bergamot/citrus blast with lavender undertones, in a couple of minutes Geranium enters the stage. For the next 2 hours the perfume is quite linear focused on Geranium with floral hints of jasmine and rose due the related chemistry (linalool, geraniol and citronellol). And what we have here is not the sharp, abrasive Geranium found in the Ropion´s Pour Monsieur but a soft and creamy one. And that is exactly how it´s supposed to be, in order to enable a smooth, almost imperceptible transition to a beautiful, byzantine church like, myrrh-frankincense scent in the dry-down. Scent 8,9/10 Longevity 7/10 Projection 6/10 Sillage 6/10

An extremly versatile creation ,Risque Parfum Pour Homme is the perfect definition of the real gentleman with an unexpected dark ,sensual hidden facet.The fresh bergamote/citrusy posh opening followed by the flamboyant rich incense note with Master Roja Dove's own touch puts Risque Pour Homme among the first places in the best incense fragrances top. Sadly this amazing fragrance was discontinued(why not...was one of the best ...)leaving this gorgeous incense perfume fans with mixed feelings.Why Risque and why now?

The Roja Riske Pour Homme perfume is a refined fragrance that embodies luxury and sophistication. It opens with a burst of fresh citrus notes, including lemon and bergamot, which create a lively and invigorating start.
