First of all, it must be mentioned that there are two different versions of Reckless: an older one, with light yellow liquid and a scent distinctly marked by aldehyde, and the new variant, which is rather reddish in color and has a heavier, sweeter smell. Since there is already a very good comment on the old version, I would like to focus on the currently available reformulation. The opening is unusual: it already hints that an opulent bouquet of flowers might soon bloom before us, but for a few minutes, a spiciness dominates that I would describe as mossy, slightly earthy, and bitter green. In an online shop, I once read about oak moss as a supposed base note, and although my nose would like to believe this, a look at the official fragrance pyramid does not confirm it, so my suspicion falls on coriander. By the way, I notice this effect even more clearly in the EdP - and for my taste, this unconventional beginning could have lasted a little longer, as it is so contrary to what follows. Because this phase hardly lasts, shortly after, the floral vanilla bomb explodes, and I can hardly distinguish its individual components. Neroli stands out the most, but it blends with May rose and jasmine into an overall impression that has often been described here as tuberose-like to gum-like. I can understand this well, but I don't actually believe in tuberose here; rather, I suspect that the interplay of neroli, May rose, and the quite sweet vanilla is the cause of this scent experience - in any case, the strict, penetrating indolic part of real tuberose is missing, so those of you who are rather averse to that flower need not necessarily flee. In the background, there is a slight soapy quality and a hint of bitter garden green, so the fragrance, as full-bodied as it is, also fits wonderfully into summer for me. I cannot discern a clear development towards the base, except for an increasing sweetness, even after hours; flowers and vanilla remain the main players and easily last 10 hours with persistently good sillage, which, with careful dosing, does not hit you over the head. In my imagination, I see Reckless on a cheerful woman who falls in love at a garden party on a warm summer night - or at least plays with the thought of falling in love. But one should not imagine Reckless as an innocent, flowery water; rather, it smells extroverted, feminine, and walks a fine line between playfulness and seduction, which makes this fragrance so appealing to me.

In the first seconds, even while spraying, I am practically intoxicated by the alcohol. Aldehydes coat my airways... make my breath catch. As if I had inhaled Lady Guerlain from 1936. (Not meant derogatorily!) Direct comparison to the EdP Chanel No 5. I´m not amused. However, the shock freeze effect means that I don’t miss a rapid development of the fragrance. Hmm... a mix of zesty lemon emerges, blended with an incredible amount of soap. From the biting soap, the mixture fades to soft, clean soap. Simply indescribably beautiful, soft, and good. Just as I relax and think: Wow, a really fine clean-soap scent!... it turns powdery. Now it’s an exciting interplay between soapy soap and powdery powder. The perfume lingers in this state for a while, leaving me slightly dazed. The images of this fragrance stage are hard to describe without becoming cheesy.. The perfume connects tradition and unconventionality cleanly. Interwoven with soft corners and sharp edges. I can imagine the scent on a modern lady of today as well as on a woman from my parents' generation. The scent could be worn by a stylish bride in ripped jeans and an off-the-shoulder shirt just as much as by a lady in a classic suit with high heels. Even though the fragrance invites or even demands a touch of old-fashionedness, I don’t think it should be classified into an "age category." Fragrance needs imagination and no boundaries! Well, after quite a prolonged mental cinema, one could gradually smell fruity notes. Floral freshness. But above all, a woody spiciness bursts through in the emerging base, taking the perfume in a completely different direction. A hint of leather, mixed with soap, wood, and spices makes this scent adventurous and wild, profound. This cowgirl movie also lingers for quite a while. Until the good end, the perfume becomes cuddly. It remains spicy, but the initial hardness and determination are exchanged for warmth and dreaminess. For me, despite all the contradictions, it’s a clear women's fragrance with a very loud sillage and good lasting power for several hours. A special scent, not for every day. Another Roja that takes time. A perfume that manages the balancing act between classic and modern well, without appearing formless. Multifaceted and strong. Let’s rock! Or let’s dance?

That I surprise myself with blind buys of fragrances might be acceptable, but buying shoes without trying them on turned out to be reckless. The left shoe fit perfectly, but the right one pinched uncomfortably. Of course, the receipt was lost. So I offered the stylish shoes to my friend, as she has the same size as I do. Tada! They fit. Joy on both sides, and she kept the lovely pieces on. On the way to the city, I looked at her feet with emotion - and thought about how similar we are in many ways. Two softies navigating through life. Sometimes in a bad mood, sometimes amused - sometimes we get on each other's nerves - and sometimes we really fall flat on our faces. But time and again, we lift each other up. In the perfume store, we reached for Aura in sync, notably drawn to its soft, charismatic scent. One cannot and does not want to escape its warm-hearted aura. The citrus notes are harmoniously balanced with the green aspects of the fragrance - and the carrot seeds have a musky, nutty effect. The flowers appear delicately elegant, with the violet peeking through with a slight bitterness. Sweet vanilla walks hand in hand with supple suede. A thoroughly likeable fragrance, with a special ethereal statement that justifies its title "Aura." My friend takes the bottle to the checkout and hands it to me. Without words.

So for me the smell is definitely way better than a 6.5 which is the current average rating. I'd give it an 8.5. For me it's the best Y Fragrance from the line (on my skin, not necessarily on paper). And on my Skin it also smells by far the highest quality. So I actually get the official marketing text saying "highest quality ingredients etc.". After testing it on skin I would get it over the EDP, the EDP intense and the le Parfum. Not for retail price of course, but you can get it for a quite decent price right now. It's very masculine, it's fresh, a tiny bit fruity, a bit spicy, a bit woody. Incense and oud is minimal to non-existent, but the rest seems quite high quality to me for a designer fragrance. On my skin it reminds me a lot of Bleu de Chanel but I think I even like Y l'elixir a bit more because I find Bleu de Chanel so very boring. I say it's quite a good blue fragrance, not for retail price but for discount for sure. Now to the name. Is the title of elixir fitting for this fragrance? No absolutely not in my opinion. It does not seem to be super beast mode for me, it's not experimental or ingenious and it's not super dark and concentrated. For me it's just the highest quality YSL Y perfume and that's that. So I can understand the disappointment, but the scent itself is fine. Edit: Okay so I finally bought Y l'Elixir and got it yesterday and gave it a full wear today. So far I'm loving it. Especially for the 75 € I paid for it. I sprayed 3 sprays on my neck (mainly on the clothes) this morning and I still smell it quite a bit on myself after 8 hours. So for me Sillage is good, Longevity is good. And I perceive it as indeed way darker, way richer and a bit more incensy / smokey compared to the rest of the line and indeed a bit unusual / daring with a tiny bit of oud. For me the best Blue Fragrance right now with an amazing Dark, Incense, floral special twist. In the Marketing Text it's called a "dark and white fougere" which for me fits perfectly. Thus for me elixir is in the end an okay label for this scent. But it is very well blended and I think you need to be quiet sensible to get the quality and the nuances of the ingredients. The only thing I don't like is the bottle. It should have gotten at least a magnetic cap and a nicer package. It's really mid. So that's at least my take on and my experience with the Y l'Elixir.

This fragrance gets so much hate. Yes it is a designer release and we do not expect a niche smell; It is kinda expensive for this category, I get that; but if we wanna talk about scent profile, longevity, etc, we have a fairly good release here. The smell kind of grew on me. It is made by "Dominique Ropion" after all. I think this is a new interpretation of elixir and it fits the title as it has a dense feeling in the smell (same as other elixir fragrances but here mainly on a lavender based scent profile, which I found it done well) and lasted on me nearly 24 hours, so this thing is strong! P.S. On skin it smells better than on paper specially after an hour, which mid and base notes start to shine.

Upon first spraying I recognize this immediately as being apart of the Y line. The geranium here is the one that is found in both EDP and Intense. But, a much more prominent role. Now, sometimes geranium can have a slight apple like smell to it, but I’m sure they just added a touch of the EDP mix to create a small hint of Y EDP’s opening act. nulltheless, that blue-ish tone is very much muted. Lavender and geranium are the stars here, particularly the latter. The lavender gives this one a clean and soapy kind of aroma. But, that is more than offset by the spicy, earthy, crisp, woodsy freshness of the geranium. Very cold and fresh in these early stages. Not as blue or bold as EDP for example. Though, this one has some depth and I enjoy how tame and easy to wear it is. Oud adds to the base and the woodiness. However, it just isn’t all that massive of a note here in the early stages. Also, an incense note provides a smokiness which also isn’t too pervasive. Both are really nice in the support of the other two notes. Elixir isn’t too complicated of a fragrance. The back half is going to be a lavender led affair, still clean and with a soapiness to it. More of a woody feeling to it, than the earlier stages of the wear. Regards

Nice, simple and clean frankincense with a dose of fresh lavender, very aromatic. Gives me church vibes but kinda dumbed down? I don't know, it just feels empty, lacks purpose. I enjoy the scent but i don't get how or where this has "natural oud" in it. Way overpriced althought i said i like it i don't think i will ever get a full bottle once my 10ml decant runs out. Maybe another decant if i feel like irresponsible with my money again. Fun fact, i mostly got negative feedback from my friends, family and coworkers. Performance is average, standard 5-6 hours-ish with medium sillage and projection. When the best part of the fragrance is the bottle (which indeed looks good like all other fragrance from the Y line), you know you fucked up. Try it, if you like frankincense and get a bottle off Notino for almost half the price because it's regulalry discounted on there.

Upon learning of this release, deep down I was eagerly anticipating something groundbreaking and out of the box to add to my collection…perhaps something similar to what Dior did with the Sauvage Elixir.

I got a tester of it in a fragrance shop in London and it was a lavender bomb and its very sexy but i really don't know when to use it as an date night or daily but 8,5 out of 10 i would say. It really really reminded me of a smart business man that everybody wants to be around.

First spray you can tell it's on the Y line, you get similar notes to the EDP/EDT. Then it starts to grow more woody and resinous, like, a lot. On my skin, what I feel the most is the incense/resinous vibe of this scent, which reminds me a lot of what JPG Elixir, Bad Boy Parfum and so on do with this note.

I don't quite understand why the Y-Elixir is often referred to as one of the worst elixirs. In my opinion, it is not; on the contrary, it is a very beautiful composition that lives up to the name Elixir, especially considering the Y-line. The scent takes the original DNA and makes it darker, more complex, and, as I find, quite oudy as well.

This perfume smells atypical compared to other Elixir perfumes. Usually, these are the flagships of a line or even a brand, but here? NO! Here we have Y-DNA on a fresh laundry base with an OK longevity. Oud and incense? Where are you? You are listed among the notes, but there's nothing to smell from that. Rather just a lot of geranium and lavender.

I really like this particular Roja perfume. I’ve tried several that are just overbearing and difficult for me to wear in general, but this one is not it. To me this one is super easy to wear anytime of the day or evening. It’s versatile, meaning you can be worn to church, work, or even a night out dancing. It has a nice fruity smell that isn’t like a fruit cocktail and I smell no bergamot at all. I smell beautiful florals and a little bit of raspberry. It’s really quite lovely. Sillage is pretty good as well. Longevity is several hours.

I am perplexed, looking at the rating and the other reviews. Did I get a counterfeit discovery set?? I absolutely cannot smell what others here smell. No "floral", no "powdery" (ok, maybe some), and not even close anything "oriental". The perfume opened with the usual Roja screechy fresh something (decidedly _not_ bergamot) alongside a fruity candy (quite fun, actually). The sparkly fruity candy was rather fleeting (unfortunately, as it really is a fun note), and after that the smell morphed into something fresh, very sharp, synthetic (like calone, or laundry musks, or something of the kind) and indescript. I cannot smell florals (at least naturalistic florals) or much else, quite frank. The base seems to be woody - again, something reminding me of Molecules (or, rather, their Escentric ones). There also seems to be a bit of something sweet like vanilla or vague fruity notes in the background. This stage lasts about 1-2 hours. As the perfume continues to develop, it gets more and more sweet, with vanilla and fruity candy re-emerging. The fresh synthetic part subsides, but doesn't go away entirely. This is a nicer stage, it is far less sharp, but still largely fresh synthetic. I noticed it is very typical of Roja perfumes, to have very loud, sharp and screechy opening and the first 1-2 hours, and then turning into something nicer. In roughly 3 hours the scent gets considerably quieter. On skin it smells vanilla, fruity hard candy, something woody synthetic (very lightweight and fluffy) and laundry musk. There is something powdery as well, but rather faint - but only close to the skin; in general I would not classify this scent as "powdery" at all. After 5-6 hours there is only a faint powdery slightly sweet scent left on the skin. Overall, the smell would not suggest the price that is being charged for this. The esthetics is more like a designer fragrance - I would not be surprised to see something like this in a Versace line up, say. Maybe a Parfums de Marly would be more apt a comparison. The good thing about this perfume is that it does go through stages of development, so it's not linear - which makes it more interesting for me. Another good thing is that the base does not completely break down into something illegible, so this is not poorly constructed.

Elixir Pour Femme parfum Elixir is like a fuel for the soul. It makes my mind crystal clear and it feels like some vitamin bomb giving energy for the muscles. It is a delightful and invigorating blend of Raspberry and Peach with delicate flower bouquet and a complex soft powdery base. All notes are masterfully blended to perfection and like most of the Roja’s perfumes, Vanilla in the base, even it being the main note, doesn’t make this “Vanilla scent”. It’s so sophisticated, sleek and sensual which is opposite to gourmand cozy Vanillas. Elixir is lingering around you in the seductive way all day long and you can complete the beauty of it with Elixir Supreme Hair Mist which I think is a must have for me. This scent is perfect for warm days and it’s one of my favourites to wear at the gym. This is sweeter than for example 51 and even Enigma since there is all - Raspberry, Peach and a Cherry like sweetness of Heliotrope- in this. I could see that this fragrance is liked regardless of age - everyone would feel like a goddess with Elixir. This is not extra ordinary unique scent but definitely refined and polished Roja quality. Main middle notes: Rose de Mai, Raspberry, Peach Main base note: Vanilla I will edit this review soon since this was first written on IG where the space is very limited. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

Somewhere it once said: “This magical elixir radiates effortless sensuality and gives you the power to light up a room, leave an impression, and get what you want.” I assume it was from Roja itself. Hmm. Well, lighting up a room with perfume, that’s fantastic! Currently, right now. To the point! Right off the bat: If you don’t like raspberry at all, neither in scent nor in taste, maybe JUST BARELY the color, then you should stay away from this. And if you don’t like rose, then this is not for you either. To everyone else, I can reveal the following: No matter how cold, how warm, how early or how late it is - when you spray Elixir, it’s really lovely. It’s not that sticky syrupy raspberry that immediately clings to the body and is supposed to fade away after a short time. It’s a very cool, velvety soft, shy raspberry that no one has ever sniffed at, which is why it smells so beautifully, completely. Raspberry red. Apparently, this little one is still under the watchful eye of the proud (May) rose, as it almost immediately joins in and keeps its protective hand over the little fruit. Not overbearing, no, it gently watches over it, accompanying the berry throughout the day. (Probably this incredible harmony comes from all the other ingredients that are supposed to be in there.) I have been using Elixir for quite a while now to light up the room. And no matter what mood I’m in (I can be moody. Sometimes.), this scent makes me a little softer. At least that’s what I tell myself, and that’s enough. Even today, when I was unreasonably annoyed by nonsense, and annoyed that I was annoyed (that’s the worst kind of annoyance!), I can almost feel a velvety little raspberry nudging me and looking at me hopefully with big - violet-blue, if you will - eyes. And it smells so beautifully that I can’t help but smile. Let’s see what Roja says about it today. “Elixir has the unusual ability to let this quality linger on the skin throughout the day.” true. It goes on like this all day! With the lingering. The only thing I don’t like about raspberries are the seeds. And there are none here. Elixir is, for me, a very fine, unexpectedly likable, unobtrusive - almost shy - scent that is always there, spending the whole day with me in its delicacy. I find that impressive. Elixir smells like how a raspberry feels. If you are careful.

Hello again, my sniffing fans :) So, where have you all stuck your noses today? :D I, for one, am here with a very high-quality luxury fragrance, namely Roja, which is known for offering scents that are more expensive than cars. Well, okay, one fragrance from Roja that costs 3000 euros is at least more expensive than my first car. And also more expensive than my second car. In fact, it’s much more expensive than both cars combined (Peugeot 105 and Fiat Cinquecento), argh :DD Anyway, today I’m talking about a comparatively much more affordable scent from this brand, which averages “only” 450 euros (for 50 mL): Elixir. At this point, I should pull myself together, as a freak and nerd like me can only think of elixirs in terms of life elixirs, which are especially needed in video games when one has been unable to play well and has lost a lot of life energy :D I could tell you stories here, but they probably wouldn’t interest anyone… *sigh* But I’m not entirely wrong with my thoughts. According to Greek mythology, an elixir is indeed a “potion of life” that is supposed to grant immortality. Here at Roja, it’s also about preserving certain memories forever with the help of scents. After all, it is said that fragrances can awaken or recall certain memories in us. Things we might not have thought about for years or decades suddenly come back with the perception of a particular scent or fragrance composition, and we then indulge in memories. And that’s actually true for me as well, as certain scents (but not always specific perfumes) remind me of things from my childhood, for example. That’s something beautiful in itself, as those things we hadn’t thought about for ages haven’t been lost. And that is precisely the theme of this fragrance here. The Scent: At first, I smell raspberries that are sweet and fruity, then come light and gentle powdery notes (probably from the violets) along with some ylang-ylang, which matures the initially youthful character of the fragrance. Just a little later, sweet lily of the valley and roses join in, emphasizing the feminine aura of the scent. A bit later, the fragrance remains soft due to the mix of gentle notes like violet and vanilla. This causes the ylang-ylang to take a bit of a backseat, or rather, it is softened, so that the fragrance, despite these heavy flowers, doesn’t smell too cloying or heavy. By the way, you can still clearly smell the roses later on, as they increasingly become the main note here. So… to be honest, the fragrance doesn’t change much further on. It remains powdery and soft, smelling of sweet, floral notes like violet with a hint of vanilla, and there is always a bit of ylang-ylang in the background. Only the roses become noticeably weaker towards the end. And that’s about it. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is initially quite good, but soon you would need to get a bit closer to smell the fragrance on others. The longevity is lower than expected for a Roja, as the scent lasts about eight hours, but at least half of that time it projects quite weakly. The Bottle: The bottle is rectangular and feels very high-quality as always. It has a gilded label on the front, which is said to contain real gold elements. At the gilded neck, you can see Roja’s engraved signature. The heavy cap is also made of real gold elements and is handcrafted, as the many Swarovski stones are set by hand. In this bottle, all the stones are white or glassy. All in all, a beautiful bottle that also dispenses a fine spray mist. So… despite my title, which is actually an award for the worst films and actors and is re-awarded every year like the Oscars, this fragrance is certainly not bad. My title refers more to the golden elements of the bottle, which are a trademark of Roja, as well as to the scent of the raspberry, which is the first note you can smell in this fragrance. As I said, the scent is quite nice, feminine, and beautiful. You might have guessed it, but here comes my “but”: The scent, for me personally, somehow doesn’t smell that special. It may be beautiful, but not extraordinarily beautiful. It is nice, but there are much more beautiful fragrances out there. Sure, it has no noticeable synthetics, as is the case with every Roja fragrance, but I find that the scent doesn’t smell significantly better than similar (rose) fragrances that can be found everywhere, whether it’s Chloé or whatever. In short, despite its quite nice scent, Elixir is by no means worth 400-450 euros for me! Well, otherwise it is a spring and autumn fragrance, as it is neither too light nor too heavy. It could be used as a carefree daytime scent. So you can certainly give it a try, but you won’t miss anything if you skip it. That’s it again. Wishing you all a lovely evening, see you then :)

This question arises again and again when reading the pyramid of many Roja fragrances. Their components are so classically familiar that they inevitably tend to repeat themselves. And here, most creations follow those of Guerlain and Christian Dior, among others: The well-known classic fragrance notes define the outer framework.

Elixir le Parfum is a wonderful beauty from the house of Roja. A fruity fresh liaison of raspberries, roses, and peaches is what this fragrance revolves around, in my opinion. The rest, made up of a hundred other scent ingredients, is merely supportive embellishment.

Whoever calls this scent mainstream is absolutely right. But with refinement and polished to a high shine. Every fragrance component is finely tuned and creates a harmonious overall impression. As a daytime scent or signature for a young and young-at-heart audience. Not a great sensual seduction, but rather a joy-giver for dark and gloomy days.

The initial cloud is an explosion of pure mandarin – ripe and juicy. And then, like a sudden slap to the face just as you relax and get comfortable – tomato leaf. Aromatic. Green. But before you manage to spring back up and understand what happened – it's all already mixed. Freshly mown wild grasses. All sorts of wildflowers and weeds just cut down by a scythe are now on your skin. Adorable, gentle. Delicious. If I were a cow, I'd love to graze on it. It projects at first, but for a short while and only a little bit. A fresh aura barely 30cm away from your skin. Inoffensive and light, but once you lean in for a hug – unique and clearly visible. Gone in an hour. After that there's a gentle vague scent stuck to your skin – green, citrusy. Mostly just smells clean. Fades away and leaves the musky base behind in another hour. Musk clings to you long into the evening. Soft, cozy, not sweet. Loewe's playful take on a fleeting citrus cologne. Not too special, and probably unnecessary if you already own something like it. But I'm glad that my fleeting citrus cologne is this.

It’s reminds me Tuscan Leather from Tom Ford, but richer, deeper and more gourmand. Scent 10/10 Longevity 2/10 Sillage 2/10 Cocoa and Coffee, and other people ingredients make Tuscan Leather Longevity and Sillage are very poor. Sad

Your epilogue: “What happened to us? You have become a stranger to me. I look at the beautiful bouquets from you and yet I do not feel safe with you. We both wanted to talk, you came with flowers, I with cake, just like back then, only now we curse incessantly, we are arguing again. If you are honest, you know I don’t deserve this. I am slowly getting scared that you can no longer love, that you cannot reciprocate the feelings I have. It makes me sick when you say that’s not true. You still talk about great happiness, yet behave like a child, you don’t look me in the eyes and now appear not only deaf but also blind. Why are you doing this to me? Where does the hatred in you come from? I didn’t want to realize that I am losing my place - the sunny place in your heart, deep in your soul. Now your carnations sit like a noose around my throat. You no longer listen to me, I have no significance anymore. My thoughts fly through the room, crisscross. You are afraid. Is it okay if you flee because of this? Why does the shamelessly arrogant and intrusive dental assistant with the bleached torch curls and the torch smile call you at nine in the evening, on a Saturday night, on the very day we have our four-year anniversary? Better you leave right now before you see my bitter tears.” I sit here with a hot chocolate over the photos of us, from happy days. Us together, so free and happy, before you suffocated me with flowers, with gifts - and I suspected it would not end well. The smell of your bad conscience has overshadowed every bouquet. I taste nothing. Everything tastes bitter. Tired. Coffee. Thoughts spin in circles. «Когда тебя предали - это всё равно, что руки сломали. Простить можно, а обнять это уже не получается.» («When you are betrayed, it is like having your arms broken. You can forgive them, but you can no longer embrace them.» L.N. Tolstoy) Cozy blanket. Window seat. The home full of warmth, it no longer reaches me, I feel like a stranger, trapped in my own four walls, which are closing in ever tighter. His epilogue: “It is a moment that takes your life and it doesn’t matter if we are both against it. For the fate of us all, we wait for the day. And the loss will come like the nail in your end: the wooden coffin.” --------------- In case someone didn’t understand the dental assistant: She is personified saffron. If this was too chaotic and too “meta” for someone: Sorrynotsorry. Just never read my thoughts again. If someone finds “the basis of the main text in German quotation marks” familiar: Bushido - Augenblick (2005)

If love were a scent, it would have to be the scent of freedom, for the absolute beauty of love reveals itself only of its own accord, independent and complete in its freedom. Impatience is the fire that becomes the downfall of every love. It is the ancient theme that zealously kills love. I feel it as thousands of reflections of my “Appetitus Sensitivus” - like fragments hidden in small interludes - throbbing in search of satisfying a lack. Therefore, I consciously chose patience and gave the fragrance time, testing “the love” often and at different times of the day. “Un Amore Eterno” is meant to be a tribute to the fragrant letters of Casanova. I already find the idea exalted and over the top. I conduct the Y-cut on the fragrance and note: Scents like an open handbag, lipstick, leather, dull scarlet sweetness, earthy-floral and woody-nutty aromas season the air at my horizon of perception. The strongly marked, yet somehow affective creation with its ancient aura does not really reach me. It feels heavy and suffocating, like a requiem. The combination of tuberose, clove, and saffron ultimately gives me the rest. My idea of eternal love is bound to the scope of lived feelings. If something is eternal and infinite, then it is also everywhere. Eternal love is like being kissed by a soul, bare-lipped and uncertain. A kiss that echoes for all eternity. Love awakens like spring, unstoppable and warm, smiling and dancing. “Un Amore Eterno” is unfortunately a love that lies on its deathbed. The scent is rather “dirty.” “Carnal Desire” would suit the fragrance better. Even then, the scent would not be more bearable for me. Often, scents evoke musical associations for me. However, this one makes me think of a less dignified figure like the lonely writer Gustav von Aschenbach, the main character of the novella “Death in Venice.” “Un Amore Eterno” also shows me that the fleeting ecstasy of sin only creates confusion of the senses and catapults one into sudden abandonment. It is precisely this suddenness of the mysterious that reveals the drive that Roja pursues and that Gustav paradoxically finds shameful, as the one profound impulse of creation. Hours move slowly, without flying, poetically blasphemous and lavishly rudimentary, like a last apocalyptic wish for desire, blinded and unable to perceive that love has already died in its far too tight garments. The scent of the Brit would have been a good scent for the novel. Similar to the chaos of the torn writer, I experience an unwanted stop in no man's land with “Un Amore Eterno.” Standstill. In this phase, carried by sweet boudoir opulence, Roja's creation somewhat resembles “1889 Moulin Rouge.” This only lasts briefly. It is followed by one of the few positive aspects of the fragrance, the grandiose marriage of patchouli and iris. These moments are a true compensation for the initially dreadful tangle. The fragrance calms down here increasingly and becomes more harmonious. The overly potent spicy-floral and dull-nutty moments from the opening, paired with the ancient clove spice, are now only faintly perceptible, yet they feel pleasantly supportive and, above all, fitting. It is not the eternal love, far from it, but an average good Roja scent. Not a fragrance one will remember; there are clearly better ones at ROJA Parfums. I am left with the regret that Roger Dove takes up this beautiful and eternal theme and then misses it so mercilessly.

.... the first impression, artificial and therefore not very inviting. Okay, the combination of cocoa and coffee makes a great cappuccino with milk, but what do they want here in a perfume with magnificent flowers? For me, initially an unusual olfactory challenge. No matter, one should never be deceived by the first impression. Let's see... Violet and orris root, my beloved May rose.... hm hm Jasmine, very very fine, best quality. Although everything about the scent seems valuable and thoughtfully selected, there is initially no harmony to be discerned. The individual ingredients are raging and arguing amongst themselves. Not that they can't agree, the classic protagonists have known each other in various other perfume masterpieces for ages. No, rather it’s about something new, something never seen before. In this case, it’s coffee and cocoa, which want to make a name for themselves in the high perfume politics these days. For about three-quarters of an hour, the argument continues on my skin, everything keeps falling apart again. This coffee-cocoa mixture annoys the flowers, the base notes are trying to calm things down. I am almost inclined to wash off the perfume because of this. Oh dear, apparently a fraudster Roja has persuaded, in times of coffee to go, to equip a scent with contemporary insignia to be particularly noticed. After about another hour - I am sorting clothes in the wardrobe - I am again surrounded by something.... A fluid, of delicate violets and my beloved May rose, in a shared floral accord, carried by patchouli, woods, a little musk, and clove, further away stands a coffee to go cup…. Ahhh, finally it has come to this. After long negotiations, an extraordinarily precious scent has emerged. The wait was worth it. It will definitely remain in my collection. PS About seven hours later. I bring in wood for the fireplace, outside the air is damp and cold. Patchouli, cedar, and Kashmir wood, the deepest tone of this perfume, feel incense-like and sacred. They still carry high above on their shoulders the May rose and the violet, the undisputed queens of flowers through the cool breezes....

Do you remember the scene where Johnny Depp, in the movie "From Hell", pours the absinthe down his throat? That exact scene came to mind when I applied the Loewe. I don't know why, but the scent would fit right in. It has something of absinthe, even though there is no wormwood or anise involved. - Synthetic drill, mixed with a strong alcohol note, drenched in thick lemon juice that can glue everything together. Freshness that only pretends to be one, wriggles around like a piglet throughout the entire experience, trying to clash with some sweetness. The whole grotesque atmosphere is killed by an overly exuberant jasmine, which also argues with the rose over who takes the lead here. Stuffy. Gloomy. Old-fashioned. Not made for this time. More for the nights from From Hell, mixed with the strong smells of the street. The scent is more horror than wearable perfume. I can hardly imagine that it would perform well on anyone, no matter how hard I try. Thank goodness the scent doesn't last very long and dissipates extremely quickly. Not to mention the sillage. Perhaps Loewe wanted to create a specter here? To briefly dive into mafia freshness, to stock up on lemons, while being flooded with jasmine and rose? Pure horror for me, as I am not fond of too much lemon. The bottle is much more beautiful than the content. It would suggest a powerful potion of the forest. It looks somewhat comical, but unfortunately, it is just a deceptive package. Definitely one of the worst scents I have ever smelled. From hell. Of hell. Thank you, I have had enough absinthe for today.

My first thought was: Ooooh! My second thought, after looking at the gender specification: Mmmmmh... And my third, after checking the fragrance pyramid: Häääää? Well, the lion is really a bit loco. But let's take it step by step. I received the scent as a sample and was somehow convinced it was a men's perfume. Still, I sprayed it on my hand and found it a bit sexy. Citrusy, somewhat aquatic, so not really my thing, but still sexy. The lemons and limes flew around me, but it wasn't as bad as usual because here it's somehow not as mundane and boring as it often is. Then I checked on Parfumo and lo and behold: a women's perfume? :-O I wouldn't have thought that. Aire Loco is not harsh and really pretty for women, but I would have at least categorized it as unisex. Looking at the fragrance pyramid, I was convinced I would find a bunch of lemons. Neroli IS an oil derived from oranges/pomerans and is thus citrusy, but somehow I expected something much milder, especially because of the top and base notes. However, Aire Loco remains quite straightforwardly fruity; I smell neither vanilla, nor patchouli, nor cedarwood, and the flowers were never there. Malicious tongues might suspect dish soap/toilet cleaner, but I'm not malicious. Overall, it's a mediocre scent; better than your average 08/15 waters, because it's simply deeper, but still not a candidate for me to buy.

Muse opens with an aromatic dry iris that makes you think it’s going to go in the same direction as Dior Homme Intense (2011) but instead there’s a soft sandalwood in the base instead of the dryer cedar/vetiver combo. I was hoping the frankincense or ink note would materialize and make it more interesting but it never happened. Essentially it’s like Santal Austral Eau de Parfum but with the focus on the iris instead of the sandalwood. Or like Gris Charnel Eau de Parfum without the cardamom or tea notes. It’s alright, but not premium, either in material quality or complexity, compared to, say, Iris Torréfié . Muse would have been better suited to YSL’s department store line rather than their private line in my opinion.

I would smell like this!!! I’ve come across ink notes in perfumes before, but this is the first time I’ve actually wanted to smell like black ink straight out of a pen. I’ll admit, the opening of Muse feels incoherent cause that ink note is just so realistic and intense (especially if it’s a note that’s new to you). It’s strange, but in the best and most artistic way possible. As it begins to settle and make way for the other notes, you are met with a sweet and slightly boozy vanilla, wisps of lavender, and a creamy orris. Not iris the flower, orris the earthy root that accompanies the flower. You also get hints of the frankincense and dry woods. It’s very dark, mysterious, but also has a “come closer” vibe to it. I know I call just about every fragrance sexy, but this one is reallllll sexy. It’s very addictive and it’ll have you sniffing yourself like a fiend. And the purple juice is the cherry on top. This kind of iris is quite novel to me, although I have seen it compared to Velours (2016) and Black Tie Eau de Parfum . Performance wise, this has been great so far. The sillage is strong for the first few hours and it’s not a scent that dies down quickly. You’ll continue to get wafts of it as you move, even around the 6-8 hour mark. I must say this was a very successful blind buy for me, even though I would NOT recommend blind buying this. The season in which it’s been released confuses me (it’s very hot where I am now), but I am so pleased to add this one to my small collection of iris scents and to my fall / winter artillery.

It’s been a long time since I fell instantly in love with a scent! This was an immediate full bottle buy for me, and I bought the biggest size. I love the opening and find it so addictive. Muse is a very comforting, classy, sophisticated, mysterious, sexy, feminine scent. I can smell all the notes, but I really love the ink. As a hater of Blanche bette and Gris Charnel, both of which I find dull, I don’t think this smells similar to them at all. Smelling them side by side, Muse is actually very close to Black Tie Eau de Parfum . It has the same elegant, powdery, softness but with the addition of the ink note, setting it apart from any other fragrance on the market. Perfect for spring, autumn and winter, and suitable for any occasion. 100% signature scent worthy! Now I can take Black Tie off my wish list. This is so very well done and just absolutely stunning!

Smells a bit like the makeup aisle at some cosmetics stores — powdery, creamy, soft, and somewhat artificial. It's nice enough, and blended very well. It stays close to the skin, and doesn't last too long, which I find a bit disappointing given the price point. What I'm missing in this perfume is some sort of personality. A muse is supposed to inspire. I don't know if ink is the place to look to capture this idea.

Saint Laurent (or rather the artist behind it, Marie Salamagne) has once again hit the nail on the head. Well, my enthusiasm for this creation might also be related to the fact that my personal crème de la crème of fragrance notes come together here: vanilla - lavender - iris. I don't think it gets any better for me. In this regard, I had very high expectations for Muse - and one thing will hopefully be clear through this review - they were exceeded. If you are looking for the scent of new designer clothes, packed in unnecessarily printed tissue paper and then stuffed into a much too large designer shopping bag, you will find it here. Muse smells like the moment you arrive home, open that paper bag, and admire your much too expensive piece of fabric once again, indulging in it anew. Yes, yes, everyone knows this joy doesn't last long, but it is there - for a brief moment. And now imagine finding a fragrance that captures that moment?! Muse gives you the opportunity to extend a moment of happiness, to even transfer it to any conceivable piece of clothing, to any conceivable body part (please stay on topic…) The lavender is very understated, anything but dominant and strict The vanilla is subtly woody and it too opts for gentle softness And then we have the iris as the third major player. The delicate flower in a cream-powder manner expresses itself no more than the rest. That is exactly the strength of the perfume. Understatement is the motto and I love everything about it!

There are scents that speak. Others whisper. And then there is Muse . A fragrance that doesn't need to be loud because it has long been writing on skin, on heart, on forgotten page. As soon as it touches my skin, I lose myself. I inhale it.. and I exhale myself.

Here it is, the new “Muse” Eau de Parfum. I have been eagerly waiting for this perfume over the last few days. Admittedly, a bit of skepticism crept in over time. Not because of the listed notes, but rather because one of the marketing images features a very stylishly dressed woman. Is it too feminine for me and will it spoil the notes?

"Now - I let you take your time to consider what I saw, and as you took the time to truly perceive my flower, you hung all your own associations with flowers onto my flower and you write about my flower as if I think and see what you think and see about the flower - which is not the case." Georgia O‘Keefe‘s response to the eroticized perception of her works.

Colmar in autumn - the sun cast golden light on the old cobblestones as I wandered aimlessly through the streets. The air was mild. At the corner, a small inconspicuous church from which a breeze of incense wafted into my nose. In my hand, I held a fragrant vanilla pastry from the pâtisserie. At first, I didn’t notice it.

- You are my new find. You are calm, you are unobtrusive, but you are soooo mysterious. - On paper, Muse smells exactly like what it says: A LOT of lavender, and for me personally, almost too much ink. But I wanted to love it, I wanted to celebrate it and call it my treasure. Of course, scents always behave differently on skin than on paper. The next day: the next mission.

I would never have discovered Loewe women's fragrances without a sample from my online go-to perfumery PD. I had never heard of the brand before - and yet the sample turned out to be a little insider tip and a candidate for my wish list. A floral-powdery-gentle scent, slightly sour and for me also a touch fresh... for the first time I perceive a pleasant leather note in a perfume. It doesn't hit you over the head but rather sneaks in slowly and gives the fragrance that certain extra. In the right situation, the scent can indeed be seductive. There's nothing against a stronger application, as "Aura Magnética" is rather understated. However, the scent is still easily noticeable and envelops you in a pleasant cloud of flowers, powder, and leather. I wouldn't call it a 0815 perfume; you rarely smell something similar. While I have recently been focusing my perfume collection more on autumn/winter scents - this one intrigues me a lot. A very feminine, well-groomed perfume with an overall polished yet still exciting aura. It has made me curious about other fragrances from the house of Loewe. I appreciate it when you can wear fragrances anytime and anywhere, regardless of the season, mood, or occasion. Just spray it on and feel good. "Aura Magnética" is such a scent - my nose is at least magnetically attached to my wrist, and the sample will surely soon be replaced by a full bottle.

Today I curiously sprayed Aura magnetica and thought: Hm, a scent that doesn’t disturb - so so. But the Loewe was just resting, lying in wait, because after a while he came out of the bushes on silent paws, impressing me with his majestic beauty and grandeur. He doesn’t roar at me; he is too sublime for that - he simply makes his presence felt. We exchange deep glances that touch my heart and warm me. His aura is indeed magnetic - and everything about him draws me in. He is also fond of me and lets out a deep, sonorous purr - before gracefully settling down and studying me. So is the scent. Bergamot and mandarin are fresh and harmless, but with the amber, something special is already in the air. Jasmine sambac has an attractively calm elegance, and the leather note speaks of hidden wildness. The patchouli wafts smoky above it, and the vanilla provides comfort and security. I want to snuggle up to the lion's magnificent mane and be his companion. From my hasty "so so," a clear "Oh la la" has emerged, because the scent is very touching. It awakens desires in me - for longing and intuition are intertwined - one drives the other forth.

Yvresse is a Voluptuous 50's Pinup Model obviously a Bottled Blonde faux Tan Jayne Mansfield, Mamie van Doren, Marilyn Monroe, In a Red skintight Sequinned Mermaid cut sleeveless Gown with her hips slowly gliding to a gentile Rumba of an Old Nat King Song Quizas Quizas Quizas, On an Old Record player, The note of Peach is the Champagne she sips from that matches the Liquid luster of gold Bed sheets in a Luxurious Red & Gold Penthouse overlooking 5th Avenue On New Years Eve, As Yvresse dries to the middle the Innocent note of peach Fades and the notes of Lychee and Smoky Caraway turnes Yvresse from a Girlish ingenue to a Temptress, hungry and Full Bodied semi-sweet semi-tart lychee adds a bit of a Uninhabited Territory before the pluck of the First Fruit of Eden Brings Primal touches To Yvresse, Cardamon with juxtaposition of Cinnamon Dries the lychee As we Enter the Final Phase of Yvresse The First spice that comes steeping into the senses Caraway Dry dominates the first minute then Cinnamon sweeter Supports the Caraway The Underpinning of Patchouli gives the base an Semi sweet earthiness Amber & Musk Enrich the scent with it's sweet Texture And Hidden note of Incense the Styrax Note And Fiery Sandalwood Finishes Yvresse. This Perfume is not for the Shy or a woman not to make wave Yvresse is the Opposite She Not Only Demands it She Screams IT! She's Larger then Life, Diva in a Bottle Nothing is Subtle about her but if you want to stand out She's a Perfect Friend.

If someone had told me prior to testing Yvresse that it is possible for a fragrance to smell fizzy, to give one a feeling of small bubbles tickling the nostrils, I probably would have laughed. How this fragrance has managed to encapsulate every quality of a glass of sparkling white wine is beyond me. Yvresse opens very tart, fruity, strong and yes, fizzy. Whether you like the scent or not, the olfactory experience you witness is unlike anything you'll ever come across. Just like a glass of champagne, Yvresse entertains us with sophistication and intoxicating appeal. The incredibly unique blend of notes throughout makes this fragrance truly unforgettable. One of a kind. The apricot, nectarine and peach do come on rather strongly at first and in some ways the result could be described as sharp. It is actually this quality however that I enjoy. There is only a touch of sweetness in this fragrance, which is mostly caused by the coconut, cinnamon, litchi and vanilla. This sweetness is not unpleasant, just a little odd at first. Something that your nose will need time to adjust to. There is no doubt in my mind that this fragrance has been aptly named. Champagne is exactly what it smells like. I love that the later name has been derived from the word 'Ivresse' meaning intoxication.

More like Sauternes than Champagne, but I don’t want to start another trademark issue for this fragrance. Yes, this has similarities to wine, but it seems much more like a sweet dessert wine than anything else. And, yes, there is a chypre base to Yvresse, but overall the fragrance is much more about fruitiness and sweet florals. A well-made sweet wine is one where all the fruit/honey/sweetness is balanced by a proper degree of acidity, though the acidity is a small element when compared to the sugar. The point is largely lost on me with dessert wines and I guess here as well. I get all the other comparisons---Chinatown but without the full dose of the chypre base; Femme, but with less cumin and more honey. But the real point of comparison to me is another Grosman work, Prescriptives Calyx. Calyx has all the fruit, all the rose, but a bit less sugar and more moss. Granted, a different flavor (guava v peach) makes for a qualitative difference, but compositionally, there’s much to compare. Calyx’s success is taking the fruitiest of fruit scents, one that you can almost taste (ripe guava) and balancing it with enough moss and dry rose to compensate for the sweetness, leaving a heady aroma with a spectacularly balanced drydown. Yvresse uses sweeter fruit, adds honey-like amber, uses a sweeter rose, and less moss. Yvresse does lose some of the sweetness as it ages, but what is left without the sweetness? It gets threadbare. I applaud YSL for making a sensible-shoes version of the 1990s fruity floral, but I’m picky about my fruity chypres, and this one I don’t quite love. Seen as a fruity floral, and compared to the raft of sticky sweetness that was selling like mad at the time, it is a smart choice. But as a fruity chypre, it can’t hold its own against Diorella, Cristalle, Chinatown or its YSL sibling, Y. I can see why fruity chypres might have been seen as fertile ground to create more ‘accessible ‘ (read: better selling) fruity-florals at the time, but it’s the balance that’s lost. Remember: this was the year Cristalle EDP was released. Cristalle, but sweeter, less sharp and nicer. God god, who wants that?

I am glad that Yves Saint Laurent YVRESSE was renamed from CHAMPAGNE--not because I agree with fastidious French law regarding the use of that quasi-sacred name, but because many people will not know that "ivresse" means "drunkenness", as opposed to "piles of damp sisal rugs" or "straw basket factory in the tropics," which would be far more apt names for the lengthy middle phase of this distinctive chypre perfume--were Demeter only able to isolate and capture those scents in a bottle! YVRESSE, in fact, helped me to refine my concept of chypre, which I now believe to contain essentially within it a big, big and abiding sillage that follows me about constantly reminding me that I am in the midst of a cloud of chypre dust! On the oakmoss to vetiver continuum, YVRESSE lies much closer to the vetiver end. I love the damp sisal/straw smell of the middle phase of this fragrance, which has excellent staying power in the edt. I am not as thrilled by the somewhat fruity opening--but it disappears as quickly as a champagne bubble, and it's certainly not painful to endure. The middle sisal/straw phase gives way eventually to a slightly sweet but beautiful drydown that remains chypre but is less damp and a bit more spicy. I highly recommend YVRESSE to chypre lovers who crave that fascinatingly paradoxical fog that hangs heavy while somehow elevating the wearer at the same time. This is a perfume with a serious chypre sillage.

I was 19 when I discovered this fragrance. It just came out. My best friend has swapped Champagne pure perfume for Dior Poison pure perfume with me. Little I new how this not so attractive then gem will grow on me over many years. I don't remember what I have done with this treasure as it was far too much for me , literally about 30 ml of pure perfume. 25 years forward I started craving a memory of this scent . With light hand purchase full bottle of Yvresse old formula from eBay for eye watering price. One spray and I am hitting a spot , yet again 19 year old , in night club with my friend. Now I appreciate it. I am instantly becoming the most seductive , intelligent and sexy woman in the club. This is how this undiscrbable fragrance makes me feel. It is a true gem, but not as deep and seductive as my long lost treasure.

Controversy can either hurt or help a fragrance. I did neither for Yvress. If you have the original bottle its highly collectible, when it was Champaigne. It is totally the early 90s trademark that seemed to be everywhere. The composition itself pays tribute to the classic chypres of the past-Cotys original, Mitsouko and Y.

Said by Yves Saint Laurent at the launching of Champagne in 1993. Three years later renamed Yvresse, which means drunkenness. I guess Monsieur Laurent was not pleased, when he was sued by Comité interprofessionnel du vin de Champagne for using their famous brand name. But then again.

After reading here in the forum that a perfume enthusiast received a compliment for their respective fragrance, I too can rejoice in a compliment. And it was for Yvresse, of all things. Since I have Yvresse in the cube form and also the cork version in my collection, I wanted to own the original Champagne as well.

What a cheerful, fruity, fresh little chypre this is. Hicks! Do you know punch bowl? It can be prepared in various ways. I make it as follows (since it smells almost identical to Yvresse): Pit fresh fruits, peaches, apricots, nectarines, and soak them overnight in white rum - don’t be stingy with the rum - and chill very well.

Nostalgia! I have owned this fragrance for a very long time. In the past, when everything was just better, perfumes seemed to have a certain quality.... :) It is still the old, unchanged scent and after all these years, it hasn’t gone off one bit. Immediately after spraying, it is round and fully present.

A sweet powdery cloud of pear and violets tends to settle into either one or the other. On my partner's skin pear took centerstage. I, unfortunately, got the violets. I think my body just doesn't run hot enough to bring out the sweeter flavors properly. Once the flowers mellowed out a little, a beautiful earthy woodiness started peeking through. Sleek, damp and absolutely gorgeous. I wish there was more of it. There wasn't. Or, rather, it felt like I just couldn't get close enough to it. Like standing on wet slippery rocks near a waterfall on the river. The forest is on the other side of the stream, just outside my grasp, with its beautiful wet soil, lush with decaying leaves and growing mycelium... and no way to get there safely :( It disappeared almost entirely from my partner's skin in under two hours. On me at that point it just started getting softer and sweeter. The aggressive floral cloud subsided and I could finally sniff it up close and personal! Unfortunately, the earthiness I longed for had already disappeared by then. I could feel the sweet pear again, I could differentiate the flowers, but the magic was gone. The gentle flowery scent was objectively pleasant as it slowly evaporated from my skin in the next ~3 hours, and I felt almost sorry that I didn't enjoy it. It was right there with me and it was adorable, and yet I couldn't help but long for that beautiful forest floor... Interesting, albeit melancholic experience. I might wear it again sometime once I forget the details, but a full sized bottle will likely outlive me.

Not too long ago, I tested 7 Elixir and Esencia Elixir and was positively surprised. A brief heads up: unfortunately, there will be no praise hat trick with Earth Elixir . Since I don't look at the ingredient list beforehand and want to test the fragrances blind at first, I was a bit unsure about what to expect. A fragrance called Earth will smell earthy? But the bottle color speaks a different language. After spraying it on, it quickly became clear that it is a very floral scent. Initially still a bit fresh and lightly spiced (perhaps due to the truffle note), but unfortunately, it becomes rather expressionless as it develops. The mimosa lives up to its name and shapes the scent with shy restraint. I'm a little surprised that the oud note is not perceivable to me at all. There are only 12 users registered on Parfumo so far, but at least 42 percent of them are male. I would have guessed the female percentage to be higher right off the bat. But that could still change with increasing user numbers. People are referred to as sensitive souls when they are very sensitive. This metaphor was adopted because the mimosa reacts very sensitively to external influences and immediately folds up when touched. That such a fragrance does not perform in a beast mode way may almost sound logical. I could perceive four sprays on my neck for about four hours. The bottle fits the floral character of the fragrance, but somehow I don't see much connection regarding the naming. Sure, the little flowers also grow from the earth, but when I hear the name "Earth," I immediately think of other color tones. The fragrance is consistently unremarkable, both in terms of scent DNA and performance. Accordingly, I find the almost 180,- euros for 100 ml to be too much to ask. While 7 Elixir and Esencia Elixir could impress with natural/authentic minimalism, Earth Elixir is too minimalist in all evaluation criteria.

I love lilies, one of my favourite flowers along with gardenia, tuberose and lilac. I have tried Tom Ford Shanghai Lily and also Lys Fume, but this is the best lily soliflore. This extrait has fantastic sillage and excellent longevity. Its sweet and green with lovely spicy note in the base. Just lifts my mood when wearing this parfum and love love love.

A warm summer night is stylishly accompanied by Roja's "Lily": floral, balsamic, and rich in dreamy beauty! Once again, Roja Dove shows how he can create enchanting compositions from even the most ordinary fragrance notes. "Lily" is not puristic either, but rather characterized by floral opulence and sensual warmth. How could it be any different? After a brief classic freshness kick from bergamot and lemon, the gate to Roja's grand flower garden in Grasse opens once more. He strolls with us through the abundance of blossoms and scents, almost casually assembling a lush bouquet centered around the well-known, fragrant May roses and sensually ripe, large-flowered jasmine, to which he adds some porcelain-like frangipani blossoms this time. Their uniquely special aromatic mix (which seems to contain a hint of jasmine, a bit of vanilla, and a touch of amaretto/almond) marries exquisitely with the fine spice of the slightly old-fashioned garden carnations that I love, thus creating a successful transition to the sensual encounter with the vanilla goddess Aphrodite, who must not be missed and envelops herself in a veil of erotic-animalic musk, which she skillfully spreads like a finely woven net of scent over this seductive splendor! The alluringly developing beauty of this fragrance tempts one into romantic dreams. With the typical longevity of Roja, the individual fragrance notes have all the time to unite tastefully; they entwine with each other in a fragrant dance. Even though "Lily," the proud, scent-intensive lily, is missing here as a fragrance component, this expanding magic delights in its own unique way. Here, romance in fragrance bears the enticing name "Lily"!

It would be lovely if a fairy appeared to me now and granted me a perfume wish. But wait! Only one? And then: Which one? Actually, I already have some floral chypres like "Dia Woman," although it is much soapier, more floral, and sweeter than "Lily" by Roja. Or "Quelques Fleurs" by Houbigant, which is bursting with floral notes and not so soapy. Or "Tosca Parfüm" - I mean the real perfume - which is a classic oriental floral chypre with everything that entails. All three mentioned do not, at least for me, perceptibly contain some of the flowers that can be slightly unpleasant to overwhelming for me, such as jasmine, lily of the valley, lily, and certain orange blossom notes. The exception for me is ylang-ylang, which I actually like for its somewhat piercing scent, but I cannot perceive it individually in these complex fragrances. However, the three listed scents also do not have any noticeable tuberose and tiaré like I can distinctly smell in "Lily." I explicitly write: Not perceptible to me. Because they are probably also incorporated in the polyfloral scents. "Lily" is, in contrast to the mentioned and other floral chypres, a distinctly more robust floral scent, starting off green and cool. The citrus notes apparently blend immediately with the heart note for me. I immediately smell jasmine and lily of the valley, but also tiaré, and again in the third test, I can perceive the tuberose. I recognize tiaré, but I cannot describe it. The rose seems to be one of the modern ones with a green and fresh note. The flowers that initially smell slightly animalistic transform after a while into a holistic, not overwhelming floral mixture that I find exceptionally enchanting. The robustness clearly comes from the cloves and later on from the spice clove. The clove notes with a subtle wood tone tame the floral mixture, making it more robust but not dominating it. Therefore, there is only a subtle creaminess. Above all, "Lily" is not sweet for me; vanilla seems to only work in the background. I qualify "not sweet." Because "Lily" certainly has the sweetness of the flowers with the mentioned green notes, but no nectar or honey sweetness. After some time, even the clove note fades, and the flowers become more delicate and transparent. The longevity is very good, and the sillage seems rather moderate. "Lily" is declared as a feminine scent. I can imagine that men might also like it for its balance of floral and spicy robustness. In my opinion, Lily is a perfume that one could also wear at the so-called "big" events without losing its scent in the general perfume and odor cacophony. I cannot compare "Lily" with any of the scents I have tested so far. It is lovely to be able to test this preciousness at all. And for two to three special occasions, the sample is more than enough. Heartfelt thanks to the generous giver.

Over a year ago, I walked past the then-new bottles of the Le Vestiaire series at Oberpollinger. Even then, I was enchanted by Velours, but I had already spent my budget on other bottles that day. The price of Velours (€246) made this dream fragrance feel somewhat distant, and I thought back then, "Who came up with this silly idea of launching 125ml bottles, and who needs that much?" Just before Christmas, I happened to come across it again at Breuninger in Stuttgart; the YSL counter then told me that they had just added the series to their lineup. I had to spray it on myself again immediately... and bam... a day before Christmas, it literally knocked the Christmas ornaments off the tree, along with the candles... Two days after Christmas, it was time to get it. The exact words at the counter: "No... unfortunately, it's no longer available... it's sold out!" Since then, the counter has a bite mark from me;-)! In that moment, I knew how Schalke must have felt in May 2001, 1.5 hands already on the championship trophy/bottle... and at the last moment, the mother snatches the lion cub away again!!! After an apathetic 5 minutes, I was able to speak again, and the nice lady at the counter managed to track down a bottle through the Düsseldorf branch, which was then sent directly to my home... Thanks for the great customer service at this point! Velours is a dream fragrance for me, a jewel, a masterpiece. A scent of the kind that makes me flip out a maximum of only 3 times a year, just like with Oud Radieux or Fars. Unfortunately, this doesn't happen to me more often. This gem, as if it came from a manufactory, makes me revel down to the tips of my hair; I have rarely experienced such fineness, such velvetiness, except as mentioned above. This dry-powdery opening immediately captivated me, a blend of muted Dior Homme (sweetness), the velvety-powdery Oriental Express, and the dry-woody and mildly incense-like Bois d'Argent makes my heart race. Especially since I unfortunately cannot perceive Dior Homme and BdA for long. Sensual... yes, also soft... slightly feminine-tinged, but still masculine enough... but it is precisely this velvetiness that is unparalleled. As it develops further, a wonderfully dry teen note emerges, which I can best compare to the note from Neroli Outrenoir; the similarly high-quality vanilla could also be from Guerlain. For me, Velours maintains the optimal balance in every respect; nothing pushes itself vainly to the forefront, neither the spice nor the sweetness is intrusive, thus the fragrance does not wear off because it does not constantly occupy the nose yet is always present. Throughout the day, it becomes slightly more robust, resembling a buttery soft leather note, which evokes comfort and warmth in me. I was able to perceive the fragrance all day long; it never became too much, even today in relatively mild temperatures. The sillage is strong at first, then settles into the upper mid-range... perfect! For me, it acts as a membrane (only lets the beautiful through) and a shield at the same time! Anyone who lets themselves be misled and influenced by the YSL mainstream program, who is deterred by the seemingly "unmanly notes" from a test... and does not recognize or want to recognize the still existing superb quality of YSL... is simply to blame if they miss out on this fragrance!

"... Sometimes you think it can't go on, everything is already set and done, but then suddenly depths and perspectives appear that you thought were unattainable and now present themselves in all their fullness to the accumulated experience. I often feared that I was dried up and broken and would hopelessly stand before the black curtain of boredom - yet this curtain has often been torn, and I have been able to glimpse boundless horizons - which has brought me the greatest feeling of happiness, so I want to express it, moments of true pride." - YSL This life motto of Yves Saint Laurent, which he proclaimed in 1983 at the opening of his exhibition at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York, resonates in my ears as I make the acquaintance of "Le Vestiaire - Velours." Although the fragrance was composed long after the master's death, I feel that a curtain of fragrance boredom has been drawn for me here as well. For the scents of this brand have not particularly excited me for a long time - in fact, never really. So I approached the testing a bit casually and was promptly punished for it! A delicate infusion of black tea, not sparingly perfumed with black and pink pepper, greets me. Oh dear! What does my sensitive nose with its pepper allergy say? Will it cope or will it be punished with long sneezes? It's amazing: I tolerate this interesting mélange, despite the allergy, and enjoy this aroma! The elegant iris takes a few steps back behind the beautiful, but also somewhat dominant, white large-flowered jasmine. What a display of floral abundance presents itself at this moment! Frankincense, wonderfully harmonizing with the previous scent materials, completes a very appealing olfactory painting. Creamy vanilla in full warm scent; woods, skillfully ambianced and placed in this wonderfully flowing progression, and a pleasant dose of musk refine this fragrance in a sophisticated way. Thus, a fine hint of noble suede emerges, which stands in a well-balanced relationship with the bright flowers and does not necessarily seek the foreground. For someone who is not a big leather fan, like I am, this is a very pleasant fragrance phenomenon! Which, with a longevity of several hours, is truly a joy. How often have I almost desperately tried to wash off a suddenly bothersome leather note after a certain time and failed due to the extraordinary durability! This time, I perceive this elegant fragrance creation as a soft embrace that invites cuddling! A YSL fragrance, even if from a time long after the tumultuous life of the great magician, that I really like: I am amazed and thrilled!

This fragrance from YSL is very intriguing and has two faces for me - but first, the description; ultra-powdery like lightly floral, fine, rosy blush from a high-end cosmetics brand, simultaneously soft-leathery and then develops into a dreamy woody, slightly sweet vanilla. Now, this fragrance could be, on one hand, that edgy, quick-witted, hot goth teenager who wears torn fishnets with chunky platform boots and pairs her short velvet dress with an oversized 80s black suede jacket lined with lamb's wool, as well as the quirky, somewhat aging neighbor who lives at the end of the street in an old-fashioned attic apartment. She has aged well, is very delicate and pretty, but wears a bit too much makeup (which is quite difficult with increasing nearsightedness) and has three fluffy, groomed dogs. I would love to be both, and both smell like YSL La Vestiaire Velours. Now I have described two wonderful clichés from a US series or something similar, but this fragrance is really very special, and I like it precisely for that reason.

I love leather perfumes. From strong to light, dark black SM dungeon leather whips to the bright leather interior of a new car. La Vestiaire Velours is a stylish middle ground here. Far from an animalistic beast, but more refined than new, clean leather seats and handbags, like those from Bottega Veneta. The suede scent of a theater dressing room on a premiere night is how I imagine the setting of La Vestiaire Velours. Many well-kept suede jackets, slightly rough and velvety, a bit smoky in the nose, but cool because their wearers have been watching the reinterpretation of "Waiting for Godot" for half an hour. In addition, there are very present iris and jasmine from well-perfumed ladies' coats, which adds elegance to the whole. Apparently, one or two theater guests enjoy orthodox masses, as that must be where the hint of incense in the small room comes from. In the end, everything is warmly rounded off by a musk note, which almost reminds me of the scent of skin, skin that slips back into the expensive jackets after the premiere and warms itself in them, just like I do in this fragrance, I received it as a sample because I had indicated leather as my favorite note in an online shop. I was all the more puzzled by the fragrance pyramid of this scent and had no great expectations of it. Now it has become one of my new favorite leather treasures, but of the cultivated kind. It is quite intense and captivating on me, and since that doesn't bother me, I also wear it during the day. The sillage and longevity impress me; after about 7 hours, it was still perceptible, which I don't usually experience with such floral scents. I am truly deeply in love with my theater dressing room and can only recommend it if leather is your open or secret passion, but you don't want to scare anyone with it.

Velours, an almost elusive fragrance, despite having been released in 2016. A candidate that makes one wonder why it had to be discontinued. In response to my predecessor's question, I would like to address it as well, as I hadn't considered it myself until now: Yes, I find it good to test and review discontinued fragrances. At that time, I tested Velours knowing it had already been discontinued. Back then, there were still a few more Souk offers, but it has been rather quiet around it for the past few months. Recently, however, I did manage to get another sample, which I will use sparingly. I wanted to test it back then nonetheless. Fragrances with such good reviews and comments always intrigue me. I want to test this "treasure," this now rare find, and I want to be captivated. Long searches, sometimes paying high prices per ml, and sometimes you get lucky and come across such popular discontinued fragrances, pure joy. And so I want to rave about this fragrance here and perhaps inspire one or two people to test it. I don't know why, but testing such fragrances is becoming more and more enjoyable for me. After the initial excitement, there's often disappointment when the fragrance isn't as good as hoped, because then getting a bottle is significantly harder than getting a sample. But I'm willing to take that risk. Now, let's talk about the fragrance itself. The pyramid looks enticing. Black tea, iris butter, suede, I like all of these base notes. In the top note, the black tea is initially skipped; for me, it starts immediately with iris butter. Soft, dense, but not as creamy as one might expect from Francesca Bianchi. It becomes a bit powdery, and gradually the suede comes through, which I can also recognize as suede. A bit rough, yet soft. The tea now emerges in the background, adding a gentle note. In the base, a dark frankincense-vanilla joins in, only subtly sweet, rounded off by woods. The performance is just right, a slightly perceptible cloud when passing by, but to truly experience it, one must come closer. No attention-seeking performance. Elegance and refinement describe Velours very well. I am a big fan of leathery-powdery DNAs, especially leather with iris butter. Rarely found, even more rarely well-executed. This combination of powerful leather and delicate iris butter works wonderfully. Overall, Velours strikes me as a somewhat dark and alluring fragrance, with intriguing notes that are beautifully harmonized, and the quality is good, as is often the case with this line. The bottle looks absolutely elegant with this slight dark purple and black running color. I must confess, neither leather-vanilla nor iris butter-vanilla combinations are new, but so far I don't know of a fragrance where it has been executed better, at least not when considering the entire fragrance progression. So anyone who can still snag a sample somewhere should seize the opportunity!

Sometimes it just clicks. These are moments that you don’t plan; they simply happen. Actually, most major brands in the fragrance market disappoint me at regular intervals. Sometimes there are surprises, but that is rather the rare case.

If this scent were a suede cape, I would wear it every day and stroll through the city... I haven't smelled such a wonderful fragrance in a long time, and as we all know, there are a H-U-G-E number of great scents out there! However, I had to warm up to it first.

Do reviews of discontinued fragrances make sense? ... Probably not. Does it make sense to test discontinued fragrances? ... No (at least from my perspective). So much for theory. Practically, I accidentally tested a fragrance that has been discontinued, namely this one. I didn’t know that - that it was discontinued.

Super boring. Do yourself a favor and go look for a “nice, musky” perfume elsewhere. This is such a stripped down, lifeless perfume and a huge regret to own. It opens up a bit citrusy, but it quickly turns into a fresh jasmine with some amber— there is a sweetness that I really didn’t expect and really don’t like. Not a good musky scent and the performance is very poor even when over spraying.

What can be said about RDHP20? A perfect floral ambery perfume for all seasons! Really luxurious... its performance is really good! Once when I wore it at a family meal, my sister told me that she can't stop smelling me and that it's my best perfume in her eyes... and I have a respectable collection;) This is the only Roja perfume I bought in a blind buy because I bought the numbered bottle number 1 that the company makes. 8.5/10.

RDHP20 (ROJA DOVE HAUTE PERFUMERIE 20) Roja Dove 2024 I have been wearing this now for many days, in different kind weathers waiting if I get some challenging facets out of it. I have to say that this is quite safe perfume - if you already love Roja’s creations. It doesn’t mean that it’s boring or simple, no way, but it’s easy to love for sure. Since there are many people waiting some opinions on RDHP20 I want to keep this review simple. I concentrate on the questions which I have got the most and on the other hand I want to compare it with some scents so you maybe get the idea of the scent easier. COMPARING DOESN’T MEAN THEY ARE SAME. What comes to the scent of RDHP20 there is nothing same with Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2019) which is a surprise for some if only checking all those notes. They share so many but believe me, you don’t get a sister of 15. Rather this is like an older brother, the male version of this pair of Chypres, it’s like the opposite as is the colouring of the labels. Still RDHP20 is very unisex, and on my skin it stays a bit softer and lighter than on my husband’s skin, where the base is much deeper and darker with clearly musky and enjoyable Oudy undertones - but on my skin it never screams masculinity and it’s a bit sweeter. The opening is sparkling with aldehydes, and citruses are detectable longer than in 15. There is somewhat familiar cola vibe in the opening as well which not only reminds me of Enigma Pour Homme but also of PDLN3. Yet, this seems to appear more clearly on my skin and not so much on male skin. However, it disappears as the scent develops. This is ambery and mossy, all the flowers are not like a huge bouquet in 15, they stay totally in the background. Violet and Peach which both has a major role in 15 is tuned down here as well and I don’t find any traditionally feminine characteristics. This is Chypre but not even close to Diaghilev neither to Chypre Extraordinaire. I have them both and I love them as well a lot but this is very different. If you want to get the idea of the scent from the notes, you should just think of the base. It represents this gorgeous scent. Fresh and spicy, even smoky feeling from Frankincense, deep woods dipped in Peru Balsam, and Vanilla together with Benzoin bringing a little bit of sweetness and a lot of warmth.
