Oud, Musk and mosses are finishing the whole blend making it an incredible classy, somewhat nostalgic (not dated) and utterly luxurious elixir. RDHP20 works well in hot weather as well but for some people it can be too much. I love these kind of scents in warm weather when I can detect even the smallest details of it. This is absolutely office safe when spraying sparingly but since I only have a sample I don’t have a possibility to test this in all possible environments, temperatures and moods. As I have tried to get as many wearings as possible from this precious sample I don’t have experience of overspraying which I love so much btw. Longevity is good even without overspraying. Full bottle worthy into my collection of 24 Rojas. Absolutely gorgeous scent. Top: Aldehydes, Bergamot, Lemon, Lime (RDHP15: Aldehydes, Lemon, Bergamot,  Grapefruit, Mandarin, Orange) Heart : Geranium, Clary Sage, Magnolia, Freesia, Rose, Jasmine, Ylang Ylang, Violet, Peach (RDHP15: Lily of the Valley, Geranium, Jasmine, Cistus,  Heliotrope, Violet, Peach, Red Champaca) Base: Rhubarb, Clove, Mosses, Cèdre-sur-Orris, Sandalwood, Clear Woods, Amber, Vanilla, Benzoin, Tonka Bean, Labdanum, Patchouli, Peru Balsam, Cypriol, Frankincense, Aoud Wood, Musks. (RDHP15: Coriander, Ginger, Pepper, Moss Notes, Patchouli, Vetiver, Casmir Wood, Amyris, Sandalwood, Benzoin, Vanilla, Tonka Bean, Peru Balsam, Orris, Frankincense, Labdanum, Ambrarome Absolute, Civet, Musk) The house mentions key notes: Aldehydes, Lemon, Lime, Rose, Jasmine, Violet, Clear Woods, Amber and Vanilla. Imo Clove, mosses, Benzoin, Peru Balsam, Frankincense and Musks are definitely key notes as well. Without them this would be a way too linear. Thank you for reading, I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more

Hello everyone, A few weeks ago, I received the sample of Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2024) (thanks again for that). A really common question is whether there are differences compared to Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2019) . Yes and no! What do I mean by that? I had the old Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2019) for quite a while, and there are few fragrances in this scent world that bring the elegance and class of that one, and that was exactly the reason why I ended up using it much less frequently, and ultimately that was also the reason why I sold it... Do I regret it..., somehow yes... And what about the Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2024) ? It carries this "class" with it and you can tell, but it is not as exorbitant as in the Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2019) ! Differences: The Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2024) - is more pleasing - easier to wear (less heavy/bulky) - more unisex than the old one (the tendency there leaned more towards feminine) In addition, we have again the typical and proven structure of Roja = starting citrus fruity, moving to floral - lightly with creamy and slightly sweet musk. Performance: Very similar in both H/S! How is it received? Since it is easier to wear, regarding work, leisure, and parties (not disco), it is very well received... But there is one difference that I notice again and again...! It always smells like a "Tony Iommi Monkey Special | XerJoff" over time - without the passion fruit and without the leather. I have a 21' "Tony Iommi Monkey Special | XerJoff" that is less pronounced, but a current 23' and 24' really come close. And that makes the scent really beautiful, exciting, and experiencing such a twist nowadays (despite new batches) is truly nice. I can't wear this daily, but it is really nice to have ;). Can I recommend it? Test it and then decide..., I'll put it this way, if I ever get a leftover bottle, then I might not say no! And now have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______ (Now the same as almost always - because it applies!) Now to the topic of luxury: As you can see partly in my profile, I have really smelled many fragrances, and there are scents where you can smell a certain (partly) strong synthetics, and you quickly realize that some fragrance houses focus more on quantity than quality, and there are some where you can tell "oh come on, let's add more + better ingredients" and you can really smell that at the end of the day. Just a brief note on the topic of packaging, bottle, sprayer: I'll keep it short; I give a 10 out of 10 in every category, and I know very well that tastes are very different. So, if someone honestly rates this with a 7 or less... - PHEW. Beautiful and very high-quality cap, nice timeless bottle design, etc. .... so I find it very hard to rate it differently, and I say this not because I like or dislike a brand! Now a short note on my opinion: I am not sponsored, influenced by anyone, receiving money, or anything else. I approach the topic of perfume as I am, honestly; everything else is not my style. My true personal opinion is very VALUABLE to me, and I hope maybe ;) that this is noticeable. If I don't like something, such as packaging, bottle, sprayer, or H/S, then I communicate that too!

Hello everyone, I’m back with a review of a new Roja that could actually become a "crowd-pleaser classic." I mean it in the sense that there are Rojas that throw many, many fragrance notes at you all at once, which can be overwhelming and sometimes (for me) too much. In my eyes, for example, that’s a "Diaghilev (Parfum) | Roja Parfums." And please don’t get me wrong. Fragrances like the latter are CLASSICALLY composed, but just not easy-to-wear. Yes, yes, they are not meant to be daily scents, but I also don’t have to buy a fragrance that is simply too much for me. I hope you spare me for this opinion. However, the Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2024) is completely different for me. And so my second perfume review begins. Scent: Roja Dove draws on THE unisex start of the brand. Fresh and slightly citrusy with aldehydes, lime, and bergamot. Sounds familiar to me, sounds familiar to you, and is certainly well-received. After a few minutes, the fragrance fully develops on my skin. (It might also be because I store the perfumes in the fridge and they need to warm up on the skin first. What’s your experience with that?) The flowers slowly bloom. Rose, freesia, and magnolia fight their way to the sunlight (please excuse this wording; it might be a professional hazard :D), while the sage always ensures that the scent never drifts too much into the feminine and remains beautifully wearable for all genders. But what would this fragrance be without its main player? Roja chose an old acquaintance: the peach. When I first read this, I was worried I had made a bad purchase because I’m not a particular fan of this note. I’ve smelled it often, been bothered by it often, but Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2024) has reconciled me. A light and floral peach like this has fought its way back into my fragrance heart. This playful mix of notes lingers for many hours and lifts my spirits. true to Roja, the fragrance slightly changes its character from time to time, while all the notes play alternately with the peach, with the base type never deviating too much. I also find it very beautiful when the moss from the base shines through and leads to a "gentle momentum." Once the peach is gone and has taken all the flowers with it, a long, faintly woody base remains, where the very clean oud along with the synthetic fragrance ingredient Clearwood lingers on my skin. Something still happens here, and that’s what I like about this perfume. The rhubarb flashes briefly, adding some last exciting moments before everything calms down, which I hadn’t expected at all. All in all, I find it not too sweet, definitely fruity-fresh-floral, and occasionally slightly creamy before it drifts into a light woody scent. The progression is very well coordinated. You can at least expect that at this price, but I still want to mention it here. Longevity: It accompanied me on my several test days in a row from 8 AM to easily 10 PM, even though it’s not strongly perceptible later on. But I like that, and I’ll elaborate on that below. It doesn’t bother me to wear this one scent all day, as it often changes for me and doesn’t come off as rigid or linear. Sillage: I understand that the fragrance development in recent years has increasingly leaned towards scents with extreme longevity and room-filling effects (at least that’s my perception, WARNING: subjective!). However, I’m only partially a fan of that. I don’t want to burden my surroundings with the next powerhouse every day. I want to wear a fragrance that (ideally) accompanies me throughout the day but just accompanies ME and doesn’t drive anyone away. Of course, I have those kinds too, but I only wear them when I can’t stand someone ;). The Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2024) radiates more strongly from my skin in the first hour(s) (never too strong) and noticeably backs off afterwards. Especially the last phase described above is super pleasant because I can perceive it, and the people immediately around me can too, but the room can still "breathe." That’s how it should be in my eyes, but other people have different preferences, and that’s perfectly fine. Bottle: Do I need to say anything about it? Roja-typical upper class from the sprayer to the design (the pompous design will always remain a point of contention). Enough said! Who is this for and how is it received? I think it’s unisex and can be used across a very wide age range, and you can never go wrong with it in spring/summer. The biggest difference to other Rojas, in my opinion, is that it’s not only suitable for the most noble and rare occasions but can also sweeten your everyday life. Give it a try and feel free to share your opinion with me, but I find it versatile despite, or perhaps because of, its high-quality fragrance ingredients. It’s not a Swiss Army knife like, for example, a "Noble XXI: Art Deco - Cypress | Clive Christian," but always good enough to leave a polished impression and stand out positively. I have always received positive feedback. Would I buy it? No. The retail price of a full bottle is certainly not worth it to me, but as a decant (thanks to David @MscGrmt), I wouldn’t want to miss it in the current season. Hats off, Roja, for the perfect release timing! Maybe one day it will be available as a leftover bottle at a better price. So, that was quite a ride, and I hope I could share a bit about the Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2024) and my impression of it. Thank you for reading, and have a great time! -------------- P.S.: Feel free to take care of the question of whether a synthetic fragrance ingredient belongs in perfumes of this price range.

When I first sprayed this on it blew me away. I got hit with that beautiful orange and cognac. I tried a ton of different fragrances that day and this smelled like nothing I tried before. It was an instant buy for me. Sweet but masculine and sexy. It’s got really good longevity and sillage but not overwhelming. I couldn’t love this scent more.

In the evening, a poker night at the casino with the boys was on the agenda for Saturday, so Money for Nothing and Sharp Dressed. Earlier that afternoon, tactically smart, I went to the Saturday market downtown with my better half. Who wants to spend forever examining strawberries at the fruit stand when you’re going to pack some anyway? So a quick "Hey sweetie, I'm in that store back there" later, I found myself in the perfumery I trust. Alongside the always laid-back owner in his fabric pants and dark glasses, I also encountered the new YSL L'homme 2022 there. Boom. Bullseye. The scent: It can work magic. The top note is zesty fruity fresh, but not that sticky apple freshness; rather, it’s the blood orange sparkling in combination with bergamot, with the first two or three kicks from its friends in the base note. If they were blank, the two would smell different together, but something masculine from below helps, is that vetiver already? Fantastic. Packed. Interesting thing, Yves, you never let the heart note stand alone; to be precise, the top note very slowly transitions directly into the base note, so that the masculine-fruity top note takes the noble, but never overly present lavender by the hand and immediately slaps it with the spicy wooden board. The transition lasts a solid 1-4 hours and remains groovy-masculine with masculine fruit, sweetened oak wood, and a herby green, very complex mix to boot, with the vetiver perfectly dosed here, showing once again how multifaceted this one green component can be. There are at least 2+ other scent aromas helping out in the background, but they are not listed. Bullseye, it grooves. The ride through the heart note track is the best part of the new L'Homme, all with a hefty portion of scent quality; the price is definitely reasonable. Well. ... imagine sitting relaxed and without appointments in a white linen shirt, armed with sunglasses, in a bar in Havana City, sipping an ice-cube-chilled Cuba Libre at a very unorthodox time, the smoking Monte Cristo casually resting in the ashtray, while the daily newspaper is briefly set aside to have a quick chat with the bartender about classic cars, and the ocean sun is shining through the palms into the large, dark brown wooden windows; then I’ve just described the feeling of the base note. The scent will remain in my collection until it is discontinued. Oh yes, never stop at blackjack on the way to the poker table!

Orange bottle, 10x bitter orange mentioned in the marketing, a split orange on the advertisement... There is no way around it, one must suspect that the bitter orange is meant to shape the main character of the perfume. Therefore, it is all the more surprising that the scent smells a bit different than I expected. Yes, in the opening, this advertised bitter orange is indeed recognizable BUT much more subtle than expected. I would have anticipated a sparkling, zesty orange with a slight acidity, but in this case, the bitter orange is very unprovocative and quiet, blending under the woody notes. If I had to illustrate this metaphorically, I would say it’s as if not only the orange was thrown into the juicer, but also the branch it was hanging from. But different than expected does not necessarily mean bad. I like the opening, even though it is rather quiet and unremarkable. However, the orange fades relatively quickly, and after 20-30 minutes, unfortunately, a synthetic note emerges. Probably triggered by lavender, which has made me extremely skeptical whenever I discover lavender in a perfume's ingredient list. Because unfortunately, it is usually associated with cheaper designer scents, as is the case here. Towards the end, it becomes woodier and a bit creamy. Fortunately, at least the woods are not overly marked by synthetics. The manufacturer particularly promotes one of the woods: "An elegant upcycling ingredient - oak wood infusion. Distilled from oak wood chips from cognac barrels." The term "upcycling," which comes from "recycling," is about enhancing a waste product, in this case, used cognac barrels, through repurposing. It’s a nice thought that the wood from old barrels is incorporated into perfumes, thus giving it a second life. The only question is which alcohol the wood prefers, in the barrel or in the bottle?! There is a fundamental problem that I keep hearing in reviews of the "L'homme" series from YSL, namely the weak performance. Unfortunately, this is also the case here, as four sprays on the neck last only two hours in self-perception. For an EdP, this is very weak, and accordingly, I find the price too high. The bottle fits perfectly with the color of the bitter orange and immediately indicates that this is a "L'homme" scent from YSL. This perfume is a solid flanker, but it could definitely show a bit more courage and present itself stronger and more provocatively. La Nuit de L'Homme Bleu Électrique feels like a more electrifying alternative from its own house.

Yves Saint Laurent, it must be said bluntly, has a catastrophic marketing department when it comes to naming perfumes. Whether for men or women. It’s almost a miracle to order the correct and intended one among L´Hommes Parfum, Le Parfum, Parfum Intense, or Intense Le Parfum (I believe some of the examples above don’t even exist like that anymore… Or do they?!:-) ) What times those were with iconically distinct bottles and names like Opium, Kouros, Jazz, and the like. One longs for those days… As for the perfume itself, the Eau de Parfum is a quite pleasantly crafted all-rounder. More autumnal than the fresh-violet-toned EdT, a bit cozier, yet still casual and suitable for everyday wear, without drifting atmospherically towards the October storm season. Overall, a rather warm opening, carried by a very softly enveloped orange, which is accompanied by a nicely rounded lavender undertone. Compared to Caron’s “Pour un homme…” or even Gaultier’s “Le Mâle,” where the lavender appears very natural or at least clearly graspable, here it hides a bit under or behind a slightly sawed-off powderiness. Perhaps the oak wood, which comes to the forefront quite early, is to blame, as it somewhat vanillan-toastily-woody stifles any hope for ethereal spaces. The good thing: The scent is not breathtakingly original, but one wishes that certainly more men would opt for this at least smoothly crafted, harmonious fragrance rather than torturing others with horrors like “Sauvage” or lab news from Boss or Davidoff. My 20 cents on that.

It happened on a Monday morning in November, as I was getting myself and the kids ready for school. There I stood in the bathroom, contemplating which fragrance I wanted to wear that day, and I remembered a sample I had received with Babycat (a gift for my wonderful wife) from YVSL. A spray on the left and right, and one on the neck, and et voila, I was Ready to Go. The kids were already set with their school bags, and my wife sent me off with a “Hey, you smell great.” And off we went on the first drive to my daughter's school. The scent of YVSL L'homme had not escaped my daughter either, who called out compliments from the backseat during the drive: “Dad, you smell really cozy.” I had to smile and thanked her politely ;-) “Well,” I replied, “do you really like the scent?” “Oh yes, Dad, the perfume smells amazing.” With such confirmation, the day could only get better. Dropped off my daughter and the second drive with my son to his school, and he was also impressed, saying: “Dad, the scent is really very pleasant and smells amazing. Good noses, those two little ones! About the fragrance: L'homme is a very successful all-rounder that can be worn well now in autumn/winter for almost any occasion. It is a scent that, due to its well-balanced composition, does not clash and pleases everyone I have encountered. The fruity start of bitter orange is clearly noticeable and gives the fragrance its signature, which is then accompanied by woody nuances and what I find to be a slight sweetness. The lavender is well integrated and never intrusive. Overall, a well-rounded package and a “cozy” flanker that YVSL launched in 2022. The sillage is good to very good at the beginning; however, the longevity for an Eau de Parfum is rather mediocre, and one wishes for a bit more performance. For me, it’s a scent that will be added to my collection this year.

What a great scent! Orange meets lavender and creates a very modern, woody-sweet blend. Right upon spraying, it becomes clear that the orange is the focal point of the fragrance. The opening consists almost entirely of a wonderfully pleasant orange. Towards the end of the opening, the lavender note joins in. These two notes together define the fragrance.

There are clear parallels to see/smell with L'Homme L'Intense . Firstly, the bottle and the color of the liquid, and secondly the scent itself. Regarding the bottle: Like all fragrances from the L’Homme or La nuit de L’Homme line, it follows the same style. The hexagonal cap and the chrome, reflective cap in the L’Homme line.

This fragrance was the first designer scent that started my collection. It felt special, which is a feeling that many collectors probably still remember from their first bottle. Accordingly, I associate a lot with this DNA, which I will always love for its fresh-woody uniqueness.

This is my first perfume from Loewe that I am testing. Since no comments have been posted yet, I took the time to look up some information online about the development of a perfume. For example, how much does "Un Paseo por Madrid - Tras la tormenta en el Jardín Botánico" cost? At least I haven't been able to find this scent anywhere, except here on Parfumo. It is one of those perfumes that I have smelled before and always find irresistible. It is comparable to some Montales and, in my opinion, to "Bois d' Oud" by Perris Monte Carlo. It starts off with a beautiful woody note, slightly smoky, I perceive vetiver in dark green. As my previous experience with oud scents goes, oud transforms with saffron into a medicinal oud note. This is also the case with the development of "Un Paseo por Madrid - Tras la tormenta en el Jardín Botánico." The animalic note is not noticeable here at all. However, I love the medicinal oud scent (in many cases, I also like the animalic variants). The purely woody-smoky scent lasts a long time, along with the typical saffron-oud blend with a hint of an aromatic yet very subtle patchouli. But after a while, I perceive a faint yet distinct rose scent. Violet root is also listed. I interpret this as giving "Un Paseo por Madrid - Tras la tormenta en el Jardín Botánico" a slight creaminess, but it also quickly dims the sillage to at most mediocre. I already fear that "Un Paseo por Madrid - Tras la tormenta en el Jardín Botánico" is not very long-lasting. Now I have been wearing the scent for 5 hours, and it is still moderately and close to the skin. Therefore, I assume that it has a decent longevity. In the meantime, there is a phase with a slight fine leather note. After that, the rose scent becomes a bit more pronounced and powdery, and patchouli stands out more. And there is not much more happening with "Un Paseo por Madrid - Tras la tormenta en el Jardín Botánico." It is a beautiful perfume for me. It is a subtle everyday alternative to all the other oud-saffron scents with a rose note. I particularly like that this scent is not as "loud" compared to many others of this type. That the rose note does not dominate everything but rather distinguishes itself in the blend with patchouli from the other scents in this direction. Of course, I classify "Un Paseo por Madrid - Tras la tormenta en el Jardín Botánico" as unisex.

When I opened the fragrance mail from Turandot with the Roja scent samples, I was quite astonished to find that, besides the "Arabs" I love so much, there was also a fragrance specifically for the European and American markets. No camel dung this time and no rummaging through the spice boxes from Alibaba's wonder cave! What would I discover? Would I like it? I find wonderful bouquets of flowers bound with fragrant gemstones here! I immediately associate "Karenina" with St. Petersburg; a love story always goes well, and Leo Tolstoy surely agreed with his novel "Anna Karenina." The Roja house also relies on this with its "Russian Collection." At the beginning, you feel the icy cold; the streets along the Neva covered with a thick layer of snow, where the splendid sleds produce a muffled sound: the wooden pavement under the snow cover comes to mind. But the little bells ring bright and confidently: they herald a festive evening! Roja's "Karenina" begins with Anna's entrance into the impressive palace, where one of the magnificent balls of the season is taking place. Aldehydes shine like the numerous candles in the sparkling crystal chandeliers, the freshness of bergamot pleasantly masks a certain mustiness that has settled over time in the grand staircase: a very pleasant start! The white and gold ballroom is adorned with magnificent floral arrangements; what opulence of color and scents can be found here. The exotic aromas of frangipani, jasmine, and ylang-ylang accompany the ever-touching spiciness of cloves; a staple in floral arrangements and here a beautiful centerpiece of the scent composition. At the same time, it is also innocently young and full of expectation. It is no coincidence that the clove symbolizes engagement in the classic language of flowers, as engaged couples were still innocent and full of hope back then! An island of red-blooming, uniquely fragrant geraniums draws attention: their vibrant red and green create an effective and lively contrast to the room's white and gold decor. The ladies in their precious gala gowns carry small bouquets that do not hinder them while dancing. In these delicately tied, ribbon-adorned bouquets, there are violets and softly colored grass roses, while orange blossoms often adorn the intricately styled hair. This girlish floral variety also contributes to the warm, feminine fragrance painting. In contrast, the noble gardenia is worn by the gentlemen as a boutonniere on their tailcoats. Under the increasing warmth of thousands of candles and dancing people, a wonderfully romantic swirl of floral scent emerges: this ballroom becomes a grand mixer of the previous aromas. Not only the candles but also feelings flicker throughout this evening. And so, a warm, spicy atmosphere develops, underscored by strong clove notes (cleverly chosen to complement the numerous cloves in the floral bouquet) and sensual waves of vanilla and musk; from now on, Eros and Aphrodite join in the dance! A hint of cedar and green freshness, arising from the Eaux de Colognes of the dancing gentlemen, leaves its surprising scent trail. "Tout St. Petersburg" dances into a new day, and Roja's floral bouquet "Karenina" reaches its impressive climax with a final swirl of all present fragrance notes! "Karenina's" scent composition initially sounds immense with its numerous impressive fragrance notes. Of course! The Roja brand leaves no room for anything less. And yet, it is a delicate, very feminine, almost slightly old-fashioned floral scent that surrounds its wearer radiantly yet surprisingly quietly. A bit of "old fragrance nobility" has clearly prevailed over the newcomers here. Sillage and longevity are, of course, "Roja-like"; anything else would be an insult: it is always done grandly and not half-heartedly! However, it can also be done without oud and all the "pleasant scents of Arabia," as "Karenina" shows. A noble lady sent me Turandot; well aware of the joy this fragrance brings me, knowing my preference for "Pomp and Circumstances." Even "fish-blooded" people like me can enjoy such elaborately composed fragrances that resonate and shine! "Karenina" will invite me to dance a few more times; a small remainder is still in the test vial. The metamorphosis from world literature to fragrance experience is very successful here. Conclusion: I am falling more and more for Roja fragrances! It doesn't matter!

What am I talking about? About clove, but the queen in all her hypostases. She is kind, very beautiful, very elegant, very feminine, a little melancholic and romantic) She is not alone, she has her court with her - the whole bouquet of flowers. They are not "too much," but tender and simply there. They adorn and emphasize her. I feel them all, but still in the background. The aldehydes in no way make the scent old-fashioned or stale, no - that's a whole different story. They are simply packaged and interpreted differently - they are not dominant and piercing, but powdery and even cozy. And this powdery note lasts a very long time, I can smell the fragrance all day. You just have to spend a little time with the scent and give it the chance to bloom on the skin. So again - a very harmonious and successful interpretation. Balanced, well thought out, understandable!!!

When reading this review, one might think it's nothing special. But where does the 8 come from then? It's definitely a justified 8; I would even give it more. Well, the opening is not that impressive, a bit dry, musty, one could also say old-school. But that doesn't last too long. I smell something rosy, along with frangipani. The violets perhaps provide the creaminess, while the ylang is more of an accent. Used so subtly, I really like it. Additionally, for the first couple of hours, there’s a subtle green note, quite natural, like freshly cut stems, but restrained. It also has a slightly clean aspect once the opening is over, probably due to the cedar. I don't find the carnation in this fragrance to be sharp or scratchy at all; on the contrary, it has this delicate fluffiness reminiscent of the filigree feathered carnations in the garden, very subtly spicy. I don't smell any clove at all. The fragrance is only slightly powdery. Very late on, a subtle vanilla joins in. The opening is rather lush, but over time, the scent becomes pleasantly light, yet still distinctly noticeable. It lasts around 12 hours now. Good things take time, because you have to endure the opening. And it’s a typical scent that needs skin to develop.

A slow starter maybe, but with everlasting stamina. Once the floral aldehydes get going, they will wrap you in a Dove soapy aura for the whole day. In the base a clear moss. Bright, rather dry. Vetiver is not pronounced in scent, but I do feel its vibrance boost. The overall scent remains airy, soapy, powdery. In colors white/beige, rather than green. For me personally, the perfume doesn't trigger any close associations or nostalgia. Obviously, it does feel like something of a while ago. Eighties, I guess. Compared to modern releases, it is quite a peculiar scent. Unique, that is for sure. Not at all offensive or sexy/seductive. Cool, but not cold. So that makes it very suitable for office settings.

This is in my top 20. This is also in my top 3. Rive Gauche is one of the best perfumes I have ever smelled. I have known, owned and worn it for more than 35 years and it keeps amazing me. The complexity of the scent and the many notes make it way more interesting than a lot of other scents, even though it is more than 50 years old. I will not write about the composition, the notes or the smell. I would like to share a few memories of how this fragrance has influenced my life. I was given this perfume by my father. I was 15 years old and he came home after being away for a time. I loved his presents and this time I was really happy since the smell of the perfume was so good. Back then I was used to perfume in glass bottles so the concept of a perfume in a metal can was quite interesting. I loved it. My next RG was a present to myself for passing an exam. I have always celebrated a passed exam with a “me”-present. This time it was my favourite perfume. I remember a friend asking why I bought an “old” perfume and not one of the new and flashy ones. I told her that there was nothing “old” about RG - just pure joy. Today I have a 2008 edition. I know that a lot of perfumistas can tell the difference from the original version. Luckily, I can not. To me it is still pure goodness in a bottle. I own an original Parfum, but this is way stronger and with other notes so the two can not be compared. If this is ever to be discontinued I shall buy every bottle I can lay my hands on. 156/365

I love this one but I really don't get it why that beautiful glass bottle became plastic.More powdery than the original pre-reformulated Rive Gauche. A little bit spicy and green.If you enjoy woody perfumes with a vintage nostalgia this one will fits you great.Remember, it is quite strong and not easy to wear!!

Surviving its brutal reformulations, "Rive Gauche" still shines brightly today. A spray could save me in the overpowering Italian August's overheat. First spray is a pure and metallic shower of freezing ice cubes. I put it on, and I feel cold. And "Rive Gauche" is cold, austere and beautiful in all of its evolution. The drydown is pure bliss: an elegant ethereal flowers bouquet emerges from the cold mist. I can sense a melancholic, powdery, iris throughout of it. Powerful scent. Nostalgic and uncanny at the same time.

⏲ 126-127 grams as new (100 ml flacon with cap attached and without box) - for your info. A true masterpiece, an unisex fragrance which surprisingly remained the same as I knew it from the 80's. It is literally for everyone under the condition of a good taste of clothes (simple but well chosen) it screams luxury and rich pokets. Mysterious, airy, luxurious, a little bit powdery and metallic, aldehidic and clean but everything inside it is about extremelly good tastes and a great education level. This fragrance choose you, not viceversa. Agnetha's (ABBA) favourite fragrance of all time. Love it, I have soaps, bubble bath pearls, oils, pure perfume and around 12-14 different flacons of EDT and EDP and still worried I could run out of them in the future haha. The EDT is above all, the best and the strongest in performances. I found out late that Rive Gauche and I are "the same age." My little "I-Se-Le" with his top hat and monocle! I had already loved him for years, although I think it's the perfume I've used too little for how much admiration I've had for him since I've known him. To me, this perfume smells like heaven. If anyone ever asked me what clouds smell like, I would run to my closet of treasures and bring back this fascinating, strange, unique bottle, which has remained the same for over 50 years. Categorized as a floral-aldehydic-powdery-green-earthy fragrance, or however else the experts classify it, Rive Gauche takes you back in time, carries you over green lands, then lifts you up to the clouds, giving you what you only encounter in dreams: the power to fly! Lately, I have been wearing this perfume more than I have worn it in years. I am rediscovering it, and it is rediscovering me in turn. Almost all the perfumes I have give me a feeling of well-being, even happiness, of fulfillment on all kinds of "levels." They cheer me up, make me feel important, special; in short, I get a lot of feelings from them, just as you surely do. Rive Gauche gives me something extra: a breath of hope, fresh air, inspiration. This perfume understands me, forgives me, always has the power to help me quickly find an antidote to something bad or a solution. Try it—if you don't know it—the "strange" Rive Gauche. This little tube hides a story inside it, always new, always surprising, always with a happy ending.Whether you'll like it or not, I don't know; but I can tell you for sure that you'll know what the blue sky "smells" like.

Have you ever seen two different twins? The one , Chanel n.5, is classic, classy, in its precious glass bottle , worn by ladies with strings of pearls. The other, hided in its metallic bottle, is more alternative ,it can be worn with a hippy blouse and a pair of vintage jeans...

Tested this from a sample (from a perfumery) yesterday after having sprayed Givenchy III in the morning and liked it, but wasn't sure if it was because I also could smell my Givenchy III (2007) So had to take a shower to give this a proper wear the rest of the afternoon and evening. I do like the aldehydic opening but I don't like the final drydown.

I got it as a gift and at first I really liked it but .... it became very heavy and looked like antique perfumes, which I really don't like .It is interesting that although it contains citrus, I unfortunately did not notice them in the least.Definitely not for me.

What lies behind a green floral Chypre, what can be so fascinatingly disturbing? The present composition is already malicious, elegant, and quite striking, no chance of confusion. But that would be all. It is the people and the constellations that can tell more about a floral vetiver.

A hint of black lace flashes beneath the shoulder-padded blazer. She wears a pantsuit, has tamed her bob with gel, and applied red lipstick. During the day, she holds the strings in her hands. Women can be anything. Chief physician, CEO of a corporation, artist. Men no longer stand above the matters and the women. It’s the early eighties.

My daughter brought me another new fragrance from Vegas. The bottle is, like almost all from Victoria's Secret, made of plastic. But it looks quite pretty. (The wrong cap is on my picture.) The scent is surprisingly fresh, less sweet than one would expect from Victoria's Secret. A bit fruity, floral, with a hint of the sea. Unfortunately, the fragrance fades very quickly. Since it is not as inexpensive as the regular Victoria's Secret scents, I am a bit disappointed.

The citrus note struggles a bit to break through the light woody, albeit somewhat DIY-like, opening and remains conventionally restrained thereafter. It offers a barely noticeable hint of cheesy bergamot, the so-called mandarin delivers synthetic wateriness, and the verbena, if you will, does not even begin to tap into its potential, rather being shyly delicate, even accepting that the freshness may come off slightly musty due to the relatively prominent wood note. In return, this freshness shows remarkable endurance. It seems as if the fragrance wants to avoid standing out at all costs - which it accomplishes quite brilliantly. While turtles sprint by on the left and right, the scent gradually drifts further towards wood with a subtle hint of spice, before closing in the evening on a frothy-mossy-creamy smooth base. Perhaps 'Esencia Sport' is conceptually better understood as being defined "downwards" rather than "upwards." The user does not get hit with a fresh punch in a blender-like manner, but this also eliminates the often rapid fall into synthetic wood elsewhere. Still, I find the fragrance rather bland. Not bad - just bland. This may be a desired appearance for a declared sport fragrance, but I wouldn't recommend it in good conscience even to older hobby golfers, as it is to be feared that even slight sweating could throw it off course. It would likely be better suited for a quieter environment. Perhaps at the land registry office or in the depot of a local museum. I thank MisterE for the sample.

... in the new bed comes true - my mother always used to say. Today it was time - the new box spring bed was delivered. It reminds me of the illustrations in the fairy tale book "The Princess and the Pea," where the sensitive one sits high up on a mountain of mattresses. I, as a garden gnome, will need a ladder to climb in. My husband always has his ladder with him. To guarantee us sweet dreams, I am looking for a pillow scent that appeals to both of us. Oh, Esencia Loewe Sport could be suitable. It is fresh with bergamot and mandarin - but soft with geranium. Musk and amber make Esencia Sport pleasantly cool and smooth. The scent is unisex for my nose and not too intense. I don’t find it sporty - rather balanced and calm. It embodies friendly serenity for me. As a bedtime treat, it is fitting - of course, it is also an uncomplicated companion during the day. I will remind my husband to remember his dreams when we climb the "mattress castle." My dreams are always memorable to me.

Do I look stylish? - Sure, if you like gray. Am I important? - I don't think so. Do I quickly fade into oblivion? - As a perfume, only after 6-7 hours, but as a scent, maybe already in 2-3 years. Am I the best Loewe Sport? - Nope, not that either. I found the Pour Homme more pleasant. Am I extraordinary? - Yes, due to the soapy-green bitterness, I can't think of much similar. What is my relationship with my father? - I haven't tested the regular Essencia on skin yet, but there is actually only a distant kinship left at the innermost core. Will I be available again? - No, you're not a hit but also not a flop. Am I still wet behind the ears? - You come across as rather mature, bitter, spicy, and soapy. Almost experienced in all waters. Am I worth my price? - You have quality, but you're not worth €80 in my opinion. Would you recommend or wear me? - As a test, yes, because you are not an ordinary sport scent. Sadly, nothing more. Am I wearable during sports? - Yes, but it's not your favorite hobby. Am I wearable in the office? - Definitely, a very modern interpretation of an office scent that bridges to the soapy 80s. Am I a stinker? - Oh no, 60-70% don't get a stinker from me. Which direction does my path lead? - Not into my collection, not into the history books. Will you also test the 2 missing sport scents from the Loewe line? - Yes, because the sport variants were among my favorites, especially when I think of the Loewe Solos.

Lakmé was created for The Royal Opera House Muscat in Oman in exclusive limited edition by Harrods. For this opulent creation, Rose and Iris, inspired by the famous 'Flower Duet', weave a delicate harmony. The bright and radiant character of the Lily of the Valley joins the performance. A fragrant opera! Lakmé opens with a brief sparkling citrus freshness and a shimmering nuance. It quickly moves on to the fruity floral center dominated by the stars of the composition: a beautiful earthy buttery iris intertwined with deliciously differentiated dewy fresh roses [What a Quality]! Leading this main duet are the main supporting actors: a white lily with a very striking peach, tender and velvety. Towards the apotheosis, it begins to acquire a light balsamic facet, incensed, woody at the base and powdery on drying: provided by a touch of incense and a hint of 'oud mixed with the creaminess of sandalwood, resins and noble woods, bringing more depth to the fragrance. Added to vanilla and benzoin, they make the ambery accord embraced by musk and ambergris that with the waxy iris make a slight musky/powdery suggestion. Delicate Complex Delicious Perfume; Rich and Smooth Sweet, Fruity and Warm; A fresh amber woody floriental for those who mainly appreciate roses and irises against the backdrop of amber, balsamic, incense, woody, musky facets. Very versatile fragrance for cold/heat, day/night; very good performance. Shareable perfume leaning in my view 60/40 for the feminine but men can wear it quietly. A beautiful work of art by Roja Dove. Exceptional Quality!

“The worlds of fragrance and opera were brought together for three nights in March 2019 when The Royal Opera House Muscat, Oman, asked Roja Dove to capture the essence of their new world premiere production of Lakmé.” This is maybe my most delicate, subtle and ethereal scent which I own. It’s fragile and innocent. It’s sensitive and elegant. So amazingly beautiful! Lakmé is a bouquet of fresh, soft and warm roses. It shines in all kind of weather but I love it most when it’s warm enough. Lakmé is the pure quiet luxury. It opens up with sparkling aldehydes and indulgent Rose de Mai and Taif Rose shines from the beginning until the end. The concoction remains quite simple yet enchanting and fresh. Woody and powdery base of Sandalwood and Orris with Musk creates a soft bed for the roses. Is it redundant if you have Turandot? Absolutely not! Turandot is more complex potent bouquet of many other flowers together with roses and Lakmé is more a rose scent. Turandot is Chypre and Lakmé is powdery, velvety floral scent. Despite those stories behind , Turandot is a scent for the queen and Lakmé is a scent for the princess. This may feel first very weak but it's not. The bubble which is around you is absolutely attractive and charming. Men - don't be scared to wear this one! Top Notes:  Aldehydes*, Citrus Notes Heart Notes:  Lily of the Valley, Rose de Mai*, Rose Taif, Magnolia, Peach Base Notes:  Pink Pepper, Cypriol, Casmir Wood, Sandalwood*, Aoud, Benzoin, Vanilla, Orris*, Frankincense*, Labdanum, Ambergris, Musk *being the main notes I will edit this review soon since this was first written on IG where the space is very limited. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

Roja Lakmé was a blind buy for me. Of course, such a purchase is always quite bold when it comes to a Roja fragrance and also costly. With Lakmé, even the unboxing is a lot of fun, because the bottle with its colorful metal plaque looks simply stunning and very high-quality. I have to give this bottle a full 10 points. Lakmé is a Roja fragrance that clearly distinguishes itself from the other Roja perfumes I have tested so far. Normally, Roja always has that typical Aoud DNA, Chypre, or floral orientation. This is only slightly the case with Lakmé. Lakmé is a very creamy, slightly powdery scent. Right after spraying, I can smell a fresh citrus and a note of aldehydes that Roja frequently uses. However, after 2-3 minutes, Lakmé breaks away from this familiar pattern and evolves further. Now it becomes creamy and powdery with a floral and fruity nuance. I smell iris, rose, vanilla (the vanilla creates that creamy sweet scent), lily of the valley, peach (which serves as a kind of contrast, like an antagonist in poetry), amber, sandalwood (which always gives me a sweet creamy note), benzoin, and for a twist into the unisex realm, a very gentle oud note that adds depth. Now to my association of what Lakmé reminds me of: My grandmother still uses the typical Nivea and Bebe cream in the tin can, and that scent has been forever etched in my memory. I primarily associate this scent with my grandmother. Of course, I also encountered this typical cream scent repeatedly during my school years, as some girls always had this cream with them and used it regularly during breaks or when my class returned to the classroom after gym class. The cream scent is simply something memorable for me and a reminder of when I was younger. However, my grandmother has particularly shaped this scent for me. The longevity is very good. I could perceive Lakmé for 10-11 hours, although the sillage is somewhat more subdued. Lakmé always stays just under an arm's length and becomes more intimate after 8 hours. I find Lakmé also very suitable for men, especially men who love fragrances like "Irisss | XerJoff" will find this one appealing.

Pierre Loti (actually Julien Viaud) was a French naval officer and writer. His novel Rarahu, later renamed Le Mariage de Loti (1880), established a literary exoticism and impressionism of the South Seas, particularly about Tahiti. The bestseller is still considered a classic of French exoticism and served as the basis for the libretti of the operas Lakmé by Léo Delibes and L’île du rêve by Reynaldo Hahn. The opera "Lakmé" transports the audience to an Indian town during the colonial period. The story takes place in the 19th century, when India was a British colony. Lakmé lives as a Hindu priestess in a temple, hidden behind trees and dense foliage. In this sacred grove, the British officer Gérald and Lakmé meet and fall in love by chance. However, the Hindu religion forbids such a love affair. Lakmé's father, Nilakantha, watches over this. Since Gérald has desecrated the sacred grove, Nilakantha seeks revenge. He injures Gérald with a knife. Lakmé finds him and nurses him back to health in a secret place. They want to stay together forever, but Gérald hesitates at the vow, as he does not want to part from his army permanently. Lakmé sees the impossibility of their relationship and takes her life with the poisonous Datura. From the very beginning, it was an unequal connection that had to end tragically. On March 28, 2019, the Royal Opera House Muscat in Oman presented Léo Delibes' opera "Lakmé" in its first original production. Roger Dove was commissioned as the perfumer for the production. His task: to create a perfume for the opera Lakmé, which would then be sprayed in the audience at certain points during the performance. However, he was not engaged by the opera director but by a member of the Sultan's family. Just one thing in advance: I will not participate in the discussions about whether Roger Dove is merely the Creative Director or/and actually the perfumer of the company. For two reasons: The first reason is obvious; only Roger Dove himself knows who has composed the masterpieces of ROJA Parfums. The second reason is rather mundane: what I cannot prove or disprove, I do not concern myself with. I am grateful that this fragrance exists, and that is what matters to me! The scent of Lakmé represents the lushness and fertility of nature, without any intrusiveness. I was infinitely happy that the aldehydes in the composition are almost imperceptible. The fragrance is as delicate and yet as shocking as the voices in the “Duo des fleurs / Sous le dôme épais” from the performance. For all those who reject ROJA Parfums in advance due to various prejudices, I recommend you spray Lakmé on, close your eyes, and listen to what the voices of the soprano and mezzo-soprano, together with the fragrance, are capable of stirring within you. That is all that counts. Life is not calculated and measured; it is lived with all the senses. Cheap, inexpensive, expensive, Underground vs Luxury… none of that matters in this moment anymore. The fragrance envelops the skin like a mist from the very first moment. I do not share the view that the perfume is close to the body. Nor is it loud. If there is a perfect sillage, then it is Lakmé. Every movement of yours is enriched with the siren voices of the fragrance. I see Catherine Deneuve seducing Susan Sarandon in “The Hunger.” Yes, I admit it, I am hopelessly infatuated with Lakmé. I rarely share brief assessments regarding fragrances. Here, too, I must correct myself, as the scent is by no means only floral-powdery. Lakmé is complexly powdery-woody from the start. Sandalwood plays a significant role in this wonderful creation. It is the flame that longs to be recognized. This note carries the certainty of the beautiful Lakmé that Gérald will not return her love, that he will not stay with her. It must not be forgotten that Roger Dove has a very special relationship with the lily of the valley: ROJA and the lily of the valley. In Lakmé, the perfumer combines the fairy-like bell-like voices of the lily of the valley with gently earthy yet delicately floral iris root. Everything becomes cooler, infused with elegance and softness, and enchanted with mystique. Wonderful! I see Lakmé as one of the most beautiful creations from the (now) traditional British house. This fragrance will never leave my collection. I have now finished listening to Lakmé and connected every second with the development of the fragrance. So many fragrances from ROJA Parfums reside high on the “The best of - Scala.” Why not Lakmé?

Jazz opens with a bright and fresh mix of nutmeg, cinnamon, cloves, and lavender, then dries down to sandalwood and cedar. Projects well for a couple of hours, and lasts a good 6 hours minimum. Due to availability in my area I got to nose Ralph Lauren Safari eons before Jazz. When I finally got to smell Jazz I was astounded by the similarities. Eventually I also tried the reformulated Pasha de Cartier EDT and that was even closer to Jazz, albeit weaker. I'm told Salvador by Salvador Dali is also in the same vein. Just goes to show how influential Jazz was in the early 90s. When Jazz was launched, the designer perfume industry was at crossroads. Unfortunately most designer houses chose the metallic freshie path of Cool Water and Eternity over this style, and the industry never recovered. Just my humble opinion. Masculinity Level: Di Caprio in Inception.

I'm a huge fan of YSL fragrances, until the last Y line. That line is a bit disappointing to me. But fortunately, I have many other YSL fragrances to enjoy, like this gem here. Jazz appeared in 1988, when Cool Water was launched and the world was preparing for a change. Fresh, clean and aquatic were the themes and things like animalic leathers of chypres were starting to disappear. Jazz shows a different path. Lavender, jasmine, oakmoss and nutmeg. A beautiful Fougère with Spicy-floral nuances. Super high quality and very masculine in a classic Fougère way, but with a freshness that puts it apart from the other fougère offerings out there. I don't know why YSL decided to discontinued it but probably it didn't well in sales. In 2011 they re-lauched it in a different bottle but the formula changed and it seemed somewhat flat and watered down. I think it's now discontinued again or only available in some places. Anyway, if you like fougère fragrances but want something slightly different and high quality, try to grab a bottle of this beauty. It's really fascinating how a fougère appears to be familiar but in the same time different and modern. One of my favourite fougères and a classic that would stood the test of time if L'Oréal didn't had decided to reformulate it. 4/5

Jazz is a great illustration of the point that the aromatic fougère of the 70s-80s had reached before Cool Water changed the rules. It has a warm spicy opening (cardamom, cinnamon) that plays against the artemesia that becomes noticeable at the end of the top notes. The artemesia holds strong and seamlessly ushers in the longer-lasting notes that define the heart and base, the coumarin, moss, cedar, tobacco. Jazz has a major/minor chord interaction that maintains my interest as it unfolds. It’s a bit too blended to be one of the strident fougères like Azzaro pour Homme that preceded it and Troisième Homme that followed it. Still it is an aromatic fougère of the old school and feels warm and enveloping rather than limpid, fresh and sweet/tart like Cool Water. Where would the aromatic fougère have gone without the ascendance of dyhydromyrcenol? Jazz, while lovely, seems like one of those genealogical lines identified by archeology that became extinct when the faster, more viable predator (Cool Water) was better able to cull its prey, the male herd of the late 80s/early 90s.

Jazz was the third offering in 1988 for men by YSL. It wasn't as massive as Kouros, but then, nothing will ever compare to it. Jazz was still very large and very potent. It was trend setting as well. I rushed out to my local mall and bought some EDT and several bath products that were offered. Like a jazz recording, the notes stuck out everywhere. I loved the heady florals, yet there was something about the sandalwood that dominated this masterpiece. Nights were my favorite time to wear it! Otherwise, it was a very traditional leathery Fougere. Most of the time I would re-spray some because the notes were livelier at first. Yes, it easily lasted 18+ hours. This was one of the last giants from the 80s. Its later reformulation that I picked up in 2007 seemed quieter. The closing lacked tobacco and contained minimal oakmoss. I was able to track down a vintage for comparison and indeed the changes are there. The original is from a time in my life that I would stay up drinking and dancing until 4AM. I guess the reformulation fits my life now that I am older. Today its gone forever. When I feel nostalgic, I give my vintage plastic bottle a spray and turn on some Miles Davis.

My favorite perfume in my collection. A fresh, woody Aromatic, spicy perfume which reminds me of good times in the very early 90s. The bottle design on piano keys is spectacular. I own 2 full bottles and the old empty one. Masterpiece, I recommend it for those who are confident, open-minded, enthusiastic and smiling. Enjoy it.

Drakkar Noir and Ungaro pour l'Homme I style green fougere, so we're talking Dihydromyrcenol and herbaceous/floral notes. All in all it gives a sensation of shower gel, resulting fresh and invigorating. You can smell the lavender, I can't smell the nutmeg but I can smell the coriander and a light leathery accord.

For the past few years, I’ve immersed myself in the captivating world of perfumery—a realm where the nose becomes a compass and scent, a language. It’s a thrilling, almost alchemical journey: exploring hundreds of raw materials in both their pure and diluted forms, discovering how they harmonize or collide in unexpected ways.

I can hardly put into words what a brilliant scent this is. But I will try… After a swap with the extremely likable Parfumo Profumorist, I was now the proud owner of Jazz in its "original form," with a black-and-white plastic bottle.

The world full of jazz music with its jazz cellars, where dancing and celebrating continue until dawn. This facet of Paris particularly stands for freedom and joie de vivre. So far the description on the product page of Yves Saint Laurent. Utopian? Jazz is truly a fragrance of the good old school.

A very rich and very complex fragrance consisting of a fruity opening of peach and a pineapple feel for a cocktail effect overlayed on top of dirty animalic oils, resins and dirty woods. The notes that help the transition of the fruityness to the animalic side are in my opinion rosemary, geranium and cistus ladanifer, which also make this fragrance a tad feminine. If you're a Roja consumer already I assume you will feel this as a bit safer and if you're looking to approach the brand for the first time it may surprise you but I wouldn't call this an overly offending fragrance.

Fruity-floral scent with a smooth base of musk, saffron, leather and woody notes. Just a touch of animalic civet. Drydown goes towards a more warm, vanilla, ambery and woody scent. Peach and florals are blended together really nicely, creating this round bouquet of slightly sweet, powdery nuances. Peach is just a bit more dominant than the florals, allowing the fragrance to continue sweet throughout the journey. From juicy and fruity peach towards warm, ambery, vanilla sweet. Civet simultaneously gives a subtle dirty, slightly animalic touch. Adding depth and texture to the overall scent. The base is very soft and gentle despite having oud, ambergris, different woody notes, civet and leather. It’s in a classic Roja fashion where smoothness, round and soft are key words for most of his work. Oud and woods are merely a smooth base on top of which the other notes play.

One thing in advance: I have never been to Kuwait. But I have been outside the tourist world in the 'Middle East'. The gap between rich and poor is often much wider there than what we have experienced in Germany so far. Those who have money in the Orient like to show it off, and they do so with a lot of bling-bling. There can never be enough glitter and shine in the form of gold, crystal, polished stone floors, and polished wood. The gardens bloom very lushly even in times of water scarcity in the country. In the air, the warmth of the day mingles with the scent of spices, fruits, precious woods, and flowers. ‘Kuwait’ by Roja is a fragrance that skillfully captures this overflowing opulence. When I read the fragrance pyramid for the first time, the thought crossed my mind: could this all be a bit too much? It is indeed too much by German standards: a lot of noble ingredients and a bit too much of everything. Just as the oriental dream is. In ‘Kuwait’, my nemeses are rhubarb, saffron, oak moss, birch, and leather. However, with the abundance of all the fragrance notes, they have no chance of bothering me. We are dealing here with a lush, powerful, oriental perfume that is sweet and slightly smoky at the same time, and which, when applied sparingly, is my dream even in the German summer and winter. For spring and autumn, it would be too much of a good thing for me. The sillage and longevity are also very high, corresponding to the price.

Actually, I consider myself a fairly composed, rather cool person. But I gladly admit: When I hear Roja Parfums, I feel like a truffle pig! I have to tug on the leash until I find the right tree or have a sample under my nose. Recently, it was indirectly suggested to me that I lack style. Just because I enjoy fragrances from the brand Xerjoff and even comment on them. So what would I be with my enthusiasm for everything that is called Roja Parfums? Nothing remains of the modest, shy young woman who was taught to blend in. As the saying goes: "A rascal thinks ill of it!" Anyone who wears Roja Parfums stands out! All the fragrances I have encountered so far are loud, pompous, sometimes ostentatious, mostly overloaded, and so on. Even the bottles are not elegant, finely cut pieces of jewelry from Lalique or Baccarat: They are "eyecatchers" with a bang, mostly in black and gold, representing a different world, a different culture, different values! The magic of 1,001 Nights is modernized here: The romantic nobleman on the richly adorned steed becomes the smart dark-eyed owner of a sleek motor yacht with a mooring in Monte Carlo. Already with Stéphane Humbert Lucas' luxurious scent "Harrods," I asked the question: "Do we need it?" The answer back then was "No"! And that also applies to the oriental beauties from Roja Parfums: No, we do not need them! But we are allowed to love them; we are allowed to indulge in their luxury and opulence! We are allowed to sink into their overflowing scent embraces and hope that our personal fairy tale from "1,001 Nights" is just beginning. "Kuwait" is one of the particularly rich fragrance creations, where peach and oud stand at the forefront for me: they dominate on my skin, and all other components blend into them. Citron - a very special type - and rosemary open fresh and spicy and truly not shy. Even this entrée corresponds excellently with the two powerful leaders. A lush flower garden, worthy of a magnificent seraglio, opens its gates and welcomes with open arms. Roses, jasmine, violets, and delicate orange blossoms - all these floral ladies, whose delicate to lush aromas spread softly on warm skin. Heliotrope in its dark violet already prepares for the erotic and simultaneously protective warmth of vanilla. And then it officially makes its entrance: the peach! Ripe and juicy, sitting plump in its velvety skin and smelling seductive! Cistus envelops all previous components with a resinous-honey-scented net, thus building a spicy bridge to the base. Here, not only the classic fragrance components gather, but also the finest spices and resins of the Orient. Generously, all the artistically crafted boxes and embroidered pouches from Aladdin's cave of thieves and wonders were reached into to create this fragrance magic. Honey-golden amber shines on the fruity-floral opulence, which has meanwhile developed into a spicy and smoky scent with distinctly animalistic nuances. The little, somewhat dirty predator has indeed awakened and is flirtatiously languid with a good dose of oud: neither can resist the other! "Kuwait" can thus touch all senses; it can delight, seduce, or of course also repel! Here, the initially mentioned motto applies: a little too much, a little too loud, a little too sultry = breathtakingly beautiful!! A sensual dance under a deep blue starry sky - infinitely far into eternity! The earth still breathes the heat of the day, generously exuding it and thereby intensifying all aromas! Rich scent trails lead from today into tomorrow and remind in the morning of the night! A magical night, perhaps followed by another 1,000! All of this is "Kuwait" by Roja Parfums: An intensely fragrant journey: whether it begins with a flying carpet or a luxury yacht!

I recently received Roja Kuwait as a sample because I planned to test the entire Roja Gulf collection and ultimately buy the best 1-2 fragrances as a bottle. Kuwait was supposed to be my first test, more precisely, my first review, as I am still taking notes on the other fragrances. I imagined Kuwait to be something fruity with oud, saffron, and a bit of rose. Unfortunately, I was a bit disappointed here, as the rose particularly stands out in the fragrance pyramid for me. Certainly, some may like that, but unfortunately, rose has never been my fragrance note, at least not as a main note. The rose unfortunately drowns out the beautiful fruity notes. The great oud scent is definitely present and shines through. I also dare to claim that Roja Dove has created a kind of modular principle here, as this fruity, slightly fresh, oud and sweet base is present in all the fragrances from the Gulf collection, oud, FM the Parfum, etc. I find the idea behind it good and also understandable to save work. Unfortunately, in Kuwait, this masterful base is far too much overshadowed by the rose. For me, the oud base clashes with the rose. Only after 5 hours does the rose recede, and the wonderful oud base comes to the fore. I consciously wanted to avoid going into the individual notes, as they are likely well-known to anyone who has smelled a Roja oud. My focus is more on the differences to the well-known base and the implementation of it. Unfortunately, I find Kuwait unsuccessful, or let's put it this way, the fragrance is unharmonious for me. Of course, the fragrance does not stink or anything, but Kuwait simply does not meet my expectations, especially not those of an absolute luxury product. Roja Dove should take another look and revise the fragrance. The longevity is very good; Kuwait lasted over 10 hours on me. The sillage is also strong, particularly for 5-6 hours, clearly beyond an arm's length, but not room-filling. After 8-9 hours, Kuwait becomes very close to the skin for me.

Loewe says its main notes are Bergamot, Vetivert and Absinthe. They also say this scent is for women, but Agua Drop has a unisex quality which shouldn't deter anyone from giving it a sniff... On me, the orange notes lack sweetness, which is why I would describe the aftermath as aggressively citrusy. Perhaps on someone else the citrus would be described as "rich" or "lush" because Agua Drop, like other Loewe perfumes I've tried, has an incredibly elegant take on nature and its notes. It feels expensive and clean. I can imagine this perfume on upscale restaurant owners, "gallerinas", and street tomato vendors. Wearing this on an incredibly foggy day in December feels incorrect. The correct day would be sometime in July, in between swimming in the Adriatic sea and lounging in the sun next to the love of my life, reading the most random non-fiction book to ever find its way onto my Kindle. The scent is strong and lasts longer than its sillage would imply.

For me, this is a very subtle, elegant, and fresh scent that can practically be worn for any occasion. Now, in terms of sillage, it is really very discreet, but I can perceive it on my skin for a long time. Over the course of about twelve hours, the scent has changed very subtly and steadily. It starts with a spray that makes me crave a jump into the sea or a cool lake with crystal-clear water, depending on the moment it could also be a pool, in which I consciously perceive and enjoy every moment. The color of the water ranges between a light sparkling green-blue, the swirling air bubbles glisten in the mystical sunlight that shines silvery-golden through a fine veil of mist onto the water's surface. As I slowly resurface, embraced by the refreshing water, I take a deep breath as my head reaches the water's surface, which has a slightly hesperidic quality that makes me feel reborn. It is this kind of morning or evening swim that gives you that special tingling dose of new energy. Afterwards, I wrap myself in my softly warm bathrobe lightly scented with orange blossoms and settle down on a leather-rattan lounge chair to fully absorb the elements of water and air once again. To smell, to feel, to see, to taste, and to hear a gentle splashing in the background. With this scent, you are doing something good for yourself, and it took me in thought to a refined wellness experience. During my next spa stay, I will probably wear this scent; I can see it clearly in my mind…

I cant describe my love to this lovely exotic(thanks to ylang ylang), tuberose, amber/musk/patchouli scent. Awesome longevity, beautiful smell, my favourite perfumor... What else I can want from a scent? Absolutely gorgeous. Mature but not annoying. You wanna smell more and more. Tuberose magic... Long lasting on clothes. This is gem scent.

Oh if I’d just smelt this before buying Armani Privé - Vert Malachite Comparing Armani Privé - Rouge Malachite , Armani Privé - Vert Malachite and "Le Vestiaire - Supreme Bouquet | Yves Saint Laurent" side by side, Supreme Bouquet does actually drown the other two out. The smell of the scent is very similar if not identical to Vert Malachite, just with a light fruitiness, but it does also have a spiciness to it similar to Rouge Malachite. All of these fragrances are absolutely divine, but Supreme Bouquet is better value for money than both Armani Prive scents. It’s extremely long lasting, it projects a lot more and you don’t need much to create a scent bubble. Both Armani Prive scents on the other hand are skin scents. Supreme Bouquet is also cheaper, since one bottle of this is like a combo of the other two. I still love Armani Privé - Rouge Malachite regardless, and would have bought that anyway, however I would have bought Supreme Bouquet over Armani Privé - Vert Malachite , if I’d just smelt this one first!

The perfume was launched in 2014 and was a part of the oriental group, then the shape of the bottle was changed and they added the perfume to “Le Vestiaire” prvate group in 2017. The perfume was created by Dominique Ropion, whose creations can be noticed in many of Frederic Malle's perfumes. As for the scent... What a beautiful, a woody floral fruity scent… Fruits are not mentioned in the perfume notes, but I smell peaches, strawberry and a creamy note it may come from coconut. And as for the flowery note, Supreme Bouquet has ylang ylang and tuberose. While the base is ambery, musky, creamy, mixed with fruity notes along with touches of pink pepper. Patchouli and animal notes are mentioned, but for my nose are not obvious. Although it tends towards the feminine side a little bit, I consider it suitable for both.

When we tested this fragrance, my friend and I were reminded of an old classic by Karl Lagerfeld, good old "Chloé" from the 1970's. Something about the lush flowery bouquet with its accent on tuberose points into this direction. For the first 30 min, we thought this would be a winner, a modern retro-scent with strong sillage and a powerful message. But gradually, loads of artificial patchouli, ambroxan and other aromachemicals take the lead and the drydown is done in the style of all the latest YSL-offerings (think "Black Opium" or "Manifesto"). The only difference is the concentration. I can still smell the scent on my scarf after two weeks. At the price of approx. 170 Euros, I would have thought that originality would be more important than sheer volume. But I was wrong again.

"I noted 'A fragrance to kneel for!' when I received a small sample of 'Supreme Bouquet' last year - and that’s exactly what I thought again yesterday when I stumbled upon this perfume in a perfumery: Creamy and floral, but above all SWEET in a way that forbids any contradiction! Either the surprised tester opens their (olfactory) beak wide to inhale the olfactory mother's milk in large gulps - or they turn their head away in disgust because it’s just too much mother all at once... 'Supreme Bouquet' is overwhelmingly intense and immediately takes me into its oversized arms. A blissful grin spreads across my face. For me, the sweet floral notes dominate this fragrance, but that alone wouldn’t be anything truly extraordinary: Tuberose, Ylang Ylang, and Jasmine can be found in many floral perfumes, where they unleash their superpowers alone or in combination. But in 'Supreme Bouquet', a fragrance note joins this all-star floral diva lineup that I didn’t know until now and that fascinates me: It must be the amberwood. Yesterday, in my ignorance, I would have sworn on stone and bone that it was Oud, as I felt reminded of its slightly medicinal note. I am not an Oud fan, so I am really glad that it is (apparently) not included in this perfume. Amberwood, however, is a new player on my scent stage and deserves closer examination. Thanks to Wikipedia, I now know that amberwood comes from the amber tree, which is mainly found on the North American continent; its wood has a spicy scent and is very popular among artistic carpenters, while its liquid resin was once used to make chewing gum. Hmm. Could it be that this last component contributes to the (early) childhood appeal of 'Supreme Bouquet'? This 'Oh, no matter how old I am, I want to go to mama' effect? It would be really interesting to sniff amberwood pure to understand how it works in combination with others. In 'Supreme Bouquet', it seems to contribute to making the scent experience very personal, yes, very animalistic; it’s no coincidence that corresponding notes are listed in the fragrance pyramid. Sweet therefore does NOT mean sugary in this perfume, but rather as naturally delicious as some babies smell on their heads. (I vividly remember the distinct chocolate scent I once perceived on a child's head - in that respect, I can very well understand the previous comment from a perfume lover!) Back to 'Supreme Bouquet': The perfume has a massive sillage and great longevity, surviving even a thorough shower. During the development of the fragrance, all creamy aspects quickly recede and give way to the spicy-sweet. It almost becomes a bit too much for me; as I said, I suspected that the all-powerful and omnipresent Oud had kidnapped my sniffing spot on my wrist. But ultimately, it’s only ALMOST too much, and the scent remains pleasant. It would be worth trying to apply 'Supreme Bouquet' to a piece of clothing to find out if this incomparable 'beak open!' effect lasts longer there. Fortunately, I still have the sample from last year, as I must say, despite all the fascination, that a price of nearly €200 is just too much for this sweet orgy. 'Supreme Bouquet' leaves me somewhat divided: The first second is pure ecstasy, the first minute bliss, the first hour the greatest joy - and what comes next I find pleasant, but I wouldn’t buy it. Therefore, unfortunately, no full score for 'Supreme Bouquet'. However, for those who enjoy being breathless from a fragrance, I recommend indulging in the pleasure of taking a deep sniff from the spray head: That’s all it takes to lie blissfully babbling in the cradle again!

Foreword :) Before I get stoned here, imaginatively, for my opinion about this fragrance, I want to mention upfront that I really like sweets. Sweet scents and yes, also other edible sweet treats. Since I am currently distancing myself a bit from the latter, it is quite possible that I will help myself with one or another new fragrance.

Noble wonderful white floral scent that immediately catapults me to heaven. Thankfully, I don't smell any animalic notes, but mainly white flowers and a hint of wood.. The fragrance is somewhat similar to Rouge Malachite but without the spiciness.. Supreme Bouquet is somehow denser, fuller, and much more elegant..

I seem to like tuberose in fragrances. It started with Hypnotic Poison Eau de Toilette and ends with my latest acquisition "For Her Musc Noir Rose | Narciso Rodriguez." But it is rare for tuberose to play such a prominent role in one of my favorite scents. I actually stumbled upon Supreme Bouquet by chance.

Hmm... it smells heavenly here. Gold starts fresh, fruity. The bergamot gives the opening a citrusy touch, but it also reveals a tiny hint of urine for me, which sounds worse than it is. However, I can immediately smell the pear. This note carries through to the end.

Delightfully, not in the sense of girlish. I find "Le Vestiaire - Supreme Bouquet | Yves Saint Laurent" absolutely feminine, elegant, and well-groomed. Not old-fashioned, a hint of exoticism lies in the sillage (Ylang Ylang, without sunscreen vibes). The blend makes it, no overwhelming tuberose. By now, I can also appreciate patchouli in homeopathic doses.

This. Is. An. Amazing. Fragrance. Much underestimated in my humble opinion, possibly due to it being not so known. How to describe it... a fall into a cornucopia of fruit and toffee? Warm, fruity, just a tad "sticky" but in a very pleasant way. Vanilla not too prominent, but present as the perfect link to connect fruit and white flowers. Not crisp at all, but clean and creamy. I found the word: moreish! Seductive? Absolutely! Intriguing? Hell, yeah. Floral fruit and gourmand lovers, this is "summer truffle sandae meet jungle queen - the panther! - for a night of passion" ...

I received "Quizás Seducción" as a gift from my dearest friend. The words translate to "Maybe Seduction." The "Spaniards" here will surely know what it means; it seems to me to be an idiom that leaves open whether and when one will be seduced. And that is exactly how "Quizás Seducción" is for me. I have worn it several times now, and I always find it initially beautiful, herb-fruity, citrusy. And then an unpleasant note reveals itself to me, which I have come to frequently perceive when patchouli and fruits are mentioned in fragrances. Although I do not smell patchouli distinctly on its own, in "Quizás Seducción," this combination initially gives me a synthetic Maoam note with glue. In many fragrances, a note of this kind lingers until the end, dominating throughout. However, after wearing "Quizás Seducción" for a while, it initially recedes in the sillage, which is quite strong at first. And I do not think further about "Quizás Seducción." At some point, usually after an hour, I notice again that I am wearing a perfume, and I like it. It smells like a sharp mixture, where I can at most recognize the orange, but not the flowers. I cannot identify jasmine and tuberose. It remains predominantly a herbaceous fruit scent with woody undertones. By now, I also know why I like "Quizás Seducción" more and more after a while. It is galbanum, albeit probably synthetic, that is partly responsible for the fruity scents. I like galbanum. If anything, I would claim that osmanthus has been added with a certain softening dried fruit note. The chewy candy note is no longer there. Just because I do not recognize or perceive any flowers does not mean that no floral scent materials have been used. They simply get lost in the overall composition of the fruit scent for me, softening it. In principle, I do not like fruity scents. But either I have gotten used to these new fragrances, or "maybe" the creation in "Quizás Seducción" is particularly successful. Whatever fruits are mentioned above, I now know all too well that it is all more or less skillfully mixed chemistry. However, that does not bother me. In "Quizás Seducción," it has been quite well done. Caramel and vanilla are also mentioned. I cannot smell those either. If anything, I smell an indefinable slightly bitter-woody note as it develops further. This could refer to the caramel-vanillin note. I also think I perceive a slightly cinnamon note. But where is the patchouli? It appears many hours later in the fade and gives "Quizás Seducción" a new distinct twist. That is what I perceive in myself. However, when I wear "Quizás Seducción," I am always complimented on the "beautiful" scent, which I am not used to. And when I return to the room where I am testing it, like this evening, it smells like a "really" beautiful fragrance. Usually, fragrances are not perceived on me, except by myself. But "Quizás Seducción" is evidently perceived in my immediate vicinity, so that people tell me this with genuine admiration. Consequently, the sillage is not "from bad parents."
