I consider "Quizás Seducción" to be a pleasant everyday fragrance that should be applied sparingly. Surprisingly for me, I like to wear it from time to time. No, "Quizás Seducción" will not make it to my signature scent pedestal. But one does not wear clothes for very festive occasions in everyday life. So, I do not wear my absolute favorite fragrances every day. Instead, I have alternating fragrances like "Quizás Seducción," which I choose based on mood and occasion. Lastly, the question of whether it could be a unisex fragrance. I perceive "Quizás Seducción" as a herbaceous, dark scent. Men could wear it. However, "Quizás Seducción" has something inherently feminine about it, or at least that is how I feel.

Yesterday I picked up my reserved Cuir Fauve from my regular perfumery. Of course, during a visit there, I let my eyes wander to see what else is on the shelves. And what do my short-sighted eyes discover? Various bottles from the brand Loewe! Years ago, I had bought a bottle from this label blindly online - and I was very taken with it. But I had bought it as a gift, and although I liked it, I stuck to my resolution and passed it on. Unfortunately, I searched for Loewe in stores in vain afterwards. So yesterday was a great reunion joy! The saleswoman gave me a little bag of Seduccion, which I awkwardly opened at home. Part of it landed on my hand, and some flowed down the bag. But both on my skin and throughout the room, a warm, full aroma spread. Now that's a sillage! And I can only confirm the longevity described above. The opening is fruity but soft, and then jasmine and tuberose compete with each other - very lush but unobtrusive. The delicious factor comes from caramel and vanilla, deepened by patchouli. Here, elegance and gourmand notes go hand in hand. Seduccion has no heaviness despite its assertiveness, but surrounds me lightly and airy. Moreover, it embodies the warm sunshine of Spain, even though it is not a direct summer scent. No, it also fits well on a winter evening when one has dressed up in "fine attire". I am happy that the impressive Loewe has crossed my path again.

This was the title of a hit song in the tango style from the 1930s. It was sung by a certain Eva Busch. Unfortunately, I couldn't track down the lyrics, and when listening to it on Amazon, I found it hard to understand the words clearly. What does this 30s revue number have in common with the new fragrance from the brand Loewe? The theme of Spain and kissing, but nothing more. Quizás Seducción is, for a change, a tuberose perfume that, despite its pronounced sillage and long-lasting nature, doesn't get on my nerves. However, my fondness for it doesn't extend to the point where I would actually buy the fragrance. One doesn't have to wear everything they like. As already mentioned, the tuberose, along with orange blossom, is the defining scent from start to finish. From the fruity accord at the opening, I can only sense a subtle background noise, and more fruit wouldn't have done the fragrance any good. The tuberose-orange blossom duo even manages to silence the jasmine almost completely. Only after a very enduring heart note does a hint of vanilla sweetness emerge, and the orange blossom begins to weaken a bit. Quizás Seducción is a perfume that I can hardly imagine on a man, as it is simply a touch too sensual for that.

Kingdom Of Bahrain by the British House Roja London of Niche Haute Luxury Perfumery is a oriental woody citrus aromatic balsamic unisex perfume. It is part of the 'Gulf Collection', and was released in 2017, it is currently discontinued; the nose behind this fragrance is Roja Dove. ‎ Kingdom Of Bahrain has a bubbly and acidic citrus opening mainly due to the FANTASTIC lemon and lime. The heart of spicy rose, jasmine and violet propels the scent into a clear, clean space that hovers over the voluminous, dense base with its peaceful 'oud and gray leather gaining a fleshy dimension thanks to subtle brushstrokes of birch tar, pine, rubbery saffron, pepper and an earthy patchouli. Perfume is saved from weight by two things: First, a surprising cotton candy note adds a hint of sweetness and delicacy to the leather and smoky wood accords, elevating the scent firmly into versatile, unisex territory. Second, fresh citrus top notes join a radiant ambergris at the base to effectively brighten the scent, brightening your darkest corners and breathing air in your crevices. Masterful, charming, elegant and full of spicy heat, yet fresh and smooth Kingdom Of Bahrain is truly a perfume fit for a king. A masterpiece by Roja Dove!

Roja Bahrain is the strange one from the Gulf Collection. But strange in a very good way. This scent takes you through a journey of ingredients. It starts fresh (because of the lime) but grows more and more in a mature scent. Sweetness and freshness together in a very smooth and interesting juice. Lovely done! The dry down is to die for. Almost a fresh baked cookie joined by a little oud and ambergriss in the background.

An invigorating interplay of citrus and freshness from Lemon, Lime, Clary Sage, and bergamot becomes even more uplifting with an introduction Pink Pepper and spicy Saffron, made untamed by a bouquet of Violet Rose, and Jasmine, caressed with the unusual note of candied floss (cotton candy). After an hour the dry down comes front and center with an overture of woods including Cedar, Cypress, Casmir, Pine, Birch, and Aoud Woods, with an underlying base of Vanilla, Ambergris, Leather and Tonka Bean.

In olfactory terms, when I think of "London," I think of the eponymous Eau de Parfum by Tom Ford. It leans heavily towards the spicy-woody direction with a good amount of cumin and a rather dry to barn-like standing. This evokes associations with the cultural melting pot of the British capital, with a nod to its historical past - at least that's how I would interpret the scent. Now, the Texan Tom Ford is known to be neither a Londoner nor an Englishman - which makes the comparison to the same theme from the perspective of the Brit Roja Dove all the more interesting, who at least operated his "Haute Parfumerie" in the upscale London department store Harrods ... and interestingly sold Tom Ford fragrances there as well. I would have expected Dove's "London" to be a much sparklier, if not even somewhat more luxurious scent - not necessarily specific ingredients, but something that I associate with extravagance and/or clubbing. Whether coincidence or not: this London reminds me very intensely of Tom Ford's namesake in its direction. At least both creations share labdanum, cardamom, coriander seeds, saffron, cedar, frankincense, as well as may rose or geranium (which gets totally overshadowed). Okay - some of these can be found in what feels like every third fragrance, but the first four are quite present and together in this combination are rather less frequently encountered. While cumin is missing here, which is quite dominant in Tom Ford's version, this dry spiciness definitely takes center stage, paired with some resinous or balsamic notes. The rest of the pyramid is hardly perceptible, except for a bit of lavender. Only late in the drydown do hints of vanilla and benzoin emerge. I can hardly imagine that Roja Dove was not aware of the four-year-older "London" by Tom Ford or even analyzed it intensively. I wouldn’t call it a scent twin, but at least an "inspiration source." In comparison, I find Tom Ford's "London" to be a bit rounder, more appealing, and pleasant. Both are, of course, at the upper level in terms of longevity and sillage, while Roja Dove pushes the price spiral even further in typical fashion. Of all the perfumes I have encountered from the house of Dove, this one seems rather meager to me - but at a truly high level.

Oh man, "roasted" is a gross understatement of the smokiness of this fragrance. This is like, the vanilla for people who think By the Fireplace is not smoky enough. But I'm getting carried away with myself. Let me start with the opening. The notes don't remotely do the opening justice. There's a spiciness and greenness to this opening that is wonderful and natural. Kind of reminds me of Ballena de la Pampa Perfume , and there are a couple of other Fueguias that gave me the same vibe. Then the smokiness begins. The fragrance I thought of in this stage is Cruz del Sur I . My problem with that fragrance was the opening, which I thought smelled just like olive brine. But here, there is that beautiful spicy green opening that masks it and lets you simply enjoy the smokiness. During this whole time, the namesake vanilla note is very much in the background and provides a slight sweetness. This is not just vanilla lightly toasted in a pan, this is like hickory-smoked charbroiled vanilla. It is SMOKY. Slowly but surely, the vanilla gains ground over the smoky woody notes, and only about an hour in does Roasted Vanilla actually become a vanilla fragrance. Though the sillage is not great throughout, it seems to somehow get stronger over time, with the vanillic sweetness and boozy depth warmly wrapping around the wearer. This is one of the best vanilla fragrances I've ever tried, and well worth the high pricetag. Sorry to the fans of these two, but Sultan and Babycat don't hold a candle up to Roasted Vanilla.

I have always been astonished at how living beings that cannot see orient themselves - especially humans, who neither have a particularly keen sense of smell nor whiskers or anything like that. What I’m getting at is that should I ever, God forbid, go blind, I would always smell when I am standing on soil where oaks grow. Of all the earthy scents I love, I like the smell of the earth into which oaks stretch their roots the most. This - brown-salty. This - Yes. One must have smelled it…! "A novel change of homeland" it means to me. "Modern times come over the places of my childhood." Why?! Quite simply. When I had nearly finished my teenage years, thousands of young oaks poured over our city. And only another ten or twenty years later did the earth of our parks and green spaces suddenly start to smell this way. Whenever I smell it, it never smells of the past, of memory, of old times - it always smells of renewal, of growing up, of modernity. Beuys, that old rascal, made it so that acorns now always fall on heads and car roofs, for years now, for decades, which have now actually been so cheeky as to quickly spread across the country - - avenues become dark-cozy, and trunks become powerfully thick, and yet: The smell always smells "new" to me. Who can blame me for loving it…! This scent is almost unrecognizable in Roasted Vanilla. Almost. It embraces its buddy, the red pepper, which I have greatly appreciated since MY PEARLS, so tightly… In between somehow lies vanilla. As a supporting actor, as - an ingredient? - I was almost disappointed because it is just a sidekick, as I am currently in the midst of an extensive vanilla phase. Slowly, I am beginning to recognize that the trio together creates something entirely new - bitter, cheeky, natural, even somewhat serious - something new that takes the boozy touch as a surfboard, but smells itself. This stuff is truly t e s t e n s w e r t. Update to follow. 1. Update. After a while, it becomes punchy and pleasantly bitter. Not in the way that you would chew on an acorn, but rather bitter like black coffee, or Loomi-bitter. Still: The interplay of naturalness and perfuminess, of booze, intense rosé pepper, oak, and a hint of vanilla, of bitter and sweet is showcased - - however, in the end, I ask myself (!) : What for?! - I miss the kick, the dedication, the enthusiasm, the shock fascination in my emotional palette regarding this pure autumn scent, which somehow slithers between target groups and occasions without even brushing against any of them. Conclusion: After initial enthusiasm for the unusual comes the hope that the punch will bring a surprise, and then the disillusionment - one turns away, bored, almost. - XD - Yes, yes: Also a way to head-note-blend ;D !!

Roja Dove Bergamot does a good job for an essence which is commonly used without being a common fragrance. It smells rich, the citrus part last a good 1-2 hours. It starts with a floral touch that becomes more intense as the time goes by. The opening is more bitter, fizzy, with a lemon aura, and then the refreshing and more sweet side of citrus accord gets in evidence. Later, the scent shows its chypre side, but more in a modern way, very intense in the jasmine and with a musky and patchouli edge. It's unissex, but maybe more in the feminine side than masculine one. If you want a rich and expensive citrus chypre fragrance, this one is a great option.

Imagine a sun-drenched Mediterranean coast at golden hour — that’s the first spritz of Roja Bergamot Extrait. Bright, zesty bergamot bursts like champagne bubbles, followed by a silky embrace of neroli, herbs, and refined musks. This isn’t your average citrus; it’s citrus in a tuxedo — crisp, clean, and impossibly elegant. • Genre: Citrus Aromatic / Luxury Fresh • Best Time to Wear: Spring & summer days, upscale daytime events • Performance: Moderate projection, long-lasting for a citrus (6–8 hours) • Rating: 8.7/10 • Vibe: Sunlight in a decanter — refined, radiant, refreshing

Of this perfume I have the old frosted bottle. A friend let me smell it and I was sold but I was new to the perfume business. After sometime I couldn’t let it go and searched till I found a full bottle. I must say this is gold in a bottle. I think because of the age of my bottle it’s smoother and creamy but it’s by far one of the most pleasant perfumes in my collection! 10 out of 10z

Some perfumes simply command respect, and despite their great allure & temptation, one hesitates to test them. Even with experience & knowledge, you are not sure if you can do justice to the scent, the expectations, the bottle & especially the price. But in the end, isn’t it just a perfume? Doesn’t Roja also just cook with water like everyone else, albeit very expensive water? Today, on a stifling hot day on Düsseldorf's Kö, I faced this highly praised summer Roja, hoping to find some answers to my questions. Bergamot, unlike many other Roja perfumes, as far as I know, is only available in the Extrait version tested here - very chic, not confusing at all, finally a clear statement. The scent starts with a top note that lives up to its name. Pure, cooling, zesty, slightly scratchy bergamot. Luxury bergamot. There’s also a green undertone from the very beginning, something like grass or the stems of flowers. Plus neroli & vetiver. You can tell that the scent forms a triumvirate with overlaps with the extraits of vetiver & neroli. If I had to make a prediction, I would bet on vetiver as the one that suits me best. But let’s wait and see when I dare to approach the two brothers of bergamot. After an hour, you are surprised to find that the core of the scent is almost a genuine chypre, with woody musk, a lot of green oakmoss & a bitter feeling. Soft is different; an annoying signature scratchiness remains almost consistently present, but this is probably due to the pure & high-quality, highly concentrated fragrance materials that are not so prickly & vibrating. Still, I would have wished for a bit more finesse, gentleness & elegance here. Nevertheless, it remains a royal chypre, for an equally royal price! However, it doesn’t come close to my favorite bergamot scents like Le Labo's Bergamote 22! Bottle: royal, shiny, almost outrageously rich. Sillage: best for summer & spring, but it remains an extrait & should not be underestimated! Longevity: you can tell here too - a good 7-8 hours! Conclusion: a bit scratchy & green, less/shorter pure bergamot than expected, of course too expensive for what is offered, as anticipated. Still, overall a luxurious & modern spin on a summery chypre!

"Bergamot" is a green herbaceous scented perfume, (thanks to Aggeliki for the sample of the extrait). It is followed by a slight soapiness and becomes spicier, but never very intrusive. The flowers and musk are noticeable. However, they hint at giving the herbaceous quality of bergamot and the harsh green a touch of creaminess. The sharp ginger is not uninteresting. Vetiver also comes across as fresh and green, it seems to me. Is there still patchouli? From here, I pass. "Bergamot" is too diverse and complex with its scent components. What is positive for me is that the oakmoss holds back very modestly. Thus, this perfume, which is perceived as somewhat poly-aesthetic, remains a very noble and not too harsh chypre. Oakmoss does not dominate all the fragrance notes as it develops. After a while, a wonderfully bitter, slightly creamy accent appears. A very fine extrait and also quite masculine. "Bergamot" is not really innovative on one hand. However, on the other hand, it is a high-quality, quietly and gently designed, and thus modern chypre. If only the price weren't so high.

Meanwhile - perhaps one must at least be allowed to ask why a rather classically cut fragrance of the citrus theme must command a price 5-6 times that of what, for example, Dior's "Eau Sauvage" costs the end consumer. Well, Roja can do that, Roja must do that for reasons of self-imposed image.

Hello everyone, how are you doing? Today I'm writing another fragrance report for you and I decided to reach for a fresh-scented fragrance from my samples, now that it's still warm and such scents are better described in summer than in winter. But ultimately, that's probably just an excuse so I can keep rambling and writing here :) Today it's about Bergamot by Roja.

I'd ordered a new 50ml bottle of the original Libre EDP on a famous UK beauty webshop and discovered a few seconds too late - I'd peeled off the foil, making it unreturnable - they'd made a mistake in sending me the EDT. Normally an expensive mistake because EDT's famously get eaten ASAP by my skin. (The longest lasting EDT to date - and I'm 45 so not just starting a perfume journey - gave me 4hrs [Burberry Brit], the rest barely makes 1, or even 2). I decided to test the initially unwanted liquid and... amazed. Never in my life have I been able to smell an Eau de Toilette past the 3-4hr mark, but one spray on the top of my lower arm in warm weather lasted 8 hours. A definite skin scent the final 3 of the eight hours, but remarkable nonetheless for an EDT on my very dry, perfume eating skin. That in itself made me reconsider my thought to sell it and test the actual fragrance for scent a bit more, because initially that wàs disappointing. (Check original first week review further below. Directly underneath is a review of the next season macerated perfume). Edit: JULY 2023: WHAT A DIFFERENCE A YEAR MAKES. Switching out my true winter fragrances for my Spring & Summer collections has given me quite a few nice surprises, but none so much as Libre Eau de Toilette. You can read the original review starting with "September 2022" too, but I think I'm now holding the "Real Libre EDT. That first review was written after a few tries shortly after its arrival. Not only did I deal with the disappointment of receiving the wrong fragrance and not being able to return it anymore, but after I had posted this review my experience with it became worse. After a week or 3 it had apparently recovered from its trip overseas and gave me "the tea". In this case both the figurative and the literal: suddenly all I got was a strong bergamotty opening, followed by a mere whiff of Orange blossom and then a major blast of tea that remained most of the perfume duration time. Tea, particularly the Jasmine tea I used to drink at the Chinese restaurant I worked at shortly before going to uni, is yummy. But I prefer not to smell like it. I did keep it though, not entirely sure what to do anymore. When switching my fragrances I sprayed a few - leading to keeping several I initially wanted to sell because they'd blossomed from initial 'meh's to very nice perfumes. The Libre was, as said earlier, the biggest surprise. This wasn't the fragrance of the first 2 weeks, and definitely not the Jasmine tea strong juice afterwards. No, what I got was a liquid much darker than its EDP sister and thàt came through in the smell. The Vanilla must have macerated big time in the period October to June because... wow. Libre EDT doesn't have a typical EDT vibe anymore. The cologne dna that the EDP has is nowhere to be found. If anything, I would say EDT's running towards the Intense. Just in a much smoother, more elegant way. The tea is still there, but that note is no longer the main accord, but simply part of a gorgeously blended whole. The lavender is only noticeable if you have a very good nose and still then it is pretty vague and just there at the start. Bergamot has stopped screaming and it's now just a part of a freshly sweet opening that lasts but 2, or less, minutes before going into the Jasmine- tea- orange blossom heart - a heart that flows straight into the base and remains part of the dry down. The middle pyramid Jasmine is sultry, seductive and somehow innocent at the same time. The white flower gives a luscious scent, but isn't indolic or overpowering in the least. The Orangeblossom gives EDT a tad freshness and goes perfectly hand in hand with the Jasmine. Together with the tea they aren't just part of the heart, but giving Heart to this fragrance. All that time the Vanilla is already part of the entire concoction, both sweetening and smoothing the entire heady perfume. The ambergris and Musk aren't noticeable as separate notes but blended to perfection and give, together with vanilla, a similar backbone to the one Intense has. I can't believe I'm saying this, but the EDT - with now much better projection too - has pushed EDP and Intense off their pedestals and taken first place. This fragrance is everything I want from its pyramid and even the tea has earned that spot by giving EDT a freshness and difference that's not just needed in warm weather, but seperates this fragrance from the others in the line. My Libre love has renewed. What's more: I have a new entry in my Top 5 SS perfumes. Yes it has something typical fresh AND something different, but overall Libre EDT gives sultry, smooth & sweet... thàt is the Tea! [SEPTEMBER 2022... What about the scent? >> Initial first week review: Well it is both a bit of a disappointment AND a nice surprise. Disappointing because on my skin it has nothing of the original classy sexiness and boldness Libre had/has. When I'm wearing Libre I feel like anyone could be my b*tch and love it. Had I still been working as an editor-in-chief of a magazine in a man's world (l interviewed politicians, other leaders & influentials in the transport, -and environmental sector and was the only female manager in the entire publishing house) this would've been my signature office scent. The EDT...not so much. It's not giving me any of the lavender and even the opening is strangely missing any of the citrus notes. In other words: I'm sorely missing versatility. What DO I get? My two favourite flowers in perfume: Orangeblossom and jasmine. I get a whiff of tea, but more like you're sniffing a handful of jasmine and orangeblossoms close to your nose and someone happens to put a pot of jasmine tea on a table in the same room. That whiff disappears after an hour and then the rest of the heart remains almost too overpowering for the base. For a white floral enthusiast Libre Eau de Toilette is still nice to have, even when it misses complexity. I deem it a particularly good scent for spring and summer. It does have a lightness, despite some sweetness. If you're not into all those fresh laundry/ citrusy/ aldehyde-salt fragrances, this one could be perfect for you ~ in a wide variety of ages. When the weather gets colder its performance decreases a lot, but it does well in 20°C and up. Libre EDT is a well performing Eau de Toilette but still performs the least out of all the Libre perfumes. But that should not come as a surprise, the rest being all EDP's. To put it all together: On me this Libre is white floral sweet with a tiny honey tinge. I do not get the citrusy start, nor the much hoped for lavender, nor the feared strong tea note so many claim to pull out mostly - I get it but a small and short-lived whiff. For that reason I think even Libre lovers should get a decant/sample/trip to the store first. If you love the idea of tea you might not get it, and if you despise it it might be all you smell. Not to mention what'll happen to the topnotes. As the title already mentioned : I'll keep it. Had I not gotten it by mistake I do not think it would have ended up in my collection though. Once my 50ml is finished, or maybe even sooner, I'll go seek new summer scents. I fear Libre EDT, predominantly as a result of the way it smells with my skin chemistry, is too linear & could get boring fast. And the last thing I want is ruining my love for jasmine, orange blossom, and most importantly: my love for Libre.]

I almost scrubbed this off. This immediately reminded me of Downy Unstoppable Scent Beads for your laundry, but way more intense on the lavender. Like to start, all I got was that lavender. The citrus wasn't present and I wish it were because they need something to cut the lavender, to not make it so overpowering. Then the scent moves onto generic white floral smell with still a background of lavender. This reminded me of my grandma back in Kentucky, when she was dressing up for the horse races. So it does give an "air" of being rich, but old rich. The middles notes don't last long either, they move quickly to the dry down which was just the lightest of musk, vanilla, and the lavender (because you cannot escape it in this fragrance). The fragrance did last about 4 hours on my skin and the projection was decent during that time. So, if you want to smell like beast mode laundry and a rich old white late in Kentucky, you can buy 30mL for $85.

i know the answer is money, but i will never truly understand why flankers are made when they don't smell distinct from each other. i think edt & edp are similar, more so than edp & intense which at least has a vanilla note. edt also performs worse than both as i only get ~4 hours out of it & it turns into a skin scent halfway through. as of writing this, i have yet to try all the flankers (le parfum is on my list), but so far edp is still the clear winner.

Libre's excellent Eau de Toilette flanker opens on sharp lavender and bergamot, with a haze of white florals and musk just below the surface. The spiky top notes are what many perceive as masculine; there's a fougère-like cleanness that evokes shaving foam or fresh laundry. Initially, there's a tension between the intensely dry, herbaceous opening and the softer, warmer heart and base notes; it's almost as if two different fragrances were trying to assert dominance on the skin. But sometime within the first half hour, the lavender starts to soften and the scent becomes more rounded, as the florals and vanilla become more prominent. In the heart, I initially get more orange blossom than jasmine, and certainly nothing resembling jasmine tea. The floral notes are hard to distinguish from each other, as they're smoothly blended into a pillow of soft vanilla and musk. The lavender is still there, providing a herbal counterweight to the sweetness of the vanilla. It is a pleasing contrast, nowhere near as confronting as the raw tension of the opening, but playful and sophisticated. The lavender-floral-vanilla accord remains well into the dry down, which feels similar to the heart but turned down in volume. I do get more jasmine from the florals and, finally, the occasional whiff of jasmine tea. Projection is excellent for the first few hours, perhaps too much so, given I prefer a closer scent bubble. But it is a little more muted than the original Libre Eau de Parfum , and eventually sits closer to the skin for the last few hours. Longevity is very good for an Eau de Toilette - at least six to eight hours. Compared with the original, the EDT is fresher, less heady; otherwise, there isn't a huge difference between the scents. I prefer the EDT because it still has excellent performance and is overall easier to wear.

YSL Libre EDT is my favorite of the Libre line. I came to this line wanting fresh, citrusy lavender, and this did not disappoint. The tea note gives it that special je ne sais quoi that rounds the entire fragrance out, nicely. The vanilla/musk/ambergris base is perfectly balanced to not overwhelm the freshness of this fragrance. For an EDT it lasts quite a long time. The dry down stays sweet for hours on me, though I’m always pleasantly surprised when I respray later in the day and get to experience the bright burst of its opening again. I know a lot of people say this is their least favorite of the Libre flankers, but I think they’re looking for a scent that’s more gourmand. I’ve got samples and travel size of the EDP, EDT, and Le Parfum. I’ve sprayed the Intense version a few times just to test, and may end up getting it just to complete my collection. In comparison, I feel this EDT is exactly what it needs to be, which is the brightest, freshest of the flankers. Because of how fresh, citrusy, and lavender smelling this fragrance is, I’d recommend it for a day out shopping or a rainy day when you want a pick-me-up, drinking tea and reading a good book. As always, though, I revert to my motto about fragrance, which is wear it when you feel most comfortable and want to smell it for yourself!

Sometimes I forget how beautiful you are, even though I wear you so often. I probably just get used to you, my everyday companion, my work colleague. And then it suddenly hits me again: Wow, you are so fresh at the start: juicy bergamot and freshly picked lavender greet me in the morning.

Libré then. A fragrance that I have consistently ignored until now because it didn't interest me further during a spontaneous test after its launch, as it struck me as rather indefinable generic sludge. However, on a Monday in the drugstore, a bottle was sitting there waiting for its second chance (by the way, it was the Eau de Parfum, as I later found out).

There are four types of samples/refills for me: The ones that just won't run out because the scent is terrible... The ones that run out very quickly because the scent is terrible and just has to go... The ones that run out very quickly because the scent is absolutely dreamy...

Immediately after spraying, bergamot blooms along with something fresh that I unfortunately can't quite identify. Is it jasmine tea? It is a fresh scent that reminds me of tea. This specific tea scent makes me think of something natural and subtle. Since I received the fragrance as a sample, I thought I could start by writing about Libre to warm up to writing and reviews.

A fresher, more aromatic version of the original. Very beautiful orange blossoms with jasmine tea.. In my opinion, it is a forgotten and incomprehensible love.. It is the epitome of a spring and summer perfume, because unlike most fresh perfumes, the longevity is very good for me and the projection is also remarkable.

I happened to be listening to Andrea Bocelli and Mary J. Blige sing What Child is This as I put this fragrance on. The beauty of the notes matched the swirling song. Bergamot, Orange, Lemon in perfection, heartfelt florals and a stellar base. No one citrus or floral really dominates--or underperforms for that matter. Somebody give this fragrance a gold star. No, it doesn't reach the heights of Roja's triumphant Haute Luxe (aka Roja), but it's up there in the heavens nevertheless. Too often lately I've tested a fragrance only to have it turn to watery nothingness in only moments, never having gotten off the ground. Not Innuendo. It's a beauty of a modern oriental. Instead of blasting off like the 80's orientals (which I do like), you ride on a soft magic carpet to the sky and just sit among the clouds, smelling svelte. Very nice. A bit heavy for summer, but light for winter, this is a spring/fall fragrance. My favorite seasons.

I had the opportunity today to try out a few Roja fragrances. Innuendo was among them. At first, I thought to myself, "wow, this smells beautiful!" and I also had a vintage lipstick association. I immediately had the nice saleswoman spray the fragrance on my wrist. After leaving the store and repeatedly sniffing my wrist, it occurred to me that the scent seemed familiar from another memory corner. At first, I couldn't place it, but then while strolling along Rotenturmstraße (Vienna), I passed a Lush store and it hit me: A few years ago, I worked at Lush alongside my studies, and after a 10-hour workday, my entire clothing usually smelled like a homogeneous mix of all the products we had in the store. Not bad - but not particularly special either. My colleagues and I had a name for this unique smell: Lusheln or "here it smells like lushel!" :) and well, I find that Innuendo captures this scent exactly. For example, different Lush bath bombs that are stored too long next to each other at home eventually develop the same scent, this very scent. ^^ Please don't get me wrong, the fragrance is good, but with the association it triggers in me, it simply isn't worth the money for me personally.

My mom's best friend is Inge, a lovely person, always dressed discreetly and stylishly, who often visited us with her well-mannered little white poodle. Her dog played charmingly with our male poodle, who adored her. I also enjoyed having them as guests. Moreover, her owner is blessed with a delightful shyness - a trait that always attracts me. We chatted about this and that - and during our conversation, Inge's enchanting scent wafted into my nose, accentuating her lovely nature. A fine but unpretentious fragrance - just like her entire presence. Innuendo. Bergamot, orange, and lemon give the fragrance a refreshing openness, while jasmine and rose add elegance. But in an accessible way - without any stiffness. Iris and patchouli provide warm undertones - and the tonka bean harmoniously ties everything together. As harmonious as our peaceful togetherness. We simply fit together - people and animals formed a unity. And this connection is also radiated by the fragrance. There were never any disagreements between us - for as the Greeks say - friendships are made in heaven.

Innuendo has long gone unnoticed by me. Other fragrances always pushed themselves to the forefront. After several attempts, it, like Danger, has captured my heart and my nose in a whirlwind. (Ohh noooo, I was in Düsseldorf..) But now, with spring here and the sun shining, Innuendo is just the right fragrance. Definitely a Roja Dove! Innuendo starts fresh and fruity. Sparkling. A sharp beginning. A distinctive start. In the first phase, it is loud and unyielding. A striking sillage. And that lasts for a longer period. Then there is a delightful interplay between rose and jasmine. The violet makes its appearance much later. Sometimes the rose takes the lead, sometimes the jasmine dominates with that sweet delicate honey note that I love so much. The rose is fresh, light, and vital, as if morning gray dew drops belong to it. For a long time, the fragrance behaves as if it were a noble rose scent, which has gained a bitter note. I suspect musk is behind it. After a while, the freshness disappears. A spicy, very powdery, balsamic gourmand note emerges. Probably the blend of sandalwood and tonka bean. Here too, like with some other Roja Dove fragrances, the long-lasting base, still strongly accompanied by the heart note, is a dream of balanced, harmonious, cohesive spiciness and develops a creaminess that captivates. The fragrance is now very soft, warm, and close to the skin. Only those who come close to you will be enchanted by you ;) Innuendo is, for me, the most surprising and evolving of the RDP tested perfumes. Versatile and exciting. Here too, the fragrance possesses an indescribable complexity that leaves one in awe. Innuendo is an extremely multifaceted and profound scent that has very good longevity as an Eau de Parfum. In my opinion, it is a very feminine fragrance, from beginning to end. It would give color and shine to a gray mouse. To a femme fatale, it would provide a delicacy and softness, without diminishing her self-assured presence.

I find this an often misunderstood fragrance since one can't help to compare to its original and rightfully so since La Nuit de l'Homme casts a huge shadow however, judging it by its own merit it is a very nice scent and honestly I don't get why it gets so much hate. My only complaint is regarding it's uniqueness. Eau Électrique follows a trend many other fragrances have already mastered and some in a better way. All in all, Eau Électrique is a very good buy but far from ground breaking. It clearly went for an Eros vibe and honestly, I like it way more than Eros

Tried it today in London Luton Airport. To my nose it resembles the original La Nuit to some extent, however seems a bit fresher, with a certain bubble gum aspect (what a surprise..) in the opening and mid notes (not very prominent though). The sweetness level is pretty much the same as well. The problem with it; doesn't feel unique at all. It lacks character. When you smell it, it might give you the impression that you just mixed the 10 most popular fragrances for men and applied a new label on it. Performance seems ok though, as it's been 5 hours since applying and it's still noticeably there (as a skin scent). In conclusion, i wouldn't buy it. La Nuit and La Nuit L'Intense seem to be much better choices if you are looking for a fragrance with more identity.

Generic smell, perfume based on few notes, according to my standards it is more feminine. After the opening, in which the apple prevails, vanilla is predominantly felt which covers the presumed central and base notes. It's another senseless product, to be fed to the masses who are attracted by the brand, by the bottle and who only expect others to feel it when they wear it.

Disclaimer, I've had this fragrance for about 6 years, so the scent could of changed by now. A barbershop opening adjacent to La Nuit de L'Homme Bleu Électrique with a drydown reminiscent of Eros Eau de Toilette making it versatile and an easy pick for any occasion. Usually I'd want to describe how a certain fragrance makes me feel, but with this nothing comes to mind.

Eau Electrique opens with a noticeable apple and some citrus notes. The apple, tonka, vanilla, and lavender are really present up top with the main tonka bean note. Really, apple and tonka bean. Then, the second wave brings in geranium paired with that lavender sitting under a tonka/vanilla combo. The notes in Electrique have some overlap with Versace Eros, but, I think they are two different fragrances and the similarities aren’t that noticeable. Eros is a much louder and has more of a citrusy aroma than does Electrique, though, the tonka bean and apple notes are shared. Update: I could also compare this to Montblanc’s Legend Night, but noticeably lacking the heavy cardamom note. Electrique is understated and while it has some sweet elements, it never becomes overbearing. I think the prevalence of the cashmere was a nice touch and gives Electrique some more separation from the original La Nuit.

I had a bottle of this and used it quite a bit earlier this year. It was nice, but wasn't anything special. It had the sweet vanillic base and cardamom of regular LNDH but the opening was a dry mint and green apple. I have heard many people comparing it to Eros and I strongly disagree. They may share some similar notes, but they are extremely different in execution.

The scent is quite heavily criticized in the community! This is somewhat understandable, as the L'Homme line has been milked with countless flankers by now. Plus, it’s a sweet young fragrance, which doesn’t always have it easy among enthusiasts.. But, what can I say? I don’t find it that bad.

Since YSL believes this fragrance is electrifying, I thought I'd find you an act and song that captures the spirit. And et voilà - not so hard at all ;) *After you've played the song and put away the air guitar, let's continue...* About the scent... :) I find the color and name not optimally chosen.

DISCLAIMER: I am NOT proficient in the French language and had to Google the translation of my title. "Eau Douce". I hope "sweet water" was translated correctly. Since "Acqua E Zucchero" already exists and is also Italian, the appropriate translation for French had to be found. But how did I even come to this? Électrique. How on earth does electricity smell?

Wow, my first comment and I have absolutely no idea what to write. Moreover, I must say that I am totally hopeless at recognizing individual notes :-D and since I only sprayed it for the first time this afternoon when it was delivered, I can't really provide feedback. The beautiful, fascinating La Nuit DNA is definitely present (thankfully, I love it) Compliment magnet?

At first I admit that I didn't understand if it was for me. Then trying it for a few days I had to buy the bottle. Opens citrusy, dusty and incense. It evolves divinely, without ever exceeding. Slightly edgy, but perfectly wearable. Leather that looks like a sofa, dust that looks like a wooden counter. Versatile Chypre, but not for everyone perhaps. Love Roja

Yes, it is a somewhat "crazy" scent that demands the attention of all senses, including the nose. At first, there seems to be a chaotic jumble, a hodgepodge of fragrance notes. Bits and pieces of all kinds fly by, almost tangible, visible, and audible, but above all, perceptible by smell. Fresh golden-yellow fabric pieces with floral patterns, flakes with peppery mosses, little balls in the shimmering colors of various spices, earthy root pieces of sweet grass, which, together with patchouli leaves, aim for dominance, then the branches of various woods, on which resin droplets shine. All of this rushes by at first before it begins to settle! Now I can also follow along. From all this confusion, a quirky but beautiful scent crystallizes, which encompasses warm joy (citrus), nostalgia (flowers), a touch of "vanity" (cardamom, cinnamon), quiet "anger" (the slightly sharp pepper), melancholy (resins, smoke), as well as a good portion of "hope" (benzoin, vanilla) and calm composure (vetiver, mosses). So "crazy" it no longer seems. But unique. And distinct from almost all the scents I have known so far. A little later, the vetiver does take the lead. Together with the "birch smoke" (leather??) Everything else recedes a bit, yet remains latently and subtly "tangible," "visible," "audible" (like a rumble deep down) and perceptible by smell. Interesting and extraordinary :-))

"I thought of leather in a man’s world." (Roja Dove) That’s a statement that holds true. I would describe Fetish as masculine, old-school, and almost conservative. It’s not surprising to me when you look at Mr. Dove’s portfolio. Many variations of classic fragrance themes can be found there. They all seem to be of high quality and natural, but somehow I miss a bit more modernity, a certain twist. Andy Tauer would be the other extreme as a perfumer: His creations are mostly extravagant, unique, and innovative. However, I have yet to want to wear any of the ones I’ve tested (L'Air du Désert Marocain, Au Coeur du Désert, Lonesome Rider, Lonestar Memories). Roja Dove plays it safer. And so, even with Fetish, he hasn’t incorporated too much daring. At the beginning, one might be put off by the combination of smoke with an animalistic leather note that reminds me of smoked ham. Fortunately, it only takes a few minutes for the warm leather to become more wearable. The typically dry, woody tones found in Roja’s men’s fragrances emerge beneath it - Fetish has a slightly earthy quality. In my opinion, there’s a part of 51 pour Homme in this perfume. However, 51 seems even more animalistic to me, albeit a bit more balanced. Both fragrances indulge in the leather fetish quite thoroughly. Unfortunately, its almost vulgar dominance obscures the fine, spicy notes that gradually come to the forefront. Cinnamon and vanilla provide a reconciliatory warmth to the base and are supported by a hint of sweetness. For lovers of distinctly masculine and mature scents, Fetish is definitely worth a test.

Fetish pour Homme - on one hand, undoubtedly a reliable companion. On the other hand, it does show twists and surprises, although it operates within a manageable framework. A cloud of sour-rough, campfire-smoky leather opens. Aha, the base rings through immediately. Indeed: Elemi, leather, pink pepper. Foamy-scratchy notes of oakmoss and patchouli allow the tastefully subtle astringent citrus fruit (the manufacturer explicitly highlights lime) to barely make its presence known. My first surprise: On the third testing day, the smokiness of the opening lasts relatively long. Close to the smokehouse, of course, just narrowly avoiding the ham. Continuing on. An idea of minty freshness, very noble and elegant. After five minutes, primarily spices. Black pepper, aromatic and voluminous, almost smoky. Cinnamon is acceptable, moderate, with gentle, supporting sweetness. I can imagine a contribution from coriander sourness (more pronounced in the ground version), which transitions the citrus notes into the development. Cardamom fits well after half an hour and remains an important player. And suddenly I find myself (second surprise) back in the 80s. Although I missed out on significant fragrance experiences back then, I have tested some of the relevant heavyweights in recent years. The now austere, multi-note, robustly spiced-herb-green appearance surprisingly reminds me of that style. Only, this comes across far less overpowering than what the old veterans often offer, with which I reliably have certain difficulties. With Fetish pour Homme, however, despite the abundance of aromas, I can clearly discern various individual components in almost glassy transparency. And yet, the fragrance does not unravel. It has character, and I feel extremely noble, yet characterfully scented. Moreover, Fetish exudes a subtle masculinity that is appropriate even for a thin, bespectacled business economist like me. Already during the first hour, it becomes clear what the purely quantitative pyramidal distribution of the notes already suggests: This fragrance is essentially a single base note. The supposed heart note plays hardly any role for me. At most, I would want to highlight a leathery violet. The verdict from my favorite colleague after an hour was clear and concise: leather. In projection, it appears to be dominant early on. Personally, I also insert a slight eugenol intermezzo after two hours, which may involve spicy clove. Cinnamon alone does not seem sufficient to me. By lunchtime, the piercing impression, however, takes a turn. Sweet throat pastille leather takes over the reign, underpinned not only by foamy oakmoss, but rather a whole host of subjects forms a carpet of foundational warmth. A trace of gentle, ambery-creamy sweetness. Some accents from the sweet-resinous corner - benzoin, but primarily minimally dirty labdanum; I even contemplate opoponax. As a counterbalance, some wood resonates alongside, and I occasionally sense echoes of the sour leather direction, as represented by fragrances like Epic Man. The new motto is undoubtedly 'Volume'. The glassy transparency is history, now creamy-connectedness is in vogue. This thoroughly transforms the character of the fragrance. And alongside, that ultimately indefinable 80s twist always wafts. Perhaps that is what makes Fetish pour Homme special - the combination of the 80s vibe with a predominantly sweet-creamy leather note. In my few hundred tested fragrances, I have not encountered anything like this so far. Later in the afternoon, I would even attribute it a hint of barbershop attitude. A classic clean impression, a touch of aftershave. Original. Yet, consistently, our sweet-creamy throat pastille leather note takes the forefront, nearly brushing against the sweet licorice. With Fetish pour Homme, no one ever goes wrong, and I like it very much. Is it too expensive for that? Any answer remains necessarily subjective. Everyone is right, of course. I simply avoid a public stance and limit myself to two rather general observations: 1. People who value exclusivity and quality but do not wish or cannot delve deeper into this, our matter, may be tempted to suppress their need for high-quality through price, hoping it will guarantee what they desire. Fetish pour Homme meets such expectations unreservedly. 2. Fetish pour Homme shows no signs of "fragrance fatigue" throughout its entire duration, which would be inappropriate at the present price level - at least there should be agreement on that. I thank 0815abc for the sample. PS: Yes, I actually tested the EdP.

I have not hitherto been greatly fond of Kilian perfumes: I have found them a bit tepid, to be perfectly honest - certainly as-considered-in their price-brackett. But these two (this and the 'feel' one, are a different matter! Yes, I know it's a triumvirate; but it is these two I am talking about, and to my mind they form a complementary pair. A description of one, except insofar as they differ in the sheer ^content^ of their ^flowery^ component, is effectively a description of the other. Both are extreme musk (or quasimusk) bombs, and such floweriness as they possess is perceived not but through a shimmering haze like unto a force-field such as they have in Frank Herbert's ~Dune~, or some similar thing. Actually (it is now 5th of April) I am not supposed to have these yet, as the official release-date is 16th if April; and I think I was genuinely at least somewhat privileged to get them. Also, the getting them has serendipitously rehabilitated Kilian with me more generally speaking; as whilst I was settling for them, someone squirted themself an assay of another Kilian 'fume - one that I have already got (rose oud), & the düft plucked me askance; and, "whoa! that is so gorgeous! I seem to have misprisen it somehow all this time!": but, not insuchwise that these became anytheless outliers by virtue of it; and they remain that to my mind - outliers in a big way. I do really very strongly emphasise that. So, basically what happened here is that my Kilian apothecary, who has suspected for a long time that I have been unquick about her produce, despite my efforts to conceal it (perceptive, she is!), has placed these (and the third one of the triumvirate) in front of me, and I, with a (probably scarcely concealed) inner sigh said "alright I'll give them a try then" ... go through the motions somewhat reluctantly ... but then! what's this!? (the 'Feel' one) ... now this is actually ^something^! Try the next one (the 'Taste' one) ... same effect! To be perfectly honest, the third (can't remember what it's called now) doesn't grab me in the same way; but we have an epiphany here - suddenly we have two outstanders! My Kilian apothecary is ^well^ pleased, I can tell you. I know I hadn't exactly been brutally honest with her all that time; but I had been honest 'in a sense' - in the sense that whenever she had asked me what I thought of her produce I would try to find in my mind some real good thing that I could say about it, rather than actually ^fake^ a high opinion; but she could always tell I was struggling to find that ^good thing^. So such honesty as I had broached unto her now payed-off big-style, coz she knew my rapture was real! I do emphasise again that I very strongly recommend these, as they are to my mind ^really very^ good - even for the price, which is ^well into^ the high-end brackett. They are also different ^in detail^; but the respect in which they are different is to my perception secondary to that inwhich they are similar. This one is more of the fresh-æry-aqueous kind: it's actually got mint in it! and that usually puts me right-off; but in this the mint is so exalted by the quasimusk it just _doesn't_ matter! [As for the particularities of its °partner° (the ~Feel~ one) I would say the following. This one is thick & heavy & perhaps even a tad narcotic - the ylang-ylang note is prominent. It is rather on the sweet side, but not gourmandy - no, this stuff way transcends the gourmandy÷not-gourmandy dichotomy! But I think even were it a lesser 'fume with a similar profile it would not be gourmandy forall its sweetness.] These twain are a complementary pair. I normally abhorr that idea as a marketting stunt; but in this case I _do_ think they actually are. And then I did something really bad! She kindlily invited me onto the waiting-list for the limited supply the store was appointed ... but I hesitated ... and then (but at least at the same store) another apothecary (my chief) one, arranged, by °irregular° means, to get me them in my hand!! The Kilian apothecary was ^very^ cross - she tried to conceal it just as I had tried to conceal my thitherto-unfavour towards her produce; but she failed, just as I had failed!

One of the best fragrances I have encountered in a long time. Extremely fresh but at the same time very soft, it actually reminds me a bit of a Mojito, but more of a non-alcoholic or quite clear one with lots of ice. The scent is very linear and simple - nothing changes from the opening to the drydown. But in this simplicity lies the genius. It captivated me from minute 1.

Pfffft… Here I am writing in countless comments how "delicious" ladies with certain fragrances should smell (although this phrase probably doesn't sit well with some), and suddenly a fragrance from Kilian appears that translates to: "I like how you TASTE". Not "I like how you SMELL", but actually "taste". A fragrance name! So it's not so wrong if I occasionally (or quite frequently :D) use the term "delicious"! Right?? :DD He he he, and now here comes a unisex fragrance that hopefully makes not only ladies but also gentlemen (especially me!!! *sigh*) smell a little more appetizing! The bottle already makes a nice impression. The fragrance: Oh wow! The opening somehow blows me away! I smell lemons and mainly a wonderful peppermint, which smells very refreshing to me. The emerging green leaves are not just simply green, but also a bit herbaceous. In any case, the top note is very very nice and brings not only a slightly fizzy refreshment but also good mood. Of course, the top note fades a bit soon, or rather becomes weaker. Nevertheless, the fragrance remains pleasant with its now softened peppermint notes, and floral scents seem to emerge as well, although I can't really say if they smell like the indicated magnolias. Unfortunately, the fragrance becomes a bit dull towards the base. I can hardly smell the indicated vetiver; the earthy note initially comes across more like patchouli rather than grassy vetiver. Additionally, the base has turned out sweet. I'm not sure where the sweetness comes from, but I suspect it's from the magnolias. Only a bit later can I detect hints of vetiver, although I still perceive a patchouli note. As I said, the base is the least spectacular, and I find that very disappointing since the top note started off so wonderfully. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is average, and you will only be able to smell it a little from close up, initially of course a bit better. The longevity, on the other hand, is good, which must be due to the sweet base. In any case, I could smell it well on my skin for about eight hours. The bottle: The bottle is rectangular, thin, and tall. Unlike most of Kilian's black bottles, this one is white, and on the front, you can see green brush strokes that look like grass. Otherwise, the typical chrome metal plaque with the name and brand name is visible on the front, which looks nice but can sometimes be harder to read depending on the light (at first glance, at least). The cap is also chrome and cylindrical. A beautiful bottle! So,… this fragrance from Kilian leaves me with rather mixed feelings. On one hand, I find the top note incredibly nice and refreshing, making it almost immediately tempting to buy, even if the wonderful top note isn't really worth the high price, as there are many fragrances with a nice top note available for much less money. On the other hand, the fragrance is rather boring in the base and only smells earthy-sweet, and honestly, not even really great or convincing. Thus, the fragrance, despite the sweet note, does not turn out to be as "delicious" as one might think (or rather as I would probably write :D), and overall, despite a nice start, it is less convincing, which is a shame because the disappointment is all the greater after such a beautiful beginning if one finds the base, as I do, a bit too trivial. Of course, one must consider that such fragrances, which are intended for summer, usually smell rather trivial towards the end, so often only the top and heart notes are really good; this applies to most fragrances, but here with this fragrance, the price-performance ratio is really poor :D Otherwise, I would have said that one could quickly re-spray the fragrance to enjoy the top note longer, but no,… nearly 200 euros (by the way for 50 mL!) is not worth it for me. If you are still looking for a great peppermint fragrance that smells just as good, then try Menthe Fraîche by Heeley, which I find much more successful! The base on that one is still nice, and the fragrance costs much less (about 125 euros for 100 mL).

I got a tester of this one when shopping. What can I say? It is not unbearable, but it is quite poor. The beginning is fresh, woody, hesperidic. Kind of boring standard frag. Ok, there is some violet leaf that gives it something more interesting. But after a few minutes: Sickly sweet and synthetic. A typical cheap minty after-shafe-accord that stays and stays. This scent just smells cheap - the level of an axe deodorant. It is absolutely not worthy of a notable designer brand. Shockingly, Oliver Polge (yes THE Oliver Polge of Dior Homme) was one of the noses of this frag. He shouldn't prostitute himself for something like that, how disgusting! To my nose the "nuit" flanker is much better! Conclusion: Avoid this one. For the price tag there are far more interesting options. If you would like something fresh with violet leaf go for Eau de Cartier - just to name an example.

L'Homme Libre is basically violet leaf, basil and pepper. Opens in a great way, but then dries down to something quite boring which reminds me much of Channel Bleu. In my opinion there are other alternatives to this one. Sillage, lasting power and projection are average.

It's 2 days that i am using this stuff. The opening is great and the scent is amazing. I love it.After less than 1 hours all the good scent settles to another striking scent that does not as goo as the opening. Finally and sadly, the great smell descends significantly as u can smell it just near the skin. It's my view: the longevity is great (at least 6 hours) although the projection (or Sillage) is disappointing! All in all, I think it doesn't worth to buy.

Yves Saint Laurent L’Homme Libre is probably the most underrated flanker of the whole line and I personally believe this unique fragrance deserves some more credit. The very present violet leaf gives you a burst of freshness whilst respecting the original L’Homme identity. This is clean, herbal and uplifting. Perfect for the warmer days and definitely office friendly!
Very weak, it smells like sweetened water, mediocre release from Yves Saint Laurent. Longevity: 4/10 Smell: 3/10 Silage: It's not even skin scent

I simply think the YSL fragrances in these round, chic bottles from the L’Homme line are great. I have tried most of them, and there is hardly a scent that I didn't like. Even the possibly underestimated Libre here is a very, very nice fragrance, which unfortunately will most likely not make it into my collection; you'll find out why shortly.

Ginger, bergamot, violet, and basil. I totally love the composition. I sense a warm spiciness and I have this Wrigley's Spearmint feeling on my skin, but not too fresh, rather tenderly spicy. I simply feel comfortable and secure. Far from trendy scents and sweet promises. No pressure to impress anyone. One focuses only on oneself and enjoys the moment.

...that's exactly what I think of the first two or three hours after spraying it on. Not that I've suddenly been in such a shop or owned such a soap, but in my imagination, I’m wearing the finest tailored suit and strolling around the Parisian streets around the turn of the last century. Somewhere in a side street is the shop where they sell the best soaps in the world.

After over 30 years, there is a new "freedom water" from the house of Yves Saint Laurent. While my last commented "Eau Libre" took on a genderless role, "L'Homme Libre" presents itself as a masculine fresh fragrance.

It starts with a very cool opening. Immediately, the typical L'homme-violet can be smelled. Next, a certain sharpness joins in.. this is probably due to the ginger, which is now being included in every French fashion fragrance. However, the tone is set by the citrus peels. Aha, after a few minutes it suddenly becomes a bit spicier.

I am currently testing the summer discovery set from Roja for women and I’ll say right away: I can only relate to the fragrance samples from "Oceania | Roja Parfums", which I already have in my collection, from A Midsummer Dream and from 51 Essence de Parfum . All other scents smell to me like any random floral fragrances from a designer in the 90s. I don't warm up to Burlington 1819 at all. Reckless (2023) Eau de Parfum , which is presented as Essence de Parfum in the manufacturer's sample, initially smells aldehydic with neroli and mandarin (I don't smell bergamot), then jasmine and geranium join in, later it becomes a fine, slightly sweet, but generic floral mix without recognizable notes, like a designer fragrance. Not unpleasant, but interchangeable. I don't smell musk, vanilla, or sandalwood at all - unfortunately.

It cannot be denied: “Reckless” also carries the typical “Roja” scent signature (its unmistakable DNA), crafted just as skillfully as its now quite numerous relatives from such wonderful fragrance notes and is not shy or quiet in its presence due to their sheer number: “Reckless” shines, radiates, and vibrates with fragrant life! But unlike the creations I have tested recently and discussed in this community, “Reckless” is not heavy, dark, animalic-dirty, and profound, but rather floral-sweet and filled with summery life and cheerfulness. I do not know where this peculiar name comes from: Reckless is in no way, in my opinion! Perhaps I also missed the point in the naming of the fragrance; I cannot come to terms with it because I do not understand! Who can I ask? Well, anyway: We all have to live with our name, whether we like it or not. But back to the fragrance: As already mentioned, “Reckless” is also a typical Roja Dove scent; just from its structure, as is often, actually always, found in his creations. The shady citrus grove with its woody accents from the trees, their bark, the lacquered dark green leaves, their flowers and fruits of various kinds, shapes, colors, ripeness, and finally aroma forms the opening, the top note; the overflowing floral garden near Grasse with all its blossoms, the heart vibrating with fragrant beauty, color, and liveliness, and a warm enveloping, spice-laden smoky note form the base, in which occasionally the scratchy, barbed oak moss can be found quite naturally. But these apparent repetitions do not matter at all: The dosage and ripeness of the fragrance note variety and their ever-changing composition vary from scent to scent, thus ultimately creating an independent fragrance personality! And of course, “Reckless” also greets with a fragrance fountain supported by aldehydes, bursting with sun-ripened aromas of citrus fruits: lively, refreshing, and slightly herbaceous-spicy. The magnificent bouquet, whose lovingly and tastefully composed heart note consists of numerous flowers from the coveted white Grasse jasmine, sought after by perfumers for their creations, and the May/Grasse roses, which can only be found there and have now been "re-cultivated" after their fields were sacrificed to the construction frenzy of real estate madness not so long ago (in the 1970s) and were paved over because of this "concrete gold." Meanwhile, there are more than one initiative advocating for our beloved roses! Richly fragrant, dark violet violets with friendly velvet faces and the fragrant embraces of the vines adorned with ylang-ylang flowers naturally join in. And of course, the “English/Rose Geranium” with its herbaceous-spicy, so distinctive and familiar leaf and flower scent compounds must not be missing here. For fruity sweetness, plump, ripe, juicy peaches with their rich aromas provide the touch. This may sound kitschy and overloaded, far too pompous for the mundane reality of current life; and yet, each fragrance note has been thoughtfully selected and finely dosed to achieve this so touching “warmth.” This floral-sweet and summery cheerfulness in the fragrance also needs a fitting rich base, which is, of course, also Roja-like: Warm, cinnamon-spiced musk-vanilla cream with a hint of pink pepper and coriander gently caresses the already awakened senses before being embraced by the resinous, slightly sweet smoke of benzoin and styrax, the resin that harmonizes excellently with cinnamon and vanilla (I learned this many years ago from tele-shopping: so television does educate!). For me, “Reckless” is a radiant summer day on the skin, richly accompanied by fruits and flowers, whose enchanting twilight slowly and gracefully transforms into creamy spicy musk-vanilla warmth and styrax dark violet. I still cannot come to terms with the name of this fragrant work of art (I simply cannot associate "reckless" with the friendly, harmonious scent progression; even "daring" as another translation does not fit!), yet the sillage and longevity are again typical of Roja Dove: Full-bodied, round, and long-lasting - a true pleasure to which I always fully surrender out of enthusiasm for these fragrances! Whether one likes “Reckless” and its numerous relatives that roam our fragrance world or not, calling them tasteless, loud, and overpriced: That does not disturb my personal enjoyment! Or, to simply invoke the competition here: J’Adore! = I adore this scent!

Hmm.. Until recently, I was a big fan of Kilian's Love don’t be shy.. Not as a scent for going out, it's too girly, generic, and not special enough for that, but I loved Love don’t be shy for home use.. Slowly, however, I'm realizing that I have actually grown tired of the scent and I reach for it less and less.. The relatively weak H+S after the reformulation, considering the price, has increasingly bothered me.. Enough about Love don’t be shy.. Now, I come to my problem with Reckless. Reckless smells to me almost 100% the same, just more watery and, believe it or not, with even lower H+S.. A diluted, insignificant version of Kilian's Love don’t be shy.. A very girly marshmallow scent, where the O-flower has been replaced by orange compared to Love don’t be shy.. I can't really distinguish the rest of the notes and honestly hardly perceive them at all.. I honestly only smell a very watered-down version of Love don’t be shy.. No one needs this in my opinion… I think I have to slowly accept that I am not a fan of Roja. Either outdated or insignificant.. The price/performance ratio is often poor in my opinion.. Such honesty must be said even if Roja is celebrated by many as the number 1 luxury brand.. It simply isn’t my brand..

First of all; a pretty, shy scent that unfortunately is in a hurry to disappear... It starts off subtly citrusy, with no sharp, overpowering bergamot; a glass of mild orange. From the very beginning, "Reckless" is very soft and reminds me of a perfume my mother used to wear; somehow I "suspect" the neroli, which evokes memories. A bouquet of flowers sprayed with a sweet mist, yet not a childish girlish sweetness, I don't think of a young girl when I smell it. In between, the flowers become a bit purer, as if the "sugar" is trickling away, yet the floral sweetness remains like a creamy body lotion applied to still damp skin after a shower, which is never intrusive or loud. For me, the scent has a somewhat "damp-summery misty" quality due to this creaminess. It remains floral-misty-woven, I don't necessarily pick out individual notes. After an hour, it becomes very quiet and close to the skin, all in all a very gentle and reserved scent that is not particularly exciting (I don't need complicated art on my skin, it can be pleasant and wearable, but not boring and not so weak in sillage and intensity! Especially for the price). In the drydown, which I reach after 1 1/2 hours, it actually smells sweet like bubblegum and more girlish, yet not cheap or intrusive; on the contrary, I perceive it only quite faintly. It has often been compared here to "Love, don’t be shy," which I actually have never smelled until now, but which is certainly much stronger. "Reckless" is a pretty scent, I will definitely try it further, but unfortunately the longevity and intensity on my skin are really not good enough to justify a purchase.

Splash of Lemon reminds me very much of the instant lemon iced tea that I always call Krümeltee:-) As a child, I would always put a certain small amount into a bowl, dip my tongue in, and suck it away :-) I would like to express my sincere thanks to our dear Parfuma "Verbena" for this beautiful and somewhat quirky memory, because when I think about doing that again today, it makes me shudder and I would probably test positive for diabetes :-) The lemon comes across very fresh, but also sweet, and the bergamot, with its slight herbaceousness, ensures that the top note does not appear sweet - cloying. The lemon is still subtly perceptible in the first part of the heart note and bids farewell in leisurely steps in the second part of the heart note. This constellation can be sniffed on my skin for about 15 minutes before the heart note takes over. First there was a Krümeltee, and now a woody - fresh rum pot is served, where the sugar from the Krümeltee probably contributes even more to the fact that after the first glass of rum, one is quite tipsy :-) The rum is kept very fresh thanks to the nutmeg, which, together with the cedarwood, gives it a pleasant woody note. In the background, there is something slightly rosy, which comes from the rosewood and gives the fragrance a small floral note. One could say that we have a wood - rum pot garnished with rose petals. The heart note can be sniffed for exactly 5 hours on my skin before the base asserts itself. This becomes very clear, warm, but also distinctive. Pure, full vanilla and sweet - spicy amber are responsible for the warm yet deep accents in the base. At the same time, the base also has something very clear, which in this case comes from the musk. Patchouli emphasizes the clarity of the musk with its slight earthy tones and gives the base a distinctive aura. Overall, the fragrance can be sniffed for 7 hours on my skin. The sillage is designed from the beginning to be clearly perceived at half an arm's length, and this is maintained until the third hour, before it then gradually diminishes until the fragrance finally fades completely.

How I will find it in a few weeks, I cannot say yet. In contrast to most lemon scents, which rush straightforwardly towards midsummer and fleeting refreshment, Kilian builds a real aromatic split here that, on the whole, seems to work well. Overwhelmingly lively, strong lemon, which is already reminiscent of the power of Chanel's "Pour Monsieur". However - and the fragrance doesn't need 5 minutes for this - a subtly sweet-spicy, rum- and amber-like note is already emerging in the background, indicating that it won't just be cheerful and beachy. There’s also a hint of patchouli, although quite light and sweetish (in the "Héritage" spectrum), pointing to the split between European feel-good summer and oriental undertone. For my part, it could also be Caribbean, although the rum is being strongly pulled towards the Orient amidst patchouli and amber. Longevity and sillage are extraordinarily rich and juicy; the lemon has power. A bit confusing for the nose, the aromatic split already seems to appear after 2 hours of wear, although "Straight to Heaven" belongs to the category of well-wearable fragrances. Definitely something different... As for the price: 150 euros for 50 ml is already in the realm of the outrageous, considering that the aromas used are not among the most expensive and a true "Aha!" effect is rather lacking.

The "normal" Straight to Heaven has always been an ambivalent presence for me. On some days, I couldn't get enough of it; rum in fragrances often has that effect on me. On other days, it simply annoyed me...annoyed in the sense of being tiresome, exactly the parallel to Jazz Club by Margiela. The beautiful bottle and the extraordinary name have prompted me to test it multiple times. The Matisse version is, for me, a mix of Acqua Viva by PR and the normal Straight to Heaven! Citrusy like Nimm2, thick-oily just like PR, uplifting but not really refreshing. I know that Acqua Viva can be annoying over time. But already in the background, you can easily recognize the Straight DNA. Muted rum, like diluted or stretched...the combination, in my opinion, is very well done. Exciting, different, and extraordinary. A slightly green-herbaceous note that I didn't pick up in the normal Straight, along with a good portion of Earl Grey tea. I also can no longer detect the much-cited mustiness of patchouli; I perceived it differently in Straight anyway. Splash is certainly a fragrance that can elicit a "Wow" during the first test in perfumeries; it did for me as well because it is appealing...it has that certain something. I'm just not sure how long I would enjoy it, as Splash is not a scent for casual wear; "demanding" would be too much to say, but it "occupies" you...it takes you in! But it also triggers a fascinating sniffing at the wrist again and again. It is persistently scratching at my wishlist. Plus, it is €50 cheaper than the normal Kilians, which can easily tempt me...let's wait and see;-)! The longevity is very, very good; it lasts comfortably for 7 hours with a high sillage. So it has everything needed for a megaseller...if it weren't for the rum, which I quickly tire of like a fig! Still, it's an uplifting scent, which is quite useful in these days and(!

There is not much to say about vintage Opium edt, that hasn't already been said. I just want to mention that it wears remarkably well on warm summer days - in small amounts, of course, this is a potent fragrance and you do not want to suffocate yourself or the people around you. But the heat of the sun awakens the floral aspect and allows the carnation to really shine against the spicy background. A great love, in which I am always comfortable.

Opium can be worn by everyone. Not on any occasion or on any day. But it is so complex and so unisex, that I think of it as a modern fragrance to meet the demands of a time when gender is a more fluent and abstract than it was when I grew up. This has it all - in my opinion. Apart from being one of the most delicious mixes of all times it has a warmth and a fullness that makes me shout “bravo!” with enthusiasm and belief. Beautiful, wonderful and timeless. 233/365

Do you want to have an idea of how trends in the perfumery field have changed? well, compare the original Opium from 1977 with the male counterpart released in 1992 (if I remember correctly) and, between the two, tell me which one seems more feminine to you... the feminine is definitely more masculine than the masculine, yes! absurd huh? true opium is a perfume that today could easily be sold and worn for men, it is dense, resinous and spicy to die for, balsamic but NOT sweet. The resins used, of unquestionable quality, are not the modern chemical ones with a permeating and omnipresent sweetish scent. The scent always remains very warm and enveloping but at the same time very dry and sharp. Beautiful trail and persistence, never cloying, never sweet, but truly narcotic and opulent. It's a resinous spicy woody that's in a league of its own compared to modern filth. The perfume I would like my partner to have.

I get a juicy citrus opening with pepperiness. Then a strong, warm drydown of different incenses and resins, myrrh, a fruity note, yes, a distinct rose and cinnamon, warm and inviting. And a final stage of warm, thick, peppery-spicy woods. Long before the days of Iso E Super- this is an opaque, fusty cloud of spices and woods. The whole thing is a bit sweet, enough to draw you in, but not too sweet at all. What a seductive and enveloping scent. I don't know how people could have hated this in the 80s. It's probably my favorite Oriental. Richer than Shalimar Eau de Parfum , more wearable than Ambre sultan Eau de Parfum and warmer than № 02 - L'Air du Désert Marocain Eau de Toilette Intense . It projects an air of decadence and iniquity, and so I think of it as one of the spiritual successors to Habanita (2012) Eau de Parfum and am looking for more great perfumes that fit into this succession. If, like me, you're tired of clean and minimal scents, come over here and spray on some Opium.

There’s one perfume I remember from my childhood, and that is Opium 1977, I remember the bottle on my mom vanity, I remember my aunt using it first, and I remember thinking it was the perfume of femininity, the perfume of the grown up. This introduction alone should be enough to suggest I have a potent relationship with this perfume. To this day it’s still one of the most seductive, rich, spicy juices I’ve ever put my nose on. A true ambery masterpiece.

Yves Saint Laurent himself once stated that Opium was to be his greatest creation, his magnum opus. I could not agree with this statement more, as Opium in it's original state is likely one of the greatest fragrances ever produced. It's popularity upon release is proof enough of this, but it's enduring legacy and cult following has cemented this opinion into fact.

I have a distant aunt in Berlin who is now over 80. Incredibly educated, impeccably dressed, no polyester has ever touched her skin. Tailored by her trusted seamstress. A teacher of the old school. If anyone remembers the film by Loriot Ödipussi - the mother of the protagonist is spot on, although my aunt has 30 kg less on her hips.

When I was about 20, I tended to wear so-called "men's fragrances," like Aramis, Trussardi, Polo, Puig, etc. Firstly, they weren't sweet at all, and secondly, they were significantly cheaper than so-called "women's fragrances." Therefore, OPIUM was unacceptable to me and was disregarded.

There are perfumes that leave an indelible mark on our olfactory memory, and some of them signify the beginning of a great passion, as was the case for me with Opium. As a child, I was allowed to play with my mother's perfume bottles, and that is where my passion was born. The perfumes she used back then and still uses today were: Trussardi, Valentino, Moschino.

When you were born, I was already here.. When we met, you moved in with me on the same day luckily you had very little luggage..
