To this day I can't say, what defines you… only that I was very young, not even 16, and there wasn't a day without you.. For many years and days and nights you were my coat, my summer dress, my handkerchief, my sun hat and my umbrella..

"Say, head: what is actually 'special', 'something special'? How must something be for it to be 'something special'? Hm? Is 'special' always synonymous with 'unusual'? With 'something different'? With 'Oops, that's extraordinary!'? Or can 'special' and 'something special' also be somehow simple? Simply BEING is also something special. Right? Hm?" "Don't bother me, I'm chilling." Mpf. ---- "If something is simply beautiful, is it then something special? Or if I feel very, very comfortable with it, is that then special?" ---- "Does there always have to be a WOW for it to be special?" ---- "Or is it not enough if something is just the way it is supposed to be? That's actually special, right?" ---- "If something could stay like this forever, you know? Like 'To the moment, I would like to say,...' You know how?" ---- "If something should never go away again? Is that then something special?" ---- "Or is that then boring? Because: It's not anything special now, right?" ---- "Soft as a whisper, says Roja Dove. Hm." ---- "That fits, I think." ---- "But it really smells nice, right? So... Calm somehow. Can 'calm' smell?" ---- "So I find it quite special that I can smell 'calm' here. With flowers. And citrus, somehow. Hm?" ---- "It also smells somehow... Like... Well... I really can't describe it well... Doesn't bother me. Nice. So... Easy, you know?" ---- "It smells like 'everything is alright'. Somehow. Like 'What a beautiful day'. Hm?" ---- "A bit sleepy, so totally relaxed, you know?" ---- "But you can't really smell relaxation, as a feeling, can you? But here I somehow smell it. Strange." ---- "But... Maybe that's also the whisper that smells so nice here. So gentle and soft and... What do you think?" ---- "Should probably measure my blood pressure, I'm definitely totally calm. Great! Really beautifully calm. Totally relaxed. Head?" ---- "So sometimes you annoy me. I'm chilling now. My life probably. Just like that. Just don't bother me..." .................. Innuendo (Eau de Parfum) is a wonderfully beautiful perfume for me. And 'something REALLY special'. Deep inhalation with effect.

Hmm… I’ve been writing for over 500 comments that I think you ladies can be prickly creatures or at least can be, and now I’m testing a fragrance whose perfumer, Roja Dove, was inspired by you ladies… specifically by the softness and delicacy of a woman… pah, who believes that! … okay okay, don’t get upset right away… Yes, I admit, you can be soft and delicate, maybe even sweet, but all of this is also true of my tomcat, and he still scratches sometimes, actually quite often, which can hurt quite a bit… hmm… somehow there seem to be certain parallels between cats and ladies… hmmm…. :DDD Well, before I upset everyone, I’d better quickly get to the fragrance, which according to Roja is supposed to exude pure femininity. The Fragrance: The fragrance (whose liquid is somehow slightly oilier than usual) starts with bergamot and especially neroli. But somehow there’s also a slightly medicinal, camphor-like note in the background, which gradually becomes resinous, then herbal, and then transitions into a sultry floral scent or transforms into ylang-ylang. Presumably, this olfactory impression (the resinous-herbal) was a combination of the ylang-ylang, which had not yet unfolded, with the neroli. Next, you can recognize rose and jasmine by their distinctive scents. This makes the fragrance both sweet and floral. All these notes are surrounded by a small, gentle, and powdery veil, which should come from the iris, but which you cannot smell yet. The ylang-ylang, which I initially thought was more of an herb or something, now smells more intense, and you can really recognize it as ylang-ylang. Nevertheless, there is still a slightly resinous note in the background. Some earthy patchouli adds to it and makes the fragrance a bit heavier along with the ylang-ylang. In the end, it remains with heavy floral notes, which makes it seem a bit mature, but it has still turned out soft, which is probably thanks to the iris and tonka bean, which give off their nice, powdery scents here and make everything a bit more fragrant. The sweetness at the end comes increasingly from the musk rather than from the jasmine. Overall, it’s quite okay, but for me, it’s not exactly the best Roja fragrance. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is not bad at all for a delicately scented fragrance. It radiates quite well and is therefore still detectable even at a greater distance; moreover, you definitely leave a scent trail behind you. Roja fragrances are usually known to last forever, and this fragrance is no exception. Normally sprayed on, it lasts from morning to evening, and if sprayed heavily, it probably lasts until the next morning. The Bottle: The bottle is made of heavy glass and is, as always, very high quality. The gold-plated label is made of real gold and, like other details of the bottle, is crafted by hand. The cap is also gilded with real gold particles, and in the lower area, Roja's signature is engraved (on some bottles, the brand name is also engraved). As mentioned, it is high quality, but I like this bottle a bit less than the other Roja bottles, which is due to the fact that the cap is only made of gold and no sparkling Swarovski crystals have been embedded here (even though the shape is there), which usually makes the bottles look so beautiful. Still not bad. Okay, I admit, the fragrance smells quite nice. It is soft and delicate, but the heavy ylang-ylang also makes it smell a bit more mature. I would say that younger people might not relate to this fragrance… It is suitable for evening wear in autumn and winter, as it could come across as a bit too heavy and especially intense at work. However, one could possibly try to use less… that would need to be tested. In any case, I liked Innuendo, but it still doesn’t belong to the best fragrances I know from Roja. However, it’s worth testing; maybe you’ll like it better since I don’t particularly enjoy heavier floral fragrances. Does the fragrance smell of femininity now? Well,… it at least smells like a ladies' fragrance :D But like the delicate warmth of a woman (who is probably quite prickly in reality!)? Well, for that, I would actually have to sniff you, but either you would scratch then… or, and this is more likely, you freaks smell of 1000 different fragrances, so that one would perceive all sorts of things, and for sure, one would also notice some men’s fragrances because you even wear OUR fragrances from time to time… :DD

Wolle and his crew had planned to visit England because Wolle's cousin Bolle lived there. After quickly getting excited about the local drinking culture, Hotte asked whether there were any leather fragrances available. Bolle assured them that Royal Leather Mayfair would be a real heavyweight. A scent that, of course, could be seen as a nod to the British royal family, particularly the Duke of Westminster. It sounded excellent to the Herne crew. They decided to leave the motorcycles in Germany due to concerns about the English traffic. Especially since they already had trouble following the rules in Germany, let alone not falling off. How would Udo have known that there is a ban on enjoying the wind down below while naked in the city? Anyway, they arrived in England and stormed the pubs. Bolle wanted to present the Kilian product to Wolle and his entourage. So he sprayed a few times into the air: “Bolle, what's going on? Is that baby powder?” “No, that's iris, sweet, powdery, dry, very unpleasant.” “This is Leather, very rough.” “There's supposed to be hawthorn in it, which smells rather rotten. Maybe that's the weird sweet element.” “Yes, very leathery.” “You can't spray that on yourself; I'll just pour some beer over it, that smells better. Does the Queen powder herself with this? I'd rather be on another continent.” “But highly recommended by a guy called Bald Bastian, well known as Flower Power-Basti.” They then moved on to a nice game of darts, where Hotte ended up in the hospital after accidentally throwing a dart backward, which literally went into his eye. They forgot about the fragrance because every time someone smelled it, it felt uncomfortably sharp. It didn't smell like leather at all; rather, the putrid element pretended to be some kind of leather, but it smelled more like an imitation. Of modest quality. Later, they brought up the fragrance again after Udo, completely drunk and covered in fish and chips, was sleeping on the floor. “Look, Udo really overdid it. All the flies buzzing around him. That's the rotten smell of the fragrance. Fascinating how the perfume attracts flies; it really smells awful.” “Uh... well... Udo didn't even spray the Kilian.” Everyone took a step aside. “There's no development either. It just stays the same.” “Well, I can smell leather. With cinnamon or something on top.” “We call it very fauny, cravachilicious.” “I call it very modest.” Not much happened after that. Time passed, and the scent remained as it was. Rotting is certainly an extreme element, but not rough. Leather that is drowned in floral and sweet elements is not rough. Of course, all of this is subjective, but there is very little leather here, and it is rather powdery. There are probably better alternatives.

It was one of those days. A day when she didn't expect anything earth-shattering, a day like any other. Almost. It starts with bergamot, probably meanders through flowers, and ends in moss. You think so, darling. Even before the first ray of sunshine, the phone rang, and she heard what had been unspoken until then. She didn't think about the perfume she was wearing. When she hung up the receiver, she was happy. There are different kinds of happiness; she felt that calm yet complete "I could scream!!!!" happiness. That breathless one. Where you can't get a word out, that happiness. And around her, bright flowers shining everywhere. A storm of blossoms. Loud, but not shrill. Embracing, overwhelming, enveloping, like a cloud of cold, soft cotton, maybe a bit scratchy, but still somehow invitingly beautiful. She thought. As far as that was possible in that state. The world had turned upside down. Just for her. All of a sudden. Eyes closed. At some point later, she opened her eyes. It had become warmer on the cloud by now. Cozy. Really familiar, beautifully snuggly. To stay, to never leave. Mossy-cuddly-cool still, yet at the same time so beautifully woody-warm. Not entirely clear, but fascinating and incredibly beautiful. Unusual. Bumpy now and then. Unique. And so much had been said by now, but so much had also not been said. She knew a lot now. And some things she only whispered softly. Unspoken is not easy. But beautiful.

There are moments for which there are or need to be no words. Roja's perfume "Unspoken" is such a moment; a moment transformed into an opulent, spicy-floral fragrance experience. When it comes to discussing Roja fragrances, I am biased; I gladly admit that. I love strolling through their rich and colorful floral gardens, experiencing their gala appearances, hotel and business visits up close, enjoying grand operas together with them, or simply listening to their stories. All of this they have offered me so far! "Unspoken": a seemingly simple name and at the same time a problem for me as an extremely communicative being. Perhaps I will simply let the master speak for himself: "Whose heart does not skip a beat when someone special catches our eye? A glance - so expressive, without a single word. Perfume can express this better than anything else, which is why I created a classic chypre structure and added an unexpected overdose of jasmine on top. This fragrance captures our attention and speaks without words - effortlessly" (Quote from Roja Dove about his fragrance "Unspoken".) This means a fragrance fireworks triggered by aldehydes in his namesake perfume: Classic, fruity bergamot and impressively exploding bright bursts of pale yellow ylang-ylang vines, delicate and caressing neroli accents, noble elegant roses, and the jasmine mentioned above: Rich, large-flowered jasmine in full radiant white sensuality, ready to seduce! These fragrance notes bloom and float clearly and sustainably above a deliciously composed base. "Chypre" is also the magic word here: Thus, we naturally find strong oak moss, vetiver, and patchouli (both known for their moist-earthy qualities) and masculine, slightly animalistic sandalwood as the usual components. Rich resins, such as labdanum and precious doses of amber, meet well-spiced, warm cream-white vanilla, sparkling-sharp ginger, and the special, silky cedarwood aroma that I love so much. Proud iris reigns in a nest of fresh green fragrance notes and crowns this multifaceted fragrance fireworks with a finely woven powdery veil. Enough words have been exchanged; Roja's typical sillage and longevity speak a clear, now familiar language to me. "Unspoken" is once again an opulent composition that caresses the senses, inviting to enjoy silence with its resonant fragrance harmonies.

Thank you for this scent strip as well, dear Seymour. It seems to me that the fragrances - at least the women's fragrances - from Roja Dove are incredible powerhouses! This one is no exception. The neroli and bergamot opening is overwhelming! Rose and ylang-ylang - one of my favorite flowers - are nowhere to be found! Instead, there is an abundance of jasmine, supported by sharp ginger in the heart note. The sillage - also overwhelming here - carries the scent quickly into the room, and I am close to fainting. Resins and vetiver contribute their part in the base, while the rest is hardly perceptible. Mind you, I only have (thank goodness) one scent strip! But that is enough for me. I willingly forgo a live test in this case!

Powdery cream scent, disguised in an SM bottle... Anyone hoping for a dark beast here is completely mistaken. Keep stumbling around with lacquer and leather in the darkroom. The all-over Jeremy Fragrance outfit fits better here. Thankfully, it doesn't get too sweet, as hawthorn, the jobberry, and my new friend iris provide the right kick. Yes, in the drydown, I get vibes of Penaten cream/ moist towelette a la Lattafa Love and Peace. I found it off-putting in the first test, but I wanted to test it again... now I have something completely different, but I'm also satisfied. H/S is rather moderate like with most of the brand (except Black Phantom and Intoxicated). But too much hawthorn can also drift into the medicinal. Creamy jobberry and powdery iris dance a duet, oh how nice the scent is as it moves further away from Love and Pride.

... perfectly captures this scent for me. Mirabella gifted me this fragrance, and it hit me like a grenade. For days, I wandered through perfume shops, sniffing around without success. This time, I wanted something sweeter, fruitier with a wow effect. I had set my sights on 2 fragrances: Amouage Sunshine was great on the test strip, but it's currently too expensive for me, so no skin test. M.Micallef's Art Collection - Rouge N°2 was also wonderful on the strip and on sale, but unfortunately boring on the skin. My frustration purchase was then Le Heure Bleu and Omnia Amethyst, both lovely but not what I actually wanted. Then came the early gift package, and since I was stressed and it already had a slight scent, I opened it early... just in case something might have leaked. But it was only an incense stick. Now, onto the fragrance. The name is just silly. I had the vial in my hand and thought: What is this supposed to be? Do I want to smell something that slowly kills me? It must be dreadful, this little water. But well, now it's here, so let's hop onto Parfumo and list it. The bottle, however, I liked much more. It reminds me a bit of a black Fabergé egg... pure luxury. However, not quite so noble, but rather edgy in black latex. I think of BDSM. A dark side, something evil, dishonorable about greed and suffering. Ooohhhhh exclusively available in Russia. That sounds interesting, I think. I like Russia; they tend to keep poodles, and the ladies are very disciplined. Icy winters, furs, caviar, luxury, people, and free dogs living in subways and heating shafts to avoid freezing or working hard for little pay. The country is vast, and there are very, very poor and very rich people, metropolises, and open land. A completely different world than the one we live in here. Somehow, the bottle fits. My curiosity is piqued. So, a test directly on the skin! I smell sweet lychee and tart blackcurrant bud. The top note starts with strong sillage, incredibly beautiful. Bitter-sweet, I want to bathe in it. It's rare that I've smelled such a lovely combination. Deliciously fruity, not synthetic, and yet not overpowering. Unfortunately, the top note fades quite quickly, and the scent becomes slightly floral, creamier, and softer. Like a light, freshly washed chiffon kimono, it envelops me. A hint of nothing, cool silk that still keeps you warm. It's almost like being naked, only that the delicate silk fabric, printed with fruits, buds, branches, and leaves, embroidered with delicate flowers, moves with every breeze and brushes against my skin. Innocently clean and cool yet warm and erotic. And like a wonderful dream that continues to fade and become more unreal after awakening, having touched heart and soul, and the longing for this bliss almost tears you apart inside as you realize it keeps slipping through your fingers. So the name makes sense. Unfortunately, the longevity on my skin isn't great, and after 2-3 hours, it's sadly all over... or so faint that I can hardly perceive it. That's why the 5ml is already used up after 3 days. But because the dear God sometimes looks out for me, he placed a whole bottle for me at a bargain in the souk ;)

I'll be honest, from the scent description from the brand I wasn't going into this expecting much. However, I have to say I was pleasantly surprised at how fresh and light it is. For the summer this would be very easy to wear. Gives the impression of fresh honeydew or cantaloupe on my skin, reminiscent of picnics by the lake with friends.

I'm a big fan of the original I Don't Need A Prince By My Side To Be A Princess, and the Eau Fraiche didn't disappoint either! It's just what I imagined. The fluffy vanilla marshmallow and green tea are exactly the same as in the EDP, but everything is a little lighter, fresher and airier - as it should be with an Eau Fraiche. The biggest difference between the two is the pronounced ginger note in this. It's fresh-spicy and invigorating, especially in the opening, while it was only a light accent in the original. The bergamot might add to that effect. If fragrances were drinks, Princess would be a green tea cheesecake drink from a boba shop and Eau Fraiche would be a sugared, carbonated iced green tea with a touch of vanilla. Still very sweet, but in a more transparent way. I can't imagine that anyone who enjoys the original would dislike this, but I also don't think you really need both. Except maybe when Princess is your absolute favorite and signature and you want a version that is more appropriate for summer. It's hard to decide between these two, both are truly lovely if you're into gourmands and tea scents, but as I have Princess EDP, I won't buy the Eau Fraiche anytime soon.

I am thrilled with the scent. It opens with a fresh vanilla lemon and I perceive a slight saltiness. Simply pleasant and soothing. The vanilla or the marshmallow is so light and fluffy due to the lemon that the fragrance is ideal for spring and summer. A carefree spring and summer gourmand. In the drydown, the scent smells like warm, slightly salty skin that has been previously moisturized with a sweet lotion. Simply pleasant and beautiful. For me, it is a feel-good fragrance. Longevity is about 3-4 hours and the projection is well noticeable in the first 2 hours; afterwards, unfortunately, it becomes very close to the skin. I will certainly use up my decant and I like the scent, but due to the unsatisfactory longevity and sillage, it would not be a candidate for purchase for me.

I have the version in a purple bottle. And yes, it is Samsara, but the light version. You have to spray a lot, I mean a lot, in this case it is a necessity. I stand for about 20 seconds in this cloud and go crazy - it is unrealistically beautiful. I had a vintage Samsara and I could not wear it, even if I used it under the knees. But Roja did his own “Samsara” and this is exactly what I need. I bought it on the official website during a sale for 140 euros and I can say that this is its price. The original price of 300 euros is definitely overpriced.

Scene: Mrs. Lohse in front of the fragrance shelf in the morning. Mood: hectic Dialogue: Mrs. Lohse, Mrs. Lohse Today Danger? - Yesss! Too good for work. Take it out for an evening. - Yeah, wait a minute, for an evening I’ll take Black Orchid or Decadence! I mean for a nice outing. You can’t go to those old dives with Danger, come on... - And where am I supposed to go out nicely? When do you even want to wear it? You might as well sell it if you never wear it. - But it’s so beautiful, I can’t sell it. Never! Well then wear it sometimes. - I will, at the right occasion. EVERY TIME. Silly, right? Danger's arrival took a year. I struggled with myself for that long after the test. I liked it immediately. Very classic start. Not sour or bitter citrus. Then powdery flowers, rounded spice, and the most beautiful sandalwood melt I’ve encountered since Samsara in the vintage version. So seductively powdery-creamy with exactly the right amount of sweetness that can make a fragrance feel sublime. Floral cream wood par excellence, the notes flowing smoothly into one another. Danger lingered. Not just in my mind. Also on the Fitbit bracelet. It radiated from my skin for days. So soft, smooth, noble, sensual, yet distinguished, elegant, ladylike, and damn mature. Porcelain teacup finger spread to wear, but also for the opera, weddings, or in a negligee. I never forgot the fragrance after the test, and so a year later, I quickly seized the opportunity in the souk. And now it has been sitting there for months, and I’m struggling again. It’s always wearable. Everyone likes it, everyone notices it. Because Danger is a compliment magnet -》 Oh, let me smell, how lovely, what are you wearing? That seems familiar. Is that Tresor? Well, please, Tresor, what blasphemy. Here, it’s King Roja, take this, you dilettante. I’m surprised that the fragrance is perceived as foreign; to me, it feels very close to the body, close enough to fall into, to embrace: it smoothly and silkily goes into symbiosis with me. By the way, I smell neither peach, nor vanilla, nor Tresor. More like Samsara, in that vintage version. The struggle has a reason: I want to crown the queen of my fragrances with occasions. That never come, after all. And after a conversation with the Roja queen of the forum herself, I now decide: I am the occasion. From today on, it will be worn regularly, no more saving and shelf conversations. Decadent is how the world goes to ruin. Just one more question, who will buy me a new bottle when this one is empty?

After two test sprays, I was able to acquire a bottle here. Although it's the older model in the 100ml bottle, the scent is still perfectly fine, as I compared it with a sample. Thank you for that. In a very brief and minimal way, I can smell the citrus top notes, but quite quickly this beautiful creamy-powdery note spreads on me, which I love so much. The floral notes are very pleasant, rounded off by a beautifully integrated Ylang-Ylang. I can't detect the fruity note of peach on my skin, and I find that good. Clove, patchouli, sandalwood, and tonka bean hold back nicely, providing only a light spiciness, or contributing to the creaminess, but they do not stand out, and thankfully the tonka does not leave a chocolate note. For me, one of the most beautiful and wearable Roja fragrances, very noble and elegant.

After testing "Reckless" from the line, I wondered if "Danger" would be just as light a breeze on my skin, but "Danger" is stronger and more expressive. Right after spraying, the scent hits me powerfully and slightly sour, yet it remains soft. Just like "Reckless," it again reminds me of a fragrance my mother wore; I find it quite retro, but not in a negative sense. Instead of girlish fruity sweetness, the gentle yet dominant grapefruit with mandarin stands out brightly, paired with a very elegant, light soapiness. Very elegant and mature. It follows with a very intense floral note, entire bouquets, whole spring gardens with shady coolness. Furthermore, it reminds me of the floral, often powdery scents my mother wore; for decades she wore "White Diamonds" by Elizabeth Taylor (now she has also added a few other perfumes), and "Danger" reminds me a bit of that. I hardly smell sweetness here; it is quite green, a bit bitter, with subtle floral sweetness mixed in. The combination of jasmine and gardenia also slightly reminds me of "Ellenisia" by Penhaligon's, but where "Ellenisia," which I like very much, feels fairy-like, "Danger" feels feminine and strong. A creamy spiciness spreads, somehow moist-earthy, yet gentle and elegantly enveloping, slightly smoky veiled by patchouli, with the iris dusting lightly. The scent feels very alive to me; it develops an intense character on my skin. In the end, a very delicate, light green vanilla remains in the drydown on the skin. A perfume suitable for the office, business lunches, a picnic in the park; a picture that seems to have sprung from a valuable painting, for a woman aged 30 and up. I don't find it dangerous, but self-assured and down-to-earth. A perfume that reminds me of my mom :)

There are perfume names that make you wonder what they have to do with the scent. Because with Danger, one might imagine something daring, wild, or something strong. Certainly not a fragrance like this one, which smells not only gentle and soft but also has a slightly classic character. Perhaps the scent could entice one to approach a woman wearing this fragrance, as it smells good and is really pleasant to smell on someone (even if it doesn't smell that special). And perhaps that woman turns out to be a frightening Femme Fatale or something, who throws plates and vases around, and you could quickly end up with a bloody nose… in that case, the scent would not only be dangerous but rather even deadly!!!.... The scent: The beginning is citrusy, but not in a zesty way. However, I can't quite say which note I really perceive from the top notes. I suspect it's lemon. Additionally, the fragrance has a somewhat classic smell, followed by floral notes, especially roses and heavier Ylang-Ylang. By classic, I mean the way women's fragrances smelled in the 90s. Of course, there are also pleasant sweet and fruity notes to be detected here, presumably from the jasmine and peach. Towards the base, the scent smells slightly floral, sweet, and with lingering citrus notes. A somewhat spicy clove adds to it, along with earthy patchouli and lightly powdery vanilla. A little later, you can also smell the tonka bean. Naturally, over time, the citrus notes fade away, so that later you have a soft, slightly powdery, and sweet scent. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is not as strong as I thought after looking at the average ratings of the perfume edition earlier. So, sure, it's not that weak, but it could definitely have been stronger. Perhaps a tiny scent cloud remains, but after two hours, you really have to get a bit closer to smell it on someone. The longevity is around eight to nine hours, which is quite okay. The bottle: The bottle is rectangular and has somewhat thicker glass sides. On the front, there is a hand-applied golden label with the name of the fragrance. The cap, made of real gold, is cylindrical on the bottom side, where the brand name is engraved. The upper part is rectangular and usually has Swarovski crystals embedded, which seem to be missing in this fragrance (?). In any case, the bottle is, as always, very high-quality and elegant, although the bottles with white or red crystals look even better. Roja Danger is, let's say, quite nice. It smells really good, and you hardly detect any synthetic components. However, I must also say that I have sniffed many similar fragrances that can be bought for much less money. Sure, Roja is a luxury brand and therefore costs more, which is also reflected in the high-quality bottle, but olfactorily speaking, I find that the scent does not stand out significantly from many other fragrances. Since it smells good, I think it is particularly suitable for special occasions when going out, though one would wish for a slightly better sillage. On the other hand, the fragrance shines with good longevity. Hmm... isn't the meaning of a Femme Fatale that an attractive woman seduces a man only to lead him to ruin? If so, then the fragrance name might actually be well chosen, at least as a warning for us guys, since the scent, as mentioned, smells good on a lady and one could quickly be seduced... *sigh* So it can be tested if one ever gets the chance.

When Ms. B goes to bed at night, she likes to apply one (or two) of her decants on her arm. Just to get to know it better, but without disturbing anyone. Last night, a 10 ml decant of this Kilian fragrance was up. Just like that - because Ms. B has never worn it in public and actually didn’t really remember how it smells anymore. It has been sitting untouched for over a year, probably bought blind because of the raspberry. The opening is heavy-floral with a gum-fresh overlay (but it has been chewed on already - just saying), not so great, but it will suffice for sleeping. And then Ms. B couldn’t fall asleep for a long time. Not because of the scent, but because during the holidays, the sleep rhythm always gets thrown off. And after HOURS, her head was still sleepless on the scented arm, her nose twitched and Ms. B said to herself: Wait a minute, she knows this. Sniffed again. Huh? Did she remember wrong which decant she applied? Parfumo on. Every applied fragrance is recorded without exception. No, Ms. B wasn’t mistaken, it WAS KDL. Sniffed again - she smells Portrait of a Lady. Quite clearly. Next morning: the test. One arm POAL, the other KDL. Shit, it smells completely different - looked closely. Oops - accidentally applied Love & Tears. So KDL on a free spot next to POAL. Opening: totally different. Brief disappointment. POAL is a heavy rose scent, like a fully bloomed dark rose, but one that you know will wilt tomorrow. Like just before tipping over. But not tipped over yet. KDL greets me again like the wilted bouquet with chewed gum. It takes 4 hours and then - sniff - yes, definitely: POAL is a bit weaker. Ms. B feels like she has achieved something that day (yes, dear God, one must also be able to enjoy the little things) Due to the strange opening, the long development time, and the similar price, the conclusion is: No, you don’t need this one.

I love fragrances from Kilian like Back to Black and Love. Both are very full-bodied, sweet, heavy scents with good sillage and longevity. Now I sit here with a sample of Kisses Don't Lie and feel a bit perplexed.... why? Let's start: The first impression on the skin is zesty from the bergamot, with just a hint of pepper. After a few seconds, the rose comes through, accompanied by a bit of green. The spiciness is now only subtle to almost nonexistent, and the zest has disappeared, replaced by a nice powdery scent. Does anyone remember those Turkish rose-flavored chewing gums? As a child, they were available at the Turkish shop around the corner. And that's exactly how the fragrance now smells, like those rose chewing gums tasted, delicately rosy, slightly sweet, and very lightly spiced. But never typical of chewing gum; anyone who knows the gums will understand. It's basically rose water in chewing gum form. Considering how loooong it took me to get a few drops of this fragrance and how quickly I used to be at the shop around the corner :))) The scent remains delicate and rather close to the skin. After 4 hours, I have to put my nose directly on the skin to smell it. Is that it now? Is my childhood rose chewing gum fantasy trip to the past over? So it seems... It's a lovely scent experience. Unfortunately, it's hard to find and not cheap.

I am completely blown away...in a positive sense. One spray of "Kisses don't lie" and that was it. I am not a direct lover of rose scents; that’s more my mother’s domain, but here...I cannot deny my delight. This may be because the fragrance doesn’t start off rosy at all, and throughout, a powdery note skillfully keeps the rose in check. I can hardly keep my nose away from my wrist and keep thinking: Wow, wow, wow!!! Why is this fragrance only available in Russia?

"Bergdorf pour Femme" is also one of the commissioned creations that Roja Dove executes with great stylistic confidence every time. Just moments after application, the fragrance reveals the exclusive spaces, the magnificent ambiance of Bergdorf Goodman on New York's 5th Avenue: breathtaking, gleaming, and as stunningly luxurious from floor to floor as this successful fragrance composition. "Bergdorf pour Femme" not only shimmers, the scent radiates with impressive depth. And although "The American Way of Life" is not particularly close to my heart, I am once again delighted by what has been created here from a multitude of fragrance notes. Despite the unofficial subtitle "Gardenia Fragrance," which startled me a bit in hindsight, I am still fully engaged in conquering this fragrant glow. But first, this fragrance being conquers me! A light, zesty opening with bergamot greets me before I dive into one of the well-known yet always new fragrance explosions from this often controversial creator. Floral elegance prevails in the radiant heart of the fragrance, with the beloved May rose from Grasse dominating its rich center, illuminated by the intimately fragrant gardenia blossoms. With sensually feminine jasmine, bold dark violet, and noble white tuberose, Roja Dove remains true to his line, albeit rearranged and staged anew here. In the base, one encounters the now-familiar theme of fragrance notes; why turn away from success? Casually summarized and then almost randomly falling apart like Mikado sticks, aromatic woody, richly resinous-smoky, and animalistic-erotic fragrance nuances like vanilla and musk create a magnificent finale. For of course, a luxury shopping experience translated into fragrance on New York's 5th Avenue must lead opulently to ever new heights. "Bergdorf pour Femme" does not skimp on impressive "Oh!" and "Ah!" moments throughout its rich fragrance journey. As always, the great longevity allows each individual fragrance note the opportunity for the most beautiful personal unfolding before they are artfully intertwined into a whole. This Roja fragrance once again opens the door to a world of luxury, into which I love to dive again and again; this time thanks to Turandot's fragrance filling. Whether in Europe or here in America, it makes no difference: "Bergdorf pour Femme" also offers pure luxury in fragrant fascination.

HELP! Get me out of here! As soon as a tiny drop leaves the sprayer, I understand how a hedgehog must feel before hibernation. Around me, kilograms of flower petals. Noble, fragrant blooms, the best of the best, handpicked, flawless, rain down on me and bury me beneath them. Leaving this heap of flowers is not permitted for quite some time; there's only one thing to do: hold my nose and push through. However, I postpone my idea of quickly running to the bakery, as I'm not sure I could handle an additional scent of chocolate, cinnamon, fresh bread, and butter. Some other Rojas I’ve tested also overwhelm with this explosive start, so I bravely endure. Will I be rewarded for my courage? Well: Yes and No. Bergdorf transforms into an opulent floral explosion - yet still quite wearable, without immediately putting the surroundings into a floral coma. Just like other Rojas - especially the Extraits - the sillage relatively quickly returns to being well perceivable, but no longer filling the room. The luxurious floral richness is gradually complemented by resin, musk, and a hint of wood. Over time, Bergdorf develops this Roja-typical base that excites me, composed of tightly woven spices, flowers, and resins, where I can't clearly detect any single component. Here, one could quite confidently pass this scent off as one of the old Guerlains. As a hint, this Roja scent increasingly delights me. At Bergdorf, everything is very dignified from start to finish; for me, it feels less old-fashioned or vintage, but rather more conservative. In my opinion, Roja has perfectly catered to the audience one encounters at Bergdorf&Goodman - alongside tourists. Those looking for a perfectly crafted opulent floral bomb with a beautiful base that lingers on the skin will find themselves in the right place. For those of you familiar with some other Rojas: To me, Bergdorf is situated in the realm of Gardenia and Danger. My nose perceives Gardenia as a wonderful floral scent that I often wear at work and is well received by those around me - yet it comes across as a bit naïve and innocent. Danger is much more exciting for me, with a touch of lust and animalism - and I think more carefully about when I wear it. Bergdorf is more like Gardenia times three - and I can think of very few occasions in my life where I would find it perfectly fitting. However, I am sure it can be a wonderful signature scent for anyone who falls in love with it. Yet, despite all my admiration for the perfection it radiates, Bergdorf could not conquer my heart. Lastly, I must note: While I always preach that the distinction between men's and women's fragrances is for the Hugo, with this lush, rounded floral scent, where a Sophia Loren immediately springs to mind and not an Arnold Schwarzenegger, I find myself pondering quite a bit…

In the creation of this extraordinarily noble fragrance, Roja Dove had the vibrant, stylish, and exciting Manhattan in mind. He wanted to create something stunningly feminine and sensual. First and foremost, I am enveloped by a rich bouquet of flowers, a blend of the finest blooms, very elegant and well-selected. They wrap around my skin like a delicate powder cloud. But the scent is not simply floral, patchouli and the noble woods provide a solid foundation so that it does not take off and dissipate without leaving something behind. It becomes warm, soft, and wonderfully melds with the skin. Yet it remains very seductive and has that unmistakable Roja elegance. In New York Concrete jungle where dreams are made of There's nothing you can't do. Now you're in New York, These streets will make you feel brand new Big lights will inspire you. .....Alicia Keys would probably say..:)

Long name, short fragrance pyramid, even shorter realization: this (still) rather under-the-radar Kilian is sexy as hell and knows what it's doing! Especially between the sheets... but actually everywhere else too! "Yes I Was Madly In Love, But That Was Yesterday" is a spectacularly fruity-dry leather stunner from which there is hardly any escape. Raspberry kisses charred black leather and delivers slightly latex-like whip cracks. A head cinema scent. Hot and greasy, dirty and raunchy, rough and angular. It definitely polarizes, can surely get annoying quickly, but I find it a lot of fun. Dominant and playful at the same time. In comparison, Christian Grey and his playmate seem like the Care Bears... although, they usually do. This Kilian is no poser and comes dangerously close to the real deal. A hot fragrance, a true raspberry explosion in the top note. Then it quickly becomes drier, more serious, and more mature, without completely losing its sweetness and wink. The quality is already given with Kilian. Close to kitsch and trash, but mostly damn seductive and positively enticing. Something new! It can only hurt... Bottle: kitschy but cool Sillage & Longevity: a true dominatrix with far-reaching consequences. Double digits in terms of endurance. Conclusion: highly erotic, slightly wicked, exotically intrusive and fruitily frivolous - Yes, I am in love and will still be tomorrow! SM ecstasy. Bunga Bunga party in the ball paradise.

Why irresistible? Normally, after a sharing decanting session (here filling 6 pens in a row), I usually don't feel like the scent anymore. But what did I spray on myself the next morning? - with pleasure - yes, again with Madly in Love. Somehow it doesn't let me go, and I could spray it on in the morning and evening without it annoying me, boring me, or becoming too much. But let's get to the scent. The top note: It roughly goes in the direction of Black Perfecto. But it's not quite as sweet and fruity. Without licorice and rose and with less leather. It's a combination of pleasant fruitiness, just about bearable sweetness, a lot of light smoke, and, as I perceive it, a pinch of black pepper. The heart note: Smoke and sweetness decrease, the raspberry is still there. The jammy note from Back to Black joins in (a combination of honey and plum jam, in my opinion). The base note: Basically the heart note with a splash of Black Phantom and a lot of smoke. And everything connects wonderfully and captivatingly. It becomes softer but at the same time more radiant. Black leather smells different to me, but smoke and light, dry wood fit. The raspberry occasionally flashes through. Although from the base, I wonder if I wouldn't have guessed rhubarb in a blind test. Longevity and sillage: A drop is enough to clearly scent an entire office including the hallway for 2 hours. I can't complain about the longevity either. Assessment of the scent: It qualifies as niche, but I could imagine it being very well received by the general public. The more often I wear it, the higher the rating… The bottle: Looks chic and high-quality. The round glass ball stands on its head. The phrase “Yes I was…” is on all four sides of the cap. The sprayer is easy to use. I was able to decant quite quickly and easily without a funnel.

The opening features strong orange blossoms with their slightly bitter sweetness, quickly followed by an equally powerful mix of jasmine, tuberose, and gardenia. For 2-3 hours, "Scandal" presents itself on me as a true floral bomb. Very creamy white and floral-sweet, but unfortunately also a bit cloying, as both slightly perceptible indolic accents resonate and the floral cream overall becomes very, very warm, which pushes the entire scent to the edge of being overly warm or cloying for me. To my dismay, some perfumers often equate femininity with the scent of indolic white flowers; I've noticed this negatively not only with the Supreme scents from YSL like "Supreme Bouquet," but also with several other perfumes labeled as ultra-feminine, and so it is with this fragrance here, which, although 90% pleasantly floral, especially appears very feminine due to the tuberose, still carries this unclean note that reminds me of unventilated boudoirs or overly made-up ladies in heavy fur coats (although this scent is not nearly as distinctly indolic as "Supreme Bouquet"). After about 2 hours, however, it gets better; it gets properly aired out! Once the cloying phase is over, fresher floral notes emerge in the form of freesia, a clean rose, and fresh lily of the valley. With their help, the somewhat too warm floral scent transforms into a soft-floral and lovely companion with a sweet but clean tuberose, warm jasmine, a spicy freesia, and a fresh and clean-smelling rose (which I only perceive very faintly as a rounding note). Clear lavender and clean musk should serve as additional "airers," while velvety sandalwood and powdery, slightly woody iris provide a very welcome, airy powderiness that lays over the creamy floral notes and lightens the dense scent. Conclusion: From a loud opening in the form of an extremely densely woven wreath of tuberose, gardenia, and jasmine to a somewhat too opulent, overly warm, and "madamish" white flower scent, to a soft, clean, and, in my opinion, elegant feminine floral fragrance that still offers a lush floral bouquet in the second half of the drydown, which then appears more colorful, varied, and at the same time airier and less oppressive. I find "Jardins de Bagatelle" by Guerlain similarly heavy in floral weight and densely creamy; however, the Guerlain is more pleasant for me from the start, as it is not indolic, overall fresher and more airy, even though it is not exactly lightweight, and easier to wear.

I have tried hard to like this fragrance but I have failed. The notes can be very pungent, particularly to non-arab noses. I generally adore rose-oud combinations but this one has been particularly challenging. It opens with a slightly spicy-powdery, salty-metallic, animalic note and proceeds to a dark and heavy leather-oud base with whiffs of a dark rose. Neither mass-appealing nor appropriate for daily use in my opinion. Longevity are sillage are very impressive; one spray ought to suffice. Overall, I can see why some people would find beauty in this perfume and call it a masterpiece, and I respect that opinion. Personally for me, I wish I could have my money back and spend it one something more palatable instead.

You were my first niche fragrance. I never would have thought in my earlier life that I would spend so much money on a perfume. In my youth, designer fragrances were already quite expensive for me. Actually, I only came across you because I had to use an Amazon gift card, so I browsed around and since I wanted a new perfume, I noticed you. Sweet, floral, creamy, that sounded good to me. So you arrived after 2 days and I unboxed you. What a wonderful feeling it was to unwrap such a luxurious scent... I sprayed you on my wrist and my shirt and it was love at first sniff. I smelled exactly what I expected. I love jasmine and orange blossom very much and I can smell them here as well. I also get the rose in the opening. The initial sweetness fades a bit in the dry down, and the fragrance, despite its sweet creaminess, has a fresh, well-groomed quality. I enjoy wearing it in everyday life and I think it suits many situations without being annoying or overpowering.

When it comes to Chypre fragrances, few do it better than @rojadove @rojaparfums . Whether you see it as a homage or a reinterpretation of the classics, his love letter to the genre shines through, always intriguing, sometimes breathtaking. I used to own Musk Aoud Parfum, and what a scent. But as gorgeous as it smelled, the performance was easily one of the weakest I’ve ever experienced. That’s where the Absolue Précieux comes in and it completely transforms the experience. It takes that same rich DNA and gives it depth, projection, and staying power, all without losing its signature elegance. It lingers in the air with a kind of refined intensity. This is a Chypre with oud at its heart, a timeless mix of bergamot, rose, ylang-ylang, and just a touch of jasmine. But what grabs you from the very first spray is that dark, musky, leathery ambrette accord. It’s dirty in the most luxurious way, regal, not rustic. It feels expertly crafted, like old-world opulence with modern finesse. If you’re into musks or Chypres, you owe it to yourself to smell this one. It’s a true gem and another masterpiece from Roja.

Hello everyone, Straight to the point without any detours or big BLABLA, I want to get right to the important 1, 2, 3 points in my opinion. First, let's address the reasoning behind the title. When I started this hobby in 1999, I told myself I would never buy a fragrance for 200 DM... In 2012, I accidentally discovered the niche world, and quickly my spending mindset became a wishful thinking... we soon moved towards the 300€ mark, and many of my NIshane (Prestige Collection) exceeded that with prices under 500€. Then I told myself I would never spend over 500€! Well... a few weeks/months ago, the "Alexandria II Anniversary | XerJoff" was released for 580€, and I bought that too... and NOW (!) I'm talking about a 1000€ fragrance... strange world... About 2 - 3 weeks ago, I received a leftover bottle of Musk Aoud Absolue Précieux from 2015... and WOW how beautiful is this?! What do we have here exactly? Describing this fragrance in a few words borders on a true majesty - insult, but I will try to keep it brief. We have here a LUXURY OUD fragrance with very very (!) little ANIMALIC notes, with other extremely high-quality woods, a spicy component of nutmeg and ambrette seeds - which act like a wonderful and light (final boss) musk, along with leather, and YES it does smell like chocolate in the drydown.... (Pure Love) (I also know some fragrances from EO and ALD, and their musk is really harsh..., here everything is easy/soft and truly completely fine, otherwise I wouldn't be talking about it like this!) The performance is (for me) when I talk about numbers, then we are in the "noticeable" 20h range (and more), even the sillage is still there after 14h, which is more than remarkable... A quick note on the packaging, the bottle, sprayer, cap, and so on, anything less than a 9 or 10 I consider to be NONSENSE. When it comes to the pure quality of the sprayers, only Chanel and Dior come close (no XJ, no PDM, no Nishane, and certainly not Amouage), and then maybe Clive Christian! Yes, everyone can see and evaluate the cap and the stones as they wish = it's a matter of taste, but the REST is top-notch! Regarding the price: I’m somewhat TIRED of talking about it, because it’s relative = just like my words..., but I am, among other things, a businessman, and at the end of the day, I also evaluate the overall package, and 1000€ for 30ml is not just sporty... you have to want it and be a FAN of the brand or the fragrance... I will NEVER say something like RECOMMENDATION TO BUY or buy THIS, but one must say..., it is indeed INSANELY GOOD! Is it worth it? NO! Do you need it urgently? NO! Is it good? YES MAN! Is it worth a TEST? Somehow yes... Would I honestly buy it again? Now that I have it and know it, I would probably be LYING if I said never, but let’s put it this way, if I find another leftover bottle at a fair price, I might not say no! Why? Such a special fragrance is only worn for very selected occasions (that's how it is for me). And if I were to wear it more often, its charm and magic would quickly fade - besides, you don’t spray 10 sprays of Musk Aoud Absolue Précieux , as it is simply too potent! That’s why it will also last a WHILE ;) It is definitely worth a test! And now have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______

Rojas Aoud perfume collection is a delight for the senses of all those who are open and curious about dark, earthy-dirty oud scents. Just discovering the deep dark “Aoud,” the golden “Amber Aoud,” the so unusual “Fruity Aoud,” and also “Musk Aoud” was a sensual pleasure for me. And now as a culmination: “Musk Aoud Absolue Précieux” - this is chocolate oud at its finest! So-called “rose-oud” nuances have surprisingly captured me quickly; but I was not prepared for this deep dark and dirty and slightly oily chocolate variant, refined with rose petals; I didn’t even know such a thing existed! This deep oud-dripping, viscous dark brown is pierced by bright splashes of fruity bergamot and lemon scent fragments; thus, beautiful light reflections are created, akin to cut gemstones. In addition to the already mentioned rich May rose aromas from the flower fields of Grasse, we also encounter the radiant white splendor of intensely fragrant jasmine and cheerfully glowing ylang-ylang flower vines. The already awakened scent desire is transformed into a truly luxurious experience by a pompous and rich base. With sophistication, all the fragrance notes of the previous composition are added: Powerful spicy oak moss notes meet earthy, gold-brown veined patchouli, intensely fragrant noble woods, and musky spiced, very dark leather: A rich blend of the finest quality! My senses are already vibrating as the noble sandalwood aroma lightly brushes against them, and they are ready to absorb before warm, erotic vanilla with rich tonka bean sweetness and animalic-infused soft musk dosage unfolds its full beauty in rich waves. “Roja luxury at its best!” envelops with extraordinary depth and intensity for several hours, with new scent soundscapes continuously emerging, which connect with the utmost refinement in an impressive manner. “Musk Aoud Absolue Précieux” is not only a suitable and passionate companion for the cool nights ahead. I encounter a fascinating magician in fragrance, who truly lives up to his name and has immediately and completely enchanted me.

No, the headline is meant to be quite positive, no panic ;-P It’s really not easy to describe this scent.... Shortly after spraying, I perceive a rather filthy note... sweet-animalistic and quite wicked... slightly dark and dirty, yet very sexy.... not a musty oud, but real luxurious dirt! It is followed by a wonderful and fine freshness - something like mint, but that’s not really it.... it feels fresh and cool, yet the scent overall is warm.... I can also detect oak moss, which brings in a chypre edge, slightly musty.... like old wood - slightly charred - after a long rain..... really hard to explain.... Later, the scent becomes finer and softer... musk increasingly comes to the forefront, soft, sweet, and heavenly delicate.... yet strong and powerful! The scent is truly very complex and is somehow always "in motion"... every time I sniff again, I "discover something new".... The Musk Aoud AP is a bit wilder, more wicked, and more animalistic compared to the Amber Aoud AP.... dark, mysterious, and dirty.... A wonderful masterpiece has been created here, really.... hats off and into the "dirt" ;-)

Fetish (Parfum) opens with an orange-green citric petitgrain with significant ashy green oakmoss support before quickly moving to its heart. As the composition moves to its early heart the ashy green oakmoss takes the fore for an hour or so, gradually ceding the starring role to very leathery castoreum rising from the base that grows in intensity as time passes, supported by hints of cinnamon, deep clove and a subtle, primarily tuberose driven white floral accord. During the late dry-down the leathery castoreum fades as restrained cedarwood is unveiled with the remnants of the oakmoss turning slightly powdery in support through the finish. Projection is good and longevity slightly above average at about 10 hours on skin. Fetish (Parfum) was a composition I sampled without any expectations one way or another. The "Pour Homme" version was supposed to be a big leather composition along the lines of Puredistance M, but I found it more woody than leathery in truth. After the surprise with its "Pour Homme" counterpart, I really wasn't expecting the significant leathery castoreum focus of the mid-section of Fetish here, but that is exactly what I got. What I also found surprising was the amount of ashy oakmoss found in the composition. In this age of dreaded IFRA restrictions, I honestly don't know how the folks at Roja Dove pulled it off. The ashy oakmoss and leather really work well together in Fetish, though I have to wonder if the composition marketed to Women could have easily been marketed more as unisex (or dare I say even as a masculine). If there is any real minor deficiency (apart from the above average performance metrics that are less than I would expect from a high quality parfum concentration), it would have to be in the late dry-down as the natural cedar driven finish smells excellent but is nothing new. All-in-all, I think I prefer its Pour Homme counterpart, but Fetish (Parfum) is largely successful as a very classically structured chypre with top-notch ingredients that one might have expected was released before IFRA meddling. The bottom line is the $480 per 50ml bottle Fetish (Parfum) could use a bit more oomph with its performance metrics (and a lower price point), but it represents a largely successful blast from the past that will appeal to Men and Women alike, earning a "very good" 3.5 stars out of 5 and a solid recommendation.

None of us would seriously claim to be enslaved! No, we are all emancipated and so free ... Roja's "Enslaved" questions all of that! Aren't we all, those of us wandering around here, slaves to our desire for scents? Aren't we all in more or less fragrant chains, to which we even tug from time to time? I must honestly answer this question in the affirmative for myself! I knew this even before I got to know "Enslaved" - many thanks to the donor of this sample! A surprisingly fruity top note greets me: I feel like I'm strolling through a grove of shady citrus trees, their fruits ripe and invitingly fragrant: voluptuous, ripe, and fragrant! How much I love the scent of the garden carnation (symbolically: the flower of the betrothed) is well known. Its spiciness delights me time and again - not only due to nostalgic feelings: after all, the carnation bouquet was obligatory for coffee invitations back in the day! Rose geranium always scratches me a bit at first, but here it is quickly dominated by the power of the gigantic jasmine blossom: but "Hello!" - this "flower goddess" deserves the stage! A somewhat old-fashioned rose in this composition exudes its enchanting scent; the tenderness of the orange blossom caresses not only heart and soul - no, all the senses! A golden web of ylang-ylang (one of my special loves!) is woven over the previous scent tapestry; it's really magic! The base of this enslaving fragrance creation is simply dreamy: oak moss and vetiver provide a great sense of earthiness: dark green, lush, moist, and incredibly sensual! The erotic vanilla meets the often slightly powdery iris: they enter into a partnership that is always touching! The air vibrates - "panta rhei": everything moves; the senses are awakened! Musk stimulates, labdanum lightly scrapes at the already sensitive surface of heart and soul: Hello! Are you ready?? The spicy, silky-sensual cedar envelops with wide-open arms and whispers: "Come, come to me!" What remains is: unconditional surrender! Surrender to a golden magic - amber closes a fragrance circle that touches heart and soul: it is accomplished! For several months, I have been a slave to my not always desired feelings. Maybe that's why it is so easy for me to follow "Enslaved" - to give myself up completely: for many, many hours! My acquaintance with Roja is still young, and I am notoriously very critical! But still: I am completely devoted to "Enslaved"! Maybe my feelings here follow a kind of "unconditional surrender" - who knows? Maybe I am addicted; maybe I am trying to capture dreams: "Enslaved" realizes dreams! Gags, demands, binds - makes one dependent! And leaves one extremely happy; at the same time also extremely unhappy! "Unconditional Surrender" - that is it! Is it? "Enslaved" stands for no half-measures - it enslaves! Completely and ruthlessly! Scruples are unknown to this fragrance being! Those who are not ready to surrender should keep their distance! "Enslaved" takes and gives: ruthlessly and yet generously! Roja created a fragrance here that takes and at the same time gives with both hands One must not be fearful: this fragrance demands everything - but it also gives everything! My soul and my heart have been in chains for quite some time: "Enslaved" is symbolic of that! "Be careful!" says the ever-present mind; "Let it be!" and "Follow me!" says the feeling! Really: It's your own choice! But think: "The Winner takes it all!" (The Loser's standing small beside the Victory...) It's your life (say what you are and what your heart beats for ..) My heart, be careful!

Enslaved?! How does one come up with such names? What may sound controversial at first (probably especially for Americans with their past in slavery) is actually related to the fragrance. One is a slave to the scent because it is so good that one cannot get rid of it, etc... Roja himself said he wanted to create a fragrance that enslaves you upon smelling it, meaning that you become a prisoner of love. Ugh,… how cheesy that sounds :D Well, anyway, you’ve probably already seen from my title what I had to think of again. And that’s Leia from Star Wars (Episode VI), where she is in a damn hot slave costume while being Jabba’s prisoner. And besides, Leia is just one of the coolest female characters! Forget Rey from the new films, or Padme from the second trilogy, neither of them could ever hold a candle to Leia, at least in my opinion :D … oh, I could ramble on about Star Wars forever, and I don’t even particularly like most of the films, yes, you wouldn’t have thought that, would you?? But I don’t want to digress further and scare you off again, no, I want to tell you a bit about this fragrance here, or rather, how it smells and whether you really become a prisoner of love when you smell it… The Scent: The fragrance starts right away with a multitude of scent notes. In the rising scent cloud, you mostly perceive “only” resinous notes with cloves and neroli, sweet jasmine, and general floral notes, but upon closer sniffing, you can discern a bit more. First of all, there are the cloves, which give off a slightly spicy scent, but they also fit well with the somewhat heavier floral notes that remind one of ylang-ylang, but smell less cloying. Neroli is one of the main scent notes, at least in my opinion, as I can perceive this note very well, just like the resinous scents, which should come from labdanum. At the beginning, there is also a slightly dry-floral note (but I don’t mean stuffy) in the background, which gradually disappears. Also, quite early on, the oakmoss appears, which becomes stronger as the fragrance develops. By the way, I can hardly perceive the citrus notes listed in the top notes. Towards the end, the fragrance becomes softer and softer. You still smell resinous notes with neroli and a little clove, while the jasmine gradually bids farewell, and in its place, beautiful amber appears, which continues the sweetness of the fragrance. Since the scent is now slightly softer than at the beginning, upon closer sniffing, it also seems a bit powdery, but well, that’s probably due to the iris and vanilla :) It’s actually a beautiful scent, but it also comes across as a bit old-fashioned, and you get the feeling that you’ve had such scents under your nose before. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is good, as one is used to from Roja. The sillage is even initially very good, as I could smell the fragrance very well with my arms outstretched. As the fragrance develops, the sillage does weaken a bit, but only in comparison to many other Roja fragrances that remain stronger for longer. However, with this fragrance, you are definitely very noticeable. The longevity is also reliably long, and you can definitely smell the fragrance for more than ten minutes. The Bottle: The bottle is rectangular and looks damn high-quality. According to the description, the bottles are made in various countries and contribute to luxury, as the golden elements like the writing on the sides of the bottle and the gold of the cap are said to be made of real gold (or gold particles mixed with metal). The places for the Swarovski crystals on the cap seem to be sealed, so it appears that no crystals were used here as in the perfume variant of the scent. The brand name is on the neck of the bottle, the label is also gilded, and overall, the bottle is quite high-quality and beautiful, although there are prettier bottles (for example, I much prefer the bottles where the crystals are embedded in the cap). So, this scent is also successful and smells high-quality, as you can’t detect anything synthetic in it. My points of criticism would be the following two points: First, this scent has oakmoss, which not only has a subtle scent but comes across quite strongly, and thus the fragrance is certainly not for everyone who doesn’t like oakmoss, as it makes the scent seem a bit old-fashioned. And second, I must admit that the fragrance didn’t really come across as particularly special to me, but more like (or almost like) a 0815 scent, meaning a fragrance that smells good, but you’ve probably had it under your nose quite often already, possibly even with one or the other Roja fragrance. Therefore, the scent isn’t worth the many euros that are demanded for it (around 300-400 euros… for 50 mL!). But for those who are not bothered by all this, Enslaved offers a beautiful, classically and maturely smelling fragrance with sweet, floral, resinous, and soft notes, which would be especially good for lovely, elegant evenings. Especially on cooler days in autumn and winter. I myself will not become a prisoner of love through this fragrance (finding love will probably take a loooong time anyway :DD),… ugh, that sounds so cheesy with the prisoner of love…! So I’ll stop now and prefer to think about Star Wars again, because I’ve been thinking about it more often lately, especially since I built a spaceship from the films out of Lego and am now eyeing a new lightsaber. And don’t say ANYTHING, absolutely NOTHING, I know myself that I’m nerdy, so pssssssst!!!! So, have a nice evening and see you next time :)

This version is a more romantic and spring-like interpretation of the original Princess. It smells like rose flavored marshmallows sprinkled with matcha. I can't detect any ginger though. Princess Rose de Mai is powdery, soft, a bit sweet and perfect for spring time. Longevity is good (around 8 hours) and the sillage sits rather close - you'll be able to smell and enjoy yourself but likely won't distract anyone around. I personally like this one so much that I have made it my 2020 spring signature.

...............the ambulance opened the door, the injured woman was pushed inside. It was not a pretty sight. After a marital dispute: the man complained about the many scents and bottles of his wife that were scattered everywhere, she lamented about his miserable football games on television............one word led to another, the woman raged............bottles flew, she threw the slippers.......then it ended in blood. Due to the noise of the shattering bottles and the screaming, the neighbors called the police, the emergency services were alerted............a battlefield of shattered glass awaited the responders and it smelled as if one were being showered from all sides with x fragrances in a perfumery, the television was still on. A little later in the hospital...........the woman was still screaming and crying, but she did not remove her hand from her forehead, where a bottle was stuck. "Doctor Kilian please to the emergency room, Doctor Kilian, please to the emergency room......... immediately!" the announcement echoed .........the woman had this beautiful bottle, a golden sphere that is usually placed in the cap. That was the last bottle the man managed to grab before the police arrived, before the argument ended. However, the cap did not stay put and so the man rammed the bottle with the cap into his wife's forehead, just above the left eye socket, digging a furrow above the eyebrow .......... the nasty dent was not yet visible, but blood was dripping from the wound. The bottle was still firmly held in the woman's hands.............she simply would not let it go. "Maaaaiiiiiin darling" one could hear her murmur the whole time.........."maaaaiiiiin darling", she contorted her face in pain. She was like possessed and could not be moved to let go of the bottle. Dr. Kilian had no choice, a dose of Hallol intravenously for the lady and she could finally be properly treated on her head. Her last words were supposedly "I don't need a prince by my side to be a princess!" Rose de Mai is sweet, through the marshmallows, rosy, a bit of ginger is also in there and maybe a few drops of tea. If you leave the cap off, the bottle looks like a bomb and so is the scent - loud!

The bottle looks great. High-quality and absolutely not run-of-the-mill. The golden ball is nice to look at and makes quite an impression. The title of the fragrance also caught my attention. I thought it would scream, "HERE I AM AND I DON'T NEED A PRINCE!" Now to the scent. After reading the description, I was a bit skeptical. Normally, I prefer sweet scents. And then I saw ginger and tea. The description somehow intrigued me. A very lovely perfumer exchanged with me, so I held the fragrance in my hands a few days later. I unboxed it and was simply afraid of being disappointed. The first spray. Unfortunately, it was just as I expected. I smelled it right away and immediately detected something fresh. Something that didn't fit at all into my collection. A few hours later I smelled it again, and suddenly it smelled sweet. But not sugary sweet, rather fresh-sweet. The floral note was just right, not too synthetic or too intense. I suddenly liked it a little. Maybe I just needed to get used to this freshness? Mh, I gave it another chance the next day to convince me. And I must say, it succeeded. It is fresh and sweet at the same time. Just right for everyday wear or work. It doesn't scream "Here I am," but is still noticeable and present. It holds surprisingly well on me. Confident, free, young. Just like a princess. I really like it now as it can be worn daily. However, I would say it is better suited for spring/summer due to the freshness it offers. It may not have been love at first "sight," but definitely at second!

Yesterday was our anniversary and my husband was feeling generous. He willingly followed me to Douglas and let me browse in peace. Oh - Kilian is now on the shelves! The long but beautiful name made me smile. And the scent also reveals itself to be humorous and cheerful. Fortunately, the ginger is not sharp, but harmoniously adapts to the full rose. Then it becomes lovely with the sweet May rose - gently surrounded by a bright teen note. The marshmallow note feels delicious and attractively playful. Little Tina does not want to be picked up from the Douglas children's paradise. No, she wants to ponder this interesting scent. This transition from initial elegance to playfulness is quite unique. But I'm still considering a purchase. I then gladly received Assam of India by Berdoues as a gift.

Some time ago, I received a sample of "Encke" by TT with the purchase of another fragrance. When I first sprayed the scent, I immediately realized that I would not warm up to it. The fragrance starts off very spicy and ends in the drydown with an overdose of labdanum, sandalwood, and a bit of musk. The scent DNA is almost piercing to my nose. It even crosses into the realm of being unbearable over time! Sillage is still very good, but with this fragrance combination and its longevity, it's hardly tolerable for those around you. The bottle is the only positive!

Christmas Eve was a proper occasion to finally wear 51 pour Homme as an EdP. It’s just too precious for the office and unfortunately a bit inappropriate in summer. No, this is definitely a candidate for special situations and suitable climatic conditions, the latter being more likely found in autumn or winter. Some might wickedly claim that it’s well-suited for Halloween, but let’s not get ahead of ourselves ;-) Admittedly, the opening of 51 pour Homme is quite animalistic-stable-like. Despite the usual Roja Dove citrus top note, which somewhat tempers the start, this could be an almost insurmountable hurdle for many. Those who are brave and endure will experience minute by minute how the creation softens, leaving only a slightly rough leather note from the stable-like opening, which blends with the other opulent ingredients into a spicy-oriental fragrance. The citrus notes remain quite perceptible for a long time and give the whole composition a sprightliness that is not often encountered in conjunction with oud and leather. What remains in the end until the dry down is more of a warm leather note with a timid oud undertone, embedded in an oriental-tinged woody to spicy mix including a slightly bitter twist. Nevertheless, shortly after spraying, I wondered if I had really made a good choice to visit my father for dinner, as the stable note would definitely catch his attention and he wouldn’t be able to hold back a comment. However, everything turned out positively, which may also be due to the fact that the projection, in my opinion, was relatively subdued. Accordingly, he appreciated 51 pour Homme on my wrist as a quite pleasant and noble scent. Regardless, the Eau de Parfum is rightly rated so highly in general assessments. Of course, a comparison with the perfume version would be quite welcome, as it not only achieves a higher score here but is even classified as spicy-leathery. That’s intriguing!

Yes, Roja is always a little challenge for me, and I find it exciting to test this brand again! It's often not quite easy, as the scents are very complex and quite intense. I have already embraced many of them in my heart, while some I have removed from my mind because they were simply too overwhelming! Recently, it was time for the 51 p.H. There are both the EdP and the perfume version available. I tested both and find them very similar, but somehow I find this one a bit finer and more suitable for me. As soon as it is sprayed on, you can tell what you are dealing with. A very noble and interesting elixir that you can't help but keep sniffing. A blend of bright, slightly sour, and also sweet fruits mingle with the finest floral notes sprinkled with a hint of strong spices. The lavender occasionally stands out slightly and then retreats again. Oud, in my opinion, is very restrained here and very pleasant. The finest leather becomes more apparent as time goes on, quite strong and dark but also very pleasant and not too dark. I see a large glass in front of me, filled with a very expensive cognac, me half reclining on an ottoman made of medium brown leather standing on a creaking wooden floor, a pipe in hand filled with vanilla tobacco, and jazz music playing in the background. It has a flair from the 40s-50s. An incredibly wonderful and fine scent that invites me to dream. I believe I wouldn't wear this outside, but rather at home when I want to relax and take a little time travel. It's actually a men's fragrance, but I think women can wear it well too if they like it a bit stronger and spiced. Longevity and sillage are typically superb for Roja; I can perceive the scent on me for over 10 hours, with the first 3-5 hours being quite strong before it pulls back a bit. In my opinion, it's a scent that can be worn throughout the year; perhaps it will come across a bit differently on cooler days, which I still need to test, as I only know it on quite warm days. I will savor my sample carefully, as unfortunately, the scent is no longer available in the EdP version.

It doesn't happen very often that one changes their signature scent. At least not for me. So far, it has always been fragrances that do something to me. Beyond the pyramid and the olfactory. Beyond known scales. They make my inner resonance body vibrate. A wonderful form of self-induced external influence. So, when I am to describe 51 pour homme EDP, I am not the analytical chemist, nor a connoisseur of the field who can characterize and classify the naturalness of bergamot. Fragrances are - despite their absolutely identical composition in the bottle - something very subjective when experienced. Upon spraying the EDP, I am always overcome by a deep calm. An inexplicable feeling of lightness. I have only experienced something similar with Spice and Wood. I, the fan of orientals. A bit like arriving after a long journey. Grateful for the experiences I have had and the reward found in the simple being of the moment. Indeed, signature. Essence of the self. Olfactorily, the 51 EDP starts with a fresh, almost fruity note, which never tips into a specific direction or becomes explicitly sweet or identifiable with a fruit that one could attribute this experience to. Very quickly, base accords come in that suggest subtle leather and a sensual, swirling oud. Yes, the pyramid should rather be read as what will gradually say goodbye to notes over the next 12 hours. For the appearance is a complete one. The entire pyramid says "Hello" and has come to stay. Profile: fresh-spicy-sensual. In all of this, there is an incredibly calm yet focused essence. Distinguised and yet completely unpretentious. A pool of possibilities. Eager to see what you want to experience. Just as multifaceted as you are individually. A magnifying glass for the moments that matter. PS: My title is a quote from Sorcha Richardson's - Last Train, which is currently alternating between the original and the Lexer Remix playing for me. Call: "shot gun!" in your car Don't care where Drive me far Out of the city with the windows down Somewhere where we can't be found Spend this sun and months Learning how to hunt

Right at the opening, there is a slightly fruity rose spiked with cardamom and saffron. The more I wear this, I am unsure whether the fruitiness at the top is coming from the Turkish rose used or if it's one aspect of the tobacco leaves I am picking up. It is spicy and warm, but a little bit austere. It's definitely a masculine-leaning rose. Then comes a warm, slightly rubbery incense and tons of damp, moldy patchouli. It kind of smells like the inside of an old church - gloomy, moldy, dusty, slightly smoky from burned incense, and yet at the same time, uplifting. The real wonder of the scent, though, is the tobacco. It smells wonderfully dry, fruity, papery, toasty, like sheaves of tobacco leaves laid out to dry in the sun, their enticing aroma filling the air for miles around. In Criminal of Love, I am astonished and touched to find one of the truest portraits of real tobacco I have smelled outside of Tabac Aurea. It is genius the way the dry, woody aspects of tobacco leaf are accentuated by the papery smell of the papyrus note.

Criminal of Love - Verbrecher der Liebe I don't know why, but when the word "love" appears in fragrance names, I associate it with something sweet and gentle. However, most of the time they are rather harsh, floral scents, which surprises me. Maybe I just have a different "understanding" of it. * Well, anyway, when I see the bottle, which is black-golden and egg-shaped, it somehow reminds me of Marquis de Sade. Mysterious, dangerous, sensual, aggressive, and passionate. Although I don't necessarily associate passionate with sex! Marquis de Sade is considered sadistic, pornographic, and disreputable. But actually, his book is about virtue, incest, maternal hatred, and the improvement of morals! Actually, because time and again, erotic tales, intrigues, and the whole arsenal of depravity appear. But what does that have to do with "Criminal of Love"? In that sense, nothing. But if you read the fragrance notes, you can already recognize one or two words of depravity in a positive sense.
