CoL is not a "depraved" scent and also not a scent for "man-eating" women. But it has something very special and thus comes across as very self-assured and "tight". Right at the beginning, the nose is enveloped by sweet-spicy, ethereal oil that exudes cardamom. Saffron, on the other hand, has a slightly citrus-spicy note reminiscent of ginger, very aromatic. A spice mist like at a bazaar. Indian papyrus is said to smell woody. Well, the scent has woody undertones, but whether that is really due to papyrus? I would rather attribute it to the Atlas cedar and immortelle. Woody, spicy, herbaceous, yes exactly! That fits. Oh the rose and the incense... beautiful, pure, and radiant red, a rosy scent like real roses that you sniff in the wild. Slightly sweet as well. Then the incense, so clarifying, pure, smoky, and resinous at the same time. Not heavy or overwhelming, but floating around the scent. Patchouli - oh no, not really my thing, but here I only smell it subtly, far in the background. One might think that as the body temperature rises, THEN something earthy comes under the nose, but only then. CoL is an exciting scent and surely attracts a few with a sniffing nose to their own neck ;-) It is woody-herbaceous, slightly rosy-sweet, and becomes softer the longer you wear it. It doesn't get close to the body, but is always present. Thus, it has recognition value for me - definitely. BUT, I don't know which fragrance note it is - I think it's the rose, patchouli, and cedar - but after a while, a sweaty note develops. Sharp and not nice. But I will continue to test it. Maybe it's more suitable for winter!

Hello everyone, Tonight, I would like to share a few words about Aoud Absolue Précieux . I have all 3 (crazy luxury = I know), but each of the fragrances represents something, and I find that really wonderful! Amber Aoud Absolue Précieux = the sweet oriental ;) Musk Aoud Absolue Précieux = the most angular of the three Aoud Absolue Précieux = the most elegant and classic/simple Is it simply equally bad and boring? In certain cases, yes, but here I am absolutely saying no! But why? Honestly, I have tested nearly 100 (!) Rose - Oud fragrances in almost 25 years (!) and have encountered everything from very, very affordable ("Oud Mood (Eau de Parfum) | Lattafa / لطافة" to some from EO, like "EO N°3 (Pure Parfum) | Ensar Oud / Oriscent", so I know my way around "somewhat". In any case, about 80% always have a disturbing component that they work with, such as caramel, a green-herbaceous touch, dried fruits, too much honey, too many (dried) fruits, or jasmine. Here, "thankfully", it is almost a pure Rose - Oud fragrance of the highest QUALITY. Yes, it becomes increasingly sweeter in the drydown, due to the saffron ;), but the existing notes are a backdrop and never come to the forefront, in the sense that one can say = "ah, that is xyz", one might still smell the leather note in the drydown after x hours. It starts rosy with the oud, it transforms a bit over time = at first it is medicinal, then a bit drier with the leather, and in the drydown, as I said, the SAFFRON comes through, and from then on it becomes quite similar to the beginning. Just without the medicinal oud. Rose - saffron - wood in beautiful, noble, and nearly perfect... For me, it is a work of art, a truly real one! And when I think that it has been discontinued.... -_- The performance is (for mine) when I talk about numbers, then we are in the "noticeable" 14h range (and more), even the sillage is still there after 10h, and that is more than remarkable... A quick note about the packaging, the bottle, the sprayer, the cap, and so on, anything less than a 9 or 10 I consider to be NONSENSE. When it comes to the pure quality of the sprayers, only Chanel and Dior compare (no XJ, no PDM, no Nishane, and certainly not Amouage), and then maybe Clive Christian! Yes, anyone can see and evaluate the cap and the stones as they wish = it is a matter of taste, but the REST is top-notch! Regarding the price: I am somewhat TIRED of talking about it because it is relative = just like my words..., but I am also a businessman, and at the end of the day, I evaluate the overall package, and 1000€ for 30ml is not just sporty..., one has to want it and be a FAN of the brand or the fragrance..., I will NEVER say something like BUY RECOMMENDATION or buy THIS, but one must say..., it is indeed INCREDIBLY GOOD! Moreover, it is such that you cannot "credibly" explain to an average-earning person that they should buy a fragrance for (almost) 1000€. That is certainly no "shooooot", but I just mean ;). Is it worth it? NO! Do you need it urgently? NO! Is it good? YES, MAN! Is it worth a TEST? Somehow, yes... Would I honestly buy it again? Now that I have it and know it, I would probably be LYING if I said never, but let me put it this way, if I find another leftover bottle at a fair price, I might not say no! Also, since I know it has been discontinued.... Why? Such a special fragrance is only worn for very selected occasions (that's how it is for me). And if I were to wear it more often, its charm and magic would quickly fade - besides, one doesn't spray 10 sprays of it - it is simply too potent! That's why it will also last a WHILE ;) It is definitely worth a test! And now have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______

After I wanted to test the Aouds from Roja, except for the Musks, and have done so, I would like to briefly share my thoughts with you. This one, the Aoud Absolue Precieux (AP), represents pretty much the culmination, the throne. I also tested the "regular" Amber Aoud (AA) and the Amber Aoud Absolue Precieux (AAP). I skipped the regular Aoud due to the supposed stinky Aoud, and now that I know the Precieux, that was probably the right decision. This one, the AP, moves confidently and straightforwardly. While the Ambers play with fig and a lot of fruit, the AP comes in, unmistakably, saying I am the boss here. A bit herbal, slightly musty Oud (the emphasis is on slightly, making it quite bearable and reasonable to wear) comes with a nice but muted citrus note. Soon, flowers mix in, and that stays like this for many hours. In the drydown, dream notes emerge, soft, slightly fruity, a bit sweet, simply wonderful. Sillage, as is often the case with these ultra-concentrated fragrances, is strong but still manageable and wearable. Still, less is more here; 1-2 sprays are completely sufficient. I once had 3, which was definitely too much, as the Oud becomes overwhelming in the first hour. Longevity is incredible, not as intense as an OSM or Air Tiger but 1-2 levels below that. Whom do I recommend which fragrance? I cannot recommend the AAP. It has the grandiose fig of the regular one but very muted, and this is mainly what distinguishes the two lines. Moreover, I don't understand why I should pay €30 or more for a ml of it. The regular AA has more unique features, is significantly cheaper, and it also comes in the Crystal version, because the brown juice you get here is really intense; the Precieux are even syrupy and slightly stain my wrist after spraying. So directly wearing a white shirt over it or in the hair and off into the beige leather of the convertible is not really the way to go and recommendable. And then, as I said, the AP comes around the corner, hard shell, soft core, unbelievable quality, and makes statements with slightly barn-like Oud but still an incredibly soft development. Is it worth it? Of course not; it's probably not a fragrance worth €30+ for a ml, but I’m still glad I dared to try it because you simply have to experience it.

I have long known that you exist, Aoud A.P., but I always enjoyed myself with your younger brother, Amber Aoud A.P. Amber Aoud A.P. is wonderfully soft, velvety, delicately animalistic, and a real charmer... Amber Aoud A.P. is liquid gold, caressing me, kissing me, and carrying me in its arms... yes, that is Amber Aoud A.P. And you, my dear Aoud A.P.... you are older and more mature.... you are a bit more complex.... a bit grumpy.... not a romantic... no, you are more the "bad boy"... wild, arrogant, captivating, tough as nails... you tolerate no competition.... When I met you, you completely caught me off guard, did not charm me sweetly, no flowers to greet me.... no romantic words, no fancy rendezvous... no, straight to the point...! You are wild, impetuous, but you still have a loving side... you just need a little time to open up... once the beast is calmed, you can also be cuddly and tender.... outwardly, you would never admit that.... only those who really know you understand that you have an almost soft core... yes, almost, because the wild daredevil comes out every now and then and shows who is boss... With you, I feel protected.... warmed.... but I am always on guard..... you are a moody creature.... Even though you need to be enjoyed with caution, I have fallen in love with you, my Aoud A.P. And yes, I love your brother, Amber Aoud A.P. too... I can't help but love you both.... you are quite similar in certain ways, yet you are so different.

This review is short and to the point. Received a sample and so glad I did not blind buy a bottle off Ebay. I would have been pissed. This is a cypriol bomb. I do not like cypriol dominant fragrances. This reminds me of when I blind bought Promise by Frederic Malle. This has the same medicinal cypriol oil. Majestic Aoud has no AOUD! null. It might have been a great move for Roja to discontinue this.

I don't write a lot of reviews on perfumes, but I'll go out of my way when something: 1. Blows my mind. 2. I feel that it is incredibly under the radar and it is amazing and should receive much more deserved attention. 3. It is hyped to death due to discontinuation and it's actually shit, or close to that. With Majestic Aoud, it's the latter. Not only do I find this to be a poor perfume and a very poor rendition and attempt at an oud accord, but the name, the Roja marketing, the few people hyping it, and the price just make this one a comedy through and through. I won't call Roja out saying there's no Oud in this. But to me, it certainly smells like none. This smells to me like the cheapest way to attempt an Oud accord, using the cypriol and patchouli combo. Classic and cheap way to do it. When I sprayed this, I immediately thought to myself, "Oh boy, I smelled this Oud before". It reminds me of the cheap oud accords one could find in designer houses, or most certainly in Robert Piguet's Oud. That one uses a similar Oud accord, heavily built around Patchouli and Cypriol. So, yeah, no Oud in here. I don't care what they say. Anyone who has a decent experience with natural oud, will not fall for it. So, the oud is out, you ain't getting it. Moreover, there's this annoying Amyris used in the base, also known as the poor man's sandalwood. So the idea of luxury gets shipwrecked further. Basically, the main notes that I get, and define this perfume to me are, the cypriol, patchouli, and amyris in the base, a bit of synthetic cviet, Osmanthus, and some aromatic elements in the opening. So, it is an aromatic-floral perfume, heavy on patchouli and cypriol. I can only imagine the disappointment in shelling 2000 USD for this stuff and smelling it for the first time. I think they pulled it off the shelves afraid of getting sued lol. I am no fan of this house, at all, but this one has to be the most disappointing one in the entire line, and I have tried almost all of them. That being said. As ridiculous as this perfume is, and as much as I disregard the house, I still ADORE Diaghilev and consider it one of the best Chypres ever created, even though heavily inspired by Mitsouko. That one is exceptional, and a top 20 perfumes ever for me. This one is disastrous, and the entire story around it makes it even worse. Please do not blindly buy this, get a sample first and save yourself the expense.

There it stood. A desert full of sand, with only the search for his own happiness and that of his men on his mind. Ali Baba knew he was in the right place. The cave that showed the way to happiness, its massive iron gates an insurmountable obstacle. He took a deep breath and spoke the magical words. SESAME !!! … ROLL ! But instead of the opening of the gates, the sand beneath his feet began to feel strangely loose. Quickly, it disappeared into the ground and Ali Baba along with it. A trapdoor let him fall into an endless black void, until he realized he was sliding down a rocky slide beneath the cave. In the end, he landed softly in the sand, which had probably not been touched by a human soul for centuries. Only a beam of light in the distance provided hope that he had not ended up in a lonely grave. The light fell directly on a golden balcony, ancient and finely decorated. Art from another time. On the balcony stood something he had never seen in his life, an intricately crafted transparent cube of glass. On the front was a metallic plaque showing an engraving. “Roja - Majestic Aoud” could be read. What is this? It looked so delicate, he had never seen anything like it in his life. A message from the future? It had to be something far removed from this time, an object of divine origin. Something that people would still worship for centuries to come. Majestic Aoud is not only majestic, it is a story, art, memories. Even the description of the scent does not do it justice; it only scratches the surface. At times, it even makes my beloved Nefs seem like a very Western creation. The scent is less accessible than the common oud fragrances and simultaneously sweeps the floor with most of them. For the majestic here is the oriental influence. A consistently delicate note of castoreum makes the scent demanding, elegant, and warm at the same time. Animalic, which fits perfectly into the DNA of the fragrance and makes it the most oriental of the Aoud series from Roja. Warm, balsamic, spicy, viscous. The honey-like liquid clings to the skin, blooms, and makes me rave. This is how I imagine the perfect oriental fragrance. The Sultan would be envious. Apart from the common oud-rose combinations, Roja manages to present me with a scent that hides the high-quality rose in the deep background. To stay in the vernacular, the rose gives “Roundness.” The second companion is in most cases saffron, which, with its typical aromas, plays a very supportive role, adding even more softness to the whole. While osmanthus unites balsamically, a hint of woodiness comes through in the background. No specific note, a weave of various aromas. Ethereal woodiness from rosemary, without the green part. Vetiver in delicate form, cypriol with its patchouli-like earthiness. Labdanum, which strengthens the animalic aspect while making it bearable. Majestic Aoud evokes memories of my travels in North Africa, as it would fit just as well in the palaces of the Arab Empire. A fragrance that could not better describe a specific region. Authentic, real, fitting. The Sultan listens with interest. A creation that, while it may not match the brutal longevity and sillage of other Rojas, will certainly draw attention with its distinctive DNA. Saffron, ambered spice, light oud, and castoreum. Ethereal woody, warm, and sticky. Yet in a way light on the skin. My perfect oriental scent. I would even sacrifice my Ombre Nomade and my Nefs for a bottle and would never feel guilty about it. I particularly enjoy the impression at the current temperatures when it is really warm. It hardly gets more beautiful and warmer, and it enhances the oriental impression. You are my doomed love affair. Discontinued. I want to cry, but I hope to see you sometimes in my collection.

On my skin, I only smell musk..., bright musk. Unfortunately, no flowers, no roses, no flowers at all. I thought... Because gradually, a pleasant soapy rose unfolds. However, the freshness is absent. Musk Butterfly lingers in this soapy creaminess for a few hours on the skin. The rose remains perceptible until the end. The sillage is good and pleasant. Those who enjoy delicate rose scents will find a truly well-crafted fragrance creation here.

I would love to give this wonderful scent a 9 or more everywhere, as it simply smells fantastic. It is and remains linear from start to finish. And that's exactly where the problem lies.... In the finish. It comes far too early. The scent itself is a knockout. Oud comes out beautifully, accompanied by lovely musk and vanilla, which makes it a bit creamy. Nutmeg shines through very nicely - beautifully spicy with a slight sweetness (I am crazy about coriander and nutmeg). Patchouli and cedar are not recognizable to my nose. However, I like the scent just as it is. I don't like fragrances with strong projection, so I appreciate that this scent does not radiate very strongly. For many, it will probably be too subtle. However, the longevity is unfortunately a bad joke. So, I said it. And having to formulate this sentence hurts so much, as the scent DNA is simply genius.

Risque (Parfum) opens with a slightly sweet citrus spiked airy rose and slightly powdery ylang-ylang tandem before moving quickly to its heart. As the composition enters its early heart the ylang-ylang takes the fore with the citrus and rose quickly receding, as it is joined by co-starring white floral jasmine. Later in the heart progression the jasmine and ylang-ylang remain but slightly diminish, allowing a lush hyacinth floral accord to join the others, taking the lead in and out for about an hour with a subtle white musk undertone resembling high quality detergent in support. During the late dry-down the floral aspects dissipate as the composition turns significantly woody through the use of cedar and ever so slightly sweet through the relatively sanitized patchouli, ambery labdanum and faint hints of underlying cinnamon peeping in and out through the finish. Projection is excellent to near outstanding and longevity is outstanding at well over 15 hours on skin. Wow, what a pleasant surprise! With a name such as "Risque" I expected something super-daring and challenging to wear but Risque Parfum (or "Creation R" as it is called in the States) is anything but. Instead of a challenging composition the wearer instead gets one of the finest and most pleasant smelling floral concoctions I have encountered. The initial ylang-ylang and rose floral tandem is absolutely sublime and super-high quality. The florals seem to just float in the air with significant projection and sillage but never overpower. Speaking of florals, the hyacinth that joins the party later-on in the composition's mid-section has got to be the best integration of that note I have sniffed to date, and the result is absolutely outstanding. If there is any relative weakness to the composition ("relative" being the operative word) it would have to be the late dry-down, where things get a bit more subtle and restrained. At the end of the day even Risque (Parfum) at its worst is better than 99% of compositions at their best. As an aside, while I rarely mention stereotypical "masculinity" and "femininity" in my perfume reviews as I believe all compositions can be worn by anyone, I dare say that Risque (Parfum) would truly smell absolutely striking on a lady in particular. Coming full circle, I return to saying this stuff is absolutely brilliant! The bottom line is the $480 per 50ml bottle Risque (Parfum) is a near reference quality airy floral concoction that may have a name that is unfortunate, but the composition itself is unquestionably brilliant, earning a "near masterpiece" to "masterpiece" rating of 4.5 to 5 stars out of 5 and an extremely strong recommendation to all, women in particular. Start saving up your funds for this costly one!

Like almost all my purchases this was a blind buy a little bit over a year ago and I had a quite good “picture” about it in my head but I didn’t know how gorgeous it is. This very complex Chypre has an exceptional luxurious glamour from the past and imo it fits in the same category (doesn’t mean that they are same) with beloved Chypres - vintage Givenchy III (1970) Parfum (mine is from 70s) and original Miss Dior Extrait de Parfum Original (mine is from 60s). If you love those ones you would probably love this one too. Like those two, sadly this gem is discontinued as well. This scent is rich, intoxicating, floral, earthy and mossy with sensual Civet and velvety soft leathery touch in the base. This is for special occasions but whenever you want to feel confident, mysterious and sexy, go for it. I don’t have any of Rojas Essence de Parfums but I would love to have Risque Pour Femme in that concentration as well. In-depth review later. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more

In the truest sense of the word. Risque is not packed with risks that drive me into the deepest, darkest corner of sin. Not even remotely daring. No. Rather, Risque is a smooth chypre that does no harm to anyone. Beautifully composed, but by no means unique or hard to replace. Risque starts off very beautifully sweet. Packed with delicate flowers and a fine layer of spices that prove to be very rich and broad in their appearance. In the background, there’s a hint of lemon. Just like with water lily, I began to get excited about it, but the enthusiasm quickly wanes, leaving only a flat aftertaste. At first, it seems bitter due to the spice, but this is almost smothered into nothingness. The flowers quickly lose their luster, and for my taste, the perfume develops too quickly and, unfortunately, heads into a negative phase. The heart of the perfume is then the broad layer of powder that settles over all that came before. Very gently, I really sense a soft layer of chamomile, which doesn’t quite fit in here. However, there’s more ylang-ylang, which then takes the lead with the powder. Freshness always wafts around the artwork, but nothing seems to waft towards me. Everything feels so pleasing, almost staged. In the dry down, the scent becomes slightly resinous and woody, which reflects positively on me again. The woodiness gives the fragrance more attractiveness. What is supposed to be dangerous about wearing it remains a mystery to me. It is not a dangerous good, not a scent that drives anyone into sinful chambers. The mysterious revelation is completely absent. Rather, it is a simple chypre that is by no means bad, but also not the end of the world. This was one of the first Rojas I got to test, and what can I say? It is nothing special and does not appeal to me personally. I would prefer many other options instead. The longevity, in my case, is over 9 hours. So, quite okay. The sillage is also found in the upper range. I look forward to the next Roja testing phase, as there are samples waiting that not only come off particularly well here but also promise a lot. Since they fit more into my preferences. With this perfume, however - no risk, no fun! Unfortunately.

That sounds almost like the title hit of a blockbuster film from the forties! But that is exactly how Roja's "Risqué Parfum" is! Light-footed and initially a bit innocent, this Roja composition steps onto the fragrance stage: the spicy lightness of chamomile with its fine powdery undertone meets the lively, sparkling aroma of bergamot at the opening. The spring-like touch of hyacinth, childishly radiant jasmine, and a youthful rose dream surrender completely to the finely fragrant, all-encompassing embrace of ylang-ylang! One almost believes they can see a light short skirt swaying in the spring breeze! This buoyant scent innocence playfully bites into one of the ripe peaches that are always ready in a large bowl for the fragrances of this brand and must not be missing. Its sweet and creamy juice blends with the rather uncharacteristic scent opening typical of Roja. But into this innocent scent lightness sneaks in a leather note that is not mentioned here, yet quite mature. A subtle animalic note spreads out before a sensually rich base develops. Here they are again: a noble oakmoss nuance; vetiver, as always earthy in scent; followed by richly brown-golden patchouli lengths. A very delicate cocoa tone appears together with silky cedarwood, before warm-spicy labdanum spreads finely smoky over everything in the end. "Risqué Parfum" is for me a sensual promise of the fragrance being transformed from girl to woman over the course of its extraordinarily long-lasting wear! This refined transformation is richly sprinkled with many facets from a woman's life. This is how a classic chypre creation with floral decor can also develop! Roja Parfums has once again succeeded in surprising me. At first, I was astonished by the unexpectedly youthful freshness, which soon reveals itself from an almost inconspicuous caterpillar to a dazzling scent butterfly. What emerges is an adult, sensual chypre fragrance creation that boosts confidence without stepping on too many toes or being too loud. To wear "Risqué Parfum," you don't need much: a few spritzes and then the seduction begins! Everything else is left to the adult imagination!

At first, I find "Risqué" really beautiful and at the same time a traditional feminine scent. I want to be truly enthusiastic because "Risqué" starts for me with a lovely floral blend, very little citrus. I also don't smell any animalic white flowers; "Risqué" is simultaneously light green. Then follows a bitter phase where I think I can identify the chypre character. However, "Risqué" then transforms into a powdery scent, slightly prickly in the nose and strict. And I perceive labdanum very strongly with its honey-sweet and balsamic lemony note for me. I think about what could be causing the prickling because at that moment I haven't called up "Risqué" yet. I note that I recognize a similarity to "La Panthère" by Cartier. However, the panther is more moderate and, as it should be for such an animal, smoother, although not as lush regarding the presumed real ingredients list. I also note that there are quite a few aldehydes involved here because after 90 minutes, I find that "Risqué" becomes very soapy and it burns on my tongue. Since it is a high-priced scent, as I know from Dia Extrait, one must be very sparing when applying the fragrance. But I was indeed sparing; I only dabbed a few square centimeters on my wrist. So the sillage is already quite impressive. When I now call up "Risqué," I see what the cause of the prickling is, namely ylang-ylang. At least that's how I smell it. I also recognize chamomile because I find chamomile sharp as well. But the entire base hardly reveals itself to me - fortunately. At least not in a way that I could pick out individual notes. Because I don't like oakmoss when it is clearly detectable. However, the lemony labdanum is perceivable to me throughout the entire course. Nevertheless, I agree with Angua. "Risqué" is somehow unbalanced. It started beautifully for me and then became scratchy and biting. "Risqué" is a scent that is not smooth and pleasant, although it is indeed a floral chypre. I believe that musk and amber are missing or that they are used very sparingly. Because what is listed here is certainly by no means the complete formula of "Risqué," but at best a hint. I still find it nice that I can test this precious scent because Angua was so generous to leave me some of it.

In fact, I can say today that I have found my first 10 out of 10 rating. Getting Sunsation was no easy task; I searched for over a year to at least test this fragrance. But recently, the opportunity arose to acquire a bottle. Thanks to a very fair Parfumo, I got it at a great price, which made me very happy. This fragrance was exclusively for the city of Tel Aviv; it was/is only available there. By the way, Tel Aviv is a great city! I was there 6 years ago. Young, dynamic, hospitable, a bit pricey, and outstanding culinary experiences. The people were fantastic, and I still fondly remember Israel, where I was able to accompany a professional project. It is all the more fitting that not only the country and its people but also the exclusive Tel Aviv fragrance completely convinces me. But now to the scent. Sunsation does have similarities to "Rosso Pompei | Tiziana Terenzi," yet it is different in some details. Rosso Pompei, who would be surprised, was one of my few 9.5 ratings. Of course, you either love Terenzi or you don’t; I, for one, am a big fan. While Rosso Pompei starts with a very strong, fruity grape note, Sunsation behaves a bit calmer and less loud. The opening is characterized by bergamot and orange, which is clearly noticeable. Underpinned by a fine spiciness, probably from the juniper. Wonderful! Gradually, a floral base joins in, which I would describe with the color white. In this regard, I primarily smell lily of the valley and jasmine. For me, this does not drift in the direction of "feminine," as the initially described notes remain consistently present. This DNA is enveloped by a gentle, soft, and harmonious wood note. I don’t really pick out patchouli here, although this note can certainly be quite bold. In contrast to Rosso Pompei, Sunsation is significantly softer, a bit quieter. The strong fruity note is elegantly caressed by floral elements, making me perceive Sunsation as distinctly more elegant. Both are clearly distinguishable from each other. Compliments are generally not a criterion for me in a review, but during my visit to the dentist yesterday, I was approached multiple times about the scent. To be honest, this happens to me quite rarely, but this fragrance was described by the dentist and the dental assistant as "extraordinary." They actually described it with the words "fruity, elegant, and masculine," which made me very happy. Some Terenzis do slide quite far into the feminine realm, becoming very floral. However, here the fragrance retains its robust spiciness in the background, which I believe makes it perfect. Projection/sillage and longevity are very solid, but less "aggressive" than, for example, with Rosso Pompei. Thus, this rarity is suitable for almost all occasions. With the story surrounding Tel Aviv, my enthusiasm for Terenzi, and this fragrance DNA, it is the logical consequence that Sunsation represents my first 10 out of 10 rating, even if 0.5 points are certainly of an emotional nature. But let’s be honest, without emotions, it would be boring! :)

I am not really good in describing fragrances and I can only tell if I like a scent or not; in this case it is a like but you should be a lover for sweets. Funnily enough I can smell the hazelnut as a dominant note but some seconds later I smell the lychee and some traces of rose. As it is a Kilian it is not a sillage bomb but the staying power is better than the ususal suspects (IMO all Russian Exclusives by Kilian have a better longevity than the "normal" ones) of this brand. Maybe it is for people who loves the sweet Profumum-fragrances but did not want to "choke" their environment.

When I was a child I happened across a book called Russians as People. It was illustrated with photos of smiling peasants on tractors and heroes of industry toiling away in steel mills and the like. Blatant Cold War propaganda in other words, designed to persuade us capitalist running dogs that the USSR under Khrushchev was something to be admired. And now the boot is on the other foot. Kilian are trying to convince Putin's Russia this poor cardboard rose is really Good Perfume.

We are in the year 2014. Our esteemed master perfumer Roja D. is sitting in his "Chambre de création créative" - oops, directorial error (he is British) - in his "Chamber of creative Creation" and pondering what theme his next fragrance should follow. "Hmm, I'll start with the classic ingredients that I have plenty of experience with. I'll think about the certain something later," he thought and first tossed the basic materials of a typical Roja fragrance into the pot: cardamom, vetiver, labdanum, jasmine, bergamot, lavender. "Alright, it's spicy enough, slightly floral and citrusy... so it can't be a flop. But what now? Maybe some incense and pepper... hmm." So he pondered and mused, and while he juggled two small vials of the fragrance materials 'incense' and 'pepper' over the pot with the words "What should I take?", his Hubba-Bubba gum slipped from his tongue, right into the pot! It was his favorite flavor "Fancy Fruit" - the well-known pink variety that was very popular in the 90s and literally on everyone's lips. Immediately, the fruitiness of a peach combined with the sweetness of a tonka bean joined the classic notes of the previous ingredients. Wow, that's it! Spicy and fruity - why hadn't he thought of that right away? This should be his new perfume. Of course, he knew he had to somehow recreate the taste of Hubba-Bubba with natural ingredients, but that shouldn't be a problem for him - he had plenty of employed chemists who would manage that. Now the child just needed a name... At first, he thought of the name "Scandal" - after all, it is almost scandalous to sell perfume with chewing gum flavor... but, darn... he had already given that name to another perfume! How about "risque"? - after all, it is a risk to publish such a creation... what if people said the Hubba-Bubbas with cola flavor were much better? ;-) Okay, the name is cool, he thought. But to make the risk even riskier, I'll misspell the name and turn "risque" into "risqué" with an Accent Aigu. That's it! Back to the year 2019. The fragrance has since been discontinued. Only the pour Femme variant remains. Perhaps because pink chewing gums are more for girls... who knows? What remains (at least in remaining stocks) is a great fragrance. Spicy-sweet and still wearable up to +20 degrees thanks to citrus notes. Almost a go-to. And surely another masterpiece.

My knowledge of Roja is still quite limited; "Risque" is currently number 4 of the ones I have tested, all of which are men's fragrances. With women's scents, I never got beyond sniffing the bottle, as my aversion to the first real spray was too strong. For me, it's rather heavy-floral and definitely too much of everything. I would describe it as old-lady-like. The men's fragrances are different, but none have really blown me away so far. However, I must say that they all have something beautiful about them and are finely crafted. The "Risque" was a blind buy based on the fragrance pyramid. Everything was very appealing except for the geranium. I have now worn the scent on my skin for the fourth time and can draw a conclusion: Basically, it does indeed get better with each wear. I actually like the chewing-gum-like opening the best. It reminds me a bit of "Mandala," bringing liveliness and joy, and represents for me the feminine phase of the scent's development. I wish this phase could last a bit longer and, above all, be significantly more present. I absolutely cannot confirm the often-mentioned strong sillage. It is rather a subtle, almost skin-close presence. However, it may be that women spray more discreetly due to the relatively high price. After 30 minutes, the chewing gum is spat out, and it becomes finely smoky. There comes a moment when all the fragrance components are intertwined and emerge. Everything is there, connected into an aura carpet, close to the skin, fine, subtle, and quite noble. In the transition to the pure base, the scent loses me... however, my skin also loses the scent. After a good hour, I can hardly smell anything but the earthy vetiver and delicate smoke. For me, the vetiver note has the longest staying power. But after 4 hours, it's over here too. I can no longer perceive anything, not even with my nose on my skin. It's as if the scent has turned to powder on my wrist. This impression remains: Nice scent, absolutely unisex, subtle, reserved, unremarkable, and for the price, there are surely alternatives. I can certainly imagine wearing the scent, but I don't have to. I would have wished for more strength and endurance overall. Who knows, maybe "Risque" is indeed designed solely for men's skin and develops completely differently there.

At the end of November, Roja Dove made a small tour through a select few perfumeries in Germany to present himself and his work or creations - including at my regular perfumery in Düsseldorf. A friendly staff member alerted me in time, and I also received a nudge from a good friend. Why not, I thought, and had myself put on the guest list. After all, I could take a little time off that evening and see what the grand master of self-presentation and marketing has to say. It would be especially interesting for me to see how he would come across. Would he be rather arrogant, considering himself the center of the perfume world? Or perhaps submissive and begging for people to buy his fragrances so he doesn't have to suffer from hunger? Maybe he would even give away some of his perfumes if I was lucky. For the small presentation, there was, as is customary, free champagne, which I didn't necessarily expect, as well as a sparkling Roja Dove. Behind several tables, where a decent part of his portfolio was displayed, he talked about his first inspirations and successes, handing out some of his fragrance highlights on numerous test strips. He impressed not only with British wit and charm but also with each individual perfume to the audience, which consisted of about 25-30 potential customers. In the end, of course, one could also ask him questions and purchase his perfumes with a personal signature at a pre-Black Friday discount of 20%. Due to a lack of cash, I unfortunately had to forgo this, even though I could have easily bought an additional mainstream fragrance with the savings. Nevertheless, I made sure to have him sign his rather extensive main catalog in German and chatted with him about his work pace (according to his own statement, 6-24 months of development per perfume, several fragrances at the same time) as well as the naturalness of the ingredients (everything natural, only the very best. If prohibited, then synthetic in exceptional cases). He seemed anything but arrogant, but very open-minded and was quite pleased and grateful when I congratulated him on his vetiver, which I consider one of the best I have ever smelled. As a little bonus, the perfumery later gave each visitor a golden pocket spray of a Roja Dove fragrance. I first received "A Goodnight Kiss," but knowing its floral nature, I quickly exchanged it for "Risqué pour Homme" as an Eau de Parfum, which satisfied me more and now we can finally get to the fragrance description. It starts off quite sweet and fruity, but is quickly tempered by the bitter citrus notes, initially unfolding like a large colorful fruit salad, where you might feel that perhaps a few too many lemon splashes have made their way in. Olfactorily speaking, at least a welcome note that runs a bit differently than initially expected. Especially in the top note, Risqué pour Homme oscillates between the sweet fruits and the emerging spicy to bitter notes, with vetiver eagerly joining in, even though it should actually only become noticeable in the base. What follows is a rather broad front of incense of the highest quality, flanked by various complex spicy to woody notes. These become weaker towards the end, with the incense gaining the upper hand and fading out until the dry down. One could possibly criticize Risqué pour Homme for a few things, but not for having a predictable and boring progression. From so fruity sweet to smoky bitter, that's quite a significant unexpected turn. And in his large brochure, Roja Dove also describes this Eau de Parfum as "on the edge of the forbidden," but categorizes it as a warm and dry chypre with a fresh, sweet, and soft attitude. He summarizes by noting that this creation represents a deviation from the decent, initially appearing disciplined and revealing itself over time as darker and more complex. With each breath, it subtly gives more and more fleshy sensuality. Well, I personally understand fleshy sensuality in a different olfactory sense, but in principle, the calculation works out, as the initially laid-out tame trail leaves the expected path and drifts completely off. I have found that the scent behaves on my skin more as I described above, while on the paper strip it lingers much longer in the sweet-fruity mode and takes more time for the metamorphosis. Also, projection and longevity on the living object are lower compared to being sprayed on fabric or even in the air. All in all, I now see Roja Dove and his work in a new light and bow to this composition.

"[…] A scent that seems disciplined but reveals itself to be darker and more complex over time. The scent appears to be gentlemanly and refined, but with each breath it subtly reveals something more carnal. Risqué Parfum Pour Homme - something that should be kept behind closed doors." (Roja Dove) Behind closed doors, Risqué should indeed be left. Wearing a fragrance with such a start and paying a lot of money for it is indeed risky. I pondered for a while what this fruity sweetness reminds me of: Coumarin? No. - Shisha tobacco? Not really. - Gummy bears? Quite conceivable. - Now I’ve got it: canned pineapple and possibly a hint of coconut. And this is supposed to be worn by an adult man? One needs quite a bit of patience before this fruity accord is toned down and other nuances come into play. I can initially sense something floral, and looking at the notes, it turns out that geranium is responsible for this, as it contributes its slightly cooling effect. Since the sweetness has spread quite a bit, it is difficult to filter out individual notes from the base. It goes classically dry-woody, but above all, the smoky duo of frankincense and myrrh (I would have thought of the sweeter opoponax) as well as pepper and tonka providing more spice are noticeable. Whether one would call the whole thing sensual ('carnal') is up to each individual. I suspect, however, that most would shake their heads.

I am rarely moved enough by a perfume to write a review about it. Extreme Oud by Kilian is one of those rare fragrances that makes me believe, even if it's only for a while, that my quest for that "one" perfect scent is finally over! Although we all know such a thing doesn't exist, we still hope that some day we will find it. Refined noses can't settle on a signature scent: there are different seasons, various times in a day, diverse moods and many distinct life occasions to limit ourselves to JUST one perfume. Calice Becker has delivered an oud fragrance that is very reminiscent of ASAQ's Kings Blend. I'm surprised this has received low ratings by some fellow members, but then again I need to remind myself that I have spent the last five years sniffing hundreds of ouds, natural and synthetic, to develop an acquired taste and to appreciate its endless nuances. Extreme Oud is made of rich, dark Cambodian oud. Cambodian agarwood is highly sought after, for its hypnotic and tranquilizing aroma. It is ideal for scenting oneself and for those times when you just want to relax. The first wisps of smoke are intensely sweet, narcotic, cinammony, with some nutmeg, and a healthy dose of berries and figs. As the chip continues to burn, the scent becomes more woody and earthy. Finally, like Kings Blend, the whole composition is permeated with majestic wild flowers and first rate ta'if rose. However, this is NOT your typical oud/rose combo: it's lush, deep, intense and dark and smells natural, yet otherworldly. Extreme Oud is one of the few fragrances that seduces the primal reptilian part of my brain, as I unwillingly (or willingly?) surrender to my vices... This is an oud lover's dream journey! For an authentic Middle-Eastern feeling, which is the target audience of this Middle East Exclusives line, and if you are really, really into morphing, undulating, sensuous ouds, you must have this. I am so grateful to have found this masterpiece!

I find Roja Dove fragrances unfathomable. The ones I have tested strike me as elegant, valuable, aristocratic. Great emotions surface. Cocktail dresses, long satin gloves. WOW, what a pleasant surprise! With a name like "Risque," I expected something very daring and challenging, but Risque Parfum is anything but that. Instead of a challenging composition, the wearer receives one of the finest and most pleasantly scented floral blends I have encountered. The initial tandem of ylang-ylang and rose petals is absolutely sublime and of super high quality. A large country garden with plump, full blooms and a wonderful variety of colors among grasses and ferns plays out in my mind like a movie. A bit of earthy and mossy note. The head and heart blend softly. For me, jasmine, rose, and ylang-ylang dominate, but there is also a bit of freshness: citrusy. This harmony lasts a long time. Quite late, the blend of very gentle patchouli and musk sets in. A thoroughly magical fragrance. A drop is enough to dream.
... no, I risk nothing.... with this "Risqué" one can feel completely safe, risks absolutely nothing, relatively harmless and for a Roja, or Chypre, quite disappointing.... Too bad!

This has nothing to do with my beloved Love, Don't Be Shy. It's a very harsh, barnyardy oud scent that greets you with a blast of cow manure in the opening. There is a bit of woodsiness and the tiniest hint of rose looming underneath it, but the oud is so strong and fecal. If you like rose & oud scents in the vein of Oud Bouquet or Oud Satin Mood and hoped for a mix of that with the marshmallow and orange blossom DNA of LDBS, this will likely not be to your taste. Of course it gets a little less terrible after it has dried down. At some point there is a hint of orange blossom to be detected, and on the next day it smells okay, like a classic amber scent with an animalic undertone, spicy and fizzy-sweet. But who wants to wait for that for a whole day? This is long lasting and intense, hard to scrub off, but luckily it doesn't have an overwhelmingly strong sillage. I usually test any fragrance I review at least 3 times, but with this one, twice is more than enough. Life is too short to surround yourself with perfume you hate. And if you look at my profile, I don't hate a lot of fragrances, so this is saying something. Maybe some seasoned oud connoisseurs will like this, I don't know. This is a taste that I don't need to acquire. PS: After I wrote this review I scrubbed the fragrance of. While I did that could smell a little bit of the sweet white floral notes of LDBS, but I still stand by my point that the awful oud note overpowers everything in this.

Love's Special Blend is easily misunderstood, outspoken; yet gratifying. An eccentric personality like this is very much acquired taste. There is a raw, animalic opening compared to the essence of a barn or barnyard. This is due to the use of real oud, but understanding its nature can make this admissible. Synthetic or westernized ouds are often immediately likeable and skips the harsh stages. It's the ugly duckling of perfumery, but evolves beautifully when intermixed with specific notes. In this case, the vanilla, rose and white floral accord compliment the dark and murky oud. How is this different from the original blend? It is simply Love Don't Be Shy surrounded by a dense cloud of oud that eventually settles. Through the darkness the Love Don't Be Shy you know and love is still there, but bitter sweet. This is where perfume becomes art and the appreciation is found in the innovation and inspiration.

Kilian calls Calice Becker: ''Bonjour Calice! Rose/Oud seems to be quite a hit!?'' ‘’Yes…’’ ‘’.. and Love don’t be Shy is our bestseller..’’ ‘’Yes…’’ ‘’Magnifique, then mix A LOT of Oud and Rose into our LDBS formula et Voilà!’’ ‘’.. but Kilian... alright, I’ll try. I should be done by tonight.’’ 80% ''stinky'' Oud, 15% Rose and somewhere there should still be % LBDS… What a pity.

I have two "commissioned works" for the house of Roja available as samples and had to decide in advance which comment to favor: will it be "Bergfeld"*) or "L'Oscar"? (*) sorry, JonasP1 rightly points out an error: the fragrance is of course called "Bergdorf"; here "Schusselchen" was at work again! When you remember something incorrectly ...) In any case, both fragrances are worth discussing. A look at the website, which promises that L'Oscar is "one of London's most romantic hotels," immediately makes the decision for me. After all, I am currently more in the mood for a stay in such a house than for a visit to a shopping temple in Manhattan, no matter how glamorous it may be. The first spray already transports me to a noble reception area, where the fireworks of aldehydes capture the sparkle of polished floors and skillfully arranged mirrors and lights, while the freshness of bergamot and mandarin suggests airy generosity. Fine, I like this; I will feel comfortable and linger here! The now unfolding lush bouquet of early summer flowers also immediately delights me. Here, a connoisseur of the fragrance world has precisely instructed the gardeners from Grasse on how many of which floral beauties should be tied into this fragrance bouquet and where. The early summer promise of pink May roses, finely aromatic neroli, delicate orange blossoms, and intensely fragrant violets is wonderfully realized. Spicy garden carnations meet here with lovingly entwined, strongly scented, and flower-rich jasmine and ylang-ylang vines: a decoration for this bouquet. A more robust, compact scent note is now brought in by the rose geranium, while dark violet heliotrope skillfully replaces the usual vanilla. Thus, the transition from the floral-opulent heart of the fragrance, which conveys the illusion of a luxurious romantic boudoir, to the equally impressive base is very well achieved. For the "vanilla bridge" heliotrope leads directly to the tonka bean, which allies itself with the proud iris: both give this previously so radiant fragrance bouquet a rich, powdery note. Resin, wood, and spice accents are tastefully distributed, while leather and musk are still undecided about who among them gets to represent the crowning finale of this fragrance creation. Once again, our little not-so-clean civet takes advantage of this; it leaves its animal charm, and suddenly the two "quarrelsome" ones reaching for the final appearance are in the second row! And Roja's "L'Oscar" receives a fine animalistic round of applause! Floral, aromatic, sensual, feminine - all of this is "L'Oscar" in abundance! Once again, it has been bold rather than subtly done, and once again, every little nuance fits so precisely with the others that nothing less than a luxury fragrance kaleidoscope can emerge from it! Thus, a prolonged stay amidst this romantically grand fragrance backdrop is offered, which everyone is free to enjoy. I have this preference for luxury in general, luxury hotels in particular, and therefore I could immediately embrace "L'Oscar" in my heart; I quickly felt at home amidst this pompous fragrance world! And my fondness for the fragrances of this brand is probably already known. (Sometimes it just has to be a Ferrari and not the serious Rolls-Royce!) A little "Pomp and Circumstance" in everyday life certainly doesn't hurt! (Hm, is a fanfare or just a red carpet missing for the finale?)

Thanks to a lovely perfumer, I was able to test this truly "noble drop" today.....my heartfelt thanks to the donor :-).... L‘OSCAR smells fresh-floral-creamy and pleasantly clean to my nose.....Aldehydes provide a subtle soapy quality at the beginning, which - in my opinion - recedes somewhat as it develops......however, for those who do not appreciate soap at all, this might still be too much..... L‘OSCAR is a bright and gentle fragrance that envelops the wearer in an extraordinarily well-groomed and flattering aura.....I like it :-).... To my great surprise, I notice a distinct similarity to MADISON SOIREE (Bond) in the first 10 minutes....both fragrances essentially "sing" the same song.....however, as the scent develops, a significant difference becomes apparent, making L‘OSCAR undoubtedly my favorite: BOND plays this song on synthesizer strings... ROJA on a Stradivari..

To confess right away: I'm not really the type for powder puffs. Nor am I the romantic type. Not even when it comes to fragrances. Therefore, I am completely clueless in the realm of powdery scents, and I actually categorize them into just two groups: Puder-Luder and Baby-Puder. And l’oscar clearly falls into the category of the most exclusive baby powder - luxurious Nivea cream ever! The animalic note in this fragrance, on my skin and in my nose, is at most that of a warm-sleeping baby, with fine downy hairs slightly dampened and pressed to the head. The opening consists of a full dose of aldehydes. Just a few months ago, this would have meant the end of the fragrance for me. However, a curious effect has occurred. Aldehydes no longer send me rushing towards the faucet and soap; instead, they fill me with a quiet nostalgia, a memory of some of my mother's fragrances, from the time of permed hair and clouds of hairspray. And through my newly kindled love for vintage scents, I also know that this sometimes quite penetrating top note can quickly dissipate. And so it is with l’oscar: Practically immediately, a shower of floral powder - violet powder, rose powder, jasmine powder, clove powder, and several other varieties - gently descends upon me in an overall delicate composition. By delicate, I certainly do not mean inconspicuous, but rather that the floral scent, which can often be overwhelming to the point of being narcotic in perfumes, must submit to the powder here. The base, which once again draws on the tried-and-true Roja base combination of spice, wood, resin, and musk, is above all one thing: powdery, with a hint of cream. Only relatively late can I detect a trace of animalic notes: perhaps a hint of leather? Nevertheless: No dirty powder seductress here, but rather a softly flattering, innocent powder scent. So how does such a fragrance find its way into my collection, which usually goes in a completely different direction? Perhaps it is indeed the subconscious memory of security as a baby, because I wear this scent when my professional life is completely overwhelming, and in the evening, after what feels like an endlessly long day, I find olfactory comfort and luxury to be an absolute necessity. And l’oscar perfectly fulfills this need for me! Both the comfort and the luxury!

After a brief "intermezzo of cleanliness," I continue my rose journey: No worries, it's not far to Roja's rose garden in Grasse, and this will also be the final stage of my "rose trilogy." Like many of his collections, the series I call "Blüten" consists of a manageable four fragrances. I have experienced "Lily" and "Lilac," I will likely skip "Gardenie," but "Rose" deserves some thoughts now. As simple as the name suggests, "Rose" is not; it is a creation from Roja Dove's grand fragrant garden. And unlike the two predecessors of my "rose trilogy" ("Rose in Wonderland" and "Rose Pompon"), we find here a much more mature scent, where the well-known May roses languidly and sensually bask on a rich cushion of awakening fragrance notes. (At this point, I would like to thank everyone who ensured that the concrete desert around Grasse, which promised big money, became rose fields again with the cultivation of this almost forgotten variety. The battle against concrete and money has been won by the rose breeders here!) Bergamot in its well-known fruity freshness opens the gate to this rose realm, where "Her Majesty" has already crossed the threshold of delicately fragrant virginity. Heavily opened, weighty heads, made of fleshy, velvety petals that slightly roll outward at the edges, release their ripe, very feminine scent. Cozy buzzing bumblebees and colorful fluttering butterflies can be found there. These sensual scent clouds are accompanied by the spicy and therapeutic aromas of the rose geranium, also known to us as "English geranium." Ylang-Ylang cleverly weaves through this arrangement; it lightens this lascivious scent density once again. For the bed on which this rose fragrance rests is rich in exotic spices and fragrant treasures that reached us long ago, among others, following in Marco Polo's footsteps and have since become native here. Cinnamon, nutmeg, and pepper spread warmth along with the sensual, languid vanilla, enticing us to linger in a generous, lush embrace: The "Woman Rose" stretches and extends! Where stretching and extending is done with pleasure, patchouli must not be missing: Its deep earthy scent brown appears creamy flowing and golden marbled in this rose creation. Galbanum and benzoin send out their rich smoky aromas, like waves, causing the previous composition to resonate. A flower queen, resting on such noble "spices" of the fragrance world, naturally requires a corresponding cloak. Once again, we turn to the oriental-spiced vanilla, which now, together with cuddly soft musk, forms an erotically and finely animalistic-scented envelope, a fragrance cloak with a train that allows us to feel this magic of roses for a long time! Roses and vanilla represent for me the softer, but no less sensual counterpart to roses and oud in the fragrance world. Both companions highlight the charm of roses in their own special way, pleasing us women. Wrapped for a long time in Roja Dove's "Rose" with its rich spiced warmth, we feel particularly special! This feeling, which the fragrance treasures of this house always convey to me, also appears in the so simply named creations: This man loves to dress women in fragrances just as much as Christian Dior did before him. Each in his own personal way, but with only one goal: to honor and adorn women! Three different rose fragrance creations caught my attention while sorting my fragrance samples. They show how variable the majesty of the flowers can appear: From the delicate rose-white of the English, to the slightly sensual one of the Goutal ladies, to this warm-spiced, exotic-erotic glowing composition. Even those who do not like rose fragrances will be amazed at the variety of possibilities that the three I mentioned already offer! There are indeed many possibilities, but I will (as promised) leave it at these three fragrance images. So let us celebrate, in the midst of the "golden autumn," the beauty of roses before they too disappear into the November gray. Roja's "Rose" leaves behind more than just a memory of warmth and light with its rich fragrance trail!

Sparkling and shimmering in a diamond-studded dress, you have lured me in, oh Rose! You are no ordinary rose... you are noble, blood-red, and fleshy-lustful! I gladly let you rest on my arm: The dream begins with a walk through the enchanted garden.... I walk past the bergamot tree, delicate and green, but by no means too intrusive... very fine and fruity-citrusy-fresh... I encounter gardenia and warm ylang-ylang, which are well-presented but not overwhelming.... They integrate wonderfully warm! The garden grows warmer and warmer... Then finally you come, oh Rose! You are the star here in the beautiful enchanted garden! Elegantly dressed in a blood-red, diamond-studded gown, you stand there... surrounded by pepper groupies and vanilla paparazzi! You are a bit vain, oh wonderful Rose..! But you can afford it, for you are a true beauty! You blow me away, oh Rose! I must admire and sniff you for a long, long time, so fascinated am I by you.... And your beauty lasts and lasts and lasts...

I have to agree with all the commentators here. Cravache is right, Roja's Rose has something, and I understand why the scent excites him, as it is unique and captivating. But it is also herbal, dark, fleshy, and overpowering; the statements are equally understandable. Shortly after spraying, I was quite euphoric, especially because Roja's Rose is simply thick, fleshy, and juicy. That can certainly be beautiful, just dark and sublime. Unfortunately, my mood changes quickly with the progression of the scent. The rose does not open up as Roja wants it to olfactorily; rather, weeds overgrow the rose bush so much that you can hardly see it anymore. Rose geranium joins in, but I suspect that this is not all. Rose geranium fits perfectly with the rose. I suspect it adds a certain bright herbaceousness. So beautiful, so good. Yet Roja's Rose develops on my skin in such a herbaceous and green way that it really only becomes a background rose scent. It feels more like a loud, dense green-herbaceous-floral fragrance that shows more nuances of nettles than of desired herbs. That is too much herbaceousness for me; the splendor and beauty of the truly grand rose note here is simply crushed instead of being suitably accompanied. So, rose is only present at the beginning. After that, the petals have fallen, still lightly fragrant on the ground, and above all, I get an olfactory image of a green and prickly rose stem. Roja's Rose sounds soft-ambery and, compared to the loud opening, ends unspectacularly but very pleasantly. Rose is now only very subtly perceptible, but a balsamic-sweet-floral scent that could also come from good cosmetics seems to dominate. Everything feels very natural. The sillage is great, but for a Roja, Rose surprisingly becomes quiet and close to the skin quite quickly. It really feels like only good raw materials were used here. Roja's Rose absolutely does not smell like a bad fragrance. However, this implementation feels a bit rough to me at the beginning and somewhat arbitrary later on. From the same label, I prefer the rose in Roja's Aoud significantly more, even though it appears less eccentric and bold.

Rose by Roja Dove is meant to olfactorily depict a rosebud that is initially closed, only to then unfold in all its radiant splendor. After testing around 3000 perfumes, I am both demanding and skeptical. Can a rose scent still excite me? To get straight to the point: Yes, Roja Dove, this Paganini among perfumers, succeeds. Rose by Roja Dove leaves me more or less astonished and speechless. I am enchanted. Occasionally, one reads that Roja Dove's fragrances are flashy, showy, and lack passion. How inaccurate these statements are is impressively demonstrated by Rose. It feels as if you are holding a delicate little plant in your hand that unfolds into a majestic rose bloom; you can almost sense the gentle breath and the fine, yet passionate heartbeat of the flower. Upon spraying, fresh rose geranium is detectable. The rose geranium is bright to medium red, fresh, slightly sweet, rather delicate, and not really profound, but rather an innocent, young bloom. A hint of citrusy-fresh bergamot underscores the innocent floral morning freshness of the geranium. Quickly, May rose joins in. The May rose smells full, sweet, intoxicating, warm, and has a faint note of nectar. The scent of the May rose reminds one of the first warm rays of sunshine. Enveloping, harmonious, and certainly romantic. The May rose is accompanied by not overly prominent, floral white ylang-ylang, which adds a touch of allure to the May rose and conjures a sweet smile on its face. After some time, the previously delicate bloom begins to unfold. I smell the petals of a red, radiant floral, velvety Bulgarian rose. Galbanum provides a fresh, green counterbalance, reminiscent of the green of a medium-stemmed rose. And then suddenly, the bloom is there in all its radiant, majestic, intense splendor. The scent of a wonderfully, wonderfully beautiful rose unfolds. Taif rose. Deep, profound, majestic, sublime, glowing in dark red, yes even the most radiant, intense, fleshy, with an almost breathtaking, legendary beauty. The rose has a way of being three-dimensional and charismatically occupying the space, as if one were standing in a surreal, magnificent, fairy-tale rose garden. A touch of patchouli gives the magnificent rose bloom additional depth and a slightly earthy hint, while oriental spices, namely pepper, nutmeg, and a touch of cinnamon, provide a dry-warm spicy undertone. Towards the base, dry, soft, warm vanilla and a background resinous note join the rose. Downy soft, gentle musk cradles the rose in the drydown on a sensually soft and rose-velvety bed. Rose exhibits the scent behavior of an extrait. I initially perceive the sillage as strong, and as the fragrance develops, it becomes less noticeable when you smell your own skin. Rose is strong but not overly loud, with great inner strength. The scent is still perceptible in the room when you leave and come back after some time. With Rose, Roja Dove has created another masterpiece. A rose bloom that slowly opens to blossom in deep radiant, intense floral splendor, warm and soft. In terms of price, the fragrance is on par with the venerable extraits from Guerlain. Rose is of such seductively charismatic floral beauty that it would be a shame not to wear the scent daily. I am floating in olfactory rose heaven. Truly a fragrance that excites me incredibly - authentic and blessed with passion, leaving me at a loss for words.

You know how sometimes a fragrance has this incredible power to evoke vivid memories and transport you back to specific moments in your life? In a way it's like a time machine for the senses! Whenever I catch a whiff of Starwalker, it instantly brings back thoughts, feelings, and memories associated with my uncle & for this fragrance, I'm forever grateful.

For a long time, I was searching for a Neroli scent that could convince me 100%. The search took quite a while, and Roja Neroli was my last purchase in this quest. The last candidates that failed or were discarded after some time include: Sun Song , "Essenze - Mediterranean Neroli (Eau de Parfum) | Ermenegildo Zegna", "Shooting Stars - Nio | XerJoff", Neroli Portofino Eau de Parfum , Neroli Portofino Forte , Neroli Portofino Acqua . At least the Neroli Portofino found a place in my girlfriend's collection at home. Now let's discuss the reasons why the other fragrances did not meet my expectations. Nio was too green for me; I always had the thought of tree leaves. Neroli Portofino was too floral for me, and Sun Song was the same as Neroli Portofino, while Zegna was too spicy. Now we come to Roja Neroli and the question of whether my search has finally come to an end: Yes, my search is finally over. Roja Neroli gets everything right for me. The fragrance opens beautifully fresh with citrus fruits and petitgrain. In the heart note, there is a floral component that is fortunately soft and perfectly dosed, which is geranium. This floral note is accompanied by neroli and orange blossom. What I particularly like about Roja Neroli is the interplay of similar notes. Neroli as a rather bitter and green floral component, petitgrain is rather bitter and slightly woody. Orange blossom is lightly sweet and floral. The use of all components of the bitter orange is what fascinates me about Roja Elixir. However, the neroli note is the most dominant. I can hardly recognize the base notes apart from oak moss and a bit of styrax. The longevity is in a solid range. About 6-7 hours is acceptable for a very fresh scent and is nothing to complain about. The sillage is always within an arm's length. After about 5 hours, Roja Elixir is almost skin close. I am now very happy to have finally found my neroli scent after a long search. Only the price is far too high when I look at the MSRP. Since I like the scent so much, I would even be willing to pay it. Unfortunately, our hobby is simply expensive, and there is probably no need for a discussion about whether it is sensible or not.

Here we have Neroli, a simple name for a luxury fragrance, but it doesn't always have to be complicated, does it? Well, this will be my third Roja scent that I’m testing, and Neroli already sounds great, after all, it evokes spring and summer. I mean, the days have been looking quite sunny lately, but it’s still really cold and sometimes even quite stormy. Just now, my cat came in from outside (wasn’t that clear, just when I vacuumed my room and everything was dust- AND cat hair-free…) and has laid down on my arms, and I’m noticing how icy his paws are :D And I can also tell how fat he really is, as he weighs so much that I feel like there’s a ton of weight on my arm, but I digress… From Roja Neroli, I actually expect just a high-quality scent for warm days, possibly with a longer lasting power, but whether it’s also significantly different in other ways remains to be seen,… The Scent: You first smell the bergamot, which smells quite natural and also has a hint of tea, which I particularly like. In addition, I detect a slightly bitter background, but I can’t quite say what it is; it smells floral and bitter. Perhaps it’s the combination of floral notes with the bergamot and also the lemon, with the lemon becoming quite zesty. Moreover, the mix of bergamot and lemon later reminds me more of green tea. You can smell the neroli in the heart note, but I find that for being the namesake of the fragrance, this note is comparatively weak. The bitterness from the top note actually becomes a bit stronger, and the scent smells slightly bitter, somewhat like the peels of citrus fruits. Towards the end, I can confirm the oak moss indicated in the fragrance pyramid, although it is somewhat weak and doesn’t necessarily make the scent seem very classic due to the combination with lemon or bergamot (and thus somewhat more mature, as some say). Frankincense and myrrh or any resinous-smoky notes are only lightly present in the background, if they can be perceived at all. Oh, and despite the amber, the scent is only slightly sweet. The Sillage and Longevity: The projection is typical for citrusy, summery scents, and it is just as strong as with most other perfumes. Rather average, so you can only smell the scent up close, although it occasionally wafts nicely into your nose. However, you can enjoy the scent longer, as it has a good longevity of about eight hours. The Bottle: The rectangular and handmade bottles from Roja are always particularly elegant and high-quality, which also drives up the price of the fragrances. After all, the golden elements are made of real gold, even the label, which is also handcrafted. Additionally, there are countless Swarovski crystals integrated into the cap. In this scent, you see white crystals that look like diamonds. But as always, it’s a nicely made bottle that appears elegant but not necessarily ostentatious. Hmm, Neroli by Roja is a good scent… yes, but here comes my but, so BUT: It’s nothing you haven’t smelled before in other similarly composed fragrances. However, the scent comes across as somewhat more high-quality and is surprisingly long-lasting for a fresh scent. Aside from that, it’s a bit too bitter for me personally over time. Of course, it is purely a spring or summer scent, it refreshes for a long time, smells pleasant, especially for those who like (slightly bitter-smelling) citrus fruits and tea in fragrances, and just feels good. It fits perfectly for leisure, but also for going out, not for partying, but rather for when you want to eat outside or go for a walk in the summer or something like that. Whether it’s worth the price, everyone has to decide for themselves. For me, there are other scents that smell just as great, but as I said, this scent here has turned out quite well.

The most beautiful day of her life has arrived, sisters, mother, grandmother, and cousins surrounded the bride to prepare her for this day. Her hair was intricately braided, intertwined, and pinned up, with small, white orange blossoms interspersed, complementing the floral crown of the veil and the bridal bouquet. She wore delicate, cream-white silk lingerie that exuded a certain romance but also sophistication - for the wedding night. The women carefully pulled the lavish lace and silk wedding dress with beautiful embroidery over her head and fastened the small, round buttons at the back from her neck to her waist. A delicate, slightly innocent yet somewhat sultry makeup accentuated the bride's beauty, with her lips highlighted in a bright, velvety red. When she looked in the mirror, she could hardly believe it herself. WAS that her? This young, blooming beauty in this dreamy dress? Her heart skipped a beat, and she reached for a small bottle with a white-gold label that her beloved had given her for their engagement. She wanted to wear this fragrance today, on this very special day. She sprayed it on her hair and neck, and immediately a wonderful, bright scent of neroli and orange blossoms filled the room, enhancing the fragrance of the real, small flowers in her hair and creating a very special, festive aura. She remembered the walks in her father's orange grove, the dark, wonderfully green-orange scented foliage of the trees, and the small, white, intoxicatingly fragrant blossoms that she loved so much and that would now accompany her to the altar. Then the moment arrived; all the women had disappeared to get ready themselves, and there was a soft knock at the door. The door opened at her "come in," and her father stood there, in an elegant black suit, white shirt, and bow tie, with a small bouquet of orange blossoms on his lapel. His gaze contained everything he had given her throughout her life: all the love and affection, the protection, support, courage to pursue and realize her goals, and a great happiness, paired with pride, for this beautiful daughter. When her gaze fell on his lapel bouquet, she had to smile and sprayed a bit of her perfume on her father's hair. Her father handed her the bridal bouquet of champagne-colored roses and white orange blossoms, and they left the house arm in arm on their way to the church. All day long, she was accompanied by this wonderful scent of orange blossoms and pomeranate flowers. In the late evening, her fragrance reached a deep and dark-warm note, and after all the photos were taken, the tables cleared, and all the guests had left, the newlyweds retreated to their private quarters. The soft, fragrant bed was strewn with orange blossoms, and her perfume exuded a dark, warm, sweet, and promising eroticism that was sure to spark that night.

Due to the name I hoped for a smoky version of Libre, but apparently the "Flames" here are more like sunrays. This is a warm, beachy floral take on it and not smoky at all. It still carries the Libre DNA of very clean, fresh lavender and orange blossom. Compared to the original it doesn't feel as soapy, but it's lighter than the Intense and Le Parfum flankers. I think it's a bit lighter on the lavender and heavier on the orange blossom and vanilla than the pillar fragrance. There is something about this that feels warm and almost buttery. Palm flower is the most interesting looking new note for this flanker, but to be honest I have no idea what that smells like. So, of course, I looked it up, and the internet says it has a vegetal scent that turns into a sweet, sunny floral with accents of caramel. I don't get anything vegetal/green here, but the rest of the description tracks pretty well! The addition of tuberose to the notes list makes sense to me, too, as this flower can lean tropical. I do not get any lily here. Libre is one of those perfumes where I prefer the flankers over the original, and this is another pretty addition to the lineup. It's not vastly different from the rest of the collection, but a nice alternative for the warmer seasons. It would make a good summer night perfume. My favorite Libre is Le Parfum and this doesn't come close to it, but I like it.

I received a free sample of this fragrance from YSL (thanks direct marketing on instagram)! First, the atomizer on the little sample bottle was amazing! As for the fragrance, I do not get a strong lavender opening, maybe slightly herbal. I do not get bergamot at all. After the opening, I smell a strong white floral, it leaned more jasmine than lily in my opinion. I do smell the palm tree accord. If you’ve ever had a bath/fragrance product with “palm” in the title, you’ll recognize this accord. I smell coconut in the sense of like a “sun-warmed” atmospheric note, but not in a tropical or sunscreen way. To sum it up, it is white floral + vanilla + palm tree. I think the palm tree accord lends a slight airiness to the fragrance. I think this would be a nice spring or summer scent for day or night. I get moderate longevity (~6 hours, turns into a lighter vanilla as time goes on), and moderate-strong sillage (more than an arm's length but less than 6 feet). I think this is a well-blended, high-quality fragrance. I recently bought Mugler Angel Elixir, and I think they have pretty similar vibes. Although I enjoyed this sample, I don’t find it super unique, and I likely wouldn’t pay ~$3.50/mL.

A different approach to Libre. While the first one in the line comes across as loud and shouty, this one is soft and balanced. Libre is certainly recognisable, but the orange blossom is now much softer. Coconut also makes it a lot creamier. You have to take your time for this perfume. Do not smell it on a strip or briefly on your wrist. But sit back and relax and I'm sure you will recognize and acknowledge the quality of this perfume. The first from this line that I can appreciate and even bought.

Look. Libre EDP is one of my all-time favorite fragrances and I enjoy the Libre line, However, in my personal opinion, this was the most disappointing flanker they have released this far. This smells exactly like Libre EDP, okay, not exact...but the differences are so minor they are pretty much undetectable. I can verrry faintly pick up a "coconut/beachy" note but I really have to seriously focus to find it to the point that I'm wondering if I'm just imagining what I'm smelling. That being said...this smells very nice, but it if you already own Libre EDP, this isn't worth buying unless you're trying to collect all the Libre's.

I like it but it doesn't blow me away. I can smell the vanilla and coconut notes that I like. It's similar to the other perfumes in my collection that combine these two notes. I have a miniature of it. I don't think I'll buy it in large quantities. It doesn't last long on my skin. Of course, it has a different intensity on clothes, a much higher one. I don't think its price is fair, in the sense that it doesn't perform for the money. Rating: 8/10

At first, there is a distinctly floral-fruity note, and one might almost be inclined to think of ZARA Gold Man EdP, just less fruity and significantly more amber-like. Not bad at all! But then it unfortunately becomes rather tiresomely average. Amber, sweet with a slight rubber note.

The Libre line from Yves Saint Laurent is already quite extensive, and pretty much every year a new one is added. Sometimes it’s not even worth writing a review or giving too much attention to certain flankers. In this case, however, I find this one really great: the Libre Flowers & Flames.

I never wanted to have a Libre bottle in my collection... Libre, everyone wears it, permanently in first place, no day without Dua Lipa, no day without promotional displays in turquoise, no day without a Libre sample. If I had collected them, I would already have a bottle by now.

Libre Flowers & Flames rightly mainstream I treated myself to Flower and Flames because I love the original Libre very much, and the fragrance did not disappoint me.
