I wore it often last year; the 30 ml bottle is more than half empty. Flower and Flames resembles the wonderful original but has a warmth, spiciness, and creamy note to it.

The opening is much lighter and creamier for a Libre. The lavender is not as squeaky and piercing as in the original. This version is more powdery and sweeter. I find it really pleasant. I like the Libre line and probably an untrained nose won’t notice much difference from the others in the line, but the fragrances are truly beautiful and elegant.

It won't be easy for me, but I will try to set aside which house Nüwa comes from. I also want to put the cart before the horse and vehemently disagree with the classification of this fragrance as a women's scent. When we see who already has this fragrance in their collection, I am not alone in this view. The sillage is pleasant, the scent makes its presence known but without recklessness, and the longevity is very satisfactory. Now to the crux of the matter. I have read somewhere that one should not rely on comments from other users when it comes to descriptions. But I have no choice but to align my thoughts with Labormaus, as she is completely right in her review - and that is precisely why I like Nüwa so much. We can really forget the top notes, and yes, the heart notes also play a subordinate role in this fragrance. If Roja Dove lists these notes, I will take it as a given. I can neither grasp the blackcurrant nor the immortelle. But while I am still pondering this, the fragrance shows where its strength lies, as it is truly the base that has a different function here. It does not serve as background noise, nor as a fixative, and certainly not as a conclusion, but rather as the theme that this bouquet of notes presents, giving the fragrance a dark, quite animalistic fluidity. It may be speculation, but perhaps Roja Dove has indeed recalled his past at Guerlain with Nüwa, as for me, the perfume is a dark chypre with an exciting, soothing timbre, similar to what I experience with Parure, for example. When I consider the feminine side of the perfume, I want to draw another parallel with music. Here we do not hear radiant sopranos, but rich, minor-sounding alto voices. I really like that. Neither the Orient nor any trumpets pouring flowers over us were employed here. Even less was there any attempt to please, and therefore I can understand well that Nüwa falls outside the norm for some noses. How wonderful that our world of perfume is so diverse.

First of all, a heartfelt thank you to Ms. Angua for the sample! Phew! How should I best start? As you may have already noticed, I love and appreciate the Roja fragrances very much! And now comes the BUT.... The Nüwa is somewhat like an accident; you don't want to look, but you can't look away either! In the price segment of around 1000,- a special composition should make all other fragrances pale in comparison. It should be something spectacular, luxurious, extraordinary, which unfortunately is not the case here. Certainly, the scent is of high quality, yet it does not suit my taste. Based on the fragrance pyramid, you would hardly recognize the scent! Citrusy start? Huh, no, I'm sorry. Floral heart note? Hmmm, next question please! Base? Yes, finally something is happening! In summary, for me, the Nüwa starts with the base note. All the many fragrance components from the top and heart notes are probably in such low concentration that they completely fade away! You can hardly believe it, but the Nüwa appears quite linear, in contrast to all the other Rojas. It starts and ends with birch, cumin, iris, oakmoss, and a hint of vetiver. Especially with cumin, Uncle Roja did not hold back, and most know what that means! To put it mildly, it smells a bit musty and sweaty, reminiscent of wet shaving! The dose of birch is also not typical for Roja, but maybe the good man had connections with Mr. Tauer, who knows. Of course, this is still not a bad scent, just..... too specific, let's say. Despite the enormous longevity, the sillage is limited, which is fine with me in this case. Oh, how glad I am to have saved 1000,-; I would rather look at the other wonderful Rojas!

My first ever review. Here it goes! This is quite a pleasant scent. Nothing ground-breaking or Earth-shattering, but still nice. There is this open, airy, aromatic quality to it, but still has a little bit of a backbone to it, thanks to the woods and cardamom. This opens up nicely with lime/green-citrus and mint. Not too sharp or bitter off my skin at all. I'm positive the note list on Fragrantica is incomplete, because there must be lavender in this, and it makes itself known pretty quickly when the green-citrus dies down a little (after ~10 minutes). The ingredients seem well blended for the price point (can be found for $40-$50 AUD if you look for it), and you'll have a hard time offending people with this scent. Longevity and projection seems to be a little fleeting. I can smell this for about 3, maybe 4 hours at best, however I have received compliments after the 5 hour mark, using two sprays on the neck, and one on each wrist. The compliment factor for me is surprisingly good with this fragrance. I usually don't get a lot of unsolicited compliments from either strangers, or people I know in general. However, this fragrance has gotten me compliments from women whom I don't know around my workplace, ranging in age from 20's to 40's (I'm 23 myself). I don't think this fragrance shares a lot of the typical "Legend" DNA at all. Having said this, I'm yet to get my nose on the original Legend, but own Legend Intense and Legend Spirit, and whilst those two fragrances share some similarities to an extent, Special Edition 2014, seems to be a black sheep, so to speak. Perhaps best suited for Spring, hot Summer nights or warmer Autumn weather, this is my favourite fragrance from the Legend series.

Rive Gauche has grown on me. I’ve always liked it, smelling it a bit late in the game in the early 1990s on a friend who had a perfect balance of chic and practicality. She had a discerning, unpretentious knack for picking from high and low cultures what suited her best. She wore Rive Gauche and it fit her perfectly. Recently I wrote that I preferred Paco Rabanne’s Calandre to RG. Call me sometimey, but today I prefer RG. Their similarities allow their differences to come into view clearly. Calandre is an aldehydic rose floral that winds up with a vaguely bitter green chypre drydown that I wouldn’t have expected at the outset. It’s a beautiful trajectory over time. RG’s aldehydes last longer and move the rose into the sweet viscous shadow of a tonka/galbanum gumminess that feels like a thick incensy resin. Despite Calandre’s reference to metal (chrome grill), RG has more of a metallic feel. It’s cool with a bit of that flinty smell shared by metal and stone. There is a constant question among the perfume set. What is a good rose for men? Here’s your answer.

I wasn't aware that YSL had reformulated this fragrance and I'm rather disappointed that I'll never get to compare the original to this scent. I'm usually back and forth with aldehydes. In some fragrances I love the powdery and soapy quality that it gives, while in other scents, (for example, Chanel No.5), I hate how it smells sharp and unpleasant. When I first sprayed Rive Gauche I immediately classed it as a sharp and unpleasant aldehydic fragrance. It was so strong and nose-burning, that it was almost like a bomb had hit me right in the nostrils. I quickly stuffed this sample into my pocket in case I became nauseated from the scent and soon forgot about it. When I finally got home I emptied my pockets and wondered what smelt so elegant, rich and flowery. It was Rive Gauche. When the aldehydic opening softens, the scent becomes feminine and romantic. The rose note is delicate with the gardenia, magnolia and jasmine creating such a beautiful floral blend. It has that delightful, classic type scent which I love. It's difficult to re-create these types of scents which hold so much class, sophistication and elegance in a bottle. Although I feel as if I'm a little too young to start wearing Rive Gauche, I can always look forward to growing older in hopes of one day owning this wonderful scent.

Rive Guache was a cultural staple in the 1970s with those trendy commecials on the TV. My mother caught YSL fever and had a bottle in the 1976. Ah yes, every Friday at cocktail time she would don her fur, spray it liberally and it lingered behind. For a few years it was her signature. I was fascinated by its chic character. And it came in a can! Revolutionary! The Designer Imposters followed. I found a large vintage can last year-indeed its a lifetime supply. It is a cold metal aldehydic rose-jasmine-ylang ylang masterpeice. I would say more than 30 notes or more. It works best in the cold snowy winter as the revolving door of florals drift on the wind. The metallic quality has since vanished from the current market. Just how was that note created? The drydown is reserved. It lasts a nice 16 hours. The can just feels good in your hand. I tried a smaller refromulated version in 2005. It was not right. Somewhat plastically and wierd. It only becomes authentic during the drydown. This is simply too late in my opinion. I knew something was wrong at YSL. By 2009 when L'Oreal Paris took over, I knew the end had come. Rive Gauche is now discontinued

This has an Manish presence to it it's almost unisex the scent of dry woody Aldehydes makes it adrogymous. i can detect fringes of rose there is a sort of bitterness in this that makes it unique then other women Fragrances dries down into lemon. the scent reminds me of sequoia burning or the scent of burning Paper the violet brings an powdery feel. This has a 70's chic feel to it with it's Blue and Black and silver lines running horizonaly though an cylinder shaped flacon conjoures up Paris in 1977 with it's smoky discoteques and open air cafes. this is a scent for women who dares to be different to break with conventional Bourgeoisie.

If you are a vintage scent lover, chances are you have already smelled this beautiful scent and know how wonderful it is, so I won't bore you with my take on this cult classic. However, I recently purchased a bottle of the vintage cologne and I didn't expect much longevity, but I am thrilled to report that the cologne lasted an entire day and and lingered into the next morning. So, the good news is if you are having a hard time finding an affordable bottle in the EDT, you may want to give the cologne a try.
This was every where in the late '70s to early '80s and was very popular amongst women in their early 20s.

If you name your profile "rive gauche," you should dedicate the first post to this fragrance. When "rive gauche" (rg) was launched in 1971, it was advertised with a young woman in a gray wool flannel suit at a blue telephone, with the slogan "Le parfum des femmes imprévisible.
She was the first perfumist I encountered in this life. It was 1987, I had just turned 19 and she was not much older.

On page 191 of the English edition of the novel "The Children Act" (published in 2014 by Jonathan Cape, London), there is a sentence that perfectly describes the personality of Judge Fiona Maye in a single fragrance association: “Her perfume was Rive Gauche.

Recently, I ran into an old acquaintance whom I hadn't seen in many years: Rive Gauche, a true Parisian. During our casual chit-chat, I increasingly felt that she had lost quite a bit of her esprit and savoir-vivre since our last encounter. I discreetly studied my counterpart.

...Spoiler: There is a happy ending! I really like the original Black Opium. Unfortunately, it had to move out again sooner or later because its H+S (on me) sadly disappointed. Accordingly, I was very eager for the Intense variant, hoping for more "staying power" from it. Fortunately, I was able to snag a bottle from a nice online retailer in Italy. It arrived today, and with great anticipation, I immediately applied the fragrance generously... Act 1: I rejoice with delight! Shortly after spraying, I am enveloped by an incredibly intense and dark fruity note, paired with the full aroma of freshly brewed black coffee. According to the fragrance pyramid, blue absinthe should also make a guest appearance here... Unfortunately, I have no idea what absinthe is supposed to smell like. With alcohol, I prefer it, surprise - surprise, rather fruity and sweet. Act 2: Suddenly, the love story takes a dramatic turn! The heart note spreads, creeping in the form of the now well-known 'Jasmin-Sambac'. Suddenly, the scent changes completely and reminds me a lot of "Alien" by Mugler. I am incredibly disappointed, almost angry about this development. I have nothing against "Alien" itself; I even owned it for a long time. But... If I want to smell like "Alien," I will just reach for "Alien"! Annoyed, I stop sniffing my wrist. I sulk, curse everything and everyone. (Hey, it is indeed a drama!) But then... Act 3: The redemption comes in the form of an espresso macchiato, crowned with vanilla milk foam. It drives the evil jasmine away or pushes it so far into the background that it remains perceptible - but at least the Alien has been shot back into space. Relief spreads. The audience breathes a sigh of relief, applause rings out. That's how it should be, and that's how it can stay. And it does! Because the H+S is truly successful, and the beautiful, deep blue shimmering bottle rightfully carries the addition "Intense". All's well that ends well.

I bought the fragrance blindly at the airport. From the bottle, I was immediately convinced and had to add this scent to my collection. By now, I own every fragrance from YSL. I was very skeptical, as I have often been disappointed by "Intense" scents. Unfortunately, many smell like the original. But here, the coffee and the creamy sweetness stand out clearly. When you spray the fragrance, a light breeze of coffee first wafts into your nose. Generally, I am not a fan of this scent, but here it fits perfectly. After a while, the lightly creamy sweetness joins in. To me, it smells like café au lait. But really just delicately. The vanilla softens this fragrance a bit and makes it rounder, but definitely much more "Intense" than the original. Of course, you immediately notice when sniffing that it is Black Opium. The sillage is enormous and perhaps too much for some. You definitely fill the waiting room at Dr. Stefan Frank's office. Whether some ladies or gentlemen will agree with that remains to be seen. Otherwise, the fragrance is very captivating and erotic in its own unique way. I have often been approached, especially by male acquaintances. Some find the scent attractive and wanted to know the name, others wanted to know the time.

Hello you beasts (I mean you ladies, but I mean that in a nice way, honestly :D)! After I introduced a rather terrible sweet fragrance yesterday with Aquolina "Sweet Me," today we have Black Opium EDP Intense by Yves Saint Laurent, which is also quite sweet and synthetic, but smells significantly better, and you can really "see" how to do sweet and/or synthetic fragrances right. I should mention beforehand that such fragrances still may not suit everyone's taste, so this scent might not appeal to some of you despite my review. For those who enjoy such a scent, however, this is a great going-out fragrance (even if there are better ones). A fragrance to appear particularly sweet and sexy, with which they can then lurk somewhere in the night for unsuspecting guys to pounce on and… get a drink bought for them? Sure, until the next, better-looking guy appears and you get thrown into the water like a rock, boo hoo hoo :DDD Ugh, I should probably not write about sexy fragrances when I'm not in a good mood, or else I'll just complain even more about beastly ladies, he he he :D But anyway, let's get to the scent! The Scent: The scent starts off sweet and slightly bitter. The sweetness mainly comes from jasmine, alongside a bitter note that I can't quite identify (which might be the absinthe?) and it also has a coffee scent, which, due to the sweetness, reminds me of sweet iced coffee. There are also powdery notes included, which make the scent softer and gentler, thus enhancing the aura of a feminine fragrance. This is further intensified later on, as the scent comes across as quite creamy and soft due to the powdery and sweet notes along with a hint of coffee, which you can hardly smell later on. This not only makes it pleasant but also gives it a sexy vibe. Overall, the scent remains as described, but I find that in the later base it starts to smell a bit too sultry, as I perceive the floral notes as somewhat heavy. Aside from that, the scent has a nice quality and remains quite sexy for a while, even though it is not a very complex fragrance or something entirely new. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is good, although I wouldn't describe it as extremely room-filling. Nevertheless, the scent is very noticeable. The longevity is quite high, lasting twelve hours or even more. The Bottle: The bottle has the typical shape of all Opium fragrances. It is slightly oval with a large "porthole" in the middle, allowing a glimpse into the fragrance liquid. This time, the bottle is more blue than violet, but still has the familiar glitter elements "sticking" to it. The blue color of the bottle makes everything look like a night sky filled with many stars. The cap is hemispherical and resembles a button to press. Overall, a beautiful bottle. So, I liked the scent. I found both the sweetness of the fragrance and the coffee note quite nice. As mentioned at the beginning, this fragrance is also quite synthetic, but in a way that does not make it smell too cheap; rather, this synthetic quality is simply typical for certain mainstream fragrances. It doesn't bother me here, but I can imagine that this scent will not appeal to everyone, even though I believe it is not just a fragrance for very young girls. Especially since after a few hours, the scent becomes noticeably heavier (which I could have done without, but that's a matter of taste). In terms of fragrance direction, it is not an everyday scent, but more suitable for going out. This could be for a date (*sigh* I should have one too… :D), for dancing or partying, just to appear hot and sexy, and such things. All of this is best in autumn and winter, as it could be overwhelming in summer due to its high sweetness. I would recommend you to try it, but since I already said that the scent won't please everyone, I hope you won't complain too much with me if you sacrifice an arm for the scent and it doesn't actually appeal to you :D With that, I'm done. I wish you all a lovely evening, and until next time :)

Yesterday, my perfume sales associate offered me Black Opium Intense - which I immediately identified as a treat. I also enjoy the original Black Opium and was curious about this flanker. With just one spritz, I envisioned a delicious Irish Coffee - topped with a fluffy, creamy dollop of whipped cream. I personally don’t drink alcohol, but I enjoy the scent of it in various drinks - including Intense. The jasmine brightens the fragrance - and sandalwood wraps it up. A friendly scent that gives you the hint of a buzz - without having consumed any alcohol. A hangover is definitely spared - only the association of a cuddly little kitten remains. For me, it's a sensual fragrance that pairs well with my original Black Opium.

30 ml for under 40 euros? You can order that blindly. I have the "regular" BO as a sample, so at least I know that one. It arrived today, and it’s wonderful. Absinthe seems to be something more "herbaceous," but I find the Black Opium Intense to be very floral and elegant at the start. But then the licorice note quickly comes in for me. It makes the fragrance exceptional. It never risks sliding into any 08/15-floral scent that I've already smelled a thousand times. Since I’m a coffee lover, I wish the coffee note would come out a bit stronger for me. Even with the "Black Opium (Eau de Parfum) | Yves Saint Laurent," I unfortunately don’t smell it that well. But it doesn’t matter; the licorice compensates for that. So, Black Opium Intense adds a lovely floral scent with a depth of licorice and a (too) subtle coffee note to my fragrance collection. Blue is one of my favorite colors; the bottle is so beautiful with its black base and blue glitter. It gives it a mysterious touch and fits nicely with the fragrance.

Black Opium is a bit meh for me. I don't think it's bad, but it's quite short-lived and rather generic. However, I have always found a coffee note in perfumes extremely interesting. That's why I gave the Intense a chance. And indeed, it has that certain something that I miss in BO. I smell more coffee, which makes it more interesting.

When I first tried Black Opium Intense on the test strip at Douglas, I thought to myself, what a bitter mess, who would buy something like this? So, I ordered a sample of the standard Black Opium from a dear Parfuma and compared it with the dupe from La Rive. I was a bit disappointed because I had hoped that the original would smell longer and more intense than the dupe.

...at least that's what I thought. When Black Opium intense was released, I had to test it. After all, the original is already delicious. So off to the big M to give it a try. Yes, damn it, what was that supposed to be? It smelled to me like old men's perfume. What a bummer. This won't do.

The scent often reminds me of the first dates with my husband. How we sat one evening in a bar and ordered coffee instead of cocktails while the rain tapped against the window. The smell of coffee spreads throughout the bar within seconds, accompanied by the scent of several men's perfumes.

For me, there is no comparable scent, and it broke my heart when it was discontinued. No other fragrance from the line comes close to it. The absinthe is very sparkling at the top, the sweetness of the licorice nestles beneath it, surrounded by jasmine, all underscored by strong coffee. Fragrance notes that seemingly do not fit together, but harmonize so enchantingly.

The name! The name just doesn't sound right. Beguiled. That's why I wear this perfume very rarely, because I can never remember how "it" actually smelled. And every time I realize: What a HUGE MISTAKE! I will simply write "Betört" on the bottle. The word doesn’t sound much prettier either, but at least I know what it’s about. Beguiled starts off fresh and fruity and really very, very beautiful, but it doesn’t blow me away. I’m not captivated yet. But! When it then secretly and slyly connects with the body and its own warmth, an aura is created that cannot be ignored (and won’t be wanted to be ignored). It should actually be visible around me. In the color of the sky sometimes, rosy lilac with a bit of sun in the background. And a scent develops that is truly enchanting. I want to hug myself constantly, gently yet with ulterior motives. It’s probably the pepper. Floral, soft, caressing, somehow familiar and yet to be enjoyed with proverbial caution. Kankuro has already hit the nail on the head in his statement about the perfume. I’m actually writing this review just so that the next time I look at "Beguiled," I immediately think: Ah, THAT! (I’m still not sure if I’ll relabel the bottle...) Of course, it’s a floral Roja. Of course, you can tell it’s a floral Roja for women. Of course, you can tell that Roja has floral scents for ladies. He just does. And? That’s okay. Beguiled is still different. And when I finally wear it again, like today, I still don’t know WHAT exactly it is that captivates and fascinates me about it. But that’s okay. I believe that one rarely knows exactly WHAT it is that one finds attractive or indeed ENCHANTING about someone or something. Witchcraft? Could be. In any case, I find myself extremely enchanting today. Primarily for myself, which is enough for me, because Beguiled lasts long, but it’s a rather quiet scent, with which you will only captivate those who come almost too close. Perfect in that respect!

While I love the original Black Opium for the powerful, sexy, yet approachable vanilla-jasmine-coffee bomb that it is (those are three of my favorite notes, after all, so of course I love it), it never felt like "me." Illicit Green does. It's still powerful and sexy, but it's also bright and a little bit playful and fun. The fig-pear combo is so juicy, fresh, and sweet. I was so sad to see this discontinued, and right after I ran out of my last bottle! It was one of the last designer perfumes I had in my collection. I'll keep trying the newer additions to the line as they come out but I doubt anything will ever beat this for me.

Illicit Green starts out lighter and cleaner, in my opinion, versus the original Black Opium EDP. With that, the opening has always felt pretty messy, especially compared to this. Here, I get the green mandarin note, some of the pear. But, what really comes through from the jump is the fig/fig leaf. This opens greenish, somewhat fruity, with plenty of the coffee note already peaking through. Really, the pear and mandarin are adding a sparkling brightness to the mix and some sweetness. However, those two note are never particularly massive on my skin. I dig its freshness and its less heavy and cloying than many of the others in this Saint Laurent series. As we move along, the fruitiness that is there will tone down. You will get more of the vanilla and coffee that the original has. For me, the coffee is the stronger of the two throughout. That, with: fig, jasmine, orange blossom and some patchouli. The final dry down is a light coffee aroma, with the vanilla, and what’s left of that fig and jasmine note. Kind of sweet, soft, with a bit of a powdery feel to it all.

I'm on the fence with this. The initial spray is almost unpleasant - I get a bitter coffee and some sourness. That very quickly dissipates and then I get a bright fresh green scent. This feels unique in that very few wintery scents have this level of brightness, but the coffee and creaminess brings in squarely into cold-weather fragrance territory. I love fig scents but with this one, the fig scent is mild but I do get it on the dry down. Overall, I am not sure what to make of this scent, I'm not sure it's something I'd reach for in my collection, but it is an interesting and unique scent in the Black Opium line.

Fig, coffee, jasmine, vanilla. Very green and almost sour in the initial spray, which then settles down into the regular black opium DNA. It’s perhaps slightly fruitier/fresher than the original, but not by a lot. It’s very smooth and creamy, but also quite deep and dense, so not a scent I’d reach for in summer. Absolutely perfect for winter, though. The fig is luscious.

Initial spray is pure greens and citrus, enough to give you a headache. Then dries down to a spicy, zesty mixture, and finally fades into a warm, woody patchouli. I don't know how this is marketed as a sweet gourmand perfume, as I am getting no sweetness from this. It's just very...green. Definitely prefer the original Black Opium.

My collector's heart has been eager since the first sight of this new offshoot of Black Opium: would I want to let one of those brightly green-windowed bottles into my collection? BO is not my fragrance direction, on the other hand, I love green bottles, and the prospect of a version of this bestseller in "my" color awakens desire.

Today I received the fragrance as a sample in my mailbox. Right after spraying, I was initially pleased, as this version had nothing in common with the original Black Opium (which I can't appreciate at all). I detected an almost citrus note that I found refreshing and light.

Yesterday I entered the branch with M to quickly buy a few drugstore items. I actually wanted to hurry....yajaaa. But I just can't walk past the perfume department without testing a few scents. I tried a bit here and there, but nothing really caught my attention yesterday.

Inoffensive and somewhat soapy from beginning to end, but that doesn't mean it's boring. I find it quite hard to decipher, in fact. The musky, warm, and slightly woody base is perceptible early on already, which I quite enjoy. The iris and neroli feel like a natural continuation of the opening citruses — which, while quite enjoyable, are rather fleeting — and, at the same time, act like a perfect segue into the depths of the comforting base. Once in the spotlight, the clean musk and mild woodsy undertones make it clear what this scent is: a lovely second skin.

Tested at printemps shop which have all the ysl vestiaire collection. I find this which attires my curiosity. Finally nothing of news a smelling of neroli which reminds me neroli villa bdk or prada day for night and even tf neroli portofino Difficult to find a fragrances which has new scent. Doesn t matter i don t buy this. Perfect for summer and unisex Hold weak maybe 3 hours

Apparently not a widely known fragrance, Trench. Only 16 Parfumos own it, and only 4 of them are men. Both of these facts surprise me, as I find Trench neither bad nor feminine. Completely unisex, just as it is declared. Moreover, I have never let the gender-based percentage distribution stop me from buying a fragrance that is predominantly owned by women. The l'Homme from the same house is more feminine/metrosexual - and it is declared as a men's fragrance. Trench starts with a wonderfully fresh, slightly woody, and somewhat fruity top note, which comes across as very elegant, modern, and unobtrusive. The composition is led here directly by bergamot and fig, underpinned by iris, musk, and fir. There is also a slightly bitter/sour note that makes it more interesting than other standard citrus fragrances. I would be lying if I didn't guess that this comes from the tangerine or neroli, or the interplay of the two. I like it anyway. Keyword iris: it gives the fragrance a perfect measure of powderiness and adds elegance. The Prada l'homme, which also whistles a very similar tune, has overdone it with the iris in my opinion, making it too dominant, so that the fragrance comes across as somewhat "heavy" and cloying. Trench has solved this better. Once the iris distributes its powderiness, it is replaced by neroli with a handshake, and together with the musk and cedar, you get a wonderful, slightly greenish base note that lingers until the fragrance fades away. All in all, an extremely pleasant, crowd-pleasing yet distinctive fragrance, suitable for any occasion and any time of day. Perfect for spring and summer, for the office, for stylish outings during the day, or as a room fragrance for those for whom money plays a less important role in life :D The only thing that makes me smile a bit is the longevity. It is not terribly bad for a fresh fragrance of this class, but it could certainly be better, considering the price. 5-6 hours are quite achievable, although Trench becomes more intimate after 4 hours and no longer radiates. I can definitely recommend it - Trench will surely accompany me often this spring and summer and be a member of my wardrobe.

Today I received the envelope from the boutique with the sample they sent me to try before getting my full bottle – and I have to say, the fragrance is absolutely fantastic! It opens with a bright, uplifting burst of orange and peach that immediately takes you to the skies. Once it starts to settle on the skin, you can sense the familiar DNA of Diaghilev Parfum coming through – but in a much younger, lighter, and more wearable version. It’s less spicy, less heavy than the original Diaghilev, yet still retains that refined elegance. The blend with Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2024) adds a smooth sweetness of vanilla and amber that perfectly rounds it out. This is definitely a fragrance for those who find the original Diaghilev too bold or mature – this one makes that profile much more approachable and versatile. Extremely well done and high quality. A scent that fits so many situations, and in my opinion, absolutely worth it for anyone who loves this kind of olfactory profile.

It was a warm summer evening in London, and the sun was slowly disappearing behind the rooftops of the city. I had been waiting all day to finally open the small, heavy bottle that I had picked up from the dealer with trembling hands. There were only 210 of these, and one was now in front of me. The golden light of the evening filtered through the glass, making the contents shimmer like liquid amber. With the first spray, a radiant citrus accord spread through the air-bright, clear, almost like freshly squeezed orange juice, but more refined, smoother, restrained by an invisible hand. I closed my eyes and for a brief moment felt as if I were back on the first floor of Harrods Perfumery, where Roja Dove once had his boutique. The notes evolved further, and with them, my mood shifted. After the radiant opening, a warm, almost velvety vanilla settled on my skin. Along with it, a hint of peach, sweet but not cloying, more like the smile of a familiar person you meet again after a long time. And then, suddenly, the depth arrived: leather, amber, a dark, sun-soaked labdanum. The fragrance took on a gravity, a seriousness as if to say, "Beauty alone is not enough; you also need presence." I caught myself standing in front of the mirror longer than usual. The scent felt like a garment that you don’t just wear, but that transforms you. Suddenly, I was not just me-I was a little taller, a little more confident, a little more in harmony with myself. When I later stepped out onto the street, the sillage mingled with the cool evening air. A stranger woman paused briefly, looked at me, and smiled. She said nothing, but I knew she had noticed it. Not just the fragrance, but also what it had awakened in me. In that moment, it became clear to me: Roja Dove Perfumery is not just a perfume. It is a memory of all the journeys, conversations, and encounters that Roja has woven into the world of scents, and at the same time, a small piece of eternity, captured in 210 bottles.

Here it is. As a big Roja fan, I had to get this fragrance and was already invited to the official launch event at Harrods by the Roja Dove Perfumery. There, I had the chance to meet Roja Dove himself. He shared a lot about the history of his works and how this fragrance came to be. Interestingly, it was his employees who came up with the 21 idea. At 21, you are really truly of age in the UK. So, does the fragrance smell grown-up? Mhm, yes and no. For me, it’s just right: You take aldehydes - the floral notes of Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2019) - the fruity aspect and peach from Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie (2024) - the juicy orange juice opening (thankfully not too sweet) of Lost in Paris And underneath, it pushes a more modern and pleasant atmosphere with a clearly recognizable DNA from Diaghilev Parfum . Et voila. We have the fragrance. I love this version. If I could only keep one of the three, it would be this one, as it brings everything together. For some, it might be different, but I am happy for the chance to meet Roja and to have acquired the fragrance. The Perfumery releases have all been strong, including Chou Chou and many more, but unfortunately, some of the recent Roja Parfums releases have been less exciting. Let’s see how Elysium Noir turns out in the fall… I hope you get the chance to test it.

After months of waiting, the long-awaited fragrance finally arrived. I have had almost only good experiences with Roja so far, which is why I was particularly excited about this one. As soon as it arrived, I had to test it immediately... And WOW! It starts with a real explosion of scent from light citrus, soft leather, and above all one thing: vanilla. It impressed me so much that I had to write my first review about it.. Over time, more notes emerge: After the citrus quickly fades away for me, subtle floral notes, amber, and labdanum join in. However, vanilla remains the star of the show, although it now also gets a co-star. Peach! I was particularly looking forward to this as it has definitely become one of my favorite notes, and it fits perfectly here. From here, a certain familiarity with the scent profile develops, and I pondered for a long time where I knew it from... until it finally dawned on me: "Triumph of Bacchus (Eau de Parfum) | Argos." This combination of peach and vanilla bears an extremely strong resemblance to the ToB for me. This is not meant to be negative at all; I think it smells amazing, but well, it is also quite known... We don't need to discuss price-performance; like most Rojas, this one is also very expensive, and everyone has to decide for themselves whether it is worth the money :) The bottle and lacquer box are, of course, a 10 as is typical for Roja. Is the fragrance good? Definitely, for me a 10/10. Should you get it? Well, aside from the bottle, the packaging, and the fact that it is limited, I would say that you can definitely get the ToB for a better price. Best regards, Maik :)

Caban has a unique quality to it I’ve tried hard to describe, even to myself. The best way I can express what this perfume evokes in me is to equate it to the cooking of sugar. Bear with me. If you have ever cooked sugar, you may be familiar with the few seconds between the sugar (glucose) being converted to fructose (or goes a second too long and is slightly burned). This is where the concoction rests on a knife’s edge between sweet and bitter. Caban, to my nose, does this. Balances the sweetness from the tonka, the tanginess of the elemi with the bitter notes from the (my guess) sandalwood. It hangs there and for a moment my nose isn’t sure if it will go bitter or sour. It never does; it’s stays dancing there like those few seconds between sugar’s changeover. This tug of war keeps the entire experience interesting from start to finish. It’s never too sweet. Never too tangy. Never too bitter. It’s Goldilocks—just right.

It is very pointedly sweet at the beginning. Not dark, broadly sweet, but pointed, in one note extremely sweet. I can't smell any pepper at all. It's more this pointed gummy bear sweetness. For me, it's actually too sweet, slightly even a bit chemical, but not in the way one might imagine, rather like industrial syrup. Once it has completely unfolded, it doesn't really change its DNA. The tonka bean comes through very slightly. The gummy bear aspect diminishes a bit. Still, one of the sweetest fragrances I have ever smelled, and for me definitely a women's perfume. However, I don't really like it in general, as it is way too sweet for me.

Caban is the fragrance that everyone forgets when talking about Babycat or Tuxedo . To me, Caban smells like an autumn evening in the city. I walk through the cool streets. Golden light. Leaves rustle underfoot and the trench coat fits perfectly. On my way to the restaurant, I already sense that red wine and good conversations await me. The opening is like a little toast: a hint of liqueur, warm and sweet, barely there, then gone again. Then pepper crackles on the skin. And then comes what makes the fragrance so special: sandalwood in its most beautiful form. Creamy, soft, almost velvety. How beautiful you are! Tonka bean brings a delicate sweetness that never tips into dessert territory. Patchouli gently blends in and adds depth. The most beautiful balance between sweet, spicy, and woody. Caban is grown-up and elegant. A fragrance that acts like a statement without ever being loud. For me, it is the epitome of autumn chic. The most beautiful sandalwood scent in my collection - and perhaps the most underrated masterpiece in the YSL universe.

The sun shines on the sparkling water. We take the boat to downtown Stockholm. Shy Swedish summer. Not too warm. Not too cold. Actually just perfect. My Anna has decided to test perfumes. With determination, we head to NK. I haven't dealt with perfume for years. Out of conviction. Today, I want to engage with it again. I expect nothing. We browse through the standard scents. But just like in my memory: Actually, everything in this area is too alcoholic for me. Too unremarkable. Too loud. Too sweet. I am mostly here for her sake and browse. Still without expectation. Since she also doesn't find anything suitable, we actually ask an advisor. I don't even remember what we asked for, but then we stand in front of this chic line from Yves Saint Laurent. The La Vestiaires. My design-loving eye is pleased with this minimalist elegance. He shows us two scents from this line, and right from the first one, I am blown away. I can hardly believe it. Caban. It flows softly onto the skin. Noble and fine, without shouting it to the world. My nose immediately detects a very light coconut scent. Wrapped in a cozy blanket. Very comfortable, very sensual. Not too sweet, despite the very light hint of patchouli. It smells exactly like we want to smell. Confident, with a touch of playfulness. Calm, yet well aware of its enchanting fragrance note. Cozy like a delicate cloud bath. There it is now. On our wrists. And as we continue to stroll through the city, we have to keep smelling our wrists. It smells like vacation and at the same time like a warmly wrapped afternoon in the favorite cozy corner. We don't buy it that day. We want to test it. We both wish for its longevity and a very light sillage. The next day, we almost rush back because we can't get the scent out of our heads. However, its longevity was not particularly good the previous day. The sillage was almost nonexistent. Standing in front of it, we decide against it again for those reasons. For the price, you just want everything to be right. A week later. Anna orders this new favorite scent. It simply has to be hers. She finds it heavenly. Loves it. It smells like her. I give the scent another chance as a sample. For me, scents generally tend to get darker. After a few hours, the gentle coconut scent fades a bit into the background, and patchouli becomes a bit stronger. Overall, a hint more spice comes through. Especially when I am in motion. That makes it even more interesting. It reminds both of us of the days in Stockholm. Of that shy summer by the sea. Of joy, friendship, lightness mixed with a delicate blanket of coconut and coziness. A coziness where one also enjoys exchanging interesting slightly spicy secrets. Nothing about it screams. And yet everything about it is simply beautiful. #coconut #vanilla #spicy #patchouli #cozyjumper #skindew

To me this smells straight up like church! I received a bottle of this as a gift alongside a little sample and while it is a beautifully blended scent with (in my opinion) high quality ingredients, I can't get over the fact that this smells exactly like church. Perhaps if I didn't have this association I could more easily wear this fragrance, however unfortunately that just isn't the case! That being said, having smelled quite a few of the other fragrances from the Yves Saint Laurent Le Vestiaire collection, this might be one of the most interesting and unique fragrance from the entire line. I am sure that the right nose can appreciate this more than me. A positive of this fragrance is that it is INSANELY long lasting! I could still smell this on me after having taken a shower. Therefore, while the perfume itself is quite expensive you really get a bang for your buck!

Dear Calice, dear Yves, thank you very much for your wonderful holiday impressions from the Orient. Your powerful words and images made your experiences feel so real that I felt like a part of your little travel group. In one photo, you are wearing a kaftan. Very unusual, as you are otherwise associated with high fashion and haute couture. But it fits your attitude that even the small details must be just right. Just the description of your hotel (Yves, the casual mention that it was a 5-star resort was unnecessary, because you wouldn't be Yves if it weren't a luxury hotel) with the delightful scent of fresh, zesty mandarin spiced with plenty of pepper already impressed me. I could immediately feel the pleasant contrast between the heat outside and the refreshingly cool air inside. The markets there must have been a special experience as well. I could immediately smell the aroma of spices and resins that unfolded their unique scent in the shimmering air. Surprisingly, they are not as dominant as I would have imagined. Not brutally spicy-resinous, but more a hint of both. Very invigorating and perfectly balanced. Although this was not your first trip to the Orient (I only recall the 1970s when you were already so impressed by the Orient that you launched Opium as a fragrance), you continually discover new things. Calice seems to be the perfect travel companion, as she apparently shares your passion. After all, how else can her intense collaboration with Kilian be explained? Of course, you visited what could be visited in such a short time. I know how inspiring new impressions are for you. The old Sultan's palace must have truly captivated you. Thick walls that create almost an icy cold inside, forming an exciting contrast to the heat. I also found it remarkable that this palace apparently managed without pomp, being rather sober, modest, and almost sacral in appearance. Your impression that a nearly clerical, cold scent of incense lingered in the walls fits perfectly into the picture. Normally, I shudder at this type of incense, as I don't particularly like it, but in this case, it must be a special incense. Who knows, perhaps the bowls anointed with musk ensured that the incense, despite its coldness and severity, also had something soft and harmonious? But one doesn't have to uncover every secret. Sometimes the allure lies precisely in the non-deconstruction. You asked me how I would describe a fragrance that would capture what you experienced. Well, I would say it is warm and cool at the same time, graceful and noble, dark and light, hard and soft, present yet reserved. But all together in a balanced and very harmonious ratio. What would I name it? Well, Kaftan of course ;-)) I look forward to more travel reports and experiences!

A topic that I have long overlooked in my fascination is incense. The thought of dealing with this cold smokiness left me literally cold. Certainly, there were one or two fragrances that hinted at incense in their scent pyramid, but never so clearly that it came across as a prominent or dominant note. Even "Ombre Nomade | Louis Vuitton," which was in my collection for a long time, was actually an incense fragrance that, however, opened up very well packaged and rather warm on my skin. However, those really nasty church incense scents stayed far away from me, as I wanted to spare my nose that experience. To further my education on my fragrance journey, I inevitably had to bring the "Blue Beast" Interlude Man under my nose. It was simply necessary as a learning effect for me to experience the scent that many refer to as THE Oriental incense. What can I say? It was neither very oriental nor a dominant incense. I felt more like I was near a glowing coal stove in the Italian countryside. Mainly oregano dominated, as if the Nonna was just starting the tomato sauce and there was no prominent smoke. Rather, a light hint of smoke that hardly came to the fore on my skin/in my nose. I was already surprised and disappointed that there was little of what I had expected. Perhaps Ombre Nomade had already toughened me up a bit. During a short visit or vacation in Stuttgart, I strolled happily into the Breuninger there with the goal of discovering something new. I sniffed around here and there and then rather accidentally passed by the YSL stand. Most people went straight for the Opium bottles, while I took the opportunity to test "Le Vestiaire - Babycat | Yves Saint Laurent," which had already caught my attention on the Parfumo site. Besides this, I wanted to try something else, and from the listed aromas, "Le Vestiaire - Caftan | Yves Saint Laurent" quickly shot into my field of vision. Pepper, incense, and resin? I simply had to test it. The beginning of the fragrance is certainly not easy and not for everyone. For my nose, a very citrusy component clashes with a gnarly, intense cistus. This feels quite exhausting and certainly a bit challenging in the first five to ten minutes; however, the further development is so convincing that a bottle was allowed to join my collection. So let's return to the beginning. This cistus feels dry, dark, and very blunt, as is usually recognizable from the darker labdanum varieties. Mixed with notes of orange and lemon, it feels crazy and totally unfamiliar, hence quite strenuous. In the further course, this impression is completely replaced by new and harmonizing notes that actually beam you into oriental realms. A fine note of pink pepper comes through. Some spiciness, a slight pepperiness. A fine benzoin note joins in, which comes across as very soft, slightly sweet, and lovely. The used benzoin contains aromas of light vanilla and delicate, rather unsweet honey, which is why the fragrance smells very noble, balanced, and high-quality. Additionally, there is an incense component that contains little cold smoke but rather feels warmer. In general, the light smoke is paired with the benzoin, which makes a great partner that enjoys being caressed by this light smokiness and thus appears suitable for many occasions. Because one must say directly, this is not a showstopper, but a gentleman who has manners and knows how to dress. A fragrance that does not fill entire rooms in the office but is elegant enough to distribute its wonderful aroma so that the right people notice it. A fragrance that can be worn at a chic party and can also act as a feel-good scent. A great companion in autumn, lovely resting on the neck in winter, and even a delightful companion for romantic summer evenings. You can enjoy the fragrance for at least eight hours, and depending on the conditions, it can last even longer. It is an oriental allrounder that one can only wish for and that truly knows how to charm the wearer. It is the fragrance that could have been Interlude, but Amouage opted for the Italian showstopper. Those who want to smell noble, desire a pleasant allrounder that truly fits everywhere, should take a look at Caftan and test it. Certainly, the first minutes may not be to everyone's liking, but the further development compensates for that in full. Of course, ladies can also wear this wonderful fragrance, as this combination of light smoke and beautiful resinousness is definitely unisex.

When I first sprayed the fragrance in the small perfumery, I immediately thought of my grandmother's spice drawer in her kitchen. My grandma could cook fantastically and made dishes from all over the world, which was quite extraordinary for an older Danish lady in the 60s and 70s. Because these were such unusual spices, we grandchildren loved to peek into her drawer, open the little jars, and dive into 1001 Nights adventures, at least in our imagination. Her drawer smelled strongly of oriental and exotic spices. Dry, very spicy, somehow adventurous, yet warm and inviting. That's exactly how "Le Vestiaire - Caftan | Yves Saint Laurent" smells. Extremely spicy, super dry, very oriental and warm, also so unique and a bit addictive. A bit like being in a spice souk in Arabia somewhere. I hardly notice the fruity notes, but I do clearly perceive pink pepper. Later on, a lot of incense comes through, a very, very spicy incense that is made sweet, rounded, and almost warm by a dreamy benzoin. In the drydown, a lot of musk comes through, but overall and until the end, the fragrance remains a dry, warm spice bomb that admittedly smells fantastic. For some reason, the scent exudes a lot of elegance at the same time. A fragrance that Cleopatra could have worn. I spend the whole day wondering whether I like the fragrance or if it is just too spicy? I love the scent as an experience, as a state, or as a memory of my grandma, but whether I would wear the fragrance is now the big question. Do I want to smell like a spice souk?? Hmmm?? I believe you have to wear a special outfit to carry the fragrance well, if that makes sense; otherwise, the fragrance carries its wearer and not the other way around. Classic and hyper elegant/strict.. H+S is quite good…

During my decision-making process, I need an incentive to choose to purchase an expensive perfume. Two factors are particularly important here: It must be distinctive and perform strongly. In terms of the quality and purity of the ingredients, Caftan is undoubtedly a good perfume. However, Calice Becker has drawn inspiration from many uniquely crafted oriental perfumes. When you take a close look at Caftan, you can find traces of the following fragrances in the background: YSL M7, Gucci pour Homme (2003), Bentley for Men Intense. Rather, the character traits of Lupin's Idole are present. Caftan is oriental, resinous, warm, wintry. Beautiful, but nothing special and widely available on the perfume market. The performance is in the green zone. However, the previously mentioned perfumes are longer-lasting. The purchase is worthwhile for those who do not have extensive collections of oriental fragrances or who have only recently started exploring the world of perfume. For veterans, Caftan is not unique enough.

I am quite perplexed why L'Oscar isn't talked about more. When sprayed it, I immediately sensed a bouquet of different notes. It opens up with mild grapefruit note which in seconds dies down and gracefully stays in the backround. There is a really beautiful labdanum note which gives almost green leathery creaminess ( it is quite hard to explain), I guess the nice sweetness comes from the mayflower and the mild spiciness comes from carnation. The base has very nice woodiness ( from sandalwood, guaiac wood and cedar), which is very well accompanied by the spiciness of the pepper and nutmeg and also complemented by the earthiness and bitterness that comes from the oakmoss and vetiver. And let's not forget the celery seeds, which is an interesting addition that in my opinion, makes this fragrance more memorable. It is a very well blended ( well duh. It's Roja) and unique smelling fragrance. I wouldn't call this a "compliment getter", but if you wear this- you will stand out and make an impression. I would say L'Oscar belongs in the same category as for example: Creed's Royal Oud, in the sense that if you wear a simple t shirt and jeans, the fragrance will wear you and not vice versa. This is as bourgeois, posh as it gets. You have to be at least semi- dressed up to "fit" this fragrance. I would say this could be worn easily in spring, fall and winter. Summer could work too, if not too hot. Longevity and sillage is quite good. I like it.

I associate this scent with the essential oils diffused into the air during massage therapy. It has tranquil aroma-therapy-like qualities. A touch of pungent sour-like citrus freshens the scent, especially in the opening, but it is quickly dominated by cistus (incense-like, resinous), a very warm bouquet of spicy-fresh florals, all of which are anchored by Roja's signature opulent woods. The scent can be described as citrusy, resinous, warm, spicy-fresh floral, smooth, herbal, earthy, and peppery.

The headline summarizes my impression after about 20-30 minutes. L'oscar pour Homme was one of the Roja fragrances that really interested me, but unfortunately, I have to speak of disappointment again. This time, not in the form of the scent being bad, but in the form of seriously, is Roja Dove today Dua? L'oscar pour Homme only differs from Dalmatian Sage for 10-15 minutes due to a slightly different top note with grapefruit. I really can't describe L'oscar pour Homme at all. The fragrance pyramid is not reflected in the scent at all. I smell sage, citrus, vetiver, and a bit of leather (the leather makes a small difference). Unfortunately, I see an 85-90% similarity between L'oscar pour Homme and Dalmatian Sage. L'oscar pour Homme also has the same development as Dalmatian Sage, only the Roja is a bit denser and deeper due to the higher oil content. I simply find it difficult to describe a fragrance that completely deviates from the fragrance pyramid, especially because it makes it harder to recognize individual notes. The fragrance pyramid has always helped me have a kind of red thread when testing a new scent. I really cannot recommend anyone to buy L'oscar pour Homme, unless someone is looking for a Dalmatian Sage with better performance, but to pay a 5 times higher price per ml for that is of course possible, but I was really taken aback because paying €285 for such a dupe is not okay for me. The longevity is good at 9 hours, as is typical for Roja, and the sillage is good at about an arm's length. L'oscar pour Homme only becomes close to the skin after just over 8 hours. I simply cannot give a better rating due to the astonishing similarity.

The Hotel L'oscar London has been lavishly restored and designed by star interior designer Jaques Garcia. With its opening in May 2018, London gained another boutique hotel, this time with a very close collaboration with Roja Parfums. Thus, fragrance candles from the brand can be found in each of the elaborately designed rooms, which celebrate the opulent style of the Baroque. Everywhere there is velvet, leather, and precious woods. Upon closer inspection, everything reveals itself as a skillful interpretation of Baroque in our time. Modern materials and quality meet overflowing aesthetics that touch all the senses. "Every Saint has a past, Every Sinner has a future." The motto, so to speak the theme of the hotel, leaves room for imagination. After all, the building in Holborn was previously used as a church. So it is hardly surprising that the collaboration with Roja resulted in not just one exclusive fragrance, but one for each gender. Which of the two poles is that of the Saint or the Sinner, I gladly leave to you (when the opportunity arises) to decide. In terms of composition, L'oscar pour homme is clearly a Chypre. The (pink) grapefruit starts citrusy-sour and only minimally fruity. And yet very fresh. It is especially refreshing to not have bergamot presented as the opener. Right from the start, the floral accords announce themselves quite prominently, to say the least, almost a bit "loud." However, after a few minutes, everything organizes itself very skillfully, and it should be said that one should (like) (garden) cloves. They dominate the described burst at the beginning. The Mayflower (better known as lily of the valley) smooths the somewhat angular clove and, together with the grapefruit, creates a fresh-sour-floral bouquet. After a short time, resinous notes come into play, very subtly. Both galbanum and cistus contribute balsamic, slightly woody-smoky notes. They accentuate the described bouquet and give it depth. Something darker. Really beautiful. The pepper (from the base) radiates punctually into the composition and repeatedly adds a touch of spice, with a slight sharpness that fits very well with the clove. As the fragrance develops, green-herbaceous notes of moss and vetiver slowly complement the woody base and round off the scent in a masculine direction towards the drydown. L'oscar pour homme is, for me, a daytime fragrance, like most EDPs from Roja. It fits perfectly for the office or even in the beer garden. It performs well between 6-8 hours and is very easy to dose with the sprayers. It leaves room in the evening to wear another fragrance (depending on mood and occasion). Despite its masculine tendencies, I would also attribute unisex potential to it if you like herb-floral Chypres. Whether you are a Sinner or a Saint with it, I leave to you. Both are contained in this fragrance. PS: The fragrance can only be purchased at the hotel itself (in London) or via email (info@loscarlondon.com) for 245 GBP (+shipping).

I always felt like such a weirdo, when the original Libre wasn't my fav, I didn't hate it, it just wasn't me. Even the intense one. I am not the biggest vanilla girl, but something about this is just so well balanced. It smells expensive and floral and not heavy. The bottle is stunning oh my days it is gorg and i like this perfume a lot girl.

I love everything in the Libre line - Le Parfum is my favorite. I will say that to me, they all smell largely the same. Le Parfum is just more syrupy and intense. I love vanilla as well and fully expected Vanilla Couture to be my favorite. I like it a lot but honestly I do not smell a huge difference from the rest of the line. For me, VC seems a touch more blended and smooth. But I don't get a strong vanilla, and in a line up, I'm not convinced I could distinguish between this and some of the others. I suspect the lavender/orange blossom combo is so overpowering that my nose doesn't pick up on nuances between the flankers. That said, I really like this, it has great longevity, it smells pretty and sexy. Lovely date night perfume.

I was very curious about this new flanker in the beautiful bottle. The typical Libre DNA is recognizable here as well, just significantly simplified. The orange blossom has been toned down considerably, and the lavender is also much more restrained than in the predecessors. During the first half hour, Libre Vanille Couture evokes the least from all the flankers in the series for me. Familiar yet different, it feels a bit too arbitrary. Hm... Once the opening settles, the new promised twist becomes apparent. A vanilla that beautifully shifts between soft sweet and warm soft. I don't catch any rum in my nose. Too bad, I could have imagined a well-crafted boozy touch as an exciting variant for cold winter evenings and fancy occasions. On the other hand, Libre Vanille Couture thus avoids drifting into the more gourmand territory and can maintain the more mature aura of its predecessors. Overall, the fragrance becomes significantly more harmonious from this point on, gaining a snug quality that I can particularly envision for the colder months. So, is it a new candidate for purchase? I love the Libre line mainly for its rather "edgy" DNA, the interplay of cool and warm, bossy and feminine. This somewhat gets lost in "Libre Vanille Couture | Yves Saint Laurent," which is why the fragrance will probably not replace my favorite variant "Libre Le Parfum | Yves Saint Laurent," which it actually comes closest to for me. For anyone who already has one of its sisters in their closet, it’s probably not a revelation, but still nicely done and worth a test. Even those who found the predecessors perhaps too harsh might find happiness with this toned-down version.

Do I really still need you? I thought to myself after I heard about the release. I see the bottle .. read the notes .. YES, my Libre collection is probably going to get bigger! Ordered online from Paris right away .. a few days later it was there and I got to smell it for the first time .. once again a pricey blind buy. It was worth it! The original Libre is still there although for me it’s more the Libre Le Parfum but with such a dreamy vanilla drydown .. heavenly! I am in love! By the way, I don't perceive anything in the rum.

Here you initially get the original Libre DNA - lavender, orange blossom, and jasmine combined with vanilla - so nothing new at first. However, the scent is distinctly warmer and more vanillic from the very beginning (and of course throughout its entire development). It strongly reminds me of the Libre Le Parfum variant, but it is actually "different" in its vanilla. The listed candy vanilla shines through wonderfully here. An authentic, slightly earthy, and perhaps even minimally animalistic vanilla. So definitely not a mundane baking vanilla or something similar. I find the twist very exciting. However, I don't get the listed rum or any other boozy note. The bottle is also a dream and a "must-have" for Libre collectors and lovers. The limited edition makes it particularly appealing. Anyone who generally likes Libre and is not averse to vanilla should definitely give it a try. But please make sure to test it on the skin and give the scent a little time. The scent on the test strip was not remotely like it was on my skin even after several hours.

Wow.. the appearance is already a highlight, and the scent even more so! At first, I was a bit hesitant due to the price, but my eyes simply made the decision. It feels significantly more sensual than its predecessors. I imagine it being perfect for winter, with an elegant coat, red lips, and a tightly pulled-back ponytail on a date..

Libre is unfortunately not my line. I’ve tried them all, and somehow the lavender note doesn’t resonate with me here. Only the Libre Eau de Parfum Intense was the warmest for me. It's a shame that this one is limited. I would immediately add it to my collection after just one test!

A new Libre Eau de Parfum means only one thing for me as an ultimate Libre lover: I need a sample as soon as possible. Said and done. I had high expectations, as I own every Libre. Upon the first spray, I was smitten. I had fallen in love. The Libre DNA is present and is further complemented by notes of sweet vanilla. Important.

During my little short vacation in London last week, a visit to Harrods' "Salon de Parfums" was, of course, a must. On the 6th floor, strangelove nyc, Henry Jacques, and of course Roja Dove are all present, and as luck would have it, I actually had the opportunity to meet Roja in person. I felt like a little boy and had to take a moment to catch my breath and search for the right words so I wouldn’t come across as a total fool. It’s probably the respect I have for him that led to my initial gasping for breath ;) Anyway, we started chatting, and he actually took the time to guide me through his creations. Yes, of course he does that, and it’s certainly part of his sales strategy. However, at that moment, that was completely secondary to me. Rather, I enjoyed being treated as a customer in such a way that no wishes or questions were left unanswered. I felt absolutely wonderful! Semi-Bespoke 4 is a very beautiful fragrance, very finely crafted and natural. I have the feeling that all the ingredients come across much more clearly and intensely than in the "standard" Rojas. However, this might also be due to Mr. Dove using a variety of “fancy words” during his “sales pitch.” Doesn’t matter, the opening, with its zesty citrus fruits, is something special. The heart notes suggest a strongly floral DNA, which is not the case, as cinnamon, patchouli, and sandalwood from the base join in quite early on. The drydown is a dream of creamy-woody notes, a slightly powdery iris, and a varied play between earthy-bitter patchouli and sweet vanilla. The fragrance costs around €875, which is, of course, well beyond my budget. I am also sure that there are many very good alternatives with a similar DNA that cost significantly less. Nevertheless, it was an experience and a pleasure to enjoy a feeling of luxury in a truly extraordinary store, including Roja Dove. Wishlist!

…but this one comes in to a very close second… the people who say that the performance differential between this one an the 2017 version is minimal are lying to themselves… The scent is smoother, rounder, cleaner, and fuller than the 2017, and the performance is by far longer and stronger… I still prefer the EDP over this because it feels more “full” and has a more “mature” feeling “swagger” to it. I got an easy 10 hours of performance off of 6 sprays, and it opened with a 6ft radius of projection that lasted 5 of those 10 hours easily. The ending is quite loud as well. Very, very nice indeed. I’m much happier with this one than I was with the Parfum edition.

This IS an improvement from the 2017 version in -arguably- every sense, some people (me for example) will miss the nice violet+green apple mix note, but it lasts more. It DOES NOT last 10 hours, or even 8 hours like youtubers say, they probably don´t sweat and are not using it in summer. This is not by any means a beast fragrance like its sister EDP, it is right there and close to the Live version in performance, Live more stingy to the nose and better suited for open places, 2022 EDT is a tad softer because of the lavander and better suited for close spaces. It DOES last way more than the original EDT, if the 2017 lasts around 3+ hours in summer (on my skin, mild sweating on summer from time to time), the 2022 version lasts around 6 hours. maybe 7 tops hidden in your skin. Overall good, but I won´t recommend it at full price, if you want to get it, get it at a discount.

What initially caught my eye was an advertisement that claimed an increased longevity of the new 2022 EDT over its predecessor the original Y. I came across a sale on the Yves Saint Laurent website not long after seeing this advertisement, and with your purchase they gave you a sample of Black Opium for women. Having already owned Y Eau Fraiche and Y EDP, I took the opportunity to get the new Y EDT and Y Le Parfum and gave the Black Opium to my daughter. Now onto the juicy gossip…I must say that after wearing this for the first time the claims of increased projection and longevity were not wrong, it will last you all day and then some. To me this has a lot of similarities with Y EDP but comes off as less thick and softer. I would say that this is better suited for warmer weather and the EDP is best saved for the fall and winter months. In conclusion, if blue fragrances are your thing, you can’t go wrong with Y EDT it checks all the boxes and gets the job done. I have no experience with Y Live but if you’re looking for a one size fits all approach to the rest of the Y line I would recommend you go with Y EDP.

The reformulation has struck. For many, this change came somewhat unexpectedly and without much announcement (at least I found out about it almost by accident). Often, the properties of a fragrance deteriorate when it is reformulated. Frequently, the scent is just a shadow of its former self. Right off the bat: This is not the case here! The fragrance actually starts somewhat differently than the original formulation. Significantly more pepper, with trimmed synthetics, underpinned by woody notes. Only in the drydown do the new version and the original formulation converge, and there are only marginal differences. I believe the reformulation is indeed heading in the right direction. It takes the fragrance a step further without forgetting its DNA. All in all, the fragrance feels much more harmonious, crafted better. Especially for those who found the synthetic notes too prominent, the fragrance is now a new candidate for testing. I find it quite good as an everyday scent for almost any season. It definitely deserves a chance.

When you wear this fragrance, you feel as if you have just stepped out of the shower, and everyone notices how fresh and well-groomed you are. It embodies the perfect balance between decency, masculinity, and sweetness. You can wear it as a young businessman in the office or when going out on a summer afternoon. The sillage is very good. The longevity for an EdT is also impressive. I would recommend this scent to anyone who doesn't want to dig too deep into their pockets and is looking for a fresh, sweet, masculine, elegant, and not too overpowering fragrance.

The YSL Y EdT was one of my first perfumes. I received it as a gift back then, and since then it has followed me and its sillage. And I follow it too, because I have had to buy this perfume so many times. For me, it is the best of the Y line. While the Eau de Parfum is indeed stronger in terms of longevity, they are not that different.

A freshness enveloped in aldehydes with a slight tendency towards fruity nuances. Its character is one that can be perceived somewhat more frequently in the designer segment. It is not particularly outstanding. But to the scent: It is quite a modern shower gel scent for men. A bit cool, quite clean, and simply a clean character.

When I was at Harrods recently, I would have loved to move into the perfume department, so of course I had to take the opportunity to test the "H - The Exclusive Parfum". The bottle is beautiful, it catches the eye, I like this color combination of gold and light green. The fresh, fruity opening, which is citrusy but not cleaning-product lemony, seamlessly transitions from the very fruity berry-peach duet into a floral bouquet of orange blossoms and jasmine. The gardenia and rose are merely there as support, without stepping into the foreground. Gradually, the precious woods also reveal themselves, without falling apart for me as individual components. A beautifully composed fragrance up to this point, which actually makes me consider whether I should surprise my wallet with an impulsive purchase. But the daughter of a mother is not really an impulse buyer, and I decide to enjoy this beautiful floral-woody dream for the rest of the evening, perhaps to go back to Harrods the next day. The next morning (yes, the longevity is indeed good!) I am enveloped by a penetrating, overpowering vanilla scent! I have a suffocating vision of "vanilla kiss" deodorant from long ago in my nose, I look at my daughter reproachfully, just about to start complaining indignantly, when I realize: this artificial, dull vanilla sweetness is coming from my forearm, which the lady at the Roja stand had so generously sprayed the day before! Oh no, where was the floral abundance, where were the woods? Where was the patchouli? Well, most perfumes don’t last until the next morning, but couldn’t the woods have taken the old vanilla with them when they left?! And what have I learned from this? Before making impulsive purchases in this price range, it's best to sleep on it for at least one night, which saves both the wallet and the olfactory cells.

Come let us weave dreams from boundless joy with open hearts and open minds rushing through space and time Let us break earthly chains fly with the starlit wind free the enchanted in dreams feel how the soul swings Strolling on the rainbow writing our names in the book of heaven and waving from the gods' loges to the lovers of the world as a greeting Come let us weave dreams quickly before the morning light before in our senses a piece of eternity fades away. -Manfred Poisel- At first, it seemed like a dream to me, but I feel that H is exactly what I have been searching for, I believe I have arrived. For the first time, I was ready to sacrifice so many fragrances to possess the One, and that means something; my constant "being in love" has turned into love. Thank you so much, Kirthi.. You will be our witness!;) I waited and waited and thought I could detach myself again, but it doesn't work. H is perfect for me; it has everything a fragrance needs, the fresh top note is pleasant and not too intrusive, then it transitions into a sea of fruit and flowers, but refined, you don't feel overwhelmed, the entire progression has such a flawless elegance and flows hand in hand like a perfectly preserved record, without any skips. Then it becomes warm, soft, and spicy, but loses none of that mentioned elegance. The whole experience happens at a very high level and feels like a second skin, SO fitting! H ensures that I feel good, even on days when I can't really get along with myself. From all corners, it whispers: SIGNATURE FRAGRANCE! I have struggled with this so far; let's see how long I resist before I give in!:)

For a minute, let's just disregard the massive hate that has surrounded this release. Yes, it's the 14th or 15th flanker of L'homme. Yes, it has a massively redundant name. Yes, YSL has disappointed in the past. And on and on and on... But put that aside for a moment, and let's take a look at this juice objectively. On the initial spray, it opens up like a shower gel version of L’homme. It’s INCREDIBLY generic to the point of almost making you want to cry out in exasperation, "Noooooooooooo! NOT AGAIN!!!" But the L’homme backbone is clearly there for a few seconds. Suddenly, it takes a turn towards LNDL Eau Electrique, with a tonka-ish sweetness coming out. A few more minutes in, Invictus Aqua (2018) starts peeking out from behind the shower curtain asking blithely, "room for one more?" Big smile. Sure, why not. Why the ______ not. Finally, when everything has settled down at the 15 minute mark, the lavender in Cologne Bleu makes it smell very similar to Diesel Bad. Coupled with the marine notes and sandalwood from Invictus Aqua, and the apple, geranium and tonka from Eau Electrique, you get an incredibly mass appealing and forgettable mishmash of overly done nonsense. The far drydown continues to bounce between all 4 scents, but doesn't mask the overall intention - that this is essentially YSL's answer to capitalizing on the hype generated by Invictus Aqua. It’s smooth, it’s aromatic, it’s slightly sweet and it smells like an Invictus Aqua take on Diesel Bad, with a lingering nod to Eau Electrique in the background. If you were to give this as a gift to a man, they would probably say “Wow, thanks! I now smell like a person.” So if you're an enthusiast, I can see why this could be a massive disappointment. After all, Cologne Bleu just smells like a bunch of other popular things mixed together. What else is new these days? But heck, perhaps this is the first fragrance you’ve EVER smelled, in which case it could possibly be the GREATEST thing since adolescent horniness. You could definitely do worse. But IMO, you can DEFINITELY do better. Scent – 6.5/10 Longevity – 6.

Luca Turin dismissed the original YSL Homme with a quip about how Pierre Bourdon would be richer than Berlusconi if he only had a dollar for every Cool Water clone. Cologne Bleue takes the Nuit flankers back to their aquatic roots with a predictable medley that probably wouldn't make Bourdon a billionaire, but it should by rights buy him a yacht on the Côte d'Azur.

Imagine a day so hot and without any wind, even breathing is hard, a faint scent becomes a strong scent, even Bvlgari Man Glacial Essence would be too strong, YSL L'Homme Sport would be borderline. For those kind of days a cologne suits better, YSL L'Homme Cologne Bleue being one of them, spray with confidence but not that much because the cardamom and black pepper could be cloying in the opening. The proyection won´t last that much, half an hour to an hour, and will become a skin scent after that, activated only by movements of your body that will push some whiffs of scent to people close to you. Something fresher for those extreme hot days would be Dior Homme Cologne, this one spray with confidence, even in the hottests days people will love it. Proyection is weak after an hour, but will net some whiffs when you move for a couple hours.

L'Homme Fitness Studio would be the fitting name for this mild aquatic freshie. Very light and smells like the locker room of my gym, infused with all variations of "Cool Water" and Axe deodorants. Cologne Bleu is less sweet and spicy than the original L'Homme. The scent is primarily carried by the marine notes, which are of artificial origin but do not come across as overly synthetic. The blend is successful, but one should not pay attention to the "Cologne" in the name, as it will surely lead to disappointment. Cologne Bleu is weak and sits unobtrusively on the skin.
