When you start to sweat, the sillage will certainly improve, making it suitable for the cross trainer. The L'Homme line was still missing the shower gel scent, the Aquat. Now it’s here, but who has been waiting for it? The lack of projection and identity will likely cause this flanker to disappear from the shelves soon.

D5 means a dilution of the original substance by a factor of 10x10x10x10x10 = 1:100,000. This fragrance is suitable for homeopathy. You can hardly smell the original scent. Therefore, I used my 100 ml bottle as Pre-Shave. It works so well. But who pays CHF 133.00 to CHF 54.00 for such a thin little water? Well, since the Cologne Tonique was a revelation, as a fan of the original scent, I also bought this very last flanker of the series. Only the iconic bottle and the beautiful blue are very good. The scent itself is so utterly insignificant. A shame for YSL!! Stay away!!!

I took a risk with this flanker. I really like the core DNA - I love freshies/blues - so let’s give it a try. I've had more dubious blind buys, even though this flanker wasn't cheap. Based on the comments and reviews, I mentally prepared myself to defend it and somehow convince myself that it’s okay. What a lovely surprise - I like it!

First of all: My rating is a bit positively biased due to several factors that I will mention at the bottom. First, I want to focus on the perfume itself: No matter how the notes are listed here, the perfume is a continuous synthetic without a clear direction. There is (in my opinion) no note that can be clearly identified.

Not bad at all. Opening is strange (synthetic) but when it calms down the play begins. Vanilla is in “safe” modus here, not loud but it’s there. Reminds me of Cuir Beluga (drydown) but less “excited”. Is it old cotton fabric ? Or is the combination of Vanilla & white oud turning into “leather”? If I want to experience a vanilla based scent I’d go for Cuir Beluga. This one is not bad at all but not groundbreaking.

Oh, oh Only love, only love can leave such a mark But only love, only love can heal such a scar Oh, oh Magnificent The lines from the wonderful U2 song fit this amazing fragrance very well. Magnificent Gold is truly a protector, a cocooner, a scent that sends a delightful shiver down your spine. Here, after what feels like an endless summer, the first white layer of the year is forming. Incredible... just last week it was T-shirt weather, and now I need to quickly get my down jacket out of storage. My brain can’t quite process “the white” out there yet and first lowers my serotonin levels completely, releasing an extra dose of melatonin. That’s when MG comes in just right! The scent radiates, shining extremely at the beginning, a golden vanilla bathed in light, more real pod than baking pouch, combined with a fine rum note, glowing gold-brown, both so incredibly well balanced that my heart starts to beat a few beats faster, warmed through. Noble vanilla and rum - wasn’t there something? - yes, it does remind one of Spiritueuse Double Vanille, and the quality is such that no paper can fit in between, the subtle freshness in the background also reminds of Guerlain’s masterpiece. However, with MG there is also a subtle amber note in the background, often vanilla-honey-sweet, sometimes with a slightly sweaty note, here glowing golden, very subtly reminiscent of the “fossil amber” from SHL, although not quite the same quality. The slightly dry wood note (could be guaiac wood) in the background is also very pleasing for rounding out and providing a slight contrast, even though MG has already become very calm and subtle in this fragrance phase (after about 45-50 minutes). SDV for me only smelled of vanilla from the heart note onwards, not on my own wrist, but when standing in the sillage of another person. MG justifies its existence solely through the wonderful, soft, cozy scent blanket in the base. Potpourris, open fireplaces, angora underwear, underfloor heating, or hot water bottles can be safely forgotten; the scent is more than enough. Conclusion: A truly great fragrance, wonderful, heartwarming, high-quality, but also with a subtle similarity to the house's own Velours, the bases do resemble each other a bit. The longevity is good but not outstanding, the sillage is only strong in the first hour, which is completely sufficient for this fragrance direction, as the nose's habituation effect with vanilla tends to occur rather quickly. Everyday suitability: 8/10 Comfort factor: 9.5/10 Wow effect: 9/10 Price/performance: 7/10 Packaging/bottling: 9/10 Idea + implementation: 9.5/10

Yes, it just never ends with the vanilla scents! And it gets even worse: This one is only the penultimate; I have another one for tomorrow! But of the two, this is definitely the primus inter pares. Because this one is sooo delicious! I can't say much about it; in my opinion, not much happens in the development even after hours. I don't know if only the two ingredients were really used - I only smell these two. And what do you get when sweet vanilla and sweet oud pair up? A soul food for the ears, a particularly sweet vanilla pudding, oh, pudding, a cream of the finest kind, maybe a crème bavaroise. Although there is cream in that. Not here, I believe. Vanilla pod, dark and very, very spicy, undiluted, can easily turn two kilos of sugar into vanilla sugar if you put the emptied pod into the sugar. One pod has such incredible vanilla power - here it is presented in all its beauty. Added to that is this incredibly expensive oil, which can only be obtained if many "ifs" come together: IF the heartwood of the agarwood tree is injured and IF the tree seals this wound with resin and IF this resin is then infected by a very special type of mold and IF this mold process is as advanced as possible... But who am I telling this to, you already know all of this. I just say it again to emphasize why oud is so precious, so much more valuable than the gold that has already risen in price. IF now this wonderful oud enters into a liaison with the pretentious vanilla, which is also so precious, more precious than silver it was just recently... THEN something truly great is created, a multidimensional sweetness that holds surprise effects in all directions because it comes from two different sources. Personally, I perceive the two notes as a very balanced coexistence; the oud is not weak for me, but rather present alongside the vanilla spice tones. I don't perceive any other secondary notes, as I said, except - but only now, after hours (therefore a small addendum at this point - an amber note that really takes the vanilla out of the sweet-sweetest-sweet curve. All in all: A very beautiful scent with a not exaggerated sillage that every true vanilla fan should try at least once.

It has been some time now. I was waiting at Stockholm Airport for my delayed flight and browsing through the Duty Free area. Up until that point, I only knew the standard offerings of the big perfume chains. Everything smelled somewhat similar, and I hadn’t encountered any truly exciting perfumes until then. And then - after various failures - the friendly salesperson presented a beautiful golden bottle. YSL Le Vestiaire - Magnificent Gold. Hmm, it didn’t smell bad at all. And not as artificial as most of what I had smelled before. The price? Almost €200? Wow, that’s complete madness. At least that’s what I thought at the time as I headed towards the airplane. Later on the plane, a pleasant and subtle vanilla scent spread. Was that still my wrist? Yes, indeed. And even in the evening, it still smelled of vanilla. But not overpowering. Sweet, but not too sweet. Nestled in light woody notes. A brightly embracing scent. A pleasant feel-good atmosphere. So a few days later, I set out to find it. At the perfume chain around the corner? No luck. At the independent perfumery in the neighboring town? Nobody knew it. I just wanted to sniff the tester again. And then I found it. In Düsseldorf on the Kö. The same incredible scent as a few days earlier in Stockholm. I was smitten. What started as “just wanting to sniff” quickly turned into a purchase. And so this beautiful fragrance joined my small modest collection.

Don't be afraid of the vanilla; it is dry, beautiful, very subtle, and is wonderfully enveloped by the gentlest oud. Unfortunately, it vanished on my skin within 2 hours, but it is stunning on my scarf. The special thing about this fragrance is that it connects subtly with its wearer without immediately thinking of perfume, which gives it a signature characteristic for me (I fear this word doesn't exist). A somewhat pricey delicate restraint that leaves me wondering, is less more?

After I became aware of Magnificent Gold some time ago, I got myself a sample. Of course, partly because I am a vanilla lover, and then because the white oud intrigued me. I have no idea about and no experience with oud, only that it sometimes appears in a rather unpleasant guise, that seems certain.

In search of "THE" vanilla scent, I tried out some great samples of various fragrances here. However, none have really knocked me off my feet so far. And then came Magnificent Gold: Pure, dry vanilla meets absolutely wearable white oud. A combination that invites you to dream.

I love the original Opium.... But many do not...I say to all Opium haters - Try this , is is nothing like original Opium at all. .....Now i love them both , but they are two very different perfumes OPIUM VAPEURS is such a classy , wearable summer/spring scent - Gorgeous ! Ive had so many compliments when wearing this. true its an oriental , but one that you can comfortably wear in hot weather . This is a light and breezy scent that also lasts quite well ( for a scent of this type) . The orange blossom/mandarin/jasmine combo is just delicious. A keeper this one!

Opium and her subsequent flankers appear to have gone through some major changes over the years. The original formula of Opium was a spicy, rich oriental. However the modern interpretation as we know it today, is much softer and more of a crowd pleaser. As a result, flankers such as, Belle d'Opium and Opium Vapeurs de Parfum, are not really spicy orientals at all. They have little to no relation to the spicy Opium from the by-gone era. The only spices to be found in this composition, come in the form of pink pepper, (which is so zesty and sour that it could be mistaken for pineapple), and powdered nutmeg. Opium Vapeurs de Parfum is a surprisingly subdued floral, wearing almost like a skin-scent. First of all, I love the bottle. It was such a shame that I didn't enjoy the scent enough to buy it. I would have loved to have displayed that powder pink bottle on my dresser. I'm quite a fan of orange blossom in perfume, however the orange blossom note in Opium Vapeurs de Parfum struck me as a little synthetic. The floral notes in general were mildly soapy, with the nutmeg creating a smooth, musky blend on the skin. I sprayed Opium Vapeurs de Parfum on my left wrist and walked around the shopping centre sniffing it occasionally. I found it pleasant but nothing outstanding. It's not worth the YSL price tag, at least not in my opinion. Opium Vapeurs de Parfum is such a blasé fragrance. The projection is like a whisper on the skin, with the lasting strength being quite poor also. Not impressed. Opium is starting to lose its charm. Original review written: May 2013.

Orange blossom is enveloped by a hint of mandarin and vanilla. This makes it mild-sweet and slightly muted, then over time it becomes a bit more oriental, increasingly taking on a spicy-woody character, but it continues to pulse very orange-blossomy on the skin. A beautiful round and full base. The scent pleasantly surprised me; however, it has nothing to do with the original Opium or the other flankers in my opinion, it is a completely independent fragrance and in that sense, well done. It wears wonderfully, with orange blossoms being both fresh and elegantly warm.

I am interested in coincidences - simultaneous events in life. So the sun hid itself for days - just as our awning was installed. However, when I carry an umbrella with me, the sky laughs. If I go for a walk without this prop in a thin jacket, it is guaranteed to rain cats and dogs. When I seek peace and solitude in the bathtub - the phone rings incessantly. If I wait for a call, the thing stays silent - even if I at least get the soap wet. But scents also work the other way around. If the sky is gray and dreary, a bright fragrance lures a few, albeit hesitant, sunbeams out. Amazing. Maybe the scent just sharpens my eye for everything beautiful and bright? That’s how it was for me today with Opium Vapeurs de Parfum. The weather was not exactly inviting, and I was wandering around tired - but a spray of Vapeurs gave me energy. The fresh mandarin, spiced with pepper, is extremely lively and invigorating at the same time. I slipped out of my lethargy and joyfully got to work in the garden. And lo and behold, the sun generously sent me a few rays, mixed with bright jasmine and radiant orange blossom. A pleasant bitterness emanates from the fragrance, but it does not drift into the bitter. The wind is still cool - like the scent. I can also imagine a beach walk that is always refreshing, even when the sun is shining. The fragrance also promises sunshine - without oppressive heat. Spicy patchouli and cozy vanilla lead me back to my garden. Vapeurs encompasses closeness and distance - entirely according to one’s mood. At the moment, its bitter freshness makes me think of sailing trips on the seven seas - or on the calm Sorpe Lake - also entirely at one’s leisure.

Opium Vapeurs de Parfum is another representative of the Opium line from 2012. I purchased it at the beginning of 2014. It was a set with a Yves Saint Laurent fabric toiletry bag, a 30 ml bottle, and a small travel spray. Apart from the name, it has nothing in common with the original Opium fragrance, but I didn't have such expectations. I bought the scent because I also liked Belle d'Opium, which I had acquired shortly before. Therefore, I gave this flanker a chance as well. Opium Vapeurs de Parfum is a gentle, feminine fragrance. It starts with juicy mandarin and a hint of pink pepper. Jasmine is present but not too overpowering. Orange blossom unfolds immediately and gives the scent a certain powderiness, not too strong. Over time, I have noticed that this powderiness holds up better in winter at cooler temperatures. In summer, on the other hand, it hardly feels powdery to me, and the orange blossom becomes more citrusy. The base is said to contain patchouli and vanilla, but this is rather subtle. Overall, I perceive the scent as orange-powdery. It is not too intrusive and is well-suited for everyday wear. I would categorize its longevity as average. It leans a bit towards Coco Mademoiselle, but is gentler. The bottle is chic, and the rose-peachy hue fits well with the bottle. For me, Opium Vapeurs de Parfum is a candidate for repurchase and one of the better ones among the many Opium flankers.

I was damn curious about this scent. I really didn’t expect much. But I was eager to see what L'Oreal would use to lure in the teens. So, while out shopping, I stopped by Dougi and sprayed it on generously. The pyramid doesn’t even come close to describing this scent.

Today I bought the OPIUM Légère - Vapeurs de Parfum - from YSL. I had wanted it for a long time. But I always bought other great fragrances instead. The bottle already looks super nice. When I held it in my hand, I felt good. The spray button, ah yes, be careful, don’t pull it off ... I know that. I also love the old OPIUM, but this has nothing to do with it.

Taken on its own, this "Vapeurs de Parfum," whatever that may mean, is quite a nice, pleasant summer Eau de Cologne. Light, sunny, fruity, it has the same effect as a refreshing shower after a day at the beach. Creamed up, cared for with After Sun, deodorant on, one can head towards the evening promenade again, enjoy the sunset, and see what else will happen that evening.

Recently at my favorite perfume seller around the corner: When I asked what else there was besides the already known summer scents, he mischievously smiled and reached into the Opium section. My horrified shriek was discreetly ignored, and before I knew it, Opium Legère (this very Vapeurs de Parfum) was on my wrist. Come on, Opium is not my thing!

As an absolute fan of some YSL fragrances (Saharienne, Parisienne, Black Opium & Belle d'Opium), I was of course very curious about this one. According to the individual scent nuances, it had to be something for me; my absolute typical taste. The only thing I was a bit skeptical about was the word 'Opium'... I really couldn't connect with the original Opium at all. Brrr.

As a horse owner, I can't ignore the name and a little picture of a horse on a bottle. Enough has already been said about this perfume so I'll try and keep it short. Anyone who ever had a contact with a purebred Arabian horse will know one thing - their stamina, fire and durability are almost unbelievable. Some people find them "over the top", too fiery, too bold, too unpredictable, "too much"... But on the inside, they are delicate, graceful, so "talkative" and bond-seeking, you just have to be attuned to them. Once you form a connection, you'll soon be able to recognize all of it's finesse, complexity and layers. :-) Beneath that fire, they are sweet and fragile. That's all I'll say about Arabians Tonka. :-D

Wow, I simply love this fragrance: The rose, the cane sugar and the oud in contrast with the tonka bean, make it unique and addictive. The sillage is extreme (one of the strongest fragrance I have) and longevity is also good, it stays on my skin for around 7-8 hours, on clothes even more. I would recommend Arabian Tonka for anyone looking for a warm, sweet and rose based fragrance, perfect for the fall and winter (to avoid in summer). The price is also very reasonable, making it a must-have for anyone who like sugary/sweet fragrances. Thank you Montale for this creation.. P.S. This is perfectly unisex but on a man is the top!

And it's full of sweaty, tightly dressed men dancing to Perfume Genius. The horse walks over to the bar. "ID?" goes the bartender. The horse doesn't have one. It doesn't even understand what the bartender is trying to do, doesn't understand the concepts of an occupation or monetary exchange. The horse sweats, shakes its head slightly, starts to walk away from the bar over the beer-stained floor. A kind young man strolls over. "Lost?" he says, stroking the horse's mane. Horse knows it has been addressed, doesn't respond. "Wait, it's friendly!" says the young man. "Let's get selfies with it!" The young men dance over, pull out their cell phones, begin taking selfie videos with the nervous horse in the bar. The waft of stale alcohol rises out of the floor as dozens of aggressive masculine perfumes clash in the air. Human and horse sweat mingle with the odor, and underneath it all runs a repulsive, electronic metallic scent of overworked phone batteries and camera flashlights. One of these photos will be shipped overseas, get tossed in a pile of images selected at random by large corporations and magazines to sell products, and be dragged out by a bored Montale executive who, by some miracle, slaps the horsehead on a bottle of perfume that smells exactly like that horrifying bar night so many horse moons ago.

As it is a projection beast that lasts and lasts… potent from begging to end, leaving a sillage footprint like no other. Performance wise… perfection… As to the scent itself? For me, the Montales that I’ve tried are too “abstract”. They are like the Picasso’s of the fragrance world. Finely done indeed, but beyond my ability to “appreciate”. I bought this one, (and the other 2 that I tried) because “CurlyFragrance” recommended it (and the other 2 :-P). I agree with her taste MOST of the time, but I can’t vibe with the Montale scents. This one has a strong tonka note, adds a middle eastern feeling oud accord to it, and pairs it with a rose note that makes it difficult for me to wear. Don’t get me wrong, I LOVE some middle eastern frags (Amouage is a favorite house of mine, and I love Shaghaf Oud), but this one is just so loud in performance, and absolutely unique, that I can’t seem to pull it off. Honestly I wish I could wear it, as I shelled out $180 for it, but this is one I’m pretty sure I won’t be able to wear very often.

Nothing special. It's very similar to other sticky sweet heavy tonka bean+sugar based fragrances. Great sillage, great longevity but not worth the price. Reminds me of Armani SWY Intenseley. It's not same but very similar like %70-80 percent. I prefer SWY for price/performance. I think most people will not be able to feel the difference except those who paid this much money to Arabians Tonka (: Don't get me wrong it's ok fragrance, if you have money and into super sweet fragrances go for it but you haven't i think you will be happy with SWYI very much.

Have you ever seen a wild horse ? Or touched one ? Or be touched by one ? Here's your chance. But you must be very careful because it's also very dangerous. Arabians tonka opens with a very thick layer. Thick, sugary sweet, leathery, dark and mysterious. It sure needs time to settle and you need to let it rest.

I got this fragrance when the hype really started to begin. Claiming to be 'beast mode' (14+ hours of longevity). In the opening, I am blasted with sugar for the first minute before a different saffron starts to unveil itself. The mid isn't quickly noticeable as the rose and oud do not combine but rather compliment each other.

The first spray of Arabians Tonka opens with a very strong leather mixed with a sort of burnt sugar smell. The juxtaposition between the harsh leather and sugary sweetness was a bit jarring to my nostrils at first. However, as it dries, this fragrance takes you on an exciting journey.

Peaceful versatile and still an interesting scent. There are some similarities to Risque PPH and I can not tell you exactly what they are. SB10 is cozy, warm, fruity and creamy! All this whilst still being well-blended. I could imagine this combination becoming quite screechy in modern perfumery but The Dove has done a splendid job at creating SB10. I would wear this all year round, no exception. I get cardamom, peach, frankincense, moss and maybe some orris to give it that creamy sensation I experience?

A manly scent with just the right amount of spice, powder, and creamy notes, in fact a nearly perfect blend of all three. In my view it's suitable for all seasons, but it leans toward fall and winter. It strikes me as similar to Égoïste Cologne Concentrée with less spice and without the off-putting animalic notes. This is something high-powered businessmen and professionals in New York City wore in the 90's, something nice to throw on after work before a dinner, hot date, show, or a cocktail reception. The fragrance still captures that vibe. An upscale, metropolitan, complex, and cool fragrance with a personality all its own. The original bottle for Jazz (1988) Eau de Toilette was really cool, so it's a shame that YSL stopped using it, but it's a boon that this quality fragrance is still available to purchase.

"Jazz" was the second men's fragrance that YSL launched in the 80s, after "Kouros" had made a huge impact in 1981. At that time, "Jazz" featured both floral elements and a light tobacco note; otherwise, it was an aromatic fougère that lasted for hours, one of the last great classics of this genre. The newly released re-edition contains no tobacco and little oak moss. Instead, the fragrance starts warm and spicy with coriander and cinnamon, before wormwood (English: Artemisia) becomes noticeable. The base consists of coumarin, cedar, and a bit of patchouli. "Jazz" plays with these different components but is more discreet than its big fougère brother "Azzaro pour Homme." The re-edition is quite nice, but it only lasts a few hours on my skin. An "old school fragrance" that comes across as classic and unremarkable, lacking the ingredient that is often added to men's fragrances today to make them feel fresh: Dihydromyrcenol (the main molecule in "Cool Water"). The new "Jazz" is a trip back to the pre-Cool-Water era of the 80s. The fragrance flows pleasantly along, but ultimately leaves me indifferent, as the notes that once made my heart race are not present in the new version.

At first, the scent somehow reminded me of Calvin Klein's classic Eternity for Men. Mainly because of the fresh-green-spicy opening. However, it's a class above. And this class runs through all the phases of the fragrance. The reason why Jazz has nearly the same rating probably has to do with the disappointments regarding the reformulation. I can't explain the 6.7 any other way. YSL Jazz does not smell like a jazz club, not like Maison Martin Margiela's "Jazz Club". No trace of musty sofas and stale beer, but rather a fresh-happy spicy "Aramis Light". The spicy and woody opening exudes a pleasant warmth that is neither sharp nor piercing. Additionally, I perceive the scent as green, floral, clean, soapy, leathery, and fresh. The spiciness almost leans towards citrus and emphasizes the freshness of Jazz. Although I perceive so many nuances, I do not find the mix overloaded but rather elegant. Over time, the fragrance splits between the woody undertones and the fresh-green heart notes. I keep sniffing the scent and find it simply elegant. Perhaps the name Jazz fits the musician who stands on stage and is meant to exude a spicy freshness? I don't care, the scent is good. Longevity is over 8 hours with good sillage. And where Eternity has long struggled with green-fresh artificiality, Jazz continues to play effortlessly.

The French largely enjoy tarragon. Of course, this essentially transforms an unloved "hollandaise sauce" into a classic French "béarnaise sauce," albeit presented in a simplified manner. The distinctly herbal spice is at least a clear characteristic, and this is no different with the fragrance "Jazz." Why this lively music genre as a name? There are also French references here; originating in the southern states of the USA, New Orleans is often associated with it, and there, it is said, a piece of France lives on in the United States. Olfactorily, the pronounced tarragon spice brings music into the mix, which is essentially quite rounded, not representing a erratic, restless jazz, and is grounded with woodiness. The usual suspects here are patchouli and a type of cypress. This is indeed the case here as well. At the beginning, a hint of coriander appears, but fortunately, the soapy unpleasant context remains subtly in the background, and rather, its positively fresh, slightly citrus character unfolds. Basically, it all seems quite simple, and the perceivable components are clear-cut, but here, simple does not necessarily mean easy. For example, it navigates the dangers of over-seasoning, as tarragon can easily evoke a pharmacy feeling, or coriander can quickly give the impression that one is biting into a pure soap. However, in the drydown, something emerges that has a musty sweet, slightly honey-like undertone and brings a bit of unrest into the harmony. This is difficult to specify and leaves room for speculation. Fixatives, by the way, the perfume has an extremely high longevity, should actually have little to no scent of their own. Perhaps this is a bit different here, and that’s why this unpleasant background noise sometimes appears in the base. While this is annoying, overall, one finds much pleasure in the French herbal jazz. In this respect, it is a largely successful contribution from Yves Saint Laurent and perfumer Jean-François Latty to the traditional tarragon culture of France.

This Jazz is a great Fougère scent. It lives up to its name. Like a relaxed jam session, it has both seriousness and somehow a "chilled drive" that sweeps you away. If it could make you tap your feet, it would be music. And a relaxed atmosphere. It’s not the kind of complex chords that only an expert understands, but rather a melodic jazz with good rhythm, percussion, and trumpet. The very distinct tarragon and coriander notes "feel" sandy-powdery with a long "afterglow" of the finest fragrance dusts. Serious and heartfelt, deep yet relaxed, this impression is created by the earthy patchouli, the woods (I call them sound woods with soft tones), and the mosses /not listed here, but easily recognizable/. Or a xylophone with wooden sound elements. Round, soft, long-lasting. But this "spicy powder" is such a fantastic fragrance accessory for my nose, I LOVE IT! The only similar scent I know is 1881 pour Homme (2005) Eau de Toilette and its even older predecessor. Here it is even more pronounced. But Jazz is even finer in the combination, with very good longevity and sillage. An all-around successful bitter scent!

The fragrance unfolds between floral, spicy, oriental, and especially chypre-like accents. It is a classic spicy chypre with an important resinous base. It reminds me of some old chypres from the perfumery of the 30s and the 70s and 80s. The opening consists of a note of lavender and aldehydes, but the characteristic complexity of the chypre is present from the very beginning. A beautiful note of Mysore sandalwood appears almost immediately (similar to J'ai Osé by Guy Laroche), which forms the core throughout the duration of the perfume. The type of Mysore sandalwood that is no longer used in perfumery reveals itself immediately through its many aspects and facets: warm, enveloping, talcum, amber, and spicy. All the qualities of sandalwood are highlighted by just as many wonderful and perfectly balanced notes: iris rhizome, jasmine, ylang-ylang, and rose. After the first 20 minutes, the perfume settles on the skin as a warm and enveloping scent, a kind of spicy fragrance, but not in the strict sense; here the spices are only hinted at, overlaid by the iris rhizome and amber, which softens the opulent aspects. In the base note, the mythical Mysore sandalwood, oakmoss, patchouli, amber, and vetiver are always present. The vetiver note, which for decades was almost exclusively used in men's fragrances, is actually found as an important component in many chypre women's perfumes from the 30s, 60s, and 70s. I want to emphasize that the best olfactory aspects of vetiver come to the fore when it is combined with floral notes and spices (elements that are almost always found in chypre fragrances). The earthiness, the freshness, the distant hints of the green note of tobacco leaf make it a fundamentally important element. As with many other fragrances, Roja also wanted to evoke the history of perfumery here by incorporating various aspects of different scents. The fragrance has no trace of "modernity," but is filled with overwhelming quality and complexity. I love this scent because I believe that quality, complexity, richness of facets, and olfactory layering are much more important than innovation. There are direct connections to Guerlain's Guet Apens (spicy and fruity iris rhizome), J'ai Osé (Mysore sandalwood combined with a good dose of benzoin and oakmoss), Roja's Haute Luxe (floral triptych: jasmine, rose, and ylang-ylang combined with amber and especially labdanum). The review refers to a rare EDP version, which I greatly appreciate and received thanks to a very special person at Parfumo.

Unspoken arrived as a sample to me over the weekend. I was very curious about what to expect, as Unspoken has been declared a women's fragrance. I was hoping for a softer and lighter version of Roja Chypré Extraordinaire, especially since the price is much lower. Right off the bat, Unspoken is definitely unisex; I cannot understand the classification as a women's fragrance at all. Unfortunately, Unspoken is not well executed. The entire scent feels very chaotic. Here, Chypré is battling against the oriental notes. Unfortunately, Unspoken is neither here nor there. In the top note, we have a classic Chypré, which is well done. However, after 10 minutes, everything shifts, and only spices and resins remain. Unspoken is a strange and overly dense creation. The longevity is unfortunately disappointing on my skin. I can hardly perceive Unspoken after just over 6 hours. The sillage is okay, but not great, lasting just over 3 hours at arm's length and from the 5-hour mark, it's only close to the skin. Unfortunately, Unspoken is one of the weakest Roja fragrances I have tested. Unspoken feels to me like it was put together without care.

I like these somewhat subtle fragrances. Especially after this morning a) in the supermarket queue and b) in the bakery queue, I was olfactorily overwhelmed twice by two(!) men with steaming clouds of... want to guess or is it too simple?!.. - yes, I was assaulted by Dior's "Sauvage". Yves Saint Laurent's "Grain de Poudre" comes across pleasantly mid-range, harmonious, and delightfully spring-fresh green. Sage is clearly recognizable, flanked by citrusy-soft bergamot, underlined by slightly cool violet, and grounded by a very fine hint of suede, which is used significantly more subtly than, for example, in "Tuscan Leather" or other heavyweights. Suit-casual, I would say, slightly open shirt, strolling around on one of the first warmer days of the year, maybe in April, maybe in Paris. Where one is immediately reminded of the beautifully melancholic jazz classic "April in Paris" by Louis Armstrong and Ella Fitzgerald, which one hasn't heard in so long, but whose sonorous name keeps wandering around in the back of one's mind. Enough digressions - what I simply want to say is: YSL has created a fine, rounded all-rounder here that radiates subtlety without drifting into the banal. I wish the same for "Sauvage".

I must confess that it only caught my attention quite late, meaning after 2-3 hours it developed excellently. At first, it is very green and for me quite hard to get used to. Sage has something dry and slightly bitter-green and dusty about it. Coriander is also a very special ingredient, a bit like a herbal cocktail. I initially ignore it, and then it sneaks in very gently and pleasantly into my heart. I’m sitting in the car driving home, thinking let me be, I need to concentrate. It’s very fine, and I catch myself repeatedly smelling the scented areas of my body, wonderful. Lightly with a fresh, sweet-bitter powderiness, this direction is completely new to me, but it is given a real chance with me. It really only worked on the second look, but then truly. I find it perfect for summer - it’s intense without being fruity, sweet, or floral. I immediately called my best advisor and my favorite scent confidant and confirmed to him yes, you were right, it’s great, I give in, and he then... I knew you would like it. It’s not a girly scent but an adult fragrance with the character of a very multifaceted perfume, and it lasts incredibly long. Maybe it will also win you over on the second look, give it a try... In my opinion, it is suitable for ladies and gentlemen who value something special - you don’t encounter this every day.

Grain de Poudre is a fragrance that you wear for yourself. It has quietly snuck into my heart. It is neither loud, nor intrusive, nor eccentric, yet it is unique and very memorable. The blend of green and powdery, without slipping into floral or woody notes, is something I haven't encountered before. At first, it starts off very herbal and plant-like, and then develops into a more powdery dry scent with a herbal spiciness. I can't actively perceive leather here, but there is certainly a cozy note. The fragrance reminds me a lot of when you trim the herbs in spring and it is still very cold outside. Your hands smell of freshly cut woody sage stems while you bury your face deep in a wool scarf to keep your nose from freezing.

A scent that far too few have on their radar, as it is unjustly labeled as a women's fragrance. This sensual treasure definitely has signature character and an amazing composition that makes you think, what can it not do? A refreshing tingling underlined with a subtle sweetness and at the same time green!? Is that even possible? Try it and you'll realize that this is not all that it has to offer, as pepper joins in, providing the necessary spice and the edges that I love so much. It is rounded off by a permanently accompanying soft powderiness, so there is no conceivable moment for me when this fragrance does not fit. In short ,,Magic the a Bottle„

When I bought my Caftan from the YSL Le Vestiaire collection in my hometown of Copenhagen, I naturally had to test the entire Le Vestiaire collection. I love this collection because it simply screams niche and uniqueness, and because each fragrance has something truly special. Each scent from the collection is a new wonderful journey of discovery. In my opinion, this is a collection that receives far too little attention. I have already had many of the fragrances in my collection, and I have only tested many others. Then, of course, there are fragrances that I have never tested because they simply weren't my direction, as could be inferred from the notes. However, the super nice guy at the YSL Vestiaire collection "smuggled" many samples into my shopping bag.. So when unpacking at home, the small sample of Grain de Poudre appeared. A fragrance that, according to the notes and just by the color of the perfume, practically screams that it is absolutely not for me. The scent is not really my thing and will probably not work for me, but folks, this fragrance really smells damn good. There’s something magical about this scent that makes me constantly sniff my wrist. I am even more surprised that I immediately liked the fragrance because I usually don’t like many of the notes. The first thing I notice is sage, which, together with a hint of violet, creates a wonderful blend of something slightly spicy and something slightly sweet. The scent immediately smells elegant, very well-groomed, and very special without being off-putting. I would even claim that most people would describe this fragrance as super beautiful. Although the scent is not complex, it smells expensive and niche. After a few minutes, I can clearly smell a suede note, and even though suede is not listed in the pyramid, I would bet my hand that suede is present in this fragrance. I usually don’t like suede as a note, but here I find the suede so perfectly blended with the sage that I must admit that the suede in this fragrance simply smells heavenly. In the further drydown, I distinctly perceive coriander and a very light peppery note. Musk gives the fragrance a slight powderiness throughout. The labdanum is very, very subtle and gives the fragrance a little twist.. It is a light fragrance, the longevity is good, and the sillage is moderate to "intimate." A perfect scent for people who do not like beastly perfumes. A perfect fragrance for the office, for home, or when going somewhere where you simply want to smell great, special, well-groomed, and very sensual. A fragrance that surprisingly appeals to me, despite the notes, is lightly powdery/spicy, with a hint of suede.

When I first smelled it, I thought, "Oh, it's beautiful, but I don't want to smell like a cake!" I decided, that I will only smell, not wear this one. But a few weeks later I just realized, that I used up my third sample, so I have to think about to buy a full bottle! What a suprise! Now however I want to smell like a cake, beacause it is amazing! :)

Well, first of all... before trying this one, I expected it to be all about one thing: Chocolate, chocolate, and more chocolate! I thought is would be nothing but one note for the whole fragrance. How pleasantly surprised I was! Chocolate Greedy, despite it's name, actually reminds me not of pure chocolate, but of many things. Warm, aromatic tobacco, freshly baked chocolate cookies, and even dried, roasted cocoa beans. It's so complex that it always gives me a surprise when I wear it. It is a very versatile gourmand fragrance in my opinion. I would recommend it to people who don't even like gourmands too much. Perhaps this has some of the Thierry Mugley - Angel Men vibe going on, but I don't find this heavy or cloying in any way. It reminds me of aromatic tobacco and cocoa. A wonderful combination. Highly recommended!

Having trouble finding your fav gourmand perfume? Well you might not have sneaked into Montale Chocolate Greedy For Sure !! Its the yummmiest of the perfume i would have ever smelled. Whenever i spray it on my skin, it just make me keep sniffing my hand and yes make your feel very different. A real seductive perfume for Men .! Luckily i have a 30% Oil Concentrated version so it lasts 13 hrs easily with enormous projection..!! Thumbs Up !!!

To me it smells like nutella with orange in the background. I am not fond of nutella. I was expecting dark chocolate with orange, so I am very dissapointed. It is strong and intense, it stays there for hours so it has that. And its not like a BAD smell, its just not what I was expecting. The notes told me it was gonna be at least a bit dark and misterious, but no. It also doesnt change much, which is fine, not every perfume needs to take you on a journey of different smells through the wear. I am kinda impressed i havent seen someone calling it nutella smell cause its literally all i get from it. But maybe my nose is weird.

This scent is quite amazing. Its starts kinda strange, bitter.....but wait, let it settle. After a few minutes it changes and comes the best part of this awesome scent, cocoa,vanilla..... white chocolate, sugar.......makes you want to eat your neck, wrists.......simply amazing and a total gourmand. To mention that longevity is enormous, 3-4 sprays and will last all day long.

I will admit that there is something deep within me that longs for a fragrance that smells just like dark, molten chocolate. It is very low-brow of me, I know. So, I am not too sure if I am attracted to, or repulsed by Montale's Chocolate Greedy. Perhaps it is the fact that, on me, Chocolate Greedy is as much about the smell of wheat as it is about the chocolate.

Bought a sample of this on my hunt for the perfect chocolate fragrance. Unfortunately this is not the one, its incredibly strong and cloying, borderline overwhelming in the first few hours. It smells like a badly burnt, over vanillaed batch of brownies that you're already too full to try but you force down anyway and then you're sick.

Wow, this is straight up chocolate brownie batter! Fudgey, pour-able, but with chunks of the dry chocolate-y powder throughout. I didn't get any orange/citrus, or dried fruits. Really fun with how realistic this is, but not something I'd personally want to wear - I love gourmands, but this one would make me too hungry haha.

Exit to Dark, strong, very black chocolate and then vanilla appears, giving it the sweetness of a chocolate. She has me absolutely in love. I think it would make anyone's day. Then the coffee appears and gives it a certain seriousness, bitterness; makes the chocolate more complex. At the end, the nuts are felt, giving the fragrance depth.

In Love Again, this one the La Collection version. I bought it to layer with Kelly Caleche. They play nicely together being variations on a theme first explored with ILA, then petalled up for Rose Ikebana and then kid leathered up for Kelly Caleche. Jean Claude Elena has stated that his Hermes perfumes are for day use, in keeping with the staple wardrobes of the fashion house. Let's not forget those Hermes scarves either. You can femme up for evening but it is good to reach for a perfect day fragrance. Without resorting to Light Blah this reworking of YSL's "In Love Again" joins the fragrances that I will wear when playing with my grandchildren; that probably means skin to carpet and rusk smearings. Narciso Black, Pierre de Lune, Eau du Sud and In Love Again.

When I visit my father in the home, I usually apply a bit more perfume. I mentioned this in a comment before, that many residents feel cold because they can hardly move. For this reason, open windows are quickly closed again. My toothless admirer, who had a fondness for fragrances and particularly liked “Private Collection” and "Apercu" on me, is no longer with us, and my father tends to notice my appearance more: “You used to have nicer hair! Fix your collar.” Well, some things never change. So I apply generously whatever I feel like. Recently, before my visit to the home, I used a decant that has been in my collection for a while but, for some inexplicable reason (too much choice?!), has only been worn once. “In Love Again” by YSL, a fragrance by Ellena, who is a giant in the fragrance world and to whom we owe many enchanting scents. An authentic, sweet mandarin envelops me and is tamed by my favorite fruit in fragrances, the blackcurrant. Here, it provides a fresh, slightly tart, and sparkling note, keeping In Love Again from being too sweet. Rose and peony join in only as a rosy whisper, while the fruits remain dominant. In the base, this friendly fruit basket is supported by light musk, which adds a slightly powdery and clean note. “In Love Again” is a cheerful, uncomplicated women's fragrance; the name says it all. Ideal for hot temperatures, but even now in autumn at 20 degrees, it’s still pleasant. Sillage and longevity are in the medium range. By the way, my father noticed that I smelled delicious and immediately grabbed a mandarin from the fruit bowl. And my sand-colored denim jacket was also positively acknowledged: “I’d like one of those too,” scents make for a gentle atmosphere :o).

"In Love again" stands out from all the YSL fragrances I have known so far. To my surprise, after the first test, I realized while categorizing it under "Collection" that I have it on my wish list. Why? Oh yes, it was created by Jean-Claude Elléna, whose fragrances always interest me, plus it’s an almost pure fruit scent. I have never been fond of fruit fragrances, no matter how beautiful and gourmand they may be. "In Love again" is a lively, sparkling, and light spring and summer fragrance. I can definitely recommend a test to those who love fruit scents but don’t want to smell like red fruit compote. "In Love again" starts with a light but very authentic mandarin scent and then continues to present delicate, barely sweet little fruits. But really, just like you can enjoy them in a fresh sorbet that moves in a sparkling fruit juice spritzer. I even like it. The black currant is very light; it seems to me that it’s just the floral aroma. But basically, I can’t really pick out the fruit notes individually, except for the initial mandarin. With a hint of subordination, I also smell an apple rose and hints of peony. Bright grapes contribute light green notes and a bit of sweetness. And what I particularly like: a hint of spiciness that gives the fragrance a very special note, possibly green pepper. Even though I tried to dissect this fragrance, which I consider extraordinary, it stands strong in a very short time and has a very long lasting power, no matter how delicate and melting the scent may be. Musk, it must be the so-called white musk, is also extremely sparingly dosed. A perfect spring and summer fragrance. "In Love again" is so far the only fruit scent that I like to wear, and I will also use the rest in the test spray. "In Love again" is undoubtedly a typical J.-C. Elléna fragrance for me. And yes, it is mainly a feminine scent, which I believe men should decide whether they find this light fruit scent wearable for themselves.

"In Love again" - especially the unreformed version - is a delicate yet present, feminine and beautiful summer fragrance. . I am wearing it today and I constantly smell the rose around me, my beloved, slightly fruity blackcurrant and the slightly tart notes of blackberry and mandarin. I only notice the musk now and then, more in a skin-close way. . Like a little butterfly, happily floating through the air, pausing briefly at every beautiful flower to take in the world around. A moth gently flutters its wings out into the light of the distance softly carried by the summer wind where longing and dreams abound... Up and down in the sun's glow the pair of wings rises high cheerfully flying in warm currents and jumping crickets chirp to you in chorus... This fragrance is truly for lovers, those in love again, or those who would like to fall in love. Okay, also for those who simply want to wear it. . It brings good cheer, you feel fresh, alive, and just great - without the feeling of just having showered. Fruity, rosy mmm... Tschaka *laugh* Now I just need the unreformed version back in my closet - that dented cap has its charm ;-)

I tested the fragrance without knowing the notes and it immediately reminded me of grapes. When I then read about mandarin and blackcurrant in the top notes, I was confused for a second, but then I discovered grape in the heart note. Because this is immediately and omnipresent after spraying, it is a true grape scent. Subtly sweet, crisp, and fresh at the beginning, then a bit more bitter (like a more bitter grape) until the roses come in and turn the whole thing into such a lovely rose-grape scent that I immediately think of a nostalgic garden where a half-rusted white swing bench with curls stands among flowers and fruit trees.

Like most Roja scents there is a core DNA to Elixir that I find really pretty. I feel like it sits somewhere in between 51 and Elysium Pour Femme in terms of scent profiles for me. Elixir is fruity and fresh with a bit of a slightly spiced base. However there's and oddly cool and almost metallic twang I am getting from Elixir that I don't love. I'm not sure what is causing that on my skin but it's a little odd. Overall Elixir is a nice, approachable and likeable scent, but it doesn't really stand out to me -- either from other scents with a similar profile or from Roja's own line. As such it's not one I would flash Roja cash for.

TL;DR: Elixir Eau de Parfum is a delicate, feminine spring and summer fragrance with floral and fruity notes. It starts fresh and develops into a fine bouquet of flowers. It lasts about four hours and is less complex than other fragrances by Roja Dove. Elixir Eau de Parfum was one of the scents from the official “Women’s Discovery Set” that was previously unknown to me and impressed me. Even though it is not a masterpiece, the fragrance continually drew me back to the sprayer to sniff it. To echo BelleRuth's statement here: I believe that “Feminine without the need for seduction” hits the nail on the head. Elixir Eau de Parfum is an unmistakably feminine fragrance that brings delicate, fruity, and above all fresh, floral notes. Similar to "Sakura | Acqua di Parma," which is also a rather feminine, fresh-floral scent, I think this fragrance could be worn by a well-groomed man. However, that would undoubtedly be unusual, perhaps even a bit extravagant. At the beginning, the fragrance unfolds wonderfully fresh with distinct floral and sweet-fruity notes. It is accompanied by a pleasant creaminess that somewhat resembles face cream. A soft, velvety scent emerges, artfully reminiscent of the delicate texture of tulip petals. After thirty minutes, the creaminess diminishes and the floral notes gain strength. An interesting, barely noticeable green note is added, which harmonizes beautifully with the flowers. It can be described as the entirety of a flower: from the gently scented petal to the plant-like aroma of the stem. At this point, Elixir Eau de Parfum smells like a fine bouquet of flowers with a fruity undertone derived from raspberry and peach. A pleasantly fresh-floral cloud lingers in the air, evoking the image of a blooming spring. In the first hour, Elixir Eau de Parfum remains unchanged, with individual facets of the fragrance repeatedly becoming more prominent. Even after an hour and a half, the scent is still beautifully floral, although the freshness and fruitiness gradually decline. Additionally, there is an extremely light hint of wood. After two and a half hours, Elixir Eau de Parfum is still floral, but only perceivable close to the skin. The base notes slowly open up, giving the fragrance a certain warmth. Compared to the fresh opening, the scent now seems somewhat “dull.” In the fourth and fifth hours, the fragrance is finally very close to the skin and resembles a few days old bouquet of flowers (read: less fresh and fruity). The flowers bid farewell but are still perceptible. A light sweetness from the vanilla emerges, while the wood becomes more pronounced. In the drydown, Elixir Eau de Parfum is by no means a woody or typical vanilla scent. In my opinion, a longevity of about four hours is acceptable for a fresh fragrance. On hot spring and summer days, for which Elixir Eau de Parfum is perfectly suited, one would likely want to wear a lighter scent anyway. Compared to other works by Roja Dove, this fragrance seems less complex and progresses more linearly. Those looking for a truly beautiful, crowd-pleasing, yet still unique floral fragrance and are willing to pay the price will not go wrong with "Elixir (Eau de Parfum) | Roja Parfums." By the way, for anyone considering trying other fragrances from the “Women’s Discovery Set” by Roja Dove, I can recommend the following: If you enjoy the light creaminess of "Elixir (Eau de Parfum) | Roja Parfums," you should definitely test "Isola Sol | Roja Parfums." This fragrance evokes fresh vacation days in summer and the gentle breeze of sunscreen. If you prefer something a bit more complex and opulent, you should definitely try the sweet-spicy rose in NüWa (2015) - one of my absolute favorites.

Dense and syrupy, that's how it presents itself in the opening. Plums and cherries cooked with sugar over open fire. Seasoned with cinnamon cardamom and other oriental spices. Honestly, if you cross out all non-edible ingredients from the pyramid, it actually sounds like a reasonable recipe for a winter fruit punch. Everything is balanced with light woods, not a trace of oud. The tobacco does not come across as burnt or dry at all, but rather like a moist shisha tobacco. Although there are hardly any fresh and rather dark notes, it has a very youthful appearance. I can also imagine it as a great clubbing/going out fragrance in winter. All in all a solid thing. I see similarities to Amouroud Oud after Dark or a bit more distant Arasbesque. In terms of style, it is similar to Montale Oud Tabac, but here in a more fruity direction and less honey/vanilla. Longevity Montale typical top. In terms of the rating, I think it's a bit exaggerated at the moment, but I would give it 7.5-8 out of 10 points. Not hyper-realistic or naturally rich, but that's almost impossible with cherry notes anyway. Simply a solid scent from Montale that is sure to rank in my top 5 from the house.

Infinity may be a great example of well-executed fragrance maximalism. It does exactly what it says on the tin, and by that I mean the notes are almost all easy to identify, even while being well blended. It starts with beautiful, deep yet luminous, juicy plum and black cherry which, on my skin and clothes, persist through to the very drydown and base. The other players, like the rose, the tobacco, the cardamom, the tonka, and the musk each take their turn to shine brightly throughout the 8+ hour voyage. Oh, yes: longevity is insane/incredible. On clothing, a full day later you still get a plum/cherry/oud mix that projects. Which brings me to the strong notes here. You have that oud alongside leather, saffron, and vetiver, and they've all been dialed up to... 9.999. The oud is smokey, the leather provides heft, and the saffron and vetiver bring a bit of spice/sparkle. These are four baritones, none of whom has a solo but all of whom have still been instructed to show off during the song. It's a lot, a WHOLE lot, but somehow they still don't clash. Almost overwhelming, but never quite getting there. Olfactory brinksmanship. Which ends up meaning that Infinity is strong. It is a beast. It lasts, it stays, and it projects. To the point where I, someone who cares about longevity and sillage, have started wondering whether there's a dupe of Infinity that's a bit less bombastic, for when I want to smell this exact combination but on a casual, calm night in. The constant interplay between the notes means the composition is at times boozy, at times musky, at times powdery. It's honestly kind of magical. As always, but for this one especially, try before you buy!

This has a little bit of everything the house is known for. I initially was looking for a cherry tobacco fragrance to replace Initio's Narcotic Delight, but I found myself in love with this even more than the fragrance I wanted to replace. Though they are quite similar, the cherry here isn't as prominent and it's a better blend of all the ingredients as a whole. Lasts a long time and is, overall, a very pleasant cherried spiced plum tobacco with a strong vanilla supporting role, a rose/oud/leather that adds a touch of mysterious masculinity, and a musky amber base that smells amazing the next morning in the shower. I recently got rid of some Montales I never wore, but I had to keep this. It's just versatile and while slightly on the sweeter side, I can tolerate it. I'm not the biggest fan of super sweet (why I didn't much care for Narcotic Delight) but this is sweet done perfectly.

Montale Infinity is a 2023 release, a blend that includes the very common (to the line) rose and oud combination but with a prominent black cherry note that keeps it dark while also sweet, juicy, and fruity, along with an uncharacteristically long list of notes from which I also get a bit of leather, saffron, and pepper, vaguely, with a pinch of vanilla. It’s a pretty great blend but it’s a bit sharp and heady between the oud, cherry, and rose, so it’s not as easygoing of an entry as Oud Dream or Oud Edition, but is perhaps a little more daring than either. Still, I’d recommend checking it out if you’re a fan of this genre of fragrance, particularly within Montale/Mancera, who reliably put out a lot of oud/rose-type fragrances to the point of redundancy, so it’s just a matter of sorting out which ones you like the most. I don’t think that this eclipses other recent favorites in Montale Oud Dream or Mancera Precious Oud but it’s still very good and I’d surely wear it a bunch if I had a bottle. The oud is a bit sharp but not animalic or medicinal, so it’s acceptable within normal parameters of the house. Infinity has the standard Montale pricing of $170 for 100ml, sold through retailers like Olfactif, from whom I bought my sample, and it does not currently appear to be available on the secondary market. 8 out of 10

"If the doors of perception were cleared, everything would appear as it is, infinite." -William Blake Infinity is a fragrance that has contrasts inside it: sweet, with its fruity notes ( of plum and cherry first and foremost) and hard ( with Oud and suede notes ) at the same time, impressive and delicate, but absolutely beautifully structured. Fall in love with this symphony and feel a feeling of infinite greatness, like love. As soon as I tried it, I loved it; I found it elegant and distinguished in its own right. It is more discrete than the other Montales and literally won me over. Perfect for all occasions and seasons. "Woman contemplating the sunset" painted by Friedrich.

Phew, I actually just wanted to write a short statement, but somehow I ended up having a few more words to say. I sprayed it on today for testing, and the scent initially knocked me out in an olfactory sense. I saw stars, I tell you. I have no idea what all I perceived, but it was a lot and so dense that it took my breath away.

First of all, I want to say this: Besides "Arabians Tonka | Montale," I really like this Montale here very much. It's just a tad better than the Arabic one, "best horse in the stable!" Although most scents from Montale usually trigger discomfort or confusion for me, here it’s simply different. I like it, in a pleasant way.

Pierre Montale gifts himself and us with the fragrance Infinity for 20 years of perfume creation. As is customary with Montale Paris, the new scent is also significantly influenced by the Orient. The renowned perfumer presents us with a fragrance that impresses with great radiance and remarkable scent quality.

This fragrance definitely needs to be reviewed by me. I wanted to test this scent for ages, and it had already been on my wishlist as a potential blind buy. The test and the blind buy - nothing had really come together, and by the end of this year, I finally managed to get a small sample.

I tested this perfume a few months ago shortly after its release at my trusted perfumery and was initially not very surprised. Nothing special, I thought to myself, and I put the test strip in my pocket and forgot about it for the rest of the day.

Prior to 2025, I hadn't smelled a single scent with a retail price tag above €1,000. In the last 2 weeks, I have gone through 5 such fragrances from British niche brand Roja Parfums with the ultimate product being this very fragrance, i.e. Tea at BG . One opinion that I have firmly stood behind is that a higher price brings superior product, as best indicated by most of the niche market leaders being €500+ fragrances, e.g. Nefs , XXI: Art Deco - Blonde Amber , Jump Up and Kiss Me Hedonistic and others. However, after having smelled these 5 fragrances, I cannot help but conclude that the next tier above €1,000, esp. as it relates to limited product, is there strictly to take the money of the inexperienced sucker as if there was a parabolic relationship between price and product. And it doesn't take long for me to come to this conclusion with Tea at BG because there's never a single phase of this scent's wear where you'd say this is worthy of a price tag anywhere near the $1,100 at which Bergdorf Goodman managed to sell out this product. The scent opens as a combination of a citrus tea fragrance like Nishane's Wūlóng Chá Extrait de Parfum and an airy sandalwood-iris scent like BDK's Gris Charnel Eau de Parfum . Subsequently smelling the fragrance on skin, the citrusy qualities are very piercing as the listed lime note included in Tea at BG appears to take inspiration from Roja's own Elysium pour Homme Parfum . This prominent citrus accord is initially flanked by light sweetness and a developing spiciness, somewhat reminding me of the way Ex Nihilo structured The Hedonist Extrait de Parfum , specifically the Extrait version. The ultimate drydown also has this sweet citrusy tone against a very noticeable spiciness which I am allocating to the violet and black pepper. As it evolves a little more, I have an easier time spotting the floral accord that everyone says this fragrance is dominated by, as a light white floral accord is used in either the base or the heart of Tea at BG . Additionally, when you go looking for notes by putting your face in it, I get a fairly typical amberwoody base blend. Somewhat inconceivably, there was never a stage where this fragrance smelled fruity and the voting on such an accord feels puzzling. I think the most underwhelming part about Tea at BG is that unlike with Lost in Paris , this scent never offers up anything to even indicate that this is suppose to be a premium product. The scent doesn't come off as some sort of a special nor unique tea fragrance and I would argue it doesn't even match the quality of the product currently at the top of the smoky tea genre (where you have scents like Matsukita , Indigo Smoke and I-III Russian Tea ). It is this lack of quality that I feel is a driver in how I am rating the scent, albeit there is no upside from the profile either. This commentary isn't even inclusive of the price and the fact that this is a limited product that is sold out. I feel like I've seen this game play out before in many different avenues: with the sneaker community as Nike flooded the market with dunks and Jordans after the pandemic, with the gaming community as developers started gaming-as-a-service where they'd launch incomplete product and sell you cosmetic items within the game at half the cost of the original title, in consumer electronics where peripherals were separated to charge you extra for headphones, chargers etc. Ultimately, while product like Tea at BG isn't a market-moving product by any means due to the low stock, it serves as an example of the direction where the fragrance market is heading when the product is not only tolerated, but also promoted. At the end of the day, even if I am not the one carrying water for Roja's premium bracket, somebody else is and that somebody, in my eyes, is the sucka.

Hello everyone, Today I would like to say something about Tea at BG . I am a person for whom honesty is very, very important, but I know that nowadays this doesn’t always go down well, and especially online it’s often a certain "ride on the razor's edge". Nevertheless, I feel it is right and important to share this with you. When the announcement came a few months ago that it was to be released, I was already a bit curious. And whether Roja Dove was actively involved in the creation, I do not know... Now it is here (sample, no bottle) and off we went to test it. The first minutes are exciting. A bit citrusy, fresh - fruity, and also somewhat bitter due to the tea used create an appealing opening, and its effect on other people is very, very good - especially the ladies really like it... After that..., yes, not much happens anymore... - unfortunately! Beforehand, I thought that it would play a bit (in the drydown) with Amber Aoud Parfum , "United Arab Emirates | Roja Parfums", and possibly with certain hints of Great Britain , but that is not the case. You perceive individual notes more or less, but none stands out significantly (in the drydown) and it feels more like a "heap" of x components. If I only evaluate the opening, then we can talk about an 8 to 8.5, but the pure drydown, well... I am not a fan, and it is also not (!) my intention to put a fragrance down and so on, but there is one aspect of Tea at BG that strongly drives me towards "RAGE MODE", and that is the price! It is always extremely thankless and sometimes unfair to evaluate something like this, because it is subjective. Nothing more and nothing less. Here you are of course paying (massively) for the fancy bottle, the cap, and the company behind it, the box, and exclusivity - these factors should not be overlooked... Nevertheless, we are talking about 1000+ (new) and clearly over 10€ per ml... That is a lot of money that you first have to have... Is it worth it...? HELL NO and not even close! From a collector's perspective, it might be okay. But owning and wearing/using it for that price I consider very, very difficult. If someone had shown it to me and I didn’t know what it was..., I would have said we are talking a maximum of 100€ - 300€ for what it would be worth. With the knowledge of 1000+, I’m out! A general note about Roja (maybe interesting for some): In the past, this company was, alongside Amouage, XJ, and CC - my favorite house, because there were sooooo many wonderful and, in my opinion, unique fragrances, like for example Harrods pour Homme , Manhattan Parfum , the golden Roja (Haute Luxe), and the 3 APs... , and when I see what is happening there starting from 22/23, it breaks my heart. (If you want to read my blog about it here - https://www.parfumo.de/Benutzer/Sirbennyone/Blog/Eintrag/roja-der-grosse-player-der-vergangenheit-und-der-heutige-weg-in-das-mittelmassige) Nowadays it is just another house among many that operates significantly "overpriced" and their fragrances are a uniform mass, lacking anything high-quality, no edges, and everything is somehow fresh - citrusy - floral with a lot of sweetness + a certain creaminess.... - what a pity! H/S? Yes, good+ what is relatively typical for the house (even nowadays). When - where? Leisure or at a nice dinner or possibly for partying, and from September to May, I would say it fits quite well. In summer, I don’t recommend it, as it becomes too cloying, sweet, and sticky, which is quite disturbing. My tip - test over several days, then possibly buy and NEVER blind. Because I am very glad that I didn’t... And now have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______

Tea at BG is a special fragrance in several ways: Not only because it is limited to 100 (or according to some sources: 130) copies and was exclusively available for a few days at Bergdorf Goodman in New York, but also because it could be one, if not the last fragrance personally created by Roja Dove. Just a few weeks ago, the Roja house announced that starting next year, Antoine Cotton will be responsible for the house's fragrances for the first time. This is reason enough to approach the test with particular interest and to ponder how the founder of the house might say goodbye. Immediately after spraying, the opening begins with a fig wrapped in pale yellow citrus. This fig, which achieves a good balance between woody and fruity nuances, is meant to remain dominant for the first third of the fragrance's development. While the intensity of the lemon accord quickly fades, the fig remains pleasantly tart for quite a while thanks to it. In the background, green players quickly join in: Basil and bergamot flicker, dimming the bright top note a bit, pulling it in a more complex direction and giving the fragrance a certain looseness for a moment. Slowly, the fragrance develops in a familiar direction, and here I agree with DavidB: At times, there is clearly more than just a hint of "Oceania | Roja Parfums" in the air. At this stage, the fig begins to recede into the background, and the tea takes the lead. The creamy base tips into the powdery, a soft leather is surrounded by violets, but above all, there is the green-tart tea. The progression of this fragrance is as complex as it is beautiful; new nuances flash up repeatedly and then disappear again in the Roja-typical blending. Sometimes I smell the sweet-tart blackcurrant, sometimes I get the impression of a subtle green fresh mint. In the end, alongside the powdery-creamy woods, there remains a cocoa underlaid with vanilla, reminiscent of "Britannia (2016) | Roja Parfums." And so the perhaps last fragrance journey that Roja Dove takes us on comes to a close. Tea at BG is a distinguished fragrance that manages to stay youthful without drifting into childishness, to be serious while remaining approachable. A wonderful release, from which we can only hope that it finds its way into mass production.

Nowhere as dark as I thought it would be. In fact, only the opening is stark, woody, and raw. Deceptively, it led me to believe that it would remain as such. A serious linear and inky fragrance. Actually not all that pleasant up close. And then, out of the blue, a rose emerged. It initially appeared, strangely enough, as I took my nose away from my forearm for the third time, resigned to the fact that I was going to smell like a bloke for the rest of the day. Visions of a crimson rose growing out of a dark mass struck me … and then it grew, and grew, until this very much became the predominant note, totally shadowing its woody roots. Do I like it? Not sure. I prefer my roses gourmand and this one definitely isn’t, but if you want a red rose with great projection, this will be right up your street. ... Now, I have to come back to tell you that I presented my neck to my beloved and “Turkish Delight” was his verdict. However, when I asked him to smell my forearm, he looked at me puzzled, and declared that it smelt completely different. No idea why. Fact remains that if I could smell what he first smelt, I probably would adore this perfume … but I don’t, so I stand by my initial assessment.

I really thought I would love Black Aoud by Montale. It was said to be similar to the more recent release, Portrait of a Lady by Frédéric Malle that I absolutely adore, so if so, how could I *not* love this too? Well, after now trying the Montale, I do see where the comparisons are coming from with both scents relying on a rose, patchouli and Oud combo to create their dark rose accords... Unfortunately, that is where the comparison ends, IMO... Black Aoud's synthetic Oud note that mixes with the rose early on immediately strikes me as a bit bizarre. It makes the rose a more watery, "feminine" and slightly rubbery that just does not fit my tastes much. A nice dark rose scent to be sure, but hard to wear, IMO. With Portrait of a Lady I find a much deeper and natural smelling rose opening with a superior quality patchouli heart that makes it a lot more easy to wear and appreciate for me, at least. Black Aoud has very good projection, but longevity is somewhat lacking on my skin. I get about five hours longevity with it at decent strength and that is well-below average for me. So the bottom line is Black Aoud is a good scent and it deserves a lot of credit for bringing attention to the rose, patchouli, Oud combo that is so popular nowadays. That said, Portrait of a Lady perfects the blend with much better quality IMO, and adds raspberry to the mix for good measure for a more wearable and balanced package. Portrait of a Lady would have to be a "must sample first" before buying Black Aoud, IMO. A weak thumbs up for Black Aoud by Montale and a 3 stars out 5 rating.

Lots of patchouli-rose-oud perfumes exist these days, and many of them are much more about rose and patchouli than they are about oud. Montale BLACK AOUD is an exception to the general rule, with just as much oud as rose and patchouli. The combination of the fairly declarative oud note along with the labdanum produces a scent very similar to leather, so this composition is bound to appeal to anyone who likes leather. I do not find BLACK AOUD overly masculine, and it is certainly wearable by women who like dark leatherish scents laced with roses, so I'd have labeled this creation unisex and marketed it to gals and guys alike. I see that many women own a bottle of this perfume, and I am not at all surprised. I imagine that BLACK AOUD would be the perfect scent for a woman working as an undercover agent who uses her powers of feminine persuasion to extract state secrets from her unwitting victims before leaving behind a trace of toxic carnelian lipstick from her farewell kiss.

Black Aoud is appropriately named, because it smells dark, smoky and resinous with the floral note mostly obscured in the opening. As it dries down, the floral note comes out more but is still somewhat concealed by the smoky resin. It has the most strength of any Montale offering that I've come in contact with and can say that this is one of the few fragrances where one spray is enough and two - maximum, if you're wearing it out. If you're wearing this in close quarters, like an office environment, even half a spray may be too much. A couple of dabs with a fingertip is more than enough. Quite honestly, I wouldn't recommend wearing this to the office at all. This scent definitely has a more masculine edge to it, although many women seem to like it. Sillage and Longevity are unrivaled.

This is a well done blend of dark roses, oud and patchouli that has a great sillage, lasting power and projection. After the medicinal open, the roses show it's splendour together with the oud and patchouli. In my opinion this is unissex. It's a heavier version of C&S Dark Rose. Definately a great scent that deserves at least a try. Updated January 2014
unforgettable masterpiece imho best aoud frag ever created ,rose,musk ,patchouly all together to make arabian world go straight to your skin

Let’s start with the good news: nearly all ouds by Montale share the same exact boring artificial oud notes, while Black Aoud doesn’t really. It’s very different from any other oud scent by Montale (still good news here), and actually it doesn’t seem containing oud notes in the first place for me.

It seems like this stuff is better sprayed on the hand or wrist - stay away from your neck and chest with this stuff. But either way, my tongue still tastes the chemicals (gross!). And the smell isn't all that good.

Starts with a very lemony, almost lemongrass-like note. This citrus lasts for a good 15min which then reveals the cedarwood underneath. It further evolves to a kerosene or gasoline-like note which I, suprisingly, dont mind and even like! The rose in this reminds me of the expert rose from the Parfums de Rosine line.

I love this parfum extrait. Its spicy, gourmand and yummy. First spray hits you with cumin and then the other spices. This parfum kind of reminds me of Amouage's few of the Opus collection, specially the ones with heavy cumin. This one has soft cumin, not overbearing, fantastic silage and longevity about 24 hours. I could still smell it strong after a shower and post 18 hours on my wrist. Just love this one a lot. I can still smell it strong on the perfume strip three days after. Roja is a genius no doubt and way above Amouage and other niche brands. His perfumes develop smoothly and slowly taking into the next level.

This is the exact coffee perfume I was looking for. The others are just too bitter, too floral(rose, lavender), too much liquor. This is creamy coffee that smells delicious without smelling sticky or burnt or too literal. Perfect balance of coffee and fragrance. The rice notes were a genius touch.

My girlfriend zooms off to her favorite city, St. Petersburg, whenever she has the time. She would love to have me as her companion, but I dread the long flight - curled up in my seat, the back of the person in front of me on my knees. But when she shows me photos of the legendary "White Nights," I am so fascinated that I start to waver. Bright nights under a spectacular sky - along with many people strolling up and down the elegant boulevards. No one seems to be sleeping - everything is awake and alive. And then there’s this mysterious, diffuse light. I would stroll along the river with her, chatting, and then sip a glass of Crimean sparkling wine in a bistro. Nuit Blanche would fit perfectly into this "twilight" somewhat surreal atmosphere. It is soft like the light, calm and relaxed like the flâneurs on the streets - awake, yet leaning towards dreams. There is also something comforting about it - just as it always calms me to know that I am not alone in my sleeplessness. The coziness that emanates from the fragrance makes me pleasantly drowsy, and I look forward to my bed - and to a beautiful dream. For the dream is a piece of life.

Oh… sleepless night. I could sing a song about it. No, I could record a whole album about sleepless nights… La la li la la do re mi *sing* Okay, don't worry, I'm not going to start singing now; in fact, I don't think anyone has ever heard me sing (at least I hope so, since I can get a bit loud in the shower… so singing!! Not what you think… arrgh). But you can probably guess that I belong to the group of people who also suffer from sleep disorders and hope to fall asleep before 2 AM at some point. And even if it gets later, I'm usually awake again by 7 or 8 AM, even on weekends.
