Well, not always, but it happens sometimes… *yawn* Since we're talking about sleepless nights: That's also the name of the latest fragrance from the Black Opium line, for which I received a free sample from YSL (thanks to everyone here who pointed out the promotion in the forum!). I have already tested the regular EDP of Black Opium and found it okay, but already from the heart note, it felt rather weak. I hope this fragrance does much better… The fragrance: As with Black Opium EDP, you can also perceive orange blossoms at the beginning here. However, this time not together with the coffee, but rather with sweet notes that smell like jasmine, which is not indicated in the fragrance pyramid. In the background, there is a slightly spicy, but not piercing pepper note. I'm not sure about the rice steam, partly because I don't really know what rice steam smells like. In any case, you can soon smell the vanilla, which gives the fragrance, as always with vanilla scents, a gentle note and, together with the sweet note, makes it appear slightly powdery. The coffee note also slowly comes through, but it is not as intense as in the regular Black Opium and remains more in the background. In fact, the coffee seems to disappear again soon, so the fragrance mainly stays sweet. The musk adds another sweet note to the fragrance and makes it appear a bit more elegant. The fragrance is rather less woody. The sillage and longevity: The sillage starts off similarly to the EDP. Quite strong and also filling the room. But unlike the EDP, the fragrance radiates significantly stronger later on and is therefore even better to smell, which I find good. The longevity is comparable to the EDP of Black Opium and lasts about eight hours. Well, maybe a tick less. The bottle: The bottle is a slightly color-modified version of Black Opium. It seems that the bottle is more reddish (but I don't know if it is transparent; I only know the bottle from photos so far). The "glitter effects" also seem to be a bit brighter and more intense. As always, there is the large porthole giving a glimpse of the fragrance liquid. The neck and the hemispherical cap are light pink and shiny. A very successful bottle. Black Opium Nuit Blanche is truly a great upgrade of the original Opium and smells really good. It is a bit more long-lasting and, above all, a bit stronger, making it great to smell on someone. Moreover, the name this time fits the fragrance better. With its sweet notes and generally pleasant scent, it is perfect as an evening and party fragrance, as it simply must appear sexy on a lady. You know, blah blah delicious, blah blah especially attractive, blah blah *sigh* This is also one of the main differences from the other fragrance. Nuit Blanche has a barely noticeable coffee note, but shines with its beautifully sweet scent. Therefore, definitely worth a test. If I were a woman, this fragrance would surely be made for me, because of my sleepless nights. To everyone else, I wish a good night :D

As a big fan of Black Opium, I bought nuit blanche without testing it first. Upon the first spray, I was still excited; it smells a bit more harmonious to me than the original. I was looking forward to a lovely winter day with a great perfume, but before I could even leave the house, nuit blanche let me down; the scent completely vanished, so I sprayed myself again - the same result. What a shame, I’d rather stick with the original.

Since I really like the original Black Opium EdP, I had to test this one. It was convenient that I received a sample. I indulged myself during the testing with a full dose of five sprays... but where is the scent??? This is exactly how I imagine an EdT - like the EdP, just much weaker. I don’t understand why so many perfumes have completely different lists of notes for the EdT and smell entirely different? I always thought it was supposed to be like the EdParfum, just weaker. That is exactly what Black Opium Nuit Blanche is for me. I find it smells like BO EdP, but simply much weaker in every aspect. What a shame for the beautiful, expressive coffee scent. What a shame for the lovely vanilla. What a shame for the beautiful fragrance! What a waste of money! The scent shows up very weakly on my skin despite the five sprays. Even in direct comparison of all three on the paper strip, this one is the weakest of all. Not necessary. Unless you really like the scent but want to consciously have only a weak dosage. In my opinion, this is the "real" EdT.

Smelling this perfume closely on skin reminds me of Mancera Red Tobacco. At first I was very disappointed since I already own Red Tobacco. But when I smelled it in air everything changed. For all the Hungarians out there this smells like a cinnamon chimney cake(fahéjas kürtöskalács). It is sweet fromt he honey, spicy from the cinnamon, almost gourmand territory. I would definitely recommend giving this a try especially around december, close to the holidays. It definitely has Christmas vibes.

Oh where do I start with this gem, I know where I can start by saying this is my favorite Montale so far. It starts with a sweet honey note, with just enough spices and oud playing nice in the background. Not a blind but your fragrance because if you are not used to niche your type fragrances, then you might not like it. But it's a true love for me.

Initial spray is very delish. It doesnt smell synthetic either which is surprising for a honey scent. If only the honey were long lasting because sadly, within 10-15 mins it disappears and all you smell is a very generic men's cologne. Its certainly not bad its just very very boring. The dry down almost resembles a cheap eau de toilette from the local drug store. I suggest before purchasing this let it sit on your skin for 20-30 mins then you get an idea what this fragrant is all about. The intial spray is impressive which is what led me to immediately purchase it. But its also misleading in that the honey COMPLETELY disappears shortly after. I tried this on my friends too just to check if the perfume perhaps wasnt syncing with my skin in particular but noppeeee. The honey note vanishes quickly on them too. I was so disappointed in honey aoud that I ended up selling it at a low price just to get rid of it quickly. Definitely not recommended if you think you be smelling like honey all day long.

This is the only way I like my honey fragrances, it’s striking and unexpected, slightly intoxicating, but not overwhelming, quite universal too, great for colder months but you can use it on a cool summer night. The quality you get for the price is very good, it lasts until you shower, stays on clothes until you wash them, the projection is insane too, perfection.

The top note of "Honey Aoud" shocked me a bit, as it smelled like I had just opened a can of tuna. But I can already say that this note fortunately disappears almost entirely after 30 minutes. However, I still notice a slight hint of it until the end, but it might just be a matter of perception. After the top note, an interesting scent develops, but it does not appeal to me at all. Unpleasant memories of "Kalemat" or "24 Gold" come to mind. So sweet, a lot of cinnamon, amber-heavy, musty, rotten, damp cellar. And like a coarse "Ambre Narguile." The Montale goes even further: the mixture of oud, patchouli, and leather makes the scent even darker and dirtier than the mentioned predecessors. Of course, in typical Montale synthetic quality, because I can't really distinguish specific oud, leather, or patchouli, but rather just a dark, slightly disgusting mass. This somewhat crude mix of honey-like, sweet vibes combined with dirt/grime will certainly find many happy recipients, but it's not for me. I'd rather take a fundamentally similar "Musc Ravageur" and enjoy the highest quality and excellence. Only the base can somewhat reconcile me; a dry cinnamon with a slightly floral vanilla arrangement almost smells delicious. Sillage and longevity are also impeccable.

About a year ago, I visited the Floris perfumery in London and came across their Honey Oud fragrance. "A dream," I thought, but unfortunately not within my budget. So I hoped to find a possible alternative and then discovered Montale's Aoud Honey, hoping the two would be similar. Fortunately, I also found a perfumery with a large Montale selection, including Aoud Honey.

Dear Mr. Montale, why do you make it so difficult for me with your fragrances? I really wanted to build a small Montale collection. I already own Roses Elixier, Chocolate greedy, and Vanille Absolut. I love them to bits! Overall, I also ordered about 14 samples from ALzD. Only Roses Elixier was a blind buy and my very first Montale.

I purchased this fragrance in anticipation of the upcoming cold days in Hamburg, after testing several scents from Montale. I didn’t really like it the first time I smelled it, or rather, I wasn’t convinced. However, when I went back to the perfumery the next day and tested it again, I really liked it!

You feel like Winnie the Pooh, you can't get enough of the honey... at first, when I applied Honey Aoud, the woody oud is quite strong and dominant, until over time the sweetness of the honey ignites and you subsequently perceive the oud much less, while the honey increasingly comes to the forefront.

I tested the fragrance 4 years ago in a perfume shop. The scent lasted all day long. I would recommend not buying this fragrance blind, as I have some friends who do not like it. The fragrance starts with a beautiful honey note and good oud and spices, so it will actually please almost everyone in the first 10 to 20 minutes.

Splendid Wood by the French Maison of Yves Saint Laurent from the exclusive YSL Luxury Perfume line 'Le Vestiaire des Parfums Oriental Collection' is a woody spicy aromatic balsamic smoky unisex perfume; was launched in 2017, this fragrance was created by Marie Salamagne and Amandine Clerc-Marie. The exclusive YSL line "Le Vestiaire des Parfums Collection Oriental" was inspired by Yves Saint Laurent's retreats in Morocco; and the fragrance Splendid Wood was inspired by the exotic wooden dresses and accessories of Yves Saint Laurent. The woody notes warm and stimulate the senses, while a fabulous cardamom of the best I've ever felt in perfumery and incense structure the perfume with a slightly smoky woody pattern, jasmine brings a classic balance hand in hand with the usual 'oud & rose combo. The cipriol heats and blends with a woody, dry cedar gives more depth to the woody base. This composition enhances an arabesque brown color palette. Unisex fragrance with masculine inclination. Woody, spicy, aromatic, balsamic, smoky perfume.

The quality of this scent is insane, that explains the high price, but I do believe the reason this fantastic perfume is almost discontinued has to be because is an expensive perfume for a designer brand, but as I wrote before, for me the price is justified by the quality, the perfect blend and the performance. I was looking for a woody scent to replace the Gucci pour Homme 1 perfume because I love cedar and incense, so when, by chance, I found this perfume, I was obsessed. Very smooth oud and intense cedar notes that are balanced with exquisite cardamom and rose. The cedar is a prominent note, so elegant, so sexy, the oud is a very pleasant and elegant oud, is not a prominent note, is just there to give depth and balance. I also smell rose and a hint of Jasmine... The bottle is very beautiful 125 ml or 75ml, you can read on the bottle " Cardamome-cedre" Just for the record, Splendid wood does not smell like Gucci pour Homme 1, probably because of the cardamom note, if you are looking for a similar scent like Gucci pour Homme 1, I can recommend you to go for Bentley Homme absolute, also a great perfume, high quality for a very low price. At the moment this is my preferred scent for night dates and formal tuxedo events.

It is a fantastic fragrance.This is my first fragrance from the Yves Saint Laurent niche line. To my nose, the cedar smell is intensely felt, mostly with woody notes. Splendid wood reminds me of being in a ponderose pine forest on a windy sunny day. it feels like walking among jasmine flowers! Definitely smells luxurious and special !

Marie Salamagne has become one of my favorite perfumers (Is that the correct gendering?). I would marry her immediately, no joke. The Arabic Rose created under her nose at Armani is a milestone in the history of perfume. YSL's Oriental Collection is becoming quite rare. The places where one can experience it here in our country can be counted on one hand. The quality of the line is overwhelming. I am happy to admit this, but the price is correspondingly steep. One must pay over 200 euros for a bottle from the Oriental Collection. Splendid Wood is so mild, deep, and rounded. It is the olfactory squaring of the circle as it gradually transitions into buttery soft wood tones. "Still waters run deep," is a saying often quoted. And this noble, elegant, and refined fragrance underscores the significance of this wisdom. Essentially, it does not draw too much attention to itself. Extremely beautiful fragrances often run the risk of sinking into blandness and drifting into pleasantry, as there are no distinctive traces to divide people, leading them to take sides based on individual attractiveness. Splendid Wood is beautiful and attractive at the same time, a very difficult balancing act, in my opinion. Especially the Armani Prive fragrances manage this Herculean task flawlessly. Here, the beauty is presented undisturbed, yet it possesses so much natural, oriental grace that the fragrance envelops itself in a captivating aura. On my skin, there is no cardamom at the start, and later on, I cannot detect any jasmine either. The fragrance goes straight to the point and presents me with a saffron-oud. A fabulously successful synthesis of East and West wafts around my nose. The aura is so oriental, but somehow I also perceive a hint of Paris. The scent is so delightful. I love it when a fragrance conveys its pure devotion, as uncompromisingly dense and emotional as Splendid Wood. I feel as if I am in a secret world on the threshold between East and West. There is also a certain kind of stability emanating from Splendid Wood. Although it is so elegant and delicate, it does not lack a solid foundation on which this magnificent wood stands. This solid foundation is just as convincing as that which resides in every Amouage, giving it its characteristic Amouage sound. Even though the name promises a strong wood scent, it ultimately does not turn out that way; it is too densely composed and far too fluffy. When the saffron-oud aura fades, it slowly transitions into such cuddly and soft wood tones. Splendid Wood is a medium for a journey through an oriental, woody atmosphere. The threshold between East and West runs through the entire fragrance, which enchants with convincing longevity and an elegant, measured, yet distinctly perceptible sillage.

Splendid Wood has long been on my list of rare colorful unicorns that I hunt for my little perfume garden. "Velours" was my first fragrance from the "Le Vestiaire" line, and it has a fixed place in my collection. Velours really surprised me positively back then and made me crave for more. It is so fine and well-crafted, following the path of the powdery-sweet scents that I love so much. :) And then there is actually a perfume in the line that even contains cardamom - one of my absolute favorite fragrance notes! Moreover, it is a main player in my favorite perfume of all time, La Nuit de L'Homme, which is also by YSL..! So it’s definitely a must-buy and test, this Splendid Wood. About the scent. The first impression I had was, "This smells similar to Velours!". I then thought about why, and I believe it’s the fine craftsmanship with which YSL has woven the fragrances of this noble line. Splendid Wood is so rounded and seamless - you can't describe it better. Like the shiny wooden floor of a luxury yacht, freshly laid and pure. Simply a solid piece of craftsmanship, perfectly tuned and balanced. No unwanted edges or splinters. In terms of notes, Splendid Wood has nothing in common with Velours, but what I noticed is that I perceive a leathery touch from this scent! It is said to contain oud and woods, but what comes across to me is more of a smooth, slightly sweet leather, with a hint of smoke. The smoke likely comes from the included incense, but it is so well integrated into the overall composition that you feel it simply stems from the oud. This classic oud impression that you know from M7 or Oud Wood is not as noticeable here; as a whole, Splendid Wood reminds me more of Godolphin or Ombre Leather than anything else. Still distinctive and individual, but that’s the association that came to me. The cardamom is not "tingling" and anchored in the top note like in La Nuit de L'Homme, but rather radiates more from the heart of the fragrance, and has a smoother, rounder quality. Yes, smooth and round captures it; that’s how you can imagine Splendid Wood. Smooth, green-balsamic, slightly spicy, sweet leather. At least for me, and I’m sure people who can isolate notes better and are more at home in the oud spectrum than I am can analyze this scent more analytically. But that’s my impression, and that’s what this is about. In any case, it’s a pleasant, high-quality scent that I believe no one will find bad. It has a very noble quality, sometimes reminding one of an expensive new car, or something like that. Which also conveys a certain luxurious lifestyle feeling, which you might not necessarily want to feel all the time. However, it can perhaps uplift you on those days when that’s exactly what you want. For me, it has earned a fixed place in my collection, and I will surely enjoy it more often, especially in the cooler seasons. :) It should also be mentioned that the packaging, like the golden mirrored bottle, magnetic cap, and fine packaging, makes the product as a whole cohesive. In this price range, it’s almost a must. Definitely a test recommendation for fans of leather or oud fragrances. :) And I can only recommend the Le Vestiaire series to everyone; I’m really curious about what else is coming my way. ;)

I am working my way through a Roja Women's sample pack and recently it was Recklesses turn. I sprayed it and immediately I thought "I've smelled this before." Low and behold I had skin tested this once months ago in an orange blossom sample spree I went on. In that time I had also completely forgotten about it. Needless to say I don't really think my opinions have changed on this one in those few months. It's pretty. Reckless starts off a soapy orange blossom that takes on a more animalic quality as wear progresses but it's never overwhelming or overly pungent. I actually am reminded that I like the scent overall but I find it overall little bland and forgettable. Performance for most Roja scents I have sampled doesn't seem to be great. Overall nice but average scent, less than average longevity and performance, stunning packaging. Like most of Roja I think this is overpriced for what you're getting and you can find more reasonably priced similar scents on the market.

Reckless - Eau de parfum for women (75 ml) Carefree is the woman who holds this chic bottle in her hands and tries the fragrance. She will want to have it on hand at all times. A lovely sweetness awaits her. Creamy, soft, and lovingly embracing in winter. Light, fresh, and clean-smelling in summer. Tender at all times, with a smile. The new formulation comes in a new bottle. The scent, as always with Roja Parfums, is masterfully woven. I can perceive vanilla and sandalwood as well as floral notes. The fragrance shifts slightly. Different facets of a diamond shine through. The young and young-at-heart woman wears Reckless. She is not careless, but rather enjoying life with optimism. She is not reckless, but curious and self-determined. A man can wear this scent if he has pronounced feminine traits or simply in memory of his first love, the ideal woman, who could also be the mother from childhood, or just as a fresh, soapy-clean aura. The bottle is excellently designed. Just the wonderful bottle is worth the purchase. Like a beam of light, it shoots high up, with a gold crown set with sparkling, very light blue gemstones. This light blue tone finds its fine echo in the glass base. The gemstones are lighter in blue than in "Oceania" and even "Isola Blu" - so different batches were not simply reused here. On the top, a beautifully curved "R" is engraved (not "Roja") - this also seems new to me. The cardboard box is almost completely white, reduced in design, and rather not worth mentioning.

This fragrance has been hiding in the stacked lineup of Montale but it is really awesome. The name is very true; just Dark Vanilla. Not overly sweet, but balanced. It dries down into a very pleasant leather (not very animalic). Once you sniff it, you instantly get the classic Montale DNA and as with most of their releases, performance is very good as far as longevity and sillage are concerned. It reminds me a little bit of Mancera Oud Vanille which is more woody and oudy than Dark Vanilla. It leans masculine but I believe women can pull it off especially in cold winter days. Pierre Montale, Merci monsieur

After reading the reviews of Dark vanilla, I had the impression that this would be a very manly scent, but I personally think that this is unisex fragrance. It has a very sweet and creamy vanilla that a woman could wear but it also has some dark notes that is very suitable for a man. Vanilla and spice and everything nice, if you don't own this, I think you should consider. A very nice Montale!

I am so glad to own a full bottle of this (I really need to stop blind-buying), it's such an underrated scent that does lean slightly feminine however doesn't matter at all! It starts off somewhat earthy and very spicy with elements of sweetness and vanilla. There is a hint of patchouli that probably gives it that earthiness that gives it this animalic, dirtiness for the first few minutes. The mid is where is begins to evolve more with an addition of suede becoming more evident, the patchouli also calms down and becomes unusually creamy with sandalwood. The base is probably why I put myself through that animalic and dirty 'phases'. It becomes a seductive blend of vanilla, suede, patchouli and sandalwood. On my skin, this beast was still projecting (not as powerful but evident) and lasted roughly 14 hours altogether. If you can sample or smell this at any chance, please do so!

I got a bunch of decants from Montale to try out every vanilla they have and sadly most disappointed me. Dark Vanilla is one of the few I like and would wear again. It's reminiscent of a Kayali fragrance with the heavy vanilla and amber, and you get some oud and spiciness coming through that makes this stand out. Like all Montale fragrances, it has strong silage and longevity. I could see this as a nice evening/date night scent.

I sought advice in a niche perfume shop. I wanted a vanilla scent that has depth and isn't just sweet. Sprayed on the test strip, I already liked Dark Vanilla very much. This strong but not overpowering leather scent combined with the vanilla suited my skin even better.

Yes, as always in my still few reviews, there is an association that came to my senses immediately upon the first spray of the sample. ---> As mentioned in the title. :) The scent caught my attention due to my underlying inclination towards leathery fragrances. I must say that I find scents with a leathery note very sensual and seductive.

Dark Vanilla is a beast. First of all, you have to be a fan of the slight synthetic quality that often accompanies Montale fragrances. The scent doesn’t smell extremely high-quality or luxurious, but it doesn’t have to. Here you get a unique dark vanilla scent, as the name suggests, that leans slightly towards Ombre Nomade.

Upon spraying the fragrance, a sweet-spicy vanilla awaits you. Over time, the scent develops more into the mysterious, as the pleasant leather and warm vanilla together create such a character. The perfume has an above-average longevity and leaves a very pleasant scent trail behind. Montale demonstrates with this perfume how incredibly luxurious vanilla can smell.

I really don't understand how this fragrance didn't receive the most hype at Montale. What makes it special for me is that the scent allows men to smell very masculine through the leather, while still remaining feminine for women. This elegant mix of vanilla and leather simply makes everyone smell great in their own way.

Sexy but in a innocent girlish dolly-like naivete called Baby doll a scent gives an impression in two ways I'm not a Child and yet not a Woman like Bravado or a Woman child- sexually a Woman plays a vulnerable and yet an a woman with full of dreams and a bit head in the clouds kind of Romantic view of the world ala the roles Marilyn Monroe was famous for, a complete contrary to the Pragmatic Pierre Balmain's Jolie Madame, Tough as Nails Robert Piguet's Bandit, and the Fiery and Tempestuous Sister Opium. Oranges open with an crisp and citusy brightens your senses then dries with tart and juicy pineapple then in a few minutes the scent dries deeper with black currents adds a sexual undercurrent then sour green apple dries the opening. Light and delicate freesia with it's airy sweetness blown across the summer sky then heliotrope a warm vanilla like scent comes steeping though has a bit of a cloyish quality Demure pink roses gives it a Velvety elegance. The drydown is simple with the usual Sandalwood dryness and the typical Powdery finishing of Vanilla. Baby Doll conjours Innocence like the cutest dollies with big and soulful eyes with long eyelashes circling your room in a protective spender white Persian kittens purring sleeping beside each of your bed in a comfortable slumber then a gentile breeze of spring blowing though a thinly diaphanous curtain, Baby Doll capture the Essence of Childhood in all of us.

I was looking for a slightly tart scent, so got this even though I hate the name & feel too old (forties) to have a bottle like that around. It's great, though. On me, the sweet and tart fruits combine to smell like redcurrant, which I rarely find in perfume. Sweet-tart, refreshing, not too candied. But I hide the bottle! (042709)

I did not expect to like this fragrance as much as I do. I figured it would be similar to Versace Bright Crystal but Baby Doll is much better in my opinion. I liked Bright Crystal but it was just "okay." It smelled typical and generic. Baby Doll smells more "special" to my nose. On my skin I get a lot of rose and pineapple and the scent is juicy and refreshing. Not overly sweet and not cloying. A nice perfume for wearing during the warmer seasons. The bottle is also very cute and pretty. I gave away my bottle of Bright Crystal but Baby Doll is a keeper!

I received this perfume as a gift along with 3 other fragrances, so it went unnoticed for a while. When I finally got around to wearing it, I was quite pleasantly surprised. The first initial spray is a strong, citrusy burst of pineapple and orange which smells a lot like tropical fruit juice, but in a nice way. The fragrance quickly mellows, and although you can still smell the citrus notes, there are more flowery notes like rose and lily of the valley. Wearing this fragrance is a lot of fun, making you feel really girly and comfortable. However, be warned that this perfume is rather strong and that it has been known to give people headaches if used in large quantities.

Baby Doll repesented for me the pinnacle of my infatuation with fruity florals - a candied fruit sweet, tartish, lovely height to be transported to. Other reviewers below have beautifully described it's effervescent fruity floralcy. 100ml of Baby Doll is a lot to get through, though, and by the end of it I was looking to different genres for scent stimulation - to veer off on paths promising vanillas, woodsy florals, musky florals, tantalising licorice, bright bitter bergamot, woody earthy, gourmand, anything, give me anything but don't make me wear Baby Doll again. If you've had it, you probably know what I mean.

Carefree, flirty, and slightly mischievous. Playful but never reckless, sweet but not saccharine. A little bit of innocence, a little bit of tease. It opens with a tart, juicy explosion of berries. Blackcurrant, rhubarb, and grapefruit. Then came the florals: watery, slightly soapy freesia, lily of the valley, and a whisper of rose, adding a light, airy touch.

bought this when it premiered in 2000... spritzed it on this morning and it still smells FABULISCIOUS! this shimmery-pink juice, with it charming glass bottle and golden cap, never ceases to amaze me both visually and scent-wise.

I'm sure it's a scent that everyone will never forget. There are times when I want to smell it too. If you wear this, everyone will become like Sailor Moon (sorry, don't laugh) Baby Doll has a scent that only Baby Doll can produce. It starts with grapefruit syrup, and it feels like it's getting heavier and heavier while shining...

Now I have to tell a little about myself. I am tall, slim, athletic, and now naturally gray. In everyday life, I am mostly classic to elegant, and in my free time, I am usually out with the dogs, dressed in a sporty-classic style. And in January, I turned 52 years old. With a wink, I explained to my husband that I will spend the second half of my life as a diva.

I just climbed the rickety ladder to the attic with trembling knees, because there are still boxes with unknown contents waiting for me up there. I opened the first one out of curiosity, and immediately came across Baby Doll - in multiple versions. This is my mom's favorite scent, and she likes to stock up.

Semi Bespoke 24 is the first Roja from the Semi Bespoke line that I am dedicating a review to. The notes made me hope for a floral, slightly chypre scent, but I was probably mistaken here. Semi Bespoke 24 is more of a fruity sweet fragrance with a gentle floral component. I really like the scent, although I can only distinctly recognize the lemon, bergamot, raspberry, and musk; the other notes are not clearly identifiable. It feels like a kind of shell around the aforementioned notes. For a Roja, this is truly surprising, as there is usually an incredible richness of notes to smell, and fruity scents are also rather atypical for Roja Dove. Now to the reason for the headline: The scent is certainly convincing, but unfortunately, I always think of Kirkè when I smell Semi Bespoke 24. This shouldn't be seen negatively, as Semi Bespoke smells more high-quality, but not significantly better to justify buying 8 bottles of Kirkè. Unfortunately, in this case, the very high price and the resulting lack of distinctiveness are a deal-breaker for a purchase. The longevity is good. Semi Bespoke 24 lasted a good 10 hours on my skin and had a sillage of an arm's length for 7-8 hours. Great scent, but for me unfortunately a bit too little innovation to justify paying the premium as a owner of Kirkè.

Initial spray is a wonderfully rich tobacco with a bubblegum smell alongside it and a vague scent of citrus rounding it off. Very unique! As it drys down, the oud comes more to the fore, it’s a creamy, Westernised, sweet oud, not an aggressive, overpowering one. The longevity and sillage is excellent, easily 8-10 hours. 8’s across the board for this one, with maybe an 8.5 for value. Really nice.

Oud Tobacco is one of Montale’s recent releases and is a mix of the two eponymous notes, with some citrus, spices, and sweets, which yields a sort of spicy, sharp, woody, resinous, sweet mix that’s very workable and apt for cooler weather. Cumin is the main listed note that accounts for the spicy, slightly animalic quality present throughout, but the oud itself does not contribute in an animalic or medicinal way, from what I can tell, but rather supports the sort of smoky, resinous undercurrent below the cumin, tobacco, and sweet contribution of tonka. The citrus / orange blossom notes are faint, at best, as the fragrance does not seem to express them very clearly to me at any point. Rather, there’s a generally well-blendedness and creaminess throughout most of the fragrance, and I imagine that the orange blossom especially helps facilitate a smoother blend. Overall, it’s a very powerful and very agreeable entry, even though it somehow reminds me slightly of designer releases (i.e. Bvlgari Man in Black, albeit with less of a V&R Spicebomb vibe) while having its own character. It’s not quite as interesting as a couple releases from Mancera / Montale from about a year ago (Precious Oud and Oud Dream, respectively) but it remains impressive that their empire can churn out good releases so consistently. In the US, Oud Tobacco is sold by Krystal Fragrance and Beverly Hills Perfumery with the standard pricing of $170 for 100ml. 7 out of 10

Montale as a brand produces a lot of hit or miss juice, this is hitting hard for sure. This was my first niche and when I first sprayed it I could smell only grape but as my nose got better I could see the complexities of the fragrance and how the spice and sweet citrus made it seem like a grape note. The opening is great in my opinon , its very sweet with a note of a sweeter pipe tobacco which isnt smokey at all, just more of a bolder statement note. Orange blossom and citrus which are different then a classic citrus, instead of being refreshing and "Clean" this is more of a mix between herbal citrus tea and those creamsicles. Cumin doesnt really make the scent spicey but more of an influence on grounding it and calming the sweetness so its not gormound but more of a sophisticated slightly sweet aroma of formality. The dry down doesnt change the dynamic it only refines the scent and adds a creamy factor to the overall feel. Also the bottle is amazing red+gold is sexy and for 70$ on jomashop its a steal.

No tobacco, no problem. Maybe they should name this Oud Tonka. It starts off very bright, then settle into a Tonka with Oud . It does become a little creamy. So it's Tonka and cream with a little oud that's very faint. I do get some type of floral at the beginning maybe it's jasmine along with some citrus, that's more like the peel of the orange . That is all coming from the first spray and I will have to give this a full wearing before my final judgment. So a second review may be coming soon.

This scent is not for the faint of heart. At the beginning, a tobacco bomb unfolds that I have never experienced before. Once the Oud Tobacco settles, there is no escape. A sillage of this magnitude is very hard to come by. A good friend told me that after an evening visit, this Montale had permeated the scent of the entire hallway until the next afternoon. One must be careful with the dosage, but it is a knockout. You either despise it or you love it! A showstopper as ever. I got to know and love it in the perfume shop without any actual intention to buy; for me, it's a perfect scent for special evenings paired with a shirt and fine Scotch.

The notes sound so promising, YouTubers praise it to the skies, it has great reviews - I had to have it! And I really wanted to like it. Maybe it's my skin chemistry, or my nose, but unfortunately not much happens on my skin: In the top notes, I smell tobacco and after about 10 minutes it smells like an average men's drugstore fragrance.

Tobacco and Oud, Oud and Tobacco. No matter how you turn it, I can confidently say that I have a certain fondness for both notes. Thus, it was only logical that I would eventually take on Montale's Oud Tobacco. And as luck would have it, my last perfume order included three samples from Montale - including the fragrance discussed here.

The Oud Tobacco by Montale... Definitely not to be confused with the Tobacco Oud by Tom Ford. The latter smells exactly like its name suggests. Anyone expecting an explosion of Oud and tobacco with Oud Tobacco will likely be disappointed. Nevertheless, the OT from Montale is a true surprise.

Upon spraying, I am immediately greeted by a spice-oud-incense-spice and intense citrus splash that I have never smelled before. It's a shame, as I find the mix too much and the citrus note completely out of place in my opinion. This disappears after 1.5 hours. Thank goodness. They could have left out all the citrus flavors, including the sumac.

It starts very citrusy and ends rather spicy-fresh. Oud and tobacco are more in the background, but slightly noticeable. The tonka bean is mainly perceived at the end. One spray and I'm instantly in love! This fragrance is a power bomb! Very intense and with a high recognition value. With this scent, you will definitely stand out. Compliments are guaranteed.

I love Roja’s pour femme line of fragrances - Madison is similar to 51 in texture but on my skin this is more fruity and has more amber/ woody incense whereas 51 is silky powdery Orris/Iris. On my skin the predominant notes are: mandarin, black current, Violet , Orris, cedar, incense and Benzoin. Madison also has great projection for a Parfum. The dry down is very oriental and I love it. If you can find a bottle for a fair price and you like the notes- go for it. (Smells nothing like Diaghilev or other suggestions)

that’s how I felt about “Madison” when I first tested it. Quickly formed a judgment, just as quickly wrote a statement, and just as quickly rated it. And once again, one of the unwritten rules for perfumes proves true: “You shall not write hasty statements!” My first statement about Madison has long been deleted, as I repeatedly caught myself being drawn in the morning to the small remaining liquid in my sample box. This made me ponder deeply. How could it be that a fragrance I had dismissed as mediocre was worn by me far more often than, for example, my favorites “Danger/Roja” or “Vol de Nuit/Guerlain” or “Cuir de Russie/Chanel,” all of which I felt from the first spray were “must-have” scents? As the sample slowly and inexorably approached its end, it gradually dawned on me: I simply feel good with “Madison” - and it fits perfectly for me during work hours. Not too much, not too little, not too extravagant, but not too simple. I spray it at noon and occasionally reapply - and then I really enjoy that fresh opening it offers. It greets me cheerfully with bergamot and other citrus scents, unsweetened, but far from bitter or scratchy. Within minutes, Madison becomes like a veil dance. The different notes lie on top of each other, revealing and covering each other again, only to let other layers become visible shortly thereafter. Depending on what my nose focuses on, different and sometimes contrasting scent impressions float into my consciousness. Gentle incense, unobtrusive musk, peppery spice, a hint of wood. Interwoven in between is a floral variety. May rose appears when I check the pyramid - and that makes me very, very curious. I have significant difficulties with rose scents; rose is often too sour, too spicy, too dominant to the point of being overwhelming for me. Here I might have caught a whiff of jasmine, but even that is not certain. The floral note of the perfume is hard to grasp. I associate it with neither a radiant white flower nor anything dark, but rather something in between, elegantly feminine, yet absolutely not dowdy. With Madison, I can only approach a description of the scent with the help of the provided fragrance pyramid. It is not easy to grasp, as this interplay of different notes forms a complex composition that completely overwhelms my nose without assistance. My experience with fruits in perfumes is similar to that with rose: a tricky topic. Raspberry and strawberry, which for my taste appeared far too often in perfumes for a while, often remind me - I ask for the forgiveness of all the fans of this note - of the fruit dwarfs that my children once devoured almost obsessively. With Madison, I actually unmistakably smell a fruity note that is listed in the pyramid as black currant. And that captures it wonderfully. Black currants with their tart acidity and the slightly metallic taste they leave in the mouth when eaten create a wonderful counterbalance to the sweetness and spice that otherwise dominate the scent. Madison becomes increasingly powdery on the skin, ethereal and translucent, without losing its presence and contour. I perceive the aspect of tart acidity, which I attribute (with knowledge of the pyramid) to the black currant, even into the base - and it makes Madison exactly what I use it for: a daily wearable yet extraordinary companion! Since I currently have incredibly long workdays, such scents are particularly important in my collection, and I am glad that I had a generous sample of Madison - and thus the opportunity to get to know and love this beautiful fragrance. And how does the rating look now? I had given it a (for me actually devastating) 7 - and now I easily place Madison between 9 and 10! And once again from me: A toast to the souk and the opportunities it offers us all!

A few times a year at least this body spray crosses my mind. If I close my eyes and will it hard enough, I can sometimes even still smell it. Nothing will ever compare. It has been over 10 long, hard years without this scent gracing my nostrils. All I can hope for is that somehow, some day, Victoria secret will rerelease this body spray. I would sacrifice my first born child for one singular whiff. The sheer turmoil I experience every time I think about this spray knowing I may never smell it again crushes every fibre of my being. It’s a gut wrenching pain from deep within. If our lord and saviour above really is watching down upon us, may he release this scent back into the universe once and for all to relieve our pain and suffering.

I'm not sure I can start talking about Roses Musk without getting tears falling down my face.. I'm sitting here, in front of a screen, I raise my scarf to smell the Roses.. Roses Musk is delicate.. fragile.. it's a sensational whisper full of promises ...reflected in the enchanted lovers eyes... Don't be fooled by it's vulnerable nature.. They will caress you and you will feel like it's the first time you truly see the world... Time will stop ticking. Some roses are dowagers; others are jammy fruity florals; others are orientals. To my nose, Montale ROSES MUSK--at least the batch from which my sample was drawn--is really a masculine rose. Lots of ambergris (ambroxan, it seems) suffuses the rose petals of this composition. In the opening, I also smell a blast of iso-E-super cedarishness, and it lingers throughout. There is more ambergris here, I'd say, than musk, but the musk contributes no doubt as well to the overall effect of this perfume which pushes it all the way to unisex, and just a touch over the edge to the masculine side. I am quite sure that men could and would wear and enjoy this creation, if only they knew! I actually feel a bit like a traitor saying this, given the glowing review below by Turquoise, but ROSES MUSK does not settle down into a snuggly rose scent for quite some time, and even then the ambergris-musk base stays around throughout the entire duration of the wear. I read the reviews on the German side, looking for some sort of affirmation of my perceptions, and I found that there were a couple of naysayers over there. So it seems to be true: to those who are sensitive to ambergris/ambroxan and musk, they really dominate this composition. Others may well (and apparently do) smell right through them to a heavenly rose. I have enjoyed wearing two full milliliters of ROSES MUSK--a generous manufacturer's carded sample--and can report that the longevity and sillage of this creation are superb. However, I do not really consider this to be a rose perfume, as strange as that may sound. It's just that I've worn so many more rose-centric compositions that next to those, this one seems like a rose-tinted ambergris-musk perfume. There is something very animalic and altogether foreign to rose going on here. In a word: ambergris. Guys, come on down!

TL;DR: Isola Snow surprises positively. A cool-fruity pear opening meets a refined, powdery-floral heart phase. The synthetic note is clearly perceptible, but well integrated. The woody drydown makes the fragrance suitable for everyday wear and gives it more character than its predecessors. With a mix of optimism and a hint of doubt, I spray the new Isola Snow on my wrist - and I am pleasantly surprised! The fragrance has a strong, synthetic opening that, unlike the previous release "Elysium Noir | Roja Parfums," smells significantly better. The pear adds a cool, slightly fruity undertone, while a floral powderiness gently rounds out the scent in the background. Isola Snow feels clean and exudes a certain coldness, reminiscent of "Pegasus | Parfums de Marly." The fragrance has a distinct synthetic note, which this time is more carefully woven into the rest of the composition. In the first thirty minutes, the synthetics continue to diminish, while the floral-powdery heart notes become more pronounced. It is precisely this powdery note that gives the fragrance its warm effect. One can imagine it like a cozy fur coat in the cold winter air. In the background, the rose also makes its presence known, providing a certain sweet aroma. Isola Snow becomes softer and more floral as it develops, while the pear sometimes breaks through more strongly. Although the synthetic aspect is clearly noticeable, I do not find it off-putting or overwhelming, but merely unusual. In the drydown, the woody base notes come into play, providing a warm, almost creamy finish. Overall, Isola Snow is not a typical Roja fragrance and not a groundbreaking creation either. In my opinion, it is still an interesting and pleasant scent that has more depth and character than its predecessors. It evokes the end of winter when spring slowly arrives and feels like a relaxed, everyday fragrance that gains a special nuance once the heart notes emerge.

First of all, this is my first review, so please be gentle with me. But now to the fragrance, the name says it all. It smells cold, yet delicate, beautiful but not really flashy, just like Snow White, which is why I find this comparison quite fitting. However, the pure scent of snow is not enough for me to consider it a good fragrance, and it seems Antoine Cotton shared this opinion as well. At first, you definitely perceive the direct cold, as if you were opening a door and snow was blowing in, but then a lovely sweetness from all the fruits and flowers comes through. As it develops, it becomes a bit spicier, the cardamom makes an appearance, and the cold fades a little. In the drydown, a bit of wood comes in along with amber, and the fragrance has now completed itself. Not only very beautiful but also full of character. Price-wise, we are again at a point where you really have to think about the fragrance, but if you are willing to pay for the top tier, you will definitely not be disappointed here.

How much of a catholic does one have to be to wear this fragrance? If you didn't get enough in Sunday's service, with a few spritzes of Full Incense you can easily revive the sacred feeling in no time. Montale did not promise too much: Full Incense is a full load of church frankincense! Decency is not the matter of Pierre Montale. Perfumes like Oud Cuir d'Arabie or Chocolate Greedy show that he is honest about what he does. We may put Full Incence in the same line. Incense fragrances can differ a lot from each other. Often, they are simply just especially smoky, but they keep a certain warmth which make them good company on cold days – L'Homme Sage by Divine would be one of that kind. But Full Incense is different, and this is best described with an image. I remember biking trips in midsummer, perhaps France. It is one of those far too hot days that you arrive at a medieval abbey, somewhere in the countryside. Its ancient walls promise a relaxing cool. You enter a dark gothic or romanesque nave, and instantly you sense the cold and stale frankincense leftovers of the last service. It is always cold and damp in those ancient masonries, even with summer heat outside. How beautiful it would be in November, you may think, facing this deathly cold that seems to creep from the undercroft – that strange blend of frankincense, mould, foxing, dust and dampness. There is only one little thing that modifies this impression in the heart note: there is a distinct resinous note with a somewhat synthetic appeal, probably the elemi. Its quality might direct you towards a hyper-modern Comme des Garçons fragrance. But this short irritation blends in consistently. I remember the strange, synthetic depth of Neil Morris' Vapor, which this note resembles – that pervasive ethereal fragrance that reminds of white clouds on an infinite blue sky. So, the ashen, gloomy grave's atmosphere contrasts well with the glaring, surreal colours of summer – an enormously deep, suspiciously blue sky with sharply drawn white clouds and the almost unbearable brightness of a midsummer's noon. Okay, you can blame frankincense to have certain effects – supposedly similar to a runner's high caused by fast biking in the heat. Some things in there may fit together. For me, it is just this contrast that prevents Full Incense to slide into the kitsch of those Gregorian chant and medieval abbey fashions that come up once in a while. What can be more uncanny than sepulchral cold in midsummer? Only the drydown is somewhat conventional with its increasing presence of patchouli – but one can reapply. And so, I would like to recommend Full Incense as a true summer wear – to all friends of dark romanticism who prefer to keep an alternative state of mind amidst all summer's joy.

I've been wearing Montale's Full Incense (albeit sparingly) in tropical weather over the last week or so, and have come to the conclusion that this is definitely the 'one' Incense to have if this happens to be a favourite note. A 'heavenly' blend of Labdanum and Frankincense is faithfully supported by a good dose of Patchouli and a dry Cedar, but there is an inherent sweetness here too. I'm wondering whether the Elemi is responsible for that, because its characteristic 'pine and lemon' sharpness is not evident here. Elemi sometimes lends a 'clean skin in the sunshine' vibe ... at least to my nose, but that is not apparent here either. Rather, Full Incense brings back vivid memories of high holy day Masses in the stone cathedral where I was an altar boy in my youth ... but then it would :). I don't think one can get very far away from these images when Frankincense is included in a fragrance. One could, however, get less inspired renditions of this note in a fragrance. I have tried a few of the well known offerings including Tauer, Heeley and CdG ... but all have left me a little flat and quite frankly, bored. Sonoma Scent Studio's Incense Pure runs a respectable second place to this one, while the only 'better' Incense frag I have ever sampled is by Killian's Incense Oud ... which one must sell a kidney to afford. Superlative sillage and great longevity will attest to the high quality of raw materials used in this offering by House Montale. I get at least 8 hours on my perfume munching skin and have had tons of compliments while wearing this. One of my friends (who knows that I am a complete fragrance whore LOL) even said that I should never wear anything else, ever again. All in all, Full Incense does the best job of faithfully recalling memories of childhood while not breaking the bank to do so. I highly (and humbly) recommended this one as the reference Incense fragrance to own.

Montale Full Incense smells like an ancient story of aromatic pine, strange, sugared crystals of frankincense, and fresh, grounding cedar shavings. It’s sacred and a bit weird, like an epic legend with an unexpected instance of surreal comedy. Perfume-wise it’s a bit comparable to CdG Avignon, but where that one conjures a chilly, off-putting atmosphere, this is woody and warm and somehow beautifully wacky, like hallucinogenic incense smoke rising from a cracked clay vessel balanced on smoldering embers in the desert woodlands, but in a locale far removed from our reality. On the world of Thra plays out a drama between the tyrannical Skeksis and the Gelfling, as a darkening blight threatens the existence of all. Full Incense is what I imagine scents the scene wherein the Gelfling heroes have arrived at the Circle of the Sun and encounter the kind Skeksis known as the Heretic and the Wanderer. What ensues is the weird and brilliant puppet show within a puppet show, and they all must have thought wow, am I high right now? I feel a bit like that myself when I wear this scent.

Every time I spray the capri I go on a wonderful journey. The sun is calls me. So where? Wherever the Mediterranean sun makes me happy... For example, in the south of Anatolia... In Caria, Lycia and Pamphylia. In all geographies where Roman and Hellenic civilizations left their mark. Also, these are the places where beautiful citrus fruits grow... As someone who likes to travel and explore, I follow the call of the sun. I am using the capri at Soleil these days. It opens up with a sweet pleasant delicious, citrus scent. From the opening, the citrus effect is a little more dominant than the other notes. It gives a different and soft - gourmand feel. This may be due to the pleasant harmony of kumquat, grapefruit and white flowers. Because over time, the citrus theme becomes fruity - citrus and white flowers make themselves felt. About half an hour after opening, the fruity - citrus effect is balanced by white flowers. The scent becomes more balanced. White flowers are in harmony and solidarity with pleasant citrus scents. Fruity citrus effect and creamy white flower aura are intertwined. These notes support each other. Finally, a wonderful, soft creamy-sweet citrus scent develops. That's very likeable. At this time it has a nice and slightly mysterious background, and the creamy effect can give a slight buttery smell in the background. This odor continues to smell the same linearly on my skin over time. After a while, the white flowers gradually disappear and the scent turns into a sweet candy scent. Therefore it's a fragrance that tends to be feminine. Then it dries softly and lightly. I've been trying this fragrance for a while. generally I'm satisfied with it. As a man, I like to use this scent, even though the scent tends to become feminine over time. Sometimes I also use it as a room fragrance. I think it is suitable for warm weather and summer evenings or afternoons. Also soleil de capri isn't a very strong scent. Therefore you can re-spray every 5 or 6 hours. It lasts more than 7+ hours on my skin.

…in a fairy-tale time, when wishing still helped: One only had to tightly squeeze their eyes shut - and found themselves on a warm late spring day in an Italian ice cream café. Unfortunately, it’s not that simple nowadays. We have to resort to other means. So: I really want spring. And if you want something with all your might, what better aid could there be than a corresponding Montale? After all, they also want something with all their might. And indeed, recently as part of a swap (many thanks to KC2503!) I found a sample of a Montale in the envelope with the magic words ‘Soleil’ and ‘Capri’ on it. Deus ex machina. The opening offers not only the promised palette of citrus fruits, but there’s also a green note in between, possibly a corresponding leaf. Alongside that is a slightly artificial prick from hesperidic peels, like freshly grated lemon zest. I also find it smells a bit like fresh fig. I borrow the “crisp apples” from the comment of the esteemed Taurus1967, as they fit perfectly too. The white flowers are very understated. The same goes for the spices. I am genuinely shocked in a positive way that a Montale can come across as Mediterranean. Only in the third hour do the aforementioned spices achieve any notable presence. Cinnamon, yes, has already been mentioned. But also things like clove, nutmeg, or allspice. Just their aroma, no sharpness, no prickliness. The flowers, on the other hand, remain elegantly unobtrusive and almost merge with the creamy musk base. Around midday, the spice becomes more pronounced. The prickliness of the citrus fruit is gradually replaced by spicy pricks. For that, the aforementioned spices simply had to become a bit more defined, to exploit their potential more strongly. It happens so slowly that I suddenly wonder if I have been literally led by the nose for quite some time. The afternoon offers another shift, new moisture-retaining elements are called from the bench to the field. Two variations come to mind: First, I imagine a hint of diffuse woodiness alongside the musk, possibly a light artificial wood note is involved. Second, some daffodils have white flowers, and there’s a light, airy bitterness in here…. Be that as it may, it somehow remains fresh. Not really citrusy towards the end, but fresh. The fragrance lasts about seven to eight hours in total, until only soapy musk remains - very decent. Conclusion: A straightforward sunny scent that skillfully extends its freshness through spice, perhaps wood, and possibly daffodil. No olfactory acrobatics, simply beautiful. And - what can I say: It worked! After a still frosty morning (including scraping ice off the windshield!), there was bright sunshine all day with at least double-digit temperatures! I can’t ask for more in mid-March in Hamburg. Well done, Soleil de Capri!

Excerpt from the script in short form: A man living in the wilderness of Canada returns to the civilization of the first half of the 19th century after a year. Apart from dense, long matted hair and beard, as well as dirt and layers of leather and fur clothing, one cannot discern the man's appearance. Man in a room with a wooden tub filled with steaming water. On the edge of the tub lies a piece of soap. He removes his layers of fur and leather. Underneath is a soiled onesie. The man sits lathered in the tub. Only a small piece of soap remains. The man stands with a towel around his loins in front of a small mirror, shaving his beard and hair with a razor. Camera pan: In fresh everyday trousers and a shirt with suspenders, with a freshly trimmed beard and still damp cut hair, the incredibly attractive young Clint Eastwood is visible. ………. This is amber the way it should be: teasing in the opening, surrounded by bergamot and geranium for sparks; giving in to vanilla in the process, but never too sweet; only just kept in pace by coriander and vetiver. I am still trying to understand what it is that is so "blue" about this amber. Perhaps the cool notes used in the formula or the calming note of bourbon geranium? In which case would make it a metaphor. Blue Amber opens up minutely spicy and herbaceous. The combination is almost medicinal, but soon dissipates leaving you with a cozy, creamy, yet powdery dry down. This particular amber gets straight to the point, but holds little complexity. How does this differ from Histoire's Ambre 114? Thyme, nutmeg, sandalwood, cedarwood. Which makes Ambre 114 perfectly gender neutral, drawing the line down the middle. Blue Amber lacks those wood notes, so it leans ever so slightly feminine, but everyone's perception is different. While Histoire's Ambre 114 has more depth, Montale fragrances are more concentrated. This was not intended to be a groundbreaking fragrance, but one that caters to amber lovers.

Sweet amber and that's it. The sweetest (but not cloying) pure amber. The opening is a bit spicy, but then dries down to a goergeous amber and vanilla smell. Much more wearable than Ambre Sultan, its very mineral. For me this is as good as Ambre Précieux, but this one has better lasting power. Definetely a wonderful amber. Updated January 2014
