I wound up buying both but sadly, I no longer own Red Vetiver because I used it all. Contemplating on buying another bottle of it though. Blue Amber had some kind of allure to me when I first smelled it.

For years, I wanted to finally write a comment about Blue Amber, as it has long been one of my favorite fragrances. In the meantime, many great comments have been written that contain pretty much everything I wanted to say, some even with the same phrases and images that went through my mind. I will try to avoid redundancy as much as possible.

... my old, somewhat haggard history teacher (his resemblance to Yoda was always unmistakable) used to say when he entered the classroom. Protests from the students ("...but it's so cold outside..") he would dismiss with a shaking head and a smiling "no no no" and get to work on opening the window.

Everyone knows the proverbial "black sheep" in families, perhaps not from personal experience, but at least by hearsay. This "title" is not really a compliment; it doesn't just fall into one's lap but must be earned. All in all, this "distinction" is rather negatively connoted.

Intro To me this is very elegant, sophisticated, luxurious, rich feminine scent. Occasion Suitable for most occasions, especially the elevated ones like a gallery opening, an evening dinner outing. This is not a scent for events like children's parties, you need to give it respect it deserves. This is not a playful perfume for teenagers or 20-somethings. It does not smell like an old lady (no age shame but you know this vibe from some other perfumes) but it smells like a confident, smart, elegant, sophisticated woman that you would love to have long conversations with. Season Spring or early summer or summer evenings, well into early fall. Notes & composition It is floral, powdery and a tiny bit sweet/ gourmand. A lot of white florals but it's not white florals overdose. Some cherry in the background adds gourmand fruitiness while a bit of leather & oud although almost non-detectable create depth & dimension. It is quite complex with the amount of notes, and they are well blended. The note accord play is incredible: one moments you detect a certain notes combination & some other time - you detect something in addition to that. Performance It is quite present but not screaming in your face, confident but not intimidating. This is a woman who worked a lot on herself, knows what she likes and wants and looks like and seems like soft & kind which some can mistaken for weakness but there's no weakness in this perfume. It is a strong person who lived through a lot & like a Phoenix re-built herself & can now be soft and kind but that comes from and with incredible strength. Like a Queen - gentle & moving softly and slowly but there's confidence & power in every move, note, and color. It blends beautifully with skin, lasts a good day on skin & like a week on clothes. Incredible scent. Outro If you have the budget - go for it. I have over 150 FBs and this has a special place in my heart/nose.

If Torani decided to make a fragrance, it would smell a lot like this. It is a extremely sweet, strawberry-scented corn syrup kind of scent. Almonds and vanilla add a bit of "flavor" in the drydown. Besides syrup, one could compare this perfume to the scent of a Strawberry Shortcake doll but without the strong plastic note. Unlike most fruity perfumes, Mukhallat lasts a very long time, about 7-8 hours on my skin. I have a 2 mL sample I purchased a few months ago, and I haven't been able to get through 1/4 of it. Believe it or not, this is even too sweet for me. I won't be purchasing a full bottle.

I am so happy this one did not turn out to be yummy or overwhelmingly gourmand on my skin! I hardly recognize the notes, but the most prominent smell I get are waxy almonds with a few drops of sweet strawberry syrup over them. It gives the bubble gummy feeling and although it does not smell natural but rather plastic and rubbery, I manage to like it! I have never tried anything similar to this... Great fragrance!

On one hand, I do understand reviews that broadly compare this to the scent of bubblegum, strawberry flavoured to be exact. It is sweet. Broadly fruity. Unnatural. On the other, I absolutely detest the opinion of anyone and everyone who doesn’t primarily see this as an oriental fragrance. When someone says “synthetic bubblegum” I think of a westernized version, like the scent of Hubba Bubba or something. This is vastly different. The association can be understood, but the feeling of this perfume belongs to that of an Arabian or Indian princess. Very oriental, very balsamic. Spicy, even. On fragrantica this was voted similar to Snow Fairy by lush. I had to hold back laughing because while they are the same coin, they are completely on the opposite sides. The scent itself isn’t similar in the slightest. One is a modern, civilized Barbie, the other dates back to the medieval times and could be used as a charm potion in the East. Sidenote: This also reminds people of headshops or doll-heads, which I read on various platforms in different fonts. While that association is definitely more spot on than the previous, it fails to capture the rarity and exlusivity of this one. This is special and never felt before. Whether you like it or hate it, your memory will never escape this thing. Baraka chique if you will. Nothing extraordinary or unwearable, YET something to remember, which directly contrasts the bubblegumy feeling (bubblegum is usually used derogatory, when something feels generic, consumeristic or easy to digest).

Mukhallat is an Arabic word meaning mixture. Mukhallats are blends of essential oils and fragrance materials. The Arabic Mukhallats typically contain rose, musk, oud, and amber notes. Montale's Mukhallat is different. Musk is already included. But the wild strawberry scent dominates everything. It smells like Hubba-Bubba, Emily strawberry, fruit gummy candies, and it is incredibly intense and synthetic. The scent probably calms me because it reminds me of childhood or youth; in any case, I was in a bad mood today and therefore sprayed my neck with Mukhallat. Two sprays, a killer dose. After that, the family tester M wanted nothing to do with me. I had to think of "50 ways to lose your lover." Sneak out, hop on the bus (and drive away), lose the key, or spray yourself with Mukhallat. Family tester Q also finds it terrible. I myself got a headache, but it may not have been due to Mukhallat. The projection is strong, the longevity is good. I would find it strange on men, or even stranger than my surroundings find it on me. It is probably intended for 13-year-old girls. Mukhallat can be used year-round as a therapy or repellent element. After a few hours, the projection weakens. I am also allowed to participate in family life again.

There’s really not much more to say about this fragrance! Oh yes! Because I have my very own story about this specimen :) My best friend from Trier visited me last Monday in Cologne, and since we are both very interested in perfumes and I found a store that also carries Montale, we naturally went there! I had already been able to test some Montale fragrances beforehand, as well as having some in my collection, and Mukhallat was of course familiar to me! My friend was very interested in the scent, I was less so, as I never thought it would be something for me ;) Well then, we tested various houses, I also tried some unknown Montales (2 of them came home with me that day) until I spotted Mukhallat, sprayed it on a tester, and held it under Kathy's nose! She was immediately smitten, and I was transported back to my childhood! To me, it smells exactly like Wrigleys Extra for Kids in the pink packaging! Wow, I thought! But do I really want to smell like this?!? Before we left the store, Kathy sprayed herself with the fragrance, and we headed towards the train! Time and again, a waft of scent came my way with the wind, and I thought: okay, this is how you MUST smell :-) I was now very much taken with it and ordered it the next day! Yesterday, the lovely item arrived, and I sprayed it twice on my wrist around 12:30 PM. Now it’s 7:00 AM the next day, and there’s still a hint of fragrance to be sensed! This fragrance really does a great job in terms of longevity and sillage! And do you know what the best part is?! My friend also received it yesterday, and now we have a scent that always reminds us of each other and connects us! We are so far apart and yet so close, as we were able to share this fragrance experience together :-) This fragrance is great LOVE for me, and it’s perfect for autumn/winter now :-)

Have I mentioned that I am susceptible to advertising? When I read the quite a few reviews and statements about Mukhallat, I thought immediately: I have to have it! The scent seemed to fit me perfectly. Synthetic strawberry bubblegum with vanilla, musk, and almonds - it sounded so kitschy that it was almost beautiful. No.

From the life of the gourmand aunt: I am standing in the perfume store, the small, thin, and really nice-looking young saleswoman is searching for a scent for me. Not easy, as I have become quite spoiled by Escada Collection (unfortunately, it remains simply unattainable *wine*) and Mugler's Essence Absolue. She is really trying hard, sweet, gourmand, fruity puhhhh.

Some time ago, I felt the urge to dive back into the wonderful world of books and sought out a small dusty esoteric bookstore in my city. I was immediately welcomed by clouds of incense, meditation music, and dream catchers hanging from the ceiling. This time, I chose the magic corner and immersed myself in the world of witches and wizards.

Oh man.... it was so good at first... on the test strip, the scent lasts wonderfully long, smells wonderfully fruity-vanilla, just delicious enough to bite into. Somehow like cheap chewing gum, and that’s not meant to be insulting. How long it followed me. For weeks.

Montale likes to be different and that's not a bad thing, but here they have somewhat missed the mark compared to the fragrances I have tested from this perfume house. Even when I remove the cap of the sample, I am greeted by a hint of Hubba Bubba Cherry gum.

I would buy it if I could find it anywhere. Unfortunately, that's not the case and I have to make do with my sample from the sharing. Recently, I've often thought about how much I would be willing to spend if a fragrance is as beautiful as this one. I won't list all the components mentioned in the pyramid from top to base. I can't perceive them distinctly enough from one another anyway, and arranging words around the pyramid would just be a chore. I find this unnecessary. What particularly impressed me while wearing the perfume was the fruity iris, which is juicy and in no way dry or dusty. The peach note is warmly ambried, excellent! I smell a patchouli shimmer, clear and mild, no mustiness, no crypt. It is art to assemble parts into a grand whole that, when considered alone, are not particularly special. This fragrance is complete in itself; any additional embellishment would be too much. Moreover, the longevity of eight to twelve hours is remarkable. I can still perceive this lovely scent on my scarf days after spraying it. I like this Roja so much that I have to throw my reservations overboard. I'm not stingy, but the thought that with just one press of the spray button, six to eight euros irretrievably evaporate into the atmosphere gives me a headache. I will jump over my shadow and take the coins from my piggy bank, which is a Holstein cow for me, to wear this fragrance on special occasions. This could be a visit to the lending library or on an expected heavy day at work, where the fragrance carries. It does so even during Puccini's and Verdi's operas. When worn, compliments come quickly. This is usually followed by the obligatory question about which fragrance it is and, above all, how much it costs. And then, at the latest, I will be awkwardly embarrassed again. Especially when I know the personal circumstances of the person asking and realize that they have to stretch every cent. It's a bit decadent, and maybe I'll consider a different strategy and announce that I've forgotten the name. Oh, my Rome, how beautifully you burn!

Biene Maja and Willi have consumed too much poppy. They lie with wide-open eyes in the poppy field and are on a psychedelic journey.... On their trip, their meadow looks so different...so many various blooming treasure chests....they fly from one radiant beautiful blossom to the next...rolling in sweet pollen. They fly on to fruits and slurp the most delicious fruit nectar. Covered in pollen and fruit nectar, they take a nap on fragrant woods. Some colorful, snorting oxen pass by. After several hours, our little bees have returned to the here and now and buzz contentedly on. ...... LOVE is a complex Roja masterpiece that surely deserves a poetic review at a very high level... So sorry... I'm not in the mood

One of my favourite vetivers and favourite Montales. This fresh combination of spices and vetiver seems to appeal me a lot! I just purchased a full bottle from this beauty. This scent is really relaxing, and sets my mind to a relaxing, confident state. This smells like a hay of dried vetiver roots splashed with Grapefruit and Black Pepper. I smell Elemi, Patchouli, Cedarwood too, which adds to the complexity of the scent. These notes stay in the background, never overpowering the vetiver/spice notes. Great longevity and sillage. On a sidenote: I have and use both Terre d'Hermes and Montale's Vetyver. I admit they are similar, but if you "listen", you can smell the differences. Honestly I can recommend both.

Red Vetiver is exclusive and gorgeous. It is far better than Tom Ford's Grey Vetiver because this RV smells so rich and elegant. I like this better than Chanel Sycomore (sweeter and milder) & even with my Terre de Hermes EDP & EDT. RV is strong but non cloying. It is a scent that would make a statement that you've got a wonderful taste in fragrance. It is rich, the vetiver is formal, the projection and longevity is to die for. So far, I have tried many Vetiver fragrance from designers to Niche vetivers even the 1902 Vetiver. But of all these frags, my top is RV, second is Encre Noir, next would be Sel de Vetiver, TDH EDP, Sycomore & L'Occitane Vetyver. Red Vetiver is good to blind buy so long as you have an idea what a vetiver note smelled from other perfumes. You can't go wrong with RV. It is for me, so far, Montale's best after trying my other Montales: Red Aoud, Black Aoud, Patchouli Leaves, White Aoud and Aoud Ambre. Montale Red Vetiver: 9.5/10 ... It is almost a holy grail, almost, a wonder!

Yes, Red Vetyver is mostly like Terre D'Hermes, BUT with a better lasting power in my skin. In my opinion the spices added to Red Vetyver gives an edge to it. Wonderful scent for summer/spring, althought it can be used all year around. Sillage is medium, lasting power is around 10 hours and projection is medium-heavy. If you are in doubt, just buy both them: two great scents.

Citrusy start, clear vetiver dry down. I think of this as a "middle of the road" vetiver - not too dank, not too heavy, not too earthy - but not as bright or light or dry as other vetivers I've smelled, like in THoO's Each Other, for example. I found this scent to be fairly straightforward and linear. Citrusy top faded quickly, as these are wont to do, leaving my impressions of this fragrance as mostly just a vetiver. A lovely vetiver, but basic and straightforward nonetheless. The comparison to Terre d'Hermes is obvious and must be commented on. I found it less complex and interesting than TdH, which I was surprised by. I also found it had less longevity and sillage - also a surprise for me given this is an EDP. Perhaps I went noseblind to it? Also notably that the flinty notes I love so much in TDH are absent here.

Yesterday, my sales associate specifically descended into the deep cellar to serve me Red Vetiver. With Montales, I am always cautious, as they can be hits - or completely miss the mark. But the cellar association remained intact - and led me to the dimly lit vault in my grandfather's house. There, I crouched anxiously under cobwebs, carefully groping for the wine rack. The scent of his numerous riding boots hit me, which he meticulously treated with leather grease and other tinctures. Leather and sharp. Biting. On the shelves lurked dubious bottles adorned with creepy skulls, exuding medicinal scents. These were not to be confused with the wine bottles. The bare light bulb cast long shadows and distorted my silhouette. And just as distorted and eerie do I find Red. No soft - earthy vetiver - but bare, echoing cellar walls. Quickly grabbed a wine bottle - regardless of the condition and vintage - and off I went. This flight reflex is also triggered in me by Red - straight to the saving faucet.

"Hello! Good morning! Please wake up, please! It's getting loud here now! And please clear the desk, okay?" Only with great difficulty did the words penetrate the layer of leaden fatigue. Yet at the same time, the glaring artificial light had ignited and played its part. Coffee. Coffee. But first, wash up.

Caution, the fragrance has punch. I tested it in winter in Antalya (Winter/Antalya: sic!) as a sample. Two sprays after showering on the chest/neck and off to the center. Unfortunately, it started to rain on the way back to the hotel. Quite heavily, quite unpleasant. Pretty wet. I went from strolling to a brisk walk pretty quickly.

Indeed, I was about to give up, but Montale has surprised me once again with a completely different type of fragrance that does not fit into their typically loud, hairspray-like, penetrating portfolio. Subdued, green, earthy, without the shrill rose nonsense, "Red Vetyver" has become a more serious, cooler, distinctly more masculine scent.

Yesterday, I received a sample of RED VETIVER and compared it with my VETIVER SPECIAL RESERVE from Castle Forbes. My impressions: Castle Forbes ... is for me the so-called "northern" variant. At first, it is citrusy-green, yet soft, but overall it becomes "drier" as it develops. It feels a bit more distant. It represents a more masculine aura. Montale ...

Montale's interpretation of the theme "Vetyvver" prompted me to test it as well. In a perfumery I trust, which has finally added Montale to their selection. Not all of them, but some popular fragrances. "Wonderful, a 'new' Vetyver. Gourmand food for my nose!" !! I immediately grabbed the tester and..... Pffffft!.... there it was.

I have been very interested in the Montale brand for some time, so it was only a matter of time before I purchased Sensual Instinct, which is obviously comparable to Baccarat Rouge 540. Everything in theory says that the fragrance will satisfy the person who likes the scent of Baccarat Rouge 540 to a great extent. Unfortunately, the assumptions do not always turn out to be true. I was surprised when I smelled Sensual Instinct for the first time after buying it blindly. It is definitely not similar to the EDP 540 version. In the foreground we get a huge dose of rose, but in my opinion the smell of amber, cedar and oak moss will bother us the most. And the word bother is not chosen randomly, because the smell is very powerful in projection. it will be a challenge for our noses to withstand such a dose of smell. We will absolutely not feel the well-known baccarat ingredients in this fragrance, such as saffron and fir resin. My review is a comparison with the EDP 540 version as I don't know EXTRAIT 540. Nevertheless, the fragrance itself is interesting when you don't overdo it.

Personal: 7.5/10 – I like it! It's a sweeter, syrupy cousin to BR540. Mass appeal: 8.5/10 - Sweet, heavy, and loud. BR540 woody amber. Very likable. Performance: 8.5/10 – It’s Montale. Loud, strong, and long-lasting. Nearly nuclear. Value: 7/10 – Montale pricing is fair for the performance, especially compared to MFK’s price tag. Great option for people who want a similar DNA. Uniqueness: 6.5/10 – This is basically BR540 with Montale's fruity syrup and density. Not original, but it’s a twist. SCORE: 76/100 Full bottle buy? NO, I enjoy it but prefer this DNA to be lighter and less syrupy. Blind buy? YES, if you know you like BR540-style sweet woody ambers. Recommend? YES, for fans of Baccarat Rouge who want nuclear strength at niche-lite pricing and potentially want a sweeter twist. Date night? YES, sweet, seductive, and compliment-pulling. Office safe? NO, way too loud and syrupy for confined spaces. Pros: Affordable BR540 DNA with Montale’s trademark projection and sweetness. Cons: Synthetic compared to the original. Too syrupy and loud if oversprayed. Sensual Instinct is Montale’s take on the iconic BR540 woody amber and slightly sweet DNA. Which, of course, means MUCH sweeter. It adds some depth and darkness with the oakmoss and coffee base, but it's still mostly woody and ambery. If you like the BR540 DNA, you'll enjoy this at least some. It's similar, but distinctly not a clone, and frankly, one could easily argue that it's a proper standalone fragrance that isn't even that similar to BR540. To my nose, it's at least a pretty solid nod towards it. It's still sweet syrupy rose at the top, but it's toned down enough so that I don't even notice that as the primary note. It's worth smelling, maybe not owning. Montale's signature syrupy take on an iconic woody amber DNA. Lovable and mass appealing, though loud to say the least. Review #104 in my fragrance journey – this fragrance I own as a decant

BR540 has been a complete success since its launch and has been my signature scent ever since. But do you know that feeling? This restless search for "What could top this?" for a better fragrance that still goes in a similar direction? Thus, I stumbled upon Sensual Instinct and had the chance to test the scent in a chic perfumery in Hamburg. After the first spray, I was deeply disappointed; a juicy, syrup-soaked rose hit me right in the face, and I found the opening to be fruity and liqueur-like. THIS is supposed to smell like BR540?! Hmm.... Never! But as you know from Montale, it feels like it takes a very long time for the actual scent to unfold :-) So I took the opportunity to test other niche fragrances and linger in the perfumery. Half an hour later, a very familiar scent wafted towards me, wait, I know YOU?! Sniffing again at my wrist, yes, you can immediately tell which fragrance the perfumer was inspired by ;-) The name says it all: Sensual Instinct is sensual, captivating, although unisex, I perceive it as very feminine. The rose is present throughout the entire scent development, and with the coffee and praline notes, Sensual Instinct leans more towards the gourmand direction. Somehow, the scent reminds me of Baileys, sugary-sweet, liqueur-like; I think I also read somewhere that Sensual Instinct contains a whiskey note, although this is not listed. The juicy oakmoss note in the base is to die for! Yes, the scent has that ambered BR540 DNA, that cannot be denied, yet it is "different". Of course, I immediately took Sensual Instinct with me; it cannot be missing from my collection! The longevity is unbeatable, typical for a Montale due to the high fragrance concentration; even after 10 hours, I can still perceive it very well. To be honest, since I started wearing Sensual Instinct, I have received more compliments and positive feedback from my surroundings than with BR540. If you like BR540, you should definitely test Sensual Instinct. Better longevity, bomb sillage, warmer, denser, deeper, and more gourmand; not quite as medicinal (that's mainly what bothers many about BR540, I like it). I am extremely happy to have found Sensual Instinct. For me, it's the perfect scent for the cooler seasons, although I have already worn it in summer :-)

I must confess, until now I wasn't really a big fan of Montale. I often encountered a lot of loudness in the fragrances that I don't particularly like. There's a bottle design that I'm not fond of. And so far, there have been four tested fragrances that I didn't really like at all. Now the opportunity arose to test Sensual Instinct, and I thought to myself: Come on, give them another chance. After all, the ingredient list contains fragrance notes that I appreciate. What can I say - I am extremely positively surprised and even a little excited. I spray it on, and it starts to resonate. First, briefly diffuse and then quite clearly: Tom Ford's "Noir de Noir". I consider the classic from the Private Blend line to be a beautiful, desirable fragrance that is also part of my collection. Unfortunately, unfortunately, unfortunately, on my skin, it usually comes off just a tad too floral-sweet and thus a bit too feminine for me, which is why the occasions on which I wear it are really rare. However, the Montale, while it does many things similarly to the Tom Ford, appears to be a touch less floral-sweet. There is the rose, which, although present in its beauty, is not too strong in the foreground. Together with the resinous-sweet flowing amber note, the fragrance takes on an incredibly smooth quality, but not overly sweet. Thus, I consider Sensual Instinct to be the more wearable version of Noir de Noir for men. Anyone who likes the latter should definitely give Sensual Instinct a chance. And you lovely representatives of the female world should do so as well. All just because of the price discrepancy between the two fragrances. Otherwise, I find Sensual Instinct to be a nice, successful evening fragrance, or one suitable for primarily evening leisure or festive occasions. Since it naturally lacks lightness, it is not necessarily a candidate for summer, especially during the day. The sillage and longevity are impressive. This also speaks in favor of it as an evening fragrance and less as an office scent. But yes, this is a Montale that gets a big like from me.

What a successful blend. Coffee - but only a little, more like a Viennese mélange with a freshly bloomed tea rose gently spreading its aromas. All in all, a very skin-close, soft but immensely pleasant companion. A friendly partner for many days and nights. But let's delve a little deeper, light roasted notes with a warm, slightly powdery-sensual component.

SI starts with a dark red warm rose, which shortly thereafter becomes somewhat liqueur-like on me. But it gets even more interesting: A medium-dark tobacco follows with a slight rosy-fruity flavoring. I am amazed, yet I like it a lot. In between, there is a slightly soapy note.

First of all, anyone who, like me, is looking for coffee should probably go to Starbucks and Co., because it definitely doesn't come out for me. What I get instead is a BR540 light. Certainly a great alternative for those among us for whom BR540 develops wonderfully and who don't want to spend too much. In my case, unfortunately, it doesn't develop nicely at all...

Sensual Instinct is my first Montale and was a random blind buy, because it came cheap in a package, because of curiosity. One thing upfront: I find this tin can packaging terrible, but I can certainly imagine that there are enthusiasts for it. I had read a lot about the typical Montale DNA beforehand, Beastmode blablabla..and yes, it has that.

After the first spray, I didn't understand at all what it smelled like, but it was very beautiful, bright, magical. I fell in love with it. It is so versatile. It has several different phases throughout. I was very surprised when a few minutes after applying, I could perceive the aroma of strawberry jam... where it came from, how, why - it's not clear.

It starts with a transparent citrus and oily floral scent, followed by sweet and sticky honey and leather notes. Similar to Honey Aoud of the same house but more sensual, darker and hippie. Here oud is a slightly smokey background combined with the spicy side. It's not a typical Rose Oud and the rose scent is expressed like a massage oil or a love gel, instantly reminding me of a moment of love. All of the perfumes I have tried this year, I would say that this is the best night time perfume.

I decided to blind purchase this fragrance (like always) so I didn't really know what to expect. So, my first time wearing this fragrance I really didn't get much of anything. I decided to let this puppy rest a couple of weeks then BOOOM. It only has three notes listed, but I GET PLENTY of notes starting with Oris root, And I'm very surprised that no one picks up the similarity between Amouage Meander and this. A very creamy fragrance with the notes of Oris and vanilla. Very smooth and velvety.

Great strong long lasting fragrance for events like a funeral or a fancy dinner,not everyone will like this but if you like oud and rose you certainly will. The hairspray looking bottle looks much nicer in person. Not great for a signature best for fancy events. Smells fantastic and not the least bit synthetic. This thing is luxurious as hell the only problem is the automizer is possibly the worst automizer I’ve ever used. Again not a signature but great for big events. This stuff projects to atleast 7 feet I noticed that as soon as I wore it in public, that’s with only 4 sprays so you don’t have to worry about over spraying. The scent starts off rich and after about 8 hours it fades into a fairly sweet skin scent until it gradually fades away. This fragrance will give you a lot of attention people will definitely smell this. Some will love it some won’t. Again not mass appealing. But great for big events. In conclusion this is a great fragrance.

While Montale doesn't share its notes on the website, they do list them in their boutiques. For this fragrance, they list the following notes: Top: Bergamot, Cardamom, Coriander, Black Pepper, Sweet Honey Heart: Rose, Oud from Laos, Leaves of Patchouli Base: Cedarwood, Leather, Amber, White Musk Hope someone from Parfumo can change the notes on this page accordingly.

I actually just wanted to look for patchouli fragrances. Among others, Montale's "Patchouli Leaves" was recommended to me. When I wanted to gather information here, I saw on the right the new fragrance from Montale: "Oud Dream," which is also listed with patchouli leaves, oud, AND rose. Oud and rose are always worth a try for me. But with oud and patchouli, it's a bit of a mixed bag; I have "Aoud" by Micallef, which is also called patchouli; it has a slight leather note in the sillage after some time of development for me. While I hardly perceive patchouli. So oud and patchouli could mean a slight leather note for me, which I don't particularly appreciate. However, I found an offer for a small amount of "Oud Dream," after I realized that "Oud Dreams" is not yet available online. This sparked my hunting instinct: I had to buy it immediately! Applied early in the morning, I immediately smelled a moderate woody oud, then a fruity note, rose or raspberry, and at the same time during the first test, a sweet licorice note. But also a clove scent, at least a spice mix in that direction, which disappointed me a bit. Then a fine creamy musk developed underneath, and "Oud Dream" became softer, more pleasant. Oud had meanwhile disappeared from my perception; I smelled at most something woody. However, time and again, I caught a whiff of that clove scent from my wrists. Clove, yet not quite, what could that be? Moreover, I realized that "Oud Dream" is not a typical Montale fragrance. At noon, I wanted to know for sure: I applied the fragrance to my décolletage! And there it no longer smelled of licorice and yet had a hint of sweetness. Overall, "Oud Dream" rose a bit softer, more pleasant to my nose. Although not balsamic-resinous. The longevity is very good; I smelled on my wrists a clove-heavy spicy-woody, slightly cold-fresh scent, menthol-like, and otherwise more musk, hardly any rose. The typical Montale oud I did not smell at all. Still, a nice bitter fragrance, somewhat unusual - for Montale. And then the various fragrances from Lutens came to mind that I have tested, all of which smell of cloves, and I thought amused: Montale goes Lutens? Such as: 'L'Orpheline/Vitriol d'OEillett/Féminité du bois/Iris silver mist' by Lutens. "Oud Dream," however, is not so sharply clove-like. Moreover, the clove scent is not entirely identical to that of Lutens. Since I couldn't find "Oud Dreams" online, I called up Montale's website, and there it said about "Oud Dreams": "A wonderfully exotic, spicy and honeyed fragrance. Gently sweet and slightly musky, Oud Dream is a sensual and bewitching fragrance. The Rose, the Oud and the Patchouli leaves envelop, as in a dream, this new refined creation with a leathery sillage." I do not perceive the leathery sillage. Otherwise, I was right about the spice and the musk. There is also a bit of sweetness. But I still couldn't quite grasp "spicy fragrance." Then, however, I remembered that I recently bought some pure wood, resin, and balsam essential oils to have them as reference notes during testing. They were all strictly woody, resinous sharp, mineral oily, camphor-like, depending on which one, except for Mysore sandalwood oil. (Since then, I have serious doubts about whether I, as a layperson, will ever be able to match that with perfume notes). It has also become even more puzzling to me how such beautiful perfumes can be made from them. But I found in my detailed notes on these oils: Rosewood oil corresponds roughly to the spicy note that I perceive in "Oud Dreams." I did not apply it again to my skin, just a trace on a test strip. Because these oils are highly irritating to the skin, as I found out. Rosewood oil smells sharp-woody and like a mix of clove, menthol, camphor or/and menthol, and after a while slightly like ozone. That could fit what my perception of the quasi-clove oil is. Meanwhile, after over 12 hours, only a faint scent of musk and/or sandalwood could be perceived on my wrists. After I had checked that, I threw the rosewood test strip in the trash and took a shower, protecting everything with odorless cream, checking whether there were still traces of "Oud Dream" to be perceived, and applied "Oud Dreams" again quite generously. Everything is as it was before. I like "Oud Dreams" even though I had imagined it differently. It is not a sweet fragrance and not at all what I have known from Montale so far. I have not owned a fragrance of this character yet; I have always postponed a purchase from Lutens whenever I saw the prices. Therefore, I do not regret my spontaneous little blind purchase at all; on the contrary. Anyone who likes Lutens fragrances and bitter scents with clove should test "Oud Dream." Unisex? Sure!

In my opinion, the name chosen by Montale could not be more misleading. Upon the first spray, I had to check the label of the bottle twice to make sure I hadn’t picked the wrong one. But there was no mistake, especially since it was a manufacturer’s filling. Neither Oud nor, for that matter, Rose were recognizable in the slightest.

I recently ordered some samples from the Souk again and received "Montale Oud Dream" as a bonus. In the end, the bonus turned out to be the best fragrance sample of the order. A great scent for anyone who wants to gently dive into the topic of "OUD." The combination of Oud, Rose, and Patchouli comes across very pleasantly and not too overpowering.

Sometimes it is precisely the small perfumeries that know their customers best. During a visit to my regular perfumery, the nice saleswoman included a fragrance sample with my purchase, saying, "This is just right for you!" Once I got home, I naturally didn't wait long and tested the fragrance immediately.

Some might label the scent as boring, not complex enough, already seen, or not loud enough. But perhaps that is precisely its competitive advantage among all the well-known oud-rose classics: it is a charmer, a friend and buddy, presenting a simple yet excellent fragrance composition and performance from start to finish.

So here you are. You are straightforward, some might even describe you as a bit undercomplex. But that is also a strength of yours - you remain very clear, are not fleeting, and transform slowly and subtly in the drydown - thus, you are not a disappointment, unlike many others.

Hello everyone, today I want to share my thoughts on this fragrance and a bit about Roja. Some of you may have read my blog post https://www.parfumo.de/Benutzer/Sirbennyone/Blog/Eintrag/roja-der-grosse-player-der-vergangenheit-und-der-heutige-weg-in-das-mittelmassige . Before I say something about the scent itself, a general note = the bottles are usually a 10/10 and true eye-catchers, especially here with the gradient = MEGA. Stones and sprayers... can anything really be improved in that regard? Difficult! _______________________ About the scent: It is fresh, fruity citrusy, becomes floral creamy and has a soft, slightly sweet and fluffy drydown... and that’s it? Yes... and for that, according to the homepage, 495€.... Now to the BUT: In my blog post, you can find something very general about it, = My problem with it ... Growing on bushes along the lanai outside my vacation room were hundreds of white tiare flowers. Tiare is a type of gardenia plant that grows in the Pacific islands, native to Polynesia. Every day I would tiptoe out along the stone path and stick my face into these bushes and in those moments I truly knew heaven. Montale Intense Tiare was my selection for the third day I spent in Hawaii. My friend balked at how strong and sweet the smell was after I had just put it on, almost like grape juice. "You're going to get chased by insects all day!" she warned. Luckily that never happened even though we spent a large part of the day in a tropical botanical garden. I'm not sure how much was the perfume and how much was my surrounding environment but all day I was surrounded by the sweet almost honey like scent of tiare, coconut, ylang ylang and jasmine. It was gorgeous, made me think if Thierry Mugler's Alien went on vacation and traded her edgy city slicker garb for a sarong and sunglasses. This was my favorite of the three sample vials I had packed for my trip. Quite lush and elegant. Two thumbs up.

Edited two weeks after review below: I could not stop thinking about this scent and ordered a bottle. Simply something I must have in my collection. It's so cheerful and loveable! I just think it's very important to use this very - and I mean VERY - light handed. Too many sprays may kill the beauty of this perfume. I even can imagine it may be best to mix one spray with an unscented bodylotion or body-oil and to devide that over ones body. I'm gonna try that tomorow. I used two tiny sprays just now, one on each side of my neck and it is nuclear, so one bottle will last for ages! But oh, it's lovely! --- Sampled this on my search for summer fragrances. Before I asked for a sample, I let my boyfriend smell it and I'd never seen him react so positively. Unfortunately we don't share my love for- and interest in perfumes. (he always says he doesn't care for perfumes because he likes the way I smell whithout any perfume which is why he does not really care about what I'll wear and, though I could take that as a compliment, it sometimes is very frustrating when I want an opinion :-)) Anyhow, I had never thought he would like this scent because he always claims not to like sweet perfumes...When I showed him my surprise concerning his likes for this....eh...well...rather sweet scent, he said that he meant by that 'not liking perfumes that are too overwhelming'. I will never understand how he perceives fragrances, lol :-). Then he continued to explain: " Well there is nothing sharp or edgy about this scent, that's why I like it". I guess that what he likes are not perfumes, but maybe certain aroma's Because I love this scent, but I'm not sure I'd call this 'a perfume'. In my opinion this falls into the category of 'aroma's'. It is a scent for reminiscing and, in this case, reminiscing about summer-vacations and such. In that perspective I love this!! It's very 'Tiare' indeed, I don't get too much coconut (thank god) or sunscreen vibes. Nor do I smell anything synthetic like some. It's a scent that is very true to nature in my opinion, true to the Tiare flower. Sillage and longevity are outstanding which means it is best not to overspray. So I will use my sample a bit more this week to find out if I like it enough to buy a full bottle or if I will hunt down a lotion that smells of Tiare (Therme had a bodycream in the past that was called 'Lomi Lomi' (can't find it anywhere anymore) and that smelled quite much like this (and had quite good sillage as well!), maybe I should search for that online. Edit: It's a few hours later and..OMG I really LOVE this! The drydown is so soft and feminine! Still very 'tiare', but acting more like a perfume.

This fragrance took me right back to San Diego, where I lived years ago, at the beach. It starts with a sort of over ripe fruity note, even though it lists Tiare as the top note. I was not very impressed, but decided to give it an all day wearing, as to write a review, it needs time to get the whole fragrance picture. The next stage, after about an hour), was a plasticky, slightly floral vibe. Then the suntan oil presented itself! This was the scent of the beach, where everyone gathered with their boards to catch some waves. I wouldn't have minded that so much, but that slightly over ripe fruit note kept drifting in and out, and was very off putting. In it's defence, the fragrance does have good longevity, and isn't shy to show it's stuff, but I think for the price, it is definitely not worth the price tag! i was expecting a distinct, and prominent tiare flower, but, instead got coconut and a strange plastic fruit smell. I suppose I have been spoiled by my other lovely florals). This is the second Montale I have tried, and will purchase some other samples, as this house has a wide range of choices. Unfortunately, this wave just wasn't worth catching!

Intense Tiaré is just that: An extremely loud, intense, everlasting tiare bomb. In my opinion this is one of the classics and reference scents when it comes to tropical florals. It smells like a beach holiday in a bottle! Heaps and heaps of tiare, lots of ylang-ylang and a touch of freshly blooming jasmine make it smell like a traditional body oil extracted from flowers. If you remember the monoi products by Yves Rocher, this is very similar, but an obvious upgrade in quality. Maybe it's the subtle jasmine and rose that make it more sophisticated. Vanilla and coconut add some warmth to it, so the oily aspect of the scent doesn't become too sharp and overwhelming. As expected, they become stronger and stronger in the drydown. Otherwise, this is a relatively simple and linear scent without surprises. If you want tiare, that's what you get, if you want something more complex with a little extra, look elsewhere. I think this is a well-made and beautiful scent, but I also strongly feel that it wouldn't suit me. Almost like I'm too pale to smell that sun-kissed, even though I really don't believe in assigning fragrance by hair, skin or eye color. Guess I just like lighter forms of beachy scents for myself. Try it for yourself and see if you can handle it!

As the title says. It caused some sort of allergic reaction or sensory overload. First spray right off the bat, I didn’t care for the smell of it. It was instantly off putting, and smelled heavy to the floral. I guess it somewhat smelled like tiare, but mostly it reminded me of vintage “old lady” floral fragrances. It was strong, heavy, and overwhelming. Within a half hour, I had a horrible headache, ended up feeling nauseous and flushed, and lightheaded. I washed my skin and changed my clothes. Unfortunately, I couldn’t get it all off after washing my skin so the fragrance and reaction lasted for several hours. I’m not sure what ingredient or chemical is in it that may have caused a physical reaction. I know for me. Synthetic chemicals sometimes cause the reaction. Just be mindful if you have fragrance sensitivity.

Syrupy tiare vanilla! A sweet summery white floral. On similar perfumes: There is no similarity to TF Soleil Blanc at all, there is some similarity to Guerlain Terracotta (terracotta is less sweet and less vanilla-coconut), but this is like a cousin of Mancera Coco Vanille.

I have tríed many perfumes whit the tiare flower note. But none like this one. A beautiful perfume with a very tropical aroma, transports you to the parado se islands of the Caribbean. A floral where the protagonist is the tiare flower And coconut milk create an elegant And Long lasting aroma. Leaving behind the simple aroma of sunscreen.

Monoi Tiki Tahiti - I love applying coconut oil with Tiare flowers on my skin after a long sunbath and find the subtle blood scent of this product very pleasant. Tiare flowers, as well as Frangipani and Ylang Ylang, are among the blooms that always attract and fascinate me on long journeys, where nature shows its olfactorily most beautiful side in the tropics.

Interesting, despite the completely different fragrance pyramid, I detect distinct hints of one of my favorite perfumes: "Datura Noir" by Serge Lutens. The same sensual and not at all powdery creaminess that immediately makes me think of an (expensive) sunscreen and the same tropical floral notes.

During a marathon perfume testing session, Montale's Intense Tiaré was also part of the long line of bottles I tried. I believe my nose was completely numb, but this scent immediately captivated me and had to be at least sampled. Wonderful, noble, well-groomed white flowers with the summery creaminess of Tiaré and coconut. Simply delicious.

For loukhoum lovers only, Montale SWEET ORIENTAL DREAM is just that. To my nose, this composition is slightly less sweet than my memory of the first perfume in the Keiko Mecheri trio. However, my reception of the KM loukhoum perfumes may very well have been affected by my non-expectations of super-sweetness, given that I had no idea at the time what loukhoum even was! My suspicion is that some reviewers of SWEET ORIENTAL DREAM (at other sites), too, lacked previous loukhoum experience. What is even more strange, given the name, is that people are complaining that this perfume is sweet. This is a rare case of total truth in advertising! I could definitely understand such complaints, were this perfume simply named ORIENTAL DREAM and marketed as unisex. Then any guy who purchased this scent unsniffed would have a valid claim in requesting a full refund. In this case, however, the sweetness is unabashedly and unapologetically revealed up front and center. If you do not like sweet perfumes, why in the world would you be purchasing something called SWEET ORIENTAL DREAM? Perhaps reviewers simply like to bitch in general. That would explain why they get all bent out of shape whether the name falsely or accurately claims to be this or that thing. But I digress... SWEET ORIENTAL DREAM is a confectionary perfume with more almond nougat than anything else. The roses are akin to the ones made out of frosting and poised atop store-baked birthday and wedding cakes. But anyone who is actually looking for a loukhoum perfume should give this one a try, provided that they have a triple expresso and a pitcher of ice water close by! The longevity of this perfume is typical for loukhoum-centric compositions, at least those I've tried: quasi-infinite. Loukhoum sticks around until you submerge your perfumed naked body in a bath! That's a good thing if you like it, but a precaution to those who are testing for the very first time. A fine loukhoum perfume, in my estimation, but it is what it is, and it's not what it's not. If you have not yet walked down loukhoum lane, this would be an excellent place to start (and, for many, to finish).

I have to say that the first time I tried SOD i didn't like it that much, but with a few wearings I fell in love with it powdery sweetness that never gets cloying (though the first impressions make you think It could become a cloying mes, but it doesn't). I got 20ml free from an order to Montale, later 50ml...later 100ml. I love the perfect mix of rose, almonds (most almondy fragrances feel too "plasticky" to my nose, but this don't), spices and vainilla. It last for ages with a very good sillage. I love to get constant whiffs of my fragrance and I enjoy the aura this fragrance gives me. Definitely unisex. Most of my friends love it and ask me for a little so they can wear it every now and then.

This is wonderfully delicious! I adore the scent of Loukhoum and this is as delectable as that Turkish delight gets. A mouthwatering combination of almond, vanilla, honey and sugar with lovely hints of rose in the background. I was taken with this fragrance from first sniff ... sweet, luscious and nutty. If you like Keiko Mecheri Loukhoum (like I do), they're very similar but Montale Sweet Oriental Dream is even creamier on the skin.
if you like loukhoum by keiko mecheri or the lutens loukhoum creation you will probably like this ,in my opinion the best gourmand ever created

I personally CANNOT wear this oriental dessert: loads of honey, nougat, sugar, vanilla, rose-jam equal a "loukhum perfume" without the oriental delight, without any delight whatsoever. Hints of the "in-house built in" standard aoud-accord render the scent even worse and add up to one sickly sweet, cloying mess. Beware: This one is head-ache inducing and there's nearly no way of escaping it once it is on your skin, the ultra-potent mix lasts for ages. One of the worst Montales I ever tried.

This is what I've been looking for in an incense fragrance, although looking at the notes you'd never think incense. The opening is Nag Champa which I love. The bitter almond middle does have a slight medicinal quality and is indeed a little bitter which could be unappealing, however on me I feel it is balanced and manageable.
"The Orient is a place of the soul as well as geography." Close your eyes and smell Sweet Oriental Dream. A wonderful fragrance with three main notes as protagonists: rose, almond and honey.

Very Very Clean and powdery smelling to me. It smells like when you are doing laundry and have a beautiful smelling detergent and laundry sheets all wafting through the air. It is really pretty. Perfect for bed and daytime in the winter. I haven't tested it fully yet, but will update as soon as I do.

I just wore Sweet Oriental Dream when the Eurhythmics started playing their hit "Sweet dreams" on the radio. And the fragrance also has hit qualities. It reminds me, like the music, of my youth in the 80s, when people dared to be a bit bolder. Sweet Oriental has a bold attitude and makes a statement.

Namely one like the ones you always find at medieval markets. Lokoum, I read about it in almost all comments. I didn't know that stuff was so well-known. Probably from a vacation in the Orient :) SOD actually smells like an oriental sweet. There is nothing artificial about it. It truly scents as if you were standing in front of a bazaar.

When it comes to product with limited availability or a very high price point, there is no other brand for whom the moniker "can do no wrong" is better suited than Roja Parfums (or in 2025, Roja London). Time after time, I find myself wondering if I'm the lone idiot or if the hardcore fans are duping themselves into thinking that Roja Dove has yet again turned water to wine. It happened last year with both Lost in Paris and Tea at BG , now it happened again with Neiman Marcus . And the story is quite underwhelming from start to finish. I'm reflecting on my experiences from testing the scent in-doors twice, once in the morning and once in the evening. I'm sure some will find the very first thing that I wrote in my notes amusing: "Ouch. That quality f*king blows." In both wears, Neiman Marcus opens fruity-spicy-sweet-creamy. This opening opposes a creamy raspberry part (think fruitchouli or the style in which raspberry is done in Kilian's Angels' Share Paradis ) with a rubbery saffron part, a clear indication of the underwhelming blending. I've smelled saffron like that in many places before, e.g. Moresque's Scirocco , but the rubbery smell also has some reminiscence of the dry-down on Initio's Blessed Baraka . In the on-skin dry-down, you mostly smell the rubbery saffron opposed by suede/leather and in some parts, I can also sense the orris/pastry buttery accord that Roja used in Lost in Paris last year with the orris likely accentuating the spiciness alongside the saffron. To my nose, the floral tones never pop. The final dry-down beyond 3 hours is the buttery pastry accord from Lost in Paris with no suede/fruity aspects aside it. And the package that I just described has me puzzled. The actual scent and the listed notes imply that the goal was to deliver a creamy raspberry fragrance built on a leathery base. However, that idea completely falls apart in the execution where the leathery-spicy parts outshine the raspberry in the dry-down. I'd say the performance is just average and of course the value is subpar as well. The delivery of the saffron is incredibly lackluster for a fragrance retailing at €515/50ml, basically putting it in competition with S-tier market leaders like Nefs and Jump Up and Kiss Me Hedonistic . But make no mistake, even if the pieces were to fit together better, that wouldn't give Neiman Marcus a high enough ceiling to be competing with scents like Nefs & Hedonistic, because there's not enough depth to this profile - it's just a tame leather with sweet spices & creamy raspberry.

It’s like sitting out on the terrace on a cold morning with a still-warm blueberry pastry you just picked up from the bakery. You take the first bite, and suddenly the whole day feels like it’s off to a good start. The air is chilly, but the sweet warmth of the pastry balances everything out perfectly. It opens with a blast of berries and sugar. Super Juicy, super sweet and honestly the first thing that hits me is this mix of blackberry and blackcurrant. They're definitely in that candied, jammy territory. The opening kind of reminds me of a warm berry puff pastry, like something you’d get fresh from a bakery where the fruit filling is glossy and sweet. After a couple of minutes, the fragrance starts to shift. The berries calm down and the suede steps forward, which is honestly the best part of the whole composition. It's buttery, soft and a little smoky, gives the perfume this more grown-up, classy vibe. There's also a touch of saffron that adds additional warmth, so the scent doesn't stay as a simple gourmand. It's still sweet, still gourmand for sure, but the suede stops it from feeling childish or too dessert-like. Perfomance is pretty solid in my opinion. On my skin it lasts around 8 hours, and the projection in the first few hours are surprisingly strong. If you like berry gourmands, this is a solid option.

Let me start by saying if you own a lot of Montale fragrances, then this might just be an average fragrance. If you are starting a collection or just getting into fragrances, then chances are that this will be a love at first sight ... The combination of a tart but sweet green apple mixed with a nice red rose with a little touch of amber. This is a nice fragrance but for me, I own a lot of Montale fragrances and it's something that it is very similar to, but I just can't put my hands on it.

Personal: 6/10 – It's nice, but it's not something I could wear at all. Mass appeal: 7.5/10 – Sweet fruity florals with musk are safe and likable. Performance: 8/10 - Very solid, but not where most Montale frags are. Value: 6/10 - Fair pricing, but still niche-lite prices for something kinda synthetic. Uniqueness: 5.5/10 – Fruity-floral musk bombs aren’t unique, and this doesn’t break new ground. SCORE: 66/100 Full bottle buy? NO, I’d rather wear other fruity citrus musks. Blind buy? YES, if you want a safe, powerful citrus floral musk. Recommend? YES, it’s a solid compliment-puller if you like citrusy musk bombs. Date night? YES, it’s playful, fruity, and strong enough to be noticed. Office safe? NO, too loud, a common theme with Montale fragrances. Pros: Loud, long-lasting, fruity-musky citrus fragrance with great performance. Cons: Synthetic, generic, syrupy. Not niche-quality blending. Starry Nights is Montale’s take on a fruity-floral-musk that’s more polished than their usual rose-syrup bombs, but still is distinctly Montale-like with its sweetness and synthetic nature. It's not bad at all, but it's not something I find particularly wearable. To me, it smells kind of chemical-ey and cleaner-ish. It's for someone, but not me. I want to like it, as citrusy musks are something I usually love (Creed SMW) but this execution just isn't it. A fruity floral musk on Montale steroids. Nothing unique, but very recognizable. Review #105 in my fragrance journey – this fragrance I own as a decant

No, it's not scary at all, quite the opposite! Finally, another one from the Essentials line, so without Oud:-)! Fruity-fresh, zesty and bright opening, fresh-sour including the typical Montale sharpness. Quite unusual for Montale, it doesn't feel forced, despite its synthetic nature! Quickly it becomes floral and herb-spicy, taking on a masculine touch, despite the jasmine! I don't find parallels to men's deodorants from Axe or shower gels completely absurd, but still on a different level. The scent mix can be pleasing without being thrilling! Far from bad or underground... I don't even consider it average, but the spark just doesn't quite ignite.. and it doesn't have to. It has very good longevity of about 7 hours with the typical Montale sillage. It makes no mistakes and remains relatively unchanged until the end. It belongs to the better, albeit more inconspicuous ones from Montale. My favorite from the Essentials remains Red Vetiver.

Okay, it’s not a typical summer fragrance; actually, it’s more of a summer scent for those who dare to go for something a bit more striking... at least in summer!! This Montale starts unusually fresh and isn’t as heavy as one might expect from Montale.... AT FIRST!!! At the beginning, I smell a fresh shower gel note, but one that can’t be purchased at dm or Müller, rather in a more exclusive store! A shower gel that George Clooney might use... xD After a while, however, the scent becomes softer and the typical Montale DNA reveals itself.... it almost becomes a bit powdery!! Who would have thought! But it is! Since it is fresh yet soft and powdery, I find it wearable for summer ;) but it would also fit well in other seasons, as it doesn’t come off as ONLY fresh! The name is somehow fitting.... because I associate a starry night with something fresh, but also with a hint of romance and mystery! Just like this Montale :) Definitely a candidate for purchase for me :) Regards Angelina

It was on a warm spring day in Seoul when Starry Nights and I first met. A young woman walking several meters ahead of me was wearing this fragrance. Every time a gust of wind tousled her hair, I was completely blown away. It smelled sweet, fresh, and luxurious... and had something magical about it. A unisex scent that turned my head. It was love at first sniff, and I convinced myself that our meeting was fate. I couldn't help but approach the woman. Back in Germany, I bought the perfume without smelling it again first. That was probably my mistake. I was too naive, wearing rose-colored glasses. The scent suddenly unfolded completely differently on my skin than I remembered. It smelled much more masculine all of a sudden, and also very sour. The fragrance felt heavy and immediately became unpleasant in my nose. I couldn't explain it. How had I been so mistaken about it? After a few hours, it became a bit softer, sweeter, and more feminine - completely different from right after spraying it. All in all, it's not a bad scent, but it should be approached with caution. I don't wear this Montale like ordinary perfumes, because this is not a fragrance you want to constantly have in your nose. It's too strong, too heavy - almost numbing to the senses. However, if you apply it to the nape of your neck or put a small spritz in your hair - then Starry Nights unfolds into something beautiful and undoubtedly unique.

When I read the notes, I was very taken with them. It sounded really interesting. Right after the first spray, I smelled this totally pleasant freshness - wow! But the top notes slowly faded away and something about this scent felt incredibly familiar. What was it again? This sense of security I feel when inhaling and this familiarity...yes, could it be? Indeed.

Starry Nights is one of the most underrated fragrances out there for me. Montale sometimes doesn't get the best reviews, and yes, the bottles are really bad. The scents used to often not be very good either, often coming across as very synthetic and somewhat scratchy.

Starry Nights is one of my favorite fragrances. I find that the scent gives off a special aura. No matter when you wear it, people look at you differently. Starry Nights smells fresh, elegant, and oriental-floral. Just like a little nighttime adventure that stays in your memory for a long time.

The final and devastating verdict right at the beginning: Starry Nights is a pretty average fragrance in almost every respect. Citrusy-fresh with a slight musk note to make things a bit softer and rounder.

I stumbled upon this fragrance by chance, and if I had gone by classic visual stimuli, the bottle would have rather put me off (but it didn't in the end). If you are not familiar with Montale bottles, you might be startled at first and think that it is empty, but due to the material, the bottles are feather-light and the 100ml content doesn't really weigh anything.

This is an elegant tuberose scent that remarkably resembles my 1960s bottle of Fracas Extrait I treasure. Its signature is more modern, but still smooth and rich seductive tuberose. Its gorgeous, haunting and elegant.

From constant sniffing I've learned I'm in love with white florals, especially scents that feature Jasmine and Tuberose with Orange Blossom or Neroli and Musk or Civet. This combo appears in many a startling beauty including Boucheron, Jardins de Bagatelle, Clive Christian's X Myrrh, Bogue's Maai, Chanel No. 22, Panthère de Cartier and others. In this fragrance, the addition of Peach and Plum freshens, Cinnamon and Vanilla add warmth, and Cistus luxury. The result is narcotic, something few Tuberose lovers could resist. If I didn't already own so many in this style, I'd snap Roja Dove's Tuberose right up. For now I'll make do with the large decant gifted me at the Roja Dove counter when I spent so much time there two days ago, emptying my wallet. Not sure what I'll do when the decant is empty, too.

There is something in Montale that fascinates me. It’s amazing how they ruthlessly bottle the worst “cheap-designer-in-disguise” scents in a niche dress, and manage to actually sell them. Some are actually decent, but most of them are just tacky cheap stuff. Still, they’re there, and they’re niche. However... Wood and Spices, friends, is their masterpiece – their “IgNobel” winning scent so far for me. Basically it smells exactly (I mean it: exactly) like those modern “aromatic fougères” cheapos, the woody-ozonic-spicy-fresh colognes like Ferrari scents, or Police. Completely, nauseatingly synthetic, flashy and tacky, despicably stuffed with metallic stuff and artificial “roundness”. Trust me, I am not being too grave or severe: it’s utter supermarket rubbish. Many niche fans want to smell expensive: Wood and Spices smells terribly *inexpensive*, instead. In perspective, I should raise my ratings of all other Montale’s, as this one is really the worst of them all. One of the worst scents I’ve ever tested. 2/10

I have 2 Montale selections and they both serve one very specific purpose - nostalgia for the 1990s and that is it. When I was on the cusp of turning 40, I bought several 1990s to early 2000s era frags for the magic of olfactive scent memory and feel nostalgia for younger, more care free, and quite plainly for my life experience, more fun times. Did they do the trick? I suppose, albeit in a lesser fashion than I’d imagined they would. My nose felt they were less than they had been - be it the quality of oils used, IFRA changes that occured and necessitated altered formulations, or simply watered down offerings due to the frags being selections that had gone through multiple reformulations in the years since they’ve fallen out of fashion en masse. Tommy, Hugo, The Dreamer, Dunhill Desire Blue were all standbys in my teen years rotation. Sculpture was one I didn’t personally own, but I knew several that had it and would “borrow” some sprays from time to time. Enter Montale’s Fougeres Marines and Wood & Spices. Off the top Fougeres just hits my nose like a 90s one two pinch of Tommy and Hugo. At opening much more Tommy and into dry down sort of an equal mix of the two. I’d heard / seen several compare Wood & Spices to Sculpture, The Dreamer, and Desire Blue and to my nose I get equal parts of all of those. I don’t wear either of them often and while I’ve got several fbs from the sister company, Mancera, and enjoy those quite a bit, I have not, and don’t plan on delving deeper into Montale. They hit their sweet spot for me and there they shall remain within my fragrance wardrobe, no more, no less. If you, too, are looking for that 90s nostalgia but from a brand that offers options that project and last as long as I would imagine one could desire, and don’t want thinner or watered down versions, while being willing to pay a tad more in line with what those 90s frags went for back in those days, this may hit that sweet spot. I enjoy the heck out of some of my more refined niche frags, but I can also appreciate these for what they are. I say that because I know Pierre Montale’s works can spark “controversy” within the fragrance community. To some they’re just a synthetic mess, to some they’re an affordable gateway to niche, to some they’re absolutely outstanding. I appreciate them for what they are. Some of my Manceras I can’t imagine parting with. Are they going to hit my nose like Roja, Royal Crown, Stéphane Humbert Lucas, Francesca Bianchi, among others - no, certainly not. However, they do, at times and situationally hit my nose as simply perfecto for what my nose craves. These 2 fit the perfecto bill when I want that 90s feel and for that reason, I couldn’t imagine wanting to ever sell or trade them away. Sillage, Projection, and Longevity, like all Montale and Mancera I’ve experienced is about as potent as I could want. Refinement and quality of ingredients is lower spectrum of niche - they’re synthetic and not “natural ingredient” smelling, but they’re as good as it gets for doing what they do and what my expectations could be for their doing so.

This fragrance opens with a spice and wood blend that is cleverly done to smell sweet and fruity. I associate this accord with the smell of hot, honeyed fruit infusion. The fragrance is velvety smooth, warm, fruity and slightly spicy. It is a perfect comfort scent for cold winter days; it is also very powerful and has great sillage. It is a nice fragrance no doubt, but I find it rather uninspired.

Montale WOOD & SPICES definitely tests my wish to believe that all fragrances are potentially unisex. The opening, in particular, verily screams out "Cologne Guy!" Maybe this is the Montale for Cologne Guy? I mused over this possibility for several minutes while waiting for the huge cloud of fumes to dissipate. It took a while, but eventually the ebony drydown arrives, and it is quite nice. Here I find that WOOD & SPICES is truly unisex. But getting there is another story. I have no idea what accounts for the Cologne Guy opening, but I'm not sure that it's worth waiting out, since I know of a couple of good ebony perfumes which do not require any sort of endurance training: Tokyomilk DEAD SEXY and Love & Toast POMME POIVRE. Both were created by Margot Elena. I do very much appreciate the drydown of WOOD & SPICES, but I would not acquire a bottle because the Cologne Guy opening is simply too annoying, not only for others, but also for me. This is not a case of enjoying a guilty pleasure in the privacy of one's own home and them journeying out once the drydown has arrived. No, the opening is not a guilty pleasure. Just guilty of smelling like Cologne Guy.

First of all, I ask for your understanding. This will not be an ordinary comment, as I don’t feel sufficiently inspired for that, even though I like the scent. It’s just an extended statement because I need a few more characters. So please don’t think that the Spee is falling short in literary quality. This is the first "Montale" fragrance I’ve tested; I was curious and reached into the range. "Wood&Spices" sounds like it could be appealing, so I tried it (by the way, I find the bottles rather silly, but that’s beside the point), and - good! What you read is what you get! Nicely woody-spicy, the woodiness is not too dry and extremely pleasant, fine stuff! Classic, masculine, agreeable, prim! The oud is not too stinky, and the incense is not too extreme. Later on, it turns into a slightly sweeter, but still pleasantly spicy direction - by no means sticky. Anyone who thinks the keywords "woody-spicy, slightly gourmand" might fit their taste should definitely give it a try. The main reason I’m even writing a comment is that so far, all reviewers have highlighted a similarity to "Nikos Sculpture." That knocks me off my chair! I remember Ni.Sc. as a dreadful, horrendously bad piece of work (and I very, very rarely say such things about fragrances!), and also as going in a completely different scent direction. Now I was quite surprised because apparently, I stand very alone in my assessment that these are two completely different fragrance directions. I critically asked myself whether it might have to do with the fact that I tested Nikos in an airport perfumery (or something similar) and this one here in a rather elegant, stylish, yet highly pleasant fragrance shop, where I was surrounded by a beautiful and highly competent consultant (and both were extremely friendly and accommodating)... So looking at the ingredient list: practically not a single ingredient matches! So I stand by my opinion, sorry, all you previous reviewers, nothing like Nikos!

At first, one can perceive a very intense fresh sparkling lemony - fruity note that brings along very soft, subtly powdery nuances, and I initially guessed mandarin and mint; orange blossom and pepper also came to mind.

Sometimes you wonder why a distinctive perfume needs a more expensive twin? Wood & Spices is clearly based on Sculpture Homme by Nikos. A half-side comparison is in order. The top notes of both perfumes are identical on my skin. No difference to be detected! Both are spicy sweet, with a slight cologne note in the dry down.

So, I might not be testing many Montale fragrances here unless I have some samples of them, where I then think: "Ah, another Montale!" Well, actually it's because I hardly see any Montale bottles in the fragrance shops around here, and thus the brand has somewhat faded for me.

My expectations for Wood & Spices were high, as I really like Nikos Sculpture, but not its modest attributes. Blinbuy?! Oh no, better not, they usually fail for me about 75% of the time... So I got a decant, 10ml of the Wood & Spices juice here, which is enough for testing and forming an opinion.

I would like to share my impression of Wood & Spices with you. To get straight to the point: I love this scent, which in my opinion is an absolute all-rounder. I can imagine wearing it anywhere for any occasion. Perhaps not exactly in the height of summer, but that still needs to be tested.

This is a nice one from the semi-bespoke collection. Its powdery in the dry down, It smells fresh in the beginning and then the floral notes take over. This was not mind blowing but i think its a nice summer scent. I went down to Roja to try them all, although i didn't try this one on skin, its 3 days now and still strong on the perfume strip. Speaks volumes about the quality ingredients used, Next time will have to try on skin. Good thing about visiting Roja's Haute Parfumerie, is even if you don't end up purchasing anything, you still come home doused in his perfumes.

I'm not sure what Montale was trying to achieve with this one. As much as I am generally a fan of "fruitchoulis" and of raspberry in perfumes, this doesn't quite work for me. It starts off as an orange-chouli, similar to Nicole Miller Frenzy, but less complex. This passes after a few minutes, and it becomes predominantly about the "red fruits." This reminds me of the raspberry version of Junket Danish Dessert, a powdered pudding mix available in the US (it's based on tapioca starch rather than gelatin). After an hour or two, it develops a fizzy/tangy quality (I would guess from the geranium). I love Italian orange and grapefruit sodas, which are closer to tasting like the real fruit than ones like Fanta or Orange Crush, but don't closely resemble fruit juice. I haven't tasted a raspberry one, but I feel confident that it would smell like this phase of Dark Purple. I love certain coffee fragrances about which others say, "I don't want to smell like I spilled coffee on myself." I can't discern a reason why I LIKE to smell like I spilled coffee on myself, for instance. But, with equal illogic, I must say that I don't enjoy spilling Italian raspberry soda on myself. So Dark Purple is not for me.

I was trying to see if I can find gourmand scent with plums notes in it. Montale outperformed himself in this fragrance. Fruits are very alluring within few minutes, it is almost like someone opened jam with plums, but patchouli kicks in so hard, leaving you with Montale’s signature DNA mixed with tiny rose notes. Longevity lasts for 4 hours. Silage is okay, not over powering. I would love to hear more plums here, but it is what creator wanted, similarities are easily detected here as in other Montale’s fragrances. Personally I will try to dig deeper in funding my own Montale’s bestseller. This one is okay-ish.

Dark Purple used to be my go-to fragrance for winter nights, but over the past couple of years either my bottle or my body or both changed, and this doesn't quite click anymore. The rose now far overpowers all other notes (I loved the plum ;_;), and something about it feels far more mature than I am. Maybe I'll try it again when I'm grayer. Incredible longevity, though, and still luxurious; I've taken to spraying just a touch on a scarf or something instead of my skin. Even when I wore this regularly, I'd apply one spray and have to partially wash it off; it's that strong.

A sample of "Dark Purple" was included with an online order, and I spritzed it on with enthusiasm: This stuff is potent; more than two sprays from the small tester does not sit well within my interpersonal action radius. This was my first Montale, and I must admit that it surprised me quite a bit: The first impression is decidedly heavy on the medicinal side; I immediately think of the characteristic smell of adhesive bandages and only later realize that it is the rose here that possesses an almost sharp spiciness (Plum? Orange? Nah, they don't stand a chance against this intense disinfectant aura. I can easily imagine that Doctor Schnabel from Rome used something like this against the "pestilential vapors" in the Middle Ages). The top note strikes me as artificial at first, which may also stem from the very strong concentration. Right from the start, one becomes aware that with such a fragrance, you are making an olfactory statement. If one (or rather, a woman) does not want to stand out in a particular crowd, one should not reach for this purple elixir. Yes, this top note is clearly too cheap for me; I think of a 2-Euro fruit peppermint bath from the supermarket, which also justifies the title of this tasting, as I inevitably feel reminded of Fisherman's Friend Cool Cherry pastilles, which I do enjoy but certainly do not need to have around all day. The heart and base are then considerably quieter than the initial 'headshot'; geraniums and sugary sweets from the kiosk cling like the plague and often capture my attention until I wonder: My God, will this stuff ever come off? Scrubbing and soap do nothing; Dark Purple must be 'biologically' broken down, meaning it has to evaporate from my skin on its own. I hoped until the end that the lifebuoys mentioned in the pyramid, teakwood and patchouli, might at least provide a conciliatory conclusion, but unfortunately no... those elements have drowned. And unfortunately, I now have to banish this member of the gummy bear gang to exile on the Virgin Islands for good.

I chose this title because the name and the fragrance notes promise more than the scent ultimately delivers. What did I expect? Dark Purple, yes, that naturally suggested something dark and deep. Especially the anticipation of the plum, which I not only eat in all variations but also particularly enjoy smelling.

After participating in a well-organized sharing here in the Souk, I was able to call a 10 ml decant of Dark Purple my own. Before this, I only knew Pure Gold from Montale. I thought it was quite good, but not spectacular. Dark Purple, great…..I like plum scents. I don’t own a perfume in this direction, but I do have scented candles...Yankee Candle, Village Candle...

Interesting to know: The fragrances from Montale and Mancera are said to have a fragrance oil content of about 30% and would thus be classified as Extrait de Parfums :). The scent opens strongly synthetic, as one knows from Montale; personally, I like this unique signature of Montale.

One of the few oud-free fragrances from Montale. Those who believe that Czech & Speake's "Dark Rose" is artificial and hardly wearable should try "Dark Purple," the "fruit cocktail on a pleasantly warm base"...

Montale. Hmm, I don't know it. No, rather... I DIDN'T know it. At least not until the moment when I got to know and prefer various scents here in a short time. I received Dark Purple as a little goodie with an order about a year ago. When testing, I thought, yeah, not bad, but I didn't perceive it particularly well on myself and quickly forgot about this scent.

I was born in 1964 as well, at the crossroads of modern perfume history when Y was introduced. Y was the cornerstone of an empire that would eventually dominate my world. I had an older cousin who lived in Detroit before it collapsed-say 1973. She played David Bowie and Elton John records and wore Y. She was my idol! Enough said. It was forever branded for cool people only. It was massive and unforgettable. Detroit, my cousin and Y have sadly since disappeared. I found a perfectly preserved vintage spray last year and have rediscovered its majestic power. This epic masterpiece is perhaps the definitive chypre behind Mitsouko and Coty's original. I have described it like Mitsouko on steroids. Why? Perhaps more redolent florals in the composition? It seems so tighly compressed as if it sat in the vat for centuries! Micheal Hy was a genius in his brief career. Calandre and Rive Guache were to follow. I suspect he worked on YSL Pour Hommme. The opening is indeed incredible.
