The fruit has an aged fermented quality to it. This particular bottle takes a good six hours or more to work through the florals. Indeed, the brilliance of the chypre is defined here. Time is required for the novice. It can last 24 hours or more depending on the wearer. Expeiencing it in its original form is the only way. Around 2002, I tried a mini and was heartbroken. Although Y was never as commecially successful as Opium, it had a cult following. Did YSL think no one would notice? The oakmoss and vetiver was gone! It has finally been raised forever at the brutal hands of L'Oreal Paris. Maybe one day it will return? I cannot loose hope.

It’s no wonder that people love this scent. It is beautiful from so many angles, and so deftly balanced. And, wonderfully, this balance doesn’t seem the result of consensus. This is not the middle of the road in a bottle. It contains the best of green florals and grassiness, a smart fruit choice, a confident dose of moss and just enough darkness in the basenotes to make it meld with your skin. It is a quality of many chypres to sink into the skin over time. This one becomes a skin scent, but one with sillage, almost instantly. There is something so poised and charming about Y. It has confidence yet never seems to have to prove itself. There’s just that hint of a knowing smile. God, I wish I were Y. Interestingly, while other green scents suggest flowers, grasses, things you might find out-of-doors, Y is in fact outdoorsy. It has all the city sophistication of similar fragrances (Cristalle, Silences, No. 19) but seems perfectly at home in the woods. Y was released in 1964, the year I was born and a year I’ve never quite made sense of. I remember what the later 60s were like on the east coast of the US where I lived at the time. Yet photos from 1964 look like the mid-50s to me. Y captures a bit of this for me. A few years earlier and Y might have been Jolie Madame, a few years later, Diorella. Y is a bit like the gen-X of green fruity chypres.

Y may just be one of YSL's most underappreciated fragrances yet. Being overshadowed by all the glitz and glamour that YSL seems to represent today, this bottle is often lost among the sparkly Parisienne or the candy pink Baby Doll. This fragrance is a classic, especially in the way that it doesn't have to be loud or ground-breaking to be so loved. When I first smelt Y the word 'clean' came to mind. I wanted to say soapy and fresh, however Y isn't either of those things. It's clean in a very natural and simplistic sense of the word, like something that becomes you, rather than announcing to the world that it's a perfume. It isn't heavy and it isn't offensive. Y is classy and sophisticated but also versatile enough to be casual and alluring. It's green and woodsy with a somewhat powdery quality. It doesn't feel dated and I would not have guessed that this fragrance originated from the 1960's. Although not particularly outstanding, the scent itself is quite addictive. It was something that I had to smell over and over again just to embrace its beauty. I must add that this fragrance isn't as dry as some chypres, it has a delicate moistness, possibly caused by the rich green notes and the earthy, wet patchouli note. The fragrance also tends to smell a little musty. The aura of Y is incredible. It conjures up thoughts of cleanliness, fresh bouquets of flowers and soft, burning incense. Perhaps slightly 'churchey' and refined in its manner. I could talk about this fragrance all day, as there are many levels to be experienced here. Y is one of those fragrances that leave a profoundly good impression despite its subtlety.

Forget Guerlain's "Little Black Dress." YSL made the perfect LBD in Y. This is the epitome of chic and style. The wear anywhere, anytime, with anything fragrance. An effortless wonder that is green, but not too green. Clean, but not too clean. Mossy, but not too mossy......I could go on, it is never too anything, it is just perfect. In fact if I could only have one fragrance, it would probably be this. Wonderful.

Compared to YVRESSE, YSL Y seems very dry and austere. I'd call it a dried grass chypre rather than a fruity one. There is certainly a connection between the two compositions, but YVRESSE seems fuller, in addition to being fruitier, while Y seems clean and direct. Actually, I think that the naming of YVRESSE makes a lot of sense, in relation to Y: it contains more detectable, thicker notes, so the name has become thicker (longer) as well. I should say that I never really found YVRESSE very fruity (and it seems to me very un-champagnelike...), until I compared it side by side with Y! Y reminds me a bit of a couple of the Balmain perfumes, inhabiting with them the same general neighborhood as CORIANDRE. On my skin, Y is less green than brown, and the aldehydes do evoke vague and distant memories of ARPEGE, as another reviewer (at a different site) has pointed out, but ARPEGE develops and undulates, while Y seems more linear and univocal--notwithstanding the lengthy list of notes, which are obviously very finely blended! Y is nowhere near as green and wacky as MA GRIFFE. Y is a conservative, classic creation, for women who appreciate aldehydic perfumes which are neither sweet nor very floral. If green is your thing, then you'd love this one--although I cannot comment on the reformulation, since my bottle appears to be vintage.

Sometimes I feel lucky. In one week I was able to get my hands on two vintage edt - one splash and one spray - and one vintage perfumed deodorant of this wonderful fragrance. All three are in incredible good shape and smell like heaven to me. Having read the other reviews there is very little I can say that has not been said already about how it smells and how gorgeous it is.

What I am so tired of reading is that the perfume gives the impression of an "old lady fragrance," when the commentators actually mean "chic," "elegant," or "top-notch" (and should write that). Let's be honest, which post-war grandma really smelled like Arpège, Igrec (Y), or Chanel No 5?

I would also like to share my impressions of Yves Saint Laurent's Y. Its outer packaging is white and simple, yet it appears high-quality, indeed, for me elegant, with its embossed folds at the edges and fine cardboard quality. On it, as well as on the bottle, a golden Y is embossed in fine lines with a narrow side shadow, along with the usual information.
If I had known something about the fragrance pyramid back then, before my first encounter with Igrec, and had even been aware of the above, it might never have happened.

It must have been around 1977 when I entered the payroll office of my training company and smelled this fragrance for the first time. A temporary worker (younger than me) had applied it, and I loved it from that moment on. As a farewell gift, she gave me the sample bottle because she didn’t like the scent.

Montale's Herbal Aquatica is one of the nicest niche fragrances for the hot summer times i have tested. For me (as also seen in the similarities) it comes close to Xerjoff's Erba Pura especially in the opening, but as it develops it appears with a bit more herbal and sweet tone. The scent is described exactly like the title suggests, it clearly has herbal notes, which are very pleasent and not pungent att all, these notes are accompanied by marine notes and bergamote, which really fit together nicely in a somewhat symbiotic way, completing each other in their smell, creating a very well put together scent. The scent as a whole therefore feels really light and sweet. The longevity is above-average with a fragrance-oil proportion of 40%, which is really good for fragrances in the range of 100-150€ (per 100ml). I can really recommend going into a niche perfumery and go see for yourself. I love this fragrance and can't wait for summertime to wear it!

That aquatics in the mainstream often come across as far too soft, synthetic, and shower-gel-like is well-known to anyone who has spent more than five minutes with perfumes. However, that some niche aquatics can also be just as challenging due to extreme algae, seaweed, salt, or even more intense scent impressions - one can come to this realization just as quickly. “Herbal Aquatica” by Montale attempts the balancing act - and does so as an extremely accessible and almost fruity-gourmand niche water man… Has it been washed damn well? Or does this combo sink? “Herbal Aquatica” has strong parallels to “Erba Pura,” but the successful Xerjoff has become such a memorable power fruit aquatic and bestseller that one sees similarities almost everywhere (similar to how Ford’s “Oud Wood” or his “M7” have shaped oud or Guerlain’s “Vetiver” has defined vetiver). Nevertheless, the similarities here are particularly hard to overlook. Only very late, in its final phase, does it become the king of the surf for me. It swishes and swirls as if Poseidon himself has taken the helm. And still in a highly pleasant way, that’s the art! I really like that! Before that, however, I have some issues with its bubblegum-like moisture. I had the same with Xerjoff’s hit. It’s as if you’re in a fruit punch in the Mediterranean. And the water splashes into the bowl! Not bad, but close! Still, one must say: “Herbal Aquatica” will manage the balancing act for most, it could make aquatics socially acceptable. Or at least contribute to that. Its hairspray apple (?) is a shaky candidate, though. Along with its spicy green, its dessert creaminess, then the sound of the sea paired with (in the worst case) caramel. The line between cacophony and symphony is indeed thin… Sandalwood and vanilla must first be interpreted aquatically and still remain mass-market friendly. Even if not every ace up my sleeve works for me. A bit of the Disneyfied ocean. Bottle: inconspicuous as always with Montale, but the color choice fits Sillage: potent without burning Longevity: much longer than the aquatic average (8-11 hours) Conclusion: one of the tastiest and more gourmand aquatics out there. I prefer to enjoy my dessert with a sea view, not directly in the sea…

Hi, I was looking for a floral scent that still smells masculine. I was about to buy Pura Erba by Xerjoff when Montale was recommended to me as a fragrance twin. I must add that I have only smelled Erba Pura on the tester. In the top notes, both smelled similar. It’s probably due to the Calabrian bergamot. The base notes of vanilla and amber are also identical. But I would need to buy and wear Erba Pura to explore the parallels over a longer period. I have no reference to declare Montale as a fragrance twin. I hope someone in the community has both scents and can evaluate them. I am very satisfied with the scent. It is fresh and aquatic, and the sillage is truly remarkable. It is still good to smell after 7-8 hours. Best regards

Recently, in the perfumery in front of the Montale shelf, a woman next to me sprayed a fragrance on a testing strip. I thought to myself, "Wait a moment, I know this one!". I had to think for a moment about where I recognized it from and then orient myself whether we were in front of the Montale or Xerjoff shelf. When I asked the lady which fragrance she had used and she showed me Herbal Aquatica, I had to test it on my skin. And there, the almost identical notes in the opening from Erba Pura were very clearly noticeable. This carried through until the end. A hint of freshness and a little bit of typical Montale DNA was added. This is what subtly distinguishes it from Erba Pura. I find it more pleasant. But I still prefer to smell both on others rather than on myself. Both somehow feel too overloaded for me.

As mentioned in the title, it's a take on Erba Pura's DNA, and it seems like Montale thought, "hey, everyone is doing it, why not us?" So I've had this fragrance for about more than 2 months now, and I find it phenomenal. Imagine Erba Pura but less sweet, more "masculine," and balanced-nothing is off, everything is in harmony. It lasts a very long time, and the scent feels like it becomes more and more amazing over time. It has an incredible sillage, and the green tea note is very well done. It's simply phenomenal.

Herbal Aquatica was for me like the first leap into the vast ocean of perfumes. Originally, I had my sights set on Soleil de Capri, but as fate would have it, the tester was empty - and so I was guided by a very nice consultation to Herbal Aquatica. A lucky find? Perhaps even more.

When I was looking for a fruity scent for summer, this one was offered to me as a fragrance twin to Erba Pura. The opening is almost identical to Erba Pura, but Herbal Aquatica remains consistent compared to the Xerjoff scent. The longevity is probably one of the best among all summer fragrances and even surpasses most winter perfumes.

I am wearing the fragrance for the first time today and was surprised right from the application. I had imagined the scent to be more synthetic, but this artificial note fades away quite quickly in my opinion. However, the fragrance is really pleasant.

I came across this fragrance by chance at Albrecht, and the name immediately caught my attention. At that time, I didn't really have any experience with Montale. I know that they make good perfumes, as their fragrances are often discussed online, like Arabians Tonka, etc. Regarding Herbal Aquatica - I tested it, and it appealed to me right away.

I have to say this scent is really good for summer. We have great fragrance notes like bergamot, vanilla, maritime notes, lotus, and sandalwood that really shine through. The scent is similar to Erba Pura by Xerjoff, but I find Herbal Aquatica significantly better. For me, this fragrance is not too much and not too little, but just perfect for summer.

It has secretly smuggled itself into our solar system behind Pluto. Astronomers discovered it through the Hubble Telescope and are now calculating its trajectory. Astrologers are going berserk, smoke rings puffing out of their ears. One of Jupiter's moons is no longer in the 5th brothel! Fortune tellers are eating their cards without sunflower oil, because it's all gone. So they have to choke down the stuff dry. Professor Pirkheimer says that only absolutely clean citizens will survive the impact. He recommends making calf wraps with self-felted scrubbing rags, which have been soaked in old coffee from an 80-year-old coffee machine. On these, one spreads a paste made from squashed "Nimm 2" candies, vanilla sugar from "Ja," and orange syrup for Soda Stream fizz makers. Afterwards, one scrubs themselves with root brushes and anoints themselves with linseed oil. The whole thing can be subscribed to as a complete package. It will be delivered every 3 months and will be charged. The meteor flies past Mars and takes the last survivors of Mars Attacks with it, the ones Tom Jones sang about back then. Now they swear revenge and want to transplant heads on Earth again. To be able to breathe the Earth's air, they chew on musk gums, which are more chewing gum than musk. So the Earthlings are wondering what to do. Bruce Willis is also no longer interested in a new Armageddon. But Tom Jones belts out: “Sexbomb, you’re my Sexbomb” (I love this song and old Tom anyway). The bomb part is somehow true too. The meteor makes a full stop, does a U-turn, and thanks to this flanker, disappears into the universe.

In the past, it was customary to study in Berlin. The city was political - meaning there were many demonstrations - and it had no curfew - meaning you could go out around the clock, which, however, got in the way of intense studying. I only visited my wayward clique on weekends - otherwise, I preferred to be "deep in the West, where the sun gathers dust" - as Herbie Bochum aptly sings. My excursions to Berlin were enough for me. And so it happened that we ended up at the trendy disco "Neuer Dschungel." A punk joint that I was curious about. We paid our entrance fee to colorful-haired Iroquois - and found ourselves in a glaringly bright room where many colorful people danced with sunglasses on their noses. There was no shortage of neon tubes in this establishment. I was somewhat startled by the brightness, as I had expected the usual dim disco lighting. Yet this large office atmosphere had something - a completely different intimacy, as you could look your counterpart straight into the pupils. Uncompromising and real. Along with the music from The Clash, Sex Pistols, Ramones, etc... Black Opium Neon would have fit in perfectly with its open artificiality - especially because of its charming nonconformity. Colorful gummy bears tumble about - drenched in vanilla and coffee. Petals float above, mixed with wood shavings. Anarchy in the U.K. I can't help it - I have to dance.

Actually, I don't like shopping malls. But do you know those large, airy ones, with calm music and few people, all of whom are relaxed? Where there is ice cream and waffles and, yes, milkshakes. With the first spray, I take a big sip of such a milkshake. Tropical-fruity, I think of mango, but it’s probably the dragon fruit. And a large portion of vanilla. With my huge cup in hand, I stroll around. On the rim, there’s a large white flower attached, whose scent rises to my nose with every sip. Orange blossom, mixed with something else. I pass by a perfumery, from which comes that sweet-heavy hint we all know. But I don’t go in, I just take a bit of floral and musk with me. On the other side of the aisle is a café, from which there’s also a fragrance. Over time, it becomes increasingly clear that someone has probably poured a big sip of dark-spicy coffee - or even Original Black Opium - into the cup. Nice, I think to myself, and continue strolling, with a last bit of milkshake in hand. I don’t like coffee, I don’t like shopping malls. But I really like this scent. It doesn’t differ much from the original for me. Vanilla, orange blossom, and what must be coffee. This one is fruitier, especially at the beginning, also a bit more synthetic, which probably bothers some. One could see it as a light version. There’s nothing neon about it, but that’s okay.

Right after applying, I smell artificial blueberry (or dragon fruit, if you prefer). After that, the scent reminds me of the original Opium, but without vanilla, instead with a lot of sweet fruit. Black Opium Intense is still my favorite by far, but this scent here is very special and actually feels more like an independent creation than a BO variant. It is youthful, playful, piercing yes, due to the artificial fruit, but it doesn't overwhelm me, which is not a given with such a sweet fragrance.

I have to add my two cents here after all. Yes, for people who already own a fragrance from the Black Opium line, this flanker might not be anything special. But in that sense, it applies to most of the fragrances I know from the Black Opium range - you might choose one for your collection that you like best, and the rest are not necessarily needed, as they are very similar; the dominant BO base is almost identical. In my case, it was actually Black Opium Neon that I had to constantly sniff on my wrist or test strips, and which ultimately made it into my collection. I find the name Neon very fitting and am surprised that this has not been addressed in any review yet. Neon light is glaring, it practically screams "HERE I AM," it stands out in the dark, it is synthetic, colorful, and yet many people find it pleasant to hang around at night in the light of neon tubes - whether at parties, in bars, or at the snack bar around the corner. And just like the beam of neon pink light tubes at night, the synthetic sweet dragon fruit-citrus note stands out from the dark coffee-vanilla BO background. Yes, it is glaring, but it does not illuminate the entire night; it stands out, but it does not dominate the fragrance. I am surprised that no one perceives the strong contrast as I do - when smelling this fragrance, a glaring neon-colored flash in the night was indeed my first association. Now, such a fragrance is certainly not an everyday scent for the office or for every day; over time it would be too intrusive. And it will not be everyone’s favorite. There is - as with most fragrances - the right time and the right occasion for it. For me, it is a going-out scent, and as such, I really like Black Opium Neon. It is also well received in my circle in this context, despite the synthetic sweetness. Or perhaps because of it? Synthetics can be annoying, but in this fragrance, I find that it fits perfectly. The contrast between the fragrance notes makes it possible. I am surprised that it scores so poorly here - at the same time, it does not surprise me at all, as most of us prefer the "natural," the warm, gentle daylight.

Hmmm.. I got a small tester and I have to say. Not for me but also not bad.. I'm not a YSL fan but this scent is at least a bit interesting even though it smells super artificial, almost synthetic.. I smell coffee first.. Not as present as Montale Intense Café but still quite noticeable.. Along with that come a lot of fruity and floral notes that I can't really distinguish..

Montale PURE GOLD starts out as a fruity-floral blend with a lot of clean resinous musk. I find it somewhat nondescript, especially initially, when I have trouble discerning individual notes... except for the musk which is quite big. Later this perfume starts to seem more like a nice floral with a slight soapiness. The floral component seems to me to be mainly jasmine. I was thinking that PURE GOLD was similar in some ways to Jennifer Aniston and DKNY Pure, but in side-by-side comparisons I changed my mind. PURE GOLD is much better than those. Perhaps the idea is similar, but in this case we have much better ingredients and execution. JENNIFER ANISTON veers too far in the industrial direction in an attempt to be clean. DKNY PURE has a touch too much woodish aromachemical stuff for my tastes. PURE GOLD is perhaps how those perfumes should smell, but they don't, which is probably why they are on their way out of the stores already... PURE GOLD is another example of Montale going beyond their area of expertise (middle eastern-inspired oud creations), to produce a decent, if not extraordinary, perfume.

If you're looking for a signature everyday scent I think this is the perfect fit for that, it's so pleasant and bright, I call it my "happy day perfume" because it genuinely smells like a happy day. Nice sweet juicy mandarin and apricot opening followed by beautiful white flowers that settle into a luxurious clean laundry scent that lingers for DAYS, I also believe this would be great as a gift, as I haven't met anyone that didn't love it, truly a great fragrance.

When you hear Pure Gold by Montale, you immediately suspect the worst, knowing the hits like Black Aoud or Sweet Oriental Dream. Of course, I also immediately thought of the legendary Gold by Amouage, and an oriental expectation set in before testing this rather overlooked Montale. No wonder with the flood of releases from the brand; they are going totally wild and exaggerating at times. And it's particularly unfortunate that such unexciting, rather calm all-rounders like Pure Gold can quickly get lost in the shuffle. It's time to give it some attention because it is one of the most beautiful Montales I have had the pleasure of smelling, liquid gold. The scent is a calm, almost meditative experience that persistently demands time, patience, and sensuality from the wearer. You can hardly imagine a greater all-rounder and versatility master; Pure Gold fits everything and everyone. While it’s not a chameleon that constantly changes, it is simply perfect, soft, lovely, and perfectly intertwined. The scent is most comparable to one or two fragrances from the MFK line, just with very slight sandy-Arabic hints. It is a floral scent, orangey and fruity. Additionally, it has a bit of powdery, creamy, balsamic quality. Very soft, light, like a breeze in the Sahara. Orange blossom, neroli, and vanilla blend together deliciously. I don’t know anyone who would criticize the scent, which might already be its biggest weakness: a bit too few edges, corners, and hooks that stick in your memory. Bottle: the golden ones are among the most beautiful Montales. Sillage: I wouldn’t say very quiet, but you expect something different with that name. Longevity: lasts almost all day. Not quite double digits. Highest quality, perfect transitions, an almost uncriticizable, perfect scent that delivers quite the opposite of what was expected. I Love It!

I am not a fan of floral/fruity scents. Something usually screams at me, sometimes it’s flowers that dominate in an intrusive way, sometimes fruits make my mouth water when I smell them. It’s often quite delicious, but I don’t want to smell like that. But if I had to name a term for Pure Gold, it is indeed floral-fruity but so skillfully harmonious that it is simply beautiful. I have forbidden my trainees to say - this is a beautiful scent. But here this description is completely accurate. From the very first drop, a fine aura unfolds like diffuse light. The flowers do not evoke kitschy pink or glaring white. Yes, it is liquid gold. I can hardly define the transition to the heart note. It is a harmonious flow into a soft now floral-powdery note. There is actually nothing extraordinary about this scent. No distinctive note, no exclamation mark, no Aha effect except for this skillfully unobtrusive elegance. But I think that is precisely what makes it special. Pure Gold is not a scent for someone who wants to stand out. On the contrary, someone who loves Pure Gold will never provoke, will never play the leading role, nor will they ever take the initiative, but everyone will feel comfortable in their presence.

Yes, it is beautiful, a truly beautiful fragrance, one can say that in the absence of other attributes. It is just beautifully floral fruity soft, not too much of anything, so even a flower skeptic like me can like it; everyone can probably like it, so pleasing is it, and that’s exactly what gets annoying after a while... For me, it triggered pleasure immediately after application, and only during the all-day test did it initially become somewhat banal in its beauty, and then after about 8 hours, I literally had my nose full! It had to come off, I could breathe again and now I reach for something lighter for the evening with a few imperfections, edges, and corners. So much "perfection" is probably not for me... It's like in the movies, the villains are sometimes fascinating, and the only-good-and-beautiful ones, yes, they get a bit boring too. Longevity: like tar. Sillage: top.

Freedom is my sea. A rolling ocean between the shores of my soul. And so I travel. Briefly to distant places, breathing in the scent of the moments. Work and leisure, cities and countryside, music, painting, and literature, storm and beach. Pure Gold is right in all these moments. It is for the globetrotter, lover, friend, artist, and much more within me.

I can't pick out the individual notes in this fragrance either. I've never experienced such a unity in any other scent. I apply it and Pure Gold is there. Not individual notes. A beautiful whole. And what keeps happening to me with this fragrance: the people around me feel good. Unconsciously, PG is perceived but not as a perfume.

Summer is coming to an end, and I'm testing citrus scents here... inappropriate? Not really, then I know what I could wear next summer. Besides, November is surprisingly warm! Well, the truth is that I still have a lot of samples here and, as always, I randomly grabbed one and this time it happened to be Pure Gold by Montale.

I have tested the fragrance several times and extensively, at different times of the day, in different weather conditions, and also in different moods, and unfortunately, I come to the conclusion that it obviously does not work with my skin chemistry. What I get with every test is a mixture that is both sweet and medicinally bitter in the first 15 minutes.

First of all: Floral/fruity is not really my thing, but a woman is open, curious, and willing to indulge in a (fragrance) flirt. The mostly positive comments convinced me to take the plunge. Thanks to the lovely Süchtig, I received a sample. Fragrance package arrived, sprayed on my wrist... and initially didn't pay much attention. Just like with a flirt.

… and if you like sweet scents, you better grab it while you can still find it. My prediction is that it’s gonna be remembered like the Invictus Aqua that everyone started loving after it was too late… It’s got a great scent. You can tell it’s the Y dna, but it has a younger feeling sweetness as a backbone. That sweetness actually outlasts the Y dna in performance, and it’s what remains on the final drydown. As stated below, it kind of feels like a more mature version of Invictus… KIND OF… Performance is excellent, a strong opening with a wide projection radius that extends an easy 4ft, and it has a nice sillage that trail lingers nicely for a solid 4 hours. When it pulls back it still smells nice and strong and the final performance on my skin is a solid 8+ hours. Seriously, if you like the Y line and/or you like sweet scents, you should grab it while it’s still out there, because it only gonna get love when it’s impossible to find… and that’s when everyone is going to want a piece of the fun

YSL Y Live it's like the younger brother of YSL Y Edp. More youthful, more bright and zingy, happier and more versatile (imho). YSL Y Edp on the other hand is a bit more mature, grown up and more masculine. Also, I am seeing Live more wearble in the summer while Y edp being sweeter I see it more suitable for spring, autumn and even winter. Many people resemble Y Live with invictus and I can partially agree in the sense that both have that juicy and fruity aroma but Live maintains that YSL Y Dna. I see Live as being very versatile (office, casual, meetings and so on) and a huge compliment getter. A dumb reach without the slightest doubt. Performance is awesome in my case. I am getting 8-10hrs of longevity with pretty nice projection and scent trail for the first couple of hours. The only downside it's the fact that it's discontinued and pretty rare to find already. As always I recommend to try it first and see if it suits you. Overall : 8.75/10

Scent: Smells like a diluted version of YSL Y EDP + a bit of Invictus | 7/10 Compliments: Really very good - has always been well received by the girls | 8.5/10 Longevity & Sillage: Weaker than the EDP, better than the EDT, 6 hours of longevity and about 2 hours of projection - it could be better | 6/10 Occasion: Only useful in spring/summer, too weak for fall/winter in my opinion | 7/10 Conclusion: A nice, safe & modern scent that brings good compliments but lacks the best performance or uniqueness.

I know I’m going to step on the toes of many "Y" lovers, but I just have to share my opinion on this. About the scent: what can I say? Synthetic to the core. It’s so synthetic that I’m afraid to spray it on my hand. In the end, I might grow a sixth finger and start a career in Cirque de Soleil (by the way, I had to Google the word Cirque du Soleil). It smells citrusy fresh but in an unpleasant way. Very artificial, somehow made without love, in the hope of creating a mass pleaser. Maybe I’m just too spoiled, but I find it terrible. I would neither recommend it, nor wear it myself, nor give it as a gift. The only situation where it would come into play is if the Thai restaurant went overboard with the chili again and I’m running home with a pained expression because I need to use the bathroom. Then and only then would "Y" come into play.

... slightly synthetic. But is that a reason to dismiss it so harshly? I don't think so. I believe it has potential and can be worn well on warm days. Yes, I admit that it is not a masterpiece that turns the fragrance world upside down. Upon application, a nice pear with citrus notes emerges. There’s also a floral note that softens it but doesn’t make it feminine. The tonka bean adds a slight sweetness. I can't detect the cocoa. The longevity and sillage are good. This perfume can be worn by men who enjoy a sweet, fresh scent with a hint of pear. Age doesn’t matter; if you like it, wear it. This scent can be worn for any occasion. Those who enjoy fresh and sweet fragrances might have fun with this one.

From the very first spray, a feeling of synthetics envelops you. No clear top note can be identified; instead, the orange blossom in the heart dictates the scent's progression. It is too dominant for me, the fragrance too one-dimensional. It remains consistently boring. The cocoa and tonka bean also get overshadowed. There are certainly cheaper alternatives out there.

This is one of the few jewels in all numerous Montale fragrances. No musc, a reasonable longevity, and office safe (!!!). Moreover, it is a beautiful iris, slightly sweetened with sandal. If you are not a fan of iris (as I am) still recommending to try it, it might change your opinion about iris perfumes.

When "Intense so Iris" arrived at my place and I cautiously sprayed a little on after a few hours, I thought: Is this the scent I wanted? I have had "Intense so Iris" on my wish list for some time. However, I couldn't find it in Germany when I wanted to buy it. I live in an area where there are no perfume shops, just the usual cosmetic discounters. This year, I didn't go anywhere where I could have bought or at least tested it. Now I have it! And I bought it blind at that price. However, I know myself. When I get something I've really wanted, I tend to feel a bit distant at first. I might be uncertain and a little disappointed. So, I have been testing "Intense so Iris" for a few days now. In doing so, I reflected on what kind of iris scent I actually wanted. I have several iris fragrances and don't want another one like the ones I already have: the light floral "Iris de Champs" by Houbigant, the earthy and nutty "Bois Farine" by L'Artisan, and the beautifully exquisite smooth festive iris scent with a - for me - ebony note from Roméa de Améor "Les Impératrices du Japonaises". The latter is one of my signature scents. I wanted a more rural, earthy iris scent in the direction of Lebreton's "Incarnata." "Incarnata" has the earthy note I desire. Unfortunately, it also contains other scent notes that I don't find pleasant. Additionally, in "Incarnata," I perceive the iris note more like an unwashed root still covered in fresh earth, meaning that I find it overdosed. In my search for an alternative scent to my iris fragrances, I kept landing back at "Intense so Iris" EdP. (It is sometimes labeled as Extrait, but it is an EdP, and nowhere on the bottle or packaging does it say "Extrait"). So first: Yes, "Intense so Iris" is the scent I wished for. And yet, "Intense so Iris" is somewhat different from what I imagined. I unconsciously expected something more in the direction of "Iris des Champs," that is, sweeter and smoother. Now to the increasingly captivating "Intense so Iris" by Montale. I always forget that it's a Montale fragrance, as I find it too untypical for Montale. First, I am greeted by a strong eruption of a non-sweet and quite sour-bitter lemon note, half freshly squeezed juice, half freshly grated zest. The first time, I was startled because I thought it was heading towards a Cologne, which I don't like. But it is a bright, unsweetened lemon note that within a second already lifts the iris. A beautiful, distinct, slightly brittle earthy and powdery dry iris note. I smell neither carrots nor any other root vegetables. After a few minutes, on the décolletage it can take up to 20 minutes, the fresh lemon note retreats significantly. Apparently, due to the listed musk, which I do not perceive at all, the bitter-fresh lemon note transforms into a very soft delicate lemon blossom note. Although the lemon note always lingers quietly in the background, "Intense so Iris" remains bright, fresh, and airy. Thus, the earthy iris is never dull or musty-stuffy. Shortly after, a restrained creamy sandalwood note develops. It gives "Intense so Iris" a refined smoothness without diluting the character of the rural iris into the trivial. Otherwise, nothing else happens in the main development. In the first seconds, "Intense so Iris" seems to have a strong sillage. However, "Intense so Iris" has a medium sillage. With the moderate sillage, the fragrance also has a medium longevity. However, "Intense so Iris" is still perceived close to the skin for a long time, with the creamy sandalwood becoming more pronounced then. I can say: "Yes, this is exactly the iris scent I wanted. And the inspiration of the perfumer with the unexpectedly fresh lemon note is, in my opinion, the highlight. Lipstick note in iris fragrances? I can't relate to that and don't perceive such a note in "Intense so Iris" or in any other fragrance that is supposed to have this note. Why other users expect and often perceive a lipstick note in iris is incomprehensible to me. I can't recall any such lipsticks at any time; I would have to be at least between 90 and 100 years old. However, I do not want to deny that others perceive exactly that because they associate this note with the smell of old lipsticks. As I see it, quite a few men also own "Intense so Iris." I agree with the classification due to the absence of any sweetness and the lack of a lush floral character. My search for iris fragrances is thus over for a longer time.

So this would be my first "properly" tested fragrance from Montale. Previously, I had tested a few scents more or less in passing and was anything but impressed. Way too loud, way too much Oud or Aoud, as one might call it at Montale. Oud/Aoud or whatever, we just don’t get along anyway. But Montale can do it differently. In a comprehensive sample package, a splash of Intense So Iris also came my way. One might think the name is indicative of what to expect. However, that is only partially true. Iris is indeed very noticeable and lingers for a long time, but nothing about it is intense. I'll start with the bottles, which I prefer to call containers. I find these aluminum things extremely unattractive. I've read comparisons to thermos bottles, deodorant cans, or nuclear warheads (yes, just pull the trigger and it goes puff...), and those might be quite fitting associations. Pretty is different. I'm not someone who places a high value on packaging, especially not when the contents are lacking. Conversely, some wonderful fragrances can be found in less appealing bottles. So let's keep it simple. But Montale's bottle design does not appeal to my taste. But that seems to be part of their overall appearance. What does the scent tell me? Yes, we have the Iris, who smiles friendly at everyone. She is nice, pleasant to deal with, but somehow she doesn’t quite come out of her shell. She gives the impression that you have to pull everything out of her. That becomes tiring over time. And I get another impression as well. Namely, that dear Iris is a huge fan of carrots and shovels them in by the handful. But do I want to smell like carrots? And that all the time? Hmmm, for a fragrance that is supposed to cost around €150, that feels a bit too little and boring. I prefer carrots on my plate because they are nice and healthy. Either raw and grated, with apple, or as a delicious side dish or in a stew. After a few hours, a faint woody hint makes itself known in the scent, along with something creamy that could come from the musk. However, that is not enough for me to make Intense So Iris more exciting. Thus, dear nice Iris remains friendly and subtle for me, but also somewhat bland and a bit boring. She doesn’t want to tell me anything more and continues to sit quietly with her carrots. There is no further development to be noticed. It is and remains a carrot-like experience. What I would like to note very positively is the longevity. Despite her weakly pronounced self-confidence, the nice Iris has a considerable staying power of easily 8-9 hours. I find that quite impressive. There are fragrances that try to show off and have already spent their ammunition much earlier. I’m glad I had the opportunity to get to know the nice Iris. But I won’t be inviting her in, that’s for sure. My thanks go to Verbena, who made this introduction possible! I could now unleash a whole series of carrot jokes... Well, one always works. The Iris walks into the pharmacy and asks: "Do you have carrots?" The pharmacist replies: "Of course I have carrots!" Iris says: "Darn, you ruined the whole joke!" Wishing you a fragrant Sunday, with or without carrots.

... what a thing! A Montale that has no hairspray or commercial note and yet appears completely natural and fresh. I have never experienced Montale like this before. Bought blind, I was completely satisfied with this beautiful fragrance from the very first sniff. It comes very monothematic. Basically an "Iris Attar without Rose," if I may cheekily take that designation! It starts much deeper and noticeably woodier than Infusion d'Iris and strikes me as significantly more unisex. It captivates with an incredibly pleasant freshness and appears much more powdery than its fragrance twin from Prada. In the drydown, the woody component becomes increasingly pronounced and gives the entire fragrance a certain degree of masculine wearability. I never get the impression of carrot, and if I do, it's only faintly in the background. It radiates brightly and offers excellent sillage for a fragrance in this category. The longevity on my skin is over 8 hours. Yet it remains gentle, unobtrusive, and impresses with an almost pure impression of high-quality iris. Those expecting significant development here will definitely be disappointed. As mentioned above, it becomes a bit woodier over time, but it never changes character. It remains strong, radiant, and bright. My fragrance for sports, hot summer days, and for all occasions where one wants to be perceived as pleasantly fragrant without wanting to appear too progressive. Clear purchase recommendation. If you like iris and are looking for a slightly louder fragrance with a certain freshness: buy!!!!!

First of all, a quick note, even if it distracts a bit: For everyone who liked Iris Rebelle by AC but found it far too weak, just like I did: Try this one. This one has substance! - And now please forget that right away. With Montale we get: Fresh fresh Iris! And the one with the famous little carrot, as if you just broke apart a fresh young carrot and with the crack of the carrot, a little juice splashes in your face. This would have suited the name Iris Rebelle, which comes at you with power and is yet the typical carrot-Iris at the beginning refined with a bit of citrus and fresh green. Absolutely charmingly woody. Wood with light gray grain. After about a quarter of an hour, the scent settles and stays. It just barely sneaks past a Haaspray note - luckily, because AugustA doesn't need that at all. Slightly creamy, but not buttery, the scent remains and remains and remains. I catch myself thinking about what one could layer it wonderfully with, so puristic is this Iris. Puristic, not powdery. After two hours still no powder whatsoever. The charms that Iris can play in combination with other flowers and especially woods are completely absent from this scent at first. It’s almost surprising because one tends to mentally complement the scent, to imagine something that isn’t there. A blank space, an open field. But that is precisely the allure of the composition. Fresh pure Iris, little that completes the association chain - no noble elegance, no severity, no powdery sensuality, nor dreamy melancholy. And yet - all of that is part of Iris after all. The Iris: rainbow, messenger of the gods, iridescent, wind shape, always a bit otherworldly. Although a root, not a bloom, it eludes direct access. Spherical. Woody and dry. Here you find it as directly as possible. This Iris scent is completely - naked. Not notions of nudity or the like. But naked Iris, uncovered by other scents or fragrance note concepts. I couldn't even say who the scent would suit, not whether it’s for young or old, man or woman or whatever. Not a target group scent that’s been overly styled, not a green one and also not an oriental. An Iris, as you might (recognize) it, but always only in combination before. When I notice this, the scent has captured me, and it can remain just as it is for hours. What it initially does. Then, after about 3 hours, the scent imperceptibly softens, musk alters the surface and gives a bit of fluff, very soft fluff. The pure now becomes a tad creamier and more sensual. The musk is delicate and soft, does not (!) remind one of laundry detergent or soap, but gives the Iris a quality that evokes skin warmth and a touch that was not present in the scent before, precisely because it was so naked. Now it has become more tactile. The perfumer probably didn’t want to add much more to it.

The opening begins lightly citrus-alcoholic and then the scent disappears for a moment. But after a while, a beautiful iris reveals itself, softly floral and powdery, lightly woody with a hint of cream. The sillage is rather low, ISI retreats to the skin quite quickly. Nevertheless, the scent occasionally wafts into my nose with movement.

Although I used to prefer floral perfumes (and still like them today, even though I have learned to appreciate many other scents through Parfumo), the note of iris remains somewhat problematic for me. Either it comes across as very powdery to me - dry, in extreme cases like the iris perfume from L’Erbolario, which I perceive as almost "dusty.

The pyramid was clearly imagined by someone, because I smell lemon wood, and not the one from Southeast Asia that is only called that because of its color, but one that probably only exists in my imagination. From the first spray to the end, it smells of lemony wood: Fresh, freshly cut, juicy, gentle, uplifting, and bright.

I am reviewing this based on it's inclusion in the Roja Women's sample pack and this is more or less a first impressions review. Firstly, Roja Danger is very clearly a well blended scent -- it's round and it does take the wearer on a journey throughout the day though, spoiler, the start of that journey is the best part. The opening of Danger is really wonderful and I get cloves, musk and fresh citrus right away, distantly there is a bit of spice from the patchouli in the base. The opening is driving into the sunset on a warm autumn afternoon. The cloves really are a delight and the musk note is my type of musk. Clean but a little flirty yet not overly animalic or dirty. Unfortunately, about an hour into wear Danger takes a hard left turn into straight up baby wipes. I usually like powdery scents but this was overwhelming powded. I always test with a light hand and did only a spritz and I still felt like I was inhaling baby powder. Gone was all of the earlier warmth. I nearly considered scrubbing it but for the sake of testing, stuck it out. Thankfully the baby powder bomb is temporary and around the 3 hour mark it settles down into a pleasant, soft, if somewhat nondescript vanilla. It's in this cozy vanilla state that it stays as a skin scent for about 7 hours. If I compare Danger to Roja 51 from the same sample pack, I feel like this is the fall/winter sister to 51. They share the same rough skeleton but 51 is lighter, brighter and fresher whereas Danger is definitely more robust. However, in this instance I think 51 would be more worth the money. From the fantastic opening, disappointing mid and generic base, Danger left me with an overall "safe" feeling that has me a little disappointed. It was nice, but I don't think I would buy a full bottle, certainly not for the price.

Definitely a fall time in Manhattan kind of scent. Not the Bronx, Queens, Staten Island, or Brooklyn; Manhattan. I'll go so far as to say had this had NYC etched into the glass, with no other naming, this would have been one of the most recognizable and most sold perfumes of all times. The lackluster marketing definitely handicapped the embrace of this one. A beautifully made, chic, masculine perfume. 10/10

In the early part of the 2020s, it is becoming increasingly difficult to find a masculine scent that's not heavily infused with vanilla, Tonka and other overly sweet notes and accords. Also, to find a primarily masculine fragrance that's also not a fougere or chypre AND not sweet is almost unheard of anymore. "Le Vestiaire - 6 Place Saint Sulpice | Yves Saint Laurent" is that fragrance. Woody, spicy, resinous, dense enough, masculine. In the same vein as Bvlgari Man In Black but a more top shelf version, if you will. The spicy leather with the saffron is perfect for a man who doesn't want to indulge in the overly sweet or gourmand fragrances that are being pushed out by damn near every fragrance house on planet earth. Easily overshadowed by "Le Vestiaire - Tuxedo | Yves Saint Laurent" and "Le Vestiaire - Caban | Yves Saint Laurent" but definitely no slouch. An awesome designer release.

Leather, labdanum and tonka combine to create a beautiful leathery and spicy amber base being flanked on all sides by lavender and sage, creating an addicting aura of aromatics. Shares similarities with Gris Charnel Extrait, but this has a more refined dry down and composition. Where GCE has a bitter and spicy sandalwood, fig, and tonka, 6 amps up the warmth and sweetness with the Tonka and lavender. Definitely takes the suede/leather accords from 24 and 37, and adds some much needed depth and complexity. Tied for best of the Le Vestiaire line with Tuxedo.

6 Place Saint Sulpice arrived as a surprise sample in a fragrance package - heartfelt thanks to Cafénoir for that! Fortunately, it was a bit cooler yesterday after a heavy thunderstorm; otherwise, I would have had to postpone the sample. Because one thing is clear: This scent is not for high summer temperatures. This time, first my short notes, which I always take before writing a comment and studying the fragrance pyramid. LEATHER! (like in Bottega Veneta), resin (really quite pure), spices (cinnamon, nutmeg, meat pie spice), increasingly noticeable lavender (after about 40 minutes), becoming stronger and rosemary (like herbs from Provence). It becomes more floral, vanilla-like, softer, beautiful base, lasts forever (8 hours plus!) I usually don’t include these short notes in the comment, but here something is happening that I have never experienced so clearly. I smell what is listed in the fragrance pyramid of “6 Place Saint Sulpice” almost from back to front - how curious is that!? Now, however, a few sentences that hopefully do justice to the scent. The opening really reminds me a lot of Bottega Veneta with this wonderfully soft caressing leather note. This is the finest handbag leather of the highest quality. I confess, I have a bit of a fetish and belong to those people who really sniff handbags (and other leather items) - just like with books, because I love that special paper/ink smell. But I digress. The leather in the scent is truly caressingly soft, but is accompanied by resin - and in combination, it’s quite a potent mix. Almost from the beginning, fragrant spices come into play - both spicy and sweet and bitter at the same time. Phew, this is exactly the moment when I’m glad the temperatures have dropped: In humid heat, it would have been too much for me by now. Luckily, I can follow the development of the scent in a more floral direction. But don’t think of roses, jasmine, or orange blossom or anything like that! No, it’s definitely lavender that comes to the forefront here (and it smells like opening a can of “Herbes de Provence” that has a lot of lavender in it!). Now the scent becomes increasingly softer and more pleasant, a bit of vanilla (of the spicy and not the sweet kind) comes in, and it all becomes creamy warm and cozy. I find the scent wonderful - but I also love Bottega Veneta for its leather note. Where Bottega is a bit more gentle and floral, YSL remains uncompromisingly on the leathery-spicy side. A beautiful scent that, for me, does not fit into summer - and therefore immediately moves to the “Test again in Fall/Winter” list!

I first became aware of this fragrance about 1 1/2 years ago when I visited a friend whose girlfriend had quite an opulent perfume collection in her bathroom. I mentioned it to her, and she was happy to talk with someone similarly enthusiastic about scents. Throughout the afternoon, she showed me some of her fragrances, and this one stuck in my mind from that moment on. When I smell it, I think of a dry fir forest and a forester wearing leather boots right in the middle of it. In the opening, I mainly get the lavender, but leather and labdanum quickly join in. From there, the scent development on my skin is quite linear - only a slight sweetness comes into play. The leather smells to me not rough and strong, but rather like a nice smooth leather jacket. The longevity on my skin is above average, and 3-4 sprays are definitely enough for the whole day, although it only projects strongly for 3-4 hours before it settles into a closer scent bubble. I don't think I need to say anything about the price... Typical YSL Vestaire Collection, after all. I hesitated for a long time before buying it, but I ultimately have to say that it is worth every penny for me!

The 6 Place Saint Sulpice is my second dark bottle, after the 24 Rue de L'Université . I personally found the latter too dusty and dry, so it didn't stay long in my collection. The 6 Place Saint Sulpice , on the other hand, captivated me from the very first spray.

With this scent, I am reminded again that I urgently need to harvest the blackcurrants... but it is so terribly hot! However, an authentic blackcurrant scent is not what SC offers! I bought it because I liked the body butter. Yes, it was also super sweet, slightly artificial, with a hint of spiciness. But I liked it anyway! I don't wear this scent to the office, with clients, or when going out, but as a feel-good scent for my leisure time (just at home alone). For a scent in this category, I don't expect anything sophisticated or refined - for that, I have a battery of niche fragrances. Therefore, I find my rating of 70% to be quite fair! I got what I expected! At a good price.

So, let's be transparent. Montale/Mancera is known for their infinite takes on oud. For most people, this gets repetitive. However, you can't be upset for having too many options. If oud is not your thing, there are also plenty of non-oud options Montale offers. Something you should know about oud, whether synthetic or naturally sourced... it's harsh, with medicinal tendencies. Oud is not pleasant on it's own, so you often have to be patient. Oudmazing had to grow on me, because I am not fond of grape. Montale says it's "pink grape", so maybe there's an exception. Eventually, the scent finds balance and is much more enjoyable in the drydown phase. I personally wanted more patchouli, as I don't smell it at all. There is a fruity/floral facet to this oud, yet still somewhat gender neutral. Leather? Questionable. Orris? Check. Vanilla?? Minimal, but you you REALLY have to wait for it. There is also a presence of rose. Bloomingdale's lists it, but Montale and Fragrantica does not. Overall good quality with notable longevity and projection into the world. Oudmazing is very date night and more of a sensual and romantic oud. A safe blind buy from Montale for oud lovers and oud rookies. The end result for me was too feminine, so this will make a wonderful Christmas gift for someone unsuspecting.

Not a masculine only perfume and I’m surprised that I’m saying this because even the most fruity floral unisex perfumes that please to a good amount of women in general I’m here not liking them I mostly find them more masculine for my liking I think I’m more a girly type of scents ( not anytime tho ) But this one is a really prominent oud and a perfect unisex fragrance I will wear this for getting me out of my confort zone but mixing with another fragrance that I want it to have this oud note

Personal: 6/10 - More syrupy sweet fruit than oud. Typical of Montale. It's meh. Mass appeal: 6.5/10 – Loud fruits and oud have their fans, but it's love/hate. Performance: 9/10 – Nuclear. This stuff sticks around for a LONG time. Value: 7/10 – Montale pricing is fair IF you like the DNA, but I wouldn't pay for it. Uniqueness: 7/10 – Oud and fruits isn’t new, but Montale pushes it to such extremes that it earns some uniqueness points, especially for the syrupy take. SCORE: 71/100 Full bottle buy? NO, I respect it but I’d never wear it. Not for me. Blind buy? NO, syrupy fruit bombs with 'oud' (synthetic) aren't for everyone. Recommend? YES, if you want a loud fruity oud that performs like crazy. Date night? NO, even with two sprays it'll be cloying and not at all seductive. Office safe? NO, HR will send you home in 30 minutes. Too headache inducing. Pros: Loud, long-lasting, attention-grabbing. Fruity oud done youthfully. Cons: Overwhelming, syrupy and synthetic. Feels headache inducing to me. Oudmazing is what Montale does VERY well, which is syrupy fruits and a pretty nice synthetic oud. It's approachable, and a pretty solid intro to oud, though not quite a mature fragrance. I think it's a great option if you want something a little bit darker but still sweet, bright, and fruity. It's a somewhat generic DNA, but done... differently. I find it a bit cloying, though, because I don't really enjoy these EXTREMELY sweet fragrances. But again, I appreciate the gentle, synthetic, intro-complexity oud. A nuclear fruity, syrupy bomb. Amazing, but only if it's really your thing. Review #92 in my fragrance journey – this fragrance I own as a decant

I initially had Oudmazing as a small sample. After extensive testing, I really liked it, and so it was clear that the large bottle had to come home. With Oudmazing, you get a sweet, yet not edible, lovely fruity scent that brings a pleasant edge. The fragrance opens with citrus notes and then transitions into a fruit mélange. I also perceive jasmine, but not in a dominant way; rather, it is well intertwined with the fruits. From the fruits, I can most distinctly smell pear and grape; those looking for a fig like Philosykos will not find it here. However, it is important to emphasize: none of the notes stand out unpleasantly and loudly for me. The aforementioned edge in the fragrance comes naturally from the oud, but also from patchouli and leather. Both give the scent depth and a certain maturity, if not even a mysterious quality. Oud is often a real nemesis for me, as it too often has a stable association that I cannot handle at all. You need not fear that with Oudmazing - stable is not on board here; instead, there is a woody, slightly smoky note. Leather is (thankfully) only perceptible when I smell directly on the skin. Leather in fragrances is unfortunately often difficult for me and occasionally causes headaches. That is not the case here; the dose of leather is very well tolerated :-) Oudmazing is for me a darker scent that I associate with the colder season. Regarding the target audience, I think the fragrance can definitely be worn by men - they should, however, enjoy sweet scents! I would not recommend Oudmazing as an office scent, but rather for going out. Personally, I also enjoy wearing it at home, just for myself. The longevity and sillage are typically very strong for Montale, so one should be cautious with the dosage ;-) Conclusion: One of my favorites from Montale - well wearable oud scent - very unique - bomb-like longevity and sillage My rating of the fragrance? Scent 10 out of 10 Longevity 9 out of 10 Sillage 10 out of 10 Price-performance 10 out of 10 Recognition value 9 out of 10

Oudmazing, what a name. It sounds like the best Oud fragrance is about to come. This doesn't make me very happy, as I don't like intense Oud. In the past, it was even worse; I couldn't stand Oud at all, but nowadays I find that subtly used Oud can smell quite pleasant and good in fragrances. At this point, of course, a big thank you to a certain cat-obsessed perfumer for the sample of this fragrance, although it might be difficult to guess who she is, as most people here are cat-obsessed. How else can one explain the fact that some people often check my profile? Am I actually interesting to the perfumers? No *sobs*, of course not, they all just want to see my cat *sigh* This little rascal. I’m going to quickly give him an evil, jealous look. *staring at the cat* Crap, he just woke up, looks at me all confused, lets out an incomplete meow (incomplete because he starts to meow, you can hear the "Mi," but he can't continue because he has to yawn! So it's a Miiigäääähn!) and therefore looks adorable as always. Now I have to give him a kiss too. *cat kiss* … *removing cat hair from lips* … Stupid rascal… confused, sleepy, but his hairstyle is ALWAYS on point, so he still looks good :D Hmm… I seem to be digressing,… oh yes, the fragrance Oudmazing: The Fragrance: Wow, a powerful Oud cloud is released right at the beginning. At first, you can hardly smell anything but Oud, but that doesn't last long. The Oud remains extremely strong, but in the next few minutes, other fragrance notes also come through. The top note has a generally fruity undertone, and I would say that you can best detect an orange here. The other fruity notes create a kind of fruity mix,… something like a fruit conspiracy. I also smell a slight iris, which makes it softer and more powdery. The jasmine is easily recognizable with its almost unmistakable sweetness and… of course… makes the fragrance sweeter. But the patchouli is almost as strong as the jasmine, so you can also perceive the typical earthy patchouli scent. In my opinion, I find the patchouli even too strong, so that together with the strong Oud, it might come off as a bit overwhelming. I almost wanted to write that leather is missing, especially for such a fragrance, but in the base, the fragrance actually releases a leather note, albeit a bit weak. The vanilla, which comes in later than usual, adds another sweet note (or almost replaces the jasmine) and makes the fragrance softer, like the iris. Otherwise, the fragrance mainly smells of Oud and patchouli in the base. The Sillage and Longevity: The fragrance is strong. Really damn strong. A single spray is basically enough for everyone to perceive it well from a distance. A large scent cloud definitely lingers for a longer time with a few sprays. You can imagine that the longevity is also quite strong. Alone on the skin, you can smell the fragrance from morning to evening or even late into the night, although after many, many hours, of course, the scent starts to weaken eventually. Oh, and by the way, it still smells on the skin after a shower! The Bottle: Well, I just can't warm up to the bottles from Montale. To me, they look like small (possibly medical) bottles with the caps unscrewed. Anyway… This bottle is shiny black. The label is gold-plated, and a logo plaque hangs around the neck. It's nice in itself, but as I said, there are prettier bottles for me. Wow, it smells so strong here! Due to the summer, I have logically been testing more summery fragrances lately. And what do you know about most summer fragrances? That they are naturally fresher. And that they usually have a rather low sillage. So I unconsciously applied way too much of this fragrance here, so now my whole room "stinks." No, the scent has filled the entire apartment, probably the whole house. Oh, what am I even saying… I mean, you can smell the fragrance throughout the whole neighborhood, and it's hot today, making the scent feel more overwhelming than on cooler days! Phew…! But it doesn't smell bad. Okay, it's not necessarily my fragrance, as I'm not really into strong Oud scents and I don't like patchouli that much either, but Oud lovers should quite enjoy this fragrance, especially if they're looking for something strong with Oud for autumn and winter, which still has nice sweet notes with a soft background. Usable anytime on cold days, but at work, you should really apply it sparingly. You can apply more when going out if you want, although for partying, the fragrance isn't sweet/pretty enough, well, at least in my opinion. So, as I said, Oud lovers should check this out. But those who can't stand Oud will probably just look as confused as my cat or even run away :D

I have always had great respect for the fragrances from Montale, to say the least: a certain apprehension, because they have the reputation of being quite strong and opulent, which is not really my thing. By nature, I am more of a quiet observer than the diva in the spotlight. Now I dared to test one, and I must say, my caution was justified.

Is "Oudmazing" Montale's final word on their specialty? Is the world begging for mercy on its knees here? No, at least not to question one, For the oud here is everything but pure. A very feminine, floral-fruity veil, not the same old Montale tune. But "Oudmazing" does not suit me, if only because of the brutal jasmine layer.

Once again something new from me. A fragrance that has been sitting with me for a while and that I have tested several times. This scent hasn’t really been put to use yet, but it is definitely an enrichment for a multifaceted collection.

Oudmazing is super long-lasting. On me, it lasts clearly more than 12 hours with just one spray. The sillage is strong on me and the expression is sweetly oriental, in the direction of LVEB. Oud is hardly noticeable on me, but it makes the sweetness of the fragrance a bit more rugged and drier. I'm still not quite sure what to think of this scent.

Delicious....... finally a fruity scent on my skin that doesn't turn soapy, hooray! So I am a difficult skin type for light, floral, fruity fragrances. I tried Pulp two years ago and thought it was fantastic at first, then I stood in a flower shop and thought, what smells so horrible here, until I realized it was my wrist where Pulp had been sprayed.

First of all, I would like to address some potentially negative statements upfront. Yes, it is a Montale and yes, it has the well-known Montale hairspray note (synthetic). Also, rose plays a dominant role again and yes, the bottle quality is the same as it has been for over 10 years. Now, let's get to the scent. :) Right after spraying, I get such a strong "fresh basil note" in my face that it startled me. Fortunately, this initial basil note disappears as quickly as it came, and the coffee comes to the forefront. In the background, a mixture of the previously mentioned rose note joins the coffee, along with a not-so-fresh basil note. This trio then stays for the first 1-2 hours. Gradually, the vanilla and caramel take over from the coffee and share the stage with the rose and basil. For me, this is FINALLY, after about 2 years of waiting, a really beautiful Montale scent again. The last successful Montale for me was Dark Vanilla . With this fragrance, the longevity and sillage are FINALLY also on point again. However, Montale has not overdone it with the sillage this time, unlike with Arabians Tonka . Therefore, the scent is very well received in my surroundings and is not considered intrusive. However, I do have one major criticism. The fragrance is currently not available in Germany and is only obtainable in Italy. Very, very unfortunate :(

Once again, a review of a Montale, a brand that is very difficult to navigate due to its numerous releases. Testing through all of them is really challenging, so I don't even try. However, I have to test selected fragrances from this brand, as they are quite enticing in their presentation. This Rendez-vous a Milan was one of those. Not only the name, but also this wonderful fragrance pyramid. Most of the notes are indeed very present. I'm surprised that this scent hasn't received more attention. It is really hard to compete with the hype fragrances from this house, as they are especially hyped on social media. I can definitely recommend this one, and this fragrance has been on my wish list for a while. The price-performance ratio of many Montales is quite good. A great balance between designer and niche prices, and most releases fall within that range. The bottles may look quite pretty in pictures, but when you hold them, they feel significantly cheaper due to the material. The box also leans more towards designer. The cool Montale pouch that this bottle comes in is a nice touch. In terms of scent, this is my favorite among the sweet Montales. I haven't tested all the relevant Montale fragrances yet, but this one is really cool. A wonderful sweet-spicy scent that is also quite wearable in milder temperatures. It's not a heavy fragrance, and the basil note gives it really nice green-spicy vibes. You should test it if you're looking for sweet fragrances for transitional weather or the evening. Listed as a similar scent is Intense Cafe from the same house. Yes, they do go roughly in the same direction: coffee, rose, vanilla... quite a few elements these fragrances share. However, this Rendez-vous gives you significantly more breathing room and is perfect for those who don't prefer an atomic sillage. It projects well, but is rather an uncomplicated fragrance that radiates a lot of sensuality. You get a wonderful blend of sweet, spicy, gourmand, fruity, and that unique basil note that keeps it a bit lighter. The opening is characterized by that basil note, which is also listed in the heart note. This note definitely lasts a long time and works wonderfully with the gourmand undertones. This fragrance never becomes too gourmand, but the sweetness remains throughout. There's also a light coffee note that isn't too intense. The rose note is very active here, coming across similarly to how it does in Intense Cafe. A slightly fruity DNA underlies this rose-basil note. The sweetness, which should come from caramel and vanilla, is present throughout. It's never too sticky-sweet but rather beautifully soft. Clove and musk-amber also play a role. The main players are clearly basil, rose, and a lot of sweetness. Overall, a wonderful sensual fragrance that can be worn very well on mild days. Those who enjoy sweet fragrances, for example in spring, will find a great option here. Everything is very rounded, soft, and simply seductive. Moreover, this fragrance is absolutely unisex. The performance is perfect for those who find a beast mode sillage like Montale's too much. The scent is well perceivable but still extremely suitable for everyday wear. The longevity is also extremely solid. You can treat yourself to this for the price. A very pleasing fragrance that convinces and lives up to its name. This would be a great date fragrance, but it also has everyday wearability.

The Rendez-vous à Milan is a truly successful fragrance. It starts with a basil note, which I find particularly special and really like. You rarely encounter such an accord. Unfortunately, for me personally, this accord fades a bit too quickly. After the lovely basil accord, the fragrance transitions to coffee, rose, and sweet notes. Somehow, this feels familiar to me.. hmm :D It brings back memories of Intense Café, and I currently have Dahaab Saafi, which smells almost identical to Intense Café. The vibes that these two fragrances have are also clearly felt here in Rendez-vous à Milan. This is my personal opinion and perception. As time goes on towards the end, it becomes subtly sweet for me, but without the coffee vibes. More amber, caramel, and vanilla come to the fore. Interestingly, these sweet components seem to float on a slightly fresh cloud for me. Perhaps it’s also because I washed my hands from time to time and the soap came through :D Longevity and sillage are good. Overall, for me, a good Montale fragrance. Definitely worth trying. This one will surely find many fans again.

I am not a fan of embellishments, ostentation, or luxury, not even in the world of fragrances. Display-worthy bottles are a nightmare for me. A bottle must - I think - be able to be tossed casually into any crazy bag (from handbag to sports bag) without losing its cap or even its contents. The Montals can do that to some extent. They jingle delightfully in my bag thanks to the clip, but if one were to complete the deodorant bottle character and put a cap on, they could actually become scent-tight. Well, that's my personal feeling about the bottle. I would also harmonize the somewhat trashy exterior presentation a bit. For fans of simplicity, the scent that is supposed to interpret a sunny day in Milan is definitely worth a journey. The top note is magnificent, an authentic basil scent, freshly grated, almost a bit tipsy and extremely cheerful. I see myself - freshly out of the hotel shower - happily hopping through the Milanese fashion world. But the first clouds are approaching quickly. Unfortunately, this sparkling sensation does not last beyond the top note. Too soon I find myself sitting in front of coffee and a Milanese pastry, right next to the rose bush, which I personally find unfortunate. The start was sooooooo beautiful. What is really good is the prominent basil note. I can clearly perceive it for 2-3 hours. It supports the Italian metropolitan flair and prevents slipping into the (scent) province. The ensemble of coffee and green sometimes reminds me a bit of cardamom and remains unobtrusive throughout the entire scent progression. The sillage makes the scent an all-rounder for me; others might describe it as "mediocre." You certainly won't offend anyone, but you also won't necessarily stand out positively. The scent simply underscores a beautiful day in the city and lasts through the entire shopping tour. For me, it's a well-balanced summer daytime fragrance, suitable for any gender and any situation. I’ll toss it in my bag right away and test it this weekend in Turin. I'm curious to see if it fits that occasion too ;-)

Milan is one of the cities where I absolutely want to spend an extended weekend in my life. Strange, why this elegant fashion metropolis in northern Italy has never been on my itinerary until now. In any case, I now know which perfume I would take with me - because Montale shows with this local rendezvous that they still know how to do it… and how! “Rendezvous a Milan” overlays the typical Montale coffee DNA (for example, from their milestone “Intense Café”) with an extraordinarily delicious basil-green. Is this addition enough for a bullseye? Yes, because this Milanese date brings even more spice and uniqueness to the table than simply slightly altering the aforementioned legendary DNA. It remains a Montale, it remains a coffee delight with minimal hairspray milk in it. But Milan certainly adds enough character and individuality to stand out. It has become a really good everyday scent, that much is quickly clear. Elegant, delicious, a gourmand for summer?! Montale pulls many strings here. A real insider tip in their (far too broad) portfolio. A citrusy rose, soft basil (the absolute unique selling point!), high-quality coffee with a hint of caramel. Never sticky, always wearable. With a remarkably high compliment density. Delicious. Italian. Stylish. And yet playful enough. This is not just a rendezvous, but close to love at first sight! Bottle: at least a bit more playful than usual due to color and pattern Sillage: Montales are never really quiet. No matter which city. Longevity: manageable - 7-9 hours Conclusion: Milan is still beautifully green behind the ears… Style and fun finely combined in one of the better Montales in years! Coffee culture at 35 degrees - Bellissimo!

... if it weren't for that Indonesian clove. Otherwise, it's a super beautiful, soft scent with rose and coffee at its heart. It starts with fresh and spicy notes. Most reviewers smell basil, which is also listed in the fragrance pyramid. I only detect a spicy note and predominantly perceive the coffee.

For me personally, alongside Dark Vanilla, this is one of the best Montale fragrances out there. And they are not only unique but also underrated! It has its pros and cons. Well, now to Rendez Vous A Milan! About the scent itself (9.15 out of 10): A gourmand fragrance with spice, fruity and oriental aspects.

In the old town of Florence. I sit in a cafe and order an Aperol. The sun reflects off my gold bracelet and it looks like it's sparkling on my wrist. A light breeze blows and spreads the Montale scent in the air. … This fragrance is simply perfect. The basil in the opening paired with the rose and the spice of clove! A true dream

... that fits its name so well. Rendez-vous à Milan instantly transports me to Milan. At first, a huge cloud of basil hits you, but not in a negative way. Shortly after, a delicious Italian coffee and yellow fruits fresh from the tree join in. The basil becomes weaker but remains noticeable. All in all, it creates a dreamy blend that lasts for several hours.

I find the scent Rendez-vous à Milan by Montale smells warm and elegant. The combination of rose and warm woody notes gives the fragrance a refined depth that feels both sensual and noble. Later, a sweet coffee note emerges that makes the entire scent very interesting. I bought the fragrance in Paris at the store and was thrilled with the knowledgeable and friendly advice.

Dusk wants to spread its wings, The trees stir ominously, Clouds drift like heavy dreams - What does this dread mean? (From: Twilight - Joseph von Eichendorff, 1788-1857) - - - SB7 is not a scent of the forest, no, it can be found in the metropolises of Paris, London, and New York. SB7 is nocturnal, in the twilight of dusk, at the transition from day to night, it opens its gates. Here we are not presented with a fair-weather scent, no, we are dealing with a dazzling natural force in the corset of urban parks, grand villa gardens, and rooftops above the city. The lavender does not show itself in its dreamy-lovely, provincial side; rather, it reveals its profound depths, together with its companions anise, castoreum, and civet. The reflecting parallel worlds of SB7 enter into an intimate and challenging relationship with the wearers of the fragrance. The scent is made for generations that move between nightclubs, opera houses, bars, and grand hotels. - - - “For me, the woman, every female being for the man, is a potential bearer of salvation. In the ritual of sexual union, the sacred seems to emerge.” (From: Parisian Apprenticeship - Nicolaus Sombart, 1923-2008) SB7 is a fragrance that lives from nights soaked in pleasure; here, the one who wears the scent rules and makes the man or woman submissive to them - while also protecting, challenging, but not surrendering the counterpart. This lascivious and profoundly cultivated scent, underscored by amber, incense, and labdanum, was created for special moments. Flower bowls in the salon are graced by distant candlesticks with dim light, the rose bouquet rests in magnificent vases, while the moon peeks through a slit in the silk curtains into the bedroom. SB7 breathes the scent of the old world, is nostalgic, arrogant, and always desirable. Archaic and high culture form a whole in SB7. - - - With deepest thanks to R. for sharing this rarity!

This is an insult on bakery and bakers all around the world. A vanilla cake? Sure, maybe a box mix cake made with expired milk, fertilized eggs, and an oven with faulty wiring.
