And after the biohazard comes out of the "oven", it's then left to sit out in the sun for days, weeks, maybe even months. This is my first ever review. I created this account to warn people about this odorant. DO NOT BLIND BUY AT ALL COSTS. If you ever think about smelling this in a store, be weary and stay safe.

Notes look incredible. Name is incredible. Do not be decieved. This is such a woody and smoky scent. My grandma said I smell like pine trees. I don't personally smell pine trees but anyway, how is there no incense note listed? Or at least some musky woody notes or something like that? Yes, this is so very sticky and sickly sweet, yes there is a strong creamy syrup vanilla, but to my nose, the vanilla gives a playdoh vibe. Idk it's just so underwhelming and non-edible. It also has the tendency to smell pissy in a beach sand way on my skin, which sucks. It legit feels illegal for me not to like this but here I am I guess. I really wanted to like this so bad. It's just not the vibe. If u like gourmands, STAY AWAY

In the dark season, I often crave something sweet - no wonder, as the dopamine levels need to be lifted. But sweet treats stick to the teeth - and to the hips. So my mom taught me to reach for a vanilla scent, which, according to her experience, calms the "sweet tooth." So Vanilla Cake came in very handy. An oven-warm vanilla strudel, topped with almond slivers and drizzled with caramel sauce appears like a hologram before my "gawking" eyes. I want to storm the cake counter at Kstadt, armed with a cake fork and a dazed look. But - hold on! In between stands a car ride - and, even worse - the search for the car keys. But this delay turns out to be a blessing - as mom's prophecy comes true. This sweet, soft cake aroma has successfully calmed my synapses - and peace returns. A desired placebo effect - so to speak. I feel satisfied - but not uncomfortably stuffed - and can enjoy the delicious scent. Even my husband buzzes around me kindly - and senses a "cozy" atmosphere. I can only agree.

The scent is many things, but for me, it is not primarily vanilla. That it would be synthetic, sure, no surprise, it could have been done well or interestingly synthetic, but this one is really rather strange. At the beginning: for me, caramel-chocolate plus hair conditioner, and a very penetrating waxy note comes to the forefront, (somehow also musty) that reminds me a lot of an old jar of lip balm that had been left open for too long. Then vanilla-strawberry scented candle. A bit of modeling clay. The "My Little Ponies" of my childhood; plastic and still that dull, waxy note, which I find really disgusting, but at least it gradually recedes into the background. Toasted American ready-made muffins come in later. Cold milk with sugary cereals. The wrist keeps coming back to the nose, just like ready-made products full of flavor enhancers can be addictive, but I would rather not wear this, just like one can feel disgusted after a binge on bad, artificial food. There are much better vanilla gourmands that smell tastier and/or more stylish.

Montale Vanilla Cake - a gourmand fragrance as it should be. A scent that already smells so sweet and strong from the sprayer that it almost knocks you over or makes you float on cloud nine. Upon the first sniff, it is clear what this is about: nothing other than juicy cake, the name says it all. This is not the case with every Montale, sometimes the names can be misleading. I find it difficult to categorize these scent nuances into a pyramid, as so much comes together at once: vanilla, sugar, cream, a bit of roasted almond, along with strawberry and cherry in between (even if not listed). It actually smells like a perfect strawberry tart made by grandma, prepared with love. On the side, a hot milk with honey makes this cozy winter dessert perfect. One is already full from smelling after just a few minutes :-) Vanilla Cake envelops the wearer in a strong sillage for quite a long time, which has the potential to fill an entire room. Perhaps for this reason, one should be cautious with the spray bursts. The fragrance hardly changes over hours and remains largely linear. The light fruity notes slowly fade over time, leaving behind a sugary vanilla base. Somehow, you can't keep your nose away from it; you’d prefer to constantly bite your arm. Yes, Vanilla Cake is definitely more feminine but can definitely be imagined as a unisex fragrance. Perfect for winter, perhaps for a date, Vanilla Cake is simply irresistibly tempting.

Upon my first sniff of the TZ with the sample, they immediately came to mind - those colorful gummy candies with a vanilla-milk aroma, shaped like cows. The manufacturer "T..." is probably not as popular as the two big competitors that start with "H" and "K," but they do have the most garish and likely the most synthetically tasting range.

Smells to me 1:1 like freshly baked vanilla cake, also in terms of sweetness. Incredible that this is possible, I was blown away the first time I smelled it, just like my boyfriend. My entry into the world of gourmands. I couldn't detect a significant scent evolution, which I personally prefer.

Today we are having guests from Mississippi. It's unusual for people to wander so far into our little village, but it makes sense when you know they want to participate in a special sporting event here in the region. For all our guests, I always bake a fixed but very fine cake as a welcome treat.

Warm and sweet and delicious, if I have to sum it up briefly. For those who have a bit more time: The scent gives me a feeling of security and coziness. This is probably because it smells almost exactly like the semolina pudding my mother often made for me. Especially in winter, when you have to go out into the cold early: a lifesaver.

I’m very sorry, but I unfortunately find this scent quite terrible. It smells like one of those vanilla air fresheners that you hang in your car. Extremely artificial and overpowering. I had hoped for more, as I am actually a huge vanilla fan, but this just doesn’t do it for me.

This perfume really sneaks up on you. Capeline was a perfume that I surprisingly disliked when I first smelled it, but now, I’m a huge huge fan of it. Capeline is a wonderful combination of lily and vanilla, with a bunch of supporting notes not too far off in the background. I mostly pick up on the ylang-ylang, sea notes, neroli, and musk here. I also slightly pick up on the vetiver, which adds a gentle aromatic touch to the overall scent. The opening is a bit disorienting, but once you give it a moment to settle, it’s really magical. It’s sweet, ever so slightly spicy, fresh, bright, but very complex and deep, all at the same time. It’s really incredible. My boyfriend usually likes a lot of my scents, but he was full on digging his nose into my neck when I had this one on and he kept saying how good I smelled. As to who this scent is for, I can’t say vanilla lovers will love this because lily really is the star of the show. But, I definitely think it’s worth a try for those that want to add something a little different to their collection. Capeline is so aptly named too. It smells like a sexy, freshly lotioned woman on an expensive boat / yacht, eating some sort of sweet, vanillic dessert after having gone for an afternoon dip. It’s giving luxury, it’s giving new money, it’s giving summertime fine somewhere out on the water. It’s just gorgeous really. And I LOVE the saltiness of the sea water note here. It just adds a beautiful salty and realistic touch to the scent. The performance on this is decent. moderate sillage and moderate to good longevity. Yes, the price tag is hefty, but for the size of the bottle and for the quality of the scent, I think it’s totally worth it. I think I’ll be wearing this a lot over the summer.

What a perfume! Now that's what I call a floral scent! After testing other fragrances from the "wardrobe line," my expectations were not too high due to the low success rate. But this one is anything but mediocre. Anyone who liked the floral scents of the 90s will also enjoy Capeline, as it is a relatively intense floral fragrance. The opening is dominated for just a few seconds by citrus fruits (bergamot, mandarin), after which the heart notes floral arrangement kicks in, igniting a scent fireworks of lily, ylang-ylang, and neroli. Very floral, somewhat lighter and sweet - which sets it apart from the heavy floral scents of the 90s. This combination, especially with the lily, is new to me yet somehow familiar. I do like lilies and find it a shame that their scent is increasingly being bred out in the floral industry. A fragrance lily is hardly available anymore. Yet lilies are noble and nostalgic and are used as floral decoration in English manor houses, so the smell of lilies combined with floor wax has a wonderfully antiquated scent. Well, Capeline does not smell like floor wax. In Capeline, the lily is not so dominant. No, it rather integrates, perhaps sometimes a bit reluctantly, into the floral community between ylang-ylang and neroli. Occasionally, it dares to flash through briefly but is quickly put back in its place by the others. But it doesn't give up. And so it remains a fine floral scent with a little presence of lilies. Unfortunately, after a rather short time, the flowers then quietly say goodbye and give the musk-vanilla base a little chance to say together with the wearer: "Come spray again, and we will return." And bam, they're all back. Charming. How one could come up with a floppy hat for this fragrance creation is a mystery to me. Because if it has to be a headpiece, then it could at least have been a little cocktail hat. Because this perfume is indeed something special. Elegant, feminine, and not everyday. It is not the green bouquet but the fully ripe, slightly sweetish bloom. Anyone who does not like oversized floral scents, or lilies in particular, or even gets headaches from them, should steer clear. Because flowers are the main actors here. For me, it is another enrichment of my fragrance world.

Don't worry, the scent is beautiful, so if you want, please continue reading: Capeline: means floppy hat...aha! Thanks to Parfumo, learned something new again, since obviously I wasn't paying attention in school, Google will do in a pinch. This term just doesn't fit the bottle, which contains a mauve-colored fragrance liquid, or perhaps that's precisely why. One would expect a darker, more bitter, and spicier scent, something with more melancholy (Sadness). A golden fragrance liquid (Summertime) would be more fitting, but that would be complaining at a high level, and only the content really matters here. And as soon as I get a whiff of this, I imagine summer, sun, beach, and sea...a scent for the warm season, but not a typical generic blend, rather a composition that expands the senses! Visually, it evokes a Grace Kelly driving along the coast in a convertible at sunset or, in contrast, a field full of sunflowers with a daisy in her hair, cruising through the Palatinate Forest in an old VW Beetle convertible! The lightness of being! I really like that kind of thing, and due to its gracefulness, I wear it for that reason. It works perfectly for petite brunettes in a Kia in the city on a dreary day! Opposites attract, as they say. Capeline is a mood booster, bringing sunshine to the heart, uplifting, and feels airy and well-groomed. You are always well "dressed"! Hence: La Vestiaire: "The Wardrobe"! The slightly citrusy start with bergamot and mandarin goes straight into a liaison with the largest and most beautiful summer bouquet I know. Once again, I can't figure out which bloom fascinates me so much, ylang-ylang or lily?! Nobody knows! In any case, the orange blossom is relatively tame; I also think I smell tuberose, but I'm probably mistaken. I'm just a fragrance novice, and I think in this case it really is ylang-ylang or simply this unique fragrance blend that ultimately settles into musk and non-edible vanilla. More of the woody scent of a fresh vanilla pod. Not too fresh, not too sweet, just perfectly composed! I am in love, so much so that I had to buy it despite the proud price. Capeline is actually not my usual type, but that's where the greatest love stories often build! Sometimes like in real life (I refer again to opposites). I have nothing to complain about regarding longevity and sillage; you leave a well-perceptible scent trail as you glide through the rooms, and it lasts on the skin easily 6-7 hours, if not even longer, as you can still catch a decent whiff in the evening since it holds up really well in hair and on clothing. I hope I could bring it a little closer to you through my description. Many thanks also to the lovely Parfuma, who got me hooked on this scent; otherwise, it would probably have flown under my radar. I urge you to test it, but I advise against overly eager blind purchases, as opinions can vary widely. Unfortunately, it's not so easy to find for sniffing samples; I ordered the full-size version in Belgium. With that said, I wish the community a wonderful weekend and let Capeline bring sunshine into the house, as the weather isn't so great!

I really enjoy this. It's a true honey, like cloudy set honey, with the pollen type musk, a little like Tokyo Milk - Honey and the Moon but less sweet. I don't really get what's Arabian about it. The date notes probably deepen it and make it richer but is indistinguishable. It's a well balanced honey musk, made a little fresher with bergamot and slightly floral due to the white flowers and pollen. More feminine leaning. I think overall it's a really well balanced fragrance. Arms length projection and fairly long lasting.

Arabians Musk has perhaps a misleading name: the connection is made undoubtedly to one of the mainstays of the brand, namely Arabians Tonka. Well I am sure saying that both fragrances have nothing in common, and personally they transport me into two completely different dimensions. Arabians Musk is the smell of oriental nights, of a walk surrounded by the aroma of orange blossoms, with their bitterish scent mingling with a barely noticeable sweetness of dates and notes that slowly become cleaner and cleaner. I think it has a very defined personality basically, it is a polarising fragrance, which definitely would appeal on those loving orange blossom and slightly oriental vibes, with a clean drydown but keeping the basic essence profile of the fragrance. A truly pleasant, elegant and decisive perfume. ‘The Thousand and One Nights by Vittorio Zecchin.

Sampling Montale Arabians Musk, released in 2024, the second flanker to Arabians (after Arabians Tonka), the original being one of my very favorites of the line. Like Arabians Tonka, Arabians Musk is a significant departure from the original, involving some honey and fruity but mostly a sharp, musky, woody blend that’s fortunately not too intense. I think it’s pretty well done, quite bright with the infusion of honey and dried fruits into a sharp woody experience, frankly better than what I would expect from the note breakdown, but it probably does not need to be connected to Arabians in name, as I do not sense much of a connection at all, scent-wise. It performs quite robustly, too. I doubt I’ll pursue it further myself, as its sharpness does not work for me as well as, say, the sharpness in the original (and quite different) Arabians.

Caught my attention just from the name. At first, it definitely feels more “Arabians” than “Musk.” It’s a pretty loud fragrance, but definitely pleasant if you’re into those notes. Honey and orange blossom really stand out, along with tonka bean. After about half an hour, the musk side kicks in and cleans up those warm vibes a bit, but paired with these notes (especially the lingering tonka bean), it’s not really my thing. Still, it’s really nice!! It’s a clean, Arabian-inspired scent. Totally different from the typical Montale DNA — that’s for sure! Perfect for cold months, but I’m starting to rediscover how some warm fragrances can actually work great on summer evenings too: cozy and intense.

As with the rest of the line, concentration is EDP and retail pricing is $180 for100ml, sold in the US via boutiques like Olfactif and Ministry of Scent, but also via the grey market, as is generally the case with most releases from this house. 7 out of 10

What did I hope for with the release of Arabians Musk? A more wearable Arabians Tonka . Less loud, less sweet, a similar DNA, but less in your face... The new Arabians Musk has little to no trace of the Arabians Tonka DNA. What do you get? A clean, sweet, creamy, powdery, elegant, and cozy fragrance that is definitely suitable for everyday wear.

Arabians Musk surprises me with a powdery and creamy scent that exudes pleasantly light baby powder vibes. The tonka bean is softly present without pushing itself to the forefront. For Montale standards, the fragrance is surprisingly harmonious and understated, making it perfect for everyday wear.

Yesterday it finally happened, my Arabians Musk that I ordered blind has arrived and I must say I am more than happy! For me, it is an absolutely beautiful powdery clean scent! If there is oriental cotton candy, then it has this smell.

I approached the fragrance with some skepticism after the initial reviews. Opinions on social media are also quite divided. I have now been able to test the fragrance and can already say that Arabians Musk has NOTHING to do with Arabians Tonka. I see the Musk here as an independent scent that does its job quite well at first impression.

Arabians Musk is a really great fragrance from the "gentle Orient". You can feel this relatively strong musk fluff, pleasantly sweetened with honey and date. Additionally, there is this orange blossom, but a really pleasant and fitting orange blossom. I absolutely cannot understand why the ratings are sometimes so low here.

Let me start by saying that I bought it, and ended up returning it. What happened? I first saw it and tried it, and in fact what got my attention the most, was the really good looking bottle. I tried it, and enjoyed it, a nice fresh scent, ZERO sweet, smells literally like a lemon gin. Gives you a frozen feel, mildly metallic from the ambroxan (or another of its forms). It’s actually quite pleasant for my nose. For the nose of others… not so much. It has a decent projection, although more of a skin scent, and normal longevity, around 6 hours (but spray it on clothes and it will last longer). Every time I asked someone if they liked it, it was “ok” at best… it reminds me a lot of the other Y, which I never loved, because of the sage note, but a much more frozen feel. The smell is very undistinguished, it could be anything really. In short, it wasn’t a fragrance that made me enthusiast about it, nor any of the people around me. In certain ways, it smells like an Invictus Aqua 2016, but not as good, in the way that it’s super synthetic… enjoyable, but the best thing about it, it’s the bottle. Returned it

"I know this one!" she said proudly.  "It's… Tobacco-Lemon!!!" I struggled hard. I don't know of a perfume with that name, Y Eau Fraîche doesn't smell like that to me, and I don't own a perfume with theses notes (aside maybe Lagerfeld Classic Eau de Toilette , but I believe it's not the two notes you'll have in mind with this one). But for the sake of love, I remembered just having lectured her a few day earlier about the playful grapefruit-cannabis accord in Mugler Cologne - Fly Away . My bad. Thou shalt not mansplain. But indeed she surely remembered this fragrance. I wore it a lot in summer 2022, where I emptied the most of my bottle of Y Eau Fraîche. I wore it during our nice trip in the country side of France, a holiday whose memory we both cherish. As for the fragrance, well, it opens fruity and very shower-gellish, a pleasant if not very original blue fragrance. The drydown is smoky, which makes it more standing out in my collection at least. I tried the Y Edp in stores and it seemed very close (with likely a better longevity?). The longevity is correct on me and I won't complain about the price as other reviewers as I got it for a cheap price (round 30€ for 60 ml, second-hand). All in all a fragrance I enjoyed in summer. Today I emptied my bottle and wrote at last this review. I won't buy a new bottle (which seem nowadays harder to find as it seems discontinued). I feel the need to move on, these days with "FR/18 | A.N Other" which my sweetheart enjoys too.

I grabbed this one because I like the Y line, and the hotter seasons are approaching the USA. It’s another one of those scents that you absolutely CANNOT buy unless you test it on your skin. Why, you ask? Well, on paper the Y dna does NOT show itself much, if at all, but on skin you immediately notice it, despite it being somewhat camouflaged beneath the lemon/citrus opening. Just this fact alone is absolutely HUGE, as it is an almost day to night change. DO NOT BASE YOUR DECISION ON WHAT THE STRIP GIVES YOU. Some might like the fact that there seems to be less Y dna (on paper), some may wish there was more. Spray it on the wrist and let it evolve. Now on my skin, here’s my opinion. I like the way this one smells, for the warm weather. There’s an almost “cooling” sensation that radiates from it, more so in the opening. A really strong lemon/citrus dominates the opening, together with a soapy feeling that it gives a fresh out of the shower vibe. It’s a very light, very bright sensation. Underneath this, you sense the Y edt dna. Not the EDP, but the original, soon to be reformulated EDT. It’s there, noticeably present, but almost as if that shower fresh vibe is stacked on top of it, rather than blended/mixed together. This may be good for some, but it will be bad for others. Note that that’s how it is. Forgive the analogy, but it’s like a wet white shirt. Imagine that as how the scents sit together. The soapy lemon/citrus is a thin white shirt that is soaked in water, and the Y edt is the wearer. That’s how it feels in the opening. As it dries down, the lemon fades away, and it becomes more of a soapy fresh, what feels like sky blue freshie. That light turquoise color in the sky on a bright sunny day; that’s the blue I get from it. The Y edt dna gradually makes itself more and more visible as time progresses into the base drydown. When it finally gets to the end, it’s that Y edt sitting there in a 60/40 ratio, but now blended together with the soapy turquoise rather than stacked underneath. Performance wise, this one is debated profusely. On my skin, it projects loudly in the opening, easily reaching 3ft of radius, but the projection dials back very quickly, to very soft 1ft bubble. Sillage trail does the same thing. Following you strongly for the first 1-2 hours, and then becoming almost nonexistent. Longevity on my skin, however, isn’t as terrible as most reviews say. I get an easy 6-8 hours, although the majority of it is a skin scent. A very noticeable, easily detectable skin scent. I don’t have to bury my nose into my skin to find it. Is it for everyone? No. Is it a blind buy? Absolutely not. Do I like it, and am I happy with it? Yes I am.

It's a nice scent, Fresh and Bold. This is the best fresh perfume that was launched in 2020 and the Y line! You can't go wrong with it. If you like Polo Blue and Acqua Di Gio, you will like this one. It opens up with like a clean citrus, ginger and slightly pepper then dry down is green woody. The art of bottle design is cool and it has frosted glass. This is the perfect fragrance for the spring and summer. It smells very pleasant like ocean breeze! I really enjoy it and I love Y Eau Fraiche. Highly recommended. Two Thumbs Up . Bravo YSL ! Rating : 9/10

A fun version of the Y-line, but if you own YSL Y EDP (which is the one that you actually should own), then prepare to be disappointed, as this does not have a strong projection nor smell as strong as that. Like, at all.... As a perfume for itself, it is a good designer perfume. Extremely fresh. Eau de Toilette is the concentration for this Eau Fraiche - just so you know. Perfect "young boy" perfume that is extremely fresh. I don't know many other perfumes that are this fresh. It's also a bit sweet. It only lasts 4-5 hours on skin, and the same on clothing. A bit disappointed, but the smell is so nice.

Y Eau Fraîche comes in a stylish compact bottle. Chic and beautiful. The scent offers no more and no less than one dimension. I like it. Although the floral accent of geranium is always present and almost destabilizes the fresh base concept, I find it cleverly resolved here. Mint and lemon compete for dominance, creating this successful combination.

As a huge fan of the Edp, I was very pleased with the fragrance sample that was included with my last order. I can say upfront that I really like this scent as well, possibly even more than the Edp (I still need to compare them more intensively), and in my opinion, the difference is significant enough to have both in the collection.

I am a big fan of the Yves Saint Laurent Y line. I like the EdP, the Live, and especially the EdT, and I am already looking forward to the new EdT that will be released soon. I searched for the Y Eau Fraiche for a long time and finally found it in Bielefeld at Galeria, at a good price (42€ for 60ml).

It was love at first sniff - the DNA of YSL Y. Sometimes you just smell something and it goes straight to the heart and not to the head. There was something about this blend of freshness/sweetness - the apple note and light citrus with a hint of synthetic - that captivated me.

Was disappointed with this when I first got it, as according to cardboard strip test, it seemed a bit sort-of - negligible, especially given the price-brackett. Earlier, I decided to give it a run out, havng °salvaged° other seeming disappointments by the simple expedient of actually wearing them, as opposed to cardboard-strip-testing them. I put it on - thought "where is it?". Ten minutes later "oh! it's there!". Twenty mnutes after putting-on "IT'S THERE!!". Half an hour after putting-on - it just won't give me any let-up!!! Seems to evolve in the opposite direction to what a more modest 'fume does. Not only sheer strength, but its nature & inner structure also. It's becoming a bit like when someone you thought was really bland & dull reveals to you that they've been to 27 countries, nearly died of cocaine addiction, been in prison for armed robbery, etc etc. I'll get back to you when I've completed its run-out. I've completed it's run-out now. I would like to digress a little into general principle. [Most of the rest of this is now in the thread ~Miscellaneous / Ultra-Expensive Perfumes~] Last night I ^did^ get ^a^ compliment. It's not surprising really, coz I was veritably honking of the stuff. It's seriously powerful stuff, if you can just ^let^ it be! And one might bear in mind that the spray mechanism tends to be ^particularly^ well-made on Roja Dove perfume bottles, and doesn't dispense a large amount per spritz. I'm wondering what to put on now, coz I'm going to the Sunday afternoon concert at the Whitworth Art Gallery; and, you know, I think I'd better use it again, as I'm still honking of it. What a remarkable transformation! I've gone from being cross at it for seeming to be rather a damp squib to being cross at it for not letting me try a different 'fume the folliwing day by virtue of its being too puissant!

The joy is immense. A dear perfumer has included a sample of Roja Perfums Lily with the fragrances I ordered from her. It is the first time I am testing a scent from Roja. When will I ever get to Harrods? That’s where The Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie resides. Of course, on the sixth floor. So close to heaven … This is what the British perfumer Roja Dove promises for his fragrances. They are supposed to make you feel the heavens - be silk and satin, crystal and black lacquer (?!) And they are supposed to smell like an exotic boudoir. Gulp, I think. Then they are probably not made for me. But I cling to the name: Lily … My favorite flower. It is not only beautiful but has one of the best scents I know. So I spray. Soon this wonderfully cool lily scent will envelop me. The anticipation rises. But what is this? No lily in sight. I only catch a very exotic-sweet scent that I immediately identify as “bewitching” - and thus a no-go for me. Indeed. It’s as if frangipani, ylang-ylang, geranium, tuberose, and tiare all attacked me at once. Jasmine en masse not to forget! Good thing I’m staying home today, I think, in light of this passionate tropical flower orgy that does not suit me at all. Strangely enough, such bewitching scents have been crossing my path repeatedly lately. Starting with Mukhallat by Montale, which is supposed to smell like strawberries. Now this game repeats itself with the nonexistent lily. How can you name a perfume Lily that doesn’t smell a bit like lily - and has no lily in the fragrance pyramid? But maybe Roja Dove dedicated the scent to a lady of that name and not to the sacred flower? In any case, all lily fans should be warned: It says Lily on the label, but it’s not inside. I double-check to make sure I really got the “right scent.” Yes, I did. Still no lily. What a shame! Alongside the ubiquitous frangipani, there are various opulent notes such as ylang-ylang, clove, musk, and vanilla, as well as the spice notes that I generally do not appreciate. In a word: Blech. Not for me. I’m glad I didn’t buy this scent. Because it is expensive. For 50 ml, you already have to shell out € 450,-. Or you can buy 100 ml for € 900,-. Of course, there’s no bulk discount with this luxury brand. Noblesse oblige. But one must look at it positively: Luckily, I don’t have to grapple with whether I can afford this scent or not. At the beginning, lemon and bergamot were supposed to make their refreshing appearance. But they don’t show up for me either. It starts right away with sensual, exotic, floral, and sickly sweet. Lush hypnotic white flowers, too penetrating and intense for me. I try to find something in this scent that justifies its high price. Does it seem particularly elegant, particularly precious, noble, extraordinary, innovative, perfect? null of that. It doesn’t give me an aha moment. I realize: I am not the right person to judge Lily because I simply do not like this overtly exotic overload - not even as a room scent or fabric softener. Shake! Surely there are ladies who like Lily. Even without the lily. Unfortunately, I also don’t perceive any of the beloved lily of the valley. But they would get lost in the tropical frenzy anyway. I feel sorry for everyone who likes this scent, but for me, it has something cheap about it, no matter how expensive it is. It’s that typical, intrusive, hypnotic, supposed-to-be-sensual tropical flower scent that I can’t really imagine on an elegant lady with class. But, as is often the case, it’s a matter of taste. Maybe some ladies feel like queens with it. Who knows? Not me … Aside from whether one swoons over bewitching tropical flowers or not - the scent has something smooth, superficial, lifeless about it and doesn’t change much. It is not an intellectual challenge. Not even a thought-provoking idea or inspiration. The longevity is strong. It takes a long time for the drydown to come within nose range. Will Lily develop that sweetness I wished for from the beginning as it fades? Unfortunately no. Even in this final phase, Lily remains opulent to the point of excess. I would say the scent is made for women who like to stand out and be the center of attention. The evening scent of a diva for grand appearances: galas, festive balls, Oscar ceremonies, festivals, opera visits … Opera visits?! Oops! I hope I don’t have to spend my next opera visit (I like Wagner…) next to a lady who is wearing Lily.

I love clean musk fragrances. But in a sea of variations on a common theme, I don't think the stars will ever align for me on this one. It is quite unremarkable. Does it smell good? Yes, totally decent. Outstanding sillage and if the Body Shop White Musk isn't loud enough for you- check this out, for sure! White Musk is all that it can be- fresh, light, synthetic a little powdery and green. It is in that safe zone of clean side musky perfect for day wear- it's not too sweet or cloying and it is unisex for sure. But unexceptional for the house of Montale. I was so excited on my fragrance journey to encounter the complete line of currently available Montale scents, with so many raves about "Intense Cafe", "Fruit of the Musk", "Red Aoud" and others...I almost forgot to sample this one, inspite of my core love for White Musks. Well, that would have been no major crime, in this case. White Musk is somewhere on that spectrum of things I can live with or with out- or can be easily substituted in my olfactory directory. Sometimes when I walk into a great fragrance boutique I play a quick mental game called "Zombie Apocalypse Must Have Fragrances" (I know that seems ridiculous on so many levels- but, it's fun!). The rules of the game are quite simple- 1.It's a Zombie Apocalypse 2. You need to grab 3 fragrances to last you until the next supply run from the safe house where you'll be hold up with the rag-tag band of strangers and no running water, indefinitely. 3. Someone else is taking care of the essential survival supplies like food, water and antibiotics- You and you alone are incharge of the fragrances.) Which 3 do you grab? Well...o.k. so, all that to say, Montale White Musk never even came close to making the short list from Montale.Since they are all in that similar metalic spray bottle, I will eventually fall prey to one of them and it will eat my brain, I'm sure- but today I escape to the safety of the compound with "Chocolate Greedy". Hey everyone, we can survive on the smell of Chocolate for a month, right?

Not being much for big musk perfumes, I have been pleasantly surprised by Montale WHITE MUSK. The name is perfect because the musk is really very clean and pure. I barely smell any flowers at all, but I have noticed that the musk in this composition appears to be similar to that used in Chanel NO 5. Now that everyone uses synthetic musk, there may be more convergence among musk perfumes than there were back in the olden days when unsuspecting musk deer were "relieved" of parts of their anatomy in order to satisfy wealthy people's desire for luxurious perfume. The question becomes: if every house from Jovan to Montale is using synthetic musks to make their musk solinote perfumes, then why in the world would anyone choose the most rather than the least expensive of the available offerings? Not being a musk connoisseur, I have to admit that I do not know the answer to the question! I did notice today that the remnants of By Kilian LOVE AND TEARS, which I found to be a rather hum-drum and dry jasmine soliflore, mingle quite nicely with the Montale WHITE MUSK. To make sure that I was not misinterpreting the Montale, I also tested it on the back of my hands. It's a clean white musk, no question about that. What I'm still not sure of is whether I like it better than The Body Shop WHITE MUSK. Well, I happen to have some of their perfume oil here somewhere, so let me go find out the answer to the question right now. I'll be back in a jiffy... I'm back. There's actually a huge difference. The Montale WHITE MUSK is smooth and creamy and clean, while The Body Shop smells somewhat sharp and soapy. I definitely prefer the Montale, and recognize now that not all synthetic musks are created--or combined--alike!

Kleos Musk Series Part 20 When I was still searching for the perfect musk fragrance and because the comments appealed to me, I ordered a sample of this scent from ALzD at that time. This is a bright, powdery, clean, completely unsweetened musk scent that does not undergo much development. It remains largely as you spray it. I do not detect the indicated flowers, and I actually find that a pity in this case, as a little bit of pep would have done this fragrance good. I perceive it as neither warm nor cool. Unlike many other white musks, this one has no synthetic note, and the longevity is more than remarkable. Conclusion: Personally, I find White Musk too one-dimensional, but sometimes you might want exactly that. I also think it would be great for layering. It reminds me quite a bit of Muschio Bianco by Tesori d’Oriente, which is available for considerably less money, although it cannot compete with the longevity and has a synthetic note at the beginning. I do not find this Montale fragrance bad at all, but it would not be a candidate for purchase for me.

I received the White Musk by Montale as a sample from a dear perfumer. This fragrance has prompted me to write my first comment on Parfumo. Not because I can unconditionally surrender to it, but because it divides me mercilessly. Rarely does a scent manage to be both hated and loved by me. Therefore, I would like to share my experience with you. My expectations for this fragrance were quite high, according to the comments. It was supposed to be a clean, white, pleasant scent. Something to wrap myself in, to feel cozy. When it finally arrived, I sprayed it on with anticipation. But right from the start, my nose wrinkled: "Wow, eww, what is that supposed to be?? Musk?! I don't really know it like this... Smells so stale and somehow weird." I was very disappointed and turned to the other samples, mentally having already written off this scent and physically having released it to the Souk. "Get rid of it! I can't do anything with this, yuck." However, I left the sprayed test strip lying there. "You never know what else might come." A few hours later, I went back to it and smelled, "Hmmm, now it's not so bad. Actually quite good. I think I have to keep it after all!" Quickly went online, deleted it from the Souk. In the evening, I ponder what perfume I might wear tomorrow. "My boyfriend smells bad at the moment, so it can't be anything too special, I want to save that for him ;) But I do want to wear something nice tomorrow... hmmm... let's consider the White Musk, who knows." This morning, I rushed back to the strip and decided, "Wow, that smells good, THIS IS IT!" Sprayed it on and again had a strange feeling: "Where do I know this strange scent from...? I like it. Don't I? Or do I??" Then a lightbulb moment hit me: "I know where I know it from!" A long time ago, I experienced a fire in the basement of our apartment building. Everything that was in that old wooden structure was, even if only partially, scorched or burned. Many of my old toys, stuffed animals, and children's clothing did not survive the fire. But what survived, we washed with very strong soap (I think it was gall soap, in case any of you know it :) ). THAT is the smell! It is the smell of the soap that washed some of my things clean again, with which I also associate misfortune and fire. I think that is the reason why this scent divides me. Why I love and hate it. Why I perceive it in such a distorted way. To me, it has something soapy, pure, soft, but also something rough, penetrating, even smoky... And that's why it deserves a comment from me. I am wearing it today. And today I love it. Who knows what tomorrow will bring.

Today was the day of the often postponed dentist visit. For me, it’s always a trip to Canossa. I hate the rummaging around in my mouth, and I would rather take a nap for a reasonable fee in such matters. But today I wanted to be brave. Well, what can I say - after the ordeal, I had sweated through two shirts - my doc did too. I was too exhausted for a subsequent spa visit at the perfumery, so I wobbled homeward and blindly reached into the fragrance wonder bag. I sniffed, and my trembling slowly subsided. I had grabbed Montale White Musk - the purest nerve balm. Creamy and trustful, musk embraces the skin, and to enhance its gentle message, it has brought along a lovely violet. The geranium blooms softly above it, paired with slightly bitter ylang-ylang. Alongside the smooth creaminess, there’s also soft powder - and my breathing calmed down. White Musk is the perfect wave smoother - the longed-for calm after the storm. And although I’m not particularly fond of unisex fragrances, it fits like my soft nappa leather glove. For me, it’s not a going-out scent - but an introspective one. I think a larger bottle would be worthwhile.

Montale creates strong fragrances. Not always in terms of quality, let alone creativity, I’m just saying Oud, but almost all have power & punch. This is no different with a musk fragrance that goes by the delicate name "White Musk." Even such an airy scent can be transformed by the French masters of quantity. Understatement is foreign to Montale.

Ahhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh! What have I been missing with this wonderful fragrance?! Through the lovely powderiness, I immediately see myself sitting on a little cloud, legs dangling and simply enjoying. Somewhere in the distance, fairies dance with flowers in their hair, performing a round for me, but I just stay here, on my fluffy cloud, letting everything happen around me.

I have been looking for a good fragrance for a while now, one that I can wear in casual settings or at the office, a scent that is clean and fresh while not overwhelming my surroundings too much. Ideally, something floral, not citrusy, and also unisex.

Yes, thank you GiuliaSofia for this wonderful sample. I first tested the Musc from Reminiscence, which I also liked quite a bit. But in terms of longevity and powderiness, it cannot compete with White Musk at all. White Musk is a floral fresh musk scent with delicate, slightly sensual undertones.

Nivea, shower gel, hand lotion, dish soap, soap, all these scent associations come to mind for me and my surroundings after spraying Montale White Musk. When I found a sample in my package, the expectations were quite high, especially regarding longevity and projection, but more on that later.

A wonderful scent with a sadly rather subdued sillage. Once again, as with so many Roja women's fragrances. However, this also makes the fragrance versatile. For an occasion where you want to smell great but not stand out negatively, like in the office. Or even at the first meeting with the in-laws or other family events. Not an offensive seducer, but rather a sweet and cheerful flatterer that brings a certain depth in the base. The dominant note here is peach. A velvety powdery peach embedded in a softly citrus floral bouquet. Beneath it lurks something dark and seductive. Delicately intertwined dark, real vanilla bean specks. Along with musk, which becomes slightly dirty together with amber. Patchouli and sandalwood are very restrained here. This base is super attractive. Once the citrus opening settles, an authentically scraped vanilla pod emerges. Everything now feels deliciously sweet-creamy, a bit like a cup of peach melba cream ice cream. An all-around good, successful fragrance with a clear progression that develops wonderfully. The fruity peach reminds me of Cassili by Parfum de Marly. Only, Cassili has a significantly stronger performance, both in terms of sillage and longevity. Hugo Boss The Scent also comes to mind, but it seems less complex. Actually, I haven't come across anything comparable to Enigma, apart from the various fragrance concentrations of Enigma offered by Roja. If you like floral peach cream vanilla ice cream and are looking for a calm, unexcited, but modern fragrance of good quality, you might want to give this a try. I like it very much overall.

The new Opium is a magical work of mimicry. How do you create an Oriental perfume of orange and rose layered over a heavy cloud of myrrh, clove, and spicy carnation - without using the key ingredient eugenol, that makes up a huge amount of the composition? You don't. You use things that point to the same smell, the same tone, that haven't been indicated as causing issues. So: We have a juicy citrus opening with bergamot. Then, instead of the clove, carnation, and cinnamon rosy floral, we go straight into myrrh and jasmine. Sweet warmth, yet without the heavy, spicy weight of the mid of original Opium. Then we dry down with light, ambery-floral sweetness, instead of the almost choking, not quite sweet, and extremely opaque cloud of woods in original Opium. Luckily, the new version lasts quite long, though not as eternally as the original Opium, and with less projection - but still detectable at 5 hours. There are differences in the consistency of the juice, too: the original Opium Eau de Toilette from the splash bottle is thick with oils and slightly greasy to the touch. The new one is not. The color of the old version is slightly darker amber, but this might be down to the difference in ages. The result is still recognizably Opium, and extremely beautiful. Is it the same? No. It's a stripped down, less antagonistic version. I'm glad we still have this, and I'll spray it with abandon. If the ingredients are not too scarce, and the issue is simply sensitivity, I'd gladly buy the original, more dangerous formula of Opium with a warning label attached. Although - maybe if things were different, and YSL had stuck to the original version, there would not be enough popularity to warrant Opium's continued production. And that's a world I don't want to live in. Perhaps Opium needed this update. Although I love it for exactly this reason, original Opium is as big and outrageous as the 80s themselves, and I see how it could feel dated, choking, or offensive to people in 2025. So, I will have and treasure my beloved bottle of Opium original for special occasions, and I will continue to enjoy my modern Eau de Toilette. One is the queen, one is the princess, both are lovely.

So far I have tried the current Eau de Parfum, and the vintage, and I find this version quite good. I would actually say that the Eau de Parfum is a smoother and deeper version of this but this version does have a spiciness that reminds me more of the vintage classic fragrances like Cinnabar and the classic Opium etc. I don't feel that this version projects as strongly though, and I think I would recommend the modern Eau de Parfum as a stronger choice. However, I do see this one as a more wearable unisex leaning fragrance, as opposed to the Eau de Parfum.

I love that they update classic scents and make them more palatable for the younger generations. This Opium is just perfect. It has no sticky sugary sweetness of Black Opium but neither it smells dated. My 14 y.o. said it smells like you mean business and ready to conquer the world. I thought she would get scared of it, but she actually appreciated it.

I remember Opium from the past when I was young and always found it a bit too 'obvious' and 'distinct' and so I wore Youthdew by Estee Lauder. I tried the newest formulation of Youthdew some time ago and, though I hate complaining about reformulations (because they often are done for a good cause, due to IFRA regulations), I missed the bright and 'funny' cocacola note in the newest composition. Well here it is! Opium (2009) Eau de Toilette is much brighter, playful and interesting than in the past to my nose and, though it is a different scent, I really get some 'youthdew vibes' by smelling some cocacola in here. I also find it a bit more 'soapy' than the former formulation, that well groomed feel I get from it while still wearing something mystical (I struggle to find a synonym for 'oriëntal' because I know that's a controversial word), is pure bliss. I guess the fresh bergamot and mandarin do that. I find it way more authentic and versatile than the former one also. I sprayed some on my wrist the other day and....OMG..the way it behaved in the cool, late summer air when I came outside...So lovely! Ran straight back to the shop to get me a sample. The myrrh is so beautyful, the way I always imagined what it would smell like when, in Bibleclass, the teacher would tell us about the gifts from the three wise men from the east when Jesus was born (I'm agnostic, but always loved many Bible stories in class). A rich, ancient scent, but nowhere near 'dated'. Sillage and projection are good as well as longevity. May buy a full bottle when I finished my sample.

The new Opium mix from 2009 is not Opium. It is more a beautiful yet different mix of an oldie but goodie. It is way more feminine than the original an in my opinion a bit more uninteresting. This is both good and nice - but it does not have the same aura or ‘in your face’ attitude as Opium. 235/365

This question has surely been asked more than once. What a huge uproar went around the world when the "real and only" Opium was launched in 1977. Loved, demonized, and cursed, leading to a massive outcry over the name.

To get straight to the point: I love oriental perfumes - at least many of them. Not all, of course. They have to suit me. That means they should be soft and cuddly, sweet with jasmine, roses, and vanilla, mysteriously balsamic, perhaps nuanced with noble wood notes from agarwood. In this sense, I like Casmir by Chopard, Obsession by Calvin Klein, and especially Shalimar.

Today, in this sweltering heat, my friend and I dragged ourselves through the flea market, our eyes still sharp, searching for bargains or curiosities. My friend lingered at every stall - from cute plush toys to lumbar supports, and I let out more than a few sighs.

After finishing half a bottle of the currently available Opium EdT, I would like to write a short comment about it. In 2009, the old Opium was replaced by this version. Many Opium lovers were greatly disappointed with this diluted version. I also had to get used to this new Opium at first. However, I still gave Opium 2009 a chance.

... write a comment about Opium. Apparently, I want to. But I haven't written comments in a long time and I'm not quite sure what to say. I don't have a touching story and I'm not particularly gifted in poetry. I just want to praise my new acquisition a little. After testing, I decided on the Eau de Toilette. It really packs a punch.

One of the best patchouli based scents that i have ever tried. Opening is raw and earthy and takes a while to settle down. Then join the vanilla and make it creamy and sweeter - thats the moment it remembers me of Coromandel. Projection is huge and also the sillage and lasting power (over 12hs). Updated January 2014

The earthy aspect of patchouli, and the warm stone-scent aspects of cistus labdanum are the thread that joins these two key players in Patchouli Leaves. Sweetness isn’t hidden, but certainly isn’t pushed to the front. I find the patch that is there exactly the viscous, hippy patch that I was looking for. But it’s perfectly matched by amber, vanilla, and musk, which might make it sound candy sweet, but it isn't. They serve to add a rounded, cushioned feel. The whole fragrance reads like patchouli on a stack of pillows.

Montale PATCHOULI LEAVES offers a lot of dark oily hippie patchouli in a luscious labdanum-amber base with just a touch of sweetness. Wearing this perfume is like wearing an old worn-out sweater that feels cozy and comfortable and even cuddly but is not something that I'd want to don in public. It seems somehow too personal and too suggestive for anywhere but home. I cannot help chuckling at the reviewer (at another site) who said that this would be great--were it not for the patchouli! I realize that some people do have a patchouli problem, but I think that the name in this case is a sufficent red flag... Recommended for patchouli lovers and hippies, this perfume has excellent longevity and smells totally groovy!

What prevents me to loving this is the heavy amount of amber as the opener the amber had a bit of an curdled smell but that my only compaint. of course you've got patchouli but it drowns in a wet saturated sea of oils but want makes it dry is the Labdanum with the deep fiery smokey scent plays a part of this fragrance and the animalistic spots of Musk and the drydown of vanilla.

Out of the vaguely familial group of ambery, vanillic patchoulis, I find Patchouli Leaves to be one of the most satisfying and comforting. The marketing copy for this boasts that the patchouli leaves for this fragrance were first soaked in vanilla extract and then left to macerate for two whole years in an oak barrel. The top notes, consisting of insanely rich but dry patchouli that has a raisin-like booziness to it, like aged cognac, suggest that this might in fact be true. The dark, boozy patchouli is joined very quickly by a buttery, warm vanilla and amber that serve to sweeten the mix. All in all, the impression is of a warm, golden river of almost drinkable, spiced brown patchouli, boozy vanilla, and thick amber. In fact, Patchouli Leaves is easily the friendliest patchouli fragrance out there. It is mouth-wateringly good; almost gourmand in a way. The amber is slightly resinous, adding at parts a slight roughness to break up the smooth vanillic undertow and a touch of powder towards the end. This is not for people who like their patchoulis raw or as they might say, 'authentic', since the patchouli here has been shorn of its claws and stripped of its menace. But my God, it is sexy and rich and as comfortable as putting on a great big woolly sweater over your work clothes when you come in from the rain.

Because it is POTENT!!! Feels like a patchouli field is growing in your nose if you spray too much. I blind bought this (my second attempt at trying Montale), and I just don’t think this brand fits my style. Don’t get me wrong, it IS indeed what it claimed to be; a patchouli bomb that resonates quite proudly. Now will you ENJOY the explosion? That is the question….

My husband loves patchouli and likes really strong fragrances because his sniffer doesn’t work very well so I have been looking for a strong *clean* patchouli perfume for awhile now that I could wear for date night. Yes, this is strong. 100% patchouli. Mostly clean, but still has a dirty, sharp earthy undertone that lessens as it dries down.

You can't make patchouli smell softer than this. A composition, a masterpiece! The smoky-earthy scent of patchouli is elevated to airy heights by vanilla and amber, like white clouds in the sky. If they could smell, it would be like this. And you float for a long time, even throughout the whole night.

What’s going on here? I really love patchouli scents, but this one is the second in this fragrance direction that doesn’t fade even after repeated washing, following "White Patchouli" by Tom Ford, which I was already not happy with. So the topic of longevity is already settled: it seems to have been designed with the motto "forever" in mind.

As a pharmacist who learned in a time when herbal drugs were still filled from large wooden barrels, the scent of pure herbal patchouli is, of course, a lasting memory for me. By the way, patchouli was bought back then to drive moths away from fur coats.

Only few words can describe Dark Aoud: heavy, dense, linear, raw. It's a very unidimensional scent: sandal, oud and musk from the beginning to the end. Also there's a tiny note of incense (maybe frankincense due to the small sweetness that appears after some hours). There's no comparision with other sandalwood bases fragrances: this is totally different. If i could compare, i would say Bois des Iles is a little small bird and this is a hungry hyena. Sillage, lasting power and projection are hazardous. One of the best Montale releases so far.

Dark Aoud is one of my favorite fragrances. Obviously, the scent is woody and Sandalwood seems to stand out the most. As far as woods and Aoud, this one doesn't seem to be very harsh and leaves a very nice trail. Sillage and Longevity are outstanding. Don't overspray this one or you'll clear a room out.

A rather linear (not a negative thing), yet beautiful blend of truly dark, somewhat medicinal aoud and sandalwood. Aoud lovers will almost certainly like this. I like it myself. I can imagine waring this in colder months of the year, and maybe at night, which in my opinion goes well with the dark mood the scent creates. I do not think Dark Aoud is feminine at all, but that does not mean ladies should not try... Longevity is great, projection is very good. Very interesting!

When a piece of metal is cooled to well below freezing, say by dipping it in liquid nitrogen, it becomes capable of burning the skin, paradoxically enough. It's not really a burn but a freeze, but it has the same damaging effect and the pain is probably very similar as well. Upon donning Montale DARK AOUD, I was struck by the unbelievable density of this composition. It's so black that it could easily induce the olfactory equivalent of white spot afterimages. For a brief period, I was even struck by what seemed to be a dark shoe polish-like scent. This is incredibly woody, including oudy, but it is also very dense and thick, as though the wood has been compressed to one-tenth its starting volume. I initially thought that I was smelling the base of so many recent launches, and I do continue to believe that there is significant overlap with, for example, Le Labo ANOTHER 13 and Balmain CARBONE, but DARK AOUD pulls out all of the stops in its quest for absolute blackness, and the result is somehow better not worse. I suppose that I can tolerate this woodishness in an exaggerated dose because it's not clobbering everything else around. Why? Because there *is* nothing else around: no flowers, no fruits, no citrus, no sweetness or light--nothing mitigating at all. This is deep, dark wood in every form, from fresh hewn to petrified. To me, this is obviously a masculine perfume, and I'm not surprised to see that although it is classified as unisex, three times more gents than ladies own this prince of darkness.

I may be anosmic to some components (I am very skeptical about “selective anosmy”, though) but I don’t get anything “dark” here, not even by mistake. And no oud either, but that’s no surprise with Montale offerings. Dark Aoud seems to me a very inoffensive, quite pleasant, slightly boring and extremely artificial cedar-sandalwood scent with a polite, understated, mannered dry look – almost minimalistic, in some way. It feels very clean, slightly earthy-herbal too, with a mild touch of spices to add a delicately sparkling edge to the core woody galore. That’s it. No oud, not even a synthetic hint of that, and no darkness for me, at all. Quite the opposite, actually (you know what scent Dark Aoud reminds me of, if any? A Quiet Morning by Miller et Bertaux). Despite the criminally misleading name and a certain feel of flatness it’s a decent scent though, almost nice - a very clean and discreet everlasting woody blend with no particular sparks of interest, but effortlessly enjoyable. A very safe and versatile workhorse, I guess. One of those clean, generic “IKEA-like” woody scents, just with some spices and an eau de parfum strength and longevity. Not exactly the catchiest scent around and definitely overpriced, but there’s worse than this. 5,5-6/10

This is very one-note for me. Even if you love woodsy Aoud smells (as I do) I have to kindly advise you against this one. It's so overpowering and offensively spicy. This much pine smell belongs in only one place: the sap dripping directly onto the bark of a pine tree.

It looks a lot like lattafa qaa'ed, but a little more refined and darker variant. In the drydown everything combines with something from Asdaaf (Lattafa)Majd al Sultan Brown. Spicy cardamom, sandalwood and oud are the notes that give personality to this fragrance. If you find it at 40 Euro is worth it , if not, the Arabic alternatives are quite ok for 15-20 Euro.

This is a good smell. Slightly encre noir, slightly duro but not much. It's masculine and warm, woody. Longevity is decent, 10 hours plus. But it's not strong, it's veeeery mild and close to the skin. Unfortunately. If it were a powerhouse as is expected from Montale, it could be very very good. At 2x strength. As it is, it's a good skin scent.

One may have their opinions about Montale and its flood of similar perfumes, mostly Oud-heavy, but at least you know what to expect. Especially in terms of longevity and sillage, there is never anything to complain about. When you take the deodorant-like bottles in hand and press the sprayer - you know that you will smell like this for the rest of the day.

Finally, a Montale perfume has made it into my collection. During my stroll yesterday along Düsseldorf's Kö, I had to make a stop at Schnitzler as usual. After I had already sniffed several scents on test strips by myself, I told the saleswoman to recommend me an extraordinary oud fragrance.

I'm working my way through the Roja Women's Sample pack and I have to say I am surprised by how much I like Scandal. Although maybe I shouldn't be, because I do love white florals...And for me, Scandal is just a really good white floral. The Lily of the Valley, Gardenia and Jasmine are very clean, green and fresh -- almost laundry detergent-esque but the absence of aldehyde stops it from veering to hard into the laundry scent. Overall, this is an unabashedly feminine scent. The combo of tuberose and sandalwood really add a lovely creamy soft base. However like most Roja scents, my skin seems to eat them up and the longevity is maybe not the best. However the scent is so pretty I am not sure it matters. That said, if I were to buy a full size Roja bottle based off the sample pack it would be either Scandal or 51.

This is a real gem of a fragrance. They named it perfectly by calling it "M7 Fresh", and it really is like a fresher, lighter, summer version of M7. This was when Tom Ford was still in control with YSL, and he oversaw some of their best work in my opinion. M7 Fresh opens up with beautifully fresh sour and tangy citrus, and this stays for a long time. What I love about it, is that it has a ginger note. It reminds me a lot of South-East Asian cuisine (specifically Vietnam). If you've ever had Vietnamese food (especially Vietnamese salad), this is what it reminds me of. Fresh lemon and sour grapefruit, with hot spicy ginger. It's a really beautiful combination. Yes, there is Oud (Agarwood) in here, but it's toned down. In the original M7 the Oud was syrupy and dominating... a darker note mixed with incense and burnt spices. Here it's in the background, mixing with the hot ginger to give it a tangy, medicinal aspect (some people say like traditional Chinese medicine). I feel that if the original M7 is like the smell inside an old Asian Buddhist Temple, this is the smell inside a Vietnamese kitchen (preparing lunch or breakfast), specifically the smell of fresh fruits and green salad components. I really miss this fragrance, YSL discontinued a lot of the Tom Ford era stuff. But I feel that there is other similar fragrances out there if you want to experience this lost gem. It's basically a Citrus-Oud combination, with an emphasis on fresh Citrus rather than the smoky wood. To me it smells like Vietnam. I love it!

Everyone knows what is Oud at this point. But back in 2004, only YSL and Tom Ford did knew what it was, and they wanted to spread the word to the world. M7 (2002) was a groundbreaking fragrance and put Oud on the map (although is more an accord rather than the material itself). 2 years later, they came out with a fresh interpretation of it, and they nailed it, again. OK, M7 fresh is kinda predictable in terms of what you'd expect as a fresh flanker of M7, but it's very well made. Jacques Cavallier knows how to do a good and original fresh fragrance. It starts with a big dose of fresh and bitter citruses. Bergamot and Mandarin orange play a big role here. A dance between the juicy sweet mandarin and the bitter green bergamot. After this initial burst, that lasts about 10min, there's some aromatic nuances that i can't put my nose on. Maybe ginger mixed with the citruses makes this aromatic facet shines but it's only there for this transition between the opening and the mid, which is all about grapefruit, and the "oud" accord of the original, which in here, is very toned down and in the background of the composition. This is a citrus woody aromatic fragrance with the added "oud" accord twist. It's pretty much it. In the drydown, there's vetiver but just supporting the fragrance and make it last a bit more. Talking about lasting power, the fragrance lasts pretty long to be honest. Not a beast in terms of projection (Just average to good in the first hour or so) but will linger for the whole day. 8+ easily. I'm enjoying this one a lot and i'm glad i picked up a bottle but i do not recommend paying the online prices that we see on ebay, amazon, etc... Around 60-70€ would be a great deal but not more than that. The grapefruit-vetiver combination reminds me a bit of L'Homme Ideal Cologne. Not so fresh and almondy but in the same vein. Overall, a fresh and citrus take on M7, as you'd expect, but very delightful. A sunny oud, as bashke81 said below. I love it and will be a good companion this spring/summer time. 4/5

A lighter version of M7. The grapefruit note is blended almost to perfection in this flanker. It definitely stands out from the crowd and if you want to smell different try this one. It is so sad that it has been discontinued. That being said you can still find it for reasonable price. A masterpiece from YSL. Scent: 10/10 Longevity: 7/10 Sillage: 6/10 Uniquness: 10/10 Price: 5/10

The Naked Truth “I know that I have advanced fashion and opened up a previously forbidden universe for women. I simply have a gift. It is mysterious, but nature has given me a talent: to know, to feel what women desire. And at the right time. I don’t need to go out and travel for that. I just have good antennas. Nothing is more beautiful than a naked body. The most beautiful garment a woman can wear is the embrace of a man who loves her. And for those who do not find this happiness, I am here!” (Yves Saint Laurent) And with a naked body, the life of “M7” also began. Although it was not a naked woman but a naked man. He really showed everything and thus distracted a bit from what he was actually advertising: At the center of the campaign should actually be “M7,” a men’s fragrance by Yves Saint Laurent. In 2002, under the direction of Tom Ford, who was Creative Director of the Yves Saint Laurent house from 1999 to 2004, one of the first perfumes with oud was created. And even though the advertising campaign with the naked penis caused quite a stir (let someone claim that there’s nothing “off the rack” at YSL), the strongly scented oil with the unusual name was actually the special thing about M7. “No one had used it until then, no one knew it,” reports Alberto Morillas, one of the two perfumers who created M7 at the time, alongside Jaques Cavallier-Belletrud, in an interview with “Die Zeit,” “and it still has something magical.” In Arabia, however, this intense fragrance material, derived from the resin of the agarwood tree, has been known for over 2000 years: there, the resin infected by a specific combination of fungi has long been used and is even attributed with aphrodisiac effects. At Yves Saint Laurent, they refrained from mentioning oud in the advertising campaign for “M7” in 2002. The scent was obviously meant to speak for itself. With the new concept from 2011, this changed: “M7” became part of the noble series “La Collection Yves Saint Laurent,” and since then, the bottle has also read “M7 Oud Absolu.” “The oil has something animalistic, woody, but at the same time modern,” perfumer Morillas is quoted. “It smells warm and sexy and always different. I dream of creating more oud fragrances.” The selection has since become almost overwhelming: After Yves Saint Laurent, numerous manufacturers followed with their own oud creations. But, as so often, Yves Saint Laurent was once again ahead of his time: Yves Henri Donat Mathieu-Saint-Laurent was born on August 1, 1936, in Oran, Algeria. He passed away on June 1, 2008, in Paris. He was an internationally renowned French fashion designer who founded the fashion house “Yves Saint Laurent” in Paris in 1961. He was referred to during his lifetime by the professional world as a “revolutionary” of fashion design. He had a significant impact on the fashion world and is still reverently called a luminary in the field of high-end and elegant women’s fashion after his death. He began his career as an assistant to Christian Dior and embodied like few other designers the French haute couture fashion. His greatest influence came in 1967 with his creation of a pantsuit for women (“Le Smoking”), which elegantly and matter-of-factly showcased the female form and thus also had an emancipatory effect. The company and thus the brand Yves Saint Laurent, or YSL for short, still exist today and have been owned by the Gucci Group since the end of 1999, which was gradually acquired by the French PPR Group from 1999 to 2004. The company offers high-priced prêt-à-porter clothing for women and men, as well as leather goods, shoes, watches, jewelry, glasses, accessories, perfumes, and cosmetics in the luxury goods segment through its own network of boutiques and high-end retail worldwide. The chief designer of all fashion collections has been Hedi Slimane since March 2012. Under Slimane, the fashion division was renamed “Saint Laurent Paris” in 2012, while the company itself continues to operate as “Yves Saint Laurent S.A.S.” Regarding the “M7” from 2002, it is noted here on “Parfumo” that Alberto Morillas and Jaques Cavallier-Belletrud initially used real oud. Allegedly, a large quantity could be purchased cheaply in 2000, which was then used in conjunction with the synthetic replica “Oud Synthetic 10760 E” developed by “Firmenich” at the request of Yves Saint Laurent. This was aimed at covering certain undesirable properties of oud. When the supplies ran out, only the substitute material was used until the fragrance was temporarily discontinued in 2009. In any case, production apparently only began when “Firmenich” delivered the synthetic oud base in September 2002. The “M7” created in 2002 (and kindly provided to me in a sample) begins fruity. Mandarin and a bit of bergamot. But the ripe and dark mandarin is in the foreground. There is another note as well. The often mentioned “cola note” is something I can very much relate to. Also the impression that the scent would “fizz.” The top note is dark despite this (in itself) fruity start. This mentioned “cola note” then intensifies - still with a dark overall orientation - in the heart note when the oud comes to the fore. The “dark mandarin note” is still perceptible. Almost like dried fruit. And this sharp oud joins in. However, our oud here does not see itself as the main theme. It rather wants to be one of several components of this fragrance. It wants to be a (medicinal) counterpart to the dark-dry, but still fruity, mandarin. Interesting. This medicinal character of our “supporting oud” is then enhanced by a slightly herbal note. This must come from the subtle use of vetiver. This note then remains: A tension between fruit (mandarin) and medicinal-(slightly) sharp oud. Towards the end, it becomes rounder and softer with warming amber and slightly rough musk. And thus also more conciliatory. However, this tension remains (in a subdued form) in the base. In 2004, “M7 Fresh” was also created. But isn’t that a - to put it in modern terms - “Mission Impossible”? A heavy oud scent for summer? The beginning is also fruity. But these citrus fruits (bergamot and mandarin) greet us much friendlier. Much fruitier. Much brighter. Yes, almost a bit citrus-refreshing. Although it is the same fruits compared to the “M7” from 2002, they now seem almost refreshing. Initially, there is no trace of this dark beginning of the “M7.” But this citrus-refreshing start lasts only a short time. Because shortly after, a “cola note” also appears in “M7 Fresh” and points to the kinship with the “M7” from 2002. However, this is much brighter, much friendlier. So to speak, a “cola light.” But still a product from the house of the famous soda manufacturer. I also think I can sniff a bit of oud. But only very lightly. A hint of oud. So to speak, “oud-light.” Because the scent progression remains dominated by the bright and friendly citrus fruits, which now even have a (pleasant!) sour note. As I said: Surrounded by this “oud-cola note,” which refers to the kinship. In the base, we then expect musk. But even this is not dark and gloomy. Additionally, it is equipped with a slightly grassy-herbal note, which I attribute to the vetiver. After a few hours, this citrus-fruity “cola light” fades out slightly musky-grassy. The “M7 Oud Absolu” from 2011, on the other hand, begins again dark-fruity: A mandarin, an orange, and a bergamot. Not sparkling-sour, but rather ripe-dark-mysterious. Even this fruity beginning seems as if these citrus fruits had not ripened in the bright summer sun on a gnarled tree but rather in a dark cave in the farthest Afghanistan. Everything in the top note is already dark and mysterious. But also very interestingly done. Shortly thereafter, it becomes extremely mysterious: No light in our dark mountain cave. The promised oud reaches our nose. An oud not of the medicinal kind, but rather mystical and exotic. Speaking of “exotic”: In addition to “Godfather Oud,” someone has now also lit a few incense sticks. They must come from our friend, patchouli. However, everything is beautifully spiced. And still slightly fruity, as the mandarin from the top note has not yet disappeared in our dark cave. What a wonderful combination: The gently fruity mandarin and the mysteriously (patchouli)-spicy (rosemary) oud. That’s great!!! But even in the base, everything is brought out that goes in the direction of “dark-mysterious”: First of all, warming amber: A small fire burns in our height. Hardly suitable to bring us light into the dark. But willing to bring more warmth to our hearts. Musk and myrrh penetrate to us. Dark. Mysterious. My conclusion: The “M7” from 2002 is a milestone in the history of perfume as a pioneer of a whole wave of oud fragrances. In addition, it has a unique “cola note.” This is then picked up by the “M7 Fresh” and presented in a much friendlier, more summery light. This is ensured by the brighter and more citrusy fruits. The “M7 Oud Absolu,” which clearly sees itself in the tradition of the “M7” from 2002, lives from the unique tension between the ripe (almost dried fruit) fruits and the (caused by oud and patchouli) dark (cave) mood. All three are really well-made fragrances. Each very interesting and with individual justification for existence. “Coco Chanel gave women freedom, Yves Saint Laurent gave them power.” (Yves Saint Laurent). “And for us men, ‘M7’” (Naaase).

The recently tested and purchased M7 has quickly become one of my absolute favorite perfumes - rarely has Oud been this wonderful! And it didn't take long before this summer version, M7 Fresh, was bought. Similarly rare and expensive, unmistakably an M7, and yet one of the best perfumes a man can wear in summer. M7 Fresh starts fresh, citrusy, and very creamy. But that's something we've seen often. The truly special aspect is how well the musty, thick, special in-your-face character of the original has been adapted for summer. With soft Oud and a sexy cuddly factor. Although toned down, even my girlfriend said: There's some Oud in there, right? Incredible, I would have thought that impossible. So, it's not that my girlfriend recognizes this now, but that Oud can be so pleasantly incorporated into a summer scent ;). Even if it might not be true Oud, the overall impression has been cleverly conveyed - however that may be. M7 Fresh is straightforward and quite simple - especially compared to the voluminous original. First, there's the creamy mandarin flash, then it moves into bitter orange (could also be the orange peel) and later a bit of musk. And all of this is underpinned by that special, wicked Oud note. Simple and convincing! The bottle of my 50 ml version is the same as the one for M7, only here the sides are colored brown. Both side by side: Perfect retro style! Longevity is a bit disappointing for me at 6 hours, raising doubts about the authenticity of the Oud. The sillage is almost dandy-like strong for a summer scent, but never unpleasant! Not quite at the reference level of the warm-winter M7, but damn well executed for a summer theme!

"M7" is a term known to almost everyone, a visionary and misunderstood genius who was ahead of his time. Today, however, the question is rather where Oud is not included anymore. Agarwood has made a significant entrance into the fragrance realm.

A completely different scent from the well-known M7 is the variant M7 Fresh. The commonality lies in the mention of Oud as a component of the fragrance, that moldy wood which is currently so popular. However - I did not perceive the Oud in the Fresh variant. The differences prevail. M7 presents a highly complex development, a tour de force through various fragrance directions.

He is not particularly fresh, the m7 fresh; one must measure him by that, after all, he is named so. The first minutes of the top note offer a rather tasteless fruit explosion, which certainly does not have a monopoly on liveliness.

He inevitably embodies the 'egophilic type'. This type of man is quite strongly narcissistic, primarily seeking attention. He combines designer pieces with second-hand or mass-produced items and shops across all price ranges. His patchwork style is colorful, youthful, and body-conscious.

But that doesn't mean this fragrance lacks character! The resemblance to M7 is still noticeable, but unlike the original, this version is absolutely suitable for summer. On my skin, I first notice a wonderful blood orange note. Ginger brings in the freshness. As it develops, it becomes creamier, and in the end, a light fruity note lingers with a hint of wood.

I received Montale’s discovery kits for my birthday and I was amazed how many vanilla scents variations in it. “Sweet vanilla” is simple, but at the same time interesting combination of vanilla and apricot notes. I like how it opens up within few hours and I can see why people recommend to layer this perfume with other fragrances, due to musky sweet dried notes. It gives gourmand sweetness and luxury feel to it. I don’t know how others can hear this scent for 6 and more hours? It was gone on me within few hours and I have to reapply again. I like perfumes with more complexity then this one. It was great way to experience this fragrance, but to my taste I like “Vanilla cake” for very gourmet scent. If you like very light perfumes, it is still good choice.

A fragrant friend of mine sent me a sample of this perfume along with Maison Mataha Escapade Gourmande and Andromeda's Moon Tihota. I sprayed each on different parts of my arm and smelled one at a time. I was immediately drawn to Escapade Gourmande (I now own a full size bottle and am obsessed with it!) and put the other two away because they didn't really do anything to catch my attention much. A couple of weeks later I was messing with samples in my closet and decided to give Montale Sweet Vanilla another go. I sprayed a little on a paper strip and inhaled. And oh my goodness, it was GOOD! I could smell something that was almost lemony at first (looked at the notes and it was apricot..not sure how that read as lemon-like to my nose but it did) mixed with a beautiful vanilla.
