And then the dry down of that beautiful, sweet vanilla came through and I decided that I had to have it. I ordered a bottle and while I was waiting for that to come, I wore the sample and realized that, although I loved the smell of Sweet Vanilla, that glorious opening fades after a few minutes and then I am left with that lovely, but hard to detect, sweet vanilla scent. I have to put my nose right to where I sprayed the fragrance to actually smell it, and really try to smell it, which is a bummer. I have read and heard so much about this fragrance being a projector and I didn't even get a scent bubble from it, which would have been ideal. I will still use Sweet Vanilla because it's such a lovely scent, but I will be layering it with some of my other vanillas so I am not left with the sense that I am not even wearing perfume. Edit: I decided to spray Sweet Vanilla on after over a month and now I can smell it much better!! That sweet vanilla apricot cake scent lasts way longer now!! I love it!!

I'm a beginner in the sweet perfume corner, and it is my first Montale perfume, so to me it was definitely an overwhelming experience, at first. First of all, DO NOT OVERSPRAY THIS!! And I mean it, because even with two sprays your nose can be easily overwhelmed, but with a light touch it is a great experience! This is a very linear scent, you definitely smell vanilla and apricot, all the way, from the beginning to an end. That being said it is not a "warm" evening vanilla, it is a bright and sugary vanilla if you are wondering. Same with the apricot, this is not a fresh apricot scent, it's more sugary, candy, apricot jam, so if you are looking for a natural one, this ain't it. I always heard about the signature Montale synthetic scent in every bottle, and I definitely sense it, but not in a bad or strong way. At the beggining the scent is very strong and sweetly fresh, but after an hour or two ( if not oversprayed) it becomes a more subtle, still very noticeable, but "easy" and more natural scent. And that's why I came to like it very much. I would say on my skin, the sugary apricot is the first note, but vanilla is very much there, and after a few good hours the vanilla becomes a bit warmer, and overtakes the apricot just by a bit. I wouldn't say this is a crazy gourmand scent, but this is a sweet pleasure. To me, this is definitely a "female" scent, but who cares eh. If you like sugary fruity candy smell, this is an easy buy. Just be careful with the amount. Over all very pleased, and ready to explore more of Montale, and sweet scents in general. PS : I have been also layering it with basically any perfume I have / am testing , as well , goes great with most! ( a part from sweet perfumes IMO ) So just overall a great add on of a perfume!!

I’m about to eat my own arm. Rating: 10/10 I’m not much of a vanilla fan when it comes to perfumes, probably because of some scent back from the 80s that I remember smelling and hating. I wish I could remember the name of it, but it was sickeningly sweet. But, I digress. This perfume is delicious. I love how the scent of vanilla is comforting, and it lasts all day. When I wear this fragrance I smell like a vanilla cupcake and cake is my most favorite thing in the whole world. I’m buying a entire bottle of this one. Sillage: 6 feet Longevity: 9 hours

This just isn't it for me. I got a bunch of samples of Montale vanillas and they all have an underlying DNA that I am simply not a fan of. It's a bit musky and rich but fake smelling. That said, if you're looking for a sweet gourmand vanilla, you found her here! You get strong vanilla, I don't really get the apricot but do get the general bit of sweet non-acidic fruitiness. I don't really like this or want to smell like this personally.

As always, my husband watched various YT videos about perfumes and now he absolutely wanted a vanilla perfume. And not just anything with vanilla, no, it had to be sweet vanilla. I suffer greatly from headaches when a perfume is too sweet, so I had always tried to avoid that.

I have become a big fan of vanilla and am still searching for the ultimate vanilla bomb! Here’s a little comparison of Montale vanillas: “VANILLE ABSOLU”: creamy, high-calorie vanilla pudding, very delicious, pure... people will just say “What smells so much like vanilla?” without realizing it could be a perfume. They smell it before they see you...

First of all, I love standing out with my perfumes, whether negatively or positively! My fellow humans have to deal with it. Since I travel a lot for work, I was sitting on a train one day. After boarding, I quickly snagged a seat, and suddenly a woman behind me said to her acquaintance: "Why do some people always smell like food, like" "quark balls.

I am currently on a mission to test Montale. So I am ordering samples until I drop. Some Montale fragrances have really disappointed me and hurt my nose. With "Sweet Vanilla | Montale," it’s completely different. Love at first spray! In the opening, you get a lovely, jammy apricot with vanilla. Warm, soft, and sweet. Really like an apricot jam with vanilla bean in it.

When I smell it, I just fly away, I find myself on a vanilla cloud. It smells like an edible, delicious vanilla, vanilla cake, slightly fresh and sweet at the same time. A woman can smell this delicious, so anyone who likes edible vanilla scents absolutely needs this fragrance, I can recommend it 100%.

Not sure if it’s the fig or the black currant, but one of these two fruits comes off very green and earthy. I don’t think the notes listed portray the green aspect of the perfume, but it does have that fresh and almost clean touch. It also has a nice prominent rose and geranium mix that adds to the girliness of the fragrance. Really pretty actually, but the performance is absolutely horrendous and it also stained my white shirt.

I had this perfume, for me it was a clean fresh rose, simple rose from the garden, like natural smell of rose, with a touch of green note in it. I can feel the fig leaf in it. Is unisex , but mostly i see it suitable for women use. Is moderate good sillage and peristent. I find it suitable for day use, worm or hit wheather , casual wear or office. I don't think ia an offesinsive perfume and can be enjoyed by people who love light rose perfumes. Not very complicated smell.

The best blackcurrant scent I have ever smelled (Enchanted Forest, for example, did not convince me at all) - bright, contrasting, lively, practically bursting with energy, with a wonderful scent trail and good longevity. An instant wow effect. Later, a floral note comes in, the blackcurrant remains, but the fragrance becomes more familiar, like a floral aquatic. On one hand, it feels natural, on the other hand, like a very glossy picture. Wow.

It's time to get properly indignant. After I recently upset the guests of the "Cafe Montale," it's time to make amends. I wanted to know some time ago how Montale interprets the 4 cardinal directions, so one each of incense, wood, pepper, and *pardon* gourmand was ordered. And because sometimes you're not sure, the Wood & Spices presentation was also ordered for those days of indecision. The only Oud-free "Full Incense" would be my favorite if one hadn't slowly but surely worked its way into my consciousness and sneaked past my supposed favorite Montale. Have I mentioned? I also like pepper when it's not just used as a sidekick. I really became aware of this back with "Bang." On the skin, it might be too powerful for some, but it leaves wonderful trails in the environment. If it were niche and had a more appealing name, it would be significantly more popular. The "Spicebomb effect" is clearly at play here. Montale's "Intense Pepper" sometimes uses a fruit commonly referred to as "pink pepper," which is actually not pepper at all. It provides a diffuse, fruity-citrusy opening that I wouldn't want to clearly label as orange. Floral notes (but not clearly identifiable for me) from the heart note also play a role, and the black pepper certainly doesn't want you to focus on its subordinates. I understand well if someone doesn't like the top note; I understand if the heart note might not please. But what awaits us here, if you don't give up right away, is very wearable art and a fine menu for the nose. Eau de Parfums are known to be somewhat tenacious; if you expect the base after 15 minutes, you're on the wrong track. For me, it takes between 1-2 hours, and it's a celebration every time when the base notes announce their arrival with a perfectly trimmed pepper. What does "Intense" mean here? I’ll try to illustrate: A spritz of "IP" on the Extensor Digitorum Communis (muscle in the forearm, now my preferred testing ground;)) can easily stand out against 3 spritzes of "Aventus" on the neck and collar. With 2 spritzes of "IP," you can get through the day well, making it possible to take this artwork to the office without your colleagues secretly crafting armies of voodoo dolls. This is the second fragrance to receive a 9.5 from me; I am so convinced by the Montale concept overall. I generally only buy fragrances whose base notes I enjoy and that don't evoke associations with other fragrances in my collection. I wouldn't wish for a linear scent progression here because I can live very well with the idea of having 2-3 fragrances in my portfolio where I can be sure I won't smell "myself" a second time on the go. And in this case, less agreeable top and heart notes are almost always guarantees. (It's perfectly mistrained on YouTube to attribute "sexiness" to a fragrance based on the top notes. Anyone who takes longer in the bathroom for styling & co. has already lost. :P In any case, I've found my first Montale that can stay with me not just as a sample. No praise without criticism: I would wish for at least a prettier color for my preferred Montale, especially since the gentlemen are so uncreative regarding the flacons. "IP" is designated as a men's fragrance. I can easily imagine it on women over 30. Probably it's a men's fragrance because the marketing department at Montale knows that women prefer to stay 29 forever. The end & Oud :)

"What a great smell is this?" I asked myself as I strolled through the practice. Not a soul in sight to whom this fragrance could be attributed. The scent, strong, dark, but not unpleasant. Masculine, woody, spicy, and resinous, it somehow reminded me of incense. And I love incense. A week later, I walked through the waiting room, and again the same scent. In the waiting room, there were only a few patients, two of whom were men. The circle of suspects was narrowing, the noose was tightening. I used my people skills to identify the guilty, fragrant culprit who was flooding the entire practice with his scent. I discreetly caught him alone and asked him about his perfume because I really liked it. He wasn't quite sure, didn't know the name off the top of his head, but promised to Google it and look it up. So I approached him again a little later and found out it was "Intense Pepper" by Montale. I hadn't heard anything about Montale before as a perfume novice. "Intense Pepper" also seemed a bit strange to me, and I was somewhat confused. Was that really the pepper I had smelled that reminded me of incense? Is this really the right perfume? I thanked him for the information and decided to search for more information at home on the internet, so here. After the patient left, you could still smell him in the room where he had been for at least another hour. He surely didn't apply it sparingly ;) The fragrance pyramid made me doubt my nose; I was disheartened. Was it really the right name the patient had given me? But the perfume, this scent, simply wouldn't let me go; I liked it, and that meant I had to have it. So I ordered it, hoping that I had received the right information. Anxious waiting, a few days of uncertainty and tension. Finally, the package arrived, opened it, took out the perfume, removed the safety pin, and pfft on my wrist. At first, the pepper is clearly dominant, and the floral "orange" is subtly perceptible in the background. Anyone expecting an overwhelming top note will unfortunately be disappointed. Unless they are a hardcore pepper fan. And I think this is where most of those who have tested "Intense Pepper" already form their opinion and dismiss it prematurely. A big mistake. Because you have forgotten the first rule of Montale. "The first rule of Montale is: Never judge a Montale by its top note." Over time, the pepper becomes a bit milder, and now the scent becomes woodier and also resinous. For me, it took over one to two hours on the skin for the scent to undergo a wonderful transformation and unfold its full potential. Only then did it start to smell like I remembered it from the practice. And now I was sure I had bought the right scent. I consciously chose to wear it out yesterday because I knew it would carry me well through the evening without a portable sprayer. I applied it a bit earlier so that it could unfold its effect after more than an hour at the destination. Even though it was a venue where smoking was allowed, I could still perceive it well on me for several hours. If I had also sprayed it on my clothes, it would probably have absorbed all the smoke in the venue and replaced it with its own scent ;) I would say that after applying it to the skin, it is at least perceptible in its surroundings for 4 hours, then slowly retreats, but remains noticeable on the skin for a solid 6-8 hours, even longer if applied to clothing. I am always modest with these claims because I don't want to exaggerate. It can certainly last longer, depending on skin type and other factors. Once home, I could still smell it well on my skin after more than 6 hours. My shirt, which had only passively come into contact with the scent, still smells of it even a day later. I think with direct spraying, it could definitely last several days. All in all, a really beautiful scent that some doubters might want to take a closer look at, smell, and test again, but don't forget the first rule of Montale! The wait is worth it.

I never thought I would encounter a Montale that, upon spraying, doesn't crash through the door along with its frame, or rather, the entire wall into the house. Mr. Pierre can indeed be quite - subtle! The pepper is not sharp, but aromatic. This may be considered a cliché elsewhere, but to experience that a Montale named "Intense Pepper" does not turn the pepper up to brutal intensity, but instead presents itself as merely intense-aromatic, is quite something. And this is actually a Montale? Where I initially had to check near the skin with my nose if anyone was home at all? But it gets even more astonishing. Fruit. And mild fruit at that. Fresh and juicy. Orange, possibly even bitter orange. In any case, deeply fruity and veeeery delicious. At the very beginning, there’s a hint of something sourer. Perhaps lemon or lime. The pepper nearly gets overshadowed by the fruit. At least, if you approach the scent with the cautiousness typical of Montale. However, those who bravely take a sniff later will notice it distinctly again. It primarily delivers aroma and character, akin to light incense. Of course, it also has a woody component. We'll get to that later. The fruit and the pepper tingle amusingly remind me, after ten or fifteen minutes, of Fanta. After a quarter of an hour, I detect something leguminous. That must be the pink pepper, which is making every effort here to prove its botanical difference from "normal" pepper. Yes, that fits. However, I find the trendy "floral notes" quite difficult. Unless… How do pea flowers actually smell? Unfortunately, unfortunately, unfortunately, by the course of the morning, an artificial wood note à la Carbone appears, including the coconut-ivy note. It reveals that the present Montale apparently consists fundamentally of a synthetic wood note that - as mentioned above - had already greeted from afar with the pepper. This wood note can be loved, one can be downright infatuated with it. I compare this to the glutamate in potato chips, often hidden on the ingredient list under names like "yeast extract." These euphemistically called "flavor enhancers" (as far as my knowledge goes) essentially trigger a form of dependency, that craving which, together with salt, usually leads to at least half the bag being devoured immediately. I believe this wood note has a similar effect on the sense of smell. Tasty, but in a instinctively-addictive guilty-pleasure way. That bothers me a little. And after such a nice start, I also find it a bit disappointing. This note persists and persists and persists. All day long into the evening. Those who enjoy being swept away by it will find "Intense Pepper" to be excellent. PS: The sillage is - self-perception notwithstanding - not to be underestimated. PPS: It should not be overlooked that the scent was quite well received. I thank Kovex for the sample.

Consider yourselves warned, what comes next will be a true hymn of praise. Recently, when I tested Amber & Spices, Black Aoud, and Intense Pepper at the perfume store, I was thrilled by all three. I bought the first two immediately, and Intense Pepper landed on my wish list. You can't choose just one among these three; the poor soul only finds peace when it possesses them all. So today I bought Intense Pepper, and what can I say? This is truly a dream of a fragrance, with that wonderful pepper note upon spraying, even better than freshly cut Imbuia pepperwood; you would want to bathe in it, roll around in it. The medicinal, slightly biting quality that Black Aoud has at the beginning (which I actually love) is not present here, just a delightful pepper note that lasts easily around 3 to 4 hours. After this high enjoyment, things really get going; slowly the Oud emerges from the background, accompanied by the wonderful resinous amber, perfectly harmonized. A feast for the senses. So beautiful that I get to experience this. People ask what it is and jot it down; I can understand that well, I would do the same if I didn't already know. You can see those who are hesitant to ask are torn about doing so. Longevity and sillage are very good, unfortunately not quite as powerful as with Black Aoud, but that's lamenting at an extremely high level. I can only advise you to get this Intense Pepper; it will make you happy.

Just the name piqued my curiosity, as I am known for my love of pepper and its abundant consumption - pepper in all variations and from different countries of origin. From jungle pepper from Sri Lanka and Madagascar to Tellicherry pepper from the Malabar coast of India, to shadow-dried red Kampot pepper. Hardly a meal goes by without being crowned with freshly ground pepper, and when I’m out and about, there’s usually a mini pepper mill in my handbag, in case there’s only the dusty, lifeless powder in the shaker - the greatest culinary insult for me! As soon as I discovered “Intense Pepper” here on Parfumo, I got the chance to participate as the second-to-last participant in a sharing and eagerly awaited the arrival of the pepper fragrance! The opening is fresh; yes, there is indeed the scent of freshly ground black pepper, the exciting moment when the essential oils with their multifaceted aromas are released at the moment of grinding. It smells typically peppery with dark fruits and dark smoke, interspersed with intensely fresh bright and resinous notes of eucalyptus and pine needles. Over these tones, the resinous-bitter sweetness of pink peppercorns asserts itself, which faintly reminds me of juniper. It feels like a scent duel between both spices for dominance in the top note, which lasts delightfully long and plays along until the end. In addition, I smell a wonderful, very prominent fruitiness that can never come solely from the pepper: it is the scent of bitter oranges, unsweetened orange syrup, and candied orange peel, which are not mentioned at all in the pyramid, but are so present that their bitter-fresh orange note dominates the floral heart notes, which I cannot pinpoint individually, and extends into the base. Only here do oud, cedar, and a rather defensive amber manage to overlay the bitter orange, but they cannot completely overpower the fruit - much to my delight! Thus, “Intense Pepper” is a fruity-peppery, almost cheerful gourmand with a woody base, not heavy like some other gourmand fragrances that derive their opulence from dates, cinnamon, cocoa, honey, or almonds. “Intense Pepper” is therefore not just a fragrance for dark autumn and winter days, but is also perfectly suitable for wearing in spring and summer - perhaps not necessarily during the bright day. But I can wonderfully imagine it on a balmy summer evening. “Intense Pepper” truly deserves its name: it is as intense as I like, while not being heavy and lasting quite a long time. A fragrance for pepper lovers, orange fans, and wood enthusiasts, equally exciting for men as for women.

Sometimes I wonder why I keep writing comments when sometimes the statements below already say (almost) everything important. A joy in writing? A drive for subjective clarification? Mydarkflower speaks of 'orange juice mixed 50/50 with water and pepper grinder on top'. Yes, I can and must agree with that, as it contains the essence. But there is still more to add.

The fragrance is a dream, unfortunately the design of the bottle, as well as the sprayer, is of the cheapest quality a la Made in China. After a short time, when spraying, there was no fine mist coming out anymore, just complete splashes that couldn't be properly distributed on the skin.

The house of Montale, for some a blessing of "power fragrances," for others an olfactory assault. As controversial as the scents from this house are, Intense Pepper is, in my opinion, a great fragrance that definitely doesn't need to hide behind Arabians Tonka !

If you like it sweet and have a bit of spice in you, then Intense Pepper is a great choice. Not only men can wear this scent, but also women. As a woman, I prefer something more striking and like to make statements. The constant claim that the bottle looks cheap is completely unfounded; it is very modern and youthfully cool.

For me, Intense Pepper is a fragrance that will always stay in my memory. On one hand, its spicy-sharp sillage is very present and invigorating. On the other hand, it creates a feeling of warmth and maturity through the floral, woody foundation with a good portion of orange. A combination that I find very underrated!

One smells a lot of fruit right after spraying, which reminds me a lot of the seasonal scents from Escada. Throughout the wear, not much really changes. The clementine stands out clearly. In the base note, vanilla is supposed to be present, which makes me generally cautious. In fact, vanilla is only very faintly noticeable to me, if at all. For me, this is more of a plus point that makes the perfume suitable for summer. The amber note also holds back quite a bit. There could be pepper present that tickles the nose. Is this scent "very sexy"? That is probably a matter of taste, as always.

How to start.. If you want to get rich in just one night and to be seen around you and give you a feeling of luxury and you don't have a dollar in your pocket, this is the undisputedly awaited perfume. If you are a fan of the oud note, but it is not the usual strong animal repulsive note, but the light, youthful and elegant oud, which is blended in a professional way, as when adding orris and benzoin with musk, this oud perfume gives a feeling of good narcissism and forgiving vanity, thanks to the right mixing method and the way the notes are arranged in Appearance, emission, and reaction during the day. Beautiful Stuff, Amazing quality, Strong longevity/sillage Really masculine, i simply love it ! 9,5/10 ! (Because nothing is perfect ;) )

YSL 37 is a cherished gem in my perfume collection. (Hard to find these days where i live so i need to be carefull with spraying haha ) The opening is fresh and inviting, while the heart reveals a soft, creamy warmth that wraps around me like a comforting hug. The subtle cedar and white musk add a beautiful depth, which makes it perfect for any occasion, whether I'm at work or enjoying a dinner. I love how it evolves throughout the day, creating an intimate sillage without overwhelming. YSL 37 Rue de Bellechasse holds a special place in my collection. If you’re searching for a scent that feels personal and transformative, I cannot recommend it enough! This one is a Real GADA

From the moment I first smelled this fragrance, I knew I had to add it to my collection. It is an opulent scent that is rich in depth. The combination of oud and incense, accompanied by a beautiful iris, blends it all together perfectly. It is dark and resinous, and simply put, it's beautiful, and bold all while being refined at the same time. I'm not entirely sure how it connects with the old building, but I'm grateful that it has translated into this incredible fragrance. My only wish is that it were more accessible and easier to find. For me, it’s an easy 10 out of 10.

The Vestaire des Parfums Édition Couture brings together a collection of three woody scents: 6 PLACE SAINT SULPICE, 24 RUE DE L'UNIVERSITÉ, and of course, 37 RUE DE BELLECHASSE. In the heart of Paris - at the northwest corner of the intersection of Rue de Bellechasse 37 - lies the Abbey of Penthemont, which is now the headquarters of YSL. Overall, the fragrance is meant to represent the atmosphere of this abbey house - and with it, the entrepreneurial spirit of Y. S. Laurent. Everything feels a bit reverent, elevated - almost formal. Just like in an old monastery. I myself was on the lookout for another iris scent. I love iris for its distinctly clear and honest nature. This time, it was supposed to be dark, suitable for evening wear. This can be quite difficult to find, especially when it is not paired with overwhelming sweetness. Many do that, and I do not like those many. Especially the ones with vanilla often go far beyond any targets and end up in mundane, mass-appeal epics. Let the iris shine, give it space! I then found - with the help of Aleyzs during a souk testing - the true dark iris treasure. In general, the souk is still the best opportunity for testing. Thank you all again for that! Yes, a minimal sweet touch also brushes Rue 37 in the deepest drydown of the night, but it is only a grain of benzoin resin responsible for that. Overall, Rue 37 feels very resinous to me. You can probably imagine quite well what these resins combined with nagarmotha, pepper, incense, and oud result in. Plus a hint of patchouli. What a conglomerate! It smolders reverently-pastoral in these rooms, balsam vapors ground the hidden. And then - high above in the naves of Penthemont - only one reigns: the iris. Black liquid. Dry white in the twilight. And it is allowed to shine, spreading its wings over everything and everyone in this former abbey and tells you: Everything is good! Thanks to TahaScents. Wishing you a healthy 2021!

I have thought long about which fragrance to write my first review for. When I recently bought this scent, it became clear to me. I am a very big fan of iris, and the Dior Homme line has been my favorite fragrance line for a long time. What makes Rue de Bellechasse so special for me? I have a picture in my mind: A large dark room in an old manor house. Noble furniture, lots of dark wood, heavy curtains in front of the large windows, and a bowl with partially burned incense in one corner. The room radiates wealth, tranquility, but also something dark. On a table illuminated by a sunbeam that falls through the gap in the curtains, however, there is a flower. Delicate, bright, beautiful. It is this interplay that makes the fragrance so special for me. Oud, patchouli, and resins create a deep woody, slightly smoky scene. Noble but also somewhat decadent/dirty. The iris rises from this, however, very bright and slightly powdery. This creates, in my opinion, a heavy, rather masculine scent with a twist that makes it so attractive and perfect. An absolutely unique creation that I no longer want to be without!

A very concentrated opening, focused on very dry, blended, grassy notes. It feels almost a bit mystical and slightly Asian, which is somewhat surprising given the name after a Parisian street. Juniper and the Asian grasses merge into a dense, dry wall, with pepper sprinkled in between, not sharp, rather subtle and earthy.

Finest oud, slightly leathery and smoky. The oud is not too overpowering here. The iris brings a pure powderiness to the development and rounds off the entire profile. Musk and patchouli form a perfect base. The scent unfolds mysteriously and reflects the sophistication of the creations made at 37 Rue de Bellechasse, Paris.

About 20 years ago, I was on vacation in Morocco with my family. I must say that we like to do adventurous things, like cutting straight through the desert with our Fiat Uno only armed with a compass, when the wind had blown sand across the roads, or for the simple reason to go fast. One day we saw two little boys who were standing at the side of the road and were stopping cars. We stopped, took them in and drove them to their place of home. When I remember back now, to this day I cannot figure out how to interpret the look on their father's face. Was it horror that the boys went on a ride with strangers, or was it surprise that we brought them home? Anyway, we were invited into a large Bedouin tent which was put up in the middle of the desert. We were offered heavily sweetened tea and sat on piles of rugs. My mom and I received silver bracelets and carpets were promised to our men (my dad and my brother). My mom brought out salted peanuts which were not really appreciated by our hosts. Using "hands and feet" to explain, plus the little broken English they had, they insisted that nuts are sweet and therefore the salt is not appropriate. This day in the desert is etched in my memory. And this is exactly what "Sandflowers" smells like: Dry heat, desert sand, salt, aromatic notes, and a whiff of sunscreen which was a must for our pale faces. This fragrance seems to confuse other people - I have already heard "you smell like a caramel biscuit" or "are you wearing 'Sunflowers' today?" The sillage is amazing ... even after 4 hours, my colleagues in the office could still point out the room where I had been last. I myself can still detect a faint scent of "Sandflowers" on my skin after 6 hours. On clothing, guaranteed to the next day. Originally I had expected a desert memory association from another scent 'Saharienne' which is a pleasant enough perfume but has nothing to do with the Sahara. Oh yes, half a year later, rugs were delivered to us by mail.

Montale SANDFLOWERS evokes immediate memories of Comptoir Sud Pacifique AQUA MOTU. Something about the algae and the sea water. In waves, SANDFLOWERS has a strange oriental vibe to go with the muskiness. AQUA MOTU is even muskier and perhaps more musky than aquatic. The biggest difference between the two is the juniper in SANDFLOWERS, which is quite marked especially the opening, making this creation seem rather aromatic and the algae very mossy and green. My understanding is that Pierre Montale was formerly associated with Comptoir Sud Pacifique, I presume as the perfumer. The similarity between SANDFLOWERS and AQUA MOTU may not therefore be my imagination! The bottles are similar, except that the Montale version of the aluminum can ends up looking sleek and niche, while the Comptoir Sud Pacifique version imparts the decided impression of being some kind of budget drugstore body spray. Is it just the trinket on the Montale that makes the difference? I don't know exactly why, but I really like the Montale bottles and really dislike the Comptoir Sud Pacifique bottles. I am not much for aquatic fragrances, so SANDFLOWERS is not really my kind of thing, but anyone who likes AQUA MOTU is bound to like this composition, which is unisex and even leaning a bit toward the masculine side. I consider this to be an atypical perfume for Montale. It seems more like a vacation scent to me. Maybe it should be called SAND DOLLARS?

This Montale, despite its marine aquatic nature, feels both moist and yet dry, like the fine sand you walk on barefoot. It doesn't cling to the skin - and you don't sink in heavily. The air is ozonic and soft, with a slight salty note. Spices are also in the air, along with something herbal. I assume it's beach grass, mixed with yellow flowers that grow on the dunes. I don't perceive any seaweed - although there is a subtle green note present. The dry breeze is made cozy by sandalwood, yet remains airy. Oak moss doesn't weigh down the fragrance but adds depth and longevity without being bitter. A scent for beach walkers that is also pleasant to wear indoors.

I really liked Dobbs' comment on Sandflowers and was looking forward to a test, as I was sure this scent would be something for me. What I immediately notice is the slightly oily film on my skin after spraying. When fragrances have this consistency, they are often more long-lasting on my skin, which I consider a positive aspect. I am disappointed by the first impression; a slightly medicinal note hits me, with no trace of sea breeze or freshness. I had imagined it differently. Well, take it easy, I tend to be impatient when the top note doesn't appeal to me right away. This scent is quite unusual; I try to let it affect me and note what I feel. Salty air, damp sand, mud, fine spice, and beads of sweat are the images that Sandflowers evokes. This is not unpleasant, but in a strange way gentle and calm; flowers or berries, which are mentioned in the comments, do not appear to me, or I do not perceive them. Aquatic or fresh, this scent is not at all to my feeling. I seek advice from my husband, who sniffs and says: "Nope, I don't like it." "Do you find it fresh?" "It's not fresh at all, rather dull." For me, Sandflowers has a rather linear scent progression, changing little; I like the base note with the woody foundation the best. A peculiar scent, I can't say if I like it. The longevity is quite good, the sillage is in the medium range; I only know the bottle from the photo, Montale bottles are not my thing. I will keep the sample and take it with me to the seaside in spring; there, Sandflowers will be tested again, maybe it will reveal itself to me then.

The sea! The sea! One might want to exclaim this when the scent of Sandflowers wafts into the nose. Whether you align more with James Joyce, seeing the sea as a great sweet mother, or with the Greek troops who finally arrived at the Black Sea after the Persian campaign, the sea touches everyone in one way or another. Regarding the fragrance, I would say that I don't necessarily smell the sea itself, but rather get the impression of being somewhere by the sea. It’s not a vacation beach; there are beach thistles and juniper bushes, along with a lot of wind and spray, the scent of which mixes with the foliage. Most of all, my surroundings have the smell of sunscreen, which I can't confirm for myself. In my opinion, this is not an aquatic, fruity, delicious vacation scent; there has been a serious attempt to convey the impression of beach and shoreline. There’s also a salty note that I can detect.

At some point, I stumbled upon the page for this perfume and read the components. 'Brrrrr', I thought, 'am I a fish'? By the way, I don’t like fish. I came across Paul because he also lives in the water and surely knows how this scent should smell. Maybe he even likes it on his many-armed women and helps many oracle-like offspring into the world.

Whatever sand flowers may smell like - I can't detect any flowers of any kind here. This fragrance has instantly transported me back to my childhood and youth by the sea, to a sunny summer day with strong winds and a choppy sea. I smell the spray, salt, the seaweed washed ashore, the warm sand, and a very light hint of sunscreen.

Sandflowers is a perfume to which I must surrender. I can't get a hold of the stuff! Aquatics are not my thing, but what is listed in the pyramid for heart and base notes should actually fit. But I can't manage it! During the first test, I applied quite generously.

What do sand flowers smell like? Well, in an internet search, I found out that this flower occurs in Peru and is used there as a medicinal plant. In addition to women's and prostate ailments, a Flor-de-Arena infusion is also used for detoxifying the body and calming the nerves. Forewarned and with the term "Flowers" in mind, I took on the test.

I still need to submit a review for this fragrance: Sandflowers from the house of Montale. This scent has been in my collection for several years now, and I am quite satisfied with it. By now, I have quite a few fragrances with this typical algal DNA à la Acqua di Sale in my collection, including this great "original.

Vinyle opens up with a nice blast of spiciness, smoke and resinous smell. The presence of pepper and Myrrh adds a lot of character to this perfume. While pepper adds to the spice levels, Myrrh adds a mysterious and resinous smell to the perfume. Along with the spices, the perfume also smells like a powdery gourmand. This could be due to the presence of the Immortelle and Vanilla notes. While immortals adds a dry tobacco smell to the mix, the vanilla adds the sweetness. If you like resinous fragrances, then this perfume will work wonders for you. I think it's quite unique in terms of mixture, and is also very well balanced. null of the notes become overpowering and you can keep enjoying the creamy, resinous, sweet texture of this fragrance. Performance wise this works pretty good on me. I keep getting whiffs of it for 4 hours on my skin. After that it becomes a skin scent and stays for a couple more hours. Definitely recommend this one.

Interesting that Yves Saint Laurent has finally discovered the niche for itself. I have been waiting a long time for this brand to step on the gas and take off again. "Kouros," "Opium pour homme," and "M7 Oud Absolu" as masterpieces are now many years behind us, and the eternally stagnant circling around the bulky "L'Homme" in 47 variations has not offered anything innovative for a long time. The name "Vinyle" immediately brings to mind old school, vinyl records, and the comfort of past times. My expectations - especially in light of the above 8.1 - are high. ParfumAholic hits the nail on the head quite precisely with his statement below. He writes of an "undecided scent," and I would like to agree with him. Without a doubt - the new YSL is accessible, designed for everyday wear. With the ingredients mentioned above, you can't go too wrong, but given the abundance of similarly autumnal-soft fragrances, you also can't automatically get everything right. In my opinion, "Vinyle" lacks a bit of precision. Soft-spicy start, powdered pepper, a hint of anise to it, quite velvety enveloping. Immortelle, which should actually smell a bit curry-like, I can hardly recognize. One can undoubtedly like this; it is coherent in itself. A subtle vanilla note envelops the inherently soft-creamy spiciness as it develops, while myrrh and licorice round it off with a slightly dry, sweet resinous quality. Many will undoubtedly like this as well. There is nothing to suggest that there is anything not to like about it. But I must say it frankly - this "Everybody's darling" scent bores me extremely after a short time. There is an almost clean, bath-like cleanliness and roundness to it that somehow robs "Vinyle" of any tension or distinctiveness, leaving it looking exceedingly dull. What a shame.

I thought it was just me, after reading the first review here though my suspicions were confirmed, I smell Bergamot! Bergamot is not listed but that's what I get, Patchouli and Bergamot. Jo Malone's Oud & Bergamot comes to mind when wearing this scent. Patchouli, to me, is really nice, conjuring images of a dark/earthy environment but can easily become olfactory overload. Great quality and more for casual fare, though easy on the application because I'm guessing that there are plenty of folks that find patchouli an overbearing fragrance note.

Now that I have a bit of free time in 2019, I dedicate it to this special little scent here. Vetiver Patchouli by Montale was recommended to me as a somewhat more affordable alternative to Orage by Louis Vuitton. When it comes to fragrances, I usually tend to be the type who cares about "as long as it's original and in the bottle." This is the first time I didn't care about that. And I haven't regretted it. Vetiver Patchouli has once again a very functional name, following the credo "what's on the label is inside." I haven't come across the Montale brand before, and I don't know any other scent from this house. However, it might be worthwhile to give it another sniff. VP has almost a sour opening, with a complete absence of citrus, which was new for me. One almost wants to step back, as the first inhale really hits hard. There is a crisp freshness in the composition that has been unique to me so far. Vetiver as a single component is good and very long-lasting, while the other components are not really distinguishable for me. The scent progression remains relatively constant, although I believe that from the base note, Patchouli seems to become stronger. The longevity leaves nothing to be desired. VP has nothing sweet, gentle, or soft. It is quite distinctive, yet still remains somewhat in the background. It doesn't take over the space but surrounds the wearer with a rugged, fresh aura. I can't think of any situation where it wouldn't fit. Definitely the best choice is probably the workday, even in customer contact, as it becomes somewhat more subdued despite its initial intensity. I could imagine that it might become a bit musty in the height of summer, but that remains to be seen. VP is declared as a men's fragrance, but in my opinion, it is also well-suited for the confident ladies. If you have the opportunity to test it, it's worth it and costs less than half of Orage, with better longevity and a fantastic bottle. The pin just needs to be removed before using the travel bottle. Thanks for reading.

The green, broad, coolness of the vetiver is spiced with crushed pink pepper [and yes: it must be exactly this juicy, spicy pink pepper]. The patchouli chimes in with its green earthy tone. Everything is earthy. Everything is green. Key of C major. And from some background, an almost menthol-like tone makes its way through. It brings every single note - earthy, ungrave patchouli/green-green vetiver/juicy pepper pink - to shine. Menthol-like. Minty almost. And friendly. Unrealistically friendly green. Radiant. Fiery? Vibrant. The Bourrée from Handel's Water Music. The recording with Neville Marriner and his Academy. When the brass and strings toss the notes back and forth. A spectacular performance. What a dance over the water. Fiery! A radiant work of art.

After recently expressing my thoughts on my absolute favorite fragrance, it's now time for this one. I will try to write as politely as possible. I don't want to offend any lovers of this scent. But what the hell is this? One thing is for sure, I don't know of any occasion where one should smell like this. But maybe my senses are just going crazy with what I smell and perceive. As always, for testing, I only sprayed one spritz on my forearm. And I immediately detected a medicinal scent. As if I had rubbed myself to clear my airways. And they did clear up. Unfortunately, this didn't turn out to be an advantage later on. Is this supposed to be the fresh green scent that everyone raves about? Well, it's not for me. Although the opening is still the best part of the fragrance. And now for those who may have only tested the scent briefly on a test strip. After about half an hour, the fragrance changes drastically. As if you are standing in an old house where the floor is being removed to replace the clay layers with insulation. It smells slightly musty. But if you think that's all there is, you are mistaken. Shortly thereafter, you suddenly find yourself in a cemetery, smelling a freshly dug grave with damp earth. So this scent development is quite genius for those who enjoy such things. But I don't want to smell like that. And for everyone who always imagines certain people with a fragrance, I picture an old man in a worn work jacket and rubber boots. A cemetery gardener who walks through the cemetery in the morning, with damp earth sticking to his boots and old, musty leaves clinging to the wet earth. So for me, this scent is nothing. The longevity is probably good. But I couldn't test that because I had to wash the scent off. The bottle is typical Montale and thus still the best part of it all. I really wouldn't recommend this fragrance, but for those who think this is exactly what they need, I definitely recommend not buying it blind but rather trying it out first.

With Vetiver Patchouli, Montale has introduced a third patchouli fragrance in its current lineup this year. Or rather, "Patchouli" is part of the perfume's name. While the other two are typical Montale powerhouses with plenty of punch - Patchouli Leaves is a hardcore patch and comes across quite loudly, and Patchouli Leather makes the leather whip crack impressively - Vetiver Patchouli is a quiet one. In the opening, there is a strict citrusy vetiver note, like bergamot, refreshing, which remains throughout the entire duration. The scent progression is linear. There is hardly any change. Only the initial strictness softens after 5 to 10 minutes. The fragrance then appears rounder. After about half an hour, a hint of patchouli can be gently sensed. But really just a whisper. In a blind test, I wouldn't have guessed it. After about 2 hours, when the vetiver loses its dominance, jasmine steps a bit into the foreground. After 4 hours, the Montale has faded away. Quite short-lived, actually. The sillage is okay, I think. More doesn't need to be. Anyone who enjoys fresh, green scents, likes vetiver, and is looking for something for summer should give it a try. A masculine fragrance with an aftershave character. A classic that my father might have worn in a slightly different variant. I associate it with shaving soap, barbershop, tweed suit, Sean Connery, Prince Charles, Earl Grey, green nature, and cool streams. A nice little fragrance that always works and never bothers. I prefer to stick with Patchouli Leaves, Profumum Roma Patchouly, and Patchouli Noir. And for the really hot days, I have the (new) Elixir from Reminiscence. I just let myself be tempted again. I had a feeling about it, somehow. Not my cup of tea. Many thanks to Dunki, who was able to decant 5 ml from his sharing for me!

Today, I took it to heart to write a few lines about my twin love ❤️❤️. Vetiver Patchouli from the house of Montale is the little younger twin brother of the big older brother Orage from the house of Louis Vuitton. Both have a special magic that allows their scent to unfold for a long time.

I knew Louis Vuitton Orage from a colleague and was looking for an alternative, as I simply find Orage too expensive for the performance it delivers. The recommendation was VP from Montale, and I was not disappointed. It starts fresh, spicy. Vetiver and pepper come through clearly. After a while, the patchouli also makes an appearance. I notice the carrot less.

I am thrilled, I smelled it and immediately knew I had to have it.... For lovers of citrus or sweet scents, this is not for you! Vetiver Patchouli is an incredibly beautiful, light, fresh, and spicy fragrance at the same time. I believe it can also be worn in summer, as it is not too heavy; you just have to like spicy scents!

Vetiver Patchouli is my second vetiver fragrance from the brand Montale and what can I say: Yes, this time it fits just right! I started my first attempt with Red Vetiver . The fragrance did not manage to convince me at all, and so it quickly left my collection.

I am writing a review because this is one of my favorite frags, and I think it is a shame that no one knows about it! I enjoy this more than Babycat and Tuxedo from the same line, but I have not tried enough of the others to tell how it compares. I find that this wears surprisingly well in all seasons, including summer, because of the fresh violet leaf and overall dryness of the scent. In my opinion, this leans very stereotypically masculine with absolutely no performance issues. I imagine a chic, 25-30 year old, guy wearing this with a long-sleeve button-up, chain, and nice watch while going out at night. I'm sure this would work for older men, but that is what comes to mind for me. This perfume could easily be summarized by saying that it is a woody, spicy, smoky, leather, with a prominent violet leaf opening. Compared to others in the genre, I would say that it is more intensely leathery and smoky than most, but definitely not on the extreme end of smoke, leather, or animalics. This might sound a bit boring considering the number of other violet leaf leathers, but I haven't found one that I enjoy as much as this. I think I enjoy it more than others because of the light oud, light sandalwood, and a somewhat prominent clove note, which adds intrigue to the composition for me. Opening is immediately ozonic, watery, and green. Violet leaf and oud dominate. Oud is not particularly animalic, but not completely tame either, with a very light funk (to my nose). There is a light petroleum sort of smell in the background, as well as the feeling of a light, nondistinct, floral. The oud is well done, has a depth to it, and doesn't smell completely synthetic. Shortly after, a distinct orange note becomes stronger, and the perfume becomes a bit sweeter. I sometimes feel like I can detect some light aldehydes and have lately picked up strongly on cloves and/or cinnamon. Over the course of an hour, leather begins to make its way towards the forefront of the composition. This shift also marks the introduction of a creamy texture to the background. I believe sandalwood, vanilla, or Iris could be contributing to this, but I am leaning towards sandalwood. The scent becomes progressively drier and smokier until the late drydown, when leather begins to fade. As the leather fades, a slightly dirty oud/musk, Vanilla/Sandalwood, and a light amber in the background are left. Performance is excellent, lasting 10 or so hours (on skin) with relative ease. After hour 8 or so, I find that the fragrance becomes a complete skin scent, but it seems to project solidly until then. While I occasionally go nose blind for periods of this fragrance's life, I often receive comments up until the 8-hour mark.

tested in the spring of this year at the spring store on Boulevard Haussmann in Paris. I was a little disappointed by the lack of innovation in this creation. after careful consideration, I tell myself that this perfume is still interesting. so it smells of oud and at no time leather, nevertheless it is a light oud, elegant and accessible to Westerners. it reminds me of spirit of dubay meydan but lighter. a masculine fragrance favored for fall and winter. I do not recommend it for under 25s, I do not recommend buying it blindly. the sillage is correct and the hold is also 5 hours

To start, the YSL Cuir is truly a great fragrance. Oud and leather make for an incredibly cool masculine combination. I purchased this scent at the Galleria Lafayette in Paris and wanted to wear it for dinner. I received many glances; you automatically have that aura that many dream of. The longevity and sillage are such that half of it would still be better than that of Ombre Nomade. However, after dinner, I only realized it then; the scent was so strong that I got a headache. I tried smelling coffee to neutralize my nose, but even that didn't help me. So, as a brief conclusion: Very good fragrance but so strong that you can still smell it the next morning after showering.

Cuir, the rebellious leather scent from Yves Saint Laurent, is a special fragrance and should definitely not be bought blind! I do enjoy buying blind, it's probably the thrill for me, I have no idea, but Cuir really should not be purchased without testing. It is incredibly strong, pure leather, and very very smoky. The smoke somehow reminded me of Falcon Leather, but the one in Cuir is significantly stronger and more intense, you really have to like that! I had left my test strip lying around and then simply forgot about it, and what can I say, after 2 days it still smells so intensely of campfire in my office that for a moment I thought a cable was burning. No, that was Cuir! But after these 2 days, it actually smells better and almost pleasant! However, I don't want a fragrance that I have to wait 2 days for ;-) Decide for yourselves

I find it quite similar to Sweet Diamond Pink Pepper | 25 without Kayali’s strong, metallic saffron note. Montale’s version amps up the rose into a jammy one and pairs it with brown sugar. Reminded me a bit of rose lokoum, without the powderiness. Personally, I didn’t detect a green note coming in from the violet leaf but my boyfriend did, so I guess I was nose-blind to it? Saffron is very subtle and soft compared to the fragrances I own that have this note. Amber and vanilla start turning this fragrance into something sweet and warm. Rose remains the strongest note with the brown sugar. It’s a very lovely scent, but it’s not something unique. Like I said, Kayali’s version is very similar and I feel like it has more depth, more complexity and better performance than Montale’s which is the main reason why it won’t be making it into my collection. Still, it was something I was glad to try out!

(sorry for the title) disclaimer: I have a weakness for rose scents with strong masculine notes, so the enthusiasm was to be expected. crazy in love opens floral-fresh-synthetic with something medicinal in the background, I briefly felt like I was in a doctor's office (just a little bit). the freshness fades quickly and is replaced by a very pleasant resin that dominates together with the rose. simple but so beautiful. you can enjoy this for a long, long time, and the sillage is solid. among the 3-4 Montale scents I have tried so far, this one ranks second best for me :D I definitely wouldn't wear this in the office, it can quickly become overwhelming, simply because it is such a strong, confident bomb and not a crowd pleaser. in my opinion, it's made for going out on cool nights, and it smells exactly like Zendaya looks in a suit (millennial here). whenever you wear it, it's worth having a coffee with it; I had freshly brewed coffee earlier and the scent in my nose and thought "wow"! I’m already looking forward to waking up one Saturday morning slightly dazed from partying and smelling the scent from the night before; until then, I'll definitely spray it on while having coffee ✨

Actually, I don't like amber scents, but I have to admit, this one is not bad, as the roses definitely take the lead. Despite the saffron and amber. It doesn't seem heavy or "cloying" to me at all, which I sometimes fear with Montale fragrances. It is warm, but still allows me enough air to breathe. Starts off energetic, then becomes cozy. "Crazy in Love" is not so crazy, but rather a feel-good scent, confident, zesty, modern. Naturally sweet, so for me it's girly, not unisex. One immediately thinks that the scent is secondary - if you stay within the Montale family, it is a child of Roses Musk Eau de Parfum and Arabians Tonka . To me, it also sounds like a mix of Delina Eau de Parfum and Instant Crush . So, my conclusion: it is a radiant, spicy rose-amber scent. Not retro at all. Definitely good for going out, even in Corona times, you will smell it through the mask. P.S.: If it is too overpowering for you, but you like the direction, you might be happy with Explicite ;)

The scent is a knockout in terms of longevity. One spray is definitely enough to fill a room. This is my first niche fragrance and I was so excited when my order arrived. I smelled it on my girlfriend and had to have it immediately. So I ordered it somewhat blindly... What can I say, it really is amazing. You feel confident and sexy with this fragrance. I love the sweetness paired with the saffron. I seem to have developed a weakness for it. But unfortunately, it sometimes annoys me, as the wild rose and I have had our disagreements. Unfortunately, it keeps pushing through at various points throughout the experience, and I'm not always ready for that.

Hello everyone, In July of this year, after a long search, I decided to go for Crazy in Love. I must say the scent itself is great. A lovely rosy note with a hint of piercing vanilla. The first impression was very feminine for me, but after a few seconds, this changed significantly. A beautiful summer fragrance that reminds me of a lovely dinner with a sunset in Greece. However, I find the longevity quite shocking for the price. The scent lasts relatively short for me and also for others, which makes you think twice about whether it would be worth the investment. Nevertheless, it can be said that it is not an everyday scent and sets you apart from the crowd.

Montale Crazy in Love is like being in a flower meadow in Spain during summer and taking a deep breath… you simply feel free and fulfilled. The blend of vanilla and floral notes is truly for everyone, whether woman or man. You might not want to wear it to a meeting, but in the evening at the beach with a cocktail, it is the perfect companion.

Because I have Duro by Nasomatto and this scent was bothering me ... including the price - I started looking for a perfume with a similar scent max. After a few different attempts (there were swiss arabian, some strange companies) I found Montale, which has a very decent perfume - in terms of durability and projection, and the special ones with oud (aoud) in the name. Because I'm not a fan of rose in men's perfumes (Arabs use it very often in various men's products - it rejects me), and there are a lot of rose products in Montale - in this case - AOUD MUSK - there is no rose (Yupii), and the ingredients are the same . I read, checked and ordered without castings and samples - based on ingredients, the Internet, opinions of foreign portals and opinions of foreign critics' noses and their publications and ... BINGO. Ladies and Gentlemen - if someone likes and keeps smelling the wrist sprinkled with DURO (Nasomatto) - he can buy blindfolded. Great fragrance and extremely complementary. It stays on for a long time and smells distinctly, and the price ... can be bought at a very good price. Very long durability. And I don't have to save a bag of money to pay Nasomatto for 30 ml of perfume, because it's not worth it anymore. As for the smell - the power of OUDU (synthetic agar), wood, musk - expressive, very slightly sweet (I don't like sweet perfumes) - for me 99% similar to DURO. Skin tests on both hands. A pro by DURO- holds 30% of the fragrance in relation to AOUD MUSK (Montale)! I tested it. Besides - in my opinion no. 1 when it comes to Montale, and in the next places for me (Dark Aoud, Vetiver Patchouli, Full Incense, Bakhoor)

For me Aoud Musk remembers Amouage Opus VI, which i find a little bit more balanced. Aoud Musk is indeed a wonderful fragrance but quite linear. Lots of ebony wood, a little oud and of course, musk. Lasts for a long time with excellent sillage and projection. Unisex and really sexy. Worth it certainly. Updated January 2014

Aoud Musk is another of my favorites and one of the best that Montale has to offer. I get compliments every time I wear this out. In terms of sillage and longevity, this one is off the charts. It's every bit as strong and long lasting as Black Aoud, if not stronger.

A bottled lasted me for years, to the point I became anosmic to it. Strong, pungent, chemically-oudy. My girlfriend loves this one and hates Duro, which instead I slightly prefer. But I get her point: this one is strong but dry, while Duro has more going on from head to body, making it "sweeter". It takes time to evaluate both in comparison. In my case, it will take weeks or months to be able to perceive their whole depth again, after years of daily use. Edit: after sampling Amouage Opus VI, I find it the closest match so far, just smokier than Aoud Musk. Opus VI is my favorite among the three.

I came across Montale's fragrances while searching for a perfume with good longevity. Secondly, I wanted a scent for special occasions that should have a noble aura. I have now found Aoud Musk for the time being. The Scent At first, the scent is a bit piercing in the nose, which is why some might be bothered by the "medicinal" smell of Montale's top notes in the Aoud range. I find this less troubling, but it takes a while to unfold. It stabilizes after about half an hour. The listed fragrance notes can mostly be detected at first. Especially the woody-resinous notes, which are likely to represent the oud, and herbs that probably come from saffron and initially remind one a bit of sage or cumin. The fragrance notes intertwine increasingly in the first hour, making it harder to distinguish them individually. However, one is rewarded with a successful, harmonious unity that appears quite noble and smooth. The musk seems to me more like an impression than a prominent fragrance note. Perhaps it has something to do with the wonderful balsamic, masculine warmth that Aoud Musk radiates. Probably the amber also supports this soothing effect, which can also be observed in Montale's "Amber Blue." A hint of sweetness, if at all perceptible, is then subtle and in the background. Thankfully, this "Aoud" completely avoids the Montale rose. The Dosage (1st Warning) I must urgently point out that this fragrance stands and falls with the dosage. Although my skin generally has issues with sillage and longevity, I would consider one spray and at most - really at most - two. With more than two sprays, the scent tips over, as the line between penetration and pleasure is extremely narrow here. The good and pleasant sillage then expands by several meters and can become overwhelming in that case. The Occasions Compared to other oud fragrances from Montale, such as "Black Aoud" or "Red Aoud," this one seems significantly more pleasant and socially acceptable. One cannot deny the masculine sex appeal of the scent, although it is not necessarily a date fragrance, as it could overwhelm someone interested in a relaxed lightness with a certain seriousness. I, in my late twenties, recently wore it at an orchestra and at a wedding, for which it is wonderfully suitable. On colder days, I could even imagine wearing it in the office in a well-dosed manner, despite the rather strong sillage. For summer, the scent seems too heavy, but it is certainly wearable in the cooler evening hours. For the warm season, one could instead opt for Montale's "Aoud Ever," which has similarities to this one but is dominated by a beautiful, non-chemical lemon that is supported by the oud and woody-resinous notes. The Longevity (2nd and 3rd Warning) The longevity is phenomenally typical of Montale. It lasts all day and into the next morning. I would like to issue a second warning regarding application on clothing. It lasts significantly two to four days on that. A third warning seems warranted regarding skin contact. With a close physical greeting, you can "infect" your counterpart with the scent, which some may not always appreciate. The YouTuber "Redolessence" has compared this effect to the multiplication of bacteria, which seems like an appropriate analogy to me. Overall, a beautifully warm and noble evening scent for men in rather smart clothing and for special occasions.

With Dark Aoud, I was already convinced that I quite like oriental agarwood when it is not used too dominantly. Following Ergoproxy's tip, Aoud Musk was the next promising test candidate for a (A)Oud fragrance that does not completely overwhelm beginners. And it truly does not, as long as one is not put off by the top note, which, typical of Montale, is quite pungent.
Regarding "Duro," the often-cited twin fragrance, I have previously expressed plenty of sharp and harsh criticism; I can hardly tolerate the flat, loud, sweet 5.1-surround wood-balm pressure.

Sometimes one wonders why Pierre Montale still enjoys a relatively noble reputation. It must be due to the chic bottles, because he often quite obviously fires up the copier and still doesn't make it any cheaper. Inspiration aside, that's not necessarily a bad foundation. What is more decisive is that his attempts at copying are more or less worse than the originals.

In search of fragrances, while reviewing my bottles and considering which of my preferred scent directions needed to be complemented, I concluded that I was missing an alternative Oud fragrance to my beloved "Bois d' Oud" by Perris Monte Carlo. An Oud fragrance with at least subtle flowers, without rose, but not too smoky and not too animalistic in its intensity.

I must admit that I find the scent theme of Oud quite fascinating. O.K, the scent component has a rather peculiar aroma, but the interpretations of the various brands of this component are often extraordinary, sometimes even borderline. Auod Musk is a real surprise for me! From the name, I expected a proper stink bomb. But I was mistaken!

I like fresh and citrusy scents. And this fragrance feels more robust after the woody heart note. It's a completely different direction from Yves Saint Laurent. Most fragrances from Yves Saint Laurent lean towards the spicy oriental direction, while this one goes in the fresh direction. The longevity is decent at 6 hours. The sillage is also acceptable.

Kouros, M7, Rive Gauche, Pour Homme... and those are just the most prominent ones from the men's line. All groundbreaking, grandly daring fragrances. And for some time now, YSL has only been releasing unnecessary flankers to its bestseller and flagship L'Homme. I believe it’s hard to get any less bold than this. With this, YSL has reached a new low, similar to Gucci. But unlike there, the great classics have not been completely discontinued, which is worth something. L'Homme Sport is, in short, the original, just lighter, more citrusy, duller, more summery, and therefore certainly not a bad fragrance. But it has as much justification and sense to exist as a broken little toe. A creamy-serious apple, for all fans of Boss Bottled or those who find the original too heavy for high summer. However, I would definitely still prefer to use the original even in summer, just with a restrained finger on the spray head. The scent feels like an aldehyde- and iron-infused L'Homme and is not particularly suited for any sport. Cardamom is in every second new designer bottle anyway, so to speak the sweet all-purpose weapon that simply annoys and frustrates me with such releases. And that with a fragrance that actually smells fine. Times change and so do you! Bottle: used to be nice... but even that annoys me by now. Sillage: summer-appropriate, muted, and lighter than L'Homme. Longevity: 5-6 hours withstand a vigorous workout. At least with the once super successful L'Homme line, YSL has now reached Boss level and annoys those I know. Better to discontinue everything except for the two origins of this L'Homme plague... because La Nuit and the original are worth every cent and real gems!

The topic is not new: anyone who already has a successful fragrance "on the market" and launches further flankers more or less profitably inevitably wants to bring out a sport variant as well. Of course, this is legitimate and tempting from a short-term economic perspective, but it could dilute the brand in the long run. With all the flankers of L'Homme, hardly anyone can keep track anymore, so the sport variant doesn't really matter anymore. At least L'Homme Sport comes just as one would imagine: classic with a high citrus content, somewhat pleasantly bitter at the beginning, then a bit sweeter later on. If you dive in a bit too deeply, its artificiality is revealed, which can be forgiven due to some fresh and well-balanced light spicy notes. Besides aldehydes and bergamot, the individual components are difficult to identify. It feels like 2/3 of all shower gels that can be perceived between the shower stalls of typical fitness studios or swimming pools smell similar. This is somewhat acceptable, but from YSL, I would expect more than just a red stripe and an average shower scent in the bottle from a quality sport flanker of the L'Homme series. Back then, the label was considered quite innovative olfactorily. It seems they have moved away from that, as here they prefer to extract a lot from the umpteenth flanker with little effort and investment. One could also see it as sporty, but it is not!

Hard to believe, but among all the Night, Nuit, Black, Dark, and Intense fragrances, a Sport perfume has made its way back! Surprising, since the boom of dynamic representatives was already two years ago and has noticeably faded...! However, since there is already an "intense" counterpart with L'Homme Parfum Intense, L'Homme Sport has long been overdue! I now adapt "L'Homme" to "L'ooooongweilig"! With "Sport," this is already the 11th offshoot - practically a whole football team! More shouldn't come, aside from further unnecessary Eau d'été's...the cash cow is, in my eyes, really milked dry, and it's time for something completely new (see, for example, L'Homme Idéal by Guerlain)! Nevertheless - the bottle - still always stylish and masculine. But no longer as high-quality as it once was. Connoisseurs know that the massive metal cap has unfortunately had to give way to cheap plastic! The spray tube is kept in typical "Sport" red. The face, always - unlike the flankers - is the French actor Oliver Martinez! This time sleek on a motorcycle and in a black trench coat! As for the scent - the opening impresses with a lovely shiny bergamot. It gently settles in the nose. A mild, slightly sweet citrus aroma makes me think of Dior Homme Sport and The One Sport by Dolce & Gabbana. In my opinion, the direct scent twin is the new Boss Bottled Unlimited. The classic L'Homme Original, on the other hand, comes across as really distinctive and angular! As it develops, floral, spicy notes (cardamom) already signal the fading of the scent! After half an hour, the fragrance retreats more and more - I can no longer perceive it after two hours! Disillusionment sets in! The drydown is a generic mix of dry, woody nuances. Absolutely monotonous and interchangeable - present in a thousand other men's drugstore fragrances! L'Homme Sport doesn't offend, but it also doesn't stay in memory! It lacks depth, character, and flair! I also miss the typical L'Homme lemon note that runs through the entire progression. The longevity with sufficient dosage is about 6-7 hours...most of the time, however, the dull base takes over! Sillage is virtually zero... In summary, L'Homme forms the crowning "L'ooongeweile" conclusion of the series! What started cheerfully and interestingly ended in bitter disappointment - no matter how relaxed, cool, and casual Monsieur Martinez cruises around on his scooter.

Sport, xtreme, what else do I know. All these labels have been experiencing inflationary and sometimes annoying usage for about four or five years. This is the case with this offshoot of the otherwise good but also weak lhomme. Unfortunately, I recognize nothing that makes me want to applaud. No, I bought this fragrance in a mood where I somehow thought of the good, new, excellent, to wear in over 30 degrees. Unfortunately, this is not the case at all. Now I have this bottle and find the synthetic flanker simply inappropriate. The father lhomme is somewhat similar to the Bottle from Boss. Also not really the egg of Columbus, but still wearable and acceptable. This Sport, however, in comparison to the Sports from Dior or Kenzo, simply falls short. No Messieurs de Loreal, you have many better perfumes with style and charm, but this Sport is only male. Unfortunately, the aldehydes are so dominant that the actual building blocks like bergamot or cedar are completely pushed aside. This remains the case even after a long duration. The scent unfortunately remains consistently uninspired and flat. From a design perspective, the presentation of the bottle is impressive. Still, it is always about the building blocks of a fragrance and not just the design. Since I only know good fragrances from Loreal, I am very disappointed with this one and cannot understand how such an unfinished product could be brought to market. If something is not particularly good, even the best marketing is of no use. In marketing, one usually starts from the opinions or tests of consumers. This was probably somehow forgotten in the rush in Paris. Presumably, Monsieur Demachy from the other big fragrance manufacturer is so dominant that everything normal had to be thrown overboard in haste and fear. I am eagerly waiting for a new fragrance surprise from Loreal, where I can once again be the first to sing a great hymn.

I hope Yves Saint Laurent finally stops ruining the beautiful, classic "L'Homme" by diminishing its reputation with ever-new, fleeting fragrance trends. Why release a sport version of an already fresh-spicy scent?!

The L'Homme line from Yves Saint Laurent wavers between genius and madness. The new offshoot in a chic, trendy sports outfit clearly belongs to the latter. The opening is still quite pleasant, as it strongly reminds one of the round citrus original, which is not for nothing a modern classic. After that, however, this new "L'Homme Sport" becomes somehow strange.

Well: the fragrance is not as bad as it is made out to be here. It has only a slight L'homme DNA and no significant development, which I do not hold against the fragrance. It leans more towards Armani Code Sport (but less piercing) or Allure Homme Sport (but rounder and less chemical). The longevity is normal for a citrus-based fragrance (normally low).

A word of caution, to start off; don't be fooled by the bottle and its seemingly innocent appearance. The elixir within is far removed from any semblance of purity. ToyBoy is an interesting fragrance. That's the simplest way to explain it. Interesting. Unfortunately, however, ToyBoy is anything but simple. It's complex, nuanced and a head scratcher (and turner) to say the least. Now I haven't had the pleasure, or privilege, of putting my nose on many (or any) particularly high end rose fragrances, so I won't be able to comment on how it compares in terms of quality. However, for something so inexpensive, it doesn't smell too terribly synthetic to my untrained nose, nor does it smell like your traditional, deep red rose (a la American Beauty). No this is a greener, less mature flower. And that's what makes it so decidedly erotic in my opinion. It smells like the remnants of an encounter of the most personal nature, like walking into a gathering after indulging your baser instincts only minutes prior. And in this specific scenario, it's decidedly feminine. However the fragrance as a whole, is absolutely not. The "green" smelling rose is mixed with a spicy clove accord that flits through, taking from the delicate nature of the rose and adding something rugged to it. And as the scent goes towards it's dry-down, the clove and rose is joined by a warm, woody musk, and something bitter and earthy, to flesh it out even more. The rose accord stays throughout, and is prominent, but is tempered by the other more traditionally masculine notes coming into play. Don't get me wrong though. This is anything but a subtle seductress. It is powerful, and lays claim to your body as its own, so be prepared to wash it off and burn your clothes to get rid of it. I wouldn't say this is a unisex scent. It is masculine, no doubt about it. But it takes a certain kind of man to pull off, and it's definitely not everyone's cup of coffee. It takes a great deal of confidence in yourself and your sexuality to pull this scent off. But if you're unapologetic, then the salacious blend of taboo and carnal want that is ToyBoy will definitely suit you. ToyBoy is risqué, unapologetic, and evokes imagery of the least appropriate nature for mixed company. Is it worth trying? Absolutely. Is it blind buy worthy? Most definitely not. To summarize: Erotic. Bold. Unapologetic.

I knew this almost a year ago in a local perfumery. I have to say though, if you haven't tried this fragrance already, smell it with an open mind. You might think: Why? Well, it is a very unique smell. I think it is extremely challenging culturally here in Mexico, even to the point where i have known at least one comment of a person in a perfume group being afraid of projecting a "gay" image of himself for wearing it. It is still quite a taboo here for a man to wear a floral perfume, (The same way it is also quite a taboo saying that a men uses "perfume" instead of "lotion", equivalent of "cologne" here in Mexico, damn with those boomers...) and the LGBT - culture - influenced ads of this perfume also add to this overall taboo using Moschino Toy Boy. That is exactly the same reason that makes this frag a sexy beast. I don't think it is particularly masculine, it leans towards masculine but it is quite unisex, yet, i don't see women wearing it. To my nose this is one of the weirdest fragrances i have ever tried. Let's describe it as a rose covered in pink pepper, and you throw on top of it a huge juicy pear... In that sense, it is a purely italian fragrance. And to some, the opening smells like tamarind, a typical mexican "fruit". (I am from Mexico and i personally don't know what the heck a tamarind actually is) Then it dries down to an extremely sexy and lovely, powdery rose, and in the base we have some musk and woods. So, its drydown consists of the pepper - rose combo with woods, mainly of vetiver, amber, musks, and it also retains a slight citrus nuance throught, i guess from Elemi or the pepper itself, since bergamot has faded away pretty much completely by then. I personally am very happy of knowing this and having one of the greatest memories in my life while wearing it. I used it on a first date that i was wanting to get since i met the lady, and it went so nicely, i would actually say it was the greatest day in my whole life. Having met the girl (Surprisingly she asked me for my number) while i was wearing a leather (faux) jacket and looking quite edgy, i didn't knew what to wear on the actual date. I asked a friend who recommended me showing a refined, even delicate aesthetic. I then put on a cardigan sweater over a t shirt, wore a quite messy hair and some all black Chuck Taylors. And on top, the greatest thing i could have worn: The rose Moschino frag. Unfortunately i sold it some months ago, not because i disliked it, but rather because i needed some money and it reminded me painfully of that person and the ending of the relationship with her, my "guera". (A gorgeous, slightly blonde girl from the city, the person i have loved the most in my life) Bottom line: I am biased with this frag, it is part of a mixture of memories involving several senses such as sight, (Looking at the city) smell, (This frag) hearing, (Music) eating chocolate with her and touching her hand as the most awaited and wished thing i could ever do.
