Smell it PD: Some say it should be used ONLY in winter and by night. Are you serious? I have worn this in dog days of summer where i live and it comes out perfectly fine. Not its best climate by any means but it's swiss knife - versatile as well. Just control the sprays. Nor formal nor heavy projecting by any means as well. Don't be ridiculous

This is a gorgeous scent. It is a very pleasant smell that I think is totally unisex. The opening with that soft pink pepper and pear is so addictive and moreish to smell. The smooth Rose blended with the vetiver gives a silky smoothness to the perfume. It's a very pretty smell. Definitely no skank or hardness to it. But the vetiver and amber base stops it from being overly feminine. And makes it cling to the skin. And gives it a solid foundation. So good longevity and Sillage overall. Amazing and unique. Scent 10/10

My friend and dear YouTube subscriber Eduardo commented yesterday on my channel that he would appreciate if I said something about this fragrance. So, I went to the shopping mall to smell it. Let me start with the bottle. I really don't want this in my cabinet. It's insanely tacky, looks cheap and didn't feel good in my hand. Also, the advert, a half naked man in leather pants, looked quite off-putting to me. I mean, a naked man in leather with a kid's toy on his lap... let's better not continue this thought... I'm a teacher, I teach little kids, and something like that just doesn't feel right to me. The only good thing about the bottle is (since I really want to find something positive about it), that the word 'DECAPITATE' reminds me of Sheldon Cooper. TBBT fans will know what I mean. Now to the scent... HOLY CAT, IS THAT BAD! I want to get rid of it NOW. And I have this feeling since I've sprayed it on MY SKIN. Why do I always sacrifice myself like this... ROFL! It's terribly blended. The opening made me gag. There was some very peppery, spicy-resinous pear with the quality of a cheap celebrity-perfume fruit. And this resinous something slathered over it was just WRONG. Maybe, what they wanted to achieve with that is creating a sexy-erotic fruit... Because of... toy boy... FAIL. And then the worst thing happened: A cereal-nutty smelling flower appeared, a very strange rose I have never smelled before, and cloves. WHAT THE CAT IS THAT?! Now, in the very drydown there is this cereal-nutty flower and a huge load of cashmeran which tries to decapitate EVERYTHING including some very synthetic ambery animalicness which has a slightly sour-earthy background. Might be some vetiver but in combination with the cashmeran and the animalic-ambery something it's just... WHY?! Final thought: Let's take a shower and SCRUB THE HELL OUT OF MY ARM to make it disappear. One more positive thing: What comes out of the decapitated teddybear is STRONG. It projected and projected and still does. After 2 hours. I need a shower.﻿

Disagree: Don't get it wrong, this is not a rose forward perfume, this is a spicy first, floral second perfume, I tested this and then let my wife smell it, she said it smelled like a bunch of freshly cracked peppers on cutting board made out of rosewood, and that's a pretty accurate observation, pink pepper has that floral undertone to it which helps the rose shine even more, so it's not a punchy in your face rose. Agree: It's creamy and a little juicy/fruity, and up until that point everything is slightly masculine, but no more, as soon as it becomes a skin scent, this delicate amber sweetness comes into play, and now it turns completely feminine, so feminine in fact that I decided not to get it, this has nothing to do with boldness or confidence, if you are the most masculine man out there, you're not gonna be comfortable wearing feminine perfumes, that's just a fact, however I agree, it's a unisex creation, pretty unique and pretty bold of Moschino to market it as masculine, but that's to be expected, Moschino are nothing if not bold. Disagree: I'm also finding myself come to a complete disagreement with people saying that this is a linear, one dimensional fragrance, opening is spicy floral masculine, the dry down is resinous sweet feminine, it's like a two faced clown, and not a funny one, but rather a surprising one, in a very pleasant way. Notes detected by my nose: pink pepper, floral notes, pear, cloves, sandalwood, amber and bergamot. Not blind buy safe at all, this is a very specific and acquired taste, not for everyone. Performance is monstrous for both longevity and sillage. Although unique and really pleasant, sadly the dry down turned my away from this fragrance, my wife might get it though, lol

"OK Boomer" is a catchphrase and meme that gained popularity among younger cohorts from 2019, used to dismiss or mock attitudes stereotypically attributed to the baby boomer generation. When you look at how this perfume is presented, the bottle in a shape of bear you might be under impression that it more for a younger audience.

Toy Boy opens with a blast of green immediately followed by nose-hair-singeing pepper. Very strong pepper. The rose begins to appear and is quite clearly present but the pepper dominates. This transition completes shortly after initial application and the fragrance remains linear after that for hours.

* NOTE: This is not a complete review because I haven't been able to try the fragrance multiple times in different occasions for reasons which I describe below: * I don't like talking about fragrances that I dislike, but given the immense hype of this "Toy Boy", I feel obliged.

When I bought it I was a bit worried about what many mentioned "love it or hate it" because of the rose, floral, unisex and feminine side, but that is something subjective and that each nose develops and evolves according to their olfactory experiences.

THIS IS A ROSE! No way around it. The rose isn’t playing backup here—it’s front and center. It's the whole damn show. Toy Boy perfumes wonderfully while not being thick and lipsticky like Portrait of a Lady, and it’s not syrupy-sweet like Oud Satin Mood. It’s also not that soft, airy vibe you get from MFK's L’Homme À la Rose. The best way to describe it?

At first smell, it is very reminiscent of Tuscan Leather. But a few moments later it's own identify emerges in full bloom. A soft leather sweetened with a dried fruit accord and spiced with saffron. In. Perfect. Proportion. Because its dried fruit, it's not a fructose intense like fresh fruits. And because it's a dried fruit accord, it's not fruity smelling either. It you've ever had fresh dried fruits then you're aware of now it's fruity and sweet but not intensely fruity and richly sweet like fresh fruit. A lot of you at this point are probably wondering if it's similar to the Serge Lutens dried fruit accord. No it's different. Serge's accord is more of a compote. Stewed dried fruits where the fructose is escalated. Over here the fructose is muted. The saffron accord smells solid. Like a concentrate of saffron. There's a milk tea we prepare over here that is emphasized with saffron. Some people add strands of saffron to the boiling tea or while it steeps. I like to drop a few strands into a 20ml cup of boiling water then let it infuse for a few minutes. You end up with very concentrated saffron water. But because you add it to liters of tea it's not bitter. The saffron in Noble Leather is like this. Robust and concentrated but perfectly balanced with the dried fruit accord. Highly recommended if Tuscan Leather , Clive Christian C & Cuir Ottoman appeal to you.At first smell, it is very reminiscent of Tuscan Leather.
THIS 1 START CREAMY LEATHER WITH HINT OF VANILLA,AROUND A NICE FRUITY BACKNONE!! "MASTERPIECE" IN MY BOOK, IMAGINE THE MAGIC OF JUBILATION XXV MIX WITH RUM,HINT SPERITEUSE DOUBLE VANILLE!

Empty bottles, men, and barrels were everywhere. Although the men were rather the opposite of empty. It smelled terrible of leather, alcohol, stale smoke, and other reminiscences of a night spent partying. Wolle and his rockers were celebrating his successful roadshow regarding his candidacy for mayor of Herne. Last night, victory was expected. How did it come to this? Flashback: With the help of his lawyer Cravache and the bald millionaire Bastian, Wolle founded his own party, aiming for comprehensive alcohol supply. Wolle noticed that schools only offered drinks like milk and the like. Worse still: various restaurants didn’t sell beer. So he felt compelled to act and founded the BRU, the Beer Belly Rocker Union. With catchy slogans like “Beer even before four,” “No power to drugs except beer,” and “Wolle, you flamenco dancer,” they laid the foundation for the Beer matter movement and thus also won the hearts of the people of Herne. They expected from Wolle a disruptive politics, a breakthrough into new times. For this reason, the sitting mayor Salomon Sucher, known to everyone simply as Schatz or Schatzischmatzi, had to dig deep into his repertoire (hahaha, I’m so funny...) and found a fragrance with which he wanted to counter Wolle: YSL - Noble Leather. This fragrance opened with the often-smelled leather plus a fruity touch. Here, it was not raspberry but dried fruits, reminiscent of Charriol - Royal Leather. However, the saffron is subdued; unlike the reference work, it remains very sweet and minimally fruity. The leather remains dignified, rather creamy smelling than really smelling like leather. Perhaps it is appropriately a high-gloss leather for YSL. With this scent, Sucher felt equipped. High-gloss, not too wild and fruity, he found that fitting yet still attention-seeking. So he wandered from event to event and delivered his speeches. But everywhere, his scent was compared to the Ombre Leathers and Tuscan Leathers of this world. So was his politics. Nothing stood out these days. Thus, Salomon Sucher gradually became more of a sweet-talker in his quest for votes. Or was it the fragrance? It now offered more room for vanilla, becoming sweet. Wolle, on the other hand, traveled from corner pub to corner pub, often falling drunkenly from the podium or being brought home in a beer cart or wheelbarrow, often pulled through the crowd. The people of Herne liked that; Wolle was one of them, Wolle stood for the local color of the Ruhr area. When Schatz Sucher then also came up with the idea of the pubs, it was too late. His scent had faded or was just a sweet-creamy leftover potpourri, and there were no more listeners. Slowly, it dawned on Salomon. The triumvirate of Wolle, the devil-dancing lawyer, and Master Clean from the region would defeat him. Present: “Wolle!” “W-w-what?” “Wolle, look at the clock, we’re late for the election!” Wolle looked at his watch with the yellow sponge on it. “W-w-what’s the big deal..,” Wolle mumbled drunkenly. “We were well in the lead, and even anti-alcoholics like our lawyer C. Ravache wanted to vote for us.” “He’s lying on the bathroom tiles; must have had something else too much...” “Most of our supporters will go to vote despite our premature revelry yesterday.” “Your words in Ceres’ ear, Wolle.” And so it happened as it had to: Wolle and his team lost the election by a landslide because almost everyone in Herne had gotten so drunk in anticipation of victory that simply no one went to vote. No one? Well, a trickster from Herne-Crange did, but otherwise only S. Sucher and his small base. Noble Leather was already no innovation at the time of its release. Nevertheless, it offered a wearable leather fragrance for anyone who doesn’t like leather in the sense of Tuscan Leather but still wants to smell that way. Today, it is one of many, as over the years fragrances like Ombre Leather have emerged, which can easily be classified in the same category and are significantly more popular. Thus, Noble Leather has been caught up and now blends into the masses. Unfortunately, it is also not as good as the reference fragrance I mentioned from Charriol. Although saffron becomes more prominent after hours, much has happened by then. Noble Leather is therefore not bad but, in my eyes, just one of many.

Even after what feels like the hundredth leather-fruity scent à la Tuscan Leather, this combination remains beautiful... although worn, well-known, and somewhat boring-lacking innovation, it still smells extremely elegant and sexy. It's actually a shame that none of these dark-sweet leather fragrances are in my collection yet. Noble Leather has jumped on this successful bandwagon quite late, but it does differ somewhat noticeably from the Tom Ford trendsetter. Noble Leather truly smells fantastic. Dark leather, but this time absolutely soft, sexy, and without losing any of that slight aloofness. In the end, there's only soft vanilla that can compete with the finest in the industry. Before that, alongside the leather, there's a light hint of fruity shisha tobacco and definitely a slight oriental feeling, so the name is indeed fitting. For going out in a dark suit, I believe you can't smell any richer. These leather fragrances smell to me like pure luxury, money, and many even say drugs. As for the latter, I can't say for sure, but a Tony Montana would definitely not say no to this oriental leather bomb! Bottle: I actually find it charmingly beautiful and fitting for this type of collection. Sillage & Longevity: 10 hours with more than good sillage - that's impressive! One of the softest, most charming, sexiest leather fragrances and more than just a latecomer clone!

Raspberry-leather (or here dried fruits) is currently very much in vogue in Flui's nose. And there are already quite a few comparable fragrances out there. Starting with Tuscan Leather (ridiculous price), over Godolphin (who needs 125 ml?), Vicolo del Sellaio (a lesser-known La Collina Toscana, but a bargain) to Black Saffron by Byredo. Although Flui has little to no affinity for Yves Saint Laurent, today Noble Leather was tested. Among the fragrances mentioned above, NL is truly the most delicate and also the most subtle. NL feels more spun than crafted. The scent does not convey any impression of heaviness or effort. Quite the opposite, it represents olfactory lightness, a serious leather of nonchalance. The oriental character? In Flui's opinion, it has turned out to be very non-committal, not at all overwhelming. And this is really beautifully designed, as it is so restrained, almost shyly composed. The vanilla is not sunk in but rather blown in. As for the leather, we have here finely spun leather. A taut canopy unfolds. A leather canopy with oriental supports. In contrast, Tuscan Leather is more like a massive skyscraper and a waterfall, whereas NL represents a fine fountain. Through the wafted vanilla, the canopy stretches a bit and begins to arch slightly. Here, in my opinion, there is a strong contrast to Tuscan Leather, which showcases its concentrated smokiness. NL displays its spirit-lifting quality. NL does not bubble, it glows, finely balanced. It never pushes beyond itself. What I find fascinating about NL is that it does not strive for depth; I perceive the opposite, the noble leather somehow strives upwards. I would like to interpret the leather in a somewhat dreamy direction. The sweetness is the spirit that builds the body. Without the sweetness, Nobile Leather would not be Nobile Leather and would be an indecisive spirit. So strong in the background, and yet so much in the foreground, the sweetness provides the soulful strength.

When I started here a few years ago and embarked on the wild ride of fragrances, I first had to orient myself. For me, with my drugstore knowledge, there were three scent categories: very good, okay, and terrible. But since I couldn't really get anywhere with these criteria here, I had to do some research on what the "real men" wear. So come on, "leather.

I personally don't have much experience with leather scents, so during another visit to what most here call the Turquoise, I discovered Noble Leather by YSL, which was filled in a truly elegantly designed bottle.

Noble Leather truly smells exactly as described above: leather, amberwood, patchouli, and the dried fruits are very clear and transparently identifiable. What makes the fragrance interesting for me is the impression of something burnt, charred - smoky-resinous, like burnt, cooled firewood.

When I stumbled upon this fragrance through random research, I remembered that I actually have a sample of it that I had saved! I immediately tested it and was surprised ;) In the opening, you are instantly greeted by the La Nuit de L'Homme L'Intense DNA, which I really, really like. It’s truly delicious and sweet, with dried fruits and spices.

I suppose the easiest way to describe this would be a warm, earthy (with slightly herbal opening) spicy scent. However the floral quality gives it a soft warmth (especially in the dry down). An unoffensive, warm scent that lingers and shines on your skin. A different scent among so many.

Moschino Uomo? is a fresh aromatic woody scent released by the house of Moschino. This is a very classy underated masculine citrus Italian scent. Although released in 1997 it does not smell too dated. I get the velvety lemon notes from the Kumquat and also some sage on the opening and then the woods and cinnamon come more into play on the dry down. There is a little sweetness perhaps coming from the cinnamon leaf and wood accords I think Uomo? is a very versatile scent which could suit any occasion but personally I think it works best for an office or work environment. Also I think this fragrance could be a compliment getter so it would work as an evening scent as well. I find the scent to have quite good longevity, around 7-8 hours . It is not a heavy fragrance so it has average projection and silage. I like the bottle design and although it has a plastic cap it fits very well with a secure click. This fragrance is also very inexpensive and because of the versatility and its uniqueness of notes I think this would be a great purchase. Overall 8.5

Scentrack: Jovanotti - Serenata Rap Like everything from Moschino Uomo is playful, charming and relaxed. Similarly to Moschino Forever it starts with exotic citrus fruit, followed by rosewood reminding me of the classic guitar smell and some aldehydes. In the heart cinnamon rides on the wave of flowery notes and gradually morphing to base of ambergris and musk. Easy to wear, typical Italian charmer. Like a watery aquarel of notes. Spring is a perfect season to wear this Italian good guy made by Olivier Cresp. Rating: 6.5/10

Stunning fragrance ! Clean, Soft and Light. It opens up with like semi sweet fresh citrusy , slightly spicy and floral notes in the background then dry down is musky woody. Moschino Uomo smells so good and very pleasant. This is perfect for the all seasons. I really enjoy it and I love Uomo ? MOSCHINO EDT FOR MEN. I'm so glad that I have it in my collection. Bravo Moschino ! Two Thumbs Up. Rating : 8.5 / 10

I don't know why i never reviewed this yet but here it is. Uomo? created in the late 90's by the great Olivier Cresp, is a fantastic value for the money you pay. I think the brand is discontinuing this (or they did it already). You find a bottle of 75ml for less than 20€! This is a complex scent. Nothing cheap or trendy. It's a soapy musk with citruses and some light sweetness. It opens up with the kumquat and Rosewood. The same rosewood you'll find in Égoiste but in a completely different scent. Its sweet, lightly rosey and citrusy. The Kumquat is the key to give this citrus sweetness glow to the fragrance. As it dries down, the soapy qualities became more pronounced and a more aromatic cinnamon note appears. It's not as dry or sweet as in other compositions. Here it is fresher (the hedione is floating somewhere here) and gives the light sweet alluring aspect to the fragrance. It's like a very fresh soapy scent with woody-spicy elements and a light citrus smell in the air. Very unique, alluring, masculine, versatile and great for the spring and summer! A fragrance that has good performance (i own a vintage bottle with the big black nozzle in the sprayer) and a bargain price. A must have in my opinion. 4/5

Clean sexy masculine but feminine enough that a woman can wear this the sage note makes it bright and evanescent with it's strong foundation of mahogany as the top notes the heart is an mildly spiciness or coriander and some green and leafy jasmine scent and the drydown of semi bitter ceder and rosewood for it's woodsy effect.

Very nice summer scent, just close your eyes, and you are in Italy. More in the warm city than on the cost. While notes can also be part of winter/autumn scent, surprisingly this is quite fresh but elegant at the same time. This is one of the summer scents without citrus fruitiness, it a great all-rounder. If only performance would be better.

Say what you want about the Italians, they do citrus RIGHT. Anytime a fragrance has a wonderfully classy lemon or other citrus note, I like to refer to it as an "Italian citrus". The original D&G pour homme had it, Versace pour homme has it, and this one definitely has it. Think of the clothing worn in "The Godfather" trilogy and you'll start to get the idea.

It always brings a smile to my yap when a blind buy is outrageously successful. Case in point I just picked up a 4.2oz bottle of Moschino Uomo? Online for the everyday low low low price of $18! A most satisfying fragrance that has some nose catching notes inside and ends with an animalic finish. Now this contains Ambergris and I'm not sure of the quality.

One doesn't have to pronounce the name of this with rising intonation @ the end does one? I'm not doing anyway! This is astounding - one of those outliers, value-for-minlet-wise. According to certain reports of its composition, it has real ambergris in it; & to my mind it does have the aroma as of one having it in.

Built from precious ingredients and expensive materials such as the sensual ambergris,the expensive orris,the unbelievable beautiful note of oakmoss,violets and peaches,sweetened by vanilla and complemented by fine woods and smooth labdanum,Semi Bespoke 5 is the fragrance that built an entire cult,making the whole world kneel at its feet. And then it was gone.poof!And Haute Luxe Roja was the main player...cause why not right? It was 2500 pounds for 100 mls(still is,but nevermind me),the advertising campain was describing it as the second coming.But then again,there was Unspoken,a 50 mls Roja Parfums which was pretty much there with SB5 and Roja Golden Flakes.The paper label Unspoken is unforgettable,it's so close to the both that is almost painful to pay the huge amounts for those than looking for a paper label 50s of Unspoken(which was discontinued and then reformulated and moved to heritage collection)which is not easy to find(people are NOT imbecils and they've noticed the huge similiarities)BUT not impossible. Nevertheless,if you get a chance and you love Roja Roja Haute Luxe,it's waaay better a SB5 or an old Unspoken xandra over

LIVE JAZZ comes in the clever guise of a folding screen. It's multi-facet panels (literally) reflect the multi-dimensions in Jazz and juice. The design details on the bottle are all about Contrast. And if you can't already guess, you're going to find out why ! The opening blast is lemony cool, high-lighted by spearmint. The lemon and grapefruit are more peel than juice. The accord is airy, fresh, bitter green, and "ozonic". A hint of grassy herbs in the background distinguishes this scent from the pack. But sooner than you can change into summer gear; a warm creaminess creeps in. This accord transitions into a "mid" -where suddenly, the (dinner) table... Flips ! Amber is the catalyst that begins to "cook" everything in it's warmth. The herbs morph from plant-like, to food-like. Reminiscent of the minty, lemony dish of seasoning that come on the side with your Vietnamese Noodle Soup -dominated by coriander (read cilantro), and simmering in a creamy rhubarb broth. What keeps this from turning altogether savory, is the sweetness of vanilla in the base, throbbing like a consistent beat. Personally, the addition of vanilla made this otherwise strangely refreshing scent a bit nauseating to my nose. But I must admit. This is wayyyyyyy interesting...and will no doubt leave few heads unscratched. LIVE JAZZ is a funky trip to Mabel's kitchen... To hear her nephew's jazz trio improvise, while she's cooking ! Certain food-like qualities to this composition (cilantro and rhubarb) may well be Pierre Bourdon's inspired cross reference of Jazz Music with Soul Food ! (Food for thought, anyway : ) In-spite of the intellectual shenanigan -LIVE JAZZ (as a casual fragrance) is ultimately an unpretentious, versatile, and unique alternative scent. Do I recommend it? It all depends on whether you have room on your playlist -for something as interesting, but just as flawed as...well, live jazz ! Longevity:7/10 (base notes) Projection (fall temperatures):6/10 (in mid) Art/Creatives: 8/10 (bottle and concept) How: year round, daytime, casual, free-spirited, laid-back. (Worth testing).

This is a refreshing one! I can't see why many people find fault with this fragrance. The opening is mint and grapefruit, very zingy and fresh, and perfect for hot weather I should imagine. This is the fragrance that brings to mind sipping cocktails on the beach, or coming in from the hotel swimming pool on a hot day. Very inoffensive. Yes it dries down to rhubarb and coriander, but that isn't a bad thing here! So maybe this "vegetable" thing (which I don't get here by the way) seems to turn people off but to me this shouts out "I'm fresh"! Personally I think you could do a lot worse than wear this on a spring/summer day. Plus, it's YSL and it's at an affordable price for such a house. I find it ideal for the hot weather! I believe that there is always an ideal situation for every fragrance... give this a try on a hot day by the pool and you'll see what I mean.

Very unique fragrance i must say, i didn't find anything similar to this one. Its refreshing but at same time is kind of warm to the skin, dont know which notes makes that probably amber. Definitive spring, summer scent which i enjoyed a lot

I'll start by saying that not everyone will like this fragrance. To be honest, I was turned off it at first. It seemed too sharp, too citrusy, too synthetic. It does improve as it settles, however the initial scent may have you running for the scrubbing brush. When I say too citrusy, that's not just me complaining because citrus is not my thing. The lemon and grapefruit tend to clash, creating a strange, sour sharpness that is more headache-inducing than refreshing. The mint is more like toothpaste than the fresh, green kind. The top notes, to my nose, just seem all wrong. The scent does improve thankfully with the introduction of the slightly spicy rhubarb and coriander. Live Jazz actually begins to smell somewhat delicious and starts to hint at an element of freshness, possibly even sexiness. The base is rather smooth, nutty and woodsy. I unfortunately didn't get much in the way of the vanilla, which was something I was looking forward to. Live Jazz has me changing my opinions every few seconds. One moment it will make my nose wrinkle with its acidity, the next minute it intrigues me. Personally, I probably wouldn't like a significant other of mine to wear this, seeing that it is so strong and so sharp. For some it may be their holy grail. Live Jazz does have a touch of classiness, however its ruthlessness happens to suggest otherwise at times. My only tip would be to apply sparingly, in fear of people dropping like flies in their millions.

Is it just me or does anyone else realizes that Live Jazz & Image by Cerruti are almost identical? Is it maybe the mint opening they both share? I think so! What Image has going on is a beautiful mint/pear opening that is so fresh, so crisp, so clean & out of the shower, while Live Jazz is fresh & clean but thats where it ends as far as the opening goes.. Live Jazz does not have that pear opening to give it that nice crisp edge but this is not a bad thing! As the scent progresses I still smell the mint along with some form of dusty lemon trailing the woods & vanilla base. I really like Live Jazz as Yves Saint Laurent makes great frags.. But for me this seems to be lacking longevity. I can smell it on me about 4 hours.. I would have to spray my shirt to get a longer scent life, over all I don't think its better than Image when it comes to the opening or the longevity... However, I will still enjoy this as it is well done!

I wonder why "Live Jazz" was discontinued. I wonder why "Live Jazz" hasn't been reissued and revived. I wonder why not more people celebrate it, know it, have it in their collection. I wonder why YSL can't manage that today. I wonder how one can slide so coolly at the threshold between the 80s and 90s (despite being from '98).

Actually, I wished for the JAZZ and received the LIVE JAZZ from my new perfume wizard for a test sniff. I must say upfront, it would have been a blind purchase, as I know neither JAZZ nor LIVE JAZZ, only the descriptions here in the forum and with the knowledge that one of my favorite noses, Jean Francois Latty, created the JAZZ.

So here we go... after several attempts to get acquainted with this individual scent, it's finally time for a summary. At first, I was quite sure: "The scent suits me," but then I became skeptical again. Overall, I tested it 4 times and came to a different conclusion each time.

For me, a very special men's fragrance that especially suits younger individuals. It comes across as very fresh and lemony and has something of a "just showered" vibe. Later, the warm, woody notes develop, although I personally can't detect any vanilla to save my life. I could even imagine this scent on a woman, although I don't particularly like it on myself.

Received as a gift for Christmas, hadn't smelled it for a while. Overall, a pleasant, invigorating fragrance. It starts with electrifying grapefruit-mint sprightliness; you can immediately tell it's made for the warm months. The mint really powers through strongly and revitalizingly in the first quarter hour.

I Love Love is very different from the original Cheap & Chic. There are very few similarities. This fragrance is quite fruity, Summery and fresh. But like all Moschino fragrances, do not assume that this scent is like any other. What starts as sugared fruits, almost like lemon flavoured sorbet, intensifies and becomes quite a crisp and colourful blend of both fruits and flowers, with a touch of pepper. I disagree with those that find this fragrance similar to D&G Light Blue. In my opinion there are no comparisons. Light Blue is quite sharp with its lemon notes and woodsy undertones, however I Love Love is so much sweeter and certainly more feminine. I would definitely choose this fragrance over Light Blue any day. The rose and the pepper notes in the heart of this fragrance, in my opinion, is what makes I Love Love so amazing. It is that transition from a bright citrusy opening into a soft, flowery yet spicy scent which gives this fragrance that undeniable charm. With fantastic lasting power and so many positive reviews, how can you not pass up the chance to own such a wonderful, (and may I add), affordable fragrance?

Moschino does a pretty good and bright citrus scent, and I suppose they do it by not burdening the blends with too many ~* serious perfume *~ staples or adding some kind of a twist to it. I Love Love has, like already stated, little to nothing in common with the original Cheap & Chic, which is probably for the better because it feels somewhat dated in the contemporary world. Short and sweet: I Love Love opens with a delicious grapefruit that is just tangy enough to make the mouth water, but sweetened just enough that it won’t turn sour at any point of its presence. Soon the grapefruit melds into sweetened berries laced with sugar powder and a little spice. The bouquet deepens and darkens a little until after 2-3 hrs it dissipates into a radiant white musk that lasts for hours and hours. Longevity is definitely one of the many happy surprises about this lovely edt. If I had to categorize, I would say I Love Love is a very young, carefree fragrance that is suitable for young girls looking for a cute perfume, but wholly suitable to older users as well provided you like sweetness and berries. I kind of wish the grapefruit lasted a little longer because it seems to me to be a hard note to play just right (as in not sour in my book), and Olivier Cresp, of Mugler Angel fame, does it flawlessly. It’s a spring/summer day scent that will surely brighten up anybody’s day and draw compliments from those who detect it. I’m definitely a fan and adding this to my wardrobe ASAP!

I am a Moschino fan, so when I saw this one on sale I grabbed it without sniffing (there was no tester and I have never been disappointed yet with a Moschino) Boy! Is this a fruity-fresh-summer-orangey-with-surprise-in-the-drydown scent! At first spray a freshly squeezed orange with zest and a bit of grapefruit greets me like it's the first morning! It's quite refreshing and cheery. (At this point I am wondering if it will be like Happy by Clinique?) Shortly after the citrus fruits popped their heads up, I can smell a hint of a red-current note and "can it be?" I smell far into the distance a flower note? Rose? Hmmm it's quite different. And halfway towards the drydown I can detect a soft powdery note that urges the fruity notes to calm down and settle. In the drydown it becomes apparent that the fruity notes listened and on my wrists there is now a powdery soft and very yummy fruity floral that is being embraced by cedar, musk and a hint of pepper notes. It's very yummy and a wonderfully cheery sunny summer scent, yet it's also very comforting and relaxing. To my nose it's not like Happy by Clinique -- Happy is far more linear whereas this scent is going through several stages of development that are fun to sniff! It's also nothing like another orange 'suspect' that I own and love, Liberte by Cacharel -- Liberte has patchouli & sandalwood notes that give it a smokey sensation. No, I can't detect any 'smoke signals' in I Love Love. No: I Love Love is the happy middle sister of the other two. A wonderful fruity/spicy/floral (more fruit and spice than floral) and is great for summer days & nights and all occasions you want to feel happy & sunny. Silage is: "Boy, this is one weird sunny yet delicious fruity aura" -- Longevity is:"I started out very citrusy, but give me a moment and I will be sweet, gourmand yet powdery for the next 5+ hours". Great fun to wear and a real happy scent for those 'pick-me-up moments'. Sniff before purchase it is a 'weirdo' that you will love or think too nuts for an orange! ; )

Citruses, unspecified berries. Very soft sillage, nearly immediately became a skin scent. I had to go look at the notes to say "yeah, I suppose that does kind of smell like currant" and nod to myself in a very smart way like I knew that all along. It didn't even necessarily smell too artificial. Just... cheap. Low quality? Either way, not great. Which is a shame, because I quite liked the notes below. Humid, warm and hay-like. I suppose that was rush? I wish there was more of that. I wish it ditched the upper notes altogether and just concentrated on refining that wonderful hay scent. But it is what it is, I guess. As the upper notes got softer and started fading away in about ~1 hour, it became almost pleasant. Warm cozy rush, faintly sweet rose and vague woods below. Cutesy, simple. A wee bit unique, but sensible. If it was made out of better materials, I think I would've genuinely loved it. But my nose felt like it was wearing a pretty frilly dress it bought for $20 from AliExpress. Adorable from a distance or if photographed in a dimly lit setting, but now it's 35°C and you're stuck at a crowded convention covered head to toe in cheap polyester blend. Gone in ~3 hours. Ah well.

I Love Love is the first 'real' perfume I ever bought, with my own money in high school, so it's always going to have a special place in my heart— and in my collection. Scent: The opening is very fresh, very citrusy, almost sour— a realistic lemon. This might be too strong for some people, but I love it, because I like smelling like a lemon. Also, I'm pretty sure this perfume has solidified my love for citrus scents in general, haha. It dries down to a softer scent, though, once the lemon has petered out. I can't identify all the notes individually, but it smells woody and spicy and just… good. Definitely a summer scent, very youthful. Good for everyday use too. 10/10. Longevity: The lemon doesn't last long, but I feel like citrus scents just don't last long in general, so I don't much mind it. The heart and base notes stick around, though, for 4 to 6 hours. 7/10. Bottle: Ok I know it looks goofy but I personally LOVE the bottle. The Olive Oyl shape, the contrast between blue and orange details, and the 'splotchy' design… they're iconic to me. I just wish they didn't put 'I LOVE LOVE' around the neck of the bottle, haha. 8/10. Value for money: If you buy it online instead of in a mall or perfume shop, this actually has really good value for money. It's tough enough for an EDT and it smells fresh and nice. Like I said, I like smelling like a lemon, and this is a cheaper alternative to, say, Maison Margiela's Under the Lemon Trees. 9/10.

I Love Love was my introduction to fresh citrus scents back when I was in my late teens. At first I really liked it, but over the years either my taste changed or this perfume detoriated as it started to smell bad to me. When I loved this fragrance it opened up with a fresh lemony smell. Almost like a zesty sparkly lemonade.

this is definitely the girliest scent i own. the opening is like sticking your head into the bubbliest sweetest cutest bottle of soda you've ever seen. also the olive oyl branding is sooo fucking cute. this really feels like a scent for the modern oyl. i can definitely smell the cinnamon notes too- this rocks i love how cute this is.
I have always liked D&G Light Blue and when my friend wore this to class i thought she was wearing D&G but it was this instead. not too bad, curious to try the lasting power

Usually not a huge fan of citrus scents but 'I love love' is surprisingly enjoyable. Juicy Grapefruit and sweet oranges are the initial stars of this perfume. I find the Lilly of the valley and rose tea notes stand out and the slightest touch of cinnamon. This is a great summer fragrance, it reminds me of going on vacation. Its giving me beach vibes.

I didn't pay attention before last summer. I was interested and It became loved from the first test. I purchased 100 ml and it's the best piurchase ever. It's sugary, spicy salad with grapefruits, mandarin, lemon. I wish it didn't be discontinued and was more long-lasting. One of the best smell of date of my birth (2004)

Parfumo forgot one of the most important and dominant note here: peach. It s a beautiful fragrance, a classic, and the one from this collection makes no.exception. it is very similar with the old Yvresse, it is potent and distinctive. Like NU, I have no doubt it will be soon put out from production. La Collection was indeed, a beautiful one.

My dear school friend Lena gifted me this fragrance for my birthday. It was a very thoughtful gift, as we had recently reminisced a lot about our youth, and this nostalgia often led us to think of a mutual friend. This friend was a classic beauty, even as a teenager, but not just that. She always managed to dress stylishly. She didn’t just follow trends; she had her own style, was individual and unmistakable. Her demeanor was light-footed, and everyone liked her or was in love with her. So did we. Moreover, she lived in an old villa surrounded by lush rhododendron bushes. To us, she was a fairy. And we were gnomes. We felt bulky, angular, our outfits were eclectic to downright ugly. We were not her. Of course, she also had a fragrance. Several, in fact. She was the first person I knew who layered scents. To this day, I don’t know anyone who can do it really well, but she simply had that talent for aesthetics, which extended to the olfactory as well. Many of the fragrances actually belonged to her mother, which is why she wore a mix of trends from the early 2000s, but also from the 80s and 90s. One fragrance stood out, however. I still remember how I smelled it for the first time when we were getting ready to go out. It smelled so good and warm, luxurious and mysterious. It was a scent for adults. Not Escada's Sexy Graffiti, a sugar bomb that I wore at the time. I asked her what this fragrance was called. She said, with her naturally perfect French pronunciation: Champagne by Yves Saint Laurent. From that moment on, the scent was etched into my olfactory memory. I associated it with the woman I wanted to become in my dreams. Rich, beautiful, sublime. Sitting with a glass of the finest champagne in front of a fireplace, engrossed in conversation. With a clear laugh that mingled with the rising bubbles in the glass into a radiant sprightliness. Flash forward to 2021, and I’m sitting with Lena over a cup of coffee, unwrapping her gift. At first, I’m astonished and curious about the bottle. She explains to me that it’s Champagne by YSL, just renamed to Yvresse. I can hardly believe my eyes. This is the scent of my youth! (Even though I never owned it). Nervously, I open the packaging and give a first spritz on my wrist. What feelings will arise when I smell it? Eagerly, I hold my nose to it and am confused. Is this really the scent? Somehow similar, but something isn’t right... I ask Lena what she thinks, but she seems to recognize the fragrance again. I attribute my confusion to my memory perhaps having distorted the scent over the years. I use it occasionally; I want to like it, but with the dry, earthy taste of champagne, this fruit bomb has nothing to do with it anymore. I don’t transform into the elegant woman by the fire, but remain the gnome with a few rhinestones glued on. With rose, violet, and the fruits, Yvresse is more like the big sister of Sexy Graffiti than the mysterious potion from my youth. In my opinion, the fragrance lacks the depth that the previous version had. The longevity is above average, which became a problem for me over time because I started to smell it everywhere. However, I’m not a fan of sweet and fruity scents, and this, combined with the bitter disappointment of not getting champagne but dessert wine, makes my review anything but objective. I hope you still enjoyed reading it; for me, this is my first contribution on Parfumo.

...there was a beautiful elegant fragrance. With a certain freshness, fruity-floral brightness. It was called Champagne back then, and like champagne, it also bubbled for me. I never owned it, but whenever possible, I liked to spray it on. Then it was reformulated, and the name was changed, and it was no longer as beautiful. Now I tried it again in the store, and reminiscing, I not only sprayed it on my hand but also on the sleeve of my jacket. A grave mistake, because after just a few minutes, a heavy, synthetic scent unfolded there, which only vaguely resembled the former Champagne. And this scent lingers and is very present. Unfortunately, since the jacket hangs in the hallway, it reaches me every time I walk by, intrusive, far too heavy and synthetic. I couldn't take it anymore and washed the sleeve. Well, sometimes you have to accept the past as past and let go! Looking back can have dire consequences.

I always enjoy testing Yves Saint Laurent fragrances, but this one was a tough nut to crack. "Yvresse" starts off quite harmless and sweetly scented like peach and powdered sugar. If someone has never sniffed powdered sugar; it smells only very subtly sweet, soft-powdery, and indeed like the respective fruit, but rather not like the original fruit, yet still nice. Now I see, it’s not peach, but apparently a mix of mandarin and lychee. However, this quickly fades into the background, because suddenly the fragrance becomes the most powdery one I have ever encountered. It is so powdery that it scratches my throat and I have to cough, and this happens repeatedly whenever I sniff it for a while. For a date where you want to get closer to someone, it might be better not to wear this fragrance. I imagine someone burying their nose in the other person's hair... That it still smells nice, I can only recognize much later when the scratchy character has faded and only a very smoky rose with a hint of violet remains.

My husband has the black Toy Boy and I have the pink Toy 2 Bubblegum, and I love both, so I was very eager to finally try the clear original version. Would be cute to have the whole family of bears in our home! Even though this is marketed as a feminine perfume, I find this rather unisex. It's very fresh and clean and smells like a good laundry detergent, which is a gender-neutral scent to me. I imagine the teddy bear from the fabric softener commercials would wear this, but I'm not sure if that's accurate, as I never use fabric softener. Notes-wise, the green apple is very prominent, which adds a shampoo-ish touch to the general cleanliness of the scent. Usually green apple is one of my lesser-loved fruit notes, but I enjoy it in his context. A touch of sparkling, sweet mandarin orange is noticeable, too. The rest of fragrance mainly consists of a radiant, fuzzy, modern white musk, maybe with a touch of woods. It's clearly a synthetic scent, but let's be real here, it would be impossible to have a natural smelling perfume that is reminiscent of fresh laundry. Clean always means artificial. Here, the synthetic vibes don't cross the line into harsh and scratchy, and that's what matters to me. I think this is great for summer, it makes you feel freshly showered on hot and sweaty days. Maybe I'll get a bottle if I still think about it next year. A child for our two Moschino bears.

1. Essentially, it is a clean blanket-like scent that has just finished washing. 2. I think anyone can wear it regardless of gender. This is not in the sense of unisex, but in the sense of asexual. In South Korea, where I live, men actually wear this kind of perfume. Byredo Blanche, Clean Warm Cotton and Cool Cotton, and even Bvlgari Omnia Crystalline... 3. The blanket-like scent gives a clean, neat, and refreshing feeling, but it also gives an unpleasant feeling on rainy or humid days. Probably because musk particles are big and heavy. However, Toy 2, which emphasizes the light and transparent scent of Fruity, has no such disadvantage. Instead, it doesn't feel cozy like a hotel. I also think it suits very young people only. 4. If you want a clean, cute scent, it's a pretty good choice. If you expect more from perfume, it's just so-so.

Toy 2 is pretty immediately sweet and fruity on application, but in a way that reminds me of Dawn green apple dish soap. It doesn't change much on the dry-down, either, so it's really just as though you've washed your hands... with Dawn green apple dish soap. Certainly fresh and clean, but might be better used as a layering scent with something that has a bit more body.

This one was really bad smelling to me. It smelled of super synthetic sweet bar soap, but inside a dirty shower full of mildew. I find it more floral (80%) than fruity (20%) and the longer I wear it the more nauseous I get. Will be scrubbing this off now, can’t wait long enough to determine longevity or silage. My sample was from a reputable decant site.

I bought this fragrance because I saw it being compared to Byredo's Blanche. I don't think it's a dupe, but I can see how they're similar. Overall, a successful blind buy! Toy 2 is a clean laundry scent, like the most comforting, cozy, and fresh detergent smell. The musk and floral notes are blended well so I can't pick them out individually. The green apple stands out the most, giving it a fruitiness that distinguishes it from Blanche. Completely inoffensive and office safe. This scent will never choke anyone out even on the hottest of days. The sillage and longevity are not great; on skin it fades quickly, maybe within 2 hours. It lasts longer on clothes, but I don't think it projects. Luckily it's affordable so I spray a lot. I actually use this one a lot more than I thought I would; rather than growing tired of it I continue to find it refreshing!

To start, I do not want to discredit anyone who likes this perfume! Everyone's nose is different. However, this simply wasn't compatible with mine. After spraying, it read as synthetic, strange, and overall, I felt that something was missing from the scent. It smelled like it should have rounded out to be warmer, but it was crisp and jagged instead.
... are made of this Who am I to disagree?

From the sea of bottles at Kstadt, the glass bear immediately caught my eye, and I had to hold it in my hands. Moschino had already delighted me with the original "Sidolin" bottles - but a teddy bear is even more my thing. What a sweet idea! I expected a sweet, playful fragrance - but not at all.

Hello you scent enthusiasts! :D Finally, I’ve written another review! Today, it’s about a fragrance that you may have seen often or at least noticed its bottle, as it features a cute bear. I’m talking about Moschino “Toy 2,” although I must admit that I don’t know the first fragrance at all and I’m only trying this one because a sample just fell into my hands.

.... And have no idea if I like myself today or not... ... And I'm hungry, but have no idea for what... ... Well, then I can do something with the bear. The bottle is cute, to say the least, although I had to laugh when I read the word 'uncanny' in one of the previous comments. The scent is not bad.

It is - and I am not sad about it at all - not even remotely mine: the world of the boulevard with its glaring lights, shrill sounds, and cheap bling. With centimeter-high letters in red and black on white, shockingly exposed, cringe-inducingly sensational. Colorful, Bild, Express, and whatever they are all called - over there on the island, it's The Sun. They show pictures I do not want to see and print texts that are so shallow and sandy that often not even the printer's ink holds. Boulevard, yellow press, fly-on-the-wall paparazzi - what good can come from that when they are the godfathers of a fragrance, I thought, even and perhaps especially when Roja Dove stands next to it?! Balsamic resinous-spicy opens "Buzz Entertainment Bottled" on my skin - the citrus-freshness of the pyramid may have swallowed the heat of these days; it cannot be found, no matter how hard I try. Instead, my nose detects a hint of hairspray, characteristic of white musk, which, however, is not listed. It feels a bit scratchy, but not really unpleasant. Minutes later, I imagine wood dust - a newspaper paper hint? - and a little later, vanilla strengthens on my skin, that smoky-tropical-dark one from "Noir Tropical" and "Eau des Missions". It is warm, it is gentle, and beautiful, not loud at all, not glaring and shrill - no paparazzi annoy me on my skin, nothing seems superficially covered up for the sake of effect. Summer-warm flowers are soon added, sharply cut - somewhere metal flashes for just a moment. It becomes warm again, sun-warm, wood-warm, flower-warm - a classically beautiful fragrance, very friendly-feminine, engaging and mature, indeed also elegant. With heart, with brain, with sensuality. A Roja - surely, though. What that has to do with the boulevard - no idea. And why it is discontinued, I now understand, whoever wants to. I will wear my last drop tomorrow - and say goodbye with a little sadness. PS: Bigalchen - thank you!

So, here we have a safari jacket. When I look at the advertising photo and the content of the rather straightforward bottle, I can only think of one association: BEIGE. I hate beige. Well, to be honest, I have nothing against the color itself, and I am not haunted by any traumatic childhood memories ... bullied and dunked headfirst into a school toilet full of beige liquid ... Unfortunately, I always see two types of people in my mind's eye when I encounter this otherwise quite understated elegant color. Both are German and give me an uneasy feeling. I guess I fear that I might someday recognize myself in them. On one hand, there are the over-70s who get open wounds from the slightest breeze ("IT DRAWS!"). It's certainly not nice, but I still find it incomprehensible why, after a certain age, one would dress entirely in plaster colors. After all, this way the latest Hansaplast doesn't stand out. Completely beige seniors, from sandals to fishing hats, are still an aesthetic thorn in my side. Iris Apfel is more my role model. On the other hand, I immediately think of the type of German tourists who wonder during their vacation in South Africa why people in Cape Town don't ride lions to work. Of course, they wear beige outdoor functional clothing with shoes from Jack Wolfskin even in the trendy hipster café in De Waterkant - safari jacket included. This scent has absolutely nothing to do with these two nightmares, and that delights me. Instead of a beige safari jacket, I smell a white shirt, so white that it almost hurts the eyes. It is worn by a handsome, cultured man (what was that again about recognizing oneself?), who might actually just be coming back from a safari. Or from work. Or from a shopping trip. Now he is sitting freshly washed, scented, and in a bright shirt comfortably by the pool of a beautiful winery in the Western Cape. They often have overnight accommodations, fine dining, and phenomenal views of the green, blue, beige of the breathtaking landscape. And pools. But one doesn't go in, because sitting nearby and sipping white wine looks much more "sophisticated". And that is how "Le Vestiaire - Saharienne (2015) | Yves Saint Laurent" smells to me! Very white and yet somehow colorful. Very green-citrusy-fresh, even though the initial explosion only lasts a few minutes. The scent quickly becomes intimate, as the sun slowly sets by the pool. At such times, one doesn't wear loud, long-lasting fragrances, because soon you retreat for dinner with good friends. You get closer, speaking softly. "Le Vestiaire - Saharienne (2015) | Yves Saint Laurent" also holds back and feels well-groomed. Then night falls and it gets cold. Off to bed, lights out, fragrance off. It was nice, even if it was just a brief pleasure.

On paper, this fragrance seems to be the ideal summer scent. And it actually delivers on its promise, but I was still disappointed after the initial sniff. According to my analysis, there are two reasons for this. 1) The neroli is lacking. With this note, the sun rises; it combines fresh citrus with warmth. But in Saharienne, it is a bit subdued. The opening is refreshing, which is further enhanced by the pepper, and as the fragrance develops, it becomes spicier, but remains cool and also a bit too clean. In the drydown, however, a nice earthiness emerges. 2) The scent sits on the skin. ..and does not melt into it. I suspect the musk behind this. Under this name, a range of scent notes can be hidden, from skin-like to laundry detergent-like. And here we are probably dealing with the latter. This gives the fragrance a certain soapiness. In itself, Saharienne is a nice scent, but in my opinion, it is a better candidate for a room spray or shower gel.

Saharienne is definitely zesty and certainly not my fragrance, but it deserves a review because it truly smells wonderful and evokes childhood memories in me. The scent starts off super bright, zesty, and very citrusy. I don't know why, but it reminds me a lot of citrusy men's fragrances from the 70s. That's how my father always smelled when he came out of the bathroom, freshly shaven and smelling like a lemon tree. That doesn't mean it's purely a men's fragrance, because it would smell just as great on a woman, but I just see my father in front of me, who unfortunately has not been alive for many years, when he came out of the bathroom well-groomed, fragrant, and in a good mood. I also see myself in front of me. I'm sitting in my pajamas, tanned from the sun. It's midsummer, and my almost white, typically Nordic hair is sticking out in all directions. I'm sitting at the breakfast table waiting for my father, who is still in the bathroom. Finally, he comes out. He sits down at the table and gives me a kiss on the cheek, and his usual "lemon scent" spreads through the room like a big sun of security.. For the first half hour, the fragrance smells very citrusy and fresh with bergamot, but also quite green from petitgrain. When the scent settles a bit, it becomes noticeably warmer and radiates like the sun on a warm summer day. Somehow, the fragrance exudes a sense of security, even though it is so bright and zesty. Neroli becomes more and more present now, and the sage adds a touch of spiciness/green to the scent. I honestly hardly smell the jasmine because the neroli is very dominant in the drydown. In the further drydown, the scent becomes earthier and even greener, thanks to vetiver and patchouli. A hint of musk sprinkles a little powder over this summery and very fresh fragrance. A scent that, as I said, is not at all my style and will certainly not find a place in my collection, but I still find it so pleasant and radiantly beautiful. Like a postcard from my childhood, with my father's signature. Radiant, warm, and always in a good mood.

I've looked many ways at this funny glass cleaner-shaped bottle which stayed on the drugstore shelf, but I never tested. Today I sprayed it on the papaer strip and on my skin too but I realized that this fragrance is really similar to a glass cleaner : fresh but very synthetic, quite similar to Davidoff cool water (or chalou blue by Lidl!!). Moschino's creations are particular and original mainly outside, but this one doesn't at all justify the price. I'm sorry, but I don't like it.

Super artificial raspberry, flowery air freshener and alcohol. The '00s are back and so is my mother who's already drunk again at 10AM in the morning. Only took 10 minutes to give me a headache. Once the initial raspberry cloud started dissipating, it managed to hit a new low and transform into a scent of body odor poorly hidden behind a cheap flowery perfume. Thankfully, it's pretty weak, so about an hour and a half into the experience most of the upper notes were already gone. Past the second hour mark the only thing left on my skin was patchouli. A shame, I really liked the fun campy bottle. Wish it didn't come filled to the brim with a visceral feeling of disgust.

I kid you not, the opening smells just like Windex or any other "zingy" household cleaning solution: synthetic citrus + strong chemicals. The dry down comes quickly, and is a very generic, unisex, bergamot-musky scent. This was too synthetic for my taste - but the bottle design is very fun, and they did make the "Windex" profile feel somehow wearable.

Windex, but make it *fashion* Moschino Fresh Couture smells like spring cleaning, elevated. If you've ever scrubbed every inch of your house with various products that smell like citrus and linen, you know the vibe. Squeegeed windows, polished woods, waxed floors, fabric softened sheets flapping in the breeze on the line in the backyard. While the top notes of bergamot/mandarin are really only present for the first ten minutes or so, the ylang-ylang hangs around to smooth out the heart of the fragrance. The middle notes are really interesting! Especially what the osmanthus does for the raspberry and peony. The raspberry turns almost sour, like it's not quite ripe, but not unpleasantly so. It's not a candy sweet, juvenile take on raspberry. The peony is green and woody, more unisex than I usually see in peony heavy perfumes. The base note patchouli and woods warm up and smooth the sharper elements of the scent, keeping it from being too uncanny and sterile. This is unisex, clean, suitable for daytime. An office friendly scent good for spring, summer and fall. I admit it was a bit odd at first, but I kinda dig it! -- This review previously appeared on another site under the name "PrincessPrickleson." That's me! I'm moving my collection to Parfumo.

Very disappointed, was expecting clean & fresh, bright, citrus forward… got kind of weak generic cheap weak citrus. The smell did not last on paper or skin, for more than an hour. The bottle is so cute though, just don’t be mislead by it! The other “Windex” scent (the gold bottle) isn’t any better.

I really wanted to love this perfume because the bottle is so clever in design, however, it is greatly disappointing. It has almost no longevity nor sillage. The scent is synthetic citrus with no middle or end notes at all. An hour later and this scent is all but gone forever, therefore I can’t justify the cost despite the really cute bottle.

Name: Fresh Brand: Moschino Line: Designer/Women/appears unisex Perfumer: Alberto Morillas Year: 2015/2016 Size: 30/50 ml Gender: metrosexual Price: 30-55€ Test basis: Manufacturer sample / one-time wear over a day Concentration: EdT Purchase options: Internet, somewhat rare. Not seen in stores yet.

One thing is definitely successful here: The scent absolutely corresponds to the bottle design and the image of the campaign. The second complete marketing gimmick after Toy also follows the same pattern: I have to at least test it. The result here too: You don't need a full bottle, and the scent is really nothing special. Fresh is, as the name suggests, a fresh fragrance.

Jingle cats, jingle cats Jingle all the way Oh, what fun it is to ride without a Putzfimmel or a Katzenwäsche by the way Hey, jingle cats, jingle cats Jingle all the way Oh, what fun it is to hide a bad Putzmittel by the way! Hey! Jingle cats, jingle cats Jingle all the way Oh, what fun it is to clean with a little smoky Himbeerrose by the way! Hey!

I find the scent absolutely terrible! I don't like fresh, unremarkable fragrances. Unfortunately, this one is such a candidate. But here I definitely count myself among the packaging victims! I just had to have the bottle. I own many fragrances, but I've never come across a bottle like this. And to top it all off, I had to buy the matching phone case for a staggering 80 euros.

My favorite Moschino: I adore Orientals and this one has that rare mix that smells wonderful on my skin. I adore Patchouli (in the right amount!) and this Moschino happens to deliver just that. A wonderful silage and a powdery dry down that always lures you with a hint of Patchouli! Wonderful!

For years now I have been passing this fragrance by on the stores, I never had any curiosity to try it, though I really love Moschino as a house and I really respect them for their unpretentious, simple and quality creations. So come months earlier I suddenly got my hands in small of bottle of this classic 80's scent, and oh what a pleasant surprise! I agree that this is spicy and soapy at the same time, a perfect combiination for cold winter days as the spiciness warms you up and the soapiness gives a clean feeling. You can immediately feel this comes from the glorious 80's, it has a loudness, it has a character. I cant feel the floral notes but i believe they are there to subdue the strong spices. I enjoy so much wearing it, probably my most wearable for the last months.. I think I will always have a bottle of it in my collection.

I find classic florals, such as Moschino by Moschino, more to my liking than the most current floral releases. Why? Because of all the reasons so eloquently stated by the previous reviewers. It's a perfume's perfume, with a richness, depth and maturity that recall a bygone era when mainstream perfumes weren't afraid to make a statement.

To me this is very herbal, spicy, warm and a little fiery but at the same time, a calm scent as well. The fire cools on you and lingers in the background. I get a lot of the amber, so in this respect it is a lot like a spicy, ambery type scent, perhaps somewhat like an Ambre Sultan type thing. The galbanum also reminds me of the incense vibe in Opium eau de parfum female version, and I find this fragrance equally amazing in it's dry down. I really like this fragrance, and whilst I originally bought this as a gift for a successful woman. I find it intoxicating and enjoy it on my skin as well (as I did with the richer, EDP female Opium by YSL). I think if you are a very successful type of female, probably in late twenties, early thirties onward, this can be a power scent. It says "I'm here, and I got here because I worked hard to be here" kind-of-scent. REAL women wear this, women who work hard and matter in their job etc. Very classy... and definitely highly recommended.

Utterly charming and mysterious perfume: musky tones, lovely flowers, a touch of vanilla, warm wood. Associations: cold winter mist, white damask, short days, a celebration, maybe even a wedding.. So glad I own a bottle.

Moschino's signature fragrance, MOSCHINO, is a real gem: a layered, complex, chypre-like oriental which stands out from the crowd with its marked marigold (tagetes) note and conspicuous absence of the sweetness which has taken the oriental category by storm.

Moschino is no doubt a classic fragrance which has somehow slipped under the radar during the last few decades. I very rarely hear of this signature scent by Moschino, it seems that their fruity florals and more modern offerings have gained them more success. A shame seeing how elegant and refined this fragrance actually is. Moschino is spicy yet soapy.

This is such a great fragrance for cold weather wear. If you like spicy Orientals, this is a must try because it is hands down one of the best iterations of the genre. Spicy, bitter, sweet, resinous, dry, floral, herbal, woody, and warm. It has it all and is all wonderfully done. The performance is beast mode in the best sense.

OMG... To think I almost returned this because I felt guilty for the impulsive blind buy (though it was cheap)! The shop wouldn't take it back though because it had been on sale, so maybe this was meant to be :-) I had set it aside for a few weeks, and just tried it yesterday. I love it!

First off I really wish I was around in the 80s to remember how vibrant it was, alas I was a child of the 90s. Wearing this beautiful scent makes me feel like I'm in the 80s, so intoxicating and alive. All the notes blend wonderfully with the patchouli really shining through. Can't recommend it enough all the other reviews say it best.

Yesterday, I happily received the sample of Floral Shock, as I enjoy the original Black Opium, and it even gets a good reception from my picky husband. The deliciously cozy coffee note appeals to both of us. Now the cover promises: the shock of an iced coffee, between pleasure and adrenaline. While I'm not directly shocked by the sweet fruity start - I am somewhat taken aback. The fruits make quite a statement, but the hoped-for coffee note only gradually and very shyly makes an appearance. I miss the coolness of iced coffee - it’s more like room-temperature, heart-friendly flower coffee. Speaking of flower coffee - some blossoms also peek out from the harmless drink. Not a bad scent - but pleasure and adrenaline just don't seem to kick in. Maybe I'm also disappointed because Floral Shock doesn't have much in common with the original Black Opium. If you consider Floral Shock as an independent fragrance, you might actually like it. But the title Black Opium is better left forgotten.

Since I quite liked Nuit Blanche, I requested a sample of Floral Shock. Before I comment on the fragrance, I must point out that I had quite high expectations, as I really like some scents from YSL and the bottle appealed to me. I can usually get very excited about extremely floral-sweet fragrances, so I became curious. Scent: At the beginning, I clearly perceive a very sweet milk coffee. Whether cold, iced, or warm: it doesn’t matter, this note stands out prominently for me. Along with a hint of cotton candy, popcorn, milk chocolate, and vanillin. The pear comes across as overripe and sweet; more like from a can than fresh and crisp. Lemon??? No, I don’t notice any of that, no matter how hard I try. I am usually very sensitive to lemon notes, but no, that’s not where the fragrance fails - it’s the flowers. Floral notes can be smelled, but they are very subtle and restrained. This is not how I imagine a Floral Shock!!! The freesia and orange blossom are drowned in the overly sweet milk coffee, which simply dominates everything. Here, the fragrance disappoints me enormously; I would have wished for much more pronounced flowers and expected the scent to be much fresher. On the test strip, the flowers develop much more clearly than on my skin, but ultimately, what matters is how the scent smells on a person. The fragrance is sweet and pleasant, but it does not meet my expectations at all, which the name Floral Shock suggests, and in my opinion, it is a victim of poor marketing. Sweet Sugar Latte would have been more fitting. When I smell it, I constantly feel reminded of La Rive dupes, which often come across as overly sweet and slightly synthetic. In comparison, the fragrance still holds up quite well, but it’s not quite enough to make the scent interesting enough for me to want to wear it as a perfume. It’s not a brutal flop, but I’m not exactly thrilled either.

In my opinion, the entire line of Black Opium is a complete flop, lacking character, expression, and any distinctive recognition value. Everything essentially has this cheap, fruity-sweet, and in this case, floral-shock, flowery-fruity-sweet mainstream character, absolutely interchangeable, replaceable, and basically negligible. There will be no Ooh's and Ahh's with this fragrance, and in response to any potential question "What are you wearing?" one would probably be very surprised that it is supposed to be a YSL - which used to stand for style formation, revolution, and exclusivity. The kicker is that for this fruity-sweet synthetic concoction, where the bottle is likely more expensive than the content, they still demand a very high price.

So, I will now also try my hand at a review. But where do I even start… I like Black Opium. I own the majority of the flankers (Illicit Green, Extreme, Intense, Floral Shock) and the original - and I have to say, Floral Shock is the only one that stands out to me. All the others smell absolutely identical on my skin after 1-2 hours. For some reason, that’s not the case with Floral Shock. At first, I strongly perceive a fresh pear, yes, sometimes even a bit of the citrus notes. Over time, the scent becomes sweeter and the typical Black Opium coffee/vanilla blend emerges. BUT: Floral Shock remains consistently lighter and fresher on my skin. Although I also like the regular Black Opium, I think this one is a bit more interesting, but also lighter/fresher. It’s suitable for spring, and for those who are bold, it can also be worn in summer. In my opinion, this is the best Black Opium here.

... full of anticipation, I naturally ordered 90ml and am torn. It smells sweetly floral but actually quite similar to Dior Girl. I had imagined a perfume shock in a positive way, similar to what I experienced with the new BonBon Intense. I will use it, but it won't become my new favorite scent, which is a shame for the price.

What a pity! Not nearly as floral as its name suggests. For me, the weakest fragrance in the line, a light version of the original Black Opium with a hint of floral note. Also in terms of longevity and sillage, it's a light version; after about an hour, I can only perceive the scent up close. On my skin, an unpleasant plastic note additionally develops.

...OK Floral Shock...we might have overdone it a bit. There isn’t much floral here and I didn’t get a shock either. I really liked wearing it back then. For me, it’s a light, airy, almost standalone floral mandarin scent. For die-hard BO fans, it’s probably a disappointment because the familiar DNA (coffee and vanilla) is nearly absent.

It started with a very bright, strong, cherry-flavored bubble gum ball - the kind you get out of a dispenser machine at the mall. Then, just like those same bubble gum balls, the bright flavor fades quick -- into a very soft hint of rose, a dash of rubber, and some powdery sweetness. I came here for the bubble gum notes, and expected those to last longer. I agree with a reviewer elsewhere - it's mostly just a sugary-powdery-sweet "basic rose" scent in dry down. Pleasant enough, but pretty quiet + synthetic. I prefer Bubble Gum Pop , and "Le Bubble Pop | Urban Outfitters" , over this.

Really loved this, it's like a sweet/ bubble gummy fragrance with a tropical hint, reminded me of Britney Spears candied fantasy ! The bubble gum/tropical vibe is so similar, the only difference is that, Moschino doesn't dry down with white florals. The scent is very sweet and pleasant, very comfortable and super easy to wear !

This may be an unpopular opinion, as this fragrance seems a little divisive, but I love this scent. Yes, it has more rose than you think it would, but it's a very sweet rose. I definitely still get that candy-like bubblegum scent from this, but more like a rose-flavored bubblegum. It's powdery, and a little warm (a hint of cinnamon). I generally dislike rose but this fragrance does it for me - plus it gets me compliments from my partner.

I've eyed this for some time before buying it, and I was a little disappointed now after I actually bought it. The bubble gum note does not last as long as I would like. I should have paid more attention to the roses note, since I am not a fan of rose, and it really dominates the scent. I also get a really fake Play-Doh note in there at first. However, after playing around with it some more, I now like it! I just can't go too heavy on it or the florals and rose will be too much for me. I really wish the longevity of the bubble gum note was better.

This perfume to me is just ok, I generally love bubble gum scents but unfortunately on me that note does not last long. This mainly smells like a very sweet rose heavy perfume to me. I would call it more of a sugar candy than bubble gum scent. However I have to say that it's very long lasting and the sillage is impressive. I only used one spray of this on my wrists and my sister told me I smelled good about 9 hours after I had applied it. It's pretty much an all-day perfume. I won't be rebuying this but I would still suggest trying this if you like sweet scents because the performance is great. I also love the bottle.

I'm surprised to see so many notes listed for this perfume, for me its more on the simple side but its still a pretty scent. Mouth watering pink bubblegum and the tiniest hint of blueberry and peach. Drying down to a beautifully bold Bulgarian rose. I love the perfume bottle, its super cute and the atomizer works great too!

I like this scent, it's really bubble gum. I tried it on at the airport (I'd like to offer my apologies to the people sat next to me on my flight for that) and I loved it. I bought the little set that also has shower gel and body lotion. The bottle - no need to mention anything, right? It's unique, it's beautiful. A cute bear. The scent - yes. Bubble gum. Absolutely.

I love this. I love the spot on bubblegum scent you get at the start and then the beautiful tangy rose floral on the dry down. A beautiful and totally wearable day to day perfume. It dries down to such a lovely rosey floral that still has that modern sweetness to it that I think it's an absolute banger. The bottle is a bit too much for me but it's not a deal breaker.

My first review, and then right away about a perfume that I received as a sample today. I briefly stopped by my regular perfumery during my lunch break (is there such a thing when you live in a place with only one perfume shop...?) and met my trusted saleswoman there.

The bottle is - as usual for the brand - quite a statement. It brings to mind children's bubble bath or, in the case of my 10ml travel bottle, even a Pez dispenser. But what you see is only in the first minutes what you get. It doesn’t start with Pez, but rather 1:1 with Hubba Bubba - chewing gum.

Opens with a huge lemony blast that slowly calms down but remains untill the drydown. The drydown remembers me of Azzaro, probably because the oakmoss note. It also reminds me of Armani Eau, but even this La Collection version is heavier than the newest Armani Eau (2013). While this is more citric/fresh and Azzaro is more aromatic and heavier. Both are wonderful fragrances in my opinion. YSL Pour Homme may smell outdated for new guys. Sillage, lasting power and projection are medium-high.

Pour Homme and Eau Sauvage are the yin and yang of citrus/chypre, they're at different ends of the spectrum. Eau Sauvage is light and ethereal, Pour Homme is rich and dark. Lemon and peppery spice give Pour Homme a rawness which is underscored by moss and patchouli. The other main element is civet, a note that smells luxe and dirty at the same time. Pour Homme is about the (unwashed) body - as much as the scent itself - and with moss, spices and civet it's almost brutal. The influence on dark spicy scents like Havana and Cuba is plain to see. And it seems that Pour Homme had the force of destiny behind it. A full three years after it was released it won the first ever Men's Prestige FiFi. Ripe and rich - in the classical French manner - Pour Homme still divides the sheep from the goats, and the chypre from the citrus. 4*

As a child, I spent a few summer vacations in a small town in southern France in the mid-70s. There, I likely encountered some olfactory experiences that I stored in my subconscious, because a few years later, when I began to take an interest in fragrances and wanted to choose one for myself, some of them felt surprisingly familiar. I was clear that I definitely did not want to wear these scents, as they reminded me of the older men from Avignon, Montpellier, and that little town Millau. I, on the other hand, wanted to smell young, fashionable, not so 'old' (in Germany, men at that time did not typically wear a fragrance, at most a shaving lotion...). So it ended up being ‘Antaeus’, which I could soon smell on every corner in Paris. Much later, I learned to appreciate the fragrances from my childhood: they were, as I eventually found out, ‘Eau Sauvage’, ‘Equipage’, Guerlain’s ‘Vetiver’, and Yves Saint Laurent’s ‘Pour Homme’. In exactly this order, my relationship with them relaxed, although I must admit that the latter, Yves Saint Laurent’s ‘Pour Homme’, remains a challenging scent for me. Sometimes I find it magnificent: the sunny freshness, the juicy, tart lemon, the aromatic mint, the strong, earthy-mossy base - like the rough, rugged brother of the much smoother, more civilized ‘Pour Monsieur’ by Chanel. But then, when that strange animalic note reliably blooms during the middle of the scent development, which characterizes this fragrance so distinctly, I think: what for, what’s the point?! Who needs it? The scent would be so beautiful, so classically beautiful without the animal! But okay, the animal is there, and I fear it is meant to be exactly where it is: right in the heart of the scent. Because ‘Pour Homme’ is indeed ‘Pour Homme’, not ‘Pour Monsieur’.
