And so this ‘Homme’ is also not - see the now-iconic advertising photo with the completely naked Yves himself! - clad in fine tailoring, freshly shaved and neatly combed, no, this ‘Homme’ sports stubble, long hair, horn-rimmed glasses, and nothing else - except of course this fragrance! And yes, even freshly showered, or washed (people didn’t shower constantly back then) he still smells a bit - like a man. Fragrances like ‘Jules’, ‘Yatagan’, and especially ‘Kouros’ have picked up on this and highlighted it even more - the scent of a man that smells at times more, at times less quietly animalic and, at least for noses of that time, quite erotic. But wait, what does ‘animalic’ mean here? Civet? No. Castoreum? No. Ambergris? No. Musk? No. Animalic? Actually not. But where does this dirty note come from? The notes listed on the bottle, Citron, Petit Grain, Mint, Patchouli, Oakmoss, are certainly not responsible for it. If you research further pyramids attributed to this fragrance, quite different notes are sometimes mentioned: in addition to those already mentioned, also Lavender, Sage, Marjoram, Thyme, Rosemary, Rosewood, Cedar, and Vetiver. I find Marjoram and Thyme particularly interesting here. Anyone who often cooks with fresh herbs and strips the small leaves from the stems knows these earthy-dark, somewhat dirty undertones that accompany the typical aroma. They disappear again while cooking, but freshly crushed between the hands, they are unmistakably present. Aha, so it’s not animalic after all, at least not animal-based, rather a kind of plant-based animality - which is a contradiction in itself. But plant aromas don’t always smell pleasant either; sometimes they can smell pungent (Sage) or sweaty (Cumin). Marjoram and Thyme also belong to those herbs with questionable scent facets - here, however, tending more towards the fecal. Sounds awful, doesn’t it? But it’s not. At least not for me. Although I - as I said - took a long time to endure this rough aromatic hint. I’m not yet talking about ‘wearing’, just about ‘enduring’! In the past, I actually found it awful. Even when I discovered my love for 70s fragrances a few years later, ‘Pour Homme’ was still an absolute no-go. ‘Yatagan’ and ‘Azzaro pour Homme’ were fine, even though they both had a rather obscenely animalic undertone, but not the scent from YSL. And to this day, I find this blend of fresh chypre with a herbaceous-aromatic heart, to put it mildly, an acquired taste. I feel similarly about ‘Para Hombre/Pour Homme’ by Loewe. A fragrance that follows a very, very similar concept, although the herbal aromas here are not highlighted quite as dirty. I don’t really find either of them wearable. I find the Loewe scent a bit more bearable than the one from YSL. On the other hand, they both smell great, just somehow time-bound, like they are pinned down in the early 70s. ‘Eau Sauvage’, on the other hand, is completely timeless - at least for me. But ‘Pour Homme’ beams me back every time to southern France when I was just 11/12 years old, no longer a child and not yet a teenager, and the men I encountered often wore these heavy herbal scents - however, no deodorant, which created a confusing amalgam. Maybe the day will come when I can also wear ‘Pour Homme’ without hesitation. Who knows. I have also learned to wear ‘Kouros’ - in homeopathic doses... For now, I’d rather pass. If my memory serves me right, the latest version is quite close to the original. Longevity and projection are enormous for a citrusy chypre, which is probably thanks to the mentioned aromas.

Yves Saint Laurent is considered a designer of the century! As a women understander! For me - alongside Karl Lagerfeld - the last great "fashion creator" of the 20th century! No one has shaped the act of "making" and "wearing" fashion like he did! His trademark - the distinctive, thick horn-rimmed glasses! His motto "to give women back their confidence"! Saint Laurent is regarded as the inventor of the pantsuit, gifted women the tuxedo, the trapeze line, the Shiavago, and safari look. His longtime friend and confidant Pierre Bergé once said, "Coco Chanel gave women freedom, Yves Saint Laurent gave them power." As the youngest couturier of all time, he designed what was then considered audacious: He said goodbye to Dior's wasp waist and allowed women to breathe in the comfortable yet elegant trapeze line of his wide, knee-length dresses. Knit models with turtlenecks, leather jackets - haute couture had never been so buoyantly youthful and casually unladylike before! With his label "Rive Gauche," he was also a co-founder of prêt-à-porter - basically from the runway to the street! "A bas le Ritz! Vive la rue!" In English: "Down with the Ritz! Long live the street!" was the motto. Saint Laurent was one of the first designers to book black models and even threatened the French Vogue with ad cancellations because they refused to put the then 18-year-old Naomi Campbell on the cover in 1988. Alongside her were also Loulou de la Falaise, Betty Catroux, Catherine Deneuve, Jerry Hall, Carla Bruni, and Laetitia Casta, inspiring muses, models, and longtime companions. YSL revolutionized and shocked. All under the motto "only this way would one remain a topic of conversation"! For his first men's fragrance in 1971, he posed completely naked and caused an uproar! The next sensation came five years later. Just based on the name of his oriental women's perfume "Opium," the next scandal was pre-programmed... But as provocative and scandalous as YSL and his brand may seem - Yves as a person was reserved and shy! Due to health reasons, the master withdrew from the fashion business in 2002 at the age of only 66. Tom Ford, Stefano Pilati, and currently Hedi Slimane - who had already worked for YSL in the 1990s - took over the reins, but stepped into big shoes! They gave the house their own touch and polished the star that began to shine half a century ago. Slimane even went so far as to discard the famous "YSL" logo, designed by graphic designer A.M. Cassandre, and revived the old "Rive Gauche Paris" logo. But fear not! The trademark will only affect the fashion line - the old one will continue to adorn all beauty products! Glitz, glamour, luxury... yet the man Yves Saint Laurent seemed to lead a shadowy existence. Withdrawn, even isolated, he spent his last years in his villa "Majorelle" in Marrakech. He ultimately passed away on June 1, 2008, due to a brain tumor. At 72 years old, he thus left the earthly stage for good. Personally, this hit me hard at the time - for me, a living legend died! What remains is the legacy of Yves Saint Laurent, which Pierre Bergé maintains in the form of the "Fondation Pierre Bergé - Yves Saint Laurent." YSL fans of "Rivegauche" are not entirely innocent or uninvolved in the fact that this legacy increasingly captivates me! Especially regarding the fragrance collection, which has produced several classics by now - they are significant to me and have piqued my interest. Foremost Opium, Kouros, Rivegauche, and also the classic Chypre "Pour Homme"! Admittedly, I couldn't really relate to the fragrances listed here at first... When I discovered the world of perfumes at my tender age of 18/19, these scents were simply outdated, stuffy, overpowering - even unbearable! Ten years later, with an expanded horizon - sprinkled with a dash of courage and optimism, I approach these "old-fashioned" classics again and see them with entirely different eyes! Yes, I even own an older version of Opium now, and the Pour Homme version from the "La Collection" series will likely soon find its way into my collection. Loyal readers will rub their eyes - "Pour Homme is trying to win over that critic whose original from 1971 he condemned!?" Well, as mentioned, I have become a bit more confident and find the Pour Homme version of the "La Collection" series quite interesting - as it is more wearable... many thanks to "Neree" for his sample. Pour Homme was reworked again in 2011 - in my opinion, it feels a bit more relaxed compared to the older version, although the character has not lost anything at all! Pour Homme also starts with a "nuclear" lemon explosion! Hello, toilet duck! ;-) Citrus, citrus, citrus in abundance! It seems one wanted to offer or even surpass Dior's Eau Sauvage or Chanel's Pour Monsieur! This almost sour note with a soapy character envelops the fragrance throughout and thus defines Pour Homme. As the citrus load slowly loses power, mint brings a certain metallic, radiant undertone into play. Slightly floral nuances soften this strictness a bit and give the whole a slightly sweet touch. Oakmoss (IFRA seemed to be generous again) pushes the fragrance development in a bitter, slightly musty direction. Thanks to the floral notes mentioned above, it maintains an acceptable balance, although I would have liked it to be a bit more relaxed. So I must - casually and unfairly said - think a little of grave soil or cellar spaces... The drydown ends powdery, woody. Just as a Chypre used to end! ;) 6-7 hours are easily achievable. In summary, Pour Homme 2010 is a very interesting and exciting fragrance that brings the flair of the 1970s into the 21st century. Lovers of Paco Rabanne Pour Homme or Boucheron Pour Homme will surely get their money's worth! Interesting detail at the end - in humid, warm air, the fragrance (similar to Eau Sauvage) gains a bit of momentum again, making it ideal for sultry days... it's going on the wish list!

I was looking for a fragrance for my little uncle, who proudly now carries the number 8 in front. So I asked for something nice for the more mature gentleman - who nonetheless does not count as "old iron." Uncle has put away his fine banker suits, but still shines in stylish casual wear. His sporting activities are limited to regional skat tournaments, from which he emerges successfully. He is not too proud to play a few cards with me - and now and then I even win, which is certainly not due to my refined play. He knows how to have fun. Well, with age, eyesight diminishes - but humor increases. Comforting. That’s why I was very much in favor of the suggested Pour Homme. The fragrance has expression and style - it’s old school - but not at all outdated. Oldies but Goldies - that comes to mind. The ingredients are finely balanced - especially the mint-lemon blend appeals to me. The oak moss stands gently in the background, and patchouli emphasizes the mature character of the fragrance. I can best imagine Pour Homme on experienced gentlemen - the wearer shouldn't be too youthful. Although the fragrance is not directly serious, it does have a serious statement. I look forward to our next skat evening, accompanied by Glenn Miller, when uncle winks at me and says: You deal.

I received Pour Homme in a swap and have been wearing it with pleasure since then. Here we have a classic citrus chypre for men. Not really current in today’s context, but simply timelessly good. Upon spraying, there is clearly lemon, mint with a bit of petitgrain to soften things up. Clear, natural, but possibly a bit scratchy for some noses.

Recently, I acquired this fragrance because, as a fan of Eau Sauvage and Armani eau pour homme, I was curious about it. However, after wearing it a few times, I’ve had enough. The former... I always expect a fresh, slightly Mediterranean flair from citrus scents that keeps me in a good mood throughout the day.

Cheap & Chic. Oh, it's definitely Chic! I only wish it was cheap! I would stack up on this crazy looking bottle out of fear I can't find it anymore; because I love this fragrance! There is something about Moschino perfumes that make them feel and sense like black or purple velvet. You want to touch it, and put it on. Most Moschinos are soft, yet distinct and take your sense of smell on a magical-mystery-ride. This one is no exception. Opening up with cyclamen and freesia, vanilla and a naughty rose join, bringing a hint of violet. Musk storms in and drags cedar along sprinkling coriander. I think they are having a party and I am the guest of honor : ) The dry down is divine. The silage is 'magnetic' and the longevity is amazing, especially on clothes. Every time I wear this people wanna "sniff" me. It's odd but I can't blame them. It's a very unusual scent, easily recognizable and attracts attention like a magnet. It is slightly reminiscent of my other beloved Moschino Moschino (so good they named it twice ; ) But this one manages to have and keep its own unique personality. It's just something you must smell! If you don't know it, ignore the word "Cheap", then go to a shop and spray....Now; do you feel it? Yes! That is love, magic and sex in a funky bottle.

Cheap & Chic fascinates me with its diversity and unique blend of both spices and fruits combined with a soapy and clean accord. I will admit that this fragrance will probably not capture you instantaneously, instead it will grow on you and develop into a scent that is truly difficult to resist. I love how the coriander blends with the peach and citrus notes in the opening. Together they create such an unusual yet classy scent, which is not too spicy nor too bitter or sour. The heart is pretty, but not overly feminine. I prefer it that way. It has more of a raw, 'don't mess with me' kind of approach, which would really suit a strong and determined woman. The musk certainly dominates the drydown, however I don't see this as being this fragrance's downfall. It is a rather nice finish to an incredibly alluring scent. From start to finish it is obvious that this is an Italian fragrance; such class, such distinction. Beautiful from start to finish, I advise anyone to try this scent.

This fragrance is so lovely, but the name is terrible. For one, the word “cheap” doesn’t fit the cost unless you find it used at a garage sale. Second, it dilutes the beauty of the perfume itself, giving it a negative connotation, a sad fate for such a lovely blend. The bottle itself is interesting. I don’t own one, but I’ve seen photos of it. I have two views on that part. One: some people love quirky bottles and I think that’s fantastic! It’s not my style though. I prefer a beautiful bottle, one that is on the more glamorous side. It’s almost a “joke” bottle for someone like me, which is why I never bothered with the scent until I received a decant and realized how lovely it is. The perfume is just so nice, even during dry down. It is floral and becomes creamy, never overbearing, only tiny flowers poking up their cute little heads to say hello to me. It’s versatile. It can be slept in, worn at work, or on a hot date. It’s not screaming for sex, but your date will want to come closer to sniff you to see where that wonderful, mysterious scent is coming from.

I remember when this perfume came out in the 90es: with its Olivia*-shaped bottle, it was almost a provocative and surely funny scent! But this one isn't a toy for little girls. Its acchord is rich and well balanced , with unusual aromatic notes giving a particular character to this scent perfect to wear mainly in the cold season. Unfortunately the sillage isn't so strong and the name too "Cheap and chic" isn't really right for this scent , more particular than "chic" and not so cheap! Anyway, a pleasant fragrance which is a modern classic. *Italian name for Olive Oyl

After years of hopeless searching, I was able to track down an original bottle of Cheap & Chic with the original logo from the mid 1990s. In that decade, Moschino was the cutting edge of couture. I had a pair of those jeans! That bold retro modern commercial caught my attention with Olyve Oyle gave me smiles and curiosity. What could this smell like? As the century turned, Cheap & Chic apparently suffered a bad reformulation and logo alteration. Bad reviews abounded here and elsewhere. The notes seemed odd to begin with, so I passed on this for years. Yet that bottle kept calling me...What would an original one be like? Today I found one and get to catch a glimpse of the original formula. Yes, it is Avant Gard. It opens with a blast of light florals not unlike Issy Miyake. I was afraid this would head into aquatic territory. Cyclamen, water lily and peony give it a modern powdery character, while the traditional rose/violet/jasmine are in the back seat. This is totally contemporary and fresh. Then the lower notes begin to emerge. There is lots of oakmoss and vetiver here set against a thick resinous dark caramel vanilla/tonka musk with a delicious sandalwood base. I assume the powdery character comes from the buttery iris that is carefully weaved through the entire composition. I get a little coffee here as well... Cheap & Chic should have been a major player amid the sweet gourmand trend. It is lighter than what came before, yet not weaker. Sweet, powdery projection is big for about the first 20 minutes and then it settles to a delightful skin scent. This was in the running with Gaultier Femme and Le Male with those campy commercials and break through fragrances. I assume a Popeye tribute was next with a spinach note-deep green with modern notes for men? The wind changed directions and Uomo? came next. Everything became sheer and almost invisible. Maybe the industry was preparing for the sweeping changes to come... My final verdict is this is a late century marvel that was quickly changed to accommodate the industry regulations. The obvious offending ingredients(oakmoss and sandalwood) were quickly swapped out for nasty acetone plastic fruit notes that the "Cheap" is a self- fulfilling prophecy. Those vulgar flankers are basically Alice the Goon!

Once again, a fragrance that has captivated me since its release. Only back then, I wasn't ready for it. Something stood between us, or rather, one of its notes. But since I've been "revisiting" older fragrances lately that were too much for me at their peak but have remained in my "nose consciousness" to this day, it was time for it to undergo a current test as well.

This bottle is one of the most beautiful I have ever seen, so minimalist, in simple colors, red, black, a bit of white, with golden lettering, absolutely perfect. I buy it because I want it as a decorative object for my apartment.

Following the motto: I haven't worn this in a while, I could use it again, I chose C&C last Sunday during my daily "which fragrance do I feel like today?" selection. And I didn't regret it. I had almost forgotten how delicious it is. I was invited to a birthday party and was approached about the scent there. It starts fresh and actually remains so until the end.

I like I love love and that's why I boldly got myself a household bottle of Cheap and Chic, assuming we would become friends. I also find the Olivia bottle cute - that's why I ordered it untested. But what is this? It immediately stings my nose. It can't be the coriander, because I like it in other fragrances. Overall, I find the fragrance pyramid appealing.

I must break a lance today for this fragrance, which may be underestimated and underrepresented due to its age (created in 1995), but certainly not because of its bottle, which the inclined anglophile reader can only describe as "whimsical." The scent has, I openly admit, flown under my radar for a long time.

"Yes, yes,... of course you don't wear blouses!" you're probably saying now. "... after all, you're a man!" Yes, that may be true, but did you know that originally, a blouse did not always refer to those loose and... sometimes even slightly transparent (aaaah...! :D) tops for women, but simply to loosely hanging garments that were also worn by peasants, knights, sailors, and so on? But no, of course, you ladies had to come along at some point and claim this piece of clothing just for yourselves, supposedly to make life easier for us guys, since we would have one less type of garment to learn how to iron (though you probably meant that we guys have no clue about fashion and could do without blouses!). Well, there is some truth to that: I actually hate ironing and have my difficulties with certain garments like shirts (aaaaargh, ironing shirts always means the end of the world for me!!!), so I'm glad I don't have to iron blouses. And do you even iron blouses? You see, I have no clue again...!! Anyway, the fragrance was named after a blouse... because it smells like one? I don't even know if blouses can smell different from other garments?? Well, if a woman is wearing the blouse, then maybe it does smell nicer... than if a guy were wearing it... uuuurgh....! Well, welcome to my commentary on "Blouse" from Yves Saint Laurent's "Le Vestiaire" collection. The Fragrance: At the beginning, you actually smell exactly what is listed in the top notes here. Green-bitter and herbal galbanum, sweet-spicy pink pepper, and a hint of lemon (or rather bergamot). But soon, the roses make their appearance. In the background, there is a scent note that I can't identify; it's certainly the interplay of the various notes, but it leans towards coriander. However, this doesn't last too long and disappears after the top notes. A little later, the fragrance smells powdery-sweet (probably due to soft notes like cashmeran). You can still smell pink pepper, and now the roses become more pronounced. A bit of musk also slowly appears. The green notes are now far in the background and continue to fade away. In the end, the fragrance remains soft and slightly sweet, smelling beautifully of light roses and still of musk with a lingering hint of unidentifiable flowers in the background. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is above average and should be noticeable for a while to everyone nearby. The longevity is also above average, lasting about six to eight hours depending on the dosage before it weakens significantly. The Bottle: The bottle is rectangular, tall, and made of thick glass. The label is white and square and quite simple. Overall, the entire look of the bottle is quite simple and clear, fitting in with the exclusive fragrance lines of Dior, Chanel, and similar brands, but it looks much better to me. The cap is cylindrical and has a nice tactile pattern. A simple but beautiful bottle. Okay, so the "blouse fragrance" here turned out to be not so bad at all. Well, you should like roses, as they are the main theme here, especially since they have an intense scent in the middle part. They smell soft due to the gentle notes, which makes for a more pleasant perception. However, I still find that the fragrance is mostly not that special, as it is just another rose scent that only slightly distinguishes itself from other rose scents by occasionally coming off as herbal and green. It is wearable like an all-rounder, but it may tend more towards warm days. By the way, it is less suitable for going out, as it might come off as rather unspectacular despite its nice scent (you just have to try it), but it could be well worn at work due to its pleasant fragrance. So do blouses smell like this? Well... as I said, I have no idea, since I have no way to sniff blouses (especially with a lady in one :DD),... and I'm certainly not going to go into town to sniff blouses in a women's department... I already have a hard time with women, they don't need to think I'm some possibly ridiculous or even perverse freak,... :DD Waaaah! No, no,... :D Well then, that's it again! Have a nice evening, see you later :)

Recently, I met a - no longer young - colleague in the office late in the evening, who usually goes home quite early. She didn’t seem to be in a particularly good mood - as often happens when you wanted to be somewhere else long ago - and eventually confessed to me that she had actually been 'on a date' for the past two hours, and he was now keeping her waiting every half hour because it was taking him longer. And she was outraged - half at him, half at herself - that she was wasting her time WAITING FOR A MAN. And I was genuinely surprised that she was doing just that - waiting. There I was sitting with this fifty-year-old woman - successful, smart, and confident, sometimes a bit cynical but not bitter, attractive and stylish (she wears the necklace made of Fimo elements that her daughter, whom she raises alone, strung together years ago, with the same cool and self-assured attitude on Mondays as on Tuesdays with Cartier) - who was excited and nervous before a date - and surprised and irritated with herself that she was (still) so nervous and excited. And that she was actually waiting. And yet self-ironic enough to laugh about it with me. In Love, in love. It can happen to anyone. Maybe tomorrow. Again and again. You can't prevent it, can't force it. Can't suppress it and also can't prolong it. It happens at twelve and at twenty, at fifty and - why not? - even at eighty. It is new and exciting every time. And it can be terrible, but you don’t know that beforehand and can’t control it. You can’t buy it and can’t practice for it, can’t prepare for it. It has to be given to you. And it is so immense every time that it overwhelms us - perhaps it is the most overwhelming feeling in the world. What a great idea - to try to capture all that I briefly outlined in the last paragraph in a perfume bottle. Knowing that every potential buyer will again know that you can’t bottle and buy this feeling. But finds the pure thought that it might actually work beautiful. Nothing else evokes as many memories, longings, and dreams as this feeling: in love. And with what other associations could a per se unnecessary luxury product like perfume sell better than with just that: memories, longings, dreams? In Love Again by Yves Saint Laurent - and I believe this is intentional - pays tribute to the agelessness of being in love in that it is also an ageless scent. Not overtly girlish, not pointedly ladylike, certainly not elderly. For a fruity fragrance, it is surprisingly rich and not overly sweet, artfully blended and - meant without any negative connotation - very interestingly crafted. Berry / Flower / Balm could be a simplified summary of its triad, yet it lacks that sweetness which is otherwise so typical for berry scents. Instead, there is something fresh, something breaking through, and something beginning - astonishingly capricious for an Ellena - and that fits wonderfully with its theme and name. The top note eventually fades and gives way to a vibrating warmth and physical sensuality - just as it should be when you are in love. Theme beautifully executed, Yves Saint Laurent. Conclusion: around half past nine, he finally got in touch to say he was ready. In the end, nothing really came of it. But since that evening when I sat with her for that half hour, we have been having coffee together a bit more often than before. Maybe next time I will tell her about Yves Saint Laurent's In Love Again.

YSL In Love again - I remember it like it was today: A long car ride in 1998 from Braunschweig to Wuppertal; in stop-and-go traffic, I pull out a sample of a new fragrance from my handbag and am blown away from the very first moment: I had never smelled such a charming, uplifting scent in my life. Back then, I knew neither what a fragrance pyramid was, nor could I have recognized the individual components of a scent. My untrained nose only distinguished between "like" and "dislike," at best "like - but not for me." However, it had enough sensitivity to notice that this mainstream fragrance (a term I didn't know back then) not only created a damn good mood but also stood out clearly from the usual offerings. There is probably no other perfume that combines three of my favorite scents: the aroma of blackcurrants, the intensely herbal scent of tomato vines, and delicate, fresh rose petals. Especially cassis and tomato vine are not a combination that guarantees success for a perfumer. Both are very specific, intense, and not to everyone's taste. The fact that they blend together so harmoniously in this aromatic fragrance, soothing, igniting, and merging with one another, makes both the nose and the soul happy and is surely attributable to the virtuosity of the transparent fragrance master Jean-Claude Ellen. In Love again became one of my truly great fragrance loves. There have only been a handful of perfumes I could say the same about throughout my fragrance life. Immediately after my return, I had to buy the bottle. Admittedly, it was a time when there weren't 40 bottles in my cabinets, but I used it up completely and repurchased it. There aren't many 100 ml bottles with which I have managed that. Years later, this dreamy scent was taken off the market, and when it was relaunched in 2011 in the oddly cumbersome bottle in a colorless version, I immediately and blindly ordered it from England. The disappointment followed promptly: This was no longer my scent! The new one was sharp, it felt clumsy, angular, and above all, it lacked the wonderful tomato vine note. It didn't stay with me for long. This month, I had the luck to buy a new, unused, and still original-packaged In Love again. As someone who has since been washed with many fragrances, opening a bottle is still a lovely ritual, but I hadn't been this excited about In Love again in ages. Is it still good, just like before, have I idealized it in my memory, and was it perhaps not that beautiful? Does old love possibly rust after all? It IS my scent, just as I loved it years ago. In the opening, delicate, dark, unsweetened berries - tart blackcurrants and soft, gentle blueberries, soon joined by a young, radiant rose and zesty grapefruits. Where other fruity scents either come off as unpleasantly sour or berry-sticky-sweet, In Love again impresses with an appetizing, mild freshness and harmony. The kick undoubtedly comes from the tomato vine aroma, without becoming dominant. In Love again is a cool but not aloof beauty full of joie de vivre. Optimistic, but not frivolous. Young yet mature. Despite the berries, there are no gourmand nuances. I don't recognize vodka as an alcoholic note, but perhaps it is what enhances the cassis aroma and cools it pleasantly. Musk gently rounds off the scent and gives it the relatively unusual longevity for a fresh summer fragrance throughout the day. By the way, the many years in the original packaging have done nothing to my fragrance. It is absolutely fresh. Anyone wanting to secure a bottle need not fear a skewed top note. Should this bottle ever run out and replenishment no longer be available, Cartier's L'heure folle would be a worthy successor for me. In character as well as in its mood-lifting effect, it resembles In Love again (1998) much more than the reformulated scent - albeit without the tomato vine.

is a book by Johannes Mario Simmel that has helped this fragrance achieve a certain cult status. As perhaps the discerning reader may know, Simmel had the habit of letting fragrances play a secondary yet significant role in his novels. Not all of them were familiar to me in terms of scent, but I already knew In Love Again when it was released as a "limited edition" in 1998, back then with the amusing harlequin cap. Between that and the 2011 version in a simple plastic cube bottle, there was another edition, shaped like the harlequin but with a hammered gold cap. I own this one, but it is now almost empty. First, about Simmel: In the aforementioned novel, the protagonist wears In Love Again, and the fragrance is described passionately and praised in the highest terms, which led to a true rush for the scent shortly after the production ended and the book was published. This, in turn, caused eBay prices to soar to incredible heights, which likely prompted YSL to bring the fragrance back to life. A good decision, YSL! About the scent: At that time, the non-sweet berry note was groundbreaking, paired with a zesty freshness and a latent earthy note. Even now, the fragrance has not lost any of its individuality and finesse. It was truly ahead of its time, which has apparently kept it alive until now. Of course, I feel that, like with many relaunches, the original version is the best, but the modern variant has much to offer as well. It starts relatively fruity, fresh-sour-delicious and refreshing-sparkling. As time goes on, a higher proportion of red fruits becomes noticeable, and the fragrance becomes heavier. In addition, there is a sensual earthiness, a dry, alcoholic note, similar to the DKNY scent in the slender bottle. Throughout, there is a very nice, unusual pleasantly sour note that makes it seem suitable even in warmer temperatures. Well perceivable, even without a sweet note, long-lasting. Like vintage Paris, Champagne (Yvresse), and Opium, I consider this fragrance a milestone from the house of Laurent.

Years ago, my mother-in-law gifted me this fragrance. She is a devoted No 5 wearer, and I expected something in that direction. Hesitantly sprayed on - and my heart leaped with joy! What a charming fresh green scent! I closed my eyes and was in Sicily in spring. Sitting on a stone wall, with a crispy olive bread in my left hand and freshly picked aromatic tomatoes in my right. The sea breeze blows coolly over, mixed with the delicate scent of nearby lemon trees. The pier smells woody and pleasantly of seaweed. A yellow rose bush sways gently in the wind, and the seagulls laugh above me, infecting me with their cheerfulness. Pure bliss - refreshing and aquatic at the same time. Waking up, I looked gratefully at the bottle. What a beautiful journey!

This fragrance is a small milestone for me, particularly regarding the tomato. I received this perfume as a gift, so I would never have bought it for myself. From the very first spray, it becomes clear: This is a fresh, fruity scent, but not sweet; rather, it has a green-leafy quality. Truly delightful for fans of this fragrance direction! And it seems to me that the cited tomato is already coming through. But it doesn't smell like the vegetable. Have you ever smelled a tomato plant? Held your nose to a pack of vine tomatoes? Rubbed a little branch of cherry tomatoes between your hands? That's it! And I love this smell. In "In love again," this comes through beautifully. The other notes skillfully balance out the potentially feared herbaceousness. It remains a lightly floral-fruity, fresh, green scent that envelops you all day with an initially strong, then subtle but steady aura. The rose is hardly noticeable to me. The woodiness at the end is also very subtle, so I did not classify it as "woody" (if anything, I would associate that more with the "She Wood" variants from Dsquared). So, the little tomato has cheerfully settled into my fragrance memory and is here to stay. :-) Since "In love again" is becoming increasingly rare, I have found a good alternative: DKNY Women.

Well, I really am a clever girl :-) and I consider myself lucky to still own an original packaged bottle of the original version from 1998. I haven't tested the reformulated new edition from the YSL Collection yet; this cube bottle in beige is not really very nice to look at and completely unspectacular. What was YSL thinking?

Surely we all (from our mother, aunt, or beloved grandma?) have tried those wonderful liqueurs made with various berries or aromatic leaves in alcohol. Well, my Aunt Sofia is a master at it!!! She makes the most delicious liqueurs from almost anything you can think of... and the best part is that she always let us try them (just a tiny bit as little kids)...

The opening of this fragrance is beautiful, elegant, and fruity - soft apple, soft blueberry, and the bitter black currant comes through nicely. Vodka - perhaps to keep everything sterile? An invitation to vodka should never be declined, say the Russians and vodka lovers.

At just 14 years old, I smelled it for the first time, on a trip to London in a duty-free perfume shop in France, and I immediately fell in love with this scent, which will forever remain one of my two favorite fragrances! Back then, I obviously couldn't afford it at all and was sad to hear that it was supposed to be a "Limited Edition".... Still, I thought to myself...

Out of all the flankers this one is the most beautiful. From the stunning burgundy colored gem cut bottle with the bow to the perfume inside- it’s a masterpiece. The main character in here is the rose of course. But this rose is a true princess here. It shines like nowhere else I have seen accompanied by the masterfully blended accord of addicting black currant, lovely raspberry, sparkling bergamot and mysterious datura flower. The dry down is sheer sexiness with very smooth patchouli, musk and cashmeran. I wore it several times for everyday, but when I put on my new little black dress on and turned on the romantic music, I realized this perfume fits perfectly. It’s made for an evening out. Some perfumes just should be special like that. You can wear it everyday of course, but it’s just made for a grander time. I could not believe how good it smelled and I just couldn’t stop smelling it on myself like an addict. I hope it stays in production because it would be a true heartbreak to lose this Rose gem. As I mentioned before in my statement, it befits true hopeless romantics. What season is it? I think it’s very versatile from winter to spring to summer nights. You can pull it off anytime, but for everyday I would probably choose the original Mon Paris or Mon Paris Floral. Although for now, I personally will prefer this one. The original Mon Paris is more about the raspberry florals and patchouli. In this one, raspberry is beautifully blended and Rose is at the center. A gorgeous fragrance that I like much better than Midnight Rose by Lancôme for sure.

What sorrow I have carried. My beloved signature scent "Gaultier Classique intense" is no longer produced. Prices skyrocketed. And since the separation was already in sight, better not to delay, but to find something new. I ordered masses of perfume samples on Ebay, because in the store, after a few scents, the nose quickly gets "full." Of course, I know which fragrances I like. Primarily vanilla, jasmine, and also the orange blossom, which many find annoying, I enjoy. Likewise, rose scent, as long as it doesn't come off too synthetic. But in the end, it's all about the blend. The other Gaultier fragrances are all not my style at all. In the store, the finalists were actually Yves Saint Laurent and Libre as well as Mon Paris. Also "Dior the One gold." Mon Paris quickly became irritating and is now being resold on ebay. The same goes for The One. Libre is very special, but it will definitely stay with me. However, it wasn't suitable for everyday wear. I always found Yves Saint Laurent in general to be far too heavy and too musky. I can't even count all the scents I've smelled in the meantime. And how often I've taken a shower in between to get rid of smells, I can't recall either. And then I stumbled upon Mon Paris intensement as a sample on ebay. The first impression, the top note, was actually almost too fruity. I usually prefer everything that is creamy and soft. And at first sniff, the scent seemed almost too girlish to me. However, with the onset of the heart note, it quickly became clear that the fragrance is more adult than it initially appears. Feminine, sensual, and soft. In the base, the scent is not too heavy; musk and patchouli are very balanced. It remains lovely, soft, and feminine. Actually, the scent is not at all what I have worn so far. Nevertheless, I won't part with it. Now I just have to keep my fingers crossed that it won't be discontinued soon and that I won't have to start the search anew. A little addendum: as pretty as the scent is, over time I miss depth and a certain level of sensuality. The fragrance is harmonious, beautiful, and wonderfully balanced. Still, over the days, I haven't been able to shake the feeling that something is missing.

When listening to Charles Aznavour (the campaign song), I don’t immediately think of Mon Paris Intensement, more on that later. But first, the bottle: it is shaped like the other MP flankers but in a magnetically appealing color, including a matching bow, and for me, it is the most beautiful in the series. A dark magenta-purple, sensual, mysterious, one expects something "heavy" from it. The longevity and sillage are decent, and one should be careful with the dosage even though Intensement is not as intense as expected. Now to the fragrance: Mon Paris Intensement (MPI) starts berry-like, fruity fresh, and alongside the berries, I can clearly perceive the pear. This pleasant sweetness increases and becomes rounder towards the heart note; I perceive a slight soapiness after about 10 minutes, which I find a pleasant counterpoint to the fruits. As the flowers take over in the middle, the sweetness steps back again. Here, I also notice the oily rose described by Igli in humid-warm weather; in dry, cooler weather, the "prickling" of the thorn apple prevails, just like with the EDP. What I notice with MPI is that the heart note lasts a very long time, which I greatly appreciate. But - and now we come to a downside - unfortunately, I perceive little patchouli in the base, and almost no benzoin :-( There is basically only white musk, so nothing intense... My conclusion: MPI is a successful, modern fragrance and despite its sweetness, it is very wearable. It has quite a punch, but ultimately it does not have the intensity I wish for or imagined with the addition of Intensement. Very unfortunate :-( Back to the song: the remix fits (at least instrumentally) with MPI, the young modern bohemian indeed... the bohemian era that Charles Aznavour lyrically sings about would probably have suited L'heure Bleue better ;-) So, what do I do? I will definitely use up the bottle; it is beautiful after all, even if it lacks depth. And I still have the EDP (favorite)... and then I’m considering whether I should treat myself to the blue hour from the master Jacques Guerlain again :-)

Not as fruity as I expected from the notes. There's definitely something sweet on top, but I can't at all pick out what it is, definitely not getting that wet summer sorbet smell I expected from peach, rhubarb and pears. Instead I get a lot of orchid, with maybe some sweet fruit notes on top. Love the bottle design though, I know that it's a divider but I enjoy a fun novelty bottle that isn't clumsy and cheap.

I find the "Sidolin" bottles very original! I could gladly dedicate such a "flacon" to my humorous friends. However, the previous scents were only imaginable to me as room fragrances. But Gold is a delightful exception. I really like its sweet-oriental touch on my skin. This scent has no cleaning image - and does not remind one of the "golden scrubber" of a top housewife. From that perspective, it is perfectly suitable for me and my friend, as neither of us makes a fuss as cleaning whizzes. She has an eager cleaning lady - and I have a diligent and tidy husband. Gold is therefore not a clean scent at all, but warm, soft, and chocolaty. Yes, I perceive a non-listed nougat note that I really like. The peach is also delicious - but Gold is not a gourmand. It remains light and transparent due to the aquatic pear - and bright through the jasmine. Sandalwood confidently embraces - the sweet vanilla is smooth. This pleasant, light oriental could have also fit into a typical rounded bottle, but I find the Sidolin sprayer all the more amusing.

Not only does the bottle make a statement, but the content is also VERY promising!!! Moschino Gold Fresh Couture is the third Eau de Parfum from the legendary Italian designer label in a cleaning spray bottle..... Playful, sensual, and elegant, this fragrance is ideal for women who enjoy floral-fruity notes combined with woody accords... Upon first application, Gold Fresh Couture impresses with very pleasant fruity nuances like pear, mango, rhubarb, and grapefruit. These components create a cheeky harmony. In the floral heart note, jasmine, lily of the valley, and orchid form a radiant, feminine, and above all, sensual note. With patchouli, Akigalawood, sandalwood, vanilla, and musk, the fragrance transforms into a warm, sensual golden elixir... The perfect scent for the self-confident woman.

First of all - a magnificent scent blend, just the right amount of fruity sweetness, a bitter note in the background (from the very beginning!), making it suitable for the over-25 age group, and still a very rounded overall impression without coming off as cheap. Really pleasant and diverse, I’m thrilled. But - is it just me or does the scent disappear without a trace after 2-3 hours? It’s affordable enough to reapply constantly, but that’s not ideal. Such a shame!

Moschino Gold. This fragrance brings me countless memories. Moschino Gold was my absolute favorite scent from the age of about 15-18, and I still enjoy wearing it today. However, I have never really been able to describe what it smells like; the pear is clearly present, as well as the musk, which I believe contributes significantly to the freshness of the fragrance. The perfume smells fruity, fresh! Marketed by Moschino as their freshest scent AND they are right, yet it is not typical citrus-fresh or herb-fresh, rather it is warm-fruity/fresh. The scent is the absolute all-rounder, perfect for summer, whether in everyday life or on a date, at a picnic or dining with friends, the fragrance just works all the time. Despite the low price, I have not found a comparable fresh/fruity scent for myself. Moschino Gold is my most repurchased fragrance; there have rarely been a few weeks when I didn’t have it at home, I have repurchased it time and again and will continue to do so.

Many thanks to Janne and Nico for the miniature of Gold Fresh Couture :-) I don't find this fragrance bad in itself. The golden spray bottle stands out quite a bit. Unfortunately, the longevity on my skin is quite lacking at around 5 hours. The sillage is hardly any better. The top note starts fresh, synthetic, and very fruity-sweet.

Sweet summer scent, quite fruity - zesty like an elaborate cocktail, I can't wear it every day. More of an evening scent, it lasts a very long time. Actually, it smells best on the discarded clothing the next day.

From Kouros it has only the name ... it is a generic cologne. I cannot understand what is YSL ideia, their intention, with this flanker, with another massmarket production... They're destroying the fantastic reputation and quality of the original Kouros. They did it with Jazz, Rive Gauche, M7 and YSL pour Homme.

This perfume really deserves its name. I feel the sage and green apple more in its content. A little fresh, nice and sweet male odor. This perfume gives me joy when it smells You will never regret. This perfume has an average life. Suitable for spring days.

I was recently at the cinema - in one of those gigantic movie machines with twenty screens, where nachos topped with yellow plastic cheese sauce are sold in pizza box-sized bowls. Right next to us sat a young man, whom I would have liked to report as being sixteen and pimply, but it is likely that he was already twenty-five, if not thirty. That gentleman (his self-image and the image others had of him likely differed significantly) entertained his neighbor - as well as us and several others - before and during the film with lengthy announcements about how every woman who had ever had the fortune of knowing him (hundreds! Oh, thousands!) had forever changed the flow of her blood. He had applied Kouros Silver (which I had only known through magazine samples until then, but you recognize it immediately, at least) - generously dosed, who knows who else might be allowed to look at the gentleman's face later after the cinema? - and so there lay a leaden apple sweetness (or something reminiscent of sour apple rings) between the seats and something rather superficially herbaceous and lecherous (sage? Sage doesn’t smell like that!) that it would have been almost amusing if one didn’t have to sit next to it for a good two hours. It was a scent that - even if it had been applied more discreetly - crawls into every fiber of clothing and body and then ages quickly and unappealingly, as it draws its entire essence solely from its top note - flashy, sexy, and almost unbearably hot - which loudly proclaims: 'Today is your lucky day, babe!' For the sake of fairness, it should be added that Kouros Silver precisely represents that type of fragrance - top-note heavy, overtly sexy, and synthetically sweet - which is likely to meet with little favor among supposed connoisseurs like us, as it lacks depth, complexity, and refinement. However, since it shows no hesitation in bastardizing a 'good, old name' like Kouros for its transgression, this cannot be considered mitigating. Conclusion: I amused myself for a while with the thought of what it would be like if that gentleman really did manage to undress with a lady. And how he would then - with a remnant of Kouros Silver on his chest - glumly watch through the blinds as she waits alone for the night bus outside after the aforementioned question.

My first thought was that this (please excuse my pronunciation) puddle of some haphazardly thrown together ingredients surely comes from the no-name segment, costs maybe €1, and the perfumer has completely misjudged the situation. Because instead of a "perfume," he has created a scent for the most intimate area of the house. The toilet. For me, it is an extremely unpleasant smell of biting apple that shows itself very harshly in the opening and repeatedly draws its breath into my body like a stormy hurricane. It is fresh, yes. According to our most intimate needs, but also when we scent the room or just air it out. Um? *chuckles to myself* Total weird stuff, my husband thought so too, calling it Febreze. The scent itself quickly glides into nothingness. To make matters worse, there is a very peculiar freshness in the fragrance. The biting apple smell combines with this, creating an even more petulant connection. Something spicy lays over it, but this does not make the scent any more interesting, as the spiciness is not really identifiable. Perhaps some stale herb mix that has been sitting in the dark cupboard for years and is completely dried out. A lukewarm little scent that then throws in a bit of wood afterward. Totally insignificant. Paired with strange nuances of apple, stale herbs, and a freshness that has nothing to do with the cool waters of a river, but much more ends up in the sewer. I'm so sorry, but this is really unacceptable! Synthetic breeze from Febreze. This is the new Kourus Silver. Nothing more. A horror awaits anyone who engages with this. The good thing is that it doesn’t linger long and quickly seeks the exit. It doesn’t last more than 3 hours and seems totally insignificant in every situation. This is such a bad scent that one could almost cry when seeing which house it comes from. If this should really work for someone, then I doubt any human taste. A no-go! The downfall of YSL? So here it definitely applies: (sorry again) An absolute grab into the toilet. 10% for the bottle and that’s it!

Kouros was never really revolutionary in my eyes, nor did it set any trends! It fit perfectly into the opulent 1980s, where "animalic" fragrances like Chanel Antaeus, Dior Jules, Jil Sander Man Pure, Azzaro Pour Homme, or Aramis were in their heyday. In terms of sales figures, Kouros was riding high on the wave of success! A pillar-like bottle made of opal glass and a "heroic" (god-like) advertising campaign with shimmering heat, athletically appealing bodies, and the salty waves of the Mediterranean. God-like campaigns can also be found in the 21st century with Versace Eros and Paco Rabanne Invictus! Kouros has become a brand within a brand, with great summer "colognes," yes, that existed even 10 years ago *laugh*! Kouros is a myth, and although many say it has been reformulated to death after nearly 35 years, no offshoot can hold a candle to the original; after all, the footprints are simply too big! Therefore, in my opinion, it borders on blasphemy when such a youthful fragrance candidate adorns itself with the letters of the (All)Father! I don't know what the advertising strategists always hope for - do they want to attract a youthful clientele with such name derivatives and slowly introduce them to such established classics? Hardly, it's tactful "namedropping," new wine in old bottles. But that's the way it is today, unfortunately! The name "Silver" is programmatic; after an unspectacular start with a synthetic apple/pear composition, sage releases a lot of ozone, "metallic" shiny freshness! It smells like Mentos chewy candies - Invictus sends its regards! As the scent develops, the oh-so-trendy fruity sugar note awaits again, creating a muddled brew of dull, candied nuances reminiscent of Versace Eros. Booooring! The base is reached after about 2 hours. What remains is an indefinable chemical cocktail of woody, sweet notes. I don't even want to wait for the end. My disappointment is evident, so I want to get to the conclusion quickly! Kouros Silver is a clear challenge to the aforementioned counterpart fragrances and corresponds to the youthful spirit of the times! The vocabulary fits the theme, and the campaign featuring male model Mias van der Westhuizen against a steel-blue sky underscores this. Longevity is roughly 5-6 hours. The sillage is initially good, but the scent quickly becomes intimate. Although I always evaluate perfumes subjectively - Kouros Silver is, after L'Homme Parfum Intense and L'Homme Sport, by far the biggest disappointment from YSL! Monsieur Laurent himself must be turning in his grave, the gods are closing off Olympus, and I prefer to reach for my Kouros summer versions again...! PS: Thanks to the benefactor of my sample, whose vial I would like to pass on to the first interested party!

Not long ago, I believed that YSL simply had a few weaker years and would eventually recover creatively and artistically, but "Kouros Silver" has now proven me wrong. The idea that a YSL fragrance could ever receive less than 6.0 or even 5.0 points seemed completely absurd to me, but 4.4 - I must confirm - is unfortunately only fair for this vile concoction.

I have been following the comments on Parfumo, noticing how poorly KS is rated and practically torn apart, and this automatically raises the question for me: "IS IT REALLY THAT BAD?!?" Mmmmh.... I then found a well-stocked perfumery that carries it, I tested it and I find that the scent, taken on its own, is actually quite okay.

What can one write that is so great about this newly released Kouros Silver? In my opinion, it is nothing special. It is clearly made for the masses. Nothing more, nothing less. When I read here that it is produced by L'Oréal, it became clear to me which direction it was supposed to take.

I am a big fan of Body Kouros! I was thrilled when I saw that the house of YSL was releasing something "new" in the bottle of Body Kouros. And yesterday I smelled it! I almost had to cry :) Well, Body Kouros wasn't a HUGE hit in the early 2000s either, but it had its own reason for existence. This one is just... hmm... clumsy... loud...

First off, this bottle is stunning. This is my new favorite bottle. It's holographic and mirrored. I got this for the bottle since I collect pretty bottles. Now for the juice. At first in the opening I got a little Light Blue Eau Intense but unfortunately that only lasted for 5 seconds and then it turned into this sharp citrusy, screechy, spicy mess. I think it's the oregano that throw this all off the most and just doesn't mesh with the rest of the notes. As a unisex fragrance I think this definitely leans more masculine.

Fragrance Notes Top Notes: Sorbet, Lemon, Oregano. Mid Notes: Sand, Freesia, Jasmine. Base Notes: Cypress, Vetiver, Musk. First thoughts, it's an Aromatic/Aquatic Sweet, mixed with Jasmine and Sand accords. - The opening begins with a airy lemon scent, mixed with Jasmine, creating a very aquatic light citrus lemon mixed with Jasmine notes. The mid and dry down has a sweet aromatic, Herbal and white floral scent. - I sprayed a total of 5 times. Twice behind each ear, twice on the front of neck, and once in front of my chest. The projection and longevity is really good, it lasts approximately 9 hours on my skin, and projects for about an hour before turning into a skin scent. (Depends on skin types) Overall Rating (8/10) - Toy 2 Pearl is a sweet aromatic, white floral dominated fragrance for both men and women. The sand accord makes this fragrance unique and definitely stands out with the other fragrances on the market.

...because I have a soft spot for the Moschino teddy bear perfumes. The packiging is kind of cute and kind of awful at the same time, definitely eye-catching. And I like the actual scents inside! Toy 2 is a nice fresh laundry scent, Toy 2 Bubble Gum is a really cute rosy bubblegum (duh) and Toy Boy is a surprisingly good masculine rose. Toy 2 Pearl is the weakest link so far. I don't hate it, I just don't like it as much. So, this is essentially a clean scent, which links it to the original Toy 2. Otherwise they're not similar. I get a lot of lemon here and I understand why it gets compared to D&G Light Blue. They have a very similar structure, but notes-wise, Light Blue feels softer and a little sweeter. In Toy 2 Pearl the lemon blends together with the oregano note, which in my opinion doesn't smell that realistic, but still noticeably herbal. Together they remind me of lemongrass scented products. I don't get much of the florals or the mysterious sand note from this. The base consists of vague fuzzy woods and white musk. It's a bit sharp and synthetic smelling, but not unbearably so. This is exclusively a warm weather scent, in winter this kind of synthetic freshness just feels off. It needs warm skin to give a freshly showered effect to. It's firmly a unisex scent, neither masculine nor feminine, just clean. A genderless robot couldn't go wrong with it. I'm a bit puzzled about the name "Pearl" and the oilslick coloring of the bottle. There is absolutely nothing in this scent that reminds me of pearls, not even remotely, and if I had to assign a color to this scent, I would chose a bright, yellowish green.

I bought this perfume without knowing any notes or what it smelled like. This gorgeous, crazy bottle is what caught my attention! Not an other boring lemon scent.. Lemon, lemon and more lemon! That's all its giving. Its smells good but its nothing special. Smells like every other basic lemon perfume out there. Its a great vacation fragrance, reminds me of being on the beach in the hot sun.

I blind bought this because I love the bottle and found a small 30 ml at a good price. Based off reviews and notes I knew it was going to be close to Moschinos I Love Love, but supposedly stronger and longer lasting. It’s very close to I Love Love however the lemon is creamier and the oregano is very blunt. It is indeed long lasting which kind of surprised me for this scent profile but it easily stuck around for 6ish hours, however I’d say sillage is at the low end of moderate. It blooms nicely in the heat and stays fresh despite to herby-ness that tags along. I wish I could smell the freesia, it would take this next level. It’s a little too masculine and the oregano just doesn’t sit well with me. It is a nice smell and a refreshing take on a summer citrus scent but this one is going into the trade or sell pile. I already know I won’t reach for it. Versace Dylan Turquoise or Versense have the same unisex citrus freshie vibe and I’d go for one of those instead.

When I received a sample of this fragrance, I had no expectations at all. The packaging automatically triggers associations, and I honestly had prejudices. Nevertheless, I tried it and was positively surprised. I like this fresh, slightly herbal little water and have even been complimented on it. Toy 2 Pearl was my surprise of spring 2024.

... a lemon sorbet with lemon cream on this hot day at a beach in Cyprus, that's just the right thing. I also ordered a cappuccino and enjoy this under a sun umbrella. From the terrace, I have a wonderful view of the Mediterranean and watch the ships and surfers. Most of all, I enjoy watching the people strolling along the promenade.

It is a beast in a bottle. A powerful citrus with spice that fills the entire room of an aroma that projects a high class scent, fresh, citrus, woody spicy with slight barbershop feel.. There is an animalic tone, light aquatic & after shower fleeting along the spices. It is winter evening when I applied this, all over my neck, wrist & chest. My whole room smells far from an air freshener despite a dominant citrus. I went out of the room to prepare dinner & after an hour, my room still smells awesome. This is one of the real powerhouse perfume that does not cloy. I never though this will work on minus temperature/cold nights. I highly recommend this to men late 20's & up. This is versatile, all-weather, all occasion because power bottle it may be, sillage & longevity monster, this will please the weare & definitely attract both genders to get near you. Women would love this on a man especially when worn right after a bath. Is this a cuddly scent? Give it an hour and you will be irresistible to your loving partner. This can match those highly reviewed niche fragrances. Well refined, rich, manly freshness & very pleasant spice that exude "sophistication & a classy gentleman". I rate this 9.5/10 for over all quality & compliments. One of the best chypre with citrus & spices. I even smell some hints of leather on heart & base.

When I tested the fragrance, I was quite taken aback and simultaneously surprised that it has been around for quite a few years, to be precise, almost 35. I did not expect that, as it seemed timeless yet not outdated. Unfortunately, I have not yet had the opportunity to compare it with its successor "YSL Pour Homme," which I would have been very interested in. I would like to thank Moenti for the sample. Fragrance Development: In the opening, the fragrance starts off with a full-bodied lemony freshness, but tempered by a noble, classic spiciness. Both notes are very well balanced and feel very high-quality. Throughout the development, there is hardly any change, just nuances. The juicy citrus quality remains until the end, providing a consistently penetrating freshness. The slightly herbaceous-spicy elements stand almost equally alongside the hesperidic notes from the heart, allowing enough space for the latter to breathe. Upon closer sniffing, one can discern that the lemon is a mix of full-bodied and citrus-herbaceous. The spicy elements are still restrained at the beginning and then slowly become more prominent. I perceive the citrus note throughout as exclusively bitter-herbaceous with a now slightly soapy undertone. After about 1 hour, a wood note joins in with a subtly animalistic-dirty touch. In the base, a honey-sweet, fir-like element adds to the fragrance, making it overall very elegant, well-groomed, masculine, and somewhat sexy. Longevity and Sillage: For such a citrusy fragrance, it has a long-lasting presence. I could perceive it well on the skin for 7-8 hours. The sillage was also above average for such a scent. However, it is by no means unpleasant and can be perceived for a long time at a whole to half an arm's length. Conclusion: A full-bodied citrus-spicy fragrance, situated between retro and modern. Essentially timelessly classic, fresh, and elegant. Therefore, it is not only suitable for summer but also wearable in the other seasons. I find it a tad too dominant in lemon, but aside from that, it is a very pleasant, well-groomed, masculine, fresh scent with style that actually fits any occasion. For lovers of citrus-spicy fragrances, it is a real insider tip that is unfortunately no longer available and also hard to find in online stores. If available, then currently at acceptable prices. I am curious about the comparison with the current Pour Homme!

Vulgar, extremely vulgar. But with style. Saint Tropez. Günter Sachs throws roses from the helicopter to win over Bardot. With the Porsche to the highway rest area, a quick number in the restroom, but in an Armani suit. Anyone who can afford to spend their everyday life in the midst of this fragrance without encountering problems has definitely made it.

I can hardly bring myself to write a comment on whether I am worthy of this divine drop; I do not know. With trembling fingers, I removed the cellophane, reverently lifted the bottle, and carefully anointed my wrist. Humbly lowering my head, I inhaled... what a temple aroma, the scent of the finest offerings to the gods! Citrusy on the surface, beneath it hums like a sovereign rhythm the incense... and various other noble ingredients that I cannot immediately identify in my first intoxication. This is how the priestesses and druids in Avalon must have smelled during the highest holidays. In any case, it is a fragrance that surely pleases the gods and that truly not everyone can wear, and the occasions for it are likely quite rare. The devoted servant may approach the altar of sacrifice with it; the finest occasions might also be deemed worthy, but for everyday life, this is nothing! Too heavy, too exalted, too divine is this darkly shimmering cherub! I now fall silent again in awe and humility and pay homage to my wrist.

Before it goes Out-of-Print (that's what they say about movies^^), I quickly order this Top 100 perfume on eBay for relatively little cash... I expected luxury, warmth & a fresh scent... all of this was indeed delivered well, but in a strength reminiscent of A*Men... really intensely strong, almost headache-inducing... Definitely too intense for summer and personally too incense-heavy for me... so after the first day, I can't agree with the high rating... lemony, flashy, old-school. As a 23-year-old, you really don't know when and how to use this bomb... I hope I can warm up to this scent, otherwise it might be my first bad purchase :-( ADDENDUM: after wearing it several times, I correct myself from 50 to 70%, the trick is not to sniff it so closely with your nose, as it is way too strong & unpleasant at first... but it still won't be a top scent!

......Acapulco was not far away, the party in New York quickly accessible, and the nightclubs in Paris or London just around the corner. JET SET I received my decant of Haute Concentration yesterday and was really excited. Admittedly, I had some doubts, as I have been at odds with almost all YSL fragrances (except for Opium pour Homme).

Here it is, the Badass Lemon. It hits you with a strong, highly concentrated, spicy lemon like a punch. A freshness tsunami for the olfactory cells. The grandfather of lemon fragrances! The Mugler among citrus scents. If Johnny Knoxville had worn this fragrance in the movie Bad Grandpa, it would have fit his role perfectly.

A blind buy from the eBay before the good stuff sinks into the nirvana of fragrance history. I sprayed it, and the first impression was stunning. Wow, what a surprise!! A dark, dirty lemon comes flying at you. Better said, it tries to knock you down. Nothing fresh or cheerful. Behind it follow all the well-known and beloved chypre notes, including a hardcore oakmoss note.

I went down to Roja Dove Haute Parfumerie at Harrods in April 2016, and tried 16 of the semi-bespoke collections. Wowzer! all of them were nice but was blown away by no 11. Its heady, opulent, intoxicating, mind blowing perfume I have ever come across. The silage was monstrous and longevity was just shy of 24 hours. Love, love, love this parfum. The staff were just wonderful. Well done Roja Dove, for creating this masterpiece!

With this fragrance, you can't go wrong in the summer. When you apply it, you float in a citrus heaven. The longevity isn't great, but it doesn't hurt the wallet too much if you spray it generously from head to toe and treat yourself to a new freshness kick every 3 hours or so. The bottle is beautifully appealing, colorful, and there's a lot to admire. Especially when placed well, it's a real eye-catcher. For color lovers, it's a nice collectible, but unfortunately, for extravagant fragrance enthusiasts, it's not a standout. In my opinion, you can even wear SO REAL while exercising, because it makes you smell good even if you might not look particularly great. And everyone knows that when you smell good, your attractiveness increases. The fragrance always finds a place in my handbag during the summer because I like to apply it on the go, even if I've used a different scent in the morning; SO REAL works in summer, really.

Most of you here probably feel the same way: some fragrances evoke a certain memory within you. As long as that memory is positive, those fragrances are my favorites. Recently, I found myself in the drugstore with the horse logo. "Just testing, not buying" was (as often...) my motto. I actually wanted to check out those Rammstein perfumes, but they weren’t available there. The funny yet somehow ugly bottle of Cheap and Chic - So Real caught my attention. So I sprayed it, just to be safe on a test strip. Okay - citrusy-fresh, nice, a bit like Light Blue, do I need this? Probably not. I tucked the test strip into my handbag. Later at home, I took it out again and suddenly thought of my mom... And of a wonderful summer vacation in Tuscany, where my father, due to his very rudimentary Italian skills, had rented the entire building for three weeks instead of just an apartment in a country villa. That was really ages ago, almost 30 years, my mother couldn’t have used this perfume back then. Maybe it was a sunscreen, a body lotion, another perfume? I don’t know, and unfortunately, I can’t ask my mother because she passed away in 2006. In any case, the scent doesn’t stay so citrusy but develops a very slight creaminess after a while. Even on my skin - because by now, Cheap and Chic - So Real was allowed to move in with me after all. It also becomes a bit floral, but the peony remains subtle and doesn’t become sharp as it unfortunately does with some fragrances. I would classify H/S as a good average for a summery-fresh scent. For the price, I can definitely reapply - and think of Mom :)

You can't really dawdle, wander, or meander, well, you can, but not in department stores and perfumeries. And since I needed a few haberdashery items today (what a lovely old-fashioned word!), I decided to go to the larger drugstore that, unlike my small market nearby, has a slightly broader (drugstore) perfume selection. So I checked out what’s new (not really much, a new Laura in pink and a new white/yellow La Rive), what’s on clearance (some from Betty Barclay), and what else they have. Then I see the Cheap and Chic line, all in 30 ml and right at the bottom of the shelf. I love love and So real are discounted, but not Olivia. So I test the two blue ones and I actually know I love love; it always reminds me of Light Blue or Desigual Fresh, nice, but I already have something like that, so on to "So Real." Surreal, that’s how the bottle appears to me, asymmetrical, the winking eye, the colorful glass bottle, I don’t find it tasteless; I find it funny and it has a sense of self-irony. The many little symbols remind me directly of a cheerful Picasso or a mischievous Dalí. Spain, Italy, lightness, vacation, Dolce Vita, and the scent of lemon blossom, I’m already on a little journey in my head. Sprayed on, fresh and citrusy but slightly fruitier than I love love, without becoming a fruit salad; we remain here a refreshing little water, very Italian, invigorating, and full of cheer. The blackcurrant particularly captivates me. Later, it becomes a bit more floral, fragrant, peony but subtle, my dear jasmine, fresh and green, a few light woods, a bit of oak moss in the base, why not? It harmonizes wonderfully with the bitter orange. So real, I call it Surreal... because I could use a little escape from everyday life... it’s a fresh light yellow sunbeam in the blue pre-spring sky, a pink cloud, and a breeze of confidence, courage, and optimism that blows towards me. Bought.

Today I discovered a new Moschino in the perfume shop - wrapped in an attractively colorful packaging. The outfit immediately caught my eye - but the "old" Cheap is still waiting in my scent chamber for its discovery. I haven't quite warmed up to it yet - despite the original Olivia bottle. However, the sky-blue flanker managed to score points with me - so what was so real? My husband likes to call me "out of touch with reality" - and I pointed meaningfully to the tester up high. In this case, reality was indeed far from me. Are all realists over 1.80 m tall? My husband gallantly fished down the pretty bottle for me - and even the first spray said: Yes! A staircase of fresh oranges rolls down towards me, delicately sweetened with raspberries. The peony blooms finely and the jasmine brightens the fragrance. Despite its fullness, so real remains transparent. The cedar adds a woody note - but it doesn't weigh down the scent. Oak moss acts only as a whisper and adds a bit of depth. So colorful and lively, real life can be. Pure good mood - and this lasts for hours. I will also kindly turn my attention back to the original mother Olivia - because the beautiful flankers cannot lie.

I agree with the review below mine that says it is "uncomplicated beauty" or something along those lines, but I'm not being positive when I say "uncomplicated." It is so low key as to almost not be wearing anything. I don't hate how it smells, but I also just...I'm like it's a floral. Sure. It's a floral. Not the kind of smell that sticks with you, which I'm sure is a draw for some people, but I use fragrance for memory and emotional regulation, so having something that feels incredibly generic (it's nice! I swear! just...generic) doesn't work for my lifestyle.

This is a very bright, fresh, floral scent. Longevity and sillage are above average. I smell magnolias and peonies. The musk is very light, clean, and not sweet. For me, unmistakable and unique. The fragrance seems simple, but it is so beautifully composed that you want to wear it all the time.

At the first sniff, I was immediately in love. Magnolia and rose are old acquaintances, but for me, this combination sounds absolutely fantastic. It is a perfectly tuned and well-rehearsed duo that presents a floral melody in a very successful way. For both the magnolia and the rose, I think of light pink blossoms. It's not about sexy blood red, but about delicate light pink shades. The floral main theme is introduced by a whisper-thin citrus note and rounded off by slightly woody base chords. It's a pity that the scent doesn't last too long. Still one of my favorites.

There's a lot to like about Cheap & Chic Light Clouds, mostly in the way that it's refreshing, subtly sweet and pleasing to the nose. Moschino makes some lovely Summer scents, so I whole heartedly recommend the line for specific warm weather use. Light Clouds opens with what smells like mashed pears and baby powder. This is a surprisingly likable blend, especially when the peach note makes an entrance. I feel lightened by wearing this fresh, clean and airy scent. The drydown takes on more of a musky skin-scent, with a cedary base that somewhat resembles D&G Light Blue. It has an undeniable comfy-ness about it that I really like, hence the reason why this fragrance is getting such a good review from me. The longevity, in all honesty could be better, but it's certainly not bad. However on clothes Light Clouds tends to hold a lot longer, scenting them with a musky citrus and peach blend. My favourite Summer scent from Moschino is still Funny!, however Light Clouds is a close runner-up.

So clean and yet so quirky-sometimes the bottle just fits the scent like two cheeks on a toilet seat. “Light Clouds” is squeaky clean, no question about it. The cedar provides a blue, slightly spicy sport shower gel freshness. The white musk brings a cozy freshly-washed feeling. The lotus makes it beautifully aquatic-fresh. So it hardly gets cleaner than this. But that’s not all. Because “Light Clouds” is in a very quirky way futuristically sterile. Not sterile in the hygienic sense. But sterile like the whole wonder world under the sign of the bitten apple. Smooth and shiny like white piano lacquer. Deliberately sterile-somehow. Plastic-like. At the same time, from start to finish, there is a very strong synthetic violet note that reminds me of several scents from about 15 years ago. Above all, it reminds me of “Baby Rose Jeans” by Versace. Powdery, squeaky, beautiful. Thus, this olfactory iCloudchen has a distinct retro note despite all its futuristic sterility. Conclusion: A crazy little cloud. Or the kitschy, shrill techno interpretation of a cloud. Like neon blue clouds on ecstasy, with a heartbeat faster than 200 BPM. However, the miserable longevity spoils all the fun. After at most two hours, the clouds are gone.

Come with me, we’re going Somewhere and then We’ll look up and see The clouds I take you by the hand And pull you along behind me I wonder why it’s so hard I think you don’t want it anymore Is your nature So hard to read for everyone If I can’t understand it How does it feel for you And when you leave I watch you go See how the end twists What the beginning promised The weather will be Cloudy to bright again The clouds move on (Alin Coen - Clouds) This song lyric fits like a glove! This is one of the few fragrances that I simply cannot rate. I don’t know. From “ecstatic” to “deeply depressed,” this fragrance really has EVERYTHING in it. So where do I even begin? I saw Light Clouds today at TkMaxx for an unbeatable €29.90... 100ml!!!! I just had to buy it blindly, knowing that normally just 30ml already costs €30. I had never sniffed it before, but I had read so many reviews that I had been eagerly waiting to finally get my hands on it. Unfortunately, there’s no way to test the fragrances at TkMaxx, so I was brave... with the cute bottle, I was sure it could also make a great birthday gift if I didn’t like it. Apparently, many women find it great, so I thought I could easily sell it on eBay... that was my first thought. Bottle: The bottle is incredibly cute and encourages you to buy it so much that you order/buy it completely blindly and think unreflectively, “if the scent is crap, I’ll just toss it and put a nicer fragrance in the bottle.” As I said, unreflective, since you can’t open this bottle without breaking it. Still beautiful. The scent: With my Plan B in mind (to sell or gift the fragrance on eBay), I sprayed on Light Clouds. Now I understand what my predecessor meant by LSD-neon-clouds. Guys... the opening almost made me cry. It was so disgusting. SO DISGUSTING. You could also call it “retro,” but you don’t have to :D I couldn’t even figure out WHAT I was SMELLING. My nose felt numb from this synthetic attack. For the first 10 minutes, it smelled really strong like varnish... and at best like Pantene Pro V (5 different types of silicone in just ONE shampoo bottle, you don’t want that on your scalp!) At some point, I think I discerned that it was artificial peach. Shortly after, I detected (or so it seemed to me) artificial musk and mega artificial rose. What came next, I absolutely cannot identify. Must be artificial lotus. And all in all, what possibly makes this opening so dreadful: artificial violet. Light Clouds really smells cheap, but not chic. Really like the CHEAPEST ingredients that China has to offer.
