Additionally, there’s a very light woody note in the background, but in my opinion, you can't really tell that it's cedarwood. However, it mostly smells like roses later on. Nothing spectacular, simply constructed, quite okay, well, maybe slightly synthetic, but in a not too disturbing way, even if it does make it seem a bit cheaper. Only towards the end of the scent, after about four or five hours, does it smell like a nondescript, cheap something, at which point you know it’s time to reapply the fragrance. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is normal, meaning you will be able to smell the fragrance from a not too great distance. The longevity is about four to five hours, after which it smells increasingly trivial and worse. The bottle: At first glance, the bottle actually looks like a cleaning product, just like its predecessor, although the predecessor, Fresh Couture, looked a bit more like a cleaning product due to its blue color... are there even pink cleaning products?? See? I have no idea about such things! :DD Anyway, I find the idea cool and funny. It would have been even better if you could pull the "trigger" to spray from the nozzle. Instead, you pull off the "spraying device" like a cap, and underneath is the actual spray head. Well... still a funny bottle. Okay, based on the bottle description, you now know that you can't spray this fragrance like a cleaning product. However, I must sadly say that people seem to be inherently foolish. It can happen that one of the guys doesn’t want to give up right away and fiddles with the sprayer. At some point, he pulls out the part (in this case, the cap), discovers the spray head, but doesn’t think that it could be a fragrance,... and starts cleaning the windows with the scent to "show his wife that he can also engage in household chores!" And I bet this scenario has definitely happened more than once, especially if the wife has her fragrances in the bathroom (by the way, not necessarily recommended), where there might also be some cleaning products... Well, anyway, this fragrance is nothing special and mainly smells (later) of slightly synthetic, sweet roses. Not really bad in itself, but unfortunately has a bit too much of a drugstore cheap fragrance aura. Still usable and of course much better than most of those "drugstore fragrances," but interchangeable or a scent that no one will really miss if it were to disappear, except maybe for the interestingly designed bottle. In my opinion, it’s not really worth testing, but the bottle is worth a look :D

The most delicious jammy rose patchouli. It has a warm, rounded, honied quality, with the most yummy patchouli and vetiver lending a dark and sexy quality. I agree with the reviewer below, all of the other notes in this composition are there purely to add depth to the main characters, and do not shine as such on their own. The jasmine and tea notes bring relief to the composition, preventing it from becoming too heavy or jammy.... this is not a heady and intoxicating perfume, it retains a character of lightness, cleanliness, and elegance whilst being undeniably rouge, sensual and romantic. You could definitely wear this as a day-to-night scent, though perhaps not at work! I won't lie, it makes me want to sell my bottle of Le Fille de Berlin because this kind of jammy geranium-rose suits me a lot more.

As an avid lover of rose, I expected to like this one. But tbh, I think I’ve fallen in love. The scent bubble this leaves around me is absolutely hypnotizing and I’m constantly thinking about wearing it. RV is arguably the most well balanced rose-patchouli scent I’ve come across. And when I say well balanced, I mean 50% rose, 50% patchouli. While I do get the other notes in this composition, they are there to support the main characters, and they do so in the best way possible. I get a lot of the jasmine and the vetiver here, but the tea and pepper add a gently spicy/aromatic touch and the jasmine add a sensual softness. It’s so well blended and has a smoothness to it that makes it feel rich and expensive. If silk had a scent, I would imagine it to smell like this. While the composition feels simple, it’s rather interesting and keeps me wanting to inhale more and more of it. This is a wonderful floral for the cooler weather and the early spring, and gives me romantic vibes. It could be one for work if applied lightly, but I see this more for date night or more sexy occasions. Right now, I have a 30 ml decant of it, but I will most definitely upgrade to a full 125 ml bottle of it when the time comes. Idk why this one doesn’t get more attention of all the Les Vestaires line from YSL.

I discovered this perfume today at the Printemps Boulevard Haussmann in Paris. a great discovery, before smelling it I was worried because the seller announced a rose perfume and I am rarely a fan of this type of fragrance. but this one is different the smell of rose is different and light it combines very well with other elements, it is a rather feminine perfume perfect for mid-season. it is neither heady nor bewitching but rather classy, ​​elegant and refined, it restores its letters of nobility to the rose. too feminine for me to buy it but I'm putting it on the wishlist for Madame's collection

An amazing combination of tea, rose, and patchouli. The tea adds lightness and freshness, preventing the composition from becoming too heavy, as often happens in many other perfumes with this combination. The rose is very beautiful here. Autumnal, but not grand, rather somehow cheerful. The fragrance is beautifully composed, and the bottle is lovely.

I love Moschino, their fragrances are either classy or crazy but they never disappoint, Couture follows in that tradition. Despite the pepper note, on my skin Couture opens up in a sweet and rather soft fashion. Citrus and floral notes mingle in wonderful harmony with the pepper and prevent it from making it a dominant note. The middle phase is all about jasmine and has a woodsy feel about it. Woodsy with a slight vanilla edge that makes it very unique in its overall composition. The woodsy feel doesn't drown the flowers out, I can even smell the poppy! The dry-down mixes all notes into an unusual scent experience. It's a sensual and 'soapy' scent, very bold and noticeable. It has a heavy vintage vibe about it, yet it's also modern, a 'bi-polar' scent that seems to combine the best of these two worlds. It reminds me a lot of Estee Lauders "Cinnabar", but Couture is more bold and gutsy whereas Cinnabar (to my nose) is shyer and demure. It's a scent that makes a statement its "Couture a la Parfum" and wants other people to know that too. The bottle is also cute, who can resists a flacon with a ribbon AND a heart? : ) Silage is: "I am noticed and I should because I am classy and beautiful" -- Longevity is great: 7+ hours. A bold, heavy and beautiful Moschino that is wonderful for evenings, dates and all those occasions that you want to make an impact. These days it's harder to get, but if you find it you must -at least- sample it, it's a vintage in the making.

Moschino Couture! is a truly delightful scent. Often mentioned by celebrities themselves as being one of their favourite scents, Mena Suvari being one of them, this fragrance has certainly gained a lot of success. It's not hard to see why Couture! has captured so many people's hearts. The fragrance opens with peppered citrus which is both unique and classy. The scent is feminine without being overly sweet or fruity. Whenever you suspect that this fragrance will become too predictable or girly, it hits you with a note which completely changes your mind. The pepper in the opening, the pomegranate in the heart and the benzoin in the drydown are examples of notes which continue to change the composition and give Couture! that unusual and distinctive appeal. Its spicy and woodsy type scent blends so well when worn on the skin. Couture! has such a natural feel to it, almost as if it isn't a perfume at all. Hard to believe that something so wonderful is sold at such an affordable price, I highly recommend.

Couture! by Moschino, one of the few that survived my decluttering phase years ago. I miss some (like L’Insolent by Charles Jourdan), while with others I wonder why I kept them. This one falls into the latter category, a frustration purchase from years ago, and I never really warmed up to it (until today:-). However, I do find the bottle really pretty, which was probably also the reason it was allowed to stay. Well, today after such a long time, I’m giving it another try and I’m pleasantly surprised: The opening must have scared me off back then, because I’m not greeted by a single peppercorn, no, it’s even a whole mill! But - thanks to the bergamot and the slight sweetness of the mandarin, it becomes immediately softer and more pleasant, even delicately soapy, just enough for me to like it, because I don’t like it too soapy. On my skin, there’s now a clear transformation: although the flowers are now showing, it never becomes too sweet or too floral, the jasmine does seem a bit fresher due to the pomegranate blossoms, yet a pleasant powderiness emerges that merges with my skin. The longer I smell on my arm, the more fascinated I become! Fine, slightly sweet vanilla is enveloped by a cool, somewhat bitter breeze… This combination is so tempting and enchanting, I could bathe in it! Luckily, it also lasts the longest in this phase, I can perceive it for up to 4-5 hours. Conclusion: Certainly not an easy fragrance, one that you have to discover, that unfolds, and I needed time to understand it. You have to be a bit careful with the dosage, otherwise, you might get peppered! I wouldn’t want to wear it daily, but now and then when I need something special, then definitely! However, I can imagine wearing it in any season, thanks to the coolness it radiates, it would surely be well-suited for summer evenings. I’m glad it still has its place in my display…

Couture! is a fragrance that I certainly wouldn’t have added to my wish list based on its scent pyramid. Even in the perfume store, it probably wouldn’t have caught my eye right away, as it makes quite a discreet impression and doesn’t immediately stand out. And it behaves the same way when tested on the skin. Neither mandarin nor bergamot are perceptible at the start for me; there is no freshness at all, but rather an immediate alcoholic note. Essentially, Couture! reduces itself to its base notes. There is hardly any development of the scent. Cedar and benzoin create a kind of distance from the fragrance, while vanilla brings it closer again. Couture! never truly merges with the skin, as is often the case with other vanilla scents. It is a well-tempered fragrance, neither warm and cozy, which one might expect due to the vanilla, nor cold and harsh, which could be caused by the benzoin and cedar. These three ingredients are very nicely balanced and well combined. If you look at women's fragrances, these components are found in some scents from the late 80s or the 90s. However, Couture! was created in 2003 and has taken up this concept again, but in a much more minimalist way. For me, despite its release date, it feels a bit old-fashioned. Many thanks to Ingepetra for the sample.

Rather too discreet, I'd say. So you'd have to use much more than you'd normally do in order to feel it as you'd like to. The scent is very elegant, a blend of rhum, vanilla and some other spices, as far as I can tell, and not sweet at all, which is a major plus for me. A bit overpriced, given the excessively discreet nature, yes, that would come to mind.

To say it right from the start: this will not be a grand, impressive commentary. It is an attempt in response to the question: "Can I still do this?" or (very importantly!): "Do I still want this?" Because I am not entirely pleased with the developments of the past weeks here either. Those who accompanied me in the past know that. So: Let's see! But now to the topic: After an interlude with the enchanting scent dreams of Hubert de Givenchy, I recently ventured into "Le Vestiaire - Cuir" by YSL on a dark and rainy evening. This brand and I have never really harmonized: even "Opium" (in its pure form at the beginning of the eighties) developed more herbaceous-spicy for me; the erotic component was lost due to lack of body warmth. Perhaps that was for the best: a rather prim blonde being, as I was back then, would have been quite shocked by the power that "Opium" is known to possess. This attempt was not uninteresting, but it shaped our further coexistence: YSL and I kept a polite distance from each other. So "Le Vestiaire - Cuir" was once again a journey into adventure. I sprayed cautiously and was left wide-eyed in astonishment: Hey, this is a "cave of comfort" inviting for a cozy winter sleep! Behind a heavy wooden double door, a snug atmosphere prevails: dark warmth, interrupted by dancing flames and islands of light! The cocktail served upon entry, based on spicy rum, warms and pleasantly stimulates the senses. What might have been mixed into this dark brown-golden drink? Ah!, the slight sharpness of ginger and precious saffron: what a noble entrée! Heavy dark furniture, arranged with thick cushions in autumnal colors for lingering, and drawn velvet curtains enhance the cave-like character of this environment. Spicy wood and "well-loved" leather exude aromas that appeal to the senses. This fragrant ambiance could seem purely masculine; also due to the faint hint of pipe tobacco that pleasantly wafts through the room. - But it does not! Gold and brown tones and shimmering dancing lights, transformed into scent here, warm and lead to the silver-glimmering tea set on a tastefully prepared dresser. Floral-spicy osmanthus and a noble black tea infusion offer soothing warmth and fine aromas. Sensually awakened by the warming golden top note, this bitter-spicy scent development can be enjoyed holistically and gender-neutrally. Sillage and longevity correspond to what can be expected from this brand: a long-lasting full-bodied scent comfort. The house of Yves Saint Laurent offers me with "Le Vestiaire - Cuir" an unusually cozy-scented cave of comfort that once again awakens my annual recurring desire for winter sleep! Something I can retreat to, that envelops me protectively when the world becomes demanding once again. By the way, demanding: "Le Vestiaire - Cuir" requires open senses and trust in its perhaps somewhat alien darkness. Crossing this threshold opens a feel-good area that invites you to linger!

She does not remember her past. Did she even have one? She was never alone. She only knew the wind. How it blew around her. It lifted her up. Her and her sisters. Together they flew. It was beautiful. Now she was alone. Too long in this place. All ruffled. In deep longing to fly once again. Past the docks with the workers and their rum. The shoeshiner and the fine leather shoes. The pipe tobacco of the coachmen during their break. Longing. Then she sent a summer breeze on her last journey. Farewell. I was torn whether to write a comment on this fragrance. Normally, I test on the pulse with a spray. Then I check if I generally want more and add a spray on the upper body. Well, with "Cuir" I needed two sprays on the pulse and was significantly more generous on the upper body. And yet I still had the strange feeling that there is something, but it is not present. When I stepped outside, and the wind played gently, suddenly a timid leather-rum combination built up, which is really beautiful. However, hardly present. More precisely, from the very beginning it was close. A subtle sweetness with tobacco rounds it off. Even with skin warmth, the fragrance unfortunately did not project further in sillage. So it remains the playful summer breeze that will hardly disturb anyone. Which is not a bad thing. Perhaps my mistake was expecting a bit more "space" from such a high-priced fragrance. I can recommend the fragrance to anyone who values subtle understatement in business rather than show. To anyone looking for a scent for cuddling and possibly also for the night. A fragrance for beautiful, quiet moments. Perhaps a picnic. With a summer breeze. A small addendum: The fragrance suddenly took off after about 1 hour. Why? No idea. A generous dosage, like in my test, resulted in more compliments than protests. I would now say that the sillage can be very well dosed "per spray." After one hour, the fragrance was then very present for 5 hours and carried me through the day. Now (after 8h) it is really close to the skin and presents itself wonderfully ambient. (Although there is no amber in it at all) :)

Leather is the new Oud - we’ve all known that for a while now. And orange blossom is the new leather? Rumor has it... Anyway, let’s not stray from this chic leather oriental. Because whoever first catches my attention from the new YSL Private Collection must have something special! "Cuir" is a mix of a black leather jacket and CH Men Privè - only finer, more expensive, and more upscale. An oriental bazaar where expensive leather goods are offered right next to the shisha bar and the dusty desert. Saffron fans will find more to enjoy here than leather enthusiasts. But Cuir just sells better than saffron or spices as a name. Yet I love my leather jackets just as much! Gentle, sandy, dry, and moist at the same time. Like shisha tobacco that you coat with Sahara sand and rub on your Harley Davidson jacket. A bit of Oud also mixes in the background, never losing the oriental direction and reinforcing it once again. Close to a going-out scent, yet too well-mannered and almost too chic. It varies greatly and seems to react aggressively to skin warmth. At times, it can scratch a bit and jump into your face. But most of the time, it’s a gentle treat before the spice lord. Like a desert breeze in the late afternoon, drifting into a Moroccan luxury hotel, where you’re just indulging in an English Harbour Rum and the exotic companion is already waiting in the next room... only dressed in leather boots. Bottle: worthy of an exclusive line - magnetic cap, heavy, sturdy, fine color gradient. Sillage: like 5 leather jackets at a spice bazaar. Longevity: 9 hours. 11 hours. No, almost 14! Conclusion: more of a tipsy saffron charmer than a harsh leather scent. Very delicious and very youthful. A fine fellow, far removed from club-goers or fakes. At first glance, the tastiest of the "Le Vestiaires"! An alcoholic-spicy delicacy.

I bought this fantastic scent for my husband, who only used it once and was immediately convinced. No, I don't like it! I always say: What the farmer doesn't know :-( Yet it smells so masculine, in a smart suit, standing tall with both feet in life! Even the bottle says: Here I am! Angular and heavy but still very elegant. The cap glides on thanks to magnetism, like many other fine fragrances. At first, it comes off quite fresh and floral, then it becomes softer, almost soapy. The leathery scent remains a bit sweet, like Uncle Klaus's pipe tobacco (he always used cherry tobacco), reminiscent of the fragrance from the 70s. I think of an Opel Admiral in rusty brown. Now the noble fragrance has finally found a new owner. What a shame, I thought the scent was great; it definitely sparks my imagination ;-) really a pity!

This is something a little different from Montale. Instead of being carried away to souks filled with exotic spices and fragrant resins, Greyland transports the imagination to a bleak, moonlit desert-scape ... and the desert does get cold at night! Per the Montale site, this "man's blend par excellence is composed of Cedarwood, Sandalwood, Vetiver and Kayak (sic - I think the intention was Guiac), combined with the spicy scents of Ginger and Black Pepper over a base of Arabian Leather, Musk and Tibetan rock Rose." While it does fall more toward the traditionally masculine, if one enjoys fragrant woods and Vetiver, I would not discount this one for the fairer sex. Greyland begins with an intense blast of black pepper and spices, almost sinus clearing! Invigorating and relatively short lived, as this stage subsides, the woods and Leather emerge and eventually dominate the composition. Never becoming loud or prickly, the Leather here is as smooth and refined as the finest chamois. Sadly, the Sandalwood is barely discernible, but Greyland is more about my favorite Cedar, ultimately exhibiting aromatic shades of grey. There are also hints of animalic sensuality here in the Musk, ... think of the term 'rode hard and put away wet' ... and draw your own conclusions ;). I have been working from the note pyramid provided on the site as I was baffled by the "Rose" listed in the breakdown on this page. There is definitely none in Greyland ... probably a typo as 'rock Rose' or Labdanum is definitely an ingredient of this fragrance. I really like Greyland ... I find it Byron-esque and broody! Think Heathcliff striding across the misty moors in polished riding boots, dark hair flopping languidly above steely eyes ... riding crop in hand ... *sigh*. But I digress!!!! Greyland has a decent but not overwhelming sillage and I find the longevity here not up to usual Montale standards. That said, it is also a fragrance that appeals to my romanticism and sensuality ... try it, if you dare ;).

Got a sample based upon a fellow fragr's suggestion as an upgrade to Bentley Absolute and DAMN! I have enjoyed every whiff I get from this. I love this on myself, and it is very masculine, but being it is unisex, this could be incredibly sexy on the right woman. I've picked up on different facets of it but it is mostly linear. Usually that great piquant Cedar-Pepper-Vetiver combo, but sometimes I get a beautifully smooth Leather-Sandlewood note. Halfway through my sample, and I want a big bottle. This shit is straight sexy sexy sex sex. Sweaty, Raw, and Dark. But also Serious. Because Greyland has a very serious feel. I think these two things are what turns people off, and that's ok with me. My only- and I mean only- gripe is performance. Granted, a big part of a fragrance is how easily you can smell it and for how long, but I am willing to look past the fact that it's pretty much just a skin scent that lasts for 6 hours or so. The first time I experienced this was a sample I got and admittedly didnt expect much because looking at the pyramid, everything seemed... Ordinary? I know how that sounds, but nothing jumped out at me. But damn if this isn't an example of not always (ever?) being able to judge by reading notes. That first experience, I wore it in the evening and gave it my full attention, and was blown away. It has a very similar opening to Bentley Absolute and Gucci Pour Homme I, with that peppery cedar wood, but also kind of body sweat, note. It is pretty much this for most of the time, and not much projection. But it is so very good. If you like GPH1 or Bentley Absolute, it's like they had a sexy sweaty baby and named it 'Greyland'.

Greyland by Pierre Montale We are in the year 3101. The blue planet lies in ruins and ashes. The world is gray. Among the debris and dust, remnants of things can still be found, signs that tell us of a once magnificent and shimmering time. We suspect that there must have been a cultural diversity here that is beyond our imagination. A bottle. A thick layer of dust covers it. We carefully free it from the dust. Inside, the remnants of a fragrance. - We cautiously sniff it. What is this? This fragrance also tells of a truly splendid time. A precious spice must have once carried it, lush the most beautiful roses. Noble woods. This scent seems to have once been a perfectly composed beauty. Captivating and fascinating. But time has taken away all its edges and peaks, covering it like powdered sugar with a dull layer of dust. Like the rest of this desolate world, this fragrance seems to have lost its character over the years. What a pity. With difficulty, we decipher something beneath the scratched surface of rock and dust: M ::: E ::: M ::: O ::: I ::: R ::: M ::: A ::: N Our time is running out, we must return to base. Somewhat nostalgically, we leave this "Greyland" behind and dream of a world, a time, for which we lack the words to describe it.

Today is once again one of those gloomy and dark days. It is cold and diffusely dark....the world no longer spins. Today is the day for Greyland. This scent awakens in me an icy and longing melancholy. When I wear Greyland, I always hear and see a video clip in my mind. Björk...All is Full of Love!!! In the clip, you see two machines...Cyborgs!!!.., who love each other in such an aesthetic way that it is hard not to burst into tears. It is one of the most beautiful and saddest videos of modern times. This scent fits perfectly. It smells like the pheromones of a machine.... To me, it smells like liquefied electronics. It is a cold, extremely cool, and repelling scent that it exudes. It feels repelling-attractive to me, like electricity itself. Greyland feels to me....melancholically beautiful. A scent that one wears in another galaxy, something we are not yet ready to wear because it teleports a sadness too powerful for us. Hard to describe...this scent spreads a heavy warmth to me. One thing is still very noteworthy about Greyland, its base note... it smells of woody-cool machine oil. This scent is not for depressive people; it could pull them down even more. But for those who want to maintain a cool distance, it is the perfect scent.

Greyland is a great fragrance! And broadly speaking, I agree with Imel regarding his associations. But at this point, I diverge: Desert? Yes! Dry, no water in sight. But the Wild West, steppes, and prairies are not the setting of Greyland. “Greyland” takes place in the desert of Iraq, on the border with Saudi Arabia! No cowboy on a horse, but a small caravan of camels peeking out from the slits of their headgear to protect themselves from the swirling sand. It’s almost sunset, but the air is still thick. The sun sets in a fiery red, the air shimmers. Sand is in the air, it smells of oil everywhere, and on the horizon, you can see a source here and there that has been ignited. Greyland is a dark fragrance. It smells smoky, but not of burnt woods, rather of synthetic materials that slowly smolder. What is easily detectable is the sandalwood; unfortunately, the rose does not reveal itself to me. But I also don’t know if I would have wanted it here. A truly floral note wouldn’t be very fitting here, have you ever seen a flower bed in the desert? Furthermore, guaiac wood is very present, but I have come to love this material and can hardly get enough of it! Earthy. Synthetic. Leathery. Slightly woody. That is Greyland. However, the fragrance is not so extreme or overpowering that it becomes almost unwearable. It is quite elegant, perhaps not as much as a “Black Tie” or an “Explorer,” but this scent can definitely be worn for going out or for dinner. No problem at all. Of course, Greyland will not be to everyone’s taste. And that’s a good thing ;) I give it 90%.

It's nice to test a Montale that doesn't have "Aoud" in its name! And yes... it clearly stands out in scent from its millions of brothers and sisters. After numerous tests on paper strips and occasionally on skin, Greyland was somewhat of an acquired taste, rather dull.

I initially categorized Greyland a bit hastily after my first wear as follows: Top: Avignon. Base: Memoir Man. Not only in terms of this assessment do I wholeheartedly recommend the wonderful comment of my predecessor Reckoner. I hold both Comme des Garçons' and Amouage's creations in high regard.

She has lost all her floral qualities, but one can imagine that she was once a beauty. The youthful floral character had to give way to a mature spicy ego. The childlike lightness had to make room for adult seriousness. She seems somewhat bitter, life has been hard on her.

Here I can smell coolness. Slightly damp coolness. Like fine mist creeping over the land. Carrying the scents of a woodland. Somewhere in Norway, just before the sea begins. Exactly, a fjord! At the start of a day in the Nordic autumn, when the days are already noticeably shorter and the sun rises at 8 AM only to dip below the horizon again by 5 PM.

Ah, a picture of clichéd Western romance. The shrub rustles through the scene, carried by the wind. A lonely cowboy rides on a weary horse through the sadly vast, dusty prairie. Around him, only sparse bushes and in the distance an old wooden cabin, barely discernible. The view blurred by grains of sand in the air, they burn in the eyes.

Got this coz I liked it so much instantly in the store. On the way home with it in my bag, I started thinking "I reckon this'll be just a carda-bomb and - "that's all folks!"". I recently made it my olfactory panoply for the day, and was greatly relieved to find it a stout harness. It stays the course alright - morphing into a more incensey brew certainly, but never completely shorn of the cardamom note - which I found impressive, as it is my experience that cardamom is generally highly fugitive, which is what sparked my doubts in the first place. I approve. I no longer have any doubts about my prudence in acquiring this.

I thank Callas very much for giving me the opportunity to compare NU Héritage with my original. I love NU a lot, but wearing it in everyday life often felt too intense or simply inappropriate. With NU Héritage, I now have the chance to surround myself with the somewhat mysterious atmosphere of the fragrance as well. If one accepts that this is not just NU re-released in a new presentation, but rather intended as a tribute to the original scent, then this fact can certainly be regarded as successful. I also believe that the floral notes come through more clearly and the base certainly does not consist solely of incense. It is much too soft and almost powdery for that. It should also be noted that while NU Héritage is indeed a light subtle fragrance, I find it to be much softer and more sensual, even more intimate, than the old NU EdT. It is completely incomprehensible to me that NU Héritage is (still?) not available in Germany. I had initially feared that it was just not listed at Müller, but a colleague was told at a YSL fragrance seminar that this perfume will not belong to the German Héritage line.

This is the latest member of the Nu family. Again conceived as an EdP, it clearly resembles the original, radiating the special, oddly foreign, mysterious beauty. Once more, there is the strong, almost harsh opening, very spicy fresh, and already underlaid with the cool, unsweet floral note that can also be found in the original and in the EdT. Here, however, it is much more pronounced. The smoky resin undertone is also quickly recognizable and forms, together with the flowers, an accord that becomes increasingly gentle and softer over time. The very long-lasting base is flattering, soft, and clearly noticeable in the immediate vicinity. Of the three variants of this exceptional fragrance, the EdP 2001 is my favorite. It is the uncompromising original formula with the clearest statement. In the EdT, Nu appears to me softened, more subtle, as a suitable everyday companion. Nu Heritage slightly alters the clear statement; the fragrance now gains a few small ornamental details and becomes a bit more accessible. If I were to assign colors to the different variants, the original would be deep night black. The EdT would be dark velvet blue. The Nu Heritage deep violet.

Now I had the chance to test the new version and I was not disappointed. Sprayed on both wrists, I could compare well. The first impression was tamer, not as intense, somewhat less animalistic. The old version is sharper, stricter at first. Bergamot with spicy cardamom made the beginning again. Jasmine (not listed here) plus orchid made an appearance; it became softer here, in contrast to the old version more lovable, but again connected with a slightly peppery, resinous note. In the base note, only frankincense is listed here. That cannot be correct. Earthy, musty vetiver and also musk, paired with sandalwood, make their way. Those who do not prefer it too animalistic will enjoy Nu Héritage; the floral notes blend into the base note, which is denied in the old version. I am excited about both variants and glad that no completely different reformulation came out. The turquoise one has been available in the Netherlands (among others) for some time; in Germany, it seems to not be on sale yet. I would like to thank Guusje once again very, very much for obtaining and sending me the bottle.

I love oriental-spicy fragrances with a distinct note of smoke. So I had to have "Nu". It fits perfectly into my taste... As soon as it arrived, I tested it immediately. The opening features intense bergamot and cardamom. However, the bergamot quickly retreats, and a beautiful, strong note of incense joins the delicious cardamom spice. Absolutely to my liking! Unfortunately, this pleasure lasts only a short time, as quickly and intensely as it appeared, the incense disappears again, and a magenta-colored, cool, unsweet orchid blooms. A barely perceptible note of smoke and cardamom remains, but after a short time, it ultimately becomes soft, gently powdery, and orchid-floral with a very "clean" note of incense; my color association of bluish-cool magenta-pink remains present even in the base. My bottle also lists patchouli as an ingredient... where exactly in the fragrance development is that supposed to be? I don't smell any of it, which is a real shame. After about four hours, the scent is no longer detectable on my skin. Even though I had applied it generously as a frequent and heavy sprayer. At first, I thought that years of intense use of oriental powerhouses had somehow destroyed my olfactory cells - but even my husband, who rarely uses perfume and is generally very sensitive to scents, detected absolutely nothing of "Nu" after those four hours when sniffing me. So it really is "naked". Now I also understand why the fragrance is named that way... Conclusion: Unfortunately, disappointing for me personally. I had expected more resin, wood, spice, warmth, and especially smokiness. And from an Eau de Parfum, I expect significantly more in terms of fragrance development, intensity, and longevity. Here, unfortunately, only lukewarm floral air instead of a strong scent! This is definitely not an autumn-winter fragrance for me, as it has far too little spice and warmth for my taste; it feels too cool and distant to me. I will probably wear it on warm spring and summer days and reapply every two hours... although I still don't know if I can even warm up to it; it just doesn't seem to fit me at all. I find "Nu" to be very floral; way too floral for me... The cardamom-incense note is great, which is why it gets 70%.

Nu starts off rather strong for me, I wonder if this pyramid is really complete, as I perceive something peppery instead of just bergamot and cardamom. However, this phase passes quickly, and cardamom becomes very prominent. I like cardamom, but here it is a bit too dominant for me, and I am waiting for the heart notes.

My husband says it reminds him of a `Bar-mitzvah` It makes him feel sorounded by kissing aunts :-) I LOVE it. After the initial medicinal blast it softens to a delicate Aoud ,smooth and creamy base that's magical and comforting. With an apealing mix of vanilla, rose, jasmine, cardamon, labdanum I love the rose in Montals perfume-Exquisite. I especialy adore it in Aoud queen roses-sublime

Old houses in the Deep South have a particular scent to them. They smell woody, but they also smell musty in a distinctive way as a result of the oppressive humidity especially during the summer months. They smell a bit like rotting wood, but also a bit like dust. The opening of Montale WHITE AOUD very well captures that scent. I am not sure what is creating this effect, but the light aoud note may be one contributing factor. The roses are perceptible as well initially, but they seem far away, like dried petals pressed within the crumbling pages of old books. The overall olfactory experience ends up reminding me of my grandmother, a bona fide Southern Belle. I realize that this makes it sound as though I am calling WHITE AOUD an "old lady perfume", but this particular instantiation of that idea is very different from what most people appear to mean by the expression. No aldehydes and no oak moss here. Nor does this smell anything like SHALIMAR or L'HEURE BLEUE, which some have remarked is the dominant scent of senescent women in retirement homes. As WHITE AOUD dries down, the "old house in the South" effect fades a bit, and the rose and patchouli come forth much more. I like some other rose-patchouli perfumes better than this one, but WHITE AOUD is nice for the trip down memory lane which it affords.

One of the best releases of Montale. Opens with a medicinal oud that remains for a while. The drydown is simply a wonderful blend of roses surrounded by vanilla with hints of saffron and patchouli. The oud settles down at this point. Unisex and sexy. Sillage, lasting power and projection are high. Updated January 2014

The color white in the title and on the bottle captures the character of the scent very well. This is a dusty white cloud of saffron, rose, and vanilla, like a delicate Indian pudding freeze-dried, pulverized and made aura. For once, the medicinal oud used by Montale doesn't bother me, and indeed I think the sweet, dessert-like properties of the fragrance need its antiseptic, 'hospital corridors' sting to provide lift and make it airborne. There is a cheap rosewater smell to the fragrance that I find moving and nostalgic, perhaps because it reminds me of the Roberts 'Acqua Distillata Alle Rose' rosewater facial toner I used in Italy. Due to the dusty dessert saffron, rose, and vanilla, there is a slight familial resemblance to Safran Troublant, one of my all-time favorite fragrances, and a definite point in its favor. I enjoy the sting of the medicinal oud and the way it takes the central rose-saffron-vanilla accord out of the straightforward gourmand category. But most of all, I find this sweet, milky oud pretty, easy to wear, and thoroughly enjoyable from top to end.

I swear: That’s it for me with Montale tests for a very long time. With "Aoud Night," there was actually a decent scent from this line recently (although I'm not entirely sure if wearing it more often wouldn’t lead to nasal fatigue or even numbness for me). The pattern with Montale is somehow always the same and simple: Almost everything that sounds oriental is mixed together, stirred, then a generous amount of rose oil is added, sometimes even gourmand elements are mixed in - and then a sillage is conceived that reaches even 10 meters against a North Sea wind. I am stunned - "White Aoud" confirms that the "Dark" variant was rather the half exception that proves the rule. A penetrating floral opening that somehow comes across as synthetic, hairspray-like. It could - once again - be due to a mediocre saffron that veils everything in a plastic-like manner. Be that as it may - an Arabic potpourri presses and pushes that urgently needs sorting and structuring. Cardamom, oud, various woods and spices - the jasmine and rose petals swirl around in it and press against the nasal walls. It’s sweetly woody, floral, waxy, annoyingly saffron-like (and that with endurance!), and this lasts for many hours, very penetrating, very voluminous. I have often had my issues with the often clumsy, loud, and blatant scents from Nasomatto, where the nose is often "matto," but Montale evidently does not fall short in this regard. I don’t want to write more about it.

'Boom!' it rushes in, Montale's White Aoud - with all the capriciousness of a top model or perhaps a freshly blonde oligarch's wife. Here it is - Oud and white flowers, all clear? - it's cool and sexy, loud and sweet, it's now and here!

My hope for a completely new fragrance experience has been fulfilled, thank you. I always think there must be more than my good old scents from the past and the "modern" little perfumes that I encounter every day in the store. There has to be more.......and how much more. I can't get enough, and Perle is right about the addictive factor.

Something is not right. What could it be? The room is decorated, the guests are here, the heating is off, which is good because the main character is dead. As much as I regret it, the liaison between the flowers and the sour wood strongly reminds me of a morgue. Certainly not a bad scent, but just inconsistent. (I also don't like goulash with chocolate sauce.

Am I getting a headache now? And if so, from what? From the leather spray I just used on my new shoes? Or from White Aoud? I am extremely prone to headaches, but they almost always come from the weather; I've never had a perfume intolerance. It will probably be the same this time. And yet: this is not going to work.

Thanks to Hermessenz for the sample!! Montale fragrances are always an experience if you like Oud. I tested White Aoud simultaneously with Aoud Leather, and I must say that I like White Aoud significantly better. Right after spraying, a beautiful hint of rose and jasmine greets you, okay maybe a bit feminine but not too much.

When I first brought the bottle to my nose, I immediately smelled jasmine, but then it faded into the floral notes. Spritzed on my hand, it began to smell like a gummy bear with cherry, then mimosa, geranium, and a little bit of bergamot and hawthorn came into play. A very unusual start. But to its credit, this beginning is very pleasant and rich. In the middle, rose, jasmine, lily of the valley and violet begin to open. Very pleasant middle, very floral atmosphere, as if you are in a flower garden. It is worth noting that both at the beginning and in the middle there is this gummy bear, and if at the beginning it was obvious, then in the middle it seemed to become a shadow, and was hiding behind the scenes of the whole movement. Well, at the end it starts to smell like cedar, sandalwood and musk. Then, after a while, moss comes in. A very pleasant combination, fresh, but even among it you can find some sweetness. I really liked it

Rose roses, minimal lipstick hint, light gray musk, even more flowers, musk, musk, musk. Not clean, not airy-powdery, but dense, with a slightly sexy undertone. Very perfumey, almost artificial. My boyfriend comes home and asks what smells so good. The sillage seems to be good. Unfortunately, it reminds me too much of the 80s.

Recently, one morning I stood somewhat indecisively in my bedroom and wondered what I should spray on today. Since there was nothing special planned for the day, I quickly decided to reach for “Paris” by Yves Saint Laurent, a fragrance that I wear very rarely because I find it beautiful but also a bit old-fashioned, and my colleague once mentioned that it gives her headaches. However, I knew that my colleague wouldn’t be there that day, so I thought I could give “Paris” another chance… Good decision: It’s so wonderful! I had completely forgotten how lovely it is. Maybe it’s also the season - it’s too floral in winter and too opulent in summer, and I probably unknowingly picked the absolutely perfect day for “Paris.” It’s always a bit of a thing. The fragrance and the outside temperature need to match; otherwise, it just doesn’t work. Some fragrances only work in winter, others only in summer heat, and some need proper dreary weather. But how does “Paris” smell now? It smells of flowers, mainly roses, but there are also other flowers like jasmine or iris. It smells as if you were sticking your nose into a gigantic bouquet of flowers. Not a measly little bunch, but a bouquet that costs at least €50, one that movie stars receive after a premiere, lavish and abundant. The flowers themselves are fully bloomed and radiate their enchanting scent in all directions. No delicate, still-dewy buds, but wide-open blossoms stretching towards the sun. You can smell their nectar, which attracts the bees, and you can also sense that they will soon wither. The flowers are basically at the peak of their beauty and simultaneously just before decay. At least, that’s how I perceive it. On my skin, the fragrance develops a velvety honey sweetness over time, which is easily noticeable and simply beautiful. Several people I interacted with that day came up to me and said something like: “It smells good in here. What is that?” That almost never happens. And at the gym, the men suddenly became unexpectedly charming: “Should I help you with the weights?” Or was it more about spring? Moreover, “Paris” was unusually long-lasting. I could still faintly perceive the scent even after showering. That’s how it should be. I will wear it more often now. I’m glad I rediscovered it…

As a young girl in the 80s, I received a mini perfume as a gift and used it up to the very last drop because it simply smelled fresh, floral, powdery, and unmistakable. Back then, I didn't have the financial means to buy the perfume myself; perfumes were an absolute luxury, and every woman who owned one was admired. Some time ago, I bought Paris and was full of anticipation, but it is no longer what it used to be. I only smell soap and something synthetic, whether it's from the bottle, on paper, or even worse... on me. I don't give up easily, and my hope was probably very high, but unfortunately, my opinion hasn't changed. Very sad.

I bought this because I was craving a pear perfume. I hardly detect pear in this. It is all clove, sandalwood, and musk to me. Together, these notes seem more fitting for a candle or incense, not a perfume on skin. Longevity is great; it sustained a 30-minute shower with a light pouf scrubbing.

While it does open in a big pear explosion, it's not fresh. It reminded me more of a "pears in wine" dessert (with too much emphasis on the "wine" part). Not the good kind of wine. Super sweet, sugary, yet very sharp and alcoholic. Once the pear dissipated a little, I was immediately hit with a suffocating sweet cloud of my childhood church's smell. Carnations. I don't know what made the church ladies back in the day think that overspraying a carnation-based perfume would help them seduce the priest, but I'm afraid I will have an antipathy to this flower forever now. I gave up and scrubbed it off after an hour of unpleasant memories and vague disgust, around the time when base notes started peeking through and transforming the composition into my grandmother's musty closet.

Pear is rarely found in the fragrance pyramid and even less often smelled in the perfumes themselves. It used to be occasionally used in women's fragrances, but even then only very peripherally. "Wild Pears" was on my testing list just for that reason. Here, the sweet fruit, which always stands in the shadow of the apple, both in reality and in olfactory life, must not only serve as a supporting role. "Wild Pears" is the must-test fragrance for pear fans. If there are any. But for my taste, there was more potential here. Or perhaps the pear, like the strawberry, is simply difficult to translate olfactorily in a stylish way. One prefers to eat them rather than smell like them. Who knows. But "Wild Pears" cannot be the ultimate in this area. It can't have been. I refuse to believe it. "Wild Pears" smells like Nivea - Limited Edition - Pear. This cream edition doesn’t actually exist, but it would probably smell something like this. "Wild Pears" is not a pure fruit scent, although an earthy-chemical, annoyingly slightly pungent pear is clearly the core of it all. Clove at the beginning and later lily of the valley make the fragrance appear very feminine, hand cream-like, and soft. Restless but unfortunately also for quite a while. If it didn’t sting and seem so unnatural, it would be great. As it is, it remains okay. Maybe it’s my skin, maybe it’s the fragrance. But in my opinion, one should be able to do more with pears. Even in a perfume. This one feels like a wild quick shot. Elegant is different. Bottle: enough has been said about the bottles, and there isn’t much more to say. Why don’t they write the fragrance on the samples/Mini-TZ?! Sillage: medium loud Longevity: Montale rarely disappoints - 7-9 hours Conclusion: a floral-synthetic pear cream that gets on my nerves quite quickly. This rarely used fragrance material deserves a finer scent. Even if "Wild Pears" is anything but bad.

... in Ribbeck in Havelland - a pear tree stood in his garden ... I had to think of this beautiful Fontane poem when I read the title Wild Pears. And I am enveloped by a complete pear tree with the first spray. But unfortunately, this is very synthetic and does not fit at all with the heartwarming poem. Unfortunately, no art - but artificial. Loriot fits better here: My sister - is called Polyester.... Even the lily of the valley seems to be made of wax - just like the entire scent appears to be waxy coated. I have experienced a pear much more authentically in other fragrances. The other ingredients disappear in the synthetic pear fog. Here, unfortunately, neither blessing nor the hand - of von Ribbeck in Ribbeck in Havelland is offered. I would rather wash my sprayed hand, because this Montale unpleasantly stings my nose and signals a headache.

At the beginning, everyone is still uptight. There’s a bite of warm pear cake with a wonderful vanilla aroma. As that is almost gone, pear soda is served, probably with a kick, because after a short time, naked pears are sitting in a wooden tub with a cream bath to party animalistically. However, not all night, just for 2-3 hours. Somehow nice to have a pear swinger party, I could really imagine that happening more often.

I was really curious about this scent, pear is one of the few fruits I like in perfumes. I had heard multiple times that it was just pear and super sweet. After spraying it on, I thought, no, absolutely pear compote like the canned pears from Rio Grande or something, it smells good but not like a perfume.

After the MDCI Pear, which was released this year and is really well done, here comes an intense pear fruit bomb from Montale, aromatic and fruity with a successful sweetness that is gently tempered by the base notes.

A fragrance that divides opinions. The family says it smells like cheap hand soap and they don't even notice the pear. For me, however, it has become a favorite. Zesty, fresh, and yes, a bit of synthetic pear at the beginning, but this synthetic note fades quickly. Then it becomes very warm, fruity, and cozy.

Partly, I understand why this fragrance hasn't been rated very highly: it is not a complex masterpiece of perfumery. But: this scent is magical and it does something magical to me. One spray of it instantly transports me to some childlike vacation.. This fruity freshness.. What is it? .. Did we spill this pear lemonade as kids? ..

I stumbled upon this fragrance by chance, and it immediately evoked vacation feelings for me. The scent reminds me of sunscreen due to the pear and bergamot. The pear remains constant throughout the scent's progression, but it loses intensity and becomes more floral, creamier, and finally woodier.

I use to own the edp version of Mon Paris and I really loved it, now I got my hands on the edt and I love it just as much. They are very similar, both are sweet, fruity, juicy and fresh and has that patchouli in them that makes them smell so good and last trough out the day. The edp is a bit stronger though, and the patchouli is heavier so I do think I prefer the edt, it's softer with more musk and sits like a veil around you.

While browsing in the perfumery, I tested one or another fragrance without a specific goal. For my birthday, I received a voucher and currently just can't decide which one I really want to add to my collection from my wish list. Maybe someone else knows this phenomenon, that as soon as you own a fragrance that you assumed would be truly wonderful, after wearing it a few times, the initial enthusiasm slowly fades. Fortunately, this doesn't happen with every purchase of mine, but it has happened to me about 2 or 3 times. Without any expectations, I sprayed Mon Paris edt out of curiosity for new releases and added a second fragrance to my other wrist. The first sniff was already very appetizing, but there were also other scents I had tested during this visit. Indecisively, I left the perfumery and strolled through the city to run some errands. And yes... you probably guessed it, you've all experienced it... I've read it many times here: What unfolded on my wrist within a few minutes was simply heavenly! The fragrance began to vibrate as if alive, and it felt like tiny glitter particles, colorful butterflies, and flower petals dipped in sweet berry juice were cascading from my wrist as I started to gently sway it back and forth. The scent has a romantic side; a bit cheesy perhaps, as these fruity raspberries and blackberries, combined with the thorn apple, create a distinctly pronounced sweetness that almost tickles the nose. It sparkles and hisses, pink, frothy and bubbly sweet with a citrus note. I find this fruit cocktail extraordinarily delightful. It's not a cotton candy sweetness like LVEB, but rather a berry-like slightly tart sweetness with wonderful aromas. There's a bit of princess and pink in this bottle. The flowers are a hit for me: Neroli, peonies, and jasmine all enjoy my admiration. With patchouli and white musk in the base, many of my favorite women's fragrances are equipped, and here too, all the notes fit together wonderfully. Perhaps it's the ambroxan that gives this fragrance its radiance and makes it feel so rich and full. All in all, a very appetizing, sweet, fruity women's fragrance that appears cheerful and playful, yet still has a subtly seductive side. I can easily imagine this scent on a first date when one is already in the mood for flirting and joking but doesn't want to reveal everything about oneself right away - especially not their dark sides. I am thrilled by the intensity of the scent, even though it is just an edt; a quality that I miss in many fragrances and is crucial in determining whether a purchase is worthwhile for me or not. I always find it quite difficult to assess the sillage without support, but I would say that it radiates well, as with movements of the wrist and swirling in the air, the fragrance becomes present again. It lasts on the wrist for up to 7 hours. What this fragrance does not offer, in my opinion, is offensive sensuality, pure seduction, a mysterious aura, or even a factual, clear elegance or coolness, as is often desired for an office scent. I perceive the fragrance as rather romantic, charming, cheerful, and perhaps a bit cheeky. The scent reminds me very much of Miss Dior Chérie. Back then, I was completely crazy about that fragrance and find it a shame that it was discontinued. I would also cautiously suggest a bit of similarity to Miss Dior Absolutely Blooming. I will have to test both in parallel again to assess that more accurately. I am also familiar with Mon Paris edp, but I find the edt to be better executed, as it is less one-dimensionally sweet. In any case, this fragrance remains on my radar and is in the running for my wish list.

Today would have been my little poodle Sami's birthday - and I want to bring him red roses. But before the arduous journey to the cemetery, I stop by the perfumery to prepare myself. I had already had good experiences with Mon Paris EdP - why not try the EdT? And it is just as vibrant and sweet as my little missing darling. It feels as if the little one is sending me a piece of colorful rainbow - and barking at me: Cheer up! The bergamot is fresh and cheerful - and blackberry - and raspberry are charmingly sweet. Elegance is added by jasmine and peony, and patchouli imparts a thoughtful touch. All of this reflects the character of my lovely little dog. Moreover, Mon Paris is "tres chique" - and fits the aura of my poodle. No wonder the French claim the origin of this beautiful breed for themselves. In any case, I am walking today under a protective rainbow.

The large windows in the living room and bedroom are wide open. From afar, you can already hear the thunder, still faint and hard to distinguish from a truck on the country road, but it’s Sunday. In a fit of clumsiness, I spray Mon Paris directly into my face. No joke, I narrowly save my eye from the big drop I didn’t expect. I can even say something about the taste of the perfume from Yves Saint Laurent… not recommended. It is bitter and fresh. It reminds me of summer days in bustling pedestrian zones of affluent cities, where many women take great pride in their appearance. That’s the scent you smell in the boutiques and cafés. Or at Douglas. When you walk in, it’s roughly this base scent that greets you. There’s something fruity, but that quickly fades away. In the meantime, one thunderstorm later, it bores me like all the new ones that call themselves something different yet smell the same. A bit warm, a bit sparkling wine, a bit pretentious, not exciting enough and not different at all. Too much citrus reminds me once again of various cleaners… I’m just as much a fan of Black Opium and its siblings. Slowly, YSL is becoming less and less appealing to me in terms of perfume. So I remain on the path of searching and am glad that this was just a short, harmless shower in the form of a free sample. Although a real impact would have brought some light into the darkness once again.

This fragrance instantly brought a smile to my face when I sprayed it! As berrylicious as fresh red currant from the garden, it transports you straight back to summer days of childhood. A few minutes later, the scent becomes elegantly floral, only lightly underscored by berries. Now you're truly in Paris, strolling along the Champs Élysées, très chic, yet relaxed and very feminine. This gentle berry-floral quality lingers for hours, neither sweet nor overpowering for me, just cheerful, pleasant, and relaxed. At no point does anything unpleasant stand out, as is the case with most other fragrances. Even after hours, I find myself smiling spontaneously when I catch a whiff, and I feel immediately at ease. I wear it daily; only for going out should it be something more enchanting.

Completely against my habit, I reached for the EDT here. And...I must say, not bad at all! Raspberry, wild strawberry, one could debate that. I'm definitely not a fan of sweet scents, so I'm glad that I don't have an overly sugary marshmallow strawberry or jelly raspberry from Haribo in the bottle. The scent is quite linear, berry, for me not synthetic meets patch.

This is not a bad scent, but still disappointing for a gourmand lover like me. I mean, look at the name, the bottle and the notes! I expected something heavenly sweet and intense, and maybe still a bit more sophisticated than some cotton candy drugstore spray. And I got... A harmless tropical floral with coconut milk and vanilla. It's not really a pink scent and doesn't smell like candy. It is sweet, but rather subtle for a Montale, and overall a bit undefined. The opening is slightly burned caramel popcorn, but I mostly get that on the blotter. On my skin it's gone super quick. Then the scent turns into a mix of frangipani, creamy coconut, bright vanilla and a touch of fresh citrus. I get no honey at all. It's a nice holiday scent. A beachy floral with a touch of fresh fruitiness and gourmand sweetness. It's not even super boring, just not that impressive. I'd surely wear this if it was the last perfume on earth, but I see no need to buy this when there are so many greater tropical scents on the market.

The fragrance is okay, but we've gotta talk about the chosen name and the color of the bottle. This would've probably been a better hit if it had been named "Tropical something" instead of Lucky Candy. I was expecting something sweet, gourmand, sugary and delicious like candy, instead I got a generic summer frangipani and coconut fragrance. It's not bad per se, but it smells like something I've already smelled in a designer fragrance somewhere. I only get frangipani and coconut. I've gotta give it to 'em, at least they used a different flower than the usual ylang-ylang-coconut pairing. It smells floral, tropical, slightly sweet, creamy and powdery. Where's the caramel, where's the honey? Nowhere to be smelled (at least to my nose). The fragrance should've been associated with a bottle sporting a soft yellow color instead of this bubblegum pink. It would've represented the fragrance better. Anyways, it dries down into a sweet vanilla fragrance with a hint of warmth and coconut ghost. It's a nice fragrance, but nothing very unique. If you're looking for a coconut perfume that uses a different flower for a tropical vibe, this could be a nice one. I'm not so much a fan of coconut which is why it won't be making it into my collection. On to the next!

Lucky Candy opens with a full-on throwback to the early 2000s. Think Britney Spears Curious on sugar steroids. It’s sweet, musky, and nuclear in that unmistakable mall-perfume-meets-body-spray kind of way. If you grew up around Bath & Body Works or celebrity scents, this will smell eerily familiar… maybe too familiar. The pyramid promises “coconut cream,” but if it’s in there, it’s buried under a pile of synthetic musk, florals, and generic sugary fluff. There's no real coconut here, just the ghost of a plastic tropical lotion memory that never quite materializes. What you get instead is a cloying sweetness that doesn’t evolve much, hovering somewhere between nostalgic and juvenile. It’s not offensive, but also not inspired.

Despite the mixed reviews, I decided to go for it when I discovered a leftover bottle filled with 25ml. So how does the new Montale smell? Upon spraying, a distinct popcorn note emerges, which is quite nice but not really exciting - neither super caramelized nor particularly burnt or sweet. Then it quickly becomes quite creamy and frangipani-heavy. The cream is lightly enhanced with unsweetened honey; coconut is not really noticeable to me. And that’s pretty much how it stays. After a few minutes, an undefinable, softly piercing note develops, which has been described in the comments as similar to “maggi herb.” The scent can still be sensed the next day, but the sillage and longevity are poor for Montale standards. The “cloud” loses intensity after several minutes and becomes close to the skin. In summary: Not for me! “Lucky Candy” wants (my interpretation!) to give a creamy Hawaii-South Sea-Spa vibe, which it simply fails to achieve. I find the piercing frangipani-honey cream rather unpleasant, and the popcorn opening does not fit the fragrance pyramid. Sillage and longevity are poor. If you are absolute frangipani or cream fans, then go for it ;) I will definitely be passing on this one!

I bought the fragrance blind based on the scent pyramid. Based on the name, I expected a cardboard sweet Montale (I love sweet and heavy scents). Admittedly, the name is a bit misleading. The scent has a light round sweetness for me, definitely not cardboard sweet or candy-like. I would even say it has a sensual sweetness. A bit mainstream (I detect a similarity to Lancome Miracle), but that's not a bad thing; on the contrary, I find everything here very rounded. It is by no means intrusive yet still present. Just right (for those who prefer something a bit casual). It can also be worn perfectly in everyday life or at the office. For me, it does not smell at all like toilet spray (how different tastes can be... haha). I can smell a light rose even though there isn't one in it, a beautiful rose. Light, not too sweet, and yet somehow sensual. Slightly powdery. That must be the frangipani. I like it a lot! After about half an hour, it becomes a bit powdery (very slightly, the floral notes clearly dominate here). And from that point on, I find the scent really beautiful. If you like floral, slightly powdery fragrances, this is just right for you. I am glad to have this in my collection I would categorize this scent as a feel-good fragrance. Sensual, lightly sweet. Feminine above all. I also always spray fragrances in my hair; for me, that's one of the best scent carriers. I have to keep smelling it again and again :-) If you like Lancome Miracle, you will like this one too. Best to test it yourself Sillage/Projection I would describe as good, not beast mode, but just right for everyday wear, a feel-good evening, or for work. Edit: The shirt I wore this morning while testing still smells strongly of the fragrance :-)

Completely different than expected is this fragrance that promises the full blast of sweetness and gourmand with everything it has (name, bottle, scent notes)! I think it’s absolutely great, it’s perfect for spring and summer, totally pleasant, lightly sweet and creamy, and has a clean quality.

I took the plunge and swapped for Lucky Candy blind. That says a lot for me, as I have never been a big fan of Montale fragrances until now. These scents have never wowed me; they always felt too sweet and somewhat synthetic. That changed today with the arrival of Lucky Candy. Without expecting much, I cautiously sprayed the fragrance.

It has a pungent fresh lift from the Carnation and Orange melded with a slightly dirty, dry and earthy sweet Patchouli that really punches through. It has a real creaminess as well from the Vanilla, Magnolia and the Jasmine that gives it an extra sweetness and a soft white floral heart. It feels quite masculine to me though with that tickle of golden resinous Myrrh. It is very strong and potent for an EDT. It is Daniela Andrier's work also. Edit 2023.. This is an absolute Masterpiece! The way the orange and bergamot cut through with the Patchouli with just a tickle of Carnation and Jasmine. Gives it the most gorgeously refreshing waft I think I've ever experienced in any perfume. And the Myrrh and Vanilla give it a real heavy duty density whilst still remaining fresh. It envelops you in the most perfect cloud of tart, creamy sweetness and it's fucking amazing and addictive!

It's not too sweet, giving it the balance that Goutal's Myrrhe Ardente lacks. I think it's lovely, and this is coming from a person who doesn't like a lot of vanilla scents. In overall mood and in this balance, Opium Fleur de Shanghai reminds me strongly of Tommi Sooni's Eau I, although the balancing is done in a different way.

I've always been a fan of the original Opium (1977) for its distinguishable, spicy scent. Despite the fact that I found it a little dated and cloying at times, I cannot see myself growing to love nor understand the now reformulated and re-packaged Opium, which is now only a shadow of what it once was, and a complete waste of space, in my opinion. Making the Opium flankers a permanent fixture on the market may have been a better move, because Opium Fleur de Shanghai certainly deserves more recognition. This flanker is a softer interpretation of Opium, with a touch more citrus in the opening and a smoother, vanillary drydown. The spices are still present in this composition, alongside a delicious, syrupy blend of amber and myrrh. I don't think I'd wear this during Summer, because let's be honest, Opium Fleur de Shanghai is still a rather heavy scent, but it could be applied on a nice sunny day. It's a somewhat demure oriental, with all the spicy qualities that you'd expect to find, just presented in a much softer and less offensive way. Opium Fleur de Shanghai is not as dark as its predecessor, instead it smells quite delicate and floral on the skin. My first introduction was an blend of subtle, spiced orange and bergamot, with a refreshing hint of jasmine. The heart takes some inspiration from the original Opium, with resinous, smoky and ambery accords, blended with rich carnation. Vanilla, both smooth and creamy, envelops the woods and spices in the drydown creating a cuddly oriental feel, nearly gourmand in nature. Although the sillage may not pack the same punch as the original, Opium Fleur de Shanghai is still relatively strong and should be worn in moderation. However, the scent does soften ever so slightly as the fragrance develops. The longevity is looking good so far, as I write this five hours after application. It's a shame that this was a limited edition, however I believe it's still relatively easy to find online.

First of all, I can't stand all these flankers that are currently flooding the market; there’s an "Eau legere" and "L’Eau" for everything and everyone, and I don’t know what else, it annoys me immensely, and therefore, after some bad experiences with the Shalimar Ode and Eaux, I’ve kept a wide berth from them. Now, I’m writing a comment again after quite a long time (including a perfume crisis:-)) and this... about a flanker! I only got the sample of Opium Fleur de Shanghai because of the beauty of the bottle, expecting a diluted imitation of the original. But this Opium is a fragrance of luxury class. I was never a fan of the original Opium; it was always too strong, too loud, too garish, too heavy, and overwhelmed me with its spices and sillage. With Fleur de Shanghai, all the familiar Opium spices appear right from the start and begin their dance. Accompanied by the wonderful fruitiness of mandarin, it’s a very special interplay. It strongly reminds me of the original scent, but only in wonderfully composed nuances that absolutely retain their individuality and are not mere imitations. An elegant dream fragrance envelops me, and I am, against my will, completely enchanted, sniffing again and again, thinking, was it really this scent, it can’t be? But the similarity to the original is undeniable. If this opening is already superb, then the transformation that this fragrance undergoes about 30 minutes after application is an absolute dream. It becomes creamy and infinitely soft, really soft, like luxury nougat, melting, but not sweet at all, while being so, so elegant. Imagine the original and lay a delicate blanket of cocoa butter over it. I could envelop myself in this phase and bathe in this scent. Like the finest and softest luxury blanket, it wraps around me and radiates such a luxurious aura that I feel like Cleopatra when I wear it, so special... There’s just one question left: WHY on earth is such a fragrance a limited edition that is only sold for one summer? Don’t they want to make money at YSL?

I wasn't sure what to expect, given all the polarising reviews (on all the other forums) that Montale gets, when I bought this one. A lot of the positive reviews were from people whose reviews I trust and understand. And based on that alone, pretty much like most times, I jumped on this one. And boy was I surprised! Straight to the point- this is an incredibly nice spicy-leather scent with a generous helping of saffron and ambergris. Very potent opening. Will easily offend people who are not into these types of perfumes. The initial citrus accord is very bitterish-spicy but very short lived so it's just fine. Black Pepper and Saffron are the two notes that dominate the life of this scent, in incredible depth. It doesn't smell exactly the same all the way. Different shades emerge as time goes by. The cardamom, something I'm not usually fond of, brings great depth here to the other spices ( I get traces of cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf) and the saffron accord. The leather here is very soft and smooth. Very polished and subtle (atleast on my skin). There's also a boozy vibe to the whole thing that, together with saffron, pepper, & leather kinda reminds me of Bentley Intense. (It is quite similar in terms of the overall vibe.) And beneath all this is, what, to me, feels like, really good quality Ambergris. It's salty, slightly sweet, with some ambery-floral nuances. And finally, the Oud. It's extremely subtle here. Not at all the dominant note. Just something like a catalyst of sorts, added to bring out certain facets in the other elements. It's there - slightly medicinal and dark - but more like a filter added in post-production. It just adds a certain vibe to the main theme. Projection, sillage, and longevity are all on the higher side. All in all, beautiful. An incredibly nice spicy-leather scent with great depth and a classy vibe. 8.5/10

OK I'm not claiming to be an expert on anything but I do have an extensive collection of leather fragrances. TF Ombre Leather 2018 is just like this. The 2016 version is no way close and far superior but it's interesting to see that this was released almost a decade earlier. Its a good price. Leather is smooth and the base supports it well. It's not a massive projector and the 2021 version has moderate performance. Just interesting to find another fragrance that is so comparable to others.

The Aoud Leather from 2009 is the second leather fragrance in Montale's Oud line, alongside Oud Cuir d’Arabie. It is considerably more subtle than its older brother. While Oud Cuir d’Arabie features a clean, radiant leather (like a new leather jacket), the leather in Aoud Leather is more of the musty variety - more like worn, ancient suede. With this, Montale now represents the opposite side of the spectrum of leather notes. There is not much Oud to be sensed either. Unlike in Oud Cuir d’Arabie, it has been used very subtly here. Without knowledge of the pyramid and the name, one would not necessarily recognize it. Spices are also present, blending into the subtle picture. An inappropriate lemon freshness at the top annoys me a bit; but perhaps it is important to keep the leather from coming off as too rotten. A bit of amber rounds things off and adds a very subtle warming note. Additionally, the perfume is slightly sweet, which I personally do not like and raises questions. I can well imagine that Oud Cuir d’Arabie was too pronounced and too extreme for many customers. Thus, a "Light" variant was needed. In this sense, Aoud Leather is indeed a successful perfume, embodying the understated note. I would not generally speak of elegance in a suede fragrance, but that is a matter of perspective. Those who find Oud Cuir d’Arabie too exaggerated may enjoy Aoud Leather. Definitely suitable for fans of lighter suede fragrances.

After the shock of testing Black Aoud, I dared to try a Montale fragrance again, and from the very first second, I thought, wow, this is Tom Ford's Tuscan Leather, perhaps not quite as brutally smoky, but the opening and the further development are so similar that I have to call this a fragrance twin. The longevity may not be quite as high as TF Tuscan Leather, which often blooms again after a shower, but the price is also not that far above the pain threshold like with Tuscan Leather. The fact that it comes across a bit softer than TFTL is not so bad; not everyone needs the black knight's glove full on their olfactory organ. Compared to TFTL, it's almost a bargain price-wise, and I find the leather theme perfectly implemented and wonder about the rather modest rating so far. There is still room for improvement. By far not as overdone and artificial as Black Aoud. I was already afraid that Montale only offers those oriental chemical sledgehammers. Tom Ford's Tuscan Leather is still a bit better, but Aoud Leather is very close. So test it and see for yourself.

Thanks to Hermessenz for the sample! Recently, I have tested a lot from Montal, they all somehow smell similar in structure, they use different ingredients but the structure is always the same, so I already knew quite well what to expect when I sprayed the fragrance. The scent starts with pepper, saffron, and a lot of bergamot, slightly fresh but overall a bit more spicy; unfortunately, this note gives me the impression that it only exists to pave the way for the Oud that follows. Bam, as soon as you think that thought, the Oud comes out, mixed with cardamom and some indefinable spices, the spicy note from the top note becomes significantly stronger. After about 1 hour, the base comes out, which, alongside the leather promised in the name, is unfortunately only present in very small amounts on my skin, and the amber emerges, which adds a smoky direction to the fragrance in addition to its spicy note. Unfortunately, I have to say that I find the scent progression on my skin weak and boring; moreover, the perfume itches slightly and my hand turns a bit red. The longevity is unfortunately not great either; I would estimate it at 3-4 hours. So in the end, I can only give a rating of 60%, but you should test it; however, I would recommend spending your money on other Montal fragrances.

Montale's leather fragrances are in a class of their own. While I love Leather Patchouli above all, I do not like Curie d'Arabie. Aoud Leather is somewhat in between. a light, good leather jacket note that I find elegant. Therefore, the scent suits fashionable leather jackets. Not an oud leather scent. A bit wild, a bit daring, a bit fresh.

The fragrance starts off very fresh. Of course, you immediately smell the leather note and you know right away where the journey is headed. Very similar to Tuscan Leather, however, the leather is lighter and less overpowering, making it much more pleasant to wear.

At the first sight this perfume seems meant for "dark souls": the black glittered bottle promises a strong and heavy scent. Not at all. This fragrance is quite gentle and the touch of "darkness" is given only by the coffee note,fragrant and very noticeable, which hits immediately your nose at the first smell. But after the fresher fruity-flowery notes arrive giving a gentler character to this scent: mainly the pear, less the orange blossom, very light and not so vibrant (at least on my skin) .The cedarwood and patchouli base is only suggested and this is a problem for the longevity and the sillage of this scent. On my skin I don't perceive them! So, this scent could be compared to a girl in black with a very sweet and romantic heart. The darkness is only appearance, but there is many freshness inside. In comparison to the quite weak sillage, the price is high. Forget the classic Opium, people. this one is another story!

Hello and good evening, you sniffers :D Welcome to my comment on Yves Saint Laurent’s newer fragrance “Black Opium.” Yes, I know, the scent is actually not new at all, as Black Opium has been around for several years now (since 2014, if I’m not mistaken? And the original Opium came out in the 70s!), but since well-known fragrances are often re-released time and again, there’s once again a new version of the Eau de Toilette of this scent, namely the 2018 edition. If you’re lucky, there’s basically little change, so you either don’t notice the differences at all or they aren’t too bothersome. Sometimes, however, a new version can ruin the scent for some perfumes (or parfumos), leaving you heartbroken as you search for the original fragrance to enjoy it for a while longer and to store some in your scent treasure chest before they become unavailable. I think some of you have had such experiences with various fragrances already. In any case, I don’t know any EDT of Black Opium, only the EDP from 2014 and Nuit Blanche. So I’ll jump straight to the scent description and can’t really write a comparison comment, but hopefully that’s okay… The scent: At the beginning, I smell a bit of blackcurrant and some coffee, which I actually find quite nice, albeit unspectacular.
