A little lemon adds a touch of freshness, but that quickly fades away. Then the pear appears, adding another fruity note. However, the fruity notes soon lose their strength and quickly blend with other scent notes, making it a bit difficult to distinguish or filter these notes. You can still smell the coffee, along with now sweet notes (I assume these come from the jasmine, even if it’s not specified here), which come across pleasantly, even if they have the well-known “mainstream synthetic” quality of large and very popular mainstream fragrances. A little later, you can also distinctly smell neroli, which fits well with the sweet scents. The coffee is still somewhat present and smells especially nice with the cedarwood, while the sweetness is complemented by musk and patchouli adds its earthy note. Even though patchouli is only present in small amounts, I could have done without it here. In the end, the scent still smells of orange blossoms, light coffee, and sweet notes like musk. Then it becomes a bit more humid, as it suddenly gains intensity and somehow smells floral-sweet-humid, which lasts for about 1-2 hours, after which the scent suddenly fades away and comes to an end. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is good; you’ll be noticeable with the scent for a while without other sniffers having to get too close! The longevity is about seven to eight hours. The bottle: The bottle is rectangular when viewed from the front but has an oval base. It is reddish-pink and has a glitter effect. In the middle, you can see the famous “porthole,” as known from some YSL fragrances. The black cap is cylindrical at the bottom, where the brand name is visible, and ends in a hemisphere at the top. A very beautiful bottle, although I preferred the black version. So, first of all: The scent is not as bad as most have rated it here, but of course, that’s a matter of taste. I can well imagine that most people might not really connect with this scent, as the synthetic note might bother them, which isn’t terrible, but is quite noticeable here. Moreover, the scent has a bit of an aura like those types of fragrances that are mainly preferred by 16 to 18-year-old teens who are starting to use fragrances more, as at this age, boys are no longer “yuck” but appear more interesting (or other girls, depending). The girls themselves seem to be becoming physically more mature (hm, I hope that doesn’t sound wrong...), but mentally they still remain a bit brainless (the boys too,... and I must mention that boys are even dumber and stay that way longer than girls...) and become primarily one thing they can never shake off: catty! You can see that here with you ladies... uh... isn’t that so? Mu ha ha ha :DD In any case, the scent seems like a going-out fragrance, but those girls probably use such a scent at any time, which is okay, but unfortunately, these girls often have no idea about dosage, so you can smell them, for example, from the other end of the subway :D But as I said, boys do the same, I’ve seen that often enough in the men’s fragrance department (yes damn it, I don’t ONLY test women’s fragrances, argh!!!). In my opinion, a test isn’t really worth it now, but you can still take a look if you’re interested. Because I really don’t find the scent that bad, but there are many, many, really a whole lot of more interesting and also prettier fragrances, even among the regular mainstream ones. While this one smells about as good to me as the EDP from 2014, I find Nuit Blanche much more successful and would recommend that one more. Well, that was my opinion on the scent. I wish everyone a nice evening and see you soon :)

Why is that? Why do major brand leaders have to endlessly flank and reinterpret classic fragrances? It truly puzzles me. Bestsellers are made universally appealing down to the smallest detail, so that in a few years, every household has acquired this scent. Of course, one doesn’t need to reinvent the wheel, but more independence and courage to explore new, unknown fragrances that are extravagant and spectacular - that would be something! As you can tell from my reading, I am definitely not a fan of thousands of flankers. Especially since the resemblance between the fragrances is undeniable due to the entire presentation and advertising of the scents. Live and let live, they say. So, my expectations were not high, and then during the first sniff, I was surprised by what my nose detected. The fragrance starts with fruity pear and slightly citrus notes. Very pleasant and different. Nice, I think to myself, and keep sniffing my wrist. Then a light, very mild coffee note spreads. It is by no means as dominant as in the Eau de Parfum. Surprisingly, I can also detect the orange blossom, subtle and fine, not too much and not too loud. So far, I really like the scent. Now patchouli and cedarwood join in. This gives the fragrance a slight depth, and the woody heart of the scent begins. I really like the progression of the fragrance. To my surprise, I really enjoy this scent. It is different, so contrasting, and yet so complementary to each other. Citrus and coffee? Sounds like a pick-me-up, like a wicked night. I find this combination very interesting. Admittedly, the regular Eau de Parfum has always been too loud, too dominant, and too smoky for me. Here, I have found a really nice alternative. I can imagine this scent on a lovely girls' night out, in a cocktail bar, and during other leisure activities. I can also envision it on a beautiful summer evening. I believe one should simply try the fragrance. For some, the composition of lemon and coffee may seem bizarre, but it is definitely worth giving the scent a chance.

Who wants to smell like chocolate cake? Sometimes you eat so many sugary desserts that even thinking about dessert makes you nauseous. This scent makes me feel like I'm in a sugar coma. Although it has no chocolate or cocoa in it, it smells like chocolate cake and hazelnut chocolate wafer. Maybe if I was 10 years old it would interest me, but I worry about going into a diabetic coma. Stays on fabric for over 8 hours. The rate of spread decreases after 4 hours. If you leave a room, your scent will still be felt in the room. Projection: 9/10 Sillage: 9/10 Longevity: 8/10 Fragrance Quality: 2/10

Not long ago, I thought Montale would be unbearable for me. I had long since weaned myself off vanilla. Dark, warm woods are my personal horror. Ylang-Ylang triggers my flight instinct. “Vanilla Extasy” is bursting with Montalinade, is predictably very vanilla, but also dark-woody (with a slightly malty tobacco note) and on top of that has the typical scratchiness of Ylang-Ylang. And yet, my nose does a little dance of joy when I spray “Vanilla Extasy” on myself. I see bright sunbeams on a rosewood-colored cashmere sweater, I see skin, I see softness. No sign of a flight reflex. It goes without saying that I have to wonder. Is “Vanilla Extasy” so pleasant for noses like mine that prefer warm scents because creamy light benzoin resin is part of the mix? Because amber here particularly skillfully imitates the scent of warm skin? Quite possible. However, I suspect something quite, quite dreadful behind my enthusiasm: dreadful at least for the lovers of the fragrance. I think it is primarily the delicious, slightly floral-synthetic hairspray note that makes me so euphoric here. Not three-weather hairspray, but rather a hint of salon-quality hairspray cloud. A downright philistine reason for my enthusiasm, I admit. And now light your torches and chase me out of the scent village. But I hope that one or another fan of cosmetic fragrances (a fellow philistine, that is) quickly comes around with a veto.

After reading numerous reviews, I eventually decided to acquire this rather controversially discussed fragrance in the form of a sample. As a vanilla advocate, I approached this scent with a lot of skepticism. On one hand, fragrance notes that I personally favor - on the other hand, those bad reviews that almost deterred me from purchasing it. In this case, I came to the realization that one should ultimately rely on their own nose :). The first spray: OK wow! I am enveloped by this indescribable mix of apricot and vanilla. Don’t get me wrong, it’s not that sticky synthetic air freshener apricot. No, it feels almost refreshing, light. I would even say it’s the early-ripening apricot that takes away that cloying sweetness. Over time, the vanilla increasingly dominates, but it doesn’t impose itself; rather, it takes on the role of the “shy” one. Perhaps this is also the crux of the matter, which is why the longevity (in contrast to the other Montales) is rather low. In my opinion, this perfume is suitable for both warm and cold days. The sillage seems to be good, as I received a compliment for the second time already. Well, the bottle color looks dull, boring, and unremarkable. It definitely does not reflect the interesting content inside. By the way, a colorful (orange) accent would certainly attract more attention. Because this scent truly deserves it. Ultimately, I believe, and this is my personal opinion, that Vanilla Extasy should not hide behind the other Montale fragrances.

Suddenly it has become cold. After it was over 25°C just two days ago, the temperature has plummeted to 10°C. So it's time to light the fireplace, put on the thick winter slippers, and indulge in warm, cozy scents. On my left hand, I am wearing Chocolate Greedy - and it does exactly what I expect. On my right hand, I have applied Vanilla Extasy and - I am surprised! VE starts off with vanilla right from the beginning, but even stronger is a ripe, juicy, honey-coated apricot that emerges. The fruit is carried by the vanilla, which overall smells less sweet than the fruit. As the fruity aspect fades, a white floral note slowly joins in, still accompanied by the vanilla. This vanilla remains rather dry and not sweet throughout, giving the fragrance a refined and mature character. The base, finally, is vanilla in a warm woody tone, though this is very subtle. Only here does the vanilla take center stage. I would classify VE less as a gourmand fragrance and more as a "vanilla-ized" white floral composition. I believe the wearer should not be too young, as this scent has nothing playful about it. However, a more mature lady would lack the innocence that gives this fragrance a delicate touch of eroticism. But on the right wearer ..

Vanille Extasy is warm, soft, fine, slightly sweet on me, not overwhelming at all. And I smell flowers and apricot fruits. The vanilla carries the scent with a delicate, lasting presence. Not a gourmand, but floral in expression with a hint of fruitiness and delicate natural vanilla.

The whole world, the whole life is an extensive system of unconscious forces that act through our individual consciousness. Just as one can create a liquid from two gases using electric current, one can also form a higher consciousness from two types of consciousness - that of our concrete and that of our abstract being - through life and the world.
Tested briefly on the arm, very sweet, reminds me of Vanilla Fields by Coty For vanilla lovers, it might be a must, but vanilla can be bought cheaper. And if it's just a room fragrance....))))

Every nose is different - according to the description, I was expecting a sweet gourmand scent. But for me, it is very woody and then develops into sweetness after a few minutes. The vanilla rounds it off beautifully.

This is the only "sport" fragrance that I own, and like Dior Homme Sport this is not a typical aquatic sport fragrance, in fact it is very well made and really worth the money. It's just a shame that it's discontinued. It has a couple of unusual notes for a so-called "sport" fragrance. Jasmine and cyclamen. I think I really like the tangy mandarin, bergamot and citron that slowly turn to jasmine and cyclamen with a hint of cedar. It's really nice... and in my opinion, not a sport fragrance. It can be worn at any time as an Eau de Cologne. The bottle design is very nice, clear glass as opposed to the matt white surface of the original. I really like it. It's just a real shame it's discontinued. I have no problem using this one for work or for playing tennis or something. It feels more classy that a simple "gym" fragrance, and it is in no way synthetic. A really good one, and different from a "typical" sport flanker.

I couldn't have imagined in spring 2003 - when Kouros Cologne Sport (KCS) was launched - that my life would become so "Greekified" for the next five years. A very good friend decided a few months earlier to emigrate to Crete forever. Through her and other friends, he stood before me half a year prior. The Greek, who spoke fluent German, had studied classical archaeology in Thessaloniki and loved the German films of Fassbinder. He had been her Greek teacher and still says today: "She was my best student so far." I have always had a love for Mediterranean countries and the lifestyle, the laisser-faire that we Germans often lack. My parents took me somewhere there every summer, and in my larger family, celebrations were always lively...without alcohol: "no chance." In this respect, I was somewhat prepared, especially since my family always went to our regular Greek restaurant for meals. A few months later, we visited them in their house near Chania, a converted olive oil mill, on a hill right by the church. The terraced garden was 1000 square meters and offered a fantastic view of the sea over grapes, figs, pomegranates, quinces, and lemons...it was unbelievably beautiful. The interior of the house was also brilliant; the actual owners had been architects. The lagoon-blue tiles of the kitchen wall were also embedded in the dining table. A staircase led to the sleeping area, which hovered above the kitchen. Their cat Apollo (the name was obvious) immediately annexed me, and I had to leave my T-shirt there after departing so he could continue to smell me. Since that summer, it was clear to me: "No summer without Kouros Cologne Sport." Two years after Tom Ford became creative director at YSL, KCS was launched. Kouros Fraîcheur was discontinued, and at the same time, the packaging and care line of the classic Kouros were renovated. The classic Kouros had always been too heavy for me until then. I cannot relate to the comments discussed here in the forum about urine, etc. KCS was completely different. All animalistic ingredients were banned here. There was no need to be afraid of it. It starts with a fresh cocktail of various citrus fruits (bergamot, lemon, tangerine), which is immediately accompanied by a hint of jasmine and violet flowers. The entire scent progression is not very complex and passes quickly, but the longevity and sillage are excellent for a Cologne. In these fresh notes, a hint of warmth from musk and amber mixes, giving the fragrance a bit of the aura of sun-warmed skin. In the base, a large amount of cedarwood becomes noticeable quite quickly. In one description, I read that it is supposed to be an iced cedarwood accord accompanied by menthol. I can confirm this because shortly after spraying it on my skin, a kind of "camphor and menthol effect" develops, as if one had used rubbing alcohol. A hint of "hot-cold" medicine for relaxation after sports...I thought the idea was good. It must be the type and amount of ingredients used because KCS still reminds one of Kouros. With the nickname Sport, Tom Ford once again proved to be a visionary...the current sports trend was still far off. The oud wave also learned to fly when Tom Ford incorporated oud into M7 back in 2002. Of the many Kouros flankers that had appeared over the years, it remains the best. How many bottles of it have I emptied over the years, not counting the summer versions. However, I have always used the fragrance only in summer; the character of the scent doesn't really fit into other seasons. For me, all summer versions up to 2006 are very usable; after that, the quality declined rapidly...since 2007, L'Oréal has been the owner of the YSL cosmetics division. Ozone was incorporated into the fragrance formulas, which I do not like at all. The version from 2008 is still okay, but the last two from 2010 and 2011 I find terrible, especially since Kouros is no longer recognizable in any way. My years with the Greek passed by; we lived together. We traveled to friends in Athens and stayed privately. We came from Athens to Piraeus by ferry to my friend in Crete and drove with her car to the beach of Falassarna, brilliant. His parents sent us freshly roasted beef from the village by plane with a friend...already sliced for freezing. I will never forget how she stood at the airport with that 3 kg plastic bucket in the shape of honeycomb full of honey, wonderful...and how did she get through security with that? I attended a Greek wedding (Germans, become Orthodox; it's much more fun), celebrated Greek Easter with the classic red eggs, and received plenty of help in Greek music: Anna Vissi, Elli Kokkinou, Haris Alexiou, and of course the handsome Sakis Rouvas (but he makes terrible music), etc. The films of Angelopoulos are also excellent if you enjoy three-hour epics. I already knew ouzo from my grandma, who always had a bottle in the fridge. The Greek cuisine is different from what is usually presented to us here in Germany in most restaurants...and only the Greeks make the real café frappé. In Kopanisti, a sheep cheese cream, I could dive into...during that time, I also gained a few kilos..."ligo krasi parakalo!" Just as my time with the Greek came to an end, so did the production of KCS. Even my friend who emigrated is back in Germany. I learned about the discontinuation of production in 2011. However, my stock and the production code there suggest to me that the last bottles were filled in 2009, a year after our separation. So far, I have not found any produced bottles after that...but I am not looking further. With the annual summer flankers, they created their own competition; there were summer versions of KCS in 2003 and 2004 as well. Besides the Cologne in 100 ml size (briefly also in 50 ml), there was a shower gel, a deodorant stick, and a facial care product (Soin Express Visage). That was several years ago now, and I look back on it fondly; I like that way of life anyway. My consumption of KCS has also significantly decreased; over time, one discovers other fragrances, evolves, and falls in love anew...exactly. Here's to that, a ouzo.

While Chanel and Dior launched classics of the late 80s and early 90s with Égoïste (1990) and Fahrenheit (1988) respectively, YSL presented a wide-ranging spectrum during the same period: Jazz (1988), Jazz Prestige (1993), Rive Gauche pour Homme (2003), Opium pour Homme (1995), Body Kouros (2000), and M7 (2002) mark an incredibly productive phase in YSL's fragrance division. Kouros Cologne Sport (2003) was released simultaneously with an initial edition of Kouros Eau d’Été (2002) - almost like a precursor to the 'Peak Time' of flanker chaos. However, it stands out distinctly in design: the bottle of Cologne Sport is so elegant and minimalist that it could just as easily be a sketch by Adolf Loos or Josef Hoffmann with their glassworks - or today, an architectural model by Junya Ishigami or SANAA. I can't think of any other bottles from this time that created such lightness with silver and, above all, a lot of transparency. This theme continues in the scent: Kouros Cologne Sport achieves what only perfume can do so well - heaviness is made light, solidity becomes permeable, and a whole range of qualities that already characterize Kouros (1981) are simply turned upside down. Kouros aficionados might consider this pure heresy: such an idiosyncratic alpha scent tolerates no latecomers - and if so, then only the Eau Fraîcheur (1993). I see it more relaxed. Cologne Sport contains a light, almost homeopathic pinch of Kouros essence, which remains clearly recognizable as Kouros even in this lightweight version. Francis Kurkdjian managed to create enough distance from the original with a fascinating aldehyde-musk hairspray accord [similar to Helmut Lang's first Cologne (2000)] so that Cologne Sport develops a distinctly own voice. Unfortunately, the scent was soon discontinued in favor of the summer editions - the first of these Kouros Eau d’Été's were still very close, indeed almost identical to Cologne Sport, but the special lightness was reserved solely for the grand packaging of Kouros Cologne Sport (2003).

My little Kouros Cologne Sport sample surprised me today in multiple ways, so much so that I hope it is indeed this one and there was no mislabeling... but I think that's rather unlikely with the professional who kindly left me several Kouros samples some time ago. 1) Normally, I would have thought I could roughly guess what a Kurkdjian or Ellena is by now... but I would never have associated this cheerful-sunny Kouros version with Kurkdjian. Which brings us to 2): for me, Kouros Sport is quite close to the animalistic, somewhat challenging original... or at least closer than a few previous reviewers have assessed it. My sample still definitely smells like Kouros - sure, brighter, more citrusy, cleaner - but completely without animalistic instincts, Cologne Sport is not. Which is good, because otherwise, it could have been given a different name. Still, these different impressions leave me contemplative, although this is actually nothing extraordinary in terms of perfume. The simultaneously tested Kouros Tattoo/Tonique 2007 has, however, moved much further away from the original, appearing more modern and normal - but more on that in the respective comment. Kouros Cologne Sport starts for me with a beautifully Greek-stony citrus mélange. Imagine white marble stones in the sun, on which oranges, lemons & co. are evenly squeezed. Still Greek, masculine, Kouros, but without a strong urine note. That's right, it's hardly there anymore. But Kouros, full of stones, sun, and also sweat, is still very much present. The way Mr. Kurkdjian skillfully and cleanly navigates away from the original is impressive and shows an unusual facet in his perfumery art. This bright-dry sun aspect could well come from the cyclamen, but the rest of the second half of the fragrance pyramid is not directly discernible. Bottle: smooth, transparent, aerodynamic - fits well with sports & I actually like all Kouros bottles. Sillage: doesn’t harm anyone lifting weights Longevity: after 6-7 hours including sports, there's still a hint left Conclusion: it's a pity that this original-close, contour-rich Kouros Light was swapped for interchangeable summer flankers... a Kouros Sport would have sufficed & pleased here!

The theme of "Sport" in men's fragrances has surely reached its absolute peak this year! By now, every designer brand has a "Dynamic" variant in their lineup! Launching a sporty version of well-known and successful classics is bold, as the original usually sets the bar very high! The risk of tarnishing the name is significant! Additionally, there is the expectation and hope that the big brother (or sister) has not been "diluted". With Kourous Cologne Sport, this attitude can be thrown overboard, as it smells completely different from the classic from 1981. Aside from the Kourous summer flankers, which have been around since 2002 to my knowledge, a first variant was already released in 1986. "Kourous Eau De Sport" smelled, according to a Basenotes entry, somewhat sweeter, rounder, and softer than the original - simply less synthetic. No chemical vibes whatsoever - yes, the original would have even been rated inferior by this comparison! I cannot specify the exact lifespan of Eau De Sport, but by 1993 it was replaced by a new "fresh" variant, the "Kouros Fraîcheur". However, this one was again very close to the original. "Rivegauche" told me that there was nothing sporty fresh to smell...1993 indeed! ;) Ten long years later, the Fraîcheur was replaced by an even more modern, fresh flanker version. "Eau De Cologne Sport" presents itself in a crystal-clear and modernly shaped bottle. It is a modern interpretation of the original design and appears almost futuristic. The advertising campaign showcased the bottle against a white background, surrounded by "bubbling," rising water bubbles. Unlike the original, I could connect with this interpretation of Kourous - I even love it and it accompanies me during the summer. It was even my signature scent on my vacation in Italy last year. The opening of the fragrance is zesty, with the citrus notes coming across quite penetratingly, similar to the original. The further development feels sour, spicy - almost medicinal. When sniffing, I detect similarities to Paco Rabanne's "Pour Homme". Maybe that's a bit far-fetched?! The drydown unfolds with a floral freshness and velvety feel thanks to the alpine violet. The base is characterized by a sour/sweet amber. Although the fragrance is presented as Eau De Cologne - the longevity has Eau De Toilette quality and lasts a good 6 hours! A year after the fragrance was launched, a summer flanker with the complicated name "Kourous Cologne Sport Eau d´Ete Summer Fragrance" was released. In summary, a truly interesting composition that stands out in the current sport fragrance craze! Unfortunately, the Eau De Cologne Sport version was discontinued last autumn. However, it can still be found with various foreign suppliers on the "bay" and currently at quite reasonable prices.

No, really, I must strongly agree with Leimbacher's comment under mine and clearly disagree with the majority of the other predecessors. The "Cologne Sport" is by no means a completely different, new fragrance compared to the original from 1981.

Let the civets mark their territories in the wild - Kouros benefits from the absence of their urine. The white giant has undergone a cleansing, no longer promoting the cult of man with sweaty armpits.

Is this supposed to be a fresher interpretation of the original scent? Not at all! In my opinion, this is a completely different fragrance. Nothing reminds me of the original (thank goodness!). Kouros Cologne Sport is a truly fresh, light sporty scent. I wouldn't want the original for any amount of money, this one is a really pleasant fragrance!

Beautiful light and summery variant of Kouros, although some notes of the original are simply missing. Those who find the original Kouros scent too extreme might like this one. Much more subtle, it also works well as an office fragrance.

I have bought this perfume blind. I Hope find here a really intense cherry, something like Lost cherry by Tom Ford, but with the montale's performance. However the cherry here is very subtle. What i get the most is a very nice vanilla-musk-rose fragance, very close to intense café but changing the subtle coffee on that one for the subtle cherry here. The performance as the montale It is is good. Very good longevity and moderate sillage. Regarding the unisex tag i am a man i am perfectly able to wear It. It is true that the opening is a bit more feminine but the dry down is basically vanilla. Just un case i would recommend to try before buying because if you are a Man Who Live very masculine fragances (with leather, oatchouli, Woods, Green notes...) Probably you would find this one a bit too sweet and floral for you. Scent: 7.5 Longevity: 8 Sillage: 6 Quality/price: 5 Versatility: 9 Originality: 6 Global: 7

I’m not really a passionate fruit eater, but cherries are an exception. They have to be juicy sweet cherries. So I planted the dwarf cherry Lapins in my garden. I’m not tall, and I wanted to comfortably harvest the fruits without a ladder. And the little tree has obediently stuck to the guideline and has not exceeded 1.80 m so far. Moreover, it bears plenty of sweet aromatic cherries. Unfortunately, the harvest season is over now - but Intense Cherry brings them back to me. The woody start symbolizes the entire little tree, next to which the rose "Roter Stern" blooms abundantly. In addition, jasmine subtly mixes in, intertwined with delicate vanilla. As a crowning touch, the plump cherry melts on the tongue, with its round sweet flavor. A feast for the senses - just like my garden corner. Montale provides me with fruity gourmand delights - with a touch of elegance. I can hardly wait for Lapins to bloom again and satisfy my cherry cravings.

I generally don't warm up to Montale. This scent is quite nice. Cherry blossom that comes across as if you had just showered with a cherry blossom shower gel. It strongly reminds me of "Rituals-Sakura," just a bit more upscale. The perfume is not heavy or opulent, suitable for everyday use or as an office scent. Not intrusive, pleasant. If you don't find a good deal, I find Montale quite pricey for what you get. The bottle is certainly a matter of taste, but the price-performance ratio is, in my opinion, rather mediocre. The scent is quite nice, but for me personally, it's not a candidate for purchase. Anyone who likes cherry blossom fragrance should feel well accommodated with this perfume.

in perfumes was new to me until I received a sample of Intense Cherry . At first, I was a bit skeptical, as I am more of a peach fan. But this fragrance convinced me. The cherry is clearly in the foreground, while other notes serve only to round it off. This creates a fruity-floral scent that brings joy. Longevity and sillage are good for me; this perfume is not a powerhouse. But anyone willing to spend some money on a good cherry scent won't go wrong here.

The name of the perfume "Intense Cherry" sounded very promising. I have tried quite a few Montale fragrances, and unfortunately, most of them are not for me, as they often smell too synthetic. Intense Cherry is one of the Montale fragrances that I don't find so synthetic.

Delicious composition based on strawberry and roses. Despite being feminine, it's easily unisex in my opinion. A bit linear scent, opens with a lot of strawberry and roses, but nothing too sweet: there's no candy like smell. After the initial notes, there are some citruses that fades quickly. The development of the scent is not too noticeable: there are a vanilla and amber notes that joins and gives it a depth. Sillage and projection are medium-high. Lasting power is around 8 hours.

Rose Elixir opens and cruises through the central notes with a bucket full of candied strawberry fruit compote. A dash of roses, a bit of fruit juice, a tiny whiff of orange blossom round out the strawberry dessert. I happen to like strawberries which is a good thing. There is no gourmand excess other than this particular event thankfully. The vanilla is reasonably restrained. The ambergris and musk bolster the entire decadently rich fruitiness into a marginally elegant drydown. But really it's all about strawberries. It could easily be a fruity chypre if they just threw in some oakmoss and a tad of patchouli. This actually reminds me a great deal of Miss Dior Cherie EDP 2011 with it's stewed strawberries as well. As fruity florals go, it's an excellent fruity floral. Those who truly enjoy strawberry will love this.

An oudless rose perfume from the house of Montale? Yes, here it is: ROSE ELIXIR. This creation really caught me off guard. First, I assumed that the "elixir" would be amber or benzoin or some other resinous note(s). In fact, the elixir is a super sweet and concentrated fruit syrup! My guess was "red berries," but strawberries are identified as the primary source of the fruitiness of this composition. These are not straight-up strawberries, though. No, they have been cooked and reduced in a vanilla sugar syrup to produce a liquid with the viscosity of an elixir but the flavor of a candy. An all-natural, delicious, sparkling and bright candy, but it is candy nonetheless. By the drydown, some of the sugar syrup has evaporated away, leaving behind a very nice layer of rose, but this perfume really is quite sweet for an hour or so. It may seem difficult to believe that Montale would release a fruity-floral perfume such as this, and I have no doubt that there were some disgruntled blind buyers who assumed that this would be a part of what one of my fragrant friends refers to as "the holy rose trinity" of Montale rose perfumes: OUD ROSE PETALS, ROSE MUSC, and OUD DAMASCUS. No, ROSE ELIXIR, defying its name, is much closer to Yves Saint Laurent PARISIENNE. If that happens to be your genre, then you cannot go wrong with this scrumptious-smelling candied strawberry rose, but only fruity-floral lovers need apply!

I sprayed this on about 4 times and thought, eh, it's just a sweet fruity scent that's kind of light. 5 minutes later, it just exploded with strawberry and roses! It was still very light and airy so that it wasn't cloying, but boy was it sweet! I felt like I was floating on a cloud of cotton candy in a rose mist with a fleeting lemony taste. When I put my nose closer to my skin, I pick up a muted sour note resting in musk. It seems to counter the sweetness quite well, since there's nothing else in this mix to really keep it in check. I definitely detect the jasmine in this, as it seems to stand out from all the fruits and pink roses but still somehow remain part of the crowd. This is a scent that doesn't develop much. It does deepen a little with a bit of a musky, powdery feel, almost resinous. However, it has a synthetic feel to it, which I don't fancy too much. Overall, Roses Elixir is very pleasant and feminine, almost girly, even. It speaks of youth and happy thoughts, of a carefree time when bills and responsibilities don't matter quite so much. This lasted around 6-7 hours on me, with the last two hours being rather soft, otherwise sillage was rather decent.

Such an unsteady perfume! 1. Delicious, sweet rose with honey and fruits, the fruits are citrus, maybe strawberry, raspberry or currant, so some berry. I really like this stage. 2. Heavy resins. No, thanks. (Orange blossom?) 3. Beautiest metal and fruits, fresh, genuine, powerful. (Surprisingly I could identify this stage with top notes.) 4. Cheap, dry, strong soap. If the stages would be competitioners, I would chose the third one, and would not sniff any other from the 4, but unfortunately there is no choice, I have to hold on till the end. ROSES ELIXIR in my opinion is definitely for women (I beg your pardon, Gentlemen, who prefer to wear this, of course it is possible), strong and lasting.

Well! This IS the twin sister of Cherie, no doubt about it! As for all twin pairs, tiny differences distinguish them - so here the musk is more pronounced and sleek than in Cherie. A must, and again a well deserved 9/10 for Mr. Montale - because Cherie, my dears, has that bolder, bubblier personality I love, but I don't mind her sister's company one bit!

Personal: 5/10 – I don't enjoy it. Sweet and super synthetic. Mass appeal: 7/10 - Fruity rose a sugar is a crowd pleaser, but this is too synthetic smelling for most. Performance: 8/10 – Typical Montale: strong, loud, and long-lasting. Value: 6/10 – Montale pricing is fair, but what you get in this bottle is mediocre.

..I will love it. Do you know that feeling? You test a fragrance and it leaves you feeling ambivalent at first. There’s a note that somehow doesn’t sit well with you. But overall, the fragrance is quite beautiful and interesting, not least because of that disruptive factor.

So... I really don’t understand the negative comments at all. It was my first Montale. I only ordered it because I read it was very similar to Miss Dior Cherie from back then. Which is true, but it is more intense, fruitier. And absolutely fabulous! Seductive, delicious, floral, rosy, fruity, zesty!!!! And yes, an absolute outsider in the Montale family...

No, that was probably nothing. Not at all. This stuff is so sweet, so artificial, so strawberry-like. I felt completely queasy :-) . Somehow, the crazy song by the crazy Klaus Kinski comes to mind: "I'm so wild for your strawberry mouth." Maybe they sprayed poor Klaus with something like this before the recording in the studio. Creepy. That would at least explain the song...

while on business trip, I had 5 hours to kill at Charles de Gaulle airport my least favourite airport if I may add. What’s with the €13 Euro coffee & muffin? I was having none of this so I started hanging around the newly redone perfume section, and let me tell you that was heaven. I made a bee line for YSL counter wanting to try magnificent gold, tuxedo and the rest. There were no sales assistants about so I smelled every single perfume in the golden bottles. I knew of magnificent gold and this one was a total surprise to me. It was heavenly from the Initial spray, or you may want to say exquisite! It was rosy, fresh spicy, smooth yet piercing. It was beautiful and familiar, I loved it! When I finally got to my meeting, I opened my bag to pick up my phone and all I could smell was exquisite embroidery. It had overpowered all the others. The opening is amazing and it lasts for a long time but the dry down is equally beautiful with smooth ambergris and hints of oud. When I got home, I realised why it smelled familiar, it reminded me of Oud Satin Mood! It was less sweet, with even less oud and maybe a little airy. Importantly, it has that comforting scent aura that stays with you all the day. I’m in love with this scent, and I own both this and Oud Satin Mood. I find them different enough to have both. I also credit my growing love for ambergris to this little beauty, it is just amazing. According to YSL, exquisite embroidery has ginger and nutmeg in the opening, which is probably why it has that zing when you apply it. Give it a try!

This is really beautiful and interesting. It opens with a lot of roses and then transitions into nutmeg with a hint of musk and patchouli. I'm not sure I would say this is a rose perfume, as the dryness leans more towards the gourmand side. I feel a bit uncomfortable wearing rose perfumes, but this one is truly wonderful. A solid love of mine.

It has a slightly feminine scent, yet smells more masculine than feminine. But how often should we hear these genres associated at all? Perfume exists to be worn by people — not boxed into categories. It is precisely in the deeply personal experience of scent that any attempt to catalog perfume into a rigid genre feels improper. We should approach perfume with the purity and innocence of a child, drawn by the desire to discover new sensations that appeal to the soul rather than to reason. Perfume belongs to the wearer. Everyone should choose based on the emotions and sensations a fragrance stirs against their skin — not based on gender. Take Arabians by Montale, for instance. Despite its inspiration — the magnificent Arabian horses — there is no raw animalic smell here. Instead, the scent is an artistic creation: bold, resinous, dark, leathery, and richly oriental. Arabians greets me with a powerful opening of creeping red thyme and velvety lavender, blended with cardamom and mint. It carries a slightly camphorous edge, tinged with something mothball-like — perhaps from rose petals or thyme leaves, though not quite as they smell in nature. The opening is an overdose of herbs. Usually, thyme and cardamom are supporting notes, but here they charge to the forefront, dragging a hesitant lavender with them. The result is an unusually sharp, green opening — vivid, bitter with cardamom, and softened only slightly by lavender’s faint sweetness. As the aromatic face fades, the rose steps forward. It’s a clean, sexy rose — neither syrupy nor dirty — playing delicately among the other notes rather than dominating them. The camphor note persists on my skin, lingering like a ghost even as the rose unfurls. Later, patchouli, vetiver, and oud arrive. The scent transforms — growing darker, more grounded, truly earthy. The earlier herbal notes don’t disappear; they simply slip into the background, still contributing to the overall aroma. Leather only emerges in the final stages of the drydown — and even then, it feels more like velvety suede than rugged hide. Leather and oud combine into a soft, slightly animalic accord — dark, but never overwhelming or dirty. As with the rose, the oud is mellow, without the medicinal sharpness often found in traditional Middle Eastern blends. Arabians is undeniably an oriental fragrance, but it’s not a typical rose-oud composition. The additions of vetiver and patchouli balance and soften what could otherwise have been a too-heavy oud. As it dries, what remains on the skin and fabric is a musky, salty accord — with moss expanding over time, casting a faintly masculine veil that is perceptible from the start. Fittingly, the scent feels like an homage to the noble strength of the thoroughbred horse. In conclusion, Arabians is excellent — non-offensive, non-restrictive, and highly wearable. It starts loud, but softens into a skin-friendly scent over time. Here, neither rose nor oud is the star. Both serve as supportive players in a complex, evolving composition. Its performance may not roar like other Montale fragrances — but I don’t mind. I love the scent, even as it clings quietly to my skin. Arabians feels like a dark autumn cloak — perfect for colder months, best suited to evenings or nights. Arabians feels like the memory of a storm passing — the scent of wet earth, cold air, and the soft tread of unseen hooves. It clings to my skin like a story half-remembered, haunting and comforting all at once. This review is based on a bottle I have owned and loved since October 2022. — Elysium

A wild Arabian stallion ridden by a thief with a saber. In the dry, dusty desert. The imagination starts to run wild when you read the name and see the bottle. I expected a scent like Oud Assam. Fecal note and a bit dirty. However, something different awaited me. The fragrance starts with a certain lightly fecal medicinal note. I'm a bit torn about what I should perceive it as. The rose is already playing a part and is moving in the direction I expect. The scent is already somewhat restrained. As it develops, it becomes sweeter and surprisingly pleasant and simple. The oud note slowly retreats completely, leaving behind a floral sweet scent. The cardamom beautifully embraces the whole composition, and the fragrance knows how to please in its own way. However, I find the theme completely missed, and when I think of a wild Arabian, a completely different scent comes to mind. Something similar has been smelled often. The fragrance is quite restrained and offers a subtle sillage and a longevity of about 4 hours on my skin. The bottle is stylish, and I somehow like the tin cans from Montale. My favorites from the house remain Blue Amber and Red Vetyver. Best regards, Sebastian

Another expensive "oud plus rose & honey & saffron mix." Some years ago, this arrangement started out as a popular "niche" - combo and has now made its way into the posh segment of L'Oréal et. al. - Not in the least original, this "Majectic Rose" is lush and opulent and it is just what you'd expect from the lively interaction of the partners mentioned. The arranged marriage with "Mr Oud" seems to be "Rose"'s destiny. Time for new maritial options.

Some fragrances take us back to specific moments, to memories that will always stay with us. Dallachai is one of those fragrances that I consider as such, of which when I had the privilege of trying it, I didn't even suspect its release. I put it on one early autumn evening, in one of my favourite cities: Cannes. The joy of that moment, enjoying the atmosphere of a place that is magical to me, being in a place that until recently I could only watch from afar (but that's another story) and not least, being stopped by people asking me what perfume I was in, can only have made it so special. For me, it is a wonderful Cappuccino with oriental and spicy nuances, chic, gentle, but also impactful, enveloping you with a wonderful scented cloud, which trust me, lasts a very long and follows your body, making itself perceived and then vanishing unexpectedly, creating something extremely charming. It reminds me of unexpected kindness, smiles, beautiful and genuine encounters. Truly a beautiful creation, which I can definitely say I listed among my favourites. ‘Balloon Girl’, a beautiful work of art by Banksy.

Dallachaï seems to be rated as a "bad" fragrance according to the reviews. But that is definitely not the case! Don't be misled by the typical pre-criticism of Montale. It feels like Montale is rated poorly even before one has smelled the fragrances. That is not okay and is partly typical of Parfumo members. I ask you to approach the scent completely neutrally. Dallachaï starts off, in my opinion, exciting but still slightly unbalanced. The scent is still trying to find itself, and that is still happening. At first, it gives me a fruity-spicy impression that, as mentioned, takes a little while to settle. In any case, we get a relatively authentic passion fruit vibe. The passion fruit gets a spicy twist from the clove and cardamom. The coffee note can also already be sensed in the background and contributes to the spicy impression. Over time, all the notes find a nice common path. For me, it takes about 20-30 minutes for the fragrance to form this wonderful symbiosis of the mentioned notes. The scent then, in my perception, follows a rather straightforward path. It doesn't change significantly. The only thing is that the fruity component slowly and gradually retreats. The spiciness also becomes a bit milder. Otherwise, the scent progression is, in my opinion, quite linear, and I don't find that bad at all. I like the scent just as it is. By the way, it is also well received by others. Especially women notice the scent and ask what wonderful fragrance one is wearing. Dallachaï is wonderfully unisex wearable, and the performance is typically Montale, not bad. This time we don't have a "beast," but the longevity and sillage are really quite okay.

My son, who is usually totally in love with my scents, said to me right after I sprayed it: Mama, you smell, this perfume is terrible. My two-year-old just replied, baah, disgusting. I wanted to love it so much, I am in love with the bottle. But unfortunately, I have to say, it is just totally off. When I spray it, I get the feeling of heartburn, just like after a vodka passion fruit, after a while it becomes smoother and the coffee joins in, at one point you briefly think it might be the brother of intense Cafe and wonder if the scent development will still take a turn, but in the drydown it is like a mix of intense Cafe and erba pura for me and unfortunately, I can't warm up to it. I have to say that everyone in my circle reacted poorly to it, such a shame.

Fortunately, perceptions and tastes are different. It would be boring if we all liked the same food, the same drink, or the same fragrance. In this respect, all related feelings or impressions are legitimate at any time. Furthermore, there are many brand groupies or fanboys/girls/? who push everything that a certain brand brings to market; the "brand haters" behave in an obviously contrary manner. Fragrances from Montale are particularly controversial. For SOME, they are odorless, sharp, and penetrating fluids from a test tube; for OTHERS, the holy grail of perfumery, concise, creative, affordable, and long-lasting...everything is OK! I own some of these fragrances. The ones I have in my closet, I obviously like very much (otherwise I wouldn't have them). Even Arabians Tonka is, in my opinion, great and I enjoy wearing it. However, I find nearly all rose fragrances (for me!!) unbearable. I initially got to try Dallachaï in a perfumery in Hanover and liked it immediately. Whether the fruity note truly resembles a passion fruit, I honestly can't say, as I don't even know what passion fruit smells like. But the combination of coffee, spices, and something fruity is quite exciting. It's strong...of course...it's a real Montale...But: It lacks the sharpness that many (ironically) describe as the typical DNA of this brand. At first, the note of a lightly spiced hot beverage dominates, and the fruit of passion holds back. This changes after 2-3 hours. The coffee-like bitterness fades, and a pleasant, soft tropical sweetness makes its appearance. Somehow, I imagine that I now even perceive something oud-like, and I can faintly hear Oud for Greatness Eau de Parfum approaching. Definitely an interesting development. Must you like "him"? No! Because "he" will polarize...as something special always polarizes...I don't care, because he now stands in my closet.

I think the scent is great! I don't understand the many negative reviews. To me, it smells of pleasant spices, paired with a delicious passion fruit scent and something soft, creamy. I smell neither plastic nor Maggi. I was in Istanbul a few years ago. The smell reminds me of a warm evening in a nice hookah bar near a spice market. I've had the scent for 2 days and have already been complimented on it (positively!) Don't let the negative reviews guide you, just give it a try yourself (important, it needs to rest on the skin for a few minutes until the typical Montale metallic scent fades away).

First spray.. Wow, what is THIS? Passion fruit hits with full fruitiness, clove adds a spiciness, and a slight coffee breeze lingers in the background. I've never smelled anything like this before. And that's meant positively. I like it when scents smell different and new combinations hit the market. This combo is really bold! Hats off!

Do you know that feeling? You're in a decor store of a well-known chain and are just trying out the selection of room fragrances? That was my first and positive association with this scent (even though I don't really like the decor stores themselves). I haven't been able to smell a similar perfume so far; perhaps a knowledgeable nose will correct me.

I received the fragrance as a sample with my Arabians Musk and ordered it after testing it for a day! Dallachai is definitely a "challenging scent" that needs to develop, and yes, it either comes around in a really special way or it becomes a nightmare!

The base of the fragrance is unmistakably exactly the same as that of Roses Musk, which is why these scents are obviously similar, at least to me. What bothered me about Roses Musk: the top note is far too green for me, it feels more like the cut green stem than the rose - that's not the case here in Dallachai, where the top notes are all lovely and rounded.

One thing upfront: The scent is definitely not a people-pleaser. However, I still can't quite understand some of the negative reviews. Dallachaï is a very spicy-fruity fragrance that admittedly overwhelms you at first. But once it has settled a bit, I find myself repeatedly smelling my wrist, it's that interesting.

With Oud Pashmina, I pick up on four main elements: gasoline, leather, purple roses, and vanilla. It came as a shock to discover that the fragrance actually has less notes than what I am smelling as accords. I think this is a stunning, high quality, and perfectly blended mixture. Performance is excellent. It's the best rose/oud I've ever smelled. You'll kind of feel like a biker dude from the 70s with greased up hair. I love how masculine this smells in the sense of the leather and the gas. My dad is a mechanic and and this reminds me a bit of what he'd smell like when he came home.

This is one of those fragrances that really catch you off guard, not just because it's a great scent but because of the reaction that the female counter parts give you. Now on my skin , this is not the typical oud rose combo but it's much much more. With the sweet note of vanilla and fruits at the top along with a touch of leather and just a touch of musk in the dry down really sets this apart from all the counter parts out there. A very nice touch from the house of Montale, get it if you can and you won't regret it.

I received Oud Pashima as a sample with a purchase at the souk. Montale is a brand that I haven't found particularly convincing until now. The fragrances often come across as too synthetic and sometimes border on giving me headaches. Fortunately, Oud Pashima is different; the scent is strong and has solid projection. The sillage is noticeable for about 3-4 hours at a little over arm's length and then quickly becomes close to the skin. After about 10-11 hours, Oud Pashima is no longer detectable. There is nothing to criticize regarding its longevity. It lasts a good 11 hours on my skin. I don't need to say much about the scent itself: It is a fragrance with rose and oud, with the rose being rather softly dosed, which I appreciate. Oud is clearly recognizable, but this is not a fragrance with an extreme oud note; I don't expect that at a retail price of €125 for 100 ml. The musk is clearly dominant for me. The longevity and performance are clearly achieved with the musk. The quality is good, but it's just not Roja, Ensar, Xerjoff, etc. One shouldn't expect that here. I can definitely recommend this Montale and am already considering purchasing a bottle.

My text is aimed at those who might want to consider Oud Pashmina as an alternative to Ombre Nomade. Let's start with how I came across this fragrance. I smelled Ombre Nomade for the first time in my life and had to make this scent mine. This unique DNA combined with its longevity and sillage is simply amazing. However, when I saw the price of Ombre Nomade back then, I realized that a more affordable alternative was necessary. However, I must mention here that once you like the scent DNA, you should rather go for the original, as there will always be something in the alternatives that will bother you in the long run. Anyway, while searching for alternatives, I came across various fragrances, such as those from the Arabic houses, Royal Nights,... and also Oud Pashmina. Since I wanted to get Arabians Tonka anyway and there was a 20ml fragrance of your choice as a gift with every purchase at Montale, it was the perfect opportunity to test Oud Pashmina. Said and done. The fragrance arrived a few days later, and I tested it extensively. The scent is a lovely rose-oud combination, all nice and good, but is the scent an alternative to Ombre Nomade? For me, Ombre Nomade is characterized by a mix of earthy, dirty notes and a beautiful raspberry note, accompanied by atomic longevity. Let's go through the points: Are there earthy, dirty notes present? Yes, but they are very, very subdued compared to Ombre Nomade. Is there a fruity component? No, in contrast to ON, OP completely omits the raspberry. And how is the longevity? For me, it lasts a good 6 hours, but you can't call that beast mode, while ON probably only has to hide from Air Tiger. In my opinion, OP is a fragrance that aims for a similar direction but wants to remain completely independent at the same time. I perceive OP as more feminine due to the subdued earthy, dirty oud note compared to ON. I wouldn't recommend the scent as an alternative, but if someone is looking for something more accessible, less "dirty," and in the direction of ON, they might consider making a purchase.

Those looking for a slightly more feminine alternative to Ombre Nomade will find it in "Oud Pashmina | Montale." The performance is truly strong. The longevity on my skin is about 24 hours with a booming sillage. Since the complexity of Oud Pashmina is somewhat limited and most of the aromas are consistently present, I will skip the top, heart, or base notes here. The scent is floral, dark, oriental-spicy, woody, sweet, animalic, leathery, fruity, and subtly smoky. I detect aromas of rose water, oud, musk, raspberries, suede, amber, benzoin, as well as a hint of vanilla. In the end, I find Oud Pashmina quite successful and thank Sören for the sample.

One of my favorite fragrances from Montale. Longevity and sillage 8.5/10. It is a very seductive scent that smells similar to Ombre Nomade by Louis Vuitton. The oud combined with rose is just incredibly perfect for a night walk in the rain with a girlfriend. I can recommend it to anyone who likes Ombre Nomade.

This is definitely an aromatic fougère fragrance. The dark woody notes make it unique and interesting to wear. I must admit I was turned off by the mention of the whole "barbershop" vibe. But now I'm sure that this one stands out as a very dark and greenish woody fragrance that will suit most users and can be worn as a day or night time scent. I find it an intriguing one to wear and would certainly recommend it.

... (Continuation of the text under the Light Version) The Intense variant is unmistakably a Rive Gauche (powdery lavender, anise, shaving feel, very noble & fine), just a bit darker, earthier, and more patchouli-heavy. More suited for the evening, even more powder & chalk, and with a hint of chocolate or spiciness. We had a similar case recently with Armani's Diamonds Black Carat compared to the original. I would clearly prefer the Intense variant over the airy Light version, but it still offers me too little added value compared to the all-rounder original. I am also still uncertain whether such extremely close variants of a bestseller are really more sensible than today's flankers, which often offer completely new approaches and could have been marketed under new names. Flankers are generally not the golden egg of perfume... Bottles: all very cool & stylish - my design favorite is just slightly the Light version. Sillage: Light is really very, very light. Intense not much heavier than the original, just as indicated, definitely darker. Longevity: Light: 3-5 hours (too short!), Intense: 8-9 hours (similar to the original!) Conclusion: Even though the two flankers are only of interest to die-hard Rive Gauche PH fans, they are still worth a look & deliver almost exactly what the names promise. Unlike nowadays where flankers often have no similarities with the originals anymore, both here stay very true to the name... but no one has to mourn that they are no longer available for purchase!

No comments yet on this offshoot of Rive Gauche pour Homme?! Let's change that now. I have only recently discovered the fragrances of Yves Saint Laurent. Unfortunately, very late. However, I have always liked Opium pour Homme very much, but I always thought it was too drastic. Only in today's time and with increasing age do I truly appreciate its uniqueness. After Rive Gauche pour Homme completely blew me away upon careful testing, I thought that a more intense version for the evening would not be a bad idea. This little drop is still available online. I don't find the differences between the original and the Intense version to be that significant. What makes this version, in my opinion, more suitable for the evening is the more subdued soapy quality. It is still present here, but not as piercing. The whole thing develops into a very slightly powdery direction. This very light powder note has nothing to do with Dior homme. A very pleasant and elegant going-out fragrance. Why do such small and affordable treasures never receive the appreciation they deserve?

The top stage may give a slight headache. It was powerful, deep and penetrating. I was disappointed, at first, right after a spray. I thought oh no, this is the same as Montale Aoud Lime. Aoud Lime is a hate to my nose, gave me the strongest headache just by a spray. I thought this Red Aoud has the same attack on me, but only, I smell rose (though not listed), pepper, along with the moderate aoud. But as seconds passed, it is not as terrible cloy as it was like Aoud Lime. In fact, the scent is very attractive, lovely, I just have to convince myself that this cloying stage would be over soonest and it did. Don't get me wrong but this top stage is a stunning fragrance. I did my first test inside my bedroom under a normal room temperature. Few minutes after, I was mesmerized by how the scent performed a wonderful floral and woody dance that my nose and smelling perception was hypnotized to utmost admiration & joy. The heart to base was on my skin, linear, the blend of light rose, strong spices and aoud done just right, all the way, amazed my heart to beat along this fragrance dance. A formal romantic dance with a beautiful woman, wearing a gorgeous, sleeveless red dress. Her charm was very inviting. Her aura captivates anyone, woman and man, within her sight. That was how I imagine Red Aoud on my nose, with just a decent spray. Two weeks after, I decided to wear this on a minus 18 winter mid afternoon, two sprays, going on a friend's birthday bash. I met two female friends at a cafe, before heading to the celebrant's pad. I brought with me my sample, to ready a spray should I stay at the occasion for the next 5 hours or so. At the cafe, they smelled a whiff & right then, I received wonderful compliments, asking me to share a tiny spray to their wrists. We all felt the rose, the unfamiliar aoud scent, the blend of a fragrance perfection. As we are at the party, Red Aoud projected in the living room, like the gorgeous dancer in red dress, it floats everywhere, wanting to be noticed, balmy, woody, some fruity & floral, synthetic in the best way & well spiced. It was this wonderfully infecting our senses that it came to be a topic for a while. I have no choice but to spit out her name.. Montale Red Aoud The next morning, after an evening of fun and a few drinks, I took a shower and to my surprise, I can still smell this beautiful perfume on my skin. I was convinced that this beauty is an immortal. A beast in projection, a goddess in longevity, a fragrance to desire and to possess.

Montale Red Aoud surprised me with a blast of sweetness straight out of the sprayer. I initially tested on the back of my hand but it was instant love so I decided to empty my tiny partially used sample vial. Soon after a full application, I noticed the freshness of this scent. This is a rich, opulent sweet freshness that I could not ignore. I was pretty impressed because I expected a heavy, dark, pungent Oud but instead I got a niche quality gourmand with a masculine edge. I did not detect the Oud note until around 8 hours after I first applied. I continued to get delicious whiffs throughout the day but I beamed as a salesperson stuttered through his spiel because it was interrupted three times by, "Damn you smell good!" Of the notes listed, my nose only knows Oud and vetiver. I suppose the vetiver can account for the freshness but the sweetness remains a mystery. I would compare this gem to Taueraide but I won't because both can't be Best but they are running neck in neck for Fresh.

Along with White Aoud, Red Aoud is definetely one of the best Montale's releases. It smells heavenly and it's a masterpiece from this house in my opinion. Oud is not loud/harsh and does not play the main role here. Lots of pepper, caraway, sweet roses and orris root give it a depth and a nice amount of sweetness. It's sweet and warm, and trully unisex. Sometimes it reminds me of Dior Homme Intense. Thumbs up for this masterpiece. Updated January 2014

MONTALE RED AOUD is a hot scent for a cold night, where you're escorted past the velvet rope and invited to the VIP section. But, nah, the woman in RED AOUD is ready to go home and have sex. From roses to a slinky vanilla, all with projection and longevity--talk to me lover!

You are enjoying the most beautiful sunset of your life. The sun is immense, and it shines like a colossal ruby ​​red ball in the sky full of clouds. Twilight gets darker every second, and the sun tints the sky with incredible hues of gold, hot pink, bright red, orange, and purple. If this scenario were a perfume, that perfume would be Red Aoud. It is my second take on Montale after wearing Roses Musk. We are on another planet, and if this doesn't make you love the rose, nothing will. The combination of oud is unfamiliar, although it has been performed many times in many ways. It's phenomenal how the rose covers the oud like it's not there. The dustiest oud I've ever smelled, a powdery rose's cloud sprinkling of saffron and cumin, backed by a delicate woody base of vetiver, sandalwood, and coumarin. The notes seem to blend seamlessly into each other. It is warm, mysterious, comforting, spicy, bright, deep, fresh, and truly gorgeous in every way. The oud is very precise in it, just enough to make the scent so interesting, complex, and oriental. I feel a floral scent mixed with some spices at a first sniff. I am pretty impressed because I expected a heavy, intense oud, but I get a niche quality gourmand with a bold edge. The smell of oud and a strong pepper arrives. I love the oud, but here the things in the background defeat it. It could be this blend plus the oud hint that gives this juice a woody sense. The oud note here is not as powerful as in other perfumes with the same note but still noticeably present. It is exquisitely delicious, with a sweet and salty woody character similar to caramel with a hint of a sour dry red rose. I don't get black pepper, but something like chilli or pink pepper. The pepper note remains throughout its life, being very strong in the opening and delusional in the dry, and keeps the chip from getting too rosy. It is red because of the red rose and red pepper. The heart smells precisely like some silky, creamy praline, white chocolate truffle with a rose confiture centre. Hidden hints of cocoa provide a certain sophistication and a kind of gourmand quality. Here the rose is exquisite and cold. The saffron enters, giving the impression of dark vanilla and hints of caramelized nuts. Wow, I am amazed when I smell this grace. The cumin flavours the saffron resulting in a strong spicy aroma. I love the rose-oud combination, here opposite to what we find, for example, in Essence Oud . Saffron and cumin are soft but distinct, the former slightly leathery, adding an exotic floral hit that spreads in the breeze. The flowers are held back by the spicy sweetness, and the sweetness is held back by the flowers and woody components. The middle stage is a brilliant saffron tango with a rose full of expressiveness and dynamism. For me, this is a gourmand on the beautiful dry side. Then, it softens more and more, over time, revealing a persistent sense of creaminess in the background, a mix of sandalwood-vanilla-musk. Earthy, but instils a feeling of sublime rapture and comfort. A beautiful rose that remains there, elegant, together with vetiver and sandalwood, a slightly powdery floral, with something pillowy and welcoming, which I believe results from notes like cumin and sandalwood. A delightful combination of sandalwood and vetiver follows; I love how the vetiver plays its role here, making it dry and very sensual. The notes are pretty precise and well-balanced; none of the notes dominates each other. At this stage, the oud is gone off the scent to my nose, but I can feel the iris but not the lipstick you find like in classic Dior Homme. Ultimately, oud isn't screaming here; it's just whispering. It is less medicinal and sweeter, softer and more floury than the other oud-based scents I have tried, both from this house and others. Saffron, rose, iris and sandalwood are the dominant notes in my nose. It is like a veil of dark chocolate on my skin with a rose, not too firm, not too sweet, just beautiful. I can also see myself wearing it day and night in cold months. The composition is velvety, very intriguing, but soft and adherent to the skin. Longevity is pretty remarkable. You can smell it on your clothes until you wash them. As for the oud, this is the most easily wearable and most acceptable for a new oud audience. It is unashamedly unisex and has a beautiful rose for men to wear! This review is based upon a decant I have owned since January 2021. -Elysium

Tonight after my bath, I decided to play a bit of Montale roulette, which involves reaching into my hat box (seriously...) of samples from this house and wearing whatever I happen to select. RED OUD it was.

Red Aoud has an opening so obnoxious that you just want to slap its face. Really, it is quite an ugly cacophony of notes - red pepper, that fake chocolate/wheat note from Chocolate Greedy, the sour fizzing Montale oud, and bready cumin - all tumbled in together with no thought as to the outcome. But wait half an hour and all I can say is, Oh. My. God.

Red is definitely one of the most striking colors there is. Red associates with warmth, passion, pure joy of life, sin, the color of blood, warning, anger (the redness of rage), and much more. Anyone wearing red clothing will be noticed and cannot hide behind it.

What is this? That was my first thought when I applied “Red Aoud” by Montale. At this point, a big thank you to Inala for the sample. But let’s start from the beginning. For some time now, I have been testing one Montale after another. At first, I couldn’t really get into them at all But gradually, that changed. And how it changed!

I have already thought a bit about how to describe this perfume since I couldn't quite categorize the scent. For me, this perfume is a woody-spicy fragrance bomb ;) the longevity is very good, and the scent is extremely intense!!! After applying, this scent has almost an ethereal quality to it; I perceive Oud (earthy smell, slightly musty, but not negatively!

this one smells so sweet, dark, sexy, mystery, elegent and sensual with main notes of Damask Rose, Blackberry and Leather and first it's open with rose and blackberry rose made feeling sexy and rich blackberry made feeling naughty and cute both are dark and mystery in base notes more sweet with vanilla and luxury by patchouli, all are cover by smoky note like incense. for me Parisienne A L'extreme is one of all beautiful purple scents include rose and berry (each Lancome tresor midnight rose, lanvin jeanne lanvin etc ...) but on my skin it's so sweet at first in top notes, but smell bad on heart and base long lasting and a little bit heavy sillage

YSL is one of my favourite Houses. They make such good perfumes. I have a goal in life, that one day I have smelled all their perfumes, both male and female. I am working on it. There is a long way to go, still. Fabulous journey! When I spray this, I feel lifted. The berries and the rose give it such a magnificent freshness, a bit like in Elle YSL. I love to wear this whenever… well, just whenever. On my skin it does not become dark or sensual. It is a fresh, light and delicious rosy scent with loads of berries. The bottle is like a faceted gem. The way the glass turns darker at the bottom, like a violet syrup sinking in a drink. Simply marvelous. 170/365

If the commercial with Kate Moss had promised more than Parisienne can deliver in all its variations.... If Parisienne a l`Extreme had been released as the first version... If the fragrance had gained more expressiveness in its composition.... then this latest version would surely be better received than carrying the burdens of its predecessor. As it stands, this is a dark-floral scent with a pleasant creamy note at the outset. Like a subtler version of XS/Paco Rabanne. Less red berries and without a zesty top note. In a way, it feels diluted. However, a soft suede note develops quite pleasantly - at least to my nose - roughened by a hint of incense. I quite like that, but overall it still feels too little for me. I wanted to write: too light, but that’s not true at all. The perfume comes across as the umpteenth copy of a beautiful original. What remains feels pale, blurred, and I would like more of it. And I would also like it to last longer, as the longevity is only mediocre. But as I said, it’s almost impossible to approach this fragrance without prejudice. I would have loved to say: "Why not do it this way from the start?" But for that, the improvement would have needed to be significantly greater.

Ah, the fragrance mail has arrived! YSL Parisienne à l‘Extrême. Let’s get started! *Pfffff* Association 1 (just the first seconds): *Hicc* oh dear, ‘ssss let’s call it a Booooowwwlllleeee, thunderrrrrific!!!! Such a fruity*hick*thingnnnn*hick* Association 2 (the first minutes): A juicy berry carpet (mind you, not bear~), but dark and ripe, blackberry-like, blueberry-like, fresh-bitter-sweet. Above all, NOT squeaky, but rich and full-bodied. Association 3 (after about 15-20 minutes): The juiciness of the berries is joined by something smoky, but by no means the typical incense note, rather subtle, like lightly smoked berries over dark wood. An unusual but tasty campfire. Association 4 (after about three-quarters of an hour to an hour): Now the smoked berries get to ride on leather saddles, wild of course, fitting their character, but not in a gallop, rather in a gentle trot, which allows them to retain their smoky berry essence, but adds a slightly dry velvety touch. Association 5 (after a few hours): The trotting smoked berries on their wild leather saddle tuck a little rose behind their ear, just a small one, but deep dark red, it has to match the outfit. A vanilla pod hangs at the corner of the mouth like a cigarette, wild remains wild. Conclusion: An extremely successful fragrance composition, from my personal perspective and my scent preferences, a significantly better variant of the original Parisienne, which comes off too raspberry-squeaky-sweet for me. The l‘Extrême is darker, fitting the hand-friendly bottle by the way, much less sweet, but creamier, fuller, and through the (incense) smoke and leather note, more mature and mysterious. Very rounded and well-coordinated fragrance notes with an interesting scent progression. There are worse berry scents on the fragrance market, a test is worth it here!

I find "Parisienne à l'Extrême" doesn't smell very different from "Parisienne." It starts soft, light, and sweet, floral and not candy-like. The orange candies are also absent; the fragrance is defined solely by raspberries and roses, with a hint of mandarin, as I imagine, along with the distinct scent of violets and a bit of vanilla. I don't smell leather there. Unfortunately, this fragrance is also far too delicate, making it almost exhausting to smell at all. But otherwise, it's a great scent.

For me, it's a beautiful scent that always reminds me of my vacation in Spain. Because there, on the beach promenade in a small perfumery, I discovered it. It wasn't exactly love at first spray, but I just couldn't forget it, so I went back the next day and bought it. Thus, it is something very special for me, as I associate this scent with that time. I can, however, understand that it may not appeal to everyone, as you either love it or hate it. My surroundings notice it, but it's not a scent that draws all the attention to itself. It's rather subtle and feels like a second skin. Therefore, it's suitable for everyday wear. Personally, I enjoy wearing it in the summer, as I find it develops even more beautifully on the skin. I find it beautiful and delicate on the skin. For me, it has something soft and creamy about it. On clothing, I can still perceive the scent days later. This scent must not be missing from my collection.

From my perspective, it's not such a great scent. The musk is very sharp at first and stings the nose. After a while, the amber comes through, but it doesn't really improve the overall package. Personally, I wouldn't wear it; a colleague who smelled it wanted to order it right away. So I can only say, either you love it or you hate it.

A sexy scent with a relatively weak longevity for Montale. It is perceived like a molecule fragrance. It lasts several days on clothing, but on the skin, I only notice it for a few hours. For a designer fragrance, the longevity would be above average, but I am used to something different from Montale. This doesn’t necessarily have to be a bad thing, especially on warmer days, I appreciate a subtle scent. In my opinion, it can be worn by both men and women, but it's best to start slowly. With too high a dosage, it quickly becomes overwhelming. A true masterpiece from Montale.

Ambroxan greets, amber and musk are only very faintly perceptible, it has something creamy about it and lasts and lasts. I don't find it bad at all, it's very close to the body, only noticed by the people in my immediate vicinity. And yes, it has something synthetic about it, it might smell like a beautiful female alien. I find it feminine, a bit too sweet for men. This scent can definitely be good for layering. I have been approached about the scent almost every time - it smells very good to my environment. Some perfumes need a second or third chance. I think this is a very softly erotic seducer. After a while, you no longer perceive it yourself, but then you are unexpectedly surprised by its presence. It’s not the mega extravagant scent but the nice and friendly-good girlfriend from another planet (wink with the eye, Nano Nano, Mork from Ork) laugh, it will find its followers, it has already captured me, lasts really very long and gently scents my beautiful clothes on the favorite scarf in the closet. I am a fan of Montale fragrances and I really like this one for the upcoming dark and cold season. It is welcome and may stay.

Ferragamo Black has been an authentic discovery of surprising beauty for me. It has been the first Ferragamo fragrance that I have tried and it has awakened in me an interest in trying other fragrances of this brand, including those for women. Perfumery -in this case, brands- continues to surprise me, thanks to Venus and Nefertum The beginning of Ferragamo Black is exquisite: an explosion of quality based on lavender, apple and pepper. I feel the herbaceous note of coriander and maybe some sage. I also sense the undeclared presence of cardamom and maybe nutmeg. But if the opening already denotes an unusual complexity and a set of balanced notes, its superb development and drying is yet to come, When resinous labdanum and leather (not declared on the file) make an appearance, the fragrance becomes more masculine and stately, like when an Oxford history professor comes to the Dean's residence for dinner. Ferragamo Black is intense, sensual, complex, luminous and deep, mysterious and brilliant. It has an unusual sillage and duration in today's perfumes, with great quality in its nuances and notes. I hope it hasn't been reformulated and lost this beauty.

F Black has a strong longevity and medium-high sillage and projection. Smells great and sexy with lots of tonka bean rounded by sweet lavender and some pepper. Remembers me of Chanel Allure Pour Homme.That's a good surprise from this house. Updated January 2014

For the sake of heaven, how come I waited so long before buying it? I do have several Ferragamo colognes in my collection, namely Uomo and its siblings, still F and any of its flankers, for a reason I don't know, never fit in the shopping basket. But, recently I had a chance of ordering some testers and F Black was available for a couple of bucks, so I blindly bought it, and I gave it a true SOTD wearing. First off, F Black comes with an original bottle, mine is miserable without a cap, which might happen if you accept to buy testers, and contains a pale grey juice supposedly with oriental woody tones. On my skin, F Black opens up with an explosion of sweetness and freshness from fruity apple and pungent lavender, all the way. It smells good, I get the crispy apple unquestionably.
