Originally, the sweetness and sourness of the green apple are stronger than the lavender smell and they stand above it, yet a few minutes later it tones down and the lavender boosts in all its aromatic and harsh aspects. Ain't bad in any aspect, rather it is a bold, deep, punching loud, and dark lavender, more herbaceous and less flowery, far away from Davidoff Cool Water, for instance. The opening is amazing, is posh, is fruity and spicy, at least my bottle and batch are. The heart introduces a good amount of black pepper, which adds some spiciness together with coriander seeds, all that in your face. The mid note of coriander begins to come through very pleasantly and seems expertly blended in the way it reveals itself. I do not get too much spiciness, the black pepper is dosed consciously and well mixed with coriander. The first time I wore it, I did not notice a fresh, clean and soapy accord in the heart with a certain powdery sweetness almost like the atmosphere of the lipstick, yet today it manifests itself in a remarkable way. The mid-notes then seamlessly transitioned into a beautifully delicious dry-down. which is a combo of sweet and spicy with a bit of a powdery note that usually comes from labdanum or amber accord. The profound and sensual association of labdanum and tonka bean in the dry down mimics the masculinity of the warming heart notes and rounds out this amber and woody cologne. Still along for the ride, the lavender note remains present, but more subtly and smoothly. Aside from the punchy opening this one seems expertly blended and has the feel of a niche quality product. I agree with other reviewers who find some small similarities with Chanel Allure and YSL La Nuit de l'Homme. I mean, F Black is not a clone of those colognes, however, it reminds Allure in the opening and then turns int YSL La Nuit de l'Homme in the heart and drydown. Notwithstanding, F Black is a nice fragrance per se with its personality. The notes I get most are lavender, black pepper, and tonka bean. F Black has been created to be worn for evenings on the town and special occasions, anyway, today I'm rocking it at the office and did not get any disappointment. It's a cologne that fits perfectly with the colder months, Fall and Winter seasons, daytime, evening out, and rainy nights. The sillage and projection are average in my opinion, and the longevity is very good, I get around 8 hours on clothing. Overall this is a great cheapy to have in your collection, so if you can get past the lavender-heavy opening, you may be pleasantly surprised. Honestly, it doesn't blow me away in any particular aspect but rather is well above average across the board. No regrets. -Elysium

Only had it for a year, but I have a love/hate relationship with this one - as many others do. I really do not like the opening, it's very very strong and for me it's lavender/pepper all over. I've learned that I really do not care for lavender, so this is why it's a uphill battle for me. On the plus side, after an hour or so, the scent does become better for me, It's still a strong scent, so do not over spray. I find myself reaching for this one, when it is really cold outside, as in below 0 degree Celsius. I would go with 1 or 2 spray max. Have used it for work/college and casual settings. It is cheap, around 25-30 euros/ 100 ml and the longevity is crazy..... I can smell it the next day.

After a lot "top ten, top masculine, top seductive, top......whatever" videos and hyped by Jeremy, after a very good discount to 16 EUR for 100ml TESTER, i decided to push the button. I expected something bold or piercing, something a bit daring maybe. Something like intense version of Sauvage EDT or Fahrenheit, something spicy-oriental with western touch like TF Black Orchid or Tuscan Leather or Guerlain Ambre Eternal. Or maybe Bentley for man Intense........but what i got is creamy, mild peppery-sweet-fruity scent, that didn`t punch me at all. Even my girlfriend, who likes only fresh and delicate fragrances, said that this one is very pleasant for cool weather. Nothing offensive. Wolf Of Wallstreet........not at all. More like Labrador Of Wallstreet. Don`t get me wrong, i love sweet and calm scent, i love this one too. Bottle is uncomfortable but interesting, not stylish. To me it is very good signature scent, appropriate for office, for family meets, for date out, versatile. I skip it only in hot days.
I am revisiting this one after buying it almost a year ago I do not like the opening so much but let it sit a while and Dang is it GOOD!

First time I encoutered this scent was when boyfriend got it. What an amazing scent this is!!! OFFTOP this is one of the few perfumes I loved out of the male section, as most of the time all manly perfumes remind me of either deodorant or washgel, except this one. LOVELY scent of lavander, followed by a gentle touch of apples... such delicate scent.

So, I've been watching Jeremy Fragrance(sadly, quality now is just very bad) for long time and I saw this perfume in one or couple of his videos. It was hyped not even by Jeremy but also in comment section, that, it is cheap but smells amazing. Well, I decided to try it and made blind purchase. I would like to say, it's not bad, but not even close as good as some people say.

I like this more than the Armaf Club De Nuit Intense Man. Although the notes are different, they serve the same purpose for me (daily riders) . It' s less alcoholic than Armaf CDN, and tries to blend less smells. It reminds me of the generic mid 2000's Men' s perfumes, with Lavender and Vanilla combinations.

One of those Jeremy Fragrance recommendations that fell flat on its face. To me is meh. Too spicy for my taste. The pepper is way over the top. Good for winter. Suppodsely the wolf of wall street cologne. To me is more like pepe le piou cologne. 300 300 300 300 300 300 300 300 300 300 300 300 300 300

Montale’s fragrances have very authentic aoud DNA, but this one doesn’t have quality of oud and not ever forestry at all. Marine and citrusy notes are very dominative and in few hours they are gone like a light breeze. Scent was done very close to “Eternity” by Calvin Klein. I feel like perfumery repeats itself with same like clones and identical accords. Longevity is very poor. Rose here is very shy or in minuscule proportion. If you want aromatic, synthetic, marine feel, why not to purchase less expensive version? Dupes are widely available. Gems are rare.

I got a sample of Montale Aoudforest today with another Montale/Mancera samples. It open with lemon note ( strong opening ) then it dry down to a kind of ginger honey beer, salty smell according to Seawater note mixed with grapefruit, i still smell it all the way like that until it's gone. I think it's versatile, you can use it any time any season casually, for me it doesn't smell formal or sophesticated, and it can be used by both genders even if i think it suits men more than women. About projection and longivity, it project good, not beast or soft, longivity i get around 2 - 3 hours only. Not bad, i give it 7 of 10 .

I cant smell any oud on this one, but only a watery note with some vetiver and ginger. Nothing new on Aoud Forest. I did expect more. Smells like a less sweet version of Vetiver Des Sables. Not worth it in my opinion. Updated January 2014

Montale AOUD FOREST opens with a decidedly Pine Sol-y demeanor: citrusy, aromatic, and relatively loud, with a lot of evergreen trees creeping in shortly thereafter. What I interpret as brash may well seem merely bracing to others, but I don’t think that anyone can really deny that, at least at the outset, AOUD FOREST is far more masculine than feminine. As the citrus and aromatics begin to fade, a dry vetiver-like woody base shows its face, reminding me vaguely of some of the more masculine Bond no 9 unisex edps (MONTAUK, BLEECKER et al.), especially the ones with gentle leather in them. I’m not smelling much in the way of aoud here, but it’s becoming plain after a few cases that Montale wields aoud with a measured hand. Most of the “Aoud” perfumes I’ve tried from this line do not emphasize the note, though they include it in the name-—perhaps for marketing purposes or to justify the cost? I’m thinking that some of these should be renamed: FOREST (with a jot of aoud), ROSE PETALS (ditto), etc. I do find the smooth quasi-leather (would that be the ambergris?) vetiver drydown of AOUD FOREST rather likeable and something that I wouldn’t mind wearing in certain moods, but the Pine Sol opening is all-too-jolting for this tender nose. Désolée.

... Yet Aoud Forest sounded so enticing with "forest delight." The Aoud reaches me clearly - but from which tree does the resinous scent originate? Even my Mr. Forester is lost in this question - it seems to consist of phantom trees, as we both discover no greenery. The Aoud is also gnarled and dry - not a drop of seawater in sight. The addition of Forest is strangely chosen - at most, a barren forest after a dry spell comes to mind. There was no shortage of rosemary, which only makes the scent more unwieldy. A splash of lemon is merely a drop on a hot stone and fails to deliver the expected freshness. A resinous - spicy scent that reminds more of scruffy underbrush than a cozy woodland area. For me, the scent is too masculine - but even my husband graciously declines. This time we agree. Aoud Forest does not present itself as particularly inviting. In front of this ghost forest stands a rusty sign - with the inscription: No entry.

I must honestly admit that Montale is exerting an ever-growing fascination on me; just these beautiful, striking bottles reminiscent of "magic lamps" made from aluminum-like material brighten up my home fragrance shelf in a rather exotic way. So, of course, are the scents themselves: they are all a true homage to the Orient, more specifically to Saudi Arabia.

Aoud Forest is one of those Oud perfumes where Montale attempts to create a bridge. Essentially, it is a fragrance from a different scent direction, to which Oud is added. In Aoud Forest, everything is very green.

Not everywhere where Montale says 'Aoud' does this claim do justice to the content. After testing several fragrances from the Aoud collection, I must admit that a bit of, well, not resignation, but something like disillusionment has set in.

By now, I often have the feeling with Montale that the fragrances are "decoys." Why? Because time and again, what you expect or what the name promises is not actually there. I feel the same way about Montale Aoud Forest. Without letting myself be influenced by previous comments, I tested Aoud Forest and expected a fresh, green, and woody summer scent.

Earlier, I took a detour to my favorite perfumery in Bonn, searching for a subtle office and leisure scent. Not too sweet, not too floral, not powdery, rather earthy, woody, oriental with incense, vetiver, musk, and also a bit citrusy were my criteria. In the "mainstream corner," there wasn't much unfamiliar to discover, and no new finds revealed themselves.

Nu is a fragrance that I don't tend to hear much of. While it seems to have disappeared from most stores, there are a few select places that I know still stock it. I was lucky enough to try Nu, although I would have loved the opportunity to sample the EDP as well. Nu is quite a spicy and sharp fragrance at first. As it settles, the jasmine and iris tend to create a soft, loving bouquet, which is complimented by rather peppery cardamom. The overall blend has a somewhat smoky aroma. The composition has a bite to it. Nu is not a fragrance for the shy. There are so many dynamic ingredients that it's quite flabbergasting to find how beautifully balanced they all become on the skin. It's an incense-based fragrance, yes. However, the pepper and floral accords really give this fragrance that little something more. Up-close, Nu may tingle your nose a little. It has enough peppery-ness to make you want to sneeze. However from a distance, this fragrance is something special, despite being quite heady stuff. The longevity is really impressive, as is the sillage of course, as you may have gathered. Really a shock to think this is not something that YSL proudly sells anymore. I find Nu far more captivating than the patchouli-oriental, Elle. It's worth discovering.

Can there be scents that smell just like their color suggests? Or is that pure unconscious projection? I can't answer this self-imposed question with complete precision and scientific grounding. But I tend to lean towards the former. For the first time, I encountered the fragrance "NU" these days after an interesting swap, and before testing it, I had a certain intuition. The "fact of smelling" was able to confirm and support this intuition. It is as if one is smelling "liquid night." Perhaps it is the special coriander note, or maybe the white flowers that bloom in the evening, which shape the fragrance just as much as the strong balsamic touch from incense, myrrh, and woods (cedar?). But it is certainly the way the fragrance notes are combined. The smoky aspect makes "NU" very mysterious (aren't nights still like that??!!) The "indolic" power of the (not too sweet) flowers: Does it not remind one of late evenings, as they tend to smell particularly strong at that time of day??!! In this "fragrance type," I could lose myself, philosophize, reminisce, immerse myself in it, explore it..... It is deep, after all. And violet. Shimmering in all its shades from the deepest "lilac night blue" to the delicate stripe on the horizon in pastel violet. And "textile-like" from shimmering velvet to iridescent silk to coarse, cool linen. What images such a perfume can evoke is often only realized when one sniffs it while writing. At least, that’s how it is for me. And... a nice side effect: It can be incredibly soothing to reflect on it and put it into words. If it fits, even in the middle of the night :-))

The EdT from Nu (2001) has the same essence as the original fragrance. On my skin, however, it develops in all phases of the progression more subdued, more discreet, lighter, and with a softer base. Velvet dark blue instead of deepest night black. Here too, the predominant note is the cool, unsweet, slightly smoky woodiness, underlaid with a light, exotic floral scent, mysterious, elegant.... Juliane describes it wonderfully; there is nothing to add. In direct comparison to the EdP, this version is very suitable for everyday wear, wearable around the clock, for most occasions (except perhaps for sports, as it is simply too elegant for that). The longevity on my skin is half as long as the EdP, so still around 12 hours. Sillage is noticeable with closer contact or when a breeze passes by, but, in keeping with the theme of the fragrance, it is restrained. Like Nu (2001), it is a very special, an exceptional fragrance.

NU is just as clear and yet simultaneously mysterious as its name and the deep blue, heavy glass bottle. What does Nu stand for - the exciting new, sensual nudity, or a dark night? The strong, almost screaming bergamot note in the opening, paired with the herbal-green freshness of coriander, appears like bright shimmering reflections on cupro or black precious wood, before revealing smoky-floral ornaments. The comparably very slow fading of this strong top note feels like a curtain slowly drawing back or a rice paper screen, behind which we now see noble incense sticks flickering on a small black Japanese shrine at the floor of the mat-covered room, surrounded by white orchids. Meanwhile, the bergamot freshness remains in the background, and the arrangement is minimalist, so the scent impression is not warm and oriental-opulent, but rather East Asian cool, dry, and distant, like a starry summer night with a gentle breeze. Nu is therefore not fiery sexy like typical orientals, but rather coolly attractive, like an erotic game of closeness and distance, warm skin and dark wood. Thus, the fragrance suits women who also play with contrasts and who are surrounded by an aura of distance and minimalist elegance. Nu is the simple completely black look, silk shirt, and tight leather pants, the perfectly tailored deep dark blue jeans - making it suitable for any season. You just have to be a little bold. Because Nu is not sweet, but a true child of Tom Ford (back when he was Creative Director at YSL): strong and somehow different. Honestly, I wear it very rarely and then feel a bit "dressed up.

I used to think this was wayyyy too sweet - something along the lines of Pure Tonka - but I guess my nose must have evolved. The opening on paper doesn't do it justice - generic sugary thickness that we've all smelled a hundred times before. But unlike Pure Tonka which remains fairly linear, Ferragamo Uomo changes for the better. If you're thinking that you're going to get tiramisu right from the gate, you're wrong. Like most gourmands, you need to put it on warm skin and GIVE IT TIME. The notes open up after about an hour and the dessert feel starts to come through. Think cream filled pastry with a chocolate powder. A bit of orange gives it some character and the tonka bean fills out the rest. But despite the woody notes, it's not heavy. Instead, it's incredibly aromatic and can easily get cloying with more than 3-4 sprays, thanks to beastly longevity. I accidentally sprayed the back of my hat 2 weeks ago and my closet STILL smells of the stuff. And let me tell you, in MILD doses, it's simply wonderful. One of the biggest surprises I think is the persistence in quality over time - meaning that it degrades really well. Instead of the chemicals falling apart over time and smelling awful like with most cheap frags that use inferior fixatives, this one remarkably maintains nearly its entire fullness and balance throughout its duration - on clothes especially. So bonus points for that. Unfortunately, the projection on me isn't great - but like I said, it's probably better that way. You know - in mild doses, like all desserts. My guess is that people who hate on Uomo are like the old me - not giving it a fair shake, and at least a months' wearing. Oh well, maybe it's just not their thing. That's cool too. For me though, I'm looking forward to using up my decant so I can get a full bottle before they water it down. Now if you'll excuse me, all this talk is making me hungry. I'm getting a donut. Update: 2 years later, this has become my #1 compliment getter. I don't know WHAT I was thinking when I said the projection wasn't great - then again, I didn't have a full bottle then. Now I have 2 back up bottles. That's how much I appreciate it. Broken down, it's funny how much the base reminds me of Coach for Men, but dusted with a synthetic chocolate powder that just lasts and lasts. Performance is beyond stellar, and in the colder months, that's EXACTLY what I need - a fragrance that can dish out the goodness well into the frigid night. Warm dessert anybody? May the forks be with you.

Let me introduce you to the Tiramisù, a classic Italian dessert with Ladyfingers. The original recipe consists of egg, sugar, mascarpone cheese, Savoiardi biscuits (Ladyfinger), strong Moka coffee, a bit of Marsala liquor, and cocoa for dusting. That's it, and the final fantastic taste and smell are supposed to be the backbone of Uomo... Let's see. To start off, it is pretty evident that the bottle is remarkably similar to that of Lalique's new fragrance for men, L'Insoumis. Although they have different logos embossed on the two sides of the bottle, the concept is identical. nulltheless, the two scents have nothing in stock, and they are diverging from each other, Uomo is oriental-gourmand whereas L'Insoumis is woody-aromatic. Smelling Uomo on a card won't give you anywhere near an accurate idea of how it will smell on your skin. This is a gorgeous scent. Similarities to ZARA "Ganache Tonka" I feel but much smoother, more complex and far better I'd argue, with the plus of Tiramisù secret ingredient. Uomo is non-linear, yet it follows the familiar structure of spicy top notes, praline-like middle, and woody-ambery base. Uomo starts very strong, it opens with a blast of licorice-coffee-coconut like accord, blended with balsamic green cardamom, and spicy black pepper that kicks in a few minutes later. The velvety bergamot is just a hint, like a drop in the ocean, not dominating the opening. At first glance, the scent is overtly fresh, balsamic, and sweet but not cloying, indeed gourmand but not obnoxious. So far, so good, but... where is the dessert? Here it comes. The heart announces with a dominant accord of Tiramisù, so smooth and pleasant, the concoction of cocoa, coffee, Marsala, and vanillic-cream is crystal clear, supported and balanced with some other sweet notes, perhaps the soft touch of orange blossom. And then the dry down, the base is a kind of powdery cacao and roasted tonka bean vibe, yet blended with the creaminess of the blond woods, cashmere, and sandal to extend the sweet-vanillic aroma. Tonka here is a great choice, instead of overwhelming everything which came before with vanilla, the tonka picks up the coffee and cocoa transporting them to the final moments of Uomo. That said, Uomo is still pretty impressive, all things considered. Many seem to classify it as cloyingly sweet, but I regard it more as a delicious blend with more traditional aromatic masculine elements. The Tiramisù is front-and-center but doesn't dominate the fragrance nonetheless. The sweetness is paired with sharper details to start, and in the dry down, the experience becomes smoother, more relaxing. It's slightly spicier at the opening due to the cardamom and black pepper. They give way an hour later to the Tiramisù, and eventually to woods and tonka in the dry down. I admit I don't get much bergamot or orange blossom, just a hint --not really any citrus or floral contributions at all to this. It's mainly a sweet and woody composition to my nose, which is beautiful by me and unbelievable. On my skin, Uomo has 7-8 hour longevity and average sillage, which makes it suitable for work and several occasions. Its sweet, woody, sensual notes make me preferring it for fall-winter cold seasons, for a particular time, yet for leisure, party, and clubbing. Although the recommended target is young people, I do like it and don't find it inappropriate for middle-aged silvery foxes men like me. -Elysium

This one smells absolutely DELICIOUS!! I get a load of the Tiramisu vibe as it holds, and it leaves me wanting some coffee to wash it down. I personally think that it could easily be a unisex fragrance; especially during the opening. Not that it’s too feminine, it’s just something that could easily accent a woman’s beauty as well. The drydown is where it really shines in my opinion; such a rich and smooth tonka vibe. The longevity is good; an easy 6+ hours, and the sillage trail is nice, but not overwhelming. It projects a good 1-3ft bubble that lasts, but remember that it’s a gourmand vibe, so it’s not going to stand out as very “unique”. It’s a great cooler weather scent that would work well on a date or in a cuddling session. I’m happy with this one, as I love my sweeter scents.

Uomo by Ferragamo is sticky sweet like wearing a candy bar. The epitome of a 21st century modern fragrance. It really is sweet, like the tonka bean cashmere woods in the base line. It's nice and powdery fresh like a buffet at a high end casino. If i play the slots and win thousands of dollars I'd run out and buy a few bottles of the stuff. The bottle is cool looking with a nice brownish tan color that reminds me of a coffee house somewhere in New York City. Cardamom Black Pepper and the ever present Bergamot blast off in the opening and i only get hungrier from then on. 7hrs of longevity is nice but i wished it gave me a few more on the skin. All and all this is a nice offering from 2016, and I'm usually not this kind to modern fragrances because i think modern perfumerie is lazy that makes different fragrances that smell similar. This one is nice i don't regret buying it. Can be found in almost any store so i suggest you to give it a try. Uomo by Ferragamo is a winner that comes in like a smorgasbord and leaves me feeling full. The End

This stuff (to me) smells like a hotel breakfast in Italy. Really does kinda take me be back there. You can smell the freshly washed sheets, a long with coffee being brewed. Really does give a care free Italian feel. For the price 8.5 I got mine off notino for 25€ for 30ml. Thats a hard price to beat.

GEEEEZUS! I wish my future wife smells like this. Straight beautiful sweet gourmand fragrance. Shocked that this scent is made for men. I got looks at work and comments on the train. It brightens my day. I used four sprays; one on both wrist, on my neck and work shirt. It's a gentle beast, that wants your attention like a cute puppy.
This was much-hyped on release, particularly in the youtube fragrancesphere, but after spending more time with it and waiting for the hype to die down, does it still stack up?

I tried Ferragamo Uomo once and it didn't generate much for me, then I got a very good offer and decided to have it so I could try it in more detail. I think it can be easy to like, but particularly the sweet and gourmand ones are not my favorites, so from that place I give my opinion. The exit seemed very difficult to me, but very difficult.

A synthetic fall and winter gourmand fragrance that manages to stand out from the crowd with a tiramisu twist. Not groundbreaking or mindblowing by any means, but it has decent performance and nets great compliments. People love this one.

Yes, it does happen sometimes. The moment when a fragrance hits you so (positively) hard on the first sniff that you can't really "process" and absorb the sensory impressions and scent notes. "Uomo" is such a fragrance for me. I can't remember the last time I was so overwhelmed and surprised by a scent.

I will start saying that I like very much the Montale/Mancera concept : strong, complex fragrances at affordable prices. Aqua Palma is a freshie with peach note and also some understated citruses, it will not choke you from the first sprays but it will be very long lasting, with a decent silage, great for summer and those sunny days in which you want to smell nice and fresh. The price of 120€ for 100ml is very good in my opinion and you get a good quality in return, in a perfume that does what says on the tin (haha, this time really is tin): Smells like a day near the Aqua (Sea) maybe on the island of Palma (de Mallorca). For more details, please watch my video from below. Thank you !

It was one of my earlier perfumes, but I thought it was great back then and still do today. It's a matter of taste what one thinks of it, because not everyone wants such a summer scent, but I actually find it really great because I really like these fruity notes. I don't think this is really a fragrance to lie on the beach or sit in a bar, but for a relaxed sunny day outdoors, I definitely think it stands out, and I would also say that people notice it. So my conclusion is that you can buy it, but it's not a must.

From the name Aqua Palma, I would imagine something different.. the feeling of vacation, sun, and beach doesn't really come to me here; I see it more in a German summer or in the office. Nevertheless, it's a super "simple" scent, which is by no means meant negatively, and a pleasant fragrance with great longevity. A bit sweet and fruity, but still rather masculine. I would not describe it as a particularly citrusy scent.

I was an average student - accustomed to the standard math grade of five. What bothered me much more was that I wasn't chosen for the school choir. No, I really didn't inherit my mom's beautiful singing voice. But she passed on her musicality to me. So, as the choir reject, I was always chosen to play the piano at festivities in the auditorium. For this purpose, I liked to dress up - a dress in old rose, knee-length, would do just fine. My parents were happy that my usual flashy school clothes stayed in the closet for once. And Aqua Palma would have matched this subtly festive outfit well. This positive tingling before the performance is also well reflected in the fragrance. It is cheerful with the sparkling peach and festive with the tuberose. The scent has something buoyant - just like I presented my music. Also to the goodwill of my math teacher, who otherwise didn't have such a relaxed time with me. Everything in its time. Music: Rondo alla Turca by Mozart

If you find original Opium intriguing but intimidating, this might be the version for you. It seems to remain true to the original notes and composition, with the same strong projection and longevity, but is simply much lighter and less aggressive.

I own several Opium variants, and I like them all, but Orchidee de Chine is my favorite. It reminds me of long nights when I wore my silver Chinese dress, which fit like it was painted on. Along with the spicy scent of de Chine. That was a performance! I met my friend in a club in that outfit, and she still raved about it. She just had to approach me. I seemed to her like Miss Shanghai herself - such were her animated words. And then there was that special exotic scent that spoke of distant gardens. Pink orchids - with which the dress was also embroidered. Enchanting. Exactly our taste. The charming dress no longer fits me, and unfortunately, my dear friend is no longer with us. But now and then, I treat myself to this unique scent and look back into the past.

This smells like an overly sour copy of Layton Exclusif. When you smell Signature by itself you can convince yourself that it's OK, but if you compare it with Layton Exclusif the similarity and the difference becomes pretty obvious. Signature has a cloying, artificial and even sickly sour note, which spoils the scent for me. The sourness is coming from cardamom, which I don't like, and orange. For those who don't know Layton Exclusif, the base in Signature is bold and rough, like the bottle, yet warm, maybe even sweetish. It is warm and spicy, but not in an aggressive way. The top reminds me of Valentino Uomo and Pasha de Cartier Parfum. In all three the top is mediocre, and Signature has the best ratio of top to base. Of the three, Signature wins just because the base is good and relatively strong.  of my perfume reviews at The Scent Stories: thescentstories.substack.com

Salvatore had to be a fan of coffee & the sweet kind like a cappuccino or a French vanilla blend.... . This fragrance, sweet & spicy, yet slight dab of citrus that I think makes it, a bit sticky. It is quite pleasant even at first smell, not synthetic, considering the price you'd think it would be a little bit. The manderine orange & pink pepper blend well with the sweetness in the Tonka bean, cinnamon & coffee. You get hints of all this at first, It's even a bit fresh behind it all. . This is a scent you could def wear to work if you don't spray too much because it may not sit tooo heavy on the skin, it'll definitely last on the cloths. At least that's how it is for me, but I would mainly save it for night time. It could absolutely be a fragrance you start to wear anytime you go out during a date, adventure out with the fellas & it does lean more masculine. . The dry down is more leathery-sweet but still doesn't fall too far from when you first smelled it. I can see some people thinkin this is a slightly "cheap" smelling fragrance because of how sweet it tends to be but in the air, all that goes out the window. It just takes a certain nose to point that out. . Salvatore fa un buon lavoro

…but it’s not as “loud” as they portray it to be. Honestly, none of the Ferragamo’s perform very “loudly” in any facet of the word. Sillage, projection, and longevity are all the same, pretty much always. A 1-3ft bubble that goes for maybe 6 hours, and lingers nicely, but not laying any trails that point to the wearer. They’re great, don’t get me wrong, I love all the Ferragamo's I own, they’re just not the “beasts” that a lot of YouTube reviewers claim them to be. Now back to the main point, the SCENT itself. I was intrigued by this because a lot of the hype was mentioning “a coffee note that makes this different then the tiramisu based original”. Nope. It smells VERY similar to the original, but it’s dialed back a little in sweetness. Nothing “jumps out” at you that makes it absolutely different. You can absolutely tell that the scents are related, and less enthusiastic noses won’t be able to tell at all. Don’t get me wrong. It smells VERY good. Sweet, soft, and dark. A very good date night scent. 100% worthy of the prices you can find it at on FragranceNet. Does it PERFORM like they say it does? Nope, not on my skin anyway.

This UOMO is well-done. A strong, heavy, sexy and mysterious fragrence for the night. A bold kind of sexii that speaks for you. This can be worn dressed down or dressed up. I love mixing it with the UOMO edt. On my mama I be feeling like than man when I walk through. Rich Hommie Quan aint nuffin on ya boi on that walk-through when wear this Signature scent, yo. Hood Im on. Wipe me dyyyyyyynnnnn!

I love it! It is difficult for a flanker to surpass its mother fragrance, but, from time to time, the light is made, and these “rare avis” appear, which surpass everything that is expected of them. In general, it has the DNA of the mother line, but it shows that they have taken care to mature it, adding, as some colleagues say, a much darker and less sweet base, which makes it more mature and elegant, leaving the Uomo original as something more informal and casual, and this new Uomo Signature as something more formal, but with a rather rogue air, something like ... a young executive dressed and elegant, very formal and polite, but when he comes home and he relax, dress casually and go with friends to have beers ... At the beginning, citrus fruits are clearly noticed, but they are immediately overshadowed by a sweet blanket of coffee, leather, cinnamon and tonka, an exotic elixir, elegant and sweet, although, somewhat less sweet than its original version, but still a sweet teddy. From here, the aroma develops little, except for a progressive reduction of the initial sweetness and an accentuation of the patchouli in the final drying, but, for the rest, little more change. The sweet notes are very well contained by the leather, by the fresh and dirty nuances of the cardamom and by the balsamic freshness of the cypress, creating a quite harmonious and pleasant set, personally I love it, it is not the perfuming panacea, but it exceeds with its task. The performance is quite good, staying in your skin 8 or 9 hours without problems, with a fairly noticeable wake in the first hours, then down a bit, and although it is not as flashy as at the beginning, it still feels without problems, so, in this aspect, meets what is expected. I see it as an aroma of cold and temperate times, and because of its dark, more night-oriented vibe, although, as I always say, this is very subjective and personal, and everyone will use it when they feel like it. The truth is that I liked it a lot and it surprised me for good, a well-made and necessary flanker on the line, bringing a little more maturity and elegance to the jovial informality of the original Uomo. Your test is highly recommended.

I got it for a tester. Nice fresh opening with grapefruit, mandarin, pink pepper. Projection is a little underwhelming; I reapplied two sprays one hour after an initial 4 sprays because I couldn’t smell much anymore. A little later the base of tonka bean comes to the fore. The dry down is more woodsy, I don’t get much Cypress or coffee. Lovely fragrance.

Fragrantica rating: 4.33/5 Warm spicy, coffee, aromatic, leathery, sweet. Such a perfectly balanced mix of strong ingredients. Spices mixed with roasted coffee beans in a sweet leathery base. Before getting this, I tested Halloween man X too but contrary to popular belief, I found them miles apart. It wasn't hard for me to pick uomo signature over it.

This is one of those perfume that grew on me, quite a lot. Uomo Signature starts spicy and one can right away feel the kick of pepper. I do not catch a heavy coffee note, to me leather and tonka is more prominent in the dry down. To my nose, this is a great evening-out fragrance, something that can also be born in a loud, crowded environment.

"We ain't goin' nowhere, we ain't goin' nowhere We can't be stopped now, cos it's Bad Boy for life We ain't goin' nowhere, we ain't goin' nowhere We can't be stopped now, cos it's Bad Boy for life" Oh yes, these lyrics remind me of my youth and the accompanying hip-hop phase.
A perfumer who has designed sillage bombs like Oxygene by Lanvin or M7 Oud Absolue, and later many Armani fragrances for the Coty company and for Euroitalia the Blue Dylan, has achieved quite a lot.

Not a new melody at all, but a pleasant one. A fine balance between deep aoud notes, leathery warmth and oriental spices (saffron, clove). This well-known Montale-tune is amplified by notes of Egyptian jasmine and a faint rose in the background, but the accent is clearly on the spices, the leather and the aoud. A touch of cedarwood, sandalwood and amber was added in the drydown, but I can't say that "Melody" is ultra-strong. Is it only me or would others also say that the staying-power of many Montale fragrances has become less remarkable? "Melody" offers medium longevity (4hs on my skin). Since my sample has to be dabbed on, I can't tell you much about the sillage, because I only applied some drops of the perfume onto my wrist. Nevertheless, "Melody" doesn't seem to be a sillage-monster like "Black Aoud" or "Sweet Oriental Dream". It's a scent I'd recommend to everybody who is looking for a seasonless aoud-fragrance which is neither too pungent nor too heavy. The ideal choice for people who still need to discover if the specific "Montale-sytle", this Europeanized kind of orientalism, agrees with them or not.

Once a pioneer of the Oud wave, Montale has for years ensured the return of the same old thing. Recently, this brand has bewildered with far too loud, extravagant experiments. But the latest fragrances are worth a look again! In Aoud Melody, Montale shows that Oud can also be used quite subtly, and only as a top note. Here, we encounter a noticeable hint of what Montale stands for: rainforest-friendly Oud, for which hopefully no tree had to be cut down - but pleasantly fragrant, elegantly crafted, and better than some of the questionable bases found elsewhere. The rather restrained Oud opening sits in a fruity, floral, and spicy environment that is exceptionally harmoniously composed. Normally strong spices like saffron and clove contribute their character only very gently. For me, this is the concept of an Arabic Mukhallats (blend), where notes from all directions are woven together. Thus, it is not easy to want to read something from the fragrance notes. All I want to say is that friendly, fruity impressions of scent emerge here. Through its warmth, Aoud Melody wins the wearer over. We have here a pleasant feel-good scent, something one would like to have around in a familiar environment. I sense a beauty here that opens the heart. Aoud Melody never imposes itself when worn - its possible facets come and go, and nothing that this fragrance can gift us can be forced. This is where the tension and liveliness lie. When wearing, Aoud Melody is not simply present - one must listen to it, register what comes and goes when. The well-known temporal sequence of a fragrance pyramid falls short here. It must be taken into account that the various components of the fragrance exhibit different strengths and projections at different times. This is met by a wearer whose perception of the scent throughout a day with Aoud Melody fluctuates between very sensitive and accustomed. Thus, a hardly predictable, lively interplay of perceived facets arises, the sequence of which can be a little different every day and can only be imperfectly captured with the pyramid scheme. Despite its captivating nature, Aoud Melody is a demanding fragrance, certainly not for beginners. The keyword is: projection. Anyone who sniffs directly on the sprayed hand in perfumery effectively blocks access. Because there, one smells a seemingly uninspired jumble that can overwhelm the nose and temporarily blind it. Over hours, different facets appear again and again. The saffron-Oud component seems to have completely disappeared at times, only to cautiously re-enter. Then again, everything is very powdery and empty, and one believes to be at the end of the development, yet perhaps warmth and fruitiness return once more. Aspects of an intimate skin scent seem to emerge. The highlight of the fragrance experience for me are moments when Oud and spiciness completely recede and a creamy-fruity note appears briefly, reminiscent of tangerines with cream, Grand Marnier, or even papaya. It resembles the beautifully creamy tangerine from Frapin's Passion Boisée. I believe Aoud Melody is, to a greater extent than usual, a fragrance in which everyone can find something different. I would love to read other opinions about it.

How I love the "left-hand-right-hand battles:)!!! Today, "Oud" by Maison Kurkdjian and "Aoud Melody" are going head to head! Thanks to Aunt Lilly (one of the warmest, most patient, and generous people here on Parfumo!), I got a sample of Aoud Melody... also because she rediscovered a lot of "Oud" from MFK in this fragrance, which is currently my absolute holy grail. Mille Grazie a Vienna:-)! Yesterday in the "stand-alone test," it was a 99% twin to "Oud" for me...almost identical! Today in direct comparison, you can pick out tiny nuances. AM starts off a tad less sweet in direct comparison...the saffron is a touch less sweet than in "Oud," to be precise. But still a 98.9% twin...the same dreamy note...the same beautiful creaminess and melt as in Kurkdjian's Beau. I could use the same words as in my Oud comment...they would all apply 1:1. In a blind test, I would have no...not a chance at all to separate the two. It's basically like "Red Vetiver" to "Terre d'Hermes"...you "know" immediately which fragrance you have in front of you, yet it is a bit different without knowing exactly what is different. With Red Vetiver, it's the slightly lower (grape) fruitiness...here it's the lower sweetness...somewhat like vanilla to tonka...subtle...but recognizable. I can't detect the usual Montale touch (overloaded and a bit too much of everything) here...and that is not(!) to its disadvantage. The same dreamy and delightful balance...the same unforgettable fragrance experience! Apicius writes in his Oud comment that "Oud" smells like a luxurious body lotion, and he is not entirely wrong...that's what I mean by creaminess and melt; I got the "Oud" body lotion (I'm addicted to the scent...I admit it;-)) about 2-3 weeks ago...you can still notice the small differences there...the lotion is a bit warmer and smoother, which of course is not completely surprising for a cream;-)! Therefore, I agree with what he wrote...lotion and fragrance together create a dream. AM is a bit "brighter" and at times seems a bit more complex to me...also because it takes a small development...which I couldn't detect in "Oud"...but I don't really care. However, AM does have a little surprise...no, it's not the usually expected monster longevity from Montale and expansive sillage...it is just as stylish as its twin...but after 3-4 hours when "Oud" is at its creamiest, AM even becomes a touch fresher...with an even smaller bitterness...especially in the base note, that is of course not to be expected! That is another super beautiful nuance that enriches the fragrance! I do have 2 comments though. Since both fragrances from Montale were released after their twins, one might think of blatant copying...I'll leave that open. My second comment is that it is impossible that the same Parfumos could have tested both fragrances...otherwise, such a blatant difference in ratings would not arise...it is too large for me! However, from my own experience, I can well imagine that many are annoyed by the almost monthly "Montale Oud" (i.e., a new Oud fragrance every month) and that the image has suffered somewhat due to the flooding with these fragrances. For me, MFK also has a small bonus...due to the exclusivity and the noble presentation. At least, that's my feeling. Longevity is, like with "Oud," easily over 6 hours with a similar subtle but still well-perceivable sillage. T H E big plus of AM is definitely the price, 100ml/139€ online compared to 70ml/165-206€...that is quite a significant difference. I love both equally...and they have both (inevitably) replaced Gris Montaigne as my holy grail...albeit narrowly. What two fabulous fragrances...2x thanks to France and 1x to Austria with a kiss:-)!

Well, it's not that boring after all. But anyone who carries a positive allusion to music in their name sets high expectations. Unfortunately, these are not met here, even though many commentators praise this Montale composition in almost the highest tones. Speaking of composition: I actually only perceive two fragrance notes that set the tone here. One is, as the name suggests, Oud, and the second is Rose. The former comes across as extremely softened, while the latter cannot hide, in contrast to the agarwood, that it is of artificial nature or rather naturally artificial, so it really comes off as quite synthetic. This is a problem that many perfume enthusiasts feel with quite a few Montale fragrances. In 2014, these Oud-Rose duets may still have been quite original, but by now they have almost become overexposed. Truly outstanding creations are those that venture more into the dark and mysterious direction, such as Santal Royal by Guerlain, which also made its debut in the world of perfumery that same year. That EdP plays almost the same tune with a few different fragrance notes, but it comes off as much more complex, mystical, profound, sensual, and also of much higher quality. Almost a small symphony orchestra. I wouldn't say that Aoud Melody, in contrast, sounds like a fairground tune, but rather like a kitschy pop song. At least this damned rose brings me to that comparison. Some elemiharz, saffron, jasmine, and ylang-ylang also mix in, but they are so quiet on their own that you can only perceive them faintly. Therefore, Aoud Melody cannot really convince me - at least not in this quality. At least it doesn't cause olfactory tinnitus.

Aoud Melody intrigued me primarily because of its supposed similarity to the MFK Oud. I remember that one as a beautiful clean and creamy scent, but somehow the price asked for it has always seemed too much to me. Now, it has been a while since I had the MFK under my nose. So I can't make a direct comparison like DaveG. However, back then I perceived the Kurkdjian quite differently, even if that might be due to a changed perception of scents. AM starts for me with a quite pronounced saffron-oud combination. It is somewhat medicinal and typical, but is balanced out by a lot of sweetness and creaminess. As I recall, I was less able to pick out individual notes in the MFK, which I found very pleasant. Neither the oud nor the saffron were that dominant or had such a pronounced sweetness; I mainly experienced it as round and creamy back then. However, due to my faded memory, I must evaluate the Montale on its own and I am somewhat torn. It is a beautiful scent, you definitely smell good with it, but somehow everything feels a bit loveless to me. The sweetness is too scratchy, the saffron too dominant, and the very pronounced sandalwood note smells somewhat muddy-plastic. Somehow, the fragrance notes seem somewhat unharmoniously coordinated to me, as if not enough time was spent on the scent. The scent aura, the big picture, smells quite good with AM. I can well imagine that one receives compliments for the scent and that it is quite easy to wear for the wearer. So if it should be something cheaper for everyday use, then AM might be a good choice; certainly a nice scent. But for special occasions, I envision something different.

Aoud Melody evokes in me the image of a domina or a seasoned man. It is a spicy oriental with a strong opening. I smell Aoud, leather, saffron, clove... And after about 90 minutes, it transforms into a soft, lovingly cuddly amber kitten, tomcat. Amber now carries the scent, with a woody undertone. A beautiful fragrance, almost tender. I just didn't perceive the floral notes.

Opens with a beautiful aquatic accord surrounded by a great and well balanced ginger note with a touch of violet and then... nothing. It does smell GREAT in the opening, but it does not last more than 30 minutes in the skin. I wish the ginger note with the aquatic one lasted more, that's why it let me down. If this fragrance lasted more it'd be one of the best summer scents easily. Revised January 2014

From the now extensive L'Homme line by YSL, which could easily fill a football team, I have tested quite a few, but only the original and of course La Nuit are truly noteworthy and really good. And since there was no decent tester of the new, utterly unnecessary sport flanker at the airport, I spontaneously sprayed the Cologne Gingembre on the back of my hand, as I had only seen this live at airports until now. Cologne Gingembre could be unkindly described as a diluted original, with a delicate ginger note resting on a beautiful citrus base. So far, so good. A pleasant scent. But unfortunately, you have to get so close that after 10 minutes you have to concentrate so intensely to perceive the fragrance, which is a rare experience. If it were about three times as strong, it would still be suitable for summer and highly recommendable. Some found L'Homme too sweet, a bit too heavy; they might want to give this more watery, bright, partially metallic alternative a sniff. But such a weak scent is actually too little even for those who prefer to hold back and rely on understatement. This is more of a non-statement than understatement. Good fragrance, but they simply hit the brakes too hard, causing the entire vehicle's engine to burst after just a few minutes. Bottle: very heavy, high-quality, icy, and magnificent as always. Sillage: even less than an average EdC Longevity: 2-3 hours is a joke without a punchline, which is only surpassed by the sillage. Even for die-hard L'Homme fans - this one is simply too quiet and harmless to be called a perfume, scent, or EdC. I still prefer the original in a well-measured dose during summer!

I had already briefly touched on the theme of the fragrance industry regarding so-called "Sport," "Aqua," and "Cologne" variants - in my opinion, simply a marketing gimmick. I see the same with the new L'Homme Cologne Gingembre. The addition of "Gingembre," which is French for "ginger," is completely unnecessary here. Aside from citrus notes, I hardly perceive anything else, or in my view, it is a "lighter" version of the original. Therefore, just "Cologne" would have sufficed ;) Anyone who knows and appreciates the original should stick with it, as the longevity is significantly better! The Cologne Gingembre is hardly recognizable to me after 2 hours.

Hello everyone, today I would like to say a few words about L'Homme Cologne Gingembre and indirectly issue a warning. I know there are many who love the fragrance direction of the old La Nuit de L'Homme Eau de Toilette and some almost worship it. That's one thing. On the other hand, I am not a fan of 321 flankers^^(fictitious number), but with this one... phew, you really have to want it. Why? From a collector's perspective, you can take it, BUT if a "Real Cologne (Eau de Cologne) | 4711" or almost any Mexx, Bruno Bannani or, for example, Calvin Klein, Playboy scent, etc. performs better (meaning drugstore fragrances), then I really QUESTION whether you need this? Is it worth it?... You can say 1, 2, 17 words about the performance, but if it is truly - really not present, then that is quite a piece..., in the sense of spraying it on..."here I am, here! and gone..." no joke... I recommend for those who want to use it... - better leave it and invest your good money in something GOOD instead... And now have a nice day/evening or whenever you read this review, best regards, Benny _______

Scented greetings to the community, this is my first review of a fragrance on this site, so please don't be too harsh with my virgin words ;). Shortly after inhalation, several thoughts rush into my mind. First of all, I must say that this EDC smells very familiar and fresh. I definitely perceive the aquatic notes and bergamot. Only the ginger, which is so prominently advertised on the bottle, remains a mystery to my nose. (Maybe it's also because my little nose isn't very refined yet, who knows) However, the durability/sillage and thus the price/performance level (This fragrance apparently is no longer available, yet the internet keeps throwing up prices between 100-150 Euros) are abysmal. As soon as the fragrance is sprayed on, it only delights my olfactory receptors for a vanishingly short time. That's too little for an EDC, even for me. In conclusion, I can say that this fragrance was a nice find in my old cabinets, albeit not much more than that. Cheers!

This is one of those that causes my déja-vue reflex to spin out of hand. But that's one of the best of all signs for a perfume. It's almost tautological to say so, as the °frenzy° of deja-vue ^is^ the wonderful olfactory sensation, not merely a ^is a token^ of it. There are quite a few perfumes that do this; but not ^all^ the perfumes I deem excellent 'fumes do so. It is a ^sufficient^ condition of a 'fume being excellent, but not a ^necessary^ one - to use strict logic. And when I say ~déja-vue~ I do mean a kind of ^abstract^ déja vue, in which none (or none but one or two) of the threads actually terminate on any specific recollection, either real or fabulous. I have heard it said that this is not an orangey fragrance. I would ^somewhat^ disagree with that. There is an accord in it that I would call 'evocative' of orange: it is probably a synergy of the oudy note & the bergamot, at least primarily. It is a ^fairly^ complex fragrance, looking at the notes list, and beautifully composed - the notes fitting together like the blocks of which the walls of temple at Karnak are built. And it is ethereal, in that it seems to shimmer around one; and yet, a tad skanky - the skankiness & the ethereality complementing rather than conflicting - a sign of the well-use of the oud note. In the whole, I am ^extremely^ pleased with this what was in fact a °blind purchase° - one of those bull's-eye or triple-twenty scores (or the preferred analogy).

A perfume, as Leimbacher already says - quiet/calm/soft! I perceive it as a pleasant oud scent that does not weigh heavily on the chest but instead gently wraps around the wearer. Soft touches of fruit that settle on the skin, mild spices, planed wood that has been dried by the sun, and a few accords of violet. All well combined with oud. It becomes somewhat leathery over time, although the leather remains quite in the background and does not exhibit a harsh character. The perfume shows no strengths. It is not powerful, but soft, marked by elegance and beauty. The beauty of silence. Sometimes silence is also golden. That could fit Orange Aoud perfectly. I find it well done. I feel comfortable with this quiet scent from Montale. I just wish for more longevity. It lasts a mere four hours on me, and then that's it. What a pity. To enjoy it longer, to let the fruits kiss me longer, and to stay longer in its aura, which exudes a certain silence. It all feels as if one has been encased in a bubble. Lonely. Calm. If you shake it, flakes fall upon you. No snow. Just grains of desert sand. However, it does not come across as dusty at all. Orange Aoud is the silence around you. It slowly devours you. It caresses you with its soft character and invigorates you with its spice. Thanks to a dear perfuma from the swap game who sent me this scent.

And I quite like I T!!! Through a lovely perfumer, I came across a leftover bottle of Orange Aoud. One of the few bottles that has stuck in my memory from short tests at Breuninger. With Orange Aoud (as with Aoud Melody), Montale shows a calmer, more subtle side.. yes, one could almost say mild and soft! A fruity, zesty top note of bergamot, orange, and mandarin mixed with soft oud can be immediately appealing and requires no acclimatization period. There’s no pinching, poking, biting, or creaking here.. everything is in the "flow".. a rather soft and sensitive scent that suits calm moments very well. The very soft leather reveals itself to me quite late and also very subtly. Scents that contain leather usually get an immediate "zonk" from me, with the exception of Chambre Noire and this orange beauty. But it also has that slightly piercing-synthetic quality typical of Montale, which has never bothered me, except for very few exceptions. The creaminess from the heart note makes up for a lot! Over the further wear time, it develops gradually into a more masculine scent, especially in the base later on. Here, the herbaceous-spicy leather note becomes noticeable, while its slight fruitiness remains until the end. One of the very few, if not the only Montale fragrance that features or mentions oak moss. Unfortunately, the base comes a bit (too) early, which is atypical for Montale; after 4 hours, it’s nearly over, leaving only pleasantly scented remnants. Orange Aoud is already skin-close after 90 minutes, making the 100ml worthwhile. Whether I will repurchase it soon when the 10-15ml is used up, I do not know yet! Especially since I have sworn to myself that only scents that absolutely "wow" me may remain in my collection. This one is great, and a test is worth it, but it doesn’t quite reach much more for me (anymore), as Aoud Melody offers more and more beautiful aspects in every respect. This scent is very well suited for oud or Montale beginners and fits very well into the current season.

The good thing about private perfumeries and one of their biggest advantages is that most salespeople have absolutely no problem making a small decant when there are no samples available for a new release. Such was the case with Orange Aoud, which, along with Aoud Melody, marks the first Montale double pack this year. An orangey citrus scent with oud as a main factor - I couldn't think of any significant competition. Therefore, I was quite curious about Orange Aoud, which left its new release sibling far behind at first impression. This led me to take its decant and set Melody aside for the time being. But both seemed better to me than their current miserable rating here. There seems to be quite a bit of frustration and anger building up over the ever-new, similar Oud Montales. Nevertheless, one shouldn't dismiss OA too prejudicially, as it definitely has its soft, beautiful sides. For example, it starts off super relaxed and creamy with a citrusy oud, in which I could bathe. The beginning is different and dreamily beautiful. Also completely different from the usual heavy-handed style of the brand. But that was already the highlight of the perfume, which from then on only declines further and never finds its way back. Especially the completely poor sandalwood base is a nuisance and one of the few examples where a scent just keeps getting worse. The minimally present rose, which Montale probably can never completely forgo, combined with saffron and chocolatey patchouli, can't save it anymore. Bottle: the gentle orange tone fits well with the scent. Longevity: 4-5 hours is a disappointment. Can't say it any other way. Sillage: the quietest Montale scent I have ever smelled. Little orange, gentle oud, a lot of restraint, pleasant creamy feeling - Montale is on a different path, which could do the company good and connect the familiar with the new. However, there are still some rough edges.

Montale - is it too strong, am I too weak, or am I too strong and the scent too weak I wear Orange Aoud and would have wished for a powerhouse scent, in true Montale style. Because I find the expression of OA so wonderful. But far from it. Delicate, chypre, and really naturally citrusy. On me, the scent is rather quiet from the start, almost delicate. I have the intense tiare from Montale and that scent is so strong that I can't wear it all the time. And if I understood the literature correctly, Montale approached AO and designed the scent to remain extra quiet and delicate. But I feel it's a topsy-turvy world. Intense tiare is so loud that I have to be careful not to be told off for too much coconut vanilla... and AO is so delicate that I constantly feel the need to reapply. A dream of a scent, but the longevity is rather short, considering that I can smell it without having to stick my nose in it. Max. 5 hours I give it with goodwill. In conclusion, super scent, delicately creamy genius, but I am probably too strong for it or it is too weak for me. But I will wear it anyway. Only here do I finally know why it is 100 ml. You need to use it up quickly. The bottles from Montale are rather uninspired. But orange looks very good on the metal deo containers. The natural scent direction of citrus fruits paired with musk, involving leather and woody notes, is impressive. Clear recommendation to test.

October 2022 - I go to my personal perfume god because I need something new. My nose is used to my two autumn and winter fragrances. Ideally, I want to top what I have, but I also know that this will be very difficult; I really like my two for the cold season... I take my time in this beautiful store.

A completely normal day in Parfumoternia. Bald Man, also known as Prince Bastian, had recently successfully repelled the wild Soukhorde and was now dedicating himself to testing YSL Wild Leather, Yves Semi-Leather. As a prince, he always wore his blonde wig, which is why he was also called Blondie. Actually, that’s what his friends called him. So he boldly sprayed the fragrance on, already tinkering with a comment full of esprit and wordplay. But suddenly he heard the voice of the sorceress, who was the only one to know his secret: “Bald Man, we need you! The dark forces are breaking through the fortress, the World Stone is in danger!” “Alright, Gandixeress, I’m on my way!” So he hurried to his tiger (actually a chicken) and spoke the magic formula: “By the power of Baldhead, I have the hair tonic!” And off he went, his steed or rather his oversized giant chicken, Battle Polly, took off. In the process, he became aware of the scent of the perfume. At first, leather emerged, which was slightly sweet, Bald Man thought of something like licorice. Soon vanilla joined in, adding a new facet to the leather, softening it while not making it too gourmand and sweet. Rather, the scent was balanced, the leather rich and present while still smelling moderately. Alongside the licorice came a woody note, rather delicate and also sweet, the guaiac wood intensified this side of Wild Leather. As Bald Man rode and pondered, his wig flew away due to the strong wind. Annoying. Arriving bald at the castle, he immediately grabbed his hair tonic, poured it generously on his head, and charged with a wild battle cry at the fiends who wanted to invade the castle. Meanwhile, Gandixeress conjured up buckets of scents with a skunk accord to fend off the opponents. In any case - to fast forward a bit - in the end, only Bald Man and his antagonist, a man with full, long hair, faced each other. Bald Man attacked, slipped on his somehow scattered wig, and accidentally poured the hair tonic on the unnamed antagonist, who immediately transformed into a gigantic hair tuft formation. “And of course, nothing grows on my plate...,” grumbled Bald Man. So he and the sorceress once again defeated the enemies. Battle Polly was meanwhile sniffing at now again Prince Bastian and Wild Leather. She noticed that the scent had almost disappeared and turned into a mushy potpourri. Very pleasant, now more like freshly treated suede, with a slightly bitter leg note. Jokes aside, Wild Leather is not wild but quite the opposite, the scent is tamed. This is absolutely fine because here we have the rarely functioning attempt to make leather more appealing and accessible to a broader audience. Vanilla and similar companions were incorporated thoughtfully, the leather does not drown in it. So: YSL - Wild Leather is a good entry-level fragrance when it comes to leather. It is also suitable for fans of moderate leather scents. Thanks to Gandixeress and Bald Man aka Prince Bastian.

Wild Leather is the new fragrance from the Le Vestiaire series by YSL. What have they hung in the wardrobe for us this time, after we had to wait a long time for its release: Wild Leather or Suede? Because suede doesn’t necessarily have to be wild. Everyone has their associations. For me, they are often the suede men's blousons from the 1990s. Stubborn wearers still sport them today. One looked and still looks quite well-dressed in them. Otherwise, there are shoes, bags, gloves, upholstered furniture. However, the name likely does not refer to suede, which in English is more commonly referred to as suede or velour. It is supposed to be wild leather. Or is it not? The fragrance pyramid indicates suede. Also black leather. Although with my eyes closed, I probably couldn't smell a difference between a black and a brown leather jacket. To make it short: it is not wild or even wicked leather. It is a soft, yet noble leather. It even starts a bit fresh-peppery with a bouquet of flowers. Clearly unisex. The accompanying leather note is not dominant; it blends in, and thus the overall impression leans more towards a fine handbag, briefcase, or leather gloves that come from a department store where the leather goods section is right next to the perfumery. It is not the leather smell of a new school backpack, and the leather does not come fresh from the tannery. It has taken on a fine hint of flowers and spices, yes, I would even say a hint of luxury, without being ostentatious. I see, or rather: smell this fragrance on ladies and gentlemen, not particularly on the younger ones. For me, it could have been a bit rougher. Ah, the listed licorice note does not reveal itself to me. At times, I quite like the combination of licorice and leather. The longevity and sillage are enormous, and the scent lingers even a day later in the shirt. Would I wear it in summer - probably not. Maybe on a cool summer evening when the citrus cologne or the aquatics worn during the day has long given up the ghost. Wild Leather is nothing new or unusual, and in terms of price, you can often find comparable fragrances for less. But it fits well into Le Vestiaire - into the wardrobe of men and women who appreciate quality.

Aoud Safran is just okay. Nothing new neither unique. Basically roses, a little of oud and a lot of saffron. Smells much like as Attar (but less sweet) with average longevity. Be careful: sometimes it smells like sewing machine oil. Updated January 2014

Synthetic leather saffron opening with a woody base. This perfume reminds me of many others out there. The only beauty of it is if you spray it low on your stomach, the wafts of scent are quite pleasant throughout the day. As with all Montales, it lasts and lasts. This is not a true saffron scent, nor do I detect rose in it. Don't smell it up close and it will create a wonderful aura of perfume around you but it is nothing to go out of your way for.

Well, it's not easy to be in the starting lineup as saffron in this Montale (but which Montale would that even be?). The dusty saffron of the opening is quickly brushed aside. However, not just with a dust cloth. Because the rose is the same as in Black Aoud: The one that dances with the General. General floor cleaner, 'Summer Fresh' variant - just a bit of citrus in the mix. And with that, the dust or saffron is particularly thoroughly swept away. At least for now. The oud impression (if one can speak of it under the dominating rose) is on one hand medicinal, on the other hand leathery-sour-dull. Aha: leathery-sour oud with sour-water rose. Once again, I am reminded of Black Aoud in its contrast. Only in the fourth hour does the General Rose loosen up and finally cede the field to a powdery-dusty, almost grainy saffron. The lady is not defeated and still stirs florally underground, but the colleague has the say. Underground? Not at all. The return to the office after a good hour of absence holds a surprise: A powerful portion of rose hangs in the air and stays there all day. The projection is thus her new main field of activity since she has been exiled from the skin. The oud has evolved into a more woody form, which also becomes lighter over time. I find a floral-grainy-mashed potato note somewhat disturbing in the early afternoon. It has become so dull. A certain relief occurs, however, when around the eighth hour a powdery, saffron-lightwood scent emerges, which is still accompanied (especially in projection - see above) by the rose unchanged. In the late afternoon, a musk base gradually comes through. Perhaps amber and sandalwood are still playing in the background, which is perfectly fine after more than twelve hours. The projection is dominated by surprisingly present musk. Even the next day, it is still noticeably there. Conclusion: Not my thing. I apparently have difficulties with the Montale rose. Turning a rather watery noble rose scent sour-oud-supported to full volume is, in my opinion, not a good idea. However, it cannot be denied that this so-called overdriven way of use has a high recognition value and may have addiction potential for those who perceive it differently. I thank Ergreifend for the sample.

Yes, I know, the title sounds like an ad for a dominatrix. But the title reveals much more about the character traits of Aoud Safran - strong, narrow-minded, with a dominant streak and truly stubborn! What adds to this is the fact that all of this is spread over a sea of ripe blood-red roses. Whiskey, a hint of smoke, a roaring sea of blood-red roses. Noble, vast world. The dress long, form-fitting, stretched out against the body of every sin. An affair. A wild event. Balsamic harmony of wood and saffron makes the heart almost leap out of the body. Aoud Safran wants and cannot be quiet. It must overpower everything. It spreads very broadly on the skin, allowing the wearer to disappear under a veil. The sea of roses begins to rage hellishly. High waves reach the wearer's senses. One feels pulled tight, pushed against the wall. Straightforward. Motionless. It feels frantic and aspiring... At least at the beginning. Then, out of nowhere, a light, sweet undertone emerges, slowly catching the frenzy. Aoud Safran slows down and gradually returns to calm. The blood-red sea of roses seemingly sinks into a deep sleep. Nothing rustles anymore, nothing creates high waves. It has become quiet. So quiet that I already wondered if the whole performance is over? No, far from over. Because the components have peacefully blended together and form an excellent community. They seem coordinated with each other, and the initial aspiration has been completely stifled. Oud is not the main theme here. Rather, it is the rose that takes center stage. Aoud Safran clings to me forever. It cannot and will not let go so easily. The sillage is expansive. A dense fog of the Orient settles throughout the space when one is there. I can already hear the tongues clapping and all the greedy eyes that want to devour me. Aoud Safran seems sinful, noble, and sexy to some. Strangely enough, many in my circle like it, but I cannot give it the love it might deserve. Because I would have hoped for a little touch of animalism and a warm, sandy depth that holds me like in a hand pit. It is well-made, and I also give it a good rating, but it does not quite meet my preferences and sensations. Now and then, I like to sink into the red sea. But this is becoming increasingly rare. Nevertheless, Aoud Safran is a bold number, richly spicy and with rose, rose, rose. Underlined, painted, sketched... however you want to put it - a painting. Red smudges on black wallpaper. Bloody lips, pain, and a revolver. Sad and numb is the night. I would like to shoot through my thoughts. But I dare not. I am too cowardly. The black mistress enters the room. A sea of roses overwhelms me. It flattens me. Quiet and silent, I accept this.

Rose and saffron, this combination has come under my nose for the fourth time now. Black Tie by Tremmlet; Dark Rose by C&S; Regal by BtV and now Aoud Safran. As similar as these fragrances are in some ways, they are of course also quite different. The noblest and definitely the most masculine is definitely Black Tie! Dark Rose and Regal have more commonalities, being more unisex, with the latter being even more intense. However, for those who prefer something really intense and long-lasting, they should reach for this Montale. The prerequisite, of course, is that you like the Oud note in the top. Aoud Safran starts with the characteristic, slightly medicinal scent typical of Oud. The fragrance takes its time to truly honor its name. The accord of saffron and a lush rose slowly rises, lasting for hours. This accord is truly outstanding, but can also be slightly numbing in case of overdosage. The base then receives a slight warmth from the woody notes. Here, I find Aoud Safran particularly sensual and almost addictive! I can't stop smelling my arm. A truly heavenly devil's stuff!

Where are the star marketers of Mr. Montale? The ladies and gentlemen who develop concepts to successfully position the product? They must be working underground. Because no fragrance from the house is, in my opinion, more underrated and misplaced than this one. This scent should be the actual Oudmazing. I have to agree with the previous speaker 100 percent.

Aoud Saffran is once again a successful Oud fragrance. Here, the rose is very subdued compared to BA, Aoud Rose Petals, Aoud Flowers. The highlight is the combination of Oud, precious woods, and saffron. It reminds me of a noble, old, and well-maintained antique piece of furniture. That's roughly how I imagine its scent.

And here we have another release from Montale, who has incredibly few fragrances bearing his name (irony). This time it’s "Aoud Safran." This Montale starts off typically Montale. After that, it feels very dry to me... but only for a moment. After 5 minutes of wearing it, I notice the rose starting to emerge. After 20 minutes, I sense an association with shower gel.

About 9 years ago, Aoud Safran was one of the first Eau de Parfums to explicitly highlight the theme of oud and saffron. Nowadays, these two can be found in what feels like every second fragrance related to agarwood. But what was fashionable back then is today, to put it mildly, "overfamiliar," if not even overused.

Saffron - no idea what that smells like. Let's leave it to Montale to decide. Here’s the development of my face while wearing it: :-/ :-/ :-| :-( :-[ :-| :-{ :'-( >:-( :-)))) The last documented smiley appeared after wearing it for an hour. With Montale's Aouds, it seems to be not so simple. At first, you shouldn't even try to smell it.

Some may wonder, and not without reason: What is the purpose of PARISIENNE eau de toilette, launched one year after the eau de parfum? One reason is obviously just to launch something. They had the bottle the idea, they had done massive marketing, now a follow-up could be successful too, parasitic as it was on its predecessor in many different ways. Is the eau de toilette merely a weaker solution of the eau de parfum, as one might well expect? No, the compositions are slightly different. However, they are far more similar than they are different, with the result that most consumers will probably not notice the difference at all. From the notes, it might seem as though this eau de toilette would be more complex than the eau de parfum. Aldehydes? Really? In fact, they are not detectable to my nose. The vinyl listed among the notes of both of these versions of PARISIENNE is also quite light, which is good news for people such as myself who have a low tolerance for vinyl and plastic notes. I wonder, actually, whether it helps or hurts to list vinyl among the notes of a perfume? In any case, PARISIENNE edt is less sweet than the edp. I smell wood in the drydown more than I do in the edp but the red berries are pretty much the same, as is the abstract floral quality. Overall, this, too, is a fairly generic pink fruity-floral fragrance geared toward younger consumers. I think that the quality of these two fragrances is slightly higher than that found among compositionally similar celebrity scents, but these are not perfumes which I myself would buy. They are much more about red berries than they are about rose.

Today, a visit is expected, so it can't hurt to dust off the perfume shelf. In the process, I came across Parisienne. Oh, Bonjour, we haven't seen each other in a while. Spraying it brings back fond memories. A light aldehydic scent, mixed with delicate cranberry and gentle rose subtly reaches my nose. I like cranberry juice, so this note is very appealing to me. Lily of the valley and violet leaf add color to the fragrance and make it playful. The iris, on the other hand, is elegant and mature, and the suede touch that overlays it is very exclusive. Oh, la la. I see a casually chic Parisian hurrying across the Place d'étoile. Under her left arm, she has tucked the "Figaro," and from her shopping basket, the traditional baguette is sticking out, while she walks a fluffy little poodle on a leash. She heads towards a slightly dented Renault, says "Alors" to the little dog, and both hop into the car. Then, boldly, without signaling, she merges into the dense traffic. This casual chic, paired with lightheartedness, is what Parisienne conveys. A fragrance for French moments, even in the German everyday life.

First of all I must say that I like this fragrance. But thinking of its name and looking at the black bottle I thought it was stronger, more "mysterious" and with a good longevity. The acchord is perfect , but the fragrance remains too light and evanescent. Anyway,on my skin this scent smells quite good altought it's evanescent and I like the total black bottle which keeps better the fragrance contained in it.

I received a decant of this perfume from one of my subscription boxes. It’s a nice blackberry and supposedly has tuberose in it, but I can’t smell it whatsoever. I smell blackberry and vanilla, that’s it. It wears down nicely throughout the day. I think it can be worn at any time given it’s simplicity. It’s so uncomplicated that I would reach for it to wear on general errands when one wants to smell nice, but not think about it. There’s nothing more I can say about this perfume.

It's airy and botanical with realistic fresh blackberries and white florals which give the impression of elderberry. As it dries down, the top notes don't dissappear but become accompanied by a dark patchouli and creamy vanilla. Honestly not as sweet as everyone's been saying, nowhere near. Surprisingly androgynous on me. Beautiful scent bubble with subtle tendrils of perfume that waft off you as you move.
