Even with 'over spraying' this doesn't become a wall of scent or overwhelming, the scent tendrils just reach a little further. Layers really well with Encre Noir and Khair Confection, both at once and separately. Encre Noir amps the dark and botanical aspect here and further leans into the androgynous with how the vetiver plays off the blackberry. Khair Confection is basically a younger and sweeter take on Signorina Misteriosa with a pear instead of the blackberry, delicious layered though but very feminine.

Omg this one is sooo good!! It's like everything I've ever wanted in a bottle and it's easily becoming one of my favorites of all time . If you're a fan of super super super sweet fragrances and gourmands, then this will be right up your ally. This is probably one of the sweetest perfumes I've ever smelt in my entire life. To me, this smells like creamy yummy vanilla marshmallowy blackberries with a mega sugar overload. SO good!

Whip cream and berries sounds great, but the milky sweetness in here has a synthetic edge to it, which makes it a touch odd to my nose. I mainly wore this in winter, because in warmer weather I had the nagging sensation that the lactose in here would turn sour. You need to spray industrial quantities of it on your clothes for good projection and longevity.

Autumn Day Gentleman: It is time. The summer was very grand. Lay your shadow on the sundials and let the winds loose on the meadows. Command the last fruits to be full give them two more southern days push them towards completion and chase the last sweetness into the heavy wine.

Recently, I visited the medieval market in Monheim with my girlfriend, which took place around the beautiful Marienburg. I love medieval novels and felt very comfortable near noble knights, proud steeds, lovely maidens, and original jesters. Unknown foods were being roasted and baked, and the scent of smoky crystals wafted over the scene.

It feels as if you are wrapped in black velvet, dark and soft, and slowly a radiant golden warm light unfolds from this darkness, enveloping you in pure warmth. A fabulous scent for autumn and winter that lasts throughout the day and develops slowly and magnificently.

In the perfumery, a beautiful black bottle with a bow caught my eye. Of course, I had to test the fragrance and was immediately smitten. I then ordered the fragrance online. Unfortunately, my beloved bottle is still in the USA where I studied, but I managed to snag a sample through the Souk, which arrived in the mail today. Many thanks to Süchtig for that! I sprayed it and...

About a year ago, I discovered it. I did some research and often read that it was beautifully blackberry-like. Everyone experiences scents differently, but I love to be dazzled by fragrance notes that I absolutely cannot resist. Blackberry is one of those. Time and again, I circled around it, should I or shouldn’t I? Do I dare to try it?

Personal: 7/10 - It's fine. Sweet, creamy white florals aren't my thing, but I like it. Mass appeal: 8/10 – Citrus and sweet, vanillic white florals are super safe. Performance: 7.5/10 – Surprisingly strong for such a sweet/fresh DNA. Value: 5/10 – Montale pricing is okay, but this is more designer than niche. Uniqueness: 6/10 – It smells nice, but nothing new. Citrusy vanilla neroli freshies are everywhere. But props for making it so long lasting. SCORE: 67/100 Full bottle buy? NO, it’s pleasant but redundant with other sweet white florals. Blind buy? YES, safe enough if you like citrus-vanilla freshies that are floral. Recommend? YES, if you want a louder, longer-lasting summer freshie. Date night? NO, too bright and sweet. Not seductive. May work for summertime. Office safe? YES, clean and cheerful, but spray lightly. Vanilla and citrus are loud. Pros: Easy to wear, cheerful citrus, white floral, and vanilla. Solid performance. Cons: Generic, redundant, leans juvenile. Not niche-feeling at all. This isn't quite what I'm used to seeing from Montale. It's not very dark, or oud forward, rather it's not oudy at all. It's a bright, sweet, summery citrus with vanilla and lots of soft white florals. It feels VERY designer, though. Montale usually puts out something that's kind of niche smelling, but safe for niche, and this one just feels straight off the Sephora shelf. It's not bad, by any means, but it's not what I would expect from a niche lite brand like Montale. It's fine, but not memorable, and definitely a bit boring. It's super summery and pleasant, but... it's kind of boring. Review #93 in my fragrance journey – this fragrance I own as a decant

A legend, linked to Ottoman influence, tells that in Greece, painting houses white and blue was a way to express one's identity and attachment to the homeland during Ottoman rule. Day Dreams is a spring walk through the streets of Greece, where the aroma of citrus fruits are, sparkling, and the attractive symphony of white flowers. A simple, fresh fragrance that brings joy, wonderful for those who love flowery perfumes.

Overall very lovely fragrance even though I'm not a fan of tropical / coconut scents. Montale has that distinguishable synthetic accord that doesn't mesh well with my skin, although here it's a bit more smooth and palatable. The beginning smells like warmth, citrus fruits and fresh florals. Neroli brings that soapy freshness, while jasmine is more on the fresh, aquatic side of things. Don't be fooled though: coconut is the star here, rising from the depth of the bottom notes and permeating most of the scent. The florals recede to the back as a powdery, sweet coconut takes up almost all of the space. As it moves on, sandalwood becomes more noticeable with a creamy, woody note. Paired with the coconut it makes for a warm, sweet, powdery and almost creamy tropical vibe. Drydown becomes more sandalwood and coconut with an added touch of subtle, sweet vanilla. It's an everyday fragrance for warmer temperatures. Overall, it's very nice, but since I've decluttered all coconut fragrances from my collection because I wasn't as much of a coconut fan as I thought I'd be, this one won't be making it into my collection. Was still ncie to try out!

We became aware of Montale through a YouTube channel. Enchanted by the bottles and excited about the fragrance pyramids, we ordered our first samples. This is how we came to our Day Dream sample. The typical Montale DNA, which is a bit medicinal-synthetic, is less pronounced here than in others. The opening reminds me of an afternoon in the midst of a flower meadow in summer, with a glass of freshly squeezed orange juice in hand. Now just hold your face in the warm sun and relax. I love the scent of Tiare that beautifully emerges and surrounds you as it develops. But not too intrusive; despite its floral character, it is a fragrance that men can wear well. So maybe not lumberjacks with Harleys and beards down to their knees :) But the classification as a unisex fragrance is, for me, accurate despite the floral notes. A hint of vanilla in the dry down, yes, but I really don’t smell coconut. The longevity and sillage are good but not as strong as in other Montale fragrances. The longevity is around 7-8 hours, then it is really only perceptible very close to the skin. Clear recommendation to buy. I myself also got the bottle after the test. If I had to categorize it, I would wear it more in spring and summer.

I don't understand why this fragrance has such bad reviews. It is a very light orange-vanilla scent that makes you very suitable for everyday wear with various flowers. I really liked the scent, and my boyfriend even took it to school! The sillage and longevity are, as expected from Montale, incredible. Clear recommendation, test the fragrances yourself and don't just rely on reviews on Parfumo!

I tested the fragrance in my perfume shop, and at first, I was very convinced. I took the test strip home and honestly couldn't get enough of it. Then I bought it, but unfortunately, it has become way too overpowering for me and bothers my nose. It's too floral and too feminine for me, unfortunately. I probably should have gotten a small sample first and tested it longer.

Today I treated myself to YSL Mon Paris - and only discovered at home that in elegant script it also says Couture on the box. Oops - what can I expect from this? Couture for me is a pair of blue jeans - combined with a white T-shirt and white sneakers. With "haute Couture," I throw on a blue denim shirt. That's how I feel top chic. My father saw it differently. For an invitation to a fancy restaurant, he added: But please not the denim shirt - we all know that one by now. I was a bit offended - isn't that a cool outfit? I reflect and have to admit that it might also come across as a bit... boring? When he picks me up, he personally looks into my closet and pulls out an asymmetrically buttoned plum-colored blouse - paired with a black flared skirt - and black pumps from the shoe rack. What I have in there... Amazing. I get dressed - and Dad sighs: finally not so student-like anymore! At the restaurant, my sister is amazed: How pretty she looks - when she is nicely washed and combed! As a finishing touch, I should have worn YSL couture, because this round, buoyant chic scent would have crowned my casual elegance. Transparent and fruity, it envelops me - deepened by soft rose and light patchouli - and musk gives it a subtle shine. The orange blossom bathes couture in warm light - just as our table is illuminated by candles. But this friendly scent also elevates my everyday couture - I’ve tried it out.

I recently tested the original Mon Paris. I don't like this one at all. I wrote a statement about it. Hmmm, so at the beginning, strawberry and raspberry jump out at you. Really... Full blast... In your face... These two notes dominate throughout the entire fragrance journey. It became clear to me that strawberry in fragrances is not my thing. So MP was out for me. Shortly after, I saw that there is a Couture version. I found this immediately interesting ---> no strawberry, grapefruit, and lychee (I think grapefruit and lychee are great in spring and summer fragrances). Of course, I had to test it. At the beginning, raspberry, lychee, bergamot, and grapefruit dominate for me. I really like the grapefruit and bergamot here, as they prevent the fragrance from becoming too syrupy-sweet. And they give it a bit of freshness. The scent develops really nicely: for me, it's a raspberry-grapefruit mix. Along with lychee, rose, musk, and patchouli (which gives the fragrance some depth and earthiness, like in MP). If I had to describe it in a few words, I would say: sweet-citrusy, fruity, fresh, a bit rosy + musk. As for longevity, I can't complain. I applied MPC in the morning and still noticed it in the afternoon. I would categorize MP more for autumn, winter, and spring. I think it's too much for summer. MPC, on the other hand, can be worn all year round, in my opinion. With grapefruit and lychee, this fragrance is a great summer companion. I don't know the other MP versions. As for MP and MPC, I must clearly say that MPC is the better MP for me.

Hello everyone, I'm back and as always, I hope you can at least somewhat tolerate me this evening. I won't ramble too much and… oh, what am I saying?... Of course, I will ramble, so you will have to endure me :D So, today I'm talking about Mon Paris Couture by Yves Saint Laurent. First of all: No, I haven't tried the other Mon Paris fragrances yet, so this won't be a comparative comment. Otherwise, oh yes, Paris… the dream city for many people. One dreams of beautiful streets and corners, romance, the Eiffel Tower, and pretty French girls. I think all of that doesn't always hold true… the last time I was in Paris, where I stayed (which admittedly wasn't exactly a posh district…), a huge trash can was set on fire by teenagers on the very first night. But it could be that the boys and girls thought they could enhance the romance by setting the trash can on fire, so to speak, as a "campfire romance" :D This would also explain the many couples seen everywhere on the streets (and bus stops) passionately kissing… (oh, a dreadful sight for singles… :DDD). Be that as it may, I will just assume that Paris is still a beautiful, romantic city. And before I ramble on forever (I did warn you), let me get to the scent "quickly"! The Scent: The beginning is floral, citrusy, and sweet. It slightly reminds me of refreshing, delicious fruit ice or tasty candies, which admittedly makes my mouth water a bit (so this is once again one of those scents that makes you want to bite the lady next to you :D). From the citrus notes, I would guess grapefruit and lemon, and for the floral notes, especially rose. Fruity notes seem to come from raspberry, while other sweet scents remind me of musk. A little later, patchouli comes in, whose earthy scent makes the fragrance feel more mature. At first, the patchouli seems to become stronger, but then it fades a bit in the base, making the scent appear sweeter again. Otherwise, in the base, you can smell an amber-like sweetness, which is soon caught up by the musk. And although the scent occasionally appears slightly synthetic, overall it has turned out quite nice. It is pretty, maybe a bit too sugary, but indeed pretty. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is quite okay. So neither too strong nor too weak. There will definitely be a scent cloud for a while, so you will surely be noticed with this fragrance. The longevity is about eight hours and a bit more, as the sweet notes linger longer. The Bottle: The bottle is rectangular with beveled edges on the top. In terms of shape, it slightly reminds me of the bottles from the Mon Guerlain line, only this one is a bit rounder. It features a beautiful black bow with white dots around the neck. The cap is rectangular and transparent. A very beautiful bottle! Conclusion: So… that was the scent with the name of the city of love (ugh, how that sounds… well, maybe I’ll think differently when I have a girlfriend :DD We’ll see!). So… the scent isn’t really bad. I even think it deserves more than the average 6.9 points here. But here comes the BUT: Most of you will probably not like it, simply because the scent, except for a brief moment in the heart note (where you can smell patchouli), is quite teenager-like and thus more suitable for significantly younger girls. Of course, I would also quite like such a scent on adults or… women who have surpassed the age of 25-30 (uh… and more) and think they are too old for such a scent, and find it quite appealing :D However, I am also a quirky bird here, it’s incredible that my comments are still considered helpful :DD Sometimes, though, the patchouli seems to flash stronger again, making you feel that the scent isn’t just for younger people. But since it is said that scents differ on every skin, there’s only one thing to do: Get to the "meat,"… uh… oh God, I probably shouldn’t say that when speaking to you ladies… I meant, get to the scent and test it yourself :DD By the way, since I mentioned Guerlain earlier, I must say that I find the Mon Guerlain scents, with few exceptions, much better; you should definitely try them when you get the chance :) Well, that’s it again. Please excuse me if I said at the beginning that I currently can’t relate much to the city of Paris. But the year is still young… who knows if I can end my eternal single life this year (hey, you could place bets on that, wouldn’t that be an idea!!), then I might have a different opinion about Paris… unless someone sets a trash can on fire while kissing again… :DD Well then, until next time and have a lovely evening, everyone :)

This fragrance was allowed to join my collection after the classic "Mon Paris," and I had to grab it at a bargain price. The opening for me begins with a somewhat soapy grapefruit note, which relatively quickly fades away after a few minutes, while the scent develops into red berries. I didn't think of raspberries directly, but rather of a plate full of various red berries dusted with a fine layer of powdered sugar, bringing a sweetness that I don't find exaggerated at all. As it progresses, I start to smell the roses. Much less noticeable, until after about 2-3 hours I can no longer perceive it at all. This could certainly be due to my nose; nevertheless, I can only report on my personal experiences. I don't find the scent bad and I'm not too disappointed about its longevity given the good price. At times, the fragrance reminded me of "Miss Dior Absolutely Blooming," which also contains some similar scent notes. I find the fragrance very suitable for spring and would describe it as relatively "unobtrusive." I like the bottle and it looks great next to the classic scent. In comparison, I find the Couture quite similar, but still a bit sweeter than "Mon Paris." I find it difficult to give an age recommendation for fragrances, as it also depends on the type and how the scent develops individually, and tastes are indeed different!

Blu is the second installment of the Acqua Essenziale trilogy, launched on the market a year after its namesake "Acqua Essenziale (Eau de Toilette) | Salvatore Ferragamo". First, it smells nothing like the preceding version. If I have to be honest, as soon as it came out in 2014, it didn't blow me away. It didn't have the same spell as its predecessor, perhaps because of that strange sweetness. The fact is that I still added it to my arsenal about two years later, even if it was not under my radar. I have not regretted it—anything but another rock-solid scent by master perfumer Alberto Morillas and a great hidden gem from Ferragamo. The colour of the juice portrays the smell well. It could have been named "Navy Blu", "Dark Blu", or "Sugar Blu." I will not compare this to any of the other blue colognes cause I think this is unique with its notes and how they are blended. Indeed, it is sweeter than most blue frags, perhaps the sweetest one. Acqua Essenziale Blu unfolds with some aromatic, citrus, sweet, and spicy bright and refreshing accords. It's rather acute, and honestly, it could be a bit spilt. Ambrox pops up from the very beginning. A pinch of green cardamom puts out of the vibrant oscillation of citrus notes; I don't get too lemon or too much bergamot, just a nice well-mixed harshness. There is also a dusty aspect, perhaps from lavender and tonka, so you may not like it if you are not in powdery colognes. I get refreshing aquatic accords that break on delicate lavender nuances and come into play with a medicinal soapy sensation in the heart. Also, there is a subdued aspect to black liquorice. So, if you're anything like me, you'll get soapy liquorice dropped in the middle. Besides, if you get a harmonic of smoky and leathery chords with a mainly green, woody, earthy tone, this is cypriol. The fresh floral notes burst in a pleasant and orderly way, but I believe the cypriol oil is the sophisticated touch Alberto Morillas has kept for this Ferragamo creation. The heart is quite sweet, but the notes of cedar prevent the sweetness from slipping into a too syrupy smell like cough syrup. Fresh citrus, floral, rupture a few hours after the spray; I have it under my nose now, and it is a fascinating perfume. I get a nice sweetness in the base with three notes of patchouli, tonka bean, and benzoin. All together, they give a pleasant and mellifluous feeling. However, the sweetness of the scent pairs with a strong dose of salty ambroxan, which provides it with a damp, musky animal feel, a bit like wet stones. The ambroxan note in this fragrance is dry amber and powdery musk. In case you missed it, the ambroxan and patchouli dyad is a well-known pleasant pairing, which is present in many blue colognes such as "Sauvage (Eau de Toilette) | Dior", "Versace pour Homme Dylan Blue (Eau de Toilette) | Versace", and "Polo Deep Blue | Ralph Lauren" to name a few, but still is its own thing. I found this scent extremely good. The tonka and lavender in this one are intoxicating. While it doesn't have brilliant performance on my skin, as both sillage and longevity are moderate—powerful at first, but then come close to the skin—it's an inexpensive fragrance with a well-blended quality. It is a versatile fragrance as I can wear it in virtually any warm climate, from spring to autumn. It works well as an office and daytime fragrance but can turn into a decent nighttime fragrance. I'm probably not going to use it as a winter scent, but that is more up to you. I find Acqua Essenziale Blu an excellent option for a casual evening out as someone who likes lavender. It is well-liked and often praised by others. Ferragamo and Alberto Morillas never cease to amaze. This is popular for a reason. I based the review on a 100ml bottle I have owned since August 2018. -Elysium

Alberto Morillas makes another Gem! This hits most of the check boxes for the quintessential blue fragrance. It evolves nicely and settles down with ambroxin with a hint of tonka and it seems like the lavender sticks around and the patchouly adds a little darkness. For an EDT this has good performance. This is a great fragrance in the blue realm and you can’t beat the price if you compare it to what other options ate out there. For me this is a solid 8!

My friend gave me this fragrance as my birthday gift. All I can say is another inoffensive fragrance from Alberto Morillas. Since there are some people stated that Acqua Essenziale Blu is similar with Bleu de Chanel EDT. Here is my opinion. I admitted Acqua Essenziale Blu shares a little fresh vibe with Bleu de Chanel EDT, but both fragrances moves to different directions. I have tried both of these fragrance, and I get generic scent from Bleu de Chanel EDT. As for Acqua Essenziale Blu, I smell a little synthetic scent. (Don't get me wrong, the scent is still good) Do not expected the performance and the sillage of this fragrance (It last on my skin for 3 hours only). it is a low-priced fragrance, yet the scent is pleasant and not offense. In my opinion, if you love the generic scent of Bleu de Chanel, you can skip this fragrance. If you like BdC EDT vibe and you are looking for a substitute fragrance, I recommend you to try this out.

A lot of Lavender! In addition to a bit of a mintiness and a lot of sweetness. I don't know why but at first I get a resemblance to Ferragamo F Black... maybe because they both share a huge load of lavender and Tonka. As the first blast moves away i get a mixture of Eros and BDC with sparks of F Black shining through. A synthetic nature stays all the way trough the scent. I would describe it as an beginners allrounder. Average projection, average Sillage, average smell. Whats not average is the bottle which I find absolutely stunning, so elegant. If you have any other blue scent you don't really need that one

Alberto morrilas is great at making blue fragrances, and this one is no different. A really underrated gem, and for the price it’s really good. I am mainly into niche fragrances, but I still find myself reaching for this £35 fragrance often. Bought it for spring a few years ago and has been solid throughout my entire fragrance journey. I would definitely reccomend

Okay, okay. My perception of fragrances is often a bit different. But I really can't explain the comparisons drawn here to Bleu de Chanel and Dylan Blue. Apart from the color of the bottle and the "Blue" in the name, they have, in my view, hardly anything in common. It starts right at the beginning of the development.

...not only allows the aromas to unfold better in hot beverages. For my nose, this fragrance differs from the usual blue aqua waters. First: I like the aquatic scents. For me, aquatic fragrances are the true "sport" scents, whereas I believe that the declared sport fragrances are only rarely needed at all.

First of all, to address the discussion here: for me personally, the scent has a distant resemblance to Versace Dylan Blue, but of course, it is still quite different. It might have a hint of similarity to Bleu de Chanel, but no more. Acqua Essenziale Blu was a great surprise for me.

As a bonus with a purchase, I received this fragrance in the form of a sample. I had come across the name Ferragamo a few times, but I had never tried a fragrance from this brand. Accordingly, I was very curious about what to expect. Fragrance development: The scent starts off zesty-fresh with lemon and bergamot and the aromatic-minty green cardamom.

To get straight to the point: the original was one of the most unnecessary releases last year - this is not the same in blue, clearly better, but still somehow really boring. Call me spoiled by niche perfume, but unfortunately, that's how it is. And a rip-off on top of that - but one thing at a time! With Blu, you expect an aquatic, watery, fresh scent...

Moschino CHEAP AND CHIC HIPPY FIZZ reminds me immediately of Salvatore Ferragamo INCANTO BLISS upon application. There is a kind of citrusy quality, something of a fruity-floral demeanor, and a bright and shiny sheen to this creation which places it directly into the twenty-first-century category of SSRI fragrances. Both of these fragrances list lotus as a note, so that probably accounts for part of the similarity as well. I think that the quality of HIPPY FIZZ is just a notch above that of the Salvatore Ferragamo INCANTO flanker series, which work for me much of the time when I'm dashing out the door and want a quick spritz of something inoffensive and kind of nice and good for public places. Every once in a while the synthetics clash with something going on. Is it the weather--the temperature or humidity--or is it the wearer? Not sure, but the point is that sometimes they work; sometimes they do not. In the case of HIPPY FIZZ, I have not yet had a "bad trip", though it may simply be waiting to happen, as this, too, is obviously a synthetic composition which is bound to clash with something sometime somewhere. Today, however, it smells quite nice: bright and cheery and light and citrusy with an inviting woody drydown, which I--perhaps through the power of suggestion--thought might even involve a bit of patchouli. Anyway, it smells good: the moss and the cedar are producing a sort of pseudo light-patchouli effect. I like this perfume, for what it is. Nothing profound, but a good choice when only an SSRI frag will do! The bottle is oddly adorable, too.

I don't understand the hippy reference here. I usually connect patchouli and incense to the scent of a hippy. However, this sparkling citrus fragrance is certainly fizzy. Hippy Fizz is very similar to Funny! by Moschino. Although lemon and bitter orange is not listed in the notes, they are certainly present, especially in the top notes. The scent itself is very crisp and Summery. Refreshing in fact. I don't sense much in the way of rose or violets, however the lotus and magnolia blend in well with the citruses. I was a little disappointed by the lasting strength which was extremely poor. So all in all, I'd suggest Funny! as a better alternative as something that is very similar and longer lasting.

I don’t understand why Hippy Fizz was discontinued. They could have done the same as with I Love Love, which is basically a simple dupe of Dolce & Gabbana Light Blue, or So Real, which smells like Fanta or even Petals. It’s such a pity. I also tried Funny, since some reviews mentioned a similarity, but I don’t feel it at all. I just can’t understand this decision.

To me, Moschino has always had a very modern vibe. It is a house that seem to reach out to a very young audience and therefore some of their bottles are what I would call childish or somehow tacky. Still fun and interesting, though. No matter what, looking at their success they must be doing something right. Kudos to that. This scent is a surprise. What a start! So citric! Marvelous to me. A beautiful combination of the bitter fruity and the floral aspect. It is done to perfection. A great summer scent. Not much happens during the hours, but it is really fresh. This bottle is cute with the very bright colours. I do like the original Olive Oyl shaped bottle best because the whole image with the black, red and white colours and the characteristic top, but this variation is perfect for the shelf of a modern into-fashion mid 20 kinda gal. Fun, chic and delicious. Before buying this one should know that both sillage and longevity is poor. A travel size bottle to go with it is a must-have. Then you are prepared for summer in the city. 137/365

No, no, no! I just can't bring myself to criticize it. The bottle is just too cute. Go test it yourself. Fresh? Yes. Zesty? At first, yes. Aside from the lemon, you really can't detect any other components. That's about it. The base is so annoyingly synthetic that the headaches come on their own. But, ... maybe I'll like it better next year. I had already dismissed Versence in 2009 and this year I viewed it with grace. Must be the age!

Dear Mari has given me a bag of time - thank you very much for that ;-) - so that I finally have the chance to comment again. I came across "Hippy Fizz" through a swap. To be honest, I like it better than I could have imagined. The scent is like a fresh shower, and it maintains that freshness until the end, which is very pleasant after a long workday, in my opinion.

I had it shown to me this afternoon, as I am looking for a zesty, fresh summer fragrance. In warm/hot temperatures, I like to wear something refreshing and lively... This scent could also be applied as a body spray, said the "expert" in this nice little perfumery. I smelled a test strip and the opening was already great. Gradually, I realize that I like citrus notes.

As far as I know, the bottles are inspired by the silhouette of Olivia (Popey). I find the idea quite amusing. I definitely need to go and sniff it out. Update 11.05.2010 If you don't like it as sweet as Escada, you should go for this one. Fruity, zesty summer scent. I like it very much! Available for about €30 for the small 30 ml bottle.
But the bottle is really genius. I generally find all the bottles from Moschoni great. I will test the fragrances soon.

Scentrack Pet Shop Boys – Domino Dancing This summer Kouros opens with unidentified citric notes, immediately followed by strong marine, salty sea wind accord. At first sniff, it smells banal, and overly synthetic. It takes time to recognize hidden layers, consisted of cold incense note, musky freshness, pale fruitiness, and driftwood accord made of gentle Guaiac wood and some cedar. The usage of fresh and cold incense in summer scent is the interesting part of Kouros Tonique. Kouros Eau de Toilette Tonique has normal projection, but longevity on my skin is great – up to 10 hours during hot or humid summer days. I did not expect this Kouros will be such a compliment getter. Apparently, the ladies really like its distinctive and fluffy freshness. The whole composition has some 80s cheap, but good vibe. Something Sonny Crockett from Miami Vice would wear. 6.5/10 More on Scentimentalwords

Who hasn't had a summer scent? This year's Kouros Eau de Toilette Tonique can confidently be included in the selection. Whether to point new customers towards Kouros, or to convince the true fans of this stinker about the trend of a second fragrance - for many years, YSL has been launching one flanker after another. They come and go, serve their purpose, and approach the original to varying degrees. You really have to search for the Kouros in this Tonique. What we get here is a well-crafted fresh scent. Citrusy notes are paired with pleasantly herbal ones, and a subtle aquatic note is also part of the mix. This feels very pleasant - one might almost think that the times when aquatic scents smelled like a chemistry lab are over. The three aspects are in good balance with each other throughout the entire scent development, which lasts a few hours, with the expected moderate sillage. However, the Kouros could have been left out entirely. At the beginning of the scent development, the famous indolic side of this Greek is briefly perceptible - but only if you pay attention. Towards the base, a very gentle hint of Kouros seems to come through here and there, far too little to please true Kouros fans. So, the best thing that can be said about this idea is that the Kouros in Kouros Eau de Toilette Tonique doesn't bother further. For the many perfume lovers who do not like the very specific Kouros, this is rather good news.

It’s quite confusing with the Toniques. What you’re testing in the store might have been sitting on the shelf for 1-2 years; you would hardly recognize which vintage is in front of you if you didn’t look at the photo on the cardboard packaging. The bare male torso is on it, so it’s from 2013. At first, after spraying, it’s hardly perceptible, likely due to the low outside temperatures, which makes it clear that the Tonique only makes sense between May and September. Slightly citrusy, slightly sour. The mugwort is probably responsible for the slightly minty impression, which feels pleasantly invigorating. Compared to all the sporty and summery fragrances of recent years, it must be noted that the "Kouros Tonique" really comes across as natural. The DNA of the powerful original becomes recognizable after a quarter of an hour. In fact, a note shines through, likely created by the trio of jasmine, cinnamon, and patchouli, which brings it close to a light, diluted, less dirty "Kouros". The scent is definitely maritime, slightly mineral for sure, and refreshing in any case on a warm summer day. A subtly dirty-animalistic, somewhat harsh undertone is created, likely due to the patchouli, reminiscent of a rain-soaked field. Pleasantly, the scent distinguishes itself from almost all artificial, sharp wannabe summer fragrances. The leather in the base feels quite diluted, only shining through in a grounding manner. It can be a good purchase for hot days, and even "Kouros" haters might appreciate it; it’s really very solidly made.

Don't we all always wait for summer? :-) Especially now that it has just recently passed and it will take almost half a year until it comes around again... With Kouros Eau de Toilette Tonique, I had the chance to have summer back on my skin immediately. Its packaging is typical with Greek symbols, this time it is kept in bright white and turquoise blue. The bottle is the same, it has the typical Kouros shape and is also very aquatic, in turquoise blue. The scent starts off spicy with mugwort and citrusy notes. After about 30 minutes, the spicy note fades away and the aquatic, marine notes come in, giving the fragrance a big freshness kick and a cooling character. Jasmine and cinnamon are completely overshadowed by the freshness. In the base, cedar adds a majestic coolness. Overall, the scent has very little in common with the original, which is now classified as an absolute sillage powerhouse in the spicy-woody-animalic direction. So, those who love the classic above all and expect something in that direction will not find much joy in this summer flanker. However, for those who always found the original, let's say, extraordinary, like I did, this refreshing version can be wonderfully used to slowly get accustomed to Kouros. If you like it refreshing, cool, and aquatic, you are exactly at the right address here. It still inherits the longevity from its big "father"; on me, it lasts over 10 hours. Have fun with this limited pleasure :-)

At first, when I saw this Kouros variant, I thought it would be the rare Sport or Fraicheur. But this Tonique version is also limited and not bad at all for summer 2013. Even though I am 1. no longer 100% sure if it was the 2013 version or the 11 version, and 2. I do not approve of the flanker flood at Kouros, these 2 summer versions probably don't differ much anyway, and I hardly believe that in a well-stocked perfume store there are still 4 packs of the 2011 version rotting and being advertised as new! Kouros Tonique 2013 smells like pure summer. A refresher with simple DNA, but slightly dirty undertones (probably from the original), which are pleasant and don't come off badly here. Clearly one of the better new summer scents of the year, and I can easily imagine bathing in this fragrance again after a cool shower. It starts with a citrus peel kick paired with a bit of spice. Then it becomes aquatic but no less revitalizing. Here, this often overused word finally applies - fresh, energetic, energy-giving, awakening, tingling. Like sparkling tonic water! The cinnamon is only hinted at, but leaves a slightly animalistic and dirty touch in this otherwise untypical environment for it. This feeling vaguely reminds me of Kouros. In the dry down, it somehow becomes cool, slightly sweaty, and leathery. Sillage is adapted to summer and not too strong. But definitely noticeable and suitable for the chest hair machos of the new generation. Longevity was unremarkable at 6 hours, and the bottle is Greek, bulky, and somehow cool! Overall, not quite as great as Body Kouros, but better than the King Kouros that I tore apart back then. I definitely need to test this one again with a significantly improved sense of smell! A good, not too smooth summer all-rounder with good longevity!

I am currently doubting myself a bit. During my first encounter with this fragrance, I smelled a long-lasting cinnamon scent with an orange note and was so thrilled that I immediately ordered a large bottle of it. At the same time, I wrote the following comment: ------------ ## 09.05.

This smells like Thallium, Dior Homme Cologne 2013 mixed with a sweet coffee note. It's really nice, but not worth retail. I only bought it, because I wanted it...and couldn't wait for the price to drop. Awesome office scent, no one will be offended. I know a lot of people didn't like the original Uomo... Because of the sweet notes, along with everything else. Then you should try this bad boy out. Get a free sample from the nearest Salvatore Ferragamo boutique. Yes, it has the DNA of the original, but it's not as sweet or dark. The light version...ah yin and yang if you will. Hope this helps. I used six sprays...both wrist, back & front of my neck, chest, and front of my shirt. Will I buy this again?...No, I don't see myself finishing this bottle. Like I did with Salvatore Ferragamo Uomo (two times over). Should You Skipped It, Sample It First or Blind Buy It? Sample it (it smells like Uomo & Thallium Yves de Sistelle mix together). Can you use it as a unisex scent?...Yes! Is it the old or new formulation? New(First Batch) SKU Number: 8052086372979 Batch Number: 00H59E1 (Production Date: May 2017) Age: 21+ From: Amazon Size: 100 ML Scent: 3.75/10 (Uomo lite with a strong lemon scent). Value: 1/5 (Cost $70.52). Sillage: 4/5 (Three to six feet). Longevity: 3.75/5 (Eight hours plus). Creativity: 4/5 (Sweet glass of lemonade & coffee). Projection: 3.25/5 (90 Minutes). Versatility: 5/5 (Anytime & anywhere). Compliments: 4.5/5 (Just alright, but the complements only came from fellow fragheads). Until next time, I'll catch you on the flipside.

Salvatore Ferragamo Uomo Casual Life is marketed as a male fragrance, but can actually be used by members of the opposite sex, too. It's opening is a blast of florals, and it stays more or less like that throughout its 3-hour life span. Not bad, but nothing to write home about, either. This scent leans toward the younger crowd (people in their 20's) and is sharp on opening, gradually softens until it whimpers into the night by 21/2 to 3 hours. 6/10

Hello dear readers, this will be my first comment in this forum. Unfortunately, I do not have the ability to pick out all the fragrance components from a perfume. However, my description of my experience or impressions would be too long for a statement. . “Wow! You smell so good again today!” my pretty colleague whispered to me quickly this morning, throwing me a seductive glance over her shoulder as I stood at the threshold of the boss's office, asking me what this wonderful scent was that I seemed to wear all the time. “Ferragamo,” I replied with a smile, to which I received a pleasant “Hmmmm, delicious! And it sounds good too!” from her. I went into my office and secretly chuckled to myself. “Today again,” she had said, and “wear all the time.” I grinned. I am wearing the “Ferragamo Uomo Casual Life” for the first time this week! I don’t wear it all the time, but obviously, I smell “so good!” all the time. While just under two years ago I would simply spray on whatever I happened to receive as a gift for Christmas or my birthday (e.g. Le Male Terrible, Joop Thrill, Boss Bottled), nowadays I deliberately choose every day what I will “immerse” myself in. Whether it’s “The One” by Dolce & Gabbana, “Acqua di Gio’ Profumo” from the good Giorgio, or Valentino’s intense man - I leave nothing to chance! :-D One of my favorite scents is Salvatore Ferragamo's “Uomo.” This sensual, sweet coffee scent has captivated me. When “Casual Life” hit the stores, I didn’t hesitate long and got it for myself. I really like both bottles. They stand side by side like good friends on the shelf, and I believe I can even smell the connection between these two perfumes. In my opinion, the “Uomo Casual Life” captures the DNA of “Uomo” without resembling it too closely. I perceive a pleasantly fresh lightness, in which a subtle, not too sweet coffee note is integrated. The scent feels to me like the little brother of the adult “Uomo,” who lets the soul dangle during a summer vacation. It strikes me as fresh, light, and unobtrusive. The slight hint of sweetness pleases me very much and fits - for me - perfectly into the warm season. And let’s be honest: coffee is always a good idea! Maybe soon with the pretty colleague from this morning… ;-)

When a fragrance is called "Casual Life" and promises a citrusy freshness in its pyramid, I can't resist for long... And yes, right after spraying it on, I switch to casual mode, slow my breathing, think about chilling in hammocks, and imagine hearing smooth jazz from somewhere. That's the kind of feeling this Uomo flanker from Ferragamo seems to promise. But it's not quite like that - at least not for me. Because soon after spraying, alongside the citrusy freshness, a strong coffee praline-like note becomes noticeable when sniffing my skin. Well, to each their own... Meanwhile, at about arm's length, a finely tuned blend of citrus, floral, and gourmand emerges - for about half an hour. After that, the top notes begin to recede a bit, allowing the praline to take center stage in the projection. That's the moment I prefer to slip into the background. Because gourmand isn't really my thing... Yet Casual Life is quite honest. It carries the praline in its heart, and there it is. However, here it’s called "Iced Coffee," which can also pass for Tiramisu, thus confirming its relationship to the Uomo classic. With about 60%, it now asserts itself against the citrus, while the violet remains perceptible but proves to be a bit too sweet and out of place. After about 3-4 hours, the base notes make their appearance, with the overall tone of the fragrance becoming increasingly soft and rounded due to the musk and the woods used (here, a white cedar is at work, which has nothing rough about it). In this respect, the Tiramisu reduces back to about 50%, and Casual Life becomes quite balanced and pleasantly light towards the end. Well, ultimately I ordered this treat, even though I should have known that this praline hit, despite all the citrus, wouldn't quite suit me. But that's what experiments are for ;-) My slight aversion to gourmand shouldn't lead to the conclusion that this fragrance is somehow bad. On the contrary, it could be a hit for gourmand fans, as something truly unusual is woven here: lightly tart citrus freshness paired with pronounced praline sweetness, both well balanced. Thus, this flanker is a thoroughly harmonious scent and has decent power on a shirt for 7-8 hours, also in terms of sillage. I usually don't comment on the bottle, but this one has something nice: a sprayer designed like a cap, with the recessed mechanism preventing accidental spraying - really cool. Overall, a rather successful fragrance that I recommend for use in spring and autumn, especially for leisure. While it's not quite suitable for me, it’s definitely a tip for gourmands with a penchant for invigorating freshness. Because its powerful citrus holds up until the end and is harmoniously balanced with a praline Tiramisu, which is called Iced Coffee in this Uomo :)

Casual is my favorite word when it comes to dress code for an invitation. I always feel somewhat overdressed in fine attire. That's why I was excited about the Casual Life sample - especially since I already liked the Uomo EdT. I spray the Casual on the left and the Uomo EdT on the right. Well, I must say, the EdT with its soft spiciness appeals to me much more. And the hoped-for casualness is unfortunately not found in Casual either. On the contrary - I perceive it as rather strict - a note that thankfully does not occur in Uomo EdT. The promised coffee scent also remains hidden from me. Instead, there is a bitter woodiness that is further intensified by the bitter lemon peel. The other ingredients fade away behind the rustic wooden wall. Perhaps it suits some gentlemen well - but in my circle, there is no suitable recipient for this fragrance. I can't imagine it on ladies at all.

Salvatore Ferragamo Casual Life has been my summer fragrance on really warm days since last year. I purchased the 100ml bottle on sale at a perfume store and unfortunately couldn't test it, but for the price, it was worth the risk. When it's so warm that you don't really want to wear anything spectacular, Casual Life is just right.

Today my order arrived and this fragrance was included as a sample. It has little in common with the original. At first, it comes across as very fresh, thanks to the lemon and violet. I can hardly perceive Ambrox. There is a slight sweetness present, but I wouldn't have thought of iced coffee. In the end, there are also slightly bitter notes.

Recently, just in time for summer, I had the opportunity to get a 100ml bottle of Uomo Casual Life for just under €20. - Cardamom in the pyramid and yet a summer scent? Check. - Coffee in a fragrance that I've been eyeing for a while? Check. - Recommendation from Jeremy? Unnecessary, but present - hopefully it won't hurt - Check.

Bright, fruity-floral and easy to wear. Chic Petals opens with a playful burst of pomegranate and red berries, then settles into a soft, slightly musky floral base. Light, cheerful and very much in the Moschino style. Great for everyday and warm weather, though it doesn’t have the uniqueness the Moschino hippy fizz has (

I initially struggled with Cheap & Chic from this label, but then it came back into my hands, and upon re-spraying, I couldn't understand why it had been exiled to the attic. We finally became friends. And the chic flowers also don't make it easy for me, as they have such a clean statement that they appear freshly washed. I am reminded of my soap Dioressence, which I keep in the closet between my laundry. This similarly fine soapy note accompanies the floral aspect of the fragrance - and overshadows the strawberry. The ginger and woods penetrate the soapy curtain - but I hardly perceive the fruits. Likewise, the floral components disappear behind the committed cleanliness. Now in summer, the fragrance is still quite wearable - if you are a fan of clean scents. Unfortunately, I do not belong to the clean scent fans - and the ginger is a bit too assertive for me. Perhaps I need to get used to the clean Petals first - or store them in the attic as well.

No color could fit better than the color RED. And if one had to describe the scent in just one word, it would surely be the word RED. CHic Petals exudes a sweet freshness that instantly lifts the mood. A fruity gourmand with depth. Cheeky, sexy, feminine. Tart notes of fruits and berries emerge. Wrapped in warm, woodier notes. An ideal interplay of various components makes this fragrance a true summer symphony, resonating on the skin for 5-6 hours, with floral tones appearing in the final chord. A beautiful scent that brings happiness.

In the last few days, I have been hauling basketfuls of fruits from the garden into the kitchen and preserving them for the winter. This is exactly what I associate with Chic Petals by Moschino. Sweet, ripe, delicious fruits and a hint of sugar. Not too sweet and not too fruity, the blend is perfectly achieved. Hinoki wood and musk ensure that the berry basket has a pleasant base. The scent is delicate and fine, lingering on me for a long time. I find the bottle very beautiful. A very nice addition to the Moschino fragrances!

Due to the fragrance pyramid, I bought the scent blind. It perfectly matched my fragrance passions. I was particularly taken by the described top note. I looked forward to the fruity aroma of strawberries and pomegranates; the base note also made me very curious. Noble woods have such a pleasantly calm and quietly powerful effect on me. However, my body chemistry threw a wrench in the works... From the very beginning, and very intensely, I was greeted by the Chic Petals, that is, the flower petals. Of the three little plants, the geranium is the most noticeable and present throughout the entire time. A sharp note also mixes in for me, which I attribute to the ginger in this case. The otherwise quite invigorating sharpness unfortunately does not work in the composition on me. On me, the scent simply smells unpleasant, somewhat piercing. The bottle features the well-known silhouette of Popeye's girlfriend Olivia, which is typical for Moschino fragrances, but here it has been adapted with patterns and color play to the ingredients and fragrance composition. The glass part of the bottle shines in a bright red that makes fully ripe strawberries pale with envy; it is beautiful to look at - also wonderfully playful is the cute floral print on the upper part of the bottle.

I actually really like sweet, vanilla scents - like Hypnotic Poison & Roberto Cavalli. But constantly wearing these heavy, noticeable fragrances? Not necessary. So I bought this scent without sampling it first. A risky move - some know what I'm talking about - either this purchase is a total flop or the 50:50 chance was on my side. And YES, it was.

One should open doors and gates to cheerfulness when it arrives - so says an old proverb. And especially in this gloomy and uncertain time, this holds true. So I was eager to try Mon Paris Floral, as I also like the EDP for its buoyant nature. I was not disappointed, as Floral is just as carefree as the EDP, but makes an even more floral statement. The jasmine shines brightly, and the orange blossom warms the scent gently. Datura and peony have a subtly sweet effect - yet the fragrance remains light and airy. Patchouli gives it depth without weighing it down. Cashmere wood contours this friendly scent - and lends it a casual elegance. Nevertheless, Floral remains suitable for daytime wear, as it presents itself very relaxed. But even for an evening out, it is a stylish companion. It appeals to me even more than the EDP, as it seems even more adaptable. Light-footedly, it dances onto my wish list.

Yesterday we went out for Indian food with friends. Very delicious! I had Chicken Dopiaza again and everything was perfect: the chicken, the tomatoes, the onions, the sauce, the rice. Mmmmhhhhh..... I was quite greedy yesterday, I had to have dessert as well. Mmmmhhh.... So far, so good. The conversation took a different turn: They talked about Italy, about Ravenna and Faenza and sightseeing that never happened. About degrees, grades, challenges that life brought along. Back then. One tends to present things in memory a little differently than they really were. Justifications, excuses, and competition over who had it the hardest, who had the worst conditions. And so on. You probably know it. And it can also happen that one gets a bit cranky, to put it very gently. Then a topic change is needed very quickly: the present. But: not much better. Again, justifications, excuses, and competition. So much stress in the last months. Everything is so terrible. Yes, especially for us. What about you? And so on. You probably know it. And then a new topic change is needed quickly and... yep! Finally! It worked! And here comes the perfume into play that I want to evaluate and describe in this comment: "Hey, smell me, how do I smell?" - "Like perfume?" - "Right. What do you think?" - "Uh... good. What does it smell like?" - "Like plum! [it was "Hypnotic Poison"]" - "Oh!" - "Yeah, lately I've been getting a bit into perfume and..." - "Great! Great! You have to advise me! I absolutely NEED a new one, mine is empty!" (Unbelievable state: ONE perfume? And it's empty?) - "Yeah, sure... what do you like?" - "Uh... it shouldn't be too heavy!" "Ah, ok..." - "It can be floral." - "Ok?"- "Rose. I tried one at [niche perfumery we trust]... it was called... it was..." - "Oh, great, you were there?" - "Yes! It was by an Englishman..." "Penhaligon's? That was expensive..." [turns to husband:] "What was it called again? It was with oats..." - [He:] "No, barley... beer..." - "No, I know now: Barney." "Barley? Rye?" "Yes, Barley... it was an Englishman..." "MOOOMENT... Superperfume researched... Yes, "Poppy & Barley" by Jo Malone! Unfortunately, I don't know it! I'm sure it's great..." "No, it was great. But it was too strong." "Oh, I see... and otherwise..." "There was another one... turquoise, elaborate packaging..." "Tiffany's?" "Yes, exactly... that was nice too... But it shouldn't be sweet. Not with vanilla..." "I also like Tiffany's. But it must have been very different from Jo Malone?" "Yes... it can also be with rose. Or not. And subtle. I used to always have Guerlain." "Really? I can't remember, I wasn't into perfume back then. What was it called?" "I don't remember anymore. It can also be more robust." "And woody?" "Yes!" "And resinous?" "Yes!" "And green?" "Also!" "Or rather floral?" "Yes! With rose. Or not." "Ah... ok... I'm searching for you..." And as you can imagine: I will fulfill this difficult task by first recommending this: "Mon Paris Parfum floral". I believe it has everything my friend is looking for. It is: fresh! At the beginning wonderfully fresh and light! There is a very, very delicate green note amidst a fresh, light floral bed. So beautiful! The orange blossom gives this gentle freshness that bergamot or similar stronger citrus notes can never achieve. Accompanying it is the bouquet of magnolia and peony, which are already very gentle and subtle. In it, the delicate green is only faintly perceptible, you have to make an effort, but you can sense it. Instead of a showy sweetness or a strong, overemphasized tuberose, a delicate powdery note joins here, balancing the beautiful bouquet in a wonderful equilibrium: flower is flower here, not sugar. Powder is powder, not a thick layer of dust. Everything is so delicate and fine and has a very subtle sillage. Unobtrusive, but sophisticated. A little hidden is the thorn apple. Here there is no "Datura noire" and no "Datura blanche" to sniff, just a very, very delicate note that might hint a bit of it. The whole thing clings fantastically to the beautiful base of musk, patchouli, and cashmere wood: While patchouli is hardly noticeable, the base is very reminiscent of the beautiful "Code Cashmere" and is also balanced with the other notes. Nothing screams loudly here, nothing is raging around. Everything finely tuned in perfect harmony. And: not sweet. Minimal green. Minimal powdery. Minimal woody. Very beautifully floral. The perfect scent for my friend, I believe. I am so curious to see how she likes it. And if she doesn't like it, maybe I should move on to Yves' classic "Paris". Then we would have the rose.

Macchia and olive groves, gentle vineyards and ripe wheat fields embrace the city of Florence richly. Not to forget, the vast sunflower fields and the little woods that alternately provide shade with the olive groves. Here, the summer sunlight is merciless: no breeze, hardly any shade. Except for the shadows of the cypress trees, drawn in black like silhouettes, the guardians of this landscape. The air vibrates under the tireless courtship of the numerous cicadas; at times, they can be a bit nerve-wracking. But as Goethe, who was known to be a wise man, once said: "Happy are the cicadas, for they have silent wives!" Not polite! No, Mr. Geheimrat, it really isn't!! But the thought that the female creatures would also be heard: oh, dear! The landscape in Tuscany lives from rich colors: brown, ochre, yellow, and many shades of green enliven it. And not to forget: "La terra rossa," the fertile red earth, which reminds us of itself everywhere here. What a treasure it is, how valuable it is and how valuable it has been through the centuries! Countless red bricks have been fired from it, from which so many cities of Tuscany were built. Just think of Siena, the "red city," which even gave its name to a shade. There stands the tower of the Palazzo Pubblico, "like a lily, whose white stone flowers are on a long red stem; a monument to female purity." (Quote from a novel.) With these images in mind and in my heart, I approach Ferragamo's composition: will I be disappointed? A fresh, yet not biting opening of noble citrus fruits presents itself; not surprisingly, it brings with it the magic of roses. Roses that crown Florence alongside iris and sunflowers. Roses that seem to pay tribute to the beautiful women of this city, such as Simonetta Vespucci, with their noble aroma. What would their beauty be without the roses? What would we women be without roses? The tree-like guardian of the landscape, the slender cypress, lends its slightly resinous spice to this enchanting entrée; still sun-warmed, it develops its balsamic powers. Labdanum - no, that must not be missing: the resin of the rockroses, which are found here in abundance and variety. How beautifully everything harmonizes together. What an idyll is already spreading on my skin! The highlight of this lively fragrance composition follows immediately: patchouli! Golden brown, earthy, and creamy, it flows along, this fragrance stream that opens the senses and ultimately enchants them. Golden amber notes and the tastefully presented sweetness of the tonka bean form an adequate accompaniment to this all-dominating scent. For it is quite clear: patchouli is the undisputed king of this fragrance creation! It now forms a harmonious whole that enchants heart and soul! Can one capture the diverse, so fertile landscape of Tuscany in a fragrance? I would have denied it had I not had the pleasure of getting to know Salvatore Ferragamo's "Terra Rossa." What a charming monument this grand seigneur, who loved the city of Florence so much, has conjured up here in flacons! "Terra Rossa," one of the "Tuscan Creations," evokes a gentle and hilly landscape in the light of the late afternoon. Everything seems to be lazily dozing after a long siesta; stretching slowly and breathing a sigh of relief: the scorching sun has turned into a golden warmth. "Terra Rossa," the red earth of Tuscany: so vibrant, so fragrant! A fragrant vibration of the area that has produced so much beauty and culture. Here, a knowledgeable hand with a great passion for art and beauty was at work. Thus, a fragrance creation was born, as true as the landscape that gives it its name. This scent impression is well done; it was skillfully crafted in these wonderful, sensual earthy tones and sun-drenched with love for detail. "Terra Rossa" is a tribute to the landscape and a beautiful fragrance discovery. It is not only enchanting and charming, it is also very clingy. It remains loyal to me for several hours; the scent flow changes slightly from time to time - becoming quieter, softer; then again heavier, earthier: I feel how "Terra Rossa" breathes on my skin! A fragrance that breathes the magic of an entire landscape - how enchanting and at the same time mystical!

It was one of those vacation days when you don't have high expectations and wish that time would fly by ... (Hold on: TIME? Does TIME even exist? Is it true that NASA is feverishly working on the development of a TIME MACHINE? Has the question of PARALLEL UNIVERSES finally been resolved ;) ? Questions upon questions ... ) On that day, it was raining heavily, a dense, dark cloud cover hung over the quaint Dutch Zeeland, and the approaching thunderstorm had chased our usually tough, now trembling dog under the living room table. Our holiday home, which had been a cool shade provider just the day before, transformed into a damp, cold cave. In search of a little comfort, I grabbed my Ferragamo, wrapped myself in a thick blanket, and made myself as cozy as possible with my reading on the couch ... I awoke to the scent of the soft, copper-red spice of an aged whiskey, which was enticingly glowing beside me on the Italian terracotta table. As I inhaled its aroma deeply, I noticed the fire crackling in the fireplace, warming me tenderly. The bright, double-winged terrace door of the Tuscan villa was wide open, revealing a view of the magnificent garden. I stepped outside and inhaled the smell of damp, cool earth wafting from a freshly planted bed. Golden sun rays played with my hair, tickling my nose as I began my stroll, which led me to an old, nearby olive grove after about 30 minutes of walking. Enchanted by the sweet-earthy aroma that the setting sun coaxed from the red earth, I settled down and sank into a deep slumber, enveloped by the scent of Terra Rossa ... When I opened my eyes, I looked into the copper-lit face of my landlord, who stood before me with two glasses and a bottle of red wine. The cloud cover over Zeeland had now completely dissolved - I just caught a glimpse of the rapidly fading light trail in the sky ;) , before we set off with our bottle of Colli di Luni to the beach to bid farewell to the setting sun and let a few shooting stars fly around us ... Conclusion: This fragrance is simply incredible! For me, it embodies comfort and grounding. During the first testing in a private perfumery in Aachen, I immediately fell in love with Terra Rossa. Its sillage is strong to very strong (but not overpowering), its development is very multifaceted, and the ingredients are very well traceable in every phase of development: In the relatively short-lived top note, I perceive woody, fresh, and a slightly alcoholic note - a good, old whiskey, spicy yet rounded and soft. The heart note with patchouli and labdanum reminds me of fresh, turned earth - without the patchouli accord appearing musty or moldy. Amber and benzoin in the base note leave a sweet, woody-earthy impression and have a calming effect, wrapping you up - and with a longevity of up to 12 hours! However, I do not assign Terra Rossa to a specific season: For me, it is an all-rounder that can warm the soul or cool a heated spirit. A comforter in every sense: Whether "hunger," "pee," or "cold" - with Terra Rossa, everything is only half as bad! I increasingly feel the desire to one day "bathe" in this devilry ;) - and there is only one alternative to the bottling (Thank you, dear Angua! :) ): At least one bottle is a must, and quickly! :) P.S.: http://www.parfumo.de/Benutzer/Landlady/Bild/66376

Yes, one can indeed rejoice in this Italian creation. Ferragamo, who piles up an awful lot of useless stuff in his standard range nearly to the ceiling, apparently allows his perfumers to work much more carefully and thoughtfully in the niche segment. The "Tuscan soul" reveals itself as an extremely harmoniously crafted autumn fragrance in a rather moderate sillage range, exuding a cozy, comfortable aura. Slightly sour orange splashes at the beginning, mixed with already waxy-resinous components, create a somewhat bumpy start, which soon rounds out and harmonizes. The citrus notes fade away, becoming mere background noise, while a trio of very carefully dosed rose water, fresh patchouli, and cuddly, slightly resinous-sweet amber pushes its way to the center. Undoubtedly so smoothly coordinated that even patchouli haters might open their hearts wide here. All three aromas merge very skillfully at times, with the rose shining through in a herb-fresh floral manner, while the earthiness of the patchouli prevents the amber from drifting too much into the planar sweetness. Longevity is good, sillage is suitable for everyday use - truly a delightful, because extremely balanced creation in this quite broadly established style category.

Terra Rossa is for me one of the most beautiful patchouli scents I have had the pleasure of discovering so far and is the first of its kind to join my collection. It didn't sneak slowly into my fragrance heart; rather, it burst in through the door, completely captivating me with its first whiff. Terra Rossa also makes it very easy to like it, unless you have an all-consuming aversion to patchouli. On my skin, the first note you can perceive - surprise - is patchouli. A slightly bitter aromatic scent spreads out and reminds me of rain on warm earth that you can sometimes smell before it actually starts to rain where you are. In the next moment, it already shifts into a sweet warm-spicy scent. Orange frames everything in a subtly fruity way and supports a wonderfully radiant fragrance aura. After a while, I can also clearly detect amber, which adds a bit more softness and gentle expressiveness to the scent. Its compactness is repeatedly lightened by slightly citrusy accents, which I personally find really great because it keeps the fragrance from ever feeling heavy, instead laying like a protective but airy veil over you. Terra Rossa is a scent for all life and emotional situations. It cheers me up when I'm sad, calms me when I'm angry, balances me when I'm stressed, and grounds me when I feel a bit lost. It is gentle, strong, demanding, kind - and all at the same time. It lasts about 10 hours, and the sillage is quite decent in the first 2-3 hours before gradually tapering down to skin level. The bottle is high-quality and feels good in the hand; I particularly like the wooden cap. So - anyone looking for a gentle, spicy patchouli scent should not miss out on Terra Rossa and definitely give it a try.

Terra Rossa is a perfume that brings both well-being and subtle eroticism. You feel simultaneously sensual and enchanting, enveloped in a gray-black cloud, and then again very lovely and noble, in a delicate, feminine way. Deep waters are indeed deep, I thought right away upon our encounter. For I did not expect such a beautiful cloak from Salvatore F. It doesn't hit you right away and doesn't come off as shrill. It arrives on velvet paws and slowly wraps around me. I love that. A scent that envelops and drapes itself around the wearer like a wool coat. Perfect for rainy days and the upcoming winter. I can hardly wait to feel the cold when I step out of the warm apartment and draw in the biting air. Unfortunately, the effect in the city is not the same as in the village, somewhere on a mountain peak, at 9:30 in the morning, when you are the first on skis on the groomed slope, looking down at the valleys. When I think of that, I get quite sentimental and can almost grasp the icy air and pull it into my body. Such strong images arise from a seemingly normal everyday moment that occurred so often in my childhood and youth. But when I moved to the city, these images became fewer and fewer. You rarely get to do something you once loved so much. Unfortunately! Terra Rossa will be a big theme for me, especially in winter. A scent that clearly makes my days easier, as it envelops me in an earthy, warm embrace. Slightly "orangey," fruity at first. But these are just seconds, if you ask me. Under the cloak, it creates a sort of intermediate layer. The body is separated from the cloak and the outside world by a spicy wall. There is a timid sweetness in the background and the overpowering patchouli note, which has been integrated so well here that its intensity is not bothersome at all. The scent becomes deeper and warmer as time goes on. It creates pastel tones around the soul, caressing it joyfully and sensually. I feel noble. Noble and also secure when I apply it. It suits really elegant outfits and also presents itself as very distinctive at night. The earthy note feels powerful and is repeatedly illuminated brightly. The spicy front that develops in the scent lasts a long time, and over time, the patchouli becomes very creamy. You feel filled with warmth. As if you were filling your soul with warm pudding. A bit of powder wrapped around it with a distinctly more bitter sweetness - a perfect scent that will surely remind many of you of Coromandel. However, this version is significantly lighter and doesn't immediately brandish its weapons in your face. The deeper you connect with it, the longer you stay in this position. It lasts a long time, and the warmth fades only after what feels like an eternity. It's like a spooning position. This connection. With the close, familiar partner who holds you tightly and awaits the cold but calm winter morning with you. Outside, it is pitch dark. Only the snowflakes blink slightly and fall serenely onto the cold ground. Yes, it is also good for such things. Not just for "wearing under the cloak and appearing noble," but also for the intimate things in life. Also for those moments when you simply let yourself fall after a warm shower and enjoy the evening. While drinking warm tea or cocoa and watching the snowflakes outside. The bottle is kept simple and makes a statement. It fits well in the hand, has a good and solid weight. Linear designs are my favorite anyway. And it is just that. Simple yet so clear. I especially like the half-wooden cap. Come with the first snow, leave your footprints in my soul. Spread your arms, so that I can pull you close to me. I hug you tightly, so that your scent, together, like in a snow globe, embraces us firmly.

If you're expecting a romantic text here, I must disappoint you. Recently, the collection Tuscan Soul was renamed to Tuscan Creations. I will analyze the technical changes this brought about in this comment on the fragrance Terra Rossa.

Moschino TOUJOURS GLAMOUR opens as a rich elixir in some ways evocative of Kenzo FLOWER and Guerlain L'INSTANT, on the one hand, and FERRE edp, on the other. Happily, the vanilla-infused baby powder from FLOWER and L'INSTANT is absent from TOUJOURS GLAMOUR. This creation also has less fruitiness than FERRE edp and showcases florals other than iris. I smell more violet than anything else, but jasmine, heliotrope and lily of the valley are listed among the notes. Despite all of these differences, I do think that the four perfumes all lie fairly close to one another on the grand olfactory map and are kindred spirits. TOUJOURS GLAMOUR is definitely more of an oriental than a floral composition to my nose—thanks in part to cardamom and almonds—which I feel to be the case for FLOWER and L'INSTANT as well. The opening of TOUJOURS GLAMOUR is bright and shiny, like the arrival of smiling celebrities at the doors of the Academy Awards ceremony, with paparazzi bulbs flashing all over the place, the effect of which is multiplied by utra-bleached pearly whites ricocheting light every which way. The stars stroll slowly into the theater—each with a comely guest at his or her side—and within a couple of minutes everything has become golden and, yes, glamourous. The ladies are all wearing haute couture rock-studded jewelry on loan, and the tan-faced gents all look as though they just returned from St. Tropez—or Cannes. Red carpets cover the ground; velvet-covered chairs abound. This aura persists for about thirty minutes, during which time I really find TOUJOURS GLAMOUR to be a splendid perfume. I am a big fan of both benzoin and violets, which explains part of this composition's appeal to my nose. The problem is that, unlike its more famous neighbors, TOUJOURS GLAMOUR fairly swiftly fizzles out to nearly nothing, and as it fades away, it seems slightly less coherent than in the opening and mid-stages. It's not that the drydown is particularly bad; it's just that it's disappointing after what came before. Similar to the sad specter of a picture-perfect celebrity in a stunning evening gown sashaying her way up to accept her statuette and then sputtering out a string of nonsensical verbiage studded with solecisms. All of which just goes to show once again what we always seem to forget, that you can't judge a book by its cover or a perfume by its bottle, though hope springs eternal that the packaging may be matched by the product inside. In the case of TOUJOURS GLAMOUR, it is entirely feasible (given the modest price) to obsessively reapply the edt and just pretend that it continues to deliver on the promise of those luscious opening minutes. As though the painful acceptance speech never happened at all.

The top note with spices, sour fruit note, and floral garnish is furious. My nose didn’t identify cardamom, red currant, and violet, but the list of initial fragrance notes read here is absolutely plausible. Spices, fruit, and flowers harmonize beautifully, smell naturally pleasant, and create anticipation for what’s to come. Unfortunately, not much more follows, as after the evaporation of the top note, what happens is what occurs with many new releases in the mainstream segment over the last few years: the fragrance drifts off into the usual, seemingly still trendy, quite arbitrary vanilla-sweet-feminine direction. The vanilla part is taken over by heliotrope (vanilla flower, smells practically the same as vanilla) in Toujours Glamour, and it becomes additionally sweet with benzoin resin and musk, while instead of wood, there’s bitter almond for a change. However, the scent impression of the heart and base is the same as with what feels like another 98% of new releases since 2004 in the women’s mainstream sector. It smells pleasant, feminine, and nice; the wearer will hardly ever offend anyone (except in case of overdose), but it’s become sooo boring. I recently read somewhere that perfumers in the mainstream sector use all their art and effort on the top note because marketing research has found that most buyers make their decision for or against a new fragrance just a few minutes after testing it. Apparently, Toujours Glamour is crafted according to this pattern.

My curiosity made me take the plunge and I blind bought this mysterious "lost YSL". My box arrived, somewhat shopworn-I liked that. It's very authentic with only one batch produced to my knowledge. I was reluctant to break the sacred seal. I couldn't wait any longer-it was finally in my hands. I have been a jazz fan since 1989. It's related to the original yet takes a different direction. Down to the smokey cellar of some Parisian jazz club. This is hot, dark, Swangin Jazz. The notes are all over the place. Sandalwood is bold and big like Samsara! It dominates the composition. I love that note, and since its gone forever this bottle is priceless. The opening is sharp and dark green. Bergamot, mint and spices grab your attention and hang around longer than expected. Ylang ylang, carnation, rose and "jazzmine" play for hours amid that rich sandalwood base. It starts to act like an oriental and then it quickly morphs to a classic leather Fougere. Coconut pairs well with coumarin giving it a silky texture. The sandalwood, amber, tonka, patchouli and oakmoss are loud until the end. Like Kouros Fraicheur, it is not a flanker, yet an original lost YSL creation. Both are difficult to find and classic YSL. "It's 4:30AM, I am pretty drunk, and the music keeps roaring on. The piano keeps playing that familiar melody. It's too cold outside to go home." This is one of those nights to remember, indeed. Ah, that sandalwood!

Jazz Prestige is a really bizarre scent, and one of the few whose name perfectly reflects the juice. I am a big fan of jazz, and this scent is indeed “jazzy” as regards of its composition and evolution; it’s daring, creative, playful, unpredictable and most of all, with the same “clashing” structure of a free jazz improvisation. It has a really bold and perfectly crafted interplay of shades and lights, bright notes and darker nuances. What strikes me the most to this extent is the opening phase, which also perfectly integrates the “prestige” feature: an incredibly radiant, fresh, crisp and sharp green-citrus accord with breezy flowers (geranium above all) that, however, smells just deeply different from, well, any other “citrus floral accord” you may think of: not sure what it is due to, but the term that comes to my mind to describe this would be: abstract. Not in a theoretical meaning, rather I think of abstract art: it’s all just colorful, dynamic and almost chaotic, like a Pollock painting. Take a conventional citrus-herbal-floral accord, throw it in a blender, replace it there, here’s Jazz Prestige. And underneath that, a really formal, cozy and classic fougère structure as in the classic Jazz version, a “barbershop” symphony made of sandalwood, lavender, herbs, carnation spices, smoky notes, maybe a hint of leather too. The coexistence of these two “veins” – basically, “classic” and “creative” – is mindblowing. This flanker is a really precious, special and deeply creative rewriting of the original Jazz, which adds both artsy madness and a luxurious feel of golden refinement – due to the peculiar treatment of citrus-greenish flowers notes, again: crisp and clean like a freshly ironed shirt. You know what I thought of too? The “brat pack” group of novelists – McInerney, Bret Easton Ellis, that group of American authors which portrayed the conflicts of the young, wealthy and spoiled generations of the ‘80s and early ‘90s, their pop luxury, their “camp” culture. Not sure why, but I feel Jazz Prestige shares the same “vibe” of many of those characters – it smells “rich”, ironical, bizarre, vibrant, almost naughty. Playing with classic notes like a postmodern composition. And I am not saying it smells like something those guys would wear; I mean more like an olfactive depiction of them. Not sure if that makes sense and surely isn’t helping much to understand this fragrance, so... just this: it smells fantastic and really – really! – ahead of its time. A true gem worth looking for. 9/10

Was "Jazz" a success for YSL back then? At least not a flop, I would claim, since with "Prestige" and "Live" two very high-quality offshoots were still released. And back then, it was well known that one wasn't bombarded with three flankers per year... While I always found "Jazz" good, never outstanding, the recently fluttered "Live Jazz" was even excellent. And what can the "Prestige," which even fewer people know, have or want, that is sandwiched in between? Is it perhaps the lost gem of the series? "Jazz Prestige" can best be described as a rough-green pineapple barbershop scent. A fruitier and more festive version of its father fragrance. Masculine florals, mentholated anise, chilled patchouli. I like it very much. Totally 90s, totally Jazz, totally upscale designer class. The exoticism of the West. The wink of the boss. The soft heart of the macho. A jazz freestyle of the most confident and fluid kind. When fruits didn't have to ooze with sugar and synthetics. When real men could still radiate floral vibes.
