Also reminiscent of the legendary "Insense." Bottle: stylish and typically Jazz Sillage: upscale projection Longevity: 8 hours - back then, one hardly had to make compromises with designer releases! Conclusion: I can actually recommend the Jazz series from YSL consistently. It's a shame about their disappearance. "Jazz Prestige" is a chest-hairy-fruity blend of its two brothers and quite playful, juicy, yet mature and noble enough. Great blend. Not a pretender.

I really loved this Jazz (Prestige) back in the day! A very unique scent that did not represent an imitation of any trend. Yes, unfortunately, one must speak of it in the past tense, as it is no longer available for purchase. I personally find that very unfortunate. :-( Jazz smelled neither distinctly spicy, nor fresh, nor mellow in the top notes. It started directly with a very successful blend of the aforementioned components and moved towards the base, to a pleasantly sparkling softness, without becoming heavy or sweet. A fragrance of the category open-minded, urban freshness with very good longevity! One of the best from YSL! I don't like the new version anymore; it somehow just smells herbal-scratchy. More for Old Spice wearers.

Everything about Signorina was meant to not_impress me. The fact that it's a secondary product to a high-end fashion accessory line, the obviously fruity-floral-gourmand composition, the cute bow, the very pinkness of the perfume. And yet, when I sampled it, I was immediately taken in. Make no mistake, this is not some run of the mill scent ordered by the marketing department so that Ferragamo may have something to console those who can't afford their shoes. Thought, soul and effort have actually been put into this juice. Scentwise, it strikes a balance between coffee shop sweetness and the crisp tartness of Cassis, with a tendency to get sweeter over time. The Panna cotta announced in the base makes itself obvious from the very start and blends well with the florals, of which Peony is the most prominent. Drydown is mostly Musk with maybe just a smidgen of Patchouli. Compared to some of the Miss Dior (Cherie) flankers, Signorina seems to boast much better quality of ingredients. My only minor concern is the Musk which does tend to get a bit shrill when the perfume is applied on fabric. Yet, on skin this doesn't manifest. I've been wearing Signorina every once in a while for some months now, and it's proven a very welcome addition to my collection of stark chypres, full-blown orientals and pearly aldehydes, a tribute and outlet to my inner child whom I finally learned to appreciate.

Salvatore Ferragamo is usually hit or miss with me, but the strange thing is that the very same perfume can be a hit or a miss on two different days! For some reason, the base which appears in most of their fragrances can be appealing or unappealing to me, depending upon, well, who knows what circumstances! In the case of SIGNORINA, the musky base seems a bit less chemically than in either F or F FOR NIGHT (which is the eau de parfum of the "daytime" eau de toilette). The rest of the composition is a fairly familiar refrain: pinkish florality, sweetish patchouli, all quite detectable but without going overboard. The pink pepper must have been wielded with a very light hand, because I barely detect it and am usually quite sensitive to that note. In my experience, pink pepper (baies roses) often overpowers the rest of the components with which it figures in a fragrance. This is a perfectly fine everyday perfume. It's pretty and polite but has just a touch of a naughty edge because of the patchouli and the musk. I am reminded by this creation of La Perla J'AIME, except that J'AIME crosses over the line to the dirty side with a somewhat heavy muskiness which I do not find very appealing. SIGNORINA is more like the younger sister of the racier J'AIME. Still innocent but looking perhaps one day to emulate her older sibling, the cheerleader who got knocked up in the locker room.

When I saw advertisements for this fragrance in magazines some time ago, the thought immediately crossed my mind that there is an attempt to reach the successes of scents like Coco Mademoiselle and Miss Dior. The bottle design strongly resembles the Miss Dior appearance. That's not necessarily a bad thing and is often practiced. One thing the advertising campaign achieved: Mari's curiosity shot through the roof. Checking it out here, the fragrance composition also sounded promising. After Feline's comment, I couldn't hold back any longer. Soon, I stormed into the nearest perfumery with rosy cheeks from excitement. The object of desire was quickly found, even quicker it was sprayed, and just as fast the nose was wrinkled... For a fleeting mini moment, the scent was fresh, the blackcurrant came, waved, but quickly left. Then the fragrance became very floral - and something incredibly musty was added. Could that be the panna cotta? Something definitely smells like bad milk with rotten flowers. No, Mari doesn't like that! This note comes very quickly and stays until the end, making it impossible for me to wear the fragrance. I tried it a few more times, but no, no, this is not going to work out between the Miss and me. Nothing creamy, nothing delicate. Strangely sweet-sour. Just a big BANG and shaking. It actually makes me feel nauseous. I find that sneaky. I'm sure Signorina will find her fans. I will NOT invite her to any of my legendary pajama parties. Ha!

I watch the World Cup with interest - while I appreciate the athletic performance. That "our boys" have been knocked out doesn't bother me, as I found their performance weak. But at the moment, I do feel a tendency towards England rising within me, perhaps because I have experienced beautiful times on the island. I like the British dry humor, accompanied by exquisite politeness. I cannot free myself from sympathies either. And so, the Signorina EDT has long held my sympathy. It is chic, with a kick of cheekiness. Of course, I also want to fairly give the EDP a chance, but I search in vain for that cheeky attitude there. The EDP is more sensible and, due to its rosy notes, more ladylike. Jasmine conveys elegance, and a smoky note feels mature. The berry panna cotta is somewhat delicious but unfortunately fades away too quickly. The other ingredients, especially the patchouli, shine through in their longevity. To stay in World Cup language - this is a Signorina with extension. Although the EDT is more fleeting, I prefer its carefree attitude and its more pointed design. A football game doesn't necessarily gain class through an extension.

A visit to a perfume shop is - to put it bluntly - a bit like (love) life. We have a large market with all kinds of models, colors, shapes; there should be something for everyone’s taste, some test just one and remain loyal to it for a lifetime, while others switch regularly and need fresh air more often. There are also those who never find the right one. Some are true objects of desire, we long for them and want to have them, they exude an incredible allure - and either we eventually dare to approach them or remain unhappily in love for various reasons. And sometimes, we come across ones we never had on our radar. But then we like them right away, so to speak, the legendary love at first sight. That’s how it was for me and Signorina. I would have never noticed this fragrance had it not been on the sale table in January. Here were all those who had to spend Christmas alone and didn’t have the luck of lying under the Christmas tree and making someone happy. What a shame! Signorina was part of a set, red packaging, somewhat clunky design - no wonder this special edition package didn’t sell. But hey, now there was a 40 percent discount! So it was indeed worthy of a sniff, and the perfume saleswoman (or should I say: matchmaker) and I were equally astonished. On my skin, this fragrance is... How should I put it... Delicious! The panna cotta is the note that stands out the most for me, paired with floral peony and fruity currant. Fortunately, I can’t smell any pepper or patchouli, as those are my no-go notes. Here we are again with real life: everyone has some traits within them that the other doesn’t quite like. I was really surprised by how long Signorina stayed with me. Normally, I diligently reapply throughout the day, but here it’s enough to apply the perfume in the morning. Plus point for loyalty. I also find it pretty, pink and bows are totally my thing. Overall, I think Signorina is an underrated gourmand that comes across as very feminine and whose sweetness is also office-friendly. Those who find LVEB too heavy and are looking for something smarter will like this one. If the squeaky, intrusive quality of Sì doesn’t appeal to you, you might find happiness with Signorina. And if you think the strawberry in Celebrate Now could have been designed a bit less candy-like, you should take a sniff of Signorina. Well, we have many ideas and plans - but who knows where love falls!

...was my first thought after spraying it on. Sour blackcurrant in the background and a lot of pepper stinging the nose. The latter is always tricky for me anyway. Plus, a massive sillage after 3 sprays. With that, I thought the matter was already settled. I would have given the fragrance 4 points. Certainly no more. But wait...

Oh this bottle, so sweet, so adorable! It caught my eye first! And then the scent, mmmh, I just find it heavenly. The blackcurrant, summery, fresh. The floral bouquet with the rose and peony pairs very well with the berry and makes the roses even juicier, more full-bodied. The erotic aura of the flowers is subtle yet exciting.

I got to know Signorina through a sample that positively surprised me, but during testing, it didn't exactly evoke storms of enthusiasm. I was amazed to notice in the following days that, standing in front of my perfume cabinet, despite the large selection of highly valued fragrance favorites, I repeatedly chose to wear Signorina once again. What was that?

. . . I have discovered that this Signorina pleases me and my nose. Hm, I would have never bought it - no idea why. Maybe because I don't like the name Ferragamo *g* Silly, I know. Since I really, really like blackcurrant and rose, I managed to get the Signorina in a swap game. I admit, with the first spray I wrinkled my nose and thought... ah yes, I thought.

Having snagged a sample, I tried it right away and quickly found it unsuitable: this Signorina is too loud, too peppery, too floral, simply too abrasive. On my skin, the top note consists solely of pepper. Pepper that burns in the nose and closes it off, blocking almost all receptors. No, this is not my Signorina, I thought, and tried to wash it off quickly with water.

As I clicked through the various Kouros variants to find the version I have of "Kouros (After Shave Lotion) | Yves Saint Laurent," I couldn't help but be surprised by how often members of this community apparently visit train station restrooms. I must admit that I can't recall any situation off the top of my head where I would have been bold enough to voluntarily undergo this olfactory (and sociological) martyrdom. However, I am quite sure that "Kouros (After Shave Lotion) | Yves Saint Laurent" does not smell like a free-to-use train station toilet in the year 2025. Not even the toilet cleaner association, which also comes to mind for me with some citrus notes, can I endorse. Kouros may not be a beautiful, certainly not a gentle scent DNA, but it is definitely a perfume fragrance and, my goodness, an unmistakable statement. I smell a 40-year-old aftershave here that would probably be sold today as an EdP Extrait. An aftershave with an animalistic base tone, whose sillage fills houses, and whose over-the-top fruit-flower combination is almost painful. There is a force in this scent that makes the thought ridiculous that a man would rub two or three spritzes of this behemoth between his hands in the morning of 1984 and then pat his freshly shaved face with it. The fact that it must have been this way shows me how long the 80s really are gone. Only a time when chain smoking was common in trains, offices, restaurants, and lecture halls, and where cross-border hypermasculinity was the order of the day, could produce such a natural force of scent. Personally, I would not want to wear "Kouros (After Shave Lotion) | Yves Saint Laurent" in public, but as a cultural historical document and for nostalgic reasons, I can warmly recommend testing a vintage version of one of the Kouros offshoots.

In my statement, I asked how it can be that the AS receives almost sky-high ratings, while the EdT gets a loooong boring middle position (perhaps also because it seems there’s apparently no alternative for this scent between “10” or “0” :))). And the AS hasn’t been commented on yet?! So, the AS must be absolutely insane. The fundamentally friendly atmosphere here in this forum is probably the reason why the obvious fitting answer to my (stupid) question wasn’t given: “Don’t ask, just buy it yourself….”. Done now. For about 40,- euros. The EdT only costs a mere 7,- euros more *scratches head*. Praising Kouros and rating it well - regardless of the variant and fragrance concentration - is not difficult for me. I totally love this scent. That’s why I wondered why there is such a noticeable difference in the rating of the fragrance. I’ll try to capture this now, but I’ll keep it short: The AS smells like the EdT :))) Hooray, what a revelation. It’s probably simply due to the scent development, or the less intense penetration of the nose, that the AS is rated better. After the (for me) intense alcohol cloud (felt “worse” than with the EdT) and nuclear sillage, the scent indeed becomes much softer after about an hour. Somehow, the AS then smells like Kouros used to smell! However, this unfortunately passes too quickly - at least on my skin. The scent clings to every corner of the face but remains rather close to the body over time (imagine this: There are 10 narcotized colleagues lying in the hallway….typical false self-assessment :))). So for me, I have now found the following combination. The AS refreshes, doesn’t burn, nourishes, and simply smells a bit more restrained than the EdT. Moreover, it’s just nice to take a bottle in hand in the morning after a (wet) shave and pretend that it’s normal to use AS instead of EdT. Okay, for all Kouros opponents, here’s the result: I now use both (see imagination). However, the EdT is now (significantly) used less (1 spray, okay maybe also 2…;)) and gives the AS its missing endurance for the day and possibly evening. This way, you at least avoid the unbelievable bad habit (by the way, of a former colleague!!!) of shamelessly rubbing oneself with an AS continuously in front of everyone to get through the day :)). Edit: For this review, I used the current production. I know (used) but (also) the vintage versions. Update 04/23: Now it seems to have been taken out of the program. Everywhere "out of stock".

Scent It is a sweet fragrance and a bit musky and tiny 'citrussy'. The scent is similar from top notes until base notes. Longevity The scent's longevity of this fragrance is medium. For non 4-seasons countries, it is suitable for evening and night use. The longevity can hold around 4-5 hours. For the 4-seasons countries, the longevity is around to 5-6 hours. This fragrance is very suitable in the night and for sleeping. Performance The performance of this fragrance is okay, especially for evening and night use. Sillage The sillage is regular. The sillage is quite good on the top notes, in the first 30 minutes after use it. Uniqueness The uniqueness of the bottle design is over-shadow the scent of the fragrance. The scent is an ordinary scent. However, even many articles mentioned that this is a female fragrance, the truth is, this is a UNISEX fragrance. Bottle Design The design is a teddy bear. Among the most attractive bottle design for a fragrance. Toy collector is a must to own this fragrance.

The best marketing gimmick of last year undoubtedly came from Moschino. And for me, everything about the idea, the artistic execution, and the campaign just works. It feels interesting, funny, unusual, and perfectly calculated to attract attention. If a pleasant, beautiful fragrance had emerged from it, it would have been a completely successful launch. However, that is not the case for me. I perceive Toy merely as a classic men's fragrance that I absolutely do not like. Everything I find unpleasant is mixed in, leaving a fresh, green scent that mainly reminds me of lavender. A bit spicy here, a bit citrusy there - simply not my thing. If you prefer a classic men's cologne, you probably can't go wrong here. I had already thought that my impression would likely end this way, but I assumed that at least there would be a certain versatility in the fragrance. However, as it is, Toy just feels too banal to me and somehow does not do justice to its campaign. That Moschino as a brand had crazy ideas even before collaborating with Jeremy Scott is proven by the Cheap and Chic bottle inspired by Olivia Oil. I still find the Toy campaign extremely successful. It made me want to test the fragrance. My problem with the scent may also stem from the fact that Moschino fragrances generally seem to be too firmly anchored in the fresh category. Therefore, I fear that hardly any fragrance from the brand will match my taste. Nevertheless, the successor this year is also hard to surpass in terms of curiosity and clever marketing, making this fragrance one that you would also want to test.

My niece is currently into sweet fragrances. Recently, I went out to eat with her and recognized her scent “La vie est Belle.” This surprised her. “How do you know that? You don’t like sweet fragrances, do you?” “That’s true, especially that one, but I test everything and sometimes the whole bus smells like that fragrance.” It’s worth noting that I have come to enjoy sweeter scents a bit, thanks to Parfumo. I noted about Emozione: Sweet round peach with a citrus note, fresh rose accompanied by a hint of powder, chypre that makes you want to bite your wrist, lively and friendly! Slightly nutty-spicy, it plays in the same league as S by Escada and Si by Armani. “Emozione” releases joyful emotions in me, the name says it all. The peach smells authentic, and the peach sweetness doesn’t become sticky thanks to the citrus additions of bergamot. After a short time, the fruity note is supported by a fresh rose, accompanied by a hint of powder. The whole thing has a spicy, somewhat nutty-almond note that gives the fragrance its own character and prevents it from becoming an interchangeable floral-fruity mix for summer. To my regret, I am still waiting in vain for the wild leather note. The scent ends in a well-groomed and neat base of fine musk, with patchouli only faintly noticeable. Emozione is not a fragrance that will make history in perfumery, but it is one that lifts my mood and takes the gloom away from gray rainy days. That’s quite a lot, isn’t it? Since sweetness in fragrances usually annoys me quickly, I also know that my relationship with Emozione is more of a hot flirt than true love. Longevity and sillage are in the medium range, best wearing time from spring to autumn, oh what, it also has a mood-lifting effect in winter. Probably not suitable for men, except for sniffing on their partner. And after I have added about 25 fragrances from my collection to the virtual collection section “Ready for leaving” (more will follow), I already feel freer, and the physical separation will follow. And now I have space again… Thank you, Dusnatli.

The day before yesterday, a special friend gifted me two special fragrances for my 36th birthday, both of which I had already grown quite fond of on her and could easily imagine on my own skin. That's why "special," because both have the ability to convey a bit of coziness to me when everything else seems dull and hostile. One of them is "Emozione." As soft as the peach skin itself, the scent of white peaches blends with the powderiness of a charming iris. While the rose accords lend an elegant volume, heliotrope keeps it feeling light like a whisper. The white musk combined with patchouli underpins everything with a pleasant warmth, cozy and fine like a cashmere sweater. However, that is just the part of the fragrance that can be sniffed. Its effect goes far beyond that! It makes gray days appear brighter and fills moments of inner emptiness with a great deal of comfort! A fragrance with an aura of gentleness that is unmatched. For me, "Emozione" has become pure, scent-turned feeling!

Hello dear ones! I'm on a roll, so here’s another comment on one of my favorite fragrances: Emozione (“Emotion”) by Salvatore Ferragamo, who was originally an Italian shoe designer but launched his first fragrance in 1960. There are now about 90 fragrances, for her and him. I must say, Emozione is by far my favorite of all the fragrances I know from this brand. I came across it through a swap - a stroke of luck and a bullseye. Yes, fragrances evoke emotions. They can stir you up, act as aphrodisiacs, but also calm and soothe, lift your mood, and conjure up memories. The scent "Emozione" is, briefly described, (Nivea) cream with peach on white musk, so it is primarily fruity and creamy with a powdery sweetness (just right for me). I believe there is an undeniable similarity to the vintage Trésor by Lancôme. I can also detect a light, fine leather note. As simple as all this sounds, the perfume feels elegant, complex, and delicate, more than I would have expected. I feel very balanced and at peace with myself when wearing it. It just suits me! Due to its noble aura, "Emozione" is suitable for both everyday use and going out. I must praise the sprayer of the bottle; it releases a fine mist that distributes evenly and not in droplets. The longevity and sillage are above average. This fragrance is also available online at sensationally affordable prices. My recommendation for women who are looking for something special but don’t want to spend a hundred euros.

My husband and I were at our local only perfumery last Saturday to redeem my last birthday gift card for this year. I had in mind something: powdery, for certain moments/occasions, for evenings and not too floral. The sales assistant showed me Emozione, and I had removed this scent from my wishlist because previous comments had somewhat put me off. Well, whatever! I have ATTIMO and I love it very much! Let's just hold Emozione under my and Mr. Baum's noses, because it probably won't be that bad. I sprayed the scent on the test strip and held it under my and his nose! What a wonderful soft and elegant whiff of fragrance! At first, slightly fruity (citrusy) and then slightly sweet, powdery, elegant, and soft! I also detected something floral, but not too floral, and I recognized a light hint of rose. My husband was also quite taken with it. Emozione had to go on my forearm, and it simply smelled noble, harmonious, slightly powdery, soft... The whole composition is a bit hard for me to describe, but my husband, the sales assistant, and I agree that Emozione suits me as a woman. The bottle is also very noble and beautiful. After a few minutes of consideration and in response to my husband's question ("Honey, are you taking that with you?"), a 30 ml bottle came into my possession. I kept bringing my nose to my arm because Emozione is so lovely! The scent lingers on me in the mid-range and lasts for several hours. In the evening in front of the computer and on parfumo, I then realized that my 30 ml bottle does not contain the chain that I saw on the tester and that it is the work of my favorite perfumer Alberto Morillas. I find several of his perfumes really great/beautiful and suitable for me. Furthermore, it belongs to the Chypre-Floral fragrance family, and I have now realized in my 5 years as a "parfuma" that I find this family really beautiful/great and also suitable! I will wear Emozione for certain occasions/moments and/or in the evenings, as I find it quite elegant for everyday work and leisure!

Since Salvatore Ferragamo captivated me with his extremely green fig scent for/against this ingredient, simultaneously enchanting & now making me allergic/hypersensitive, I somehow inextricably associate the noble Italian luxury brand with spring - green, sunny, cheerful, light, Dolce Vita in a serious way. And that is exactly what the new women's fragrance Emozione from the gentlemen of Italy embodies. Moreover, it is finally a scent that fits perfectly with the chosen season of release. Emozione is a cheerful, life-affirming spring fragrance - it awakens good feelings, love, joy & curiosity, making the name quite fitting. However, one should not expect overly passionate feelings; rather, it is sweet, cool, pretty & bright. A kind of fruity-green chypre, it bridges older, soapy classics like Cerruti's 1881 to the sweet little fruits of recent years. Peach meets iris, rose kisses musk, green smooches yellow. A positive new release that hopefully doesn't fly too far under the radar of everyone - so Dougletten: Please continue to distribute samples like to my friend & drum up some publicity! Bottle: Very pretty, almost Lalique-like. Sillage: still manageable even in warm summer Longevity: light entertainment for 5-6 hours. Conclusion: S. Ferragamo remains true to his subtly Italian line even for women & is always worth a test - true disappointments are rather rare!

On the weekend, I was sniffing new scents in a well-stocked perfume shop. That's when I spotted Emozione and sprayed it on. At first, it was very fresh; I even thought I could smell a hint of mint...yes, yes, I know...that can't be ;) Then the fragrance became soft yet still fresh...a bit like freshly washed laundry that has dried outside in the garden.

First of all ...'Noble and fine? That could easily be another ...Ferragamo' ...........:) But now: 'Emotion after emotion ...' ...........feeling follows feeling, as Eros Ramazzotti once beautifully sang, back in 1984 ...

Today, during a sunny city stroll, I spritzed Emozione as I passed by. The positive scent matches the sunshine and the relaxed mood. I am not in a hurry - I can dawdle. And the fragrance takes its time as well. The opening of bergamot and peach is bright and pleasant. The iris adds some depth, and the rose is soft and floral.
In recent years, I have hardly ever owned perfumes that are suitable for summer. I tend to lean heavily towards scents that belong to the autumn/winter category.

Yes, I like such classic scents that are rounded off with a hint of chypre. Yes, it is also true that there have been or still are similar ones. For me, this is a beautiful, soft rose scent with a touch of powder from the iris root. Emozione, the name fits the fragrance. Rose scents always have an emotional statement. The iris adds a hint of baby powder.

My mother still has some of this perfume extract in exquisite flatten down bottle. She used to wear this one on special winter nights many years ago, when my nose was starting to notice there were immense unknown territories of excitement out there for me to explore them. This was quite unusual when it was launched so I find myself intrigued by it. I still find it playful, joyful, rampant, boon and sweet. One of the few 90's fruity classic scents I admire.

I can now remember why "Yvresse" felt so foreign to me, even though I owned both the perfume and the Eau de Toilette back then. There was that legal dispute over the name, which Yves Saint Laurent promptly lost. The name "Champagne" is protected and could therefore no longer be used for the fragrances. As a champagne lover and after not-so-great experiences with YSL fragrances, I was intrigued by the bottle. It was designed to resemble a cork wrapped in gold foil. A truly special "eyecatcher"! Despite the name, nothing sparkled or whispered; no, something warm, heavy, and spicy presented itself. For the scent was a completely new experience: so many spices, some of which were ordinary kitchen spices, had never before been combined in a fragrance. Someone had clearly raided Grandmère's kitchen. Together with mostly Central European fruits and flowers, it managed to create a truly opulent, almost oriental fragrance composition. Foreign and yet somehow familiar! It was fruity-floral despite everything, until after a while the somewhat more exotic base note made its presence known. I particularly remember Styrax; that was a completely new experience for me: the scent became "black and warm." And thus incredibly exciting! After "Opium," which almost every woman wore at its peak, "Champagne," as I still call it, was an unusually rich, exotic fragrance. Not golden and warm, like, for example, the artworks of Jean Patou from that time; no, this was a provocation of a very special kind. Not for women who want to go through life inconspicuously or for gentle, soft beings. This fragrance creation from YSL was exotic: very feminine, sophisticated, and incredibly sexy! One could definitely get a little tipsy from it! I almost fear that the time for such fragrances has somewhat passed. When was the last time there was a woman to whom the term "vamp" would have applied? Perhaps this very special fragrance was discontinued for that reason? Surely not just because the name had to be changed, thus missing that "certain something." However, I recently realized, while wandering down the "street of scent memories," that these bottles must have been in the large beautiful tin box that somehow disappeared from my closet. That is annoying; there were other treasures in there too. In any case, I now notice while writing that I loved this "noble water" very much. Even though I had long forgotten it. But did I really forget it?

Again the usual: in my younger years, I owned the EDT, later I managed to get the Extrait. My first EDT has since dried up, but I was able to buy two intact small sprayers. As you can see in my pictures, they all (except for a Splash Mini) still bear the original name "Champagne". With the EDT, I clearly perceive the yellow stone fruits (peach, apricot, and nectarine), which remind me more of fruit liqueur than champagne, as this perfume has too much sweetness for that. The Extrait is very similar in itself, but in my impression, it's a tad more robust than the EDT. Nevertheless, both versions have something sparkling (perhaps due to the lychee or even the mint), although this note comes through a bit stronger in the Extrait (which could also be due to the possibly differing ages of the vintages). But peach punch does indeed contain sparkling wine, so the (original) name "Champagne" is quite fitting. However, "Champagne/Yvresse" cannot be compared to the fruit punch-like perfumes from the Escada summer limited editions, which (since 2001) are significantly sweeter and sometimes come across as a bit synthetic (and I say this even though I still like them and buy the new limited edition every year). In my younger years, I wasn't an enthusiastic fan of Carnival (as we call it in Bavaria), but now and then I did go to a costume ball. Since my mother's death in 2013, that is forever over - I will never dance again; the dark half of my life has begun. But for such occasions, I always found "Champagne" quite fitting back then. A sparkling-fruity-floral, moderately sweet scent against the winter blues. And for the evening, the Extrait version - as so often - is a little more elegant and refined.

Somehow, I’m on a little vintage retro trip, and I don’t know what made me buy this drop. Well, it was probably the bottle that invited me to write about it. The old classic bottle with a stopper that tends to fall off is a real eye-catcher and elegant... Vintage style. In the first few seconds, I’m rather surprised as it’s not as alcohol-heavy as I thought... that’s probably due to the mint... the caraway is quite noticeable and makes it heavy and spicy from the start. It develops a bit more fleetingly and almost smells like tea, lingering well on the skin. Now I’ve let some time pass and I still perceive it well in the base as a good companion for the night. It becomes sweeter and more flavorful. I don’t really smell the coconut. Amber, benzoin, and cedar are noticeable to me and I don’t find them disturbing. Not a scent as expected. Champagne is well captured, but I find carbonated tea more fitting. But how does that sound? Carbonic Acid Tea??? No way... Champagne!!! Dance, men, the princess is in the mood!!

A bomb of anise and peach with flowers that last all day Fruity with mint and anise at the start, followed by a light cinnamon scent with a very strong floral aroma about an hour after spraying the fragrance. The base is what the perfume revolves around, a strange scent like the name of the perfume. Anise returns to the facade and we notice patchouli with wood and vanilla and a very warm and deep floral scent that differs from the flowers we are used to. The opening of the fragrance is similar to 17 Rosso by Roberto Ugolini, however the latter has no anise scent and the mint is, in contrast to champagne, cold. A winter-autumn fragrance that is never suitable for non-cold weather and is very creative on snowy and rainy days.

To start off, this is a great perfume! You get cardamom and nutmeg, sadly only hints of coffee, and a powdery accord very reminiscent of Dior Homme Intense (2011) and "Gentleman Givenchy Réserve Privée | Givenchy" . Another user mentiomed that this has "Babycat | Yves Saint Laurent" vibes, but I don't get those: there is no leatheriness present, nor any vanillish notes. To me this is much more reminiscent of "Cardamom Coffee (Perfume) | Lush" . "Cardamom Coffee (Perfume) | Lush" has more coffee, that's for sure! But this takes that cardamom accord and surrounds it in a powdery cloud, the ginger peeks through occasionally. As it dries down, floral notes appear, giving it that "Toy Boy | Moschino" florality, even though it's very different to the predecessor. I was very hyped for this and so far th3 hype is deserved!

Fragrance Review: First thoughts, the opening has an aromatic, warm spicy sweet woody scent, almost similar to Burberry Hero flankers but sweeter. • Toy Boy 2 is mostly a sweet woody amber vibe with a touch of coffee aromatic scent, versatile, mass appealing and completely different compare to the original Toy Boy. • I sprayed a total of 5 times. Twice behind each ear, twice on the front of neck, and once in front of my chest. The longevity is good and lasts approximately 8+ hours on my skin. This fragrance projects poorly though, with about a 6 ft radius for 30 minutes, and a skin scent after. (Depends on skin types) Overall Rating (8.5/10) While it's a unique release by Moschino, it does smell bitter sweet at times and I know the projection for this fragrance just isn't the best for a sweet woody scent. It's definitely suitable for the autunm/Winter Seasons. PERFUMER: Jordi Fernández

Unexpected start, beautiful first impression. Fresh, woody, briefly leather-like, deep. Then floral and lovely, pleasing. Shifting between roasting aromas and dark resins and equally dark sweetness. I soon perceive roasted coffee beans and a gentle smokiness. The scent of caramelized rice from childhood or caramelized sunflower seeds on the palate. It is by no means a gourmand, merely my personal association with its resinousness. Less interesting is it after the drydown with its sweetly lovely floral notes and somewhat ordinary sweetness. The woody spiciness is rather discreetly perceptible. More creamy, unless a subtle soft-bitter leather shines through again. For the asking full price, I wouldn't have indulged in the successor, but the Parfumo-Souk is always good for a fair price find, and as a collector, I didn't want to leave my "Toy Boy" standing alone. As outstandingly unique as the predecessor, the EdP fails to become. A bit disillusioning. Here, marketing has trimmed the lawn strictly according to statistics. Accordingly, less creative. However, it is somewhat better than its competitors. Compared to its predecessor, it is less complex, significantly more pleasing, and can be placed in the "Phantom", "Victory", or even Initio universe in terms of craftsmanship. You can definitely sense the synthetics here. nulltheless, it is less densely packed and, in terms of progression and composition, more interesting ...and successful. It offers a circulating exchange within its fragrance notes and varying impressions. It is an evening perfume, suitable for pleasant, sociable coffee bar visits of an intimate nature. No controversial sensually wild marketing representation like the predecessor. Yet the well-groomed man, who knows how to dress neatly, will also know how to use this one in his leisure time, as well as for seduction.

I have always found Toy Boy to be really good for a designer fragrance. It lacked nothing in creativity, and overall it was very successful, but it never quite made it to a purchase for me. When I saw that there was going to be a new version, I simply had to test it. Aside from the fact that the bottle is in a beautiful matte black, the scent completely convinced me from the very first test. It opens extremely sweet and creamy, with a hint of Babycat that is perceptible to my nose, combined with the typical Toy Boy DNA, but presented in a more modern way. In the heart, spicy cardamom unfolds, carried by a coffee-like sweetness that is not dry but almost resinous. This is accompanied by ginger, which gives the fragrance that certain something. In the drydown, some of the familiar Toy Boy character comes through. Angular Akigalawood takes over, contrasting sweetness and spiciness that give the fragrance character and depth. Woody, almost powdery and mature, with an extremely strong projection and remarkably long-lasting durability. A successful release, in my opinion.

... basement club. He wears a brown leather jacket with a white shirt unbuttoned down to his navel. His blonde chest hair is spilling out. He positions himself at the bar between an attractive woman and an equally attractive man. He orders an espresso and a whisky. Both the woman and the man are drawn to the toy boy. Upon applying this fragrance, the first thing that hits the nose is a sharp dark spicy leather scent. A coffee aroma mixes in with a hint of pepper. This perfume is earthy and resinous with just a touch of floral accords. This scent is masculine and dirty. The longevity and sillage are good. Here we have a men's fragrance that differs from the original. In the original, the dark rose is dominant, while here it is the dark leather. I can't really imagine this scent on women, but as always, ladies, please test it for yourselves. I would say the entry age is around 25 years and open-ended upwards. During the day, I can see it in the office, at a lunch, while shopping, or with friends in a café. In the evening, for a date, in a bar, in a club, at dinner, or even at the theater, it also works well. Anyone who enjoys a sharp dark spicy peppery earthy resinous floral leather scent with a coffee twist is exactly in the right place and could have fun. But beware, this is a fragrance that can also rub people the wrong way. Then especially.

On the contrary, while his shiny brother comes roaring around the corner at full throttle (I love him), this bear comes to me like Baloo dancing out of the forest and calls, "hug me, for I love you and want to be your friend!" So he approaches me: scruffy, beautifully cuddly, and not at all animalistic.

It was in the autumn of 1978 when I met you! You were then in a beautiful bottle without a spray... great, provocative, the look and the name symbolized the forbidden! You were purchasable, but not cheap. You were sultry, but not vulgar. You were sinful, but not evil. You were a rebel, but elegant. You were everything I absolutely wanted, because good and lovely little flowers were repulsive to me. My timid attempts at self-discovery with the scents of a friend, Lavin Arpège and Chanel No 5 went completely wrong, those were fragrances for "ladies" and I was too young and not at all ladylike..... But I was finally old enough to wear you, your scent was Rock'n'Roll! But the price of almost 100.00 DM was a problem, I had my first own apartment, so rent and utilities, phone, television and my income was limited, there was no room for luxury...... what to do? Quite simple, I lived on canned ravioli (cold), toast and cheap jam for 3 weeks!!! Then... unforgettable.... the first contact.... this feeling of lifting the heavy glass stopper and your scent on my skin. You were my first great love and I will never forget you. You wrote fragrance history, nothing was the same afterwards. Today you have changed, the wildcat has neatly manicured her sharp claws and purrs instead of roaring. But that's okay.... I will never forget my first great love. And .... suddenly even my mom loved you and wore you on her last journey at 96 years old.

"It was down in Chinatown, that I met the Opium queen...." So sang Amanda Lear in 1977 in her disco song Queen of Chinatown. And coincidentally, that year also saw the release of the often controversial Opium by YSL. The disco wave was at its peak, and fashion was shifting from platform shoes and bell-bottoms to glitter, satin fabrics, and sometimes daring outfits that showed a lot of skin. The somewhat harsh and green fragrances of the early 70s no longer fit this new vibe. It was time for opulent and sensual scents. I owe it to dear Susan that I now own both an intact EdT and an EdP of the 1977 version of Opium, and what could be more fitting than to compare the two versions. One thing is for sure: in terms of longevity and sillage, all versions, including the Extrait, are on par. In other words, Opium lasts like crazy and effortlessly fills a ballroom. Accordingly, the fragrance must be dosed carefully. Too much can, like the namesake narcotic, cloud the senses and lead to physical reactions such as discomfort or shortness of breath. The EdT behaves somewhat harsher in direct comparison and has a slightly soapy opening. The floral components come a bit more to the forefront, and the spices are somewhat less intense. Additionally, the fragrance is less sweet in the base. The EdP is, like the Extrait, a bit spicier, softer, and sweeter in the base. Moreover, I perceive the scent on the skin as if it were lightly glowing or shimmering. The abundance of notes is masterfully intertwined, and at no stage does any note disturbingly come forward. I will not make a comparison with the current version, as it cannot really hold a candle to this olfactory masterpiece. Whether one likes the scent or not, it was style-defining, and there were indeed some imitators in the more affordable price segment back then. I will wear both versions with delight, regardless of what my surroundings may think.

In 1971, Robert Altman directed his legendary anti-Western 'McCabe & Mrs. Miller'. The film tells the story of the gambler McCabe (Warren Beatty), who arrives at a godforsaken place in the Northwest of the United States around the turn of the last century and opens a saloon. He meets Mrs. Miller (Julie Christie), who opens a brothel there. McCabe falls for her, and she is quite fond of him as well, but she always keeps the relationship on a business level. In the end, he is shot in the deep snow while she, entranced, smokes opium to Leonard Cohen's haunting voice. Julie Christie plays Mrs. Miller in a wonderfully damaged way - with eyes that are sometimes steely and then again clouded, almost extinguished. Mrs. Miller is a businesswoman - confident and self-determined - which is not a given for an unmarried woman in the Wild West. She is aware of her physical charms - after all, she lives off selling them - and yet has an almost tragic softness and gentleness beyond her worldly hardness, which Altman captures in pale dark gray, pulsating reddish-brown, and enchantingly muted ashen images. Before opium lovers now indignantly exclaim: 'loewenherz said it smells like a madam...' - no, that is not what he says. Nevertheless, Opium is a mature, physical fragrance and a polarizing one - at least in this 'old', i.e., original version. (Its younger version and its offshoots are tamer.) It comes from a time when orientals were still sultry floral and amber-sweaty - and with a nose socialized in the present, disturbingly not-sweet for a women's fragrance. Demanding. A lot of everything. Sensuality and sinfulness in ashen dark gray reddish-brown. And a bit melancholic. Conclusion: the Opium in the Eau de Parfum variant that I smelled was a finger-high remnant in a nearly forgotten bottle at the back of a top shelf in the bathroom of a lady friend who presumably hasn’t used it for decades. It is hard to say how intact its condition still is - with 'old orientals' like this, that is particularly difficult. And yet it tells me of Mrs. Miller, who sits in the bath with a clouded gaze smoking opium (and in my imagination wears it), while the pale snow outside sweeps through the town.

Salvatore Ferragamo and its crew named Acqua Essenziale, e.g., Essential Water, to this cologne, and that name suits flawlessly. By magic, the perfumers who created Acqua Essenziale have invented a new molecule found inside, which mimics the scent of water. Acqua Essenziale is the first of three fragrances with the same name, followed by Acqua Essenziale Blu and Acqua Essenziale Colonia. The redolence fascinated me from the very first sniff. I remember I was strolling with a friend of mine, and we tested it when it was launched in the market. Unexpectedly, or hopefully, I got it as a present for my birthday. What do I feel? Acqua Essenziale is an olfactory trip that evokes a feeling of absolute freedom. The combination of an essential natural element, clear water, and the highest authenticity, essence. As I write this review, I listen to soft ambient music, distant, relaxing, calming. In the background, there is a cuddly drizzle. If I close my eyes, it seems to me to be immersed in a tropical forest, the drops pattering on the green leaves, the green and earthy scents released into the air. The presentation to my taste is one of the most successful ever: simple, with the logo placed at the base that gives that extra touch and makes the bottle truly special. Acqua Essenziale is a blend of delicate citrus, flowers, and musk wood. It belongs to the fougére family, and there is no question about it. After application, it immediately flooded my olfactory system with a wave of precious citrus and balsamic notes. I feel the sweet and sour grapefruit, crunchy green notes of peppery mint, a sweet mandarin, and a riot of lemon leaves. Mint, lavender, and petitgrain lemon create a kind of sharp, refreshing, and spicy aromatic scent that assails the nose, a camphorous aroma that has a clinical, sharp, disinfectant-like odor. The fragrance heart turns into Irish Spring bar soap as if the aquatic freshness turned into mountain spring freshness. Sharp and clean. It reveals aromatic aspects of rosemary and lavender, with the support of green geranium leaves. The fougére is palpable. But what reigns in the intermediate phase is Cascalone, which infuses an aquatic breath into the fragrance. It is a fresh, synthetic molecule with aqueous, flowery, and clean undertones of freshwater; a sweeter, more watery version of Calone with a transparent floral signature, and without the fruity melon-like aroma. In the dry-down, the scent turns woody and musky. Here I feel the touch of the patchouli, followed by shine vetiver, and again a riot of musky accord from the Helveltolide. It is a stylish musky note with a fruity pear aspect for those not familiar with such a molecule. It is one of the few musks that appears from the very beginning as a top note." Ultimately, Acqua Essenziale is a precious accord of vibrant freshness combined with the aromatic and woody notes of the Mediterranean. Because it is enigmatic, polite, gentle, wise, and slightly floral, I find it perfect for ceremonies, weddings, graduations, and other lively and unforgettable activities. It's not an overwhelming fragrance, so you can easily use it both day and night. Try Acqua Essenziale if you like fresh and traditional fougére-type colognes. I feel the longevity and projection are average; it lasts all day on me. Versatile. I like it very much. It reminds me of a deserted place on a rainy day, without a luxurious or sophisticated atmosphere, simply a meeting between the greenery of a pristine place with water. My best compliments, Mr. Alberto Morillas, you deserve it. People who passed me always ask me for the name of this perfume. Since it is not very demanding, I often wear it on hot days when I don't know what to wear or when I find myself in contexts where the choice of perfume is difficult for me. Acqua Essenziale has a casual soul, perhaps one of the most casual I know at the moment. I based the review on a 100ml bottle I have owned since November 2015. -Elysium

This is a very good fragrance that I would put up against any other designer aquatic on the market! Acqua Essenziale opens with an aromatic top of mint, lemon leaf, rosemary, and lavender. It's an accord that smells sweet, fresh, and clean in a modern, "I just got out of the shower and used some sporty body wash" kind of way. There's an oceanic aspect to it as well, but it comes across as more of an abstract ideal of the mind than any real, natural smell you may find near the sea. Seabreezes are typically not as sweet or clean as that which is presented here...no problem for me. It's well composed, and while you can pick up on a slight synthetic quality up close, for the most part Essenziale is smooth and watery without that annoying scratchiness that seems to be a trademark of cheaper aquatics. It produces a very pleasant sillage that although familiar to some degree, is done the right way. To elaborate, I'm most impressed by the texture of Essenziale--the light, airy, watery quality that aptly matches its scent, while diffusing gently around its subject. Acqua di Gio possesses this quality as well--where the smell and texture sit perfectly together, and take the fragrance to a higher level beyond the norm. There have been a lot of comparisons made between Bleu de Chanel and Acqua Essenziale, and I agree that they smell quite similar. However, I think Essenziale is perhaps the superior fragrance due in part to this often taken for granted element of texture. What I mean is that it seems to possess the appropriate consistency for its smell, whereas Bleu can seem at times too heavy or chunky for its own good. Therefore, the performance of Acqua Essenziale is quite effective. It works well in warmer temperatures without every becoming cloying or irritating, and doesn't fall apart as some fragrances can in the heat. Essenziale is linear for the most part, its dry down a nondescript fade into a typical white, musky-woody base. I'm okay with this because for about 4 or 5 hours I get the very pleasant, excellently composed sillage described above, and I have no desire for it to change. Projection is just right. Longevity could be better, but it's adequate. I would give Essenziale a solid 80--85 out of 100. If you're tired of the whole aquatic genre, that's understandable. However, if you're looking for a designer aquatic you can pick up at the mall or online for a decent price, this is a very good option to consider. And if you're a fan of this style of fragrance, this one's definitely worth adding to your wardrobe.
wonderful. i love it and i am glad to have it .after seven hours i can feel it in my skin .silage and longevity are very good .

Acqua Essenziale, one of my all time favorites, my first oceany cologne as well. Reminds me of my young teens. The opening smells clean and inviting with the lemon, grapefruit and mint, they combine to form a wonderful blend of fresh notes. The heart of this fragrance is a floral, somewhat delicate touch adding complexity to the opening, and in the base forms a muskey touch. Truly an underrated scent and will wear until I die. Preforms like a typically fresh scent. And the longevity is suprisingly better than expected. I was able to get a full size bottle for just $23 usd. A true bargain. I recommend this to anyone in need of a cheap, clean and reliable scent Scent: 9/10 Longevity: 6/10 Projection 8/10 Notes: 8/10 Bottle: 7/10 Cost: 11/10

The bottle design reveals it right away: This is all about summer, good mood, and lightness. These attributes cannot be denied when it comes to the contents. Especially in comparison to many other purely fresh, summer-oriented men’s fragrances, "Acqua Essenziale" does not have to hide in terms of naturalness and harmony. At the beginning, there is the rather typical mix of lemon and mint notes, invigorating for sure, although unspectacular. I can still detect a hint of honeydew melon. Its great advantage, particularly from the heart phase onward, is the quality of the ingredients; there is no artificiality encountered, at least none that is obvious. Only the marine notes seem a bit "forced," but in conjunction with the other elements, it’s acceptable. The ingredient list above seems overly embellished to me; the complexity that one might suspect is definitely not present in the fragrance. Neither vetiver, rosemary, nor patchouli can I identify; the scent remains, even after 1.5 hours, in a fresh-oriented, subtly marine spectrum with hints of lavender and musk. Certainly not a great achievement and olfactorily rather mundane, but at least quite decent and bearable.

Acqua Essenziale actually has excellent potential for a true summer hit. First of all, there’s the visually appealing bottle that promises a high-quality fragrance. It looks modern and elegant - ideal for a minimalist chrome-glinting bathroom. The strong blue color is also a clear statement in today’s times, signaling a return to natural ingredients.

The Acqua Essenziale line from Salvatore Ferragamo is fantastic. Alberto Morillas has once again been allowed to unleash his creativity and showcase what he does best: creating fresh fragrances. Acqua Essenziale somewhat resembles Acqua di Gio EdT, also by Morillas. The citrus notes come through right at the beginning, combined with an authentic, fresh mint.

Aside from the new Beau Male and this new release from Salvatore Ferragamo, there wasn't a single fragrance on the men's side of the perfumery today that I hadn't tested yet. I might really have to start testing on the women's side soon. While the new, summery Le Male performed well to very well, Acqua Essenziale is anything but essential and important.

The first sniff was still quite okay. I applied the fragrance about two hours ago and just wanted to see how it develops. Well, I would say I was mistaken, because even now the scent has almost completely faded away. This is really weak. Initially, the sillage is quite strong, but it diminishes after just a few minutes.

The poorly rated and unknown brother of Acqua Essenziale Blu Eau de Toilette I ordered right away and it turned out to be the one that convinced me. Disclaimer right off the bat - it doesn’t stand out particularly strongly, nor is it a must-have, but with my heart for fragrances that aren’t so well received here, I was pleased that I like it.

This was the fragrance my wife used when I met her. This perfume is unforgettable and will always be associated with my wife. A floral, fresh, powdery, energetic, singular fragrance, something aquatic too. I am sorry that this fragrance has been discontinued from Moschino. Nowadays, it is rare to find and when it appears on the market, prices are indecent. Curious, this perfume was launched in 1996, in the same year as Acqua di Giò pour Homme, my signature fragrance in the second half of the 90s and which is still in my rotation today.

I used to own OH! when I was a teenager. OH! was fresh and very powdery. Right after spraying it on it has a very soapy, and iron-like smell. A bit of alcohol seeps through as well. It does remind me of laundry detergent. After about 30 minutes the alcohol, overly soapy and iron-y notes have mostly disappeared, and you're left with a subtle, slightly floral and woody scent. At times I will catch a whiff of the powderiness too. However, when I'm not specifically looking for the notes it'll smell like a watery face mist with some indistinguishable flowery and earthy smell. It just does not remind me of perfume at all, it's too watery. Overall I wished this was a bit more fruity. There's supposed to be an apricot and peach note, but I was never able to identify it beyond it having a somewhat fruity smell. This is mostly a pleasant fresh and powdery scent to me.

Moschino Oh! has been a constant presence in my collection for several years now and is pretty much the only one I have repurchased a few times. Unfortunately, it can no longer be bought in stores, not even in Italy, and it has also become rare online. I don't know if it is still being produced at all. I researched the fragrance notes: Top notes: Peach, Apricot, Bergamot, and Violet Heart notes: Rose, Iris, Jasmine, Heliotrope Base notes: Cedarwood, Sandalwood, Vanilla, Amber The scent starts off sharp, alcoholic, almost synthetic. But it's worth waiting for the further development! After a few minutes, the fragrance changes, becoming softer, powdery, and melding with the skin. It exudes a pleasant freshness that reminds one of a bed made with fresh linens. In the end, it becomes slightly woody and a bit creamy. It is lightly sweet but never sticky. For me, it belongs in the category of fresh laundry/freshly showered scents and fits well in spring and summer, in my opinion. The longevity is not outstanding, but it's okay.

I had this fragrance years ago. Whenever I wore it, it felt like I smelled *freshly washed* - not that this is a negative thing, but somehow it didn’t feel like perfume to me, more like Lenor or Vernel. I passed it on after a while, as I wore it so rarely. PS. The bottle is really great though!!

I thank my mom for generously passing on her fragrances to me, but in the nursing home, she has to make do with a "ration" due to space constraints. One of her treasures is Paris Eau de Printemps. I do like the original Paris, but I think I prefer Printemps even more. There is certainly a resemblance - but Printemps is a note lighter, more supple. At the same time, it is a distinct fragrance - not a half-hearted copy. The rose and violet are beautifully mild, woven into the delicate, sweet honeysuckle. Jasmine gently joins in, and the peony quietly waves. Musk and sandalwood allow the fragrance to gently fade with a light spiciness. Subtle elegance with a touch of cheerfulness. When my aunt celebrated her birthday, I gifted her this fragrance - a risk, as she has a very particular taste. But the response was very positive. She would never dare to gift a fragrance, yet I managed this feat - so her words of praise. She will repurchase it. But I also find Printemps to be a hit - not just for spring-like temperatures.

Ah, dear noses. Let me tell you something. “Paris Eau de Printemps 2009” is truly great YSL cinema! For those who appreciate “Paris,” the original scent, let it be known: This flanker has everything that “Paris” has and what makes it so unique: Only the floral sweetness is slightly reduced, and the retro charm is dialed down a bit. Otherwise, everything is the same and just as kneeling-worthy as with “Paris.” The great mother has not been neutered! For those who do not like “Paris” because it is a bit musty, too sweet-soapy: As already mentioned-- The mustiness is gone, the sweetness dialed down. If even Flori (see below!) is striking a conciliatory tone here, then you can also believe the Peanut: “Paris” skeptics could become fans here! (However, anyone who generally does not like pronounced floral scents will not be happy with “Paris Eau de Printemps 2009.”) For those who do not know “Paris,” I will try to quickly bring this original scent closer to you (a pointless endeavor in itself, as “Paris” belongs to the fragrances that make verbal descriptions extremely difficult). It is a hopelessly romantic, infinitely floral scent with pronounced soapy sweetness (without being piercing). Even though the rose stands out here, “Paris” is a tornado of spring-like, dancing flowers. The whole thing is imbued with a certain charming mustiness that is not dusty but radiant, flowing, and sunny. Bright, light-filled mustiness. Clear? “Paris Eau de Printemps 2009” has all of that too: Just a bit airier, less sweet, and less musty. I will not go into the scent progression of “Paris” and “Paris Eau de Printemps 2009”: It is not particularly dramatic in either case, and a forced dissection would only make this text longer. So: The Parisian floral orgy continues unabated in this spring version. With the usual intensity, brilliance, and adorability. The sillage and longevity have also not suffered: They are top-notch here as well. And I probably don’t need to say anything about the appearance: I would personally build an altar for this bottle. You, dear Flori, I include in my prayers: I thank you from here to Paris for the generous decant.

I knew and used Opium by YSL back in the day, and I also smelled Paris on an acquaintance. Thankfully, I’m out of the Opium phase and I could never warm up to Paris. However, YSL has released several spring fragrances inspired by Paris, roughly on an annual basis. So it took me a whopping 20 years to finally take a closer look at at least one of them. And I actually acquired Paris Printemps! When I took the bottle out of the packaging, the first thought that came to mind was “aha, so it’s Paris after all.” Then I went pfffffffffffffffftt... ...and it blew me away. What an amazing scent; I smell the honeysuckle, I smell the rose, I smell the jasmine, and also the peony. The violets are subtly in the background, but the others are THERE, and how! I constantly hold my arm under my nose where I sprayed it and enjoy this wonderful scent. YES, it fits spring, it fits summer, and I would wear it in autumn too - at least on nice days. In winter, I wish for something warmer. These floral notes last a long time. So far (almost 2 hours), I still don’t smell any musk or sandalwood; I’m curious to see when it comes and if the scent changes then. I will update if necessary. Now I’m glad that I gave in to my desire and got this 100ml bottle. IT was really worth it. YSL Paris Printemps is definitely my fragrance direction. This one is not quite as sweet and not as prominent as Printemps by M. Micallef, which I also own, and it smells quite different - which is very good, as I now have two Printemps that couldn’t be more different. CONCLUSION: I’m happy that I gave YSL another chance. * Addendum 15.5.11: my enthusiasm for this wonderful scent led me to also acquire Roses de Bois and Roses Enchantees. I can’t stop indulging.

Like the Pink Bouquet by Moschino - Toilet Duck! This one just smells of candied lemon and orange blossom, after half an hour it becomes a bit "softer," but it remains cheap, piercing, toilet-like. Lily of the valley and jasmine further enhance this impression! I would feel more embarrassed with this than comfortable, just like with Pink Bouquet. The bottle is also terrible! I can't assess the longevity, as I washed it off.

Ribelle is nostalgic for that 00' year vibe. Sweet, girly girl fragrance, she's innocent and suitable for anyone and everyone who wants to smell sweet and gourmand. I get a blast of freshness at the start with the subtle, tart mandarin orange and the beautiful pink pepper. I get a hint of fruity pear somewhere, but it only adds to the freshness. The florals don't take too long before having their turn. Ylang-ylang and frangipani are the strongest on my skin with their carnal fruitiness and tropical feel. Nothing too overwhelming on the tropical aspect: the fragrance doesn't strike me as a vacation scent. Jasmine adds a very welcome creaminess to it all. At that point, it's a well-blended mix between fruity sweetness and creamy florals. As it moves on, I start getting more creaminess from the coconut milk and the gourmand vanilla ice cream. The latter is what ties everything so well together and it's so well made! It has that beautiful mouthwatering feel to it. Sandalwood is in the background, adding warmth and creaminess. Very lovely fragrance, something anyone could wear when they don't want to think about complicated scents and artistic compositions. A feel-good fragrance with a beautiful creamy, fruity, floral composition. I've got limited space in my collection which is why it won't be making it, but if I had the space, I would probably go for a full bottle!

I love vanilla ice cream so I've been trying out the perfumes in the notebook, but it's not vanilla gelato at all. It smells like the erasers I used to buy at the candy store when I was a kid. It says vanilla gelato, but it's just a twist on vanilla scent to make people want to buy it. It smells like the scent you'd get from a boring, average gal. It smells like Don Quixote. Also, even though it's a parfum, it doesn't last at all. After 2 hours it becomes clear and the scent disappears.

So! Finally, I own Signorina Ribelle! I am very excited to be able to write the first comment on this fragrance here on Parfumo. The pink square bottle with a bow and a round rose-gold cap is simply beautiful! It borders on kitsch, but I find it a dream in red-pink and looks very high-quality and elegant. With the colorful bottle and the name Signorina Ribelle, "the rebellious one," I expected a provocative scent that challenges. However, that is not the case at all. In the opening, a wonderful intense mélange of radiant white flowers and creamy, pleasantly sweet vanilla ice cream garnished with a piece of fresh pear delights the senses. The pear disappears after a while, or rather retreats, but the longer you wear this fragrance, the creamier, more luscious, and simply better it becomes. This vanilla ice cream note is simply delicious! It harmonizes wonderfully with the white flowers and smells irresistibly sweet, yet at the same time elegant and creamy, not artificial or overpowering at all. The white flowers are not cloying but silky soft and radiant. I can't detect coconut milk right now, but sandalwood in the background beautifully rounds off the scent. I think an ivory-colored bottle would have suited this fragrance better. I find this scent radiates an incredible femininity, security, and warmth, like a heartfelt hug. As it develops, the sillage becomes closer to the skin, but that does not diminish the pleasantness of this fragrance. In my surroundings, I received consistently positive feedback about Signorina Ribelle. Whether man or woman, it was always "Oh!" and "Mhhhhhhhhh!" or "Wow, that smells good!" or "Delicious!". A friend tried it from me and then promptly ordered it for herself. She was absolutely thrilled and says Signorina Ribelle is her new favorite fragrance. This fragrance is perfect for an evening out or for dates, but it can also be worn well during the day. I also love wearing it when snuggling into bed at night, simply because it smells so beautiful. The longevity is very good at about 8 hours. Conclusion: A caressing, seductive feminine fragrance that knows how to impress. Definitely worth trying!

.. but unfortunately, the pleasure lasts only about as long. What a pity. The scent is extraordinarily beautiful. An extremely creamy vanilla note (which really reminds me of ice cream), a subtle citrus fruitiness (especially in the opening), all nestled in white flowers. A very pleasant gourmand, wearable in any season. Unfortunately, there is a problem: In this perfume, the scent is right, but I consider the longevity to be weak. On my skin, it becomes very close to the skin after just 2-3 hours and is 95% gone after 4.5 hours. I expect more and am quite surprised, as I usually only associate weak longevity with fresh and light scents. I wouldn’t describe "Signorina Ribelle (Eau de Parfum) | Salvatore Ferragamo" as particularly heavy either, but it is definitely sweet and creamy. Quite a shame. Scent-wise, it would be a potential candidate for purchase. Only the performance puts me off a bit. Fortunately, it is also more affordable than many other designer fragrances - so a larger bottle could be in order, and I could just reapply it from time to time. It’s tricky. The scent is lovely, though. It should particularly appeal to sweet-toothed individuals. I can also imagine it very well on women who otherwise enjoy fragrances like Poison Girl Eau de Parfum / Poison Girl Eau de Toilette . It falls into the same category for me.
I also have to write a bit about this relatively inexpensive women's fragrance. It's a very pleasing piece that caught my attention with its seductive pyramid.

Signorina Ribelle inspires me in a nostalgic way and takes me on a magical journey through time. Back to 1987. I see a teenage girl before me who has lost her heart head over heels to a young Italian. And I mean really lost it. A great first love. My soul was wondrously touched and positively shaped.

I like the scents from Ferragamo; they last longer for me as a body lotion than in the bottle. In any case, this is a successful blend that lasts quite a long time, is very pleasant, very wearable, and very feminine. Overall, it is better than other fragrances on the market. I also like the bottle.

So, I need to pull myself together for a moment. Since this fragrance is called Cinéma, meaning cinema, I will try not to mention any current movies in theaters like… well, Star Wars :D Especially not when it’s a women’s fragrance. Although it might sound cliché, very few women are actually interested in Star Wars… *sigh* It was the same when we recently went to see the new Star Wars film. We guys went in, really excited about the movie (so much so that each of us was wearing at least one piece of clothing with a Star Wars motif… I myself had a T-shirt showing Darth Vader watering a plant, which grows into a Death Star plant :DD) and what do the girlfriends of some of the guys do? … They go shopping in the city… and then go out for sushi, hmm.. delicious! :DD Well, I ended up talking a bit about Star Wars… I hope you haven’t run off and are still reading… *sigh* Because now I’m getting to the fragrance, honestly!! The Fragrance: Hmm, since I don’t know the original Cinéma, I can’t say if there’s a hint of the original fragrance's DNA here. I can definitely smell beautiful oranges at the beginning, which are not bitter but rather softly citrusy. There’s also a lovely sweetness from the jasmine and a bit of rose. Additionally, it has other floral notes, which are not as strong as the aforementioned notes, but they are detectable, though I can’t identify them… Sage and rosemary should actually be recognizable, but I find them so weak that they only emit a slight, herbal note and are hardly distinguishable on their own. Only a bit later can you at least pick out the rosemary, but only if you smell really close to the sprayed area, as the fragrance is otherwise overshadowed by the floral and sweet notes. In the base, the citrus notes are of course only faintly detectable and fade away more and more over time. Mainly, it then smells floral with roses and sweet with jasmine, while a light, powdery sweetness from the (here light) vanilla adds a softness to the fragrance. There seems to be a bit of amber as well, but I have more difficulty perceiving the musk. Overall, it’s a very beautiful fragrance. The Sillage and Longevity: I find the sillage good, as the fragrance can be smelled well from a normal distance for a while, so you don’t have to get too close. And if you spray a lot, it leaves a small scent cloud behind. I found the longevity to be quite good at around seven or eight hours. The Bottle: The bottle is rectangular and filled with clear or slightly yellowish fragrance liquid. The cap is square and gold-plated. On the front, you can see a golden, radiant sun with large spikes, whose rays extend to the edges of the bottle. There also seems to be a bottle variant with a rounder sun that radiates in a circular manner. Both variants look very beautiful. Are you still there? If not, then you just missed out on a great fragrance here! Or you’re just ignoring my comment, which is actually worse!!! *sniff* *sigh* Cinéma Festival d’Été has become or rather was a very beautiful summer fragrance, as it seems to have been discontinued. It is floral and sweet, and despite good sillage, in a relaxed way, making it particularly suitable for spring and summer. You could wear it both during the day and for going out. By going out, I mean not just in the evening, but also during the day, like at open-air events! Because it is wonderful, beautifully feminine, gentle but also sexy. If the fragrance were a dress, it would definitely be a showstopper! But since it is a fragrance, it’s more of a scent to be sniffed at,… but that sounds kind of silly! :D In any case, it is worth a try, especially if you want something floral sweet with good sillage for the summer that fits all sorts of occasions and thus makes for a great all-rounder in the summer. As I said, unfortunately, it’s no longer available, but maybe the regular Cinéma smells just as good? Because after all, it reads quite similarly according to the description… hmm, I should test it when I get the chance… as long as there aren’t too many girls bustling around in the ladies' section… :D

On another site, I saw the notes for this listed as lily, rose, freesia, grapes, anise, orange, heliotrope, amber, vetiver. The truly amazing thing is that I cannot smell a single one of these notes! This isn't unpleasant, but has a generic, synthetic smell that makes me think of Johnson's Baby Shampoo. It's something one would give to a 7-year-old girl who wants to wear perfume but can't be trusted not to dump the whole bottle on herself at once. Otherwise, there would be no particular reason to wear it. (Other scents in this line are quite nice, but no one gets a perfect score, right?)

I received L'eau Cheap&Chic as a sample and immediately tried it on my hand. At first, it smells very strongly of Autan (that anti-mosquito-and-other-annoying-insect stuff). That's okay, I like that scent. Later, this smell mixes with that of soap, which I also don't find unpleasant, although it is strange. It may be that this soapy scent comes from the freesias and jasmine, but I can't swear to it. The further development of the scent is practically non-existent for me; it remains a mix of Autan and soap that lasts a solid two hours before fading into nothing. The longevity is thus absolutely disappointing, and since a bottle of anti-mosquito spray is anyway cheaper than this perfume, I can only advise against purchasing it.

This stuff is one of my favorites for daily use. The opening is a bit "soapy", but not in a bad way. Then it changes in to a fresh spring/summer scent with a bit of soap in the background. The bergomot here is really nice, as is the dry-down, which is pretty unique and amazing smelling--hard to describe. My only complaint is that at times the Clary Sage is a bit too overpowering to the point where it is imbalanced, but then it calms down again. I love sage anyways because it reminds me of nature walks. The sillage and projection is pretty good for a few hours, and it lasts as a very nice skin scent for about 6-7 hours for me. All in all, a good one, and quite unique. It's kind of an aquatic spring scent, and quite well made.

I’ve been in the habit of watching a few videos on the Watch section of Facebook for some time before falling asleep. Well, I love the videos of HeXtian. This brilliant artist transforms a simple Barbie-like doll into a reproduction of a famous character, changing the hair, the body, the clothes, but above all, the make-up thoroughly. I find it thrilling. But besides these videos, I also often follow those of Jason Makki, a hairstylist & senior barber known for sharing styling tutorials, time-lapses of his cuts, and a variety of Grooming Hair MakeOver videos. Why did I tell you about that? Because the Acqua Essenziale Colonia by Salvatore Ferragamo is a refined and modern fragrance with a pleasant barber scent. I imagine I smell this perfume when entering Jason Makki Men’s salon in Dubai. The scent is the third in the brand’s fragrance collection, and this one mainly combines aromatic, aquatic, woody, and fougére accords. At first, it welcomes me like a classic eau de cologne, a fresh green, semi-tart barber’s scent, with an abundance of white citrus blossoms. If you like colognes like Echt Kölnisch Wasser Eau de Cologne , you should know what I mean. A well-recognizable note of brilliant Italian bergamot blends with honeyed orange blossom, perhaps some other citrus peel, and they release a pleasantly fresh and tart aroma. I can barely feel the spiciness of the coriander, just a hint of harshness from the green leaves. Instead, after the zestiness has subsided, a watery atmosphere oozes, neither salty nor marine, more like the freshwater droplets of an unforeseen summer storm. A singular olfactory signature, with ozonic and aromatic notes, accompanies a light and an elegant hint of orange bloom. Over time, it changes into a soapy and clean vibe. In the heart, I get a loud clary sage note. Compared to the other Eau de colognes I have or I know, this one is featuring sage in the heart instead of rosemary, thyme, or any other aromatic herbs. That’s what makes Acqua Essenziale Colonia something apart. The balminess grows and mixes with a floral lavender. Now orange blossom shines and screams at its best, while citrus moves in the background. As it dries down, I get hints of soapy vetiver, here replacing the patchouli of the original cologne, mixed with the heart trail notes, making the whole thing smell like Italian soap. Ambroxan smells very pleasant with an oceanic and mineral undertone to it., is there, but it’s muted. I thought that Acqua Essenziale Colonia was a vetiver scent, but not a firm presence in this scent. Ultimately, there is a sweet and roasted tonka, here as a complementary note that balances the salty ambergris and the earthy vetiver. I appreciate the composition, and it would make a good office scent. Let’s not the name “Cologne” fools you because this is an EDT and has a respectable duration and projection, approximately half a day on my skin. Sillage is moderate while longevity leans towards intensely. The cologne-like aroma makes it preferable during the warm months, Sprint and Summer are the right seasons. The whole concoction in this fragrance ends up smelling like a delicate Italian soap, and I enjoy it. It has an old-school sort of feel to it I enjoy. Fresh, aromatic, citrus, a bit woody and a tad spicy, that’s it. I am proud of Alberto Morillas's work, the Acqua Essenziale trilogy is sublime and the colognes differ from one another. This review is based on a 100ml bottle I have owned since June 2017. -Elysium

Perhaps it was a coincidence that both Acqua Essenziale Colonia and Dior’s Sauvage edt were released in the same year, because I can’t help but think that if Dior was an Italian brand, this is what Sauvage would smell like (notice the similarity in notes??)
