To me, the opening is extremely reminiscent of an herbal green soap - definitely along the lines of AdP’s Colonia but nowhere near the authenticity. There’s no blast of alcohol (a surprise to be sure from a relatively cheap fragrance), but a sharp bergamot comes out in full force with clary sage and perhaps a tinge of orange blossom to give it an almost petitgrain quality. I absolutely love the opening and wish it would stick around for longer, but within 2 minutes, the fragrance begins to make some weighty turns. As the greenness quickly overtakes the citrus, it brings in a slight minty affair (along the lines of a lavender leaf) and combines with the emerging aquatic notes to produce an interesting aroma that to me, is reminiscent of bad breath. You read correctly. There’s something in the blend on skin (definitely a product of lavender and something else) that gives it a weird funk during the transition at about the 5 minute mark. Fortunately, it only lasts for about 8-10 minutes before the sweet tonka breaks through and produces that ever-so-contemporary contrast between citrus and heady sweet notes. Fifteen minutes in, the contrast peaks with a sharp, orangey bergamot and clary sage on one end, and a sweet tonka and amboxan (aka sugar water) on the other. And now for the coolest part - amidst the eye of the hurricane, a smooth lavender note lovingly bisects the two ends and squeezes them all together into a single blend. The end result is a sweet, quasi-barbershop combination of lavender and tonka, lying on a bed of powdery greenery and ambroxan. Whew. What a ride. Of course, there are a few tiny hints of that bad-breath odour that peek through at about the 30-40 minute mark but they dissipate rather quickly (never to return) to be replaced by that soapy vibe once again. Total longevity is about 4-5 hours on me, but that's to be expected from a freshie. Overall though, the general vibe I get is of a traditional Italian green-lavender soap made “modern” by immersing it in ambroxany sugar water. I know, I know. It is even worth mentioning anymore? I suppose the traditional nature of the fragrance could remind some people of grandma’s bathroom, toilet cleaner, or the disinfected tiles of a european barbershop, but to me, it’s far more understated and perhaps even a little too much so. Personally, as far as Italian-leaning inexpensive fragrances go, I slighlty prefer Ferrari’s Bright Neroli, and for just a little more – Intenso by D&G. At the very least, both will give you better projection and despite preferring the smell of both Acqua Essenziale Blu and the original, neither will give you that soapy vibe that Colonia has in spades. A simple fragrance, sure, maybe even a little boring, but I’m keeping my bottle just so I can continue experiencing that awesome introduction – an opening…..I can’t refuse.

This fragrance is an absolute stunner. Another masterful creation from Alberto Morillas. I've been testing it for the past few days and I find it to be an enjoyable, mood lifting fougere fragrance. Based on my personal experience, it is best when it's applied right after that morning shower. The soapiness vibe in this fragrance, keeps you feeling refreshed for many hours even when its really hot. Season: Spring/Summer Time of Day: Best from Morning to Late Afternoon. Evening wearable too. Presentation: 9/10 Scent: 9/10 Longevity: 8:10 Silage: 7:10 Value for money: 9/10

The opening note combo is the worst aspects of Acqua di Parma Colonia, mixed with Dial bar soap, and I LOATHE it. So, when I sprayed it on (the morning after I bought it), I was immediately about to go wash it off. But, suddenly, as I frantically waved my arm about, trying to clear the air with my non-tainted wrist, this light touch of orangey lavender wafted past, and I thought, "Whoa, where was that from?" Being kind of thick that early in the morning, I did not immediately realise it was the fragrance I'd just sprayed, and instead, I tried to follow the smell. Five minutes of stupid later, I reflexively scratched my nose with my scented hand, and, lo and behold, that lovely aroma was coming from my own wrist, where, buried under the '70s nose-bomb opening, was this lovely spring-summer freshness. Colour me stunned (which is a shade of rainbow, accented with dark clear, or so I've been told). A mid-afternoon warm breeze carrying orange, lavender, and the smell of clean laundry, with a distant whiff of the sea. That's this scent in a nutshell (after that atrocious opening), and It's a mainstay in my summer rotation now, because it's that good. ...I just need a nose plug for the first 5 minutes.

Ferragamo Acqua Essenziale colonia is hands down one of my best summer fragrances. It's simply magnificent. From the juicy bergamot, Manly lavender and the modern Ambroxan this fragrance brings some classic notes and modernises them. Perfect for formal situations in high heat.

An incredible fragrance by master Alberto Morillas, with a nose marked by aquatic and citrus notes, of bergamot, orange blossom, sage and lavender. The latter gives a spicy aroma, with notes are well mixed. A fresh scent to use and abuse in spring or summer. Very good! Presentation: 8/10 Scent: 8/10 Longevity: 8:10 Silage: 7:10 Value for money: 9/10

This scent opens up green and classic barbershop style, but it dries down very blue and modern. The opening is kinda alcohol harsh but after it chills a minute, it goes thru stages and changes as the hours pass. I liked it alot. I gave the last bit of the bottle to my pops cuz he said he liked it. The performance was good (7hrs) on my skin, and it's priced affordably.

It suits the brand Salvatore Ferragamo well to draw on the classic Italian perfumery. It is the Zagaras, brought to Cologne by Johann Maria Farina and exported from there to the whole world, that stand at the beginning of modern perfume art.

After Salvatore Ferragamo more or less completely failed with the two previous Acqua Essenziales and even the excellent Pour Homme became too timid for me, I was slowly running out of current arguments for the brand. But the new Colonia from the Acqua Essenziale line somewhat made up for that.

Forget its name for a moment. If you have a soft spot for Uomo Eau de Toilette , don't buy this without trying it because they are two colognes apart, and this is not a flanker nor a spin-off of the OG. The gourmand and nutty facets are missing. That said, Urban Feel is a beautiful fragrance in the mineral, woody, and watery genres. To begin with, the cologne expands with a splash of fresh citrus, warm woods, and aromatic herbs, evocative of some of the other fresh, blue colognes. I can think of one in particular that I've used, but the name escapes me right now. I perceive the sapidity of citrus peels, the creamy bergamot, that of green lemon or lime, sour and rough, with a pleasant touch of slightly ozonic saltiness and a balsamic caress that recalls cardamom pods and spruce. Sometimes, the balmy and minty nuances reminisce the Vicks Vaporub ointment. Also, the smoky and resinous undertones of the base quickly come to the fore. I'm unsure if there is a coffee accord; I don't perceive coffee beans or espresso. Then, the crowd-pleasing treaties that dominate the opening are mentholated, balsamic, and herbaceous. Fresh, but without that barbershop or fresh out-of-the-shower vibe. The heart of Urban Feel keeps the initial airy and watery freshness, which I can breathe in the centers of northern cities near the sea on crisp late winter mornings when spring is upon us, and it has recently rained. The woodiness comes from dry cedar wood, very perceptible, even if not too similar to pencil shavings. In the middle of the journey, incense smoke takes its place. I am fascinated by the watery aspect, which is not the marine one. Here we find humid and dewy nuances that mainly come to me from driftwood and ozonic accords. Despite cumin, the overall scent doesn't resemble BO or sweat. The dry-down stays within the comfort zone, nothing revolutionary. The leathery cistus and smoky incense are the most noticeable notes on my skin. Instead, the patchouli barely reaches me, perhaps too cleaned up and overshadowed by the other elements. Finally, both sillage and longevity are moderate, say half a day, with an intense fragrance during the first hour, which is not expected from a perfume with ambroxan. It is an ideal scent for spring and summer rotation, the day, and the office. About the name, Urban also means local, cosmopolitan, modern, a sort of city feel, and this cologne admirably fits it. I'm basing my review and opinion on a sample I've owned since March 2021. -Elysium

Why do we mourn the scents that were trendy and cool twenty years ago? Why do we not find the fulfillment in today's Ambroxan jungle that we remember from the past? Was it the pseudo-romanticism that today's populists want to deceive us with in a folklore memory that never really existed? Or is there really something to the past with more simplicity and honesty? Politically speaking, probably not, but in terms of fragrance, a clear yes. Today, you buy a scent with the remark that its longevity is above average, and you end up with a eunuch that screams the highest notes in the first two seconds and then only longs for its missing balls and the successful time of past potency. Why did Dior discontinue Eau Sauvage Parfum after just two years and then release a cologne version with the same name? Why do fragrances that have a sillage that can be called strong only offer sweetness, liqueur, or lipstick with a powder accord? Because the Marlboro Man has long been dead. Currently, we only get designed, watered-down fragrances on the market that are a bit stronger in sillage. The robust summer scents like Versace l'homme, Aramis Havana, or in extremis a Kouros have ended up in the trash like tobacco advertising. Good for some, unfortunate for others, as strong scents also represent a strong possibility for the individuality of each person. This is unfortunately not so easily achievable with the many gum and cotton candy products. You take a fragrance and quickly disappear into the anonymous crowd. This is a shame and, given the high prices, almost unnecessary. When you enjoy a Chinotto in a café on a summer evening, you usually get hit from the left, right, front, and back by the same fresh, sweet family. Thus, we praise fragrances that still escape the zeitgeist today and evoke a bit of nostalgia with a stronger sillage. One must not misunderstand the criticism; of course, there are good to very good fragrances with a sweet, pleasant theme, but in this time of many resentments towards differing opinions, it is almost a test of courage. We praise fragrances like this Uomo Urban Feel, whose namesake actually belongs to the Playboy and Boris Becker fragrance faction, but otherwise, it is a very pleasant, light, yet still more intense scent that can be worn well in summer. For the darker days, it feels too light and lemony until the slightly heavier fragrance time with the incense arrives. This incense is the second base, where other woods usually come in. Therefore, it is also a bit more special than the products with similar lightness this year. Those who like incense, not in the heaviness of Armani Privé's "Bois d’Encens," but in an airy lightness, will find this very satisfying. Unfortunately, the longevity is not very long-lasting; the brothers from UOMO can do significantly better, with the Signature being the standout, which can also be worn in summer. This Urban is a positive product compared to the current lightweight fragrances, which can be worn as a good alternative when it's hot, as the incense is still slightly recognizable after hours. In the hope for times with greater sillage and a return to better simplicity, I wear this fragrance and regret nothing; all we have is the now.

Ladies and Gentlemen, it’s time for me to add my two cents again. This time it’s about another fragrance from Alberto Morillas’ workshop - Uomo Urban Feel. Preface: Those who have read my previous reviews know that I like Alberto Morillas’ fragrances. I have particularly taken a liking to Acqua di Giò Profumo, so I decided to test more of his perfumes. This led me to both Bvlgari Man Terrae Essence and Uomo Urban Feel, which I probably wouldn’t have noticed otherwise. The Fragrance: As soon as I opened the packaging of the perfume, a strong cloud of sage rushed towards me, causing my eyes to widen in surprise. Wow… phew… okay… interesting… One thing was certain, I had never smelled a perfume like this before. Often, perfumes start off with a citrusy freshness from bergamot or the like. Bergamot is indeed included here, but upon spraying, I perceive more sage and ginger. You all surely know the sage candies from a well-known Swiss manufacturer?! Then you have a good impression of how Urban Feel smells at the beginning. The opening is something new and I am excited about it. Gradually, the sage recedes and the typical Morillas freshness takes its place, delighting the nose. I already made the comparison to a thunderstorm with Acqua di Giò Profumo, that metallic freshness that wafts around your nose can also be found here. I’m not sure, but I believe it’s the frankincense, which is present in both Profumo, Terrae Essence, and Urban Feel, that creates a certain similarity in the base. Please don’t get me wrong, all three fragrances are completely different and independent, but in the drydown, they share a similar DNA that I really like. Fresh, yet masculine. Unobtrusive, but still seductive. The fragrance is unobtrusive, if you disregard the first 10 minutes right after spraying. It lasts quite well. For the first 4 hours, it holds up nicely, and for the following 6 to 8 hours, it is close to the skin but still noticeable. At times, I also associate it with freshly washed laundry once the sage has dissipated. It is excellent for the hotter days. Although it has a certain spiciness, it is somehow a cool, fresh scent. It is suitable for men from about 25 years old and can be worn in leisure and at the office. Conclusion: Characteristic of this perfume is the sage, the (not listed) ginger, sea salt, and frankincense. A slightly sour sage spiciness that transitions into a metallic freshness and has a light woody base. It is a special fragrance with a recognizable character, and I can only recommend testing it. The bottle is a slightly curved one, in a dark blue. The name of the label “Ferragamo” is embossed on the edge, modernly styled like graffiti. Unfortunately, the bottle does not have a cap or lid. It only has a semi-circular plastic ring that is clamped under the spray head. The sprayer itself is mediocre. It serves its purpose. A major downside is that the glass is opaque and looks like cheap plastic. You have no chance of seeing the fill level. Only weight and a small shake test could provide some insight here. Unfortunately, the bottle does not convince me, but luckily it’s about the content, and that is good. The price of Urban Feel is also quite reasonable. Summary: Fragrance: 7.5 Longevity: 7 Sillage: 7 Bottle: 5 Price-Performance: 8 Even though I have now added my two cents about this perfume, I hope it hasn’t affected the fragrance experience ;) Mustard and sage probably don’t go well together haha. As always, thank you for reading until the end, and I hope my contribution was helpful to you. Best regards Your Gentleman

Smells broader and fresher for a short time after spraying, then becomes a typical, fresh shower gel scent, in the direction of Dylan Blue, just a bit quieter, much quieter. If it hadn't been so cheap, I wouldn't have bought it. The Tiramisu Uomos are much better for longer. This one has nothing in common with those scents, except for part of the name. For me, it's just another unnecessary fragrance. The longevity is also poor, just over 2 hours, then it's over for me.

Uomo Urban Feel was my first real summer fragrance - purchased before influencers shaped my taste. For me, it embodies a fresh, citrus-spicy breeze with a Mediterranean flair - almost like a stroll along the Italian coastal city. Especially the mandarin-bergamot vibes, combined with sea salt and sage, feel light yet characterful. I believe this fragrance receives far too little recognition - it is easy to wear, unisex, and distinctive. A true underdog in the summer shelf!

Out of curiosity, I tried this wonderful flanker of the classic Paris. It's a big, hefty bottle with stenciled design embellishing it. I paid twice the original retail price as it is now a rare collectible. These were limited editions in 2007 and I would pick them up at Sephora. I passed over this one. It now takes its place in my collection among my YSL shelf with always seem so precious as the days go by. Its contents pay tribute to the classic Paris. It moves far beyond the original formula while still fitting inside the iconic bottle. What makes it different? The green note is turned up. What is the green note? I never figured it out, but I love its fresh earthy character. This is Paris stripped down. The top notes are restrained with hints of the classic formula. I get no mimosa. There is rose, violet, lily of the valley and the biggest surprise is the lilac which takes this formula back a century to 1907. Its old fashioned in the best way. This is an all-ages production that can be worn from anyone from 3 to 113. Children would love this. It's so gentle, almost delicate that to say its unisex is silly. I use it as an aftershave, as its soothes and tones the skin.

Today I come to Golden Acacia from the Tuscan Scent fragrance line by Salvatore Ferragamo. As it often happens, or as it sometimes happens with me, I briefly think about the fragrance name. Golden Acacia. So, golden acacia. By now, you know that I am somewhat ignorant about various plant species,… after all, I mention this often, but I’ll write it down for all those who didn’t know yet. This means that, off the top of my head, or if I were to see a picture of an acacia, I wouldn’t know that it’s an acacia tree. By name, I would even assume that they might be related to pistachios, because the names (in German) sound so similar. But of course, acacias and pistachios are about as related as we humans are to bananas. On the other hand… according to scientific studies, it turns out that we humans share quite a bit of DNA with bananas, and that our enzymes (and thus, especially our metabolism) are about 25% identical to these fruits (the DNA is even 50% the same!). So, in that sense, it’s 25-50% cannibalism if we eat something related to us, right? :DD Well, the comparison is obviously flawed, as pistachios and acacias are much more similar than humans and bananas. After all… they are both trees, so these two plants are quite similar, making it okay if I can’t tell them apart, right? :D Phew… just managed to get back on track, he he he! Be that as it may. After I looked up what acacias are, I also had to check if there is a species called “Golden Acacia,” or if this in the fragrance name is just a reference to the honey contained, but lo and behold, there is both acacia honey and the Golden Acacia! Nice, right? :D Now let’s get to the fragrance! The Fragrance: At first, I smell intense woody and earthy notes. I can’t identify the woods (uh… acacias? :D), the earthiness comes from the patchouli. There’s also sweet-spicy honey, which stylistically reminds me a bit of Thierry Mugler’s Angel fragrances (just significantly less piercing!). Additionally, the fragrance is very warm and slightly floral. Shortly after, the sweetness comes not only from the honey (but still mostly from it), but also from the distinctly noticeable amber. However, I don’t really perceive the indicated orange blossoms. By the way, the spicy, woody, and sweet notes also remind me a bit of those roasted and caramelized almonds at a Christmas market, which I really like. A little later, the fragrance becomes even warmer and softer, although it still has a slightly spicy scent and remains quite intense in projection. This softness comes from the resinous notes, but I wouldn’t have guessed that the resinous scent is opoponax without looking at the fragrance pyramid. Even many hours later, I can still smell the fragrance very well on myself, and I now also smell even softer scents. The honey is no longer as spicy and has completely blended with the amber regarding the sweet note of the fragrance. The resinous scent has become significantly more intense, which could also be the reason why the fragrance appears even softer and warmer in the later base. Meanwhile, the fragrance is still a bit woody. All in all, a very beautiful fragrance! The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is intense, so the fragrance can be smelled well on someone for a long time. One leaves a large scent cloud and should therefore be careful not to overdo it. The longevity seems almost eternal, as I could smell it for more than twelve hours, or from morning till evening. The Bottle: The bottle is black and gets wider in height. The name and brand are in golden lettering on the front. The neck of the bottle has also been gilded, making the bottle look particularly elegant. The cap is cylindrical and gilded on the inside. The outer shell of the cap seems to be made of wood, which makes everything appear more high-quality. All in all, the bottle is very well done. Oh yes, I really liked this fragrance! It simply smells great with spicy and sweet notes, especially honey mixed with amber, which is a wonderful combination. I also really liked that the fragrance reminded me of candied almonds. Additionally, it has a strong projection, so it can always be smelled well, but it belongs only in the autumn and winter. For me, it fits especially well in the evening or for going out. During the day, one should rather use less of it. In my opinion, it’s also one of those fragrances that one could wear especially for special occasions. Unfortunately (for us gentlemen), the fragrance turned out to be more feminine than unisex *sigh* So I think this fragrance is definitely worth trying! Unfortunately, it seems that the fragrance has been discontinued… By the way: Colloquially, acacias are sometimes also called robinias, which might not be entirely correct, as they are only somewhat related (but at least more related than acacias and pistachios, since acacias and robinias both belong to the legume family,… well, a bit of pedantic trivia is also necessary sometimes :D). And… yes, I must also say, I would prefer the robinia. Why? Well, think about it, the word contains “Robin,” the sidekick of Batman! Do I need to say more? :DD (… however, I must admit that I was never a very big Robin fan, although Tim Drake as Robin was really cool! You probably don’t know him, but that’s okay! :D). Oh, and don’t worry if someone thinks they are 50% banana now :D The same DNA segments usually concern the regions for common blueprints responsible for the fundamental functions of all living beings, such as metabolism, organ formation, etc.… and the higher the common affiliation (e.g., humans and mammals), the greater the similarities. The DNA blueprint of a mouse’s organs, as well as their limbs, is, for example, fundamentally almost the same (just in different size scales), it’s just the small fine differences like certain genes that make them what they are and which are not found in other living beings. In short: Feel free to eat bananas :DD

... is a deciduous shrub that can be found all around the Mediterranean. In Sardinia, beekeepers take advantage of the short flowering period of this small tree to place their bees on it. They produce the dark, bitter Corbezzolo honey from it, which is not comparable to the floral, gentle acacia honey that the name of the fragrance suggests. This honey is not something you can eat by the spoonful or add to tea; this honey does not do things halfway: It is bitter, sweet, and spicy all at once, just like Golden Acacia. For me, this fragrance not only smells like this specific honey but also like the Sardinian maquis, that evergreen shrub that you can already smell from the ferry when it arrives in one of the Sardinian ports in the morning. Bitter, sweet, and spicy, somewhat resinous, intense, and long-lasting, this is how this fragrance is, and for me, it is closely connected with the scents of this wonderful island in the Mediterranean.

Sometimes you come across offers that tempt you to buy the fragrance even if you are blind or almost blind to it. For example, when you see one of the Private Line from Salvatore Ferragamo for almost half the price. Still, the price is quite wallet-friendly, so you don’t end up buying it. Simply because you don’t know the scent (well enough). That’s how I felt about Golden Acacia, a honey shocker that, in terms of presence & extroverted sweetness, could easily be a fragrance from Tom Ford or other heavyweights. A Salvatore Ferragamo usually smells much finer & more subtle - good that the quiet ones can also turn it up! Golden Acacia would probably be called Golden Honey at Tom Ford & become a bestseller - because it’s a bombshell, just as they are currently trending. A potency monster where Baloo the bear would feel right at home. Everything sticky is in here - heated sugar, beeswax, syrup, tree resin, melted nuts. But above all, HONEY. I have rarely seen honey turn up so intensely. A delight for sweethearts. It somewhat reminds me of Polo's new Supreme Leather, only much stronger & more concentrated, darker & more majestic. For evening events, three sprays - ready to impress! Not everyone will love it, as it can be truly mercilessly sweet. However, it is impossible to go unnoticed & it will surely earn impressed comments. And despite its thick, juicy honey, it doesn’t lose its elegance - at least not completely. It remains a cultured Italian, unisex & not clumsy. It can really hold its own against the best bombshells. "Tobacco Vanille" or "Obsession for Men" should definitely be prepared ;). Although, as far under the radar as this scent flies, neither competitors nor wearers really need to worry. Hardly anyone knows it, let alone wears it. The rest are too timid. An Alphasugar. Bottle: worthy of a deluxe luxury line. Sillage: a bear of a scent - a honey bear! Longevity: 10 hours is brutally good. If you can handle the beast. Conclusion: Honey Honey, how u get so fly? Honey, not really edible delicious, but still delightful. Thick, rich, powerful - a standout for those who love it sweet!

This perfect flanker takes you from the sexy red chamber of the imperial palace to it exotic April garden within the Forbidden City. Its perfect for warm weather evenings. It is still very loyal to the original classic. What is different? There is still lots of spices. The florals are the biggest change. The carnation is less bitter and lily of the valley is gone. In its place is the imperial flower-almond blossom. Its utterly wonderful-soft, creamy and sweet! It fits into the composition like an old friend. The base still has lots of sandalwood, vanilla, amber and myrrh. Its not as smokey or heavy. Its also very romantic, to be shared outside under a spring moon... It was offered as a limited edition.

Yesterday I was sleepless in Bo again and dedicated myself to Lisa's fragrance surprise bag. I was in a melancholic mood and listened to Marianne Faithful over and over again. No, I have never driven through Paris - in an open sports car, with the warm wind in my hair. I can understand Lucy Jordan well. But before I completely sink into self-pity, I discover Imperiale. A lucky find, because the scent envelops me softly and so comforting. The neroli cools my forehead, and the clove wraps me enchantingly. The woody notes gently catch me - and the sweet vanilla warms me from within. The fragrance is not cheerful, but it goes along and shows understanding. I feel safe and secure with Imperiale - exactly what I needed.

This fragrance is like a warm hug from a trusted friend. It has a deep and cozy scent that feels perfect for cooler days. It starts with a burst of freshness that settles into a rich, leathery embrace. It's not overpowering, but it lasts long enough to keep you company throughout the day. The bottle is sleek and elegant, just like the fragrance inside. If you like the idea of smelling sophisticated and approachable at the same time, this one's a good choice.

Replace the musky violet-leaf note from the EDT with some more leather and add a tiny bit of iris, and you have this fragrance. I catch wafts of this every once in a while while sitting at my desk. The leather note is strikingly similar to the one in Tom Ford's Ombre Leather, which was a pleasant surprise. My favorable impression of this fragrance may be partly due to my low expectations going in. Perhaps it's the red apple note, but this fragrance is sweeter than Ombre Leather, making it more wearable. It's around 30% similar to Ombre Leather, with noticeable differences up close, but a very similar overall vibe in the air. I wasn't the biggest fan of Ombre Leather, so I might opt for this one instead. Overall, this fragrance isn't a must-try, but if you're wandering around the department store with nothing else to do, give it a sniff.

Imagine yourself, aged 6, snuggled up in your father's leather jacket during a long evening at your parents' friends' house. This fragrance takes me back to my childhood; it's similar to certain fougère fragrances from the 90s. A touch of modernity provided by the leather makes it truly post-modern. Very easily adaptable to different situations, it is nevertheless quite mature (+25 years old).

I first had tested this at my local Nordstroms. The opening was alright. It’s grown on me. It was when in my car both my daughter and I noted the drydown was very nice. In fact magical off my skin. I have other leather scents. But I like this because Ferragamo Intense Leather’s develops on my skin quite nicely, it’s that journey we all seek. I get that earthiness which at first smelled dirty but in a nice way. It gives that edge to this fragrances. Then a leathery sweetness slowly fades in while the earthiness slightly fades into the background, but still lingers like a memorable kiss. I’ve produced music and this fragrance speaks to me. It has notes that pan in and out. But the sweet leather and Iris are always there till they gently fade together into this pieces sunset. I’ve clocked this scent on my skin for 8-10+ hrs overall, again on my skin. It really clings to my skin and clothes. Peak performance? 4-5 hrs, again off my skin. I’ve got Ombré Leather and its clones, but I prefer Ferragamo Intense Leather. Thats the way this fragrance hobby goes. Some fragrances just work, from the jump, even when doubted at first, or it grows on you. It’s like an individual and that specific scent were meant for each other.

Still uncommented. Today I stumbled upon it in the perfumery. Anyone expecting a leather scent here, like the ones created by Tom Ford, which indeed focus on rough, oily notes, will be disappointed. The style here leans more towards broader wearability. The opening is definitely dominated by a fruity, subtly tart note, gradually revealing a warmer, friendlier leather underneath. More like a school pencil case than a naughty biker boot. :) Quite pleasant, not entirely free from a slight synthetic touch, but still very solid.

Little Leon and his friends find a treasure map. They see the X on the map and search for the corresponding location. They quickly find it just outside their village, in a meadow, next to a large oak tree. They have brought their shovels and are now digging at the spot.

Y: Yacht harbor yuppie X: Xantippe W: versatile, wonderful walk of shame V: seductive depravity U: unattainable primal force T: profound tuberose S: collecting sandalwood R: plentiful pink rose petals Q: quirky quartz P: clumsy patchouli O: without opoponax, open on top N: still ordering notes M: by no means modern L: lascivious vice loves lustfully K: no caramel J: jubilant jasmine I: irritating iris root incarcerated somewhere H: snobbish hyacinths from behind G: green honeysuckle stolen across F: furious for fans E: sublime, earthy oak moss D: served back then, depressingly gone C: charming chypre B: impressing bigwigs! A: Amen

I became aware of Attimo through the campaign in print media. A lady lies on the bed. She is wearing a nude-colored, chic dress, matching her simple make-up. She has beautiful red high heels on, which are about to slip off her feet. In her hand, she holds Attimo, which she has just freed from its gift packaging. I find this image incredibly elegant. Immediately, it sparks my imagination - what will happen next? Therefore, out of curiosity, I tested the perfume. The campaign fits very well with the scent. It is feminine and timeless. It smells romantic and a touch erotic, yet reserved. For me, it has the right dose of sweetness. Not a loud fragrance. Pure elegance. The pear makes the opening sparkling, then the scent becomes warm and floral. Peonies are indeed my best friends. I find the scent develops wonderfully. A warm, floral fragrance lingers long after. Thumbs up!

I tested this fragrance and had to have it. I liked it very much from the very beginning. Attimo is actually a fresh, zesty scent; the pear is not too dominant but noticeable. Together with the lotus flower, it creates a successful blend of fresh and floral notes. For me personally, this top note could last a bit longer; it becomes even more floral in the heart, but, no worries, not too much. The peony doesn’t quite dare to stand out for me. Attimo develops quite powdery, becoming softer and warmer over time, slightly woody. Very, very beautiful. An elegant, always wearable and suitable perfume, certainly not too elegant and heavy. Especially fitting in spring and summer. Now comes the only downside for me: I can only catch a whiff of the base note for a short time. The scent fades relatively quickly for me, just 2-3 hours, and then I can only sense a hint. Sometimes you hesitate to write something like this when others don’t share the same opinion. But I can’t lie, and I have tested it extensively, over and over again. So I will probably not keep my newly acquired 30 ml bottle, which I got here at an extremely good price, for long. It will likely run out faster than I thought. For this price range, it’s just too quick. I still give it 80% because the scent is so sensational and delicious; if it had more longevity, it would score even higher.

In which novel I read and copied this saying, I no longer remember. From time to time, I jot down a few things that I like in the now somewhat worn-looking little book that dear colleagues gave me 13 years ago. If these two knew that I still use it and enjoy it: shouldn't such a gift be cherished? Most of these notes have source references; this one does not. "Un Attimo" - a moment! This graceful Italian creation from the house of Ferragamo is named so. A moment often lasts only the blink of an eye and yet influences many lives; a moment can be decisive. This moment begins with ripe, juicy, and softly pale yellow pears (I not only love these fruits in fragrance form), instantly spreading a summery mood through the delicate, almost incidental lotus note. The sun shines warmly, the grass under bare feet feels invigorating, and the yellow pears glow on the old trees in the orchard, whose leaves create a lively play of shadows. A small pond, fed by a little stream, gurgles cheerfully nearby and adds additional freshness. A southern flair already permeates this moment. The initial scent is elevated by the noble blossoms of frangipani and gardenia. In contrast, the large feathery heads of the peonies not only disperse their aromatic fragrance but also lend a certain cheerfulness and tranquility to this delicate painting. Thus, this delicate fabric becomes less refined; the country child from so many farm gardens peeks around the corner with exuberance. This moment is not made for great drama; "Attimo" already smiles the most beautiful smile of every woman! A bright scent being is born, positively affecting the mood. However, it does need a bit more stability to not be so fleeting. A tasteful musk note and the slightly earthy flow of patchouli create a harmonious base that perfectly matches the already developed summer scent image. The spiciness of cedar, which wafts around this charming person like a gentle breeze, is exactly the icing on the cake that crowns a delightful, typically Italian fragrance composition: the magic of Tuscany flashes for a moment. "Attimo" is feminine, cheerful, and a bit capricious: this fragrance plays with the moment! A few spritzes on skin and hair - the smile appears, and what makes a woman more beautiful than a spontaneous smile?

... one should definitely take a moment or even several for this fragrance. I actually became aware of it solely because of its name. As a student, I once worked at the telephone exchange in the Italian Institute for Foreign Trade and was always happy when I could connect the various callers from Italy with my minimal Italian skills ... "un attimo per favore" ... phew, lucky again. And I had to think of those happy thrill moments when I first saw Attimo in the perfume shop. I liked the first sniff. It didn't quite fit my usual preferences, but it made it onto my (then still mentally noted) wishlist. A few weeks later, I tested it again, but then it was too spicy and woody for me. Eventually, I did buy it a few months ago at a good price, but my nose was not really reliable after various other fragrance samples. After reading the comments about this fragrance, which is often described here as floral and sweet, I thought I had acquired the men's fragrance instead of the women's. But no, it is indeed the one for the Signiora. Only for me, the flowers don’t develop at all, but the pear, that is softly present. Otherwise, I am wandering with Attimo in the cedar forest. Perhaps it’s in my genes; as a carpenter's daughter, the subtle woody notes always hit me hard. But what a cedar forest it is. I enjoy wandering in it and occasionally picking a little pear along the way. Because there are indeed pears in this forest. I am into soft, round, gentle, and bright fragrances. Attimo is not round, but rather angular, yet completely without sharp edges. And this flattering cedarwood cube, with its gently rounded corners, fits damn well in my hand, and I actually like it a lot. Attimo is a rugged elegance with a hint of spicy, warm sensuality, for me a perfect fragrance for autumn and winter. It works well for the office and business meetings in combination with very feminine styling. It has a somewhat rugged-serious quality that pairs perfectly with a lovely dress and stunning high heels.

I have had Attimo in my collection for so many years now. I bought the first bottle in 2011. In the meantime, I have repurchased it once - and since it is unfortunately no longer being produced, it will probably be the last one. What a shame, because among the Ferragamos, I found it to be by far the most beautiful. Attimo smells soft, warm, fruity (but not like fruit drops, rather noble, not artificial, and very pleasant) and delicately floral. A thoroughly pleasant, very noble fragrance. Yet suitable for everyday wear and all sorts of occasions. As long as you don’t overdo it with the dosage, this beautiful Italian will hardly disturb anyone, as it is unobtrusive and quite close to the skin. At least for me, but I only spray it 2 - 3 times. The pear comes across soft and gentle, not as squeaky-fruity as in Petit Cherie. More like smelling a freshly picked pear. Lotus makes the fruit beautifully light and does it good. In the heart note, I can best recognize frangipani, and the peony makes the fragrance beautifully fresh and prevents it from slipping into tropical realms. A hint of gardenia adds a friendly floral note, but it hardly stands out. In the base, cedar provides a balsamic woodiness, and a bit of musk adds creamy warmth without becoming animalistic. I don’t perceive any patchouli. The longevity is good; I notice it on myself for about 5 hours, then the scent begins to fade gently. R.I.P. Attimo!

So, I finally have it. I actually just wanted to quickly grab my mousse at the mall after work, but only a tiny "moment" passed, and the little gem was in my basket, shrinking my wish list by a small piece.

Hooked by a sample from a dear perfume member, I acquired this scent. A few times I sprayed it with great delight - first the fruity pear, really fine and transparent, then a delicate floral accompaniment (here I believe I recognize the frangipani) and finally a very pleasant, slightly woody musky base. Perfect!

Just before Christmas 2010, I sprayed Attimo on a test strip and was immediately taken with it. This scent is simply beautiful. The top note is fruity, but very subtle. Normally, my favorite fragrances have a much stronger opening. This one consists mostly of mandarin, bergamot, peach... pear in the top note is something completely different.

~ Inspiration ~ I discovered “Attimo” while browsing on Parfumo and got myself a sample. ~ Bottle ~ The bottle looks like offset, stacked discs, forming a small tower. The shades of nude and silver are simple yet elegant. “Attimo” means something like “moment.

I am not a fan of fresh, aquatic scents and especially not a fan of pear. But this perfume has something!...it's so interesting and fluid, so soft and light and warm and calm! So perfect that I am truly taken with it. The pear does not overwhelm with its sweetness, probably thanks to the lotus. It is warm and transparent.

This first official Opium flanker has popped up on the ebay market. I had to have it simply because its under $50. Its from the same era all of those YSL gourmands-In Love Again, Vice Versa and Live Jazz. Opium final gets its day in the sun, literally. I cannot wait to try this on the next hot day. How can you lighten the dense heavy original of legend? (Opium=hot & spicy decadence.) You cant really, yet this is a nice variation It is alcohol free and acts like a body spray or EDC. I imagine it was thought up for those Opium lovers who want to wear it to the beach in the sunshine. Indeed, it has a "suntan oil" quality. Its almost a little too synthetic, yet not as fake as the current 2009 reformulation. It opens a with an effervescent orange tang. The spice is turned down to a whisper with ginger and white pepper most prominent. You get Opium echoes at times. Mostly the greener floral notes and some amber smoke. It reminds me of the body cream that tames everything down, yet you can tell its Opium. A times I get the Coca Cola and vanilla caramel in this. I have to say its the most distant interpretation of the classic before 2009. That alone was a bold move in the day. It qualifies as a light warm weather compatible cousin to Opium. Oh, did I mention its playful and has a sense of humor? You cannot help but smile when you sniff this.

Opium is opulent, spicy, oriental, diva-like, and a true cold-weather perfume. Certainly a rather heavy task to create a fresh summer variant from this winter milestone... but somehow the creators succeeded brilliantly in '98. A great achievement, in my opinion, that could have been showcased for longer than the few months/years of the limited release... but it was probably measured against the sales figures of the original, which one can only lose against. Or it was just switched to the annual summer flankers. I hope anyway that my sample fits the bottle shown here, as my Opium Eau Fraiche is stuck on it. Opium Fraicheur is a citrusy oriental. The bergamot and mandarin weave a net around the smoky spices of the original. And this net is under constant tension, the Orient wants to break free. But ginger, mandarin & co. hold on as best they can, allowing the notes of the original to gain the upper hand only after hours. Really beautiful, really skillful, surprisingly fitting. Who would have thought that Opium could also be summer. But when people are behind the controls who know what they are doing & are fans of the original themselves, then something like this can really work well, against all expectations. I am also quite sure that Fraicheur is better than all the following summer d'etes... but that is just a guess. Or maybe one of those is the 1:1 reincarnation. Bottle: summery cult Sillage: heavy for a fraiche... for those who need their grand entrance on the edge of the bearable even in summer. Longevity: Opium remains Opium... 10 hours! Conclusion: an extremely successful summer adaptation of a theme that couldn't have been less suitable for summer... Chapeau!

For the summer, I ordered Virgin Island Water, which I was able to receive today with friends. Included: A black little box with three samples from the "Tuscan Scent" line by Salvatore Ferragamo. My clear favorite from it is Incense Suede. Why is that? Well, because the scent character can clearly be attributed to another perfume that I already own: Amouage Jubilation XXV Man. The same blackberry in the top note, referred to here as dried fruits. Along with the sour, conifer-like heart note and the oudy-smoky-oriental base. The focus here is mainly on the blackberry, and the scent feels a bit dirtier than the Amouage (stable note), which I quite like. In terms of complexity, quality, and performance, it doesn't come close to the original. Still, a solid scent that attracts me mainly because of this dark temple-cellar-vault vibe, which the Amouage lacks. As I said, this one is dirtier, but unfortunately also simpler. Since the price is also in the niche fragrance range, I would prefer to reach for the Jubilation XXV. All in all, however, a quite successful oriental fragrance.

Hey guys, today I'm commenting on the fragrance Testa di Moro, also known as Incense Suede by Salvatore Ferragamo. I had a sample of this fragrance lying around and I'm always happy when I have samples of women's fragrances :D On the other hand, it wouldn't have been a problem to test such a fragrance in the women's section, as I no longer have such big issues testing women's fragrances in public, especially when the bottles look like this one. I do feel a bit uneasy now and then when I have to pick up a bottle that looks pretty, sweet, cute, colorful, and just very feminine, like the fragrance Signora from the same brand, which comes in a pink bottle with a cute bow. Or fragrances like Chloe, Prada Candy, or the worst of all: Juicy Couture :D (Although most fragrances from these brands smell great on me, I mean on a girl :D). But anyway, at least it's not as extremely bad as it was some time ago when I could only test fragrances in the women's section if I was wearing an invisibility cloak or something :DD That being said, here comes Testa di Moro from the slightly more exclusive collection of Salvatore Ferragamo. It is a beautiful, resinous fragrance with leather notes, but "see" for yourself: The Fragrance: The fragrance starts with intense incense, which as always gives off a resinous-sweet scent and, if you like this note, smells quite good. In the background, it has an herbal-spicy aroma. There’s pink pepper, which smells both spicy and slightly fruity, and then there’s something “kitchen spice-like,” perhaps it’s the saffron that comes across as nicely spicy. You can also distinctly smell the dried fruits, although I must admit that without the fragrance pyramid, I would never have guessed that it was dried fruits (you just don't encounter this note in enough fragrances to remember it well, but now that I know, I can say that it smells like dried plums to me, which also comes across as sweet). A little later, you can also clearly smell the leather. Otherwise, it mostly remains with the resins and leather, as the fruity-sweet notes fade a bit into the background towards the base, making the fragrance not very sweet, and thus it comes across as more woody-leathery and spicy-resinous. Much later, the resinous and leathery notes are most prominent, while the woody and spicy scents recede a bit more. All in all, it’s quite a nice fragrance. The Sillage and Longevity: The sillage is strong at first, but settles into a moderate range as the fragrance develops, so you can't smell it very well from a distance, but you also don't have to get too close. The longevity, on the other hand, is significantly better, as the fragrance lasts over eight hours on the skin. The Bottle: The black bottle appears cylindrical, but is actually rectangular, with all sides slightly curved outward and the bottle seeming to get slightly wider in height. The brand and name are written in gold on the bottle, topped off with a cylindrical, brown wooden cap with a golden underside. A beautiful, elegantly designed bottle. Okay, I liked the fragrance. Not so much that I feel I need to have it, as I'm not a huge fan of leather notes, but overall I find the fragrance very successful, so I would recommend testing it, especially if you like resinous and leathery notes. Because you can't really complain about the fragrance itself, except maybe that "Many-Fragrance-Tester" (sounds like an Indian name :D) might see it as one of those fragrances that have already been tested several times. But that's just how it is when you try many fragrances. It becomes increasingly difficult to find something truly new (and pleasant-smelling), but that doesn't mean that the thousandth resinous fragrance can't smell good for someone! In terms of type, I would place it in autumn, but also in spring, as it is neither very light nor too heavy. It is unisex, although I would lean more towards the masculine side. And there’s really not much more to say, so I’ve reached the end and wish you all a lovely evening :)

Could a fragrance start more beautifully than with - incense? In this case, a quick puff of white correction fluid incense; meanwhile, I suspect Elemi resin for this twist and urgently request any relevant information. Then a bright wood note briefly appears. But soon the scent becomes strongly smoky-tarry-acidic. More charred or smoked wood than leather. In style, it is close to Mona di Orio's 'Cuir', where leather is also predominantly found in the name. In another top smoker, namely Naomi Goodsir's 'Bois d’Ascese', there is mention of smoked cedar-juniper as an ingredient. I still haven't smelled it in nature, but the mere term fits here associatively as well. The Ferragamo calms down quickly, surprisingly swiftly for a representative of this fragrance direction, and becomes comparatively elegant. Almost, at least, as it remains characteristically distinct and lasting into the evening. Therefore, it is to be suspected that the predominantly restrained volume is exactly intentional. On the website, there is talk of the tobacco notes of mate tea. No idea how that stuff smells, but tobacco can surprisingly be interpreted into it without difficulty. Very aromatic, thus naturally unsmoked. More Brazil than Sumatra, with excellent depth and spice. Even a non-smoker can appreciate such things at this point. From the third hour onward, the fragrance components merge a bit with each other, as if they were given a barely perceptible, creamy base. And just as an Italian suit gently envelops the body while still emphasizing it, the strong notes are carefully integrated without being trimmed in their nature or individuality of appearance. The wood steadily darkens over time, an impression that is intensified by the resin/smoke and the subtle acidity of the as-if tobacco. Ebony, mahogany, and the like come to mind from the afternoon onward. For leather, I initially need a bit of imagination in this phase, but then it can be sensed again, even in a birch-tar-like way. After all, there are variations of it that are stylistically related to the previously mentioned colleagues. Incense Suede remains true to its line until the end. The wood may become a bit airier from the seventh or eighth hour, but those are nuances and by no means age mellowness. No drifting into common, possibly dull base products. Upright walk until the end. Conclusion: I hadn't had Ferragamo on my radar at all until now. Unjustly, as I now realize. Ergoproxy has packed me a real gem - thank you very much! Those who lay down around 150 euros at the perfumery with the sharp vowel at the front will be rewarded with a characteristically powerful, noble smoke-wood-tobacco-leather fragrance in an apparently very attractive bottle. P.S.: I don't know what that has to do with Tuscany. Does the tree burn that much? The name can be irrelevant to me.

I've been searching for a rose fragrance. I never knew exactly what I was searching for but I think I've found it with Pure Love! The biggest complaint I've had about most rose fragrances I've tried is that no matter how nice they are they're almost universally somber. Pure Love has finally shown me that rose fragrances can be bright and energetic! The opening is clean, almost soapy rose. Very little sweetness and an almost smokiness, likely from the ambergris/vetiver and leather. This fragrance has the syntheticness that you would expect from Montale and Mancera. That said it is very well blended and quite nice. And unless you're very put off by anything synthetic it's tolerable. This is the type of rose scent that most men could pull off. Performance is decent too. Projection is quite good for the first few hours off skin and better off clothes. Deep dry down off skin is sort of a standard woody vanillic scent. Overall I definitely recommend this to anyone searching for a rose scent. Especially men who have found that most rose scents are either too somber or too feminine.

It was time for a new fragrance again. I went to a perfume shop and sought advice. I wanted something that not everyone could wear and had a distinctive character. I told the lady in the perfume shop that I had recently smelled Café Intense by Montale and would like to smell more from the brand. The lady introduced me to various Montale fragrances, and the second one was Pure Love. After the first spray, an explosive cloud of rose made itself known and dominated the other notes - no room for vanilla, leather, etc. Now comes the twist: After a while, the rose gradually recedes into the background, allowing the vanilla to emerge in combination with leather and sandalwood - a perfect interplay that is addictive.

I bought the fragrance as a blind buy. Upon the first spray, I thought: Uhh, upon smelling it again: Ahh. Conclusion: The scent needs a little time. Now it’s one of my favorite fragrances. A very spicy-leathery scent that initially smells very much like leather combined with rose. Over time, it develops into an incredibly sweet-vanilla scent that I also like very much. I can really recommend it, especially for the price. The longevity and sillage are not extremely impressive, but still sufficient.

Looking at the fragrance pyramid, it suggests a sweet-spicy scent. This is definitely true. At the outset, this fragrance smells quite woody, which I attribute to the sandalwood. Then the beautiful Montale rose joins in, but it never stands out distinctly for me; instead, it blends perfectly with the amber. I personally do not detect vetiver. Vanilla is also part of the mix, and I only smell leather when I sniff directly on the skin. I’m glad about that because I generally like leather in fragrances - but when it stands out too much, it unfortunately often gives me a headache. So that's not a problem here. I bought the fragrance blind back then. And at first, I thought it was a completely failed blind purchase. During the first test, I was almost a bit shocked. Only after further tests did I understand the fragrance a bit better and get used to it. Now I like it a lot. For me, it was a bit like love. Because it also needs to grow and is not fully there right from the start. Although the huge wow effect is honestly rather absent with this fragrance, it is still a pleasant caresser that I can wear year-round (more in the evenings during summer). I wouldn’t want to miss it in my collection, as it is very pleasant to wear and fits many occasions for me. Not every fragrance has to have the potential of Baccarat Rouge, as I could never wear that daily, for example, because it is just something very special. My rating: Scent: 8 / 10 Longevity: 7 / 10 Sillage: 7 / 10 Recognition value: 8 / 10

That's exactly how I felt while testing. Not vanilla crescents but fruity spice cake. At first, I briefly thought of oranges studded with cloves. That must be the mandarin that I confuse with oranges. But very quickly it goes in the spice direction, but not in the bitter, rather in the sweet. Hence my comparison to the spiced cake with fruits. After about an hour, the spices also take on a slightly softer, creamier note. So very nice, an ideal winter fragrance, not just for Christmas. But: after only two hours, I had to sniff my wrist quite a bit to perceive anything. Already after 3 hours, it was all over. Apparently, it doesn't suit my skin chemistry. Really a shame, I liked the scent, but for such a short pleasure, it's too expensive for me.

Tuscan soul opens fresh with bergamot and petit grain and a some kind of tea note. maybe that are the citrus leaves who makes it a bit woody. The scent does remind me of Italie with his orange and lemon trees. Its an easy to wear scent on skin it becomes slightly warmer but it suits in my opinion the best on warm sunkissed skin

A beautiful, light citrus based scent that one can certainly imagine wearing on a warm Summer's day while strolling along the beach feeling the sand between your toes. This scent is so refreshing and delicate, almost like someone has squeezed lemon juice and mandarin orange directly onto your skin. Such an energizing and delightful feeling. Be warned that this is a very intimate fragrance, stays very close to the skin. Tuscan Soul is not the kind of fragrance that will overwhelm the people around you, rather it will please yourself and the people that you allow to transcend past your personal boundaries. Salvatore Ferragamo has shifted back to their original approach to fragrance compositions, leaving behind their most recent fruity floral presentations aimed solely at the younger market. Tuscan Soul is for the older market, men and women who prefer their Summer scents to exude class and distinction.

My local fragrance dealer sells me opened bottles very cheaply - even though only a tiny bit is missing. They are for my mom in the care home, where full bottles occasionally go missing. The opened ones remain untouched. I told him this annoying story, and he had the idea to bring her barely used tester bottles. And Tuscan Soul fits perfectly into her preferences. The scent is citrusy fresh - yet sweet and expressive - like the Tuscan landscape that we loved to explore together. There, the air was filled with bright bergamot, herbaceous - fresh petitgrain, and the aroma of lemon trees. Delicate rosy floral notes are brushed into the Tuscan picture by magnolia, emphasized by gentle orange blossom. The gnarled wood of the fig tree gives the refreshing scent character, and the iris adds a soft powderiness. The alluring soul of Tuscany is well captured in the fragrance. Since my mom can no longer travel, this "mental journey" will do her good - and I will gladly accompany her.

If the soul of Tuscany is as shallow and simple as this, I would find it quite sad. Salvatore Ferragamo is still becoming the right fig brand, even if this green plant takes up far less space here than in the discontinued Geheimtipp Pour Homme. Actually good, because there are notes that I prefer. However, Pour Homme had a clear goal, is striking, extremely bright green, and still masculine, which almost makes the fig shortcoming forgettable. Tuscan Soul is really a lukewarm hotel room scent for men, women, children, dogs, cleaning ladies, hotel managers, freshly showered people, and perfume haters. In short: green, summery, defensive, fresh, very citrusy, just exaggerated. Like an Aqua Universalis on sleeping pills or on a subscription plan. Sensual and seductive is something else. Stinky and unpleasant, but definitely that too. Still, there are so many better perfumes for summer that Tuscan Soul simply calls out its performance like a follower, but nothing more. Bottle: below average Longevity: below below average Sillage: below below below average It is probably only possible to rate this scent better than average if you have stayed in one of the hotels where it is sprayed or distributed and thus associate it with nice memories. Because the scent itself desperately needs some pep and color; it is too pale for me.

My first impression - it’s not Mediterranean at all! The citrus notes are strongly overshadowed by the magnolia from the very beginning of the fragrance development. The scent changes only minimally until the base. In the end, the soul of Tuscany is a bit spicier and no longer quite so banal. However, I don’t experience the scent of fig wood through this fragrance, and the powdery aspect of the iris is also more than subtle. It’s a scent that I find just okay, but it doesn’t blow me away. I would have liked to give this fragrance a more extensive first comment, but unfortunately, it didn’t really have much to say to me.

"Tuscan Soul" came back into my hands while I was organizing my perfumes after quite some time. "What kind of scent was that again?" I thought to myself, and sprayed it on the back of my hand. Something fresh tickled my nose, and it smelled like "more".

I know that this fragrance is viewed as that result of crossing two other Montale scents, but I see it as an exercise in abstraction. A sharp, whistling musk, like the one in Thierry Mugler's Cologne is the perfect match to a woody quality that makes for a sort of leather scent-mirage. The wood seems like patchouli plus oud, inflected with something in the mace/nutmeg/cardamom range. Black Musk's cleverness is in creating a tarry quality with patchouli, spice and just a taste of oud, then dry-cleaning it with a prickly musk that someone along the way surely told the perfumer was the wrong musk. No pillowy soft or bosomed musk. The result is a cool, inky leather scent that focuses more on the sharp nature of tanning chemicals than that of the hide itself. I'll take this chance to own up to a bit of fumie apostasy. I don't particularly like oud, and since it’s usually the overwhelming center of perfumes that contain it, most oud perfumes don’t capture me. Likely this quirk has saved me a pile of money on niche perfumery and the laughingly late-to-the party top-shelf lines from the designer/perfume houses. This implicitly self-defeating strategy of the perfume houses launching ‘exclusive’ lines in order to appear ‘niche-y’ has produced an inordinate number of oud fragrances. (To witness niche, copying designer, copying niche, please see the Kilian Ouds.) Very few use oud as a minor part of an accord, one where you might not even recognize oud, such as Black Musk’s delicious vinyl/leather accord. Shame, yeah?

Musky and musty... not sweet and neither powerful as other Montales. I smell lots of nutmeg with some woods and leather. This can be used all seasons. Remembers more Musk to Musk than Black Aoud. Its similarities with Black Aoud ceases in the first 30 minutes. Updated January 2014

Black musk has a thousand guises, Viscous,glutinous,adhesive,viscid,dark,black,opaque,death-like,mysterious, esoteric,heavy,authoritarian,autocratic,dictatorial,imperious,decadence, villains. There is nothing Sparkly about Black Musk, when you wear this it's like your entering the Edge of darkness where light hasn't penetrate not even the bright hues of amber and fiery Sandalwood note stand on there own,they sink in this Black Abyss. I Can Picture Vilians like Le Chiffre from Casino Royal, Jaffar from Thief of Baghdad and Lestat from Queen of the Dead, Black Musk is not for everyone it's only for a select few who appreciate the Fine art of fragrance not your typical day at a office kind of Scent.

If perfumers were allowed to create freely, without the constraints of sales - we would probably only have strange perfumes: fantastic scents, testaments to the greatness of their creators, and likely all of them unbearable! One person might not join in - Pierre Montale. He has a very special passion - Arabic perfumery. I notice that among Arabs, there is hardly any cult of genius. The names of the perfumers remain largely unknown, and traditional Arabic perfumes sometimes seem to be of extraordinary simplicity. Often, it’s really just about a popular fragrance note - Oud - which is available in various nuances and qualities. Besides Oud or agarwood, there are floral notes, especially rose, sometimes saffron as a spice, then amber, sandalwood, and finally - musk! Pierre Montale also operates within this manageable framework with many of his Arabic-inspired perfumes. However, the extensive range of the Montale brand is divided into 3 lines: - Western perfumes of different directions, completely without Arabic influences (Boisé Vanillé, Fougère Marine, Red Vetyver, ...), - Traditional Arab perfumes, mostly centered around the classic rose/Oud combination (Black Aoud, Steam Aoud, Aoud Flowers...) or other traditional focuses (Amber & Spices, Greyland), - Perfumes that combine the classic Arabic art of perfumery with Western, often contemporary fragrance directions and trends (Wild Aoud, Oud Cuir d'Arabie, Louban, Aoud Forest...) Whenever Montale releases another perfume oriented towards traditional Arabic art, he can be accused of repeating himself. Because often it is only nuances that differentiate the individual Montale creations in this direction from one another. They all operate in a field between the extremes allowed by the fragrance notes from Oud to sandalwood outlined above. For blends of different perfumes and fragrance notes, the Arabic perfumers, to my knowledge, have a specific name: Mukhallat. Black Musk would also be such a Mukhallat, but Pierre Montale has already named another of his perfumes with this designation. Black musk is certainly included, but not exclusively, and so I do not consider the naming successful. Black Musk begins like many Montale scents with this typical, harsh hairspray note. It lingers here remarkably long. Oud - or a synthetic substitute - is definitely involved. I cannot yet say exactly what black musk is supposed to smell like. Musk has so many variations; I believe I can now recognize the light creamy, powdery, and even soapy musk notes well. A comparison with "Misku-l Ka'ba," which AbuSaffia once provided me, revealed no similarities with Black Musk apart from a general harshness and dark tone. I rather see a slight tendency towards amber, not ambra. I have experienced this in Arabic perfumes in a light to strong smoky manner. The confusion between the fragrance terms amber and ambra (as indicated in the pyramid) would be a topic in itself. The sandalwood note in Black Musk is very pronounced and somewhat dominant; there are also different synthetic substances that represent various nuances, to my knowledge. I dare to say that Black Musk contains a lot of Javanol. I perceive nutmeg and pepper notes in Black Musk, if at all, as general spice and sharpness. In a way, Black Musk is a Mukhallat, as it is placed right in the circle of the different Arabic Montales. So there is a bit of everything. On one side, there is some Oud, which connects Black Musk with Montale's dark and heavy Ouds. Then we have sandalwood and amber - making it similar to the perfumes Amber & Spices and also Greyland. And then there is of course leather. The leather note is the same as in Montale's Oud Cuir d'Arabie, just a bit more subtle, and it fades as a heart note after about an hour. As a common ground, Black Musk has resulted in a generally darker and harsher perfume. It is difficult to make a purchase recommendation specifically for Black Musk, as everything at Montale is closely related. In doubt, the interested buyer will not find all Arabic Montale perfumes gathered on a shelf for testing anyway.

Leave me alone with Montale! I want to scream this louder and more emphatically after every single one of their tested fragrances. Once again: loud, thundering, hair spray-like force and penetrance. The main thing is noise, 4-6 blue lights on the roof, and stinking 30 meters against the wind. "Black Musk" drones from the very first second. A lot of hair spray-like musk, coarse, hearty, glazed, somehow also chemical, headache-inducing. Behind it, there might still be a mix of nutmeg (dry, over-seasoned) and sandalwood hiding somewhere. Otherwise, this is simply a horrendously made penetrating scent of the worse Montale variety. They have made 1-2 somewhat solid things (in the rose area), but even with those, 7.0 points is already a generous rating gift from me.

With Black Musk, Montale presents us with another fragrance that couldn't be more typical for this brand. For Black Musk has, like several others from this exclusive series, dedicated itself to the highly characteristic leather/oud theme; Pierre Montale seems to enjoy exhausting himself in this area, as he is considered a leading expert in the field.

The facts: Leather. Dark, coarse, freshly tanned beef Parker. Context: Sweet little girl musk, soapy, dirty, unrefined, skin-like, cheeky but still cute. Ethereal: Pine needle scented bubble bath. Combo of agarwood/mace? Not edible but enjoyable.

There are fragrances that you need to test multiple times before discovering your love for them, and then there are fragrances like Black Musk, where just one spritz is enough to fall in love immediately. At least that was my experience during testing, as it has everything I expect from a good, high-quality scent.

Musk... One imagines something soft, sweet, perhaps even something unremarkable, since there are so many musk fragrances. But wait! The first sniff truly knocks you off your feet. What comes is intense, spicy, dark, leathery, and wild. Blacker than black. Freedom and adventure. Perfect for the modern cowgirl or cowboy riding into the sunset on their Harley.

"Black Musk" surprised me quite a bit, because... it doesn't have the punch that I know from the other Montales. The beginning is the typical Montale opening that you recognize from many of this brand. I think I can also detect a hint of rose, which is not listed here. So, another rose-oud perfume from Montale?

Rummaging through my endless supply of minis, I came across this gentle and forgotten beauty. It had little time on the stage. I can compare it to Yvresse and it definitely takes a different direction. Some of the best flankers arrived from YSL in the 1990s. This can be counted as one of them. It is truly light and warm weather friendly. The rose is barely there. The focus is mimosa, peach, lilac and possibly freesia/lily? It's almost aquatic and a little gourmand. There is a small chypre accord of patchouli, oakmoss and a whisper of vetiver on a most fragile base of sandalwood/cedar. It lasts about 3 hours with minimal projection. At the end of the 1990s, YSL was all about testing the market while trusting the classics as the foundation of sales. The first flankers for Opium, Rive Gauche and Paris were introduced. Paris Baby Doll was a hit. Everything else just vanished into perfume history. Sadly after 2009 everything was radically changed by L'Oreal Paris. This is required sniffing for all serious YSL fans. Otherwise, its getting expensive and not a public favorite.

Anyone who enjoys sewing might be familiar with this phenomenon: A fabric is appealing because it has a certain structure. However, the color might not be particularly special. Or conversely, the color is wonderful, but something is off with the structure. If it’s smooth but has a pattern in "matching" colors, the structure might be too much of a good thing. If it’s solid, a striking structure fits well. I sometimes feel similarly about fragrances. With this "Yvresse," it’s quite peculiar. Here we have both the color: pastel purple, "old rose," the structure: small bumps in finely woven linen, as well as the pattern: flowers, delicate garlands, and "grass." All of this is not uniformly spread across the entire piece, but has partially self-contained phases, while at times the "pattern" transitions into the structure, leaving the "color" on the outside. Or: right in the heart of the fragrance, the "color" dominates without being influenced by structure and pattern. In the base, however, the slightly "rough" structure stands out clearly, while during the initial stages, the pattern emerges even into areas of the "heart." Yet, there are no larger, overloaded dissonances because everything engages in a fairly "competitive" manner. I can only speak of good "craftsmanship," of competent and imaginative perfumers who have created a small masterpiece. Elegant, yet robust and cheerfully "patterned." Like a good fabric for sewing... ;-))

So, I have now found this "old" classic with me, and felt the need to describe it. Once again, a fragrance from Yves Saint Laurent, with a classic note, which was probably discontinued in production. This treasure is a wonderfully light, somewhat fresher classic that was a bit different from Yvresse, which is quite fruity and rather heavy. Unfortunately, this variant of Yvresse (Legere) is no longer available. I do believe there are quite a few users who would love this perfume! Yvresse Legere is very similar to the classic Yvresse, but Legere is lighter, fresher, not with such a fruity bouquet as is the case with Yvresse! This fragrance has a velvety quality, starting off slightly fruity-fresh, which then transitions into a wonderful cuddly velvet note with a hint of cinnamon and cardamom. The blackcurrant is not as prominent here as in Yvresse; the mimosa, citrus-scented rose, and woody notes clearly play the main role alongside spices and slightly mossy facets. Nevertheless, the spirit of the classic Yvresse is also clearly perceptible here, just as mentioned above, not quite as fruity, rather fresher, lighter, not so oppressive, as I felt Yvresse was back then.... Yvresse was not my perfume, but Yvresse Legere is an interesting second variant of the classic Yvresse, which is similar yet different and appeals to me very much! I always thought Yvresse was more of an autumn fragrance, but Legere is definitely wearable for summer as well! So, please test it or search for the scent, it's worth it!

Today was an exciting day for me, as my husband and I met the new partner of my dear mother-in-law. I was so nervous, as if I had my first date. My husband was visibly unimpressed and shook his head in disbelief at my clothing "vernissage." Chic, but not over the top - casual, but not sloppy was how I wanted my look to be. A dress, a skirt, or pants - what should it be? My husband dryly asked me if I had made such a "fuss" at our first meeting as well? Uh - to be honest - no. He still remembered my checkered cotton shirt, paired with jeans that had "real" holes in the knees. Well, I was only responsible for myself back then. Confused, I called my mother-in-law, and she understood, as she had picked out a chic dress for herself, only to realize in the mirror that it was a nightgown. Also a good solution! We laughed heartily, and the tension faded for both of us. The meeting turned out to be harmonious - without any mishaps, and now I reflect on the day. Ferragamo helps me with this, as it mirrors the events. The lychee neroli blend starts fresh and exciting - but is gently calmed by powdery iris. The orange blossom warms, and the patchouli conveys closeness. Relaxation sets in. So was my day - and may the lovely couple also enjoy good times together.

Hrrmrmrm… it’s evening again. The whole world is waiting for my new comment. The whole world? No… all the perfumes and parfumos! All the perfumes and parfumos? Nooo,… not all,… if I’m lucky, there are two or three here who are reading this despite the warm weather *sigh* And yet I write day after day, at least as long as I still have samples or have tried scents in the city. Because I write many comments in advance so that I can totally spam here every day (but also to show my presence here so that you heartless lot don’t forget me, waah!), and because I don’t test fragrances every day (yes, yes, I’m not THAT much of a fragrance freak like you, I could theoretically survive for months without sniffing a single scent! Well, can you say the same about yourselves? “Being on vacation and therefore having no time for fragrances” doesn’t count, by the way! :DD). He he, well, today it’s Salvatore Ferragamo’s turn. A brand from which I haven’t tried many fragrances yet. But if I stay here for a while longer, I’m sure I’ll have tried quite a few scents from this brand soon… which could be quite nice, considering the beautiful fragrances that seem to exist when you smell this one! The Scent: I have some difficulty smelling the lychee listed in the top notes, but I do smell two wonderful, soft, and beautiful fragrance notes at the beginning, namely a powdery iris that seems to come off a bit creamy, as well as lovely neroli, which gives off a nice, not citrusy-splashy, but still fresh scent. I quickly also smell the musk, which isn’t too sweet at first, but its clean aura pairs excellently with the also clean-smelling iris. The scent has something of some of those beautiful Prada Infusion fragrances, which all come off nice and pure, only this scent here is less soapy, which is often a noticeable characteristic of the Pradas. It also smells as described later in the base (with the neroli being weaker then), but then another note comes in that somehow smells nutty. Yes, that might come from the patchouli, but to me it doesn’t smell earthy or really like patchouli, but really quite nutty. After a while, however, these notes fade again or become weaker! The musk becomes a bit sweeter, but doesn’t become heavier or oppressive (for warm days, it’s quite pleasant despite the increased sweetness) and the rest remains as described. The Sillage and Longevity: The projection is rather weak, and therefore the scent is only noticeable from up close. It will soon seem quite weak to oneself as well if you don’t spray it properly on your clothes or something! The longevity is average for a summer scent, meaning it lasts about three to four hours and then is hardly noticeable anymore. The Bottle: The bottle is cylindrical or slightly oval and widens in height. It has a very thick glass bottom and is filled with light violet fragrance liquid. At the neck, there is a chrome band on which the cylindrical wooden cap sits. The name of the fragrance is visible on the front, below which is a signature that serves as the company logo. A beautiful bottle. Ah, the fragrance with the long name has turned out to be very pleasant, even though it is actually quite simply structured and therefore hardly stands out from other similar scents. It belongs to that type of fragrances that convey a feeling of cleanliness and purity in the form of a pleasant scent, making you feel good and the fragrance sits nicely in the nose without ever becoming annoying.
