The scent is wonderfully powdery soft, slightly creamy, and due to its looseness, it’s a damn good summer companion, as it can be worn very well on hot days due to its non-intrusive sweetness and not too strong powdery notes. And it’s also very suitable as a vacation scent, for example when you’re at the beach and enjoying yourself under the sun and of course in the sea, lying on a water mattress and admiring the beautiful landscape made up of blue sea, blue sky, bikini tops and bikini bottoms. Sometimes even one-pieces. And more bikinis, and more one-pieces and more… damn, woe to anyone who says I desperately need a girlfriend, don’t say that, that’s nothing new!!! Come up with something new instead... or am I talking about myself here? Hmmm.... :D (Next time I’ll just tell you something about Batman again... well, that’s what you get!) As I said, the scent is definitely worth testing if you like powdery and clean fragrances and don’t mind occasionally perceiving a nutty scent.

It’s a village in summery Southern Italy. I woke up late and it’s already getting quite hot outside. I’m standing at the open window in the kitchen of the old stone house, looking directly at an orange tree that is in full bloom, being pampered by the summer sun right outside the window. In the kitchen, various ingredients are chaotically spread out, used for making pastries and sweets. In the oven, several trays of something sweet are baking. The aromas from the oven mix with the scents of the blooming orange trees, the garden, and the heated grass that are flowing in through the window. "My God...", I think to myself, "how good I have it..." Last Saturday, I stood in the Montale boutique in Paris in front of the shelf with the 2023 releases. I think there were five (?) last year. I sniffed three of them - all three are good: Infinity, Holy Neroli, and Lucky Candy. I actually wanted to get something completely different, but in the end, I bought Holy Neroli (+ Infinity Travel Spray). Holy Neroli is exactly what I was looking for. A not too complicated, strong, Mediterranean, sweet summer/summer evening fragrance. Love Don't Be Shy Perfume Regarding the similarity to Love Don't Be Shy by Kilian: I’m holding the bottle with the last drops of the old Love Don't Be Shy and the new bottle of Holy Neroli in my hands. There is the initial similarity of sweet orange blossoms. After that, LDBS goes towards fluffy toffee/marshmallow, while Holy Neroli heads towards spicy petitgrain honey. One could say that while there is this similar idea of orange blossoms on sweets, it is more robust and perhaps "masculine" in Holy Neroli. This means that Holy Neroli is not a replacement for LDBS, but ladies and gentlemen who like Love Don't Be Shy but find it too "feminine" should definitely give Holy Neroli a try! P.P.S. with all understanding for different tastes - giving the fragrance a 0.5 is trolling.

It is a warm summer day around 1987. I can still see it as if it were yesterday. I am about 7 years old and standing with my grandma in a pilgrimage church that she visited once a year. She rummages through her old black handbag and pulls out small single-use packets, each containing a refreshment wipe, among tissues and other odds and ends. She opens one of the small blue packets, and even as a child, I wondered what exactly she was refreshing with this not-so-cool and slightly damp paper towel. In any case: Holy Neroli is exactly the scent of that little wipe from back then. And just now while writing, I get goosebumps at the coincidence, due to the name Holy and the connection to the pilgrimage church. Can such coincidences exist?

Can we please talk about this beautiful bottle? Wow, orange and gold represent elegance but also playfulness and zest. That's how I would describe the scent as well. Are you looking for Neroli!? With this fragrance, you get it in charged power! I experienced this spicy-sweet Neroli note on my skin for about 6 hours. Just as it greets me in the opening, it stays quite consistent with me. Only a bit of freshness adds itself, which I found very pleasant, as it was already quite captivatingly sweet in its Neroli-spice cloud. After 6 hours, I still detected sweet-soft vanilla paired with musk. It surely lasts even longer on clothing. I would advise against a blind buy here, as it is quite specific. I like Neroli-vanilla scents, but this one has perhaps too special a touch for me due to the included spices. Sillage is very good. Even after showering, you can still perceive it.

The name promises exactly what it says. The scent smells completely of Neroli, and I really like that. Fresh scents always appeal to me, and even though it’s not a citrus fragrance, I am still very positively surprised by this scent. I received it as a sample after ordering it with my Arabians from Montale, and since then I’ve been considering buying it. The fragrance is so fresh and simply extremely floral. I really feel like I’m lying in a flower meadow and just feeling happy. About the bottle: The "tin cans" from Montale often receive a lot of hate, but I actually like them very much, especially this one. The pattern on the front is also very appealing. In my review of the Arabians from Montale, I already mentioned that sometimes I feel there’s a lack of diversity among the scents from Montale, but here it’s exactly the opposite; it’s an incredibly unique and good fragrance. As I said, I’ve been considering getting this scent for a while now, and I think that all in all, the fragrance is really excellent and the price-performance ratio is too. I can only recommend it.

This fragrance opens with a shockingly overpowering blast of neroli. Thus, this scent sends everyone, including myself, who is put off by orange blossoms, running for the hills. After a good half hour, the calamity is over and neroli comes across sweetly and reconciliatory-could it be the vanilla? I am indeed pleasantly surprised now. After about 6 hours, neroli is hardly perceptible anymore, but it becomes distinctly oriental and spicy. Montale has not convinced me so far, although I count this one among the better ones, even though the opening is truly frightening.

Sometimes a fragrance wants more than it can actually deliver, and Holy Neroli is such a candidate. The opening? Clearly, neroli takes the lead here. Fresh, floral, almost a bit soapy - like a sunny morning, but one where the alarm clock has pulled you out of sleep too early. Somehow, this neroli lacks the depth that makes the heart race.

This fragrance was a blind buy, but a successful one. Montale has created a wonderful, fresh, and yet extraordinary scent here. Of course, you have to like neroli. Those with a 4711 trauma should stay away from it. But for those who already love Aqua Allegoria Nerolia Vetiver, like I do, this is a must-have.

I love Neroli scents. That's why I had to test this one. And what can I say, it was love at first sniff. Neroli is mostly associated with the classic 4711, and maybe that's also the reason why one feels warm in the heart when perceiving these scent nuances. Because almost all grandmas used to wear 4711.

This is like a stripped down, cleaner version of Fleur de Shanghai. It has less of the orange in the opening. But still with the Bergamot sparkle. I love the more prominent Jasmine in this. But the basil like Clove note pokes through a little too much for my liking. Also has less of that Myrrh smokiness. Making it a more clean formulation. Shanghai is better though IMO as it's brighter, more tart and complex with the Orange, Patchouli and Myrrh. This leans more towards Bergamot, Jasmine and Clove.

This is a really good leather scent. Saffron and some warm spice. Thought this had vanilla until i read the notes but I guess not. Kinda reminds me of other warm spice scents like Spicebomb and Bottled boss absolu with the patchoulli This is a good gift if you’re thinking about getting your husband or an older guy a smooth fragrance and you know he likes leather

I would like to start by saying that I am quite picky and critical when it comes to leather fragrances, as they are often too opulent and mainstream or too strong. This fragrance opens very quickly with a beautiful warmth and a lot of presence. The notes are all distinct and bring something very reassuring and, above all, self-confidence. It is a superb companion for night work, such as in clubs or bars. It has good staying power and longevity and projects well (6-8 hours). For the price, it is an absolute must-have!

I like it very much. Extremely pleasant and easy to wear. Leather here doesn't have that harsh impact on the nose. However, longevity is weak and projection is even weaker, so while the scent is well thought, the performances of the fragrance are bad quality. 100% wearable, but not if you're going out.

I'm not really a fan of leather scents, but this one is quite good. From the start, it’s very spicy and leathery, BUT the leather is lighter and more pleasant than other leather fragrances I've tried. Now the pepper - it does give a harshness to the fragrance. I think that’s why I don't feel "sexy" wearing it, more just classy and put-together. For dates there's probably better options. But this is a good office scent. I think it’s also going to shine in winter. At an online discount retailer, you can get this guy for around $55, so this is still a steal for such a modern and classy cologne. And regardless of the harsh quality, I think this is a good option when you're in the mood for leather. Just use a few less sprays than you might otherwise and that should take the edge off. And in the depths of winter, I can see the pepper quality in its element. Got a full bottle.

For anyone who isn't necessarily a fan of leather scents like I am, this fragrance is still worth a try. A great opening: sweet, fresh, and spicy, with a hint of rum and conjac, but only subtle leather. As the freshness and fruitiness fade a bit, wood and earth join in. A very masculine yet sweet, rounded leather scent that is noticeable but not overpowering. It has this addictive quality and is versatile. It has a sensual, seductive note, making it suitable for dates. Perfect for the masculine gentleman. It has made its way into my current top 3 fragrances and is my favorite in this category. It somewhat resembles Armani SWY, but is more masculine and a bit darker, yet still fresh and sweet. It's one of those scents where I wish it would stay as it is in the first hour. This phase is not spectacular or extravagant for me, but still world-class. After that, it becomes leathery, woody, and smoky, but remains pleasant. It reminds me of Harley Davidson and a pub, but in a positive way, without becoming too dirty and dark. You definitely have to be a certain type for this. Not a scent for everyone, but for a leather fragrance, it leans more towards mainstream, at least in the first 90 minutes. And when you look at the list of perfumes that Antoine Maisondieu has already released, you know that an absolute professional was at work, who knows exactly what it takes to create a hit. For me, already a classic.

The beginning is spicy, with a hint of leather. After 6-7 minutes, only the leather remains as the main note. The leather has a slight edge for the next 20 minutes, then it fades on the skin. In the end, an earthy note comes through. The aroma, if it had a greater intensity, would receive better approval. I give it 6 points, the bottle is beautiful.

VII. Poem from the Rose Cycle The clear fresh rose blossom gently caresses my closed eye lightly -, as if it were laying a thousand cool lids, one on top of the other, over my hot lid. And a thousand slumbers it then spreads over my deception, beneath which I wander in the scent of the labyrinth. Rainer Maria Rilke (1875-1926) For the sake of completeness: I smell a small, fresh garden rose. Everything else has been filtered out by my nose.

The critics on the internet were right: this version of the spring fragrances from YSL's Paris is truly the most beautiful. The rose is present from the very beginning, and very present it is. Violet and orange blossom are at best supporting characters, allowed to hold her train but otherwise required to stay in the background. Lily of the valley and apricot in the heart note fare similarly, but with lilac, the rose forms a wonderful alliance. The intensity of the lilac, influenced by the enchanted, light pink rose. She wears the lilac like a chinchilla collar around her neck, and one is almost inclined to bow before her. She is truly a beauty, an unreal, fairy-tale, enchanted beauty. Even as the lilac then gives up and turns from chinchilla into rabbit, the rose is still present and seems to proudly say, look here, it’s me. Sandalwood and musk at best allow her to prepare a soft, comfortable resting place, but nothing more. I am truly surprised by this fragrance. The rose is - from the top to the heart to the base note - the mistress of the proceedings. A beautiful, enchanted fairy-tale rose, almost too beautiful to be true. And that is the point: the longevity is also not in line with the price and value of this fragrance, although the sillage is noticeably better than that of Paris Roses des Bois. The entire series of these Paris spring fragrances from YSL is a lovely and well-executed idea, even if it struggles with longevity. It is a joy to collect the scents from this series, especially since they are only available for a limited time.

This starts out green, citrusy and floral with a bit of a spicy/peppery kick. Ferragamo pour Femme brings to mind a grassy wildflower meadow on a cloudless spring day. The top is a lovely blend of flowers, citruses and green grass. This scent has such a fresh, bright, yet soft and classicly romantic feel to it. No specifc flower stands out to me above the rest, but I probably detect the rose and lily of the valley the most. The florals here are very fresh, clear and vibrant, not jarring or sharp at all. If anyone remembers the sadly discontinued Clarins Elysium, this reminds me a lot of that scent. I guess that this is technically a fruity floral, but not in the current trendy, candy-sweet way at all. It is more sophisticated than that, but still young at heart. The drydown reveals some similarities to the drydown of Versace Versense, with it's transparent musk and hint of woods, but here it is of a more green floral character here than a citrus one. At this point, Ferragamo pour Femme starts to move away from the floral/fruity-floral category and a bit more into floral woody musk territory, all the while retaining it's fresh green vibrancy. I picked this up blind from TJMaxx for $19.99 and am so glad I did. I can't wait to wear this come spring.

Upon initial application of FERRAGAMO I was having a serious déjà senti experience. Then suddenly I remembered what this reminds me of: PLEASURES by Estee Lauder. I have not worn PLEASURES in a long time, though at one point I was trying to convince myself that I liked it and managed to get through nearly half a bottle. I cannot say that they smell the same, but they make me feel the same, if that makes any sense. FERRAGAMO, too, has a strong peony presence, which apparently does not sit well with me--at least in what appear to be certain synthetic renditions. This edp seems rather clean, just as PLEASURES does in some ways, but for some reason it does not agree with my body's chemistry. Rather than soapy or green, I find these fragrances to be slightly metallic. Although they are not repugnant or emetic, I don't find them particularly agreeable or enticing either. In general, I find the fragrances of this house somewhat synthetic, so they are always touch and go with me. On good days, they work. On bad days, they don't. That said, FERRAGAMO would appeal, I think, to anyone who loves PLEASURES. Best suited for summertime, I think.

I really do enjoy wearing Salvatore Ferragamo. It's certainly a different type of fragrance, not your typical fruity scent. It is much more complex than most other perfumes I've tried. Firstly, I will review this fragrance by describing how it smells on paper and on my skin, because they both differ considerably. On paper Salvatore Ferragamo begins as a soft, almost soapy and refreshing blend of grapefruit, green notes, black currant and bergamot. However on my skin the spices are much more prominent and I can clearly smell the pepper, coconut and anise. The middle notes are so beautiful, flowery and sweet on both skin and paper. The rose note is delicate and fresh, while the spices mantain that unique balance in the opening. At this point I much prefer the fragrance when worn on the skin because it has much more 'oomph' and character than on paper. There is no doubt in my mind that this is a very classy scent, which is a truly hard to find characteristic in most fruity fragrances these days. Salvatore Ferragamo is sure to impress, captivate and be complimented this Summer, so I urge anyone to try this amazing scent.

This is a lightly sweet floral-aromatic musk, situated in the 90s abstract clean scents world. It reminds me of CK One Eau de Toilette and Cabotine Eau de Toilette . Not in all of the notes but in the abstraction. Complex and yet light white musk like in CK One, abstract florals like in Cabotine. This is what I get. It opens powdery-fresh, with a tiny hint of citrus, and a twist of anise (milder than the anise in Lolita Lempicka (2012) Eau de Parfum . There is an aromatic greenness that follows after. A barely sweet, watery floral heart. A scratchy sensation in the nose, something like black pepper or carnation. A soapiness. And a lightly sweetening clean white musk that makes me think ambrette. At the base, light scratchiness. Maybe it's the woods. It reminds me of the anchoring woods in Dune Eau de Toilette but not strong at all. Not a bad scent. It's interesting to think of this scent profile as dated, since it smells so ageless, but people are wearing stronger scents these days. Also, in the thirty-plus years since clean scents became popular in the 90s, we've had some different trends in their development. Carnation is not present in clean scents that are being made today. Now it's more iris and pink pepper as in You Eau de Parfum , or just straight up Cetalox/Ambrox and some additives, like in Not a Perfume Eau de Parfum . I also notice that accords lists tend to be shorter these days, even compared to the 90s clean scents. Maybe a marketing decision, to simplify what companies are telling consumers to smell for? Or maybe they're not trying to evoke so many accords. I don't know. At the same time, though, some things have stayed the same. Musk and citrus of all kinds have stayed a staple of clean scents.

Emozione by Salvatore Ferragamo recently pleased me and has already made itself comfortable in my wardrobe. So I browsed through the descriptions of other Ferragamo fragrances. And I took the plunge, bought Pour Femme, blind…. A fresh opening, bergamot is clearly noticeable, yet the citrus notes remain rather elegantly restrained; Pour Femme does not turn sour, as is the case with some fragrances containing bergamot, grapefruit, and neroli. Gradually, Pour Femme becomes spicier and greener, the blackcurrant is unfortunately only faintly present, I wish it could be a bit more prominent. I do not notice coconut, which is better for me. Pepper gives Pour Femme a pleasant sharpness that tingles in the nose. After a while, a bouquet of flowers blooms, dominated by delicate lily of the valley - without ringing too strongly, but the clove also chimes softly in between with spicy tones. Pour Femme ends in a woody base with a lot of musk, finally a base without the sweetness of tonka, vanilla, etc. Pour Femme remains consistently fresh and herbaceous, the sillage is in the medium range, and the longevity is surprisingly good at 6 hours on my skin. For me, this fragrance leans towards a green floral chypre with fruity elements, even though it does not contain oakmoss. Those who enjoy herbaceous scents and love fresh spice will be well served with this fragrance. Even the "clean and fresh" faction could feel addressed, because with this fragrance, one feels just like in the advertisement "when it should be clean and well-groomed." Pour Femme is a classic all-rounder, and it will surely develop even better in warm temperatures. I can't say anything negative, just one thing, it's a pity I didn't discover it earlier.

...as I read from the longevity and sillage evaluation. At least for me, it shows quite a bit of endurance and projection. Not a booming "perfume bomb," but rather subtly present and even still well perceivable by me after a longer stay on the skin. This "Ferragamo" starts fresh-citrusy and very green-bitter with a "fruity touch.

Incredible that no one has commented on this almost classic yet 0_o The EDT is pleasantly light overall - but has almost no projection and sillage; the EDP is more interesting in terms of composition, but this one also had too short a lifespan for me. So I took the chance when I finally saw it as a pure perfume.

...and with that, the most important thing has basically been said! This fragrance wonderfully reflects Italian grandeur and uncomplicated chic; Ferragamo not only creates brilliant fashion, he also knows how to enchant the nose....

Pretty and delicate, inoffensive yet unoriginal. I'm a little disappointed in Young Sexy Lovely. Yves Saint Laurent usually comes up with interesting and in some ways, unique fragrances. However, in this case, Yves Saint Laurent played it safe. It is neither too fruity nor too flowery, it's a nice balance between the two. Young Sexy Lovely is yes, young and lovely, but definitely not sexy. Flirtatious maybe would have been a better choice. The scent from the opening to the drydown is very soft and intimate. Pear, peach, cherry blossom, magnolia and musk are the most dominant notes to my nose when I smell this fragrance. In my opinion, this would appeal to a relatively young audience, age 13-20. It's nice in a casual, everyday use, inoffensive sense.

When a well-meaning shop-assistant tried to point out the assets of this fruity little number to me, I burst out into laughter. I'm neither young, nor sexy, and honestly, I don't want to be "lovely" either (and of course I am not, otherwise I would not rant against this stuff, would I?). "Young,Sexy,Lovely" is a very common type of fruity-floral perfume, and I would be hard pressed, if I had to distinguish it from all his brothers and sisters on the playground. Why does YOUNG and SEXY nearly "automatically" involve a fruity-floral note? Does the perfumer really think that cherry blossom, nashi, black-currant and mango are "sexy"? Yves Saint Laurent used to do unforgettable perfumes like "Y", "Opium" or the fantastic "Rive Gauche". But this "Young and Sexy thing" simply follows a popular trend in perfumery, thus failing to set any. Dismal.

Yves Saint Laurent is the House behind my all time love, Rive Gauche. If I were to pick one scent to bring with me to a desert island, it would be RG. YSL is also the House behind Opium, Champagne, Parisienne à l’Extrême, Manifesto d’Elixir, Paris… extremely wonderful and skillfully composed perfumes. Every one of them would make anyone famous. From the male range I can mention Kouros as a favourite but Y and Jazz are also milestones for the House (and for me). My enthusiasm for YSL cannot be underestimated. I am a fan. All of these masterpieces… And then there is Young Sexy Lovely… but not in my world. No. 191/365

YOUNG A fruity start with currants and mandarins. I don't perceive any pears. A young, fresh scent! SEXY Cherry blossom and magnolia form a pretty heart. A young girl might feel sexy with this. For me, it feels sweet. LOVELY The base is also very nice, harmless musk with a hint of wood and amber. And there’s a surprise too! Suddenly, the pear appears. The longevity is not famous at 4 hours but okay. I see this scent on a young girl who is using a fragrance for the first time that doesn't fall into the drugstore category.

a bright, clear, light perfume with many fruits. Attention: again something for pear lovers the natural sweetness of the ripe pear is dominant here, complemented by cedar (but I smell it more like birch...) and surrounded by flowers that cannot be distinguished individually.

Attimo pour Homme is a fantastic blend of both fresh and spicy accords. I wish I could remember who recommended this fragrance to me, because I am very grateful to them for having made this perfume known to me. Attimo pour Homme opens with lots of pepper and cardamom, freshened up with a zesty burst of mandarin orange. At this point, the fragrance is sharp and masculine. The scent also projects quite strongly. I had hoped that Attimo pour Homme would be the perfect scent for my man, but in some ways it's a bit too serious and bold for his tastes. However, it's very much to my tastes. I love its 'in-your-face' nature. Due to its rather strong sillage, I would apply Attimo pour Homme with a light hand, so as not to offend. The heart becomes quite fiery with the introduction of paprika and saffron. It's enough to set your nasal cavity on fire. But just like hot and spicy food, you'll either love it or hate it. Surprisingly Attimo pour Homme remains fresh throughout its development, but never smells clean. Just spicy, peppery and tart. I must add that the longevity is superb, lasting almost a whole 12 hour day. Some people mention a sweet accord in Attimo pour Homme, and while I do smell it myself, it's only very slight. I wouldn't call this a sweet masculine at all. Spicy sums it up perfectly.

I really have nothing to criticize about this scent. It's a crowd-pleaser that doesn’t clash, more suited for the warm days of the year. However, I had something different in mind based on the listed ingredients. Cardamom and black pepper as the main scent contributors? Where exactly? Okay, cardamom can have a slightly sour note, but I actually smell a concentrated burst of citrus freshness. I already have enough perfumes of this kind. I would also gladly keep Attimo, but others of similar quality came before it. In terms of its basic tendency, it's really not far from Versace pour Homme, Bleu de Chanel, or Cerruti 1881 Acqua Forte... I just wonder where this citrus freshness comes from! The mandarin is usually found in sweeter refreshers, and otherwise, I see nothing that points in this direction. Which I find a pity, because isn’t a scent defined by its ingredients?! On the other hand, I've often experienced this: Something catches my attention while reading, "Yeah, mint," "Wow, water lily," "Strong, vetiver," "Cool, incense" ... and in the end, it was all nothing! ;-) Not that we misunderstand each other. I like the scent, as I said, even though the H&S are rather mediocre, as is the case with all three Ferragamos I’ve tested so far. I believe this is a brand you can't go wrong with, but it also doesn’t have a real standout in its lineup for me. Now let's hope my nose isn't broken! ;-) Just think "citrusy-fresh" instead of "spicy-woody" and you'll be on a good level!

A quite nice fragrance, somewhat in the style of "Bleu de Chanel," a bit lighter. Opening: a mix of fresh and slightly spicy notes, light fresh mandarin, a hint of marjoram, and subtle pepper. The sillage is rather moderate, little room presence, almost shallow. The heart is oriental in a homeopathic measure, a bit of incense and sage, all very subtle. In the base, a balsam-tinged musk. Overall, quite pleasant. Friendly yes, but all in all uninteresting. Little profile.

This is called Tropical Wood, but it is only sweet Oud—masculine on me. To my husband it’s sweet floral on him. Neither works—wish it reversed! The longevity is good, so is sillage. I smell slight pineapple. Nothing stands out to us.

My nose, curious and appreciating Montale as a brand for its long-lasting and niche fragrances, inhaled a sample of Tropical Wood deeply and repeatedly. It vaguely reminds me of a scent I had many years ago, I think it was called Ypno. So, TW's expression is already familiar to me from the past. T W smells sweet, warm, fruity on me, and the ingredients come together to create a scent expression. It lasts on me for about 8 hours. I do not perceive leather or rose. It smells like pulp of tropical fruits with musk and vanilla, but all blended together. The violet adds a slight spiciness, which, however, gets lost in the sweetness. The feeling is that too much is flooding my nose at once. Sorry, I don't want to speak poorly of the fragrance, but it feels somewhat chaotic to me and thus overwhelmed by the ingredients. What is supposed to be the Wood in this fragrance? It does not reveal itself to my nose. Test it for yourself; it is no longer an enhancement for my collection.

I would like to skip a lengthy introduction to Montale Tropical Wood and get straight to the fragrance description. Packed in a typical Montale bottle, one expects a fruity, summery scent with woody undertones in this blue-gold flacon. Montale is not among the most expensive niche brands (115€ for 100ml, 65€ for 50ml for Tropical Wood). The fragrance pyramid piqued my curiosity, so I got a sample. The opening is very fruity with immediate spicy-woody undertones reminiscent of oud. The combination gives off a truly tropical, summery, and cheerful vibe, which unfortunately fades disappointingly after a short time. Whether the fruit in the opening is supposed to smell like passion fruit is debatable, as I have no comparisons. I can't really perceive pineapple. In the following minutes, Tropical Wood becomes more floral, subtly rosy, and sweeter. As the oud nuances slowly disappear, my nose detects unpleasant secondary scents that remind me of rubber. Really unpleasant and should not be in this fragrance. After about 2.5 hours, the woody oud tones have completely vanished. In the base, sweet vanilla pushes more to the forefront and merges with the fully synthetic fruit mix, whose individual components are indistinguishable. The further development of the scent remains linear, sweet, and fruity. For my taste, the fragrance leans more towards a feminine direction. The idea behind the scent, to combine tropical fruits with tropical woods from the agarwood tree (which primarily grows in Southeast Asia), from which oud is derived, is fundamentally interesting. In fact, Montale has succeeded well with the tropical opening. However, the woody note simply falls short for me; I would have preferred woody base notes instead of vanilla. This could have potentially countered the synthetic fruit better. Montale has by no means missed the theme, but the "Wood" has been neglected. The longevity of TW is good at around 8 hours, with sillage on my skin being moderate. Nevertheless, I will not be purchasing a bottle; I had something better in mind, and in the end, it feels too feminine for me. It seems to me that the perfumer did not take the time to perfect this fragrance and released it prematurely.

... yes, exactly this combination I never expected to wear in summer. However, Tropical Wood makes it possible, especially by adding rose and violet. The latter clearly dominates the entire fragrance for me. The passion fruit remains surprisingly understated - just by studying the fragrance pyramid, I would have expected more. But this does not make the scent any worse; I just imagined it differently! In the first 5-10 minutes, the violet-rose combination overwhelms me with a very authentically soapy smell. It feels like you have just washed your hands with a floral soap. After these 10 minutes, the fragrance goes through a brief phase where it smells completely clean like freshly washed laundry. After that, the fragrance really unfolds. The floral notes slightly recede, and leather, oud, and a bit of passion fruit come into play. Nevertheless, the clean rose-violet combination remains dominant, while the other notes merely resonate in the background. As leather and oud stay subtly in the background, giving the fragrance only a woody, leathery, oriental touch, the character of the scent remains floral-clean. I find it much more floral, but also actually fresher than expected. The performance of the fragrance is impressive. It lasts several days on clothing, and on the skin, you can easily get up to 15 hours of full intensity. The sillage is never overwhelming, so you shouldn't annoy anyone. In my opinion, the character of the fragrance doesn't allow for that at all. I am really very positively surprised by this fragrance and feel that it runs a bit under the radar among the Montale scents.

Can leather, rose, and oud work in summer? Yes, if you also add a good dose of musk, violet, and a mix of various fruits. I do love Arabians Tonka, but it is too "heavy" a scent for spring/summer. Tropical Wood has a similar base structure, but it refreshes with slightly floral notes and the mix of fruits, which I can't quite define, but passion fruit and pineapple could be close. I would rate the longevity and sillage as slightly weaker than Arabians Tonka, but still very good - even after several hours. I was pleasantly surprised by this Montale scent in a tropical way, and it definitely deserves to stay in my collection.

This fragrance opens with an light almond accord. This is not Louve's bitter almond (liqueur), it is sweet and milky with only a touch of the bitter almond's typical sharpness (at the base) to keep the accord interesting. This is needed, because the scent smells so clean and musky like it was a body lotion. As the notes bloom on my skin, the almond accord develops into a sugared milk accord with a dash of vanilla. Pleasant and much easier to wear than the piercing Louve, this Montale it will be definitely a disappointment to true almond lovers. Despite its lightness, this scent has great sillage and tenacity.

Not all almond perfumes smell like Dior HYPNOTIC POISON, and Montale AMANDES ORIENTALES is a case in point. Bitter almonds and musk are really the keys to this utterly addictive perfume. It opens like an unsweetened loukhoum--as oxymoronic as that may sound--with the same alkaline powder quality but instead of sugar there is an almost greenish aura surrounding the almonds. In some ways, it's like the outer dark coating of roasted almonds--not the inside yellowish fatty part, but the edges of the almonds, as though they have been peeled and only the shavings appear here. The musk is very strong and seductive indeed, and eventually the composition dries down to become more sweet and less bitter, soft and smooth. It's like starting off an evening in a heated argument over some controversial political topic and then waking up the next morning in bed under soft down comforters.

I had been warned. I had read about horse stables and the remnants of their inhabitants, about candied plastic almonds and noses turned up in some places. Statements that urged caution, careful handling of the residue in the sample vial, which wanted to be dabbed, not sprayed. One drop, at most two, strategically well distributed. Much more, I must confess, I would not have dared, not on that first day, for the first rendezvous. The first impression then on my skin: All clear. No great wild beast inflates my nostrils, no horse apple falls into my lap. And yet I know exactly what those meant who found the scent too almond-like, but too animalistic. "Amandes Orientales" places me in the old town of Granada, whose air is saturated with the scent of blooming jasmine - not the delicate light one that wouldn't harm a fly, but rather insistently indolic, almost fecal. This first encounter, now several years ago, with the extremely characteristic, highly memorable fragrance I found downright shocking and, yes: repulsive, because for a child of my time and culture, a smell that seems so little fresh and clean is first learned to be "yuck." Despite all olfactory experimental enthusiasm, not much has changed to this day; scents with clearly indolic components still have a hard time with me. Perceptibly indolic is already the opening of "Amandes Orientales," and not in small measure - that nonetheless no toilet paper-roll-hand-washing reflex is triggered is due to the remarkably soft-warm-ambered enveloping of the presumed jasmine, which takes the sharp edge off the indolic and bathes the scent from the very first moment in a resinous-balsamic light. Dry-spicy-warm it feels, and somehow cozy like - well, if you will: a horse stable, of course a clean one with fresh straw and a gentle horse. Outside the door, daffodils are apparently blooming, whose scent, although not listed, wafts into my nose again and again. In general, it seems to me, the pyramid keeps many secrets, for I would wager a lot that "Amandes Orientales" also contains Monsieur Montale's dearly beloved oud, which seems to be responsible for the subtly animalistic undertone that piques the interest of the man beside me, to which a certain erotic attraction cannot be denied. The horse stable, yes. All of this is caught and held after at most half an hour by a dark, more tropical than oriental vanilla, as I have encountered in "Noir Tropical" or "Eau des Missions" - attractively smoky-sweet, yet at no time sticky-cloying-bulky. Over the course of the first hours, all the indolic gradually retreats to the skin, ultimately fading completely in favor of a daffodil-vanilla I-stay-with-you note with distinct burnt-something hints, in which I would gladly find the namesake almond - but alas: It does not show itself. Not clearly and distinctly contourable. Sure, I can imagine it, can interpret it into the crunchy-sweet smoke - but I could do that with many others too. And I find that is not a disadvantage. "Amandes Orientales" seems to belong to those fragrances that unfold particularly individually from wearer to wearer and whose perception appears extremely dependent on the respective imprints and associations. Several test days yielded no significant changes regarding the development on my skin; only the daffodil seemed a bit pricklier, more rebellious, more dominant in wind and weather, on unprotected, cooled skin. Despite consistently maintained drop dosing, "Amandes Orientales" unfolds a well-perceptible, yet not intrusive aura that surrounded me until the shower the following morning.

Amandes Orientales is one of those fragrances that severely damage the heart by tearing a large hole in it. So caustic, so overwhelming is this Montale that one turns away from it in disgust. Naturally, holding one's nose. Yet the caustic nature of this scent burns itself deep into memory and heart. It may only heal slightly over time, but it will never be completely filled. It remains hollow and it pains every perfume lover's heart. If that is passion for a fragrance, then I might as well jump from a high tower. It's practically suicide - for the nose, for my feelings, and for my love of scents. Let's start at the beginning. I got to know this fragrance about two years ago. Even back then, it agitated my cells, in the most negative sense, and I partially suffered from aggression, as the scent overshadowed me so shrill. And today? I experience the worst excesses just by smelling it! So bad, you ask? Yes, because the scent drives me to the brink of madness, as it burns me so. It doesn't suit me, I don't suit it. Nothing fits here. Apologies to all you lovers, but this scent has me utterly horrified. A pale tone of gourmand is initially not bad - but then the almond club comes on quickly. It is a very cloying, heavy form of almond. Then a sugary glaze is drawn over it - stuffy air that presses against everything. Massive, damp sand that settles in my body with all its grains and simply crushes me from the inside. Vanilla pods that have been lying around for a long time seem half-heartedly added. Initially not so rich in their appearance, but then the vanilla becomes ever deeper. To top it all off, there’s a club full of animalic filth that joins in here, as if it were the immediate dot over the i on a fat cake devoured by depressed children. It fits in here not at all. This animalic quality with the hysterical sweetness that spreads over everything and everyone. And it becomes a heavy burden that I can no longer (bear) carry. Everything feels totally overloaded and I had to wash the stuff off. It sticks like a paste, first feeling greasy, then extremely hard on the body. This fragrance tears a hole in my heart that will probably never close. Because now and then, one stumbles over things that one has long thrown overboard as completed. For me, a NO GO of fragrances and a horror candidate!

Will a Montale ever make it into my real or virtual shopping cart? I increasingly doubt it. Unfortunately, even the simplest and most melodious Montale creations turn out to be rather useless perfumes. One would think that with the three ingredients "roasted almonds," "vanilla," and "smoky notes," there isn't much that can go wrong. Most fragrance houses or perfumers would likely conjure up something solid here. However, Montale prefers to take the more complicated route. At least in terms of the result, because with the formulation, I fear it leans more towards the cheap to qualitatively subpar side. The culprit is a rather artificial almond note, which, as can already be read in some comments, seems to have come into too intense contact with plastic wrap. Even the vanilla smells overall too sweet and more like Dr. Oetker pudding powder. This is just as confusing as the slightly animalic barn-like note in this almost gourmand environment. Such things can easily spoil one's appetite or ruin the good feeling while wearing it. Only much later, when the oriental almonds, which unfortunately lose all their exoticism, have calmed down a bit in the nose, does the true soul of the EdP come to light. Then, marzipan-like almonds and vanilla blend with a truly delicate smoky character into a relatively pleasant scent that one no longer expects, but better late than never to be served. This saves AO from a total crash, but it certainly doesn't lead to a recommendation.

I have my difficulties with oriental fragrances; the only one from this direction that I can absolutely identify with is Shalimar. So I was rather skeptical when I tested Amandes Orientales. However, to my surprise, it develops on my skin in an absolutely pleasant way, unsweetened, smoky, and soft.

That the aforementioned fragrance notes develop in this direction... who would have thought. Namely horse manure. I sprayed the scent on my wrist before going to bed to test it a bit more. Yes yuck, my whole bed smelled like horse-yuck! I don't know what kind of almonds they used.

I wrote this post some time ago on Beautyjunkies. I'm copying it here: I tested this fragrance this evening. Oh dear, all I can say is. It actually smells (forgive my choice of words!) like a full diaper! I think I need to learn to better decipher the descriptions at Wuchsa.

I was really looking forward to the sample, the description with the smoky almonds sounded just too interesting. And then this. I don't even want to write it, but I can't get around it... it smelled on me like, um... "stool"... And quite clearly, it's unbearable. Neonatura describes the (initial) note as unpleasant and that the scent has a morbid touch. Still, she likes it.

The sample of Amandes Orientales has been sitting untouched with me for almost 2 weeks now, which is rather unusual for me. You might know the feeling: You receive a bunch of new samples and can't decide which scent to test first. So every little spot on your arm gets dabbed and sprayed... With AO, it was different.

Lovely fresh sparkely young rose fragrance. this isent as sharp as the other Paris . this is a bit more fruity and works more around the softer notes . Rose and violets gives a fresh and clean feal. whit musk lifing it up lillyoffthe valley just right to give that crisp fealing off spring. Truly a beautiful perfume. Uplifting and charming. You can tell its in the same range as the other Paris. but much more tolerable do to lessno hyasinth. This would be a charming roes perfume to a joyfull and happy bride IMO

Basically, I could almost write the same thing as I did for Paris Eau de Printemps 2009. But just almost. Sure, it’s in the same direction, it’s a rose scent, and it’s one of the spring versions of YSL's Paris. But to limit this fragrance to these few lines would be doing it a disservice. Paris Roses des Bois is also not for rose scent haters. In contrast to Printemps 2009, it is more subdued, warmer, and woodier. The roses here are wild roses that grow everywhere, especially at the edges of forests. These roses have a very special and natural scent. It is neither the slightly musty scent of white roses, nor the opulent scent of red roses, or the juicy, fruity scent of yellow and orange roses. It is a completely natural bright and fresh note that wild roses exude, and you can almost sense the scent of the rose hips they will later become. Roses des Bois has this scent. I can’t perceive any violets or lily of the valley, just a gentle touch of orange blossoms, which rather highlight the rose scent. Musk and sandalwood make this fragrance warm and cozy, but also less fresh than Eau de Printemps 2009. What I regret very much is the weak sillage and the poor longevity. Nevertheless, I give it 80% because it is really beautiful, even if only for a very short time.

Today I was looking for a fresh scent that shouldn't be citrusy sour. In the perfume shop, a colorful little box caught my eye, adorned with maritime symbols. And the title Oceani di Seta also evokes oceanic feelings. The opening is fresh and clear, with a subtle non-sour citrus note. The main role is played by the aquatic element, which is infused with a hint of sea salt. The magnolia and heliotrope float lightly above, also contributing to the refreshing effect. A transparent yet long-lasting fragrance that fits well in summer. I can easily imagine it on both ladies and gentlemen. My Bonnie is over the Ocean... comes to my mind.

I made a blind buy with this fragrance.....and I was disappointed. When I sprayed it on, I was overwhelmed by a feminine magnolia. I can't find anything, absolutely nothing, that even remotely reminds me of a unisex scent. The magnolia is just too overpowering. I don't perceive the salty notes at all. Moreover, the fragrance remains linear from start to finish and doesn't change. I find this rather boring and after about 10 minutes, it becomes just annoying. Additionally, it smells very synthetic and rather cheap. Although the fragrance is not exactly inexpensive. 80.- for 50ml is rather high for this little scent, which first overwhelms you and is already gone after 2 hours. Definitely not a blind buy. Please test it first.

Starts very fresh and citrusy. Sicilian lemon and neroli are thus the strongest that jump to my nose. Doesn't take long before I do get a bubblegum sort of accord (made me think of Hubba Bubba bubble tape). It doesn't last as long as I thought it would, given the name. Florals are next with some jammy roses and creamy / powdery white florals. There's a hint of spicy cinnamon somewhere in here which adds much needed complexity to this scent. It becomes very feminine right about here. Drydown gets weirdly sweet and synthetic with a dissonant spiciness. Didn't get any toffee down here. It's nice but, not really my thing. Very feminine (a bit too pink for my taste) with a synthetic streak in the drydown. I do have to say the bubblegum accord in the top notes was very realistic and nice to smell. The rest is just okay, not great enough to add a full bottle.

I could recently test Montale's Bubblegum Forever. It reminds me of two different scents, the first one which could not been better described with the title itself, is obviously Bubblegum. A very sweet note, but not sticky in any sense. Furthermore the scent of Bubblegum is not the only thing which caught my attention, the Bubblegum is quickly accompanied by a nice floral note (some kind of rose). I did not thaught, that a combination of those two scents could ever be forming such a good combination, but the sweetness of them both connect very good. The longevity of this perfume is good as in all of Montale's fragrances. I have not tested many women fragrances in my life, but if i was to judge I really thing it is a excellent fragrance for women, you can basically wear it on a fancy night out or just a nice warm day, if you feel fancy enough yourself.

A scent that immediately stands out - but in an unusual way.. Right from the first spray, it’s clear: This is not a classic rose composition meeting fresh citrus notes, but rather a blend that reminds one of chewing gum from childhood. Sweet, sticky, pink - like a freshly opened pack of bubblegum, with a splash of lemon soda thrown in. This interplay feels playful, but also a bit artificial. The first seconds are lively and zesty: a fresh citrus note, slightly sharp, almost fizzy, like the moment you drop a fizz tablet into water. Then a sweet, slightly floral cloud settles over it - somewhere between rose, cotton candy, and chewing gum aroma. The fragrance has that typical, slightly synthetic sweetness known from chewing gums or "children's perfumes" - quickly becoming too much for many noses. After a while, the combination feels flatter, almost soapy. The freshness remains, but the balance between lemon and rose tips: What initially seemed playful and "cheeky" suddenly takes on a hint of bathroom cleaner or room fragrance - clean, yes, but also somewhat sterile. It’s this ambivalence between “cheerfully fresh” and “too artificial” that makes the scent hard to pin down.

Unfortunately, a blind buy that tempted me because of the reviews.. I find no gum at all and only sweetness hits you. I imagined it would be minty-sweet with that typical bubblegum flavor. I smell none of that and was very disappointed. It is not a headache-inducing scent, the Montales never are, but for me it is one of the low performers in terms of fragrance direction. Longevity and sillage are (unfortunately for me) great. It could use a bit more lightness and zest.

Unfortunately, I have to admit that I really did not like the Ferragamo Bright Leather at all. At times, a certain sweaty "muff" drove my colleagues away... The longevity on my skin is only 5 to 6 hours, which is quite limited, and the sillage is therefore rather restrained. Once again, this is a fragrance where I can't boast about a top, heart, or base note. The scent starts off refreshing, citrus-fruity, herbal, woody, and greenish, but unfortunately, the whole experience quickly becomes rather musty. I recognize aromas of violet leaves, grapefruit, bergamot, fig leaves, lemon peels, mandarin peels, rosemary, basil, musk, cedarwood, and patchouli. I completely miss the leather - sorry! In the end, I was quite disappointed with the "Ferragamo Bright Leather | Salvatore Ferragamo." What a shame! Nevertheless, I thank Kamyar for the manufacturer sample.

Unlike most leather fragrances, this one lacks the typical animalistic nuance that also brings a certain "heaviness." Bright Leather is a bit fresher, which makes it significantly lighter and more wearable. The bright leather is complemented by citrus fruits, and a slight freshness is also noticeable. In the drydown, you find patchouli and cedarwood, which makes it a bit woodier once the top notes have faded. For everyday wear and the office, it is a good option during the warmer seasons. H/S is admittedly not the best part of it.

and was not disappointed one bit. My very first niche fragrance was Roses Musk and it became true love. For months, I tried some other Montale scents and learned to like or dislike them. And then curiosity arose, can Roses Musk be even better??? Yep, it can. The Intense Roses Musk is a bit deeper, just slightly sweeter but not over the top. The crucial difference to RM is, in my opinion, a significantly better sillage. Really amazing! And yet, people around me don’t drop dead and no one rushes to open the windows for fresh air. The dosage is absolutely crucial: I’m wearing just a single spray since this morning and I can still perceive a delicious rose in the soft, cozy musk! The RM is already much closer to the skin and more subtle after so many hours than the IRM. Anyone who knows and likes Roses Musk should definitely give this a try. A strong recommendation! A mega fragrance and price-performance ratio with the amazing H+S simply top.

I tried Intense Roses Musk to test another rose fragrance. So far, Weleda Jardin de Vie is in my collection, and it serves as a perfect comparison with Montale. These are two different interpretations of rose. While Weleda focuses entirely on naturalness, Montale prefers to go to the store for highbred noble roses. But that’s not necessarily a bad thing! With Weleda's scent, you fall into the wild rose that is in full bloom. The bees are buzzing, and you could almost think that honey is already dripping down. My fingernails are black from gardening, I’m sweaty and exhausted, and soon I’ll treat myself to a cup of tea. Huh? Didn’t it just smell like roses? Hmm, gone again. With Montale, the blend of jasmine and clean musk creates a different mental imagery. I’m wearing an elegant evening gown, and since I don’t have a date, I buy myself a bouquet of roses. Not cheap gas station roses, but a bouquet where each flower costs at least six euros. They are full, dark red noble roses. Interspersed in the bouquet are small jasmine flowers, and it’s wrapped in crackling foil. At the Japanese restaurant, I order expensive delicacies and put on my high heels. Am I going out? I’m definitely ready. But to a luxury lounge. Montale Intense Roses Musk is a great, noble rose fragrance that brings the theme out of the garden and into the world of luxury. At least that’s how I perceive it. My mother loves it; she finds it much better than the Weleda scent and said, “This is almost greasy! Is there oil in it?” Hehe, yes, that’s called a 30 percent fragrance oil concentration - at least that’s what I read about Montale. For me, it’s not the best Montale, but a successful interpretation of rose that could perform a bit better for my taste, especially regarding sillage.

Intense Rose Musk is my third fragrance from Montale and has once again convinced me of the brand after my previous purchases! It smells very strongly of rose, although I find that you don't notice it at first; it develops into a very feminine, strong scent that is (typical of Montale) very long-lasting! I mainly smell the rose, but I also find it has fresh nuances, it smells very expensive, not cheap or overly sweet. Those who love rose fragrances that smell very natural and not too sweet will adore this one. I think it can be worn in any season and at any time of day.

A beautiful rose in musk. The fragrance contains floral aromas of roses and white flowers with expressive delicate musk notes and quite mild amber notes. I find it to be somewhat softer than the original. The rose in the original is rather fresh and cool, while here it is warm and sweet, even very sweet. I envision the image of a confident woman, a bit playful and loving. I think this is a successful creation by Montale.

With an Intense version, I imagined the scent to be significantly stronger than it actually is. The rose somehow only comes through faintly, and the fragrance is more reminiscent of a bouquet that doesn't particularly stand out. Therefore, the scent has not made it onto my wish list.

I had high expectations.. I hardly dare to say that I don't like it, because many people enjoy the scent. Unfortunately, it's just pure rose; no musk, amber, or jasmine came through. Very strong - strong headaches. Anyone who enjoys the scent of rose will like it, but for me, it was nothing.

Sometimes you don't find the fragrance - the fragrance finds you. That's exactly how it was with Intense Roses Musk and me. I was in the perfume store when a customer suddenly approached me: “You have to try this one, I love it!” Said and done - and what can I say? Thank you, unknown fragrance fairy, you have given me a new favorite.

This fragrance is designed as a lighter version of the classic "Paris." It has a bit more sparkle in the top notes. It is neither an independent creation nor surprising, rather a "Paris light." If you like the original type of the great Grosjman perfume, you can get a lot out of this one, especially in summer. YSL has released many of these variants in recent years. They differ only in bottle and packaging and are mostly marketed only in the UK and France, as the old Paris is no longer performing well here in Germany.

I am someone who does not understand the scents of Montale. More specifically, my expectations and reality do not align. This was also true for the perfume Velvet Fantasy. The fragrance notes of this perfume belong to the group of oriental floral scents. It is the scent of red fruits and berries, a bit of incense, and musk. The aroma is somewhat sharp, definitely not suitable for everyday wear. Making more than one spray does not make sense. An overdose can also cause headaches. The longevity is several days, and I often receive compliments. Nevertheless, I like the scent, even though it smells different to me than described.

What can I say? Once I smelled it, I fell in love immediately. Kirke by Tiziana Terenzi was the first niche fragrance I ever tested. What followed was a lasting enthusiasm for scents. The sweet, fruity notes of this perfume still impress me today. I wear it only rarely now, but I look forward to it even more each time I do. When the days get warmer again, I’m sure it will be unpacked more often. The feedback from those around me has been overwhelmingly positive; several times I was asked what I was wearing that smells so good. You get a very sweet and fruity monster here, where the pear and raspberry stand out absolutely for me. 3 sprays are absolutely sufficient, and you immediately fill the entire room. This fragrance brings good energy to the space. Compliments are not lacking; it’s usually just a simple, “you smell good,” which is more than enough to brighten your day. Longevity is amazing; 7 hours after spraying, it’s still clearly noticeable!!! If you love Erba Pura, you can only love this fragrance as well. Compared to Erba Pura, Kirke is a bit lighter on the nose and, in my opinion, even a tad better than Erba Pura, but everyone has to test it individually; it’s not a blind buy, but it’s definitely worth a try. Must-have, people.

An extraordinary, fruity gourmand that does not smell synthetic. When reading the notes, it says "fruity notes." For me, banana and citrus fruits come out on top. I don't smell rose, incense, or amber. The opening is a fruit explosion. The citrus fruits are not too dominant, not too sour or zesty. After that, the fragrance becomes sweeter, creamier, and reaches the most beautiful banana smoothie dry-down. Extraordinary, authentic, and cheerful. A more feminine variation of Erba Pura with a hint of banana.

I hope you forgive me the little wordplay regarding the name. But without a doubt, this fragrance is exceptionally cozy for a representative from Montale's Fruits Collection. I have used my sample several times now and today I took the final test. When I applied it at 9 AM, I could not have guessed that later in the day, at 9 PM, I would think: Wow, how present it still is. And it is! Even now, at midnight, I can perceive the remnants of it on my skin. In my opinion, Montale perfumes are quite one-dimensional, but strong. I have noticed this with many fragrances from Montale. They do not change so drastically that one would attribute a specific progression to them. What you smell in the top note remains until the base, or one could certainly also say that you start with 80% of the base. The opening here is already very nice. I smell lemon less here. There is also nothing citrusy to discern. A typically fresh opening like in other fragrances with orange (blossoms), neroli, or bergamot is therefore not present. Instead, the room fills with a mixture of red berries, vanilla, and coconut. But beware: subtle vanilla. Not a blatant hello-here-I-am-I-want-to-eat-you vanilla. And this impression lasts hour after hour after hour after hour ... Hours later, amber and musk join in. You can actually notice that, even without knowing the fragrance pyramid. The coconut note recedes into the background but remains present. The fragrance has a note that could be described as cotton or flax, which I have only known from Pure Virgin / Eve by TheDifferent Company. It indeed smells somewhat like fresh laundry. But stylish laundry. Perhaps that’s where the reference to velvet comes from. Or I imagine that in the past (and perhaps still today) the Hollister stores smelled like this (I haven't been in one for ages). One can only fantasize about that ;) But that should in no way devalue the fragrance. By the way, I search in vain for bananas here, but I agree with the synthetic aspect. The blend of Velvet Fantasy is nothing you would find anywhere else and therefore cannot be classified as natural. It is beautiful nonetheless. The longevity alone is insane. But what good is outstanding longevity if you don’t like the scent? I can definitely imagine how it will soon be the first Montale to join my collection.

What a perfect flanker this is. It is indeed a lighter version of classic Rive Gauche but in a smart, fulfilling, unpredictable and very compelling way. It's not simply a "washed-down" version of it, not a "sport" flanker, it hasn't "just more citrus" as it often happens with "light" flankers; instead, as other reviewers already noted, it is 95% Rive Gauche (this implying it bears the same DNA of an amazing contemporary barbershop masterpiece) with a subtle, yet amazingly recognizable and brilliant tweaking of a couple of key knobs - notably, anise and geranium for me. In fact, it smells at once a bit more "azure", crisp and slightly more sugary thanks to a little more anise, and at the same time, kind of subtly fresher in a floral, "watery" way, thanks (I guess) to some more geranium. Just think of the immensely beautiful "new wave of barbershop fougères" embodied by Rive Gauche pour Homme, with the abovementioned variations. The difference with Rive Gauche is quite subtle, but so cleverly made that it makes it absolutely not redundant to own both. Actually they smell much "complementary" for me - the Light flanker is slightly, elegantly fresher, more suitable for the day, also slightly less bold and thus something you can spray more liberally. While classic Rive Gauche is a bit more mature, more darker, somehow more formal too, and probably more powerful (although this Light version is definitely strong and long-lasting as well, don't worry about that). Again, not a massive difference, but not even that negligible. This is how flankers should smell for me - subtle, yet interesting and clever variations. Fantastic per se (it's Rive Gauche, after all) and a great addition if you already own Rive Gauche. 8,5/10

Even though my other hobby, the perfume obsession, has been somewhat overshadowed lately (I’m just saying Fantasy Film Fest in Cologne) and as a result, the quantity of comments has suffered, probably to the delight of some whom I’ve been annoying for years^^, I am of course still testing in the cinema. And I won’t let comparisons like the two now very rare YSL Rive Gauches (Light & Intense) slip by for too long. I am an absolute fan of the original, know the powdery-modern barbershop classic & Brut successor inside and out, wear it frequently (for my standards) and was very curious about what the two flankers have to offer. Both come from a time long before the current flanker craze and shortly after Tom Ford left YSL. Hence this continuation comment. I was definitely glad that I hadn’t applied the original in the morning as I had thought, since all three smell incredibly similar and only differ in nuances. So there is by no means as much of a difference as, for example, between M7 and M7 Fresh. Therefore, I only wore Light on the left and Intense on the right, which should actually differ the most from each other. But even here, even novices can recognize the RiveGauchePH DNA blindfolded. For me, this consists mainly of anise, lavender, powdery aftershave, musk, and a woody base. A scent for dreamers & businessmen in one. The similarities to the For Him line by Narciso Rodriguez never leave my mind when wearing both lines (especially the Musc edition). Both lines are absolutely recommended and milestones for me, not just in a suit. Rive Gauche Pour Homme Light starts, as the name suggests, lighter than all other Rive Gauches. Airy anise, almost a fresh, cool mint breeze is present. Anyone who could never imagine the Rive Gauche DNA in summer will be proven wrong here. Only a hint of the woods and patchouli remains; describing this version as a dilution of the original is certainly not exaggerated or offensive, perhaps even intended. However, in this regard, I believe they may have gone a bit overboard, which can be seen especially in the longevity and sillage (in the continuation under YSL RG PH Intense). One doesn’t necessarily have to make every classic summer-ready and force it. Luckily, there’s no Anteaus Fraiche or anything similar (or not anymore!) ... (Continuation under the Intense variant)

There was a time when some manufacturers took years to launch a new perfume. Today, money (unfortunately) flows mainly into marketing. And long before the "flanker" craze, there were already offshoots of established fragrances. However, these were not - as exaggerated as today - thrown onto the market. Today, I feel almost overwhelmed and somewhat burdened! Back then, one had the impression that a flanker version of a successful perfume not only delighted the loyal customers but also attracted new interested parties who weren't quite as fond of the main fragrance... Of course, the focus was also on making "quick" money back then, but one didn't feel that greed as strongly as today! Rive Gauche - the name of the left bank of the Seine, the artists' district, the cafés, and the young people. Place to be and the title of YSL's prêt-à-porter fashion line, which was founded in the mid-1960s. The eponymous women's fragrance in a metal bottle - an optical revolution and with a pronounced fragrance and care line, THE perfume par excellence! A must-have for many women! Accordingly, the idea of a men's counterpart was unthinkable, it was almost blasphemous! But decades passed, and with Tom Ford came change, a glimmer of hope, a look forward, and the forging of new paths. He completely revamped the dusty image, gave it a hefty dose of sex appeal, and adorned Opium and Rive Gauche Pour Femme with a new, lascivious campaign touch! Karen Elson did his best! After Nu (2001) and M7 (2002), Ford launched Rive Gauche Pour Homme in 2003, the third (new) perfume under his direction! It came to market alongside the reformulated women's version and was both a homage and tribute to the original from 1971, which his mother used and loved for years! After the men's counterpart withstood criticism and seemed to establish itself, the YSL executives (Tom Ford had long since left the company) pushed out a limited summer version in 2004, named "Rive Gauche Pour Homme Light." Admittedly, the name is a bit clumsy! This "light" version was also available in Germany, but I never spotted it in our rural areas - as is often the case! "Light" was also available as a women's version. However, both were not promoted nearly as heavily as their larger siblings! An advertising campaign showcased the two silver bottles, along with sunglasses and accessories on a pair of jeans. The message was clear: a lighter variant for leisure activities on warm/hot (holiday) days. As a reminder: With Kouros Cologne Sport, there was already a fresh offshoot created under Tom Ford's direction, which was an early harbinger of today's sport fragrances. To finally get to the point: RG PH Light starts with a bitter, spicy bergamot and is rounded off by a radiant mint as it progresses. This cheerful accord is accompanied by an ozonic freshness that only slightly misses the aquatic theme. In contrast, the opening of the original seems a bit dull and almost subdued. Light manages to bridge the gap to the (aldehyde) women's version with this shiny top note. Floral accents thanks to geranium. Gradually, the familiar RG PH notes set in. Star anise enchants with a sweet, ethereal flair. Lavender contributes the characteristic fougère spiciness! Patchouli and guaiac wood reveal balsamic warmth. Yet, despite all the parallels - everything feels a bit weak - "Light" indeed. For me, it's more "even lighter"! The sillage is far below that of the original - close to the body! I perceive RG PH Light only very faintly on myself. RG PH Light was very well made in terms of presentation and approach! However, it clearly fails in terms of longevity and performance. While the original can be consciously perceived for a solid 12 hours, the 2012 "La Collection" version also achieves a very good 10 hours! The "Light" version, on the other hand, falters miserably with just 4-5 hours! For many, including myself, RG PH Light is simply a "watered-down" version of the original, which cannot even come close to its big brother! An "Eau de Cologne / Eau d'été," which would sound more fitting in my eyes! For Rive Gauche PH lovers, it's not a must; for all those who find the original too heavy, it offers a transparent, perhaps more accessible option. My 10ml sample will last me a long time....or maybe not, depending on how you look at it! ;-)

I don’t know what’s wrong with me, but when I smell “fresh peony” or “fresh magnolia” scents on the atomiser, they smell kind of fishy to me. This one was no exception, and it was very offputting, so I hesitated to try it on skin. However, once I did, it exploded into a shockingly strong powdery floral musk. I can appreciate a floral musk, but it’s not something I usually feel like wearing, and if I AM going to wear one, it’s gotta be a Serge Lutens. The base notes of Emozione Dolce Fiore - which is basically the entire fragrance for me - give me a beachy lotion feeling that's almost identical to Datura noir Eau de Parfum . I even feel like this shares a bit of the rubbery latex accord from Datura Noir, but that might just be by association. The white musk completely overwhelms everything else on my skin; I get no citrus or peach or whatsoever, and no suede either, which is disappointing because those notes would make this scent a whole lot more interesting. The only other thing I detect here besides the incredibly loud musk is a bit of fresh floral (mostly peony I think) which wafts around for the first hour or so before evaporating. All of that probably doesn’t sound very complimentary, but I actually found myself rather enjoying this, purely because I love Datura Noir and this reminded me of it. However, is it something I’d wear? No, I rarely feel like wearing this kind of scent and when I do, I’m going to just wear Datura Noir or another Serge favorite. Also, I don't really see the point in wearing something I can't appreciate fully because my skin chemistry doesn’t bring out all the notes. I’d be interested to smell it on someone else. P.S. Although Parfumo has entries for both an EDT and EDP version, someone said that this is inaccurate and there’s actually only ever been an EDT. Well, if that’s true, it’s VERY strong for an EDT.

Salvatore Ferragamo Emozione Dolce Fiore was a gift from a friend and I just adore this fragrance. If ever there was a tender, delicate, inoffensive and innocent sweet, light floral this is it. She is sheer, uplifting, very soft like a baby's blanket; floral-sweet with zero heaviness; the citrus here is anything but sharp, serving only to provide a subtle crispness; the fuzzy musk is soft and slightly warm; the florals dance above the musk and the vanilla plays an invisible supporting role. One word to accurately capture this fragrance is "charming". Performance: moderate at best, this lasts on textiles and hair far longer than skin. Value: Looking at the prices, the value is good/ not too costly. Bottle: I think it's GORGEOUS. So 10/10 on that.

Dear friends on Parfumo, today I would like to share my fresh impressions of Emozione Dolce Fiore EdT. First of all, it is a dreamy fragrance! The package with the bottle just arrived, and I am reporting to you hot off the press about the scent because I must share my enthusiasm with you. I ordered it blindly online because the notes sounded so delicious and the offer was unbeatable in price. Peach, grapefruit, peony, suede, vanilla... all of this sounds to me like it comes from the ingredient list of olfactory bliss. Quickly opened the package and sprayed the fragrance. So, how does it smell? In the opening, it smelled very juicy and fruity. The grapefruit and peach formed a fresh unity, with no component standing out. It almost reminded me of pear. After a few minutes, a floral component emerged. Here, the peony is especially noticeable, appearing dew-kissed and gently woven into the scent's progression. All of this created a harmonious fruity-floral accord. A few minutes later, the suede could be faintly sensed in the background, giving the fragrance a fine spiciness and a noble elevation. The suede smells delicate and white and incredibly elegant. Bottega Veneta can pack it up! Although the two fragrances really can't be compared. But I find this one better. The musk in this fragrance smells clean, bright, and clear. I can't really pick out the vanilla, but it probably adds a slight sweetness to the scent. Emozione Dolce Fiore EdT is lovely, pink, delicate, floating, attractive, feminine. It is a finely constructed fragrance that knows how to enchant. I think it fits perfectly for a date because it smells so feminine. But it also works well in the office, as it has a pretty good sillage for an EdT, yet is still discreet enough. I can't say anything about the longevity yet, as I haven't known the fragrance long enough. Conclusion: Another successful fragrance from Salvatore Ferragamo, which is delicate and feminine as if one had kissed a peach and reminds one of pink sunsets. My new favorite!

Today I discovered a pink sample in my shopping bag, alongside my new fragrance acquisition. That’s the second best thing about buying perfumes - the sample addition! Oh, joy of beautiful divine spark - Emozione Dolce Fiore! I enjoy wearing the original Emozione, and I generally hold Ferragamo fragrances dear and valuable. And right from the first spray, I am convinced by the positive statement of Fiore. It is, just like Emozione, a friendly, buoyant charmer. The white peach is airy light, and only gently sweet, softly dusted with iris. Here, a touch of elegance comes into play. The musk note is bright and shiny - and gives Fiore substance. A fine, well-balanced fragrance that doesn’t make you feel “dressed up.” Despite its lightness, it has a special radiance and good longevity. Regardless of the inhospitable cold, I put on my hat and head to the fragrance dealer on the run. But my intention to buy is not fulfilled - the fragrance is not yet in stock. So for now, I still enjoy wearing Emozione.

How often have I received YSL fragrances as gifts from French women in the past, from exchange students, teachers, and accompanying persons of the exchanges, from guests and friends from the partner city. Always with the remark that these were true Parisian scents. I was happy, simply because they were gifts. But apart from the underlying scent that I perceive in all typical YSL fragrances: Something green, fresh, and at the same time powdery, and back then nothing else identifiable for me, I didn't like any of them, no matter which one it was. The base note bothered me, and I could never notice any significant differences. That's why I also don't know which fragrances I owned as 50ml bottles. For sure, Opium or any of its flankers were not among them. When I saw the prices in France, I always felt guilty. I wore the fragrances out of politeness as long as the guests were there. It then smelled like that all over the house for me. Afterwards, I gave them away. And I wondered why they were received with joy and a certain reverence. Yes, that's how I was! That was already 8 years ago and much longer in the past over the decades. What a barbarism on my part. When I cautiously dabbed "Paris Roses de Vergers Springtime" from the vial today, that typical scent was there again. The faces of the people who were our guests, those of those we visited in France all came to my mind. And a longing to travel to France again, the Atlantic, Provence, Normandy, Charente Maritime, etc. How often have I been to France, and I always felt at home there. These kinds of fragrances from YSL are also the scent of France for me. Now I can distinguish these fragrances, do something with them, and I like them now. The "Paris Rose in Orchards in Spring" are delicately green-scented wild roses that wonderfully complement the cherry and pear blossoms. It must be noted that cherry, plum, apple, pear, almond, and quince trees belong to the rose family, as do blackberry and raspberry bushes, and surprisingly strawberries. Therefore, the mentioned blossoms generally match the rose scents of a perfume. The scent "Paris Rose des Vergers Springtime" then develops a fresh green and light floral sillage to the YSL base scent, a little almondy, hinting at the cherry blossoms. Just as it might smell in spring in a somewhat overgrown orchard: grasses, wildflowers, lily of the valley, woodruff, the blossoms of currants, fruit tree blossoms. Above all, the scent of briefly blooming wild roses, which have grown into large wild rose bushes from the mother stock of a robust wild rose, whose grafted noble rose shoots have long since died, overtaking everything. These wild roses bloom with small flowers in white to pink briefly early in spring only to then develop rose hips. Rose breeders know how this happens and what I mean. After a while, PRdV takes on a slightly creamy note, the powderiness of the base scent lightly settles over it. I cannot perceive any woods, and the musk plays no noticeable role. This fragrance has a long-lasting effect on me for hours. Since I've been dabbling here in Parfumo, I've also come to love these fragrances from YSL. And I don't understand why I had no access to them back then. "Paris Rose des Vergers Springtime" is a delicate scent for all occasions. You will never stand out or overwhelm others with it. It is a spring and summer fragrance that can also be enjoyed in winter if one has the desire for it.

I would classify this as Dark Aoud EDC or Dark Aoud 'Sport'. Opens with a great combination of citric and green notes that remains for a good amount of time. Then joins a vetiver note and a wonderful (but light if compared to Dark Aoud) sandal note and this way it dries down. Thats the reason i call it Dark Aoud EDC. After some hours i can detect a light leather note, so its basically sandal, vetiver and a bit of leather in the late drydown. Longevity is around 8 hours, sillage and projection are great. By the way i dont smell any oud.
