That being said, Aoud Queen Roses is still a very solid choice, especially if what you're looking for is closer to a rose soliflore but still has noticeable oud and patchouli in the mix.

Montale AOUD QUEEN ROSES (plural according to a house-produced carded sample--and also the bottle depicted above) is a regal treat of primarily roses, aoud, and patchouli, with a big emphasis on the first two terms of the triad. The other notes add some zing and zest, no doubt, but I think of this as primarily, as its name suggests, a rose-oud perfume. There are many rose-oud-patchouli compositions out there today, but my impression is that we have Pierre Montale (or reasonable facsimile) for bringing oud to the un-unwashed masses: we Western gringos who have never set foot in Oman and would never have encountered this note in perfumery otherwise. The rose depiction here is like a huge bushel of rose petals, but this is not a soliflore because of the equally important oud note. AOUD QUEEN ROSES was my U.S. presidential election night selection, once the winner had been announced, and I got a bit carried away, spraying myself with all 3 ml of a generous decant sent to me by Couture Guru, who obviously has excellent taste. Three mls is a lot of perfume to apply, I realize, but I was not overwhelmed at all, because the blend is perfect, so spraying more on just meant more of a good thing. Basically, I was walking around within a moving cone of rose-oud scent. I was thinking today about the houses which produce perfumes which must be applied sparingly or else the whole experience is ruined--Lalique and Caron leap immediately to mind--but this perfume from Montale does not become toxic or unbearable in any way. Intoxicating, yes. For three days I could smell this beautiful perfume on a cashmere sweater I had worn that night, and it never suffered any degradation or degeneration at all. It also smelled great on my HRH Emperor the next day, which is always the sure sign of a well-constructed perfume--a royal one in this case! (-; AOUD QUEEN ROSES is one of the best of the several rose-oud perfumes I've tried (a bit less oud-y than ATTAR, which is also excellent), and it is now on my wish list. Thank you, Couture Guru, for introducing me to this gorgeous creation!

It opened with a woody and watery rose and a good dose of hibiscus. I got the mental image of a rose bouquet floating on a log down a lazy river. After a minute or so, it changes. I get a loud rose with some oud and patchouli. The oud and patchouli blend nicely to have an almost incense quality. There is also a hint of leather in there. The "incense" note is dominant in the drydown. It's very beautiful. The longevity is amazing and sillage was a little too loud to be called personal. Jun 03 2014

Smells almost the same as Attar, but weaker. The main difference is the hibiscus note and the leather in the base. Not sweet, but sharp and green roses. Sillage, lasting power and projection are weak if compared to other releases. Updated October 2014

Queen Roses as a name fits this superb fragrance like a bespoke tailored jacket. This is definitely a 'royal rose', distant and untouchable but radiating extreme beauty in the glare of paparazzi flashbulbs. An oud bodygaurd protects this Queen from being handled as she proceeds amongst her adoring public, spreading her grace and dignity about her like a finely crafted piece of Valenciennes lace. Getting back to reality ;) ... Aoud Queen Roses is a masterful blend of Oud and Roses, probably one of the best from Montale. It's not loud or harsh as some of these combinations tend to be, neither is it too sweet or 'jammy'. Rather, this rose is captured in the stillness of dawn, while she's dewy and fresh ... and before the heat of the day has made her sleepy. There I go again ... waxing lyrical :). A truly beautiful fragrance from Montale with above average sillage and longevity ... and with the curious power to transport one into the realms of fertile, rose scented immagination!

My wish: a beautiful rosy Oud for myself. Unfortunately, I didn't find anything in the perfumery I trust (A review of Rose Oud by Kilian will follow). But I thought, what the heck, you'll be in Paris next week. And if I can't find my rose oud there, then nowhere. After a brief search online (why hadn't I stumbled upon Parfumo before???

Aoud Queen Roses actually reminds me of the beautiful Queen Elizabeth Rose that thrives in my garden. It shines a delicate pink - with a silver touch and exudes a fine, noble scent. The Montale also keeps the rose subtle, with a certain silvery coolness.

The name Oud Queen Rose suggests an opulent oud that carries a magnificent, majestic rose. In fact, Montale takes a step back here. The oud is used much more sparingly than in many other oud fragrances. The rose is given precedence. It is beautiful, but also somewhat weak. This is still a young queen, almost still a princess.

Aoud Queen Roses is an oriental spicy fragrance by Montale with long-lasting power; I can smell it on myself for about 9 hours. I find the scent to be just right according to its title. Aoud makes the opening, and the rose immediately joins in. It smells as if they are dancing around each other. Pleasantly subtle leather notes provide a solid erotic overall expression.

Attention, here comes a medicine. At least I perceive the first minutes as somewhat medicinal. A surprise for me, how leather can smell. Mixed with roses and agarwood. The queen of flowers wraps herself in woody notes and boots, or something like that. No, seriously.

Ferragamo's INCANTO opens with a big bold shower of peach and plum, making it impossible for me not to think of TUSCANY PER DONNA and TRESOR. The peach dominates in all three of these creations and is harmoniously blended with a variety of floral and spice elements. I am mystified as to why INCANTO is categorized as oriental woody when the other two are oriental floral. My own label for all three would be oriental fruity-floral since the peach is most prominent throughout all stages of all three. Although I obviously do not find it unique, I find INCANTO deliciously wearable. This is definitely a very sweet perfume, and the woodiness is all but masked by the strong allspice. But if you love TRESOR and/or TUSCANY (or LALIQUE...), you'll like this one as well.

In my search for the creamy juicy summer peach, I came across Incanto. The reviews gave me courage! The clear bottle gives clean vibes. It seems a bit unwieldy at first because it is so oddly wide. At least it’s flat, I can fit it well in my bursting-at-the-seams fragrance water cabinet. The spray head releases a nice mist. I like that! As for the scent: the first sniff has a certain alcohol hairspray synthetic note. Thankfully, that fades away. After that, a bit of peach unfolds, in a clean way. I miss the creaminess here! Alone, this is a good everyday cheapie, it doesn’t stand out much, doesn’t cause headaches, all is okay. But that’s not enough for me! The lily is noticeable, but it also gives the scent a somewhat green-airy quality. Plum? Where is it, please? Incanto pairs very well with other fragrances. I must say, not every scent can be combined, especially if the scent itself already brings a complexity. Incanto is simple, and that makes it a good layering partner. My first attempt with Muse Poudrée I like so incredibly well! I’m wearing a lovely powdery creamy peach scent now and feel like I’ve doubled the sillage of both rather subtle fragrances. Alone, it’s quite a nice scent that I find very suitable for spring; for those who prefer it more subtle?

This scent is simply sweet on my skin. So sweet. It doesn't smell fresh, floral, fruity, or anything like that, just sweet. You won't lure any cats out from behind the stove with this, but it will definitely attract wasps in late summer. Since this is the first comment about it, even though it has been around since 2003, I assume that most perfume writers found the scent so boring in the store that they didn't even bother to test it on their skin. That others can see it quite differently than I do is shown by the other reviews. I mean: You can wear it, but you don't have to.

Strong (as expected) and extremely screechy, high-pitched aromachemicals in a container. So unpleasant I had to srub the fragrance off my wrist after one hour - I could not stand this combination on my skin. One of the worst Montales I tried. Metallic-sour overtones kept haunting me in my sleep, probably the strong lily-of-the-valley-note. Artificial ambregris and musk don't improve this scent. No balance here, let alone beauty. I'd love to know what role "nature" played in the creation of this fragrance. It seems utterly artificial/synthetical to me. But, of course, this is a subjective observation, very subjective. "Crystal Flowers" don't obtain a place in my fragrance hall of fame. I advise them to my personal hall of shame.

Montale makes excellent Middle Eastern-inspired perfumes. Most anything with the word 'aoud' in the name is going to be a worthy representative of the ever-growing class of aoud perfumes. Once one steps out of the aoud range, however, everything is up for grabs, and it's anyone's guess what the perfume may be like! CRYSTAL FLOWERS is a good example of a Montale which might have been a mainstream designer launch. It smells fine to me, a perfectly wearable office-ready, inoffensive fruity-floral frag. The flowers are abstract but not to the point of being unwearable. This composition reminds me of perfumes such as Creed SPRING FLOWER or Bond no 9 CHELSEA FLOWERS, both of which, too, fit into the category of office-ready inoffensive fruity floral frags. This really is a genre by now, and when I say fruity-floral, I mean more abstract floral than fruity, but there is a touch of fruity to give the overall composition a brightness. The musk used, too, is clear and clean, not dark and sweaty. This is a twenty-first-century type of perfume which has gained a legion of followers in the last few years. In some ways it may seem superficial, but it is also likable to many consumers. Precisely because this sort of perfume is the sort of thing one runs into at Sephora among the current bestsellers, it may not be the wisest investment of one's big Montale bucks. Try before you buy.

Montale is one of the more exciting brands among niche perfumes for me. Some of the scents I have tested so far have been quite special, but that's exactly what I find interesting. When I sprayed on Christal Flowers, I was expecting a rather fragile, cool, and above all romantic scent. Think again! For the first 5 seconds, I could hardly smell anything, but then!!!!! The scent dam broke and a sea of roses and mandarin peels surged over me. Like Esther Williams, I let myself be carried away in the delicious waves of roses. Now and then, a lily of the valley floated past me. The rose water then slowly became a bit spicier. Sperm whales sang their sweet amber song in the rose waves. But slowly I could sense an impending doom. The rosy sea darkened and the waves became stormier. Then, all of a sudden, the horror came in the form of the evil musk sea monster from the depths, spraying its all-corrupting, all-destroying hairspray poison. As if I had received a resounding slap in the face, I awoke from my fantasy and rushed towards the bathroom to terminate the musk monster. But somehow, this scent combination fascinated me, and I let the monster be. Ultimately, the hairspray note turned out to be fleeting, and I dove headfirst back into the sea of roses. Anyone who likes roses should try this Montale. The musk note takes some getting used to but is then very interesting. C, thank you for this scent!

Before I start my comment here, I must come out....I am a Montale FAN! A Montale freak maybe :) Still, I will judge this fragrance very objectively! :) Anyone who knows Roses Musk by Montale will immediately notice a very strong similarity! At least at the beginning... It is indeed a typical rose-musk scent from the house of Montale Paris, but it has a little peculiarity....it is more FLORAL than Roses Musk! The musk reveals itself after a few minutes, but it is not as overpowering as in Roses Musk.... The floral note (that must be the lily of the valley) plays a big role, which I really find beautiful about this fragrance....this is finally a Montale that can also be worn in summer without causing others to struggle for breath! It reminds me of the first lovely sunny days in spring that one has eagerly awaited after a long winter! The sillage and longevity are also above average with this fragrance, lasting about 8 hours :) a 100ml bottle will therefore last a very long time!! Although I am someone who likes to apply 6-8 sprays of a fragrance, I am careful with this one...2 to a maximum of 4 sprays should be MORE THAN enough to fill a room ;) typical Montale indeed... Regards A Montale Freak

Although it is called Chrystal Flowers, the rose comes out the strongest for me. Lily of the valley and mandarin disappear immediately. Amber is very subtle. What remains is a wonderful rose-musk blend. It resembles Juliette Has a Gun Miss Charming a lot for me, only that Chrystal Flowers is more radiant, clearer, brighter, and "edgier." The "edginess," coolness it has in common with Lady Vengeance (also Juliette Has a Gun). Miss Charming is a bit more powdery/diffuse and a touch sweeter and more charming. Chrystal Flowers smells radiantly bright and unsweetened fresh, very captivating. The longevity is top-notch, Montale-style.

Montale draws attention with its very unusual bottles, all resembling a very stylish thermos in colorful, eye-catching design. When wearing "Crystal Flowers," beautiful, delicate pink roses unfold first, accompanied by a hint of lily of the valley, evoking dreams of a stunning sea of white and pink shimmering flowers.

~ Inspiration ~ "Crystal Flowers" by Montale made it onto my wishlist partly because of the pink packaging, and of course because of the fragrance notes. ~ Bottle ~ You can immediately tell it's a Montale by the cylindrical, minimalist shape - here in metallic pink. ~ Scent ~ It starts fruity-sweet with mandarins and sugared, pink roses.

Crystal Flowers, in my opinion, it could also be called Crystal Rose, is a bright, long-lasting scent from Montale. Longevity is typically Montale, around 10 hours or more with my skin chemistry. The sillage is in the higher medium range, very decent. On me, rose and musk dance a waltz the whole time, it's a lively expression with harmonious interaction.

No, this scent isn't that bad. The "bottle" is somewhat misleading; it's really not bright pink and screamingly artificial. At drugstore level, the usual synthetic floral accords are gathered here, very artificial and clumsy, but quite consumable, neither overly shrill nor aggressive, just sweetly floral and rather harmless.

This is a delicate more lighter sister of the original Opium with it's pepper notes incense benzoin Opopponox bitter balsem woods and coriander. this version can be worn anytime then the original. the opening has the same scent as the predacessor but it's silage does'nt last long like the first one and it fades very quickly on my skin. maybe because of my chemistry or it a vital sample. but netherless i prefer the originial.

A hammam garden in the sunshine, a breeze rustling through the leaves of the plants, ornamental mosaics in shades of blue and green on walls and stone benches, a shower with handmade Moroccan soap that gently scents the skin with citrus and fine spices, quickly slipping on a white dress shirt and sliding into sandals... This summer version of the classic Opium is the perfect embodiment of what one imagines a summer version to be. The appeal and base notes are almost the same as the original: on top, a gentle, sunny bergamot note has been added, and the fragrance overall is lighter, more transparent, yet still retains its oriental character. Opium Eau d'Été also serves as the optimal alternative for anyone who finds Opium too strong. (The other summer versions I have tested were more floral and not as pleasantly fresh, e.g., Opium Orchidée de Chine.) Nevertheless, while it is the quintessential summer version, Opium Eau d'Été - as one might expect from such a strong oriental perfume as Opium - is a fresh, modern oriental fragrance that can be worn every day in any season.

Recently, a friend came to visit - a lively person whom I greatly appreciate for her temperament and emotionality. Due to her vivacity and casual charm, she could be an Italian Signorina, but she is actually Hungarian by birth. However, Steffi often "cooks" blood that is probably infused with paprika. She can fall from the brightest joy into deep sadness - a trait that can sometimes be a bit irritating. We joked carefreely in the car until suddenly her ex came to mind, and she threw herself onto the steering wheel, sobbing uncontrollably. Three traffic light phases were cried through until we finally moved on. Much to my relief, and that of the line of cars waiting behind us. But she is very lovable, and as already mentioned, a chic appearance. She has chosen her fragrance well - Signorina. It is also lively, emotional, and has a casual Mediterranean charm. Lychee and grapefruit are invigorating and refreshing, while the rice steam is mild and aromatic. The Signorina becomes wonderfully soft through the delicious milk foam and noble cashmeran. The fragrance features interesting twists from fresh cheerfulness to soft soulful warmth. A likable Signorina, full of surprises with high allure. Today, I treated myself to a bottle - simply because I felt like being close to Steffi.

Opens with a harsh lime and powerful oud. Then, after many hours, dries down to a beautiful sweet sandalwood and roses. This reminds me of AMBER & SPICES sometimes. As SL's Arabie, Aoud Lime needs some time to be completely understood. Sillage, lasting power and projection are high. Updated January 2014

Aoud Lime from Montale Luxury Niche French Perfumery House is a 'Oud Rose Woody Spicy Unisex perfume. Aoud Lime was released in 2005; and the nose responsible for this fragrance is Pierre Montale. Very tasty perfume! With quality and a great cost benefit, in addition to powerful creations, easy to please, and without challenges make Montale an excellent option for the transition to Niche Perfumery. A classic 'Oud & Rose somewhat linear. The great positive point is that in Oud Lime clearly the woody portion overlaps the rose. Unlike Black Aoud where the rose is the empowered one of the time. Aoud Lime is very potent, as are all Montale I've met, but he's not an invasive atomic bomb like Black Aoud. I have no idea why 'Lime' in the name has nothing of lime, lemon or any other citrus reference in this perfume. Aoud Lime is easy to please and will earn compliments. Saffron also appears but not in its most usual leathery facet in perfumery, here it comes in the form of a condiment even though it only gives a slight spice in this composition. A dusty amber accord with the iris bring a slight softness to the fragrance. As I said, the woody part overlaps over the rose; With the leaves of woody and earthy character of the patchouli and the 'oud as the protagonist, a very well built medicinal resinous woody synthetic 'oud without difficulties or challenge.

Oud fragrances, especially from Montale, seem to be as plentiful as sand on the beach. I have never been able to warm up to Oud, and this scent is no exception for me; however, I tested it and will compare it a bit with Aoud Safran, also from Montale. The scent: Uuurgh, what a start. It begins with a strong alcoholic note, quickly transitioning into a disinfectant/medicinal scent. This is the typical agarwood, which often seems to have two faces. When used subtly, it can smell quite good (in combination with other fragrance notes), but as strong as it is here, and with a good sillage, it comes off as piercing and very overwhelming. It certainly does not smell good (of course, one must also know that I don't like Oud at all). The second strongest note here is patchouli, which is quite okay, but it hides far in the background. I don't even want to talk about the other fragrance notes that are hardly noticeable, although at times it does have a slightly floral scent. I'm not so sure about the saffron here, as the Oud seems to overshadow almost everything, but the saffron does seem to be stronger than in the fragrance that is supposed to contain saffron, namely Aoud Safran. Later, the very intense Oud scent becomes milder, allowing one to detect some sandalwood, saffron, and rose, and it becomes a bit sweeter. Longevity and sillage: The longevity of such fragrances seems to be exceptionally high, and I think Aoud Lime clings for more than 8-10 hours. The sillage at the beginning is truly bombastic (overwhelming). The Oud seems to spread throughout the entire atmosphere before it fades a bit and becomes bearable, yet still radiates well. People who enjoy strong sillage and like Oud might be thrilled. However, my room now somehow smells totally like medical stuff... The bottle: The bottle has the typical Montale shape and looks like an aluminum drinking bottle. It is shiny black/gray and has the typical Montale screw-cap-like spray head at the neck, with the metallic logo dangling from it. It's actually quite nice, but nothing more. Oh no (oud no...), this scent is nothing, absolutely nothing for me. I don't like Oud anyway, but the way this fragrance component rages in the top note is particularly repulsive to me, even though it becomes a bit milder and spicier with the saffron after about 30 minutes. Those who enjoy such a fragrance direction will especially appreciate the long longevity and brutal sillage; all others might run away screaming when someone applies the scent (just) now. Well, as I said, later it is okay and could certainly be liked, but there are better fragrances with Oud. Aoud Safran, which I also had lying around as a sample from Montale, is already a better choice. Otherwise, I would only wear this fragrance in autumn and winter, as it could be really overwhelming in summer.

I think this perfume is just amazing. I had to try such a bold combination. Here lies the difference between a test strip and applying it to the skin as far apart as day and night. At first, I was a bit skeptical about the purchase, not because of the oud and lime but because of the almost overwhelming scent of rose for me. Apparently, my nose picks up the rose very strongly here, as I could also describe this perfume as lime-rose. Unfortunately, I normally do not like rose scents at all, but in this combination with oud, it just blew me away somehow. I can only say it is a very, very fresh oud scent with a strong note of lime and rose; you can also clearly smell the saffron. Amber and sandalwood appear very deep in the undertone, and the iris always plays a slight role. Highly recommended for those who love extreme scents!

I just can't learn - I've tested another Montale fragrance again... Even though I know by now that here, disgustingly hyped, noisy concepts are clumsily sold at completely inflated prices with the cheapest components, and that this whole thing is just not acceptable! Or...? "Aoud Lime" this time. And I am surprised: although it is characteristically loud, metallic, cheerfully direct, and in high gear, "Aoud Lime" is, to my astonishment, by no means the flat-cheap noise that makes my eyes water. In any case, the opening with the usual silvery-bright (some say medicinal) oud note and the equally familiar synthetic rose is this time surprisingly well and seamlessly integrated with the addition of a bright yellow-green, herb-fresh citrus lime, which fits quite well with Apicius' perception of these notes. Not that there are any major developments or that depth and density are revealed, and the components do not shine with multi-layered texture or artisanal complexity; these are all loud synthetic one-dimensional molecules, but here they are well combined - no, what you smell first is what you get all the way, so to speak, but even that is honest and works quite well, very dry and slightly sour for hours. In the drydown, I am again tortured by the disgustingly sweet sandalwood synthetic along with the pitiful remnants of the rose component, and to top it off, there's patchouli, but that's just Montale. Definitely not for me, hopelessly overpriced, but in any case, a great relief compared to "Black Aoud" and the like.

...at least from Montale. Oud Fragrance No. 2 (no, not the good one from Aigner *g*) from Montale was up next. After recently trying the first sample of Montale's "Steam Aoud," and having a rather mediocre opinion on the topic of Oud, I must say that this one is even worse. The advantage, however, is that I now know how Oud smells.

Yuck, that doesn't fit at all! Fresh lime and earthy-woody oud truly belong to different worlds. What has emerged here is an extremely sharp, scratchy version of oud. It gets better when the lime note fades, but it’s still bad.

"In Love Again Jasmin Étoile" crossed my path rather by accident, so I simply had to poach a test spray... The top note is fruity and somehow toffee-like. I suspect amber as that often sports the same kind of pervasiveness. Next the fragrance reminds me of the strange note of wet dog I find so typical for the Hermès Jardin fragrances and which I dislike. I'm not that keen on the smell of dogs even when they're dry. So, ambrated wet dog. I can't pair this up with the notes given: Aniseed? Well, perhaps it could be part of the wet dog smell, but that's no definite. Jasmin? Nix. In the very first beginning I smelled something which reminded me of urine - should that have been the jasmin? If so, it snuck off quickly and thoroughly. That's lucky of course. A leaking wet dog would be too much. Cassia - that should smell pleasantly like cinnamon and a bit like hay, but I can't smell any of that. What a pity. Mandarin? Yes, but only the variety canned with syrup. Instead of being fresh and tangy it smells distinctively of cooked fruit with a metallic whiff from the can to boot. (Probably have been stored a few years past their best-before date...) Sandalwood? Nope. Granted, that belongs in the base notes and they're not due yet. Vanilla - a whiff, yes. Not obtrusive at all. And cedar will probably become more pronounced in the base notes, but there's a whiff of pencil shavings noticeable already. In Love Again Jasmin Étoile fades quickly, the wet Hermès dog straying on while the rest is dominated by canned mandarins and pencil. I don't get this fragrance at all. I would not even use it if someone gave it to me as it starts to give me a headache, too. But then! Two and a half hours later, the heart note puts paid to canned mandarins and pencil shavings. Instead there is a resemblance to the Hermès Jardins fragrances. They too have this lovely and extremely foreign, no, this extraterrestial sweet flowery scent that doesn't seem to have anything to do with the notes listed. This lovely sweet flowery and arresting scent stays for hours, far into the faint but softly woody base note over which it hovers like a lovely UFO. This fragrance is not for me, even if I am fascinated by the lovely alien flower scent. I'm not patient enough to sit through the wet dog and the canned mandarins until I like what I smell on my skin. Im very very curious however what is this smell of wet dog turning into lovely alien flower.

The fragrance itself reveals itself as a bouquet of "stars" with star anise and star jasmine that intoxicates the enamored senses. The journey into the universe begins with orange mandarins, dark red currants, and deep black 'licorice'. Jasmine takes off like a rocket and makes this perfume instantly feminine. The woods ensure it never gets cold on the way to Mr. Spock and company. Perhaps just a tiny bit too much vanilla. Thank you, Evita! ;)

Sapparot means Pineapple in Thai, a very important fruit in the culture of this beautiful country. It is used in many rituals and ceremonies, as an offering to spirits, temples or monks. Its yellow color is associated with sunshine, light and joy:Oud Sapparot blends a juicy and full Pineapple, full of sweetness, to the smokiness and harshness of Oud . A fruity Oud, deep but also joyful, playing in a balance between the two ever-present parts, which alternate in a really interesting way, transforming over time into a soft and enveloping symphony. A must-have during summer evenings. "Concetto Spaziale, Attesa" work created by Lucio Fontana.

Not a safe blind buy. I wouldn't say this fragrance is true gourmand for those looking for a gourmand oud fragrance like others by Montale, as Arabians Tonka is. It's a mature scent. The pineapple is minimal to my nose in the middle and base, as is the coconut and vanilla. Top notes are a bomb of juicy charred pineapple but quickly fades. The leather and wood are smoky and the strongest and longest last notes, possibly the saffron and cinnamon too although I dont really pick up on these notes. They are all offset and made lighter, less overpowering and a little sweeter by the cinnamon, vanilla and slight creamy but almost undetectable coconut. This is a very unisex fragrance, maybe even slightly masculine leaning. It's not sickly or overpowering as I was fearing. It doesn't screech, but as typical for Oud it is rich, deep, and smells expensive, but all the notes seem to balance well. On skin it isn't the longest lasting, probably 8 hours. It radiates arms length to intimate. On clothes and hair it lasts a lot longer. 12 hours plus. Top notes until it fades to middle and base could be considered slightly medicinal. This is a good evening fragrance or for special occasions. I'm unsure how it will perform in summer as I originally attended.

I have owned my Oud Sapparot for about a week now, and since then, I haven't wanted anything else in my daily life. This is the first thing my hand reaches for after my morning shower. I really spray it generously on the back of my neck along the hairline, on my knees, and in the crooks of my arms, and I can't help but let out this delightful and uncontrollable Mmmmmh paired with the realization "I am in a good mood." I am already a Montale fan, and among other things, I am fascinated by the way Montale manages to capture fruity scents. If I were to perceive this fragrance with my eyes closed, I wouldn't doubt for a second that I was sniffing a pineapple juice (or liqueur). I don't perceive Oud directly. If someone is "afraid" of Oud - don't worry, it is not present here, but it does ensure that the pineapple doesn't sound too straightforward. I also don't perceive other notes (leather, saffron, cinnamon). However, I think they also contribute to perfectly showcasing the pineapple. In my perception, this is a mono-fragrance: Pineapple. However, pineapple here does not smell creamy or particularly gourmand - for me, it is just right, as I do not like very pronounced gourmand directions (often caramel or chocolatey). My conclusion: I never want to miss this fruity good mood maker before a workday in summer. I can smell it on me for several hours, but I also like to refresh it every few hours. I find that you can't overdo it with this fragrance; it feels a bit like a very elegant deodorant, you don't come off as "perfumed" but rather fruity-fresh. The (classic) Montale bottle emphasizes this perception.

I actually grew up with this scent. My mom has been wearing it since my childhood on special occasions. And yes: This fragrance is also something special for me. Only a potential partner should not wear this scent, that would be strange and I would always think of my mom :D With this fragrance variation, the longevity and sillage are simply amazing. The scent even survives a wash cycle on clothing. In the top note, it comes across as fruity and citrusy. I recognize bergamot and mandarins. The heart note then becomes more oriental and offers a hint of jasmine flowers and a lovely smokiness. The base has that unmistakable scent of opoponax. One simply has to think of incense and myrrh here. It smells dark, balsamic, and mystical. And also a bit like the obligatory church visit at Christmas - simply really wonderful and full of nostalgia!

Opium, this scent has been familiar to me since my childhood. It epitomized the elegant, sensual woman. For me, it was a symbol of sensuality, intoxication, depth, and abyss. I never owned it myself. In perfumeries, I always sniffed the samples and was enchanted. Until that moment when the formula was changed (in the late 90s?). It was still somewhat similar to the original formula, but only like a roughly pixelated image next to an original painting. It was a shame. Now, I was always driven by the longing for the original, the desire to experience it once more. I acquired the perfume second-hand, and when I gently dabbed it on my thumb, the spirit came out of the bottle. I was enchanted, actually done for. An explosion of memories surged within me. It truly has a dark, shimmering depth that is hard to describe. This is how the 70s smelled, this was my image of adulthood as a child. Now my judgment is all the more decisive: Today's Opium does not deserve the name. It belongs in the trash, an insult.

Montale Oud Island has something truly special for me. Right from the start, you feel this slightly tropical, almost sunny sensation, combined with a subtle Oud that is neither too heavy nor overwhelming. It's as if you're inhaling a warm breeze by the sea, bringing with it a sense of depth and elegance. The fragrance remains pleasantly present without being too loud, and it becomes softer over the hours. This very blend of exoticism and tranquility makes it a scent that can be worn both in everyday life and on relaxed evenings.

When I had the opportunity to choose some samples at Montale, Oud Island was thankfully among them! About the scent: - It starts very citrusy and fresh, with lemon and tangerine being very prominent, immediately accompanied by a light animalic note and deep wood dimension, unbelievable. For a rather "fresher scent," it lasts incredibly long, lasting at most 3-4 hours less than Arabian Tonka, which is generally known from Montale to last seemingly forever. What is also very atypical for Montale is that it smells very natural, meaning it smells 0 synthetic, which is very positive. Conclusion: - Great scent for spring or everyday wear, anyone looking for light pleasant animalic notes combined with a wood dimension and an insane fresh citrus character should definitely give it a try!

Not bad, not bad at all. As a person that usually dislikes fruity florals of this kind, I found myself enjoying its fruity freshness and appreciating its bright and youthful charms. I particularly like how Incanto Charms opens with passionfruit and honeysuckle which gives it that tropical and slightly unusual appeal. I was rather glad that this combination didn't end up smelling like cheap shampoo. This fragrance sparkles with life. Incanto Charms never becomes dull or putrid, it continues to be Summery and fresh from beginning to end. This isn't a particularly unique fragrance, I'm almost certain there are replicas left, right and centre, however if I had to choose from a majority of fruity florals on the market today, I'd certainly choose this. Unfortunately the lasting strength is pretty weak. Not terrible, but certainly disappointing. Dismissing the fact that this scent hardly holds, I like Salvatore Ferragamo's approach when it came to creating this sweet, flirtatious and youthful fragrance. I recommend this fragrance especially to teens as a pleasant Summer/Spring alternative.

~ Inspiration ~ Years ago, I got to know "Incanto Charms" and it has stayed positively in my memory, so I ordered a bottle online (factory seconds - unfortunately without the beautiful cap). ~ Bottle ~ The flat glass bottle is adorned with a colorful pattern, which reminds me a bit of a mandala. The colors blue-turquoise-pink match perfectly with its cheerful aura! ~ Fragrance ~ Upon spraying, it is immediately fruity-fresh with a slightly tangy passion fruit. Jasmine and roses provide a floral undertone. With cedarwood, musk, and a hint of amber, it gently and quietly fades away. ~ Longevity ~ On my skin, it lasts about 4-5 hours (a bit longer on clothing and hair). You can comfortably use several sprays without feeling overloaded or too sweet. ~ Occasion ~ A cheerful fragrance for the warmer days of spring and summer. Also a nice, unobtrusive office scent! ~ Conclusion ~ I love this pleasant, enchanting little fragrance!

This is a fragrance that took me twice wearing it to really appreciate the fragrance. My initial impression was that of a really smooth but boring leather, then I decided to try it again just because it was a blind purchase... And I'm glad that I did. Not only is this a creamy and smooth leather but it also has some complexity to it, citrus from the grapefruit along with the rose and now it's love. Definitely last 8hrs for me on my skin.

In the community of fragrances, much of them is woody, no doubt, but not all of them come together so well to form a welcoming whole as Oudrising does. This unusual blend brings us a large amount of the insanity that an animal feels when it hunts in the wild woods. This is how I would describe another great creation from Montale. First a little about the presentation itself. Satisfactory, but without that WOW impression. Definitely the form of perfume from Montale has become a bit dated, and painting a beautiful bird on the facade of the bottle unfortunately doesn't save it. It's not something I would have expected from such a fine interior. When you spray this fragrance on yourself, you are applying a piece of the forest world to your skin. You can certainly feel that whiff of wet leaves and the shattered wood of overgrown plants underfoot. The composition opens with an unusual combination of wild leather with fresh bergamot, pink grapefruit and spicy pepper. These ingredients make us feel a hint of freshness combined with very raw materials. Right from the start, we are able to tell that we are in a leather goods manufactory strewn around with wild citrus plants. After such a luscious opening, we are transported to a primal world of trees, smoke and aromatic flowers. It is this great middle ground that gives the whole fragrance the impression of wild escape through the forest amidst grand old spice-smoke trees and intense floral aromas. Interestingly, the plants do not impart any femininity, conversely they stimulate the sexual thinking of men, awakening the wild hunter in them. I have no hesitation in saying that this is an extremely erotic fragrance. This whole is surrounded by intense notes of tobacco, incense, cedar and musk. These give an ambery warm spicy character that brilliantly underlines its companions. It adds a touch of sweetness encapsulating this wild whole. It is a VERY long-lasting fragrance, one of the most long-lasting I have in my collection (and there is a lot of that kind). Such a powerful perfume needs to be applied with care. As I have mentioned several times before, this is ultimately the wildness of nature reworked into the essence of a perfume. The price is very satisfactory for such a rich and high quality fragrance. One so beautifully complex that will appeal to particularly refined tastes. I highly recommend it to bold women and men who know how sexy they truly are, and want to try something new and unusual.

I got the fragrance at a good price and actually wanted to get rid of it right away, without opening the original packaging. But since Montale has always impressed me so far, I couldn't resist And lo and behold: am I disappointed or not...? The opening hits hard, it's probably the pepper. But then, WHAT? I love it! But I know this scent, right? YES, it is a copy of Santal Royal... I can't describe it any other way. Of course, it's much louder, but even the Montale performance doesn't seem as special next to Guerlain's The bottle is stylish, but in the 50ml version I have, it's less impressive. No pattern.

At the beginning, a fresh explosion of grapefruit and leather with a bit of sharpness. The leather is rather light. After a while, you can also smell the oud. I would generally say that the development of the fragrance is linear. As mentioned, it starts off a bit fruitier but becomes very linear as it progresses. A distinctive mix of leather and oud with a certain sweetness in the background. In my opinion, the fragrance is somewhat synthetic but not as extreme as other scents from Montale. The projection is good but not exaggerated. You can also wear the fragrance in the office if you don’t apply too much. The longevity is about 7-8 hours. Somehow, Oudrising reminds me of Ombre Nomade by LV but absolutely not as elegant and balanced; however, that’s just my personal feeling. However, this will probably be my only bottle from the brand, as I find the fragrances a bit too synthetic.

Oudrising is one of those fragrances that I really didn't like at all the first time I tested it. It just struck me as dark, leathery, and unpleasant. However, over time, this has changed quite a bit, as I had significantly different impressions during my second test. Still, I won't become a true fan of this little potion. The scent definitely starts off noticeably leathery. However, it actually has a citrus facet that resonates. Grapefruit is listed, and I think that can be confirmed. A bit of grapefruit and bergamot gives the opening something special alongside the leathery impression. I had only known this kind of combination from Memo Paris, and Memo Paris simply excels at this. Montale has also managed this quite well with Oudrising. However, this citrus impression is definitely weaker compared to the leather. Over time, the citrus impression recedes more and more. The leather remains, but is now more pleasant. Accompanying it is a rather dark type of oud, some rose, and patchouli. A smoky veil is also already noticeable. Towards the end, I even had the impression of perceiving a very slight sweetness, and the fragrance generally feels a bit rounder.

With YSL fragrances, I feel somewhat similar to Kenzo fragrances. If you love one, you love them all. However, with some limitations. I appreciate them, but they are not my favorite scents. However, when I need a light, effortless fragrance, I do like to reach for a Kenzo. I no longer own any YSL fragrances. And upon reflection, there is something common in the type of scents between YSL and Kenzo. Both have light, floral, effortless, and pleasing fragrances that do not vary much from scent to scent. Therefore, both brands have a high recognition value regardless of which fragrance you choose. In this observation, I exclude the Opium fragrances from YSL, as they belong to a different class. While Kenzo fragrances are more playful and sweeter, YSL fragrances - all that I have smelled and tested so far - have a bit more maturity, they are "more grown-up." It is not so easy to identify the individual scent components and the presented fragrance notes. Above all, I always smell this green, light floral, and slightly powdery YSL scent. What do I perceive in the "Bridge of Love"? A light fragrance, a bright floral blend with a hint of wood note. "Paris Pont des Amours" is less sweet than, for example, "Paris Rose de Bois," less lovely, and less expressive than "Paris Rose des Vergers." I cannot identify individual flowers. The sillage is very weak, but the longevity is not, as it is still noticeable after I shower. Overall, a weak fragrance, somewhat characterless, although it is a typical YSL. Addendum: After having had several YSL fragrances and testing quite a few, now reviewing my detailed notes on them, I have understood what makes the signature of this YSL Paris fragrance category (excluding Opium and flankers) so unique: All powdery, velvety, delicately floral scents that transform with creamy sandalwood, featuring this special signature. No harsh and sour citrus or vanilla notes are used.

It's a great fragrance, Fresh, Crisp and Clean. One of the best Salvatore Ferragamo men's perfumes. It opens up with like fresh citrusy , slightly spicy and floral notes in the background then dry down is green musky. It smells similar to the breeze of Amalfi Coast in the morning. This is suitable for the spring and summer. The art of bottle design is very wonderful. I really enjoy it and I like Subtil Pour Homme EDT for Men by Salvatore Ferragamo. Longevity is average. Thumbs Up. Rating : 8 / 10

SUBTIL POUR HOMME... subtle. Almost like the name was an inside joke during the production of this EMBARRASSING cash-grab of a fragrance. I have NEVER crossed paths with a cologne this lackluster in it's performance. NEVER. The scent itself is a solid one. A nice, fresh, gingery medley with a hit of sweet citrus. A flowery undercurrent is noticeable and indeed welcome... but that's it! Once worn, you will be shocked to discover that in a half hours (yes. 30 minutes. Not a gross-exaggeration), the scent has all but vanished. Totally undetectable, my guess would be even to the dogs! No sillage. No faint whiff. Not even a scent on the skin. Nose to wrist; THERE IS NOTHING THERE. What a total shame, because the smell itself is very pleasant. This could have made for a solid freshie indeed. As is, SUBTIL PUOR HOMME is the most useless fragrance I have ever tried on personally. It wouldn't really be worth reviewing if not for the fact that there are still bottles in the wild, despite House Ferragamo seemingly discontinuing it justifiably. Avoid at all costs.

The Duden translates the word "subtle": with care and a lot of sensitivity. A closer look at the fragrance pyramid makes it clear that this scent is far from the arbitrariness of what is currently "in": no lemon, no cedar, no bergamot, no sandalwood, and certainly no tonka and vanilla! - Such a fragrance pyramid is immediately associated by connoisseurs with a women's fragrance. But that is exactly what SpH is not!! SpH starts fresh. Mandarin, cardamom, and ginger are clearly identifiable. The top note lacks any sweetness. A bitter freshness, without herbaceousness! That is unusual! - This freshness remains, but transforms through the violet into a bitter sharpness, which in SpH is not balanced or softened by any sweetness as it is in pH. Experiencing rose and violet so bitter and sharp is definitely worth a sniff! Only in the base note does a hint of amber and patchouli soften the bitterness and sharpness. - A scent that I can only imagine on very bold women with a pronounced sense of self-worth - and on "intellectual", subtle men, who nowadays truly have a hard time finding a scent that suits them!! Matching the fragrance is the sillage: present, but hardly noticeable. The longevity on the skin is quite decent - up to 6 hours for me, where others often last only 2-3 hours. In comparison to the highly praised Laliqze White, SpH is clearly the more interesting and better alternative for me!
Because this scent is so soporific, boring, and bland that you fall asleep immediately! The chloroform of perfumes! Ugh, good night!

In this review, I wonder how close I can get my nose to the sprayed area in order to properly evaluate the scent? 50 cm: Embracing amber-tonka. 5 cm: Fully sweaty leather saddle. Right upon spraying, it smells as if I’m pouring a Grand Marnier, great start. The grapefruit adds a bit of freshness. As I get closer to the spray area, I also perceive a slightly prickly sharpness from the chili. It’s the first time I can actually identify that. After a while, the beautifully ambered tonka bean takes over the scent, warm, flattering, not overwhelming. I do not perceive leather WHEN I KEEP MY DISTANCE. As mentioned above, when I hold my nose close … sweaty leather. This raises the question, how do you smell it right?

The mango scent is strong and very accurate, but I would liken the scent to unripe mangos more than just mangos. After the initial green mango layer the fragrance mellows out to the light honey smell of oud with some of the green notes leftover for freshness. I love this fragrance so much for the summer.

At first, I thought my predecessor was exaggerating a bit, but no, she is completely right. The scent reminds me of spoiled fruit lying next to fully ripe cheese. For my nose, the fragrance is unbearable, and I also have trouble categorizing it within the Parfumo categories. If someone really wants to wear it, please only in their free time, and only when they are alone or with like-minded people. The season could be winter, but preferably not in a heated room, rather during a snowy walk and below zero degrees. In summer, otherwise, myriads of fruit flies will follow you around. Who might enjoy this is a mystery to me, and apart from sweet and fruity, I don't perceive any other notes. I would be very interested to know what the artist was thinking with this work; he must have a lot of humor.

I love manga, but only the really well-drawn ones. Manga can be more than just cartoons like Heidi, Pokémon, and the like. Nowadays, there are illustrated books, series, and films for every age, even down to pornographic images and films. Alongside the series Ergo Proxy, the two films Ghost in the Shell are among my absolute favorites in this art form. A fragrance with this theme naturally piqued my interest, and I expected something a bit kitschy sweet and primarily synthetic, but not this "scent"! The opening indeed has a somewhat cheesy quality! Where does that come from? Overripe mangoes don’t smell like cheese, and it can’t be oranges either! Manga? Did dear Sailormoon finally take off her plastic boots to let some fresh air to her plastic-wet feet? Who can say for sure? The fruity cheesy foot note fades relatively quickly and reveals the relentless scent of the heart note. The flowers have a somewhat bitter-sweaty quality, and the synthetic hint gradually increases. It’s not that the smell is disgusting; it’s more eerily strange. Do you know the scent of older ladies who are always freshly washed, wear their unwashed synthetic bras for several days, and then spritz on a floral fragrance for shopping? That’s exactly how MM smells in the heart note on my skin. The base also quietly sweats away, and the woods elevate the strange scent impression almost to the bizarre. This Montale is extremely special, and you have to be able to wear it!

Today, I stumbled weakly and under-sugared into the perfume shop, as Docki had summoned me "sober." This even meant forgoing the invigorating morning coffee. So, a reach into the shiny Montale selection felt really good! By chance, I grabbed Mango Manga, and I was amazed by its squeaky colorful cheerfulness. That’s not typical for Montale at all. A whole crate of mangoes rolls towards me, followed by a kilo of oranges. A vitamin boost and a pick-me-up. Happy hour in the perfume store. Jasmine looks through kindly, cooled by neroli. I think of a vitamin drink on ice, decorated with a colorful little umbrella. This Manga tingles pleasantly on the skin - gently cushioned by subtle oud and soft ylang. I don’t notice oakmoss, and the cedar is just a whisper. Overall, a feel-good scent that speaks to me.

Of course, the fragrance pyramid piqued my curiosity, as it often does. And critical comments don't stop me from having my own experiences. Sometimes, that’s exactly what challenges me... :-) So much for that topic. Cheese? Organic waste? Sweaty feet? I'll add a new facet: On my skin, MM developed into an absolute synthetic bubblegum alarm! And it maintained that from the top to the base note with ease. Even desperate glances from my side at the indicated pyramid changed nothing about this scent disaster. Conclusion: I think this is only for young girls...

boooaaaah! At first, you get a basket full of overripe, sweet, mushy, yes, half-rotten mangos thrown into your nose. This is intense! This takes getting used to! Well, over time the cheesy smell that emanates from the oud softens a bit (or you get used to it), but the overripe, sweet mango remains strong.

The scent descriptions were promising and particularly tempting for mango lovers in the hot summer. I was looking for an exotic fragrance experience; a sparkling, slightly sweet refreshment with a certain sultry depth.

... for Mango Manga to smell good on it? There may be people who give the scent a chance, spray it on the test strip after the first sniff, and then don’t immediately run to the next wet spot to rub it off. I am not one of them; after the first whiff on the strip, I just looked at the nice Thai lady questioningly and managed to say, "Do you know this fragrance???

This one did not work for me. Smells like Kouros diluted ten times. It's an inoffensive aquatic with weak lasting power, projection and sillage. The base notes are barely detectable due to excess of calone. Updated January 2014

Convivio opens with a nose tingling blast of bitter grapefruit before slowly transitioning to its heart. As the composition enters its early heart the grapefruit smooths out, but remains as it joins coniferous green, woody cypress with a mild synthetic blonde woody undertone. As the composition moves through the heart phase the cypress becomes the focal note with the grapefruit receding to just noticeable support, as the synthetic blonde woody undertone gains a bit more prominence. During the late dry-down the composition eschews most of its coniferous aspect, leaving the remnants in support of the smoothed out synthetic blonde woody accord with subtle underlying traces of rugged leather through the finish. Projection is average, but longevity excellent at around 15 hours on skin. Convivio starts out with a really nice fresh blast of grapefruit, but that kind of thing has been done many times over. The composition truly starts to distinguish itself from other fresh perfume when the coniferous green, woody cypress takes over in its mid-section. This is also the point where the synthetic blonde woody accord makes itself known. The blonde woods are derived near certainly from cashmeran, an ingredient that usually is a deal breaker as it tends to overpower most compositions. Luckily, in Convivio's case, perfumer Fabrice Pellegrin has done an outstanding job of keeping the cashmeran-derived blonde woods to a very subtle, well-controlled level that supports the cypress surprisingly well. The late dry-down, however, is probably the best part of the composition's development as the cashmeran joins ambroxan to smooth out but also enhance the blonde woods with the remnants of the cypress adding just the right natural smelling woody counter with even a touch of leather detectable late. The composition is far from perfect, and the cypress can be just a bit much as it reaches its peak mid-heart but all-in-all Convivio is a refreshingly light blend of naturals and synthetics in harmony with each other, creating an appealing result. The bottom line is the $190 per 75ml bottle Convivio has its flaws, but is particularly notable in the way it utilizes cashmeran so skillfully that it adds to its appeal, earning it a "very good" 3.5 star out of 5 rating. Certainly recommended smell-wise, but Convivio's full retail price may be a bit of a stretch.

Smells very feminine for me and a little old. It's a bit linear: camphorous opening and dries down to a dry old school type vanilla, actually dry, with a very light vetiver note. Sillage, lasting power and projection are high. Updated January 2014

I have hardly dealt with Montales so far because I find the bottles terrible, and if I don't like the bottles, the scents hardly stand a chance with me. Oh yes, prejudices! The bottles from Montale all look like an atom bomb with a pull cord for the timer, and this one is even black. Creepy! Or the bottles could be the first craft attempts of Wernher von Braun for the V 2. Peenemünde was then bombed by the English, but maybe the idea of the rocket served as inspiration for the bottle designer. Strange inspiration! The scent is surprisingly beautiful and unusual. It starts with a natural and freshly scraped vanilla pod and transitions into a sea of roses. So not Peenemünde, but Rosenmünde and sea fits again. Nevertheless, the base lacks the moist-cool moss note and the earthy smell of patchouli, but the chypre theme is well captured and implemented, with distinct woody notes and a hint of well-placed incense. No sweetness dominates this scent, otherwise the name Chypre would have been overstated, but it has a warm overall note. Well, one can sit by the fireplace in the evening with their personal V 2. Perfect for cool evenings, paired with a good cognac jacket! Cheers!

I have always admired the Montale fragrances on my stepmother - because they suited her perfectly. She was an imposing lady - and somewhat intimidating. That’s why I kept a respectful distance from the fragrances for a long time. I feared I wouldn’t be able to handle this slightly strict elegance. But that is a misconception. Elegance yes - strictness no. Chypre Vanille certainly has a noble demeanor - but it is neither rigid nor pretentious. The midnight blue bottle is lovingly wrapped in a velvet pouch - which suits the fragrance. For I perceive it as blue and elegantly velvety as well. The Tibetan bergamot is softly nestled in a vanilla base - flattering but not sweet. This exquisite blend is gently surrounded by incense and powdered with iris - an exclusive impression - without arrogance. Tonka and sandalwood smoothly bring these valuable ingredients together. I am completely drawn to this chypre vanilla fragrance - and its original composition. Chypre Vanille conveys closeness - without being intrusive. It would have suited my self-confident, yet soft-hearted stepmom well - but it also appeals to my type - feminine and rather girlish. I will gladly wear this exquisite Montale in her honor.

Montale Chypre Vanille was under the Christmas tree for me last night. I hadn’t smelled the fragrance before. And as a true perfume lover, I immediately sprayed a sample on my wrist. I am very surprised by the striking accord. A Montale that comes across as classically beautiful. Like a true diva. Montale is known for having created fragrances that often represent more provocative statements. Not this one. Vanille Chypre is strong in sillage, with an expression of mature, distant elegance. For me, it’s more of a classic. It’s clear that it won’t please everyone, but I really like it. While I was astonished by this fragrance wonder, it’s not a Montale as I know these scents, but fine, noble.....Amazing. A non-sweet vanilla strolls in a fine floral chypre dress. Non-sweet, not the typical vanilla scent. A similarity in elegance to Boucheron is undeniable. Longevity is 10 hours and more. Unisex, but with a feminine touch. Every woman has masculine traits and every man has feminine traits. Well, the Montale bottle is typical, functionally unbeatable, lightweight, not fragile.....But beautiful is different. As a dress, I would say Vanille Chypre would have a warm but present color and a very unique cut.

It was supposed to be just a statement, but the characters are far from enough. I was done with Montale. Too artificial, too biting for my nose, and too strange for my skin chemistry. Then, in a letter while hiking, a sample of Chypre Vanille happened to come my way. Another artificial bomb. And then vanilla. This can't turn out well. I expected a penetratingly sweet baking aroma. What I got was a time travel experience. Bam, back to the late 90s. Where everything was loud and artificial. But also beautiful. Does anyone remember those little children's perfumes that looked like tiny fizzy candy sticks? We had them (me and my friends) in our Advent calendars. (Alternatively, the Hawaii Barbie perfume works too. Had the same DNA?) About the scent itself: The first half hour smells exactly like that children's perfume: Childlike, floral sweet, artificial, retro. However, unlike typical Montale, it is rather flat and not incredibly loud/intrusive. There is no typical Chypre beginning. The fragrance pyramids simply don't allow for it. However, then comes the Chypre-like masterpiece. It becomes unsweetened and angular. Unfortunately, I can't describe it any better. This makes the scent perfect for hot summer days for me. Although it is noted that production has been discontinued, the perfume can still be found at ALZD. Arrival date: soon.

just tested... Rose at the beginning,.....a lot of Rose that you don't know as a top note. #then for me something very strange that I can't describe, smells like Vicks Vaporub which I always got as a child when I had a cold, and now it smells like chewing gum, what were they called again with the tattoos inside???? When a lot of AROMA was still allowed???

So. First: Many thanks to Adan for letting me have this gem at a very, very fair price (originally packaged!). Second: Incredible how the guy stands after 13 years. Fresh as on the first day. Third: 5 photos and no one wants to say a word? Shame on you all. Yes, it was a limited edition for one year, but still. It deserves respect. Well, then I'll do it. So. First: The pyramid is original. It smells like Kouros. Just not quite as extreme. It is supposed to represent the summer version. That's exactly it. Animalic notes significantly toned down, but still present. Just floating, lighter. Less smoke. Instead, subtle (!!!) pleasantly fresh citrus notes. Just for support. No worries to all who can't grasp Kouros because it's too masculine: This summer edition is also not for you. The basic DNA is definitely present. Just a bit more modern, fresher. That's why the title. Sang Bleu (which I also love, but unfortunately is almost empty) is at least 85% similar. Kouros Tonique '08 might be a bit more balanced and fresher. Floating, more summer. Both great if you like this direction. But definitely the same idea. Did Le Galion steal? Let's say politely, they were heavily inspired by all the Toniques when they created Sang Bleu. Which is cool. Better well (!) copied than poorly made ‍️. Perfect, exactly my style. Sad side note: There was a time in the mainstream when YSL summer flanker 138 galaxies were better than the twice as expensive plastic junk they release today. Sad. ‍️ (Y, L'Homme, etc. are not worthy of his name). Just my 2c. PS: My girlfriend LOVES this scent on me ‍️

L'Attimo Eau Florale was described by many reviewers elsewhere as a fresh and light springtime fragrance and a fairly safe choice for a blind purchase. To me, the scent started with an interesting and summery, somewhat exotic mix of yellow florals and a slightly watery fruity sweetness with a remote resembrance to Cabotine Rose. It turned problematic when the florals developed an intensity supported by heavy woody notes (probably the patchouli) that left me wanting for more relief with a breath of lightness or relaxing softness. This would be "freshness" of a more aggressive nature, and not unlike other scents of this type, this fragrance offers well-perceptible projection of an arm's length with a longevity of half a day. In short, I personally would not recommend this as a safe blind purchase candidate for those in search of a more 'rounded' or balanced fragrance without any edges. In a way, I see L'Eau Florale in the same category as Burberry Body: Both seem more appropriate as ambience or amenity fragrances used in impeccable hotel bathrooms with modern and feminine interiors. Therefore, I felt my association confirmed when I found the matching shower gel and body lotion offered as an "ideal enhancement for your luxurious bath time". While the Eau de Toilette could not be worn comfortably, I certainly would enjoy it as scented bodycare.

I like Attimo L'Eau Florale . It's a easy to wear citrus floral . Unfortunately it has a mixed reception from a audience point of view as it is similar to Clinique Happy and I had a co worker who was allergic ( migraines) to Happy . So YMMV. I get the kumquat , peony,rose,a bit of Jasmine and a clean scrubbed patchouli for the most part.

Just a reminder: when I give a bad review, it’s only my personal opinion, and I’m not trying to step on any toes. But I think Aoud Greedy is absolutely vile, and I don’t say that about too many fragrances. I don't get any licorice (this isn’t good because I love the smell of licorice), and it smells like cheap amber. But there’s more..… I wasn’t sure exactly what the problem was, until now. SOMETHING (not sure if the fragrance, chemicals, or both), but something in Aoud Greedy reminds me of a hangover. I don’t make a habit of getting hangovers, but smelling Aoud Greedy is that same feeling/experience, only not quite as bad, but still the same. I cannot imagine anybody wearing and liking this hideous creation.

A fragrance that I really like. I mostly notice the anise notes; the oud is hardly detectable at all. It is very long-lasting and somehow mysterious. Sometimes it feels a bit warm and sweet, sometimes almost sharp. I'm not exactly sure, but it somehow lifts my spirits and is different from other scents I have.

“Ah, you visited our website! Nice!” “Yes… but it did confuse me a bit… this abundance…” “Really? It’s all well organized. But I understand what you mean. Our goal at Montale is, as you know, to represent the entire range of moods and life situations. So it’s great that you came by in person, I’d be happy to show you around! Let’s start right here. Rows 1 to 3 are the Montales for those who got up too early in the morning. And then it splits: Was the shower water cold or warm? Was the toast okay or burnt? Is there a dentist appointment or a date coming up? And so on. Rows 4 to 7…” “Uhhh… O.K., I got the principle!” One question: Why Aoud with an ‘A’?” “Well, that way our creations are quite near the top of every list. And anyone browsing fragrances from A to Z in an online shop might get a bit tired and sluggish with the mouse hand after going through our offerings. You might lose a little bit of the desire to check out the competitors’ products, heh heh. So we prefer to write ‘Aoud’ at the front in case of doubt.” “Even if the scent has nothing to do with it… uh…” “…exactly. What’s the problem? Do you think when you buy ‘Boss Bottled’ you’re getting a bottled boss? And what about ‘Sécrétions Magnifiques’! Do you believe the staff at Etat Libre d'Orange is being milked for that? I beg you!” “Alright, let’s leave that. Let’s focus specifically on this scent here: Aoud Greedy. What’s it about?” “Quite simple:” *sprays on paper strip* “You and your girlfriend just broke up. Not ‘wife’, that’s important for us at Montale, because regarding breakups, in addition to the general variants - Aoud Na-endly to Aoud Inwahrheitunzertrennly - we also have specific additions explicitly for breaking up with a girlfriend: Aoud Undwerzahltnunfürdy to Aoud Diehüttekriegtdieny. So: girlfriend. And you’re now walking through a cozy, late autumn fair to distract yourself. You quickly pass the stand with the caramel candies. Instead, you grab a few whiffs of those lollipops with salmiak in them, you know? You’ve always loved those and you eagerly reach for them. Yes, and the scent that goes with it is just the first part of Aoud Greedy. “Aha…” “But it goes on. Suddenly, from the carousel, an old hit by the Comedian Harmonists sounds, namely ‘Mein kleiner, grüner Kaktus’: You hear the beginning: ‘Flowers in the garden, about twenty kinds, of roses, tulips, and daffodils’…. The other 17 types of flowers remain in the dark in the song. Similarly in the scent. Only they all stay in the dark there.” *sniffs paper strip* “You can save yourself that, young man, you have no chance. We don’t even know what kind of flowers the perfumer mixed in there.” “…” “You turn right at the carousel and - you actually run into your now ex-girlfriend. Immediately you smell that creamy, mild, sweet, delicious scent of her skin that always drove you wild…” “Please stop! That’s… uh… really close to home…” “Ah, I see, you just experienced something like that. Great! How wonderful!!! You should try the scent right away!” *spraysprayspray* *sniffsniffsniff* “Hmm, oh no…” *gulp* “... somehow not really my thing.” “Well, how about Aoud Millivanilly right next to it? There you don’t turn to some undefinable floral scent at the carousel on the right, but to a latently nauseating candy smell at the candy stand on the left and bump into your overly perfumed ex-mother-in-law-to-be…. No? Then here - Aoud Klebrigebrisy: You meet your boss at the cotton candy stand and he’s wearing his nasty Aquatic again. Not that either? Wait, wait, I’ve got one more - Aoud Jetztwirdsheily: You cut yourself on a broken wine glass and Mother Teresa herself disinfects your injury in the medical tent. Still nothing? Well then… too bad…”

Today it was very hot again. It's summer, June! But I didn't want to wear a cologne, no beautiful Elléna scent. I wanted to wear "Bois d' Oud" by Perris Monte Carlo in the heat. Usually, something so bird-like often indicates a migraine for me. But I felt completely comfortable with the oud scent. No migraine followed. So I thought earlier that I could test "Aoud Greedy" again after swimming. Greedy means "greedy." I do not perceive the scent overall or the oud by itself as greedy. I applied "Aoud Greedy" and raised the rating as my first impression. Today I find "Aoud Greedy" to be a bright, beautiful, and rich summer scent. "Aoud Greedy" starts slightly fruity, a bit citrusy, and immediately the typical Montal oud scent is present. Medicinal, bitter, a bit sharp, yet moderate. It could always be that licorice plays a role in creating the oud character of Montal scents, that's my thought or speculation. The bright fruitiness of this scent is not sweet for me. The light citrus scent remains perceptible until the end. Through the licorice, the licorice note gives a slightly sharp and unsweetened sweetness in "Aoud Greedy," perfectly dosed. Who doesn't know the salty licorice, the sharp ones, which we could only buy in the Netherlands before, the salmiak pastilles? We Northern Germans knew them; older generations knew the sweet licorice much less. Moreover, many herbal bitters, herbal liqueurs, and schnapps also contain licorice balm. I smell all of this in "Aoud Greedy," especially the herbal bitter with a bit of liqueur-like fruit sweetness. Licorice is "Lakritz" in English, liqueur comes from "liquor," liquid (a nice, euphemistic understatement). The etymological roots can be smelled here. I cannot distinguish the floral notes from the fruity ones, nor can I identify the other ingredients. However, one should at most be able to do this to some extent when testing a good scent. If you like the scent, in my opinion, you can forget the pyramid, the ingredients, and just remember the overall scent with: Mmmh, I want to wear that now, that's what I need right now. So liqueur-fruity with the bitter oud, slightly resinous, the scent lasts a long time. Anyone who enjoys fruity aromas in scents without "red berry compote with a hint of vanilla," who likes this oud note, has a suitable scent here with "Aoud Greedy" that is at least worth a test. The sillage is moderate, not too expansive. A serious scent; no fear of little girl fruit lollipop scent. Unisex? I wouldn't want to determine that. I find "Aoud Greedy" rather feminine.

Just by looking at the bottle, one could forgive you for thinking that this would be a strong, perhaps spicy or dominating scent. In reality, F by Ferragamo is quite sweet, flowery and feminine. The initial sweetness in the opening certainly took me by surprise. My nose was assaulted with something that smelt like a bag full of lollies. Thankfully this was a scent that I rather enjoyed. Later a peppery, almost spicy note made an appearance, adding an unusual twist and providing a good introduction for the entrance of the orange blossom, jasmine and rose notes. I feared that this fragrance would become quite boring with the presence of such predictable florals, however the scent stayed true to its strange yet unique beginning. I think this fragrance would suit anyone of any age, it has enough versatility to do so. It also could be worn all year round, throughout every season. I urge you all to give F by Ferragamo a try.

I blind bought this one. And it was a fail for me personally. Way too powdery/ sweeeeet violets candy . As described in the title it's like those cheap candy necklaces that look like SweetTarts but taste ( BLech!) . My grandmother loves powdery scents though so I gave it to her for a birthday gift. She liked it and it works well on her. Her other favs are Ombré Rose ,Mary Kay Today , and Lucky # 6 & Lolita Lempicka Fleur Defendue( which I like too) .

Yesterday I was looking for a fragrance for my cousin - one that shouldn't be too overwhelming, but also not overly reserved, as she is an extroverted type. Then the F bottle caught my eye, which admittedly posed a riddle for me. Only the technically skilled husband managed to open the cap with a deft half-turn. But the "trick" was worth it! F envelops me with a distinct sweetness that neither clings nor leans towards the overly sweet. An interesting note with a slight woody touch. The orange blossom gives F transparency, and the jasmine shines brightly through. The rose softly lays over it - also sweet but not sugary. A voluminous scent, yet without heaviness and attractively expressive. The longevity of F is also remarkably good, but not overwhelming. Monsieur K has once again done a great job. If you don’t overdo it, you are surrounded by a sweet - elegant cloud for hours. I think I can score points with this gift.

Like all women, I am of course a shoe fetishist. In this regard, Salvatore Ferragamo is as much a dream for me as it is for any woman. I admit, I could never afford them (unfortunately), even though I once owned 70 pairs of shoes. Salvatore Ferragamo (1898 - 1960) created his first shoes at the age of nine; for his sister on her confirmation. Over the years, he had more influence on shoe fashion than we are aware of today. He worked for film stars like Greta Garbo, Marlene Dietrich, Gloria Swanson, Mary Pickford, developed the ballerina for Audrey Hepburn and the 11cm stiletto for Marilyn Monroe. Thus, not only the classic women's sandal with a heel can be traced back to his creativity, but also the wedge heel he developed as early as the 1940s, which is still a firm part of today's shoe collections. After his death, his daughter took over the company and continues to run it successfully. I only learned that Ferragamo also launched perfumes when I received a mini of the "F" from Ferragamo from Chanelle (thank you very much, Nelly). At first, I thought the bottle, which looks like a lighter, could also hint at a wedge heel. Yesterday, I took the plunge and was very surprised by the result. One thing upfront: it is definitely not a chypre. The opening is extremely strong and sweet-fruity. I perceive it as pineapple, honeydew melon, and peach. What I don't like so much is the extreme sweetness, which fortunately diminishes as it develops. Along with the fruitiness, a fine woodiness is added in the heart note and later on, very subtle and restrained. Throughout, I miss the aforementioned flowers. From the orange, it is more the crushed leaf than the blossom. In the base, a dry powderiness comes in, and only here can I perceive something floral. At this point, "F" reminds me of Rochas' Byzance and holds this note for a long time. Even 24 hours later, and despite several hand washes, I can still perceive the note reminiscent of Byzance. Thus, it is clear: longevity is phenomenal. The sillage, however, is only strong at the beginning, becoming weaker and weaker over time. In the base, the scent is only close to the skin. A lot of noise at the beginning, shameful restraint at the end - I would have preferred it the other way around!

What the F ??? Do you know this Campino candy? Take one with blackcurrant flavor, then you'll know what's going on here. Sweet, artificial, fruity. From start to finish. I can catch a brief impression of rose and orange peel, both giving a very candied vibe. F hardly develops. It gets a bit fizzy. Kind of like the sugar on sour cola bottles from Haribo - but just a little. The scent is very intense, one spray and the whole bathroom smells. However, F also disappears very quickly. So far, I've only caught the scent in the morning in the stairwell when my mom is out of the house. It was fruity and fresh. Very pleasant. Either it develops differently on my skin or I just shouldn't sniff too closely. Overall, I'm disappointed now, still 50%, because it smells so good in the stairwell. Additional info: Somehow, the bottle is supposed to represent a wedge sandal.

I bought a partially used bottle of this fragrance blind on eBay as a cheap addition to another auction. And the first strong spray really shocked me. The scent is extremely sweet and fruity at the start. The syrupy, sticky sweetness takes my breath away. The fragrance doesn’t smell bad, but you really have to like this fruity sweetness.

I actually find it very pleasantly sweet.. I didn't even know that jasmine and orange blossom could be so sweet together. And: Roses are sweet are sweet are sweet, aren't they? Somehow, my nose, which usually doesn't love sweet scents, gets stuck on this fragrance; it is well made and comes from the master Uncle Francis K.

Do you know those fragrances that, upon the first spray, tell you directly: “I’m here, and I’m staying!”? Fantastic Oud is just such a scent. Not a shy whisper, but a bold statement that makes it clear you should pay attention to it now. And to be honest? It deserves my full attention. The opening is intense - really intense. The oud practically leaps out at you, dense and smoky, like a fire on a clear winter night. It is immediately accompanied by a sharp spice, thanks to black pepper and a hint of saffron, which makes the entire composition shimmer luxuriously. It’s as if you receive a mysterious invitation to a room full of stories and secrets. But then... then it gets interesting. After a few minutes on the skin, the fragrance begins to lean back and relax. The initial sharpness slowly fades, and suddenly a velvety rose comes to the forefront. But not a gentle, innocent rose - no, this one is dark, almost velvet red, and enveloped in a smoky leather accord that makes the scent unexpectedly sensual. It’s precisely this balance of hardness and softness that makes “Fantastic Oud” so captivating. And then, after hours, when you think it has said goodbye, there’s still that warm, woody echo. Amber and patchouli blend with the ever-present oud, and the base becomes something that feels like a warm embrace after a cold day. Deep, soothing, but always with that underlying strength. The best part? The fragrance lasts. Whether for a few hours or an entire evening - “Fantastic Oud” has a longevity that impresses. And the sillage? Oh yes, you will leave a trail. But not intrusive, more like someone passing by you thinking: “Wow, who was that?” It’s certainly not for every day and not for every occasion. But if you’re in the mood for something dark, sensual, and absolutely captivating, then this scent might just be the right one. A fragrance that tells stories - and is worth being heard.
