It is clear that fantastic oud is my number 1 among Montale fragrances! Not many Montale fragrances have convinced me, but a few, including fantastic Oud, strike the best compromise. This refers to the resinous scent, which is perfectly balanced by the fruity side! I love this fragrance, similar to my favorite Oud Minerale by TF, which also achieves a perfect balance in an aquatic way. For me, it is an absolute recommendation, especially regarding longevity/sillage and above all the price-performance ratio! It reminds me of beautiful evenings in a relaxed gathering at a bar or simply days that are dreamily lived away!

At first, I didn't get along well with oud fragrances, as I often found the resinous note too biting. However, I cautiously approached this ingredient through milder oud additions. Oud for beginners, so to speak. If we stick to this image, Fantastic Oud is more for advanced users. The opening is already distinctly resinous, but it is softened by the gentle rose. An exquisite combination. The leather is subtly in the background - but the tobacco envelops the fragrance softly and fully. An aromatic peace pipe, from which delicate smoke rings rise. Here, the scent becomes relaxing and alluring for me. Sweet amber pleasantly rounds off this Montale. I can't necessarily endorse "Fantastic" - but harmonious and balanced, definitely. For me, a relaxed oud fragrance - that fits well in winter.

Dreamy long sandy beaches, crystal-clear water, sun-kissed skin... blissful daydreams in the middle of November. Tuscan Soul Punta Ala is dedicated to the eponymous place on the Tyrrhenian coast. A highly exclusive seaside resort, a top-class marina, and a playground for jet-setters. So how does this highly exclusive fragrance smell? Punta Ala opens with a basket full of lemons, not sharp and coming across very naturally here. It continues with an aquatic freshness, and although not listed in the pyramid, a distinctly watery melon note is noticeable. Don't stop reading just because there's melon in it; it doesn't have to be poorly done :-) Punta Ala does not drift into just any summer scent but is supported by vetiver and woods. The melon note remains but is rather subtly detectable. What I miss is the announced note of olive leaf; I would have loved an accord like in the beautiful Fiore d'Ulivo by XerJoff, unfortunately not present. Even after multiple tests, I do not smell this note. Solar accord means nothing to me; if a salty note is meant, it is also missing here. Punta Ala is a bright-refreshing well-made aquatic fragrance. The scent remains pleasantly noticeable on my skin for 5 hours; I can't say how it performs at over 30°C, but I think it will maintain a normal duration of about 4 hours. If I may be completely honest, I still miss the WOW effect; somehow the fragrance lacks a note that makes it special, and above all, I miss the vacation feeling... the salt, the sea, the exclusivity... I can't detect it, what a shame! The next point of criticism is the quite high price. 75ml for a hefty 150 euros seems to me more than "salty" for a summer water. The bottles are beautifully made, high-quality, and elegantly crafted. Here, Signore Ferragamo has shown very good taste... but the content is what really counts!
Big disappointment. Smells much like as Silver Mountain Water, with the same poor longevity. Not worth it. Bad job Mr. Pierre. Updated January 2014

The vetiver is definitely distinguished with the particularly bitter, not disgusting smell ... It is also a bit citrus with bergamot and lime to give battles over who will dominate! You can feel in the background its wooden aura without being superior to the vetiver though!

I was speculating on a Montale and had several creations in the running, which then narrowed down to three contenders. If my husband is my companion, he confidently points to a bottle and declares unequivocally: This one. If my father is present, he says: Take all three. Men are decisive - and want to "get it done." If my friend is there, she says: Spray all three - and we'll stroll for another hour. A time-consuming, but safe option. So we strolled through the city with my three favorites Mango Manga, Powder Flowers, and Boise Fruite. All three scents seemed suitable at first - but unfortunately, the Manga suddenly turned musty and the Powder Flowers transformed into soap bubbles. Only the Boise changed little, remaining pleasantly woody-fruity on my skin, and faithfully fulfilling its title. No surprises - but also no unpleasant ones. The woody, forest-like scent receives a bitter fruitiness from Petitgrain, reminiscent of the coolness of Neroli. A sense of calm emanates from the fragrance. Perhaps a bit of forest tranquility. The lime is citrusy fresh, but not sour. Vetiver is the loose forest floor on which the delicately bitter violet thrives. Sandalwood embraces, and a note of eucalyptus wafts above. This final chord was truly a surprise - but a welcome one. For me, the winner was now clear. Boise Fruite is what it seems to be. I appreciate this honest attitude - not just in fragrances.

I have also tested a few Oud-foreign Montale fragrances like Sandflowers, but still, when you think of Montale, you first think of the Oud-rose combos. This is probably also because most fragrances in other directions tend to come off as experimental and somewhat piercingly clumsy. Except for Chocolate Greedy, that one is a real gem. Where does Bois Fruite stand in the internal Montale ranking? Pretty much in the middle - it has interesting and unique aspects, but also sides that induce migraines and come off as simply piercing and rotten. Piercing, metallic, sterile, caustic, medicinal, woody, crushed, slightly rotten fruits, sparkling citrus cocktail, vetiver grass, and distorted wood. Here, almost everything is distorted and upside down. It even has a slightly salty-sea note. But I find it somehow toxic green, biting, and aggressive - definitely a scent that wants to be in the spotlight and makes you curious to smell and wait for how it develops and becomes calmer and more balsamic. I think it gets more beautiful but also less special. Bottle: I think a green tone would have suited this strange wooden fruit bowl better. Sillage: Montale never holds back here - I’m curious about their musk fragrances. Longevity: 8 hours even under the most adverse conditions and during sports! A completely different fruit scent that partly reminds me of the piercing Creed style. But it’s precisely the synthetic-scratchy prick note that fascinates and simultaneously repels. It’s not particularly beautiful, but definitely a different approach and a fragrance that urges you to smell at your wrist, then you wrinkle your nose... but then you quickly smell it again. Fascinating, even if it’s not one of the best from the brand.

Although I don't like woody and fruity scents at all, this fragrance fascinates me greatly. Yes, it has something. Somehow, I can't take the fragrance pyramid entirely seriously. According to that, I shouldn't like this scent. Boisé Fruité starts immediately with very fruity and woody notes. But there is something else that makes this fragrance so pleasant. Something sweet and balsamic appears, which I can't identify. The top note reminds me a bit of Caipirinha, so sweetened limes, but the scent is by no means sugary. Later, a slightly bitter note comes in, which blends beautifully with the sweetness to create a wonderful harmony. I can confirm a delicate medicinal note, but it doesn't bother me at all; rather, it integrates very nicely. I am truly impressed and amazed at myself.

"I rather like this fragrance" - Missk wrote this totally appropriate expression. INCANTO BLISS is a young, nice, delightful scent - at the beginning. Emits more intensive apple fragrance than Nina Ricci creations, shows almost the best face of fruits. Sadly, the flowers of the head must be too expensive, so the perfume skips this step and jumps to the stifling base, well known from noname synthetic "perfumes", turns out so indistinguishable, that if I do not note, what is on my skin, I forget it and can not identify. No problem with endurance or sillage, but it is not outstanding, so INCANTO BLISS got totally neutral vote from me.

Salvatore Ferragamo INCANTO BLISS is a shiny happy tonic of a perfume, although it is neither very citrus, nor very aromatic. Every time I put it on (usually when dashing out the door), I feel momentarily uplifted. It's bright, cheery, optimistic, sociable—basically the antithesis of thick, heavy, dark and pensive chypre perfumes. This a fragrance which I regard as more or less interchangeable—in terms of timbre, tone, and mood—with Ellen Tracy TRACY. Although they are definitely distinct compositions (with completely different notes), they serve precisely the same purpose and offer similar effects. Neither is overly sweet; neither is suffocatingly floral. All things considered, TRACY has a bit more overall perfumic integrity, it seems to me. INCANTO BLISS can be perhaps usefully compared to a selective serotonin re-uptake inhibitor (SSRI). On the one hand, it temporarily blocks the capacity for brooding. On the other hand, it is impossible to enter into a deep relationship with such a fragrance. The momentary bliss which it seems to provide proves fairly swiftly to have been an illusion: shortlived and superficial. Had I written this review under the influence, I would surely have given it four stars. (No need to worry: there are no guns around.)

I rather like this fragrance. In my opinion it smells quite tropical and fresh. I love the fruity blend of apple, yuzu and kumquat in Incanto Bliss. This combination is in no way sharp or sour, it is beautifully soft and feminine. The freesia, rose and lotus notes only compliment the scent and don't clash too loudly with the dominant fruity notes. They all come together in perfect harmony. This is by far my favourite fragrance from the Incanto line. It's different while still being pleasant and easy to wear. In my humble opinion, this isn't your typical fruity floral, it has that certain something that makes you step back and say, "that's new and exciting". The lasting strength for Incanto Bliss is surprisingly good. It held on my skin for well over six hours which is rare because fruit-based fragrances hardly last on me, let alone smell good. I give Incanto Bliss my thumbs up.

A very good friend says that it’s just me... she thinks I smell unique! Not her, only me... very sweet :) I first won it very cheaply on eBay (one could say it was a bargain) just because of the bottle and the price :) But it smelled very good! I finished it right away :) Then for my birthday, my friend gave me a new one with 100 ml! And suddenly I can't finish it anymore. I can hardly smell it on me! It merges with me, so I don't know if it's still there or has vanished. I only notice it's still there from the compliments. The perfume develops a lot! It adapts and smells different on everyone!

Well, this one was one of my biggest mistakes. One day, while I was on my way to work, my favorite perfume shop was being redecorated, and I saw this beautiful bottle. Since I am also a bottle collector, that hunter and gatherer instinct kicked in. I just had to have it. There’s a new beautiful version of it every year. So I had it sprayed on and found, or rather wanted to find, it quite nice. It smelled somehow fresh and pleasant. When I proudly walked into the office with my acquisition and had to keep sniffing my wrist along the way, it became clear to me, at the latest in the office, that it would not be my favorite scent. Don’t ask me why I didn’t return it. Maybe I wanted to give it a fair chance. But we just didn’t become friends. I can’t really describe what it smelled like. Somehow fresh and floral. But there was something in it that I didn’t like, which made it smell cheap. I don’t want to come off as arrogant, but some perfumes in the 10-15 Euro range from the drugstore smell better. I even have one for 4.95 Euros that smells great compared to this. But I am still glad that I have the beautiful bottle.

... take time. I bought Incanto Bliss because of the beautiful bottle. But the first spray didn’t impress me, and I set it aside. However, today, months later, I tried it again - and I really like it. The apple-kumquat opening is refreshing and pleasant. And now, after a while, the freesia and rose have developed as well, making the fragrance fine and bright.

Montale's Wild Aoud was a gift from the friend who initially piqued my interest in wearing Oud in the first place. The promotional blurb for this fragrance on the website reads as follows: "A smoky and diffusing character for this wild and noble Aoud combined with Teakwood, Patchouli from Sumatra and Tobacco, enveloped with Amber under a brilliant and piquant heart of Artemisia, Geranium from Egypt and Bergamot from Italy." Wild Aoud begins with a shot of candied sweetness, summery citrus and (even though this note is not listed) candied Rose petals! The Oud here is a late arrival and is definitely not of the overly medicinal variety ... finally slightly subdued by resiny woods. I only get a hint of the listed Tobacco in the drydown and the Patchouli is still hiding somewhere, but that's neither here nor there. Wild Aoud is a 'summery' Montale ... something that at the beginning of my now lengthy fascination with this note I would never have expected to find. Being the 'note du jour' that it has become, I'll go out on a ledge here and say that if one truly wants to experience Oud the way it should be handled, there are no better than the fragrances made by the people at House Montale. I can only conclude that the Geranium listed here is responsible for the 'candied Rose' aspects of this fragrance, more than likely by the addition of aroma chemical Geraniol to the mix, with it's diffusive Rosy attributes. I cannot confirm this, however ... my bottles list only Alcohol Denat, Fragrance and Eau as ingredients. Geraniol does, however, find it's way into most fragrances available today ... just turn the box over and take a look :). Apparently people with fragrance allergies should avoid this chemical ... well, good luck with that!! I also really love the fact that Montale fragrances come with a usage warning on the package. I wonder if this circumvents the draconian IFRA regulations in the EU to some extent? If so ... I find myself adoring Pierre Montale even more ... real person or not :). All told, Wild Aoud can be considered a gateway into the wonderful world of Oud. There have been reports of ghastly batch reformulations of late so I would try to find an older bottle ... but that being as it may, this remains one of my favorite Aoud's by Montale.

This fragrance opens with an accord that smells of roasted nuts; the aoud note, which is usually very strong, is not yet dominating the fragrance at this point. This soon changes when the aoud note fully blossoms and releases its typical pungent, medicinal smell. The fragrance then needs a while to find its balance, but eventually turns into a beautiful woody and nutty aoud fragrance with a patchouli base. Initially, the patchouli can be smelled only very close to the skin; later on, during the dry down, it gets more intense. This offering by Montale has a darker feel to it than the golden-glowing Steam Aoud. Lasts for more than 6 hours on my skin.

In the meantime, I can generally distinguish two groups of Oud fragrances at Montale. One part of the fragrances continuously varies and interprets the classic Arabic combination of rose and oud. The other part of the Montale Oud fragrances, on the other hand, tries to combine oud with well-known other fragrance directions. Aoud Forest and Sliver Aoud particularly come to mind here. Wild Aoud also belongs to this second group. I find Wild Aoud very amusing, as a kind of typical designer men's fragrance has actually been created here, into which oud has been added. Everything is there that belongs to a typical designer men's fragrance - a synthetic citrus freshness in the top notes, even a bit of scratchiness reminiscent of cheap ingredients, and I believe I can perceive light, bright, and indistinct spicy notes, some creaky wood, and indefinable ethereal notes. And then, of course, oud. However, it must be said with pleasure that Montale has not particularly succeeded in this experiment. They simply did not manage to recreate the typical designer scent; they only imitated it. Mr. Montale probably lacked the knowledge of how to do something like this. Everything reminds one of one of those chic designer fragrances, and yet it is also not quite that. Despite all efforts, everything feels high-quality and noble; why, I do not know. It's like currywurst on Meissen porcelain! Development aid for Douglas victims! Well, why not?

I have now gotten to know Montale a little. Typical of their scent developments in the Oud theme... the first 1 to 2 hours are unusual and can initially come across as quite unappealing to the wearer. It's no different with "Wild Aoud". "Wild Aoud" hits you with an intense sweetness, with patchouli and amber dominating so heavily that I feel almost compelled to scrub this Montale off. After 40 minutes, a bit of woodiness comes in, but that sweetness still dominates. I can't really warm up to it at all. But well, as with the Montale that is in my collection, one probably has to wait a while until the full beauty unfolds. Just like here... after about 1 hour, a balance is established, Oud and sweetness are well balanced. Still, I have a certain association towards chewing gum with a fruity aroma. It has something, but the real wow effect just doesn't emerge here. Only when the Oud has fully revealed its splendor is it good again. However, I don't quite like the whole foreplay. I believe that this time it will remain a test. I won't rate the sillage, but I think it will be decent; however, my sample was only in the vial. Longevity is top as always.

Also here a thank you to trueBlood for the sample. Wow, this is something quite cumbersome! Somehow I feel like I sprayed two contradictory scents on top of each other. The top note splits into a sweet, almost honey-like note and on the other hand into a herbal-bitter note. This smell reminds me of Ludwigshafen am Rhein, when BASF had once again blown an experiment into the air. With the heart note, a few floral accords buzz around and intensify the chemical backflash even more. Summer evening in Chemocity! In my mind's eye, memories of long-forgotten situations awaken. The scent seems quite okay from a distance. But directly on the skin, this olfactory antagonism fascinates yet simultaneously repels. The base ultimately leaves me feeling somewhat reconciled. Wild Aoud has eventually chosen the woody-sweet side. But something still bothers me! I believe it is this impression that the scent has retained a strange accord on the skin. As we like to say in my hometown when something can't really convince. It feels distant from afar! Not bad, but not for me!

it really hits hard! I caught a bit too much and thought it would blow my head off. After a short time, however, it all balances out and becomes an interesting, not unpleasant, play of oud, patchouli, and amber. Suddenly, the lion laughs at you from the mirror:-0 and tells you: You are it!!! Masculine to the power of two, turning any room into a predator's cage.

July 1983 - listening to the radio as always… Gimme Gimme - Gimme just a little smile - that’s all I ask of you… a huge hit that summer. Laid Back with Sunshine Reggae. I am not sure how many times during the day i was able to listen to it after being lucky and recording it on tape. That tape later suffered the ‘popular song tape’ death. 2012 - Parisienne L’Eau is born. It instantly reminds me of that summer. Is it the berries? The rose? I do not know. But this is a scent that plays Sunshine Reggae in my head when I spray. Magic… 326/365

Its a great combination of sandalwood, roses and a little bit of oud. In my opinion the fresh roses dominates this fragrance from the beginning to the end. Very warm and comforting scent. For me it's unisex. Lasting power is weaker than other releases, but it's very good though. Updated January 2014

Montale ATTAR is such a compellingly beautiful perfume to my nose, and yet it features a small number of focal notes: sandalwood, oud, and rose. How can it be so gorgeous? Because the sandalwood, the oud, and the rose used are top notch. This is an excellent example of the quality ingredients strain of haute niche perfumery. Instead of attaching a bunch of bells and whistles and curlicues, Pierre--or reasonable facsimile--simply presents these notes in all of their glory. I really love this Montale creation, the rose dominates the perfume but is deepened by the sandalwood and the measured dose of oud. (I agree with Aromi, see below, that sometimes oud-rich perfumes are a bit much...) There is a dark, mysterious feeling to this creation, with an almost animalic quality close to ambergris in the background, it seems to me. There is also a graininess to the texture which I find quite appealing. It is as though the rose petals were shredded and blended to form an oud-sandalwood-amalgam. So, yes, this creation seems fairly linear to my nose. But that's fine with me, because it smells so good that I don't want it to change. I love a few of the Montale rose perfumes, but this one is at the top of my wishlist!

Far away from any modern hectic "living world" in big cities, there is a forest known as the "Dark One of Secrets," which can only be entered by those who know a certain password. Others, who despite several warnings still attempt to enter without the magic word, are said to be transformed into trees according to legend. And indeed, there are the strangest wooden figures you can imagine. A "Lady with a Fur Hat," for example, who raises her arms high, or the "Old Man," whose bearded face is "engraved" in an oak. And there is often a ghostly rustling in the underbrush. No animal of the forest is known to cause this sound. Someone who had entered this forest "legally" once let something slip. It is said to be a rose bush that grows in spurts, reaching up to the highest treetops. Its giant flowers are said to have the diameter of a giant's hand. And every time the roses bloom, a "wooded one" would be freed. He or she often reappears after years, remembering only a scent that dominated their "world": the scent of roses and ancient wood..... Yet no one ever missed a "stolen time"... life continued there where it last was..... Strange? But that is how it was conveyed to me.

I promise, this time I'll keep it short: Montale's Attar flirts, at least according to the scent descriptions, with a traditional Indian Attar made from sandalwood and rose petals. It's actually one of the simplest recipes for a fragrance; the special thing about it is that the powdered sandalwood is distilled together with the rose petals. You can also easily make an Attar yourself by mixing essential rose oil (possibly from various origins, such as India, Morocco, Bulgaria) with real white sandalwood oil (santalum album), preferably from Mysore. You end up with a beautiful fragrance for both genders! This Attar is primarily full-on rose essence, but it seems to me that it doesn't aim to be natural at all. I absolutely don't mind if the intrinsic brilliance of rose oil is extended and/or supported with a bit of chemistry in a well-made perfume (depending on the direction the rose should take, whether leaning towards 'soapy', 'powdery', or 'citrusy', there are suitable fragrance components for everything), but with Attar, this has gone quite wrong. I can also only refer to the hairspray note noted by other testers of Montale fragrances, which I find absolutely unpleasant. This rose has nothing fresh about it, no sparkling acidity like Moroccan rose, and also lacks the opulence and softness of a Turkish rose. Sandalwood is not noticeable to my nose at any moment during the scent's development, hairspray until the end and at best just a hint of musk... Too little for a house that prides itself on specializing in oriental fragrances. This Montale has clearly failed for me!

Smelled this on a 50-ish lady standing next to me at a concert. She was lovely and elegant, and when I asked her what she was wearing she told me it had "an Italian name, something like Ferrari, with a yellow ribbon." Her sister had gifted it to her years ago and the bottle was so old, she couldn't read the label. Anyway, I rarely give any compliments to perfumes because there aren't many people around me who regularly wear one, so I grabbed this opportunity and told the lady I liked her perfume. It is a basic perfume and perhaps not signature-worthy, but not every perfume has to be complex. It's office-safe, and easily wearable throughout the day and year.

Sugary sweet, but rather gentle. Moderate initial cloud – could be felt an arm's length away at first, but settled close to my skin in about ~2 hours. Technically fruity, yes, but also not really. Green pear and bergamot dissipated from me pretty much immediately. Plum stayed – subdued, pretty, jammy. I could feel faint hints of rose if I concentrated on it... And none of it mattered. All of the notes came together, intermixed and made me smell like frosted flakes. So, uh, great color choice for the bottle! No, but really. It lasted around ~4 hours, getting softer and airier as time went on, but throughout the whole time I smelled like frosted flakes. Elevated, perhaps. The kind that would cost you 250$ at a Michelin star restaurant for a tiny plate. Handmade from start to finish, delightfully crunchy, plated in a quirky way with a variety of additional jam toppings you're not sure how to approach... But still. I tested it later on my partner to make sure it wasn't just my skin being weird. Nope. Pear and bergamot clung to him a little longer; the overall composition was a bit more fresh and airy and took ~5 hours in total to fade away; but it still came together and formed a consistent and delightful cloud of frosted flakes. I don't have much of a sweet tooth, but this was genuinely adorable. Cutest gourmand I've tried so far. Playful and light-hearted. 7/10.

If there’s anything I love more than a great oriental, it’s a wonderful Jasmine perfume, this one especially. In my Jasmine Sniff Fest (see my blog), Montale’s Jasmin Full won against enthralling finalists: Serge Lutens A La Nuit, Creed’s Jasmin Imperatrice Eugenie, Demeter’s Jasmine, Diptyque’s Olene, Odalisque by Nicolai, La Route d’Emeraude, Magnetic Scent Untitled # 1 and Enlevement au Serail by MDCI — each so glorious I bought them all. Yet even among these beauties, Jasmin Full stands out. It is a true Jasmin Soliflore, brightened by honeysuckle, sweetened by orange blossom. Somehow these two make the Jasmin more itself. I’m sure it’s Jasmine Sambac, rather than the Grandiflora, because I don’t smell the Grandiflora's treasured animalic stank. When to wear it? When life lets you down, or up. In the summer, in the spring. While drinking champagne. To this Jasmine-lover, Montale Jasmin Full is the next best thing to being in a Sambac Jasmine field at dawn.

Thats sweet jasmin touched by orange flowers. Kind of a linear scent, without big evolution through drydown. Great sillage, great projection and lasting power (about 10 hours easily). Most suitable to women and for colder months. Worth a try for who likes florals. Updated January 2014

The King of Flowers has made his entrance! And on my skin, what a voluptuously magnificent entrance it is! This is heady and potent stuff! Richly luscious white floral heaven for those who seek it! A hint of orange blossom peeking out for just the barest tad of soapy freshness. A middling dose of honeysuckle twining through the blend to add a whiff of spicy complexity. That being said, I am amused statements I have heard from some others about it smelling like jasmine “oils”. The natural scent is almost never extracted by enfleurage anymore. There is generally speaking, only jasmine absolute of various types. And yes of course this soliflore will smell similar to them, that IS the whole point of a soliflore is it not? That is why Montale names it JASMINE FULL no? And what kind of jasmine absolute are we referring to anyway? Jasmine grandiflorum, Jasmine sambac, Jasmine auriculatum…? They all smell different and are all made in absolute of varying batch qualities with a nice dose of indoles included. null that I have smelled are anywhere near being an identical substitute for this Montale beauty. I smell that Montale has made this a complex mixture of various jasmine absolute accords with the nasty indoles deleted, and created a jasmine soliflore par excellence. In comparison to other jasmine soliflores, this one rules over them all by far on my skin. This perfume is a jasmine soliflore done at its best. No added sickening sweetness beyond that which is held within the plants themselves. No gourmand excess. No overweighted woody or resinous base to obscure the pure floral splendor. And yes, it is a synthetic (hedione- methyl dihydrojasmonate) jasmine. No nasty fecal indoles to mar the splendor and the perfect balance of this creation. Sometimes synthetic is far better. Amen. The list of superlatives I could heap upon this work of art is endless, and on my skin and to my nose they would all be the god honest truth. Opulent, profoundly floral, sumptuously elegant, luxurious, sensuous, splendid…..I could go on and on. This brings to mind a Tang Dynasty Chinese Empress lounging about in her garden dressed in layers of lavishly embroidered silks, enjoying the summer breeze that is wafting the fragrant waves of freshly blossoming jasmine and honeysuckle vines over her as she smiles, closes her eyes, and inhales deeply. Montale has fashioned a tour de force of a jasmine soliflore perfume here, and I am completely enchanted. For what this white floral masterpiece is, and for what it achieves on my skin, it is well worth the price to me. Bravo and thank you Pierre Montale.

In this jasmin soliflor, Montale toned down the flower's fruitiness and almost completely stripped its animalic characteristics. This could have turned out quite a dull sterile scent - and honestly, that is what I expected from this Montale. But in all fairness, the outcome is quite lovely. Sure, it is a straightforward white floral without much development, but the jasmin here is as genuine as it gets: fruity, sweet, blossomy, dusty, stale, wilted. It is all there and it is all kept very much under control, unlike the wonderfully schizofrene Sarrasins or the travesty in Lush Lust. A decent, friendly version where the beauty lies in its simplicity. Remarkable.

I am baffled by the middling ratings which Montale JASMIN FULL has garnered here at Parfumo and also the strangely inconsistent reviews I've seen here and there. I'm wondering whether there may be batch issues. Or perhaps some bad samples are circulating about? Otherwise, I do not understand how this simple but compelling creation could receive anything but praise: it's jasmine! Big, thick, yes, full jasmine! This composition is very close to Molinard Jasmin--both have a bit of orange blossom thrown in for good measure. Both are gorgeous. So anyone who's on a budget needs to look into the Molinard. Perhaps people find this soliflore too straightforward to warrant a high niche price? I did see a review claiming that this is indistinguishable from far less expensive jasmine essential oil, so I suppose that might be why it has received such low ratings. Or are there jasmine haters out there rating jasmine soliflores? I suppose that such persons would bring the ratings down, but why bother sniffing a perfume named JASMIN FULL, if you are not ready to commit 100% to jasmine? I ask most sincerely. Well, I for one am ready to commit. Sign me up. It's official: jasmine is one of my favorite flowers. This composition is so voluptuously wonderful that I am lost in a cloud of jasmine. Rose? Who needs rose? That's how drunken I am on this intoxicating perfume.

I am sorry but this is just nasty. It opens with just Jasmin and it's quite nice. Then more white florals join and it is too thick for me. Then about an hour or less it starts stinking (body odor/animal stuff?). Then, and it hasn't even been on for two hours it turns indolic/mothball like with a hint of jasmine way in the back. It is a silage monster.

This is very pretty but contrary to the name it is not primarily a jasmine fragrance, though jasmine is the main note. It also has a lovely fresh honeysuckle opening and a sweet orange blossom that becomes much more pronounced on the dry down, almost wearing at times more like an orange blossom fragrance than a jasmine one.

I ordered a sample of ALZD because I wanted to sniff through the Montale fragrances. I would have liked to have spared myself this sample. My first thought when I smelled the fragrance was "old flowers." It smelled very sharp to me, like old flowers or stale flower water. I washed it off after just a few minutes, as my nose couldn't handle it at all.

What a truly hefty, indolic jasmine! Just one spray sent my colleagues at work fleeing - the scent was literally perceived as a "slap in the face." This once again shows that an intense jasmine fragrance is really not for everyone. For me, this is a mono fragrance - all other notes are mercilessly overwhelmed from the very start and stand no chance.

You receive a bouquet of flowers, fill it with fresh water, and let the flowers beautifully stand out in your home. The first petals fall off & the bouquet no longer looks good, you decide to throw it away. You shake off the slightly brownish flower water and take a small sniff from the vase. This is roughly how one can imagine the Jasmin Full by Montale.

The Incanto series have always been a hit or a miss with me. I didn't mind Incanto Bliss and Incanto Shine with their sweet and clean fruity accords best suited for Summer wear, but Incanto Bloom is different, it goes down a more floral path. I enjoyed the top notes, which to my nose smelt like a delicious blend of soapy freesia, powdery pink rose petals and strawberry jam. It was a very enticing scent to say the least. I really liked what I smelt and even applied it to my skin on a few separate occasions. On both my skin and the card the top notes really shone. I was evidently impressed by its delicacy and subtlety. Unfortunately as the fragrance progressed, the scent became blander and much soapier. At this point my opinions regarding Incanto Bloom began to go downhill. It was by no means unpleasant, but I found the heart and base rather generic. It was mostly soap and musk to my nose, sort of like the scent of a clean yet unventilated bathroom. In fact the musky base was not far from comparison to Narciso Rodriguez for Her. I must compliment the lasting strength which was incredibly good even though the scent didn't manage to captivate me for as long. The sillage was also commendable with a nice projection. All in all it's a likable scent, yet one that perhaps needs more personality to grab my attention.

Salvatore Ferragamo INCANTO BLOOM is a gentle grapefruit-floral fragrance with a balance of sweetness and tartness in the opening, which gives way finally to a light florality. Freesia seems to me to be the dominant floral, but there is also a touch of rose. I do not detect champaca in this composition, which is usually unmistakeable to my nose, so maybe here there is only a tiny dose. This is the second INCANTO flanker that I've found to be more appealing than the peach-heavy original, which reminds me a bit too much of TRESOR and TUSCANY PER DONNA, while seeming rather pale in comparison to either of those iconic creations. BLOOM, like BLISS, falls squarely within the office-ready inoffensive fruity-floral fragrance (ORIFFF) category. But somehow I like them nonetheless.

Incanto Bloom smells, as the name suggests, predominantly floral. With quite sweet flowers. I couldn't pick out individual notes, but there is a distinct fruity note, even though no fruit is listed in the top notes (Champaca is a Southeast Asian species of magnolia, as I discovered through Google). The wood remains subtly in the background, and the musk only becomes noticeably perceptible towards the base. Overall, this is a pleasant, wearable floral scent, solid mainstream from 2010, but not a fragrance that I feel I must have urgently.

Recently at Karstadt, a handsome young man approached me - with clear intentions. He held a bottle in his hand and offered me a spray. Incanto Bloom. Mmm, a sweet magnolia scent brushed against my inclined nose. Freesia and cashmere wood made the fragrance even more enticing. Along with the old-fashioned rose - a hit to my olfactory and romantic center. And later, a pleasantly delicious gummy bear scent crept into the composition, which didn't disturb at all, but rather brought back childhood days. Children's birthday in a blooming garden. Beautiful memories. No question, the fragrance had to come with me.
the perfume is floral, not a watery scent like Escada but still soft and unobtrusive. It is pleasant, subtle, without any significant recognizability. A fragrance for everyday wear or for the office.

Yes, I know, silly title, but it's true :D Rose Night was a blind buy. I was once again looking for a rose scent without much fuss, and this one caught my attention. My first Montale! When it arrived about a month ago, I was quite excited as I unpacked it. Well, there's no need to talk about Montale bottles, as they say here in the green sauce city ;) It's a matter of taste; I don't like them all either. But I must say that I quite like the bottle due to the color combination. So here we go. Sprayed on Rose Night and spent the day with it. Summary: Rose -> Yes, and very artificial. No juicy, full rose. No, quite synthetic (but not bad) Patchouli -> a hint Amber -> towards the end, just before it fades away Musk -> Nope Longevity and sillage -> insane, lasts easily 10-12 hours and wafts back to your nose repeatedly. It doesn't go through much development. The rose is dominant and becomes sweeter towards the end and maybe a bit "realer" as the synthetic notes fade a bit. As I mentioned in my statement, Rose Night is not really oriental for me. A bit disappointed, it first went to the shelf with its other colleagues and was skillfully ignored. Two weeks ago, my partner and I vacationed on a beautiful island in Greece. Naturally, the question arose: Which perfume should I take with me? Actually totally silly. According to the weather... 30-34 degrees, not a single cloud in the sky, hotel right by the sea, which idiot wears perfume there? Well, me, maybe for the evening if we go out to eat or drink... Did I do it? Yes. Twice in 10 days :D Thus, Rose Night enjoyed its existence in Greece in the bathroom there and was occasionally misused as a room spray... Until the last day. I wore Rose Night and we went to watch the sunset at the beach one last time. With a bottle of champagne in tow. We watched the ships sail into the evening glow and decided to go for a cocktail at a very nice bar afterwards. Our last evening went by way too quickly, and the next morning the alarm rang. We could only have a quick breakfast because soon the transfer bus would pick us up and take us to the airport. I suggested we quickly go to the beach and say goodbye to the sea (Yes, I know it sounds silly). This time at sunrise. As we stood there, my sweetheart hugged me and promised that we would come back soon and that I should please wear this beautiful perfume again next time... It would always remind him of the island and me.. ;(

With Montale's fragrances, I always approach with caution, as you never know what might hit you... I approached Rose Night with the same caution... One spray is enough... I perceive a slightly citrus note, which is not listed here, but somehow I still notice it...? Immediately, the rose comes in... As "Seerose" has beautifully described, it is a typical "Montale rose"... (However, I personally cannot crystallize out the Aoud, as you write, Seerose)... To me, it smells slightly synthetic, yet authentic and clear... A very mature and proud, dark red rose... Patchouli and Amra remain strongly in the background for me... but musk comes through nicely... All in all, a great Montale musk rose with a powerful presence and excellent longevity :) Thumbs up :)

In my opinion, it is not surprising that no one has yet commented on "Rose Night" by Montale. Imagine if we had never smelled any other rose or oud fragrances individually, neither in perfumes nor in nature, except for Montale scents? We might assume that this typical Montale scent is a unique fragrance plant or note, perhaps even a fragrant resin, namely: "Montale OudRose" I applied "Rose Night" and noted: For a moment, something citrusy flies by, then follows a sweaty, medicinal note. And as is typical in many Montale fragrances, inevitably trailing behind is a hybrid rose, the Montale Oudrose. I quite like that. But why are there so many clones of this at Montale? Although no oud is listed, I can smell it without a doubt. Patchouli plays an unnoticeable role. There could also be peonies and synthetic rose geranium involved. Because the initially very dense scent becomes a bit lighter, slightly floral, powdery, although I find "Rose Night" a bit too sweet and overwhelming. I taste it with a certain soapiness on my tongue. There is room for speculation here, as we all perceive scents very differently. However, for me, the symbiosis of "RoseOud" remains dominant, accompanied by a metallic accord and a somewhat synthetic moderate human body sweat scent note. For everyday use, I find "Rose Night" a bit too intense. Longevity and sillage are quite satisfactory. Unisex? A definite: I don't know!

My first review and the first review for this fragrance. First of all, I want to thank everyone for this wonderful platform that gives a stage to my new passion in life! Now to Ferragamo Red Leather ... right from the start: as wonderful as it begins, it fades just as quickly. Unfortunately! Because what greets me in the opening delights my heart. A bath in summer-fresh lemon lemonade in fine leather underwear. This scene is framed by floral impressions that know how to fit in well, but appear somewhat undefined, which does not detract from the first impression. Unfortunately, this opening fades, and with it, the leather underwear very quickly. The refreshing sensuality is completely pushed into the background in less than an hour in favor of the vetiver, which enjoys itself centrally with the violets as the fragrance develops. No question, still a pleasure... but together with the leather, it would have been a true delight and would have done justice to both the name and the bottle. So, one is left a bit wistful, trying to navigate through the botanicals. This too is quickly abandoned. The longevity is very moderate for me. The fragrance becomes relatively close to the skin and retreats to a soft herbal caramel within 3-4 hours. Pleasant. But I would have liked more.

Montale Oud Edition is a 2021 release that’s a very pleasant take on oud/rose/leather concept that Montale and Mancera have produced—arguably, to excess—in a very large catalogue that includes many scents that arguably fit this profile. It immediately strikes me as a smoother, more rounded out take on a couple of recent favorites of mine, both 2019 offerings, Mancera Precious Oud and Montale Oud Dream. Oud Edition is a bit safer than both, frankly, without the booze of Precious Oud or some of the sharper edge of Oud Dream, and it’s not over-the-top rosy, so it’s a really nice introductory option for this type of fragrance. It’s also less sharp and heady than Montale Red Aoud, Black Aoud, or White Aoud. Overall, I think this fragrance is great, but it’s simply a bit redundant with other options I love, but I’d encourage others to check it out if it seems interesting. It performs well, has a great balance of notes without any individual accord taking over, and is a great example of what this brand does so well—smooth ouds with rose and sometimes leather (as in this case), saffron, other resins, etc. I obtained my sample from Olfactif (at the standard $170 for 100ml pricing), an official retailer, and there are other official retailers/boutiques in the US like Krystal Fragrance, and it’s sold on the secondary market as well via FragranceNet. 8 out of 10

In my eyes, this is an honest, direct, and straightforward oud fragrance. The rose component manages to lighten the heavy scent a bit, but in my opinion, there was a conscious decision to avoid making the fragrance more appealing with additional rose or fruity components. This fragrance has character; you have to want to wear it, it’s definitely not a crowd-pleaser, as it is too unplayful for that. On the skin, it becomes smoky and leathery, while it remains a bit rosier on textiles. Due to its "simplicity," it is a great layering partner for me, adding an extra base to many fragrances. Longevity is very good, sillage is rather average. I really like it and appreciate it for what it is => a statement! Conclusion: Thank you for existing.

This was my first Montale. During our vacation in Tuscany, we went to a small perfumery in the city of Siena and wanted to smell the fragrances. We spent a good hour in the store. Incredible number of brilliant scents. I got stuck on Oud Edition. Very masculine scent with … as the name suggests, Oud flavor. Recently, I noticed a similarity to Ombré Nomade by LV, just not as sweet. A colleague came by and smelled quite similar to the Montale scent. But it wasn't. The small difference is the missing raspberry from ON. And I find it very good that this note is absent in the Montale scent. It may not be as prominent, but somehow better for a man. So yes - the similarity is there and the price is significantly lower than that of LV. I usually wear the scent only when going out or at parties. Not necessarily for everyday wear or the office. But I really enjoy the scent :)

I received Sweet Flowers as a 20 ml gift from Breuninger when I bought two other Montale fragrances. At first, I found it quite synthetic and almost too loud, but somehow it has something. This blend of sweetness and floral notes feels totally artificial, yet still attracts compliments. I wouldn't wear it daily, but it fits certain moments when you want to stand out. It has the typical Montale DNA; I perceive it as more feminine than unisex, but it can still be worn by both, as long as you enjoy squeaky sweet floral scents.

What to do when you're in a bad mood, feeling cabin fever, and it's raining? A gourmand is needed. A good gourmand. A true, reliable comfort scent that doesn’t pretend it can last a day and then leaves you after two hours. But one that truly does last, carrying you through the morning hours when the day still seems to hold promise, when you are alone. Through lunchtime, when everything is already in full swing. And still present in the afternoon, when a little relaxation and a hot coffee beckon. So rare as these days may be - sometimes they come, and then such a loyal scent friend is needed. In spring, for me, this is Sweet Flowers by Montale. It’s already the bottle - when I look at it, I know the scent is stored dark, so to speak, safely, and waits unchanged and sweet for me. It’s the beautiful pink-red that immediately lifts your spirits because it’s sweet and at the same time bold. Not a princess color, more one from Vogue. And then, of course, it’s the scent that I really like. Upon spraying, an immediately comforting, sentimental sweetness spreads, which beams me back to my childhood at the push of a button: To the fair that visited us once a year for a week, a temporary amusement park with roller coasters and carousels, fried fish, candy apples, and of course cotton candy. When I knew: Soon it will be fair time!, I had to save my pocket money for several weeks to try everything with my friend that there was to ride when the time finally came. When I was even younger than during fair times, I once got lost on the swan pond at the Prater with my parents: While I was circling around in my swan boat, my parents somehow disappeared. Since it was apparently me who - at least in their eyes - was missing afterward, there was a lot of trouble, which greatly saddened my seven-year-old heart. Thus, I have never been able to forget the Viennese swan pond, just as little as the fair in my hometown that I visited at 13 and 14. Over these memories, a sweet, warm, familiar scent spreads clearly, inextricably linked to these joyful events: cotton candy. Sweet Flowers is thus a little gift, an olfactory memory of sweet times, and when it hits as skillfully as in this Montale scent, then it is a very precious gift. Because on bad days, nothing comforts more than the sweet memory of childhood (if it was beautiful). But Sweet Flowers can do even more: It is not a sweet-sticky, kitschy girl’s scent that dazzles with gourmand notes and makes me look biteable to 18-year-olds. Sweet Flowers is decidedly more mature. It CAN evoke nostalgia, soothe, and lull with its notes of cotton candy and pretty fruity, natural peach. But it can also be refreshing, as its citrus notes are subtle enough that any stickiness dissipates. Above all, it can appear elegant, as the slight earthiness of patchouli and the seriousness of jasmine, which fits so wonderfully with patchouli and lends brightness and delicate airiness to the spicy-earthy tone, make this perfume wearable for women who carry responsibility and just need a hug. Sweet Flowers tenderly embraces and then returns to adulthood, and as if patchouli and jasmine were not enough, my favorite flower makes an appearance, the epitome of feminine elegance, the tuberose. In combination with the indispensable classics jasmine and patchouli, making a grand entrance after the comforting sweetness of cotton candy and peach, which never becomes sticky thanks to bergamot, and in faithful company of a rather simple vanilla, the tuberose is integrated into this perfume as if it had never belonged anywhere else. It significantly contributes to the serious effect of the gourmand scent. All in all: Sweet Flowers is not for crybabies and childish minds, not for little girls with pink ribbons in their braids and not for hopelessly in-love teenagers. It is a perfume for adult women, those who go to work without a teddy bear and make decisions there, even if they should have a run in their fine stockings. Women whose basic attitude is elegant and mature and who occasionally, from time to time, have the need to awaken the inner child within them and let themselves sway for a moment.

I love tropical fruity blends - Escada's OG tropical summer releases continue to be some of my favorite fragrances - but Montale Pretty Fruity left a lot to be desired. The opening has a blast of something sharp and chemical in nature - almost like the chemical used in a perm or a "box hair dye" used at home. Then it moves into the bulk of the fragrance: an indistinct, somewhat-synthetic tropical fruity blend. I've tried many of Escada's OG tropical summer releases, and this does feel a bit similar - the closest one I can think of is Pacific Paradise , but it's nowhere near a dupe. Unfortunately, it's not as memorable or distinctive as any of them; it felt more like if you mixed a bunch of them together, resulting in too many notes to be able to tell what's what. Dry down came quickly, with the tropical fruity notes disappearing after only a few minutes and leaving behind a single aquatic note (something like a watery melon), with a little bit of powder. I feel like some BBW mists had more realistic fruit blends, and better longevity, than this.

Montale just do everything. Aouds, Musks... and now - why the delay - one might ask - a strong, utterly screechy fruity-floral (berries, pink fruit, passion fruit...) from 2011. Some natural berries smell great by themselves, and so does passion fruit - but in "Pretty fruity" they all end up smelling sweaty and pretty disgusting. This Escada-copy must have been easy to compose: Montale simply used every fruity aromachemical available on the market and overdosed it. The result is a fruity fragrance which smells incredibly artificial. It also has tremendous staying-power. What woman/man is tasteless enough to want to smell like a basket of semi-deteriorated berries with a vile sweaty passion-fruit-note lurking through? Sorry about the rant, but this is another expensive (!!!) nauseating Montale which smells hilariously cheap. Not a fine fragrance - and not a niche, either.

When deciding to write a comment, I also thought about the title: “Not for Fundamentalist Sour Fruit Opponents.” But that seemed too political for a few sour little fruits or the dreadful rhubarb compote from the past. After reading the comments here, I would have at least expected an aromatic authentic fruit jam made from a forest fruit mix. But I hadn't read them beforehand. Montale, I thought, has some very appealing scents for me, so “Pretty Fruity” had to be tested. On my skin, I smelled an aromatic fruit scent with the first sillage before it dried in the air. But then a sharp and sour fruit scent set in for me. I didn’t recognize citrus. But I thought of pomegranate, rhubarb, and passion fruit. And it was sharply concentrated, sour, unsoftened by any sweetness. However, my husband also wanted to smell it and found the scent “lovely.” His comment was why I wouldn’t buy such a perfume for myself. Even later, when a green waxy note like that of waxy sour apple peels with a hint of musty tuberose set in, he maintained that “Pretty Fruity” smelled nice on me. He understood me, I would disdain the truly tasty fruits, but “Pretty Fruity” would really be a fruity scent for adults, not at all like silly fruit gummies. I explained to him mercilessly that I would never buy “Pretty Fruity” and would wash it off before going to bed; I already had a fuzzy and sour feeling on my tongue. I couldn’t sleep with that. But before that, I had to endure the scent for a while for testing purposes. He found that regrettable but peacefully stated that I would have to know that myself. As time went on, the sour sharpness remained; I also smelled coumarin and something like vinyl synthetic. A little while later, namely now, I also smell something slightly bitter, a hint of musk, and also vanillin. This makes “Pretty Fruity” milder, the sharp acidity is neutralized. But now only a strangely synthetic-waxy plastic smell remains, green and indefinable. “Pretty Fruity” now reminds me more of cosmetics and cleaning products with apple aroma. When I think about it, “Pretty Fruity” is a one-dimensional scent. It is a gourmand for lovers, and as I found out, for lovers of sour, very tart fruits. I tested from a new, unused original sample.

This Montale also has fruits and musk as its main theme. This one starts off with a powerful burst of fruits. A very sweet and fruity composition greets me upon spraying. The scent of a fruit basket, a medley of several very sweet notes, somehow I can't pinpoint exactly which fruits are involved. Very sweet and almost overpowering. But over time, it calms down a bit and becomes softer and quieter. Musk in the background adds a slight powdery note, and thus over time takes some sweetness out of this fragrance. At the same time, I can also detect a slightly tart but still fruity note, which is blackcurrant. While the initial note almost overwhelmed me with its extreme sweetness and I wanted to wash this perfume off right away, I am now amazed by this development. Almost nothing of the sweet fruit basket is recognizable anymore. The tart-fruity blackcurrant on a powdery, slightly soapy bed works well on my skin. Whether this fragrance can stay with me is still uncertain, although I also like the bottle, as the initial note is very off-putting for me. Longevity is actually quite good, but it could definitely be better for the price.

For a long time, I avoided Montales because they seemed too serious and overly elegant to me. But Pretty Fruity speaks a completely different language. It is extremely cheerful and delightfully "childlike". A colorful fruit basket is presented to you - filled with ripe, plump fruits. This fits well in the autumn. The fruit still radiates the warmth of sunny days. Aromatic apples, tart blackcurrants, and sweet raspberries reach my nose fully and softly. The scent is truly "pretty" and lightly playful, without drifting into childishness. I rather see a precious porcelain bowl filled with fruit - like in old paintings. The citrus notes refresh Pretty once again. This vitamin kick is also very long-lasting - just right for the shortening days.

Yes, it might be a bit basic, but it is still a very nice spring and summer fragrance that is not offensive or intrusive to those around you. It lasts a long time and has a subtle sillage for a fresh summer scent. At first, it is really a bit sour, but then it becomes softer, sweeter. (Y)

1740 Histoires de Parfums right? Everybody knows this definition of “niche”? Or like a good friend once said: “ italian classe”… I remember when i was in italy in a restaurant with friends. We where the first clients. Along the evening went on, more & more people came in & they systematically took place next to us. One of my friends said “ well your perfume attracts people”. I had 1740 on. Why the comparation with leather Patchouli? Niche niche & more niche !!! Leather, Patchouli (Patchouli is dominant here) & earthy. If Amouage Interlude & initio Oud for greatness will ever collaborate…leather patchouli will be their outcome. Love or hate, can we relate? Everybody is seeking for something new,something special. But sometimes Its Just in front of you!! 10/10 And If you dont like it dont come near me!!

I have collected Mancera and Montale for over 7 years and have tried most of them. Pierre Montale churns out too many fragrances in my opinion, they are always hit and miss. Many smelling similar with the odd note change here and there. But that’s how the brand works. They are not high end niche and not pretending to be, which is what I like. A cool bottle of nice smelling and long lasting juice at a comfortable price is all we ask.nLeather Patchouli I actually bought 2 years ago, but have only just opened the bottle. I am a leather/Oriental fanatic so anything described as leather I buy and try. nThis fragrance has no top notes to think of, it’s straight in with hard leather, smoke and a slight barnyard oud. It’s extremely masculine and I don’t smell vanilla at all. It’s not sweet it’s quite the opposite. nI would also say it’s an old school fragrance, reminded me of how my teachers smelt at school, of second hand smoke and coffee. No coffee in this but it must be the patchouli playing tricks on me.nThe longevity and sillage are strong. A dark sexy scent to be worn on a sensual night out. The juice itself is very dark so be careful wearing this with a white shirt.

Some of you may still remember the underground comic series "The Fabulous Furry Freak Brothers." The adventures of the hippie commune from San Francisco were published from the late 60s to the early 90s. All the clichés associated with the hippie, flower power, and drug subculture are addressed here. The long-haired, perpetually stoned protagonists Phineas, Freewheelin' Franklin, Fat Freddy, and sometimes his cat, Fat Freddy's Cat, are usually on the road in their old, painted VW bus, always on the hunt for some psychoactive substances, enjoying themselves with voluptuous hippie girls at the next love-in, or getting high with dope and the music of Grateful Dead at various festivals, I have no idea if Fat Freddy even wore a scent. At this point, I will indulge in another cliché and claim that the guys smelled like all hippies, of patchouli; specifically, the pure patch oil from the India shop, poster shop, Cri-Cri, or whatever. Maybe also a bit of sandalwood, musk, amber, etc., mixed with the obligatory cannabis and cigarette smoke and stale pub aromas. A perfume was a no-go, and 100 bucks were gladly invested in a Black Afgano, but certainly not in the one from Nasomatto. Well, maybe it was simply the smell of Fat Freddy's old biker jacket, with the fringes that, despite its age, still exuded that sharp leather scent and mingled with the aroma of patch oil... and maybe Fat Freddy does occasionally wear Montale's Leather Patch for certain occasions. Just for a change and yet not far from old habits. Montale Leather Patchouli is not an elegant leather scent like those from Tom Ford or Aqua di Parma. I would place it between Patchouli Leaves and Aoud Cuir d'Arabie, also from Montale. The base note is very similar to that of Patchouli Leaves. When smelling from the atomizer and spraying it on, I perceive, alongside patchouli and leather, a hint of citrus freshness that quickly evaporates. Then only a very strong leather scent remains. No, actually, it’s not leather yet, but rather cardamom. It's as if I'm smelling a spice jar filled with black cardamom pods. The scent of cardamom has always reminded me of leather, and I have always liked it. An enormously strong, slightly piercing cardamom scent that dominates all other ingredients. Patchouli is present from the start, but not in the foreground. It seems to dance around the leather. Behind the slightly piercing note, I suspect the oud. Additionally, I perceive a slight sweetness from the vanilla. Saffron and incense remain rather hidden in the background. Overall, it seems to me that all the ingredients have completely intertwined, making it difficult for me to pinpoint the individual players. There is no scent progression. The initially strict, almost piercing notes gradually fade away, and the Montale becomes overall calmer but not quieter, smoky, rounder, and warmer. The cardamom note seems to transition a bit more into a leather scent. The slight sweetness of the vanilla increases without becoming sticky or overpowering. Patchouli and vanilla come a bit more to the forefront without dominating. The main player is and remains the leather from the very beginning. Thus, the scent lingers for the next 4 to 5 hours. Now the leather slowly bids farewell, leaving behind a very nice base of vanilla, incense, and patch, similar to that of Montale's Patchouli Leaves. Both remind me of the scent that used to greet you upon entering an India shop. Or of smoldering incense sticks. Longevity, as expected from Montale, is very long. Sprayed in the afternoon, still noticeably present the next morning until showering. A somewhat different leather scent, apart from the well-known Russians and Cuirs, etc. A composition under the aspect of "Leather + Patchouli." Elegant hippie. For me, a welcome change that I have already included as a decant in my small patchouli collection. Not a scent for every day, rather a special one for in-between. Peace & Love & Patch, Brothers & Sisters A huge thank you to the lovely Parfuma for this decant and the many nice extras!!!

An incredible scent. It smells, as the name suggests, of leather and oud. Grandiose. Unbelievably oriental. And the typical synthetic oud scent for Montale does not come into play here. Many, however, find this fragrance unpleasant. Some told me I smell like a cow shed, others said I smell like a spice market. But many also gave me compliments for this scent. This fragrance smells like a Russian mafioso in a black turtleneck, arriving in a black G-Class. Super cool scent!

This scent is JUST WOW!!! It smells just like my old Petroff punk leather jacket after a decade of use. I slept in that jacket, never took it off even during sex. It helped me through the cold streets of Brixton. It was danced in and soaked with beer, and now it hangs on the wall as a reminder of old times. And Leather Patchouli has exactly that scent and also matches my 20-year-old Schott leather jacket. A fragrance that evokes memories and never ages. Three sprays and you still smell it on others even after 3 days. What is Aoud Leather compared to this... it just smells like car leather seats and elegance. Here, I have a wow experience upon spraying! A flashback of memories! Montale has truly outdone itself here. And if the rest of the people around me only smell patchouli, that's fine by me. My girlfriend is also in love with this fragrance experience. Therefore, at this price, it's a steal. I have 3 bottles well stored, which should last a lifetime, but eventually, it will no longer be produced and then... Certainly not a scent for everyone, but definitely a scent for connoisseurs and lovers of really strong fragrances.

A blind and random purchase as I used to wear the original. A nice surprise to find a flanker that can delight as well. This is like a very well behaved daughter perfume. Something streamlined to wear in an office or a polite place. A shadow of her original heavy duty, naughty nights, 80's mum. A gentle incense carries a spicy carnation on a gentle breeze of rounded citrus with soft florals. All nicely balanced by a pretty green toned, earthy garden. Powdery spices and floral notes blend seamlessly to weave a well balanced and incredibly pretty, light, oriental floral. The patchouli applied with a gentle hand to merely ground these florals and not dominate. The vanilla just sweetening enough to stop it being sharp but never going sweet. The spices and incense are just enough to stop this being too floral. This very good daughter perfume is gently suggestive without being too naughty. This might be nice on a hot day, to just smell clean and fresh but be a bit more interesting than just pretty. I couldn't see work colleagues objecting to this one. It sits softly, close and skin scent-ish. Eventually gets so soft, it is like spicy talc.

The Montale naysayers tend to maintain that this house simply produces perfumes combinatorially, by rolling together different proportions of a fairly small number of notes. My response: so what? When a perfume is a beautiful as DEEP ROSES, I could care less how it was hit upon. The key notes--common, it is true, to an amazing number of Montale perfumes--are rose, oud, amber, and musk. The top notes are listed as peony and mandarin, but honestly I do not detect them at all. The roses sweep in so swiftly to take over the show that the ephemeral top notes are simply lost in the shuffle. Not that anyone should care, because the proportions of rose and oud and amber and musk are just right. If we were to create a cloud-type depiction of the note distribution, but using instances rather than word size, it would look something like this: ROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSE ROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSE ROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSE ROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSE ROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSE ROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSE ROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEROSEOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUD OUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUDOUD OUDAMBERAMBERAMBERAMBERAMBERAMBERAMBERAMBERAMBERAMBERAMBERAMBER AMBERAMBERAMBERAMBERMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSK MUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSK MUSKMUSKMUSKMUSKMUSK --- This little cloud illustrates why DEEP ROSES is designated as a perfume for women. Key word: rose. To me, these seem to be red roses, blood red roses with velvety petals and no stems or thorns, as this composition is not green in the least. The musk and amber serve as a slightly animalic base, and oud is but an embellishment, like a dash of salt to an otherwise already excellent dish. As simple as it is, DEEP ROSES is nonetheless one of my favorite Montale creations. Now that I've drained two full sample vials, it's going on my wish list!

Deep Roses could easily be Extreme Roses. Opens with a huge blast of sour and green roses that remains for about 2 hours. After that there just a little development in drydown: the oud joins the composition along with the amber. But they're little players only... the major player here is still the rose. I also detect a honey note in the late drydown, after 6 hours or more. There's no medicinal smell which is caracteristic of many Montale scents. Actually there's not much development in the fragrance phases, that's why it can be called as an unidimensional fragrance, which isnt a problem for me. Unisex, but towards the feminine side. Sillage and projection are medium-high and longevity is about 10 hours.

The first Montale rose that is perfect for me, just as it is! In the opening, a fresh yet ripe (sweet) mandarin paired with delicate peony.... Then, it only takes a moment, and there it is, the beautiful elegant pink rose! It is so authentic that I want to bathe in it, simply a dream! The Aoud listed in the fragrance pyramid has, in my opinion, been used in a very subtle way, for which I am absolutely grateful... instead, the white musk comes through strongly for me, perfectly rounding off the beautiful rose! For me, a wonderful rose.... The second bottle is almost at the end again ;)

Roses, roses, and nothing but roses, a whole field of roses. I smell deep red roses and absolutely nothing else. Yes, I love roses in every way. And these roses are real! Still, I miss something that makes this scent a perfume. null of the aforementioned ingredients stand out to me, except for the full load of roses! It’s just too one-dimensional for me!

Some time ago, I used the following quote to describe a rather tame and impeccably clean violet scent. Here’s a slightly altered version: Be like the violet in the moss, modest, humble, and pure, but if one were such a rose, who would want to be a violet? Deep Roses is an "over-rose," it is seductive and opulent, it has class and somehow something unattainable. If you don’t pay close attention, you smell nothing but rose; but if you let it unfold a few times, you realize that its companions, without actually having a standalone presence, do nothing but highlight the rose scent. The rose in the top note is floral and fresh, the rose in the heart note is mysterious and dark, and in the base, it ultimately becomes warm and soft, but it is always unmistakably rose. What could have motivated Montale to dress such a dark, opulent rose scent in such an inappropriate candy-pink outfit? Can you imagine a Marlene Dietrich in a candy-colored dirndl? I believe she would have rather jumped off a bridge. This faux pas has probably also been noticed by those responsible at Montale, and they have now given it a dark brown elegant twist.

~ Inspiration ~ I received "Incanto Charms" as a gift a few years ago and I really like this scent, so I was curious about "Incanto Dreams." ~ Bottle ~ Tacky, sweet, and girly - However, a bit unwieldy for small hands. The colorful gradients of pink, red, and yellow promise a sweet summer fragrance. ~ Scent ~ It starts off a bit sour, but also fruity-sweet with ripe pineapple, mango, red apples, and a handful of currants. In the heart note, freesias and lush peonies come to the fore. The base concludes with musk and sandalwood. ~ Longevity ~ On my skin, it lasts about 5-6 hours (a bit longer on clothes and hair). You can spray it multiple times without worry, as it only leaves a small, subtle scent veil. ~ Occasion ~ It fits well into the warmer days of spring and summer (also suitable for the office). ~ Conclusion ~ While I prefer "Incanto Charms," this version is not bad either. Personally, I find it just a tad too sour.

Today, although it is not exactly summery, it is pouring rain, but I have brought summer into my home with Szenario d`ete. Lime, mandarin, and orange provide a Mediterranean opening. A few rays of sunshine are already reaching me. And then the beautiful bright jasmine! I imagine my garden when it is immersed in this friendly scent. The vanilla in the drydown deepens the fragrance without weighing it down. No, it is light as a feather - yet substantial. It skillfully brings to life the scene of a summer landscape. Musk adds a bit of spiciness and gives it longevity. A lovely summer fragrance that can also be worn in cooler temperatures - or at least as a prelude to summer.

I have a weakness for lime fragrances, particularly in the summer, and I must say that this is not your typical light citrus aromatic cologne. Aromatic Lime is indeed aromatic, but the deep lime is surrounded by honeyed saffron and resiny myrrh. There's a synthetic density here that I associate with other Montales. It's long-lasting as well. Not to my taste, but very Montale.

Very different from most Montale's releases, Aromatic Lime has some kind of metallic and citric smell with a barbershop vibe. Very different, may not be a pleasure to everyone. Lime and myrrh are the main players here. Smells like Fougere Marines and Aoud Lime mixed. Deserves at least a try. Updated January 2014

Well, how does one write a critique while trying to remain objective? Actually, it’s not possible at all, because critiques are critiques. But I will still try, without the perfumer jumping off a bridge, the perfume house going bankrupt, or the lovers sharpening their knives. Lemons! Limes! Picked in their unripe stage, very sour! From the category "I’ll pull all your holes together." But at least it’s organically grown. The electric juicer must have exploded on the poor perfumer. It smells very metallic! Afterwards, there was a cable fire in the basement of the laboratory, oh sorry, that’s patchouli (the basement). But still, the perfumer must have somehow scorched the wooden fragrance organ (original French craftsmanship made of sandalwood). Well, maybe Aromatic Lime just smells this sour and biting on my skin. Surely it smells wonderful on other skins. But I don’t know that.

I bought this fragrance blindly because it was on sale and I wanted to own it. Afterwards, I read the comments here and was plagued by a mix of skepticism and concern about whether I would like Aromatic Lime, or if it was a purchase I would regret. Aromatic Lime is, compared to the overall very good longevity of Montale fragrances, even more, almost unbelievably long-lasting on me. It lasts more than 12 hours, almost up to 24 hours on my skin. It smells dry, fresh. Lemon is prominent. Patchouli and sandalwood give it a spicy woody note, but in expression, it remains behind the lemon. I find it incredibly good, despite its extreme fragrance direction. I don't perceive it as biting or harsh, but rather, in its citrus orientation, dry herbal and very pleasant. Very pleasant because the fragrance notes all blend homogeneously in terms of scent expression; otherwise, it would be poorly made, which is definitely not the case on me. Caution, skin chemistry also plays a role with such unusual fragrances. Therefore, I recommend testing such scents on the skin and not, like I did, buying them blindly out of curiosity without an intense test. Even a great offer becomes expensive if you can't smell the fragrance. It is strong, it is more masculine-oriented..... But dry fresh and wonderfully wearable for me as a woman. I don't hold back in the fragrance department of the strong gender anyway. For me, a brilliant scent for the strong days in a woman's life.

Aromatic Lime - something fresh for summer? No, no, and again no. The opening is more than nasty and elicited an "Ugh!" from me, and while I held my arm as far away from my nose as possible, my husband grinned and said, "What did your chemistry teacher tell you in school? With unknown liquids, always just waft and don't hold your nose directly over it..." Ha-ha. I'll laugh tomorrow... I smell neither lime nor lemon, nor any other citrus fruits. Bitter orange? I would be lying. At least this time the patchouli doesn't bother me - at least not more than the rest of the ingredients. There is no used-sweaty note this time, but it is still way too woody-spicy for me. It's simply not for me, leaning more towards the barbershop direction than even remotely fruity. I expected something completely different; perhaps the pitch-black and not lime-green bottle should have been a warning. In a blind buy, I would have been terribly annoyed. The name does not reflect what one expects. A classic case of label deception.

Aromatic Lime starts refreshingly crisp - citrusy and slightly sour - fruity. And it smells like hairspray and even still like the good kind, and as a hairspray user, I find that quite amusing :-) I would like to express my sincere thanks to our dear Parfuma "Verbena" for the sample that allowed me to test this fragrance.

This Montale fragrance doesn't really have anything to do with aromatic lime. Therefore, the naming of this perfume, as well as its classification as a unisex scent, should not be taken too seriously. I can't imagine this harsh, strict, and even bitter scent on a woman.

From the name, I expected a true explosion of lime here, as the Montale fragrances I have tested so far have always been quite intense. But unfortunately, there isn't much lime (or citrus fruits at all) in this one. If you were already geared up for lime, the opening of this fragrance feels a bit strange.

(Imagine Dragons, Night Visions, 2012) Yes. It's cool. The average rating here of 6.0 says a lot. Fine, I'm just not the target audience for girl perfumes. That means: sweet, dessert, lipstick, vanilla, gourmand. I don't want to smell like food. I don't want to smell like makeup. Not Marly. Not Dior Homme Intense. Not gold bars. No.

Oh no, I bravely sprayed Aromatic Lime on my arm and now I can't get it off, even with soap and scrubbing. Help? Anyone? I can actually smell nothing but vetiver, and I don't like to smell that on its own anyway. Unfortunately, I can't say much more about it; it's a truly terrible scent for my nose with a fantastic longevity on my skin.

Oh, I do detest. Such a shame seeing that I love Salvatore Ferragamo fragrances so much. The grapefruit and apple notes in the opening were far too strong and nauseating for my overly sensitive sense of smell. I kept hoping that this initial fruity blast would disappear or soften making way for the peony, apricot and hibiscus. I waited patiently but that moment never came. Another immediate disappointment was that the scent barely lasted more than an hour on my skin. It was all sharp fruits and then nothing, not even the slightest hint that a perfume even touched the skin. In lots of ways this fragrance reminds me of Envy Me by Gucci which I'm also not a fan of. Perhaps it is just my personal taste and skin chemistry that reacts badly to these scents, however with that being said I still won't be recommending this fragrance to anyone in a hurry.

Incanto Heaven has an interesting, slightly herb-bitter top note - the grapefruit! Not that I identified the grapefruit, but the description of the top note makes the slightly bitter first impression plausible. The spicy-fruity-herb opening with the bitter undertone raises hopes for a beautiful, interesting, and not too sweet fragrance.
