However, after about an hour, an unpleasant synthetic note develops, and then it tips into a sea of floral-sweet fruitiness. I would have bet that there is vanilla in it as well.

After sniffing through a few Aoud fragrances from Montale, I must say this one is my favorite. Although I find the name a bit misleading. In fact, there isn't much to notice from the "Flowers"; they fade away after a while, or rather, they recede into the background so much that they are more to be sensed than smelled. The various woods come to the forefront so strongly that nothing remains of the little flowers, and the musk keeps everything nice and soft and creamy; I couldn't perceive the bitterness that my predecessors mentioned here. The scent accompanied me throughout a whole workday and was still noticeable at home in the evening, without reapplying, mind you! Although I thought that overly woody fragrances wouldn't suit me, this one proved me wrong. Definitely worth a test!

I have to admit, I love the Micallef Oud fragrances. I enjoy their softness, sweetness, and the great cuddle factor. With Aoud Flowers, I somehow expected a mix between Oud and Floral from Micallef. A big - very big - mistake. Aoud Flowers has not only nothing, but absolutely nothing cuddly about it. The opening comes across as very alcoholic and piercing to the nose, with a beige scent reminiscent of vinegar. Just sour. Even when a bit of green-herbaceousness comes in - I assume it's the bergamot - it remains very fresh, very green, and sour. Much later, I can also perceive a tiny bit of rose, which unfortunately is almost completely overshadowed by this sour note. The fragrance also refuses to show any other note on my skin, and I feel like I'm stuck in a waiting loop. Is there more to come, or is that it? It simply becomes more and more bitter, woody, but retains that unpleasant sour note. There is no balance to it, and I was very glad when the scent disappeared after 7 hours, as it was very noticeable even from a distance throughout the entire time. Maybe I had the wrong expectation. Maybe my skin chemistry highlighted this sour note even more. This fragrance is truly only for real lovers of bitter, green, hardly floral scents, and I would definitely not consider it a women's fragrance or unisex fragrance.

Pierre Montale has been accused of repeatedly launching new fragrances in the Oud line that only differ from one another in nuances. This is true for some fragrances in this line - including Aoud Flowers - but less so for others. To get straight to the point - Aoud Flowers comes very close to the epitome of a Rose-Oud perfume. Rose and Oud are both prominent, yet very balanced against each other; everything else is secondary: The geranium perhaps modifies the rose into a brighter accord, but does not appear independently. Wood is present and noticeable, but harmoniously integrated, far from the intensity of a Black Aoud. The light citrus note in the top makes it all quite piquant. It is also worth mentioning a bright musk accord in the background that contributes a certain softness. As with other ouds from Montale, one must endure a sharp hairspray note in the first minutes after spraying, which quickly dissipates and clears the way. Aoud Flowers is fundamentally a very dark fragrance. Despite the floral notes, it is not sweet at all. Instead, a certain citrus bitterness is very present for a long time. The proximity to Black Aoud and Steam Aoud is unmistakable. Montale describes this composition as masculine on the verge of femininity. Rose seems to be a shy deer. During the scent development, it steps back a bit, and the fragrance becomes more bitter. Personally, I would prefer Aoud Flowers to the well-known Black Aoud because it is not quite as extreme and the woods are more bearable. I am undecided about Steam Aoud. While Steam Aoud offers a very nice dry spiciness, Aoud Flowers can score points with the depth and tranquility that the rose radiates. Aoud Flowers is the perfume from the Oud line that comes closest to the highly elegant dark rose perfume “Black Tie” by Washington Tremlett among those I have tested so far. However, it does not quite reach its elegance for me due to the earthiness of the oud, but also because of the existing citrus bitterness. My recommendation: Those who want to test the Montale ouds and are more interested in dark men’s fragrances should consider Aoud Flowers as one of the most typical Rose-Oud scents.

Hmmm. It's a changeable perfume. Now I like it. I've worn it about 6-7 times and I didn't really like it. I was hoping I would like it and it is. I feel it as a synthetic, spicy, fruity, floral, earthy, sweet perfume. I received the 30 ml bottle as a gift. I also have its miniature as a gift with a purchase. It is part of an advent calendar with miniature perfumes. My advice is not to rush to draw conclusions about this perfume the first time. It is a more difficult perfume. You need to give it time. Also, wear it in the cold season. I wore it this summer and the pungent smell bothered me. Rating: 8/10

I kind of like this. It really does smell like dessert. I don't like ambroxan, but it didn't give me much of a headache. It's similar to something, but I can't remember exactly what it is (I'll add it if I remember). Hmm...it reminds me a bit of cloud. Yes, it does smell like sweets, but it doesn't smell like tiramisu. I wouldn't recommend it to tiramisu fans. Also, it doesn't have a luxurious scent, it feels a bit cheap.It's just a gourmand that is easy for the average woman to wear, not a serious gourmand. Edit: Okay. You might say I'm lying, but this is similar to Yara. Another addition to the Yara family. The marine notes, with a hint of tropical mango, definitely remind me of Yara. This is a list of similar scents. So I'm not needed. "Yara / يارا (Eau de Parfum) | Lattafa / لطافة" Pepe Jeans for Her Rich/Warm/Addictive Eau de Toilette Signature Eau de Parfum

There is no opening as such, it is flat. It is not particularly sweet and pretty dry. On my skin, I can only smell tart citrus and a pinch of something vanilla. No violets, and certainly no tiramisu here. The sillage is very intimate, almost watercolor-like. The durability is low for its price. The bottle is sturdy, in a beautiful red-orange color, convenient to carry with. I do not understand those who write here that they expect this perfume to be "girly". Come on, it is clear that this fragrance is designed for adult women. It will be too boring for children (especially compared to what I doused myself with in my teenage years). This Unica is ideal for the office, because it is maximally politically correct, unobtrusive, just to smell nice. If you compare it with Unica from Intimissimi, the second Unica is much sweeter, more beautiful and lasts a long time on the skin.

I can smell the tiramisu so well. Wonderful. The mandarin and the marine note make it not too sweet but beautifully fruity and fresh at the beginning. By the end, it becomes nicely creamy. I really like the Signorina line, and the Ferragamo fragrances are little hidden gems. Definitely try all the Signorinas.

That's right!!!! In this regard, I have to agree with the nice, very dedicated, and truly competent lady in the perfume/beauty store of a Düsseldorf department store. I was looking for a scent that would transport me to a summer garden in full bloom. Well, fitting for the season. Fresh citrus scents dissipate very quickly on my skin with only a few exceptions. Unfortunately, this includes wonderful candidates like Creed's Virgin Island Water, Amouage Sunshine (which I wouldn't have purchased anyway after hearing its price - hello, I go on vacation for that! Long story short, it should be a very floral scent. Not an easy task with my skin chemistry. It doesn't like iris (very common in floral scents, I find), violet, or a dominant rose; the ubiquitous oud is absolutely taboo, and patchouli in the base is borderline,...! The aforementioned lady then said that only two scents would actually be suitable for me: Supreme Bouquet and Magnificent Blossom by Yves Saint Laurent! Because more flower is not possible!!!!!! She first sprayed Supreme Bouquet on me - which immediately put a blissful smile on my face! And then Magnificent Blossom - hmm yes, nice, I thought! I was then advised to wait a bit, perhaps with a glass of Prosecco! I stood there sipping Prosecco at a counter where three other ladies joined me. It immediately became a nice and fun group. Each one sniffed at the wrist of the others and then shared their opinions. However, after about 20 minutes, my favorite was not the previously beloved Supreme Bouquet but the Magnificent Blossom. My, as I said, fussy skin chemistry simply decided differently. To my dismay!!!! I kept my opinion to myself for the time being and waited for the reactions of the others. When all three ladies (aged between 26-58, I was the second youngest) agreed that it could only be the Magnificent Blossom, that the Supreme Bouquet would now smell like fruit gum on me, the decision was made! I don't base my purchasing decisions on others; my taste is not mainstream and occasionally just too specific, but in this case, it was really nice to receive such wonderful unanimous reactions. Everyone thought that this is "me" in all (possible) facets! That’s how a perfume/scent should be, I think, right????? The aforementioned nice lady, i.e., the perfume saleswoman, seemed surprised herself at how well the perfume was received by me and the others and also said she preferred the Magnificent Blossom on me. Supreme Bouquet was simply too sweet on my skin. Should this review find readers (it’s my first one ever!!!!) and you should then wonder if my wish to be transported by the perfume to a summer garden has come true: Yes, definitely!!!!! I then bought the matching shower gel and body cream Gelsomino from Acqua di Parma - a very fresh (Calabrian, I was told) jasmine as the main theme of the scent! Super nice in combination. I then had the store issue me a free customer card through which I received a discount on the three "fragrant" items - which was good for me, as the original price would have made me swallow even more. However, I think my credit from the house's ancillary cost statement (which seemed too low to me) was very "fragrant" beautifully invested this way! By the way, I was not the only one who bought the perfume. The oldest lady in the group was so enthusiastic about the perfume (on my skin, mind you) that she also bought it. Although her daughter, who came to pick her up, said it didn't suit her, however - after a quick sniff at my wrist - it suited me. I had to tremble a little because at first, it was said that there was only one left, and the lady had declared it "bought" seconds before me. But someone seemed to have taken a liking to me: It was found two more times! So there is indeed love at second glance, sorry, second sniff.

... and another oud à la Montale, this time particularly synthetic, unsubstantial and plastic. Basically you get the usual artificial and dry woody-rubbery note they (and many other brands) insist on fraudulently call “oud”, here dusted with a powdery-soapy feel which kind of smells like a spray cleaner for glasses and floors. Not being sarcastic; that’s literally the smell (ta'if rose? At that price? ...). More clumsy than other ouds by Montale, and as much clumsy as also loud and overwhelming, at least for a while when applied; on the drydown is tames down a bit, remaining identical as regards of the smell but just more wearable (and bearable by people around you). Not a complete disaster, as it basically smells like a dozen of other ouds by this brand (although they’ve a bunch which are actually a tad above the others), but surely not that pleasant or elegant either; just somewhere between mediocre and cheap/decent, also considering the price - which isn’t high, after all....but well, still not worthy for me. 5/10

Opening is very medicinal oud note and then turns to a faint sweet roses smell. Smells like Aoud Queen Roses and Attar mixed. Unisex for sure. Great fragrance, but do not expect anything actually unique. Updated January 2014

September is just around the corner. The warm days are not yet counted. The emphasis is on WARM, not HOT. The nights are sometimes quite cool. Good for roses. Often they bloom again in all their splendor. From apricot colors to dark purple. The first mists are on their way. Covering fields and forest floors, fine and subtle. Time for berry harvest. Blackberries, blueberries. All in dark magenta to violet. Autumn colors. Ripening colors. The colors of late enjoyment. And of scents. Woods and barks are fragrant. Damp soils give off earthy aromas. Accompaniment of berries and blossoms. Slightly melancholic melodies accompany the scene. Not-quite-summer----- --not-quite-autumn. Between the times. A lot of major--- Some in minor. It can be felt and sniffed. Heavy scents with light undertones. No time for lamenting. Time to enjoy. No "false notes" of a somewhat "quirky" melody. Everything is right in the right place. Even if sometimes a quiet nostalgia sneaks in. Early autumn indeed. Not the end of warm days, but a hint of a notion.

The "bottle" (can you really call this grenade-morning star thing...?) sets the tone: another creation from Montale that is hard to surpass in artificiality. Dark purple is an appropriate color association for this fragrance, velvety, heavy, soft, and flattering. I can't identify a single note listed in the pyramid; this is pure synthetic, but quite flattering and cozy, not unpleasant. Dark violet velvet, this image keeps coming to my mind. However, it's made of synthetic fibers, later also with slightly fruity, faintly sweet notes (plastic blueberry...? towel blackberry...?). I wouldn't know who would need or buy this fragrance, but anyone who feels they absolutely must own a rose scent despite hating roses and leaning more towards gourmand fragrances might find this one quite suitable, if it weren't for the outrageous price.

This is a very beautiful fig fragrance. The citron opening is very bright but when it settles in you get a strong, juicy fig with some floral touches. Lasting power is very good and projection is good too. I’m not a fig lover so I won’t be buying the big bottle but I’d recommend it to people who do love fig scents.

I confess to being a bit of an Oud addict :). This addiction was in no small way aided and abetted by House Montale, being that the first time I came in contact with Oud was via some of their perfumes. Unfortunately, the Oud explosion of the past few years has taken this note from relative unattainability to commonplace, rendering the search for 'really good' Oud fragrances an ongoing passion. In my fascination with Oud as a note, I have come to the realisation that I cannot abide it unadorned. The medicinal, 'un-mucked-out-stable' effect it sometimes presents my nose with is quite intolerable, so my Oud MUST be softened with florals (predominantly Rose) and sweet-ish resins and incenses. The problem is that Rose/Oud combinations invariably end up smelling similar ... as is the case with Montale's Louban. I have definitely smelled this fragrance before ... in other creations by the same house, in fragrances by Nejma, Killian, Arabian Oud, Al Haramain and Ajmal ... to name but a few. Each carry their own slight distinctiveness, but the underlying Oud and Roses in those I have tried (and own LOL) is dizzyingly similar. In Louban's defense, the addition of Violet Leaf is the saving grace here, bringing a lovely green freshness to the composition. This 'green-ness' is comfortably enveloped by the richer ingredients, as if the Violet Leaf being too chilly needed a wrap of Frankincense, Patchouli and Sandalwood to keep it warm. This is a really lovely fragrance and presented with the opportunity I would probably add Louban to my collection ...

Louban smells like a dusty rose with some hints of musk and incense. The roses here are not green as they are in many other Montales, but more like dry rose petals. It's not like other Aouds: this one stays close to skin with a big lasting power. Unisex for sure. Definetely worth it. Thumbs up! Updated January 2014

What? Just one critique? And a completely wrong one at that; so no. Louban deserves 100% because someone really put in the effort here. Mr. Montale took all his "White Oud" bottles and meticulously covered them with gold leaf (or something similar). After years of searching and hoping to snag White Oud in the souk, you know who you’re talking to. My joy was all the greater to unveil this blind buy bottle. Finally here. Rose.and.oud. That’s all there is to say. No frills, no pretentiousness, no sugary nonsense, and no Piedmont cherry on top. A RED rose and the rotten wood. That's It. And now go ahead and beat me up, I use this all the time, well, preferably in summer as a deodorant. Those who know Montale know that sillage is written in capital letters here, and my earlobes are too close in this case. ..but the backs of my knees would be too far away. A great signature scent with high recognizability. Strong, clear, unmistakably Montale, feminine, and very human. The opposite of a laundromat.

This perfume also belongs to the Oud line. But it is a rather lighter representative of this genre. There is an episode of the Addams Family where Morticia Addams receives a bouquet of roses. Overjoyed, she cuts off all the blooms, throws them away, and places the stems in a vase. Exactly this has happened with the rose in this perfume. You no longer smell any blooms, only fresh stems (except for Louban, you can find this strange scent also in Twill Rose by Les Parfums de Rosine). Thus, it is an entirely green perfume.

The description of my predecessor's comment is brilliantly fitting for this scent. On one hand. That's why I was very pleased with the sample that I received. I really like the name of the scent. First impression: Oh, very interesting, it piques curiosity, no ordinary scent experience is on the horizon. There is Oud and Rose here, otherwise I smell nothing else. Hmmh, I would really like to enjoy the combination of Rose and Oud, it's so unusual and special. Here, it's truly a red, not a black-red, rose and the "grotto" wood. And that’s where it stays. Absolutely and undoubtedly. For me, it’s more of a "grotto-like, crypt-like, muffled" scent - not meant negatively. On the other hand: If I ever visit dark, crypt-like, slightly damp caves in my life again and dress in black while feeling a bit "depressed" - then definitely with this scent. Above the caves and grottos and crypts, I couldn't wear it; it feels so dark. Not for bright life and everyday life - at least for me. This "scent" conveys a feeling of life, one that I know, but don't often want around me. This scent makes me feel "somehow depressed"... Perhaps I really am not used to anything direct and straightforward in the depths anymore, sigh.

I am very curious about Montale. Irini kindly sent me 5 Montale samples, and I want to test one every day. The name promises incense, alongside which I expect a Montale Aoud Rose. Right up my alley. In the first few minutes, I recoil. What develops on my skin at first is a herbal-woody-medical cloud. Aoud and vetiver, I would say. Intense.

Wood in the base, green in the top, no vanilla and also unisex, what could possibly go wrong, thought my naive self. However, it seems that the fragrance is no longer available, but thanks to the Souk and the dear SebastianM, I quickly got a sample of the quite green little water. I am on the hunt for a lasting (!) woody basil herb WITHOUT smelling like a men's salon. Not so easy. High expectations for Rinascimento (I will only have to work with copy, nobody can write that without mistakes), as the Renaissance was the transition from the dark Middle Ages to a time characterized by cultural diversity and the pursuit of knowledge. My art teacher would hopefully be proud of me at this point... A really discreet spray on the wrist and my green sample mutates into Herb Hulk! Wow, this stuff has power. Very, very delicious basil, Basil Smash says hello, and some undefinable herbal scent wafts into my olfactory organ like a truckload of Ricola. If the top note is still the clever Bruce Banner, then the white flowers of the heart note tear the white jersey apart and unleash the Hulk, collateral damage in the immediate vicinity included. Short digression - I like hyacinths. In spring, I like to buy a little bulb that soon blooms at room temperature and smells wonderful. And because I think of Giersack when I see the next garden offer at the hardware store, "Oh look, 3 at once on sale," my poor husband has no air left at home the following week when the three monsters bloom at once. Back to the Hulk. Hulk aka Rinascimento has meanwhile decided to imitate the most brutal hyacinth on earth. Does tuberose smell like hyacinth? A bit, right? I really like lilies and iris and other white flower stuff, but this hammering white heaviness threatens to overwhelm me. Stay brave! It’s a lot, almost too much, but somehow not bad at all, just maybe instead of 15 white lilies, two would have sufficed. We have now reached 3 hours of wear time on the skin, and Hulk, uh, the white monster flower continues to smash windows. I still hope that it will eventually hit wood in the truest sense of the word and then reduce the frequency of its strikes. 5 hours. The storm has raged and is slowly subsiding. And now my resistance against the temptation to wash off these killer flowers pays off - it’s getting nice! Moderate, harmonious, this is workable. Yes kids, a bit over the top, right? I can’t always spend 5 hours in the fresh air.. however, I could excellently use Rinascimento as green kryptonite against the not-so-beloved favorite colleague.. unforeseen possibilities... Rinascimento is like a will-o'-the-wisp in the forest, you never know if it wants to show you the way back to the light and save you or lure you deeper into darkness and straight into ruin.. Longevity is impressive for me, sillage was already hard on the edge of tolerable with minimal dosage (definitely the first 2 hours) - I will definitely not try the little monster close to my head. The lost treasure is not to be hunted down, but I will probably use the sample sparingly.

Parisienne Edition Singulière smells very similar to the original Parisienne with dominant rose, violet, tart berries and the vinyle twist. The fragrance has a creamy texture, which also reminds me of Hanaé Mori butterfly. The sillage is close but intense at the same time. The longevity is as good as the original version. I would definitely recommend it, since it's as good as the original Parisienne. But obviously, those who already own the original don't need to bother about it, unless you happen to finish your bottle and want a change of colour.

This sultry Parisian arrived as a "side dish" in my birthday package. My friend thought this heavyweight scent lady would be better suited for me. In her opinion, "Madame" belongs in the big city; she doesn't feel comfortable in the Swabian Jura. We circled each other for a while; "YSL Parisienne Édition Singulière" was coy before revealing herself to me. The black, faceted bottle turned out to be a kind of magic lamp: A very dark, heavy fragrance full of ripe fruits and flowers welcomed me. Not delicate and quiet, but full of power and mystery. Damask rose, violet, and peony - all in full bloom - harmonize very well with the berry top note. Vinyl and leather make this scent already quite extravagant in its creation - yes, capricious. This fragrance composition is perfected and rounded off by the sensual components of the base note. Surprisingly, all four components are equally balanced: there is no designated "leader"; even musk (usually a bit forward) submits to the overall picture. With patience, the fragrance develops over time: it becomes lighter and thus also softer, more wearable. An average longevity allows for the conscious perception of these changes. And yet, this YSL scent still possesses many edges and corners; it does not become soft and tender. "YSL Parisienne Édition Singulière" is neither suitable for business nor for the concert hall. It is very dominant and can quickly become bothersome to those around due to its pronounced leather scent. The extravagant, sensual lady in black velvet with patent pumps finds a stylish companion in this fragrance. She just has to be confident enough to be in the spotlight. Somehow, "YSL Parisienne Édition Singulière" screams for a red carpet, spotlights, and many cameras. Who among us can provide it with that background?

... from the name: this is NOT a strong scent. It starts with fresh-flowery notes joined after some minutes by a very noticeable sour cherry which melts into the flowers and stays there for some time. Unfortunately, I can not add as to the development of the dry down as SUBTIL then disappears. Too bad - especially as it is an edp - it is very likeable and fits well for a carefree day in the city. Perhaps it performs better in other seasons?

Ferragamo's Parfum Subtil smells almost simular to Lancome's miracle but parfum Subtil opens with the spiciness of tulips a flirty blast of red cherries the last top note is delectable fruits the drydown has a musky vanilla undertones miracle has more of a mixture of peony and orangy undertones. it's a bit powdery but not overwelminly so the perfume ends with vanilla like a cherry shortcake Delecious!.

The name here, I think, is not really representative. I bought the fragrance blindly and did not regret it. Although the composition and the appearance of the bottle suggested a different direction, I was pleasantly surprised by this extremely sociable tiger. An almost urban tiger that has adapted to interacting with people. I do not perceive the scent as animalistic. The oud is hardly noticeable to me, if at all. In the opening, it is rather the bitter orange that stands out, but after 5 minutes it benevolently steps into the background. Now a slightly smoky and elegant woody-creamy aura comes to the fore. Iris and leather dominate here lightly, without the iris bringing any powderiness. At first, I was a bit skeptical before the fragrance settled on me, wondering if it would turn out to be another oud-rose combo where you smell nothing else. But, somehow fortunately, I can hardly perceive the rose here. Everything feels well-rounded and harmonizes with each other, except for the initially mentioned bitter orange, which makes the fragrance enjoyable for me only after 5 minutes. What remains on the skin after 7-8 hours is a soft bed of fragrant woods with a touch of cream. Sillage is typically Montale, immediately filling the room. Only the bottles are and remain a disaster. I’ve had deodorant bottles that looked more high-quality. Well, it is what it is. The content is what counts, and it is truly enchanting. On cold days, its potential really comes to light, as I had to notice.

Initially a very normal, everyday scent. I definitely expected more from this. Not fascinating at all. With a name like this I want to be captivated! Neutral, simple and inoffensive.. It's not a bad fragrance, but there are definitely better and more interesting options in its price range. Strangely enough it is one of those scents that make me feel better when I'm down. When I'm low on energy or feeling nauseous F for Fascinating will make it better. My nausea will disappear and I'll be high on energy again. This is usually the case with citrus notes for me. Personally I don't care much for the scent, but the fact that is works almost like a medicine for me makes me appreciate it more.

Wonderful perfume wearable all seasons and for all ages. Long lasting a little spicy and fruity. The Jasmine note is not heavy, thats really good. S Ferragamo has captured a higly reccommended combination which will not let you down. Overall I am glad with my choise, that is really a high class perfume which can stand out. Do not overspray. EnjoY!!!

F for Fascinating is very pink and girly. In a way it is subtle, especially with its clean-like quality. It smells to me like a very feminine bar of soap. Clean and pretty. The mandarin orange isn't too strong in F for Fascinating, in fact it is somewhat synthetic. However this aspect does not bother me. Honestly this fragrance can give you a bad headache if you over-apply. As soon as the patchouli kicks in, it takes on a whole new meaning of sillage. I do love the patchouli though. It gives this fragrance that interesting earthiness. I'm not too familiar with chypres as I haven't been exposed to many, but from what I've experienced here in this fragrance, I understand the concept a lot better. F for Fascinating is simplistic yet fashionable. The lasting power is very good. I'm actually excited to wear this fragrance during Spring and Summer.

At the latest since Prada's bestseller, the word Candy immediately conjures up a tooth and nose burdening sugar bomb. When the house Montale also offers a Candy paired with rose, I fear the worst right away: an extreme gourmand with a piercing floral note. I have ignored the present sample long enough because I was so sure about what to expect. Only today, in search of a suitable sweet fragrance addition, did I dare a little test. And lo and behold: I must apologize, because this Montale surprises me greatly. (I should have guessed it; at the latest when Hannali started a sharing with CR some time ago, because it actually fits perfectly into her prey scheme.) For me, completely unexpectedly, "Candy Rose" is a light, delicate rose scent, a French ballet girl in a pale pink tutu, and not an oriental seductive treat, as is often the case with Montale. The dominant rose is accompanied by a bright fruity accord that takes away its dull mustiness. Only a very fine layer of powdered sugar lightly rests on top, not covering it but allowing the pink-white secret to shine through transparently. Initially, the poor "Candy Rose" only received 40 points from me, mainly because I am not a declared fan of rose scents. But that now seems a bit unfair. The fragrance is very well balanced, very elegant and feminine, making it very wearable. Lovers of delicate, fine floral scents will surely enjoy it. Nevertheless, it is questionable whether Candy Rose has enough character with its subtle restraint to make one want this particular rose. It does not necessarily come across as a compelling recommendation in the sense of "This rose and no other." At least a few fragrances in the "floral-fruity-transparent" direction come to mind that are similar. Perhaps the Montale-typical good longevity would be a decisive plus point against the competition.

~ Inspiration ~ I received "F for Fascinating Night" from the lovely Labello1. Before that, I wasn't familiar with this line from the brand Salvatore Ferragamo. ~ Bottle ~ The flat bottle with a wavy bottom has a black cap and a sort of "handle" on the neck, which I find a bit awkward when spraying. The name addition "Night" really doesn't fit... ~ Fragrance ~ Upon spraying, it is alcoholic and then fruity-floral. Sour mandarins create the citrusy opening. Roses provide a floral presence, rounded off with musk. Unfortunately, I don't perceive jasmine, patchouli, or amber at all. ~ Longevity ~ On my skin, it lasts about 4 hours (not much longer on clothing and hair). 2 sprays are enough; otherwise, it becomes too scratchy in my throat. ~ Occasion ~ It fits the mild days and evenings in spring and summer (I wouldn't wear it to the office). ~ Conclusion ~ It is too piercing in my nose. Unfortunately, it is nothing more than a generic synthetic fragrance :(

When I see the word "night" in a perfume name, I expect a heavy scent. In my opinion, F for Fascinating Night is light, floral, a bit fruity, and above all, feminine. But let's go in order: In the top note, you can perceive a fruity and somewhat sweet scent. Later, the rose joins in and pushes the fruitiness aside. The base finishes off the fragrance appropriately. The perfume is very feminine to me, but at the same time also light. The longevity is good. Since opinions on this perfume vary quite a bit (see diagrams), I would recommend testing the scent before purchasing to form your own opinion. The bottle is a bit unusual, as when I spray, it can happen that some of the perfume gets stuck on the black rim.

Are you looking for a scent that will make you stand out in the summer? Then Aqua Gold by Montale is just right, as it has an extremely good sillage, but the longevity on my skin is only about 4-5 hours. With its citrusy and spicy notes, you will definitely catch attention at the beach. It’s hard to describe the scent as it is sweet and fruity but also not overly fresh and spicy. I think the middle ground of both describes it very well. You can imagine the scent as being in the direction of Creed Aventus, just a bit fruitier and not so extremely masculine. Personally, I don’t like the scent as much anymore after some time, even though I really enjoyed it at first. I would also say that you should definitely not blind buy it‼️

This fragrance is one of my favorites. I am very glad that one day a friend of mine brought it for me to try. I applied this perfume to my wrist and simply lost my mind. I kept sniffing my wrist and inhaling the surprisingly thick, floral syrup. A rich brew of white flowers, honey, and molasses. Beautiful, a bit bitter, sweet, and absolutely feminine. I wear this perfume in every season. This is femininity and splendor in a bottle. For those who love expensive-sounding white flower compositions in perfumery, I can only highly recommend trying it out.

This fragrance certainly did not shock me. It was unexciting, bland and common in my opinion. Definitely not a fragrance that lived up to all the hype surrounding it. I wanted this fragrance to have that little bit of 'oomph', but instead it left me dissatisfied and waiting for more. The peony, ginger and mandarin notes were just a mess. I honestly would have liked to have seen more of a complexity in this fragrance, it was far too linear. The scent remained the same from the beginning until the last few seconds of the drydown, which was fairly average, consisting of around 2 hours. I'd probably skip this fragrance altogether and stick with the original Elle.

I have to agree with Miaw2, MOON AOUD is really a nice release, I gave for longevity and sillage also 75%, but after testing 3 oud from Montale and much more oud from other Perfume Hauses, I am not amazed. Rose and Sandalwood are almost compulsory accompanist of oud, saffron intrudes also very often to the picture. Heart notes can make MOON AOUD differ from other fragrances, unfortunately they do not get enough space and/or time on the stage. Even so this scent is more metallic, a bit winy, woody, and less sweet than other (braver and lamkin) ouds of Montale. I also have to tell, that who smelled real oud, that will find out within 10 seconds, that Montale's oud is synthetic. It is not a bad thing - taking into account the benefit of wildlife and nature, but it is also not the real thing.

Moon Aoud is not as loud as other Montale's releases. It's a low profile aoud based scent with a good lasting power as always. I pick up mostly roses and leather. Actually not very unique, but a great fragrance that deserves at least a try. Updated January 2014

When my dad was feeling "down," he would visit "his" antique dealer to feast his eyes and soothe his nerves. He was an advocate of "comfort buying" and also advised me to seek out a "feel-good place" during my emotional downturns. For me, that is "my" perfume shop. Immediately, I reflected on the shiny bottle of Moon Oud - as I have fond memories of Montales from my stepmother. It’s lovely to be reminded of dear people by fragrances. And Moon Oud is soft and rounded like a golden crescent moon. The oud is not harsh, but mild, perfectly complemented by precious saffron. Velvety rose joins in, and the leather note caresses the skin. Sweetness and creaminess are added by amber and sandalwood, which give the calm moon even more shine. One can sink into a contemplative "moon observation" - just like the two gentlemen in Casper David Friedrich's famous painting. A beautiful, contemplative evening scent - with a tendency towards romance.

I can only agree with my predecessor - if you know one, you somehow know them all; a criticism that seems quite valid for Montale's Aoud collection. Admittedly, the marginal differences are deeply hidden in the details, sometimes so concealed and intricate that one wouldn't even want to search for them for long. Therefore, anyone who wants to seriously approach this brand should bring a lot of patience. As expected, Aoud Moon seamlessly fits into the now quite confusing Montale universe; keeping track of it has become difficult and laborious. However, it is the mysterious name that caught my attention regarding this Oriental. When a fragrance bears the name "Moon," I think of a subtle, quiet, dark, and perhaps somewhat floral perfume. Indeed, Aoud Moon is clearly one of the more subtle Montale Aoud scents; for this time, it is not a showy, hot-headed Arab, but rather a romantic(!), though it is not a true wallflower either, but at least it keeps itself in check. However, attributes like mystical, melancholic, or mysterious are unfortunately not present here, but at least this attempt seems to have been made. Looking at it quite soberly, one could also claim that this is simply the umpteenth diluted version of Black Aoud, but Aoud Moon is fundamentally more than that. In this respect, my impression of this scent was quite accurate. Aoud Moon is once again a high-quality and (wonderfully) beautiful Oriental, but anyone who already has a Montale Aoud at home will be able to live without Aoud Moon without any problems.

I got a bottle of this last month and I'm very happy with it. I get compliments from many people. Everyone loves it..! It's a little bit more citrusy than the original which makes it amazing Scent : 8 most people like it Longevity: 9 lasts a whole day long Sillage : 9 can fill a room the first 2 hours and still projects well afterwards Price : 8 Get a bottle of it, you won't regret it! :)

"Black Aoud" by Montale was an oud milestone, even if the rose is just as prominently featured as the agarwood. No one with our hobby could avoid "Black Aoud" a few years ago. At least for a test of it. A true breaker, a polarizing legend. Now it's also in my collection; I just couldn't help it. Too unique, too dark, too gothic. Too good. A Batman rose. Even if I hardly wear it, only on winter evenings for fancy occasions... Now comes "Intense Black Aoud." As if anyone needed an even stronger version of it... But "IBA" leans more on the fame than the scent of its big brother and could have easily been called something else. At least it's not an even more explosive version of the black rose giant. That would be difficult. Much more, "IBA" is a fruitier version of this or the typical oud-rose combo from Montale. An overripe mandarin tries to balance its power and counter with zesty, prickly accords. It works okay, if not less. I prefer to stick with "BA," which goes all the way. This one feels like a compromise and an experiment. Patchouli makes it softer, but overall it feels very scratchy and unbalanced. Far from bad, but neither pleasant nor well-crafted. Montale seems to have hundreds of fragrances on offer. This one, despite all its punch and its big name, won't stick around or stand out. There are both better ouds and better mandarins. And roses even more so. In no discipline is this above average. That shouldn't be the goal. Difficult. Bottle: the gold-black gradient is nice and fitting. The rest is standard. Sillage: similar to "Black Aoud" or other heavy hitters from Montale - you won't fly under any radar with this... Longevity: you’re already asleep when the scent disappears... 12 hours. Conclusion: "Intense Black Aoud" connects a bit more mandarin-like to "Black Aoud," but is neither more intense nor better. But anyone who knows "Black Aoud" knows that its potency is enough for three ice ages... Rather, "IBA" is brighter, easier to wear, sharper. More artificial and hyperactive. There are easily a dozen prettier (A)Ouds in the wide Montale wardrobe!

I don't know how many Montales I have already held in my hands (especially thanks to Bartholomeo), but I have mentioned several times that this brand has a pretty clear concept in my mind: quite loud, very rose-heavy, aggressively oriental, hefty, enveloping. "Aoud Shiny" also largely hits the familiar mark, with an expansive rose at its center, coming across relatively pure with an eastern accent, slightly fruity, a bit cooling from violet leaf, drifting slightly into earthy-sweet territory through patchouli. Where the namesake oud is supposed to be, I’m not quite sure, aside from the aforementioned rather intense three aromas, of which the rose clearly maintains the upper hand. Those who enjoy it lushly rose-oriental will find "Aoud Shiny" to be one of the somewhat better, more wearable, not quite so affected Montales. Personally, I don't really take to any of them.

I had planned to gradually try out the Montale Aouds over time. Was that really such a good idea? They are all so similar! Aoud Shiny falls in line with Black Aoud and Steam Aoud, but has much less wood than especially BA. And the rose has noticeably changed with the addition of violets. It’s just a bit lighter here, that’s all. This makes Aoud Shiny a tiny bit sweeter than Aoud Rose Petals, which it is quite close to. The scent also has a slightly soapy quality, as if there were musk in it. I had imagined the violets to be a bit more pronounced and hoped for a kind of Montale meets Prada pour Homme. But that’s not the case, unfortunately! Of course, the quality of the scent is on par with the other ouds. There’s nothing to criticize there. It’s just that whether you choose Aoud Rose Petals, Aoud Flowers, or this one, it makes almost no difference. Well, this one is a tad milder and perhaps a bit more feminine. But still quite unisex. With so many similarities and so much choice, it’s pretty difficult and time-consuming to find a personal favorite. In direct comparison, I can say that I actually prefer Aoud Rose Petals, as it’s somehow more sparkling, not so soapy-creamy. Anyway, I’m not complaining; I wanted it this way! I will continue my explorations of the Montale Aouds, but will only comment briefly if they continue to be so similar.

Where to start with this wonder? Whenever I lay my eyes on the box with the characteristic blue/black/silver colours I get goosebumps. That is how good this perfume is. I have the EdT and I use it quite often, because I know I can still buy it, event though I know it is the new edition from 2003. But this… the parfum. No longer available and therefore a fragrance I treasure. I only use it on really special occasions. Last time I wore it, was at my father’s 80th birthday. I am amazed every time how unique and perfect the mix of notes is for me. Longevity is also immense. That is why it is so great for parties – it lasts the whole night through. I get compliments, when I wear it. It sneaks up on people and seduces them. You cannot resist Rive Gauche Parfum. My dream is to own a Rive Gauche EdT from the 70s. Year 2, 171/365

This fragrance was a blind buy, where I realized more than ever that you should test scents before buying them! The smell of old, unpleasantly scented soap with a hint of stinky flower is unfortunately not for me, sorry… If you like soapy scents, you might want to give it a try, but unfortunately, this fragrance will not stay with me.

If I really try, I can just about keep track of the essentials, but I've long given up on the Aaaaaaouds! Since I quite liked the "orange line," I consciously ordered this sample, but somehow I must have missed the fact that there is a pink sign painted on top. Because Orange Flowers is thoroughly a women's fragrance that clearly acknowledges this and doesn't always pretend to be the obligatory lukewarm "unisex"! Orange Flowers slightly reminds me in the top note of the unsweetened version of Cedre by Serge Lutens... but that was just the calm before the storm, as a monster wave of flowers, blossoms, and great sweetness follows! The only thing I can really pick out from the potpourri is the orange blossom, which you can recognize in hints from APOM Homme and Femme, more Femme of course, and the delicious honey. However, it's hard to focus on a single note, as the nose constantly has to battle with something new, which can be quite exhausting at times. Nevertheless, it smells quite good from a man's perspective (on a woman!), even if it becomes sweeter and unfortunately also more cloying hour by hour, without being a gourmand, as nothing in this fragrance is sugary. In the middle part, it briefly reminded me of Narciso (EDT/EDP), even though the roses are missing up top... that only flashed briefly and was then swept away by the next wave of flowers. At the end, I can still detect a small dose of laundry detergent musk, but that's about it. The longevity is, as usual, very very good; it easily lasts 8 hours, and the sillage is very strong, here 2 sprays should be enough to fill the office. Not a bad fragrance, but also nothing that blows me away; I'd rather invest the money in APOM Femme or APOM Femme Elixir, as that one has real style!

I’ll keep it short and sweet today - just like the hot pants that are supposed to be banned in schools *gg* Orange Flowers immediately reminds me of "Nuit de cellophane" by Serge Lutens upon spraying. It’s quirky, herbaceous fruity, and smells like summer. Orange blossom, mandarin, jasmine, and ylang-ylang are absolutely prominent. Underneath, there’s a hint of vanilla pod, which, however, brings very little "sweetness." It’s a scent that can quickly become overwhelming if applied too generously. Better to spray lightly again later. Otherwise, it lasts great, and you keep catching whiffs of that delicious orange, the flowers, and really, all that’s missing now is a big flower in the hair, coconut shells on the breasts, and a grass skirt, yayyyyy.... laugh! *oops - sorry*

Vetiver des Sables is not a fragrance that captures the authentic scent of the sea; rather, it olfactorily conveys the abstract image of jumping into cold seawater for me. The moment of diving in, actually far too cold, but with no way to do anything about it, you are enveloped by cold water, refreshed and awakened. There is no progression in the classical sense, and the fragrance pyramid hardly helps in the description. A very cool, almost icy synthetic freshness is constantly perceptible. It is made as well as, for example, in Nomenclature's "shi_so". This freshness, clearly underlined with marine accents and salt, initially has a slightly metallic quality. The almost rusty impression that lingers for a long time I would attribute to a straw flower. Diffuse wood notes from ISO (a material I usually find little appeal in) are very well integrated in the background. Increasingly, Vetiver joins this feeling of jumping into the cool water. Strangely fresh-green, it shows a new facet alongside the cool synthetic notes. A Vetiver sea ice on a stick. Impressive! The base becomes softer. Distinct musk notes provide warmth, but the fresh impression remains. So far, I must say, my expectations of Montale were rather low. Especially due to the overwhelming Aoud collection, from which I have not liked any so far. But with this fresh fragrance, they have surprised me. The longevity is very good, and the sillage is noticeably perceptible for a long time. I do not see a similarity to Fougere Marine. Those who appreciate well-made synthetics should definitely test this!

The sabers of vetiver, truly apt and fitting. Until now, I had only associated Montale with its various oud-rose interpretations, maybe a gourmand or two. But a vetiver scent? I wouldn't have expected that from them, especially not one so sharp and extraordinary. A fragrance like the clashing of sabers - sharp, silver-glimmering, and piercing. Not entirely to my taste and a bit too resinous and high for me, but definitely worth testing, and I have never smelled vetiver interpreted like this before. The scent starts like a repelling synthetic bomb, a rusty saber stab from an old pirate right into the nose. Minty-fresh, but totally exaggerated and metallic. Slowly, this cold spray clarifies, and the pirate scent becomes more restrained, sandier, creamier. Now it lives up to its name and shows an airy vetiver, or better said, vetiver grass. Quite dry, marine, cool. Like a creepy ghost ship that emerges from the fog, covered in algae, and runs aground on a sandy beach. This ship is made of the darkest mahogany wood and was probably a real masterpiece before its ghostly journey. In its current form, I wouldn't even accept it as a gift, nor would I want to wear the scent. Bottle: of all Montales, I find the silver bottles to be the most lackluster, even though they shine beautifully. Sillage: strong for 1 hour, especially for a vetiver. But as it becomes creamier, it gets tamer. Longevity: good to very good at 8 hours. An interesting vetiver variant, even if it turned out a bit too harsh and rusty. Still a sharp piece that once again proves Montale's class and sparks interest in testing the supposedly similar vetiver scents from Annick Goutal and The Different Company.

In this fragrance, a crucial ingredient that gives it its name has been forgotten! Namely, vetiver! Where is it? Under this gigantic blanket of peppermint oil? This scent is so sharp that it almost brings tears to your eyes. It almost burns. By "spices," I mainly understand a peppery menthol here, paired with woody notes that I can't particularly dissect. It might be patchouli; after a few hours, the scent reminds me of Patchouli Leaves, also by Montale. Very earthy. Freshly sprayed, the fragrance is several sizes too big; it hits hard and around. A bit ... hard to say ... moldy. Not nice, but rare. No, I definitely do not recommend this. It's a bit too much menthol and mint for me. By the way, I didn't find a single blade of vetiver.

Vetiver Des Sables has somewhat passed me by among the Montales, as I didn't find the listed sparse notes particularly exciting. I expected a herbaceous-woody autumn/winter scent from my finally ordered sample, but I was thoroughly surprised. The first thing that hit my unsuspecting nose was insect spray. Yuck. For about 2 seconds. Upon closer sniffing, the penetratingly synthetic insect repellent reveals itself as a strange metallic freshness accord, and not nearly as off-puttingly synthetic as it seemed at first. Something like a combination of mint and clove oil, or better yet menthol and eugenol, on a sharp lemon note creates an image of a harbor basin full of old rusting ships, iodine-laden cool sea air, and a stiff breeze that slaps cold spray in your face while your mouth is full of ice candies and lemon juice. It smells just as strange as it reads, and many will surely find it quite awful. I find it - admittedly after a brief adjustment period - rather fascinating. The similar, but non-metallic seawater accord in Montale's Fougere Marine was also appealing to me, but Fougere scents can be quite difficult for women to wear. This spray here is definitely more unisex. The slightly sweet ice candies are sucked away after a good hour, the lemon juice spat out, and the harbor basin with the rusted barges lies behind us. The salty sea freshness lingers for hours, now underpinned by a woody base. The titular vetiver grass adds a bit of woody green, but you really have to search for it. The vetiver actually grows here in loose sand - no earthy, creaky root note in sight. How exactly the "sand vetiver" reaches the sea is probably better left unexamined from a botanical perspective. The spices remain hidden from me - which is a shame. I would have found a journey from the harbor basin along the beach to an oriental bazaar quite exciting. Anyone hoping for a vetiver scent like MPG's "Route du Vetiver," Lalique's "Encre Noir," or Villoresi's green-earthy-herbaceous "Vetiver" will likely not be happy with "Vetiver Des Sables." Those looking for a lonely cool beach by the sea (without sunblock-soaked tourists) might find it more to their liking. In a similar direction are, for example, Annick Goutal's Vetiver (whose scents unfortunately develop into strange creations on my skin) and the Vetiver from The Different Company. I found "Sel de Vetiver" very beautiful, but it was a bit too light for me. The very salty and iodine-rich vetiver beach from Montale is more my style - far less subtle, more sea, though for my taste it could have used a bit more vetiver and a bit less ice candy. Still, a strong candidate for the next summer that (hopefully) will come someday. The longevity is, by the way, very good for a seawater freshness scent.

Unlike its Creed’s namesake sibling, which is all about “royal” with zero oud, Royal Aoud by Montale contains a ton of (synthetic) oud with a very little dose of “royalty”. In fact, like most of other scents by this brand, it isn’t exactly the most refined or “luxurious” scent around; but I admit I do see the efforts of making something a bit more sophisticated than their average standards. Also, contrary to many other more recent ouds by Montale which contain the same exact flat accord of mostly dry cedar with a weak oud-like shadow, Royal Aoud seems belonging to their “slightly-closer-to-reality” family of ouds – the nicer and more quality ones. Don’t get me wrong, oud here is still artificial to the bone, but it’s quite substantial, and it shows some complex, even nearly-natural-smelling nuances: the note smells in fact medicinal, compellingly woody, slightly “fecal” too at the beginning, quite robust and dirty, with a solid earthy-oily foundation just like real agarwood. Shortly it’s not just a slap of depressingly linear and shallow dry-cedary rubber, and that’s already something with Montale. So far, I got some “good imitation oud” only out of White Aoud and Aoud Cuir d’Arabie – and now, Royal Aoud. Also, it’s surely enjoyable how they chose to pair it with an initial solid whiff of clean, bracing citrus, and a sort of floral-resinous, slightly candied base accord, which sweetens and tames down the acrid, medicinal-dirty nature of the oud note, finally revealing a quite pleasant, comforting musky-soapy rose heart with a classic British “barbershop” vibe (an association also enhanced by the presence of citrus). There’s even quite some evolution as hours pass: from a sharp, bitter, dark and quite bold citrus-oud opening to a mellow, powdery, clean yet somehow a bit stale “whiter” rose-medicinal drydown still bearing some light fruity-grassy echoes of citrus, reminding me a bit of White Aoud’s drydown (less sweet and plushy, still musky-vanillic but a bit fresher, darker, greener and more austere). That’s quite a transition overall, which is another evidence of the above-the-average quality of this fragrance - compared with other Montale’s, I mean. Nothing to break the bank for, but more than nice to wear and also quite “easy” to pull off. Kudos! 7/10

I am currently in an oud testing phase and have thus arrived at Royal Oud by Montale. Since Montale is considered a master of oud fragrances due to its many years of experience in the Middle East, I thought it was worth a try. I am a pure oud enthusiast, but in the original sense, meaning where oud naturally smells like oud! This is not the case here! The oud smells rather synthetic, and the worst part is this EXTREME medicinal note that almost causes a gag reflex during the first hour after spraying. After the first hour, the medicinal smell fades, but it remains present until the end. I didn’t smell any spices at all. Grapefruit does give the fragrance a certain freshness, yet the medicinal smell is still the most noticeable! So from me, the rating is: terrible! Nevertheless, I will test some more Montale ouds.

royal Oud Yes, we have that here. The Oud note is finely balanced and perfectly dosed. It is accompanied by some truly delightful companions. Grapefruit and kumquat provide a certain freshness and fruitiness. Spices, which I cannot specify further, accentuate the grace of the Oud. It comes completely without any sweetness, and the longer it is on the skin, the more beautiful and softer it becomes. Overall, an elegant fragrance, definitely suitable for year-round wear.

Very nice smell. Sweet, vetiver, little bit smokey. Masculine vibe for sweetness. Excellent. Little bit baccarat rouge vibe in a drydown. Very pleasant, very affordable, sexy sillage. Good price. Some people smeels like maison martin margiela by the fireplace… absolutely no, thos is airy vibe not choke sweet

Poaaah, Egon Kowalski would say. My neck hairs stand up and I start to sweat slightly. I’m sticky all over, but that’s OK because I’m in the swinger club of my choice and I know everyone can smell me. Whether you like it or not, I don’t care at all because I polarize. Jokes aside, the beginning of this fragrance is intoxicating; it feels like I had my nose too close to super glue and now I’m in a mess…. But time heals all wounds, and after a few minutes (which feel like hours), I’m enveloped in the pleasantly warm notes of incense, wood, and tonka, inviting me to enjoy the evening in ecstasy. A demanding fragrance, an absolute bomb for my nose. But I can also understand anyone who doesn’t like this scent DNA. Well, luckily for me, that means more Coc…. uh, I mean of course Wood on Fire.

I received six Montale samples for my birthday, and the first one is "Wood on Fire." When I read the name, I thought it would be a nice woody scent. Nothing stood in the way, and now I've sprayed the first spritz on my palm. Immediately, a smell hit my nose that felt very familiar. I didn't have to think long, and Tom Ford Ombre Leather popped into my mind. At first, you strongly smell the leather with a hint of lemon, which you don't really notice until you smell it a few times. After the third sniff, I realized that this scent is very strong, which I noticed by getting slight headaches. After a few more minutes, I could smell the sandalwood, but I can recommend the scent to those who love leathery fragrances or want to experience something strong in their nose. Definitely a scent that has power! Update: After a longer time, you can hardly smell the leather, but instead, the incense, which is much more pleasant to smell.

Fruits of the Musk is a completely, desperately synthetic fruity scent, as much milky-syrupy as pungent and artificial. White vanillic musks on the base, together with a dry, dusty and artificially earthy note of patchouli. That’s it, perfectly identical to itself for hours. Boring, cheap, plain, with the same quality, elegance and creativity of the worst celebrity fragrance out there. 4/10

Have you ever known someone extremely wealthy who has, let us put it as diplomatically as possible: less-refined tastes? Well, Montale has issued a perfume to cover that niche: FRUITS OF THE MUSK. I was really hoping that this would be the fruity-floral to refute all of the stereotypes: the shining example of how even in this homely genre, great perfumes are to be had. Sad to say, but I was wrong. There are some rich and delightful fruity-floral perfumes around--though they certainly do not abound and are in fact quite difficult to find--but FRUITS OF THE MUSK is not a member of that tiny group. Instead, this composition seems like a very straightforward mainstream designer fruity-floral fragrance featuring the proverbial "red berries" and "abstract flowers". FRUITS OF THE MUSK is really nothing to write home about and even less to spend big Montale bucks on to acquire. This juice would have fit quite nicely in the next garish-hat-topped Coty Prestige flanker bottle. Désolée.

From my perspective, there isn't much to say here. It's an average good and rather rare composition. Initially, unfortunately a bit artificial and synthetic, this fragrance develops a warm, slightly fruity musk note in the base. Dear Montale, please refine this, there are people who have been waiting for such a combination!

What a name: "Fruits of the Musk". Sounded very exciting to me, as I like musky scents as well as fruity perfumes. This one smells great of musk and raspberries. A very nice musk note accompanies the entire perfume, it neither becomes soapy nor sharply artificial. Really very well balanced and harmonious. The top notes are also well chosen. I can already detect a fruity component right after spraying, clearly raspberry, not too sweet or cloying, but really very pleasant, not at all intrusive. In my eyes, it fits excellently with the musk accord. A slightly delicate rose scent in the background comes into play over time. Everything is really wonderful, a lightly powdery rose with raspberries. If it weren't for this green note that starts to mix in at some point. I can't quite place it, maybe the "strawberry leaf", but unfortunately I have no idea what that smells like. In any case, this green slightly herbal note is the disruptive factor for me in this scent. It takes away the raspberry's light sweetness and blends with the powdery rose. After a while, I no longer recognize any fruity notes, and the rose note has receded more and more, leaving behind a green musk accord. Not bad, the scent now feels fresher and also more unisex than in the initial phase. But it's not what I was looking for. Longevity is very good; I could perceive the green musk note on my wrist for a long time.

I have a tester bottle which says "YSL Baby Doll" and "Eau de Toilette magique, Eau de Toilette légère/Magic Eau de Toilette, Light Eau de Toilette". It looks like the one posted by Aquila2110 with the silhouettes of people on its shoulder. As mine is however even a lighter edition (EdT légère) of this flanker (a flanker of the flanker?), it lists only the three following notes: passion fruit (top notes), fresh jasmine (heart notes) and musks (base notes). Either they omitted to put the whole list on the tag or it is a lighter fragrance altogether. In any way this EdT starts with strong juicy, mouthwatering passion flower, in which the jasmine mixes gently in. It is a very subdued jasmine note while the passion flower still goes on strong. In the base notes the passion flower is less loud but still noticeable while the musk has only a tiny support role. All in all a wearable spring and summer scent with a tropical vibe which is quite noticeable and stays for quite a while when sprayed abundantly. The whole flanker business is beyond me, but probably because in the end I don't care that much for this perfume.

hmm, you are in my opinion the better Arabians Tonka in the rose category, also your oud I find better/more intense, more powerful. But you can't really be compared to him. You are actually the Oud Republic from which I would have expected this nuance, a bit rougher, not so red rosy, very elegant. Actually, it's hard to categorize you, more of a women's or men's fragrance, but the woman who wears you probably has no problem taking on men. Your pink outfit somewhat misleads about what’s inside you and your brand doesn’t have the, let’s say, best reputation. In conclusion, I see you as one of the top 5 new releases of 2025 that have come my way, and I will probably be accommodating you soon.

I like leather in all its forms. My relationship with rose is far less clear-cut, and usually it's more of a no than a yes. (That's why I always get even more excited when I come across a rose perfume that can truly captivate me).. The duo of rose and leather, which is anything but original, has never managed to win me over until now. It's different here. The leather-rose dance is absolutely perfectly choreographed, down to the millisecond. And there’s nothing else there - just rose and just leather. And I miss nothing. And: the rose comes across so relaxed and rounded here that I even enjoy wearing and smelling this scent in the heat - while all my other leather favorites have been put into hibernation. I find the longevity to be above average, even among the Montales, of which I already own several: I entered my office after 5 days of vacation and immediately smelled the Arabians-Rose-Leather. Speaking of Arabians. This scent is absolutely not Arabic or oriental to me. Rather, it feels very European. It could be from Armani Privee ;) P.S. You have to give it a second chance. Upon first sniff, I only had the impulse to sell it quickly, and I listed the sample at the souk. Luckily, no one bought it so quickly, otherwise I would have missed out on this love. Thanks for that! :)) P.P.S. A few days later, I want to add to my review: The longevity of this perfume is simply amazing. Even though I wear something different every day (and usually not in small amounts), this scent lingers in every room where I spend time for days, definitely surpassing everything in terms of longevity.

From the first spray, pure femininity flows towards me… rose geranium, pepper, myrrh, dried plum, cistus, bourbon vetiver, incense, cedarwood… I perceive mandarin and incense only as decorative embellishments that do not really stand out but blend into the overall composition. A composition that is, for my nose, perfect, resting on a soft bed of vanilla that I perceive, although vanilla is not explicitly listed. Gentil Suono clings delicately to my skin, exuding a veil of the finest fragrance notes in my immediate surroundings without being intrusive or ever too much. The sprayer is very fine and lays just a mist of the scent on my neck. I receive many compliments for it and wear it even in the office. I can imagine Gentil Suono almost year-round; the test and purchase were at around 24 degrees, and it was amazing, but even now, with slightly more autumnal temperatures, the love between us has only grown stronger. At first, it is a bit liqueur-like, but it becomes beautifully soft and feminine over time, ending with a woody-gourmand base. I myself do not perceive the scent as much after about 5 hours and then apply another spritz, simply because I love the scent so much and want to sniff it again and again. The fragrance is quite exclusive; you can find it online and in very few Salvatore Ferragamo shops. The entire collection is worth a sniff test… I was able to test them all in the store in Paris… it was pure perfume heaven. The ladies there in the shop were very accommodating and helped me patiently and supportively with my selection without being intrusive. I would definitely advise against a blind purchase; the SF fragrances from the Tuscan Creation collection come across quite differently on the skin than in the description. I crown Gentil Suono as my signature scent; it has completely captivated me and is the perfect companion for hopefully a long time…

I purchased the Eau de Toilette Incanto Bloom online at a good price. The bottle is really pretty. Attractive design in pink - rose. Unfortunately, the scent is not as lovely and balanced as one might expect from its appearance. Upon spraying, it smells very alcoholic - fruity to me. It really reminds me of a fruit schnapps. I couldn't say which fruit it is made from. Most likely, it's raspberry. After about 30 seconds, it develops into a somewhat prickly, generic scent with medium sillage. You really have to endure that for a good half hour. It smells fruity - green with a skewed woody undertone. After an hour, the perfume starts to round out. The prickliness dissipates, and to my nose, it becomes fruity - floral - sweet. Only now does Incanto Bloom consider becoming pleasant, so as not to completely scare off its users. I perceive the sweetness that you smell now as a floral sweetness. I think I smell rose. Maybe it's the yellow tea rose. That reconciles me with the perfume again. I find it quite wearable in summer. You can have it - but you don't have to.

What can I really say about this relatively new fragrance? One of the usual fruity scents. "Incanto Bloom" starts off carefree, synthetically fresh, citrusy, and with a green note. Ambroxan, like in one of the usual perfume sections of drugstores or department stores, wafts steadily through the room. Then the direction changes, "Incanto Bloom" becomes indifferently fruity. What I mean is: I can't determine which fruits are intended, it just smells like a bag of mixed gummy candies. I certainly enjoy eating that, but I don't want to smell like it. Then, however, "Incanto Bloom" turns honey-sweet. Here I would suspect cistus/labdanum. This sweetness cuts down a good part of the Ambroxan dominance. It doesn't create a particularly distinctive scent for "Incanto Bloom." But now I can imagine that perfume users who like fruity scents and also sweet ones will get along well with it. And now I notice: Huh, where are the listed floral notes? I haven't perceived them. I had a fresh original sample; otherwise, I would think that the bottle might have suffered. But maybe the sweet honey scent can be interpreted as a floral note. However, I don't find tea rose or even the strong white floral scent of champaca magnolia represented in "Incanto Bloom." The longevity is good, the sillage is subtle. It is, of course, a feminine fragrance.

~ Inspiration I love my "Incanto Charms" by Salvatore Ferragamo and have been repurchasing it (since 2001) time and again. While browsing, I came across "Incanto Amity" and ordered the fragrance, so to speak, blind. ~ Bottle ~ The oval, colorful glass bottle is cute and playful, just as one expects from the "Incanto" line. A flower and a small hummingbird are depicted on the front, with green and pink colors dominating. "Amity" translates to "friendship." ~ Scent ~ Upon spraying, it is floral-fresh. Zesty mandarins create a slightly tart opening (the special melon, unfortunately, only comes through very faintly in the background). Jasmine and lotus flowers form a floral-aquatic heart. With cedarwood and a hint of musk, it softly and gently fades away. ~ Longevity ~ On my skin, it lasts about 4 hours (not much longer on clothing and hair). 2-3 sprays are enough for me; otherwise, it unfortunately becomes quite piercing and synthetic at the beginning. ~ Occasion ~ A fresh, floral-fruity, green-aquatic (office) scent for the warmer and hot days in spring and summer. ~ Conclusion ~ I had hoped it would be somehow sweeter due to the melon and jasmine notes. Unfortunately, it lacks the special quality that I love in "Incanto Charms," and it remains just an average drugstore fragrance.
I had bought this body spray twice back then - when it was still available. A great addition to the EdT. It emphasized the entire scent close to the skin. You can't say more than that!

It is a nice Woody fragrance, Light, Fresh and Aquatic, Longevity is average. It opens up with like fresh citrusy and green notes in the background then dry down is musky woody. This is perfect for the spring and summer, The art of bottle design is beautiful with heavy cap . I like Incanto Essential Pour Homme EDT by Salvatore Ferragamo. Rating : 7.5 / 10

Today I would like to contribute a comment on this wonderful platform. I have chosen Incanto pour Homme Essential from my collection. Originally, I only rated it 30%. However, for various reasons, this has positively improved to 70%. When you apply this fragrance early in the morning after showering, the ingredients used feel invigorating. The slightly citrusy note of yuzu unfolds gently, not intrusive, and remains detectable for some time alongside the rosemary. After about an hour, you can smell a hint of violet leaves, which mixes with sandalwood and cedar. The musk is barely noticeable. It lasts then between 4 to 5 hours. I like this scent because it gives the feeling of starting the day fresh and clean. In my opinion, it fits well in offices with several colleagues, as it stays in the background and doesn't disturb anyone. It is not a particularly refined scent. Nor is it loud. It is functional.

With the men's perfume "Salvatore Ferragamo," this brand released a wonderfully elegant and rare combination of fig leaf and vetiver, a true stroke of luck and unfortunately already discontinued. Since then, what has come out in men's fragrances has belonged to the background noise of the perfume industry for me. Mid-priced middle-class and rather unremarkable. Now I received a sample of Incanto pour Homme Essential from Ophelia, but unfortunately, I couldn't change my opinion. Incanto pour Homme Essential belongs to a fragrance direction that I only moderately appreciate - an aquatic fresh scent with a distinct musk base. Citrusy top notes (where is the lychee?), the typical sharpness and scratchiness of many mass-market perfumes, and a somewhat synthetic fresh note - at least subtle - are the main characteristics. I can't quite identify the indicated violet leaf note; I think it is meant to refer to an undefinable light candy-like sweetness at the beginning of the fragrance development. After just half an hour, the musk takes the helm on this ship; the aquatic-fresh impression now completely gives way to a penetrating soapy scent. Incanto pour Homme Essential is a perfume for those people who feel comfortable smelling like soap. Fortunately, there aren't too many of them. Personally, I still find occasional mishaps with the dosage of Le Male, Kouros, and A*Men more likable than the annoyance of soap.

At first, I think: Oh, it starts like Swiss Arabian Oriental Rose or much softer than Montale Intense Café. But this impression lasts only a moment, then the fragrance direction shifts slightly towards the fresher, citrusy side, so I now believe I have a descendant of Ajmal Wisal Dhahab in front of me, although it sometimes feels quite cool to me. Quickly, however, it becomes quieter and more reserved, and even this last impression eventually fades away. On my skin, the rose finally comes through a bit more, and the scent gains a "citrusy rosiness," while saffron with its slightly bitter note comes through more on fabric. So I have, in a way, two different fragrances from the same bottle. The vanilla cushions everything nicely on any base, rounding the edges, and together with musk, it creates a wonderful symbiosis. Oud remains in the background for my impression, contributing its typical note very delicately and almost casually. Amo Ferragamo Oriental Wood definitely stands out from the other women's fragrances in the family. A beautiful and, in my opinion, only slightly sweet oriental that delights the nose and senses with its beautiful aura and tender warmth. I could also imagine it on a gentleman, despite the above-mentioned tendency towards women's fragrances, who finds the usual men's scents too ordinary. Despite the restraint (with 2 sprays), I perceive it again and again. It surrounds me like a small fragrance dome, but it never overwhelms me. I admit it... I was drawn to it because of its beautiful bottle color. This stunning royal blue with a slight violet gradient towards the bottom immediately captivated me. That the scent residing in this almost magically appealing bottle is also so wonderful borders on a "Hole in One" hit for me! Or rather, a positive fragrance experience completely "out of the Blue"!

If you want to learn more about this fragrance, I recommend first reading the comments on the rive gauche Eau de Toilette. The classic EdT can be found here - in short - in a diluted form. It starts in the top note with a bergamot-freshness, the well-known strong aldehyde note has initially been banished in favor of the desired summery atmosphere. From the heart note onwards, the main focus is on the soft floral notes of freesia, jasmine, and rose. They have successfully tried to conceal the sharper elements of jasmine and rose. These then come through with the use of a hint of airy aldehydes, striking a lighter and carefree tone. The vetiver appears more subdued and forms a green woody connection with a trace of galbanum, which never becomes heavy, earthy, or even smoky. The oakmoss has also been reduced and comes across to me as a bit drier and less bitter in combination with the skin-like musk accord, which emphasizes a slightly summery mood. The fragrance is overall simply lighter, fresher, and more cheerful compared to the EdT, making it easier to wear in higher temperatures. I do not recommend the normal EdT for the summer heat due to the complexity of the scent. The 'Light' will either be immediately disliked by the classic 'rive gauche' customer, who will want to banish it as a "crétin": "My God, even lighter after the reformulation, just a shadow of its former self." Or she will immediately take it to heart because she can unabashedly spray her 'rive gauche' in the summer...finally one for Saint-Tropez at 28 degrees, where she enjoys her first drink at "Sénéquier" with friends in the evening before disappearing with her entourage to a small & chic restaurant in the countryside: "Well, there where there are no tourists, n'est pas." For me, the fragrance is successful because it represents a beautiful and truly new variation. 'rive gauche' has never been this clear, cheerful, casual, and above all modern before. You still recognize the classic 'rive gauche' aura, and thus also the actual date of origin of this fragrance. So, if you like fragrances in the "retro" style, you can gladly test this one, provided you can still find this edition somewhere. The longevity and sillage are good. Unfortunately, the 'Light' was released as a limited summer fragrance alongside the 'rive gauche pour homme light' and was only available in the summer of 2004. The 100 ml bottle cost only 39 euros back then...a nice offer. There was even a small advertising campaign where both 'Light' versions were lying on a pair of jeans along with various accessories like sunglasses and keychains, etc. The 'Light' flacon was shown here naked and unpainted except for the rings (a bikini?!), you can see the pure aluminum. Only a clear coat was used for sealing...mon dieu.

This one is from the same alien planet like Aoud Blue Notes. Where Aoud Blue Notes is more of a synthetic alien oud, this one is a synthetic alien grapefruit. It's metallic, synthetic, sour and fresh. The sourness is unique and strong and I really like it, it gives a different kind of fresh feeling. It's perfect for summer or hot weather.

Absolutely wonderful, luxurious, elegant unisex perfume. To me this smells like a cream of clean laundry and flowers. Really creamy and clean. Reminds a bit of aqua digio but much more rounded creamy and refined :-) Incredibly surprised, such a shame for the price. But this is absolutely spot on!

If only I knew which perfume this reminds me of… It is a floral, delicately feminine, and very clean-smelling fragrance. At first, it is quite synthetic, but that fades after about 15 minutes. The sillage is okay, the longevity is good. Actually, it is somewhat flat. And yet, I like it. It smells floral clean, and since I recognize the notes from somewhere, I feel transported to old times. A pleasant everyday scent that, in my opinion, suits younger ladies better.

I am grateful to Monsieur Montale for such a joyful interpretation of the appointment in/with Moscow.
