At first, I thought: is this going to be one of those scent clubs that knock you out on the train? But somehow, it behaved differently. Yes, the rose is lush, and patchouli gives it a good punch, but it doesn’t come off as cheap or overloaded. After a few minutes, it softens. The musk comes through, a bit of amber, everything draws closer to the skin. Someone mentioned during the evening: "You smell like something between rose and motor oil, but in a good way." I had to laugh. Between ambroxan and a light fruity note, there’s indeed a nearly metallic-clear warmth that reminded me of a scent I used to smell on a buddy (he drove Jaguar Classic Gold back then, so maybe the comparison isn’t entirely coincidental :-) ). In the room, the scent was distinctly noticeable, but not in a way that overpowers everything. I felt like it was always in motion, with something new emerging again and again. It has strength, but no rigid structure. Not a pure crowd-pleaser, but also not one that polarizes at any cost. The next morning, it was still on my scarf. Not dominant, but present. And somehow, I felt like the evening was a bit denser, a bit more tangible because of it. For me, it’s a scent for exactly such situations. Not for everyday life in an open-plan office, but for moments when you want to take up a bit more space without coming off like a perfume bomb.

Acqua di Colonia's Muschio has incredibly faint sillage, which is really its only drawback. Otherwise, this is a beautiful, almost mythical- powdery soft anisic and cardamom-laced musk- with a touch of creamy vanilla that is uniquely sexy without being particularly dirty. There is a dry talc note to this musk that is in a whole different category of what we often describe as "white" musk, as in it bears absolutely no resemblance to the Body Shop "White Musk" or OSMO's "Musc Bleu". This is my current favorite summer fragrance- it is intimate, natural and faintly soothing. Wearing this I feel pretty and simply stunning in a thin white silk dress. Acqua di Colonia is an ancient house- originated in 1612 with extremely pure high end formulations, thus another distinction is very little fixative chemical or irritants in these bottles. The bottle it self is a frosted clear glass version which matches well with the character of this scent. Reapplication is required about every 4 hours to detect the faint spell on my skin. This fragrance brings to mind images of a magical balmy summer night filled with luminescent fire flies dancing around a beautiful unicorn in total peace and safety- hidden far from the prying eyes of mere mortals.

Musc perfumes usually smell too synthetic to me, this is the most "natural" smelling musc I could find. The composition is very simple. It feels white, powdery and a little bit sweet, almost like toothpaste sweet, but in a good way. Makes me feel clean. Gives autumn/winter cozy white jumper vibes.

Sweet powdery musk and brightened by a bouquet of barely-there flowers and rounded off with warm amber. I don't really notice the rose. It's all rather homogeneous and one-dimensional; very nicely blended. It reminds me a bit of "hot shower steam", and ever so slightly of white chocolate. The sweetness is more subdued in the drydown.

I still remember my very first flight clearly. I was five years old and we were headed to the island of Rhodes. Everything was so new and exciting. The takeoff, the speed before lifting off, and especially that feeling of being pressed into the seat before the plane ascends into the sky. I found the landing to be cruel. That terrible pain in my ears that wouldn't go away even after many hours. The chewing gum recommended by my parents didn’t help at all. However, what fascinated me the most was something else. It was the clouds: The bird breaks through the cloud cover and you see those cozy-looking, brilliantly white cotton clouds from above. You have the feeling that they are stable, that you could just jump in and snuggle up. An illusion that makes children's eyes shine. I feel exactly that when I sniff Muschio by Santa Maria Novella. I have never experienced such a fine and wonderfully composed musk fragrance before. If there is a high-end category for pure musk scents, then this fragrance definitely falls into it. We have neither laundry detergent nor fabric softener here. That would all be too sharp and too synthetic and would not do justice to this wonderfully fluffy scent. It simply smells delicate, very lightly fresh, perhaps a hint of a noble skin cream that was applied a few hours ago, and it seems to melt on the skin, creating a noble overall composition between the scent of one's own skin and this perfume. It is so incredibly simple and yet so beautiful. In the base, the scent becomes slightly sweet, but always remains delicate and fluffy-fine. Even though the sillage is not very pronounced, I was able to perceive the fragrance I sprayed in the afternoon well into the late evening hours. A cozy white down blanket fits perfectly. It definitely has to be white, that’s the scent image. White like the clouds viewed from above. I see that Yatagan had this image as well. And just like him, I see this fragrance primarily on the feminine side, though it should not be denied to gentlemen. And I also agree with Susan, who got me hooked on this treasure. This fragrance, as simple and delicate as it may be, is damn sexy! My husband was enchanted and liked it immediately, and believe me, that doesn’t happen very often. Since it unfortunately wasn’t in stock during my shopping trip in beautiful Zurich yesterday, I have now pre-ordered it and will pick up my new fragrance love there before the end of the year. A heartfelt thank you to Susan, through whom I was able to get a first impression of the fragrance. It was so good that I tested it again and am now deeply in love. White clouds, here I come!

I would never wear a fragrance during a time of mourning. I have always thought this, no matter how much I love fragrances, how terrible it would be if a scent later reminded me of a sad time in my life? But perhaps that would be exactly the phase when I would need it the most: Before I tested Muschio in spring, only musk was listed as a fragrance note, and I read keywords like: Powdered sugar, feminine, like freshly creamed, fluffy, and ultimately, the angelic associations that made me want to test it. When I finally got to test it, my first impression was positive; I could easily relate to the associations. Sprayed on, it smelled creamy, sweet, delicate, fluffy, and the association of being freshly creamed fit perfectly. It was simply enchanting. However, there was something about Muschio that initially puzzled me; what was that animalic note? The scent of musk, in its purest form, fascinated me. So this was the scent of musk, all of that, but also spicy/bitter and animalic, yet so rare that the fragrance would not lose its tranquility. This is how it would probably smell in heaven if angels had a spa day. This perfume is truly something very special in my collection. I am usually drawn to extravagant scents that would likely be too strong, too sweet, and generally too much for others. If some of my fragrances could speak, they would probably talk a lot and be loud; some might even scream, they would definitely attract attention. And then there is Muschio. Muschio would not say much, beyond whispering. It would speak gently to you, like a good friend giving you advice. And a few months later, when life shows you again that you should truly enjoy every moment with your loved ones because you never know when a journey on this earth is complete, then Muschio feels like a hug that gives you the sense that everything will be alright. Yes, a perfume that feels like one of the most beautiful feelings - security. I know that you, where you are now, are not lonely and happy, and who knows, maybe you are smelling the same fragrance right now, because where you are now, angels are having a spa day.

Today, thanks to a dear Parfumo, I got to walk on soft, fluffy clouds. I jumped from little cloud to little cloud, daring a dive into a particularly fluffy and rose-colored cloud and was gently bounced back into the air. Stars twinkled in between and then disappeared. Star anise? Muschio is like a daydream.

When I first spritzed it on my skin I found it repulsive after 10 minutes I had a sort of a rose smell, so better than the opening but still nothing special after half an hour the smell had gone...so a no for me. At no moment I have thought this smells good. I got a decant and I even won't use that.

In the bottle and on my skin, by far, the most breathtakingly beautiful rose soliflore I have ever encountered. I have never experienced a rose so fresh, so pure, and yet so incredibly rich, deep, and heady. It's a gloriously intoxicating shower of roses dream. Everything I've ever dreamed of having in a soliflore rose blooms to extravagant perfection here. EVERYTHING! From bottle, to initial spray, to complete drydown, this is magnificent. I even love this just sniffing away at the bottle cap a la aromatherapy. I ADORE it on my skin. The base is also a smooth, rich, elegant mix of woods with a touch of incense. Still, the rose reigns supreme here from opening to drydown without any medicinal hospital antiseptic accords or rubbishy wilting chemical petal accords. No sickeningly sweet candy, vanilla, or other infantile sugar to sully this magnificent creation. The natural moderate sweetness derives from the very high quality of the rose extracts here. It is unique as far as rose scents go. There are dozens and dozens of rose scents out there. Fresh ones, clean ones, dark ones, spicy ones, oud ones, orientals, woody ones, and so on. This particular perfume has THE BEST rose absolute in it......of ALL OF THEM that I have smelled. I'm not saying it's the best perfume because we all have different chemistries and different tastes. I do feel confident in stating that to my nose, the quality of the rose absolute itself in this one is the best I've ever smelled regardless of what TYPE of fragrance you prefer. You can even detect the quality of it from just smelling the bottle top before spraying it on your skin. So, to clarify, I am making the comment regarding the particular quality of the rose absolute itself outside of what it smells like on my skin. (I happen to insanely love how it smells on my skin as well.) This lasts about 8 hours on the skin and is a parfum extrait. This is not a shy EDT or EDP. As far as I'm concerned, no other rose soliflore even comes close. If you truly love roses, this could easily be your holy grail of rose soliflores. Without question, it has become mine. Pierre Montale, you have my heartfelt gratitude for this creation, thank you.

This one simply knocks you off your feet: rose oils - in their purest and most concentrated form. And this is where my objections starts: You might as well buy pure rosa damascena, turkish rose and rosa centifolia oils and mix them yourself - ready is your "Highness Rose Fragrance" (at a much lower price). Where is the artistry in that? The perfume feels like a fantastic aroma-therapeutic rose oil session, but it is devoid of any creativity and offers no fresh ideas on "roses". I'd rather stick to the good old Perfumer's Workshop Tea Rose ... - since Tea Rose comes much closer to the scent of real roses on a stem in your garden. "Highness Rose" smells of rose OILS - a very different smell from the actual flower outside.

A Benjamin Button situation of a rose. At first spray, it's plumes of something an antique-y and vintage-y. It put me off for a while before I revisited it. I think it's the rose in combination with the stringent petitgrain. But it soon relaxes and the tension gives way to something more youthful, sweet, and lemon-y. It's actually a dead ringer for Skinfood's Black Sugar mask which has a light citrus scent. So that's probably where I got the sugar-lemon association. In contrast to a lot of other reviewers, I think it's a modern offering from SMN compared to their usual, aged apothecary assortment.

Rose fragrances are not my thing.....it is solely thanks to the persuasive power of the very competent Gesa Hotzen from Santa Maria Novella Munich that I even tested this scent.... “You don’t like rose..? Then this is the perfect rose fragrance for you...!! A completely new interpretation of this note...” And how right she was..!! The combination of rose and citrus fruits creates something completely unusual and unique......the acidity of the citrus fruits lightens the rose, removing its heaviness and stuffiness, making it shine with a fruity-fresh quality....as if there were such a thing as a “rose fruit”.......this surprising and beautiful first impression is underlined by a gentle floral hint.......really just a hint..... Soon a fine herbal note joins in......not pizza oregano and not sharp-biting T-bone steak pepper......the herbs rather sprinkle the scene with a subtle spiciness that gives the fragrance an extremely noble quality......I spontaneously picture an elegantly dressed, striking Milanese woman who masters the game of seduction as well as the trade in stocks.... The scent development concludes with an incredibly beautiful and warm gentle-mossy base..... All in all, it is a very subtle fragrance......understated and with remarkable class......it smells to me of dignified calmness and complete femininity ..

Year 1221, Monastery Santa Maria Novella, Florence, Italy. The monks of the Dominican order decide to establish the house Officina Profumo Farmaceutica di Santa Maria Novella. In the garden of the monastery, they cultivate medicinal plants, study their healing properties, and prepare unique essences, balms, and healing ointments. The turning point comes in 1533 when the monks create the perfume “l’Aqua della Regina” - the first perfume of the house Santa Maria Novella. The reason for this is the wedding of Caterina de Medici and Henry II - King of France from the Valois dynasty. For a long time, production was secluded and only carried out within the monastery walls, but in 1612 the pharmacy opened its doors to the general public, making its unique products accessible to everyone, first in Italy and then beyond. The Grand Duke of Tuscany grants the production the title “Workshop of His Royal Majesty.” Even to this day, this oldest Florentine pharmacy has preserved its traditions and proudly presents its unique creations. All products are made only from herbs and ingredients of natural origin and are not tested on animals. I have come to know “Acqua della Regina” (Water for the Queen), a citrus fougère fragrance that I also liked very much and noted down, but I particularly highlighted “Rosa Novella,” which absolutely must find a place in my collection! “Rosa Novella” is the epitome of the scent that fills the garden of Santa Maria Novella in May. At the start, the cologne gives a proper citrus burst that feels zesty and fresh, and then makes way for a subtle rose scent. It is so beautiful! This rose is rather green, not least because it is composed together with oregano and moss. It is without oily or velvety heaviness in the background; on the contrary: it shines like a debutante at a ball - fragile, graceful, full of dreams and plans… Rosa Novella lasts on my skin for up to 4 hours, which is remarkable for an Eau de Cologne. A light, delicate veil remains, and I am glad that it is time to spray myself again with this amazing feel-good scent!

At the latest since Julia Fischer's novel "Gallery of Scents," I have also come to know the "Officina Profumo-Farmaceutica di Santa Maria Novella" in Florence. Also, during the writing of this review, I drew on "Parfumos" knowledge and, curious from the announcement of the novel, bought this book back then. Since then, I have been a regular visitor to this traditional establishment while reading, admiring every room, every corner, every shelf, and strolling through this fragrant narrative with the protagonists of the novel, whom I have grown quite fond of. Two generations of lovers from Florence and Munich find their place in this fragrant tale. Anna, the student from Munich, ultimately loses her heart and a little more in a night under blooming apple trees in a magical garden to the charming Giovanni Fontini, whom she believes to be a carefree painter and dreamer. She decides to escape the enchantment of the city and the man and returns to Munich. The two little apple trees he gives her as a farewell gift find a special place in the garden of the marital pharmacy and, of course, also in her heart. Twenty years later, her daughter Johanna dreams of business relations with the Fontini family company and unknowingly follows in her mother's footsteps, getting caught in the scent nets of two of her men: Giovanni's nephew! Here is the charismatic and creative whirlwind Alessandro/Sandro, who is currently working on the limited anniversary scent "Porcellana" for the four-hundredth anniversary of the company, and there is the diligent Luca, who immediately loses his heart to her but is overshadowed by Sandro once again and withdraws. Even "Contessa Giulia," the mother of both men, finds a resonant counterpart for her further life in the somewhat eccentric neighbor of the Munich family, Ludwig Korn. "Florence, romances, and scents at their finest!" one can only say and continue reading. Not only "Porcellana," but also the traditional fragrances "Acqua della Regina," "Acqua Santa Maria Novella," and finally "Acqua Angeli di Firenze" make their appearances in this worthwhile novel about the magic of scents. ("Angeli di Firenze" were, by the way, the numerous helpers from all over the world who dug Florence out of the mud after the flood of 1966. This scent was dedicated to them.) And now, therefore, "Rosa Novella," a smiling Eau de Cologne of a very special kind and delicacy. Captured within are impressions of the awakening spring in the gardens of Santa Maria Novella. May, with all its beauty, sends its greetings: fresh citrus notes unite with the enticing sweetness of noble ripe May roses and white flowers (Jasmine, are you here? I greet you!), before the herbal green of oregano and pepper joins in. Soft, moist moss forms scent islands between the classics of golden-brown patchouli, aromatic sandalwood, and silky shimmering, spicy cedarwood. This base wonderfully supports the airy delicacy of the previous rose scent, in whose rich waves typical Florentine Angelini delight with cheerful smiles. They playfully spread a light musk veil over the entire creation, full of warmth and grace! "Rosa Novella" embodies spring in Florence: seductive, floral, and warm. Even now, when winter still lingers in our bones, this scent beauty unfolds its fairy-tale magic. A scent being develops on my skin, telling of the unforgettable beauty of this city and many small and large romances within its walls and gardens. Romances that must have taken place very close by during the creation of "Rosa Novella": they left their tenderness and dreams in this rose cologne. "Rosa Novella" promises cheerfulness and charming Italian lightness. This promise is indeed kept. I greet this day with "Rosa Novella" and will conclude it with a fruity glass of rosé! Today is "Rose Day" for me, no matter what the calendar says!

Finally, I understand why the creations from Santa Maria Novella are so highly praised! I was really looking forward to my first scent journey with fragrances from Santa Maria Novella and consciously chose the original eaux de cologne from the Officina Profumo-Farmaceutica.

Fresia, Italian for freesia, does not truly smell of freesia at all but of a creamy bar of Camay soap. There is definitely an appeal in clean, warm, soapy floral perfumes, as evidenced by the popularity of the reformulated Ivoire de Balmain (French white soap) and Infusion d'Iris Homme (Irish Spring soap) - people just love the idea of smelling like they've just emerged, Venus-on-a-shell-like, from a bath. There is a faint idea here of nostalgia for childhood bathing rituals, perhaps, folded piles of laundry, or the idealized vision of cuddling up with a loved one in front of the fire and having him nuzzle into your clean, freshly-scrubbed skin. Fresia is highly recommended, therefore, to girls (or indeed boys) who believe that cleanliness really is close to Godliness. Personally, it's not my kind of thing at all.

When I first read Fresia on the bottle label in the Via del Carrozze store, I made a beeline for it. I adore freesias and I have long been searching for a soliflore freesia perfume. The search still continues to this day, as Fresia is not really about freesias at all; freesias appear only briefly in the opening, launching themselves powerfully on little musk bubbles that are quickly burst by the violets and the iris. The overall feeling is a classic soapy scent of freshly washed, starched to perfection laundry. My go to perfume for crisp white shirts, jeans, and structured handbags, for when I want to look and feel preppy-neat. Good silage and longevity.

I fondly remember the time when bouquets of freesias and yellow tea roses were often brought to family and friends' gatherings. The bare, long stem of the freesia, which only resides in a nest of leaves, was concealed by the foliage of the roses and delicate gypsophila, making these arrangements always appear very graceful and light. Gypsophila lived up to its name and laid a fine floral net over these blooms. These three were also commonly found in bridal bouquets: for the bride, larger and usually arranged as a white-yellow floral cascade, and smaller bouquets as adornments for the bridesmaids. Ah, freesias are indeed very romantic flowers that bring smiles just through memories. Although I also recall that they had to be banished from the rooms in the evening; these fragile creatures possess quite a strong aroma, and in my small apartment, they often had to spend the nights on the balcony, as their scent was so overpowering by evening. This enchantment was captured by the traditional house Officina Profumo Santa Maria Novella in Florence for its fragrance creation "Fresia." In the old romantic language of flowers, the freesia represents the mysterious unknown. Thus, "Fresia" tells a bright, delicate, and creamy story, like a piece of particularly beautiful soap, and has won my heart not only through its unique floral scent but also immediately. Gradually, it unfolds its softly fragrant secret of floral beauty. For I love stories and also pieces of soap; both reveal their secrets only over time. My friend just sent me a selection of many different small floral soap pieces for my birthday; she knows my habits and thus my passion for such "trivialities" that can brighten a day. Freesia soap is not included, but I discovered the Florentine "Fresia" in a spray among my new samples and was immediately transported to another realm, enveloped in this delicate yet slightly earthy floral scent. There, cheerful little fairy beings sit comfortably in the nest of leaves; they wear these delicate-colored floral bells as hats and skirts - just enchanting freesia fairies! A charming idea with this light yet floral-rich scent composition. For I also sense violets and a hint of roses in their company, something earthy-powdery seems to be present as well. A pleasant sillage, not extremely light for an "Acqua di Colonia," harmoniously and charmingly accompanies for several hours, making this bouquet of blooming freesias so likable and also well-suited for higher temperatures. So now I have the choice between two lovely freesia scent creations for summery, light days when the warmth has not yet embraced us with its thick down pillows. For besides this Florentine lady, I still adore my "English Pear & Freesia" from one of Jo Malone's older collections. Here, alongside the appetizingly ripe pear, fine earthy, woody, and smoky notes play in this scent concert. In this quintet, the light yet intensely fragrant freesia is beautifully accompanied. With these two lovely scent beings, I will gladly spend the upcoming summer days and therefore welcome "Fresia" by Officina Profumo S. Maria Novella with open arms and full anticipation for the experiences yet to come.

One can’t help but be charmed by the history of this fragrance, from the oldest perfume house in the world. Of course, this is not the original formula from 1533, commissioned by Caterina de' Medici as a gift for the king of France. And utilising some carefully crafted copywriting, Santa Maria Novella don’t outright claim that it is. Perhaps wisely, given that to do so would be claiming invention of eau de cologne some 150-odd years earlier than any other. This is a very classic eau de cologne – refreshing citrus mixed with aromatic herbal notes. The citrus notes in this opening are reminiscent of sweet orange fruits, with neroli and light orange blossom acting as the bridge (commonly the case with classic eaux de colognes). The interplay between the citrus and herbal aromatic notes is very important in any eau de cologne, and this one achieves it quite well, with the lavender note coming through with the citruses in the opening. As with most colognes, this fragrance's longevity is fairly poor. Once the volatile citrus notes dissipate, the herbaceousness of lavender and rosemary comes through quite prominently, perhaps drawing from the house's pharmaceutical roots. This leads to a somewhat medicinal quality to the scent in the dry down, which I imagine could be off-putting for some. Those expecting or wanting a blast of bracing, refreshing coolness are likely to be disappointed here. It’s a great little collector’s piece, particularly if you can pick one up from their beautiful store in Florence, but as far as eaux de colognes go, I do think there are better alternatives out there.

Simple, classic, beautiful. It`s easy to be charmed by the freshness and zest of this cologne, unencumbered by too many facets, it`s a tall glass of water for a hot summer day. The rosemary is zingy, the lavender is not overly masculine, it`s a perfectly balanced unisex fragrance. I like this a lot more than the other classic which it reminds me of, Echt Kolnisch Wasser. It`s pretty linear and it does disappear after 2-3 hours, but in my humble opinion, it seems a bit more consistent than Echt KW.

Acqua di Colonia, also informally called the Queen's Cologne, is a very nice, natural eau de cologne that features a bright, sour bergamot note that gives you the feeling of being drenched in ice-cold water on a hot summer's day. The bergamot smells like a greener, more bitter lemon, with some of the intense scent of the dark green leaves and rind thrown in for good measure. Like any good cologne (Acqua di Parma Colonia, Cologne Sologne, Neroli Portofino, 4711, etc.), the purpose is to refresh, not to last or to perform as a proper perfume. And indeed, if you're in the market for a summer cologne, this is an excellent option; natural-smelling, one of the purest bergamot notes in the business, and not badly priced per ml. Once the brief, volatile citrus notes have died away, what's left is a creamy, slightly soapy neroli note, green but with a touch of orange blossom dancing around the edges. It is far from complex, but as with all eaux de cologne, sometimes simple is best.

I will conclude the 'Neukölln' series with traditional citrus colognes today with episode 30. The 'Colonial Goods' series, which deals with woody, spicy, and herbal colognes and is currently at episode 22, will end at 25. Together with the first series 'Colonia statt Corona', I will have reviewed and compared 75 colognes: I didn't think at the beginning that the topic would grow so much, but I enjoy exploring this continent. I hope to share at least a little bit of that with the readers. In the future, I intend to focus a bit less on colognes, but of course, I won't completely ignore them. I will start a fourth series with them that will again cover 'yellow/white' and 'brown' colognes, just like the first series. As a concluding piece of 'Neukölln', I have saved this scent, which pretends to be Alt-Cölln, namely the first cologne in the world. According to the manufacturer's website, "the fragrance, also known as Acqua della Regina, celebrates the perfume whose development Caterina di Medici commissioned from the Dominican monks in 1533, and which she took to France when she married Henry of Valois." Well. Those who are legally trained know that formulations like "this fragrance celebrates the fragrance that" are usually recommended by the legal departments of companies to avoid a loss in court if the competition were to sue for unfair false claims. In other words, I assume this scent here has nothing to do with a fragrance from 1533 (if such a thing even exists), and that has been hidden behind the flowery party-pleasing wording. I also can't really imagine that this scent here is the original cologne, 250 years older than those from Farina, 4711, among others, and that this would have remained hidden in all standard works on the history of colognes. The confusion is compounded by the fact that this scent is sometimes referred to as "Colonia," simply "THE" (traditional) Colonia of this company (and that's how it appears on the bottle depicted here on Parfumo), but sometimes also as "Santa Maria di Novella by Santa Maria di Novella" (as here in the perfume database or similarly as "Acqua di Santa Maria di Novella by Santa Maria di Novella," as currently stated on the company's website: https://uk.smnovella.com/products/7010311. As just mentioned, it is also supposedly known as 'Acqua della Regina.' As Yatagan, who is knowledgeable, assures me, it is definitely all the same fragrance. The fragrance notes are similarly confusing, as "white flowers" are indicated here, while the company's homepage lists rosemary and lavender (classic Farina ingredients). Be that as it may, all of this seems like too much nonsense, carnival tricks, and hocus pocus to me; everything gets lost in a friendly southern vagueness, in a historically ungraspable diffusion, where instead of clear geographical toponyms, only a similarly laconic yet poetic "Hic sunt leones" is noted on the maps. I stick to the scent (thanks to Yatagan for the sample) and state, not so poetically but just as laconic: A fragrance that is hard and uncompromisingly dedicated to underperformance in terms of projection and longevity, pleasantly classically citrusy cologne-like, with minimal green undertones, a medium sweetness, and a somewhat untrustworthy fluffy softness (musk alarm level yellow). After a total of four fragrances from this house (Russa, Sicilia, Cuba, and the present one), none of which I disliked but none of which truly excited me either, I am putting a checkmark next to 'Santa Maria di Novella' (despite the beautiful bottles).

The only 14-year-old Catherina de' Medici had to leave her hometown Florence in the autumn of 1533 to marry Heinrich of Orléans in Marseille; her groom was only 14 days older. The young woman would have been largely isolated at the French court had she not carved out a place in the inner circle of her father-in-law. Thus began her victorious journey, which ended as Queen of France and later Regent/"Queen Mother" for her underage sons; even though her husband, the king, was under the strong influence of his beautiful mistress Diane de Poitiers. Catherina had learned to adapt and to forge her own path. Truly a very strong woman, especially for her time! So it is no surprise that the established perfumers of the city of Florence pay tribute to this impressive woman with corresponding fragrance compositions. Not only did "I Profumi di Firenze - Spezerie Palazzo Vecchio" create a fragrance of the same name in her honor, which is known to me as "Catherina de' Medici Concentrato" and also as Eau de Parfum; I have already written about it here. The Dominican monks of the "Officina Profumo Santa Maria Novella" dedicated a fragrance creation to her, which, according to legend, this young lady commissioned herself there in 1533. Thanks to her uncle Pope Leo X and other family connections, she did not have to be stingy; she was more than a "good match" and extremely self-confident! Thus, she took a memory of a homey Florentine monastery herb garden with her into her new life by Heinrich's side; wherever that might lead her. I can well imagine that its invigorating freshness (not that of the king!) was a blessing given the hygienic conditions of the time; a kind of "scent bottle," perhaps? ("Quick, neighbor lady! Your bottle!") For "Acqua della Regina" is, as the name describes: a fragrance water of wonderful freshness and spice, but also of relatively short longevity. Here it is: spray often - and one enjoys doing so here! A selection of fresh ripe fruits from the monastic Hesperides garden was draped around the classic bergamots. These were supposed to be the leading notes here, but the strong-herbaceous rosemary and blooming lavender push themselves forward on my skin. This skin is known to be somewhat particular and sometimes adapts only with difficulty. Thus, the bitter aroma of petitgrain and the noble, flattering neroli can only arrange themselves in the second row. But they do this very well, and were it not for the classification in the pyramid, this fragrance development would be quite natural. But now these citrus fruits are also cleverly spiced with cloves! This creates a bitter-spicy refreshment of the senses that delights. Earthiness is added to this mixture by a hint of earthy-rich patchouli and a light musk veil that is generously draped over everything like a loose hood. "Acqua della Regina" is a wonderful summer companion; even without being burdened by a king or his realm! Fresh and charming, with pleasant spice and appropriate earthy depth, one finds here a fragrant impression of summer Florence, completely without tourist crowds. A refreshing walk, accompanied by a true queen in scent: "Acqua della Regina"! Shall we go?
A disappointment, my dears! I need the emergency calming (cinnamon - clove spice, joyful Christmas everywhere...) lozenges from this pharmacy immediately...

Please excuse the rather mixed title, but that's exactly what went through my mind when I smelled the "fragrance" on me. My comment will also not be very extensive, as the perfume does not undergo any recognizable change for me. Forgive me for already making an association with cleaning products for the second time in a row.

I had to delete the original comment today. After some discrepancies arose during the purchase attempt, I was able to test the "right" Classica - a big thank you to Yatagan for the express delivery :-) The Classica EdC is indeed very close to the typical "Cologne Water" scent, at least in the opening.

I was really looking forward to Santa Maria Novella and thought it would bring me joy to start my fragrance journey through the gardens of a Florentine monastery and the surroundings of Florence with the original eaux de cologne. So I ordered a discovery kit with 8x 2 ml Eau de Cologne, which also (accompanied by 2 EdP samples) arrived surprisingly quickly.

This feels like rolling around in an herb garden, crushing the thyme and rosemary in your palms and inhaling deeply the rich, earthy, camphoric green aroma. It's so deeply satisfying and welcome on a hot summer evening. The opening is just gorgeous, laurel leaf with citrus, acerbic and fresh, it reminds me of cooking in the south of France, on a late summer evening. It starts off strong, like a typical Italian cologne, grabbing your attention, filling the room with your presence, but settles beautifully into the most comforting aroma of a woody patchouli that stays with you for a good while, not something I've experienced with a lot of other Santa Maria Novella fragrances.

If it weren't for the (good) longevity and the hint of patchouli in the end, this could be mistaken for a mix of essential oils and herbs meant to purify, heal and refresh rather than to perfume. It's a very old cologne and I have no trouble imagining it ressembles what it was in 1828 : sugar-free camphor, rosemary, thyme, laurel... I don't really get the lavander. This one makes no apology and doesn't try to please anyone. A timeless apothecary potion. Nevertheless I find it very wearable, being a lover of all things aromatic. I have only tried it in the heat, where it brings a welcome cool cleanliness, curious to try it in winter ! Very pleasant in the morning after a shower, in quintessential cologne fashion. I'm a woman but I would guess this used to be a gentleman's cologne. If you like your herbs, give it a sniff !

Hello, your complaint? Blocked nose, cough, and slightly elevated temperature? Sounds like a cold. Please don't go to work this week, I prescribe you this potpourri from Santa Maria Novella, it's basically like Tiger Balm, just weaker - like chicken soup, only without the chicken, but please don't drink it! The herbs will give you strength and slowly get you back on your feet. Here's the recipe, get well soon! Phew, finally home, let's follow the doctor's advice. Hmm, it says potpourri on the label, strange that it was recommended, what can dried flowers do? Well, let's put it under the nose.. and? Smells like herbs, not flowers. Rosemary, thyme.. and is that bay leaf in the background? It's hard to say for sure, the main thing is that it helps. Indeed - it reminds me of Tiger Balm, just weaker! Good thing, the real stuff would burn my nose hairs off. Pleasant. Later it seems less intense and more towards spices.. I can indeed smell the chicken soup, good thing the doctor warned me not to drink this stuff. 6 hours later, thankfully the medicine wears off, slowly the whole scent becomes lighter, the herbal, green, medicinal scent begins to say goodbye. It seems to have helped me indeed, but my nose needs a break now. The bottle goes into the medicine cabinet for next time, thankfully there's no risk of confusion with the rest of the collection due to the old-fashioned, medicinal-looking bottle. Good that I'm feeling better now, so the medicine cabinet can stay closed, along with this bottle, and I can now use my beloved fragrances again and take a break from this one. For risks and side effects, please consult your doctor or pharmacist.

Fieno/Hay opens on a very fresh, green note that combines the smell of unripe hay with sweet clover and meadow grasses. It is refreshing, but not tart or stridently-green - rather, more honeyed and floral in character. As it develops, Fieno takes on a boozy almond-like note, leading me to believe that coumarin is the main material used here. But Fieno leans on the more honeyed, powdery aspects of hay than its dry, sun-baked aromatic side. Its boozy almond undertone and sweet hay notes make me think of Chergui, a powdery, sweet-hay oriental, more than aromatic fougeres such as Azzaro Pour Homme or Jicky. There is also something about the powdered marron glace dry down here that puts Fieno clearly in the oriental category, although given its green start, it would be fair to call it a fresh oriental. A silky white musk, with perhaps a trace of heliotrope, finishes Fieno off on a wisp of powder and lends the fragrance a nostalgic feel. Simple, but elegant, I find myself haunted by my sample of this long after it's gone. It's one I'm constantly considering adding to my collection.

Fieno by Santa Maria Novella => the oldest pharmacy in the world, Florence 1612. The Dominican monks developed the first formulations there. Anyone visiting Florence MUST visit this pharmacy! An unbelievably beautiful place. And the handmade soaps, candles, oils, and fragrances are something truly special. A museum is also attached, and there is a small café, a dreamy spot. When Catherine de' Medici became Queen of France in the 16th century, she received her personal fragrance from here and named it "Eau de la Reine". The scent is still produced today under the name "Acqua di S.M Novella" and is a bestseller. A unique shopping experience, the products are displayed in various rooms, and you receive a card to go from counter to counter to note the products you wish to buy. At the back of the store, you show the card, and there you receive the products beautifully wrapped. There is, of course, an online shop and 75 shops worldwide, but none can compare to Florence. Fieno (Hay) has been available since 1886! Fieno means hay in Italian; I spent my school holidays at my grandparents' farm and was addicted to the aromatic, herbal, and slightly honey-like scent of dried hay. We played hide and seek behind the hay bales for hours, and only after sunset did Grandma call us home, where we got warm milk, a slice of bread from our stone oven in the yard, and homemade butter. Back then it was taken for granted, today it's priceless. Noblest, soft hay surrounded by myrtle hedges in the monastic midday sun. For me, this scent has something warm, nostalgic, and reminds me of my childhood, my grandma, and carefree, seemingly endless summer days. Caramel-like herbal Italian summer, we smell not with our noses but with our brains. If you don't have emotionally charged hay memories, this scent will smell different to you. Vintage vibe, but not old-fashioned. Good hay smells fresh and floral/herbal, definitely not musty, moldy, or sour! It smells fresh, summery, spicy, and even in winter, it reminds one of a freshly mown meadow. Admittedly, many people don't even recognize hay and straw. It's easy to remember: straw = grain, hay = grass. In addition to hay, you can smell lavender, myrtle, jasmine - a soap that smells like this can be found in expensive boutique hotels on the Amalfi Coast. The aromatic embrace of delicate sweetness that neither suffocates nor overwhelms. Hawthorn is also included. From a distance, the scent may appear sweet and subtle. Up close, however, the hawthorn has a strong sweetness, even herbaceous to some, bordering on overpowering. Warm, herbal, aromatic, but soft and ethereal. Accompanying this is plenty of myrtle (I wish it appeared more often in fragrances!), which subtly counters with its fresh, medicinal bloom. The note of freshly mown hay is the heart ("fieno") and I smell a dose of real hay absolute - the only other fragrances in which I have discovered it are Serge Lutens Chergui and Lorenzo Villoresi Yerba Mate. It in no way reminds one of barnyards or "horse smell"; no, this is the hay itself, in bales, under the sun. Sweet hay-like, fresh creamy soap, like my grandma always had. Lavender, herbs, late summer fields. Cozy. Rustic, a cross between cheerfulness and melancholy. It reminds me of autumn drives through the Tuscan landscape. I love the scent of hay because it plays a similar role to tobacco in fragrances, but is much lighter, more feminine, and grassier. Fieno is extraordinary and triggers so many images in the mind, decent sillage, longevity is about 4-5 hours, Fieno is an olfactory ode to the charm of the Tuscan landscape. This scent is characterized by a bouquet of woody and floral notes and evokes the irresistible scent of freshly cut hay. The scent of freshly mown meadows, hay, leaden heat over Tuscany; cicadas sawing, olive trees adorning the landscape like cotton clouds.

How often do we get annoyed when we fall for a beautiful top note in a perfume shop, lacking the patience to test the entire progression of the fragrance, only to find out at home that not much happens after that. Nice, and that’s about it. I think this has happened to all of us, and sometimes we suspect that our impatience is calculated by the creators of the scents to quickly generate sales. Well, it can also go the other way, and I perceive Fieno as an example of a perfume that doesn’t hit you over the head but reveals its beauty only to those who take the time to get to know the scent at leisure. The citrusy and rather one-dimensional opening leads us into a heart that, with spicy notes, presents the theme of Fieno in an aromatic and almost clean soapy manner. The rose adds elegance to this theme. In my opinion, this is not the usual rose scent with green accents; rather, it is the exact opposite, and I find that extremely appealing. No one needs to have concerns about the hawthorn here. The note gives the fragrance depth and lasting strength, and I perceive it as a skillful transition to the vetiver-heavy finish, which is warmed and softened by sandalwood. I still notice the aromatic heart note, and yet this almost powdery base is already settling over Fieno, allowing the scent to fade away in a remarkably friendly manner. The perfume develops completely harmoniously, which actually doesn’t reveal a true three-part pyramid, as the notes skillfully blend into one another, as I have also noticed in other perfumes by SMN. Once again, I am impressed by the care and dedication with which the perfumers of Santa Maria Novella create perfumes full of expressiveness and nobility without chasing trends or pandering to current mass tastes.

The names of perfumes are always a tricky thing. Sometimes they are meant to name the theme, reveal the contents, or tell grand stories. Often they fit, but here I don't understand the connection at all. Because I neither smell hay nor do I have to think of it. What I smell is as follows: Chunks of soap fall onto dry wood and melt away, rose buds are bitterly squeezed, aldehydic rose water drips out. The citrus note here doesn’t feel refreshing at all, but rather warm and dull. It can be compared to the warm scent when washing hands with hot water and fresh soap. The vetiver is also of a more classic form, not one of the modern smoky, dark varieties, but rather greenish and soapy. Overall, the main theme of this fragrance remains soapy, yet not particularly foamy; the consistency of the scent impression is rather creamy in nature. What’s quite clever is that the fresh, warm lemony soap shifts into an almondy one. Bitter, white, skinless almonds. And these become more and more prominent, leaving the soap almost behind. Overall, the scent is pleasant and nice, but somewhat out of date. I wouldn’t want to smell this on young people; there are clearly more modern interpretations of cleanliness. Thank you for reading my comment.

Rosa Gardenia lives true to its name: roses, check!, gardenias, check! Both are detectable, sweet, noble, maybe even a touch snotty, but that snootiness is mitigated by the sweetness of the flowers. This rose is Italian: the squeeze of bergamot says that. But me thinks it grew in a French garden, somewhere at Versailles, because the gardenias make it seem so powdery, like a giant puff of white powder that was applied to Marie Antoinette`s rosy cheeks and wigs. This is only slightly vintage, I think the Marie Antoinette I`m thinking of is young, in her prime, so the perfume is still innocent and pure.

... then it probably smells like Rosa Gardenia. The boutique's window magically drew me in... and the store itself upon entering! Like a fairy tale, worth a visit, whether you find something or not. I tested various fragrances with the help of the saleswoman... all quite beautiful and special. But somehow nothing that brought a smile to my face (except the special editions in their beautiful bottles, nestled in a romantic book-perfume box! What an experience for the eyes & nose) I also found Tabacco Toscano Eau de Cologne quite wonderful, but unfortunately my boyfriend vehemently vetoed it - at least it’s available in the sample kit :) Then came Rosa Gardenia! And yes, it was love at first sniff! I smiled when I smelled the fragrance for the first time and even half an hour later, just before I took it home with me... THE FRAGRANCE: Is sweet. Initially synthetic. But somehow it immediately captures the "princess" feeling that the boutique has been conveying to me the whole time. Romantic, sweet, young... all seen through dreamy rose-colored glasses. Over time, it develops into the absolutely most beautiful floral scent... a sea of flowers and roses. The synthetic notes fade away, leaving only natural flowers. Without being intrusive. Romantic, feminine, noble. One of my favorite Diptyque candles is "Geranium Rosa"... the candle is a bit more floral-fresh without the slight powdery sweetness that remains in the perfume. In the drydown, the base notes come through. Time and again accompanied by a hint of rose. The longevity is really decent! I can smell it throughout the day. My surroundings have positively commented on the scent several times. For me, the fragrance is 0.0 unisex. It’s a women's fragrance to my nose (and also to the noses around me ;) ) I own Delina Exclusif , and Rosa Gardenia is - for me(!) the perfect addition to my collection (The two fragrances cannot be compared!, but they are for rose scent fans), Rosa Gardenia is lighter, somewhat synthetic, powdery, floral... I simply love it! In terms of complexity, it cannot compete with Delina Exclusif, but it doesn’t have to, considering the price range of both fragrances. I see it as a light fragrance for spring and summer. As a Christmas wish, the matching shower gel for the perfume is on the list. Whether my opinion is objective, I don’t know; the visit to the boutique was a full-circle moment complete with butterflies in my stomach... a wonderful city, a beautiful window and boutique, great service, emotions that the fragrance awakened in me at first sniff... all these emotions and now also Florence memories come alive when I wear Rosa Gardenia.

I bought the fragrance directly in Florence at the Santa Maria Novella - what an experience! I had no great expectations of the oldest pharmacy in Europe. However, those expectations were surpassed by miles during the visit. Simply a beautiful atmosphere. But now to the fragrance: This one caught my eye first while testing the entire collection - it’s no wonder it’s the bestseller. It starts with a combination of zesty bergamot and nutmeg, which, in my opinion, really comes through. Over time, the fragrance becomes more floral until it transitions into a creamy scent. Overall, a very, very beautifully crafted fragrance!!! If you are looking for a fragrance with strong sillage and longevity, you are definitely not in the right place here, as the scent fades quite quickly (about 4 hours on my skin). However, since this purchase was more about the memories, the Alba di Seoul simply had to be taken home.

That a walk in the woods is good for body and soul, allows for deep breathing, conveys serenity, and provides a break from everyday life is, for heaven's sake, nothing new. But in our time, everything must have a name that is as interesting and extraordinary as possible, so that the information-overloaded person engages with a topic, no matter how normal and well-established it may be. So I had to pause and then smile recently when I read that the relaxation one can gain from a walk in the green lungs of our cities is now called "forest bathing," and that contemporary authors find it necessary to write books about it and identify the trend as Japanese, because we fact-oriented Europeans apparently are no longer capable of immersing ourselves in the relaxing and strengthening atmosphere of the forest without guidance. I don't want to claim that Alba di Seoul is, so to speak, the forest bath for the handbag, but the gentle conifer scent does entice me to breathe deeply. Unlike some other forest fragrances, I don't feel like I'm about to spray resin spots on my clothes, or that around the next corner a forest troll or the last unicorn might appear. Alba di Seoul is much more subtle and gentle and reminds me not of Japanese gardens or pagodas, but rather of the airy pine forests that let sunlight shine down to the ground and where, at this time of year, the swamp gladiolus are blooming nearby. The woody notes do not give the impression of about to get a splinter, and the oriental scent notes actually represent the Far East for me rather than the Near East. The fragrance is soft, calm, and cool, but without the chill that some green-fresh scents cause me. The clear theme of the fragrance is aptly depicted on the packaging, as it shows the silhouette of a forest in a paper-cut style, with light shimmering through the trunks of the trees. As with Citta di Kyoto, the Italian perfumers have also succeeded in Alba di Seoul in uniting Asian-meditative flair and Mediterranean art of living in a fragrance.

Pure Musc is a big, soft white flower fragrance, and the first thing that came to mind when I smelt it was something pristine. A bowl of tender white petals. Pure Musc feels more elegant and substantial than your average floral and musky scents. It's raw, carnal, earthy, sensual, soft, organic, flowery, powdery, and all so elegant at the same time—a calming yet very sophisticated fragrance, like the work behind each Narciso Rodriguez. Musk needs your warm skin to come to life; it needs to express itself on your skin. Deep, radiant musk breathes through the entire composition. Soft, dusty jasmine takes on a slight indole chord, but it's a fresh flower, still on the hedge. Musk here creates the central accord, which is not rich and penetrating. Instead, it is soft, inviting. Imagine you are in a serene oriental garden with jasmine, hedges in full bloom, climbing the wooden terraces. As you walk, the sun warms your skin. The gorgeous flower aroma fills the air, blends in harmony with soft jasmine and a bright bouquet of fragrant orange blossom. Pure Musc is beautifully done. And it influences my skin, which sets it apart from the rest, being relatively fresh and centred on greener white flowers. It unfurls with an aldehydic boozy accord, hairspray in the 70s, so it gives it a nostalgic feeling. He reminds me of when I was a kid, waiting outside the local hairdresser for my mom to cut her hair and dry, and I could smell the hair products all over the salon from the heat of the dyers. That sensation fades away a few seconds later, yielding the seat to sweet orange blossom, a rich bouquet of green and floral scent, so wet with a magnolia-like vibe. The white musk is already there as a top note; I get nothing animals. It is not as strong as #Rodriguez for him. Instead, it recalls the now rare White Musk Eau de Parfum . In the heart, it has a smooth musk note, sometimes soapy, which seems soft. Combined with the dewy flowers, it has a flair I've never felt with others. With the heat of the skin, the musk grows and grows; it turns dominant, demanding. Despite the fragrance characters of the white musk, it is not just another White Musk Eau de Parfum , White Musk for Women , or any other musk based fragrance. Instead, the musk turns out creamy, soapy, with a fresh laundry feeling, a sort of out-of-the-shower freshness. When the scent approaches the dry-down, I can feel the glowing and creamy aspect of the cashmeran, with a smidgen of dirtiness added by patchouli. The delicate woody and amber note at the base hints warmth. It's a clean, powdery musk-centred fragrance, but I also almost sense a note of patchouli adding this light, earthy and comforting aura. Overall, the flowers are sober and subtle, the moss clean and non-animal. It is like a breeze that you can feel brushing your skin. So sweet and so touching. It's raw, carnal, earthy, sensual, organic, powdery, and all so classy at the same time. A calming fragrance and yet very sophisticated, like every Narciso Rodriguez work, you can give time to his scent. Musk needs your warm skin to take life. It must express itself on your skin. It could be safe for daily use at work if used with a light hand or a night out in casual dining—a very inoffensive powdery musk scent, perfect for a subtle day when you're in a nothing-special mood. Pure Musc does not scream; it is a more intimate scent with moderate sillage and projection. Though it lasts longer on my skin and clothes, people near me can catch it even after several hours. I find it an ideal perfume for the mid-seasons. However, it doesn't smell too fresh and clean that it would be weird to wear it in all seasons. When you wear this perfume, it invites you to a hug. You get so many compliments, and everybody wants to know what you are wearing, and they always expect a secret niche perfume. Pure Musc will be my bedtime story, my pillow's scent. I based the review on a decant I have owned since May 2021. -Elysium

NARCISO RODRIGUEZ Pure Musk for Her Sonia Constant 2019 So beautiful clean florals and musk. Delicate and tender, fluffy and very innocent yet seductive. Scent of an angel. Scent of a hope. Scent of the bright future. It’s like opening your eyes in the morning when the sun is shining through the window. You have your beautiful lingerie on, you put your soft slides on and the softest luxurious long cashmere cardigan which you have. It’s a cozy hug with very relaxing breeze. Pure Musk is not soapy neither powdery. It is “transparent” compared to cubes (Poudree and Rouge) which are creamy with richer texture. Thank you for reading, I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

This perfume is excellent for when you just want to smell clean and neutral. I recently transitioned at work to a desk job after working out on the production floor and this was the first perfume I went for to wear to my first office job. Out of the 125 full bottles I currently have, Pure Musc felt the safest. (Most of my collection is safe, mass appeal type stuff, but this just stood out to me as the cleanest.) It is clean and cool, fantastic longevity and while it doesn’t have a huge scent bubble, I can smell it on myself all day. It smells the way laying your face down on a cool pillow feels. Refreshing yet comfortable. I don’t feel that it is creamy, but I associate creamy with lactonic, and this is more vibrant. The bright white bottle suits it very well.

I remember smelling this on a friend for the first time and being absolutely captivated by how good and CLEAN she smelled. A few days later I pulled the trigger and bought a bottle for myself. This is possibly my most worn perfume! EVER! I don't know how else to describe this other than clean and musky. To me this smells like you've just stepped out of the shower or like a clean batch of laundry that you've hung out to dry on a sunny spring day. I wear this scent to work, when running errands, before I go to sleep, even to the gym! It is so incredibly versatile and something I want to reach for when I want a "my skin but better" scent. It's also quite the compliment getter - multiple people have complimented me while wearing this. To my nose, this scent is quite linear and doesn't necessary develop much after first spraying it, however I think that is part of its beauty. It does also sit quite close to the skin. In terms of longevity it is unfortunately disappointing, so much so that I recently bought a small version of this to keep in my purse so that I can freshen up throughout the day. It lasts a mere 2 to 3 hours on my skin before I can no longer smell it. However, given how much I love it, and given the fact that this scent often goes on sale with various online retailers, I do think it's worth what you're paying for!

When you dont like animalic musk but also you like white florals... Your scent is... PURE MUSC EDP! That can be my rare likes in Narciso Rodriguez collection. I dont like for her edt, fleur musc, for her edp, amber musc. But I like this scent. Because white florals can close musc's animalic effect. Floral, animalic, calm type. Reminds me snowy days. Longevity and sillage =medium.

I love musk scents and this one is one of my absolute favourites! It reminds me of skincare creams that my mom used to apply (so very nostalgic) and smells incredibly cosy! Clean girl scent and very elegant. I definitely recommend this scent for this price, very good value in my opinion. Also pairs nice with pure musc rose by the same brand.

When I first got this, there was no hint of musk and it was pure ylang ylang x jasmin cream affair, and very feminine. I loved it, and now have been wearing it for a few months. I don't know what happened, but now I see why it is called Pure Musc. The beginning still starts out as clean, cold, soapy, creamy florals ("mom's skincare").

This perfume smells very clean and simple, but at the same time, it is unique and recognizable. To me, it evokes the image of a sexy, confident, polished woman over 30 with a very interesting personality. I think this is a very versatile perfume and can be worn on many different occasions all year round.

It is a good, everyday musky fresh perfume and I liked it. I don't think I have tried a NR perfume that I didn't like. That being said, I expected it cleaner and soapy from the reviews and the description, but it was more floral than I expected.

I love the minimalistic bottle and was expecting something a little more cool, esp. because someone mentioned it's masculine leaning. On me it's not. At all. It's 100% feminine, soft, warm, almost floral. It's very prim and proper, good girl goes to Sunday church after neatly putting away laundry. Something reminds me of a baby. But also of an adult, loving, caring woman.

Warm, sweet dry woods underlying rich yet delicate blended floral notes, lightly spiced, with some powder and a suggestion of oakmoss. This is absolutely *not* the green floral Parfumo’s summary notes indicate! It is in a more oriental vein. Lovely, unusual perfume with good lasting power and projection.

It is a perfume full of tenderness and innocence. Its aroma is rosy in color, like that of a beautiful baby's cheeks. Memories of my childhood also come back to me, since its smell reminds me of the solid wax air fresheners that my mother hung in her closet, and when I say air freshener I don't mean it in a bad way, in fact these air fresheners smelled very good. They were like little pearls that were inside little plastic boxes. The rose and jasmine (although I also perceive nuances of orange blossom) are wrapped in a fine and clean talc. Afterwards, the musk is quite noticeable, leaving even the powdery in the background. For those who like musky scents, this may be for you. In general, it is a simple perfume, which easily pleases its wearer and the people around him. Its aroma provides well-being, warmth and security. For the first 3-4 hours it feels intense. From here, the intensity gradually decreases, but throughout the day small bursts of its aroma come and go, reminding you how beautiful this perfume is.

I love this one. I had the decant but got my hands on a fb recently. I am obsessed. The name says it all for me. The powdery scent is like a cloud of light pink organza trailing behind you for at least 6 hrs for me. The sillage is not overwhelming but larger than Rouge. Poudree is more feminine in my opinion but has the unmistakable Narciso dna underneath. All in all a great one for me!

I have Bois Doré by Van Cleef, which I rarely wear because it is so boring and monotonous, so "suffocating". So, I blindly bought Rodriguez Powder and after 20 minutes it sounded like my BD, but lighter and more pleasant. You can wear it all day and it will be comfortable. And I also realized that these two perfumes mentioned have a distant resemblance to Hypnotic Poison, such a common vibe, but only my personal nose determined it that way. I am happy with the purchase.

Poudree became my favorite perfume and my signature smell, I love it so much. I wouldn't exactly describe it as sweet, from the NR cubes rouge, the red one, is a sweeter powder. Poudree is way more of a musky woody powder. The white floral is there, but definitely not the star, the wood and the musk are by far the strongest smells, and it is aromatic in an almost spicy way. In the beginning, the spiciness is stronger and in general, is not the lightest perfume, it applies quite strongly at first, but with time it settles in a sweet vanilla, with warm woody muskiness on the skin. It is a cozy smell, but not in a "books and hot tea" way, but in a" cozy sexy time" way.

I own the discontinued white cube Narciso EDP and the red one. They are the only two reasons why I can contain myself from also buying this one. They all have the same wonderful DNA, so maybe two are enough. I'm not sure though, they do have their own character. Contrary to the name, this one is not that powdery, it's ultra creamy. Compared to Narciso EDP this is more floral, sweeter and more girly. Poudree doesn't have any of its woody notes, but the same beautiful musk as the main note. Here the musk is complemented beautifully by a bouquet of rose and jasmine and some sweet vanillic powder. It has a bit of that 'doll head' accord in the drydown, but blended with the warm creamy musk. The nude pink of the bottle matches the scent very well. A few days after testing it for the first time (ages ago) I dreamt of using a pink sweet musk perfume and then I had to try it again. It's really beautiful and also made me appreciate Narciso EDP more again. If you like NR in general, musks, creamy and/or slightly sweet fragrances, it's a must-try!

2018-03-07-##-## UTC -- This just swathes one in a blanket of sheer gorgeosity: one becometh veritably ~espargenomenon~ in said blanket. The muskiness is just intoxicating - it's the °whoozy-swoony° sort of musk - and transfigures the rose-jasmine accord - or whatever it is - it almost doesn't matter.

I must say, something in the opening is very off-putting/unpleasant for me. Based on the scent profile, I can't figure out what it is. It's not so bad that it's a scrubber, but it does annoy me slightly. After about 2 hours of wear and beyond.... GORGEOUS! Very feminine and gentile. Perfect for an evening out and date nights.

NARCISO RODRIGUEZ Narciso Poudrée Aurelien Guichard 2016 Narciso Rouge Nadege le Garlantezec and Sonia Constant 2018 I fell in love totally with these cubes (Narciso line) - brands cozy, soft and subtle yet rich perfumes with NR’s signature musk, like the delicate and more simple clean musk scents as well from “for her” line. Both of these two are very feminine.

I really don't know what all the hype is about Narciso perfumes. This one in particular is the most depressing of all. Its smell is as depressing as its color, like old fart-stained lingerie. Damn I wish I understood Narciso.

Ahhh man!!! This is similar to the white cube, but a little more wearable, soft, rounded, less crisply "white". null of the hard cedar, you can still smell a little woodiness, but it's way less scratchy. I have undying love for the white cube *because* of it's character, but I can absolutely see why people often prefer this. It's very, very plush.

So beautiful! I don't understand why this is the rose flanker of Musc Noir. It doesn't smell all that rosy to me, it's more of an intense, richer version of the Musc Noir concept. If I could switch it up, I would call this Musc Noir and the first version Musc Noir Légère or Florale. Well, at least the darker bottle fits the scent. This is such a sensual fragrance . Warm, jammy plum and an ever-so-slightly indolic, very hypnotic tuberose that is reminiscent of ripe jasmine. A touch of vanilla and comforting musk. It's not the typical strong NR For Her kind of musk, it's something more subtle and skin-like, but still sexy. There is something about this that smells like suede, and it's almost a little smoky in the opening. Later it turns more balsamic. The rose is subtly blended into the plum. All in all this is not as clean as Musc Noir, especially in the drydown, but not dirty either. Many reviewers online said Musc Noir reminded them of Dior Poison, but I actually get much more of the Poison vibe with Musc Noir Rose. It has that touch of vintage attitude incorporated into a modern scent. Really, the first one was nice, but this is superior in any way. It feels velvety and mysterious. Perfect for nights out, but honestly also during the day. Especially in autumn, the plum note feels perfect for that time of the year.

I absolutely love this scent - in my mind, this is the perfect Capricorn fragrance. It is easy and feminine with a hint of villainous flair to it with the dark rose. Fresh but still creamy, vanilla but not sickly, rosey but never described as one dimensional. It's complex but easy at the same time and there's not a situation or event that this wouldn't be appropriate for in my mind. 10/10 no notes and my go-to signature scent.

I felt that I needed something easy into my collection. Something classy yet comfortable and cozy, something delicate and not so unique. Sometimes I feel so exhausted that I don’t even have power to understand my own mood. If I wear some bold scent with a big character while feeling like that I just get confused. With these two scents I don’t have to think absolutely anything, no weather, neither clothes, not even how I really feel. Do you recognize that mood? NARCISO RODRIGUEZ Musk Noir Rose Sonia Constant 2022 I fell in love with so many scents from NR while trying to find something inconspicuous, almost imperceptible yet attractive and sensual. I love the powdery clean musky dna in them, they are like a tender hug, I feel like I’m wrapped in an enormous fluffy cashmere blanket escaping this cruel world. Musc Noir Rose has a sweet twist in it from Plum and Vanilla. All of them smells irresistible on cloths. Rose is more noticeable here than in others but it’s not “noir” in any kind of way and it’s not so natural smelling Rose, it rather stays very abstract. CHANEL Coco Noir Jacques Polge and Christopher Sheldrake 2012 Delightful very crowd pleasing mix of flowers in a warm woody base - I don’t find anything so “noir” in this one but there is a gentle breeze of warm spices. The scent is seductive and traditionally feminine. It’s delightful but it doesn’t force me to be in a good mood. I have an extrait of this one at it has that “noir” confidence boost in it. Anyway the name should be Coco Mademoiselle Noir. Full reviews of both coming later. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

Nice enough, but neither here nor there. The tuberose can be a bit bubble-gummy at times, but not grossly. Smells like it could be your friend’s mom or something. Mostly floral and musk with a very vanilla base. Almost like a shea butter body cream kind of vibe. Between this flanker and the original Musc Noir, I think the latter is prettier to me.

Love made of buttery slightly sweet spicy musk, sensuality, dark tuberose, plum jam, and sexy vanilla. With a touch of bergamot! The characterization "Noir" probably refers to the thoughts one makes when they smell it around them, a highly erotic, highly addictive fragrance. The musk note, like in all For Her perfumes I have tried, is almost animalic, it's soft and powdery, and creamy, but also kinda "dirty", but not in a bad way, but in a hot way.

I bought this because of youtube and as a blind buy. Plus the price was unbeatable ($49.99) so I figured, why not? I am so happy that I did. This is not a beast mode fragrance, but it is a stunner. Perfect for work, and anytime. I can definitely smell the musk and the vanilla, along with a light rose.

I love it! Such a nice scent for the evening — that’s when I prefer wearing this kind of fragrance. I usually do just two sprays, and it’s more than enough. It’s classy, soft, slightly sweet with a touch of rose, and it lasts beautifully. A safe blind buy, in my opinion :) My friend said it’s ‘too heavy,’ but she’s not really into perfumes, so I don’t mind at all :)))

I smelled a sample bottle on a whim and bought my own within a week. I've tried the OG For Her and found it too powdery and floral, but this flanker is the perfect sexy feminine perfume to me. I don't enjoy those leathery scents that tend to fall in the 'seductive' category, rather I'd categorize this as a floral fruity gourmand with musk.

Ah. I actually don't like roses. Just like I didn't like cheese as a child. This fragrance is similar to what baked cannelloni did to my cheese phobia as a little kid: I was cured. As a big fan of Musc Noir, I already like the original a lot, which makes it hard for other fragrances - especially flankers - to impress me.

The air is filled with your seductive scent, the pink clouds drift across the vast horizon, in feelings piled up like roses. The air is filled with your delightful scent, heart full of tender sensuality. a bright rose in silky hair I worship your inner beauty.

The perfect Patchouli fragrance for my soul. It has a bit of everything - nature-like smell, dank, earthy, dusty, liquor-like, spicy, medicinal, only slightly sweet, and with a brilliantly poetic addition of rose. It is a soul-stirring, unfiltered, and brutal depiction of this note. I love many approaches to patchouli, from the dusty cocoa to the ambery ones. The variety that leaves me indifferent is the "modern" and "clean" patchouli scents a la Coromandel and Co. I like them as musty, dusty, earthy, and close-to-nature as possible. The Santa Maria Novella is that and more. I think it might be too literal for many, specifically if one is used to having their patchouli pampered by balsamic, woody, and floral notes. This one is as close to nature as it can get, further made challenging by the cold, almost metallic, and medicinal blast from the opening (very clove-forward), the raw earthiness (practically can nearly chew it), and the minimal sweetness and fillers. As with other perfumes from this house, it smells very high quality, quite butch, and medieval. With this one, I picture a dank cellar in a castle. The cold and wet opening, coupled with the boozy, liquor-like facet (like a liquor made from the earth) and the earthiness, all make me think of a cellar. There is, however, one aspect that helps bring out a lyrical and romantic face of the fragrance, and that is a vivid rose accord. It comes across as such and may be the suggested imagery of the combination of eugenol, geranium, and rosewood listed among the notes. Still, it's a rose nonetheless. Crimson petals of a withered flower dangling on the cold and wet earth. It allows a sensitive side of the perfume to show and prevents it from being too simple-minded and brute. This duality of darkness with speckles of diaphanous light makes me reminisce of the way Lestat dreamed of Claudia: "The smell of crushed rose petals wafting from her curly hair." I can see a character like Lestat de Lioncourt as an embodiment of this scent. The perfect balance of malevolence, starkness, timeless beauty, with a hint of romance. CAVEAT: Review based on the frosted bottle version, which differs from the current, clear-glass, and paper-label one. IG:@memory.of.scents

My family is quite a large one. Both my mother's parents and my father's parents got divorced and remarried prior to my being born, so growing up I had a lot of grandparents to show me love. To make it even better, I was the only grandchild until I was 12, so for years I was able to be spoiled beyond reason. One thing I found interesting across my very large family, is that almost all of my grandparents had a passion for fragrance, with many of them still having large collections. My father's father was a simple man, loving scents like One Man Show and a random Tommy Bahama I can't seem to remember, his wife frequenting Dior J'adore. My father's mother was an avid wearer of YSL Opium, and her husband a lover of Dior Dune. My mother's father, who's collection is larger than my own, swears by Aramis and Eternity, and his wife an enjoyer of none other than Chanel Cristalle. However, my mother's mother was a different breed than the rest. She was, no matter how cool the rest of them were, the cool grandma. On special occasions she might have worn Aromatics Elixir or Rive Gauche, but her daily scent was a blue glass spray bottle of pure patchouli oil that she purchased from a small shop called 'Feather Falls' whenever she would visit her best friend in California. I grew up craving this scent more than any other. A hug from her was, and thankfully still is, the most magical thing on the face of the planet. Of course, she has not worn patchouli like that for years now, but every time I smell a whiff of pure, unadulterated patchouli, I think of her. Well, thanks to Santa Maria Novella, and this EDC in particular, I have been transported back to my childhood through this marvelously simple piece of perfumery. This is the closest thing I have found to that specific patchouli spray that my grandma would wear, and it's magical to say the least. There is not much to say about the depth and composition here, as it is really truly just patchouli, but it is the perfect patchouli. Sweet, spicy, earthy, a tad bit chocolatey, and immensely warm. It's a lesson in how sometimes less is more, and that even the simplest of fragrances can make our hearts sing. This will definitely remain a staple in my collection as long as it is manufactured, as it truly transports me back to a time I wished I was still living in, no matter how much I might have wanted to 'grow up' at the time.

A bright, white floral, and aromatic opening with a rich, earthy and bitter patchouli that keeps the overall feeling rather dark. It is not a syrupy or chocolatey patch, and I find it works well in warmer weather. It makes me think of a deep indigo blue... like a blueberry, earthy and refreshing (but it doesn't smell like blueberry haha)

I thought Etro's Patchouly was the most straight-ahead patchouli on earth until I smelled this. Side by side, the Etro emerges as slightly floral and herbal, whereas SMN Patchouli is just raw earth. Patchouli is a Holy Grail for patchouli lovers everywhere. Raw and direct, it smells at first like fresh, loamy soil and rising damp. Later, it dries out a bit and takes on the gold-brown richness of an autumnal landscape, as if a tincture of crisp fallen maple leaves has been drip-fed into the brew. But whereas it gains in richness, it does not end up mired in an oriental base of sweet amber or vanilla, as so many patchouli fragrances do - this one is raw-edged, honest, pure, and totally to the point. It makes no apologies for being patchouli. Patchouli also has a green, leafy bitterness to it and a slightly antiseptic undercurrent, but far from being off-putting, these elements cut through the brown gloom and pushes air into the room. The aroma is a thick one, but it wears surprisingly sheerly on the skin. I think it's an incredibly sexy, earthy fragrance, because it makes a feature out of its own severity. Think of every stern schoolmistress you ever feared and ended up crushing on, and that's Santa Maria Novella Patchouli.

As a patchouli aficionado, I was very excited about this fragrance, as it has been produced since around 1450, making it the mother of all patchouli scents. During a visit to Santa Maria Novella in Florence, I didn't hesitate long and had the bottle wrapped up without testing it first. Oh dear, I should have done that. Because as the saying goes: Trust is good, control is better. When I eagerly opened the bottle at home, I was hit by a harsh smell of alcohol.
