This is just to explain that, when I say I love the ever-loving sh*t out of Marescialla, I mean that I really love the ever-loving sh*t out of it and am not just saying that as your typical fragrance reviewer who exalts the artistic merits of a challenging fragrance only to never again touch it outside of that one review. Which, to be fair, I have also done. That said, Marescialla is a scent that probably 95% of people who smell it will think is repulsive. The opening is a grotesque cacophony of paint thinner, medicinal notes, herbal salve, floor wax, and creeping mold, all underscored by a screechy citric note as harsh as it is unlovely. It’s a bit like walking into an ancient church that’s just been scrubbed down with peppery, neon-yellow antiseptic fluids that cost 0.57 cents from a hardware store. This piercing scent – the aroma of mace, really – mingles with the damp old wood and stone, creating an atmosphere that’s both a little terrifying and enthralling. If you told me someone had used a bucket of Marescialla to cover up a ritualistic killing or exorcism gone wrong in an old church, I’d believe you. The mace adds a clove-like twist, emphasizing the swing between the purifying and the unholy. I find the scent oddly comforting, though. I bought Marescialla the day after a particularly gruesome medical procedure I’d undergone in a podiatrist’s office one dark, rainy night in Rome, an office that I realize now must have been repurposed from an ancient crypt or cellar, soaring architraves and all. Marescialla smells like my experience that night – there was a needle of anesthetic (teasing me with the sweet promise of deliverance), there was blood, there was medical gauze soaked in a brackish, clovey antiseptic, a herb-scented tissue to bring me round after I fainted, and most of all, there was the smell of ancient wood, creeping rot, and damp stone. It should be no surprise then that fear and loathing and relief (at it all being over) are mixed up in the aroma of Marescialla. It is already an intensely evocative fragrance – for me, it is memory incarnate. As it settles, Marescialla reveals a bracing and surprisingly clean blend of clove, rose, wood, and patchouli, reminiscent of skin that’s been thoroughly washed with Pears soap or coal tar. Though not a conventionally attractive fragrance by any stretch of the imagination, when I wear it, it is one hell of an aide-memoire, and at my age, any aide to the old memoire is deeply appreciated.

Marescialla is not a bad fragrance - just different. However, let’s not forget that this scent was created almost 200 years ago. It’s truly from a different time, which is what makes it super unique. It smells more like a barbershop fougère than a the spicy-woody scent described on Santa Maria Novella’s website. This is not a fragrance for the weak. Well, the beginning isn’t. It smells like rubber and Listerine. There’s not really a middle, so after the top notes dissipate, you get what you get; and what you get is warm spit and iris-flavored toothpaste. Powdery, warm, and soft. I hate to be so blunt with the description, but it’s true! Regardless, if you enjoy old school Old Spice, you will love this. Now, I read every review I could on this fragrance before purchasing… Which, looking back, were full of vapid, poetic descriptors more than anything. Nothing relatable (hence my bluntness). I mean how am I supposed to know what a witch mopping the floor of an ancient church in autumn is supposed to smell like? Not this. Back in 1828, Marescialla probably smelled so lovely and clean, refined and elegant. But in 2024, Marescialla is a dentists office and the dentist is wearing Old Spice.

The title suggests it, I would like to loosely connect my comment to that of my predecessor. Maresciallo translates to something like sergeant, Marescialla would therefore be the female sergeant, or, historically speaking, more likely the wife of the sergeant. I still cannot associate this designation with the scent even after activating the back of my brain, so this information is just a side note. When Susan brought the sample to our Corona miniature perfume get-together - she knew that I appreciated the brand - I was not yet familiar with Caligari's comment. And I was therefore unprepared for the biting sharp fumes that wanted to wage war on my nose. Marescialla starts off very specifically, yes, unpleasantly. I actually smell something like linoleum wax, reminiscent of the high corridors of our old school (or a police station?), resinous turpentine (perhaps the sergeant's wife is painting?), model glue (?), and a hint of sweetness from an overripe banana (the leftover from yesterday's lunch pack?). I also cannot think of anything that would even remotely compare. I had already internally written off the scent, testing other - more boring - fragrances throughout the afternoon, temporarily losing track of Marescialla. On the way home, however, a fascinating, spicy-soapy scent wafts into my nose. While driving, I try all the previously sprayed body spots within the realm of possibility and quickly find myself lingering at the right elbow. Marescialla develops into a patchouli-wood accord that is not necessarily pleasant but is nonetheless captivating, with the brand's characteristic soapy note embedded within. There is reddish spice, dry earthiness, a hint of banana-like residual sweetness that fits in wonderfully and subordinates itself, there are creaky woods and curling pipe smoke, and indeed mild, Italian soap. Even though I will not be acquiring the scent despite all its captivating fascination and the ultimately not unpleasant development - I am not that masochistic - Santa Maria Novella impressively demonstrates here the range of fragrance directions they are capable of covering with consistent quality. I understand the attraction this scent seemingly has on my predecessor, but I can just barely escape it.

Time and again, the level of exposure and attention a fragrance receives through comments, statements, and the number of users makes me think and despair. I know it is absolutely pointless to use my own feelings as a benchmark for others. And yet, I cannot get past the fact that seven owners have so few comments, statements, and even reviews. Somehow, this also reflects the peculiarity of this fragrance. When I received a sample of it as a gift a few months ago, I initially didn't know whether to be happy or annoyed. Not about the gesture, but about the perfume itself. It was and still is a unique scent, to which I couldn't even name a fourth-degree relative, let alone a fragrance twin. As children, we spent a few days each year at my grandmother's house, which was about 40 kilometers away. She lived in an old farmhouse that, in my perception, had not been significantly modernized since the death of her husband. We children always slept in a small room at the end of the hallway on the upper floor. It contained old furniture from the 1950s and even older. There were no wallpapers on the walls, and a gray mottled linoleum floor framed the rather strange "ambiance" for us kids. There was neither insulation nor heating, so the room was rather damp and somewhat musty. The smell of this room, with all its dreary to morbid aura, is the only thing that even remotely resembles Marescialla. Consequently, I was shocked after the first trial! How did this come about, and who bottles something like this? The feeling was between repulsion and fascination. A few weeks later, I mustered the courage to do a generous day test. This time, my nose was more composed, and the pendulum swung more towards "fascinated." However, had I not had this association from my childhood, the sample would have been discarded long ago. Now, in front of me, is finally a bottle of Marescialla. When I smelled it at the atomizer, I first thought it was off. Like stain remover. Solvent with sharp fruitiness and also somewhat plastic-like. Only the comparison with the sample confirmed that my memory had played a trick on me, as both are identical. I don't know what it wants and what it is supposed to be. And I am completely surprised that there are at least six other people on this planet who are either also fascinated or even attracted to such a scent. In fact, the producer is a monastery pharmacy. And that makes a bit more sense to me now. It could be a) a rub for colds and/or muscular problems or b) a nearly bitter, fruit-infused medicinal (cough) syrup. When I wore it a few days ago while exercising, I was unsolicitedly told that I smelled particularly strong of freshly washed laundry that day. I was prepared for a lot (of criticism) that day, but that was the last straw! Contrary to my usual habits, I cannot, in good conscience, recommend this. I have no target audience in mind and am left puzzled with the bottle. No idea if I will ever wear it again. But I can't part with it either. The bottle comes in a small box with a lid and a separate, screw-on atomizer, which I appreciate (e.g., for the purpose of decanting). However, it doesn't fit back into this packaging with the screw-on atomizer by a few millimeters, which is simply thoughtless and silly. The atomizer has a large output and works reasonably well. The bottles are uniformly printed, by the way. Only a small sticker on the back bears the name of the content. In this case, the bottle has a golden-yellow content, as seen in the photo below by TomLavender. This makes it half a promille more attractive to me. If it looked as milky-creamy as depicted above, I would likely have had to vomit.

After trying Bleu Noir EdT and liking it enough to buy it, I went back to the shop to try the EdP. In my mind I thought I would get more power, more longevity with some minor differences. I was sorely disappointed upon smelling it. No strong opening with the spices. That first contact left me a bit sad since I could not recognize what I believed Bleu Noir should be in its EdP version. Months passed and, despite my initial and almost imediate dismissal, somehow the beautiful blue tinted bottle always seemed to exert some fascination on me whenever I went to the perfume shop. I tried it again on skin some months later and I could then see the similarities between the EdT dry down and the EdP. Adding to that, I had been growing fonder of the dry down of the EdT and some weeks and a couple more tries later I finally decided to buy the EdP. This is a very elegant creamy musky wood based scent, without the spices and strong opening of the EdT. For me this is one of those fragrances that are perfect for the office. I had never worn the EdT in the office precisely because in the first couple of hours it is fairly strong. With this I can finally wear some Bleu Noir to the office without worrying about disturbing colleagues (office has AC, but most days it is a bit wacky and way too warm for my liking). Performance is reasonable for me. It is a discreet scent at all times that does not project much. Longevity is actually very good at 8h-10h+. You get a nice, albeit tight, scent bubble that people who come closer will notice and you'll get whiffs of the fragrance when you move. Highly recommended for anyone who likes musk and woods. Update: after wearing it more I've increased my scent score to 9.5 - I absolutely love this scent. It is discreet but has good longevity and works with any weather. The scent itself is extremely classy and pleasant. Perfect for any occasion, at any time.

There are things subject to opinion, but there are others that absolutely not... And much of what I have read about this perfume, is simply a lie. First of all, I got it... So at least, I know perfectly what I am talking about: I don't write a review based on four snorts on a cardboard. For me - without a doubt -, this perfume is at the highest level of designers quality... And in my honest opinion, one of the best recently launched: the definition of a modern masterpiece. This perfume is deep and fresh, comforting and modern, creamy and elegant... A highly seductive fragrance. The main player here is musk, wrapped in sophistication, romanticism and mystery. Characteristics: - Mood: Sensual, seductive, elegant, classy. - Projection: Moderate. At the opening, it has the length of an arm ( 10h. This scent acts as a deep cloud of refined musky aroma around you, for a looooong time. ... So if you really know the perfume, in no way will you believe the words of someone saying that it doesn't last: Possibilities: - 1: The guy in question simply hasn't been tried the true perfume. - 2: It's a simple lie. - 3: His nose doesn't work or is broken; I have read that some people are not able to detect the smell of musk well, but I don't know if this is really true. - 4: Maybe his body odor is so smelly that it exceeds the perfume; musk is a "bass" smell (making an analogy with sound), which can be completely masked with body odor, if it is excessive. ... But if you are a clean and neat person, this would not be a problem, right..? NOTE: It should be noted that this EDP version it is quite different from the EDT, which is the one that has a slight resemblance to TdH & Declaration. That doesn't happen in this EDP, although the versions still maintain some common DNA. Between the two, I prefer the EDP: It's more elegant, more seductive and lasts longer, but the EDT hits and projects more in the opening, if you're looking for that. It's different... But a solid fragrance, too.

Opens sort of sharp, almost citric I would dare to say, but 5 minutes later, turns into this really nice musky scent, with the undertones of cedar. I wouldn't say is complex or anything really groundbreaking, but I really like it, is sort of a simple but really rich scent. Projection is moderate, about an arms lenght projection, for longevity I get 6 hours on skin, getting strong whiffs during the day, and in clothes, 7 hours or so. I would say this is usable on any weather, except high heat. Ocassions: Office, formalish events, dinner with the family. Day or night I now made the mental connection that musk reminds me of most old school or matureish fragances. Really nice experience with my first fragance by Narciso Rodriguez, still trying to get ahold the original For Him.

This is a great fragrance. It doesn't reinvent the wheel, and will definitely smell familiar to most noses. This woody-musky-fougereish DNA has doubtlessly been done before. However, the blending, quality, and the manner in which Bleu Noir EDP pulls off that DNA off is notable. First off, I will say that I have not smelt the EDT, so I can't say how it compares. I will say, however, that this has absolutely NOTHING to do with Terre d'Hermes beyond the fact that they both contain vetiver and wood. There are shades of Cartier's Declaration here, but only just; this is not by any means a clone of that fragrance. Bleu Noir EDP is dominated by a smooth, creamy, clean musk and supported by woods and amber. null of the spiciness, bitterness, dirtiness, or really complexity of Declaration is present here. This like Declaration trimmed of all its sharpness and edge, rounded off and smoothed over. Overall it is an exceedingly simple fragrance (in the best way) with little evolution which is completely inoffensive, comfortable, and easy to wear. If you love clean musk, this is one of the best in the designer realm for men. As others have commented, this is a fragrance of contrasts. It absolutely lives up to the name "Bleu Noir", i.e. "dark blue". There is definitely darkness here - dark woods, deep amber, rooty vetiver - but there's light, despite the lack of citrus, and transparency too. The musk is at once dense, creamy, and fresh. The mental image I get when I smell Bleu Noir is almost exactly the same as the bottle - a sheet of dark, cobalt blue glass, opaque but transparent enough to see through, with a light shining behind it. Because of the contrasts, I could easily see different facets of the fragrance emerging depending on the weather. I've only worn it in warm weather thus far, and I've been getting mostly the lighter side of things in the heat. At the moment, the dark ebony and cedar only seem seem to emerge in the deep drydown. However, I could easily see this being just as well-suited to the cold as it is to the heat, with the woods and amber taking center stage. It truly fulfills its role as a "blue" fragrance, being a Swiss Army knife that can be used for all occasions in all seasons. I have not had the performance issues that others have had at all. 4-5 sprays lasts me about all day (7-8 hrs) with soft but noticeable projection for the majority of the day and arm's length sillage. It creates a very pleasant but somewhat restrained aura around you, which in my book is the best kind of projection. I'll have to test how well it performs in colder weather, but performance in warm weather has been surprisingly strong. Overall, Bleu Noir EDP is an easy to wear, dark, classy, clean, and sensual fragrance that I've worn the hell out. I think this one has flown under the radar, which is easy to do in this blue designer market. If you wear Bleu Noir EDP, you won't necessarily smell "different" per se (though rest assured, this smells nothing like Bleu de Chanel, Sauvage, Dylan Blue, or Elysium), but you will smell great. For men looking for a great all-rounder that stands apart from the currently trending, I rate this is as a top pick. This is the kind of fragrance that wears like a perfect pair of jeans. It's comforting and cozy, stylish and suave, sleek and a little bit sexy. It's not a statement piece, and it's not even necessarily a huge compliment getter, but what wardrobe is complete without a great pair of jeans? For the price I paid ($56 for 100ml with a great presentation), I couldn't be happier.

I'm a fan of Narciso Rodriguez's frags, I own for Him (EDT and EDP) and the original Blue Noir. They all smell great and the only issue to me is the longevity of Blue Noir which is subpar. That being said I blind bought Blue Noir EDP (on sale) and immediately regreted the purchase after testing it on paper, it was pretty much the same as EDT moreover the reviews in fragrantica were awful pointing longevity as a major issue and smell as cheap however the damage was done. I had to test it so during a rainy afternoon I sprayed it 7 time on myself and the opening was quite nice but when it started to hit the mids the magic began. It's like a creamy musky scent, it does share similarities with the BN EDT but the absence of cardamom is noticable and this makes a difference, it's just gorgeous. As for longevity well, I'm 5 hours in and still going, I doubt I'll get to the 6th which is not stellar for an EDP concentration but it's not awful either (in the tropic all frags last less than other places). My girlfriend loved it, I love it and I can recommend it, just test it first since taste is subjective Update I do get about 8 hours longevity so it's all good, projection is moderate so it's inoffensive, it's not a beast and I'm ok with that @Carlitos01 I like EDT better than EDP too

Just listen to the famous song "Still got the blues " by Gary Moore and close your eyes: imagine the blue notes resounding in the darkness. Well, now imagine all these things made scent: it's Narciso Rodríguez for him.

I have to admit this lasted a lot longer than I thought it would. It lasted my whole 8 hr. work day and then some. The scent is pretty good and office-safe. It is worth buying, in my opinion, and is a good all-season fragrance. I get the musk, cedar, and the ebony scents. It became a skin scent to me around the 7.5-8 hour mark.

I smell the drydown of this fragrance as if it was quite a precise mix between Cartier Declaration, and Azzaro Chrome. If you like either one, you will like this one. Besides that I don't get much more from it. Pretty straightforward: Declaration made fresher by bringing in the scent profile of Azzaro Chrome.

From the start, you do get the similarities to Dior Homme Intense. Not exactly the same, by any means, but elements are there. However, the opening act here doesn’t touch that of Intense, which is fantastic. This has similarities, but isn’t nearly as enticing as the Dior. The iris is present early, as is the signature Narciso Rodriguez musk note.

So I have a decant of this along with blue noir edt extreme and parfum. I was most excited to try this edp version as I had heard its very good and not the typical blue frag. It smells like a medicine cabinet to my nose/ Very old school masculine and medicinal. Its not for me. I would not call this frag blind buy safe, You should for sure sample it.

A bit of a tease, this one.  The gasoline/leather top notes  give the expectation of a true gas-pump fantasy. But along with gasoline’s scent, Nostalgia has gasoline’s volatility.  Still, the crackly woody drydown of Nostalgia is a wonderful scent in its own right, top notes or not. And for those of you who like woody fragrances but don't want a warm, harmonious feeling, Nostalgia remains fairly cool, carrying the chill of evaporation that gasoline has on your skin. Two thoughts. One, this is an interesting option for those still mourning the loss of Fahrenheit’s original formulation. Two, Nostalgia points out that in the language of perfumery, gasoline is a woody note.

Well, I couldn’t say that I spent much time around vintage Italian sports cars; therefore, I don’t know how close to the brief Santa Maria Novella came when they put together Nostalgia, a perfume that, according to the brand, is trying to capture that certain smell. If I didn’t read anything about the backstory of this fragrance and were to dive into it blind, I don’t think that I would have made that association. Yes, it captures specific smells that to me have a nostalgic feel, but I never would have guessed they were hinting at sports cars. As a perfume, this one is quite an oddity. I would have gone as far as to say the weirdest in their line, but then there’s Marescialla. I think both are unusual and difficult, in different ways, since they smell nothing alike. And even so, something is appealing in both. Some bits make me recoil, while there are also parts that I love. Both of them prove to be a “difficult relationship” case for me, and yet they smell so unlike anything else that owning them is the only way to remind myself of such peculiar compositions. The opening of Nostalgia makes me smile, recoil, crave more, and run for the hills, all at once. It hits on all fronts with no backing off: smoky leather, burnt rubber, plastic, glue, wood laminate, turpentine, and an old-school aromatic accord that reminds me of the vintage shaving foam my grandfather used to use. I still don’t know what to make and how to feel about this introduction. Luckily, it settles down quickly, with the lesser appealing facets dissipating and the more appealing ones sticking through. Hence, once the more “synthetic” nuances burn out, what remains is this smoky leather accord, quite supple, not harsh, paired to the aromatic component that is so prevalent in all the house’s compositions, and an increasingly strong resinous warmth with subtle sweetness. It remains distinctive still, but now it feels more recognizable as a perfume and less as chemical warfare. At this stage, if not for the aromatic component that runs through it, it could have been linked to other resinous, smoky, leather perfumes, but the former anchors it nicely into a slot of its own. It’s quite a bumpy ride, one that starts with a crash for me, only to improve as the race moves on. A race in reverse, if you want. I know some folks love the opening, so I guess for them it starts with the number one finish. So yes, a race in reverse, nevertheless, and whether it’s going to be “a crash” or “a win” upon first sniff, it’s up to you. Just be patient, it gets really good shortly after. IG:@memory.of.scents

At first, this has a big hit of fuel (not quite gasoline - maybe more like kerosene) that's odd but not displeasing. When it dries down, it becomes smoky-spicy-savory. It's a denser Bulgari Black with more soul. If you're a fan of BBlack's odd rubber or Lonestar Memories'pungent smoke, you'll probably like this. Unfortunately, this doesn't last long on me, but I don't mind spraying it often to enjoy that delicious drydown over again. (If only it weren't so expensive...) (020911)

Nostalgia is supposed to smell like an Italian racing car on the track, complete with gasoline fumes, rubber seating, and all. During the fleeting topnotes, Nostalgia pulls this off in spectacular fashion with a pure petrol note that would put the current version of Fahrenheit to shame, followed quickly by a shot of sweet car-seat rubber and leather. The smoke and fuel dissipate rather quickly, however, leaving behind a sweet, rubbery, vanillic tailbone that smells rather too close to Bvlgari Black to justify the price (since writing this review, both Black and Nostalgia have been discontinued, so I'm leaving in the reference for the sakes of posterity). The scent is nicely woody and quietly masculine. Beyond the arresting opening, I don't think Nostalgia is particularly challenging. This is just different enough to provide good fun and shock value, but sweet, woody, and generically aftershave-like in the drydown to reassure novices and big ole scaredy cats.

The Mille Miglia is considered the most famous classic car rally in the world - and Nostalgia is likely the perfect companion for it: A fragrance dedicated to a car race. But it contains everything: The rubber of the tires with its signs of wear, a dab of engine oil, leather-covered seats. And not to forget the beautiful Mediterranean landscape of Italy through which the route winds. A few citrusy splashes and creaky Hesperides trees, under which one can perfectly take a cigarette break in the warmth of the early summer sun. Very nice and very special. Masculine and possessing a certain resemblance to Annick Menardo's masterpiece Bulgari Black. However, Black here is more like the trendy bling-bling brother while this candidate is the rugged man-man. And it also maintains an air of understatement. Impressive.

For the 75th anniversary of the 1000 Miles race, which takes place on public roads in Italy, Santa Maria Novella launched this fragrance in March 2002. Since these car races have been conducted as a kind of "orientation drive" for historic vehicles since 1977, the scent has also been formulated with a touch of nostalgia, reminiscent of men's perfumery from the 30s to the 70s.

As a lifelong underpowered user of rusty Dutch bicycles, I must decisively break a lance for this wonderful fragrance. One truly does not need to be a horsepower aficionado to thoroughly enjoy this extremely wearable, characteristic, and by no means exaggerated little potion. Admittedly: the top note is original and captures the theme of "Mille Miglia.

If a perfumer you loved and trusted because he produced one of the best perfumes ever, bribed you to cover his pending betrayal, what would you do? Perhaps I'm being melodramatic. Can't help it. I'm an author and melodrama is one of my instincts. Seriously, though. You might wonder how I managed to own an FB of this back-stabber of a perfume. Well, here's the story. Hubby, who adores the original Narciso Rodriquez For Her above all my other perfumes (being male and captivated by its outright sexiness) and knowing I love rose, happened upon an ad for Fleur Musc and grew excited. Had I heard of it? Wasn't rose a favorite scent and therefore shouldn't this new Rodriquez be a mind-blower? I stared leerily at the ad because my nose (which, fyi, is a little psychic) felt suspicious, but my husband's excitement only grew. It wasn't all that expensive, he said, proud of himself for finding it. Perhaps he could be persuaded to buy it for me, he teased. I couldn't crush his joy. Instead I faked it and said yes. Soon enough the little betrayer arrived, all gorgeous in its dusky pink carton. But what should fall out of the box with it? A watch. Honest! A gleaming gold-toned thing with no insignia, only gold and cream hands on its lovely floral face. What? Grudgingly, I put the watch on I didn't want. Prettily it ticked away, keeping perfect time after I set it. Warily I tried the perfume, which validated my suspicions. Both my nostrils snapped shut immediately in self-defense, warning me to stop smelling asap. Too late. My brain had already detected the chemicals, already smelled notes from flowers that never grew on this earth. Angry that I'd let my husband spend his money on this, I told him the truth. It was dreadful and I'd suspected it all along. He wasn't that wounded. He'd struck out, but knows there'll be another chance at bat. Guys are like that. Me, I just felt completely betrayed and bribed to accept a perfume that has no more business next to the glorious Narciso Rodiquez For Her than a paint can has next to a meadow of wild flowers. All right, all right. I'm probably being too harsh. The whole planet does not have my nose. There are probably many undisturbed by the aromachemicals that cause me instant anosmia. If you're one of them, if you like scents like (gasp) J'Adore, do try this gentle, musky, dusky rosiness. I wish your nose and it happiness together. Pardon me while I find a hammer for a watch. Yes, I'll serve my time in melodrama jail, but first a plea. Dear Narciso Rodriquez, you of the wondrous For Her, please don't abandon us, your admiring customers, to the unworthy artifices that lure perfumers today. Unleash your genius again using the high quality ingredients that once bowed to your creative command. Okay, I'm done. Off to jail.

It is a perfume that inevitably evokes the color pink. Its aroma is pink, but not the typical smell of roses, but rather a clean and cared for rose, since it reminds me of the aroma that the steam gives off when ironing a freshly washed sheet. The base notes are very well combined, giving rise to very subtle woody notes where patchouli stands out, but also powdery notes, where a beautiful and soft violet shines. It is a simple and very youthful aroma. It is very pleasant to smell it throughout the day on your skin and clothes, especially in the spring season. Good projection and performance, lasting 8 hours on the skin.

Lush pink pepper and floral opening - the top is floral, yes, but the florals are so juicy that they almost read like a fruit accord to my nose. People describe it as "dense" or "thick" and I think that's apt. Musk notes come through. Drydown is a nice amber, gives me musk and sometimes a creamy rose. I can see why patchouli is listed, but its a subtle backdrop to the rose and only if you're really searching for it. Dignified, not young but not really mature either. Longevity is decent. I wore this for spring and summer, and when vacationing to warmer climes, for a couple years. I still enjoy it somewhat, but I reach for it much less often as I gravitate towards more complexity and less femininity in my scents.

I was so sad that my signature L'eau was discontinued so I grabbed a 100ml size of fleur musk (to finally find a whole sale bottle on ebay of L'eau). Big bottle, big mistake. It will last a life time because you need so little: a ver dense, overwhelming balmy rose with peony and pink pepper. Impossible to wear in warm weather, leave it for cool and cold nights. It is very loud and has a great sillage. Very feminine and quite sweet. I will leave it for postpandemic life. It is just too much now! It is reachable even through the mask.

I love roses, so rose perfume is something I own a lot of, however, this one is a sample. I tried it last summer, but the longevity was rather short. Now, in the dead of winter, I try it yet again. It’s very strong. One spray and it fills a room. Absurd sillage. That can be good or bad depending on where you’re headed. As for me, I’m only headed into a conference call—alone. I can smell my wrists from my keyboard and it’s strong. Perhaps I would have squirted less of it, but that’s impossible. I love the smell of the rose and peony so much! There is a musk behind them, but this is definitely a floral perfume. The amber softens it and the patchouli is way in the back on me. It’s nearly nonexistent. Overall, the longevity has been poor on my skin, even in winter, but It’s sexy and warm while it lasts.

A more ladylike version of its' urban EDT and EDP sisters. Sweet rose and iris-y musk; instead of that typical laundry musk trail, with a dash of pink pepper in the opening yet lacks the warmth amber brings and "worn up white t-shirt" effect of patchouli in comparison to the original offerings.

A White shirt, a simple and elegant tailleur, a simple veil of make up: this is the modern woman who could wear this scent, as feminin as discrete . A "suggested" bouquet with a powdery touch in a minimal and classy pink bottle.

First, three things: I love Narciso. I hate pepper. I’m into pink. Wonderful, this flanker fits perfectly! Wait, no. There’s something. It’s right there, bold and clear, in the fragrance pyramid: pink pepper. Oh no. Seriously. What is incense for one, vanilla for another, is for me the pepper. I can’t and won’t warm up to it.

"For Her Fleur Musc" reminds me, at least in some aspects, of a good friend of mine, a truly hot number! Blonde, naturally curly lion's mane, endlessly long legs, a voluptuous décolletage, a perfect hourglass figure, sparkling blue eyes, and a radiant smile, plus she is a really kind-hearted person.

My husband is currently in budget mode due to a looming unwanted car purchase. The politicians are only vaguely clearing their throats on the subject. Nevertheless, he pleasantly wandered with me through the fragrance shelves at Kstadt and reached for an appealing pink bottle. Narciso - well, who would say no?

This summer I stayed in Milan, right by Gelsomini station on the M4 metro, and every time I descended the steps to the subway I kept thinking of the Passeggiata del Gelsomino (Jasmine Walk) at the Vatican. This elevated passageway has a great view of St. Peter`s Basilica and in the right season, the most beautiful aroma of blooming jasmine washes over you. I didn`t like Milan. Most of it seemed too new, too commercial, too "cleaned up for the tourists." All the time I was there, I kept wishing I could run away to Rome, a city I love. Wearing this Gelsomino Eau de Parfum while strolling around those sterilized streets consoled me a little. It`s such a beautiful, feminine jasmine, no frills, just the right amount of white flowers and citrus to make you feel fresh, light, presentable. I went through 10ml decant of this pretty jasmine in one week, this is how much I wanted to isolate myself from that fashionable Milanese environment.

The creation of my watchlist is breathtakingly arbitrary. The casualness with which fragrances land on it sometimes astonishes me. And so my nose stumbled completely unprepared over a carefully selected addition: Gelsomino Eau de Parfum Jasmine scents always enchant me, as long as they manage without indolic notes, which is why I boldly moistened my wrist: Bam! A heavy olfactory slap in the face with a whole bouquet of flowers. Ouch! Wait. I need to collect my thoughts. Who am I to review fragrances from the oldest pharmacy in Europe? And now this jasmine wonder, whose ingredients made their way from Goa to the strictly guarded greenhouses of the Grand Duke of Tuscany - Cosimo III de' Medici - in 1688. I can understand old Cosimo. There’s something about this jasmine, once I’ve recovered from the initial shock. Sniff again: There’s natural freshness (bergamot) and a bit of sharpness (pepper). Then there’s a certain kind of indole (I believe), but it doesn’t come off as fecal or urinous, rather it just lets a hint of ammonia waft through the nose. Before I can think about whether I like that or not, Goa Jasmine hits me. This doesn’t come across as delicately monothematic; instead, it has rosy-lemony notes in tow. Ylang-ylang surprisingly contributes a softly honeyed sweetness, which allows the heart note triad to fade harmoniously on the skin. Wait. Did I say “fade”? Wrong word. It lingers, and for quite a while. As befits such a noble and well-protected Medici plant*, it sits somewhat motionless on the skin for hours, allowing itself to be admired for its naturally beautiful floral quality. And I must give Gelsomino credit: the scent truly comes across as naturally beautiful. To my nose, completely free of “synthetics” aka artificial lab sludge vibes. I think of real flowers. Of old alleys in Florence. Of sun-drenched landscapes. Of the Villa Medicea di Castello (as if I knew what it looks like). The chances that this olfactory daydream can also be picked up by my surroundings are not bad: the sillage moves between cultivated restraint and feudal desire for recognition. That’s something to work with! One last sniff for farewell: The musk-cedar combo from the base was announced, but ultimately shied away from making a grand entrance. The radiance of the heart notes is too strong. Probably too intimidating. Lastly, I must mention the pretty bottle, which is shaped in elegant simplicity but knows how to charm with ornate decorations on the cap and logo. In this way, the scent and bottle fit together wonderfully. Flower enthusiasts who like it lush but not too sweet: please give it a try. Thanks to the Medici. *Of course, the Medici did not "invent" or breed Goa Jasmine. Cosimo simply knew how to protect his precious gift from the profane noses of Europe. Gatekeeping deluxe.

Ok, first things first, I have no idea how people are getting Musc Noir or Musc Noir Rose from this, I’m definitely not smelling it (no fruitiness, no suede, no heliotrope, which I personally pick up a lot in MN). Musc Noir is my favorite from the For Her line, but Nude is coming in strong. I find it heavier than Musc Noir, sexier, sweeter, spicier, and kind of darker, almost heady. Nude is a perfect name for it because, to me, it’s definitely a ‘night activity’ perfume. I find Musc Noir also sexy, but also more classy and versatile, I see Nude more as an evening/night scent. I’m not sure I’d personally wear it during the day or in warmer months, but from what I’ve seen, that might put me in the minority, I have no idea what’s going on It might be the tonka beans, which on my skin come off as spicy, sweeter, and almost tobacco-like, while the musk adds a clean quality (the white flowers contribute to that too) and it's powdery, it has a slighlty skanky quality, not in a bad way it has the vibe of perfumed skin after sleeping in it or, honestly, after sex.

Got a tester along with a tinted moisterizer and lipstick that I bought today. I had not expected much of it because I don't like very 'musky' scents. With first spritz I thought: 'No, not my kind of perfume indeed'. I found the opening very heavy. I couldn't relate the scent to any concept of 'nude' at all. After some time however, I got whiffs of a pleasant powder that does not remind me of any other powdery notes in perfumes (nothing babypowder-y I mean). I like the sillage (those whiffs I get) much better than smelling it on my skin directly. But I was wearing Azurēe (2015) today and I think that was taming the sweetness in this scent and Musc Nude tempered the bitterness in Azuree, so I should test this perfume on unscented skin one day (or maybey those two could be a good layering option, but I'm not into layering) Still, I can imagine this to be headache inducing, especially when I sniff it on my skin directly. On the fence with this and for now not something I'll buy because I promised myself that the next perfume I'll buy should be a 100 % love.. But I think it is a well done scent for the right person and a good blend for what it is meant to be.

Wow, is such a lovely soft musk! The name is really fitting, it's a "your clean skin, but better" kind of scent and also a perfect match for the nude-ish, warm pink of the packaging. I see how this is a descendant of Musc Noir and Musc Noir Rose. They all have the same kind of musk, a touch of plum (not listed for this one, but still noticeable!) and a hint of spice. Make no mistake, this is not the musk from the classic NR For Her fragrances, I believe they started a new line of scents centering around a specific kind of musk with Musc Noir. In Musc Nude, it's woven into a very creamy, skin-like, slightly dense scent. To me it's a mix of the DNA of Musc Noir with the creaminess of the older Narciso cubes. If you haven't tried many Narciso Rodriguez scents before, let's just say it's a creamy, clean musk with a surprising darker undertone that only comes out if you pay attention. It's not the completely innocent white musk that feels like clean laundry, it has something subtly seductive about it. A very sensual, but not overtly sexy scent. I'm very impressed by this scent. I already own and love Musc Noir Rose, but I think they're different enough to have both. I haven't smelled this combination of creamy-clean and subtle warm spiciness before, so it stands out from other musks. I might add it to my collection soon.

Instant obsession! This is everything that I imagined Musc Noir Rose to be (mini the performance because MNR has a strong performance). It is creamy, sweet, peppery on the beginning with some weird inky /olive hints for the first hour or so ( yeah I smelled the same thing as other reviewers, but I enjoyed the ink. It adds some character The dry down is pure witchcraft. It so warm and cozy and fluffy I want to drown in it. It lasts 6 hours on my skin so the performance is average for me

This is her signature. Drugstore Musk, pink bubble gum, and cigarettes. Well, darts, technically! For Her Nude is feminine, but also classy-trashy with greasy hair. Not afraid to bust you with a hockey stick or snuggle with you overnight in your house car. Powdery, a bit smoky, a smidge animalic. The opening smells like heliotrope to me, so I get why some folks think this is akin to Musc Noir. Maybe a boudoir version of that. Personally, I like it and know it will get a lot of wear.

Atention, this can be the summer (or at least spring) perfume for people who usually prefers creamy and musky perfumes and struggle to find something for the warmer days! It is true like it feels like a mix of the For her line. The notes list can't sound more boring and generic to me, but this perfume is not generic at all.

Musc nude for her by Narciso Rodriguez is the latest flanker in the for her line. The perfumer is Sonia Constant who has done several works with musc, including Musc K from her own Ella K line. This is a rich musk full of facets with a strong floral component, it has some waxy oily facets as well. For more details please check out my YouTube video where I review this perfume.

Recently, I stumbled upon this new Narciso sprout here on Parfumo. “Sounds interesting…” thought my fragrance heart, and during my next visit to the turquoise scent dealer, the beautiful bottle immediately caught my eye. I must admit, I already love the Narciso bottles for their simple, elegant, and completely opaque design.

When I first sprayed this blind buy on my skin, I initially thought, "Oh oh... something floral in the direction of lily... I don't like that!" But after 5 minutes in the fresh air, that note had vanished for me, and I sensed a vibe of Musc Noir Rose, as well as Pure Musc, and Poudrée.

The rain patters against the skylight, an endless staccato of drops. Plop. Plop. Plop. She no longer consciously registers the sound; it has become background noise as she lies on the bed staring at the ceiling. Time and again, tears gather in the corners of her eyes and run down her cheek. She doesn’t wipe them away. Thoughts spiral in her head. How they met.

This house has an amazing range with something for almost anyone's taste, but almost criminally under-discussed in fragrance circles. This one has also made me want to explore the note of oppoponax more in perfume. Hope you enjoy and thank you.

Why music? Because it's the title of a favorite, intentionally eclectic album by guitariste extraordinaire Joe Satriani, and it fits. Opoponax is Strange indeed. Sun-drenched, earthy, tobaccoey, leathery, hay-like, dusty, markedly medicinal and un-perfumey, rich, big and joyous yet somehow quiet and contemplative... Bitter-sweet. Therapeutic and mind-cleansing like incense in church. Opoponax is Beautiful. Beautiful in a way a bigboned villager might be, healthy, fullblooded, with perfect, if a bit dry from all the sun, freckled skin and laugh lines in the corners of the eyes. Not a trace of makeup, anemia or pretence. It's straight talking, delivering down to earth, biblical wisdom, not pseudo esoteric Coelhian cliches. As far as Music goes, Opoponax very evidently consists of one and only note, sang in a husky, smoked voice, and yet it couldn't be farther from monotonous or one-dimensional. It evolves constantly, sweeping through sun-beaten fields and shadowy olive groves, touching down in the stables and on the beach and finally landing in the soft, furry, Shalimar territory hours later. Simple and great.

After reading the ingredients and good reviews about Opoponax, I had high expectations for the fragrance. Since I love Italy, especially Florence, and visited there on a field trip during my studies a few years ago, I had to get a scent from this house. Unfortunately, due to COVID, I can't go there at the moment, so I ordered the fragrance blind. I expected something spicy and woody, but on me, it smells citrusy, fresh, and a bit mossy. So exactly what I actually don't like. The scent lasts maybe 2-3 hours on me, and the sillage is virtually non-existent. I'm also starting to wonder if a wrong fragrance was bottled in the flacon. Nevertheless, I will keep it for the peak summer and test if it performs better then. Still, I am somewhat disappointed now, as the price-performance ratio is very poor. I hope that the house has better fragrances than this one, but hopefully next time I can test it on-site.

The master sits in his workshop and stares at his workbench. He is surrounded by the finest woods and his tools. The air is filled with the scent of shavings and the work of all the years. He has created great things here, sculptures as tall as a man and figures as small as his thumb. Throughout the realm, he is known for his works. When he sees a piece of wood, he recognizes the inner form of the figure hidden within and only needs to uncover it. This has always been the case, a gift since his childhood. However, he has not started a new work in months. Better said, he has started one, but he will not finish it… It was months ago when he placed a cedar block on his workbench and contemplated it. He saw the form before him, as he always had. So he took his steel and made the first cut. But then the miracle or the curse happened, depending on your perspective. Sweet resin dripped from the cut and filled the workshop with its scent. He had never smelled anything like it before. So captivated was he by the spicy aroma that he only later realized that he could no longer recognize the shapes in the woods. He had lost his gift. The wound in the cedar block, however, never closed; the resin remained forever fresh. So the master sits before his workbench, gazing at the cedar block and breathing in the spicy air. He has enjoyed the fruits of his gift for many years and created great things. Now he can only take pleasure in the scent. He sighs lightly, takes his needles in hand, and knits the next sock… ---------- With Opoponax, Santa Maria Novella has created a brilliantly simple fragrance. Many warm woods, with cedar bringing a fresh, lemony note. Then add Opoponax, balsamic, spicy, sweet (but not too sweet), and it's done. Perfectly simple - simply perfect? Not quite, as the longevity is rather modest for me, lasting 3-4 hours on skin, 4 to 5 hours on fabric, so unfortunately far from an unending source. Still, a great scent. Platonic thanks to Toppine for the sample!

Lily of the Valley is a flower dear to my heart, it was the favorite of an aunt that isn’t no longer with us, and forever will remind me of her. She had gifted me a plant of Lily of the Valley; and I was sniffing them when they bloom, their scent is so pretty and iconic, I knew I had to search for a Lily of the Valley scent and my choice was this from Santa Maria Novella. This brand makes fragrance so beautiful it’s hard to keep up. Mughetto is exactly like a Lily of the Valley scent, but it’s also pretty and dainty with a touch of powder somewhere. This is something I could imagine a Jane Austen character wearing (well, like several perfumes from the brand). Absolutely adore this!

Lily of the valley. I couldn't stand it for a long time. I found its scent somewhat penetrating. I always smelled something like wall paint when testing a lily of the valley perfume. I associated the scent with something artificial, ugly. But since I got to know and own Coralie from Ikiryō, everything has changed. I love this wonderful, almost a tiny bit dirty soap foam scent of lily of the valley. And which house does it best as a soliflore, if not Santa Maria Novella? Oh yes! Anyone looking for a beautiful, authentic, and wonderfully cozy soft lily of the valley scent should indulge in Santa Maria Novella Mughetto. For me, it epitomizes a bubble bath fragrance. So comforting, so relaxing, so clean, so beautiful. And yet there is a tiny bit of dirt that continually greets and can never be completely washed away. Jasmine is present here as well, just like in Coralie. And a very delicate indole, which never really comes off as dirty, cannot be denied here either. Mughetto could be the grandmother of my dearly beloved Coralie. They are certainly related. Both are dominated by lily of the valley and jasmine. Both have a delicate sweetness. In Mughetto, it's benzoin, while in Coralie, it's Ikiryō's dirty musk, which always brings a bit of sweetness along. Mughetto always appears very classic and pure, while Coralie interprets the theme a bit more modern. Even though this is a thoroughly Italian cologne, Mughetto mentally transports me to Great Britain. I see green meadows, many sheep, and young women frolicking through the blooming landscape. They unmistakably smell of Mughetto. Soapy, clean, and at first glance pure and innocent. But they have a lot of mischief behind their ears. Beautiful. Simply beautiful. The house of Santa Maria Novella has once again convinced me. Many thanks to Gandix for the opportunity to test.

Does anyone else smell eucalyptus in here? There's something that gives Lana a steamy spa-like allure that is sooo freaking captivating. I can't stop smelling my wrist! As always with Santa Maria Novella, this is such a sophisticated scent. Definitely close to the skin, but oh so memorable. I am in love

i'm paraphrasing a review i posted on fragrantica a few months ago--i'm moving all my stuff over here but i couldn't not talk about my girl lana. i bought this on a trip to italy a few months ago: i tried it in store and left without it, but couldn't stop thinking about it for days, so i had to go back. i've worn it a TON since then. lactonic scents are often too cloying for me, but this one isn't too sweet. like sandalwood, figs, and rose petals steeped in milk. musky and understated, but with good sillage and longevity (especially for an eau de cologne). it's comforting, but still sophisticated. not overconfident, just comfortable. it's definitely not blind-buy safe: some people whom i've shown it to have really disliked it.

I’m going to stick my neck out and invent a new fragrance category: the “Vegetable Gourmand” LANA starts with a distinctly noticeable fig note.....mixed with something herbal......I can’t perceive cardamom - as I know it -....perhaps it’s not the pods but the leaves that have been used here..? That would at least explain the kitchen herb aspect.... Next comes the olfactory main impression of this fragrance: PAPRIKA.....to be specific “Ratatouille”......that’s exactly how it always smelled in my kitchen when I was going through my one-year vegan phase.... Unfortunately, you wait in vain for a dessert....it remains at “Ratatouille” ....a bit better cooked over time... Musk and woods..? Hmm...well....with a lot of goodwill and an extraordinarily sensitive nose...maybe.....personally, I only perceive tiny little dots.....so to speak the “spices” in the Ratatouille.... I perceive LANA as an outright food scent....the “healthy” ones, of course.....the ones from the organic store.... No trace of LANA (wool)....it could of course be that the name reference to “wool” is more about the hand-knitted sheep wool sweaters of some organic consumers (shame on me ;-)..) Even though I personally can’t relate to this “vegan kitchen atmosphere” at all, I can still imagine that the fragrance will find its followers....possibly among the PHILOSYKOS lovers.....Because: It’s definitely not poorly made :-)

I am a huge Narciso Rodriguez fan, I think the house has given us some of the best perfumes and some of the most iconic as well, I have never smelled anything bad from the house, they do align with my preferences that much. My signature smell is the Narciso Poudree my favorite so far from the For Her line is Musc Noir as I discovered from a sample some days ago and I also think that the male perfumes are severely underappreciated as well, so imagine my shock when the All of Me came out and the negative reviews started to flow. I hadn't had the opportunity to smell it for myself so I put a sample immediately when I found it online some days ago and I have to say, that I understand but also don't understand the negativity around this fragrance. As other commentators said most people were comparing it to their favorite fragrance from the house especially the For Her line and I think this is where All of Me lost, but there was no reason for a battle either. I can understand people comparing, but the perfume is a stand-alone and not in the For Her line. Notes on the official site: white peony, geranium bourbon, rose centifolia, heart of musc, sandalwood So, All of Me is a very flowery fresh perfume. It is pretty but nothing extraordinary. At the opening personally got more magnolia than peony as listed in the notes of the official NR site and I am not the only one as I have seen. I get a very prominent fresh magnolia smell after it sets the rose and the geranium come forth as well and it continues to be a very fresh flowery perfume, I don't get synthetic, I don't get creamy or woody I only get a very fresh, very flowery, but light floral not at all screechy or heavy and slightly powdery smell, but the minuscule powder I get it is from the flowers and not from the musk. The musk is kinda non-existent. Even after it completely sets the wood and the musk are not present, I personally cannot detect them maybe if I stick my nose to my wrist I can smell a tiny bit of the musk, but the sandalwood not at all. The perfume is a very light flowery scent, that is very fresh, it is not a bad smell at all, it is actually quite pretty, but with not much depth or longevity. I know people who have issues with NR and longevity in many perfumes but I never had an issue, the perfumes last, it is just that the sillage, especially after some time, is very very intimate and I personally like this, here the longevity is an issue the perfume after around 3-4 hours was not there it was not the intimate sillage. The absence of the sandalwood and the musk have hurt the longevity and the depth of the fragrance even if the smell itself is dainty and pretty. Unlike many NR perfumes is not for every season imo, it is more of a spring perfume, and maybe for a very crisp, sunny, bright, winter morning as well and that is ok, it shouldn't be because the perfume is not in the For Her or the Narciso line. The perfume's biggest flaw is the longevity and the lack of depth I think with a slight reformulation, to make the musk and the wood prominent after some time, people would actually give an equal amount of love to this fragrance as they do for other NR perfumes. Smell: 6.5 -> It is a very fresh, delicate, dainty, pretty floral. I would give more if I could smell the musk and the sandalwood, but I can't so... Longevity: 4 -> 4 hours, 4 points Sillage: 6 -> For as long as the perfume is there the sillage is not that bad or intimate, for sure people on the other side of the table won't smell you, but the person next to you might give a compliment for the cute flowery scent. It's not Poudree where people first smell me and then see me for example. Ok, All of me is not "that girl", I will not invest in a full bottle not even in a smaller one after the sample empties, except if a reformulation occurs, but many reviews I found dramatic AF

Narciso Rodriguez used to be easy to categorize. They had two different kinds of musky DNA, one for the Narciso line (cube bottles) and one for the For Her line (tall bottles). I was always a big fan of the cube. In recent years, some newer flankers came out that didn't follow the familiar pattern even though they came in the same bottles. Musc Noir for example doesn't smell like For Here, and Narciso Cristal and Ambrée don't have a lot in common with the (sadly discontinued!) original white Narciso EDP. So I guess it was time for something completely new. But this? I don't understand it. It isn't a distinctive new take on musk, like For Her and Narciso were when they were new. It's musky, yes, but very vaguely so. Also floral and powdery. I can definitely smell rose, and after looking at the notes I can see magnolia, too, but it's all so undefined. The notes get lost in the blend. Now I don't mind inoffensive daytime scents and I don't think that every perfume has to reinvent the wheel. But some scents are just boring and unimaginative, and this is one of them. If someone told me this was from Yves Rocher or some random drugstore brand like Betty Barclay or s.Oliver, I wouldn't doubt it for a second. Meh. It's just so okay, nothing more than that. Bring back Narciso EDP!

In recent months I’ve been testing more designer fragrances alongside niche simply to get a better sense of what that segment truly offers. But most of the time, I can’t even keep them on all day: many are so unpleasantly synthetic that they make me feel physically uncomfortable. However, I’m a big fan of Narciso Rodriguez, particularly the Narciso line and the For Her line. The cube fragrances are wonderfully rich, effortlessly chic, and deeply indulgent. The For Her line, by contrast, has a charm rooted in purity and a breathable texture. And unlike many brands whose flankers vary wildly in quality, I genuinely think every fragrance in the For Her collection stands on equal footing, none have been a flop. All of Me, however, is completely different from previous NR releases. It slips into the category of countless other designers by being an impersonal floral fragrance. The opening is promising - fresh and natural, like a morning walk through a garden when flower petals are still damp. The aroma even reminds me more of Mangolia than the notes listed. I only wish this phase lasted longer. After about fifteen minutes, the scent shifts into a typical designer profile, and a slightly unpleasant synthetic edge starts to bother me. The clear, bright, airy freshness disappears, replaced by a sharp, somewhat pungent floral mix. It will certainly appeal to those who generally enjoy designer fragrances, but I’ve always loved the white musk in Rodriguez’s creations, especially the way it’s used, and it simply doesn’t show up here. That white musk has been the special element that made so many niche-fragrance lovers fall for NR in the first place.This fragrance has no Narciso Rodriguez dna at all. Sandalwood is also one of my favorite notes for adding soft creaminess, so I’m baffled by where it’s supposed to be in this fragrance. You can’t smell it at all - instead, it seems to give the fragrance a thick, waxy feel rather than the creamy quality a genuine or well-executed sandalwood accord provides. As for the floral notes, I won’t go into further detail: they just don’t smell realistic. Unfortunately, All of Me ends up having the same issue I encounter with so many basic designers: the initially pleasant, momentarily charming opening devolves into a repulsive, overpowering chemical muddle. I truly can’t imagine wanting to smell this for even an hour. Thank you for reading, I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

Since there are many new fragrances on the market at the moment, I had to check things out at the Karstadt perfumery. The scent-sensitive husband accompanied me. First, I headed towards L`elixir by La Vie est belle, as I like their flankers. But the husband wrinkled his sensitive hunting dog nose and indicated that this flanker didn’t make the cut for him. However, he pushed me further to the Narciso stand, as I also host a few Narcisos. And lo and behold, he lingered beside me as I sprayed all of me. Its sweetness is light and lovely, and it dances a bit out of the straight Narciso line. I find it a successful outing. The flowers harmoniously blend together, and even the tuberose is not too dominant, but willingly integrates into the floral ensemble. Amber is a soft cushion on which the flowers are presented. A captivatingly feminine scent that even elicits a nod of approval from the critical husband. Narciso has skillfully taken a new path here.

Everyone tears apart this beautiful new powder fragrance, which could well be described as a blend of Narciso, Narciso Poudre, Narciso Cristal & Fleur Musc. Many are bothered by the apparent chaos and refer to it as "mush" of all previous Narciso scents. This happens when one approaches it with the expectation of a linear, uniform fragrance and only tests it briefly. I also approached the sample this way and was disappointed. Now I love it and am already looking forward to when it can move in with me. It is an absolute all-rounder, although I will only wear it for business appointments like all the others from Narciso, as it creates a very clean, pleasant, calm, peaceful atmosphere. Recently, for example, I had applied a bit too much of Narciso Poudre and was about to apologize when my colleague reassured me and said she thinks it’s very nice. The bottle looks unremarkable at first glance. However, upon closer inspection, it fits much better in the hand (-Taache) than its angular predecessors. The matte and elegant gold design and the subtle lettering also impress with understatement. Overall, it can be said that it is a successful fragrance that, especially for fans, often needs a bit more than the 0.6 ml sample to adjust. However, if you allow yourself to embrace it, you have a wonderful companion - a daytime scent that is wearable in all seasons and appears as subtle and peaceful as hardly any other among all the loud new releases this year.

I received a small tester and tried the fragrance yesterday. Of course, I had read a few reviews beforehand and didn't really want to believe that the scent was rated so negatively. Unfortunately, I have to agree with all the negative reviews. The fragrance is not what I would expect from a house like NR. The scent itself is nothing special.

I have to say I don't understand all the negative reviews. And that was actually the main reason for me to write a review here :) At first quite floral, but after one or two hours it becomes wonderfully powdery and still has something distinctive "lasting." I've only had it for a week and have already been approached several times.

As John Legend beautifully describes or sings, I love everything about this fragrance. I absolutely cannot understand the negative review and was a bit shocked by it. But as they say, you can't argue about taste! For me, this perfume is an absolute feel-good scent that works anytime and anywhere.

"All Of Me | Narciso Rodriguez" came to me as a manufacturer sample in one of my beautiful gift packages, and I tested it yesterday. Before the test, I was quite surprised by the numerous negative reviews.

I have various fragrances from Rodriguez, which mostly smell very similar. I like that this scent does not smell like most Rodriguez fragrances. It is beautifully powdery-floral without becoming too sweet. Wearable in every season. I cannot understand the negative reviews, and it does not deserve them. For me, it is a very beautiful scent.

Muschio Oro translates roughly to Gold Musk, which sounds rather Italian Gigolo-ish (or at least it does to me). It is an extremely soapy white musk with a bright, sharp edge to it, like a sheer wash of sulfates. I suspect the presence of aldehydes, although they are not listed. It is not unpleasant, but there are far better white musks out there (including SMN's own Muschio, the original) unless you are deliberately seeking to replicate a fond memory involving anti-bacterial soap. For people who want to smell aggressively clean and shower-fresh at all times, I suspect this fragrance (and Fresia) would be their idea of heaven.

Because I'm a musk girl, I absolutely wanted to have this fragrance. I have already found my blissful musk (Muschio Nobile), and many other pleasant musk sidekicks from delicate to smart, but there's always room for more, that's my idea ;-). I stumbled upon the website of a Berlin online shop (highly recommended, by the way) thanks to a tip from a Santa Maria Novella fan among us Parfumos, and there I immediately spotted the beautiful bottle with the deep golden liquid of Muschio Oro. Aaah! Golden musk! Velvety, creamy, oily, animalistic, and highly sensual, musk on my skin is generally melting and without fuss, it was instantly ordered blind! The desire overwhelmed me, my mind stayed in the cool apartment as I picked up the phone on the summer-hot home terrace and inquired about various options in the shop, ordered 2 samples (free) and then subsequently placed my order online. Rarely have I awaited a fragrance as eagerly as this one. Muschio Oro has a beautiful bottle. Muschio Oro is of a beautiful amber-golden color. But Muschio Oro does not smell golden, but rather platinesque. The golden drop transforms into matte, cool metal as it touches my skin, heavy and very soapy at the same time. The opening is almost sharp; I gasp for air. Not sharp-alcoholic, but sharp-soapy, almost hard and cutting. Now it’s time to wait. Will the golden sun rise again once the soapiness has faded? After about an hour of waiting, I must admit: this is something for fans. For specialists. For extremists. And now I quote the really very friendly and helpful gentleman from the aforementioned shop, whom I called a few days later to share my experience with the fragrance: “This musk fragrance is for absolute experts and connoisseurs. It’s more of a fragrance for gentlemen. For special gentlemen. Gentlemen in pinstripe suits and brown shoes. Gentlemen who love gardening and drive vintage cars. Italian gentlemen also appreciate this fragrance very much.” But since I’m a girl, don’t wear pinstripe suits, own only a pair of old-school Puma sneakers and a pair of summer sandals as brown shoes, which surely cannot be meant here, and also don’t drive a vintage car, and my gardening is limited to reluctantly mowing the lawn about every 2 weeks in the summer, I probably don’t belong to the target group (and I’m certainly not an Italian gentleman). This is also reflected in the fragrance. As it develops, it at least redeems me with increasing smoothness and depth; it becomes softer and warmer, but only a little, and it is still most beautiful on the blotting paper that I have had lying on my dresser for a few days after filling some sample drops from the pouring bottle. Whenever I walk by, I catch a fine, elegant whiff of musk that is not piercing, not cloying, not soapy, but simply the noblest musk in its highest potency. By the way, everything has already been said about the fragrance development, in case one should feel that the information about the fragrance itself is somewhat lacking. It should be noted that it has a reasonable longevity for a cologne concentration (about 4-5 hours), an elegant projection strength (well perceivable, but doesn’t disturb anyone), and once again the appreciation of the dreamily beautiful bottle, which inspires fantasies of various kinds. In my humble opinion, the quality of Santa Maria Novella fragrances is beyond any doubt, and whoever considers themselves part of the target group for this special gentlemen's musk or is curious about this expert fragrance experience is welcome to contact me. Because since I’m a girl, I will never be able to empty the 100ml until the end of time. However, next month, I have decided to order the Angels of Florence, as I have already had the chance to test them and have received approval from several sources, including my own, the reasonable brain side ;-).

Scentrack Fun Lovin' Criminals - Love Unlimited Musc has a deliberately synthetic nature (an undeliberate oxymoron). It is created to expose all the multiple nuances of synthetic molecules. It possesses strong contemporary, cold, but sexy urban vibe. Red berries from the start are easily detectable, but they don’t smell like natural berries. More like a sweet shadow of red berries. They are present, but cannot vouch they are not some kind of olfactory mirage. The iris is again semisynthetic with wet powdery aspect. It reminds me of entering the flower shop with its humid atmosphere. The musk is huge, and also multifaceted. At one point is clean, like a clean cotton candle, on the other some darker amber, animalic note emerges. However, this dark side is well hidden and not easily detectable. Probably the Janus-like musk is created by using the multiple musky molecules, like a Takasago’s Musk T or Oxalide T, but one should be a professional to distinguish these complex musky aspects. Deep in the background, I sensed some already smelt part of the original For Him like a touch of patchouli (could be also a part of the dark side of musk) and green violet leaf fougere tendencies.

Musk is a cornerstone of perfumery, yet, daring solid musky fragrances are few as fingers! What a surprise. For Him Musk is one of those challenging musk-oriented fragrances. The perfume begins with the same dirty animalic sweetness of musk glands. This straight manner repulses me a bit but since I'm a fan of musk I really can't stop sniffing. Sniffing loyalty and pureness. For Him Musk begins with musky fruity aquatic theme and powdery iris note in the base. The iris note is not so premium but this lack is covered by good accord of musk. Not mentioned here, but apparently coumarin and very slight dose of vanilla intervene the base of the fragrance. Longevity: 7/10 Sillage: 6/10 Scent: 6.5/10

Musk perfumes are quite rare, especially among the men's fragrances. It is a special type of fragrance: not that much complex but always neat as a pin! They are a delight to those who want an air of cleanliness and trimness around themselves. Perfumes like those of Musc Collection do not achieve that by linking to the type of scents that can be found in so many deodorants and shower gels, they invoke the idea of trimness as it comes from cosmetic remedies like hand cream and balms. I'd like to presume that those creamy-floral perfumes rather appeal to the ladies – who are then supposed to buy a fragrance like Narciso Rodriguez' Musc Collection for their lovers. Musc Collection for Him is creamy, soft and floral – and only the flowers may be a bit more discreet compared to the ladies' scents of that type. I think one or another musk is floral in itself, however, not smelling like a particular flower. To present Musc Collection for Him as a gent's frag seems rather a marketing decision, the scent itself is not more than unisex. This reasonable priced mass market perfume offers a decent quality. Only the longevity is a bit short. However, there are alternatives both less or more expensive. If you want to save money, the Musk by the traditional Berlin brand of Harry Lehmann would also be an acceptable choice, and in the niche sector Keiko Mecheri shows us with their Musk that such a perfume does not have to be boring. It can be vibrant, sensual and seductive – and this is the reason why I do not need Musc Collection for Him.

First of all i love work of Maison Francis Kurkjan . He is really a genius perfumer . I had few experience with real musk fragrances and Areej La Dore War & Peace 2 is one of them . War & peace was like a Musk Bomb , very Animalic realistic musk and also the Musk Noble from Guerlain which is also a fantastic Musk Based fragrance . Ok lets talk about Narciso Rodreguez for him EDP . The bottle design looks fantastic , the bottle itself symbolizes the Musk . I tried a decant from a Frag Brother and the first impression was Ohh !!! its a floral fragrance and its a proper unisex fragrance but after half an hour i changed my perception . It changed and became clean musky with little animalic vibe and the floral part was also there but in the background . And it became very manly at that time , now my statement is its just for men only . This is really a good performer and if you love floral fragrance with twist , you may give it a try . Mt overall rating - Solid 8.5/10

We cannot forget the scent of musk. It is a damp, earthy, and good smell that permeates the nostrils and the memory, the aroma of mystery. With strong persistence, raw material with an unusual odor, with hints of undergrowth, evoke the earth, wood, damp leaves, and autumn walks. Even though all of humanity knows the name of musk, nowadays, few people have had the privilege of smelling it. It was the scent of kings and emperors, and the mere mortal could only smell it in the wake of the mighty of the earth. Its reputation as a powerful aphrodisiac is because of the very animal and almost corporal smell that gives the wearer an enormous charge of physical attraction. Better than fantastic and better than fabulous, it creates an orgasmic aura of happiness. There are two types of musk in perfumery: the animal one and the vegetable one. If you are like me, you cannot avoid associating the smell of animal musk with the bush's scent, the natural smell of the human pubis. That sensual smell is close to the mushroom's earthiness. It has nothing to do with the synthetic white musk created in the laboratory that is reminiscent of clean, blackberry, and fresh laundry. I accidentally ordered this by mistake. I thought I ordered the EDT version. Damnation. I went ahead, opened it, and sprayed it off. It was an instant attraction; I like heavy floral scents. I like Iris, and this is an Iris bomb at the start of the explosions. Clean, soapy, musky. Pure elegance. It's so good. Musk plays a fundamental role in Narciso Rodriguez for Him and evokes the idea of wool in grey and earth tones. It's a fragrance built on musk and iris root, creating a soft greyness that is intimate, and unlike many masculine fragrances, it isn't afraid to embrace femininity. It's an earthy, grainy musk with hints of spicy pink peppercorn and mushrooms. There is a hint of the original about the fragrance on my skin, so I assume the pyramid of notes is misleading and reductive. It opens with a honeyed floral accord. The first spray is a smooth, healthy musky green iris with a noticeable dash of pepper. The pink spice adds a sweet aroma to the concoction. It is very thin and well done. It's such a distinctive smell that it cannot be confused with other peppers, namely white, green and black. The initial phase lasts quite a few minutes, and it is not like the citrus Hesperides that vanish in a while. Its heart comes with the gentle, musky, and powdery accord. Soothing musk blended with orris wrap my body as a tender puff of talcum after a relaxing bath. The way the perfumer uses the iris here is dramatic and sensual. I do not find a lipstick vibe, as in Dior Homme, instead of something wetter and leafy, as if violet leaves were there, either, but not the combatants of perfumes like Grey Flannel, rather full of a sappy vibrancy and sweet. I'm not sure why violet leaves aren't listed in the pyramid of notes, because for me, this is an incredibly smooth and straightforward fragrance that showcases a greyish floral violet note mixed with and backed by powerful animal musk. The middle stage is very flowery and may cause some to reject it too soon. Wait for the tour because once it melts around half an hour later, it becomes a musk demon. The dry down results in a tactile, woody, and earthy accord. Oh, what a joyful and elegant musky thing this is. That sweet and perfectly matching musk blends perfectly with a soft woody powder that sings the choir's voices. It softens a lot as it dries and gets a little warmer and more floral and not as edgy, but keeps the base green and earthy. The longer it dries, the better it gets. The green and super dry earthiness fades more and more and leaves mostly the slightly powdery floral notes. It is still greenish but not as dry as a bone, not as earthy, and much softer than in the opening. Intense is the more formal version of the classic For Him, and it has a very seductive scent on my nose. It's warm, hugs the wearer, encourages terrible thoughts, isn't overbearing at all, and is incredibly polished—a manly smelling EDP. The smell starts relatively healthy, as YSL Kouros does, but then settles into a pleasantly fresh and clean fragrance. It could be the perfect suit and tie for the well-dressed metrosexual. The perfume is a beautiful cologne of class next to the skin. People will smell you, but you won't shock them. The original, which smells like wet asphalt, is much more impressive in terms of performance. However, this fragrance smells very good and is more bitter than sweet, in my opinion. To sum up, what a musky bomb indeed, I think this perfume by Narciso Rodriguez is an excellent EDP. It is brighter, more transparent, smoother, and more lively than the EDT, which I am very fond of. An intense essence, very seductive, which incites, but does not provoke, with a very virile tone. Very dry, almost to the point of being a bit sharp. It looks quite green and almost earthy, and even a bit moldy. Its scent envelops you like a warm blanket. It's often heard when spreading from the chest to the nose, but it also has a subtle quality that doesn't offend from a distance. It suits the cold days and nights of winter. However, on a foggy spring morning, you feel encouraging without using Hesperides. -Elysium

I wanted to love this, and I got an excellent deal on a 100ML bottle. The opening is beautiful. An ozonic, cool, iris. It forms an instant cloud of fragrance which is dense and palpable. I really haven't smelled anything like it. It smells like the color grey. It smells futuristic. After 5 minutes, this fragrance becomes anathema to me.

It's intense alright, a blast of musk you're wearing and while standing in the crowds, one will go up to you and ask what is it you're wearing it smell so good. Probably like aged whisky barreled within oak wood. Upon releasing, it's smooth yet refined. This intense is like NR for him but the musk is stronger and very soft. When you are wearing this, you won't go unnoticed.
