I'm not sure why violets aren't listed in the note pyramid, because to me this is an extremely smooth and simple fragrance that showcases a grayish floral violet note blended and backed by a powerful white musk. The iris note is also very white, airy, and floral.

Narciso for Him - This for me smells too musky and has a dark vibe to it. Something about this fragrance reminds me of the musty smell of a damp concrete building and is not pleasant. Although it has good projection and silage I think this is over rated and I fail to appreciate the scent. I regret the purchase!

This was an unexpected surprise. My first contact with For Him was at a Department store where while browsing through fragrances the girl helping me suggested Narciso Rodriguez, she sprayed the EDT version and I fell in love with the scent.

In 2019, I bought 4 packs in Seoul and brought them home. W.Dressroom produces "dress perfumes" or room sprays, which can mostly be used as a quick "freshen up" sprayed on oneself in between. Especially in summer, these "refreshers" are very popular: the subway in Seoul smells exactly like these sprays. It envelops you in a wonderful "fresh laundry/freshly showered" cloud, and you feel refreshed, especially on hot and stuffy summer days! I would definitely describe the scent as "artificial" or reminiscent of fabric softener. For anyone who simply wants an uncomplicated spray that makes others think, "Oh, how can he/she still smell like freshly showered/fresh laundry after such a long day?", I recommend this spray!

...in Italy. Perhaps even by Lake Maggiore. The sun is blazing and the air is filled with an incredible heat. I am sitting by the water in the shade of ancient trees, and for a brief moment, a cool refreshing breeze sweeps over to me. I am wearing Verbena! Verbena starts sensationally!...with a herbaceous, bitter, and fresh verbena note. Citrusy, cool, and edgy. I also think I can sense lemons or lemon peels. After about two hours, the scent settles and becomes close to the skin. It calms down and creates a beautiful aura around me. Verbena becomes softer, more delicate, and hugs the skin. The longevity is enormous, and the sillage is very noticeable in the first two hours. Verbena is a beautiful fragrance for midsummer. I find this scent to be definitely unisex, as long as the ladies are not afraid of herbaceous, green notes. Summer can come :-)

Narciso Rodiquez has a way with musk. This isn't the most potent scent ever, but it's certainly an hypnotic Rose, Iris adding a lovely muted twist. Though Essence doesn't begin to challenge the incomparable Narciso Rodriquez for her, it's a superior and entrancing floral and affordable, too--more seductive, more interesting than most rose scents. A fortuitous blind buy indeed.

I'm not usually one for soapy, clean fragrances, however Essence by Narciso Rodriguez is more than just pleasant, it's lovely. One reviewer termed this fragrance the 'laundry queen'. While the scent does remind me of crisp, white linen, this scent is not overly sharp, laundry detergent or anything like nose-burning soap. The floral notes are what balances out this fragrance. The rose and iris notes take on an almost powdery quality which compliments the rich, soapy scent well. Essence is very pure in a way. Innocent, delicate and refreshing. There is a tiny touch of sweetness towards the drydown which reminds me that Essence is more than just clean sheets swaying in the breeze. This fragrance although not overly complex, is enough to capture me with its musky charm. The lasting power is very good and the sillage rather average, but certainly not soft, it has a presence. I find this fragrance far more superior than Narciso Rodriguez for Her, which I found disappointing to say the least.

I found Essence Iridescent to be very similar to Essence, with a little more glam and glitter. If Essence is your HG musk, than you won't be disappointed. If you are unfamiliar with the differences between the NR for Her iterations and Essence... I can only say, that for me, where NR for Her was a definite "No" in all it's formats, Essence poses a definite "Maybe", due to the switching of the 'sexy Egyptian musk' with a slightly less raunchy daytime version of musk and a bright, clean powdery iris and rose complex. Back to that NR Essence signature musk note- you'll find a generous dose here that seems to pop up a few minutes earlier than in the original Essence. Much to my chagrin, the lovely powdery iris and rose are diminished and I find the overall effect to be a bit screetchy and sharp.I swapped this off eventually realizing I couldn't wear it in comfort, it's just a tad irritating and synthetic, reminding me of dry cleaning chemicals, intermittently. Overall, the bottle and the beautifully shimmering pearlescent fragrance look more enticing than the original Essence and the shimmering effect on the skin, makes it something special for a Summer evening date, for example.

Some say love it is a river… there are 30 years between the song, The Rose sung by Bette Midler, and Narciso Rodriguez’s Rose, namely Essence. Both are so much more than a tribute to the wonderful flower. Whereas the song is about waiting for the right conditions for love to finally grow and blossom, NR has made a tribute to the rose, so amazing and marvelous, that it feels like a poem when I spray it on. Therefore it has a place in my top20. I love roses. I love the rose note in a lot of perfumes. But imho, NR has found the sublime expression. The sillage, the longevity and the balance is perfect. Even the bottle is beautiful. Alberto Morillas has done it again. So beautifully. 159/365

"On the sky shines a silver streak The evening turns dew into frost The pallor that snows from our cheeks Makes us beautiful like angels They should go down on their knees And pray that the moon remains veiled" These are the lines from the song by Subway to Sally or by Eisblume that I think of and wish to quote when I spray this fragrance. It is delicate. Vulnerable. Not a "make me strong" scent. A "with you I can be weak" scent. Like a white silk scarf with silver sparkling stars. Like a drop of dew on a rose petal. Like an ice crystal on a windowpane. Like pale pink lips and a bright complexion. Cuddling up in a light blanket. Gently melancholic. A beautiful melancholy. Thoughtful, not depressive. A delicate silver ribbon on my wrist, on which I rest my head while reminiscing about my vacation in Iceland. A scent like cool wind before I saw the Northern Lights. A scent like an eraser. Not by smell, but by effect. Erasing heavy thoughts to make room for new, fresh ideas. Lightness. Purity. Everything is good again. Nothing is too much. Nothing is too little. Everything is as it should be. And it remains so for a few hours. Without dragging others along forcefully. Rather quiet. But intense for me. "The day hastens out of the city It drinks its fill of shadows And reveals its true face The puddles already shimmer like ice" Sorry that I didn't go into the individual components. But the simple, yet worship-worthy quadriga really speaks for itself here. I wanted to write more about the emotions and what the scent evokes in me. Thank you for reading. THE END

Yes, here comes another non-binding purchase recommendation for clean bears: I just can't help it when my fellow species (this time: Lobelia) keeps providing me with new product samples. But I can promise you that this stuff fulfills absolutely all the dreams and cravings of a hungry clean bear-in premium quality.

I know, it may be that the title sounds a bit grandiose and kitschy. But this very image suddenly emerged after spraying Essence. I became aware of this fragrance thanks to the fantastic comment from Peanut. Clean is great and always fits. Many thanks also to Nuidette for the nice Soukdeal. For once, it was not a blind buy. I tested it months ago and found it desirable.

Essence is not: Sweet, fruity, opulent, enchanting, sensual, clumsy, decadent, oriental, floral, loud, overwhelming, synthetic, animalistic, aphrodisiac, balsamic, citrusy, earthy, mossy, bitter, woody, smoky, herbal, minty, narcotic, heavy, spicy, or fougère.

Wow, someone has quite a bit of mischief up their sleeve, right?! Silver, cool, and clear she comes, the young lady, innocent-fresh in her simple little dress and with a glance that seems to say she couldn't harm a fly.

Today, I came across a beautifully shaped chrome-colored bottle that immediately caught my attention. The bottle feels cool yet soft in the hand. Narciso essence. The Narciso EDT had already won me over, so I gladly take a spray. Mmm - the essence also conveys that cultivated quality that I liked so much about the EDT.

Lavanda Imperiale is a very high-quality, true-to-life lavender cologne, smelling very much like when you rub or crush fresh lavender between your finger and thumb to release their aromatic oils. Whether you'll like Lavanda Imperiale depends on how much you like lavender, of course, but also on how pure you like the note to be presented in perfumes. Lavanda Imperiale is a fresh, unadorned lavender, with nothing but a hit of green citrus to keep things clean. It is properly pungent, classic, and simple. Personally, I prefer my lavender to be plush and orientalized, as in Fourreau Noir, but for those who like it straight, this is a great option.

Lavender as a scent is certainly not to everyone's taste. Its use in scented sachets or potpourris gives it a somewhat old-fashioned vibe - and many recall their grandparents' bathroom, where a lavender water was always at hand. I don't have these associations, as neither my grandma - being the youngest of a whole line of children and my parents becoming parents late - used lavender water nor did we have scented sachets in our household. I only knew lavender as a plant - and I found its scent wonderful even as a small child. I shared my love for fragrant plants with my mother, and during long hikes (which I hated as a child!), she would pass the time with smelling and sometimes tasting everything that bloomed and grew. Herb gardens have always been and still are a fragrant paradise for me, and monastery gardens often house - sometimes old - rose varieties, and in combination, these are patches of earth from which it is very hard to move me away. My husband and sons can attest to this during our family outings, which, unfortunately, are becoming rarer as the boys grow up. Lavender is at the top of my list of plants I cannot pass by without brushing my fingers along to take in the scent, and additionally, this very special blue is one of my favorite colors in the garden. Thus, a visit to Provence when the lavender is in bloom is also high on my list of things I would still like to do in my life. Until that time comes, I console myself with lavender water and perfumes that prominently feature lavender. The purer the lavender scent and the closer it gets to the plant, the happier I generally am. And “Lavanda Imperiale” perfectly fulfills that longing of mine. Therefore, I find the description of the scent as floral-green to be completely wrong: It should clearly and without a doubt say floral-blue! The beginning is fresh-herb with a hint of citrus, but it does not stand alone; it is immediately enveloped in lavender, lavender, and more lavender. I am somewhat surprised that Ylang-Ylang and sage are listed in the pyramid. For my simple nose, I would not have detected either one. When I focus on it after reading, I feel that the lavender might be a touch sweeter than in nature - perhaps due to Ylang-Ylang, while the bitter-freshness of the sage remains completely hidden from me. Lavender itself has a certain kind of bitterness, and everything I smell in “Lavanda Imperiale” supports my imagination of how a fully bloomed, violet lavender field must smell in the hot summer sun. And since the lavender in my garden is freshly sprouting, I make another comparison - and I am astonished: the scent that clings to my skin when I gently rub the fresh shoots between my fingers is practically identical to the scent of “Lavanda Imperiale,” which has been residing on my wrist for some time now. I find myself pondering, as the description as “green” also has its justification - but that is merely a philosophical question for me. I have only worn “Lavanda Imperiale” as a sleep scent so far - and the bottle is already half empty. Now, as I delve into it through this commentary, I almost feel guilty, as this scent is truly lovingly crafted and deserves to be enjoyed during the day as well! It wouldn’t work for me at work, as I simply prefer more complex scents. But on a beautiful day like today, when I plan to do a bit of gardening in my mini-garden, it will accompany me in the sunshine. And I am absolutely sure that I will enjoy it very much!

The color is a soft rose, like the hues of the first flowers in the emerging spring - powdery delicate, and so is the scent. The first spray envelops me in a veil of delicate blossoms kissed by the sun's rays - my nostrils deeply inhale these first spring messengers - beautiful. It is warm, fresh - sweetish with a gentle seductive power that piques curiosity. Are those the freesias that smell so new and different, or is it the combination of all the flowers, topped off with the warm and bright orange blossom? In the drydown, after a good lasting hour, we are embraced by the familiar and beloved musk accord that ends with the bright creaminess of cedarwood. This new perfume lasts a very long time - like the length of an endless spring day that wants to lure us into the coming warm summer. It is definitely worth getting to know, prices as usual for this beautiful brand. Here is something different for me… fresh - gentle - creamy sensuality. And also somehow natural and very feminine. Petals that have become fine scent dust. Perhaps some may want to layer this scent with one of the other cubes.

I have been missing for about a year now, and I must admit: my taste has somehow changed during that time. While I used to always go for the “big hitters,” I now appreciate the more delicate fragrances as well. Yes, I even prefer to wear them, at least in everyday life. My love for the NR fragrances has also grown during this time. I like the concept behind the brand. The straightforwardness. Still, I must admit, there is one thing that has always been somewhat lacking for me. The freshness. Yes, scents like “Pure Musc” do smell very clean, but also powdery or creamy. I have always wished for a Narciso fragrance that includes the well-known NR DNA but smells brighter and more sparkling. This flanker offers me exactly that. It is indeed powdery, has a pleasant, light sweetness, and also feels wonderfully bright. Radiant, fresh. No velvety petals, no. Much more like delicate petals with morning dew. I don’t think any of the included flowers stand out in any way. At least not on my skin. They merely caress the fine powdery base. I find the scent really beautiful. A great fragrance for everyday use or work. Clean and powdery, but not boring.

I have had a kind of love-hate relationship with Narcisos for a long time. To reach the very beautiful drydown for me, I have to go through a few more or less intense hours, depending on the version of the perfume, during which the scent can be quite bothersome at times. In winter, for example, I can wear the For Her or the Poudrée best. Even with the milder Pure Musk, it's the same. Although I perceive the Narcisos as very good and high-quality, they are too much for me in the first 2-3 hours, even with careful spraying. That's why I have passed on the two fragrances I had used so far. After I heard about Narciso Cristal through a YouTube video, I became curious and tested it in the perfumery. For me, the right version! Finally, I can wear a fragrance from this great brand without reservation. The Cristal starts differently than other Narcisos, less intense, with freesia and orange blossom, fresh, clear, and slightly sweet. Very pleasant. After about an hour, it then smells to me like the Poudrée with rose, jasmine, cedar, and musk in a light, still powdery form. This is exactly the scent I love in the Poudrée the next day in my scarf. Close to the body but long-lasting with the typical Narciso - DNA. This perfume will probably be too weak for some. But I love it!

Since I am new here, I realize that I still don't have much knowledge when it comes to professional fragrance descriptions. I was looking for a powdery scent that is fresh but at the same time suitable for winter. It should have something warm and soft, so that I can really snuggle into it. Narciso Cristal fits surprisingly well into my desired direction. Normally, I prefer fresh scents; they must not be sweet at all. Narciso Cristal is actually my "sweetest" fragrance, and I find it absolutely wonderful right now in this very cold season. Perhaps because, alongside the powdery aspect, a fresh nuance remains throughout. In any case, I am currently very happy with this fragrance direction. For me, it's not a constant everyday scent, but a great change to explore a different direction that I couldn't imagine before.

Which fragrance was it?! Idôle? Miss Dior? Oh dear! About two hours earlier, I had tested my way through the medium-sized perfume store. Nothing had convinced me. But, as so often happens, a hint didn't land on the test strip but on my thumb. And there now blooms a delicate, powdered-sugar-dusted rose, mercilessly dragging me back into the perfume store and retracing my steps. What a relief when we find each other again! This love at second sight, the subtle echoes of an on/off relationship, has remained to this day. If I don’t wear the fragrance for a few days or even weeks, my enthusiasm is limited - to put it mildly. It starts off as if all the women’s fragrances from a department store perfume section had conspired with a few cans of hairspray under my bed to jump out together and spray me all over. Orange blossom and freesia swirl around me, it’s sweet and shrill, and a brief panic seizes me; I’m not 17 anymore, I can’t smell like this. But once this shock has passed, this beautiful rose blooms, softly nestled against jasmine. The freesias pull back, becoming more delicate and clean, just as I like them, and make room for a powdery, slightly elegant, never overpowering musk. How beautifully caressing, relatively sweet; I can’t suppress the smile. This is what good mood, warmth, and cheerfulness smell like, without drifting too much into the banal. By evening, the sweetness has faded, and now the fragrance smells most like Narciso Rodriguez, powdery, slightly woody, and creamy, and I am determined to wear this beautiful scent, this pure happiness in a bottle, again the next day. Until I crave something else. And then the fragrance sits on the shelf for another week until I reach for the bottle again - and then the dance begins anew, the fragrance molecules prepare for attack, I wonder what possessed me, and we finally laugh and embrace.

Narciso is, for me, one of the safest brands in the women's department. I have never tested a fragrance from this brand that I did not like, even among the men's releases. Admittedly, the releases are not very bold, extravagant, and they usually don't blow you away.

This fragrance smells to me like freshly showered and moisturized skin. It brings a lovely cleanliness through the freesia and soft musk, but I also find it somewhat boring. In my opinion, anyone looking for a scent in this direction would be better off with ‘Lacoste pour femme’. Still, it’s a nice fragrance for everyday spring wear.

....or Narciso can also mean clean scents. For those who find the Radiante too clean, synthetic, and are not fans of lily of the valley in a cotton bed, who are looking for a bit of the typical DNA but with less musk, this is a candidate. Yes, it is not bad, unobtrusive, clean floral, even a relative of Chloe (Freesia). Would I buy it...

I love Poudreé, but unfortunately not on my skin and generally on me, as it gives me headaches and makes me feel quite strange even though I love the scent! Then came the Eau de Parfum Cristal… I tested it at a Duty-Free shop in an airport during a trip and fell head over heels immediately. I usually prefer heavier fragrances, but this one is simply enchanting.

It was a blind buy and unfortunately, I am not convinced. Neither by the scent nor by the longevity. It smells very synthetic and like lily of the valley; I don't perceive the iconic musk DNA at all, not even in the drydown. For the rather piercing opening, the longevity is poor. nnThere are surely fans of this fragrance, but I am not one of them.

This has to be the essential Musk Perfume nothing in my honest opinon captures the note of musk then Narciso Rodriguez It's translucient to a point of a clear skin scent due to the presence of osmanthus sweetens the musk base bergamot adds the zest and tinges of amber dries the top 20 minutes later Narsiso turns woodsy with burnt edges vanilla gives it a warm delicious touch, There is no such thing thing is the basenote in Narciso the musk osmanthus abd vanilla plays it's self The Final verdict It's Chic Sexy Clean And Modern but advoids the fake facade of the candy dandy scent that has smered the perfume world.

I get a very distinct wintergreen, sweet ylang and vanilla mixture, up front. The sillage is initial bombastic for the first hour (about one meter off my arm) no one seems to mind on my journey through the department store. I think this scent really sums up modern high end perfumery. The notes are not over the top unique, but the synergy of the composition is certainly intriguing. It a bubble gum vibe in a hole in the wall Vampire's club. A weekend Goth Cosplay scent that is masterfully layered over the signature Narciso Egyptian musk base. The middle is smooth and ambery and rounded out by a lovely light smattering of spring like orange blossom Not as cloying as Hypnotic poison or Aqua Di Parma Mandorlo, but of the whole NR collection I find this to be the most gourmand. I think this was designed to be a 3 season signature scent with the ability to cross over from day-to-night affairs flawlessly and without reapplication. It is a valiant effort and certain expands the NR portfolio with a sort of soulfulness, for lack of a better term. It also transforms after about 4 hours to a soft-sillage, fresh not-at-all-sweet, woody floral musk base that works well for Spring and Summer nights. If I could get past the initial candy-like connotation, I would add it to my collection because the bottle is a striking metallic plum monolith that reflects light and darkness at different angles...very handsome, indeed. The longevity is excellent- I had to shower after 6 hours...because it's just not my thing, but if you are "lovin' it" - it will spend the whole night with you and not leave you unsatisfied, for sure!

I found myself really enjoying Narciso Rodriguez for Her Musc Intense, which surprised me seeing that I wasn't a huge fan of the original. The musk accord in this flanker seems smoother and more elegant. The original EDP smelt strongly of rose and patchouli, whereas this flanker has softer notes of ylang ylang, jasmine, white woods and musk. This new and approved blend is both delicate and alluring. The scent's projection is strong, but I wouldn't call it intense. I'm usually anosmic to musk, however in this particular composition the musk note is easy to smell and recognise. In my opinion, Narciso Rodriguez for Her Musc Intense smells more clean and feminine, than animalic or sexy. I actually prefer it this way. It tends to work with your skin, rather than against it. Despite its muskiness, Narciso Rodriguez for Her Musc Intense would make an excellent office scent, but I also wouldn't rule out wearing it on a date or to the clubs. I find that it smells best during the cooler months. I can imagine Narciso Rodriguez for Her Musc Intense being a hit with men, especially those that can get close enough to smell your neck and drown in your fragrance. It might smell clean and classy to some, but that's not to say that it doesn't lure the menfolk like bees to honey. I sincerely hope that this so-called limited edition remains on the department store shelves for at least another year. I'd be sad to see it go. Original review written: March 2013.

With this fragrance, I will find you and never lose you again, perhaps that already says enough. For Her Musc Collection is an extraordinary scent; I would recognize it among dozens, no, in a crowd of women immediately. Long before I got Narciso Rodriguez' for Him from the Musc Collection for myself, I got to know the scent "for Her Musc Collection" and fell in love with it. No wonder that Narciso is also one of my favorites. I was already in love with the woman, but the combination of woman and fragrance was unique. It starts warm, slightly powdery, becomes creamy with a lightly fruity, floral sweetness that continues to linger, enveloped in enchanting musk. For Her creates sensuality, and any man who doesn't think of love and eroticism in its presence probably doesn't know what it is. Yes, I am a man and not a woman, yet sometimes, when I went on motorcycle tours, I could beg her for three spritzes in the vial, and so she was always with me on the road, like an angel watching over me to ensure nothing happens. It is a tragedy that this fragrance no longer exists. Although the scent twin "For Her Pure Musc" reminds of what once was, if one wanted not just fragments of memories from a long-gone time but to bring back everything-the beautiful sensual moments, the adventures, the closeness, the love, and the desire-then that could only be done with For Her Musc Collection.

It is autumn. Blazing light ignites the leaves of the trees in a bonfire. My summer fragrances remind me of the Mediterranean and do not suit the cool air and the scent of foliage. The lovely lady in my corner perfumery is diligently working her way through a selection of scents: warm, powdery, autumnal it should be. With Goldea by Bulgari on my right and For Her L’absolu by Narciso Rodriguez on my left wrist, I move on. I have been fascinated by For Her in its various forms for years and always want to shout: Oh moment, linger a while! You are so beautiful. But For Her is not for me and simply refuses to stay. L’absolu is at least a bit more clingy. In the forum, I read about the Musc Collection and realize that this is the advanced version of L’absolu. I blindly order a 30 ml bottle. Days later, the package arrives. Opened, applied: cough syrup. Great disappointment, this will be a case for the souk. Saturday morning, the bottle is still there and we try again together. Mhmmm! This scent is a living being, a fairy that dances around me exuberantly. She is wrapped in beige silk, with a bit of gold glitter, the hem flashing deep red lace. Around her forehead, she has entwined flower vines. She loves to drive. There she pulls out her bouquet of flowers and waves it around joyfully. During the day, she sleeps nestled against my neck and only nudges me occasionally when she stretches languorously. In the evening, she is already waiting impatiently in my coat and calls out to me: Come quickly, out into the still warm evening air. Let’s walk a few meters along the river and stir up the leaves with our feet. On the opposite bank, the last rays of sunshine get caught in the glowing red treetops. For Her Musc Collection: a character scent, dazzling like the sun in autumn, delicious like crème brûlée, enchanting like tropical flowers at dusk, a being with its own mind and moods just like me.

Actually, I quite like the "Narciso Rodriguez for her" line. My husband probably does too, as last year a large bottle of the "Musc Collection" was under the Christmas tree. I was thrilled, but unlike him, my enthusiasm faded relatively quickly. In the top note, I perceive a synthetic, almost medicinal undertone that bothers me.

Help, my bottle is empty! This is one of the few fragrances that I actually want to keep in stock at all times. I feel like I can never go wrong with this scent. Sensual, pleasant, soft, cozy. From the very first molecule that hits me, everything remains the same and perfect. In summer, I find it a bit too sweet, as I don't notice any fresh notes here.

I have repurchased this fragrance time and again; it has a distinct addictive quality for me. A scent that hardly changes even after years - unless one's perception is disturbed by other essences - This fragrance can also be beautifully worn on skin that has been cared for with a light "soft cream." The creamy, cozy note is, in my opinion, highlighted more this way.

I can't say much about this unfortunately discontinued perfume companion... so I'll leave it at a few kind words. Whenever the temperatures drop, this bottle pulls my hand in its direction. It's certainly not due to the iridescent exterior; the fill level is hard to gauge, the bottle is somewhat bulky and tends to attract dust. However, the inner values speak for themselves.

For me, there are two types of fragrances: those that say "I am," and those that are "just pleasant." Recently, I only wore those from the second category. This made my surroundings happy, as they all seem to prefer Zen by Shiseido more than I do. I then tried a character fragrance again (Marni) and felt uncomfortable for half the day because I "wasn't that.

An elegant magnolia that is a bit powdery and soapy. I don't know why, but most of the things I have tried from Santa Maria Novella remind me of those old-fashioned milled white soaps. Not that that is a bad thing. This really resembles Chance Eau Tendre from Chanel, minus the quince and citrus. It starts off very strongly, but it mellows out with wear, although the evolution is pretty linear. Frankly, I prefer Eau Tendre, because it lasts more than Magnolia on my skin. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- O magnolie eleganta, un pic pudrata si sapunoasa. Nu stiu de ce, dar mie tot ce incerc de la marca aceasta imi aminteste de sapunurile parfumate de pe vremuri, nu intr-un mod rau neaparat. Pot sa simt asemanarea cu Eau Tendre de la Chanel, dar aici lipsesc gutuia si notele citrice. Incepe foarte puternic dar se aseaza si se linisteste cu timpul, desi evolueaza destul de linear. Interesant ca suvenir, dar nu stiu daca as spune ca isi merita pretul acela piperat.

I have no idea what Magnolia smells like, so to me this perfume smells like fresh green apples with fresh flowers. I find it very beautiful and not synthetic at all which is my usual complaint about fruity+floral fragrances. It is very simple, light and airy fragrance, perfect for summer days. I could see a person of any age wearing this. Also wouldn't mind smelling it on a man. Shower, white shirt, this fragrance and you are good to go.

I'm a man, and I love many of Narcriso Rodriguez's scents for women. Narciso Rodriguez For Her EDT (created by Francis Kurkdjian [!] AND Christine Nagel [!!] ) is a bonafide masterpiece, and many others in the women's collection are simultaneously well-crafted, unusual, sexy, and crowd-pleasing. I keep buying men's fragrances from NR, hoping to like one. With Bleu Noir Parfum I am, once again, disappointed. Bleu Noir Parfum is a let down because it SHOULD be where this house shines: A gender-bending, understated but sexy take on a well known perfume genre (in this case, the recent "iris for men" trend). It fails to achieve any of that, and is instead mediocre, very butch, very sweet, and very linear. Other notes: - Has very little to do with the original Bleu Noir (which I liked but found too masculine for myself) - Contrary to hype, it is not even faintly reminiscent of Dior Homme Intense - Performance is good, as expected from NR - Anyone else annoyed that across designer perfumery, "parfum" has no technical meaning? There is no noticeable difference in quality, projection, or longevity between the various Bleu Noirs (EDT, EDP, Extreme(?), and Parfum.) It would be nice if these words actually referred to concentration. - To the marketers at Narciso/ Shiseido: We've had enough Bleu Noir flankers. The world is ready for a new, daring Narciso Rodriguez for Men.

This is a joint review of the following four Narciso Rodriguez fragrances: For Him Bleu Noir EdT For Him Bleu Noir EdT Extreme For Him Bleu Noir EdP For Him Bleu Noir Parfum Testing these four was a valuable experiment for me. I determined two things: 1. I don't like strong cardamom scents 2. I don't care for very powdery fragrances. Since three of these four fragrances have these two characteristics in varying degrees, three were rated lower while a fourth was rated better. Now, let's get into the specifics of all four..... For Him Bleu Noir EdT was the most cardamom forward of the four fragrances but also fairly low in the powdery attribute. The strong cardamom, which was evident from the start, really caused me to immediately dislike it. For Him Bleu Noir EdT Extreme did not have cardamom and wasn't powdery. Surprisingly, as a flanker, it went off in a totally different direction. It is a nice freshie. I'd describe the scent as fresh, woody and slightly green. Pleasant to wear but not an outstanding fragrance that would induce me to buy a full bottle. For Him Bleu Noir EdP is an in-between fragrance. The cardamom note, although still quite noticeable, was toned down compared to the EdT but the powdery attribute was dialed up. The scent clearly sits between the EdT and the Parfum. Because of the still strong cardamom, I didn't care for it. For Him Bleu Noir Parfum dials the cardamom down even more than the EdP but significantly dials up the powdery attribute. I did not care for the strong powdery aspect. If I had to choose one, it would be the Extreme which I certainly wouldn't mind wearing. Regarding performance, all four were rather moderate in the projection department after the first hour. Longevity was a mixed bag. The EdT and EdP had very good longevity even though they hung close to the skin. They were still noticeable after 12 hours. The Parfum dropped out after about 8 hours while the Extreme has the worst performance. It was gone in about 6 hours. My recommendations would be as follows. If you're looking for a strong cardamom fragrance, definitely go with the EdT. If you want a very powdery fragrance, go with the Parfum. If you'd like something more in between, go with the EdP. If you want a freshie, there are a lot better options than the Extreme.

Nice iris scent, classy clean vibe, perfect for the office or restaurant, but still playful with some sweetness. I really think this one's underrated, especially the longevity and sillage, for me it's definitely better than the ratings are. I easily get 4-6 hours longevity at least, with good sillage. It's not a powerhouse, but definitely reasonable in my opinion.

The Narciso Rodriguez For Him line is already really good and highly appreciated by me. The endless women's line For Her is also among the best in the designer sector for me. The sub-line For Him Bleu Noir already includes 4 pieces, of which I own 3. Only the EdT is still missing. The other 3 live up to their name Bleu to some extent: fresh, lightly blue, shower gel-like, but in an elegant way. This one, however, stands out quite clearly from the rest. It could also have its own name and bottle, but often the product is marketed with a well-known name and design. However, they all share the note of blue Atlas cedar, probably also the reason for the bleu name. Without a doubt, this is a fragrance in the style of Valentino Uomo (Intense) and its counterparts. Powdery, leathery, sweet. Nevertheless, I must say that I particularly enjoy wearing this, even just in between. Simply a crowd-pleaser that is easy to like and works great in everyday life and is never "over the top." This fragrance is available in 50 and 100ml. It's not cheap, but it's in the "normal" designer range. You can get 50ml for around 50 euros, and the 100ml usually for around 80 euros. Price-wise, this is fair, as I find this fragrance quite high-quality. Those looking for a pure evening scent should rather reach for Valentino, as that one projects better. I find all the bottles really beautiful, but they are rather secondary for me. When you spray this fragrance, you are immediately greeted by that familiar sweet-powdery note that you have smelled so many times before. Anyone looking for something completely new will likely be disappointed here. If you already have one of these fragrances in your collection, you don't necessarily need this one. However, I find it great for everyday wear. Like a light version. Sillage toned down, with a bit of freshness added. Even though the sillage is not as good as its relatives: it remains in a very, very pleasant range. It doesn't bother, and if someone comes close to you, it is definitely noticed. Sometimes just the right thing. The iris and leather are very present from the start. However, the leather is rather pleasantly in the background throughout, which I really like. The floral-powdery-fresh iris is simply convincing and comes across as extremely uncomplicated here. Cardamom is also present, but nicely mild. A slight freshness is also in the mix. The base and the dry-down then come across very softly: a gentle woody base with sweet and leathery accents. Cedarwood and creamy-sweet tonka fade out very sensually. Overall, a great creation that ranks very high for me in this fragrance type. Due to its unobtrusive aura, you can wear this fragrance almost all the time, and it is perfect for people who do not want to forgo sweet scents in everyday life. I enjoy wearing this fragrance even just in between, as you can easily overspray it and it has a pleasant performance. The longevity is okay, but for this type of fragrance, there could have been more. Overall, for me, a worthwhile alternative, especially for everyday use. Where the others are rather too much, this one convinces with a sympathetic restraint without really being too weak. For me, a great release.

A bit like the old Lanvin "Arpege Pour Homme" but even more delicate and modern, this sensational Narciso Rodriguez comes across. Is it still a "Bleu Noir"? Not really. On the other hand, the line didn't have the absolute and consistent scent DNA for me - but the Narciso Rodriguez brand certainly does. And "Bleu Noir Parfum" fits perfectly and is absolutely a new highlight! "Bleu Noir Parfum" is an airy iris masterpiece. Light blue to pink. Very delicate, very fine, very unisex. With a certain NR muskiness casually. This may not suit or please everyone overall. But I consider it one of the best designer fragrances that have emerged this decade so far. Especially since Dior is struggling so much. "Bleu Noir Parfum" makes even its already good "brother fragrances" look outdated, but fundamentally it is a completely different playing field and its own thing. Lipsticky, sweet, royally floral. With beige leather accents and a certain lightness of being. All year round. Simply delicious, simply stylish. The opposite of macho and masculine, rather androgynous. And yet I can wear it very well, even though I look zero androgynous. It complements itself. This is how you create fragrances that are in tune with the times. This is how Narciso Rodriguez surpasses himself. Not the reinvention of the male iris - but the ideal rounding. Bottle: strong, heavy, beautiful, minimalist Sillage: always perfectly balanced between soft and strong Longevity: 7-8 hours - rather typical scent and house than typically "parfum" Conclusion: a direct iris classic... Powdery, not sloppy at all, absolutely brilliant. The best "Bleu Noir" - even if it’s no longer aquatic... Phenomenal and delicate. Could also be YSL in its best phase. Makes the nostrils flutter and the soul indulge.

I purchased the perfume at my local perfumery. I find the scent heavenly. But unfortunately, the following happened: I applied my usual six sprays, got into my car, drove off, and picked up a friend. She got into the car and said after 5 minutes: "Wow, you're not wearing any perfume today?" The problem is: my car is a "cozy" two-seater.

Very good understated scent that never feels overdone, although a little more sillage would do it good! As for the fragrance itself, it is fresh, starts fruity with a sharp sweetness, and is truly very multifaceted and versatile from the first spray to the drydown, which sets in after 3-4 hours.

Calm, elegant scent that doesn't smell very synthetic, it really worked on my skin. Good start and in the end, it becomes somewhat generic. Citrus and iris are well balanced (I was excited at first). A blend of the DNA of the Extreme and the original. Longevity 6-7 hours (5 sprays) 1h30 projection.

I had, to be honest, high expectations and great anticipation when I first tested the new Bleu Noir perfume. -Because in my optimistic imagination, I envisioned a heroic autumn king… And the test gave me - No, (unfortunately) no euphoria. No, (thankfully) no resignation. But: SURPRISE! And indeed a very surprising surprise… ‘You know this one, don’t you?!

... adults with its dark side. With this perfume, I imagine being out with my girlfriend or friends while dining, at a bar, or in a club. Upon applying this dark woody scent, you are first greeted with a spicy freshness accompanied by a green note from the cardamom, cypress, and citrus fruits. The iris and musk give it a slightly creamy powdery quality.

This flanker is probably my favorite of the line and I understand why it’s not being so well received by Narciso’s musk lovers. This is an osmanthus perfume with fruity, floral and leathery facets on an ambery vanillic musky base. Osmanthus is what it makes it a for her flanker, but the backbone of the perfume would be more for Tom Ford or, more precisely, Ella K Lettre de Pushkar lovers. In my YouTube video you will find more details about the comparison of the perfumes and the aesthetics.

Yes, that was quite a surprise A rather atypical Rodriguez. NR fragrances have a high recognition value. Unfortunately, on my popularity scale, it has slipped way down, yet I had to test the latest version. NR has created a nice fresh floral scent here, which is also somewhat of a run-of-the-mill fragrance and could simultaneously be a drugstore scent. It’s not bad, as it could be worn well in summer, but the typical NR character is simply gone. White flowers with peach, and the Calabrian bergamot doesn’t help either. If you want to smell like this, save your money and buy two fragrances from Bruno B.

...But this NR is indeed an Eau de Parfum intense. I am still quite a novice when it comes to perfume, and my nose needs more training, but I will attempt to describe the scent as I perceived it. Right after spraying, the scent almost overwhelmed me. Not only because of its intensity, but also because it was so different from what I had expected. In the first short hour, I wasn't sure if it smelled more like a unisex fragrance or a purely masculine scent. Yes, the peach comes through well, but the rest was really an acquired taste for me. Later on, I liked it much better. I love associations, and this scent gives me vibes of the late 60s/early 70s - at least as they are portrayed in film (I was born much later). I don't smell much fruit and flowers here, but rather a powdery quality and somehow also a strong bitter note with a slight sweet touch. All in all, this fragrance experience impressed me greatly, and I enjoy smelling this scent because I find it so interesting. However, I am looking for something different for myself; this scent doesn't suit me that well.

As a big fan of the NR fragrances, especially the For Her line, I own 6 of these scents and am building a collection - the trend is thus increasing. 3 of the Musk For Her fragrances, including "For Her Pure Musc (Eau de Parfum) | Narciso Rodriguez," the classic: "For Her (Eau de Toilette) | Narciso Rodriguez," and the beautiful "For Her Musc Noir Rose | Narciso Rodriguez," are essential for my everyday life and count among my favorites and signature scents, which I also love to layer. I also really like the For Her Musc Nude from 2024; I adore the classic musk of the For Her line. The new 2025 release, NR for her - eau de Parfum intense, almost made it into my collection; fortunately, when I repurchased one of my other favorites from the brand, "Narciso (Eau de Parfum Poudrée) | Narciso Rodriguez," I received a 5ml maxi sample and a 0.6ml sample, allowing me to test the scent. The new Intense differs somewhat from the For Her classics; it is more floral and fruity, and the legendary musk DNA of For Her takes a backseat in this fragrance. At first, a fruity note of peach is noticeable, which quickly blends with dominant floral notes. The floral notes are perceptible throughout the entire scent, and the musk here is somewhat different from the other For Her fragrances, giving the floral scent a warm and creamy quality, along with a sweetness likely coming from the vanilla notes. The fragrance also has a somewhat synthetic quality to it. Overall, it is an average perfume for me that can be worn daily. It is an all-rounder that could fit almost any occasion. Unfortunately, the For Her Intense is nothing special for me or something I feel I must have in my collection; it’s a bit too boring and average - I’ve smelled similar scents before, and it doesn’t blow me away. But that’s just my opinion, and many love and seek out average crowd-pleasers. I also own and enjoy all-rounders, but this one is not for me. I don’t really get Baccarat Rouge 540 Eau de Parfum vibes from this either. The longevity is present, and it is indeed intense.

Once again, something about this great, now huge Narciso Rodriguez For Her line. The flagship fragrances of this line are of course the two scents For Her Eau de Toilette and For Her Pure Musc Eau de Parfum . These are likely the bestsellers of this line. However, there are many more that deserve a bit more attention. With a score of 6.6, here’s a fragrance that could be considered poorly rated: the Eau de Parfum Intense, which was freshly released this year. Of course, with designer releases, every year flankers of bestsellers are sold. Whether it fits into this line or not, it’s all about marketing. I find this one, in contrast to the majority, really good as it adds great fruity notes to this clean DNA. Floral notes also make it easily a Fruity-Floral, but it is balanced in my eyes. It should be clear to everyone that it goes in a slightly different direction than the others in this line with the peach note. I like peach, especially in women’s fragrances. Thus, I like this EdP Intense. Perfumer Sonia Constant has created some great bestsellers, including some from this Narciso line (like the Pure Musc). She certainly has talent. This fragrance seems to divide people a bit. Available in 30, 50, and 100ml, the price is relatively reasonable. Like most of the releases, you can get these fragrances for a relatively normal designer price. The red bottle is quite beautiful and fits well with this sensual peach. Otherwise, everything is as usual with this line. In terms of scent, this flanker goes in an individual direction. Of course, some accents from previous releases are present, but with a completely new twist thanks to this fruity peach note. The peach note is not so fruity-fresh, but rather warm and sensual. Thus, I see this more as a transitional scent for spring and autumn rather than for really warm temperatures. This sweet peach smells truly attractive and has something totally sensual and appealing. I cannot confirm that it goes too much in the gummy bear direction; however, this peach note is also not too authentic. Great musk notes follow, which are actually characteristic of this line. These notes have a clean, fluffy, and slightly powdery character. Floral notes also come into play, making this creation very feminine and fitting wonderfully with this musk note. I specifically perceive white flowers. In the base, warm notes of vanilla, amber, and musk emerge. A great dry down from these sensual notes provides a wonderful finish, and I find this creation very harmonious. A very modern release with peach, making it super wearable for young ladies but also for those of more advanced age. The scent is theoretically suitable for everyday wear, but even better for evening wear. It is not too intrusive, but it does stand out. Performance is really good and lives up to the Intense name. You easily get 8-10 hours of longevity, and the projection of the fragrance is also relatively good. Overall, a great feminine and sensual flanker that you can try out if you like notes like peach. This fruity note makes this DNA very lively and should also appeal to the masses. One should not be deterred by the poor ratings, as fruity-sweet women’s designers are often somewhat penalized.

... on the terrace. The garden is blooming and lush. On the glass table sits a bowl of peaches and citrus fruits, next to it a bowl of sugar. The friend comes with coffee and hot peaches drizzled with vanilla sauce. It tastes wonderfully fruity, creamy, and sweet. When applying this fragrance, the first thing that hits your nose is a fruity sweet scent.

Oh you beautiful beautiful scent. You start with this impressive peach note, then the floral and powdery notes join in. You really smell lovely! But I know you?! A mix of Pure Woman Eau de Parfum with a bit of Sì Eau de Parfum . Nevertheless, I really like you. But... why on earth does this beautiful scent last only until noon?

I can't really understand the negative review of this fragrance. But tastes are known to differ. I really like the scent because it is totally uncomplicated. It works in all seasons, is suitable for any occasion, and doesn't come off as intrusive. The opening is fruity - almost juicy - with peach. However, it quickly becomes softer due to the musk and vanilla.

Tested and allowed to move in. It's an all-round talent. I can't really smell the individual notes, but I still like it. Especially the drydown on clothing appeals to me. Longevity on the skin could be better, but it's still detectable on clothing two days later. I've already received several compliments for it. I will definitely buy it again.

I actually used 2 bottles of this perfume this summer. Personally, I really like this scent. It smells like a juicy peach. After the first sniff, I also suspected cherry, but that is actually not the case. I think the longevity could be better! That's probably why I've already used 2 bottles, as I tend to use a few more sprays than with other perfumes.

Wow! This is a zesty perky fresh light tonic in the style of "4711" and other light but persistent citrusy colognes. Perfect for a man or a woman in the hottest most humid heat of the Summer, this one will provide that fresh clean feeling without the soapy note. This fragrance peaks after about 20 minutes and opens into a confident feel-good scent kind of like an icy Italian Soda in the midday sun, not particularly sweet but sunny art and invigorating describe it best. A wonderful daytime office scent, it wears fairly close to the skin but will leave those around you with a positive impression of your clean crisp aroma. It's definitely going on my FB list for unique daytime, yet professional wear.

Research on various broom species initially confused me rather than enlightened me. Since I have never consciously seen, let alone smelled, broom here in the Alpine foothills, my impression of this shrub is limited to yellow-flowering landscapes that passed by me during various train journeys. I recall the Eifel, the Rhine Valley, but also the Swabian Jura. If Ginestra from the house of Santa Maria Novella is supposed to capture the typical scent of the plant, then it is for me a pleasantly unsweet floral fragrance. "Herb" would be too drastic, but nothing about the perfume reminds me of the usual floral scents that currently shower us with orange blossom, tuberose, jasmine, and similar floral messengers. No citrus notes are employed to first promise us a floral-fresh scent with a pleasing top note, only to then reveal a base dominated by musk, amber, or vanilla after a floral intermezzo. The mood of Ginestra is consistently friendly; perhaps there is also some heliotrope involved. At no point does it awaken a desire for exotic travel to the Caribbean or even the South Seas. The scent also has no spectacular progression. This may sound boring, but for me, it is not a flaw. Not every fragrance needs to tell me a story; sometimes I simply enjoy the mood of a landscape, the feeling of having arrived, or perceiving an imaginary smile. This is certainly the case with Ginestra for me, and with surprisingly long-lasting wear. A side note about Santa Maria Novella: The brand has long maintained an elitist image characterized by the fact that the fragrances were only available in the famous, venerable store in Florence and in selected perfumeries, at the point of sale and not online. I was quite surprised that at least in Munich a flagship store was opened, and I was even more astonished to find that one can now order directly online through the company's website. Unfortunately, there are neither decants nor discovery sets available for purchase, but perhaps that will change as well. I am certainly sure that one or two fragrances will find their way into my collection.

I'm not a big fan of the original For Her EDT (black bottle). There's something about it that is just too overwhelming and loud to my nose, that turns dirty and sweaty on my skin, that I just can't deal with. It's funny because I often read others describe it as an inoffensive, clean musk for every day, which couldn't be further from my perception. Even funnier is that other fragrances with a similar musk note are a mixed bag for me and the line between like and dislike is extremely fine. So, I wasn't particularly interest in trying this flanker, but I got a free sample. And... it's fine! Pleasant even! You can definitely smell the For Her DNA here. Forever has the same sultry musk note. The overall impression is different to me though. Lighter, fluffier, more floral, even a bit sparkly. The dominant orange blossom of the EDT is gone, the flowers in this are creamier and smoother. I like the tropical sweetness of the frangipani and the apricot-like tone of the osmanthus, and I also smell a phantom citrus note that makes everything fresher. These are all nice additions. It's still not a scent I'd want to have on me all day, but I would enjoy it on someone else in passing. I'm just wondering if it was really necessary to release this in 2023. There are not only countless flankers in the Narciso Rodriguez lineup, but also hundreds of similar fragrances by other brands. For Her Forever doesn't feel like a big revelation, it's more like "Yeah, whatever, another take on this scent profile, groundbreaking". I would recommend it to someone in search of a softer version of For Her, but if you're not specifically looking for that, you won't miss much if you skip this.

After all the hype given to this fragrance it has been my most anticipated perfume ever, and also my biggest disappointment. It just smells like a much lighter version of the original For Her edt. Where are all the added florals? I certainly couldn't find them here. Reading that note profile I was certain this would be a beautiful tropical floral fragrance, which was a genre missing in the Narciso lineup. I was counting the days when it would be available in the US, but it certainly wasn't worth the wait. How did Sonia Constant manage to make it smell almost the same as For Her edt when she used a somewhat different note profile? I find that very strange. Not that this is bad fragrance by any means, and is actually quite pretty, but neither is it different enough from For Her edt for me to get a bottle.

I have read and watched several reviews and have the feeling that this fragrance is not received very well by most people or leaves them indifferent because it is quite similar to the EdT. I understand where this impression comes from, but hold on a second: NR For Her Forever just bursts with floral elegance, the tuberose and frangipani underscore this beautiful musk bouquet in the background, and I can still smell the wonderfully creamy, soft drydown days later on my scarf. In my opinion, the EdT cannot compete with the sweetness here; I find it stiffer, harder, and cooler. Forever is floral, soft, sweet, and absolutely suitable for everyday wear. I especially see it in spring and summer and can hardly wait to call the 100 ml my own soon. Conclusion: for me, this is the most beautiful Narciso flanker ever created. A masterpiece for the 20th anniversary.

Maybe I'm becoming more mellow with age, or I'm just expanding my personality again. The fact is, I suddenly find a Narciso appealing. Maybe even really appealing. I already liked Musc Noir Rose, even though it was a nostalgic memory that built the bridge for me. But because I liked it, I was tempted to spray For Her Forever on myself. And I'm impressed. I can also smell the similarity to the other two For Her fragrances, the EdP and the EdT, which has already been mentioned several times here. And yes, I would initially confirm that the scent seems weaker, less intense. BUT that is precisely what makes it strong for me. Both the EdP and EdT of For Her are hardly bearable for me and candidates for headaches. I find them intrusive, artificial, and often overly dosed. For Her Forever is different. The lady comes around the corner much more relaxed, effortlessly exuding a weightless lightness that is underlined by soft musk. She doesn't overpower the wearer but adapts, is present, yet doesn't need to push herself to the forefront. The white flowers complement each other excellently, especially the jasmine, which I find beautiful, and I can also distinctly smell the gardenia. The scent is not sweet but fresh and light. I need to test the longevity and sillage more closely, but so far, I'm satisfied with it. It doesn't always have to be loud.

The women's and men's fragrance lines from Narciso Rodriguez have accompanied me for many years now. Even though the most formative scents from Narciso are no longer available, I can recall their scent from memory with my eyes closed, and with those memories come the associated feelings. Ultimately, this is how we all feel about our fragrances and memories, right? So, I don’t have to think long about what I associate with the “Narciso For Her” line. There was a time when my then-girlfriend would ritualistically spray “For Her Musc Collection” on my scarf before my motorcycle tours, so that I would return to her safely. Yes, I exclusively associate this perfume with that time and that woman. It remains the best from Narciso. But now there is also “For Her Forever”. Undoubtedly, Narciso has somewhat overdone it with the number of variations of this scent, and sometimes the results have not been so impressive. In the end, I’m not surprised, because connecting to the past while simultaneously creating something new is difficult. Somehow, Sonia Constant has managed to do just that with this mysterious, creamy musk carried by sweet floral white blossoms. Narciso truly means emotions for me again in 2023, and since the scent has only been on the market since this year, this review can only relate to quite current emotions, aside from the scent itself. There was briefly the question of whether it would be better to approach it more objectively and soberly. Well, I tried - and deleted everything. In the end, I have no choice but to describe this scent with all the emotions, with everything that comes to mind and all the thoughts associated with it. Otherwise, this review would just be a foolish attempt at repression and wouldn’t even begin to represent what one would call the whole truth. And what is the whole truth now? The truth is, For Her Forever represents happy moments when you feel the “we”, when with every meter and every minute spent together, you feel that intense connection, when you can express words and feelings without speaking, when you can say everything with just touches and glances. Forever means longing, sensuality, eroticism, passion, and - above all else - an intensely felt love for that person, who is ultimately what this is all about. A love that makes me feel happiness like a lovesick teenager in one moment and, in the next moment, makes me realize how serious everything really is - namely, that you can’t and don’t want to imagine a future without all of this and that person (damn it) forever. Yet the future seems anything but certain right now. Clarity and determination repeatedly swap sides with uncertainty, doubt, and heartache. The current reality blocks much of what was recently counted among the happiest moments in life. And where does all of this go now? Forever preserved in a bottle? No, amidst this reality, there is still this scent, representing everything that was recently, what is currently, and what will be. Can you smell it, can you feel it? It fights with you and for you for your future. It shows you that there can be another reality besides the current one. It shows you that behind difficult decisions, which would be associated with losses and great efforts, a beautiful future still awaits. Yes, it’s not easy right now, but I won’t give up that easily. After all, it’s currently called “For her forever”. And besides, a man once wrote: “In the end, everything will be okay, and if it’s not okay, it’s not the end yet!”

Narciso For her edt was my all-day fragrance for years in my early 20s. Sexy, mysterious, creamy, and personally appealing to me. Now it’s here, his little brother! Makes the big one seem fussy. Forever is more floral, a bit tamer, but otherwise I don’t perceive any significant difference. Those who don’t like for her edt will find no joy in Forever either.

I remember when I first saw the perfume among new releases, pure anticipation. I could hardly wait to smell the scent, imagining how powdery and creamy it would be. I am a big fan of the "for her" line. I didn't really want to order it blind, I was torn back and forth. I waited a few weeks, and on the day of the release, I went to the perfume store to finally test it.

For Her Forever - an anniversary edition of the infamous Narciso Rodriguez For Her - and rightly so. Unlike the For Her EdT, this one features a much softer, less scratchy opening that transitions into a wonderfully creamy dry-down, without losing the characteristic For Her DNA. As a fragrance, it is particularly suitable as a signature scent for everyday wear.

From the few fragrances I have tried from Santa Maria Novella, I was not necessarily impressed. Nevertheless, I have always found the house to be highly likable, because unlike pseudo-historical brands like Creed, Carthusia, Rancé, etc., they do not endlessly dwell on a story that demands authenticity, but rather casually mention that the products are made in a state-of-the-art laboratory with modern materials like traditional oils and not with alchemical tinctures based on original medieval recipes (Nostalgia refers to old race cars and not the Florence of the Medici). Although they do have a long history to look back on. The anniversary fragrance Ottone is also a very traditional scent, which - similar to many Villoresi classics - creates a beautiful Mediterranean arc from the citrus fruits, herbs, and spices of Italy to the balsamic resins of the (literally) Near East. This style can be found in many Italian and Spanish eaux de toilette and is certainly part of the collective memory of male "grooming culture" in these regions, just as citrus-lavender-floral-powder-wood is for the English (or at least it used to be). The quality of the raw materials is excellent and the composition is skillfully done. The citrus-floral opening has no chance against the quickly spreading herbal notes, but it continues to resonate. The oregano does not smell overwhelmingly like pizza seasoning, but rather like a robust bundle of fresh herbs that soon blends seamlessly into the clove and soft cinnamon. The incense does not stand out for me, nor do we have to deal with a overpoweringly dry "cedar-e-super" note and intrusive santalol. Instead, the fragrance glides thoughtfully on my skin into a soft balsamic base that, whether it is or not, smells harmoniously and unobtrusively of natural oils. As Apicius already writes, solid and conservative - this is not about surprises and innovations, but about honoring classic perfume tradition. This is achieved brilliantly and can be worn with great enjoyment.

Farmaceutica di Santa Maria Novella makes itself and its products quite rare. You can't order anything online; you would have to make the effort to go to Florence yourself. At least in Germany, there seems to be no official point of sale. At least they have finally put some content behind their web address - it must be magnificent, museum-like spaces! As a visitor to Florence with an interest in fine fragrances, one must definitely go there. With the men's fragrance Ottone and its female counterpart Porcellana, SMN is now celebrating its 400th anniversary. They have released a few bottles into the big wide world, and so I was able to test Ottone in a Berlin department store. A look at the range tells me that they must all be old, traditional scents - the names suggest it. And Ottone is above all one thing: a classic-conservative Italian men's perfume. With Ottone, SMN appeals to a clientele that appreciates tradition without any ambition for fragrance experiments. After a somewhat citrusy top note, we have a subtly spicy scent before us. The restrained spice is embedded in a dark, warm, only slightly sweet and ambered environment. I perceive similarities in style to spicy men's fragrances, such as those known from Halston - however, the spice in Ottone does not stand out as much. After about two hours, the spice fades, along with a good part of the ambratic warmth. The scent now becomes slimmer, dry, and smoky; incense becomes dominant. At this stage, Ottone largely corresponds to the incense-heavy perfumes L'Homme Sage by Divine and Pontevecchio by Nobile 1942. A long drydown follows over several hours, during which nothing else happens. So, it’s all quite alright, solid quality indeed - but you really don't need to lay down for this perfume! I am somewhat bothered by the break between the warm-spicy heart note and the smoky drydown. Distinct fragrance developments can be interesting, but the overall impression must remain coherent. Here, however, the scent changes its character quite abruptly. Personally, I prefer the style of the base note over the heart note, but I would rather reach for Pontevecchio or L'Homme Sage, which fully embrace this smoky direction. In the splendid sales rooms of SMN, furnished with ornate furniture, Ottone will probably sell like hotcakes. The shopping experience seems to be simply part of the product, and so it fits. But as a pure fragrance, Ottone does not completely convince me.

The vetiver of the kind of Guerlain, Carvin, Givenchy or R&G is nowhere to be found. What you will smell is a concoction of aromatic chemicals claiming to smell like the notes in the pyramid - to my nose, an impossible task. Well, maybe giving it a full wear would change my opinion, but as far as I could get, I could not give it many chances, I scrubbed it as soon as possible.

This perfume recently arrived in Australia, and I was very excited to try it. I love vetiver notes in perfume more than anything else, and this had me intrigued. So, the day it came out, I went over to the department store near my office, sprayed a bit on my wrist, and gave it a fair go. At first, I was a bit disappointed, but as I went back to it, my disappointment turned to surprise. This was a very surprising one for me! The first thing I noticed is that this is not a vetiver perfume. Not even close. There is a vetiver note hanging around in there, but it's not the star of the show by any means. What I did get, however, was a minty geranium, some vegetal musks, and a prominent, seaweed-like aquatic note. Minty geranium is nothing new in men's perfumery, sure, but I love the smell of geranium anyway, so it's always welcome. The musks give it some density, not too much but enough to keep the scent going, and the aquatic note is surprisingly savoury, which I really liked. This is weird. Very weird, and very bold. The brand and the manufacturer could easily have produced something boring for this name, but they didn't. This is unapologetically green and I love it. I'm so glad that they've chosen to do something weird with this. Green perfumes are here! I like this a lot, but I'm unsure if I'd buy a bottle. I have other perfumes that I love that I would see myself wearing in the same situations that I would wear this. Maybe I will, just because it's weird.

I wanted something fresh for my summer vacation for everyday use. I'm bored with this citrus fresh fragrances what's why I searched for something new and landed here. I wasn't sure at first because it sounded unique and weird when I read the notes. I have to say its unique pleasant fresh can be worn all the year for casual or office purposes. a very nice all arounder. If you don't like citrus fresh fragrances try this one and you will be positive surprised. However the fragrance is a bit unique so I would not recommend to blind buy it. If you have any question let me know and I will try to help you ^^.

Sample enough fragrances and read/watch enough reviews, and you'll get used to the subjectivity of olfactory appeal. A fragrance that somebody loathes, somebody else will love. A fragrance someone washes off right away will be someone else's addiction. I'm one of those guys for Vetiver Musc. This is just what I needed. As others have pointed out, if you're looking into this scent for a vetiver-forward experience like that of Guerlain or Lalique or Tom Ford, you're setting yourself up for disappointment. I feel that Vetiver Musc is a pretty linear scent. It might take a few minutes for the vetiver and spices to come in, but what you smell is pretty much what you're going to get all the way through. While it might not have a shifting progression, it does have layers, like ogres and onions. This isn't top/middle/base notes, exactly; I kinda visualize it as three curtains, each hanging behind the one before. The first curtain is occupied by musk and geranium. This is, first and foremost, a creamy, soothing, cooling fragrance. It is clean. It is calming. As someone who tends to be high-strung and eager to relax, this is exactly what I need. It chills me out in a way that few fragrances do, and the only one that comes close off the top of my head is A Balm of Calm by Penhaligon's. If you don't get along with this 'curtain', you're unlikely to enjoy Vetiver Musc. If the fragrance were nothing more than this, it would be boring, but fortunately, there are two more curtains. Hanging behind that first curtain, the second is where the vetiver comes in, with the cypress and nutmeg. The cardamom's probably in there, too, but my nose isn't so particular to that scent to identify it. The combination gives this rich, dark green background to the soft musky and floral first layer. It's not very woodsy or earthy, just green with the spices giving a little texture. It's masculine for the man who doesn't need to prove it. Further down, the last curtain is a very subtle aquatic current. It's not strongly seaweed-marine-y or anything, and I'm not sure if the algae note is carrying this all on its own or not. But there is just something about it that's ever-so-quietly aquatic. This, combined with the first curtain, makes me put Vetiver Musc in the extended family of Zaharoff Signature Seraphim Red, which is a bolder, more expensive, more floral musky-aquatic, still calming but also a very happy summer scent. I understand that what I find so revitalizing and soothing in Vetiver Musc may be a boring letdown for others, but this showed me a kind of scent I didn't know I wanted. I'm definitely keeping my eyes (and nose) out for variations on this theme. In the meantime, it's great to have a signature scent available at very reasonable prices.

Calm, soft and timid in the beginning. Creates a beautiful aroma around you for 30 minutes then ”poff” it vanishes. Nowhere to be smelled again. Smells great but its achilles heel is that it dont last. It reminds me of a forest infront of a beach, just after the rain. nnHonestly one of the best smells i’ve smelled. It hurts me that I can’t even smell it at all after an hour. Hoping for some kind of reformulation so it atleast gets 4-6 hours.

I would say Narciso Rodriguez is my favorite go-to brand in the designer men's fragrance sector. I can say this with quite a bit of conviction. Their transparent-elegant musk DNA is simply unique and exactly my style. I am very glad to have some of their old treasures displayed. Together with Dior Homme's Iris as the only competition at this level.

... and a gentleman in a stylishly modern tailored suit with a discreet tie enters the room. He exudes a gentle fragrance that complements his charm and charisma. He is so discreet that he stands out again, and people turn to look at him as he crosses the room.

....into a herbal spice world. For at first, it becomes wonderfully green, the cardamom and cypress release their scents. As nutmeg draws fine olfactory paths - also darker and spicy. Already in this initial phase, patchouli whispers earthy to itself and will pull through the entire progression.

I actually found it by chance and found the entire male line appealing. After several video mentions from Leniscents and multiple visits to the perfumery, I decided on the Vetiver Musc. I am particularly drawn to the green notes, the light woodiness, and the fact that as a whole creation it is floral, fresh, and green-herbaceous, yet still has a nice masculine touch for me.

I was also interested in Monotheme's Zagara, but I tried this one first. Therefore, I can't compare them. The prices are also completely different.This one has a very natural and clear scent, and is also green.The scent is not as complex as note. For those who like aroma oil blends, it is not difficult to understand at all. However, for those who dislike geranium and galbanum, it is difficult to recommend. It is not outstanding, but the atmosphere is somewhere. Rather than a soft and warm orange flower, it has a refreshing, airy, and green scent.Bergamot that is not artificial. It doesn't smell as complex as note. I like and love this green note, but if you want a clean orange blossom, I think there are other options. Or if you're looking for a designer fragrance-style orange marshmallow, you'll be in for an unfortunate encounter. Very unisex. Almost a single note. And I think this perfume is feeling quite out of place in the recent beast mode boom. But it wins hands down in terms of transparency. When you're tired, I think this kind of natural and gentle scent would suit you. For people who work a lot in the city, this kind of scent can help you recover mentally faster sometimes. It's not fashionable, but rather a very personal fragrance, the kind of fragrance you would wear for yourself. It fades very quickly, and depending on the person, it may disappear in an hour, or even minutes. That's a bit of a problem. However, there are probably people who want to experience this aroma without worrying about the price. I like this fragrance, but it's expensive, so I'll look for a more realistic and less expensive Zagara. Yes, it's the type of fragrance that you won't regret even if you use a lot of it.

Recently, I exchanged interesting samples with a fellow Parfumo member, and one of them was labeled in large letters as Zagara. I took a quick sniff of the sample, delicious orange blossoms, and added it to the "Interest Stack." If only I had checked Parfumo beforehand to see how many Zagaras there are. The generous exchange partner also wasn't exactly sure what kind of perfume it was. But then I noticed that Acqua di Cuba was the only sample from this exchange that had the same writing, the same color, and a similarly round sticker, so it must also be a Santa Maria Novella fragrance. I hadn't had any direct contact with the brand until now, which isn't surprising given its rare distribution and extremely limited sales. Nevertheless, I had heard a lot of good things, and there are definitely fans among my Parfumo acquaintances. The brand's rich history dating back to the monasteries of the 13th century, along with its simple yet beautiful creations and formulas, sounds enticing, especially fueled by Fischlandmens' great comment. Normally, I would now provide my description of the scent, the most important part of the comment. But on my skin, Zagara is simply a beautiful orange blossom. Pure, summery, fresh & sparkling like neroli, later becoming slightly woody and masculine. Minimally sweet, not overly floral at first glance, making it absolutely unisex. A bit citrusy, very bright, and simply refreshing. This is one of the most refreshing flowers in the world. There's not much more to write and rave about. Everything is simply - simply beautiful. Bottle: really somewhat monastic and old-fashioned, but not ugly. Sillage: never intrusive, very summery light. Longevity: EdC level - 3-5 hours. A great introduction to the SMN world and a simply beautiful orange blossom scent... still my favorite bright flower, miles ahead of osmanthus and the like!

.....they don't make it easy for you. Really not, but it's worth it ......But let's start from the beginning. During my explorations in the world of fragrances, I am drawn to scents that are hard to find, those that are less known or have a special story behind them. However, the best is when a fragrance house combines everything in one. With the products of the old apothecary house "Santa Maria Novella," I have found just such an object of desire. Just the venerable appearance of the brand captivated me. This fascination for the products then grows immensely when I learned about this tradition that dates back to the 13th century. The origin of the products and the first formulations actually go back to the 13th century! Where can one get these scents? I asked myself for a long time.... The search for sources for these fragrances proved to be difficult. Manufactum has one fragrance in its range. There, I learned that the products are actually only allowed to be sold directly online by Santa Maria Novella, making a larger selection very hard to find in Germany. However, I was successful at MDC Cosmetic in Berlin and dove into the tradition of this special fragrance story. Under the button "Brands," the history of this line is beautifully and informatively described. http://mdc-cosmetic.de/info/Santa-Maria-Novella.html Enticed by such enticing words as "long-lasting freshness of Sicilian orange blossom" to "a cozy winter scent, rich in resin notes, rose, and woods. Brightened with orange blossoms," I eagerly pressed the order button on the site.
