In the meantime, I call the Ottone, the Zargara, and the Non Alcoholic After Shave Balm my own and have been able to get to know the Col. di Cuba, the Col. Pot Pouri, the Col. gold Musk, and the Col. Citta di Kyoto through uncomplicated sample fillings. I mention this because, despite how different the fragrances are, they all share one thing in common. They don't make it easy to engage with them. They all have a very strong character. They are different from what the descriptions lead you to mentally anticipate, and they have a rather unconventional scent progression, consisting of only 2 notes. Top and base note. Bam. Nothing confusing about scent facets. One theme, and that’s it. And that is so wonderfully soothing and calming once you’ve embraced it. But now to the fragrance to which I dedicate this comment. The Orange Blossom (Zagara). In the description of this fragrance, it mentions Sicilian orange blossom here on Parfumo. On the mdc site, there is nothing about the fragrance components, and thus I had a scent image in my olfactory mind and was initially confused when I ordered this scent blindly. Where was the orange blossom? Where was the buoyant lightness I expected? null of that flowed into my nose. Instead, a cloud of scent full of cool earthiness and slightly herbal soapy water made its way into my nose. Oh, disappointment set in. Good thing it lasted only about as long as the top note. 3 minutes, because after that, a wonderful mixture of 1/3 bitter orange, with 1/3 mint, filled with a mix of wild herbs made its way into my nose.... "The plant parts mature in a traditional way in vessels made of fired clay, in which a humid climate is maintained for weeks," so the manufacturing process of the fragrances is described, and this image is characteristic of the scent. Once you have opened yourself to this fragrance, you are rewarded. Rewarded with a truly extraordinary fresh mixture of bitter orange + mint + herbs that also lasts long (6-8 hours) and never feels overwhelming. There really isn’t much more to report about this fragrance. It is as simple as it is brilliant, true to the motto: "Less is More." I cannot confirm the classification as a purely women's fragrance by any means. At best, unisex. For this fragrance, I give a solid 100% for the scent. P.S: The non-alcoholic After Shave Balm - scent direction Grapefruit - is an absolute recommendation. Rarely have I felt so cared for and fresh throughout the day after shaving.

I like the original Essence by Narciso Rodriguez, and while there are not many differences between the original and this recent flanker, I do enjoy the muskier undertones and also the brighter citrusy accords in the opening of this fragrance far more than in Essence. This fragrance is quite airy. It's light, delicate and refreshing. It occasionally reminds me of the ocean air; salty and cooling. However the musk provides an interesting sensuality later on. The iris and rose blend together beautifully, like a soft floral bar of luxurious soap. It's hard not to like this fragrance. The musk is not unlike the prominent musk note in Narciso Rodriguez For Her. Musk really is making a comeback, particularly in a sensual way. Essence Eau de Musc, for me is a toned down and less creamy offering. On the skin it's like soap bubbles rather than laundry detergent. I'm not certain which one I like more, the original Essence or Essence Eau de Musc. All in all, this is a bright, fun and soothing scent that was a worthy Essence flanker in my opinion.

In search of the perfect musk fragrance Part 11 Why this one was allowed to move in with me a second time, I don't really know. I'm still looking for the perfect musk scent and I don't find this one bad at all. I had it once before when it was released, I even finished the bottle, but didn't repurchase it. Now I had a voucher to redeem, and I chose Eau de Musc, even though my feelings about this fragrance are still ambivalent. Eau de Musc develops on me after a short citrusy start to be rather fresh and cool, and a bit later, powdery. The freshness and coolness are already expressed by the silver, smooth bottle, which I really like. Warm and cozy, Eau de Musc does not become (unfortunately) for me. What I like about it is the delicate, clean, powdery aspect. What I don't like so much is the very slight hairspray note and the low longevity (about three hours on me, after that it's still detectable, but only very, very close to the skin). Although sometimes that's quite alright with me, because Eau de Musc is perfect for the morning when you want to smell fresh and clean, but haven't yet decided on the "main scent" of the day or - as I often do - can't decide. At the same time, I also tested the EDP. It lasts significantly longer, but personally, it's too rose-heavy for me (it's a different scent, although the two are quite similar in the base). I much prefer the Eau de Musc because it is more delicate, lighter, and fresher. So far, this is the only Rodriguez scent that I can handle. All the others scratch, bite, and kick me. It's not the perfect musk fragrance for me, but it's definitely a pleasant companion in spring and summer. It will surely be finished this time as well. And if I don't find the perfect musk fragrance, I might even repurchase it someday.

This is a skin scent as it should be. To me, it smells like clean, warm skin, spiced with a bit of citrus and a hint of musk. So cozy and snug warm. A true crowd-pleaser. Refreshing in summer due to the citrus, but I can also imagine enjoying it in winter, thanks to the musk! EdM was once again a blind buy (thank you again, Springflower!), sparked by the comments here. My concern that it would fade too quickly was unfounded. It lasts on me! Interestingly, not everywhere equally (better on the upper side of my forearm than on the lower, totally crazy!). I also wonder if you perceive it less yourself because it smells like skin. Whenever I think the scent has really faded, I suddenly catch a whiff again. And a few days ago - I had applied it in the morning - the man of the house asked me after work if it was me who smelled so much like perfume. Thank you, dear Mr. Rodriguez, for this wonderful feel-good scent!

To begin with: I love the EdP from Essence and have already written about it. Hoping for a delicate, fresher summer variant, I also bought the Eau de Musc last year. In the opening, I find it very piercing and somewhat soapy. However, this first impression fades and becomes rather fresh with a spicy hint of bergamot, which reminds me of the Earl Grey tea from my youth. Overall, it has something of a salty sea breeze or spicy Provence air, but it cannot maintain the feminine elegance and warm skin closeness that the EdP has set. Many perceive the Eau de Musc as a comforting scent, judging by previous reports. For me, it is not. It smells like fresh - albeit perfumed - laundry, but it is not warm enough, not intimate enough to be cozy. This is, however, purely subjective. Of course, everyone determines for themselves what is comforting and has their own expectations and associations. For me, its "big brother" is a comforting scent because it comes across as warmer. The EdT is fresher and more lavender-like and remains bergamot-spicy-powdery-musk-like on the skin over time. Nevertheless, it is a beautiful fragrance and a skillful variation of the base scent, which can still be recognized well when both are worn and compared. I share the experiences of Smellslikeme (see below): At Douglas, the saleswomen were not informed at that time that this is an independent fragrance. Those who prefer a "clean" scent more akin to fresh laundry will feel very comfortable with Eau de Musc. However, those who mean "clean and pure" as skin that should not be clinically sterile clean, but innocently delicate - will likely prefer the EdP. (If anyone is interested, feel free to visit my blog, where I have also discussed other fragrances as "clothing accessories").

My boss is very taciturn. And when he does say a few words, it’s only in passing… It’s difficult to gauge whether he means something funny or serious, or what he actually means and wants from someone. So, psychic abilities are a prerequisite for employment at our company! That’s why a colleague often says to him: “Boss! Please subject - predicate - object - period!” This fragrance reminded me of him. There is just as much unspoken and incompleteness in the air here. It starts off very promising: slightly citrusy, delicately floral, and wonderfully fresh. And what remains after a very short time is just a big powdery musk heart… It’s the first fragrance where I felt a strong urge to “layer”... Only after that did an exciting scent composition emerge. This confirmed to me that Essence Eau de Musc unfortunately does not work for me as an independent fragrance. It really just lacks 1-2 longer-lasting unknowns on the skin to make it interesting and complete.

Essence Eau de Musc is not a regular EDT from the original Essence, but differs significantly from its predecessor. Reminiscent of the original is the fresh, musky powderiness. In comparison to Eau de Musc, Essence is almost dusty and overly white.

Mr. Rodriguez can do the plain white T-shirt. With this one, a bit more fabric softener has been used. This little water starts off citrus-fresh. Then the fabric softener iris reveals itself. Finally, it gets ironed out, smelling of musk and powder. I am heavily disappointed by the longevity; Mr. Rodriguez can do better than this. Minimalist scent, minimalist comment.

At first, I had to wrinkle my nose a bit... Phew! Hold your breath until the alcohol has evaporated! Schnapsdrossel olé! Then a citrus accord follows, which transforms into a light powdery creaminess *drool*! Light floral notes, clean musk, cream body lotion to spray, yes!

This fragrance is for me a small fine olfactory delight. Gently and tenderly it caresses you all day long, until everything softly fades away by the next morning. The top notes are initially very present, but over time they transition into a sensitive and soft form, delicately settling into the powdery base. The iris makes the citrus notes pleasantly creamy.

When I learned in the summer of 2011 that there was finally an Eau de Toilette of the original Essence, which I also find very beautiful, in a smaller size and at a lower price, I went to the nearest perfume store with rosy cheeks to test "Essence Eau de Musc.

I’ve ordered well over 500 perfume samples and “Quercia” was one of the best out of the 500 I’ve ordered. Upon first impression I could smell the lavender upfront and center and it was one of the most wonderful smells I had ever smelled. I wound have purchased a full bottle but as a man I wouldn’t be able to pull off such a wonderful floral perfume so I went ahead and showed it to my sister and she said the same thing although she said “oh yeah that really pretty but thats straight up for a man…” so with that opinion I went ahead and bought a full bottle :) It’s been about a year now and I don’t get any of the lavender anymore all I get is a very woody cool toned aftershave with a texture similar to that of charcoal? And a little oily? Anytime I wear it I’m bound to get compliments I’ve been told I leave a trail behind me anywhere I go and that’s there’s always a cloud around when standing still. (Around 5ft radius) The scents last well over 8-9 hours before becoming a skin scent. Overall I’ve gotten good positive feedback on it and have had people ask what I’m wearing. 10/10 I usually wear unscented lotion and spray it Once on each neck pulse point (2) Once on the back of my neck (1) Once on each shoulder on clothes (2) Sometimes once inside my shirt (1) Usually 5-6 sprays in total

I talk a lot about grey overcast skies and thunderstorms and fog and mist and loving the glooms, but even I can appreciate an objectively beautiful day. Quercia is that day...clear clear air, clean clear water, when people say fresh air or water is sweet, this is what they mean, a sharp lucidity you can taste. Something green but not heavy, not dense forest green, lighter than that, the pale spring green of new growth and tender stems crushed underfoot releasing their watery juice. A cloudless, cool spring morning that makes you genuinely think "I am glad to be alive," the kind of day that feels like a gift you didn't ask for but accepted anyway. Dappled light pooling through ancient oak branches, the tree itself barely present except as shadow, as the reason for this filtered sun, this meadow existing in its patient protection. Lying in the grass eye-level with buttercups and bluebells, yellow and blue blooming heads, their petals hold that papery, delicate sweetness, barely-there floral, more like the idea of flowers than their actual heavy perfume. They're good-natured about being trampled. They know they'll be growing on your grave one day, gentle and insistent, reclaiming everything with the same cheerful persistence. For five hundred years, the oak has stood watching smaller things bloom and fade and bloom again, and you're just another small thing, bright and brief and beautiful. Studio Ghibli sunlight, that glowing animation warmth where death exists but doesn't overshadow, where graves get flowers and flowers get walked over, and it's all the same turning wheel, all the same dappled afternoon. The shadow is there - hence the coolness, the morbid turn - but that's the way of things. Just keep enjoying the flowers while you can.

Quercia is a new eau de parfum from Officina Profumo Santa Maria Novella. According to Santa Maria Novella, "Quercia pays homage to the imposing tree of the Medicean Villa di Castello, a symbol of strength and longevity, which has defied time and the seasons for over five hundred years." I picked up my bottle at the perfumery in Firenze. The fragrance opened with lavender in the top note, which also came across a bit soapy to me. It was quite enjoyable and lasted a bit longer than I expected. The middle notes are made up of vetiver and patchouli. Neither seemed to dominate the other and was quite pleasant to wear. The base is oak wood. The perfume is long lasting. Ten-and-one-half hours after I first sprayed it on, my wife could still smell the fragrance as I walked past her. Quercia can be worn daily, day time or evening. It's appropriate for office wear and should not be offensive to anyone. If you like woody aromatic you might want to try this.

The brand Rodriguez has quietly made its way into my heart, as these fragrances are neither smooth mainstream nor overly interpretative niche. They always offer something special, have their own character - but are not overwhelming. This is also true for L`absolu for her. The dark purple bottle already raises expectations, which the scent fulfills. Surprisingly, I am greeted by an unpeeled orange - bitter yet soft. Against this backdrop, full-blooming climbing jasmine spirals upwards, with the enchanting scent it particularly exudes at night. I love to sit in the dark with a lantern, inhaling this magical aroma in my garden. The musk bathes the scene in a golden-yellow light, like the flickering candle. Patchouli deepens the nocturnal feeling, and the sandalwood is as velvety as the night air. I open the window, and L`absolu blends perfectly with the garden scent - and with my dreams.

This bottle! I must admit that this wonderfully eggplant-colored bottle immediately attracted me magically, as deep purple is one of my favorite colors. Upon first testing, I also liked the scent; it seemed just as dark purple as the color of the bottle. However, when I received a sample and applied the scent at home for the second time, I was met with a strong sweetness alongside the mysterious, dark notes of jasmine, musk, and patchouli, which initially struck me as almost candy-like and bothered me so much that I distanced myself from the fragrance. Since then, a few months have passed, and I have now tested another comparably dark jasmine scent, "À la Nuit" by Serge Lutens, which I find very herbaceous and green, yet still feminine and wonderful. Interestingly, since testing the more herbaceous Lutens jasmine counterpart, I perceive "For Her L'Absolu" by Rodriguez completely differently and can experience it anew. In contrast to the Lutens jasmine scent, Rodriguez could now seem overly sweet to me - but it doesn’t! On the contrary, although it still comes across as rather sweet to my nose, the sweetness no longer bothers me; instead, it evokes positive associations in me such as sensuality, warmth, and erotic tension. A sweetness that is so relativized by the iridescent jasmine, the warmth of patchouli, sandalwood, musk, and amber that I can have it around me comfortably. I can place both scents, "À la Nuit" by Serge Lutens and "For Her L'Absolu" by Rodriguez, on equal footing and find both wonderful in their own way, two different interpretations of the same theme. For Her L'Absolu is definitely a cozy winter scent for me; it fits a cozy evening for two or even among many, signaling for me mature femininity, sex appeal, and good mood. I perceive the sillage as medium strong. It is noticeable on me for about six to eight hours, becoming more intimate after a few hours. For me, a candidate for purchase this winter.

A truly sensual-beautiful-slightly sultry seducer with fine night jasmine. A distinctly noticeable sweetness clings to this perfume, which one must like and prepare for - it stays. Everything is refined by a lot of musk and the gentle warmth of amber. The jasmine peeks through very subtly, not pushing itself to the forefront, fitting in well. Somehow, it is a beautiful and dark vintage scent; perhaps it is the patchouli that has its own signature... I rate its longevity at a good 6-7 hours. It is well-suited for a grand appearance but also for intimate cuddle hours with a loved one. The next morning, a fine musk trail lingers along my body.

What I perceived when I first sniffed "For Her L’Absolu" I liked very much: sweet, slightly powdery, and not necessarily light - rather seductively dark, just like the beautiful bottle that impresses with its simple elegance. I lifted my wrist once more to catch this lovely scent and there was... nothing. It was simply... gone. I was astonished - and very disappointed - because fragrances usually last a long time on my skin (some distinctly noticeable for up to 24 hours or more); at least on average. That a perfume evaporates from my skin after just seconds is something I have never experienced; all the more regrettable, as it is truly a beautiful fragrance. Narciso Rodriguez has created a scent here that is classic, seductive, and unique at the same time. A fragrance that, despite its uniqueness, remarkably fits in everywhere, as it adapts to any situation, yet is always present without being overwhelmingly dominant - if it indeed stays. Less volatility would have definitely made it a candidate for purchase for me.

I believe I should slowly start to overcome my fears regarding fragrances that carry the additions "Absolue, Intense, Noir, Extrait, Night, Essence, etc." I have been circling around them forever, waiting for the right moment when I am absolutely certain and far from having a headache, and before I apply a subtle spray on my wrist, I will quickly cross myself again. Of course, I have already sprayed on a paper strip, just in case it knocks me off my feet. In short: I am afraid. Afraid that I will get a headache again, afraid that the stuff won’t come off my skin or will linger in my clothes (scarf, coat) for days... I only say: Chanel Coco Mademoiselle! Devil's stuff! Smells fantastic but kills me! If it’s too strong, you’re too weak! In short: this morning it was time! Death-defyingly, I grabbed it for a test and sacrificed my left wrist. A moment of wonder occurred, all my senses were either heightened or tense, because I smelled something very quiet, unobtrusive, pleasant. Is that jasmine? Without edges and corners, without peaks. Insignificant. Interchangeable. I was somehow disappointed. It felt like being roared at by a lion (the name Absolue) and then realizing that the lion has no teeth in its mouth. I don’t like being bitten, but I would have wished for a few "little teeth," meaning something more expressive, right from the start. Towards the middle, the scent becomes louder, but still round and without that certain something. Still interchangeable. Now I also recognize the jasmine. What remains towards the end is a mishmash of amber, musk, patchouli, and sandalwood. Wildly mixed together. It reminds me very much of the moment when you walk into Douglas on a Saturday, where countless fragrances have already been sprayed all day, and only the heavy and strong components have held on, now engaging in a wrestling match with each other. Time to run away. I cannot find any similarities between the EDT and EDP of the fragrance "For Her." No flattering creaminess. If I had to classify it, I would label it as a noble evening fragrance for women. Rather not for girls or young women.

A very fine and elegant fragrance. For me, it is a bit floral, but not too much, a bit sweet, but not too much, a bit bitter, but not too much. At the beginning, it has a slightly fresh note that later disappears. Somehow, I see so much in it, and it takes me on mental journeys.

Lovable. About 2 meters worth of initial sillage that slowly settles close to skin over the first ~1,5 hours. Lily of the valley above – a crisp and vibrant white floral. Clean softness below. A fantasy white flower accord – sugary sweetness, subdued and somewhat chalky, like children's candy necklace. Musk – cozy, dreamlike. The whole thing smells like slowly waking up from a dream on a distant spring morning. The rays of sun are just barely reaching edges of your bed. Warmth of the clean white sheets is enveloping and lulling you back into a sweet oblivion. A faint scent of an ideal mother's perfume is getting closer and closer. Another minute or two and she'll come in and gently wake you up, just like in the movies, and your whole life until now will fade away like it never happened, and everything will be safe and okay. But for now – mom, please, just a few more minutes. It's very pretty, but it's also making me melancholic. I love the contrast between lily of the valley and fantasy white flowers below! Both are technically shades of white, but when put together side by side – the end result glistens in the morning light like the inner layers of a seashell. Iridescence. Mellow, yet mesmerizing. Once it settles on skin ~1,5 hours in, lily of the valley quickly fades and cotton flower becomes center of the remaining composition. Well, the idea of it. In reality cotton flowers don't have much of a scent, but if they did – this one would fit them quite well. Soft and fuzzy, gently sweet. Warm and textured more than it is flavorful. If it didn't make me feel sad for no reason, I'd love to wear it again. Over the next few hours it fizzles out to a faint aftertaste – white musk. Clean sheets, warm air. Not for me, but it's a beautiful shade of white. I can see why they named it radiant.

As a big fan of Narciso Rodriguez, I collect the fragrances, and among my favorite everyday companions are "For Her (Eau de Toilette) | Narciso Rodriguez," "For Her Pure Musc (Eau de Parfum) | Narciso Rodriguez," "For Her Musc Noir Rose | Narciso Rodriguez," and "Narciso (Eau de Parfum Poudrée) | Narciso Rodriguez." Therefore, I always test new scents from the brand, including the new Narciso Eau de Parfum Radiante released in 2025. The scent is, to say the least, better than expected, a true clean girl fragrance. The fragrance is fresh, floral, somewhat silky & soapy, fresh, creamy & clean, and also slightly synthetic, which is pleasant and not artificial; a pure synthetic note is perceivable. Soft, delicate, comforting & beautiful, Narciso Eau de Parfum Radiante smells of fresh cotton, with the cotton dominating the scent and blending with the typical, synthetic pure and warm musk scent. The vetiver adds another soft note to the fragrance, and floral notes are clearly perceivable, but the cotton and musk notes dominate, running through the scent from beginning to end. I like Narciso Eau de Parfum Radiante so much that I will treat myself to a 50ml or 100ml bottle, as I have been looking for a new beautiful clean girl scent for a while - which Narciso Eau de Parfum Radiante definitely is - another great fragrance bomb from the house of NR, I am thrilled!

It is that moment when you take fresh laundry off the line, still warm from the sun, with a hint of pollen in the air. Narciso Eau de Parfum Radiante captures exactly this feeling - clean, light, and radiant. The clove in the top note gives it a subtle spiciness. Then it becomes gentle. Cotton flower and musk settle on the skin like an airy shirt, dry and powdery rather than creamy, almost floating. In the base, woods remain discreetly in the background. Narciso Eau de Parfum Radiante stays linear, but that is exactly what makes it so soothing. With 5-7 hours of longevity and an intimate sillage, it stays close - not a statement scent, but one you can feel. For me, a fragrance that will accompany me in everyday life and at the office.

I love Narciso R.! Especially 'For her' EdP, Pure Musc, and Fleur Musc. I thought it couldn't get any better… I don't want to overshadow the other fragrances, but when I smelled 'Radiante', I felt like I had finally 'arrived'. The longer I wear it, the more my senses scream 'Yes! Yes! Yes!' I have been waiting my whole life for THIS scent, all my expectations have been met! It starts fresh, floral, a bit soapy-sweet, yet so creamy soft! I distinctly perceive aldehydes and cotton blossom. In the drydown, the Narciso musk unfolds richly. The scent is in no way associated with 'doctor's office'. No trace of the sharp note like, for example, Baccara Rouge. It is the epitome of cleanliness, but without the laundry room… As a clean scent fetishist, I naturally own Blanche and also The Muse. But this one tops everything, as it is creamy soft. I wouldn't compare it to Lengling No. 1 El Pasajero either, as there is no vanilla involved in 'Radiante'. Both fragrances are masterpieces of their own kind. I have been wearing the scent for several hours now, and it is still intensely perceivable. Love!!!!!

Completely different from the other NR fragrances. I was expecting something spicy and oppressive again during the testing. I was pleasantly surprised! This fragrance starts with something that reminds me of the opening of JLo Glow - a bit soapy, powdery, but as it develops, you get a freshness that recalls laundry detergent or a fresh fabric softener in a milder form. I think of the Muse, but here it is also beautifully delicate and takes the form of bright, fresh iris. The impression lasts a long time, and I find the longevity really good. I can still smell the fragrance on my clothes the next day. The fragrance really stands out with its clarity and softness, and I am glad to have it in my collection.

Today I stood in the drugstore in front of the Narciso Rodriguez shelf - I wasn't aware of how many fragrances this brand has. But I'm still new to the club of fragrance lovers. So far, I had only tried the For Her Eau de Parfum and the new For Her Eau de Parfum Intense, and I expected this scent to follow the usual direction.

This cube is completely different, clean, soapy, bright floral, and strikingly pure. It evokes a household cleaning product vibe, even the scent impression is reminiscent of disinfection in a clinic. Not a natural floral scent, but in vitro. It is a clean musk from the chemical barrel with a few flowers from the Petri dish. Headache...

.. finally a NR that doesn't overwhelm you with the familiar musky powder puff. Clean, aldehydic, Take a Shower, clean white cotton bed linen, a bouquet of lily of the valley. For me, a clean scent not in the sense of the Muse, but something more femininely floral.

... meeting a friend for breakfast. My friend is not here yet, but a very well-dressed lady sits down at the next table and orders her breakfast. From her comes the scent of soap, cotton, and a clean freshness. Simply clean and sexy. And then my buddy arrives and smiles at the lady slyly, and she smiles back. She knows exactly what kind of aura she has.

I actually like all the fragrances from Narciso. This one was a blind buy and to say that I am disappointed would be an exaggeration, but for my taste, it's too reserved. Of course, this could also be a plus point for other users. I find the lily of the valley very prominent at first and then it quickly transitions into a light cotton scent.

I actually think the scent is great. The only thing that bothers me is this piercing smell (because the perfume developed slightly cola-like on my skin). I generally tend to be the candidate on whom perfumes develop sweetly, often regardless of the notes. On my boyfriend, however, it developed spicy and smoky, smelling masculine and really good, I would say like cigars (in the best sense). Gelsomino was my favorite from Santa Maria Novella. Maybe also because it suits women better than Incenso.

Exquisite composition by Sonia Constant, radiating an smooth aura of inviting and supreme sophistication. There is a delicious opening of icy green mandarin and basil; fine, fresh ... Blended with a heart of sensual cedar, seductive musk and mysterious ebony. I have the three fragrances from the Bleu Noir collection by Narciso Rodríguez: For me, this EDT Extreme is a step further on the path started with the original but in a smoother and "aerial" direction. This new version is fresher but deeper, and softer but more seductive - in my experience - than the first EDT (which is safer and more versatile throughout the year). It makes a perfect match with the EDP to cover all the situations to get closer... The juice has excellent quality, but be careful: It's a fragrance of delicate nuances, so it is not for rude noses: Projection is soft - just as it must be a true classy scent -. Possibly, it won't be loved by "loud" guys. - Duration & Projection: Moderate to soft; for me it's a long lasting subtle projector: + 8h of refined scent waves. - Mood: Cool, seductive, masculine, inviting... - Age: >25. - Scenario & Ocassions: It can be used at any time, but will shine especially on spring, summer and early fall sunsets... - Conclusion: An elegant, contemporary and excellent "designer" release. I just love it.

After a long hike you retreat and grab yourself some ice cold orange juice with a dash of lemonade and sip this heavenly juice. This is what this smells like. Atleast from my perfume oil inspired version. Not too much going on here as per the notes but it's quite enchanting, uplifting, yet unique and softly seductive. If you have worn Fa Heat Control deodorant, then this fragrance has some memories to it. Nothing synthetic to it btw. The green mandarin is as real as it gets. Performance may not be a strong suit but for the smell, grab it and douse yourself with it. Such a diamond in the mud discovered. 10/10 for me. P.S: Ladies, you might want to check this one out. Totally unisex.

Narciso Rodriguez, a great brand that is very popular with a few lines and stands out more with many flankers. For women, of course, there is the beautiful For Her line and the "Narciso" line. Very nice and truly recommendable. For men, there is the musk bomb For Him, which I also own. The men's offering is rather small with the For Him line. The Bleu line now includes 4 flankers with the EdT, EdT Extreme, EdP, and the parfum. This is my first test and purchase from the Bleu line, although I would certainly find the new parfum in the Valentino Uomo style exciting as well. I had my eye on this fragrance for a while, especially since I wanted to have a fresh basil scent in my collection. While I do own "Armani Code Sport (Eau de Toilette) | Giorgio Armani," I wanted to test this fragrance with the great pyramid. You have to like basil here. For me, it’s a great sympathetic note in understated style. The bottle is simple and designer-typical. Nice color gradient with silver lettering. Well done and very attractive. The fragrance scores points for me primarily with its sympathy. It’s not a scent that totally impresses and knocks you off your feet. Rather, it’s a scent that accompanies you through the day in a sympathetic-fresh way without much fuss. The green mandarin starts with a bitter freshness. This fruit has a green-bitter touch, not fruity or sweet. Overall, there is zero sweetness in this fragrance. Instead, there’s basil, the star of this creation. A wonderful mild note that is quite unique compared to other freshies. This basil note has a slightly peppery quality with a mild spiciness. 100% pleasant. Of course, the typical Narciso musk is also present, here combined with woods. Overall rounded, fresh, pleasant, and never too much of a good thing for everyday situations. However, the performance is not extreme, even though it is quite decent. I would estimate it at 5-6 hours. Thus, it’s a great casual fragrance to smell fresh and sympathetic. For me, it’s an absolutely wonderful fragrance that makes you feel comfortable. You should test it if you like basil and are looking for an understated scent.

The bottles of the line appeal to me very much, and otherwise, you only hear and see the EdP and perfume variant. For my taste, they are simply a bit too soapy, which is why I chose the generally less popular EDT Extreme. Clean, fresh, blue, slightly aquatic, easy to wear, made for hot days just like a cool spring, basil, slightly citrusy. Daytime, everyday, all-rounder, office, gym, friends, date. There is definitely a similarity to terre d'hermes EdT, which I love, but without the orange and less of the intense vetiver, instead featuring the clean musk. In my opinion, it can cater to many scenarios and offers little spectacular. However, it provides a scent that everyone enjoys smelling. Not intrusive. Longevity and sillage for a blue fragrance are completely fine, but generally quite subtle. Great blue scent without many artificial notes. Absolutely top for summer, freshly showered. Not a blind buy, but testable everywhere.

Narciso Rodriguez for him bleu noir. A fragrance completely unknown to me, a completely unknown brand. Until recently. I smelled the fragrance on one of our members at the gym. And it piqued my curiosity. The EdT Extreme is, like the EdT and EdP, a pleasing, clean, and blue scent. One associates it with fresh laundry, a suit, or, with some reservations, summer by the sea.

- Hey Nasemann, what fragrance are you wearing today? - Oh, that's the "Narciso Rodriguez Bleu Noir for him Eau de Toilette Extreme"! I need a whole ten words in 2.5 languages ("Narciso" should theoretically be pronounced in English, but in Spanish or - even bolder - German pronunciation, it just sounds better!) to accurately name this pretty scent.

... freshness I get here. I stand near a market stall at the Viktualienmarkt where citrus fruits are offered. They rise beautifully to my nose. On this day, the cold from the ice cream stand next to me adds to the experience. For me, this day is sunny, beautiful, and fresh.

I stumbled upon this fragrance by chance, as it was supposedly on sale at Türkis, so just under €40 for 50 ml. The scent itself is lovely, very fresh, distinctly citrusy in the opening, with subtle aquatic notes. This is complemented by the described creaminess, which gives it a certain snugness and softness. So it's actually a perfect summer fragrance.

Rarely does a rose perfume inspire in me such happiness as this rose. I have tried sooooo many rose perfumes and it happens to be one of my favorite notes. When I smelled this rose, however, I was astounded. It is fresh, deep and at the same time light. Vibrant. This rose is still attached to its roots. It's alive. Though the cologne is not my favorite medium of scent transmission, in this case, it works beautifully. Splash on this acqua liberally, on clothes, body or bed. It is neither too strong nor too fleeting. I love to use this on multiple surfaces as it maintains its character. There is a bit of lemon in this but it is nothing like other lemon roses: a bit spicy but not sharp at all. This is a rose that simply makes me happy. Beautiful.

Yes, I love roses and I have gladly accepted the designation Rosenliesl or Rosenresli. That doesn’t mean, however, that I have to know, test, and like all rose fragrances. As beautiful as I find the bottles from Santa Maria Novella, the rose scent is - with all due respect - nothing special. It has a somewhat sharp, alcoholic opening of rose surrounded by roses. Just freshly cut garden roses that together make a lovely bouquet in a vase. The petals, the leaves, and the dark green stems - all three contribute to the overall impression. This rose rightly carries its solo name: it is clearly a soliflore when it comes to rose. However, this type of rose fragrance is available from many brands, following the motto we must also have a "real" rose scent in our range . Personally, I find that a bit too little, almost a bit boring. But for those who prefer exactly that, Rosa by Santa Maria Novella is perfectly suited.

It's the Goldilocks syndrome, it has to be 'just right' So, if we're preaching to the converted and you're familiar with 'For Her' Black or Pink, or 'In Colour' or 'Musc Intense' or Narciso 'White' then you are programmed to be quite receptive anyway. Goldilocks went to the Bears house and tried their porridge, came back the next day and tried their armchairs and finally, third time lucky, (or not so) when the little bear's bed was 'just right' she fell asleep. My battle with NR is not with the perfumes, but the naming of them. As with Lolita Lempicka you can't just throw a name at your friends who might enquire after your perfume....ah yes, it's the pink bottle that has a black box, no, no, I've got it wrong, it's the black bottle that has a pink box, oh dear, it's the eau de parfum with the lovely sillage, but no, hang on, it's the EDT that wafts around??? Isn't that right? Confused? It's soap, but not as we know it. Narciso 'Black' EDT benefits from a generous application, more sprays than you would normally use, but suitably nuked it will last many hours. Another reviewer (Christianne on Fragrantica) says she wants to hoard it and I have to confess I do too. It's gong to be at your perfume counter, easily sampled, so I won't go into the fragrance notes. My husband loves these summertime musks when I wear them and sometimes in my perfume memory a candle strength of Houbigant White Musk flickers through them and makes me feel young again, now that's got to be worth the money.

Narciso Rodriguez understands musk like no other—regardless of the perfumer, they just get it. The house signature, if you will. Every fragrance in their lineup boasts masterfully blended musk accords—a symphony of clean laundry musks, soft creamy musks, woody and animalic musks, fruity musks, and powdery nitro musks. I started my journey, into the world of Narciso Rodriguez, with Narciso for Men EDT—its wet concrete-meets-urban decay vibe was mesmerizing. Then came Narciso for Her (EDT), in the tall, black bottle, and I adored it even more—luscious white florals over a woody musky base . Next, the black cube entered my collection—and without a doubt, it’s probably the finest musk fragrance I own. It opens with a luscious blend of creamy roses, and peonies, kissed with fruity nuances—full-bodied, diffusive, and utterly intoxicating. The voluptuous creaminess owes much to peach lactones (aldehyde C-14), enriched by velvety cedar-like woods and earthy vetiver. Hints of patchouli weave their way through the mix, adding depth to this perfectly formulated composition—short, concise, and designed for pure olfactory impact with zero distractions. Elegance, sensuality, warmth, sophistication—this fragrance embodies them all. An absolute dream in cooler weather, when its layers unfurl, revealing their full splendor. If musk is your thing, and roses/peonies intrigue you, then this is a must-have. 9/10

It is well past midnight - the friends have left, you have sat together, chatted, smoked, and had a glass of wine. This relaxed, cultivated atmosphere was accompanied by Narciso. This fragrance has a pleasant presence without being intrusive - it has style without any pretension. It fit into the gathering like an additional welcome guest. And now, with everything quiet, it lets the evening resonate with the good wine and personal conversations. It mingles with the noble scent of roses that wafts in through the open terrace door. It has rained, and the garden breathes a fresh, spicy scent of wood in gratitude. Narciso carries the fragrance and the tranquility into the house. Although it is not a "cuddly" scent, it exudes a certain emotional closeness, and I would almost say - sensuality. The kind of sensuality that makes you reach for a good book - and not for a negligee. A beautiful scent to enjoy the end of the day.

I don't know how it is sometimes planned & executed by companies like Narciso Rodriguez, but with the EdT version of "Narciso", work must have started long before the recent launch of the original (EdP). It seems that NR pays no attention to success or criticism and consistently implements its philosophy & visions - commendable & truly uniquely great! If only a few more companies could free themselves from success & sales figures like this. And I really liked Narciso as well; it was a creamy delight, so another version for me personally, even if a bit too quick, certainly doesn't raise any eyebrows! Both fragrances are unmistakably related, but the new EdT (completely in black & glass) is much brighter, more everyday, & floral. The flowers have been turned up three notches, resulting in another creamy scent, but now much less unisex, which I had attributed to the original. A pretty young saleswoman in a flower shop applies neutral, expensive hand cream to her hands and then continues to work normally. She cuts the bouquets correctly, repots small trees, and sorts new flowers of all colors & varieties. That's roughly how Narciso EdT smells. Bottle: I prefer the white one slightly more for its minimalism & elegance. Sillage: due to the increased floral notes, it seems more expansive, less pure to me. Longevity: similar to the original - 5-7 hours. Conclusion: the now clearly more feminine alternative, full of blossoms, purity, a bit of cream & clean skin!

Narciso Rodriguez is one of those fragrances that I really struggle to pronounce. But not because Narciso or Rodriguez are difficult to say, no... but because something else always comes to mind when I hear the name Rodriguez. Namely, Robert Rodriguez, the director and producer of films like Desperado, From Dusk Till Dawn, Sin City, or Machete. You know, those are the films where, like in splatter movies, blood and guts are flying around, but in a somewhat more stylish way. Because there are also too many cheaply made films in this genre where the film only lives off the gore factor and where you can no longer see the actual movie because of all the blood that even splatters on the camera… um… I just realized… that this is not such a good introduction to a women's fragrance :D Anyway, here I come to the Narciso scent, which simply (rather unimaginatively) is also called Narciso and seems to be quite popular, making me all the more curious about the fragrance. Especially since this is actually my first Narciso that I am testing… even though I have seen it everywhere so often. Well, let’s spray it on… *spray* The scent: You immediately smell the roses at the beginning. I can't really distinguish between peonies and "regular" roses, but to me, the top note smells sweet and also slightly powdery. In any case, the scent is very pleasant and of course very feminine. I'm not sure, but it seems to me that a light citrus note occasionally appears in the background, something like oranges or orange blossoms,... it doesn't last long and is probably just my imagination, but it still feels a little like that (or could it be that peonies perhaps smell a bit fruitier and that's why it seems that way to me?) Anyway, the scent then becomes rosy again, which it has actually been the whole time. You can also smell the musk well, which makes the fragrance sweeter. The base is rather weak, as you can only faintly smell the woody notes. In any case, the scent continues to smell of roses and is also sweet. However, I couldn't detect any vetiver at all. The sillage and longevity: The sillage is incredibly intense at first. But shortly after, it becomes a bit weaker, yet I find that the scent can still be detected quite well on a lady for a while. The sillage is also very good; it lasted about ten hours on me. The bottle: The bottle is rectangular and black. The area where the fragrance liquid is filled has been dyed black, so you can't really see the liquid. The cap is rectangular and transparent, allowing you to see the black spray nozzle behind it. There is no label on the front; instead, the name is printed in capital letters on the bottle. A simple but still quite nice bottle. Wow, at first, the roses smell quite intense, but then the scent becomes a bit weaker, yet still remains detectable for a longer time. Also, I can't shake the feeling that I perceived something like oranges or neroli and wonder if this is due to the peonies. But to be honest, I don't know the difference between roses and peonies. The scent is essentially an all-rounder. Despite the sweet notes, I don't find it overwhelming, so it should also work on somewhat warmer summer days. And I think it fits especially well for going out, as the scent is very feminine, very delicious (and don't worry, this time I won't say that the combination of feminine and delicious results in something like "biteable" :D) and just smells good, so I would definitely recommend giving it a test. Since I also liked the scent very much, I will therefore also test more Robert… um,… I mean Narciso Rodriguez fragrances over time :D However, the scent is nothing special, as you have surely sniffed it or similarly scented fragrances thousands of times somewhere, but it still smells quite good and can be worn anytime, and that's the main thing, right? Hmm… did I really connect this fragrance with bloody splatter films in the introduction?? I can already see it coming… tomorrow my subscriber count will drop sharply because of this… *sigh*

By that, I mean Narciso Rodriguez, who has a knack for my fragrance taste. Since I am enamored with the older cream-white sister of this scent, the likelihood was high that Narciso would also charm me with the supposedly lighter EdT. When it comes to liking it, definitely. I can take my time with the purchase, you will soon understand why.

This fragrance is an elegant companion in business, for official occasions. The composition of white flowers and musk is striking, yet remains subtly in the background. Narciso EdT is the sheath dress among perfumes. Cedar and vetiver as masculine notes in the base make it a bit more vibrant and cheeky than the soft, milky EdP.

I am usually not a fan of mainstream fragrances, but since I received samples of "Narciso Eau de Toilette" at the perfumery, I decided to test the scent. It is a good, everyday floral fragrance, led by robust roses that "bathe" in a hint of musk, with a beautiful woody and earthy base; I can clearly recognize the vetiver, and it lasts a long time.

Amber Musc by Narciso Rodriguez riffs on the basic framework of the original Narciso Rodriguez For Her EDT (sweet orange blossom, musk, and patchouli) by adding amber and oud notes to spin it off into a more oriental direction. The result? A fragrance that retains the clean skin sexiness of the original while gaining a vaguely soukish exoticism. There is an antiseptic cleanliness to the musk and a stiffening breeze of Iso E Super in the drydown. Meh.

Recently at the airport, I struck up a conversation with the saleswomen after asking about something they didn’t have. We talked about different fragrance directions, and after a while, they showed me Narciso Rodriguez For Her Amber Musc and Rose Musc. I liked the Amber Musc so much that I ordered it after the trip. The fact that it is for women didn’t bother me; when the package arrived, I immediately sprayed it on and noticed that the top note comes across as very feminine. I can’t clearly identify orange blossom and musk; rather, it’s a mix of all the ingredients and, as I said, very feminine. However, after a few minutes, Madame bids farewell, and the notes that made me cling to the scent strip come to the forefront. Oud, patchouli, leather-this fragrance is dominated by the heart note, and the base ingredients round off this accord nicely. Now I can also smell the musk. From this point on, I would classify the scent as unisex. At first, I considered whether to put it in the souk because it might be a bit too feminine for me; I’m not exactly the feminine type. But the longer it stays on my skin, the more I think I should keep it. After 1.5 hours, I perceive it more and more as a men’s fragrance. Leather is animalistic with a hint of smoke. I don’t smell vanilla, and amber plays a subordinate role. Conclusion: a fragrance like a metamorphosis from woman to man. Fascinating and extravagant. Sorry, dear ladies, this one is not going to the souk for now; I like it way too much.

This week was shiningly golden - alongside the special edition of Arabian Night Men, I simply couldn't ignore this golden bottle from Narciso Rodriguez in the store. No matter if for ladies, regardless of confusing marketing chaos & strange naming - Narciso Rodriguez is always one of my go-to brands in the designer sector & simply genius. Special, different, unique, high-quality, knowing how to do it, with a persistent musk DNA, expressing understatement, simply cool as hell. No wonder I briefly felt like James Bond's most famous adversary - Amber Musc For Her drew me in like a magnet. And rightly so - very close to love at first sniff. If the lady by my side has this on her shelf, she has won & lost at the same time. Won because my fragrance heart quickly jumps to her, lost because I would also use it often ;) For Her Amber Musc stands out, both in the store and in any collection, no matter how big it is. And not just because of the massive gold bar exterior, but also because the scent stands out. The cold, wet, often somewhat masculine musk is feminized here by fruity-dark nail polish oud. This scent & an expensive, golden dress: BAM! Gold always seems a bit cheap, and here the oud does too, synthetic & initially screaming, but in the end, you quickly realize that this is not mass-produced, but custom-made. Not a counterfeit, but an original. A golden pop dress, sure, but one for 1000€ from Gucci. Or in this case from Narciso Rodriguez. It's worth it. When a brand that is otherwise so down-to-earth and minimalist dyes its musk gold, finally makes something for evening wear, it's damn great. Just as noble as the Musc Collection for men, only with more sex, sensuality & glamour. Bottle: I love gooold! Sillage & Longevity: I wear my sunglasses at Night! Conclusion: the brightest & goldest scent from NR that I have had the pleasure of smelling so far. Still fully typical NR musk DNA & absolutely on my fragrance wavelength!

On a boring Sunday afternoon, I browse through this great forum and go from one topic to another, landing on Amber Musc (for her - once upon a time) now for Everybody's Darling. I'm shown a golden, simple bottle that I find very appealing at first glance. Fragrance notes: Amber, Musk, Oud, Frankincense - I like it, I like it, I don't like it so much, I don't like it so much, but when I think of Amber/Musk, I always think of Gaultier². I liked that one a lot. I read a comment that awakens a strong desire in me. I quickly search for it online and lo and behold, I could have it for € 98,-. So far, I haven't dared to make any blind purchases; should I start now? The next comment, from a woman, warns me emphatically that the concoction is supposed to have a very masculine side. Then I'd better skip it. Two days later, I find a sample in the souk and promptly order it. And once again, I made a very nice acquaintance, just as a side note. Unfortunately, the post took forever, as it always does when you're eagerly waiting for something. Four days later, it finally arrives. Cap off, and I understood why there was talk of a masculine side. The disappointment was about an 8 on a scale of 10. Still, I sprayed it on a test strip and sniffed. It starts off very musky; is there Oud in there too? Thank goodness I didn't order the bottle. The next day, I grab the test strip again: Oh wonder, it smells wonderful now. So it's clear, I need to test it thoroughly once more. Round two: The top note still strikes me as quite masculine. Round three: Saturday morning 8 AM/- 2.0 degrees, I'm scraping my windshield free, and there it is. It groans and croaks as if something ancient is finally being released. I think of Aladdin's Wonderful Lamp. The genie whispers to me, finally you give me the air I need to breathe. It envelops me completely. Warm, soft, velvety, and round, and I float in this wonderful cocoon all Saturday. Yes, I'm in love! And it loves me back, because it stays and stays and stays…. And the moral of the story is, the € 98,- bottle is no longer available…. understandably! Edit: After persistent searching, I managed to snag the Wonderful Lamp, and it smells even better from the bottle than from the sample. The bottle is an absolute feast for the eyes.

It was love at first sight between us. I heard about you from an acquaintance and was immediately fired up. She is a sprightly retiree, a former interpreter, 74, slim, chic, and open-minded. She loves Rodriguez. She has quite a bit from him. I was familiar with many of them, but you are quite rare here in the country, so you were completely new to me. You are sensual through and through. And mega hot! Seriously, you practically radiate heat. A sweaty rider in a leather vest under the prairie sun could smell like you. Honestly, I first pick up on those animalistic moments - amber, musk, leather, smoke. There’s no trace of flowers and delicacy at first. They come later and mix in vigorously. The longevity is absolutely fantastic - I can still perceive you the next morning. Like a soft sweet veil after a night of revelry. A night filled with drinking, dancing, flirting, kissing, loving, and even arguing. But am I the only one perceiving you so crazily? The wearer finds you elegant and classically beautiful. And you are. On her. And on me, you are pure seduction. Is it your gypsy blood, the mom jokes. Yes, I’m humming that song too - "Belle" from "Notre Dame de Paris." Esmeralda could wear you. How I searched for you! Well, a decant was quickly organized. But that's just how I am - when it’s love, I want a bottle! And you were also available on eBay, but somehow it never worked out between us. Until this summer. Bulgaria, Sofia, airport, duty-free. So already on my way home, I discovered you on the shelf. Yes, it was you. The last bottle. You were waiting for me. Bought without a second thought. Of course, the vacation budget was more than empty because of that. But it doesn’t matter, dreams are meant to be fulfilled! I suspect we will experience quite a bit together. You can definitely be worn to the office, just not too much. You have that certain elegance with a slight wink. I've already worn you to the opera, and you fit in perfectly there. And of course for a date! Which I actually have planned! And you will accompany me! Here’s to a lovely evening!

This is how the moment sounds when you realize you've found your fragrance, THE fragrance, the moment when it becomes pleasantly warm, when you'd like to devour the test strip, want to wallow in the scent, and then never see it again. Something like that happened to me with this little treasure. But I can already give you a heads-up: There was a happy ending!

I have become extremely sensitive to certain oud notes. And here we have it... the nasty kind. You can find it in Montale or in Juliette Has a Gun Oud as well. Hair spray-like oud. Absolutely synthetic, shrill, loud, and bright. I don't think it should even be called oud. In real oud, you won't find any aspects that even remotely resemble this strange smell.

Ah yes, sometimes I come up with crazy ideas.. It might be the weather or maybe just me.. I always diligently browse the souk and read the comments about the fragrances.. Of course, in fast-forward, don’t want to waste any time. And what do I do then?? Buy!! I have a few Narciso fragrances.. A 7.

I have tried so many times to describe the magic of this fragrance in a review. So often I have searched for the right words and yet found none. The scent is more of a magical aura, a strong statement. You cannot break it down into its individual parts; it must be viewed as a whole. I discovered Amber musc through a dear friend.

I bought this fragrance "on a whim" and the very first spray knocked me off my feet; even at home, people asked what was being sprayed. At first, I was very skeptical and oscillated between disgust and fascination. After reapplying it a few days later, it became that deep connection I mentioned, a scent with gigantic resonance, warm and cozy, enveloping.

Light and and floral. I can sense the lily of the valley, but it has been added with a light hand, and is not overwhelming or cheap smelling like it can be. Apart from that, I smell musk in the background, then a little white floral and perhaps some of the peony. It doesn't smell much like the amazing Narciso Rodriguez for Her either edt or epd, and on my skin and in my opinion they have missed if they were hoping to create a "younger, fresher" version of the original, and have simply made a light, lily of the valley based floral.

What can I say if it is my signature scent? I adore it because it is so versatile: not too sweet, not too fresh, not too dry and not too aquatic. Great in cold and in warm weather. I get more the patchouli, musk, lily of the valley and peony. I enjoy it as a water sign and think it could go with an air sign as well. beautiful for a soft shy nature, for young and more mature women.

Actually, Lolle deserves the honor of reviewing this brand new flanker. Or to write a few sentences about it in your soap blog. Because it is so white, it can't get any whiter. The white rose giant. Persil with cuddly musk. Muguet de Ariel. All that and much more. The first fresh whiff opened my nostrils like a Fisherman's Friend. A fresh, tangy peony blast blew the cold winter air out of my nose and caused a slight discomfort. Was it my mucous membranes attacked by a slight runny nose or "just" my antipathy towards peonies? Fortunately, the peony left no lasting damage. The iced lily of the valley also proved to be just a white flower of the fresh-soapy kind, not aggressive, not destructive, as in other lily-of-the-valley-heavy fragrances. The base is what personally makes the scent likable to me again: cuddly soft. With a freshness guarantee. Beautiful musk, as I know and appreciate from Narciso. I wouldn't buy it, but I would recommend it as a summer rose to interested parties in this direction.

Today I feel sluggish and in need of rest - a day for the sofa with a hot water bottle in my arms and a book in hand. Of course, craftsmen come barging in, the neighbor, the delivery service. But I want my peace - so I reach for the sample of L`eau for her by Rodriguez. L´eau sounds promising of gentle, quiet company. The opening fulfills my wish as well - gently, Jasmine, Alpine violet, and peony greet me. Cuddle up and keep reading. But then the fragrance calls "Hello" and demands attention - with rose, lily of the valley, and amber. It lays itself over my book pages and wants to experience something. Silence is not its forte. I also wouldn't have expected the prominence of patchouli and musk in this intensity in an Eau. I admonish it to be patient, which it does not like. It fidgets and wants action. On other days, it would have given me a kick, and I would have jumped into my boots to match its adventurous spirit - but today I am really too sluggish. I don't want to do L`eau a disservice - I just had it set with the wrong expectation. For me, the scent is more "abroad" than "home". On another occasion, we will try again together. P.S. Today, in a more adventurous mood, I tried it again - and it promptly got to come home with me.

What to do when searching for a new fragrance for the ladies in your life? Simply try the female counterpart to a beloved men's scent. Unfortunately, the classic "for Her" is far too heavy and rosy for her. It's a good thing there's now an L'Eau on the market, but what can one expect? A watered-down version of the original? The scent of water roses? Or perhaps aquatic notes to soften the intense rose accords? The bottle, along with its packaging, comes in a powdery light pink that is very discreet and unassuming; the color gives no hint of anything aquatic. The bottle itself is shaped in the usual large and heavy form that I love, standing solidly on the shelf and feeling good in hand. The small version, presumably intended as a handbag size, is unfortunately almost unbeatable in its lack of care and creativity - it could just as easily be nail polish remover. The scent is inherently similar to its original, just with lighter and more aquatic notes. There are floral notes that represent lightness: jasmine, lily of the valley, cyclamen. However, they are a bit too intense and thus almost overwhelming. There are no fresh notes to soften them. Instead, rose accents come through, but unfortunately of the synthetic kind. It doesn't help that amber, musk, and patchouli in the base add a sweet and heavy layer. Sadly, the bright flowers quickly fade away, leaving the synthetic notes to dominate. I would describe the sillage as medium to weak, but still strong enough that the artificial tones are always detectable. To complete the misfortune, the longevity is a mediocre six to eight hours, which is quite decent for the wearer. If I wanted to gift my girlfriend plastic roses, I would shoot her some at the fair. Unfortunately, she doesn't like those either. The aquatic theme has been redefined in conjunction with roses and other flowers, but unfortunately not aquatic enough and far too artificial.

The entire "Narciso Rodriguez For Her" fragrance range has captivated me. I am addicted. Yes, truly addicted to these scents. They draw me in, they caress me, they ensnare me, they captivate me. What causes this? Now I have it. Finally! Enchanted, I lean back, close my eyes. I can't help but press my nose to my wrist.

First of all, I love NR for her EDT. However, since I only wear it in the evenings because I find it too intense during the day (at least for the office), I ordered this lighter version. You can clearly tell that it is an NR because it is also very musky. Personally, I only smell the rose (which I love so much) and the musk.

In my last perfume order, there was a sample of this fragrance included in the box. I only knew that it was supposed to be a spring scent; I am not familiar with the "normal" for her and didn't look at the fragrance pyramid at first. Just smell it. My first thought was quite blunt: "I haven't smelled something so unpleasant in a long time.

... I do love the Essence line from NR and also the For Her EDP... although it's not my favorite. Of course, when a fragrance hits like this and turns all the women’s heads, it was clear that soon, after the euphoria somewhat subsides but a solid base of loyal buyers forms, flankers would have to shoot out from the Rodriguez ground..

How differently fragrances are perceived... I find l'eau as well as the eau de Parfum for her very elegant, trés chique, very feminine and as soft as a wonderful aura! I just can't understand how some people smell differently... Toilet bowl cleaner??? Oh, that really annoys me because I think the scent is REALLY GREAT!!! Beautiful fragrance!

I can't mix perfumes, and I've never attended a weekend perfumer course; I leave that to the professionals. But I can cook quite well. In the past, I followed recipes, but lately, I've become confident and experienced enough to experiment on the fly. If I were tasked with baking a "Pizza Russa," I wouldn't try to recreate Russian specialties by drenching the pizza in borscht instead of tomato sauce or cooking the dough like pelmeni instead of baking it. I would choose a classic Italian pizza base recipe with a crispy crust, (plenty of) tomato sauce with oregano, and (rather little) cheese, then add a lot of vegetarian toppings, maybe some vegetables, carrots perhaps (definitely no onions), and a lot of arugula. And then pine nuts (or even better, possibly walnuts, we'll have to see). And my Russian twist would be, in the end: Fragrant roasted buckwheat (Italian "grano saraceno") sprinkled on top. That would be a thoroughly Italian pizza, but with a somehow foresty-bear-like-Slavic touch, and whether it would be "truly" Russian wouldn't matter to me, and probably not to the guests either. I think this is also how the (unnamed) perfumer from Santa Maria Novella approached it: by conjuring up a quintessentially classic, very Mediterranean cologne with a playful Russian twist. "Russian" often stands more or less synonymously for "Russian leather" in perfumery, which in turn refers to "birch tar." This path was not taken here. Instead, the slightly Russian-heavy, brown-spicy nuance that breaks the cheerful citrus cologne vibe is achieved through clove and benzoin. I find this a brilliant idea! The scent starts off, at first sniff, as a beautiful bergamot cologne (not a soliflor, but a citrus cologne blend with a bergamot predominance; there's little lemon, hardly any sharpness or acidity), including a bitter and fresh green, almost floral tendency. It feels so quintessentially Italian and mega-classic. But the whole thing also seems, if you sniff attentively, from the very first moment a bit captured or cushioned, as if someone is pressing the gas pedal of a Ferrari with one foot and tapping the brake with the other. Not that it falters or is enveloped in a cloud of musk or chemicals, but more as if the scent is trying not to release its full sparkle too quickly because something else is coming. Soon, a fine clove note makes its presence felt in the gap that has formed, never stepping too much into the foreground and not unfolding into a bouquet of spices: It never becomes a Tabac Original or Old Spice; it always remains primarily a citrus cologne, but with a spicy twist. And towards the end, a lovely balsamic benzoin weaves itself into the scent. This is unspectacular, it's simple, but it's good. For now, I'm giving it 8 points. I might adjust that later. If I do, it will likely be upwards, once I've tested it again in a more suitable, warmer season. * * * Regarding the history of the company, Yatagan has already said quite a bit in his review of the aftershave brother of this scent. If we can trust the official statements from the manufacturer, its roots lie in a monastery pharmacy in Florence around the year 1200. Then in 1612, the monks went public and opened a formal pharmacy outside the monastery walls, which earned them money and was well received in noble circles. In 1866, the church property was secularized, and the state handed the pharmacy over to a private individual; it remained in the possession of this family for several generations. Today it seems to have been sold, to whom exactly remains somewhat unclear, but certainly not to a large corporation. The company operates two interconnected websites, one more for showcasing the company and its history - https://www.smnovella.com/ - and one as an online shop - https://buy.smnovella.eu/ENG/ The sites are wonderfully designed and opulently illustrated (typically Italian in the best sense), but unfortunately a bit confusingly structured. You constantly get lost, which is why I can't currently find the historical overview from which I quoted above from memory. You can purchase the products not only online or in Italy but also in a few selected stores in Germany; in Berlin at MDC on Knaackstraße, where I plan to take a scent walk soon. I find the bottle so stunning (in the pictures) that I am deviating from my rule and rating it (with a 10) without having held it in my hand.

When I first tested Colonia Russa, I immediately noticed two things that prevented me from buying it. First, a very dry-herbaceous, almost piercing top note, in my opinion. And second, the fact that it had a perceived (smelled) longevity of 45 minutes on my skin. Today, six months later, at 28°C, the whole thing presents itself differently. I am currently using the corresponding soap "Colonia Russa, Sapone per Uomo." This soap, along with its sister "Pot-Pourri," is among the most pleasant and nourishing I have used so far. In the morning, I lather up nicely with "Russa" (what a foam!), then rinse off cool and after drying, I apply 2 to 3 short sprays above the navel. Nothing more. The soap and perfume complement each other. The soap forms the fresh-soft-floral base. At higher temperatures, the components of the perfume gradually waft up. This highly harmonious interplay lasts 6 - 8 hours, depending on activity. It is remarkably temperature-stable and sweat-neutral. It always smells fresh and clean. There is no cloud that my surroundings would find unbearable. Anyone who has the opportunity to test the scent and its corresponding soap should take their time and not inhale deeply right away. Even if Uomo is sometimes printed on it, both men and women can wear it. I recommend especially storing the two mentioned soaps and perfumes in the linen closet. In high outdoor temperatures, this can be a small treat in the evening and morning. "Russa" conveys a light, pleasant, cooling effect. High quality, still affordable, and not found everywhere (also important). However, it is not for those who prefer something "cuddly." There is no trace of sweetness in it.

Since the opening it caught my attention, it's a unique combination of amber, birch, benzoin and orange, giving a citrus-amber vibe, but not too sweet. It reminds a little to the smell of Blue Amber, that cozy feeling of an old loft, something melancholic. Although it's not listed, it has something leathery, I suppose that's the birch-benzoin part, the effect is quite cool. Opening sillage is around a meter and a half, good quality of ingredients. There is a subtle mix of lavender-jasmine that adds to the old smelling effect that it smells old, giving more uniqueness to the chord. My partner didn't like it, she said that it smelled very strong and heavy classical, such as Shalimar could be, but even heavier, however I was not harassed by the bursts from my neck, I think it lasts longer than it projects. After three hours there are citrus, orange, the vanilla touch of benzoin (perhaps this also contributed to the old smell effect). Now that it is drying it feels even older, but I'm enjoying it anyway, I understand that this phase is difficult and it's not for everyone, it requires a certain tolerance. It smells to another era, not the typical "it smells classic of the 70/80", it's the smell of The perfumist, of Grenouille.

Just when you think you have tested all sorts of amber perfumes, a small miracle like SMNA comes along. The sweetness of amber and benzoin is held in place by a strict yet light-hearted combination of birch, bitter orange, neroli and sandalwood, supported in the background by bergamot and amalfi lemon. The lavender to me seems like a brilliant final touch. This is a delightful amber concoction, lifting my spirits from spray one! Downside: Longevity and sillage are rather minimal

Amber smells completely different than expected......and in fact, much better.....and above all, more distinctive..... Taking a look at the complete fragrance pyramid quickly reveals the reason for this unexpected scent experience: Top notes: Bergamot, lemon, bitter orange, neroli Heart notes: Jasmine, lavender, rosemary Base notes: Amber, birch, sandalwood, benzoin From the very beginning, birch wood takes the lead and remains, in a way, the main motif throughout the entire fragrance journey.....it smells woody-smoky and slightly leathery..... At first, my nose perceives mainly neroli and bitter orange....however, not dominant, but rather as a supporting melody to the birch......for brief moments, something fresh, almost eucalyptus-like, also flashes through......perhaps this impression arises from the combination of the currently active fragrance notes..... A little later, lavender and rosemary join in......the smoky-woody-leathery base theme is now complemented by a herbal impression......but note: “complemented”.....not “replaced”.....I can hardly perceive jasmine at all......but perhaps it is the reason why the fragrance is now slowly becoming a bit calmer and softer.......where “soft” should be understood as extremely relative.......AMBRA is by no means a “soft” fragrance..... At this stage, the fragrance lingers for a longer time.....and just when you think not much is happening anymore, sandalwood and amber make their appearance...... The strong birch note noticeably steps into the background now, but remains present as a fundamental vibration.....the fragrance becomes softer and more balsamic and ultimately fades out with a delicate amber note..... Personally, I see amber more suited for men.....nonetheless, I would wear it myself.....not daily, but certainly now and then.....the fragrance has something fascinating about it.......something that is hard to put into words...

Roses have always been my mother's favorite flowers. Therefore, it was not uncommon for us to have a fresh bouquet of roses at home, which I loved to sniff. While I personally prefer yellow flowers, roses have always held a special place in my fragrance heart. Creating rose scents is - I think - no easy task. So much in everyday life now smells of roses that I can understand if some people are fed up with the scent; whether it's room spray, hand soap, or fabric softener - roses are omnipresent. For this reason, I am not necessarily drawn to perfumes that list these flowers as dominant notes, but there I was recently with the opportunity to test the EdP Fleur Musc and the EdT Florale. The scents remind me a bit of home and the fresh rose bouquets. Very lovely, soft, natural. A hint of powder, a bit of warmth. While the EdP lets the roses glide into a warm bed of musk and patchouli, in the EdT the rose petals seem to be carried skyward by a fresh breeze. The EdT is "slimmer," lighter, perhaps a bit cheekier. The combination with bergamot makes the scent floral-fresh, while in the EdP the musk note stands more prominently in the foreground, creating a beautiful, creamy warmth. Two truly successful rose creations, each with its own character, yet both very natural and feminine.

For me, it first smells rosy and fresh, and after a while, this typical NR creamy, spicy, fresh note comes in. I find the EdT better for warmer days than the EdP Fleur Musk, which is sometimes a bit too floral-sweet for me; I only appreciate it after a few hours when the flowers have faded and only the heart note is perceptible. With NR, I always weaken; it always fits and is never too much for my sensitive nose! This is my 6th NR in my collection, I love them all!! This unobtrusiveness simply has class. I also really like this frosted bottle!!

I once stood next to neroli blossoms and initially stepped back because a somewhat too harsh and musty smell came my way. Sniffed again, a subtly green, fresh, citrus note emerged. Still, yes, one must like neroli. Neroli and orange blossoms make up the fragrance. They give it that southern, subtly harsh, deep character. Frangipani makes it a bit lighter. Musk and amber make it for me so incomparably powdery/creamy. Cedar wood adds a bit of harshness again. For me, it is also a summer scent, but not for over 30 degrees. A floral/harsher caress on the skin. However, I would wish for more sillage. So I only get to enjoy it myself.

Can a tuberose scent be elegant, chic, yet sensual and classic? This is IMO the case of Tuberosa. You can feel the white flower bouquet leaded by the beautiful tuberose just from the beginning, ylang introduces in the potion the powdery velvety slightly carnal effect, while a hint of clove connects it to classic pre-1960's perfumes. The drydown is soft, powdery, woody and creamy, but still airy. It isn't a dense thick perfume (not so resinous as you would expect looking at the notes listed), it is a cologne, feminine, sweet, cheerful of an unconcerned aesthetic that still can't be felt as innocent in any way. The evolution is quite fast on my skin as it tends to be the case with edc. On my skin it lasts 4 to 5 hours, on clothes it stays for days, what I consider a pretty good performance given the concentration. Don't get the pyramid fool you, this has a transparent polite sillage, which makes it a non offensive day use perfume for an educated nose that has a love for both tuberose and vintage aesthetics. I wonder if Germaine Cellier knew this one? Fracas can be a rebelious, provocative, noisy, fruity and spoiled daughter of Tuberosa. If you love Fracas but find it difficult to pull it off for everyday casual use, try this gem. I want to give it an extra point for being fairly priced as opposed to the new trend quickly spreading all over niche houses giving crazy, out of proportion prices to their offers. This one gives great value for your money.

This is simply put, just as advertised. I am a fan! I love it when things are true to their nature and uncomplicated. This is Tuberose that can be worn to work without a big migraine or a fuss. This is a gentle water breeze with nothing to hide. There is no sweetness to this beyond the natural essence of the blossom itself. There is no struggle of juxtaposed accords or brash statement of art- the flower it self is the delicate dewy water soaked flower alone in the garden and it is truly beautiful. Tuberosa is a fully unisex Tuberose, you can't go wrong. OMG, am I gushing?! It's most likely due to the fact that I really want to delve into Tuberose lately- but honestly I look at my bottle of "Carnal Flower" like it is a hostile and alien extraterrestrial some days. I am not enlightened enough or anymore for my beloved "Fracas". L'Artisan's "Nuit De Tubereuse" sported such a hefty dose of Sandalwood on the dry down that I had to admit defeat. And so it goes...I find myself at the House of Santa Maria Novella- reknown perfumers of the likes of Catherine Di Medici. Founded in 1221...they know their stuff! This is probably one of the few houses that I can say, I've sampled most of and they are pretty safe for even blind buying- if you want your Vanilla/Vaniglia- light and creamy without sugar- you shall have it...If you crave sunny lemony-fresh bright yellow scotch broom/Ginestra- just as it sits on the hillsides of the Mediterranean regions ...Yatzee!
