And every single scent I buy from them is eminently wearable- uberlight sillage, perfect for chemical sensitive coworkers but persistent enough for personal joy and expertly crafted, Tuberosa will be no exception. I have also had great success with layering from this line because each scent is like a layer of fine silk.

When it gets cold and snows, you need something warming. I can recommend a bath or a shower with the Sapone per Uomo "Sandalo" from Santa Maria Novella. To this day, I have not encountered a bar of soap that is as woody-soft and calmingly fragrant. (Also a dream for shaving). After 1 - 2 hours, then a couple of spritzes of the Acqua di Colonia "Sandalo" over the navel and at the hairline on the neck. It is quite distinctive, and some may find it a bit old-fashioned. I say it is unadulterated and traditional. The overall scent impression feels natural and absolutely rounded. It is a feeling of "powdered and creamed". There is the soft, warm sandalwood. A creamy-soft herbal note and this subtle soapy base. And if you ever have trouble falling asleep, place a piece of the soap or a handkerchief sprayed with the Acqua di Colonia on your nightstand. I can fall asleep wonderfully with it.

Do you know that feeling when you’ve just taken a shower and have just applied lotion, and your skin is still steaming? That’s exactly what I associate with this scent. And somehow I have an idea of the scent of the old Nivea Soft Cream - no one knows why. The scent progression is very clear, all components are present at the same time, acting alongside and with each other. However, the Ylang Ylang stands out a bit more than the other components. The fragrance is wonderfully creamy, minimally woody, and very beautifully floral due to the Ylang - without the strange vibes that can arise from too much Ylang. The jasmine is perceptible to me, but well balanced, and so we have a wonderful fresh cream scent. It is less powdery than other Narcisos and less piercing than the original Pure Musc, which makes it less layerable. When I wear it, my husband always says I smell more diesel-like than when I wear the EdP. All in all, I like the scent; it is creamy, but to a certain extent also fresh - and yet creamy. And above all: Extremely wearable.

A silky cloth that glides over my bare skin, pleasant shivers run through me, gentle touches, almost like tickling yet stimulating and exciting. Like the first touches, like first love, like a deep, enduring passion... ____________________________ That's exactly how For Her Pure Musc Eau de Parfum Absolue feels to me. Sensual, smooth, caressing, enchanting, stimulating, and yet still impeccably refined. Heavy, animalistic musk, whipped creamy, blended with the finest jasmine oil and refined with a hint of ylang-ylang and bright cedar woods. These notes make this Pure Musc almost even more beautiful than the EdP, but they also make it rounder and softer. Yes, it is truly smoothie. It comes without any edges or corners. The EdP is significantly more exciting in its progression. The Absolue lacks a bit of that certain twist. Nevertheless, I really like this Pure Musc, especially because it is so soft and feminine. It practically merges with my skin and creates an absolutely sensual, attractive aura. In terms of character, it strongly reminds me of Musk | 12 - I find that one incredibly sensual as well. It is definitely dreamily beautiful, BUT... yes, now comes a but, one that makes me quite sad. Unfortunately, for my nose, the scent only remains present for a maximum of 2-3 hours. Then it becomes an aura scent that I no longer perceive as strongly. However, it is still enormously present for those around me. I then feel the need to reapply, and it can happen that it gets overdone, as it is still noticeable to others (perhaps also sensitive) noses. This unfortunately does not make it a candidate for purchase for me. Even though I love my decant, it probably won't be joining my collection, as the price is just too high for me. The For Her Pure Musc Eau de Parfum has developed into my signature scent over the past few months. The Absolue just can't quite keep up with that. Nevertheless, this soft, truly more exciting version of the EdP is definitely worth testing.

This is my go-to scent of choice, when I'm too frazzled to be able to choose a scent for the day. It's a clean musk, so don't go looking for a heavy breather raunch fest in this one, you'll be disappointed. Musc For Her is a freshly showered, soft skin musk, very mild and gentle. It won't stand out in a crowd of heavily perfumed people at a big event, but I promise you the hugs you'll get will last longer than you're used to.

... for my wallet! Because I also find this fragrance great! My best friend has Musc for Her, and when I visited her once, I got to test it out. Not a run-of-the-mill perfume. High recognition value. Initially slightly fruity, then "velvety". Very feminine and sensual, mature. Enchanting. Those are my associations. Personally, I don't like woody scents, but this one completely convinced me!

I almost always prefer the EDP, but here I made an exception; the light pink bottle winked at me intensely, but a test of both versions clarified everything immediately. The EDP is really not my thing. The black EDT captivated me right away, and the direct comparison made the difference clear. Musc for Her EDT is, of course, musky, and I feel it with every movement of my body. For me, the musk theme has been excellently executed. A gentle introduction with sweet osmanthus flowers, roses, and for me, always a hit, orange blossoms, which are nestled in amber and fine woods, with a delicate vanilla that holds back quite a bit. I have the feeling that musk is always, really involved in every note, and that is exactly what makes the uniqueness of this fragrance, which I cannot compare to any other. Because I am only talking about involvement, not dominance. That’s why I belong to those who are not overwhelmed by the musk in this fragrance, because I think it has been dosed with expert hands. Musc for Her is a soft, velvety scent that truly accompanies me faithfully throughout the day. I give this fragrance the label "EROTIC"; men react strongly and clingingly to this scent, I have simply noticed that. Compliments came exclusively from men. Not a scent for EVERY occasion. I would like to share one more experience. If I wear Musc for Her for several days in a row, I feel that the scent does not always change favorably. Wearing it is once again a matter of skin! In warm weather, I no longer wear it at all; warmth somehow doesn’t suit either of us. Perhaps it also has to do with the acidity of the skin or the hormone levels. I haven’t figured it out yet. Despite this little quirk, I love this scent, and this has been the case for years with us.

First of all: Narciso Rodriguez is an American designer of Cuban descent. He describes his fashion style as: "I create modern things with classical means." His fragrance composition is supposed to be inspired by Egyptian musk. Even in his youth, he is said to have had a particular fondness for it. That musk* corresponds to his olfactory preference can be clearly sniffed in this scent. What I smell is: musk, musk, musk! Fruity notes and floral scents are only present in homeopathic doses here. Thank you very much, Mom, for sending the sample. That was a nice attempt, but I'm not a musk cow!!! *Musk is the term for a glandular secretion from the musk deer living in the East Asian highlands. Up to 30 g of secretion is found in a walnut-sized gland on the deer's belly, in front of the genital organs. It contains components that have structural similarities to pheromones. These are said to have an aphrodisiac effect. Since 1888, musk has also been produced synthetically. Chemist Albert Baur was the first to successfully create artificial musk. However, this does little to diminish the desirability of the animal original musk, especially since it also holds significance in Traditional Chinese Medicine, where no synthetic substitute is used. (Same report also applies to the EdP version).

When NR edt for her was launched in 2004, I was immediately love-struck: after the slightly annoying orange blossom opening, this wonderful musk base slowly developed - to this day the signature of the brand. The Musc Oil from NR is my personal dream version of the fragrance and my absolute favorite NR: straight into the base without detours. The oil has another advantage: it is very close to the skin and therefore suitable for daytime wear - noticeable but not overwhelming. So well blended that you don't perceive the individual notes, just this clean-powdery veil that gently envelops you all day long. By the way, this scent is identical to the Limited Edition Musc Oil Collection that NR released a few years after discontinuing this fragrance. It's such a shame that it's only available on the gray market now…why, NR??? I can only speculate that for many consumers, an oil perfume is less attractive than a conventional perfume due to its weak sillage, higher price, and greater susceptibility to spoilage. To experience the full beauty of this fragrance, it should be applied on a warm day - the warmth brings it to life. I am wearing it today in over 30 degrees and find it wonderful: this sexy-clean musk goddess is simply dreamy!

This is a lovely wood scent for the ladies! The flowers give it a feminine touch while still keeping the robust base note intact. Just to my taste and already made it onto my wish list!!! Perfect for the colder season.

The Radiant Magnolia is said to be very similar to the "Valentino Donna Rosa Verde | Valentino." To be honest, I find the Radiant Magnolia more pleasant, especially since there is also a certain fragrance progression to be noticed. The performance is also significantly better. The longevity on my skin is around 12 hours with a solid sillage. The top note starts greenish, refreshing, citrusy, and spicy with aromas of blackcurrant buds, bergamot, ginger, and lemon peels. The heart note smells floral and still greenish thanks to magnolias and green rose. The base is woody with a hint of rosewood and a bit of musk. Overall, I quite liked the "Radiant Magnolia | Narciso Rodriguez." I thank Libelle11 for the sample.

Radiant Magnolia is simply *awesome*! I have my absolute Narciso favorite (Pure Musc), but Radiant Magnolia could actually challenge it for the throne. The new fragrance from the Les Transparences Collection (what a great name, even if it doesn't quite fit the scents - they are just too intense for that) is exactly my style. Already after the first spray, I immediately had the image of a wooden bowl full of water with lemon slices, pieces of ginger, and magnolia flowers in my mind. Fresh, zesty citrus aroma with a strong dose of ginger (I love it!) and a proper amount of magnolia - that's how this fragrance greets you. Ahh. So cheerful and friendly, so full of zest for life, it comes across from the very first moment. Unfortunately, this wonderful top note doesn't last too long. After a few minutes, the heart note unfolds. Sweet from the magnolia, but at the same time green, slightly aquatic, and bitter - this gives the fragrance a very special twist. Rose stays more in the background, instead, the typical Narciso musk dominates. The heart note remains well present until the fragrance gradually fades softly musky-woody on the skin. Tonka bean is at most an accessory, and I can't perceive osmanthus at all. Still, or perhaps precisely because of that, I find it fantastic. A fragrance that surely shines best in spring or summer. I would buy it immediately - if it weren't for the outrageous price. Unfortunately, the fragrance doesn't last long enough for that. But still - test it and feel it. P.S.

Rose lovers, musk addicts, and long-time iris devotees, fresh flower sniffers and cleanliness fanatics, this is THE ultimate fragrance - and exactly mine, for certain hours together, during shared meals with the best friends. This scent creates an incredible closeness. It is a fragrance that warms me from within with sunshine. Like a hot cup of milk with a dripping spoonful of flower honey, floral and mild. It welcomes you in the most beautiful way, gently embracing you, cheek to cheek. The night is clear, you can hear the blackbird softly presenting its love song. The divine sparks in the sky shine in the most beautiful light. Rose and musk meet for a love play, in an open field, visible from all sides. Iris and amber are also part of the game, although the strong rose likes to mark its territory, enjoys dominating but has a fondness for musk and therefore takes it by the hand and shows it where the journey goes. The iris prefers to stay in the background, peeking out from its hiding place occasionally and observing the love play from a safe distance. After the love play reaches its peak, amber dares to come out of its hiding place and waves to the rose and musk. You can only hear a little whispering in the bushes, very subtle, fine. A fragrance that I cannot assign to any season. It can be worn in any season, it can captivate both young and old, but only those who are willing to be captivated by this love play ;-) Longevity is remarkable, as an intense variant should be! Sillage is moderately good. Floral like the other musc fragrances, but the rose comes out more and more prominently in this version. I really like it :-)

As an absolute fan of clean/laundry scents and musk, I've been eyeing the classic Essence for a while now. If it hadn't developed so strongly soapy on my skin, it would have been in my collection a long, long time ago :) Additionally, it was a bit too present for me during the first two hours. Even my mum, who hardly perceives any scents, asked me if I had looked a bit too deeply into the (fragrance) bottle... At that point, it had already been 1 1/2 hours since I sprayed both scents on my wrists for a direct comparison. Now for the comparison... How does Musc Collection Essence EdP Intense smell? Unmistakably related to Essence. Also very clean, also very fresh, with the rose dominating the opening along with the musk. (I can't identify other flowers exactly, but you can tell it's not just the rose.) It's like pressing your nose directly into freshly washed bed linen :) However, Intense is a bit softer, more floral, and quieter. At first, I could hardly perceive it because my other wrist was so dominant. I was already thinking, "So this is supposed to be Intense? Intense is probably just the price difference, right?" I was even a bit disappointed... Now, half a day later, the classic Essence has completely left me. Nothing! No trace! But Intense is still there :) Warm, soft, fresh, and clean... Simply beautiful! Come cuddle! Freshly showered with a rose shower gel and delicate, baby-smooth freshly shaved skin in a freshly made bed; the fabric would be associatively white silk, and you can feel how the body heat warms the fabric.... So beautiful and right at the top of my must-have list :)

This is the first scent I tried from the Oriental Musc Editions. I was a little surprised that this isn't very musky at all. It neither has the typical musk of the For Her line, nor the one that is used in the Narciso line, nor any other kind of dominant musk. It could be from any designer and doesn't smell like a typical NR fragrance, and it's lighter than what I expected from the presentation. Which isn't necessarily a bad thing, I don't think that heaviness would suit this scent profile. Musc Jasmine is a sweet white floral, very on par with current trends. The titular jasmine is really noticeable and nicely done, it smells similar to a blooming jasmine shrub, but slightly cleaned-up. Tuberose and vanilla are also going strong in this one. Besides that, I also get a sweet fruity note that is a bit reminiscent of white gummy bears, but blended with the jasmine it doesn't come across too playful, at least not after the first blast has cooled off. Maybe it's just a fruity rendition of ylang-ylang. There is something about this that reminds me the tiniest bit of bdk Pas Ce Soir, even though the overall scent isn't very similar. All in all it's a nice fragrance, as long as you don't expect a musk bomb like the mainline NR perfumes.

Oriental, delicately melting, and warm! This is exactly how I perceive my latest acquisition "Jasmine Musc | Narciso Rodriguez." For me, it is the most beautiful jasmine scent I have ever had the pleasure of smelling. Just one whiff and I was instantly in love! To me, "Jasmine Musc | Narciso Rodriguez" represents a beautifully fragrant, almost graceful princess from the Orient, who enjoys her evening stroll at sunset through the flower garden of her palace. Her skin glows in the evening light in soft gold, and her long white dress flows majestically like a veil over the sea of flowers. A gentle breeze awakens the scents of the floral diversity of jasmine and gardenia. The "Jasmine Musc | Narciso Rodriguez" truly melts warmly on the skin only through the harmonious support of woody notes and a ripe, noble vanilla component. A truly successful masterpiece in every respect. A scent to feel good, a scent for going out, for everyday life, summer evenings, cold winter days, or simply to feel particularly beautiful and feminine, this scent is always suitable and shines as bright as can be! Its longevity (at least 10 hours) has proven to be more than reliable. I will never let you go!

... I received my sharing sample today and thought while unpacking: hmm, you know this from somewhere! Then I put a tiny drop on my wrist and kept wondering: Where do you know this from???? Suddenly it hit me: The Righteous Butter by Soap & Glory. Soap & Glory is a British cosmetics brand that was quite popular here for a while - with the British drugstore counterpart (blue writing and starts with B), the brand is still extremely big today, as the quality is great. Anyway, I had imagined something "more feminine" with "Jasmine Musc | Narciso Rodriguez" - sweeter and so, well, you know how expectations are. What I "received" is a very nice unisex scent - that is neither too sweet nor TOO harsh - creamy, a little fruity - and in the drydown totally "diverse". A scent I would find great on anyone - BUT please not with 20 sprays! Please, max 3 sprays if it absolutely has to be and then stay at home for 5 hours - personally, I would otherwise feel nauseous (this scent really hits my stomach at first). I believe this scent has a chance at a BEAST Oscar 2022 - so better take less right away and maybe add 1 or 2 DROPS (a small TZ or vial can be carried in anyone's pocket - no, the scents don't spoil after 2 hours, they last a few days like this) For me personally, unfortunately not a bottle candidate - but this shows once again how one can be mistaken =) Update: to be honest - somehow I am totally unsure now with the S&G scent ... but I know this scent!! Help =)

THIS is supposed to be JUST a beard and after-shave care product? NOT at all, and if someone likes, they can apply it to their chin and cheek. For me, THIS is a fragrance! And a magnificent one. It feels as if I suddenly stand in a damp piece of forest, with herbs and ferns among the trees, a few flowers in the brighter spots. Wild azaleas, rare and fragrant (especially the leaves), dog roses (Rosa Carnina), damp puddles surrounded by irises, blue like midnight, spreading powdery aromas. Bark and forest soil, mosses growing on old trunks. In terms of "intent," this area could be somewhere in southern England (images from a beautiful documentary about it are vivid in my mind). When the damp fog rises in autumn, it is still pleasantly mild. This is when scents can particularly stand out, as the mild moisture holds them and carries them far. Meadows between the forest patches send herbal aromas around, a green-bitter medley of the finest kind. I would love to travel there once and experience the beautiful southern English countryside in person (a vacation consideration worth pondering after the pandemic). Until then, I use Melograno whenever I feel like it. Even if I don't have a "facial hairstyle" or need to shave ;-))

Uncommented Fragrances No. 155 My father was already over 40 years old at my birth, having been forced into war at 18 and soon ending up in Russian captivity. He was fortunate to have had not only terrible but also good experiences, and he maintained a love for Russia that some contemporaries found inexplicable throughout his life. He spoke Russian, traveled with my mother to Moscow and Leningrad in the 80s (not a given during the Cold War), regularly listened to Radio Moscow, used Russian Leather as aftershave (even though it came from Farina in Cologne), but he was not a Russian spy, as some might now speculate. I also have a strong sympathy for things with a Russian label. "Russa," like Russian Leather, does not come from Russia but from sunny Italy, specifically from one of my favorite brands: Santa Maria Novella. The fragrance house from Florence traces its history back to the founding year of 1612, with some fragrance formulas allegedly being even older (such as the simple Colonia of the brand), as the historically documented Farmacia goes back to a monastery pharmacy from 1221. This would make it the oldest known pharmacy in the world. I also appreciate that all products, including those from the cosmetics line, are made without animal testing, using only natural herbs and lipids. Recently, there is also a flagship store in Munich, Germany (mdc-core.de). Moreover, I was once again looking for a new aftershave, preferably natural cosmetics (see my collection 'Grooming'). I have had particularly good experiences with many monastery products for sensitive skin (e.g., Lotion Opaline, Caldey, Ganagobie), and this is also the background of my sympathy for Santa Maria Novella, even though it is no longer a monastery manufacture. Thus, there are quite a few good reasons to test the After Shave / Dopo Barba Russa from Santa Maria Novella. This is not a Russian Leather product with birch tar, resins, or an amber base, as is often the case, but rather a light yet quite spicy product, similar to Cologne waters. Citrus, bergamot, petitgrain, and green notes represent hesperidic freshness like in a Cologne / a light Cologne, while the clove adds a dark hue and the Russian temperament (caution: stereotype!). Benzoin should represent a resinous-balsamic base note, and it does, but not as strong as some might expect; instead, it is very subtle, very weak, more underlying. Both fragrances fit well into my collection of Black Colognes (see there).

Narciso stands for a modern fragrance, and this one was supposed to be a floral-woody scent like a radiant bloom unfolding its fragrance in the moonlight. But it backfired. The warm, floral scent of the jasmine tea accord is intensified by the fruity notes of white peach. At the heart of the fragrance, tuberose and jasmine combine into a very strange composition where you no longer know what you're getting. Cedarwood and musk save the fragrance a little as it becomes creamy after a while. But despite everything, it is neither one thing nor the other. Such a pity! The bottle also leaves much to be desired.

I was able to snag a bottle of the oil at Do*glas and thought it had that wonderful DNA from Rodriguez. Unfortunately, that is not the case. On me, it only smells like fresh, real lily mixed with urine. It only changes in the first few minutes and then stubbornly stays where I applied the drop. The longevity is enormous for that. Despite trying to wash off the scent, it really lasts more than a day on my skin. Applying a fragrance oil is definitely different from wearing a scent. But I like this, and I find it interesting that there is no sillage around you, but rather an intimate scent that you can only smell at a closer distance.

I got to try the scent at the airport in Duty Free on a test strip. I sniffed the strip the whole flight home, wonderful. I was already annoyed that I hadn't sprayed the scent on my skin. At home, days later, the scent was still detectable on the test strip. So the perfume had to join my collection. The perfume has a pleasantly light powdery scent, quite pleasantly smelling of patchouli, white flowers envelop you and it ends with a warm, cozy vanilla. The scent is really long-lasting on my skin and the sillage is a dream.

Patchouli Musc is a great fragrance. Patchouli is beautifully soft here. Not scratchy and only minimally earthy. It is slightly damp-earthy and paired with this wonderful vanilla. At first, however, there is a burst of spices, but everything is nicely balanced!!!. Such a beautiful scent. I have always been cautious with patchouli fragrances, but this one is top-notch. I can only recommend it. It has won my heart!!!

After being a big fan of Narciso's Amber Musc, I was quite eager to test the Patchouli Musc. That's why I was very diligent in the fall and pulled out all the stops to make this "supposedly" beautiful little fragrance my own. In my mind, I envisioned myself, on lovely winter days, cheating on Amber with Patch. I think when Patchouli Musc is on the label, one should expect it to take center stage, and this is exactly where the problem lies. Up front, I perceive oriental, sweet spices layered over vanilla. Undeniably, there is patchouli and musk, but they do not make a breakthrough, and thus I had a different expectation of what was ultimately presented to me. Longevity, sillage, and bottle design are worthy of an oriental; the scent, like everything in life, is a matter of taste.

this is perfect as an easy-reach, go-to vanilla for everyday. it's got a brightness (almost a slight bubblegum quality) that keeps it light enough for warmer weather and daytime, but the depth from the cashmere that makes it perfect for cold nights too. it's just such a cozy, sweet scent. it's nothing complex or mind blowing, but it's the kind of scent i can't imagine anyone disliking. i reach for bare vanilla or one of its many flankers as my daily scent all the time. i just wish it was stronger--for a vanilla cashmere scent, you'd think it would last longer and project more.

I finally found one - a fragrance that got me a compliment from my boyfriend! I switch out my perfumes and fragrance mists every single day, and he never seems to notice. I bought this last year and after I sprayed it on myself for the first time, my boyfriend told me I smell good and asked me what it was. It's a keeper! It really is a more straightforward vanilla, the gourmand is there, but it's not too heavy. I've found my new go to scent for the forseeable future. It's one of my true loves and I buy every flanker they release.

This smells like straight-up vanilla extract used for baking. If you like vanilla scents, you really cannot go wrong with this. It also lasts a decent amount of time, especially considering it's only a body spray. I mostly use this for layering whenever I wanna sweeten up a perfume just a little. My most recent obsession has been layering this with Montblanc's "signature"! This combo will have you smelling like a delicious sweet vanilla cupcake with lemon-flavored icing!

I get glorious rich vanilla and cashmeran and nothing else. The vanilla is sweet but not sickly so and the cashmeran is not overdone as I have smelled it in fragrances where it was stronger than it needed to be. It is basic in a way that I love to embrace, it is liked because it is likeable. I love to wear this post shower and pre-bed, it makes me feel warm, cozy and cuddly.

I am picky when it comes to the perfume I will wear as I have a very sensitive sense of smell, but this is one of the few perfumes that I can stand throughout the day. I love how warm and cozy the scent is, and one compliment that has stuck with me is that I, "faintly smelled of skittles." Definitely a fun thing to be told! When it comes to sweet scents like vanilla, it can be easily overpowered and thrown into the "sickly sweet" category, but this perfume isn't like that. It is just a simple vanilla scent. My only downside is that on the initial first spray(s), it does have a bit of a chemically smell, but after waiting a tiny bit, it goes into the vanilla scent that is enjoyable and not headache inducing.

Actually, I have always kept my distance from this brand. (I have never bought anything from them.) I actually didn't purchase this scent (and the body lotion) in a VS store, but simply bought it in a Müller. I must confess...my vanilla addiction is currently just too strong.

I never thought it would happen, but now it has! I have fallen in love with a body spray!!! I am generally skeptical about body sprays, as they have not been able to compete with an EDT in my experience, and I rarely feel like spraying myself all over.

Vanilla body spray with a slightly burnt scent note and relentless longevity, which requires careful washing off if you don't like it (I wish Victoria's Secret had sent me one of their angels along with the spray to take care of that for me ...).

Yes, there are better vanilla scents and also higher quality ones. But this one has its own unique charm. When I've been sick in bed for a few days and want to feel human again after a shower, or when I just want to smell good without thinking too much, I use this one with the matching body lotion. In combination, it even lasts for a few hours.

I have already bought a second bottle because I have fallen so in love with the Bare Vanilla Body Spray from VS! It is perfect for layering with vanilla perfumes or soft floral scents. Due to the relatively simple notes, the body spray harmonizes very well without being dominant.

Saffron Musc is a really beautiful scent, I love the saffron note - it is warm and luxurious. The musk adds depth and elegance. However, for me personally, the fragrance is too masculine, so I wouldn't wear it myself. Still, it is an interesting perfume for anyone who enjoys strong, spicy musk scents. Great fragrance that I wouldn't wear myself, but definitely recommended for fans of masculine, noble scents.

The fragrance is new, and I usually approach completely new scents with skepticism: after all, I am the one who prefers classics and modern classics, while also having real difficulties with newer and more current fragrances and scent directions. I absolutely cannot stand oud. Now everyone is into cannabis. Well, trends have always existed. I've mentioned this in other reviews and examined it more closely. And it has to be that way. Many things come back in parts, repeat themselves, some are brought back - in fashion, music, perfumery, in designs… it has to be that way. Somehow, the wheel is not being reinvented, but it is always being pimped (to use this neologism). Well, today everything is so loud, present. Fragrance is a status symbol. Status symbolism: I have a Rolex. I’m wearing a Moncler jacket. It’s boldly displayed everywhere. Over the Stone Island sweater, whose emblems are, of course, impossible to overlook. The pants fit the outfit - shoes, Gucci? Balenciaga? Not pretty, but eye-catching? And yes, exactly, the fragrance must reach everyone. Everyone! Whether my fellow humans want it or not. It doesn’t matter (to many perfumed wearers in the cinema, gym, or on the train…). Because(!) - that’s what people probably think - I can afford the most extreme and loudest oud, the heaviest scent that Mr. Gebauer has in his collection, or the sweetest temptation, against which the old Givenchy scents look like orphans. Unfortunately, I find: There is nothing fine and private left; just like it used to be. When a girlfriend back then said you smelled good (after getting closer) and not from 7 meters away. Safran Musc is also modern (you can tell) and more potent than scents from the 90s or 00s, but it is not annoying or omnipresent in the room. It has that certain something. Fineness, beauty, classic. It reminds me of the classic leather bag. One that has existed forever but is still modern. It tops and enhances every modern outfit because it shows that the wearer has class and style. That they know how to incorporate stylish timelessness into their appearance. That is this fragrance. An old library. A classic leather armchair. A cool antique desk in my home office. Heavy and massive, yet timeless and cool amidst all the new, between Ikea and Co. Musk, saffron. Especially the saffron is simply there. The name is program. The fragrance accompanies its wearer. It gives them aura, carries them through the day, in what they do. But here, one wears a (great) fragrance, and it is not the fragrance that carries them. The gentleman (or lady, as every skin is individual, just test it out) enters the room and is accompanied by a fine, soft, harmonious, rounded, slightly(!) sweet-leathery saffron-musk scent that underscores the personality of its wearer. It is not the fragrance that affects the room, followed by the wearer. That fits, I like that. Pleasant, no headaches. Not too much leather or resin. Just a true signature scent that is independent enough to claim that title. Well, experienced label, they should be able to do it, and their classics have been on the market for many years - which speaks for itself. They have really achieved something wonderful here. The price is indeed steep, there’s no two ways about it. I would consider it worth it, but that is a personal decision. Currently, it is quite ambitious; perhaps one or another online retailer (of the well-known dealers) can come down a bit in price… let’s hope so.

I must highly reluctantly admit that I really like this scent. My teen daughter wanted a Victoria’s Secret scent for Christmas, and since I’m interested in perfumes I thought I’d go have a look, even though I have an instinctive aversion to Big Brand Perfume. I think I smelled every perfume they had in the store - it was superfruity this and megaflowery that. Until I tried this one. Yes, it was flowery and fruity like the rest, but it also had a clean freshness and a top-notch citrus tone that toned down the fruity flower potpourri. Whenever my daughter wears it and passes me, I notice that she smells fresh and pleasant in a quite sophisticated - but still young - way for being a teen girl. I would certainly recommend this to young women, maybe up to 25 years of age. A note is that I find the name a very good one for a perfume, but for this one it is highly misleading – a better name would be Fresh & Pleasant (which sucks as a name, but would be more informative).

It has a citrus scent reminiscent of an unripe peach. Citrus has a more peach-like tone. Although it is quite light, it offers average permanence and projection. Also, a herbal scent is evident at the opening (not fruity). I likened this tone to tree resin. It's more like a teenage girl scent under 30. Lasts up to 8 hours on fabric. It disappears on the skin in the first 3 hours. Projection is slightly below average. Longevity: 6/10 Projection & Sillage: 5/10 Fragrance Quality: 6/10

another perfume thats foundational, bombshell will always be good. bright, refreshing, fruity, flirty, very little to dislike about it. the fact that it's so safe may seem like a detriment but every time ive smelled this on myself or someone else all i could think was "wow this smells good" give this or any of the flankers a try. victorias secret just makes good perfumes! sorry!

Where's pineapple, strawberry and passion fruit? Why is it marketed towards women? I wish it was fruity. It's anything but! I get bergamot, jasmine, musk and a hint of oakmoss. In fact, this leans masculine to me, like a masculine body wash that's marketed as "Energising". There's freshness to it, the kind you feel when you leather yourself with a thick layer of body wash. I have no idea why i bought it, albeit only 10ml. And while i often like unisex and masculine leaning perfumes, Bombshell is not my cup of tea. Will see if i like it better on my husband.

You know that girl in school who was perfectly nice but not terribly interesting? Basically pretty, well liked but not super popular, ultimately inoffensive? She'll sign your yearbook with hearts and bubble letters and a very nice Hallmark-level sentiment but you haven't spoken like, ever? You have definitely heard her full name every single day since kindergarten during roll call and have never once remembered it? She'll probably become a dental hygienist or veterinarian and marry the first guy she dates in college? Her. Sweet, pleasant, simple, forgettable. Still nice to have around sometimes, though. -- This review previously appeared on another site under the name "PrincessPrickleson." That's me! I'm moving my collection to Parfumo.

Bombshell by Victoria's Secret is a fruity, tropical perfume, perfect for warm weather and beachy vacations. Being a VS fragrance, it's not very complex, but it's juicy and delicious. Imagine a Kern's brand Guava juice or one of those Guava Hard Candies; that's exactly what this smells like.

Bombshell does not fare well here. Most Victoria's Secret fragrances have only one to a maximum of two comments. They don't seem to be very popular. However, they do have their fans, as numerous YouTube videos prove. I find it a pity that Victoria's Secret does not ship fragrances to Germany via their homepage.

I received the perfume as a gift some time ago and liked it very much, but over time I forgot about it. A few weeks ago, I was out in the city and was amazed by this wonderful scent that seemed to mysteriously follow me.. Until I realized that I was wearing a jacket from back then and identified the scent as Victoria's Secret Bombshell. Since then, I am head over heels again!

The concentrated dose of fresh, cheerful mood lifters is immediately present here. Once tested and immediately deemed good. Anyone who is feeling down or unsure if they have a good summer fragrance at home should definitely try BOMBSHELL, as it is as soft and airy as a summer cocktail. Everything is harmonious and fragrant. It also smells a bit like melon.

A friend wore this fragrance and sprayed it on my skin. The first 15 minutes were meh, but then the scent unfolded and became the typical clean scent that I love. The longevity was okay, the sillage average. I find the bottle very beautiful, especially the black ribbon, which I think is great. This is a nice scent for home and for the office.

A successful blind buy. I ordered it recently; normally I shop in local retail. The scent is pleasantly floral-powdery. The currently high rating of over nine seems exaggerated to me, but it is definitely a lovely fragrance. It feels elegant and feminine, making it suitable for evening wear or going out. However, since it is rather subtle in this concentration, it can also be worn well for everyday and work. So, anyone who likes floral-powdery scents can't go wrong with this one.

this scent is so slept on, but this is one of my favorites from vs's core line, along with bare vanilla. it's more of a gourmand coconut than a lot of other coconut scents, which can pull really sunscreen-y/tropical. although this has a little freshness to it, it's also got so much sweet vanilla that it's wearable even in winter despite being a coconut scent. i tried it for the first time when my freshman year college roommate and i would share perfumes, since she had it, and i fell in love. i remember her and i going to meet some other friends, and one of them asking, "do you smell cupcakes?" i'm not typically a coconut lover, but this is lovely, and the performance is decent for a mist.

Chergui is apparently one of the best sellers in the Lutens line. When I test it and read the list of notes, I'm a believer more or less. I can make out the notes I'm told are there. Yes, there is hay, tobacco, musk. But lord know I've nearly derailed going too far into the madness of a 'list of notes'. 'Notes' are in fact suggestions. But what lies behind a set of notes is an intent. Does the list of notes describe? Or do notes try to convince, that is, lie? Somehow, despite the recognizeability of the notes, I'm not convinced by Chergui. Testing, on blotter and on skin, I say yes to the notes but no to the whole package. It doesn't suggest a Moroccan wind, as the fable goes. Notes aside, Chergui shares the sensibility of many mainstream men's fragrances of the past 10-15 years. The strategy, for want of a better word, is Creedian. Sell it as nich-y, but aim for the height of the bell curve. I don't mind the strategy. As I've mentioned about the current Guerlain line-up, the big sellers in a line should better the odds that the lower-selling oddball that I love will remain in the line. Either that, or the take-away for the perfumer is that the bell curve is a sales strategy and every perfume should should be a best seller. I try to be optomistic.

Chergui opens with a sweet dose of sugary hay. The heart notes appear shortly afterwards, showcasing a deep pipe-like sweet tobacco amber combo, with clove-laced honey and incense accents. The scent winds down with the tobacco and amber combo receding, while joining a pleasant musk base finishing off the scent's development. Longevity is quite good, with average projection. I am not a sweet scent fan at all, but I definitely like Chergui. The tobacco and amber combo is really addictive, and the incense just compliments it so well. I think the scent is very unisex and would work for just about anyone. I have only smelled a handful of scents from the house of Lutens to date, but I am quite impressed. Chergui is highly recommended to all, but a "no brainer" for sophisticated sweet scent lovers, IMO. It is a gorgeous composition earning an excellent 4 stars out of 5.

One thing that I love about Serge Lutens scents is that so many of them paint a scene so vividly in my mind. Chergui evokes the image of a ghosttown somewhere in the arid expanse of the American west, where a hot dry wind blows dust and tumbleweeds through deserted streets and abandoned buildings. I see this town at dusk, with the last remains of a blazing sunset. The feeling is eerie, but calm, and you can almost sense the life that used to inhabit the place. If this aroma were a color, it would be red - burning embers, spices and hot baked earth. Honey and amber lend a golden sweetness that offers relief from the dry heat and almost desolate feeling of this scent. Unlike some Lutens that I really admire but have trouble wearing (ie, Arabie and Douce Amere), I have no trouble with this one. It is a deep scent, but not overpowering and (perhaps owing to the musk) melds well with my skin. Just a beautiful perfume.

This isn't the east wind that picks up spices, dust and heat. It is the east wind that infiltrates nomadic tents and absorbs the odours of honey, tobacco, animal bedding and dusty iris and rose. Chergui is a cozy, dusty blanket seeping sweetness. From afar it stays linear, but as i am want to do when i wear this, i cannot stop smelling close and recognising its various elements taking turns at showing themselves. Moderate projection and excellent longevity. Try this in warmer weather as well. It blooms.

Wow! A thousand times wow! It is not often that I immediately am captivated by a fragrance, let alone a niche fragrance. I'm usually quite picky but when I received this bottle in a swap (thank you again Tomaz) just now and I took the bottle out of its very carefully packaged box, I got a very promising first whiff of what is inside this bottle. So, I took off the cap and sprayed some on, carefully. Just a little. Carefully brought this to my nose, exhaled a bit and then softly inhaled.. WOW! This has a note that I recognize from Santal Majuscule, only it's softer in Chergui. More round, and sweet. Most Lutens' I've smelled were very strong, usually too strong for my taste. But this, wow! I'm so very excited by this! When I picture a Moroccan desert wind, it makes it even more beautiful. I am totally captivated by it and I can't stop smelling my wrist. So yes, I know this has a vast group of people loving it but I was a bit scared that besides sweet it would have a particular note in there that would put me off. However, this is not the case. It's balanced nicely and the ingredients are pure. The quality is better than many mainstream or designer scents, though I can't imagine a lot of people disliking it. I think it's safe to say this is one of the more approachable niche offerings out there? I'm somewhat glad I did not get a bottle of Santal Majuscule, as I have been doubting about that one for a long time. I really liked that, but sometimes I felt like I didn't want to smell like that. But now, Chergui has come along. Bringing me that part of Santal Majuscule I really loved but in sucha sweet, round and refined way. I am a VERY happy man!

Most of the notes here seem sort of expected for a sweet oriental unisex perfume with massive sillage and longevity - the amber, leather, musk, tobacco, incense, etc., but I feel like the hay is responsible for that interesting little twist in Chergui's personality that makes it instantly recognizable. That stuff lying around the barn that horses eat . . .

At first try, the incense (or is it hay?) knocked me out and gave me a headache. The second time, it was still mostly incense but not overwhelmingly so. The third time, reapplied directly after the second, was LOVE. I don't think I have a lot to say that others haven't said already.

I’ve had a few weeks to spend cozying up to Chergui. The reviews and various online forum opinions are so polarizing. To be frank, the notes are a bit intimidating. I was at once curious and trepidatious about trying Chergui. However, nothing beats testing perfume to skin. And how glad I was! My grandmother used to smoke clove cigarettes.

I would like to write this review as a tribute to one of my top 10 favorites perfumes. Chergui means "Eastern", so you should expect kinda Eastern scent from this masterpiece, which is not only very rich but also so attractive and dusty like historical Eastern ruins.

Chergui is a beautiful fragrance. The name itself means "Eastern" in Arabic (????), and it is the name of a wind that sweeps across the Sahara desert and into Morocco. The idea here was to evoke that same wind, and all the various smells from the desert and the surrounding environment.

Initially, I find this to be a little offputting. There's a bitterness somewhere within the fruity notes that gives me the impression of sweat or body odor (Perhaps because this is 'sexy', it's an intentional decision, reminiscent of pheromones?) I'll try wording it a different way - it's an odor similar to peach schnapps, that vaguely alcoholic tang of peaches. Something about it seems a little... naughty. (Which is fitting.) The drydown is much sweeter and inviting - fresh florals, sweet vanilla and pears. Definitely pleasant, fruity and feminine. Also quite a 'flirty' scent. Like most Victoria's Secret fragrances, this one disappears very quickly from my skin. I prefer 'Sexy Little Things Noir' because it's a little truer to its name, and lasts just a bit longer than this one.

This is a scent that I would have worn between the ages of 16-25. It's happy, pretty, joyful, sweet. But it's not elegant, classy or upmarket at all. And there's nothing wrong with that. But I think you can find so many others like that for cheaper, in body mist form. However, I think this is an amazing perfume to start with for a young woman who is just getting into perfumes and starting her collection and wants to dip her toe with something linear and simple but still very pleasant. I have a small amount of this left and I will use it and enjoy it, however, the lasting power is really, really poor. I sprayed it on my clothes AND myself and two hours later, I could not smell it (nor could others, so I didn't go nose blind to it!).

I only tried Tease because I love Tease Crème Cloud so much that I became curious for the original. VS is not that easy to find in my country, so I have never tried the older bottles of this scent before. Well, this is soo pretty! It's very similar to Viva La Juicy, but it's better to me. The glossy caramel/praline base is my favorite part of VLJ, and it's the same in Tease. VLJ has strong white floral notes that come across as too sour on my skin and ruin the gourmand goodness for me. Tease on the other hand maintains the balance between fresh fruity floral and warm vanilla gourmand perfectly. It also has a lovely pear note that reminds me of fresh pear juice and really lifts the scent. My favorite VLJ flanker is VLJ Noir, which I own, so I also compared these two. Noir also leans warmer and more gourmand than the original. In direct comparison with this one, Tease is lighter and brighter. I never found VLJ Noir woodsy, but next to Tease, the sandalwood in it suddenly becomes quite noticeable. I don't need both, but I like them equally. If you enjoy uncomplicated, sweet and girly scents for every day use, Tease is a top choice.

Very fruity and juicy-sweet. Doesn't at all match its name, as this is not at all a "sexy" scent. Nothing about this is a tease - it is a linear fruity-sweetness in your face from start to finish. Smells like something from Bath and Body Works. Younger people and gourmand lovers might enjoy this. It is too juvenile for me now.

Sexy Little Things - Noir Tease gets 10 out of 10 stars from me. Why? This perfume is, in my opinion, the best fragrance creation among Victoria's Secret scents. I always associate the scent with London, one of the most wonderful and romantic cities on this planet. I first encountered the fragrance at the Victoria's Secret store on New Bond Street 111. A beautiful and noteworthy corner of London. What a city and what a scent, folks. This fragrance impresses from A to Z. It smells incredibly sensual and sexy with its floral and woody notes. And transforms every woman into a wonderfully fragrant and alluring goddess. Although I'm not a big fan of freesia as a fragrance component in perfumes, it doesn't bother me at all here. In my opinion, the perfume is not a mainstream scent but stands out significantly from other compositions. The bottle is so sweet, so elegant, so sexy, so pretty, and so mysterious... fitting to the character of the fragrance and perfectly aligned with the brand. Victoria's Secret indeed. A mysterious scent. For a mysterious lady. For mysterious moments. I am enchanted. Spread the word. :)

Arrival at Zurich Airport. Frostbitten. Tired. At least A380. Plenty of space. The oversized thing is never full. On the way to the underground train station. 20 minutes left. In front of the lift to the platforms, my gaze lingers. Victoria's Secret. Jet black letters stand out against a rich pink background.

It starts as a beautiful jasmine garden; a few other floral companions, a light hint of mandarin. The perfume is very pleasing, doesn’t take many risks, but doesn’t need to. It still smells diverse and is simply a feel-good blend. Vanilla and a very light sandalwood quickly become present and pleasantly envelop the subtly fruity floral magic.

I have the body cream and the body spray and the melon with the freesia smells sort of sour and tangy to me. It clashes on my nose or with my body chemistry. It is synthetic, sweet, fruity, the floral and citrus throw me off. It wants to be fresh and gourmand. It doesn't know how. I'm sorry I don't like this, but I don't like much out of Victoria Secret.

To express it in the words of the lovely YouTuber xKarenina, who got me hooked on this unbelievably amazing scent..! I love to generously douse myself with it or apply it on my body before going to bed. Definitely a recommendation to buy!!!!

I’m from a small town in Connecticut. Not, Suburban-New-York-Connecticut. New-England-Connecticut. In my 1960s-1970s, the New England countryside was a place of wonder and democracy. The woods were a frame of mind as much as they were a location. Though I never thought of anything local as particularly exotic, pine was the scent of local magic. Pine was the scent of outdoors and the change of seasons. It was omnipresent and always welcome. Fille en Aiguille’s pine is bittersweet for me. It is 30% sense memory and 70% longing. I now live in Southern California in a climate that I struggle with every day for nine months out of the year. Its climate is almost universally loved, but is unbearable to me and anathema to my pale Celtic body and spirit, a reality that is inexplicable to those around me. Fille doesn't offer me a solution to my dilemma. It doesn't give me relief from the heat or an alternative to the deathly brightness. It triggers memory, remembrance, beauty from an an arcadian past. It reminds me of the magic. And if there's magic, there's hope. But mostly there's just longing.

A richly atmospheric juice of burnt embers and incense; where woodbark, brown humus and evergreen leaves lie strewn with red sweets. No picnic in the woods this but Hansel and Gretel abandoned in the Dunkelwald (Dark Forest). A beguiling tour de force that resonates with something deep in the unconscious. (Fairytale inspiration courtesy of graindemusc)

Masterpiece, perfect in every way. The right amount of woods, incense and dried fruits for my taste, I find it a very sexy unisex fragrance, dark red and mysterious. Not for the daily use, just for those especial occasions, too much of a special fragrance.

After taking a few months off from my journey through the land of Serge, I decided to continue my search for the perfumes of this house which might work for me. So far I have not had all that much success, although I probably will be acquiring one of the triad FEMINITE DU BOIS, BOIS ET FRUITS and BOIS DE VIOLETTE at some point in 2014 (once my self-induced austerity campaign has come to an end). FILLE EN AIGUILLES was recommended to me as a "must sniff" and probable "must have". I'll accept the former of those two claims without argument. The composition is seriously dense and rich in much of what I find to be unwearable about ARABIE--the dried fruits and heavy souk spices--but it is tempered by a fairly hefty pine note. By the drydown, the blend smells pretty nice and reminds me a bit of L'Artisan Parfumeur FOU D'ABSINTHE in its somewhat Christmasy demeanor. While wearing this perfume, my mind conjured up a variety of previously disconnected memories. I recalled camping in the Rocky mountains as a girl with my sisters and dad (my mom never went because she hates that kind of thing). I also recalled eating Moroccan food on the Left Bank. What do these images have to do with one another? Until now, not a single thing. Now, they have been linked by Serge Lutens FILLE EN AIGUILLES. Once again, I find that a creation by le Grand Serge serves more as a psychedelic drug surrogate than a perfume which I would choose to don in just about any public venue. What I like above all about these oddball creations is that they force me to address over and over again this question: What is perfume?

The term "unisex" can often project a sense of ambiguity or hesitancy, but this Lutens has something markedly distinctive for men and women both. For men, it's the scent of the woods and fresh-split pine firewood, where a man can be proud and satisfied with his work. For women it's a celebration of a warm woodland's promising bounty and comforting acceptance. Lutens' fragrances can be wonderful and unique but difficult to wear at times. While admittedly distinctive, this is not at all the case with Fille en Aiguilles. If you are looking for a Lutens to suit your man, yet are reluctant to go with the safe-yet-less-distinctive Chergui, this is the one to choose. If you are looking for a warm memory of the forest in summer in a fragrance that's most suitable for Fall and Winter, this is the perfect one as well. Not quite as well-known as some in this line, but distinctive and comforting in a way that those who hope to claim familiarity with the Lutens line, yet have not sampled this, are missing out. Does it sound like, as a man, I have some myself, and find joy in wearing it? You bet. But not before my sister bought a bottle for herself.

While there are better scents from the house, I did indeed enjoy sampling Fille en Aiguilles from Serge Lutens. It starts off with a nice coniferous pine note mixed with semi-sweet candied fruit. The pine quickly recedes and the fruit remains, mixing with bay leaf and other spices along with incense.

Another completely evocative scent from Lutens. This is the smell of the Christmases of my childhood. This is picking out a Christmas tree with my dad at a roadside stand, with the scent of pine, fir and spruce in the air. This is also the smell of the air itself –fresh, crisp winter air.

I did expect more from Serge Lutens. This is not as complex as Arabie, neither as innovative as Ambre Sultan. For me it's just a spicied and incensed pine smell with low projection and weak lasting power. Updated January 2014

I think all of Serge Lutens' perfumes can be classified into four categories: 1. Very experimental and innovative, but difficult to wear 2. Simply good quality oriental. 3. To earn money, plain and monotonous. 4. Fille En Aiguilles Fille En Aiguilles is an unusual fragrance that is a bit far from what we expect from the house of Serge Lutens.

Am I the only one having associations with the Middle Ages and Gothic architecture after wearing this scent? When you enter under the vaults of the domes and feel the aroma of incense and heavy pine doors. What hairpins? I hear Bach, incense and the rustle of velvet. A rich sound, not for every day, but definitely for an opera or a concert with cool rock.

To me, the spray and body lotion smell like fruit-loops. It smells gourmand even though its supposed to be fresh. This smells better than Bombshell to me. One of the only Victoria Secret fragrances I like. I like Cherry Blossom, Jasmine and Peach. I also tried the "Candied" version of this expecting it to be sweeter but it was honestly more gourmand.

i got this as a gift about 2 years ago. i thought this smelled really nice, fruity, basic but a staple. for some reason, this has turned genuinely nauseating. smells like expired bathroom cleaner. some drugstore perfume smells better than this. idk what happened honestly. maybe the scent matured? maybe it saw the sunlight or something and went bad? i genuinely dont have an explanation for how this changed so much for me initialy about a 6, now a 3-4

Like the title says. It reminds me of going out clubbing when I started uni. It's a fun fragrance- sweet, fruity and feminine. It's absolutely delicious. It's a scent that lasts on your skin and clothes, and just smells incredible. If I had to choose one fragrance to wear for the rest of my life this would be a strong contender because it just doesn't get old.

What else can I say? It smells really, really good. It's one of the scents that made me realize I love a peach note in my fragrances. It smells fruity, sweet, and girly. I smell a bit of a citrusy opening that isn't in the listed notes on the bottle, but seems to be grapefruit according to the notes here. Yes, it's not a mature scent, but it doesn't have to be. However, due to their longevity, I would never pay full price for a VS body mist. It's fun to wear this scent out with friends because we all have strong scent nostalgia for it. Nothing like being a middle schooler and smelling VS body mists everywhere.

I absolutely LOVE this fragrance. It’s my favorite from all of the vs/PINK body mists. I own 9. The hints in it are Cherry Blossom and Peach and that’s exactly what it smells like. It stays on for a while and keeps me smelling amazing all day. I would highly recommend this. I love it

Bought the body lotion version. Really awesome fragrance. I feel fresh. I have very bad experience about VC body mist longevity. The body lotion is a bit better. Atleast the fragrance stays for 40 mins closse to skin. . The notes are good. The fragrance is better than Davidoff cool water women. But longevity and sillage really lacks lacks. Original price,

This smells just like the air *inside* Victoria's Secret! I walked in to test something (just in the mood to try something), and sprayed this...only to think...'This smells like...*here*.' It's soft. It's a little fruity and smells like like bergamot, but in a soft way. There's an indistinct floral undercurrent, but it's mostly just powdery and perfumey. Nothing is distinctly sandalwood about it, but it's soft, and feels like the texture of sandalwood along with plush musk. So if you like the way the Victoria's Secret store itself smells, this is for you. It encapsulates the overall vibe in one bottle.

I was so excited to try this because I love skin scents, and anything musky. I also generally love VS fragrance - but this was a major let down for me. All I got was a lactonic powder, and not in a good way - I saw someone else compare it to "baby vomit", which was similar to my experience. The dry-down also came fast, and all that was left was baby powder with no other notes. Based on the rave reviews from some, it seems this varies widely depending on your skin chemistry - so I would definitely suggest going to your local VS, to use a tester and see how it settles on your skin. Really glad I didn't blind-buy!

I was expecting a powdery, floral citrusy scent but i did not get that! I got a sweet ( but not a sugary or warm sweet), kinda creamy & bright citrus without leaning too much into a “citrus cleaning product”. Very light but definitely one you can overspray and get headaches from at the same time. Can have a “your skin but better” feel to it. Is it something new and never been done before… no. But is it a nice fragrance overall.. yes!

Update 3/11/25: I was wearing both the lotion and EDP in this on Saturday (3/8) and hugged my friend and she said I smelled incredible, and yesterday she told me her clothes still smelled like me so A) more positive feedback on how it smelled and B) more info on its longevity! 2/16/25: I happened to go into Victoria's Secret while they were running a sale and got a set with a lotion and miniature perfume and tried both when I got out of the shower. I then went downstairs for a snack and my roommate walked into the kitchen a few minutes later and IMMEDIATELY goes "you smell good!" so if they could smell me across the room while I was eating chips and queso that's a good sign. This is sweet and fruity and a little creamy and just so GOOD.

A very, soft and fluffy scent - quiet and inoffensive. In hindsight, I find that it lasts quite a long time, though with no sillage (as it never had any to begin with). This could probably be a good base for layering, it is not very powerful on its own. Musky with the light floral touch of violet, with only a slight synthetic-ness that fades after the initial opening. Overall a nice scent, but not strong enough.

I am surprised pear was not listed as a note. When I wear this fragrance most of what I smell is sweet pears with a vanilla underbase. I don't get much orange, but the sandalwood (though faint) is there. The sweetness level of this fragrance is mild, it is not sugary sweet or cloying but those who are not a fan of sweet fragrances might want to stay away.

The Bare line is the best thing to come out of VS in a while (along with Daring Eau de Parfum ). This is a nice neutral kind of scent that just has a smell of warm clean skin but better. The mandarin and violet aren’t distinct and the sandalwood is soft and creamy, not sharp or pickly.

I had this fragrance brought over from the USA and was not disappointed. At first, a strong fruitiness comes through, and in the drydown, I get a lot of wood with amber in my nose. I have to be honest, I don't wear this scent on its own. It's not exciting enough for me to wear it alone. I use it for layering with Libre, Tein de Neige, and Suicide Blonde.

During my school years, I spent quite a while in the same class as Belinda. Belinda was one of those girls you absolutely wanted to be friends with as a young girl. She was popular, athletic, always tanned, and had a way of charming everyone with her delightful personality.

Here I can only describe the body lotion, but I think if the EDT is like the scent Coconut Passion, then the comment comes across quite well. Amber Romance develops after application, but only later. Poetically expressed, it is a "scent of the winds." When I have my nose close to it, I don't really perceive it. However, with every movement, it leaves a hint of oriental seduction. It is more of a pure sandalwood scent. Black cherry and crème anglaise remain (at least with the lotion) strongly in the background. It works well in summer (I tested it in summer) as well as in winter. The sandalwood spreads a pleasant spiciness. It clings to the skin for a very long time and develops there in a very multifaceted way. Just give it a try!

Despite the notes listed and the name, this is not particularly floral at all. If anything I think there might be a creamy jasmine as a supporting player in the mid - but it's still subtle and mostly in the background. Instead, this feels like a beautifully-boozy marzipan. The almond portion of the booze-soaked marzipan does become slightly more toasted in the base - but it remains fairly linear, and has an overall sweet, creamy, and musky-ambery feel throughout wear. To my nose, this blend is perfect for cooler months. I get a solid 6 hours of performance, becoming softer at the 4-5 hour mark - but still impressive for a mist. The projection is not as loud, but the sillage is decent - leaving a lovely scent trail whenever moving my arms. Like other Victoria's Secret "core" fragrances that have been around for many years ( Bombshell Eau de Parfum , Bare Vanilla , Coconut Passion Fragrance Mist , Love Spell Fragrance Mist , Pure Seduction Fragrance Mist ), Velvet Petals also seems to have changed a bit over time. To me, the most recent iterations of all their core scents feel flatter, have less dimension, fade more quickly, and in some cases feel clearly more synthetic - so it's best to try them in store, and possibly look for an older version on resale platforms. With that said, my bottle is (and therefore, my review is also centered on) a version from 2021. I do think this is one worth hunting down an older version of, as there's a noticeable difference to me (in the ways mentioned above) between what's in store now and the older bottle I own. If someone shares images of the bottom of their bottle, you can use this code on a batch code checker site to figure out when it was manufactured.

absolutely love this one. i didn't actually purchase it until really recently since i have snowflakes and cashmere, which is very very similar, but this is just a bit fresher and more floral. it's a perfect year-round scent that's got enough depth for cooler weather but enough floral freshness for spring. it smells a bit generic but it's also got a creamy depth and a general coziness that's hard to dislike. it's perfume-like but sooo cozy and lovely. longevity and performance are on the stronger side for victoria's secret's mists surprisingly too!

I bought he shimmer version. Fragrance is awesome. However I found it similar to the Japanese cherry blossom body lotion by BBW. However this does not worth the price. I bought it at 1000 in sale. Still it does it worth. The fragrance last for maximum 20 mind and that's also close to skin. Almost 0 projection and longevity. Usually shimmer versions lasts long. But in this case shimmer version id performing like this.

I am not a huge fan of the Bare line in general, it’s just not for me. But when going to work one day and seeing this in the shipment boxes… my coworkers & I got so excited! We put the, out and i fell in love with this basically lol. It isn't a really sweet vanilla like i usually like, it is more of a woody, roasted & slightly nutty vanilla. It reminds me a lot of the Vanilla Bean & Macadamia VS used to have but woodier. I know people say it smells like Vanilla Skin, i don't get that. Vanilla skin smells like Bare Vanilla (the mist & lotion lol), & that doesn't smell like this at all. But definitely test this out if you can. Cause when we put this out & started testing it, on one coworker it smelled like straight cookies & another it smelled more like i how described it but she thought it smelled like smoke on her when she would smell her skin.

I fully tried this because of TikTok and I'm glad I did. It's so creamy comforting. I personally don't get any of the spicy notes listed, but I do get the warmth from the woods which I really like. The milk note feels more like a warmed cream to me, but the saffron keeps everything super light and airy.

Bare Sueded Vanilla is a really gorgeous vanilla that’s right up my alley. I’ll admit that I was disappointed when I first smelled this, because I’d seen it described as a milky vanilla, and I don’t get any of the milk, saffron or suede notes that I was anticipating. But it does have something of the texture - if not the actual scent- of suede to it. And once I came to appreciate it for what it was I didn’t care about what the notes were. I couldn’t stop wearing it. I misplaced my travel size and immediately bought another, then a full size bottle. This is easily one of my all-time favorite vanilla perfumes, and a standout from Victoria’s Secret. The Bare line in general is some of the best perfume they’ve put out in ages, maybe ever. Bare Sueded Vanilla is the one that strays the most from the Bare DNA, but to great effect. I usually find vanillas to be too gourmand, smelling like a Bath and Body Works dessert-flavored candle, or too woody (think The Architects Club , Bo - beautiful in their own right but not exactly a celebration of vanilla. This is what I imagined Vanilla Powder Eau de Parfum to smell like (instead of a coconut ambroxan bomb). Bare Sueded Vanilla Eau de Parfum is a delicious creamy vanilla and cosmetic powder scent, like Coty Airspun powder. It feels classy, sensual, and cozy and I can’t get enough of it.

This smells nearly identical to Phlur Vanilla Skin and DKNY Cashmere & Vanilla Essence. I have all three and while they are sooooo similar, Bare Sueded Vanilla is slightly sweeter. I’ve found that I don’t really like it on its own because of the sweetness, but it works really well layered on top of deeper sandalwood perfumes. Right now I am wearing it on Guerlain Samsara EDP and I smell like super sophisticated sugar cookies. It also works well on This Is Him! by Zadig & Voltaire. It just needs a richer base to elevate it. It is nothing like anything else in the Bare line. I haven’t liked any of them, they all have an off putting siliva type of scent to me, Sueded Vanilla however does not have whatever note causes that for me. While this works great in cool weather, it is horrible in the heat. Turns into a heavy soured vanilla milk that makes me nauseous. All in all, this is a mass appealing, creamy, woody vanilla at a decent price. I don’t understand the current hype as this scent already existed, but it is easily obtainable and affordable and you can’t fault it for that.

I smelled it in the store and smelled nothing. Then it blew up on social media. I have had a couple extra dollars so I got the travel size. At home I got a completely different experience. It’s a milky creamy lactonic lightly sweetened tea perfume. You smell the vanilla cream. You smell the milk and the saffron. You get a subtle tea like spice creating a warm vanilla milk tea. I don’t get any wood or suede which is great bc if I did pick it up I wouldn’t have liked this scent. I Combine my perfume with Rosie Dulce Milk lotion, Nemat Vanilla musk oil and Phlur Heavy Cream body mist. Last for hours. The main star of the fragrance is Bare Suede Vanilla. I get so many compliments. It’s my favorite date night combination too which is weird bc I’ve never think I’d like this for a date night but people seem to really enjoy the milky vanilla. So do I. I love spraying it before bed and waking up to smell it as I make breakfast in the morning. I can wear it all day, go out, come home, eat, take a nap and its still there!! I’ll definitely have to get a back up bottle bc I can’t imagine living without this elite clean girl vanilla perfume for less than $100.

...and that is, that she is now making high-quality fragrances. I stumbled upon a short video on YouTube by chance, which was about new trends in the perfume world. The conversation turned to this new scent from the Victoria's Secret Bare line. Milk notes are currently the hottest trend, so it seems like every niche brand has already released a milk fragrance.

~ This to my nose is what the true "taste of heaven" is! It evokes in my mind riding on a comforting smokey cloud of incense and pleasant lavender. It also carries my nose away to what it would be like to inhale deeply in the middle of an actual field of lavender with the early morning chimney smoke of a nearby cozy cottage rising in the background. This Sheldrake creation is definitely an all~season pleasant scent that is very safe and not challenging at all for me. As my first S.L. full bottle Gris Clair will make another classy choice as a personal pleasant companion during my daily chores of yard work, quiet times reading or even present an air of debonair with a suit and tie at my place of worship....how fitting for a true taste of heaven ~ Kind Regards, Platinum1 ~

I'll go somewhat against the grain in saying that the clean lavender opening of Gris Clair is the best part of the scent, IMO. It is a refreshing menthol mixed with a nice natural lavender that led me to think for a moment that Gris Clair was a rare exception to my "no lavender scents" rule. Unfortunately the top notes disappear in seconds, and then a powdery iris note (another note I can't stand) appears in full force and mixes with the lavender making the scent near "scrubber" material for me. The iris continues to build even further as the scent develops, making it more and more powdery and less to my taste. Finally, amber adds a touch of sweetness to the iris/lavender combo to finish off the disappointing development. Sillage is average, and longevity is well above average. This one started off with a lot of promise with its uncommonly appealing lavender rendition, but in the end the iris ruined it for me and made it a mild thumbs down overall. I could see iris fans enjoying this scent plenty though, so please do try it if iris and lavender are notes you enjoy. In my case they are two of my least favorite notes, so the odds of me liking Gris Clair were low to begin with. Oh well. 2 stars out of 5.

The Hilliard Ensemble is a British group of singers specializing in the interpretation vocal compositions from the Renaissance to the Baroque period. As I'm writing this review, I'm listening to their rendition of Johannes Ockeghem's “Requiem” and “Missa ´Mi-mi´”. The Ensemble's interpretation is divine: incredibly soft, pure, meditative, ideal for a quiet winter evening spent by the fireplace, preferably with a glass of mulled wine to lift one's spirits a bit higher. I started this review by mentioning the Hilliard Ensemble because lately I've been trying to match various musical compositions and styles with appropriate fragrances. I once sprayed on Serge Lutens' “Gris Clair...” while listening to the aforementioned CD, and was amazed at how effortlessly the music and the scent complemented each other. “Gris Clair...” is a melodious interplay between two notes, namely lavender and tonka bean. Thanks to the lavender, the head of the perfume is markedly herbal and aromatic. The lavender note provides a generous amount freshness to the perfume, evoking the feeling of genuine joy. Gradually, the herbal character of “Gris Clair...” is toned down and substituted by the spicy sweetness of tonka bean. The initial feeling of joy is transformed into nostalgia, meditation, even a longing for the unattainable. Lurking somewhere in the shadows of the fragrance's two stars is iris, so delicate it's barely perceptible to my nose. Due to its straightforward, aromatic freshness in its opening, “Gris Clair...” initially displays a different character to the other perfumes I've sampled from the Serge Lutens line thus far. Simultaneously, it is firmly embedded in Lutens' olfactory philosophy owing to its emphasis on the quality of raw materials, substance and the belief in the artistic value of perfumery. “Gris Clair...” might never become the most celebrated Lutens fragrance, but it surely is, just like medieval polyphony in music, one of his most comforting ones.

Lavender and I are not the closest of friends when it comes to perfume. For some reason the note often strikes me as harsh and sharp. My favorite lavender scents have been smoothed out, but even the best of the best I consider for the most part to be aromatherapeutic inducements to sleep. I also bathe HRH Emperor Oliver in lavender bubbles because it seems to calm his nerves. Given my attitude toward lavender, it might seem that I would not take very well to Serge Lutens GRIS CLAIR, which opens with a pretty powerful blast of an ink-like dark purple lavender. It's strong enough to evoke vague memories of the essential oil concoction offerings from the house of Lush. Fortunately this composition is not intense and caustic as are some of those--I don't feel my nasal passages burning! A rich iris note comes forth with more force as the perfume dries down, but the lavender in GRIS CLAIR really covers everything up in the opening, and remains dominant throughout the duration of a wear. After the somewhat strong, almost lavender-oil opening, GRIS CLAIR swiftly settles down to a smooth ambergris lavender layer. I thought initially that the base was musk, but apparently it is ambergris. In any case, the texture coheres with my concept of ambergris: similar to a supple metal mesh. While wearing this creation earlier today, I thought of Gandini LAVANDA ED AMBRA ORO, so I decided to compare them side-by-side. Despite the vast differences in the other notes listed in the official hierarchies of these two creations, the lavender and the amber are dominant in both. Where GRIS CLAIR features "old wood", LAVANDA ED AMBRA ORO features patchouli. They are closely enough related compositions that anyone who likes GRIS CLAIR would probably like LAVANDA ED AMBRA ORO, and vice versa. GRIS CLAIR is better, I believe. There is something appealing about this rich layer of ambergris and lavender embellished with iris, and I understand why so many people love this composition. For me, the inky lavender is a bit too strong, but GRIS CLAIR is nonetheless more appealing to me than some of the other perfumes from this house. It's definitely one of the best lavender perfumes I come across in recent times.

Gris Clair from Serge Lutens makes me think of Moira Rose's observation in a later episode of Schitt's Creek, where she's strolling along the path outside their hotel room and remarks to her husband that she "detects a scintilla of lavender" in the air. Gris Clair is several scintillas of astringent lavender, crisp linen, and sharp, smoky resins in a cut-glass crystal bowl. I actually love to layer this with the pillowy vanilla Lea from Calypso St. Barth's. Together these fragrances lend depth where nuance is lacking in one and buff out the bitter edges of the other.
