I only have a few VS perfumes, but this one is AMAZING! It’s reminding me of the OG Donna born in Roma, but ampted up fruity juiciness and minus the bourbon vanilla. It has a sparkling champagne quality about it too. It never turns too perfumey like others do. Very sexy, flirty, feminine. I already bought a back up bottle as it’s limited edition.

Much, much better than the original Layton. Unlike it, this has much more personality with that added oud and patchouli base to add some bitterness and complexity to what was a sweet mess. It kind of reminds me of Black phantom by Kilian. Don't buy this at a retail price, but at a discounter. It has a bitter, complex vanilla apple pie smell which interests me much more than the original, and may be worth a bottle in my eyes. To me, the added bitterness has entirely removed the shower gel nuance Layton gave, and really secures itself as a premium £200+ fragrance at retail. Sample before buying, of course. Really great stuff.

before i begin this write up, I just want to say that i think this is a well done, and fairly unique fragrance, especially for PDM standards: this is not for lack of quality in either the blending or ingredients. but man this shit might just not be for me. my relationship with oud is fairly open, as im cool with it in my juice(you can say we're polyandrous) as long as its not the overwhelmingly dominant note in the fragrance. its not even in my top 10 of fragrance profiles, but i do possess and have tried other oud based or included scents that i enjoyed rather muchly. ok so the opening...is fantastic. i mean its really brilliant in the way it takes some (not all) of Laytons strengths and blends it with PDMs choice of oud; makes for a unique and sublime experience really. but that opening only lasts for about an hour (at least on my skin), and then its just straight wood. and ots really not even an unpleasant wood either, its just not my cup of tea. after about 8 hours or so, i feel like ive been going on adventures with Star Lord and the gang cause brother, I Am Groot. now, i am holding out. a sliver of hope. when i first smelled Layton, im gonna keep it funky; i wasn't impressed in the slightest. it smelled of a high end version of body wash in spray form, you know the kind they hand out in goodie bags at the Illuminati meetings. but as my nose has opened up and ive gotten a chance to lay my honker on other fragrances, i went back to Layton and came away intrigued and wanting to spend more time with it. the more i wore, the more i whore; wait, sorry wrong group. the more I wore Leighton the more interesting intricacies I picked up the more respect and adoration I gained for it so I'm hoping that exclusif is something similar. the longevity is pretty good as i get about 9 -11 hours, sillage is fine and projection isnt super loud but good enough. you can find this on certain sites for $200 and at that value or slightly higher, its well worth it...of you sample first. well you should samlle before you buy most of the time (blind buying is such a rush so i wont ever discourage that). again it's...it's honestly a great frag, just not for me.

If someone is deciding between Layton and L exclusive, then maybe my feeling about this fragrance could help them a little. I have both. I keep Layton in my bag for when I forget to spray myself in the morning. It's not a top fragrance for me, not even a top 50. I was looking forward to LE. There are about 5 seconds in common. It's an apple fusion of both scents. Next, LE turns slowly into the appley Amouage Interlude, where it stays for several hours. It's a dark, beautiful scent with a nutty, appley, woody undertone. Really great!

Applepie seems to be a common thread in the fragrances I really like lately. It’s a sweet comfy scent that just feels like home. Also the case with the first couple of moments with this Exclusif. Spray on and oh yeah that’s home. However, this turns fast. It’s far from the cinnamon heavy chrismas frags like Kilian’s "Angels' Share | Kilian" and PdM’s own Oajan . It turns into a great, powerful masculine woody powerhouse. It’s dry, powdery almost. There’s a candy in The Netherlands called black and white candy, that reminds me of it. All in all it’s a fantastic combination. Sweet enough to lure you in, serious enough to make a deal.

This fragrence is undeniably one of the best I've smelled in my life. It highlights a lot of great notes and gives each it's right. Also the vanilla in there is perfectly balanced and is just the right amount ! Its longevity is also great and my girl could smell it even after 8 hours of work in the car. It is my first horse but certainly not the last because PDM has certainly impressed with the complexity of this piece of art

Though I’m aware this is a Layton-derivative, L.E. is such an overachiever that it could have been considered for being anointed to a horse of its own. Nevertheless, describing how I experience this horsphaned (horse-orphaned?) fragrance is an easier job if done in comparison to the originator.

Compared to the original Layton, the projection and sillage of Exclusif is about the same while the longevity is stronger by a few hours. Online reviewers often describe this as a more mature Layton, and that is a spot on description. For me however, there's something that I personally find a bit too animalic, dirty and herbaceous- ultimately off putting about it.

When I first smelled Layton Exclusif, I thought to myself, ‘How can a fragrance be this masculine!’ It felt as if I was smelling an armored knight. At that moment, I believed it was the most masculine and attractive fragrance I had ever encountered. Back then, I didn’t know much about niche perfumes, so my nose was quite inexperienced.

To me, Layton EX and Layton share absolutely the same base. The difference is basically this: take away the minty note away from Layton and replace it with oud....what you will get is a less fresh and more earthy vibe from the otherwise same DNA. In everyday wear, replacing mint with oud makes Layton EX darker, more mature, less playful than the OG.

In the store I was deciding between Layton 125ml & Layton Exclusif 75ml. They were priced almost the same, this one had more luxurious box. Went with the Exclusif, used more than half of it, then gave it to a friend. Layton was more wearable daily, this was more dark and spicy, a bit sharp. Not for hot weather or for daily use. Evening out is the best purpose.

This feels like a blend of Vanilla Lace Fragrance Mist and Sizzling Vanilla (and Sizzling Vanilla feels like a mix of Fresh Cream Eau de Toilette + Bare Vanilla to me). If you've never smelled any of the above, Gilded Vanilla is a creamy, almost lactonic, vanilla-forward fragrance. The sandalwood isn't prominent, and is well-blended into the rest of the fragrance; just adds to the warmth (almost leaning a bit towards melted caramel). The jasmine adds a subtle, soapy-floral undercurrent to the rest of it to prevent Gilded Vanilla from feeling tooth-achingly sweet - but it's soft enough that this wouldn't be considered a floral fragrance. Vanilla Lace Fragrance Mist had a musky, almost incense-like depth to it, and Gilded Vanilla also had something incense-like on my skin that wasn't present on the tester strips. The longer I wore it, the more that element started to feel "burnt" - somewhat like the burnt dry-down I also experienced with Frostmelt . This is the closest fragrance from Victoria's Secret to Vanilla Lace Fragrance Mist since that one was discontinued - so Gilded Vanilla is definitely worth trying if you miss Vanilla Lace.

A beautiful vanilla-sweet scent highlighted by the gentle floral notes of jasmine. I like it even better than Bare Vanilla. It somewhat reminds me of Phlur-Vanilla Skin. I will definitely buy it again! Longevity and sillage are, as expected, rather on the lower side. But the scent is special and unbeatable for the price.

Those who know the Parfums de Marly house will know that their creations are named after famous horses, including Percival. However, Percival or Perceval is one of King Arthur’s legendary Knights of the Round Table. In Welsh his name is Peredur. One version of the legend depicts Percival as a thief whom Lancelot took under his wing. Having displayed the virtues of a knight, Percival was made a knight and invited to join the Knights of the Round Table. Percival became one of the “greats” of Arthurian legend when he was one of the knights to find the Holy Grail. Back to the scent, Percival will not thrill people who were expecting another creative gem. This is not in the PdM style. It belongs to the group of fresh and aromatic perfumes. The citrus, herbaceous, spicy, slightly musky but, above all, salty notes are very noticeable. Strangely, no one mentions the overpowering ambery facet, which explodes and persists forever. Resinous, musky, and salty ambroxan in a good way! Percival begins with a fiery blast of citrus and salty accords, with a masculine slant. The bergamot and the mandarin appear harsh with a briny twist, and I figure out some sliced fruits topped with marine salt. Despite aromatic and spicy nuances’ dominance, the pink peppercorn is pleasant, and the usage of the ambroxan in the recipe is clear. No question about it. The latter, herbal, and other nuances, cause Percival to be associated with other design perfumes such as Fierce Cologne or Legend Eau de Toilette , which ultimately all belong to the same olfactory family. On the paper strip, the aromatic notes are amplified, instead, the citrus and salty notes pop up from the warm skin. Moving toward the heart, Percival takes a dry twist and shows a woody edge on a citrus underground. Yes, the citric accord that gives it a very juicy burst stays with it for a long time. I get the creamy and fougére facets of the lavender, with some more complex accords that come into play. Animal musk, a little bit of spicy cinnamon, and a little bit of pungent coriander add depth to the fragrance, boosting freshness with a touch of spiciness. I also catch a kind of mintiness, yet PdM does not mention mint. From the violet, I do not get any powdery or dewy edge, while a slightly sweet and floral jasmin oozes smoothly. The musky, amber and spicy base blends perfectly with the other notes perceived so far, giving it a very consistent and masculine scent. I think there is a gorgeous accord of synthetic woods and musks that I find intoxicating, especially after a long day of wearing it. With this, I don’t mean that women who love the genre can’t wear it; instead, that it is very reminiscent of the barbershop genre without crossing the threshold of the classic cologne. There is a sort of smooth transition from start to finish, but the citrus stays vivid on my skin throughout. Any similarities with A&F Fierce? Percival turns around a citric and briny backbone, whereas Fierce is nearly green and resinous. To me, they have nothing in common with one another. Overall it is a fresh out-of-the-shower scent. Is it an innovative perfume? At all. It is a fresh, bluish, and clean type of perfume whose formula resembles cheaper designer fragrances that often garner a lot of compliments. Yes, this is mass appealing and incredibly versatile. However, what it does, it does it well. It’s a year-round scent that you can wear for virtually any season, occasion, and time of day or night. Still, I like wearing it from late spring to early fall, and mostly on summer evenings. For such a fresh scent, the fragrance’s performance is quite surprising. On me, the scent projects strongly for a few hours and lasts nearly all day long. Percival is ideal for the office and suitable for both formal and informal events. Again, Percival is a rocket of amber and ambroxan, so you must like it to appreciate all its qualities. I'm basing my thoughts on a bottle I've owned since July 2021. -Elysium

I used a similar title for Bleu De Chanel as it was the one being borrowed from, but this time I feel this is now from the perspective of the borrower. I don’t say this as a jab at it, not at all. As someone who enjoys blue fragrances I like what is happening here which I will explain along the way. And with that I say,… Good morning everyone. It is time for another test from the discovery kit of Parfums de Marly, and today’s choice is Percival. I am just going to jump right in to what you came here for, the scent. Instantly I get a good strong smelling fragrance that reminds me of a number of blue fragrances I either own or have tested. Some designer, some indie and some niche. The lavender definitely brought thoughts of Sauvage and Luna Rossa Carbon. Sauvage because of the strength of it, and Carbon because I am getting a little soapy smell from it. I get Dylan Blue from the violet but of a higher quality. I am also reminded of Legend, but not from Mont Blanc as listed in the similar tab, it maybe does smell like it but I don’t own that so can’t attest to that, I do however own Legend 2023 from Aaron Terence Hughes which I smell here. I also felt like I was getting a little bit of 40 knots from Xerjoff. All of this probably sounds like a mess but it’s not, I am just giving people an idea of what to expect. It doesn’t smell like one of these fragrances on their own like a clone or something but rather that the notes are reminiscent of the fragrances mentioned. Though it is not listed in the notes there is definitely ambroxan in this. Being a lover of blues I would have loved to have found this at the start of summer, because I love blue fragrances and this is way up in my top 3 blues from what I am smelling so far.This is the kind of blue I have been looking for, for a while. Even though I say I would have liked this at the start of summer I should mention however that this is a blue that I feel is very versatile and can be worn all year round especially because it is very strong and could cut through the cold air in winter without problem. If like me you are looking for a good quality blue fragrance to add to your collection and don’t care if you have smelled similar blues already this would be one to add to your list if you like the fragrances I mentioned. It’s not as unique as 40 knots but it has that kind of quality to it. If you are someone looking for something new you have not smelled before and already have a few blues you are happy with I think you should pass on this. Especially if you have Luna Rossa Carbon or Sauvage as the lavender is strong in this one. To you I would say try something like 40 knots by Xerjoff which to me is Xerjoff’s fresh blue take on their Naxos fragrance. After roughly an hour the strong lavender and soapy feel starts to tone down slightly and the violet takes its place giving me a closer resemblance to Dylan Blue. I am not saying they smell the exact same, just that is what the violet reminds me of but without the incense and some other notes that make Dylan Blue what it is. It’s close to the shower gel kind of blue is what i am trying to say and projection is not as strong as it was with the lavender up front. This is something I have noticed in Parfums de Marly fragrances, there are notes that like to dance around one another taking turns in the spotlight and when you think one of them has gone for good it will pop up with a cheeky grin saying hello now and again and if it was a strong protecting note that took its strength with it when it left it brings it right back with it during these periods when it pops in and out every so often. A while later something strange happens, the top note of mandarin orange starts giving off a slight sweet juicy smell to it which is a nice welcome that was totally unexpected. Once that has all happened I feel like the projection starts to fade and another surprise happens when the lavender that we smelled at the beginning comes back and brings that strength with it once again. So I have a little more to add here. I thought I was imagining it earlier but after a 2nd application with more sprays there is actually a mint in this and it actually helps cool the skin which I presume comes from the balsam fir. I thought I maybe had sprayed Sedley by mistake, but nope, Sedley’s spearmint is unmistakable. This is Percival for sure. I am getting a very fresh, cool mint with ambroxan and I think the cinnamon is just there in the background also giving this masculine feel to it. This phase of the fragrance would be great for a very hot day. Shame that it’s grey overcast here today lol. There is not much more I can say. Do I like this? Yes absolutely, I can see a number of my other blues not being used as much when I get a full bottle of this, oh yes this will be a full 125ml purchase for sure. Unless there is a sudden change like I had with Greenley yesterday which ended up leaving me with the smell of an Aventus profile for the entire day but instead of the smoke being accompanied with pineapple we had apple instead which made it a non purchase for me which is a shame as the first 3 hours were gorgeous. So far as a first impressions Percival has everything that I like from a blue in it , and the little dance of notes popping in and out makes it a little more exciting than the regular blues and of course the quality is good. I just beg it doesn’t turn in to a smoke only fragrance that I will be trying to scrub from my hands and wrists all day. I don’t mind smoke if it is mixed with some other notes, as long as it is not just smoke and a single fruit note all will be good. I will come back if there are any drastic changes that make me change my mind, but so far this fresh blue scent is smooth sailing. And I can come back and say that I did discover there was that further stage with the mint and cinnamon I spoke of and not a single bit of smoke to be detected. It’s a good day for Percival and a good day for me.

Percival is one of few colognes I own a bottle of, at the same time It's not one I would immediately think of as one of my favorites. The bottle perfectly represents the juice inside it: pure blue. Percival is a safe bet. It's a mass appealing, familiar, performant blue fragrance and it's the definition of "dumb reach". With Percival you know you'll smell good the whole day. That's why it's one of three full-sized 125ml bottles I've got in my collection. However, the reason I won't immediately think of it as one of my absolute favorites is that it's simply too boring in regards to my other colognes. It's not unique, it's not interesting, but Percival is made to be a mass-appealing beast, and damn straight it is. Therefore I think Percival is worth every penny and should be in your collection.

Percival is a great scent if your looking for a great spicy and fresh scent. The bergamot and mandarin makes the citrus really come through and the pink pepper, coriander and cinnamon adds a great spicy scent to it. It lasts around 6-10 hours depending on weather which is quite okay for being a lighter fragrance. Cant justify the high price but great scent overall.

How do you improve on a perfume that basically embodies the 00’s? That must have been the mindset of the perfumer. Fierce Cologne is fresh synthetic and it’s also very familiar. Not an easy task but PdM pulled it off. Whereas Fierce is very linear and keeps its freshness and Barby-like syntheticness its whole (short lived) lifetime, Percival shifts into a smoother, more lifelike version of Ken. It’s got a warmer, creamier drydown, a hint of cinnamon here and there, some florals too. My first impression was like, who would buy this overpriced copy of a cologne? Now I’m like, yeah it’s worth the price difference to go for a more delicate, more grown up version of a classic.

This is a true signature scent, can be worn anywhere, anytime. It is worth wearing in warmer weather. It is long-lasting, its projection is not bad, although at this price one would expect more than its scent being similar to A&F Fierce and Mont Blanc Legend. By the way, if it were a designer scent, it would definitely hold its own.

Girls love it, it smells masculine, not an everyday smell. People compare it wit AF Fierce, but this one has much better dry down, quality and longevity. I love this fragrance and everybody around me loves it. Easy blind buy. With other words, don’t look at the reviews who compares this with other perfumes.

This is one of the fragrances that got pretty much hate. Many people stated that this Pdm smells like a cheap deodorant. The "more polite" ones stated that Montbland Legend it's also 1:1 with this but with a lot more better price. I have them both so I can share a few words for each.

This fragrance is strange to me in that there is something in it that I want to smell, however the overwhelming ammoniated chemical assault on my aroma sensors is too much to bear. It is horrendous. This is like a housecat broke in to a fine art gallery and urinated into a recreation of the Holy Grail. Test with extreme caution.

When I first opened the 4.2oz bottle box, I was a bit disappointed as the fragrance reminded me of men's deodorant and had weak sillage/projection with no lasting power. I made a decant, as I do with all of my fragrances, and let the bottle sit for a month or so. Fast forward to the next time wearing it and I was very pleasantly surprised.

Chrome Peony is pretty...and exceedingly sweet. I saw this at a thrift store today and was happy to smell it because I had read decent reviews. To me however, the sweetness is verging on corn syrup, and smells of hyper-sweet soda with a hint of berry. However, the berry isn't tart at all, it smells like a berry punch, and I personally find it cloying. There is a distinct effervescent quality about this, but I personally never did care for sparkling berry punch or the type of New Year's fruit bowl types of drinks that this evokes. I do think it lives up to the notes, but my tolerance for hype-sweet berries and wine is pretty low. I passed on the bottle, but I hope it finds a good home

I have Blushing Bubbly since January 2023 and then I got Chrome Peony a few days ago. Compared to BB, CP smells heavier because of peony. It's easily suitable for cold days, gives a party vibe. Design: 10/10. Looks like a crystal Smells like raspberry lemonade Gives the vibes of mid 2000s - early 2010s

Sedley from parfums de marly reminds me of a citrus soda similar to sprite or 7-up. Sedley suits great for the summer as it it a very light scent with great fresh notes. It is a bit sad that it doesnt last that long on skin because the scent is really good. If you have the budget and you want a great summer scent this would be a really great candidate i would say.

I only bought Sedley very recently, even though I had tested and dismissed it a while back for smelling too much like a shower gel. I remember telling myself that it does not smell as expensive as it should be. Why I would pay such high price to smell like soap or shower gel. So I didn’t think much of it and shifted my focus to other summer fragrances. But after getting into the summer with its scorching heat, and after an immersive journey in the world of niche perfumes I found myself urging for Sedley to come into my collection and finally falling in love with it. I certainly love to wear it during the heat more than anything else I have, perhaps except for Torino 21. Both are perfect summer scents that you would love to keep smelling no matter how hot it gets. Anyway, Sedley is very solid and loveable by everyone, even when I didn’t love it, I still didn’t hate it at all. I prefered it compared to Greenley or Galloway. I believe that among PdM freshies, Sedley is the one to get. Regarding longevity, it cuts through those first 5/6 hours easily with a noticeable presence, afterwards it becomes a skin scent that can also be smelled easily in well ventilated surroundings.

Parfums de Marly has been on my list for some time to try and I tried out Sedley, amongst others. For me, Sedley starts off a little bit of lemon and mint, and maybe some grapefruit or something similar. Crisp and clean smelling to me. A little lavender pops up through the middle along with a bit of an herbal compliment. It warms up with a little resin. By the dry down it turns to a soft woody scent with fresh linen. This is good stuff, but it is incredibly boring to be honest. It's incredibly safe and can be a daily office wear type scent. It's a bit pricey for that AND what it is. It sounds negative, but it is what it is. It is a good, inoffensive scent, but almost to a fault in my opinion. Zero chances were taken in the making of this fragrance.

Sedley, a refreshing spearmint and citrus scent, is a mature and approachable fragrance. It stands out without being attention-seeking. IMO Bleu de Chanel Parfum is superior, but Sedley surpasses standard designer blue fragrances like YSL Y and Sauvage. Sedley is an excellent choice for daily and office wear. It is a perfect fit for spring and summer, but its versatility allows it to be worn year-round. Unless you’re an avid collector, Sedley may not be worth the price. There are many superior fresh scents available at a fraction of the cost.

I am going through a Parfums De Marly kit at the moment and after starting off with Layton which smelled nice but just didn’t project for me at all I was surprised to see that Sedley has a lower sillage score than Layton but there will have been votes before and after the changes in concentration so maybe that’s why. Personally speaking I am getting crazy projection in Sedley compared to Layton. When I first sprayed this I got that same association with Aaron Terence Hughes again that I had with Layton. I am positive they get their ingredients from the same source because it’s not that their fragrances smell like one is copying one or the other, but rather that you smell notes that come off very differently from when you smell them from other house’s products. Like most designer notes when you read them will all smell similar to each other, however with Parfums De Marly and Aaron Terence Hughes they both share those high quality ingredients that I am yet to smell anywhere else. This is why I think we see the two being compared in my opinion. I am going to warn you now and it’s kind of crazy to have to put this in a fragrance review,but with the experience I am having I feel like if you are reading this without having worn Sedley for yourself that I am spoiling what could be a wonderful experience for yourself, so if that is the case you may wish to skip the next paragraph, you have been warned. This is like telling someone the ending of The Sixth Sense but instead it is about the sense of smell and in this case also taste. SPOILER STARTS HERE This is a fresh summer fragrance with something very strong in it that leaves a bit of a funny sensation that I find hard to describe. I feel like I can reference The Sixth Sense twice in this review because that’s kind of what I am getting with this experience which is hard to describe. Let me try. It’s like whatever it is, is sat on a very fine edge between your sense of smell and your sense of taste, and while it smells really good it has a weird taste accompanying it, which you hope to yourself that it’s going to be temporary, and luckily it does wind down as suddenly this spearmint starts to take over and leave a lovely sweet minty taste in your mouth and smell replacing whatever it was that was bothering me a minute ago. I love this spearmint note, it’s like you have had something you didn’t like to eat and went and ate something like a Polo spearmint sweet with the blue speckles through them. It’s crazy in a good way like the fragrance knew exactly what was needed and came along and delivered it on a velvet pillow but you had your eyes blindfolded as it was introduced to you both in your mouth and your nose. This is an amazing experience wearing this for the first time when none of this is expected. This is the kind of experience in fragrances that make you keep looking for your next big thrill and Sedley delivers 100%. SPOILERS OVER. I recognise other blue fragrances in the background of this, something close to a Sauvage/Luna Rosa Carbon kind of smell or actually speaking of Aaron Terence Hughes it reminds of his Legend 2023 with some spearmint on top. I am actually surprised there is no apple in the notes because i feel like I get a real sense of a juicy sweet green apple blended in with that spearmint. If I recall correctly I think I have seen people also compare this with EROS but I think this is a much fresher fragrance that can be worn easily in higher heats than what EROS EDT could be worn in at least. I can’t speak for the EDP or Parfum but I do have EROS FLAME and I would say they both have their uses. EROS FLAME can be worn in high heat but it is a different fragrance from Sedley and you don’t get that amazing experience I talk about in the spoiler section. I love that I can even say that about a fragrance. Sedley to me is a more natural mint fragrance than EROS and with what I have experienced so far I have to say that I was recently talking about when I run out of EROS EDT I would buy the stronger concentration but they are said to be a fresher experience without the heavy thick vanilla which is what divides the EDT and FLAME for me but so far on my testing of Parfum De Marly Sedley is definitely one that I will be buying and is in top place over Layton due to the poor performance I had with it. So I would buy this first over any more EROS to be honest. This is my first time experiencing a nice sweet mint anywhere other than EROS and it is definitely something that I enjoy. It gives a very fresh, clean sweet, vibe with wonderful projection. I used to be a big lover of winter fragrances because they were deep, rich and usually very strong but this summer I have been swayed by many good freshies and Sedley keeps me swinging over to the light side. It’s great when you find a fresh fragrance that thrives in the heat and today it is a beautiful day here in Scotland. I had to pop to the shop which was full of people and as I walked through them all as I was leaving after being served I could feel the fragrance giving out this wave of scent that I know everyone had to be smelling from me. As i opened the door to exit with my shorts, trainers with no socks on, pair of shorts and the sun just beaming down with the slightest of cool breeze that is so refreshing even though the sun is that of a perfect temperature with no humidity in the air leaving you soaking at all, and as I felt the smell of Sedley coming off of me it was like this perfect moment that brought all those elements in to the perfect moment as I felt so much joy to myself. You know when you walk past someone who is dressed well, they are wearing the perfect clothing for summer weather, their hair is done and they are smiling as they just stride and flow in the warm weather and you wonder what is it that is making that person look so happy and just glowing. That is how I felt today as I walked out of that shop door. Like I was that person instead of me looking on wondering, I for once was the one in that moment and for that alone, this is an absolute buy for me. I truly wish i got this at the start of summer, but I will gladly buy this for the last month or so that we have left. If I am going to feel like that when I wear this? Oh yes it is going to be worth every minute of it. There are days when I think to myself that I have more than enough fragrance in my collection and that I don’t need any more until you get a discovery kit and something like a Sedley comes along and has you going, nah I ain’t finished buying more, not when I experience what I have in just a few short hours of wearing the Sixth Sense of fragrances. If you haven’t experienced it yet then I suggest you do before you see a spoiler. LONGEVITY Well this is saddening, what started with such enthusiasm and an amazing experience had to fall short only 3 and a half hours later I am already back to talk about longevity. This could be a batch issue as looking at the longevity ratings it seems about 2-4 months ago others were rating it low, but before and after it has higher ratings,but I have to go with my experience. Probably the batch. SCORES Scent 10/10 Projection 8.5/10 Longevity sadly Sedley gets a lowly 3/10 for the terrible 3 and a half hours that this starts to vanish after. I don’t know what to say. Read my longevity paragraph. Value for what I experienced at first was a 10/10 but after the longevity issue it’s a 5/10 = 7.5
This fragrance is masterful in the opening. It's not a clean mojito like in Torino 21. Instead, this is like a bright citrus with spearmint gum, not crushed mint leaves.

As the wormer days are comming (even that in Germay will will have to wait a bit for it) I am tending to use more and more fresh scents. When you are looking at the house of Parfums de Marly as a men you basically have 3 options: Sedlay, Greenley and Perciva. For me personaly Percival was not an option as I have the foconero from TIziana Terenzi.

Tried and true, this fragrance has been the backbone of many unbearably warm days and is simply a stunner. While its DNA is not ground breaking nor is its style pushing any boundaries, it stands confidently on its own within this genre through having its own identity. Olivier Cresp has created a wonderful, long lasting for its class, and highly versatile fragrance.

I feel like I’m taking crazy pills because I can’t find any reviews that mention the similarity with Platinum Egoiste. I mean, I love PE, so that means I think this smells great, but why the hell would I pay PDM prices when I can Chanel for cheaper? Performance is pretty similar as well.

I knew it was a freshie, but Frankincense is some serious stuff. Patchouli too. But WOW, first spray and I was blown away. After quite some time now. And I own many niche perfumes, and being a connoisseur for years. Did not expect this much longevity out of fresh notes in a freshie scent. Or any scent for that matter. And then the Frankincense and the rest of them.

this is the yummiest scent my nose has ever been blessed with smelling. its soo sweet but in a light and airy way, its not cloying at all. if i spray this enough, i can still smell it after washing and drying clothing. i NEED to find a dupe of this because when this gets discontinued, i think im gonna cry. pls lmk if you know anything that smells similar. update: this was my favorite for months, but it has started smelling off to me. theres something plasticky/playdoh-like that i cant get past.

The best explanation I can give is that the initial “kick” of the core fragrance is not there in this line. Instead you get a whipped cream scent with a “twist.” Example - fluffy, lactonic whipped cream with a Pure Seduction twist. This removes all of the screechiness of the original. unfortunately I didn't keep mine because the scent was not long lasting.

It opens with a crisp, almost astringent green-ness, as if in order for the scent to unfold, the rhubarb stems need to break to make room for what’s to follow. It is slowly but surely sweetened by the lichee and after a few minutes have passed to allow the top notes to shine, the star of the show walks in, sensually — the damascena rose. The rose’s classic, sometimes stern personality is softened around the edges by sweet, almost girlish peony and as the fragrance has had a few minutes to bloom on your skin, it’s difficult to place — neither too grown up, nor juvenile, it’s less sweet than the bottle and sugary marketing suggest, a bit of the juicy, verdant opening is still there… only one thing is for certain: this is not a basic perfume. It commands attention as a modern classic in the best sense — complex, surprising, and instantly recognisable in a sea of floral-fruity-rose fragrances. As the base unfurls beneath the floral heart, the scent becomes creamier and more grounded, gaining depth from woods, musk, and vanilla. A true olfactive journey from start to finish. Praised for its impressive longevity, which is quite rare in the floral-fruity family, especially among lighter scents — Delina is every bit a signature-worthy perfume. Worn generously, it can carry you through a moment as grand as your wedding day; worn with restraint, it becomes an airy, elegant choice for everyday wear, even at the office. Delina — a rose fragrance for those who don’t want to get lost in a sea of perfumery’s classic and some may say even overused note. The irony is, of course, that what is meant to be an unmistakable, personality doused perfume has been on everybody and their mother’s minds and wrists for the past year, original and dupes alike (a practice we do not condone). Thankfully, however, the “I’m not like the other girls” fad of the 2010s has passed and finding yourself wearing the same outfit as someone else in the room is no longer the end-all be-all faux pas it once was. The truth is, much like an outfit, a perfume doesn’t wear you — you wear it. You are what makes it memorable, distinct and entirely your own. We give just as much meaning to our perfumes as they give to us. So in a room full of 100 Delina girlies, be the 101th. Bring your own magic to the table.

A beautiful fruity rose. I’m trialling potential wedding scents at the moment, and this is the first one my partner has liked enough to compliment. There’s lots of lychee and rhubarb upfront, which then settles down into a powdery rose with undertones of musk and vanilla. It’s a very soft, pretty, feminine scent, which projects nicely and lasts well. Definitely a potential winner.

Since venturing into the community of fragrance enthusiasts and reviewers, Parfums de Marly has been one of the most recurring fragrances in my feed. I had never heard about this fragrance house prior to that. The rave had me interested, but the pink, plastic-looking and very feminine bottle design had me doing U-turns avoiding it at all costs. I was creating my own sample set for purchase and among classics like Baccarat Rouge 540 and Oud for Greatness, I sneaked in Delina, just out of curiosity. Delina by Parfums de Marly is a light and quite fresh floral fragrance. I cannot distinguish any specific notes except rose. To be frank, it is an absolute disappointment. I understand why most people like it, florals are usually pleasing to everyone, but not me, which makes me more critical. What positive words I do have to say about Delina, is that it has a potent longevity and I could smell it on my skin all day. The opening note is a fresh floral, but the dry down revealed a soap quality to the fragrance that had me smelling like I just had taken a bath with a bar of rose soap. Comically enough, not liquid soap, but a realistic scent of a bar of soap. Oddly specific. Close to the skin, Delina is a little sweeter, but the whiffs I got during the day made me frown in displeasement. I read reviews and searched for the note composition, which to my surprise had many other elements aside from florals, but my nose only caught the smell of a wild rose Walther Rau bar soap. It is not the first time that I find myself not liking a community favourite, always a trick to be the odd one out, but I stay true to my words and thoughts and Delina will not be revisited by me anytime soon.

I’ve never been a fan of the overhyped Delina. It’s always felt far too rosy for my taste. However, in light of recent events, I decided to revisit this scent and give it a proper wear to see if my feelings had changed. By "recent events," I mean none other than Snoop Dogg declaring his love for Delina — apparently, it’s his signature scent. Now, let’s be honest: I’m pretty sure he was paid an obscene amount of money to mention it in that interview, and I’d bet good money he doesn’t actually wear it. Still, the idea of smelling cool and Snoop-approved was enough to make me curious. So, I spritzed it on and braced myself. Delina is still very rosy — no surprises there. It’s a powdery, soapy, clean kind of rose. What saves it for me is that delicious lychee note and, my favorite part, the sharp, citric rhubarb opening. That tartness is mouthwatering and keeps the rose from veering into vintage, matronly territory. For a while, it’s a bright, juicy balance that’s surprisingly enjoyable. It stays fairly linear for about two hours, but eventually, the fruity notes fade, leaving behind a dominant powdery rose and soap accord. In the drydown, the vanilla peeks through, adding a touch of sweetness, but it never becomes cloying or syrupy — just smooth and subtle. Performance-wise, it’s solid. The scent itself is naive, fresh, and flirtatious. I can see why so many people love it; it’s crowd-pleasing, versatile, and perfect for fruity-floral fans who adore pastel vibes. But as for me? I still can’t see myself wearing it — or Snoop Dogg, for that matter. Maybe if I smoked a ton of weed and got the munchies, I’d understand the appeal a little better. Who knows?

Personal: 6/10 - I don't love rose, I don't love rhubarb, but this is... tolerable. Mass appeal: 8/10 - Fruity florals are always popular. Rhubarb may lose some people, but it's pretty safe. Performance: 8/10 - Solid performance for a floral. It sticks around longer than I'd like though. Value: 5/10 - Expensive at niche pricing, but it smells like really high end designer. Not worth its price tag. Uniqueness: 6/10 - It's famous but not groundbreaking. Delina is a smoother take on the tart fruit, rose DNA. SCORE: 66/100 Full bottle buy? NO, not for me. It's wearable, but I'd never reach for it. Blind buy? NO, rhubarb and rose are a bit too polarizing to buy blind. Recommend? YES, if you want a high class tart fruity floral that feels designer. Date night? YES, feminine, pleasant, and romantic in a polished and bright way. Office safe? YES, but don't overspray it. It gets cloying quick. Pros: Polished, fruity, girly, fun, and smooth. Fairly approachable for niche. Cons: Overpriced, overhyped, and not unique. Rose forward, so not for everyone. Delina is the wealthy woman's go-to. It's expensive compared to some cheaper but similar designer fragrances, and the wearer doesn't care. She walked into Saks, smelled it, and bought it without asking the price. It smells like white dresses and white Audis in the summertime. It's rose forward, but fruity and fresh enough to make it approachable. It's just a high-end designer (but niche) rose. Good, but not great. *Review #53 in my fragrance journey - this fragrance I own as a decant*

On a strip of paper, this is a gorgeous fruity-floral that almost feels like a sunrise to me. On my skin, it's completely different and comes off mostly as dominantly carrot-seed in the beginning: a little bit bitter but fresh, earthy, and herbal.

If this perfume was a word, the word would be “Lovely.” First of all, this is a rose scent, very much so, for rose lovers only. It smells like a beautiful fresh flower in a luxurious mahogany room. The rose rests on a luscious woody base and is amplified by the incense, but it’s a realistic rose all the way, maybe even with a touch of essential oil intensity.

I had seen Delina being hyped everywhere on social media so I got curious and got me a 5 ml sample and wow. I thought it must be overrated and not worth the price but it really is BEAUTIFUL. I don't know if it's super unique but it is extremely long lasting (stays on my skin for 9+ hours) and very pleasant, not too strong and not nauseating.

By far the best way to describe this scent is simply "pretty". A very pink and classically feminine scent. I love the fruitiness and slight tartness added by the lychee and rhubarb. This is also a very clean scent in my opinion. Occasionally, as I get whiffs of it, it does come across a little like a fruity shampoo, but honestly I don't mind.

Delina is a perfume that I can't wear everyday, nor is it a scent that I reach for often at all. However, from time to time I have a "craving" for it. This perfume is unique compared to other fragrances on the market, or at least it was when it was first released.

I found this to be a flat, synthetic mess. I am reminded of Axe body spray by how generic and waxy this is. Whatever musk they use is so boring and none of the notes can be identified. It was nice of Victoria's Secret to try and make something less gourmand and perhaps a little androgynous, but this fell short of expectations. Perhaps they were expectations I should not have had.

it’s totally possible that I have Tease Crème Cloud on the brain, but I really get a lot of pink pepper in this one. It’s not listed as a note, but after the dry down it’s mainly what I smelled. It was actually very sweet on first spray. Once that settled, the pink pepper and sort of fresh earth smell remained. It smelled faint and seemed a little weak to me. If I'm totally off base here let me know! It seemed like it faded really quickly on my skin.

I get it that this gets a lot of hype and just because of that some people won't like it, but I really do love Greenley. The first time I tried it I agreed that it sort of just smelled like green apple shampoo, but after a little bit of time I really came to appreciate it. I am in the camp that Greenley is the superior PDM fresh scent over Sedley. It's citrusy, woodsy, and that mixture of apple and oakmoss just really works for me. If you like oakmoss and apple please try a sample of this. The performance is also pretty great for such a fresh scent, but the price is definitely up there. The bottle is also beautiful which helps make that price a bit easier to swallow.

When i smell greenley i get a strong apple note but not a sweet apple. I get a fresh and crisp apple similar to a green apple. I also get a strong scent of grass. Pure garden grass. Really wierd to smell but it does smell really good and fresh. Bottle looks really good and the price is high but i wouldnt justify it myself. Great scent overall.

this deserves the glaze it gets it smells like a dark mossy forest, personally i don’t get as much apple as others describe but the opening is slightly citrusy. performance is good for a fresher fragrance too i really enjoy this fragrance. it is slightly overpriced in my opinion and wasn’t what i was expecting but it grew on me and is now one of my favorites

People talk about 'shower gel' fragrances. I rarely agree with those conclusions, but this is straight up a rich mans Irish Spring. Don't get me wrong, it's beautiful - I don't know if I've ever smelled a better green scent...but it is quite decadent. It may even come on too strong, so I recommend trying before buying. This is something you could wear in the spring or summer when you're trying to feel bougie. I think as a daily driver, it would get a little bit exhausting. Worth getting a decant of for specific occasions, but may be difficult to justify buying a whole bottle. If I had a whole bottle it would probably last me like 5+ years.

Greenley is a goofball. It's a daft golden retriever of a fragrance - cheerful, crowd pleasing, playful, a little clumsy, and completely loveable despite the quirks. The hullabaloo with this one has always been and will always be the green apple opening. And fair dues, because it's great. Vibrant, punchy, juicy, apple-y apple. Does it smell almost exactly like Garnier Fructis shampoo? Yep! Does it smell naturalistic rather than synthetic? ...eeehhhhh...? But it smells really good, and it's a note that I imagine most people will find inoffensive, if not plain likeable. From there, you dry down into a nicely blended, pleasant, but not particularly remarkable blue-ish summer freshie with some green tints at the edges. On me, it stays on the blue side of things: not exactly aquatic, but far from mossy or vegetal. You've smelled stuff like this before. That doesn't make it bad, at all: it's good at what it does. But it just underscores why the apple is the killer feature here. I'm somebody who errs on the side of UNDERspraying: I wear my fragrances for myself, and actively avoid loud or heavy scents if I know I'm going to be around others. So I was pretty surprised when one of my friends picked this one up on me last time I wore it, especially considering he was standing on the other side of a cafe counter and was actively working an espresso machine at the time. I didn't think it was a particularly heavy-projecting fragrance, but he got it clear as day. So, be warned: this stuff is livelier than you might expect!

I purchased this as a semi blind-buy (forgot what it had smelt like) and prayed that it was something I would like. At first, you are hit with a crisp, fresh apple that is slightly mossy. This was not expected as I somehow remembered it sweeter. This lasted about 20 minutes before it transitioned into an unexpected yet pleasant petitgrain and cedar.

An apple orchard being treated with insecticide. I don’t know how else to describe it. I had high hopes for this. I now need therapy. It’s like a first date with a girl you think is awesome but then she farts and burps louder and more frequently than you do, it’s a no go for me.

I've owned Greenley for over a year and I'm writing this review because for the first time ever I am getting a new note and it's coming in strong, and it has given me a newfound appreciation of the scent. I've always known Greenley to be a bright green apple soapy fragrance and I've honestly loved it for that. It was surprisingly refreshing and it was always a favorite.

Another dive in to the Parfums De Marly discovery kit today and i am testing Greenley. So far this will be my fourth test between the discovery kit and 2 free samples I got with it of which I have tested, Pegasus, Layton, Pegasus Exclusif and Sedley.

This sparkling green apple opening is easily the most invigorating of any freshie in my collection. The dry down is alright if not a bit disappointing compared to opening. What's left is mainly cashmere and cedar. I find it's best suited for wear in the springtime and strongly associate it with the feeling of the first warm days here in the mid-atlantic.

this opens with an almost cleaner-like (unlisted) sharp pineapple note that i lowkey cannot stand. sometimes it smells like a pina colada candy but other times i get that cleaner smell (maybe also an unlisted lime note?) and i just don't vibe with it. luckily it fades for the most part in the drydown to just a woody floral coconut (with just sweet rather than sharp pina colada touches) that reminds me a little bit of synthetic pineapple + coco paradise from bath and body works, which i also didn't love. overall, this was pretty disappointing tbh just bc it was hyped by reviewers and it's just alright to me. it performs and lasts surprisingly well for a summer fragrance though, so if you tend to enjoy summery scents (i don't--i just got sucked in by misleading notes and blind bought it), i could see this being a love for a lot of people.

My-my-my… This scent is… Wow, wonderful! A fougère spin on a contemporary Oud accord, a dash of playful sweetness lending from praline, and a very punchy aromatic opening from the sage; all combine beautifully between a rich semi-rubbery leather/saffron blend. Jordi Fernández did AMAZING work with Haltane. One of my favorite parts of this is during the dry down: When the praline attains this deeply satisfying creamy chocolatey note and it lays beside the wood accord. It’s sensual, a little carnal with the saffron adding a rich spice to the mix, but my lord does it smell absolutely stunning. Masculine, confident, but not overbearing. All of this beauty dries down to a bed of musky woods after 9-10hrs, touches of sweetness lingering until it’s a skin scent. Noble yet delicate and playful and balanced with precision. Between this and Layton Exclusif , I can say that these two are the only PdM’s that are worth the price tag for me. If you haven’t smelled this, get a sample/decant, it’s well worth it if you enjoy surreptitiously crafted woody-aromatic scents. I’ll openly admit, I wear this leisurely when I’m at home. I don’t know why, don’t ask… Sweatpants and a t-shirt on but I’m leaving a trail of wood and sage behind me, enjoying my own sillage. Is this meant to be dressed up? Absolutely, it’s deserving of such treatment, but I enjoy it enough to spray it anytime. Senior. Fernández, has crafted a luxurious and masculine addition that’s worthy of the PdM price tag and the Thoroughbred name. Don’t sleep on this one.

This is a masterpiece. But its not a crowd pleaser and more of an acquired taste It's the definition of Addictive Woodsy & Earthy. Like you're one of those tribesman from the movie Avatar and you walked into one of those fresh untouched forests from another planet. Glowing plants, fresh soil and exotic woods & flowers touch the air and you smell this. This and Oud for greatness are 10/10 fragrances for sure. Haltane is less strong but still good performance and a lil sweeter with the praline so its easier to wear. Ladies also LOVE this scent especially on a man. So gatekeep ts at ALL COSTS

IDK how i feel about this one, honestly. It’s definitely a strong frag. A room filler for sure. Its not my taste, per say BUT i wouldnt not wear it. If that makes sense. Maybe its the oud but Haltane does not go away. Its for the people who love it and love it only. I don’t think its a safe blind buy, at all. What i can say that it is one of the best sweeter oud frags on the market, right now. Side Note: I see that some people are comparing this to BR540. I don’t see the similarities at all. Not even a little bit.

When you dive headfirst into perfumery with little or no limits to your budget, especially the highest-end artisanal brands that distill rare, natural, and wild oud oils (e.g. Ensar Oud, Agar Aura, Areej le Dore, Bortnikoff, etc.) you quickly realize that your newfangled scent preferences have transformed so drastically that you've cursed your taste for lesser "oud" (note the quotation marks) fragrances permanently. Haltane has no real oud in it. Rather, it's a combination of synthetic chemicals that create an "oud" accord, thus the quotation marks. This accord plus saffron and praline notes make Haltane quite sweet -- almost gourmand. It's pleasant and appeals to the masses, but it has none of the aromatic, dynamic qualities of a real oud oil fragrance that I've since become accustomed to. As far as longevity and sillage go, Haltane is a strong performer. This sticks on clothing for a full day and can be smelled by people within 6-8 feet of you for the first few hours. People who find themselves in closed quarters after a heavy spraying of Haltane will likely find it to be cloying. If you had asked me 3 years ago if Haltane was an excellent oud fragrance, I would have unhesitatingly told you that it is. But in the last 3 years I've bought, worn, and/or smelled dozens of pure-oud oils, attars, and high % real oud fragrances (some costing as much as $1500 per gram or $5000 per 30mL) and now there is no going back...smelling the soaring heights off REAL oud is transformative. Accordingly, one of my prior favorite fragrances has been reduced to a middling "oud" fragrance. I've been struck with the oud curse and become a fragrance snob in the process. I don't like it, but ignorance truly is bliss.

As we know, PDM and Initio are "sister companies" and this gives them the luxury of purchasing high quality ingredients at a cheaper price (due to volume) and they can access top perfumers and use them for both of the houses. I like very much Layton, Herod, Oajan and Musc Therapy .. the rest are questionable for my nose. Haltane is the big elephant in the room, called Initio Oud for Greatness put in green clothes for Parfums de Marly and with more ML for the price - which is good. I do not appreciate at all the saffron dose in it, it will take all my air out and I cannot enjoy it - even if I like the complexity of the notes and what the result is. I have a problem with the Saffron notes in many perfumes, not only with the Initio. Haltane is nice, has high quality lavender and bergamot when it starts .. then it is following with a sweet praline note and a ton of saffron, after that I can´t sniff it anymore. Thanks for watching my video :)

Edit: I recently acquired a late 2023 bottle, and I am not sure what may have happened with the other bottles/samples I had, but this new bottle performs so much better on me. Not a beast still, but easily going on the 9-10 hour mark on my skin with noticeable projection for the first 4. My love for Haltane sparked once again, and I can't get enough of it.

This is easily in my top 5 PDMs. Such a gorgeous scent (sorry I haven’t smelled OFG, so I cannot compare). It’s so rich and vibrant. It’s definitely versatile, but it fits better in a scene where one is dressed well, as it will compliment your wardrobe to perfection.

I started getting into fragrances not too long ago. Weird enough, it was triggered by my search for a scent that someone wore that was so bad to my nose, I couldn’t even understand why someone would wear such an atrocious perfume. And so came to life my search for that frag.

Yes yes, we've heard it countless times since it's release..... "This smells like Oud For Greatness" "This is a PDM money grab" "They are too similar to warrant a buy"..... I agree Oud For Greatness and Haltane are VERY SIMILAR. Where I see a major difference is in the mass appeal, sweetness, performance, and complexity. Overall, Haltane is a much easier fragrance to love.

I've had haltane for a month now and it just keeps vetting better and better. I've realised that when you smell a fragrance for the first time it smells underwhelming, but over time you start to unravel its complexity.

The brands are different, yet the colour of the bottle is analogous, a scarlet red one and Baccarat red the other, and even the scents have a few points in common. Here and there, some puffs smell the same, but when compared side by side, Baccarat Rouge 540 Eau de Parfum and Kalan are two distinct scents, each with its own unique character. I see more contrasts than resemblances between the two. Kalan smells like a more manly, robust, woodier and darker version of Baccarat. Perhaps, Baccarat has a more feminine touch, whereas Kalan has a more masculine slant as if they altered the original formula for getting two complementary fragrances. Two fraternal twins of different sexes may smell very similar but not precisely identical. Kalan is a splendid example of a perfume that can be like many classic perfumes, but the use of some notes in this perfume both takes it away from them and makes it look different from them. Well, the comparison ends here. Let us now get to the heart of Kalan's description. Kalan is a small fern, virile and highly sophisticated, and feels like a modern barbershop fragrance, both spicy and green, and vaguely floral. Although they classify it as oriental spicy, it has a fougére tendency, with a fluffy, unsweet, salty, cotton candy feel. Created by two Mane Company perfumers, Celine Ripert and Nathalie Templer, it opens with an extraordinarily fresh initial note of bitterly aromatic blood orange, black pepper and spices for a burst of energy. An observable syrupiness, thick and gooey, with a touch of medicinal, tastes of dried blood orange slices, expertly spiced with freshly ground black pepper. The blood orange does not have the sweet scent commonly found in fragrances. Instead, it feels like unripe or unsweet orange with a sour taste, filthy and full metal nuance. The spices mentioned must include dusty nutmeg and precious saffron, I'd bet, as I get a bitter leathery nuance in the initial blast. The spicy mix plays a role throughout the entire lifecycle of the fragrance. I get a synthetic plastic smell in here for just a moment, but it's just an illusion. I am blown away by that accord. Whilst it might not sound appealing, it is precisely the smell I figured out in my mind before buying or even sampling it. It releases an accord of aromatic lavender herbs and orange blossom in the heart, evoking the majesty of ancient French gardens. It is gorgeous, although difficult to interpret and describe in words. I catch a resinous roasted sugar, and a few whispers of earthy oakmoss from the base are already detectable if I press my nose to my wrist. I doubt it could be a crowd-pleaser because of the very distinct bitter notes that drive it. The lavender comes to the front and gives it a very slight fougére vibe. I'm sure this unusual volume and dosage of lavender will surprise you. Even if I don't know what perfume the solar note should have, the heart is heated; it warms the surrounding atmosphere, and the essence makes me think of a cold sunny day rather than a rainy one, so it has achieved the result. So the middle stage has a warm aroma, spicy and slightly metallic. At last, it evolves into something earthly. And when I say earth, I don't mean dirty patchouli or similar; instead, something more like moss and wet dirt or soil. Moss mixed with wood gives the illusion of aged and damp wood. White sandalwood, immersed in musk, woody notes, amber and tonka beans, melts on the skin and ignites the imagination. Now the scent toned down. It is calmer, more agreeable. Smooth, bright, utterly mesmerising. And I get a massive amount of warm, creamy, kind of burnt and caramelised sugar from roasted tonka. That smoky sugariness slant, in the end, is tamed by an animalic, musky and earthy moss, which already came up at the opening. It's so smooth that it is perfect. There's no overbearing ambroxan or ambergris here, like in so many other contemporary men's perfumes. Just delectable amber, sweet but not sticky—a chocolate sweetness, I would say—that keeps things from ever getting too dark or deep. Longevity is excellent, and the sillage looks good too. It hangs in the air, especially in the first few hours after application, but I get a puff of burnt sugar sweetness here and there when I move my arms or turn my head. The heat it gives off suggests that I wear it during the coldest days and evenings in winter, at least in the spring and autumn months closest to winter. What to say? I wanted this perfume from the first moment I saw his presentation, and I loved it at the first sniff. So freaky Glorious, and Gorgeous. But from the other reviews, Kalan is a polarising fragrance, no doubt. One faction thinks this is a magnificent and soothing scent and another that finds it disgusting and vexatious. So, don't just dwell on the appearances or impressions of others, including mine, but experience Kalan on your own skin... it may pleasantly surprise you! I base the review on a bottle I have owned since December 2021. -Elysium

I forgot to leave a review for this scent. I was scared after reading some hate reviews that I would dislike it, nevertheless I decided to get a small perfume oil inspired version. Well, I was blown away. I was surprised how many people couldn't like this at all. It's a really well blended scent with soft spices (not harsh) caressing the blood mandarin with a touch of lavender adding some freshness. As it dries down, you get a nice sweet accord that feels very niche to the nose. I believe this is another good unisex scent. I have never smelled anything like this before. It reminds me of the feeling I got when I first smelled Terre d'Hermes. It feels like a totally new experience and you can tell that this is not lazy art perfumery. I wore this to bed and rewatched 300 and wow I felt like I was one of the spartan soldiers on a mission. It has that royal/aristocratic vibe that is perfect for the office. It's worth a try.

This fragrance had me hypnotised for a while. I ordered some decants of the house of Marly. I expected Kalan to be quite fresh, judging by the notes and what everyone says about it. I heard the term peppery red orange popping up. So I was looking forward to this one, as I love my freshies. But this aint a freshy I can tell you. I was so shocked I ordered a new decant just to see if it was the correct fragrance they sent me. And it was. But! Even if it's no freshy, I do like this one a lot, it really deserves a review. I find it to be nutty and spicy in a way, very balsamic and creamy. I don't know if it's a thing outside of The Netherlands but it's reminding me a bit of Speculaas. I believe that would mean a mix of cinnamon, cardamom, nutmeg, ginger and pepper. So this would really be one great perfume for the holidays. It stays on clothes for quite a while, but it's not heavy and cloying as Haltane can be.

When i first saw kalans beautiful red bottle i had really high expectations but when i smelled it they lowered real low. Kalan smelled like wet soil when i first put my nose to it and later it got a little better when some of the citrus came through. But the perfume was still sadly not my thing. Make sure to try it before buying it.

Peppery and spicy with a hint of blood orange, a real masculine scent. The drydown is divinely delicious. The quality is excellent, the durability is also It's a bit like BR540, but it's more like a masculine version :) It also performs very well in warm weather, but temperatures around 20 degrees are the most favorable for Kalan. 10/8

This one is wild. Grit. Dirt. Sun. Burnt Orange. This is a pretty fun scent, although could be polarizing. It's extremely unique. I guess this is what they mean by "niche". There's a primal element to it, but not in an animalistic or musky way. More like a fruity earthy way.

Ok, hear me out..this is a fragrance that you’d love after you hate it for a long time. I mean, no fragrance got me confused the way Kalan did. To start with, I get why people get so polarized about Kalan, I mean that opening is the absolute worst I have ever smelled but wait for it..

Pretty harsh, with an extremely strong personality, combining warm spicy notes (especially a lot of cumin,so make sure you know what you're getting into) ,with warm amber, precious sandalwood and a beautiful aromatic lavender, Kalan is the perfume that through the harmony of the notes manages to remind of the famous and much loved Baccarat Rouge.

"Kalan is a fabulous creation, I believe—piece of art. And the opening is a bit rough. Of course, we knew before we launched it that the black pepper is maybe a bit strong at first, so we tried to tune it down to make it more accessible, but then we were losing the magic in the dry down.

… you know that viral picture of a blue and black dress that some people see as white and gold? I truly wonder this, because I simply cannot get the notes that the people who dislike it describe. A lot of people say the opening is bad, rough, or difficult bear. I don’t get this. Right from the beginning, it’s fantastic for me. A spicy feel indeed, but bad? No.

I have both Delina and Delina Exclusif and this is more subtle version of Delina. You definitely know it’s Delina, but it’s missing the rhubarb scent which I seem to have love and hate relationship. Sometimes it’s too much for me and the more powdery Delina Exclusif is the answer. It’s more of a winter choice and I use OG Delina in the summer. I have received many compliments wearing Delina Exclusif which is pretty strange since I own quite many popular niche perfumes and this is the only one that gets compliments. If I needed to choose only one Delina, I would go for Delina Exclusif.

Am I broad-sleeved, too generous, forgiving, and understanding if I give 10 out of 10 to this perfume? I don't think so, but let's see why together. I state that I have not yet tried Delina Eau de Parfum , and therefore I cannot compare the two. If you are looking for a comparative review, then this is not. But for sure, I can say that how Parfums de Marly has interpreted the rose in this perfume is sublime. We face a graceful, creamy, and powdery rose, but not like the well-known marriage with oud, with coffee, with patchouli, with incense, or with leather. Forget Montale, Mancera, Initio, or anything else of the Middle Eastern sort. Exclusive is a charming, seductive, creamy, and fruity rose to the umpteenth degree, with underlining woods and mosses. According to my knowledge, this floral rendition of Delina is unparalleled. Although I have a handful of masculine or unisex targeted Parfums de Marly creations, such as Godolphin, Herod, Kalan, Layton, and Percival, Delina Exclusif is the very first feminine target I am adding to my collection and reviewing right now. It begins with a fruit opening, so luscious. Yes, it is rosy, but the first note I smell is that of pear, ripe and buttery, and soon the lychee kicks in with its sweet rosy nuance. There is just a tinge of bitter grapefruit, barely perceptible, which does not come out too loud, harsh, or citrus. As the overture unfolds, there is a captivating aura, so creamy and airy, with a floral and fruity powderiness. Besides, there is no trace of sourness on my skin. In the heart, a bouquet of velvety roses, the Damascus variety, adds that floral touch, and the scent transforms into delicious gourmet lokum, a Turkish rose delight. Imagine a tray adorned with bunches of rose petals and soft, dusty, gelatinous pieces of lokum lying gracefully on top of this bed. Incense grains and vetiver root pair this dreamy aroma and give it a faintly smoky, dry, and leathery undertone; however, not all too churchy or earthy. Boy, oh boy, I can get lost in this fragrance more than Delina is Deliziosa! If you have a well-trained nose, you will catch a powdery and waxy violet, which makes the rose more unique. For clarity, it smells rosy, sweet, and powdery, though it is not a gourmand. On the finish, earthy, dusty, and inedible vanilla notes emerge, together with clean and soapy white musk and a molecule that replaces oak moss with a softer scent. At the same time, the sweetness of the lychees and the dustiness of the rose petals I experienced at the beginning remain. Delina Exclusif is the rosiest, sweet, and powdery perfume imaginable. It's addictive and insanely delightful; honestly, I can't get enough of it. Perhaps among the woody notes, there is cedar, which I love in perfumes because it often gives the atmosphere of the wood shavings of the pencil. In this case, it does it very well, just enough to give it an interesting and exciting atmosphere with sweetness and rose jam. Delina Exclusif is best suited to be worn during autumn, winter, and spring evenings and nights. If I spray it sparingly, as it can get cloying, I can wear it even on cool summer nights. It is ideally suited for special moments, cocktail parties, dinners, or dates. The projection is average, and it lasts for a long time. Delina Exclusif initially smells like a pear cocktail with a pink undertone. Then, the rose becomes creamy and ends with a hint of musky vanilla reminiscent of freshly cleansed skin, sprinkled with a generous veil of body milk. I base my opinion and review on a bottle I have owned since October 2022. -Elysium

I really love Delina, I even wore it to my wedding reception. But there is one small downside: In my opinion the scent only blooms when it's at least slightly warm. I wouldn't wear it in winter, it doesn't smell bad when it's cold, but doesn't show its full beauty. As I live in relatively cool climate, that makes me wear Delina less often than I would like to. Delina Exclusif is the perfect solution to this problem. It's the warmer, sweeter, deeper Delina that can be worn in spring, autumn and winter, maybe even on cold summer evenings. Both have the same sweet, inviting rose and juicy litchi. They smell very pink and girly in the best possible way. Even though this one doesn't list the rhubarb note of the original, it also has the same refreshing tartness in the opening that makes me think of rhubarb. Maybe it's just the mix of grapefruit, rose and litchi. Both versions live from the contrast between sweet and sour, but Delina Exclusif leans a little sweeter because the vanilla note got amped up considerably and the dewy peony is missing. The creaminess that Delina has in the base is present right from the start in Exclusif. I also think the incense note is a little stronger, I did not get anything smokey from the original, but I get hints of it in this. Such a gorgeous scent. I like it just as much as Delina. It's obviously quite expensive and similar to the pillar, so I'm not sure if I can justify a purchase anytime soon. If I had unlimited money and time to wear fragrances, I would add it to my collection immediately. It's worth a try for those who loves Delina, but also for those who find it too sour, and for all lovers of sweet rose fragrances in general.

I can't think of a single other perfume more dear to me. Intensely powdery, in the same way that powdered sugar is- saccharine and warm but never sickly, although it is probably the most potent perfume I own. Lasts for weeks on clothes and days on my skin, even though I always apply a maximum of two sprays. It lacks the sour rhubarb and headache-inducing splash of ambroxan the original Delina has, instead replacing them with smooth amber and incense. If the original is silk then this is velvet- thick, heavy, and luxurious. The rose and fruits are enveloped in powdered sugar, while the woody notes give it depth. It is vaguely reminiscent of baby powder, but in a nostalgic way rather than being infantile- if anything, it feels like a commanding and head-turning presence. Fit for an empress draped in warm fabric and pearls. Definitely more of a winter scent, as the cold weather allows the fruit notes to bloom without being overshadowed by the sugary sweetness.

After hair dye, it smells like conditioner applied to the hair. This scent is almost identical to the scents often used in hair shampoos and conditioners. The fragrance has a very creamy and powdery undertone. The rose used is definitely not like a red rose. Probably a pink or white rose. The intensity of the rose fragrance is light, but the rose makes itself felt quite a bit. The rose scent is not sharp, but soft and powdery. The vanilla scent does not manifest itself alone. It is revealed with fruit notes. The fragrance has a sour tone. A sugary tone is not dominant. A sour and aromatic fragrance. This fragrance is quite similar to the fragrances of the Armani Si range. In general, it is not a heavy scent, but a light scent and a scent that will suit people with white skin. The smell does not bother you in the middle of the day, but it is felt. It stays on fabric for up to 8 hours. It disappears on the skin in the first 3 hours. If you leave a room, the smell disappears. Projection is not high. It is felt in the first 2 hours from a maximum of 2 meters. Longevity: 6/10 Projection: 5/10 Sillage: 4/10 Fragrance Quality: 6/10

Book matches cover. THE princess perfume. Historically inaccurate rococo rose, with syrup-soaked lychee and soupçon of vanilla. Imagine rosewater lokum dusted in powdered sugar. My favourite part is the lychee, which really ignites on my skin (stays rosier on fabric). So succulent.

A fruity, juicy rose. A rose interpreted by Quentin Bisch so to my nose wonderful. Fresh, spring-like and intense, as if you could squeeze its petals and drink its juice. What can I say, I find it more decisive than the la rosee version and much more in line with my style. Gorgeous, I want it. On wishlist.

This is my GFs "I want you now" scent, and she pulled it out once her intentions were clear. I think its very well suited for the purpose. You can stop reading right here. At first it was too much to handle - and in some way, still is. There is nothing subtle about the scent, nor about the message it sends - it's a men catcher.

This is probably the most romantic perfume I have ever smelled. It's a lovely rose-forward fragrance that is tempered by the telltale sweetness of vanilla, with opening notes that give a little kick of lychee fruitiness.

I tried this at Dillard's and if it weren't so expensive I would've bought it on the spot. It's such a gorgeous, light rose with one of the few powder notes that I actually enjoy. If you were to make a fragrance that evokes the phrase "pretty princess" this is it. It's not subtle but there is a softness to it and the rose holds for a while too.

The almond comes through and the berries linger in the back, as it dries down, the espresso and sandalwood show up. The different blends and how they all play so nicely together make this one of the most interesting fragrances I've ever tried (so far). And it's a gourmand which I don't typically really like or feel like it suits me personally. Please try it out when you have the chance.

Opens with a strong burst of citruses—grapefruit leads—but right from the start, you can already pick up the dry, slightly dirty woods and earthy vetiver in the scent composition. As it develops, the balance shifts: the woods and vetiver become bolder while the citrus lingers, just not as loud. So yeah, still citrusy, but the ratio leans more woodsy the longer it’s on skin. Not love at first sniff, but it grows on you. It has a unique character. There are moments in the mid that might remind me of some aspects of Terre d'Hermès Eau Givrée , but overall, it stands quite apart in my opinion. The vetiver is prominent—like in "Elysium Parfum Cologne (Eau de Parfum) | Roja Parfums" —but not as green, and it’s definitely paired with more woods here. So regardless of the comparisons, this still feels like its own thing. Performance is no joke—strong projection and serious longevity (more than 12 hours on me), so definitely in the compliment-puller category because of the performance, probably due to the ambroxan (marketed as ambergris accord), and I wouldn’t be surprised if there’s some clean, light oud hidden in there too—but they seem to have kept that chef’s kiss a secret. Overall, it’s a bold and unexpected release for a freshie. Still growing on me, but there’s definitely something addictive about it.

This is one of Parfums de Marlys latest creations and my expectations werent super high as i thought it would just be another fresh normal citrus scent. But when i tried it i actually really enjoyed the scent! It opened up with a blast of grapefruit which is one of my favorite citrus notes and then it got more citrus, woody in the dry down. Great perfume from PDM but sadly a bit overpriced.

Initially I dismissed Perseus as just another fresh, citrus Terre d'Hermès Eau de Toilette clone. But giving it some more wears it actually has this intoxicating, addictive edge to it. Where the defacto office freshy consists of a woody base, this one is citric all the way. It has a bit of bitterness of a grapefruit/pomelo. It has the acidity of lemon and lime. Truly freshness in a bottle. It lasts, it packs a punch, do I think it’s worth full price? I think it’s steep. Do I want it? Yes very much indeed!

I generally don't have a lot of great things to say about PdM fragrances. They are often too sweet and cloying or seem to be a facsimile of other fragrances on the market with just a slight tweak by the perfumer to make it just different enough. It has been discussed adnauseum in countless forums so I don't need to get too into the weeds about that here. While Perseus does follow a similar path the thing that I appreciate about it is that they finally decided to come out with a new release that isn't so sweet that it borders on giving the wearer Type 2 diabetes. Perseus opens with a very photorealistic grapefruit that we've experienced from some of the Dolce&Gabbana Light Blue Pour Homme flankers like Forever and Italian Love.
