It is bright, tart, and ever so slightly effervescent. Similar to the D&G LB flankers, this beautiful rindy grapefruit opening persists throughout most of the life of the fragrance. Blackcurrant is there but very shyly providing a touch of sweetness to balance the tartness of the grapefruit. This opening is soon met by a nice dose of aromatics in the form of mandarin, bergamot, geranium, and vetiver. This combination takes some of the best parts of Terre d'Hermes and blankets it under the grapefruit opening. As this continues to work its way to the dry down some of the fluffy and musky attributes of the cashmere woods show up to keep the fragrance light and elevated as geranium specifically can start to travel down a green and dank path if left unchecked. The "dry woods" and ambergris (I have to assume it is an accord and not the real thing) are most likely an overdose of ISO E Super and Ambroxan used as a fixative to provide lift and projection. In terms of performance, this fragrance comes out of the nozzle SCREAMING and will project for a good distance for the first 30 minutes to an hour. Afterward, it does settle into something more tamed and refined. You can expect 6 to 8 hours out of this fragrance and perhaps a little more depending on the weather you are wearing it. I can see the initial wave of PdM enthusiasts who live and die for Layton, Althair, and Sedley to say that this is better for a more mature man, or that it is dated because of the geranium. For me, this is one of a few select PdM fragrances that I feel are meant to be worn by men and not just a unisex fragrance released in the male-targeted bottles.

Perseus is aight. Not the best but its high quality Similar to Percival its kinda basic for a niche fragrance. but unlike Percival, Perseus doesn’t feel like the king of its kind Theres so many other good citrus grapefruit scents: Bvlgari Tygar, Vibrato Soapiro, Blu de chanel, Terre D’hermes And for orange scents Versache or Louis Vatton costs around the same or less Id say skip Perseus it doesnt stand out. Buy something else with that money. Theres a ton of other good fresh zests scents that you can buy 2 or 3 bottles for the same price.
I see a lot of hate for Perseus and primarily it hate is not because the scent is bad but that it takes the idea of cheaper smells (like Eau Givree).

https://parfums-de-marly.com/collections/to-share Eight of Parfums De Marley's men's fragrances are officially recognized as unisex fragrances by the brand. Six (Herod, Pegasus, Kalan, Oajan, Carlisle) are also properly classified as unisex in Parfumo, but only Althair and Perseus continue to be incorrectly classified as men's fragrances.

I've been testing it for weeks, A very different perfume to what Parfums de Marly is used to. A very rough start with grapefruit, accompanied by vetiver until it becomes the protagonist, with a woody accord in the background, a background that is present in other perfumes such as Kalan. It is undoubtedly his interpretation of vetiver.

This is a grown and sexy grapefruit in a business suit that is quickly becoming one of my most worn scents out of over 300. Its a beautiful citrus with a light and clean vetiver that lasts 6-7 hours on my skin. Often compared to Terre d'Hermès Eau Givrée, I find Perseus younger and a lot more wearable than Eau Givrée.
It's not exactly a secret that Parfums de Marly make basic and largely unoriginal product.

this smell is so nostalgic, sweet and comforting. perfect everyday winter scent. (for me, this is a cold-weather scent only. it's too sweet for spring or summer imo) this smells like going to a christmas market. that's the vibe. caramel, sugar, fruit gummies, this perfume could give you cavities (in the best way possible) not similar to other love spell flankers or the og at all!! if you like og love spell idk if you'll like this.

The person who came up with the note pyramid of this fragrance should be fired. It's already difficult to accurately describe a fragrance using only real-world objects that most people know the smell of, but here it seems Parfums de Marly are intentionally trying to mislead you. The two notes that should be at the forefront of this pyramid are 1. leather, and 2. raspberry. Any other note present here is entirely secondary/support. If leather and raspberry remind you of Tuscan Leather Eau de Parfum or Ombré Leather (2018) Eau de Parfum , you are correct. Godolphin is a slightly fruitier interpretation of that DNA and thus is probably redundant to own if you own at least one of those. But I think any collector who has even a passing interest in leather should own at least one of these three. Godolphin is an easy-to-wear leather scent with a woody-musky drydown. It has a bit of a sharp biting "metallic" quality in the opening, but it is soon smoothed out by soft woods and florals. Probably in the middle-of-the-pack as far as PdM's oeuvre. Definitely doesn't get any points for creativity, but is a decent addition to the collection.

Those more informed will surely know that the perfumes of the Parfums de Marly house take their name from the horses of the royal stable of King Louis XV. Hence, Godolphin is one of them, named after the renowned Arabic stallion. The Godolphin Arabian, also known as the Godolphin Barb, was one of three stallions that founded the modern Thoroughbred—the others were the Darley Arabian and the Byerley Turk. They named it after its best-known owner, Francis Godolphin, 2nd Earl of Godolphin. Born in Yemen, they gave it to Louis XV of France in 1730. It seems as it was a present from monarch to monarch. On Godolphin, Parfums de Marly put the accents on smoky, leathery chords that remind me of a beloved smoky suede jacket - which was a custom after leaving a pub or club in the last millennium when smoking inside wasn't a problem. It comes out with fresh notes of herbaceous thyme, here extremely prominent, spiced black saffron and woody cypress, which create a pine-like sensation with a slightly dry and smoky tone. It oozes a solid, leathery scent because of saffron. I can't help but observe an ashy tinge kicking off after the initial blast, fading a bit, with a pinch of moss added to it all. I don't perceive any of the passionate fruity undertones that others are talking about. The whole initial blast gives it that exclamation "Damn!" at the first sniff, but then it will blow anyone's mind. I really love the saffron note in here. It's such an underutilized ingredient outside of these more niche designers, but it's fantastic. A floral trio of jasmine rose and iris anchors the aroma. While the first two flowers seem muted to my nose, they are in the back seat and not too prominent on my skin. I clearly capture the dusty iris, which adds a touch of dustiness to the middle phase. Indeed, the protagonist in the heart is still a glamorous suede, which grows after an hour. The scent becomes darker and denser. Rather than the horse, Godolphin reminds me of the smell of its saddle. Then, it veers towards a woody edge and leather in the background with the seductive tones of white cedarwood that carries the aroma of pencil shavings. The bitter vetiver here takes on an inky and gummy vibe and occasionally reminds me of Encre Noire Eau de Toilette with that dark, smoky shade. There is a bed of animalic musk, which stands out with a slight hint of vanilla and amber, almost imperceptible, but in a balanced and well-blended way. Reveals the vetiver note deep in the base with cedar and cypress undertones serving as an aromatic. Godolphin is definitely a cologne with a masculine and robust cut. Of course, women with a penchant for fragrances like this might wear it, but there are no fruity, sweet, and floral tones in the overall performance. In my experience, I don't get the smooth rose, mellow vanilla, and welcoming amber. Instead, I get an imitation of the leather from a well-crafted blend of dry saffron and wild vetiver, darkened by thyme leaves and cypress shavings. As for the projection, it is strong enough for the first few hours but then becomes much more moderate. It has good longevity and lasts longer when sprayed on clothes. Since no one around me complained, I bet it wears well during the day as it doesn't overwhelm others. At the same time, it suits late autumn when the days get colder, and the winter months, it's perfect for special occasions, formal events, and a night out. It has a sense of intrigue and sensuality that will attract compliments. It will surely attract everyone's attention. You will get compliments on this. I base the review on a decant I have owned since January 2022. -Elysium

Godolphin opens with very intense flowery notes of Saffron, Thyme, Cypress toned down with some green notes, and with some added muskyness to the whole. The other things I notice after the heavy floral opening, are the Fruity notes with Vanilla, and some Amber. These together gave me the impression of leather. I have read some reviews(on other sites), which described this, as more of a floral scent than a leather one. For me it is clearly a leather scent, but not the "raw leather jacket" type of leather. For me it is sweet gourmand leather, with flowers. At later points I can feel some dry woodsyness to it also. It could be labeled as a unisex, maybe more on the feminine side. Give it a try if you like leather scents!

You might say this is a copy of Ombré Leather (2018) Eau de Parfum but then again, it's leather. Are all leather scents copies of Tom Fords bestseller? What I get out of this beautiful golden bottle is a gentle, sour-fruity leather. It's so squishy it makes my mouth water. It's nothing repellant, animalic or petrol-like. Also it's pretty linear, maybe the fruitiness takes the upper-hand over the leatheriness in the end, but we're talking about skinscent by that time. So where TF: OL might be your John Travolta black leather coat from Grease, Godolphin is more of a sophisticated suede jacket you wear to a well dressed party.

I'm not sure which smells like which, but this is SEXY. To my nose, vetiver and iris take the stage here. The wood is warm and wet (giggity) here and definitely tones down the scent to be silent and strong. This is gold. Definitely a must have for the 30 and up club. This goes perfectly with dark clothe, a black button up and some grey coal jeans. This isn't a "pAnTy DrOpPeR" but an consensual undergarment remover. Great stuff from a great overall house, PDM.

i love tuscan leather and ombre leather, but this stuff made me want to dry heave. There's a very repulsive smell this gives off, i think it's the abundance of fruit notes mixed with the rose. It's noxious. I do love the smell of rose, but i've found when it's mixed with leather...i become very repulsed.

The opening of this fragrance resembles Tom Ford's Ombre Leather, only weaker, dryer and less sweet. A few minutes after the opening, something medicinal comes to me and this, together with the leather tones, makes me feel like I'm at the local shoemaker. The fragrance is not unpleasant, but there is nothing new.

…this is how I would describe the fragrance in one short phrase. The leather is very smooth, not as dirty as in most leather fragrances I have tried before. Add roses. Lots of roses. Add Iris, a base of smooth wood accords and a very slight hint of earthiness. What results is the most well-blended leather fragrance I have smelled to date.

In the world of politics, Marxists and Leninists are close to each other. In the world of fragrances, this is less the case with Marlyists and Guerlinists. The Guerlinists prefer classic perfumes, while the Marlyists are enthusiastic about modern scents tailored to a younger and prestige-conscious audience.

My predecessor Val raves in the highest tones about "Godolphin," and I must say, with this Marly fragrance, you are indeed dealing with something special. Whether it is a Freudian slip or not - when I first looked at the sample, I read "Gandalphin.

Honestly I'm not trying to offend anyone with this hot take, but my nose can't stand this cleaning product! Literally reminds me of a toilet that is promised to cause headaches, with screechy lemon/peach notes and alcoholic base that just can't seem to work with my skin chemistry nor wash off with soap! I was promised a clean girl scent based on other favourites I have, but unfortunately the cleaning quality is a bit too intense and synthetic. (Side note on the bottle: I love vintage looking things, but I find it so tacky when it's paired with this silver, modern cap. Of course this is just a personal preference, like everything is). All in all, disappointing, and not for me!

Valaya from Parfumes de Marly is lively and elegant and immediately brings to mind the heroine of a period romance, someone you might describe as beautiful, free-spirited, and headstrong. And she probably doesn’t want to marry or have children or live by society’s standards or conventions, and she may, in fact, get kicked out of finishing school because she punched one young woman in the mouth and kissed another young woman in the same place. She runs away to Europe, holds feminist salons, and becomes both a secret political power and an ungovernable poet of no small renown. She smells of crisp cotton and luxurious linen pantaloons, the dozens of verdant, woody ferns which adorn every square inch of her Parisian apartment, and the delicate, musky nectar of a ripe peach which she is frequently seen biting into, her sharp, small teeth pausing to smile enigmatically between juicy mouthfuls.

Oh dear, this is a loud scent! Valaya is a cousin to Ex Nihilo Fleur Narcotique, and I love Fleur Narcotique with all its synthetic cleanliness, but this one here is just too much for me. I actually tried this for the first time before I even knew Fleur Narcotique, and it made me a bit suspicious of the original. This starts out quite peppery and sharp, and then quickly takes a turn into citrus territory. It's fizzy like a soda, sweet like peaches and mandarins, but there is also something about it that reminds me of the packaged lemon towelettes you get in Turkish restaurants after eating. Imagine that mixed with sweet fruits and a huge dose of the persistent musk molecules found in many modern niche fragrances, add a wisp of creamy white florals, and you're pretty close to Valaya. I don't hate lemon towelettes, and there are moments where I enjoy Valaya's freshness, but still... this is not something I want in a perfume, especially not amped up to eleven with strong musky fixatives. Overall this scent feels cold and harsh to me. It's not scratchy on the throat or anything like that, not quite as obnoxious as Erba Pura or Kirke (sorry to the fans, but these are two scents I just can't deal with!). But it gets on my nerves after a while. Most other female releases by PDM are much more elegant and fine-tuned to my nose. Delina for example is not exactly a quiet scent either, but it feels so much rounder and better blended. And Valaya just won't go away. I sprayed it on my leg wearing shorts and it still managed to be noticeable on my sweater the next day. It gets reactivated in the shower, so you really have to scrub to get it off. Good for those who love the scent, I guess, but I find it obstructive.

At first in was in love with Valaya because she is fresh, fruity and full of sunshine. The top notes are what I really liked but as the perfume dries down, she gets very powdery and super chemical and this lasts forever. On clothes you can still smell her after several weeks. So the performance is damn good, unfortunately this is now one of my least favourite perfumes from PDM as I just can’t live with the strong chemical cloud I get from her. Also I haven’t received any compliments when wearing her.

It may have Quentin Bisch' (and Julien Sprecher's) name on it, but this stuff comes straight from the Givaudan factory. All prefab materials ready to be put together. Forget traditional perfumery and artisanal fiddling. This is big corporate at work, conquering the selective markets with maxed out ROI. The scent profile is highly reminiscent of detergent with a lily-of-the-valley touch. It combines fresh citrus top notes with minimal fruity sweetness and a drop of vanilla to round it up. Utterly artificial, but you know what, who cares? Not every perfume is made for the snobs, the unicorn hunters. Behind this uninspired commercialism lies a scent that actually works. Easy-going, focus group proof and most importantly: plain "nice and fresh”. Nothing wrong with that, once in a while.

This perfume is beautiful, it’s not my style personally but I did want to review it for one thing: it performs incredibly. I have never tried a clean, aldehydic, fruity perfume that lasts so well. I tried on my sample this morning, very lightly just one spray on each wrist.

I got a freebie sample of this with another order and I would've never picked this to try based on the notes as I don't like peach or florals as a general rule. It shocked me because I did quite enjoy the powdery muskiness of it and the brief whiff I took from the cap I thought I would hate it.

After all of the negative reviews of Valaya, I was hesitant to give it a try. Luckily, this has become my favorite from the PDM feminine line! I get that "clean laundry" feel with this, but not in a way that is straight up fabric softener. Valaya is soft, slightly fruity and extremely ethereal. For reference, my favorite fragrances tend to be "clean" smelling (i.e.

I ordered a decant of Valaya because I read good things. It has a fresh musk smell which is nice but there's also a synthetic note that overpowers the others. The bergamot and Musk are noticeable - giving it clean almost aquatic feel too. But there's a sharp synthetic scent that can be overpowering and makes my eyes water.

Loads of peach, bergamot, and orange which combine beautifully and all linger well beyond the initial spray. Quite pithy and bitter, so definitely not as sweet as I was expecting. Woody and musky notes emerge in the drydown. Overall very clean and fresh, but still warm; sunlight on fresh laundry.

I love fruity fig fragrances - and for me, this one left a lot to be desired. The fig note was fruity, but so faint I had to lean close to my skin to smell it. The honey came across like a honeycomb, which was nice - but that faded all too quickly. The dry-down, which showed up in less than 10 minutes, was just an indistinct, soft sweetness - no distinguishable notes, and SO quiet. A better fruity-fig mist alternative: Pink - Sweet Fig . That one has a robust fruity-fig, deliciously-sweet honey, and more depth in the musk + a touch of coconut (and excellent longevity + projection for a mist!).

It really smells like a Japanese floral detergent that I like washing my bedsheets with because I like to feel the scent when I sleep. As a perfume, though, with that price tag, not sure how revolutionary or amazing this is. It's cute, I can see some teenager, myself as a teeny bopper, loving this, nothing wrong with that. But seriously, why so expensive? After trying so many interpretations of a sweet Turkish rose at all price points, I don't quite see the point of this. Just as an example off the top of my head, for anyone who is tempted by this, why not try Chloe or When a Woman Falls in Love (at a fraction of the price of Delina, and much better blended with more interesting facets)?

Opens with an effervescent pear and lychee blast before subduing into a blend of transparent notes composed of watercolor rose and delicate peony. The heart is by far my favorite part of the fragrance — it’s light and aquatic and unexpectedly fresh. The dry down is a pleasant but uninspired woody musk with fruity floral undertones. This isn’t a beast mode scent, but projection and sillage are on the higher end of moderate/lower end of strong; people around you will know you’re wearing it. Longevity is around 8-9 hours on my skin. It’s lovely, but in the end, it’s just a little too much for my tastes: a little too fruity, a little too sweet, bordering on cloying. Which is perhaps a verdict to be expected from someone whose primary goal in life is to smell like a witch in the woods, but even forest crones like to get their sparkling pink on now and again and I’ll enjoy using the rest of my sample even if this isn't full bottle worthy for me.

It's not a surprising scent, not the most original, but I am not gonna lying, it's nice. You can't miss the lychee opening and it goes well with the floral heart notes. Talking about flowers... Even if the roses are here, peonies are also very present. No one is going to be hurt or annoyed and most people will like it. A nice perfume for those days when you don't know what to wear. Edit : after 2 days using it from a sampler, I am seriously considering buying a bottle. It might not be the most original scent I have ever smelt, but it's a very nice one and it has a very good longevity all day without being annoying.

Delina La Rosee is a young and fresh rose, after a rainy day, still with drops on its petals. Fresh rose petals, slightly sparkling but also with sweet variations (thanks to the play between litchi and pear), which is refreshing, a perfect portrait of spring, very usable in the warmer seasons. I may be biased (as we have understood Quentin Bisch is my favorite nose), but it is truly a splendid fragrance, apparently naive but which in reality conceals a very strong personality. In particular, for those who love roses like me, it will represent a sublime olfactory portrait. Beautiful.

This is a very airy fragrance and which I think is mainly due to the strong Lychee top note. It’s very inoffensive and clean smelling. I love the creamy woody base and think it compliments the floral and fruity middle/top notes so well. This would be safe for all seasons, especially warm weather. Overall, this is a wonderful and safe freshy choice suited to pretty much any occasion.

To me, after the more “Delina”-like opening it settles into a watermelon-esque scent. Dew and sweet and fruity with a bit of floral. It’s not my usual style (usually more of a warm floral and vanilla lover and I like the OG Delina a hint more than this but find it hard to know when to wear it).

I have tested all Delinas and this was the one for me. It is a year-round scent for sure. Aside from the notes displayed here on the website there is a note in here that reminds me of the Barbie dolls I used to play with as a child. It’s like the plastic hair of the doll. It’s not overbearing by any means, it’s nostalgic and makes it a very unique rose fragrance.

toned-down, dewy, crystalline version of the OG Delina, just perfect for summer. Lots of lychee and rhubarb in the initial spray, followed by a watery rose. Musky in the dry down. Less overpowering than the original, but still sticks around. Delina was my wedding scent, so will always occupy a special place in my heart.

Yesterday, early before work, the selection had to be quick today.. I searched through my decants and pulled out Delina La Rosée from the box after a long time. It should be something soft, unobtrusive. When working with elderly people, it doesn’t have to be a "knockout". But what I didn’t know in the morning was how positively this day would stay in my memory.

I must admit I had high expectations for Delina La Rosée. Why? Among other reasons, because Delina Exclusif smells very, very special to me. Don't get me wrong: Delina La Rosée is a beautiful fragrance. It starts fruity with lychee and smells very natural and high-quality.

It is a pretty scent but nothing too crazy. Smells like a very stereotypical fruity fragrance, has a kids shampoo scent vibe going on. The raspberry is the most prominent one to me and it is just fruity, not getting any sweetness from it just that typical sharp fruit scent. Definitely a heavy one, more than two sprays you will be giving everyone headaches.

Loved the beginning: berry, musky, hint of vanilla amber. But in less than 30 minutes, it quickly changed into a musky-amber-burnt-plastic-powder blend, with nothing else. If this had stayed with the berry/musky/vanilla amber notes from the beginning, I would have loved it - but the synthetic dry-down killed it for me.

Oh, she's a beautiful feminine-leaning fragrance. At first spray, I get this lovely, mature Froot Loops scent: fruity, with a touch of sugar and a creaminess As time passes, each fruit gets a place under the spotlight. I could smell a touch of candied citruses, bright and zesty, tempered by the sugary aspect. Following that, there's blackcurrant, a lovely darker fruit that gave off a tangy vibe. Then there's raspberry, a realistic tart raspberry that's juicy and delicious without the synthetic note I often get from this fruit in perfume. It's a beautiful fruity cocktail. Following this lovely assortment of fruits, there's marshmallow and cream that slowly takes the stage. Marshmallow is a powdery, sugary treat while the cream gives off this warm, comforting vibe. Ambrette is faint, but gives a little kick at the edge of the scent. I really appreciate this perfume as it's delicate and very well-blended. I don't get any cloyinjg notes, there's no overload of sweetness and it does last on my skin during a reasonable amount of time. I do understand why it's part of so many collections. On my skin, raspberries end up mixing with marshmallow and creams to create this divine dessert. People who love gourmands, fruits and sweetness will definitely be falling for that one.

Yes, Oriana is in the same “gourmand orange blossom” fragrance family as LDBS, Sintra, Guimauve, Watch, Neroli Blanc Intense, LPBJDMV. When it comes to it’s level of sweetness, 1 being least sweet and 5 being very sweet, it’s a 3. The orange blossom is more floral than sweet and syrupy. The berries are in the background with citrus fruits dominating the fragrance. Rounded rather than sharp, creating a “Froot Loops” vibe. I pick up more ambrette and musk than cream or marshamallow. Very nice but it projection is polite unless you spray a lot and for the price, even for a 30ml, I’m not sure it’s worth it. I have a vintage bottle of Love and a 2020 travel bottle. Also Guerlain’s masterpiece gourmand almond/orange blossom “Bouquet de La Marieè and it’s EDP LPBJDMV are for more superior in performance and scent. If you’re looking for a polite floral orange blossom with an emphasis on citruses that’s not too sweet, Oriana is a good choice. I’d you’re looking for a richer more syrupy gourmand experiences, there are better choice out there.

When I first put this on, I had a good chuckle because the opening is a dead ringer for my "signature fragrance" from Middle School. In the early 2000s, there used to be a cheap kids cologne called "cotton candy" by juice bar. It came in a bottle that looked like a cleaner spray and you could get it at Wal-Mart and similar stores. I thought it was heaven in a bottle. After that initial "blast from the past," oriana dried down into a smooth marshmallowy aroma, very similar to Love Don't Be Shy, as others have mentioned. However, I actually think this is much better than LDBS. Somehow, it smells less synthetic to my nose and doesn't have the plastic note that I get from LDBS. Overall, this isn't my usual taste in perfume and reads a bit juvenile to my nose, but that is definitely because it triggers memories from middle school. However, if you are into sweet designer frags, this is a great one to try! It is definitely sweet and playful and will likely get you some compliments!

Sweet, sticky oranges coated in powdered sugar. Hints of raspberry and caramel. Loads of creamy marshmallow and musk. The comparisons to LDBS are there, but Oriana is stronger, less floral, and just a tiny bit powdery. I find LDBS to be a touch lighter and more airy. Both are deliciously beautiful, but Oriana has the edge in terms of sweetness. My partner also likes this one, so that’s a bonus.

This one didn't click for me at first. There was something a little synthetic in it, but after a couple of wears I fell in love. Great for days when I want something that is sweet, fluffy, and a safe wear. Not overpowering, and layers well with caramel or vanilla scents. Sillage and longevity are good but not overwhelming.

A cartoon marshmallow-berry mushroom cloud. Caps lock MARSHMALLOW, subscript berry. And then a muscly bubblegum. I want to say it’s like a roll of Hubba Bubba, coated in that dry, powdery gum starch. Surprised there’s no tuberose listed. Unfortunately gave me a kneejerk dental fluoride vibe.

This is an absolute stunner of a fragrance. Sweet but light, fruity but decadent, it really highlights what makes a house like PDM so highly regarded. It is excellently mixed, moving seamlessly between top, heart, and base notes and has excellent longevity and projection to match its price point.

this is by far my favorite scent ever! it's so beautiful & feminine. never fails to make me feel like a princess! i just wish it lasted a bit longer & had better sillage. but alas! if it were a tiny bit more affordable, i'd wear it every single day - even to bed! i just want to live within oriana's scent bubble

Oriana is such beautiful fragrance, it’s fun, it’s bubbly and it’s flirty. It’s very similar to Love don’t be shy, but I actually enjoy Oriana more because it has fruitiness that LDBS doesn’t have. I enjoy Oriana a lot but struggle to find the occasion to wear it.

Opens extremely soapy akin to old school public bathroom air freshener, but mellows out to something that is very sweet and playful. Reminds me of necco wafers or conversation hearts. Marshmallowy for sure with the slightest bit of citrus (Tang style). Wish it had the longevity and sillage of Delina.

Bombshell Magic was love-at-first-sniff for me. I can't believe I haven't heard more about it! I know that juniper berry isn't listed, and neither is pine - but to me this smells like a chilled juniper berry wreath in the winter. The blackberry (again to me, it smells like juniper berry with my skin chemistry) feels cool/chilled but also sweet, dark, and delicious. The patchouli is mild, but still musky and earthy enough to ground the fragrance (and add a bit of sexy magic). This wears beautifully in cold weather - would be the perfect addition to a thick coat, and the start of snowfall on a cool winter evening. It also has amazing projection, sillage, and longevity - lasts through the day/overnight on my skin! I Iove it so much that it's in my top fragrances - it will be my staple for the holidays in years to come!

Tried it once, but not preferred. It's not the worst or bad fragrance, but a lot of improvisation is required. A whole top note of fruity accords passion fruit, strawberry, and pineapple, with a fresh floral middle note (peony, redberry, lily, jasmine) and a woody and musky base note gives you a myriad of fragrances with less silage. It is a very sweet fruity floral fragrance with a zesty and woody touch. and sometimes the smell of oakmoss just pops out like anything.

Parfums de Marly's Pegasus Exclusif, and maybe I am extrapolating a bit from the brand’s copy, promises a ride on the back of a flying stallion, a journey into a realm of masculine virility and exhilarating power. But I think we need to temper our expectations; the description would have us believe this is the fragrant equivalent of a noble winged steed, all myth and muscle, soaring through the heavens, presumably being the fantastical equine embodiment of toxic masculinity. I'm not saying that I actually wanted any of that, but instead, what we are presented with is a pastel carousel pony, all heliotrope powdered sugar and cracked porcelain. Now, there are some things I am not up to speed on here, which is to say that Pegasus Exclusif implies the existence of a Pegasus not-so-Exclusif, and if that is the case, I haven’t smelled that yet, and maybe that one is a dusty plastic marzipan macaron as well… so I am not sure how this one differs. And unlike other reviewers, I don’t get anything complex or dark or rich out of this perfume; the promised depth and complexity and woods and spices never materialize, leaving a one-dimensional sweetness and a sense of artificial whimsy that smells more like a My Little Pony collection than the epic journey of a majestic beast. ⁝ share

Oh, what a beautiful scent. This is a fragrance that many folks, even people that don’t like many things perfume-related, have complimented me on. This is basically the OG-Pegasus with more almonds and a bit of oud. Hours go by and you still get whiffs of sweet/bitter almonds every hot minute. The sillage is to be reckoned with; do yourself a favour and go easy on the trigger! The scent performs well and can be worn in any season, somehow, though it might be best to only wear it outside on a hot day; else, you might choke out some people. I hope this review is helpful and perhaps motivated you to try out this flagship of a fragrance. Cheers, have a good one!

Love PDM especially Herod. I liked both original Pegasus and Layton Exclusif too but didn’t like them enough to pull the trigger on the full bottle. The original Pegasus was a little to punchy and sharp in the opening and that’s why I didn’t love it. I gladly was able to try the Pegasus Exclusif at Nordstrom. OMG!!! Love it so much at the first sniff and got the 125ml bottle right away. It doesn’t have the sharp aggressive opening and it’s definitely warmer, darker, smokier, smoother than the original. I love they added cardamom and Oud to it. I also love the bitter almond. It has the exclusif accord that I love. It feels like a mix of the Pegasus original and Layton Exclusif so this is a perfect combination of the 2 of my ‘likes’ (then it became LOVE). It’s a 10/10 for me.

Im impressed by how the accord between spices , vanilla , almond is a succes you will discover those olfactory notes on another olfactive angle ( very different than desinger ) . The smell is strong and lightweight ( transparent ) powerfull sillage , the smell pervades the room even when you leav it and so long lasting (14h) i remembered depiste i washed my dress it sill smeling for me it 's the best perfume of marly . The 2nd is : ojan 3 : layton

I was never too much of a fan of the original Pegasus, so I wasn’t expecting much from this edition of the scent. However, the opening of Exclusif, is a much better balance of notes than its predecessor. This one doesn’t feel like a bomb of almond and vanilla. Instead, there is a tad more of the bergamot citrus, a better spice from pink pepper, and the soft heliotrope. I’m still getting some of that almond and vanilla, but I also don’t get the same sort of chemical overhang that I do with the original (maybe it’s just me who got that smell). After 10 minutes or so, the pink pepper and bergamot have faded substantially. Cardamom steps up and I get more of the influence of the middle notes. Yes, almond and vanilla are here for the duration, still not completely dominating anything. It’s softer with a dry freshness to it. On my skin, I pick up lavender and geranium jockeying for influence at different times during this wear. I do like when the geranium hits its heaviest, really adding a colder aromatic vibe to the blend. The main difference between Pegasus Exclusif and the original, is the guaiac wood. The sandalwood probably also has a stronger influence here than in the original. However, the warmth and smokiness that is unleashed here by the guaiac is a really great addition. The dry down is much the same. It’s woodier for sure, but we still get the vanilla and some almond that’s left. It’s an ambery wood finish with those two other notes adding support at the tail end.

Pegasus Exclusif, for me, was not very enjoyable. I would choose the original Pegasus instead, especially since I enjoy wearing it as an office fragrance, which I believe is the most suitable setting for it. While Pegasus Exclusif does resemble the original, it gives me the impression of Pegasus OG mixed with Amouage Interlude.

Pegasus Exclusif has a pronounced oud note and a darker, spicier, and more woodsy smell. It has a more refined and masculine feel than the original, lacking the harsh opening and metallic edge. After Layton, it has swiftly risen to the top of my list of favorite Parfums de Marly fragrances.
Parfums de Marly, Pegasus Exclusif, is a flanker to the 2011 release, Pegasus, and like the Layton Exclusif to the original Layton, Pegasus Exclusif is darker and dryer than Pegasus.

This is another underrated Fragrences that no one really talks about. Pegasus’s and Pegasus Exclusif. This one opens up woody and sweet. It opens with some pink peeper cardamom bergamot, and transitions to some almond, white florals and lavender.

I want to be fair and refrain from giving a rating for this fragrance, excluding longevity and sillage. I justify this by saying that both "Pegasus" and "Pegasus Exclusif," due to the dominant bitter almond, do not fit my preferences, similar to Tom Ford FF.

I LONG for more feminine perfumes that capture this warm sand accord as well as VS has done here. It smells of mandarin, sand dried on the skin, and guava on a bed of white blossoms. The perfect beach scent for those who are tired of sunscreen perfumes. Pairs fantastically with fruity body sprays or simple fruity perfumes like Fragonard Mademoiselle Amour. I once received a Bombshell and Sundrenched rollerball as a gift and fell head over heels for the perfume. However, I must say, the rollerball smells a bit different and even better than the perfume. The latter sometimes has a men’s cologne note that comes and goes. I don’t know what causes that. Unfortunately, it is no longer produced, but you can always find something on Vinted or eBay.

I would like to dedicate my first review to a limited fragrance that has received very little attention here - in my opinion, unjustly so. Anyone expecting high-quality or complex perfumer's art from a Victoria's Secret scent will inevitably be disappointed, but those looking for an uncomplicated, summery light fruit cocktail that they haven't smelled a thousand times before might enjoy this one just as much as I do. The scent transports me to a beautiful beach in the South Seas. I am lying near coconut palms (not directly underneath, as that can end badly), enjoying the lightness of being while sipping a delicious fruity mandarin cocktail. The warm wind occasionally brings me a gentle note of tuberose (but not overwhelming or gum-like) and a few exotic, unspecified flowers (perhaps guava blossom or coral peony?). When I open my eyes, I find myself on my balcony in Bavaria with a mandarin soda in hand, but one is allowed to dream.

This is a short but sweet review. It's a very subtle and very plain kind of vanilla scent. It is definitely intended for those days where you want to smell sweet but not like the whole dang bakery. I like that its a barely there smell but if you are wanting something to make a statement then this scent is definitely not for you. I wish the Vanilla was more authentic smelling though it does hit the nose at times just like icing, it isn't my favorite of the Vanilla scents that I own. I will use this one till it's gone, but will not purchase again.

The opening of Meliora is beautiful. It opens smells like a high-end fruit punch beverage, then dries down to be more floral and musky with that fruitiness still present, just not as foward. I don't care to wear this on hot and humid days because it ends up just "feeling" sticky and comes across sickly sweet. But now that I know that, I try and only wear it on less humid days. This perfume makes me feel like a garden fairy.

Meliora starts off strong with a tart and tangy scent that reminded me way too much of fruity alcoholic beverages. After a while, it calms down a bit, but the tangyness on my skin felt a bit sour, almost acrid, which was a complete disappointment. 30 minutes later, I could sense the florals trying to peak out, accompanied by a green tinged floral jasmine tea. The scent turns floral and sweet, slightly powderish at the edge, with the sour fruit accord blanketing it all. It dries down to a complete vanilla drydown with cedarwood adding warmth to the perfume. Unfortunately, the fruity sourness combined with the herbal jasmine tea and the florals did nothing for my nose. I have the feeling my skin chemistry played a large part in how the scent turned out as when I sniffed it on a strip of paper, it was a wonderful fruity tea fragrance. Oh well, at least, my wallet is happy!

Meliora is for the minimalist pretty girls. She’s soft, she’s light, but she’s definitely grown and sexy. This is one of the more mature fruity scents out there, and is an easy reach for when you want to smell good but not do too much. Also, the bottle is just so beautiful to me. On my skin and to my nose, I mostly pick up on the black currant, berries, and florals, with a hint of muskiness. I don’t get the cassis at all, which can be a hit or miss note because it can resemble cat urine. I don’t really get the vanilla either, but it doesn’t really need it because the sweetness of this fragrance comes from the berries. It kind of reminds me of a dry white wine, like a Chardonnay or Sauvignon Blanc. I really enjoy wearing it but my only issue with this scent is how light the projection is. It’s not totally intimate, but it’s not moderate either where you’re going to get it from arms length away (or not after wearing it for a few hours). The longevity is pretty good at 7+ hours and it stays pretty linear through it’s wear. If you’re looking for a grown woman fruity scent for everyday this is a good one to try. Meliora works well in the spring and summer, and I could see her being used for early fall days. Sure the performance isn’t the best, but the scent itself is amazing. Also, don’t pay full price for this. Only get it when you can get it on discount.

This is an inoffensive fruity floral. Not overpowering, but it basically smells like an inexpensive, decently made, berry scented body lotion. I’m not super impressed with it, but it’s not terrible, just not that original. For a fruity floral I prefer Delina by far—Delina just has more sophistication. This stuff does have pretty good longevity though: 12+ hours.

Meliora is a very beautiful fruity-green perfume. It’s delicious and at the same time very fresh. It feels like you are walking through a fruit orchard, but it doesn’t feel juvenile like some other fruity scents do. Meliora is well blended, fresh and sparkly yet sophisticated, and it is actually one of my favourite perfumes from Parfums de Marly. I absolutely love the bottle as well. This is compliment getter, apparently the only one besides Delina Exclusif, at least where I live.

I feel like I must have a mislabeled sample or something, because the perfume I have smells nothing like the notes, and nothing like the reviews! To be fair, my skin chemistry can be a bit strange, so it could just be that. On me, Meliora is a super flowery jasmine bomb. I don't get any fruit or vanilla at all, just floral for HOURS. A miss for me sadly.

It's interesting the first two notes that immediately popped into my head are not actually in this perfume at all. My first thought was Peaches or Nectarines. Then after a little while, this reminded me of Asian snacks and candies I have had with lychee fruit. Sweet, unusual, and just slightly tart.

I like most perfumes from Parfums de Marly, but this one is the most special to me. The way i would describe this scent is: a sparkly, brown- sugary champagne with freeze-dried berries and fruits that turns slightly creamy. At the same time, it feels like you can point out every single note, especially the blackcurrant and the jasmine tea.

Meliora is much fruitier off the top, mostly a sweet (not cloying), juicy blackcurrant and raspberry. I don't get any citrus. Then, once it dries down, it's a lily of the valley, lightly musky floral that sits close to the skin. This is beautiful and unique, but not too intrusive, so this could definitely fare well in basically any environment.

A pure baby wipe/lotion scent that dries down to a creamy sandalwood (thankfully I'm a massive fan of babyish smells). Very sweet and fruity in warm weather, which makes the stone fruits and frangipani shine, giving it an almost tropical feel. Wearing it in colder weather allows for the red currant to break through- it's juicy, tart, and just sour enough to give the creamy sweetness an edge. Very pleasant and smooth, an elevated fruity floral with some depth.

Cassili is such fun, fruity and peachy floral yet it has some sophistication as well. It’s perfect for days when you would want to escape to a tropical paradise. The longevity is moderate as well as the sillage, so it’s perfect to wear in the office. Cassili is one of my favourites from Parfums de Marly’s women’s collection and would repurchase any time.

This is a bright fruity floral but still quite warm and powdery fragrance. I've noticed I only like it in those kind of fall and early spring days when the air is very crisp but the sun is out, when you need a wool coat and sunglasses. In warmer sping or summer days it feels stuffy, and in the winter the bright fruitiness feels out of place for me. I wish they had it it a 30 ml format, because I don't think I would get through the big bottle.

I really loved it at first. In fact I loved it so much I used 50% of my 75ml bottle. But that was when I was a perfume virgin and just googling scents which people recommend. Once I got more into the niche market and started sampling scents with more complexity I realized how basic this fragrance is, almost to the point where it feels childish wearing it. In fact its so basic that the Dua Brand did an exact dupe where its near impossible to tell the difference. Thats not to say its a bad fragrance. It does smell lovely. I do not smell and sandal wood or red currant or plum. I mainly smell a creamy peach and pineapple pina colada minus the rum. Doesn't smell synthetic in the slightest. Very fresh and sweet scent typical of parfum de marly and other french perfume houses. I would recommend it as a good starter perfume for fragrance newbies but other than that....meh

You sip from a crystal flute of nectar during breakfast on a crisp Sunday morning. On the cafe table is a small, but thoughtfully arranged, vase of fresh blossoms. You're seated on the patio and there's a slight breeze, but you don't mind because it's beautiful outside. Paved cobblestone paths curve through a charming village, lined with assorted flower bushes and greenery. The sun is still low in the sky, and pale beams of light cast soft angled shadows on the stones. The sweetness of the nectar melts into your tongue and fills you with energy as you ponder your plans for the day. When wet on skin, this is definitely reminiscent of fruit juice: tart, but not bright, and incredibly sweet. Underlying that is a feminine powdery smell. Upon drydown, the juiciness fades, and you're left with a softer fruit scent, like sweet-smelling plum skin, gently layered on top of powdery wood and quiet flowers. Maybe there's just a slight brush of honey too.

I am trying, but I can´t befriend myself with PDM perfumes. I was hopeful Cassili would change that, but it didn´t. It feels childish, too fruty for my taste, quite a bit unsophisticated. I miss the finesse, the evolution.
Hello, you scent monsters (ah, I've never called you that before, he he :D)! Welcome to my description of the fragrance "Cassili" by Parfums de Marly. So… what does Cassili actually mean?

When I look at my collection, aside from a certain preference for tuberose bombshells, gourmands, and a tendency towards heavy winter scents, I can't really see a common thread. What is completely missing for me are fruity fragrances. I don't like them, never particularly have, and never will. You think so.

In search of a spring fragrance that should brighten up 2021, I came across Cassili. The reviews and my research on this scent convinced me. So I didn’t think long and ordered it blind. The packaging is rather simple, yet crafted with high quality. The bottle is - I would say - a matter of taste. I was totally surprised that the cap is adorned with a stone.

I am not impressed by the new Parfum de Marly. I have to say that from the scent notes alone - overall too much flower - it was clear that it would not be MY fragrance. I even considered for a while whether to participate in the sharing. However, curiosity won out because I think Meliora, Delina, and also Safanad are great. And Herod too.

Extremely pleasantly smelling perfume. Saffron, Frankincense, resins, apple. What is not to like? But that's not all. This one is special in a way. Develops into a fine blend that resembles camomile throughout the life of scent. In a best possible way. Not like tea. Like you are smelling camomile flower. Intensely and very life like. And then there are top shelf notes I mentioned. Wore it only few times, many people asked about it. Always with a smile. That in my mind is a true purpose of a good perfume. You like it. People around you like it. It starts you conversations.

...but only if you dare! A lot of people recieve the Apple Note as Dominant but in my opinion it s the best rose oud combo if ve smelled. It s sweet and spicy, sometimes even smocky with leathery nuances. But also is very well blended. The saffron is decent and gives a hint of luxury. The Opening is sweet and get s more ambery as time passes by... Another artistic crowd pleaser:-) sillage and longevity are good, for mature guys, definitely worth the money

As soon as I smelled Habdan, the opening seemed very masculine to me, but then, with a surprising evolution, this fragrance transformed into something truly special. There is a smoky part, saffron and amber hints that frame everything. Strong, virile perfume, but which hides a docile heart. Like this wonderful breed of horses.

To me this resembles a walk in holly Mecca bazaar, Oud shops such as Arabian Oud and Abdul Samad Al Qurashi burning gorgeous Indian Oud wood that gets you gravitated towards, a sight of white clouds coming from their outdoors "Mabkhara" that compels you to walk towards their shops only to start picking up other notes including rose and fruity notes of their perfumeries, mixed with the smell of wood and leather you get from antique shops on the way. It's a journey, an Andy Tauer's like tale of Mesopotamia written in perfumery. A masterpiece that is quite different from other PDM's Niche-Designer schizophrenia.

This is a sweet resinous long lasting one. It opens with a punch of frankincense that is a bit off putting to my nose. The saffron works as an underlying carrier of notes in my experience. The apple is not a green apple but a red firm apple. The type that can be cooked and still have some substance to them. It pairs well with the caramel note in this fragrance. This is really what i get. It notes Rose, Oud but after 12 hours I am still searching for them. I would wear this in sub 60 weather. To me its good for day, night, date night etc as long as its cold. If worn in warm weather I would definitely limit the sprays. It could be cloyingly sweet as well.

Habdan! One of my favorite fragrances! An absolutely classy and refined gentleman's fragrance of amazing quality, skill and sophistication. A Masterpiece. I would classify it as an amber, spicy and fruity fragrance. It has that PDM DNA (sweet, clean, smooth and long lasting) as well as being fresh, dry and soft.

PDM makes interesting fragrances. Just when I thought that all fragrances smell similar, Habdan comes to prove me wrong. The opening of Habdan is strong, and has a strange buzzy and woody feel. Immediately, it was followed by a grape-fruity scent. However I try to describe it with familiar notes, it feels not doing it justice.

The opening of Habdan hits with a bunch of saffron, some apple, and frankincense. It’s a lovely blend of sweet/spicy/smoky and honestly grabs my attention from the get go. Now, I’ve seen this cologne compared to Bvlgari Man in Black, and I do see the similarities. Habdan, does have a leather-like aroma at times, but no leather note, and also a smoky spice.

As I already mentioned in my comment on Oajan and tried to explain, the fragrances outside of the major flagship Layton not only surprised me but also convinced me so much that I want to engage much more intensively with the brand. Because Oajan really ignited the big cinnamon explosion among the mass of gourmands. I received Habdan at the same time.

After Habdan was promoted as a hidden gem in some YouTube videos (quote: “criminally underrated”) and the idea of an apple-caramel Marly sounded appealing to me, I eagerly organized a sample. Unfortunately, this was nothing Marly. Habdan is a mild apple water, quite linear and uninspired.

Pear and Orange...opening notes. No mystery here...it's been done lots of times. But this fragrance has a sort to double mystery. First, let me thank my dear friend, and member Pipette for sending me a very generous decant from her precious bottle, so I could try, and understand this unusual, and lovely fragrance. This is a Perfume House I have not heard of, nor have I seen people on other forums recommending it. I went on to their very fancy website, and looked at the other fragrances they have for offer. First of all, most of the fragrances are for men, or classed as unisex. There is one other fragrance for ladies. And ,this one as well. There seems to be some sort of connection with horses, or the names of certain breeds of horses.I won't elaborate on this part of the fragrance..as that is Co. logo or intention). Now, on to the actual fragrance. First of all, the Pear....I am not a fan of fruity fruit orientated perfumes...so was really impressed with this pear note. I didn't detect orange...not at first, just the pear..and it was like a burst of real..organic fresh dewy pear...just opened whilst testing the freshness at an open air market. This was just an introduction to the perfume...It sparkled for the first five minutes with the pear, then I recognized the Orange Blossom..also completely natural..like walking in an orchard in bloom. It lists Iris as a note, but very briefly got that leather handbag note, which Pipette mentioned...we all have different perceptions of notes..which is wonderful! The dry down is soft, and lovely...I pick up the Amber the most...The sandalwood and vanilla are not prominent here...but might be to another wearer. I believe this is a quite expensive perfume. I would say the ingredients are very high quality. I applied this fragrance fully, as I would as if going out...and sat and read a book. The mystery of this fragrance came in waves..weaving in and out. I was very impressed with the the whole concept. If you ever have the chance to test this...please do...it will be a chance to experience an original organic fruit scent..without that jarring fruity vibe) blending into a wonderful soft, interesting and elegant fragrance.

Safanad is my first bottle from PDM, I was never interested in this house. My friend told me that I would love this one so I ordered it and don't regret at all. The bottle is so pretty and I'm surprised how much I love the juice itself. Safanad is a rich composition with gorgeous, narcotic, natural smelling Orange Blossom with sweet Pear and Orange in the opening, both of them making the florals a bit sticky and candied. An addictive tropical breeze from luscious Ylang-Ylang and hypnotic jasmine melds enchantingly into the base where golden Amber, sweet attractive Vanilla and creamy Sandalwood complete the full-bodied blend. It’s bright and luminous, absolutely a scent of happiness. Safanad was released in 2012 and maybe it was quite unique back then, but nowadays it's not groundbreaking in any way, but it's still beautifully blended, the aroma is very rich and the scent lasts forever even on the skin. I think this can be too much for some people. I don't find this similar with Classique Eau de Toilette since this is brighter, not so complex and it doesn't have that sensual mysterious character which original blend of Classique had. There is Orange Blossom and many other same notes but Safanad is clearly Orange Blossom scent with candied fruits while all the notes in Classique are melting together and it evolves into sensual powdery scent and creates a seductive, irresistible veil into your skin. Even if Classique is more complex I think it's easier to wear. I think Classique Intense and Le Parfum Eau de Parfum has more similar vibe with Safanad since those are bright, even a bit solar perfumes and the blends are simpler by focusing more on Orange Blossom than the blend of Classique Eau de Toilette does. Thank you for reading, I hope you liked my review and it was helpful. I would appreciate if you follow me on my IG and/or YouTube (English subtitles available): @ninamariahperfumes It gives me a lot of motivation to write more.

Although the notes are listed as pear and orange blossom, my untrained nose cannot really make these out ... instead I am smelling something reminiscent of a fine leather note. Such as the smell of a brand new leather bag, smooth and soft, incredible, no exaggeration. This elegant perfume develops with powdery fullness, does not overwhelm but has a definite sillage, so much that when I re-enter a room, I can find the scent molecules present in the air. They also remain in the clothes so that it could become something like a signature. However, this scent is demanding a formal occasion to really make its entrance, with pomp and dignity. Top quality. Top price. My tiny sample vial is now guarded like a jewel.

Safanad from Parfums de Marly. Oh my goodness. Never, ever has a fragrance before elicited such an immediate response from me of “holy moly, this is what I imagine so-n-so smells like!” Safanad is a rich, velvety amber, projecting an opulence amplified by orange blossom’s bewitching florals and jasmine’s heady musk, which always seems to me both elegantly amorous but also offers an animalic eroticism. This is a fragrance that seems at first vexingly overbearing and almost outrageously assertive but the better you get to know it the more you appreciate its sumptuous exuberance and enthusiasm. And of course, I am envisioning none other than everyone’s favorite flamboyant and glittering space aunt, Lwaxana Troi: daughter of the Fifth House, holder of the Sacred Chalice of Rixx, and heir to the Holy Rings of Betazed. And much like this character, Safanad at first seems too much, nearly suffocating in its madcap glamour, but underneath its gorgeousness runs a deeply woven thread of melancholy, obscured for a time by orange blossom’s more hypnotizing facade but which, in fact, masks some really somber, sorrowful facets. Both Safanad and our beloved Betazoid intergalactic life coach Lwaxana are complex, compelling, and thoroughly beautiful.

Parfums de Marly Do you get angry when someone calls you a horse? As a rule, they should not, because horses are noble, smart and most beautiful animals. Legends say that from the time of Suleiman, the Queen of Sheba gave King Suleiman a mare named Safanad, and in translation means "pure". Safanad is believed to be the matriarch of all Arabian horses and the oldest of all horses. It is believed that Safanad was an animal endowed with spirit from the North, strength from the South, speed from the East and intelligence from the West. This perfume is an extremely delicate, but also a complex floral fragrance with a composition that shows me every note and leaves a trace of grace and luxury, and a bit of tropical harmony. After the first spray, it leaves a trace of orange with a three-dimensional note of pear, the heart of the perfume itself is sweet ylang-ylang in combination with iris and orange blossom, which gives me a creamy feeling. The base of the perfume is amber, wood and vanilla. A simply stunning fragrance reminiscent of the most luxurious sunscreen. If you like Classique EDP and EDT, Safanad will surely be your favorite.

Safanad is unfortunately not the one. I mean, it smells nice and everything, but it turns out a bit bland on my skin. At the top, I do get the pear and the orange. It gives off a soft, mellowy (almost marshmallow) citrus scent that's pleasing. Petitgrain stays at the edge, giving it a tangy layer. When the florals arrive, it's a soft blanket of powdery florals.

Very nice and powdery smooth ylang-ylang/pear/iris with hints of blossom. Not at all what I was expecting! I have valaya too and I find that lovely and powdery despite not being a big 'powdery' frag fan! Its nice and amber-woodsy. A fruity vanilla with a floral twist, its sweet and fresh and IMO very wearable.

Pear is dominant in the opening. I find the pear to be a little boozey and mushy, as if it's been baked. It's overall warm and spiced and cozy. Not at all a crisp or fresh pear. Orange blossom can really go many ways as a note -- soapy, marshmallowy, animalic, indolic. I find the orange blossom here to sort of be all of and none of those things at the same time.

I'm about to burst the bubble of ecstatic reviews: Safanad is an extremely uninspired fragrance. Many people seem to pick up strong orange blossom, while all I get is jasmine, jasmine, and more jasmine. It’s not that I dislike the flower, but the overall effect feels too simple, too "clean", too bland, for my taste - especially considering the steep price tag.

This was the first perfume I bought with my saved pocket money when I was 14 years old. Perfumes have always interested me. I saved my pocket money for weeks to finally buy my first real perfume. It was at the airport, on the way to summer vacation by the sea, when I first smelled this perfume. My 14-year-old self immediately fell in love with the scent that was clean and airy, yet sweet and reminiscent of marshmallows. I bought it and carried it in my hand for the next 5 hours, smelling it. If I had to describe the perfume now, I would say it smells like sweet fluffy marshmallows and delicious sour currant. Almost 15 years have passed since then. I rarely use it so that it doesn’t run out, because it holds a special place in my heart.

I was pulled towards Athalia due to the frankincense note but, to be honest, I don’t get it at all... Now, what’s making me want it over and over again, it’s the combination of iris and musc . There is something In that combination that gives me comfort, a sense of safe place . When I wear Athalia I fell like nothing bad can happen to me and that’s why I chose to wear it mostly when I go to sleep. I feel also a subtitle suede smell but that I assimilate to the Musc , maybe cashmeran . Also there is a small vetiver somewhere in the very back of the scenery.! One of my favorites from my collection.

Powdery opening; must be the iris. It’s really quite nice—but definitely animalic, with a note reminiscent of Nishane’s Afrika Olifant. I’m surprised at how dark this one is. I definitely get some incense at the beginning. I’m surprised to find I like it, because I don’t tend to like really powdery scents, but there’s something intriguing about this one. I won’t be wearing this regularly, and I definitely don’t want a full bottle, but i admire the perfumer—it’s really well put together.

Athalia is quite lovely. There is a light incense note, at the top, which gets a bit smokier as the wear moves on (but never too much). However, what I mainly pick up at the start of this is orange blossom, orange, and some rose. The iris powdery quality is hanging in the background, with a clean aroma, but it is secondary at this point. After about 10 minutes, Athalia begins to shift more into becoming an iris-led floral perfume. The rose is not really that powerful to my nose, I mostly get the iris and orange blossom, with some of the smoky quality of the incense. Athalia gets warmer, as it moves along, but I wish that orange bitter note still hung around. I really enjoyed that, in the opening act of this fragrance. nulltheless, this perfume moves forward, with a surprisingly nice blend of iris, amber, and vetiver. There is still some orange blossom and vanilla, but those two notes flank, these main three. That’s about what you get for the rest of the wear. The longevity is really quite good, as well. It seems to sit somewhere in the 8-10 hour range, on my skin.

A beautiful, elegant scent my iris-loving mother passed on to me. Gorgeous composition with prominent iris, powdery, and smokey notes with amber in the drydown- very mature and appropriate for more serious occasions. It's one of those scents I adore on her, as an older woman, but can't see myself wearing due to how mature is smells. There is no sweetness from the orange blossom on my skin, and I simply can't think of an occasion that would suit it. Athalia is undeniably smooth and luxurious, and definitely smells expensive, but it simply isn't for me- yet.

Athalia is wonderful. I think it's very different from the rest of the PDMs I've tried. The iris is paired with a lovely incense note, musk, amber and cashmeran. There's a little bitter orange on the top and some orange blossom, but I don't find them to be prominent. Floral, slightly powdery, deep but playful with hints of musk and incense. Interesting and lasting, but not too strong or too high of projection. I feel confident, complicated, interesting and expensive. For me, this is how a rich, glamorous philanthropist smells - I'm choosing to be benevolent, but I'mnot someone to be trifled with. I'm indecisive, but this is absolutely in my top 5 favorite perfumes.

There are larger ones, larger than you. There are purer ones, purer than you. There are more beautiful ones, more beautiful than you. But you are the queen. When you walk through the streets No one recognizes you.
