The longevity is actually pretty good. I'm at about 9 hours and it's still detectable. My overall problem with B-612 is that the scent itself isn't very pronounced.

Nishane B-612 is a gem. Unique and very pleasant. Reminds me just how unique were some 80's and 90's classics. But in it's own pleasant way. Smooth scent. Longevity is very good, projection solid first few hours. Not too sweet, just the right amount. Fresh but does not feel citrusy at all. Possibly I will get a backup bottle at some discount.

Wearing this fragrance was absolutely great experience! The "nose" behind this one is Chris Maurice, guy well known for his brilliant creations for houses like Xerjoff/Sospiro/Kemi, Jazeel and many more, then of course house of Nishane. I personaly think that B-612 is extremely underrated. It works perfect in hot weather and in office or work surrounding.

“ Here's my secret. It's very simple: you can only see clearly with your heart. The essential is invisible to the eye." A phrase as famous as it is true taken from the Little Prince (from whom this fragrance is inspired, specifically it is the name of the asteroid in which he lives), who speaks through notes.

This is like a fougere without any rough, sharp, ends. Let’s say, imagine Platinum Égoïste without the platinum or Brut without the tangy citrus element or even an updated, niche, version of Azzaro pour Homme; this is that. As I get older, I notice my scent sensibilities have changed. No longer do I really appreciate sweet fragrances. The overly sweet ones, at least.

I am a big fan of teas aside from fragrances, and I've been on a hunt for the perfect green tea scent signature for a year now and I've finally found it. Opens up bright, crisp and green with the tea right in your face, giving that iced green tea with lemon feel, right after the first few seconds litsea comes to the front and boosts the scent into a spa. The scent bubble for the first hour or so will be a spa experience alongside some tea. After that though the green-ness fades a little and gets replaced with a combo of yuzu, fig skin and some herbs and it gives me the impression of being laid out on a massage table and you can smell those oils that they put on you. Until it finally evolves into soft-spicy green musk. This is THE only scent I've smelled that simultaneously feels optimistic, energizing and relaxing at the same time. So good in fact that I've made it my signature. MUST try.

Litsea is a fruit of a small evergreen tree native to the Far East. It is said that angels like its scent so much that they are deeply grateful when we spread its aroma. An aromatic, slightly citrusy aroma that reinforces the opening of this splendid fragrance created by one of the most talented noses in perfumery: Rasquinet. The green tea notes, always accompanied by aromatic accents, do nothing but make this fragrance energizing, very pleasant, with a more incisive personality than the already wonderful Wulong Cha. Here, from the X line, this is a very perfect, harmonious and sparkling reformulation. I like. “Four Belties” painted by Lin Fengmian.

I really, really liked the original Wulong Cha, even though I would have found the scent more appropriate in a luxurious spa than on skin. I don't dislike this X version either, but I couldn't use the words "I like it a lot" with a clear conscience. The two Wulong-Cha's don't seem that similar to me. In Wulong I, the cubeba litsea covers everything from my perspective, sending the tea somewhere in the back. By contrast, in Wulong II, the green tea note is obvious even to me, and the litsea is barely noticeable, dominated by bergamot at the top of the pyramid. The main battle is between the green tea and the white magnolia (that easily recognizable magnolia accord once you've repeatedly smelled perfumes that list the note, but which has not the slightest connection to the real magnolia). I don't know if in this case it's the happiest of combinations, it seems to me that the tea somehow turns the magnolia sour and that's not exactly ideal. At first glance, it vaguely reminds me of two other perfumes, and the two are neither the original Wulong nor Green Tea, but Magnolia en Fleurs (Avon) and Amyris Femme (MFK). Somewhat ironically, my favorite of the three is the outsider Magnolia en Fleurs. Good performance.

I still detect a mellow citrus fragrance as soon as I applied the perfume to my skin, but this time, there's a herbal, almost floral accord underneath that seems to cut through everything. Tea this time is green: a more fresh take on Wulong Chà. Citrus fruits end up leaving in favor of a green tea flavored with thyme. The latter adds freshness and a bit of spiciness. After awhile, magnolia takes the center stage and stays until the end. I thus end up with a tinge of green tea, supported by floral musks and a hint of figs. The drydown evlves into this spicy forward perfume with magnolia and musky figs. The green tea has been choked out by the spice. Magnolia takes way too much space on my skin for me to add this perfume to my collection and the drydown is definitely not to my taste. Floral musky figs turn into this weird plasticky scent that I really did not enjoy. I wish green tea had stayed a little longer as it was quite refreshing and unmarred by other notes.

I was overall disappointed with the X collection sample set, they all seem the same but with minor differences between them. Except this one, it one stands out from the rest. Its such a unique citrus. At first its like the peel of a fruit, bitter and a little bit sweet. The best part is that citrus doesn't go away, it blends in with the tea, thyme, and magnolia to make a slightly bitter citrus earthy chamomile like scent. That middle blend lasted for some hours. It will eventually start to dry down into a sweet and slightly earthy musk. This scent lasted for at least 6 hours on my skin. It projected well, especially for a citrus and musky scent. Its the perfect scent for working in an office, it projects enough to catch people's attention but not so much where you get into called into HR.

This is not AI. I love this fragrance This is the fragrance of a young spirited but old hearted samurai that has fought many battles to defend the Japanese Empire. After finishing his last battle against an invasion, the veteran samurai decided he will resort to his remote home, out in the lush rainy forests of Japan during monsoon season, to finally rest.

Opens with a citrus KABOOM. Like being punched in the face with lemons. After drying it becomes possible to detect the tea note, and the musk strengthens and warms too. This is absolutely glorious. It's a beautiful blend of bright citrus and light floaty musk and is very nicely balanced between sweet and sharp and creamy and fresh.

Very nice opening good fresh scent strong too blast of citrusses at the start and it smells like that for a good halfhour. but just like the og maybe even more so, after the citrus kind of dies out it becomes like a little white flowery and it just kills the scent for me as a Man. In this version with the magnolia it might be even worse.

The note Litsea Cubeba is described as “a lemon-like, sharp, fresh smell with a sweet undertone” and I think this perfume really gives that vibe. Wulong is a bright citrus tea scent with hints of a white floral such as magnolia. I like the scent and it wears very strongly for the first 3 hours.
